Well, I've been waiting months for this taproom to open and it finally has! Today at the soft opening from 2-6pm, the boys, Christian and Gar, opened their doors with 5 brews on tap and lots of growlers to fill. The taproom has great curb appeal! This place, which has a cozy, cabin-like atmosphere, belongs somewhere in Colorado on the cover of a magazine! Great views from the taprooms 2 bar areas (upstairs and downstairs) and large upper and lower patios as well. I can already picture snowy days here...all they need is a fireplace (Hint, Hint). From upstairs you can look out in the brew room, and much to my surprise you can also sit in there and enjoy your pints where the magic happens! As for the beer, if you haven't tried any of them yet, though they have been available at many bars, restaurants and filling stations, it's quite tasty. My faves so far are the Basil Rye Man and the Cutaway IPA. And I hear there is a sweet potato stout on the way as well. With room for 12 taps, there is much to look forward to! Cheers!

Do not subject yourself to this place!! Came here with a group for a bachelorette party. Collectively we have pretty realistic standards in that situation. Just wanted a fun place to hang out on Broadway, it didnt need to be too fancy. Well they did not disappoint. With a group of 9, there was not much room for us so we stood near the bar. A very nice table of women got our attention and told us we could have their table because they had dinner reservations and were on their way out. Well the manager apparently took issue with this and approached me personally to say "do not harass my customers and ask them to leave. You are making them uncomfortable." I was rather shocked because we absolutely had not asked them to leave. He yelled at me repeatedly and then had the nerve to come over and barked at us that we needed to order food. Another person from the place came over to apologize and say "sorry that's just how he is." As the manager of a restaurant, your policy is to berate a large group of new customers?! No thank you. They still made us pay for drinks, and we promptly left. Buyer beware, you may get a lecture with your overpriced drink.

Visited Ole Red for the first time this weekend and we found ourselves choosing this place over and over during our vacation. Today was our last day in Nashville and we went back to have lunch at this incredibly air conditioned gem! Not only were the food and drinks phenomenal, our server Aaron (from Texas) was amazing. He was very attentive and professional, and he provided great customer service while we enjoyed the music for a couple of hours. We will definitely be back to Ole Red next time we're in Nashville!
Hate to complain, but the food just wasn't good. Nobody in my family enjoyed it. The music was great, and the service was average. Could've gotten better food at McDonald's to be completely honest.

We came here right around 10PM and our kind waiter told us that the kitchen will be closing soon so we ordered the quickest and fastest food to make, shrimp scampi and bison burger, we just want to eat, we are not picky at all we just want ant to try their food but everything we got are a huge disappointment I ordered a shrimp scampi,  but it's more like buttery spaghetti, I couldn't even tell if White wine was ever poured in it(the ingredients detail was in the menu),  and my husband bison is still red in the inside  not even half cook, we didn't complain because we agree that it's was our fault and maybe the cook was  in a hurry and has other plans but later on hubby and I agreed that we are not coming back here again. The only good experience we had here is the music.  anyways this review is meant to help  those late night eater like I am.

Great venue with a wonderful variety of performers for all ages from Classical to Pop to Jazz to CHildren's programs to a unique (not exclusive to this area) live performances of music by the symphony accompanying movies (West Side Story was the one we saw).

Helpful staff, polite ushers literally bend over backwards to accommodate patrons - even those who seems to refuse tis sit in their assigned seat. (We saw one woman who apparently wanted to sit with friends, moved by ushers 3 times, twice interrupting our view of the performance. Ushers continued to be professional and polite.)

Accommodations for people of all ages and 'conditions' - physically challenged or otherwise. 

On site cafe serves light sandwiches and salads before most performances, wine and other beverages available inside as well. (This is one aspect I appreciate but wish they would as patrons to not bring drinks into the performances. Saw two examples of spilled drinks in aisle near us at the last live Pops Concert we attended this week (Franki Valli).

Love the mix and match build your own series. Overall, a super venue for live music and performances for all ages and all tastes.

Met some friends after work, had a cool two for one beer special. The atmosphere is really chill and they had a live band which was really nice to not hear loud music just hanging out. I always drink their southern whit which is always a good go to. Upstairs they had like a walk over to a patio that looked really cool, just too cold to go. You can see into the whole brewery. Even had a little open seating next to the tanks. It's not the biggest place inside, but in the summer I bet the patio will be awesome. It's right under the freeway so parking can be a little iffy but not hard to find

Tried medium spicy chicken and burned my tongue so badly that I wanted to cry. And I love spicy food. They brought me a second serving of non spicy when I asked though which was ok. Beware when eating chicken even if advertised as medium....it's not.

Great venue! Even though the Hawks lost, we still had fun. It differs from United Center in that this place has so many more bars to stop in and sit and have a few. It's a great sports venue, smaller than Chicago but really made well. Just has more places to gather and sit at bars and relax instead of just sitting in your seat. That idea is a lot better, translates to more convo with your friends. 
Also worth a mention is that the outside doors leading in to the arena are packed before games! It's like a parking lot party! People bring chairs, sit and watch the game on the huge screens of the building. 
There's vendors selling BBQ goodies, too. Nashville has some great fans!

Whenever Sue and I are traveling, one thing we love to do is check out local beer.  It really gives you a sense of a place if they have a local beer scene.  I don't know why.  It just does.

This was the only official brewery we were able to get to on this trip.  We did drink a few other local beers while in Nashville, but Tennesse Brew Works was the only place we were able to go to and it did not disappoint.

First off, the day we were here was beautiful.  It was in the 60's and that made it the perfect spot to sit outside on their deck and relax with a beer in hand.

The place was rather crowded.  There is a beer bus in Nashville that takes you around to breweries and I believe we arrived just as a bus dropped off a group here.  After a few minutes we were able to get to the bar and order a few beers.  I had the Southern Wit (a Belgian style white), Sue had the Natchez (an American Pale Ale with rosemary).  With beers on our person we made our way upstairs and to a table outside on the deck.

After a few minutes a few people joined us at our table and we struck up a conversation with them.  Very friendly atmosphere here.  A few of the other tables had some games going (Jenga and such) and it was just very laid back as you would expect from the south.

Look for this place.  It is a bit off the beaten path in the Gulch, but worth the stop.

I love this place, we had suite tickets which included free food and drink.  The food was absolutely amazing, but I did have to knock this rating down to 4 stars because I found a very long piece of hair in my salad.  Otherwise, the food was over the top good.  The chicken was moist and had an awesome flavor.  

They had tons of deserts, unlimited popcorn, beer and wine.  If you are going to go see a hockey game, this is the way to do it!

Id like to actually rate how the music or drinks were here since it came highly reccommended, but I cant. The barely old enough to drink himself bartender decided to not take my out of state Id for some reason (im 32), so we never got in the door. Maybe it was because I was with two people of color? Avoid this place.

We had not one but two Great experiences here during our weekend trip and Jeff was our server on both occasions!  Our experience was excellent from the food, drinks and the timely and consistent service during both visits! Thank you to Jeff and Mitch!

Definitely a tourist trap but worth a stop in. 
Margarita's are ok. I have had better. Landshark beer is their staple as well. 
I didn't have any food. 
They had live music going at noonish which was cool. 
Of course better options for traditional Nashville feel all over Broadway.

Situated right on Broadway itself at the intersection of 5th Avenue, Bridgestone Arena is "Smashville" - home of the Predators, grazing ground of Gnash, and a pretty decent place to get some hot chicken during a hockey game. Much like the Staples Center during a Kings game, there really are no bad seats at Bridgestone when the Predators take the ice. The nosebleeds in section 301 still have an awesome view. In section 117 you can see the puck rock the back of the net off Forsberg's wrist shot before the red light goes off and Tim McGraw starts singing "I like it, I love it" and the residents of Smashville chant "You Suck!"
I guess they also have music here once in a while, and not just on the Band Stage between periods. Whatever. Let's go Predators!

Place was a bit of a dive, but the artist was good. Disappointed in the beer selection and it was all bottles. Bartender was very nice and charged my cell phone for me when she heard me say my battery was low.

Just went to our first hockey game here, and found the arena just OK. Frankly, having seen Nashville Airport , the Country Music Hall of Fame, and so many other sites around the city, I found this arena surprisingly lacking in upscale amenities.  We were in the upper bowl...this one was very steep and cramped...there was little room on the landing, seats were very narrow, and the rows were very closely spaced. The seats themselves were comfortable, but the stupid cup holders were too small to hold anything (at least they could not hold the reg size soda or bottled water we bought)...who designed this?? The men's room near us was also very small and cramped...it had three urinals, three sinks (no mirrors), and one entrance/exit.  As a result...LONG lines. Finally, and I can't honestly say I remember too well, but I can't recall seeing ANY auxiliary scoreboards/displays other than the large central one. Please correct me if I'm wrong, but I don't remember seeing a single out of town score?

Most importantly (for me at least), the food was expensive and completely nondescript...we could have been anywhere in the country. The only local nod was some BBQ nachos, and these were only available at a few scattered locations. Otherwise, you could get PLAIN burgers, hot dogs, fries, nachos. No dressed up anything! SO BORING! As expected, it was also pretty bad. 

The game experience itself wasn't anything special either...what was memorable was what had to be the worst introduction/rev up to face-off I have ever seen at a pro game. After warm ups, the teams clear the ice, the lights dim, and the announcer cranks up the music. You then watch a montage on screen for  ten minutes while they send the Zambonis out to resurface the ice. Then they lower a giant Preds head, crank the music again...and you watch another montage. Then the cheerleaders come on and slide by while the music is still cranked. Finally, the players from both teams kind of infiltrate the ice while the announcer plays the player introduction montage (but the starters are already on the ice so it's not like they spotlight them). At this point, your ears are bleeding since they ironically (you are in Music City after all) don't understand the meaning of crescendo and everything has been at "11" for twenty minutes. 

It is hard to say anything about the game atmosphere and fans since the Avs put three on the board in the first period alone. However, even though they announced that the game was a sellout, there were many empty seats at face off, and it never really got loud, even when it was still a game. The announcer definitely could have done a better job psyching up the fans...as it was, it seemed he just preferred to play the usual rock anthem snippets and unending crowd cam shots. I do have to say the usher in our section was very nice and polite, however.

Can't say anything about the parking, as we stayed at the Renaissance and walked. The Hilton did seem like it would be more convenient, however.
One of the best arenas I have been to. Very clean, spacious, a lot of venders, great view even from the top, and friendly workers.

Although I love Nashville and there were many positive things about the arena, the seat size, Patron Platinum Club, and ticketless events are the reason for my low rating. The arena was very clean and had a lot of drink and food options. Starting with the ticketless entry when you are directed to swipe your credit card at the gate and the major fail for us. Going to dinner they swiped our card and their machine went offline. It took us over an hour to get in because it said our credit card was already swiped. We missed dinner reservations and never actually got tickets but were allowed in. The seat size in 107 section was the absolute smallest for any arena I have been in. I do not recommend Patron Platinum club for dinner. It was over 50 for a subpar buffet. There are a lot better options in Nashville for food.

My favorite brewery in Nashville by far! Beers are delicious, workers are so kind and helpful, and that chicken sandwich is the BEST I HAVE EVER HAD. Such a cool atmosphere, if I lived in Nashville I think i'd come every week!

Finished the night at Layla's after visiting several overly packed bars with so/so music. We are not 21 anymore, and do not have what it takes to push through the traffic! I wish we had went to Layla's to begin with. Jeremy made our night! He is so much fun to be around!!! The band was awesome too! Wish I had gotten the name! Good prices, good music, great atmosphere, amazing service! If I am back in Nashville, I will be here!!!

I drove from ATL to Music City for 2012 Grammy Nominations concert   I parked on a street not far from the Arena.  The area was empty but as I walked closer to the Arena there were many police officers.  Entering the arena was very easy, there was a large group of concert attendees but the line moved smoothly.  I got lost in the Arena and walking past my section all I saw were large black curtains blocking the entrances to the aisles. There were two women sitting at a table and they asked me if I needed assistance. I gave them my ticket and one said that due to last minute stage changes, they were going to give me seats that were closer to the stage. This may have been done because the show was being televised live however I still was happy that I was closer to the main floor without paying floor seat prices. It looked as though if I were to sit in other sections of Bridgestone I would have a pretty good view of the stage.  I have to say that everyone I encountered at Bridgestone was nice and helpful.  Leaving the Arena the police officers directed traffic and ensured that the large crowds leaving the Arena crossed the street safely. I do agree with some other reviews that the sound at the Arena could be perfected but I had fun.  I hoped to return this year but the Nominations Concert returned to LA.  If the organizers decided to have it again in Nashville I would go.  The Arena is also a good option when you want to see a concert at Philips but the good seats go fast!  Check out the ticket options for Bridgestone!

Bridgestone Arena is a really fun place to be. Got the chance to attend a Preds playoff game and boy this place was lit. Smashville has the best fans I have even seen. Plenty of concessions and merchandise stand throughout the arena. It is fairly easy to navigate and the lines moved fairly quick before puck drop. Go Preds!

Great venue location! I visited Nashville for NewYears and saw a show at Bridgestone.  From a music perspective it had great acoustics and more than ample room to handle a ton of rowdy electronic music fans!  All of the venue employees were accommodating and friendly.  Beer was expensive but what do you expect at an arena?

How this place got 2 1/2 stars is beyond me. One of our party received half their order. There was no silverware because it was all in the "dishwasher". What?  We were here in the morning before a Titans game and noticed a huge line outside this place. Turns out it was for a different restaurant. Wish we were that smart. Stay away from here.

We tried coming here on a Thursday I believe, but were dismayed to see a "closed for private event" sign on the door. See, we would've known that if they had picked up any one of the 7 calls I made prior to leaving my friend's apartment. 

We tried again Saturday night and I again called prior to leaving just to make sure it was open to the public, but keeping with my short tradition, they didn't pickup. Luckily, it was open! 

We went at night, so we couldn't tour the brewery, but you get an awesome view either through the windows or from a second story platform inside of the brewery. 

We each ordered a flight and sat down to enjoy some beer, fried frog legs and sweet potato poutine. 

The flight was excellent. You can't go wrong with locally-brewed beer especially when it's in-house. My personal favorites were the Extra Easy and the Country Roots (description in the photos.)

I've never been a hops guy, so The Cutaway was tough to swallow. Literally. With an IBU of 70 (pretty much double of the aforementioned beers), I just couldn't do it. It ended up being the last beer to go but mainly because my friend taunted me and said some very not nice things about my manhood. 

But The Extra Easy. Man oh man that was a beer. The Country Roots was also spectacular as I've never had a sweet potato stout before. 

The frog legs were awesomely cooked with a nice spice to them, but I was not a fan of the sweet potato poutine. Not because it wasn't cooked well, but because I couldn't get behind the concept. Some sort of gravy with melted cheese (not curds) with a fried egg on top. And obviously, sweet potato fries. I don't know, poutine is a traditionally full on savory dish, so the sweet of the fries really messed with my palate. My friends liked it though, so I was alone in that department. 

Oh we also had wings. They were okay. 

Obviously the beer is the star of any brewery, and they did not disappoint. I'll be sure to come back to get the full tour experience next time. 

Also, the service was a bit....curt. That needs to be worked on.

Great venue with a fantastic floor, guaranteed to have a good view wherever you're standing. Paid parking is not too expensive, but I've managed to find street parking most of the time. The only reason they're not getting 5 stars is for their bar. Yes, they have two bars, which should help the flow of things, but my god, they're both always so packed and they need more staff.
Music was great. Didn't know what to expect walking in, but such a hidden gem amongst the big name hot spots!

You remember right after 9/11 when TSA made everything really slow at the airport?  You appreciated the effort to secure your flight/trip and therefore,  obliged to the inconvenience?  Well,  tonight felt like that.  Except it's 2015. We bought Frontseat tickets for a show.  Arrived earlier than the opener.  Waited in a massive line (?).  Didn't mind the delay for the metal detector.  You know,  safety and all.  But after all that wait for a pre-purchased ticket,  we had to wait 45 minutes to get a drink.  There were 2 bartenders for a 50 ft bar packed 4 ppl deep. Ridiculous.  The show was Amy Schumer.  She would be disappointed with the wait for a drink.  So was I.  I can handle overpriced at a show.  But  waiting 45-an hr for a $12 beer for an expensive show is too much.  I'll select a different venue next time
Horrible Staff. Horrible Service. Horrible Selection. Horrible music. I would recommend to skip this place. Hopefully it's gone soon
Don't waste your time coming here. The bartender was pleasant, but the owner/manager was a jerk and completely ruined the experience.

The worst. They were supposed to be apart of a 90's bar crawl that I paid money to participate in. We get to Winners and there were no specials and no 90s music. Very disappointing. If you're not going to participate then don't sign your bar up.

Came here with coworkers and had a blast. Everyone ordered alcohol so I asked the bartender to bring me the sweetest, most candy-like drink they had. He brought me the Don't Stop the Carnival drink and after everyone tasted it half the table ordered one as well. It was definitely the best sweet drink of the night. 

I've been before but it was so long ago I didn't remember anything and wasn't yelping back then. Luckily, we all ordered and shared food (my dream!) so I got to try a TON of things. 

I found I love some of their shrimp items, but not all. I actually disliked their Coconut Shrimp which is weird because I LOVE coconut shrimp almost everywhere. The New York Strip Steak had a good flavor but it was too rough for me. I forgot I prefer a different cut. The Pretzel Sticks were just not good to me. They were doughy inside and the dipping sauce was a sharp mustard that I couldn't stand. The grilled chicken tasted a little blackened, which I didn't enjoy. Otherwise it was good. The Key West Quesadilla tasted ok by itself but I know if I could've eaten the sour cream and salsa with it (forgot to ask my coworker for some) it would've been great. 

It was a great experience to have with my coworkers. I think the drinks were the best part of the night but the food was just ok. Nothing really special. Maybe we just picked the wrong things. 

To Try:
Beach Tacos
Island Kabob

Loved: 
- Chocolate Banana Colada
- Don't Stop the Carnival (alcohol) (fav)
- French Fries
- Grilled Blackened Shrimp
- Lava Lava Shrimp (with extra sauce!)
- Ice Cream with chocolate sauce 
- Island Rice
- Key West Quesadilla (with sour cream and salsa)
- Mango Salsa

Ok: 
- 5 o'clock Somewhere (alcohol)
- Corn
- Green Beans
- Grilled Chicken Breast
- Rum Runner (alcohol)
- Sauteed Island Lime Shrimp
- Shrimp Trio
- Strawberry Margarita
- Volcano Nachos

Disliked: 
- Cilantro Lime Cole Slaw
- Crispy Coconut Shrimp
- Conch Fritters
- Horseradish-Orange Marmalade
- New York Strip Steak (medium)
- Pretzel Sticks
- Yukon Gold Loaded Mashed Potatoes
Great hangout. Great taps with trivia. Small food selection - off on the edge of town- uber to get here not walking to other locations nearby.

We stopped by in the afternoon on a weekday. There were perhaps only half a dozen other people in the building. We just stopped in for a quick flight. The decor and ambiance were fun! We tried the Basil Ryeman, which was really interesting! Only try this one if you like basil, as the basil flavor is very strong! We liked it, though. We also tried the Farmer's Beat, which was reddish in color from the beet root. It had the beet flavor, but it was subtle, not very in your face. We had the Country Roots Sweet Potato Stout, which was my favorite! I think it's kinda hard to find a unique stout in this day and age. The sweet potato gave it a sweet, slightly earthy flavor. We also had the Wildwood Flower Honey Blonde. It was good. You could definitely taste the honey. The staff was nice. We enjoyed the visit!

Not a popular choice on Broadway since it's a chain but they have great live music just the same.  The perfect margarita gives you the most bang for your buck - all other Broadway drinks are $9, same as this one, but much weaker.  Go here and drink a few and then venture out to the local bars.

As a die-hard Parrothead who frequents this joint, I was so sadly unhappy with the service received tonight. Our waitress, Annie, was slow and not attentive to our needs at all. We ordered a drink that clearly needed a straw and by the time we got them, they were melted. She was slow to bring our food as well, our nachos were already room temp and the cheese had dried and hardened. Not able to tell her because we didn't see her until we were about ready to walk out. No service at all. By the time she came back, everyone in our section was hollering for her attention. We usually only sit at the bar and have always had a good time, but tonight was just plain awful from waiting 20 mins for straws for frozen drinks and then served cold food. This is service that JB wouldn't approve of. I couldn't leave fast enough.

We had a great experience. Our waitress, Kiersten, was incredibly nice and friendly. She took great care of us. The 5 o'clock somewhere was a great hangover cure for the morning for my girlfriend. We would definitely come back because of Kiersten's hospitality.

Very nice arena. Came to see Drake and Future and it was wonderful. The arena is along the strip with over 20+ bars so you can have a drink or 4 (like i did) before you head to your festivities. You can check in with your phone which is very helpful. Place has so many bathrooms. Not once did i wait on a 5 mins women's bathroom line. Thank god. And Katie at the box office was a doll. I had a terrible situation with my tickets and she helped me tremendously !
We have gone to see several performances, we love Brody Dolyniuk, when he preformed Queen in 2014,  I have requested they bring him back, but they haven't yet.

This place rocks! Came here based on recommendation and so glad we did. The Basil Ryeman beer is a great compliment to the Impossible Veggie Burger & fries. I don't even know what was on it but boy was it good. Burger & fries was $18- so a little pricey, but enough for 2 people to split. Don't miss Tennessee Brew Works!
Awful service burger was raw when asked to be medium well. Waitress was rude dropped the food ran away dropped the check ran away. They werent even busy. Go some where else.

Oh wow! wow! wow! wow! wow! wow! wow!!!!

Nashville has a first class symphony hall.
Like everyone else has said, the acoustics rock.
Seats are cushy and comfortable, with plenty of leg room - nothing like a jet...

It's absolutely first class..
Their whisky inventory is very limited.
My Old Fashion cost $8.
Son got apple juice (2x) and water = $17.
Valet - $20.

We went to see the rock classic, "Music of Queen," and were about 10 rows from the stage - center.  Excellent seats, nice people sitting next to us.
We were on our feet quite a bit, dancing in the isles..
Place was packed and they said all three nights are sold out.
That's the way it should be.
Bringing in youthful music is bringing is a more diverse mix of audience.

We will return for sure, and next time, we'll park at LP Field, walk over and into the symphony hall..  No big hike.. and there's an elevator in the River Center bldg..

Very glad I experienced this great place, took a lot of photos, had great seats, and enjoyed the music immensely.
Will probably buy season tickets.

I watched a college basketball game here and had some fries. They were average but the game was all right. You can see the brewing plant from the bar which is pretty cool but the tables are pretty full and depraved

Absolutely love this venue. I was here last night to see Bonobo/Jungle and being the geriatric that I am.. definitely took the whole.. show starts at 8 thing as.. Oh the show must actually start at 8. FAIL. HOWEVER, everything was A-OK when I realized the venue is attached to a pretty cool bar that you can access easily. TIP- you can drink at this bar and save yourself $2 on a beer... plus they serve craft beers on tap. When I was there they had the 312 IPA, A bock from chattanooga (Amazing), Red Hare, and a couple of black abbeys. 2 craft beers was $10. 2 domestic tall boys are $9. Heads up-- Happy Hour is until 7pm on weekdays and they had awesome specials that include 2 for 1 drafts. Outside seating is great-- a bunch of picnic tables. Plus/downside is outside is smoking. WHICH means inside is no smoking- which I cannot believe. It was so nice coming back from a concert and not having knocked off a couple years from my life + not having my amazingly beautiful hair reek for the next week. 

Venue is a pretty large warehouse. Great acoustics. The cleanest bathroom I have EVER seen at a club/music venue. AND there was no line. Seriously. 

Loves it! Now I just need to get a kimono, cropped top, high waisted shorts and body glitter so I can fit in.

Usually not a big beer drinker but the flight here was too good of a deal not to try. Only 10 bucks for a sampler of five, it's a steal. Forgot their names but the super dark one all the way to the right of the platter was my favorite. It went down pretty well with their frog legs. Ended up buying a case of the Southern Wit and the Extra Easy after my meal. 

Overall awesome experience and a must visit place when coming to Nashville!

Every time my friends and I go downtown to bar hop we always eat here first! It is always delicious.  

I totally recommend the fish tacos..O-M-G! The best I've ever had! The fish has this magical seasoning on it with fresh cabbage and this wonderful sauce, it also has some salsa type stuff but I opt out on that. The tortilla is always warm and I seriously can't get enough. It comes with black beans which I'm not a fan of period not just theirs, I substitute fries instead! 

The only reason this place is not getting a 5 star rating is because of the long wait, which I understand a long wait when busy, but almost every time we've gone(at least 10-12 times) everything takes a long time from the drinks to the entree. 

We always get a shot of tequila and an incommunicado it's the best drink ever! With around 6 different liquors and I think 3 or 4 different juices it is simply amazing! I suggest anyone to try it, it's not too sweet but not extremely strong which can make these dangerous. You could get extremely drunk extremely quick because they taste so good without the burn of all the alcohol. 

We will be back very soon this is definitely my favorite place downtown and more so my favorite place to get fish tacos!

Stopped in on a Friday night, this place was hoppin! It's a smaller dive bar, but the band that was playing, Eskimo Brothers, could be heard from the sidewalk and drew us in! These guys were AWESOME, hillbilly county music, had the crowd engaged, and they were hilarious as well. Definitely stop in Layla's for something a little different from the rock country/cover bands.

Bridgestone Arena ushers go out of their way to make sure you're not enjoying the event you're paying good money to attend. 

My wife and I were in attendance for the Amy Schumer event and had the displeasure of dealing with the annoying ushers. My wife had her phone on the lowest brightness setting and got a notification on her phone and all she did was glance at it (we're out of town, we should be able to look at our phones in case of a family emergency). Two seconds later, some rude usher threatened to kick us out for "attempting to take pictures." We didn't have this issue the night before at the Nashville Predators & Chicago Blackhawks game. 

I'm going to do my best to avoid attending any future events at the Bridgestone Arena.

Marathon Music Works is a great venue - the building alone deserves five stars. It's old, historic, and absolutely amazing. The building itself is also home to a variety of other shops and offices, including Nashville's independent radio station, Lightning 100.  Inside Marathon Music Works, you'll find three different bars, so you spend less time waiting in line when you could be watching your favorite artist do awesome things on stage. The bathrooms are usually immaculate, and they have an attendant to give you soap and paper towels. How fancy? Oh, and the artists they line up every year are the perfect mix of local and nationally known. Three cheers for great music and a great venue!

Growing up in the Nashville area, there was one thing that anyone from the area rarely did: go hang out on Broadway.  It's just where the annoying tourists went to buy overpriced cowboy boots and butcher the classic standards at karaoke.  Even though the city has changed a lot since then, it's one thing that remains: there remain very few good reasons to go to Broadway unless you just want to play tourist.  National Underground is one of those reasons, because it's so unlike any other bar on the street.  It's never crowded, it's very 'low-key'.  The bands are very good (the band there when I was last in, Brian Wain's Hushpuppy's Daddy, was phenomenal), I've never had to pay a cover, the beers are reasonably priced, the staff are always exceptionally nice, and it just has a really good non-pretentious vibe that is missing from its neighbors.  I've never had the food, but I am anxious to try it.

The reason it's docked a star, then? When you ask for a water, they charge you $2 and give you a 16oz bottle. No bueno, guys.  Fix that, and you'll get five stars.
What a shit show. Waited an hour for food that never came. In the middle of a lovely city this looked cool. What a mistake. Didn't even comp us the iced tea.

Just a tourist-friendly place, in my opinion. I'm not really big on Jimmy Buffett, only being familiar with four of his songs. I like his image and style though, and that's why I chose to come here on my vacation. It's pricey, as one would expect, plus its got a decent gift shop. I'm more than happy to provide for Mr. Buffett's yacht fund (laughs). 

The food was great: I had the Cheeseburger in Paradise, with fries. I'm like Jimmy, I like mine with lettuce and tomato, a cool kosher pickle, french-fried potatoes and Heinz 57. You got to be in that state of mind! I topped it off with two Margaritas. There's not just one, but several different flavors. I chose simply the basic. The waitstaff is very friendly and they seem to love their job, which I value. Check it out if its in the city you visit!

I visited on a Saturday night, live entertainment, busy on both floors, a good atmosphere. Drinks were okay and food was decent, this is a place you visit when you want to have a good time with some friends and chill.

Key Lime Pie was excellent! Great to bring back to your hotel room and finish off while watching TV. The live music tonight was great! They sang songs I new every lyric to! I didn't catch their names but they were a man and woman duo that both sang and both had guitars! As a musician I felt they were quite in time with each other and they seemed lively and into the people in the restaurant! There was also a woman on stilts making balloon hats for everyone! I have a latex allergy but it brought a smile to everyone's face! I've been to many Margaritavilles and this is one of my favorites!
We loved this bar!!  The bartenders and drinks were great.  The bands were amazing.  We had a lot of fun here!  We will definitely be back to Layla's!

when I visit Nashville,  I always eat here.  I love the beer, the food and the live singers.  I had a beer and a shrimp dish this time.  the shrimp was perfect, spicy but not too spicy.  I have had wings before and they were perfect.  the bartenders are always friendly and attentive to the customers.

I had never been to this venue until recently, and I am almost ashamed of myself for that.  Why haven't I been here before?!  This place is great!  Huge open loft-like space, great sound, great shows...I will be a repeat offender for sure now.
The shows here are relatively inexpensive and they have a wide variety of acts and performances.  They have two bars though the lines can get pretty long.  Unless I missed something its mostly street parking so factor that in when attending a show.  I'll be able to give a longer review after the next time I go, but I attended a Music City Burlesque show here (PS the MCB shows are fantastic and fun, I highly recommend them to one and all unless you're a seriously boring person lacking a sense of humor and are easily offended) and it was a riot.  There was some seating at this particular show, can't imagine that's the norm, but the sound was quality, the space large so you didn't feel like you were on top of everyone, and you get a pretty good view of the stage from any vantage point.  Probably some of the nicest restrooms at a musical venue ever too, as a plus.  But the lines for the bar were very long, and moved slowly, but the drinks were good and reasonably priced so I guess that kind of makes up for it.
I'll be checking out more shows here and will update this review when I do, but for now its safe to say that it's a great place to see great shows.

Great location! Located next to many fun bars and restaurants in a pretty tourist friendly part of town on Broadway. The drinks were good, but not great. However, the service was very good. We visited on a Wednesday evening and had drinks in the bar while we watched live music. The entire bar floor was being serviced by one server, who did a great job engaging with all of the guests and making sure everybody had what they needed. I can't seem to remember her name, but she was very nice. Definitely a fun place to spend your evening in Nashville!

We stopped in for lunch and were pleasantly surprised at how delicious the food was. We had the Nashville chicken sandwich and the bbq pork, both exceeded our expectations for being at a brewery! The beer was also great! Atmosphere was good as well. The only reason this is not a five star review is because our waiter did not check on us once after we got our food and we had to go up to ask for the check. However, it didn't ruin our experience.

This review is for the symphony.

 The Symphony offers a ticket package for young professionals and students at a severely discounted rate. The program is called Wave Length. Being under 30 we decided to participate and buy a complete package for the classical series, which set us back $150 per person. Seriously amazing price, y'all.  The discounted rate doesn't mean that we have bad seats either, we are sitting in the orchestra towards the middle.

The classical series has been excellent so far this year. The musicians are very good and the pieces have been well played. The concerts are on Friday and Saturday nights. If it's a more popular piece, there is a Thursday performance. 

We ended up getting tickets to Handel's Messiah because we enjoyed the shows so much. The guest conductor did a great job and the choir and musicians were amazing. I can't wait to see it again next year. 

People usually dress up for Symphony performances. I would categorize it as "Sunday Best". I usually wear a nice dress or skirt. There is always at least one girl in a full length formal dress. My husband wears a jacket and tie. The center is well heated so don't worry about being cold when you are seated. 

They sell drinks that can be taken into the show. They are a little expensive but that's expected. 

I wouldn't suggest valeting because it takes forever to get your car back.

5-star service, 5-star ambiance, 3-star beer.

This brewery tasting room is trendy and modern with dark exposed wood, two stories with views into the production brewery warehouse. Upstairs is a large bench seating area with games like Connect Four and others floating around. From here, you have a great view down into the production brewhouse. 

The beers here are all made in house with about 6-8 on tap at any given time. It looked like they had 4-5 core brand beers on tap, a couple of seasonals, and one very special beer. I tried just about all of them in a sampler flight. The core and seasonal beers were definitely in the 3-star level. None of them were bad, but few were good enough to finish. 

Core Beers: Their Southern Wit tasted soapy with some husky malt off-flavors. The Bluff City Pale, Cutaway IPA, and Extra Easy Ale were all astringent moving to anesthetic, medicinal bitterness (orange cough syrup). Their sweet potato stout, Country Roots, was very thin bodied with a schwarzbier flavor of black olive, prune, and smoked salt.

Seasonals: Their Walk the Lime was not bad at all, fairly watery and bland with small lime acid bite. Quite mild overall. The Nashweizen tasted like orange dial soap, was quite bitter for a hefeweizen, and ended with a slight chemical bite.

Specialty: They really redeemed themselves with the Wit Wine Cabernet BBL Aged, which I thought was going to be a sweet strong ale. Instead, this "wit wine" strong ale had soured in the barrel and picked up some really nice funky, buttery oak barrel. Flavors of oak vanillin, prickly acetic acid, and salty peach came together really well for this full-blown American sour blonde ale. Delicious!

Came here before PBR at Bridgestone and I had an awful experience.  I ordered a pasta dish that was way way way too spicy. It was obvious something had gone wrong while cooking the dish.  Atmosphere is fun as expected. I just wasn't lucky enough to have a decent experience with the food.

Started the 2018 St Patrick's Day Pub Crawl here... This place is awesome! Out of all the bars on the list, this one was THE BEST!! Great Music, Great Service!! We came back and enjoyed this place all night! Don't miss out next year!
Food sucks, service sucks, would not come back. Not a lot of choices food wise. Drink menu small.

I am actually a repeat customer to "The National".  I had a pretty decent experience the first time I went a while back (I'm a Nashville resident).  This time, though, was pretty terrible.  The service was o.k. (but for the fact that we had to have our ID's checked several differen times - I'm almost 37 and my girlfriend is almost 33 - it just started to feel like they didn't have their act together).  The burger was o.k., but slightly burnt.  What killed me, though, was the $13.00 Vodka Gimlet that came in a small plastic cup (we were sitting inside).  When I say small plastic cups, I mean those tiny clear cups they give you when you ask for water at a restaurant.  I did specify Ketel One, but the last time I paid that much for a drink was at the top floor at a skyscraper bar in Hong Kong.  They don't give you a menu, so you aren't even able to tell how much you'll be fleeced for before you order your food/drink.

THIS PLACE HAS BECOME A RIPOFF.  It went from a mid-top choice to a "never again."

The waiter was so rude it just ruined our entire experience. As three girls from NYC, we have a pretty high tolerance for rude but having just stepped off the plane, hungry and tired, we were hoping to be welcomed with a little southern hospitality. 

My one friend forgot her ID. After I and my friend showed our IDs, my friend, desperate for a beer, asked if she could show him a photo of her passport. He said no and I told him she was 25. He still refused (which is fine, I respect that), but what really pissed me off was he patronizingly said "yep, it's the law in the United States. You have to be 21 to drink." Thanks, asshole. I had no clue. 

He nickel and dimed us for everything. We ordered water and he came back with BOTTLED -- what?! My friend ordered a burger and he charged her for fries (who serves a burger with chips) and asked her what kind of cheese she wanted -- charged for that too. 

My friend and I split BBQ wings and a veggie burger. Both mediocre. 

Total tourist trap, rude rude waiter and mediocre food. Bye.
Go here if you want to experience Nashville. All the other bars like The Stage and Legends are full of tourists now and preppy little girls in cocktail dresses and boots.

A lot of great bands play here, don't get me wrong. I just don't want to pay $9 a beer to partake while I watch them. haha. Everything food or drink oriented is grossly overpriced. 

I saw the Black Keys here recently and had a fantastic time, it just wasn't quite the same as the Ryman or Cannery Ballroom. The view was so-so and it lacks in character and atmosphere. However, when I saw the Summerland Tour last year we had floor seats and it was so much nicer. If you can afford it, go as low as you can to the floor.

The service was fabulous the margaritas were wonderful. We had the volcano nachos it was large enough for at least four my only complaint was that the toppings weren't throughout the entire dish and it wasn't hot barely luke warm. I would order again

Bridgetown is the home of the Nashville predators as well as an excellent music venue for large acts.   Bring lots of money as the adult beverages are extremely pricey.   Most of the seating is excellent just avoid the top deck

Service was great! We had had a long day of birthday celebrations and exploring Nashville, so it was refreshing to sit down and enjoy ourselves. We had a huge table so service expectations weren't high but they were definitely met! Plus they had the balloon artist (who was also on stilts?!) make a birthday balloon hat for our 21 year old! The beer is surprisingly cheap too! Food was great and they were accommodating on my changes.
Great gluten free menu. The service was fabulous and the live music was awesome! Definitely recommend.

Great experience. Had some great local brews and a fantastic burger! Unique vibe, good music, definitely different from most bars on Broadway. The best places are normally hidden away holes in the wall, and this place attests to that! Will definitely be returning.

You go here because of the name, the atmosphere and the margaritas. The margaritas were surprisingly small. The food was in mostly extremely large portions! We ordered a club sandwich  that was large enough to feed at Least two people. I would recommend a piece of Keylime pie. It's ice cold, sweet and tart and delicious.
Really really small and crowded.  If you are here for the band, get to the front of the bar because you can't hear or see the band back at the bar.
What a gorgeous venue. I was incredibly impressed with the architecture and structure of the building. The food was excellent and the performance was fantastic. Definitely worth every penny!

Though it was a little pricey, our group had such a positive experience.  We walked in as a group of 18 without a reservation knowing we would likely have to split up.  After only a 25 minute wait (while we grabbed drinks at the bar) we were seated all together on the second floor.  The wait staff was quick and attentive.  There was another large party that sat near us and placed their order at a similar time, so there was some confusion with our food coming out.  A few of us had to wait a while, but everyone was so apologetic and even brought out 3 dessert platters for our entire table.  Great wait staff, friendly hostess, and accommodating management.  Get the fish tacos. We will be back!

Another fantastic Schermerhorn experience!  Registered for "SoundCheck" for students and got some incredible tickets for Mendelssohn's Elijah for $10 a piece.  Best kept secret in town!  For less than the price of a movie ticket I got to listen to over two beautiful hours of orchestral and choral music.  Absolutely incredible-go check them out!  Breaks my heart that there were any empty seats!
Best beer in Tennessee hands down. My girlfriend usually only enjoys bud light but when she came here she loved every beer that they had on tap.

I have a love/hate relationship with the Bridgestone arena. 

I LOVE going to see hockey games here, I hate seeing concerts here! I understand that there are some musical groups that require a large venue for their popularity and/or stage show, but it never sounds very good to hear a live performer at this venue! The only redemption for live shows at Bridgestone is if you have seats on the floor. I have found that that helps improve the quality of the sound and experience. 

The food is horrid, bordering inedible, but if you are desperate I'd stick to popcorn. I've somehow made the mistake of eating here twice with the same results. Gross. 

Parking is pretty nuts unless you want to walk a ways, and most of the garages fill up for big events so be mindful of that... traffic is the same deal. 

Overall, great for sports not for music! :)

We usually go to the restaurant in Myrtle Beach and  a few years ago had decided not to go back since the food and drinks were really not that good and certainly not worth the usual long wait. However, this is Nashville and it was lunchtime and we were hungry and there was no wait. Glad we went. We got seated right away and had some delicious Landshark on draft which is always a good start! My daughter had Coconut shrimp which was delicious. I ordered the Fish Tacos. Our server recommended upgrading to Mahi Mahi which I did- great choice!

Great service, good food and beer. I really liked the 1927 IPA and the Basil Ryeman...Sweet Potato Stout was OK (4 stars there). Had the hot chicken...it did not disappoint. Great start to our trip to Nashville...definitely worth a trip to the Gulch (great part of Nashville!!!)

One of the best arenas I've ever been to. The seats are always amazing. It's a breeze going through security. Great location, clean, and the bathrooms have cool sinks. The catfish tank was a lovely addition as well. They always offer a wide assortment of events, with affordable prices.
Ole Red's is great. Great music. Lot's os food selections. Lot's of drink selections. I had the smoked wings. Awesome!!! Wife had the biscuits and jam and fries pickles. Large food portions.

We have to give some allowance for this being a new establishment. However, the service was pretty bad. We waited awhile to find a seat-no problem. We finally got a seat at the bar. The bar tender was less than quick to help. After about 45 more minutes, our food came and it was wrong. They tried to correct it and it was wrong again. We ate anyway at that point because we couldn't wait any longer. The food was ok, nothing you can't get in any other restaurant. They've got some work to do to get their processes and service on track. The music was by far the best part.

I've been to this venue several times for different events and it was okay. The parking is very close, however for big events, the spaces definitely fill up quick and you have to walk a far way down the block. The employees are not the nicest.
Not a bad seat in the house! Easy parking. GO PREDS!

I was impressed by the Tennessee Brew Works.  They had ample space both inside and out, plus a second story.  There were a wide variety of beers.  All of them were good, but nothing to me really stood out as exemplary.  Our friends with us ordered the meat tray.  I thoroughly enjoyed the food and watching the brewing team in action from the tables on the second story.  This place gets's a solid thumbs up.
We had a great time at Layla's. It was so fun and the music was amazing. The band we heard was the best one we heard all night.
Great meal with the family! Our first stop on vacation. The Black and Bleu burger was phenomenal as well as the "It's 5 o'clock Somewhere" margarita. Live music was an added bonus.

BJ was a great server!!!   I had the nachos and they were absolutely delicious and I topped it off with a "perfect margarita" I will definatly be back great food but the service was the cherry on top!!!
Great atmosphere! Loved the rooftop bar! Rooftop menu was limited but the food was great! Will definitely go back!!

Layla's was hopping last night with The Eskimo Brothers on stage. They were super fantastic, talented musicians and really got the crowd involved. High energy, great music, and the most animated performers we saw during our trip. Super, super time!

Went there in May 2015 to see Nightwish, and I came back very impressed!

The venue is housed in a cool, industrial looking part of town. There are nearby shops. Very convenient is a coffee house down the street (Garage Coffee Company). You can chill there till 6pm when the coffee house closes-- WiFi, air conditioning, being away from overly zealous fans with no social skills. 

The inside of the venue is pretty clean. There are two bar sections on the side wall and back wall. Average music venue prices: $7 beer, $5 red bull. Disappointed there were no food options whatsoever, but I guess that's one way to keep it all clean. There's a good bit of natural lighting that comes in, so if your show is early in the day or in the summer time, except a brightly lit show. It doesn't have a dive bar feel. If anything it'd be closer to artsy/hipster. The stage is easy to see no matter where you are inside. The floor is flat, no gradient or raised levels. Sounds system was great. I could hear the vocals and insturments clearly, and I didn't have a ringing in my ear afterwards. 

Staff was never rude. I was surprised by the presence of a bathroom attendant. In fact, it may have been the best bathroom experience I've had at a concert venue. Definitely tip the guy. 

Outside, you can see the area where the bands load up pretty easily. Unfortunately, there's a metal gate, so it would be hard to meet the bands if you're into that kind of thing (I know I am).

This was the first stop for our group's one night in downtown Nashville. First impressions: three young bro-types immediately hit on one of our group's older women, two girls were dancing like no one was watching to the mediocre band, and it took several minutes for our large group to get the attention of one of the 3 chit chatting bartenders.

The band sucked, the energy was bad, so we ditched this place after one drink. MEH.

We had a great time - we went on the tour and also had a few beers. We tried the flight and then saw an employee drinking a half and half containing the Bucha and Walk the Lime. Beers on the flight were fine but nothing special. The mix was awesome though! 

We would suggest going here to hear some good music, play board games, have a cheese plate and hang out with friends.

I've seen several shows here and really enjoy the venue.  The layout and sound are good.  It's clean and has a good atmosphere.  There's parking nearby and I feel safe walking from my car to the door.

I highly recommend this place. Fun environment with openness.  We had some excellent smoked wings for appetizer, which had a very interesting ranch/blue cheese dip.  The Champagne of Chicken - Nashville Hot was some of the best chicken I've ever had.  It came with homemade biscuits and white gravy that was great!  Not blow you away hot like most Nashville Hot chicken places and a sweet and tangy flavor.  Tried their burger, catfish corn dogs, and desserts, all very good.  Service was a bit slow but it is everywhere at 2pm on Saturday downtown.  It was good food, good times and we will DEFINITELY be back soon!

The band was good, but it was my first visit to this venue and I did will-call for the tickets.  I will never do that again!  So disorganized that we missed the opening band waiting for the will-call tix to even be available.
Excellent outdoor seating, live music, great service. They are dog friendly! The beer was great, and the falafel was tasty!

I have eaten here at least 3 times in past year or so. I always get the same thing, their signature underground burger. Last night was no different. It was just ok. Not good. Not great like it was almost a year ago. Nickel and dimed for fries, cheese, water and get this, the table too! Beer wasn't good and is overpriced. To top it all off, they didn't let us go back inside to use the rest room after spending almost $100 bucks on dinner. Adios. Not more trips to this joint.

The only reason this place gets one star is because our waitress was great. The food, however, is terrible. My sister ordered their veggie burger, and after waiting well over 45 minutes, it came out cold. She sent it back, and 10 minutes later it came out rock heard. Literally, you would chip a tooth if you bit into it. Sent it back for a second time, meanwhile, the rest of the party still hadn't received their food! We waited an additional 15-20 minutes , and my "grilled" chicken was overly blackened and dry. They messed up 3 of the 4 side dishes (chips instead of fries). When you order ice water, you get bottled water that they charge $2 for without telling you. After all of the hassle, they did comp our bill $18, but it's not worth the long wait, terrible food, or expensive water. I will never come back and I wouldn't record this place to anyone looking for good food on Nashville.

Highly disappointed!  We decided to try Underground after a day out on Broadway.  We were enticed by the signs suggesting they had best burgers in Nashville, but quickly found out they were not.  We asked to order a cheeseburger, they responded with 'we don't have cheeseburgers, but we can give you a hamburger and add cheese?', so that is what we went with.  We added various toppings and a side of fries.  Our burger with the fries ended up being over $20, when it was advertised on the vague chalkboard menu as being $11.95.  Don'y let the packed bar and patio fool you! Never again!
Sorry Blake but your service sucks! Went to the roof top bar and couldn't even get waited on. Even asking for a server no one came over. Disappointed

This place is HUGE! I don't think there is a bad seat in the house. There are plenty of restrooms around the corner for each exit, which is not the case for other places. There are also many concessions to chose from out side of every exit. This place is conveniently located and very clean. There are several entrance/exits which is very nice. I was surprised at how cold they can make this place for the training we had, even though it is a hokey station, it just so big. Great place!

When visiting Nashville, I was told to visit this horrible establishment.  The burgers are about 1/10 the size of their picture and are covered in this disgusting sauce.   There are too many great places to eat to ever go here again.

The food was good but a bit expensive.  The margaritas were fun and plentiful! The best part was the music! I'm in love with all the live music in the area. It was a Monday night and the main road was still alive it music when we headed back to our hotel around midnight. I can't wait to come back to Nashville!

We only went to the bar here to listen to the live music. They had a couple of guys playing acoustic guitars -- they took requests and interacted a lot which made it fun. I got a strawberry blended margarita which was delish & we shared a slice a Key Lime Pie which was heavenly. The waitress was friendly and attentive. We had a great time here!
Hockey night and so a little slow. Service was just okay. The food was not worth the cost at all. Dry sandwich.

This was a rad arena. Came here to watch my LA Kings play. My team got shelled, but the crowd was amazing. They have a very passionate fan base. The food here, compared to back home in Southern Ca, was amazing! They need to bring the menu to staples center.

Let's start out about how excited I was to try Ole Red since I'm a huge Blake Shelton fan. His restaurant has to be as great as he is right? Unfortunately I was totally wrong, I've been twice & both times were very disappointing. Both times I sat upstairs on the rooftop & the service was HORRIBLE!!!! If your ok with waiting 30 mins before someone even acknowledges you and than another 30mins to get your food this is your place. Not to mention both times our waitress never checked on us and both times we had to flagged down someone else to bring our check. Don't waste your time.
Needed a place to hangout while waiting on another reservation, reminded me of why I hated bars in college. If people are belligerent at 8:15pm, something is wrong.

As other reviewers mentioned, the man that I am guessing is the manager  really does spend his time running around harassing customers and yelling at staff. At first we did not realize he worked there as he was wearing an oversized baseball hat, oversized graffiti T-shirt and chains (he looked like he stepped straight out of a rap music video) and when he was not picking fights with customers or staff he was lurking in a corner smoking behind the bar 

We were waiting in line for acme and saw this place didn't have a line or a cover so we decided to give it a try. We were a group of 4       professionals and their spouses and we spent quite a lot of money ordering drinks before we sat down in a corner of the bar to quietly mind our own business and listen to the music. The place is nothing special but our drinks were only watered down the normal about for broadway and the band was decent. 

Not 15 minutes into our visit this manager physically grabbed me by the arm as I was walking to the restroom and proceeded to yell at me, refusing to let go of my arm. Since he was dressed like a gangster rather than an employee and I couldn't hear what he was shouting I just broke free and ran away from him ... but he followed me back to my group and started physically assaulting other members of my group and yelling at them. It turns out that one of us had a small water bottle with them and he was trying to take it away because, as other reviewers mentioned, this place charges for water, even if you just spent a ton of money buying top shelf liquor. When he was done berating and assaulting us he grabbed the water bottle from the table and wandered outside with it. 

While we awkwardly finished our drinks we watched him yell at other customers and his bartenders. We left as quickly as possible and will never ever return. I hope someone sues him for assault.

I like catching shows at Marathon Music Works.  This is a very cool venue that shares an old car factory building with Lightening 100 and Corsair Distillery.  It's fairly trendy and even a sold-out show is comfortable to attend and it's easy to find parking.  We paid $5 for a lot, but you could easily park on the street a block or two away.

My wife and I saw Trampled by Turtles and Apache Relay there on Saturday.  It was an excellent show and Winston Marshall (Mumford and Sons) played banjo for a couple of songs (it's ok to be jealous)!  We also caught Yonder Mountain String Band there earlier this year.

This venue is standing only.  I'm probably getting old for this type of place, but you do have a lot of younger folks in attendance.  That also lends itself to a lot of stupid in the crowd.  The good news is that there isn't really a bad spot in the place.  If you get sick of fighting for a spot, then just retreat to a corner somewhere and enjoy the show.

There are two main bars in MMW and they have a surprisingly good beer selection with even a few craft choices mixed in.  I was a bit surprised by that.  With this being a small venue (it was sold out for TBT), the lines are short.  

This is an excellent venue to see a concert.  It's fairly intimate and everything about it is easy--parking, sight lines, and drinks.  You will stand for the entire show, but everything else is great.

Note I'm posting this before he end of Game 6. What a shame that the operators of the arena soooooo OVER-PRODUCE the artifcial sounds played during 100℅ of the breaks. 

Why not allow the fans the respect of non-led chants?? EVERY BREAK WE ARE SUBJECT TO A FAKE ASSAULT ON THE SENSES which belittles the fans and wrecks the game. 

Noise. "Music." Effects. Announcing. Hip hop. Organ. EVERY break. All too loud. Just ONE break with something more...normal, quiet, respectful would be appreciated. 

Whoever is in charge should know that this also wrecks the viewing experience for the TV crowd. 

Shut it down.

We stopped here one afternoon for lunch. The wait wasn't too bad and once we got seated the waitress came over as soon as we sat down. She took our drink orders and we each got a margarita. I asked for mine to be frozen. She brought us our waters and then took our orders. We waited and waited for our margaritas and they did not come. Our food came out and right after that our drinks finally came. We had waited 25 minutes for them. The waitress apologized and said that the bar was very busy. I agree the place was packed but people around us were all getting their drinks and we still had not gotten ours. And we didn't have anything "special" that should've taken that long. My drink was not frozen like I had asked. I asked our waitress about it and she said that the blender was down so they couldn't make it frozen. At this point I was just annoyed that it took 25 minutes to get it and then it was not even when I had ordered. We began to eat our food which was excellent!!! I had a taco salad (which I couldn't even finish it was so big and I can eat ALOT of food haha!!), my friend had fish tacos and she said they were great, and my husband had the seafood mac & cheese and  my sister had a burger that was very good. As we were eating the waitress brought over two different frozen margaritas that she thought I might like since I got a drink that I did not order. I was impressed that she did that. She left them there and just said for us to drink them all. We were very grateful that she did that. And the ones that she did bring were good! I cannot tell you the person who was playing music in there that afternoon but he was awesome! Very good at getting the crowd involved and the songs were great as well. All in all, besides waiting for drinks, it was a great experience!!

Pros: Great GF options, awesome server, friendly service, affordable prices, short wait on a busy weekend night. 

Cons: food was just mediocre.

The food was decent, when we did get it. The drinks were way overpriced for premixed drinks, but that's where they make their money, so I'm not focusing on that.

Our "waitress" was Brandy. She came to our table three times during our meal, had no personality, and forgot to order my second drink after she came and brought us our food. So I ate the whole meal without a drink. 

The food runner didn't know which table to bring our food to, and tried to give our food away twice. 

The food was ok. Fish tacos were OK, small and the fish was definitely frozen. The dipping sauce for the coconut shrimp was horrible, and should have never been paired with the shrimp. 

The only highlight of the evening was the fact I was able to catch up with a friend.
There are other places on the strip to go.. Skip it. The drinks are weak and basically all ice. Food is mediocre. The wait is long. Not worth it.

We are having a great time, good food, great drinks and best of all our waiter Jesse stevens. He is the best. Stop by and ask for him he will make sure you have a great time. Thank you Jesse Stevens!!!

I road tripped it up to Nashville from Atlanta to see Dweezil Zappa here on 1/21/2017, since I'm a huge fan of his tribute band and they put on an amazing show when I saw them in Atlanta about 2 months prior. I was a little concerned after I bought my ticket and saw the reviews of this place that said that the sound is not very good. 

I ended up being pleasantly surprised. If you read my other reviews then you will know that I am pretty picky about acoustics. I have to say though that I was not disappointed at all by the sound inside of Marathon Music Works. Sure, it isn't the prettiest venue in the world, as the inside of it looks and feels like (and might even be?) a warehouse. But I don't go to concerts for the attractiveness of the venues. I highly recommend Marathon Music Works to anyone who is an avid concertgoer.

We've been to Margaritaville in Vegas and were hesitant to stop in since there were so many other honky tonks. The main reason we stopped was to get a couple landsharks on tap. The dance area was very spacious and the music was good. The bartender was very quick to get our drinks refilled and always had a smile. Everyone seemed to be having a good time. Seems like the bar could be expanded or have a 2nd area for service I had to squeeze through a crowd for drinks.
Valerie was the most kind and fun server.  Very accommodating for our large high maintenance crew.  Great atmosphere and lots of fun!
Great beer, and had one of the best burgers ever. Get it with the egg on top. I'm drooling just thinking about it.

My wife andI were on vacation and we tried a lot of tap rooms.

I ordered an IPA,good stuff.

The bartender was cool. good times with my wife.

Great arena to watch a hockey game!   Most of the time it's easy to get in and out.  Almost all of the seats will provide a great view of the game.  The bathrooms are clean and the people working the service areas are friendly.

My wife and I stop here everytime we visit Nashville. The space is very cool and the beers are solid and well-priced. My wife's favorite is the Southern Wit, which is a nice take on a wheat beer. They also had 2 rye beers on tap, and ryes are a special favorite of mine. 

During our visit in June of 2014, we got to sit on the deck (there are two, and upper and lower) and enjoy the weather and the beer. There happened to be a music and food festival that day, and siting outside enjoying the weather and music was awesome. This is a very cool place, and we'll make sure we're back in the future.

Bland, bland, bland food, over priced also. Two Margaritas and one appetizer, almost 30 bucks. Margaritas were almost all ice. Quesadilla was tasteless and one tables spoon of sour cream, quac and salsa, when we asked for more salsa we finished the Quesadilla before the second table spoon of salsa was brought to us, would never go back and would not recommend to anyone. Ended up going to a local Mexican restaurant and had margaritas half the price, lots of food, bill was much cheaper and service was outstanding.

If Roberts is all jammed up and a$$es to elbows, this is a solid honky Tonkin second choice. Good prices on bottled beer (no draft) and they usually have some talented musicians on stage. Last time I was here, I was treated to a tap dancing man with a zz top beard in full overalls. But I can't promise he'll be there all the time. In fact, if I could, Layla's night edge out Roberts in my honky hierarchy.
Best bluegrass kickass music I experienced in Nashville, great environment, great crowd, highly recommended.

Great venue, absolutely love watching the predators here! My only real complaint is the lack of leg room in the upper section (300 level). Super annoying trying to keep your knees off the person in front of you. Love the concession options, there's literally something for everyone! However, the drink prices are extremely steep.

We went to Margaritaville Saturday night after the Predators game.  Our goal was a quick drink and bite to eat.  Unfortunately it took a long time to order, receive our drinks, then receive our food.  After what seemed a longer than average wait time we asked where our food was.  the server said it's coming soon.  The kicker was the table that sat well after us, got their food first.   Then when our food arrived and we asked for ketchup and mustard. It was "dropped" on our table. We weren't impressed at all.   I wouldn't go back.

Loved the vibe and the beer! Super neat space with refreshing craft beers. I had the Belgian wit which was nice and light. Perfect for summer! There was a large outdoor space both upper and lower patios. Looks like dogs were allowed outside - which I love! It is a bit off the beaten path so it took us a minute to find it but was totally worth it!

Hands down the worst meal we had in Nashville.

As a vegetarian, we had made reservations here so that I could try the BBQ mushroom sandwich. I was pretty pumped. There were only two of us with reservations for lunch. It was not packed at all and yet, every aspect of the meal was a mess.

First, we were seated by a window and there were these tiny gnat bugs flying everywhere which was kind of gross. The window was closed.

Second, we ordered the red and white sangria. They were not good- just straight wine with a few pieces of fruit in it. We swapped these out for margaritas which were much better, but definitely from a bottle. Our waitress left the sangria on the table. She didn't bother clearing them.

We ordered fried pickles as an appetizer to share, I ordered the BBQ mushroom sandwich and my mom ordered the hot chicken sandwich. Our pickles came fairly quickly and were ok. They were sliced thin and long so the breading kind of came off of them. I've never seen fried pickles like that. They were ok but messy.

45 minutes after we placed our order, we were starting to get restless as our waitresses hadn't given us an update and we had other things to do that day. Around this time, she informed us that they were out of the BBQ mushrooms. This was at about 1:15 now so early in the day! I was very disappointed and really annoyed it took that long to inform us. I decided not to order anything else as the cauliflower steak didn't seem appetizing and I can get a veggy burger anywhere. It took the waitress another 10 minutes to come back to check on my order and at that point, my mom just asked for hers to go. We waited another 15 minutes or so and now my mom is annoyed also. We had been there over an hour. 

The store manager did bring us the check at this point and made a fuss about waiving the BBQ sandwich and the Sangrias, the sandwich we never even got and the Sangria which we didn't even drink! um, thanks??

Trust me, you can find a much better restaurant in Nashville! Don't bother with this one!!
Good food but the server Karah was Great!  Always nice to have a server take care of you and she is super friendly!!!

The food was amazing here! I ordered the Caesar salad with hot chicken, and my husband had the Nashville hot chicken sandwich. Both were fabulous and we also loved the beers. This place is dog friendly with a great patio so had the pups with us. This was one of our favorite meals in Nashville. We will be back!

The new ownership has really nailed re-opening 12th n Porter.  the concert room is renovated and they have great acts performing there all the time now.  The drink selection is great, and the FOOD IS STELLAR!  One of my new favorite spots for lunch or dinner in town,  the Candy Fries are amazing and the menu us full of delicious items.  I won't be able to order the same thing every time like I usually do at my other favorite spots!  So glad this place is open again and killing it!

Industrial, fun, went for a concert and the sound wasn't amazing, but it wasn't terrible.

Cheap drinks, friendly staff.  A great experience.

First time I've been to a Margaritaville. My expectations weren't high because it's only rated 3.5 stars, but it was a Friday night and any place that was 4 stars or higher had a long wait. Wish we had waited! The staff was friendly, which was the best part aside from no wait at 7:00 on a Friday night - that alone should say something! The food was no better than what you would find in your local bar/pub, but it was priced about twice as high. My final bill with tip for 6 people, which only included one beer and one margarita, was close to $200. That was with no appetizer, either! I love Nashville and have been there a few times, but I won't be back to this, or any other Margaritaville. Sorry Jimmy... You all dropped the ball here!

Terrible Management (Angie)and services was horrible. After 2 hours, and at least 4 conversations with the server, the manager, and other staff, 2 people from our party, never got their food. The manager first told us they would take care of it, 15 minutes later, we asked again and we were told the order had just been put in. Fifteen minute after that, we were told that food takes time and it says that on their menu. Thirty minutes later, we still did not have Nachos and a burger we ordered, while the rest of our party had finished eating. The manager finally said she would take off the burger and nachos from our check, yes, the ones we never got. Then when the server brought us a check, it was the wrong check and when we tried to pay it she all but accused us of trying to pay someone else's check that was less than ours. When we did get the correct check, the burger and nachos were still on their as well as several other things we did not order. We spoke with the manager and she said she would take care of it and when we got another "corrected" check, it still had items on their that were not ours. In the end we wrote on the check and figured it out ourselves, because I don't think the staff would have ever got it correct. Throughout this whole situation, the manager kept saying "I am sorry you feel that way". It was never about how we felt, the hard fact is we did not get our food, the check was incorrect, and the entire time no one apologized for their mistakes. We won't be back.

There's 20+ bars here pick any other bar. After waiting 20 mins for service to order a drink I was told, "there's 3 of us and 700 of you" this place had maybe 50 customers. 

So bad it prompted me to write my first ever Yelp review
This place blows. No tap water. Ordered a sandwich, got a salad. Waitress had a weird demeanor. #1 burger in Nashville? #1 burger in nowhere!!!

Love this spot!! Some of the best bands I've heard in Nashville play here. Wide variety of drinks. The staff was kind and fun! More authentic/real than some of the other places in the area. Comfortable atmosphere and definitely a must-go next time I'm in Nashville!
Awesome double decker patio, great spot to share a drink on warmer nights. Excellent food as well!

Food was disappointing but the duo playing music was enjoyable.  We enjoyed the nachos and the onion rings.  The cheeseburger was reasonably good, middle of the road.  Fish sandwich came out under cooked and had to be sent back.  The pork in the Cuban sandwich had that old roasted pork taste which forced me to leave half the sandwich uneaten.  Personally I would not eat here again, but my wife is a Buffett fan...

I've never written a review before but felt compelled if not even obligated to write this one. STAY AWAY!!! We got here at opening before going to a Titan's game. Our group ordered breakfast which arrived incrementally if at all. As the food arrived we were told to hold on because there was no clean silverware. No Clean Silverware?!?! They just opened! Anyway, do yourself a favor and skip this spot...

It was semi-crowded. There was a wait for a table so we sat at the bar. We have 2 kids but it is a family friendly atmosphere which is one of the reasons we stopped in to listen to live music versus other places. The bathroom was disgusting but considering the location, I didn't expect too much. Our server was quick to serve us. Prices are reasonable for the area.

Can I say we had the best waiter ever - Chris. Very friendly, helpful and accommodating which hey I think is a rarity at most places anymore. Nice restaurant on Broadway. Very clean, open, and not too loud. If you're getting an appetizer go for the $16 nachos...they will not disappoint.
