Best time ever.  Enjoyed the band and the people. The afternoon bartender was from the Boston and very personable.  When we came back the second day he asked where my Blackhawks cap was, as he was a Bruins fan.  Really enjoyed the night bands   Good time I recommend.

I had a good experience at Margaritaville - Nashville. I didn't have high hopes for the food, but my jambalaya was quite good. The margaritas were a bit weak, but the service and entertainment made up for it. The atmosphere is ok and it seemed to be a decent place to bring the kids also. Margaritaville is worth a stop if you've never been to one, but probably not a place you want to go to over and over again.
Sat on the roof top and was awesome. Food was good but on the rooftop the menu is limited. Cool atmosphere and relaxing.

Music and margaritas were great - my cheddar BBQ burger was ok...nothing special. In fact, my homemade burgers taste better. The sweet potato fries also left room to be desired. Thankfully, the Fins to the Left and Tropical Waters were tasty. I probably won't be back though...

Lots of potential but the sound is absolute trash. I've seen Purity Ring and Chvrches here. I've also seen those two artists perform in other venues. They sounded completely different when playing here. To put it quaintly, they did not sound good. 

It's a cool space though. If they could just fix the acoustics then this place would be top notch. Until then, I'll always be extremely disappointed whenever I see a band I like is playing here.

This was my favorite of the breweries in the gulch area. This brewery had a lot of space to hang out inside, had an outdoor patio with plenty of seating as well. If you walk upstairs to the top floor they have plenty of fun games to play along with a separate bar to order drinks. Here I went with a wit they had on tap as my drink. For some tapas I went with wings, a cheese plate and frog legs! If your
Gonna be in town got to try frog legs at least once. The beer was fantastic and this is a great place to come hang out, watch the game and drink beer.

The Schermerhorn Symphony Center is just as beautiful as the music the Nashville Symphony plays. It's always a treat to attend something at the Schermerhorn. I'm honestly surprised that this building was built in 2006. The style makes to look like it's been here for a century, albeit, well kept. The the Neoclassical design with the large columns at the entrance makes it look very stately. Inside the theme continues & there's a grandeur to it all. 

The 1,844 seat Laura Turner concert hall is equally impressive. I really don't think there's a bad seat in the house. We saw Kristen Chenoweth a few weeks ago & sat on the upper, side balcony. We were able to see everything, including the symphony from above. The sound in that hall is amazing. I prefer the side balcony to the seats down on the floor because the seats aren't the theatre type seats & have more leg room. They've always got a bunch of volunteers helping to assist you in finding what floor/door you need to go to find your seat. 

My only issue, and it really isn't with the symphony, & that is parking. The valet at the Schermerhorn Symphony Center is $27. We've never done it because of the price but there's always a long line in front of the building. It almost seems like the just park all the cars in front, I'm not sure how they do it, but it always looks like a madhouse when people are arriving & leaving. We usually stick to finding a spot along Korean Veterans or park at the R lot at Nissan Stadium & walk over the pedestrian bridge.

After a hard day of working in the morning and a tedious 5 hour drive to Nashville, my friend and I were looking for a mellow place to drink and relax. Ole Red was that Safe haven in a sea of loud crowds. So thankful for the 5th floor and the amazing view that was provided . As an extra bonus, we got a GREAT cardio workout walking up all those flights of stairs. AND THEN BRITTANY OUR WAITRESS was outstanding!!! She was personable and treated us like we were her number one guests for the night. Thanks Brittany and Ole Red for this experience, much appreciated!
I really like the atmosphere We had a good time! Just planned on some drinks but ended up eating dinner. The buttermilk fried chicken was delicious. I would go back here.

I like Margaritaville, I like all of them, and I'm not a chain restaurant fan usually. But something about those baby blenders with a huge straw and a frozen strawberry margarita inside does something to me.

 I only order the fried pickles, which are a must. My friend and I started our day here at around 11:30 (him the fins out margarita in a blender, and me strawberry marg in a blender) and listening to music and drinking margaritas at the bar this past Sunday. Good spot to stop at, Jimmy Buffett does it right always.

 Don't forget to write on a dollar and stand on the bar to staple it on the wall!

Stopped by on a Wednesday evening after checking out the different entertainment for the evening. The Bluebird Cafe didn't look as promising tonight, but Margaritaville did.  Decor was neat. Very touristy feeling inside.  Wasn't too crowded. I had the shrimp wedge Louis. It was HUGE! But it tasted great! Nice and fresh veggies and the shrimp was not grilled to death. Server was fantastic.  Entertainment was good, but I prefer their own music to their covers. Definitely recommend.
Blake knows food! The Redneck Nachos and Chicken Champagne bucket were amazing.  More than enough to feed 3 adults and a preteen. They also had great live music. Amazing experience!

We enjoyed the patio the weather was so beautiful so we wanted to be outside. We went on a Tuesday night and the band was pretty good. The beers were pretty cold and the bartender seemed burned out, but overall it was ok.

This review is based off of their camera policy. Brought a DSLR with a fisheye lens and 16-35 zoom and they gave me grief about not being able to have lenses that were disconnected from the body. This is a bs rule. Limit the zoom. Not the amount.

Yes, had an absolute ball. Friday night - first act was very good, place was half full and comfortable. We sat up top and watched the action below. Second act was fabulous, and the crowds grew but not to the point of being crazy. So happy to be able to hear that level of talent in a relaxed and fun environment. Why run around the street when you can settle in, have a few drinks, and get to know the place while the music gets better and better?
What could be bad?? Its all good!! Especially when you make it on the jumbo tron!!

We walked in not knowing what to expect and loved it! Servers were very friendly, helpful and efficient. The food was great (try the Island Rice!). Drinks were dangerously good. The live music was entertaining and not at all overbearing. The piano stairs was an added bonus!! Check it out if you're in the area.
Loved this place, must try the tranquil waters drink and nachos if you're there.  The entertainment was great and a fun time was had by all.

The only joint on a sunday morning that had breakfast on the way to the game. Sat down outside at a table that was stacked against the wall and fell over when we sat down.....because it was being held up by the wall!!! felt bad for the poor waitress who was frazzled but my lord, this place was a dump. Food was horrible, drinks took forever to get and weren't even cold. It was 11 am and we were told that was the last "cold" bud light they had. AHHH, whaaaaat?? It was sunday, football game was in town, and that's the last cold bud you had? To top it off it was really expensive. The bartender was rude, asked to pay my bill so we could get going and she just blew me off. Sorry Nashville, I loved every place, BUT here!

I've got to admit that moving to Nashville has made me into a little bit of a beer snob.  I have always been a fan of trying local craft beers whilst traveling around the country.  However,  I find myself staring at a craft beer menu and making my selections on where to dine based on what time of craft beers they offer more and more often these days.  Nashville's local craft beer scene is on the rise as the city grows.  Microbrews continue to pop up all over the city with their own unique flavors and styles.  Tennessee Brew Works is one of Nashville's breweries that is certainly doing some right things!  They have an awesome Taproom at their brewery with TVs to watch the games, darts, and a great outdoor patio area.  If you go to the Tap Room on Saturday's be sure to see Haley at the bar, she's the best!  They typically have food trucks outside the tap room to give you some food options, and I've heard some rumbling that they may be opening their own kitchen.  I went on their brew tour and their equipment and processes seem to be state of the art compared to the other brewers in town.  Their brew master was extremely knowledge and passionate about her product.  They offer 5 different types of beer year round and have multiple secession (seasonal) and barrel aged drafts on tap as well.  My favorite beers by Tennessee Brew Works has to be the Souther Witt with the Basil Ryeman being a close 2nd.  I'd recommend the tap room and tour to visitors of Nashville, beer fanatics, or anyone looking for a chill place to enjoy super fresh and delicious beer in a unique atmosphere.

My friend wanted a plate of volcano nachos very badly.  Met up with him here.  Live music was very nice as was the food.   Big detractor was the speed of service.  It was a Saturday and it was busy but we were there for over 2 hours. Waited at least an hour for our check after we finished meal. Had to flag the wait staff down to pay our checks so we could leave.

Thank  you Bridgestone Arena and Nashville Predators for the most wonderful weekend I've had in my many years.  Although I did not participate in the hockey experience because we were in Nashville to celebrate my twin daughters birthdays (yikes they were 50) and chose your city in which to celebrate we were overwhelmed and surprised by the fantastic event put on there for the NHL All Star Event.  From the music to the marshmallows the event was well organized and families all around seemed to be having a wonderful time.Whoever was responsible for the venue should be commended.  My only disappointment was that I only saw 2 Sabres fans that entire weekend (but of course I was not inside). Go Predators and as one gentleman told me Go Sabres - he explained to me they are a young and upcoming team and will soon be a force to reckon with.  Dare I hope?
Drinks were good. Appetizers were tasty, especially the Lava Lava shrimp. Services wasn't that great.
Just amazing! Atmosphere, service and food top notch. Great band playing and people having fun as far as the eyes can see!

Not impressed. Bartender wasn't friendly and when we asked for water, we were given bottles. Didn't think we'd be charged - just that that's what they do. Nope, $2 each. Are you kidding? 
Menu is only a chalk board - so if one of the pillars or a person is blocking it, good luck...
Go elsewhere - plenty of better spots on the strip.
Large modern facility. Games are great, parking and traffic can be a pain, as expected in Nashville

Finding this place on foot was a little bit of an adventure, but once I got there--what a treat! I live in Seattle (the home of a few good beers), and I thought that TBW's beers were goood!! Also, I've been dreaming about the sweet potato fries poutine with chicken jus, white cheddar and egg. That might have been one of the best "snacks" I've ever had!! I ate most of it and ruined my subsequent dinner at Pinewood Social with absolutely no regrets! Basil Ryeman, Natchez and Rye IPA were only a few of the delights in my flight!

Cavernous. I mean compared to many other venues, this place is WIDE OPEN. Lots of space can be good and can be odd. Lots of space means room for two bars, two sets of bathrooms, space to sit, space to stand, space for open shirt guys to run around on drugs doing some kind of traditional Russian folk dance on the floor without running the risk of kicking someone in the head. Anyway, I liked the venue for the most part because of the space and I did like the acoustics. Also looking at their line up since opening, they've managed to book all sorts of different genres and variously famous people here. 

Parking: When we turned off Jo Johnston Ave on to what I guess was 14th street, heading perpendicular to the venue we were stopped and asked to pay for parking. I had just been to Marathon Village earlier in the day and was hoping to find street parking as I had then. Basically I felt forced to pay this guy $5 to guide to parking in the nearby nearby funeral home lot. Well maybe someone will be watching the lot while we're inside, I thought to myself - of course when we came out at 11:30 no one was there. I couldn't help but feel we were partially scammed. If we had come towards the venue form any other direction we wouldn't have been asked to pay for parking and would have probably found a street spot, especially because we got there so early. I'm not sure if Marathon is aware of this guy or if he's just doing his own thing but it's slightly shady in my opinion. 

Bathroom valets: WTF. I don't get this at ALL...I once went to an Aquabats concert at The Music Box (now closed) in LA and they had Valets in there. Let me explain to you that the Aquabats plays to teens mostly and they had someone in the bathroom expecting tips from teenagers for handing them paper towels and squirting soap in their hands. It's a music show for TEENS wtf...not the damn Oscars. No wonder the place is closed! So when I went to the bathroom at Marathon and found out there was someone in there selling Scope and handling the soap I was shocked all over again. WTF I would rather you employ these people in a real job like bartending then have to feel awkward and forced to give someone $1 for handing me a paper towel I could have gotten myself. I do not get it at all, at ALL, someone explain.

Would I go back to Marathon for a show? Absolutely. Next time I won't pee and I'll take Lyft.

One star is one too many but the long and short of it is that the staff was unfriendly and rude from the get-go and seemed completely annoyed with having to breathe, let alone take our drink order. Not just one, but all of the 5 or 6 bartender girls we encountered were equally cold and lame. Miserable people all around. Forget this place.
Great food and service and a band that plays every song you want to hear acoustic with no breaks! Beautiful building too! Nicely done Blake!
Bridgestone Arena is a great place to see a game or a concert. Easy to get in and out of with a food food selection.

I've never had a worse experience at a restaurant/bar.  We sat for at least half an hour before we finally walked to the bar to get some water.  After we returned to the table, we sat for another while before chasing down a server and requesting someone visit our table.  Owner, Rick, approached our table a little while later telling us that he was going to need our table.  We explained that we would LIKE to order food and drinks, but no one would serve us.  He was hateful and walked off as he was on his phone.  We chased down another server and asked again for menus and a chance to place an order.  It was about ten minutes before she made it to our table.  She didn't ask for drink orders, but she did take our food order.  We had to continue to visit the bar for water and drinks, which were forgotten and never arrived most of the time.  Rick brought our baskets of food out to us.  It was incorrect.  He was hateful as usual, put the food down, and walked away.  Our server came over and explained what happened.  Shortly after, while visiting the restroom (our untouched food, drinks, phones, etc were still on the table), our table was bussed and cleaned.  After this, we were missing food and a cell phone.  The servers were less than interested to help, but, after insisting on a tab, had no problem charging us for the food and drinks.  Did I mention that "our" server had since clocked out and was outside counting her tips?  Never found the cell phone... I asked three different servers to look for it, but they were not interested in helping.  WORST EXPERIENCE EVER!!! It's surreal to even think about things like this happening.  And, the fact that an owner is so hateful and rude is awful.  Why is this place still open?????

Enjoying Broadway like the rest of Nashville, my best friend and I didn't really want to go to a chain-type establishment.  But we noticed two seats at the Margaritaville bar available and the entertainment for the evening sounded better than most.  So we were going to grab a drink and leave.  The bartenders were so awesome though.  We stayed there all night!  I highly recommend going there and sitting at the bar...let them pick a couple of shots for you.  These were our favorites!!!

Got recommended to us by a local. Great location but didn't put much effort into making it a memorable experience for it's guests. The burger was...good, the beer was...good, the service was...just ok. Didn't hate it, didn't love it. If I was walking by, I might stop in for a quick bite but with all the great choices in downtown Nashville...I'll probably look elsewhere next time we are in town.

Um. The doorman lets me in. I head to the restroom. He grabs me and stops me 1 step from the door to tell me I have to buy things. I don't know if he wanted a credit check, but there's literally 20 Bars I could've stopped in. Meanwhile probably 10 people underage snuck in. This inspired me to drink one beer, average busy bar service nothing more, no personality. And leave. Disappointed.... Was getting my $7 one time ever more important than no extra flushes?
Delicious beer. Super friendly brewers. Great service. Good music. Food looks bomb too.

Zero stars. You get kicked out by the owner for dancing. If you're I the pedal tavern or sprocket AVOID!!!! No fun, lame entertainment, and the OWNER SUCKS!!!!!! We took 12 people in there during our sprocket rocket bar stop and the OWNER told us to stop dancing because the old people were getting upset. Acme is next door, go there.

Should've read the reviews!! Everything others say is true. From the mediocre food to the rude service. Seriously....$2 water and up charge for fries when it's already almost $12. BTW-Not "The Best Burger" despite what they write on their chalk board. And while we were there, we watched "management" physically confront and block the way for people that wanted to use the bathroom...even questioning PAYING CUSTOMERS!! What a HORRIBLE place. There a TON of other options downtown...even on either side (Acme/Rock Bottom) and across the street (Hard Rock) of this atrocity...go with those restaurants or ANY other nearby for a better experience.
Food was way too expensive. Wait staff was rude and Didn't know the menu. Cool vibe, but missed opportunity.

The food here was bad. The service was not good. The music playing upstairs on a Saturday night was not good. The musicians missed chords and lyrics on several songs. The charm of Jimmy Buffet doesn't outweigh the bad food. However, tourists will continue to go and the chain will continue to thrive.

We were here on a tour.  They knew we were coming, they only offered us three choices on the menu, and, yet, it took them over an hour to get food on the table.  Granted, the food was pretty good, but the service was pathetically slow.  i would cut them more slack if we had just wandered in, and were ordering off the regular menu, but that was not the case.  They really dropped the ball on this one. 

The only reason they got three stars was because the veggie burger we ordered was pretty darn good.  Both the roll, and the patty itself had good flavor and texture, and you don't always find that in a veggie burger.  The fries were tasty, too.  

I like the food, but they could have done a whole lot better job with the service.

First time visit to Nashville. We flew our daughter in from college and we flew in from San Diego on the day before our daughter's 21st birthday.

Since our daughter wasn't 21 till midnight, we ended up at Margaritaville. They serve food and have a bar so they allowed her to stay inside as we ate a late dinner.

Our server was Katheryn. She was fantastic. She checked our daughter's ID before midnight and promptly served her drink of choice at midnight. Band also brought her up for a song. 

Food was great. Drinks were great. Great venue. Definitely stop in!

After reading many reviews on this spot the fellaz and I decided to check it out!

Pro's: Location is very easy to find and literally located on 12th & Porter. Parking is free, located adjacent in a gravel parking lot, or you can park on the sides like a lot of people did. Not a very big lot so i recommend if you have a show to see at 8pm etc. i suggest being there at least an 30 to 45mins early to secure a spot. Upon walking in to 12th & Porter you see a bar like setup where people are ordering food & drink. To the right you will see table and chair setups. To your left there is a check in boot where a guy/girl takes your ticket for whatever event you came to see or if you. Immediately to their right is the entrance door to the club/dance floor/ where the stage is where the band will perform. On this particular night DJ Joseph(i think was his name) was on stage RIPPING IT! I've seen a lot of DJ in my time but this by far was the coldest white DJ i have ever seen!! Dude mixed up every great hit song old and new and you could tell EVERYONE in there couldn't help but to fight the urge to dance! BOI WAS BADD!!! Ok now back to setup....

Now upon walking in to the staging area to your right is a bar where bud light cost 5$...not bad. There is an upstairs sitting area that has stools and one table but i warn you ITS SMALL AND HOLDS ABOUT MAYBE 10 PEOPLE MAX! Not everyone up there gets to sit down on a stool cause there's only about 5 of them if that...recommend if you want to sit GET THERE PLENTY EARLY!!  Below is the standing room only...I repeat STANDING ROOM ONLY!!  so if the artist you are there to see are normally late for shows be prepared to stand for a while and get yourself a drink to by the time AND I RECOMMEND wearing some shoes with cushion for long periods of standing....I made the mistake of wearing some nice dress boots but by the end of the night my feet were DONE SON! Could barely walk back to my car!

The stage for the performers was a nice size and the sound as well as the lighting effects where top notch! Its defiantly a place where real musicians should perform at in my opinion. Bathrooms are small but very clean at least the guys were, and the crowd was a mixture of all races just enjoying the music.

Con's: It was very hot in there!!! I was lucky to find a spot close to the wall where air would eventually hit me from time to time but for the most part i was sweating as was everyone else in there. Like i said the best thing to do is get a drink and sip on that badd boy to keep cool because once it gets packed getting back to the bar is a adventure!  That is my only complaint...:(

Will defiantly return! :)

As a pop series season ticket holder I had been to see the Nashville Symphony more times then I can count, but almost every concert exceeded my expectations.  The talent of these individuals and their abilities are tremendous and always a pleasure to watch and, of course, hear. The new building is so beautiful, I always enjoy that aspect of the experience. In my opinion there is little to be desired, from the doors to the floors you can tell everything has been pondered over. I look forward to more nights spent with a glass of wine in the company of such fine talent.

Been here two times so far.  The atmosphere​​ is fun, of course,​ it is always​ great to hear live music.  You can make reservations online, which I recommend​.  One of our visits was around 4 and it was already hopping. Both times that we have been here the service was very slow.  Not really a big deal when you are enjoying the music, you don't feel rushed, but our drinks were often empty.  The fried pickles were amazing, a very​ large portion, plenty to share with a group.  We ordered the bucket of chicken to share.  A whole​ bird came with two biscuits and a very small container of dried up gravy.  It was just OK. We will probably go back with out of town guests b/c of the novelty of being Blake's place.  I was really hoping this could be a go-to spot for us, but we will probably pick a different spot next time
Worst Moscow mule ever. The "ginger beer" tasted like flat 7-Up. The server just gave us more lime juice to make it "better". Try again...

What an amazing Father's Day experience I had at this place. First off it was my 2 children 7/9 my wife and myself, the environment was totally kid friendly and even had board games for them to play. So we get there and Zach the manager (which we didn't know at the time he was the manager) takes care of us personally, we order a cheese plate and a flight of beers, he and his coworker did a great job describing the characteristics of all the beers to us. Time to order food, the kids menu is rather small so Zach personally made my youngest chicken tenders. All in all the bill was nothing compared to the service and food we got, and they give a military discount!!! We will be bringing many people here soon!!! I highly recommend and it's close to the farmers market so so that's where we usually come from.

Our band played a set, they sold tons of beer, then handed us a bill for $44 of burgers we ate that we thought were free. By the way, don't let them fool you, the burgers here suck.  The manager here is a jerk. We came through here and they ripped us off.

I was visiting my friends who recently moved to Nashville (see Ashly M's review). On one of their trips down from Buffalo to drive their belongings down in the early fall, they called me and told me to look at their website as she was going to bring me a growler of beer of my choice on their drive back! It made it is one piece (was a close one there!), was very tasty, and now I have a cool growler to use around Buffalo.

We came when I was visiting for their Valentine's weekend Beer + Chocolate pairing event. Unfortunately, it started on a bit of a sour note as when we got there on Sunday, we wanted to order some food to go with our beer and were told they were out of food. 

Apparently the event was super popular on Saturday to the point that they were cleared out of food altogether on Sunday. We had "liked" the event on facebook, plus my friend "liked" TBW's facebook page and their was no posting as such. It would have been super easy to post something to let people know and we would have been notified. We would have still come, but maybe stopped for something light for lunch. Some people may not be able to make it through a flight with some food in their stomach. I saw later in the day they re-posted their menu, so I don't know if things changed or what. I just think in this day and age of internet connectivity that there is no excuse for a quick update. Also, the husband of my couple-friends was our DD, and since they don't even carry pop, he was out of luck for having anything besides a bite or two of chocolate.

In regards to the beer, I did enjoy it all a lot which is why I am rounding up to 4 stars. Good variety of different things and maybe only one I probably would have passed on having a 2nd round of. I was impressed that they kept the consistency of quality from light to darker types. I thought the chocolate was decent, too. Just was heavy on dark chocolate which is not my #1 fav. Was a little pricey due to the holiday I am guessing as well. I still wanted some of that grilled cheese I had been promised though :-(

I did like the industrial feel and the view of the brewery which added to my rating. It was a really nice vibe. We got there early in the day, and it was just filling up as we were leaving, so I am not sure how loud somewhere like this would get. It was nice they had restrooms on both levels. Some may be drawn back from the communal tables that take up a lot of the upper area, but hopefully next time I am there it will be patio weather (and food).

Went here for the Zelda Concert. In a lot of ways this place is better than Jones Hall in Houston. However, the seats can be quite uncomfortable at times. That being said, the acoustics are superb and the concert was amazing. Now I just need an excuse to return for another performance.
Kim and Brittany were great!  They got us a table for our friends!!  They really went out if their way!!

This is the best for Bach parties!! Our server Shane was absolutely wonderful!! He got out drunk super fast, he was very attentive. There was a lot of people and we were still super pleased with our experience! Next time we come back we will be asking for Shane specifically!! Thank you!!

I am so glad they added a kitchen. We have several tap rooms in the area that don't serve food, or if they do, it's pretty limited. I had the fries with a hot chicken sandwich (be sure to tell them if you want it local hot). Both were great. They also have a mean burger, and I hear the frog legs are good. And all of the recipes include their beer in the recipes. The beers are always a nice selection of session styles, and with the new laws, maybe a few high gravity offerings. If you want to eat AND get well made local beer, this is a must try. There are a few other breweries nearby if you want to do a mini crawl, but check the hours.

A friend and I went to the St. Jude Rock n Roll marathon concert. The performers were fantastic but the staff not so much. It was very unorganized. We were front row middle behind the pit and a security guard came up to us and screamed at us to sit down because the people behind us couldn't see and told us it was "common courtesy". I was unaware that you had to sit at country music concerts. We paid for our ticket like everyone else. However once we sat down the security guards stood in front of us so we couldn't see, it was very rude and disrespectful. Next time I come to Nashville I refuse to step foot inside that place. The staff needs continuing education on customer service.

We flew up from TX to see Styx play with the Nashville Symphony in concert. The weather dropped below freezing this morning and there was light freezing rain and snow most of the day. Travel conditions were lightly impacted. We learned about 2 hours before the show that the Symphony canceled their performance but Styx is still doing their part of show. The venue did offer to exchange our $150 per person tickets for another event between now and July. This is not too attractive to us because of the airfare and hotel costs.

Styx was awesome. They dropped Madam Blue from their regular set which we believe they would have done had the Symphony been there.

We are disappointed and feel like the Symphony are being fair weather friends in this event. Two stars for that.

I've always felt bad for this place while waiting in the around-the-block line for Acme. Never again will I think twice about "maybe we should just go in there". 

First of all, the menu is on a big chalk board in the front - which is no big deal except no one told us and we waited around thinking menus were going to be brought to us. When our server finally came back to take our orders, we were like "wait - where's the menu?" 

Secondly, I asked for water along with my Jack and Ginger and she brought me a water bottle with no label??? I asked if I could have a cup of water and she said "I will get in trouble if I do that". Hahaha what? By the guy in the puffy sliver space jacket out front? 

Lastly, they didn't split the check (I understand a lot of places don't split checks) but it's just inconvenient. I also thought the place was much bigger but it's just that one small room. 

Don't go here guys! Wait in line for Acme.

I've been to two events at MMW in the past few months and I think it's a great venue.  Great acoustics and great layout for whatever your needs are (stage, multiple bars, multiple bathrooms, outdoor area in the back).  Plenty of parking nearby.  I don't love the outdoor area - I always feel like it could be so much better, but then I remember that they frequently have food trucks and the like out there, so they can't really do much with it.  (and people smoke outside, I wish they didn't, but for you, maybe that's a good thing).  Also, if you're trying to be outside, that freight train can get pretty loud (but you can't even hear it from inside).  Bathrooms are much nicer than one would expect at a venue like this.

Haven't been to a regular concert here, but when I do, I'm sure I'll update!
The band last night was great. I think they have a great band all the time. Come on in and grab a seat. Lots of good drinks and music

We went here basically only because of the beautiful weather and the fact their bar and open seating area was by wide open windows and a good band. So in regards to atmosphere it was a 5, and the margaritas were good. 

Other than that, it was way too overpriced (which was expected) for the quality of food.

I got the fish tacos, $17, and the amount of fish on the two tacos you got was less then I would have wanted on one taco. I know Broadway is gonna be overpriced but at least I was a decent amount for what I'm paying.

In other words, it was fine I guess if your expect mediocre overpriced food, which I was. So fine go there only if you can get a good bar or open seat spot with a good band playing on a warm day, other than that go somewhere else.

We came in on a Saturday night and even though it was ridiculously crowded, the section we sat in wasn't very loud.  Mary was our server and she was very attentive and made some great recommendations.  The prices are pretty reasonable and the serving sizes were pretty large, I took half of my hamburger home!

I would say I received bad service, but I actually received no service. The burgers are ok, but not nearly worth the price. Past Perfect is a block away and serves much better food for the same money.
We had a short wait, the food was amazing and the music good. I would recommend it as a great place to eat in Nashville.
Amazing margaritas, food, live performances, and service. Definitely a must if in Nashville.

By far the best burger I have ever had. Five beer burger add the bacon of course! The seasoned fries paired with the basil ryeman ketchup is the pair. Not to mention the view and the beers. This place is a must!
Awful. There's a waiter pretending to be the manager .  Needs to be more specific about what is and is not on the menu.

Ole Red was on our bucket list for Nashville and did not disappoint.  Got there when it opened and found wonderful entertainment with Steel Magnolias. Topped it off with poutine, something I'd never had before and found delicious - and a great cocktail.  People were super friendly and service excellent! Hope I can return tomorrow!
Great new place. Very attentive wait staff. Huge portions. Great smoked pork. Lots of room with an open airy feel.

We went there before a concert. The atmosphere was wonderful. Great music, great decorating, and excellent music. The food was good as well. However, we ordered cheese curds, and a burger with a salad instead of fries. We got our curds quickly. However, the burger took over 30 mins to come out and they gave us fries instead of our salad. Had such high hopes. Just fell a bit short.

Went for dinner at Music City Pizza and had some delicious pizza. We had no idea that we were walking right into such a great music venue! We had the absolute honor of  sitting just a few feet away while listening to Jane Ellen Bryant play - keep an eye out for her! She has such soul and grit that shines through in her enchanting and mesmerizing music.  A great gem of a music venue for some intimate music!

Fun atmosphere and very friendly service, but I wasn't too impressed with the food. There are no vegetarian options on the menu when I went, but the server allowed me to make meatless tacos, which were pretty bland.  My mom enjoyed the crab dip. They might have better options, but I would definitely recommend vegetarians go elsewhere.

It's basically what you would expect. Expensive and gimmicky. The band area was too crowded to see anything and the drinks were weak and not worth the cost. You can go for the picture and to say you had a margarita at margaritaville but I don't recommend hanging around.

Great atmosphere with open air windows out to Broadway. Little stage with live music like nearly everywhere in Nashville. Club sandwich was tasty and the sweet potato fries were excellent! Ate at the bar with awesome service from Eric B. Drinks are a bit pricey but guess that is to be expected in a tourist area. Had a small mishap when I noticed lipstick on my glass of Shocktop. Eric was very apologetic and made it right by a new beer on the house.

I've been to most if not yet all live music venues in Nashville and though some have perks that surpass Marathon and are better suited for specific needs, Marathon may be my overall favorite venue all things considered in the Nashville area. It's basically an old converted warehouse so it's just a huge open floor area but for a rock show it's the best option as long as you stake out the spot you want to be in. However, I have found depending on the show and the audience you often can leave for drinks or a bathroom run and still navigate your way back to your approximate spot. I will say that if it's a sold out show particularly if its an energetic band it can get tight, full and sweaty!
Drink prices are fair. There's very little actual food or drink (other than coffee) within walking distance of this place though so it's not the best venue to eat or pregame prior to a show and though it probably isn't directly associated with the venue there is a huge parking area directly across the street that is directed in and out for only $5 which makes this the easiest venue to catch a show at in the area regardless of what night of the week it is. 
So, 3rd & Lindsey is better for a smaller audience if you want a meal and a relaxed experience, Exit/In and the End may get a little messier and active and the Ryman might be secular church but for just convenience and steady quality of acts Marathon gets the slight edge.
Nice relaxing place. Clean crisp tasting beer. Good variety. IPAs are really good. Truly a great beer joint.

Current (and standing for a year or so) favorite brewery in Nashville. The beers are all next level. All of the flavors are pronounced and they're mostly full bodied. I'm especially enjoying the barrel aged selection lately. 

I've enjoyed a few nibbles from the menu-- frog legs, cheese board, and the bacon wrapped dates. All great! I recommend the dates, but know that it comes with 5, which is an odd choice seeing as most people are going to split them. Even numbers people!

The staff has always been super friendly and helpful in a very genuine way. Lately I've noticed a lot of new faces that perhaps don't have the service experience as the seasoned vets. Hopefully they won't be green for long though.
Excellent Food! Best burger I've had in a long time. Live music was awesome. A duo named Brittany and Matt played, they were awesome. Staff was very friendly and attentive. Good value for the money.
We Loved this place. Nice staff, great food and dog friendly patio. Get the Mac and cheese, and the hot chicken sando, Nashville Gem!

We had a great time at National Underground.  The music was good and not too loud.  We sat at the bar and we served right away.  We enjoyed it so much we came back the next day for brunch.  My wife had biscuits and gravy and I had the hamburger.  Both we very good.  We will go back when we are in Nashville.

The chips for the spinach dip were stale (defiantly came out of a bag).The crab cakes were dry and full of filler, I couldn't eat them, I sent them back. The server was nice, but disappeared for 20 mins while we were waiting for our food.

The bartenders were nice but the guy by the restrooms and ice cooler, who i was told was the manager, began yelling at me, threatened to kick me out and called me a "prick" for standing next to their ice cooler even after i respected his request not to touch the ice cooler. 

I have never experienced such awful treatment by an establishment's "management" in my life. I was with a group of 12 people who were all respective and not causing any issues. I would not return to a place where this type of unwarranted hostility and verbal abuse was acceptable...ever. If I could give them negative stars I would.

Looking at other reviews it appears that many other patrons have had similar experiences here which is extremely sad and unfortunate.

Went here on karaoke night. Laid back fun atmosphere with dance floor and bar in the back! Some of the people that sang were amazing! Honestly! Not as tourists and more of a local hang out which was nice to experience! They also have a patio area. Everyone was so friendly here we met so many people! A much younger crowd and age appropriate for our group compared to Broadway- but Broadway is a must and you will still have fun! This is a place you have to visit when in Nashville!

I come here pretty often to watch the Predator games. The arena is always clean and the food vendors they have are pretty good! The staff here is amazing. Everyone is so kind and willing to go out of their way for you. Even the employees that get swarmed with people at the main doors that operate the ticket scanners and metal detectors, are just so nice and friendly. Love coming here!
Very new place to having good time!   Good for Drinks&Food and Music and Music and Music!

We stopped in Ole Red 2 days in a row. Love Blake! 
So the 1st day we sat on 2nd floor. We waited for a server and finally after 10 minutes we asked for a server. 
Took about 20  minutes to get a drink. When my husband got a beer they didn't pop the lid. He took it off with his teeth... lol..... couldn't find the server.
Very slow service. 
Day 2, we went with a few others,  again sat up the top, waited and waited and finally asked a couple of people (not one) to be served. We had been sitting 15 minutes already.
Finally drink order was taken and still 20 minutes wait on the drink. After our drinks we asked for the bill. 20 minutes later we were asking again for the bill and our waitress comes out from the back and she has forgotten that we had asked for it. We wanted separate bills as requested and she came back with 1. It's not that they were really busy. There seemed to be a lot of waitresses walking around in a daze, not paying attention to what was needing attention.  I spoke with manager and she just said "I'm sorry". When we left I asked if there was another manager. Answer was no, and I spoke with the hostess and she said the same 'sorry'.....that's it. 
If this was a one time experience the I would not comment, but I sure would appreciate the feed back if it was my establishment. 
Sorry Blake, love you,  but there needs to be some improvements! 
Great atmosphere, great music!
Josie was an excellent server at Margaritaville. Fast service, bottomless drinks, and decent food. Plenty of seating for big parties and a really good vibe from the live music.

Have eaten at Margaritaville's before in Myrtle Beach, Key West and Florida and this one is the worst. Burger was okay, hard to mess up a burger, wife's fish sandwich tasted bad (they comped her meal--good part), drinks and shot overpriced. Better options for food and drinks in NashVegas.

went here for the first time last night to see Ledisi.  my two complaints are (1) valet didn't take cards and you couldn't pay the valet directly.   you had to pay inside.  (2) the air. i am cold natured so i travel with jackets and sweaters, neither helped!  the establishment was beautiful and sound system was exceptional.
Food was delicious. Steak cooked perfectly. Wait was short. Love land shark on draft. Bathrooms were a sad mess. But the food is delicious!

One of the coolest places in Nashville I've ever been to. The owner happened to be around and took my friends and I on a personal tour around the brewery, super cool guy. The main bartender has a doctorate in something no one has ever heard of ;) ( cellular structure stuff)  she's made an amazing concoction of kombucha. Ask for a beer bucha.. A natural antioxidant, you'll be feeling amazing in no time!
Honestly you have to go, you won't be disappointed.
Awesome atmosphere, food, friendly staff. Fried green tomatoes and mac and cheese where amazing

Perhaps it was a off-night, but the crowd at Jimmy Buffets was actually pretty lacking the night we stopped by. The first floor had a live band which was pretty solid but there was not much of a crowd or any dancing. Even on the second floor it was kind of quiet - most people were just eating dinner though it was fairly late into the evening. 

We ended up sitting here a while to rest our tired legs before moving on. Seemed like a fun place with a good setup for listening to live music, maybe next time I'm in the area it will be a bit more fun.

Some of my older (baby boomer) colleagues chose this spot on a recent business trip to Nashville.

The service was slow, food unremarkable, and layout stank.  The place was about 50% full but the hostess sat us at a table uncomfortably close to the bar (people continuously bumping into our chairs to pass us).  Took over half an hour of our napkins on our plates being ready to go before we could even get our waitress to get us the check.

There are tons of great historic spots on Broadway, don't waste your time or money getting suckered into a subpar place like this.

I have been to Bridgestone many, many, many times for sporting events, concerts, entertainment shows, etc. I really love this venue. They recently updated some of their food stands (I think that's what they're called) and they are DELICIOUS. I think my fav item is the mashed potato bowl at the Chicken stand - oh my YUM. Bridgestone is massive so it's easy to get lost in but wherever you sit in the venue, you've got a great view. Love the atmosphere when a crowd is packed in there. Unfortunately, parking downtown sucks. I can never find somewhere close to park for less than $15-$20 bucks. Of course there are cheaper spots to park further away from the venue but if I'm meeting friends, and walking alone at night, I prefer to be closer to Bridgestone for safety reasons. 

If you haven't been to an event here, come. It's a great way to spend any day/night, the alcohol selection is wonderful and the food is yummy!

Band was awesome, great vibe, they pulled them off for a surprise guest! Which no one knew and wasn't that good. They took our barstools and made us stand away from the bar so people could come up to the bar. Over crowded and not worth it.
Really enjoyed visiting. The live band was great and on a Thursday night the atmosphere is very chill and inviting. Definitely one of my favorite spots downtown.

Margaritaville's atmosphere, service and quality of food have always been good. My favorite room to dine in is the Tiki Room. Though upstairs in the Cowboy Room is fun as well, but might only be arranged for larger groups. If you are going for a drink and app, I would suggest the Lava Lava Shrimp. It is sweet with the right amount of spice. If you get the Volcano Nacho make sure you are hungry and ready to share. It is an impressive stack of covered nachos. For entrees I would recommend their Fish Tacos or Jerk Chicken. If you save room for dessert, you can't go wrong with the Key Lime Pie or Cheesecake.

When we got our food, it was good.  

The ups:
Live entertainment, that rotates between floors, when they aren't on your floor, there are tvs that you can see it.  
Food was good
They give kids these neat wiki stix packets instead of coloring stuff

Our experience negatives:
I ordered the Al Vacado burger, without the jalepeno mayo.  They literally brought me a plain cheese burger.  

They brought me tomatoe and lettuce on a plate, when I mentioned it. 

After everyone was done with their meal, my corrected meal plain.

Someone in our group ordered a steak, med-well.  He got med-rare.

Our second round of drinks came 40 minutes later.  

What they did:

The didn't charge us for the steak meal, which was a more costly than the hamburger meal.

They gave us a round of desserts.

I attend Ethos Church here on Sundays. The huge, expansive venue fits a generous, large-to-medium sized crowd, with a modest stage space. For a mostly music venue, their bathrooms are always quite clean as well. If you're going for concerts, they have a decent bar, though I've never been here when it's active.

Structurally, I love how you can see just a bit of blue sky peeking out of side windows on the industrial, high ceilings every Sunday morning. The natural lighting also compliments the space well, given the overwhelmingly industrial feel. I would say a minimalist triumph in concert and venue spaces.
Terrible. Overpriced, long wait, and the food took forever. The jambalaya was as if it was cooked in a microwave. Don't go, nothing positive to say. My friends plates where garbage also.

Marathon is a great space in a cool part of town. Intimate setting which is great for smaller bands. You can feel the energy and if you see a cool band like Moon Taxi (Nashville natives) then you really get an awesome show.

Bad food, GREAT margaritas... 
Excellent ambiance, like you are on vacation in the tropics, and they had live music all afternoon.  I had a blast when we were here.  I will definately come back to this one next trip

If you can get past the hostess and her lack of knowledge and service it is worth it! Waitress repeatedly told us she wasn't taking reservations or anymore names. But the second floor and roof are first come first serve. We found a table! It was dirty but someone eventually came to clean, and we used our phones to view menu. Waiter was great! But he seemed frazzled, he just moved to Nashville 2 weeks ago. Food was delicious and hot!!! Biscuit was one of the best we have had in Nashville! Nachos were huge for four of us to share and were great! Band was playing, loud but still could talk over, I felt he was taking more breaks then I have seen other bands take at other establishments on broadway. Would recommend and go again but either make a reservation a month or more in advance or get ready to test your patience with the terrible hostess and her disorganization.

I'm not a big beer drinker. But...

Tennessee Brew Works is doing a great job of making stellar, craft beers right here in Nashville.  They join the ranks of Yazoo and Jackalope as some of the best local brew around.  The building is super cool. And there's a new menu of enticing small plates!! (including hot fried frog legs)

I play music now and then at the TN Brew Works too, and I always really look forward to it. There's an assortment of acoustic live music Thursday - Saturday nights.

Thank you Chris M. for making us feel so welcome as guests! You took time to give us tips and a map of where to visit. I can honestly say that the service you provided was the best I have ever encountered (even from high end restraunts)! I hope to come back and see you again soon!

Great place for live music! 3 stories of music, food and drinks. 

Good food, great drinks and a really fun atmosphere! Wait staff is a little inexperienced but they've only been open 2 weeks! 

Blake Shelton and partners hit a homerun with this venue! It's a must see on Broadway when in Nashville!

My husband and I stopped by for a drink and ended up staying for three and appetizers. Loved the food and the drinks were awesome, but what was really above and beyond was the service. Our waitress, Stephanie took really good care of us, made the visit very personal and made sure we had a great time!  Really didn't expect this level of friendliness on a busy tourist destination.

$2 domestic beer in long neck bottles on Funday Sunday

May 18th, Sunday, Tony and I decided to Urban Hike today again in Nashville. So, after we made a few stops we ended up here...Winner's Bar and Grill on the West Side off Broadway near Vanderbilt University.

It is a Sunday and about 11am..so its not really crowded...A good thing!
Our Waitress was very friendly and quick to greet us, but didn't give us her name..We liked this bar right from the start. Well lit with Natural light and decor was in Football, with TV on the screens so it reminded us of a sports bar. There is a corner band area, not really large but right size...the tables are all high tops and one large booth. They are spread apart for ample room to move around. 

The waitress brought us menus and got our drink order. She immediately told Tony the drink special is Funday Sunday $2 domestic long necks...Great price...so Tony ordered his favorite...can you guess...??? Budweiser
I ordered a soda...we looked through the menu (very simple two sides only) but we opted not to eat here. We already decided on Five Points on the other side of town..

The music was casual rock and country blend..nothing major. They allow smoking inside and out on the patio...a plus in Tony's book. They have on street parking (if you can grab a spot) and a private parking lot you can access from the alleyway. The patio area is nice and large..

I really liked this spot and I would go here again..The prices were right, staff friendly and quick and menu looked adequate...next time will have to try some actual food...lol !!!
But the beer pricing was great...$6 for both drinks with taxes and tip

The Southern Grilled Cheese is something dreams are made of. Pecans + bacon + cheddar... its decadent in all the right ways. 

This place really hit the spot on service too. Everyone was super friendly, informative and went out of their way to make you feel welcome. Great spot for both locals and tourists who appreciate craft beer and upscale bar bites.

Pimento cheese appetizer is a DO NOT MISS!  Oklahoma burger was also delicious.  We expected the place to be more about the ambiance and music- but it was clear that just as much attention had been paid to the food.  Very family friendly (at least at lunch time)- everyone was very welcoming to both our 9 year old and 11 month old.  Ole Red was our absolute best meal and experience in Nashville.  Don't miss this place.

The fish tacos and the normal margarita are good, not great but good. Just about everything else our party of 6 ordered sucked. Decor is lame, it's too loud to have any conversation, even early on a tuesday night. It was lame, I'll not go back

I can't say for sure why we chose to spend our afternoon at Winners and not Losers when we all know where my friends and I stand. However, with some folks (not me) it's probably difficult to diagnose the full extent of their problems with a cursory glance, so they let us inside anyway.

In any case, Winners might look like your average sports bar, but they did have complimentary bail bonds koozies, picklebacks, buckets of six Bud LIghts for $12, and the sweetest bartenders around. 

And although the food is just your standard fried fare, the cook will gladly give you handful of flour as long assure him that you just want to slap your friend in the face with it.
Stopped in late at night.  Had the mile high nachos and margaritas.  Great service.  Tasty nachos.  Fun atmosphere and live musicians.  Would love to come back!
Stopped in to get a late lunch. Shane was our server and he was great. There was live music which we enjoyed. Would recommend you stopping in to eat or just to have a cold one.

Tennessee Brew Works is an absolute must when visiting nashville, from the friendly, welcoming staff, to the amazing beer and best bar style food you'll ever have. DEFINITELY give this place a tour when you're in town or if you're moving to the area!

We visited Ole Red for supper tonight. I really wanted to like it, but the menu didn't have a lot to choose from. The atmosphere was enjoyable, good music, and we had the sweetest server that was very attentive, that being said the food took longer than I would have expected as it was not very busy. I had the Nashville Hot Chicken and Biscuit with fries. The biscuits were nothing special and the chicken was not very hot (spicy) but it appeared to be made with dark meat and it seemed like every bite had one of those tendons in it that made it hard to eat, I couldn't even finish it. My daughter had the Redneck Nachos, they were just okay, not near enough toppings for the amount of chips they give you. Ole Red does not appear to be a traditional Honky Tonk so I would have expected more out of it as a Restaurant - more to choose from and better quality for the price. I probably will not return.

Ieri sera, attraversando la via principale è più importante di Nashville, pienissima di locali dove fanno musica Country, siamo entrati in questo locale. Non è caratteristico come altri sulla strada ma ha un layout carino. 

Nonostante c'era molta folla all'interno del locale, abbiamo avuto il tavolo dopo pochi minuti. 

Abbiamo preso il classico hamburger con patatine fritte. Niente male sia il cibo che il servizio. Il personale è molto scoppio e pratico e parla velocemente quindi è difficile stargli dietro. 

Il locale è decisamente grande ed offre, come tutti gli altri locali sulla strada, musica Country. 

Complessivamente una buona esperienza.

Well let's see...my wife wanted to go here. We had already had dinner so we stoped to use the potty and have a few drinks. The music was AWESOME!!!  They had several couples dancing and the band did a good job not butchering old songs (Folsom prison blues). Our server BREE seemed annoyed that all we wanted were drinks. Then when we got our check there was a "LBD Tax" on there. They claimed it was for cleaning up the street. I call BS.  Then in the restrooms there were attendants. I'm not a 2 year old, I can get my hands washed all by myself. The guy in the men's room actually asked for the tip. All in all we had a great time and will be back; for dinner next time.

Slightly disappointed. Had tickets for a show that was standing tickets. Drove 3 hours and when we got to the show it was a standing ticket. Never was told of options for a standing ticket. The building is and old warehouse with a bar and even had someone in the bathroom to groom you but then you have standing tickets does not make any since. I was very disappointed in that seeing I'm a woman who was wearing heels. Drinks are moderately priced

We stumbled into Tennessee brew works, thirsty after an afternoon of Nashvhille tourist activities, and they didn't disappoint. They had maybe 10ish beers on tap. I had the Rye IPA and it was very good. The food was stellar - I had fish tacos which were excellent, and my husband was happy with his burger. My aunt and cousin both raved about the grilled cheese too. My favorite thing was the cheese plate - at $15 it was a steal, included 3 different cheeses, and lots of accompaniments. We sat upstairs and watched football on one of the TVs, but there's also ample outdoor seating and live music downstairs as well.
This place has it all! Great brews, a delicious food menu, live music, patio seating, and awesome service. We will be back!

I don't think I'll be seeing another concert here until they fix a few things. First of all, the stage is so low, it is hard to see anything, unless you are in the front row. Second, they need to fix the sound, it isn't loud enough. I can always hear people talking to each other and not the music. And third, they seriously need to fix the audio mix. However, I do like the bar(s) and going to non-concert events here.

One of our favorite spots downtown! The Ole Red beer is so good, we accidentally got to try Big Red which is a cream soda which was also pretty good if you like that stuff. We ordered "The Champagne of Fried Chicken half bird" and it was probably the most delicious meal we had that day! The chicken was so juicy and the biscuits were perfect. The live music was always great every time we went. More than 5 stalls in the ladies room would be a plus but other than that Ole Red is perfect!!
Great drinks, amazing staff, and unbeatable food! The hot chicken sandwich was to die for... Plus they treated my dog like a king!

Came here for the Summit 2016 and came here every night cause they just had amazing food and live entertainment! Fun place to be, food is good, loud environment but that's Nashville for ya! My go-to place when I come to Tennessee!

While it's not such big, this symphony canter is a perl that needs to be properly valorized.

The sound quality is really great. Its central location is kind of a problem in terms of parking, but it's nice to walk around downtown after the concert that brought you there.

Elegant, and well maintained facility, I love it!
It's just a pity that they don't play "good stuff" so often.
Look up for discount coupons before buying the thicket on line. I randomly got the 50% off out of mine.

This place was happenin' on a warm Saturday evening! Albeit packed, the service was quick, friendly, and efficient. Flight of five beers was ordered, which included the Cutaway IPA, Basil Ryeman, Country Roots, Bluff City Pail, and another I can't remember (perhaps a special guest). The Cutaway and Ryeman were the favorites for sure, although each was tasty. Country Roots is a sweet potato stout, so that was the runner-up for me. TBW lies a little off the beaten path, and luckily being in that strange area, (makeshift) parking is easy to find. Fairly large outdoor seating that happens to be pet-friendly is personally always a plus, and this place fits that description. Unfortunately, my partner and I had already eaten, but the food looked delicious! Two of the three times I've been, there were special events planned in the evening, which weren't stated on their website, so perhaps following them on social media to find out unusual closing hours would be wise. Overall, great atmosphere, service, and good product. Would recommend stopping in for a taste (or five)!

A great experience overall! Food and drinks were delicious! So happy I took Tammy's suggestion on the appetizer also! Crab dip was sooooo good! Tammy has to be the best server I've ever met; such a friendly, funny, attentive woman! Great service!

About a week ago i was in Nashville for a bach party and did we have a blast!! Our server shane was awesome! Very fun and informational about the menu. He knew exactly what we would like and helped us all night! Fun guy and great server! I will be back for sure and asking for shane!

We stopped in at this place after a good hour and a half of walking around people watching and seeing the sights on Broadway. There was a live band playing at the time we walked in, but they ended shortly after we walked in and ordered (around 3 pm).

Median demographic was on the over-50 end, including the band. The room with the band was a little small which made it nice to be not too far from the bar or from the band. Service to our table was prompt and friendly.

Margaritas were very good, maybe a little on the sweet side but definitely not weak. If you like tequila, the unflavored variants were mixed well.

Protip: try to snag a corner window seat in the room with the band to maximize people watching in and out of the restaurant as well as the band.

Not one of my favorites in Nashville. Your going to experience more of the Vandy college crowd if you go here during the weekends. I love their karaoke though, you would be surprised most of the people are pretty good. The bathroom situation is horrible. It can become crowded, so if you want to experience Winners my advice is to go early. I have never tried their food so can't comment on that. But if your visiting, or over 25, I wouldn't recommend this establishment. The only reason this is getting 3 stars and not 1 or 2 is because the service is exceptional.

Honky tonk in Nashville is a bucket list of mine.

I crossed that off during a 28 day road trip and a pit stop at Layla's. After walking up and down Broadway deciding which place to venture in to, we picked Layla's and it didn't disappoint. We got a chance to get out of the humidity, relax with a couple of cold hard ciders and listen to The Risches play for almost an hour.

My only complaint (and the reason for the 3 stars) was there wasnt wifi access for those of us coming from outside the US. We unfortunately are traveling with a very limited data plan so any chance for free connection is a double plus bonus score. Otherwise it was just the right amount fun at the right time during this epic trip.

This was an awesome place to have a beer! There's a ton of seating inside and out, live music and fantastic beer. I would recommend grabbing a flight to figure out which beer is your fav. They offer several great beers, all of which are completely different. Check it out, just be prepared to wait on the train if you go down Fogg Street.

Skip the beer, this is about the food. I was part of a Nashville tour of local establishments, and this was our last stop. I was hungry and ordered two dishes and was not disappointed.

You can see and get close to the brewery and it is the cleanest I have ever seen. Service is adequately prompt, the staff is friendly and the decor is wonderful.

When we were there, the stage was occupied by a young lady solo artist who sang wonderfully. This is Music City, after all.

They have a great outside deck, but the view is not great. It will get better when the road construction is finished.

First, I ordered the frog legs. They must have come off a bullfrog. These were the best frog legs I have ever eaten. They were tender. moist and meaty. A light texture crust covered the meat, but it was nice and crunchy. The sauce as akin to Nashville hot chicken, but not firey.

Fish tacos were next. The presentation was nice, but I was taken aback by the fact that the fish was basically a fish stick. Put aside your early childhood memories of this kiddie staple. The stick was a nice size, was moist and tender and the coating was wonderful. Chef was a genius in creating this dish because the shape of the fish stick was perfect for wrapping in a tortilla. Topped with a nice slaw and sweet sauce, this dish was a "keeper".

Go there.

The food was the only thing keeping me from giving one star. The service was nearly non-existent. Our waitress was not around after we placed our food order. Other tables came in after we had ordered and got their food long before us. When the food did arrive, only half the table was served, then two more dishes came out 10 minutes later and we waited for the last dish another 10 minutes. When someone asked for ketchup, she rolled her eyes and argued with another about the lack of dressing on her salad.  She should be working for the DMV, she'd fit right in.

I have been wanting to visit this brewery since they opened. Just the patios outside alone made it look like a fun place to visit. I was definitely not disappointed. This is now one of my favorite breweries in Nashville and I will definitely be back. The staff was so friendly and you could tell they actually love their jobs there. Their food is also very good. I got the grilled cheese and it was possibly one of the best I've had in this town. I would recommend going on a Wednesday night because it's 2 for 1!

Food and drinks were good.
However, the waitress took absolutely forever with our order, we never recieved silverware and had to take it off neighboring tables. Alsp got charged double for every drink we recieved even without asking for a souvenir cup.

Just left this place. Was hanging out trying a beer sampler and having a sandwich. A couple of young guys and the bartender which clearly was their friend decided it would be funny to make fun of me for smelling and tasting my beers. That's funny because to me I actually like the smell and taste of beers and really enjoy them. The food was good but that bartender was terrible she really needs to figure out where she works and what she is serving. I'm sure my LA hat did not help me out either but I would expect some better hospitality from  a brewery.  6:38pm 11/12/17
Great tap room great beers and really great food.  Not at all your typical bar food - much better.  Love the hot chicken.
Acoustics still suck!  They spent a lot of money on upgrades, but still can't get the sound right!

Extremely understaffed!!   So many tables were open on main level, but wait was over 45 minutes.  We got seated upstairs, great view of the band, but we only saw our server ONCE!  It took us going to the bar to get her to come the first time, we got our own silverware, then continued to go to the bar to get our drinks.
Extremely slow service, poorly prepared food and over priced. This is what happens when someone wants to play music for a living opens up a restaurant.

Schermerhorn Symphony Center is absolutely beautiful.  The acoustics are top notch.  The Nashville Symphony has classical and pop series. Other artists go there as well. The building itself is a true symphony hall and it is wonderful and very classy.  You can check their website to see the schedule:


http://www.nashvillesymphony.org/tickets/calendar

Good food and amazing island drinks! I had the Bahama Breeze and Bananas and Havanas. If You like coconut blended drinks, then you will love these drinks! It reminds me of being somewhere tropical! They always have great live music too. Friendly staff who like to get to know you while you are there.

I went to my first concert here a month ago, and was really surprised with how awesome this venue is. The big open space was enough for a sold out show full of standing folks, and yet it still felt like a very intimate setting. Acoustics are excellent, and there's plenty of space to dance! Parking is also easily attainable down the street, and some of it is even free! There are two fully stocked bars in the space, so even if the lines are long at one, chances are you can get through at the other.

The only thing I wasn't pleased about were the bathroom attendants - I always feel so guilty and yet annoyed when someone expects a tip for handing me a towel!

For our first time being to Nashville, we had such great service from Shane M! Very friendly person! He is great at his job!! If you eat or drink at Margaritaville, I would recommend having Shane M as your server!!

New management, new bartenders and servers, and a new grasp on what this bar/restaurant can do for Nashville. Everything seems to be ran much better than before and we had an excellent time at their Bluegrass Sunday Brunch. I recommend trying this place out again if you had a bad experience before.
What a stunning place! The architecture is beautiful and the inside is very clean. I saw "The Lord of the Ring" and the acoustics were on point. I will definitely be seeing another show here.
Really cool place!  We loved the beer, atmosphere and the nachos.

We visited Margaritaville and had a wonderful lunch. Our server, Ethan T. was very helpful and even entertained my 2 year old daughter. The band that was playing was pretty good too. Overall the atmosphere was good and the food was great. I would highly recommend visiting this restaurant/bar if you are in Nashville.
Awful, slow service. Messed up our order multiple times. Up charged without being told. Over priced for what you get. DO NOT go unless all you want to do is sit at the bar and drink.

This rating is primarily for the bartender and the duel entertainers that performed when we were there. We had some drinks and appetizers. The bartender took really good care of us. We really enjoyed the entertainment, Kassie and Ben Wilson. Beautiful sound with variety and an intimate feel in the bar area. Only thing that would have improved the experience is if there were lounge chairs to relax in...but then we'd never leave!
Very casual spot for lunch. Really good bar food though. WARNING: the buffalo chicken tenders and hot hot hot! Delicious though. Keep a beer nearby.
Good venue,  Great food,  handicap assemble,  Great music.  I had the chicken quesadilla,  it came with guacamole,  Pico,  and a line flavored sour cream. Delish
Sucks balls, let waaaaaaay too many people in for their whiskey jam...think country hipster convention...I went home and killed myself after

Too Crowded for me...and tourist in there with kids about 12 yrs old and 5 yrs old..I know its a tourist location..but there should be rules about it..I think its child neglect or abuse or something. I know I wouldn't want my kids seeing a bunch of loud drunks partying..just because Johnny and George once walked these floors..
come on parents..get a sitter or go to disney world if you are going to take your kids on vacation...NOT BROADWAY!!! 

Tourist trap...Budweiser $6 and fountain soda $3..
too high...too high...

We sat allllll the way up top for the Stanley cup game 2 playoffs!!!!  .. almost at the ceiling ... but still felt like a "5th team member!" The fans are bananas! Those chants were hilarious and surprisingly chanted by EVERYONE in SYNCH!!!!!! This  was an amazing experience ...national anthem .. amazingly performed by non other than ... freaking  brad paisley!!!!
We were excited to visit here on our first night in Nashville. Very disappointed in the music talent on the night we attended. Was my least favorite of the weekend.

From the jambalaya, to the live music, the bar, and the souvenir shop with all the Parrot/5 o'clock themes - this place rocks! It feels like such a relaxed place with a great vibe to it! I missed it in Las Vegas, but was glad to make it here in Nashville! The prices are a little bit high, but the waitresses were fantastic, and the value you get for the money is amazing!

I love this place. Its an awesome looking arena from the inside and out. What a great place to catch an NHL game. Nashville has the friendliest NHL fans in the league. I love coming to games here. I have friends near by in Brentwood so I catch a few games a year here. I met Amy Grant, Vince Gill and Carrie Underwood here, I got expensive tickets. One my fav venues in all of sports and its literally right off Broadway so you can hit up the honkey tonks before or after the game. Nashville traffic can get bad from time to time thou, you are warned. Other than that I would recommend this place to any NHL fan or anybody that wants to a rip roaring good time and Nashville natives are super friendly, people will actually talk to unlike cities like NYC or Chicago.

I was craving something other than beer and bbq. Jimmy delivered with a decent margarita and the best ever coconut shrimp / orange marmalade. Only reason for not getting a 4 is the boring "island" loop they play on every tv. It was fine the first 10 times .... but come on. At least have some in the bar and some on the floor with a game on.

Stopped in for dinner.  Very busy and lively.  25 minute wait for table.  It's a Saturday night so busy was expected.  Spent a little time in the gift shop and saw a couple things we wanted for the game room/bar.  Decided to have a couple drinks while we waited for the table and get trinkets later.  Bartender was exceptional.  Ordered two frozen margaritas- they were out of limes.  He told me that he'd get some limes to us.  10 minutes later, here he comes with a cup and freshly cut lime - way more than we needed -  went back to him and added some to his tip.  He was really good.
Got out table and waited almost 30 minutes for our appetizer - which also arrived with everything else.  I had ordered a steak, which was so bad it wasn't worth eating.  Well over cooked.  Waiter didn't come back to check on things until we were almost finished - everything else was OK.  
Waiter said manager took my meal off and never offered to make another one.  Now I'm a little pissed.  Paid our bill and on the way out, I addressed the manager about his lack of presence to find out he never knew about the issue in the first place.
Needless to say, I decided not to buy the cool stuff for the bar because why would I want a reminder of such a lousy experience?
It's Nashville, it's Broadway, I guess the standard shouldn't be really high, but for a chain establishment - it should have been better.
On a food note, I don't have to rearrange the walls in the game room to accommodate new parrot head stuff!
Crawfish boil! Extremely friendly staff. They saw us standing up with our kids and brought us chairs. Delicious, cold beer. Great outdoor space

Quiet possibly the friendliest and most spacious restaurant on the Broadway strip. The waitstaff (a lot of waitstaff) are there to make sure your every need is met to an extent. I also enjoyed the fact that even though they have two stages (one in front for small acoustic sets and one in back for full bands), they use one at a time as not to overwhelm costumers with music. The steak quesadilla's are to die for and even if you feel like you've been forgotten, one of the many waitstaff is sure to ask "How was your meal?"

A little dive-y. Has karaoke, which is why we were there. It's not crowded at all - even on a Friday night. We were there with a group of ten people, and there wasn't a wait to sing! Typical beer selections. Not bad, but it's basically a place to go for karaoke!
Loved this place! The food and service were both top notch. The tater tots were the best ever

Layla's is probably my favorite bar on Broadway. It's non-pretentious, and doesn't get *too* full, though it can get a good amount of people on the dance floor.

They don't do draft beers, only bottles. They have a decent selection though, which is nice.

There are tables along the walls, and some bar seating.

I saw the Eskimo Brothers here, and they were one of the best live acts I saw that week in Nashville.

I was only here for a few days and went to Layla's twice for drinks and live music. Couldn't help but come back a third time to pick up a t-shirt. It was the last one in my size, so the bartender just plucked it off the wall. It had a staple hole in it, cost $20, and smelled like beer, but it's probably the most authentic souvenir I brought back with me.
Was wholly disappointed with the beers here. Sampled all of them, and all of them tasted like watered down brews...cool space though.

Saw some old reviews on here that weren't so great but heard it was redone and much better so I decided to try it. THIS PLACE IS GREAT. It's right on broadway and has a great unique vibe. I had a burger and it was delicious. Can't recommend this place enough. Great beer selection too!

The music was good but the food was NOT good and there were fruit fly/gnat things flying all near our food. So gross! Our waitress was very unfriendly. We hardly ever write bad reviews but it was just such an unpleasant experience. We won't come back here
I wish they would have posted on their website that they were closed for renovations.   Very disappointing. Made a special stop to watch the Richie sisters on the way home to Wi.
Great place to see a concert in Nashville. I have seen Gwar and the Dropkick Murphy's at this venue and the sound was great. Highly recommend this venue
