No Southern Hospitality here! After one employee invited us in from the cold for drinks, a friend and I were immediately confronted by another employee asking if we were going to buy food or drinks.  I told him that we are waiting for the remainder of our friends to get their ID's checked and then we will decide what we wanted to order.  Immediately the bouncer told us to leave because we were not paying customers.  Rediculous.  Poor customer service. Rude employees.  Definitely will not return.
Ken and Chris in the merchandise store were SO nice!! Ken was super helpful and friendly and Chris was so sweet and generous I walked out with a pineapple pin! Made my night!

Great vibe- locals and some sporadic tourists. 

It's a great place to hide from the downtown scene. Would recommend to any beer aficionados.

Would you like salt with your steak / salad?
Ordered the $26 steak it had so much salt I could not eat it. Manager took it off the bill. She got me a salad which had as much salt on it too. 2-Stars. Nov 2016

Absolutely no complaints about this location! Our server was Chris Rhodes. He was wonderful. Friendly and fun. Recommended a great drink that I had never had before (not a menu item). With our drinks we had the crab dip, and it was delicious! I would definitely love to visit this location again next time I'm in Nashville, and I recommend Chris as your server!

I like this arena and all but almost three weeks later I'm still pretty annoyed about my last experience there.

Wanting to watch the Canadiens warm up, I asked an usher if it was cool if I could go down to the ice. She said no I had to wait until 5:30 (6pm puck drop) and yet all these people were taking good spots. So I asked the usher one section over about this and he told me to head on down. Still not sure wtf that was about. I've never been restricted anywhere and she was clearly the only one following such a rule. Had I waited until such a time I would have had no place to stand and warmups would have been well in action. And since I managed to get myself a puck that would have REALLY sucked if I hadn't been able to go down there.

Still like the arena overall, it's one of the only places I've been where sitting in the upper bowl does not translate to jam as many people in small seats as possible width wise. But I think they have raised their concession prices a bit too high. Not that it stopped the legion of douchebros in front of me from reeking of shit beer, so I guess maybe robbing fools is better than appealing to the masses...I mean I can't argue...if you wanna overpay for light beer instead of go to a bar literally across the street who am I to judge.

Lastly can I just say please don't put those ads with Mike Fisher eye level for doing your business in a bathroom stall. Totally can never look at the guy ever again. Or listen to Carrie Underwood.

Props though for letting people hang around during the crazy tornado warning thing.
My hostess Cori was such a delight! She welcomed us with such a big smile and even shared things to do in the local area. She was such a great start to a wonderful evening of food and fun!

First, we have been to Margaritavilles all over the country. so, our expectations were set by our previous experiences. The restaurant full but not overcrowded. We found a tble near the band and dance floor. After about 10 minutes our table was bused from the previous customers. Ordered food and drinks. My $9 Landshark arrived about 10-15 minutes later. We ordered our go to, Volcano Nachos with grilled chicken added. The nachos arrived and we noticed there was no Guacamole on them. After several minutes we were informed that the kitchen was out of Guacamole. As we dug in, we discovered that 3/4 of the chips were topping free. Under the crown of melted cheese there as a scoop of chili covering about 3 inches. next to that a scoop of cheese goo covering about the same area. The grilled chicken that we normally get turned out to be small cubes of pressed chicken mystery meat. (smaller than a crouton). My wife finally said she didn't want to wast the calories eating this.
The music was really good. the 3 piece band was engaging and tried to get the crown involved. The night before we were in the bar and the duo playing were also very good. 
The entertainment is why I gave them 2 stars.
First bad meal I have ever had at a Margaritaville.
Great place in general and specifically. Came for a concert, saturated for the beer.  Great environment, haven't tried the food but it smelled good.

To the bartender who thought it was necessary to ask me to leave.  I made the comment that you should clean tables as well as ask People not not stand on bar stools.   Thank you for kicking me out. I end d up in a great place with a clean tables bitch.  The music was awesome
Smaller venue then most Margaritavilles. Friendly staff and good music that took requests. Good drinks (of course). No food taken in, sorry.

What a great experience, both times the bands made you want to dance and sing along! Lots of fans going, so you don't sweat. A fun experience, just what you think of when thinking of a fun bar in Nashville!

Stopped in for a couple of Bahama Mamas during Memorial Day weekend. Interior design was very tropical and authentic. The bar area had large bay windows that were opened to the street. The restaurant location is a corner spot right in the heart of all the action on Broadway Avenue. I didn't eat anything but had a great time, loved the drinks, decor, and location. Definitely stop by and get your favorite beach drink and sit in the bar area/cocktail tables.

For this location in the prime spot off Broadway, the service was great. Walked in was seated right away listen to
The live band and ordered our food- fish n chips and pretzels.

Great venue. Love music and chill vibe. The grilled  cheese and fries were great. Also loved the hot chicken sandwich (giant, could definitely be shared). Lots of good beer selections including some unique ones like beet beer.  Looks like the outdoor section is super cool but it was too cold this weekend to sit out there!  Definitely check it out.

Full disclosure: Booze and band only.

The doorman said the band could play anything. The band could not play "anything", only the favorites. The bartenders were nice and the price is right considering the location and amount to drink. Big plus, they have Yuengling!

It wasn't crowded and the acustics were pretty good. If you just want drinks and music, this is the place to go.

A 20 minute wait, yet 15 tables open...this place won't last long!

It took a while to flag down a waiter, at least the drinks were good.

Out of the local breweries this one has the best menu and options for snacks and non-drinkers alike. I really appreciate that. I do love a good brew, but I like having something special for my non-drinking friends as well and their kombucha is really good! They also have reasonably priced snacks. 

I adore the seating situation. Tons of outdoor space in the shade, sun and in between, and also a cool fenced off area inside the brewery. On perfect weather days it can get a little crowded but the set up feels pretty fluid and the lines move quickly. 

As a local brewery they have a few 'regulars' on the menu - if you are a stout person try the Sweet Potato Stout, it is amazing! But honestly through sampler trays and sampling from my friends 'trays' (aka glasses) I've never had anything I made stink face too. Thats pretty rare.

Parking is actually fairly decent across the street, a little bumpy and tore up, but easier access to park then the other local breweries in the area.m In fact, if you don't mind a walk, just mosey on down the street/across the tracks to try the others! Ask a local, they will know! ;)

Prime location on Broadway, alongside all the bars/nightlife/must see tourist stop! We actually ended up in this bar because 1)they allowed my kids in who happen to be way under 21 and 2)offer vegan options on their menu!
The place is quite spacious and set up to allow everyone a great view of the band playing that night.  Bathrooms are impressive, as well, albeit up one flight of stairs.
Drinks were on point and the food was good enough. I was a bit disappointed that my impossible burger substitution for the bbq pulled pork did not have sauce on it or shredded. Wouldn't have considered it a substitution so much as just a burger...
The waitress Liz is phenomenal. Very pleased with the food. Service. And drinks. If downtown, and need a cold beer and some grub. Go see Liz.

This is an update of a previous review.

Stopped in here again last weekend, mainly because after I wrote an unfavorable review (due to the lack of darker beers) the owner, Christian, reached out to me and very politely mentioned they would be coming out with a Sweet Potato Stout shortly.  Well, I finally had a chance to check it out and I loved it.  As far as Sweet Potato Stouts go (one of my favorite kind of stouts) I thought it was delicious.

Also in my previous review I mentioned that the service was not that great... well, I can assure you it was 180 degree turn-a-round this time.  The staff was beyond friendly -- they practically waited on us while we were playing "Cards Against Humanity" ... that is something I certainly don't expect from a brewery.  Anddd, they now do flights as well!

And did I mention they have a TON of free games to choose from?  They also have live music, TVs, an AWESOME outdoor patio, and a food truck which I presume will be a staple over the summer.

Given their location and beer types, their main competition has to be Yazoo and Jackalope.  Let me tell you -- there is no competition.  TBW beats Yazoo on every category of where I want my next "Sunday Funday" to be ... service, space, atmosphere, etc.  Trust me -- next time you want to enjoy a beer on patio somewhere, give Brew Works a shot.

From my initial 2-star review, I could not have been more impressed on my second time around.  So glad I gave this place a second shot.  I would recommend to a friend, and I'll definitely be back.

So, I didn't see much of the arena because we basically came in and sat down but the Preds game was a whole lot of fun and during the intermission they have a band there playing live music. I went on a Tuesday but they had the Thursday special in effect which was 1/2 price beers and soda and free popcorn. I have to say, pretty sweet.
Wasn't let in because I "seemed like I was having trouble".  I had three beers the evening and clearly sober.  Will never go back because of how rude the bouncers were to me.

Takes over 20 minutes to get a drink from any of the bar tenders, also not a set last call time and as soon as they called for last call they would no longer serve anyone in my party that was there. The only reason they are even getting a star for me is the band. The bar tenders are extremely rude, service is disgustingly slow and they don't have the words customer service in their vocabulary. Will not be going back and I'm extremely disappointed that my large party was treated that poorly, I will make sure that any other large groups do not visit this business, they can spend their money at a better bar with actual customer service.

This place feels like my home away from home.  I've worked in here since 2002.  It's not too big and not too small. It's located right in the heart of downtown.  If you're lucky enough to have a hotel room in downtown Nashville, you can walk to the arena without a problem and then spill out into broadway and 2nd ave. after your event.  I believe the building is aging gracefully as they continue to add new features.  On the south end, there's the new "Tavern 96" which faces the Country Music Hall of Fame and new convention center.  When inside the arena, be sure and check out the "Krazy Kyle" sign in the 1st level at the north end.  That is my spot!
This is a really nice spot to hang, plenty of table games and tvs to watch sports. I really enjoyed the summer wit beer!

The Schermerhorn is simple a world-class facility.  The acoustics are excellent, the location is very convenient to dining establishments and hotels, and the building itself is stunning.  You should definitely come here for a performance, but make sure you see the Nashville Symphony itself in addition to any "traveling shows" that may be coming through.  Our Symphony is one of the top-rated in the country and a real hidden gem in terms of things to do downtown.

Finally, do yourself a favor and call to get a tour of the building when there's no event going on.  The design and the mechanics of the facility itself are incredible.  It's over-engineered to last 300 years at a minimum, but should easily outlive that.  The organ is also a sight to behold, especially when you consider that only about 5% is actually visible from the performance hall.  The Schermerhorn is a jewel in Nashville's crown.

This is no state of the art arena by any means at all... 

Average arena, that pulls in some Superstar entertainers though!

I am at The Highway Happy hour which is great but bartender and wait staff are rude. Highway needs a venue that is better for their fans. Margaritaville just doesn't get how to treat people and increase sales. Why wait in line for 3 hours in the sun without being able to buy a beer. Siriusly

The hubby and I are trying to hit all the Margaritaville's across the world!  This one was quite big since they have a large second level.  The food was good but bummed they no longer do their drink sampler.  That was amazing!! I only gave it three starts because he went there two nights in a row and the second night we sat in the bar so we could listen to the live music.  The bar was very crowded and I didn't think a lot of was done to manage the craziness!! I was sitting at the bar eating and had people leaning over me all the time.  I did end up claiming to the manager and then left pretty quickly thereafter.  I do love Jimmy, so the food, drinks and music did not disappoint.  I think this is our 15th one we have visited.
Sucked. Waited for an hour with nothing going on.  No seats, no tables, etc. Don't do it!!!!
Service was slow and food was mediocre at best. Don't waste your time or money here! Way too expensive for what you get. Food came out cold.

I was enjoying myself. The concert was grooving and my hips were moving. But then it happened. Some arrogant jack hole spilled his beer on me. Also, the seating sucks. If you can't get floor seats, don't go. It's that simple. Also, the sound quality is poor.

We stood in line from 1-3:30 to get into see The Highway radio show. Great food and staff is over the top great.  It is worth the waiting in line with nice people. Buzz Branard was very nice and love the show support of Law Enforcement and Military.

Nails the Jimmy Buffett vibe in the middle of downtown Nashville. Eclectic mix of live music, which was a very cool experience.

A special shoutout to stilts-walker extraordinaire Natasha who's also a self-taught balloon artist. The hat you made me was one-of-a-kind. My parents and I were downtown for one night only, and you helped make it the best experience of the trip. Thank you!

We were very excited to come for a friend's show but between low quality food that is barely above McDonald's quality, overly expensive watered down drinks, flies everywhere and some idiot stilt walker wandering around and blocking the stage... We will not be back. Out of all those the stilt walker is the one thing I could really not forgive. Really inappropriate to have a side show when people are singing their hearts out on stage.

We ordered the 1/2 bucket of chicken with mashed potatoes and biscuit. The wings as an appetizer are tangy and bring a little heat. The pulled pork and tatie tots are a delightful meal. Love the music and enjoyed touring the top deck ! Great scenery.

Tennessee Brew Works is located just a few miles from Broadway and just a couple of right turns from the interstate 40 off ramp were Ewing Ave and Vine St meet. Tennessee Brew works opened it's taproom in 2013. In 2014 Tennessee Brew Works was recognized as the "Best new Brewery" and "Nashville's Favorite Brew", according the their Facebook page. NBC is a brewery, taproom and live music venue close to the heart of Downtown Nashville. NBC strives to create craft beers through a "greener" brewing process. NBC is the first in their industry, within the US, to utilize various techniques and equipment to achieve these goals. NBC aspires to create high quality craft beer and serve their community.

I dropped by NBC's taproom on a Tuesday afternoon during "Happy Hour". The brews were not only tasty but half price. The discount, the well crafted brews and attentive/knowledgeable staff resulted in a favorable review. During my visit I tried a sampling of NBC's beers via a flight and a snack from the menu. The flight sampling consisted of NBC's Southern Wit, Cutaway IPA, 1927 IPA, County Roots, Walk the Lime and a secret, extra, sampling from the "Mixed Tape" tap. The flight consisted of all the brews on tap, during my visit, and for $10 was well worth it. Southern Wit was the winner of the night for me. To accompany my assortment of alcoholic appetizers I ordered the Chips and Dips. The chips were smokey and crisp. Each chip was dusted with seasoning and had a hard crunch. The dip was French Onion and was thick and creamy. A dollop was placed onto a plate then the chips were placed into the dipping sauce. This arrangement didn't moisten or reduce the crunch factor of the chips. It allotted an almost perfect portion of dip per chip. The serving method seemed very scientific and removed the whole burden of dipping each chip your self. I fought it very efficient.

The interior was festive and in-line with the philosophy of the "Music City". The taproom and restrooms were clean. The staff was engaging and knowledgeable, of their product and other breweries in the area. I highly recommenced stopping by if you are every in the greater Nashville area and thirsty.

This venue was a little difficult to find when we were visiting because of local road closures. The staff was a little rude compared to other venues we have been to. The acoustics and sound here were actually pretty good and you didn't have to stand at the stage to rock with the band. Anywhere you stand (unless there's a tall guy in front of you) was a good view. The bathrooms have attendants which always weirds me out and they weren't that clean considering they're paying someone to attend to it. I'd rather it be swept than someone put soap in my hand for me. (This is not a reflection of the actual attendant just on what the venues priorities seemed to be.) there is no re-entry which is disappointing. Sometimes you just need to get some fresh air or drop off band merchandise at your car. It would be nice if they had a stamp or wristband system. The experience here was only good because of the band and our friends playing, if the staff and their rules were nicer and accommodating the experience would have been better.
Alexa is the bees knees son she hooked us up.Got her section on my first time in here in nashville. I hope to see her again she made my visit feel like home.

Beautiful concert hall. Very intimate, and great acoustics. I came to see Kem in concert and left a very happy lady. 
If you have trouble walking, please arrive Extra early. There's quite a bit of walking and stairs to climb. We didn't opt to use the elevator due to the long wait time.
Great musical entertainment and very cold beer. If you'd like to dance this might be the spot for you. One problem I had was the bathrooms could've kept cleaner.

Sometimes you find the perfect place and Tennessee Brewing was and is the prefect place. The beer was good the staff was amazing the food was delightful.  The atmosphere was perfect.  The upper deck allowed for a picturesque view of the city. The lower decks and patios gave the feel of your own back yard with family and friends. The staff was so helpful with explaining about their beers.  They took the time to describe their beers and how their flights should be drank to get the most enjoyment from flavors.  Once we settled into a spot and began to soak in the view and tease our taste buds with some down home great beers our food showed up. We were just knocked of our feet with the flavors and visual presentation of meal.  It was our last night in town and the experience at Tennessee Brewing was spectacular.
Best margaritas in town and theit strawberry spinach salad was the best. Ask for Tammy for your waitress she's the best.

So this place is IT. This was my favorite place for live music in Nashville. It wasn't typical honky tonk nor was it classic rock or top 40 hits. The band we saw had a cello and violin and it was just DIVINE! It's very divey, but comfy, inviting, great seats for viewing the band, and a really neat atmosphere.

Its a shame that one bachelorette party had a bad experience and the whole group posted one star. The food is so surprisingly good. My friend ordered the grilled romaine salad and I reluctantly tried a bite. It was amazing! I came back the same day and ordered it again. Its simple and amazing.

The burgers are great, and the buffalo wings were amazing. They werent friend, they were grilled with lots of meat on them.

The service was a little slow - but considering it was a busy Sunday with the Titans/Cowboys game - worth the wait.
This place is very unique. They have very interesting bands play here. Always a good time.

Nice people, great music, and perfect location.  Even though it was snowing during our recent trip to Nashville, we made our way to Winners for Whiskey Jam on Monday night. Talk about a good time...we laughed, we listened, and we met some wonderful Nashvillians who couldn't have been nicer. Looking forward to seeing the Whiskey Jam crew in Chicago on April 20th. Thanks for a great time, friends.
I wish I could say that we actually tasted anything served here, but we did not. Instead, my best friend was harassed because her I.D. expired THE NEXT DAY. FOR HER 50TH BIRTHDAY. Will never return.

This is the bar we ended our trip to Nashville in, and we ended up staying for longer than we were planning to because of the awesome band performing and the great atmosphere. We got here at around midnight and were lucky enough to grab a seat on the second floor overlooking the band performing below. The music was absolutely amazing, decorations in the bar were fun, and overall we wished we had went to Layla's for more than one night. 

Definitely recommend this location. It has a different feel from the other bars - a bit more laid back perhaps - and we enjoyed it immensely.
The food is really heavy, fried and cream based. The prices are high at least $12 an order no alcohol included. The beer is great. Recommend stopping for a drink and show but no food.
So glad we had our company retreat here! What an honor to listen to Gordon Kennedy -Grammy award winning songwriter. Staff was fantastic!

I can't attest to the hockey experience at Bridgestone which is after all why it's here to begin with--I do know the local fans are enthusiastic to say the least (though many are heartbroken at the moment over the Cup they almost snagged). I just haven't been to see one as I'm not much of a hockey fan but one of these days I might give it a shot. I have now seen two live rock shows at Bridgestone which is what my review will reflect.

First of all---it is a general rule for me that live music is best in small-medium venues where you can see the act from the floor in your line of sight. As such I've see many up and coming and (in my mind) established and proficient acts of many genres in the many other venues scattered throughout the city since my move to the area a few years ago. You can see great shows at Marathon, Exit/In, 3rd & Lindsey, The End, etc. But there are simply some acts that will not play such a modest venue and when it comes to an arena act, Bridgestone is a solid, in many ways superb, choice. For one thing there's not really a bad seat in the house. On the floor, in the stands, even in the top left or right stands, the stage and set up is always in your line of sight wherever you sit. For another, because it's an ICE HOCKEY ARENA this place is not sweltering and damp. Some venues will have you feeling like you're in a sweat lodge but things remain comfortable and even somewhat chilly here at Bridgestone no matter how packed or active a show. To top it off, the crew and staff are remarkable at working a crowd through the line at a remarkable pace--safely and securely. You have no problem getting through a line and to your seat in plenty of time. Even leaving your seat to hit the restroom and get back in time for the next act (or to get a snack or drink) is painless.

As for negatives, it's doubtful that any are unique to Bridgestone and aren't just part of every arena experience--no decent parking that isn't $25 and up (depending on the surge) in the area (but even then you're in and out of nearby lots pretty quickly), insane concession prices ($10 for a 'refillable' cola, I can only imagine the beer prices), etc. All in all though, if a major act is coming to the area Bridgestone is a good place to catch them,
Came back a second time on a second trip. Always great beer and food. Will come back again soon.

Best thing about this place is the music. Everything else is pretty mediocre. Service was timely but not really friendly, didnt talk to us or introduce herself. Only asked if we were ready to order. Mac and cheese below stereotypical. Food is greasy. Cauliflower is good. Basic Broadway minus the restaurant is a little spacious. Wouldn't recommend it.

On a vacation, the temptation might be to invest wisely, like Warren Buffett, but in Nashville, the temptation is more likely to leave you drinking like Jimmy Buffett.  I actually don't drink, but as a fan of his music for many, many years, I've been to over a dozen Margaritaville's so on a recent trip to Nashville for a Paul Simon concert, of course I had to stop by this one for lunch.  

Live music is a common feature of Margaritaville, but not often during lunchtime, so I was pleasantly surprised to see a performer when I arrived at just before noon on a Saturday.  He was working his way through a mix of cover songs (think the theme song from The Dukes of Hazzard) & I was quickly seated by a welcoming hostess.

While I have been to many of their restaurants, most Margaritavilles do have one or two unique area dishes (e.g. their take on the po' boy in New Orleans), but at this location, I opted for the French Dip & Sweet Potato Fries & settled in to watch some old Buffett performance clips on one of the many tv screens hanging in the restaurant while I waited for my meal.  

It arrived quickly enough, as did a refill on my drink order, & the food was excellent.  The space in the venue is such that it's not too noisy that you can enjoy a conversation & still hear the music being played & the service I experienced was quite good.

After lunch, I visited the retail shop & while I was a bit bummed on the lack of locally themed merchandise (I have enough t-shirts for the rest of my life that I was hoping for a little more variety), most casual visitors should walk away happy.

Great selection of concessions. Seating is terrible. People were leaving and going to the ticket office to request reassignment because the seats were extremely small. It was amazing that an arena that was recently updated has such tight seating. They were very good about trying to accommodate the people, but when you pay $60+ for a ticket you expect to be able to sit in the seat.
A very crazy place! Very friendly bartenders and great music. We mostly had drinks but also the fried shrimps and it was amazing!
Best band we found on Broadway all weekend! Not too crowded and the service was great!

We came to Nashville for a girls weekend. Ended up at Ole Red on Saturday night around 8:30-9. We found awesome seats on the rooftop bar, but the band didn't play but a couple country songs. The kitchen closes at 10, so put your order in well ahead of time. We placed an order for food, but the chef "lost" our ticket and refused to complete our order after we were told (past 10). Disappointing to say the least.

Hopped in here on a 2nd trip to Nashville. Was harassed by a worker about using the bathroom first before buying a drink. I thought it was odd. He continued until my friend gave her credit card up to buy a drink. He still continued and lectured me after I got out of the bathroom. I find the place rude and won't be coming back.
Cool place! Out of the 5 or so places on B'way that we checked out, this was the best. Music was good, people were cool, ambiance was genuine, vibe was right.

My only complaint is how early they close on Friday nights! 10 PM seems a little too early for me...BUT we did really enjoy this place! They had a unique beer selection and we enjoyed each of the drinks we had. I also really liked how they had games available, from old school games, to multiple darts boards. There was plenty of seating, from their two patios to the double stories. I also liked how you could look out into their brewery area and walk through it.

This place was crazy packed and extremely loud. When we walked in no empty tables or chairs were there. We listened live band music in standing. It was Friday late evening on Broadway, Nashville. The band was pretty good, even if it was not country music.

One of the better places to drink a variety of local brewed beer in town especially if you're a tourist staying in close proximity to downtown and don't want to venture too far outside the city to checkout other breweries like Fat Bottom (East Nashville) and would rather not sit in a big tourist trap like Big River. The beer is pretty good, some are a bit adventurous for my taste (Basil Ryeman), but I just don't like herbs in my beer. The full bodied and citrusy Southern Whit is top notch and for me the best they have to offer. The small, yet reasonably priced menu is probably the most "sophisticated" any local brewery has to offer. The sandwich section consists of a burger and hot dog gilded with boutique garnishments that would make a Whole Foods proud. The entrees are mostly French culinary standards masquerading as southern staples, but what it lacks in innovation and creativity it makes up for in value. The frog legs were eccentric, but tasty. Definitely worth checking out when you're checking out Nashville
The 5 beer burger and seasoned fries were ridiculously good. Cool vibe and the Travel Channel was shooting a special there while we were drinking so it has to be good!

Bridgestone is a great venue for concerts, as I've been here twice for the Maroon 5 and Bruno Mars concerts. 

I do agree with Sheena T. that musical groups don't sound so good performing live here. It was hard to hear the live performer because the music was way too loud. I went to a Bruno Mars concert at the Fox's Theater in Atlanta two years ago and the sounding was much better (Of course Bruno's singing is still godly!). However, the lighting was awesome! The lightning is what I love best about this place. 

I was lucky to grab floor seating for the Bruno Mars's concert. I was placed in these tiny chair closely placed next to each other. Although the chair was comfortable, I wish they didn't put the chairs so close together or get bigger chairs (I am pretty petite so that says something!). At the concert, this one obese lady was siting next to me and she literally sat on her chair and 30% of my chair...her "boyfriend" put his arm around her neck and kept hitting my shoulder (and tried to hit on me too -__-). I barely had room to stand or dance when standing up because she hogged the space (no pun intended). 

The food was average to me. My friend liked the fried chicken tenders a lot but I thought it was bland. Also, they don't let you carry water/soda in a bottle. Any drinks have to be put in a cup so the crazy fans can't throw the bottles around. 

Traffic is horrible every time there is a big event. Arrive here 1 hour early to avoid the traffic and find parking as most of the closer parkings are filled up quickly. I was late for the last concert and had to park 2 blocks away from Bridgestone (behind Hume Fogg HS) and it was pretty safe to walk. It costed $15 to park till the next day. 

2013/#72
Need to go see the bartender with the half shaved hair. Had a blast.  Great music great fun at the bar.

The BEST hot chicken sandwich EVER. I did not want it to end. My husband had the burger. It was almost as good as the chicken. Cool place, free parking, off the beaten path and good beer. Visiting from out of town and so happy we found this place through Yelp!

We were wandering around aimlessly downtown, looking for somewhere to go that has live music and good drinks. Jimmy Buffet's had an open area of seating and live acoustic music so we decided to stop in. There were 2 guys doing some cover songs which made for good background music. Buffet's music was everywhere...in the menu, written on the walls, on the tv, etc. Our server, Monte, was really nice and was on top of everything. I would give him 5 stars but I can only give Jimmy Buffet's 3 for being so mediocre. I ordered a cheeseburger and for almost $11, it was comparable to fast food. I ordered a hurricane which was very weak. This is a very touristy spot. As a local, I've learned my lesson and will try somewhere else for a good cheeseburger and stronger drinks. This place is nice for live music and people watching if you sit in the front out in the open.

I'm just going to go ahead and update my review (again) -- because every time I come here it gets better and better.  They have DARTS now!  And more TVs! And more patio! And live music!  And more beers!

Would love to see a few more darker beers on the menu -- the stout is fantastic, their season burbon aged is a gem too... would love to try a coffee porter from them!

TBW has quickly become our favorite brewery in Nashville.

Staffing people to prevent patrons from exiting at the end of a capacity event is unsafe. Minus one star for each of the two exits staff people told me I could not exit this past Tuesday. 

Minus another star when floor staff person asked me for tickets to prove my seats were on the floor, when half an hour earlier he had checked my tickets for our initial entry. That must have been the cause of the line. Hey ushers and arenas! It's not patrons fault paperless tickets are the norm and we don't have paper tickets in hand.

Minus another star for $20 for a double mixed drink (before tip).

Decent facility but price gouging, no arena parking, and ridiculous staffing make this a place in need of some improvement!
Nice place, cool vibe. Had lunch. Food is ok, not great but not awful. But the gnats! So many! Gnats in our faces, poking at our drinks, tasting our food.

I've been here a few times now, and each time I keep hoping it will be better, but it's just not.

The food is fine. Not bad, but not great either.  Pretty middle of the road.

The service is awful though.  Every server I've had hasn't been rude....they've just been non-existent!  Every time it's the same, it takes forever to even get drinks and then the server disappears completely.  The last time I was in it took 30 minutes to get a grilled cheese sandwich, and there were literally two other tables in the entire place.  That was after waiting 15 minutes for a mixed drink and another 15 to have the server come back and take our orders.  Just ridiculous.

I think by now I've finally learned my lesson and won't be back until there's a management or ownership change of some sort.
Fantastic brew pub. Great food, awesome beer, and fantastic service. I genuinely felt like the staff was committed to assuring I had a great experience.

Oh Winners, you fascinating little Midtown gem.  Many nights have been spent here, listening to karaoke (avidly avoiding the singing on stage part myself), enjoying buckets of cold brews, singing and dancing along with the crowds.  I always find it ironic that you're less crowded than your neighbor Losers, but you're always busy on a weekend night and you offer the fantastic Whiskey Jams on Monday nights, showcasing local talent and surprise guests.  

I can honestly say there has never been a night where I've come here and not been entertained or amused.  You're quick with the drinks, you have a great patio, and a prime location.  I'm not sure much else needs to be said.  You're a great little Nashville haunt, a fun place to go on any night; though I'd appreciate it if you outlawed the singing of slow songs after midnight (can we say fun sponging?).

'Bouncers' need an attitude check. My friend walked around the corner and swayed a little bit and we were thrown out. She didn't even fall. He probably wanted to look cool in front of his friends he was talking to.They are douche bags here.. I used to go here all the time and wouldn't step foot back in there again after how we were treated last night.

The Basil Ryeman is so unique I consider it a required tasting if you go there.  It has a great balance.  I would add the sweet potato stout to that as well.  I think it's called Southern Roots.  Probably the nicest brewery facility in town with lots of elbow room.
Lots of indoor or outdoor seating.

Southern as PBR.  Ok that's not completely accurate.  The atmosphere is decidedly music focused.  They have live music everyday and almost the entire time they are open, tip the performers - Lower Broad tradition is they all play just for tips.  

We stopped in for lunch with the kids.  The food was southern influenced and felt filling if not heavy on the stomach.  We opted to try several appetizers and share them at our table.  All were good and could have been a meal on their own.  

The bar was open and in full swing at 11am when we arrived.  If you enjoy a cocktail with your meal they have a fairly long list of options, along with several beers on tap.  

There is also a gift shop if you aren't hungry or thirsty you can always pop in and grab an Ole Red shot glass or tshirt.  

We are locals and this is one of those places we will return to for performances and when out of town guests come to visit.  A nice addition to the Lower Broad scene.  

The building is pretty fun too, google it.  It once housed a quite famous shop and now has 5 floors of space open via the Ole Red venue.
I've eaten at the original in Key West and this was pretty similar. The food and service were very good and I've been here several times. I would recommend this place for sure.

This bar, it made our night. The best lemon drop shots we've ever had, the bartender took her time squeezing fresh lemon juice for us at 11 pm on a Friday night. Thanks for a great time, be sure to come by this place. I wish I knew our bartenders name, she was the awesome.

This is such an amazing venue! It was beautiful, the acoustics were incredible, and no matter where you sat you had an awesome view! I'm very disappointed in myself for never having been before! This first trip was to see the Video Games Live concert. It. Blew. My. Mind! If they bring this back yearly, I think it could bring more interest from younger generations that don't have exposure to classical style orchestral music. It's safe to say that I will be attending more shows here in the future! 

The only problem is that I saw on the local news that the Schermerhorn is going into bankruptcy! Say it ain't so! Days after finding this gem I hear this terrible news! If the hall survives this I will certainly be buying season passes. The arts deserve our support, and make no mistake this is at at it's finest.

On the night I went they had free parking at LP field with a $3 shuttle to take you to and from the center. I don't know if that is for every show, but if it is, that's a great parking deal!

Also, for those that didn't know, free concerts in the park for the community are held during the summer. Check it out!

This is my favorite restaurant and every time I come there I am greeted by the hostess, Shacora. She is very pleasant and gives my family and I the best seating possible. She has a very great attitude which brings my family and I back everytime
Fantastic bar with great drinks! Live music! Bartenders Randi and Brandi were great! Great place to cool off in Nashville summer heat!

Winners really ought to post something, somewhere, on their website that says they're only 21+. With a website that promises a "great culinary experience", my boyfriend and I (who are 20 and were visiting Nashville) decided to try it out and catch some football/grab some lunch in December. We got there at noon, hardly anyone else there, and a waitress who didn't give us her name comes up and says, can I see your IDs? We were confused, but gave them to her and she says, "um, you people are too young. You need to leave right now." We were shocked, as a place marketing themselves as a bar and grill with a decent menu selection is rarely 21+ at all, let alone at noon. Total letdown, and even though we'll be over 21 next time we visit, we certainly won't be heading to Winners or Losers.

We sat on the 5th floor. We did not realize when booking our reservation that there was a limited menu on the top floor (appetizer only). This would be great if it was communicated when booking. We had the seafood platter, baked pretzel, burrata cheese. All decent, but nothing to brag about.  The crab legs were served with no claw crackers which made them very hard to eat normally. Could have used 2 more servers. Busy for a Saturday night so it took extra time to get drinks, silverware, and plates. This place is new so I will assume they are working out the details of running a successful roof top restaurant and bar in Nashville.

Proximity to the Ryman was the initial draw to this restaurant.  We had valeted the car there and with the frigid temperatures, we wanted something close by.  As soon as we stepped through the doors, we felt good about the choice.  
We were seated immediately and the life music was wonderful.    Our server was reasonably attentive and even told us about other events going on in the area.  
I ordered the shrimp trio and enjoyed it but since the grilled shrimp was my favorite of the trio, I was wishing that I'd just ordered those. 
It is definitely somewhere that we'll go again.

This is a tourist trap.  The reason this place is here and successful is because there is a steady stream of tourist in this town.  The food is terrible and the service is just as bad.  They are not worried about either because they don't have to worry about either.  Find another place to eat.  The food is nnnnnooootttt good.

Best part - the band played started at 9:30 and went almost until 1:00. They were great and kept the audience engaged. The dance floor was never empty - everyone heard something they could dance to. 

Service - we were a group of four and we were seated promptly after we walked in. We got lucky with timing and got a table right in front of the stage. 

Food service - was extremely slow and each round of food (appetizers and main course) ended up being served after a long period  waiting. Almost 45 minutes between our order and receiving the food. 
We also wanted to order dessert but when I tired to our server said they're not serving dessert anymore. I wish she informed us they were changing their menu. 

Food - decent shrimp dishes. Everything else tastes mediocre. 

Drinks - decent drinks although I've had better margaritas. Most of them ended up being more sour than I expected (blueberry margarita, watermelon margarita, tranquil waters, and last mango in Paris. )

Although it was a great place with a talented band, the service did not match up to it.

Lunchtime on a Thursday is a good time to go if you want quick service from the kitchen and immediate seating with live music while you eat. It is rustic inside yet very bright. There is a small gift shop just past the hostess stand with everything from growlers to dog collars for sale. There is also a huge upstairs balcony and bar area near the bathrooms. We were seated close to the main stage and our server took our drink orders very quickly. He seemed to hover a bit too much for our liking. Almost had to wonder if they thought we wanted to eat and exit in a rush, There were plenty of open tables and plenty of servers standing around. 

We had the pimento and cracker appetizer which was very good. Definitely all homemade and delicious. We then ordered the Barbecue Cobb Salad with pulled pork, and the Smoked Chicken dinner served with vinegar slaw, TN Buckshot Red Grits and pickles. I also ordered the local greens with pork shoulder side but there was only bacon mixed in and it was very spicy. Not pepper but something that made it very hot. The chicken was tender, juicy and fall off the bone and it was a big enough half chicken that there was leftovers. The Red Grits were very good and very rustic. The pickles were also very good. Some were very sweet and some were more dill but they were all mixed together. I liked that. We did enjoy our meal and would return, I just would not have Aaron as my server.
TIP: Portions are huge and shareable and if you don't finish, get it boxed to go as there are plenty of homeless outside who are happy to take the leftovers.

This was my first time coming to the Bridgetown Arena for a concert in Nashville. The venue was big enough for the band and honestly I had no idea who they were until my niece asked to go. 

They did have plenty alcohol options. Their food options were ok, what you expect at a music event. The staff were very professional and helpful. 

Great concert venue.

If I could give this place 0 stars I would. This week marked my second time eating there, and will absolutely be the last.

Food:

Had the chicken and waffles on my first visit. Chicken was really good, waffles were obviously frozen, bought in bulk from Sysco. This visit I decided to try their burger (which they claim was voted best in Nashville by a local publication. Unfortunately, there is no evidence online that supports that claim. So, liars?)

The burger patty itself was good. Quality meat, cooked to order, and decently seasoned. However, there was way way too much arugula, so everything just tasted peppery. Oh, and like onions. Probably because they put 3 rings of raw, red onion cut at least 3/4" thick. Now, I love onions, in any form, on or in pretty much everything. This was overkill and would have rendered the burger inedible if I hadn't removed it.

The fries were awful. Limp, soggy, hand cut wayyyyy too thick. The seasoning blend on them were delicious, but I was only able to force myself to eat 2 or 3. I guess that's okay, because I only got seven (7!!!!!) fries in my side order, which I substituted for chips.

Which brings me to one of the biggest issues I have with the food: the price. I ordered a bacon cheeseburger, with fries. The burger, which is normally $12, became over $18 by the time my bill came. $2 for bacon (that was not good bacon, too thin), $1 for one slice of American Cheese, and $2 extra for the horrendous fries described above.

Bar/Booze:

The bartender on duty both trips had NO idea what she was doing. Although she was sweet, we caught her consulting her phone and recipes behind the bar to make drinks that, quite frankly, any beginning barkeep should know. I stuck with beer this last time, and while I appreciate their variety of quality beers, $6 for a bottle of local Hefeweizen or $7 for a local Stout? Seriously?

Prices:

Even for the tourist trap that is Broadway, as touched on above, their prices are ridiculously out of line for the quality, decor, and service. $25+ for a burger, fries, and a (low-gravity) draft beer is robbery.

Decor/Interior:

Standard dive bar. Decent patio area. Non-smoking inside. Nice sized stage, but no one was playing either time we were there. TVs throughout, most on either sports or soap operas. Restrooms were small but clean. No soap in the men's room. And no paper towels, only a hand drier. Also, the lock doesn't work, apparently.

Management/Service:

First visit it was slow inside. Us (party of 3) and 2, maybe 3, other tables. Manager(?)/cook and bartender both sitting at the end of the bar, both eating and watching TV. The manager guy was smoking an e-cig and never once washed his hands before going in to the kitchen to (I assume) cook.

This second visit I was with 3 other people, all women. The bar was much busier, but we still got our drinks and food withing a decent amount of time. Ended up chatting with the owner and the door guy for a bit. He's the less famous brother of a C-list musician, and boy, is he something else. Alternating between rude and creepy/sexist. I won't delve into details, but suffice to say, this guy should stick to anything other than owning bars.

Overall:
Food: 3/5
Decor/Interior: 2/5
Service: 3/5
Prices: 0/5
Bar/Booze: 2/5

AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

Update: After talking with one of my female friends about this place and the review I posted, she told me that Joey, the owner, kept telling her about the expansion they're doing and asked her if she wanted to see the "upstairs". Like I said, creep.

Also, this dude mentioned his bar in New York more than once, so I decided to check them out on Yelp. Not only are they closed, but the reviews are pretty comparable to the ones on here. One even mentions their weird door guy, Sasha, by name. He's the guy who stands out front and catcalls women trying to entice people into the venue. I also just noticed this guy is featured on these Yelp reviews for NU. No surprise that they have to have employees leave positive reviews...

Insanely busy! But what would one expect from doing the "Broadway scene" in Nashville? Stood in line at the bar for about 15 or so minutes to get a drink when I asked a waiter that walked by if there's a quicker way to get a drink. He explained that we could take a table in the dining/ entertainment area. We took a table down front near the Dance Floor area. The band was great! The drinks were good and the service was reasonable considering how busy they were. In comparison to the Vegas Margaritaville it is much smaller, but all the bars on Broadway are pretty small in Nashville... At least the ones I saw and entered. The atmosphere was on point and I would most definitely go back again.

We were here on a Monday at lunch. The place was nearly empty when we arrived, and yet it took over 2.5 hours to complete lunch. The world's slowest service. Live country music (not one Jimmy Buffet song in the bunch). Sub-par food (stale chips, soggy chopped salad, taco meat worse than Taco Bell's). Good burgers and drinks.

Solid bar and grill. Ate dinner and had drinks during whiskey jam. Food was good, service was great too. Drinks weren't over priced nor was the bill. All alcohol wasn't under done, which made for perfect drinks.

I went with friends that are musician and were playing.  I got a Tuna Melt and it was okay nothing to complain about for the food.  What I did not appreciate was the drunk sound guy telling me the band sucks and that he hated the lead singer and like to "F@ck with her."  To get a drink I had to walk to the bar, but the bartender was a very sweet girl.
Had a great time. Food was good too. And we got to hear a live band. Service was great. Everyone was very cool. The place has a really nice vibe.

Simply beautiful.

This is the perfect home for the Nashville Symphony; a classy and very elegant space, with comfortable seats, great views and stunning acoustics.  It is hard to find a bad seat at the Schermerhorn, or to not enjoy the inside and outside of this remarkable campus.  This really is an exceptional venue space and Nashville landmark.

We came here for the first time to see Kathy Griffin, and we're already excited to come for a symphony performance or concert.  We found the ushers and staff to be helpful and friendly, and the interior of the building to be large enough to accomodate everyone comfortably, without long lines or that uncomfortable crushed feeling that sometimes accompanies venues like this.  The seats are tiered in such a way that everyone seated on the floor can see the stage easily, and the venue is small enough that no matter where you're seated, you can still see the faces of every performer and the strings on every instrument.

How lucky are we to have such a wonderful space to hear exceptional music and experience comedians, dancers and other entertainers?!  We'll definitely be returning.
Very new place to having good time!   Good for Drinks&Food and Music and Music and Music

Margaritaville is a great place to stop on Broadway for a sit-down meal with a full menu, without missing out on the fun of live music. My husband and I had lunch here while in Nashville and were not disappointed. The food was an appreciated change from hot chicken and tater tots that can be ordered at most bars on Broadway. The food boasted both quality and quantity; be sure to come here hungry! Our server Karah was super attentive and very pleasant. Overall this was an excellent dining experience, and we will surely be back our next time in Nashville.

OK, I've got to downgrade my score a bit after my second experience. 

Came in with a decent sized group after attending wine on the river, so I must admit that parts of this meal are slightly hazy. However, after doing a bit of detective work, I have pieced together my experience. 

What I remember: 
-Ordering a turkey burger and the famous potatoes on the side
-Having one well liquor drink
-The potatoes being extremely soggy and floppy

Fast forward to two days later. This is me checking my credit card statement:

"Holy $*&^ I spent $50 at National Underground?? How did that happen?"

Then the pieces started falling into place. 
-I picked up the tab for my BF (still. TWO burgers and two drinks- a beer and well vodka should not be $50)
-We had to buy BOTTLED water. That cost $2 extra per bottle. 
-There was an up charge for the potatoes that were floppy and not good

Yikes. That's a lot for a drunken meal that I half remember. I had a good experience the first time when I was a bit more coherent, so I'm definitely going to try and be a lot more careful when eating here. If it's late night, I'm choosing Broadway Brewhouse, and next year I think Mexican food is more appropriate for post wine on the river food.

LOVE THIS PLACE!!!  Tucked away in a neighborhood you wouldn't expect, but the place is nice and has awesome beer!  Definitely do a Beer Flight.  The Basil Ryeman is my favorite!  Service was good and to top it off, our server learned it was our anniversary and gave us our Pints FREE!!!  Great service and did a little extra with giving us a free pint of beer. We will definitely be back to imbibe some more with FANTABULOUS BEER!!!

Very inviting from the sidewalk with patio space for us ladies and our pup. The white whiskey moonshine was a good starter on a hot day especially on vaca. The service and food are also worth the trip.
Tour lasted less than 15 minutes, no excitement or enthusiasm from these brewmasters!

Atmosphere was great...as was the live music.  The food was just "ok." Not a very big menu.  Fried pickles and cornbread were our two favorites.  Also had the Fried chicken and pork cops...which were underwhelming.  The service was good and friendly...and relatively quick.  Would probably only go back for drinks and skip the food.
Beautiful venue, and excellent customer service.  Had a great experience hearing the Nashville Symphony play alongside Leann Rimes last night.  Would recommend to anyone to visit this place.
This place is cool til the bartenders shove you for trying to order hose water. I mean really, who gives a shit about being generally hydrated? -2 stars, would not go again.

We just went to the Rat Pack show, yesterday, and this was our first visit to the Schermerhorn Sympony Center.  The outside of the venue was very nice, with a courtyard for sitting and a small cafe / bar, just inside the venue.  In addition, it looks like each level has the ability to have bar service, although they were not open, yesterday, likely due either to it being Sunday or the fact that it was a 3p show.  

There were a number of volunteers eager to assist us along the way, and even to suggest things to tour and see prior to the show, since we were there a few minutes early.  We had seats in the balcony, which were pretty comfortable seats / leg room, and we were able to see the stage and experience the show quite nicely.  It was a wonderful experience!  We also ate lunch at the Farm House, and used their valet parking to simplify our trip to the symphony as well as to enhance our overall experience!

Came in for a tropical drink to beat the heat. The service was solid. Live music playing downstairs when I was there was good. Stairwell to the second floor is painted like a piano and responds to you touching it. That was a cool touch
Shane was awesome. He took care of us and made sure we had everything we needed. Great service and the food was amazing.
We love this brewery. Not only are all of their beers fabulous the food is amazing. Best burger in Nashville. It is a must!!
Typical Margaritaville. Slightly overpriced but dependable food and beverages. Good wait staff and the best guacamole ever!
The sign says "#1 burger in Nashville". Should say "worst burger in Nashville".  Gross and dry + stale bread.

Great rooftop bar downtown. I was meeting friends for drinks and an Emily Ann Roberts show and it was so fun. Watched the show and then went upstairs to the roof to hang with friends. They were super busy but it didn't seem overly crowded. We shared some apps and they were great. I would recommend Ole Red for any occasion. Oh, and the bartenders were super cool :-)

It's my own fault for coming in.  I mean, what was I expecting?  "Margaritaville".  Who the heck goes here when you're on music row in Nashville?  This idiot.  Revel in my tragedy.

Looking for a good beer?  Forget it.  Standard bud-lite garbage (you can salvage a Blue Moon out of the ordeal).  Good music?  Nope.  The guy (Dusty) was certainly personable and nice, but the selection (and I ended up seeing him play the next night and he was AWESOME) was super vanilla crap that you'd expect from a chain restaurant.  And, of course, they had to play "Margaritaville" while a guy on stilts danced around shaking a cardboard cutout of a salt shaker.  

The beers took so long to come out that we almost dipped out the large picture window (so as to avoid our dancing stilted friend), but I didn't feel like getting into trouble.  

Perhaps it wouldn't have been so bad had the entire experience not come with the opportunity cost of exploring another awesome bar in one of the nation's music capitals, but what can you do.  Well, you CAN just avoid this place, which I recommend.  If you're a tourist looking for a safe, generic, experience, here's your new haunt.

Bad customer service will always ruin a restaurant experience. My sister and I stopped in to The Underground for a morning snack during the CMA Fest going on in downtown Nashville. We wanted a mimosa or two and a bite to eat before the next concerts started, so at first we ordered waters, the unlimited mimosas for $20 per person, and an egg sandwich to split. 

We were given bottled waters - which we didn't realize we would get charged for, because who pays for water at a restaurant? We thought the bottles were just a friendly touch for festival attendees to be able to carry out with them, but our check let us know they were an unspoken up-charge. 

About halfway in to our first mimosa, we decided we actually just wanted the one drink each and asked our waitress to change our order in the system from bottomless to just one. She checked with her manager and told us that it wasn't possible to change the order. Having worked at restaurants, I know it is definitely possible to make a change like that to an order. 

The egg sandwich tasted good and was the only saving grace from the experience - until I went to the restroom and along the way saw the chef in the kitchen flipping fried eggs with his bare hands. 

When we were about to leave, it started pouring outside, and the manager was standing on the covered patio barking at pedestrians who wanted shelter from the 10-minute storm that they couldn't come in if they weren't paying customers. Amid that, my sister and I stood there waiting out the rain and I took out our water bottles that had been in my purse. The manager saw me and immediately started yelling at me that outside beverages were strictly not allowed in the restaurant because we might be carrying vodka or gin in the bottles. Thumbs up, guy; it's always a good idea to yell at your customers who just overpaid for watered down mimosas and had a below mediocre experience accusing them of sneaking in booze. 

Overall, worst restaurant I've been to in a very long time.
Cool music and great beer. They offer a variety of selections of craft beer to meet anyone's tastes. Highly recommend checking it out.

Excellent music. Accomplished young musicians. Girl fiddle player was good and the guy is an excellent guitar player. Local beers were available as well,which was a plus for me.
Found out the band were siblings and played as Jypsi
Bridgestone Arena has crammed the adjustable seats so close it's painful.
Overall the show was great and I liked the minimalism of the venue, but the security were pretty rude and overly aggressive.
The Nashville symphony is well worth the money and is a Nashville institution that never receives the credit it is due. A fabulous way to spend the evening.

Marathon Music Works is situated inside a revamped warehouse, so it's no surprise that the sound inside reflects that. The Ryman spoils all Nashvillians on sound quality.  It's very stylish inside, but I prefer substance to style. With all the great sound engineers in town, MMW should bring one in to evaluate the acoustics. They weren't terrible, but there's room for improvement. 

The drinks are fairly priced and if you hit the right bartender, poured well too. Consistency left something to be desired...my drinks ranged from stingy and sadly poured to very strong like I make at home. 

Bring cash! The tab system looked complicated and I overheard complaints about minimum charges and service fees that were applied. Management should institute a cash only line to keep things moving.

I've visited Bridgestone Arena on multiple occasions for various different types of events.  There is literally not a bad seat in the house when it comes to watching a sporting events such as the Nashville Predators or a concert.  Bridgestone is a world class arena that attracts premier talent and performances.  The event staff and ticket office staff is always extremely helpful when it comes to finding your seats or putting you in the right direction.  They always have awesome promotions going on during the Predators game such as free merchandise and vouchers.  If you're ever in the downtown area and looking to kill some free time stop by and check out the Tennessee Sports Hall of Fame located near the main entrance of the arena.

It's five o'clock somewhere! Stopped by here just to shop but the bar looked so good we decided to take Jimmy Buffet's motto to heart. The shop is nice and has a lot of good stuff for parrot heads alike. 

The restaurant has really good food. Just about everything on the menu is eatable. The bar is what we came for. Lots of tropical drinks and beers for all to enjoy. Stop in to shop and drink if you are on Broadway!
I liked this pub a lot!! Fun bands, seating, good crowd, decent drinks.  Pop in while you're on the strip, take a listen to some bands and enjoy!  Great place for day drinking!

We stopped in late on a Saturday night to check it out and the line wasn't too long to get in, so we headed in. It gets super packed downstairs and the bar line was really long so we scooted past that and headed upstairs which we found to be pretty empty on the second level. I would definitely bypass the downstairs bar and head upstairs and you can look over the balcony and watch the band. We headed up to the rooftop as well... it's a lot of stairs! The rooftop was beautiful and not super busy. You can see all of Broadway and across the river, and look at all the other bars that are jam packed with people and be happy you have some breathing room.

My only issue was the inconsistent pricing at this place. I ordered two shots at the second floor bar, two lemon drops, and the total was $22. When I went up to the 3rd floor, I ordered two more lemon drops and two Bud Lights and my total was $28. I was paying cash, so I feel like the guy pocketed a bit of that money, and they obviously don't give you a receipt. So I don't know if I would go back with the fear of being ripped off each time I went to the bar.

Like the name suggests, there are wonderful margaritas available here! Also, I love Jimmy Buffett's song so it was awesome to be inside one of the locations. 

As soon as we sat at the bar, we were greeted by the Bartender and he promptly checked on us during our entire time at Margaritaville. 

We had the Margarita flight for $15.75, all the samples were delicious. I ended up drinking their frozen mango margarita with an extra shot, yum! They had live music the entire time we were there drinking. The ladies performing did a fabulous job, very talented! 

I purchased a margaritaville shirt that says "take life with a lime, salt and tequila" - love it! It was a little over priced $25 but I still got it haha. 

The bathrooms were clean which is always a plus. All in all, I had a wonderful time!

Not too crowded, great food, great decorations, tremendous live band, and fantastic food selections for people! I had the veggie burger - and then to watch a band play some "real" sounding country music was cool! Wait staff works pretty quick and also ID is checked at the door. Great time, I recommend it!
Bologna sandwich on trio is gross! Looks more like a prison sandwich (as I would imagine). Come on- get a little more creative!!

Great staff. Solid beer selection. Croque Madame was outstanding. 

Out of the way but worth the trip.
True country honky tonk dive bar. Cold beer and good music all day and night. Really liked all the license plates.

We had an excellent experience on Sunday 4/16 at Margaritaville.  Everyone was so friendly and nice.  Our server Madison was one of the best servers I've ever had.  He made excellent suggestions for types of beer my husband would like and was so helpful and attentive.  Add all that to the Caribbean vacation vibe and you've got a recipe for success.

The music was great, family friendly environment, good location.  Bowie was our wonderful server,  gave us advice on things to do with our 16yr old daughter.  We ordered the volcano nachos that can feed about 6 people. The only thing I would say could be better are the bathrooms.  Writings all over the walls, and the faucet falling apart. The whole place really could use some serious renovating. I guess what you may expect from more of a bar scene.  Nashville is growing at a rapid pace, construction is everywhere.  But businesses must be booming, We will definitely be back!

LOVED every single thing! Excellent beer (the Wit and the triple belgian) and $5 a pint is a steal!! Husband had the hot chicken French toast and raved. I feasted on the house burger and am sad it's gone!! Excellent value and quality. Can't wait to go back!

Both our friendly hostess and our nice waitress (Colleen) were quick and helpful.  Nonetheless the recommended Margarita was super sour, although Colleen gladly replaced it. Cajun chicken Caesar salad provided chicken so dry it seemed like jerky.  The medium-cooked burger was so overcooked, it was like a hockey puck.  My daughter enjoyed her veggie burger while my fried chicken salad was fine.

Cool space, but I wasn't a fan of their beers. My group got a taster flight and nothing really stood out to any of us. Maybe we chose the wrong beers? The place had a few people in the afternoon but I imagine at night it could get buzzin'. Looks like they had a solid food menu, but I didn't get to try anything.

Marathon is bringing some my favorite bands through lately. It's large, but not so large that I feel lost in the crowd. And Robert is the bomb! Saw Devin Townsend last night (someone I never thought would come through Nashville) and I'm giddy!

Wow! I never write reviews, good or bad, so imagine my frustration with this place to actually take time off my busy schedule to write a review.  The blond and brunette female bartenders were the rudest and most racist people I have ever met in my life. I am so disappointed at the way they treated our group.  We were a very diverse group with people of all backgrounds and based on how we were treated, one can deduce that if you're any other race than white, stay away from this place!!! It's awful being discriminated against even though you speak the same language as they do and were born and raised in this country, just like they were.  They lost our business and we will NEVER go back there because they don't deserve our business.

As a former usher at the Schermerhorn, my review may be a bit biased. But this place is just absolutely spectacular. Management and customer service is killing it (with kindness) and the cleaning staff is very detailed and thorough. 

From the classical concerts, to modern artist accompanied shows, to the kids days on the weekends...the Schermerhorn hits it out of the park every time.

Just another Margaritaville.  A happy atmosphere and a selection of burgers and fish dishes. Only difference is that this is Nashville so expect music most of the day. Tonight I am listening to a duo called Triple Run. Drinks are good and the service is always very good. Not gourmet but good Americano food. Prices are on the high side, but, in line with all of the other establishments on Broadway strip. Of the many venues in this 2 block area, this location is a classy stop compared to the other bars. Not a bad stop for a drink and some laughs.

I live in Nashville and for the "downtown scene" I think the Beer is cold, the music is great but the bartender with pigtails is always a turd. The prices are also never the same for the same 2 beers.

Skip this place. Nachos were NOT good. Prices are somewhat ridiculous for a tourist place when you compare the food and service. Get off this street and visit a local place with real food and better hospitality. Jimmy Buffett would be disappointed.

I've been here several times for Predators games and have a blast every time! There's honestly not a bad seat in the house. There's $10 parking close by or if you're persistent or arrive early, you can usually find street parking depending on how popular the game is. And I just read there's free parking at the Nissan stadium?! Awesome!

On Thursdays, they have half-priced beers until the 1st intermission I believe. And if you're a pass holder, it's half-price for the whole game!

If you're seated in the Fan Zone area, there's a station that serves FREE popcorn, nachos, hot dogs, a rotating hot entree and soda. Unheard of bargain for a sports arena!

Seats can be small and the walk areas are NARROW. So plan accordingly if you're a klutz like me. (Hint: No high heels!)

Now, my one pet peeve is if you order your tickets online not directly through ticketmaster but through a third-party, they MUST be printed. You cannot use the online ticket to scan in. I've been turned away from a game before and had to run down Broadway to the nearest Kinko's just to print out my ticket. Lesson learned!

Overall, great venue and a great time!
While visiting Nashville, my boyfriend and I got some tickets to a Predators game! Decent beer, great looking food (we ate before), and a fun, fun game! Great way to spend an evening in Nashville!

One of my new favorite breweries. I loved the Walk the Lime Bourbon Barrel which was my first bourbon barrel to enjoy!! I loved the industrial feel and the food looked good. The bar manager told us about the brewery on our "tour" and was very helpful.
You have to stop by have some drinks and unwind to a good evening you have to stop by here good food good people good friends stop on my
Awesome atmosphere and if you get a chance to se what's going on you will not be disappointed. They are doing something special here and worth a trip to whiteness history in the making!

Love this place! Great beer, fun environment,  and good food (get the nachos)! I only wish that the live music wasn't so loud. Sometimes you just wanna hang out and be able to talk but the live music is always so loud here.

Very nice venue. Very clean. Nice staff. Here for a Predator's game. Lots of good food choices. Lots of alcohol choices. I wish they had not passed out those STUPID clapping sticks. Extremely annoying and rude. A pin would be really nice about now. The game is great and having fun despite the sticks. 
Scott Hamilton is here tonight. Fun to see a celebrity in the crowd. 
Definitely needed to dress warmer. Lol

This brewery is top notch. They have games upstairs (jenga, connect four, etc.) and a dart board room, which I imagine could get potentially dangerous in the hands of an aggressive person. Pints are $5 served up in a tulip glass. Brews are pretty good; IPA is my favorite. Definitely located in a somewhat shady area, but if you could get past that you're in for a real treat.

Spectacular.  The building is beautiful, the range of types of events hosted here is fantastic, the Nashville Symphony itself is wonderful, the parking isn't bad, and there are boozes and baked goods. 

I've been here 3 times now for 3 very different events. Whether it's the actual Nashville Symphony, a singer accompanied by the symphony, or a keynote speech, the Schermerhorn is basically perfect.

The Nashville hot frog legs were amazing! I love frog legs, but the hot chicken seasoning brings them to the next level. I really like this venue as well.. nice layout with indoor and outdoor seating on 2 levels; just a really cool and open plan. The beer is on point as well.

Very nice bar and venue. We visited for a local artist and I was very impressed with this place. The staff was nice and the place was clean and newly renovated. They even have valet and well my husband and I had a few to many drinks and ended up riding home with a friend and they was kind enough to understand and let me keep my car there over night and went back the next day and it was just like I left it.
5 stars just for the courteous service by Adam who was running the front register. TBW is well worth the visit!

Very nice venue but parking was a nightmare. Over an hour to drive 3 blocks to the prepaid parking space we bought from Ticketmaster (Pinnacle Parking) ZERO traffic control. Give yourself extra time or better still, treat yourself to a nice meal at one of several restaurants and use their valet for the event - two for one! (Just pick your car up before they close.)

If there was an option to leave 0 stars, I would select it. Absolutely terrible service. It took them 50 minutes to get my burger ready. I complained to the manager and he was very unapologetic. My friends ordered a quesadilla and fish and they were out of both. The food was good, but because of the awful service and the attitude of the manager the experience was my worst ever. I feel like they discriminated against us as well because of our young age (21). They treated the older people behind us a lot more kindly. I would not recommend this to anyone.
Got drunk here and picked up a 10 ( two 5's).  The downside of this place is they got one pisser. My type of spot.

Great experience! Redneck Nachos are the bomb!  Great service, Destine was awesome.  I'm sure this place gets a little crazy in the evening, but we loved our experience on a Weds afternoon for an early dinner before heading to Memphis!

Rarely do I go with four stars without eating but this is one of those times. How can you go wrong with a margarita at a place called margarita like margaritaville?? The reason this place is getting 4 stars is the music! We followed Matt Rausche and Jet Huffman from Baileys. We couldn't get enough of them while eating outside at Merchants, great food!!! They charmed me....Anyways, it's a typical margaritaville and the bartender is attentive and pleasant, bathroom is clean too. The decor is chain but not over done or old per se. I'll be back in sure. Alright, I've been here almost 3 hours! Not once did a server ask if we were OK!!! I'm still in love with the band but the service definitely missed out... The band got a round, the bartender got tipped... They got nothing!!!!

When you are in town you have to stop by Margaritaville because it's well-known, and you got to try one of their best margarita flavors!!!  Well, we did and I was not impressed.  First of all, the glasses were so small (8oz) for $10, it was filled with alot of ice cubes and almost no room for the actual beverage.  There were four of us, and after our second round, we asked if they have a pitcher that we could buy and they don't.  I think the restaurant should consider selling them in a big pitcher, we would be more likely to hang around and buy more food and drinks.  

I have had better experienced at other Margaritaville in Key West and in Vegas.

So I was all set to give 1 star cuz the hostess has no clue what "reservation" means. My self and another couple were complaining about walk-ins getting seated while we stood there waiting. But anyway...I had a burger (I love burgers). The locally sourced beef had a great flavor. With the pimento cheese, lettuce, onion, and tomato - excellent burger. The drinks were really good and fair priced compared to the expensive mixed drinks on Broadway. I had a cherry lime-aid cocktail with a big surprise: a moonshine soaked cherry! Very good drink. My wife enjoyed he white sangria (it is Blake Sheltons place after all). So overall the band, drinks, wait staff, and food more than made up for the clueless hostess.

If I had a nickel for every time I'd been to Bridgestone.. well, I'd probably only have like a dollar & a quarter, but you get what I'm saying. Bridgestone is a pretty nice arena. We used to come a lot for hockey games, not so much this year. Hockey is an entertaining sport to me because there's always something going on. Also, a drink will keep you warm in the arena, & who doesn't love a drink. More on their drinks later. 

We park in the "R" lot which is located across the river, next to the Titans stadium. They open the lot for events at Bridgestone. They've got a website with the dates it's open. A simple google search of "R lot Bridgestone" & you should find it. They run a shuttle that is 3 bucks a person (cash) but if you're cheap like me, you'll make the short walk across the pedestrian bridge to Bridgestone. 

We stopped in a few weeks ago for Amy Schumer. We had floor seats, which were located towards the back from the stage. Luckily, they had plenty of large screens & cameras on her. Speaking of cameras, if they say "no cell phones, no cameras" they mean it. I bet I counted like 25 people getting removed for trying to take pictures. Security is no joke.
