I had no issues with security except for when Amy was taking to a heckler they were trying to remove. One of the security officers came up quickly to my boyfriend who was on an aisle seat. We both thought he was getting onto us for something, but he was asking what was going on up front by the stage. Ummm, we don't know & we won't know now because he was talking to us about it. Don't they have walkie-talkies to figure that stuff out? 

Anyway, drinks are pricy. I wouldn't dare by more than one because I'd like to keep some money in my 401k. If you're smart like me, you'll have a couple drinks beforehand, or warm boots that allow for collapsible flasks. Oh I kid, I kid.

I'm not a fan of bars downtown, especially in the more tourist areas but this has to be my favorite bar downtown by far. There's usually a decent band on the stage and it can get pretty lively on a Saturday night but not too crazy. Service is always really hit or miss, but I never have huge expectations. They serve hot dogs outside and not going to lie, they definitely hit the spot after a drunken Preds game. And you can't go wrong when you offer bluegrass music!

Love the vibe of this place - well decorated brewery with good beers and amazing food. Their 5 beer burger is one of the very best in town. However, I give this place 4 stars because of their food prices. $15 for a burger and fries at a brewery is very steep. The veggie burger is $18. Taking a few dollars off each food item would be perfect. I still go, but I have to "splurge" and plan on it. If it was a little more affordable, I would come much more often.
A quality music venue to see some real honky tonk. I visited here several times on my trip after realizing some other places in the neighborhood aren't what they say they are. Layla's holds true.

My fiancé and I like to travel to different hockey stadiums and this one impressed us because it was nicer, newer, and more spacious than a few others we've been to. I'm giving 5 starts just for the fact it was a memorable experience and a great overall weekend in Nashville. I got to see my buddy play against the predators and I loved the fact we could walk to the stadium since its in the heart of DT, no uber necessary. 

Great atmosphere as well but not better than the untied center.
Nice bar with live music and a cool gift shop right in the heart of Nashville.

I rarely write reviews when traveling but this food is absolutely terrible. There's a nice man wrangling people in with the audacious claim "best food in Nashville"( and that's why I went in, so good for him I guess) , but that is honestly the most outlandishly inaccurate statement that could possibly be made. Stay away. Beer served in 12 Oz plastic cup too...

Atmosphere - ok
Food - not worth it.

Ordered fried chicken and pulled pork.

Everything was ok, looked like it sat under a salamander for too long.  Coleslaw smelled like the dumpsters you walk past when not walking Broadway.   Just not the best...

Would love to meet the executive chef and see him eat this coleslaw...  Disgusting...

Decent experience, nice gift shop.  A definite tourist trap, very pricey weak drinks.  Didn't have a margarita, but probably should have, they did look good.  Service, average.  Female bartender borderline rude.  Not likely to stop back w/an option every two doors.
Nice place in the middle of abandoned buildings.  Interesting selection of beers.   Extra easy was the fav.  No food but gourmet popcorn for purchase.   Lots of seating and clean large restrooms.

The best beer ever!!! Not just in nashville... The best beer I've ever had. I really fun location really close to Broadway there taproom is great you can get growlers from them. I recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville. I can't wait until I can buy in stores.

I attended the Journey tribute.  I had an awesome time.  The singer was exceptional.  The symphony played well.  It was sad to see this wasn't a sell out event.  Come on Nashville!! Support your symphony!!! You be got a great asset here.

Beautiful bar food was okay nachos a little too salty and a weird combo for me I got the chicken biscuit and it was awesome loved the homemade tater tots and the mash were delicious if I came to dinner I would of tried to get the cauliflower steak as it sounded awesome and weird at the same time
Down falls we're the wait server took forever to greet and take order felt like it was about 20 min and food didn't come for another 45 and we were getting a little hangry

Best Brewery in Nashville. Haven't had a beer from here that I didn't like. My favorites are the Cutaway IPA and Southern Wit. Haven't tried out there food yet, but I heard it's awesome too. 2-1's on Wednesday's doesn't hurt either.

So many places to choose this looked nice. Plus comfy air conditioning inside to escape unusual warmth for October. Good band playing at lunchtime. Nice menu, lots of options.. burgers, salad, famous fir their huge nachos platter. Sit near the front and hear the band or way in the back ( as we did) where it's cool and relaxing.  Ordered the taco salad and my husband had a chicken sandwich.  Taco salad is excellent! Chicken sandwich good too! Glad we stopped in

My wife and I went here on Thursday 6/26 while exploring downtown on our honeymoon. We were seated very quickly despite the place being extremely busy. Our server was excellent and very prompt. The atmosphere was very nice and the musician was very talented. Here's our problem. We ordered the Valcano nachos and the pretzels which alone came up to $23.00. I can understand that being a touristy restaurant and in a downtown area that the prices are going to be inflated but the real issue was that not long after we left and were heading back to our hotel we both became sick. We have to assume it was the nachos because I didn't have but 1 bite of the pretzels. Not only did we have to spend the whole evening/night in our room but it ruined plans that we had. Our total bill with the 2 appetizers and 2 teas came to $36.00. I'm not sure where the other charges came from but it definitely was too much money to spend to end up sick and miserable.

I went there on a Saturday night and it was a seat yourself setup. I sat in the upstairs part of the restaurant. I ordered the wings and their menu sangria. BOTH WERE DELICIOUS! Hands down the best sangria I've ever had. They also had a live band playing and they were great! Our server was great too!

I'm not too sure why they've gotten the "best burger in Nashville" award because really, their burgers were at best, mediocre. I definitely don't think their prices are great, over $14 for a burger (extra cost for bacon and cheese!) and even a charge for fries! Not just that, I barely even got a handful of fries (9 to be exact) and they just weren't that good. 

The wait for my ridiculous, over 45 minutes and there is was hardly anyone in here. It's constantly loud and I feel like everyone is yelling at one another. Also, it was rather cold in there and no one seemed to want to do anything.  

Overall, I'm not overly satisfied with this place. Not worth it.

Nice place to visit and staff was professional and friendly. Got seated quickly and place was clean. Drinks were cold and well made. However, food was sub par at best. 
No flavor to the coleslaw and the "Hot" chicken sandwich on biscuit was very disappointing. Not spicy in the least and the biscuit was dry and just fell apart. 
The only reason why I am giving it 2 stars and not one is the band they had playing last night was outstanding. Very difficult to carry on a conversation while they played but that was ok. We were even upstairs. 
Will go back, but not for the food.

Bad food. Sad service. Only bottled water ( no tap water).

Seriously, just walk to ANY other restaurant and you'll be better off.

That's all.

I love Blake Shelton but, this bar is not typical Broadway.  We were disappointed because there's no where to listen to the band.  You have to sit at a table. Even upstairs you can't see the band.  So, people are just sitting there.  No one is getting into the music.  Boring. Then we walked past a messy ally full of garbage cans both times we visited it.  Disappointed.

Cool bar/restaurant, def a must. Destinie was a gem, wonderful server and made sure the busy day went as smoothly as possible. Long wait for food, under staffed but overall glad to have been abele to check it out!

Mixed experience. Courtney on the second floor did a great job as our server. She was friendly even though you could tell she was tired; our order came quickly and was accurate. The security staff is very professional and promptly solved some situations that could've gotten out of hand. Unfortunately, hostess team at the rooftop was another story. I put my name on list for a table of 2 and got the confirmation text at 8:06. We went to 2nd floor to listen to music and wait it out. And hour and 15 later I went upstairs to check on table and was told I had been seated already. I never even got a text that table was ready. There was no apology no explanation and no table.  I hate to say the music was a disappointment. There were 2 bands and they both sounded like amateur karaoke. Much better music out on Broadway.  There were 2 other couples next to us and they were shocked as well. 
On flip side, it was very clean, not too packed and we were able to seat on a couch for several hours and watch the myriad bachelorette and bachelor parties.  A different Broadway experience. Good if you're hungry or want a place to chill.

Ordered food and beer.  Had to sign a waiver for "hot" chicken. It was hot but not waiver worthy hot.  Asked for another beer it never came got check left. I am with everyone else not worth going back.

Winners Bar & Grill is the crossroads for locals, college students and musicians. This dive bar is located right next to their sister bar, Losers. The venue isn't much of a looker, but they do have a covered patio with a bar outside and inside is another bar and high top tables. Whether you're here for karaoke on the weekends, live music or just to have a "bootwacker" (just try it, its good) there is a good time to be had here. Admittedly this is not my favorite place to just come hang out but the reason I'm giving them 4 stars is for hosting Whisky Jam. 

Whisky Jam is held every Monday night at Winners. This is definitely one of the coolest live music experiences you can have in Nashville. Famous artists, (Melissa Etheridge, Chris Stapleton, Kasey Musgraves, etc.) rising stars and local bands have performed here, so you never know who may show up! They do have a set schedule for each Monday of the performing artists. The night that we went we were coming to see a specific local artist and the lineup started about 30 minutes late meaning that we actually ended up having to miss seeing him because it was after 11 pm when he came on (hey some of us have to work the next day). We did see a few bands I had never heard of which is always very cool to discover new music. They set up a stage near the entrance by the windows of the place and indoors it gets jam packed with people. In between bands, there were 2 MCs trying to entertain the crowd (unfortunately failing miserably) but they were giving out free beer, so that definitely made up for their fumbling words and awkward conversation. If you can look past these small misgivings then you will enjoy yourself. 

Do yourself a favor and check out Winners for Whisky Jam. You will be #winning at Winners for this truly Nashville experience.

It has now been over 2 months. After my last post, I recieved an email requesting my phone number from the kitchen manager to which I immediately responded. I still have not heard a word.  It definitely shows that they could have cared less what I went through because they have no intention of ever addressing the issue. I guess lessen learned. When your at Margaritaville,  don't order the food unless you don't mind being sick for 3-4 days, just order the Margarita's!

While the interior of the building is nice, the patio is great (minus the view), and the employees are friendly, the beer itself is nothing to write home about. My wife and I got flights here, and nothing was very memorable. I had come here intending to get a growler of whatever I liked best, and I left without one at all.

This is without question the best brewery in Nashville. We did our best brewery crawl, and TBW was by far and a away the best spot. They use local ingredients to make sure their beers are representative of Tennessee. Also, the food is amazing. Just like the ingredient for beer, they make sure the food is locally sourced and delicious.

Bridgestone has me torn in two, I hate seeing concerts here (I blame Nashville, with its spoiling me with excellent musical venues) but I enjoy me some hockey games.  The staff is always helpful, even when the place is crazy busy, and they have a lot of places to acquire food and booze throughout the arena.  So I'm giving you, Bridgestone, 3 stars, because for concerts you get a 1, and for Preds games you get a 5.
 
Unless you can manage to get stellar seats (in which case, lucky you) music just doesn't sound as good at Bridgestone as, say, the Ryman or 3rd and Lindsley.  If you want a decently-priced seat you're most likely sitting in Knoxville (aka your head is hitting the Bridgestone ceiling).  I've been here many times for shows, and even sitting close (on those days when it was lucky me) it just doesn't sound as good.  But I've been spoiled here, and I'm not denying that.  Nashville has so many great places to see acts...even strolling down Broadway on a weekend night you see people playing in the street who are good.  But there's something about Bridgestone that I can't put my finger on...it just doesn't translate into great shows.  I'm hard pressed to go when I can spend the same amount for a nosebleed seat that I do for local music festivals or up and coming acts (that end up at Bridgestone eventually).
 
But for some reason this does not seem to be the case with hockey games, or other events held at Bridgestone.  Maybe it's the energy in the crowd, and fans get riled up to support their hockey teams.  There are entire sections in the third tier filled with rabid fans that make your night more fun.  
 
The arena being downtown, be prepared to park and walk, and pay a lot for the privilege, especially since the paid lots are more pricey on event nights.  The food is typical fare for arenas, but the staff are always nice and willing to help.  I don't beat down the door to get to events at Bridgestone, but I don't mind going.  If your favorite 80s bands are there, it will be crowded but by all means go and have fun.  See the Predators play if you haven't already.  And it's downtown, so once you've paid an exorbitant amount of money to stash your car someplace take advantage and stay out.  I guess what I'm saying is that you won't be upset for taking in something at Bridgestone, but it may not be the best show you've ever seen either...unless its hockey, then its always awesome.

Jasmine and Beth were very helpful!!!! The food was great!

We had a party of 7 and the food was brought out quickly and hot. Everybody left happy and well nourished.

If I could give this a place 0 stars, I would. Horrible, horrible, horrible service. Our waiter, Clarence, was TERRIBLE. It took him over 20 minutes to come to get our orders. After he took our orders, he brought our drinks and waters out relatively quickly, then disappeared for an hour and 15 minutes without once checking in on us. We were seated upstairs, and we attempted to get the attention of a waiter before a manager finally came to check in on us. We described the situation to her, she told us our meals would be compensated for, and then Clarence came out with our food shortly after (we waited for almost 2 hours). The food was cold, as if it had been sitting out and forgotten about for a while. Clarence was unapologetic this entire time and did not seem to understand why we were upset. We waited an additional 30 minutes for our bills to be brought out, only to see that we were being charged for everything. It took us another 15 minutes to get Clarence's attention, he told us he would correct the bills. We waited for 20 minutes before getting frustrated and heading downstairs to speak to a manager about the ridiculously poor service. Clarence appeared out of nowhere and chased us down the stairs. Overall, horribly disappointing experience. I will definitely not be back.
Service was not rude, but was not the most friendly either. The cheeseburger and Bloody Marys more than made up for it. Water consists of a $2 bottle so beware if you're expecting a free drink.

Well the place wasn't initially all that bad. The singer of the band playing told a paying customer to basically "f-off" when she requested a song and to put money in the tip jar.   In all fairness she looked annoyingly drunk, but it's important to always remain professional. Lastly they closed at 2 which was an hour earlier than everyone else and they didn't even sound for a last call.  So we stand at the bar for close to 5 minutes waiting for my card and our check and we are being ignored until one of the bartenders turns and tells us they're closed. I reply that I waiting for my card and she goes t retrieve it. In the meantime a busboy rudely shoves past us and exclaims for us to get out that they are closed. By this point I'm fed up with he rudeness of the staff trying to corral everyone out and telling me to leave before I can even get my tab closed. I don't leave a tip to make my point of being dissatisfied with being ignored for the last 20 minutes of our visit. As we are walking down the street the waitress chases us down to explain she "works for tips".  Well that's funny because I tip for work. Try having your staff not be so rude at closing time.
Absolutely great spot that I have not been here in a year. The food menu is great and the service is smart and friendly. Awesome beer and very great atmosphere !!!!

I usually only post positive reviews because I understand a restaurant can have an off day but this was the worst food I have ever had.  I had the southwest salad.  It didn't look appetizing, the lettuce wilted,  bland and I don't know what kind of dressing it had on it.   My friend had a taco salad and said the meat tasted terrible.  

On top of all that, it took forever and this was at 2:30 pm on a Friday when the restaurant was slow.

One positive the nachos were okay.  They looked good but not much flavor.

The beer is great no questions. But the customer service is what won me over. They were slow with our food and when I inquired the lovely girl at the taps rushed downstairs then rushed back and informed me that they dropped our food going up the stairs. So Adam (manager) brought us a couple free beers and said they were covering our entire tab which included probably 4 or more beers. All in all Adam and the gang at TN Brew Works understand beer and business and deserve to succeed in every way!

Solid solid bar! Great food!!! cheap ass drinks, great bartenders. Did a one hit wonder on karaoke night when i was wasted. I wish this place was around me because I would be there once a week. Awesome Nashville spot

Not a bad seat in the house! Gorgeous building, efficient and friendly staff who stop at nothing to make the experience amazing. I think this building may make even me sound good, but let's not put us all through that torture! There is nothing more I can say other than you must try it!
Thanks so much national underground for the amazing experience. Great food and wings I am from california and we had a amazing experience will took great care of us. Great ambiance great drinks.

Beautiful venue, great acoustics and friendly staff. I went to see REO Speedwagon here back in October and had a great time. Prices for tickets were very reasonable and we had a good view from the orchestra level towards the middle of the room. Drinks were reasonably priced and I believe they had a cafe type place as well but we did not purchase anything. The best part, aside from the concert itself, was the amazing staff. Everyone I encountered was very friendly and helpful! I look forward to seeing another concert or possibly the symphony here in the future!
Tennessee Brewing! Hard to find, worth the effort! Cool old building. Beer was great!  Hot Nashville chicken sandwich was great. The artisan cheese board app was excellent.

Food was flavorful, music performer was amazing. Great atmosphere, the decor was nice and classy/rustic. The Poutine was really delicious, as was the peanut butter ice cream (a must try!). Our server was busy (as it was 4th of July) but she was as attentive as she could be, very nice and welcoming. One star was deducted because the chocolate cake was not moist, not very good. But would have the peanut butter ice cream on it's own for sure!

This is an insanely cool venue. This venue serves as a brewery, a live music hub, and a place to grab a couple of beers with good friends after work. All of their beer is made locally - you can actually take tours of the distillery on sight and walk out onto the floor - and try it before you buy a pint. If you want to try them all, they've also got an awesome beer flight option. It's a really cool open space with great indoor and outdoor seating, so it's perfect in any weather. I would highly recommend - already looking forward to my next trip!
Love live music in a comfy place with no smoke and great drink options?  Come on down!!!  Fun atmosphere, and easy to get to.  So nice to just be able to sit and enjoy great tunes!

Overpriced Sysco food is about the only way to describe it. Our server was terrible and paid very little attention to our table. My wife and I both had two different frozen margaritas and could not taste tequila in any of them. We will not be going back to this location or any others.
Funny thing, sent email nearly 3 weeks ago as requested and haven't heard anything. Must not matter one way or the other.

Nashville's Bridgestone Arena is an extremely well managed sports, music, and event venue. Although it's getting on in age (built in the mid 90's), it's been updated well and offers great concessions (including local craft beer!) in addition to pretty good seating. If you've got the scratch, I recommend sitting in the club level, as you'll have access to better dining options and actually get a waiter for your section, so you can spend more time enjoying your event and less time waiting in line for concessions.

This place kicked me out tonight. The "owner" came up to me and said I was a "homosexual" and that they don't allow that at the bar. I had done nothing that portrayed a homosexual manner. I went up to the bartender and asked if he was really the "owner" like he claimed to be and she said "no, just ignore him." Then he came up to me and again told me to get out, and the bar tender was like "yeah, you need to leave." The guy continued to harass me and yell at me to get out of "his" bar. I've never been in this situation before and don't plan on ignoring it. Gavin Degraw, who I love, is apparently the actual owner and did NOTHING about it.

While waiting for the 98 degrees concert to start at Ryman down the street (yes that's right!), we decided to get a couple of drinks on Broadway. I didn't want to bother with the overly loud crowds of some of the more famous bars so we decided, why not? Let's try it! We typically try to avoid chain restaurants but we wanted a margarita.

It was actually really relaxing. We sat at the bar and of course they had live music. But they didn't just play country music. They were also really engaging.

My favorite Margarita was called perfect margarita (something like that) it was about $9-10 but it was so worth it. It was so much stronger than their regular margarita and it wasn't as sweet.

This place is huge, too. They have a really big dining area perfect for families.

I just needed some food between bars, so I was glad that they served something solid here.  I got a simple grilled cheese sandwich, which was good...but very expensive for what I expected for grilled cheese.  Maybe they use brie, so it's a bit fancier?  I was bummed there was no live music while we were there, but did appreciate the food.  

At the time it was too cold to sit outside and I didn't get a chance to try the drinks, so my experience was far from optimal.  Wish I could have enjoyed it more, but for how things were that day...I am indifferent about TBW.

Walking down lower Broadway, it's easy (especially as a non-local) to get distracted by the numerous, and similar-looking, restaurants touting live music and cold beer. Unless you're intimately familiar with the country music scene, choosing one restaurant/music club over another is nigh impossible.

Before visiting this restaurant, I asked locals where I should eat, and almost all of them said to visit Old Red. Maybe it was because I was a tourist, or maybe it was because it's a good place to eat. Either way, I went and was not disappointed.

The food was good (though mostly fried) and the service was friendly and attentive. The live music was fantastic, but of course your mileage may vary depending on who's performing.

Long-story-short, it was good. Eat there.

Went in about 5pm last night.  The back room was mostly empty except two large groups.  With a room full of empty tables she tried to sit us next to one of the groups.  I'm not talking a table away I'm talking next to.  The lady in the group had to move her purse for us to sit down.  I asked if we could just take a table near by.  With a grunting noise she let us.  She gave us a couple
Of menus and there we sat....and we sat........and we sat.
At least 4 different waiters or runners walked by our table on multiple times.  Not one made any effort to acknowledge us.  In the meantime I fixed their wobbly table, you're welcome.  Two people walked in and sat with the group that was about ten feet from us.  They were promptly asked if they would like something to drink or order some food.  At that point we left.  I told the hostess and the fella she had been standing talking and laughing with at the front podium for the last 20 minutes about our lack of service.  Blank stares was the reply.   Food looked good but we never got a chance to try it.  The restaurant reaches out to me below.   With NO way to communicate with them without publicity posting my email.  No thanks!  They don't care.  Plenty of other places to go in this town.

Decent bar food, but what makes this place great is the music. However, arrive early or prepare to stand all night.  If your not lucky enough to get a table, it is difficult getting to the bar to order drinks.
Loved this place...1st wedding anniversary here...a mountain of nachos and margaritas!!!

Best hamburger ever.  The menu warns that service might be slow, but that was not our experience.  Waitress was attentive and knowledgable, and the entertainment was fantastic.  One of the highlights of our trip into the city!

1st time to Nashville and really enjoyed having a drink and a starter to share. We didn't get a main dish cause we wanted to keep checking out other places. Live music was good, drinks were good and appetizer was good. Service was excellent. What more can you ask for!

We went here to see a friend's band play live. The atmosphere was great. It is kid friendly yet also a place where you can go with friends to hang out. The food was good but the server we had was awful. The other servers seemed to be more attentive to their tables and seemed live we just got a bad one. The portions of food they serve are huge.
Came here on a Monday night, the band was great.  Mostly cover songs, but very well sung. Being from California, I rarely hear  live country music performed so well.  Great time.

I have visited this area multiple times for concerts, shows, and hockey games. It is centrally located downtown and is HUGE! For an arena of this size, the main thought that comes to mind is why are the ladies restrooms so small? 

There are many vendors and the layout is easy to follow. I have been to some arenas that are so complicated that it is easy to get lost. Not the issue at all with Bridgestone. Only two levels. And it just goes in a circle. Simple! 

Of course the prices for something as simple as a bottle of water are quite offensive, but hey, that's part of the experience, right? Overpriced food and drinks to consume with the entertainment. Overall, it is a nice venue, and I am looking forward to the next event I attend there.

I went to Tennessee Brew Works for the first time yesterday. They've only officially been open about one week and I was really impressed with several things. First...the taproom is a great hang and has a very different and cool feel compared to other breweries in Nashville. Second...the staff was incredibly nice and welcoming. Even one of the owners was on hand to greet every customer in the tap room. Third they have good beers, which I guess is the most important part anyways. I am a big IPA fan and theirs, the Cutaway, was great. Lastly, their did options are limited but good. Pork Sandwich, Kettle Corn, etc...

Overall, good hang and I'll go back.

I saw the Foo Fighters many, many times in the last year. The show at Bridgestone was fantastic, of course, but it was the STAFF and the FACILITY that I was so impressed with. I would be back in a heartbeat. So impressed with how organized and friendly they were in contrast to other arenas I saw shows at this summer. What a refreshing change to the usual rude concessions, angry security and disorganized lineup procedures...or lack there of. Great venue, and well run. Bravo!
We were in town from Chicago for a birthday celebration, and Tommy P. took awesome care of us.  We had a party of 10, we sat at the bar, and the service was amazing!!  Tommy P. is the man!!!

We finally got to make our first trip to the Schermerhorn to see "The Legend of Zelda: Symphony of the Goddess" event.  The building is beautiful and the Grammy award winning Nashville symphony was a treat to see/hear.  It was also fun to see the posh Schermerhorn overrun with nerds...

They offer valet parking for a whopping $27 so we opted to find our own.  We parked at Pinnacle at Symphony place, which was a very short walk to the orchestra hall.  We paid $15 BUT the Pinnacle closes most enterances to their garage except for the main one.  We did not know this and ended up walking around most of the building before we found that unlocked entrance.

Unlike other Nashville Arts venues, photography is allowed while the house lights are up, so feel free to take your phone/camera to snap some pics of the beautiful interior.

The hall is like a vast maze, but there are plenty of staff that will be glad to help you find your way.

Excellent nachos!  But our waiter Chris M. Made them even better!  His service was excellent and he shared some great Nashville history with us as well as some wonderful ideas for our next trip.  If you visit, be sure to ask for Chris.

Visiting Nashville and as a margarita drinker, I figured I pretty much had to stop here. All in all, decent, but pricey. The drinks are stromg, but I've had strong drinks for much less. I had the Teriyaki Chicken; it was delicious, but again, pricey. The bartender, JJ, was very nice. He's the reason I gave four stars instead of 3.

The atmosphere, music and most importantly beer are absolutely phenomenal. They have a great take on different styles of beer. My wife, who doesn't even like beer found one that she really enjoyed (southern wit). This place gives you a great taste of Nashville and is a must see.

On a recent first time visit to Nashville, our bnb host suggested this place among the many choices on Broadway, and I'm glad she did!  Layla's  is very unassuming, but the music is good, the beer etc is reasonable, and the staff was friendly.  There are dozens of honky tanks to drift in and out of along these touristy blocks, but if you're looking for a calm place to sit, kick back with a cold one, and enjoy some good Ole Nashville music, you'd be hard pressed to beat this little joint!  We went back a second time and were just as pleased.  And, if you need something for comparison, Roberts Western World, next door, is a good alternative if you must...
And if you're wondering why then it isn't a 5 for me? Well, there wasn't a better place I saw...but to be perfect, I'd suggest a little more seating, which they can't really expand, and some killer food...which I didn't sample.  But it's the first venue I'd return to in that area, next time around!  Thanks, Layla & company!  And a special tip of the hat to the band one evening, led by Chuck, who only referred to himself as "Chuck the f*** and his f***ING band"...so they might be a tad hard to track....lol...but they were three hours of pure, talented, and sincere entertainment. So Layla, please tell these guys to get a better way to follow them, 'cause we surely would!

we love this place!! it rocks!! 

http://www.watchonlinevideos.org/twitter-links-hitleap.html

Very friendly staff, clean, well organized. This was a wonderful venue.  Every seat in the house had a great view.  I had the pleasure if exploring both the front and back of the house.  Well maintained by the staff.

I loved this place. It's quieter than most other SoBro bars and they have a great burger. Staff was super friendly and the music wasn't country. After honky tonking for two days, a change of pace and style was welcomed. We watched the Hissy Fits play 50's swing rock for over an hour. Definitely going back.
Tommy and Melissa are awesome.  Sit at the bar for great service from these two and a great seat for the music!
Honestly all these honky tonks are pretty indistinguishable from one another. But that doesn't mean they aren't at least a little fun.

We like to go to breweries all over the country and this one was a great find! The decor inside and out is very inviting and unique and the beers are nothing short of that! You can tell the Brewers put a lot of heart into what they are making!

There's a bouncer at the door checking ID, ensuring that you are 21. Friday & Saturday nights are the most popular and it's wall to wall inside. ....just like walking on the street. 

Seems like the music is pop rock as all the 21 year old girls in the audience know the words and sing along with the band.

The norm is no cover,  and beets are about $5. Male sure you tip the band when they pass their Buckley around!

Always a fun time, and you might actually hear some good music.

Went to a Preds game when visiting from LA. This place is awesome. Nashvillans are too nice. I was wearing a Kings jersey and only got some mild smack talk. People, stop complaining about the food, it is not a restaurant.  The popcorn was amazing though. And whoever thought of half of beer during first intermission deserves and handshake.
The burgers are good enough in my mind to justify the cost, and I live 4 blocks up the hill... It's nice to get more music variety. I hear that Gavin Degraw owns the place...

attended the CMA awards and was impressed.  The place was clean and the acoustics were great.  Also attended the taping of the CMA country christmas.  Great views of the stage and no echo, the venue could be different for sporting events, but for the two music shows we attended, i thought it was a nice place.  Lower the prices of the drinks and snacks though, geez.
Margaritaville lived up to the hype. We had a wonderful time. The food was plentiful and really good. Our waitress Tammy was awesome. She was knowledgeable about the menu, friendly and entertaining.

The home of the Preds! What is there not to love about this place?!
But even if your not a Preds fan... I know there is a good chance you will feel right at home here anyway. 

You can tell that Bridgestone Arena is a place in constant movement, there is some kind of improvement going on all the time. New seats, new places to eat, drink, shop, it's always happening!

Don't miss the waffle and chicken stand by section 110!
The only place not on my favorite list is the Jack Daniel's bar (the one on the inside-outside is good), many times they only have two bartenders which is WAY not enough... Not going there any more. 
Instead, I choose the bar to the right (right after entering from the square on Broadway and then keeping right) if I'm lucky I'm getting service from the wonderful lady named Pam!  

If you like to upgrade your hockey or Consert experience add tickets to the Lexus Lounge where they serve food and drinks. They usually 3-4 food stations with everything from nachos and hot dogs to steak and shrimp cocktails. And don't miss the flat bread pizza station! Fresh from the Owen and so good. 

Staff is really friendly and so helpful everywhere you go. I like the fact that you keep seeing the same faces every time you come back too, a lot of regulars here. Just like me! :)
Not as full as Roberts next door, but not was ok. No drink specials on a very dead Monday night, while next door was great. Sad because it was a nice venue.

Certainly touristy, but that should be expected! We came for a meal before going out and I have to say the location is awesome, you're in the midst of all the fun. They have live music and the crowd is always huge. We waited a while for our food but also expected it because of the day of the week/time. I felt as if the food was a tad bit on the saltier side. Portions are large too!
It's a brewery, there are a lot of them around.....with that said, this one did have a cool vibe and feel. I loved their Southern Wit and they have ample space both indoors and outdoors.

Just in Nashville for a day and found this place on Yelp.  Awesome brewery!  Great decor and great beer selection.  Very nice staff.  Lots of seating throughout.  Had Sunday brunch and it's a smaller menu but is fabulous.  Large size version of connect four was fun for the kids.

Music was very good. Our waitress was ok.  Food was not so great... Thought it was a bit expensive.  The worse was the ladies bathroom.  Diirrttty.  Needs walls washed and painted.  Dirty cover below sink, no paper towel holder.. Floors gross.  Would not go back. Jimmy send in someone
The volcano nachos could feed an army. The margaritas could knock out an army. Otherwise, nothing too spectacular.

This place is so cool! We met friends here for a Saturday afternoon beer tasting. We did not do the tour but enjoyed spending time in the tasting room trying out several beers.  

The outside patio area is great and look forward to returning when it's warmer. The inside tasting room area is very nice and cozy. The staff is beyond friendly and very welcoming. While tasting there were 2 acoustic performers that added a great piece to the overall atmosphere. The upstairs tasting room overlooks the brewing operation which was neat to see. 

We tried 3 different beers that were good and served in a snifter glass at $5 each. This trip we missed out on a sweet potato stout that sounded delicious!

I really like this place.  Very nice vibe, lively, friendly cheerful staff and people, good food and good beer (and they have wine), pleasant surroundings, nice music.  

The one drawback is that when they run the credit card you are given three options: 20% tip, 25% tip, or "custom amount".  This really is a turn-off.  I'm glad to give a good tip, but I do not like being pushed, particularly with 20% as the minimum tip.  Particularly since you have to go to the counter to order, so it's not like they are doing a lot of work.

Also, parking is an issue.
Nashville Hot Calamari , stopped in for a drink and a bite to eat. Drinks were good food was over cooked

This place is awesome! Most of the time I go to a new brewery and I only like one or maybe two of the beers, but all of their beers are excellent. The place itself is pretty cool, especially the balcony that looks out into the brewery. This place is a definite contender with my all time favorite Yazoo.

Came here to see the Blackhawks take on the Preds in April 2013. Friendly staff, clean bathrooms w the speaker system so you don't miss any of the action, fast moving drink lines, etc. Aside from the loss, I had a great time, even made friends with security.

Went to Jimmy's this past weekend for dinner. Only went because it was a 45 minute wait without reservation. It actually took longer than expected, which is understandable, it was just an estimate. Had a Bahama mama margarita as we waited. It Was surprisingly weak. 1.5 hours later we were seated. Had an awesome waitress, we all ordered chimichurri flat iron steaks, it comes with French fries as a side. The server brought our food out & all of them were missing the chimichurri sauce. She apologized & went back & brought us some. We finally get to eat & kid you not, the steak had NO flavoring, just char from being grilled. Even with the chimichurri it was still missing something. So basically we paid $20 for a small steak & small order of fries, that was completely bland. They sell rubs & marinades in their gift shop but they do not even use it on their own meat. It was very disappointing & upsetting that we spent over $70 for two: for bland food & weak drinks. It got two stard bc the wait staff were amazing.  Definitely wouldn't return & definitely do not recommend.

Really enjoyed this brewery... Not only good draft beer, but great atmosphere to consume tasty beverages! The outside seating was great, plenty of activities, such as darts, board games, live music and sports on TV.  My favorite Brewery to visit.

This place is a poor excuse for an arena and organization, for that matter.
The way the staff at this Arena (corporate) treat their employees, potential employees, and customers is a disgrace.
If you're considering going there for an event, take the below into consideration:  
The food is overpriced, tickets are overpriced, staff is rude, service is slow, and it's less than an exciting experience.

However, if you're even REMOTELY considering working at this venue, you most definitely should abandon that idea immediately.  
I have never in my life encountered such a biased, cruel, and demeaning corporate staff in my entire life.  I recently went to a "job fair" at this organization and was hired on the spot.  But, I was astonished by the types of people who were getting hired left and right and the illiterate and sloppy folks who were walking through those doors and the arrogant rednecks who were doing the interviewing.  I figured there would be some classy, educated, business-savvy, smart folks working in a place that is so centrally located in downtown Nashville, one that has a major impact on the city, but I was sadly mistaken.  I was hired, put through the mill to continue the next steps of the hiring process, did as I was told, and then when it came time to pick something up from them in person, I was treated as if I was some sort of lowly peasant and they had "no idea" who I was.  Was denied the final papers I needed to continue the process without any explanation, was told I'd be called back, and never received a call (and this was AFTER I was hired on the spot).  I decided to call them back and then they tried to retract statements they had made and randomly explained that they weren't hiring me and to come back next time...again, AFTER I was already given the job.  I was treated so disgustingly and with no explanation by three of their executive staff members.   I am not originally from Nashville and had moved here just a few months ago.  I had turned down another job for this one being that they made it clear this was a sure thing and after months of looking for work, was excited to begin with this company and had the job taken from me with no idea why before I could even begin.

Word of advice to all who consider working here...if you weren't born, raised, and intend on dying in this city, don't bother walking through those doors.  They treat out-of-towners like lepers who don't deserve to be in their presence.   I am sickened by this experience and this company surely does not do Nashville justice.  Do rethink going to this venue if you at all care about equality and how people are treated.
My boyfriend and I shared the flight (5 samples) all of the beers were very good! Prices were fair as well.

Wow...after coming home from the great of place of Nashville with that great Southern hospitality, tours of the Grand Ole Opry and Ryman.  It is sad to say...we experienced some of the many reviews of the Ole Red restaurant. The standard procedure in many bars and restaurants is to swipe the credit card before the customer orders and is given service, (i.e., the credit card must be swiped and returned after the swipe). After at least 45 minutes our order was not received, then one hot dish was served but cold. They took it back. 
But the manager was nice and gave us his business card, apologized and said it was OK to leave. We were not provided a charge bill upon leaving. A charge was submitted later without my signature and most importantly, without my knowledge of being charged along with a tip. 
The is very sad...Blake is class act and we loved 'seeing' him at the back-stage tour of Grand Ole Opry. Thank you, Blake and congratulations, on being a member of Grand Ole Opry. Maybe.... a new song "Waited One Long Hour." 
Peace, love, happiness and most of all staying strong for everyone!!!

This is a solid choice for food and drinks on Broadway. It has a great atmosphere with almost continuous live music. The cherry limeade was delicious. If you are hungry I highly suggest the tater tot poutine. They have handmade tater tots that they cover in pulled pork, rich white gravy, and a fried egg.

Bad service...seated 20 minutes without a server.  When a server finally came by, they asked us to wait a while longer..  this place has some work to do to get it together.. unsatsfied customer.. update... i ordered a cider beer at the bar and they said they were out.. sitting at a table (with no service for 20 min) the table next to us was served 2 while we were waiting...
The atmosphere and phone the best on broadway! If you get a chance to go to the roof top ask for Jade great bartender.

Great nachos.  Our 4th margaritaville we've visited and it was very pleasant and clean except the women's bathroom,  that was gross.  Quick wait and very quick service.  Perfect for live music when on Broadway with young children.
Fun time! Nice pours on the cocktails. Awesome band. No cover saturday night woo woo. Like most places but still nice.

Been to 2 shows here, it's great venue for live music, classical or otherwise.  They sell beer! and wine.  Ain't cheap, but hey, it's a classy joint.  Support the Schermerhorn, you'll be glad you did.

The place was clean (having been newly constructed). Food was a mixed bag - pickle flight idea is good but meh, no one loved it. Wings were surprisingly good - very flavorful and well done, even though it took forever for them to cook and serve. Not a ton of other options on the menu. Service was pretty good. I wouldn't make a huge effort to go back since the music kinda sucked (come on, aren't you supposed to have the best talent?).

Great bar. The bartenders were awesome and very friendly. The atmosphere was relaxed but fun. The music was terrific. Go sit at the bar a spell. You are sure to drink too much and solve the worlds problems.

Bought tickets beforehand and had to wait in line outside for ONE HOUR BECAUSE THEY HAD ONE PERSON CHECKING IDS ON NEW YEARS EVE. I understand waiting in line on NYE but not that long if we bought a ticket in advance for a concert. Ridiculous that I paid to wait in line with for an hour. Not worth it.

Last night's concert, Nashville Symphony and the music of the Rolling Stones, was amazing in this incredible venue.  Should be lots of pics and video posted based on what was going on around us. Apparently not really enforced!

We ate here yesterday! We were with a tour group, and had 10 people with us! We waited 20 min for a table which was great!    Then we got sat as did others behind us! It took a while to take our order, and then we waited, and waited for our food as we watched others who came behind us get food. We all ordered burgers except 2 who ordered sandwiches! It took one of us asking what the eta was on our food 30 min later to find out that their computers were down again. I've worked in restaurants for many years, and it doesn't matter if your computer's are down. Have a back up! You shouldn't need a computer to make food at a place like this. Have they ever heard of paper check. They didn't let us know it was going to take an hour to get our food from the time we ordered. Which btw is ridiculous! When the food came out it was only certain people got their food, and the rest had to wait several minutes longer , and part of it was cold. We had 2 1/2 hours for eating and sightseeing be four our tour bus picked us up. We spent almost all of our time here waiting on mostly cold food. The management did give us a small discount, but it was an awful experience. We won't be back to this location. I had a Cuban, and it wasn't good! I had a way better one at Arby's! Have the courtesy to tell your guests that you are having problems that affect them...like waiting forever on their food. Not wait for us to ask where our food is at before saying they are having problems. We would have went some place else. Honestly McDonald's would have been faster, and better for what we got for the price. If i could give zero I would! All of us were dissatisfied with the whole experience!
Amazing food , friendly staff. Overall great brewery to check out. I love the outside sitting area . I highly recommend it.

I attended "Boolesque" on October 19, 2013. I was very excited to see the show and arrived at 7:45pm for an 8pm "door open" time. The line was already over a block long. Doors didn't open till 8:15 and it was 45 degrees outside. After getting inside the venue, we realized there were no chairs left. They only had 50 - 75 chairs set up, and easily sold about 250-300 tickets. We stood on a concrete floor, I in heels, waiting for the show to start at 9pm. By the time the show started, my feet and back were already sore...and, many people were standing and straining to see. I'd say I was unable to see about 90% of the show, and that was after moving to different locations in the venue trying to get a better view. 

When you purchase tickets, it says nothing about limited seating. Nothing. 

What makes this worse is when I left a review on their facebook page, they were very rude and made me out to be an idiot. They pointed out that it says on their FAQ page that it is standing room only. Well, who looks at the FAQ page unless they have questions? And since nothing was mentioned at the ticket purchase point about seating or standing room only...I had no reason to check the FAQ page. 
Furthermore, after they ridiculed me on their facebook page for daring to leave a negative review...several other people backed me up in comments...however Marathon Music Works deleted every single comment after supporters started showing up. 

Very disappointed in their customer service. Will not be going back, and will definitely make sure word gets out about this place.

Great music, great drinks. And clean. Richard at the bar was great. Recommended some good drink choices. Went above and beyond helping my can't decide wife make a decision. Great beer options. Good mix of original music and covers.

Nashville Predators Play here.... Do I need to say anything else?
They have good concerts and I really enjoyed the beer festival;.
GO PREDATORS!

I went there to kill time before the rest of my group arrived into Nashville. I had the day to myself in Music City and had made the most of it, so I was feeling pretty tired from all the walking I had done - in the rain. This place came recommended by a local. It's popular, but not a tourist trap. I started with the flight, which was very reasonably priced. The beers came in these cute goblets. I loved each of the beers, even the stout and I never like stouts unless icy cold (so cold you can't taste the beer). I didn't get any of the food, but the menu looked good and people around me were certainly ordering food. Being that it was Music City and it was 5 o'clock on a Friday, they had a local group performing on their stage. The music great. Atmosphere great. Wishing I could have stayed longer, but had to meet up with my group. Will come back again next time I'm in Nashville.

I am not a beer expert by any means, but I did not enjoy any of the beers I tried in my flight. However, it is a great value to get the flight and try 5 different beers. Maybe, I didn't pick the right ones. Another gripe is none of the beers were chilled enough for me. I really wish they were colder and more refreshing. That being said, I thoroughly enjoyed the food! The cheeseboard was amazing! All of the cheeses were local, with the exception of one, I think it was imported. The bread is their homemade beer bread and it is perfectly buttered, pairs perfectly with all the cheeses and the persimmon butter. My husband had the burger, and it was delicious as well, probably one of the top burgers I've had in Nashville. I would recommend it! The atmosphere is actually really cool. I really liked the second floor patio. There are also free board games you can play while hanging out with friends. Overall, I really enjoyed the food, but for a brewery, I was really disappointed with the beers I tried.

My friend and I stopped in here while we were bar hopping along South Broadway. We sat in the bar section by the band. Our waitress was Kiersten and she made our experience a great one! She was extremely friendly and had some great recommendations on the menu. I would send friends and family there for a fruity cocktail or beer, and a burger! The live band they had playing in the bar area was great and created a nice atmosphere.

You stumble upon an area that is in the middle of a face lift and there is this gem shining bright. The place has a modern feel, is very clean and is off the beaten path from the rest of the Nashvegas crazies.

They offer food and I had the burger for $10 and the $7 frog legs. The burger just comes as a burger on a paper plate and I wondered....where are the chips are fries to go along with the burger? The burger is a greese bomb but full of flavors and pairs perfect with beer. You get two frog legs and they are breaded with a hot canjun seasoning. Flavor is awesome and I wish there were more frog legs to dig into. 

I tried every beer with two $10 flights and met one of the owners in the process. They are two years new and don't quite distribute outside of the brewery. They had very good beers when compared to others I had. The Ryeman and whisky bourbon aged beers were my favorite.

Live music as well and it was loud so we hung out upstairs. You order everything from the bar and it gets a bit tricky when they try to find you with the food. 

All in all a great place to grab a lunch, beer and listen to good music. They reflect a solid Nashville experience.

The food was ok, obviously frozen fish, they were out of other flavors that must come pre-seasoned and the place was a disgusting mess, trash all over the floor that not one waitress bothered to pick up,,, ewww made me feel like my food was dirty too,, we will not return there.....and then our change was $59.49 and she only gave us $59.00.... she said math was her strong point, "oh do you want the .49 cents?" Wow!!

Another great experience, one I will always remember.
Everyone on staff was absolutely polite and professional.
The symphony sounded amazing and had a great night of performance.
A Lifetime memory, thumbs up.

I had their TN No. 12, described as a Belgian-style Quad, which was delicious. Also had a porter or heavy ale, which I'd name but it's not on their on-line menu. It wasn't their Imperial, and it was acceptable, but that's all I recall.
For food, I had their pickled wings, which I didn't like the taste of. We also had a cheese plate, which included gorgonzola, a cheddar and a goat (and more), along with grilled (toasted?) bread. Quite delicious

Recently visited Nashville to see Flogging Molly at Marathon Music Works. The venue, pretty good. I liked the atmosphere, it was warehouse meets artsy type of scene. We arrived early and stood in line waiting for the doors to open. I was pleased to see they carded and stamped hands prior to getting to the door to save time, as it was cold outside. 
I guess you are wondering why I only gave it two stars then, eh? Well I contacted the venue via twitter and facebook, requesting the prices prior to getting into town. I wanted to be sure I had enough cash to cover the cost of drinks for me and my boyfriend. They never responded, to either request. Now, I know, people are thinking, well, maybe they weren't on their site, right? Wrong, they were quick posting about other events, ticket sales, etc., so I know they were on their account, but just didn't have the decency or customer service skills to respond. I find that rude, and frankly unacceptable. Being from out of town, I don't like to leave my credit card/debit card at the bar to keep a tab open, especially at a place with that large of a crowd, and wouldn't you know there was a minimum that didn't allow me to swipe my card each time. Needless to say, I had one beer there and decided I would spend my drinking money elsewhere after the concert. 
Note to management: RESPOND TO YOUR CONSUMERS! Without your consumers, your bills wouldn't get paid.
Amazing venue and the restaurant is nice for a pre-show meal.
One of my favorite breweries! A fun place to hang out, and their beer is delicious. Wish they had just a tad more variety, but their food is great too.

I attended Closing Night Runway Shows of Nashville Fashion Week 2014 and the After Party. The sound was great during the show but during the after party it was almost too loud to carry on a conversation. I can only guess that it may be this way during a live performance. This venue is spacious and easy to navigate with a wheelchair. The only real issue that needs improvement is a lack of accessible parking. I would definitely return

So much fun!  Great live music.  Service was great and our sever gave us plenty of information since we were visiting from out of town.  Recommend the cheese burger in paradise or fish tacos and washing it down with a Last Mango in Paris.  Top it off by sharing a piece of key lime pie.
Great atmosphere that anyone can love even if you are not a parrot-head. HUGE QUANTITIES (nachos) the servers are great and funny. They have a very funny balloon maker that made it much better.

If you go to one place on Broadway come here.  Most of the spots are completely touristed out and have lost their original flavor.  Layla's has not.  I came here about 10 years ago (Broadway was about half what it is now, and the place was hot).  I came here recently, still hot.

Really good music, with that authentic sound.

Bartenders are on it, and very polite too.

It's still old school, 90% of everything else on Broadway is new school.

You're welcome

Margaritaville is my favorite restaurant in downtown Nashville because it's just FUN!!!  Yes, I'm a "Parrothead".  But, even if I wasn't, this place is great for several reasons. One, it has really fun food. I had their seafood mac and cheese recently and it was really good!  Obviously, good, homemade mac and cheese is one of the great comfort foods of all time, but add shrimp and crab meat to it? Oh yeah babe! :-) And some of their drinks are as much like dessert as they are cocktails. And don't even get me started on their actual desserts! Second, after you eat, you can shop in their Margaritaville store. It's hard for me not to want one of everything.  The only downside is that the music tends to be loud.  But what most people go there for is the party, Margaritaville ambiance. And they get it in spades.  One of these days, I'm hoping they put a Margaritaville on the west coast. Right now the closest one to me is in Las Vegas.

I registered just to post this review. 

This was the single worst restaurant experience I've ever had. I ordered the chili and it came out cold. When I say cold I mean out of the refrigerator cold. Waitress sent it back and it came back scalding hot. On the third bite I was rewarded with a piece of the plastic bag the chili came in. My friend ordered biscuits and gravy. The biscuits were so stale it took effort to cut through it with a knife. 

One waitress was visibly crying and shaking from being yelled at by an old man whom we later found out was the "manager". That same manager came over and sprayed our table with bleach water immediately after we ordered and said "you're leaving right?" When we said we just ordered he left and didn't wipe up the chemical he sprayed the table with. 

As other posters have said. No tap water here only bottles water. 

I very bazaar and disappointing experience. I will never go back and would advise anyone to avoid this place.
Seems to be a trend on broadway to offer terrible service. Can not tell you about the food as we waited for about 15 minutes for a server to greet us at our table and then left.
Great venue.  Easy to get to.  Awesome place to see an event.

Good great, music good.  Service, one of the worse we've ever experienced anywhere.   Our waiter came to our table first time and asked us what we wanted.  No smile, no hello, noting.  Maybe the guys was having a bad day.  There was nothing on the table, no menu, no napkins, no silverware (remember this for later).  We were a bit puzzled by the abrupt question but went we it.  We asked for some water and...ah menus.  A few minutes later the waiter came with menus...no water.  He came back a few minutes late and we ordered some drinks...and asked for the waters.  We eventually ordered the food which came fairly quickly.   We quickly remembered that we had no silverware.   It's hard if not impossible to eat the side salad without a fork.  We had to wait a bit more to get his attention again and asked for silverware...and water.  The waiter came back with literally two forks in his hands.  No knives.  The food was very good and we eventually got the water.  As we started eating we quickly realized that napkins are a must (burgers were tasty but greasy).  Mind you by now we're finding this experience ridiculously bad and sadly funny at the same time.  My wife and I are not extremely picky so my wife half-jokingly said she'll use her dress to wipe.  Yeah that didn't last long. It's gross and difficult to eat without napkins.  We we asked for napkins and the waiter came back with...wait for it...6 bar napkins.  Come on now!!!   Bar napkins are so small!  The waiter seemed puzzled with every request we had and remember, we only asked for basic stuff that should have been available.  We ate pretty quickly and the waiter picked up our plates and said he'll bring our check.  Ok, I guess our evening was done there.  And we were more that ready to go.   We thought that perhaps the waiter was very new and inexperienced but he seemed to be able be able to juggle multiple tables at once, albeit not very well.  We didn't take too personally, the guests at the table next to us ate without napkins too. Eventually they asked for napkins too and the they got some normal sized ones.  So lucky!!!  Our impression is that the waiter was just incredibly lazy and just didn't give a crap about anything.  On a positive note, the gift shop kid was super friendly and we ended up buying some gifts (my wife is a huge Jimmy buffet fan).

I was looking for a place to get some hot chicken and found Ole Red on the corner.  The music sounded great, so I thought what the heck.  I wanted to sit at the bar, so I decided to go to the upstairs bar and take a seat there.  I ordered the half a chicken, hot, with greens.  The chicken came in a big tin bucket and it was excellent (gravy and a biscuit too).  I was only able to eat two pieces.  The greens had bacon in them and they were delicious.  

The band that was playing was Mark something, can't really remember the full name, but they were VERY good.  

I wish I could have given this restaurant a 5 star (5 star music & food), but service is a HUGE part of the restaurant business.  The female bartender who waited on me was not so great.  Not attentive at all.  I did want another glass of wine.  My glass was empty for awhile and she never even asked if I wanted another one.  She wasn't even busy.  Very disappointing.  Does she realize that if she gives better service her tip will actually go up????  Hello There????

Ole Red, I think your food and music is fabulous.  Your service sucks!!!!!!

Two words:  tourist trap.  We went on an incredibly slow night.  From the very beginning we were repeatedly reminded that the help depends on tips but we couldn't even get silverware to the table despite numerous employees standing around doing what appears to be nothing.  We had to go to the bar several times to gets drinks because our waitress could t be found and apparently no one else is allowed to serve a sitting table.  The waitress got half our order wrong.  Then, after almost forty minutes, she brought us another customers steak that was over cooked.  We know this because they were sitting right beside us and were complaining that theirs was UNDERcooked and sent it back.  The waitress tried to be cordial and voluntarily explain it all away but at this I think we were all just ready to leave.  I'm not one to be overly critical but I thought it important for potential patrons to know that if you're expecting anything short of poor service, bland food, and an outrageous bill you'll be sorely disappointed.

We held our "Till Death do Us Party!" here this weekend to celebrate the marriage of Lauren and Alex.  The staff and venue were epic!  The sound for the live band--amazing! I highly recommend this venue for your next party!

This was our favorite and go to while in Nashville. We went in each of the days/nights we were in town. This is a legit honky tonk bar. Much of what I hope is not going to disappear from Broadway. Each time we went in, the music was different, but all good. Drink prices one of the most reasonable.Fun place

Jim hit the nail on the head with the first sentence of his review. "If I could give this place 0 stars I would."

The bartender was a really nice guy but the owner or manager is a total jerk. The first annoying thing was they wouldn't serve me a water because its free. I got over it and just ordered a bottle. 

I was there drinking with two of my friends on a Saturday night around 11 pm. I spent almost $100, which I wouldn't complain about except that the vodka red bull was $11.  When I got a little drunk the owner asked me to leave, which was also fine. I stepped outside to get some air and he followed me and began harassing me. My wife and our friend were pretty sober and assured him I wouldn't throw up or anything and he didn't have to worry. He procceded to call my wife names and was trying his best to pick a fight with me. 

Glad I had a good night or I would have let the guy have it. Definitely won't be going back. It's dumb that this guy has lost hundreds of dollars amongst my friends. Hope the nice bartender finds a new job.

I'll give it 3 stars just because the ambiance was great. Love music all day long, but everything else was mediocre at best. They brought out my sons nachos before everyone else's food, even after specifically telling our waiter we wanted them when all the food came out. My sweet tea tasted off and my hot chicken sandwich was dry. I asked for pickles and didn't receive any. 

All in all, great atmosphere but don't plan on an exceptional meal. Should have taken my husband and my $100 elsewhere. I was really hoping to find a new local joint.

Came here after the craziness of CMA Fest. Finally there wasn't a line around the building. Service was excellent and the food exceeded our expectations. Drinks were awesome as well. Good job BS, great restaurant and bar!

So the food was good but a little overpriced but it was all worth it, our server Darrell was awesome! He was super attentive and seemed dedicated to our experience! He was so fun and he had us laughing the entire time. He had suggestions on where to go afterwards and we tried to get him to meet us but he still had a few hours left on his shift. Anyway, we had a great time.

I recently visited this establishment and enjoyed every minute. Our server was Mandie and she was an absolute delight. Drinks were great and I will definitely be back. Mandie gave the best service possible and I will be requesting her when I go back!

Saw Maroon 5 at the stadium last weekend ~ wonderful stadium for a concert ~ I am NOT a big fan of being amongst a crowd of 19K people ~ the staff at the stadium did a nice job of crowd control ~ can not speak of other experiences at the stadium as I am not a local ~ however, I never felt as though I would be trampled with so many people in 1 area ~ would definitely consider attending another concert at this venue!

So they advertise the best burger in Nashville. When it arrived, it looked really pretty but was literally cold and like raw inside. We sent it back and they forgot to make a new one and we had to chase our waiter down, he'd forgotten about us at the table. Never, ever, ever again.

Beautiful hall with great sight-lines pretty much no matter where you're sitting. 

We've been twice now for two very different concerts: Trey Anastasio of Phish with the Nashville Symphony performing arrangements of Phish songs, and then last month for a concert consisting of a Corigliano work, and Brahms' 1st Piano Concerto with Emanuel Ax as soloist. 

For the Trey Anastasio performance we had seats in the balcony with a direct view of the stage. The sound was great from back there. The orchestra was clear and well balanced and Trey's guitar was mixed perfectly. With the Corigliano/Brahms concert I made a miscalculation and bought super close tickets, front row on the far right side and got an earful of viola and cello, but the piano definitely was not covered up and it was still a very enjoyable experience. Next time when I buy the cheap seats I'll remember to go back a little bit further. 

The entire building is very nice, and comfortable with an old school classical architecture feel. I like the courtyard off to the side with a few benches, enclosed from the outside mayhem of downtown Nashville. It feels secluded even though you're pretty much right in the center of the action. The outside sound does not bleed into the hall at all, which was something I was moderately worried about. 

Gift shop is actually pretty cool, and I like that they have all the CDs that Nashville Symphony has released on Naxos, including a nice 6(?) CD box set of their complete recordings. They have recorded some fairly adventurous stuff; I picked up their recording of Ives' 2nd Symphony which is fantastic. 

If I had one single complaint it would be this: do we really need to stand and sing the National Anthem before the concert? I was not happy about that at all. Is there some sort of rule that at every gathering of people we have to pledge our allegiance to the flag? I love this country, and I love the symphony, but I thought that was a bit unnecessary. I was tempted to sit down for it, not out of some sort of political protest, but because I just thought it was ridiculous.

If i could give you zero stars I would. Friends at our table ordered nachos at the same time as we did. Theirs came out 20 minutes before ours and ours came out cold. Only redeeming quality is our waiter. Ordered a medium well burger and it came out medium. He turned it back it in. Better places to choose from on the strip. Typical chain franchise.

Absolutely beautiful, both architecturally and structurally.  Recently had the most incredible invitation to join some friends in their box for the Lord of the Ring performance of the Nashville Symphony.  Absolutely incredible experience.  We were seated right above the stage, in line with (my personal favorite) the oboes.  You could see the conductor's face.  My own face whipped back and forth as sound came to one of my ears before the other (trumpets/percussion to my right, violins on my left!).  

All sorts of performances, great for all sorts of visitors.  If you're a student, you should register with them, as they offer up $10 tickets to many of their shows!

During a bachelorette weekend we did a party barge that took us here. 10 girls at around 2pm on a Saturday, so it was a pretty empty bar. We all bought drinks, shots, and the bartenders and 'bouncers' were all having a good time with us. The bathrooms are each a big bathroom, one marked for men and one marked for women, the women's was occupied so we were told to us the men's. We left, continued our party barge but ended up at winners/losers at around 3:30. 3 of us entered to use the restroom. The bouncer waved us through, saying he remembered us. We used the men's bathroom, as the women's was occupied, as they they told us to before. Yet when we came out we had about 4-6 men bartenders/bouncers staring at us telling us to get out, we're not allowed back 'don't even think about going to losers because your kicked out'. Really!? Well the rest of us went into 'losers' side, peed and then went to red door saloon, where they were baffled by your bipolar mess. Maybe get on the same page, okay?

Two words. Loaded Landsharks: landshark beer and a shot of lime tequila as a floater. YOU NEED TO GET THIS. you don't even taste the liquor.... We discovered these in myrtle at that Margaritaville.

We stopped here for lunch with  our group of a bachelorette party. Everything was completely packed since it was a gorgeous day on a Saturday in downtown Nash. We slipped on in and they seated us right away. decent items on the menu, a little pricey(but it's the touristy thing to do).

KIERSTEN was the bomb!
We have great memories at Margaritavilles all over the world but the best service we've ever gotten was by this lil sweetie! The front area was super packed but she handled the entire crowd single handily. Her service was on point! We had the nacho "mountain" which was yummy, the coconut shrimp, and several boat drinks. I also ordered a key lime pie to-go but ended up giving it to a beggar. Gonna have to go back before we leave Nashville.

Decent spot for drinks before a Saturday football game. Sydney is a great bartender and delivered prompt, polite service. Cocktails were $6 a piece, and the band wasn't bad. Good spot for a quick stop.

I am amazed that I can't even give one of the facilities on Broad any rating above a 2,  but we stopped for dinner on the way to a concert at the Ryman and it was delicious. The fried chicken is amazing, service was impeccable and we so enjoyed live music. If the rest of the food is anywhere near the caliber of this chicken this place is going to be a huge success just for its food

Definitely worth a stop while in Nashville. A great venue, great atmosphere, and great music. The service was decent and the beer was cold. I'm just hoping that they expand their menu in the future, right now it's a lot like every other greasy burger joint in town.

I have been to Winners Bar and Grill at least a twenty times in 2013 and 2014 since several of my friends wanted to go there and since it was very close to the University but I would say that this bar is not worth your money and that you should go to one of the better ones instead.

This bar is easy to access since it is close to Vanderbilt University and in the heart of Mid-Town, and it has an outdoor patio area. The good thing about this bar is that you get live music once in a while which is pretty nice.

Parking will be very challenging in the area so make sure to get there early. The drinks here are acceptable but be ready to have a LOT more ice than alcohol for the price you pay... Also, this bar is very often empty, so it is hard to have a good time in there, expect if you come with many friends.

Finally, I would qualify the food they serve as low-quality bar food.

Overall, my experience with Winners Bar and Grill was rather negative and I would not recommend it. There are better bars in Nashville! Feel free to message me for any additional details that you may need!
I've been to a couple of shows here and it just sucks. The sound is always bad and standing for shows is really uncomfortable. Never again.

I've been here for hockey and concerts. This is a GREAT concert venue! Sound is spot on. The food in the Lexus lounge is pretty good too!

They should probably pay closer mind to people's intoxication levels. (Although, since they were quick to clean up peoples vomit, and nobody puked on me.... they still get five stars.)

You'll never know how many people need rehab until you see a concert in smashville.

The food was amazing!!! I had my 12 year old daughter and niece so it was nice to go to a place that was kid friendly. The hamburger that I ordered was amazing. The staff was super friendly and the entertainment was great!

Reasons to stop by here:

* Sit by the large wide open windows and see the Nashville street life unfolding in front of you. Like being outside, but better!
* Bartenders, they are fast and friendly.
* Margaritas! 
* Live music
* Crisp coconut shrimp.... Yum!
* Their hot chicken wings are really, really good. (#wingpicky)

The epitome of customer service. First, upon mentioning it was my husband's birthday the hostess got us a table immediately (I wasn't asking,just conversing). Then when a steak was presented well under done, the manager came out and delivered a new steak and comped it (again, not expected). Shea, Callie and Lavaysha...thank you!! We'll be back!
Predators foundation but on another great beer fest. Food was really great this year too!

This is a cute restaurant. It's nicely set up, with a couple of floors and a nice rooftop. Our server was great attending to a party of 8. I ordered the Nashville burger and the Some Beach cocktail. The burger was delicious! My cocktail was a bit weird. I couldn't put a finger on it, but it  had a weird aftertaste. Overall it was a good dining experience.

he third and final brewpub imbibed at during my first evening in Nashville was the nearby-but-not-necessarily-easy-to-get-to Tennessee Brew Works. Sure, it's only a half-mile away, but when you take the shortest route, the road runs over a railroad track. Not that big of a deal unless there happens to be a train stopped in the middle of the road, which there was. Luckily we were walking, so my wive and I could just climb over...

The effort was worth it. If Tennessee Brew Works has one thing down, it's definitely the location. There's outdoor seating, cozy indoor tables and even a balcony that provides even more outdoor space. The brewery felt trendy, welcoming and cozy all at the same time, which isn't necessarily an easy trio to pull off.

And the beer was pretty tasty too. Again, thanks to outdated southern beer laws, there was nothing above about 6.3 percent ABV.
