Info for getting in. We were told to get in line at 11 for the 3 o'clock show. However it changes each week depending on time of year and weather. Here's what they do....you get in a line outside that goes around the building (Margaritaville on Broadway) they start letting people in about 2. They let between 20-30 in at a time. This helps the bartenders to keep up. It is on the second floor (stairs) and inside. Did not see an elevator. Call to check. Cramped for sure. There are bathrooms on the same floor. They search everyone coming in to include handbags, etc. they check IDs for alcohol. You can purchase food from the menu.  FYI Brett Young stopped by for a chat and Rae Lynn was scheduled to come by too. We left early.

Terrible service and disorganization. wanted to visit this new Blake Shelton place while in Nashville. At 4pm we signed up for a table. Was told it would be a 45 minute wait even though there were many empty tables. After an hour of waiting and still not getting a table was told they had to wait for ok from kitchen.  Since we couldn't get answers from employees and we had been waiting for 90 minutes, We left. Disappointed

I was pretty impressed with this stadium. I came for game one of the NHL Playoffs against the Stars and had a great time. My buddy found tickets online and we ended up sitting in the absolute last row of the stadium. Even though we were so high up it was still easy enough to see the action.

The the whole place ran very smoothly. They had almost every seat filled and we had no wait getting in. Heck even the bathrooms and concessions moved like clockwork. The energy from the raging fans was contagious. Even though the Preds lost 3-2, it was still a hell of a game.

I was out waiting on my friend to get off work so I decided to come grab a drink at Margaritaville while I waited.  To be honest, I was really craving their Third Coast Margarita.  It's the house margarita mixed with sweet tea and Jack Daniels whiskey.  It's my favorite drink and what I order almost all of the time when I visit.  Tommy P. was bartending the Chill bar up front and got me my drink quickly.  The house band was performing on the stage in the back so I went to go check them out for a bit.  Overall, a great time.

Came in on a Wednesday for Bluegrass and beer.  Enjoyed a flight and a delicious and well planned cheese board.  Stayed for their BOGO specials and tasted almost everything they offered on tap.  Great atmosphere, fun vibe.  Excellent music.

We simply love going there for various presentations, but this past week we just had to go see The Music of Journey with the Symphony.  
Very cool and a great night!
Five stars for the band! The bar was super average with weak drinks. Music was rhe best part.

We came in at 6:15 and put in our name. It was a 45 minute wait. We sat and ordered our food and drinks by 7:15. We got a few drinks and an appetizer all by 7:45. Our dinner that we ordered with the other food did not come out until after 9:00!!!! All of the tables around us came in after we did, ate and left before we even saw our food. We asked our waitress after about 45 minutes and she said "the Mac and cheese comes out fresh so they are making it now, it should only be a few minutes." We literally ordered Mac and cheese and a hot chicken sandwich. That should take 30 minutes at the most. At about 9:20 we got our food. Our waitress said the manager would "take care of us" because of the wait. The manager came over and told us the kitchen staff dropped our slip so they had no clue they had to cook for us. Why would our waitress not notice earlier that she is bringing other tables food and ask about it instead of us asking? Also, the Mac and cheese wasn't very good. The manager ended up giving us a discount which was nice but we still ended up paying over $40 for something that wasn't very good and we sat there for 3 hours. They're lucky they had entertainment even though we heard the same songs 4 times each.
Interesting menu. Great fried Colliflower and Nachos were awesome. Drink selection was very good
Great Honkey Tonk on Broadway. Live music was great on a Tuesday night, the beer was cold the atmosphere was a room full of fun. So many options in the area... pop in and grab a drink!

Thank heaven there are honest music places left!  This place was definitely raw.  The band was edgy, not commercial country or rock.  It was real music.  We just stopped in for a beer & stayed for several.  I see this venue is "not claimed" by the owner.  That should tell you what they feel about commercialism.  If you want polish, go elsewhere.  Real music.  Here.
He had a great sound system in the bar. I thought it was a bit to fancy/new meaning so clean. Did not eat there so not sure how food was

Our waiter Phil was very nice and very helpful. All of our food and drinks were delivered on time and he was patient with us since All of our food and drinks were delivered on time and he was patient with us since we were new and had no idea it was good on the menu.

Purchased Jimmy Buffet tickets, then managed to break my femur in a skiing accident.  Tried to get some assistance re getting in and out of the venue and seating.  Told nothing could be done, but come the day of the show and they would accommodate.  Went as instructed. Told would have wheelchair available to transport from pickup spot to seats.  Arrived at the venue and was then told nothing available, sorry.  Looking for an ADA attorney in Nashville if anyone can make a recommendation.

So. Much. Food! Would suggest splitting an app or entree with someone so that you don't end up wasting your food as the portions are SO big!  10/10 would recommend as it was a great vibe and the food was very good!
Our favorite place in Nashville! It's so big and the music is so good!! If you are reading this and wondering if you should go you should!

This restaurant was truly disappointing. If you're looking for an overpriced commercial chain type restaurant that spends more time worrying about the quality of the their gift shop shirts than their actual food, then this is the place for you.

Mediocre food, good service, great music. We were seated downstairs and it was freezing. Ambient temp was 68 degrees so we ate quickly so our food didn't congeal. Very expensive for what you get. Been there, got the t-shirt, don't plan to return.

My husband and I had the best time yesterday afternoon, we had the quesadilla and a couple of beers and listened to some fantastic music!!! Thank you JJ for making our outing once a year downtown special!!!!

This establishment assumed that five people that bought tickets for the concert of the night made people leave for being "intoxicated" when they had zero proof and didn't let the accused defend themselves when they paid good money to attend the concert that was proved at their venue. My group and I paid over 50 dollars to attend this concert and we were kicked out before we could even see the band. Marathon music works is rude and senseless to say the least. They don't care about the wellbeing of their attendees. I give zeros stars. They also called us stupid Jews which is very derogatory. I would not recommend.
Fancy place ... nice stage set up. Didn't get to hear the band though.... a very long break. Finally left but checked out all the floors that were more unique than any other bar we saw on Broadway.

Honestly I can only give this location a 2 star rating.. The food is amazing to begin with the fries are delicious! (Were cold when served) but over all to die for you don't even need ketchup! The burgers are amazing! The cheap shredded $1 lettuce you can buy at Walmart is not what you should put on a $17 burger in my opinion but hey that's just me! Can complain of the quality of the food could have portioned more fries again for the price of $17 with $1 shredded lettuce on it. One reason for the 2 stars also is because I ordered the blackberry margaritas (caution it says start with one but don't listen because) they definitely did not put BARELY any alcohol in mine or my partners drink again not worth the price of having no alcohol in it but the waiter sure was ready to ask if we wanted another one (ya no thank you). Also one thing I do hope is I noticed a $4-$5 labor fee on the receipt if I read correctly plus another $4 for tax my hope is that it goes directly to the waiter. Plus your 20% tip suggestions math was not correct on the bottom of the receipt.
First time here and had hair on 2 of our orders. One was on our order of chicken wings(pictured) and on the vegan quesadillas

Waited too long for our food. Not alot of vegetarian options. Server was nice though. 
Salad was smothered in too much cheese-like way too much. Couldn't eat very much of it. Waste of $$.

The best thing about this place is all the outdoor seating. There's literally 3 levels of outdoor patio seating and the place is huge! There was live music right inside at the bar which was also cool. There's darts upstairs on the top level inside. The beer was meh - of the 5 we tasted there was only 2 I would actually order, 1 was okay, and 2 were undrinkable in my opinion. 4 stars because of the atmosphere and outdoor seating, otherwise it would be lower.

One star only because the view is great.there was and empty table with dirty dishes sitting at it for about 10 minutes. We already ordered drinks so we went over and sat down just to hang out and enjoy the beautiful night. After hanging out for about another 10 minutes the hostess cam over asking if we checked in , we did not . So she said the table was already reserved. So we went and checked in. The table sat empty for another half hour, still dirty and on the way out I saw a bunch of other empty tables with reserved on it . I told the woman that it's crazy to just let the tables sit if they want to hang out. She then rudely stated she did not have enough servers.  I will let you know we would have stayed longer- even if we got out own drinks. My suggestion is to staff the place appropriately , or if people want to sit then tell them they can until the checked in party is to be seated and it is self serve for drinks .
My ID was laughed at by security for being "fake" and I don't really understand why. It's a valid Kentucky ID.

Food and service was excellent. Highly recommend after visiting multiple other places on Broadway where good service is not a thing they care about. But at Ole Red they do you right. And the biscuits - they are to die for!

My favorite casual hang out place in Nashville! 

I've been to this brewery (literally) countless times, but never wrote a review because the visits came so naturally to me. That's the type of place this is though. If I'm bored on any afternoon any day of the week, I'll text friends to meet me here. We come, share a couple pitchers, watch a game on the screens, and chat. 

TN Brew Works is super convenient and a simple chill spot for friends to gather. I honestly try to avoid nights where live music is playing because we can't hear each other, but hey, if you're searching for live music then tadaaa. 

So food. EVERYTHING IS GOOD. The only item I can complain about is the wings and that's because they're minuscule in size ("what is this, a center for ants?!!"). Other than that, burger = good, hot chicken = good, fish tacos = good, and so forth. I kind of don't want to review or recommend this brewery because I don't want it to gain any more popularity and get crowded, but it definitely deserves respect. All beers are wonderful but the Basil Ryeman is my personal favorite.

My friend and I had a horrible experience here. The chips and salsa were taken back twice because they were stale and tasted like thick stale uncooked taco shells. The 2nd time the waitress assured us the manager dolled out the next batch and they were the same yucky chips only these weren't warm. The margaritas are watered down and extremely pricey. I felt so giped that I couldn't wait to get out of there and find some place to get real food. We left starving and broke! The one star is for the location only. If I had Jimmy Buffets email I would tell him he needs to to get in there and sample some of that he would flip.
"Always start a winner before ending up a loser"...aka start your night here before stumbling in next door to losers...always a good time! :)
One of the original Nashville Honky Tonks and still fabulous local, live musicians! I highly recommend you stop in and see a piece of Nashville history!

Visited Nashville for the weekend and heard some really good things about Brew Works so we stopped by - and I'm happy we did. Flights were $11 and each beer we sampled was great. Also got the wings which were amazing I would definitely recommend getting those as an appetizer. The inside is nice and theres a spacious seating area out front if the weather is nice.
Tammy Cook, our waitress, made this entire experience that much better.  Food was great, and can't beat the atmosphere!

Came here with a large group from out of town and rented out the entire place, paid for a DJ to perform, and an open bar all night. Staff was extremely rude to our group as a whole. Underage were allowed to enter the bar but were consistently followed around all night by staff members asking to see what they were drinking and checking for IDs even when only drinking soda. 21 and over were also harassed about their IDs repeatedly throughout the night and questioned even after they were checked at the door by a bouncer. Overall a terrible experience here and wouldn't recommend to anyone. If you cannot treat guests that paid thousands of dollars to rent out the entire place with respect, I'd hate to see how they treat normal guests.
The food was great and the music was wonderful! Only thing keeping it from 5 stars was that it took am hour to get our food. We chalk it up to the size of the crowd, being CMA Awards week.

Walking down to will call at the Schermerhorn, I felt like I was on the Titanic. Equally, wandering around the ornate hallways and even restrooms on our way to the orchestra level, I couldn't help but imagine that's exactly what it would have looked like when it flooded back in 2010.

It took me too long to get here but the symphony was really as beautiful as everyone said it was. Just gorgeous. The sound is also excellent. We saw Smokey Robinson which was a great experience. I love how they have pop acts in addition to traditional symphony performances such as Handel's Messiah. 

The balconies were stunning and I can't imagine there's a bad seat in the house. This is something anyone who lives in Nashville must do once (but you'll want to do it more) and is also great for tourists. Since the venue is in the heart of downtown, you could easily make a big night of it by going to the honky tonks in your dress clothes afterwards!
Long wait, less than thrilled hostesses, waitress that doesn't know the menu, and a 35 minute for cold food. Disappointed.

This place has the best trash taco! The presentation is beautiful and ingredients are top
Notch ! 
Everywhere life music is present and all musicians are soooo talented. Needless to say great live music here. AJ is awesome musician and great vocals!

Well... what a disappointment. The drinks were very pleasing and did a good job buttt the problem ended up being the price of the salad I got. I have gone to Kroger and got lettuce and chicken for $5 and this establishment decided to charge me $16 for this nonsense. But other than that great place!

Yo listen up, here's the story
About a little guy that lives in a blue world
And all day and all night and everything he sees is just blue
Like him, inside and outside
Blue his house with a blue little window
And a blue Corvette
And everything is blue for him
And himself and everybody around
'Cause he ain't got nobody to listen
... I'm blue da ba dee da ba daa
Da ba dee da ba daa, da ba dee da ba daa, da ba dee da ba daa

My wife and I had a memorable lunch at Margaritaville. We had a friendly, funny and helpful waitress - Sydney. Good food, great wait staff and listening to live country music. What a nice lunch. We will make sure Sydney waits on us when we come back.

Had drinks on the rooftop bar during Labor Day weekend.  Nice view of the lake and of the other buildings around.  Service was excellent with friendly staff.  Drinks were overpriced and my specialty cocktail was unimpressive.
Just ok ... service was ok food not so great ... Burger  came out a little over cooked and nothing was hot .... more like Luke warm French fries were cold. Never got my second beverage.

From Florida  and looking for a mid-day snack and a drink on a busy day of sightseeing and shopping in Nashville.  We stopped at Margaritaville because it was a familiar name, and honestly some of the nearby places were so crowded and didn't look like they would pass their next health inspection!   This place had live music in the bar area and plenty of open seating so we came in to check it out.

There were five ladies in our group and we decided to order a few appetizers to share. We got the appetizer trio, an order of buffalo chicken wings, and a southwest salad with chicken and split them all up.  We asked our server for 5 sharing plates.  The salad was good & easy to split up.  The wings were meaty but they had  a little too much watery buffalo sauce on them.  As for the trio; the southwest egg rolls were a little over cooked, and the spinach dip, chips, and chicken tenders were just ok. 

We did enjoy our nice cold beers at a good price and our service was really good.   We weren't hungry or thirsty anymore and we left recharged for more shopping.

In town for a Volleyball tournament with my daughter. Didn't check any reviews so we did not have any type of expectations. Started with the skillet cornbread. Delicious! 

The pulled pork bbq sandwich was our main dish. Really tasty...the sauce had a slight kick and nothing too overpowering. Good flavor and ample portions as me and my daughter split the sandwich and cornbread. We didn't finish everything and had plenty to eat.

The artist signing was pleasant and easy listening. Good voice and good start to the day. (Sophia Bollman)

I haven't attended any concerts here, but my friend just had her wedding here and this location was beyond perfect! 

The stage was a great size, the seating was perfect for the amount of people that attended the wedding, and the staff was very helpful. 

We had a "bridal suite" to get ready in and it was the perfect size for our bridal party. The lighting in the entire venue was great. Even the outdoor corridors were perfect for the wedding pictures and bridal party pictures. 

I'm going to have to come back to see a concert here. I've already fallen in love with the place and can't imagine this venue being a bad spot for anything.

Just had a couple of beers there and listened to music. The band was great and the atmosphere and audience was nice too! Cool area to walk around in. Different from downtown, which allows for a good bit of variation to do not only the tourist bars. Fun place to hangout late night!

Cute little bar on Nashville's Honky Tonk strip.
Seemed mostly suited for older crowds.  Live classic country and folk music.

One of the BEST honkey tonk bars on Broadway! The staff is the pure definition of southern hospitality, Haley made it worth going back again! Great music, super reasonable prices and just a fun time!!

Beer is fantastic, tons of great options for any beer palate...  crew is knowledgeable and friendly.  Love the emphasis on utilizing local ingredients.  Can't wait to go back when I'm in Nashville again.  Keep up the great work!

Overall a pretty cool arena that I had never been to until the most recent SEC basketball tournament. Some of my beefs with the experience here were outside of their control and falls more on the SEC. No way that the SEC reads this... but it is 2019 and you should sell alcohol at the games. Living in a prohibition era causes the same issues as they did in the 20s and people are going to do it illegally and recklessly when it isn't readily available. Even on the club level that we gained access to, you weren't able to take a beer to your seat. Absolutely ridiculous.

Anyway, going back to the arena, it was very clean and well organized. The staff was fantastic at every turn. And the facility itself had great seats and no real bad view that I could tell. I have wanted to come here for a hockey game and its proximity to Broadway proved to be a great time. So I will definitely have to come back.

Four of us were there for lunch on May 2nd. Since Blake Shelton is part owner we thought we'd give it a try. Steel Magnolias was on stage and they were OUTSTANDING!. My wife and I shared fried chicken and it was very good....not the best in the world but not the worst. We ordered a local blonde beer and it came out cold and was actually good for a local beer we'd never heard of. We were probably there for an hour and our waitress was attentive the whole time. I'd definitely come back.
Absolutely amazing music in a fun atmosphere! Real country music right on Broadway! Great music and good times.

Was here on Sunday night. Arrived a little after 9:30. Sat at a table waiting for service until  10:20.  We asked a couple of staff for menus and a waitress, never happened. We finally pulled another waitress over at 10:20 and she said the kitchen closed at 10 and btw, this isn't her section!
Won't be back.

Great place after shopping and walking down Broadway to stop for a drink, a bite to eat and some good ole live music. They have several floors (3 or 4) and a rooftop bar. There is a great view of Nashville from the rooftop bar. I asked for an iced tea (non alcoholic), and the bartender comped it for me.
Great place.

This is an interesting property with plenty of places to sit and things to do. They have seating options from outside on the patio to inside the big room where they actually make the beer. They have a room with a dart board and other games. They also have a stage downstairs with a live band.

The brewery is kind of hidden, so it will feel like the GPS is taking you the wrong way. It's below a bridge so you need to go around a few blocks to get down there. We went during the day and it felt safe, but it is an area with a lot of abandoned buildings so I wouldn't recommend you try walking there at night (take an Uber).

The beer was good craft beer. Plenty of varieties to choose from so you will find something you like!

A great venue location.  Its close to the night life and restaurants.  Prior to the game, we ate at the BBQ joint located a few blocks away, and then went to the arena.

Came here to see my Ducks play the Preds, and we stayed at the Hampton Inn just across the street from the parking lot.  Excellent hotel as well.

The arena is one of the newer ones in the NHL so their sightlines in the lower bowl are excellent.  The only thing about the arena that bugged me is the crowd.  I felt I was at a minor league game.  The chants and crowd reaction reminded me of going to a Long Beach IceDogs game.  The chants are ok... but at least make them positive.  Yeah yeah, I'm the enemy.. so what?  Tell me to go back to Anaheim?? Yeah, I will.  But 60 minutes of hearing this was like nails on the chalkboard.

Anyhoo, I tried not to belittle them and say they're hillbillies, but by golly they sure act like they are.

4 stars for a nice arena and great lower bowl... but the crowds... wow, really? Minus one for that.

Public Service Announcement! Bachelor and Bachelorette Parties, I highly recommend avoiding this place as the management and STAFF are EXTREMELY UNPROFESSIONAL, DISRESPECTFUL, and DANGEROUS. 

We were in town last weekend (October 5th) to celebrate my brother's bachelor party. We flew from California, at great expense, to come to Nashville because we love country music and could hardly wait to celebrate. Unfortunately, our first night we decided to check out Blake Shelton's bar, Ole Red. My brother was enjoying the live music and out of nowhere security grabbed him and another member of the party and told them to leave. While they were having fun, they were not being aggressive or disruptive. When they asked why they were getting kicked out, the bouncer aggressively grabbed my brother and threw him off a three-step landing onto concrete paving. He smashed his knee and hit his head extremely hard on the concrete.  He was unable to get up for a lengthy period of time and the police were called by people in line who witnessed the incident.  He had to go to the doctor upon return to address his injuries.  My brother is not an aggressive man and the staff's use of unnecessary excessive force was completely unjustifiable. 

The next night I went back to the bar to talk to management about the incident and they were unwilling to discuss the matter and told me to leave and "just file a police report." AVOID THIS PLACE AT ALL COSTS unless you want to be aggressively mistreated. 

As a substitute I recommend checking out Jason Aldean's Kitchen & Rooftop Bar, super-fun place with professional staff.

Atmosphere is fun. Service is excellent. Food is decent. I loved my burger and margarita. My group's enjoyment of their food was hit and miss. We had fun. I'm not sure if we will choose it again, because of the hit and miss food enjoyment. But if it opportunity came up I would try it again. After all I enjoyed my food and drink:0). Maybe we will enjoy it more as a whole next time.

The food and music was awesome.  It would have been 5 stars but based on the experience, we were sitting at the bar waiting for a seat and they took all the chairs away.   Then we went to a table to eat then they took all the tables away that was surrounding us. We were sitting in front of the stage eating on a island. It was uncomfortable because  we felt all eyes were on us and rusheto eat.

Coincidentally was in town during a hockey playoff game and was able to enjoy to the Nashville Predators vs. Dallas Stars.  Really nice stadium and fun giveaways while we were there.  Fans were really friendly, including the Dallas Star fans.  Food was pretty good (hot dogs, burger, bbq) and quiet a few bars within the stadium for beer/wine/spirits.  Arena is right in the downtown area where all the "action" resides!!

Came for lunch and drinks. Good live music and quesadillas were awesome. If you try an appetizer, definitely share a quesadilla. They're huge and have some good sides. But, the drinks were meh and overpriced. Service was horrible! We ended up getting our own drinks from the bar after waiting 25 minutes. Come hungry and with low expectations and you'll be fine.
This is a really nice place. Everyone is very kind here and it's very organized. I love the lighting, it's really beautiful. I would go here again.

The Schermerhorm Symphony Center in Nashville is a beautiful new venue built in 2006 for the Nashville Symphony and is located off Broadway near the new Country Music Hall of Fame and the Nashville Predator hockey arena.

I remember when the Symphony played a TPAC and worked so hard and long to raise the money for the new venue.It was built to acoustically enhance many types of music and they have the ability to change panels for different performances.

Not only is it acoustically pleasing venue, but it is beautiful as well with all of the natural stone and woodwork.

I have seen everything from the symphony to Bill Cosby at this venue and I have never been disappointed in the seating.

We enjoyed their beers, the venue itself was spacious and had a nice patio. The parking on the other hand was confusing and slightly difficult due to a large delivery truck blocking the way. Service was relatively slow, but we weren't in a huge hurry. We shared a flight of IPA's.

Great beers! Had time to kill before heading to the airport and stopped in for a couple of brews. All were great. Atmosphere was good and the staff were all super friendly and helpful! We also had 2 kids with us and the environment was good for them in the afternoon hours.

We went for the Friday happy hour w Sirius xm the highway. Now, I know jimmy buffet is a star and his place is a tourist trap and no matter what it draws a crowd regardless. But the drinks were 10 bucks a piece and taxes on top of that. I ordered 2 drinks from the menu and my total was 24$. That's highway robbery. No pun intended haha. But furthermore we'll go back bc it's fun and it is margaritaville.

We walked over to Tennessee Brew Works, one of Nashville's popular craft breweries, after hitting up Jack White's Third Man Records shop nearby. Both businesses are located in Pie Town, a neighborhood on the southern edge of downtown Nashville. There's not a whole lot of stuff in this part of town. These are definitely two of the highlights.

Tennessee Brew Works opened on August 18, 2013. It's popular. This place has won numerous awards and earned plenty of recognition including the best brewery in Tennessee according to Yelp. These folks are all about being local, green, and sustainable. The taproom is two stories with views of the brewery from both floors. There's a patio with both covered and uncovered spaces (mostly uncovered) as well as a small, string-lit rooftop patio. As this is a brewery, the property has an industrial, warehouse feel to it, much like the other businesses in Pie Town. It's clean and modernized. The first floor of the brewery features a small stage for live music (a band was setting up on our way out) and the room upstairs, which is much more spacious, has TVs playing sports and nice overhead views of the brewery floor below.

Brewery tours take place every Saturday at 3pm, 4pm, and 5pm. It costs $10 plus tax and a fee per person. Tickets for the tour can be purchased online.

Along with high-quality craft beer, the brewery also serves food. Their limited menu includes apps/snacks like Baja fish tacos, Springer Mountain chicken wings, salads, burgers, and sandwiches (including a Nashville Hot Chicken Sandwich). Food prices range from $8 to $18 per plate.

We grabbed a few beers and hung out inside the taproom downstairs. Downstairs, they use barrels (some with tabletops) for tables with bar stools. We showed up around 2pm on a Saturday and the place was busy. It wasn't slammed or jam-packed, but most of the tables upstairs and downstairs were taken. Our group of six was lucky to find a table in a corner next to some brewery windows. The atmosphere was very relaxed and laid back. The staff was cool and friendly. We all enjoyed our time here.

I don't think Tennessee Brew Works has dedicated parking. We parked for free on the street (Middleton Street because we also went to Third Man Records). This isn't the nicest neighborhood so I wouldn't leave any valuables in your car.

Horrible food. Server was great but the food was horrible. It was so loud in here and music was horrible too. Not worth the money or the time. And darn tho. Supposedly jimmy was there yesterday. If he had the southwestern salad he knows how bad it is. NO TASTE. The chicken grilled in any other restaurant is way better. I'm highly disappointed. Won't go back.

I've enjoyed concerts at the Schermerrhorn in past years but am excited that they have really stepped out of the box and have been offering so many diverse options for enjoying their venue. They're truly trying to draw and entertain all ages and tastes. 

I've recently attended two concerts that I purchased tickets for through Groupon; the music of Elton John by Michael Cavanaugh and big band music styles with Seth McFarlane. Both concerts were incredible. In each case the seats are limited to certain areas but there are no bad seats there. We were in the balcony last night and the acoustics are phenomenal. Purchasing tickets off Groupon is an affordable way to experience some of the best talent of Nashville's musicians. The Nashville Symphony played two very different styles of music and killed it both nights. The can rock out or romance the heart. 

If you've never been then a good thing to know is that you don't have to dress up. Pull yourself together in your shorts or jeans and just go. Of course, there are plenty who choose to dress up but don't feel you have to. 

Purchasing through Groupon has been an easy process too. We've had no issues.  Again, there are no bad seats in the place. I've sat in several different sections now and have been pleased each time.

Centrally located close to downtown. Lots of areas to hang out and games to play in a brewery setting. Since they actively brew onsite you can see them working on their brews during the day. They have a wide array of beers and use fruits in a lot of them. While I'm not a fan of fruity beer, they do a good job to not let it be over powering. They offer flights where you can enjoy tasters of your pick of beers. They do a good job instructing you on the order it which to drink them. They usually have a seasonal and rotating collaborations that are fun to try. Outdoor seating is offered but on hot days, they have an indoor area with good AC. 

For food they offer an array or Southern Favorites with a different flair of ingredients. Definitely not boring fair. The Nashville Hot Chicken Sandwhich is very good.

This place was disappointing all around. As a local on a Saturday night, we were looking to end the night away from the typical bars and have a couple drinks. As we walked in, we were told from the door guy that we had to buy something and couldn't just use their restroom. The line to Acme was long so I understand that that probably happens a lot. A waitress came up to us on our way to the bar to sit down to make sure that we were also buying something. It was over kill on their part and the service was poor from that point on. Being harassed to pay for something and then having to wait 10 minutes to order an over priced  $7 regular domestic draft beer is too much. Needless to say, I won't return and I'll be sure to pass this experience along.

How do you even justify food this bad?  And the service was okay, but our nachos ( liquid cheese, just don't do it) were cold, twice! (We sent them back but the server offered no condolences when they were cold the second time.  It wasn't even worth it at that point to send it back again).   Our burgers were rare ( we ordered medium well), but most importantly, the food was just awful and low quality.    I still feel terrible two days later.

My sister and I came to Nashville for the CMA fest and decided to try MargaritAville for the first time ever anywhere. The atmosphere and wait staff were exceptional. The food was delicious and we liked it so much that we went back sunday before we left to go home. Our waiter was Clark and he went above n beyond to make sure we had a great experience. experience. Looking forward to next year. CMA FEST &MARGARITAVILLE= paradise. Only thing that'd make it better would b to win a trip to Nashville to the CMA FEST N AWARDS PLUS MARGARITAVILLE.

Last night was my first visit to the Schermerhorn/Nashville Symphony for a concert. A friend and I went to see Little River Band. A band from the 70's that I grew up listening to on the Radio.

The building itself is gorgeous. Decorated with beautiful chandeliers and box seats lining the sides of a long theater. And the view and acoustics were great no matter where you are in the auditorium.

We happened to have to test on the left side of the stage in box 25 which were excellent seats. And we really enjoyed the show. 

The Nashville Symphony/Schermerhorn Symphony was a wonderful place to see a concert. Parking was relatively close and I believe they also had valet parking. I will definitely be back soon for another show very soon.
A GREAT place to catch a hockey game. Close reasonable parking within walking distance we parked for $10. Sat in the 3rd deck but the seats were great. The atmosphere was good.

My boyfriend and I stayed across the street so decided to come by and check it out as we were driving through from Texas. The bar set up was pretty cool, the beer selections were decent, and the band was fantastic! The service was alright, but a drunk guy shoved through me to order before me though I was next to be served. We ordered beers and found a spot to stand by the trash away from everyone and a couple ran into me twice while drunkenly dancing, knocking some of my beer out, (the floor was wide open and we were right next to the trash) which was annoying. We went over to the Losers side and it was quiet--needed after Winners. Then a man came up and asked everyone on the patio from the sidewalk for money. Everyone was belligerently drunk. Some patrons were barefoot. Overall very underwhelming experience

Great food and amazing service! A must go for Nashville tourist; make sure to try the Cheeseburger in Paradise.... It's exactly as imagined. The gift shop also had a variety of options for your favorite Jimmy Buffett gear!
My family was here on Saturday for the Free Day of Music, and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves.  The facilities are gorgeous, the staff was friendly and the music fabulous!
Pretty good place, kinda pricey but that's what you get for a country star owned bar on Broadway. Excellent views of the town though.

The only reason I'm giving 1 star is because I have to and because the police doing crowd control were more friendly and helpful than the staff.

If you are over 5'5 and about 150lbs don't waste your money. These seats weren't just cramped-they were criminal. There was ZERO leg room. I spent a couple hours with numb toes and my knees literally in strangers backs before we finally had enough and left mid concert. That was last night and today I feel like I was in a car wreck and have the bruises to show for it. For 6 of us to drop almost $1800.00 on tickets, this was a huge disappointment. I saw a few reviews mention the seat are terribly uncomfortable but if you're like me and chance it thinking some folks can be dramatic, let me assure you IT'S BAD! 

In the event you want to peel yourself out of your "seat" and climb over 20,000 other people to get a break, you'll find rude employees and $15 beer. One would think with the concession prices and ticket prices they could give you more than a toddler seat. Never again.

I was only here for a couple drinks when I was in Nashville for a couple days and there was great live music but unfortunately the upstairs was closed off. Prices were reasonably compared to the other bars on Broadway.
This is a great place.  The staff was friendly and prompt. We had the tater tots and they were great.  Beer is solid and really clean.  Great work.
The bouncer was rude and condescending.  Unnecessary treatment of a 20 year Nashville native.
good enviroment for something quick.  to top it off the line on a thurs night wasn't bad at all

The staff and security are beyond rude. Waiting in the security line, I was inches away from being totally doused with water from a tent that had rain on it so they decided to shake it all off next me.. with no warning Seemed intentional to me.  Once I got past that part, I got yelled at for not showing the proper part of my wrist for stamping. 
Okay.. get in.. stupidly long time to get a drink. Watered down  $7.00 itty bitty drink. 
The Mummies come on stage to play. The acoustics were so bad that it was hard to understand the lyrics and it's all completely muddled sounding. 
So.. I decide to leave early.  My date preferred to stay and finish out the show and wanted to walk me to my car since we were parked quite a distance away and quite frankly, the area can be sketchy. 
They told him he wouldn't be let back into the venue.. despite his wrist stamp. Despite the fact that there were 2 staff and 1 security guard at the door and it was quiet at the door.  The security guard was super confrontational with my guy and almost asking for a fight.. talking to him as if he was a teenager. My guy is a businessman.. he's 61.  Really? 
SO..  all these staff and security and I had to walk to my car alone and pray that I didn't get mugged or worse. WAY TO GO !  This place was beyond disappointing . Also, my guy and about 50 other people got soaked by the rain waiting for their Uber rides since there's no shelter to wait once you are outside the building. That and the price hijacking for a holiday ( Halloween weekend ) resulted in a $45.00 ride to his office which was only a few miles away.   Nashville has WAY better venues than this...  train your folks better, get better lighting in the parking lots and maybe offer a bit of shelter for your paying guests who have to wait in the elements because staff and security have power issues and inflated egos.  Get with the times, Marathon Music Works.

Let's get the fact that getting tickets to watch my beloved Chicago Blackhawks was near impossible, and normal Saturday night tickets here would be $117, but we paid $239 when we were finally able... 
the venue is marvelous, the location itself is a bonus! Walking distance to a multitude of bars for  pre game drink. 
The stadium has PLENTY of vendors, I never had to wait for a beer! And those cans, seriously huge. The draft was amazing, bottom fill with magnets?! It was like watching a magic trick, I just wanted to get beers to watch this trick! Bathrooms were clean and easily accessible, never waited more than five deep. 
Other small details I really enjoyed:
- the band during period break
- the popcorn 
- and OMG soft serve. It was creamy and not gagging sweet. The waffle cone addictive! I keep thinking about this treat! I'd go back just for this!
Great time, of course the win was a bonus.

Wonderful venue in the heart of Downtown Nashville. Just a short walk from The Gulch Neighborhood, and a short mile to the Midtown neighborhood. I've been there for concerts, Predators Hockey, and most recently, for the SEC basketball tournament. Seats are comfortable with cup holders. Food and Beverage facilities are numerous with good variety. The only reason for no 5  Star rating is that the men's restrooms are too small. Just five urinals with lines 8 to 10 deep during halftime break.
Big changes coming to the backside of the arena! The Brand New Music City Convention Center opens in May, and Bridgestone Arena will get an attractive second entrance facing the convention center.  It will include "light retail" -- either in merchandising or food and beverage -- at Demonbreun, plus some larger retail or restaurant options likely on Fifth Avenue, creating a connection between the Music City Center campus and the existing entertainment district on Broadway.

I stopped here with a friend while visiting Nashville and absolutely loved the look and feel. They have nice outdoor seating as well as a rooftop deck. They also have flights as well as full glass pours and food. I had the Thai basil saison which was something extremely unique to me. It was delicious and well priced! I recommend a visit.

Best part of the night...Maroon 5.  Now let's dive in to the rest...... 

First off I can't address parking because we took an Uber to the show.  I despise driving in downtown Nashville do I never do it.  From what I could see though, it looked to be a nightmare.

Entry was as expected.  Never take large bags to these events unless you enjoy unpacking everything in front of complete strangers.  That's why I dont do it.  Staff at the front was friendly and professional got us moved through rather quickly.  Hold ups had nothing to do with the staff, it was all the women under the impression that a huge bag was a necessity and unwilling g to let go of the cell phone for even a second.  But...I digress.

Did not like the fact that a bottled water was $5 and it had to be poured in to a cup with no lid or straw.  That was a pain in the ass to carry around.

Although the sections themselves are easy to find the rows were difficult in the dark.  We managed though.  The seats were awful.  I can not express enough the torture of sitting in that chair for 2.5 hrs.  There is zero room.  I had nowhere to put my arms and Lord help you if your neighbor has a drink...in a cup...without a lid...next to you.

Leaving was the typical cattle herding that always follows these types of things so nothing out of the ordinary there. 

We were taking another Uber back to our car and there is a specific area that you have to meet them at.  That area is not clearly marked and unless you go to Bridgestone all the time you really just have to keep looking for the yellow vests to ask for directions.  We asked one of the security guards who replied with "the south doors".  I'm one of those "make a right at the rusty tractor" kind a gals. South is just a noun to me.

So in short.  Come on Bridgestone.  With the cash you have coming in...get some dang signs made and stop making people deal with cups.

Always great! Huge shout out to Genesis for her awesome service Sunday. We really enjoyed her humor. 
We've tried other places but always return to Ol Red for the consistency.
I love going to hockey games here. Great food choices, the employees are really nice.

I was very excited for my first experience at the Schermerhorn Symphony center, but oh was I let down. I recently went for a movie concert, where the symphony overlays the scores from the movie. Neat idea and well executed. The talent of the symphony is unrivaled and that was an absolute pleasure to listen to. My poor rating is the result of my dissatisfaction with the entire staff at the symphony center. I was defrauded out of my two tickets when I showed up because the box office printed the wrong tickets and voided the bar codes on my tickets. I ended up not being able to get in and was forced to sit outside for the entire first half of the show. When I raised the issue and showed my proof of purchase, each information stand sent me to a different one. No one would take any responsibility and even after the fact, they told me I was SOL. It's truly unfortunate when you pay hundreds for tickets, take a nice date, then completely embarrass yourself at the hands of someone else's mistake and they don't even take responsibility for it. Oh well, I don't plan to return. My advice is to get there very early and plan for issues to arise so that you're not left epically disappointed.

4 of us went here last night for dinner and some music. Cool vibe. Decent beer selection. The music sounded good, but we never made it to the music room for the show. We made the mistake of getting dinner. The place wasn't crowded at all. Maybe 4 tables of people and a few people at the bar. But it took 45 minutes for our food to come out. Then when it arrived it was not so great. My husband's burger was burnt tough and way over seasoned. Our friend's meatloaf sandwich had a gassy flavor. Just not good.

But our biggest mistake? Bringing our concerns up with the staff. Our waitress was great about it. Immediately apologized and insisted on getting a fresh burger. The chef of the night came out to talk about the meatloaf. He was friendly and explained the flavor was just a result of their smoke and deep fry method of making the meatloaf...? 

But then. Then! Here comes the manager. I don't know if he thought we were causing trouble or trying to get free food, but he was immediately hostile, accusatory, defensive, and down right rude. He demanded my husband give him his plate even though the waitress told us to keep the plate and eat the fries while the new burger was being made. When we tried to explain that, the manager threatened to charge us for 2 burgers if we kept the plate. He insisted on taking the plate, removing the burger, and bringing the fries back...? It was so incredibly bizarre. My husband refused to give up his plate and the manager left in a huff. 

Then, here comes the executive chef who just so happened to be there having dinner himself. He was initially abrasive and up in arms about us not liking his food, saying his reputation was on the line. He was very pushy, repeatedly asking what we did and did not like about the food. He got really enthusiastic about it, punching his palm to emphasize his point. It was all very uncomfortable and intimidating.

The waitress came back a few more times for clarification on our complaints. The chef of the night came back again about the burger. The executive chef came back again at some point. Soooo many people kept coming to talk to us about the issue. It just got blown way out of proportion. Needless to say, that completely soured the whole experience for us. 

Before the manager came over we were enjoying ourselves despite the food. Planned to spend the money to go see the band. Talking about how the place was cool and promising. But now I don't think I'll go back. New businesses should bend over backwards to make customers feel welcomed and appreciated. I felt like I was in trouble. Just not at all how I wanted to spend my night.
Can't lift a finger in the place place without their try hard bouncers harassing you but they do have some of the dankest bacon I've ever eaten

Awesome location and great experience.  Server Jen on rooftop bar was excellent. Blake showed up several times that week because it was CMA fest week.  We were there for my daughters college tour at Trevecca.  Couldn't believe missed Trace Adkins from the previous day.  The line looks long, but moves quickly and it was busy during CMA Fest.  Efficient staff who handled the crowds well.  We went several times during our 4 days in Nashville.  Food, drinks and service all good.  They know what they are doing...Giant pretzel is fun as an appetizer.

The food here is great, but the service and the wait are horrible. Waited over and hour for our food (with very few people in the restaurant) and was then informed that our ticket was never put in. We won't be back.

The man. 
The myth.
The legend.
The sub par franchise on lower Broadway.

My friend and I came here at 5 pm on Wednesday night before a show at the Ryman. It was not super crowded like the rest of these newfangled country star bars popping up every other day so we were sat pretty quickly in the back. This was my preference as the entertainment upfront for the night was letting everyone know sometimes she says deez nuts while she's singing to see if people are even paying attention *charming*. 

The last mango in Paris is a delightful drink. The lethal kind where you don't taste the alcohol until after you drink all of it. In addition we split the Lava Lava shrimp which taste like the unfiltered joy of seeing Jimmy Buffett ride off into the sunset on the back of a dolphin. For the main entree I almost always get the Cheeseburger in Paradise which is ol' reliable in my book. I know it's not very adventurous but it's safe and always gets the job done. It's also my second favorite JB song so it has that going for it too. 

The reason I'm not crazy about this location is because the staff is very inattentive. We never got the side of ranch we both ordered and we never saw our server unless the food + check were ready. Water refills and another round of tequila were out of the question as she stayed MIA.

I think I dub this as more of a drinks/apps/atmosphere kind of mood instead of a full on dining experience. Choosing it as the latter may end up as a letdown as much as it pains me to say. 

But God bless Jimmy and those shrimp.

The new renovations have really taken this place up to the next level! Usually, at music venues, there is going to be one area that's hit and miss, generally the food. Not in this case, the food is great bar food, perfect to soak up all the draft beers and drinks that aren't way overpriced like they are two blocks away. It's nice to sit at the bar and catch a game, then walk down the steps to live music. The acoustics are also great, you don't get overwhelmed in the main room by the sound of the band and the noises aren't popping off everywhere in the space, considering the size. Great lunch spot, too! So happy this place is back again and even better!

Traveling through Nashville I had just one evening to see the sights and I decided to walk down Broadway and find a place that wasn't too busy and had a real bluegrass band playing. There's nothing wrong with pop-country, but I was definitely looking for something with a little more twang.

The bar service was great and the prices comparable for any major city. It never became too busy and I ended up staying until closing time chatting with lots of folks there.

If you are in Nashville and looking for a lower-key but still lively music spot, Layla's is your place!
Tammy Cook was a fantastic server for Buzz's happy hour.  Awesome time and great sense of humor!
Great service and outstanding food. Also offer bottomless mimosas for brunch! We loved the staff! Highly reccommend!! Hidden treasure on broadway!!

The Bridgestone Arena has plenty of things to like from the obvious things you would look for in an arena/stadium to the little things.  The obvious thing being, that no matter where you sit, you can see all the action.  The pricing of tickets here is also extremely reasonable, especially if you are comparing it against any bigger city.  There are always plenty of events happening, from hockey to concerts as well.  It isn't hard to get a ticket either, which is miraculous if you compare it to trying to get tickets to a show in say NYC.  My favorite little thing, as random as this may sound, there are bathrooms everywhere!  There are concession stands everywhere, and if you are willing to make the venture also fairly decent beer selection.  If you happen to live in/near or are visiting Nashville, take advantage of the arena!

Bar staff was super great. Great drinks, food was just average. Like other places on Broadway they had live music and the band at this time was kinda weird but we were sitting in the bar area so we just ended up tuning them out.

Nice restaurant & bar. The food is great and large serving. Well staffed, wait is very short. They also follow the maximum number of people they let in. The bands are great. There is also a souvenir shop inside. The top floor is family friendly, the balcony is looking down to the stage with a huge screen, the main floor is where you get close to the music. Combination of rustic & contemporary decor. Large windows, doesn't feel claustrophobic.
Will sure come back next time I visit Nashville !!!

Could be a very fun place and seemed like the people on the losers side were having way more fun!  Food was decent and happy hour prices weren't too bad either. Had serious trouble trying to pay our bill.  Their card reader was broken or messed up somehow.  That caused a huge inconvenience for the whole group.  Didn't check out the rooftop because after the payment issue we were ready to move along.  May or may not come back....there's so many places to choose from.
Ole Red's Honky Tonk (owned by Blake Shelton). Full bar, restaurant and gift shop. Across the street from Luke Bryant's honky tonk and Kid Rock's honky tonk. Tons of live music and craziness.

My first time here was last weekend when the weather was finally warm. I am loyal to Yazoo but I wanted to give this place a shot. First of all, the patio is AMAZING!! Obsessed with it. It is huge! The inside is designed really well. You can see where they make the beer, not to mention there are 2 bars and some tables made from whiskey barrels (I want one of these!). 

The beer was fantastic! I tried the Basil Ryeman previously at a local restaurant and liked it. After getting the sampler, I love the Southern Wit and the sweet potato stout even more. Can't remember the clever name for that one. The beers were reasonably priced and the bartenders were fantastic! 

For food, it looks like they were selling popcorn and had a food truck. Live music too! I'll be back.. many times.

My wife and I visited Tennessee Brew Works on a muggy Tuesday afternoon during our trip to Nashville. The bar area/tasting room was not crowded and had a relaxed atmosphere. Meanwhile the tank room was a hub of activity, and it was interesting to see the brewers at work.

My wife wasn't drinking, but I ordered a flight of beers. I really appreciated the wide variety of styles that TBW offered for their flights. I feel like some of the breweries in California have become a little too IPA-centric so it was nice to see a good mix of options. 

I chose the Southern Wit, Cutaway Rye IPA, 1927 IPA, City Winery Abbey Strong Ale, and the Chestnut Brown Ale. All of the beers were great but I especially enjoyed the City Winery Strong Ale as it had a tart cherry taste that made me feel like I was drinking Pinot Noir. 

Overall, we really enjoyed the beer and the chill vibes (although I'm sure this place is probably packed on a Friday night). We would definitely recommend stopping in and trying a few beers.

Beautiful  Place, great first floor band, roof top singer was good too. But.....Blake if you are reading this, in Oklahoma talk( fellow Okie) you need to dirty this place up a bit! Meaning, the band doesn't need to have such bright spot lights on them and be blocked off from the crowd. It needs to be more fun and interactive. 
Make it more fun!
Simply said - don't go, don't waste your time.... the men who work here are the rudest people ever!

From the moment we decided to take a Nashville trip, I knew we were eating here. Yes, it is touristy. Yes, they will most likely be a line. Don't be afraid to put your name on the list and walk upstairs to see if there is room at the bar or two couches that are open seating. While we were here the music that was being played was great. I had a beer on tap and ordered the poutine and kiss my ass quesadilla. For 2 people this was just the right amount of food to share. In my opinion the poutine was way better then the quesadilla. But everything we had was good. The atmosphere of this place was good. I think I expected something with more of a WOW factor. However, it's definitely a place to have a few beers and enjoy good country music with great food.

The review won't be long because even reviewing the arena I feel like a traitor. 

If I'm honest and this was my teams arena, I would have the same issue and there is only one. I have terrible knees so walking up all of the steps to get to the nosebleed seats was kind of frustrating. There may have been an escalator and if there was it was not marked well. I wouldn't have taken the elevator up bc I would have felt bad. 

Anyway, if I was in town again I would go to the arena for a hockey game, IF the Predators were playing the MN Wild!

Bachelor and Bachelorette parties please avoid this bar at all costs!! The employees at this establishment are unprofessional, disrespectful and use excess force when it is not necessary. I was with a bachelor party last weekend and Ole Red was the first bar that we visited. We were excited to be in Nashville and listen to some live country music. Our bachelor was near the front of the stage dancing and not bothering anyone (He was actually making everyone around him laugh and smile). While enjoying his last couple nights of freedom, two bouncers came up to our party and asked for us to move off the dance floor. We cooperated and left the dance floor. Once off the dance floor we were asked to leave the bar. Since we were doing nothing wrong we PEACEFULLY inquired into why we were being asked to leave. Without being told why we were being asked to leave, our bachelor who was just standing to the side was violently thrown out of the back door and off a flight of stairs. Unable to keep his balance due to the excessive force used to throw him out, he hit the ground causing a major knee and head injury. This use of force was unnecessary and 100% unprofessional. If you are looking for anyone in your party to be forcefully thrown off stairs go to this bar but if you are looking to have a Fun/Peaceful weekend do not go to Ole Red. Blake Shelton should be ashamed of his staff and their actions.

Everything was a disappointment.  Marginal food, very poor service, expensive.   In a world.... Lame.  Just because Blake Shelton own the joint does not make it good.   I wasted $90. Don't make the same mistake I did.
My Vietnam veteran was asked to leave do to taking pictures  in area of pissed off women who could not see the sub  par band  really Blake you  posser
If you're looking for good music with incredible food this is the place! 4 levels including a rooftop bar with gorgeous overlooks of the city really make this a must on your visit to Nashville!

For me there remains a certain reverence to walking into a Symphony Hall for a performance. It was not a place as children that we wore our "play clothes" or acted out in any way. Both my mother and my Grandma were classical Concert Pianists  who would practice the greats on the Steinway Grand Piano brought back from Germany daily. (My mom still has that piano in her living room to this day and still plays it regularly.)

So, for me maybe my impression of Handel's Messiah was slightly tainted as I am not fully up to date with our current "culture." To give some idea the last time we attended a Symphony was at the Kennedy Center in DC where we held season tickets and our last show was Arthur Fiedler conducting the Boston Pops for the annual Christmas performance. Long before computers, cell phones or yelp. Also, three grown adult children later we want to repeat what we saw and experienced. 

The symphony hall is spectacular and grand from the moment you enter. The volunteer staff provide you with great direction to get to your assigned seats and to ensure you have a program and know the start times that you need to be in place to be allowed entry. Of course we shoes up in full formal wear, including my wearing a Tux so we were totally out of place as the Symphony Hall has gone more to jeans and t-shirts than the attire we were accustomed to. No problem here, we enjoy dressing up and the lack of dress in others does not effect us. 

What we did not expect is as the Nashville Symphony takes the stage that people would have their phones out texting, recording the performance and even talking on their phones. I guess even the rules on the program and announced at various times are not intended for those who think they are special or important. Nothing beats listening to a really great solo and hearing somebody's phone with a Jay-Z ringtone go off on full volume. Oh, not once but on multiple occasions. 

We also had two young ladies in the row behind us who wanted to be heard and recognized so they continue to hoot, holler and yell at times. Apparently they were college students and wanted to gain the attention of the guest conductor and be discovered.  

The Schermerhorn Center did an excellent job, they were very professional, friendly and attentive. They did not make any attempt to create an environment for other to enjoy once inside the hall but I guess this would have maybe offended some of the noise makers and we couldn't have that. 

The Nashville Symphony was masterful and despite any distractions they did an amazing job in their performance. BRAVO!

Needed a dinner venue for a group of 19. I contacted Dena at Ole Red and she made it so easy! We were on the second floor mezzanine in our own section overlooking the live music.  The team had the taco bar set up and ready top go when we arrived.  We also ordered the spinach artichoke dip and it is so good! Melody was our server and she did an amazing job keeping the group happy and drink in hand.  The next night I needed a dinner reservation for 4 but nothing was available. I contacted Dena and she got me an awesome table right next to the stage! Above and beyond is the customer care at Ole Red.

Wow. This bar was extremely busy and we still felt like we were top priority. We went for music row happy hour and stayed for 4 hours! We never felt like they wanted us to GTFO and our experience was top notch. We ordered volcano nachos and chicken tenders. I would order just the chicken tenders again next time - the nachos were good, but they need to add ingredients layer by layer. All in all, we will make this a permanent stop when we go to Nashville!!!
I can't say anything bad about this joint. Beer flowin, friendly people. And a mash system I have never seen in Milwaukee. Straight from Belgium!! You need to visit now. And fall in love.

A fun place to catch some great live music and get a few drinks. Sat up at the bar on the 2nd floor overlooking the main stage and was treated to some lively country tunes played by up and coming performers. I'll say this, the drinks aren't cheap here but the location and the atmosphere definitely make up for it.

Acoustics are my main concern when I go to a concert, as it is more likely to make or break the experience for me than the actual artist. I wasn't sure what to expect from 12th & Porter's venue when I saw Eleanor Friedberger there, but I was pleasantly surprised by how good the sound is! Honestly, it probably has better acoustics than most of the venues in Atlanta that can hold 7x as many people.

I also ate at the bar before the show and enjoyed my pulled pork nachos. Their menu isn't very big, but based on my one trip I would have to say that the food is very good for bar food.

If you're ever in Nashville then I recommend looking into seeing a show at 12th & Porter!

Very much overrated.  Waited nearly two hours for only so so food. Small dining areas and tables turn over way too slowly.  They'd do well by having someone serving drinks to patrons waiting for a table as you couldn't get anywhere near the baR. Best part was the music for sure.

First time in Nashville and we popped in here for lunch. Victoria, our waitress, was awesome! The cherry limeades are delicious (we had 2 each)! The fried pickles and quesadillas were enough for us to share and so good! Live music was awesome! Would definitely recommend for anyone visiting Nashville!

This place is fantastic!  Nice shaded outdoor seating, beers, top-notch!  We had the 1927 IPA and the TENN No. 12 and both were excellent!  The Five Beer Burger was amazing and fries had a nice kick from the chili pepper? and other secret spices!!  Fish tacos get an 11 11 on 1-10 scale.  Wow.  Great job!!

At a bachelorette party this weekend, our group wandered into this place on a whim. Our entire experience was fantastic - as a group of 9 during the NFL draft and marathon weekend, we were seated within 20 minutes. The rooftop has a great vibe and great view, and the food was great. The best part, though, was the service. Everyone was extremely nice, attentive, and accommodating. Shoutout to Sean and Bella... y'all made our experience great! Thank you!

We stumbled in here because the menu looked so good. Later we found out that Blake Shelton owns it!! There was live music and the place was nice! The band was so good & got the crowd into it. The place was very spacious and had an entire upstairs for more dining/standing. The staff were all SO nice! Everyone was so friendly. Our waitress was so friendly, accommodating, always checked in on us, and provided excellent customer service! She was fabulous! There were so many things we wanted to order on the menu! Everything sounded so good. We decided to go with the redneck nachos without meat and the pimento Mac 'n' beer cheese. The redneck nachos were so good!! I wish they had more cheese on them, but it was piled on with so many different toppings! The barbecue sauce was SO good and everything about the nachos were delicious!! We ordered ours vegetarian and I somehow got ONE bite out of the entire nachos that accidentally had meat in it... so that was very unfortunate. The nachos were massive and definitely shareable. We saw someone else order it and thought they didn't even eat it... oh, they did, there was just no dent in it because it was so much food!! The pimento Mac 'n' cheese was not good... it was very bland. We even added sriracha to it and it still didn't taste good. I don't recommend getting that. 

Overall, the service was phenomenal, the music was amazing, & the redneck nachos were delicious!! I highly recommend coming here!!

We paid good money for this venue and the bartenders decided to cut me off after 2 drinks. The rent a cop wannabe bouncers assumed people's ID's were fake even if the were obviously well over 21. We were told we had an open bar from 7-11 but half the drinks we had to pay for and they were over priced. The treated our formal like it was the senior women's Baptist convention or something. The wanna be hardass bouncer would only let people use the bathroom one at a time like we were children. Honestly an event at a DMV would possibly be more fun then this ignorant ass shit hole. The candied bacon though was hella dope.
Amazing music and comfortable seating. Great location with an amazing staff. Love the decor and the vibe. Would come back here again and again.

Great venue for concerts. Plenty of parking. Recommend parking across the street at Music City Center, which is $15 vs. $25 at the arena. This is the home of our beloved Nashville Predators. There is a ton of eating and drinking options. There is plenty of security. The place is clean. You will have a great experience here.

Love the ambience with live music and great selection of beers. The 1927 and Sinsear are highly recommended and delicious. I had their five beer burger and fries and can't complain. Nice hidden gem in Nashville. Must try!

Stopped in for a Sunday Funday today. The upstairs had a private party so unfortunately we didn't get a chance to check out the whole place. Luckily we arrived early enough to claim two high top tables though so it worked out. The beer was pretty good, sampled several varieties around the table. The cheese board was absolutely beautiful, very impressive. A few people at the table had burgers and said they were also really tasty. The jazz music started at two and made it really loud downstairs. I'd love to come back when it's warmer because the patio looked spacious.

If you're a beer drinker, this is a must-visit when in Nashville. It's a beautiful space with a large, modern, well-designed tap room. This isn't Nash-Vegas! Take a tour, and be sure to try everything to experience the full range of what this brewer can do. The bonuses are that the owners are super friendly and helpful, and they're focused on brewing efficiently and conscious of their environmental impact.

I've never had a bad experience here, but I normally go for lunch when it's not crowded. If you're a tourist, I would go somewhere more authentic. I like this place because I love the beach and I love the vibes and I like live music. I've always liked the food, too.

Nothing stands out here, but was a decent arena for a concert, typical arena to most I've been to, the prices on the alcohol and food was a little much, but that's usually any arena you go to. Clean facility, and good sound, saw Metallica and I wasn't disappointed.

We ate Sunday brunch at Ole Red Rooftop. It was a rainy, indoor day so we didn't get the full value of the rooftop experience. $85 for a family of 4. Food and drink was ok. The service was outstanding. We had a large party and Kelsey was very patient and prompt. Next time we will sit on the main level for more casual dining and live music!

Great looking place, great server we had and great music but things went south from there.  Shocking in such a large building that the 2nd floor is where the restrooms are with only 4 stalls for ladies and with no toilet paper and hand towels and when you mention it to staff they didn't care or change it when we used them again.

I ordered the onion burger without a bun, had about 4 bites with using a knife and fork when was cutting into meat notice some foreign object inside burger.....thought it was a bug but my husband dissected this object and his conclusion was that it was part of the cows skin and hide!!! 
Showed our waitress and she took it to the manager to show him and he came back with the same answer my husband thought it was. And also my friend found same thing in her burger 3 others at our table had burgers but with buns so who knows if the skin and hide were in there burgers. I guess they get the meat locally and ground and packed right in nashville but that was disgusting to have to encounter that!!
 So disappointed as was so excited to get to Ole Red, place has lots of potential and hope Blake and his team fix all the kinks

I just had to have a drink at Margaritaville in Nashville, it was just a must. Not a very smart choice. The restaurant was extremely busy, super packed with people that you cannot enjoy it. The bartenders were not friendly whatsoever, this could be due to how busy they were..? Maybe? Hopefully... and their drinks are overpriced and lacked alcohol. There is better bars not as popular with better drinks and lower prices for you to try.

Tasty. 

The National Underground did not disappoint. My BF has been raving about their burgers for over a year now, so I stopped in over the weekend to test his taste buds. He did not lead me astray! 

We snagged a table outside and watched as our waitress frantically ran from table to table for a few minutes. After we got our drinks we had to ask about ordering food, but she dashed back over to grab our order after we flagged her down. They do not have printed menus; only food items printed on the wall with chalk. It's a pretty simple menu thankfully, so we didn't have any issue looking it over.  I had the grilled chicken sandwich and my friend had the cheeseburger, and both were excellent! The hamburger tasted homemade and had a regular sized patty; not the thick hunk of meat that often is the star of burger joints. I like that they keep it simple and delicious! My chicken sandwich was filled with flavor which is sometimes rare for chicken at a burger place. 

Apparently the grilled potatoes are amazing, but sadly they were out when we came so we had to stick with kettle chips. Also, no substitutions for other side items. I saw a deviled egg small plate that I must try on my next visit. I'm a sucker for those guys.

My overall first trip was awesome and I understand the hype now. They had a live band playing inside, so I'm not sure how conducive it is for a dinner where you want to talk to your companions, but I will definitely be back!

Food was ok but service was terrible. We were a party of 5. The server completely missed the 5th order. When the other 4 meals were served, there were no utensils and the server was nowhere to be found. Had to flag down three other servers before getting utensils. Got the manager involved 4 times in total. He comp'd the missed meal (which was still late and we got most of it to go) and offered free desserts. Told the server that we would order the desserts after we ate. Instead she just brought us the check (with no pen). Also $15 was added to the bill. The manager ended up bringing us the pen, to-go boxes for the late meal and two desserts (which is all we ordered) and corrected the bill. Wouldn't recommend this restaurant
You must eat here. I know this is a brewery, but the Chicken Wings and the Nashville Hot Chicken Sandwich...wow!!! In town for the Bowl Game but will be back EVERY time I make it to Nashville.
The beer is awesome and so is the food! We had the falafel and the fish tacos, both were great. Between my husband and I, we tried all the beer they had available. All were very good.

I've been here 3 or 4 times, and I've had a blast every time. It's a bigger room but it still has a small feel. You can't really have a bad view of the stage unless you are behind one of the two support beams on either side. You have two bars on both sides of the stage, and an actual, standalone bar called William Colliers that is connected to the venue, which people can come and go from.
Great time. We stopped in several times during our trip and it was awesome. Great drinks, great service. Katie and Barry at the bar were great! Ask for the Barry special!

Started off great, good food, good service great band, cort carpenter,  then it went to hell in a hand basket. Made us give up are table for the dance floor while we were still drinking, would not give us a different table without re waiting, manager had a bad attitude, didn't care at all about us staying or leaving, probably cost you at least another 100 dollars because I loved the band.  Long story shortened i come to Nashville frequent enough and i will never be back (which sucks because I was a big Blake fan)
Bad service, nasty food and wouldn't take a renewed government state issues I.D. For alcohol. Even with the expired license attached to it. Won't be back!

Came here for dinner tonight and ordered the fish tacos with a side of sweet potatoes. The food was great & the live music that accompanied it creates such a vacation-like environment. Definitely coming here again for beach cocktails to pretend it is a warm, sunny day.

Stopped in with my kids and wife. Greeted by a beautiful smile, sat down, and were introduced to a character of a waiter. Looked like a pirate(Chris M.)! The corn and calm chowder was amazing. Fish tacos and jumbalaya was perfect. I would come back anytime. Margaritaville rocks!

This was a really great Brewery! Lots of great beer choices and some good food! The chicken sandwich was amazing!
Service was somewhat sparse, which is why I gave it 4 stars.

I came here for the Predators Games, but this place is huge! It's well decorated for the Holiday Seasons. They are well staffed, which is great because they are all helpful and know where the good nachos are at. They have regular trash can and then recycling trash cans, that is awesome!! They have neat automatic sinks that are just a counter and that's it and automatic paper towel dispenser. Overall it's a great venue and clean!!! there's predators' merchandise is available everywhere, the shop is setup for easy shopping experience. They offer a variety of foods like tacos , burgers and etc. the only down side they only have on funnel cake stand. Last time I was there, the funnel cake stand took cash only. They is currently construction by the main entrance, so it gets congested by traffic. We usually park about a block away and walk. The arena is to downtown Nashville nightlife, so if you want to go celebrate the Predators winning just walk across and pick one of the many options. I definitely will consider coming here for a concert or 2! I just have a good time and a great experience everytime!
This is a bar has a very good atmosphere and the singer, Cort Carpenter has a very good voice. The staff was pleasant and friendly. The fried pickles are as good as my homemade ones. Enjoyed myself.

I'm not giving a review on the arena itself I'm giving a review on the concert last night everyone did well but the prize goes to baby face he did his thing it was a wonderful Valentine's concert I had a ball enjoying the performances of everyone.
Purchased a ticket online and was denied entry when I got to the concert because the bouncer claimed I was drunk when I was not. I asked for a refund and was denied. Classless venue

Good out door, double decker patio and porch area with live music with plenty of seats.  Good selection of local beers and wide arrange of options on the menu for food($9-$15). The hot chicken sandwich was not too spicy and came with fries (has a sweet & spicy flavor- which I really enjoyed!) and the Baha fish tacos were perfectly fried and flavorful.
