Their craft beer selection is on point- with flavors for all pallets. I'm not much of a hoppy beer person, so I really like their Southern Whit and their new seasonal, the Saison- tennesake and the seasonal pale ale, Wildwood Flower. If u are looking for a local brewery with a large/fun patio and unique/tasty beer options make sure this in on your list of places to go in Nashville!!

Biggest disappointment ever! Good was horrible! I had fish & chips and the worst margarita ever! So sweet! Awful! The safest part was the music. They played Santana, journey and other crisp! I didn't come to Nashville to listen to music that I could listen to anywhere in the world. Living in San Francisco I grew up on all that stuff I came to Nashville to hear country music what a complete disappointment never again.

I enjoy my time at Winners every time I go. I love the nights with Whiskey Jam. It's a good place to go do Karoje on Friday and Saturday night. On Sundays, it also a good place to watch the game. Reasonable prices on domestics. You should also try the Whiskey Jam blackberry flavored whiskey. I have only eaten fries with queso and chicken tenders here. Delicious. The bartenders are friendly, Codi is awesome.

Seriously, stopped in for the Eskimo brothers late on an afternoon.  top Notch rockabilly entertainment, as good as it gets.  small bar, nothing outstanding or different, just intimate with peeps having a good time.  The best this night for sure.

A stellar place in an odd, industrial road. It's a bit in the weeds, but worth the drive. Really great find. The staff is too notch, and eager to get you one of there awesome brews. They had 11 on tap when we were there, excellent variety and we tasted  them all ( 2 flights and a couple pints between us!). The favorites: 1927 IPA, Extra Easy and the Mild Davis. Each had great hops, and layers of subtle notes. Really great beers, and almost all 16oz pours at $6!. Now the food, we had the grilled Brie and the 5 beer Burger. The Brie was lovely, perfectly cooked and such good flavors. Pro tip: add the Bacon. The burger was unfortunately a miss for me. The bread was okay, the patty was large and perfectly cooked, and the cheese was awesome. But the onions and pickles were awful. Way too much salt, in the brine and the grilled onions. Tough to have such a good looking burger tasty so salty. But still a great bar and worth a visit!
I've Been to multiple predators games and one concert here. It's a great venue located in the heart of Nashville.

Cheers to the Bartenders!! SHANE is THE very best bartender I have had the pleasure of hanging out with for an evening of fun! He makes the best drinks, hustles the whole time all while making you feel like friends! Had such a great experience that it got us back for a second night in a row!! And we are so glad we did because two amazing singers, Jake & Faydra,  entertained the full house while Lindsey & Barry joined my list of great bartenders!!  You must try the Asiago Crab & Artichoke Dip and the Lava Lava Shrimp! In the sea of fun places on Broadway, this place is NOT to be passed up! We will DEFINATELY be back!

Went looking for local dive bar...found Dave.  After 6 requests to not be touched (on a quieter sunday night so space was far from an issue) we left because the creepy factor was aggressive and I dont take kindly to being groped. The band was great which made us sad to leave.  Everyone obviously knew each other but when we mentioned it to security on the way out, we received a less than reasonable response of mumbles before security went back to making out with his girlfriend, or flavor of the week, or whatever she  might be.

Had ran out of 3/4 of the starters on the menu at 530 on a Thursday.  Had to literally track down a waitress to order.  Don't waste your time...

Annndddd still waiting for waters...guess I shouldn't have held my breath...

This is where the visitors center and gift shop is located. It is centrally located and most of the workers inside and very helpful and great faces of the city. Just look for the spiral part of the building and you'll find the visitors center. There is also a brochure rack inside if you are looking for tips on what to do. I recommend the Nashville total access pass that they sell in here - $50 to 4 attractions plus free entrance to the Parthenon, 10% off in the gift shop and 25% off the Trolley Tour.
"Blake, I'm here!" I wouldn't miss this place for anything.   Great drinks and service on the lookout bar! Dig your pretzels too.   Omg.  So glad I stoped in.  Thanks for a great time !!

We went inside for the nice clean room and live music. We had no idea that this is Blake Shelton's restaurant. 
Deborah was our waitress she was perfect! She is a great reason to come back. The food was to die for. Simple, healthy and priced perfect. Sweet tea was real!  I will go back when it's night time. The Cobb salad dressing was bbq sauce? I thought I will try it! It was perfect
Got to check this place out! Great food at really reasonable prices. The bands were great every time we went in.

What an arena! What a fan base! Every seat in the entire arena provides a good view of the ice for Nashville Predators NHL games. I have been going to games here for 20 years and have enjoyed seeing it recently get a bit more attention as the Preds make a playoff run. There are lots of restaurant options, tons of bathrooms, and the team shopped opened not too long ago has every piece of merchandise imaginable with a Preds logo slapped on it. Outside of the playoffs, tickets to games are very affordable and the games are quite the spectacle. The fans are extremely passionate and at times the noise is intense from fans losing their minds cheering after a goal. Bring ear plugs if you are sensitive to loud noises. After the game, the arena empties out into the streets for a good time listening to live music in downtown Music City 

Can't wait to get back here. 

GO PREDS!!!!!!
Kiersten was a great waitress - knowledgable about all drinks and great personality! Give her a pin!

A group of us stumbled onto this place right before a crazy thunderstorm. We were looking for not only shelter, but food, drinks and A/C. We found it. For a bar.. the food was good. Granted, its normal bar food, but it wasnt bad (like some places can be). Our group had buckets of beer and buckets of cider, salads, fried pickle chips, cheesey tater tots, cheese sticks, and a few burgers.  The prices were AWESOME and the food was tasty. Were were in on a Saturday and they had karaoke. It wasnt like the "professional" sounding karaoke that you would find on Broadway... it was real.. just plane ol' bad singers having a good time. It was more relaxed.  Id go again.
Amazing food, better service! Stephanie was wonderful! One of the nicest bars on the strip!

This restaurant is overpriced, crowed, and full of staff that don't seem like they care about your dining experience. I had some really good coconut shrimp, but both of my friends didn't like their food. My friend got a margarita but it was much smaller that it looks in the picture and the waitress did not ask if she wanted it frozen or on the rocks. Our waitress never brought ketchup, (I had to walk around and find some) asked about our food, refilled our drinks, or brought us the check. I had to go find her and ask for the check. I wouldn't recommend going here.
Servers are either really inattentive or either really understaffed. Food is average at best. Just your basic bar food. Dont eat the chicken kabobs.

The goods: fun atmosphere, half the staff we interacted with were wonderful, and they have games like Jenga and Connect Four at the tables... lots of space too!

The bads: the other half of the staff.... They don't do flights apparently, but the bartender offered to give us some small samples so we could decide appropriately which pint to try -- no big deal.  Until his reaction to us when we took him up on the offer was one of "really, you're going to make me actually do my job and pour you some beers.  ugh, i would rather be anywhere right now" (y'all know the attitude I'm talking about from one experience or another).  So that happened....

And as far as the beer goes -- if you love pale ales I'm sure this is the place for you!  Unfortunately, if you prefer dark beers like stouts, porters, browns, ambers, etc ... this is not the place for you as they do not serve any.

We visited Nashville in July and this was our first stop when we arrived in the evening.  It was our first brewery and the best one we visited throughout the entire trip.  We walked into live music and a great outdoor & indoor scene.  The beer was, without doubt, the best we had during our time in Nashville and I highly recommend for any craft beer geek who heads to Nashville!
My first time to Nashville has been an absolute waste of time and let down. Tell the server no sour cream or guacamole and she repeats it back 25 minutes later for nachos it's loaded in sour cream.
Great Beer. Excellent staff.  Would definitely go back.   Live in Atl but this is now my Nashville place

Showed up at 3pm on Wednesday to celebrate my friend getting married that morning and they were extremely offended I didn't call ahead to reserve party tables. Was only for about 20 people ON A WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON!! Made us set up in a back corner upstairs, but only after the owner came out to try and explain a "problem". They also added 20% gratuity onto each individual tab even though we still had to go downstairs to the bar to place our order. Everyone was rude and stuck up. Go support other local breweries!

Instead of waiting 45 mins for a table at another fairly new bar in town across the street, I gave Ole Red a shot with only a 20 min wait.  Once my table was ready, I was told to walk across the room to the stairway and walk up a flight of stairs to be greeted by another hostess that would show me to my table.  The table they offered me was in the corner away from the live entertainment that was playing on the main stage downstairs.  I denied their table and found a spot at the bar on the same level that was not crowded.  I ordered a drink and sat back to relax to the sound of the band playing cover songs.  I thought the red tractor hanging upside down added a neat touch to the atmosphere inside the bar.  The drink I ordered was smooth and easy.  I just wished the band would have mixed it up with their own songs along with singing cover songs.
10 bucks for a Tito's and water in a little plastic cup. Food was average at best. Music is great just don't eat there.

The Schermerhorn Symphony Center is gorgeous. And in a city known for music, it's wonderful to have such a great symphony that hosts wonderful conductors, soloists, and pop acts and concerts. I've been for a classic symphony and a pop concert (a tribute to Ella Fitzgerald and Louis Armstrong), that were both wonderful evenings! I'll definitely be buying some tickets for the upcoming season once tickets go on sale later on in the summer! Support your local symphony!

This was the most mediocre meal we experienced during our 4 day trip to Nashville. Two of us ordered beers which were lukewarm. One friend had to send his Bloody Mary back because it had big chunks of something in it. The food was very ordinary without much flavor. Huge disappointment.
Stopped in here for a late lunch and it was wonderful! Our waitress was so great and friendly! Awesome atmosphere and everyone I was with loved what they had to eat and drink! We will be returning!

You may not come to Nashville for burgers but I've had 4 this weekend and this was by far the best one in town. Also heard so much about Nashville hot chicken and have been repeatedly disappointed until Ole Red, a nice smokey spicy bite here. Friendly staff, decent Margaritas and great music. Will definitely be back.

OMG where do I start if you are a burger person gotta have the 5 beer burger best I have ever had honestly the best staff friendly & knowledgeable about beer tried all the beer they make all are great I will say if you come here one time you will be a regular.

Came for  musical happy hour- which is the only reason to come to Margaritaville when there so many other cool honkey tonks.  Decided to battle the crowd- which was fine and the bar staff was nice but all of the RENTED "cops"were rude and egotistical!! I get the security issues, but I don't get the power trip mentality! They can ruin a good experience and buzzkill any fun to be had. Reevaluate your choices!  The only place during CMAs were the security was like this!

Update: this brewery has potential, and would give it another shot to enjoy the patio, which was quite large and looked nice. 

I'm  sure this place is awesome during the warm months if you could sit on the patio or on the balcony, but on a chilly March night I feel like I didn't get the best that this brewery has to offer. The beer selection is small, though you can try a flight of 6 for $12-14. Since it was cold, we were confined to the downstairs bar area which was pretty cramped, and had a couple musicians playing guitar which made it too loud to have a normal conversation at my table. 
Since there are so many breweries in the area, the competition is tight! 
Based on this visit, would not return
The manager Jacob was amazing! He helped us find the shirt we wanted and overall made our experience at Winners and Losers a great one! So glad we stopped in.

The staff was wonderful! I sat down and my chair was covered in water. They immediately apologized for the oversight, cleaned the chair, and gave me a free drink. The shrimp was delicious. We just got a small appetizer for two and drinks. Great atmosphere and staff.

I was so looking forward to this place.

We went on a day when Kenny Chesney was playing across the street, so it was busy. I get that, no problem.

However, we were given a menu that was rather...thin. After ordering something we didn't want, we started seeing other people having food not on our menu delivered to them.

Could we not have been offered the other menu that was put out five minutes after we sat?

The view was great. The food? For the price...very overpriced. Very nice people, but really, four people, one drink each, and a small meal nearly $200?

Don't mind paying for a great meal, but I do for a sub-par one.

Omg such a fun place.  Didn't try the food but menu was awesome especially if you have allergy issues like me.  I wish Inez's hungry lots of vegan options.  The live music was AMAZING.  Went back one night and heard Mitchell tenpenny.  WOW even then service was great.  Waiters made sure to keep everyone happy.   Security was awesome.

The food is fantastic!  Wonderful selection of wing sauces!  Most important, our server Will who appears to run the place is THE MAN!  

Cool patio!  Great music!  I hear they are expanding!

Go there NOW and tell Will I sent you!  You're welcome!

My group was hanging out at the end of the bar (at the back, not by the stage), not very busy considering it was a Friday night, but anyway bouncer comes through and aggressively tells us to get off the bar. Weird...its a bar right? Ok so a few minutes later we forget about that and just go on talking to one another and the same guy comes back and says if he has to tell us to get away from the bar one more time he will drag me out of the place. So me and my friend take a few steps away, let him pass to yell at other people, and turn to the bartender and tell her what happened, we looked around and clearly werent in anyones way (not very busy), not being rowdy or anything...so we thought it was just really weird and were hoping she would tell the guy to simmer down. But she ALSO told us he was right and they had signs posted to get away from the bar. And I would totally understand if like we were keeping people from getting to the bar or whatever, which we weren't, but still is that worth kicking people out of the bar for? So after that I just turned to my group and told them to all close their tabs and we would go to any one of the other 50 bars within walking distance. And of course down the bar is that bouncer just staring at me, presumably waiting for me to get near the bar again. So I told him he wasn't a very nice person (using some different wording), he got some buddies, I just turned and started walking myself out, he came up behind me and tried to grab my Capri Sun (w/ vodka) out of my hand but instead squeezed it into an innocent bystanders face while trying to take it from me, and I just kept walking out the door to Kung Fu. Had a good night there.

We were looking for something to do that's indoors on a COLD day and decided to visit TN Brew Works.  Looks like tasting tray is the way to go here, 5 5oz tasters lets you try what you want before ordering. Bartender was nice and accommodating while working the place alone (granted, it was a weekday).  We also had the chocolate tasting and it's good!  Makes a good combo.

I would give this place a 5, but as soon as the girl with pigtails and a Layla's tag showed up our recent Saturday with out of town friends was ruined. Brian and Haley were amazing and super friendly. But this one didn't smile and acted like she'd rather be elsewhere and witnessed her being rude to several people. (was told she is a manager-Wow). She doesn't belong in customer service at all.  I give it that downtown can get out of hands with rowdy crowds, but this wasn't happening.  I love this place, and sure we will be back-but will likely exit if she is working.
Seats are small and uncomfortable!  The cupholders dig into the sides of your leg. If you wear the new slim suits you should be fine unless you have an athletic build.

This restaurant was absolutely awesome place to enjoy a meal.  The spinach strawberry salad was delicious. Our waitress, Tammy went above and beyond to make our meal very enjoyable. I highly recommend visiting this restaurant while in Nashville Tennessee!!!

This was my first time done in Nashville. Worst bar I experienced down on Broadway. The definition of a bouncer is to keep fights from starting, but the bouncer there with neck tattoos was there to start fights, not stop them.

We were in Nashville for 4 days and we made sure to stop in every day for at least 1 beer. We found that this bar had by far the best bands on Broadway. It is very lowkey but in the best way possible, with a very friendly staff and awesome customers from all over. The best spot on Broadway in my opinion, especially if you aren't into being surrounded by a ton of crazy, loud, drunk people.

Bar setting was nice, band sounded good. However lack of service! Security let us in we sat down approximately 10-15 mins go by no one came to take our drink order. Finally went to the inside bar to ask and was told there's a bartender out there. Then asked if they served food because my group was hungry. Was laughed at by someone sitting at the bar and then told there kitchen is out of service.  There was no signs telling anyone this and there were condiments on the tables.

My favorite brewery in town. Every beer on tap is amazing. They have live music most nights. You can sit upstairs if you want to be able to talk without the music blasting in your ears. Can't go wrong.
My husband and I made the mistake of trying this bar.  Horrible service and unfriendly bartenders :(.  Odd that the manager allows this to happen.  Won't be back.

All I have to say is, HIRE NEW SECURITY. Worse customer service I have EVER experienced. Experienced people being kicked out left and right for asking simple questions. Lack of assistance, and refusal for seating. One couldn't even sit down to eat if desired! First and LAST time going, don't even waste your time. This place isn't even worthy of the one star rating.

This is one place that you do not want to miss when you are in Nashville.  It is a nice size bar with a great stage and an upper level with a bar. This is a bar that  Showcases genuine apps that live here in Nashville. They are original bands and performers working hard to keep traditional country music alive.  If you're in town on a Friday night you can see if the hillbilly casino is plain. They go on 11:00 p.m. and they are an act that you should not miss. Hank Williams the 3rd made his start here. You will see pictures and Pam and other performers on the walls.

Well let me start by saying that I traveled all the way from Houston to come see Nashville. One friend recommended me Ole Red to eat and grab some drinks. When I got there, my family and i had to wait about an hour to get seated because they only have a couple of table for 5+ people. I ordered the redneck nachos and it honestly looked like crap and tasted like it had beer in them. My dad had ordered the burger and it was small for $16. He told our waitress to put the cheese on the side but instead they gave him the wrong burger with chesse... My dad is allergic to cheese so we made them take it back. This place is great to hang out and drink but not a great place to eat...

I saw the Predators play the Capitals on 1/16 so this review is for the hockey experience. 

Let me start off by saying I'm from Chicago, so we've been a hockey city for a MUCH longer period of time than Nashville. 

The arena is very nice and quite large. Concessions are priced about average to what I'd pay at any other NHL venue, but the ticket prices were EXTREMELY CHEAP compared to other stadiums. My tickets cost by about 3/4 less then what I would pay here in Chicago (again different market) and were great seats. 

Parking for us sucked, as there really isn't a true parking lot used for the arena; more you have to find a parking structure nearby, and ours was about a 15 minute walk. That wasn't so bad as you get to walk through down town Nashville and take in the bar scene and music scene, but I'm sure for families with kids it could get dicey. 

The atmosphere itself was rather "minor-league" feel. Very quiet during games, and when it wasn't, the team had these lame college chants that felt like they dragged on forever, for different in game situations.  I mean due to the Nashville still trying to grow their fan base, they need to do these things, but at times it felt like overkill. 

All in all, I liked the stadium and the view we had, as well as the atmosphere outside the arena. The in game atmosphere left a lot to be desired as was more minor league than NHL.

My experience was AWESOME when attending a concert at Bridgestone Arena. I attended a concert over Easter weekend with a large group of family- including children. Safety was a huge concern for us, but the large amount of security manning the arena made us feel safe.

The seats aren't too bad. For our concert, we sat in the nose bleed sections and did not feel claustrophobic in the seats- a huge plus for "crappier" seats. The sound in the arena was fantastic.

Leaving the arena proved to have its difficulties. The escalators stopped working at one point during our exit which made a huge halt in the traffic pattern and ultimately took a good thirty minutes to get from our seats to the front doors. 

Another important thing to add, though it is not the arena itself responsible, is that traffic around the arena is a mad house. The parking was not cheap for a spot roughly a half mile from the doors- $20 per vehicle.
great food and awesome service from kristin tonight at margaritaville nashville! thank you for a wonderful dining experience!

This is the best music venue in town. Loved the layout and the ability to see the stage from everywhere. The bands were fantastic!  Bar service was prompt
And very friendly. 

Had we left when we got hungry, I would rate this place. 10. Sadly, we didn't want to miss the band so are there. It was terrible. I ordered the grilled ham and cheese sandwich  and the bread was burnt beyond recognition. Inedible. And the waitress said she was sorry but no offer to fix and it appeared on the bill. Would have made a bigger deal but we were done.  

Go For the music and drinks. Eat at Luke Bryan's. Where the music and drinks were also fantastic.

Busy place. Grumpy bartender. If you're going to work in the bar business in a town like Nashville you should try to enjoy people. Maybe he was just having a bad day. Fish tacos were very good. Fins up margarita was all sour mix and not very good.

Stopped in here to grab a drink and a snack while wandering down Broadway. First thing... it's insanely crowded here during the typical lunch hour so I would try to either get here early or try to grab a sit at the bar, which is what we did. Our server was attentive as she could be. The best part was the live music. Which is at every place on Broadway so not unique to this place.

Their drinks are pretty good, I got the Perfect Margarita because it's margaritaville!! We also got the shrimp appetizer which was really good. Not too fried thank goodness because I'm almost at my "fried limit" for this vacation lol. They have a cute gift shop so definitely recommend checking that out

I purchased tickets for my husband and I, as an anniversary gift. The venue looks great and parking wasn't awful. They actually have food, which is nice. The main reason I give it 2 stars is the acoustics. The entire room has so much metal in it that there's a constant ringing. There are absolutely no sound cushions (that I could see). I couldn't hear  or understand around 80%of the lyrics. Perhaps this wasn't meant to be a musical venue on conception? The reason you go to see a performing musical artist is for the music, right? But when you can't hear the music and there's a ringing in your ears, it puts a damper on the evening. Overall: would go back for a comedy show.
Went during CMA Fest and had such a good time. David was great and our food was so tasty!

I'm a big fan of this arena, especially during the Preds games. Food is really good and reasonably priced. My go-to is the Kayem's hot dog with fries combo. $7.75 but as a season ticket holder, I get a dollar off! Plenty of food at a great price; you can't be that. Also, I prefer to get my beer at the bar on the 200 level; the beer selection is more to my taste (i.e. Sierra Nevada Pale, Yazoo selections, etc.) and has a full bar. A craft bottle here costs you 6.75 compared to a $10 20 oz can of Bud at concessions. (No thank you.) And, as a season ticket holder, you get a discount as well! Also worth mentioning, the bartenders are pretty cool and courteous, as is all staff in and around the arena. Keep up the good work Bridgestone!
We met the beautiful, beefy, bald headed, bartender Jeremy here and got $2.50 PBRs. Can't be beat for the prices in Nashville.

Great place to see Predator's hockey. Fans love their Preds which makes it very fun to be part of the enthusiasm. Right down town so easy to grab a bite and a drink before or after the game. Security is simple and seats in the topic section are really reasonable. The restrooms are clean and the venue offers a variety of snacks and sandwiches.

Came to Nashville specifically for the Preds/Lightning game. Unfortunately, I think our home arena in Tampa has spoiled me. Entering the facility and getting through security was a breeze, and the interior of the arena is very eye-catching, but that's where the wow factor ended. While walking to the seats, it was evident that the arena had not been thoroughly cleaned after the last event; there was garbage underneath the majority of the seats and just looked dirty. The seats are also very narrow to some standards, similar to a cheap airline; the woman next to our group was somewhat portly and 'spilled over' into one of our seats. The prices of the beer and food were fair (considering you're at a sports arena). Other than that, great location with tons of hotels nearby for visitors, but some room for improvement.

Came to Nashville, our second day back, atmosphere here is great all friendly people.  You share your table which is fun.  The couple who shared our table bought us drinks for the nite, who can beat that.  We went to mostly all the top clubs on Broadway.  We think Ole Red is by far the best for food, drinks and good old country music.  Many bands play Big dance floor which we like.
Probably the worst place in Nashville .  Music so loud you can't talk. Macaroni and cheese and baked bees were terrible. No Tobasco So called dance floor had food and drinks spilled all over it

Had a great Labor Day weekend in Nashville for the UGA-Vanderbilt football game. The city was even better than we expected. Ended our Sunday and had a great time Sunday night at Ole Reds. Great music from 2 bands (JC Anderson Band & Taryn Papa Band), great food and atmosphere. We will definitely be back from Atlanta this fall.
Music was great!!!  We heard two groups. Service was good. Food not so good. Skip the nachos. Very disappointing. Pork bbq sandwich was so-so. Tots were good.

The only reason this was not a one rating is because 311 was awesome. I don't know how you can have a concert with no air conditioning. Sweat was pouring off everyone's faces. My fiancé who meet goes to concerts had a bad experience all because it was 100 degrees in a concert. The only thing that would have made the concert better is if it was at a different venue.
If you go there you have to ask for Chris Anthony best service we have received in at least 6 months. Chris made this meal a great experience.

Lots of choices along Broadway...we were lured by the southern rock blues vibe playing inside.  We stopped in for a quick refreshment.  Chatted it up with a great bartender who was genuinely personable, super friendly and pretty cute.  Band pulled in other singers and performers and music was loud enough to talk  over.  Recommend for casual, enjoyable experience.

Checked out this new place today and just loved it!!  The second of Blake Sheldon's restaurants named after his song. Great atmosphere!  Aaron from Texas was our server and he was fabulous. Gave us some great recommendations and info on the nighttime bands, building of the place, etc.  Live music was great. Not too loud for a lunch time atmosphere. Food was very very good.  I would recommend!!!

Came in went upstairs to bar. Totally not busy. Totally ignored by a female bartender as I sat with a credit card in my hand. Sorry Blake, but your place needs better service. The guy singing was awesome tho.

$10 for a shot of bourbon in a plastic cup. So worth it! The music was amazing. The location was quaint. Like an old dive bar. A bit grungy. Not too crowded, but still hopping. They have security at the door which is great. Being a girl, all alone, honky tonking, Layla's was the place I felt the safest.

I used to go here about once a month for a happy hour event.  I will never go here again.  I was assaulted by the staff at the neighboring bar "Losers."  The staff lied to the police about the incident, and the in house video was suspiciously "broken" when a detective returned to retrieve the evidence. Three staff members participated in beating me unconscious.  I left in an ambulance.  The incident cost me thousands of dollars.  I witnessed a similar incident at Winners a few years ago. When I asked what happened then, I was told to "mind my own business or I could join him." I sincerely regret my silence.  Being a bouncer is not an entitlement to assault people.  I would not recommend either establishment to my worst enemy.  Winners and Losers should both be out of business.

The venue itself is cool. Looks awesome.......just don't go there expecting a great listening experience. Easy parking a huge plus. But the purpose it serves is self defeating because the acoustics are terrible. Saw Stryper last night and I could not get over how such a great band could sound so deplorable. . Low end was pure unadulterated MUD. Acoustically this place is pretty much a gymnasium......and it sounded like one.
Chris in retail is awesome! Super friendly. Drinks were good quality. Food and service was great. Good tourist spot. I'm local and still like to come down for the music.

I go to concerts a lot in Nashville, but I recently visited Marathon for the first time. I have to say, it was a wonderful and spacious venue. I love how they have multiple bar locations. Very convenient. They even had three dollar tacos! The only thing I really disliked was the fact that there are bathroom attendants. It's not a classy restaurant or anything so why did they need to be there? The woman in the lady's room was very harsh and tried to force her help on you. I'm perfectly capable of pumping soap and getting a paper towel on my own, thanks though. Overall super neat venue!

It was very disappointing. The decor was not a country atmosphere. It was very modern, staff was not friendly.  How could someone put a place like this in the middle of a historic district.  The new restaurants was not even busy but the old established ones were packed. We asked one musician to play an old country song by Ray Price. He said love the song but don't play in that era which I thought how would you even be here if not for the history of country music.

Went here for dinner while at a conference, no expectations. Nice corner location on Broadway. It has a large open main floor area with a great band playing. It was lively but not too loud. Nashville hot biscuit sandwich was delightful but I must comment in the sweet potatoes tots! Oh my word! Delish! Great place to eat, take in a band and then head out for other adventures on Broadway.

This was my first visit to Nashville, and I had to check out Ole Red. My friend and I were at the restaurant when it opened for lunch and were seated promptly and welcomed by our awesome waitress Nira. Before we even placed our order, I was in need of caffeine bad and she made me a fresh pot of coffee! Everything on the menu sounded great, it was hard to decide what to choose. I went for the Nashville Hot Chicken Biscuit with a mini wedge salad and my friend got the Half Fried Chicken bucket with a side of mashed potatoes. Our food came quickly and was so yummy! The Nashville Hot Chicken Biscuit was huge, the size of a hamburger and I got the tater tots as a side (such a good choice). The fried chicken was served in a bucket, full to the rim and came with biscuits and scrumptious milk gravy (bottle that up and sell it in the gift shop)!  A few minutes after we started eating, my friend's mouth started to tingle and she realized there must've been pickles in the brine of the fried chicken. She's allergic to pickles and didn't think to ask and of course left her medicine at our hotel! Nira and the manager Sean were so great and responsive to help my friend. They quickly removed her meal and went searching for Benadryl. In fact, Sean went to a drug store close by and bought Benadryl for my friend, that's A+ service if you ask me! She ordered another (non pickle brine) meal - the pork steak (ginormous) and we ate, drank and listened to great music for the next 5 hours! The vibe and food are great at Ole Red, but for us, it was the impeccable service that will bring us back the next time we visit Nashville.
Great entertainment and great food! Pimento Cheese appetizer was the best!! Huge portions - consider sharing! The bucket of chicken is literally a bucket of chicken!
so disappointed, service was horrible. i ordered cheeseburger and bread was stale. the perfect margarita was the only good part. The waitress was totally out of it
LOVE this bar! The food, the drinks, the music, the bartenders/waitresses. Prob my fave place to be anytime we're in town! We love being here! It's a throwback to what Nash used to be and I love it!

Wow.... this place SUCKS.
Went to see our neighbor sing, waited two hours with our name on the list. Surrounded by at least 15 empty tables. The tables that were seated were not getting their drinks for 10-15 minutes. Servers moved like snails. When asked the hostess and MANAGER why there were empty tables and we were still waiting they were hesitant and said "I don't really know". This place needs to get it together or they will have no business. Would not recommend. Music was great though.
Our first night in Nashville we found this gem! Great food and beer plus live bluegrass music! A wonderful spot to hang out and enjoy Music City USA! We will be back for sure.
Great rooftop on a sunny day. Cute vibe. Loved it!!! Would return! Didn't experience lower levels. Roof was awesome.

I've eaten here 3 times now.  Twice back in February and it was Fantastic.  I tend to not venture out too much once I find something I like.  All three times I've gotten the Fajita Taco Salad which normally comes with beef but substituted chicken instead.  It comes with the dressing already mixed up in the salad and it was superbly blended.  However, I ate the same thing just recently and it was just mediocre.  I was disappointed.  Overall though, the service was excellent, we were able to walk right in and sit down at the bar and it was on a weekend when we went.  We did get there early though.  I would still recommend this place!

We dined 6/30 right at opening (11am) and came in with the waiting wave of people. We were seated quickly although most of the staff seemed to be in a bad mood. The menu is very specialized, meaning not a ton of choices, none of the appetizers really seemed our cup of tea but we did both order the Tennessean burger, it came with pimento cheese and the usual toppings. The husband got fries and they come out seasoned well and thick. I substituted  with a mini wedge salad that was really good and fresh. We both cleaned our plates! We actually had no idea this was Blake Shelton's restaurant, we popped in the day before and it was packed but stuck out because it was super clean, air conditioned and didn't reek of old smoke and beer! Definitely a good burger, we will be back and next time we will get the tots and poutine!! A little attention from the staff, refills etc. would be great and the bluegrass band playing was a nice touch! I would give it a try and if you are vegan they have quite a bit to choose from!

Great job Blake on an awesome atmosphere and decor! We loved how the feel of each floor was different to accommodate so many different interests and personalities! The look-out rooftop was beautiful! We didn't eat or have drinks here so I can't speak for that, but the atmosphere was definitely well worth a visit!

Great two for one beers on Wednesdays! I didn't eat but my friend got a hot chicken sandwich of which I took some fries and it was delicious, came out fast and served with some homemade bbq/ketchup sauce that was absolutely perfect for the sandwich/fry combo. 

I got the southern wit which was good even though I don't usually like Hefeweizens, I would give the stout a try and maybe an IPA next time! They give tokens so you can get one beer at a time so your bogo doesn't get warm.

We came here on a random Monday night while visiting. There was a little wait the service was excellent by  Victoria. The prices were reasonable and  the atmosphere was 
great. The portions of food were great and the food was tasty. We all had hot chicken sandwiches and burgers and the food pimento cheese dip.
The fries and Tater tots  were all delicious.
The performers were all great this night.
Sometimes a wait but also a predators game was happening on this night 
5 floors to the restaurant on the top floor there is a roof top bar and observation area sometimes there is a private range!
Crazy tourist trap. Rude staffers. Do not waste your time, they do not want or need your money
Atmosphere and live music is amazing! Food is just ok; pulled pork was dry with no sauce. Champagne of chicken was not a lot of chicken. Tater tots tho!! Those are made in house & very yummy
What a deal. We had a blast. The music was top notch,  atmosphere great and bartender best!  Have fun.
I went to see Mary J Blige & Nas. We had great seats and the staff was friendly. This was my second time attending an event here and I definitely will be back.
This place is awesome. Service was outstanding beer was great and the food was off the hook great flavor profile

Need to update my review. Because of my last review the manager was kind enough to reach out to me. I don't write this review because of any type of influence. On 5/31 we visited again. Kira was our server. Her service was spot on for the point of being excellent. Food was good. I wish yelp allowed 3.5 stars. Food was better than average but what you would expect from a chain. Based on this experiment I would absolutely go back. Obviously they have their thing, island drinks and appetizers. While we did not have them the nachos are huge and look pretty good.

This was my second time visiting TN Brew Works. The first time I thought this brewery was just OK since the selection of beers wasn't my style. However, the most recent time I went (back in October), my sister and I each loved our beers. She had 1927 (IPA) and I had Basil Ryeman (Saison). 

The best part was the hummus. Odd, I know. But the white bean and curry hummus paired with texas toast was just perfect. It may have just been a seasonal item but if you can grab this when you're here you wont regret it!

The staff was friendly and knowledgeable. The set-up is pretty cool, ample seating with a second floor and a deck. I'll be back for sure!

This meal was really filling, price was reasonable. My friends got tater tots as their side and I immediately regretted getting the normal French fries. The tater tots were fluffy, crispy, delicious. The mushroom burger I order was great, the bbq sauce tasted sweet and tangy. The atmosphere of the restaurant is really fun, the entire restaurant itself is huge..two levels with live music. There was a wait for one hour but we ended up getting a text that our table was ready after about 10 minutes! You should check this place out, there's a few vegan options as well which I was really excited about.

Tourist trap, overrated, SLOW AS HELL SERVICE, EXPENSIVE, DISASTER. In our defense, we had 3 small kids and that's where they wanted to go. We were told 30 min. wait which turned into an hr. It was loud and chaotic. It upped our aggravation level to wait longer with 3 hungry kids. Had we been told an hr. long wait, we would have passed. 
My friend is on the annoying "no carb" plan and ordered the burger without the bun. I ordered chicken sandwich. We also ordered vodka and water bc these kids were on our last nerve. We had to send them back bc it was club soda and vodka instead of regular water. Not a huge deal but adding to the annoyance. 
It took AN HOUR, AN HOUR!!!!! To get our +*^#^**# food!!! 
 I would think the cooks would try and make the no carb burger look a little better with nothing to hide the sloppy contents. Nope. Looked pitiful as hell!!! I mean, it looked ridiculous, almost as if they were pissed she didn't want the bun and threw it on a plate, like "here ya go, bitch." She complained and asked for more than the tiny piece  of wilted lettuce she was given. (I mean, is there a shortage!!?) That took forever to get as well. She was pretty much done (a couple of bites left) when she brought it. She asked for a manager. We got comped drinks. I had a chicken sandwich that was like any other chicken sandwich. 
The kids had a blast once they got their food. They were starving and stressed us out in the process of the long wait. They loved it. They enjoyed the complimentary silly string they got instead of crayons and a coloring sheet. 
I will never ever ever never EVER go back.

So.... This place has consistently had the best beer I've ever had and then they go and open the kitchen...  They don't make words to describe how good the food is.  I don't know what to order and that's a good problem.  The burger will change your life forever and the frog legs are out of this world and I'm just pissed cause my stomach isn't big enough to order the whole menu.  The burger is so good that you'll never be able to enjoy another one unless you're at Tennessee Brew Works.   They have some secret sauce or something that gives the burger a flavor that I can't even begin to describe.  It's super messy and that's just the way it should be!!!  They also make a veggie dish that has Brussels sprouts and it's so good the damn kids love it!   Do it.  Change your life.  You've been warned.
Love this place! The live music is amazing. Too bad I wasn't here when Blake Shelton paid a visit. They do have a few vegan options, like the a impossible burger, salad, and a mushroom sandwich.

I'll start with the good.  Service was great, beer was cold, decor really nice and good entertainment.  Had lunch with 3 other couples. The food was only mediocre.  Didn't care for their version of fried pickles at all and the nachos were really messy. Wings were ok.  I had the pig 'N' cheese sandwich (fried bologna), it was a greasy mess and I returned it, preferred to just continue to eat the mediocre apps. Oh forget, skillet cornbread was really good. Two people from our party had burgers and said they were good. My husband had the pulled bbq mushroom sandwich and said it was ok.  Was not my favorite stop in Nashville.

Not a bad place to have lunch right on the main street of Broadway.  They had brunch served on the fourth floor of the building. Upon looking at their limited selection, we opted to do lunch where we were seated on the first floor where there was a live band playing.

I got the Nashville Hot Chicken Biscuit with House-Made Tots. The tots were very unique compared to the traditional tots you get elsewhere. I guess they're really house made. The chicken biscuit itself was not bad at all. I didn't like the warm cole slaw on the sandwich, but other than that, it's a pretty solid choice.
The nachos are amazing! One tray is more than enough for 4people. Great music! Nice venue Blake Sheldon

The most authentic and non-touristy places we visited in this neighborhood. Loved the Hot Chicken and great craft beer selection. Great vibe to the place, awesome band, and friendly door staff. Robert the bartender gave us great suggestions for where else to go (East Nashville, who knew?). Loved this place.

Literally the worst place to host an event. The staff were rude. They acted essentially as fun police. Don't dance or act like a fun person at all or you will probably get kicked out. I'd give them zero stars if it was an option.

Great place for bluegrass and hillbilly music. The bands we saw were very talented. The servers are friendly and accommodating here. The crowd is a bit more laid back than some of the rowdier places in town.
It took 1 hour for our 2 entrees to get out. Our server was inappropriate and too personal with us! The food was tiny proportions for what we paid. Very unhappy with this locations!!
Fun place. Went for drinks and appetizers. Good band. Service was very good. Nachos were really good.
This bar is terrible, the bounces think that are bit shit. One bounce is like 5' 4 and will kick you out if he feels threatened. So no go here, there are about 100 other bars to go to

Ol Red - Oofdah (MN gal here) where do I start!?.  It's a clean classy place we went on a Tuesday!   

Entertainment- gorgeous (see pix - this this why there were like 8 bachelorette parties within three block radius?)

Food- fattening and full of delicious gluten (see cornbread and pickles)

Drinks- overpriced ($11 for Jack and a mixer !?) 

Overall: I'd come back, just not to drink on a night out.
Loud as fuck. If you're into loud live music and a bunch of drunks singing, this is the place to go. The food was excellent and the staff were really good.

We just ordered appetizers while we enjoyed some great music by Skyler Anderson. He was the highlight of our visit. What a great entertainer and humble guy. We stayed and watched his entire performance. As for the food, the cornbread was amazing!  I would definitely order this again.  We also ordered the fried pickles & green tomatoes which were fine. For our taste, probably wouldn't order again. The tomatoes were small chunks. I expected big round tomatoes slices. We also had the House Made Tots. These were ok. Little over cooked. The waitress was an absolute sweetheart. We would definitely return here to try a meal and enjoy the music.
Tammy Cook was our served made our night, and Jambalaya was awesome. party of 6 and she made sure our drinks were always full. Thanks Tammy
Venue for major Nashville events and of course the best live sports to watch, hockey.  Right on Broadway, so tons of things to do before and after the games.

My parents came to visit and we decided to go to Nashville after looking around for a family friendly restaurant we went into ole red. The service wasn't the best but we all got hamburgers and fries. All 7 of us enjoyed our meals and the entertainment. Awesome atmosphere, we will definitely go again.
Food was great and the atmosphere was wonderful! My only complaint is that they need a larger ladies restroom! Only 2 stalls in a popular bar/restaurant is NOT enough for women!

HORRIBLE SERVICE- RUDE - we were here for 
July 4 weekend and this was BY FAR the worst bar in the NashVegas row! Don't go here- service sux(we actually walked out before even ordering).

Hot chicken was excellent. 
Pimento artichoke dip is a must appetizer. 
Love music was great - saw 2 acts on a Monday afternoon. 
Service was not bad but nothing to brag about.

Great brewery in downtown Nashville!

2 stories, with both levels serving delicious beers.  They have ales, IPAs, porters, stouts, & more.  I love how this brewery serves food!  & not just snacks, but actual food like burgers, sandwiches, & salads.

Friendly brewtenders, servers.  They have lots of board games & television.  & as we were leaving, there was a live band about to perform.

Hummus:  This could have easily been split amongst a group of 5 & our group of 3 barely made a dent.  Served with fat pieces of buttery toast.
Fries:  Just a side of fries was plenty to serve us 3!  Flavorful & thin, & their house made sauce was delicious.

We hosted our wedding rehearsal dinner upstairs at Tennessee Brew Works, and it was a perfect night! Mara and the staff were extremely responsive and helpful throughout booking and planning (including adjusting our head count at the last minute). The pricing for space rental/open bar was much better than a lot of other places in town, and it came with a better space: it was great to serve dinner inside and let guests gravitate to the upstairs patio and dart room. The chef put together an awesome menu that accommodated our request for vegetarian and gluten free options (alongside some smoked hot chicken that was definitely a hit). We definitely have a family that cares about food, and we got so many compliments. Same goes for the beer, though we already knew that was great :) Thanks to the staff for making this special night so easy to plan and fun to attend!

I visited Nashville for an event and ate/drank at this bar.  The food was excellent and the drinks were good.  The bartenders were very attentive despite being super busy.  I will definitely visit again next time I'm in town.
Great food snd entertainment. The hot chicken biscuit was outstanding as well as the biscuits and jam. Highly, Highly recommend. Our favorite of the weekend!
Quick service for drinks. Not so great on karaoke night if you want to sing and don't know the dj. Given it two tries. Will not try again.

I took my partner and his two children to Margaritaville tonight and waited an hour after putting our order in only for our waitress to come up to the table and tell us that that they had a computer malfunction and the kitchen was a mess. I asked if she had any kind of timeframe for our food to be ready and she didn't. At this point I would have expected a free appetizer or something but nada. She comped our drinks which was nice and I totally understand things like this happen but after an hour and a half with no food I wold have expected a gift certificate or something similar to make up for that pretty egregious experience.

Response to manager. I emailed you on 8/4 and have yet to hear back so my review stands.

Hands down best waitress in Nashville! Nira provides top notch service, from refilling drinks to clearing plates, food recommendations and all around fun lovin', witty sense of humor. The food is always great! Our favorites include the bucket of Hot Chicken with biscuits and fried cauliflower! She was nice enough to take group photos and jump in on one with us!

Came in on a Tuesday night because the outside sign said "Master Chef at Layla's", sat at a table across the bar, ordered drinks and then asked the bartender, Sammy,  what the "Master Chef" was for....she had no idea. She even went outside and looked up at it only to still not have a clue. Was there for a few hours and listened to a live band that was good but she still offered no insight to the marque...she just laughed it off-Oh well, I guess. 

After the first 30-45 mins, Sammy saw that we weren't going anywhere and then became attentive to our cocktails. 
It was my 1st time in Nashville and the band was SUPER loud and conversation was difficult even at the back of the bar but not pissed about it. Tis live music. Whaddaya gonna do?!?! Had a good time and enjoyed myself.

This place was so much fun. I'm not even that much into the kind of music they played but it was just such a fun atmosphere, the band was nice, the people were all really interesting - very Rockabilly - and the drinks were average price. Really fun place to go. It's packed on a weekend.
Sent my contact info to finsfeedback THAT DAY never heard a thing...review stands. and is reinforced

We visited here on vacation and stopped by with a toddle.  First of all I love a brew place that can accommodate a toddler.  The waitress was very nice and was able to adjust the grilled cheese sandwich to not include the preserves.  We got the charcuterie board with the beer bread, it was so good I could have eaten in all day.  I also got a beer and burrata salad...you had me at burrata.  This was amazing and had great flavors.  We got the beer flight, our favorite was the Southern Wit!  I would go back here again if I could!

My girlfriend and I bought tickets to see Humming house during the grand re-opening weekend of 12th & Porter. We decided to dine at the restaurant before hand.

I have nothing but praise for this renewed establishment. The interior is hip, trendy, and welcoming. The staff is very attentive and friendly.

I had the pulled pork nachos, while the girlfriend tried the classic burger with sweet potato fries. Both tasted fantastic!

My only regret is the lack of foresight to take pictures of the food before diving in. I will definitely be returning to this establishment!

when I think about Margaritaville I think about vacationing as its typically the only time I'd stop in one.  We were downtown for a show and wanted to grab dinner and it was near by and seemed not to be over crowded as it was a Tuesday evening. 

My wife and I ordered 2 margaritas which seemed really watered down.  The service was a bit slow and again "it wasn't too busy on this Tuesday evening".  The food came out and was fairly decent but not memorable.  There are several options within walking distance I'd choose before coming back.

We enjoyed a wonderful evening at Nashville Brew Works! We stopped in for a beer then decided to have dinner there also. They don't serve typical brew fare. Originally it looked like it but what came to our table was a far cry from fried this and overlooked that. Well thought out flavors with their brews worked into the dishes. Well done!

This was the worst Margaritaville I've been to .The service was bad and the food was tasteless.  It took 20 minutes to get out drinks after we ordered them . Someone ordered a soda and waitress never did bring that . We had to ask another employee to bring us one .  Someone ordered the seafood Mac and cheese and it did not have a taste at all ,no spices, the cheese had no taste like it wasn't real cheese . I ordered the flatbread and also was tasteless.  Someone ordered the nachos which were plentiful but all the cheese was on the top of the mound so after the top layer there was nothing in them .  We ordered margaritas and there was no salt on the rim and were syrupy sweet. We were there on a Wednesday night in November so it wasn't during peak season when it was packed .  I guess this restaurant thrives on its location rather than its quality of service and food.
Went on a Wednesday night for drinks and live music. It was amazing! The band playing was great! There are touches of Blake Shelton all over. I loved the signs on the bathroom door.

I wish I could have reviewed this place properly, but I was turned away at the door at 8:30pm when Broadway was kicking! I guess they don't like visitors. Oh, by the way, I called up see what time they close the kitchen.  10pm.
What cool place two story's of yummy beer and live music on a Sunday.. a good joint to make good memory's

What a disappointment!  Jimmy Buffet would be appalled!  We were in Nashville for the weekend, and decided to visit Margaritaville.  We walked right in and our party of 4 was seated. That was the only positive thing about this experience.  When our server approached us, I asked for a bucket of loaded Coronas, something we always order when we visit Margaritaville.  Not once did she ask the other members of our party what they would like to drink.  She returned about 10 minutes later to ask for their drink orders.  Another 10 minutes before she returned with the bucket of Coronas.  We took a drink, and they were horrible.  When we were finally able to flag the waitress down, she insisted they were correct, and argued with me.  They were not filled with Lime tequila, and the tequila added was a very short pour.  When she finally decided to make them right, she returned with only 3 beers in the bucket, not 5.  Service was horrible, even though the restaurant was not busy.  When our check arrived, it was $85!!  For a bucket of beer and an appetizer!  I asked to speak to the manager, explained my issue, and he took the bill and walked away.  The waitress returned about 5 minutes later with a new bill that was $45, no explanation from anyone.  If this is how business is always done at this location, it would explain why it wasn't crowded.

Service was great! All the bartenders were friendly and quick with drinks. The music was great ! I would recommend this place for a drink and good music they have food but it is simple bar food. I will be back!

Ok, Hot Chicken BUT no tap ice water AND two dollars for a bottle!!  Nuts .. AND we left.. Would not AND will not recommend to anyone.. Go anywhere else for better service . RIPOFF... And I asked twice for tap ice water. Band wasn't a band.. Again go someplace else.

First time in Nashville, and this is the first place we stopped at (highly recommended by friends of mine) and it did not disappoint. The band was amazing, it is a bar so the food menu is small but I ended up going with a burger and it was great! The Beer selection was wonderful as well and the bartender was super helpful when being asked about the local beers and beer profiles. Laylas isn't huge, but it does have plenty of room for you to enjoy the band even from the furthermost back of the bar, and they've even got a TV at the bar that is showing the band as they play. Overall wonderful little spot and I will definitely be back!

Multiple floors with a rooftop bar just like every bar in Nashville. This venue is on the smaller side compared to the other new celebrity bars. Rooftop was closed for a private event the night we were there. Sat at the second floor bar and split the redneck nachos. Very disappointing, basically a huge portion of over cooked potato chips. The nacho toppings like the chicken, cheese, barbecue sauce, and  others were very skimpy. Really just tasteless, none of the toppings were layered. Just placed on top of the chips. The 3 stars are for the bartender. He was friendly and efficient. Zero stars for the redneck nachos.
Didn't stay to partake of anything on their menu-service was terrible with a F- you attitude and prices for domestic bottled beer were outrageous $6 for Miller lite. Won't be back.

Went to Bridgestone arena on 9/16/19 for a preseason game. Tickets were purchased through third party, game time app. Tickets were approved and sent and I had trouble sending them to my Ticketmaster account. I showed the security and ticket will call manager my confirmation of tickets but they didnt care and did not try to help. Poor management, we left and will never spend money on this venue again.

Now that I've been here for a few concerts, it's time for a review. I can't give it 5 stars because it is an arena. I much prefer a smaller to medium size venue when I see live shows. Lucky for me that most of the bands I see play in the small to medium-sized venues. 

There are occasions where I do have to venture into a large space to see some of my favorites though. 

The shows I've been to here are Tool, A Perfect Circle, and most recently, Florence + The Machine. 

The first thing to be said for this arena is the size of it. Yes... it's an arena so it's large. Most arenas are built for NBA teams or college basketball teams. I'm not sure of the exact reason this arena was built but it seems to have been built for the local hockey team and as a concert space. Since that seems to be the case, it's somewhere in between a medium and large arena space. I don't love it but it's okay when seeing larger acts.

This last experience here, I had to take advantage of the First Aid station. I was starting to get a headache. I went straight to Bridgestone's website, found where the First Aid room was with ease and went there to get an ibuprofen. Kudos to the arena for making it easy. 

In closing, if you love smaller acts but they grow to support a venue like this and they play there... you'll have a good time I believe. Buy the tickets and go have fun.

I think this is the largest music venue I've been to since moving to Nashville (besides Ascend, but Marathon will most likely be a much more regular thing, with Ascend being a once-a-Summer-maybe venue). 

Nice open space, warehouse-like, with a high stage, providing good sight lines from pretty much anywhere. Now, the show I was at was far from crowded, which definitely added to my experience, but the bars on either end of the venue with seating are a definite plus. The people working ticketing seemed to be having a bit of a difficult time despite the lack of crowd. 

Well kept, inviting, maybe a little heavy on the fog machine, but maybe that was because it's so close to Halloween. Either way, pretty decent venue that I would not mind visiting again. (Parking is kind of a pain around the area, but that's not a strike against them).

Music was great ambiance was cool and service was wonderful. Food was pretty good if you like southern fried food. I wouldn't say "you have to go here"
But if your close and it's not a huge wait check it out!

Bridgestone Arena is a fantastic stadium located smack dab in the middle of all of the downtown Nashville action. 

I was lucky enough to escape my corporate summit in Nashville long enough to watch the Predators host the Boston Bruins on a Thursday night and I will be the first to exclaim that the Preds Arena is an exceptional one. They keep the stadium spotless and the accessibility to each floor is unmatched thanks to the fast moving escalators that are seemingly everywhere. Better yet is the seating - there truly isn't a bad seat in the house and you can get on on the cheap as $50.00 tickets nets a mid rink sightline. Of course the Beers are pricey (weighing it at $10.00 a pop for a large) but welcome to the world of professional live sporting events, right?

The locals also add a lot to the atmosphere as Predators fans may be some of the friendliest in the National Hockey League and in true Nashville style there are live bands to revel in between periods. After the game the party really kicks in as the backside of the venue spills into Broadway which is the epicenter of Music City. You will watch the entire stadium empty into the Nashville bar scene before your very eyes, it is an incredible sight to behold. 

I was very impressed with Bridgestone Arena and would definitely recommend a visit to any local or visitor alike if you get the chance to watch a game, event, or concert at this gem in the Nashville skyline.
I've been here a couple of times and it's never disappointed! The Beer is really good. The food is great - I had the wings. I love the outside area. It's a really cool, chill spot.

I've been to Bridgestone arena before and knew it would be a special experience for my daughter! So I sent my 8 year old on a fun trip to watch a Preds game with her cousins. She was so excited to go to her first hockey game!! I packed her bag (small backpack because a little girl can't remember to keep a purse on her shoulder... and frankly purses are uncomfortable) with her wallet, extra sweaters, chapstick and a pair of p.j.s just in case the game ended late. When she finally got there her aunt sent me a very happy picture of her before entering. Now once she got in was an entirely different story. At the entrance she was asked to empty her bag and throw it away. They did tell my 8 year old who was now sobbing that she could walk it all the way back to the car and come back... how nice. However, that's unrealistic for a child who has hip problems to make the treck once. It was either she throw the bag away or go home (there were 4 other kids with her so home wasn't an option). So, a very sad little girl threw her bag away and sat at a Preds game with her belongings spilling over in her lap. 

Lastly, If she brought a purse she could have walked it in. I think it's a little unfair to boys/men who wouldn't carry a purse. I think your policy is very one sided and could use relooking at. Either you make it an all around fair policy of no bags or you check bags better. There is no reason for anyone to throw their belonging away especially if it's not on your policy online! Very disappointed in how you handled things.

Had a flight. Beer was great. We liked the basil ryman but they all were all tasty. We got the hot chicken sandwich. It was ok but NOT hot like Nashville hot chicken should be. We got another sandwich with a hard-to-remember name. It had ham, an egg, curry powder, and some type of preserve on it. It was awesome! The ambience was cool and the service was great. Would recommend!

We went to this bar on Monday last week mid day. There was maybe a ten minute wait which I was excited about having heard lines could've long. We were seated upstairs. Server gave us menus and never returned. We luckily still had our drinks from downstairs bar we got during the wait. On our way out I saw the server and she smiled...?!  I thanked her for the water we had asked for. She said you're welcome. I then told her she never came back. She walked away. Not a good start. Super disappointed. I work for Marriott and can't really send my valued guests to an establishment with my name on it that can't remember to wait on guests. We sat there 40 min. On a positive note it's a pretty place and the music was good. Hope they get it together....
We went for the beer which was good but were blown away by the food. The 5 beer burger was in a league of its own. It has totally messed with my emotions.

Music is why we came here 
Music is good
Food is average 
It's loud but fun
I don't know what else to say so I'm just typing til I can end comments

I came here with a friend who had previously had a great experience at the location in Destin, FL. I had never been, but was optimistic. I was also excited for live music and food in Nashville, but that is not the experience I received. When we first arrived there wasn't anyone at the host stand for over 5 minutes. We waited and eventually were seated. There were two of us but we were only given one menu and no silverware. Our waitress came over ten minutes later to finally get our drink order (water and sweet tea). The waitress brought out two waters and no tea. We ordered appetizers and I asked for my tea. She came back with the tea which was very bad. And asked us if we had ordered anything yet. We said yes repeated our appetizers. Twenty minutes later we received our appetizers and ordered our dinner entrees. We also asked our server for silverware. We waited five minutes. At this point we were out of water and still had not received silverware. My steak came out. Still no silver ware. No water. I got up and walked to the host stand to ask for silverware after asking a different server and still not receiving any. My steak was cold by the time I was able to eat it. I ordered a Caesar salad with my steak, but never received it. The mashed potatoes were awful. I love potatoes and this was my least favorite part of the meal. Our server never came back. I sat my card on the table to indicate we were ready to pay. Twenty minutes went by. She still did not pick up the card. I went to the host stand again to see if they could locate our waitress. She finally came by ten minutes later. Still no water. I am very disappointing. I was looking forward to the live music and decent food and I was extremely let down.
Had late lunch so split nachos with my husband. They were good but not much meat on them. Ordered a drink -One particular Harbour- it was very good!

Enjoyed the roof top bar. Views are top notch. I'm a local so I know some good view spots!
The food however was terrible. Party of 10. We all did a lot of sharing & trying & nothing was good! Waste of time eating here.

This is a great location for large events! They made the planning process so easy (Jennifer and Erin). The staff at the event were personable and efficient (Abby, AJ and staff).
The food was great! Especially for a large group. We had appetizers and dinner. The mac and cheese was AMAZING!!! The chicken fingers, shrimp fritters, chicken quesadillas were all hits with the group. The drinks were fantastic! The bartenders were fast but friendly! 
While this is a chain restaurant in a very touristy town, we felt right at home! I would definitely recommend!

My boyfriend and I were in Nashville this past weekend for a family reunion.  After the Saturday afternoon family festivities, we decided to venture over to Broadway to get some dinner and have a drink or two.  Being that we are both vegetarian, sometimes it is hard to find places to dine out when we're out of town.  We wandered up and down Broadway for awhile, checking out menus that were posted in the windows of a few different restaurants.  Finally we settled on Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville because we saw that they had a few vegetarian options.
The place was very crowded but we spotted a couple of empty seats at the bar.  There was a cover band on stage and the music was very loud, but pretty good.  We were greeted promptly by one of the bartenders, given a couple of menus, and we decided to have a couple beers while we waited.  The beer selection wasn't the best, but any cold beer on a muggy night like Saturday was good enough for me.  
We decided to order a couple of veggie burgers to take back to the hotel for dinner.  I ordered the El Diablo Burger (sub-veggie patty) and my boyfriend ordered the Barbecue Bacon Cheeseburger (no bacon, sub-veggie patty).  While we waited for our order, we were entertained by the other bartender on duty doing a variety of glass-tosses and bottle flipping.  It was actually really fun to watch.  Our order took bit longer than I had expected, but it was understandable considering how busy the restaurant was that night.  We each had one more beer, paid for our order (the price was reasonable), and headed back to the hotel.
We finally got back to the hotel and sat down to eat.  The presentation was nice and our server/bartender made sure that napkins, condiments, and silverware were all included in out to go bag.  The burgers were good, but not great.  The hand formed patties were a little small for the buns and a little under done for my taste (for those of you that have never tried a veggie burger, they really need to be cooked well done so that they are not mushy in the middle).  I did like the big chunks of carrot, edamame, peppers, and peas in the patties.  The El Diablo Burger was way, way too spicy for the both of us, and we generally really like spicy foods.  The Barbecue burger was fantastic.  The barbecue sauce was smoky and sweet, and the onion strings were good and crispy.  
All in all it was a good meal.  The service and atmosphere was great and the food was ok.  It's probably not a restaurant that I would frequent, but good for an occasional visit.  I would liken it to about any other chain restaurant; not the best, but good enough.  I'd say it was worth for what we paid, and definitely worth the three star rating.

I generally do NOT review or post anything.  My experience this weekend at Ole Red has forced me to post a review.  As a resident of Nashville with friends visiting from out of town we found ourselves at Ole Red.  Hopes were high, results were low and I will never visit Ole Red again and I will make sure that EVERY person that I know that visits Nashville will not pay patronage to Ole Red.  Sad place, self serving and selfish.  

We stopped at Ole Red to have a drink.   With an 11 year old child, it is tough to "stop and have a drink" because children cannot sit at a bar.  I would never encourage that and agree with the general rule.  That said, you have to actually take a table.   We got our table pretty quick and settled in for a drink and an order of fries.  

We were promptly notified by "Jesse" (our server) that we have to eat food.  Okay, well we ordered fries for the kid.   Jesse was kind enough to tell me - well your splitting hairs and that is not food and we were going to be moved.  

We opted to leave.  On the way out i asked the hostess - are you guys backed up for tables?   I see 4 open empty tables and our server stipulated that people were waiting for tables.  They indicated a 20 -30 minute wait.  Not sure how you have a 30 minute wait with empty tables -  perhaps just low staffing.

Either way - doesn't matter.  At the end of the day - High Hopes, Low Results.    New moniker for Ole Red - HHLR

I will make sure that NO ONE I KNOW will ever visit this place.

If you do visit - Ask for Server Jessie - he is the sharpest tool in the shed.
We enjoyed the music and atmosphere.  Ordered the fish and chips and they were very good.  Our server Josie was amazing!

Ole Red opened May 1 and it's quite nice!   Signs of Blake Shelton everywhere and there's even a phone that is for incoming calls only from Blake!  I ordered a white sangria that was fantastic and we had appetizers - tater tots with cheese and biscuits.    They have an in house chef that is amazing.  All the breads are made from scratch.   The biscuits came with blackberry jam and bourbon butter.    Can't wait to go back and try more food!

Quintessential Nashville bar with relatively inexpensive drinks (from a California perspective), live entertainment, and captivating decor. Layla's is linear in nature with bars on both levels and the stage adjacent to the entry. Live entertainment primarily covers country songs with the occasional pop hit. The bar is decorated with license plates on the ceiling and bar patrons can have their plates added while limited space remains. Upon arriving, I highly recommend ordering drinks upstairs and hang out there if you want to avoid the crowds. Local trick - many of the bars have entrances from the rear alley; however, that was not necessary as we had no wait on a popping Saturday night. No coverage charge.

(Was there a few years ago but I just found this saved in my drafts so I thought I'd post it!) G reat bar.  i bet it's terrifying in the daytime but it's adorable at night with it's fat colored xmas lights, license plates and red stools.  Live bluegrass most days of the week and the band that was playing when we were there (jypsi) was great.

I've never been to a Margaritaville before and had a great time. The food was great and had the BEST server. Her name is Christina and she was awesome! Very attentive without being overbearing. I'm from South Carolina and she is the reason our experience was so great. Loved it and her! We will be back 100% the next time we're in Nashville.

At first I said " great a touristy hamburger joint" the only problem is, it's good. Yeah, way touristy, but service is stellar Chanda our server was great. 

The atmosphere, well its tourist mauve. The entertainment is five star, they don't beg for tips, my feeling is these guys have just about made it. 

Now for the unexpected surprise was the cauliflower. Yes, I said it cauliflower. Damn it was good. Or rather it was so damn good. I could eat these things everyday. I also ordered the Ole Hamburger, yes for medium it was good. I think all hamburgers are served medium. But the house made pickles made it over the top. 

So in retrospect all good. I'd come here again.
The Bar itself was immaculate, the bartenders Jericho and Tim were amazing., Great conversation, and very knowledgeable. Make sure you go to the third floor for Oysters and see Kaylie..

I've always been a fan of Bridgestone Arena. It's a great venue in a nice location right off of Broadway near all the bars and such. I like that security is so tight and the employees that work elsewhere in the arena are always so friendly and will often joke with you and hold a conversation. I would definitely recommend catching a concert or show here.

Groovy little honkytonk bar on Music Row in Nashville. I was drawn in by the amazing musicians playing one afternoon. The drink menu at the bar leaves a lot to be desired, but they had no problems letting me pull up a stool and just listen to the music without buying any alcohol. Major kudos for that! I did get a soda. Really down home little bar with great performers!

Had a great time here on two evenings -- Awesome bands both nights which provided lots of entertainment and good music. Josh Gallagher (9.28) and Kelby Costner (9.30.19). 

Didn't seem to have many waitresses available and the bathrooms need to be cleaned or at least checked more often. I am definitely going back next time in Nashville.

We had been wanting to come here for quite sometime because we often drink beer from here at restaurants. The environment was really relaxed and chill and there were plenty of places to sit, both upstairs and downstairs. I feel like this would be a fantastic place to host a private party for a beer lover & guests! 

The beer was great and the prices were reasonable. I had a flight and I enjoyed the lighter beers. There was a food menu as well but we did not eat.

The customer service was subpar. No one was really smiling and everyone was kind of zoned out and seemed to just be going through the motions. Curious as to how they would operate in a busy setting.

Overall, I would come back again but it wasn't anything to write home about. I would be fine grabbing a six pack if I just wanted to enjoy the beer.
