Nice venue. Clean and seemingly easy to navigate. Didn't have to wait to use the restroom, not a single time. One draft beer was $11, and it was about a pint of beer. A 20-oz bottle of water cost $5. These prices and these remarks cover the Bon Jovi concert on February 18, 2017.

It's been a lamentably long time since I've been to a live concert--like 30 years.  The Bridgestone Arena was a great place to break that dry spell.  We were in section 101, straight ahead from the stage, a bit left of center from that perspective, and about 8 rows up.  These were great seats.  If I weren't getting older and blindy, they would have been even better seats, but for the things I couldn't eyeball, I simply had to gaze upwards to the large monitor.  Anything would have been better than the churning jumble of the people in the floor seats, where folks had to stand the entire concert in hopes of seeing anything.

I imagine that even the nosebleed seats had a splendid view of the stage, because the Arena really isn't very large.  We heard and read that the Bon Jovi concert broke attendance records for a concert at this venue, but it did seem laid back during the concert.  That's most likely because of the performer and the relatively advanced age of the attendees.  But that's a supposition...which shares most of its letters with "suppository", so take that for what it's worth.

Upon decamping the spectacle, we hiked about 4 blocks south and 2-3 blocks west before summoning an Uberide (a newly-discovered elemental wonder), because the general area was chaotic.  Broadway, which was likely already crowded, suddenly had nearly 20,000 hyped-up concert-goers dumped on it.  We got out of Dodge and retreated to the respite of the 1808 bar at the hotel next door to our hotel.

All in all, I'd like to go to another concert at the Bridgestone Arena.  It is a comfortable, clean place with short concession lines and quick bathroom access...the ultimate and penultimate qualities of a great venue.

This pub joint is simply awesome. I love the decorations of this place with an array of License Plates hanging all over the place. The band did an outstanding job. Great entertainment and Great Vibe, you simply cannot go wrong. It was a nice place too to get away from the crowds. It was simply a ton of fun!

I am a bit conflicted on this one, and for opposite reasons as Southern Grist. I love the atmosphere of the place. It just screams great microbrewery. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable and you walk into the brewery (iron fenced off) to get to the necessary rooms, so you get to smell the grain and malts. But I am not a huge fan of most of their beer.

I did a flight with friends and we sampled pretty much everything. Frankly, I don't find their large releases that interesting, so I was trying to hit everything I have not tried in a can. Of the beers I had that night, the Quad aged in Dickel barrels was, by far, the best. The barrel aged porter was a second, but far enough behind to set the Quad apart.

I am an IPA lover and I am really not into the bitter, kick me over and over again taste of the double. The malt at that gravity should tone down and push it either forward or backward, and it does neither. Of the non barreled aged, the blonde was the most interesting to me (and I am generally not a fan of blondes, so that might be another win for TN Brew Works).

The atmosphere really makes it for me. There are a few tables downstairs, a long table in the brewery, and a nice upstairs seating area. The stools are a bit hard for long time sitting, so I stood part of the time, but I really like the atmosphere. 

The food is also decent and a draw for many. And it is real meals, not just small bites. And more like a gastropub than just a brewery. Definite thumbs up in this department.

I was at the Descendents show recently, and the guy running the lighting for the night was hands down the worst I've ever encountered (I've been going to shows for more than 22 years on a very routine basis, in a variety of cities / venues). 

I'm really surprised that the lights in the venue weren't all blue, so that this autistic moron could "Light It Up Blue" for Autistic Awareness all night. Idiot kept playing with the house lights WHILE the band was playing the entire time; you couldn't see the band b/c of it. There's a reason why all the lights face the stage once the show is underway.  

If this place wants to charge top dollar for its shows compared to other venues in the South, they need to step up their game. 

See the autism, hear the autism, feel the autism, BE the autism.

Not very good at all, the drinks were alright, but the food was super disappointing. I got a salad with crispy chicken on it, the lettuce looked like it was just soaked in water and put on the salad, very soggy. The chicken on top looked really delicious, but every single bite I took had a tendon in it and I couldn't eat it. My boyfriend ordered a bison burger, and while cooked very nicely, there was literally an ounce of sauce on it. Very disappointing. Came a while back and was really good. Music was AMAZING though, Tawnya Reynolds was fabulous.

This was the worst brewery I have ever been to. The beer was not very good and all of the flavors were very bitter. I am disappointed after having a flight and not finishing any of the samples. All of the beers taste similiar and there really is no variation. I came here because it was rainy and it was not a good decision.

The ambiance of this place is awesome. They have several high top tables set up that look out into their brewing area. I shared a sample platter with my sister. All of their beers were great. If you want food, they have a food truck set up outside. On your way out, grab a couple of growlers of your favorite beer!

I wanted to love it here, truly. I will preface by saying the staff is amazing and the only reason for three stars. We ate on the 5th floor, and other than the hot chicken sandwich, the food was mediocre at best. The pulled pork was somehow dry and greasy at the same time, with no sauce and a few shreds of slaw. It had to be sent back. The fries were the only saving grace for the under-sized burgers. The calamari was extremely greasy, but not in a yummy, fried way, but in a heavily over- sauced way. Quality control needs to be enforced, I doubt the famous owners would be okay with lack of care and finess coming from the kitchen.
Ole Red has amazing food, drinks, and live music!

I have called once a day for six days to get an accidental extra charge on my card reversed. Honestly had a great time, even plan to come back but at this point I feel this is all I can do to get someone's attention. I have worked in hospitality roughly 12 years- I understand these mistakes are made but come on what's the hold up? Hopefully this message is read.. UPDATE** I have been told by the manager Jamie that he will not refund my card the $48 they took from me. Someone else that night got very lucky and left with a free bar tab compliments of me! Be warned if you go to this bar you may pay for someone else's drinks apparently. (This all comes after I made a total of 7 phone calls in 8 days trying to get this resolved). Couldn't be more upset with this bar.
Josh the bartender is very inconsiderate and unprofessional.  The bar is overrated and overpriced. Rude service. Won't come back.

Bridgestone is a great concert venue!

I attended the Florence + the Machine concert here on October 2, 2018. We stayed close enough to be able to walk to the venue, and as a visitor to Nashville, you might very well be able to do the same thing. The arena is in the heart of it, absolutely surrounded by hotels! I can't speak to the event parking experience, but following my Nashville experience, my guess it will be pricey.
The event staff were friendly enough. Certainly efficient in getting people in to the venue. We also go there pretty early, so there wasn't really a line. The first entrance we wanted to go in turned out to be for general admission only...so be ready to walk to the entire way around the building if you have tickets with a seat number. That part was a little annoying, since it was still so stupidly hot outside. And inside....it was a FREEZER!! So so cold in the arena.
Food and drink prices are probably in line with most large venue/professional sporting team locations. Which is to say...expensive.

The most frustrating part of my time here was when I was trying to find the women's restroom. We had just passed the men's restroom, so it had to be coming soon! I kept walking and didn't see it! I had to ask a staff member where the closest restroom was. It was literally right behind me...it was just not able to be seen because the concert merch booth was set up in front of it block the sign and hiding the entrance. 

As for the concert, the seats were comfortable enough to utilize when waiting for the acts to start. And they were set up in a way that even though I am rather short and we were at a slightly awkward angle from the stage, I had absolutely no problem seeing! That is kind of a big deal for me! That I left the show sore only from all the walking and jumping around I had done during the day, and not also because I was craning my head and neck around trying to see the concert!

We drove 8 hours and this was the first sit down restaurant we went to. The first bad thing we experienced was our waitress not coming over to us because she said "sorry I was having a little fun." It's a place of business, you can have fun while taking care of your customers. The next thing we experienced was her not bringing my beer on 2 different occasions. She also did not check on us very many times as we kept wondering where she was. Then when she brought us our tickets, she didn't ask how we wanted them split. She just put us on 5 different tickets. I was with with my wife. I had also ordered friend pickles and wanted to pay for them and she split them with the other people that came with us, again she did this all without asking what we preferred. Then when she gave us our tickets, names of the drinks we ordered were all mixed up which created confusion amongst all of us. We thought we were charged extra for a drink so we asked about it, a little bit after talking to her about it, she got an attitude and was very rude to my mom who was asking her about it. She proceeded to say, "Look, I have worked 12 hours." You don't say that in business, you take care of your customers. This employee was a female with short hair, we never got her name. I asked to speak to her manager and it took about 10 minutes to get someone over to us. They brought 3 managers over and apologized but the manager let the waitress that was rude to us stand and listen to the conversation which was very unprofessional. I told the manager about our experience and she just apologized and walked away. The supervisor was named Cheryl (might be wrong spelling). We spent $100 on 3 meals and it was something you could've eaten anywhere, wouldn't have been so bad if we didn't have such a lackadaisical waitress and management team. Jimmy would be super disappointed, if I was an area manager, I would be making some huge changes at this Margaritaville. It has prompted me to not go back to one.

Service was excellent we sat at the upstairs bar. Had a spicy and sweet cocktail it was delicious. Had the hot chicken sandwich it wasn't very spicy but when you added pickled jalapeños it was great. Pretty location. Live music all day was very good.

Slow service!!! 
My whole table ordered waters and were given (and charged for)  bottled water instead of ice water in a glass.  It was only 90 degrees out so we were are all fine w being limited to 16oz of water.  Got the burger every one on here was talking about.  Idk if the waitress asked us for a burger temp as a joke bc everyone at the table received a full cooked, well done burger (I ordered mine medium rare). 
Wasn't impressed w the whole experience.   Will not return.

I have called once a day for six days to get an accidental extra charge on my card reversed. Honestly had a great time, even plan to come back but at this point I feel this is all I can do to get someone's attention. I have worked in hospitality roughly 12 years- I understand these mistakes are made but come on what's the hold up? Hopefully this message is read...
Horrible food. Horrible service. At least they didn't charge us when we couldn't eat what they served.

Our party of 4 went to Jimmy Buffets Margaritaville tonite. 2 of us ordered the Bourbon Salmon. The meal was horrible. The salad was iceberg lettuce & the salmon was not edible.. it was extremely fishy and spoiled.. when I mentioned it to our waiter he sent over the manager. She said we had eaten it all except a bite or two. Which was not true!! She went ahead & said she would give us a 40% discount! When we received the bill it was more like $4 discount .. at that point it was useless to try to resolve this . I paid the bill and left . Would not recommend this restaurant if you want a good meal. It was overpriced and the food was spoiled..
Worst jambalaya I have ever had! Took us forever to get a sever to come to the table and it wasn't even busy.

TLDR: Great place for beer and food under one roof in The Gulch.

While there are a good number of food options in The Gulch, it's always a plus when you can have good beer and good food under one roof. In case craft beer and brewery crawls are your thing, Tennessee Brew Works is one of four breweries that you can walk to in the Gulch, in addition to New Heights, Yazoo, and Jackalope.

Tennessee Brew Works has an impressive space to work with - it's got two floors, outdoor seating, a space for live music, and TV's to watch the game. There are bars both upstairs and downstairs and they'll bring food to you no matter where you order and where you sit.

As far as the beer goes, there were 12 different beers on tap, as well as two ciders and two wine selections. In case you want to check out the tap list ahead of time prior to coming in, see here: https://www.tnbrew.com/on-tap. Pints are priced well, $5.50-7.00 per, and flights are available here for $11, which gives you 5 sample sized pours. The tap list does have your standard year round selections, seasonal beers, and small batch/one off/variants, etc. I went with the flight and got to try:

- Southern Wit (Belgian style white ale)
- Wildwood Flower (Belgian style honey blonde)
- King Chestnut (brown ale)
- Basil Ryeman
- TENN No. 12 - Imperial Porter

The Wildwood Flower and King Chestnut were okay, while they other three were pretty good. I particularly liked the TENN No. 12 - I think it's a great porter and if you like dark beers, you'll certainly like this one.

As you might already have read from other reviews, the food is pretty good here. I definitely recommend the frog legs and the poutine. The frog legs are nice and crispy and come with toast made with Southern Wit and pickles. The poutine was pretty unique - it was made with sweet potato fries and an egg. I thought it was a nice variation on a classic dish.

While there are no shortage of good places to eat in the area, I think Tennessee Brew Works is a solid option for both good food and good beer. Can't go wrong with that.

Food was good, and I kept it simple - burger and fries.  The drink I ordered did take a little bit of time, as did the end of my meal, with some confusion about payment.  My server was slammed, but I'll give her a pass.

When I got there, it was already crowded.  I went and put my name down for a table, and was told that if I wanted faster service, I could find a place to sit at the bar.  I wasn't in a rush, but I was appreciative that they pointed that out to me.  I didn't mind waiting, and the live music was good.

My wife wanted to come here. Once we arrived, we got into it. This place was rocking. 5 floors, full of people and music. We walked in and checked in to find out there was no seats available for dinner. The list was long. I knew that. There was a hockey game, NCAA tournament on TV, spring break and a few bachelorette parties going on. The wait was long. They recommended the 5fl. So we went up. When we got off the elevator, it was also packed but there were some people leaving so we got a seat quickly. We then moved to the bar area. The band was playing some really cool, good, fun, music. Everybody was having a great time. Singing and dancing was everywhere. We ordered food and drinks as we joined in the festivities. The service was quick and the food came quickly also. I ordered the Nashville hot chicken sangwich and the bbq sandwich also. Both were really good and plenty of food.  We took a bunch of videos of some of the bands and pictures from the roof top. Once we were done, we went back down stairs and went to the store. We purchased a few things like tee shirts, stickers and a few other little things. The store was full of souvenirs and again, people.
In all, this place was rocking and tons of fun. The food was good. The band's were great. The whole experience was pretty awesome. I highly recommended coming here, if you wanna have a good time. Well worth it.
Good food, great service, great music.  Fun, lively atmosphere.  Comfortable tables.  Clean bathrooms.  Nice gift shop.
Stopped in for a snack while spending some time on broadway. The nachos are amazing of course and plenty to share!! Great quick service as well

Awesome brewery to stop through in Nashville! It's a great space with several bars, lots of tables, and a nice outdoor spot. The guys behind the bar and back in the brewery are so friendly.

The beer was great! I particularly enjoyed the "Country Hicks" sweet potato stout. The food was great too! Generous portions, with great flavors. The fries are outstanding, thinly cut and spiced perfectly!

I always have a good time at TNBW. They offer live music, karaoke on certain nights, darts, a killer patio, great beer and food you would not expect at a brewery. 

The only miss here is the indoor seating options. Downstairs there are high top bar barrel tables , they're soo cool but it doesn't leave much room for your legs and if you have more than three people at a table you could feel very crowded, though the table could accommodate five. Upstairs, the tables also feel crowded like your stuck in a corner at in spot in the open upstairs area. If I'm upstairs I like to sit at the bar or by the darts! 

The patio is spot on, different levels of the patio accommodate large or small groups and the seating is covered and comfortable. I love when they roll up the door and let the music flow outside as well. 

Their seasonal beers are always so creative and light up their already finely crafted beer menu. As well as wine for our non beer drinking friends and family!

The fish tacos are my favorite, $10 for two fried white fish tacos topped with a miso glaze and red cabbage slaw. A must try! 

The burger is worth the $15, it's very similar to a delicious burger from the likes of Butchertown Hall. If you don't eat meat, you can order the impossible burger!

Their beets dish is so refreshing and great for one person or share with the table. Tennessee Brew Works offers a rotation of seasonal starters you'd expect from a farm to table restaurant and they also offer heavier fried and creamy options, there's really something for everyone here.

New ownership, new sound, new lights, and new bathrooms over the Fall 2013. It's new, improved, and renovated. The pizza place next door is brand new as well. Check it out on Facebook or Google. Old reviews are before the changes.

Please visit and post your comments.

Investor

I would give 0 stars after the security staff let a drunken man taking his clothes off on the dance floor on 10/20/19 after he was pushing people around multiple times. Multiple people had gone to security about his behavior. Eventually he was intentionally stepping on my friend. She told him he was "being an asshole". The girl he was dancing with then punched her in the face. My friend went to staff at the bar and asked them to call the police. They didn't. In the mean time I was pushed down by this man who was coming at me aggressively until other members at the bar grabbed me from him. Eventually security shows up and kicks them out...security tells us they can't do anything and there are "20 cops outside" who could help us. They proceed to laugh at the situation. I've never been more disappointed and disrespected in my life. Blake Shelton you should be embarrassed at how your staff handled this situation. Here is a picture of one of the security guards who absolutely should not be employed

We entered this bar at 8pm and a woman in our party was refused service because she was "too drunk" when we were not drunk at all. That wasn't the real problem because we realize misunderstandings happen like this. BUT she had a water bottle violently thrown at her by a bartender while he yelled "get tf out of here" when we were not violent nor protested at all. It was their loss, because we had an excellent time at other bars this evening. I wish we knew the name of the bartender so I could make a specific complaint about him. He was an older gentleman.
The burger is incredible and the porter beer was my favorite. Nice place to hang with friends and watch a game. Only downside is the live band is way too loud.

Stopped in for a drink here on a Sunday afternoon. I ordered the "5 o'clock Somewhere" margarita that came with rum, passion fruit tequila, Bacardi 151, orange and pineapple juice and splash of grenadine...unfortunately I did not enjoy my drink! It was way too sweet, I should have gone with the classic instead! We also ordered the Volcano Nachos to split between four people. They were huuuuge and delicious, they came with chili, cheese, pico de gallo, guac and sour cream. I would say, they could have used more of everything, once you eat the top layer you're really left with a bunch of empty chips. 

On a Sunday they had a great guitar player soothing our ears with live music. It's a really fun atmosphere. At night this place was always packed so I'd recommend getting here early if you want a seat!

If you're the RHCP, then you're Under The Bridge-Stoned. This is not that. Although they've probably played here so.

Great place to see a concert. I got free tickets to the Dixie Chicks a long time ago (i.e. I broke in to the arena and watched them free) and it was a good venue back then, and judging by the Bruno Mars concert the other night it's even more awesome now. They've had some renovations and I like it.

A lot of big artists come here and it's right on the end of Broadway a few doors up from all the little bars where all the struggling artists are playing and I think that's a really great thing because it's like this is where you play to to make it and then once you make it you move a few doors down into the arena and if you're really rocking it you just cross the river and hop into the stadium.

Best location for an arena really, anywhere.
Good drinks. Willing to make a cocktail off the menu. Relaxed atmosphere with acoustic guitar on a Sunday afternoon.

Came here with my wife and some friends to celebrate a birthday and it was our first night out in Nashville and first time to a Margaritaville...

We didn't have any reservations and waited about 20 minutes to be seated...however it wasn't really that bad of a wait and we ordered drinks and waited by the bar. We were a party of five so there wasn't seating at the bar for all of us... however for a party of two we would've been fine.

The bartender was friendly and the drinks were made good and strong; the great customer service continued upstairs where we were seated and enjoyed a live band performing. The food didn't come all that quick but we weren't in a rush so it worked out great for all of us. 

To my surprise there were plenty of families eating dinner there with young ones and everything blended just fine. 

The food was really good but wasn't anything special of course, but that's to be expected here it's more about the experience, atmosphere, margaritas, and live music. I definitely recommend this as a place to stop by or definitely a starter if you plan on going bar-hopping.

I will definitely would come back with my wife here for a night out in town again! Definitely will sit by the bar though. Didn't have a problem with the kids...but a date night away from the kids for us we would like to truly get "away" lol.

Excellent venue. Nashville is one of those towns you arrive early. Getting in and out for people staying downtown was made easy by the local police closing part of Broadway. Most definitely a return trip is in order.

Great venue for concerts. Attended a sat night concert of Counting Crows & Matchbox 20.  It is in the heart of downtown Nashville so you can hit the bars before or after. Not sure about parking because we took Uber.  I liked the food choices and bathrooms were clean and easily accessible .

I'm a big Nashville predators fan and I love this place but I had to give 3 stars for my recent visit. I was at the Tennessee Auburn game and was told I had Lexus lounge access since I sat in the front row also with my tickets went to the Lexus lounge and some lady who I'm 99 percent sure didn't work for Bridgestone arena said we weren't allowed in their after we showed the ticket. She was very rude to us and wouldn't answer our questions (really people like her shouldn't have authority to do that like her cause she didn't work at Bridgestone arena). The lady looked like she was with the SEC so I can see why she was rude. I went back to my seats since they had a better view than the Lexus lounge. 

I'm a life long preds fan and have ZERO  problems with this place when I'm at preds games for example when I sometimes have access to the patron club ZERO PROBLEMS  (I go on average to 10 to 15 games a season) love Bridgestone arena but when it's a non preds related events thing don't go as planned with me I'm not trying to be mean in this review I will for sure go back to Bridgestone to see my preds play

The food and beer here were great! Staff is friendly and helpful, I got a flight with beers all recommended by the bartender. And each beer was phenomenal! Try the grilled cheese if you get food- it's tasty with a tomato jam and mix of cheeses. Try the stouts - they were my favorite part of the flight!

We had a great time and actually went twice. We had dinner on the first floor and it wasn't special, but it was good. The bands we heard were great. We went back a couple days later to the rooftop Lookout and had a great time up there. It's got a lounge feel and good view. Less crowded and wild than the other rooftops on Broadway with good acoustic music.

This is a very laid back establishment, but almost to laid back. There is two different parts to this bar: Winners and Losers. Winners is set up for those who are wanting to eat, and relax (yes, you can get beer on this side too however, it is more geared towards eating) Losers is more of a full bar atmosphere where you can order shots and get a little rowdy! Unfortunately, for us, there was not much to see. Perhaps it is because we arrived on a Saturday around 4pm so the venue was rather boring as we were the only ones in there. The best part about this bar is it is not on the strip, near Broadway, so the prices are more reasonable. I think I paid $16 for a bucket of Millet Lite bottles? All I know is it was less than $20! The bartenders are very friendly and easy to talk to... I will admit it is nice to be able to talk to friends and the workers without having to repeat myself or scream at the top of my lungs to get a beer or even just say Hello. Very relaxing atmosphere, and if I am back in Nashville, I will have to go during a time that I am hungry and ready for some action. Come to think of it, there was not a band playing perhaps that is why it seemed so quite? I do realize it was rather early to be out, but when in Nashville on a Saturday, and day drinking I expected a little more to be happening than two empty quite bars.

This is my second time in Nashville and I'm trying to find a couple great beer places.  This place not only has a great beer selection but it's a Cubs bar too!!!  Some good food too. 

Way to go!!!

Popped in to check it out and listen to some good music. The singers/band we heard were excellent (Chad Bearden and Casee Allen), and interacted with the crowd well. The bartender, Cass, made our visit even more enjoyable. She was attentive, efficient, and offered fun conversation in between helping other guests. She didn't mind us, the visitors from Delaware, bending her ear a little. It appeared patrons as well as other staff enjoy her jovial personality. 

We liked the layout of Ole Red. Nice and comfortable. Great sound system, and the aroma of leather filled the air.
Great place to spend the afternoon w drinks, food and lots of Nashville fun!! Love this restaurant!!

Pricey alcohol and food as with any arena. Parking is available at the Music City Center across the street from the arena, and it's typically $20-$30. Definitely the best option unless you're local, then uber! For Predators hockey games, wear your Preds gear!!! If you don't have any, there are Preds swag stores located in a few different locations around the first floor. The energy is unparalleled! 
There are several chants that you will surely pick up, some a little edgy, all of them in fun!

For this season, the predators are incorporating fun technologies like their light up bracelets! They give these to patrons at the door upon arrival- note!! They have three different settings: fast blinking, still light, and off. You are completely in control of the way the bravely light up if fast flashes of light bother you! A fun souvenir for what is sure to be a fun evening!

Our visit was mid-week and in the afternoon. There was no wait for a table, and the live music was in full swing. Our waitress, Nira, was amazing. The energy in the place is great, and the food turned out to be amazing. 

Drinks are expensive ($12 for an average sized mixed drink), but delicious. My first time ever eating fried pickles, they kind of blew my mind. They come with 2 sauces. A white one, which is more spicy, and a red one, which is more sweet. 

Each of our entrees were delicious. The bucket of chicken is a great deal. The half order would be nearly enough to feed 2 people. I also spotted their nacho plates, and they are ENORMOUS. You will need 4 people to finish one of those. 

Oh by the way, Blake Shelton came in. Overall this was a 5 star experience with absolutely 0 to complain about.

1) Empty, cave-like acoustics.
2) Rude/pushy staff. 
3) Restroom "attendants". 
4) Overpriced food. 
5) Far from ideal setup for a music venue.

MMW is basically a huge, open factory floor. All of the amenities are situated against the walls of this giant empty room. The stage and the fans end up being in the approximate middle of this room, between four steel pillars. Inside those four pillars, there is barely passable sound reinforcement quality. If the crowd is large enough to crowd outside of those four pillars, those outside of that square area will experience sound quality that is atrocious.

The rules and policies of this venue are apparently to treat all patrons like unruly criminals. It's almost as though the management is implementing unwarranted sports arena/stadium policies and attitudes among it's staff. 

I have attended one show here and will NEVER attend another at this venue. My experience was of a fairly innocuous nature, but was generally unpleasant, and certainly not enjoyable. Many of my friends have attended other shows at MMW and had even worse experiences. DONT GO HERE!

they had a YEAR...read that again...A YEAR notice that we would be arriving with a large group (80+) with multiple confirmations prior to our arrival. Yet upon our arrival, at the prescribed time, we were told the room was not ready and we would need to wait....A YEAR, then there were not enough seats as we had requested...the poor bartender had to bus tables (which was great for the people waiting in line for a drink) the food was beyond sub par! The chicken was dry and like shoe leather.  This was the low-light of our trip to Nashville! Avoid this place like you would avoid the plague!  Terrible!

Dinner tonight- after a bit of a wait we were seated. Server wasn't as attentive since we didn't order alcohol as the table behind us did. Food was good - Hot Chicken was properly hot, pickles good. Hubs burger was good too but the tots were slightly disappointing.  Good music made up for the shortfalls!

I've never been treated so badly in my life. We ordered a sandwich with bacon and French toast. the sandwich came with no bacon and we told the waiter and after waiting 30 mins for the bacon,  we ate it without the bacon.  The French toast never came,  even after an hour that we were waiting there...  When the check came, it was charging me for the French toast and the additional $2 for the bacon we never ate and waited forever for.  When I asked the waiter to take these two items off my check since they never came,  he laughed at my face and said it was only $10 (and that I was being ridiculous for asking for this...) it wasn't only this,  I can't even put it in writing how awfully disrespected I felt.

We were looking for a quick meal after the Country Music Hall of Fame and before the Grand Ole Opry. We weren't expecting much but were pleasantly surprised. We had the half order of the Champagne of Chicken (can get hot or not). A half order is a half  chicken so consists of 4 pieces. Two of us split a half order. It comes with biscuits and gravy.  We ordered one side which was huge and shared among 4 people. We got the "not hot" chicken and we all agreed it was the best fried chicken we had ever had. The live music was awesome but was very loud so don't plan on having a conversation.

Horrible service. Air conditioner leaked onto the table the entire time. Top 10 worst margaritas I've ever had. Extremely over priced. Order of nachos, 1 margarita, and 2 sodas came out to $50. Save your time and money. Go somewhere else.

I stop in everytime I am in Nashville. Its surprisingly not a tourist trap like many of the other places I have been to. The food is reasonably priced. The brussel sprouts were the best I have ever had. The elevator is easy to find for us buzzed chubby people trying to get to the roof top! Service is fast and friendly. Definitely a go to spot when in Nashville.
Great place to watch concerts!!! Parking is easy and you're right on Broadway! What more can you ask for right??

I walked in on Valentine's Day around 8PM, and it  was we pretty empty .  I was surprised that maybe 8 people in the back dining section and the hostess said it would be a quick service.  I ordered a salad and burger.  I waited over an hour to get my food.  I was so hungry.  Little did I know that it would take an hour and 45 minutes to eat here.  I would not return, especially if I was in a hurry.  I would have left after 30 minutes after ordering, but I didn't want to be rude.  Very disappointed!

Always good no matter where you are at  
Even though I love Margaritaville it seems a shame to pass up all the other great bars in Nashville  It is always a great experience, I love to come here  I do however consider it a commerical chain and will be looking for 
a good local bar ( problem is its had to find a good one) !
You always know you will be happy with Jimmy !

Awesome piece of space on Clinton Street.
Enough parking for everyone, lots of other shops nearby to wander into.

Went to a concert here one night and had no trouble parking, getting into the venue, ordering a drink, getting a seat, watching the show, getting close to the performer.
The sound was awesome, (as long as you're not right up in front of a speaker), and it's non-smoking!  Big + in my book.

Getting tickets was easy. They have a box office open during lunch hour all week long.  You can either order your tickets online or head over to the box office and save yourself a few bucks.

I'd like to see some more bigger names in there. 
I appreciate small venues with larger than life performers..
And I also appreciate the fact that they have seating for those willing to pay a little more, rather than standing and watching the whole concert.

Two bars, good variety of shows, plenty of parking, good sound system, good lighting...
non smoking.

The staff is friendly, and the music is decent. The food was edible, but not worth the price. A vegetarian salad with little more than lettuce was $15. My mom had a cheeseburger and thought it was okay. The margarita was fantastic though! People beside us ordered nachos and it looked like the kitchen used a full bag of tortilla chips, so the portion quantity is definitely not small.

Hosted a company event at Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville-Nashville.  What an OUTSTANDING experience!!!  Jennifer, sales event specialist, guided me through the entire process, worked with me on the menu, assisted with budget suggestions and met me at the venue on the evening of the party.  Above and beyond!!!  

The food was incredible as well!  We had a variety of "self serve" options and all of it tasted amazing!!  The staff kept the food warm and full for our party guests!  They were engaging, friendly, and went out of their way to keep our guests happy.

I would definitely recommend this location and this team for any event you are planning!!!

Dave R.
Terrible service on the rooftop. Kayla the waitress treated us with waters but never came back. She continues to walk by and say nothing. Omg. The worst experience.

My husband and I took a short trip to Nashville after Christmas in December 2018.  This was our first stop when we arrived in Nashville.  We had no idea where we were going or what we were doing.  Looked like a dive so we happened upon it.  It was the afternoon so it was pretty dead.  We sat at the bar and had the best bartender Elaine!  She gave us lots of tips on places to go and things to do.  So friendly and lots of great drink specials!  They had vodka Capri suns!  Mmmmmmm!!!  We asked tons of questions and spotted some celebrities!!  This was a great local spot and glad we happened upon it at the start of our vacation!!!

We did the Thursday night whiskey jam as well.  So much fun!  We saw a ton of great bands and very cool atmosphere.  Well worth checking out!!

Really liked this place.  Liked the decor and loved the tractor that is hanging from the ceiling upside down.  The two guys that were on stage were really good.  Sang a good variety of songs and different artists.  They didn't have to compete with the other places on Broadway.  Most of the other places on Broadway have open air bars and the music flows out into the street.  It can be a bit much as they seem to be competing with each other and just becomes noise.  I had the Cherry Limeade. Delicious!!!  Husband ordered the Champagne of Fried Chicken and I had the pulled pork sandwich.  The fried chicken comes with biscuits and gravy.  So good! True southern biscuits and gravy.   Lots of fries chicken and it was really good too.  Pulled pork sandwich was good too.  Came with coleslaw and I chose a side of tator tots as my side.  They were different - ok.  Lots of people recommend them in other reviews.  Debra was our server and she was great!   I would go back and explore more on the menu.

My first stop in Nashville. Took a scooter there from the hotel. They have a great beer selection and the folks are ready to discuss what goes into the beers which I very much appreciate. The people are awesome! Friendly as can be. After some beers I asked for the food menu and as always asked the bartender what was good. He suggested the cheese burger and said it had won awards. I almost expect that everwhere I go but I decided to trust him and give it a try. The burger was awesome! Amazing flavor and cooked perfectly. The shoestring fries crisp and yummy

If you are in Nashville and want a good beer and burger look no further

Visiting Nashville we stopped by this venue for a
show. It's a cool setup and has a lot of potential but the staff SUCKS! The bartenders are the rudest I've ever experienced. For overpriced, water downed drinks, I don't need the attitude to go with it. Lots of better places in Nashville.
Fun place for someone not from here! No cover and average service!

Rather disappointing. All the reviews I read about this place made it seem top notch. Food was average at best. Hot chicken biscuit wasn't all that good. The home made tots are bland tasting. Not sure if it's how they make them, or if they're suppose to be mushy inside. Only good call out, they have Big Red as a fountain drink!! I'm a big fan of Blake, but go to Aldean's, it's better.

PS. Service was horribly slow!

Tennessee Brew Works has a very cool atmosphere for any beer drinkers! A combination of indoor and outdoor seating and multiple bars make this a neat place. I was underwhelmed by their beers but they have a large enough selection that you can find one you like. Go for the beer but you'll probably enjoy the atmosphere more!

Had an awesome time at Tennessee Brew Works with a good friend. We enjoyed a number of their beers and some appetizers, but because they had a private party we had to leave early.

They had a great band playing some music that night too. Very casual and relaxing place to hang out and just chill. The Patio was also a nice since it wasn't too hot

I will definitely be back and try more of their offerings very soon

Whiskey Jam is fun and the crowd can be cool, but drinks are way overpriced for what you get. My 7&7 cost almost $8, came in a tiny plastic cup and tasted disgusting. I couldn't tell if it was diet 7UP or a dirty dispenser. The bartender never asked if I wanted to keep my tab open, she just closed it, then acted annoyed when I came back for another drink later on. She didn't ask me that time, either! I'd give this place one star, except I brushed against a supposedly famous country singer who performed that night. His personality was as stiff as the bus stop benches his face is on, though.

Great bar, and a really fun environment in a great town!  Food is decent, get a burger... did I mention the music and atmosphere....?  Anyway, about average food for a chain type restaurant, nachos are pretty good too, would love to give this four stars if for no other reason it is a fun bar that has live music and is pretty good for families.... not a dive, not as hard core as some other Broadway nightlife spots so I will call it 3.5 stars... swing in have a beer, get some nachos and sing along and see how it goes.
Our server Whitney was awesome.  Very attentive and friendly even though it was very busy.

Fun atmosphere, but does not provide the typical "broadway in Nashville" experience. Food was cold when it reached our table, drinks were not mixed well. Overall not worth a stop unless you need a last resort.

Good location for people on vacation looking for entertainment with a meal.  Non-stop live music.  I only had a burger that was just ok so I can't speak for the rest of the food on the menu.  Not a  good place for conversation as the music was constant and very loud.  The service was very good.

I came here from Los Angeles to visit my son. The service was good but the good was awful, first I was told they had no wine glasses so I was served a wine in a plastic cup. Maybe 2 oz of wine. I looked at another table  and the lady did have a wine glass appropriate filled, at $7.50 s glass I was upset to not be served a full potion. I asked the waitress asked the waiter and I was given a proper glass. I ordered a New York steak that was covered in season salt. It was unalterable. They recooked the steak only to find it is an awful quality if neat. I couldn't eat it.
I would NOT come here. Bad bad bad

We had a great dinner at Ole Red.  Our server, Corrine, was attentive and friendly.  We had the Champagne of Chicken bucket.  We had the hot chicken option, and it was delicious-- and not too hot, but with a little kick.  It's a gorgeous place, and we enjoyed listening to the band while eating.
The place is nice, food is good. But I'd rather put my nuts in a rat trap than go back and deal with security and how it was ran through out the night.

Had dinner at JWB Grill on Friday night and thoroughly enjoyed the food, ambiance and service. Our server, Jessy, was wonderful, and went out of her way to make it an elevated dining experience. Highly recommend checking this place out.

I suppose the food options are more varied than the bars on the strip but only if you arrive early enough to try them.  We arrived late so the only things available were burgers.  We arrived minutes after the time and they would not budge.  In fact, we watched as they served other customers their full meals and we were only offered burgers.  We would have stuck around, but the drinks we ordered took forever and were very weak.  Not impressed.
I would probably go back again if the skinny male bartender covered in tats wasn't such a dick to my friend and I.
Fun vibe, good food and excellent music. The half champagne chicken was a meal for four. Come hungry.
Great food, large stage with excellent music. Wait staff very fast and attentive. A must stop when in town.

For the Broadway scene...this place is wayyy above and beyond expected --Happened to walk in, sat at the bar and had a really great Nashville experience--Erica was the bomb! Food was great --especially the tots:) and awesome music without the extra craziness -highly recommend!!!

This place is awesome! I have been to many arenas and we went to go see the Predators play while we were in town. While huge, it is organized and there is always someone there to ask if you need help. It is clean and bright which I really liked. Inside the arena, seats are comfortable, while still you can tell they pack in as many people as you can. Sounds was great! We only got sodas and some fries but lines moved quickly and not over priced for "over priced" event food. After the game getting out was a breeze!

My wife and I visited with our son and it was great. The staff helped us have a great experience. The beer was great and the food was on point. we are definitely going back and would recommend this to anyone who wants good beer and food and good service

To be fair I'm  not generally a chain restaurant guy. They usually are what you expect and consistent. The reason we chose Margaritaville was the variety of the menu, our 2 daughters could not decide what they wanted. Additionally, we had eaten there during CMA a few years ago because my wife wanted island style drink. Our meal consisted of spinach dip, seafood mac and cheese, a side salad, fries, 2 bourbons and a  chicken quesadilla. The total for this $70+ not including tip. Service was fine. Based on the fact seating was less than 70% full the food took way to long to get out. Our server kind of acknowledged it by the fact she said I'll go check to see where your food is coming. When it did arrive the mac and cheese was barely warm and the chicken quesadilla was burnt, to the point not only was it not edible and it smelled burnt. Not sure how you even send this to a table. In a city built on service and entertainment you would think a manager would swing by once a customer asks for an item to be removed from the table and bill. The night before we had been at restaurant across the street on the corner (place with a great bar and counter service)  that manager came by greeted us then again to check to see how our meal was. Margaritaville will continue  to survive because of its cute theme.

After I posted my review I was interested in seeing what others had to say. It seems our experience is similar to others. Whomever is responding to these reviews continues to say the issues will be addressed however it seems like similar issues again and again.

When my friend and I decided to drive down to Nashville for a long weekend away from Chicago, we decide to do an afternoon of brewery tours. 

I've been to almost a dozen throughout Chicago and Milwaukee so I know how beer is made. I usually go to brewery tours so you can learn about the beers that each brewery makes and you can try a few of their favorites. So when I say I hated this tour I really mean it. 

First of all, this brewery is hard to get to if you're walking and don't know the area. Google Maps tried to make us cross train tracks that had no crossing twice. When we finally found our way around the train tracks, it was down a bunch of dimly streets. Not a fan. I did not feel safe. 

We arrived and they didn't even check to see if we had actually booked a tour and just sent us to the back where the tour was starting. The tour ended up being a quick 20 minute tour of their machines and the process of making beer. It was supposed to be 45 minutes but apparently there was nothing to say. Nothing was said about the beers they make and a little history of this brewery was given, but not much. It was boring.

Once the tour was finished, we were given a token for a free beer. Yay. So I ordered a beer - the IPA - and it was as boring as the tour.

I would've appreciated the opportunity to try more beers on the tour but I guess they don't that. I would've also appreciate learning more about how they make their different beers. 

Overall, this was the most boring brewery tour I've ever gone on. In fact, it was the most boring alcohol tour I've ever been on. It was more boring than the winery tour I went on with my parents when I was 7 - I couldn't touch anything and I couldn't drink anything and I didn't understand anything. 

If you're visiting Nashville from Chicago or Milwaukee and have been on a few brewery tours before, I wouldn't stop here. It will just disappoint you.

I've loved the Bridgestone Arena since I was a child, when it was called the Municipal Auditorium and my first concert was the Osmond's in 1973.  Yeah, so what...I'm 137 years old.  I look really good for my age.

I recently went to see the farewell tour of Elton John.  Now I'm just gonna remind you again, I am 137 years old.
Elton John was playing as long as I can remember and he's only 49.99999 years old now.  If you've never experienced him in concert, sorry 'bout yer luck. 

The Bridgestone has the most spectacular sound system.  It is extremely loud, but it was also extremely clear.  The instruments as well as the lyrics were crisp and clear, as was Elton's voice when he spoke.  His concert being his farewell tour also tells of his journey, and it was very inspiring.  I really can't express how much I enjoyed this particular concert , or how much I have enjoyed every experience I've ever had at the Bridgestone Arena.

Was excited to go to Ole Red cause I am a Blake Shelton fan. When we got there my boyfriend tried to order an Ole Red beer and they were out. How can you be out of your own beer. The service took a long time at one point we waited for our bill for 20 minutes. Food was good. The tater tots were the best ever.

I was there with my husband and son for dinner and the food was very good...all but the crab dip. I would pass on that one. My husband had the jambalaya and loved it. My son had the shrimp and crab mac and cheese and really liked that too. I had the chicken sandwich and it was very good.
Service was a little slow but your on vacation right?!
Very commercial with a full stage, video and light show. Not the Nashville I was looking for. But Ole Red's saving grace was the roof top patio bar. Love it!

I researched this venue prior to the 311 show this past weekend, and, as I had not been there before, was pleased to see it was indoor. I falsely associated this with climate control. 
It was HOTTER THAN THE THIRD CIRCLE OF HELL; I saw people ill from over heating, myself so hot, I downed 3 bottled waters, too scared to drink alcohol. 
We sadly left the venue before 311 even finished because we felt too miserable. I was only wearing a short dress, and sweat was literally dripping down the back of my legs.; nude would have been too many clothes. 
The only source of circulation in a sea of sweaty bodies were a few massive fans about 20 feet up that only could be felt right underneath once the venue got crowded. 
I am not sure how this has not been cited as a health hazard, to close in so many patrons in the south, during the summer, with no friggin' air conditioning, but this was my first and last trip there. 
One star, because the layout of bars and bathrooms accommodated the crowd nicely. 
It was also nice to see a big band like 311 in a more intimate setting.
However, a venue so little invested in the comfort of their patrons, that they couldn't somewhat maintain even a healthy temperature, left me wasting money on tickets for a show I couldn't enjoy and a 3 hr. drive to do so.

You might have heard of Music Row when thinking about Nashville, but while that neighborhood was fairly peaceful when I visited, the bars and restaurants in Downtown on Broadway are literally bursting at the seams with music. Taking a stroll down the sidewalk, you'll find one narrow venue blasting the tunes of a country crooner, and then a few steps later the song will fade into the next bar's band as seamlessly as if you're sampling tracks at a record store. One of the tiniest taverns on this side of Ryman Alley is Layla's Honky-Tonk. You'll know you've found the right place by the pink and blue marquee and the interior Christmas lights all over the stage.

Layla's welcomes music-lovers of all ages until 6pm, and then the tiny bandstand becomes exclusively 21+. There is the smallest of dance floors in front of the stage, but the whole building is built to funnel the live music (and diners) past the stage and back towards the bar, or up to the private second floor that you could rent out for events. If you get too caught up in conversation with the bartender, worry not, for there's a live monitor showcasing whichever local band is strumming right behind the counter! You'll want to check the live music calendar if you're planning to visit, because you never know when someone like Garth Brooks will drop in for a surprise cover-free concert. I was lucky to sit down and bask in the honkiest-tonkiest tunes of Ted Buller and Just Plain Trouble. Also, Layla's staff has a knack for license plates, so if you want to donate yours to the hundreds scattered around the walls and ceiling, you'll be rewarded with a free drink!

But none of that matters. Let's get to the fries!

The food options at Layla's Honky-Tonk are simple, just like the layout of the bar itself. The drinks range from exotic to extremely domestic (shoutout to local Yazoo Brewery and Tennessee Brew Works), but nothing about the food shouts Nashville. Egg rolls, celery sticks, and pickle chips seem like a weird mix you'd find at any county fair, but Layla's has them too. Of course, we're here for fries, and they've got them for $3.

The first thing The Frequent Fryer noticed was the portion, of course: the typical paper basket was filled up but not packed and without any fancy furnishings. The second thing I noticed was how warmly they were served and how that heat lasted for the whole meal. That's good news: the fries are "freshly" prepped to order and quickly served. 

How "fresh" these frozen fries can ever be is a different matter. These spuds have no skins, no salt, no sturdiness, and no soul. They're cut longer than average, but without any taste, you'll feel like you're just munching on an extruded plain potato. There's no bite when you bite in: absolutely no crunch, and past the skin the flesh is just a few molecular bonds away from collapsing into a mushy meal. If you try to eat the basket by the handful, a handful of mush is exactly what you'll get. To top it all off, while the lame potato flavor isn't exactly off-putting, you'll find all of the cooking oil from the fries ends up on your lips.   

Layla's Honky-Tonk can be a very fun stop along the bustling streets of Broadway, and already has so much to offer: great live music, free entry, friendly staff, and a jolly all-year-long décor. Just take it from me: don't let anyone you care about eat these fries, and use those $3 to tip the band instead.

Final rating for fries: 1.5/5 Spuds.

I stopped by here earlier today with my wife for some afternoon drinks.  We had decided to come to Tennessee Brew Works because we are getting a pint glass from every state (and most major cities) and thought that their logo was perfect for Nashville.  Upon arriving to the Brewery we noticed what a nice outdoor space they had.  However the below freezing temperatures precluded any chance of us utilizing this space and so we went inside.  This brewery has two floors although we mostly stayed on the first floor.  It was simple with a stage in the front, a bar in the back and then some tables made out of barrels and high top stools around them.  You could also see into their brewing facility from here and if you want to go to the bathroom you have to head through the door towards it and get a good view of it.  Even if you don't have to go, it's worth walking in there to get a good view.

As I often do whenever I visit a new brewery, I ordered a flight here.  At Tennessee Brew Works you get to choose 5 pours for $11.  I ended up choosing the Basil Ryeman (saison), Pie Town Session Porter, Extra Easy (English Pub Ale), 1927 (IPA) and finally the Cut Throat Rye IPA.  The first one that I tried was the saison which had that funk that most saison have and it tasted pretty good.  Up second was the Session Porter which I actually thought tasted a little watery.  My wife contested that but to each their own I guess. For my third beer I tried the Extra Easy which was great.  It was a good representation of its style and was smooth and went down quite easily.  Fourth was the IPA which was bright and flavorful with a slight touch of hops at the finish.  Last but certainly not least was the Cutaway Rye IPA which was extremely hop forward leaving quite a bitterness on the finish.  If you asked me there may actually be too much hops in it.  Out of the bunch I would have to say that the IPA was my favorite with the Extra Easy being my second favorite.

The bottom line for me is that I would head back here again in the future.  Tennessee Brew Works occupies a cool space and I thought that their beers were good too.

Great atmosphere but food and drinks left us disappointed. It drives me crazy when bars can't keep their seltzer carbonated. My second drink was improved slightly after I mentioned it, from complete flat to mostly flat - my goodness !
My daughter's  burger was too greasy for her - and she loves greasy burgers
My sons pulled pork was excellent 
My salad was soggy and you could tell us was pre- chopped  hours prior , my salmon came out rare 
Such a shame 
Our last meal in Nashville - a low note . Bummer

The thing I love about Layla's is, you're not going to here fake twangy Florida Georgia Line music. You hear real honky tonk country. We come to Layla's a lot! Layla's also gets a lot of famous singers who secretly attend. I missed Garth Brooks by one night a year or so ago. I've seen Leann Womack there once. You never know who will show up. If you're in town when the Eskimo Brothers are playing, we highly recommend them. They're a blast to watch and play really good traditional music.
Our experience was great and Kayla, the waitress was FANTASTIC!!!!  I would tell Blake Shelton personally how good she is.  Very friendly, attentive, and a hard worker

5 STARS! We really enjoyed this little bar. We walked in after hearing the music from the sidewalk at around 1 PM. The band that was playing was a great honky-tonk three-piece band. The vibe in here is definitely a hole in the wall honky-tonk feel that you need to experience and hopefully you'll get to hear some great music like we did.

Cool interior and exterior. But beer is fair (coming from Chicago's 90+ breweries)
Tried a couple beers and going to another brewery since menu was also just ok

Delicious brunch on the rooftop lounge!
We read mixed reviews for Ole Red and The Lookout, but decided to make reservations for the brunch on a Sunday. Everything was great! Walking out of the elevator and getting the first glimpse of the rooftop bar/lounge/deck area started our visit off on a positive note. The décor and arrangement are inviting and balances casual with classy, unlike many of the other establishments on Broadway. We were promptly seat on the outdoor deck and presented with the brunch menus, which are in old vinyl record album covers...cool!

They have a nice variety of "brunch" drinks including my new favorite, The bandit-(Bourbon and coffee liqueur cocktail). The others in our group enjoyed the various mimosas. The one misstep in our entire visit, which would normally have me drop a place a couple stars was the quality of their regular black coffee. It was awful, weak, and definitely cheap!  The food was delicious! While you're waiting for your entrees you can help yourself to a display of fresh warm biscuits, muffins, parfaits, and yogurt.  The entrees we tried were: The Hot Spiced Nashville Omelet-filled with pimento cheese, smoked pork, and caramelized onions (delicious), French Toast Casserole-very good & very sweet, and the biscuits & gravy, which were enjoyed. The parmesan ranch breakfast potatoes which are served with most entrees were cooked and seasoned perfectly!

Overall The Lookout Brunch was a great way to start the day! Good food, drinks, service, and view! Even if you're not having brunch, check out The Lookout for drinks when you need a reprieve from the craziness of the street level of Broadway.

Great atmosphere , several great bands. Nice atmosphere. So much food it was difficult to eat. Only negative while all four of us enjoyed everything about the Resturant. There was no place to park and the cost of 25.00 for parking  was steep, for no longer than we were there.

My first predators game since moving here!!! 

Much smaller arena than the Excel back in mn. I loved it. Easier to see well even higher up.

The sound system was great sounding, loud clear but didn't hurt your ears! Definite plus for me!! 

Seats were pretty cozy and it was warm enough:) which I greatly appreciate!

We lucked out and were able to be seated in a hr. It was fun to hang out here. The drinks were good and the atmosphere was fun. The wait staff was friendly. When we received our food we were pleased. The pulled pork had a strong smoke to it and was very lean. The burgers were done correctly and the homemade tater tots were crispy and not greasy. Would we stop here again, wait a long time for dinner??? Yes, we'd all do it again.

Visited this place for lunch and I heard the food was good.  I ordered fried pickles, sangria and cheeseburger.   I left so full because everything was delicious.   I almost ate the entire basket of pickles.  Bring your appetite when you come to this spot! Also the entertainment was great too! This spot is a must if you are in a the area.

Go for the atmosphere (and the gravy).

I had an absolutely wonderful experience at Ole Red entertainment-wise. Recently-formed duo Southerland was performing and did an excellent job. It also felt surreal to be in Blake Shelton's place, such a cool vibe.

Separating the experience of being in Music City from the restaurant experience, I had the half "champagne of chicken," a big bucket of fried chicken and biscuits, with gravy. The chicken is good but nothing to write home about, more breading than meat to be honest. The biscuits were kinda dry and just not the best. But the gravy that comes with it was sooooooo good. Mouthwatering. I would have rather just eaten an entire vat of that.

Good place to come hang out, kind of expensive to actually eat lunch/dinner, but so is everywhere in downtown Nashville.

3.5

Out of Winners and Losers, Winners definitely got the name right. I've always enjoyed my time at Winners more than Losers. They both are kind of the same with outdoor covered patios, live music, and patrons. However, there are some differences.

I have only been to Winners on the weekend when they have karaoke. This usually means the bar isn't too busy which is nice for getting quick service and an empty high top. Sometimes karaoke can be painful to watch but here in Nashville, it brings out some pretty great talent. I will never sing karaoke but it's entertaining to watch. I believe during the week they have live bands and different event nights. The crowd is usually younger and might be more of a college bar than Losers. But unless it's packed, you can converse nicely with your own group or mingle with others if you're on the prowl. 

I've only ever had a drink or two here but they do serve food. Probably just your typical bar food so don't expect too much. The last time I went there I was looking for something different than a beer so I ordered a cranberry vodka. $8! Which isn't bad in Nashville but it was in a small plastic cup and rail vodka. I thought the going rate was $6 for drinks like this. This is why I stick to beer because the upcharge on liquor is getting a little crazy. 

If you're going down the midtown strip, I would suggest stopping into Winners. It has a fun vibe but is definitely nothing fancy. It's what I would expect from a touristy Nashville bar. Sometimes they will have fun drinks like a spiked Capri Sun. You never know who will be performing on stage!

What??? Plastic cup margarita? Jimmy does sell margarita Glasses in the gift shop. Was told it was Sunday and they don't wash the dishes. Only drank the one because well was vacation.

Hope the resort your building actually has what is pictured in the menu. 

What the fuck Jimmy? Not like Vegas at all.

So now for the food- volcano nachos great! Quesadilla was cold and the fried pickles were burnt. The waitress said "they told me to ask if that was ok first" they removed the pickles from the menu.

What the fuck Jimmy?
Great bands and atmosphere.  I had the triple decker ham and abs Swiss and it was huge

The music and our first Bloody Mary were perhaps the best things about this place. We opted to do shared seating which I did not mind at all. There were 3 of us and we ordered the bbq nachos and double decker ham and cheese. If you like large servings this is the place for you. The nachos were a pile of potato chips with toppings and the sandwich was huge but tasteless. I would have been better off with a burger but was encouraged to get the sandwich instead. I should have stuck with my original plan. 
We took a few bites of both dishes, ordered another Bloody Mary which was not as good as the first one and we were finished. 
I might go back for the music and but I'd skip the food.

This place is the best - food review first, drink second. 

As a local, I've been working my way through the Nashville hot chicken scene over the years. Recently I ordered the hot chicken sandwich here - the chef personally came out to ask just how hot I wanted it. I wanted hotttt. And. He. Delivered. I LOVE the beer at this place, but y'all, the food is out of this world. I've also never had a bartender pair a beer with my food (wine pairings, yes. Beer pairings? Never). She hooked me UP! Best meal I have had in Nashville in a long while.

But the reason everyone comes here (and it's in the name) - the brew. These guys are doing it right. As an outdoor enthusiast, I love that they have a beer that supports the state parks in TN. As a native, I believe in supporting local businesses - and I love supporting one that actively and intentionally supports others.

Well, and, duh. The beer is phenomenal. Highly recommend.
Paid for a double of watered down liquor. Bartender denied having served me until I showed her the receipt.  Rip off central.. I will not be back

We stopped last night, Saturday, at 7:30. The bouncer greeted us and was joking with us. Douglas Riley was playing mix of AC/DC, Tom Petty, Neil Diamond, Garth Brooks, etc. The band was really good and interacted with the crowd all night. We got a seat up front near the band which made the night. We had a good group of people sitting near us.

The drinks and shots were $9 and they offer several Rumchata shots.

I don't have much of a "review". I've only been to one show here. We attended the Death Grips show on 10/2.
This was by far the worst live show I've ever been to. The sound was garbage. We couldn't understand anything Mc ride was saying. I've seen them live in Atlanta and I could understand every lyric sang. We drove three hours to see this show. Thanks for wasting my valuable time. For this, I will never return. Very disappointed.

Had a ton of fun both nights here. We wanted to try other bars, but they just didn't stack up to this one. Great drinks and great music. Only place we could find that the bands didn't ask for $20 song requests in between every single song. Just great bands having a great time doing what they love.

I absolutely love this brewery. It's a bit rustic with a touch of class. A flight only cost $10, and I was able to sample all drafts available. My favorite was the basil beer which had such a unique taste to it I was really blown away. I also like that this brewery has board games upstairs and darts, so if you're in a playful mood you can have your beer and play the games. There is outdoor seating as well, but it was so hot and humid we opted to remain inside.

Overall, a winner in my books!

Very cool place away from the touristy bustle of Broadway.  Quality bar food, very attentive service and a very good live band.  The band covered everything from Willie Nelson to Radiohead.  Our party of 4 had a great time and plan to head back for their Whiskey Jam session on a Thursday night.  Very good spot and more authentic musically than the Broadway scene.

Waited 1 1/2 hrs. Got the call our table was ready . Then we walk up and they made a mistake. 45 min later they say it's ready again.  We go to the 2nd floor and the girl up there tells us they were wrong. Again. Very disappointed. Plus we drove out here all the way from south texas, to be disappointed!

I loved this place! Wasn't very crowded when I went, so we were seated right away. The beer I had was very good. My boyfriend got a flight that he also enjoyed. We ordered a cheese board as a snack. It probably isn't the best thing on their menu, but it was definitely filling. 

I was so happy there was live music the day I went! It can be hard to find a chill place to hang out with live music in Nashville. You could even sit outside and have it come through the speakers. Football was going on on the TVs for extra entertainment. I would definitely revisit if I ever find myself in Nashville again!

This all-purpose venue is a hot spot for Nashville. It is a favorite of big name musical acts (especially those that fall into the country music genre) as well as being the home of the NHL team, the Predators. There always seems to be all sorts of sporting and special events scheduled for this space. 

Truth be told, I have only visited Bridgestone Arena to attend music concerts. It is a GIGANTIC arena which translates to there not really being a bad seat in the house. This allows for a bathroom around every turn and a concession stand/bar just around the corner from whichever section one may found themselves assigned. 

What I really appreciate about Bridgestone is the location. It stands right on Broadway Street. For those unfamiliar with the area, this is a strip of restaurants, honky tonks, small stage venues, and karaoke bars that appeal to those looking to keep the party going into the wee hours of the morning. If catching an Uber home to hop straight into bed sounds more appealing to you, the mass exodus of those attending an event at the arena can quickly turn into a traffic nightmare. 

I have always had luck walking a few blocks away from the hustle and bustle to make a quick getaway.

Just stopped in for some drinks. Our bartender RICHARD was so nice and told us a lot of history for the downtown bars. Enjoyed talking with him! Music was good also. It was a kid that had been on the Voice.

I read all the up and down reviews online, but I wanted to give this place an honest chance. The server was very friendly! The decorations and theme was a bit weird for me.. I ordered the quesadilla and the crab dip from their menu, and both were underwhelming.  This place is located directly on broadway so I'm sure they get a decent amount of business, but unfortunately they won't be getting mine any time soon.

One of the more disappointing venues I've experienced.

Parking -  parking downtown is pretty poor in general so not necessarily this facility's issues but it doesn't help that they do not offer dedicated on site parking.

Amenities - the suites are pretty average and show their age.  The concourse areas are ok. The offerings are standard fare and there's no real rhyme or rhythm to how they're grouped together.

Sound -  I've only attended concerts here and the sound is mediocre at best.
Stopped by for lunch, our server, Jolyn was fabulous!! The fish and chips were great with the margaritas! Always love the music

Best fish tacos I've ever had, and I was born and raised in Southern Calfornia - where fish tacos are abundant in authentic and fast food form, from very fresh to food-poisoning-in-waiting.  

You get two good-sized tacos of Mahi Mahi (or tilapia) seasoned in a cajun influenced way, in a corn tortilla ... with large chunks of grilled fish inside, cabbage, and a white sauce drizzled over it all.  In-freaking-credible!  It comes with a side of black beans and an almost milky tasting rice.  Amazing.  Out of all the fantastic foods I tried and loved, these fish tacos are something I'd come back for and try to recreate at home.  

We also ordered the fried pickles.  Just do it!  

Skipped the drinks because I was driving, but there's live music up front by the bar...open air windows to the outside - we were lucky to get to listen to Eric Von.  He's awesome!  He'll play almost anything you request (someone requested Lady Ga Ga's Pokerface as a joke... and he made a country version of it that blew her lame song out of the water and back again!)  

Prices are a bit on the high side, but it's Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville.  I wasn't expecting $4 tacos.  But for the quality and portion, the pricing makes it worth it.  The fish tacos were I think $16.99, but they don't skimp on the fish.  They take care of you and your belly in Nashville!

Only giving this place two stars because the servers are nice .the food is inconsistent, one day it's good and one day really bad . First day food was good , second time it was terrible! The atmosphere is fun but it's the same u can find anyplace. Just don't bother . You'll be disappointed. If you do go , stick with apps. only .
The food was solid but a bit overpriced. Didn't care for any of the beer, but they do allow dogs outside which is nice.

We stopped by on Friday for lunch. There was no wait and we were seated immediately. The Bulleit sours were very good and strong.

We had the Nashville burgers with the pimento cheese. The rolls are thick, the burgers cooked perfectly, with thick slices of tomato, onion, and pickles. The steak fries were very thick and the tator tots were crunchy with a smashed hash brown-type of filling.

The service was very good, the food was hot, seasoned and cooked well. There was a female singer who auditioned for the voice, she was performing her new original songs. My only downside is that we had a wobbly table and chairs and no signage or tee shirts of Blake that i saw.

I was going  to give a 3 but remembered how fun the audience was and all there chants at the hockey games. The arena itself is beautiful!  The seats are AWFULLY small. Like I had bruises getting up and down in my seat. I'm not the smallest of butts but let's be real everyone said how small it was. Crazy small. Predators were so fun to watch here.
I came here for a tour on a Sunday night and the place was really busy. We came in from the alley and got a seat upstairs. The drinks were good and the music was better.

Fiends that live/have visited Nashville suggested this place and I honestly don't know why. Wanted a change of scenery from the honky tonks on Broadway...big mistake. Simply a college dive-bar with karaoke....pass #mediocre

Bridgestone Arena is the best arena we've been in. It has a escalator going up to the second floor.
We had a very good view from our seats. I don't think there's a bad seat in the house.
Getting into the arena went fairly smooth and the employees were courteous and helpful.
A can of Coors beer cost me $13. 
The cost of the food and beverages are ridiculous.
We are hoping to go to the CMA next year.

Stopped here on a Wednesday night when they have a 2-for-1 draft beer deal. Every beer I tried was excellent but the Basil Ryeman was my favorite and one of the best beers I've had. My boyfriend really liked the Tennessee No. 12 Quad. Both were so good that we came back the next day to get some to take home.

All of the staff here was also wonderful. They are so knowledgeable about the beer and made great recommendations. They offered samples of beer they thought we would like.

I would come back here if we're in Nashville again, even without the 2-for-1 deal.

So many better places to go downtown. Paid $10 for the worlds smallest margarita and $20 for three grilled fish tacos that tasted like spicy lettuce and tortilla. Our waiter was nice but we won't be back. One fork.

The black keys show was an absolutely miserable experience! It was freezing cold! So cold that I saw a group of four huddled together for warmth. The poor guy sitting next to me spent the whole show curled up in his seat. I understand it's a hockey venue  but it was just too much. I have never had such a horrible time at a concert in my life. It was such a shame too because the music was amazing but I just couldn't enjoy with it being so cold.

Amazingly decadent food. I know this sounds crazy but the bologna sandwich is to die for. The chef has it custom made from his own recipe and has nothing to do with Oscar Meyer. The tater tots are crazy good. And anything with the smoked chicken is super good. And the love music is phenomenal. My biggest criticism is that there is no NY location.

I recently visited from Michigan to see Clutch in concert at this venue. I found this to be a pretty good venue to see a concert. It's basically a converted warehouse in an old industrial district. There is ample street parking near the venue and we had no trouble finding a spot. 

Security was fairly thorough, but also reasonably chill. We did get to the venue on the early side (the doors typically open about an hour before the concert starts.)  They do have a coat-check, but I left mine in the car so I wouldn't have to bother with it. There is a fairly large bar in the entrance area so you have have a drink while you wait for the main area to open. You can either get a general admission ticket or you can pay a bit more to get a seat in the "Lux Loft", which is a raised area on the side of the stage.
