It has a good view as well as a separate, private bar and bathroom area. On the main floor, there are two general bar areas and the public restrooms (which have bathroom attendants...) There is also a taco stand that basically sells tacos or nachos (chicken or veggie.) The tacos were not too bad, although one of the taco stand employees was pretty rude (she seemed irritated to be working that night.)

The concert experience was not bad, but I felt they were a little heavy-handed with the smoke machine. Also, the acoustics were not the best despite them turning the volume up to 11 -  and you know there's an issue when you can barely hear Neil Fallon's vocals, since that guy's a vocal powerhouse. The security had to break up one little scuffle on the main floor, but it was resolved efficiently. All in all, it was a really enjoyable night and I would definitely see another concert here.
Good place. Food is good, drinks are real good. Entertainment is great. Huge place gets very crowded sometimes but lots of fun.

Love Blake Shelton and Nashville but this stop was a disappointment.  Started on the roof and had some ok service and an appetizer.  Then moved to main dining room. Food was sub-par, stick with beer as mixed drinks were very weak. The service not even close to the Nashville standard.

Love this brewery! A little off the Broadway beaten path. Good food, creative brews, and cool space. 

This is my go-to spot when I want some patio day drinking because it's got two levels of outdoor seating with sweet string lights for when the sun sets. Parking is street availability only, but you can park anywhere in the deadend for free, with no time limit.  

They can host group/company events here, and even host a yoga class in the brewing room. They have live music too, and the most amazing cheese board. Five stars! 

Pro-tip: As a bonus, brew works is also walking distance to Jackalope and Yazoo breweries, if you want to make a day of it.
I loved the concert and the arena but won't recommend the Lexus lounge.  It was crap.
Awesome place! Very clean. Beer is very good and the food is delicious too!! Highly recommend. Nice band playing. Not too loud so you can still have a conversation without yelling.

Layla was the bartender upstairs and I cannot rave about her enough!!! She was fabulous! My mother and two aunts were with her having a "great time" enjoying themselves at the bar and she did such an excellent job taking care of them, making sure to give them water in between in order for them to pace themselves.  One of my aunts is blind and she watched out for her even making sure to lead them through the restaurant when it was time to leave!  I was so impressed by her patience and caring for them.  Thank you so much!!!!

We had a GREAT time here at this Margaritaville. We heard great music there and the food and drinks were great too. We went all over Broadway and to our surprise one of the best bands we saw was here at Margaritaville. Even though the place was really crowded the bartenders were very helpful when we went up to get our drinks before we were seated.

Fun and Classy!  Food, music and service were excellent.   I love that reservations are available. This is definetly a great addition to Broadway, not your typical Honky Tonk and I appreciate that very much! I am a local and I will definetly be bringing all of our out of town guests to Ole Red, this will be my go to place on Broadway!

A great place to visit when your in nashville. Great live music with excellent servers and bartenders. The roof top has a great scenic view of downtown Nashville. We had tacos with chips and salsa. All of the food was awesome with really good sizeable portions. A really great place to go if you love country music.

WE want to like this place.  We really do because we like Blake and his music but... sterile, slick, unimaginative.  These are the words we used. I think this was my biggest disappointing place we went this weekend. We wanted an Oklahoma honkytonk not what this is. It might make money but we will go elsewhere to have fun. Please if anyone in charge reads this ... go to your roots not what this is now.  We did not eat here so we can't review that. We came 3 times in a 5 day weekend and felt the same way Thursday through Sunday.

First time in Nashville, was so disappointed at Ole Reds, I'm a Blake Shelton fan but his bar was a horrible experience. Drinks were more expensive, restaurant and bar smelled really bad. Tables were a mess.
Terrible, tiny plate for $17. Not to mention the chicken tenders were so oily I felt sick after . Not coming back.

The atmosphere is great but we were there when the band was not great! The pickles were awesome but rest of food just average or below average. Of high importance..... only one women's bathroom stall had toilet paper! Good luck to you all!

Good drinks and music but please please please clean the bathrooms!! Pee city!! :( Didn't try the food, but it's a chain and has all the typical apps and sandwiches. Many other stops on Broadway to top this place.
Margaritaville is nice, but homeless people walk in there. One came right up to my table and accosted me. I got out of there so fast. I wanted to buy a Margaritaville blender, but not any more.

The atmosphere is great and the food was delicious. We had to wait 30 minutes on a Sunday to get a lunch seat. The only downside was the service. VERY friendly but after we got our food we never saw our waiter again. We had to flag someone down to get drink refills.

Great service!!  Our server was Nira and she is fantastic!!!  We had a party of 10 and she took care of us wonderfully, she was friendly, funny, and helpful.  The food is tasty, the tater tots are yum!!  My kids devoured their lunches as well as the rest of the table.  Live music and the overall ambience is really nice.  Highly recommend Blake Sheltons restaurant on Broadway!!

We love attending the Nashville Symphony. 

We have attended numerous events at the Nashville Symphony and will attend more in the future. Who is the we? My wife, teenage son and myself.  The musicians are on a level above many and the venue is absolutely beautiful.  It makes one feel as though you've stepped back in time to a much more elegant period. 

The pre-concert talks with the conductor is always a joy and makes the concert come together in a way you would not otherwise experience. Do not miss them.  

Another do not miss is the port-concert talk with conductor. It is intimate and a wonderful end to an always great time.

Although they have great drinks the food service is not worth it. Arrived early and was told Kitchen is open At 1:45.  When 1:45 came got told that the kitchen manager had decided to open at 2:15.  Not very good customer service.  When I tried to talk to them that a pretzel should not be a big item to provide people were rude and had no customer service in mind. The night before I ordered the lobster roll. It was dry and no seasoning or sauce. Sad experience to have Blake Sheltons name associated with.

The place is nice, the owner is famous and the long lines will make you wander what is going on and you'll NEED to check it out! Stayed in line outside for almost 2 hours, like everyone else who didn't give up. I figured we don't need a table, we'd be fine with seats at the bar or whaterver, so I went and asked at the door, and a security guy said No, this is the only way to get in. Well, almost 2 hours later we get in and the host said there are no more seats in the restaurant, unless we have your name down. What name, why did we stay 2 hours in line? They didn't know about the line outside, like we were in a different world. They almost kicked us out so we went up the stairs to find SOMETHING, and we ended up the Lookout rooftop, which was almost empty, and even had a guy with a guitar playing some nice songs. So we reluctantly asked if we an seat, and they were like Yes, everything is open! Holy crap, why did we wait almost 2 hrs in line when you have empty tables here? (the guys up here didn't know about the line outside either!) Great views from the top and the food was delicious! The funny name nachos made it to Instagram instantly and had everyone around come and take pictures too, they look amazing! Same for the Tiramisu dessert! Too bad that this place is so poorly organized and so unfriendly (told the same security guy on the way out that I came at the door and asked you of other options and no one mentioned the Skylounge, his answer was Go somewhere else if you don't like it). So go to the door and insist that you want to eat or go upstairs, the line is most likely for a Spotify event, don't fall for it. Or go somewhere else.

Went tonight. The music was great as was ambience. BUT... The food and drink were absolutely awful! We only ordered beer which was skunky ( waitress replaced) and worst nachos ever!! Kettle chips with god awful toppings! Makes we three who went there sick thinking about I! Had sickeningly  sweet bbq  sauce on it, slimy cheese sauce on the bottom that didnt  taste like cheese, some kind of COLD meat on it.. chicken? And guacamole which was ok. I have never had a bad nacho before today! Blake , please fix it!!!!  Dont put on bbq sauce ,make the meat on top hot, put real sharp cheese in it etc. Also we ordered the biscuits which were also awful! And where was the honey to put on them??? Terrible food. Next time we will eat first and order water or a coke . We love Blake Shelton but he needs to know those Two dishes are awful!

One of my favorite bars on broadway! Came here multiple times on my trip! The bar/restaurant is so spacious, it is 5 floors! The singer/band was always great! I love how everything is dog based obviously because it's called "ole red." The fried pickles were good and you get so many, a whole bucket! The burgers were also very very tasty and good! My boyfriend got a beer and I ended up with a "some beach" which I order two more of after my first! This drink was soo good!!! Definitely have to go here when on Broadway!

I absolutely love this restaurant. They have amazing food and live music. The music is fantastic as well was the service. Our waiter was checking on us making sure everything is good. Also the ice cream is the best and you cannot find it anywhere else.

This is a great spot on Broadway for both food and live music. The musicians are pretty talented and play a variety of music. Occasionally Blake Shelton sings on stage too. 

Service is decent for a busy place! And people watching is a blast.

I've been to a decent amount of Margaritaville and always love the atmosphere! We sat in the bar area and had drinks. The drinks were amazing as per usual, gotta love that 5 o'clock somewhere drink! I only had a salad which wasn't bad in price however, one of my friends who was with me paid an absurd amount for nachos in which she couldn't have meat on since she is a vegetarian. When I was looking at the menu I thought the options were great but the prices were quite high - I don't remember my past Margaritaville experiences being that expensive! I wouldn't really call it a complaint but a suggestion to maybe lower the prices a little!

Cudos to Blake!   Love Ole Red.  Salads, Hash Browns, quiche and one pound cinnamon bun for brunch were the best we ever had.  The jumbo pretzels!! Omg. Had three during a weekend stay. The drinks were the best on the strip.  The roof top bar was beautiful and as comfortable as your living room. Love love love ole red.

Okay so let's just throw all of my cards on the table here; I attended a Taylor Swift concert at Bridgestone Arena and I loved every minute of it.  Moving on, this is an excellent arena - my friend and I had floor seats (obviously in hopes of getting a lock of Tay's hair), but from walking around, it didn't seem like there was a bad seat in the house.  Why five stars you ask?  Simply enough the food, drink prices, and variety of both put other concert venues to shame.  They had plenty of beer options, wine, a variety of liquors ranging from top shelf to lower end, and all below $10 - that's even for a double of Dewer's (yes, Taylor Swift should always be enjoyed while drinking a fine scotch, there just is NO other way).  Anyways, despite this venue being packed, the staff were friendly, helpful, and good at keeping crowding to a minimum.  This is definitely worth a destination concert trip, so don't doubt it.  And last, only because I know you are dying to know, the average demographic at the concert was 8 year old female.  Goodnight.

This is a very beautiful music hall that you need to experience for once if you are ever in Nashville for a visit. I have been to the Nashville Symphony twice: one trip in 12/2017 and one trip in 11/2018. The hall is always decked out beautifully during the holiday season. The sounds are amazing, and the musicians are just amazing with their skills. 

You know you will always get great experience with Nashville because of the Music City's reputation. I have not been disappointed to both events that I attended: Dave Barnes's Very Merry Christmas in 2017 and Martina McBride's White Christmas Concert in 2018. Both performances were excellent and made me felt so excited each time I entered the Symphony Hall. 

Thank YOU, Nashville Symphony. You will be always on my list to attend musical events whenever I am in Nashville, TN!

First visit here. I was impressed with how clean it was! FYI- There's a mothers' lounge on the second level between sections 210-212. It was very clean with 3 gliders, a changing station, sink, etc. Great place to nurse my baby during a basketball game!

I wanted to like this place. I really did. It boasts its little reputation of being owned by a famous musician, being a hotspot for local artists, etc., which certainly makes it appealing. But, I will never eat here again. I ordered the buffalo chicken sandwich, which was possibly the saddest, puniest cut of chicken I've ever seen, complete with less-than-fresh greens on the bun. Also included LESS than a handful of kettle chips. For 11 bucks? Are you kidding me? Service was completely sub par. I somehow got roped into getting a bottle of water - I guess I misunderstood over the loud music. Where am I, a sporting event? NIX the stupid bottle, and give me a glass. Its a restaurant for crying out loud. But more importantly, I never once was asked a) how my food was or b) if I needed more water, or ANYthing else for that matter. And there were about 8 people in this entire joint (should have taken the hint). You can make up for crap food with good service, but unfortunately both were crap here.
            Now, maybe I made the mistake of ordering a chicken sandwich at a place known for their burgers (or so they say on their sign), but still, this was featured pretty high up on the menu, and that's what I wanted. So if that was terrible as it was, how good can the rest of the menu really be? Nashville is a haven for good food, with a multitude of options. So, go ahead and skip this joke of a restaurant if you find yourself downtown. 

Cheers! :)

The place is a joke. 6.50 for  Coors Light. 12.50 for a watered down lousy margarita. Don't forget the overpriced 15.50 no taste nachos. This place is strictly for tourist with no brain who will spend 30.00 on a t-shirt.

My office is downtown and I am lucky enough to only visit once a week. On that day as many of my team try to go out for lunch together as possible. So there are usually 3-6 people. This past week we decided to try this place out as many of us had not been there. 6 of us in this group and we went a tick early (11:30).

Service: Slow, I think the girl working was the only one working the front of the house.

The menu is only in chalk on the wall, great if you are facing the wall when you sit down. Seriously get more menus or make it easier to see. 

It is $2, that is right TWO DOLLARS for water. They won't bring you tap water you have to buy a bottle. Mixed drinks at lunch are $8, EIGHT FREAKING DOLLARS for a drink at lunch on a Tuesday. Tea, coke products and the like are $2 and you get refills. 

I ordered a cheese burger, medium rare no bun. I got a fairly decently cooked burger with what looked like an American cheese slice on it. I don't mind paying $11 for a burger but seriously this one wasn't worth it. ALL sandwiches come with a small handful of kettle chips (potato chips out of bag). There wasn't a cheese selection, or bread choice etc. There was a stack that contained lettuce, tomato slice, onion and 2 pickles. One person order a side of grilled potatoes and there were maybe 4 slices but she didn't receive her chips with the sandwich. The potatoes are signed as an appetizer so it wasn't fair to not deliver both. Others at the table felt the food was MEH. 

A lot of folks don't like to spend a bunch of money on lunch, which is why they don't like to eat on that block. But let's compare. National Underground burger $11 + water $2 = $13 plus tip. On the same block burger (bourbon glaze, onion straws and Gorgonzola with fries) $10.95 + water $0  = $10.95 plus tip. Hmm better values can be had elsewhere. 

I am sad that more places don't give a hoot about folks that are stuck downtown because they work there. This place is catering/charging for the tourist crowd because they can. But here is  the problem, I won't go back and I won't recommend it to anyone. When I schedule an event for Nashville my blog post will reflect my feelings of how places treat the weekday lunch crowd. Maybe they have a killer happy hour, guess I won't know.

We were here for the Predators playoff game against Dallas. Our seats were the second to last row up high and were still great seats. There are no bad seats in this arena. The live music between periods was awesome, and Smashville sure loves their team. It was so much fun!

We had the best time at Tennessee Brew Works yesterday!  We were visiting from Minnesota and greeted warmly by the staff and got some amazing beer right away.  We played a fun round of Taboo while surprisingly listening to some of our favorite tunes (Minnesota's Trampled by Turtles, coincidentally, and Devil Makes Three!). Mine and my other half's favorite selection was the King's Wit. So good. Was also happy to see that it was on tap at Peg Leg Porker down the street later on when we went to get BBQ for dinner!

P.S: The soap in the women's room smells so good. Please never change it.
Hayden London wow!!! I loved it very relaxed atmosphere, beautiful building. I enjoyed every minute of this symphony I will definitely go again! The pastries & coffee wasn't bad either

I absolutely loved this brewery. 

Traveling: 
It's in such a fun and cool location of Nashville that I hadn't been to before. I like that it's slightly off the grid, but it's also not hard to navigate to from the interstate. It's the perfect pit stop.

The BEER:
The beer is fabulous! Their IPA is my favorite. 
You can build your own six (or four) pack and take as much as you need to go! This was perfect for traveling back up north, because I have a lot of beer drinking friends that wanted to try from this specific brewery. I didn't take the tour, but I'm sure it would have been great, as the staff was so friendly and attentive. 

The FOOD: 
Ah-mazing. I haven't tried everything on their menu, but based on the 3 plates that I sampled, I would confidently say that no matter what you get, it's going to be great. 

Overall, the atmosphere is fun, the beer is top notch, the food is great, the staff is friendly, the bathrooms are CLEAN...

the only thing that left me scratching my head walking out the door was.... why didn't they already have some sweet tea brewed? Ha! I expected to fill up on some good sweet tea in my last southern stop going back up north and was surprised when they pulled out the simple syrup to pour in the unsweet tea. Is it just me? Either way. WORTH IT.

Definitely stop by. You'll LOVE this place.

One star for our gorgeous server at lunch and one for the fried pickles. 

Nothing but derision for the insufferably toxic "manager", whose function, it seemed, was little more than that of a particularly inept doorbitch, with an emphasis on the latter part of the job description. Nowhere in the universe, that's right, even in Nashville, is it acceptable to come stampeding onto a tour bus with manufactured anger over an issue, that if all my years around the music industry have taught me anything, was due to YOUR lack of attention to detail. 

Also, your venomous, unsolicited late night dining options tirade impressed no-one present.
Looks as though my card was ran twice for the privilege, on top of. 

Sorry about whatever the popular girls did in high school to turn you into such a bitter human being, but leave that sh*t at home, it's unprofessional and no-one cares to see it.

We went on a busy Saturday night and the waiter was so attentive and got the order down perfectly despite the music being so loud (music was great btw). We got appetizers and the portions were big and tasty. The band, Frank Ray, was awesome! They played music from all different genres that kept the crowd on their toes.
Great food. Great service from Josie. It's not cheap, but the quality and quantity make up for it.

Wifie did not want bbq so we landed at margaritaville. It was good but it really did not stand out and impress me. The seating process was really disorganized.  The music was really loud so you could not hear anything. The food was good - I had the seafood jumbeleia  - wifie had seafood mac and cheese  and baby girl had shrimp alfredo. The service was ok - we did not leave wanting to go back but it was not terrible just not memorable.

Blake, you missed the mark! If I'm out drinking and eating, I shouldn't be writing this review... 

A bit clinical, sterile and not what I expected after visiting all the other local bars. I appreciate a nice place, but, Ole Red is in between. Servers are too rushed, food and drinks are slow, lighting is too bright and I couldn't wait to leave. I'm sure the roof top is amazing, but I wouldn't know, DJ? Why a DJ?
Great arena for the game or concert. I have seen Beyoncé and Jack White with Loretta Lynn here. Great location on Broadway and plenty of parking garage around for major events.

Unimpressed - My friends and I wanted to visit Ole Red since they are obsessed with Blake Shelton. Here is our story....

We showed up at about 9:30PM hoping to be seated for dinner. We were told the first two floors were at capacity and we had to eat upstairs at "The Lookout". We went upstairs and then were told the kitchen closes at 10PM and we had to order immediately. Maybe it's because I'm from New York, but a kitchen closing at 10PM is absurd to me. The service was horrible, the table was dirty and the food was gross. The menu was limited to bar type food & snacks. We ordered a bunch to share; Here is our order:

1. Big Soft Pretzel: Only decent thing we ordered; probably was frozen though so that's hard to mess up. 
2. Nashville hot calamari: Repulsive. The calamari was shaped in long, thick sticks and was a bit undercooked and soggy. 
3. Trio Slider: One of the "sliders" is a bologna & cheese on white bread.... okay.......
4. Fried broccoli: Do not order; you will burp it up for the rest of the night. 
5. Burrata: The weirdest menu item ever. It was a sin what they did to the burrata. It was plasticy and filled with some orange/red filling.... appalling. 

Blake, stick to music buddy....
Came in on night with Jake Durkin playin and Ashley serving.  By far, the best night out in a long time because of the service and the song! Will be back!

My husband and I passed by Ole Red right before it opened at 11 and decided to wait with the handful of others at the door to get in for lunch. 

We decided to sit at the bar since it was only the 2 of us. The bartender was very nice and took her time to explain the menu offerings. We really liked that most of their food, sauces etc are made in house. 

We both started with a beer (love the local beer offerings!) The one thing I didn't quite get was that the beer was served in a plastic cup. I get why they'd do that after hours once a rowdier crowd comes in, but not in the early afternoon. 

We both split the nachos and they were SOOOO GOOD!! Like I'm not even kidding. From the chicken, to the BBQ sauce and everything in between, I highly recommend the nachos!! It was plenty for 2 people and honestly we couldn't even finish it between us. YUM!!!

The interior of Ole Red is definitely a step above the rest. The stage was awesome and they had a bluegrass band playing the whole time. There are multiple levels and a rooftop bar, but unfortunately the rooftop was closed when we were there so we didn't get to see it.

I have had a great time at TN Brew Works in the past and the beers on tap are usually awesome every time my girlfriend or myself go. Well, we decided to go out in the early afternoon on a Sunday (3/25) for the special of $12 pitchers that was on their website. So we go in, sit down on the second level inside, and we are greeted by a waitress immediately. My girlfriend and myself asked for water and a few minutes to look over the menu. After about ten minutes, the waitress returned with no water and asked us which beer we preferred. I questioned if they had the $12 pitcher special to which she said they did not. Although fairly new, the waitress agreed to ask her manager who also told her that there was no special on Sundays. This prompted me to pull the website page up to show them but they declined again and stated that Monday was the new day. In the end, we decided to visit another local establishment based on the fact of misleading information from the website. It pains me to say it but as a customer in this instance I was turned away for their error.
Tim on the rooftop bar is one amazing bartender! Drinks were fabulous, service was spot on and food was delicious!

One of the last few places that we ended up checking out since the roof top looked cool from across the street. 
we came in just as many of the bars this is multi level, live band downstairs DJ on the roof top which was a nice change from all the country music. be sure to take the elevator up them stairs are pretty long & half way you feel like your legs are going to fall off. 
Once upstairs we sat by the bar area & got some cold beers, hard to go wrong it was nice just to relax, drink & listen to something other than country music it was a good break, the DJ played a decent variety of music from hip hop to pop. 
Nice looking roof top, nice seating set up & seating inside as well as a small dance floor not too bad. 
This was a decent place we enjoyed the views, music & our drinks.

I've never been a fan of the atmosphere or patrons here.  As far as Nashville bars go, they should rename this place "Douche Central."  I went there last night against my will, and I'm not sure what I did to piss him off, but the bouncer cut me off after three beers.  He physically took my third beer from my hand.

The long and short of it is that if you want to see the worst Nashville has to offer, from the basic country music wannabe's to the douchebags trying to hook up with them, and get rude service at the same time, this is your place.  It's like a bad high school party, and the prude bouncer is your mom showing up.

Had to stop in to support our OK boy Blake Shelton.  Downstairs was pretty typical of most of the  places along the strip.. but we went to the rooftop (enclosed for the winter) and liked the whiter vibe.  Our burger was terrific and has good service.  Prob pretty great view in nice weather!

This venue is breathtaking. 

I love everything from the courtyard to the statues, to the unique light fixtures and marble covered interior. This is the perfect place to enjoy a night at the symphony or hear a concert. 

I've noticed that they are trying to incorporate more comedians, popular musicians and discounted tickets to get more people in the doors, and I'm glad that they are making strides to ensure this lovely gem downtown is a success. They have multiple bars in the lobby's so you can enjoy a cocktail for a reasonable price. Put it in a plastic cup and you can bring it inside the auditorium. I love that!

Some people don't dress up, but I would suggest you do. It's just the kind of venue that screams class, sophistication, and the arts.

Great place to eat while in town! Chicken strips were super moist, and when I told them about my peanut/fish allergy they were super accommodating. The girl with the pink/brown hair was our waitress and she was super sweet! Was even given a $5 coupon before we walked in. Great place

The Schermerhorn Nashville Symphony was an amazing venue for a concert. We came to the Richard Marx concert on June 14th. Amazing!  The acoustics in the room were on point. The symphony behind Richard Marx was magnificent. The building itself was inspiring with all of its intricate details. It was very clean. There was an outside area for having a drink and enjoying the fresh air yet you were still in the confines of the building. There were bars on every floor as well. Everything you needed was right there. We had box seats on the balcony. Nothing could've been better for that night. Simply priceless!!

As someone who lives here, I know this place is a tourist trap, but my sister loves coming here on special occasions, so it's where we ended up. We had a great experience. The food was yummy, even though it was outrageously priced, and we were fortunate to sit far enough away from the band that we could hear the music, but still carry on a conversation without having to yell. Our server was fantastic and gave us recommendations as well as kept our table clear and drinks refilled. They've got the piano stairs, gift shop, nice bar, lots of drink options, and live band. Overall, the service and food was pretty good compared to what you could end up getting downtown at a busier restaurant.

As our Uber pulled up under a bridge we were a little skeptical but wow are the beers good! 

We ordered two flights which allowed us to taste the majority of the drafts. Hands down the best one was the Colts Bolts, an amazing peanut butter/almond/chocolate stout. The vibes were very chill and cozy. There was more seating upstairs and it looked really cute even though we didn't sit there. Service was also great!
Fun place to grab a cold beer and hear some great live music. Worth stopping in for a cold one on a hot day. Beers are about $5

I'm sad to say that we are still racist in 2019 , the bartenders at the upstairs bar would not serve my African American husband and when we told management they did absolutely nothing.  This truly breaks my heart

My first trip to Nashville and ended up here.  Unbelievably good food and great beer! Christian Spears has a great thing going, with a wonderful atmosphere, and now expanding the brewery (they do tours, and special events there, too!).  They really do it right in terms of knowing what makes a great beer.  Try the Southern Wit, and I particularly liked Extra Easy (most like an English bitter.)  For food, Jay Mitchell makes a 5 Beer Burger that just melts in your mouth-and a Hot Chicken Sandwich which is just lightly  crispy on the outside, and tender inside.  Would go back in a second!  Great job, Tennessee Brew Works, a bright future ahead!  (AND I'll be back!!)

It's so terrible that I'm writing a review as I sit here. Awful service. Tables are so sticky. It took about 45 minutes to get our food. Food just came and my fries are cold and my bun is burnt. How do you screw up a chicken sandwich and french fries? Also, my margarita was all sour mix. Do not suggest. Go down the block to the Tin Roof instead.

I was glad we decided to stop by and try this place. Great set up on the interior and super friendly staff. The brewer was nice enough to come out and talk to me because i had some questions on his beer. 

The food is amazing! We had the chicken wings, frog legs and hot chicken sandwich. I recommend all three they really made the trip worth it.

The beers were really good. Their specialty beers really stood out to us. The beet beer was amazing, loved the cucumber beer as well as the Thai basil, they had some really unique stuff going on.
Great beers and amazing food! The burger is out of this world. All made even better by the excellent and friendly service. Don't be intimidated by the neighborhood.

First place to grab a bite to eat on my trip to Nashville with my friends. The food was sub par. Service was weird too how you had to go pay for your bill at the bar and they didn't have a lot of napkins and looked like they were understaffed. 

My quesadilla I had was spicy, so spicy to the point where I didn't even end up really eating any of it. I had to pick apart the green peppers. Not sure sure what made it so spicy, but I was not a fan

Disappointed! Terrible service, asked 3 servers to help us. It's a drinking establishment and you can't get a drink when you are at a table and no to in the bathroom. Basics! Love you Blake, you should drop in and check up on your staff...and musicians

Great service and entertainment but the food was honestly pretty terrible. As much as I wanted to love it we were a party of 6 and no one was a huge fan. The building and atmosphere was great. Just not the food. Disappointing.
Fun vibe! We were there on a Friday late afternoon and they had great service and a great band. Eat the chicken. You'll thank me if you do.

If I could give this 0 stars it would be more appropriate!  Having Celiac is always a struggle to eat out, but I've always managed to find something to eat at every restaurant. Today I was told I could not eat anything in this restaurant!! Really???  Are you just lazy???  I should be able to eat ANYWHERE!!! Shame on you!!

Absolutely incompetent staff. Jimmy should be ashamed to have his name attached to such a train wreck. Dozens of us have been waiting for hours to get inside for the Happy Hour radio show and suddenly several dozen people were allowed to cut in line in front of us - it was reported and nothing done about - due to complete lack of organization. Repeat of New Year's Eve 2017. How hard is crowd management? Well, if you work at Margaritaville Nashville, it's impossible.

We got the soft pretzel and it was very good.  We did have to wait a long time for a server. They were serving the table next to us, but would walk by us. They had live music on the rooftop that was great!

Pros: Plenty of seating. Large beer menu. Chill atmosphere. 

Cons: Beer was just okay. I wouldn't buy it after trying the flight and my 2 guests that joined agreed.

As Broadway bars are, this one is pretty "old time" tourist popular compared to the newer bars who are using a country singers actual name. You might think that coming here you are going to hear alot of caribbean type music but that is not the case. They bring in solo/duo artists as well as bigger Broadway bands. There have a family time where younger under age performers are given a chance to break into the singing scene. 
The food and drinks are pretty much like every other place along the street. Some things have a theme and come in kitschy containers. Fun for the tourist aspect! There is an upstairs area though I have never ventured up there. The gift shop have a lot of "Jimmy" stuff and other cool surf wear.
Fun fact: they host Sirius XM shows periodically and the artist draws a big crowd so get in early.

Visiting Nashville and decided to grab a quick bite before Country Music Hall of Fame. Even by southern standards, the service is sloooooowwwww. Took 15 minutes after seating to see a waitress and 45 minutes to get a chicken salad and burger. Average food. Subpar service. Skip it, you'll be better off.

Whoever the bartender was tonight at William colliers was absolutely the worst bartender I've ever experienced. I was here on behalf of my friends playing this venue. I chose the William colliers bar vs. the main venue bar because it was 21 and up and less crowded. Every time  I came to this bar the bartender seemed disinterested, rude and  annoyed. She made ordering a drink feel like a chore and her bar was anything but crowed. Honestly, she doesn't deserve to work at one of the most popular venues in the city. I rate this one star because your service was absolutely terrible.
This was my favorite bar downtown Nashville this visit. Staff is friendly, music is awesome! We just had drinks and they had my beer on draft mich ultra!

Layla's!  Are you kidding me... this place is fabulous.  Live music is always playing at this place... trust me they were rocking today at noon.... it's Monday.  

We had a great time and should be a stop every time your on Broadway in Nashville.

Came here for dinner the other night and I have to say the food was great! I've been here before but just for drinks . The band was really good and our waitress was very attentive. I ordered the spicy chicken biscuit sandwich which was just the right amount of spice. You have to try the fried pickles because they are amazing! My son got the bucket of chicken and he said it was really good. It's a lot of chicken so a bucket for the whole table is enough. This place is clean and a great time!!

I have had the opportunity and/or privilege to see a number of acts play at the Bridgestone Arena over the past Twenty-two  years. Last night was no exception when we saw the Backstreet Boys perform here.

I have to say that I was very impressed with their show. Even 26 years later, these guys still sound great and put on a heck of a show.

The overall experience was very nice. We had great seats, listened to some great music, and a good time all around

***Reviewing this place as a venue***

I came here for a CD release party for a friend of a friend. They had rented out the whole bar as a music venue. The way this bar is set up is pretty cool. There is a stage towards the front of the bar, and then the taps are in the back. It is large enough that everyone was able to move around comfortably.

My favorite part of the bar was upstairs. There are bar games and a wall of windows that overlook the breweries. There is a smaller bar upstairs for you to get your beer fix. 

TBW offers a great variety of beers with many options for your preferences. I think this is a great venue for a party to rent out for a social or a fundraiser. The staff was attentive and great, and it was overall a wonderful experience!

Came here with our kids for lunch. Kid friendly place during the day. Great atmosphere and amazing food. We asked our server for food suggestions, as former servers we knew they would have the beat info. We chose from her suggestions and were happy we did. Tater tot poutine is a must. Champagne of chicken-half portion was enough for 2 and we actually would have had left overs if we were local and going home to a fridge.

If you're in the area I highly recommend swinging by for a drink or bite to eat. There food is amazing and I highly recommend the nashville hot chicken sandwich. Many great craft beers that they brew right there. Great atmosphere and they have had live music every time I have been there.

Had the clam and corn chowder, sat by the window people watching while the live music played along. Loved this place. It was less hole in the wall and more standardized restaurant compared to other stops along that street. Loved the music, excellent waiter who helped guide us as to what places ee should be seeing during our stay in nashville. Go to place if u need good food and a second to relax from the noise.

Tennessee Beer Works is a cool spot to visit in Nashville and the food they offer is relatively good but a tad bit pricey. My wife and stoped at this location and got the beer cheese burger and a flight of beers while the beers were great the burger was a tad bit salty but it was still great. The condiments were all home made which was a nice touch and the service was friendly which was definitely nice. While my wife and I were eating they had live music and it was great to listen to an upcoming local artist while delving into some good beer and food. This is a definitely place to visit in the Nashville area.

Ordered Redneck Nachos. Oh my gosh! HUGH! Kettle chips, chicken,chees,avacado,tomato'sour cream, &j jalapenos.  Two of us shared and could barely get thru half. Recommend. Also ordered fried pickles & tomatoes. Very tasty and huge order. I believe nachos were $14 which was great price for the amount. Think pickes $10. We had 2 beers. These were $5.50 EACH. Pricey.. 
Entertainment was Dixie Jade. The lead vocalist was excellent. Nice atmoshere & friendly. You can go in & sit @ several bars & listen to music or buy t-shirts, cups,etc. Wait time to eat wasn't bad around 5pm.Fun place. (Forgot to take food photos)

We bought $100 p/p tickets to Ole Red's 4th of July rooftop bar and unfortunately the only highlight of this night was the fireworks that were offered for free by Nashville. 6 of us were down in Nashville for the weekend, and decided to get tickets to the 4th of July rooftop bar offer from Ole Red. What a mistake!!! We paid $600 to watch fireworks!  

There was limited seating, they offered passing hor d'oeuvres which was just that passing. There was one hostess "running" around with a tray on occasion.

We were entitled to one drink with that pricetag, and the drink was limited to a cocktail list chosen by Ole Red, which by 7:30 pm was only down to a selection of 2 drinks, which neither was worth drinking. If you paid for drinks, they were outrageously priced and not that good. 

Nothing worth going back to this bar for!

The service is slow and inattentive on the roof. Waited 15 minutes than had to chase down server to order a drink. Than waited another 20 for the drink to show up without the other drink and water  we ordered. Server acted like she was doing me a favor. Avoid plenty of other options. Nothing special about this location.

A definite honky tonk bar!  Loved it!!  And there are thousands of license plates from all over hanging from the ceiling.  A lot to look at while you sipping down your drinks or listening to the bands playing.  Friendly people working there, and customers.  Was glad I stopped into this place for a quick drink.

love my rock &roll but i have to say this is a bad place to hold a rock show everybody is on there butt country town what else can i say back to indy a rockin crowd ..just have to say walking down town and stopping in all the great and famous bars was awesome.i will be back only to have a good time but i will never waste my money at this place again...

I love that the Bridgestone arena is always well-maintained. It always feels clean and not too crowded. They allowed plenty of space on The concourse for people to pass even during busy events. I don't tend to buy tickets in the 300 tier because it's just too far away from the action but other than that I enjoy this venue a lock for hockey games and concerts.

We were referred to the Diner for bfast. We waited over 20 minutes and I was looking at Facebook and saw Ole Red was open for brunch. So we got up and left. BEST MOVE EVER!!  We were seated in Edens section and she was A M A Z I N G!!'  She gave us great recommendations brought our champagne right away. The manager even stopped by to see how our meal was. What a class act. Blake you got it all right with this place. The grits were FABULOUS and the hot chicken Benedict was delicious  Do yourself a favor and get to Ole Red!!  And thank you Eden!  You are a gem!!  CHEERS!!

I came here for a convention for the work I belong in. The arena itself is pretty decent but I largely gave it 2 stars because there being a soup kitchen a couple blocks down where people would die for a warm meal and clean water. Meanwhile upon trying to go through the entrance, the security was making everyone entering throw their food away and they were taking people's water/drinks away. But the worst thing was they were taking the water bottles and just dumping them on the pavement, not even on the grass. The pavement appeared as if it had been rained upon. This was disgusting to me.

We stumbled upon the symphony center while we were walking on our back to my friend's house.  We got lucky since they were having an event for school kids at the venue so it was open.  We went in to have a look-see and was amazed by how beautiful the center is. The architectural design as well as the decor is fabulous.  I was particularly drawn to the lighting fixtures which were amazing and beautiful. 

We definitely got lucky that day because the symphony hall was open and the orchestra was rehearsing so we were able to listen to them.  They sounded great and the acoustics in the symphony hall was amazing.  I really wish I had time to catch a show or two at this venue on my stay in Nashville but time was short.  I will definitely catch one next time I am in town.

The staff members, volunteers I think, were very nice and accommodating.  They answered any questions that we had.  Bathrooms were well-maintained and very clean... a definite plus, if you ask me.

I attended the Zac Brown Band concert on Thursday and it was a huge success.  There really is not a bad seat in the house. The lighting and sound are well suited for concerts. It was a great venue for a major concert. I have attended Predator games too and love the arena for hockey games.  

There is a wide variety of concessions, even one that only sells grilled cheese sammies. The prices are high, but that is no different from other stadiums/arenas.

The only complaint is the limited number of bathrooms and the bathrooms are small. Even the men's bathroom has a long line.

Most impressed with the menu. 

Vegan & Vegetarian options. 
I will say the cornbread was SWEET like pound cake.
Atmosphere was great, very entertaining. 
Nice customer service at door and from the waitress. 
We sat right by the stage and only walked around a few minutes. 
There was dancing as well. 
We didn't walk upstairs this trip but definitely will next trip.

Food was surprisingly great. Burger was cooked a perfect medium rare as ordered. Fries were good. Staff & service were excellent. Great live music & festive atmosphere. Adorable little details throughout the restaurant (see photos of bathroom signs). 2nd floor gives a great view of Broadway. 
A must see in Nashville.

Just a standard Margaritaville you can find scattered anywhere in any city. The food is okay, service is pretty good, the menu items are on the expensive side, and the live band is pretty good. There's probably other places you can go to in the area that would be better, but if you really don't like deciding, then I guess this place is okay.

Came for the Music Row Happy Hour. Got to see buzz and had a good time. The food and drinks are typical of the Jimmy Buffet chain - mediocre and overpriced. The 3rd star is just for hosting the weekly event.

Awful, Do not recommend, we are locals, and decided to give Ole Red a try.  I know that they do not rely on a revisit (since most that visit are tourists) so they really don't care about the quality of the food or service(sad), but we will not come back or recommend it to any one visiting.  First the service was obnoxiously slow, and they weren't that busy ( around noon on Sunday) we waited so long for drinks, that we went up to the bar to get our own (the table next to us did as well, several times, they were from out of town and complained the whole time about the service)  When we finally got to order our food, we both ordered the Ribeye, $30.00 a person, with one side.  Well it was the worst cut of meat I have ever had in my life, it was ALL fat,!   I understand it is not a steak house, but I have bought better steak at Aldi then this!!!! Thirty dollars for this?  Mine was way overcooked ( I wanted medium rare) so I sent it back, It was $30 after all,  I was eventually brought another, which was rare, still mooing on the plate, but didn't say anything, it wasn't worth it to us.  It was a struggle to get the sever to come back, (that's why we got our own drinks), so we paid the tab and went elsewhere  The one good thing they had was  the Cauliflower (Ill give them that).  Also they had music playing and it wasn't over the top loud, so kudos on that as well, but overall your food and service sucks! I normally do not leave reviews but it was just that bad.  Save your self the trouble and go somewhere else!!!!!

I didn't drink or eat here so take my review with a grain of salt but in my opinion, this is one of the better bars on Broadway. I'm not into club like bars that have a DJ. Ole Red has live (good) music and the atmosphere isn't too over the top. If you want to listen to live music and have a drink, stop by Ole Red!

When I think of what Blake Shelton's restaurant might be the first thing would be a dive bar.  Of course I was partially wrong, it is a dive bar with some major modern features.  It did not disappoint. The ambiance was amazing with a great band and the food was some of the best I have had.  I recommend the wings because they have just a little bit and they fall right off the bone.  A must have is the homemade tater tots.
The beers were interesting and enjoyable for the most part (especially the basil) and the consistent live music added to the ambiance. Emptier than expected for a Saturday night.

More than anything, I really like the feel of this place. Brewery/taproom/bar/live music venue, TBW has pretty much everything you need for a beer-fueled good time. I hadn't heard of this brewery before coming to Nashville but I'm mighty glad that it's on my radar now.

To begin with, as you approach the venue, you're impressed. Rather than go for an industrial 'gritty' feel, TBW welcomes you with patio seating, gorgeous wood and plenty of open air (is that a rooftop?). TBW is a celebration of one of the key elements of beer drinking: doing so with a group of friends. Yes, the craft beer movement is a serious one but it should also be fun. The fellas over at TBW remembers that. Step inside and, again, you have ample seating, a second floor/balcony access and plenty of posters letting you know of upcoming shows. A cold craft beer and live music sounds like a pretty excellent night in Nashville. And, what of the beer? I'm glad you asked. Expect inventive flavors that, if you come here during a tour, are expertly explained and generously sampled. I am not much of a basil fan (read somewhere once that it's a carcinogen and whether or not it's true, it's stayed with me for all of these years) but it was an unexpectedly tasty treat. A saison with fruit notes, the spice from the herb elevates the beer in to something I'd never tasted before (and I drink a lot of beer). The Country Roots sweet potato stout was also a fun drink. It respects the region while offering a twist on the usual stout (coffee and chocolate notes). Since the beers (while I was there) hovered around the hoppy and bitter (not my flavor profile), the last beer I tried was the Southern Wit. This is a white ale with conspicuous sweet fruit notes (orange, honey and pear). It went down very easily and would be a perfect spring/summer beer. Are you sensing a pattern? The brewers at TBW take this stuff seriously but have fun with their creations. You should as well.

We were visiting Nashville for a few days and we decided to find a nice local pub to spend one of those nights... Boy what a mistake that was, I probably should've listened to the uber driver when he said that the downtown bars are "nicer to the outsiders". The lady bartenders were very rude to us from the beginning and they were not shy about it either. One of the ladies got irritated because I found a fly in my drink and she had to remake it, really? A few hours in they decided to express their feelings by cursing at us, we decided to take our business somewhere else because the lady bartenders made racist comments and the manager "turtle" did nothing when these allegations were brought to him. Definitely not worth you money or time!

Delicious food choices here at TBW. We had a pulled pork sandwich And a beat salad. Both were very tasty and fresh ingredients. I also had a seasonal wheat beer, I think called walk the lime which was great as well. There was music in the afternoon which was very nice. Service was very efficient and friendly. A nice brewery ambience, loud but you expect that. We will return the next time we're in Nashville.
We came to Nashville for the weekend for our birthdays and after visiting several bars margaritaville was the BEST one we went too. They have great food and drinks and the bartenders were excellent.

Loved it! The beer selection is awesome and their food is on point! Ample space on the patio and dog friendly as well! They have a small lot in the back for cars, but it might be better to park on the street-the alley is super narrow.

Really cool place to go but it's somewhat overrated. Food was good - but not better than other restaurants who are more reasonably priced. The decor is awesome and live music makes it a nice place to hang out. Considerably less of a party atmosphere than most of the other places on Broadway street. Bring the kids - lol!

For Father's Day week we were in Nashville on business.  On Father's Day my husband was taken to the Nashville Symphony: The Baseball Project with Hall of Fame Dave Winfield as narrator and host of the event.  Also in attendance was former baseball Manager John McNamara  .  Along with these two icons were vintage and historical footage from Cooperstown.  The had singers who sung classic baseball songs as the symphony performed.  They also reenacted a baseball game as you would hear it on the radio or sitting in the stand with symphony playing the organ riff you hear at every baseball game to making sounds that sounded like a crowd.  The also did a tribute to Babe Ruth, Joe DiMaggio, Jackie Robinson and Roberto Clemente.  Additionally they had a vintage baseball team that plays by the original baseball rules in the lobby between intermission and before/after the show.  We really enjoyed it.  Great Job! Nashville Symphony!

This outstanding brewery near the Nashville Gulch is a great place to enjoy some delicious craft beer, good grub and wonderful music. Dropping by during a recent visit to Music City, I enjoyed two fabulous IPAs -- the hoppy 1927 and the citrusy Hippies & Cowboys -- along with their solid Extra Easy, a malty pub ale. Paired with a tasty Five Beer Burger, the brews were by far the best I've had in Nashville.

Brew Works also serves up live music almost nightly -- the evening I was there, I enjoyed a terrific performance by a local bluegrass band. The small taproom practically puts the musicians in your lap, but you can  escape to a second-floor bar and dining room if that's not your speed. There's also an outdoor balcony with great city views. The location is an industrial neighborhood just east of the official 'Gulch,' so it can feel a bit isolated if you're walking over on your own. And while parking onsite is limited, I had no trouble finding a spot about a block away on the street. 

Tennessee Brew Works is a gem that combines great craft beer with great music. A must for any beer lover visiting Nashville.

We are beer lovers and are so happy there is finally a quality beer and food spot!!!Love the sweet potato stout! Also,
The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable about the beer and food. We always take our out of town friends here and these guys at TBW never disappoint.

This is a combo review for Margaritaville AND Grubhub. I was following the updates, saw my food was being prepared, then suddenly got an email that said my orders cancelled. Had to call to find out that Margaritaville cancelled it when the driver arrived. No phone call or anything.

Great food, great experience!  A must visit in Nashville! Service was excellent and environment was open and welcoming.  Server came by several times and was very sweet. Menu had good offerings and came out of he kitchen quickly.
Less than mediocre food. Terrible service. And much better music in the other bars. I feel like I'm at Friday's.

Say what you want about the chain "touristy" places here on Broadway, but Margaritaville is my favorite. I'm only 37, but I much prefer the laid back older style of food and fun. Dierks, Luke Bryan, Kid Rock, Ol Red, etc. They're much too loud, boozy and fake cow girl trashy at times. If you're into that, by all means. But I have been to many Margaritaville's around the world and will always find my way back. Can't beat a cheeseburger in paradise with a solo acoustic guitarist singing great country music at the bar area. Sometimes it's nice to just sit and relax and eat with some chill music.

Very enjoyable eating experience in the heart of Honky Tonk Nashville's famous downtown Broadway. More of a pleasant dining music alternative to the louder places on Broadway. Ole Red has very talented performers. Victoria our server was great. The Potato Tots are amazing and huge. The Kiss My Country Ass Quesadillas delicious. An overall great place to visit and revisit.

At $150 per ticket this is the most expensive concert I've ever attended. I paid more for a middle seat (section 107) than a full day at Disney World including parking. I've seen this band twice in a hockey stadium in San Diego since 2017 for under $70. So at more than double California prices my expectations were pretty high. 

The biggest problem is something I've never seen permitted at a major indoor venue. Tons of people were smoking e-cigarettes inside! The entire building smelled like a clown had died. I saw at least fifteen people smoking throughout the entire show in my section alone. Security saw them too, but not a single person got tossed out. Security would just stare at them disapprovingly and the smokers would huff on their hard drives the second they walked away. I also watched a drunk guy in a $300 section annoy everyone around him for an hour and security did nothing about it. Finally, the guy vomited everywhere and was escorted out by his friends. Security should have thrown him out long before that point. They hardly cleaned the mess and it looked like no one was offered to be moved to another section. Another thing I've never seen permitted at a venue like this was all the people sneaking to seats they didn't pay for. Security didn't catch half of them and when they did they just walked them back to their seat. 

The good news is the sound and lighting were great. Sometimes the mixing was off, but that was probably the band's people. The food and drink stands were all friendly and efficient. Alcohol was 11-22 dollars. They had large cans of beer within 10 feet of any seat, but the lines to the bathrooms were about fifty people long so that's probably a bad idea. The Uber to get home was 4x the cost of the ride there because of surge pricing. 

I seriously doubt I'd come back to such a poor operation at these prices. I can't believe I'm saying this, but if they could just lower their prices to California prices it may be worth going. Its actually a very nice venue if they didn't let so many people ruin the show for everyone around them.

Really great bar food! Sampled several good beers too! Nice live music. Bathrooms out of soap and paper towels ... hence the four rather than five stars. Maybe this was a fluke though. 

The grilled cheese with pear butter, goat and white cheddar was to die for! The smoked pulled pork sandwich was mouthwateringly delicious. We also liked the hot chicken sandwich. The fries were just ok, but the house made ketchup was excellent with a sweet balsamic flavor. There was a beer called the quad something, wow, loved it! Very smoky and rich. It packed a punch at 10% ABV.

I have always loved this restaurant, the food, & the atmosphere. We thought it would be fun to have our rehearsal dinner here but had concerns that it was going to be "too loud" on a Friday night for such an event.  During our meeting the week before, the staff assured us that there would not be a band playing that night since our event was already booked for the space upstairs.  Also, we were assured ahead of time that we would be provided with a microphone for family speeches.  Within five minutes of walking in the door on our rehearsal dinner night- surprise! You aren't getting a microphone because the BAND is using it tonight. Friends and family had to yell the words that were very important to us, and we were not able to hear half of what anyone was trying to say to us on our special night .  The staff was constantly complaining to our party throughout our dinner that we were interfering with the band playing (that we were told would not be there that night) and quite frankly, we felt they couldn't wait for us to get out of there!  Not happy that Margaritaville did not follow through with what they told us for our rehearsal dinner and we do not recommend this as a venue for an event unless you are prepared for everyone to have to yell at each other the entire time!

On a rainy Saturday night, I walked out with 1/2 of my party to put our very drunk friend in an Uber.  When I turned around to come back in, the bouncer would not let me in.  He told me,"you're husband is too drunk."  As I tried to explain that it was not my husband and my husband was in the bar, he told me I had an attitude and could not come in.  The more I tried to explain that the drunk friend was going home and my husband was in the bar,  more he said no and now I won't you let you in because your angry.  Of course I was angry, it was raining, I was soaked, and outside from the rest of my party because of a bouncer who "knew" who I was married to.  Another employee (Blonde lady) who I am assuming the manager came out and asked me the problem. When I tried to explain, she said, "You're angry. You can't come in."  Long story short...it took me 15 minutes to convince her to go in and find my actual husband because his phone was dead and my other friends didn't answer theirs.  Of course I was angry Layla's!  You let me stand in the rain arguing with a bouncer over who I was married to because of course, the bouncer knows best.  The Blonde employee finally got my party who had no idea what happened.  We went to the really nice bar next door for me to dry off.  My clothes were still wet the next day.  You're bouncer is a jerk.  If there is anyone that cares at this establishment, feels free to private message me.  Otherwise, I'll go to another place the next time I'm in Nashville!

4 of us were sitting at the very top bar having conversation and two other tables were occupied.  Security came up and was super rude said "we are closing this bar" "I need you to get up and get out now". Then when we looked at him in shock he said "do you have a problem?" We of course said yes you are very rude so he ejected us from the bar trying to start a fight on the sidewalk.  Never will we return and we are not tourists but residents who live at music row just a couple blocks away.

The fried chicken was great. We had the 1/2 chicken and briskets and it was plenty for 2. The music was loud but not overpowering. We had the  normal seasoning. They also have Hot that is a Buffalo Wings sauce. The 4 stars is for the meal along with a quality music show.

We have driven through Nashville for the past two summers, and have decided to stay in Nashville, so we can go to Tennessee Brew Works for beer, burgers and darts after a long day on the road. We are big fans of the Extra Easy, but we bring the IPAs home for friends. Truthfully though, we stop at TBW for the burgers and fries. You will not find better. We also love sitting outside on the deck and listening to live music.
Lively place, for a Thirstday afternoon/evening. Good beer and fine hushpuppies. Active dartboard. Fun & friendly informed staff.
Ok music. Ok Food. Had the steak and corn. Asked for medium rare steak, got well done. There is better food and music nearby. They get three stars only because our waitress was great.

After a light meal and an hour at the Johnny Cash museum, we're off to see downtown Nashville via trolley. Broadway is lined with music bars so it's pretty easy to become numb to the choices. As we were moving along at a habitual New York pace, I was struck by the sounds coming from this place that calls itself a "Hillbilly Music" bar.  To Mrs G I beckon, "Stop!!!  Check this out".

Walking into a dimly lit dive with random license plates and colorful Christmas lights, we were greeted with classic rock and roll mixed with country western. The band played songs by The Allman Brothers Blues Band (One Way Out, Southbound) and Lynrd Skynrd (Sweet Home Alabama, Gimme Three Steps) plus a whole bunch of cool classics by artists I cannot recall due to the good time we had...

Clearly this was a cover band - a really good one - that brought its own style but caught all the critical licks from the southern rock sound so.

Beer is cheap with basic choices in bottle.

We never caught the trolley tour...

First of all, GET THE TOTS. I don't care if you don't like tots, (because I don't) GET THEM. Our waitress, Megan (I think) suggested them to us and described them as deep fried mashed potatoes and she was right. SO GOOD. Burger was fantastic too! We sat right beside the stage and it was nice listening to the band.

Food is not fresh and tasty. It's super expensive. People don't eat if it was given it for free but charged 5 times the regular price. Service was slowest in the world and it took more than 90 minutes. I was ready to leave but the waiter kept saying food is ready and on the way. What a waste of precious time and money :( Stay away. This type of places should learn a lesson

I was treated to Tennessee Brew Works on Nashville Brew Bus tour during Yelp Spring Break and what a treat, one of the highlights of trip to Nashville with a tour from one of the owners Garr Schwartz, who is passionate about amazing craft beer.
Tennessee Brew Works is only one of three breweries in the United States using Belgian Meura mash filter.
My favorite beer, which my friend who is not a big beer fan, commented holy shit this is good beer is their Basil Ryeman, Belgian style Farmhouse Saison beer, which was one of the best beers I enjoyed in Nashville. 
I can't wait to return to have some more great craft beer on my next trip to Nashville and bring a growler and cooler to keep cool on the five hour trip back to Ohio.

Whether it is a concert, festival or sporting event -Bridgestone has you covered.
Great location! 
Food is good if you need a snack.
Preds Pro Shop here too!!
The bathrooms are newly renovated!
The only good part was music from Trey Odell and the view. Server was not knowledgeable of what gluten free options they have. Friends fries were cold. Server forgot to put in one item we ordered

I was excited to add this place to my list to have a drink for my first visit to Nashville.  What a disappointment.  Old decor and I did not think it was very Jimmy Buffety.  We sat at the bar and nearby was a singer.  He was ok. Did a couple of sing along songs.  That was fun. Lots of drinks on the menu.  I was surprised that they didn't have more of a selection of margaritas.  A lot of their drinks had pineapple juice in them and I am allergic to pineapples. I ended up ordering a strawberry daiquiri.  But asked the bartender if there was any pineapple in the margarita.  I know they normally do not - but like I said there was only a few drinks that did not have pineapple in them.   He asked if I was allergic and when I told him yes, he said he would wash a few things before he made my drink.  Appreciate that!  But when I got my drink?  It had a pineapple hung on the rim of my glass. Hmmmm..... As for the drink it had to have been a virgin- could not taste the alcohol - not even a little bit.   Same for the husband - could not taste the alcohol.  24 dollars for 2 drinks that weren't that good?  I wouldn't recommend this place.

Words cannot describe the level of customer service that Shelby bestowed upon me, true professionalism at its finest. You could tell she was an expert at customer service and it showed. If I could pick one waitress to serve me my food for the rest of my life at a restaurant it would be Shelby. I'm literally breath taken and I will spread the word of her legendary service.

We had a lovely time! Drinks were great. Bands were outstanding. Waitress was ok, but not the best. Some staff really lacked the southern hospitality. Very dry. 
As far as food:
Kids chicken nuggets were a hit! Tarter tots over fries!! Way better! Nachos are amazing but SO BIG!! This is enough for 3-4 people! Burgers I thought were ok. Nothing like the waitress went on and on about! 
All in all, I enjoyed our time here. Would come back again.

Put me in a setting that'll provide live music and enjoy some signature craft beers and I'll be certain I've died and gone to heaven. The location of TBW is signature and I love how it's in a location that's so industrial and raw. It's a gem and a sense of a reward once you arrive at Tennessee Brew Works.

The patio in front is beautiful with dark wood and steel structures. As a double decker patio, you can find plenty of seating inside and out. Immediately as you walk in you'll be basked in the sounds of Nashville's live music scene and the artists TBW features were fantastic! Pretty sure my friends had to drag me out of the scene as I couldn't get enough.

For those that have a thirst to quench you'll find a bar downstairs and up. Their flavors are fun and unique which they take great pride in their brews. It's possible to grab a tour at a small cost and the tasting room is situated inside the brewing room which is a score! From board games to darts you can get lost for hours as your sipping on a hop and grabbing a bite to eat at the brewery. My favorite was the Southern Wit ( A Belgian White Ale) which had a great palette of flavors but they have a beer for your personal preferences.

This was not worth the wait. The drinks are way out of line with the price. I know it's a tourist area but seriously when I can buy an entire bottle for less then the cost of one drink (which I might add wasn't even a full shot) there's a problem. The food was ok. Nothing to write home about. The service though was inexcusable. We ordered an appetizer that came Wirth an egg on top (poutine?). I noticed immediately when it arrived at the table it was extremely jiggly. Sure enough the white of the egg was vary cooked & snotty like. I had the person who delivered it take it back & asked if they could finish cooking the white. The waitress came over & said to clarify you want the egg hard. I explained no just the white cooked. The waitress's response was to roll her eyes at me. Sorry but I don't eat snot. When they brought it back out sure enough she had them take that egg slap it on the grill, bust the yolk, & fry the hot sauce into the egg. Exactly what I had said I didn't want. It defeated the purpose of having an egg on the dish. As for everything else well you can get that food pretty much anywhere for less money. Lastly, no one was checking bathrooms. After standing & waiting for a stall they were all out of TP. I certainly hope this is not what Blake would want to hear about his place.

This place is new and nice. Pretty clean as well. The staff is deplorable and customer service leaves a lot to be desired. The manager actually made a derogatory remark about the length of time it took me to get up the stairs. I was born with a rare muscle disease. I feel like anyone who patronizes this bar is likely to be treated the same way. Will not return and will let everyone I know exactly how I felt.

Bleu Butler

Went there on 4/11/18 for a light lunch. Ordered the peel and eat shrimp. I had eaten all but the last one, when I looked in the basket and realized it had not been cooked! (Spent the next 4 days sick!) Pointed it out to the waiter and he agreed it was raw. I went to the bathroom to clean up after which I returned to find 2 more shrimp on a plate. As if I would even consider eating anymore! Beware!

Great atmosphere. Good beer. Yummy food! 

We couldn't check in to our AirBnB until late afternoon so this was a perfect stopping place for us. 

My boyfriend and I split the burger and the chicken sandwich. Both were unique and yummy, but very filling. My favorite part of our meal was the French fries. The seasoning was super good. 

The beer was okay. The flight was a good value so it was nice to try a few different options, but I didn't like them enough to order a full glass. 

We brought our dog and sat outside. The outdoor seating is nice and the inside is super open. You can even walk through the brewery portion of the building.

I was so dissatisfied with the service and lack of quality and taste of the food.  Service horrible and takes forever.  Party of six normal no heavy drink orders basic food requests.  All the people in the dinner party said same.....food bad.  Does Blake eat here?  So excited no bummed over it.  People at KOA also said food bad they all went on different days too.  Missed opportunity for a Big Bang but a big flop.  Also several people said his other place just as bad.

This place is a city. It's just so so big. I remember when Bridgestone was brand new and the city was courting a hockey team. Hockey? In Nashville? Do ya know where you are? This is football country. O course, these were the days when Peyton Manning made sure that Saturdays in the Volunteer state were burnt orange. Well, history has shown that hockey has made a much better home of late in Nashville than football has (no pressure, Mariota) and Bridgestone has stood the test of time.

I don't get the complaints that it's old. The arena is less than 20 years old, people. Wrigley is old. Bridgestone is barely walking. And, despite its relative youth, it's already undergone some pretty significant (and impressive) renovations. Parking is easy.* There are plenty of access points. Three levels give goers the option of a variety of experiences. The on-site dining is choice (and that space has been redone as well). And the arena itself is massive. It's designed to hold a ton of folks but I have never felt smashed in or uncomfortable. I've also never been here for any other reason than to attend a hockey game. I know! I didn't even go to hockey games when I lived in Chicago. But, I wanted to check out some pro sports, Music City-style and until the NBA can figure out that Nashville is perfect for a team, hockey it is (change my mind, Mariota).

Watching hockey at Bridgestone is fantastic. There's not a bad seat in the arena and the good seats are *really* good. The fans are into it, support the team, make noise, and are psyched to watch the action. Nashville's a hockey town. Who knew?** Plus, there's good music, great graphics and a fantastic atmosphere. Again, I've never attended a concert at the Arena. If I had, perhaps my opinion would/will change. But until that happens, I'm more than happy to come here for a hockey game. I'd be even happier to come here for a NBA game. I'm looking at you, Raptors.

*It is. Don't argue.
**Keep in mind, Miami has a hockey team as well. Games/fans are not nearly as fervent... which is to be expected. The Panthers should move to Indy, Cincy or Cleveland.

Wow It was our First time at Broadway's new restaurant, Ole Red- Blake Sheltons new establishment. Thanks to our waitress Creuna she was awesome. Great band JD Shelborne and food was amazing.For lunch we had the burger and chicken biscuit sandwich. Both were excellent and complimented by great drinks. Very clean place and service superb. Highly recommend when in Nashville.

I wanted to add to my review that our food may not have been outstanding; but it was still pretty good.  (Our group of 5 managed to finish it off!). I also wanted to add that our server, Olivia, was outstanding!  She was friendly, helpful when we were ordering, and quick to anticipate drink needs & get them our in a timely manner.  She is definitely an asset to Margaritaville!

Great atmosphere , several great bands. Nice atmosphere. So much food it was difficult to eat. Only negative while all four of us enjoyed everything about the Resturant. There was no place to park and the cost of 25.00 for parking  was steep, for no longer than we were there.

Yes, yes, and yes.

The Schermerhorn is a fantastic venue (and wonderful addition to downtown Honky-Tonk Central) hosting all manner styles of music performances. In fact, for some people it is a bit of a surprise in this country-centric music mecca.

We've enjoyed attending a abundance of events ranging from Classic Symphonies performed by the the highly talented, 5-star Nashville Symphony Orchestra to Jazz Concerts & Pop Performances by legends such as The Manhattan Transfer, Johnnie Mathis, Frankie Valli & the 4 Seasons, to Movies...accompanied by the orchestra. That's a treat in and of itself. A live performance of the music while viewing the full length motion picture.

The offerings are not limited to classical or jazz or pop. Music of ALL kinds is presented in the on-going plethora of concerts and events. Just check out the incredible schedule: https://www.nashvillesymphony.org/tickets/calendar . It is truly impressive and offers something for every age: children to senior; every taste: classic to country; multiple venues: in the hall to in the park to smaller, intimate special parties. 

The highly talented symphony is led by world-class conductors Giancarlo Guerrero (Music Director), Vinay Parameswaran (Associate Conductor) and Kelly Corcoran (Chorus Conductor). Ushers and support staff are always courteous and willing to assist in any way possible. (Don't hesitate to ask for directions--the venue can become confusing with its myriad of hallways and transition areas.)

Parking is available in numerous downtown lots. Discounted Pinnacle Parking Garage vouchers(limited) are available prior to the performance and special discounts are given to concert series subscribers. You can also park in the public lot located conveniently across 4th Avenue under the Music City Walk of Fame Park.

I afraid my words are inadequate in describing this treasure trove in downtown Nashville. I heartily encourage you to experience it for yourself.

Travelled all the way from Hawaii to watch the Gone West Band at Ole Red, waited 3 hours outside the venue to find our that we still can't go inside because they've reach capacity and if we continue to wait, their set would've been done already. So disappointed.

The Symphony Center is located in the heart of downtown Nashville with available parking directly in fronted the building-about $35-I believe they also offer valet, but when we arrived 30 minutes prior to the show, it was already full or closed. The interior creates a very elegant ambiance with great seating. We had the "box seats" which offers it's own private bar area on each floor. A definite recommend for date night!

Awesome place. Good food--get the grilled cheese, you won't be disappointed. Live music was great. Excellent beer and accommodating staff. This place is simple a MUST! If you don't stop by, you'll be sorry. Trust me on this one. Cheers! #drinklocal

Went here for a tour on Saturday at $11!
