Our tour guide Jason was super friendly, and definitely made it a more personal experience asking where we were from, if we had been on a tour before, and tailored the tour information to our interest. We were able to taste 2 beers that day Southern Wit and a porter, Pie Town Porter. They gave us a pint of whatever beer we wanted and let us keep the glass. It was a great experience, and we stayed for a while and got another flight to taste! Great beer, great people with lots of seating (2 floors), definitely would come back here again for the ambience and beer.
The most unfriendly staff!!! Not welcoming and very rude! Sad, was excited to experience it as I've heard great things!

Female bartenders are rude if you're a tourist trying to have a good time. My buddies and I were told that we were annoying and loud and to close out our tab.  Not until after we spent a good amount of money here,were they quick to dismiss us. 

It's a cool place but with poor/rude service.  We spoke with the manager but it was obvious he is not in control there. 

I wish I could give zero stars. It's definitely unfortunate.

What a fun place! Staff is VERY friendly. I shared the wings and had the sauce on the side. To be honest the dry rub on the wings was so yummy that I didn't even need the sauce. The beer in the picture is Basil Ryeman and it was just what a saison should taste like.

I've been to a few concerts here and it's always been a pretty good experience. 

Lately, they've updated their concessions and now offer great, local beers. I really appreciate that b/c, if I'm going to pay too much for a beer, I'd rather spend an extra dollar and get one worth drinking. The staff is always friendly and helpful. The sound and ambiance is what you'd imagine of an arena (big, loud, dark.) They check purses before you go in but it's nothing too crazy. The parking is less than ideal but that's just downtown, in general.

After seeing a few shows here, I've decided I'm just more of an amphitheater girl. You get a really big show at the arena but there are just so many people and the place is so big, there's not much of a vibe. For what it is, I think it is a great "what it is." Also very conveniently located if you want to crawl around downtown after an event. Leads straight out onto Broadway and all your world-famous honky-tonks.

Fun fact: The Nashville Convention and Visitor's Bureau has a visitor's information/gift store in the arena. It's the funny looking part off the side at the corner of 5th and Broadway (with the radio tower on top.) Obviously, the radio tower is a wave to WSM and the reason that part jets off the side in a weird angle is because it's supposed to look like the building is bowing down and paying homage to the Ryman Auditorium, the first home of the Grand Ole Opry, which is located just a bit further up the street off 5th Ave. Now, go impress your friends!

So we were looking for the cut out of Blake to snap a photo and we were told they keep him hidden because people were trying to steal him. Chandler and Cassie totally made it happen. Food was great and the staff was out of this world ! Shout out to Chandler,Cassie, Lora Rin and Ryan. And the food was great!

I like this place. It's the perfect dive bar. Small and cozy atmosphere. Brick walls, license plates nailed up everywhere. It was busy but not packed. Bartenders were very attentive and the band they had was really good. Very laid back crowd. Mostly young groups of friends, but a few older couples hanging out. What more can you ask for in a bar? Had a great time.

We stopped there on a Saturday morning around 10:30am. The service was the worst I have ever had anywhere - anytime. It was not crowded - maybe 15 people in the place. It was 10 minutes before we saw a wait person, It was another 10 before she brought us any drinks. They ran out of glasses. She only returned once after we summoned her to ask how much longer until the food was out - she said it was going to take a while - 10 minutes more. We waited 20 minutes more. She didn't return, we waited 45 minutes total for the food that never arrived. We gave up and left.

Stopped in before my concert right across the street at the Ryman. I ordered the Shrimp Scampi along with the Uptown Top Shelf Margarita as recommended by our friendly server Francine. The food took a little long but it was a busy night in town and Francine kept us informed along the way. My party and I enjoyed it and will definitely comeback to enjoy a little bit more of the live music and great food.

Came here on a Friday night with some Nashville locals and was shocked it wasn't more busy, but that was fine with us. It looked like the live music had just wrapped up and there was plenty of outdoor seating. Beer was good as expected and I hope to come back and try some others another time. 

Ordered the Southern Grilled Cheese with bacon and WOW was it good. The pear butter added a unique and delicious flavor. The bacon was really thick; it was good but next time I would probably skip it. The food was really good but a bit overpriced; granted it was a very gourmet grilled cheese.

This is one place we always visit when going through Nashville or staying for the weekend!! The beer is so good and clean and food is phenomenal!!! They are dog friendly and the location and atmosphere is very cool. They usually have locals musicians come in every night and I would highly recommend the tour.

Don't go here if you're a bachelorette party. They target you in a negative way. Our bride got kicked out of the building by a rent-a-cop because she was KNEELING on a chair to take a picture. We were way in the back, of course she couldn't see over the crowds of people. He apparently "warned her" to get down by waving his flashlight from 20 yards away..  that's NOT a warning. My thoughts were that they needed to make room for more customers because not even minutes after the security tells her to leave, someone is being sat at our table. Oh and the line to get in gets super long, they search bags( which I'm okay with) but my wallet? The line is also in the sun, so bring an umbrella.

I was not impressed with Ole Red. After checking reviews, we decided to give this a try. The three of us were seated within 10 minutes and the server arrived at our table soon after we were seated. The menu was somewhat limited, typical Nashville bar food fare. We ordered one hamburger and two salads. Things were a little pricey, but we were in the heart of Nashville's tourist area and realized we were going to pay more. The disappointing part was when our food arrived. The home made tater tots were soft and tasteless. Even with salt, pepper and ketchup, they were not worth the calories. If you can't make them better than what we'r buy at the grocery, don't try.  The burger was ok, but probably was frozen patty they slapped on the grill. The worst impression was made by two of the saddest salads I've ever seen. Old lettuce, mushy cherry tomatoes, and so little of everything that you could almost see the plate through it. We ordered a piece of Nashville hot chicken with each salad for an up charge of $6. Each salad was served with a SMALL thigh. For $6, a thigh!? Top that off with having to ask for dressing three times because each time they brought a container out, it had maybe two teaspoons in it, we had made up our mind that Ole Red would not be anywhere we'd recommend or visit again. So- for over $60 we recieved, two salads, one hamburger, a beer, a tea and a water. And left hungry. Don't bother with Ole Red.

A great place to listen to underground artists. I went for a whiskey jam event which is held every Monday and Thursday, and it was a great time. If you are a person that does not like large crowds, this place is probably not for you, because it was fairly packed and hard to move around. We did not get any food so I cannot say how the restaurant was, but I loved the environment and live music.

Visited this location a few times over the weekend and really enjoyed it there! The food was delicious and there were talented musicians. I'd also like to say a special thank you to Shane our waiter on 9/23. We had a situation with one of our meals not being exactly as ordered, and Shane identified and rectified the issue before we had a chance to say a word. He went directly to a manager and took care of the situation. You don't see exceptional service like this on a regular basis, and he really stood out as a professional, right-on-top of it, outgoing staff member!

This place is great. Great service, good food and love the live music. Drinks were very good and made well. Not overpowered by the alcohol, which I dislike so I appreciated that a lot. Check them out!!!

Food is nothing really good or interesting. They had us seated right in front of the band and we couldn't hear a thing the person next to us said. We then got moved to another and it was better, but the food still wasn't :). Not worth coming to.

I'd give this place no stars if possible. They sat us, said there's no tap water here (what???) and food has taken 30+ minutes to arrive (still not here). When we were ordering drinks they said they had no menu. When asked what beers they have, they said only "everything domestic" and we basically played a game with guessing which beers they actually had. Garbage service, garbage place. Probably only exists because it's next to Acme which is popular with a line.

Table right by the stage! Nice! The bands here are a step up from some smaller bars. The food, not so much. It was a lot, but just okay tasting. I had the smoked chicken quesadillas. They didn't taste smoked. There was a lot of food, but it was dark meat and I bit into cartilage- yuck. I also ordered the tater tots- mushy. But overall an okay experience. Nice roof top bar & view.

Augh, gosh. I WANTED to like this place so bad.

My friend and I came here for a couple of beers and to enjoy some music. Lo and behold, the band playing was from Austin, TX! Nice to see some Texans, what with the states' common ground with their love of country music and all. They did a great job.

I had two beers, none of which were impressive to me, and split the burger with my friend. Unfortunately, both the burger and fries were just way too salty for us to enjoy. We were even brushing salt off the bun! I'm sure that was some sort of culinary decision, just not one I necessarily agree with.

Walk the Lime: Good, but I've definitely had better. 
1927: You know, even though IPAs aren't my cuppa, I thought I had developed an appreciation for them. I feel like this undid all of that. :( Sorry, TN. TX takes my Craft Beer Award.

On the other hand, the staff was remarkably wonderful and friendly, and even though I didn't like the beer they suggested, I appreciated their input/opinions anyway.

I recently visited Nashville to see Counting Crows and Matchbox Twenty at Bridgestone. The concert was great, but the seats were AWFUL! I was section 328, row A, my view was fine. The seat itself was the issue. 

For reference, I am a size 14 pant and am 5'7" tall. Pretty average really. I did not fit in the seat. I literally sat sideways in my seat just to fit. It was an issue for almost everyone around me. I left with very sore hips and thighs, from them being pinched under the cup holders that are attached to the arms.  Woke up the next morning with fairly bruised hips and legs. Seats were right around a foot, I measured.

Seems like normal people should fit into their seats when they pay to go to a concert, but what do I know?

I purchased tickets for my husband and I, as an anniversary gift. The venue looks great and parking wasn't awful. They actually have food, which is nice. The main reason I give it 2 stars is the acoustics. The entire room has so much metal in it that there's a constant ringing. There are absolutely no sound cushions (that I could see). I couldn't hear  or understand around 80% of the lyrics. Perhaps this wasn't meant to be a musical venue on conception? The reason you go to see a performing musical artist is for the music, right? But when you can't hear the music and there's a ringing in your ears, it puts a damper on the evening. Overall: would go back for a comedy show.

This was a bit frustrating. I decided on this place because it looked nice and the live music was high quality. It's great as a venue.  However , the restaurant aspects of the experience were very disappointing.

We went for lunch during the week and we were able to get a table on the indoor balcony overlooking the band stage. The place filled up shortly afterwards. It's nice and spacious and everything was new and clean.

The service was lacking. Our server came to our table to deliver drinks and take our order but that was about it. I had to flag her down to get a refill. I tried to order two sides with my entree but the server said I could only order one side with my entree. She asked the manager and I was told that only one side per entree or else I have to order a full-sized serving of fries from the appetizer choices.Ok whatever.

I ordered the "Hot Chicken" sandwich with a side of fries. The fries were good and well-seasoned. The chicken sandwich might as well been from the dollar menu of a fast food place. It's a joke to refer to this as "hot chicken" in Nashville. The seasoning was like BBQ Lay's potato chips. 

The smoked chicken quesadilla was pretty good but it was lacking some elements that were on the menu description.

Overall, it is not worth going here to eat. This is a perfect example of a tourist trap. It would be ok to grab a drink and listen to the band but that's it. We could have had a better meal for $15 at a fast food place instead of the $80 we spent plus the $25 in parking. I wish I went to the place down the block (the one with the name that's on the anvil that drops on the coyote on the Roadrunner cartoons)
This is a cool place. Aaron was very helpful. Looking forward to coming back. The live music was cool!

Leila is a great server. She suggested a few items to try and each was delightful. Leila was pleasant, effective,efficient  and a true hospitality artisan.

The restaurant was not perfect. Very loud and the non-stop begging by the band for tips was off putting and offensive;Play a 3 minute song, 4 minutes of begging, play another song, repeat. The non-stop begging is reson alone not to go back. If you offer entertainment they should just entertain. Beggars should be on street corners not on restaurant stages.

I feel blessed to be able to live in a city that hosts such amazing talent and outstanding venues to enjoy that talent in! The Schermerhorn Symphony Center while aesthetically beautiful, also has the best acoustics I've ever experienced. No detail was left out of the design of this space and you can definitely tell. I've been privileged to enjoy several concerts here and each one was breathtaking. It's sometimes hard not to want to fall asleep when the music is lulling you that way! 

There honestly isn't a bad seat in the house as far as being able to hear the music. There are a couple places I wouldn't want to sit just for being able to see. I haven't had the opportunity to partake in any of the other amenities of the Center. I will say that I've had friends show up about a half hour before a show to get tickets that are being sold at a discount. If it isn't sold out, they want to sell the remaining tickets! Just a little tidbit for ya.

The entertainment and ambiance was the only good memory of this place. We thought with the long lines that this place had to be a good place to eat. Sadly, we were wrong. The best part of the meal was the fried pickles we had for an appetizer. My husband ordered "The Champagne of Fried Chicken, which was fried chicken and biscuits and gravy. I sampled his and agreed with him that the only good part was the gravy. The chicken was very spicy and soaked in grease. We are southern people and love our fried foods, but just a few bites made our stomachs start hurting. I ordered the "Nashville Hot Chicken Biscuit" after the waitress said that was her favorite thing on the menu. It is fried chicken on a large biscuit with cole slaw and bread and butter pickles with your choice of tater tots or french fries. The tater tots were terrible, and my chicken was just as greasy as my husband's chicken. I ended up eating the biscuit off my sandwich dipped in my husband's gravy and the bread and butter pickles. Needless to say, the food left a lot to be desired, and we left hungry.

Both times I have been to Nashville, I have wound up at this bar.  Once cause it wasn't busy and the other so my aunt could see a Sirius XM show.  Honestly I cannot get a handle on this place. The service is either attentive or sluggish.  Drinks can be good or bland.  I'm guessing everything just depends on the day and time you go.  

Good luck

This place is awesome, the service is excellent, the food is great and... oh, the beer, yeah that's pretty fantastic as well! The staff went above and beyond to ensure my out of town guests and I were well taken care of and had the opportunity to try every beer available. 

From light Pilsner style beers to big heavy porters, this place has a beer for every type of beer lover and had some great food to satisfy your appetite.

The staff made sure to treat us right and also let us go home with a few growlers of things we loved that weren't even on the board, I highly recommend this place to beer novices, and connoisseurs alike! Happy beer tasting! :)

margaritas taste like bleach and chemicals, must be how they are washing the glasses, also the ice tastes like mold. There is black mold all over the ceiling near the vents. We are from the Keys and Jimmy buffet better get his arse over hear to straighten this shiithole up.

My husband and I drove 2.5 hours to see Miike Snow at this venue. We were excited to hear their dance music live, and anticipated a great night. However, the sound mixing made for a disappointing show. The bass overwhelmed the rest of the music, and this was the case for all 3 bands that night. We thought they'd fix it by the time MS came on, but no such luck. Despite the good lineups the place gets, we will not be spending the money on a hotel, dinner and a show at MMW unless we learn that the sound quality has improved. The staff were nice, the bathrooms clean, good drinks, yada yada yada- but people come for the music, first and foremost. If that's compromised, the whole venture falls flat.

Drinks are always great. The live music was good too. I personally think their food isn't that great. It doesn't have much flavor to it. For the same price you can go somewhere in Nashville that isn't everywhere else in the country. Our server was a sweetie though!

Unfortunately we were in town during the nfl draft so lower Broadway was a madhouse however with that being said we enjoyed ole reds the most bec over all the other bars/restaurants it was the most enjoyable atmosphere with live country music involving the crowd but not annoying like some Dj's at the other Artists bars. We came to Ole Reds back to back nights to enjoy music. Now to the food, we had the nachos (very large portion shareable size for sure) and my husband got the quesadilla and really enjoyed it! Bartenders were helpful and respectful. Also have a gluten free cider beer. Overall the best experience on lower Broadway.

Worst establishment in downtown Nashville. Blake Shelton should be ashamed at how the management and staff treat the patrons. Rude, and disrespectful. Don't waste your money... food is "ok" at best and drinks are over priced and watered down. I will never go there again.  Better bars up and down the strip. This place is a complete joke....

The Bridgestone Arena is the home to the Nashville Predators and the CMA Awards. 

All year long they have many musical and theatrical events all of which are top notch.

I attend The Nashville Predator hockey games more than anything else at this venue and they do a top notch job as the home of the Predators.

If you get the chance, attend an event at The Bridgestone Arena, you will not be sorry.
The service in the restaurant was great and the food was really good. It's a little on the pricey side, but the atmosphere was great. Went to music row happy hour after we ate.
Super cool venue! The staff was friendly. There is a spacious concession area just off the main floor. Bathroom facilities were very nice. And, most importantly, the show was a lot of fun!
The food was so good and the music was fantastic. Went there for lunch to celebrate hubbys birthday. Couldn't have picked a better place. Homemade tatter tots were device. Loved it.
Great place, it's in downtown so it's a stop for everyone. At least drop in and have a drink if you don't eat here.

First and only trip in my life thus far (do folks still use "thus) and we ended up in Ole Red on three different occasions. In my opinion a great music venue kept well maintained by an energetic staff and a selection or artists that were top notch. 
Have to admit we didn't eat anything there but still transferred plenty of cash to Blake Shelton's business account!
On the last trip we ended up on the roof deck ...not much of a view but the sun break was an awesome welcome after a full day of thunderstorms. Check out the second floor for a great perspective.
Well done. Very well done!
I loved the upstairs, great drinks and food. The main floor food was mediocre at best, beer was warm and in plastic cups. Great for walking through but not for a meal

We had the best time tonight . We were there for music row happy hour and decided to go early so we could taste the food . We got Paradise  burgers single and double meat . The burgers were delicious and tasty.
We waited for a few mins to get our drinks but we understood they were a bit busy but Katlyn one of the supervisors made sure we were taken care of as well as our server Justin. We had a great experience!

My husband and I went to a performance of the Harry Potter music, live with the movie playing on a screen.  It was outstanding!

I was incredibly impressed by how well the orchestra played - there were times I even forgot the music was live; that's how seamless the performance was!  Excellent musicians, beautiful venue, and very interesting performances.  Perfect option for date night, to share with friends and family, or even as an introduction to music for kids!
The food is great !! The drinks are fabulous but most of all...Our server Andrew Davis rocks !! He made our visit great !!

The second worst experience I have had at a restaurant- the first was at this same place - signs indicating its Ok  to park if you are going to either losers or winners - I was going to winners (where I have been going for years and about 3x a week) but not anymore- I park where the signs indicate it is OK to park and let the front door man know if there is an issue please let me know he replies not a problem at all and I am halfway through my lunch when some jack ass comes over and asked if that was my truck which I replied yes and he says you parked in the wrooooooooooong spot - incredibly sarcastically and aggressive I would caution anyone attending to be aware of the shady security people!!

Five stars for fun! Definitely coming back soon for dinner! Our friends go on and on about the food here but unfortunately they were too busy. We'll be back! The band was great! Visiting Nashville? Must add this one to your places to go! Highly recommend!

I'm not too sure why they've gotten the "best burger in Nashville" award because really, their burgers were at best, mediocre. I definitely don't think their prices are great, over $14 for a burger (extra cost for bacon and cheese!) and even a charge for fries! Not just that, I barely even got a handful of fries (9 to be exact) and they just weren't that good. 

The wait for my ridiculous, over 45 minutes and there is was hardly anyone in here. It's constantly loud and I feel like everyone is yelling at one another. 

Overall, I'm not overly satisfied with this place. Not worth it.
OMG. Best chicken I have ever had!  I ordered the quesadilla not expecting much. Wow!  Will come back before we leave Nashville!  Way to go Blake!!

We were enjoying the Music City Brewers Festival and visited the Tennessee Brew Works tent. As a craft beer lover I had tried Basil Ryman before and wanted to meet the people involved in its birth. The place was a buzz of activity, pun intended, and we met McKenzie. A great kid from Texas who works for the brewery and really believes in the place and it's owners. She spoke to us about the brewery, it's beer and the people who work there being the best of the best. We were impressed. I asked her about the swag and how I could acquire a shirt. I made a deal with her that I would put a very truthful review on Yelp if she could get me a shirt. She agreed but we would have to go to the brewery to get it. 
      After the festival we walked the .9 miles to the brewery. It's a great place with an industrial feel. I ordered the flight and we sat outside on the upper deck. The beer here is the real deal and the atmosphere was friendly and family like. 
     Mckenzie took some time to sit and talk with us, hooked us up with shirts and in the end got us a ride by using the Lyft app. All and all a great day that ended with some great beer and a meeting with some of the nicest people you could ever ask for. This place is a definite "have too" spot when we go to Nashville.
Music and drinks were good...however, the food was a disappointment! No flavor and was warm to cool in temperature. Blake, you're my homie, I love you, but the food needs help!

Sat on the rooftop here, Friday around 5:30 pm.  Managed to snag a high top table within viewing of the music stage.  Beautiful rooftop, loved the atmosphere and the decor.  We ordered nachos and wings, excellent food, service a little slow, but hey it was ok, we were on vacation.  Total time from ordering to serving was an hour, we enjoyed the music while waiting. would definitely come back!

One star just so that I can write a review . 30 min wait to be seated which was totally acceptable ... we were sat at our table with only 2 menus to share for our party of 7 ok I'll share no big deal. Ordered our food and 45 mins later no server no update and no food .. server dropped off silverware and 3 napkins for all of our place settings ok maybe she's busy no refill on drinks or water . A member of our party actually got up to get a pitcher of water to refill for our party . Our sever finally stopped the table to let us know the food would be out shortly didn't communicate didn't apologize . 30 mins later one hour and fifteen minutes after we placed our order and we were told the kitchen printer was down and had no idea when our food would be out . Communication is key and if she had kept us informed we would have been more understanding . We got up and left , no food and still hungry . The manager was no help at all as she seemed to be unaware of what was going on . The worst experience ever !!!!!

We have been to Ole Red several times. All during CMA Fest, so you can only imagine how busy it is. Our first trip into Ole Red was for a meal. The food was okay...which was disappointing because it was expensive. We ate on the rooftop, which was the high point of that visit. It has an amazing view of all of Broadway. There is plenty of seating and two bars on the rooftop.

Our other visits have been to trying to get into free events at Ole Red. There will be a long line of get in. Sometimes it wraps around the building. Don't let this defeat you. It will be worth the wait. We waited for two and half hours (with the line starting at the Lookout wrapping all the way around to Whiskey Bent) to see Chris Young. Once we got in we moved to the side of the bar with the gift shop stuff. We were three people back from the stage. It is a very up close and personal venue. We have waited for three shows like this. Each one was worth it. 

Insider tip: if you are there for a show and they are making people go in the Lookout entrance. Once you get inside the downstairs area make your way over to the gift shop area. It's less congested and you can get really close to the stage. People don't move over there for some reason.

Don't do it. One star because our server was lovely.   Otherwise do not come here.  Overpriced.  Had to ask manager if I could have cheese on the side - good news he decided he'd allow it tonight.  I cook better than this place.

This is probably the worse bar I have ever been to, which is bad since I frequently travel. The bar was severely overcrowded. They blocked the exits & only allowed you to exit through the entrance door. This was not only inconvenient, but also extremely unsafe. My friends & I had to push through a crowd full of intoxicated people, which was almost impossible & very unpleasant. To top that off, the bartender was rude & threatened to throw out my drink because I turned by back on my drink while someone asked me something. I understand her concern, but maybe letting me know to be more cautious instead of telling me you are gonna throw out my drink would have come across a little better. I will not be returning here nor would I recommend it.

My late wife and I started coming to the Symphony at over ten years ago and I have continued to attend. We long ago decided to buy the Thursday night series as that way our weekends would remain free. There are now seven concerts a year on Thursdays; I buy two tickets and have had the same excellent seats for years. 

I really like my salesperson, Misha Robledo, who is helpful and has always called me if I haven't called her, so that I can be sure and keep my favorite seats.

Thursday night concerts begin at 7 PM while Friday and Saturday performanances start a 8. I like that schedule as I get home earlier, though it makes it more difficult to eat dinner before. Before the Great Flood of 2010 revealed the precarious finances of the Schermerhorn Center, we usually ate dinner in the restaurant there. They had a buffet where the food was great and when you were finished, you could easitly waddle in to your seats. It spite of the fact that it was expensive, and usually full, it was a money-loser and had to be closed.

Now Dream Girl and I eat at the deli by the gift shop. We get a tuna salad sandwich and two bags of chips ($10) and two glasses of wine ($20 with tip) and are plenty full. In nice weather we can sit outside.

As Nashville's "It City" status has grown, it has become more time-consuming to get downtown. We often have delays especially on hockey nights across the street at the Bridgestone. I always use valet parking though there are nearby garages with lower rates. Valet parking is $27, but with a season ticket you get a discount card and it's $22.

I have never attended anything other than the Nashville Symphony concerts, but there are events there nearly every day it seems. It's a beautiful building inside and out with seemingly excellent acoustics. We look forward to our concert evenings.

I don't do reviews very often and when I do it is for a reason. This place is great from the beer, food and entertainment. The food is amazing. My daughter had the fish tacos and they were great. Then me and my wife split and shared the pulled pork sandwich and the grilled cheese. The pulled pork sandwich was excellent. The grilled cheese blew my mind and is probably my favorite meal on this trip so far.

My boyfriend and I were celebrating my birthday in Nashville and came across Blake Sheltons bar on Broadway. We love Blake!! Hate his bar... the bartenders were very rude. We had been drinking all day down Broadway (responsibly of course) and we did get drinks at Ole Red, but we like to drink some water between drinks. Not only did we get declined by a female bartender first, but when we asked a male bartender also working that night  thinking she may have just forgotten... he too ignored our request!! Absolutely ridiculous. If we are spending money there, there should be no reason we cannot order water especially when they are not busy at all!! We will not be going back, but we will continue to listen to Blake's music, that's it. (FYI, we did tip on our drinks we ordered too)

What a find! They have a good selection of good beer which is great, but the FOOD! Not many brewery's offer food and when they do it seems like an afterthought. Not this place! I don't write reviews often, but this deserves a 5 star review! I got the 5 beer burger and my husband got the P.B.L.T. Both were insanely good. It's a bold statement but I think it's the best burger I've eaten to date. Definitely top 3 anyway. Which was a huge surprise as I wasn't expecting much from a brewery. The fries were good as well! They serve them with basil ryman ketchup and that was delish. (Basil Ryman is one of their beers). The service was top notch, great music selection, nice patio, overall an excellent experience!

I have been to many Margaritaville restaurants.  My husband is obsessed.  But this location needs to have major improvement.  We stopped by and a portion of the ceiling near the bar had leaked pretty bad.  It was closed off.  The sign in the dinning area had letters that were out.  

Had the fish tacos.  It was terrible.  Overcooked to the point it felt like I was eating cardboard.  The rice and beans had absolutely no flavor.  The food was pretty bad.  

The bartenders were good.  They kept with the crowd and were very efficient.  The entertainment was good too.  Loving the talented, unknown artists. 

I would stop by for a drink and to listen to the music, but I won't order food at this establishment.
Fun environment, good staff and multi levels. This is a great bar and pub in Broadway. Amazing music and part of Gaylord Entertainment do an ownership that cares about its guests.  Fun experience.

If you haven't been to Bridgestone Arena and you live in Nashville, then what is stopping you? This arena is the hub for concerts, Preds games, and other miscellaneous events (my friend is a fan of the monster truck show they do there...bless her heart). This stadium is located in downtown Nashville on Broadway, making it highly accessible and an easy place to plan other things after a night there. The arena is clean, has friendly staff, good food/drink options and decent prices. They have plenty of restrooms and they are well-kept. 

My favorite occasion to visit Bridgestone is definitely for hockey to see the Predators. Since the Preds made it to the Stanley Cup final last season tickets have gone up but there are still some chances to get reasonable prices occasionally to games. Other than for hockey I've been to see a Randy Travis tribute concert which featured Garth Brooks, Allison Kraus, Wynonna, Josh Turner, etc. This event was fabulous, one of the best concerts I've ever been to. 

As far as venues go, Bridgestone is one of my favorite I've been to and I will continue to keep coming back! Whether you are a tourist visiting Nashville or a local, Bridgestone is a must.

I'm a regular attendee of the Nashville Symphony. The symphony itself is top notch. The musical quality has been well-recognized (including Grammy awards), and the programming is extensive and varied. While including the classics of the symphonic repertoire, the symphony also aggressively promotes American music and new composers. This has broadened my musical horizons with the result of greater enjoyment. While I primarily attend the classical series, the pops programming is strong with an exceptional conductor, Enrico Lopez-Yañez, who is an asset in a very musical city! 

The building itself is a work of art in its own right, with small local touches honoring the some of the symphony's patrons (look for the influence of horseshoes and coffee beans!). The concert seating is roomy and comfortable with excellent lines of sight. I've sat in most all parts of the audience and never had a bad seat! (Photo is from the Founders Circle, my favorite spot.) There are sufficient and well-located bars and restrooms. The only drawback is minimal dining options (the sandwich bar, catered by Urban Cookhouse, is perfectly serviceable though not extensive), but there are many excellent restaurants in walking distance. Parking at the Pinnacle building is convenient and reasonably priced considering the location. 

A special round of applause to the box office staff who are perpetually friendly and helpful with any of my requests!
Reasonably priced drinks in a lively casual atmosphere. Constant great live music. You may difficulty finding a chair.
The slowest food ever.........  and then the food showed up...... fucking awful. Avoid at all cost. Shitshow!

Took my 13 year old daughter who is a avid guitar player. The atmosphere, live music and food is great. The service on a Wednesday night was awesome for a touristy place in the touristy part of Nashville. It was all great until we walked 2 steps out the door. My daughter forgot to get a couple of Ole Red stickers for her guitar case so we turned around and proceeded back inside and the guy working the door was a complete A-hole.. he told us she (my daughter) was not allowed inside. I told him we walked out less then 30 seconds prior. I wasn't total douche but I did express my displeasure in his warped logic. In a total dick move he told me that "after 9, NO ONE was getting inside without getting past him first." I was like, Really? I pulled out my Texas ID which turned out to be my license to Carry which looks identical to a Texas drivers license. Either way it is a valid a form of ID which Tennessee recognizes. He became an even bigger Dick and told me that he wasn't accepting my license to carry(mind you, the age to own one is 21). I said my mistake, and pulled out my actual ID. After 5 minutes of this douche stroking his own ego didn't impress me. I finally got back inside and bought all of $5 worth of stickers located 5 feet inside the front door. Tool 3 minutes to complete. We had a good time but because of a sawed off little egotistical douche with a bad attitude who happens to be as wide as he is tall, kind of out a damper on it the fun. All in all, we had fun but they need to remind their security that they are not guarding a lowlife establishment and to use common sense when needed.
Food was very mediocre, and the band was more like a karaoke band! The lead singer actually read the words to one song off his phone!! So disappointed!!

Came in early afternoon on cold day. Hoping for Irish coffee... they were out of coffee. Otherwise service was prompt and friendly. Food looked really good with generous portions. Less hipster vibe and menu than Luke's place across the street. The sound system was better here too and the band was good. Overall, a good experience.

First time coming! 

First walking in felt like a winner, especially getting two adult caprison drinks! 

After trying to give with the band I couldn't handle one more second in this bar, definitely did not feel like winner.

Alright, first just take a moment to look up and listen to the song this place is named after. It is every country song rolled into one; love, love gone bad, prison, and a hunting dog. At least then the wall of bottle caps that make a face of a dog will make more sense when you visit. This place is country, but it is a upscale side of country. You find that out immediately when you walk in the front door. The stage has a massive screen behind it with the artist's name on the bottom half and a live feed on the top half. LED lights are in full effect and the sound is crystal clear. There's a dance floor in front of it and a full bar behind the tables. It is top shelf. If you look up, you will see there's a balcony on the second floor so they can listen in as well. 
     The elevator will get you to the rooftop bar and seating area. Now realize that you are atop a four story building. The view of the city and a glimpse of the bridges await you. They have it setup where dining is inside, the bar is outside and there are stools facing out along the edges. When I looked at the bar list, I was impressed. Every category (but especially whiskey and bourbon) had great offerings. Of course you have cocktails as well. I will mention that quality comes with a price, which is reflected on the cost. So just be aware.
     The place has a gift shop as well as private rooms for dining and large groups. Although there is no Blake Shelton sighting (it's his restaurant), the artist on stage was working the crowd and singing "I got friends in low places". My night was made right then and there. I will be back.


*Insider's Tip
-Just head to the roof. Unless the band playing is one you really want to see, get your food and drinks up top. Same selections and far better view. Also, you can do reservations via their website.

The Spotify House at Ole Red during CMA Fest this weekend has been INSANE! Being a Nashville local, I'm so excited to check this bar out on a "regular" weekend. 

Obviously they won't have headline names playing during a regular weekend, but the stage area is such a great concept for live music. Intimate and close with the band, maybe 200 or 300 people packed in for people like Old Dominion, Cassadee Pope and Brantley Gilbert.

Can't review the food cause I didn't eat here, but the beer was a good deal (16 oz PBR for $5) and the place was very clean especially given the amount of traffic they had coming in and out during CMA Fest!

This place is underwhelming!!!! Food was over cooked and dry and the service was sub par. 
100s of other local choices. 
AVOID AVOID AVOID !!!!!

Saw this restaurant/brewery on the. Travel Channel. I held onto the name of the restaurant knowing I was spending a long weekend in Nashville in October. I ate the Best burger I've ever had and the fish tacos loaded with such a delicious coleslaw so yummy. Also enjoyed the wings. Definitely give it a try
Terrible service and didn't receive an order for over an hour. And only got comped for one dish out of 5

In Nashville on a family reunion of sorts. One aunt (who will remain nameless because she may or may not have a restraining order meant to keep her away from Blake Shelton) casually insisted that we head to (stalk) Ole Red for dinner (possible Blake sightings).

Upon arrival, our party of 10 was told that we had a 1 hour and 45 minute wait to be seated together or 1 hour if we were willing to split up. We agreed to sit wherever they had seats and hit the bar. 

The live music on the main stage really helped the time pass... so much so that we were actually seated as a group on the second floor within 45 minutes. 

After my aunt returned from "scoping out the joint" we sat down to some tasty apps and entrees. Our waitress was attentive, friendly, and patient with my aunt asking her what Blake smells like. The food-runners screwed up one meal, but quickly made it right. 

All in all, a good dining experience, but shy of incredible. Incredible would have been Blake serving the food to us himself, while dressed in tight jeans and a plain, white, slightly see-through t-shirt. 

My aunt stole my phone and wrote that last bit. Sorry.

Wow. I'll add to the punchlines. Please don't waste your money or time here. "We only serve bottled water." I guess the sink doesn't work here. These guys are up-charge champions. The only reason to go here is if every other restaurant around it is closed (which is how we got stuck here.) Mediocre is the kindest description of this food I can come up with. 

I can't imagine this place will stay open long.
Loved the rooftop bar! Probably the best rooftop bar in Nashville! Loved the speciality drinks as well!

First place we ate in Nashville.  Two of us ordered the Redneck Nachos.  As good as any I've ever eaten.  It was a generous portion that we could only finish maybe a quarter of.  Next we had the impossible burger with sides of french fries and onion rings.  Excellent.  Service was likewise excellent.  Luckily they had two acoustic guitars players so we could hear each other during lunch.  We did go back for dinner a couple of days later but the band was way too loud.  I'm going with the 5 stars because you'll know if the music is too loud before you commit to eating there.
Great atmosphere, beer, games and service! It was a great way to spend my last day before the journey back home.

The worst service & management I have ever dealt with. A group of us were there for the first time...as it was our first time in Nashville. Thought we would try this place. It eas aweful. By the time we got out first round of drinks we had been waiting over 30 min at least. Our server was terrible. Ot was not busy & she was not attentive to us at all. We ordered our food & it was less then edible. Not even close to what we expected. The server then brought the manager over. Through the entire meal i did not get the beverage I ordered before I even ordered my meal. I sat with NOTHING to drink. The manager finally came over & started the conversation off by saying " before you all jump down my throat...she is a good server." I said.."ummmm i wasnt having an issur with her. My issue was that we have waited for beverages that we never received & i ate part of my meal & still have nothing to drink."  He was rude & defensive. He said he would bring my drink & still never did. Her never came back to the table. We all decided to pay the bill & leave. Our bill was $400.00. He didnt offer any discounts...he didnt act like any other manager I have ever encountered. Usually of there is an issue, the manager tskes good care of the patrons...this guy was absolutely terrible! We will NEVER go back. While we were there for 4 days we told others about our experience & were told by several they had heard bad things aboit the place. Wow...i dont see this place lasting st all. We expected more from a place with Blake Sheltons name on it!!!!

Our visit was April 11th 2019 at about 7pm

I was at Ole Red on the afternoon of 8/10. I am compelled to write this review because the bartender that was working on the second floor that day (Tim) was operating like a well oiled machine. We were seated at the bar for about two hours. He never stopped moving. He was constantly taking care of people in a timely fashion. He was also very friendly while doing so despite being so busy. If he was frazzled, there was zero sign of it. I didn't see anyone helping him aside from the occasional bar back refilling his ice for him. It was super impressive. This Yelp Elite gives Tim two enthusiastic thumbs up! As for the establishment, I really enjoyed the fried pickles and peach whiskey tea cocktail I had. If I am ever in Nashville again, I would definitely put Ole Red on my list of places to visit!

Great appetizer, and great drinks. Our server was extremely attentive abd friendly. The only down side was the overpriced everything. I got the a drink that was 10$  but in all honestly it was probably worth only 7, and it wasn't very big. On top of we got the pretzels as our appetizer and we only got 4 pretzels and 2 small sides of dipping sauce. The mustard sauce would have been better if it was honey dijon mustard instead of just plain mustard.

Hilarious that Ole Red claims to have a executive chef(what a joke!)when they are serving low level fried garbage. What a mistake it was to order food here all 4 us totally disappointed with the horrible mess we received from the kitchen. Without the great live music and our positive server it would be the lowest score

Beer was really refreshing after walking around all day in that Nashville humidity. "Walk the Lime" was my favorite brew. Cool atmosphere and the live music was great too. The staff are friendly, but special shout out to Jordan, who went above and beyond by hunting down a charger for my dead phone. Being from out of town your cellphone is an absolute life line (map, Uber, ect) so if youre reading this Jordan then special props!! I owe you a beer if you're ever in Richmond Va!!!

Havent had a bad experience yet. 

The Cajun Chicken wrap was superb! The best Hot Chicken I have had in Nashville, no joke.  Homemade Mac and Cheese is the epitome of comfort food - To DIE for.  The wings! I am a wing connoisseur and have tried every wing in downtown Nashville, those made my #1 spot.  Cooked on the grill and if you want them hot, just ask.

The staff and bartenders always treat me like family and the $6 shot and a beer is my fav way to go. 

Highly recommended!

PS. They open for breakfast at 9am and continue serving breakfast until 12am every day!!!!

Absolute worst service in Nashville, Richard was slow and condescending, heard him refuse service to someone in our group because he didn't feel that he had tipped enough. When I bought two drinks right behind him and tipped 30% on a watered down drink. What a shame, this place was way below expectations and won't be on the return list next time in town. Where I'm from if you work for tips you earn it with personality and exceptional service not with your hand out begging.

Just got told buy a bouncer who I had a couple grab tab with if I did not tip the bartender at least $200 I would not bet back in. He said his name is as Jon. Well let me say I spend at least $10k In a bar but seriously this guy is a dick and will never be back.  Sorry Nahville. If you want a real convo happy to take.

Good food..served hot!  Our server was trying to talk up his tip but not paying attention!  I had half of a ribeye left. Half of the potatoes  a biscuit that I asked to be wrapped and he said he misunderstood.  I guess it went in the garbage!!  Good food..not so much for the server Aaron!!

This was by far the best food we found at any of the Bar/Restaurants on Broadway! Their wings were some of the best I've ever had! Great nachos! Another night I had the pig & cheese(Fried bologna sandwich). Fiancé had the blue tick Burger! Again best We've ever had! Mac & cheese was delicious too! We ate there during CMA Fest and caught performances by Rascal Flats & Maddie & Tae! As well as some up and comers! Great place in general.

Worst bar on Broadway. Asked what was in the specialty drinks on the chalkboard. Waitress didn't have any idea. Then brought us an extra drink we didn't ask for. Admitted she messed up, then put it on our bill & refused to take it off even though nobody drank it. Waitress was extremely rude about it & said it was "bar policy" that we had to pay for it. Wouldn't go back to this bar. WAY better experience next door at ACME.

Loved this place! Great food, entertainment, and service! Only thing, bathroom is located on the second floor:(  but everything else was great! I love tator tots, so I really loved the homemade ones here. I split the Nashvillian burger with my wife and it was perfect. We had the Southern tator tot poutine for an appetizer. Thought it was really good(added some hot sauce!) mmm. The view from the Lookout (rooftop) bar is amazing!

It seems like there are a lot of very varied experiences and reviews of this place, but I thought it was solid, and as my first Nashville culinary experience, set a high bar.  We ordered the nachos, and I had their burger, which was advertised as being voted the best burger in Nashville.  It did not disappoint.  It was cooked rare, the way I asked, was well seasoned, and was just a damn good burger.  The nachos were pretty solid, albeit small.  I wish we'd have been there for some live music, but it was noon on a Friday, so it wasn't really prime time for bands with day jobs.

Prices weren't bad for drinks, service was prompt, and they have a nice beer selection.  I'll come back!

Our experience here was great. So we came back a 2nd time. The first time we enjoyed the live music from the 2nd floor with good cocktails and nice atmosphere. The 2nd time we came back later and enjoyed the rooftop bar with music and good cocktails. Definitely glad we stopped by and would recommend.

THESE WERE THE BEST FRIES I'VE EVER HAD. The shoestring fries were slightly battered, drawing extra crisp to the already maximized surface area of the skinny potato sticks. A spice blend lightly sprinkled on the fries along with a special basil-infused ketchup made this plate of fries extra special.

Oh, and the beers were also delicious. ‍

1. Fries + Basil Ryeman Ketchup
2. Flight of Beers:
(a) King Chestnut (American Chestnut Brown Ale; 5.6% ABV) Fall Seasonal. A silky smooth brown ale, made with real American chestnuts, rich with natural roasted nutty aromas and flavors.
(b) Walk the Lime (American Wheat Ale; 5.4% ABV) Summer seasonal. 100% wheat beer with fresh lime zest. Subtle notes of peach, passion fruit and watermelon.
(c) Southern Wit (Belgian-Style White / Witbier; 6.0% ABV) This unfiltered Witbier delivers subtly complex notes of tangerine, pear and honey using natural ingredients including chamomile, coriander and fresh orange zest.
(d) Mangifera Indica (Mango India Pale Ale; 6.3% ABV) This beer starts with a vivid orange hue with plenty of juicy turbidity! The Norwegian Kveik yeast imparts a slight funkiness on the nose, followed by tropical flavors such as tangerine and mango with a balanced, lingering finish. Drink up and enjoy, because like summer... it will be gone before you know it!
(e) Patsy Clineapple IPA (Pineapple India Pale Ale; 5.1% ABV) This citrus forward IPA has soft notes of pineapple on the palate with a subtle crisp and lightly funky finish. The Kveik yeast imparts some wonderful fruity esters that balance beautifully with the 500+ pounds of real pineapples in this small batch. Our summer toast to a true Nashville legend!

Top music joint on the strip. We went to numerous places and this was by far my favorite with two performers (one on each floor) which were exceptional! Great job Blake as your spot will defeneitly be my go to when I'm in town from Miami.
The band and music was mediocre at best and asking for id for a 63 year old , really!

We stopped in for drinks and to listen to some music at this fun little hole in the wall and had a great time. The band was a bluegrass group and they were really great. Definitely worth a stop in for drink and good music.

I just saw August Burns Red here and the venue was excellent! The employees in the restrooms were really courteous and professional, it had multiple ATM locations, the venue had tons of room, and great food options to choose from. The security staff outside was friendly and it took no longer than 30 seconds to get checked and have my ticket scanned to get in. You can tell they take pride in their venue as the whole place was really clean, especially the bathrooms. And there are plenty of places to park close by, so that isn't something you have to worry about. So all in all, I had a pretty good experience and would definitely go back to another show here. Keep up the good work!

Good beer and even better food. The five beer burger was one of the best burgers I've ever had! I love the thin crispy fries they have too! Cool environment and great service also. I definitely recommend checking this place out!

The newest,  hottest bar/restaurant owned by the one and only Hot Blake Shelton.  We stopped by for afternoon drinks /wine and a few appetizers. Wound up on the  rooftop with the picturesque view of Nashville.  The rooftop bar is unique, modern, very inviting and comfortable.  We ordered parmesan broccoli, and cinnamon roasted carrots with goat cheese and pistachios, both were very good. The appetizers went well with our bottle of prisoner.  James/security, Sarah &  Brittany our servers were very accommodating.

I have been to several concerts here some of them were great others the sound wasn't all that good.The drinks/food is expensive,and you have to pay extra for handicap seating and all they did was pull out a chair on the lower level.The concert was great but besides Municipal where are you gonna go to see a really big act?

Cool college bar, split up into Winners & Losers, I didn't get the point between the two but I guess it was a cool concept. If you want a good ol hole in the wall college type spot, this is the one. It's on a cool little strip of bars, its full of drunkies, but its a fun night out to let lose.

I almost gave this place 5 stars....I think it has the potential for 5 stars (and really, my rating is probably a 4.5). It's a great layout--open air patios seating, even indoor is brightly lit and "fun". There's a pretty solid craft list of constants and rotations (I assume all brewed in-house). We ordered three flights of five between the four of us---so 15 5oz pours to sip over the course of a meal! Each was delicious but I think my personal favorite was the sweet potato stout. 

So good-great beer at decent prices in an awesome atmosphere--what takes it up a notch is the food. We each ordered the hot chicken sandwich which was absolutely delicious. While not the spiciest or "truest" example of Nashville hot chicken I've ever had it was simply great regardless, great breading, great sauce, excellent bun, perfect pickles...served with a heaping side of super-crispy super-thin greatly-spiced french fries and a house-made ketchup. 

So why not 5 stars? It's close, as I said. I'm sure if I'm back and give the burger and the fish tacos a go I'll be even more inclined to inch toward the 5 star. The main hold back for me is just the limited menu as it is rather small---some soups and salads, a few sandwich choices. I get the point of a limited menu--better to have a few things you do excellently than a ton of things that are mediocre---but just a few other unique, interesting options on the food menu would send this one to the top.

While we were there the Travel Channel was filming an episode of "Food Paradises" so look for that soon.

We host our conference at Marathon every year, we love it!!! Dave and his team make sure we have everything we need. Casey is great with sound and caters to our needs. The team hangs our lights and is on call during the whole event. The space can be transformed into anything elegant and bright!

Wow. We walked in here, never been here before, heard this all guy band and they really played some "Real" Country music..
I really enjoyed them. They had an electric guitar player. Awesome--
It's located right next door to Roberts, which is one of my favorites. But this is added to my favorite list.

I have eaten there twice now and was not overly impressed either time.  Brunch had a very eclectic menu and didn't have a lot of typical brunch foods which was disappointing.  I had the hot chicken benedict but it was not hot at all (almost flavorless to be honest).  Dinner was ok but just ok. The prices were in line with all of the other new celebrity restaurants.  There was live music but they were doing a lot of originals (I am okay with it but some people just want covers). The place was clean and the server was friendly.  I guess you could say it is a typical Broadway restaurant in the "new Nashville".

SMALL SEATS!!!!! We went to the rodeo this past weekend. Everything was great (food, drinks, bathrooms, cleanliness) except the SEATS! My 16 daughter & her friend fit nicely. But if you are bigger than a 20 year old you will probably go home with bruised hips and thighs. I literally had to sit sideways the whole time just to fit. How embarrassing...... I did notice a few seats where you could raise the armrest but who knows which seats those are when you are buying online! WHY would they have seats that most adults can not fit into? My husband looked at me when we sat down and said "what's going on? I don't think I can fit in this seat?"  He is 5'10" around 200lbs. Average 48 year old male. Just a little FYI for those buying tickets..... and not "model weight & size". Wish we had known when we bought the tickets.

I am shocked, *SHOCKED* that it took me so long to come to Tennessee Brew Works. I've bought cases of their "Walk the Lime" beer at Kroger before and certainly have heard about them for a long time. Since they are in kind of an odd area of town not super close to any other restaurants and bars it just hadn't been on my radar. 

A friend and I recently came for the bluegrass Wednesdays. They also had a deal which was 2 for 1 drinks (I think the higher gravity ones may be excluded from that deal). I got their wildflower which is a seasonal beer. It was really good. The fact that they have a drink deal and there is live music are two huge factors to draw me to a place. The band was also really good. While the music was not continuously playing, if you do want to have a conversation then inside is not really the place to be. Luckily they have an upstairs and downstairs patio, so when the weather is nice you can hear the music well enough to still talk with your friends. Although their layout is a little strange it is unique and it works. 

I would definitely come back and maybe try their food next time too. The music and the beer were both good and the service was good as well. TBW is definitely a cool brewery worth visiting.

These guys have some good brew!  I don't think they are distributing yet, but I was lucky enough to taste a couple of their beers at a private holiday party.

They have a Harvest IPA that was dry hopped but was not obnoxiously hoppy...I'm no hop-head and thought it was very pleasant.

I also tried their American Pale Ale which was fantastic.  It had earthy tones and some spices that I couldn't quite pick out.

They also had a California Steam and Belgium Wit that I didn't get to try.  It's funny how tough it is to talk to someone when they are giving out free beer, HA!

Great stuff.  I'll be looking out for their release which I think he said would be some time this spring.

We went here to listen to some rockabilly music, which was really fun. There were a good number of people dancing - I really wish I could get on their level - they are so energetic!

This bar is really chill; it kind of looks like a dive bar with all the cool and quirky decorations and Christmas lights.. but not really so divey. It just had a lively and fun vibe overall. Bartenders were fast to get drinks, which were pretty cheap too! Shoutout to the guy who bought shots for an entire bachelorette party, which apparently I was in, even though I really wasn't HAHA.

Went here for lunch super packed. Live music at the front. Service could be better. I ordered nachos with steak and uptown margarita. When I got my nachos I seen no know meat. When I ask the server I was told I couldn't hear you I just put ground beef (strike one). The only thing good was the margarita. Then it took  20mins to get the bill. If I do go it will be only for drinks. Also the nachos were 16.00 with one scoop of meat and a plate full of chips.

You get very big appetizers and entrees. We only waited around 30 minutes on a busy day and the host accommodated our party size. The food is good, nothing to complain about. The music creates a great atmosphere. I would suggest visiting to try the food and get a few drinks.

We came here for lunch around 11:15AM on a Saturday. Upon entering the bar was barely filled with maybe 2 other couples and a large party of 8. After sitting and ordering just water, the waitress informed us that it could take a long while to get our food because the large party was being served, a couple was being served, and there was only one cook. She said we could order an appetizer and maybe get it quickly. So my boyfriend and I decided to leave, but not before we were still charged $4 for 2 waters. Awful customer service.

This is a pretty great brewery. Larger than some (*cough* Jackelope *cough*), great beers, good food. They have a 2-for-1 deal during happy hour (not sure if it's everyday). They have indoor and outdoor seating (lots of outdoor seating)! They have a bar upstairs and a bar downstairs - so go up if the line downstairs is long (your tab can be pulled up at either bar). They also have live music sometimes! I went to meet my friend for a beer or two. And we were there for several hours and four beers...all in all, a great place!

We planned our trip to Nashville around a Foo Fighters concert we attended at Bridgestone Arena. 

At first look, the arena is impressive. It's location is great, right in the heart of downtown and there are a lot of vendors inside and outside. I was actually really impressed by the number and variety of food options. It also looks pretty modern inside and out. 

However, once we got to our seats--yikes. It's obvious they tried to pack in as many as possible, with no regards to their customers. The seats are small and cramped. I am an average size person and I felt like a sardine. My boyfriend's friend, who is a larger person, could not comfortably sit at all. He's not 500lbs. He's just a larger person. To make matters worse, the hand rests do not move, so even if you wanted to accommodate a larger friend by letting them share part of your seat space, you can't. 

We actually went to Guest Services to see if they could do anything to help us out. While the woman there did provide us with handicap seating (folding chairs), she was also kind of passive aggressive about it ("Not everyone can be a size '4' like me.") Okay, thanks.

Once we sat down to enjoy the concert, I looked around and saw that most people looked uncomfortable or wedged in their seat. This is ridiculous considering the price we all paid for our tickets. I would've been upset if that were my experience. 

Other than that, sound and view of the stage were good.

Great Venue!  I purchased the Tito's Lounge Experience, and honestly it was not worth it.   The bar only has 2 types of beer, they can't run a tab, and unless you have the two tables on the end by the wall, you can't see a thing because the speakers are in the way.   We ended up walking down and standing by the stage.  There are several tables on the main level if you can get there early to snag one.   The drinks are pricey, which is to be expected.  $6 for a tall boy can of bud light.  The bathroom has an attendant, so bring cash for that awkward moment.  They checked bags and wanded you as you came in.  There wasn't a purse size regulation.  Overall, it was a really nice venue, just don't waste your money on the Tito's experience.  Not worth it.

One of my favorite venues in all of Nashville. I have been to countless shows here... from the classical symphony to the pop series and everything in between. i've seen Bela Fleck, Amos Lee, The Music of Prince with the Nashville Symphony, Wizard of Oz in Concert, and Cirque de la Symphonie. Everything about the symphony is exquisite. Our symphony performs are the highest caliber. The staff are awesome and will get you to your seat with a program as fast as they can. The seats are comfortable whether you're sitting in a box or the balcony.

I have also attended conference here as well as my friend's wedding reception. Every time I come, it's transformed to the event but the beautiful building provides the best backdrop.

If you haven't been to a symphony performance, do yourself a favor and TREAT YO SELF! Check their website because sometimes they have packages or deals. We purchased a 5 show package which was super fun to mix and match shows throughout the season. You can also check out their free day of music! It will give you the opportunity to check out the building and a variety of musical performances. In 2017, they had it in October but I hope that you'll go before then. The symphony has performances perfect for families, dates, friend outings, and for just you! Treat your mind, soul, and ears to quality music this year!

Stopped by all the Honky Tonk bars and this cute little one was my favorite!

There was an amazing blues band with a female vocalist & violinist that just blew my mind. They were so charismatic and had such great voices. I believe they play every Sunday so definitely come check them out!

The bartender was really funny and down to earth which was refreshing.

The decor inside is very fun and casual with a lot of Nashville & country/bluegrass influence.

Definitely stop by here if you're in Downtown!

We spent time here with the kids while on vacation (yes, family friendly!). I loved seeing folks on the outside deck with their dogs. It's a great atmosphere.The beer was great- my husband and I love the state park ale- our in laws pick us up some whenever they pass through for visits back east. They also had live music- the woman was so good that I started recording her on my phone, because I thought someday I'll hear her on the radio and I could say I heard her live!

We love Blake Shelton and had to try his restaurant. Website said to make a reservation but a waitress on the second floor was able to get us a table. Service was prompt despite the crowd. We were impressed with the food, came out fast and was delicious!!! Cost was a bit more than we prefer to spend but was worth the experience. We checked out the roof top bar and were presently surprised. We would definitely come back next time in town.

I've never felt so compelled to review a business, but in this case I have to. Long story short, we got stuck at this location with a large group for 2 hours to have a 'quick' lunch. Just an FYI that if you're ordering pizza, it's a 2 hour wait and it's "out of their control". They also don't mention this until you wait an hour for it and ask what's going on. They also don't have servers and say that it's a courtesy if someone waits on your table. This restaurant is terrible.

Dear Nashville, 

You can try, but you will never keep the Blackhawks fans out. We will find the nooks and crannies and work our way around your little system of trying to keep us from coming. Oh, we will be there alright and that we were.

Last game of the Blackhawks season and what better way than to make a road trip out of it. Nashville fans were courtesy to us (probably because most of them brought their kids along) and we were the same to them. We cheer and jeered at each other and it was all in a light heart fun. However, the best part about Bridgestone Arena was that our tickets were affordable and it came along with all you can drink (beer) and all you can eat (hot dogs, popcorn, nachos, etc)! I love the United Center, but we would never be able to indulge in an all you can eat and drink deal for what we paid in Nashville, the cons of having a Championship team, but I wouldn't trade it for the world.

The employees at Bridgestone were friendly and served us as much as we wanted, I had 4 beers with me at one time. The arena is small, comparable to our All State (Rosemont, IL) so there is no bad seat. However, you guys sing America the Beautiful during Preds vs Hawks games because of all the thousands of Hawks fans that cheer during the National Anthem. I guess you can't embrace the fact that we are hooting and tooting for our team and country. It's okay we were still there and loud as ever.

Nashville you were fun and we'll be back.

BEST ROOFTOP ON BROADWAY!!!  Nice bar all in all too.  Didn't eat, but came back a few times for beers on the rooftop​.  You can see down both ways on broadway.  One of the places we came too that the bartender acted like they were doing us a favor by ordering drinks.  Not every bartender, just one (two different​ times on the roof).   I spend a lot of time in tourist areas​ and lived in one (Charleston, SC) for several years.  Tourism is a necessary evil for towns like Nashville.  Southern hospitality is expected.  

PS: Not a Blake fan at all, and still really enjoyed this place.

We stopped into National Underground as an option on the Nashville Pedal Tour.  As I was ordering a beer - I was told by one of my girl friends that we needed to go because the manager came over to them and said in an extremely rude tone "come on girls, get out of line for the bathroom and get a beer."  

Being that my family has been in the hospitality industry for over 25 years, I kindly went up to the man, asked him his role and let him know that he now lost 8 patrons of the restaurant who were going to be spending a lot of money.  He backed up what he said by saying "we were at a tourist spot on a Friday night" (mind you, the place was empty and it was 8:30 p.m. 

We left and went to Bootleggers next door, which was awesome! We later walked past, the bouncer said "best live music in Nashville" I looked inside, there were about 10 people inside - and I notion to the manager and said - "Worst GM in Nashville right there."

needless to say, I would NEVER recommend going there to anyone I know.  Best part is, this is owned by Gavin Degraw.... who really should take a look at the people who are representing him.

We were downtown for my best friend's bachelorette party and were headed to another restaurant but the wait was a little long so this place told us we could be seated immediately so we went in.. Needless to say by the score I gave the experience was the worst I have ever had!!

First off, it took about 15-20 minutes before someone came to get our drink order. I will say on the menu it tells you it may take awhile to get your food so I am glad it gave a warning. We had a group of 10 and we were there 2 hours before getting our food but we were prepared to wait. Fast forward to the end of the meal. The girl that buses tables came to pick up some plates while we wait to pay the check. I had my arm on the chair beside me and apparently she said "excuse me" a couple of times for me to move it and I didn't hear her. She proceeds to grab my arm and throw it off of the chair. I have never been treated like that in my life in a place of service... 

When our waiter comes to give the check he tells us our bill is $250 and he can't split checks. Granted we did have 10 people and I understand that BUT they should have told us up front instead of herding us in there and giving us a table. The manager was not willing to work with us and demanding we pay all at once. 

The food was less than impressive. I ordered a BLT.. pretty hard to mess up but my bread was completely burnt. 2 hours waiting on food for a burnt piece of bread.

Looking back we should have waited the hour for the other resturant.

I visited the street-level bar area of this establishment twice during Music Fest 2012.  On the first visit,  I had excellent service by an awesome bartender. I wish that I could remember his name.   

On the second visit, I had a different bartender (Craig)....interesting that I would remember *his*name, eh?  Well, Craig was the most rude bartender/waiter that I have ever met.  He got mad when my friend and I wanted to pay for our beverages as we received them and NOT run a tab.  Later, when my friend pointed out that he had forgotten to put salt on the "dressed up" beer that had been ordered,  he grabbed the" tab" glass from the bar in front of us where we were sitting, went and filled it about 3/4 full of salt, and then *slammed* it down in front of us.  He then proceeded to chew us out about not wanting to run a tab.  Well, we didn't need to run a tab at that point as we *left*.

I should have reported this right after it happened, but didn't.  I've tried to blow it off, but it still makes me angry when I think about how rudely we were treated.  I can't imagine him still working there as his attitude must have gotten him in more trouble down the line.  

Note to Courtney (the manager that I met a few months later ?)   I am the one who found your "card" and returned it to you.  I don't keep things that aren't mine and I don't lie about how I am treated. I should have shared this with you in person while I had the chance.

I didn't eat there on any occasion so can't comment on the food or food-servers so, to be fair, I will give an A-OK rating.

Came here with 7 friends in order to grab something to eat before we went out. I guess it was a little late for Nashville since most of the downstairs was too packed and they sent us up to the 3rd floor. It's where the rooftop bar is so they only serve light bar food there no meals. Honestly, they should just skip the food all together and just stick to drinks and the view cause the food was the worst food we had in Nashville. 

We arrived around 9:45pm and the kitchen closes at 10pm so the waitress wanted us to order ASAP which I get. So we decided to order a bunch of random things and share them. We also ordered drinks and she never brought mine out so I walked up to the bar and just ordered one myself since she didn't really come back to check on it. Also she never took it off the bill which we had to get corrected at the end.

For food we ordered: The giant pretzel (edible and a pretty safe bet for bar food), French fries (another safe bet and also okay), fried broccoli (which we all were unfortunately tasting for the rest of the night), the trio which comes with a bologna sandwich?, the calamari ( not in rings and very gross, do yourself a favor and just don't order this) and finally the burrata which has pimento cheese in the middle of it. Not one of us have ever seen that in our lives and we were very confused by it, no one ended up touching it either. 

Overall the experience was overrated and I wouldn't waste my time or money going back there again.

We saw a concert here a few weeks ago while visiting Nashville. The arena itself is very nice and has great tvs in the lobby and is located in a great section of town. The thing that is keeping this place from getting a 5 or even a 4 is they have the smallest seats I have ever sat in before. The arena seats are tiny. I realize I am a big guy but I am not that dang big. Everyone around us was backed in their worse than sardines. It is ridiculous. I wonder if any one else on here is complaining about it.

Let me start by saying I am a native to this area and I am a huge parrothead.  I have visited Margaritaville at both the New Orleans and Panama City locations.  So, needless to say, I had been looking forward to the one in Nashville.  I love my hometown and was hoping Margaritaville would be a great addition to our downtown strip.

The prices (at all of the locations) is really too high.  They are sooo busy all of the time that they should be able to offer the same food for a bit less than what they currently charge.  The drinks are expensive, too.  I didn't have a drink in Nashville, but had plenty in NOLA and at least for the price, they were made to be worth it.

I loved the food at NOLA and Panama City.  I would re-visit either of these. Good selections and very tasty (especially in NOLA, where most all the food anywhere you go is awesome).  The one in Nashville, however, leaves a lot to be desired.  Why did such a place as this open up and serve the same 'ole same 'ole that you can get all over town.  Interesting food is one thing that is hard to find in Nashville, but I promise, there is better just a couple of blocks away.  As far as Margaritaville goes, eat somewhere else.  Big River and even Hard Rock have far superior food to this place, including hamburgers.  It is at least a little better than Planet Hollywood.

Just go here for drinks and music.  At least they got this right.  Yes, I said the drinks are high, but all you need is a couple and you will be too.  ;)

Disappointing for a place in a city where Jimmy Buffett fans are so plentiful.
