Nothing like a beer to start your morning vacation off. I had a delicious King Cheatnut not exactly an October fest but it perfect for this October baby. The outdoor patio could be perfect if the rain was not coming down. We started our morning off here and headed to locate a brunch place and so
Many options just walking distance. Great location, amazing patio, and good beer.

Popped in for a drink and some live music and enjoyed both here! The place is huge, clean, and had great sound quality. Also, overall it just felt like the music they hired was of a better quality/more established than other bars nearby.

The drink menu didn't have what I was looking for, but they were very flexible in making a sweet-tea vodka and lemonade for me without it being on the  menu.

Service was so-so on a Monday afternoon they were not packed, I asked for water twice, and ended up tracking it down at the bar area myself after being ghosted the second time. Would have been happy to do that from the start if I knew that was the best place to get it!

Tip: The bathroom is on the second floor, in case you're a dumb-dumb like me searching every nook and cranny of the first floor to find it!

The blender drinks were so good! I got the Blueberry Pomegranate margarita drink and it was just the right amount of tequila! The prices aren't the best for these drinks... the cups alone were $8 and the refills were $14. The place was super sticky and the bathrooms were disgusting. The saving grace was the live music!

I was skeptical to try this place because I figured it would be a tourist trap, but I ended up really enjoying it! It's definitely pricey, but so are most of the bars and restaurants on Broadway. The drinks are great and worth splurging for! The waitress was super helpful and gave awesome drink recommendations. It was nice to have someone help us navigate the menu! 
We also ordered the spinach and artichoke dip and the chicken quesadillas. They were fine but way overpriced. Oh well! I think I'll stick to just ordering drinks next time I visit.

This place has a beautiful rooftop! The drink and food here is not that impressive but you're paying for the view and the live music. The artist performing when we came was very good and he took audience request, which was nice. The place was definitely full but not too crowded like other rooftop. It also had a more 'hanging out' kinda style, which means sitting down, talk and enjoy your cocktails. 

In general, I'd go back for the view and the life music.

Is there anything better than relaxing with a beer outside?! The guys who work here are passionate and so friendly, plus they have some darn good beer! Tennessee Brew Works is one of my favorite places to go in Nashville - so chill and relaxing. It's a bit off the beaten path, but once you've found it you'll realize it was worth the search.

If you know me, you know I love a beer sampler/flight. TBW has a sampler of 5 beers for $10. If you take their Saturday tour (offered a few times during the day), it will run you $12 but that includes the $10 flight. 6 beers is all they have on tap but that's plenty enough for me. If smaller portions aren't your thing and and you want a cold, refreshing pint, it can be done for just $5. All of their beers were 4.5-6.25% so nothing overly potent, but that's a good thing when you want to sit for hours having beer after beer on their patio.

Ahhhh, their patio. When I think of their patio, I get visions of unicorns jumping over rainbows with tiny kittens on their backs holding trays of brownies with no edges. It's that good. Since it's away from all the hustle and bustle of more busy areas in Nashville you don't have the congestion you may be used to at other spots. Sometimes people watching can be fun but when you need to just get away from it all, the TBW patio is where it's at. They have live acoustic music! I liked the playlist but once the live music started in the evening --- well that's where it's at.

And if you're lucky, you'll go on a night there's a food truck hanging outside. Other than a random food truck, they offer popcorn for $5 but no other food options. I'd think it's a bring your own food type of establishment.

Service was beyond top notch while we were there. Everyone there was so friendly and when we were seated outside, one of the guys actually sat down with us for a bit and chatted Chicago beers. I really enjoyed talking to him - he educated us on the brewery a bit and gave us some Tennessee Brew Works stickers.

Beer!!!!
They have a sweet potato stout! So cool! It was my least favorite of the bunch but still thought it was a solid 3 stars. The extra easy ale, basil ryeman, southern wit and cutaway IPA were all a strong 4 stars. I love a good witbier so Southern Wit was probably my favorite of the night.

This was the best craft beer I had in Nashville. This was the best atmosphere during my days in Nashville. This goes down as being top 3 places I went to in Nashville. It's only open Thursday to Sunday & usually closes at 8pm, except 6pm on Sundays - early closing so plan accordingly.

SiriusXM at margaritaville on a Friday. So, after standing outside in 45° weather for two hours, after being frisked by an aggressive looking rent a cop, we got in to see the show. Frozen, starving and tired we sat at the table and finally got to order. The food, as posted in the pictures below was marginal at best. The Volcano nachos were mushy and cold in the center. The pic and peel shrimp was actually tasty and plentiful. The lava lava shrimp was tasteless. All in all, the experience was somewhat grueling.

The SiriusXM radio show was fun and the crowd was lively. That made up for a lot of the restaurants shortcomings. This is a restaurant chain, Make no bones about it. They have a business model and a corporate plan and you get what you get. I have rated Margaritaville restaurants in Key West, Atlantic City New Jersey and in Miami Beach Florida. Except for nicer weather, they were all the same. But hey, the beer is cold.

Great experience. Server was personable and helpful. I had a burger and mashed potatoes. Both very good. Nice live music. A little bit of a wait to get seated (even though there was no wait, no one helped us right away) and a little longer wait for the food than typically as well. Overall though, good & recommend to others!
It was really cool to see the transformation from a old warehouse to what it is today.  Can not wait to see the final product, and try all of their creations.

Great beer, AMAZING food! Tried a flight of their stouts, all of which were tasty. Me and a friend shared their grilled cheese (with smoked apple butter) and hot chicken sandwich for dinner and it was seriously some of the best food I've ever eaten. All the employees were so friendly and welcoming, too. Next time I'm in Nashville I'm definitely coming back!

I had lunch here during their opening week. 
So far, I was pretty impressed. The food was good, the flow of the building is great, and it's one of the only places on Lower Broadway that doesn't blast the live band so loud that you can't hear the conversations of the people sitting next to you at the table. 

The view from the rooftop bar is wonderful of downtown, and I can't wait to experience it more on a happening night. I think this place is getting it right straight out of the gate, and it can only get better.

I'm ready to give it a few more chances and a few more goes as it keeps progressing! Great job on the place here.

Traveled from Baltimore and our Uber driver suggested this hidden gem! We took a tour of the facility and the staff was very knowledgeable and friendly. We did a sample board of the different beers which were rich in flavor! The food was delectable , I suggest the southern grill cheese! 
I also love the fact they use and support  local farmers! Don't miss out on this local hot spot when you come to visit! We will definitely be back!
Had a great time there last night! Our server Sydney gave the best service i've had in a while! She made the night enjoyable for everyone!

This review is for the Lexus Lounge. Who knew?!!? 
Who knew this place existed?!?!? Another reason to Yelp!!
Any event the Bridgestone Arena has, will have a benefit to purchase admission to the Lexus Lounge. Totally worth the price. Call the office. Price will be between 40 - 150 dollars per event. Also season tickets to Predators get access to this area. Who knew!!!

Amazing price for what you get. If you experience it once, you will realize it is worth it. I don't go to as many concerts as I used to before baby, so this is so worth it.  Dont' need to go to dinner before, and then pay for drinks when you get there. 
All there at once. 

Lexus Lounge. Nice, Wood and glossy and seats everywhere to co mingle. We ate before we went to concert. 

Tons of selections, Honestly, I was so excited I forgot to take pics.
Let's see, Pizza, Pastas, a few different kinds, desserts, pulled pork sandwiches, hot dogs, fruits and veges. There were 5 tables in all. I don't think I ate from all, I was too excited. Sorry. What I ate was GREAT! Really all the food was good. Would definitely pay for the extra to come back for ANY event. 

Drinks were free and readily available. I drink white wine. ONLY. Tip your server and they give you the LARGE CUP. What a kick

It was a concert and when I went back and forth to the lounge and the concert. 
It was easy and fun and seem less. 

Every single person I met at the Arena was nice and helpful. EVERYONE. 
Class act Lexus and Arena employees

The bartender we had made the whole trip worth it. My fiancé and I split the jambalaya, and it was the perfect! 

Service was slow, but again, our bartender kept us entertained even though we only ordered water and food!

Was here on New Year's Day 2013, and had a wonderful experience. My dad & I road-tripped from New York the day before and this was one of the only places open. We were sat immediately and our waitress came over right away. I had a chicken quesadilla and a margarita - I can't remember what my dad ordered. I do remember that we both had fantastic meals, and our server was absolutely amazing. The place was packed and yet she was friendly and attentive, but not pushy. Having been a server for 3 years, I know it's not easy especially when most of the patrons are hungover. Halfway through our meal a musical duo came in which was great and not something that happens often (at least mid-day) where I live. We stayed to listen a bit and our waitress still paid just as much attention to us even after we settled the bill and left our tip. She asked us where we were from, etc. and seemed genuinely interested in our answers. If ever in the area again, we will be back.

I've been listening/dancing my way across all of Nashville's music venues and Marathon Music Works is a fun one. There are a lot of indie artists who play here so don't expect to see T-Swift playing at Marathon. MMW is part of the Marathon Village which is a collection of businesses all housed under the same former Motor Works warehouses which built cars at the turn of the 20th century. 

The venue itself is quite large. There is a big bar area when you first walk in with tables and restrooms. It's a good lobby/waiting area if you want to hang before/after/during a concert. They setup merch tables off to the right of the stage. If you get claustrophobic due to large crowds it's okay there's plenty of space. There is no seating area though which is the only downside to this venue.I saw Taking Back Sunday here, fulfilling a long ago wish of a teenage self. They were lively and the atmosphere was perfect for them. As far as parking, there are a few pay lots but then some street parking if you are willing to walk a few blocks. 

I would definitely see another show here. Security was efficient, the bartenders were nice and most importantly the band was great and the stage was easy to see them.

We really enjoyed the vibe here, but the food was mediocre at best. We really enjoyed the live music, the central location, the fun/happy-go-lucky atmosphere here, but it seemed a little franchise-y with the inside store. Also, the draft beer selection was awful...lots of mass produced beers, very little craft beer options, and no draft IPAs.

I had the quesadilla and don't recommend it. The table next to us got a bunch of burgers which looked BIG and juicy and delicious -- so maybe get that!

I can't so much about this place, since the co-workers and I came here for just drinks.  And it was just 1 drink.  Since we were a large group, they sat us in the back with the other large groups.

For the most part, it looked decent.  It had nice ambience with enough lighting.  It had nice decorations around the place with palm trees, pictures, etc.  Overall, it wasn't too bad.  

Rating
Food:  n/a
Service:  4
Price:  3
Ambience:  3
Overall:  3

 Would probably come back if I come to Nashville.

beautiful arena with plenty of seating, food choices and alcohol on each level.  The prices are expected of a sporting event and in Nashville. was here for a concert and ill say that the concert prices are outrageous! floor seats were $1400 each! same band at another venue in another state, $163 for floor seats. Lets not even talk about the nightmare of parking and walking on the streets to get to the arena. Wish they had their own garage in order to park. seems it would be helpful to get people to come and spend money there.

First visit and, although seating was slow & hostess was grumpy, we had a nice visit; drinks and food were excellent; music was fabulous; prices reasonable; outstanding decor & friendly waitstaff. The Ole Red Onion burger was one for my top-ten burgers list; it was really exceptional. We will return!

I wanted to try this restaurant because I love margaritas and I like Jimmy Buffett. I thought the decor was awesome it gave you an island feel. There were fake palm trees fake lanterns and a tiki area. I thought the gift shop was overpriced $16 for a 10oz coffee cup . 

The drinks were ok but not great or perfect considering I was at a Jimmy Buffett themed restaurant and he is know for margaritas. I've had better at a steakhouse and I paid 1 price for a margarita and it came in the shaker so I can refill my glass at my table. So go figure I paid almost $20 for 2 drinks that weren't as great as expected and at the steakhouse I could of paid maybe $15 with enough drink to equal both of the ones I had tonight. I think I'd been better off just grabbing a beer and drinking it with my meal. 

Now to the food this was completely unexpected from a well know restaurant with a song called Cheeseburger in Paradise because burger was not this. I ordered it well and it seemed too dry and no flavor at all. The fries were ok but it's hard to mess up fries but I've kinda slacked on eating them anyways. My husband ordered the garlic bacon burger and he didn't have any garlic flavor at all and the only flavor he got was from the ketchup. Our fried pickles didnt have any flavor either just battered pickles with no seasoning. Here is the kicker of the meal. My daughter said her chicken tenders were too greasy. This is a kid who loves her chicken and fries and if she doesn't like the food it's a no go. 

The waitress was nice and it didn't take long to get seated but kinda took awhile to get our food after we ordered and it wasn't too busy. This was around 5p on a Monday night with WWE Monday Night Raw in town at the arena. Location is awesome being within walking distance to the arena and our parking garage but I think this is how they attract the tourist that come to town. I know next time I will research the local restaurants near the area before I decide based on a name. I know this is one place we will not go back to unless its just for a couple of drinks before an event.

Arriving to town early, I couldn't check in to my hotel yet so I walked the Gulch & found myself cooling off at TN Brew Works. 
As a frequent visitor to NashVegas, I've had TNBW beers before & since I've never been to the actual brewery before, I decided to check it out. 
The beers themselves are good but nothing mind blowing. What gives them the 5 stars is the quality of service. Everyone working the taproom was exceptional & were quick to chat. Some of the staff gave me tips on other Nashville establishments that I haven't went to as well as informing me that Jack White's Third Man Records was within walking distance, which I ended up checking off the bucket list as well! 
The next time I'm in town, TN Brew Works will definitely be on my radar.

I love Winners and Losers. I always am sure to book my trips to Nashville around Whiskey Jam on Monday nights. It's crowded, live music with locals and regular people instead of bachelorettes in fake cowboy boots and hats. Last time I was there they had a $15 bucket of Music City Light, not bad for 6 beers. 

Be  prepared to stand - tables are hard to come by in the main room, but the patio is good too. Make a friend, y'all are gonna get close.

This place has a lot of potential, but the lack of customer service here was very surprising. Was here with a group of 20 ppl and requested a game be put on one of two TVs on the roof, one of which was airing the end of a horse race. There were two other small tables on the rooftop, and the bartender insisted someone was watching the already over horse race. After asking the other two tables if they cared (which they didn't), we went and requested them to change it again. They instead changed it to Nascar because the bouncer wanted to watch it. We left shortly after with our deep pockets.

We came here for a work event and went on a brewery tour and had light bites and drinks. The food was really good! Definitely steps above simple "bar food", as they had a really delicious kale, beet and burrata salad, and wings, tacos, burgers, fries, etc and much more. They also had a couple kombucha options which were delicious for those that don't drink. I would definitely recommend this place for a corporate event, light bites/drinks or even a casual dinner spot. They also had live music!

Who doesn't love Christmas movies at Christmas time?
(Husbands who've been subjected to countless hours of Hallmark Channel please lower your hands, we understand) 
So what a brilliant idea it was for the symphony to host an evening viewing of an all time favorite - Home Alone. 
They seamlessly blended the live music directly over the score for the film & blew us away with a choir for the few songs in it.
The only negatives on the night are that the seating isn't what we've all become used to in modern movie theaters & I spent the majority of intermission in line to get a couple of bottles of water & returned to my seat empty handed at the bell with yet a dozen people between me & the bar.

Ohhh we loved it here, and just randomly found it on Yelp, so thank you Yelp once again!! We sat outside and it was beautiful, and got yummy beer and ordered their cheese board. It was REALLY good, and I am a connoisseur of cheese boards. Definitely will make it a place we try again when we visit next time. You should too!

Last night was one of the most mortifying experiences of my entire life. My review is not a reflection of the venue, as much as it is the staff operating. While waiting in the women's bathroom line, which for the entirety of the night was a consistent stream of 20 women at a time, I decided to take it upon myself to enter the men's bathroom as an alternative. There was no line, there were also no men occupying the bathroom. I understand fully that this, unfortunately for me was against marathons policy. There was no security guard present outside of the bathroom, I was never told or asked not to enter the bathroom. While inside, I was grabbed by a female security guard, so forcibly that it truly startled me. As she screamed "OUT,NOW" in my face, over and over she began to push me toward the door. I did not resist, I did not argue, I calmly told her "I am not intoxicated, I am not resisting you, can you please let go of my arm" to which she responded "No, you're out!!!" And continued to use force. I am thankful for the male security guard who intervened while barring witness to the aggression of the female security guard. He calmly and kindly asked me, "are you ok? I need to escort you out now". Allowed me to walk ahead of him, unguided, without force and with dignity. 
I am a professional, I understand that I violated marathons bathroom policy. I accept consequences for my actions. In absolutely NO way do I understand why I was treated like a belligerent, violent, or resistive person. She did not ask me a single question before putting her hands on my body and pushing me forward, toward the exit. There is no excuse for her behavior. I can not emphasize enough how deeply embarrassed and threatened I felt in this situation. 
The purpose of this review, is to shed light on security procedure. Questions should be asked, or statements should be made before using force. In no way did she attempt to mitigate the situation. In no way did she try to understand why I was using the men's restroom. She did not ask me to exit. She did not ask me to leave the venue. Her immediate, and only reaction was to use force. If her role last night was to prevent women from entering the men's restroom, she took it upon herself to trap them rather than redirect them. She took pleasure in using excess force. She enjoyed kicking women out of the venue. 
I hope that this review falls into the hands of someone who can make sure this behavior does not continue, and implements a strategy to prevent this from happening to others. There were several women outside who experienced something similar to my situation. It was not OK.

I recently visited here with a group of 6 and shortly after dinner, two members of our group who had eaten the taco salad we're sick to their stomach and spent a large portion of the rest of the night vomiting with food poisoning. Aside from that, we also had serving staff that was less than thrilled to serve us and seemed annoyed by the few minor requests that we had. I am not one to typically leave reviews but being that I often take other's reviews into consideration when choosing a restaurant, I wanted to inform others of our experience. We visited Margaritaville with high hopes but we were certainly let down. With all of the other great places to eat in Nashville, I definitely wouldn't recommend this one!

So I'll start by saying I did not eat here   
We went to music row happy hour to see buzz brainard (if you don't know how who he is good neither did i, he's the host of a Sirus country radio station). 
So I we waited about an hour around 3:30pm to get upstairs to see the show. We finally got in and it was packed. The energy was pumping.  It reminded me of like a college game day broadcast. People are drinking, dancing and eating. 
We were on a bachelorette party and they picked us to go live on the show.  It was a great experience for the bride!

A local friend of mine said to meet her and some friends here for Whiskey Jam on Thursday. It looked like a good time so we trekked it this way after dinner. Downstairs was packed for the jam sesh so we didn't actually spend a ton of time down there, but we did hang on the roof for a while. Luckily we snagged a table fairly early and even though it got busy, I could always get a round of drinks without a wait. It was a fun area to bounce around as we went to Losers next and then on to Kung Fu. Fun times on a Thursday night!
I love Margaritaville. The service was great just like at every other Margaritaville. Booze in a Blender is always good.  Live music is great too.

Though the wait time was undesirable, it was understandable for the time of day. Overall I'd say it was great. The live music was great and food was the same if not better. William made the experience enjoyable as well. Knowledgeable, really good conversation, as well as being great at his job! Highly suggest asking for him!  Recommend this place for anyone looking for a wide range of food choices as well as an eclectic atmosphere.

So there we were, some local Nashvillians downtown.  (I know... what?)  We were going to eat at ACME, but saw that it was closed.  What's this place next door?  Hmmm... seems interesting.  Then a guy standing outside tells us we should eat there.  The burgers are amazing, he says.  He claims they are the best burgers, voted on by the Nashville Scene (any local will immediately tell you this is false.)  Even though I knew this dude was BS-ing, I thought we'd give it a shot.  He also said he enjoyed it because, "they let me bring my dog and sit outside."  I looked the place up online as we sat down and as it turns out, this dude is the freakin' owner!  Dude, just tell me you own the place.  Don't make up a bunch of lies just to get us in your place.  Just say you own it.  If you don't believe in the quality of your own restaurant in order to give it to me straight, that says quite a bit about your character and your faith in your establishment.  

So we sat down.  Our service was awful.  Our waitress would take half of our order and then leave.  So my food arrived before friends had even ordered even though we were all sitting there.  

They made a big deal over splitting checks as well.

Oh, the food... right.  Decent.  Definitely not the best burger or wings.  Friends enjoyed the hot chicken, but not the best in town.  

I can't recommend a place that tries to deceive people.  Also, the bit at the top of your menu about the tap water being bad?  C'mon.

We only stopped in for a couple drinks and listen to live band but we only stayed for 1 drink. We went to the bar and where there were only 3 people sitting but we were never greeted by the young brunette bartender. I had to look at her and ask if I could order a beverage where she said , sure what would you like. She got our drinks and 2 of her friends arrived and she proceeded to talk about her boyfriend issues and his travel schedule. Our drinks were empty and she never asked for another drink so we left . I completely respect if they are busy and tending to many patrons but in this case that was not a factor. Atmosphere was a 5* but the service was 1* which makes it a never return for us.

Good beer. There's plenty to choose from.
Good food. With some vegetarian options.
Great patio. It's huge. Plenty of space for you and your tribe.
Live music. Great atmosphere.
I'm glad we stopped in while we were in town. I'm a fan.

Was in Nashville for a few days on a road trip with the girlfriend. We stopped here while wandering around Broadway late on a Monday night.

Most places in Nashville were pretty dead at that time, but Layla's was definitely alive. They had a great bluegrass band, cheap drinks, and a lot of locals and people dancing (line dancing, I think. Definitely was not skilled enough to join in). We even made a few new local friends while at this bar. This bar is one of the best places on Broadway.

I try to find the best in every restaurant, some are just harder that others. To be fair, I went to Margaritaville on a Saturday night, after 11:00 p.m.,  after a show. I felt like our waiter just gave up. Everything was so slow. I ordered the Cheeseburger in Paradise and apparently the chefs gave up too. Zero seasoning. Now, for the good part: the French fries. They were on point. Look, if you like watching drunk bridesmaids dance to mediocre 90's country songs, have at it. If you want decent food and service after 11:00 pm, you may want to try Waffle House.

The drinks were amazing, the food was so so for the price, but it was worth the money for such great service. Ethan from FL was our server who was kind, efficient, and fast working. He made it feel like home and was attentive to our needs. Thank you Ethan!

Had a great lunch experience here! Very friendly staff in this spacious eatery with a huge stage. Menu was eclectic, and the food was plentiful and tasty!
The double decker grilled ham & cheese was more than a meal, as were the nachos. Had a great time here!

This is a great place to chill out and escape the crowds that are woooooooing it up on the strip.   It's not very smoky or full with clubbing crowds. Instead it's laid back vibe with some great classic country music.  Reasonably priced drinks and no cover- the bands play for tips.   If your taste in music runs towards Dwight Yokum and Cash then this is the place for you.
Stopped in for lunch today! Per Friendly! Good service and the best hamburger I've ever had!

Went here only cause one of my college friends from out of town wanted an 'authietic' margarita, even though we tried to talk her out of it, as there are so many great places around Honkey Tonk Row. Margaritaville on Lower Broadway - why? why? why? when you MARVELOUS BBQ places like Rippy's or Jack's BBQ.  If you're in Nashville do what they do.  We were told a 30-minute wait, which is normal for the area, but it went beyond an hour - why wait that long for a chain restaurant available in every city.   I know waits can be long at popular times, but I'd rather wait for something exceptional or unique to the area.

Our server was super, I think it was Jonnel!  But I sure wish he moved on to a place that isn't like the McDonalds of 'have fun' faux tropic restaurants.  It must be soul robbing. 

The wait in line was a crazy amount of time for an average burger and cold sweet potato fries.  Our waiter was apologetic about the fries and offered to re-do, truthfully,  I just wanted to get the devil out of there.  The  'authentic' margarita crew were happy. Beer was cold, but that's hardly a unique find in a Nashville bar or really any bar.

FYI there's now Margaritaville retirement communities.  Also could do without the shop full of  good-time tacky souvenirs, I live vicariously through other people's lives stuff - like a CrackerBarrell, maybe since Margaritaville is moving into the retirement community game, they'll be selling tropical-themed grampers in the gift shop. On to Margaritaville Tulsa, Syracuse and Cleveland!!!

I'm giving 4 stars because our reservation was bumped from dinner to lunch. Apparently the upstairs was booked for a private party. Big imposition for us but they redeemed themselves with great service, drinks and entertainment. They comped us an appetizer and gave us a great front row table. The food was hearty and surprisingly good. Make a reservation as this place gets crowded

My boyfriend and I decided to check out the Sunday live jazz sessions at Tennessee Brew Works. It was our first time there and I must say the ambiance and seating of the venue really was patron friendly. My boyfriend was able to order a draft beer right away and luckily there was a table available near the music. They have many seating options: at the bar, tables both up- and downstairs, as well as outdoor seating. It was a sweltering 90+ degrees outside so we opted for inside seating, however, I will definitely try the outdoor seating when the weather gets cooler. Overall it has a great vibe, reasonably priced beer, and a nice live music scene on Sundays. They also do tours!

Great Venue! 
Old warehouse. Plenty of parking in the area. 
(Both paid and unpaid in the area.)

Stage was high enough you could see no matter the area you were in. I've been to a rock concert as well as an r&b show the sound works for both genres.

Only complaint was the line situation out front was confusing and could have been better handled.

Overall a bad representation and disappointment. We had a group of 11 in town for the weekend after Thanksgiving and we wanted to go out and sight see. My wife's parents are big Buffet fans and wanted the start with late lunch and margaritas. We sat down just a few mins after 2pm and left about 4;15pm, not by choice. 

The downstairs had a medium crowd and upstairs was mostly open when we got there and we needed 1 high chair but it took 10 mins to find one. We then got settled and ordered drinks. One end of our table got forgotten about and our server took off to put drinks in and the first round took 15 mins and they didn't get to order until he came back. 

We then realized we should put all our food orders in to hope it was just a drink issue. Unfortunately, It was not. Our food sporadically came out and with most being burgers, sandwiches and salads. Three burgers came out overcooked, mine so dry it crumbled when I bit into it, and 1 missing toppings. Out of 10 orders the only one with just a salad with chicken breast came out 15 mins later than the rest, and we were missing a side of onion rings. None of us really wanted to order more drinks. 

Ate that point we were ready to move on and asked for the checks. When we voiced that we were disappointed with our experience and the server was very nice and really seemed to be trying. He was shaking and kept telling us the kitchen was the fault. He said he'd take the bills to the manager to see what could be done, he came back 10 mins later with the bills, no change and no explanation lol. I said something to the managers both on the way out and they seemed to be totally shocked sarcastically. Offered us a voucher or a chance to look at the checks again as we were walking out. We declined and just wrote it off as a loss. Good luck.

Checked this place out one evening after dinner. 

Beer sampler:
Definitely a fan.  $10 for the sampler, which has 5 samples on it.  All the beers were tasty.  I tend to leave behind the IPA's because they are usually a little too hoppy for me...but I know that Nashville seems to enjoy the hops.  

Growlers:
They actually have a growler filling station as you come in the door and technically it is a "separate" business.  This is for tax purposes.  We took a growler of our own in, which they had no problem filling and rinsed before they did so.  We purchased a growler of Ryeman.  Good beer :)  They put a little stamped tag on it so we would know what we were taking with us.  Pricing was good as well.

Seating:
Lots and lots of seating!  They have a lower level and an upper level.  The lower level has an area that apparently often has live music and did while we were there.  The upper level has tv monitors to watch the game on.  Both levels look out onto the brewery floor so that it kinda cool as well!

Tours:
The tours are $12 and that includes the tour and a beer sampler...so essentially the tour is only $2 :)  Good deal!

Staff:
Friendly and helpful :)

I'd say the distillery tour we took was more exciting, but I can stomach the taste of beer more than whiskey. At the end of the tour we got to pick a complimentary beer. I like hefeweizens, so I chose the Southern Wit. Highly recommended.

Ole Red gets a high 3 stars, maybe a low 4.  I'll explain.  

So, we were looking for a nice dinner before we went out onto the strip for the night and decided to check out Ole Red.  First of all, the place looks great!  It had a modern and hip look.  That red dog posted all over the place is pretty cool.  You can tell it's definitely a newer restaurant (which I will talk more about in a bit), and in my opinion it has the one of the best looking stages in Nashville.  It's quite impressive how big the place is, the main floor is huge and the balcony might be just as big. Got to see a great artist and band play that night, Cort Carpenter.  Check him out!

But, the service, well... let's just say they still have some kinks to work out.  I will give it to them, they were very busy the night we went and I know what it's like to work in the food service industry, so I am a little forgiving.  

First, we got there and waited about 30 minutes for a table.  Not a problem.  We were finally told to make our way to the upstairs balcony because that is where we will be sitting.  It would've been nice to be escorted to the upstairs area, but we got up there just fine.  We needed a table for four, so we were a bit surprised when the hostess up top brought us to a table that was literally wedged in between two others.  The people at the other tables even gave us a look like "yeah, that's not going to happen".  Not to mention, the table was dirty still.  The hostess put our menus down and walked away.  I was kind of in shock.  I had to flag down another server and tell her we were going to sit at the table down the way because this table is dirty and there was no way all four us were going to be able to sit down.  She said that was fine.  We sat down at a different table and our server didn't seem to thrilled about that.  I apologized, and she seemed okay after a while.  We put in our food and drink orders.  If there is one pet peeve of mine, it's when the appetizer comes merely minutes before the main dish.  We felt like we had to wait about 25 minutes before getting our appetizer.  But, like I said, they were busy and we were enjoying the band.  No big deal.  When she brought out the food and walked away, there was no silverware.  Granted it was a lot of finger food, but it's hard to eat tater tot poutine without a fork.  Had to once again flag her down and ask for silverware.  

The food though?  It was very good!  We got the redneck  nachos for an appetizer which was great and super filling.  A friend got the southern tater tot poutine, which was very delicious while the rest of us got burgers.  The burgers were great!  If I had to compliment them for something, it's their tater tots.  I'm used to the little golden yellow nuggets that every restaurant tends to use, but you can tell they make theirs from scratch.  Crispy brown on the outside, but soft on the inside.  I could've eaten that all night.  

So, they still have some kinks to workout, but overall a good experience and great food!

What a phenomenal brewery!

TBW is one of my favorite craft breweries in Nashville, offering some fantastic selections like the Basil Ryeman, Walk the Lime, and Country Roots. These are really great quality beers that experiment in pretty creative directions, and it totally, totally works. If you're a first-timer, try the 5-beer sampler for $10.

Beyond the beer, TBW is an awesome place to hang out. There's live music, plenty of balcony seating with nice views of downtown Nashville, and tons of board games (including a giant Connect Four!) What a great place to get together with friends and hang out, or just relax with that special someone--either way, TBW is a good time. Definitely recommend it, and absolutely will be back.

Most of you will go for the ambiance, the rooftop views, drinks and music, but I did not (one day...). I was there for a pre-construction tour and again today for a luncheon and let me tell you, meeting planners, the mashed red potatoes must be made with angels tears, and blessed offerings of a cow treated so gently that it willingly gave its best cream and butter. They are amazing and I wish I'd had a Ziploc bag in my purse because I would have embarrassed my peers by stuffing some in my bag.

The others at the table raved over the baked chicken and I heard it was the best one person had ever had. My wings were eh though I rate the pulled pork highly,  especially with the white bbq sauce. 

The greens were decent. But can I tell you about the banana pudding? It was so doggoned fresh and light and gorgeous. It's like getting the essence of bananas because they were smooshed and smoothed in the middle layer. And I got the unexpected pleasure of a hint of chocolate, just a smidge of shavings perhaps over the whipped cream top.

In conclusion, yum!

This is a good go to when you know you want a good diner and good service.  There was live entertainment in the bar- a seated country music artist with a guitar.  He was ok.  Some people dressed up as key political figures where standing in front of the place waving at everyone and kind of were more entertaining that the actual music.  
I always get the cheeseburger in paradise and it was cooked perfectly but I had to ask for the 57 sauce!  . I had the perfect margarita but I have to say the uptown top shelf margarita is better.  The perfect margarita was suggested because it has fresh lime but I think I would rather have the Cointreau.  All in all, it was a good experience on a very busy night.

Great place!  A spacious area with an upstairs and really cool vibe!  The beer is very interesting for sure - the flavors are just as described so if you are not into drinking a beet or root or whatever it says don't get it because it tastes exactly like what it says - a very enjoyable place to hang out and the food looked really good!

Great music and a place for drinks and music. Will not eat here again. Ordered the nachos they threw a whole chicken filet on the top of the nachos. It was like dark brown/black in color. The waitress was appalled herself and did take it off our bill. Asked for a vegan patty on a regular burger bun. It came out with a gluten free bun, my side of pickles never came out. Have been at our table 2.5 hours still haven't gotten receipts. Waitress was very kind but not good with checking on our table or in a timely manner. Kept disappearing.

I really liked this place. I can't comment on the food as we didn't eat here. The band set up was nice and the second level
Looked down onto the first floor which made it nice to be able to eat and enjoy the music if you chose to.

I have been coming to shows and events here for years. Why have I never reviewed it? Probably because I assumed that I did years ago! 
Well, making up for it now. 
I've always enjoyed attending a wide variety of offerings here.... from the Predators, to A-List concerts, to Monster Truck Jams, the CMA awards, Ice skating performances, beer tastings.. too many to name. But the point is they do them all well. Parking is relatively easy. If you can upgrade to buy a pass to park in the attached garage, I highly recommend you do. It is super convenient. 
The staff members in the suites are delightful and helpful. 
You won't get any deals on food/beverage but I'm sure you already knew that. 
We are lucky to have this gem anchor our Downtown scene.

I am a local, who goes to whiskey jam all the time because my husband is a drummer who plays there often. i unfortunately got some pretty rude service (or lack there of) by a blonde female bartender on the roof top at about 9:30-9:45 last night. 

my friends and i were on the roof top trying to buy a round a drinks. we were standing on the middle/left side of the bar. we were standing there for about 10 mins trying to get the attention of the bartenders. it was getting bad enough to where i even started hearing others next to us complaining about why they haven't even come down to us yet. the bartenders were only helping the ones that were in front of them who were coming up to them (mostly all males) so i start to try and wave to them to show them we wanted to purchase drinks. i THEN get a very nasty rude look by a blonde female bartender and she stated 'you waving your hand isn't going to get you faster service' my jaw dropped when she said that. there were about 5-6 other people (who i did not know) who heard that and were also baffled too. the rooftop was NOT that busy for her to say something like that. others even came up to me to say how rude her comment was and asked to buy my drink for me. 

i'm not one to ever write a bad yelp review. but based on this bartenders actions, i hope management sees my review on here so she can get a counseling notice or suspension as that was completely unprofessional. she could have easily said 'hey, i see you, give me one min and i'll be right with you' or at least give me a smile with a hand gesture that she is coming shortly. but NOPE i got a nasty rude look with that comment she stated instead. 

again, i am a local who goes there A LOT. i am friends with other big name musicians, and trust me when i say i will be telling them what happened to ensure you guys will not be getting any money from us anymore. we will walk over to losers or somewhere else for that matter if we want a drink.

The security staff at this place are on a serious power trip. I volunteered that I had a couple vitamins in my pocket and the security staff was all "oh yeah you can't take those in here" after asking to see them. Like I'd volunteer that I have drugs on me and show them to the security guard if they were. I threw them away because I can tell that the security staff has a collective power trip complex, but I should have just popped them all in my mouth and be done. Love this venue but the people they hire are the worst.

All the music in the bars on Broadway is going to be ridiculously fun and unbelievably talented! Layla's is a great example of this! Great music, fun atmosphere. Want to get away from the crowds? Go upstairs!

As for having my first experience in Nashville, TN, let me tell you first how great the city itself is! Honky Tonk bars - one after another! Nashville knows how to party - country style. 

There was a band playing country covers all night mixed with a few of their songs. I really wish I remembered their name so they can get a shoutout on Yelp, but I figure most of the bands are probably excellent at this bar. 

The drinks were stiff and cheap as well. Everyone was just having a great time and stomping away with their cowboy boots. 

Can't wait to come back!

I was very impressed with the Bridgestone Arena. I felt very safe entering since security checked my bag and I went through a metal detector. The first thing I noticed was all the different food vendors. There were so many choices and the food looked amazing I decided to stop at Dunk-in Donuts for an iced coffee. The lady working was so pleasant and really nice, showing me all the different self service options for coffee flavors. I found my seat with some help. I sat to the left of the stage not too high up, but had a clear view and the sound system was so clear. The lighting was also visually pleasing. The Thomas Rhett concert was one of the best I've seen. I liked the runway stage and that I could see everything. I don't think there is a bad seat in the house. Overall I was very impressed and very happy.

Great venue on the Nashville strip; go through the crowded first floor and head to the top bar, The Lookout, it has all the views you are looking for. Plenty of outdoor seating and an in crowded bar. There is a limited menu but we split a classic ole red burger. Perfectly seasoned and cooked, lots of flavor. A couple of drinks and off to the EJ concert.

I truly would not waste my time or money here. Go somewhere local and more authentic. This is a tourist trap. 

We visited Matgaritaville after seeing a concert in Nashville. My husband really wanted a margarita and this seemed perfect. 

We came in late in the night (but several hours before closing) and the wait staff was very apathetic. No one really seemed to care about what they were doing or who they were serving. The menu is also kind all over the place food-wise. And the prices for the food offerings are exorbitant - I'm guessing because of location and the brand. NOT worth it. 

Our drinks were fine and our food were fine but certainly *certainly* not worth what we paid. You can get the same thing PROBABLY MUCH BETTER from Chili's for a fraction of the cost.

This was on May 25, 2019: 
It's a long read but STICK WITH ME... 

We were in Nashville, TN celebrating my Best Friend's Bachelorette Party. We had signed up to do the Party Barge (the pick up location is behind Losers Bar and Grill-- next door). So we thought we would grab dinner at Winner's Bar and Grill because it was recommended and their website had a good menu. Upon arrival, we all sat down and waited for a server to greet us. After about 5 minutes she came over and passed out a little piece of paper with about 5 menu items on it and didn't say anything else. She came back and asked us for our drink orders, we gave them to her and she took our credit cards? Which I thought was strange because we weren't intending on keeping an open tab. We also asked for water and she rudely said: "It's over there" and pointed to a water dispenser on the bar. After we get our drinks she explains their kitchen is "under construction" so that list is all they had. It was BBQ pulled pork, hamburgers, hot dogs, and chips... We just decided to get something anyways and would have a nicer dinner afterwards (because we were about to drink and needed food...) Next, the server told us we had to order all our food at the bar because she wasn't a "waitress". Ok. So we had to wait in line and finally all ordered our food at 5:30pm and we needed to be next door for the Party Barge at 6:30pm. We then proceeded to go ahead and close out our tabs while we waited. First, the same server charged me double. I ordered a hamburger and ONE beer. She charged me $20 when it should have been $10. She also messed up my friend's payment as well. After that, I was already annoyed. But hold on, it gets worse. We are STILL waiting for our food 30 minutes later. Food that shouldn't take longer than 15 minutes to cook. We then told them again we're on a time constraint, the other bartender was rude and said it would be out in 5-8 minutes. Finally, two girls got their pulled pork sandwiches WITHOUT BBQ because they "didn't have any" although that's what their terrible little menu said it came with. Who eats a pulled pork sandwich with NO SAUCE? Also it was ICE COLD. It's now 6:15pm at this point and then two orders of hot dogs come out. They looked DISGUSTING and guess what? COLD. At that point we went up and complained and nicely asked for our money back because 1. The food was coming out terrible and cold 2. We had to be next door in the next 15 minutes. A guy comes out who I thought was the manager? But I'm not sure... We tell him all the issues and we want our money back. He leaves for like 5 minutes and comes back opens the cash register and then THROWS the $45 in 5's at me. Then he grabs the boxes of hot dogs and aggressively threw them in the trash. I said "Have a good night" and walked out. As we met the other girls outside they show me a video of the "server" and "manager" cooking our food out back in a MICROWAVE and they said once we cancelled our orders they unplugged the microwave and took it back inside. ARE YOU KIDDING ME? *PICTURE IS ATTACHED* They should have just said they aren't serving food at this time and ALL OF THIS could have been avoided but they were trying to make a quick buck by serving low quality food. The service and food was BY FAR the worst experience I have had in the city of Nashville. I will tell everyone to NEVER attend this establishment. They should be shut down for their TERRIBLE service. We have all been in the restaurant industry and could not believe this Bar and Grill is still open after we experienced their RUDE staff and TERRIBLE food.

NEVER GO HERE.

The food was good, but not amazing. The live entertainment is good, and makes up for anything. It's definitely a good place to bring your kids, if you wish. I think they must be REALLY busy, because sometimes they would forget things about what I ordered. For example, I ordered a coke, and forgot to get it for another 20 minutes. I had to prod the waitress and show her my empty coke cup.

This venue is pretty solid. It's your basic arena, but with bonuses! They have your regular event food like hot dogs, nachos, and cheap crappy beer. But they have upgrades with local craft beer and delicious food. Of course, everything is expensive but that's on par for every arena. We've been here for concerts and hockey games. The acoustics are good. I've been to stadiums where the sound doesn't bounce correctly, but this sounds good wherever you are.
Best bar on Broadway- great live music, reasonable prices for drinks, and a great time all around. Don't miss this bar!

After a concert, my group and I searched for a place open late night to dine. Because it was the closest to us, we decided to go to Margaritaville. The music was live as with many of the restaurants downtown and it was self seat. We were ravenous and ordered our meal. I picked a BBQ Burger and ordered a salad on the side. I believe we waited about half an hour for our food to come out. It was not even close to being busy and our table of five should not have taken that much time to be served.

When the server did come out, he only had 4 plates of food and our fifth had to wait an additional 10 minutes. The BBQ burger was a disappointment overall. I've been to fast food restaurants that serve more flavorful burgers than the one I ordered at this establishment. The salad I ordered also came out when my burger did and I specifically asked for it before the burger. The pickle tasted like it had been marinated in cologne and was overly pungent.

The server seemed less than pleased to serve a young table of five. Especially one that didn't order alcohol. I personally felt uncomfortable around our server and when my check was brought, the price was astounding. My small nothing-out-of-the-ordinary salad was $4.99. That's more than a half salad at Panera! Just because the location is downtown does not mean you can overcharge the food and neglect its quality. Will not be coming back here and even if someone invites me here, I will decline.
Huge venue! Clean and the temperature was cold! A lot to choose from for food and drinks.

The Bridgestone arena is a really cool place to see a hockey game. Being from New York I'm a little bit jaded because I've always gone to Madison Square Garden for my hockey games anyone who knows me knows that I am a Ranger fan. I have been to other arenas like the staples center the Honda Center Wells Fargo Ctr to see hockey games. Now I can officially say I have gone the two hockey games at the Bridgestone arena in Nashville. 

I went here to see the Nashville predators versus the Colorado avalanche. I also went the next day to see the Nashville predators versus the Minnesota wild. On this trip to Nashville I was not staying downtown so I could not walk to the arena so we had to take a vehicle. Parking can be very difficult if you don't arrive early. Luckily the person I was with is good friends with somebody at one of the restaurants and bars on Main Street the tin roof downtown and they reserve a parking spot for us. 

Once we got inside I had to go to a staff member and ask him where I was seated. The staff member took me in the person I was with to our section and Sat us. The seats here are very good for the price I purchased two lower-level tickets for $69 one for me and a friend. At Madison Square Garden I paid almost 4 times that for lower-level seats. I do attend about 4 to 5 Ranger games per year at Madison Square Garden. The person I was with ran into somebody that she knew that's a season ticket holder that has a suite at the Bridgestone arena. I was talking to them about how the price was so much cheaper to go see a game here than it was in New York. The gentleman I was having the conversation with told me how much the season tickets were for the suite. So I asked him how much regular season tickets were when he replied I laughed because for what I paid for for Lower level Ranger tickets per year I could get a whole entire season ticket lower-level package at the Bridgestone Arena. 

The arena itself is very nice it has a good layout it's in a big oval like most arenas. They do have a sports store where you can purchase merchandise I ended up buying a jersey there. For food they have a couple of different options they have this girl called the breakaway café. You can purchase burgers fries chicken tenders popcorn the normal arena food stuff. They did have a fresh lemonade stand which I did buy a fresh squeeze glass of lemonade but they only took cash. They had another place to eat I cannot remember the name of it but they were serving hotdogs sausages etc.

Both games were Great the fans were really into it. The one cool thing that I really enjoyed about the Bridgestone arena is every single time the predators had a timeout or there was a TV commercial the camera man would pan around to individual people in the arena and show them on the Jumbotron. Also in between intermissions they had a live band perform on the stage. I was told by the person I was with that they do this at every single hockey game and it's a different performer every single night. I guess it's like a local spotlight for music. But anyways I thought it was really cool and different. At one point when the cameraman pointed to this one gentleman he ended up taking his shirt off and started dancing. I have been to about 15-20 hockey games and I've never seen somebody take that shirt off and start dancing. The only thing negative that I have was when we were trying to leave they have an area that's roped off for the Fox sports broadcasting where the public can go right up to the rope and basically be in back of where the broadcasters are and get their faces on television. It's on the way towards the exit so as your exiting people are stopping and looking at the broadcasters in trying to get on television. While the people are stopping to look at the broadcasters the people that are just trying to get out of there are being blocked by them and it creates kind of a an annoying situation. 

Overall the experience was very good. I enjoyed the game and I do look forward to coming back to another game in the future. I think I'm going to look into getting a sweet or seeing if the people that we ran into have an opening. I highly recommend going to a game here it's cheaper than other markets the intensity is the exact same as any other hockey game that I've been to and it's just a really good time for all ages. 

PROS: 
- cheap tickets good seats
- friendly staff
- great place to bring a date or kids 
- live music I between periods

CONS:
- after the game on the way out gets crowded by the fox sports 1 booth.

While I admit a lack the personal experience for a truly good review of Bridgestone, not being much of a sportsball person or concert goer there is a lot to like. 

The place is very big and has stalls for food and merchandise everywhere.  The Stadiums I went to in my youth (The old Tiger Stadium, Cobo Arena, The Palace) Bridgestone is a wonderland of stuff.

Having said that of course, it's all about the mighty dollar for places like this. 12 dollars for Beer in a can. 9 dollars for a glass of Wine, etc.

While capitalism certainly supports this, I didn't find myself very excited to when I'm already spending 200 dollars for two Foo Fighters tickets.

But there are certainly worse places to spend two hours, and the Stadium IS well maintained and clean.

Arrived about 30 minutes early to see Keith Urban, a sold out event. The crowd moved through security easily and seemingly effectively....  The venue is pleasing to the eye -- big bright colorful busy -- easy to navigate. Friendly staff. Plenty of friendly vendors. Beer and wine was offered. All went well --- after the show, we were able to get out and onto the streets with no thought. We arrived by cab and walked back to our hotel so no parking info from me

Ate at the rooftop because the bottom floor restaurant was too long of a wait and what a good idea.  Beautiful views. 
As for the food we had the Brussels sprouts which were the best I've ever had.  The pretzel was huge and amazing. The calamari was okay nothing special could have done without. The wings were good. And the 7 layer dip was okay I felt like some gauc and olives would have made it better.

Great brewery -- probably my favorite in Nashville.  They have very good beer (3 different IPAs on tap on my last visit) and surprisingly good food (particularly burgers).

The setup of the building is unique and (mostly) functional.  There are two floors with a separate area upstairs, which can be rented out for private events.  My only qualm with the setup is that it can get loud upstairs since it's open.  For better or worse, they have songwriters performing downstairs about every night, I believe, and the noise travels up to the second floor.  Depending on your mood and preferences, hearing the music up there could be a pro or a con.

There isn't really a parking lot, but there is ample space to park along the street nearby.  The area can feel a bit seedy, but I've never had any issues after several visits.  Definitely worth a visit!

The food was excellent as always! The service was just okay this time. We waited about 45 minutes to get our food tonight. Yes, it is a Saturday, but we came in at about 7:00, were seated immediately, and there were many open tables while we ate. Then, someone at the table spilled their water and were not offered another one. Many other people in our party were left without refills as well.

I went to see Greta Van Fleet last night (5/14/18). Amazing band!!!! Such energy and talent! I have read many reviews of the staff being rude but my bartender was friendly and pleasant! This place reminds of the old defunct venue City Hall that was on 12th Ave. in the Gulch and is now an Urban Outfitters Store. Now the bad...they should change the name of this venue and call it THE FURNACE!!! If hell can be any hotter than this venue, then count me out the next time a band I want to see is playing there! The mercury levels and heat index had to be in the triple digits. I stood in an area where I could still see, but not elbow to elbow with everyone. My shirt was soaked by the night's end, I could feel sweat running down my back the entire evening, and went through many paper towels wiping my face. It might have been cooler having the show outside in the parking lot. The venue had many huge ceiling fans, but must have been for decorative purposes because you could see the blades of the fan as it spun...created no air current whatsoever!!! If you attend a show here, I guess hope that your favorite bands come between November through March, then it would be more tolerable to attend.

A true definition of fantastic music and class. There are no seats that disappoint even the most knowledgeable connoisseur of music and entertainment. The venue is beautiful and the symphony is fun, witty and full of energy!

this place keeps getting better!!!! last time i came they were not serving food yet. so, we got the cheese board and charcuterie board. damn they were good! and the presentation was beautiful too. great live music, delicious craft beer, dart boards, tvs to watch games on, a well thought out space and patio all make for a stellar experience. staff was stressed, but were killing it and working so hard. taking the busy day in stride. love that they have a bar upstairs and downstairs. just love this place!!! really love when places improve upon themselves. smashing it!

While attending the CMT Awards show in town this arena is HUGE!!! Very clean and helpful staff...this is a great venue for big concerts. The acoustics are awesome...

Will Definetly go to a concert here and I highly recommend it. 
I would tell everyone that goes to this arena to take an Uber ride and get dropped off as parking is not-so-good in this tight touristy area.

The Nashville Symphony does such a wide variety of performances at the Schermerhorn Symphony Center they are bound to have programming that each and every person would enjoy. The Schermerhorn is located downtown across from the Country Music Hall of Fame and is a beautiful building that elevates the whole experience. The concert hall is exquisite with romantic lighting and a large open space. 

I came here to watch the symphony play the whole score to Jurassic Park as they showed the movie. This was a truly awesome experience because the music has such a huge impact on the movie. There are so many moments where music creates suspense or builds up to a critical moment in the plot. I was truly engaged and would watch the movie then my eyes would dart back and forth from the orchestra because it was so interesting to watch them play as well. 

An older couple seated next to me and my friend said they had seen several performances by the orchestra for the score of a movie, so it sounds like they change it up and do different movies every year. They said they had seen Phantom of the Opera and a few others. I looked at their calendar at it looks like they will be doing Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets and the Dreamwork Animation set to music as well. 

Whether you are with your special someone or going as a family this is a great outing. I highly recommend it!

I've been to Bridgestone quite a few times, but tonight it was for the Chris Brown concert. Venue is nice, our seats were great. Didn't get any food or drinks this time, but prior visits both were great. The security check to get in was a breeze make sure to check the website for bags you can bring inside. I did not have a bag this time which made it go by even faster. Great venue for concerts.

Layla's was the first bar we ventured into on Broadway, and it was a great choice. The band was rocking, the beers were ice cold, and the bartender was easy on the eyes. We hung out for several rounds then decided to head elsewhere, though we ended our night back at Layla's. The bar is a little divey, but only in the best way possible. The bathrooms were clean enough even for this high-maintenance gal. I loved that the TVs were showing hockey playoffs; not something I expected in Nashville, despite the nearby Predators stadium. Definitely recommended for some good times!

Usually this chain is very nice.  This one however was a bit below expectations.  Food was not well prepared, service was indifferent, and the music was not anywhere as good as in the other places along Broadway in Nashville.  Perhaps it simply paled a bit by comparison to the Nashville scene.

Stopped in here after the Southern. First listened to music on the first floor and hubby had a beer. Great band. Then moseyed  up to the fourth floor which has a rooftop  bar. Best views on broadway!!!!!i really appreciated being able to get a good glass of Vino. Hard to find on "beer guzzling" Broadway! This will be a "go-to"  from here on in. Next time will try some snacks
Cool place with great service, but the food was average and way over priced . Live music was pretty good though.
This place is awesome! We were only in Nashville 2 days and went here both days! The beer is great and the food is awesome!
Pimento cheese dip is awesome. Atmosphere is casual. Great service, good good, great service, and great entertainment. Will be back
My friends & I ate here for dinner. The staff was polite & friendly. The food was filling but a little on the high side you pay for the atmosphere. The drinks were delicious & averaged priced.

Ok the acoustics are amazing.  It's full of snobs but what the heck.  I went to hear Mozart.  They threw in two songs that sounded like Yoko Ono being channeled thru Symphony Instruments...stick to the darn plan.  The Mozart was great...the other two songs sucked.  They seriously sounded like background sounds for a made for TV movie.  Stick to the plan...Mozart and save that crap for after midnight Rocky Horror Picture Show crowd.  If I was Martha, I'd want my money back.
Disappointing! Food and service. Limited menu and the staff needs a refresher in basics.

My Favorite Brewery Tour & Tasting In Nashville

SITREP

My hats off to the Tennessee Brew Works, and big props to tour guide extraordinaire Garr for giving one of the best brewery tours I've seen to date, ANYWHERE.

THE SETUP

There are a lot of similarities in tours through breweries (and wineries) for that matter, but where Garr really set the bar was on his most extensive discussion on "the mash" - the process of making the mash, the organic, vegetable, fruit, etc., matter you may use in mash - and the inordinate tedious process it is to clean the machinery of used-mash.

"THE MASHER".  

In fact, Garr was quite proud of their stand-alone "masher" which apparently does all the heavy lifting for the brewers that many other breweries have to do manually. 

Therefore, Tennessee Brew Works has the inordinate capability to add many more flavors to the mash process without it deteriorating the whole brew-making process.

THE BREWS

And the brews were all fabulous!  I tried their Basil Ryeman (quite exotic in flavor!) and the Belgian Farmhouse (hands down my favorite), and was delighted with both of them.  YUM!

THE LOWDOWN

A great brewery stop to listen, learn and imbibe!

Stopped by on Valentines and enjoyed their sampler paired with local chocolates. The beer was excellent and the chocolate choices really highlighted some subtle tastes in the beer. 

They has a great outdoor patio, hope the weather is great next time I'm in Nashville.

You go here for the atmosphere so it's odd to see reviews criticizing the food. C'mon, It's not a fine dining establishment. The atmosphere is soooo FUN! 

We went to the "Music Row Happy Hour with Buzz Brainard" on Friday afternoon which is broadcast on Sirius XM's The Highway. It is fun & festive. It is upstairs in Margaritaville. 

If you don't wait on line for hours you won't get a table so then it's standing room only. (There is service at the tables but we did not get a table.)
Long line at the main bar but if you go to the side room bar there was little to NO wait. 
Staff & bartenders were all friendly & fun. 

If you must sit or are grumpy or don't have a "license to chill" (JB reference!) then please just don't go. 

Surprise guest Michael Ray played a few songs. 

The happy hour was so fun!!!

Awesome range of tasty beers. Each distinct, unique and very drinkable.  the burger was world class; juicy, tasty and with really good chips on the side. Courtney tending bar upstairs was delightful. Really knowledgeable about their beers and helped match everyone coming up to the bar with the right selection. This is a "must" for Nashville microbrew tours.

Great great beer. And at great prices. Staff was super helpful and not judgey since we were amateurs when it comes to craft beer. Highly recommend the Basil Ryeman! 
Patio atmosphere was great, shared tables. Lucky enough to sit next to some friendly adults. Live music starts almost as soon as they open. Unlike a lot of other places we went to that weekend, it was not blaring loud and did not take over the experience. 
Food was delish! If you like spicy, I highly recommend the frog legs. My dad had nothing but great things to say about the burger. 
We will be back on our next Nashville trip!

I love this arena. I have been here for multiple events, and will give you separate experiences depending on what your doing at the arena. 

Hockey

The Preds games are always a blast. Lower bowl or upper bowl tickets, you will not have a bad seat in the house. A very friendly compound for visiting fans. Since Nashville is such a melting pot, you continually see away jerseys frequent the stands of Residing Nashvillians. A good collection of assorted concessions foods and beverages. Great location because one the games pile out, Broadway is the post game destination. 

Concerts 

Recently, I went to Bridgestone for the Eric Church concert. The night he played was a Bridgestone Arena record for attendance. Everything went smoothly, concession lines were not overwhelming and the crowd behaved themselves. Last year, I attended the FGL/Luke Bryan concerts. It was an absolute blast. Being the Music City I really do believe you see the artists best performances. Example, Eric Church played for 3 hours. 

Tonight I embark in a new Bridgestone venue called Areacross. Where the top dirt bike riders invade the area. Excited to see how this compared to concerts and hockey games. 

PS during hockey games they play live music during intermission...of course right? It's NashVegas

45 minute wait, bad sweet tea (tastes like dirty water), burger selections limited and once delivered the burger had blood in meat. Fries were soggy upon delivery and not crisp.

If you are a fan of Blake and want to see it, step in, add a photo or video to your social media story, and then go find you something good to eat elsewhere. You'll thank me.

Tennessee brew works was one of our favorite places while visiting this past week. We arrived around 4pm and they had live music and good seats. They have 2 levels of seating including an outdoor area and rooftop. The place is a bit tough to find but so worth it. We started with the intention of stay for a beer or two. We wound up being there for 4 hours. We ordered a flight and just went at it. My wife and I both really enjoyed the cowboys and hippie. The staff were extremely friendly and the food looked great! The music was also very good. One negative would be no AC, it was hot in there. It can be overlooked after the beers get in ya. This is a hidden gem in Nashville that should be on everyone's list.

Went to the annual crawfish boil. Got there early in hopes of getting a good seat. Unfortunately I'm not the only one to have thoughts that. The lines moved quickly and the staff was extremely friendly. The ambience was great and I'm looking forward to coming again when it's less crowded. Sadly the weather didn't hold up and we were rained out. The cover outside didn't help and they didn't have anywhere else to go given they were at capacity inside. We ended up having to leave. Hoping for another fun event here with better weather

Food, beer, and atmosphere were great. All of the staff was very nice and helpful. Only giving 2 stars because the manager was very disrespectful and aggressive to our group when we tried to talk to him about an issue. He kept his back to us while we were simply asking for an explanation. Total coward and does not deserve a position of power. Hopefully he does not hold this position for much longer considering the way he talks to his customers I can't imagine how he treats the staff.

Security was so helpful! We asked a bartender and seater and they were able to find first aid equipment that we needed  and they said "were out". We asked the security team and in a heartbeat they were able to assist us in our need! Thanks Tim and Dave for saving the night!
Food, drinks and live music were awesome too but hands down to the Security staff!

Ole Red is as touristy as they come, but it's located on Nashville's most famous street, so what did you expect? I came here around 11 am for a solo lunch and I thoroughly enjoyed myself!

A long line had formed out front before opening, but when you have a famous country music star's name attached (this is Blake Shelton's place), you should assume most visitors will want to check it out!

The dining area is centered around a stage and on the day I visited, local celebrity Jessica Rose was performing live. She was so talented, and did a good mix of original songs and covers. Of course, the Blake Shelton covers she sang are what brought the house down! 

I was seated at a small table with a fantastic view of the stage, and I was so impressed with the service. First, I wasn't rushed at all. It was an unspoken given that I would be hanging out and listening to the music. My server was on the ball, ready to take my order less than five minutes after I sat down! The place filled up quickly, to the point it was standing room only just thirty minutes after opening. 

I ordered the Nashville Burger ($16) sans bun, which was a good portion of a decent hamburger loaded with tangy pimento cheese (totally a Southern comfort food). At the suggestion of my waitress, I got the housemade tater tots as a side (so good and worth every carb)! Since I was blowing it out, I also ordered the biscuits ($6) to start (do I even need to tell you they were delicious)? I am ashamed to admit that I ate the entire basket except for one. They were that yummy! 

I also enjoyed the housemade pickles (so good) and the freshly brewed iced tea ($2.75) -- although I'd expect nothing less than perfection when it comes to tea in the South!

The food had tourist prices, but it was very good quality. It wasn't gourmet dining, but the portions were generous and the food tasty. I can't complain, even though I spent almost $40 on a lunch for one (and I didn't even order any liquor)!

Overall I loved the atmosphere and the live music was A+. A great place to visit when in Nashville.
This place plays genuine country music!!! Laid back real Nashville experience. Good service too!

One of the best breweries I have ever been too, not just because the beers are great but the food we ordered was delicious as well.  My husband and I got 2 flights, one of the top 5 beers on the menu and one of the 2nd grouping on the menu which cost us $2 extra.  It was worth it because we got to sample all of the beers they had and figure out which ones suited our tastes the best. I liked the "Country Roots" which is a sweet potato stout and the "City Winery Collaboration" which is an ale aged in a pinot noir barrel. We had the frog legs and a cheese plate to go along with our beer and both did not disappoint.  The food here is not like regular pub food. Its elevated and you can taste the quality in every bite.
Awesome people and great beer list. IPAs are solid and the cheese board is amazing. Would definitely come back
Really Blake?  Isn't this contrary to everything you represent?   Is this an Orange County influence.

Dear Blake, WHY oh why must you close the kitchen at 10pm? You COULD be the one that stays open later. Great looking menu but every time we come in, the table reservations are "booked" and no wait staff serves FOOD unless it's before 10pm & you have a table.  FFS . Also, security is constantly removing tables and chairs or booting people from perimeter seating stating that the tables are reserved for the late show. How does one even reserve the perimeter tables?????? Beer selection could be better IMHO.

Arrived on Sunday evening around 11:30pm. Band talent was terrible and could not even play basic Shania Twain. Additionally, several tables were unbussed and left with trash. Ended up having to bus our own table.

Definitely suggest you pass on Ole Red and stick to the more established places (I.e. Legends, Roberts, Tootsies, The Stage, and Crazy Town).

Ole Red's food was pretty tasty in general. The nachos were decent, but the quesadillas were amazing! My husband and I also really enjoyed hearing the live music while we ate. It was a fun introduction to Nashville that we enjoyed very much.

Beer selection was good. They also had other drinks/wine for the non-beer drinkers. Food was great! I gave the fish tacos 5 stars. My friends rated the pulled pork sandwich 4.5 stars. Prices were reasonable. Good amount of food and larger than normal wine pours. I would definitely recommend this place and would come back.
All I can say is they have the best damn beer! They even have one that tastes like a corona!

So excited to visit but it ended on a terrible note. After enjoying a yummy dinner on the 2nd floor with my 12 yr old son, we went to the first level at 8:30pm before it became adults only at 9pm to watch the performer. I walked to the first floor bar TO GET A WATER... It was two people deep, with people who had drinks, and were all facing the stage, so I said excuse me and made my way to the bar. Omg, all hell broke lose with two 65+ year old couples who screamed they were in their SPOT and ordered me to "get your drink and get the hell out of here". LOL, yeah, no. Anyway, I told her she was blocking the bar and she yelled she didn't care.
