There should be someone ensuring you can walk up to the lower level bar without being blocked by entitled people claiming their "spot" and blocking the bar and then bullying them. In retrospect, I should have alerted security/bartender about her foul mouthed harassment but was too busy defending myself, which I didn't need to do. Total bummer experience for my son after seeing Ricky from The Voice rehearsing there during the last season.
This place was great. Easy to get to, in, and around. Super fast service at the food area. Clean bathrooms. The food prices were much lower that I would have imagined.

Despite Layla's location on busy and often nutty Broadway, they maintain an authentic atmosphere of community, local music, and genuine dive-bar attitude. We visited on a Wednesday night to catch some women-fronted bluegrass, and the vibe was just what we hoped for. The bartenders were relaxed, friendly, and were happy to chat with visitors to make them feel at ease (special shout-out to Sammy!). In terms of drinks, my notoriously picky friend gave their Long Island ice teas two thumbs up. The prices are steep, because of the location -- this is the only reason I can't give 5 stars. I originally decided to visit Layla's because they seem to be one of the few places to offer live bluegrass music regularly, but I will continue to go back for the comfortable community feeling.
Omg this is the best! Blake Shelton's place is do classsy!!!! We had the best drinks!!!!

Even after all these years, I am surprised by the number of bars/honky tonks that dot Broadway. Each time I think that I've seen them all, 'new' ones creep up on me. In such a finite amount of space, there seems to be an infinite amount of narrow bars stuffed into 5-6 blocks. And, despite singing this song time and again, I'm always, like, 'haven't I been here before?'

No. No, I haven't.

I hadn't been to Layla's before and I don't know how that's possible. It's been there forever. I have been in Nashville for [redacted] years. We should have run in to each other by now. But we hadn't. Walking in to Layla's, I got the sense that this was the locals' tourist bar. Surrounded by Roberts and Tootsie's, Layla's may get lost in the shuffle but I sort of like it that way. Bear in mind, it will never be empty. You'll just have the ability to move freely, unlike at the other bars I just mentioned. If you have out-of-town friends to entertain and they've been to Nashville before, bring 'em here. They'll get that 'Nashville' experience without the bumps, tossles and woo-hoos that might bring a lesser man to tears.

At Layla's you'll hear fantastic musicians doing their thing. Despite the name, I heard more country than bluegrass. As a native Kentuckian who was with other Kentuckians, I was hoping to hear some blue and 'billy but no such luck. The musicians on the stage, though, were very talented -- as is expected on Broadway. Downstairs is a crush of humanity so I headed upstairs. This is your local pro tip for any/all Broadway bars: never stay downstairs. Upstairs you have more room, a bar you can actually get to (reasonably priced drinks, local beer in bottles and Nashville LITs if you want/need to get lit), bathrooms you can use and, in the case of Layla's, a back patio that spills out on to the alley. This gives you access to the food (grilled/fried to perfection), TVs to gawk at, open air to pollute with cigarettes (don't do this), and the chance to see musicians walk from the Ryman to other bars. This is what I mean wrt a local tourist experience. You get all the pluses of a Broadway bar without the over-the-top frenetic insanity of some of the more tourist-facing establishments.

Layla's, I'll be back with another crop of seasoned out-of-towners.

Very divey honky tonk, which was a great find! Thanks to Philly CM, Michelle, for the recommendation. PBRs here are only $2.50 in the middle of the afternoon. It felt like Philly! There was a great band playing (after having been at Rippy's across the street which was like awful karaoke) and people dancing. It was a happy older couple that was so adorable and they were at it for hours! One pet peeve about Nashville is that the band walks around and personally asks for tips to pressure you more.

Female bartenders are rude if you're a tourist trying to have a good time.  My buddies and I were told that we were annoying and loud and told to close out our tab.  After we spent a good amount of money at this place, they were quick to dismiss us.  It's very unfortunate.  I wish I was able to give zero stars.
Bar tenders know they will get people off the name of the place and make absolutely no effort at all!

The most hands down Amazing  burger nashvillian I will say ! I have had in FOREVER .... a cheat day for sure but so well worth it !!!!  Thank u to an amazing waitress "NIRA" for the recomendation  :) def we will come back for the perfect burger .

WILL NEVER GO BACK and i fact will tell people to avoid this place like the plague!! I was excited to try this place out and had heard that it was good!! that was not the case, i ordered a $16 cesar salad. I think my mcdonald's meal was better than this!! The chicken was dryer than the Sahara desert. We were seated instantly ,but did not even get talked to until about 20 minutes after being seated, which was totally fine. Then we received our drinks with no straws. I had to practically run our waitress down  in order to get us straws. Then we received our food with out silverware, waited 20 minutes before chasing down another waiter to ask him if he could get us silverware. i was not impressed and in fact kind of shocked someone would pay for this!! i was EMBARRASSED to have brought my friend from out of town here!!

update: was told to contact management & i did, but have not heard back :(

Great spot to drop in and hangout for a while.  The atmosphere was fun and the local entertainer played a nice variety of songs.  The drinks were strong and affordable in relation to other near by stops.  Barry and Katie kept the bar well and really were engaged with the guests in the bar area.

Nashville has some excellent breweries and Tennessee Brew Works is just one more example of why Nashville has more than music to be proud of.

On a recent visit I tried to of their creations, the easy ale and their wit beer. While the ale was good, the wit (or wheat) beer was the real star of the night. From a city that touched so many souls musically, this particular beer touched my soul, creating within it a simple joy.

I'll likely repeat what my wife stated so bear with me as I try to highlight other aspects of the brewery. Oh, here we go, bathroom was clean which is sometimes rare at a brewery. Ha!

The beers we sampled ranged in variety and were all tasty and worthy of individual servings. Parking in the area is a little tight especially on busier nights. We were here on a Friday and somehow found rockstar parking right by the entrance. Use Lyft/Uber and you should have no problems and not risk the OVI/DUI.

The multi tiered patio is a great place to enjoy the beer and has covered and uncovered portions for those like myself that sizzle in the sun. The only negative aspect of the patio is the possibility of inhaling some second hand smoke. 

There was a female guitarist singer/songwriter playing some halfway decent music which made the experience very "Nashvillian". Who knows? She could be the next Grammy winning artist on radio repeat. People watching opportunities are great here as all kinds of people walk/stumble through the doors.

Keep up the great work TBW!

Ole Red is a beautiful space with an awesome chandelier in the main stage, eating area. The bar is build very well and has a lot of character! The rooftop was beautiful with another wonderful view of Broadway. This place has a swanky vibe, which I did enjoy. However, I was a little surprised being that Blake is the owner. We loved our time at Ole Red!

I've been to half a dozen concerts or events (PBR!) and over 50 Predators games and have sat in almost every area on all three floors and never had a bad seat. The views are great. It is easy to get around and there are multiple entrances depending on where you park. 

The food is good enough - during Preds games go check out the Hot Chicken stand on the first floor and pick up the HOT CHICKEN MAC N CHEESE, oh man it is the greatest! 

As far as Predators games go, there isn't a better environment to enjoy a game. So loud and so fun!

Had the fried baloney and beer battered onion rings. Food was simple and delish. They have a server issue. While my server was awesome but she handled the whole bar and resturant. She did it with a smile and was the best but they need to give her help.

Not sure if this is the best BBQ in town, but a very popular place nonetheless. We were there during the weekend of a football game (tons of blue KU fans that night!). One of the spiked lemonade drinks (I forget which one) was awesome. Got the pulled pork, which was rather dry and lacked enough flavor/sauce.

Good ribs, great pulled pork plate with 2 Yazoo Hefeweizen. Pretty good country band, despite the young look ! Good experience, if you don't mind plastic forks, knives and table cloths! You will not go hungry !

I have never experienced such horrible service until going here with friends! We ordered a round of shots, the bartender never gave us change and when we asked for change she complained to us about the tip we gave her (which was already a good tip for only one round). Then another friend ordered another round of shots with drinks and the same bartender not only took a $20 cash tip, but gave herself another $30 tip on the credit card for that one round!! After we confronted her and asked for the cash back, I was KICKED OUT by security! On top of this, people were complaining about the bartenders changing drink prices all day/night. DO NOT GO HERE! Never in my life have I been humiliated and kicked out of a bar...and for it to happen over me confronting the bartender who was STEALING...that just blows my mind!

Good music and food but the dance floor is always people line dancing and nothing else. Drinks are pretty expensive. They turned the NHL playoffs on for us though which was awesome. Good to go if you like line dancing bad if you wanna party and raise your glass while you dance.

Cool place. Came by for lunch and some music. Good singer and a really nice group of servers and bartender. Good prices and better music. Wings were ok. I hoped they wood have more smoke flavor. I'd come back for the music and cold beer.

Great fun! Good prices. The band was fun, free pool and foosball tables while waiting for band and/ or table. I had the stampede sampler, and I would not recommend it. The ribs were good, the brisket was WAY too fatty, and the pulled pork was okay but too dry. I tried some of my moms monte cristo and it was phenomenal! I would recommend that all day. Overall great place, if I'm ever in Nashville, I will return here.

Food is expensive but not good. 
Our waiter was terrible and had a attitude,  the tip was included in bill and the waitress didn't deserve it. Dance floor is nice but not impressed.

Food GREAT! but I couldn't even start eating my pizza bc the music was so loud we had to leave. I even tried to put some paper napkins in my ears to see if it would help.....it didn't. SERVICE was AWESOME!

Atmosphere was cool.  Bartender Yanet was the most unfriendly depressing person I have ever seen! Nashville is such a cool fun crowd I would highly suggest a super fun, bubbly person behind the bar.  Someone that makes you feel welcome would have set a better vibe for us to stay! Maybe it was a bad day but I work customer service and it's always show time!

Pizza is really good. Quality ingredients. A medium is the same size as a dominos large pizza. Haven't had anything other than their pizza but it is definitely worth it. If you are a ranch with your pizza guy/gal I highly recommend asking for 2 sides of ranch. It is so darn good. Staff seems to be mostly high schoolers on break and hipsters but it's a tight place with good pizza. 5 stars

I was staying at the Opryland resort for a conference and a Lyft driver recommended this place if I got tired of the resort. It did not disappoint. First of all, the food was well priced compared to the outrageous restaurants at the hotel. I had a chicken and a biscuit for $8.50 which is very reasonable for Nashville. The other great thing about this place is there is live music every night. I went on a Thursday and the band playing was very country- I mean from the 1920s and 1950s country. There was a set local crowed that goes these for this particular genere of music. During the few hours I was there I witnessed a self described drifter go on stage and play a guitar with the band and an 80+ year old Elvis impersonator get on stage to sing while the band members were collecting donations. I sat at the bar and immediately struck up conversation with a couple over their 80s who came their weekly for the music. The local crowd was very friendly and embraced me like I was one of their own. This is a Greta experience if you want to see a side of Tennessee/ the South we don't get to see in the Northeast.
LOVE this place.  Always has great service and fantastic music!
Food was great and very reasonable. Got in before a concert with no wait. Service was good as well
Excellent service and great food! They have live dancing lessons and great live music! Order the French fries! You get a combo of 3 types! The fried pickles were very good!

I stopped by here for lunch on a Monday afternoon. The place wasn't too busy and I managed to find a seat at the bar quickly. I loved that there was a duo singing and playing guitar, they were very talented and were taking requests of all sorts from patrons. I ordered a Yazoo pale ale by recommendation from the male bartender and it was very very good, light flavor and very smooth. I then ordered a pulled pork sandwich with fries from the female bartender near by, she was a little standoffish and only checked on me maybe twice while I was there. Other than that, the experience was well worth it while listening to great live music. The food was pretty average, though. I'd definitely come back to grab a beer and see another set of musicians onstage.

Soulshine was found by accident when looking for food Saturday night but was so so good!  I had the gluten free Godfather and it was delicious!  Add a side a ranch and it's so good  plus there was live music which is so Nashville and I loved it!
With the number of strong pizza offerings in the midtown area, this is much more a 3 star option and one worth trying if you want live music, big variety in toppings, and a college crowd.

Ok, new rule at Rippy's. You must sit at your table and not go to the bar to order a beer no matter how bad the service is. You need to wait patiently at your table. Waiter chewed me out for getting drinks at the bar when he wasn't around. They even called the manager and bouncer over when I told them they had to be kidding. I am a local resident so I wasn't intimidated based on past trips to this bar. So, no issue here, I will drink at the new Acme bar at the end of the strip. Left without incident but will never go back again.

We had a large bachelor party stop by for some beers and pizza. The service was the best I've had in a long time. To be able to keep 20 drunk males going with only one server is always impressive. She went above and beyond to help us. 

Kitchen sink pizza was good! Great wings too!
Too big to be fun.  This place was a little too polished for my taste.  I had fun but definitely prefer smaller places with better music.  Oh, and did I mention that it's owned by the Gaylord??

Partied here with a friend two weeks ago(will upload pics later) and it was pretty decent. This was my first time going since living here in Nashville. Drinks were ok, food wasnt too bad, but good Lord it was CROWDED! Atmosphere was fun and people were pretty cool. SIDE NOTE: 1.  Not a place to get dressed up for. It was hot as hell and comfort is very advisable. 2. GET THERE MUTHA EFFIN EARLY....and I do mean that literally if you want a decent seat or to find a park anywhere in the area.  We went  about 6:45pm and it was shoulder to shoulder.
You definitely aren't going for the food. Atmosphere is really good. Plenty of live music. If you are a BBQ lover then don't waste your time. Also the fries are horrible.

1- line dancing instructor was super hot- what a butt!
2- live music by some unknown who was nice enough to take pictures with us tourist types
3- pretty great food
4-free line dancing lessons with a hot guy
5- creepy horses by the bathrooms for photo ops
6- un-manned gift shop
7. three levels of awesome
8- only one level was open when I was there because of private parties
9- what more could you want than horses on the ceiling?
10- If I lived in Nashville I'd be here all the time.
The pizza was amazing, and Leah (the bartender and server) was incredibly friendly and attentive throughout the evening. Some of the best pizza and service I've had in a long time!
Good bbq ribs! I love the outdoor seating!!!!!!

Funky little place with pretty good pizza and a lively atmosphere. We dined here in July of 2016 before heading to Titan's stadium for the Guns and Roses concert. They had live music starting as we were leaving. Big outdoor dining area upstairs. Neat little place.

Not very impressed with them. Server was nice enough but I had to seek him out to pay our bill in which I ended up giving the money to a bartender or we would've been late for our Ryman show. The menus didn't have prices for drinks either. They were $9 each before a tip. The drinks we had were a Lynchburg Lemonade and Peach vodka drink. They were good but served in a plastic cup half the size of a real cup. Granted I realize they were paying for entertainment and we didn't pay a cover to get in, but the bands had been switching over at the time so we didn't even get to hear any music. Oh and they had a bathroom attendant who gets a tip along with the server.
Loved the atmosphere! Food was alright. Had the turkey blt. I have had better. The BBQ pulled pork nachos were awesome! Great southern taste if you are looking for something different

My husband and I came into Nashville for one night. Decided on the Wildhorse Saloon as I remembered hearing that it was good food and a good atmosphere. The atmosphere was good, the band that was playing was really good. Then we got to the food. The fried pickles that the had and the  locally brewed beer was the only thing that I enjoyed. I order brisket and pork, figuring I could have some good barbeque while in the south. Food came and the brisket and pork were very greasy and tasteless. The fried potatoes were over cooked and inedible.  Plus on top of all this we waited like 40 min even receive our food. Out waitress was pleasant though not very attentive. All in all I was not please. If you just want some good entertainment and have some drinks you'll be fine. Just will never recommend eating there again

At the Wildhorse for the first time. Expecting a lot but getting a bartender with absolutely no personality. She is acting as if we are putting her out ordering food and drinks. Place looks nice but maybe having a hospitable personality is not required to work here.

I've not seen an actual play at TPAC but the set-up looks like it is a great venue for that and there are few if any bad seats in the house.
My wife and I recently saw a rock concert here and for the type of show that it was--theatrical, engaging but not in need of huge audience participation movement (dancing, moshing, etc.)--this was a solid venue. We were near the front and had a great view but I could see that those behind us and up in the balcony likely all had a solid view. 
Valet parking here is not too pricey ($25) considering you'd spend that or more in most of the parking garages in the area on a typical evening and this way you don't have to trek through one in the middle of the night.
Concessions looked okay but pricey (though not more than say Bridgestone). For a rock show this place was a bit disorganized--we lined up in several separate lines only to find out that none were ours (a general purpose ticket-holding line is what we needed, seemed like it'd be the easiest to find). Performance time listed on the tickets was actually the time they planned to open the doors to the theater room and it wasn't until that point that we were even told which line to get in.

Good margaritas but they should be for $14.  Wings are terrible but the ribs were fantastic.  Go for the line dancing and atmosphere.   Food is mediocre at best but this place is a Nashville landmark.  Have fun - "ya'all."  ;)

The food was not that great.  I'd rather go to another eatery known to the locals, Peg Leg Porker, Jack's, etc...the bartenders here were ungrateful and looked agitated taking your order.  The music was not great- more fun at another bar without a cover (even just to eat).  This has clearly become a Nashville go to...begrudgingly.

We wet here on a Sunday afternoon, it was rainy out and Broadway was pretty quiet.  

We sat in the back where the band was playing, they were pretty good and they kept us entertained.

I got the pulled chicken sandwich and it was very good.  I like the fact that it is served without bbq sauce on it (you add your choice when it comes to the table).  

The food was good, service and location were all great.  The reason for the 4 star is because they sell RC cola products, yuck!
So awesome! Didn't get a chance to try the food but the ambiance was awesome. Great for a very chill night.

The food and service was great but a bit crowded in the place. Luckily we sat upstairs with a few of the main street. We ate the burgers but they were nothing out of the ordinary. My friend had a margarita but she barely tasted the alcohol.

Roger is the stereotypical d-bag bouncer. They cancelled line dancing multiple times, and as a tour leader that effs my game plan. If you're going to be a dick, Roger, and ask us to come back in an hour to linedance, don't be upset with us when we come back and you've cancelled again. I'm sure it wasn't your decision, but your overly aggressive bullshit is just gonna send us elsewhere. #fireroger

A TEN! A TEN! A FREAKIN TEN!!!!

Came to TPAC on June 21 to attend the Martini and Marionettes show. The show itself was in the Andrew Johnson Theater, on a lower level. When we got there, the crowd was buzzing around the food table and standing in a long line for drinks from the cash bar. 

The off thing to note was that there were no Martinis to be found. Liquor drinks, Yes. Martini, no. They were announcing before the show that it was OK to bring in your food and drink to teh show. Then once you sat down an automated message came on saying no food and drink. I lol'd. 

The show:  WOW!!!  That was an awesome show!!!! Phillip Huber was able to make the marionettes come to life on stage. The moves they made and the expressions they had were just so unique and well timed. Each character that came onto stage had it's own personality and skill set.  It was absolutely amazing!!! If Huber ever comes back, I want to be there!
Great family experience. Pulled pork sandwich was amazing! Excellent customer service! Awesome location on the strip with live music.

Popped into the 2nd Ave icon but was disappointed to find they don't play live music until like after 6pm. Had a delicious Bullitt Rye and went back to Broadway.  Wall to wall talent.  Seems they'd use that celebrity stage rep to showcase local talent.  Sure would make it a more enjoyable pit stop.

Very very slow and poor service. Food delivered was incorrect and server indicated that the food runner couldn't be tracked down to correct it. Definitely did not have a customer is always right attitude. I very seldom complain or have issues with service but this was extremely poor experience. By no means was there southern hospitality experienced from staff. 

The live classic country music was very nice and enjoyable. 

Food is ok but not exceptional. I like simple food which the menu is primarily comprised of. 

I am not sure whether I would ever give this place another try. If I did, I would likely sit at the bar. 




Overall, this could be a god experience of staffing is adjusted

Great service, good food and awesome live bands.  Kid friendly, line dancing.
We highly recommend the Wildhorse Saloon over the George Jones Restaurant.

This place is a must! We tried a few times to get in and the third time was a charm. The place is huge and they have a dance floor, full stage, multiple bars, and three floors. We got there around 4:45 and got seated immediately but when we left around 6 o'clock the line was out the door. There were three different singers when we went, the first guy wasn't the best I've heard all week, and I don't know how the others were. Our server was great and came by frequently and gave great recommendations.

This bar is on the corner in Broadway across from the Bridgestone arena in the heart of downtown Nashville.  I has two stories with the upper deck being an open/covered patio w/ a small stage.  There is at least one stage downstairs as well.

This place is pretty touristy, but for good reason: you should go there.  Plain and simple, it rocks.  There will be live bands to be there on there multiple stages most evenings.  This is Music City, after all, so every one playing and singing here will be trying to make it big, so the music will be top notch making for a great and rowdy experience.

The food is decent here and not too pricey.  Not the best barbecue I've had in the south but was a perfect compliment for the entertainment.  Drink specials seem to mostly include domestic bottle of beer and maybe some mixed drinks.

Side note: the first time I came here Ronnie Dunn popped up out of nowhere, took the 2nd floor stage and played four songs (June of 2013).  Afterwards he spent at least an hour being mobbed by riff-raff and hooligans (my wife and I included) for pictures and autographs, and he was very cooperative.  Seemed to be a somewhat normal occurrence here.

My boyfriend stopped in Nashville on a Sunday so naturally at 7-8, most places were closed. We settled on this place because we wanted to try some "southern" bbq since we're from Michigan. Honestly? It sucked. The waitress had a section of over 10 tables, so our service lacked. Not her fault at all, as I've worked food industry and 10 tables is at least double what someone who cares about service should make their servers do. My rum and coke was watered down. Our pulled pork sandwiches were so dry that I nearly choked on the first bite. They had one standard barbecue sauce that we had to drench our food in.

This is the kind of place that tourists need to avoid. The only reason they had a full house was because they were open, and they had a nice upstairs patio to suck people in like we were.

We entered expecting the same , lively club of 10 yrs ago. We entered and waited at the end bar for service which never came  I had to find the bartender for service
 I paid 11.oo for a cocktail and coke
 The dance floor filled with about 20 min for a dance lessons and left after the practice
The band was excellent.  There were maybe 20 people total . Dissapointed in my favorite club
We used to drive up from Knoxville just for them

Victoria Nellums

This place is terrible!! Don't waste your time. What a tourist trap! The BBQ is dry and not cooked in-house. Live music is a draw but the food and drink leaves much to be desired. If you're in the mood for BBQ, it's much better to go to Jacks and hit up a live music spot afterwards. Prices here are extremely high as well. I would not recommend this spot.

Food was great and you can't beat the atmosphere...however, the best part was our waitress!!! Hayley from Pennsylvania was quick, helpful, and honestly pretty funny! We had a blast with her. Definitely coming back.
Can't rate the food or drinks. We never got waited on. It was a Wednesday afternoon. Not that busy. Bye bye.
If you like live music it is the place.  The portions are huge.  The food was good but not great.  We were seated without menus and napkins in our bucket so we had to ask for both.

Ambiance was cool and line dancing lessons were fun but totally underwhelmed by the food. Whoever said the fried pickles were their best ever has no taste, Hooters has way better fried pickles. Burgers had no seasoning. Service was good

It holds its promise. Very nice venue, fast service,
Line dancing and great bbq. We had the brisket, cheeseburger, chicken tender and grilles cheese. Just great. And our waitress was really nice. 
We also had the famous fried pickle in apps. Really gwood:)

Out of downtown near the Grand Ole Opry. The food was basic bar food, although the chicken strips were large slices of chicken breasts. The place has a funky fun feel and the crowd likes to dance. Saturday night was Nathan Belt and the Buckles, a real rockabilly sound with lots of 50/60's country hits. Any singer that can do Roy Orbison is good with me.

I've been to several shows at TPAC in both Jackson Hall and Polk Hall. The venue itself is absolutely phenomenal. Great seats in all sections no matter what theatre you happen to be in. I've seen 3 Broadway touring shows and 1 solo performance show at TPAC. Tickets are affordable depending on what show you happen to be seeing. The only downside is that they have no student rush and rarely ever is there a lottery rush, so no discounts unless you're in a large group. 

Other than those tiny exceptions, TPAC is an excellent structure and one of the finest theatres in the state.

We were looking for a place to eat on Labor day because it seemed like many restaurants are closed on the Holiday in Nashville.  Luckily, yelp guided us to Soulshine.  We had some pizza and drinks and enjoyed two live bands during our time here.   This restaurant is on the second floor with another restaurant below it,  and it has a second floor outside seating area.

Great atmosphere. Awesome stage with good music.  Affordable food with a good selection of pizzas, sandwiches, and Cajun food.  However, I was very disappointed in their limited selection of draft beers.  I felt a place of this caliber should have a better microbrew selection!

We have seen several shows here now.  We particularly enjoy the Tennessee Repertory Theater (now Nashville Rep) and the Nashville Ballet.  If you've read my reviews, then you've probably guessed my biggest complaint: parking.  We tend to pay $20 for parking at every event.  However, I've recently read that the library offers special $5 parking during off hours and weekends, so we are keen to try that next time.  We also prefer to purchase tickets online in advance to skip the lines.

The theaters are cozy without being crowded, the staff is courteous, and we've sat in just about every section and have not found a bad seat in the house.  We don't usually partake in concessions so I can't really comment on that, and based on the lines after the show, we have no desire to try the valet parking.  The bathrooms are inconveniently located, which is the only complaint I have about TPAC so far.

TPAC is definitely a recommended Nashville experience!

I was here for a work event on a Wednesday evening. The massive location highlighted a sparse crowd in the restaurant on the first floor. Our private party split the second floor with another party. The second floor had a stocked bar, restrooms, shuffleboard, foosball and pool tables. There are a ton of seating options too. Some of us conversed at the high top tables and others say around the balcony handrail to watch the line dance lesson. Even with half a dozen people participating, there was live music and a couple employees leading by example. I bet this place is rocking on the weekend.
Food was pretty decent for BBQ brisket served buffet style. I'd skip the mini pies for dessert though, they didn't taste like much.

As expected the place was packed... my buddy Adam was manning the bar and serving like a boss. I couldn't sit outside because of the crowd but inside was nice and friendly. The beer is cold and the Tomato and basil pizza was fine! Love this place and always have a good time here.

Best. Place. Ever.

I had the pleasure of visiting the Nashville Palace on a recent trip to Nashville. We were staying nearby and checked the Palace out on the basis of a recommendation. We loved it so much we went back a second time before we left. It is located in a strip of stores that include the Willie Nelson Museum, where I also spent a great deal of time but that's another story. Anyway, the Nashville Palace is a honkytonk of vintage variety frequented by locals. They feature live music - Western Swing, anyone? You can dance if you are so inclined, and the food is great at a great price. AND THEY SERVE MOONPIES FOR DESSERT. The next time you find yourself in Nashville, definitely make time for a stop at the Nashville Palace. You will not be disappointed.

I've never felt more disrespected in my life.... We ordered drinks through the bartender because our waiter hadn't been back in over 20 mins. Instead of apologizing our waiter told us to f@@$ off and that we should only order through him. After explaining the situation I tried to get my debit card back from the bartender which told me they didn't have my tab, after arguing she finally gave me my card back and I was told to leave the bar. I asked for the manager who at the time seemed very polite and after explaining the situation I was told that if what I said was true, those involved would be fired. I still has to leave which I did respectfully but I had to come back to let my friends know what happened... The security guard agreed with me that I was right but still couldn't let me in. I loved this bar and actually had come back for my last stop of the night but after my experience I will never go back and until they make changes I would suggest that no one else go their either

The barbecued have chicken was surprisingly good today. My expectations were surpassed and I give them credit.  The service was also good but a bit slow, we set upstairs it was not very busy but it didn't seem to take it while for our server to deliver.

The music setup upstairs is not as good as the music on the first floor in my opinion.  

Of the honky-tonks in Nashville Rippys is one of my top two but somehow seems to be overshadowed by some of the more popular joints down the street

Oh TPAC, you never let me down!

With 3 different auditoriums, TPAC can host popular comedians, broadway shows, smaller theatrical productions, concerts, operas, the ballet, and everything in between! I appreciate the variety of offerings they have, and always enjoy coming to shows here. 

They also allow adult beverages in the show, and will pre-order drinks for you so you can swing by the bar during intermission. So convenient! If you are in Andrew Jackson Hall (the largest one) they recently opened a bar INSIDE the auditorium. That just rules!

You can park for free at the capitol just off Charlotte down the hill a bit, and I always do that to avoid paying to park :) 

My only complaint is that their bathrooms aren't super accessible or convenient, and I feel their signage is small. The restaurants also seem to be crowded no matter when you go. 

I appreciate you TPAC, and am excited to see which shows grace your stage this year!

A regular stop for us when in Nashville best part about the place is the music by Paul Pace. On 5/31/16 the bartender was very attentive, kept drinks filled and even helped us order something that wasn't on the menu. It is a bar so don't expect 5star dining, but you should enjoy your visit!
Ribs and side dishes were amazing!! Beer was cold and the music was great!!

Walking in and wanting to listen to the entertainment while approached by a server stating you cannot sit at the tables unless you order a entrée per person.  Mind you this establishment is not at capacity, in fact vacancy outweighed capacity.  As a business you have a few objectives however a primary one of creating value through revenue and more so, gross profit and margins.  Liquor and beer have greater margins than food meaning costs associated with service and materials are inclusive.  Makes no business sense to push patrons out the door due to semantics.  Most of all, I feel sorry for the entertainers making a living having to reside in a poor environment with a great propensity of potential customer and tippers walking out the door. Suggestion - communicate mission statement as well as enlighten those  servers that have a poor attitude as well as a selfish mentality.  The only reason that any of us have a job or a career is that there is some service rendered and or a good received by a business and only viable if margins are reached.  Good luck Rippy's.  Straighten out service to drive foot traffic and a loyal customer base...one time tourists will not promote longevity.

Great music in two spots downstairs and the covered patio upstairs.  The BBQ is great - one of the old standby's on Broadway.  Friendly staff.  They do have TV's if you are interested in sports.  The patio on the roof is a good spot for music and broadway people watching.  It can get a little crazy before big events at Bridgestone.  And remember to tip the musicians - that's really how they make a living.

The pizza was good, but overpriced. The service was really good. They'll charge you for extra anything (I saw a review on yelp that they charged someone for ice!) but the pizza was good. The 8 inch pizza is pretty small to be a meal, we ordered salads and they were $4 and $4.50 each!! For side salads! we originally chose this place because it advertised live music and the music didn't start until 9...and the waitress couldn't tell us anything about the band that was starting. They do have a nice selection of beers on tap (local beers!) which was nice. Ultimately the environment and the service and the food was good. It was highly overpriced though which makes me not want to go back. That's really where the stars are lost. And the charges for extras.
Ribs and.sausage were fantastic! Music was good, if not a little loud! Great service!

What a disappointment- I was expecting a 
country bar/restaurant. When we arrived they had line dancing lessons - awesome!!!  When the band came out to play - I'm assuming that it will be a country band (HELLO- we are in Nashville) that we could use our line dance lessons. Nope, I was wrong, it was a rock band, granted a good rock band but we were expecting country music. Won't be back - will tell my friends not to bother!

Desperate for a place to sit on memorial day weekend, 

We went up to the second floor, the smell of fresh vomit greeted us.
Sat down, a rush and haggered waiter took our drink order.

Sat around for a few, ate some wings and onion rings, it was just not a good night to be there, bailed quickly.

After we dropped off our luggage at a nearby hotel, this was a great place to unwind after a long day of traveling. They had live music, great drink prices. I wanted to  try the moonshine cherries. Maybe next time. Have a beer, hear some music and check out the hokey museums next store. The perfect way to start our first visit to Nashville.
Very good food, band was very good. I just didn't like the fact that people were smoking right outside our window ruined our lunch hopefully they can fix that in the future for other guest

This was our lunch stop on our honky tonk walking tour. The music was pretty good, the bartender was attentive but the food. Yes! Get the rib wraps, probably the neatest (as in less messy) way to get your meat, smoke, sauce and coleslaw. Paired with turnip greens - so flavorful my mouth is watering right now! - you have the makings of a memorable meal experience. The place is bigger than it looks on the outside, so don't let the crowds deter you; c'mon in!

Noel and I decided to grab some lunch before hitting the mall...I hate going to the mall and fighting the crowd shopping, much less trying to eat..so we went to Nashville Palace for a quick bite before our RETAIL THERAPY Section..

I decided on the restaurant..I knew before we went in that its a Touristy TRAP but HEY, sometimes you have to give it a go...I am a local now, 4 1/2 yr resident of Nashville..but sometimes I like to blend in with the tour-eestas...

We went into the Nashville Palace and it is a little dark like a bar...there was a guy singing on the platform sitting on a barstool strumming his guitar...at first he wasn't have bad but as the 45 minutes slowly passed by he was featuring his song choices for one older man...he knew by name  BERT I think it was and he was wearing out the genre with oldies but goodies ...but they were like the funny songs not really anything worth listening too over and over..they were all sort of the same after you get through the first 3-10...lol !!!

Noel ordered the Mushroom Swiss with fries and I ordered the hot wings with blue cheese for dipping..and the burger was just PLAIN...and small and the fries were slightly cold..the wings were okay but sort of over cooked. It wasn't bad but it wasn't that good..my biggest problem was the FLIES...they had the window/garage doors opened and the flies were so darn bad...they were so darn  aggravating...to the point of maddening...I will definitely NOT eat there again for the sheer fact the darn flies drove me away..

I want to eat somewhere where they appreciate you and treat you with inside dining free of bugs and in the air conditioning. If I wanted to eat with the bugs, I would EAT outside on the Patio...I will NOT EAT here again...
The service was slow, but heck she was the only one working. She had to be bartender and waitress to the whole restaurant including the patio..on a friday afternoon around 12:30...they should have had her some help.

As all my reviews, I ask if you want to go here .go here..your opinion and experience maybe way different from mine..I just choose NOT to dine here again..
Valet parking is a nightmare. I hour to get you car after the show. 60 seats in a row. Don't sit in the middle unless you have no plans to get up during the production.

This is a bar with several bands that play from 11am to 2am. The lack of cover means you directly tip the band when the tip jar circles the bar. Very small place and band sound is great. The place ran with 3 bar maids, so you may wait for drink. One of bar maids had shirt that states clearly"I can see you, I'm just ignoring you". Be patient, they make really good drinks, lots of alcohol. 

Ok if you order food. You are in a bar! Don't expect a five star cloth napkin experience. The food is decent bar food abd the guy serving it cooked it too. The fried bolonga sandwich was worth $6 with fries.  The burger was a simple burger, better than fast food place but not gourmet by any stretch. Again bar with bar food. Not restaurant with a lounge!

Get your beer, or your drink and you can hit the dance floor too. This is real music place. Tourists are welcome, just remember there's a lot of locals too. Act like you've been to a bar before. They will call us tourists out to dance. They are being friendly, but are willing to laugh at you if you can't or won't dance. It's all in good fun.

We were here for a private event on the 3rd floor so I can't comment on service. 

The food was awesome though. I've had fried pickles before and these were way better than any other. The pulled pork and brisket were delicious and the moon pie pudding I could have eaten more of. So, 4 stars on food. 

I may have felt differently had we had to pay a cover charge and sit downstairs.

Great time at Rippys!! The music was fantastic, I don't remember the name of the group Singing but they were very talented and added to the ambiance of the restaurant. I had the chili and it had just the right amount of spice while maintaining great flavor. The chili came with corn cakes that were much like pancakes made from corn meal. The staff were wonderful and attentive, this was a great lunch spot.

This review is solely on the food and not the bar.  We stopped after working up an appetite after hitting up the Broadway honkey tonks.  Unfortunately the BBQ here didn't live up to the great music we had heard earlier.  We ordered the pulled pork.  The meat was a little too fatty and grizzly for my liking.  The sides were the best part of the meal.  Decent coleslaw and onion rings.     

Tip: try the spicy BBQ sauce.

When you visit Nashville, TN, the number 1 domestic destination, be sure you come downtown, to Honky Tonk Row. 
While you are there, be sure you visit Rippy's, corner of 5th and Broadway, across from The World Famous Tootsies Orchid Lounge and the Bridgestone Arena!

Rippy's has the best barbecue around, dry or wet ribs, pulled pork sandwiches or plates, sweet potato fries and your favorite beverage. 

All of that and the sound of a good, live band, you are in for a good time. 

Good food, good eats and good service. 

If you experience Rippy's once, you'll go back.

So my initial experience was pleasant.  I was sitting at the bar by myself and found out I had friends meeting me here. So I asked for a table. The host did not want to give me a table because he said I had to eat dinner. I sit back at the bar and realize there are plenty of people at the tables just having drinks. Not to mention it's a Sunday afternoon and the place was DEAD! Then my friends come and they get a table, saying exactly what I just told the guy.  First negative experience I had in Nashville. Don't want to throw race into this but I am a minority and my company looked more like the locals.

We came for drinks, no food. I cannot comment on their food because we didn't have any, but the menu looked great and the drinks were fantastic! The artist playing was absolutely awesome. They were teaching line dancing lessons while we were there. It was a lot of fun and a very kind, friendly and fun atmosphere. Definitely a must see when visiting Nashville!

Not a good review. We got there at 1145 and they sat us. They quit serving food at 1200. They served us cold chicken and cold fries. Then questioned why we were sitting there. I imagine if you get there early it's different, but I can only review what I witnessed. Will never go back. Too many options. Go to honky tonk central or the stage.

Overpriced barbecue, the only reason I walked in the place was Jack's is closed on Sunday. The pulled pork had no flavor. And they offer no combinations. And did I say overpriced?

On a side note, the place was empty, server (Victoria C #448) made us move to one of their tiny two place tables. Guess what, still empty when I left. 

And one last thing barbecue sauce, only two, one too sweet and one too spicy.
Still standing in the lobby sweating despite multiple announcements to be seated and enjoy the show.  Really?  How about you open the doors so all these people can go in?
Wow pulled pork was awsome. The bands were typical for Broadway during the early evening.  Go for the bbq and quick service.
Great atmosphere. I tried the Apollo Po Boy and it was great. Fast and friendly service. Great artwork and music instruments on the wall. Good value for the money. Definitely will be back here soon.
Went in here two separate nights performers were all fantastic.. If you get hungry you have to try the pork loin sandwhich.. Phenomenal !!

Had the pork loin melt with coleslaw on the sandwich with the potato salad on the side. Potato salad was a definite pass... way to sweet. It needed something to break that sweetness up like some onion or more salt but just way to sweet. The sandwich was very tasty. The pork was great. I wish that had given me a little more slaw on top and used thinker Texas toast but overall a good sandwich. 

The music and view upstairs was great while we dined. We thought the drinks were a little overpriced but that seems to be par for the course on this street.

It was a decent venue whilst without a cover. I had the Jalapeño Burger, which was pretty decent with the spicy table sauce. Between the two sauces, the darker sauce was favoured by my table. The stampede platter was well-received by 2 people at my table, but one person said that, despite the different cuts, the taste was very similar and got tiresome. Beer and entertainment was fun to watch. Overall, a good experience.

The only saving Grace here, is the super sweet upstairs waitress and the band!
We had the sampler platter..... It was filling
Saw a really good local performance of Inherit the Wind here. Very nice venue. Cheap food and snack options and nice staff.

The food was better than I expected! We went at lunch with 3 kids & it was fine for them. My daughter had the kids brisket & it was awesome. Enough for an adult. Pork sandwich was good too. Fried chicken was not so great. Ok margarita.

We stubbled upon Soulshine by accident, we were very impressed would highly recommend.  our server Trent was awesome! We had a mix of appetizers and some drinks. The music was great, had a good variety of performers.

I really appreciate all the different shows that TPAC is able to bring to Nashville. Over the years seen a few shows here, from Madama Butterfly, Les Misérables, the Nutty Professor, & Lisa Lampanelli, Robert Irvine Live and tonight Matilda. They've got a lot of different content presented throughout the year. 

The TLAC actually consists of actually 4 different sized auditoriums, the Andrew Jackson Hall (2,472 seats), James K. Polk Theater (1,075), Andrew Johnson Theater (256) and War Memorial Auditorium: 1,661 across the street. I've been in all 4 of the theatres, tonight we were in the Andrew Jackson. The theatre is huge. When you're in the orchestra, it's hard to see all the seats that are above in the balcony. The staff is there to assist you to find your seat and most of them are retired folks from the community that are very sweet. 

They've got a bar in the back of the Andrew Jackson Hall called Bar Seven. It's pretty much like the other little bars in TPAC. The prices aren't cheap, but they're not crazy. I wouldn't get drunk here, obviously, so prices are okay. I've posted a picture with the prices of the drinks at the cash bar (they also take cards). 

Parking isn't too much of an issue. They've got a few parking garages that charge around $10. They've also go valet up front that is $18. That's kind of high, but a bargain compared to what Schermerhorn Symphony Center charges at $27! I honestly have never had a problem finding street parking down the hill. If you show up 45 minutes to an hour before showtime, you'll probably find a parking spot fo free!

TPAC is pretty good about sending emails with what is going on, without going overboard. You can buy tickets online and the site is easy to use, with picking out seating a breeze. Nashville is lucky to have such a strong artistic community. With TPAC leading the way.

The cheeseburgers go two different types of cheese. Two!! It's absolutely what makes their burgers so special. It's not my favorite burger in Nashville but it's in my top ten. 

So the reviews are correct. This is your typical roadside dive bar. It's not clean, it's not disgusting, but it's not clean. They have plenty of games to keep you occupied and the beer runs frequently. If I lived on that side of time I would probably go more often but since I'm on the east side I would rather go to Dino's for a burger and a beer. If you love dives, this is the place for you!
Melody was awesome. Stumbled in randomly right before a big concert on the street and somehow snagged a table. Melody kept the drinks coming was personable and so adorable!!!

Food is bland. The great sounding low and show beef brisket dip, of a nice blend of cheese abd beef with the most worthless crackers. The dip should be on tortillas, I even had such a bad taste from crackers, I asked for tortillas chips. No even though they are sErved with another dish not an option. 

Rally no reason to go here other than free with room card. Save yourself! The city has so many places. Don't go to end unless you are out of choices.

Horrible service. We waited for an hour for our table and then they told us there was a wait and refused to seat us when there was not a single person standing like we were for a table. Do not dine here unless you want to be treated like crap.
Food was great and live entertainment was just as great! I would totally recommend​ the pancake pull pork​ sandwich! 100% taste and different​!

We had the best server, very attentive and polite. He made our experience very enjoyable. This was our first time here. We moved from Ca to Tn about 3 months ago and have been searching for a place with great bbq, delicious drinks I loved the peach something drink yum yum yum. Pulled pork plate was amazing, the half smoked chicken was divine, the meat was cooked to tenderness and falling apart Yum and had lots of flavor. Can't believe we waited so long to visit. We will definitely be back again and again! Thank you, keep up the great food and service!,,,  Josh & Susan Skinner. 925 584 9824 I can be reached if you have any questions. We love this place.

It's very loud! We had the bbq & wasn't worth a return trip to get again or to recommend. Very bland & uneventful This place is your typical bar period. It was very crowded so if that's not your thing, skip it. The dance floor can be overwhelming! Yet another tourist trap in downtown.

This was a really fun place to visit on our Nashville Birthday weekend adventure. Apparently, after reading the reviews of others, we came on the right evening and the stars were aligned in such a way that allowed us to get through the line to the front door fairly quickly and a table on the first floor immediately. Don't ask me how we did it, but it can be done. We didn't get a chance to order anything though because we didn't see table service and the bars were a little too busy--but, no one asked us to leave or give up our table. I guess it was the perfect amount of people for that evening--quick entry and good table all while still being busy and fun.

We came for the live music and the line dancing instruction and both were great! I think that I learned more how to stomp at the same time as everyone else more than a line dance...but if you ever ask me, I line danced while "honkey tonkin'" in Nashville.
Pulled chicken sandwich w curly fries, super yummy! Good drinks, friendly staff, good place to stop for Nashville experience!
Best bar on Broadway to listen to live music. Good atmosphere upstairs to view the strip and have a drink with some good music

I worked here for a few years. I still tell people they must go here for the fried pickles, line dancing, and horses on the ceiling, despite how things ended. I myself have returned a few times to certain private events and other random nights out and it's always a good time. 3 floors and 5 total bars here..very grand. FAMILY FRIENDLY WAHOO...it's the only place I can think of that is 100% family friend in town..there are a few places that are all ages during certain hours, that I would feel as a parent Id have to be really cautious and monitoring my kids with...BUT, not at Wildhorse...kids are welcome and they will have a great time. There's also games like pool, air hockey, and a little arcade so the kids (or your inner kid) will have a blast. Honestly, I'd say get here at like 6:30 or 7 and stay all night to just hang..but PLEASE tip your waiters because they are working really hard and have to run up and down not only 3 flights of stairs, but a basement where they fill up huge bins full of ice. This was a really fun, but challenging job..so tip tip tip them. ;)
They are now doing renovations and I'm excited to see how it turns out. It's over the top tourism, but my gosh they always have great SOLID live bands, (though I've yet to play heehee), and the food is probably the best for the price you'll find downtown. Try the pickles, the brisket, and a giant margarita...and bring your boots cuz if Skyla is working, you'll get the best dang line dance lesson in town, y'all !

Food...not good.  So the best thing about Soul Shine Pizza is the venue.  They have a nice upstairs patio.  The band was pretty decent and it's a good place to listen to some music and visit with friends.  

They have a good bar selection, but the food was pretty bad.  We were there for a party and so they brought out a bunch of stuff...a couple of different pizzas, nachos, breadsticks and chicken wings.  The chicken wings and buffalo chicken pizza were ok.  For the most part, the pizza was awful.  No flavor and greasy, which is a bad combo.  

Maybe I would repeat Soul Shine Pizza just for a hang out spot.  But I definitely wouldn't bother with the pizza.  

I have 2 GF quotes from this outing:
"Best thing here is the diet coke"
"Not worth the calories"

The atmosphere was great, the band was great, and the food was great. Our server on the other hand... was horrible. We had Jelani A aka "Lani"... up until the very end he was good. He messed up on our bill, actually had put the wrong order in for me,  and he didn't give the correct change to my friend. When I received my bill of $15, I gave a 20% tip which is $3 (out of courtesy) He actually went out of his way to ask if I was Canadian... not thinking anything of it I just answered no. He proceeded to yell across the restaurant that Canadians never tip! And it wasn't just a one comment deal! My friends who were in the bathroom even heard it. He literally threw a fit that I can him a 20% tip off of a $15 bill, and I didn't even have any alcohol! I would like to say I'd come back but Lani put a bad taste in my mouth and I hope after speaking with the manager that he received corrective action for his behavior.

I stopped by Soulshine Pizza Factory in Franklin for a quick lunch. I ordered the homemade tamales topped with chili and I was blown away by the freshness of the tamales. I will definitely add Soulshine Pizza Factory to my list of restaurants to dine.
Food is ok, nothing amazing...dont just come for the food. Overwhelming dance floor and stage and plenty of seating. Open atmosphere, seems to be a good bar..just not great food
Great pizza, and even better music.  Came here on a Saturday night during a bachelor trip to Nashville, I would return every trip through the area.    Saturday night was a blast here.

Stuff I like:
The awesome patio
The CCR Pizza (8 inch for $10) - SO good!
Really good service, even on a busy Friday night
the Bread Pudding
Cool building

Stuff I don't like:
nothing!

Overall: An average bbq food joint for large crowds.

Ambience: The place is huge from inside, spanning multiple floors of seating arrangement and bars. Music was really good, with live bands on two floors.

Drinks: There's a bar on every floor, which is great. I paid $70 for six bottles of beer. That's outrageous. The bartenders were attentive, so that's a plus.

Food: We ordered pulled pork wrap, sandwiches, ribs, Mac-n-Cheese, Beans, and a few more things. The food was great, mostly because we were really hungry. It definitely wasn't unique bbq. Any restaurant in Memphis (Beale St.) does it better.

Service: For a place this busy, the service was phenomenal. We were seated fairly quick, attended to with water, sauces, and napkins. The food was on spot, and there were no mess ups. A+ on service.
Pork Loin melt was reallllly tasty. Great recommendation by the staff. Music was awesome. I sat near the (open door) entrance and froze to death so I left earlier than I would've.

Good ribbs and great music. Had a good time while having a good meal. This place is right int he mix of all the other places in downtown Nashville. They had two guys on stage playing. Made the meal go by fast. I had the ribbs and liked them. I have had better, but they were good.

Visited November 2011

The Palace is such a fun place! Very laid back compared to places on Broadway but the music is top notch. I was impressed at how only two very hard working servers managed to get food and drinks out to a packed house. When you don't want to fight for a table and pay big bucks for parking on Broadway, the Nashville Palace is a great alternative.

We had a party of 5 from California and Louisiana out celebrating a 16th wedding anniversary. As we were leaving my mother was stopped by 2 different male employees accusing us of not paying. We just had multiple people from our table fighting over who was going to pay the check! The employees were extremely disrespectful and verbally attacking my mother. There is a certain way to ask. Don't treat paying customers like criminals.

I'm glad we stumbled upon Rippy's because based on their reviews on this site, they were not on my radar during our first trip to Nashville. We decided to give the place a shot midday on a Thursday and it was not busy at all. I am not a fan of their downstairs, could be the way the bar is set up, you cannot see the band playing from one side of the bar so spots are limited. There is also not a big area to stand downstairs without feeling like you're in the way. On our way upstairs we were met with a security dude who was a jerk. That was the impression I got from him from the second we got there and I observed him while we were there and he didn't change my impression of him at all. There were two guys by the top of the stairs who leaned over to look outside and he told them they couldn't look outside. Seriously? He was loving being in a position of power and it was evident by the way you talked to people who came in the place. 

I felt that way with most of the staff, not the bartenders though. The bartenders upstairs were great. They kept refilling my water and stayed on top of getting us more drinks throughout the entire time we were there. The bathroom upstairs is absolutely gross. The door, which I've attached a photo of came off the hinges completely and the main door to the entrance of the woman's bathroom wouldn't close either so these poor girls had to use the bathroom with the broken hinged door in the open for everyone to see, it was kind of awful.

You'd think after hearing all this our time here was awful but was actually a blast, solely because of the bands that played. On the afternoon we came in here there were two guys and a girl and they were great, took requests and played some great music. There were a couple bachelorette and bachelor party groups up there but for the most part it was pretty laid back compared to other bars in the area. We came back Friday night and had the best freakin' time. The band playing was phenomenal and the girl playing the fiddle was outstanding. They were a fun, lively band and we didn't want to leave. We kept saying, "Okay after this song we are leaving" and they kept playing great song after great song. We had secured seats at the bar with a great view of the band so we really had no reason to leave. The bartenders upstairs were again on top of refilling our drinks. People were up front dancing and having a blast. When we decided to leave, we ventured downstairs and again, thought it was boring, felt like two completely different bars. 

Moral of the story is, definitely come here and go upstairs, check out the band that's playing. Stay if you can secure a decent seat at the bar or at a table and get the nachos. We didn't have them but people around us did and they looked absolutely delicious. We will definitely be back to Rippy's next time we visit, hopefully the bathroom door is fixed by then.
Mr. Rippy and Mr. Goldberg, you own many lucrative establishments in Nashville. You have the money. Fix your female bathroom. It's been broken for months.

lololololololololololololol

i did the cupid shuffle here on a wednesday night.

First off their pizza is very good and the crust is just the right thin/thick, more on the thin side though. But my complaint is, the beer menu...  over half of the beers on the menu were not available, everyone I asked for was denied because they dont have it anymore. What?! Then take it off the menu!  It was ridiculous.  I ended up just asking, well, what do you have?  He started listing them off until I heard one I liked.  It should not be that complicated to order a beer at a place that carries such a variety of beers, or is supposed to.

My fiancé and I went here last Saturday. This place is big, clean in the area, I think. We ordered salt and vinegar peanuts, chicken wings, and BBQ ribs. The peanuts were ok, but chicken wings and BBQ ribs were very good. The ribs were glazed with honey I think.

I always feel at home at Twin Kegs. The bartenders are friendly and you can drink to your heart's content on a strict budget. Shuffleboard is a great way to pass the time, and it's the perfect place to sit and watch a game without being crowded by a million midtown-ers. My favorite dive-bar in town!

Service was slow. Our waitress never checked up on us and we used cash to pay and left shortly after getting our food. The place wasn't busy and we only ordered a side of fries... it was a disappointment.

Nashville Palace has a great dance floor with a lot of good bands. Their food is pretty good it can take a while for you to get it but it's normally due to the high volume of customers. I would definitely recommend people to visit this bar!

Sooo this was an impulse buy to have dinner and live music.  Seating was scarce. The food was mediocre and the music was worse. All of the meat tasted watery ... on a good note, the bartenders were both pretty and efficient.  Doubt I'll go back.
Cool atmosphere/decor. Service was fine for lunch. I've only been once but found the pizza to be very average and overpriced. Too much competition in Nashville to be average. Won't be back.

Touristy? Yes. But that doesn't have to be a bad thing. 
The atmosphere is actually pretty damn fun (even if you're just watching line dancers) and the food is surprisingly awesome. Packed with flavors and grease - exactly what you'd want in Nashville.
Sadly, my favorite sandwich in the world - their Western Monte Cristo - was taken off the menu which brings my review from a 5 to a 4.

Had a good time, went in to listen to music and have a drink. The bartenders were friendly and the place was homey.
Service was quick and pleasant. Music started so I decided to  order the food...it was bar food but between the music and atmosphere it passed. I had chicken wings, quesadilla and sweet potato fries...all were good for the bar.
Had  a good time...good music, good service,  good customers and it was clean.

The barbecue is great overall but the fried pickles are what brings me back. They're deliciously salty, dill pickle spears with a crispy battered outside. Seriously. An entire pickle. Fried. 

The service is commendable (even at midnight) and the food always comes out popping hot. No complaints here.

Super basic atmosphere. Music was enjoyable. Had chili with corn cakes. I thought corn cakes wold not be pancakes but something to pick up with my fingers. It was an OK place, but there is so much to explore in Nashville.

We stopped for pizza but ordered wings and Po boys instead. The wings with the dry jerk seasoning were amazing..very moist and juicy.  The sandwiches were quite good as well..we ordered the half as we weren't very hungry..r hey were small but good. We will definately come back..good food..good music and good prices.

A week after seeing the opening of Rent, I went to watch/experience a concert in the Andrew Jackson Hall..
Again, great kudos to the wide aisles so people can pass without the whole row standing up to allow one person to pass..
Aisles are lit for good movement in the dark.
And sound; the sound was good. The accoustics are good.  I would definitely return for more concerts in this auditorium.

Yes! Yes! Yes! I got the pulled chicken sandwich and some others in my group got the pulled pork sandwich and pulled pork salad. They all enjoyed theirs. My pulled chicken sandwich was on point. I was happy that they smoked it dry so I could add sauce at my discretion. The sandwich and one side were reasonably priced. I will go again when visiting Nashville.
I've been here many times before and enjoyed it! I'm only giving 4 stars because their concessions stand is pretty gross.

They accused me of having a fake ID the moment we sat down at the bar upstairs. The bartender and bouncer both bent my ID and scrutinized it then came back and told me it was fake. I have used my ID at countless establishments and never had a problem before, including nearly every bar on Broadway. I am from a different state, Maryland, so my ID looks different than what they are used to getting. I would never recommend this place to anyone, which is a shame because the live music really was pretty good. I did not appreciate them demeaning me and accusing me of being a liar. There are much better bars along Broadway and I would take my business there in a heartbeat.

Went for the CMA FEST, my mom and I had lunch there where we ordered a pretty good amount of food. The "World Famous Fried Pickles" we're good but nothing I would order again, the Caesar salad was yummy, the Chicken wings were my favorite and the moonshine margarita was marginal. Overall the dining experience was nice with good  few really great live artists. 

Since our first experience was good we decided to venture back following the CMA Fest concert, let me just say I was excited to line dance and drink! I patiently stood at the bar for 40 minutes and waited to be served, I was looked at once and said, "hi" and the very rude bar tender said, "Oh no honey, I have to go back and serve the other side of the bar" at that point I gave up! I shook it off and went out to the dance floor where they were teaching a line dance. They taught a VERY basic dance then the lesson ended. It was the only time the dance floor was full then they said "OK lessons are over." Needless to say we were disappointed and headed off to a different Honky Tonk on Broadway. This place needs more bar tenders, more dancing, and a staff that isn't stretched so thin! I missed the Bobby Bones book signing because the waiter took 25 minutes to come back and grab our credit card for the bill.

I will say this, the place has potential it just needs a little help!

I am in town doing an automotive program in the Opryland area and wandered down to see the cars in front of Cooter's and heard the music that was coming out of the Palace at about 4:30 on Monday afternoon. While not a huge country fan, I recognized the quality of the performer (that turned out to be Nathan Belt) and decided to enter and order a drink at the bar. He was really good and I stayed for his entire set plus another 30-40 minutes of the next act, Ike Johnson and The Roadhouse Rangers. I WILL be back this week, maybe even tonight ...

oh, had the wings (not the hot ones, but had the hot sauce on the side), excellent !!!

A great venue for QUALITY local music!!!!

We stopped by here for happy hour before going to some other bars hearing they were good. We go in to find a poor happy hour but we didnt mind because we were told there was a band playing. We went upstairs to find the lead singer just talking the whole time asking questions  which was annoying. The beer I ordered came in a chilled glass and anyone who knows beer knows that waters down the beer. The nachos we ordered were horrible. We get that its a pizza place but the nachos were 9.99 for about 15 chips. We pay the same price at other places for huge plates that we cant finish. We definitely felt like we didnt get our moneys worth here! The amount you should get for a side. The salsa tasted like straight marinara and the gin and tonic my girlfriend ordered was too strong to drink. Hope the pizzas better.

Really so many better places to eat and to enjoy good music and dancing.  I paid the cover, then waited for my table.  During my wait I felt like I was on a bad cruise with the cruise directors trying to get people to dance.  I was there for an hour and did not hear one, not one, country song.  I heard the Electric Slide and a Saturday night fever song!  This place is now nothing more than a tourist trap.
Food was great, pulled pork and the ribs were awesome plus a bucket or two is always a great desert.
Visited Nashville.  Tried this place. Had pulles pork.  It was dry and tasteless.  I don't normally complain about a meal but this is an exception because it was that bad!  Tsharrish@aim.com

The smoked 1/2 chicken is delicious. The side dishes are nothing special, very average. It is a fun atmosphere and our service was good at a time when the restaurant was very busy. It is very loud- you can't hear the person next to you speak. This is a good place to stop if you are looking for a loud bar to have a fun night out, but not the best place for a quiet or relaxed dinner. The beer is way overpriced compared to some other bars in the area at $7 a bottle.

My daughter and I ordered the large Mississippian and got nearly three yummy meals out of it!  The foundation of this pie was a thin crust that was fired to a well done char and paired beautifully with the sweet sticky BBQ sauce.  Somehow the melted mozzarella & pepper jack had the perfect chemistry to pull this pie together with two chicken toppings (pulled & grilled) and tasty gems of smoked bacon.  Leftovers were most welcome and left us longing for even more!

The bands which play here and staff are quite kind. While security can be a bit aggressive, I can understand that they don't want anyone falling off barstools or the balconies, creating liability issues for the bar. Sometimes the patrons, at least the ones on Saturday night this last weekend, are rather crazy, but all in good humor. While some individuals were incredibly rude, I take this as part of the tourist scene and not the fault of the establishment.

I love that they have two live bands, one on the second floor and the other on a base. It helps well with crowd control.

I could also be biased in this case, considering I saw two Chicago Blackhawks players on the stairs when I was about to go home. The things you see during a hockey convention weekend...

My Fiance and I are from the Washington,DC area and were getting married in Nashville next April. We decided to have our Rehearsal Dinner at the Wild Horse Saloon. We gave them a deposit and signed contract back in May. On July 16th at 11:00pm, we received an email stating that someone else had bought the place out and we can no longer have our event there. We are now without a venue for out rehearsal dinner. This event was planned for approximately 125 people. We have yet to receive our deposit back. Please respond if something similar has happened to you. 
Rachellauren87@gmail.com

Great pizza place near our hotel. Group of 8, each ordered something different. Two of our group went to pick up the food and didn't know they had walked out without an order. The manager ran after them to let them know. 5 star service based on that alone. Food was good, sandwiches, calzones. Crawfish soup was spicy.

I have a feeling that when I left this place with a five star feeling, the perfect weather and free tickets that I won had a lot to do with it, but Soulshine was a great place! Had a personal size pizza, priced just as I expected for a "non-chain"/more gourmet place. Also tried the Lemon Wheat beer that was on special and I loved it. Especially the $2.50 price! Live music, patio, amazing ceiling fan to cool the place down, great food....everything I could ask for! Go Friday nights after work for Lightning 100's live broadcast!

I LOVE THIS PLACE. We got there at 8:30 and had missed the 8:15 line dancing lesson, so we put in our name and we're seated within 10 minutes. The food was amazing and very large portioned. My friend and I could've easily split something and still been full. I got the hot chicken sandwich with mac & cheese and was amazed. So tasty and filling. My friend got the pulled pork sandwich and was equally satisfied. I tried some of her fries and those are great too! After we ate, we started to learn the line dance that was being taught and it was so fun! David Oakleaf and his band were great. I am coming back! Also I'm 19 and was stoked when I found out this place was not limited to 21+.
The tables are sticky, and don't get the Mac and cheese because it is Stouffer's (you can get this in the grocery.)

The music and line dancing is fun. Pure Nashville. They teach us lay people how to do it so it's a good tom even if it's your first time. The food was good too. Drinks are overpriced and not that great. The service was very poor though. It was like we were imposing on our waitress just to get our drinks and food.  Might've just been a bad night for her. Still worth stopping in.

This place was awesome. My sister is 16 yrs old and loved this place. They teach you how to line dance and we went on a night with a live band. Since we were staying at the the Opryland hotel our cover charge was waved. The gluten free menu was pretty lame and not existent. They have gluten free options but it is hard to be 100% sure. Our waiter was awesome even with the noise level and all. It was a very fun Nashville memory.

Pros: Convenient location, decent atmosphere, interesting decor
Cons: Apathetic (bordering on rude) staff, disappointing food, really loud

My first experience at Soulshine didn't start off so well when I asked a passing waiter if we could have a seat at the last open table, where the leftover food and plates from the previous guests was still sitting.  He kept walking and said, "yeah you can just move that stuff over there" and pointed to a service desk area.  Really?  I'm your guest, not the bus boy. 

Soon after, as we were sitting down, the same waiter grabbed the beer list off of our table and handed it to the two young ladies at the next table.  Umm, I was wanting to look at that myself, thanks. 

Our drinks came quickly and the food came out reasonably quickly also.  But the hummus we ordered tasted like some pasty lime-flavored goop that came straight from a package.  

The pizza I ordered sounded great on the menu, but what I got was comparable to some frozen pizzas I've had.  The toppings were OK, but a little bland, lacking in flavor.  The crust was pretty awful.  It tasted chalky and frozen.  This was disappointing. 

Beyond this, our waiter was just very lacking in customer service skills.  In addition to the rudeness mentioned above, when it came time to get our bill one of the members of our party stated that he already had a tab at the bar and asked if his part could just be added to his tab.  The waiter literally rolled his eyes and said, "I don't think so, but I'll check."  

Despite a fairly negative first experience, I'll give it another chance.  It seems like an OK place for happy hour and the overall vibe of the place isn't too bad.  There was live music, which is a plus, but for those seated in the music area I imagine there's not much chance for conversation as the music was very loud. 

Probably not a bad place to go for happy hour drinks, but I'll probably give the food a pass next time.
Had a delicious pulled pork sandwich and some bud lights. Hit the spot with a good country cover band.
