One of my favorite stops on the strip. The music has always been great, the food (especially the pulled pork sandwich) is awesome, and the servers are usually pretty friendly and on top of keeping you happy.
Awesome live band and great service and food.   Drinks were good also. Lots of lively action in the dance floor and interaction with the band.

Not. Good. Insert pizza snob rant here.

What else was not good? We ordered the garlic bread. The waitress gave us what appeared to be a cheese pizza cut in strips. When we tried to reconfirm, "this is the $1.99 garlic bread?" She assured us it was. Then our bill arrived and there is it, $8.99 for cheese and garlic bread. THAT WAS NOT WHAT WE ASKED FOR! Oh and she brought us the wrong beer.  So it may have been an off night, I get it, I've definitely been there. 

To continue, this place is not for me. I am not a fan.

So who should give Soulshine a chance? I think this place is perfect for families, kids and group outings. The decor isn't bad, the windows out front is pretty darn cool but as I said, not for me.
Pizza is okay and pricey. The staff is the saving grace of this store and the only reason I would go back.  Live music is also nice.

This place can be great and just ok.  

The atmosphere is great when there are bands but they need to chill out and let the crowd turn it into a party.  The place has a corporate feel to it.

The pizza is awesome while you're eating it but after you take it home then you can see the lower quality cheese. It doesn't heat up well which means there isn't much oil in the cheese which means they're skimping on quality.  Let me say this though, it's really good pizza.  They just need to buck up for the good stuff!

Never get the spaghetti and meatballs, not good.  And I love spaghetti and meatballs so it'd be awesome if they improved it.

They do have great music but they just need to back off a bit and laissez les le bon temps rouler.

Bartenders and wait staff is nice.  Also, please provide more beer specials for normal folks who like domestic brews.  

The overall theme of Soulshine is wonderful.  Let your soul shine, be yourself etc.  Mr. Warren Haynes would be proud.

Great music location and it's right on the corner. It is multi level with music up and down. We had food and drinks. All of it was reasonably priced and good to the tongue. Downstairs is a bit more intimate as far as being close up to the band. The service was fast and the waitress was nice and cute as well. I will go back before the trip is done.

Surly Security Harasses Mature Patron

I had a particularly troubling night at this Broadway institution. The "bouncer," of African American descent (not that I see color), had orange hair and a surly frame.  Mind you that no "bouncer" was necessary as this was an establishment that I was visiting purely for a nice rack of ribs from my favorite ribs maker, Freddy.  I digress, after looking at my ID, the "bouncer" then questioned my age, which is unwarranted as I clearly give off a mature and worldly vibe.  (I was wearing a Goorin Bros. world traveler hat, gentlemanly summer coat, and a crisp argyle pocket square). He then proceeded to bend my ID to test the validity, and in the process left permanent creases! Can you believe that he questioned my age! I implore you fellow Yelpers to look at my profile picture and see for yourself my mature face.   
 
After explaining to the "bouncer" his blatant mistake in a demeaning way so that he would learn a lesson, he shoved me back a few feet, and snapped a picture of me with his cellular device. He then promised to circulate the picture to his colleagues and announced that he has banned me for life!

Instead of dealing with his mistakes at hand, he resorted to using his illegitimate power to brush me aside! Sad! 
 
I'll be taking my hard earned American dollars to other fine establishments downtown such as Lonnie's, Brass Stables, or Big Bang.
Enjoyed the live music and drinks!  Our waiter was great and kept us laughing.  Will definitely return if I'm ever back in Nashville.

Great service and good pizza. Several choices on the menu. Live music was a plus. Will come back on my next visit to Nashville.   I sat upstairs. The band was upstairs. If your not into that you can sit downstairs and hear just enough music for background ambience.

Fortunately we went for the music!  It was really good one night, so, so another, so I guess luck of the draw and whoever might be in town. We tried the food one night (anyone who serves fried bologna sandwiches, must be okay).  However, we opted for burgers instead, and were quite disappointed..first time ever for a restaurant burger that didn't have  a toasted bun! Not eve warmed up!  Go have  a drink and dance, but eat before you go (or try the bologna!)
This place was really fun. The dancing and music was very cool. We are having a great time. Food was not 5 star but who comes here for the food right.

This place is one of the cooler more modern bars/restaurants in the area! We walked in on a Thursday night, and got carded (but you're able to be under 21). There was no cover and there was an awesome feel to this place. There was a band on stage, which was LEGIT, with lighting and everything. I felt like I was at a concert. There was tons of tables and bar space, as well as room for a dance floor, which is not typical of these bars. We got beers and headed to the second floor to watch the band. There were seats, but certain spots were blocked for a private event, oh well. They also had pool, shuffleboard and foozeball. There was no bar on the second floor open so we had to go down to the first to get more drinks. Really cool place, and the food looked yummy!! Would definitely come back.

Soulshine is a fantastic pizza stop in Midtown, just near Vanderbilt's campus.

The place always seems to be busy, they have a ton of pizza options, and lots of great beer available. Wait service could be improved, but overall it's a great go-to for non-chain pizza. Plus, they're open way late!

They often have great live music, and I love the two-story setup. Definitely would recommend.

Had such a fun time at this place! 

There was a fabulous band playing, and the line dance instructor was very easy to follow and had an enjoyable personality. Line dancing exceeded expectations. 

The food was fine as well. We didn't go there for the food though.
The service was great. Food was Delicious and not a long wait since we were all hungy. Beer was not too cold. Entertainment was great and under 21 allowed.

This was the first bar I went to when I got to Nashville and I enjoyed it a lot. I actually went there 3 times in my stay. They had great live music every night I went and the size of the shots they poured were overwhelming in a good way. Check them out if you have the chance.

I've heard so much great stuff about this place and so I was surprised with how underwhelming it was. Not bad... just, not great. We met friends there for drinks and sat for almost a half hour before being served. Good service after that, though. This place has a great patio, too. But you'll pay for it in the end.... $$$. All in all, an average experience.

BBQ pork nachos were delicious. The kitchen sink pizza was to be expected. Personable servers. 

Parking blows. Beer selection could be better. Bathrooms were dirty and didn't have toilet paper. 

Overall good, but wouldn't go out of my way to go there.
Three stars is fair.  Decent food, reasonable prices, friendly service, live music (though on Broadway in Nashville that's not all that unique).

Not the best place for CUSTOMER SERVICE. We weren't acknowledged until I raised my hand. He looked over and mumbled something. He was absolutely horrible. He was unfriendly and didn't seem to care to check up on us. Food was a-ok. BBQ kinda try, flies wanting to dine with you, and the live band was meh. I started sweatin'. I don't think they had AC. Very disappointing.

(6/23/2014) Our conference organizers rented out the Wildhorse Saloon in The District for the opening reception, what a party! Had a line dancing lesson, then a set from a house band, and a fairly generous, if unexceptional buffet.  Space is vast, three levels around a dance floor overlooking the stage.  Would be a great mid-sized venue to see a band.  Several bars are strategically located around the place, waitstaff is attentive and keeps track of you even amidst the craziness.  Pretty good selection, more upscale than in the honky tonks down Broadway.  It's touristy, it's splashy, it was fun.

A group of my coworkers and I were looking for BBQ while in Nashville, so we found this place....let's just say I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. The service was horrible and the $24 sampler was disgusting. The ribs are not good and the cheddar cheese they give you is like a cheese stick cut in half. Only thing that was acceptable was the cold beer.

We stopped in the Palace for drinks and some music and had a blast.  Nothing fancy here, and we didn't try the food, but the beers were cold and the music was authentic and well played.  Servers were friendly, too.  Definitely worth a visit!

This is where you want to come for group gatherings during the day. Two floors of open seating - seat yourselves - two decent bands doing modern country music and ballads, filling bar food, and cheap drinks. Second floor livelier than first. Younger crowd than, say, Legends across the street.

Two floors of music.  Downstairs were three performers on the stage taking turns.  Upstairs were two singers + fiddler accompaniment.

It was 11-12:00 AM, but the musicians seemed very low key.  The fiddler looked like she was quite uninterested in being there.  The best was the male singer on the first floor.  My suggestion would be to go to both floors and check it out before you decide to sit down.

We just had drinks, no food.  There is no cover, but the lead singer upstairs came around with a bucket to collect tips.

The ambiance is somewhat divey.  The windows were open, and pigeons were flying in and out upstairs.

We settled in here as it was one of the few places where the musicians were not playing crushingly loud (if you can't play well, play loud...)  You could actually carry on a conversation during the performance, which we really liked.

Overall a decent experience, but I wish the musicians had a little more enthusiasm for their performances.

Rippy's is the BY FAR the best place to go before any Bridgestone Arena event!!!
 As avid Preds fans and concert goers, we've battled the downtown "Pre-Event Rush to Get Some Grub" countless times throughout the years. Rippy's consistently delivers.The BBQ is delicious and your food comes really quickly! The ribs are smokey, sweet and tender, the beers are cold and it doesn't take forever!!!!
I think the Rippy's staff handles the Preds/concert crowds much better than most places downtown simply because they're located DIRECTLY across the street from Bridgestone Arena and are extremely familiar with event timelines. 
They handle a "rush" like seasoned vets! 
My recommendation- grab a seat, a beer (Holler 'n' Swalller!!!), listen to some talented musicians, chow down on some tasty (fast!) grub and get to the game/concert on time!!!

I don't know what some of you people are talking about this place is AMAZING!!  Great environment to grab a delicious craft beer or stuff your face with one of their tasty pizzas!  I highly recommend the Wild Bill or the Bob Marley.  Also as one of the biggest Widespread Panic fans ever...I loved when I walked in and saw the big painting of JB right by my table, even got to hear "Ain't life grand" while I was enjoying a Fat Bottom Black Betty and a cup of y'alls cream of crawfish soup (YUM!).  Will definitely be back to try more things on the menu, and as a Midtown regular for years, WELCOME TO THE NEIGHBORHOOD!!

Just came in to try their cheeseburger & fries because I'd heard good things and live nearby. Nothing fancy, or creative, no eggs on top or anything, just a good burger. This is a smoky bar, so if you don't smoke you might want to get it to-go as I did. But the best thing I've had here is the chicken wings. Not buffalo, just barbecued wings that are quite tasty.
We went and watched a band we knew personally play. It was the first time they'd played here and it was the first time we had visited ever. The crowd was great, and the service was good.

I ate there on a Sunday afternoon for dinner during the CMA fest. I sat at the bar and had the pulled pork plate with beans and slaw--- all delicious, the portion was large, and served quickly!  Wait staff behind the bar was super friendly, attentive, and a Wisconsin fan!  Food on the menu was reasonably priced and bottled beer was $6 like other places downtown. I did not order a mixed drink, but if I did I would probably ask the price before ordering!!  Live country music from a 5 piece band was good, although loud.  If in town again I will certainly check out Rippy's for BBQ!

My 8 best girlfriends & I were in Nashville this past weekend & we stopped here 2 of the 3 nights because we had so much fun. The cover band was PHENOMENAL & the atmosphere was a blast, we would absolutely recommend it.

The only reason we couldn't give 5 stars is because of the absolute piece of trash bouncer that was so very rude at closing time. We were aware we got there near closing time Saturday night so we decided not to get a drink but just listen to the band. Before the band even finished standing up to be done for the night the bouncer started screaming & cursing at every person at the bar. He was physically pushing people out & even picked up some boy who turned around to try to find his friends, knocking into people. It was EXTREMELY unnecessary & unfortunately left us very upset. 

Yes, we know bouncers have tough jobs. We have stayed at many bars til closing time, some of us work at bars but we have never seen such an overreaction to a closing 15 minutes before 3 am. We say definitely enjoy your stay at Rippy's but LEAVE an hour before they close.

The main appetizer is pushed as the fried pickles but if you want or looking for that unique flavor do the chips and onion dip
The brisket is spot on
Definitely ask for the two sauces from the back
Sweet habanero and spicy BBQ are the fest
Slooooowwwww. Decent food but not outstanding. Wonderful music. Ribs were the best yet not fall off the bone.

I'm giving this place 3 stars instead of 2 strictly because of their amazing staff. Our waiter was a younger bearded guy who was on top of the ball, always looking across the room to make sure our glasses were full, or to see if we made eye contact. Great server, probably one of the best I ever had.
We didn't try any main dishes; only an appetizers which was the quesadilla with an upgrade to sweet potato fries. Four small pieces, and a handful of fries for $10. We then ordered a pitcher, and decided to switch to mix drinks. Although the food and drinks arrived quickly the drinks were very weak, and after the 3rd mixed drink "still felt no effect" I asked the server to tell the bar tender to; put some legs on it.
So my 2 main issues are one the extremely weak drinks for the price, and the other issue I have is every 30 or 40 minuets a member of the band kept coming off stage and went to each table "begging" for money! Yeah you can call it "collecting donations." But when it's done ever 30 minuets, and the bucket is shoved in your face; I'd call it begging!!! There's nothing wrong with asking for a tip, or maybe taking one after the show, but if you resort to asking for money every 30 minuets, that's just class-less. Is the bar not paying you? If you need "X" amount of money per night that should be between you and the bar, not between you and patrons.

We were here last night for dinner and it was Status quo for southern bbq.  Wasn't overly impressed, but it was still good.  My husband had the half rack of ribs, and I had the smoked pulled pork.  My husband said the pulled pork was the best he's ever had, but I didn't agree.  He said his ribs were standard, nothing special.  Fall off the bone though!  Coleslaw and baked beans tasted identical to KFC's.  Lol.  French fries were nothing special.  Chili was decent!  Major downfall is that I don't think they make their own bbq sauce which I would expect in Nashville.  We saw a huge bottle of KFC Masterpiece bbq sauce on the server stand.  We were bummed.  Food was served on paper lined baskets which is cool, but once the paper gets soggy from the meat, it starts to shred into the meat.  Yuck!  I'd recommend using a different kind of paper!!  Service was pretty bad.  Server was busy and the place was packed so we were very forgiving.  Amazing atmosphere though and the entertainment....ONE OF A KIND!!  Only in Nashville!!

Quite the hidden gem. Best to come around 7:00pm when its live and full of energy. Family was worried that a venue like this would cost a lot. LUCKILY we were able to come in for free because we are staying in a mariott hotel instead of paying the normal 6$ a head. Loads of fun for me an the family, siblings and i are big music and dancing fans so the large dancefloor was fun. Great experience for us filipinos from Maryland on our road trip down to Nashville!

This is supposedly THE venue for music headliners and crowds. It was lame, the crowd didn't even clap for the performers and it was impossible to get service at the bar. The space is huge and looks like it has potential, but I just don't see it being the place for fun and music.
Quick to accommodate our large bachelorette party, amazing service (SHOUTOUT OCTAVIA. U da real MVP), great food to kill your hangover. Highly recommend the fried pickles & piggy mac grilled cheese.

Well, TPAC is the only place to bring the Musicals and other grand mid-sized performers to Nashville, so you know - its good for that, but I've never left being wowed by the venue or service itself; a show yes. The venue; never. 

To start - why doesn't the main floor host a restroom? Wait, what? I have to walk into the bowels of the lower levels (which house a museum in the daytime) past the darkened museum pieces? (creepy!)

Second - signage - I've been here a good 20 or more times in my life in Nashville and still get confused on what 'loge' or 'balcony' I need to que up for. 

Thirds - its just dated yo. This place could use a solid facelift into the 2000's. Hear that fancy donors? You people love to remodel. Remodel TPAC! I was in the nosebleeds for a recent show and all the lights were burnt out. I couldn't read my program. Comical almost. The main door way needs more direction, too. It is a MESS every time you try to escape that place with the fancy people lining up for their cars literally blocking the exit.

Other than that everything is just totally average. The overpriced concessions, the friendly retired ushers - everything you'd expect from a performing arts center...

Here in Nashville for a business trip. We had our group dinner here last night.  The food was mediocre, not alot of taste to it. Their BBQ sauce and pulled pork shoulder is very good though. My coworkers enjoyed the dancing. Great place over all as far as room to have groups.

My friend recommended me this bbq joint. It was my first night in Nashville and I have to give it 4 stars. I ordered the pulled chicken platter that came with 2 sides. Mac and cheese and potato salad. Chicken was very good. But the sides I had was average nothing special. Atmosphere was loud but amazing typical broadway bbq joint.

Just got to Nashville after a long flight in so I stopped here with my family to get something to eat.  Well I never did get anything to eat and so did many others in the restaurant!   I waited for 15 minutes and never saw a waiter!  This was around 2 in the afternoon and there was hardly anyone in there!  We got up and left!!

Me and a few girls went here on our Nashville trip. Ordered the Chicken Sandwich (hot) and Fried Pickles. The food was great! The chicken was so juicy and had just the right 'kick' to it. The fried pickles were a perfect blend of batter to pickle ratio. It all paired great with a Blue Moon. There was live music and in between sets they would teach line dancing. Loved the atmosphere of this place. The service, however, not so great. Our girl disappeared for ever. She wasn't the one to bring us our food. We had to ask several other waitresses for items that we needed and when we were done and ready for the check I believe we waited for over 20 mins. Maybe she was having an off day. This won't keep me from coming again. Just hope the service isn't like that all the time. I enjoyed my time there but I feel like it was a little too much extra time. Luckily I'm not an impatient person.

Whoa whoa whoa. 

Good food is one thing, but how much does atmosphere fills the void? 

After waiting for a good 10-15 minutes, our harried waitress, arms full of dirty dishes and notepad took our order. 100% distracted and had to come back twice to bring our table a round of waters.

Soggier food in Nashville. Between the salad, the pulled chicken and pulled pork sandwiches- wet bread, wet salad, even the chicken tenders were soggy and bland. Doused it with the Rippy's sauce- still fighting for flavor after pouring it on. Very disappointing after reading so much about this place.

Very dirty, extremely loud music, no silverware with our food at first. And only one kind of barbecue sauce! Bathroom was dirty and small. No "seat yourself" sign, so we were very confused. The food wasn't even that good. (Ribs were below average.) Good server though.
Throughly Enjoyable!  The band was rocking.  The food was good.  The portions are huge!  Sharing a plate would not be a bad idea.  The service was amazingly fast.  Prices are reasonable.

I've been to Soulshine twice and enjoyed it both times.  I went for Friday happy hours both times and thought the food and atmosphere was great.  Happy hour is awesome with 2 for 1 beers.  The pizza was really good too.  I had the Carnivore and Johnny's Garden pizzas last time.  The carnivore was all meat and I like this one more, but had to throw in the veggie pizza too.  Both were great and I look forward to trying another pie next time.  The atmosphere is young and exciting.  There was live music both times that I went and a lot of college students being so close to the campus.  I would go back and recommend Soulshine for anyone who likes pizza, beer and live music.

The crust!! Oh mama this is how a good pizza is made.
My absolute favorite is the one with chicken and buffalo sauce (of course) I usually choose it as a calzone, but it's really good either way.

I like their outdoor patio too, especially at night with the cute lights and just absorbing the music Row action. 

If you get a chance go see one of their live music acts! Really good music is served with excellent food and drinks. 
I was told they had to make changes and remodel to make sure not too much of their live music would be heard by some annoyed neighbors. That makes me wanna shake my head! I live in the neighborhood and this is music city, if live music annoys you, live somewhere else. 
Annywho...

Service is always friendly and sometimes they are slammed but they do a good job keeping you updated and refilling your drinks. 

This is the best pizza in the neighborhood for sure!!

Came with a large group and the place was very accommodating for that- we had our own private section at the front. The food was really good, the staff was friendly, and the music was great! There was a series of live performers who all sounded great and kept the energy alive. My group learned line dancing that was very easy to follow for a large group like ours. The atmosphere was like no other and it was my group's favorite place that we visited during the week we were in Nashville. Also, the bathroom attendant in the women's restroom was so friendly and had bought tons of products from her own pocket for people to use. I definitely recommend this place to anyone visiting Nashville and looking for a great time!

Came for a private party.  Great venue with 3 stories.  Got good seats to watch Brooke Eden.  Looks like a super fun place with a mechanical bull, games and of course lots of liquor!  Had a buffet of BBQ brisket and pulled pork.  The meats were soft and the sauces very tasty!

Thought this place was very awesome. We had a private party here and they really look care of us. From entertainment to the bar service - top notch. How they can put that many drinkers into one building and still keep up with it... awesome! Would recommend!

Got there on a Saturday afternoon.  The place was packed, and the live music was loud.  When the waiter asked what we wanted to drink, I said, "Scotch and soda".  The waiter said that this place was a honky-tonk bar, and didn't have scotch.  I thought that was quite odd, because any bar should have a cheap scotch in the well, but I ordered a Jack & coke.

My buddy and I split the sampler platter:  ribs, onion rings, sausage, wings, pork loin, and a few other things.  It was tasty and the portion size was more than adequate.

I'm here on business, and will try as many different places as I can.  There are so many other places along Broadway I want to try, so I don't know if I'll come back here any time soon.  It wasn't a bad place, not at all.  It's just that I want to try new things.
Worst service in town!!!!  Manager and wait staff are the most inconsiderate people I have ever come across.  DO NOT GO HERE

The food was Okay. But it was hot inside, doors were open so there were flush flying around while we were trying to eat. The Singer wasn't very good. He kept singing stupid songs nothing good. And we waited for a Long time for our food. I would go back here again

Stopped in for lunch on a Monday. Not crowded. Sat no the 2nd floor, listened to some good music. Pulled pork sandwich with a side of onion rings and pork loin with Cole slaw and potato salad. All well cooked and delicious.

This was a great first food stop in Nashville! Being the first time I had been to Nashville I was pleasantly surprised.  The place was packed to the rook, literally there is seating upstairs on the outdoor roof area.  Staff was running around like crazy but were very attentive to our table and never let our drinks run dry.  Our table order are large pizza and it was more than enough for 3 people.  

Will definitely come back!
A true example of Southern Hospitality, one of very few places allowing kids after 6 pm. Great staff, great musicians and great cocktails.
Great music, friendly and fast service, food is delicious!  Not sure why only 3 stars. Maybe I'm a jaded East Coast Girl who doesn't know good southern vibes but all is good here!

OMG! My tastebuds just took a trip down memory lane! I ordered the Bolgna sandwich to go and boy was I in for a treat when I got back to my office.  The sandwich was so good, it reminded me of the sandwiches we had growing up as kid during the summer months.  Do yourself a favor and order yourself one.  It is a really big sandwich, so go ready to eat with your game face on.  The only thing I woud suggest is to request toasted bread, but thats a personal preference because of how Mom and Dad made it for me and my brothers!  

Great sandwich guys, and thank you for my trip down memory lane!

DJ

This was my first visit to the TPAC & it was just OK. The theater was nice- not the best but not the worst. It was very confusing walking in. We weren't sure exactly where we were supposed to be as there were several events going on that evening...we almost ended up seeing the Dracula ballet and several people in line for Cinderella next to us were there to see something different. Larger and more direct signage would have been good. 

Parking was not bad. We parked in a lot down the street for $10. Easy walking distance even if was slightly congested to get out of. I wouldn't pay $20 for valet though!! The lines to retrieve cars were soooo long. I'll save my $10 and walk. 

The performance, Cinderella, was excellent! I was hesitant of how it would go seeing all these young girls in their princess dresses at 8pm on a Saturday evening but there was not one distracting child around...unless you count the drunk college students in front of me who I'm still not sure quite why they were there but anyways... 

The theater around us- upper tier- was fairly empty but a great view. The allowance of food in the theater was slightly distracting- again, thanks drunk girl- but not too terrible overall. The theater was, however, FREEZING. I wish I had worn something warmer than a dress and boots as the cold theatre was quite distracting. 

Overall, though, I would go back again for another performance and would likely choose the same area of the theater as I enjoyed watching the show from there.

Great service and a fun little place.  Listened to some good country singers.  I would have like it if they were more current.  I thought the drinks were a bit over priced.  We only ordered fried pickles and Onion rings and they were both  very good.  The mixed drinks were just right .  I am hoping to get back here while in town.
I've only gotten the beer here which is all right and the music performances are good. It is kind of hard to find a table. It is  on division so there are a lot of other bars and scene nearby

This was my first time at Soulshine. I really liked the décor. We sat on the first floor but could still hear the music upstairs. 

Our pizza was good, thin crust. We order one large sundried tomato pie and one pepperoni. There seemed to be a lot of interesting combinations of toppings on the menu. The pizza wasn't what I was used (because of the crust) but I still enjoyed it. The service was fast and we even got a very dessert for our friends' birthday!

Three different levels, three different bands. It was like a Goldilocks situation where each level serves it's own purpose. The higher up you go, the crazier and more crowded it gets, and the better the bands get. We started on the lowest level having drinks at a table where it was less crowded. The band was fine but the entertainment value came more from how hammered the lead singer was. After face planting off the front of the stage, she continued to insist she was fine dancing around and getting into it with the crowd. Eventually they turned her mic off and she still continued to sing into it. You could tell her band members were so sick of her shit.

We then skipped the second level and went straight upstairs to meet friends up top. The upstairs band really had the crowd going and it was pretty packed up there. Had some drinks, got my groove on and partied til close.
Great place! The hummus was excellent and the staff is super friendly. Didn't get pizza but, we'll be back soon to try it.

This spot was probably the most touristy thing I experienced on the whole trip.  It was a huge space with insanely overpriced drinks (You do however get a sweet mason jar souvenir).  The venue promotes free line dancing classes, which would have been great if the dance floor wasn't flooded with older women wearing gaudy cowboy hats who could barely keep their feet moving at the speed necessary for the song.  A little after the intro, a band came on to play, and it was the first time during my trip to Nashville that I heard a band I did not enjoy.

This place is a fine touristy music venue which allows you in for free if you are staying at a Marriott resort.  We ended up going before 10pm and there were a lot of teenagers on the dance floor dancing provocatively to Taylor Swift which made me feel old as the hills and uncomortable.  After 10pm everyone who look prepubescent left the building and the venue became rather dead on a Saturday night.  Some moron having one too many drinks upstairs spilled a cocktail on our table below but the waitress was kind enough to take care of it.  They have line dancing classes but the music everyone was learning how to line dance to sounded too much like a country version of Justin Bieber.
Best baked beans ever! Loved the pulled pork wrap with cole slaw...and good amount of alcohol in the margarita!

Came in for lunch and stuck around for a good while.  The food is pretty good and staff is fun.  We hit over 15 bars over the weekend and best bartender hands down in downtown Nashville is Annalise W.  Personality thru the roof and so much fun not to mention easy on the eyes.  We will return!

The pizza was decent if not a little over cooked but our problem was generally with the service.  Our waiter was clearly busy which is fine, but when he approached our table, he immediately started making fun of one of his other tables for their taste in beer (the fact that they didn't know what exactly they wanted was what was taking up all of his time).  It made us all really uncomfortable, but he wouldn't let up.  Finally when our food was dropped my salad order was wrong (and the salad and pizza came out at the same time).  They did replace it but there were no apologies.  They also forgot to bring silverware and plates.  Even by the time the new salad came out we still didn't have anything to eat with.  When we asked for them, our waiter only brought plates back but was in such a hurry that we couldn't ask him for silverware.  We finally asked two more people (one who forgot about us) and got silverware.  Once we asked our waiter about it, he got out his key chain and was waving a key in my husband's face saying he was the only one in the restaurant with that key and people kept asking him for it, which is why he didn't have time to come to our table.  We tried to talk to two more people about the poor service we had received, all of whom just made excuses about the restaurant being too busy.  I've never seen such horrible customer service in my life.

Pretty underwhelming food at high prices. First- we sat ourselves and had to wait about 15 minutes before anyone even came to us with menus or to even talk to us. Then the pizza was eh. 

But the atmosphere was fun and lively. People seemed to be enjoying themselves. When we finally were served, our server was nice and attentive.

The location and vibe of this place are great! I could hang here on the second floor with the windows open all day...in fact we did! I can't speak to the food, but the drinks came quickly and the music was great. If you heading to a Preds game, this is a must stop before or after. So convenient and fun.

Good grief!  Where to start?!  Dirty, three story dumping ground!  Cover charge- $12 for under 18.  The adult price of $6 was on par with downtown but 12 for minors?  The band that night was awful.  
Only the ground floor was 'a rockin' as the other two floor were ghost towns, occupied only by the plaster anthropomorphic horses and unused pool tables.  This is probably the only all ages venue from 1st to 3rd streets off Broadway so I guess the bar is set pretty low.  
Mom and Dad (or in his case, The Cool Uncle) can sit at the bar or table and drink while the chilrens dance.  The kitchen closes early, 10pm on Friday so all you really have to do is drink.  Beer from the tap was watered down or over carbonated.  (I tried two).  Finally settled for the beer special which I overheard but was not offered.  
Service here sucks, rude little men with chips on their shoulders who hate their job.  'Nuff said.  I won't be back and will not recommend this bore-fest to anyone.

Not impressed with the food at all. The BBQ pork wraps were sub par. The slaw was not fresh. I think it was days old if not longer. The onion rings are frozen and tasteless. The wings and fries were pretty good. The condiment bottles on the table were dirty and had not been wiped off. The contents had dropped down the sides of the bottles and had crusted around the rim. One condiment bottle didn't even have a lid on it. Overall, I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. On a positive note, the server was great.

A positive: huge space and we easily found a table upstairs for our party of 7. 

The downside: our service was not great. Our waitress sat our beers on the table and said "here's your beer" and walked away. No handing it to who ordered each one, no glasses or oranges for our blue moons. In general we seemed like an annoyance. No smiles. My water was empty most of the meal. When one of us got the wrong meal (pork instead of chicken) the person giving it to us literally picked the bun off of each of our sandwiches sitting in front of us on the table to see if we had the chicken. With his bare hands! 

Food was okay. Two of us got the chicken tender meal and had a ton of food that they enjoyed it. For the pulled pork/chicken sandwiches - the bread was sort of soggy. Cole slaw was dry not creamy. I wish we wouldn't have wasted our Nashville meal on this place.

TPAC som den kallas för , är en större teaterkomplex där en gemensam foajé betjänar tre separata teatersalonger. Jag var här för första gången för att se en stand up comedy show (Jim Jeffries 2016). Foajén var stor och kunde lätt ta emot och slussa vidare alla som skulle till de tre salongerna (som för kvällen var samtliga igång). Tydlig skyltning för vart man skulle gå för att hitta till de olika salongerna. Barer som sålde och serverade alkoholdrycker fanns det här och var.

Fick (som så ofta numera) gå igenom en obligatorisk säkerhetskontroll som sköttes exemplariskt skyndsamt och med respekt och vänlighet gentemot oss besökare. Därefter nästa disk där man skannade biljetten med samma trevliga bemötandet. Sedan guidades man till lämplig ingång beroende på ens sittplats. 

Teatersalongen verkade ganska ordinär, funktionell och bra. Oftast svårt å andra sidan att skilja så värst mycket mellan olika teatersalonger. Konceptet liksom ganska givet tror jag. Så nästan det enda jag kan skilja de åt emellan är komforten på stolarna, vilket här var väldigt bekväma. 

Ett plus också för kommunikation (via mass e-post utskick ) inför showen. Jag hade beställt och köpt online, och fick dels en påminnelse dagen innan samt tips på när man senast skulle komma för att hinna sätta sig inför föreställningen. Samt tips om parkering.

I made the trip up from Atlanta to catch the Summerland tour, and was pleasantly surprised by this place.  It has a nicely laid out floor plan, with a lot of seating on three floors of space, all with a decent view of the raised stage.  A medium sized venue nestled in the midst of 2nd avenue on Nashville, a popular street for nightlife, one can catch a variety of acts here, and have a decent dinner to boot.  And if you love the place enough, there's no shortage of memorabilia you can take home from the gift shop.

The saloon has a deal with local Blackstone brewery, and they carry some of the local brews, including one beer brewed specifically for this place.  A number of signature cocktails can be ordered as well, either by themselves or, for the touristy souvenir, in trademarked take home glasses.  Drink prices were average, with lots of bar space for those inclined to belly up.  The selection of other brews was a bit light, but I'd rather try something local, so I was happy.

The fare is that of the traditional American bar and grill.  I tried the chargrilled chicken sandwich, which is served with a ranch sauce well infused with avocado.  The chicken was decent, on the dry side, but the aforementioned sauce was very good.  All of the sandwiches come with fries, and these were crispy without being thin, and had an excellent flavor.  I've been trying to dial down on cheese lately, so I chose this one, but many of the other entrees were tempting, including a burger with jalapenos in a jalapeno sauce with a jalapeno infused cheese.  OK, now that I typed it, I think I should have ordered it...

When I entered, to be honest, I did not expect much from the sound system.  Much to my surprise, the acoustics of the place were quite good, and the sound man was on last night.  Vocals were crisp and clear, while the rock was loud without being overpowering.  My table was fairly close to the stage, but wandering around, it seemed to me the sound was excellent pretty much everywhere.  

For the number of tables they have, a veritable legion of wait staff can be seen flitting about the restaurant.  My waiter was great, with a good knowledge of the menu, and plentiful refilling of waters and soft drinks, and regularly checking on alcoholic beverage desires from those drinking.  He was personable and professional, and in hindsight I should have tipped him more for waiting on me for 5 hours during the concert.  At one point he even brought me a drink I ordered to where I was on the dance floor.

Overall, the Wildhorse was a very nice experience for me.  Is it a bit touristy?  Yes.  More than a bit.  But the food was decent, local beers were available, good service was to be had, and good music could be heard well.  Oh, and unbelievably, they actually serve Diet Mountain Dew, a great rarety and my soft drink of choice.  The only real detractor, and I'm nitpicking perhaps, were the restrooms.  In a venue this size, it would be a struggle to keep them respectable, but nevertheless, by the end of the night it was not great.  Also, the women's room needs expansion, as there was quite the line for what I am told were only a few stalls.  But venue restrooms are never acceptable, so don't let that scare you off from trying a show here.  And maybe take a picture with the titular Wildhorse statue!

Traditional country music at it's finest. This venue has two separate stages. Several bars, to obtain your favorite beverage in a timely fashion.  I didn't try the food, but people looked happy to receive it!

The band in front (Larry Hamilton Band)  had five main artists that had played/toured for at least 20-30 years each with numerous accolades and credits to their trade.  It was fun, and engaging.  They also got the visiting artists involved by inviting them up to sing a few songs as well. Wonderful vibe and variety. 
I'm fairly certain the owner was persuaded to share his talents as well. We heard him sing and play a few tunes through a little bit of coaxing ;-). Vocals and musicianship were on point!

Great bands in the back as well. Lots of great  seating to keep it intimate with the artists. Bluegrass artist Rhonda Vincent, and Country artist Daryle Singletary were pumping out the hits for the  CMA Fest crowd last night.  They we're up close and personal here. Not a bad seat in the house.

If nothing else at Rippy's, I want to shout out to the band that played there Saturday October 24, the Mauldin Brothers. What a great show. Our group from Missouri had just the best time and I assure you we stayed at the bar an extra three hours exclusively for the band. They were taking requests and nailing it all night and even let our friend come on stage and (attempt to) sing for about 6 songs. We'll be talking about that experience for a long time. Thanks guys.

The food was AMAZING! My husband and I had a front row seat for live music for lunch and it couldn't have been better. Very inexpensive and totally worth it. Plus they had some hilarious tshirts for sale and an equally funny staff. Definitely go here if you're looking for a place to go.

Meh. Tourist trap.. 
Apps are good, drinks are ok. 
Free cover for military or if your staying at the Gaylord Opryland resort!
Thanks for the dance lessons! I don't think I'd come back here but was a ok place!
Headed to printers alley

If I could give  zero stars I would have. We PREPAID for the Taste of Tennessee event. Only to be forced to wait in line with others that did not prepay to attend.  Never attend a special event at the Wildhorse Saloon. They do not know what they are doing. Over 50 people just walked in to eat. Either you have a special event or you don't.  You cannot successfully hold a special event and have regular dining.

They have a large upstairs area for night life on the weekends. I didn't order any of their pizza, but I had a drink. The drinks seemed to be a bit pricier than other nearby bars. They also had a band, but it was pretty typical bar band music. This place seems alright for any one young or older.

Great place to hang before a concert at the Bridgestone.  We were just having snacks and boozing when all of a sudden the band Magic! decided to make a special appearance to sing! So cool!!  The Wringley Moulin Brothers or something like that played both nights we visited and they were rocking!!!!

The second floor is definitely better than the first floor.  The service is so rude though, a waiter got pissed at us the second night for buying a round at the girl/stand that has just beers. He said "I'm waiter make sure you get all your drinks through me" real A-hole. I wanted to say "well if you would have got here fast enough maybe we would have!!!!!" Ugh sloth!

The bathrooms are the second floor are DISGUSTING!! It was worse than college. Make sure you use the first floor loo, ladies!!!!!!!!!

The food is real cheap and just regular bar food. I liked our chicken fingers and onion rings. The heaters are perfect. Definitely stop by, they have the best spot in all of Nashville!
Great place! The line dancing lesson was a blast and the atmosphere is very family friendly. I haven't lived here long but I WILL be a frequent face here.
Sat here for about ten minutes after the George Jones tribute concert, no server, no staff at all seemed present, so we left. What a waste.

Since it was choose your own table, we took a seat at a small table, and then waited 10 minutes for the waitress that never came to our table. We eventually went to the bar to ask who was supposed to wait on us and the bartender coldly told us that we had a waitress and said nothing else. Waited a bit longer and still no service. We finally wrangled in a different waiter who was nice enough to take our order even though we weren't his table, but our actual waitress never came to us. The food was fast but it wasn't that great, and we noticed several other tables leave because they weren't being waited on either.

The main reason for the 1 star is for the service. Food was about a 2 for the pulled pork, fries, and coleslaw. Atmosphere was about a 3 in the indoor bar area with live music.

In the past few years, it seems that the term "award winning" has been referenced to an extreme degree, so much so, that it is not as relevant as it used to be. Although, at the Wildhorse Saloon, the "award winning" wings are 10/10. They are perfectly seasoned and sauced while at the same time both crispy and juicy. I could have eaten orders of wings as my entree instead of ordering anything else. I would recommend this place to visitors especially as it gives you everything you could desire in Nashville (country music and great food).

While visiting Nashville we decided to try The Wild Horse Saloon. Needless to say I was and still very disappointed with my experience. We went for dinner and had to pay a $6.00 cover charge because to was 7:00 pm. Then we had to wait for a table so we decided to have a drink that was way overpriced! When we finally got a table it took 20 minutes for the waitress to show up and she explained she was not aware that they had seated anyone else in her section since she was full. Once we got our menus we found they had a very limited menu and the prices again were extremely high. We went ahead and ordered because we were hungry and when the food arrived it was terrible. My daughter's got a meal for two which had fried cauliflower on it and it was so terrible that my one daughter almost threw up from the smell alone. Come to find out that it comes with some kind of Curry sauce, it was just horrible. I got a salad with chicken and the chicken was in huge hunks and it looked like it had been through a processor and then smashed back together. Needless to say I barely ate any and avoided the chicken. It was just a bad experience all the way around. Just another high priced tourist trap!

We wanted dinner and they charged us a cover.... I've never been charged a cover to go eat dinner somewhere... They had line dancing lessons and then a band. Both were cool. We wanted to watch the Blackhawks playoff game and they made sure they sat us right in front of a TV and then changed the channel to the game for us. Waitress was really friendly and chatted with us about Chicago. Food was good, too.
Tourist trap. Horrible food. So many better options in Nashville. Ribs tasted like car exhaust. Overall, the food was like cafeteria style slop.

Really disappointed. Booked for private events two nights in a row. We called the first night and they said it was going to be open normal hours today. Planned our whole day around the lessons only to arrive and find locked doors and a sign that said "we will return at 11am" it was 5pm and they were clearly closed for yet another private event.

They should have better communication. Huge disappointment

My mother travelled ALL THE WAY from Ireland for this

I like this place! It's touristy but you know what? That's alright with me because the people, both patrons and staff, are friendly. It's the kind of place where everyone smiles at each other. They have old time live country groups playing seven days a week and it's a family friendly place. The bartenders don't stiff on poured drinks which is refreshing from the downtown Nashville scene. This place is simple, wholesome and fun. I'll cruise through here in the future when in town.

Avoid this place.  Service sucked both times I've been here.  You're either waiting for a table watching people that came in after you get seated or you get seated and the waitress doesn't even know you're there so you have to ask to be served.  Oh and a $6 cover charge for the luxury of being treated this way.  BS!  No wonder it's the only place on Broadway you can get a table at 8p on a Friday night.  Last time for this guy.  Time to shut the place down and let someone that knows how to run a place like this do it.

Came here during a crowded Predators game. The wait time was about 30 minutes to get seated for food. I ordered a bbq wrap with onion rings. The flavor of the wrap was very good, although it was a pretty small portion. I enjoyed the live music. Overall, good experience.

This place is definitely a blast. A bit of a tourist trap but I think that sometimes that can be just what you need on your first night in a new city. We stopped in for dinner on a Monday night and the place was pretty busy. It's a huge venue with a restaurant, at least three bars, a large dance floor and a stage. A band was performing when we arrived which was really cool. We were seated quickly. I didn't expect the food to be good but it was actually really good. They have a mix of barbecue food. The pimento cheese we ordered was served with this really tasty bacon jam. It was really delicious. I enjoyed the fact they served three types of fries all together, curly, seasoned and crinkled. All my fry needs were met. They offered line dancing lessons in between band sets and my little nieces really enjoyed dancing with the group. We had a really great time and I would recommend this restaurant to anyone who wants a quick taste of Nashville.

No A/C on a hot humid day, had to walk up to the bar to order food from a "couldn't be bothered" lady bartender. Music- acoustic rock songs not country songs, Pulled chicken BBQ sandwich was really good though. So, you decide, depending on what's important to you.

The outdoor/indoor atmosphere is amazing. Will give the service a A+ very atentive waiter. Just came for a recap but the band is keeping us here. Did not try the food but the food around us looms good. Positive vibes all around.

Went here for a private party. Extremely packed. 

I'm only reviewing on everything but the food because I didn't eat although the nacho plate looked delicious. 

It was packed so I stood over by two waitresses who were complaining and cursing across the room at each other. So unprofessional, I was surprised the owner let it slide multiple times. Although he looks extremely young and not really sure what he's doing. 

The staff are all pretty rude. I wouldn't come back.
Live music was great but food was burned and really terrible for 4 of the 5 in our group.

Awesome place. The band was playing old country music, and very well. Stand up bass, lap steel guitar, etc.

Drinks are very reasonable.

Really nice night at what appears to be an authentic Nashville country bar.

Bartenders are dolls. Very friendly, efficient.

Highly recommended for a low key night with friends.
Good pizza and salad. Service was fine because we were there at lunch on a Wednesday.

Pulled chicken + baked beans + collard greens = heaven! This place is so great! The band was tremendous, the waitress at the bar was an A+ waitress, the meat was hot and smokey, there is Bridgestone Arena across the street, and also the prices are solid. A must for Lower Broadway!

Oh my gosh! I couldn't say enough positive things about this place! It just made me so happy. Keep in mind that I am a bit biased since anywhere that plays country music automatically gains a few stars for me. ;]
    Don't be turned off by the first impression. We were a little confused since we thought we were on our way to a bar, but when you first walk in it's a restaurant. The second and third floors are bars. Both of the top floors overlook the huge dance floor on the bottom level which is obviously line dancing! The dance floor is right in front of a huge stage where there is live music. 
    Scattered throughout the place are these life sized horses that look a little like cartoons. They are really fun to take pictures with. The bathrooms are very clean and I met an attendant named Barbara who was the sweetest lady. 
    The drinks are little pricey, but worth it for the atmosphere! There are two bars on either side of the stage and of course big bars on each of the top levels. They do have a souvenir shop also. 
    There is unfortunately a $6 cover, but I will definitely be going again despite this. Even one of my co-workers who does not like country music had a great time!
Went for lunch. Good pizza.  Casual, laid back atmosphere.  College town vibe near Vanderbilt University. Kid friendly.

We only went to this bar at night after dinner, so we only had the drinks and listened to the music.  Loved to listen to Dennis Payne and his band.  The staff was friendly and the drinks were good.  We spent several nights of our vacation coming here to listen to the music and have a drink after touring during the day.  I believe Roberts Western World on Broadway is the sister bar/grill to this bar.  The menu and decor is the same.

this review is not about the show I saw there, because I couldn't say enough about the vulgar hilarity that is "Evil Dead: The Musical", but is instead about the venue itself. Spacious and offering many services, it's a clean place with comfortable seating. The restrooms are all inexplicably on the bottom floor, and getting a water bottle out of the vending machine will cost you $3.50, but in today's world you can expect no less of a venue.

Well,,,,service was fast but my ribs were cold. It took longer the get the heated ones back than it did to get them the first time.  While waiting I ate my two side dishes. So when I got back the exact same ribs, complete with the first bone I ate still on the plate, I didn't have any sides left to eat with my meal.  

I suggest you keep walking if you want good food.

Our Uber driver recommend Rippys for BBQ and the honkey tonk scene. It was seat yourself and, as packed as it was, we got a table right away.  We had pulled pork, pulled chicken and ribs. Dinner, including the sides, was great. Loved the fried pickles. Service was fine. Bands playing upstairs and downstairs. Music was ok. Downstairs was packed - difficult to walk through.  Would recommend.

Food was basic bar food. Nothing great. My bf had his first fried bologna sandwich. Waitress was fast and the band was fun. Loved watching people dancing. This place is bigger and a lot less crowded than the downtown location.

I went to Nashville for a quick girls trip and tried this place out the first night for drinks, dancing and food. The ribs were amazing!! Great sauce!! We tried Peg Leg Porker that got great reviews on yelp, but their ribs weren't nearly as good as Rippy's... and we had to save a table for nine of us and wait for at least 40 minutes in line at PLP.

After doing the bar crawl one night in Nashville, we finally landed in this place and loved it so much we came back the next night. I was on a trip with my sisters and we were looking to line dance. Apparently dancing isn't very big in Nashville, everywhere else we went, people were just sitting and listening to the live music. This place was perfect. It is huge with a really large dance floor and amazing live music. We loved the line dancing lessons and then practicing on the songs after to perfect our steps. Really clean bathrooms!
The rib plate was very good. The yeehaw cocktail also a good choice. The music entertainment was not surprisingly great. Check it out.

Overall our visit was pleasant.  We visited on a Saturday for lunch. We had wings and fries and a grilled cheese and fries. Skip the wings, not too good.  They had an odd taste. Our server was pleasant and the live music was entertaining.  Location of the Nashville Palace is close to the Holiday Inn and Opryland.  Within walking distance. There is outside patio seating if you happen to visit when the weather is good!
It's definitely a dive bar, but I picked up a burger to go; I must admit, it was pretty darn good! (and greasy)

TPAC did a wonderful performance of Phantom of the Opera! The performers were so talented and the costumes and scenery were amazing. My only suggestion would be that the vocal sound was a little garbled and hard to understand at times. I have never noticed that in the many other performances we have attended at TPAC so something was different. .

Love this place- all of the food is amazing- my favorite pizza is the buffalo pizza though- it's beyond delicious!  Such a fun atmosphere and live music - it's a must for Nashville and you need to try it out!
BBQ was good, not amazing. There were live bands all night which was cool. Its definitely laid back. Not a must go kind of place but not regrettable.

CMA fans do not go! Our waitress had the worst attitude and was upset that we asked for separate checks. She just decided to divide it evenly between everyone. Food was just ok. The windows were open and it started pouring down raining on our table and not a single person came to help up clean up. Our food was soaked but luckily most ppl had finished eating. Spend your money on better food and service somewhere else.

In town for a conference, read the reviews and stopped in. Love the atmosphere, live music. The drinks are very reasonable and the food is the delicious. The people really showed a Philly girl southern hospitality while enjoying watching my Eagles play. Definitely will be back .

Food was fair but the waitress Mercedes D. Was horrible. She couldn't put a smile on her face. We had a group of 9 she could have made a great tip but when the food came with the wrong order she said she " didn't ask questions" hmmm isn't that what a waitress should do if an order is wrong. Crab apple!!!!

This is a huge location and we stopped by in the afternoon and they had line dancing classes during the day.  Instructor was engaged and friendly.  A must stop by for a Nashville visit.  Several floors and plenty of seating.

This place is becoming one of our regular stops. As a transplant, we first ventured in to see a football game on a Sunday. The bartender was super accommodating and provided superb service including turning the game I wanted on one of the big screens at the bar. The manager also stopped by to see how we were doing and even put the audio for the game on the overhead speakers.

Pursuant to that, we've stopped in for a few business dinners or when we have out of town guests. The vibe is great and you'll regularly catch some live music. I spent a decade in NYC, so I have a different preference for style of pizza, but they do a good job here. The food in general is pretty tasty and reasonably priced. 

Our last couple of stops have been venturing out when the weather is nice to take advantage of the huge 2nd floor outdoor loft. It's really an awesome spot to chill and enjoy some sunshine and a nice breeze. There's always some good local music and Travis the bartender goes above and beyond to take care of you. Looking forward to our next stop!
Great service, pork loin was delicious and so is the full rack of ribs, highly recommend. Food came out really quick.

Awesome live music while you eat some delicious BBQ.  I had the pulled pork sandwich which was a great portion size.  Mixed in both BBQ sauces that are left on the table for you.  both were tangy and vinegary, one was spicier than the other but equally satisfying. Onion rings were so good; crunchy, crispy, thick cut.  Service was fine and entertainment was great. Pretty touristy but a good spot for cheap eats on Broadway.
Pulled pork sandwich was great. Onion Rings were awesome. Cole Slaw was missing something. Definitely will be back.

We really like this place.  When we went Broadway was CRAZY packed and starting to fill up with a pretty rowdy crowd.  We discovered second ave and liked how it was a bit more laid back and not as packed yet still had a lot of great honkey-tonks to choose from.  Although the Wildhorse charged a $6 cover it was worth it.  We hit the 7.30pm show with 2 way crossing and were surprised to see a fair amount of families.  We arrived at 6pm and was warned it would be a 1.5 hour wait but there were seats available at the bar so we had drinks.  We had a great server (Savanna?) once seated who was very attentive and the food was pretty good as well.  The show was really good up on the stage although after playing for about 50 minutes they took a 30 minute break!!  30 minutes was way too long but we stuck it out.

I like coming here for the drinks & listening to music on the awesome patio.. but the food & service are not so great. I had the Mississippian pizza & tried the Bob Marley as well. Both were meh. I think the crust was the biggest problem, it was pretty soggy. 

Overall, I would not eat here again but I'll be back to drink on the patio!

The worst! Avoid this place.! They do not care about their customers!

Went there for dinner and music, instead they booked the place for a video shoot for a local band. We left when it became obvious they could care less about delivering what they are 'supposedly' known for. Food is fair. The staff was very friendly but was given no guidance by their poor management.

There are so many other places in downtown Nashville you should go to before this one.

No not waste your time and money.

This place is pricier than others on the strip but you go here for the eye candy. Upstairs has open balconies that look down the strip so it has a very outdoor feel. It's slammed on weekends, I had lunch here, BBQ and it was OK but nothing at all special. The staff seem to be hit and miss, they're not big on serving overseas guests as they don't tip the 20% that Americans usually do, I know as I'm british and she had an attitude when she heard my accent but I showed here my Cali driving license and she warmed up. 

If you come to Nashville you have to stop in and make for the upper levels for a few drinks, you won't be disappointed on the view and the hang. There's better food around if you want it. The bands as all on the strip is also hit and miss, you get who's out on the night but then walk around and see who's on. Lots of kids, cougars and trendy dudes you'll have fun here. It is what it is, but it's 3 stars at best.

So we came here for lunch which was great. I mean where else do you get live music at lunch other than Nashville? There was even live music at the airport! But I digress. We came here for lunch and ordered some sort of meat and everything fried platter and it was great. The music was great so was the company, the food, the service. Honestly what more do you want.

I feel bad bashing this place because of a band member that was out of line. This place had great service, great food and a fun atmosphere! I would go back in a second and recommend it to friends visiting town. I even tipped our waiter extra because he was great with our huge party. Thank you Justin for getting back to me about our bad situation - appreciate it!!

I've read other reviews that said this place is good for tourists....this place is not good for anyone.  We had a large group and our server did the best she could.  The food was nothing special.  One in our group had an issue with her food and a manager refused to speak to us or address the problem.  Overall customer service was poor and the food bland.  Don't waste your time.

We were celebrating a milestone event.  I was very appalled by the way the hosts treated my Sister-in-law.  The waiter was efficient, the food was mediocre at best, pricing was reasonable if you like their food.  As we were leaving the establishment, two male hosts aggressively approached my Sister-in-law accusing her of (dining and dashing).  They demanded to see the receipt which she graciously showed them.   I felt like they humiliated her and should of apologized.

We went to Wildhorse for one of their free line dancing evenings as an optional team outing. Touristy? Duh. But it was great fun, as silly as I felt, and though I didn't last long, it was nice to laugh at myself. I thought I had some rhythm, but rhythm is different from counting steps, and math isn't my strong suit, soo...

It wasn't a very long lesson, maybe 30ish minutes or so, so plan accordingly to fill your evening with other plans.

Drinks were great. Full bar. And of course, a souvenir shop on your way out.

All in all the space was very clean.
I asked the bouncer if they sold water bottles and he replied, "Hot blondes only". Keepin' it classy with that southern hospitality.

Love this place.   Lots of tables, so even if it's crowded you have a short wait.  Food is exactly what you're looking for whether you're visiting or a Tennessean.  Wait staff is very alert, friendly and welcoming and gets it done better than most establishments downtown.  Oh and don't forget you can also get take out!!! Grab a table, place your order (Mac is a top notch server!) and enjoy a drink perhaps and some music while your order is being prepared.  Very enjoyable, happy to visit several times a month.
Great country music band at 6pm, acoustic singer and player food sandwiches, steaks, and appetizers.

I didn't really spend a lot of time in this place, but I saw this as a touristy attraction so I came in, checked out the gift shop and grabbed a beer. Pretty cool place, decent service, so I can't really give it a perfect score. I'll be sure to come back in the future. I understand its becoming more of a Nashville institution, and a true icon in the generational shift in Country music, meaning aiming towards a younger college-kid crowd.

What a big, fun place. Was there over the weekend for a large but private event, a dinner / awards ceremony for a high school music festival.  The live band was great (don't remember who it was). The buffet style food was delicious, especially the beef brisket, and the employees were helpful and friendly. 

My only complaint (and it's trivial) is there was a "Restroom Attendant" in the Ladies room. Frankly, I get that she's just trying to make a living...but I find the presence of an attendant who hoards the soap and towels just so she can be the one to attend to those needs for you, to be irritating and intrusive. I wish places like this would not allow people to work the Ladies room like this.

Aside from that minor annoyance, I had a great time and wouldn't mind going again on my next visit to Nashville!

Soulshine has great food! Let me start with that. Not just pizza, but salads too! The waitstaff is terrific. But, when we were there, the most godawful musicians were playing and to make up for not being very good they turned their amps up as high as they would go in a relatively small space. Louder than any concert I've gone to in Nashville - and they drowned out 4 ambulances on the street outside (which we saw as we walked out because even with fingers in our ears it was too loud). Absolutely no talking allowed, evidently...not like the Blue Bird, though, where it's the fab music that keeps you from talking, rather it's impossible with the horrific noise.
What a fun place! The B-B-Q was excellent, we got to square dance, and overall the whole environment was enjoyable! We are not in Nashville to often, but we will be back!
Terrible live music. Worse food. And the beer is ridiculously overpriced. If you come out of a hockey game or concert, keep walking.

Food was terrible.  We ordered the hamburger and pulled pork sandwich, both were bland, as was the Coleslaw.  Bartender is RUDE!  Asked her to check status of our food since it had been over 30 min at that point.  Her reply?  'I'm not allowed to check the status'.  Huh??   I must say the music was fabulous.  I suggest going to hear the music but go to Acme (down the street) to eat.

Its good for what it is...a quick cheap meal downtown.  Its not the best bbq you'll have but its far from the worst.  The homemade sauce is quite good and one in our group had the pork loin and said it was awesome, the other offerings are decent.  Its got a good atmosphere though live music, games and its convenient if your're on broadway.

This was an interesting place. The dance floor seemed small for the amount of people wanting to line dance but it worked out. We got a decent table to watch the show and our server was awesome and on top of keeping our drinks filled. I had several appetizers and they were all good. Their wings were a pretty good choice. The band was good also. It's a good place to go if you want to watch a bunch of tourists attempt to line dance. Overall it was a fun time

Love the casual vibe here.  Midtown needed another cool and casual place to eat (that wasn't tacky, aka Chuy's) and this is it!

Went to Soulshine to grab some beer and pizza to watch the Preds game.  There were lots of drink and menu options.  The bartenders were great and attentive. The food was great! Company was great!  Can't wait for the weather to get warmer so that we can eat on the front patio!

We will definitely go back.

Good  was not so good , and the drinks were ridicusly overpriced,  I guess is to be expected on Broadway but I think it's to much , the food price is not so bad , but I personally didn't like the food so much my wife had a BBQ wrap and that was better that my pulled pork sandwich

Great place to go hear some music and get your line dance on! The food was okay, but it is definitely not the main attraction. The music and dancing are definitely the main draw here. They have great sound and lighting and host some of the best that country music has to offer. A must see if you are in Nashville.

Barbeque was awful!!! Baked beans and turnip greens were marginal at best. Music was loud, but lacked quality of sound.  Too many musicians in this city to get a better sound which reflect the quality of sound and talent in this city. Wait staff not attentive, but to her credit she was working the bar too.

TPAC is a wonderful venue where I have seen many Broadway touring shows, ballets and plays. I recently saw Beauty and the Beast there, which was top-notch. The facility has comfortable seating, plenty of restrooms (although could use more for women during intermissions) and helpful and friendly staff. Parking is available by valet or many surface lots and parking garages in the vicinity. If available, I highly recommend parking in the Library garage, as it is just a couple blocks away and the most reasonably priced parking you'll find in Nashville.

Pretty good place to stop for a quick bite to eat and a drink before going out onto Broadway.

My friends an I had the pulled pork on corn cakes, they were very good! 

Good price and location. We sat on the upper level by the open windows looking out to Broadway. Quick service and there were was a lot of seating. A bit loud, but fun to listen to a live band during dinner.
Great pizza!!  Love the crispy crust!  We had an 8 inch Sicilian and an 8 inch rainbow warrior. We were both very happy with our choice :)
This review is only for the draft beer. Nice list. Sat upstairs on the deck-nice. Shared nachos-toppings were fine, but the chips were too greasy.

I loved it !! Nice place, good music, clean, service is ok.
I didn't eat just had drinks 
They have line dancing with an instructor which is very easy to fallow we enjoyed it very much. 
We got to see David Oakleaf he was great 
I would recommend you visit wildhorse saloon for some line dance fun

Nice atmosphere and wonderful live music. Only problem was the bartender, Daphne, was extremely rude. We left after one drink after she gave us attitude. Every other bar on Broadway was welcoming and the bartenders exuded southern hospitality. Very disappointed with the service here.

The pimiento cheese was the best I have ever had! I also had the house salad with smoked salmon, which was also delicious.  The amount of salmon was huge.  The service was great and knowledgable.  The band that was there was sort of annoying because the songs were all played at the same tempo and they made super cheesy jokes- but it was a Monday nightProbably not the A list.
Once again I got here and a beer Cart worker tried to act like a dick right off the bat. This restaurant is consistently terrible. As a local, I hate going here.

Jenny was our server tonight and we were a difficult crowd. We came in at different times, had multiple checks and picky people. She smiled and served us quick and well. She was a great server tonight!

We went to Rippys last night with our volleyball team last night.  We sat upstairs and there was plenty of room and tables that made it easy to accommodate large parties, live music both up and downstairs and the team had a great time dancing.  Food was great, and service was great, especially considering how crazy this place was.  We were a party of 30, there wAs another team with Pri ably same amount of guests, as well as several smaller tables and food came out in a fair amount of time and tasted great. Our waitress, I think her name was Elizabeth, handled our crazy group like a pro and even allowed us separate Checks (greatly appreciated).  The restaurant was great, with a fun casual environment, great food, and room to dance.   Will definitely be back.

Sunday afternoon, broadway in Nashville is packed. They have literally one person working the bar and the floor. 20 minutes to get a beer and forget about ordering food. She said, "I'm only taking drink orders, I'll be back for food".  She came back for food and we paid and got the hell out. Too bad. Great location.

So, I read the reviews before we went in and feared it all, but nothing could be worse than what we experienced last week at Tavern '96.  My expectations were low but something happened.....the staff (Chelsea and Kirby) were really good.  They were interactive, attentive and pleasant!  We only got wings and friend pickle spears but both were really great!  I thought nothing would be homemade yet both kind of seemed like they were, along with the sauce and dressing as well as the BBQ sauces that were available on the bar!
I can assure you that we will not go anywhere else before a Preds game unless I get a desire to write another review!!!

Band playing on the first floor and another on the 2nd floor...I'm definitely a fan! If you want that Southern vibe, this is the place to go. I had the full slab of ribs and they were fall off the bone tender and smokey! they rate up there with one of the best in my opinion. I love that Fireball; had a shot right before my ribs came. Upstairs, the music got even better! You've gotta try the Cinnamon Toast Crunch Shot.

Would love to be able to review the food here, but I can't since I couldn't get any.  My boyfriend and I came in here one night and, after being told by one mostly disinterested staff member that our best chance of getting served was to sit upstairs, we went upstairs and sat at an empty table.  We looked over the menus, chose what we wanted and waited for someone to come by.....or acknowledge our presence....or glance in our direction.....or......anything.  After at least a good 20 minutes of sitting at our table and watching staff members attend to or clear nearby tables, we did not receive so much as a greeting, let alone an offer to bring us anything to eat or drink.  And yes, they were busy, but if a waiter has time to bus the table next to ours, they have time to look in our direction.  I am virtually certain we left our invisibility cloaks at home, so I cannot fathom why the staff opted to ignore us, but we were completely ignored.  Pathetic and ridiculous lack of service.  We eventually just got up and left, still completely unacknowledged.  Would not recommend.

My teenage son and I arrived in town starving on a Friday night and Yelp!found us a gem!  We chose Soulshine because of the combination of live music and pizza, and both were excellent.

We shared a 12 inch CCR pizza on wheat crust -- chicken, Canadian bacon, small bacon pieces, and a ranch sauce.  Delicious.  The chicken was white meat chunks that were moist and tender.  The wheat crust was thin and crispy just the way I like it.

Based on several reviews that the Crawfish Soup "was to die for", I tried a cup.  I wish I would have gotten a bowl.  The reviews were right on.  The soup was creamy and savory at the same time with the just the right number of whole crawfish tails at the bottom of the cup.  It was spiced with the perfect amount of cayenne -- subtly cajun without being too much.  Reminds me of another favorite creamy cajun treat, the fettuccine alfredo at Jazz, a Louisiana Kitchen, in Kansas City.

Soulshine Pizza Factory is highly recommended, especially on Fri/Sat nights when there is live music with no cover charge.

There should be a 6 star for this. Johnny Neel from the Allman Brothers playing tonight. The guy before him was awesome. This is the reason why I love Nashville.  You would pay to see this and here its free. Of course this place has great pizza and plenty of beer options but again WOW Music City.

Home to one of Nashville's best burgers. If you're pretty broke and in need of a great juicy burger, crisp fresh fries, and some of the best priced beer then come here. If you're loaded come here anyway.

This was another "when in Rome" moment for us.  We were at the Wildhorse on a Monday night.  The live music was great.  We sat in the upper horse-shoe area and loved watching the spectacle of people line-dancing.  It is totally a tourist trap but silly fun.  We sat there for about 4 hours, just drinking, ordering appetizers, and enjoying the live music from a great vantage point (kinda felt like Statler and Waldorf, the old men in the Muppets).  

The bars in the district area have a lot that still allow smoking.
