Dive bars are fine to me and the music was really good from all of them, but at some point in the night, I didn't want anymore smoke (I believe Wildhorse is all-ages / kid friendly so there is no smoking allowed) and to sit down in a place relatively clean.  Wildhorse fit the bill.  Well worth the $6 cover, especially because I don't remember how much the drinks were... but I think $11 for a very strong vodka/cran and a pretty sizable beer).  That doesn't seem awful to me.

Decided to head to Rippy's to try out their BBQ. We arrived at the door and showed our id's. I was then promptly asked to show the contents of my drawstring bag. The door bouncer proceeded to search through my bag and came upon my prescription. He then decided to violate my privacy rights and ask what they were and what I take them for. I declined to tell him and said I don't need to share that information. I don't need to share my privacy, nor medical information with a door bouncer of a BBQ restaurant. Seems like all he was trying to do, was interrogate me so he could confiscate my prescription. 
We decided to leave after that awkward confrontation and won't be returning. 
Hey, btw, what medications do you take and what are they for?

Very laid back, live music venture. Sandy was very friendly and kept checking back about how we were doing. Had smoked turkey sandwich which was excellent. Live music was nice to listen to and the song writers/performers kept patrons engaged. Good afternoon killer.

Great band playing! It's Nashville!
Recommended by a local. 
Great Ribs and Pork rub sandwiches. 
Highly recommend!

Hmnn, not sure how to feel about this joint. Oh wait, yes I do. They are racist. They have a live band, which is cool, but what place doesn't in the neighborhood? This is not the place to give your business to. 

Yeah... let's go ahead and avoid places that yell out racist slurs towards asian tourists. Probably not a good idea. Seriously in disbelief. 

Here you go, let me hand you guys this L.

When I found myself surrounded by a thousand 11 year-old girls and their mommies, I thought I'd made a terrible mistake.  I had agreed to accompany (that means, drive and chaperone), my Wife and Daughter to a showing of "Cinderella" in the Jackson Hall one Sunday night without thinking through what this meant.  I'm pretty sure I was the only straight male in attendance, except for the octogenarian gripping his portable tank like he was worried the 1,200 Cinderellas he was seeing was an indication that his tank had been filled with something other than oxygen.

There were little girls dressed up in Disney costumes and their proud mommies posting selfies and giggling and talking about the characters together as if the characters were actual, real friends.  Which I suppose they are for many.  I thought it would be a VERY long evening, but the moment the lights went down, the place got quiet and afterwards was only ever interrupted by content-appropriate clapping, laughter, sighs or gasps.  

This was a good thing because the line at the bar before the show was so ridiculously long, and moving so mind-numbingly slowly that I had abandoned it, which may be the first time I've walked away from a bar without a drink in hand since I was kicked out of Tootsie's one morning at 1:47am back in 1999.  The unexpected perfect behavior of the audience allowed me to be distracted by the show itself, which was very good, despite the subject matter.  The voices of the performers were quite simply amazing, and there were a number of good comedic turns in the script.  But of course, this review isn't about the show but the facility.

This was my first visit to TPAC since 2008, although I've been coming regularly since 1983.  Although I would not say that TPAC has been thoroughly overhauled and modernized, neither does it scream at you that it is dilapidated and run down.  Everything is very clean, the seats are spacious compared to what you might find at other public events in town, the employees are friendly and polite (certainly what you will not find at other public events in town), and all of the lights, audio and climate functions seems to work as you would hope.  Proof that all those threats that art and theater would cease to exist if we didn't pass an income tax in TN 15 years ago were lies (as they almost always are with politicians and government bureaucrats whose guaranteed future double-digit annual % raises are at risk).

At intermission I was finally able to get a glass of wine and was pleasantly surprised to find a wide-range of drinks, including an event special named "The Glass Slipper" and champagne.  Be prepared to put a 2nd mortgage in place to pay for the drinks, but I suppose they've got to keep up with the prices at the arena and the stadium or risk looking foolish.

As with anything downtown, parking is a huge problem.  Yes, they have valet service, which means you'll be stuck in a long line waiting for the valet both before and after the event.  Just plan on the $20 parking and take advantage of one of the several options within a few blocks.  See you at TPAC.

One of our favorite bars on Broadway. We were there weekday afternoon. Quick service and got to hear a great musician. So many dark, no-light bars..but this one has plenty if you're downstairs.

I had the pulled chicken salad and the chicken was great. The only reason I wouldn't give it 5 stars is that my fiance had the nachos and there wasn't any cheese on them. Weird, right?

My family and I were visiting Nashville for the day and we starting to feel slightly parched and hungry. As we walked past Rippys the smell of BBQ drew us in. The bar and grill has a down stairs and upstairs bar and sitting areas. Upstairs can accommodate for larger groups and is air conditioned. The ribs, onion rings, pulled pork and mac and cheese are really good. I normally am very picky with pulled pork and can say this place is good. I personally ordered the sliced pork loin on Texas toast  (aka chilled cheese pork loin sandwich) and was very happy about my decision. Rippys has 2 bbq sauces (sweet and spivey). I liked mixing both together as the sweet had better flavor but I still wanted spicey.  The service was quick and you can tell the wait staff enjoy their jobs. Music is not as loud in the upstairs larger sitting area and is nice if you want to be able to talk without yelling. I highly recommend Rippys.
Expensive, yes, but I thought it was worth it. The live music was phenomenal and the staff was super nice. The ambience was really fun and light. I would recommend it.

Stopped in for a small bite of lunch, and to watch a little basketball.  Had a cup of the cream of crawfish soup, and cheese stix.  The soup was very good.  The cheese stix were good too.  They use there pizza dough, bake it with garlic and cheese on top.  The crust is nice and crispy, and goes well with the marinara given.  Would have given 5 stars if I would had ordered an "entree" type item, and found it as good.  Can't wait to come back and do so.  Too, Taylor the bartender was very nice and personable, and very good service.
Terrible food, awful service, music is nice, cute mouse that we found running around .... Although highly unsanitary. Birds fly in and out too. Only reason I'd suggest coming would be for musicians.

Food was good: homey and simple. 
Nothing to write home about..

Beer was cold and the local brews were tasty. 
Great live music and the band leader kept the crowd happy and laughing.. An easy night crowd to chat with and everyone got along great. 

For 4 beers, 2 waters, and the fried catfish sandwich w/ sweet potato fries it was less than $40 total. One restaurant downtown totaled $53 for 1 sandwich, 2 salads, and 1 cocktail. I'd rather have the easy going atmosphere, good music, and cold drinks of the Palace than pay the crazy prices for eating downtown.

Did not care for the atmosphere at Wildhorse Saloon. It's very large inside with a huge dance floor and big stage. Not quaint like most of the bars downtown. There was a tutorial for line dancing happening with a bunch of kids and teenagers. It is the most kid-friendly venue we were at while visiting downtown Nashville I guess. Upstairs there were games like pool, air hockey, and arcade games. We were there on a Sunday night and they were charging a cover after 6pm for the band. Also the food was pretty terrible.

Oh...this place. What a gem, this place. 

Ok, first things first. Twin Kegs was recently voted "best burger in Nashville". I might agree with that. The burgers are DAMN good, but I've also not had every burger in Nashville so that's not really a fair assessment for me. BUT it's definitely a top contender! The article I read stated Twin Kegs was voted best burger and listed the price at $4. This is absolutely not true. The burger the bartender recommended as their best seller was $8.50. But, delicious nonetheless. 
The karaoke was certainly a thriller. STEVIE G., please come back! This place gets very lively for karaoke, so if that's your thing, get there early! 
They have a shuffleboard table and I was pretty damn good at it! 

All in all great bar food (don't put it on a higher pedestal than that) and great times had by all. This is a perfect combination to help you forget about the bad grammar on the sign. Don't you mean "Internationally Famous"? :)

Awful.  Came in here with co-workers.  My Boss who's almost 50 had an expired ID.  We was refused alcohol service when seated.   When he drank  from a bucket of beer, he was told by the bartender :  "If I see you drinking again, I'm going to ask you to leave".

Really?  He's almost 50 and bald.  Great place.
Our favorite spot in Nashville for live music and drinks. Have never eaten here, but always stop in for a couple hours to listen to music!

New location in Franklin at Berry Farms.  Will give it some time. A bit disorganized and didn't see any "mature management" there to ensure things are running smoothly.  Nice to have other options there as well.  Went to Tito's.

We were drawn into Rippy's after we heard the music from the street. We got salads, chicken nachos and corn cakes with chili. The upstairs has an awesome vibe with a big bar on one side and lots of tables on the other side. There were three different bands playing (one upstairs, two downstairs). The woman singing upstairs had an amazing voice.  

Our server was super nice and attentive even when his section got pretty busy. The food was pretty average. The chili was good but I was hoping for better corn cakes. The nachos were pretty standard. The view from upstairs is nice and looks over all the commotion of Broadway. A table by the window is the perfect spot for people watching while listening to live music with a beer in hand.

We were in Nashville the weekend of the Men's SEC tournament and the town was busy!!  We had someone with us under 21 and were having a hard time getting in anywhere, but Wildhorse allowed it till 10:00 pm. There was plenty of breathing and dancing room for our party of 12. Only part we didn't like was they charged double for anyone under 21 to get in.

I like the way they set up different bands in separate rooms without making them clash. 
Our food was good. My husband enjoyed his pull pork nachos. I loved my BBQ ribs very much. It's worth a try. 
One thing I'm not so happy about this restaurant as well as other nice restaurants downtown is that it's really hard to find a place to park. That's the reason I don't visit this place very often.

What a freaking disaster, they make your order food within 5 minutes or they kick you off your table.....then you get to talk to security wannabe "head of security" True and the boys.......bad food, warm beer, thank god they bought the real estate before the boom in Nashville.......

My girlfriends and I came to Nashville for 3 of their 21st birthdays. Two of them had temporary ID's because they JUST turned 21 in NC last week. They both had their old ID's that expired last week. Showing the bartenders both their new paper ID and their old ID that just expired, the bartenders would not serve them. I've been 21 since January with a normal NC ID and they questioned mine as well. The bartenders were the bitchiest women and this was the biggest bummer to all of us considering we just got to Nashville today and this was the first place we came.

The food was pretty good! I recommend getting the crawfish bread, as that was the best thing our group ordered. The alfredo pizza was also very good, but the rainbow warrior left much to be desired. Ambiance was cool, and there was live music on the top floor.

On a recent trip to Nashville, we visited Rippy's twice.  It is a great place to sit and listen to music.  On most days there are 2 or 3 bands playing in the different sections of the bar. The second floor band on a Monday during the day was so good that we stayed over 3 hours. Both the first and second floor bands on Wednesday were average. Our bartender was very friendly on both occasions.  Typical bar food.  We had very good chips and queso but the fries were not so great.  Rippy's will definitely be our go-to place for an afternoon of music.

For a Friday night and live music in two separate rooms under the same roof, we got our food pretty fast and it was still hot. That is impressive considering how packed Rippy's was tonight. I got the full rack of baby back ribs and let me tell you something; much better and meatier than Chili's. You want baby back, baby back, baby back ribs? Go to Rippy's.

Line dance lessons/dancing in general. Just do it. One of my favorite places!

Downside: bartenders upstairs are slllllow.

Stopped in here after trying several restaurants 
That were still serving after 11 pm at night .
Have to say I was pleasantly surprised:)
The food was good , the service was good
And the band was great .
I will be back for sure

Went on a busy Saturday afternoon, found a table upstairs. Service was prompt and polite.
Food was average.

Good pizza - the draw of this place is probably more the live music at nights on their outdoors patio upstairs. The food is fairly typical of a pizza and bar joint, which is not bad. Pizza almost always taste great, and this place is no exception - fairly average. The outdoors patio is also nice. The inside is spacious, and of course, TVs grace the place.
Of note, during busy nights, street parking can be a little more difficult to find.

Stopped here after the Packer /Titans game.  After finally getting waited on for a drink order, the server came back to inform us they didn't have Miller Lite. She again returned 10 minutes later to take another order.  We ordered both drinks and food at this time.  The reordered drinks arrived and some were warm. The pulled pork, beans and onion rings were barely warm.  Not a place I'd ever return to.

My fiance and I have been to Soulshine twice now.  We live in Midtown and are glad that a place like Soulshine stands in place of the loud, dangerous nightclub that used to be there (when the crowd at the club used to let out, it was a risky time to be outside. We heard gunshots at least once a month back when Division existed).

That said, our first experience was so-so.  My fiance was excited to try their seafood pizza, however, it left something to be desired.  The wine selection was a bit lacking, for me, but the beer list was good enough for my fiance.  Our biggest complaint about that night (it was a weeknight) was that the music coming through the speakers was way too loud, then, on top of that, they had all of the sound on all of their TVs blasting too.  I feel the need to qualify ourselves here; we are in our 20s and can handle loud music... we go to a lot of shows.  This place was just ridiculous, though, with all of the conflicting noise.

We gave Soulshine another chance last night, thinking we'd order something else this time.  They've also renovated even more since our last visit... they added an upstairs, outdoor music venue.  We think it is cool what they've done with the place.  However, when we got inside, we could not believe how LOUD it was!  Even louder than last time!  Not only did they have a rock band upstairs, but they were STILL blasting their music through the speakers, and STILL blasting the TVs!  Having arrived absolutely sober, it was like being in a nightmare.  We would have had to have been pretty tipsy to be ok with the volume level.  We couldn't even talk with each other below a shout.  It was like being at a concert, trying to talk to each other while seated in their dining area.  It was hard enough to talk to each other, so I'd say Soulshine is not a great place to go with a group of people.

The food, again, was not very impressive.  The service was slow as well.  We will probably go back to Soulshine, since it is in our neighborhood and we like the ambiance of the place (minus the noise).  We'll probably go only during the middle of the day, though, for a drink and some appetizers at the bar.

If you like crowds and loud music then this is your place. Packed in like sardines, not clean. Don't care for Broadway, Just a bunch of tourist traps, go elsewhere in Nashville. Jack's Barbeque down the street has the best BBQ on Broadway
So much fun! We went on a Monday night so it wasn't packed but we had a blast learning to line dance and river dance!
I haven't even gotten my food yet and I already wish I could give this place -10. The waitress was a major bitch and had an attitude from the second she walked up to our table.

This review is for their room rental and corporate meetings. 
* The food - although abundant - was not good. "Eggs tasted like rubber."  Another said, "we should never come here again, this is just bad." Our vegetarian and vegan had sandwiches brought in from across the street for lunch on day 1 and brought food for breakfast.  
* The AV situation on day one as bar none, the worst performance by a vendor in my career.  I've walked in to rooms and had phones missing, power cords forgotten, missing AV gear, and the like, but in each case the situation was quickly remedied and we got about our day. This had no excuse - there was no one to remedy the situation.  We had 30 plus people in a room and we have no AV equipment to use. I cannot understand how no AV person was present during the meeting. That's frankly unprecedented for anyone who rents meeting space. 
* Day 2 was loud, between a fan belt squeaking (I understood we turned off the AC to stop the noise?) and street noise.  Again, commented on by many but at that point the team had given up hope.

This review is for food only, not the music, ambiance, or service.

We were kind of pressed for time before a concert at the Ryman and needed a place serving something (anything) vegetarian.  To their credit they served a veggieburger, which is surprisingly not easy to find in the area.

At best it was ok, as were the somewhat soggy fries.  The three stars reflect our server, who was really nice and helpful, the music, and the rustic ambiance which we appreciated.

If you are vegetarian there are numerous really good options in Nashville, unfortunately not in the downtown area.  Allow time to eat and travel to your destination.

Got take out here around 10 PM, lookin forward to a pulled pork sandwich with a side of coleslaw. Look at the sandwich - totally dry. NO BBQ SAUCE. Is this not a BBQ joint?!  If you have to add it yourself, that's fine but LET PEOPLE WHO GET TAKE OUT KNOW!  Also, no fork so I couldn't eat the coleslaw either. What a mess all the way around - total waste of my $8. Then called to talk to someone about it and no one even bothered to answer the phone. Save yourself the hassle and go somewhere else for takeout!!!

The place is big. Nice stage size and dance floor. They offer line dancing lessons. Service was okay and the drink prices were high. Feels more like a club which I'm not really a fan of. I prefer the more dive bar feel.

Good atmosphere, good bands, adequate service given the noise, good cocktails. Ribs were average, had worse but had better. Lose another star for using Sweet Baby Rays as one of the sauces provided on the table. A nice honky tonk bar to hang out at but skip there food (or ribs at least)
Stopped for a quick dinner.  Fast but not great.  Pork loin sandwich was ridiculously small.   At least service was fast. I can't recommend this place.

Came in for late lunch on a Saturday. It wasn't too busy, but the service was awful. It was as if our server was trying to be slow and not care. Food was pretty good, but nothing amazing. I'm sure it'd be a different experience if you were just there for drinks.

A comfortable corner bar that offers good Pub food.  The wings are spicy and meaty. The pork plate is excellent. The one draw back that seems to be common on Broadway is beer is only served in bottles.  We miss the draught beer choice.  Will definitely go again because beer in a bottle can also hit the spot, and the location and music was excellent!

Yes... this place is a little "touristy" but its still a good time. The music is good and they teach you line dancing (if you want.. they dont pressure you). The drinks are plentiful and the food is good. Our group  tried a little bit of everything (steak, catfish, chicken strips, cole slaw, hush puppies, fried green tomatoes, pork chops, and fried green tomatoes). Everyone liked their food and had a great time. MAKE SURE YOU TRY THE DELICIOUS BBQ SAUCE! I dont even like BBQ sauce and I was putting it on everything I could find. I even bought a bottle of it in the gift shop. Its a really big place that gets really busy, especially if there is a show going on.  Get in early and claim a table.

Stopped in for lunch today and the place was dead but we still enjoyed our time here. The live music was entertaining and our waitress did a great job taking care of us and giving meal recommendations. We had a salad with steak & an order of chicken tenders. The salad got two thumbs up and the chicken tenders got one. The French fries were really good, they must have some sort of seasoning on them! I could've just had a plate of them by themselves! Overall we had a good experience!

As I type this I am actually across the street at Baileys enjoying great service and food. I had to walk out of rippy's because the service sucked so bad. 

We waited at a table 15 minutes before it was cleared from the last guest and when it final was, they didn't wiped it down. Just left all the scraps from the last group.  So the waiter returned 10 minutes later to take our drink order. 10 more minutes to get said drink (1 beer 1 water).  10 minutes later to finally ask if we wanted to order. We told him no paid for the over priced beer and walked out.

VERY touristy. bands are very flashy. hostesses and servers are clueless. there is a 2 hour wait and about 12 open tables - once you get seated expect to wait half an hour to see a server. the dance floor is large and crowded with whoever rented the top two floors and thinks they own the place for the night, regardless of age. they welcome families and underage patrons, so if you want a night out without families or kids, DO NOT come here.

Venue lacks restroom and stairs are awful. Parking lot is unbelievable. We have season tickets to our cities theater district and we do not have to wait one hour at the matinee show. Loved the wicked show, do not like the venue or parking lot. We are still not out after one hour

Read reviews about this place online and since it was close to me I thought I give it a shot. I wasnt in the mood to sit in a bar tonight so I called and placed an order for a Patty Melt and fries.  Upon arriving I was a little skeptical about going in (Im African-American as you can see). 

Parking was...meh. Anyway, walked in and received a couple of nasty sneers from some guys at a table. Whatever. Went to the bar and the bartender, really handsome dark-haired man, greeted me and my order was ready. $6.50. Not bad!! The patty melt was cut anf two and was pretty tasty....until...I discovered that the other half of my sandwich was REALLY  pink. I didn't finish it. How did one half get cooked well and the other not?!. Nonetheless it was good and thankfully my plate was not filled with nasty grease. I won't come here as a hang out spot because its merely not my cup of tea and not my type of crowd(call me bougie I guess).  But Ill order from here again... as take out.  I'll have to make sure that I specify thoroughly that Id like my burger well done.

It was busy so I'll cut it a little slack:

Never got silverware or a drink refill

Waiter was rude.

We started as a group of three, with 2 others meeting us toward the end of the meal. One got a water and the other didn't get anything. We were charged a gratuity and the waiter got an attitude when I asked why.

Overall, I was less than happy when I left. 

On a positive note, I guess the food was decent. There are much better options if you want BBQ tho.

As a line dancer from the north, I was excited to come to Nashville to show off my skills. Unfortunately, Wildhorse is just about the only place to line dance and their line dancing is surely lacking. They only teach extremely easy dances (which makes sense seeing as they have all beginners all the time), but when the instructor started leading dances to the band she used the same couple of dances for all the songs. It was disappointing that there were tables covering half of the dance floor, because then it would have been much easier for a floor split or two stepping around if the tables weren't in the way. We went on a weeknight and the bands were acoustic, which is not very conducive to dancing! On the weekend they were full bands but still nothing too impressive. The instructor played a couple songs between sets but half the time it was hard to hear and they didn't know anything about what to play.

Out on the town we stopped in because we heard the rooftop band.  We decided to eat dinner, I got the pulled pork sandwich with Onion Rings it was good but could of been a little heartier,  but being  downtown on Broadway everything is smaller.  The husband got the pulled chicken sandwich with baked beans and he absolutely loved it.   But then again could of been heartier.  But overall service and food was good and the band was just average compared to come we had seen earlier.

This is by far the most family friendly dancing place in Nashville.  It is often crowded on weekends and in the summer.  They have a stage which usually has live music, and a large dance floor where you can go up and dance whenever you want.  The place itself consists of three floors, so its huge.  The food is good, especially the deep fried pickles.  A fun experience for the family, but it isn't overrun with only families, so it's really good for anybody.

Die Karte gibt wieder was man erwarten kann.Bediehnung sehr nett und hilfsbereit.
Die Portionen haben amerikanische Größe
und machen satt
Came in here with some girlfriends late one night, loved the band that was playing upstairs! We had a blast getting on stage with them and singing!

Ok, I am a fan of...

Soulshine's Bushwhacker. It is the BEST Bushwhacker I've ever had.  There's some kind of coconut flavor in there - I'm not sure if it's canned coconut milk, or coconut "beverage" like you can get in a carton. But the concoction of flavors in Soulshine's Bushwhacker are unlike that I've had in a Bushwacker anywhere else - nationally.  It's chocolatey, ice cream-y, coconutty, and YUMMY. It apparently can only be served in a small glass because of its alcohol content - I dunno, after two I wasn't feeling super buzzed.  (Maybe because I also ate??) But run don't walk to have this drink at Soulshine now, it is WORTH IT.
Food is great and the barter is great, Morgan will make you a great drink and give you a awesome convo!!!!

This corner bar/restaurant/honky tonk/constant party place on Broadway has never failed to provide me with a good time.  No matter what time of day I can enjoy a pretty rowdy party.  Post Predators games, happy hour, late night...it's always a good time.  Live music on both the lower and upper decks, pretty fast service considering the constant crowds, cheap beers and lots of singing and dancing...Rippy's is that honky tonk-ish place no one gives enough credit to.  And they have great simple cheap bar food to soak up the booze so easily consumed here.  I love hanging out here, especially early evenings when everyone is just starting to get going.  It's pretty hard to get a table most of the time so be aware of that, and this is not a place to relax.  This is a dancing, drinking, singing, partying, goofing off kind of place, but it can be a lot of fun if that's what you're up for.

Cover charge to eat mediocre food and $5 bottles. Loud, can't hardly hear the person next to you. My short rib grilled cheese was awful. Meat was bland, dry, jerky like, bread tasted like they cooked it in a whole stick of butter. Had to drown it in bbq sauce to make it edible. Save your money and go to honkey tonk row!
It's good,  but service is really bad.  I don't blame the servers,  I think that they are overworked. So be prepared to wait forever to get your order taken...

Yeah it's cute to learn line dancing and all that jazz, but annoying to see all of the brides to be, etc. out there in this tourist trap. Ultimately, the venue is big and nice and clean, but the acts are bland as hell (my 5 year old nephews can play those guitar riffs). It's a tourist trap and the bar tenders are younger than most of my old friendships. Pass.

First time in Nashville so I'm checking out some of the spots. Food was pretty average here, overall. No real standouts on the menu. But the waitress was super friendly and attentive, and the food came out quick (a plus cuz I was starving). And the live music was great. At this particular time, there was a folksy gentleman that played some great oldies and stuff I've never heard which was all great. I'll come back.
Just had a beer but the food did look good. Next time we'll take the time to have a bite to eat.

Good pizza -- nice outdoor space.  Gets really loud, unfortunately.  And, I really really wish they had a decent option for some wine.  Everything in mid-town other than The Tavern -- is a bar.  Soulshine has some class to it -- and it would be really great for us to enjoy a nice glass of wine too -- instead of beer.
I ordered the 1/2 slab ribs. It was kinda dry but tasted ok with sauce on it. The fries and onion rings were good. The band and the music were good too. It was a positive experience overall.

I was very underwhelmed by the Wildhorse Saloon. Although I was able to get in for a reduced cover charge due to the fact that I was attending with a large group, I regret even paying the $3 to get in. Upon entry, we immediately realized that the place had been taken over by teen and pre-teens for the night. This place is 3 full levels plus a huge open dance floor, but there was no getting away from the underage revelers as they were everywhere. Hey, I was a teenager once and I understand that teenagers want to have fun too, but I also think that this bar should enforce a curfew like other bars in the area. Something about teenagers having easy access to alcohol and dancing with people more than twice their age doesn't sit well with me. Additionally, after 10 pm an adult should be able to go to a bar for a night of drinks and fun with friends instead of feeling like they're obligated to be a responsible chaperone.
In addition, the drinks were absolutely horrible. Their "drink special" for the evening was still over $7 and consisted of some cheap-o whiskey and red apple schnapps. Eww. We ended up just ordering a rum and coke and vodka tonic, which were extremely watered-down and still cost $6.75. 
2 stars because it IS an impressive-looking venue and the line dancing instructors and house bands have the potential to make for an awesome night out (as long as you're not the only patron of legal drinking age). I really wanted to like this place, but I don't think I'd ever return as long as they charge a cover.
Amazing pulled pork sandwich, the best I've ever had. Live music was great. No draft beer but overall a great spot on Broadway

I had an amazing time watching the Predators first Stanley Cup game here! The music was spot on and Amber, our bartender was a gem! She was the first person, after a few spots before, to greet us. We only waited a minute before her smiling face asked us what we'd love to enjoy. Didn't try any food this go round but I've heard their ribs were to die for!

I give this place 2 stars only because the waitress (new from Houston) and a waiter (who's name I didnt get saved it from being one star. I walked in a side door, the place is at about 25% capacity. I find a place in the side or back room and sit down. Apparently, I broke a major rule by not being sat by a "hostess". After 20-30 minutes I got up and asked a scruffy looking waiter, who's appearance I can only guess was new wave druggie or homeless person, and asked what the deal was, because everyone's ignoring me. He said, with more than a bit of attitude, that you're supposed to wait to be sat, and then explained that it's on the sign. I said that's no excuse and was about to leave but figured I'd give it one more, if even sarcastic, attempt. So I found a "hostess" who was leaning by the door. I had to ask, since she was trying really hard to ignore me, if I needed to be sat. She said yes and proceeded to sit me almost where I already was. I moved right back to where I was. Still took another 20 minutes before anyone talked to me. When the nice waiter asked me I explained the situation and he was more than and even brought me a free, albeit warm, beer. Then, the waitress, who'd walked by me at least 10 times came by and was very nice and sweet (new from Houston). I had one drink, paid for it and left. I don't blame this on the staff, I blame this on the management. This is a training and culture issue. I suggest a change in management, someone who actually understands how customer driven business works. I won't be back. I was here at about 4pm.

Great live music with no covers and decent pizza!
The live music is the reason we went here and the band on Thursday night was good.  There was no cover and the upstairs was the music stage. The pizza was okay, I had the Mediterranean without mozzarella sub with feta. I found it okay tasty but the pizza was a little small and overcooked. They had a good beer selection of local beers like Yazoo.  In walking distance from the Gulch so we didn't worry about parking.

This was the bar my group and I started off our night as we ventured up and down Broadway. As we pulled up to Broadway to look for parking, Rippy's caught our attention because there was a mob of people standing on the corner to watch the McGregor vs Mayweather fight. We got excited because we saw Rippy's had live performers but then we realized all the bars on Broadway had live performances. I asked for a round of pickle back but they didn't have any so I went to ask for Tokyo Tea which the bartender did not know how to make so she said she will just make me a Long Island Tea (I think, it was super noisey). When she gave us the drinks, it was half filled in a plastic cup and she went to charge me $9 per "drink". The drink wasn't even strong so I just thought it was such a rip off.

This bar has two levels so check that out if you're feeling adventurous. They have live bands on both floors.

OK, this place has really improved so I felt the need to update my original review.  The burgers are to die for - especially the Spice Burger.  The crowd is mixed and the place is still divey (try to avoid the restrooms if possible) but the burgers and the friendly staff make it worthwhile.

Great atmosphere but don't come here for the food.  It's just not good. We had a 3 meat platter and a bunch of extra sides. Nothing outstanding, and nothing with ordering again. Most of it was left uneaten.

Wish I had gone somewhere else instead.   My table was dirty and still had bits of spilled food from the last customers.   I was served my food but was never given any silverware.   The people at the table next to me gave me one of theirs.   The meat was tough, dried out, burnt and fatty.   I should have checked reviews before deciding where to eat.
Food was fine, not great. Wouldn't go again, but if you're on Broadway and don't have too many options I would give it a try.

This night was probably busier than normal since NHL Stanley Cup game was nearby. Had to tip server before being served so she would serve us. Once we got seated & served, it was fun. Food so-so. Buffalo chicken sandwich was not good; fried pickles were good. Live entertainment excellent. Travel Channel was there doing a story, which was fun to watch.
Very nice people, nice patios out front and rooftop as well. Will definitely come back when in Nashville. Great location in Midtown area too.

We were there for a birthday party and Soulshine leaves a lot to be desired. The drink prices are not wonderful, there is no way to carry on any fluid conversation because its way too loud even before the life music starts, the servers are not great (we even saw one eating chips on the floor), the bathrooms were dirty in a way that is not just busy restaurant dirty but neglected deep cleaning dirty... The worst part by far is the food. Our pretty large group ordered several pizzas none of which my wife or I partook in. We had pizza at an office event earlier in the day so we decided to share nachos and a small cup of Red Beans and Rice- huge mistake! The chips were just flour tortillas that had been thrown in the deep fat fryer so they were super greasy. The chicken was dry and tasteless and the whole thing had been sat under the broiler for way too long. It should be a crime for them to serve "red beans and rice"! They we terrible!!! Nothing like NOLA, hell Nothing like Popeyes! Adding insult to injury we have both had miserable stomach aches ever since we ate! We grabbed an Uber and headed home instead of continuing on with the rest of the group!!!

If you're looking for a place to wear your boots and learn some line dances, this is the place to go! They do lessons very frequently where you could learn 3-4 dances in a night. Music was ok, nothing special.

We didn't eat here, so I can't rate the food.  But the atmosphere was fun and energetic.  The waitress was nice.  It was St. Patrick's so they were all dressed up.  The music was wonderful (country, cover bands).  Drinks were very reasonably priced.  Easy to get too.  Parking is tight since there's a free other bars right there too, but if you drive around back, side you can find something.   Has an authentic Nashville appeal, southern style building and decor.  I would def visit this place again when in Nashville.  My mom recommended it to us as they went last summer and stayed all night and had a ball.  Crowd is sooooo friendly and everyone dances, and talks.  There are tables and bar seating.  THey had a concert in the big room the night we were there.  THe porch is nice and open so you can hear the music.  Restroom was clean!  I'm a fan!  It was a good time!!!

Nothing special bbq. Sauces are pre-made and purchased. One for sure is "sweet baby rays" , the jug was sitting out. I expect a bbq place to make their own sauces. Onion rings were poor. Ribs were ok but my wifes are better. Service was average to below average.
Came to this place looking for some good BBQ and found it! Had the pulled chicken and it was so juicy! The server was very helpful and friendly. Will definitely come back when I'm back in Nashville.

We visited on a Tuesday around 4:30pm. The place was empty except for us and another couple (at the bar). Our waiter greeted us and didn't return for a while. He was busy chatting up the other staff members. It was cold inside so we decided to move outside. Our new waitress was wonderful. She was really stationed inside but couldn't have been more attentive to us. The pizza was ok. Probably wouldn't return here.

Visted on 10/16/14 Paul Mccartneys was in town. It was supper busy. We missed our back to hotel. Another one wasn't going to be there for an hour so we chalked to Rippys. It was busy and crowded. Hard to walk. Made our way upstairs. Once we got there a group left and we sat down by the bar. The bartender made eye contact with me and took my order. She made her way around. I thought she forgot about me but she told me she didn't. Watching her work was amazing. She kept scanning the bar. Opening 6 beers at once in a matter of seconds. always making sure drinks were refilled. She never once took a break.  In the hour we were there. I'd come back and try the food.
Food was great, service was excellent.  Loved live music.  Ribs fell off the bone.  Would recommend.

Not the best BBQ or southern flavor, but this is a definitely a taste of Nashville vibes with country moods and charm. We got the stack of ribs and some local beer. It was open seating for the Saturday night we went, but we managed to get a chair on the band side, close to the bar. The back was loud, crowded, and chock full of semi-drunk men playing with the boxing game. It was difficult to enjoy the music, or even a conversation with my boyfriend nonetheless. Overall, touristy spot, nothing more, nothing less.

Super upbeat and cute place to visit! Great music to put you in a good mood! Great find! Food was good and priced well - was a little disappointed they were out of biscuits so ordered the ham dinner and it was too Smokey for my liking. But we loved visiting and glad we decided to pop on!

We had a great waiter! He allowed us to have a nice long dinner without rushing us. We ordered the hot fried chicken, sweet tea pork sandwich, baked beans, mac & cheese and chocolate mousse cake. The music was good. It's a fun place for sure.
This was the only bar we payed a cover charge in all weekend and it was the WORST BAR!!! Horrible music, bad atmosphere, and rude staff. Save your money!

Came here on a Sunday night to experience a live band, line dancing, and ate some snacks. We went to one of the booths on the side, since my mom was worried it'll get too loud in front. Since no servers were serving our tables, we had to go to the bar to order food/drinks. No big deal, we knew ahead of time. We ordered a couple drinks, elephant ear ($7) and fries ($7). When the food came, the portions of the food were a bit smaller than I thought it'll be, but since we were there for entertainment (live band), we stuck around and listen for about an hour. Great for large groups and for big events. Can host big parties if needed. 

TIPS: They have lessons on line dancing at 5pm and 6pm, and a live band plays at 6:30pm. Free cover if you come before 6pm, and if it doesn't get busy they'll keep it free for the rest of the night.

Not too bad! Came on a Sunday afternoon and it was busy but not that bad. Our waitress was nice and the food came out pretty fast. 

I wanted something I can eat later on the go since we were traveling and she suggested the bbq wrap w the meat. Sauce was sweet, the side of curly fries was delish and the band playing was cool.
Great energy here. Good service, food was good (fried catfish, Swiss mushroom burger & onion rings) & good live country music. Friendly patrons & staff.

Live music was great.  The atmosphere was fun.  But really, 2 bartenders to serve a full bar and restaurant?  20 minutes before they even saw us sitting AT THE BAR?!  I had to go camp in the service area, which is useless as they don't have any servers.  Looked like fun, but no service makes for a tough review

Was told to sit wherever, which is fine by me, but then had no one come serve us for 15 minutes. Disappointed, went to talk with someone at the front counter, and was rudely told the issue "was not our problem" by staffing.

I took my out of town relatives to this place because of the positive reviews, what a big mistake.  The food was fair at the best, the hamburger buns were cold, like they had just come out of the refrigerator.  The chicken wings were very tough and tasted like they had been over cooked in old grease.  There was only one women tending the bar and waiting the tables, I saw two groups leave because they could not get service.  Worst of all was the live entertainment, a solo guitar player/singer that could not carry a tune.  I was embarrassed I took company to this dive.  I would give it a zero star if I could.

Update. I just realized I had received a reply from the manager five months ago apologizing and inviting me to give them another chance. That was a welcome response from someone that seems to care about making things better. I have not been back since my low rating but due to the response I received, I will go back. Maybe this was just a bad day of circumstances

Came here for dinner on a Friday night. The place was very busy, but the service was good and the food tasted great. We were seated in the first floor and the only complaint was how close the tables are together. Hopefully you get along with whomever is at the surrounding tables because you're all so close you'll feel like one big party.

What a fun place! We stopped in here just to check it out while we were walking around Nashville. The atmosphere is great, and the decor is very unique. We didn't order anything, so we will definitely need to do that next time we are here. It is a fun place to dance and hang out, but is a fun stop for families too. When saw several people with there children eating and dancing while we were there. I'm glad we stopped in to check out this very popular Nashville destination, and I can't wait to go back and experience some of the food the next time we are in town!

We stopped in after hockey game and at first was happy with environment the front staff was great and restroom employee was super nice. I noticed the staircase and was curious. I asked the female employee who was sitting by the stairs what was up there. I had no idea what she said she mumbled so fast and went back to her texting or game whatever she was doing. I told my husband i had no idea what she said and she immediatly stood up and screemed at me that i called her a bit*ch!!! She said something else to me but i was so shocked i was still processing what was happening then she put both hands on me like she was going to shove me! I yelled at her that she assaulted me and where do i find manager but she immediatly shouted at doorman to get me out of there! Two big big men walked me out. This was unbelievable! So i suggest you skip this place and go down the strip where bars are more friendly i ended up having a blast in nashville other than this one woman everyone else was very welcoming to this hoosier!

On the corner of 5th and broadway. Nice location with several floors.  This location tells you exactly what you should expect, a party.  

The drinks come in plastic cups and food in a basket.  Don't get me wrong food in a basket is food and it is useful to indicate expectations in a restaurant.  This is more of a bar that serves food as opposed to a restaurant.  

It's a fun atmosphere and the food is pretty good.  It has flavor and much potential.  Just hard to get past the food is made and prepared in bulk and thus not served hot.  

Had the ribs, whole rack, brisket, chicken dinner, and all the sides.  The baked beans were nice.  The Mac and cheese tolerable.  

Overall, good location for drinking beers with a large crowd and eating at tables is the back while
Listening to music with poor acoustics.

Such a fun time. Good BBQ and healthy pours at the bar. Fall off of the bone ribs. Beans were excellent. Cole slaw could use some taste. Music was great and line dancing lessons were fun. Have someone try the whipped cream shot at the bar.
Good music. Seemed best band was on the main floor. Tons of seating. Drafts 6$. Didn't order food.

Top notch!

Ribs were awesome, waiter was great and the music was perfect!!!!

Highly recommended

All I can say is hands down the best ribs in Nashville!

The menu is simple and they cater. They are known for their ribs, as the meat is tender and falls right off the bone. My boyfriend and I always split the half rack of ribs with a side of baked beans and cole slaw. 

I have had the pulled pork sandwich before and it is pretty good. It comes with no sauce, but you can choose which sauce you want at the table from the three sauces they make. A apple wood smoked sauce, spicy sauce and their specialty sauce.

They have three stories with live music and the venue next door.
My boyfriend and I love visiting Rippy's when in downtown Nashville.

My girlfriend and I were only in Nashville for a couple of hours, with it being a lunch stop on our cross country road we couldn't stay too long. Being from Massachusetts we don't have many good BBQ places to choose from. After getting to Nashville we decided to check Rippys out. From the outside it looked and sounded like they had a nice vibrant yet relaxing atmosphere. As we walked in we were greeted very nicely and were told we could sit wherever we liked. Immediately after we sat down the waitress came to our table to take our drink order. Following that we order food. My girlfriend order the pulled chicken sandwich and I ordered the pulled pork platter. The chick was perfectly smoky and tender and the pork was also perfectly smoky. Rippys does not add too much BBQ sauce to the dishes, instead they give you two options of sauce in the table, spicy and mild, both are absolutely amazing!!!!!!! Even if you decided not to eat here the atmosphere was amazing, where else can you go at any time of the day and be serenaded by music. Being a country music fan this was the best choice we could have made for a lunch stop on the trip. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!!!

Good food. Poor service. 
10 mins to order drinks. 10 mins for them to come. Soda fountain mix is way off. Food came after 15 mins, but our server took 30 mins to bring the check.

Hey again yelpers!

Wildhorse Saloon. A place to eat, drink, play games, and be merry and it certainly can achieve all those things so long as you've got the patience to put up with the service. Brace yourselves, it's a bit of a long-winded (but always honest!) review. tl;dr at bottom.

When I think of Wildhorse Saloon, images of line-dancing and loud, live music come to mind and it lives up to that image it tries to achieve but honestly, I would not go here to eat a sit-down meal and there is where my brief and slightly frustrating tale begins...

While I was waiting for my friends to meet me a while later I decided to grab an Angry Orchard hard cider and relax on the second floor to watch people play a few games of pool. Much to my distaste, the game room was overtaken by a group of immature, rowdy children. I understand that kids will be kids but their parents really should've controlled them more as they were being aggressive with Wildhorse property such as banging pool cues together as if they were swords or climbing on top of the pool tables to make a shot or spilling their Shirley Temples over the furniture without regard to where they were. I mostly blame the parents but the wait staff did nothing to minimise their exuberance and how they might be preventing other patrons from enjoying their visit.

Once my friends arrived we were able to move to a proper table (now that they weren't still taken). We had to actually get up and walk over to the bar to ask someone to service us. I get it though, I understand that this is hardly a place one would normally go to have a sit-down meal but really now.. Once we finally got our menus, it was about 30 to 45 mins to actually get our food and drinks and when it came time to pay, the server actually lost my debit card! I get that accidents happen but for things like that, servers should really take extra care when handling them.

All in all the best part about my stay was the Angry Orchard, the billiards, and the company of my friends.

Happy yelping!

tl;dr --} The food wasn't that great for the price you'd pay, the time it takes for anyone to visit your table to take orders is ridiculous, and the staff have little regard for proper healthy practises for a food and beverage environment. Only go here to drink, dance, and listen to music (really really loud music) and little else.

Racist door man, would not let my white friend in the door.  We both walked in the same way (sober) but he stopped my friend and said we had to leave after 30 seconds inside. No wonder the place was empty while other places were packed!
We didn't let a racist door man ruin our night, we spent money next door!!  
Too bad for you Rippys for employing a racist at your door Wednesday 3/7-8/18. 
I'll tell everyone of my experience there!!!
This place had a great vibe with some good food! The best part was the drinks. We got save a horse and I could have drank like 10 of them!
Super fast, excellent service. Delicious pulled pork. A great spot in Nashville

I've never been a huge fan of bbq but then I went to Rippy's with some friends. The service was okay, but the food was phenomenal. The portions were HUGE but you wanted to keep eating. I went two separate times and got the pulled pork plate and the chicken tenders. Each time I got potato salad and baked beans as a side. The live music is phenomenal and there are great views over looking broadway. You will not be disappointed if you go to Rippys. You will leave full and ready to come back again!
Food is good. Great selection of non pizza appetizers and meals. Staff is friendly and helpful. Parking can be hard to find.

Went here with my entire family for spring break. We arrived during lunch hours and got to our seats fairly fast. The service was excellent as well as the good. Our server was fantastic and kept our drinks full. We will be back!

I stopped by this place to see a friend play music and drove right by it. I had to do a double take to make sure I was in the right area.

DON'T JUDGE  A BOOK BY ITS COVER

Although dark, smokey and deliciously divey, Twin Kegs is a great place to relax with cheap beer and friends. I am definitely looking forward to returning so that I can try their famous burgers!
The BBQ WAS AWFUL.  The music was ok. The constant begging for tips by the band was annoying. The service was not spectacular and her attitude was pretty poor in general.

A standard suggestion if you are coming to downtown but it just didn't do it for me.  Subpar food,  that everyone raves about but I was not inclined to come back again.  The live music is nice- loud , loud scene and I may have been the only one there not drunk.  Typical scene for downtown Broadway bar but I expected more from the food  side.  The pulled pork was not warm, actually room temp? Onion rings must have been sitting a while - could be due to the time I went in - 5:30 - 6:00.

Didn't eat here but the small pizzas walking by looked tasty. We went upstairs to check out some live music on a Saturday night. The place wasn't packed so you could actually sit down and hang out enjoying the band. The bands everywhere we went were pretty good but band last Sat was a cut above.

What we all really loved was our bartender Tiffany. She kept the drinks coming, was very nice to talk to, and even offered us a free pizza that came out as a mistake. We had just had an amazing and very large dinner just before arriving so we passed but it's the thought that counts. Thanks Tiffany!

When on vacation I don't like to go to the same place twice. But we got an appetizer one day and ate dinner another night. It amazes me how you can cram so many people into one place and still have good service. Food was good and they had entertainment on all 3 floors.

Let me start with the bathroom lady Barbara, she was so sweet and attending. I didn't have singles to tip her, so I had to back to the bar to get change. She was an absolute sweetheart! 
The place was pretty empty for a Saturday night. They had a really good band playing called the Broseph E Lee, who had a pretty good crowd dancing. 
The beers were $6 which is not so bad. Everyone seemed so friendly and fun. It was a good time. Plus, they had these horses around the place that look pretty cool.
Awesome spot for a bucket of beers and great music. Atmosphere is amazing. The grilled cheese is also incredible.

Went to wild horse for a bachelorette party with 14 girls. The doormen were so rude we should have left. All we wanted was to eat dinner, so the $6 cover seemed a little rediculous just to pay to eat. Food was good, but our server took the bill and divided it by 3 without our consent and made it very difficult to split up the check. Line dancing was ok, but the band was on break the bulk of the time we were there and the concert announcements on the big screens were severely outdated. The line dance teachers also pushed the gift shop real hard, making wild horse saloon feel like even more of a tourist trap. We won't be back.

Of all the food in Nashville, a red flag goes up when everyone has a wait...except this place.

Came in on a Sunday night for dinner.  Was promptly seated in the second floor dining room.  Tried a local beer I asked the waiter about.  He couldn't really describe it, but said he liked it, so I tried it.  Not bad.

Ordered fried pickles as an appetizer.  They were also,  OK.  They didn't shake the basket during frying and several were stuck together, but the breading was light and crisp.

Ordered the 1/2 smoked chicken, baked beans and Cole slaw.  The sides were pretty good.  In particular, liked the creamy cole slaw.  The chicken had a nice smoked flavor to it, but was dry.  Even the dark meat was dry.  Not the best.  

Also had a cheeseburger and buffalo chicken wrap with curly fries and potato salad.  Everything comes to the table in plastic baskets, with plastic silverware and napkins in a little shrink wrapped packet.  Oh yeah, and the beer did not come with a glass, nor were we given water.

OK, so kinda low brow, but it could have worked.  The band on the second floor, though we couldn't see them, sounded good and had the crowd around the bar hopping.  But then we waited.....and waited....and waited.  The waiter finally asked if we wanted our check, and we waited more...and waited more....and waited more.

I was on the fence between a 3 or 4 star review, which evolved to a 2.  Best part of the night was their tee-shirts.  On the back it says "You pull my pork, I'll rub your ribs".  At least I had the band to listen to...
Best dive bar in Nashville. Hands down. Cheap beer, great burger. Karaoke is fun, I think it is held every night around 8

Great place on 2nd Avenue.  Very large wide open place with a large dance floor.  Service and food was good.  This place had a wide variety of folks from younger families to young groups and older folks as well. The band the night we were there was more rock than country so we didn't stay very long.  This is a great alternative to all the places on Broadway that cater to a young crowd looking to simply get very drunk.  I'd go again.
One of the nicest venue's in Nashville.  Very comfortable seating.  Excellent sound.  Would go as much as we could.

(6/23/2014)  Did the honky tonk crawl while visiting town for a conference (yes, we were tourists).  Stopped into Rippy's, were enticed by the open patio on the top level.  Did not eat here, but did get some drinks and hang out a bit.  Top level had a decent set of two guys with two guitars, singer/songwriter stuff.  Ventured downstairs to the street level bar to listen to an ear-splitting, very bad cover of "Free Bird."  Drinks were a little pricey, mostly offered rail/well or cheap brands.  Did enjoy the patio, since it's on a corner, probably one of the better views of Lower Broad.

Stopped by here with a huge group of folks attending the same conference. We weren't able to sit with our group because they said too many people in that section. So had to sit separate. Kind of lame. Sat at the bar. Bar tender was very friendly. Pork chop was tasty but so small. Pablano grits were very good.  The fried pickles were good as well. Portions could have been a bit bigger. Men's restroom attendant was kind of a pain. He was more in the way than helpful. Very loud place as well but makes sense since there is a big stage and live music.

This is one of the places we kept going back to. The bartenders were prompt with service and with the exception of one all seemed to be happy. The bands/singers were great at getting the crowds involved and played everything that was requested. One of the downsides was having to order dinner to sit at a table. I understand if the place is packed but when you have 10 open tables and paying customers for drinks seems like you're turning away business. Other than that great times!

Seriously, how do you get pulled pork from a can!!
 The service was the worst ever and the food was pathetic!! That is as nice as I can say about it!  Don't waste your time!

Bigger venue than most other places near Broadway. There were families, couples from the resort, and a few people in their twenties to thirties. 
The band put on a performance with lights and dance moves. There was space for line dancing, with people dancing to every song.

I'll revise my prior review with an extra star. This place has grown on me a little, and mostly because of the live music scene that's starting to take root on their newer patio stage. I'm wondering if they'll be able to effectively keep it going during the colder months.

I still think the food is a tad overpriced, but it's fairly standard for the neighborhood. This isn't a frequent hangout for me, but it's coming along well.

Food was pretty good, service was mediocre. Disclaimer we had a party of about 13-16 people & 3-4 of our orders were wrong when we received them. One of them was still wrong when they brought it out the second time. They should've had 2 servers taking care of us.

Meandered in here last Saturday around 3 pm-ish as the more popular bbq joint across the street had a line out the door and down the street. (That one served smoked beef brisket, this place didn't.) Rippys is self-seating so I found an open stool at a long shared island bar. The bartender, "Tee" (a petite, super cutie-patootie) came out promptly and got my drink order going. Since there was no beef brisket available, I went with a pulled chicken sandwich and potato salad. It came out warm but with no sauce of any kind as you are supposed to add it from the bottles at your table. After liberally dousing it in Mild, it was fine. Tee was slammed and took a few tries to get me my check at the end of the meal, but I didn't hold it against her as the place was busy. As far as bbq goes, it was pretty average so I can understand why this place didn't have a line out the door. I think 3 stars just about nails it.

This is neat little music/restaurant venue, right on the main Broadway drag in downtown Nashville. The place has two levels (the upstairs being open-air, and the downstairs being indoors but well-lit by the numerous windows) and live music constantly performing on both levels. We sat upstairs and nearly sweated our butts off in the humidity (no fans were running), but the musical entertainment was good enough to distract us from the ever-growing pool of sweat running off of our bodies and onto our chairs. The iced tea was brewed fresh and the pulled pork sandwich was tasty; nothing special, but the BBQ sauces on the table let you customize the sandwich to your preferred flavor. Our server was also very good about checking in with everyone and getting stuff to tables quickly, even though they were busy. This place is a dive and a little sticky from numerous nights of partying tourists, but I would recommend it on the basis of a no-frills meal with great live music!

Abysmal. Service was terrible. I waited at one of the back bars for 20+ minutes. The bartender (Melissa) was picking and choosing which customers to serve- was not even going down the line just switching back and totally ignoring my half of the bar. Oh, and did I mention she had her 2 sons (underage- the one kid had to be 11) back behind the bar? To put away glasses... insanely irresponsible not to mention ILLEGAL. I ordered 2 double drinks - watched her make them- she measured out 1 shot per drink. So I paid 2x and didn't even get what I ordered. 

We were told there was a 2.5 hour wait for a table - and behind the seats we got along the bar there were 3 massive empty booths that sat vacant and covered in glasses & such for over FORTY FIVE MINUTES. How are you that understaffed? Every surface was covered in old glasses and napkins. It was disgusting. 

I will never come back - nor would I recommend. FIND ANYWHERE ELSE.

Came in on a Saturday night for a quick bite to eat.  The food was tasty, but maybe 4/5, service a little slow but it's busy so whatever; the house band sounded really good and it was the perfect volume.  Super friendly people, I wish I could stay longer, so 5/5 from me, I'll be back.

This place was ok, we went for dinner and the music act had not started yet and the DJ was playing music and taking requests. They taught some people a line dance, which seemed like fun.

The food was ok, but it must be the atmosphere more than the food that attracts the people.  

I would like to go back & watch the live acts next time.

I just love this place. Every time I come to Nashville, this is the go to place for me. To me, food is good. I love their hot wings and the sweet potato fries. Food is reasonable to. I just like the atmosphere, people whether the waitresses or the crowd in general and of course the music.

Keeping it basic:
1. Self seating
2. Hot as hell. Up stairs. No a/c giant ceiling fans.
3. Service was bad. As hot as it is they need to make sure they refill drinks.  Never got the refill we asked for.
4.  BBQ pull pork sandwich was amazing!! 
5. Music was great. 
Will come back when the weather is cooler and maybe the service will be better since they were so busy.

Excellent experience during CMA Fest.  One of the artists performing was Maggie Baugh, she was an excellent new up and coming star.  She rocked out on The Devil Went Down to Georgia which is amazing for an 18 YO to play on the fiddle.  The whiskey drinks were amazing, I got the one with blackberry moonshine or whiskey, the brisket was great, got the platter.  Service was awesome too.  Great atmosphere and we stayed about 2 hours.  Bathrooms super clean and they have a bathroom attendant.  Only place I saw that for our whole 4 day trip to Nashville.  Definitely a must do...I liked that they streamlined the menu for the crowds....
Great wings and fried chicken!  Awesome live music and Jenna was the most amazing server!

If there was a rating less 0 I would. Ally is worst bar tender ever. Sensitive doesn't cover the abomination that is her attitude. Food was not bad, and other bartender was awesome but getting no reason removed from bar was uncalled for in this situation. Save your money and go elsewhere

Absolutely DELISH! I had the pulled pork sandwich and onion rings and it just doesn't get any better! We dined upstairs for dinner and it was a group of 3 guys playing guitars on 5/13/13. I wish I would've caught their names because they really did a great job! The service was super fast and friendly! If you are in Nashville don't miss Rippy's!!!!
had the pulled chicken platter which was huge and delicious! the baked beans were a great side dish as well!

Zoë was courteous and on fleek. She knows how to pour a drink. And picks your jacket off the ground. Marinara vats to dip your cheesy sorrows in. And beer to pick up your spirits. Soulshine, you get the coolinary cheers for service and food!

Casual, laid back atmosphere. Good food. Avoid the fries they were kind of mealy but the pulled pork, pork loin melt and beans were excellent. Upstairs outdoor eating area with live music was the perfect place to spend a muggy Thursday afternoon.

Oops, don't get a burger here! OK so, tonight we decided to cruise the strip for a 3 course meal and drinks. We decided to have a burger. We've had some good burgers in this city... We decided to stop here because, quite frankly, we were walking by. There was live music and the atmosphere isn't anything to write home about but not awful.
We ordered a cheese burger and the tomato might have been fresh but I'm pretty sure I just ate a frozen patty with a Kraft single. Maybe I've become a food snob but it was awful. I don't mind bar food or dive bars but frozen patty, ouch! The onion rings were worth the upgrade, golden, crispy and thick. If I come back I'll stick to live music and bottle beer, nothing on tap.... Actually, I probably won't be back...

El Wildhorse Saloon es otro bar clásico de Nashville para ir a beber algo, bailar honky tonk o escuchar música en vivo.

A diferencia de otros, este espacio es más elegante y exclusivo, como también lo son los precios. El lugar es muy lindo y tiene un salón sumamente amplio. Los tragos están OK, pero no son nada extraordinario, lo copado es que te los sirven en un vaso con forma de bota, el cual luego te lo podes llevar como souvenir.

Siempre hay músicos que tocan en vivo, de los cuales varios son conocidos o famosos en la región, como también hay clases de baile. Todo con muy buena onda, lo que hace que la experiencia sea bastante placentera.
Food was good and well priced. Unfortunately they assigned one waitress to a group of 20+ customers. This made service kind of slow.

The stage & 3 story building was cool but $6 cover (unless you're staying at a Mariott, then it's free). Our first waiter was rude but we moved tables & everyone else was very friendly. Kale salad with chicken was delish. The band was meh - old songs with a pop hit thrown in here & there. They also faked a journey song with piped in guitar & voice backup. The line dance lesson was less than 10 min & one slow simple dance. All in all we were glad to have given it a try but once was enough.

It was our first time dining at soulshine and we will be back sooner than later! Fast service, EXCELLENT pizza (had the five cheese) drinks were awesome too! The Moscow mule  love the love music playing upstairs too. Awesome pizza joint!

Huge place, was there for a really popular event with about 1500 other people and they handled the whole thing well. 
Just one thing -  Do not eat their "hot chicken"

Service was a bit spotty to begin. Had to ask for a menu. The waiter (Adam) was good. I order the rainbow warrior and it was good. Wife order the Mediterranean and the shrimp on the pizza were not all peeled. Overall, nothing spectacular either way.

A Nashville local took us out-of-towners here last night. We like to dance and this bar was awesome - way worth the $6 cover. It takes some bravery to get on the dance floor, but everyone is quick to teach and not judge! The band was Brother Trouble - great for dancing!  It was also a nice break from the sloppy drunk crowds that sometimes take over the other bars.

Had this place on our list of places to try. I thought the prices were a little high, but the food was generally good. We ordered the fried pickles and I have to say that was my favorite part. I got a burger and my husband got the brisket sandwich. We both had the recommended beer they only sell which was good. They offer line dancing lessons every hour which was fun. They also had live music too. It seemed less authentic than the other places on the main drag, but this place I would bring my kids to as it seemed very family friendly.

Destiny and Bernie are the best bartenders we've EVER had! Destiny made out first trip to Nashville feel like it was home. Apparently she was just training but you never would've known it by the amazing quality of her drinks and personality. 

The line dancing lessons were a blast and we really enjoyed learning and dancing! It was a fun mix of hanging out listening to phenomenal country music and dancing. 

If you go, go to the bar on the left side of the stage when you walk in and see Destiny and Bernie. Order yourself a Weekend at Bernie's shot or drink, an amazing shot that will knock you out! 

Bottom line is just go to the Wildhorse Saloon. Awesome experience and a breath of fresh air after Broadway!
Hosted company customer event in area behind bar.  Food was great and beer was cold!!
The drinks are good, the patio is fantastic, but the pizza is mediocre.
We stopped in during a weekend trip to Nashville and loved this place. The service was great and food was delicious.

During the Music Biz conference, we went to Rippy's twice. The location was prime and the food was good, so why not?

I got the Pulled Pork plate, which came with two sides. They also had two choices of barbecue available on the table. You get so much food! It's hard to leave here hungry.

The second time around, we ordered drinks, which were pricey, but pretty average for a Broadway bar/restaurant. I loved the live music both nights I was here! Great atmosphere and great barbecue for anyone visiting Nashville!

Had a great time Sunday night, 2/19. I was in town for a celebration with my company Tractor Supply. We watched a great performance by the band. The food was terrific. Lots of Bar-B-Que, some corn. And good times.

Needed some food while on Broadway. We had a pulled pork and a pulled chicken sandwich. The meat was very well tender and had a perfect taste! Price was very reasonable for the area! Highly recommend!
Seems to have good specials. I came at 10pm and live music had stopped. I was a little bummed about that. Had the five cheese pizza and it was good! Not chicago pizza, though . Overall, worth a stop.

Probably the divest dive I've ever been to. The bartenders here can be a little cold at first but warm up to you after you've been there a couple times. The drinks and food are dirt cheap. Recently I went here and had two beers and tots an the bill was $5.50. As others have noted, it can get pretty smokey in here.

First Time in Nashville and am not a huge country fan. Was there for a conference and ended up staying there till closing every night. Was one of the funnest times I've ever had. Great entertainment and drinks were reasonable .

I had no idea this place was called Rippy's Ribs until I looked at the receipt. I love ribs. I wish I was able to partake but it was late on a Sunday night. All there was was music and booze. And I'm OK with that.

First floor had a band. Looked like the male - female leads were just into each other so we went upstairs where it was an all male band and there were walls just open air and views up and down Broadway. How awesome. My drink here was definitely a stiff one. Thank you, Blondie, I mean Crystal D. The band was much better up here that it even got us out on the dance floor along with three other people. But it was fun. Good times at Rippy's.

Get you some crawfish soup on a Sunday blues jam night, in addition to a chicken Alfredo pizza with mushrooms added. Also the "Caroline" shot (ask your beautiful blonde bartender Allison) isn't a bad idea either. Thank me later. And tip the band. #soulshineyall

My older daughter had been telling me about SoulShine and today I had an opportunity to try it. We had "The Kitchen Sink" pizza and it was very good. The ingredients were fresh, the service was timely, and our server was wonderful!!! My younger daughter had the hot wings (mild) and the pepperoni bread and she really enjoyed it. I can definitely say I'll be going back. Oh, and we heard some great music coming from upstairs.

Stopped in Nashville for lunch on a road trip and I'm glad we stopped at Rippy's! The atmosphere was awesome. We ate upstairs where there was live music. The performers were very talented, and our server was very friendly and attentive. We each got Pork BBQ sandwiches and they were delicious! We were a little strapped for time and so were very appreciative of the fast service. Highly recommended!

I remember going here in my teenage years when the dancing show was broadcast from this bar and it was so entertaining to see everyone dancing and changing outfits during the commercial breaks.  The bar has been completely remodeled since those days and they now serve food.  It looks like it could be a fun place but when we ventured in, it was dead.  Might still be open based on nostalgia?

What a wonderful surprise for a late night dinner. I had the boss hog pizza- pulled BBQ pork with pineapple, onions and BBQ sauce topped with mozz and jalapeño jack!!  It was amazing!! My hubby had the kitchen sink pizza and also a huge hit. The meatball app had a wonderfully rich tomato sauce that really set off the tender meatballs. Even my unbelievably picky kids were thrilled with their pizza and calzone!!  In a very happening part of town. We happen to hit it at a night when they were trying a little karaoke. That was definitely hit and MISS. But the food was amazing.

Brutal. My daughter goes to school in Nashville so done the Broadway's scene many times. This time I brought my son with me and I thought I should give him a touristy view of the city so I thought we'd try Wild Horse Saloon for some bbq. I HATE going to the typical tourist traps but I thought we'd give it a try. Big mistake!! Both of us have been glued to the toilet since we were there!!

We ordered the spicy fried pickles and they were so over-seasoned it was ridiculous. It wasn't that they were too spicy. It's like they skipped using any batter and just dredged the pickles in cayenne and salt. Literally like putting a tablespoon of salt directly in your mouth. I could only eat 4-5 before I was getting iodine poisoning. My son ate a few more before he quit. To their defense they did take them off the bill but by then the damage was done. 

Quite frankly, the bbq was not that great either but I wouldn't have even written a review if those damn pickles weren't still grinding away in my belly!! Lastly, the main act was pretty week for a Friday night on a famous stage. I'm not going to mention his name but he seemed angry to even be there like it was below him. The dude had no energy. 

Signed,
Still crapping

Quite honestly i was not satisfied with this establishment. The food is way over priced for what it is really worth. The service is nothing spectacular. We were even charged $1 for some ranch dressing. Its $9 for six mozzarella sticks! That is ridiculous! And the french fries were bland and soggy. Not happy.

The Wildhorse Saloon is an awesome venue to see entertainment. I recommend this place for music when you can catch a really good act because the building itself is set up well for shows.

Our experience was just so-so (Monday night and all). The performer Larry Frick and his band was good, but played covers for the simple minds...our simple minds enjoyed some of it just fine. There was a lot of stretching of time by the band, some silly dance contests for tee shirts etc. and the required birthday song for a few people in the audience. 

If you enjoy the silly concept of line dancing (think "a country version of the electric slide", also an embarrassingly corny activity), this place is for you. They even have an on-staff dance coach to help the people that like corny stuff (no self respecting real man would do this in public). Good fun for those types of folks.
