This is definitely a Tourist trap...but then again, Nashville is a street carnival mask on an entire town designed to fleece people and liberate you of your money.

The best fun I had in Nashville was listening to some of the street performers and talking to the homeless and desperate trying to win a buck from you. I gave money to several needy folks and aspiring musicians...that was the best money I spent all night.

So, the Widlhorse food. An Executive Chef? That is funny! Some reviewers compared the food to the handful of American restaurant chains out there. I say those chains make better food.

The "world famous fried pickles" came to our table warm, not hot, and were immediately chilled by the blasting AC vent we were under. They were edible, but barely tasted of pickle. The breading was OK but tasted too much of the oil.

We ordered the BBQ sampler between us two (the server had explained that they were famous for the BBQ). The ribs were good, the chopped pork was fair and the brisket tasted foul, I could not eat it and this was what I was looking forward to.

The three sauces they offered were weird. A sweet unremarkable sauce, a "vinegar sauce" that was really a mustard based sauce and a "hot sauce" that was not hot and had a foreign flavor I could not wrap my head around. None of them went well with any of the BBQ products on the plate.

My wife said the black beans and coleslaw sides were fairly good. I did not eat them.

The Wildhorse draft beer is good, I enjoyed it probably the most of anything about our experience here. The margaritas were not good, but almost no one makes a good margarita so no surprise. Most people actually have zero concept of what makes a good margarita so places like this sell them easily. We had no other types of drinks here (except a rail whisky before I left, but you cant screw that up).

Cover charge was 6 bucks, children 10 or 12. Come on folks, the world does not revolve around your children. These places make money on alcohol; your children hopefully do not drink. Common sense tells you why the cover. Take your kids to Opry...this is a music bar club...and town. 

Our server was good. Once he knew we weren't your typical tourists looking to pinch a penny at every turn he was our best friend. I gave him a $20 tip on an $87 tab and he shook my hand. Like the struggling people on the street...this was good money spent; servers in towns like this deal with some pretty stupid people and deserve to have a good night once on a while.

Wildhorse? Yep, great place for music. But also a corny tourist joint for people that like that stuff. I wish we had gotten a bite to eat elsewhere and bar hopped all night, there were no covers in most of the clubs that night and they were begging for customers this Monday night. 

I would go to the Wildhorse for a show if we were in town when someone really good is plating there...but eat elsewhere and order beer or simple basic cocktails.

FYI folks, you do not have to order the beer in a souvenir glass, you can order pints. All the other cheesy souvenir drinks on the menu are apparently mandatory if you want that drink. If you want a souvenir glass, the drink menu is perfect for you, otherwise order the basics because specialty drinks are usually weak and overpriced almost everywhere...that silly little umbrella or garnish costs you a bunch!
Great atmosphere. Bloody's blow. Stick with Bud Light if you are a professional. Good live music. Upstairs too crowded to participate. Their loss.

Rippy's is named well!!  What a Rip-Off!  Our group stopped for a drink and a little food - so far so good!  When I got the bill I Shat Myself!  One person in the group ordered 3 double 7 and 7's and Rip-Off's charged me $54 dollars!!!  What!!??  I could have bought an entire handle at that price!!  We have 2000 people here for 2 days and if it's up to me NONE OF THEM WILL ENTER THIS RIP-OFF ESTABLISHMENT!!
Good food, cool live music scene, though service was exceedingly slow in all account and drinks are a bit pricey. Would go back because of the music for sure.
Best ribs I've ever had! They make an awesome Salty Dog.   Atmosphere was so much fun!
GREAT pizza place in Nashville with a wide range of beers on tap. We were just in town for the weekend, but would recommend it to locals and tourists alike.
In Nashville for only a day and looking for some live music on a Tuesday morning and I found it at Rippy's! Awesome sounds and good food! #NashvilleAndChill

This place is a good time if you want a country experience when you are in Nashville. They always have good country performers live on stage. I only listen to country music when I'm riding in my friend's truck. And I've heard some of the songs the performers were playing. 
The beef brisket was extremely tender and the chopped pork was delicious too. The mac and cheese was great. It was shells with white cheese. 
Between country performers they have country line dancing. Someone on stage walks the crowd on the dance floor through some line dancing steps. Then the entire dance floor line dances. It's fun. 
They have drinks here, of course. But you can have some great country fun without getting buzzed. Frankly, I had water.

I work for a country singer from California named Eileen Carey, she was one of the acts on the many stages at Rippy's the night they sent everyone to the garage during the Tornado warning sirens and hard rain that hit Nashville. We were there in the middle of the Country Radio Seminar taking place all week at the old convention center.

I know a tornado is no joke, but what a great bunch of people were at Rippy's that night, cause everyone stayed in good humor and concern for each other! I think the ambience and warmth of a place makes my food taste better. We were in Nashville for 5 days and ate at Rippy's 4 times! Yeah, we appreciated the opportunity to play the place, but we liked the food. Simple as that. And that house band that played our side-room after everyone returned that stormy night was damn good!

I know the food is the thing therel, and John and Eileen both availed themselves of the menu specialties, my troubled stomach found three Jr. Cheeseburgers and the fries, all I really ate on my visit to Music City! Should have brought one on the plane back to Los Angeles. 

Thanks Jim!

joey alkes

Whoa! Where do I start?.... First, I have been to this place several times since it's inception, and were it not for the good service of Ryan, my favorite server, I've had less than an OK experience here. Secondly, the food takes forever and the quality is  more often than not, poor! Tonight was a whole 'nuther experience!!!! In my 20+ years in this industry, I have NEVER...EVER been treated so rudely by a bartender/server! It took 30-45 minutes for an order of wings, and when they finally arrived and after a few eaten wings, my female companion noticed that they were very under-cooked(i.e, bloody). I asked the bartender if they could be taken off my tab...that's where it all went downhill!!! The night went from an "OK" experience to an absolutely "HORRIBLE" one!!!. I had to ask for a manager to voice my complaint about the rudeness of the bartender, by way the way, while talking to the manager, my MORE than gracious tip was slammed down on the bar by the bartender as he says he didn't want it. AWFUL! PLAIN AWFUL! Truely disgusted by tonight, and it ruined a perfectly great evening up until then.

We came in on a Sunday night around 8-9pm for dinner. There was no wait. We got seated right away with a good view of the dance floor & stage. Matt Poling was performing, he was great. We were pleasantly surprised that this is owned by Gaylord Entertainment as me & the BF are both ex-Stars. We ordered the fried pickles & they were awesome! I don't like when they over-bread fried pickles but they had the perfect ratio to them! We also shared an entree with the brisket & pulled pork with sides of collard greens & mac n cheese. This entree was just ok. Collard greens were not the best I've ever had. It was a great big portion so come hungry. It wasn't unreasonably priced either. Definitely try to check this place out! They do free line dancing classes as well!

A couple of our friends who had been to Nashville suggested this place for line dancing. It seems like a moderately local spot to go to, which was definitely a plus when we were looking for things to do. When a band isn't playing, a lead dancer goes on the stage and teaches you the moves for the dance. You learn together in a group and then the music plays for you to practice, before the entire song plays. At first, my friends and I were intimidated, but in truly Southern style, a couple of the locals chatted us up and convinced us to go up there. In our group of 3, there was 1 guy and he was truly impressed with how many girls were up there dancing. It was overwhelmingly female and fun for all.

We didn't get any food, but had a few drinks which were average and nothing special. But we didn't come for the food! And I will definitely come back for the dancing if I'm in Nashville again. So fun!

So a group of us 50 somethings go for some good music and dancing. One member of our party, a 66 year old woman did not have id. Instead of using sound judgment the bouncer said he had to mark both of her hands with a black marker so she couldn't get a drink. How humiliating. On top of that the band was mediocre. Much better music venues in Nashville.
Burgers were delicious. Service was friendly and beers were cold. Wish it was a non smoking place but oh well... good burgers almost make up for it!

Rippy's is a popular bar that features barbecue.  Multiple people gave it glowing recommendations so it was our first stop for food in Nashville.

When we arrived we were told to seat ourselves.  It took about 10 minutes for a server to greet us.  We had read that service can be a little slow here, so as soon as the waitress got to us we placed our orders.  I had the pulled pork with coleslaw (can you eat it without coleslaw?).  It was good, but I was not super impressed.  The bun was large and plain.  The pork could have used a bit more seasoning and the bbq sauce was ok. The coleslaw didn't really stand out either.  I felt like my meal was ok here and was reasonably priced, but I will probably not be back here.  I did have a friend's onion ring though and that was fantastic.
Good enough food to eat twice in a day. The bartender Dominique made the time though, great person highly suggest coming
Avoid this place if you are in a hurry. Service is horrible, but the live music, cheap food and beer make it a great spot to waste away an afternoon.

We were in downtown Nashville and happened to stumble on this barbeque place. Jennifer S was our server and was very nice and attentive. Our only surprise is that we asked for pickles with our meals and were charged for them. 
I ordered baby back ribs and The meat just fell off the bone.  The coleslaw was ok but the onion rings were great.

Good ribs - especially for being on Broadway where . Had a really good band with a surprising mix of people and ages. I was there at 9pm on a thursday night and the drunks were out, but hey its a honky tonk right?

Here during the NCAA final four. Place was packed (as was every place in the vicinity). Took a while to find a table. Once we snagged one, the service (Andrew) was fast and courteous. Me got the pulled pork dinner. LOTS of food and it was excellent. Really, really good. Yes, it was loud and rowdy. It's Nashville and final four. If loud and rambunctious isn't your thing, stay home.

Horrible bar service on the first floor. Stood at the bar for 15 minutes while the arrogant bartenders pretended like they didn't see us. Went up to the 2nd floor and received much better service. Beers and shots were overpriced.

The bartender was so drugged out and hammered that she pocketed my credit card with no recollection of doing so. She game me 5 Coors Lights, told me to "get the fuck out of her bar" which I replied "no problem, just give me my credit card" to which she had no idea what I was talking about. Meanwhile, they let me look for the credit card behind the bar like I owned the place. A patron of the bar had to go through the bartenders pockets while she was too drunk to realize what he was doing and fish out my credit card. She wasn't trying to steal the card, she was just drunk. When someone hands me something when I'm drunk, guess what, I put it in my pocket. 10/10 would come back for 5 free Coors Lights.

Started with a ton of empty tables and told I had to see hostess ok fine them told 30 min wait for a said table. Waited once seated quick devices but good was terrible. And too late once the waitress came back to complain and re order something else. And they have no concept of craft beer! Do yourself a favor and pass on this tourist trap!!!!
Fun time doing line dancing with the kids. The dance floor is huge and the ceiling is so cool with the horses. The kids had a lot of fun. We didn't stay to eat.

Everything is served in plastic. 
Coleslaw was tasteless.
Had to ask for drink refills.
Moves trashcans up to tables to clean them.
The BBQ sauce was tasty and the pulled pork sandwich was good.
$25 for 2 pulled pork sandwiches with one side each and 2 drinks...

Being in Nashville, I figured I would try the fried catfish.  Boy, was I surprised, the catfish was almost burnt, very brown and crispy...not what's you would expect from a restaurant in the south.  And for the price they charged for this (1) piece of catfish, you would think it was an award winning dish...very basic menu, no be thrills....the live band was entertaining and the waitress was friendly.

Family place up till 10 pm.

Fun place! I've only ever gotten pizza here, none of the other stuff. I have been upstairs and downstairs. The upstairs had live music when I was there which was fun. Both floors have a lot of TV's and they had the Preds game on the second time I went (I don't remember what was on the first time).

Pizzas are good. Not the best white pizza, but it isn't bad either. Good range of beers and hard ciders. The chicken Caesar salad was HUGE! 

This place goes on and off the Vandy card which is nice for students!

This place is the image that pops into your head when someone says dive bar. Small and smokey with cold beer, dart boards, and karaoke. What else do you expect? It's an awesome place if you want to get your karaoke on but don't want to head into down town. Huge book of music to choose from. Good times are always abound when you head in here. This place is definitely better on the inside.
Burger was excellent and the bbq sauce is to die for! The drinks are great and the service was amazing. Great place for lunch!

Def didn't spend too much time here but from the 3 hours I was there, I have no complaints. Live music, billiard and like dancing lessons...doesn't get much better than that! Gran a drink in a boot and keep the glass boot! Cheers
OMG!! This place was beyond AMAZING. Beautiful inside. Food to die for. Look above you in restaurant to view the horses above you (Full size)

Overall: Pizza options a plenty, service is so-so.

Food: There is literally a pizza to fit an palate.. and you can get a whole wheat crust. My only problem is a few I've had were pretty bland and I probably could have made a better pie at home. Still, I've been a few times and would probably go back because of the option to get your own personal-sized pizza with whatever toppings you want.

Service/Atmosphere: Perhaps it was my fault for expecting to take a big group there on a Saturday night.... but I wasn't impressed. We called earlier in the week, attempting to alert them to the huge group coming (ready to spend $$) and they seemed less than receptive. In the end, the crew was fed and left full and happy but.. it was a little awkward in the process to round up our own tables to push together and steal chairs.
If it's nice, eat outside! Great lil patio area.

In all honesty, I hope this place lasts! It's a nice addition to the Midtown food scene.

We stayed at a nearby hotel    Had dinner and enjoyed the Live Music atmosphere at The Palace. A local bar feel.  We had the swish cheese mushroom burger and Cat Fish dinner.  We would recommend the Catfish over the burger.  

An enjoyable dinner with live music, good service and good food.  

I could do this every night.
One of the best little dives in Nashville. Awesome burgers and a solid hang with cheap beer.
This was a reasonably priced music and food venue. The food was no frills, but I wasn't expecting anything.we enjoyed the music, the Grassy Knoll boys were really good.

The Nashville Palace recently re-opened, and Nashville is buzzing with excitement about this historic venue.  It's a spot where your favorite traditional country music can be heard, every day of the week, played by some seriously talented musicians who just happen to love this music as much as you do.
The service is friendly, and the menu of sandwiches, burgers (including a veggie burger!) and classic sides such as sweet potato fries and onion rings, add to the vibe. The restaurant/bar space is walled with vintage posters of classic country stars (Marty Robbins gets special notice), shelves stacked with cowboy boots, and a vintage-looking sliding garage door that opens off the side of the stage to a large patio deck with plenty of extra picnic bench seating.
The Palace is located just north of the Opry, and at the moment, there's plenty of parking just outside the front door.  The lunchtime shows are amazing, and the new owner, Jesse Lee Jones, leads his own band, Brazilbilly, on weekend nights.  Don't miss this!
Took 1 step in and smelt like an ashtray and walked right back out. Was excited to try this local dive but man that smell of cigarettes was so bad. If you're a smoker you'll love it.

So far, my favorite "bar/ saloon" in Nashville. They have a large dance floor and teach nightly Line dance lessons. My friends and I love to take advantage of it! Sometimes it can get a bit crowded and the food is way overpriced. But I sure do love the fried pickles!!! The decor and vibe is very cool as well.

Went here twice and wasn't bad. The band's that played were for a little older generation but I still liked it. Nice small little bar up front with friendly bartenders and food was great and u couldn't complain about the price  either.

The food was great and perfect to start a night out drinking. But the service was fine until we got the check. Then the server made a big deal that they "never split the checks" and had "done us a favor" by doing so. They never mentioned that our "large party" of 8 was going to have added gratuity and the checks shouldn't be split. There were mistakes on all of the checks and no had the right total to pay. Probably won't come with more than 2-3 people again.

Ate at this place with my brother while visiting in Nashville. I was really hungry so I got a few sides. My brother licked his plate clean from the ribs he got. I enjoyed my collard greens, curly friends and corn bread. It's was a good amount of food. Waitress was really helpful and quick with brining back my beverages. My brother said his ribs were delicious and he even ordered some more food. The IPA I had was really good too!! 

This is a great place to stop for music and a good bite to eat while I'm Nashville.

We're just stopping through Nashville on our way home from vacation, and we're a little puzzled why this place is only receiving 3.5 stars?!? We were a group of 8, 4 adults and 4 kids, and all of us raved about it! We tried different pizzas, all of which were tasty. GREAT crust, quality toppings!

We spent a day in Charleston, SC while on vacation and thought it would be some of the best bread pudding we could find in the country, but were sadly disappointed. The Slap Yo Mama Bread Pudding here, though? Spot on! Others tried the cheesecake which was met with two thumbs up and the brownie was the lone disappointment, but not enough of one to make my rating any less.

Service was excellent, the atmosphere had a hip vibe to it, and the live music upstairs pulled everything together! A fantastic spot in the Music Row area!

Great place to escape the tourists and truly enjoy yourself without the pretense in other "boroughs & districts" of town. It is simply a bar to be yourself. Amazing selection of beers, and the food is delicious!!!! Burgers brought me here, the bartenders & regulars kept me entertained, and the ambience is what has continued drawing me back. Do yourself a favor and explore this place when you're looking for a spot to just relax and just be you. 

****FRESH PORK RINDS**** A MUST HAVE!!!!! DON'T FORGET THE LOUISIANA HOT SAUCE

Decent place near Opryland! Live music,  cheap but decent food and low priced beer. Come here for a nice casual place to go for dinner and a beer with live music. Portions were a bit small though and my order did not come out the way I ordered it. Cheaper here than Opryland restaurants though.

I'm totally late writing this review and the only reason I just thought about it is because I'm going here tonight with a friend. Anywhoooo...I visit here some weeks ago by myself, on a night a band was playing. I wasn't promptly greeted when I walked thru the door and whenever I was, the host wasn't too cheerful. I let it pass considering it was a Saturday night and the place was busy. She did inform me that if I didn't want to wait on a table I was welcome to sit at the bar which was A-Ok. Ordered a seafood Calzone and an Angry Orchard beer. Received my food in ample enough time. It was a little burned on the edges but VERY delicious just the same. The cheese and seafood in the calzone was like RIDICULOUS and I mean that in a good way! The bartender(female) was excellent! This place has a cool, hippy, vibe and look to it on the inside. I didn't stay to hear the band but I just may the next time one is playing. So with this being said....yes I'm returning :-)
Well if i wanted to put this kind of filth in the Sammy machine id go to Mellow Mushroom. This place is a godamned gluten bomb. Tight ass on 2 waitresses though. I'll be back.

We went here for a bite before a Predators game as it is so close, it was very busy to be expected. Food was very good just service was slow. I have heard great things about the wings but we went with pulled pork instead, which was great. Definitely a good BBQ joint just give yourself plenty of time before the game!
This place is great!! Country Music fabulous and the waitress very attentive. The pecan pie Wow. A fun place to be. We are at a Crimecon Convention. Free booze and food for tonight . Yes !

Came out here yesterday, I got the pulled pork sand which and my son got the rib wrap since they don't sell a 1/2 rack. Food was great, servers were very attentive, live music and a local beer selection.
Enjoyed our first trip to this place. Had lunch and the food and service was very good. Very large portions, one BBQ plate was enough for me and my husband.  Loved the sweet and spicy BBQ sauce!
We had pulled pork plates and they were great. I would have liked more than two choices for sauces, but the staff and vibe more than made up for it.

Stopped in for lunch on a rainy Tuesday and the bar area was pleasantly crowded. Good live music and a very attentive bartender. Had the pulled pork sandwich & curly fries. The food came out extremely fast and was delicious - exactly what I was hoping for. I definitely recommend for a quick delicious barbecue lunch!

Fun atmosphere.  Live music on a Friday afternoon doing mostly covers.  Nice to sit on the open air second floor and enjoy a beer and love music. Service slow- hard to get refill on beer. Didn't have any food but looked like mediocre bar food. A fun first afternoon in Nashville!

My favorite place to go to if I just want to feel better about myself and my life.  Cream of Crawfish, red beans and rice, hot tamales, and slap yo mama bread pudding is all it takes to make me feel awesome all over again. The staff are so friendly and cheerful. I love the ambience of this place

John H. provided excellent customer service for a party of 11! He was helpful and accommodating. He met everyone's request with a smile! The food was delicious! My whole team had an excellent dining experience and will definitely be back! Thank you John H.!

Terrible service, we were asked multiple times to move and ended up at a high top even though they claim you can sit where you like. Drinks went empty multiple times. The Pulled pork looked and tasted like it was just scooped out of a can. The onion rings were fantastic though and as usual the music was top notch
Amazing smoked half chicken and sauces are sweet and spicy with a nice touch of tang! Good prices and plenty of beer.
The food is ok. This is not where you come for a great meal. The show is the thing. It varies nightly and its hit or miss. They have a great dance floor,rare in Nashville, and can have a fun crowd.

Fun atmosphere, good band, people seemed to enjoy the food.  I left after a drink.  I had to ask for a drink and menu and my change after I was asked for $5 for my beer.  No offer of a tab or my order.  Disappointing.
Food is horrible. Burger was soaked in dales! Smells bad and table top was about to fall off. Over priced and poor quality. Stop at mcdonalds you will be glad you did.

This was hands-down the worst customer service I have received. The wait staff was extremely rude and slow. They did not come to take a drink order for more than 30 minutes. We did not have the opportunity to order food for 60 minutes. And this was a Tuesday night.  When trying to get the attention of a different server we were blown off. We asked to speak with the manager regarding our poor experience, who obliged and was helpful. The band and atmosphere were fun. The food was good. Maybe go somewhere else if you want better service.
The BBQ was good. We stopped by before a concert at Bridgestone Arena.  The service was fast to meet the limited time that we had.  We did love the live music and drinks.

Wish I had gone somewhere else instead.   My table was dirty and still had bits of spilled food from the last customers.   I was served my food but was never given any silverware.   The people at the table next to me gave me one of theirs.   The meat was tough, dried out, burnt and fatty.  The coleslaw was bland and tasteless.  I should have checked reviews before deciding where to eat.

I didn't come here for the food, just the entertainment but this place was so fun! I really enjoyed it. The line dancing was fun. The entertainment was great and had a great singer. This place was super busy but you always had tons of room to move. I highly recommend this place.
Ribs melt in your mouth, don't even need to add sauce, music was great, service was good and would come back

The only prompt service I got was the bro bouncer and his metal detector. Way to make me feel welcome.

Beer selection was moderately overpriced, band was subpar.

Environment all suggests "here's a honky tonk run by people who don't know how to run a honky tonk."

Absolute disappointing mediocrity, masquerading as sobro authentic.

There's a bloody good reason the other bars on this block as elbow-to-elbow crowded, and this had ample open seating on a Saturday night.

Great place...very Nashville vibe!
8 seconds ride was awesome!!
Intro to fried pickles and moonshine went well!

My boyfriend and I had a nice visit. We were tired from a lot of walking and saw RIppy's on the corner. Was surprised by the self-service. I get it because it is busy. The food came quickly. The pulled chicken was okay and the pulled pork was good. The fries were good as well. Our favorite part was when the two guys got up on stage and sang. It created a fun moment. The waitress was on top of it about getting us refills. Thanks for the fun time Rippy's!

This was my first trip to Nashville and wanted to experience as much as possible.  I read that the Wildhorse Saloon was a must for line dancing.  There are three floors and the establishment had been recently renovated.  Only the first floor was open when I was there.

The following is why I did not give The Wildhorse Saloon a better rating:

There was a $6 cover charge.  I do not know why since every other establishment on Honkey Tonk Row had live music and no cover.  The band playing was good, but not noticeably better than any other band I heard the past week. 

We had to decide if we wanted dinner (to sit in a table on the floor) or drinks and appetizers (to sit at a table near or at the bar).  This causes confusion and no wait staff if at a table near the bar (we ended up eating).

The special drink I wanted came in a souvenir glass or boot.  I did not want either, but had no choice ($16).  I had to wait for them to press the watermelon to get the juice for my drink -- at least 15 minutes.  I changed my order to a beer, since my hamburger came to my table (which was delicious).  The bartender did make me a complimentary drink as a way of service recovery.

Pros:

The bathrooms are modern and clean.
The cheeseburger, fries and coleslaw are really delicious
The draft beer is cold

They have line dancing, but there was not a lot of activity while I was there.  There is a ton of competition for the Wildhorse.  They need to adopt a more customer friendly atmosphere.

Amazing Experience through and through. 
Friend of mine took her family there while they were in town visiting and they can't. stop. talking. about. it. 
Her uncle made sure to talk everyone he met that they went there and I'm so happy I was able to pass along the great reco! 
Definitely a great place to be with the locals on historic broadway. #RippysOrBust

One of our favorite bars, but they close at 1am! 

I believe we had the Sunset on 2nd drink in the souvenir glass ($16 / refills $11).  

The bands were great. We watched Broseph on Friday and Tom Yankton on Saturday. We paid a $6 cover charge on Friday and no cover on Saturday. 

We didn't realize they served food. 

Overall a great time!

I brought a group of 40 here for a private reception in the Riverview Room, and the experience was fantastic.  My group was comprised of folks from coast to coast and they all raved about the awesome "Nashville Vibe" this place put off. If you are looking for a great location, with great banquest staff (Carter is awesome and should be the first person you talk to about ideas for your event), then this is your place.

Not sure I would just come in for dinner or on my own, but for a group event, they were awesome.
Good ribs. Good music depending on the band. Band members can be a little pushy for tips. Wait staff fast and efficient.  Upstairs seems to be louder than downstairs. A fun atmosphere!

Great pizza. Live music. A good place to hang out. Casual and cool. Good beer on draught. Only been on week nights or Sunday night and never had to wait for a table and service is good.

Try the cream of crawfish soup. It's delicious and I get a cup every time I go!

The menu is diverse. They have some good specialty pizzas, and I always have trouble deciding what to order. You can build your own, or get it in calzone. They have at least four base sauces (red, alfredo, pesto, and garlic ranch) which is great. Crust is fairly thin and good as well.

We were in Nashville for  4 days and had the best service ever on Sunday, July 20th thanks to Jonathan on the upper floor!! He was working the whole floor and getting great comments from all the tables around us!!! We spent lots of money on drinks and food while listening to some great music all week but by far he was "stellar" in service!! Great to have him on your team!!

Meh.  Great location and we had great service but the pizza is just "meh."  I dug the cheap beer and wine list but nothing stood out to me after eating and leaving Soulshine, except the service.  Luckily we had a Scout Mob which gave us half off the food portion of our bill.

A dead ringer of an establishment located right on the strip of honky tonkys in downtown Nashville. Rippy's has live music everyday, sometimes with two floors of bands, a beer bible of a brew menu, dancing and good energy all around, and all bourbon and drinks one would expect in Nashville. Stop in here while making the rounds on the strip and you're in for a good time!

This southern BBQ did not disappoint! The place is pretty packed but what place isn't in downtown Nashville? There's an awesome live band to listen to while you enjoy your food. Not gonna lie - it's pretty loud and hard but the atmosphere is great! 

The ribs are a great choice to go with - top it off with their delicious BBQ sauce too! Very smokey too. 

It's also in the heart of downtown so all the other bars are right by it. 

Definitely a fun place to be and glad I stopped by!

A two toned cafe and bar, Rippy's is a double open mic bistro on the end of Broadway. If the constant music from both stages on opposite sides of the business doesn't' annoy you then the sub-par waiting will. What saves this place is the historical pictures and clippings on the walls, the talented acoustic and or 4-piece-band and the food: Possible the best cheeseburger I've ever had. The actual dining area is big, spacious and music inspired, but then again, what can you expect from a restaurant located on music street in music city.

I am rating this 5 stars because they have the best pulled pork I have ever had. It tastes exactly how it smells which is a smoky BBQ taste to it. Highly recommend if you are looking for pulled pork or brisket on Broadway. Also want to add that we went during the week at night and it had a weekend vibe to it with the live music and amount of people there. Can't imagine how it gets on the weekends but I would definitely check it out if passing it.

This was our first stop on our trip here. Maybe a little too tourist-y for me, but the food and drinks were really good anyway. Our server kind of freaked me out--he was obviously that professional type who is good at his job, but was overly phony. I love that they do line dancing--not that I participated, but it was fun to watch. We also got to see Craig Wayne Boyd perform, not that I'd heard of him before, but I'm definitely a fan now.

In town for a conference, read the reviews and stopped in. Love the atmosphere, live music. The drinks are very reasonable and the food is the delicious. The people really showed a Philly girl southern hospitality while enjoying watching my Eagles play. Definitely will be back .

Came here with family, so there was 6 of us and a baby. Got sat right away, but it took a while for our waiter to come take our drink orders. We ordered cheesy garlic bread, but it was nothing spectacular. It actually tasted a little funny when you bit into the end with the burnt cheese on it. Definitely not worth $8. We all ordered pizza. I got the 5 cheese. I could've probably gotten a better cheese pizza at the grocery store in the frozen pizza aisle. I also sat there for 20 minutes with my water glass empty.

All in all, the pizza wasn't good and the service was even worse. Skip this place and go anywhere else for pizza! Even Pizza Hut would be better.

Rippy's is a good spot for lunch on a weekend, especially if you want to check out the Broadway scene when it's not insane at night time. There were three live music areas between downstairs and upstairs. It was Sunday, so there were NFL games going on all the TV's which was great. It wasn't too loud, which was good for my parents, but still had the live music vibe. I got the pulled chicken sandwich and was pleasantly surprised. I don't like a lot of BBQ so that wasn't heavily sauced at all and I added the hot sauce that was on the table and it was really good. Recommend with the coleslaw.

Admittedly, I got carry-out because it's a bar and I'm not too fond of the smell of stale cigarette smoke.

The food is glorious. The burgers are wonderful and the sides are huge! You really can't go wrong, especially with the prices. The person who took my order over the phone was courteous and placed it with no difficulties.

I would love to eat here again.

You cant beat the Palace for a good night of music. Always a great band in the front room. You never know who will be in the back room. Special events, CD release, dance lessons. Great burgers and fried baloney and lots of other good food. Had one of my best steaks in Nashville there. Salad, steak cooked to perfection and baked potato for $21.95 (worth it)

What can I say about the Twin Kegs.... It's much more than just "two" kegs on tap. I used to be a regular at this spot about 5 years ago, and after relocating back to Nashville (albeit) a little rearranging of the setup; this place hasn't changed a bit. While  it is still what people would consider a dive bar, the same friendly faces are still there. It still has one of the best burgers in town, and cheap cold beer to boot. A little off the beaten path from your typical tourist spots, it still should not be overlooked as as a great hang out in NashVegas. Great Karaoke without a long wait, and $2.50 domestic pints.... What more could you ask for. So if you find yourself seeming lost (or not) near this little spot on Thompson Lane come on by your home away from home and say hey to Todd, Molly, Max, and the rest of the staff at the Kegs, they will definitely treat you like family.

Pros:
Great food
Cold beer
Cheap beer
Staff
Regulars
Friendly

Cons:
No liquor sales (this is only a con if you are not a beer drinker)

Rippy's is right, as in they rip you off. The bartender charged me $18 for a whiskey ginger. Wtf??? (Later they brought another beer bucket when no one asked for one)

Otherwise, the live music is good but the place is incredibly crowded.
Good pizza and great music but horribly slow service. Lots of kids at the bar on a Saturday night so just a different vibe.

While this isn't the worst BBQ I've ever had, it certainly wasn't the best either. I would highly recommend going elsewhere to eat if you're going downtown. One member in my group stated the burger was the worst they'd ever had. I personally thought the BBQ sauces were delicious. My salad + pulled pork was fine, too. The platter had a nice variety of items, although I thought the cheese sticks was a bit unnecessary (I can buy that at the store!). I was also not a huge fan of my drink, but it wasn't terrible. I would go here for some live music and move along.

In the shadow of the Bridgestone Arena, we went to Rippy's a couple of times during our Nashville vacation. The atmosphere was what I was looking for in my ideal "Nashville experience". 

Our first time to Broadway, we stopped at Rippy's for lunch because the music drew us in from the street. We sat in the upstairs outside. There were 3 guitar player/singers on stage and they were really good musicians taking requests, playing country covers and interacting well with the crowd.

I had the pulled pork sandwich with a beer, which was very good. I would say it was above average. 

I did think that the service was a bit snotty. Almost as if we weren't welcome. I later found out that this sort of behavior is normal at Rippy's.

We did go back at night, just for drinks and music. This time we sat downstairs in the back and stayed for an hour enjoying the band before moving on for our bar hopping adventure.

Great atmosphere, great entertainment....would be better with less attitude.

Really good food, great atmosphere. The serving system was odd in the restaurant... had someone serve us drinks, but when we tried to order an appetizer at the same time, were told that she doesn't serve food. I could see that in the bar area, but not in the restaurant. Again, just odd. Reducing a star due to errors in the order.

It is very rare that I leave a place and make it a point to tell people never to go back, but that's how I felt leaving Rippy's last night. The waiter was incredibly rude and very condescending to our group. Once we were able to actually order-he kept walking away telling us we weren't ready every time we tried to start ordering-the food came out pretty quickly. I got a BBQ sandwich and it wasn't anything to write home about. Prices aren't bad, but everyone thought that the food was just okay. The music is this place's only redeeming quality. There are too many other restaurants around here to waste your money coming here and eating average food with horrendous service.

So we are Las Vegas locals, and we usually go to Stoney's and whatnot down there to line dance and two-step. We've come to this saloon 3/4 nights and we love it! This is the only place on Broadway with a big dance floor where you can really let loose or sit down and relax. Great performers and nice staff.

It's been years since I've been to an event at TPAC,  but my husband and I went two weeks ago and it was a great experience.  We saw Michael Carbonaro at the James K.  Polk theater and found the venue very clean and comfortable.  The staff was pleasant and helpful in pointing us in the right direction, as there were several performances that Sunday evening and the crowds were correspondingly large and hectic. 

The seats in the theater are very comfortable and spaced so I didn't feel like I was sitting on top of anyone, and we had great views of the stage, with an appropriate sized screen also displaying the show.  

We opted not to utilize the valet parking at $20 (pre-tip) but in retrospect, wish we had.  We found a small lot just a few blocks away but paid $26 for three hours to make sure we were covered for whole show.  Next time, we'll pay for the valet and have the same cost, but curbside service.

Should have went across street to Jacks. Took forever. Small portions for the price. BBQ pork wrap was good. Baked beans had a nice kick to them. BBQ ribs wrap was tasty but small. Mac and cheese was bland and cold--couldn't eat it! Drinks are SO expensive (tourist trap). Music was good, but so loud we stopped trying to even talk to each other across table.  Don't think I'd go back.

My boyfriend and I came here recently when vacationing in Nashville from New Jersey. In general I had just an OKAY experience here. Definitely a tourist trap but worth going to at least once. 

The decor is pretty awsome! Tons of different funny horses are spread throughout the entire place. Great for taking tons of funny pictures. 

I wanted to order the Comfortly Jack to drink and wanted it without the souiveniere glass. However, to my dissappntment the waitress told me I cold not purchase just the drink without getting the glass as well, refills are less money if you do decide to get it. I caved because I really wanted the drink itself. It cost me $13.75 for it. Grantit the glass was nice but I didn't want it and the "signature drink" was to very good. There is a problem when the drink is huge and you barley have a buzz by the time it's done. 
My boyfriend just ordered a beer and that too was its a purchase of a souiveniere glass. I get the whole up selling customer thing but to make a costumer get one of those glasses is just stupid if they don't want it. 

We split two different things, one was the sampler. It came with quesadillas, chicken fingers, fried green tomatoes and fried pickles. My bf hates is allergic to pickles and told the waitress so she added extra chicken fingers with o extra price that was very nice of her. The green tomatoes were soooooooo good! Absolutely loved ! And the chicken fingers were prob the best chicken fingers I have ever had! The quesadilla was just okayyy. 

We then decided to split the Tennessee BBQ duo . The waitress tried to change our mind and up sell us to the priciest item on their menu the "Stampede Platter" ($23.00)  after we already made up our mind and kept asking if we were sure. Yes lady we are sure! Especially due to the fact that both menu items were the exact same thing but the Platter was slightly bigger. The Duo (17.00)  came with hickory smoked pork chops and shaved beef brisket. Baked beans co slaw and Texas toast. The baked beans were amazing but the rest of the meal was pretty bland. They had containers of BBQ on the table to add to the meal. I must say while being in Tennesee I had better dinners during my stay here. 

After dinner we decided to go upstairs and check out the pool tales and air hockey tales. The pool tales were very cheap and not good if your a pool player. The hockey tables were also cheap but fun. Both were free which was great and they had a lot of them. 

Overall my experience here was just okay like I said. Go there for the appetizers and beer and to take cool pictures.

DO NOT come here while conferences or other events are going on in the area. After a day at a conference at the Gaylord Opryland hotel across the street, we decided to stop here for dinner. Our group of 7 waited for over half an hour to get offered water and to get our menus. We waited another 20 minutes or so to order. The live entertainment was great, but the extremely poor service could not be excused. We were barely checked on and were not given updates about our order. After another 40 minutes or so, three of the seven dishes came out. Two of the orders were wrong and one of the entrees were cold. We waited for the remaining four meals because many other nearby eateries were already closed at this time. We noticed tables who ordered after us getting their meals first. We asked the waitress where the remaining four meals were and she said the kitchen didn't even start on them yet!!! It was unreal. Two hours later and most of us left starving and extremely pissed off. Poor service. Poor quality food. Save your time and money and dine somewhere else.

Excellent food! Came in twice, in the same day. Laura Marie kicks butt! The daytime bartender Megan, was also amazing! Great atmosphere, music, and this place has it going on! Don't miss out on the opportunity for the full experience. A special thanks to the owner, for making this happen. Y'all made my trip! Rock on, from the Harley-Davidson family.

Our concierge recommended this place when I inquired about good ribs.  I took his advice and headed down the hill from our hotel.  I enjoyed the music and the atmosphere, but the ribs were pretty lame.  No distinct flavor and rubbery.  I wouldn't go here to eat.

This place has a great atmosphere. The pizza is great! The nachos aren't like nacho chips, they are pita chips, so they are a little chewy, but still good. 
My friend had the calzone with crawfish. He said there weren't enough crawfish, but it was still good. 
Overall, it was good. I'll go back!

It's A  " Honky-tonk "  so unlike other people I'm going to rate it in the classification it falls into and what you expect to find in one! Two small stages with singer-songwriters, musicians & wannabes playing country music! The usual beer selection with a few local hand crafts! Very noisy loud! Most of the time I would give this kind of place 4 stars but I give this one 5! They smoke all their own pork and ribs on site! And it comes out hot and fresh with homemade coleslaw a little Bland but still  -A- for effort! Staff was very busy and running around like most do in a place like this you weren't willing to catch their attention to tell them you needed something more... well the truth is this is a honky-tonk!
What a great time! This was a private party that I attended. The bands were fantastic! The food was OK and the  service was excellent.  A Fun place even for those who do not dance.

I visited WildHorse while recently visiting Nashville and I was very pleasantly surprised. It has 3 floors, live music, line dancing and I had the BEST customer service while dining there. 
My two friends and I visited on a Monday night which I was expecting to be dead to my surprise there was live music and a pretty big crowd of happy people line dancing to cover songs. 
We decided to have dinner there and we all ordered the ribs which were EXCELLENT. We also had the bbq nachos which were very good different but very good nontheless. 
Meanwhile, the live band stopped playing and a lady announced on stage that she would be giving a quick line dance class for everyone so my friends and I decided to join. 
It was free and SUPER fun. She made everything very easy to understand and I had a great time.
Now I've saved the best for last, the highlight of my visit by far was our waitress by the name of Sydney. She was AWESOME. She was very very friendly yet still very fast and attentive. She took the time to give us reccommendations of where to visit and what to do while in Nashville she even wrote her recommendations down for us. By the time dinner was over we wanted to take her out with us she was SO sweet and delivered THE BEST hospitality experience of my whole Nashville trip.
Terrible customer service. Line dancing super fun especially with the woman who goes over how to do it.

So excited that spring is around the corner! I love their upstairs patio on sunny afternoons with a group of friends, pitchers of beer, and a few different pizzas. It's the perfect afternoon setup! Get the Wild Bill and you will not be disappointed!
It goes without saying the music was great. Slower tempo than the other bands down the strip. We ordered the ribs and came out great. Save your cash and avoid the mix drinks. Water down for my taste.

Loved the band... guy/girl singers! The drinks were not skimpy either!
By far our fav on Broadway.
Deep fried pickles super good!

So I'm in a group of 14 people coming into (a very empty) Rippy's at 4pm and we wanted drinks and a little bite to eat. We sat around a bar area and they asked us to move because ONE table for two people wouldn't be able to accommodate guests. Reminder: it was empty. When we said - no thanks, we like it here- they stopped serving us. Oh wait- they barely took our orders. Then they had half of the staff surround us and basically intimidate us out of there. THEN for the two people who got an order in before they wanted us out - they wanted to be paid for their beers... that they never delivered. I'm sober enough to write this coherent review so clearly we are not a group of drunks. For a town that has a bar every two feet, I'm shocked they would turn away what would have probably amounted to several hundred dollars of business. Happily sitting at Nudies!

If you like really loud ambiance then you will like this place, due to the incredible business they do, it is a bit messy/dirty with many over flowing waste bins too close in proximity to the tables of dining patrons overloaded with old food , plates and refuse, so that when the bus boys dump the garbage in them it sometimes spaltters around the can, plus you're forced to look at and smell old food. The waitress we had was friendly and nice but the ribs and pulled pork were not what we thought it would be. The first time they came out cold, after waiting until we could find her because she was so busy, our waitress brought a new batch back that was hot and she was very accomodating,  but there are better places to have Bar-B-Que in Nashville and the surrounding area. Maybe if it wasn't so busy we would have had a different experience. We will have to try it when it is not so super busy.If it were not for the over loaded waste bins so close to the dining tables and the fact that our food was served cold on the first attempt I would have given a better star rating.
Food was cold when it got to me. Didnt get utensils until 5 minutes after got our food and it plain just didnt tasts that good. Poor service AND food...

The only nice person encountered was one of the hostesses. Every other person that worked there was clearly unhappy and did not want to be there. Way to make an uncomfortable dining experience. The food was ok. The servers, bartenders, and other employees could put a smile on their face and at least pretend like they want to be at work.

I had the pulled pork sandwich, its was good but not the most amazing that I've had here in Nashville. The curly fries were really good .
My friend had the ribs and I tried some of hers. They were literally falling off the bone. They had a good smokey flavor to them but the bbq sauces werent my favorite. Its a pretty good place to hand out and the bands they had that night were actually good.

I would give this dump zero stars if I could. The food and service was a total waste of my time. The food was horrible, cold and delivered at a snails pace. The loaded nachos, were a pile of stale chips covered in wilted lettuce and warm sour cream. The fries were soggy and a mess, the wings were a 3 out of 10, but would have been higher if they weren't ice cold. The side salad looks like they took crap from the hamburger mixins bar and threw it is a paper dish.

McDonalds would have been a major upgrade to this mess of a restaurant
This was a very fun honky tonk vibes venue that is  more updates than the others in the area.   The food here was incredible.   We had the wings, popcorn and ribs and I highly recommend them all.
It's a tourist trap and we fell in.  The ribs were barely edible with sauce. The music was great, beer selection was ok, just don't eat anything and you'll be safe.

What we enjoyed most about this place was the free entertainment and outdoor patio. It was a fun place to go for drinks and music. We are lunch there and then realized that evening there was free entertainment. The lunch was good but the service wasn't very prompt. That carried in to the evening when we had to ask a waiter three times for service and he kept saying he would be back to get our order. My husband finally went up to the bar on his own to grab drinks. We were there in August for vacation so my review is a tad outdated. But I wanted to commend them on their entertainment.

We just happened to go in to the palace to see whether they had any live music going on at the time. And of course they did. So we had a beer and enjoyed two different singers. Good music is old-style country which was real good. In the evening I understand they have bands. They have continuous music all day and night and generally no cover charge. Prices on the drinks were very reasonable and we left tips in the jar for the singers. No biggie. They have a simple food menu which is also very reasonable. We didn't eat but we may go back and grab something at another time.  The servers and all the patrons were very friendly. You can tell this is a local place that locals love to come to and support their singer friends. Also the place was non-smoking! Very happy about that. And on Wednesday nights in the back room they have a swing dance party where they have country swing music and that is a five dollar cover charge.

A solid 3 seems about right...although I really really love the live music.

Location is wonderful...right across from the Bridgestone arena and basically at the start of your stroll down Broadway.  If you are staying at one of the local hotels it is a perfect place to stop in..grab a few beers and listen to a set or two.

Like other Yelpers have pointed out the food is forgettable.  I got the rack of ribs and it wasn't bad.  It did the trick...I wanted some BBQ and listen to some cool live music.  If I want serious BBQ I would have headed down to Martins, but for this trip Rippy's was just fine.

Go in here knowing what to expect.  You are going to hear some great live music...have a pretty solid selection of beers served by real bartenders.  However, the food is going to be like most other places on Broadway...it will fill the belly, but be forgettable....

Came here on a business trip and found SPF. It was a great find. Pizza, calzone, spaghetti dinner and salads were all about what you would expect. So, no complaints. The upstairs stage had some of the best blues music (and music in general) that we heard while we were in Nashville. 20 minute riffs while eating my calzone and drinking a Coke. The coolest part of it all was listening to the lead guitarist for the Allman Brothers play with his son. That's my kind of night. Check their website, as they have different music on each night. We came back on a Tuesday night to find quality bluegrass being played. Fire on the mountain! We'll be back next time we come into Nashville.
Really enjoyed the pullpork. Nachos were okay. Bartender was not only friendly but was very efficient with juggling the crowd. Always a good romr

Big dance floor, line dancing lessons, live music, good drinks, and a good time overall. There is a reasonable cover charge and a bathroom attendant who is sweet as pie so take some dollars with you to the potty.

Huge location! Nice, lit up bar! Huge dance flor area, lots of seating around. Huge stage for live music. We came here when it wasn't too crowded! They were even doing line dancing lessons every 30 minutes which was really fun! Very different than in the Bay Area! So many people join in and have fun! Bar had decent priced drinks.

This place was totally dead on a saturday- weird. The first time we walked up they asked for a cover charge- i was like nahhhh then he was like ok ok no covercharge, which was SUPER fishy. Regardless we had a BLAST. the band that was here was BA like AWESOME and i loved the fact it was line dancing- which oddly I had a hard time finding in nashville? Overall great time!

Drinks are expensive but the atmosphere can't be beat! The talent that they have is truly impressive! Also all the staff is super friendly and acclimating but getting a vodka double drink for $16 seemed a little excessive! Travel off Broadway for much more local feel & better deals!

Great live music on the roof- just had a few drinks. Great people watching. Lol love music was awesome expect I wish they wouldn't have kept letting the drunk girl on stage- just got a little trashy. Other than that it was great!

Had a fantastic time there!  Listened to a gentleman, Larry Williams, great country singer.  We actually went there twice just to hear him sing.  They have yummy fried pickles and mushrooms!  The waitresses are super friendly!

First of all, you would think Nashville is known for ribs .....the ribs here are a joke. Only good for hang out, drinks, bar food, no more or less. Don't get the ribs, they should be ashamed to serve it.

Touristy place on the corner of Broadway across from the Bridgestone arena so with concerts and sports events I'm sure they are always busy. Has 2 floors very loud there is a  live band playing on each floor . food is expensive for what you get and just ok-- seriously its bar food folks , I've had better BBQ at small out of the way places .. I rate this place Been there done that

The barbecue here was really good and comes out very quickly (we had pulled pork, chili, and smoked chicken, all were great. mozzarella sticks were cold). Our server was really friendly and offered great suggestions. The atmosphere is fun too with great live music.

The issue with this place is that the tables are first come first serve, so if you have a bigger group there is no way you're getting a table unless you wait a long time (so do not go there starving like we did! big mistake). We had the 6 people in our party scouring both floors for about an hour before we were able to sit down. We couldn't put our name in for a reservation and sit at a bar waiting to be called and enjoying our time which we had done at other restaurants, so that was a little frustrating. I don't know if the good food is worth the hassle of your whole party working to get a table.

Service was 8 of 10
Food was 6 of 10 (had tomato basil and bob Marley pizzas.)
Portions versus price was not very good. The atmosphere is the saving grace. Good place to drink if you want to spin the money.

We love this place! We usually get the burgers and onion rings. However, chicken wings are awful. Oh, and there's no liquor. Yet, there is a full size shuffle board and decent beer prices. The thing I love most, NO country music.

We went there on a Thursday night because we love country dancing. Let me say this. I you love couples dancing like we do then this is NOT the place for you. We were the only ones dancing. There were NO dance lessons like the website says just someone on the floor for people to try and follow. There is NO dance floor educate,we saw people with drinks on the floor. The "line dancers"did not leave any room for couples. 
 The first band was good but the second one put people to sleep.
 The night we went there were private parties going on so no food was served.
The drinks were on the high side also.

So if you can dance you will be upset specially since it is the only place that has dancing.

We did try to go on Sunday to see if it was just an off night but it was closed.

Their pizza is to die for!!!  The cheese is melted to perfection and the crust is just the right thickness.  Service is always great and the servers are very attentive and friendly.  2 for 1 Mimosas and Bloody Mary's on Sunday.  One of the few places in Nashville that actually plays the sound during games.  We come here almost every Sunday to watch football.  My favorite pizza place in Nashville for sure!!!

Stopped in this small bar last night to get some food to go. I've driven by this place about a bajillion times and never really thought about it until I heard they have fried pickles. A few weeks ago I made the mistake of my life by introducing my wife to fried pickles. I am now charged with finding all decent examples of this dish. Anyway, when I walked in it wasn't crowded (at 6pm on a Saturday). A few neighborhood folks in watching the ball games and b.s.-ing. I ordered my food (2 orders of pickles, a tk burger and a bbb burger) at the bar and got a Yeungling while I waited. After the first one the bar tender asked if I wanted another. I asked him how much time I had before the food was done and informed me that the bbb burger takes 20 minutes to make. After talking with the barkeep (and ordering another beer) I found out that everything is made to order (chicken tenders/catfish breaded, burgers patted at order etc). At that point the expectations were raised. I was not disappointed. The burgers were awesome and the pickles will keep us coming back. The total bill for the food and 2 beers was less than $30. Not bad, TK, not bad at all. You'll see me back.

I really loved this place.  Three floors of dining tables, bars, pool tables, with a huge dance floor in the middle. 

Bands play live for an hour or so, with an intermission where they teach line dancing while the band takes a break. 

The food was like TGIFridays...Nashville Style.  BBQ and Fried Pickles were yummm. 

Very touristy, but I loved it.  Would go back multiple times. 

PS look at their event schedule.  While we were there, they were closed more nights than not for a special convention event for Snap On Tools, the filming of the show Nashville, and a concert with paid seating.   We had to coordinate the night so we could go on a night we could get in on a general night.

I too was lead to Soulshine by Scoutmob's 50% off deal, and my overall opinion was "(shrug), meh" ... 

Our server was great, I was excited to see they had three Fat Bottom brewery selections, and the building itself was pretty cool.  I feel Soulshine's laid back "jam band" vibe is a nice addition to mid-town's stale Vandy bro AND music row pushers scene.  All that being said, the food was pretty unsatisfying.  My girlfriend and I split a bowl of crawfish bisque, small pulled pig nachos, and got two small 8" pizzas (the Bourdeaux and the hamburger pie).  Crawfish bisque tasted like canned cream of mushroom soup with four scant crawfish tails thrown in as a garnish, the nachos were greasy, gooey cheesieness with BBQ sauce and a bit of pork, but were completely uninspiring, and the pizza was the biggest let down.  My girlfriend was excited about the wheat dough option, which along with the MULTIPLE BBQ pie options, I thought were both an insult to the pizza gods.  While I admire their creative effort in adding jerk chicken to a pie and calling it the "Bob Marley", one does not just simply "dazed and confusedly" throw random ingredients on a pie and create a new menu item.  

I will go again, but not to eat.  It will be to escape the douchebaggery of midtown, grab a Fat Bottom Rye Pale Ale and watch some live music.

If you want good pizza, go to Bella Nashville in the farmers market.  Chicken little know pizza.
Average burgers, and cheap beer. Fine if you are looking for that. I had hoped for more based on reviews, but the burgers seemed like frozen patties cooked up.

For atmosphere for informal music and food venue this place can't be beat. I was surprised to find it on the tourist-Hell strip in Nashville. Great service. And the food was better than expected. I hope to come back to see more artists performing on the big stage. The food is not cheap. The fried baloney sammich was as expected. (Next time I'll ask for whole wheat bread.) The fried pickles were great. The spicy ones ARE spicy. Burgers are just fine. Kale salad was also very good. No idea whether it's worth taking dance lessons, but I will seriously consider it with my GF the next time I'm in town and have time.

We went on a Monday night with the hope of taking advantage of the line dancing lessons, which we'd never had before. The instructors just danced a bit, and then led a few dances when they were hounded by some people wanting to learn. They led complicated dances, weren't interested in simplifying or asking what sort of dance we'd like to do, and then left 5 minutes before they were meant to finish. Overall pretty disappointing, and I wouldn't recommend it. If you want a fun bar, go somewhere else. If you want line dancing lessons, it's probably best to go and take actual lessons rather than pay $6 cover for this

This theater is amazing. I've been here for two Broadway shows. Even being in the nosebleed seats, you get a decent view of the show. Will be back for another show for sure.

Some downsides are the restrooms are a bit small. At least the one on the top section only had two toilets. Also the way the seats are set up, you have to walk a long row of seats if your seat is in the middle of the row. Can be a bit difficult to maneuver around people to get in/out.

We came here late one night just for a few drinks. We didnt eat at all. We sat on the roof top terrace and listened to the live band. This little experience gives them 4 stars. That terrace is really nice. Its a good place to relax, people watch and listen to music.

I was in Nashville for a convention and walked down to this place and enjoyed the music and atmosphere. 

My wife had a pulled pork sandwich and I had a pulled pork plate. The beans were great and the BBQ sauce was great also

Apparently if someone is stealing your beer and you confront the thief, the bouncers will throw you out if the thieves tell their side of the story first.

While at the upstairs bar on Saturday a few members of a bachelorette party decided to start staling beers out of our beer buckets.  When finally catching one in the act, and confronted by a flippant attitude about the crime, harsh words were exchanged as I don't think thieves deserve any respect.  The thieves went and told a bouncer about someone using abusive language, without mentioning it was because they were thieves, one bouncers tells me I have to go.  Another bouncer was close by and listened to the part about the thievery and told me I could stay.  The bouncer that would not listen to my side of the story and kept harassing our entire group until I wouldn't take it anymore then he threw me out for disrespecting him.  If you want to go to an establishment that defends the thieves from the victims this is your place.

Awesome food, try the Spice burger and fried pickle chips yum with cheap beer too!
Great dive bar

$3 Bloody Mary's on Sunday and GF pizza crust, what's not to love!?
Great outdoor patio to soak in the sun.
Only negative I have is their service was a little slow.

Well, that was a little disappointing. The space is very nice. Unfortunately,  the food and service leave plenty to be desired.  Service was pretty slow. My $9.00 martini, when it finally came, arrived in highball glass. The food was fine-not great or in any way memorable, but fine. I'm really just left with no reason to visit again.

Huge stage & seating area for concerts. Nice little store attached with souvenirs that has very reasonable prices. Only stopped in for an appetizer, which was great, but would come back again. Later at night a line starts to form so there may be a wait. Wouldve been nice to have a larger selection of craft beer. You have to try Line Dancing lessons before you leave!

Pretty cute spot.  A little on the "commercial" side, but they offer line dancing lessons!   What's not to love about that?

Our server, Genesis recommended the fried chicken.  It was perfect!   My friend and I split the pickle chips.  Perfectly seasoned and I could have had it for my meal.  Mac and cheese was creamy and the coleslaw was peppery.  Nothing wrong with it, I just prefer sweet coleslaw.  

There were two private events going on and a dance company was on the dance floor dancing with one of the groups.  It was kind of nice seeing men dance!   So many times, you just see women form a circle and two step because none of the guys are dancing.  

I would definitely come back.  The place was clean and the service was great.   Bathrooms were immaculate.

Soulshine Pizza is a great place to catch live music, have a quality beer, and eat some of the best pizza in Nashville!

Soulshine sponsored my softball league through Nashville Sports Leagues.  My team lost in the championship game, but got a $50 gift card to use.  After getting stiffed on league fees by a couple of players, I had no qualms about taking the my wife to dinner with them.  Ha...

We arrived and drove around the parking lot a couple of times to find a spot.  This is the only negative experience of the night.  The parking is tight.  They do valet, but I think it's $5 to go that route.

When we walked up, the band was going and we were seated downstairs.  The band was upstairs.  That wasn't a bad way to go as we could still hear them and the tv monitors showed them if you wanted to watch.  We could also talk without yelling at each other. 

We both ordered the crawfish soup and it was excellent--very creamy, but not too spicy.  My wife and I then split a medium pizza.  Half was the 5-cheese and half was the Don Vito.  They are cool about doing that if the base sauce is the same.  The Don Vito is fantastic and I'd highly recommend it.  The pizza and crust are really well done--definitely one of the best pies in Nashville.

The beer list wasn't great, but they get high marks for including local brewers.  Yazoo, Blackstone, Fat Bottom, and Jackalope were all on the beer menu.  I tried the Jackalope Red Rompo for the first time last night.  It was very good.  I'd like to see a few more craft selections, but it's still very cool that they provide such a wide variety of local stuff.

Soulshine Pizza is excellent.  The pizza is great and the restaurant provides and awesome environment to enjoy yourself.

So, this review isn't so much about TPAC, but Green Day's American Idiot.  To make a long story short, GO SEE IT!!

To the delight of the people sitting on either side of me (highly sarcastically speaking), I was singing along with most of the songs, by most of the songs, I mean those that were played on the radio.  There were a few songs, specifically written for the musical, of course, that I didn't recognize.  But, the minute the play starts, you are drawn into it.  It made 90 minutes go by very fast!!

Although tonight was the last night in Nashville, the next time it comes here or you get a chance to see it elsewhere, go!  You won't regret it!
Mediocre BBQ but atmosphere was really great.  Loved upstairs and really great cover band.  Exactly what you would expect from a place named Rippy's on Broadway.

We stopped in awhile back and was kinda late but had one of the best chicken Quesadillas I had ever had. That late at night the place was kinda crazy and has a very eclectic crowd there was plenty of entertainment there! Lol
Came here while in Nashville for a conference. The pizza was delicious. Our waitress was awesome. We would high recommend this for anyone.

This place looks small from the outside, but is really big on the inside. 

There is not a bad seat in the house. The first floor has low tables in the front, hightop tables in the back, bar seating and a second floor so everyone has a view of the stage. 

There are three bars all conveniently located. The bathrooms are not obvious. I am not sure how the staff and service is as I was there for a very early professional development session.

Saturday, August I 2nd, I worked all day and decided I want to have dinner at an Awesome restaurant and have some great pizza..so I decided on Soulshine....I have never had my daughter here before and I wanted her to have some great food and check out a great building...I love how they remodeled this restaurant..it is an old warehouse style building that has been remodeled and revamped...

I LOVE THE BUILDING..
I LOVE THE DECOR....
I LOVE THIS RESTAURANT...

We got there about 7ish..and we were able to park in their lot. I love the fact that they have a private parking lot in an area near Vandy where it is hard to park anywhere...lol!!!

The place was SO NOISY..but hey its Saturday night and you are in a college area..so YES expect the noise..if you don't want noise...stay home !!!! ((( lol))))
Our waitress I believe was Anita, I really couldn't hear her name very well. I opted to sit upstairs where it seemed to be a little more noiser by the way, but I love that staircase ...so you want to climb them...

We sat ourselves at a high top table for four...We were greeted immediately and gave our drink order..Tony took a PBR, Noel iced tea and myself..Coca Cola...tall and cold please !!!! and keep them coming..!!!

Noel decided on the 8 inch small Shrimp Alfredo and Tony and I opted to share a medium "The Jacksonian" which is a chicken with Alfredo sauce ...so soo sooo good. I had to try Noel's choice also...it was good as well but I am not a sun dried tomato fan...and that ingredient was on hers...

We had a wonderful dinner. Their was sports on all the tvs..the band never played while we were there...I loved this dining experience..we had a nice dinner..

Disappointment! I've been here dozens of times and hosted many group events here. That was before all of the changes. The new building renovation looks like a New York bar with the horse figures remaining a sad reminder of fun times.  I could have forgiven that if the food was still great. The BBQ beef and chicken thighs were dry and tasteless. Service was terrible, seats too close together. Wish I didn't know how great it used to be.

Should be called Ripoffs! We live in Nashville and happen to be going to a show at Bridgestone Arena. On the way we decided to have a few cocktails and walked into Rippy's. I looked over the menu and first noticed the Bushwhacker (my favorite), I ordered one and was told that the machine was not working. I then asked for a White Russian and again informed that they had no milk, bummer. I took a relook at the menu and ordered the Spray Tan, this drink consists of Tito's Vodka and some other delicious items. As I'm watching the bartender make my drink I noticed that she was pouring Skol Vodka, which is lower grade and from the well. When I asked if the drink was supposed to be made with Tito's she replied "you have to request that"....to that I responded...."but it's on the menu, you mean that even though it says it comes with Tito's on the menu you have to request it???"......she replied "yep". Whatever, I asked for the tab and received a bill for $25.00.....this consisted of two shots (which we did order) and one drink (that wasn't even made as the menu said)......that's pretty steep. I didn't fight it......we paid and left. But I am writing this today because I feel that if they did this to me, they must do it to others. Get an itemized bill and watch what you order!
Fun place to spend the evening! Decent food and drinks and good music! Three levels, so plenty of room to spread out. They've got line dance lessons for people who don't know how to do country.

We came here for our first honky-tonk experience with the kids. Because we stayed at a Marriott hotel we were able to get in for free on a Thursday night. ($6/ adult cover). 

Large dance floor with lots of seats and bar areas surrounding. 2 stories of views. Large stage. Live music and line dancing lessons. 

We didn't have any food so we can't comment on that.
Pulled pork plate was awesome! The sauces they have at the table are delicious. Live music was pretty good. Food prices seemed very reasonable.

Live music is pretty good for having a bite.  Lots of ladies singing out loud with the country music guys on stage.  Pretty fun place. 3 bars with live performances on all 3. Pulled pork was really good... good portions.. Took a bit to et noticed but overall a great experience

The pizza is nothing to write home about. Fairly bland with a forgettable sauce that needs seasoning. Crust is blah, and got soggy quickly. Aside from the personal pizza we also got a sandwich. The bread was stale and the meat cold (it was a hot sandwich - or it was billed as such). It seemed like a "glorified" version of something you'd get in a gas station.

Beer selection was OK, thought they certainly push cheap beer. As a venue this place is OK. The service is friendly, if not a bit slow and rather clueless as to the menu.

Overall I don't think I'd come again, unless the music (that really blares out of the place) was to my liking. Then it would be beer and tunes, and I'd skip the food.

Got in late on a Monday, starving! Not a good idea to head to Rippy's. The place is huge and you seat yourself. Server was very attentive and saw us fairly quick. He warned us that the kitchen was backed up. Ordered chips and dip which took way longer than it should have for dip that was probably microwaved in the styrofoam cup it came in. Cold and not very good at all. Ordered the pulled pork which was mediocre. Sauce was excellent though. Onion rings were a bit soggy. I would only go back for drinks and the live band. Unfortunately the food was not worth the wait.

My boyfriend and I had dinner here when we stopped in Nashville for an evening. They have live entertainment which was so fun! The server was very nice and attentive. The food was delicious and even though it was busy we got our food within 10 minutes of ordering! Highly recommend!

TOURIST TRAP!

Went expecting something else.

You know its a TT when they ask you if you want your whiskey and coke in a souvenir glass.

You come to Rippy's not for the food or music but the upstairs open air patio.  These guys have some of the best views of Broadway Street.  Here you can cool off under the fans and people watch.  

The food is your typical bar food.  Nothing special though not terrible.  They normally have very loud, very average cover bands playing on the patio.  It's nice to hear some okay music and sip some ice cold Hap and Harry's beer in bottles.

Giddee Up! This country bar was rocking on a Friday night when we busted during the 2014 CMA Festival. The energy was fun and upbeat.
