There was a country cover band playing on stage, which kept the crowd dancing and singing during our meal.

The bar's service was attentive and we didn't have to wait long to place our food and drink orders.

The BBQ was above average, not the best; but still much better than some other bar establishments.

I don't know how this place only has a 3 star rating- Great atmosphere- live music without being obnoxiously loud, fantastic service- our bartender was so helpful and patient with us while allowing us to substitute different things, I felt like a pain in the butt, but it was SO worth it!  Boyfriend and I got the sampler with the ribs, pork loin, pulled pork,sausage (with cheese?), macaroni and cheese and "corn cakes" Their pulled pork was amazing! Absolutely fabulous with their sweet bbq sauce! Mac and cheese was delicious and the corn cakes were really good, although a strange concept- corn bread that's like a pancake...?  Tasty, but would've been better as actual cornbread, pancake thickness just felt like something was missing.  I have no idea why they served blocks of cheese to go with the sausage, it didn't really make sense to me.  The ribs were a bit dry for my liking, but I like them dripping with sauce so I think that was just a personal preference. 
We really enjoyed this place and will definitely be going back on our next visit. Hopefully we get the same bartender because she was awesome!
We just came in for drinks and appetizers while we wait for our concert to start the evening. Great good and nice atmosphere.

Let's just start by agreeing that all of the horses (particularly the ones that are upside down on the ceiling) can be a bit much.  Mostly in a good, fun way, but the ones by the bathrooms are a little weird.  Moving on...

My first experience at Wildhorse was for a concert (Sister Hazel, it was of course fantastic, but that's beside the point).  We had reserved seats, which were not significantly more expensive than GA and very much appreciated.  That night, we didn't eat at Wildhorse, but we did drink.  My only complaint was that you can't get the specialty drinks except for in the "specialty (souvenir) glasses" which makes them way more expensive.  But they're so good.  And to be honest, while I though they were particularly ridiculous at the time, the glasses are actually mason jars and I use them around the kitchen all the time. 

Now, as we're planning our wedding, we've been looking at Wildhorse as the venue for one event that weekend and they've been great to work with so far.  The events staff is responsive and very professional. Today we had a tasting there, and we were all very happy with the quality of the food (and the quantity.  OMG the quantity).

Do check their schedule before you go - while most nights do not, some events require tickets.  I look forward to going back for the line dancing!

Rippy's is as casual of a dining experience as you can get. However, the food tastes good and the service is excellent. My favorite server Melody is as good as they come-ask for her by name.
The live music both upstairs and down is always good. If you're ever in Nashville, make sure to stop by and enjoy.

Awesome! Each time we stopped in (on Friday, on Saturday and on Sunday) this past weekend it felt like home. The CMA Fest was going on so there were an extra 80,000 people running around town, but each day we came in with our group of 6 we were greeted with huge smiles and shout outs from Joni, Liz, Smalls and everyone working the 2nd floor bar. Ice cold beer, great food and awesome people...who wouldn't want to hang out here? See you'll next time for sure!
It's OK. I went mostly because I had my young son and this was rated "good for kids". The food did not blow me away, however it was a nice atmosphere.

Tony and I went here for lunch today...another Sunday in Nashville...and yes another Pizza Joint...I am on a pizza kick right now...So we opted to try Soulshine Pizza Factory and we were glad we did..

It is located down near Vandy...closer to Vandy than Broadway...but easy to find...gets plenty of food traffic from the University students..It is a two story location. We were greeted and seated immediately on the first floor. Our waiter arrived quickly. Tony ordered a Budweiser Bottle and I ordered a soda...
We looked through the menu..I already knew I wanted pizza..so we ordered "the Kitchen Sink" small and appetizer of Garlic bread and marinara sauce..it arrived very quickly.
Our waiter was very friendly and told us before we leave to go up and check out the upstairs and the outdoor upper level patio where they are sitting up a live band..
We walked up there after we ate...
OMG...I loved it up here...so light bright and airy...definitely going to eat upstairs next time.
I loved the interior..the service and the food..

Everything including tip, taxes food and drink...$24
Not bad..I tipped him 18% for a sunday afternoon party of 2 at noon!!!
Not bad!!!
I will go there again!!!
DEFINITELY!!!

Check your bank statements. I went there last night with party of 7 which were 3 separate checks. He brought them in bifold book so there couldn't have been any confusion. He charged my meal and also charged the other on my account as well as charging them. Whether he voided it or did by accident never mentioned hey I accidentally ran other check but I voided it out. Also you can't just call up to speak to a manager to resolve this. Everything is automated and you can't speak to a live person. Aside from that service sucked took 20 minutes to get drinks everybody's food came out and ours was another 10 mins having ordered the same time due to waiters error. Also phone service inside is terrible but they do have wifi catch is you have to check-in as being there to get access. Go to BB Kings instead better music food price and service.

Food was AMAZING. The pulled pork was so good especially with the sweet BBQ sauce. It melted in my mouth! The service however was AWFUL. The guy was rushing around so much he forgot his customer service skills at home (especially friendliness). The way he asked our table if we were ready to order was "ready? Lets go." I felt like I was inconveniencing him. I always tip 20% but he got what he earned.

3 adults 1 child 50.00 which isn't bad for the location and live music. Burgers are huge. My son loved his chicken wrap. My only negative is that they charge over 2.00 for ice tea and serve it in small plastic cups.  We were thirsty and our poor waitress had to work hard to keep our drinks full.  We will go back.

My mediocre rating is probably more due to my expectations than the venue. I was here on business many years ago. At that time is was very rustic looking with old wooden beams and a "barn dance" kind of atmosphere. Now that my wife and I are visiting the area I couldn't wait to take her back to see what I loved on that visit. Sadly, it isn't here anymore. My wife summed it up best when she said her impression of the decor was "cafeteria". We had a beer ($7) and left. We didn't order any food, so we can't comment on that. The band playing was not great, and wasn't playing any country tunes. Seems like Wildhorse isn't the place to go anymore for country music or a country feel.

I came with a friend for the dive bar experience.  I see hipsters talk about the place which was weird but it was just older southern men there.  We played some shuffleboard while drinking some beer.  We were asked to let others play before our first game was even over.  I don't get the appeal.

Visited even after reading a few not so great reviews. I have to say I was pleasantly surprised. Liked the atmosphere and had a very friendly and responsive server. Ordered the Crawfish Bread for an app. Yummy!  Got two eight inch pizzas to share. The Mediterranean and the Wild Bill. Hubby liked the spicy one best but I liked the shrimp one best. I think this place is a great addition to the neighborhood.

TPAC brings great shows to Nashville and a great variety. I appreciate how much dance they offer. I really enjoyed both American Idiot and Catch Me If You Can. Parking is easy right across the street and coat check is reasonable. 

The seats are comfortable and the acoustics are good. I love the ability to select your own seat when purchasing online, it makes all the difference for me and can mean the difference between a lackluster experience and a great one.
Martins food is much better. Ok if u are looking for something on broadway but not the best for BBQ

I LOVED THIS PLACE! Live music on every single floor, everyone seemed to be having a great time, the service was friendly, the food came out fast, and the prices were CHEAP! Ordered the pulled pork sandwich with mac n cheese, and potato salad. Quite possibly the BEST DAMN POTOTO SALAD I've ever had IN MY LIFE! Man it was so good!!!! The musicians were all incredible too. What a treat it was. The whole area was rocking. First time visit to Nashville, wish I would've had more time!

For somewhere that you think you're getting bar food we were quite surprised. We split the BBQ sampler which was more than plenty for 2.  The ribs were good but the sausage was quite special! Would eat here again!

Place is crowded and the service is terrible. I tried to order a beer 4 times and the server was gone before I would get a chance to tell her what I wanted. The food is a joke, their pulled pork was dry, coleslaw was dry, and their baked beans tastes like Busch's baked beans... I wouldn't recommend this place.

My second trip to Wildhorse was just as fun as I remembered. It is my favorite music venue in the downtown area for several reasons. One, it has the largest dance floor and the dance instructor, Chance, makes sure you have fun.  Even if you don't dance, it is fun to watch. Second, the food is much better than typical bar food. I am a fried pickle addict and they have some of the best. The platter combo with choice of meats and sides is enough to share. Three, the bands are quality.  We saw David Oakleaf and band. Four, the place is clean. Really clean.  The bathroom attendant was cleaning every time I went in and she was so friendly. Five, No  Smoke!  I could actually breathe while I ate. 

If you go before 6, there is no cover charge. But don't complain about a cover.  many bars pass the tip jar every hour so you end up paying far more than the Wildhorse cover.

It's a great place to meet a friend, good trivia night, pretty good pizza, but the thing that stands out to me is the customer service. 

I had left my credit card at a nearby bar the night before and casually mentioned it to the bartender John. Without missing a beat, he called the nearby bar, walked over, and personally picked it up. 

I was really touched by this and will be coming back for sure. Also hope the owner Chris reads this because John js the kind of guy I'd want to manage my restaurant.
Very nice venue to see a show. If I lived in Nashville (or even close by) I would be spending a lot more time there watching shows!
Great drink selection. The pizza is quite delicious, but the other few dishes I've had were meh. Overall a great happy hour place for friends!
Beers and burgers. Nice location and away from the "trendy" tourist traps that plague this city. They even have a nice pinball machine! Might make it a favorite place to unwind.

We were excited to try out our neighborhood dive bar, and I liked it, but I don't think it'll become a regular spot for us! 

The good? Classic dive bar. Shuffle board. Couple of small TVs - but not a full on sports bar with TVs everywhere! They were playing great music while we were there. Great drink specials during Happy Hour ($7/8 pitchers of PBR). They have karaoke and trivia (depending on the night). Beers on tap and canned/bottled. (I had a pint of Bombshell Blonde, and my fiance had a Black Abbey draft beer.) They also have food (we didn't try any on our visit visit)!

The not so good? SMOKY. Just learned that you can still smoke inside bars in Nashville (just moved here from Texas). I'm pretty headache-prone when stuck in a smoky room, so this is the main reason that Twin Kegs isn't going to be our normal spot. Too bad! 

A cool spot - but we probably won't be regulars!

I thought the food was great!  I tried the cheeseburger pizza on wheat and had a bite (okay two) of my friend's Bob Marley (on wheat).  Yummo!!  We also had to crawfish cheese bread and it was great, too.  The only drawback is the parking situation but that really can't be helped.
Great food, prices, and live music. The smoked pulled pork sandwich is to die for. The service left something to be desired though.
Great place to hear live music, good food and very friendly service. Bartender (lady) in side bar was beyond amazing.  Really on top of things and friendly.

Talk about a country-filled night! Came here on a Friday night and danced my cowboy boots off learning how to line-dance. The energy was palpable, the range of skill-set was noticeable, and the music was blaring. It was just a really fun experience honestly! 

They also have an arcade/game area upstairs. This part was pretty empty when I went, but the bottom floor was packed with people who had ordered food and drinks. I didn't get a chance to try their food, so I can only speak about the general entertainment atmosphere, which I found to be promising.

Went to the wild horse tonight for the 80's dance party to end Alz and was incredibly disappointed by the lack of response or interest of the serving staff in our section of the 2nd floor.  We ended up going to the bar to order our first round of drinks and food. When I asked one server if she had our table she said no but she would get our server. Never saw her.. then when she did get close enough to me, I tapped her on her shoulder. She spun around and very rudely told me not to touch her.. seriously??? I was trying to get her attention so we could get some service... her name was Mercedes. Stay clear of her if you visit there.  Her unprofessionalism definitely put a damper on the evening. Our previous visit the day before was pleasant, the place is very clean.

The music -- by Nathan Belt and the Buckles  -- was really great, very versatile and talented musicians. They played a nice mix of traditional country, rock and roll oldies, and very little contemporary.  I liked how they chose songs to spotlight the various band members  (guitarist,  pianist,  drummer) I was REALLY surprised to hear they play only for tips. Wow, the competition must be stiffer in Nashville,  because they could have had a paying gig elsewhere I'm sure. There's not much of a dance floor, but a few couples made do with space available. 

We'd checked out the menu beforehand so knew what to expect (mostly bar food with a couple home cookin' dishes). The Longhorn salad was surprisingly good (who orders salad at a honky-tonk bar, right?) -- steak done perfectly  and a nice variety of fresh greens.  Dixie chicken portion was huge.  Onion rings were ok, a little cold.
Now as to the service ... it was a Saturday night, but it was easy to find a table in the restaurant where the band was playing.  Our server, Brittany, greeted us right away,  but it was 5 minutes  before she was able to take our drink order. She was friendly and professional, though,  came back right away and took our food order. About 20 minutes later, she came over to explain that there was an event in the theater area, and the kitchen was swamped with orders, but she would check on the order. About 10 minutes later, she came back and said the kitchen was still swamped but she would talk to the manager about how long the food was taking (40 minutes by then).  We asked for some pretzels or nuts (it was 8:30 and one of us hadn't eaten since lunch), and she brought us some chips and said she was personally going to track down the order. About 5 minutes later, the manager (Tara?) came over with an order of chicken tenders and said that somehow, in the big stack of orders, the kitchen had lost ours. She apologized and said the food was being prepared now. She comped the tenders, the chips, and another beer. Brittany came back to refill drinks and apologized again.  The food came shortly thereafter. 
So here's the thing  -- mistakes happen,  orders get lost, especially when its really busy. But when the server and manager explain what happened,  apologize,  and try to make it right, what more can you expect? They took the time to talk to us personally,  it was clear they cared. So kudos to them for that. And hey. we had great music to entertain us while we waited.  I'd  recommend this place,  but maybe suggest timing your visit for a less hectic time.
Alway have a great time coming here. Tonight's show Kinky Boots has been awesome so far can't wait for act two.
Wonderful food for the price!  The ribs were so good, they really didn't require a sauce, and the pulled pork was so tender.  The side room of the joint could be better cooled down in the hot months.

Had a decent time here. Really it was our only choice since we had my 18 year old cousin with us and it was the only place that allowed under 21 since they are a restaurant. 

There was a decent band playing and we ordered some drinks. The food looked okayish and none of us where too hungry so we decided to opt out. We got one appetizer of beans with some tortillas that was pretty good. I ordered a mixed drink and it tasted like a bunch of juice and no alcohol. Overall all we had a decent time.

Tons of specialty pizzas here. We got the Godfather, which was really good. They also offer wheat crust, which was pretty tasty. 

I came here because they are offering a deal on Scoutmob for 50% off of your check. Pizzas are priced similarly to MAFIAoZa's and Mellow Mushroom, so specialty pizzas can be a bit steep. 

Glad I stopped by. Great atmosphere and would be really fun to come to with a group of friends.

If you miss Old Country Music, this is the place for you!!! The fried bologna sandwich took me back to my child hood, and with a Conway Twitty song playing like in the background it was a great time warp that I hated to step back through when it was time to leave!!! 2country4Nashville is the bomb!!! A great duo!!!
Good food and line dance lessons.  Yes touristy, but clean and brighter than most of the other venues in the music row area.

Stopped in Saturday before heading downtown. Watched Dave Cox then Ellen Rose and the Silver Threads - awesome. Nice bar with the back area being higher giving a good view of the stage. Quality of music is the best and bartender (Sara) took good care of us. Highly recommend.

Good for a quick bite. I split a pulled pork sandwich and onion rings with a friend. They were good and just enough food before the evening festivities. My friends got ribs. They were dry but again way better than I expected for bar food. And there were a lot of ribs to share!

Music was fantastic and entertaining. I wish it didn't take over 2 hours and our waitress continually telling us our food will be right out.  Needless to say we never did get to eat here since after 2 hours we had to cancel our order in order to make it to the Grand Ole Opry before the show started.  I would not try eating here unless you are only coming for the music.  Our beer came out quick and was cold.  If it wasn't for the music, I would have rated it a 1 star.

Went in while band was setting up.  Bought beer from bartender, who was pretty high on herself.  Found a small table and waiter with curly hair and pony tail asked us to make order.  We told him we just bought from bar.  He asked us if we were ordering food.  We told him we weren't sure.  He rudely told us the table was his to serve people making orders.  We left.

Took a group here to experience some "Nashville" scenery...the cover charge of $6 is totally ridiculous. We waited at the bar on the right side of the stage and it took for ever to get a drink from the pissed of bar tender behind the bar, and drinks are very expensive here. The band was great though and the women's bathroom was fabulous! I've never been to a bar that busy and had such a clean restroom.

This is a must stop if you're in Nashville.  The service is very good; food is average.  My "world famous" fried pickles were pasty; portion was generous.  The brisket sandwich with the sweet BBQ sauce was was nice and tender.  There is also an option of a mustard BBQ sauce if you prefer.  Sandwich is served with unremarkable chips ... This is an opportunity for improvement.

Don't be dissuaded if there is a line.  Tables are turned pretty quickly.

Love this place! One of our first stops every time
We come to Nashville! Great food and even better live country music!!!

Freaking love this place. Massive club with a lounge feel which doesn't make sense but if you go and sit at a table at one of their bars with some friends, you'll find yourself at some point looking up into a horse head and over to the big ass dance floor and you'll say to yourself "oh yeah! I'm in a massive dance club!". Great staff and drink selection too. Go get lost in this place next time you're in Nashville!

Great, funky place with good food!  Open air seating is always a huge plus!!

They have decent pizza, but I think more people come for the live music and funky atmosphere.  It gets quite a crowd but if you are willing to go up to the top level or down you can usually find a spot.  A funky fun evening out.

There are certain places in Downtown Nashville which are a must for visiting. The show Nashville helped places like the Bluebird (not in downtown) gain notoriety. Places like Tootsies and Nudies are classic and live off their reputations. The Wildhorse Saloon is the "real deal". Set up like a mini Ryman, there's plenty of room for dining, dancing, parties, etc. There's a second floor in addition to the main area. My colleagues and I only came for the music and drinks. Doug McCormick was the entertainment and was excellent. The large stage with multimedia effects makes this more of an entertainment venue than a restaurant or bar. The staff was very friendly and the place was exceptionally clean.

The venue is great and food was delicious but 2 stars because the bartender cheated out on my first drink, and spilled the second while pouring but only because I was watching this time, corrected herself. 

Then upon my arrival home from my trip, I checked my bank account and I SUPER don't appreciate the bartender changing the tip I left. 
It was already 24% of my bill (even after the drink mishap) but I guess that wasn't enough for the 45 minutes we were there. 
Not cool at all. A bar is nothing without a good bartender.

Went in, was approached immediately by a spritely bar tender with blonde hair.
Ordered the burger and wings, enjoyed both! 
"...cheapest beer prices in Nashville"
True.
Lots of variety too! 

I will be back.

I'd recommend checking this place out whether you're a tourist or a resident. My favorite thing about Wildhorse is that they give guided instructions on how to line dance in between the sets of the live bands. They also play pop music too so there's something everyone, or at least anyone that likes to go out dancing, can enjoy if you're going with a large group.

The last time I was here was in the middle of the week. I'd say this is kid friendly because there were a lot of what I assume were high schoolers on the dance floor. One cute couple dressed in cowboy hats and boots was dancing along with their baby!
This place is uncomfortably packed! 2 stars for the patio and one star for the very nice bartender. I would recommend this place as a tourist trap only :-/

This place could really use some remodeling, but that's the only bad thing I have to say about it... The bartender was a delight , and the food was delicious! I got the BB Burger... Very very delicious and flavorful. Will be back for another Burger when I'm in the area. The fries were also delicious!

Stopped here while sight seeing...and stayed four hours! The bands were amazing and kept us quite entertained. 

Ordered the super sampler BBQ platter and two of us couldn't finish it! It came with a tin bucket filled with enough condiments for any taste. The ribs were smoky and meaty, the sausages fantastic, spicy good taste on the wings, but beware -- those peperoncini's have quite a kick! The pork loin was good, but pales in flavour next to the other meat selections. The cheese chunks and onion rings rounded out a great (in no way healthy!) feast. 

We were well taken care of by our bartender who custom made Tootsie's moonshine shooters for us -charred cinnamon and apple pie. Awesome. Also had the local brewery Yazoo Hefeweizen which was tasty. 

If you are worried about heading out after all that, the bar has a "blow before you go" breathalizer at the door. What more could you ask for?

Checked out Twin Kegs last week for the first time after kickball and it was awesome!  It's a very small place but the beer was cold and the food was good.  I had the Big Bad Burger (BBB) and it was exactly as the name states, Big and Bad (Bad meaning good though).  It was a cool bar atmosphere which made it kind of hard to talk at times, but it was all around a good time.  I'm definitely gonna go back!

Went to this bar last night, and the bartender was awesome!  I unfortunately did not catch her name (it was super packed and very busy) but she was outstanding.  Fast, made good drinks, and was very cool.  After visiting other places, she was hands down, one of the most friendly, and the best at her job.  Music was good.  We ordered a bunch of food here, and while it wasn't life-changing, it was good.  Overall, a very good experience here.  Would come here again.

Visited with a group of friends during the day on Saturday. Live music was cool and had plenty of table space. Service wasn't very friendly and bartenders were a little hard to track down, but it was a cool environment with a group of friends. They have an upstairs area which was cool and watched little kids dance to the live music. Beer is a little pricier since you're on Broadway so maybe a weekend place for live music, but not a frequent place for me.
Great service. Love the atmosphere. Is very clean and good drinks. Didn't try the food because we had already eaten but the "Nashville Hot" Fried Pickles sound amazing. Plan to try these!

I've seen a couple shows here now (finally, right?!). Queen was KILLER amazing and Sister Act was also really fun. I've sat both up front (almost) and in the high high balcony (almost back row...but hey it was $10!). 

I appreciate that you can purchase cocktails for the show, and the cookies are really tasty that they offer there! 

Next season I plan to join my friends in getting season tickets! They get them for around $10 a ticket when you buy a package, and even way up top, that's a fun way to spend a girl's night!

Wanted to note: Valet here is no bueno. We paid $18 and stood waiting 45 minutes to get our car. Ugh. It's better to pay for a garage and hike it over.
Just bad food great service horrible chicken horrible pork was almost like eating soup

BBQ Brisket was okay, not the beat i've tasted.  Just meat with sauce.  Fried pickles were great!  Sliced covered with batter.  Crispy anf hot.  I'm not a bug fan of country music so i was getting sleepy while we were listening to the band that was playing that evening.  Typical bar food is served.  Fast service!

Pulled chicken was amazing as was the Mac n cheese (I totally love ma Mac n cheese)..atmosphere great with country band in background and windows open blowing in a warm breeze...service was great and staff was extremely friendly in that southern way... great time overall would only request some more local beers on tap

Excellent beer and they are in special. Start with the tamales I strongly recommend them. We also shared a pepperoni pizza and it was great and filling. Trent Daniels was the best server. Thank you so much

(This review is about a year old. Thought it posted...guess not)

This place was recommended by my cousin and friend who lived in Nashville for  a year. Very glad we went here. The entertainment was great and the food was good. Best fries pickles we've ever had!! The buffalo chicken dip was good but not the best (mines better). Everyone loved their meals!! Hush puppies were amazing! Now remember, I'm from CT so for me this BBQ and southern food was great. But for someone from the area may not think its as good since they get it all the time.
With this being said - if you're going to Nashville as a tourist - go here!!! They even give free glassware :)

My overall reaction to this place is "meh" - the service was okay, the food was okay, the ambience was okay. Nothing was really special about it. I'm a little confused about who they're catering to. For a pizza place, they seemed remarkably non kid-friendly - which is fine, but I wish I'd known in advance. The whole wheat crust was a nice option, but didn't taste very good. The waiter seemed befuddled that we just wanted a cheese pizza (really? that's unusual?). Their menu was actually kind of confusing - so many options that it was a bit overwhelming. 

Pros:
*Lots of options?
*Nice patio (if it's not totally full, like it was the day we were there)

Cons:
*Food wasn't that good
*Front staff seemed actually unhappy to have a kid there
*So many options that it was hard to sort out what to order (but not in a good way)
*Huge TVs in every corner so you can't get away from whatever sports are on
*Seemed unclear on what customer base they were going after
*Their valet lot is so small that it was "full" on the day we were there for lunch

Kid-friendly scale:
*Wouldn't come back again with our 3yo. They seemed not interested in kids at all. That's totally fine - but if you're a pizza place, kind of weird. 

Vegetarian-friendly scale:
*Eh, it's a pizza place, so yes.

Got kicked out because an under-educated bouncer decided that he thought I was a "jerk" and was "slurring my words." I recorded the entire episode. I was severely embarrassed in front of the party I was entertaining, all because some bouncer had an ego-trip on me. I will NEVER go back!

My wife and I went there the last Saturday in February. We did not want to get mixed up in the crowds on Broadway and this was close to our hotel. The services was very good we were promptly seated and our drink order taken. They had a fairly big bar with only 4 beer taps. Their food standard bar food, burgers, wings etc. The beer and food was reasonably priced, surprising really for a tourist spot. The band was ok at best. The patrons were on the older side and the band played older country for this crowd. Several people got up and 2-stepped and certain songs they clogged. It was fun evening and I can recommend it unless you are in your 30's or less.

This is a very small location. Looks dirty on the outside but not too bad inside. I have not eaten here yet, but they say the burgers are good. My husband justed wanted to grab a beer and myself a soda..but we will try the food and I will give a review about it then.

So I went to Nashville for a bachelorette party and we must have stopped into Rippys everyday. This was our go to spot to grab lunch or a quick bite while out on the strip. Classic Mac and cheese, chili, nachos- everything had that southern home cooked vibe that kept bringing us back. I loved the Yeehaw drink, got it every time.

Beware!!! Had relative come to town. Was at Rippys and was assaulted by 2 bouncers! I would stay away.. there are seriously way to many good bars on Broadway. I have read similar reviews about Rippys. Management needs to address an obvious issue!

Good food, the tables are spaced out so not too crowded like some of the other bars nearby, and the live music is fantastic. They have rotating local artists and they're really talented. Enjoyed this place a lot. And TVs to watch the games. Best of everything. Saw Brianna Alomar sing. She killed it.

Bartenders are the worst. Couldn't give a crap about anything or anyone. Give me a tip and get out of my face, is the attitude.
Think they are hot...LOL! 
They don't know what bar tending is. Shot and beer hookers.
What a waste of money. There are plenty of places where the bartenders are friendly.
Keep moving!
Waited an hour and a half after being told a half hour. People were rude. Manager said he would take off one of the meals and then didn't. It's a great location but no customer service.

Good pulled pork, not great. Really good sweet tea. Service was interesting. Our waiter was quick but we had to flag him down to get our order taken. But once we did our food came out to the table within 5 min. The music (not live) was TOO loud. I would have liked for them to turn it off so we could have soaked up the sounds coming from the street. Loved eating upstairs and overlooking Broadway!
At the table we had ribs, pulled chicken, and pulled pork- ribs are dry smoked but very good. Music was good, ambience reminds me of a college town bar.... Hit the spot before our concert.

We went to Nashville Palace last night for dinner. There were 8 of us so we were unable to sit inside. We decided to sit on front porch where we could see and hear the band. The food and music were both very good. The band played for over two hours without stopping. What we didn't know was that they were having a Burlesque Festival in part of the building. It was quite a parade into the building. Not appropriate for the children sitting on the patio eating dinner with their parents.

I would give four start to the entertainment and the place but I came here to eat and I was hoping for some good BBQ but instead the meat was dry and blend. I am from California and I had better brisket there than at the Wildhorse.....

Don't waste your time. Worst dive in Nashville. Worst on the inside than the outside and that's saying a lot. Busted up my front bumper coming into the gravel parking lot. Waited 30 minutes for an average burger.

First, ask for Blake. You're welcome. He's an awesome waiter!! 2nd, order the Blue Ridge Collins if you're drinking. 100 proof made with moonshine and the best tasting drink I've ever had. A little pricey but worth it. But be careful, it doesn't taste like alcohol and is dangerous!!

The food is excellent. I HATE pickles, but I found myself eating fried pickles one after another. Brisket sandwich is great, and the Mac 'n cheese is delicious.

We were trying to eat at the Tavern, but with a 2 hour wait, we quickly decided to go elsewhere.  We walked across the street to Soulshine.  I am not usually a fan of specialty pizza places, but I was hungry.

We were seated immediately, even though it was a little crowded.   The place has a modern feel to it, even though there were kids lurking about.  Our server was super friendly and responsive, even though she was super busy.

The menu had a lot of choices, and it was hard for me to make up my mind.  Which is saying a lot, since I am pretty picky on pizza toppings.  I ordered the half salad and the Don Vito.

The salad was pretty standard, but the homemade croutons really made it delicious.

The Don Vito is a pizza with alfredo sauce, other cheeses, italian sausage, and ground beef.  This pizza was nothing short of amazing.  

I would definitely go again.

Actually, do you think can ship the Don Vito to Atlanta?

Love this place !! Such a cool uniquely Nashville vibe - great food and better music EVERY night !! With a young son we don't get out much but when we do we head to Soulshine - we always take out of town guests there. You never know who will be in the audience !!

The worst country bar I have ever been to.  It is owned by the Gaylord so they don't care about having a crowd.  And during CMA fest they make you wait in line for hours and no one is inside.  It is dead an no good.  I have been to country bars all over the world and it is the worst.

I absolutely love to see shows at TPAC! But it is often challenging to distance the shows from the building/business so I will do my best.

Located directly downtown, TPAC offers several theater size options all the way from Broadway to intimate concerts and opera. Parking can sometimes be a nightmare but local spots like the Sheraton or sometimes street parking if you are super lucky can open up. They do have Valet. 

The theater itself is well maintained and they are prompt about sending tickets, selling tickets at the box office/picking up at will call, emailing you friendly reminders about upcoming shows and the like. The staff have always been pleasant and excited for show day! Seats are comfortable from the main floor all the way up to the balcony! Bathroom lines of course get super long so try to deal with that before sitting down! On your way to the restrooms there are pictures from past shows and it literally feels like you are walking down memory lane as you see old scenes from former loves. 

There are several bars and you can take beverages into the theater for the show. Just know, you will be paying premium theater pricing (i.e. bottle of water is $3.50).
Spicy [jalapeño] fried pickles were on point. The brisket and chopped pork were also delicious. Good atmosphere/ambiance.
Need some soul and good food! Great vibe great music sit outside and enjoy. Best place in Nashville

Amazing!!!!!  Staff is awesome.  Food is also Amazing. 

Crowd is respectful usually.  Great place.
Cool little joint with live music and really good bbq and drinks. Pulled pork sandwich was juicy and the smoke flavor came through nicely.

Lines out the door on the weekend so try to check this place out during the week if you are planning to go. I went on a Sunday night for dinner - $6 cover. The band wasn't great, but I wanted to see the country line dance lesson - it only lasted 15 minutes but was still cool to have done that in Nashville. The fried pickles were fantastic, but I wasn't impressed with my sweet tea pork entree. It was also incredibly loud and the lighting made it difficult to even see my food.

WORSE CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER! 
Myself and 3 others came to Rippy's on a Sunday evening. They were honestly not that busy. We headed upstairs and sat at the bar. Of the 3 bartenders there, no one acknowledged us. Again...they were not busy at all! So after about 10 minutes, we decided we would get a table. We stood at the entrance is the dining area wondering if we needed to be seated or we could seat ourselves and there wasn't a single person we could ask. One of my guy friends went to the bar to ask and while he was gone, I was able to finally grab someone who told us we could seat ourselves, but when my friend came back, he was told by the girl at the bar that we had to wait to be seated. We finally sat ourselves and it took about 5 minutes or so for our waitress to come to our table. She was sweet and attentive. She put in our drink order and came back to order our food and was apologetic that the drinks were taking so long to be made. As far as the food goes, we ordered ribs and brisket. The main entrees were really good, but the sides were just okay. So I'm giving one star for the waitress's attentiveness and another star for the good entrees, but other than that, I wouldn't come here again. The poor customer service will make you lose your appetite.

The menu looked good with several options. Those in my party who had pulled pork were happy with their meal. I had the bbq wrap which I thoroughly enjoyed. The pulled chicken was very dry, however, and had to be soaked with their bbq sauce to be edible. The ice berg salad was not ice berg at all (picky daughter). Extra dressing was requested and received, however, there was a fee (not a big issue if I had been informed). Had three to go boxes and had to ask for a bag. The waitress was not engaged or friendly at all. 
On the up side, the music was great - live band on each of their floors. And the local beer, Southern Wit, was enjoyable. 
Will not be returning ...

Food was ok. The price for the good was a little over priced. Everything on the menu was over $10. A plain hamburger with fries was $10.50. That was the cheapest item that wasn't on the kids menu. I had the burger and it wasn't that good for the price. I wouldn't recommend this place specially if your on a budget. The scenery was nice and the people who worked there were nice but, like I said just sitter pricey for my liking.

My wife loved thsi place.  It was the typical tourist Nashville bar with line dancing along with every song on saturday night.  They also had some line dancing lessons.  It was what we were looking for in Nashville.   
The drinks took FOREVER to get though.  and it wasnt even crowded on a saturday night.
Venue awesome! Band sucked balls. Still had fun! Good for dancing and watching old men creep on minors.

It's ok.  I've been here 4 times.  Twice upstairs with live music, at night, and twice during the day for lunch.  The night experiences were good.  The day- not so much.  The pizza is fine.  The beer is cold.  This last time, we spent $60 for four beers, two small pizzas and a nasty tamale appetizer.  Worth it?  Not to me.
Good drinks, great band,lots of dancing. Staff was very accomodating and definately put customers first. Love the renovations. Much more open and easy to move around in.

The ribs were pretty good. Part of dining out it service and it was just ok. The bartender looked bored and offered very little in reply when I asked questions. The beer was cool, not cold. Went to Jacks across the street and that was a way better experience.

Sandy was great today. She was very personable and prompt. She was honest about the menu and friendly as all heck to myself visiting my mother who recently moved here. I could see how this place could get hoppin but during the lunch hour- you could probably turn the speakers down a little bit. As much as we enjoyed the musician and her selections- it was hard to hear each other even on the patio. Recommend the quesadilla and Sandy.

This place by far was our favorite bar on Broadway, strictly due to the amazing bands we heard there each time. It's large inside and I believe there are three stories. We never made it upstairs because we loved the bands downstairs. Our servers were great and I recommend a drink called "yeehaw". I can't speak about the food because we didn't eat there although from the looks of the menu it's standard bar food, nothing fancy.

For the second time in a row ive had trouble purchasing tickets. It has taken over 30 mins both times. The tech dept needs to be over hauled!! The first time I called Leeroy was no help. Boo to the online and call in experience.

Came here on recommendation from a local (our bartender at Bakersfield which was way better). The pizza was as expected average nothing to write home about. Live music was good but just so crowded. Music (4) plus food (2) averages to a 3 star review. We sat at the bar and liked our bartender. One slight annoyance was a large group of people had 4 large tables pulled together and didn't use one of them, but when we asked to sit there they said they were saving it. 10mins later another couple say there with no issue. So be aware table hoarding occurs here and you might need to just sit and apologize afterwards!

Was looking for a place I could listen to some live music and enjoy some food and a drink. But did not want to go to a concert venue or any place I'd to pay a cover charge just to get in.

The Nashville Palace served me perfectly. Easy in, easy out. Attentive waitress, real good live country music and cold beer and some food.

The food is bar food, really basic stuff - so don't come here if you're looking for a wider range or/and attractive choices. But if you're happy with a burger and some fries along with your beer while listening to the band playing - they'll deliver exactly this.
Okay, the same quality type of burger MC Donalds  will give you for almost half the price, but hey - MCD won't service you at your table and of course will not have the live music.

I also liked the atmosphere in this place. The interior and the whole place just looked exactly right for the type of music played here.

Pizza here is good, but nothing so spectacular that it warrants putting up with the horrible parking situation around Division street. Prices are fair in the restaurant itself, but expect to pay at least $6.00 - $10.00 for parking if you're not lucky enough to find somewhere on the street nearby (which you probably won't). Save yourself the stress and hassle - there are many places in Nashville with good or better pizza and service and where parking is much cheaper and more available.

Great Food!
Expensive Drinks!!!
Great entertainment. 

First of all this place is mostly a bar with food served at bar or tables. They have 2 live bands playing at all times which is why the drinks are very pricey ($7 a beer). However you are getting free entertainment so figure that into the beer cost. 

I read reviews and the pulled pork was mentioned do I got that with a side of mac n cheese and it was awesome good!  I highly recommend it.  Food seamed to be average pricing too, not inflated like the beer. 

Service was also great. Our waitress was busting her ass and still treated us great.
Nice laid back venue. Live music, simple but good menu.  Large beer selection. Nice chance to relax after a long day traveling.

I liked this spot. My pizza and salad were good. Our waitress remained cool and attentive even though it was clear she either had a lot of tables and/or rough day. The outside area is pretty chill. Would go again.
I had the muffuletta and was disappointed. It was pre-packaged lunch meat with no flavor. The server was great and the vibe was very nice. Food however was less than so-so.

I LOVED this bar!! This was my last stop on my nightlife tour of Nashville, and I'm so glad we stopped in. There were 3 different live country bands playing in different sections of the bar that were all amazing. The drinks were reasonably priced, I had the Yazoo Heif because when in Nashville you should probably try a Nashville brew. One of the things I really loved about this bar was the diverse crowd of people here. There was the newly 21 crowd, couples of all ages, bros in their 50s, I could go on and on, but this place basically covered all demographics. And the best part was, everyone was having an amazing time! I would go here again in a heartbeat, and I kinda wish we had something like this in Boston.

My friend plays this cruel trick on us by ordering us a round of Bud Light Limes.

We were served quickly (these chicks open bottles lightning fast) and they were ice cold.

So... I guess... I can't really complain... ?

The best pulled pork sandwich ever.

I LOVE this place!  While it admittedly is a bit tourist-y, the food here is some of the best you can get in the area.  In particular... the pulled pork sandwich.  Top it with their spicy BBQ sauce and you are in pulled pork heaven.

They frequently have live musicians who (like most in Nashville) are truly talented.  The location as well cannot be beat, and is walking distance everything you would want access to!

Sam waited on us, really helped me find the beer to match my tastes.  Quick, knowledgeable and respectful EVERYTHING I want in a waiter at a restaurant I am trying for the first time.  Will go back, and THANK YOU!

I'll keep this short and sweet!  COOL SPOT!  Great choices of food/pizza, live music, inside and outdoor seating options, location is good, staff is friendly...that's pretty much what you want in a bar/restaurant IMO!
Great place with great food, drinks, and music but needs some serious cleaning of the bar.  We scraped some off easily but it's gross we eat here

The barbecue is pretty good. If you like barbecue and don't mind to wait for drinks this place is good. Came here for dinner with the family and managed to get a table upstairs after about 20 minutes of hovering. It's a seat yourself kind of place so you do have to wait for a table as it was pretty crowded. The service is just not that great. Yes I know they were busy and I know there's lots of things going on Nashville however at one point I had to go to the bar to get a drink because I had no idea where our waiter disappeared to.   I'm giving this two stars.  One for location, and the other for food. It might've been better if we just went to the bar for drinks and wasn't hungry enough to eat.
Great food and the ABSOLUTE BEST service in Nashville! Ask for BRANDON, he is the best ever!!!! They play awesome music and the food is amazing!

This place was exactly what we were looking for! We enjoyed both bands that played and the line dancing that was spontaneously happening during the whole first band and part of the second band. Many of the dances people were choosing were easy-only several moves repeated over and over-as someone that doesn't have a lot of line dance experience it was great-easy to catch on and everyone seemed friendly. The line dance lessons from the instructor were fun too. They had fair drink prices and we got souvenir mugs that you could get refills on. The place is huge-3 levels-not overly crowded though, and they have pool tables, shuffle board, and foosball on the upper levels. You can watch the band/dancing from the upper floors too. If you're looking for a fun place in the heart of downtown Nashville to do some country line dancing and hear some good music this place is highly recommended.

Great place to eat and enjoy BBQ! We ate here twice in two days and loved everything we ate, especially the ribs and the tasting platter. Service staff were friendly and attentive. Live music was very loud though so meant no eating conversation!!
Came here for a work party and concert. I was so impressed!! Way larger inside than I expected. Had the fried chicken, Mac n cheese, pulled pork... so yummy! Generous pour on the drinks too yeeehaw!
The lack of draft beer and the fact that they pour wine out of tiny little single service bottles was a bit of a surprise for a place like this right on Broadway in Nashville.  The music was good.
We were here celebrating a friends 40th bday. It was late at night and we'd all been drinking but the bbq still wasn't good :((. I gave this place a generous two stars just because the service was ok

Stopped in to grab a quick bite to start our night. The pork sandwich was great, but potato salad was very deli/carton-esque. Music was in some different locations and if you were relegated to sitting upstairs you couldn't hear/see the performers. Service was excellent, however. Good spot to grab a bite before continuing on for the evening.

Holy crap... This is a place with New York City prices but substandard food. Yes its a in fun and trendy midtown. 

My Pizza (Jacksonian) was ridiculously oversalted... It wasn't just me! My neighbor ordered Nachos and holy crap... also insanely oversalted. 

Yes the place feels trendy and the music is of the perfect volume - loud enough to be fun, yet quiet enough to chat... 

Oh and you better take an uber here because parking is INSANE!!! (as in 15 dollars for parking or you'll be parking illegally). 

Oh and... $5.50 for a blue moon-crazy...

Music was great upstairs and they have large TV for all sporting events. On the other hand, the pulled pork sandwich I had was a 5 out of 10. The bar girls were very nice and service was fast even with ncaa games on and full house. Would go back but not for the food.
A nice spot outside of the crowds of Broadway to catch some live music. Lots of space both indoor and out.

Always a great band and great bartenders. I have lived in Nashville for 6 years and don't often frequent bars near Opryland but if I catch a movie or do some shopping at Opry Mills I usually grab a drink here afterwards.
Cool place, fun environment. Food was just OK....drinks were very good but food lacked character and didn't have a fresh appeal. The service was also very slow...still had a good time here though.

We stayed nearby at JW Marriott and saw this place so decided to try it one of the nights we were in town. We liked it a lot!! HUGE tv, good food and service and a somewhat fun atmosphere. We had the loaded spoon fries thing, meatloaf and chicken friend chicken. Everything was really good. I'm not a southern food expert so don't know how it compares but we enjoyed it. The meatloaf was mushy - is that a southern thing? Good comfort food regardless. Our appy came out same time as meal so the Manager proactively offered to comp it we never said a word. Nice touch and good meal. There were times I server was hard to track down though.

Great music, family friendly,  good pulled pork and overall great place.

Band was great and honored all our requests except Taylor Swift which was understandable. 

Pulled pork was melt in your mouth good.

I've always ended up at Wildhorse with out of town guest and in the past 15 years always had a great time and great service.  So knowing my sister likes line dancing, Wildhorse was a must for her Bachelorette party.  I was suprised how much customer service has gone downhill.  Band was great and plenty of space on the dance floor, but the bar tenders were unbelievably rude.  
After waiting 10 minutes he helped one of the 6 of us standing there and went on to someone whom just stepped up to the bar.  One in our group rolled her eyes and he immediately told us that wasn't gonna get us served any faster.  Two of us went to one of the other bars there standing another 10 minutes patiently waiting and the bar tender left the bar went to our group and accused them of not paying him for 2 drinks.  I understand we were 1 of 4 or 5 other bachelorette parties there in black dresses so easily can be confused, but then he came back to the bar purposely ignoring the 2 of us keeping his back to us.  
As a former Gaylord Employee I can not believe how customer service has gone down so much.  We won't be back.
Had a blast here! I loved the line dancing and how they break up the live music sets with line dancing lessons. I will definitely be back!

My husband and I went here for a late night snack and while we were eating we saw a mouse come out of the walls. My husband pointed it out to our waitress and she said nothing. Then my husband went to the bathroom and saw another mouse traveling along the baseboard of the floor. Needless to say we left as quickly as we could. We at least expected some kind of accommodation from our waitress, Monica.
Absolutely the best ribs I've had here. Great smoke flavor and comedy just right.  BBQ beans were great as well.

Overall--This place is average. The atmosphere is fun and loved the music and music inspired art. Service was friendly.

We went on a Saturday afternoon to watch football with some food and beers. There are about 4-5 large TVs however wouldn't recommend this as a great place to watch a game. Beer list was decent however not up to date with what they had. Our nachos were average--the sandwiches average--and the pizza average. It was nice that you could customize a small 8'' pizza. 

Overall--average.

Well, first off, this place is huge! When we were there it seemed practically empty, even though there were plenty of people there. The food is good, not awesome. The drinks are wayyy too expensive for what you get, and especially compared to what other bars charge. Some of them come in souvenir glasses, which are cute, but you can't just refill that glass. So if you order more than one, you end up with a bunch of glasses you have to cart around for the rest of the night. And you have to pay another $13 each time you want another drink. They do give free line dancing lessons, which is fun! And when we were there, this local band called Brother Trouble was playing and they were great. We had a lot of fun, but mostly because of the band and each other's company...the bar itself isn't anything special.
Had a great time at a company event, live country, fried pickles, line dancing instruction, what more could you want?

The pizza is mediocre, the "fun and funky" atmosphere feels forced, and the service is meh.  I wanted to like Soulshine, and I wanted to give it another chance, but it's not even worth it with number of much better pizza places I. Nashville.

Great for groups and if you're afraid you're going to be terrible at line dancing, don't worry because there are a dozen other people who look just as ridiculous trying. Jokes aside, they've got really talented live singers who take you through all the steps and someone on the floor to lead they way!

This was our first meal in Nashville and it was nothing short of delicious!! Fried pickles? Pulled chicken? Pulled pork? burgers?All of the sides?  I would defiantly recommend this place to all of the Nashville tourists!!! Bucket of domestics was $6!! A couple floors of great music and great food!!

There are plenty of pizza joints in Nashville, but the newest is Soulshine Pizza Factory on Division Street. This place started down in Mississippi and you can tell what the influences are by looking on the menu .Since they have opened, I have dined in twice and had take-out once. Each time I have been there, it has not been busy. The food and service has always been good. The building is brick inside and out with smooth concrete flooring. The atmosphere is very nice upstairs and downstairs with a bar downstairs which sits under the stairs. The downstairs bar is not that big but it is cute and it works. A few tables are sprinkled in the middle of the floor while booths surround the area. There is also a big ceiling fan in the room which fits the décor. Upstairs is a larger bar, tables, a stage  and an unfinished roof patio that will be great when the summer gets here. The music is bluesy, and there is great colorful artwork on the walls including a picture of Redd Foxx aka Fred G Sanford.

Soulshine has weekday lunch specials, and the pizza at this place is really good. They have various types of pizza, and you can also create your own. The 28 pizzas to choose from have very gimmicky names like the Mississippian which has pulled and grilled chicken, pepper jack cheese and sun dried tomatoes. Sleeps with the fishes has Alfredo sauce, mozzarella, spinach, bell peppers, shrimp, crab meat, and goat cheese (does not sound appetizing to me). All pizza can be made into a calzone or you can have white or wheat dough. Appetizers range from wings to cream of crawfish soup, and hummus for you vegetarians. They have several Po-boy sandwiches such as the Mama Mia which I have had. It's a meatball sandwich with marina, mozzarella, and delicious bread (Very tasty). They also have a very delicious sounding muffaletta. My friends that I have dined with had the Greek salad which they both loved. The Greek had romaine lettuce, black olives, peppers, onions, and feta cheese. Entrees include red beans and rice, Nathan Hotdogs, and Spaghetti with meatballs. They have only a few desserts but that "slap yo momma bread puddin" is soooo magnificent the sauce is sweet with a taste of bourbon. An employee told me that it had apples in it but I did not taste the apples; however, I devoured it.

This is a wonderful place with ok staff and a lot of options. It is a great spot for groups and a late night weekend bite. We were informed that the people rent out the upstairs area for parties. They also have a psychedelic van that advertises catering. Mid-Town in Nashville is getting better with each additional restaurant. I recommend this pizza joint to anyone especially to the college "kids" (the po-boys are better than the pizza). The space next door is owned by some of the same people, and rumor is, they are going to open a sliders restaurant.

This is a medium to partly cloudy review. We came to see a friend's band (THE TRAILS!). Got there around 8pm and made our way upstairs to the heated covered patio. We've been to Mafiaosa's heated covered patio before and froze our balls off, so I came dressed to ski. Didn't need it - the temp was perfect. Go teach Mafiaoza's how to heat a patio, please.

Anyway, the downstairs looks very nice, and the atmosphere upstairs is very casual and laid back - so laid back that the upstairs is first come first served. Not a freakin fan of stalking people while they eat, along with 20 other stalkers. That was a 30 minute ordeal, along with semi-confrontations of the "Hey! I stalked this table before you stalked this table!" and "Are you REALLY using those two chairs?" variety. 

The pizza is average. Anyone who says anything like "this is the best pizza I ever had!" is either drunk, 18 years old, or friends of the owners. We also had hummus that was...pinker than expected, but tasted fine, and cheese/garlic bread that was good. Local beers on tap, prices above average for pizza joints but average for the Midtown area. 

There is valet thank goodness, but they charge $5 if you have the restaurant validate ($15 if you abuse them and go elsewhere). I'm not meaning to complain about this, just to let you know. 

To sum it up: Come for the atmosphere, the drinks and the music! Don't get too excited about the food though. Nothing overly creative or delicious going on here.

Eat, drink, and dance. I was there 2 nights and had a great time. Ordered pulled pork sandwich with slaw and fried pickled chips. Was very good. Live band performance was awesome. When band takes a break a mini line dance lesson is given. At 10pm guest under 21 are asked to leave. Will definitely return.

The service was not very good. But the food was pretty decent BBQ. The pulled pork sandwich was very good. The fries were plain (they needed seasoning). The beans and the potato salad were both very good. Friend had the BBQ sampler for an appetizer and it was very good. The hot links were great.

this place looks small from the outside but it is the perfect venue for music inside! we saw benton blount there this past week & they were amazing! made our entire time there! the prices of food & drinks were a little crazy but the souvenir add ins were just too cute to pass up! definitely a must see if you're in nashville! plenty of line dancing & quick lessons for beginners so you can dance to the bands or music playing. i don't know if i'd eat there agin (besides the fried pickles they were phenomenal) but the venue for music was astonishing
Great service. Delicious lemonade slushies with vodka or whiskey floaters distilled on the premises. Just a bit pricey with a floater
Great Spot to listen to live music & grab a drink, but don't waste your money on the extremely overpriced food! It's terrible!
$15 for a good pulled pork, beer, and live music. Lackluster menu. The band was great, but had very limited song choices.
The band awesome! Bar service was horrible on top floor and turn off the misters. Duh! Tables and chairs wet it's cool outside.....

what a big big let down.horrible horrible service and nasty drinks! the server had a "so what attitude" i saw him telling the manager what i said about the bloody mary mix,  he too gestured "what ever"

of all the places i visited while on vacation in nashville, this was -is my regret. 
it's a numbers game is why they are still open. nothing to do with customer service, good drinks or good food.

i get ticked just thinking of the nasty attitude projected on us.

never again--- skip this place!

Sorry Soulshine, I wasn't impressed with you.

Coming in on a Friday night, I was surprised to get a table immediately and had high hopes after a good start. They were busy inside, but not packed and I really liked the big open restaurant and nice patio. Our waitress started off friendly but when it took a while to get our drinks and order, I should have known we were in trouble. She was very frazzled early on; not sure if she was just new or had too many tables or what, but she came over in a panic saying she couldn't take our order because she set down her book somewhere. Um, OK?  

Once we were able to order food, we ordered the tamales and hummus to snack on, then the mushroom pizza as an entree. The tamales were ground beef and spicy, and the best thing we ate. The hummus was decent but had an olive tapenade that overpowered the hummus. I didn't love it. The pizza was middle of the line, OK, but not amazing either. 

I would probably have given them an OK rating, but trying to get the bill and get it correctly was a CHORE. We were still enjoying our drinks and our bill was brought to the table. Um... we hadn't asked for the check and were going to use a ScoutMob coupon for half off. Plus our waitress added on a drink that wasn't ours. When we asked to use the coupon, our waitress gave us an attitude and said "it's going to take me a minute to redo it." Um, we get that but we would have told you about the coupon if you had asked if we were ready for the check. Sigh. The "minute" turned into 20. We waited and waited for our check, and when we FINALLY got it, (and it was still incorrect) we just paid and bolted for the door. It wasn't worth trying to fix.

I'm not sure I'll be back to Soulshine. If the food was better I might be tempted, but with middle of the line food I think I'll pick somewhere else next time.

This was probably the best barbecue I've ever had. I got the ribs with macaroni and cheese as my side and it was absolutely phenomenal. My group sat on the left side of the restaurant upstairs where there was a band playing. The band was also very good and they played a variety of genres from rock and roll, country, and pop. I would highly recommend this place especially if you're on the look out for a good barbecue in Nashville!!

So after trying about 7 bars we stumbled on to Rippy's. This was the best bar in the downtown area. The staff was friendly and the drinks were poured generously. We ordered a sausage and cheese platter to start and then the drinking began. The platter was generous and delicious. We went here 3 of our 6 nights in Nashville. They had a band that was incredible. Jacqueline is the only person we know by name so just ask if she's performing. If she is, whoever she's with is great. You can request songs for a buck! Cheaper than a juke box. They have an upstairs area as well. It gets packed upstairs so get there early. We spent about 16 hours over 3 nights here and will gladly do it again on our next trip. The bouncers are low key and friendly, the servers are fast and efficient. All in all the best bar in Nashville from our experience.

Stopped in here twice this weekend during my cousins bachelorette party. It was our last stop on our bar hop Saturday night. Good crowd and had a decent band playing.

Then we stopped by for mid-afternoon drinks on Sunday. It was gorgeous out so we hit the second floor which is completely open but still has a roof which was AWESOME! The open layout allowed for a warm breeze and let us be outside without baking in the sun. The acoustic trio was really good. I have a feeling this bar gets a lot of the better gigs due to it's size.

Being from the Tri-state area, we were impressed at the drink prices being much more reasonable than NYC.

Also the male wait staff wear a great t-shirt. Gotta love dirty puns!

Easily one of the best nights we spent in Nashville! The band was fantastic and it was great for people of all ages... Adults had the bar and drinks and kids and teens still had many ways to enjoy themselves. The band -Southbound Honey- was wonderful and played sets that were both modern and classic country and people of all ages were enjoying the dance floor. The line dancing lessons, although somewhat basic were a lot of fun and people continued to do them into the band's sets. Overall a wonderful night and I would most definitely return!

This place is the bomb to go to on broadway for a quick meal. The waitress we had was amazing and the pulled pork and Mac n cheese were awesome. The bands that play there are some of the best to listen to on the block. Have gone there multiple times and will continue to.
The pulled chicken was very dry, as was the burger. The burger had no flavor. No draught beers and they definitely charge the tourist tax.

Cover charge to eat mediocre food and $5 bottles. Loud, can't hardly hear the person next to you. My short rib grilled cheese was awful. Meat was bland, dry, jerky like, bread tasted like they cooked it in a whole stick of butter. Had to drown it in bbq sauce to make it edible. Save your money and go to honkey tonk row!

Fun bar. We went for a private party with a band. The area was HUGE. It was clean. The food (buffet style catering) was good, and the drinks were good too. I wasn't drinking alcohol but my colleagues were. They had several holiday signature drinks which looked great. Bartenders were efficient and friendly. Staff cleared things quickly too. I enjoyed the experience, especially since it was free!

The Wildhorse Saloon is a top notch venue to experience Nashville in a truly fun way. The layout is ideal to accommodate a lot of people. Great sound system, and plenty of really good views of the stage when bands are playing. 

The food was good- typical local fare. The bars are nice and spacious, so it's easy to get service when you need it. 

Tonight I saw two bands: Brother Trouble and The Band Perry. Both sounded great I this place. 

If you want to experience Nashville's music scene check out this place!

We ended up here because the live music was great and there wasn't a wait for a table. Our waiter was friendly and took our order fairly quickly but then drinks took awhile- we had to ask for water 3 times. I ordered chips and queso/salsa for an app- never came. Food came out in pieces and the pulled pork and fries were cold- still no chips/salsa. We complained to the waiter who said sorry nothing I can do. We found a manager who said he'd only charge us half. Finally, after all the other food was out- here came the chips and salsa. 
Music was good- that's it.
Delicious !!! Laid back eclectic hip pizza place ! Patio seating , live music , beer , wine , and awesome art work of musicians !

The staff was very friendly and it was interesting to be somewhere I've seen on TV, but the food was terrible.  No one finished what they ordered, nothing was very tasty.  Go to hangout and drink I guess, but the food isn't worth it.

Food is so-so and a little overpriced for the quality, but you really go there for the atmosphere anyway.  Very family friendly, good service. Enjoyed live music and learning to line dance. Great space.

5 stars because I had the TIME OF MY LIFE at Rippy's. 

Disclaimer: we did not have any food here (except for late night french fries), which seems to be where most of the negative reviews are coming from. 

Rippy's is a huge two floor bar with an area for restaurant seating and a bar/party area on each floor. There is a separate band on each floor and there's music all day. I gathered that the bands play in shifts (open-4 pm, 4-7 pm, 7-10 pm, 10-close, etc etc). We went to the upstairs bar on a Thursday night after having dinner elsewhere. This was during the SEC Tournament that was hosted at Bridgestone Arena right across the street so the place was packed with college basketball fans (which made it all the more fun)! The first band we saw (7-10) was so good and I was so sad when they stopped playing. We almost left but it started DOWNPOURING so we stayed. I'm so glad we did because the band that played next was even better! We were dancing, drinking, singing and just having such a good time. Ugh. I'm back in NYC sitting at my desk and smiling thinking about my night at Rippy's. 

Until we meet again ~~
VERY small pizza portions. Good pizza but tempted not to come back because I'm still starving after getting a small/what's normally a personal size pizza. Step your game up.
Great local dive bar! Burgers and bites are on point and the beer is always flowing!!
Great older western music acts.  Very friendly staff and a great variety of performers.
Marissa grabbed us off the sidewalk and gave us free drinks, how can you ask for a better day?  She was friendly and knowledgeable. We will be back. Thanks Marissa!

Surprised find across from Gaylord Opryland resort hotel. Garden burger just right with fries. Tried and loved Local yahoo beer -pale ale, and dark beer.
Had live band playing during my late lunch -3pm on Saturday -amazing -took me back to early sixties country music

Total tourist trap.... loved it. Especially since there are places upstairs where you can smoke. How awesome is that? 

Place was rockin pretty hard when we got there on a Saturday night. Saw a kid jump up on the bar and start dancing.... couple guys popped out of the shadows and whisked him out the back before you could blink. Place didn't skip a beat. 

Pulled pork in the nachos... awesome. Chx wings "had some stank on em" according to my counterpart from Kentucky. (That means spicy in a good way apparently) Spicy BBQ sauce had nice heat to it as well. So much food I was able to share with the table, still didn't finish everything. 

Pretty good place to hang out.

The ribs and pulled pork are great, and the baked beans are very tasty too. I tried the Yazoo pale ale but I wouldn't try it again. The live band was good, not too loud either so we could still hold a conversation.

We met Malad, a kitchen-staffer, on the street. He was so friendly, he didn't just give us directions, he walked us right in! What a gentleman! Once seated at the bar, Amanda suggested a local brew and the fried pickles...both amazing! The Mac n cheese was a little soggy, but the baked beans were stellar.

A fun atmosphere with live music (multiple floors), and good food. Sat on the 2nd floor with a breeze blowing through the big open room which made it very comfortable. 

We had the pulled chicken platter with potato salad and baked beans and the half rack of ribs with baked beans and onion rings. Both were flavorful and worth ordering again. Would go again!
Nachos and pizza are great! Nice place to hang out in Midtown, often have life music.  A little expensive but not too bad, mushroom pizza is fantastic.!

Exceeded our expectations. Food was surprisingly good, especially the baked beans and pork loin melt. No, it's not Memphis-quality BBQ, but then again, this is Nashville and not Memphis. The upstairs bar area is great for relaxing in the breeze, and part of it is open-air, with a big bar and stage. There are also some stages downstairs, and they'll often have three different musical acts going at once. Decently sized beer selection. If you're walking down Broadway and want a place to relax and enjoy the ambience, you could do far worse.

The service here sucked. I'm generally very lenient with my Yelp stars but I have never been so  disgusted with treatment. So I'm in Nashville for a week long conference with my research group. We don't have the cowboy look down so clearly we're from out of town- isn't southern hospitality a thing? Not here. We first took a table downstairs because it was open and close to the band that was playing but when no one came around the able for 10 minutes we decided to go upstairs (plus it was warmer).

The band upstair was great as well. Very loud, but that's to be expected. Again, we sat at the table for 10 minutes with not a glance in our direction. We caught a bus boy who said he would send a server over. Nothing. I went up and asked a server who was cashing out what we needed to do and he told me the table we sat at was the bartenders territory. No problem, we talked to the bartender. It's unfortunate that I don't have a penis because that was clearly what she was paying attention to. 

Eventually we placed our order and it came out in a decent amount of time. We had the sampler plus an order of the catfish. Both were decent and together it fed four people pretty well. Obviously check out was a disaster and when I handed her four credit cards (before she even printed bills) I got a dirty look and an eye roll. Sorry, do you have conference traffic through here? It's the tourist district of Nashville, is it not? Ugh. The busboy was super nice and friendly to talk to, he had great advice for what we should check out in Nashville, the two stars are for him and him alone. I hope he got most of our tips... Would not recommend.
Food is pretty solid and the music is usually pretty solid, too.  Their fries are great!  One of the better food to music ratios on Broadway, in my opinion.

HORRIBLE!!!!!!! walked in with my friends for a bachelor and bachelorette get together and right before sitting down we ordered 9 shots 2 hours later after the meal is when we got 3 out of 9 shots and asked them for the remainder the waiter advised us the bartender was backed up mind you it was Sunday and at 730 at night when the restaurant was empty. We then ordered 5 Jell-O shots towards the end of our meal and waited a hour for those which we never got we had to go to the bar and all our shots were just sitting there in a corner  and our waiter not even showing us interest. We returned the Jell-O shots and the other 6 shots shots didn't taste good at all. When we got the bill it was only my wife and I and they charged us $14 gratuity  with out $60 bill. We spoke to the manager to help us out due to the inconvenience of us being there for 4 hours waiting for our drinks and shots and me being prior military and law enforcement I advised him and he told us he doesn't "give a F***" about law enforcement and military and called enforcement on us to escort us out. I identified my self to him as law enforcement and military and the officer even told me this place is horrible and the manager is a piece of shit. Please read this review and do not eat over there the ribs were dry and gives you major heart burn. Sorry for this review but being tourists and expecting respect and a nice time they did not give us any of that. 

Sorry again thanks

Terrible! Do not go there to eat. The worst experience I have had at a restaurant ever. The place smells of urine and garbage and the seating is fend for yourself, with people waiting everywhere to jump on an open table. We waited 20 minutes for a table to open up. We sat down and were ignored for another 20 minutes until someone acknowledged us, telling us they would be right with us. After another 10 minutes we grabbed a waiter and asked if he could take our order, he said he wasn't really a waiter and that we were at a table that wasn't being serviced. He then turned his back on us and took the tables order whom had just sat down. The people sitting at our table (in the middle of the upstairs dining section) before us were waited on, and there were menus on the table, yet we weren't at a serviceable table, what a bunch of BS. We immediately left as I felt disrespected and my fiancé ended up crying about the encounter at the next place we went. They ruined our one night in Nashville, and I will most certainly never return there. Worst. Place. Ever.

Too bad great big nice bar crappy band. Are we in Nashville? I'm sure they have much better talent in this city. Came here from California hoping to see good music venues. Hope it gets better as this is my first day. They use soundtracks!! Geez

I went here with a large group.  Reservations were planned in advance.  WOW...Great live music.  Great food and drinks.  Great service and friendly staff.  Reasonable prices for a great experience.  The country dance lessons are fun.  This place is a MUST DO in Nashville.  I could come back here every night.
