Great place to listen to local talent, grab lunch and take in Nashville in an authentic honky tonk after visiting the Opryland hotel. Service was great!

Check out the smoked pulled chicken. The food is good but the service leaves allot to be desired. This place is busy but they don't staff accordingly. You will get a seat and service if you get there after the crowd has left. Otherwise, you will have to sit in a strangers lap. Some of the wait staff is friendly but dont expect them all to be.

We were there over 4th of July weekend and it was crazy busy! Not sure if this is typical or not. There was no reserved seating so you have to walk around and hope for the best. We managed to find a small high top table and then located two bar stools in a different area. There were two live bands playing. We really enjoyed the band in our area. I am not even much of a country fan but both the male and female lead singers did a great job.  The BBQ was decent. I had the pulled pork and my husband had ribs. I think both would have been better with some different sauce options. The sides were quite good. I had potato salad and beans and my husband had fries and cole slaw.  We shared an order of the corn cakes and they were very good!  Overall, solid bbq but not anywhere near the best we've ever had.

Band was really good. Food was decent at best. I'm from the northeast and I've had better ribs up there. Chilis has better ribs. Unless your having a beer and going to watch live music, skip this place. Go across the street to Jacks..

Looking for a quick bite before heading home. This place was very good, my burger was cooked just the way I ordered it. And the onion rings were very good. They had local entertainment going on while we was there and he did a good job. Will visit again in the evening hours to listen to more music.
A total dive but cool place. Cheap beer, delightfully bad karaoke and not too crowded. A couple of things to watch out for: it's smoky, cash only, and they only serve beer.

A classic Nashville hang... If you want to hear real authentic American country music, look no further. The food is pretty good for bar fate, too! The Fried pickles, sammies and burgers are all wonderful. If you're in the Opryland area... You can't beat it.

We went to a bunch of bars on Broadway and this was probably my least favorite one. They had TV's on with all the games, which was nice, but the band was not very good and no one seemed into them. We ended up leaving after just one drink.

Nice entertainment stop in the downtown area that doesn't have music blaring so loud you can't think. We had the 3rd floor reserved for a private event, and it was well stocked. Finger foods on the buffet were all good. 

The only problem was we could hardly hear the band. It seems the speakers were aimed toward the ground floor. Also, the only dancing being done was line dancing. Granted I haven't been to a dance bar in a while, but I expected to see couples dancing (two step, etc). That was not the case here. I only saw 2 couples dance the entire night. And no slow songs were played to encourage others (who might not know any other dance steps) to get out there with their significant other. A little disappointing but overall a good night.

For a famed spot it was pretty darn good.  It's huge and not the least bit quaint, but definitely worth the visit.  The music was was great, the food very good and it's huge.  Not exactly a hunky Tonk but it's worth stopping by for the food or music.

Bottom line: you may like this place for drinks and music, but be sure to eat at home before coming.
We stopped by for lunch, having stayed at a hotel around the corner. What a mistake. We had pizza & spaghetti with meatballs. Very basic. What we got was terrible. I suspect that someone had a plan here - how to serve a menu, all just assembled from items off a food service truck, and done so consistently that it doesn't matter who works in the kitchen. 
Any delivery to our hotel room (Domino's, Papa John's, etc.) would have likely been better.

Rippy's is the biggest bar on the block, you can hear it blocks away on Broadway. It definitely got our attention and we came in to grab a bite and some drinks. There are TVs everywhere to catch sports on. 

My 3 friends all got pulled pork or chicken sandwiches that were good and filling. I opted to do something different and got the pork loin sandwich instead, which I was very happy with. The sauce that comes with it tastes like a dry rub in liquid form. It's very peppery and went so well with the sandwich when I mixed with a little extra BBQ sauce. The service was very slow though and our waiter was not interested in good service in the slightest. 

Because the bar is so big, it can get so loud. We were there on a Bridgestone concert night, so the local radio station was hosting a live party there. It kind of adds to the buzz of Broadway though.

If you want a lively place to eat, you have picked it. This place has good food and is a great place to catch some live music and drinks. I have been here numerous times and have enjoyed my experience every time.

Firstly, I really don't like giving bad reviews because i figure if its open someone must like it. Bad reviews are simply a matter of opinion and good reviews speak louder. However, i just couldn't stop thinking about how horrible this place was and after 3 weeks of stewing on it i just had to write this one.

Unless you happen to be from Oxford and feeling nastalgic, this place is a total joke. The fact that they advertise their "Live Music all the time" before their pizza should clue you in. The pizza is the worst Ive ever had(seriously) and we ordered multiple pies as well as sandwiches. All were dry, flavorless and über expensive. $24 on average with close comparison to Little Caesars....which is totally worth $5. Beer was on the high side as well at $5/pt. and to top it all off, they have the audacity to put a tip line for the band on your tab! 

Up side: Excellent patio.
Will not be going back.

'Ribs' is in their name - but don't be fooled. Just go to Jack's across the street. These ribs were dry. They were bland. They weren't very meaty. And the overly sweet sauce tasted like something off the shelf from Kroger. Ditto for the side dishes.
On this Monday night, the cover bands were OK.  The service was OK. The whole place was generally disheveled.
I won't be back.

I ate here 3 days in a row it was so good. It was as perfect as BBQ gets. Moist with a great smoked flavor!  And a great setting with great music and an awesome staff!  It's a restaurant that gives Nashville its name!

Do not recommend going here

This is totally not an authentic Nashville place, it's too touristy. Many of their drinks come with a souvenir cup and are over priced. I had a misunderstanding with our waitress about which wine I ordered. As a waitress myself, I would apologize for not confirming which one I wanted and charge the price of the wine they meant to order. She instead argued with me, she called out her manager, and he argued with me TOO. I was in complete shock as my family owns a restaurant plus I am a waitress myself. So I just paid the full bill and wanted exit as quickly as possible.

Also, we came here for line dancing. everyone recommended it as a main event. It was instead just a small group on teens being instructed very basically the steps for about 10 minutes at most. It was definitely not as fun and exciting as I would expect such a big venue to produce for something they are known for.

Very casual eating , plastic utensils and plates. 
Attentive wait staff. Quick service
The chicken was moist and prob best chicken ive had in a while. My daughter got the ribs and loved it also.  I would recommend.  Live music and the kids were allowed after 8 was hard to find a place for them.  
There are 2 floors and you seat your self.
Great music- I loved the bologna sandwich. Most of the rest of our party did not like there food. Good ambience
This place is simply amazing, especially if you have a family with small children, and it is a nice sunny day. There is wonderful outdoor seating, and the pizza is great, too. Highly recommended.

This is my first dive bar experience. They had Dos Perros on tap. I asked if there was a happy hour and the response: "Our beer is cheap." Very True

The burger was solid, no frill and yummy.

Odd things I liked about the place:
Padded bar: a good place to lean and put a knee on
Shuffleboard 
Karaoke- there wasn't a huge wait to sing

The bands were all great - all three of them! This review does not reflect the bands.

I ordered a pork sandwich with slaw on the side and was served brisket with baked beans and fries. I was going to say something, but the fellow who gave me the food left so quickly I did not have a chance. Not wanting to cause a scene since I was at the bar, I quietly ate my food (which I wish the obnoxious Kansas City royals fans would have done too so everyone else could enjoy the awesome music!). My waitress came around later with my food and figured out the mixup and dropped my side from the bill. She was sweet, but that did not counter the overall poor food.

The fries were kind of greasy, but not a good greasy. The brisket was not smoked enough, so it was bland. The beans were decent, but why would you serve them in a foam cup? That definitely detracted from the beans. Anyway, go here for the music, not the food.

To preface, I LOVE Rippy's. It was the bar I used to go to in college and I really love the vibe, but something very strange and disappointing happened last night. I was at Rippy's at 10 sitting on a stool in the corner listening to the music. I had driven downtown and was planning to listen to a little bit of music after dinner and then drive home. While sitting, a staff member approached us twice asking what we would be drinking (reminder we were not at a table or the bar). We told him the second time we were driving and had ordered a drink earlier at the bar so we didn't need a second, and he told us we had to leave. He told us that it was his responsibility to serve us in his section and keep table turnover.  His reasoning is because we had to get a drink or leave. Never have I been treated like this at Rippy's, and I can't explain the disappointment. It is a place to enjoy music as well as drink, and the pressure from a staff to order a drink was appalling, especially after he knew we would be driving. I did not think that there was a rule that at all times in Rippy's you had to have a drink in your hand or you would be kicked out. VERY disappointing, especially with such good memories from a year ago when I went to college in Nashville.

It was Tues. & they just opened so it was pretty quiet. Waitress was very bland, no personality which is unusual for Nashville. We were vacationing  & we had experienced friendly service everywhere. Food was very good. BBQ ribs, potato salad & fries. Bottom line: 2 Stars for Service, 3 Stars for Food.

If your in the mood for ribs, this is the place. The flavor is great and soooo tender. We also had the nachos which were also a hit. The queso on it is the best I've had in awhile. Service was extremely prompt and we hardly waited 10 minutes for our food. Live music was a very nice touch. Great atmosphere!

This is a cowboy saloon, well a great bar.  We went here back in August 2017 the week end that the bears beat the titans.  It was an exhibition game.  (The place was rocking, Folk's were backed up into the street to get in). My group did not like it, we were a bit too old for this 25 to 35 crowd.  Sorry we moved on, but you young Folks will enjoy WILDHORSE SALOON in BNA.
The food is good and the music is great. Very friendly atmosphere. A good spot to relax have drinks and listen to live music.

Decent place for lunch. Had the pulled pork sandwich which need quite a few squirts of their bbq sauce for flavor. Their potato salad was really tasty though. 

A good spot to drink with friends because it's attached to an adjacent bar which provides more socialization.

The only good thing I can say about this joint is the music is GREAT!!  Stayed for over 2 hrs listening to a great band on the upper level.  It's a pretty cheesy place and the food is below average.  The hamburger was atrocious.  Even after plenty of drinks, it was just awful.  Bubba Burgers taste better than this. 
  There is much better bbq in the area.  Try Peg Leg Porker instead.  Best bbq sandwich around.
If you're just looking for a good , fun, larger honky tonk atmosphere with table seating this is a ok spot.

Went here a couple of times during a stay in Nashville and I just loved it. All three or so times we went, they had Square Dancing--not sure if we were just lucky or if they have it every night. It was so much fun to learn the dances together with other diners. Their food is delicious, too, and the service has always been good. I also love the architecture of this place. They have a huge main floor with tables and seating, in the middle of which is the stage with the dance floor. They have a second floor, which is basically a huge balcony with more seating options. The ceiling is very high and there are horse sculptures "running" across the ceiling. It's pretty cool. Definitely recommend going here for some Southern feeling.

TPAC is located in the James K. Polk Cultural Center which houses a myriad of event venues including the Tennessee State Museum and Andrew Jackson Hall--the place where I spent an evening recently.

I had the opportunity to visit and see - hear "Star Trek: The Ultimate Voyage" a live, retrospective film and music performance. The show featured selected clips from 50 years of Star Trek episodes and feature films while accompanied by a full orchestra. (In this particular small venue, it was a well-balanced half orchestra of about 50 performers.)

"Beam me up Mr Scott" in this instance meant beaming a high definition video onto a 40-foot wide screen behind the orchestra. The players were very dimly lit and did not distract from the video. In addition, the orchestra was hidden in part by a pseudo reconstruction of the bridge of the Enterprise.

The concert featured many familiar tunes written for franchise favorites such as Star Trek: The Original Series, Star Trek: The Motion Picture, Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan, Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home, Star Trek: Insurrection, Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, Star Trek: Voyager and much more.

A VIP pass (for an additional cost) afforded us the chance to go onstage during  the afternoon (before the performance) and be present for the sound check as well as meet the conductor.

Pretty cool event.

I realize this does not cover much of TPAC...but that will come after future visits.

What I liked:
1. Trevor at the Catbird Seat (a formidable judge of food) told us this was his favorite burger in Nashville.  The burger was quite delicious - and helped with our hangover from the drink pairings at our dinner the evening before.  However,,,

What I didn't like:
1. The service was terrible - the one waitress was also playing chef as their normal "chef" hadn't shown up.
2. The smoke- beware - smoking is allowed.  Sadly, that over powered the tasty burgers we wanted to enjoy.

Verdict- 
Meh... not worth the trip.  Maybe an evening try would be better, but I would stick to the other strong burger spots in town.
Love this place. Always try to stop in when I am in town. First time with my Daughter. Very kid friendly and good time for anyone. Great food too!!

We sat outside under an umbrella and had beers and pizzas all around. I heard it was a great spot for live music and bushwhackers - however we were there when a private event was happening upstairs, so there was no live music....and it was a little too early for bushwhackers. We loved our pizzas, wish i could remember what we ordered! It was plenty to go around, though!

Seating in the dining rooms are first come first serve. We waited about 20 minutes for a table to open up. The waitress was very prompt with waters and our drinks even though it was extremely busy on a Saturday night. 

The Honky Tonk tea was a great drink. The pulled pork dinner was OK. 

The bands were very good and the upstairs bar seemed to be where it's at. 

Overall, fun place with good drinks and decent food.

The carnivore pizza was amazing! It was fresh out and hot.
The facility was very clean and the staff was incredibly friendly. 
We also had the cheese and garlic bread it was very yummy.
Hubby got a Sweetwater Blue beer he enjoyed very much, mentioned it was very smooth.

This place is in business because it's on broadway & people that are visiting Nashville are downtown, looking for boots or hats or something & decide to eat here. The food isn't bad, but it's not great. You could get the same food from a fast food BBQ place like Bar-B-Cutie & it would be a lot cheaper. 

The meat doesn't have much flavor. The prices are Broadway high. I can tell you that all the people eating inside are tourists that do not know there's much better BBQ options around town.

One of the only pluses about the place is the large, second story patio that overlooks the street below. A great place to people watch.

We came here Thursday night.  This place is great for kids.  They put two big M on my daughter's hands (minor) just incase someone thought she was 21.   The place is huge with three floors.  The first floor is for dinner and the second two floors you can just sit.  We came at 9pm for line dancing and stayed until almost midnight.  My kids had a blast.  The band Radio Romance was playing.  Great band doing mostly covers and a few original songs.  We had a great time.  My youngest (7 years) had the most fun out of anyone on the dance floor.  She was having dance offs with about ten girls who seemed to love her company.   Great night for everyone.

Creamy crawfish soup is good. It is also a fun place to eat. Had good service too. 
Pizza was decent (though not as good as Mellissa said it was seeing as how she and Mitch gets Giordano's and I can't). Not that it was bad, but it was not "set apart" from the competition" .... then again, I am a critical of pizza and a bit of a pizza snob. 

The do have lots of great options for toppings and I would eat the pizza again. I want to try the calzones next trip.

Updated: I appreciate the comment from the restaurant (below). This is unusual for places to do this. It shows they really care. I will be back and and check out his tip below!  Got to love Nashville businesses!

Was at TPAC last Saturday for @Midnight Live with Chris Hardwick at the James K. Polk Theater. It was awesome. Seating was comfortable. Venue was easy to find. Parking was easy. Very happy. Staff seemed friendly although I didn't have much interaction with them.

I got the chicken fingers. They were ok the batter was pretty heavy. It was a Friday afternoon and medium busy and the service was horrible. The bartender working had no personality nor seemed interested in working.

Food was not worth it, there are plenty of better places on Broadway. My ribs were tasteless and I wouldn't order meat there again based on the average-ness of everyone's plate. The only stand-out was the fried pickles appetizer--the best fried pickles I had in Nashville, they do the entire dill spear instead of the rounds. I would recommend you go for the music (it's loud so don't expect a conversation), a beer and the fried pickles.

The food was not the greatest.  The live music is great.  Cute place,  but if you came to enjoy for,  skip it.  If you want a nice little lunch place with live music,  nice environment and great music.

LOVE TPAC and looking forward to enjoying the Phantom of the Opera soon.  There is something special about live performances.  TPAC  is a wonderful addition to any itinerary.  I usually have dinner beforehand at one of the many eateries nearby in the downtown Nashville area within walking distance of the theater.  The whole experience is a ritual of sorts for me. If you haven't gone, definitely worth a visit.

We were in Nashville for the Final Four and stumbled upon this place because the music pouring out of the upstairs outdoor stage was so good. We waited about 5 minutes for a table (if) and had a super great server. We both ordered the pulled pork sandwich with fries and onion rings so we could share. The sandwiches were great, but the sauce was what made it exceptional! The fries and onion rings were also hot and tasty. The band playing was amazing, and in the 2 hours we were there never took a break! We did go downstairs at one point and the 2 different bands playing inside were just as good - one in the bar area and one in the restaurant area. I have to say, as a musician, I did not hear one bad band or performer in my 5 days in Nashville. Not even mediocre. Everyone in this town can play! And sing!

We actually like this place so much we went back 2 days later. After looking over the menu we stuck with the pulled pork with fries and onion rings. Why mess with perfection? 

The last night there we went to Tootsie's Orchid Lounge, but stood on their outside patio and listened to the band at Rippy's...kind of silently wishing we had gone there instead. 

My next trip to Nashville (and there will be a next trip) will definitely include a stop back at Rippy's for great food, great music, and great atmosphere.
Good drink prices compared to the other bars in the area, and place is pretty bumping with life. A lot of space so your are not cramped. Id come her again.
Nashville has delicious food everywhere, this place is great for food and live entertainment. They have two live bands performing each on a separate floors.
Right across from where Predators play.  Good, not great, 'cue...AND LOUD MUSIC.  Bring earplugs, folks.  Save your ears!

Had a delicious lunch at the wild horse saloon. The Piggy Mac and cheese was outstanding. I was so full I skipped dinner. The cocktails seemed overpriced and weak on the booze. They force you to buy a collectible glass with certain drink choices . Music was lovely. Didn't stay for line dancing

Hard to really give a full review of this place as we were there for a private work event. But the venue is fantastic. Love the dance floor, the game options on the second floor (though they are TOO close together), and the table seating. 

The catered food was pretty delicious and the drinks were mostly good as well. I kept trying to get a gin and tonic (and tried 3 of the 4 bars in the place) and it was sparkling water every time. Very different. 

All in all, we had a blast. The dancers were fun to watch, the band (Brother Trouble) was really great) and we had a great time at the event. 

Thanks!

Always Nice To Find Pizza After Midnight!

SITREP

This is a great spot to come to after a long evening of having dinner (Sycamore Nashville), getting cocktails at more fancy establishments (Aura), dealing with more dive bar locations (Red Patio Saloon), and then decompress on beer, soda and pizza.

THE SETUP

Located in Midtown Nashville (not to be confused with Midtown Sacramento, where I live), the Soulshine Pizza Factory has a great late night menu, and is reminiscent both at once of a Sports Bar, Music Venue and a Gourmet Pizza Spot.  We hung out on the 2nd level deck, and patio bar area.

WORLD MUSIC

There was a great band playing when we arrived that way laying down some nice funky Jamaican beats, and expanding into a world music vibe with their music selections.  To be honest, I didn't recognize any of the tunes they were playing, but it was all upbeat and good to dance to.

GIANT FAN!

Oh my god.  On this large patio deck where the band was playing, is this massive overhead / over-sized fan - it must have been about 30-35 feet in diameter (kinda taking the wind out of the sales of my much smaller by comparison, three 5-foot fans I have in my home).  It certainly was impressive

THE PIZZA

Excellent personal pan style pizza - it seemed enough for 2 gals at our table to be sharing, and one was enough for me.  The Jacksonian had chicken, tomatoes and green onion.  The Mississippian had BBQ chicken.   They were total yum.

THE LOWDOWN

Soulshine Pizza Factory is a great stop to chill after a long night of fun when you need something to eat and want to catch a chill vibe with a band, refreshing drinks and great conversation.

My family had lunch at Rippy's and enjoyed live music. You seat yourself and a server comes to the table. We started with the fried pickles which were delicious. The food came quickly and the waiter was pleasant. The meal was excellent! I had the pulled chicken sandwich and it was flavorful and juicy. This is a perfect place to stop for a bite to eat for lunch if you are with adults or kids.

Food 2-stars, atmosphere 4-stars.   Weird checkin process.   You get carded, then you checkin, but they tell you it will be quick.  Then you can sit around/drink for hour or two until they call you for a table.    $6 cover on weekends, unless a member of party is veteran of military.     Had Hot chicken sandwich....  would not order again.   Was weird.   Hot habanero chicken, with overly sweet toppings.  Fried pickles decent.   Line dancing and live music very good.   Also, very kid friendly.   I recommend a visit, but think it will leave foodies wanting more.    FYI:   Get impression staff doesn't like the business.    They said 2.5 hrs tonight, even though it didn't seem that busy at all.

Great place to go in Nashville and learn to line dance.  Made a fun night because everyone can dance without feeling self conscience.  Cover charge was worth it once you get in a lot to do from playing pool, to dancing,

Ok, seriously, I was amazed!  This place the staff is nothing but spectacular. We just happened to be walking by and one of our party recognized Big Machine store and Distillery as affiliated with Taylor Swift.  We went in to look around, and the security guard,David schooled us on the superiority of their vodka and whiskey.  Totally changed my mind about alcohol and quality, and I'm not even a drinker!  
Besides that...The bar staff helped us so much with navigating around Nashville. We were getting overwhelmed with trying to figure out where to go and what to do.  She actually saved our trip!  She told us the great places to go to eat, shop, listen to music and bars to go to.  Nashville is such an awesome place, with incredibly nice and helpful people everywhere, but this place but  Keeleligh was the most amazing of them all!  A complete Gem.  I am so glad we happened upon this place so early in our trip. 
Thank u, thank u

The "Sampler" is a must (ribs, wings, sausages, poppers, briskets, cheese, and pickles).  Unless you've got a big appetite, two can share.  Last been there over a decade ago and it is still the bomb!  Sat at the bar upstairs this time around and got good service and entertainment.

As tourists we felt welcome here. My first choice for their 12 bone pork Ribs, fried Catfish strips with fries, and a Bud Light.  Bridal shower singing and dancing to Song of the South makes it irrelevant if the stage singers are good.  'Next time', I wear my denim shorts and tonylama to blend!  An honest honky tonk bar.

Quick review for a quick stop:

Two story building. Three different live bands. One packed, happy, drunken crowd. Go and look at all my reviews... they are long... they are tiresome... they are detailed and intricate. But this place doesn't need that. This place just needs for you to know that you are going to get an amazing Nashville experience

Like other reviewers, I agree that this is the absolute worst service in town. The food is mediocre at best and the drinks are insanely overpriced. Unfortunately, they will always be busy and stay busy due to their location and tourists who do not know any better. I have honestly never had a good experience here regardless of whether I am eating a meal or just having a few drinks at the bar. There are so many other great options downtown- go there instead.

Second bad experience at this cheesy little saloon. Don't bother there is zero customer service. They are the rudest management team and staff in Nashville. Learn to line dance from YouTube. And a simple drink is a double digit price. Too many other places to spend your money in Nashville.

After previously enjoying concerts here with dinner and hearing some awesome local talent,  NEVER again. 15 Minutes to sit being the only people at podium Sat as soon as someone noticed us them no waitress for another 10 to 15 minutes with maybe 20 other patrons at tables, we left ....when I informed the manager, he couldn't care less.....won't b back

We went there for lunch. We are new to the area from California and this place was exactly what we were looking for. Great southern food and fast service. The host girl was very friendly and welcomed us. Our server was nice and attentive. 
They have kids menu, too. Food was big and very good.
Place is huge. They have pool tables on the 3rd floor which we played with our kids since up stairs wasn't busy yet. ( I am guessing it gets busy at night so no children allowed then )
Nice experience.
Don't come here if you want customer service.... the only ones that are right are the servers and hosts according to the gm... it doesn't matter if you purchase food or drinks.

Ok BBQ not the best in Nashville by a long shot.  They had unsweetened tea in the sweet tea the night I visited, and the waitress did not believe me.  I asked for a soft drink to replace my tea, she later came back and stated she tasted the tea and it was unsweetened and apologized.  Why argue with your customer?

Busy place on the corner of Broadway. Two floors at least with great live music on both floors. Lots of different menu options. I went with the brisket plate. I chose Mac n cheese and coleslaw which I was happy with. The corn bread was also a really good addition. My brisket was melt in your mouth and multiple people at the table called it the 'best' they've had!

Lunch time on a Friday. Had the grilled chicken wrap and it was great. Band was good as well. Wasn't to crowded at that time but still a good crowd. At this time they had ample servers and the food came out pretty quickly. I would definitely go back.

Way too fun here! Prices werent bad at all and I convinced my friend, who isnt a country fan one bit, to get out on the dance floor. So much life and energy. Id come back to nashville soley for this saloon!

Came for the Friday night concert series put on by local favorite indie radio station Lightning 100.  On a warm summer night this is a really great thing and very, very popular as evidenced by the hoards of people crowding the upstairs patio.  One of the things I love about this place is their support of local music.  Check out their concert listing for great stuff.

Soulshine has a lot of good things going for it such as this weekly event.  It has other good stuff like their beer selection.  

The food and service?  Meh.  We had their nachos which aren't made from your traditional corn chips but rather the pizza crust/dough.  The toppings were good but I hated the pizza crust.  Also, service upstairs on the patio was dismal.  It took forever for me to get the bartender to acknowledge.  Once outside we never saw our waitress so we went back to the bar to order more drinks (we had been sitting outside for over 30 mins) and at this point our "waitress" finally came over and chided us for not ordering from her after hastily introducing herself.

So why am I generously giving 4 stars?  I love their support of local music.  And the fact that this chain is named after an Allman Brothers song.

Just stopped in for drinks and an appetizer. Poor service in the bar. Waitress didn't clean any of the tables the entire time we were there, and when we asked she begrudgingly got a dry rag and ran it across the water rings on the table. Fried pickles were meh. Environment was decent.

Okay, this place is HUGE. It's the first place we went to when I visited Nashville, and oh man, it was FUN! There's THREE different bands playing at once, and everyone is just truly enjoying themselves. It's so loud so you have to shout, but it's fun. Lots of drinking and dancing and singing going on. My friend and I were starving so we got the pulled pork. YUM! I'm glad I got to try some good bbq while I was in Nashville. If there is better bbq I"ll be sure to keep it in mind for next time.

I have been to Nashville twice and both times I have been so excited to eat at Rippy's. Not only is their BBQ sauce the perfect combination of tangy and spicy, and the pulled pork moist and plentiful, but the music and atmosphere of the three story establishment makes it a start to a great night. The food may take a bit longer to get to the table because of the popularity, but it is well worth the wait (30-45 minutes). Also, the fried pickles are a great appetizer. Prices are fair (8 dollars for a sandwich and fries).

Great ribs great sauce. Probably the best smoked chicken I've ever had.
Good band and attentive servers. 
Loved it

My husband and I wound up here on a Wednesday when live music was playing. Food, drink, music was good. What I want to point out was how they dealt with a young country music fan. He wanted to sing and loved Johnny Cash, and I have never been in a place that was so kind, accommodating, and nice! The treatment of this young man was beyond and above anything I've experienced and that alone recommends this place in my mind. On behalf of all of us on the spectrum, sincere thanks.
Awesome spot, great location, great music. Second floor was busy and our bartender Alessandra was very attentive and quick to refill our drinks. Highly recommended spot on broadway!

Live music ! 
Local beers and nice samplers of BBQ. First restaurant tried in Nashville thanks to our Uber driver who recommended the place.

We had so much fun here. On the Friday night that we were there, they began charging a cover charge at 7:00 (waived for military and first responders- thank you for supporting these brave people). We got there around 7:30 and stayed for a long time. The atmosphere is so much fun that we couldn't bring ourselves to leave. 

There are three floors, all with a view of the stage if you are interested in the live music (we loved the first artist on the night that we were there!). On the first floor, there is a huge dance floor and there are line dancing lessons in between live music sets. The dancing is fun!!! Even if you miss the lesson, it's easy enough to pick up by just watching others. 

I will say that we didn't order any food, so I can't comment on that. I did order a drink, which was expensive and heavy on the alcohol, but delicious nonetheless.

This happened to surprisingly our favorite place downtown. It's off the beaten path right beside FGL house. We saw the word sample so we went in during the day and had a vodka lemonade slushy sample. It was so good. The bartender was very knowledgeable with my husbands questions. We had some more walking to do so we left but we went back in the evening to two different bartenders. We decided to split a lemonade slushee because we aren't huge drinkers and it hit the spot. More then the the great drinks there the bartenders and service were great. They were able to read the cues in my body language and communicated to each other wordlessly to deal with a situation with another patron that was loud, in my space, and making me uncomfortable. The male bartender was able to speak with him and diffuse the situation. Thank you so much! When we come back we will make sure to stop in again.

Rippy's was really fun. They had a great band playing and the drinks were not only cheap, but also good. The bartenders are friendly and so is the crowd. I didn't try the food, so I can't comment on that, but I'd recommend Rippy's for a fun night out.

Atmosphere great, service not. Caitlin was our bartender and we did not get one smile from her during the 10+ drinks we ordered. No hi how are you, thank you. She ruined the whole experience for us as we were having fun on the dance floor but as soon as we had to order a drink we dreaded it. Hope we won't get her again.

We loved it.  Our server Brendon( I think that was his name)  was awesome.  He was extra friendly and really helped us out on what to order.  His recommendations were spot on.  The pulled pork sandwich and smoked chicken platter were the best.  The chili was excellent too!  The cole slaw was good but needed a little salt. We thought it was much better than Jacks Bbq that was across the street.  
The band that was playing were funny and sounded great too.  I would definitely go back !
Great live music and city cold Coors Light bottles.  Really what else do you need to start you journey down Broadway?  I didn't try the the food but it looked great.

Went here this year & once last year. Idk what happened between last year & this year but there's a huge difference, and I don't mean in a good way. Last year when we visited the pulled pork was absolutely delicious, I didn't have one complaint. This year was disgusting. I usually always finish my plate. This year I had about five bites or so and was done. That's how gross it was. Definitely cooked different and more fat & chunky instead of shredded. Waitress also sucked this year. Messed up my whole order, then argued saying that's what I ordered. Definitely won't be back again. Will stick with Peg Leg Porker, Id rather stand in line for an hour there because they are much better.

Hands down this restaurant was the filthiest place I visited down town in Nashville!
The waiter: Tommy gave us the crappiest service we've ever had in our lives!
I have been in the restaurant industry for over eight years and a food server as well. This server took our order after waiting 20 minutes, never came back to fill our drinks ,never checked to see if our food even arrived & the order was completely messed up & he didn't bring 4 items we ordered (not all food we ordered was brought out). The best part of the night, was after sitting there for an hour and 15 minutes he came back to the table and dropped the check off without half of the food even being brought out or served to us. I gave it one star, because the band was good but other than that everything else was disgusting and horrible!
I would not recommend this place to my worst enemy! Hopefully you guys change your management and your server because you will never make it if you keep such a failure of a slop house in Nashville for sure:(

OK, I want to give this place more stars because the burgers are great and the beer is cheap.  Divey - definitely.  I'm fine with divey, but it boarders creepy depending on the day.  Some times have been fine and some times have been a little too "David Lynch-ish."  If you're adventurous and you want a good, fresh tasting burger and a cheap beer give it a try.

For being Nashville for the first time I thought I would have some good BBQ I've hade better in Detroit. Gave you 2 sauces and they were both ok and did not see much of a difference other than one was a little more spicy. The ribs wee good with the dry rub but the pulls chicken was dry. The slaw was bland but the beans were good and only if you like spicy. I figure this is the type of food you get in a tourist town.  I guess you have to go off the beaten path to find the good stuff. 

The one thing I did find disgusting and it wasn't the restaurant it was that whole area it smelled look old stale beer and cigarets not vert appetizing.

We were in Nashville for my daughters 21st birthday went to all the bars and trendy stuff your supposed to do while in town. Came in to Big Machine because they had a Vodka lemonade slushy on a very day met the manager Jacob and have been back everyday since. I highly recommend visiting,GREAT Vodka,Whiskey,Store and very friendly employees.
Terrible service. Won't let you sit at a table unless you can fill it. Been coming for years and service and food have declined substantially in the past year. Don't waste your time or money.

Matt Holloway should be fired! My boyfriend and I decided to check out the line dancing. Unfortunately we were unable to find out. We had waited in line to be ID & got wrist bands went inside and got a drink at the bar & started a tab with my CC. We stepped outside to smoke b/c it is a smoke free building and then when we attempted to return the door guy informed us we were not allowed inside. I showed him our wristbands & explained that my purse and CC were at the bar and he stood in front of me to physically block us from going inside. I ended up having to push past him so that I could go get my purse and close my tab out and get my CC back. As I was waiting for the bartender to run my CC the door guy approached me with the manager (Matt Holloway) who were both going to escort me out. I explained that after the way I had been treated at the door I was leaving of my own choice after I paid my tab and the manager grabbed my arm as to assist me out the door. So do NOT waste your time or money at The Wild Horse Saloon unless you want to risk being refused service and forcibly removed for no apparent reason.

Music was cool. Dinner took a very long time to arrive and when it did it was just ok. The ribs were practically flavorless. Unless you soaked them in BBQ sauce it was pointless to eat. The best thing I can say is that it's food.
Food was not good. Worst burnt hamburger ever. Very slow service. Music was good if you like older tunes.

Place got crowded real fast. Ordered a few angry orchards and just enjoyed people watching. First time in Nashville figured I should eat something BBQ considering every restaurant was that type of food. Pulled chicken had great flavor, potato salad was tasty seemed yellow mustard based, which I don't mind. Live Music can be heard from every bar, not a fan but it all sounds the same to me. If your into this scene this is heaven.

Limited menu. Food was okay but the place is really cool. We loved the live performance. My daughter loves the horses on the ceiling. We were there on a Wednesday night and it wasn't very busy so we were able to sit on the floor close to the stage. We had a good time just wished there had been more to choose from on the menu. We definitely enjoyed the experience more than the food.

Had a large group and were trying to grab something that everyone liked before the Predators hockey game. We walked in and the placed was already pretty packed ... Ended up going upstairs (which was equally as busy).

The food was good but nothing to write home about. I had the pulled pork with baked beans and cole slaw ... pretty standard stuff. The ribs looked good, the pulled chicken got some rave reviews. We also ordered a bunch of apps beforehand. A few of the dinners came out wrong but the server quickly got us squared away.

Good food, good drinks, cool honky tonk atmosphere, but best of all they got us in and out pretty quick in time for the game next door.

Country Line dancing lessons brought us here early. The lessons lasted about 10 minutes. This was followed by a boring band and you couldn't apply what you learned at the lesson. 

Quite honestly, you must need to come later, because early is boring.

The bands were great; talented and not an ounce of auto tune! 

Ribs were good. Baked beans were good. Potato salad could have used some paprika. Pickles would have been a nice touch, too. 

We got our food in under two full songs- super quick!

This place is pretty fun! On the weekend it's a $6 cover charge (except if you are military! Woohoo!) we got to see 2 bands play and have dinner and drinks. Their menu is pretty good! I got the hot chicken sandwich, which was pretty spicy and so good! The bands where good with mixing it up between their original songs and covers. Every now and again there would be line dancing lessons, and they are very easy. A few things that you should definitely know, is that it gets very CROWDED. (but in all honesty.. it's Nashville, what else do you expect..?) and that you will not be able to have a conversation with anyone while you are there (it's so loud!). The venue is set up with a large stage and dance floor with surrounding tables for dinner and multiple levels for extra seating. However there is no way to avoid the volume. Of course, I am sure everyone is going to Wildhorse to listen to music, however if you plan on having dinner, just plan on not being able to speak to your group. The food was great though! Overall, a good experience!

Enormous physical space right near our hotel, and came highly recommended from multiple people. On our last night in town, we swung by Broadway just to see the hustle and bustle, and then walked to NashHouse. What a feast! The service was friendly and quick despite the fact that they were pretty busy. We loved the live music - a boyfriend and girlfriend guitar and singing combo (@lynavenue). Big fans! Beer list was impressive, food was delicious. Fried green tomatoes, country-fried steak...wow, everything was so good! Would happily return on our next time in town. Awesome spot, thanks for a great time!

Disappointed.  Drove into Nashville to see the band and got there at 8:55 p.m. just after they shut down for the night.  Advertised for live music until 10 p.m.  Texted friends to let them know to meet somewhere else.

We had a private event here a couple nights ago. The food was wonderful. They served brisket, pulled pork, fried fish baked beans, potatoes and chow chow. I enjoyed all of it. The staff was friendly. The group doing our event brought in the music and it was great. The bathrooms were kept clean and the drinks were good.
Ribs - good rub but ribs are dry as hell. Pulled park dry as well. Cole slaw wasn't good . Beans are good. I would never eat there again. 36 bucks for crappy bbq
Awesome experience for our family!  Great entertainment, good food, amazing atmosphere.  Definitely a family fun destination restaurant.

What a gem TPAC is to the city of Nashville!  We are so lucky to have this venue, featuring a wide variety of shows, concerts, comedians and so much more, on several different stages.  TPAC is home to the Andrew Jackson Hall (where several large-scale productions are held), the Tennessee Rep and the Nashville Ballet.  I've seen productions from all three companies and they are all top-notch.  I particularly enjoyed seeing Cabaret by the Tennessee Rep 1 1/2 years ago - the small hall was perfect for this intimate show, and the show was beautifully sung, acted, danced and costumed.  I bit the bullet this year and purchased my first set of season tickets and have enjoyed every show I've seen.  

About parking - I purposely purchase tickets for Sunday shows so I can take advantage of parking in around Legislative Plaza.  I never pay a cent to park and nearly always find reliable and safe parking 2-3 blocks from TPAC. 

I'll continue to enjoy all that TPAC has to offer, that's for sure!
Waited over an hour and a half after ordering with no food and no update when asking the bar. Never received food.

Terrible, don't waste your money. Same food you'd find in the freezer section of your grocery store. Chicken fingers were hard as a rock, mac and cheese barely edible. Chicken wrap chicken was hard as a rock as well. Curly fries old and hard. Service was terrible as well. Took 15 minutes after receiving food for waitress to come back so we could ask for ranch. Another 7 to get it. Meanwhile our drinks were empty. Waitress was seen walking around eating. Smh. McDonalds would have been better.

4 of my friends of mine and I dined here today. We waited over 20 minutes for our pizza. When we got our orders, my boyfriend's pizza didn't come. We asked about his pizza 3 different times. It never came. We all finished our meal, and asked for our checks. Still no pizza. Finally we talked with a manager, she got his pizza to go. THEY STILL CHARGED HIM $2.74 FOR HIS DRINK!!!!! It was not our server's fault but the manager needs to learn about customer service. Bottom line: HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE.

Really cool place if you're willing to withstand the overpriced drinks. The band was great, but that's typical of what you get on Broadway. My wife would've stayed the whole night, but I wanted to see what else Nashville had to offer. Bartender was friendly and very attentive. I'd go back! Try that Jaco Daniels Fire, one of the only states it's available right now!

The food was meh. I ordered a calzone, my friends ordered pizza, soup, salad, & the red beans/rice. All of it was below average. I don't know how, but even the Coke was bad.

We waited for 40 minutes to get our food, which was cold. It was pretty busy and our waitress wasn't rude but she pretty much ignored us the whole time.

The check also took forever to get.

Incredibly loud, impossible to hear or talk (and that was before the live band came on).

They had free WiFi, which was nice (legitimately the only reason I survived this awful institution).

Takeaway: Don't go at night. Or on the weekends. Or at all.

I had a really great experience here on my birthday, so I must give Soulshine an updated review. 

We had a very large group come in with multiple tickets and drinks on a Friday night and wanted to hear the Lightening 100 show that they put on every week in the upstairs patio area. I didn't even call in and request a large table or reservation, we just all showed up to hang out at 5:00.  I was hoping to have a good happy hour, but they only had 2 for 1 Sweetwater beers until 6pm. Damnit! Give us some more options and a longer happy hour! But I digress, I sipped on greyhounds all night and they were tasty.  

Most of us ordered  food, and I was very happy with the Sante Fe pizza. It was much better than the mushroom pizza I had on my first visit, and the jalapenos were spicy and awesome! I also heard good reviews of the nachos, though I didn't have an opportunity to try them. 

What really made my experience leaps and bounds better from my first visit was our incredible waiter Ryan. He not only kept a LARGE party satisfied with drinks and food, he somehow got all of our tickets correct at the end of the night. No one missed a beer or had the wrong pizza order on their tab. And he didn't even write anything down. Dude, that's skill. Plus he was working the patio area with multiple other tables too. I honestly don't know how he did it. 

Not bad Soulshine. I can see myself here on a nice Friday night to enjoy another Lightening 100 show. I just hope I have Ryan as my waiter.

Much to be desired. Pulled pork was bland. Nashville "hot chicken" was good. Sides were ok but not great in a place known for great southern food. Big screen to watch the game. Live entertainment at night. Room for improvement.

We stayed at a hotel near the bar and came into town for a bachelors party and had a blast. The atmosphere is great and would definitely be back. The bar has a small town feel and has a great atmosphere. They have great live music. Their drinks are great and a great place to visit if from out of town. Has a very friendly staff and great service.
Great atmosphere! Service was very good and awesome bands! We had the fried pickles and then bbq brisket with baked beans and greens. Everything was delicous!

The entire reason for this rating is the price of their beer...$6 FOR A 12 OZ MILLER LITE. I am not cheap nor am I poor, but I am reasonable. The manager who made this pricing decision did so whilst giving all of our dear Music City's locals as well as its tourists a giant collective kick to the balls. You're awful.
The ribs and fries were great! What was better? Renita..the bathroom attendant who had a spray bottle full of soap and handed me paper towels!!

The food is excellent. They have a great selection of pizza and beers. Located in the midtown area, this establishment offers live music and TVs to grab your teams big game. The upstairs offers additional seating with a patio that overlooks the busy streets of midtown. The problem with this place is the service. It is the worst in Nashville. But I frequent this place for cold beer, tasty pizza, and good friends!
Typical Sysco food and inattentive service. Just good enough, but won't be going back. Beer selection is very limited.

Soulshine has become a fantastic place to catch live music or go hang out and grab some drinks and a bite to eat before you head out for the night on Division. They have a fantastic beer selection and their pizza is awesome.

My wife and I always opt for the wheat crust pizza :) The Carinvore is always my go to choice.

The seating in the balcony upstairs and outside is first come first serve but it is always pretty easy to find a seat at the bar downstairs as well if the wait is a little long. People come and go so typically you do not have to wait for seating too long.

Definitely recommend to any local or tourist looking for a place to hang out.
Great food and great music. Don't need the MC, very annoying. Speaks down to the audience. Let the entertainer entertain!!

The pepperoncini was salty and the ranch was straight out of a faucet. Also, the wings were dry. Plates were scarce.

The big ass fan was nice

Mediterranean Pizza = To DIE For
Good Beer
Good Prices
Friendly staff
GREAT Music
Parking can be difficult at times

I really enjoyed my time at Soulshine. I will be returning soon to see if it is consistently this good!

I'm giving it 4 stars for the quality of the music. I've seen a few bands there now. All were fantastic.  Carolyn Martin was great!  

The food...nothing special at all.  I didn't expect much, but I always think a veggie burger shouldn't be the same burger that I can pull out of a Morningstar box.  I mean Sysco sells a really good veggie burger.  I'm not even a vegetarian, but do sometimes eat veggie burgers.  Sad to see that they microwaved a burger from a retail box.  Saw the other meat burgers also and they were not good.  How hard is it to prep and plan for at least a decent burger? 

Long story short, go for the music, but eat somewhere else before you get there.

The food was quite good and you got a lot of it. We had a very large group last night.  Had a chance to taste several of my coworkers food.  Wish we had a more experienced-server though.  Not good when you ask how the catfish is and that person tells you to order the ribs.  And he couldn't tell anyone of us who he beer was good.  Several of us just went straight to the bar and ordered.

Sunday, May 6:   We were looking for good BBQ downtown and saw Rippys.  Decides to give it a try.  Our server was fantastic.  He was attentive and polite the entire time.  The bbq was so-so. Not very meaty for the price, but the sides were good.   I thought $10 for mozzarella sticks was a little much though.  The biggest complaint I have was regarding the live music.   We were on the second level, a mother/daughter duo with a male singer were performing.  They were very good.  However, I was appalled that the male singer started goin from table to table with the tip bucket, literally asking for tips!  I understand they make their living from tips, I work for tips too, but I would NEVER make my clients uncomfortable by asking for a tip.  It's the choice of the patron based on the performance or service as to whether they'd like to leave gratuity!  I was not happy about his approach and he noticed (while my husband was digging for cash to give this guy), he said to me " well if you feel that strongly about it you don't have to tip. But that's the way we make our living.  I told him I also work for tips and was still speaking when he got his money and walked away from me. Also- we saw four other live music acts the night before and we tipped every one of them, by choice.  Rippys needs to have a conversation with this guy.  His behavior was 100% unacceptable!

Staying here for a couple of weeks on vacation up the road and stumbled upon this place.  The best part of this place is there is ALWAYS live classic county music.  Great atmosphere with outside seating. The limited pub type menu works perfect when suckin back a few Busch beers listening to the great music!  You have to stop by!

Really this place is a joke save your money . They call this barbecue we had the appetizer combo for 23.50 the dish was cold the onion rings were the only thing edible. We told our server the food was garbage and that it was no reflection on him when leaving another smart-ass server offered me a quarter some customer service!

For live music and a good time I give this place 5 stars. I did not eat here and the food looked like you should expect at a pub serving BBQ. This place is all about the constant live music and entertainment and great staff. The staff hustles around in the hot sun as you kick your feet up and listen from a roof top deck to some amazing performers play Kid Rock-Miranda Lambert, I am not a country lover, but I loved me some Rippy's- the place to go in dt Nash!

UK alumni held a Pep rally and UK vs UL b-ball watch party prior to the bowl game. Woefully understaffed. 2 Bartender's and the line took over 30 minutes.  Additionally they had very few staff to take food orders. We tried to order and could never find anyone. Then staff tried to deliver other people's food to us 3 times.  Apparently they didn't know that BBN travels well.
How do they serve pulled pork without a bun!? And then charge extra if you want one! Food wasn't that great and the pork looked disgusting. Hot as balls

We stayed in the Cambria (hotel above this restaurant). It was so convenient for us to head downstairs, have some DELICIOUS southern/ American food, and enjoy some AMAZING TALENT. Their hot chicken, Mac n cheese, pickle flights, desserts, and drinks were fabulous. We ate here 5 times during our stay. The staff is incredible, very attentive, friendly and accommodating. Would recommend 10/10. Would return 1000 times over.

This venue is huge and I can understand why people tend to love it, with their live music and line dancing lessons...However, I was really excited given all the hype and I didn't really think it was THAT great. It was ok, but out of all the places we stopped in during our weekend in Nashville, this was definitely not one of my highlights.

I think it largely had to do with the crowd itself... it was very crowded with very young people. One good thing that came from it: I learned "the Wobble"

Just sat at the bar for ten minutes. The bartender (dirty blonde hair, glasses) was not very busy yet walked passed me several times and looked at me, then kept walking. I was never addressed, never greated. I walked out. On the way out she walked passed me and did a double take like she realised I was walking out, yet said nothing. What a shame because this place is world famous and I was looking forward to a good experience. Instead, I'll go back to Florida with a bad taste in my mouth (which is the only thing I was served here). What a shame.

Food was horrible and cold  , I should have listened to my uber driver Don't  eat at rippys. Everything closed so early we had no choice .  be careful  with ur receipts  pull pork was 11.95 with two sides I was charged   12.95  ,  + my 9 dollar drink , tip included in bill  3.78 + some downtown fee , and these fuckers had the nerves to add additional  line for tip  on the receipt  .   please

Not Bourbon, but distilled Big Machine Vodka.  Tito's move over. Here is the next big thing.  The Big Machine was offering Lemonade Smoothies samples and we walked right in and discovered a great tasting Vodka.  The lemonade, frozen lemon drop smoothies, were outstanding and we bought a six pack I could take back to DC, and try out on my friends for Thanksgiving.  What a unique distillery right off Broadway in Nashville.   Check it out, you'll discover the next Big thing, the Big Machine.
Haven't eaten here but went to the concert event drivin and cryin and it was awesome! Great service and nice local beer choices at good prices. I'll be back.

My girlfriends and I loved this place for the Friday night happy hour with Lightning 100. We plan to come back again! 

The service, at the height of the Friday rush, was exceptional. Our waiter was attentive, helpful with menu and is drink suggestions, and never made us feel rushed to leave despite the crowd. A++ 

We tried several pizzas- the Palermo and the Bob Marley were our favorites. The crust is tasty, thin, and available in both white and whole wheat (we liked them both). 
Several beers were on draft and only $2 during happy hour.

The music was loud and a great backdrop for revelry after a busy work week, but be prepared to shout. We loved the games and DJ antics as well, from 5-7- there are many chances to win concert tickets and other prizes. There is a local act that takes the stage at 7pm for a free show, so it's just another wonderful way to find new music. 

We got there at the magic hour after business traffic was gone, and party goers were not yet out and about, so we were able to find street parking nearby. Given the congestion of Division street, I imagine this isn't always the case, so be forewarned.
Great atmosphere and awesome pulled pork! Nice chill place to listen to music and have a few beers. Try the local brews!!
Live music and beer.  Was fun!   Gorgeous day.  They allow smoking inside he 2nd floor (sorta gross).  And food wasn't too good but live music and beer!!

This place was recommended to us by our hotel concierge (after he told us *not* to go to The Bluebird Cafe). It was good, but that's about it. The cover was way more than it should have been, and we were going for dinner, so $10 each for cover, plus expensive drinks in glasses we got to take home (but left in our hotel room because I don't need a mason jar or 22 oz. beer stein), and high priced food ended up being the most expensive meal during our entire 5-day stay. I think if you come for dinner (and order a minimum amount of food - determined by the manager) the cover charge should be waived. The band was good, and worth the cover charge, and the food was good (though overpriced and *way* to much) but there could have been a happy medium.

It is a 'family friendly' venue, so expect families with children running around, as we experienced. The dance floor is large and we participated in both line dancing lessons. Then they closed. It was like 11:00 or so, and they closed. I realize it wasn't a weekend, but other restaurants/bars/honkytonks stay open until 2:00 or 3:00am. And when they close, they close - music off, lights up, go home. Very surprising.

The bathroom concierge is not necessary. Really. I do not need someone to start my water for washing my hands, and hand me a towel, then expect a tip. If there is one thing this venue could do, it would be to get rid of the bathroom concierge. Seriously. Not needed, not necessary, and just too uncomfortable to have to deal with.

Pulled pork sandwich was just OK - no sauce or anything on it, and none on the table either. Salad was big, and good. 

I'll come back to Nashville, but I will most likely not visit this restaurant again. Too pricey, too impersonal, and closes too early.

They have a schedule for "line dance lessons" so while we were there we learned a dance at 5:00 and another dance at 6:00. We also got in some foozeball and pool on the third floor, which overlooks the lower two floors and has upside down horses hanging from its ceilings. Paid a dollar or two extra to get our drinks in glass boots which we are keeping as our Nashville souvenirs.

Wow, a great place to stop in. The atmosphere was good, the waitress was attentive and friendly, and the decor gave me plenty to take it. We enjoyed the music and the drinks and would love to stop back in. I knocked off a star because I wasn't impressed with the food options, hot dogs and fried bologna isn't my thing. The burger did look fantastic when one went by though.

I thoroughly enjoyed my visit to Soulshine Pizza... but I also admit I wasn't in any hurry and my husband and I were looking for a relaxing evening. Service was fine... no one was in much of a hurry, but neither were we. I thoroughly enjoyed my pizza, and my husband loved his red beans & rice. 

Personally, I see this as a great happy hour hangout spot. Dunno that I'd come for a speedy dinner. (We parked on the street, and I fed the meter for 2 hours. We got out and had only 5 minutes left on it. We didn't realize we were there that length of time, and we were actually shocked it took that long. Not a big deal for us that day, but still a surprise.) It's a casual, laid-back place. I'd recommend only coming if that's exactly what you want.

The only place in Nashville during Labor Day weekend that we actually had a chance to get a drink ... it was some beer stand in between the two parts of the establishment, and although it was over priced (due to no wait) it was well worth it... we have been hopping from one place to the next and have NOT had a single drink until this bar ...

great performance by the band and I enjoyed the whole lay out of the place.
Stopped in quick for a beer. Music was decent bartenders were very slow and just moping around like everyone was bothering them. Had 1 each and left.

If I'm going to eat somewhere that has Pizza in the name, then my first meal there will undoubtedly be pizza, and Soulshine does not disappoint when it comes to the pies! 

Although the salad was a little lackluster, the Carnivore pie more than made up for any short comings there. There were 3 of us, and we all wanted something different, but that was not an issue. They have a massive collection of gourmet pies with a plethora of ingredients. They have an individual 8" that's more than enough for any normal individual. That's an option I think all pizza places should have! All 3 of us made our selections and were not disappointed with the outcome. GREAT PIZZA!

Although someone needs to teach the bartender how to pour a stout, the Guinness was cold and reasonably priced.

The service was also very good considering it was a very busy Saturday lunch crowd with a private party filling the entire upstairs.

The only reason I didn't give it a 5 stars is that 5 stars represents as good as it gets, and that's not possible with pizza. A better one comes along every day.

Great Lower Broadway spot with live music and wide open windows to enjoy the weather. Would get the coveted five-star rating if they served Ketel One. #KetelTastesBetter The only food item we ordered on this visit was beer battered mushrooms, which were fine... Typical frozen bar fare, but the pork and ribs on the menu smelled good on their way out to other tables.

I've been to TPAC twice and have had great experiences both times. I saw The Nutcracker a couple of years ago and saw Beauty & the Beast this evening. Loved tonight's show, although I'm not a fan of sitting in a theater full of small children, that's the price you pay to see a Disney production. (Even though Beauty & the Beast is from MY generation! Lol) I like that they allow food in the theater now although I did not want to wait in the concession line. Seating is awesome from anywhere it seems. I have already purchased tickets to see We Will Rock You in November and I can't wait to see it!

This was a GREAT PLACE if you have your family with you! It was our first trip to Nashville and we had our ten year old son with us. Many of the places with live music only allow children under 21 until 6pm. Wildhorse was open until 10pm for kids. Great live band and line dancing lessons between sets. Food was good too!! Really recommend this place for families!!

One star is way too much for this establishment. After paying a $6 cover charge to enter the restaurant/bar I was informed that guests under 21 years of age do not pay cover. Please explain to me how someone of age- who pays to DRINK alcohol pays to enter. In my experience it's the other way around. Guests of age who will spend more money and tip workers do not pay to enter. This is absolutely ridiculous. Not to mention paying $6 per guest to enter and wait 45 minutes to be seated to eat. This is the most overrated place in Nashville I have been. As a veteran visiting 2-3 times a year to my favorite city, I will not be returning to this dump. Can you say tourist trap?

Long story short. crowded area. bouncer pushes me out of his way and into somebody else.  Not knowing it was a bouncer, I step backward pushing him back.

after talking to him, a manager, and a cop I was escorted out. 

certain people in my party couldn't even return to the table to pay their tab.

mountains out of molehills kind of thing from a security team that suffers from little man syndrome. Maybe he didn't have time to finish watching the movie "Road House" for the millionth time while day dreaming that he could have made it in the secret service if they just gave him one shot.

the chicken fingers were on point tho.

Five stars for entertainment! There was a cover to get in which our group originally found strange considering EVERY bar on the strip has live music with no cover or drink minimum...but turns out this was a more legitimate band, not a young group trying to get their name out there. Great musicians and the lineup thy have for the summer includes a number of radio favorites. The line dancing was a unique twist to the evening considering we did not find any other bars doing it. They had multiple dancers there to show you the steps. They keep them fairly simple so everyone can pick it up, but spice them up so each one is a little different from the next. The decor with all the horses is pretty cool too and makes for many photo-shoot opportunities.

Three stars for food. I was way less than impressed with the meal. The brisket was decent, pulled pork was bland but fell apart nicely, and Kraft makes a wayyyy better Mac and cheese. I think I would have been better off sticking to the apps menu. The spicy fries pickles were delicious!

But surely make this a stop on you trip! The whole experience was one of my favorite parts of the weekend. Everyone needs to line dance at least once to live country music!

Hit or miss on the food and service

The first time we are here the food was awesome.  The service was very good.  The music was great.  However, it was mid day, mid week, and they were really not busy.  We ate ribs and fries and everything was really good.

The second time was a completely different story.

It was a weekend so I called ahead.  I asked if there was a wait.  The answer I got was "it's first come first serve."  That didn't really answer my question to so I rephrased: is there anyone waiting for tables?  The answer was "no". This turned out to be a white lie just to get me to drive overs there.  The reality is that no one was "waiting" because it was just wall to wall people with everyone milling around playing the role of vulture jumping on any seat that opened up.  It was total chaos, and In my opinion that was a very dishonest way to get us in the door.

Once we did finally get seated (no where near any music stage) our server wasn't exactly warm and friendly.  There were a number of us so we ended up splitting in two tables (one of 4 and one of 5) across the room from one another.  She served both tables and oddly enough one table's food was awesome (pulled pork sandwich, and pork tenderloin melt) and one table's food was ehhhh at best (okay ribs, onion rings and fried mushrooms with golden outsides and undercooked veggies on the inside).

The best part was our waitress tells us at the end that she was nice enough to not put the 18% gratuity for parties of 8 or more.  Which is really funny since she treated each table completely separately taking our orders at different times, bringing the food at different times.

If it hadn't been for our good first experience I might have given them 2 stars.

Go to any other honky tonk on Broadway. I am a local and after this weekend I will no longer be a customer and no longer recommend this bar. Poorly owned. They treat their employees with little to no respect, even as far as allowing patrons themselves to see it blatantly. Once I heard how the owners allow their bar to be ran I immediately scratched Rippys off my places to frequent. Awful, if you are visiting Nashville go to Acme, or The Valentine, or Nudies!

Really cool place.  Local musicians, great menu, cool building, but the location can make things a little difficult.  Not their fault though.

Usually sit upstairs and it's a great place for a date especially with the other locations nearby to visit afterward.

Always sit in Trent's section.  Always does a great job and takes great care of his patrons.
Loved our food! Cool huuge place with lots of music! We will be back to vusit soon I hope!

Wasn't expecting cover charge. Great to get in and dance and enjoy music while we waited for our table. Service was good but spotty ... Partially due to extremely loud environment. Not a place to have a conversation. But dancing and entertainment great. Their nachos are great.

Walking around Nashville all day can make you very hungry. I stopped in to refuel for a quick bite. Everyone was incredibly friendly. Our waitress had shared with us that she was tired and does not usually work the day shift. We put in an order for a bbq brisket appetizer and ordered lemonade. They have this deal where you can purchase a plastic boot drink and will give free lemonade refills and the boot is yours to take home. Unlimited refills sounded like a good idea, with all the walking we were doing around Nashville. It costs about $10.

After receiving our drinks we seemed to be waiting a good thirty min for our appetizer. It almost seemed like they had forgotten that we were there. We notified them and our appetizer was on the house! The bbq beef brisket was really good and flavorful. It was nothing that I had really tried before. I am from up north and we don't eat much brisket. 

They also have a gift shop attached to the restaurant lots of tees and southern gear.  Everything looked incredibly clean, including the bathrooms. I enjoyed all the horse décor throughout the restaurant. This seems like a really happening place. We sat in the bar area but, there is a restaurant area with a stage and a huge area to dance.

Our server was quick and attentive about refilling our drinks, which was especially impressive since we were there during a football game and it was pretty packed.  

The food was meh.

The upstairs was open air (translate: HOT and muggy because it's September).  

The music, however, was fantastic.  Is there a better bar song than "Sweet Caroline" live?  I think not.  

It has a very college-y feel to it.  I would probably try some place else next time.
Great little find. Staff is friendly and food was excellent. Definitely will be going back as the music is Amazing.

Walked in and stood at entryway for 10 minutes as soon as a group of white males entered a hostess practically skipped to greet them almost immediately. When they mentioned I was there first she deopped her smile and begrudgingly looked at me as I asked if a particular menu item had peanuts. She told me to go to the bar to inquire whether a desert had peanuts on it. I exited the restaurant.  Racist.
Great environment and big dance floor. Loved the souvenir boot glasses you can take home and their Mac and cheese is delicious! The corn too!! Great for families and everyone is friendly!!
Thirty minute wait on a Saturday night. But it went pretty fast. Great service And good food. Food came out pretty fast! The apple moonshine will hit you fast!

We recently visited Nashville and made a pilgrimage to Broadway to see the sights. My husband and I both decided we wanted BBQ --there are several bbq restaurants on Broadway ---- so we flipped a coin and decided on Rippy's  We were immediately seated.  With an open air bar/restaurant it was really pretty hot in there but for early September I suppose we shouldn't expect more.  There was a trio playing when we got there.  Certainly none of them are not destined in the near future to receive any CMA awards.  But-- I ordered the pulled pork and my husband order the half rack of ribs.  When our orders were brought out there was enough food on each plate to feed a family of 4!  My husband thoroughly enjoyed his ribs saying they were extra tasty and really didn't need any sauce.  My pulled pork was ok--- not much flavor.  I tried adding the bbq/vinegar sauce and it helped.  I guess I had something else in mind when I ordered it.  The side of mac & cheese sort of tasted like it came from a box.  My husband said the coleslaw was ok but he focused on trying to finish his ribs.  If you are hungry you absolutely should stop here!.

Great music to enjoy any day of the week.  Friendly and attentive waitresses serve with pleasant smiles.   Substandard food.   Don't recommend coming here for a nice meal.  Salad served in a dixy cup/bowl.  Plastic cutlery. Curly fries no better than what you get from the frozen food section at supermarket.   Great BBQ sauce at the table. Live music made this dining experience worthwhile.

Pretty mediocre spot overall. I ordered a steak after they were out of two other dishes. The food took an hour to come out and was incorrectly cooked for two of us and looked suspiciously like it had been cut in half even though we ordered different cuts cooked to different temperatures. It's not a steakhouse so not a big deal I guess. The side was a twice baked potatoe, which was unlike anything I'd ever had in a bad way. Neither one of us had more than a couple bites. Gave a star for the live music which was decent as well as for our waiter who recommended a solid IPA.

This is strictly based on the upstairs bar and music.  Everytime I come to Nashville, I have a great time at this place.  I mean the whole block is awesome, but this place in particular is my favorite.  Much more intimate than some of the other music venues in the area, plus the band always plays a decent variety of music.  Crowd has always been great too.
Food came in 5 minutes. Very dry ribs, not good at all. Even messeg up the fries and onion rings. Waitress did not really care and was just stressed. Stay away.

Sunday evening wasn't too busy. Love performances and in between the performances, the saloon did line dancing classes for the audience. Overall, it's a very fun atmosphere with clever statues of horses in funny positions located around the establishment.

We had the fried pickles, which I highly recommend. They weren't too fried and the ranch dressing had a slight kick that made the combo delicious. 

My gf and I weren't too hungry afterwards so we shared a Pick 2 of brisket and pork with collard greens and Mac n cheese. The collard greens weren't that good in truth. It must be something they add to make them stand out. Instead, they weren't the traditional greens I wanted. The Mac and cheese was delicious.
Line dancing with the girls. DJ played request. Got there before cover being charged. Had some appetizers and drinks. Great fun had by all! Don't miss the ceiling horses.

Terrible, terrible, terrible!!! As a patron that actually lives in Nashville, I will NEVER ever step foot back in this establishment, nor will anyone in my party and then some.
