We were there for 2 hours, had the worst service I have ever experienced in a restaurant (saw our server for a total of approx 4 min in the 2 hours).....I even had to get up from the table and go to the bar to purchase a drink. The food is mediocre at best. If you are going to charge high end prices for a burger then I suggest you don't precook them in the kitchen and then warm them up so they are over well done and crunchy!!! Disgusting!!! Tourists....I really really recommend going elsewhere!! I am one to give a raving review when deserved, but it was the worst $130 (for 3 people) that was spent!

I would say food is pretty good but not great. Super fun at night, live music on the weekends. Would recommend going there for a lively atmosphere  and more of a upbeat kind of place. Pepperoni bread is great and so are pork nachos.

Ok this place is amazing. I have seen some post that day it's a little "dirty". Hello ITS A HONKY TONK!  Ribs were great beer was cold and also seen some well behaving children so it was kid friendly. Had the seasoned curly fries and also Mac and cheese. They had a roll on the plate that was like crack!  Music was fantastic. Was like going to a concert and you just have to tip!  Highly recommended.
Hands down the worse BBQ I've ever had. I've had beef jerky that was more moist and flavorful then the brisket they serve.

Wenn du country music magst ist das der perfekte Ort für dich. Nicht so überteuert wie die Bars downtown. Burger für 6$ und n Bier für 4$ . Nicjt vergessen ein paar dollar scheine als tip für die band mitzunehmen. Would go there again.

Ribs are of the dry rub style. Baken beans were good and so was the cole slaw. Mac and cheese was ok. Strong drink pours. I believe there is better ribs in Nashville. Peg Leg is better, but a bit of a walk from Broadway.
Amazing food. Try the pulled pork and mac and cheese....awesome!! Live music while you're eating...can't be beat. Satisfied customer here.

Good food. Great ambience. Awesome dancing lessons an s dance floor. Very energetic. Good for kids. Can get crowded so get there early or expect to wait. Had the brisket and was really good. Spicy bbq wings were amazing with the spicy bbq sauce. Would highly recommend for music an fun!

Seriously, I am dumbfounded by the service at this restaurant. It took a solid 15 minutes for a server to even see that we were sitting down and ask if we wanted something to drink. We ordered food. He wrote nothing down and our order came pretty fast (the ONLY perk). It took another 10 minutes, 2 servers, and a bus boy to get utensils. So by the time I got a fork, my ribs were cold. They messed up not 1 but 2 side orders, they put in the corrected order, which didn't come out till we were done eating the rest of our cold food. Our new side orders finally came out and my fries were cold. Then, I ordered a Yuengling, and a miller light came out.

Despite all of this, we were charged for everything we got, which, if you ask me, they could have at least comped a round of beers. Negative. 

Did I mention it's my birthday?

Not my favorite theater, but I like that it was small and that the chairs were comfy. Not fond of the bathrooms being downstairs. The customer service there was excellent!!! It's a small and cute venue.

My husband and I mistakenly came here before a concert one night, since we were in a hurry and I was too impatient to wait in the line at Jack's BBQ. I ordered the half rack of ribs. It came with fries and baked beans (my choices). The fries had no flavor, the beans had burned gross flavor, and the ribs tasted like what I imagine the nastiest thing you could imagine would taste like, if you put ketchup "BBQ" sauce on them. I am absolutely not kidding. I took one bite of the ribs, and stopped. My husband ate his pulled pork sandwich, but he was starving and knew we would be at a concert for four more hours. The fries had no flavor and we had to ask for utensils and salt, which they were out of... I regretted not wanting to wait at Jack's BBQ almost instantly upon walking into Rippy's. It was LOUD. It was also full of drunk people who didn't know how to dance, and obviously didn't care about the flavor of their food! The server was the LONE saving grace, because she was pleasant, if not the best. Of course the place was packed with drunkards, so it was hard to even walk through the joint. If you want music, Rippy's is okay, if you want FOOD, go to Jack's BBQ across the street.

Three levels, multiple rooms most with love bands. Definitely a cool summer place to hang. Food was pretty good 4/5. Gratuity was added on 6 people, not reflected on the check, strange... Service poor. Pretty standard any city main drag restaurant, hit or miss

My fiancé and I recently moved to Nashville and were looking to find a dive bar similar to one we liked back home. We passed this place constantly but just got a chance to go this past weekend. We walked in with a group of 5 and easily found a seat and got our beers. We ordered a few appetizers and burgers and everything was awesome. It was karaoke night, which we hadn't expected, but we had the BEST time. The crowd was in their 20s-30s for the most part, and everyone was friendly and interactive. The bartender was amazing and was running the whole bar by herself without any issues. I think her name was Hannah? She was probably the best bartender I've ever encountered. It's nice to go to a dive bar but receive fantastic service. This place will definitely become a regular hangout for us!

This was the worst dinner on vacation. I went to Rippy's with my boyfriend. After getting dismissed by the snarky hostess-not hostesses in the booth at the door, we sat upstairs and got ignored. When our male server finally arrived to wait on us, I forget his name but he had a man-bun. He spent more time flirting with the snarky girls at the door than he did taking care of his customers. We ordered the jalapeño poppers, they were a disappointment. Well done, fried jalapeño slices is the best way to describe them. My boyfriend and I shared a plate of ribs, they were dry and chewy and gave us food poisoning. $52 spent on bad food that lead to a day and a half of stomach pains and liquid shits. Just avoid this frat house soup kitchen at all costs.

Twin Kegs definitely has the best bar food in town as well as the cheapest beer! The only drawback is sometimes it can be hit or miss. The karaoke can be overbearing if your not into that stuff. Great food, just a gamble at times depending who may be working. 

Staff is all very friendly, some just handle the pressure of being busy a lot better.

Foods alright. For the wait you'd expect good BBQ! But as other reviewers have said it is a tourist trap. The line dancing and live entertainment was fun. My family was visiting from California so we were walking by and decided to try it out. Ordered the brisket and sausage, brisket was so dry! If you want some southern BBQ head down to Edelys BBQ they know how too cook it!

Super fast service, perfect pricing, and really good food. The ribs were pretty damn good and I could roll around in their delicious onion rings forever.  This place isn't the best BBQ joint I've ever been too but if you find yourself on the strip, it's definitely worth a peek!

I had been to Nashville with a friend last year, and we were going to eat at Rippy's, but he decided he didn't want to listen to live music. (I know, you are in Nashville FOR the music.) So we didn't get a chance to eat there. I went back on Sunday, 5/7/17 with my nephew and his mom. The music was great, and the food was good. I got a pulled chicken salad, and the corn cakes. Both were good. They weren't the best in the world, but I would go there again and I would definitely recommend this restaurant to others.

First off let me start by saying tonight would have been my first enjoyable fight night if all of the proceeding didn't happen. Brooke our server was taking great care of us and was not at all upset with us coming in at 4pm to stay until the fight at 11. When our friends came though everything got combined on to one tab that I personally split up at the end... you can see the pictures attached. Also we got autograted without our knowledge. I would have appreciated it being written down somewhere or us being warned since we were all bartenders and know how to take care of other service members. Nothing was an issue until a Middle Aged Caucasian security guard kicked out one of our Hispanic friends for reacting after he was pushed by the guy who was plowing through the crowd. This guy had previous been fired from Broadway Brewhouse for the exact same act to the exact same guy... fishy... following him being told he was "lucky they let him get his things" the security staff did not let my friend pay for his tab and just told him to leave. Upon hearing this I spoke to the manager Steven who took care of this problem and covered his tab after we pointed out that this seemed to us like a racist attack. The fight made it crazy inside so through trying to talk to the kicked out friend outside and still trying to hold down our table inside some other group members were having problems getting passed security to get back upstairs to our table. This caused a problem when I split our bill at the end. Not only was there a random bud light that appeared on our check but now we had the check of a friend who was told they couldn't come back up to sit with us. So in comes "manager" number 2. As whoever this man was walked up to our table in his trucker hat and rippys tshirt he immediately took an aggressive stance when my boyfriend and I put it to his attention how poor their customer service had been towards us trying to correct a misunderstanding all night. He fought with my boyfriend over at 37 dollar tab, picture also included but note this tab is not autograted like the rest. He claimed that WE should have done a better job in trying to get our friend past security and that since WE did not do a better job it was our responsibility to pick up this tab. I would have had no problem doing this except for the fact that we had been treated poorly by this man now as well and we were the last people standing in the restaurant. All of our friends had given us cash and left and it was not until I was looking at the check again did I realize that they had put an autograt on. I then broke up the pretty much fight that the manager was having with my boyfriend to say if they took the autograt off we would still take care of our server and pick up the whole tab. He sent our server back with a new adjusted check without the 37 dollar tab because the autograt was 56. After we finally got our tabs split and paid for I was very upset, almost to the point of tears that I should be dealing with something like this on a night that should have been fun and relaxing. All in all I have come to the conclusion that I will never be back to Rippy's nor will I send any of my bar guests there. On Monday I will be contacting someone above the people who were inside the building tonight, and that their security is racist.

Fun atmosphere but but the food was terrible.  I got the ribs, which were suggested to me as the "best item on the menu" and they were pretty underwhelming - lacked flavor and were cold.  I would only go there to listen to some music and hang out in the upstairs bar on a sunny day.
This place is huge. We got to watch a live performance, mostly because it took so long to get drinks and food. That being said, the drinks were delicious and the food was also.

This is one of the last dive bars left in Nashville. It's always been one of the best. It has shuffle board, allows smoking, and has some perfectly mediocre karaoke. It's great. What really sets this place apart though is the burger. I usually have their BBB (Big Bad Burger) it's two patties with traditional fixings and bacon that they put under the cheese. Today, I had the single patty BB and it was as good as always. It's a perfectly seasoned patty that I believe they cook in a frying pan. It just tastes like exactly what you want from a dive bar burger. It lingers. 

I tell anyone who will listen that Twin Kegs has one of the best burgers in town. Despite all the new fancy burger places popping up, this one still holds its own. Highly recommend.

Check out my instagram @tennesseeburgergram

A review solely based on the music would say "5 stars all the way - great mixture of artists -especially if you stay for 3 or 4 hours like we did - you won't be disappointed. And, if you're lucky, they'll pull the adorable 9 year old girl up on the stage to bust out the tunes like a 20 year pro." 

And the review that factors in service and food would go something like this: Despite us spending so long there we were definitely earning our keep in the drink department - that was until our waiter's shift ended an no one eveeerrrr came back to check on us for more drinks. Our first waitress was a little rough around the edges but I can roll with that. Maybe they were just trying to tell my parents and I that we had had enough to drink: "cut 'em off!" 

As for the food - the reviews are right - meh, meh, meh. I had the pulled pork salad and was disappointed in the lack of flavor and moistness in the meat. My bloody marys were a-okay. To add some kick, I took it upon myself to add a dose of the tableside BBQ. 

All this to say, Rippy's is great if you're thirsty and want to hear music. If you're hungry...just keep drinking till that feeling subsides.

This review is based on the food and service -- not the bar or music. Ordered the brisket sandwich, coleslaw, and lemonade. The lemonade was the worst I've ever had. The brisket and coleslaw was very mediocre. The service was mediocre and unfriendly.

This place was alright. You have to order towards the back and then find a seat. Which can be a hassle if you are going with a group of people. They do have extra BBQ sauces at the table if you need to add more flavor to your food. The ribs that day were super dry and everyone at my table ended up just taking the food home because we just were not satisfied at the moment. It was however great for our  midnight cravings after a long day.

Excellent food, service, drinks and band! My new favorite on Broadway. The spicy chili wings were crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. I recommend the Tropical Hootie drink...delicious! The band upstairs was amazing! Can't wait to go back!

If you're looking for good food AND entertainment, this is the place. Refreshing from so many of the honky tonks that are focused on drinking only. Wonderful pork loin. Band was fabulous!  My new favorite place in Nashville.

My wife and I stopped into Wildhorse to take in the tourist trap ambience, and grab some dinner. The wings were just ok, but the bartender, Bernie, made our evening a true delight.

If you go to the wildhorse, seek out Bernie, and ask him to make you a Jedi shot!
The chicken fingers and fries were good. The music was very enjoyable and the second floor is lots of fun. Great ambiance.

This rating is based off atmosphere only as I didnt eat here. Went for line dancing and the band. $6 cover, worth it! Stayed for a couple hours learning the dance and watching the band. One of the highlights of my nashville!  Mustttt go!

The band and the wait staff were friendly. But I was not impressed with any of the food or drinks. Over Priced for what you received in the appitizer basket. I would not recommend this place if you would like good BBQ.

Four stars for the service and the room. I typically try to stay away from restaurants in hotels. However, the last day of the NFL Draft had just ended and 150,000 people where walking the downtown streets. The restaurant is located walking distance from downtown but far enough away to be crowded but not overwhelmed with people. The food is adequate. Mother special but not terrible. Given the crowds elsewhere, I do not regret the decision to eat there, but I won't return.
Was ok brisket. Music was great. Great location on the corner there. Went again early Friday night for a beer. It was the first place and last place I had a beer when I arrived In Nashville.

Great place, if you are staying in the music valley area and you don't visit the palace, you missed good food good music ,great staff@ Kelsey from MonkeysEyebrow Kentucky. We visited for 10 days and visited the palace 4X, could not get enough, sure go downtown fight the silly crowd and then come to the palace and have a really fun time.

First time in Nashville, and first time stopping in to Rippy's. Five of us ate, and none of us were IMPRESSED! Overpriced mediocre food. Service was borderline insulting. Waitress brought an ice tea to the table, we all looked at each other wondering why. When she came back I stated we didn't order this, she immediately got an attitude. Later when she brought the right drinks, I commented why is the wine in plastic cups? She replied, It's Carlo Rossi, does it really matter. Seriously, there are too many places to eat and drink along Broadway for this type of service. We will definitely return to Nashville, but will skip Rippy's!
Not very diversity, I stuck out like a sore thump (Asian) but everything was great, I had fun. Deff come back again.

We visited here for a private event. Very nice spot. Three levels of fun! Waitstaff was excellent, they had line dancing "lessons" and even hosted a moonshine tasting. Look forward to stopping in next time we're in Nashville to see this spot on a "regular " night.
The upstairs patio is a great spot to see the strip but unfortunately the band was amateurish and the pulled pork was mediocre at best.  With so many choices it's not worth going here.

Super laid back environment with great live music, pizza, and beer. The roof top is great for a Sunday funday or any other good weather day...for that matter. The service has never disappointed either.

So I came back... I liked my 2nd time much better. The food was rather well balanced (not the salty well like last time). Now that I figured out the parking situation, I found this place rather convenient.

Ribs and chilly. That is DEFINITELY the way to go! My friend had the fries and chicken sandwich and she said it was awesome. The best part was the live music, and also the ribs. I expected them to be dripping in BBQ sauce, but they were dry rubbed and so juicy. The meat came right off of the bone and there was barely any fat on them. If You love ribs, you will love Rippy's.

We have been here to see a plethora of productions! I have gone with family and friends both on various trips! Every show that we have seen has been incredible! The auditorium is beautiful and the facility in general is always clean! The wait for Valet parking can be very lengthy sometimes, but there are quite a few people! This is a blessing to have in Tennessee! I will definitely be back soon and I would encourage anyone to go!
Awesome meal great music. Well worth the wait to get in.  Make sure you're before 7pm to avoid the cover charge

I was excited when I saw the menu at Soulshine pizza. We started with a shrimp nachos appetizer, which was good. Then my wife and I ordered a 16" pizza; she had "everything but the kitchen sink" on one half, and I had the Athena on the other. My wife asked for no sauteed onions or peppers on her half. Unfortunately they must have thought that was for the whole pizza, because my half had none. To make matters worse, the pizza had almost no sauce on it. As a result, my half was nothing but mozzarella and feta cheese with black olives and a few small shrimp. I was very disappointed: my pizza was dry and almost tasteless. For the first time in years I am not interested in eating the leftover pizza. I would have returned my pizza but my wife liked her half, so I give Soulshine 2 rather than 1 stars. On the plus side, the service was good, but parking is a pain, even during off hours.

Stop in for a yummy frozen lemonade slushy!!  
Friendly bartenders! Locals are super nice!! Great place! Lots of local tastes here!! Don't forget to try the moonshine!! You won't be disappointed. Smooth!

Place was dead on the first floor late last Sunday evening, however that gave us the opportunity to learn about some of the places to catch while in town. Bartender was super knowledgable and engaging. Just what we needed at the time. Will likely give it another chance at a later time.

Worst place I have ever been . We were there last Friday. My friends and i called 3 separate times during the week wanting to set a reservation for about 15. Each time they told us oh yeah we will be able to seat you. We showed up Saturday night at 730 (after calling 2 hours in advance like they wanted). It took over an hour and a half to get a table. We went up to the bar and started drinking but it was an absolute mess to get a table. Finally we pushed one together ourselves on the patio. The waitress asked me if we needed anything like menus, I told her a bigger table and we had already been waiting an hour and a half. She told us she couldn't help us and walked away. After we got a table, it took a ridiculously long time for any server to help us, she got our drink orders and disappeared. I ordered pizza, and it was so loud from the AWESOME live band playing that I honestly didn't think she heard me. It took another 45 minutes to get food and the pizza wasn't even that good. Sure the chick was nice, but there is no reason that this whole situation had to happe. I am extremely disappointed I'm the staff and do not think I will ever be returning after that experience.

Great place.  Huge inside.  We had 30 bus loads in our party (1600 people) and we fit in there well and the doors were still open. 

Bbb chicken and beef were very good.  Pork was a okay.  Three floor place with a good view from almost everywhere. Not a country music fan but I would go back many times over.
The shows are fine. Basically hit or miss, but the valet is absolutely ridiculous. Do not valet or it will absolutely ruin your night.

This was our last night in Nashville and we wanted to experience some live music with our three kids. We were a little apprehensive at first, but the manager noticed us right away checking out the place and made a point to encourage us to stay for a bit. So glad she did! The kids learned a line dance and had a blast! Food and music was great! The manager even got a guitar for my daughter to hold to pose for a picture. Very welcoming atmosphere, thanks for a fun time

Originally, had such a good experience. We went back to get shirts. Joey, the bouncer was so great, over and above, both times we went. Zach was also a good bartender and had good customer service. When we went back for our shirts because we loved it so much, Amber was extremely rude. Exhaled because we asked for shirts and had someone else get them for her. Her attitude completely put us off. Both being in customer service we were extremely disappointed. Five stars for our first experience but one for our last.

Went here twice while on vacation this past weekend and my experiences were like night and day. First day with Kirby was absolutely AMAZING, knew how to cater to her bar guests and was sweet as could be! Coming from a service background it's always refreshing to have exceptional service when going out. She definitely earned her $100 tip on a $175 bill- I even went over to the ATM to get out more cash because she was that good. 

The next day was beyond disappointing - our bartender was extremely rude and had the audacity to slam her tip bucket in front of my seat and give me an attitude letting me know that they "only worked for tips" after I ordered a drink and only gave enough to cover the drink - I pulled what cash I had out of my pocket and had every intention of going into my purse to grab a couple ones. Not to mention the fact we had been tipping all day (we were in a group of 10) and never in my life would I not tip my server due to the fact that I bartend back home. Also - automatic gratuity was added to each check every time we closed out. 

My advice? Ask for Kirby!!!! Best service I've ever had! Wish I could give her 5 stars. Not worth going if she's not there!

I was in town again and brought a group of 4 here.  Not bad.  Yazoo beers available, and a small selection on tap.  Had the ribs and fries with cole slaw.  All decent.  2 of our party didn' t think the ribs were that good.  Not bad, just ok good.  You could do a lot worse for barbecue.
Good ribs and cornbread. The collard greens left little to desire, very watery for my personal taste. This place was good and worth the stop.

Good atmosphere. Terrible service. The bartender checked in on us every 45 minutes. She proceeded to sing on stage and then text on her phone leaving us wanting the bill and waiting for it for 40 minutes. Now she's at the punching bag game as we sit and wait without service for going on an hour.

Great beer selection, delicious pulled pork...although they are know for the full rack of ribs.

Visit the second floor open bar when the weather is nice for a good people warch in experience backed by a vibrant, live band...so pick a table by the street!
I came here while I was in Nashville. I had the 3 meat combo of pork, brisket, and sausage with 2 side orders. Good food at reasonable prices.

This is a great small venue to attend a concert.  I've never tried the food, so I can't rate how it might or might not be.  As far as the sound quality is concerned, the acoustics are outstanding and there does not appear to be a bad seat or standing area in the house.  I saw Randy Houser and Lee Brice here in February 2013 during the week of the annual Country Music Radio Seminar, and the house was packed and the show was great.

If you ever get the chance, it is definitely worth it to catch a show at the Wildhorse.

Stopped in here with my nephews hockey team and families (large party - ~30 total) on Saturday night and it was perfect! They accommodated us well and we got to sit mostly together near the stage. The entertainment was great, line dancing was a blast and the staff was (mostly) friendly. The third floor had a bunch of games that kept the boys occupied while we all drank and enjoyed the music. However, The food is limited and wasn't great. Everyone raves about the fried pickles but I didn't see what all the hype was about, they just tasted like normal pickles to me. The four star rating is mostly because the food wasn't great and our server suggested a drink to us that was $16 because of a souvenir glass that we weren't informed of. $16!! For one drink! If you are offering a guest a special drink, you need to let them know so they aren't blindsided. I would've ordered something else if I knew the price.

Food was quite subpar. Served stouffer's Mac and cheese, cheap canned baked beans, and boiled then shredded chicken breast with liquid smoke to make it see like real bbq. I did think the cornbread and pulled pork were decent. We were also seated and serviced surprisingly quick.

Rippy's on Broadway is what Nashville is all about: live local musicians playing classic country tunes in a rollicking and stomping acoustic manner while patrons enjoy delicious barbecue and beers. Our waiter was excellent, just materializing with a fresh Coke for me everytime mine got a little low, and the staff as a whole seemed on top of things, even if that meant carrying a dozen trays of bbq upstairs in a feat of phsyics I'm still not sure I understand. The food was very good southern barbecue, but the highlight for sure was the music. Two first floor rooms allow for multiple acts to perform and the one that we sat by was a male/female duo of early 20's country performers doing well by Johnny & June with their classic country covers. If you're looking for great food and an even better atmosphere, Rippy's will do right by you. Highly recommended.

We've been here a few times and it's great for what it is: hole in the wall smoky bar with really good burgers.  It's been awhile since we've been there so we decided to give it a shot last night.  First, we ordered a pitcher of Miller Lite. It was flat.  Then the server asked us if we were ready to order. We were waiting on friends. When we finally ordered she said "our cook left and I'm not sure if/when he's coming back".... what?  She said she could cook up some tater tots for us though.  We won't be going back...
Good pizza and great music on Sunday nights! Apparently if you know how to play an instrument you can come and jam w the band! Anyways great ambiance, a lot of space! Definitely will be coming back!!

Good food, reasonable prices, and great entertainment. I had the pork loin melt sandwich and onion rings and both were 5 stars. My wife had the pulled pork and coleslaw - both good, but not great. Entertainment was very good and the staff friendly and efficient. Well worth your time and money!

If you enjoy having crap food with your client go to this sewage plant! What's really fun is when you get there before 10, you get to sit down and eat then some jacked up washout from Afgani special forces, a joke whithin it's own right, comes over and "cards" you in the middle of your meal to verify age then throw your i.d. back at your face, very classy!  

What I would advise doing with your wallet is instead of directly funding terrorism, go across the street to Roberts, where the locals hang, and avoid this place managed by some miscreant who has no regard for the rule of law and or any level of decency.  

Btw: the security bouncers might someday "mess with the wrong Marine" and might want to confirm their bloodtype for their next visit to the ER.

Ok.  If you seen how the Wildhorse Saloon was back in the 90s compared to NOW..........It's CHANGED A LOT and I would say for the worse!  I didn't move to TN until 2004; after moving, I decided to try out the Wildhorse Saloon and I was a bit impressed because I was getting introduced to line dancing and I was just dancing for the fun of it.  It seems after going to other clubs around Nashville or Middle TN such as Kickers Country Club or Silverados (which was an awful place) or travelling outside of TN, my days of going to Wildhorse Saloon was DECREASING a lot because these other clubs were different and they were honky tonk places and the line dancing was a bit better!

The young kids being out on the floor was/is a HUGE PROBLEM because they are running around the floor while dancers are dancing.  Parents, you need to be around your kids and set some boundaries!  Too many teens coming out on the floor and staying on the floor while dancers are dancing is ANOTHER PROBLEM.  Wildhorse Saloon, you guys need to set some boundaries!

The dance floor, from what I'm hearing, is decreasing.................WHY???????????

It's more touristy and more of a restaurant and concert venue!

I haven't been to the Wildhorse Saloon in months and the only reason I would go back is for CMA fest because those country music fans KNOW LINE DANCES!!!!!!  Other than that, I don't go back!

Was on a road trip across the states when we decided to stop and hang here for the night. We ordered chicken wings, a mushroom Swiss burger (add jalapeños), and a local IPA. Wings and burger were pretty solid, as in I would order it again. The service and the music at the place is what sold it. Our waitress was polite and helpful. So if you're looking for a nice place to sit back and enjoy some good food and some of the Nashville vibes, check this place out. Shoutout to Josie and her service!

If you want to see the band, you either have to make that explicit, or maybe you just seat your self. Hard to know because the hostesses stick their nose in an iPad and hardly look at you when you come in, let alone talk to you. I know all these places are just for tourists, but does it really have to be such an assembly line?

As for the food, we all had the ribs with sides. The potato salad and turnip greens were good, but the ribs were pretty tough and bland. Underwhelming.

Wow!  I really wanted to review this place with five stars but the waitress with the long blonde hair stole or lost the last 3 and probably $20 dollars of my money.  My wife and I arrived just as the band was coming on and the waitress got to us when she could, but it really wasn't even busy.  THe band was great and the atmosphere in the palace is down home country with a lots of kitsch.  The menu was simple, almost rustic, but fun and added to the overall experience.  The waitress would show up once in while or when I raised my hand and would hurriedly, frenetically, take my order and dart away.  When it came time to pay our check, I pulled out 2 twenties and our waitress put one on top of the other but so the bottom one showed and clipped them to her clipboard with the check on top as she hurried away.  She came back later with only one twenty and asked if I wanted change as though I had given her my check money to get change with.  I and my wife at this point said "We gave you $40."  She said no, that the 20 was all she had.  My wife asked if she would look for it.  The waitress just glanced around where she was standing.  I gave her another 20 and she was on her way.  If I was home, I would have not given in so easily but we were far away from home and in a place where this waitress was a staple.  Before returning with our change, only $1.25, she hurried around fraternizing with some customers behind us, before she returned, never looking for our money and avoiding looking in our direction.   The sad part is that I really would have tipped her well.  I have respect for waiters, waitresses, and servers, and was one myself, so I know how hard it can be especially on a busy night; she would have received better than 20%.   
Please do not pay cash in this establishment and do not get the waitress with the long blonde hair.

Our first night in Nashville started off with a bang. Rippys was our first stop walking down Broadway. The live music from Northern Lights drew us right in. They are an excellent young group. Great guitarists and harmony vocals. Quintessential southern sounds. Food and beers were great too. We had a blast. In spite of numerous other similar establishments Rippys is the only one we went back to before heading home.

Went to Rippys as my second stop for the night, first time in Nashville, I wanted to check out multiple places. At the door the bouncer asked me for my ID as expected, I presented my ID, the bouncer then asked my friend and I if we had had any drinks tonight (keep in mind I had only had 2 beers prior to coming here so I was sober) and asked us to step back and approach him again, I'm not sure why. We did so, he then let us in but before we could make it to the bar he grabbed us and told us to leave, still not sure why. I'm a very understanding person so if we were drunk at all i would be very understanding, but we weren't by any means. But we proceded to go next door and enjoy the music and the food and drinks (the place next door was packed, Rippys was dead and now I know why) Long story short I'll never be back to Rippys.

I wish I could give it 6 stars! Absolutely the best place we ate in Nashville. Came during labor day weekend supper, and there was plenty of seating (waited 20 minutes to seat a party of 5). Waitress was right on top of things, friendly, and attentive. The kids food was excellent. BBQ Brisket Baked Potato was wonderful. Nashville hot chicken sandwich...oh my. I couldn't stop despite the fire in my mouth. 

In addition, the musicians were high quality. We did have to pay a cover charge on this occasion, but it was worth the concert that ensued. Line dancing was fun, and my 3 year old enjoyed making a fool of herself on the dance floor for the enjoyment of the room. Great for kids, great for adults, great for kids to see adults acting like kids.

We did not do Nashville until we went to Wild Horse. Be prepared to drop your shiniest penny before you're done, especially if you have a taste for souvenirs and booze.
Like others have said, the service is horrible.  Enough said.  Food is just OK,   will definitely not be rushing back here.  Curiosity got the best of us.

Like all the other bars that I've been to while in Nashville, this one does not disappoint.  It has the usual multi-level floors with a different live band playing at each one, along with open air seating.  If you happen to sit right by the edge where you can peer down to the street, it's a great view of Broadway street and you can people watch.

The service is good, our server was very attentive and I felt like I never had an empty bottle of beer.  I didn't get a chance to try any of their food but may do so the next time around.

I came to TPAC for the first time a week ago for a concert. It's a massive place situated downtown. I was in the James Polk theater. Loved that they offered concessions and alcohol. It was nice getting some adult beverages before the show. The staff was really friendly. However, there are two things I didn't like about TPAC: bathrooms + parking. The bathrooms are downstairs and feel like a sauna. Seriously, every woman in the bathroom kept complaining about how hot it was and it was miserable to wait in line to use the bathroom. Parking is crappy. There is not designated parking area so you have to pay to park in one of the nearby lots. I spent $25 on parking - that's crazy. That's almost the amount I paid for my concert ticket. Bleh!
Food was absolute garbage & the waitresses were hard on the eyes. Sound quality was amazing!
Went in on a company event. Nothing special. All day long people bragged about this place it I didn't find it impressive. Maybe if you go when it's open to public it's fun.
Super basic atmosphere. Music was enjoyable. Had chili with corn cakes. I though corn cakes wold not be pancakes but something to pick up with my fingers.

We stopped in here for lunch and it didn't disappoint. We started with the fried pickles which weren't my favorite but that's just a personal opinion. They were difficult to eat and the batter kept falling off. I had the cowboy burger at our servers suggestion and it was delicious. Spicy but great flavor. My boyfriend had the hot chicken and said it was great. Tommy was our server and was very friendly and knew the menu well. He kept our drinks full and we had good conversation with him as well. The atmosphere was awesome as well. We loved the decor and games. The music videos playing on stage was a neat touch as well

Blown away by Eileen Rose & The Silver Threads and John Englind & The Swingers.  Spent a great Saturday here - stopped in for a burger, heard that girl's voice and didn't want to leave.  Burger was great! Staff was friendly and service top notch.  Good prices.  Indoor and outdoor seating. Went to the Opry and these musicians were better than anyone we saw there. Easy parking.  A must for any Nashville visit.

Our group had a wonderful time at the Wildhorse. We wandered in during our detour down 2nd Avenue which is a good take in itself. Once you get off Broadway things are a little more civilized. 
We found 4 seats at their large, comfortable, and elegant bar. The bartender made a wonderful version of the Old Fashioned which I enjoyed. They also had decent wines by the glass. We hung around for the line dancing lesson which was a lot of fun whether you participate or just watch. 
This place is notably clean and quite large so there's plenty of room to sit  or dance. We liked the atmosphere at the bar where everyone was talking to each and sharing tips about where to go in Nashville. I will definitely go back to the Wildhorse next time I'm in town

Went on a Friday night around 7PM.  Nice space, good music and has potential but the need to work on a few things.  Although the place was less than half full they were already out of or low on items on the menu. 

The server did not let us know when we sat down that certain items were low so that if we were interested in those to let him know so he could reserve them.  Instead we sat and had appetizers and cocktails and by the time we ordered dinner they only had 2 pork shanks left ( not enough for those in our party that wanted them).

The table next to us came a half hour after us and placed their orders for the shank, which left us short.  Very disappointing and avoidable.  They told us they cook it ahead of time an only have a limited number available.  More the reason the server should have let us know.  

They were also out of the local yazoo beer!  For a Friday night they should have been better prepared!
All we did here was have a drink and the roasted Vidalia onion dip, and it was good. It is a Sunday after and empty so we are moving on to a more happening spot. It was good for what we wanted.

Loud music. We walked in and were completely ignored. You can go ahead and save yourself the literal headache of this restaurant. It's for young people. One band upstairs and one downstairs. It was obnoxious. We got frustrated and found someone to seat us. After 10 minutes of not being spoken to we left.
Our waitress Tayla was great, the food was great, and staff were friendly, professional and fast

We had a group of 10 and sat on the patio for their 1st day of serving brunch and we were thrilled we did! The apps were delicious, the bacon Bloody Mary was top notch, and the servers/band were all very welcoming and kind. To top it off - the prices are great!
Good burger and fries...quick and hot. Will definitely be there for lunch again. Also received a dollar off for checking in. When I showed the on screen coupon to the server she said no problem.

The wait was long, the food was cold, and if we hadn't waited so long to eat we probably would have left.  We ordered wings, fries, and a wrap,  the only thing that came out warm was the wrap which should not have been warm  quantity not quality

Meh. Bbq wrap was kind of dry and very oily. What's the worst thing? The amount of plastic used. Plastic cups, straws, disposable silver ware. Just an incredible amount of waste. Salad comes in a paper bowl. The only thing that doesn't get thrown away is the plastic basket your food comes in.

We come to Nashville all the time and we were looking forward to eating at someplace we've never been before. 

The music was great, food was awful and service was non-existent.  We made reservations for 6pm and arrived a few minutes before. They sat us right away and next to the stage which was great because Haleigh Martin was great!  It took 10 minutes before the server came to greet us after the had walked around our table numerous times without stopping to at least say hi.  When he finally stopped by, we ordered fried pickles, our meals, and a couple bar drinks.  The pickles came out quickly and dropped off by another server. We had no plates or silverware to eat. 20 minutes later still no plates, silverware, no drinks from the bar and the server was checking on every other table but ours. We stopped the manager to let him know of the issues were having and his response was "You are more than welcome to leave". What?!? He then proceeded to tell us they were short 2 servers so service is a little slow.  A little?!  A) That is not the customers problem and B) if you are short servers then you close sections and not continue to seat customers beyond what your staff can handle.  The manager did state he would take care of our meals, not what we were looking for but he did offer. 

We finally got our drinks and our meals. My son's girlfriend for a burger that was dry and she had to drown in ketchup to eat.  My son ordered the Smoke Stack Burger which was a huge mess but decent. I ordered their brisket meal that was over cooked and dry. It comes with fries, slaw (which was good) and their version of cornbread, which let's be honest is a glorified pancake that is burnt beyond recognition (Picture attached).  My husband got the Chicken Fried Chicken, the only good meal we got, it was so good he ate every bite.  


We never saw the server again after he dropped off our meals, we did order another round of drinks and yet again they didn't come out until we were done eating and ready to leave.  

We asked for our check. When the server finally dropped it off, all food was on the bill.  We called a different manager over this time because we couldn't find the first one we talked to. We repeated our issues from before as well as the meal issues.  We agreed to pay for our drinks (obviously) and my husbands meal because the rest of the meals were below satisfaction and not eaten.  This manager looked over at my son's GFs plate and said "doesn't look like she had a problem". Really?!? Do you not see it drowned in ketchup and less than half eaten?  She didn't even eat the fries.  

I would never recommend this place to anyone.  Even when others in our hotel would share where they've eaten and asking for suggestions we would tell them to not waste their time!

Awesome place to unwind with friends and family.multiple music areas for live music and great food. The BBQ is awesome, the staff equally awesome, the service impeccable, drinks are rocking it and Entertainment setting the bar really high. Love coming back to this place for mouth watering BBQ and drinks.

I visited the Wildhorse Saloon on a Friday night at 5:00, excited for some dinner, entertainment, and maybe some line dancing that others on here haved raved about. Our experience was almost nothing but disappointing.

First off, the downstairs tables had an hour wait. We were told the upstairs was open seating, so we opted for that. The entire "saloon" was swarming with kids. I've seen less kids at a Chuck E. Cheese. It was so bad that the on-stage entertainment played The Itsy Bitsy Spider on two different occasions. He was getting visibly upset because he didn't know enough songs that were age appropriate for all the kids who filled up the dance floor.

In terms of service upstairs, that was next to non-existent. Even though we were ordering food, we had to do that at the bar. Then we had to just watch the bar for our food to be ready and go retrieve it ourselves. We ordered a bucket of beer as well. The bartender mandated that we bring the bucket back right away because he didn't have enough. The other members of our party also had to raise up their arms from across the restaurant to verify we all had wristbands on. If management wasn't too cheap to hire waitstaff to serve the packed establishment, all of this mess could have been avoided.

The only saving grace for this place was the food. We ordered the Nashville Hot Chicken, which was quite good and packed with flavor. I had pretty low expectations for the food by the time our meal arrived, but it ended up being pretty good.

All in all, though, we left very disappointed. The ownership either needs to market this place as a kids destination or as a fun place for adults to dance and have a beverage. They can't have it both ways.

I'd give this place a negative 5 if I could. Don't waste your money for the $6 cover charge or your time. Service is awful...oh, wait! There is NO service. The place was booked with private events on the multiple floors and there was no seating... unless you ordered a dinner entree per person, which we didn't want to do. Sat at an apparently open bar area and were kicked out because we were sitting in front of the private party area. Apparently, the only seating was in the bar area. Luckily a couple was leaving as we were relocating. Waited in vain for a waitress or waiter to take our order and finally went to the bar to get cocktails. No one picked up dirty glasses left at the table by the previous party so finally took them to the bar. This place has terrible to NO customer service and the attitudes of the hostesses and waitresses is disgraceful to supposed Southern hospitality. Find another place for dinner, dancing and/or entertainment.

We really enjoyed the food here.  We came here every day for a meal.  Breakfast, lunch and dinner are all good.  The Hot Chicken and Pork Shank were awesome!  Great service from Mikey, our waiter.  He made sure the grilled chicken and kale salad was just the way we like it.

Good Music, but had to get our own drinks, server ignored us. She went to all other tables in our area, but not us. Other servers did not approach us. Appeared to be local patrons, servers knew, those folks waited on promptly. We  didn't get drinks right away, but after 20 minutes, my husband went to the bar for our drinks and complained to bartender about service, but said nothing could be done  about service. Walking distance from our Hotel, but we would go again for the music, but be prepared to get our own drinks,  soda price reasonable.

Nice atmosphere with live entertainment, food was good but nothing memorable.  Had a group of eight on Friday night so it was great to find a table open as they have multiple levels and plenty of seating.  Service was good with a friendly waitress and support staff to help out made a great night for everyone.
Not well organized, we sat ourselves, asked another table for their menus and when we finally flagged down waitstaff, we were ready with our order.

I've got to admit. I'm not much of a Pizza guy, but Soulshine is great. I've been a few times and the flavors are great. It's definitely worth checking out. Their second floor balcony is great as well.

Twin Kegs is pretty much your average dive bar, although to drunk folks with the munchies post normal restaurant hours, this place is just plain heaven. 

As far as I can tell, this place is frequented by truckers and sometimes your more clean cut folks such as myself. Usually an even mix when I've been here for karaoke nights. There's a shuffleboard table and several tv screens that are usually showing sports of some kind or other. It is a smoking establishment, and you will come out smelling like an ash tray. I think possibly in warmer months there is seating out front, but I'm not 100% sure on that. That aside, the service is sometimes slow, but friendly and efficient, and the food is pretty cheap and tasty - excellent burgers, and fantastic fried pickles! They also have a pretty decent selection of beer and other alcohol for such a small place, and those are also reasonably priced.

This place has a great atmosphere and food to match. Our server was on point and made sure we had everything we needed. Food came out promptly which helped with our plans that night at Bridgestone arena. We went there several times on our trip and enjoyed the live music.

Totally paying for the atmosphere here.  Brisket resembled beef jerky and tasted the same.  Full slab of ribs are the size of a half-rack elsewhere.  Live band on each level but good luck hearing one without the other...and neither was good.  Sort of like going to a Chucky Cheese and watching the rat sing out of tune.  Not a fan.

Fun atmosphere, great service and great food. The pulled pork sandwich was delicious and fairly priced. Very visitor friendly, came down for the weekend for a Bachelors Party and was welcomed. Had a great time and would come back again.
Went for a burger and had the brisket. Was a decent price and tasted okay. The service was good and the band playing was great.

Come here for the atmosphere and fun but not the food. I got the 3 meat plate- the sausage was nothing special, brisket tasted like roast beef, and chopped pork was definitely reheated from the day before. Huge waste of $22. I brought my 8 year old daughter and she loved it. Line dancing was fun. There was an hour and a half wait for the first floor but tons of open tables and hardly anyone standing around waiting. The second floor was open seating but you had to order food at the bar and hope it made it to you since there aren't servers or numbers. The food runners walk around lost trying to figure out where food goes. They need a better system for that, like numbers. The music and overall set up is great, and there are kid friendly activities upstairs.

This place was absolutely amazing! The service was the best we've ever had since being in Nashville for 4 days. Definitely a must have if you like cheaper than regular Nashville beer and if you like great food! I got the 5 cheese pizza and it was so melty and delicious and the pizza crust was the perfect thin and airy consistency. My husband got the pulled pork nachos and they were everything nachos were supposed to me. Every bite had the deliciousness on it. The pork was tender and delicious, and the blue corn chips were just the perfect addition!
Very crowded and loud music...but it's Nashville!  Friendly and fun atmosphere. Great ribs and good service. Listened to some amazing talent.

Love! Charming throw back country music atmosphere. Loved all the memorabilia on the walls, you can tell there's a lot of history there! A real honky tonk. Live music was great, (we came specifically for a writers night) they also have a nice big patio. Our server was very friendly and the food was surprisingly excellent! Had a grilled chicken sandwich with sweet potato fries. The grilled chicken was seasoned so well, one of the best chicken sandwiches I've ever had. The fries were delicious too! Very fast service with fair prices. I will definitely be back, I can't wait to bring friends and out of towners here as well!

Bad restaurant service, very slow. Food is not good. Music was too loud and it was difficult to hear singers. Music band was good, however, music producer needs to work on balance music sound and artist singing. For 69$ a person I Do not recommend!

As a somewhat beginner line dancer, I was hoping to show up and brush up my skills/show off the more difficult ones I've managed to pick up before my trip. My biggest disappointment is with the line dancing teacher/host who we have seen on both nights visiting this venue. She says "y'all" every two words and it was almost enough to drive my group out of here. Seriously- if you're speaking to a room full of people, have some public speaking skills or at least self awareness. 

One of the many line dances that were taught were fun/difficult and the rest were super easy. Boring! On songs which we recognized as being line dancing songs, the "leader" was either absent, or leading a super simplified version that we yawned at. I understand there are a bunch of tourists and beginners, but it'd be fun to be a bit more challenged. Maybe have two sections going on- one easy and one complex, like on copperhead road, for example. Also, her complete absence during plenty of songs was a hindrance to us because we "know" the dances with a little bit of a refresher. 

The place closed early on Thursday, our first night trying it out, due to lack of activity. I think there would be PLENTY more activity if they were more in touch with what the crowd wants, because whenever dances are being done with "y'all" girl, the people flocked to the dance floor. 

On my second night, I ordered wings and they sucked. Also, the bartender was incredibly rude after he ran off with my order and then came back to confirm my name and I mentioned I had a tab. He had an attitude and then slammed down my bottle and stalked off. I guess I need to be familiar with the order I need to disseminate information here. He was short and was probably having a complex since I'm a tall, strong woman.  He was rude to my friend separately as well, and got her order wrong twice. He didn't want to fix the mistaken order but luckily someone else stepped in.  (Taller shaggy looking bartender was fine and recalled my name for the tab.

One more weird thing was that there must have been a company event "iPass" and without any warning, about 12 suits took the stage and gave some speeches. It was very bizarre and ended with a brief motivational monologue about the potential future success of their business. Um, was that necessary to do on the main stage when the place was open to the public? It would have been slightly less awkward if they'd been introduced and preceded by some type of notification. But we were like, who on earth are these people?!

The bands were great. I particularly liked "the Springs" and hope to hear of them again outside of Nashville!
Great place! Cheeseburgers, jalapeño poppers and beer- what could be better. Oh yeah the shuffle board table.

Like several other recent reviewers, I was brought in the door because of a generous Scoutmob deal. I didn't hate Soulshine Pizza, and I might be willing to give it another chance one they've worked out the growing pains of a new business and staff. 

The remodeled building looked great, and the twisty staircase to the bar upstairs was a nice touch. The staff was also very pleasant and friendly. Still, any restaurant needs to rest on the laurels of its food. I have to say, I've had better pizza for less money.

I was surprised by the lack of beer knowledge on the part of the servers, especially because they had a fairly extensive selection. My server did not know anything about the beer selection, other than the names on the list. When I asked about this, he explained that the waitstaff is not allowed to has drinks at the restaurant, even on days they are not working. 

This policy really perplexed me, as just about any restaurant will take the time to train staff about the wine, beer and cocktails served. If done right, server training should include samples in my opinion. For a restaurant that prides itself on beer selection, I really think they're shooting themselves in the foot with this strict policy.

I ordered the Boudreaux pizza, minus the crawfish tails. The Andouille sausage was a nice topping, but the pizza was overall just okay. While the $9.99 price tag was not outrageous for a personal-sized 8" pizza, the next largest size (12") was almost double that, and a large (16") was darn-near $30. That's a lot of money for a pie. I would have enjoyed a $8 take-and-bake from Papa Murphy's about as much while having plenty of money leftover for a better selection.

Our first stop in Nashville after a long travel day. Super friendly staff, cool artwork, great music and great food. The cheese and garlic breadsticks were great - huge portion. I had a Wild Bill pizza - grilled chicken, garlic ranch, mozzarella, and wing sauce. It was spicy and awesome. My wife liked it better than her pizza, which was also really good as well. She had The Mississippian bbq sauce, grilled chicken, sun dried tomatoes, and pepper jack cheese. Super tasty food - a great welcome for us!!

Neat place with a great atmosphere ~ just a note about "line dance lessons" ~ when they are listed for 1hr. ~ the instructor comes out & teaches 1 dance that takes about 10minutes & then music is played for the remaining 50 minutes until the live music starts ~ not sure that really classifies as a line dance lesson ~ the fried pickles were definitely  a great pick ~ Brother Trouble was there when we went ~ alot of fun & very friendly staff ~

When you first enter the building, the Andrew Jackson venue is to your immediate right. The James K Polk and Andrew Johnson Theatre are further inside the building. The public space is spacious enough for you to come early, grab a drink and await your show. Though I'm not sure how early the bar/snack vendors open, it was nice just to get there early to cool off from the summer heat!

I was a little confused because it was hard to find the restrooms. Since it was my first time, perhaps I missed the signs. I found a sign for them as I approached the entrance to the Polk theatre and was directed to take the stairs to the lower level. If I were there for a performance at the Andrew Jackson venue, I would have had to ask for directions. My assumption is that you would have to walk up to the mezzanine and go down the stairs.

The Polk theatre was very nice, the seats were comfortable and it seemed every seat would have a full view of the stage.

The $20 valet was busy as I walked up. The TPAC website also offers you a chance to reserve parking at City Center for $10 if you sign up online. I saved a couple of dollars by parking at the library.

Looking forward to my next visit and I'll definitely be updating this review!

Was visiting Willie Nelson & Cooter's place's when the music from the Palace caught our attention. Stopped in for a quick cold one with my wife and adult daughter. Seven hours later we left with memories worth 10 times what we paid for. The staff? Phenomenal! My daughter has special needs. Some people don't mix well with this population. Our waitresses,  bartenders and the bands and fellow guests could not have been any better, nicer or more accommodating. The food was great. The fried pickles were the best I ever had,  ever. Fried yucca? Try it. Beer? ICE cold. Get away from the downtown crowd for an evening and try the palace.

I have had many average pizzas in my life, and I have had (unfortunately much fewer) great pizzas. One of pizza's greatest attributes is that even average pizza tastes great. Even a place like Dominoes is generally an enjoyable experience.

Unfortunately, to say that Soulshine's pizza is average would be an overstatement. I am a huge fan of thin crust pizzas, but with the use of thin crust comes the expectation of more delicate treatment. It was as if  they were following directions on how to roast a turkey...it had clearly been in the oven about twice as long as it should have been. Both the white and wheat crusts had the consistency of matzo.

The sauce and ingredients were also really bland. The carnivore pizza was seemingly devoid of Italian sausage but ran amok with rubbery pepperoni and Canadian bacon. I was excited about the Magic Mushroom, but the mushrooms were really gritty and, of course, had any resemblance of life cooked the hell out of them.

Service was decent, I suppose, but this was pretty lousy. I hope for the establishment's sake it was an off night.

Amazing performances. My husband surprised me by taking me to see Beauty and The Beast. I took a friend of mine to see Cinderella. I seriously almost cried both times it was so beautiful lol. The tickets weren't expensive either 130 for two people. I ordered my tickets online which was very quick and easy. They also have a great concession stand with lots of food to choose from. I also bought a beautiful Cinderella graphic tee. I would definitely go back to see both of those amazing shows. The way Cinderella would change into different costumes right before your eyes, even hair style changing was simply spectacular! I will always be a girly girl and enjoy the Disney princess shows no matter how old I get lol!

The shrimp and grits was excellent! Flavorful and delicious. It was a nice treat to come during a Wednesday evening with live music (no cover). The restaurant is pretty big. It's close to the Music Hall and the JW Marriott where I was staying while attending a conference. My Ring Of Fire Margarita was OK--not spicy and a little too sweet for my liking.

As I walked into Rippy's, the bouncer asked me if my breasts were real and actually reached out and touched them.

I immediately asked to talk to the manager of Rippy's, as this is a completely inappropriate way to treat a customer. I assumed he would be immediately disciplined, as an employee who sexually harasses customers would probably be considered a legal liability by most sane humans.

I calmly explained the situation to the general manager and recreated what he did to me, poking her chest in the same matter in which he touched me so that she understood the complete inappropriateness of the situation.

She immediately exploded, yelling at me, calling me aggressive and attempting to deflect blame from the bouncer and on to me. I wasn't even raising my voice as I spoke to her.

She made no effort whatsoever to apologize for the fact that I was sexually harassed. 

She did not ask the bouncer to apologize. 

She did not suggest that any action would be taken against the bouncer.

This went beyond the realm of bad experience; I am honestly horrified that there are establishments in this world where this wouldn't result in an immediate termination of employment.

My email to the owner of Rippy's outlining the situation also was not returned.
Best Ribs in Nashville period. Beer is cold, music is always great, but the Ribs are #1.

It was very busy the night we were in, food was amazing. They forgot my cole slaw / pickles and I asked for it multiple times over the course of dinner. I never got the other half of my meal, but our waitress was very kind and had a manager come over... she relieved us if our whole meal ticket. I didn't expect them to comp anything, let alone the whole ticket. Manager went out of her way to make sure we left happy and full! We will come back.

Ordered 2 kids meals. It was pretty much mediocre. I had a cheeseburger. Decent size but tasted like an imitation burger.  My husband ordered ribs and sent them back. They tasted oven baked. No seasoning and the fries were half done. The greens looked over cooked and soggy. We will not eat here again

Great place to hang out with friends! We enjoyed the cold beer and had great fun trying the line dance lessons. For a group of 60+ Ladies,  that was quite a sight! Music and service were both good. All in all,  had a great time here and would definitely return.
This is our go to place as soon as we get into Nashville each time. I like their second floor bar area. Good music and fast service. Try the nachos with pork.

Been sitting here for almost 2 hours. If somebody could come to take our order that would be great.
Tried to get somebody's attention, and the staff member said he doesn't take care of our tables and walked away.
Horrible service.
Not impressed. Stopped for drinks in the afternoon. The band took 30 minutes to set up. The bar was tacky (sticky). $15 for a draft beer and a not very good 7&7. Ok I guess.

This place reminded me of Pazzo's in Lexington with a more deep south feel.  Food was good.  Unfortunately they did not offer the "southern hospitality".  After confirming my scout mob deal with the waitress before ordering, before my check and correcting her when I received a full price check she still returned without applying the discount.  After apologizing she went to remedy the situation.  She returned and told me that a $20 minimum was needed for the deal to be used.(I had spent $19) and she told me it could not be changed.  This would have been nice to know the previous three times my scout mob deal was discussed.

It got better when the manager told me the minimum purchase was "clearly stated" on scout mob when it clearly was not.  Sub par service and a pompous manager really shame the potential this place has.

Great old school atmosphere. Kind of run down and dirty, but I saw the bartender cleaning, so I don't think it is grimy, just old. Bartender was very nice, and the people that were there that seemed to be regulars, were very nice too. I had the BB (Bad Burger) and it was very tasty. They also had 3-4 porters/stouts, and I like dark beer, so this was great. The even had one of my favorite beers, Left Hand Milk Stout.

We are staying at the hotel next to the Nashville Palace and driving past it for the few days we are here, the place is always active. So we decided to check it out. 

We loved it and enjoyed ourselves so much that we are going back tonight. The bands were great! Didn't have to fight the Broadway crowds and spent half of the money we would have downtown. Draft beer is limited on choices, but other than that drinks were great and can't beat the price!

Historically, I have loved this place. Basic bar food and great country music. 

This past visit was a huge disappointment. The music was so loud it hurt ears. It was pretty obvious when we walked in because everyone was seated as far away as possible and several people had their fingers in their ears. No excuse for this in this town. 

We left because we couldn't take it. Sorry.
Catfish tacos are AMAZING.  Perfectly blackened and seasoned catfish.  A must have. Get a little extra sauce to dip the fries in

First of all, they charged us a $6 cover per person, which was surprising, but we thought, ok, maybe its worth it.  We figured it covered the cost of the band, but then again, there's a band at every saloon and they arent' charging for a cover fee.

next problem:  there was a private party renting out half the place, so we had to listen to company xyz speeches to their employees and watch them all act like idiots square dancing and dominating the whole dance floor and stage.  another reason to not charge us cover charge, if theres a private party and the microphone and dance floor are being dominated by a private company then why are we charged a cover.??  we will return to nashville but NEVER to this rip-off joint.

Then we ordered nachos with pork, there was about two tablespoons of pork and most of the nachos had nothing on them.  a $12 ripoff.  Same deal with the salad, the chicken on it was ice cold like the whole salad was sitting in the refigerator, not hot fresh grilled chicken.  Basically a bowl of iceberg lettuce for $11.  ripoff.  Next came the wings, we requested sweet barbecue and they came out plane.  Now i've never had plane chicken wings in a restaurant before, usually they are coated with sauce and delicious.  Well these were plane, looked like they just threw them in the fryer and served them without any sauce or flavoring at all.

Our server was indifferent, probably making so much money off tips from the drunk tables she didn't really give a hoot about us.  The bartender (while we were waiting for a table) was semi-unfriendly, my wife doesn't drink alcohol so when i ordered a beer for me and a pepsi for her we got a sneer.  

Lastly: a couple showed up with an infant baby in a carrier.  now this place is really really loud, and they just put the baby on the table right in the center of the place where the music was crazy loud...  We said something to the management that this was inappropriate, that in infant should be in a loud place like this and they did nothing, said it was "parents discretion".    Well some parents have no common sense, the poor baby was subjected to this loud place.... the two parents went up on the dance floor and left the baby with a grandparent- so we dropped a little note on their table- reminding them that the childs hearing could be damaged and that it was far too loud in there for an infant--- common sense aint so common anymore.  On our way out, we mentioned to the guy who took our cover charge that they shouldn't allow infants in there, he had nothing to say either.  So we left $70 poorer scratching our heads about the entire evening

First time to Nashville and we first went to this restaurant/bar. The different levels of live music were fantastic but it was a bit too loud without any opportunities to dance comfortably! So couldn't really talk nor dance.. but the food was great! I got the pulled chicken with coleslaw and mac and cheese- it was delicious. The drinks were a bit pricey, but that was expected. Overall, a good time!

For a bar in Nashville, it's nothing too special. A decent bite of ribs, an okay beer selection, and mildly helpful service. The band was just a couple dudes covering random country songs. All-in-all, there are better places for food, service, drinks, and entertainment in every direction.

The bbq was great...the prices were a little higher than expected for a place that uses plastic silverware. Overall it was a nice experience being able to sit on the rooftop and look out at the city while enjoying live entertainment and food.

Went there tonight and had to wait over an hour for a table, even thought several tables were available.  Horrible customer service and very disorganized.  Food was decent but took a long time.  Possibly worst restaurant/entertainment experience ever.  Would never return under any circumstance.
My compliments to management for hiring the hottest bartender's in town.  The downstairs blonde duo and upstairs Burnett trio are untouchable on Broadway

Good music and great food. Isn't that all you need? Rippy's definitely has both. Their BBQ is excellent and the buffalo wings had my whole party wanting to go back for more. I was truly impressed with the food. It's not typical fried bar food, but actual BBQ. The live music was great on both floors, but I honestly can't say that I saw a bad band throughout the whole strip during my visit. All bands on the strip work for tips and walk around with a tip bucket, which is a little weird, but it's normal around here so no harm. This is a definite stop for anyone's trip to Nashville. It's located on a very busy corner and gets packed late night on weekends. Luckily they have 2 downstairs rooms and an upstairs that is pretty big. Conveniently just a few steps away from Bridgestone Arena. Well done Rippy's

Atmosphere was great. Love the live music. Didn't stop for the food. Just a place to rest and hear some music. Wait staff was working hard with multiple tables. They were all nice and friendly. Dessert was ok.... nothing spectacular. My friend had a mixed cocktail and said it was delicious!

Nashville- you GOTTA get to this brand new hot spot in the heart of Downtown... Truly unique eatery with a vibe - the name says it all!  This is a tasty Southern menu and spectacular live music venue.  We ordered deviled eggs 5 ways and the meatloaf - wholly unique and absolutely delicious!  Treated to two terrific songwriter performances and had an amazing Sunday evening.  Extensive bar, great coffee options, doesn't get any better!

Been to Rippy's on several occasions and I do like this place. 

Likes:  Good food - I had brisket sandwich with sweet bbq sauce and fries. Very tasty!
Live music - always good
Location - close to everything important on Broadway. 
Fun place 

Dislikes:  We had group of eight. Server brought me check and right before I paid it I went ahead and glanced over it. Server neglected to tell me that she had added 20% tip to the check. I would have double-tipped her if I hadn't caught that small detail at the bottom of the check. I'm sure she was hoping I would miss that and she would have ended up with a $50 tip. That's just bullshit so she is the reason I am only giving them 3-stars. 

So be careful not to get scammed by your server here!

I liked this place.  Good music, and a nice roomy floor plan.  

The food was served rapidly after ordering, and was delicious.  Drinks were reasonably priced and made quickly.  Service was good.  

You'll find a large rooftop here, with music on all levels.  Wood floors, tables, and bars, and stairs.  I was here on a Tuesday afternoon and it was pretty packed, so I am sure it's even worse during the weekends. 

I tried the pulled pork and a salad, both of which were fantastic.

Manager is a complete jerk! Never ever will I or my friends step foot in that place! We order drinks at a table in the bar area. Was told we had to order food. We drank our drinks and decided to order some food. The manager came back and said we couldn't order food... That we missed our chance and to leave!  We did and will never be back! We all live in Nashville. I hope he doesn't treat our tourist that way.... What a jerk!
Ate pizza at the bar after a late night of drinking. Food was great service was great! Still could hear the music upstairs but not as much commotion. Would definitely recommend and we will be back!

Always packed, had lunch there. Pulled pork wasn't the best, lacked a lot of flavor for being in the south.

Great sides. The Mac and cheese and the backed beans were amazing, whereas the coleslaw not the best. 

Brother had the ribs and he said there were amazing

This rating is based solely on my experience of the bar on the 2nd floor, more specifically the band that was there tonight after the Pred's game. The place was mostly empty, the band was good but there was no crowd. There were 2 drunk girls dancing..that was it. The band was asking for requests. I went to give a tip, and was asked what I wanted to hear? I told the lead singer my request , he said "requests are usually $20", ok, I have $5 for a tip so no need to take my request. Thanks for making it awkward!

When in Nashville do as the tourists, so we did. Line dancing lessons every hour or so, even if you can't dance. It'll be packed and it'll be loud, but the servers will be resposive and take of you. I was surprised at how tasty the food actully was. A good amount of local beers, if you care to imbide.

Beautiful venue. Slow service and horrible BBQ. Dry brisket that taste like dirt with lots of salt. We sent it back and they brought us Ribs. Again it was dry, chewy and taste like dirt. We took two bites. Manager demanded we pay for what we didn't eat. We refused and left. We won't be back.

Large and really nice restaurant and bar with a dance floor and stage.  They were giving line dance lessons that were really popular.  We would have drank here, but we never saw a server in the.bar area.  We never got a food menu either.  We waited maybe 20 minutes and then left.

There are countless delicious places to eat in Nashville - it's not just music city, it's food heaven. So in a place where all of the food is so amazing, I don't know why anyone would want to eat here! It was by far the worst meal I had the whole time I was there. I had the mesquite chicken breast, which was completely bland, my friends had this strange plate of meat which they told me wasn't very appetizing either. It had this random block of cheese on it which became the brunt of most of our jokes the next few days. The ONLY pros: decent band downstairs, TVs to catch games (I was there during March Madness), and decent curly fries. Otherwise, AVOID!

We stopped here for a quick lunch. Average bar food, good service, we did enjoy the live music, the duo were actually very good and fun to listen to while eating. Not the bars fault we could not stay longer since our parking was about to expire and it is very expensive to park downtown.

We were looking for a family friendly place with good food, beer and good, live country music and that's exactly what we got! We were able to get the full Nashville experience with an early (4ish) dinner yummy bbq pulled pork and brisket), front row to a wonderful band with our kids. Def would recommend this place.

This was one of the worst places I have ever been to. This was the first place I have been to in Nashville. My party arrived around 12 and ordered lunch straight off the menu and not one order was delivered to our table correctly. Then at about 2pm the rest of our party joined us at kickoff for the semifinals of the college football playoffs. Unfortunately, we will have to rewatch it because all of the TVs only worked about half of the time due to bad satellite reception that the staff refused to fix. Our waiter said "I guess it'll come on when it comes on." To top things off, it was New Years Eve and so they had at least 7 staff members blowing up hundreds of balloons with long strings  and putting them all over everyone which tangled everyone up and got all in the food despite numerous complaints from several parties. We stayed for around 6 hours to try to watch the game and ended up live streaming it on our phones. We came in excited with high expectations and were thoroughly disappointed and will not be back.  Bad management. Bad service. Mediocre food.
