Had a wonderful opportunity to see Wicked recently and my goddaughter was playing the lead role of Elphaba, so it was extra special to me. We had Orchestra center seats in the 7th row. They were awesome seats, though it looks like there really isn't a bad seat in the house. Loved that there was a bar area where we were too. 

Valet parking was a godsend and worth every penny. The bathrooms were nice, though one that I went in to was out of paper towels. This is a lovely theater and I hope to see more shows here. It's not too big of a theater and the seats were actually very comfortable and much roomier than some theaters I've been in. 

We even got a backstage tour and it was so cool to see the dolly systems and how everything works behind the scenes.

This is a fantastic place for a night full of fun! I rented out the 3rd floor for a private corporate event and it was the best one yet! Great atmosphere perfect for entertaining. The salad bars, stuffed potato bars, and pecan pie bars were all delicious and replenished often. All of the staff were phenomenal! If you are looking to host a private event in Nashville, the wildhorse is the ticket!

my wife and i have visited Nashville area 2 times in the last 2 years and plan on returning in 2015, Nashville Palace is on the holy s#&* that's a great place,it was good in 2013 and even better in 2014 , i am seriously excited about returning in 2015.  The staff crazy good folks, Kelsey our server needs a big time raise , just because she is awesome and on top of her game.the entertainment is as good as anywhere in NASHVILLE.... DO NOT MISS this place.
Pretty good bar.  Lost 1 star due to lack of Guinness on tap.  The live bands were good, and the food was decent.

We went to see Paw Patrol Live on our first visit to the Tennessee Performing Arts. The theater was a lot bigger than we had expected it to be. My wife and I grew up in NY and attended many Broadway shows and this theater definitely rivals a Broadway theater in size and spectacle. The volunteer staff at the venue were all very friendly during our visit and they made sure that our kids had a wonderful time. We look forward to attending future shows at TPAC for years to come.

Wow, extremely disappointed.   They advertise great food, we must have gotten there  (only 830 pm) when they were done cooking because we got the bottom of the barrel.   We had a combo platter for 23.50 and the only thing edible was the onion rings.   Chicken wings were very spicy, ribs were very dry,  and all was peppered with the pepper sauce.  Because we  were served so fast  we think our food was cooked several hours earlier.   Band on the 2nd floor was also struggling and begging for money to the extreme.  The only thing that was good was our waiter,  he was very friendly, our advice to him is find another job you deserve better. Much improvement is needed.
Live music and ribs.. that's all I wanted and that's what I got! The service was quick even though the place was packed. The ribs were decent - great hangout place when in Nashville.

Went for lunch, wanted something fast and basic which it was. Food was great the tots were my favorite. Service was good we were the only ones there. But had to sit outside because the cigarette smell and bad smell inside in general.

Visiting our daughter who just moved to Nashville, were told a 1 hour wait for a table, waited the 1+ hour in the waiting area with drinks/appetizers (the fried pickles were great) and then seated at the counter like seats facing the dance floor while there were tables obviously untaken.  When asked if there was anyway we could have a table (There were 4 adults and 1 child) we were refused saying they were expecting a party of 20..thast party never came and the tables remained empty and we remained and ate our VERY MEDIOCRE dinner, tasteless.

The restaurant staff never smiled, were rude on several occasions and need to find other jobs. They were very bothered to have to do anything for us and believe me we are very easy people.  Not sure what their problem was. My daughter wrote on the receipt the details of our distasteful service and visit and asked that the waitress please be sure the manager sees the comments.  I am sure she never showed it to hi or her.

The ambiance and music were terrific and the décor....we loved everything about the place except 2 very important features...the service and the food.

We will be back in Nashville several times a year in the future but will NEVER frequent this place again.  Those waitresses who services us really need to leave if this place is to continue to be in business. Sooooo atypical of the wonderful southern hospitality we experienced everywhere else.

Manager...please track down who worked there last Sunday evening around 7 PM and address it accordingly.

We were so excited to eat here after hearing how good it was from others and reading other reviews. There are only 8 other tables here and it took over an hour for our food to come out. Half of our food was undercooked and cold. We asked for a manager and he asked me what I wanted him to do about it. There was no explanation or apology. I have been a server and bartender for years and that is not how you handle your guests. Needless to say, we will not be back. I really hope they read this and improve their service.
Yum! The Chicken Fried Chicken was delish! On a bed of stuffing with gravy-- great comfort food!

DO NOT EAT HERE!!!!! The first time we ate at Twin Kegs, my fiancé and I were left wanting more...we wanted the experience we read about in all the raving reviews.
Not a chance. 

On our first venture into this Thompson Lane dive bar, we were immediately gawked at by the sea of older Tennessee fans. It was as if it was sinful to come into the establishment in street clothes as opposed to orange and white. 

The service was mediocre at best, with a server that obviously thought visiting our table was a waste of time. The food was definitely no where near glamorous. My fiancé got a veggie burger that was nothing more than a grilled Boca patty and some not-so-fresh veggie toppings. Their meat burger was okay, there definitely better at other bars in the city. 

We tried to give the bar a second chance last week only just to walk out 10 minutes after arriving. Upon entering Twin Kegs, (cigarette) smoke hit you like a scene from a Cheech and Chong film. The bartender and singles server made no intention of visiting our table - focusing only on their cigarettes and conversations with the regulars. After sitting at our table for ten minutes without greeting or acknowledgement, we left and got great brews and burgers elsewhere.
Nice place to hang out, watch football, and drink beer. Open space is good for chilling. Food is pretty good. Wide selection of local beer.

Stopped in on the way to Navarre, FL. Everything we ordered was on the money. Great food and found my personal favorite beer from Bearded Iris. My family and I had a great time. Music/entertainment was great, the food and atmosphere was equal. I highly recommend stopping by!
Food was mediocre. 5-7pm was filled with too many kids. Running and horsing around on the dance floor. I'm sure it's probably better later at night.

The reviews I just read were written quite a while ago and do not ring true today. I've only lived in Nashville for a short time, but Nashville Palace has become one of my very favorite places to see some great music have a cold beer and meet people from all over the world.  The music here is traditional, no "pop" country. The staff is friendly and welcoming. Lucky for me, it's a very short drive from my East Nashville neighborhood and there is plenty of parking.  I bet my next review will be 5 stars because every time I visit, it just keeps getting better.  You can usually see who is playing on their Facebook page, so check it out and pick a night, you won't be disappointed.

Pro. Music and ambiance...have a drink but don't eat

Con : Like many other patrons, my family and I suffered the result Of poor service and mediocre food. We were seated at 6:45 our reservation time right near the stage. We waited 20 min before we finally asked for a waiter and drinks. Later asked for silverware, asked for more refills, ask to have our order taken and 2 hours later got our food. The waiter apologized but the manager didn't seem to care though we got a 1/2 discount that we asked for. This was the first time in my life I didn't leave a tip. I normally tip 20-30% and travel 3-4 days a week so I eat out A LOT! Many people got up and left mad.

The Wildhorse is a good time. Went on Saturday night, kind of early. Line dancing lessons in between band sets. Everyone gets out on the floor. Mix of country, pop, and hip hop to line dance to. The band was phenomenal (Adairs Run). My only criticism - we started out on the 3rd floor, where I'm guessing there is no wait staff. The glasses, bottles, plates, half finished just sat and were never cleaned up. We eventually moved downstairs, but it was a little unsanitary.

Mediocre food. My  Friend and I split the pulled pork platter, Mac and cheese, and cornbread. It was alright the pulled pork was dry the Mac and cheese was ok. Nothing spectacular. I honestly expected a lot more because it was recommended to us by somebody who lives down here. Next time I will definitely do more research, because all we wanted was delicious juicy bbq and rippys didn't hit that mark.
We did a group event here so did not order off menu. Our buffet had pulled pork and Berkeley brisket - both good. Overall good food and decent venue.

This was one of my top bars when I visited Nashville (and I went to most of the ones on lower Broadway when I was there for the week). 

The food menu is substantial and there are lots of choices. However if you go you should order the fried pickles (world famous as they say), the fried green tomatoes and a beer of your choice. They have a beer brewed specially for them and I tried  it...two thumbs up.

In addition to the food I found all the staff friendly and helpful, there was a good crowd and either free line dancing lessons or live music on the stage all day long. The bar is multi levelled and very spacious.

Highly recommended and worth a visit if you are in Nashville.

Went there after it being recommended by several out of town visitors. It was great, split the sampler platter with a buddy I was down with. It's multi-storied much like the rest of the town. Service: Melody our server was great, attentive and friendly to my very annoying group. Food: OHHHH HELL YEAH! All of it, delicious. Sampler came with some rib, onion rings, kielbasa thingies, and a bunch of other stuff. It was all delicious. I'll be going back if I'm ever in town again. Restrooms were nice and clean too, which is rare for a bar on a strip. Enjoy!
Slow service but the ribs are awesome! the music and atmosphere are what you would picture Nashville to be.  Combine the two BBQ sauces for perfection.
The house bbq sauce is delicious! Gotta try it on the brisket sandwich :D everything made from scratch here and the live music is awesome! Definitely recommend this place

Definitely an upscale establishment and venue for entertainment/artists.  The stage, sound system are as good as you'd get anywhere.  We went there 2x.  W-A-Y less crowded than most of the small "dive bars" on Broadway...which are a different kind of awesome.

The new Wildhorse is only surviving off its old reputation. It is a shell of its former self. Smaller menu, higher prices and horrible service. I am curious if management has changed as well. All of the servers appear to be if not disgruntled then unhappy. The building is still very cool and a must see for anyone visiting. I would order a drink and then find another place to go.

Great location for groups. We had the 3rd floor to ourselves. Fooseball, shuffle board and pool. Great food - awesome salad bar, pulled pork sliders, fries, ribs, s'mores (with real fire!), fried pickled and even chocolate covered bacon! We learned how to line dance and listened to a live band. It was a great night out!

The food was good. I will not go back because they lie on their menu and when I brought it to the waitress' attention she told me I was wrong. Went downstairs and asked girl behind bar to speak to a supervisor and she asked my problem. When I pointed out their wording on their menu she told that's the way it is and I have to pay full price. As you can see on their menu they say that all dinners come with two sides. You can substitute with curly fries or onion rings for $1 more. You can add a side salad for $2 more. I had the pulled pork with baked beans and mac and cheese as my sides. I also added a side salad. When I got the bill the salad was $3.50. I know it's only $1.50 but when I brought their error to their attention I was told if I would have taken only one side I would have got it for $2. It doesn't say that on their menu and as far as I am concerned if that's all they think of their customers I won't be back and I will make sure I let as many people know about their attitude as possible. Drinks were not great for the price either.

Would you like some good Ribs with Live Music?  Then stop at Rippy's.  If you are a soda drinker you may feel like a Second Class Citizen.  The liquor drinkers our waiter were served like First Class Citizens.   Annoying.  We had to flag him down to stop at out table why he had stopped at the liquor drinker table five times.  They were less just across the aisle.

       There are Two Floors and they both had a 'Live Band'.  

         This restaurant is across from the Bridgestone Arena and just down the street from the Ryman Theatre.

Came here on vacation with friends. We were watching a football game and the band began to set up. Well, we discussed this with management and informed them January 1 is a big day for games! We are mid game wnd about 40 people are here for the game NOT the band- THEN for no reason bc he said "I wonder if the band is aware no one here is here for the band" and the band member turns around and told our friend to GO F YOURSELF!!! You're in a dive bar band and.... Ya most people come for the bar or game and you're here to promote yourself. Get used to it.. Youre small town. Ugh, So rude! The band here "Brian James" has a long haired dude that is a complete DouchE! Beware of this terrible band. Otherwise the bar and food were fine.

I got the chicken tenders and fries, the tenders were pretty good but they will probably be better if you get them a little well done. The fries were good but would be better if they were hand-cut nothing is better than hand-cut fries at a BBQ place. Our service was fast and good! Would recommend!

Dropped in and had the chicken fried steak girlfriend had the Shrimp and Grits ..  Dessert was the Nash House Pie...  our server Amy was great!    The service was was and got to meet Andy the manager... We will be back

This place is fine. Like most restaurants/bars on Broadway, it was a fun environment with live music. I would come back for the music, especially because the volume levels were good. Not too loud, but I could hear well. They're getting dinged on food. The Mac and cheese tastes like Stouffers. They put their meat through a smoker, which is good, but the taste was a bit strong for me. Come for the drinks or the ribs -- best friend's dad got them and fell in love.

I really enjoyed this place. There was love music, service was good, drinks were strong, and food was great. I got a baked potato with pimento. This was super filling. I couldn't finish the whole thing, not even close. It was very heavy and rich but worth it. I enjoyed the atmosphere and had a great time eating and listening to music.

rippys is my favorite bar in nashville! Always an amazing selection of live music, fun atmosphere, and nice bartenders.  Met up with a bumble date there the other night and we had the best time! I look forward to going back soon!
The food was excellent.  The music was great.  The service was horrible.  I had to go to the bar to get my own refills.  Took over 15 minutes just to get bill when requested.

As a local I wanted to bring my 6 and 12 year old nephews (and their parents) here so they could do some of the line dancing and enjoy the atmosphere. I have been here many times and always enjoyed it. This time (Saturday, October 4, 2014) was the WORST! 

Our "server" came over and told us if we weren't ordering a full entree to please move to the bar area. Hello....did you greet us, make the children feel welcome or even ask us what were were ordering??? NO! Okay, I can see moving minor children to the bar area, at 2 in the afternoon, if you were at capacity or even filling up - there were maybe 20 table taken, and if you have ever been here that is hardly any tables. 

The "server" then point lazily in the general direction of several areas we could go sit - if we wanted - and then walked away. We didn't even know where to go at this point. So we decided to order a few appetizers and some of the suvenior cups for my out of town guests. We advised her what we were doing and she said "you still have to go to the bar - only full entree orders can eat here."

We opted to leave and this young lady began to mumble under her breath and then hustled to the front to close the doors for a private event. A lady stading outside asked her about coming in and the "server" curtly told her "We are closed for a private event" and walked off. 

For an place that depends on tourisum to pay their salaries, light bills and the music they bring in they sure were not very welcoming. My family left with a terrible vision of the Wildhorse and stated they would not be coming back. As for Nashville there are many great places to spend our money that value their guests. 

See ya Wildhorse!
Ick! Premade slop! Don't waste your time.  The ribs were the ONLY thing good. The sides were obviously premade n stored in styrofoam. Sooo bad

I have been coming here for over twenty years. My mother would bring me here when I was a child to see plays, and I also took many school trips here as well. Now and even when I was a child have I ever had a bad experience. I love this place and I have many memories here. I have been in every theater they have in the building and every one is nice. I have sat at about every seat you can sit and I have yet to find a bad view. The staff here is extremely helpful and friendly. They serve snacks and drinks (alcohol) that are a little pricey, but it goes with the territory, kind of like the movies. I recently saw Wicked with my wife here and it was phenomenal. Even at this show I had tickets in the balcony in which we watched the show until intermission. Then met a friend whom two of his friends did not show so my wife and I sat in their seats on the front row. Both views were different but great. All in all this is a great venue that holds a special place in my heart.
Fun venue with good variety on their menu.  Walking distance from major venues and hotels, and live music was a plus.

For a Friday they are handling the crowd pretty good! Very up to date with technology. They take your cell phone number and text you when you sign up for a table and then when it's ready!! Awesomeness! 
Kathleen is a fabulous waitress! Ask for her, she will make sure your order is correct . We had a great experience ! Prices are reasonable!
Great place to eat and drink before sporting events. It's a little loud, true sports bar, but the people are great.

Good food - Great venue  - we walked in here on a whim and sat down.. The nachos were delicious.  We had a great pizza and salads and then headed up stairs to listen to music.  We were so pleasantly surprised.  Our waitress Alison seems to keep everything straight even though the place was jumping.  She also was great about proving water.  We loved this place so much we went back the next day.  We were excited to hear the house band - they rock and then many hopefuls that got to come up on stage and play a song or two.. what a treat. Biggest treat of all Allison was our waitress again.  This place was packed and she not only served us quickly she remembered us from the night before.  If we ever head to Nashville again.. we will definitely stop here!

The Good: Great music all the time! Three levels: great atmosphere.

Tip: perfect spot for prePreds game drinks!

My husband and I see at least 4 shows a year here and love them all! They bring the best musicals to town. I also attend Tedx Nashville and a few other conferences throughout the year and love the facilities. Only improvement they could make is wifi for the conferences... It's hard to sit all day listening to speakers but not have the ability to open your laptop and catch up on emails. However! The shows they bring to town make me forgive the little wifi indiscretion. Can't wait to see Wicked!

Good pizza and the service was fine considering how busy they were.  Absolutely heavenly to sit outside on a warm spring evening and enjoy pizza and beer.  Love the music offerings too.  The only bummer is the whole noisy crowded thing but hey, you know that going in.  We'll be back!

Ah, Scoutmob, always leading to fun new places. We decided to take advantage of 50% off this new spot, and were very pleasantly surprised. 

To start, the interior is very cool. From what I understand, this is a small chain, but it felt like a Nashville local spot. It has an old brick warehouse feel to it, but was really clean and definitely set a good vibe. The music was a bit loud and had some crazy psycho jazz playing at times, but hey, that's Nashville. The big stairs towering through the middle of the room, the stained glass windows, and the beer-bottle chandelier made for some really fun stuff to look at. 

As for the food, it was pretty great. Three of us split a 16" Carnivore pizza. I forget what all meat was on it, but you can use your imagination... It was a lot. While it wasn't mind-blowing or revolutionary, it was very solid, very delicious pizza. They offer white or wheat crust, and have a LOT of specialty pizzas. There were also lots of people ordering sandwiches and they also looked tasty. 

Overall, the cool vibe, the good food, and the reasonable price make this a prime candidate for a "regular" spot. We'll be back for sure.

True Southern hospitality - from the management, servers, and food. We have been in Nashville for 3 days, and we were waiting for comfort food.  This place exceeded expectations. 

We heard about this place because of the Cambria Sunday funday pool party! Our table of 11, ordered 1 of every shareable appetizer - the spoon fries, bacon queso, and deviled eggs were our favorite! I did the BLT - hangover helper. Hot chicken was great! 

Our server was exceptional, providing us local suggestions and always checking in on us. Great conversation. He was be first man to actually treat us with respect and keep us from getting hangry! Sincerely appreciate everything he did for us! Would definitely come back!

If you like BBQ, music and an open restaurant concept, Rippy's is the place for you.

Located in the heart of downtown Nashville, Rippy's is a 2 floor restaurant with an open concept - meaning you find a seat when one opens up.  The service staff will get to you when they can and they'll return to you on occasion.

There is a bar on each floor, sit up on top and feel the breezes and see the great views of the city.

Be sure to get their BBQ, it is to die for.  It comes quickly so you won't get to hungry waiting.

Came here for a conference dinner. There are three levels but the crowd was huge so still people had to stand. The bars are at both levels but am not sure if the bartenders aren't accustomed to so many customers because the service was rather slow. The food was buffet and the barbecue meats were amazing, even the salmon. The deserts were okay. Nothing great. The live band and performance and the entire ambiance was so hip and fun and will make you shake a leg for sure!!

I came here for a conference and really liked the look and feel of the venue. The inside had 3 levels and all with overlooks of the stage. There were plenty of bar stations and the venue was right near the popular broadway area. Worth a visit!

Went in for lunch on the 26th of October. Took about 10 minutes for waiter to come to table.  Took another 10 minutes to get water that we ordered. He said he'd be right back to take our order. Waited forever for him to come back to take order. During this time the couple behind us ordered from different waiter even though they came in after we got our water. Finally gave up and left.

The Nashville Palace is a great place to find a great burger! It's a bar. There is live music. They have outdoor seating. And they have awesome, friendly service. 

For lunch, there was a handful of people dining between those sitting at the bar, in the restaurant and outside. Sandy took care of everyone and she did it well! She recommended the burgers, so that's what we ordered - grilled over an open flame, she said. Best burgers we'd had in a while! She was playful with our daughter; even opened up a bottle of root beer for her to taste without charging us. 

We even tried our first fried pickles to see what all the fuss is about among southerners. They were awesome!! I'm hooked!!! 

It's a fun, relaxed atmosphere and our daughter loved the live music. It's great for families, however after 10pm no one under the age of 21 is allowed inside. According to Sandy, the night crowd is still always a "great crowd". 

Prices are cheap; not much more than what fast food would cost. 

If you're a tourist, as we are, it's attached to a souvenir shop and Cooter's so stroll on over and take a look. 

In short; I liked it!

Free line dancing lessons during the day! Huge stage for performances. I walked in for food just knowing that line dancing was an option. They are very family friendly and allowed my son to run all over the dancefloor during lunch time.
The hot chicken was impeccable! The Cole slaw will.make.me.go back just for that though. Best i have ever had! They had pickles and banana peppers in there! It did so much for the consistency and the flavors in there. We also did the whiskey flight. Would definitely recommend it if you appreciate different drinks and experimenting with new flavors

I was really hoping to get some dancing in, but on a Saturday night this place was PACKED. And I mean there were people spilling out of the dance floor. Not my style, so unfortunately we just ate (a reasonable) dinner and left.

We went to Wildhorse for lunch.   We had been there the last couple of times we were in town.     On the particular visit we sat at the bar and were greeted by a smiling happy bartender named Destiny.    She was busy and still was able to provide us with suggestions for cocktails and lunch menu items.    We had the brisket and the brunch burger. We each had a side of the tomatoes and cucumbers.    All the food was excellent.    I had mentioned it was my birthday and we were given a excellent dessert.     This experience was so great we went back later that night.   Plus they also have a cute glass boot souvenir mug you can purchase.  We will go back next visit

We have eaten here a few times. The food is consistently good. The sampler platter is a good choice to share. I like that there are three choices of bands. If you don't like one, move to another room. They recently got a lot of new high top tables. It's generally clean.  The ribs are nice and smoky. The onion rings are huge and have a good coating. They could use a dipping sauce for them. Our friends enjoyed the chicken nachos. The chicken is also smoked. Definitely give it a try.

Tried this place while visiting Nashville.  Salads are listed as iceberg lettuce but it was mixed greens. Plastic silverware do not cut pork sandwiches. Upon complaining, the waiter avoided our table.  Over priced for quality and service we had hoped to get.

Went here a few months back and the service was fantastic. This time, the waitress Brandi, was more I to socializing than waitressing. I ordered the biscuit breakfast that was supposed to come with ham, and egg, and potatoes, and why I got was a 2 day old dry biscuit. The waitress ignored us for the whole time until someone at the table flagged her down. When we told her I just got the biscuit, her response was "the kitchen messes up sometimes, I don't know what's going on back there." She didn't even offer another choice, but she took it off the bill. I ordered a Diet Coke, and it was clear I drank it, and she passed the table multiple times and never offered or brought a refill. But she brought the surrounding tables their refills. Also, our baked potato was dry

Service was absolutely terrible and the food was not very impressive. We waited a good 15 minutes for a server to come take our drink order, and then had three different servers wait on us. I will say that it was very clean and had a great atmosphere with the live music and line dancing!

I don't know what happened to my first review of this place..
I had mentioned one of the nicest things about this auditorium are the spaces between rows for long legged people, like myself.. I LOVE the space between rows.  
The seats are nice, also.
I've sat all over this auditorium except for upstairs.  I've sat in the handicapped aisles, in the front, in the center, on the sides.....  and next week, I'll be on the extreme aisle seat on the side of the auditorium, on the main floor..  (I'll review my seat next week)

It's easy to get in and out of this auditorium. Lots of doors, the aisles are wide enough that people can most faster and smoothly... right for the exit doors on the side that go directly out to the street.. Excellent movement in and out of the auditorium.

Sound is good. Good acoustics, no matter where you're sitting.
Bathrooms are downstairs... Not enough stalls.. Long lines are eminent.
Prices are reasonable.  Some plays begin at $25.

Lovely venue. Always filled when I have attended an event. All seats are good.

Took family visiting for a fun evening at the Nashville Palace -we ordered dinner took a long time to receive-it came a little too well done -excuse given to us was that the cook was frazzled-great atmosphere in regards to the music love the venue but the food had a lot of need for improvement at this point not sure if I'm going back

Nothing super fancy, but good fried bologna sandwich and sweet potato fries!! Music is ONLY 1975 and older country which isn't really my style, but still entertaining.  My wife had the mushroom swiss burger and regular fries and all was great!!  Not sure how the ratings are not better, we liked it a lot!!

You can't come to Nashville and not line dance! We asked around where to go and were led by locals and tourists alike to Wildhorse Saloon, not to be confused with dancing at The Crazy Horse Saloon. That could've been totally awkward waiting in line with the kiddos to get into there! :)

It's a HUGE space! It was the end of our day and a nice change from the squishy Honky Tonks we had been hopping in and out of all day. It was great to just spread out and have tables readily available. The rules were a tad strange.....I believe it's 21 and over with a cover after a certain time, (I cannot remember exactly what time that was though-sorry) and we arrived just before that time, about 15 minutes or so. Despite being with the kiddos we weren't asked to leave however. Ok, whatever. I'm not going to say anything. There was no line at all when we arrived, but quite a long one when we had left about an hour and a half later. 

The bands were fantastic!! I mean really good!! I kept feeling like I was stealing or something for not paying to get into what I would describe as a full on concert with lighting and everything! I mean, this was a show! They were even selling band merch (that's the lingo those of us who have been around the biz use). 

There was an instructor who led the dancing casually which was very easy to follow, even for my 7 year old. She LOVED it!!! Wouldn't leave in fact! Really fun!

There's table service and reserved seating towards the back bar and open, first come, first serve seating on both sides of the dance floor where you can bring the drinks and food you purchased at the bar. We got a table right away no problem. 

I enjoyed some local drafts which were good and fairly priced. I got the girls fried pickles because I felt bad they weren't patrons as we were getting such a great show. They were just ok. It was a huge bowl, one I don't know who could possibly finish. In fact we gave them to the table of ladies next to us we had made friends with. I would say if those pickles were any indication of the quality of food, skip the food and just do drinks and dancing. For that alone, this place is so great! 

The kitschy horses placed all around were a hoot and great for photos! Don't miss the ones on the ceiling! So fun! The kids loved these! 

I say it's a go! 
Come at night! 
Dance and get your 'boot skoot shuffle' on!
Fantastic tour/tasting led by Tommy for our large group of 11! Very cool place with a more intimate vibe than the big name bars right on Broadway.  We would all highly recommend this tour!

I live in the neighborhood and heard this place was under new ownership and the burgers were worth stopping by! They were right - I had a veggie burger and tator tots that were super great. However, I didn't love they still allowed smoking (I left with my clothes and hair smelling like it) and a pitcher of beer was $18. Previously (at least a year or two prior) the pitchers were only $6. Overall a nice little dive but I'll only revisit when I really need a burger fix, don't mind smelling like cigarettes and want a canned/bottled beer.

My family and I were visiting Tennessee and we wanted to try a place downtown Nashville. We know someone who works here and decided to give it a shot. We were told that the food was really good and we were not disappointed! I got the buttermilk fried chicken with mac and cheese and coke slaw. The fried chicken was really good, but y favorite part of the whole meal was the mac and cheese! It was probably some of the best mac and cheese that I have had at a restaurant! We also got the fried pickles app and it was sooo good! Definitely worth the extra cals for being fried! We also loved this place because it was just plain old fun! They had live music and they even do line dancing lessons! The instructor was easy to follow and we were able to pick it up pretty quickly! We were very happy with this place!

Extremely dead on a Wednesday night and the singer was HORRRRRRIBLE!!!!! For such a big place to have 10
customers is a shame. Looked like a fun place but maybe it was the extremely cold weather or random weekday.
Best burger in town. The last of the great neighborhood bars in Nashville.

I've been to Nashville many times over the years, lately I've been eating at Jack's BBQ. For some reason I decided to give Rippy's a try this time around, I wish I would have went across the street and eaten at Jacks.

My wife ordered the Pork loin melt on Texas toast, she ask the server about the seasoned curly fries, my wife was concerned about the seasoning. Come to find out the curly fries are frozen and pre-seasoned. The pork loin was dry, tough and had no smoke flavor. The curly fries were way too spicy for the wife.

I ordered the half slab of ribs with potato salad and baked beens. The potato salad tasted like it was a pre-prepared commercial product, the beens tasted like they opened a can then heated them up.

The ribs were an utter disappointment, they were way over cooked, had no smoke flavor, and no taste from the dry rub. The ribs tasted like they were made the day before and heated up in a steam table, which washed away any smoke or dry rub flavors.

The server was slow, she never even came over to see how everything was, I had to ask for the check. I spent a little over $30 for lunch and feel violated at the shoddy quality food. Next time I'll be eating at Jack's.
Such a great new spot! Awesome menu and good service. Very impressive whisky/bourbon selection! The artwork and design is very nice.

Awesome full slab of tasty bbq ribs & delectable chicken wings, excellent live music both country & contemporary, great beer selection & friendly atmosphere- what more can anyone ask for?  Thanks Rippys!

Wow, terrible service, took 10 minutes after being seated to get the opportunity to order coffee. The coffee was, at best mediocre. After ordering food, I waited 30 minutes and it wasn't hot, but it was bland. The table next to me sent their food back and asked if they could just pay for the coffee. They waited longer than I did for their order. 
I definitely cannot recommend this place.

Never been to Nashville and I was told we had to stop in and glad I listened. A huge plus was our teenage kids could join us. The food is excellent, line dancing lessons fun, the band that night was Cumberland Run. Great music. My review would have been a 4 and what made it a 5 was our waitress Jenna. Attentive, friendly and professional. The best waitress I've had in a long while!
Music was soso.  Service was friendy, food was bar food.  Catfish was very good.  Hot dogs not bad.  After 6:30 normally better music.

We stayed at the Cambria Hotel this past weekend and ended up frequenting the NashHouse for both breakfast and lunch.  We had great burger, amazing deviled eggs, and yummy fried pickles.  We were a group of ten everywhere we went so we weren't an easy table, but every waiter/waitress we had was accommodating, patient, and helpful.  We liked this place and would recommend it to others who stay in the hotel!

Had a great time. We called ahead to make sure they could accommodate a party of eight for dinner around 10 PM and were told no problem, but when we got the at 10:05 they told us the kitchen closed at 10 PM. I searched for someone to confirm and ended up speaking to Eric, who kindly said yes but he was sorry we had been told that and he would see what could be done and what the kitchen could do. A few minutes later we were seated and menus in our hands. No limitations. Jessica our waitress arrived with water and began taking our orders. I ordered the hot chicken and she kindly warned me that the chicken was hot, but the pickles were hotter and boy was she right!!! But it was still delicious!!!!

Jessica did a fabulous job, she was kind, friendly, and attentive. We had a great time eating, dancing, and listening to music, we even caught the tail end of the concert for the night! At the end I asked to speak to a manager wanting to express my appreciation for accommodating us and for the wonderful service and Eric (same guy from earlier) came over. He was just as kind as before and I made sure to let him know we appreciated them and had a fabulous time! I totally recommend this place!

This place is terrible, last time we were here we were "drug" because we did not buy drinks from the waiter, just the bar
Today we were meeting some friend and they did not let us in unless we walked a straight line, what a joke

We went with a large group and they were very accommodating for us and gave us great service! The deviled eggs were great along with the fried pickles. I ordered the cobb salad,  it was a good sized portion and really great.  My bf ordered the hot chicken and said it was great but he would've ordered one level hotter if he were to do it again.  Also, the SoCo Mule was a great cocktail and their beer list is huge.  We'll be back to try more!

Came to this bar to support my friends performance. Her music was great, of course, but dude, this bar sucks. The service was horrible. I had to find a server rather than her coming to my table. We asked for menus, she brought 1, for a party of 3. I'm sitting at the table now, I am waving at her trying to get her attention. We've been here for almost an hour and she's only gotten us 1 beverage. The bathrooms are unbelievably disgusting and you don't even want to wash your hands afterwards because there was no soap or drying materials. The server does not care even care about her job at all. Needless to say, we are leaving her zero tip and not going back.

This is my second visit to a Nashville and this place never disappoints. The love music. The food. The drinks. The lady LOVELY WOMAN who is the bathroom attendant , as well as the service. This place is great! Highly recommended.

Ordered a coke. Came in a cracked glass.  Waitress forgot one of the side orders we ordered.  Soda refills were supplied when we didn't ask for them, we were never told they aren't  free refills like in some restaurants.  The bill was large ,the servings were small..and we were made to feel like we were bring hustled.  I love Nashville, but there are so many other places to go...NashHouse should improve their game, on many levels.

I'm a fan of this local dive because it's not only in my neighborhood, but is super chill and always entertaining. Serves beer only and has a decent variety of burgers and fried guilty pleasure snacks. My only complaint is when it's crowded the smoke can be overwhelming, but then again that's why so many people enjoy this place as well. Cheers.

My husband and sister and I came here on Monday based on the big crowd upstairs. The waitress was kind but inexperienced. The food selections seemed okay. My husband ordered the pork loin melt and my sister and I had pulled pork on corn cakes. My husband and I shared some fried pickles and I had a few of his onion rings. The food was average, not horrible, but underwhelming. I only ate about a third of my meal and took the rest to go--but never ate the leftovers because....

Within two hours my husband and I were both violently sick with food poisoning. We were up all night with cramps, diarrhea and vomiting. This is the worst food poisoning I've ever had. I called the restaurant and asked to speak to the manager but when the girl asked why, and I told her it was regarding food poisoning she told me the manager was in a meeting. At 12? In the middle of the lunch hour? Not likely. They obviously don't care if the poison their customers.

The best thing Tpac has to offer is the staff. They are wonderful. However, the broadway group for Phantom couldn't beat the staff. Christine was nasal, didn't mesh with the phantom understudy. And his acting was sub par. The opera house owners were great and showed a great relationship of work. Carlotta stole the show with the best voice, which created an odd experience.

Three stars for dinner and 4 stars for the band/bar area.

The portions were HUGE but the food was fine. I got the pulled chicken and it was kind of dry. For a southern BBQ restaurant I expected the food to be flavorful and smokey but it was simply pulled chicken and the table has BBQ sauce for you to put on the meat on your own.

The bar area with the band was great and had fun vibes. The windows were open and the fan was on, which we appreciated since most bars in Nashville had been very hot and sticky. The only thing keeping me from giving the bar 5 stars is the pushy band singer. Our group was not used to tipping the bands in bars and didn't have cash. When we told her this she got in our faces and told us that she had Venmo. I'm sorry but we just walked up and didn't request any songs and I'm assuming you are getting paid by the venue to be here.

I love Soulshine! It's Mississippi owned, so that's a plus. I've been twice before, once at the Oxford location. Each time the food has been great. The most recent time I had the Marley pizza and bread pudding. Both are awesome! I wish they had a bigger selection of draft beer. I will definitely come back.

I visited the Wildhorse on a site visit to hold a conference in Nashville.  I sampled their BBQ and it was awesome.  The sauces were great and the meat was extremely tender.  This place is known for their fried pickles as well.  I did try one and it was good, but not something that I would eat on a regular basis.  

There are a large number of pool tables and other bar games with plenty do space.
Awesome food and outstanding service! Ask for Shonnie, she's the best! Love this new spot. Highly recommend

Downtown Nashville is rather dirty, but the best part of it is The Wildhorse Saloon.  A huge venue with three floors including live music, line dancing lessons, a family environment and great food.  

We ordered the fried pickles to start off.  Tasty.   I had the Tennessee BBQ duo and my husband had the Stampede platter.  Their brisket is outstanding - tender and juicy with just the right amount of spice, and the pulled pork was deliciously smoky. They offer three types of sauce - mustard, spicy and sweet all three are tasty in their way.  

The stampede platter offers the same pulled pork and brisket but adds a half rack of tender, delicious ribs rubbed with the right amount of spice and grilled with sorghum molasses.  De-Lish!

If you have kids traveling with you, they are welcome and will have a great time. Mine took line dancing lessons and left with a huge smile on her face.  Cute stuff in their shop too.  Tourist place??  Yes but worth it.

Multi-level restaurant and live music bar. Usually a very fund and high quality band in the smaller lower level bar. We had good BBQ bar food here and really enjoyed the atmosphere. 
Not fancy, but lots of fun. Can get very crowded on first floor, but grab a table if you can.

I really enjoy this place. 

The wait is never too terrible and there is always room at the bar while you wait for a table. 

On site valet? Yes please! I love not worrying about parking. Valet staff is always courteous and prompt. (ie: these guys haul ass).

I enjoy the drinks at Soulshine but I what I love most is their casual atmosphere, live local music and tons of delicious pizza options! I also really really love that they will customize an order. Yes. I'm that girl.

Sitting outside on the upstairs (covered) patio is my favorite location. I enjoy Friday nights with Lightening 100 and I have never tasted a pizza that I did not enjoy! The names are clever - and I do enjoy a clever menu - and the flavors are always scrumptious. I go in knowing I will most likely overindulge in cheesy breaded goodness.

Also, I really like their logo/the font used for the name. 

Nutshell:
Order the "Sleeps with the Fishes" pizza. Ah.mazing. 
Definitely go. It's a cool hang.
Great food which came out surprisingly fast. Especially for how large the place is and how busy it was on a Friday night. The service was on point as well.
First time at Nash House and it didn't disappoint! Had the best time listening to Hannah Rose and the food was amazing! Chicken Fried Chicken is fantastic!

September was my fourth month living in Nashville, and in one week, I made it to TPAC THREE TIMES! Seriously.

I went to a live taping of NPR's Ask Me Another at War Memorial Auditorium (a TPAC event), a production of the musical "Evita," and a production of the ballet "Cinderella." All of the events were amazing, and I feel pretty lucky to live in a city that has such an amazing arts and culture center right downtown! 

The theaters are beautiful (there several theaters contained with TPAC, often with performances at the same time - Evita and Cinderella overlapped both nights I was at TPAC). Perfectly elevated seats for short girls like me! Comfortable seats, simple decor, good acoustics. 

Something new for me: they let you take your drinks INTO the theaters. I guzzled my glass of wine (which was kind of expensive, but are you surprised? I wasn't) during the intermission, because I'm used to theaters where liquids aren't allowed back in, only to find out that I could have sipped it classily in my seat rather than treating it like a shot of wine in the lobby. Oops. Now I know (I got a "double" of white wine at the performance of Cinderella and drank it in my seat slowly like a lady). 

Right downtown, just across from the Hermitage Hotel. My goal next time is to have a drink in the fancy bar in the hotel and then walk over for the performance. Parking can be difficult/expensive. TPAC has valet, and there are lots and garages all around. It's really up to your preference and cheapness. I'm more of a park a couple of blocks away and walk kind of a girl (except in summer, hello valet driver). 

TPAC has amazing events - ballets, musicals, plays. Nashville has everything, and TPAC has some of the city's most amazing shows! I had a great time at all three of the events I went to that were put on by TPAC, and I know I'll be back. Sound of Music? Rent? The Book of Mormon? All this upcoming season. I'll be there for at least one! I know it!

Basically I'm not a fan of anyone screaming. Especially with a voice while screaming that sounds like two cats in heat trying to bone each other. 

Why am I talking about cats boning each other in a review of Soulshine Pizza? 

Well, I've avoided the place like the plague because of those commercials they have playing on local radio with the pastor sounding dude screaming about pizza and beer. I love pizza. I love beer.I just don't like being shouted at. So, I was really fighting an inner battle. Some people have battles over doing right and wrong. Me? I have battles over choosing between beer and pizza and a man shouting at me on the radio. 

As you can see, I lead an important life. 

But! My parents had been adamant in how I needed to try the place. And, the most important part. They were buying and I'm a cheap b@stard, so why not?!

SIDENOTE - I knew it had to be good, because my dad has the temper of a rabid wolverine and snaps on a dime like Randy Macho Man Savage snapping into Slim Jim's... He will stew and steam HOURS after an incident that has set him off and let the smallest things ruin hours of a day. So, when he told me he had went and gotten into a heated argument with my mom and an attendant of a parking lot about the parking for the restaurant and then went into ' but man, I just loved the pizza '. I knew at that point, they must grind up unicorn horns and sprinkle them atop the pizzas, to pull off that kind of magic behavior out of my dad, for him to let an argument go under the table and enjoy his dining experience. pure magic

We all decided to go there on a Saturday, my kids and girlfriend in tow... We parked a few streets over and made the trek through alleys and unwalkable walkways. I made an audible groan as we approached the front of the building and saw the national meeting of douchesicles and douchebros all gathered outside in front, celebrating St Patty's Day. 

My son, who is 15, inquired why I moaned and I told him and he told me to chill. After backhanding him * I kid, I kid * He goes " but why are they all dressed in green for St Patty's Day on a Saturday? Even if you're celebrating it today instead of Monday, there's literally no reason to wear green, noone is going to pinch you and say ' you're not wearing green on St Patty's Day ' , because IT'S NOT ST PATTY'S DAY!!! " I just told him to chill. And that ' logic and reason cannot be brought into the douchebag realm. All that goes out the window if you notice the jeans they wear. what kinda dude wears jeans so tight his balls are being crushed into his scrote? ' He looked at me and laughed and goes ' good point ' ....I must point out he was wearing green neon sunglasses.. Yes, it seems I might be raising a FDA.Future D-Bag of America. But! Not if I can help it. 

Anyways. We walk inside, it wasn't busy. 3 pm on a Saturday. To be expected. Live music was playing upstairs and I suggested we sit downstairs because A. I don't wanna shout while eating to my kids and parents and B. Girls like musicians, no matter how terrible they are, and I didn't wanna risk or expose my perfect little 12 year old princess to her first taste of this weirdo musical magic that every hack singer and musician seem to posses. I wasn't risking it.

It's a nice place on the inside and while not the roomiest dining area, it's adequate. Music paraphernalia on the walls. My dad kept on raving about Joe Cocker and my son just kept snickering going ' COCKer ' I didn't know who had the three beers. My dad or my son. One kept raving about the musical stylings of Joe Cocker - meaning you have to be drunk - and the other was laughing over a little tawdry name humor.

Me and the son ordered The Carnivore. We like meat. We're men. We don't wear skinny jeans, we arm wrestle to settle disputes and we don't get manicures and we don't refer to places with names like ' the gulch ' or ' sobro ' and we have chest hair. Hence, why we ordered the meatiest meat pizza. My parents got some Garlic Ranch Chicken pizza and the girlfriend and daughter shared some girly looking pizza with olives and peppers and pepperoni. 

Vegetables deserve to be on a pizza, if you're eating it in hell. Or a girl... 

Me and the sons and the parents pizzas were GREAT. I never tried the girls pizza, because Bruce Willis is my hero and he would have just shook his head like a disappointed father if I had dared to eat such a wimpy, girly pizza and call myself a man afterwards. But hey! The girls said they loved it... 

Plus, Anytime a place has Sweetwater Blue on tap, they instantly become the ' best ' of whatever their specialty is. If there was a place where you could go to get kicked in the groin, but they had sweetwater blue on tap, that place, in my world, would then be referred to as ' The best place ever to get kicked in the groin ' 

Good Pizza. Good Beer. They even played Rocky Top while I was eating. Utopia? Is that you?

Music was great.  Drinks were a complete rip off, Rippy's? Rippy's you off, yes. Bring a ton of money.  I got two vodka tonics, $10 each for a small plastic cup...okay, to be expected.  So I ordered two doubles for my son and I as I wanted a larger cup.  Got two 12 oz plastic cups of vodka tonic, $21 each.... we had eight total drinks and our tab was $120 for eight drinks.  Holy smokes a single is $10 and a double is $21...should have called the police for them stealing my money.  Atmosphere was great, music was great but the drinks are a scam.  If you win Powerball, then go here.

We were thrilled with our Christmas Eve Dinner at NashHouse. We enjoyed the Deviled Eggs - 5 ways, biscuits and jam, and our entrees. The real winner was the banana pudding . The live music was a wonderful touch and we appreciated that it was family-friendly. Our waiter was fantastic and promptly took care of us!

Pizza was really good.  Lots of great beers on tap.  We went on a Sunday afternoon, so it was pretty calm.  Service was consistent and friendly.  I've had some trouble finding decent pizza since I moved to Nashville, but Soulshine is going in the right direction.

Was here on a Friday night of Labor Day weekend.   First the place was not filled but they had no wait staff.  We seated ourselves and waited for someone to come and serve us.  Took 30 minutes.  Had to keep reminding them that we had no service.  When we did get service, was the worst ever seen.  People dropped off food but no silverware or dishes.  Had to ask several people continually for silverware of which they said they ran out of! We got salads and no dressing.  Once again had to find someone to get dressing.  Not sure we will return.

Great place to visit while on vacation! We sat at the bar for drinks our first afternoon in Nashville and Matt, our bartender was outstanding! He was friendly, professional and gave us tips on where to visit while in Nashville. He took his time explaining all about Nashville to us and the drinks were great! Excellent place!

Now that's some good pizza!!

And super friendly staff as well!

Visiting a friend over the weekend and she took us to Soul Shine. The 2 outside patios are great...especially the upper deck with the live music playing. How fun. I tried the Greek pizza and added pepperoni and mushrooms because I'm a supreme freak. It hit the spot. The 8' is the perfect personal size and for under $10? Yes please.

Nice atmosphere. I liked how open it is. And the pizza was really delicious.

Great music horrible staff! Purposely ignored my friends and I until kitchen was closed so they wouldn't have to put in any more food orders. We wait 45 min and know asked us even if we wanted a drink.

I was in the mood for BBQ and the place was busy so I figured I'd try it. I sat at the first floor bar and the server was friendly but nothing happened quickly - possibly cause they were changing bartenders. 
I ordered the 1/2 slab which came with two sides. The ribs come out dry rubbed and the y provide you a tangy and hot sauce that you can squeeze on. To me the tangy sauce was the best of the two. The ribs looked good and they were meaty but if it were not for the sauce I added they lacked flavor. The side of mac and cheese was really creamy and the pasta was not overcooked (I hate mushy pasta) so i enjoyed that. The second side of collard greens was cooked perfectly but lacked the ham flavor and needed salt. The cornbread was really just a small muffin that was not good at all as it was gummy and had zero taste.
It seemed like a good place to have a few drinks but as for the food I am sure there is much better Que in the area.
As a side note, once the band got playing it was pretty difficult to hear.

Very much looked forward to trying out this new place--attached to the Cambria hotel--before a Preds game. We are always looking for good options for a pre-game meal, and there are plenty east of the arena to choose from. This place just two blocks west of the arena showed promise but failed in the food. 

Service was prompt, friendly. Beer selection emphasized solid local choices. Thus far so good.

But then the food. The better half found the veggie plate lacking in taste but adequate. the Cowboy burger was another matter--when it arrived it was burnt--perhaps the driest piece of beef I have had in sometime. We were shocked-- the waiter asked "pink or not"-- we clearly said pink. He acknowledged that but then the kitchen had such poor oversight that order preference meant nothing--for a $16 burger. 

Game time neared so sending it back was not an option--a reality well apparent to the kitchen on a busy game night. So they sent out a ruined meal. Shame on them--they not only disappointed us but let down their waiters who were working a big room as efficiently as possible. 

Imagine I will stay on the east side of the arena in the future before arena events

3+ Super new place, it was pretty quiet on a Tuesday night when we were there, which worked out as we had a large group. I had the Nash burger, which was pretty good - could have had a bit more flavor. Friends had the catfish, which looked delicious and they enjoyed. The corncake came out like a super hard disc and we were quite sure what we were dealing with. The manager corrected that and got new ones served, which were better. Overall, the meal was pretty good, service was great and I appreciated their commitment to doing a good job. The place has a huge TV and stage right up front. It should be interesting to see how it pans out.

Really attractive restaurant/bar. really enjoyed the atmosphere and live bands. With the screen playing country music videos while in between artists. We weren't very hungry so my husband got the fried pickles (they weren't  his favorite bec it wasn't much pickle more crust. They're shaved really thin) but was a decent size appetizer portion. I got the club salad which was very good club salad. Waiter wasn't the friendliest but I forgot his name and he wasn't very knowledgeable , I asked if there was gluten free beer and he said no/I don't know then upon looking at the menu I did find one on there only after I closed my check and was leaving. Would come back again ! They will validate your parking if you park at the Cambria hotel connected to the restaurant which is big beings parking cross the street is 20$ for 2 hours. Next tim id like to stay at the cambria hotel but it was booked.
Best chicken fried steak I've had in years!! Most items on the menu weren't appealing to me. Wouldn't go back unless I wanted another CFS.

Food is great, atmosphere is great, service can be inconsistent. We ate here four times during our recent trip to Nashville because it was on the first floor of our hotel. For the most part, service was good, but not great.

Edit: I'm changing from 2 stars to 1 star. I submitted a review on Facebook and the owners went on and replied with a snide comment instead if the standard 'we are sorry you had a bad experience. We will take your review in to consideration to improve, please have a pizza on us' but no. 

Edit No. 2: (15/7/2014) 
Through the social media grapevine, another person had a bad experience and took to their Facebook page and wrote the review.  What followed was a social media meltdown à la Amy's Baking Company. Accusations flying and bite back from the company. Truly an unraveling of any good word of mouth they had. If I could give zero stars I would. 

The review: 

I've been here three times. First time I enjoyed it. Loved the mufalatta. Second time: different story. I ordered a pizza since it's actually called soulshine pizza. Bad mistake. 

Pizza was wet,  the crust was undone. I was in a party of ten. Everyone said the place sucked. I asked for extra fresh minced garlic. On the pizza was whole garlic cloves that were cooked with the pizza. One, not fresh. Two not minced. Ugh. 

None in our party could stomach the aspiring country artist playing upstairs. I know this is midtown but no one likes that. Just please stop. 

Third time I tried the carnivore. The pizza was at least better. The music was better too. It was a band playing old jazz tunes. 

Service was good and the waitstaff have always gotten 25% from me despite the error on the second visit. 

One star for:
Being extra douchey in replying on Facebook. Go look it up yourself if you are so inclined. Unless they delete their comment. 

Their slogan is something idiotic like 'born in the dirty south' these fools have dirty manners to go along with it. 

They also get knocked down a bunch of pegs because of the huge 10 x 6 painting of the lead singer of Nicklelback at the entrance.
Very good barbecue place staff was very friendly and our food came out really quickly. Prices are good for the amount of food you get.
Ridiculously expensive place to grab a drink before a show at the Ryman. Music was good. Service comparable to an airport bar.

Really disappointed.  The restaurant was dead... only. A few diners, yet wait service was slow and dinner took forever.  I ordered Shrimp and Grits. Very disappointing.   Grits were okay but sauce was way too strong and peppery (which I typically love).  Not much food for $25!

The place seemed to be in general disarray. Sunday afternoon, not very busy at all, half the dining room was empty but yet there's a line 15 deep waiting to be seated. We(2 of us) sat at the bar to avoid the seating issue and got an attitude from the bar keep that we were an inconvenience to her and to add to that it took her 10 min to come take our drink order. If the service wasn't complete shit I could see this place being fun.

Live music, 3 levels, friendly free line dancing instructions for all ages, don't leave without trying their ribs!! I would skip the dry wings they were disappointing, staff super flexible and seated our group of 20 without a hitch at about 530pm, waitress was a dream

We were there for a work lunch.  The place is massive and full of funny full size horses that make for great photo ops.  The stage is large and they had good live music for us on a Wed during lunch.  They also do line dancing and line dancing lessons there throughout the day.

Now the food...they set up a buffet for us.  There was salad, pulled pork, baked beans and rolls.  It was ok.  The baked beans were great.  The spicy sauce that you can put on the pulled pork is nice and spicy.  The salad was not very fresh.  

They may have another menu that has great food, I'm not sure.

I am surprised Rippy's does not get more love. I think the venue is pretty fun, there were musicians in multiple room with their own sound and you could go from room to room listening to your heart's content. When I went, there was a more folksy woman in one room and more rock band in the other. I love that! I ordered some food to go and I have to say, the pulled pork sandwich was probably the best smoked meat I had my entire trip in Nashville. By that I mean you would actually taste the smoke compared to other bbq places where you didn't really get that flavor. Although, also to be fair, the meat was not that moist and was a bit dry. Never fear though, they had plenty of sauces to help with that and the sauces were good. The beans were also really good. Overall, this was probably not as good as the other bbq joints but the music was awesome and the meat actually had a smoked flavor so I think it deserves more love than it has been getting!

I would have given 5 stars. But. The kitchen forgot to send out the appetizer. However,  the food we did get was absolutely fantastic. Zack was our waiter and was very informative, willing to go the extra mile to ensure you got what you wanted. I look forward to my next visit. In a town with hot chicken on every street. They really can compete with the best of them.

We went for the Lightning 100 Friday happy hour and trivia contest. The location is great and we sat upstairs on the outside deck. We had a great time and happy hour offers 2 dollar domestic beer bottles and some discounts on well drinks. I ordered wings to start as I am a wing fan especially at a place that I have not tried. I only ordered 6 buffalo style with blue cheese. My wife who is gluten free had the hummus with veggies. My wife enjoyed her app, l was a bit disappointed by my room temperature wings that did not taste fresh. We then ordered the a small GF with anchovies and spinach which my wife loved. I had the ham and pineapple medium pizza which had canned pineapple which was a bummer. The crust was ok but overall flavor was lacking. I liked the overall atmosphere and had a great time participating in the trivia. I may be too old and expect too much from food I eat in Nashvegas but I will continue on my journey of exploring new venues.
The service and food was just ok. The ribs were overdone and small for price. I left hungry! Great music venue and drinks.

Well, I wasn't impressed.  The 17$ burger was less than edible.  It was dry, over cooked and made me thing they just had a bunch of precooked patties like Waffle House.  The server(bless his heart) disappeared for :30 and the asst entertainment manager had to get drinks for us.  We took our friend from out of town out when she got into the airport.  Reason 2002 why I don't go eat downtown at tourist traps.  There are better places downtown. And I suggest you scout them out.

The service was horribly slow. It took an hour to get a side of fries for the table. Food was good it just took forever to get it. Live band was ok but all the songs they played were slow and depressing. Did not enjoy my time here.

We came here for a private corporate party and it was awesome!! Plenty of space, great view of stage on 1st ,2nd, and 3rd floor. There is a bar on all 3 levels - all of the staff were quick and curteous. Very spacious venue, overall great place.

The food was awesome as well. They set up self -serve buffets on all 3 levels. BBQ was great - chicken and tri tip. Mac and cheese was delicious. Plain and cheesy garlic dinner rolls. Salad with topping bars. Multiple bbq sauces to pick from. Desert was assorted mini pies and peach cobbler - absolutely delicious.

The food here was GREAT and the atmosphere & decor was a lot of fun.  The only thing preventing this from a 5th star is a few minor service issues, but everyone is entitled to a bad night on occasion.  I would definitely go back if I ever find myself in the Nashville area again.

The Wildhorse is a good time. Went on Saturday night, kind of early. Line dancing lessons in between band sets. Everyone gets out on the floor. Mix of country, pop, and hip hop to line dance to. The band was phenomenal (Adairs Run). My only criticism - we started out on the 3rd floor, where I'm guessing there is no wait staff. The glasses, bottles, plates, half finished just sat and were never cleaned up. We eventually moved downstairs, but it was a little unsanitary.

Just happened upon this place after sight seeing in the area. Walked in and heard music so I was intrigued. Well they were having a live broadcast for a radio station and featured a couple of entertainers. My friend and I took a seat and enjoyed great music while eating lunch. I had a mushroom burger with sweet potato fries. Both were exceptionally good. Fries were crispy and cooked to perfection. I would definitely return for both the food and the entertainment!

Looking for a place to eat. Settled on Rippy's. Very loud. Food served on paper plates. Plastic utensils. Food was ok. Was going well until my wife reach for a napkin and had a insect fell off of it and crawled across our table. Won't be back
Great place for family fun and line dancing , the food is excellent, got vip service roped off for us , saw a horse at the bar and i will post that photo soon.
Poor service. Took forever to get our food. Unfortunately the food was not worth the wait. Food was hot just not a destination for food. Entertainment was nice. Great band

We just stopped in by chance after eating at Oak Steakhouse for dinner, and we're pleasantly surprised! This spot wasn't too busy on a Thursday night, but would probably get packed if there's a convention or something in town. The bartenders made the drinks perfectly, and the live music was top notch! The gentleman that booked the talent was so polite and friendly, and the musicians that night (Natalia Taylar and Knox Morris) were better than some big headliners we've paid a lot of money to see! I hope they go far! Such a fun night!

A large group of us were staying at Loews Vanderbilt for a wedding.   Since we arrived the night before, we wanted a nice but yet convenient place within walking distance to eat.   A young man at the bar recommended a couple option, but pizza sounded wonderful.   So we took the 15 minute walk over.  

We were early diners, so we had the pick of the place.  Landing upstairs.   Great choice for Trivia Night.   

The menu had many Italian favorites, so with 10 diners we ran the gamut.   Everything was great.   I would recommend the meatballs for an appetizer if you are gingery and ready for a starter.    It is more for two.  A friend pick spaghetti, and it looked wonderful.  My husband and I did a "build your own" pizza.  Doubled the pepperonis....fabulous!   

Around 7:00, Trivia night switches over to live music.   I would highly recommend this place.

Us tourists stopped by here on a tip from a local friend, since our desired spot was packed.  We were really just in the mood for good BBQ, and this happened to be nearby.  

I'll just start off by saying this isn't really a dinner restaurant.  It's more of a bar that serves food.  This isn't necessarily a bad thing, but it's not quite what we had in mind.  

The drinks were fine, but we weren't super thrilled with the quality of the BBQ food.  Between us, we had pulled pork and pulled chicken sandwiches w/ french fries and slaw sides.  The food was really nothing to write home about, even though they provided BBQ Sauce to coat it with.  The service was a tad off; we had to wait quite a while for our bill (couldn't find our waiter).  I didn't know places still served RC Cola!

I'm not really gonna write much about the live band or the local beers, you can find these in almost every building on the street.  Not sure I would come back, given some of the other options in the area.

This is the worst experience I have had at a Nashville restaurant. My family and I waited for over an hour for appetizers and even complained to a manager and little was done to accommodate us except for a "I'm sorry - it's been a busy day". 
Save your time and go to another establishment.

This place is a bit of a shit hole to be honest. The live music was terrible. We sat through 3 hours of a early 20 somethings duo doing bad country covers, they had little guitar playing skills and their voices were even worse. Out of all the bars we visited in Nashville this was the only one I can remember having blatantly awful music.

The saving grace is the upstairs open floor patio. 

Food look gross.

Been here twice in three days. So depends on what you are coming here for. Drinks and live music?? 5 stars. Two levels with three bands. Staff in the bar is very good. Drinks are strong. If you are coming to a "Sports Bar" to watch a game? Then one star. More of a music venue but you are in Nashville so go figure. Music is so loud you can't talk to the person across the table about the game. No audio for the game although there is subtitles. Food is super average. Nothing special at all. You can find the same fare anywhere. Lots of TV's is the only thing that keeps it at three stars.

The staff is rude, unhelpful, harassing, hateful, mean....won't let you enjoy a show without being bugged by the staff constantly.  They pick and choose who to harass, and will step on your feet to get across 40 people to tell one person not to video with a freaking cell phone.

Went here for dinner last night.  Had the Southwest burger and it was great.  The mustard/vinegar bbq sauce was amazing.  

The atmosphere was a lot of fun.  There is a huge stage with live music and a big dance floor with plenty of tables to be served to eat at.  Upstairs was a little more low key with a view of the excitement downstairs.  Upstairs was a little more laid back bar type atmosphere with pool, shuffle board, and other bar games.  I was also told they are in the processes of a huge renovation so it sounds like it's only going to get better.

Went for dinner and were promptly seated outside as the inside with the loud music was not conducive to my friend and I talking. We mentioned our scoutmob deal and were told "we aren't using scoutmob anymore and we're actually suing them because they won't take our deal down"

I get that there can be trouble between companies and what not. But if your deal is online and live, you should honor it. This left us with a sour taste in our mouth but we decided to stay. 

We ordered the southwest pizza and it was delicious! Ate about half of it and took the rest home. Tasted even better as leftovers!

SLOW. Waited over an hour for our apps... which never came out. Our dinner came out in about 90 minutes and it was so bland. They ended up comping the whole meal but it wasn't worth it.
Don't go, don't waste your time or your hunger on mediocre food.

Our flight back to Baltimore was canceled and our next available flight was 10 hours from the current flight time (noon became 10pm.) We decided on Wildhorse for some lunch. We explained to the waiter our situation, and he waited on us for 5.5 hours! We left him a nice tip, which didn't compare to the generosity he gave to us. Plus, the food was slammin as always!

Awesome little barbecue joint right off of the Broadway strip! I had the pork loin melt with Cajun fries and a side order of ribs.  Everything was awesome smokey BBQ goodness and the environment was even better! There was always a stream of people coming in and out, just enjoying their time and good food! Always a live band on stage to give you some entertainment while you enjoy your food!

Check it out!

Great location located right on Broadway.  Service was actually pretty good for as busy as it is inside.  Music (of course) was awesome.

The food is good, and plentiful.  Brisket was above average but the pulled pork required copious amounts of bbq sauce.  I would give it 3.5 stars if I could.  Good, not great but certainly plentiful.
Came here for a conference. We had the whole place to ourselves. It was awesome. Good food, music, and beer. What is better than that!!!

For anyone thinking of attending Shen Yun at TPAC. I went and left angry.
This show is advertised as a cultural performance of traditional Chinese music, dance and song. What it turned out to be, about $180 bucks for 2 tickets later, was a heavy handed propaganda piece for the Falun Gong a religious sect in China. That would be fine if I knew that going in, but there is no mention of it's real agenda on any flyers, anywhere in their ad campaign.
Hope this might save someone the $ and the "I've been had" feeling that my date and myself left with last year.
We came for the line dancing classes. The instructor was awesome and so much fun with our group. I would recommend for a girls party group.

Great music, beer and food! This place is always a ton of fun! It's not as packed as others. It's also more open, being on the corner, so you don't feel like your in a dark hole, which is great. The music is fun and pretty good and interactive. They have 2 floors and each one was great. The food is bbq, of course, and it's good with a ton of it. Overall our favorite place on Broadway in Nashville.

Awful. I had a chicken flavored salt sandwich. Baked beans were okay, maybe 2 stars. My wife wasn't really hungry so she ordered a pb&j. It was actually a smuckers uncrustable slathered in butter and warmed on the griddle. Beer selection is pretty poor. Tourist hell.

In Nashville for a few days and asked the hotel staff where we can go for a local experience. They suggested the Nashville Palace which was nearby.

Practically have to tackle a server to get any service, but that may only be if you're not a local/regular. The mixed drinks are expensive,but there was no cover charge.  

The place has a lot of history with some famous country singers playing here in their early days. It is definitely a honky-tonk bar playing a lot of old rockabilly music. Normally this is not my kind of place, but we actually had a pretty good time listening to the music and people watching.
Came into the restaurant the other day had a great time Amy served me and was awesome sauce will return as soon as possible and hope she's working

Anytime I have to hunt down staff to resolve a problem, I know it's going to be a bad experience. 

My boyfriend and I got tickets to see Free Beer and Hot Wings Live at Night. I paid $25 each for two tickets (total $75.90 with fees) that were listed as "tickets are reserved seating on main floor rows 5 and back along with elevated booth areas" on the Wildhorse Saloon website. 
When we arrived at the venue we were quickly ushered upstairs and told that we had access to the second and third floor. We could go anywhere on the 2nd floor except the railing (which was assigned seating). Once we reached the second floor, we saw that there were no tables open so we moved to the 3rd floor which was standing room only. Initially, I thought that I had purchased the wrong tickets, so we found a spot to stand and my boyfriend went to go get us drinks at the "bar" which was a single file line leading up to two bartenders (unsure why it was set up like this. Maybe just for special events?) it was odd and made the process of ordering a drink a total pain. It took over 30 mins for him to get us two diet cokes. He placed an order for fried pickles at this time as well and we were given an order number.
