On my most recent visit with a co-worker we opted to sit outside, because the weather was nice. Perhaps it's due to the fact that we were outside, but our service wasn't great. The restaurant definitely wasn't busy during our visit, so this was a bit frustrating. Our table was also very lopsided, and though we pointed this out we weren't given the option to move, though we were the only two people sitting outside. 

I ordered a Coke and opted for the Grilled Catfish Tacos, which were served with pickled vegetables, white bbq sauce, and avocado, and they came with a side of fries. The food was pretty good, but it wasn't anything special. I struggled getting my drink refilled, which goes back to the service issues we were experiencing. 

Overall, I'd say if you're in the area and looking for a lunch or dinner spot, I think there are likely better options around than NashHouse.

Great ambience, service and food! I went during lunch with a coworker. The server was awesome and gave us a quick run down of the menu. We both ordered the grilled catfish tacos. It's included two tacos with grilled catfish, pickled vegetables, white bbq sauce, avocados and of course french fries. I never had grilled catfish tacos before but it was love at first bite. You definitely want to go and get those amazing tacos!!

We love to come here on Fridays for happy hour. They have lighting 100 come in and broadcast live and they have trivia and fun games with great prizes. They also have half hour apps and draft beer until 6.  
The food is good, and they have an Ok draft list. 
We have a blast playing games and winning prizes!

One complaint I have is that every single time we've been here, we've had to get up to track down our waiter to pay our tab. Once the radio station event is over, the waiters seem to completely disappear-sometimes for a solid 30 minutes. It is so frustrating. We've even tried closing our tab early to avoid the rush at the end of event, but even that didn't help. I think a lot of it has to do with the splitting of checks with big groups. I'd recommend the waiters talk to the group at the beginning of the evening and asking how they want to handle to check so at the end it can go much smoother. 

Other than that, we love it here and will continue to come back!

Got to tag along on an amazing mini Tennessee trip.  Being the weirdo I am I instantly fell in love with the horse statues.  The atmosphere and decor gave me high hopes for this place.

The staff was friendly.  I always find with restaurant staff you get what you give.  My group was happy and we were treated with kindness.

I got to try 3 different things: the bbq ribs, a bite of Mac & cheese, and their fried pickles.  I love bbq and anytime I get the chance to try ribs I go for it.  They were good.  Coming from a northern state tjat has a lot of people who try to succeed at bbq I've tried a lot of good and bad ribs.  These weren't my favorite but I can see myself ordering then again if I lived in the area.  The fried pickles though?  Those were incomparable to any other friend pickles.  So good.  You have to get them.

Overall just a fun spot.

Went to watch the Mayweather v. McGregor fight last night. Watched a brown guy get kicked out. All my brothers should frequent this establishment. They are down with the cause.
#BlueLivesMatter

The restaurant is at a decent location, and the environment is pretty chill but the food is subpar. Did not meet my expectations of Nashville barbecue at all.

Choices:
Beignets
BBQ brisket sandwich
BBQ pork plate
BBQ sauce is clumpy, would've rather had generic brand
Had a great time at the Wild Horse!  Oscar behind the bar was awesome!   He made sure all our girls had a drink and laughs!   Highly recommend going to!!

This place has everything you want in Nashville. I went for a school trip and we all wanted something to eat and just sit and have fun, the food was to die for the entertainment was by far the live music I've heard in a long time and there was so much you could do in a little building. There was even pool tables and fuseball. The gift shop is loaded with merchandise that one would want to buy. From a tourist point of view this is defently my highly suggested place to visit or even a first stop. They even have line dancing!! The instructor was very kind and considerate and fun. He took the dancing slow for everyone who didnt know how to dance and made it fun. Everyone participated from my school and we all had a blast. I defenetly plan on eating here again.
Stopped in for a quick bite on Sunday night. Staff was very friendly and nice. The food was awful. Stick to drinks only.
Ambience and music was fantastic. I had a great time line dancing. However, the food is a let down and what prevents me from giving this a five star rating.
Loved the line dancing lessons, food, drinks and atmosphere.  Great time here in Nashville
(Almost) lifetime resident. Best burger I've had in Nashville, hands down. And it's consistently on the highest level every single time I go.

My girlfriend and I came to Nashville for a weekend getaway, and we happened to come across the Wildhorse Saloon while walking through the city. It's a huge place with 3 levels and plenty of seating. The stage area was impressive. It's a great place to watch a show and most of the patrons seemed to enjoy the line dancing. 

But this place gets a 1-star from me because I'm convinced that it's just a fancy tourist trap. The food and drinks were horrendous. I ordered the fried chicken with a side of baked beans and mac and cheese, while my girlfriend ordered smoked sausages and BBQ chicken. Our food was out in less than 5 minutes. The food seemed like they went to a local grocery store deli. It was all lukewarm, bland, and dry. The baked beans came out barely warm. The mac and cheese tasted like it came from a Kraft box. I tried their apple brown betty. They took pieces of generic sliced bread, and put baked apples over it with a small scoop of whipped cream. There were also no raisins in it at all like it said on the menu. It was pretty awful and I couldn't finish it.

This place is a scam. The prices are way too expensive for the quality of the food we received. Thankfully we got there just before they started the $6 cover charge. Stay far away from this place if you're just looking for a place to eat. There are much better and cheaper options.
Fun bar and good live music. Wouldn't go here to eat- but if you want to grab some drinks in a cool Nashville atmosphere - go for it.

Nice new place. Good stage for live music. Got a table right away but the service was lacking. Chicken was decent but not $22/chicken. Out of very common bottled beers .  PA is could come down 15db . Mix for the room not the packed house it was not.

Bartender is the most bad ass bartender I ever met! She made our whole experience! Shout out to Elle for giving us the best time at the bar! It was so busy because of first Georgia game and she was able to give everyone the attention they needed!

Atmosphere was great, our seat was next to opened French doors on second floor, so was able to watch was going out side. 
   Food was excellent, and portions were very large, more than enough. Service was good, it was packed, but the server was great. 
    Great time, and will eat there again!!!
Great Saloon atmosphere. The waitstaff is extremely friendly and a pleasure. The music is fantastic without being overbearing

So, I feel compelled to give a shout out here for customer service, kindness and of course, great shows. My family and I buy 4-5 shows per season had a little mix up with one of the shows, and when you're talking 7 seats, that's a good deal of coin, suffice to say, the Senior Manager Akil Lyle absolutely made right, the wrong and...was a total doll about it. Highly recommend taking your kids/young people to a live show, TPAC has something for everyone and, they truly DO care about you and want you to enjoy the show. BEST customer care I have ever received.
Watch the band Two Way Crossing. Great show bar. Large dance floor, great food good prices. Will definitely come back! Pictures aren't the best because of lighting.
This place is great! Definitely a good find and I will be coming back with friends soon.
Do not waste your hard-earned money on their dinner show.  The food was NOT worth the high ticket price.  The show was mediocre in variety and quite frankly, monotonous and boring.

The best thing Tpac has to offer is the staff. They are wonderful. However, the broadway group for Phantom couldn't beat the staff. Christine was nasal, didn't mesh with the phantom understudy. And his acting was sub par. The opera house owners were great and showed a great relationship of work. Carlotta stole the show with the best voicwhich created an odd experience. People need to understand broadway isn't the be all end all. It's the beginning.

Rippy's is a RIP-OFF!! Their regular drink was in like a 6oz plastic cup for $10! Ordered a double and on my bill it was freakin $21 unreal !  They should pay their bands to play if they are charging prices like this.  We talked to other visitors from London that were also disgusted with their food and drink prices.  They had a great band( Mantzel bros from WI).  Next time we come we will order water.  Too bad you can't  be a decent and reasonable establishment. You shoukd chance your name to " Rippy's you off".

Not bad for a breakfast place for a hotel in the downtown of a metropolitan city.  Either you get a free continental breakfast or overpriced.  No free continental breakfast at the Cambria and thus my review.  The service was excellent. Coffee bitter, portions very small.  Again standard downtown practice for most areas. Not bad, but not a destination breakfast
My college experience in Nashville would not have been the same without this place. It's not the cheapest bar on Broadway but it has the best music and the best energy. Must visit if you're in town!
Great dance floor and music but good luck getting a drink. I've been here 45 minutes and tried to get a drink from 2 separate bartenders to no avail. Completely ridiculous at this point.

Stayed at the dining area, less noisy but still could listen to the band. Pulled Pork (that comes either w/ salad and/or sandwich) is delicious. Side fries are very good too. Good selection of local brews. We liked the place and food.
Ps. I came with my wife and 6 years old daughter.

A unique venue with a fun atmosphere and plenty of country music vibes. Place is HUGE - has three levels that are accessible - and on peak nights can get completely packed out. So with that mind, there is sometimes a bit of a wait to get food or drinks. Has an upper billiards level and bars on each level. 

I would recommend going on a night when they are teaching a line dance or any night with live music. Food and drinks can be a bit pricey, but it is in the tourist trap area of downtown, so this is expected. Be sure to stop in and take a look at the great decor if you have never been inside.

I've been to the TPAC several times now and each time has been a good experience. I feel like the James K Polk theatre really needs to be updated/renovated because the upper tier is frequently warm and isn't accessible at all. The only way to get up there is by using the stairs, which is fine and all, but I didn't see this mentioned either of the times I've purchased tickets in that area. So if you need accessible seating make sure to spend extra money to sit on the first level and avoid the upper tier.

Other than accessibility and AC problems upstairs, it's otherwise a very nice place to go for a show. All of the staff have always been nice and helpful when we've visited.

Good food and good local bands, need I say more.  If you want to feel like a local come on in and have a beer and live music. Service is great too!  Wife had a Malibu pineapple that was awesome. I had a Yazoo Hopry  Hazy IPA. man was it good, and by it I mean 3 or 4 :).

Pro
Locals hangout
Good music
Good beer
Good food

Cons
None at all. Great place!

Fantastic service!! Friendly staff and great local music! Local talent is awesome! Pork was tender and delicious! Beer selection was delicious and recommended by Raegan, thank you for your recommendation and wonderful service!

Four stars for the second floor, open air space. I'm glad that the bottom level was all full, because it was definitely better to be upstairs with the freeze, over looking Broadway street, and there is still live music. I can't comment on the food because all I got was a corndog and fries, but it seems like pretty typical stuff.

I was there after lunch and the restaurant was absolutely empty. Despite being the only one there for lunch it took forever for a waiter to come to my table. The waiter was not helpful with suggestions, so I ordered an IPA and Shrimp & Grits. The overpriced shrimp & grits were awfull. The shrimp was overcooked and sauce was way too overpowering. I like strong flavors but this tasted like someone spilled the black pepper into the sauce by accident.  Terrible.
Service was good.  Decor was very cool country Nashville Vibe.  Service was good.  Food was good, we had burgers and they were very flavorful.  I would have eat there again.

Fun place right on the strip. Music on two levels and the food was solid. Drinks were very good and the service was fantastic for being so busy. Good bbq and cocktails spot with very talented musicians. What else do you need on Broadway.

We visited the Nash House twice while we were in Nashville.  The food was amazing.  The desserts are over the top.  The Nash pie is to die for~ it's a must try.  Live music and an incredible staff is a reflection of Andy, the front of the house manager, style.  This is a must visit while you are in Nashville.

I would've given more stars if the staff was better. We went on a Thursday night, and there was two private events. On the second floor, one private event was using half of the upstairs. 2 different employees told us the other half was open seating. We still had to go downstairs to buy drinks (which was fine) but we enjoyed the view. After about 30 minutes a third worker comes and tells us we aren't allowed to sit there, and that there's a private event. (Mind you, we are on the other side of the horseshoe completely away from this "event.") When we tell him we were told by 2 other employees that we could sit there he was very rude. On our way back down, a fourth employee comes to tell us we are allowed to sit there, but we just can't get drinks from the second floor bar. He was immediately interrupted by employee three, and told us again we can't sit there. 

All in all, we liked the atmosphere, but I won't be back. Employee 4 was the nicest by far, but it was very frustrating being told different things and not being able to enjoy our time in there. We left shortly after instead of just moving to the first floor, because we felt very unwelcome.
At Wildhorse Saloon for free beer and hot wings live at night. Seats couldn't have a much more obstructed view. Can see maybe half the stage. Buddy has a view of the sign. Seats 1 and 2 suck.

There's a good reason why the Wildhorse is world famous. In fact, the way I became aware of this place was through a dear friend of mine who does shows here frequently. Maggie Baugh is her name, and all you need to know about her is that her talent level has piqued the interest of Sony Music. I'll give you my three reasons why Wildhorse Saloon is the place to be when y'all come to Nashville. 

1). The atmosphere. There aren't a lot of places that balance class AND fun. Wildhorse is one of those rare gems. A beautiful, three level music venue with a giant stage where staff and patrons alike can learn to line dance. I dare you to not smile when you set foot in this piece of heaven! 

2). The customer service. What can I say? The customer service here is top notch! The staff here want to talk to you and aren't worried about social status. Everyone is welcome at Wildhorse. You will come in a visitor and leave as part of the family. To say anything less would be downright foolish! 

3). The food. When I first came in to dine, I ordered the Nashville Hot Chicken sandwich. While Prince's invented the culinary delight, Wildhorse perfected it. I have never sunk my teeth into a sandwich that balanced the sweet with the heat so beautifully. It wasn't just a sandwich. It was a work of art! The fiery boldness of the habanero mixed with the sweet and sensible sweet tea brine waltzed along my tastebuds as a symphony of flavor played deep into the night. I left the saloon with a big smile on my face. 

My one small gripe is that the options are a bit pricey. However, when you go to the Wildhorse, you get what you pay for: an experience like no other! 

Nashville, Wildhorse Saloon better stick around. Because the it will be a very sad day if it goes under.

Celebrating our daughter's 17th birthday so needed something fun to do with teens. We started with an early dinner downtown then headed over to the Wildhorse for some line dancing. Our group of 7 girls had a blast! They did the 7:00 lesson and mostly stayed on the dance floor until the 9:00 lesson was finished. All the girls loved it and it was something unique they had not done before. Excellent live music on a Saturday night and we got in free because we arrived just before 6 PM.  The environment was very family friendly but we did leave around 10. At 10:30 it switches to 21 and over.  Wrapped up the night at the Legendary Milkshake Bar for a fun birthday night downtown!  Get to the Wildhorse by 7:30 for best seating choices to enjoy the live music and watch the line dancing.
Excellent drinks and food! Amazing entertainment! Hands down best on the street! If you are in town, don't miss this place for excellent entertainment! Service was excellent, as well.

Super disappointed. Heard this was the place for brisket and ribs. Ordered brisket meal. The food came about five minutes after we orderedI - I was initially impressed until I took the first bite. The brisket was cold. The fries and onion rings were colder. Service was provided without a smile or care. Waitress didn't even ask how our food was or even thanked us for coming in. Maybe my expectations were too high???

The place is busy. Love the music and ambiance. Come for the drinks and music but eat somewhere else.

Everyone knows my love for pizza, so of course I had to give Soulshine a try. In fact, I was even excited! Their menu looked great online.

So maybe it was my subconscious fear that I might ACTUALLY like a place in Midtown that ruined it... but really, it wasn't.

My friend and I ordered a wheat crust pizza and before any one of you say, "That's where you went wrong! Get the regular crust next time," I'm going to stop you right there and point my finger to Mellow Mushroom and their delicious wheat option. It can be done well. After a couple of bites of my slice, the toppings and cheese slid off and I was left with seeing gray crust. Is that normal? There went my appetite that was already disappointed.

You'd have to really convince to try Soulshine again. On one hand, I did go within weeks of their opening, but then again... it's a chain. They've established their recipes. So no, thanks. Vandy and Belmont kids can have their pizza.

Last night was awesome!!! We went to Soulshine for my 30th birthday dinner. I had about 30 people with me, the wait was a little long but worth it. We basically took over a whole section. Our server Ryan (or Bryan, sorry I forgot) was AWESOME! I know it can be stressful having such a large group, but he was great! He kept checking on me and brought out my food first because it was my birthday, and some yummy bread pudding!!! We all had a blast, thanks to him. It turns out he's only been serving for a month! TERRIFIC job Ryan (or Bryan)!!!!

I went to Rippy's with my father last night before the Predators Rangers hockey game. We sat at the bar and had two beers each and ate dinner... Perfectly respectable restaurant guests. When it came time to pay, my father set out a 20% tip for the bartender, plus an additional almost $2 in quarters and dimes that were in his pocket. The bartender then came over, separated out the change from the dollar bills, shoved it back across the bar at my father, and told my father to keep his change because it's 'rude and shitty' to give loose change to a bartender. I have never had a server or bartender at any restaurant say that or be so rude. Rippy's management should take a closer look at who they're hiring and what kind of things their bartenders are allowed to say to decent, well tipping, respectful customers. I won't be going back, and that bar tender is certainly not smart as she turned down money just because it was loose change rather than dollar bills or a credit card slip.

Never went in because the security guard at the front said our friend was stumbling in. She had 2 drinks and a beer and had been looking for line dancing the entire night during cma fest. Coming from California, we were looking for some good dancing, instead receive a cold shoulder.
Easily the best brisket aside from my moms home smoked that tastes like an heirloom... Super cool atmosphere and a seriously rocking decor! As a restaurant consultant I give them a 5 stars
Great band and view from the top! Ribs are good, always a good time. Hard to get a table or bar tender.

I'm such a honky tonk, small town country girl at heart so this feels like HOME to me!

The light up guitar on the ceiling is my favorite.
But there's so much more to love as well... The stage with seating or cleared to dance! There are a couple bars so easy access to food and drink. Plenty of seating. I love the raised part with the bar and booth seats. 

I am not sure if Roots the radio station, I think that's the name of it, hosts bands all the time or if it was just when I was there for Americanafest?
Either way, it was cool when they interviewed the artists right after their show, but in front of everyone in the room so we could all listen live.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND

If I could give more stars I absolutely would. I've got the same things both times: bacon queso, fried okra, meat loaf, and mashed potatoes. The gravy that comes with the meat loaf and mashed potatoes clearly has some sort of addictive substance in it because nothing that good can be 100% natural.
These guys made a rainy afternoon so fun! Loved it each time one of them sang something original.

Their Famous Fried Pickles should be famous! These deliciously thinly shaved pickles are gently fried. They're light, tasty and we'll worth it. We also got the deviled eggs and they were delicious too! Light and tasted, not heavy and overbearing eggy. Great appetizers.
I got the brisket plate, and I was a little disappointed, and why this is only 4 stars. It _tasted_ good but dry, more dry than I'd like. Smothering it in BBQ sauce made it better but then I lost the flavor of the well smoked meat. 
Wife got the shrimp and grits, and I was jealous. So good! Highly recommend the shrimp and grits!

This place was awesome-- I ended up coming both days I was in Nashville. I got Nashville Hot Chicken breast both nights, cause it was so good the first time. Very crispy, seasoned skin that had light coating that has a little heat and a little zing (I got mild). It's is served with a cornbread pancake that adds a little sweet, and coleslaw that gives it some good balance with fresh crunchy acidic element. I have no point of comparison on Nashville hot chicken, but this may've been best chicken I've ever had!

They also have good lengthy tap list of high end craft beer. The first night they had MNF on massive screen which I enjoyed. The second night they had live music, which I also enjoyed.

Would recommend! Would come back!

My one nit-- they serve food on metal trays with thin wax-type paper. The paper shreds on a fork and knife meal and annoying to make sure you're not eating it with bites of food.

When you're hitting the downtown Nashville music and food scene, Rippy's should be a stop on your journey. Whether you just want a drink, food or listen to good music, there's a place for all. They have quite an expansive area for eating, drinking or watching bands. My wife and I ventured to the top floor where we'd seen some very talented artists performing. The music acts change frequently so there's a good chance you'll see a few performers if you're there for a hour or 2. 
They have a good craft beer menu as well as drink specials. I had the BBQ pork wrap which was pulled pork, BBQ sauce and cole slaw in a tortilla wrap along with curly fries. Very tasty and filling. For my vegetarian wife, there wasn't too much to choose from so she ended up with chips and salsa. 
The bands work mostly for tips so if you see one you like, be generous.

After a long day around Nashville we were struggling on where to eat.  Everywhere on broadway seems to have the same menu.  My mom wanted ribs at the moment so we ended up here. It also wasn't as loud as some of the other venues.  We sat on the first floor and were helped immediately. We ordered a full slab of ribs to share with curly fries and onion rings - we were literally starving.  The food came out so fast. So fast. Which I didn't mind since hangry!!!  We ended up finishing everything except the onion rings and didn't even try the cornbread. 2 well drinks and the ribs was $46.  Wasn't the best meal ever but didn't disappoint. I wouldn't choose to come back.

I had high hopes with this place.  The interior decor looked great.  When we checked in, the hostess said the different sauces that are available for the hot chicken were all good but the three varieties had a big difference in heat.  When we ordered, the server told us all three versions had the exact same sauce and the only difference was the amount of sauce.  But, we all went with versions of it.  The chicken tasted good but there was no heat AT ALL.  It was just fried chicken.  The server ignored us after his big party of heavy drinkers sat down behind us.  He was a really tall guy.  We barely saw him again.  We had a different lady stop and check to see if things were ok.  The chicken was not and she seemed shocked when I asked her if the chicken was supposed to be hot or not.  She brought us all one little dish of sauce to share which seemed ridiculous.  It helped the chicken out tremendously and it was ok after that.  Nothing fancy though and the only benefit was that it was closer to our hotel than down on Broadway where the NFL Draft had exploded over everything.

Fried Pickles great, bbq sauce great, host staff, warm and welcoming. We were there for two different bands. The first was a guitar trio and one band member had their mic turned up to the point where the singing was annoying. The second was a full band who hand a person dedicated to their sound mixing and they were very good. The food is mediocre at best. Dry pulled pork, dry brisket, bitter greens, alright pork loin sandwich. Had the biggest beef with the bar tender. Bar tender would not serve drinks from the bar, made us go through the waiter (who was busy). She than stood there and literally did nothing.

Great food and atmosphere. Not that long of a wait for being a popular place and awesome live music. The wings and fries were excellent. And, for those who care, the bathroom was super clean. Definitely want to go back the next time I'm in Nashville!

Great service and food! We had a large group and service was quick and accurate. The food was very good and we enjoyed the live music while we dined. The music was loud enough to hear but didn't hinder our conversation. I recommend stopping by for a great meal at a cool spot!

This place was amazing. My friends and I came in here to taste the vodka lemonade slushies and we stayed for 4 hours. I'd highly recommend this place to anyone in town. Ali and Jacob were top class bartenders and had so much fun with us. Definitely a must is you're visiting Nashville!

We had a great meal and heard two talented aspiring singer songwriters at Nash House on a recent Sunday night. The wait staff were super friendly and attentive. We were surprised there wasn't a bigger crowd. The deviled eggs were our favorite and the blueberry cobbler a close second.

I was surprised by how crowded Rippy's was on a random Sunday night! It's a good thing they have plenty of space here. Didn't get to try any food, so I can't comment on that. The best part about this place was the band (led by Ty Parkin). Other than the music though, this place was just average.

Just left after having dinner, 3 adults and 2 kids. On the plus side, our kids loved getting to dance and the band was great. The negatives: our waitress didn't bring us water, we asked for water, she brought half of us water. The hot chicken sandwich was good chicken, the wedge salad was not good (how?? The lettuce was brown and there was zero bacon, just weird...), the bbq brisket and sausage was blah. Husband ate half and walked away from it. Just a real bummer on the food and service bc it's such a cool place.  Waitress finally came back around w our check and we were out.

And for that bbq plate, a salad, a sandwich (plus a side of Mac) and tip (bc even if they don't show up, we do) we totaled out at $99. Dang.

Awesome place to see and hear authentic country music. We came before the show at the Opry. Seat yourself. We just had a few beers, no food. The band was great and played all sorts of classics. Very different than what you see on Broadway. It's worth the time to check out local spots to get a true feel of Nashville.

We ended up here on a whim, as it was pouring on our way to Broadway and they were the first doorway we reached. It was a Thursday afternoon and they had a lice cover band. Food was excellent! I had a pulled pork sandwich with coleslaw on it and homemade potato salad as a side. Generous servings of both and super tender pork. Good ambiance and a great time!
Don't change a thing.  Good food, relaxed atmosphere, not overly crowded for lunch, and good traditional country music!  We heard Jon Byrd and Mike Oldham last week and enjoyed both.

Hands down BEST BBQ on Broadway! the service was very impressive. We were seated immediately upon entering the building. Our hostess was super nice. Our waiter came to the table WITH water  and took our drink order. He came back quickly with drinks in hand,  they both tasted great! and then he took our food order! OMG when i say he wasn't even gone FIVE minutes after taking our order when our order came out! CORRECT, may I add, and DELICIOUS!!!    I would say they should change their name to "Quikky's" LOL but overall, it was an awesome experience. Will definitely return for the drinks, food and atmosphere!!

The staff was extremely attentive, food was great!  We had the meatloaf and the ham dinners...food was hot, tasty, waitress was fast to take our order and keep checking on us for drinks!  The band was excellent with classic country music and was interactive with the guests!

This place is fun. Live music good drinks and cool atmosphere. We came for the food though and based on that wont be back. The wait is forever long. 45 minutes to get a table another 45 to get food after the order was placed. Not really worth the wait in my opinion. Now for fun and a few drinks it's great but if hunger brings you out just know you will wait and wait some more.

This was a new place for us to try while in Nashville. The menu has a southern focus and they execute it well. We started with the fried pickles which were tasty. Enjoyed a nicely crafted Old Forester Old Fashioned. Fried cornmeal catfish was paired with a habanero corn cake and chowchow. We substituted the okra for a loaded potato. The meatloaf was topped with grilled onions and had a mushroom bordelaise sauce. Mashed potatoes were perfect. Our friend ordered the chicken fried steak and said the cut of beef was tender and prepared perfectly. Friendly service provided by Amy. She offered suggestions and told us about her favorites.  Live music was entertaining. One suggestion, might want to dim the lights a bit in the evening. Too bright!

Service took awhile. Probably sat 15 mins in the upstairs restaurant area waiting at our table. It wasn't all that busy either. However when we finally got a server to our table the rest of our experience was fantastic. The ribs and drinks were great! Fairly priced!

Went one night for dinner and was thrilled at what I saw. The venue has a large restaurant area and a huge stage. As I walked in a young lady was playing the guitar and she was excellent. 

I saw down and noticed right off the bat they had a great beer selection. I am a fan of drinking local and they did not disappoint. The server was very helpful with her suggestions and I went for the Nashville hot chicken, boneless breast. I was a bit disapointed that they didn't have the bone in any more as I always prefer bone-in since it has more flavor. It was very tasty. It came with some slaw but only a little bit.

The live entertainment was amazing. I stayed for the second act which was a woman on keyboard.

The only negative, and the reason I didn't give five starts is that the server could've been a little more attentive. It took almost 10 minutes after I paid for her to come back.

This place falls right in line with most of the bars on this street. Live music, expensive drinks and pretty much not a local in the joint outside of the people who work there. Bartenders upstairs were real nice. Overall it was nothing to write home about.
Horrible service.... Took 10 minutes to get a beer. Too many choices on Broadway to be that bad.

Walked into NashHouse and the first thing I noticed is the live music playing and the place had a great vibe. All of that in front of what is apparently is a 17ft high definition screen which has to be perfect for any game. The beer list is full of great local brews including my favorite peanut butter stout from tailgate, trust me it's amazing. I had the hot chicken  and it was super moist with just the right amount of heat. I specifically liked it because it was on top of the cornbread and slaw which balanced it out perfectly. It's been a while I found a place I felt I could not only eat but just hang out and chill. If you are new to Nashville or a local don't miss out on this place it is a gem. Oh and complimentary valet for the first 2 hours to boot.

Eight of us at work this evening ordered take out and  most had the BBB with ether tots or fries. We were all in agreement that it was the worst we've had from  twin kegs, everything from over spiced, over cooked and very salty could not have enough ketchup to hid it. Very disappointed !

This was the first place we ate at during our first trip to Nashville. If this is what Nashville has to offer, we won't come back. The ribs were incredibly dry (sawdust comes to mind) with almost no taste at all. The live music made it a draw for partying I guess, so maybe with enough whiskey the ribs would be OK. The wait staff was very short-tempered if you didn't know "the rules" of the place, so as first-timers we were treated like dirt. Honestly, the only thing I think that keeps the place open is its corner location. Never again!

Absolutely the worst. Asked for four shots of a whiskey that's usually the cheapest whiskey at a bar and the total was 45 dollars. Between the ridiculous prices and the filth, nobody should ever go here.

I have been a season ticket holder for TPAC's Broadway series for three years now and I have never been disappointed in a show.  Whether it's the opera, ballet, or traveling musical I always love coming here.  The sound is incredible, the staff unbelievably friendly and you can bring wine in with you to the performances.  YES!

If you find musicals enjoyable (and there are many out there that are fantastic) I'd suggest becoming a season ticket holder.  You can spread out your payments for your season if needed and you get discounts on other shows, plus its cheaper than singular tickets and you can get better seats at a better price.  I've gotten to see some great shows that I had heard of and some of the best shows I had never heard of.

The Nashville ballet and the Nashville opera also do shows here and they put on some amazing performances.  If you haven't seen the Nashville Nutcracker ballet at the holidays make it a must this year.

As its downtown make sure to give yourself enough time to get to your show as parking can be a pain, or just come early and enjoy a pre-show cocktail.  They also sell snacks to munch on while you wait for the show to start.  TPAC is not far from Broadway but it's a little bit of a walk so be aware of that as well if you decide to do dinner downtown first.  
TPAC has two theaters inside, Jackson Hall which is larger, and James K. Polk, which is smaller.  Sometimes they have shows running simultaneously so again, something to think about when planning a night here.  

I've never had a bad time here and always enjoyed the performances.  Amazing artists, amazing staff, and again, you can bring your cocktails in the theater with you (and they usually have a specialty drink to go with the show you're seeing).  So get dolled up and head to TPAC, you'll thank me later!
Oved the history of this place & the band that was there was amazing! Cant wait to go back & visit!

Early dinner here before Concert at the Bridgestone. Service and Food were great, live music the day we were there was spotty.
Great BBQ for a downtown establishment.

Rippy's marries 2 long bars, 2 live stages, and Barbecue without any major dysfunction. 

Downtown Nashville is an fantastic place for live music, but surprisingly there aren't just too many barbecue joints to pick from. Jack's has a prominent place on Broadway across the street but I left a bit appointed so I decided to dial up Rippy's a few days later to see if I couldn't find a winning 'Cue. More a concert venue than just a straight up barbecue house, Rippy's is big enough that there are actually multiple sections with separate live bands. The walls must be pretty well insulated, because I couldn't even hear the other band from my side of the restaurant. The crowd is rather wild and loud - if not just bone ass wasted - but the service was still excellent. 

I opted for the 1/2 Chicken Barbecue plate and what came from the kitchen was more than I bargained for as it flaunted the mentioned 1/2 Chicken that is seasoned and then slow smoked. The meat had a great smoke level, which matched perfectly with the evident smoke ring yet remained moist and juicy especially in the dark meat areas. The Curly Fries were standard issue and a bit overly salted but that did little to keep me from nibbling on them every few bites. The Chili on the other hand was flat and contained Beans - a pet peeve of mine. I would skip the Chili altogether on the next go around. 

Naturally the party atmosphere is what most patrons come to Rippy's for but the food isn't a slouch when you weigh in the nearby options of the genre and while Rippy's wasn't the best barbecue I've ever had, but it was certainly passable. I'd go back for the drinks and music any day, although I'd likely order a Burger instead.

Went here because it was close the the Marriott.  Glad that we did.  The food was great   and the prices were good.  Good selection of TN draft beer too.  Love the huge screen TV and the entertainment.  Listened to Haleigh Martin who was pretty good.  Too bad she had to start on a slow Sunday night.

Sadly this place was awful...we waited an HOUR to be seated (busy night and we had no reservations so I get it no worries) But to then wait an hour to get Apps and still have no main entree after an hour and 20 min...we left...despite being told it was "coming right out" by our poor waiter (who we still tipped 20% for the drinks and Apps after all the piss-poor kitchen staff was NOT his fault) no manager to complain to to be seen (likely cowering in the back office as we were NOT the only people leaving, or complaining) 
I had heard good things and we were looking forward to enjoying it...instead we left frustrated and hangry.  Spitting nails and warning others about the horrid ticket times.
A lovely hall for opera and the performing arts. Comfortable seats, good acoustics. Our seats were second row to the side and they were great

A great selection of food, beer, and music. We came here for an event, and really enjoyed the band, and the sandwiches. The spicy fried pickles were awesome, and it was nice to try some of the local beer while listening to live country music. The band played all kinds of country from new to classic, which was great! If I had to recommend something it would be to put spicy, fried pickles in the sandwiches. It's a little trick I learned.  The service was super nice, and everyone was really cool. The location is great too.
I haven't even had the main course but our server, Amy A said they have the best fried pickles. She was Right. The best fried pickles EVER.

Found this place on Christmas night by chance.  Had a table of 9 and service was fabulous.  Food was delicious.  We had the chicken fried chicken, meatloaf, and shrimp and grits.  Everyone loved their food.  The NashHouse pie was unbelievable.  Highly recommend this establishment.

We are staying at the JW across the street. We passed by several times and decided to give this place a try. I am SO glad we did. Sky was our server and was outstanding. He was attentive, had great suggestions, and was personable. 

We started with the fried pickles. They were great. They were served with white bbq sauce and he also brought out ranch. 

We then shared chicken fried chicken and an order of biscuits and jam. CFC was fantastic! It came with a biscuit stuffing. So good! The biscuits came with 4 different kinds of jams. So good! 

We have been to several places while visiting this time and we have been so disappointed with our service until tonight. We are going back for breakfast tomorrow. Definitely go check them out. You'll be glad you did!

Wildhorse was a solid honky-tonk to visit on our first trip to Nashville. It had a good atmosphere for line dancing, even though the performer for the night was sub-par. It was a very spacious location, with three floors(the bottom floor for eating, dancing, and a small bar, and the upper floors with bars overlooking the dance floor as well as pool tables). The food was overpriced, but not bad. Overall, it was a memorable experience, but not a memorable meal.

Our company reserved the entire place  on a Sunday night. About 400 of us filled the two floors. Live band was playing and buffet style food at both floors. Bars are plenty abound, friendly staffs!! Few of Their staffs were on the dance floor encouraging everybody to dance and even  dance lesson on line dancing.

Go for the music and/or cocktails.  The food is pretty lousy and the service is not good either.  I had the chicken "fajita" tacos, and there wasn't anything fajita about them.  The chicken was pulled chicken that was extremely dry.  Hubby had the chicken Caesar Salad.  LOTS of the lettuce was very debatable AND the chicken was the same dry pulled chicken mentioned above.  Our waitress walked past our table 5 times, with 2 of us standing and waving our arms at her, to no avail.  Hubby had to get up and go tell her we needed something.

Service was excellent. Bouncer high fived me despite having a cast on his arm-the dedication! 

Bartender was fun and upbeat and made great mixed drinks-she gave us free Jell-O shots!!

Tina wasn't there (again)....

This place was great the pulled pork was amazing! Keep in mind that the barbecue sauce is at your table the place was also very nice the 2nd and 3rd floors were the nicest on those floors there were some pool tables a douse ball table and a shuffle board table and if you are into live music the first and second floors are where u will get the best view  definitely recommend this place

This place was absolutely awful and a complete disappointment. The food was cold, like from the fridge. Ordered pulled pork and boyfriend got the ribs. All the food was cold. Mac and cheese had no flavor at all. The service wasn't good. One drink for each of us the whole time we were there. Don't choose this place for a good bbq place.

We decided on this place for dinner as Honky Tonk was a zoo. We weren't greeted as we came in by the staff who were more interested in their own conversation. Eventually we found a table upstairs and a friendly server took our order which came out in less than 5 minutes - I'd rather wait and have something freshly made to be honest.

My fiancée had the pulled pork sandwich and I had the ribs which the server told us is what they're famous for. Maybe its my inexperience of the South/BBQ but I was expecting both the ribs and pulled port to be smothered in a delicious sauce, but neither were. There were 2 sauces on the table and the thicker of the two was delicious, the highlight of the meal, but why weren't the meats cooked in it so they could absorb the flavor more? The ribs were fall of the bone but they didn't have the nice crunchy skin I like that again would probably have come if they'd been cooked in a sauce. All in all I was disappointed in them given ribs are what this place is supposedly known for. 

The music in the background was a real mix of genres and not all that good, particularly for Nashville. On our way out we wished we'd sat downstairs where there was a better band playing. 

All in all we'll definitely be back to Nashville but not to this spot I'm afraid.

Kiddos to you guys! Sunday afternoon and we were a party of 30 people who walked in with no reservation. They were so great! Got our entire order done without a single mistake! Never mind how AMAZING the bbq was!!! Outstanding and HIGHLY recommended!!

Our weekend in Nashville was definitely one for the books. This was Saturday nights meal. Went in to get a table, they said the wait was 25 minutes and they would text us when a table was ready. We never got a text the whole night and just ate at the bar after sitting there a hour waiting for a table. Our bartender was amazing! Great and friendly service. Our food, not impressed. The layout was nice but it was definitely overpriced for what we received and not cooked as ordered. Salmon and steak was undercooked big time. Asked for no cauliflower, got it anyways. Asparagus was barely cooked. Hard to chew. Just not impressed. Spent $100 and barely touched our food.
Beer was cold, food was good.  Loved the fried pickle spears!  Band was great.  Staff was friendly and took care of our group.  Would definitely go back!

Usually my expectations for a soft opening are pretty low. Sure a mixture of trepidations and hope that result in a mixed bag as a new restaurant finds its footing and works out the bugs. 

What a joy!  

The atmosphere is great - set up with a stage for a live band on one end, a bar at the other. 

Restaurant opens at 7 am for breakfast, transitions to a brunch menu and then lunch before dinner. 

Food was great (tried their Hot Chicken) and served hot and fresh. Ice Tea was tasty too - fresh and quenching.  Fries were hot, crispy and lightly salted - perfection in my book. 

Service was great - once it gets more folks, will be interesting to see if they can keep up the high standards they've set for themselves. 

Overall, very positive and I look forward to trying one of their burgers next (if I don't hit them for breakfast first!)

Very disappointed. We came to Nashville for my dad's 65th Birthday. He only wanted to go to the Wildhorse Saloon for his birthday. That didn't happen!  When we arrived a little before 5pm we reached the guy that was stamping hands and he told us very rudely (while looking at my dad in a wheelchair) that dinner wait time was an hour and a half. I said ok sounds good we will wait and he pointed us too the hostess desk (after making a comment when my dad asked if he could have his hand stamped and he said oh you are going to drink?). When we got to the desk the hostess said it would be a 1.5 hour to 2 hours wait. We said ok sounds good we will wait because this is where he wanted to go for his birthday. After an hour and and a half we went up there to see where we were on the list and was told that it would be another 2 hours!!!!!  We told them we were waiting for an hour and a half already and she rudely said well there are 2 huge parties in front of you. She never mentioned that before. Sadly we left and my dad didn't get to go to the one place he wanted to go to for his birthday dinner. I wish I could give it 0 stars for the way we were treated. I honestly think it was because we had someone in a wheelchair.

I'll start with I waited two hours because the incompetent host staff gave my table away twice. A group and I went here on a Saturday. I expected a wait, as they weren't taking reservations. I called ahead that day at 1:00 pm to see what I needed to do. They said call back closer to dinner and we should be fine to get seated. I call back and now it's an iffy chance. I expected that but the hostess was straight with me and said it was worth a shot. Okay. My party arrives at an appropriate time and the hostess stand has our name first on the list. Things are looking good! We see that the party at where we will be seated is getting their checks, so we tell the host and hostess we are going to get a drink upstairs and they said they would call us in like 10 minutes. Awesome! Half an hour goes by, so I go to check on our table. The hostess with an attitude says, "I gave away your table. You were at the bar, I didn't think you would mind." I stared blankly at her. EXCUSE ME. How is that appropriate? I'm frustrated but relent, as I'm having a good time. Another hour goes by and she has given our table away AGAIN. What in the world?! At this point we aren't happy. Unacceptable behavior. The manager had to get involved. This place gets a star because at least Brandon the bartender knew what he was doing.

Our first trip to NashHouse started out fine.  My husband and I drink bourbon on the rocks and never need a menu to order this.  When we received our bill at the end of our night, we realized that we had been charged $4.00 a drink for ICE! A total of $16.00 just for ice.  This was more than the cost of our appetizers.  The waitstaff should have mentioned this from the beginning. A glass of ice water was free.  If we had known, we would have just used that ice.  We will not be returning.
They say best burger in town, I just thought it was your standard burger and fries/tots. Very smokey, but if you like a good dive bar, this will be your place.

Great space in Downtown Nashville. Enjoyed LUNCH/BRUNCH on a SUNDAY and had no wait. Fried pickles were yummy and entrees (Kale Salad, Pork Plate, BBQ Tacos) were good, but beignets I would pass on in the future. The menu is huge so it's a nice option if you need a lot of variety or have a large group.
Great time!!! Good music, great bar food  Been all over Nashville and we will return to this place.

If you're looking for a place to truly emerge yourself into the country scene, this place should be at the top of your list. The DJ is great and the instructor was easy to follow and encouraging! It does get packed so prepare to be stumbling with others trying to follow along with the moves. 
The only reason I'm rating it 3 vs. 5 is because of my experience in the ladies room with the attendant, Barbara McGowen . She was rude from the start and kept trying to obviously assist me with simple things to make a point of deserving a tip. Although that was annoying, it wasn't the issue. When I reached for the perfume she told me it wasn't free and that she worked solely on tips. I told her I understood and then I asked my friend to take a picture of the attendants Venmo so I could tip her. Then I was held back and lectured on how people do that often but never actually tip her. I replied by telling her I understood and that I was going to tip when she told me not to interrupt her. 
Overall it was a downer and ruined the mood. Getting lectured in the bathroom of a bar is hopefully not the mood they are going for but unfortunately it's the first thing I think of when I think of Wild Horse Saloon.

Came in here after the Grand Ole Opry.. And it was awesome.. Cold Beer.. Great Vibe.. And live music.. Awesome venue... Now the food.. Well it was Awesome... And we were all extremely happy..  Y'all need to check it out.. Baked Wings.. Wow

I ordered the Music City Mule which is made with vodka, Reed's Ginger Beer. It was good. I didn't order any other drinks or food. I have attached pictures from the menus. I loved the music and how I felt we were in a sky bar but it was just upstairs and the window was open. 

Overall: I will give it 4 stars but I didn't really experience a lot of it and would be willing to try out other things if I go back to Nashville.

Came to Wildhorse tonight for the first time and bought a bucket of beer. I started a game of pool on the second floor with my friends and at 10pm a guy came up and told us he was closing the floor. We had 5 balls left on the table and he walked up and took all the pool balls out of the pockets and kicked us off the table while we were playing. Who the hell comes up to a pool table and starts taking balls out of the pockets and kicks you off while your playing
Bad bad bad. I live in Nashville and won't be back.

Romeo and Juliet performed by the Nashville Ballet, was amazing!  

Beautiful performance and amazing costumes. 

Would highly recommend!

We visited this morning for breakfast.  The meal arrived slightly warmer than room temperature.  We sent it back and they brought their second attempt which was also cold.  My eggs were not cooked to order and the biscuit appeared to have been purchased at Sam's.  I was really hungry, so if anything had been slightly tolerable, I would have probably eaten it, but that disgraceful biscuit was a decisive "NO."

Please don't waste your money. I've only has the CATFISH PLATE AND OKRA WHICH WAS HORRIBLE.  WASN'T SEASONED THE OKRA WAS tasteless.  I will never waste my money there again. You have one time to impress me. One and done.

I've been here before for food and line dancing and it was so much fun. The bands are always great and you can see and hear from pretty much any seat in the house.

When we stopped by this visit it was in between sets and line dance lessons but it was still fun to stop in and have a look. I love the look inside and interesting ceilings and lights. The dance floor is the best and most open and spacious on Broadway. Don't forget your dancin' boots if you come!

Extremely disappointing... No live music when we went and the fries were a jumbled mess of FROZEN crinkle, curly and these weird orange colored waffle fries. The BBQ brisket sandwich was great but any place that serves frozen fries is a waste in my book. How can you be in the middle of a popular tourist area and dumb yourself down to frozen fries? That's absolutely terrible. Definitely not the atmosphere I was expecting.

Finally it looked like someone was living in the men's restroom. Giant bottle of mouthwash, bucket of candy etc. Very strange.

They have happy hour!  Great food and drinks here-I enjoyed the "ride a horse" mixed drink and homemade onion dip the most. 
Good for families too during the day-free line dancing, lots of tables and plenty of room for large groups to sit together, which isn't the place in many Nashville spots....also really good night entertainment and concerts.

Well, well.  I haven't been to Rippy's since before I was a Yelper. 

As I'm a Nashville native, that should tell you something. 

Don't get me wrong, I love the front-of-house staff - I've never had a bad bartender at Rippy's. The food always takes forever, and is lackluster - except for the portion sizes, which run to the 'huge' size. 

With the location, it's not a bad place to come before a Predators game, and if you like a highly audience-focused, participatory band, Rippy's usually picks ones of that style. Solid musicians, but not always the best vocals - that might be more of a Broadway trend in general though. 

In short, it's not going to be on a list of places I'll recommend you go, but you can certainly do a whole lot worse.
Great southern food, bbq, and the best biscuits! Really good live music too. Enjoyed the food and atmosphere! Perfect spot for a night out in Nashville...

The one and ONLY reason to go here is to listen to Paul Pace and Tom Stewart sing. The service is @#$ing horrible, from both servers and bartenders. And if you're lucky enough to be sitting at the bar, the bar servers will simultaneously entertain and disgust you by slapping their gigantic floppy purses up on the coolers and get their lipstick out, primping etc. while they're supposed to be working. Does anyone NOT know that the bottom of a purse is about as disgusting as a toilet rim, and doesn't belong anywhere in food service? Seriously, stop putting your nasty ass purse on a place where drinks are served! Grow up! And the food? The food is adequate at best, and being on Broadway, HIGHLY OVERPRICED. Ribs and pork are aight but that's it. I only eat here if I'm downtown, listening to my favorite musicians and am REALLY hungry. Really, do NOT purposely come down here for the food, or the service.

Not a great place to get brisket! According to my husband I am BBQ spoiled and after last nights brisket sandwich I would have to agree. I asked for a chopped brisket sandwich and was told "we don't do that here". So then I asked for a Brisket sandwich moist (with fat for those who don't know) and I was told they "pre trim the brisket to smoke it". So needless to say my brisket was dry and if you gotta and BBQ sauce for moistness then it's not good. BBQ sauce is for flavor! Service was good and the music was good! Not what I expected for Nashville BBQ!

We decided to eat here before the Ryman's show and how I wished we went further down Broadway.

Sure they got a band or musicians playing downstairs and upstairs but when you are sitting upstairs in the dining section you'll think one is singing out of tune...yes, it's not the best seat in the house if you would like to enjoy your dinner and listen to music.

Service is ok, and if others say their bbq ribs is the best, uhm we might be talking about another Rippy's. The ribs were not the best, you can make do if you're hungry but please, the bones were thicker than the meat. Their sides will compensate to fill you up. 

Hubby's pork loin was oily and sliced paper thin I may say although he said the beans were alright. Fries were crunchy which is ok.

I think the best part was the ice cream...a big scoop of vanilla with chocolate fudge. Now you can't mess ice cream...though not impossible.

Rippy's Rippy's ripped off...I won't be the 1st one to have said that. Sorry but this didn't worked outGo further down if you're looking for a better place to eat.

Great music venue bar.   Make sure to try the BBQ.  They have a great beer selection.  The staff is friendly and helpful.  The Amy we went the live music was some of the best we heard in the city.  The only draw back is they have a bathroom attendant.  Bathroom attendants weird me out.  It is odd having someone spray soap on you're hands, hand you paper towels, offer cheap cologne and then expect a tip.

I wouldn't recommend this place at all! The food was horrible. The fried pickles had no batter, and the ranch was so watery. I couldn't eat my mac & cheese because it was basically sitting in a bowl of oil. My server was nice, but had a hard time giving good service considering he had to ring food in at the table, on a tablet. It was awkward and time consuming for him and us. Not to mention it is overpriced! Skip it.

The food was amazing! We had the deviled eggs as an app, I got the meatloaf which was the best I've ever had, my husband got the shrimp and grits which was amazing, and my daughter got the Mac n cheese which was on the kids menu and it was soooo good! We are going here for breakfast too and I am sure it will be equally delicious!

Early Valentine's dinner before a concert at the Ryman tonight. Wonderful Hot chicken and chicken fried chicken. Great music during dinner by Paige Rose. Amy D. Was a friendly and attentive server. Great experience. We will be back. Thank you.
Love this place.  Low key. Great music and food.  We stayed at the Gaylord Opryland hotel and is very close.

On the outside, Rippy's just look like a large, tourist bar, so my expectations were admittedly low coming in. However, I had the best wrap here full of smoky and tender pork ribs and tons of tangy barbecue sauce. Really good! We also had some nice cocktails, while enjoying some Johnny Cash covers.

Came here for breakfast after staying at the hotel for the night. First off, the restaurant was nearly empty so we didn't think we have a problem getting quick service. To start, the coffee tasted burnt, almost undrinkable and I'm a coffee lover. After waiting around an hour for our food and witnessing other customers sending items back, we received our food and it was completely cold. Eggs, hash browns, bacon and biscuits. The waiter also got all four of our orders wrong. The food was not edible so we ended up having to leave and find another spot for our brunch. I highly recommend not coming here.

I've always had the best time when I go here. My first time was 13 years ago when Taylor swift had just put out get first single. I was in town with my aunt and cousins and I was just like, you know this girl! She's going to be big one day. Look at her now! I heard her first at wildhorse! Love it!

This venue is PHENOMENAL! Upon walking in, I felt like we walked into a very upscale concert hall. It was a slow night, which I'm not mad about because it felt like we had our own private concert!! 

It was a very late Friday night and Wildhorse Saloon is located on one of the side streets of Downtown Nashville. We stumbled upon this street by accident because we were honestly just curious and noticed the stage from across the street. BOY AM I GLAD I DID. It was, unfortunately, a slow night, and it broke my heart a little because RadioRomance was playing, and there was just so much talent on that stage, but there wasn't much people last night. I kind of found that to be true from most of the venues I visited last night, must have been an off night, but I'm slightly glad it wasn't as crowded because I got to experience, what felt like, my own private concert! The atmosphere felt very romantic, I just can't describe it in words. I mean, I am curious to see what this place is like on a busy night, but I'm kind of glad it turned out the way it did for us! 

I would definitely recommend Wildhorse Saloon to all visitors of Nashville!

Had a great time eating dinner and dancing at the Wildhorse Saloon while in Nashville!  The food was pretty good and the band, Brother Trouble was really good!  We did some two step, west coast swing, and line dancing.  FUN evening!

Great food. 
Service could use work. Seating wasn't great. High top chair at a regular table is a little ridiculous. But the food. The food. Delicious & affordable. Don't miss this place!
Terrible food. They closed the restaurant for other guests. I should be able to eat where is stay so I had to eat at the bar. I wish they would have closed that also. Soggy fries cold burger. Yuk.

The bartender was super sweet. She served me quick and with a smile. 

But the bareback.... damn. What did I do man. Just ask you a question. What are you mad about man. I'm from California and didn't know what time a game started. It's cool if you don't know, use words man. Shrugging like a 6 year old ain't it.

Had lunch here after visiting Cooters. Sat outside and Brandi was our waitress. She was very nice, funny and an amazing server even after she got seated with like a party of 20 next to us, it did not impact our service at all. Cathfish and fried pickles were great! That batter is amazing!Brandi  gave awesome recommendations. Can't beat the prices either!

I went to Rippy's with my wife and two closest friends. We were in Nashville for a long weekend. We arrived at the restaurant at 6:00 pm on game night for the Predators. I didn't think we would have a prayer of getting a table and eating in a treasonable amount of time, but we decided to give it a shot. I was pleasantly surprised when were able to get a table right away on the second level. The service was excellent and were able to order right away. Our food came out very quickly and was delicious! I had the 1/2 rack of ribs with baked beans and Mac & Cheese. The food was amazing and I enjoyed every last  bite! I recommend this place anytime you are in town!!

We saw Disney's Broadway tour of The Lion King in the Jackson Hall at the TPAC and couldn't have been more thrilled with our experience. The venue is a little on the older side and perhaps a bit small, but I felt like every seat in the house (regardless of the ticket price) would have a great view of the show. The attendants were helpful and made sure everyone was where they needed to be. We were ushered into our seat in a calm organized fashion.

We sat in the left side box with a spectacular view of the stage and he performers. Parking was a bit of a headache, but we definitely plan on returning to the TPAC again - perhaps next time to see Beauty and the Beast!

Would not recommend. We had a table of 9, which we understand is a bigger table, but not outrageous. We waited forever for our food, and when we got it, nothing was warm. It all felt as if it had been sitting on a counter for a very long time. We complained and were told it was our fault for having too big of a table. Along with the food being cold, it wasn't all that great either. When wanting to leave, it took us a good half an hour for our waitress to get our cards back to us--and I would like to mention we were in here on a Monday night! Was not impressed at all!

This place has two sides, the bar and the restaurant- the left side (bar) was great. Great music great energy and people. The restaurant side was a little under my taste. The food was very greasy over cooked and the service was average. The stage seemed crowded, I enjoyed the left side Bc it was focused on music and drink whereas the restaurant bar side was crowded with a very small stage and TVs everywhere. I got a little sick from the food too. It was under flavored 
Loved Nashville :)

I am writing this as I sit here in the Wildhorse waiting for the food that our group had to order at the bar with no place to sit. I believe a list of issues with this place is best. 

1-1 1/2 hour wait to get a table while there is no less than 50 empty tables in front of me.
2-The only bar open is the main bar on the 1st floor. It is currently 3 deep all of the way around. 2nd floor bar is closed for a private function, and 2 other side bars in the 1st floor are just closed.
3-There are more people in the bar below 21 than above.
4-$6 cover for "the band." Nearly every establishment around, the band plays for tips. Here you pay a cover for the band that is not as good as any other band we have seen anywhere else.
5- Bar tender yelled at me to come back in ten to get my food. Do not yell at me. Ever.
6- The bathrooms are disgusting. Paper towels all over the ground and a broken faucet knob.

I hope others find this useful when trying to find a place to eat or get some drinks.

Usually my expectations for a soft opening are pretty low. Sure a mixture of trepidations and hope that result in a mixed bag as a new restaurant finds its footing and works out the bugs. 

What a joy!  

The atmosphere is great - set up with a stage for a live band on one end, a bar at the other. 

Restaurant opens at 7 am for breakfast, transitions to a brunch menu and then lunch before dinner. 

Food was great (tried their Hot Chicken) and served hot and fresh. Ice Tea was tasty too - fresh and quenching.  Fries were hot, crispy and lightly salted - perfection in my book. 

Service was great - once it gets more folks, will be interesting to see if they can keep up the high standards they've set for themselves. 

Overall, very positive and I look forward to trying one of their burgers next (if I don't hit them for breakfast first!

Went back on a Friday night for a burger. Awesome. Even my daughter (who is famous for not finishing her meals) enjoyed and finished her burger.   

BTW, live music starts a 7 pm.

I had their pizza. I expected in ordering a large I would be taking some home. I expected wrong, and not just because I'm a fat pig (although that might help). 

The veggie pizza was... kind of sad. It was thin without the great NY thin-style feel. The veggie toppings had little taste. The whole pie was large, but devoid of weight. I felt sad to be eating that pizza.

The bar, I had three bartenders in two drinks. I also waited several minutes for the bartender who was talking to the other bartender to notice their one customer (me) was in need of a beverage.

Nothing was horrible, but nothing was great. It felt like one of those pizza joints that pops up in the strip mall that's located right next to the real mall and is run by some people who like pizza but never made a garlic knot in their life and had the idea that owning a pizza joint would be fun having never worked a day in one.

Sounds harsh, but it was generic pizza and premium prices. The location is good and they've got nonstop advertising on Lightning 100, so I expect they'll do fine. I hope they get their pizza thicker, tastier, and wish them all the best. For that area I'd wander over to Mellow Mushroom, the Chicago style place four blocks away, or the joint across from Off Broadway that I can't remember the name of but man their pizza is excellent.

I have no idea what the place is like at night, but we had fun during the day. We attended a line dancing workshop hosted here. The service was fantastic and the buffet lunch they served was great. Pulled pork, baked beans, slaw, mac n cheese and brownie bites were on the menu. They have a large dance floor. If you want a good mixed drink I recommend the "hot mess."  

We had an absolute blast line dancing there.

Rippy's may be popular but we just walked out due to crappy service from the staff. It's 4th of July and it's a "seat yourself" type of deal. Well you'd make more money by having a hostess to seat and tell people the wait time when they can't find an open seat. I ordered just a coke and it was bottom of the barrel just carbonation. The heavy blonde bar tender has NO manners or people skills.  She should work at the DMV with that shitty attitude. Worst visit on a vacation ever.

We just spent 13 days in Nashville and 7 of our days we went to the Nashville Palace for great musical  performances by different bands such as Brazilbilly, Jessie Lee Jones and the Spaghetti Westeneers (with a great spaghetti dinner on Sundays), a solo performer named Jared Collins and our last night we were amazed by the great talent of Nathan Belt with some of the Brazilbilly Band.  There is a huge dance floor and on a couple of occasions professional dancers stop in and gave us a free show. The servers were all very nice and the friendly environment made it easy to meet people from all around the world.  Parking was free and we didn't have the hassle of the crowds on Broadway.  Food and drinks were also a good price.  We want to fly back from Bakersfield, CA next year and I know The Nashville Palace will be where we will go for our traditional country music enjoyment.

Being in Nashville for the first time, and with kids (8 and 12), this left us with a dilemma.  We wanted to experience the Nashville music scene, have some good food, and go to a lively yet appropriate venue for kids.

In doing research it became clear that Broadway was the place for this.  The avenue is full of restaurants and music and we happened upon the Wildhorse Salon after reading it was kid friendly.  

We could not have made a better choice.  This place is huge--three floors.  First floor are tables to eat at and some bars, plus the main stage and dance floor.  Floor two has a bar, some booths, viewing spots for the stage, and games such as pool and Foos Ball (all free to play).  The third floor we did not get to but it just looks like a vantage point to watch the stage.

We arrived to the place around 4:30.  We sat and ordered the fried chicken, piggy grilled cheese, and the kids Mac and cheese and kids burger.  We started with fried pickles and drinks as well.  I had read that the food here was at best average but we absolutely loved everything as it was all very tasty and filling.  

While waiting for the food there was free line dancing lessons (every 45 min or so) and the first band also came on.  The kids danced and then we ate and it was an absolute blast.

After dinner we grabbed a seat near the dance floor, had some more drinks and danced up a storm as the band played.  The kids even ordered a lemonade that came in a big plastic cowboy boot!

This is the perfect family place if you want good food, Nashville music, and a lively environment that truly satisfies both the kids and adults.  We stayed until about 8pm and it appeared that at that point the crowd was getting older.  I would think any time after 8 or 9 it would not be as kid friendly.

I love this restaurant. As per Nashville requirement, the live music is generally on point. With the cool upstairs deck open to the main part of the second floor, it definitely has a unique feel. I've been here several times now and have always had great service, even during night ha when it's packed. 

As far as food goes, for the appetizer, the pulled pork nachos are a must! They've got a unique flavor but they're unexpectedly amazing! Next time, I plan to try their pork sandwich. For the main course I've always gone with pizza. Cheeseburger is amazing. The CCR was good, but not as much as others I've tried. Whatever type of cheese they use, I think it's the best in town! The sandwiches are moderately priced (10-15) and the pizzas are a bit pricey for the larger sizes, but the smaller ones are reasonable (10/15 or 20-27 for larger).

I haven't tried any cocktails yet but I've heard good things. The beer was cold, with a good selection of domestics and crafts. Average pricing there.

I recommend Soulshine when friends visit.

Enjoyed the "Palace" style wings. Smoked for flavor and deep fried for crispiness. Wings had a decent amount of meat and were juicy. The sauce had a good balance of sweetness and spice. I also had the Walk the Lime draft, which is a citrus infused IPA. It was good, but the citrus notes weren't very strong. The atmosphere was great with a helpful and quick wait staff. The live music was super, with a variety of country classics and requests from the audience. I would go here again.

It's great for breakfast,lunch,dinner or late night. I especially love the Meatloaf but if u love to eat this is the place for it. It's easy to find its on the ground floor of the Cambria hotel. It's also reasonably priced.

This place has really changed over the years! W sat at the bar and bartender took several minutes to greet us or ask for our order. When I asked what they had- he replied "a lot" and walked off. I then asked about moonshine and he told me they don't have that anymore- after we ordered something they did have and wings and onion rings (menu is limited) we sat back and enjoyed the band. The music was great and the lead talented with a great voice! Before we got ready to leave- we tried to buy a T shirt- one of the guys tried and tried to find the key to sell us one- he finally came back and brought 3 koozies (there were 3 of us) and asked if we could come back to get one the next day. That was a shame- never had time to go back

Went for a private function. While there were bars on all three floors getting a drink was a nightmare. They didn't seem to have enough staff to keep up. Food was good. The entertainment was amazing. LoCash Cowboys played!!
Small place, Fast service. Friendly staff. Good band. Right on main strip down town Nashville. Very loud.

My husband and I are Nashville locals and wanted to try a new place in the area so we stopped by NashHouse. I got the salmon and my husband got the cowboy burger, both were delicious! Our server, Trenton, was super friendly and attentive during our experience. We will definitely be back in the future!
Fall of the bone baby back ribs, live music, attentive sfaff, what more can you ask for? Popped in for lunch on a whim & never regretted it.

This is the best place to hear old country music in Nashville. Plenty of parking, great bands, friendly folks, and classic country music. The food is pretty good as well. The burger and fries is delicious. For a night out of traditional country music, Nashville Palace is the only place for me.

P.S. - It's handicapped accessible for my 90 year old grandmother to hear great music. She loves watching the dancers two step on the dancefloor. We also bring the kids during the day and early evening, so it's great when family visits in town. TIP: bring earplugs for sensitive ears.

Walked into the establishment and there were 10+ tables open and they said it would be at least a 1 hour wait. Decided to go to the bar and low and behold only one bartender. Waited 20 minutes for a drink and sweated my ass off because they decided a 100 degree day was appropriate to keep the garage doors open. Only came in to eat food and the bartender asked to get my drinks before ordering appetizers and never came back
Great food and music! Food is surely worth the price. I had a pulled pork and it was amazing. Really big portions so come hungry. Nachos are also great.

Smells so awful inside I could never imagine actually eating food here. Grabbed beers and sat on the outside patio on account of walking a half mile here based on the Yelp reviews that were way too generous.
Always wanted to go here because of the history.  The food was very good.  Mother Maybelle's ham dinner was some of the best country ham I've had.  Music was too loud is the only complaint.

Stopped in here as part of a work function recently and was fairly impressed. The Wildhorse Saloon is set up with a floor level and two higher levels in a -- you guessed it -- horseshoe kind of shape. On the top floor are pool tables and other games to be played.

The day I went they provided a buffet style dinner. I liked pretty much everything I came across. The beans were excellent, the pulled pork and brisket were both very good, even the coleslaw was great. I'm usually somewhat of a picky eater, but I had two plates because the food was so good. 

The day I was there it was packed. Unfortunately, although the establishment can accommodate a LOT of people, it means many of them will be standing. I was lucky to get a table on the 3rd floor mezzanine. Others were not so lucky. To see the stage or the ground floor dancing, many people were standing against a wall behind me. As I looked around, there are tables around the horseshoe railings and there are tables away from the railings, but nearly enough for the number of people that can be in the building. Lots of people were standing against walls because they didn't have any other choice -- there was nowhere else for them to go.
