The staff was friendly at the 3rd floor bar area, although as noted in other reviews, the staff prefers a line to be formed rather than people standing along the bar. I guess that helps with a "first come, first serve" set up, why have a 15' bar top if you only need 4' to form a line in front of?

Maybe it was the event, but there was NO hard alcohol served at this place. It was kept to beer and soda, but again, that very likely was at the request of the company holding the event.

At one point a young woman appeared on stage and asked if anyone would like to learn some line dancing. She is very good at this and it seemed that people picked it up rather quickly under her tutelage. Later on, a band came out and they put on a decent show. The acoustics can be a little wonky in the building -- or maybe that's just because of where I was at, which was directly in front of the stage, but up so high -- but I enjoyed the show. Staff routinely checked on me to grab my plates and see if the people sitting with me wanted another beer.

Overall, this doesn't seem like a bad place. If it gets really busy though, you may find yourself with nowhere to sit and enjoy the show. I overheard other patrons talking to employees who said that they sell tickets to some of the shows. I'm not sure how that would work unless they limited the sales to match the number of seats available. I'm glad I got a table, because it would have been very difficult to eat and drink standing up against a wall -- which unfortunately is what I saw a very healthy chunk of people being forced to do due to the limited seating at this place.

Visited Nashville with a group of 6 to experience the nightlife. We tried all the hot spots on Broadway. Made our way up to 8th Ave and found this hidden gem! Excellent live music, well crafted cocktails, and perfect fried pickles! We had very attentive server named Paul, that made us feel right at home. We never had to look for him for another round, he had them to us before we even had to ask! I can imagine this will not remain a hidden gem for long, NashHouse can be a destination all on its own.
A great honky tonk!  Really enjoyed the music!!Don't change a thing.  Good food, relaxed atmosphere, not overly crowded for lunch, and good traditional country music.

Went there for dinner with my girlfriends. Fun vibe, right on the strip. I had the catfish strips, they were more like full on fillets. They were delicious!! And you got plenty of food for a very decent price. I love this place, would definitely go back!

We came here after a big lunch at Hattie B's that was a mistake.  Not because the food wasn't delicious but because we were stuffed.  Started with the biscuits and jam which was sublime.  The fluffy buttery biscuits were amazing.  The jams: Strawberry; peach; blackberry; tomato; grape; and butter were so good.  Then we had the deviled eggs with: bacon; pimento mayo; pickles; chow chow; and I forget what the other one was.  Delicious but then we started to hit the wall.  Had a nice Tennessee pilsener which was light and refreshing.  I ordered the Southern Burger which was a pimento cheese burger with a fried green tomato on top.  It was really good but after two bites I was so full that I had to call it a night.  Ditto for my Daughter who got the enormous pork shank which she said was delicious as well but she couldn't finish it.  I'd come back here just for the biscuits alone.  Servers were nice and friendly.  Live country music was great as well.  Lot of fun I. The Gulch.  Check it out.

Great time all around. We came for the line dancing lessons so the 12 year old in our family could experience Nashville at night. Loved the atmosphere. Amazing live music. We didn't try much to eat since we were mostly dancing. Very crowded. If you're trying to get a seat fast definitely sit at the bar where there is open seating.

By far one of the worst meals I have had in a very long time. The first dish we ordered was a basic hamburger, and the patty was wafer thin and burnt to a crisp. I could crack it like a potato chip. The lettuce was wilted and stale, and the french fries were soggy and cold. The other dish was eggs Benedict with crab meat. Could not taste crab at all. Also ordered a bloody Mary, which seem to have no vodka in it at all. I was told dismissively if I wanted to add fixings to it, I had to take it over to the bloody Mary bar, which was covered in flies, due to open patio seating. We never got utensils, we never got napkins. We are locals, and I often have guests over and refer them to restaurants on lower Broadway, but I will make sure they skip this place.

only thing they really have going is the food. it's good. today went there for friends bach party, 8 of us. we were told we'd have a 45-60 min wait. fine we went and sat in the bar area. we were at tables on dirty tables the entire wait - not one person coming up to the tables. making us have to go to the bar to get which isn't a big deal but going up taking turns so we didn't lose the table. (1 hr being there) finally got a table.. got our food and drinks ordered.. server seemed good at first. food took probably about another 45 mins to get. yes it was good so worth the wait. we're done shorty after... waiter is no where to be found for at least 20 mins ... finally found told him we had to go. said he was closing out another table and he'd be back. 20 mins later finally back and got to close us out. we were there literally for a good 3 hrs just wasting our day away. also- they add on gratuity of 20% so our server towards the middle/ end obviously knew and decided not to give a f about us anymore. smh

This was honestly one of my favorite bars in Nashville which is so funny because I was not a huge fan of going out in the first place. In fact, the next couple days after visiting I couldn't remember the name of this bar so whenever it came up in conversation I called it "Pleasant Surprise!" 

Why did I like it? Well it was a rooftop bar right next to Bridgestone Arena and overlooking the downtown strip. It had awesome, attentive staff constantly working to make sure everyone's experience was fun yet controlled and safe. The food and drinks, while I didn't have any myself, were tasty looking and quite affordable. It wasn't insanely crowded like a lot of the other bars. And the live music was amazing!!

The band playing the night we went was sassy, funny, and extremely talented. I was completely sober, out hours past my comfortable bed time, and in a bar with loud music and crazy tourists and bridal parties yet I was happy as a clam because this band up on stage was one of the most talented live performing bands I'd seen yet. They played all the way to last call (yes we stayed till last call) without a break and anything from The Killers to Lady A. 

Clearly Rippy's knows how to hire them so if you're in town and looking for a great night out with talented live music, a view, a breeze, and some pretty good food definitely make a stop by.

I came in here for like the 4th time in the last 10 years. First off, the music was good, but the amp might have been tuned up a bit too high. The bar tender was nice and friendly, but my God, the prices here are comparable to NY. This is Nashville, ten bucks for a small whiskey and coke in a plastic cup is over the top. I was told "welcome to broadway prices" and I sighed. Is this city so completely blown out? It's TN after all......So, as for the food....we got the 'pick two meat, pay extra for the brisket, and pick two sides' and I was completely dissatisfied. The brisket was dry and thin, the pulled pork was satisfactory, the Mac and cheese might as well have come from a box, and the turnip greens were ABSOLUTELY horrible, tasteless and soggy. All around, 37 bucks for a shared meal and two drinks, not bad but tourist prices and the BBQ was not at all even remotely decent. I probably won't ever come here again except for a drink and live music. Has the standard for TN BBQ gone down? I get that it's "Broadway" but I should think the price of drinks and food is wayyyyy out of hand here!

Love the classic ambiance here. Live music seems to be great everywhere in Nashville but I like that this place is less touristy and more local authentic Nashville. The audience is less juvenile and not pretentious at all. We enjoyed ourselves so much!

We used to like coming here.

My wife and I travel to Nashville a couple of times a year. The Nashville Palace was on our list of "must go" places, due largely to the music played on the stage in the smaller front bar room.

Times have changed.

We stopped at the Palace three times on our last trip. On a weeknight when there were maybe 20 people in the place it took almost 40 minutes to get an order of onion rings--which were lukewarm and grease soaked by the time it got to our table. The bartender was nice, but kept disappearing somewhere. Getting fresh drinks was a constant struggle.

The band was so-so for a Nashville honky-tonk. They were too loud for the space, their drummer was much too rock-n-roll for the format and they used an electronic toy to augment the background vocals. For the first time in our travels to Nashville we did not enjoy the music at the Palace.

The second time was an afternoon when a great solo act was on stage. this was our best experience of the three. the guy on stage was entertaining and the bartender kept our drinks full.

The third time was the worst. The band was great! However, we got NO service at our table. None.

If we had been drunk--we weren't--or had been a couple of jerks I could understand getting less than stellar service. All we did was sit down at a table, then got ignored.

After three hours of fetching our own drinks we had a talk with the bartender. We didn't get much of an answer from him, so we paid our tab after the band was done and left.

Bottom Line: The Nashville Palace appears to be changing their approach to service, food, and entertainment. And we believe the arrow is pointed down in all three areas.

This place is a tourist trap. This was the last place we went to during our bar hoping on a Friday night. There was a 6$ cover to get in. This was the only place that we had to pay cover at the whole night, so we were not too excited about that. The place is pretty huge inside with lots of seating and a massive dance floor. Drinks and food are overpriced. It is pretty much only good if you want to line dance all night.  Don't waste your time or money with this place. Downtown Nashville offers much better bars.

If you know line dancing, this is the place to be. If you don't line dance this is the place to  be. There are easy to follow instructions to get you started. 

Don't let that couple with the great moves Intimidate you, each of them are "instructors" that will have you doing some of those great moves in no time too. If you're lucky enough one of them may pull you onto the dance floor and you will be part of "that couple with the great moves". 

if your brave enough to get up on your own fumbling along following that guy or gal over there, not to worry again, because they too are instructors planted on the dance floor who helpfully guide you to look like the pro you can be. 

Just get out on the dance floor, it's a fun night you don't want to miss.

This is my favorite pizza place in Nashville.  The atmosphere is fun and I especially love the upstairs patio when it's warmer.  It's a great place to bring my friends and family when they come to visit me here in Nashville.  The parking sucks, but luckily I live close enough to walk.  If you're driving, try to snag a spot on 19th Ave S or you can valet park. 
The whole wheat crust is delicious and I've never been disappointed by the pizza at Soulshine.  They also have a couple different plates of nachos to chose from and they used to be SO good!  I mean, I would come here just for nachos because they were that good.  However, my heart is broken because the last two times I've been to Soulshine the chips have been different, and not in a good way. They used to be thick and freshly made chips that almost were like a pita chip/tortilla combination sent down from heaven. Seriously, I lived for these chips. However, they have started to use just regular old blue corn tortilla chips that I could purchase myself at any Kroger. So disappointing!! I'd give Soulshine a five star review if they hadn't changed their nacho chips. Please bring back the old chips! I miss them!!
Good music and the pulled pork was excellent. The fries were a little weak. Overall good choice
Hard to find if you aren't looking hard. Pretty ok crowd for young, hipster types. Karaoke here. Good prices. Wish we had a bar like this at home.

Well I must say if I would have read some of the reviews ahead of time and hadn't been so hungry I probably would have driven past.  Then again maybe the Dukes of Hazard museum next door would have been enough to draw me, well no I guess not. 

This is a bar in a out of the way place. I don't mean this in a bad way but the bartenders scared me, no need to go into details but I wouldn't sit at the bar again. It's close to the G.O.O and a huge hotel/convention center but nothing else really around. The music was very OK and for a place like Nashville there seems to be a hundred better choices to see live music.  Now the smoked wings were pretty damn good.  Well smoked and tasty, then again I was very hungry. 

Overall not worth the stop in my opinion.  If you want live music go downtown, it's not that far!

KT

I love it when a friend says, "Let's go dive bar hopping!" Don't mind if we do...at ALL. I have been dying to come to this place for a long time (even if I always mistakenly call it Twin Peaks...uh...wrong joint) and finally I got to go. Yay me! 

So this place is just a big square room with a bar at the back. Tables in the middle and TVs on the walls. Perfect for us to look at the Olympics opening ceremonies while also drinking some cold beer. Yes, cold beer, and pretty cheap too. Shuffleboard. Fun patrons. Smoke 'em if you got 'em. 

The best thing was karaoke. God, I love a dive bar with karaoke. YES PLEASE! No stage or anything, you just stand up by the KJ near the hallway to the bathroom and rock out. I immediately started signing up for songs. The clientele ran a little younger than me and they were singing a bunch of 90s songs but it was awesome. Everyone clapped even if you were a not-so-good singer. I rocked all my jams and had a FUCKING BLAST. Also, one dude from Venezuela or Brazil or somewhere sang a damn Robbie Williams song. Who the hell knows him around here? I loved it.

Look, the dive bars in Nashville are slowly going away to be replaced by condos, townhouses, parking lots, and whatever else. You can't make dive bars like this, they have to already be there...so let's just all bow down to the awesomeness that is Twin Kegs and patronize it all the time so that it will stay around FOR-EVAH.

Awesome vibes upstairs but it took us about 30 minutes to get a server to our table. After 15 minutes we finally asked a server who had been walking around and serving tables next to us and he said we had a different server who would be around.. we waited another 15 minutes with still no service. Finally we got someone, which was ridiculous. We ordered our food right away and some drinks. The food was good, but the amount of time to wait especially after trying to get someone to help who refused was pretty disappointing. I almost wanted to go back downstairs and wait for a dining table and skip out on the band. I liked being upstairs though with a view of broadway.

We just walked in here because it was close and looked fun.  We came back three times on our short vacation just to see waitress TAMMY.  She is fun and she is the ONLY one of all the actual bar tenders that got our drinks right.  When we went for 3rd time she wasn't working so we just ordered beer.  She is a great asset to your business!!!

Stopped into this place right after the Predators ice hockey game.  Was just across the street and looked good.   Live music was playing, which is typical here in Nashville.  I must say, Nashville has surpassed Austin, TX for the live music capitol of the world.  Lots more live music venues and bars, but then again, lots of them are country, where Austin has a various mix.

Any ways, back to the food.  We were just grabbing a late night drink and bite after game, and were craving the barbecue.  We went with Rippy's Super Sampler Platter of all kinds of meats. Wings were good, and the ribs fell off the bone.  Really enjoyed that.  The sausage and pork loin wasn't that special, but still good.  We were expecting more for the price, but still wasn't too bad.  But, I've had better.

Although we didn't eat here we came for the live entertainment and drinks. 

There was no cover with music on every floor. This was a fun place to be during the day and at night. We sat at high tables by the band and our waiter was checking on us consistently which is great considering we had a larger party and we all finished our drinks at separate times. If you're looking for a good place in Nashville with good music...Rippys is your place to be.
A good and family friendly place with live music and line dancing lessons.  Food is fine, but it's the atmosphere that makes for a great experience.

We stopped by the NashHouse looking for a relaxed brunch atmosphere and found just that! Our group of 7 all enjoyed our food and dining experience as our waiter was very attentive. The music videos being shown on the large screen was a great touch and we had no problem getting seated on a Sunday morning. Overall a great experience and a place that I would recommend to others!

I went there last night. They had a great lively atmosphere. The workers there are just awful and hateful. I bought two beers and it was $9.50 and I gave the little blonde bartender $10 and said don't worry about the change. I always tip my bartenders after the night with a larger sum. This bartender said "really fifty cents, you think I need your fifty cents" and threw two quarters on the bar. No I didn't think she needed my fifty cents, I was just trying to save her a trip back to me to deliver fifty cents. Needless to say I did not give a better tip at the end of the night as my party of 15 and I left and took our business elsewhere. I've never been treated with such disrespect! I will never recommend this place. Honky Tonk Central is much more friendly!!

Rippy's has potential to be a great bar. It's not. $4.75 for domestics make it one of the most expensive on the strip. The cost of food is nowhere near reasonable. For 10 bucks I got wings. The wings had no meat and them and were mostly batter. When I say no meant on them, I mean I saw mostly bone on the drumsticks. When I asked the server about it, she took care of it right? NO. Instead, she went ahead an added gratuity to our table of 5! Food is bad. Won't be back. Sorry to say as a Nashville native.

We were stopping here after a tour, and decided we would just eat here....GOOD decision. I had a really good mushroom Swiss burger with some fantastic fries. There was live music (at 1:30pm) and good service. Plus it was inexpensive. That pretty much ticks all the boxes. Would absolutely visit again.
Marissa was the best bartender we've had during our time in Nashville! She let us pick whatever music we wanted to play. Highly recommend Big Machine!

I was in town visiting. I figured, hell, might as well check out how they dance down here. Its REALLY big inside, looks are deceiving from the outside. Sure enough, by the time I got in, there were already peeps dancing. I think overall it was a pretty cool experience, if not for the garbage bar tender who when I asked for a drink of water (cause I'd been drinking all day and needed to sober up/hydrate) responded with "I'm in the middle of an order here, so you're just going to have to wait, OK?? Pretty amazed at his response, given that I was hella nice in asking him and not being all demanding and shit. Congratulations a$$hole, you just gave the Wildhorse Saloon 1 star on Yelp.

I was in Nashville for the night and decided to go out and explore the downtown area.  There was a lot going on and I was a little bit overwhelmed. However, after walking around for a bit I decided on Rippy's. Based on the reviews and the photos I should have left immediately, but I just really wanted to eat. I wanted to Tennessee Hot chicken but that wasn't on their menu. For drinks i got the honky tonk tea (really good) and the Tropical something(i can't remember the full name, but i didn't enjoy it. It tasted like cheap liquor and Red Bull). For food i ordered the pork loin with a double side of Mac & cheese. It kind of reminded me of school lunch. I think i was most shocked by the Mac. I was under the impression because i was in the south i was going to get some really good Mac. This  one tasted like crafts.

Cheap beer, live music (all day), and fried bologna sandwiches? Well, I could just get used to this town...

Came here after doing the Redneck Bus Tour (pretty funny, actually). We just wanted to have a few snacks before heading to the Opry (which we didn't). Enjoyed some live music and I had a bologna sandwich - which certainly hit the spot after a night on the town getting rowdy. Wish we were more in the mood for kicking back and drinking - seems like a fun place to get a little rowdy as a group.

Our waitress was top-notch.

Had dinner there for the first time last night before the Preds game.  Service was slow even through there were a lot of servers standing around, and the place was at less than 50% capacity.   Burger and Chicken sandwich took 40 minutes to arrive, then we waited another 5 to get silverware.  Food was cold and my wife's burger was burnt black on the bottom.

We just got an order of wings while watching a little college hoops.. a swing band was playing that was quite good.  The wings were enough for a table of three, just as a little appetizer.   Good service.

The main thing I enjoyed about this venue was the free dance lessons. 

The drinks were pretty expensive and lacking. 
I didn't care for the vibe. It was large and yet somehow still stuffy. 

The people running the dance lessons were great, but the rest of the staff seemed stand-offish and less than enthused. 
We ended up sitting at the bar as we were told all of the tables were occupied ( even though many were not). 

I enjoyed this one time experience, but doubt I'd go again. 
3/5
Good barbecue.  Live country music, a nice place to stop for a meal.  Friendly staff.  Walking distance from the convention center and close to the hockey arena.  Seat yourself.

the burger here is epic. staff is always considerate and make sure my glass is full. if that wasn't enough, weekend karaoke at this bar is a hell of a good time with singers of every level (broadway to tone deaf) and every genre. the crowd seems to have a great time. i know i always do. have been coming here since 2010. they just upgraded the back patio for a sweet hang-out spot. i can't ask for more.

bar is beer/cider only and smoking permitted inside. other location on Hermitage has liquor but no smoking.

Just Because .." Hello are you eating ? " Great Greeting huh..? Come In , Listen to music , have a few drinks , cause its BAR FOOD , They call it BBQ ...But its BAR FOOD ... Listen to music few brinks , More BAR FOOD..  Decent portions, Plastic dinnerware , bucket of sauces table side. Lotz of Napkins . Their ribs are over smoked with flavor TooMuch , pulled pork was ... ,However their grilled chicken was very good.  Im guessing cause that was made fresh to order, and nicely spiced . 

With that we are heading out to Honky Tonk & Nudies , too see whats going on there ..

This place is great.  Free to get in, within walking distance of the hotel we were staying at.  On Friday and Saturday when we were in town they had Larry Hamilton Band (fantastic band), which we really enjoyed dancing to.  

Nice there is a place to go to listen to good, traditional country music.  Good priced beer and great food.

We come here every time we come to town.  Another plus, there is no smoking inside, unlike another bar down the street from there.

Look forward to coming here again next time we are in town.

We stopped in to have lunch yesterday. We walked in and the office door was open and 2 women had their feet up on the desk, chatting. We stood for a while trying to figure out if they were open. There were people cleaning in the dining area, so I walked into the bar and asked the bartender if they were serving food. She just stared at me like I was speaking a foreign language. We finally turned around and walked out. We recommend getting better service and you might have business.
The bbq there was delicious!!!  Decent price. I wish the service was a little bit better. They do come around. But when you do need someone no ones around. The live music was entertaining.
This place was great for the drinks and that's about it. Ordered the bbq skillet hash which contained one small piece of meat and the rest potatoes. Biscuits were very hard and dry.
Awesome rib wrap. Great music, service, & local beers!  Wonderful place for BBQ. Don't miss this hot spot.

The BBQ here had been recommended from the customer service agent at our hostile. 

We split the Rippy's smoked Pick'em and got boned ribs, pulled pork, onion rings, curly fries and we also added an order of cornbread muffins. 

The Ribs were just Ok, but seemed a tad dry. The pulled pork was pretty good but lacked spices and we had to really lather on the sauce. 
Onion rings and curly fries were standard and cornbread muffin were ok. 

The service was very prompt. Our cups were always filled; which might be why this place was so crowded. 

We were seated in a separate room and constantly had people scooting on our table or bumping into us while we ate which made the dining experience a bit difficult. 

The sheer amount of food you get, value wise, is pretty great in my book. ( Granted I am also use to NYC pricing.) 

I don't think I'd come back for the food, but maybe for drinks. 
3/5

My friend and I went to Rippy's while waiting for a bar crawl to begin. We got there before 9 and were somehow able to snag a table.

The top level is an amazing - open air bar with seating and an artist almost always playing. The band while we were there were great! They played all covers and the mostly inebriated people would get really into most songs. Cue Wagon Wheel! And yes, the place is full of overserved people but what was interesting to me was it was people of shapes, sizes, sorts and ages - including groups of friends, couples, and families. Rippy's seems to be the place for everyone. 

Beers are mega expensive. More expensive than other places on Broadway for the same beers. However even with that, I had one of my more enjoyable Broadway experiences here because of the music, open air and actually being able to get a seat for an hour.
Stopped in to do some shopping listen to music and get another drink all this walking the wife is having me do is driving me to drink.

About my favorite place in my neighborhood now. I have watched this place blossom. Have gone through some personnel changes but have a really friendly staff. Drawing a more diverse crowd than when I first started going. Beer selection has expanded big time. And you hear the cliche "best burger in town" alot. But this place truly lives up to that billing

I can't do zero stars but this place is so unforgiving and anti freedom. If you have a confederate flag don't come here. General Lee is next door but don't exploit your freedom here. The band was amazing the service was fabulous but the management will will stifle your group activity. Visiting from Cali. Californians and free thinkers, this is not your stop. Kristen was the only bright star here.

Typical honky tonk, live bands, decent food. If you go to Rippy's make sure you sit at Jennifer Miceli's bar, she's amazing. Some of the other bar tenders come across as rude but she isn't one of them. She's always smiling, friendly and attentive. She is very easy to talk to and makes the bar so much more enjoyable. I hate going to the bar if she isn't working, by far my favorite bar tender!!

What an interesting/weird spot. I like that this place is different, but I feel like maybe there is too much going on. It's hard to imagine people line dancing right in front of a table that people are eating at. There was a live band while we were at the bar having a drink, but no dancing. It seems like it would be better left as a bar, than a restaurant. How anyone would enjoy dinner over loud music and people dancing around, is beyond me. We had one drink while people watching at the bar but promptly left. It was starting to get crowded and we had no intention of eating dinner there.

Went here a few times while in Nashville, it's a fun place, but staff can be a bit rude (which is disappointing on any vacation) Food is mediocre, typical bar food. Pretty touristy place, so don't expect to mingle with the locals here if that's your MO.

On the positive side, they've got a nice open rooftop area. Would go back, but proceed with caution.

Wow. What a venue. Got to see Nick Cave perform an "In Conversation" evening. It was a singular experience, only enhanced by the intimacy of the James K. Polk theater! The stage was perfect for an event like this, where Cave could actually walk out into the audience, and be with the crowd.

The sound was pitch perfect, which is key for such a smaller show like this. Would love to see other performances there. I'm sure that seeing symphonies, ballets, and lighter fare would be just as wonderful.

The only reason I knocked off a star was that it was pretty warm within. I noticed quite a few around me with fans. I reckon they were regulars who knew better.

Wish there was a 0stars option. Entirely too pricey for such small drinks ( they taste okay)
I'm a cigarette smoker and the pulled pork and chicken literally tasted like my fingers smell after a cigarette. So basically smoked human flesh. The sides look to be canned and taste as such. Had baked beans that looked like refried beans and Mac n cheese that was the consistency of mashed potatoes. Will never waste my time or money again.

This is a fun place to pop in for a quick taste of their moonshine, which is actually quite smooth. It was nice to see the still and talk to the staff about the spirits, but with so much more going on all around, it's not a place where I felt compelled to hang out longer than a few minutes. The sampler is worth it to try their stuff, and the cool little bottle of shine makes a nice souvenir.

I like the vibe here and the staff and management.  There are so many choices.  The bread pudding and red beans and rice will keep me coming back. Two strange things are that the pizza tastes great in the restaurant but once it gets cold or is reheated, it loses it's desirability; and that there are usually more African Americans depicted on the wall than there are AA customers. Oh well.

Btw, skip the garlic bread. It's not garlicky, seems to have yellow cheese instead of mozzarella, and is just a kids cheese pizza without sauce, which they then give you in a cup

We  went to TPAC for the very first time on January 11, 2018 to see JERSEY BOYS.  The show itself was TERRIFIC!!   

The venue, left a lot to be desired.  First of all, it was rather warm in the lobby, but I attributed it to all of the people walking around. 
Once inside, it was actually hot.  My husband spoke to the box office about it and they told him they had not turned the air on that day.  January 11th was 67 degrees at 7pm, plus that many people in a theater and no air conditioning??!!   Everyone around us was fanning themselves with their programs, it grew warmer and you began to smell perspiration, cologne, beer and frankly it was DISGUSTING.  The woman next to me had to leave her seat and go stand all the way in the back because she thought she was going to vomit from the heat and smells.  My husband said he would not return because the smell of beer was gross.  This is NOT what I expected from this venue after having paid $100 per ticket including fees.

Second, I have never been to a Theater where drinks and food are allowed inside the theater.  I was shocked at how sticky and dirty the floors were when locating our seats.  Plus my seat looked like some kind of liquid had been spilled on it and left to dry.  By the time we left the theater, there were cups, wrappers, napkins. etc. littering the floor.  Terrible.

Again, the show was AWESOME but very, very disappointed in the Venue.

I wish I had time to write a more detailed review about this place but I wanted to share a quick tip with fellow Nashvillian yelpers:  CRAWFISH SOUP.  Must try.  Fabulous.

The pizza I had was good, too.

After a big Spring Break party for Yelp, my friends and I decided to go down on Broadway Ave to enjoy the vibe and the strip of Nashville. Originally we were to meet at Robert's but it was so busy. We decided on our next location, Rippy's. 

Throughout my trip, I've passed it a few times and loved the look! This two story joint offers a lot of room! The bottom floor has a bar area and a stage for live music. One great thing about Nashville is the live music and this place was no different. When we visited, a trio was singing on stage and sang some wonderful country tunes. When I walked upstairs, I was surprised to see that the place was jammed packed! This was more of the "nightclub" version of the place. Huge outdoor windows offered a lot of fresh air. Whether or not you go upstairs or down, the beers are pretty reasonable. A Coors Light goes for about $6. 

One of the highlights of this trip was being able to meet MTV star, CT. I don't know if he worked there or not, but I saw him behind the bar and asked him to take a picture. I'm a huge fan of the shows he's on and love that guy in general. In a place like Nashville, I was certainly surprise to see him there, but super thankful I did!

At the end of the evening, I thought we had a great time. The place is perfectly located and has a super chill vibe that would bring joy to anyone's day. When I'm back in town, I'm certainly making my way back to Rippy's. Thanks for a great time folks!

We walked into Rippy's tonight and sat at a high top table by the windows. We sat there for twenty minutes and no one came up to us to ask us if we wanted a drink. Finally my friend got up and stood at the bar to order. The blonde behind the bar would not look at her. She did all she could to avoid her. My friend then stood right in front of her and when she asked for the frozen jack and cola's, she said we only sell those on the roof then turned and walked away. Ummm what if we wanted something else then!? We weren't going to the rooftop when it was raining outside. It was completely rude and uncalled for. That's how you treat paying customers!? If ever in Nashville skip this spot! There are plenty of other places to go to.

We were late getting into Nashville and wanted somewhere to eat dinner and have a good time. Wild horse was definitely that place! The food was great and the dancing was even better. In between dancing they have wonderful performers that make dinner nice as well. It's the best of both worlds. Very clean and nice. We will definitely be returning on our next trip!

When in Music City, should you ever find yourself lucky enough to be here, this here saloon, is as good a place to start or finish things as your trip winds its way. As time advances, you'll never know what band you might see, or have seen here,  who ends up making the big time. And then you can say that you saw them here at The Wildhorse, when they were just up-and-coming. This is just a great bar, with a great live music scene in one of the greatest live music cities in the entire world! And that's really all that it is.

One of the worst experiences I have ever had at a bar. Hadn't had a single drink yet and was kicked out during a lowkey afternoon after having been there for 20 minutes. Felt completely disrespected by the manager when I asked for an explanation of the situation. Spoke to some people sitting at the bar who said they thought the food was horrible as well. Definitely plan to skip this one.

Heard about NashHouse while on a Uber ride downtown with a local! I loved the space of the venue and the giant performance stage. Their was no performance last night due to the hockey playoffs being on, but I really enjoyed the atmosphere and especially the food. I had the dill pepper salmon with asparagus and cauliflower. Wow the flavor was so perfect on everything, I could have it again just writing about it now lol. For dessert I had the cobbler of the moment which happened to be apple, it came with ice cream.

A lively spot on the strip that features live local music and bbq. The smoked chicken was decent but very dry, adding a squirt of the house sauce helped. But the baked beans and coleslaw stood out for me, I enjoyed them both. I did not enjoy the spongy, seemingly factory made corn cake thing that came with my meal, it was lame; my recommendation is to skip it, it's not worth the calories. My husband said his ribs were just ok. They were served dry (you can ask for them wet), he said the sauce (served on the side) was kind of watery but the meat was fall off the bone tender and the rub was flavorful. The house band was fun although they charged $20 for special requests, which means we spent 40 bucks on Marshall Tucker bands "Heard it in a Love Song" and Brooks and Dunn's "Neon Moon"...I can't believe I'm admitting to that on the internet! They were a well-prepared cover band and that offered good renditions of popular country music songs. Sadly much of their show was spent asking for tips which left us wishing that we were at a more legit spot off the strip where you can experience true artistry from songwriters who don't waste stage time begging for money. Short story, the food is what you would expect from a touristy restaurant on the strip. One noteworthy advantage was that they let us bring our kids in. Most places on Broadway that play live music won't let kids in after 6pm. So Rippy's was a good choice for us because we got to let our kids experience a family friendly honky tonk :)

We ordered through Door stop Delivery. We waited a while to receive our order and when we got it, it was COLD! The breadstick tasted like they had been sitting for awhile. The pizza COLD. WE are not far from the restaurant and it should not have been delivered cold for the price we paid. They upcharge their menu prices for delivery,which we already pay a service fee and delivery fee. I am very disappointed!! WILL NOT BE BACK

This is a bar you MUST visit at least once during your visit to Nashville - especially if you're having a night out on the town. Located conveniently on Broadway, Rippy's is a fan favorite. The live music and beers are constantly flowing - and with that comes the singing and dancing of all that love and adore Nashville. Their rooftop is probably my favorite feature, especially in those summer months. And right across the street is Tootsie's, so after your wrap up your rooftop singalongs, you can stumble (I mean ... walk) onward to the next hot spot. ;)

Please note -- I would not opt for this place just for dinner. Choose a 5 star meal in Nashville (there are plenty!) and THEN make your way to Broadway for your shenanigans.
Food was pricey and mediocre at best. Would not recommend . Server was friendly, but wouldn't go back .

This is a place for tourists...the group I went with wanted to go here...

1. Most all of their alcoholic beverages were in souvenir glasses you can take home...I didn't partake as it seemed cheesy. 

2. Every 2 seconds they tell you to go check out their gift shop....very annoying. 

3. You can find subpar food somewhere else...the basics, burgers, chicken fingers some salads and some brisket/pulled pork sandwiches...  

The only thing that was awesome and impressed me was their fried pickles....OMG the best I have ever had. 

4. The music was ok and the dancing lessons were ok if you wanted to learn. There was some kind of local cover band their that did some Sweet home Alabama and Beverly Hills by Weezer that they made into country...I guess it was interesting. 


If you stay at the Gaylord Opryland hotel cover is free. 

I can't give it more than 2 stars because it was way too touristy for me, I know when in a touristy area that they are trying to sell the experience...but this place is trying too hard...way too hard.

I was in Nashville for the first time and only for 2 days. I didn't have too much time to explore in the evening but had to at least try to see the Broadway nightlife. We walked around a bit as we could hear talented musicians from just about every venue. We passed by Wildhorse Saloon and heard amazing music coming from the inside. We felt as if we had the privilege of attending a free concert. The music was great and the drinks were very reasonably priced. They also had one dancing lessons every couple of hours. Great quick exposure to the Nashville scene.

So I'd be lying if I didn't say this is a pretty cool venue.  It's huge, with tons of seating and a large space for line dancing.  We were seated on the main floor, because it wasn't particularly busy on the Sunday night we chose to go, but the upper floors looked pretty big, and the balconies for each floor were lined with chairs for viewing the dance floor and stage.

Every hour and a half or so, they would invite anyone and everyone up for a line dancing lesson, and then after would bring up the band so you could continue your newly learned line dancing moves.  The musicians on this particular evening were really good; we stayed long enough to see both their acoustic and full band set and enjoyed them both.

OK, so the venue is cool, dancing is neat, bands are good, so why only two stars, you ask?

All these good things cannot make-up how lousy their menu is.  It's a small menu, choices are limited and prices are high.  My husband and mother-in-law got their chicken and biscuits ($16) and both had to load up on salt and pepper to make it edible.  I ordered a pulled pork sandwich ($12), which was bland and dry and could not be saved by their (disgusting) BBQ sauce they have sitting on every table.  I've had better BBQ pork sandwiches in southern Ohio for under $7.  Also, my sandwich came with a horrible hodge-podge of french fries.  There were curly fries, and waffle fries, and some sort of seasoned fries.  Literally it was all of my least favorite fries thrown together and served to me lukewarm.  I was NOT happy.  

I'm clearly an idiot, because I decided to order a dessert to try to fill me up, since I couldn't choke down my fries or sandwich.  We got their chocolate toffee mousse cake.  The "toffee" part of the name is referring to a minuscule drizzle of caramel over a sickeningly rich slab of chocolate.  I was splitting this dessert with my husband and we didn't even finish it.

Our bill for two bland entrees, one deceptive dessert and a tip for mediocre service was $45.  We didn't even drink because, GET THIS, a cocktail is $16.  I DON'T CARE that it comes in a souvenir glass, I'm not that kind of tourist, and it just puts me off.

Come for the dancing, come for the music, but don't come for the food.  You've been warned.

I give 5 stars for the history in this place. Country legends have performed here for many years and at one point this was the place for aspiring musicians. If I remember correctly, Randy Travis worked here many moons ago. Reba performed here, among many others. 

It's decent in size and good for large groups or parties. It's also close to the airport and Opry Mills. If you are next door at the "Cooters"  Dukes of Hazard Museum, then it's worth adding to your stop. 

As for the food, I have nothing to rave about. This place needs vegetarian options badly.

I thought the whole wheat crust was delicious on our pizza. The crawfish soup is to die for! The service was good, but not out of this world. The Pig nachos were delicious as an app. Everyone left feeling full and happy. I would go back for sure.

Came here on a snowy Tuesday night - wasn't packed at all.

Ordered a full slab, beans and coleslaw.

The beans were pretty good. Coleslaw ok. Ribs were pretty dry and didn't really fall off the bone. I wouldn't say tough - but borderline. Certainly not great.

The live music was pretty cool, though they pester you with the tip bucket (and they ask you twice if you don't have cash on you) which fan seem a little unfriendly.

I'm sure this is great when it's full of great people and music but tonight it really wasn't a hit.
Just had a beer but the food did look good.

Ugh, the Wildhorse Saloon is going downhill, quickly, and it makes me sad! This used to be a staple part of our annual Nashville trip, yet the past few visits have been nothing short of disappointing.

For starters, the place is HUGE - three floors, to be exact, but they never seem to have enough staff to keep the place running smoothly. What's the point of a restaurant/bar that big if you are not going to utilize it to the full potential! 

We walked in with a party of 10 and were told it would be a 15 minute wait - 40 minutes later, we were sat. I have no problem with waiting for a table, especially given our large group, however, the issue is how those 40 minutes were spent... waiting in line at the bar! There were two bartenders on a Friday evening and it was complete chaos. Apparently, people who don't want to wait for a table can choose to sit in the open seating area and can order food at the bar... it really messes up the entire system.

Our service was decent, no complaints. I always brag about Wildhorse having the best fried pickles in Nashville - after this last visit, my friends and family think I'm crazy! The pickles were soggy and all stuck together in one big pickle lump.

Pulled pork was fine, yet things just seemed over price. Sad to say that I don't know if I'll return to this once favorite place of mine.

Honestly best service and experience we had in Nashville. Being a bachelor party of 20 was not always easy but the Nashville paLace was the sweetest! Very accommodating and food was excellent. It was not very busy during the day on Thursday when we went but we got to listen to live music and sit on their patio in the sun. Highly recommend.

The problem with Soulshine is that it is within walking distance to several other really great pizza spots with better service and better quality so there's very little reason to eat here. It's never on my radar but one night we had a group and we didn't want to mess with crowds or driving anywhere so we decided to give it another shot. Yikes! Starting off, the service...it was so bad...the poor guy was brand new and he was visibly nervous so we felt really bad for him. What made it even worse was that he had to come back to our table several times to tell us certain beers were unavailable, to ask what kind of wine was ordered and one beer was completely forgotten. Again, he was nervous so we tried to make him feel comfortable and not give him a hard time so this isn't a reflection on him, it's a reflection that training can't be that good if someone that nervous and that doesn't know the menu is working an evening shift that covers the whole patio. The food came out and it was correct so yay for our server meticulously writing everything down but the food just didn't taste that great. Seriously, there's so many other pizza and sandwich spots, this place just isn't worth the time. I did hear that they have really great happy hour specials though so maybe we will give it another shot later.

Food was pub fare, and as to be expected it was okay.

The upstairs has an awesome atmosphere and there was a live concert going on so it was basically like being outside being able to listen to it. You felt like you were outside with all the openness of the bar. The bartenders were all very nice and friendly and talked with us. Everyone at the bar sitting near us were all out of town too and they were friendly as well. Kind of expensive, as to be expected since it was on Broadway. 

Overall, great experience and friendly, quick service.

This is by far the worst place to eat in Nashville. We ordered the Chicken Fried Steak bites, Meatloaf, Quesadilla and Pork Chops and they were all extremely dry without taste. I do not see how people have rated this 4* other than the live music. If you are looking for food, stay away from this place .

First of all, we were so excited to go to this place, that is until we actually got there. Unless you're staying at the Gaylord Opryland (which we were), you have to pay a $6 cover charge. This was a surprise because there was only one other spot on Broadway that charged a cover, everywhere else was no cover at all. Only after complaining about the cover did they ask about if we were staying at a Marriott hotel. Then, we asked where we could sit and they pointed over to a bar area, hey we were cool with that. Until we went to sit down and a server told us that this bar area was reserved and we couldn't sit there. So, they pointed us to another bar. The bartender there told us that the entire bar area was closed due to it being reserved, however, all of the seats were empty. They also did not have the mechanical bull, which they were supposed to and they told us that they no longer have it. So, after a second time being told that we couldn't sit some place, we decided to leave. Not to mention the staff and servers were not very friendly which is not typical of any place that I visited while in Nashville.

Don't bother going here for an early dinner with kids. The bouncer (that alone should be a warning sign ) will only allow a certain number of people in. They actually closed the door after our kids entered and didn't let the parents follow immediately after because it wasn't "part of the process"... what?!?!  I suppose there is a specific number that's allowed to enter at a time but regardless you can't separate kids from the parents when we were right behind them. After that experience (& escalating to a manager), our group of 20 immediately left & walked a couple blocks over to Martin's BBQ where we had good service & complimentary moon pies during our 5 minute wait.
Live music and line dancing, a fun night out! It's massive and there's tons of seating, I had a great time trying to learn how to line dance and joining in with everyone.

The Tennessee Performing Arts Center (TPAC) hosts some really great events, musicals, the Nashville ballet and opera, conferences, comedy shows and more. The Center houses multiple theaters with varying capacities. The main lobby connect is clean and spacious. There is a snack bar and also several bar areas to purchase beer, wine and even some mixed drinks. There are multiple entrances as well so that you can access the building from either street you are on since the building is so large. There are also several restrooms and the facilities are all clean as well.

In the past year that I've been living in Nashville I've been able to visit twice so far (and bought tickets for a third that unfortunately I couldn't make it to). I went to the 2017 TedX Conference in the Andrew Jackson Hall and the Banff Film Festival hosted by Climb Nashville in the James K. Polk Theater. I would highly recommend going to either of these events if they ever return to the TPAC. The TedX Conference was two days of amazing Ted talks, some even from Nashville locals like Vanderbilt professors, radio talk show host Bobby Bones and celebrity chef Maneet Chauhan. The Andrew Jackson Hall is beautiful and well-kept. The Banff Film Festival originated in Banff, Canada and travels around the U.S. hosting short films that were submitted to the festivals all with the themes of outdoor sports and recreation. 

Even if you aren't so much interested in traditional performing arts like ballet or opera they have so many cool things that would really interest anyone (unless you don't like to leave your house). I look forward to seeing what they have here and I think it's one of the highlights of the Nashville cultural scene.

Came in after Packers/ Titans game,  it is pretty clear that most of the places down here were not prepared for the influx of business.  Out of Miller Lite, what?  Other beers warm.  Server trying her hardest, but the place was packed, tough to keep up.  Food came out fast, how is it that it was barely warm, tasted good, just not hot.  Thinking it would be a better experience if it wasn't so crazy, at the end of the day, we were lucky to find a place to sit down.

Clean, big dance floor. We stopped in for a drink but thought we would grab some appetizers.  We ordered fried pickles and Piggy Mac Grilled Cheese. Pickles were very good and the grilled cheese was amazing! I would have never expected so many flavors on a grilled cheese yet alone mac & cheese, pork shoulder and coleslaw. Highly recommend this sandwich but from what others said, their food was very good too!!!

Seriously, this place was awful!  If you're heading to Grand Ole Opry, save your time & money and go somewhere else.  

We went on a Friday around 11:30-noonish.  It wasn't crowded at all, maybe 3 tables total. 

Friend ordered a spicy bloody and it wasn't good.  
I had a Tito's and diet and pretty sure there was no Tito's.  

Bf ordered a chicken quesadilla and it was something I could have made at home.  It tasted like they just pulled chicken off a Sam's Club rotisserie chicken and plopped it on a cheap tortilla with cheese.  It had no flavor and was a joke to be honest.  I guess the positive there was it was loaded with meat.  We sent it back.  

 I had a burger and it actually wasn't bad at all.  I can't complain about that one.  

Friend had ...can't even remember but that's how forgettable it was.  

Service was okay.  Live music was great!

I highly recommend this restaurant.. be sure and get the appetizer
of the spoon fries, OMG..they are to die for!!!  
Service was excellent, the staff very friendly and courteous. 
Food was very good and plenty of it, southern portions are generous. 
Huge TV's all over, friendly, roomy atmosphere. 

We will be back!!

Fantastic distillery tour lead by Tommy. The tour was about 45 minutes and was filled with fun education about the distilling process. We got to sample vodka, gin, whiskey, and moonshine. Perfect way to take a break from the heat, learn something, and escape the singing groups of bachelorettes. $15 for the tour with the tastings included.

I had been here years ago to see White Christmas but I didn't remember much about the location. I knew I was sitting in the highest section and still saw everything, even though the angle wasn't great. When I heard the sequel to Phantom was in town I needed to go back. 

I saw Phantom in San Fransisco back in the 1990s on my honeymoon. My anniversary was coming up the week before Love Never Dies started in Nashville so it seemed a natural opportunity to go check out TPAC again. 

This time I got tickets in the second level, the Grand Loge. I tried to get Orchestra but they sold out by the time I got my tickets. 

I was really bummed that I couldn't find seat views of each level, so here are my thoughts about the two upper levels: Get center if you can. Everything is going to be small and slightly off presentation. The stage is framed, but if you're way up you can see over the top of the frame and less of the rear of the stage. If you're on the side you also see more backstage on one side and less stage on the other. This may make sense conceptually, but for some scenes this will make a big difference. Grand Loge is much better than the Upper Tier. And the front seats are better than the rear ones. The price difference was about $10-20 a ticket to go from upper, rear, side to Grand Loge, center, front. Definitely worth it if you can't get Orchestra seats. 

The building is nice, if a little too modern for my tastes for Broadway. I love the classical theater look better, but this is serviceable. You can buy drinks and snacks to take in as well. I tried wine and water. Both were overpriced, as was expected, but the wine was pretty good, if generic. There are stairs and an elevator. Bathrooms are available in the basement level and inside, once inside the theater. 

(If this matters, there are several Pokestops within range of the theater. You can reach them while you wait. But not once the show starts, please. ) 

As for the show itself - I was disappointed. [SPOILERS] The Phantom was a bad guy who, in the end, makes one good decision in letting Christine go. He's a tragic character who makes evil, selfish decisions and Christine realizes that by the end. But LND starts with Phantom being the exact same evil, selfish person but Christine falls for him anyway...? And what about the child? That never happened in Phantom. If it did, it happened when he kidnapped Christine and she was under his spell. That makes him even more evil! But the worst thing about LND is that the music is boring. Phantom is iconic. LND is bland. The title song was not memorable, IMO. Reprise for more than a second (if you must make a sequel). That's why we are there, right? Obviously, this is my opinion, but as someone who has seen the film, seen real Broadway cast members, knows most of the words to every song and who watched the movie the night before I was so disappointed. 

Finally, about parking. I did valet because I didn't know the area. I won't do it again. It was $25 plus tip. I waited about 45 minutes for my car after I was standing outside. That's after I handed in my ticket at the line inside. There was parking for $10 across the street in a garage. I'll do that next time. 

TPAC is a nice venue, with a good stage and good prices. Obviously shows are hit or miss, but i's great that they are coming bigger shows recently. I'd definitely recommend it and will be going back.

BARBARA (women's bathroom attendant) is the STAR of this show. sure they have good drinks and fun music, a nice dance floor. but guess what? it wouldn't be ANYTHING without barbara. she is the queen of this shit palace. i will never love another more that i love barbara. queen. she made my time in nashville
worth it. we love her. goodnight

We came to Nashville Palace after a show at the Grand Ole Opry. We were hungry and there was not a lot open in the area. Nashville Palace is a large space next to the Dukes of Hazard Museum and Willie Nelson museum. 
The venue has live music that was pretty good. It has the feel of a dive bar with outdoor seating. My sister got a burger and I got a fried bologna sandwich. The food was pretty good. The service was so so - in our server's defense it was busy and it seemed like she in particular had a lot of tables. 
We did enjoy sitting outside and listening to the music. It seemed like a regular hang out for a lot of locals. I also liked that a lot of couples got up and danced. That was sweet to see. They danced to both slow and fast songs. All in all it was an average experience.

I declare Soulshine as having the best bread pudding in Nashville. This after I have dedicated myself to finding all contenders.

The optional vanilla ice cream is unnecessary since the bread pudding is so wonderful and the vanilla flavor is underwhelming. It is cold, bland, sweet stuff.

From the minute we arrived in Nashville, the Wildhorse Saloon was all we heard about so off we went. We went on a Sunday night and it appeared that they were not fully staffed. The first thing we noticed was that the menu was VERY hard to understand. We are pretty savy but could not figure it out. When the waitress finally showed up at our table 15 minutes after we were seated, we told her it didn't make any sense to us and that we would suggest a more understandable design. Her reply was "I didn't design it and I don't care." Kind of shocked at that reply. We watched as she had to explain this hard to understand menu to others too. The food was ok, not great. The live entertainment was good.

This pains me because of the wonderful pictures of Duane Allman and Warren Haynes they have displayed on their walls,  but this was some of the worst service I have had in a long long time. 
Me and my family were the only ones on the bottom floor. We sit there almost 20 minutes before anyone came to take our order. All the time we were looking back towards the kitchen area seeing about five employees huddled and talking. 
I kept telling my wife we ought to leave but we kept on waiting.  Then finally a wait person comes to take our order for drinks and we had to holler for her to stop as she was leaving so we could give her the rest of our order. I shudder to think  how long it would of been if we had let her go. 
Now I'm not saying the waitress has to smile (which she did not) or even be friendly (which she was not) but  at least don't look like we have pulled you away from something important.  
Sadly to say I can't go back as it would be enabling this shoddy service. 
On the good side, they did play excellent music to go with the excellent pics on the wall. 
Also the guy that greeted us ( manager probably)  was very nice and the food was pretty good. 
So I guess the server and company are probably much more congenial when it's later, and the drinks are flowing, and they are around people that  they can personally relate to better then just a couple  over 40 with a child....I understand... but I also understand that is the difference in 5 stars and two. If you talk the talk, you have to walk the walk.

Like most of the bars here, there are two floors of fun here. I was happy that both floors had their all of their windows open, because it was pretty crowded (but still fun nonetheless).

What I liked about this bar was that it was pretty big and the music was good as well. I came to Nashville hoping to hear a lot of country music, but they were playing a lot of 90s rock that Labor Day weekend (Blink 182, Lit, Third Eye Blind, etc) which was still fun. Everyone was singing along and everyone was having a good time.

Drinks were easy to get, at the bar, and their little stations for beer (which I think is sooo convenient). Overall, this was a fun spot to check out while going around Broadway.

Nice atmosphere but the service, food and entertainment totally sucked. 

Took a while to get seated on a slow Wednesday night. Finally got a table and ordered drinks and it took 10+ minutes to get 4 beers. Menu is limited.  Pickles are decent, pimento cheese was fair. Brisket, Sausage & sides were garbage . (2 out of 10)

Entertainment (Tyler Jordan) sucked! I'm not a fan of today's country but appreciate good lyrics and solid guitar play...this cat has neither.

We had the whole place reserved for a private event and I was impressed. It's much larger inside then it looks, they must fit a shit ton of people in here on a weekend. The stage is large and they're AV system is top notch, you can tell they put on a good show. We watched Burning Las Vegas and the music and sound was great.  There must be 8 bars in the whole place, everywhere you turn on any of the 3 floors there is a place to grab a drink. I don't know about a typical night but for our event the service was great and the bar tenders and bouncers were professional. 

We had a BBQ buffet with Brisket and pulled pork. They had the wet and dry brisket separated and it was perfect. The pork was fantastic too especially with all the spicy sauces available. Salad, beans, biscuits and cobbler were good. Perfect accompaniments to the meat. 

If for sure eat here if I was looking for dinner, not sure on price and quantity for a menu item but for our event everything was great!

My love of country music brought me to Nashville! My excellent service at this bar will keep me coming back to Broadway! Courtney was not only knowledgeable on what was fun to do for my group, but went above and beyond! The drinks were superb ( I am not a huge frozen fan) but that lime drink was something I needed at least 3 of! Thanks Courtney for an excellent time!
Probably one of the coolest most authentic places in Nashville. The crowd is a mix of older and younger people making it a great place for any age.

Always a great show and I've been to dozens. Comfortable, roomy seats. Though it's unconventional where I come from (Los Angeles), it's nice to be able to bring in food and drink from the lobby providers. I am grateful for the quality productions I get to see at TPAC.

Pizza OK for the price, seemed salty and one visit crust was burnt, next visit not cooked enough. Also had the grilled chicken salad, OK. Decent size. Don't go out too often for lunch and not sure why we come here. The food is OK. Had wine but have not seen any entertainment. Like I said, we come for lunch mostly. What is probably the best is the cheesy bread. Add pepperoni and it is better than the pizza. Go figure.  Parking is sparse at best. Servers are friendly and the atmosphere is fun. Wish there was better food for the payoff of trying to get out to lunch. Wish the Pizza was better too. Try the cheesy bread and salad.

We waited for over 45 min, and there was an open table nearby for the entire extent of our wait. I asked the waitress if it was alright if we sat there (considering we had been on the waitlist and weren't trying to circumvent the process), and she told us we could "walk our ass upstairs". Very rude.

The saloon is 3 stories high. There were a few people on the dance floor learning to dance. The food was average. I had a double cheeseburger nothing to write home about.
The decor was Western and interesting. Nashville Tennessee.

Yeah this is a hard 1 star. I do NOT RECOMMEND this business to family and friends.

It's pretty easy to sum up my experience. Loud, dirty, bad service and even worse food.

Out of all the places I visited in Nashville this was hands down the worst. The food is bland and they try to compensate by giving you a lot of it. After the first couple bites I threw in the towel. My friend also said his was horrible as well.
I went with the brisket while he went with the pulled pork. Very disappointing and my recommendation would be to avoid Rippys if at all possible. A lot of hype with it being on the main road but they couldn't deliver anything but disappointment. Poor showing Rippys.
This was a fun place to learn how to country line dance. Very roomy on the inside. The live band was really good! Had a fun evening with a large group of people!

They have a schedule for "line dance lessons" so while we were there we learned a dance at 5:00 and another dance at 6:09. We also got in some foozeball and pool on the third floor, which overlooks the lower two floors and has upside down horses hanging from its ceilings. Paid a dollar or two extra to get our drinks in glass boots which we are keeping as our Nashville souvenirs.

Came before the last Preds game with a few friends. Luckily I saw where you could make reservations when I was looking up the menu because they were telling people it was an hour wait at 5:30. The restaurant was pretty empty and even over the course of our hour there it didn't get much busier other than a couple of large groups. Two of us arrived before the other two and we noticed our server was kind of slow at bringing us our drinks, but we thought she was just waiting for the rest of our party. 
We ordered fried pickles as our app and while they tasted good the breading just fell off because of the thin slices. We also had hot chicken and turkey plate. The hot chicken had a great honey flavor and the right amount of spice. The turkey had great flavor but not much more can be said about it. We waited forever for our second round of drinks and when they didn't all come out together we had to cancel the others in order to make it to the game in time. We didn't hate our visit but have no intentions of returning.

Good pizza place, nice outdoor area and bar. Clean (which is always important). They're big enough and in the right location to be open late night but they close at 10 or 11PM. I don't have a lot to say about it, but it's good.

Paid $25 and waited about an hour to get a cold rack of ribs. Took them another half hour to get the food out to us hot. They were busy and I get that. But there is no excuse to see my waiter twice during the meal. Didn't get us refilled drinks or anything. Complete disgrace of an establishment and will never return.
Worst service ever. Our food was awful and and out server Nikki was the worst. My first trip to Nashville and no southern hospitality here that's for sure

Ah Soulshine. I come here randomly and always have a good time, but never suggest it myself. Not sure why, it should maybe be on my radar a bit more.

Downstairs at Soulshine are tables and more of a restaurant feel. I have never once sat in this area so I am not sure what happens down there. I always go directly upstairs where there are more tables, a bar, and then a rooftop deck with a stage. There may be live bands playing when you are there and it makes it pretty festive. Otherwise it is still a nice patio to sit on as it is also covered.

Pizza is the menu...and it is just ok. I am not really a girl that likes going out to eat pizza, but most of the pieces I have tried have been good enough to soak up the beer. They have friendly waitstaff and bartenders pour a pretty strong drink.

Overall, it is a solid choice for happy hour or maybe to see a live band...or anytime you want to have drinks on a patio!

Not a fan of this place (I do have one exception here). First of all their security guard is one rude dude. I get it, some bars are now doing metal detector full body scans but you can consciously choose if you want to be a douchebag or not. Guy is straight faced and pretty intense doing up down, sides, making me turn around, spread my legs/arms, etc. It was like the airport to literally run in to gather friends to leave at the end. We did eat, got catfish strips which my boyfriend loved my FAVORITE and one thing they are doing right are their crispy thick amazing onion rings. Our served was terrible, she had short black curly hair but was not attentive, after we ordered we really didn't see her again and I'm big on servers coming back to ask if its good, right, etc. Initially we ordered a round of drinks, my boyfriend spilled his about 4 seconds after getting it, not only did no one get us extra towels but when we asked for a new drink we were charged again. So now here we are and we've spent $20 on one small plastic cup whiskey and coke. Also i snagged her to ask to add a corndog to the order and she confirmed, great, but alas it never came. It wasn't even that busy, there was a garth brooks concert that night getting started so the place had really emptied out. would NOT return.

Wow was it load. Did I mention is was loud. Great bartender, never had food but looked and smelled good. Sorry I can't hear you it's too loud. I guess when I was younger that would be a great place, but when you can't talk to someone than I guess it is too loud

It's been about 15 years since I've darkened the doors of the Nashville Palace. Back then the Palace was located up the street, on the corner of McGavock & Music Valley Drive. That was the location where Randy Travis was discovered as a very talented singer while he was employed washing dishes. I'm not sure if the tradition still exists, but back in the day, The Nashville Palace was a dinner theater that catered to tourists and to locals with family and friends in town, it was a magical place, affectionately known to the local folks as "The Palace" during the musical show they would call up employees from the restaurant to perform onstage. It would go something like this, Ladies & Gentleman please help me welcome Betty to the stage, that's right folks, Betty your waitress over there in section 3, come on up here Betty. The crowd ate it up!

My great memories include sitting at the bar listening to Minnesota Fats holding court with fantastic stories of his escapades throughout the world.  There were always friendly celebrities and musical giants in the bar area.

Anyway, today Johnny Mac is here, he's a great entertainer singing and accompanying himself on guitar. Thank You Johnny Mac for the enjoyment and entertainment.

Atmosphere / decor - 3
Service - 3
Food - NA
Location - 4
Value - 3

Overall 3.5

I had the brisket sandwich here which was pretty tasty. Drinks were the same price as the places around it.

We're so glad that we came here for lunch during our stay. Fun atmosphere, lively staff, yummy bbq and refreshing drinks. While we were eating there, they had some underground singers performing on stage and we saw some people dancing on the dance floor.
For appetizers. we ordered the fried pickles in mild spicy. It topped with some green scallions and it served with some creamy dressing on the side. 
For entrees, we shared the pick any 2 meats combo and it came with 2 sides. We chose the  briskets and chicken thighs. Marinated tomatoes and fried brussel sprouts for the sides. We were stuffed after we finished our entrees.
For drinks, I ordered a cocktail that served in a cowboy boot and my friend ordered a beer.
Our server was bubbly and friendly. In the end we learned that they called the check/bill a ticket lol
We also like how they they placed their menu on a wooden board...it matched the restaurant's theme. This is definitely a great place for tourists and big groups.

Stopped by here hoping to get drinks and listen to live music before the Brad Paisley concert on 2/22/14. 

I have never been treated so poorly by a server in my life. This is an open seating restaurant. I sat down as soon as a table became available. The male server with shoulder length brown hair asked if I would order food and drinks. Told him yes and my friends went to the restroom. Server left as I was waving down my friends. Server comes back and says "YOU CAN'T HOLD THIS TABLE" as my friends were walking to the table. Then he had the nerve to say to me because one of my friends obviously ordered A BEER from the bar already we could not order food or drinks at the table. An older couple proceeded to sit at the table while I was still sitting there! I don't usually complain about places but this was RUDE! I left immediately. I have no desire to continue being a patron of place that obviously did not want my business. 

I WILL NEVER STEP FOOT INTO THIS PLACE AGAIN AND I WOULD SUGGEST TO EVERYONE ELSE, THERE ARE BETTER VENUES ON BROADWAY. I WISH I COULD GIVE THIS PLACE NO STARS

A LEGENDARY spot that at one point I'm told had the best ribs in town. No more ribs and just simple bar food. I ordered a chicken sandwich that never came out so I went with fried balogna sandwich and an RC ( yes they have TV cola) great live house band and still the huge live room. Randy Travis once worked and performed here! A true landmark, you can eat food , drink and enjoy a great staff.

Everybody we met was friendly, great service staff.  Come here for the ambiance, the atmosphere and the music.  Noisy, crowded, wall-to-wall people populated Honky Tonk.  Come here to just say you've been.  A must stop for Nashville

Amazing space honoring the history of the building, worth going based on that alone; but then there is the food. We had six people and everyone got different entrees but everyone loved their meals. The filet was unbelievable with delicious sides and the fried chicken and the short ribs were our groups favorite. Can't wait to go back and I'm excited to check out lunch and breakfast too.

Great place.  No cover charge, cheap beer, TV, and live music!  Decor lives up to the name but an awesome place.  Did not eat here but the menu looks good and apparently they have great burgers.  Will try the food next time.

Maybe I ordered...unwisely.  The RB #2 was dry & too chewy.  I think #2 means "second day"; sent it back.  The chicken tenders were VERY greasy & WAY dry on the inside.  Kielbasa sandwich...just ok.   Not enough Kielbasa!  $40 for lunch inc tip, no alcohol.  Great service but the food is the worst bar food I've had in years.  I loathe wasting money...and wasting lunch.
Don't go for the bottomless $15 mimosas, it's straight Tropicana and no champagne. The food and atmosphere however was AMAZING!
Most fun on a Wednesday afternoon I've ever had! Service is great, the live music is incredible and the vibe of the place is very welcoming.

I am visiting from Philadelphia and attended the Preds Flyers game. I've heard about Paradise Park from many friends and wanted to check it out. Walking down the street with my friend, who is from Nashville, the door man starts immediately eyeing me up ( I have my flyers shirt on). We were laughing and having a great time. As we approached the doorman, he points to me and shakes his head and states that I've had too much. Confused since I've only had two beers the whole evening, I tell him that  and ask what the problem is since I'm visibly not intoxicated at all. This is when he calls me a lightweight... I'm sorry, what?! You're a tourist bar on a tourist street and you're not going to let me in because I'm wearing a Flyers shirt and then say I'm intoxicated?? All while my friend who is born and raised here is wearing a Preds shirt and just as shocked as me.

Hold on to your hats!!!! I read a lot of bad reviews about this place but I guarantee this will be a new one for ya! My dear old granny and I stopped into this place because it was recommended by the Frommer's Nashville travel book. Was greeted in the front by comical grandma-esque lady with 1 inch fake red nails and pointed out the sides on the menu. She was a hoot and a half when we first met her. We ordered a cheeseburger and tater tots to share. Food was decent, but it's morally wrong for them to call that the best burger in Nashville. While we were eating we saw a man and two women come in with a little white poodle. They allowed the dog to stand on the table before they got situated at their seats!!! When we were leaving the restaurant my dear old granny asked old lady in the front if it was customary to allow dogs in the joint. The lie just rolled off her tongue. She said the man was legally blind and it was a service dog. Well, that man had got up three times without the dog with him. Then, when he went outside the restaurant, we walked all over without the dog. The two women he was with were handling the dog!
 One plus, bathroom pretty clean. That's all I have to say.

Stopped in here for a little exposure to some live music and an ice cold beverage on a cool day in Nashville day. Like most bars on Broadway - you have your selection of different levels. I believe this Lounge has three different floors, however, I only explored the first two.

I would compare this as more tourist-directed than other bars on Broadway. Prices were a little steep for my taste - no one should pay $6 for Budweiser... don't get me wrong, I'm from Tampa and I promise you, although it's a delicious beer - it's just not worth that price tag! 

I ventured into this bar early in the afternoon and as can be expected, they don't usually have their top performing house bands in around 2PM.
