Both bands on the first and second floor were great, exactly what you can expect for that time of day - a little pitchy but they get the job done on setting the atmosphere.

Wait staff was friendly and courteous. Crowd had a fairly decent age range and demographic range. Overall, great place but I think you can do better if you want to avoid tourist traps. I'll go back for sure - the memorabilia and photos on the wall are worth it! Bring a Sharpie!! You can add your name to the walls!

We had a lovely time here.  You have to queue up electronically to get tickets for a table and we were successful.  this let us walk right in.  It was a great evening of music, good food and drinks.  It really gave us a feel for Nashville.

We stop by Tootsie's because it's famous so we had to. It was very packed. We were were around noon on Sunday (before CMA's) so Nashville was packed to begin with. We loved the rooftop patio despite not being able to get a table for about 20 minutes.
Great bar, great staff and good music. Can get really busy and kind of touristy. Front and back bars, saw hank Williams JR on front stage, great show.

I love me a good honky-tonking night, but it seems we're more likely to get down to Broadway when we have out-of-towners in tow. Fortunately, we had that excuse this weekend, which reminded me to write this past-due review.

PPTR earns props for always having a fun band (not just country either-they busted out a late 90s medley this weekend that made me want to dig out some Abercrombie and Fitch), great bartenders, and probably most importantly, SPACE. The back of the bar has long tables that can seat eightish, and the generous standing room let's you relax. No coming down with a case of claustrophobia that makes you two-step your ass right out the door here!

 I'll leave you with one final tip: Thin Mint Shots. This is not your mamma's Girl Scout, and you can thank me later. With a Thin Mint Shot.

When chatting about the Bluebird with people before and after my visit I got one of three responses: 1)   2) You are incredibly lucky to get tickets for anything here or 3) It's stupid that the venue is so small and that tickets are hard to get - doesn't seem worth it.

It is the MOST AMAZING place I've ever been to see live music.  

We were incredibly lucky to get tickets and didn't actually realize this completely until we got to Nashville. Tickets went on sale Monday at 9am before the Friday show we were trying for.  Both my husband and I were on our computers ready to purchase.  He got stuck in the queuing system they use but I got in and was able to snag tickets for us for the later show.  We felt super lucky about this after speaking to Uber drivers, hotel staff, and locals we met at bars over the weekend who all explained how hard the tickets are to get and many tourists don't actually get to go see a show.  

If you are going to Nashville definitely make the effort to try to get tickets.  If you don't...cry. 

I would have gone here each of our three nights.  The venue is in a strip mall and a short drive from downtown, but don't let that turn you away! The Bluebird has such charm (especially if yo you know anything about it's history and the people that have played here) - its cozy and very intimate.  There isn't a bad seat in the house as all the tables surround the musicians.  We saw five singer/song writers (including Emily Reid and the Stellas - both amazing) play in the round for about 2.5 hours.  Incredible night.  

Go to the Bluebird!!

Their brunch is so good! They were very flexible with my friends and I as far as our allergy restrictions went, and you can't beat the bottomless mimosas. The live music was awesome! The wait was not terrible either since I had a group of 12 on a Sunday at prime brunch time, and none of us cared since we had access to the bar while we waited! Haha. Highly recommend this place and I'll be back!

Just an FYI they just opened a third floor that has roof access, very excited about this!! Yes, it's new and  doesn't quite have that old feel to it, but more space to fit more people and hear MORE great Nashville music. I was a big fan of the new third floor. It was a total blast!

You can always go to the second and first floor to get that original Nashville Tootsie feel. There is always someone great playing (because it's a landmark). It's noisy, it's crowded, you may have a beer spilt on you but come on would you have the honkey tonks any other way? :) Plus you'll be too busy doing fireball shots and singing along to even notice. Always a must stop for my nights out on Broadway and especially if I have out of town guest in!
Beer is expensive, but the music is phenomenal! Artists bring around a tip jar, and you can request songs for them to sing/play. Very fun atmosphere!

I was pleasantly surprised at how good the coffee was at The Well. And reasonable. A 12oz pour over is only $2. 

There were 6 roasts to choose from (they source their coffee from Murfreesboro roaster Just Love Coffee Roasters). I opted for a Guatemalan pour over - nutty and toffee-ish. The execution was among the highest I've experienced in Nashville. 

I tried a slice of zucchini nut bread along with my coffee, made by Cozy Cottage Bakery in Woodbury, TN. It was moist and tasty without too much sweetness. 

I was only in and out, but for a caffeine fix to weather (or enhance) the Green Hills craziness, The Well is the best option I've found, by far.
Great service,  excellent guacamole!  Very casual laid back atmosphere.   Live music and pretty good food.
I enjoyed my time at Tootsie's. There are several different levels with really great bands. One of the best aspects of this bar was the awesome roof deck. Don't miss out!

This place is a sold out joke. Markets itself as a local bar but when you take a $30 uber there from downtown they tell you they are only open for 2 shows a night of random groups and won't let you in. I stood outside for 15 minutes waiting for an uber out of there and the music I heard through the glass was garbage anyway. Most groups on broadway blow them away. Don't waste you time on a commercial sellout due to a bad show that was sent off of big networks and landed on CMT. What a joke. Waste of a trip.

We went on a Sunday, but the vibe was definitely catered to an older crowd. The fries were good and the drinks were cold but my sandwich was burnt (not grilled). Service was quick though, but not as friendly as you're used to down here.

Went to this place which was super crowded.  Had to push my way through to get in. Now I'm 5 feet tall 130 pds. The bouncer who is 6.5 kicked me out because I must have wiggled my way through and bumped him. He grabbed my arm and took handcuffs out.  Really??  It was the most ridiculous thing ever. He put his hands on me who did nothing other than do what everyone else was doing to get through the crowd.  I would say his behavior was inappropriate.  Sooooo mad.  This was a terrible way to treat guests.
Great place to visit while you are in Nashville.  Great live music and sandwiches.   Bartender could be more service oriented however.

Love this place. Love the atmosphere.
Love that the location is totally random. (Keeps some of the riff raff out.)
The food is great. (Try the bbq nachos for dinner. Chicken & waffles for brunch.)
Drinks are delicious. (Try Babs on a Budget.)
Can't wait to sit outside when it's warm enough.

My one complaint..
THE FOOD PORTIONS ARE SO SMALL.
And I have a small stomach so that's saying alot.

Haven't been for a show yet.

At least they had root beer.   

Everything seemed promising, friendly staff, a good schtick, and a raging cover band next door (connected). But, the burgers were bland, the fries floppy, and the jalapeño cheese fritters lacked....jalapeño.  

Don't get me wrong, ingredients were fresh, and the food came out fast.... But it never reached its potential. ... At least they had root beer.
Wow what a place. Three bands on three different floors. Cold beer and great music. Roam the same place as as Jonny Cash ,George Jones, Hank, and any one else you can think of.

My family wanted to go to Tootsies but the doorman bent my 24 year daughter's state license and then grabbed her arm after changing his mind about admitting her to the club. She'll be 25 January 30th. Devante, the doorman was very rude and noted that SC IDs are very often fake. It isn't fake.  We asked for a manager and he was rude as well. We went to Tin Roof instead. Very nice staff and fantastic music at Tin Roof.  Too bad Tootsies can't be as cordial. It would have been nice to have an apology from them and a commitment to purchase a replacement ID for my daughter.

I waited until I had brunch here twice because I really hate giving The Stone Fox a low rating because it's a great neighborhood bar and it has such a lovely atmosphere and the waitstaff is pretty top notch, however, their brunch is pretty so-so. During my first visit, I ordered their chicken and waffles. The waffle was pretty much like an over-sized eggo--bland. Their chicken was pretty flavorful but overcooked. During my second visit I had their BLT with avocado. I also found this bland. A friend ordered their granola and yogurt and there was barely any yogurt. I would go back for brunch, if it isn't my choice and I'm not paying.
We loved Tootsie's! Fantastic music and friendly staff. Decent beer selection. Would come back again for sure.
Had a great time!  The staff was lacking in kindness. But there was a great band upstairs and the rooftop bar was fun.

A great venue to hear music the way it was meant to be.  We went on a Monday, which is first come first served. It's small, so arrive early and expect it to be cramped. An experience not to be missed while in Nashville!

Great live band tonight, and I don't even listen to country music!  Like most bars that I've been to tonight, this one had about 3 levels to it, and a different band playing on each one.  Great atmosphere good crowd.  Came here on a Monday night and it was a happening spot.  On the weekends it's toe to toe I've heard.  

The best band was on the floor level.  Lots of old school pictures on the wall, casual atmosphere, older crowd - like 30-50 year olds who just love their country music.

You gotta come here to get a taste of what Nashville bars are all about.

Jazzy Brunch all the way!!!! 

Not my favorite night time spot but loved Saturday brunch. Simple breakfast dishes at a very reasonable price. Great entertainment.

It would have been better stars but when a bar pays .40 a bud light and they charge $6.00 is a bit much. 
Bands were off key but hey everyone was having a good time. 
All in all its a nice place. A bit too crowded but nice.
Probably one of the best hamburgers I have ever eaten in a restaurant. If they toasted the bun it would be perfection. The fries were delicious also. I enjoy the atmosphere also.

Not to be confused with Footsie's, which is what I played with your girlfriend last night when we were all on a double dinner date.

One of many wonderful places to meet gorgeous people and tourists on Lower Broadway in Nashville. On such a small stretch of road there are so many different things to do and places to hang out and listen to music and get drunk. This is just one of them. It's not my absolute favorite but it's enjoyable and busy and usually very welcoming.

This bar is far from a "lounge" this is a hopin' hustlin' 4 level rodeo bar with fantastic live music on every floor. The top floor had the best music all day long- it's a staple to go visit if you come to Nashville! The beer is cold and people are tourists but very friendly and fun! 

Also the roof top looks over the entire strip which is totally awesome! Grab your cowboy boots and friends and ride on in to this fun place!

Good time for a Thursday! Came in after a bus ride into the city. Mi Madre found this place looking up late night eats in the area. The band was JAMMING! The prices gave Chicago a run for the money. $3.50 for a PBR & too damn much for a Miller Lite.

The patty melt was good, but the fries were definitely freaky-fried

Also, never seen a bathroom attendant in a dive bar before.

This is my personal favorite spot on the downtown strip! What a cool atmosphere whether you are up top on the rooftop getting to see all the lights of downtown while listening to live music or downstairs sitting up and close to the bands playing. Last nights band was awesome and we had a great time. Next time I come back to Nashville I will definitely make a trip to tootsies.

I bought our tickets to see Sigur Ros when they went on sale ages ago and from then up until the day before the show I thought the Woods was in Franklin and it would take us 2 hours to get down there with Friday evening traffic. Another friend thought it was in Mboro, another friend thought Bellevue - which leads me to believe that The Woods is actually Camelot lost in the mists of fairy land! I figured out that it's actually north and only 9 minutes from our front door.

Although I had no idea where the place was, I had done a little bit of research ahead of time concerning the parking situation and I'm so glad we arrived early and parked near the exit. We had friends who said it was complete and total chaos leaving. It took one couple upwards of 45 minutes to leave after the show. The problem is  road rage meeting the lack of parking attendants to guide traffic out. My friends said people were lifting ropes for cars to go under, honking and screaming at each other. Also VIP show goers are totally screwed because they park you up by the stage across the creek which is great when you arrive but then when the show is over the bridge that leads out is being used by pedestrians so you have to wait to leave. INSANITY.

The place itself is okay. I've heard varying things about different shows. If they set up chairs on the lawn and you happen to sit at the front right you can't see the stage. Also you are elbow to elbow with the chair next to you. If it's lawn seating you can bring a blanket or lawn chair but it's useless because most people end up standing up anyway. Strangers came and sat in our laps twice! No joke, sat on our blanket right in front of us. Seriously we almost had more than a verbal altercation go down at one point. The portable potties are horrific and the food/drink options by the stage are pretty narsty. We had an okay view of the stage but I wish we were actually closer to the middle and back for sound purposes. Some folks had even brought in hammocks to put between the trees along stage right. 

Having said that, seeing Sigur Ros at night, outside and during perfect fall weather couldn't have been more amazing. And so I would recommend seeing a show here if it's the right band, if you've eaten before you've arrived just plan to get there early and park in a good place.

I really liked this place as an out-of-towner visiting Nashville's strip. It was laid back with a good band. There were skee ball and basketball to play with friends, ample space to weave in and out of people, unusual decor (trailer park theme) and the people seemed to low-key.

Not only does the place a great music and food, it is a really cool atmosphere. A must stop. I had the potroast with mashed potatoes. Awesome. My wife had corn cakes, eggs and jalepeno bacon. So good. My son and I sampled the hot sauces. Eachwas unique and very good. Service was top notch.

Love the atmosphere at Woolworths and the music downstairs.  Our salads both came out wrong, were not that great and salad dressing bland. Waitress offered to take them back but we didn't want to wait so we pressed on. Valet Parking fees are wrong on website and is double than stated and when we asked both Valet and Young Man at desk said rates had been changed for 2 months and acted like we should somewhat magically know this.  Probably will come back for music but not food. Disappointing but not horrible.

Tried going to Tootsie's as our first Nashville bar experience. I had a small book bag with me, carrying my camera. My ID was checked, and then told I couldn't bring in the book bag - decided since there were 7 people who wanted to go in, I'd throw away my book bag and put the camera around my neck. Got back in line, bouncer checked my ID again only to tell me cameras weren't allowed. Bouncer totally dampened our first Nashville experience

Found out about this place through a co-worker. Said they had good food and a nice atmosphere. I checked it out with my fiance' this Memorial Day since we were off. We went around brunch so it was pretty much empty. Waited probably 15-20 minutes before a waiter approached us so that sucked. Finally ordered and the food was good. I had the smoked brisket tacos which are filled with flavor and heat. My fiance had the BIG Ole BLT that was loaded with bacon. We both enjoyed the food but service was really lacking.

Paradise Park lives up to its name when it's 2:30 A.M., you're hammered, and need something good and greasy to soak it up.

This trailer park themed bar and grill has a lot of charm, happy vibes, beer, booze, and greasy food. I stumbled in and immediately wanted to take on "Big Al's Challenge" which consists of eating a "Big Al Burger" featuring five beef patties and five slabs of cheese with a side of chili cheese fries or tots. 'Merica! F*ck yeah!

I'm about 6' and 190 pounds of pure salt, sugar, and general apathy. As I was about to order I turned to the side and noticed a man in overalls waiting for his order. This man was shorter than me, but easily was pushing 380 to 400 pounds. He was truly twice my size. And then it hit me. Ding! Ding! Ding!

(Drunken) Archie: Are you Big Al?

(Very) Large Man: Yes. That's me.

(Drunken) Archie: They named a challenge after you. That's so cool!

Big Al: Did it once. Never again, kid.

(Drunken) Archie: I am going to try it. And I am going to add bacon.

Big Al: C'mon, kid. Have fun in Nashville. Don't hurt yourself.

The way he looked at me with concern you'd think I was attempting to ride a tricycle off a cliff or something. But it made me change my order to a simple bacon cheeseburger with a side of chili cheese tots. Hit the spot. And I couldn't finish. I tapped out with a few bites to go. The "Big Al's Challenge" would have destroyed me.

Thank you to Paradise Park for (almost) sobering me up. And an extra special thank you to Big Al for saving me from potential internal injuries, obesity, diabetes, and heart disease. 'Merica! F*ck yeah!

Tom Morales restaurants always do well in Nashville. I think they are the most popular ones. I always like the atmospheres, and generally like the food. The same can be said here. I love what they've done trying to preserve the historicalness of the site with photos from sit-ins and reconstruction of the old diner feel. Good food too. But nothing unique enough to grab a fifth star.

I would go back. This will be a good place to bring Nashville visitors for lunch, or brunch. A space where children are welcome, but you can also grab a decent cocktail.
Great place to go to if you want a live band certain nights. Food is good. The setting is great as they have a upstairs and downstairs bar. Check the downstairs out.

In town for work we stopped in and got an amazing show, good drinks and an amazing crowd! Well worth the trip! It was so packed we couldn't get past the first 6 feet of the bar, but that meant we were right by the stage the whole time. It was super fun and I wish I could have had more time to explore all the pictures on the wall and the rest of the bar. It looked awesome.

One of the many great watering holes on Broadway.  Like the others on the block, it has multiple floors, multiple live bands, and a typical bar menu for the area.  What makes it special?  Not sure really, but I definitely enjoyed it.

We went straight up to the deck on the rooftop and it was a good mix of grudgy while still being acceptable.  Bartenders were efficient and friendly.  The band playing was very good but were clearly desperate for tips; I bought a song for my girlfriend and both she and they were overjoyed.  Beer selection was decent (a few local beers like most places in Nashville) and reasonably priced.  Photo booth on the top floor was a nice touch but it would be better if they told you when the damned pictures began.

Good place, will be back to explore more of it.

By far my favorite spot on Broadway. The interior is set to look like a trailer park, setting the stage for a divey end-of-the night beer (or three), with a side of fireball and (of course) live country music. 

Stand on the elevated stage across from the performance stage at  2 am and watch dramatic fights break out between drunk southern bells. 

Laugh as you try to lift your feet from the sticky floors and reminisce about your favorite frat parties from back in the day.

Buy a corn dog from the food window, or walk next door to the restaurant for some sit-down service. 

Play Big Buck. Play Pac Man. 

Buy a personal pitcher of beer for less than a New York City pint and relish in all that is Nashville.
Fun bar for live music. 3 levels and 3 different stages with different music. A little bit for all tastes.

Very weird themed bar. Artificial grass on the ground. It was our last stop for the night, it was basically empty besides a few others that wandered in & out. The band played for a virtually empty place. They took requests which the two older ladies sitting next to me took advantage of. There was a checkered-floored hallway that led off the another section of the bar, I'm assuming the kitchen or somewhere to order food, decided not to take a stroll down it. 
Positive- They do have a good selection of draft beers.

Tin roof has very consistent quality and very good food. The salads are very well cared for, not just a bunch of iceberg thrown on a plate. The quesadilla's are amazing. Good bar, too. I very much appreciate the consistency of the food.

We went to see the show on Wednesday December 27th .We waited outside starting at 3 o'clock for the 5 o'clock show ,the temperature was about 30°, and we still BARELY made the cutoff for the 12 seats they have available that aren't reserved.The show was GREAT we had to order from the bar, I ordered the catfish and chips which was pretty damn awesome . The atmosphere was that of a very small bar with good service and the show was absolutely FANTASTIC ! 
We heard : Neal Carpenter, Dylan Altman , Kate Bowen and Austin jenkes .
I must say Dylan Altman was AMAZING !! 
I recommend going at LEAST 2 hours prior to make sure you get a seat . After all we were there at 3:00 and we were number 8 and 9 of 12.

When in Nashville...I had to check out the Bluebird Cafe.   Went to the early show on a weekday.  Good thing, as I was a few minutes late.  Only several pew seats were still available.  No cover, but a $10 minimum for drinks/food.  Show had 4 singers in a round robin format.  The unplugged format is great!  Less than 40 feet at most from the stage, listening to music this way is so intimate & powerful!  The audience was very supportive and  respectful of the musicians.  Nary a sidebar conversation or cell phones during the performance.  Highly recommend, and I can't wait to go back!  Might need to try a 9 pm show w/cover next time!  The highlight of my Ft Campbell/Nashville trip!

Great local location.  Hamburgers are great and the tator tots are the best.  Very filling before a night out and a night at the Predator game.  The music is pretty loud, so discussions are difficult, but well worth the visit.  Very reasonably priced.  Perfect casual burger joint.

Wonderful little restaurant/bar/music venue.

When my friends in Nashville asked where our group was going and I mentioned The Stone Fox they all remarked on how isn't that the place on the West side?  Which is true.  The Stone Fox might be something that you would expect to see over near The Pharmacy but rather is on the other side of town near...nothing.  It's in a residential area.  In fact, The Stone Fox is made from an old house.

The beauty of this is the benefit of the porches.  In addition, the inside has a very homey feel to it, like the front room that has small lighting and large antique maps covering the walls.  The food is a delight, with their late night menu serving healthy apps like the kale and onion hummus pizza (gluten free).  

I would go so far as to say that this place is a hidden gem.  Because it is still newer and in a non-commercialized part of town not very many people have heard about it or been to it yet, meaning you can slip into it on a late evening and catch a really amazing live show on their inside small stage and eat really tasty, healthy food or just shoot the shit on the porch area with friends (back porch is bigger).  The night we went there was a really great 2 piece band from Mississippi playing.

It was a cold, cold night during the Songwriter's Festival and I had the pleasure of claiming a barstool at the bar, the night Tom T. Hall performed.
The room was completely filled, not a seat to be had.
Dixie, Tom's wife sat at the table, in front of me.
He performed, he told stories, he interacted with the audience for 2 hours.
It was magical.
After his show, the place emptied out and I sat at the bar, just taking it all in.
The aesthetics, the ambiance, the sound...  I was sitting in a pretty famous place...

And then something magical happened.
Mr. Hall came over to me, took both my hands, looked into my eyes and thanked me for coming out in such awful weather.
Dixie, his wife turned around to see who he was talking to, and she flashed me a great big southern smile and thanked me, as well....
I thanked him for coming out in the awful weather, as well....
And then we all walked out together, him holding his wife's hand.
We said goodbye and then I drove off and never felt so amazing, like I did that evening.....

This is truly a fun, magical, historical place to go to at least once, while you're visiting Nashville. You never know who will be in the audience, with you.

Came in one afternoon for a quick bite- sat in the mezzanine and had the best sandwich. Squash fritter poboy that I wish i could eat almost everyday. 
Boone was a great bartender. Attentive but not too much in your face. 
Keep it up

I had the Polska here, was really good topped with sautéed onions and peppers an mustard. The portion size was pretty big which I liked the kielbasa was longer than the roll which was nice I prefer that ratio opposed to shorter. It came with fries which were ok just fries. 

The service was good did not have to wait to be helped and the food came out fast. Of course there was live music for lunch which was great.

I also came back at night and realized they have a stage on the second floor as well and both stages were playing live music. I got a apple pie shine shot it was really good but I don't know how much was actually alcohol haha that was $7. Te bar tenders were super attentive and always made sure all the customers were helped. 

The night music was fun the band was large and some members were on the stage while one or two would be on the bar counter, it was a fun environment and every night they were packed!

We had a reservation but the place was almost empty. Our server did not deliver very good service. When we asked what was good on the menu, she paused and pointed out the most expensive item on the menu. She was unhelpful and unfriendly throughout the dinner. She also completely forgot our complimentary bread. We got the corn hush puppy type appetizers and they were bland and flavorless. The roasted poblano dish was very good! I believe it's the vegetarian dish but we loved it. The ribs were just ok. Nothing too excited or worth the money necessarily. I think they need some work.

Tried the chicken and waffles today for brunch. Amazing decision! The bourbon syrup really topped it. New favorite brunch spot. Also tried the sangria - it was ok. Should have stuck with bottomless mimosas.

Fun, fun, fun... Walked into this dive local bar on a Thursday night band was , upstairs band was good made it up to the third-floor, band was great and saxophone player was standing on the bar blowing his horn!

If you are from out of town and want some fun but to avoid the downtown craziness this is your place. Outstanding food , great service and real good local bands. This is a good taste of Nashville. I love the whole vibe and down stairs there are Billards in the place next door. some real fun.
p.s. That is the best club I have ever had.
The sweet potatoe hummus is ridiculously good as well.

First place we ate out at during our stay in Nashville. Located on Broadway so it was right in the heart of all the action. There was live music and we got to sit on their rooftop patio. Beautiful views, typical bar food, great vibe!
Amazing! Made me cry and laugh! So awesome to see talent so up close and personal. So fun!

A shining star in Nashville. French philosopher Henri Bergson's principle of duration explains how once we acknowledge the greatness of something, we kill it. The Stone Fox makes me think of this, because I am a bit weary of praising the sweetness that is The Stone Fox lest I jinx it. It's one of those things you hope never changes, but you can't help but fear that something--some outside force or something internal--will cause it to lose that spark. This place has amazing shows, fantastic food and drinks, incredible decor (lots of maps; you won't be able to miss it, but make sure to take a look at the huge mural map of the United States on the back wall) and accommodating staff. It wonderfully meshes a classy restaurant with a grungy bar-house. It's a place you can take your grandparents to (Monday nights: Bingo!) and also your party-prone friends. William Tyler, an amazing local musician, owns the place along with his sister. This must be how they book so many incredible musicians. I can't stress enough how much I enjoy their lineups. It never disappoints. The only thing that I don't like about The Stone Fox is that it's so far away from my house. 


Also, when you see the staff and the people who frequent this place, you'll know it's called The Stone Fox for a reason. Wowza!

The location of this place is great, located in greenhills with no other great coffee shops around. The decor is nicely done and they have beauty products (like lotions, soaps) from local business. As much as I wanted to like this place compared to other coffee shops in Nashville this place really isn't that great.  I got a cappuccino, maybe that was the problem, but it tasted mostly of milk.  I could hardly taste any espresso. Maybe the coffee is better, but a good cappuccino should be standard.

On a positive note they have lots of vegan friendly snacks!
One of my new favorite places to go when visiting our daughter in Nashville! Great food and awesome music. Grill cheese and tomato soup....I'm a fan!
Loved the upstairs outdoor deck area! Very nice and fun to have a few drinks.
Occasionally there is a decent singer/songwriter on the first floor, but overall the place is a dump and full of tourists that don't know any better.
Hands down coolest bar I've ever been to. Great vibe, better music, good beer and cool bartenders.  Absolutely loved this place. Rocking chairs were the cherry on top
A must-go in downtown Nashville.  Super cool atmosphere you just know there is so much country music history made here. Their Apple Shine specialty shot tastes like apple flavored goldschlager.

This place is always packed, so make sure you are good with standing! They have a multi level building with a great rooftop bar and patio offering the best views of downtown Nashville. The bands are great, the vibe is high energy and everyone is here to have a good time. It does get difficult to get a drink because of the volume, but the staff is quick and friendly overall. Not a good place to sit and talk, but the perfect place to stand up, dance to the music and party with hundreds of your closest friends!

The best brunch in town.  The owners, Elise and William Tyler, are real locals who put a lot of time and energy into their food and welcome EVERYONE.  This tends to be a musicians hangout.  Great front porch and the back patio is the place to be during nice weather.  Their annual  Pardi Gras Crawfish Boil, in February, is the most fun I've had in a long time.  They know how to do it right!!!

After flying into town I stopped into Tootsie's at 10:30am on a Saturday for the first time. It was a great experience and introduction to Nashville! The bar decor of old photographs was really unique and gave it a dive bar feel. The place was surprisingly busy that early in the morning and the audience was a loud fun crowd that would request songs and sing along with the band. The band playing wore cowboy outfits and had a great sound. I didn't realize until after I left that there was a different band playing on the next level of the bar. I will definitely be going back to Tootsie's before I leave town!
Loved this little bar and the country band that was playing was great! Very tiny though so there wasn't really anywhere to sit or barely room to stand but awesome place!

I've been to the Fox 4-5 times with friends and enjoyed it every time. Kudos to the owners for opening an original music venue/bar/surprisingly decent restaurant in the Nations before it occurred to anyone else. Such innovative risk-takers. I had to wait in line for brunch once, but after I was seated, I found the food to be worth it. The menu has changed since they first opened.   Some dishes I loved have passed into history. Nevertheless, I always think the food is great. Never had a problem with service either; always friendly. Only time service was slow was when the place was absolutely packed  - understandable - & the server was apologetic.  Love the Fox.
Been here several times for drinks, dinner, and Sunday brunch.  Everything has been really good.  The menu changes up enough to keep it interesting and fresh.

This may not look like the kind of place you would enjoy. You are completely wrong, turn around right now and walk back to Tootsie's.

There are 2 stages. The main act up front (if you are willing to tolerate elbows to armpits in close quarters and basically "0" service unless willing to shout over the band to bartenders forced to guess your order and pour overpriced drinks into plastic tumblers) and a great 2nd stage and bar upstairs. So, why stay here? Because it's awesome!

I must say I am 1,000,000% non-country Chicago born, New York bred, city all the way. However, there is something about Tootsie's that slips into your DNA like a designer virus that I guarantee you will enjoy. 

#1 if you want prompt service immediately go to the upstairs rear stage bar for drinks. Either stay there or return downstairs willing to stand your ground.

The music here is the best, good times in Nashville!

Slooow service. Wish I knew what the new menu tasted like? Went in at 4 on St. Patty's day.  Seating was slow. Despite what appeared to be an abundance of staff service was sad. We told waitress that we were not interested in drinking but were looking to eat. After 10-15 minutes dropped some cash and left. I am not Suttling for poor service.

My husband and I went with our three kids ages 8-14 on a Saturday night. We all loved it. The music was great. The staff was pleasant and the food was fine. Would go back for sure.  The kids got a little restless toward the end but behaved nicely.

This place had a great live band.  The cocktails were pricy for what you got, but the bartenders were super quick with their service.  If you are in Nashville and would like to see some great live music then Tootsie's is your place!
Great bar with great music!!  I had a blast even though is was packed to the gills.  Good times.

The menu is WAY over priced for what you get as an overall experience including food quality. The service was awesome, attentive, timely and she was a nice girl. After looking at the menu and history of the restaurant online, I was completely thrown off when we sat down. 
Example: Brussels sprout appetizer was $8, $3 to add (what we got was) 1/2 oz of bacon with approximately 6 Brussels sprouts cut in half. 
Probably won't return.
Good vibe- hole in the wall type bar with good music! Not a great drink selection,overpriced food and really strange smell!
Great, fun atmosphere with great bands, and a free cover!  Drinks were average priced for the Broadway area.

I'm all about shopping local when I can and I use to go to The Well a lot.  Wifi is fast and I like the random furniture.  They have lots of local items for sale which is neat, coffee is decent and the local pastries are good.  The sandwiches are pretty poo though. 

Speaking of poo, the women's bathroom is the most disgusting bathroom I've seen in Nashville. I would post a photo but I'll save you the excitement to see it in person, ladies. I've used porta-johns at beer festivals around town that I felt cleaner in and I'm not joking. I've sent them an email, a FB message and told the staff in person.  No one seems to care which in turn keeps me not caring to ever go back.

I absolutely appreciate Katy and the team that assisted her in addressing me and my families concerns and giving us a fair resolve. She not only listened to our issues but acknowledged our feelings, which really meant a lot. AND SHE WAS ON IT! It took a second for her to respond and get caught up, but once she did she didn't miss a beat with following up with me and providing a resolve. Thank you soo much Katy !
Hit this place every time We're in town. Hope to be relocating to Nashville, on the near future. Any up and coming acts that need a bass player hit me up!

Paradise Park Trailer Resort is a honky-tonk bar and restaurant that opened on Lower Broadway in downtown Nashville in 2007. I visited this past Friday night and learned, later on in the weekend, that this place is closing soon. It's supposed to close this month (July 2018) so I wanted to get my review out before they closed.

We showed up just before midnight on Friday and this place was packed. The line to get in wasn't very long, but it was very crowded inside, especially on the first floor. There were two bands, one on the first floor (ground level) as soon as you walk in and one inside on the rooftop (fourth level). I believe both bands were cover bands (definitely the band on the top floor; I remember one song they sang was the Alien Ant Farm version of Smooth Criminal). Both bands were pretty good and most people seemed to be having a good time.

There are a lot of lights and neon signs on Broadway. You can't miss Paradise Park's sign because it's one of the biggest. It's green and red and spans over two stories. It's one of the most prominent signs on the street. The space has colorful and kitschy decor (neon signs, string lights, Christmas lights, a disco ball, and more). Just inside the entrance is a photo booth and Skee-Ball. During our visit, the second and third floors were closed. The second floor was home to a dueling piano bar called The Big Bang.

We spent most of our time on the rooftop patio which was a lot more laid back and relaxed than downstairs. The rooftop has both an interior and exterior bar. The outdoor portion of the rooftop is covered in artificial turf with picnic tables, lawn/porch chairs, and high tops for seating. There was always a game of cornhole going on while we were up there. The highlight, to me, is the view from the rooftop. You get to see the beautiful downtown Nashville cityscape as well as all of the activity below on Broadway. Paradise Park seems to be in the center of it all. If it's not closed by the time you read this, the rooftop is definitely worth checking out.

If you want to use the elevator and it's not working, try punching in 0114 (authorization code). Otherwise, you'll have to get an employee to help you or just take the stairs.

On June 13, 2018, the Nashville Business Journal reported the building (411 Broadway) sold for $27 million last summer (https://www.bizjournals.com/nashville/news/2018/06/13/the-goldberg-brothers-are-closing-this-downtown.html) and will close in July 2018. The owners of the building and Paradise Park, who also own a bunch of restaurants in Nashville, are planning to open a new concept which will utilize all four stories of the building. It's supposed to open in 2019.

Excellent time here. The music was amazing and history of the place, even better. I love this bar. Will be back next time. If you go to Nashville, you must stop here. Amazing atmosphere, and excellent service. People are so friendly in Nashville, it makes you feel at home.

Shauna was incredible! We came in accidentally almost before bar close and she helped us get our drinks quickly and made them super well. She was the biggest sweetheart and our favorite bartender the whole weekend in Nashville! The night was perfectly closed with a visit to Paradise Park. Next time we're in town, we will definitely be visiting earlier and for a longer time because she was so good to us. The drinks were strong and delicious. A definite Nashville Broadway Go-To! #YouDaBest #ShaunaFanClub #Nashelorette

If you visit, you pretty much have to go to Tootsies to check it off your list. Front bar gets really crowded, but upstairs is a little less congested. We spent time in both areas and each of the bands were really good performers. They do tend to play the same songs though, obviously a lot of crowd favorites. Drinks were expensive, but it was about as expected considering the Broadway area and the popularity of Tootsies.

They serve beer in mason jars...

Hipster apocalypse! 

I really liked this little joint. I'm practically never on the westside...Stone Fox may have given me a reason to venture there now. We came for a friends show and I was sorely disappointed that we did not eat dinner here. Instead we just stood around and drank our cold mason jar beers. As a former geography major graduate I have to say I'm semi obsessed with the American wall map on the wall near the stage. I also loved the very pinteresting idea of using pallets as a fence for their rear patio, complete with herbs in between the slats. I really hope that during meal service they don't allow smoking back there. 

I will definitely come to see small gigs at The Stone Fox. I heard that it used to have better acoustics but honestly I feel like if the band knows what it's doing, it shouldn't matter too much.

Anyway worth going to for surely! Can't wait to try some grub!

The service here can be a little slow sometimes, but they make hands down the best burger I have had in Nashville and have a great selection of beers. Also, they host free/fun events such as bingo night and have a house bluegrassy band on Sundays. I think is one my favorite places in Nashville to grab a bite to eat, have a beer, and enjoy the evening!
Great atmosphere. Food is fun and delicious. There's two different scenes to keep you entertained. A must see

This was our second to last bar we visited on our girls weekend to Nashville & it was just as fun as everyone said it was! We went straight upstairs to the 3rd floor & got a drink (4 shots of well tequilla $28) (don't judge me for ordering a well brand). 

We listened to the band for a bit, which like every band we heard this past weekend was amazing. Then we went outside to the front patio which had the best view of downtown Nashville, we loved being up there. 

The only warning is try not to use the bathroom on the 2nd floor because there was an extremely rude bathroom attendant that was screaming at everybody who walked in about anything & everything. She was also very over the top with asking for tips because she says she only works for them but there would be no way I would tip somebody who made going to the bathroom so uncomfortable for everyone in our group.

Got to see Thom Schuyler, Fred Knobloch, Tony Arata, and Jelly Roll Johnson play in the round during a special NYE show. Being from New Orleans, I think I have fairly high standards for live music, and this was one of the coolest shows I've ever seen. The music wasn't overpoweringly loud. The songs and the stories behind them, told by the songwriters were the center of the show.

The Sutler is a GREAT place for cocktails and appetizers, however, I would skip out on dinner or brunch here if I were you. The menu at first looks wonderful with a lot of great options, but when the food is bland without a lot of flavor.

If I were you I would go for happy hour and have a few apps and then pick another spot for dinner!

I really enjoyed my brunch experience here. The waitress was awesome and hilarious and put up with my indecisiveness on determining what I wanted. I got the BLT with an egg on it and while the bread was a tad greasy it was the best BLT I have ever had.

The vibe is really cool and the art everywhere is fun. Their grits are good, just got cold quickly so you could tell that they were reheated. 

Their drip and sip coffee with Tennessee whiskey creamer was pretty good. 

Their French toast was good as well and I saw someone get their chicken and waffles, they looked awesome and hope to get those soon. Will definitely be back!
Amazing live music!!!! I was blown away by the band Saturday night. Cool little place!
Gotta give it a 5 star for tradition and Lindsey at the second floor bar. Stiff drinks and much appreciated. Music? Of course and muy bueno. Must see must visit.

Music on all 3 floors 
Service and music both excellent crowded but worth it view from roof top at night very nice 
A line to get in but it moves quick well worth the wait 
Drinks a little pricey but it is a tourist spot
Sit chill and enjoyed all the music and fun

We were downtown just being tourists on a Thursday afternoon, and we were amazed at how lively it was in the middle of the day, so we felt inspired to duck into a honky-tonk. I remembered this place's epic decor/theme from a long-ago trip, and from the street, it did seem like the least crowded -- and maybe the most sincere? I mean, if you can have the most sincere pumpkin patch, can Nashville have the most sincere honky-tonk? While it lays the redneck ambience on a little thick, it never seems too clever about it -- to us, it felt very down to earth. The bartender was very nice and very attentive, and she suggested a local beer we ended up loving. We opted to order our food at the counter and pick it up there -- that made it feel a little more real. I had the hot chicken, and while it wasn't Hattie B's, it was not lacking in heat, a heat that really snuck up on you. My husband really liked his burger. The fries were like I make at home, except AWESOME. There was a very relaxed vibe, and the people who did come in were a diverse crowd (hipsters, rednecks, investment bros, a 20something girls' weekend). The live music was very laid-back/stripped-down and a good range of songs, and both musicians were very friendly. Basically, this was EXACTLY what I wanted from a honky-tonk experience -- and that we were able to have fun here in the middle of the afternoon only reinforces to me what a fun town Nashville is.

Have been twice now and both times, food was great. I had buffalo shrimp lettuce wraps both times and loved them! The celery salad that came with them was amazing too. French fries are good too. I will be back.
3 stars for a wednesday night visit, but oh, how i'd love to come back on a weekend.

Come for the band!!! Period ! I can literally stop my review right here.  I mean the place has really not much going for it but it manages to PACK a massive crowd.  Monday night at 10pm and the place was shoulder to shoulder.  Walls and floors are caked in sticky-icky shit... but people seem to not mind that stuff so ehhh - to each their own.

Monday Open Mic Night at the Bluebird was the highlight of my Nashville trip for sure! The deal here is you either book tickets far in advance before they've sold out or you take your chances at Open Mic Night. We did not plan ahead, but hey were there on a Monday so why not? 

THE WAIT - We read all the reviews that said be there an hour early and thought we'd be extra cautious, so we go there 2 hours early instead.  Tourist Fail! They hire security to ensure you aren't loitering in the parking lot early and disturbing other businesses. We were shoo' d away rather quickly. We came back exactly 56 minutes before doors open and we were already numbers 35 and 36 in line. They really mean an hour early. By 45 minutes to opening there were already 80 people in line and the venue was a capacity. Note that it's the same line for those wanting to be part of the audience and those wanting to perform, so get there early. Also, pack sunscreen, I fried in the sun waiting in the parking lot line (so worth it)! 

THE ATMOSPHERE - Great little venue, true listening room (so be quiet). Tables are push as close up to the front of the stage as possible. If you are lucky enough to score the front row, you feel like you are practically on stage with the artists. Great sound throughout the entire venue. Don't let the strip mall exterior fool you, this place has a great vibe. 

THE FOOD - Limited menu  but the prices are more than fair and the food they do provide is good. Mostly snacky items and lighter meals. We had the edamame and sweet potato fries, both were tasty. They have a full bar, including my personal favorite cider. 

THE SERVICE - Service was friendly and efficient. I'd totally come back! 

THE ENTERTAINMENT - I have to say, I was really surprised at how much I enjoyed this. Open Mic nights can be hit or miss.  There were literally artists from all over the world that had really traveled to either moved to Nashville or just came in for the week for a chance to sing at the Bluebird. Almost everyone we say had real talent. It was a great show!  

I would consider this a must if you are in Nashville. Granted, it's a trek from downtown tucked away in Green Hills (suburbia). A little bit of walking and one bus ride will get you there. Or it's about a 20 minute taxi from Honkey Tonk Row.
Climbed up a zillion stairs for a smelly bar and the same drinks and music as everywhere else.  Blah.
Stopped in here with some girlfriends to grab a bite to eat.. had chicken tenders from what I remember they were good, ha!
I had as good as a time as I expected from what everyone had told me. Truly a uniquely Nashville experience.

Had a lunch here while I was in town for a conference.  I ordered the Hot Chicken Sandwich and it did not disappoint.  Compared to some of the other places on the strip the prices were more than reasonable.  There was live music and it definitely has the "dive" feel.  The gentlemen I ate with had a cheeseburger basket with fries that looked like a very classic burger.

Really good breakfast and entertainment on a Saturday. Chicken and waffles good but suggest you try other options more creative. Bloody Mary bar works well and lots of items to make each BM your favorite.

This was my first time in Nashville and I loved this place so much for dinner I came back for breakfast. Deviled eggs were to die for with that chorizo chip. The sweet potato pancakes were heaven in my mouth too. Other than that between the husband and I we had the meatloaf, fried chicken, and the corned beef hash which were all great. 

The only minor thing was the service was a little slow both times but it may be a southern thing. I'm from Chicago so we can get a little impatient if we are waiting more than a minute for a refill. 

There is historical value here too, so that added to the experience. As we walked around after brunch to Broadway a couple blocks away, there was a line clear out the door for Margaritaville which just is the biggest crime in the world when you can actually get a great meal just a tiny walk away.

This venue was a blast entertainment was awesome.  Good place to meet people from all over the country.  We stayed here longer than planned because of the bands.  Recommending to schedule more time to spend here

Very original performances from humble emerging artists usually with their own written material. When I went, there were performances from country, pop country, and bassist artists. Astounding performances and I would highly recommend anyone interested in music to attend. If you haven't reserved tickets in advance, go about 2 hours early to reserve a spot the day of. It's worth it to see a free show from these emerging artists.

I have only recently experienced all the beautiful goodness that is The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel. Now I seem to be a frequent attendee of the events on their schedule.

Old Crowe Medicine Show along with a concert pairing with Broadway notable and actress Idina Menzel with the Nashville Symphony left a nice aftertaste last year but it is 2013's schedule that has solidified The Woods as a notable outdoor live entertainment venue in my book. 

I have already enjoyed The Black Crowes and Old Crowe and still have One Republic, Alabama Shakes, FUN, and Sigur Ros left. I love the diversity of acts that are booked here ranging from Harry Connick Junior to Imagine Dragons, a little something for most audiophiles. 

Lawn parking is FREE and easy to access and there is a bit of pre-show tail-gating going on too! I generally valet and grab a cocktail at Cafe Fontanella which is located on the grounds before the show too. The beautiful backdrop of nature and greenery make you feel as if you've been whisked to a faraway place while the layout of the stage and grounds are thoughtfully executed. You can choose to layout on a blanket, bring a chair, stand or mill around, or opt to upgrade to the VIP boxes which sit high on a hill and overlook the crowd. 

The casual vibe is weaved together with local food trucks parked on the grounds and fairly priced concessions throughout. 

Overall, this is a wonderful place to catch a show during favorable weather and seasons. My only suggestion is if you plan to imbibe, bring a designated driver or to carpool since the winding roads and location are a bit of a stretch and a cab ride won't be cheap unless you live in the area. 

if you're into the great outdoors and a casual concert experience, join 4500 of your Nashville neighbors and head out to the unlikely space where country crooner Barbara Mandrell's old estate was housed. Only in Nashville, folks. Only in Nashville...

TIP: This venue may also be rented for private events and corporate functions too!

Please do not patronize this establishment. We came here as a family of 12 and spent several hours spending hard earned money.  Nashville prides itself on southern hospitality.  We sat behind the band for 2 hours and enjoyed the entertainment. When the 6:00 band came on and entire bar was filled, we were told we needed to leave our seats (that we had for 2 hours) because it was now V.I.P. There was not a place to be found to even stand. Unfortunately, we had order food for our entire group. We were told we could not cancel our very exclusive orders of "chicken fingers and fries" and they would not refund our money. After being accused, by the finger waving bartender, for taking more then what we ordered,  we went down to the lower bar, ate our sad and expensive food then left feeling extremely unappreciated, insulted and disregarded. This establishment does not appreciate or acknowledge hard working Americans!!!!  Please consider this truthful statement when you visit Nashville. This is no longer (if it ever was), a "TRUE" southern establishment. Shame on you Tootsies!!!!

Definitely a do-able bar, the staff, in my opinion, always takes too long and most of the time seems put out to have to wait on you. decent patio and decent food. everything is just ok. not awful, not great - best thing about it is the location.

If there's one activity that needs to be on your list when in the area, it has to be going to the Bluebird! 

There is not a bad seat in the house and the talent that graces the stage is second to none. 

You can make reservations a week in advance which is highly recommended! I lucked out and got 2 seats the day of by constantly checking the website for possible cancellations! This saved me from having to stand outside for a couple hours! 

The staff is super friendly. The only downfall is the parking lot, but you can park across the street at the mall and walk over! 

Best show you'll see no matter who's playing the night you go!

Best customer service every... I bought some t-shirt for souvenirs and when I went home in L.A. One did not fit and with one Email I got a fast responses and great customer service. Thank you for your kindness and hope to be back again...

Visited Nashville a couple of months ago, and we all made a note of it to stop at Tootsies. And boy, did it not disappoint! When you first walk in, it is very crowded. However, once you find a spot, you're good! We luckily got a spot right in front of the stage. The band was INCREDIBLE! In my opinion, the night we visited Tootsies was my favorite night in Nashville! The bar service was good, and the bathroom attendant was pretty awesome as well! Next time I go to Nashville, I know we're I'm heading first! I would highly recommend Tootsies to anyone who is visiting Nashville!

This was our first bar experience on Broadway.  Overall experience there was OK.  To me this was one of the worst bars on the strip. I know it is famous and all but it was very dumpy inside and they were one of the more expensive bars on broadway. $16 dollars for for two Miller Lites was to me over the top.  Also this bar the bar tenders and the bands were way more aggressive in their asking for tips.  I get that in that area they don't pay the bands and probably pay their bartenders very low. But just seems Tacky how much they have to beg.  I don't mind tipping well for good service and entertainment. I just feel they don't have to throw it in your face. Other bars on broadway or off the May Row were not this bad.

When you visit Nashville, Tennessee, the number one domestic destination in 2017, please be sure to visit "Honky Tonk Row." 

While visiting "Honky Tonk Row", there is a little orchid colored gem. A small narrow establishment, wedged in between others less crowded. Tootsie's. 

Tootsie's Orchid Lounge, named after "Tootsie Bess" and the Orchid color of the exterior walls, would one day become the place that we would dare to dream of hearing the  stories her walls could tell, and the sounds that emanate from her three stages. 

Tootsie's Orchid Lounge is known as "the place" where many new and yet undiscovered startups, dreamed, then penned the songs we have come to love. 

This little building remembers all of those nights that the stars of the Grand Ole Opry would exit the Ryman's stage  after a show, take a short walk down Ryman Alley, and right into the back door of Tootsie's, to "get ready for the next show!"

 Some of the early famous first customers were Willie Nelson, Patsy Cline, Mel Tillis, Kris Kristofferson, Waylon Jennings, Roger Miller and numerous others country musicians.

Today's successful artist are still dropping in, unannounced, to play a few songs on her stage for her customers, the lovers of country music!

Never a charge to come in, you are bound to have a great time in this iconic little country bar , on Broadway, at the foot of the Ryman Auditorium, the Home of the Grand Ole Opry. 

The sounds you'll hear, not only the ones we listen to in '17, but the ones nearly 60 years prior. 

The other buildings, nestled close to where the sounds of live country music becomes anything but the daily routine. 

Where our country music, the stars of yesterday and today were created, and are still being performed daily!

So come on down, stroll in and belly up. See what they saw, and feel what they felt. 

Enjoy the music and know that we're taking good care of the place.

Heard this place was the place to go, but I wasn't impressed. The place was packed, barely room to move about. Drinks were weak and served in plastic cups. Can't hear the band upstairs very well. Cleanliness was not up to par either.
Now I can say I came, I saw and then I left.

The ambiance gets a 10 for me ... I'm a sucker for a speakeasy . One of my colleagues was in town &  no one could decide on a place for drinks ... I yelled " Sutler " ... Everyone else voted for Rosepepper but somehow we ended up at my choice ! The upstairs was slammed ... Not unexpected for a Friday night . We were seated downstairs & my heart smiled at the decor ! The cocktail menu was awesome ... I'm a bourbon girl so I chose Don't Ask Rye. It was soooo delicious !!! My colleagues chose a drink that was in a red Solo cup . We then decided to order little plates to eat ... Mac & cheese & hot chicken bites .... I mean ... Speechless . The bread underneath sold me ... After a few drinks everything was delicious !! There was a house made white sauce that was good . Overall , the service was superb . Elizabeth was very attentive & even helped with drink selections ! I will def be back very soon ! Seems like a great place to start or finish up a fun weekend night !
Disgusting!!! I had the veggies burger it's rice and black beans in a patty, it's soft, squishy with no flavor. The hand cut fries were cold! Yuck.
Great music and attentive bartenders.  Seating is limited, but you will want to be on your feet enjoying the music anyway
When I go to Nashville, I always and I mean always will stop at Tootsie. The music is great the service is great. Its one of the funnest places in Nashville.

Since my original 5-star review, we've been back several times. I still am a big fan, but I have to say that the menu is so skewed toward the smoky/fatty/salty/messy end that I'm not going to be a regular diner. Delicious - yes - but if you care about your health, this is food that you should eat only occasionally.

Sunday bluegrass is a great way to start the week; hope that this tradition catches on. The two times I've gone in for Sunday supper (once early, once late) there was plenty of available seating.

Parking is going to continue to be a problem for the time being, but there are self-parking options beside and behind the building. Which really is plenty close (remember the olden days when there were no valet stands?).
Super fun place, we went two days in a row because we liked it so much. The band was great we stayed on the first floor. The drinks are great, atmosphere is fun, a definite must when in Nashville.
Definitely understated. Cheap beer and friendly bar staff. The music was better than most.
Took my team up the street for lunch on Monday.  Fried chicken sandwich was phenomenal.  Exceptional food, service, and atmosphere.  This makes the regular rotation.

I'm only taking 1 star off because the process to get booked here is so difficult and I've easily booked every other venue in town at least once...but alas, the Bluebird is a Nashville original! Just a word to the wise...do NOT talk..this is a listening room! You will never have a bad night of music here...it is very tiny so if you're claustrophobic this may not be your thing...I think sunday nights are great but any night there's a good show..

Made it to the famous Blue Bird on Hillsboro Pike. Woo! I love places like this because it's not what you think from the outside.  From the outside it just looks like a taco shop back in San Diego that has like 4 tables.  But it seats about 70 at a strip mall.  How's that for not judging a bird by it's bird cage?! 
     This is where the magic happens. I luv being around artist who are paying their dues and trying to make it. This place is so legendary they don't take reservations and they pack in all the time for Songwriters Nights. There's a wall of a lot of people who have played there. This is where the "Songwriters" perform who wrote and created hits for other artist and themselves . Everyone from Taylor Swift, Keith Urban, Faith Hill and omg Carol KING!!! Carol King played here. "gasp!" So awesome. And now Mel M from Yelp has took a pic in front of the entrance at the Bluebird Cafe =)  If you're into Country and or love music and always wanted to visit Nashville.  You will want to stop here for street cred.

We walked in and immediately felt the spirit of our wonderful Nashville town! What a cool place! They smoke all the meats, food is spot on! What??? My wife finally found her illusive "Grilled Romaine Salad!!!" Needless to say the food more than matches the wonderful atmosphere! We just found our place!
the bar was great. however they do not give out warnings, do not stand on chairs and dance. you will be penalized. (kicked out)

Loud, busy, popular, crowded, fun, comfortable, affordable, ample portions, accessible,
delicious, variety, efficient.

what more do you want to know?
first come first served.
line moves pretty well.

*** go early to drive around and hunt for a parking space.

We ate here last night and I am so excited that this is right around the corner from us!! They had half off drafts and specialty cocktails for Happy Hour so we tried a Hello Darlin' (grapefruit vodka spritzer) and the Gambler (basil julep). They were both well-balanced and an awesome value at the HH price of $4.50. 
We started with the Fried Pickle Bash, which had fried pickles (obviously), green tomatoes, okra, and LEMONS!! Seriously, don't be scared of the fried lemon slices. The acidity really plays nicely off of everything else plus the heat of frying tones it down. 
We decided to split some shared plates and went for the Brussel Sprout Hash, Fresh Cut Pork Fat Fries, and Pit Smoked Loaded Mac. All were delicious! They could definitely be split as side items but you could easily eat one as a meal as well. They have a fantastic menu with several twists. I can't wait to try more! 
A few side notes: 
Nichelle, our server was great. She was informative and gave her opinion on her favorites. I could tell she was excited about the menu and the space in general. 
A couple of the sides were warm-ish but not piping hot. I'm sure when the kitchen gets into their groove this won't be an issue anymore though so I'm fully expecting to eventually reevaluate them at 5 stars. 
Also, the acoustics are really good here. The music was as loud as you would expect in a venue but we could easily have a conversation at our table. 
Lastly, go explore downstairs. Trust me!

If their food wasn't  so good I would give it one star. I took my parents there for brunch. They sat us at a coffee table with tall chairs. That's fine if you're having just drinks but not for a meal. They didn't ask us for an option to sit at a table. After a HOUR wait for food, we had to eat with the plates in our lap because the table was so low. I'll go to a restaurant with tables next time.

Tootsie's...more like poopsies 

Things to keep in mind as you decide what bars you want to visit on Broadway:

1. The bouncers seemed inexperienced and unnecessarily rude. They cracked my friend's legal ID. A separate bouncer told us he could not let anyone onto the rooftop due to capacity but then prompted to let a group of 40+ dudes up 

2. Drinks / music were fine but comparable to other bars that don't have sad excuses for bouncers

This was our first stop on our trip to Nashville. The waitress was so awesome and helped us figure out the places that we should go see. It's always nice to feel welcomed in another state so this was a big plus ! Now let's talk food. I ordered the avocado sandwich and I highly recommend it. Another friend order the peanut butter and banana sandwich which was also great. The other two weren't as happy with the meals of quesadillas and the fajita sandwich. All in all I would definitely go back but maybe next time for brunch!
After the bars when you're looking for that greasy goodness they got what you need. Burgers, dogs and fries oh my!

Celebrated my birthday here, the food was fantastic, the restaurant was a bit loud, maybe because of the space.   The patrons seemed to lack respect for proper dress, this is not a Cracker Barrel!  But a piece of history, revamped into a nice restaurant.  Our server, probably belonged at a pancake house, but the food was very good, the wine very good, many good choices.   Restrooms very clean, altogether a nice spot!  We went downstairs after dinner for the music and it did not disappoint, the man downstairs was EXCELLENT!!  The venue perfect, perhaps the Hostess could do more to sell the downstairs.  I'll go back looking to try other menu items....

This place is a must visit while in Nashville. The live music is incredible. The performance we saw was fantastic. They engaged with the crowd and played a lot of the favorites. It is a very small space so be prepared to get up close and personal with a few strangers. Service was quick and the drinks were good. I highly recommend visiting during your stay.

As pointed out by others, Green Hills was in desperate need of a local coffee house to supplant the corporate monster that is Starbuck's.  I mean the area is becoming a bit of a chain-Mecca, and I do not mean that in a good way.

The Well Coffeehouse offers you something different.  And, since I just mentioned Mecca, I want to mention now the weird religious undertones scattered throughout the place.  I just do not understand why the religion was needed in the coffeehouse.  But, the owners have definitely decided that "Hey, let's make Christianity and Jesus our theme for a coffee shop!"  I understand that they are giving back through the purchases that you make in the store to those in need, but I am not certain religion is necessary to promote a theme of giving back.

The coffee is moderate, but the prices are less than Starbucks.  The food bites are moderate, but the prices are less than Starbucks.  The rest of the non-religious decor lends itself to make you want to read more, study more, and chill out more.  And, the prices are less than Starbucks.  (Sorry, I just wanted to throw that in again whether it made sense or not.)

In the end, I guess the place is A-OK as 3 stars would suggest.  I just think you can do better throughout the city of Nashville with other local coffee places.

I'll start by saying I'm a 25+ year Nashville resident, with a clear understanding of the challenges that come with our population boom, and staffing issues around the restaurant explosion in particular. That said, the experience I had today was dreadful to the point that I feel compelled to share it. Side note: I am loathe to complain in restaurants, and this is my first negative review. I've also been a patron of the Sutler (old and new) off and on for many years.

I went in for lunch, sat down at the bar alone around 12:30.  The place was less than half full.
I ordered a Saloon Burger with fries, and caught up on the football scores.  The burger was so oversalted it was absurd. Dripping with grease, tough, off-flavored, really nothing redeeming about it. Fries were nearly as bad....limp, soggy, just not good food.  

When I told the bartender how salty it was, her response was, "oh, I'm sorry" as the check was put in front of me. Most of the food was clearly uneaten and still on the plate, but there was not the slightest attempt to make things better...wow! 

I've eaten all over the world, and am realistic enough not to expect culinary miracles at The Sutler. But a decent burger with fries at a fair price ($16.95 w. fries?) is not too much to ask of any professional food establishment. Is Nashville growing too fast to keep a close eye on the basics these days?   Enter at your own risk.

Honky Tonkin on 3 levels. You can go up or down until you find some band you like. The place gets packed just about any night of the week. You will see some awesome musicians in here, the local bar bands in Nashville are the most talented I have ever seen.

Best Bar in Nashville!!
3 levels of great music- super cool staff- always jam packed & hella busy and full of fun!
This place is amazing!  Three floors of live music.  Bartenders on 3rd floor are awesome!  Highly recommend stopping by if you're ever in downtown Nashville.

I live in East Nashville, within easy walking distance of both Bongo Java and Barista Parlor, and biking distance of Sip, Portland Brew, and Ugly Mugs. I also get to Dose pretty regularly because it's near my son's daycare and my work. I should be more than satisfied with my coffee shop selection, but none of them have quite hit my sweet spot. Here's my list of coffee shop ideals:

1) Locally roasted coffee (sorry Dose and Barista Parlor)
2) Not Drew's Brews (just don't love it - sorry Sip and Ugly Mugs)
3) Option to get individual cuppings in a French Press, Pourover, Chemex, Aeropress, Clever dripper, or something. (Sorry Bongo Java and Portland Brew)
4) Soothing, homey atmosphere that isn't snotty (sorry Barista Parlor and Portland Brew)
5) Reasonable (not cheap - I know good coffee is expensive) prices
6) Decaf options for my second or third cup (sorry Barista Parlor and Dose - decaf espress just won't do for me)

Things I (personally) don't really care about or know anything about:
1) Coolness (in fact, too much cool is a turnoff)
2) Espresso drinks - I drink black brewed coffee
3) Food choices - I'm there for coffee
4) Really anything but the coffee and the comfort

All this to say, The Well is my favorite coffee shop in Nashville, which is extremely surprising given its Green Hills location. A huge selection of coffee from Just Love means there's plenty of variety in single origin or blends, whatever your roast preference (as a City roast fan, I think I have 10+ coffees to choose from!). They will make it with a pour over cone, a Chemex, an Aeropress, or a French Press - a wealth of options. I've had the pour over and the Aeropress, and both were executed quite well, creating clean and flavorful cups. 

The tables are large, the wood everywhere inside leads to a comfortable feeling, and there are couches and squishy chairs if you want comfort over utility. The wifi is reasonably fast (I'm posting this review on it!) 

And prices are reasonable - $2 for 12 oz cups made to order, with refills coming in at just a dollar! That wouldn't be cheap for coffee brewed in a giant pot, but for single-cup brewing it's an amazing deal.

Yes, the Baristas are a little slow and unprofessional-seeming, but they know how to make good coffee. Yes, the bathrooms are kind of gross. Yes, the building needs work - there are some leaks in the hallway leading to the bathroom on this rainy day. No, they don't have good food choices. But I, personally, don't care. They hit everything on MY list, which makes them my favorite. I will certainly give them patronage whenever I have the opportunity, and will be much more reluctant to go to my local East Nashville shops knowing this exists.

The atmosphere is like a step back into time.  This two floor venue is very loud.  It is hard to hold a conversation and even our waiter had trouble hearing us.  Service was very slow and waiter was not attentive.  The menu is pricey and limited at dinner.  I had the filet mignon with brussel sprouts and mashed potatoes for $39.  The filet was a generous cut and cooked perfectly.  Mash potatoes were good.  I have had better brussel sprouts.  There were only three on the plate.  My companion got the seafood gumbo.  She liked it but thought it was too spicy.  However, a would expect it to be as it has andouille sausage in it. The bad news is her gumbo came out from kitchen but my food did not.  The waiter went to check on it and came back to say it was coming but it took probably 15 more minutes.  In fact, I had called a manager to the table to inquire about my meal since my companion was finished with hers.  My food finally arrived and we were offered one free dessert.  Very sad offer for such an event.  Forgot to mention they do offer bread when you sit down.  The basket had cheese biscuits and one piece of sweet cornbread.  The cornbread looked as if it had a bite or two taken out of it. We had sweet and unsweet tea to drink.  At one point the waiter refilled our tea and put sweet tea in both glasses.  This glass of tea tasted like a fruit tea.  Upon inquiry we were told it might be mango tea.  Definitely need to get their act together. 

Attaching photos of inside main floor and movie screen.  They show old movie clips without sound on the screen.

Very affordable and divey. Lots of college aged people spilling drinks on each other and getting a little rowdy at night. The service is friendly and the food is well priced with decent portions. Nothing here wowed me, but the short line for bathrooms stands out on a Friday night on Broadway!

Coming from Chicago for a Bachelorette party of 17 girls, you know that what can go wrong, will go wrong! I had verified via email twice prior to our visit a table at the Demonbreun Tin Roof address.
It was the Saturday night of Labor Day weekend, during a Tennessee football game, and a packed place. Since I could not find the hostess, I asked the bartender about our reservations (with 16 girls piled behind me). He had no idea of our party, grabbed my phone with the email confirmation thread on it, and disappeared.

A few minutes later, the manager, Josh, came back and said they didn't know anything of our party and had a packed house. The woman who had emailed me back was new and forgot to forward it to him. After he rushed around and came back a few more times, he offered to buy us all a round of drinks (17 mixed drinks!) and quickly started setting up tables in the back room. We ended up having our own section, played our own music, had our own waitress, and danced in our own area. Josh comped 4 baskets of chips and queso, and even grabbed us all a fireball shot after the bride drunkenly yelled for some. 

He handled the situation fantastically and we were beyond impressed. It turned out better than we had even hoped! Now that is great customer service. (And the food was good!)

This place is awesome! The staff is friendly, no charge for parking, the crowd is chill, just a great back drop for music shows. The food and drink is a bit pricey. Oh, and big screens would be a huge plus IMO. But a fantastic spot for music.

This is my favorite bar on Broadway. They have a good selection of microbrews for the same price as everyone else's domestics. The music is great and the service people kind and knowledgable.

I came in the afternoon and Harold Allen is an awesome musician. We all danced, sang, did shots, and enjoyed a Nashville day.

Enjoyed my first meal there and look forward to adventuring through the rest.  Snacks & sides are both shareable, and we went for it.  I don't know if I will ever be able to visit without ordering the pit smoked loaded mac.  The blackberry cobbler with buttermilk ice cream isn't to be missed.  It's nearly impossible to listen to live music and simultaneously talk to your table mates, but The Sutler manages it.  Love the atmosphere & don't forget to visit the Cellar.

This place was recommended to me by a friend as the best spot to hit while visiting Nashville. We were only in town for the one night, and it was a Tuesday, but the service we got from Jacqui behind the bar was great. She was extremely pleasant and helpful for the duration of the evening. Would and will recommend it to others, and will definitely stop back on my travels in the future.
