We are extremely spoiled in Nashville. We don't lack in music venues right in my backyard, so to drive 20 minutes might not seem like much, but for us spoiled people it seems like a feat. Especially when you are stuck in traffic on a 1 lane road adding an extra 10-15 minutes to the trip. But I digress..

The venue itself is very pretty with stringed lights and a picturesque atmosphere. But the concession lines are LONG. And getting to the port-a-potties in the dark during a show is not exactly easy. I would prefer some better signage in the dark cause I got lost getting from the seated area. 

It was a sold out show when I attended and it was very crowded. If you are going to get general admission tickets, you have to have very low chairs, so plan on either a blanket or check your chairs accordingly. Also, get there early or else you aren't going to get a spot. 

We left the show early and still waited in line to exit the venue. But, they did a pretty good job of getting us out of there. Overall, this is a place that is nice if you are hanging out all day or plan on getting there early and taking it easy, but it's just not my favorite music venue.

What can I say Tootsie's is Crazy, lots of fun .  We where there earlier in the day and the place was packed with people.  Theres two floors both with bands playing all day long.  Upstairs  they have an outside area on the roof.  There was a big stage the band was great they really interacted with the crowd.  The singer would sometimes go  and walk on top of the bar.  And its was fun to call my family back home to go online and look at there Live Cam  they have one on the first floor that looks directly towards the stage, so we stood by the stage and waved to our family when we were there!

Came with one of my girls for brunch on Sunday. We got there a little before they opened and there was already a line outside. Once doors opened, place quickly filled up. We got sat at a bar top on the middle of the place. Was a little skeptical about being sat there, but we had a great view of the band that was playing. We did sit for a while before we were greeted and got drinks. Our server was really nice and stayed busy. We never got biscuits before or meal, as all other tables did. Off the bat we ordered bottomless mimosas, because I mean what is brunch without mimosas?!  
We both ordered the chili chicken hash. I had never had hash and was excited to try it. It was okay, was a little spicier than I expected. I don't normally eat a lot of fried foods, so naturally the fried potatoes didn't settle well in my stomach. Obviously not their fault. 
Our server stayed on top of keeping our mimosas filled up. We asked for some biscuits a little later and they were delicious. 
Bathroom is downstairs down a hallway, I assume it's a shared bathroom with another place. Decor in the place was neat. Lots of knick knacks on the walls. Boots on back wall of band and boots hanging from ceiling going down the stairway. 
Cute place for brunch.

We stood in line for the 9:30 show for about 2 hours, but it was absolutely worth it. It was the In the Round show and the musicians were mostly songwriters for big country music names. It's such a great experience to hear these songs from the people who actually  wrote them - and for whom they mean something deeply meaningful. 

The bluebird provides an awesome, intimate experience where it feels like you're sitting in a living room and listening to them jam. Also a great intro to country music for us.
This meal was outstanding!!! The pork chop was extremely tender and was paired with blackened peas and cabbage. The meatloaf was the bomb digitey!
Over rated total Dive bar.  Felt dirty coming out of there just looking for a place to stand. What's all the rage about??

The burgers and fries here are the best! The smoke from the grill exhaust hood fan smelled awesome!! The smoke stunk all of Broadway! That's  how I found this joint! The jalapeno cheese fritters are good also. They have cool live bands there too. If in the area, I highly recommend checking this place out.
Friendly, rustic, good food, beer could be colder, plenty of liquid refreshment on the  shelf!  Parking limited.

I have never been to a worst place than this place. We came in to have a drink, and after 30 minutes security came to check id's, we gave them our id'e and the guy says those white girls have to go. Security told us to leave the the venue because we weren't  spending enough money at the bar. Honestly, we were have been having an amazing time in Nashville, and this place ruined it. I have never seen just discrimination.

The Sutler is back! A once staple in the Nashville scene is back with a reinvented, retro, image and a stage for live music.  They feature a vintage- southern atmosphere with high end, country, decor (think mismatched black wooden chairs, mason jar water glasses, industrial light fixtures, rustic wood floors) and the best part?? Their stage backdrop is a bunch of cowboy boots!  The service was good and their hand crafted cocktails and local beer selection made for plenty of choices.  I was however a little disappointed in their menu selection.  It was just too eclectic for me and was missing some of the staples I look for when spending $20 on an entree. (Click to view The Sutler's Menu)  We started with the "shrimp double down". It was very good but only 6 shrimp.  We shared the "yes damnit burger dunk" which in my opinion was one of the best burgers I've had in a long time.  The bath of cheddar "dunk" it sat in was also very good.   We also shared the "spinach and rocket waldorf"  basically a salad.  For my taste is was too heavily coated in the mayo-based dressing however Damon really enjoyed it.  For dessert we shared the oatmeal cookie pie in both our opinions it was much better without the lemon zest, on top, which was really over powering.  It was a good overall experience and it would be a great place to see live music! So glad to have another one of a kind restaurant!

Awesome place! My boyfriend and I came here before a Predators game and I'm glad we did. Food was super cheap and really good. There were two sides, one had the bar and stage and the other was more quiet where families can eat. If you wear your Predators gear you can get a free bud light.

Absolutely loved this place. Awesome open space, free wifi, good drinks and snacks and nice people. They have ample parking and tables/sofas. Outside seating area for those who need some sun rays. They do have awesome things for sale on the inside including products from Thistle Farms. If you're thinking Starbucks, skip it and go here. Because let's be honest, who wants to circle the one up the street for 15 minutes looking for parking? The only downside as someone mentioned is the women's restroom.. it's pretty rough.

While visiting Nashville we both agreed this is one of the best places we went to on Broadway.  The view from the top floor is beautiful, I would recommend this place to anyone who loves a crowd and live country music in the bar scene.

We came here for Sunday brunch after attempting to go to another place that had an hour wait. Got there just before they opened at 10 and there was already a line of at least 50 people. We were sat almost immediately, the space is quite large. The servers are NOT stingy with their bottomless mimosas :-). We had chicken and waffles (savory waffle with chives I believe) and pork hash, both were delicious. 
They have the weekend routine down very well. Food was all coming out quickly for having such a rush in the morning. There is also a bluegrass band that plays during brunch, which is an added bonus! The sound and noise level was perfect to have conversation and enjoy brunch.

Wait staff is very friendly and attentive , music last night was not so good.  They had an old guy with white beard and a bunch of younger lady's in back bar and they were so so bad.  Drinks also weak, and pricey

Great atmosphere, food, and drinks.  Tried the fried flounder and it did not disappoint.  The peach cobbler was a sweet southern treat.  Tried two drinks...Sage Advice and Five & Dime.  The later was better.  The live music was just icing on the cake.
Awful wait staff and bartenders. chubby blonde girl .. awful. would not recommend this.bar to anyone! find a new bar!

Seemed cool until the artists were horribly bigoted and mysoginistic. I regret spending money here. It's not funny to make fun of gender disparity, or to write & perform blatantly sexist lyrics about women. The bluebird should do more to keep their artists in check.

Great atmosphere .  Be aware, Very very unfair bouncers.  A very sober friend got kicked out for innocently dancing on a chair.  No warnings or chances given, she had to leave. It really wasn't fair. If she was wasted and incoherent, that's one thing. But she apologized and cooperated saying it wouldn't happen again. Isn't this Nashville? Known as the friendliest town in the world? Come on now
Door what is a piece of s***. Great music great atmosphere but please upgrade your doorman new year new start seriously upgrade it f****** stupid
Very crowded, 3 floors with 3 different style of country music. Top floor was our preferred option. Nothing special about his bar.

Duane really ruined our experience. The food was good, and the drinks were fine, but Duane felt the need to flex his nuts as the all powerful 'bouncer' and ruined the fun for everyone. Duane, chill out.

Okay, so let me preface this with I am 23, I've waited tables over 3 years, and I'm a fairly frequent bruncher. The food here was decent and pretty affordable. I got the breakfast biscuit but honestly I would have been just as happy with McDonald's. The bottomless mimosas were barely refilled and tasted like straight orange juice. Waste of $17. The server seemed really irritated the whole time. We ordered coffee to which she responded "all the cups are dirty." And apparently they were all dirty for the hour we were there. Keep in mind, I'm a server. I try to give servers the benefit of the doubt when i eat out, but she was just plain rude and unaccommodating. It really took away from our experience and overall it was frustrating, I would not recommend this place to anyone.
Loved walking back in time to this iconic place. Sitting at the counter and taking in the scene was so surreal.

The Sutler has returned to Melrose and it does not disappoint. The drinks are prepared with a lot of attention to detail and the food is really good. We had the horseshoe BBQ plates and the hamburger. All of them were very good. The only reason I'm not giving the Sutler 5 stars is when you go to the bar downstairs, there is a distinctive cigarette smell. Because the Sutler doesn't allow smoking, it must be from a previous tenant of the space.

We had a great time here last night.  We made reservations the morning they opened up for our date, and had great seats in the first row near the stage though they were off to the side.  We were surprised in the suburban strip mall location of the venue, but it did make parking easier.

The cafe is quite small and intimate. They do a good job of warning people to stay quiet during the performance (which is crucial in small places like this) and the crowd complied nicely.  The acoustics were fine.

The four singer-songwriters took turns performing some of the older more successful tunes, and some of their newer material.  Some of them were better writers, some better singers, but they were all very talented.

The wait staff was unobtrusive and efficient taking orders and delivering libations and food.  The prices were not ugly, and the food was pretty good for a bar.  I had a BLT, and it was pretty tasty.

What we walked away with was a feeling that we had participated in something that wasn't quite so commercial as other music opportunities in Nashville.  Yes, these musicians are in it to make a living, but clearly their passion for their art came through in the inter-song patter.  We would definitely return!

Yeah 5 stars, cause why the heck not. Yeah maybe pricey drinks, but there's no cover charge...so I feel like it's well worth it. Don't have to get smashed to have a good night here, the music does it!

I did not have any food here, but the service was spectacular (Fenway shirt behind bar) as well as our server.  She was good with timing on drinks and kept a watchful eye on low drinks.  On  my trip to Nashville, i was most happy with this establishment for their service, as well as the quality of live music they had going on at pretty much anytime we went in.  We visited this place 3 times on the trip, usually after trying somewhere else.

Let's just say this first..
you don't go here for the quick service or good food haha. Limited menu, which is overpriced. I think it took us about an hour to get chicken fingers. NO BIGGIE THOUGH... because after the hour wait outside to get into another hour wait line to get inside, we were used to waiting :)

Loved the place. So cool to see in person. It's cozy, for sure. We went on a open mic night and saw about 33 people play one song a piece. Acts varied by...wow I never want to hear that sound again to ..oh I bet we'll see her again! Was super entertained and were seated with two lovely strangers who made it even more fun.

It's worth the wait :)

The employees at this place are major assholes...as the bar was starting to shut down the nice bartender at the top told me I could use the restroom downstairs but as soon as I walked down the security guard starts yelling at me extremely aggressively and telling me the restroom is closed. I explain to him that the bartender upstairs had just now told me I could use the lower restroom but he said he didn't care and I had to go. Keep in mind that this whole time I'm  100% sober - I  haven't even drank alcohol since January. Then as I'm trying to leave a cop is blocking the path talking to a drunk guy. I politely wait instead of trying to push through the cop and he just mimics the security guard, trying to rudely  herd me through the 4 inch space between him and the drunk guy. The only reason I give this place 2 stars is because the venue and music was awesome - but nothing is worth being treated like an incompetent idiot by stupid overly machismo asshole security guards and cops.  I will be letting everyone know about the disappointing experience and warning them about this place. Again, nothing is worth blatantly disrespecting a client and both the management and employees need to seriously re-evaluate their behavior.

Since I heard the Sutler was going to begin having 'Bluegrass Brunch' on the weekends, I've been eyeing my calendar for the perfect Sunday to make a visit. We arrived around 11am, and while I was expecting a wait, I was less than thrilled when we were given a two hour estimate. It wasn't all terrible though, as they allowed us to take advantage of the bottomless mimosas while we waited.

The bartender soon became my best friend after I witnessed her heavy-handed champagne pour that made our wait much more manageable. We were able to find a spot on the patio to sit and chat as observed the rowdy yet laid back atmosphere of the restaurant.

We got seated about 20 minutes before our 2 hours was up and got a table near the stage. The band definitely added a fun ambience as the crowd joined in the chorus of Rocky Top and other well-known bluegrass jams.

I had lost count of how many mimosas we had - the waiter was on top of his pour game as soon as he saw our empty glasses. My boyfriend ordered the breakfast tacos and I had the smoked brisket hash. While we enjoyed our food, it was just okay. My meal was slightly cold and the flavors somewhat bland, but the mimosas more than made up for it. I would be interested in coming back for dinner and at a less busy time.

hm.... drink was $6 ordered a few, paid $6 per drink on my card PLUS i tipped on the card. My bank shows I was billed $7.20 per drink plus my tip... WTF!! PAY CASH HERE

Other than that, its fun place. Bands are hit or miss, but allover its a cool little dive.

Just pay cash.

Let me start off by noting that my review has absolutely zero to do with the food they serve here. It might have been great, it might have been terrible, I absolutely don't remember. What is important is that it is absolutely one of the finest music listening rooms in Nashville, which is kind of saying something. I first went when my younger brother came to visit and I was trying to find cool activities for him to experience outside of the obligatory Grand Ole Opry experience. My roommate recommended Bleubird and I am forever in his debt. You should expect to show up early and wait in line for nightly shows. It is a small venue and it is worth the wait. I ended up coming back three more times after my initial visit and would have liked to be a more frequent visitor if school obligations and financial constraints hadn't been such spoil-sports. Don't expect to come here and chat with your friends, this is a place to listen, not to speak.

Pro-tip: Try and come on a singer/songwriter night and hear the stories behind the lyrics, very enjoyable!

Friendly service, reasonably priced drinks, and a relaxed vibe.  I enjoyed the country band playing as well.  I might have just gotten lucky, but I had no trouble parking in the lot.  Next time I'll come earlier for dinner.

When I think of a honky tonk bar, Tootsie's is what I imagine. It's supposedly the original honky tonk bar on the Broadway strip, but it's well kept and I loved my first visit. We headed straight for the top floor which includes a stage with live music and open air onto a rooftop patio that overlooks Broadway. I bet Tootsie's is regularly crowded, especially on nice days, but the bartenders were generally quick and, despite being out of my favorite Blue Moon, they had a good variety of bottled beers (no drafts, though -- womp womp). The touristy spots aren't usually my thing in Nashville, but if I ever venture back to Broadway, this is where you can find me.

Sometimes you're downtown, and you're in a hurry and don't have time for a sophisticated meal. Well, Paradise Park works, and puts out thoroughly edible, if not inspiring, food at a fair pace. One downside: if any artists are playing, don't expect to carry on a conversation with anyone. The acoustics of this place are such that even if you sit at the furthest possible location your ears will still be annihilated. In spite of this place's devotion to MEAT, my vegetarian friend said the veggie burger was at least passable.

Passable...sometimes that's all you need.

Bartenders are the absolute best.  Bands are entertaining.  Just a fun place to listen, people watch, and have a few longnecks.

My best suggestion - don't grab the front row seats, unless you enjoy "eau de Ladie's room".

Live feed on a webcam, with about a 50 second delay.

Best music, fun, energetic atmosphere. Love the view from the rooftop. Of course it gets crowded but where doesn't it in Nashville- for as many people that do come in those doors- they manage them well.
Yes, it's a dive bar, but I heard a great blues band here tonight!  Lots of tap beer!

Great place to begin (or end) your night of bar-hopping. The great thing about all the honky tonks on Broadway is that it's super easy to pick up and jump somewhere else when you get tired of sitting. Great musicians, fun crowd interaction, and cheap, cold beer. What more could you ever ask for?

Look fellas I love the bar. Great jams. But the double vodka soda left something to be missed. Just wasn't a great in my book. Some other people may have different opinions. That's what makes this country great.

This is a great place for an early pre-theatre dinner or for relaxing with a cocktail. Their fried chicken was perfectly crisp and served with the three best southern sides-green beans, mashed potatoes and spicy Mac and cheese.  Their pickled shrimp appetizer is lovely, garnished with fresh avocado and pickled veggies.  The atmosphere is delightful, with a lunch counter, booths and tables downstairs and a great mezzanine for appetizers and drinks.  Service was friendly and fairly fast, even though we got there just as dinner set up was starting!

Having had the opportunity to travel to Nashville for business and for pleasure, there is nothing quite like honkey tonking!  When you step in, you feel the history and smell the beer and sweat of songwriters and artists making it.  This place is a must see when visiting as well as many of the other places nearby!

Steve Smith, the owner of Tootsies, recently bought and demolished a 100+ year old building listed on the National Historic Register (formerly located at 2nd and Broadway) literally in the dark of night.  Go ahead and support him with your tourist dollars if you must, but be aware you are contributing to the destruction of the history of this town y'all claim to love to visit so much.

(6/23/2014) It's trashy, sticky, gimmicky, and I thought I'd hate this place, but ended up there two nights in a row.  There's plenty of space, we enjoyed the band, the drinks were cheap.  There was basically and 80s/90s cover band playing your usual frat party faves from a spectrum of country/Southern rock/alt rock.  So wish I had enough room for a corn dog, love that there's basically a fry shack in the middle of the bar, and a beaten down convertible (warning, you're going to need to decon if you get in that thing).  Monday is apparently 2-for-1 beer night (did I mention place is cheap)?  Enjoy cuttin' the astroturf rug.
No

Love this place!! It is a must every time I go to Nashville. Perfect combination of food and bar without being too crowded and annoying like some places in downtown Nashville. Plus they have a full size car inside the bar just for fun!

The atmosphere was cool and historic.  Our server was kind of snotty and didn't seem like she wanted to be there.  I was disappointed in the food.  Granted I went to a southern restaurant and ordered a salad.  The lettuce was very clearly from a bag.  I added chicken to the salad for an addition $6 and maybe got 6 cubes of chicken. There was very little blue cheese on the salad.  Overall it seemed like the skimped on all the toppings and size of their portions, but still charge a decent price. Over priced food seemed to be a theme here. I left disappointed, even though the space itself was really interesting.  I live in Germantown and would love to have a great restaurant Downtown to take guests to when they come and visit.  Woolworth on 5th will not be that place.

This place should go through bar rescue. They were busting the bags of ice they use in drinks on the pavement bumpy the alley entrance. Totally against food safety regulations. And I have no idea why the fire marshal hasn't shut them down for occupancy violations yet. 
The music was good but it was so packed you couldn't even dance.and by packed I mean people crushing together chest to back.
So disappointing! I've experienced two lousy brunches, and I would never go back! There is no treason to wait an hour for cold mediocre food.

A must see if you're ever in Nashville. I gave it four stars for the atmosphere and the music. I felt pressured order food so got some chips and salsa. Don't go there for the food just go there for the drinks and music.

After realizing my initial review of this place three years ago highlighted some of the grand-opening kinks, which have since all been worked out, I'm updating my review. I really like this place. The food is very good, always with a nice vegetarian option. The beer list is interesting, and the atmosphere is unique and welcoming. I like the little biergarten-esque patio out back. The servers are always nice. And I love having another place to go on the west side.

Great time in the back room.  Band was good, singer was good, I was entertained.  It's what you'd expect from a bar.  Overpriced drinks and a fun loving, boot stomping group on the stage, plus drunk people ogling the bartenders.  Had fun and I'd go back, but I'd leave early again because I don't like being claustrophobic.

I'm curious to see how this place will do once the novelty wears off. It'll probably succeed because the atmosphere is nice and the staff is fantastic. The food is only ok, but nothing special. They have all these games available, but half the controllers or games don't work. It can be frustrating.

Amazing service! They are quick and extremely friendly!  We just happened to stumble across this looking for a place without an hour and half wait! Food was great! I would recommend this historical and yummy place!

Delicious and a nice surprise- interesting decor although a bit dark for me for lunch. BUT that would be the only negative. My salad was perfect including all of my favorites. Creamy goat cheese, candied pecans, sweet potatoes, grilled chicken with a maple vinegarette dressing. The service was attentive but not intrusive. 4 refills of my Arnold Palmer was appreciated! Beautiful bar and interesting decor. Would recommend!

Really fun place with an awesome rooftop patio. Perfect for day drinking. 

I don't usually drink anything besides beer...but this place has a fantastic strawberry daiquiri that I highly recommend. 

Service was ok. It was busy so it's understandable they were moving a little slower. 

The live bands were tremendous!
Stopped in for a late night burger and ordered the bacon cheeseburger. It was pretty middle of the road. Nothing special at all. Probably won't be back. There are much better options in the area.
Great music and a fun place to be.  The food service is a bit strange in that you order and pick up yourself at the bar.  But the food was good "bar food".

Dinner look and feel. Average food and service. Berger and fries peeped well and to order.
Whey back again to try appetizers,  to make a fair assessment,  average,  as to be expected.
Food served quick and hot,
Had gumbo ( Yum) need a bowl of that, filled with Brussels that is a sure add on to your next meal.
Service over all was plesent and not at all rushed. 
This was and OK spot for lunch.
Great atmosphere. Best grilled cheese I've ever had, hands down. We also had the Yardbird salad which was equally as delicious!

I felt like I had to go inside Tootsie's to make my Nashville experience complete, but honestly it was much more hyped up than was actually warranted. The main problem was that there were WAY too many people let inside at once so it was almost impossible to move around & really enjoy the space. The live music and rooftop area was fun, but really, as a whole, it was a little bit of a disappointment.

Highlight of our Nashville trip.  We were lucky to get tickets, that we know, and it's as good as you'd hope it would be.  Kind of like seeing Hamilton when you're in NYC as far as the buzz factor, but once you're seated, it seems like it's just magical music taking you to a place you thought you were too old or too busy to remember.  Great service and buy a tee shirt, they are so cool and so soft!

We'd been to many of the bars/clubs along Broadway during our stay in the city, and hadn't gone in here because the bands playing when we passed by didn't seem very good. But, our tour bus guide today suggested we stop in because it's supposed to have more history than any of the other places. Yup, lots of history on the walls, but we weren't impressed by any of the three bands on the three floors. They've also got the most expensive beer prices in the city ($6 for a Bud Light bottle!). It was really crowded when we went in, considering it was mid-afternoon on a Thursday. We decided to go directly upstairs instead of standing and bumping elbows with the crowd downstairs. As we got to the stairs the bartender comes out from around the bar and grabs my arm and says "do you want a drink?". Not knowing the layout, and thinking this may be the only bar in the place, I get our beers from her. We saw her do that a couple more times with people going upstairs. Turns out there's a bar at each floor, and she was just grabbing the orders (and tips) from the people passing through before they got to the next floor. If I were the other bartenders I'd be pissed.

If you're on the second floor you get the sound of the band there, but you also hear the band on the first floor. Very poor acoustics.

If we knew before what we know now, we would have walked in, taken a couple of quick pictures, and then visited any one of the other places on Broadway that seem to have better bands, better acoustics, better prices, and less crowded.

This place was awesome. We spent 5 days in Nashville and went here 3 times. Entertainment was great every time on every level. Service was slow on the upper patio we had to ask the waitress for a drink after 4 tables of people who sat down after us were served. Drinks were well mixed (strong like we like). People watching is also amazing there too. Bartenders on lower bar level we found to be more attentive.
Best place to eat after a night out on Broadway!!! They stay open til 4am! One of the best burgers & tots I've ever tasted!!

A pretty hip joint. Great mood lighting and the place just glows. Perfect for people watching and not pretentious. Drink specials are cool. Decent bar. Cool for live music from Nashville hipsters. I think a pitcher of PBR is $9.
Depraved place with live music but there's like two areas that is very crowded. The bathrooms are very dirty and it is dificult to even line up. The drinks are all right.
One of the best burgers. TV playing college football and live music too. Tots were great too.

The Sutler (downstairs) is a eclectic, cozy, jazzy vibe setup that offers a huge bar pretty decent food and great vibe to it. The bar stretches the length of the room and then some! there are comfy sofas and chairs that immerse the candle lit atmosphere ideal for conversations on any level. Bartenders are efficient and prompt. Drinks were not to strong or weak...just right for me. The music is of different variety and at a level that invites conversation and a chill mood. 

I ain't gonna lie I did not want to leave!! :( so definitely looking forward to returning!

Amazing.  I was very skeptical when we went in.  But wow. Chris was our server and though there for only a week knew his products very well.  I had the big Blt sandwich with side salad with the jalepino  ranch dressing.  Extraordinary and even though the sandwich was large it held together and the favors were balanced  the salad dressing which is home made was excellent.   Long story short the drinks were properly proportioned and yes  the drinks and dinner while on the higher price level were actually priced correctly for the quality and portion.   I will be back

Very nice. Ask yourself how often can you eat in a historic place? The waiter was very helpful, gave some samples of local beers to choose from and gave some nice explanation about the building and it's history. And now comes the best : all of the above combined with great food ( i had the ribs :-) ) but see for yourself

I am currently at the Bobby Jones Gospel show and this event was very misleading from the advertisement.  The tickets that my family & I purchased advertised the show from 1-3pm.  I traveled to meet family from Kentucky and be here by 12:45pm. Only to be told that the doors open at 1pm and show starts at 2pm.

Then once seated in the New Era Ballroom I Ordered the 2 pigs small bites only to be told by the bartender that she didn't know if any of the small bites were available.  She later brought me the small entree and it was ice cold.    Who in their right mind would eat ice cold pulled pork and ice cold corn bread?  

I am very disappointed in the overall service of the restaurant and also the food selection.  What a disappointment to an overly hyped up new restaurant in Nashville.



Update:

So basically the Manager contacted me from my Yelp review and "promised to make it right". However what was promised was never received.  I will never + my inner circle will never return to this restaurant.  It sucks because I love the history and culture BUT it's not managed by the right people!!!'
Food was very good. Service at the bar was really bad. The bartender was rude. The waiter disappear for a long time. Service needs to improve.

I went to Nashville for the weekend and was able to book tickets for the Saturday night show.  I absolutely loved it!  We watched Dennis Matkosky, Greg Barnhill, Chris Nathan, and Gary Nicholson.  They were all amazing!  I felt like I was at an MTV Unplugged thing or something, except much closer!  =)

So a couple tips.  Tickets went on sale the Monday before the show at 8am (local time).  Tickets pretty much sold out within 5 minutes.  I recommend getting to the website a minute or two before 8am and keep refreshing until you see the button to buy tickets.  Don't ponder over the seating chart too long, because others are too!  Click a table and reserve it as soon as you can!  They charge $2 for each reserved seat and you pay the entrance fee when you arrive.  

So the night of the event, there is a small parking lot with free parking.  We parked in the lot next to it because the lot was full.  Our car was still there, so that was good.  There is one line for reserved seats and another line for waiting list.  Make sure you stand in the right one!  They don't open the door until the show time.  

There's a $7 minimum for food/drinks.  Not bad at all!  We had the sweet potato fries, and they were delicious.  

I would definitely go back to Bluebird Cafe.  Great set up, great entertainment, and great people!

I'm being completely honest when I say I won't be returning to The Sutler for the food. This was my second time dining and it was completely different from the first time I dinned for a birthday party. The menu was different, décor was different and the service was different. 

Remembering the food we had originally was what brought us back. We discovered shortly the menu was completely different and it didn't even offer the same items we were looking for. Disappointing. I ordered the Pulled Chicken Sandwich with a side of Jalapeno Mac and Cheese. The Mac and Cheese was on point...very delicious. The sandwich on the other hand was a giant bun with 3, literally 3, bites of pulled chicken and maybe an oz. of sauce. Very dry and flavorless. I've been low carb and was planning on eating just the meat so this was a huge disappointment for a $12 sandwich. When I mentioned my disappointment in regards to the amount of meat our server didn't care. I ended up ordering the chicken wings in hopes to get more protein. The menu describes them as wings Alabama white sauce style. When they arrived at the table within 2 minutes of my ordering (this concerned me) I just shook my head. They were completely plain with a side of ranch and a few celery sticks. I was so hungry at this point I tried picking through them for the meat...so gross I could only eat two. 
My husband got the steak sandwich, he also agreed that he wouldn't be returning for the food ever again. A grand total of $108 for 5 bites of chicken, a small side of mac and cheese, a steak sandwich with collard greens. 2 glasses of wine, 4 beers, and 1 shot of Jack Daniels, and 20% tip seems crazy high!

The service was a 4 out of 10. Unenthusiastic about everything, literally. Didn't care about the lack of meat on my sandwich or the fact that the sandwich and the wings were completely sauce-less. I'm never one to give less than 20% but this guy will remain nameless b/c I'm hoping he was just having a bad day. We've all been there.
 
On one positive note: Happy hour goes until 7pm..1/2 off Specialty Drinks, Beer, and Wine. 

Live music, drinks, and décor is what's keeping this place alive. Don't waste your time or money on the food.

My new favorite Nashville restaurant! It's a chill ambiance with great food. Their pickles are homemade and just like grandma's. The veggie burger, fries, and chocolate cake were incredible. Great little restaurant bar.
Love Tootsies!! Spent a few hours here tonight. We sat on the rooftop deck and enjoyed listening to a great band. One of our go-to places on Broadway! Always a good time.

This place was a lot of fun when I was in Nashville for the Half Marathon in Apr 2014.The place was jumping and each of the 3 floors had live music - a real pleasure to experience as an out-of-towner.  The bar has a nice outdoor balcony on the top floor.

The band was a little pushy asking for tips and wanting patrons to pay $20 per song request.  Other than that, the place was a lot of fun and I'd go back again.

Get there early! No, no time is too early!

Wish I could be here every night of the week. It's in a dinky strip mall that looks older than it is (1982), but man, the ambiance is incredible. It truly is a special place! Songwriters share their music and it is magical. 

I recommend you attend the Alive at the Bluebird series benefiting Live Hospice. It's a good cause.

Food: you don't go for the food, but if you have to eat, chicken fingers weren't bad. Dont recommend the BLT.

Going here raised my expectation of what Mac & cheese should taste like. I'm not trying to be dramatic, but it's sort of life changing. 
The triple guacamole appetizer was excellent as well.

This place was super busy at 11am. The hostess quoted us for 80 minutes, but we only waited 40 min, which was an awesome surprise! When we sat down, the server came over quickly and brought us a basket of biscuits with an assortment of jams. We ordered cocktails and water, which were delivered within a few minutes. And after we ordered our entrees, our food came out in about 10 minutes. I ordered the brisket hash and it was very flavorful. I was very impressed with the quickness of our dining experience, considering how busy they were for brunch!

This is MY bar, and no I don't mean that I own it, but I love it like a child I sprung straight from my womb. I have never had anything other then an amazing A+++ time here. 

Conversation that happens almost everyday:

Me: Where do you want to go for dinner? 
Husband: Hm, what do you want?
Me: I want to go to Stone Fox

And off we go. Honestly, this place is the best. The food, the amazing (and strong!) cocktails can't be beat, the staff is friendly and attentive... the back patio is great for enjoying good weather, the bands they book are TOP NOTCH... what more could a gal ask for? Throw in a few friends (which are easy to make here and I've met MANY!) and it's a recipe for a rollocking good time. Thank you Stone Fox for being so awesome. I love you and will see you tonight.

Visited on a Thursday evening. The place was full of obviously inebriated and loud students. I felt out of place. The food was not very tasty and the servers were not very pleasant.  It seemed to me that they paid more attention to the college students and ignored the more mature individuals.  I don't think I will be back.
Accidentally found this place while in Nashville for a wedding.  Incredible coffee, reasonable prices, and a friendly staff.  I will make a special trip there next time I'm in Nashville.

Food was ok. Server was visibly not interested in waiting on us. Bathrooms were disgusting. Toilets were overflowing when I first came in. I advised a staff member. I went again after my meal and nothing had changed. I'd go elsewhere.

Impressed!  Great place to dine when attending a show at TPAC but plan ahead by making reservations.  Interesting menu and attentive service.  Large portions, tasty cocktails--yum!  Wish I had room for dessert...But the icing on the cake is the atmosphere! I love the vintage vibe and the live entertainment in the ballroom downstairs.  Will definitely be back.

This is an experience not to be missed.  I am so glad we got to experience it.  We had my father attending with us so we went to the early show on a Wednesday night.  The reservation system is easy to use.  We got onto the site 8am one week prior to the day we wanted to attend.  We had no issue getting three seats at a table. The staff was friendly.  The history of the place is wonderful.  It all went by so fast.  There is a minium drink per seat but easy to meet with one drink.  The fee was $2 per seat to get tickets on their reservation system.  I also got a very cute comfortable tshirt long sleeve for $30.  I didn't know it as the time but it has "Shhhhh" on the back.  Make time to experience this place while in Nashville.  There is not enough parking so be prepared to walk.
Fantastic!! What a great place to hang out, sip a yummy drink and have a bite to eat. The staff was very friendly and the music was great! A must see when visiting Nashville!!

Don't expect good service unless your sporting an ironic mustache or are roommates/dating a server. Completely ignored at the bar with only one other patron sitting there.  Three decent beers on tap and a pbr handle. I'd drive further for better service and live music if I had a choice.

Thought I walked into a bad bourbon street bar. First floor band didn't play any country - bad covers of twisted sister, Adele, and Cranberries. Performers kept yelling about how much they were getting tipped to play these songs and they didn't even really know the words. Over priced bad juke box. I've always heard about the greats who played at Tootsies. Really disappointed that the new generation is tarnishing a country music institution.

Solid burger, good fries and tots, perfect for a casual meal.  Great atmosphere with live music coming into the room through connected bar (we were there for lunch).  Would definitely return on our next trip!
View of Nashville from the top floor is awesome.  We were there for the Blackhawks vs. Nashville playoff game and it was really crowded.  Service was good but slow because of the crowd.
Best bar for fun and live music on Broadway!! It's a blast to have drinks upstairs on a sunny day. It's always a must visit. You never know what kind of amazing talent you will see!
Great live bands and cold beer. If you are looking for a historic dive bar you found it.

Found myself here almost every night during my time in Nashville. It's seriously the place to be! Three floors ( and a rooftop) of awesome and talented musicians and singers! Drinks are a little bit expensive --$6 miller light! But they do have specials! Don't forget to sign the wall and make a photo strip in the photo booth. Love Tootsie's!!!

1 Star. Came at 3:30 pm on New Year's Eve. Sign said it opened at 5. Waited at a pub for 1.5 hours. Came to stand in line until open and worker said it did not open until 6. We waited in 19 degree weather. This is not how you treat fans and customers.

I really wanted to like you this place...love the historical significance and the setting is like being back in time, but the food was so-so. I ordered the fried chicken salad and the first version came out with the chicken cold/room temperature . I asked if it was supposed to be cold; the server said no, took the salad and tested with her finger. For a split second thought she was going to disagree with me and say it wasn't cold (it wasn't cold like straight out of the refrigerator but not at all warm). Anyway, she brought out a new salad. This time the chicken was nice and warm but unfortunately it was very dry. The rest of the salad was unimpressive. My husband got the brisket sandwich and said it was "ok". Not sure we'll give it another chance...too many other places to try to risk mediocre food.
$8 cover per person on a Thursday night.  Didn't appear to be busy or have a band.  No thanks.
This is such a gross bar, and it's so stressful inside because it's packed, but we had a great time singing along with the band on the second floor that was playing on Friday night.

After what happened to my Daughter's boyfriend, I will never step foot in this racist owned establishment ever again. I will speak badly of this place whenever I am asked about it. I will strongly encourage all of my friends to stay away from this place. Great message from Tootsie's management, racism is alive and well in Tootsie's!
Great food, hipster vibe (meh), but poor service. The food keeps me coming back time and time again.

This place was number one on my list of places I wanted to go when I got to Nashville. I will say get their early as if you don't have reservations seating is limited. We arrived about two hours before the show started and were one of the last groups to get into the door. The day of our visit they were doing a "in the round" so instead of a stage the performers  were set up in a circle in the middle of the room that made for a really intimate feel. It kinda felt like they were just hanging out and singing and we got to watch. There was some awesome original country music happening and I'm glad I got to be a part of it. There is a minimum order you have to make but it's no different than like a comedy club. One appetizer and drink later I was well over the minimum. The only thing that disappointed me was that the artist weren't allowed to use like square readers for people to buy their music. I never carry cash so I just ended up buying stuff on iTunes later. Great job blue bird you made this country music lover very happy.

My friend was looking for this place all night, easy to get in and out of with the bottom
Bar well within reach. Didn't wait long for a table, if you are going bring a sharpie so you can leave you mark. Very unique crowd and had a girl singing on the bar, overall great time

We went to Tootsie's on week night, so the crowd wasn't big, which disappointed me. The Apple moonshine is REALLY good but not real moonshine. One of the bartenders made a drink for me with the moonshine that was good and she was really friendly and I even helped her sell a few of the drinks to some girls. The band upstairs was terrible, but the band on the first floor was really good and really entertaining. The history of Tootsie's is really what is cool about this place.

very quick service. the place was packed on a thursday night and as I was wondering how my husband and i were even going to get past so many people to order a drink, the bartender stood up, hollered and asked us what we needed? we had a beer in our hands within 2 minutes of being in the bar. impressive, especially considering how many people are in there. 3 levels with 3 different acts. our favorite was the top level due to both the band and the atmosphere.. it is a little wierd that the band goes around groveling for tips but that seemed to be a consistent nashville theme. overall, beers will run you about $5 a piece. no cover. great roof top. wouldnt eat here but drinking was just fine.

My husband and I have decided this is our favorite "neighborhood" bar/hangout. They could get 5 stars out of me if they had earlier weekday hours for us parents that have to do "day dates ."  Beyond the fact that this place is just cool, the food is great (also local,) staff is friendly & fun ensues at the Stone Fox! We love their Sunday Brunch (chicken & waffles rock) good craft beers, and nightly live music. They let our grumpy 1 yr old run around pushing barstools till he tuckered out; priceless!

Dangerous and ignorant establishment. Security was a joke and didn't care that people were getting cut with glass, fighting, and kept continuing to do so for hours. Our group notified the security person on the floor we were on (3rd floor on 05/26) that ONE group was continually starting fights with random people and he just laughed. When we questioned why he was laughing he then decided to call someone that would actually do something. 

Our group and multiple others left because they didn't feel safe and despite knowing what was happening for hours, the security up there did nothing. Wouldn't recommend going here unless you're looking for trouble.
Tons of history. Live music. Overpriced drinks. Smarmy waitress. But it's a must see in Nashville.

We went here with a bunch of Yelp Elite people on our yelp elite spring break. they have a few floors, try to see if you can get on the top floor as they have great bands playing there and there's also an outdoor portion. There's no cover which is great, but apparently the bands don't get paid, so when you see a jar or hat going around, try to contribute.

I would come back here if ever in the area, it's very conveniently located so it was our second stop on our bar crawl.

Went on a Sunday afternoon and had the BEST time! It was insanely crowded but spirits were high and it just felt like we were joining in on the fun. It took a minute to get drinks but considering the crowd I didn't mind.

The top level/ roof was awesome (it was pouring rain and they had to close some of the open doors) but they cranked up the air conditioner which was an appreciated perk.

The bands had a lot of energy and played a lot of crowd favorites. I'm so impressed with the way these musicians hustle in Nashville!!
Sat at the bar 10 minutes with the bartender text and talked to the delivery guy. Never even acknowledged me. F on service

My husband and I tried it around 9pm on a Friday night and the food, drinks and service were all excellent! We happened to catch the Sutler Saloon String Band and they were fantastic as well! The guacamole trio appetizer is bomb. We also split the gumbo and brisket tacos and were impressed with the explosive flavor of both. I recommend their mules and their specialty cocktails...we loved everything we tried. My only complaint is that it's pretty expensive, but we did know that going in.

Again with the tourist trap places where a ton of old people hang out, trying to be young. 

Don't get me wrong, I'm not an ageist. Being in my (upper) 30's, I know that there is a time and place for certain bars and clubs for me, and I also would like to believe that I act accordingly (prior to a few adult beverages). Tootsie's was another place that was recommended to us by our taxi driver. He must work for this bar and Legend's because both were awful. They were jam packed with an older crowd, like no standing room to breathe....let alone grab a beer. Ughh...

There was a bouncer standing out front with a velvet rope, as if this place was THE place to be. We did have to wait until a couple of people left prior to going inside. We quickly assessed the situation, and left immediately. The band was playing death metal to adults my parents' age. 

It was all just a bad dream...I'm convinced.

The atmosphere is worth it, the bar is fantastic, I'm glad people really have a discovered it, because you can usually get in no problem. This is my go to place for events downtown, close, but not overcrowded yet.

Ok first off this building is amazing.  I love that they restored as much of the old Woolworth that was left. I hate that I was so hungry that I forgot to take photos of our breakfast orders because they were beautifully presented and they tasted even better than they looked. I had the corn beef and hash with a scrambled egg and my breakfast companion had eggs your way which came with potatoes and bacon. He is not a potato lover but these were so good he ordered more. Definitely worth the trip to eat in this wonderful piece of history. I know I will return next time I will try the lunch menu.
Great honky-tonk! The wait staff is super efficient. I had a veggie burger that came out super good. The band played some "real country" songs that were marvelous.

Not at all what I hoped for. Beyond mediocre food that was overpriced for what you get, and fried corn fritters that weren't salted let alone cooked all the way through. The restaurant was freezing and fortunately the waitress who agreed, asked someone to turn the a/c off/down but still took awhile for that happen. My napkin with silverware opened to a load of ground pepper. Surprise!  So much fun!  The waitress got me a new setting and said "that is bizarre".  Dude with dreads holding a dirty plate nearly walked in to me, on my way to the bathroom (which had peeling wall paper, over flowing trash can, and what looked likenfeces on the floor) and was so rude that I wanted to get past him. Here I thought, "Oh, cool new place to take  the wife to for her birthday!"   Yah, never again. 
Also, manager or owner came by to ask if any of us would be leaving hungry, and I couldn't hear him. Had to ask him to repeat himself because the setting is so ridiculously loud and uncomfortable. His response was to order more. What?!?
Be surprised if this spot survived the end of the year.  The "chef" has some work to do and the set-up is terrible. Appreciate the fact they wanted to restore some of the original appearance but its not conducive to the environment they are hoping for.  
Went downstairs for the free live entertainment and they were dunzo at 8:30. Oh, was charged $10 for the Argentinian Malbec that's listed on the menu for $9.

This bar is so bad, it's good. It's name is so fitting especially with the big guy with blue overalls on working the door.  Green carpet flows throughout the building and I'm pretty confident it is full of many nights of regret. If only the walls could talk... Lol  :P. There was a live band and tons of people dancing, drinking and enjoying life.  Best part, there is a car (yes a car) parked in the middle of the floor... you can get in the back and dance or whatever. Makes for a great photo! The drinks were sub par but you should definitely come for experience.

Having only 1 evening in Nashville, my boyfriend and I were trying to get the full "Down South" experience.  Taking the recommendation of a friend, we came to Tootsies after having a nice meal at The Southern.  We walked in around 9pm on a Friday night and knew we came to the right place.  While the place was pretty packed, it wasn't hard to get a drink at the back bar.  We opted for the music in the front bar and were really impressed by how amazing the musicians voice was.  The talent made it easy to overlook the fact that this was truly just a dive bar through and through.  The crowd was a good mix of young and old music lovers and a few people sang along to every song.
We ended up bar hopping after just 45 minutes at Tootsies but I wish we had spent most of the evening at Tootsies.  The music was great and the service was fast at the bar. If you are in Nashville, Tootsies is a must-see.  It didn't feel touristy and gave us a great memory of this music town.  Stay for a few hours because this really trumps all of the other bars in downtown.

One of my favorite bars I've ever been to. I've been to Nashville twice and both times I went multiple times. The bands are always great and interactive. The food was delicious and fast. The drinks were great and so was the staff! Highly recommend

This was a really cool set up for a bar. Live music was playing on every single level. Soooo crowded inside on every level and there was little room to move from place to place. Got drinks quickly and the bathroom attendant was so nice and great!

This is one of the most recommended bars in nashville.  It was also recommended to bring a sharpie to write your name/s on the walls. It's a fun place esp if you are a college student, bachelorette, or to watch football and listen to live bands.  It's a huge place of 3 floors with an outdoor/rooftop area.

The floors are sticky and the place and bathrooms are dirty, but hey, it's a bar.  The beer is expensive.  I think $5-8.  I wasn't able to try any mixed drinks, but they seem to have a good selection.  The bartenders we had were not very attentive and messed up some orders.

THE biggest drunk shitshow you will ever witness (present company included).  Stroll in there and step back in time with wood paneled walls, hard-sided booths, and short-order cooks who probably hate serving drunk people.  Almost everything is fried...so of course we got chili cheese fries, onion rings (I think), and a club sandwich.  The fries and rings were standard issue...but the club...holy smokes, it was frickin delicious.  Yes I was drunk but I know a good club sandwich when I taste one.  No alcohol is served there...thank god.  Best people watching after 2am.

Love this place!!  We walked in for breakfast at 8am on a Friday and were the only ones there (it was almost full by the time we left and apparently that's normal, so get there early).   Grabbed a couple seats at the counter, were helped immediately by a friendly server, coffee was good, food was fantastic and my husband said the biscuits and gravy were some of the best he's ever had.  The history and incredible significance of this place makes eating here even more special and we appreciated the care and detail and respect the owner took in renovating.  
We decided to come back for happy hour on the mezzanine level - great atmosphere, a mod podge of vintage seating areas, our server was nice, and the drinks were good (but admittedly, a little pricey and their happy hour "specials" weren't that great of a deal but I'd still recommend stopping by).  They also have a live music venue in the basement, btw.

Was incredibly excited about experiencing the legendary Bluebird and had an overall great experience. Only downsides were the food and the seating. The food menu didn't offer too much, but I ended up getting the chicken salad club. It was a cold sandwich and was surprisingly pretty good. It was served with their homemade chips which I did not like. They could definitely work on the food, but then again, that's not what you go to the bluebird for. 

I got my ticket pretty last minute, so I didn't have many options on seating. But I was not aware that I would be seated basically behind a pole. The staff gave me a second option right off the bat (because there was one more empty seat), but it ended up being fine looking around the pole. Just be mindful of making reservations early on so you can get a great seat!

Breakfast. What a find. Old Woolworth 5&10 renovated to a restaurant. Cool interior. Like a large diner. We stopped by for breakfast. Huge seating area. No line, lol! 
The sweat potato pancakes are 5*. 
The bacon crisp and terrific. 5*
I normally don't like biscuits and gravy. The gravy here is spot on 5*. It has chunks of sausage and the serving size is small but perfect as it is very rich. 
Biscuits are good, small but I like this serving size. 
The Service struggled as a waiter was sent home as he was not feeling good. 3* 
Manager stepped up and was very attentive. 4*
Folks a terrific breakfast, great history, terrific venue for breakfast anyway. 
We would definitely come back.

We stopped in for a beer and listen to a few songs. The place was packed, which is the norm. It was a good crowd, even though it was shoulder-to-shoulder, everyone was nice and not pushy. $5 for a Coors Light bottle but no cover so it sorta cancels out? Good spot to start bar hopping down the street.

Shame on you Sutler. I ordered the chicken and waffles and my fiancé ordered the chicken fried chicken biscuits. The chicken was so over cooked there was barely any meat and the meat that was left was so dry it would practically turn to dust once you bit into it. Pictures attached. One of the tenders wasn't even edible and NOTHING was done. The chicken should have went from the fryer to the trash. Even when the manager or who I thought was the manager walked by and saw me blatantly taking a picture of the"chicken" nothing was said. My fiancé's chicken also met the same fate and we were charged $30+ for food that wasn't edible, most expensive cornmeal waffle and biscuits and gravy I've ever purchased. To top it all off, I would have to go to the bar to get drinks 50% of the time. The ONLY reason I give 3 stars is the outstanding service the bartenders provided. If we would have sat at the bar the entire trip I would have been a 5 just for the hospitality they treated us with. My fiancé was so excited to come here for her birthday and the bartenders are the only people who made the experience enjoyable. Long story short, don't order anything with chicken, and stay away from their "Mexican" food.

Just your standard bar, but the food is a step-up from your regularly bar food. 
I hear you may run into a celebrity here, but I haven't seen any.
I would recommend going to an OUTDOOR concert here, inside is a little too small for a large concert crowd, although they do have a stage inside.
Went to Bingo on a Tuesday evening, hurry because it fills up fast, although they move VERY-VERY slowly... so plan on drinking a lot or bringing fun friends to be entertained because the Bingo alone doesn't cut it as entertainment.
The food is great but the friendliness and service is particularly awful. Good luck if you're a woman.

I have been enjoying The Sutler for several months now.  It seems to get better every time.   The food reads like a normal menu, but it's the specific way in which they prepare the food which makes standard classics like Reuben's and BLT's become unique and eclectic versions of themselves.  Today, we had the brunch, and it was by far my favorite visit yet.   The brisket hash with collared greens was perfect.  It balanced sweet with saltiness and a little spicy kick.  Just perfect.   Sunday brunch includes a Bloody Mary bar, bottomless mimosas, and a bluegrass band.  The atmosphere is well thought out.  It can be upper echelon or a fancy dive depending on the attitude you carry for yourself.  Perception is everything and this place will challenge that view. It's completely Nashville, perfect for locals and visitors alike!
It s a good bar with decent beers. But on Fridays and Saturday night mostly have a DJ and plays a lot of popular songs. But it does get extremely crowded to a point where u can't move

It was PACKED when we went in there, wall to wall packed. The floor was disgusting and covered in other peoples spilled drinks and vomit. You could barely enter without bumping into someone. I got a key lime pie alcoholic beverage which I downed before getting two screwdrivers. I only drank half of my screwdriver before I started to feel slightly nauseous. So I left and after being outside of there I began to feel better. 

It felt like I was sitting right next to a car at a stoplight who had their base up all the way! It beat against my body and my stomach. You couldn't hear anyone talking so you had to practically scream in order to talk to someone. Very annoying. The band is RIGHT NEXT to the door, so as soon as you enter you are bombarded with sound. This place is NOT for people who are sensitive to loud noises or are claustrophobic. Regardless even if I do end up going back to Nashville I am not going to that bar ever again!

((Made sure that this was the actual location I went to. The one I posted previously was at the wrong location. Sorry about that.))
3 floors, 3 bars, 3 different bands who are all amazing.  Drinks are pricey but you are paying for atmosphere.

We are new to the neighborhood and stopped here on our first night in.  We can't wait to make this a regular place.  Was pleasantly surprised by prices for really quality food.  My boyfriend's burger was phenomenal and so was the kitchen sink mac.  I love that they put enough veggies in there that it doesn't feel heavy and easily made 2 meals for me.  My only complaint is there is too much bread on the pimento cheese app, however the pickle it came with are great, ask for extras!!!  We sat at the bar, bartender was informative about the neighborhood while still allowing us a date night.  Great ambiance!

Perfect late night food! It was my first time in Nashville and I ate there both nights, which normally would be embarrassing but it's really the only quick late night food available on Broadway. I got the patty melt and the sweet potato fries were the best I've ever had! Be prepared to wait in line when the bars start closing but it's worth it!
i liked the live music here and the appetizers were all right. It was a bit dim and crowded- the only drink i got was belgian ale and it was all right

I just had to change my original post. Tin roof is good for multiple things the perks I've experienced over the few times I've gone: going out and dancing/partying in the upstairs bar area, catching/playing a show (writers round) downstairs, and the Monday night social.  It's a great way to network and hang with other songwriters& artists. I judged this place too quickly off of one visit a couple months ago and for some reason I could not find a way to delete my original review. I still have yet to try the food! Prices seem good, drinks are pretty strong!

Ok, well I've got a purse full o pork, I'm from New York and I didn't know what song I was dancing to but it was an amazing time. I would highly recommend this venue for a variety ( 2 floors of live entertainment) of musical fun.

My parents came in town to visit us and we were excited to bring them here to try this place out since it was new and seemed to have a cool vibe. We ordered the Brussels as an appetizer and the portion was tiny and they didn't have much flavor. I ordered the braised short rib, after the waiter told me that it was delicious and fell apart on your fork. Our food came out very quickly, which normally is good, but it almost seemed too quick for the meal to have been cooked, so it seemed likely that they had it already made and just reheated it. My pork was very tough and did not taste that good. The corn side that came with it was pretty good, fortunately. As cool as the atmosphere was, the food was subpar and overpriced. As my father said - "Cracker Barrel with expensive wine." Hopefully it's just because it's still new and they are working out the kinks, but I would not recommend it.
Don't ask for water with your drinks they charge two dollars for a small plastic cup of water. Oh but wait she said you get free refills. Really!!!!! Wha charges for water. I guess this place

I normally come here just for happy hour, but I noticed they added a hot catfish taco to their menu so I was slightly intrigued. Let's just say I was not disappointed. You only get two tacos. The kale peanut slaw was a delicious addition. And the cup of tomato soup was good. My girlfriend had the crispy zucchini tacos and she enjoyed it. I've been wanting to try the Mac n cheese, but I'm trying to prepare my stomach for it. 

Also, the staff is super friendly and helpful. Our waitress was attentive and sweet. I ended up leaving a tumbler in there for about a week and they kindly held onto it.
Awesome bar! Loved the balcony area. Cheap drinks (at least compared to Chicago's prices) What more do you want?!

The ultimate blended three star review (five stars once, one star once).  Came in on back to back nights.  First night the DJ and live bands were both great and had the whole place dancing and in a great mood (five stars).  The very next night the DJ was just awful.  Playing such terrible music literally no one was dancing and just standing around hoping he would play something decent.  This went on for over 2 hours.  Bands were better, but just ok that night.
I wrote a review 6 months ago and it was a bad one. I went two weeks ago and boy have things changed! Great food great service great EVERYTHING. Definitely will be back now!

Went with a group of friends last night to Paradise Park and had an absolute blast. I specifically want to highlight the customer service from one of their employees -- Kolby. We chatted with her for about 20 minutes -- she was incredibly friendly, helpful, and made us feel right at home as a bunch of tourists coming from out of town. Would go back again without a doubt!

Quick summary: Don't go to Tootsie's; their shady waitresses will steal from you.

Longer version: My waitress here changed the tip I left on two separate charges. If you're guessing that her tip went up instead of down, you'd be correct (she added approximately $20 between the two bills). Truthfully, I probably would not have noticed her shady behavior had my credit card company not tipped me off to the extraordinarily high tip, no pun intended. 

I tried to call Tootsie's a couple times during normal business hours, but nobody answered the phone. Instead of resolving things directly with them, I am now in the fun process of disputing the charges through the credit card company. It's not a lot of money at stake, but it's about the principle of her blatantly stealing from customers that makes it worth it for me. Hopefully, I will eventually reach a manager at Tootsie's to help resolve the situation (and/or maybe get the waitress fired); I will update this post if I am able to resolve it directly with them.

This is such a fun little stop in Nashville.  It is highly recommended that you call ahead to reserve a table, however if it is already sold out, you can show up early and wait on line.  They keep a number of seats at the bar and in pews open for people that day, but you still need to show up an hour early to have a good chance of getting a spot.  We were able to sit at the bar where the lovely Martha served us drinks and told us about some of the go-to spots in Nashville.  The live music was absolutely amazing and it was really great to hear the stories behind the music as well.

Okay, if you have seen the show Nashville, you probably want to stop here! It was so much fun. We arrived around 3:30 and waited outside to see if we could get in for the 7 showing. We were 12-15th in line and we made it in along with six other people behind us! We were excited. It is a very small venue, which makes it very intimate. Although the wait outside was long, we had a ton of fun with the people by us in line. So the time passed quickly. The band sounded amazing, told stories and talked about their songs. It was exactly what we were looking for! We did not get food or drinks, but we did buy shirts. They were 26 each and the perfect souvenir for our Nashville trip!

I was just kicked out for my "bag" being too big...the bag I was carrying was my BREAST PUMP!!! I have a daughter at home that I need to feed and just because I decided to go to the bar with some friends for a night AND pump in a bathroom floor (sanitary) I couldn't get into their bar. Instead I stood in the pouring rain and went next door to The Stage, where they didn't even flinch at my bag carrying my pump. Suck my milk filled tits TOOSTIES @tootsies @thestage
Yes it is overcrowded but just the same It is Tottsie's   Great Bartenders!

Lunch. No Service after 3 different employes looked me in the eyes. My story. I paid to park my car (meter) then went up to the bar to drink and eat lunch after 13min and no service I look around. Only 3 people at the bar. The employee is sitting at a bar stool talking to a guy. Looks at me then looks away. 2 other people that work behind the bar also did the same thing. I was so upset I got up to leave.  Instead I put more money in the meter and walked back in. Same thing.  Could not believe it. I ate next door it was very good Chicago pizza I think. Never will I go back

Me and my boyfriend visited the Stone Fox on a Sunday around noon. We love trying locally owned restaurants, and we were impressed upon walking in with the cute decor. 

The good impression pretty much ended there. When we finally got out waitresses attention I ordered the BBQ omelet with a Bloody Mary and he ordered the chicken and waffles.

The Bloody Mary took about 10 minute to get to us and was mediocre at best. Tasted mostly like pickle juice. 

The food took another 15 minutes to find us and judging by the temperature must have been sitting out for awhile. I ate mine because I was starving, but my boyfriend was not as desperate. 

His egg and waffle were cold and his (seemingly frozen) chicken was burnt. He ended up just sending it back and not getting anything to replace it. We have been together for 3 years and that is the first time I have ever seen him send food back. 

Again, it took forever to get our server's attention for the check and she seemed irritated when I asked her a question about our bill.

We are polite people and we weren't mad because the food was bad. We just expect a certain level of service from a server and this place didn't cut it. 

I don't usually write reviews, but we were especially hopeful and then fully disappointed after trying this place. It could have been, and I hope it was, a fluke. But I do not think we will be returning and I would not recommend it to friends.

We attended the New Year's Eve show last night and were amazed at the intimate venue and the caliber of seasoned musicians and songwriters. Everyone was very gracious and there was never a wait because we had purchased tickets. Looking forward to coming back!

I love this place.  I have fond memories of going to Woolworth's as a kid and really liked that they kept some of the old timey decor.  The place was packed, but I snagged a seat at the bar with no problem.  The service was phenomenal.  I opted for the pot roast and mashed potatoes and dare I say it was better than my mom's.  Shhh don't tell her I said that.  Perfectly seasoned, no knife needed, and not at all greasy or oily.  The portion size was enough to be comfortably full, but not stuffed.  Can't wait to return and check out the lounge as well.

I would say the artists are a 5, the venue a 3? These artists are so talented and such great performers. It doesn't even matter if you don't like country music. The talent and the energy that's in the bar is just a unique experience. 

The venue itself is not very special; it's a pretty old building. Yes, it gets crowded but it can be part of the fun. Try to go earlier if you'd like to sit. 

Overall, I definitely recommend checking this place out. It's classic Nashville on Broadway scene.

This place is trash.  The drinks are over-priced, service is slow, basically just a tourist trap.  From a nearby scuffle, my wife got elbowed in the lip by some guy.  After we left in our crowd because of this scuffle, I realized she had gotten hit so I went back and pointed out the guy who did it, security told me she would have to come back to the bar, show them her lip and then they would maybe remove the guy.  Considering they threw out the other guy in the scuffle, it made no sense. Security is a joke.  Take your business elsewhere, there are so many better options with better music.
Beer and band, a simple formula.  The music was great.  The place is loud. It's beat up.  You just sit on a bar stool, enjoy the show (music and the crowd) and have a beer.  What's not to like.
Poblano pepper entree would have been a 5 star if not for the large amount of undercooked garlic cloves. If only it had been roasted it would add a sweetness instead of bitterness to this dish.

Just returned from Nashville from a 3 day stay. Had a great time, southern hospitality does exist. Except tootsies. We went to Tootsies on a recommendation from a local. We said we would like to go to a restaurant that has out door seating and good food. Tootsies is it bye said. So on our last day we decided we would try it. What a mistake, the roof bar/restaurant had no one seating. I was basically told first come first served and great if theres a line, which there wasn't. We finally grabbed a table that was vacated by other people sat down and waited to be served. The waitress came over and asked us what we wanted to drink, we said water. Omg you would of thought you just called her a name, the look we got. She said fine and walked away. 10 minutes later our water shows up and asks you know what you want. Yes! We order, and the food is brought to the bar about 10 minutes later and there it sits while our lovely waitress plays with her phone, and texts, and texts. Finally we get pour food, and yes our food is cold. My wife had fish fingers that were extremely dry for fish and I had a sandwich which in all fairness was decent. Both came with yesterdays fries I think, based on how cold and soggy they were. Now don't get me wrong, if your drunk and don't care about the food or attitude from the waitress, then this is the place. If you do care about the food and you want to be treated like patron thats putting money in there pocket, then this isn't it. Thumbs Down! Oh i failed the mention the best part after eating bad food, the urine smell going the down the steps.

This was our first time in Nashville, and we spent all day here!  The service was amazing - you cannot walk in without being hunted by the bartender - and the music was the best by far!

The people were great as well, everyone engages in the music and has a good time.  This is our go-to spot next time we come!

I love tacos. I love mushrooms. Why not try the smoked mushroom taco?! I did NOT like it, and I like most things. Something about the taste, not sure if it was the smokiness, but something was off. I was so hungry though that I just sadly ate it. The chips and salsa helped me power through it. Plus the 3 cucumber cooler cocktails that I was downing with it. They were pretty dang strong, which I was pleasantly surprised. 

I was with a party and we were downstairs in the cellar. Really cool vibe but loud music and very dimly lit. Pretty sure I had to use my phone light to see some things on the menu. Thursday nights after 9 in the cellar turns into almost a club type area playing 90's music.

Just like that Coldplay song! Paradise Paradise...Paradi...ah crap never mind.

This place is obviously gimmicky but I liked it. Drinks were cheap enough, I think. The music was pretty good. There were a lot of people.

And then they all just cleared out like someone farted at the gym and you knew you just couldn't face another 0.75 miles on the treadmill with that vapor hanging over your head and stinging your eyes and the back of your throat. You know that situation. You just gotta get the hell out. Even if that means that you won't get to obsessively stare at the little dots as they painfully light up the perimeter of that fake quarter-mile track that you're pacing around.

Not sure what happened at Paradise Park but that kind of happened, so we left. I think we would have stayed longer otherwise.

Side note: don't look up at the vents. I said DON'T! JUST DON'T!

You won't listen to me. And you will get airborne toxic mold poisoning just by looking at the thick, black layer of god-knows-what that's just sitting up there.

You should have listened to me. But now you're ruined.

It's worth the wait! We waited in line for almost two hours in the heat and it was so worth it! What an amazing experience. It's a must when visiting Nashville. Expect to wait, but once inside, you'll be happy you did. You can make reservations if available. Our seats were up close and personal. Make sure you sit back and relax and enjoy some of the best writers in the business. Make sure you take pictures (no flash) to capture the experience. There was not a fee the night we went.

If I could give this restaurant 0 stars then I would. The customer service was absolutely terrible. I sit down with my friends & it takes the waiter, a tall white male with long strawberry blonde dreads, 5 minutes to come over & take our drink orders. One of my friends was on the phone when he asked for our drinks so she did not hear him & instead of waiting just a minute he walked away with an attitude. He comes back with our drinks & we sit there looking over the menu when my friend accidentally spills my water all over me.
