We ask the waiter for a towel, he stares at us for a good 30 seconds, grabs a towel, throws it on the table in front of me & walks away with the same attitude he had before. This is when we took the liberty of paying for the drinks & walking out, assuring him that he performed terrible customer service, which he proceeded to roll his eyes about it & chuckle. We felt extremely unwelcome & I would highly advise anyone not to go to this restaurant & to steer clear of this particular waiter.

i've been wanting to stop here since they opened. i did once but they were really busy and we just had a quick drink at the bar and bounced. last night my husband and i checked it out. our waiter was super nice and genuine. when we asked about beers he wasn't sure about what the types of beer were but he went and asked which was great. we both ordered and our food and drinks came out quickly. my husband had ordered the jackalope bear walker but we are both sure judging from the pour, color and taste that he actually got the ky bourbon barrell ale, which he was fine to drink so we didn't mention it. 

the food was good but overall the menu seemed really overpriced for what you are getting. i had the chicken tacos. the chicken was prepared perfectly. i really love the marinade. my husband had the reuben and mac n' cheese. he like the reuben okay and the mac n' cheese we both ate and liked. it looked like there was chili on the top of it though and i wasn't a big fan of that. 

i really like the atmosphere and our server. the food was good but not anything really fancy and overpriced. i would have liked to try some other things on the menu but didn't want to pay that much for it. i really struggled between a 3 or 4 star rating. 3.5 would have been ideal. also, parking was kind of problematic - maybe because of sinema. and on the way out it sounded like the kitchen and waitstaff was arguing when we passed the open kitchen. good but maybe underwhelming?

This place felt a bit too much like a fraternity house basement. And I'm not saying I'm too good to hang out in a fraternity house basement, just too old. 

There were also far too many angry dudes who looked like they were drinking straight out of their own personal pitchers of beer in order to get up the courage to punch someone (probably me) in the face. 

But at least they had Buck Hunter.

Over crowded. Girls on top floor so rude & full of themselves couldn't take care of problem! We are visiting from San Diego & we were so excited that they had a photo booth with THEIR name on it upstairs... We put in $5 & it counted down then cleared out to original screen! Brought to the bitchy long hair blondes attention & she was more concerned about her phone & the guys working that she couldn't give us customer service & either refund our money or even give us a drink!! In a customer service business it's pretty sad that they didn't take care of the problem or even put an out of order sign on it! It's Thursday & We are here until Monday too & we WONT be back!!

We stopped in with a group of 8 for a late lunch on a Friday afternoon and the place was pretty much empty, which was surprising since the place was so cool. It has a huge garage type door so that it has open air dining, and since it was beautiful out, we really enjoyed it. We got the guac, the fried pickles (they were great) and the spicy nuggets for an appetizer. The nuggets were Hot, so if you like spicy food definitely give them a try. The pulled chicken sandwich was really good as well, and packed some heat. The general manager came around as we were ready to leave and offered to take our picture as a group up on stage which was very nice of him. He explained to us about the boots hanging on the wall, and even gave us a tour of the downstairs where they have a Speak Easy and an entrance to a billiards area that opens at 4. It was cool to see the history of the building and he went out of his way to show us and explain everything which was a great start to our trip to Nashville.
Super fun - FOUR floors of different bands and bars!! Fills up EARLY.  A bit of a dive. Fun.

We went here for the food only, so I cannot talk about anything else.  The cashier was nice, but the food was less than desirable.  Everything we ordered was overcooked: the burger, the chicken...  YUCK.  

While we weren't expecting amazing decor, considering the name, the seating is really old and falling apart.  This was more than wear and tear.  All the tables were dirty, like no one ever bothered to wipe them down. 

Do not recommend nor would I eat here again.

We went here one night for dinner and the service was pretty horrible. She forgot to put in our drink order twice and the place was empty. Food was pretty good but they were out of a lot of food and drinks on their menu. Environment was pretty fun though. I wouldn't come back to eat here again but maybe to grab a drink once in a while.

You know that place you went to in college to get a bite at 2 am after the bars closed down? Fortunately, you can relive that experience at Paradise Park. Located on Broadway, in the middle of all the bars, it's one of the few places that serves food into the early morning hours and seems to be full of those trying to soak up large amounts of alcohol consumed over the last few hours. 

Actually, the food isn't that bad, when comparing to McDonald's type restaurants. It's close to a Waffle House experience where you see the cook slap your burger on the grill after you order. This isn't a nice, sit down restaurant with table service. It's cheap food meant to be consumed with and after alcohol and when you compare it to other establishments that are similar how can you complain? 

The buns are even better than you get at a fast-food place. Their BBQ sauce isn't bad - at all. And, the burgers are edible as are the fries and sweet potato fries. I ordered the turkey and shockingly enjoyed it. It wasn't some packaged turkey, it tasted like fresh shaved turkey and came on bread that had substance. 

Come with the right expectations - and you won't be disappointed. And, remember it's a perfect fit for those looking for soak up alcohol, rather than a good, Southern cooked meal.

it was too crowded so we left. Then there was a fight outside that appeared to be between two men and a woman. Worst part was they tipped over one of those cigarette depositories, spilled it all over the sidewalk and it reeked terribly.

We had made reservations very far in advance and arrived a couple minutes late due to our taxi getting lost.  After we arrived and gave the hostess our name, she had already given our reservation away.  As we were walking away, she told the line of people 5 spaces just opened up (our reservation).  We were disappointed she could have let us in, but turned us away before our seats were even taken.
Not sure why anyone would go here!!!  Crowded, dirty, service sucks, and smells like urine.  There are so many new places I'd avoid this dump at all costs!  This place doesn't even deserve one star!
Great place to eat before TPAC. Food was good and very fast. Service great as well. Nothing bad on the menu. No domestic draft beer but several IPA options. Sit at the counter if you get a chance.
This place is the most fun with great entertainment.  Don't miss Jakes Maurer he is my favorite. Always a fun time.

This is a great place to listen to great music. My family and I have been coming here for years. since the show Nashville, it is impossible get get show tickets anymore. The way you reserve tickets now is nothing but Stupid!!! I have tried my last time to get tickets for a show here.there are plenty more places to listen to music in Nashville than here!

Food never disappoints, especially from their new menu. Can't beat their mac and cheese! Downstairs has a cool lounge vibe, and you can order off a limited menu down there as well. They have a fantastic happy hour until 7 that includes half off wine, beer and certain specialty cocktails.

The energy was wild and made this place electric with excitement.  "Country roads!! Take me home!! To a place!! Where I belong!!" coming from the lungs of everyone on the roof.

Live music on all 3 levels, but the roof seemed where the party was. It had a little more room to breath with a cool (60 person capacity) observation deck overlooking Broadway. It was built for some good day drinking. 

It should be a tour stop on your own personal adventure.

While the music was great everything else about this establishment was terrible. The drinks were absolutely overpriced which is not quite a terrible thing for the location. What was deserving of a one star review was the apparent direction from management/ownership to evacuate all patrons within 5 minutes of actual last call. Any plea to finish a beverage within the coming 5 minutes after turning on all the lights falls on deaf ears and large biceps that are clearly unreceptive. Go and have a ton of fun, tip the amazing bands graciously, and evacuate well before last call.

If you want a soy chai latte with a side of religion, then you are in the right place. If you don't, you can ignore the religious undertones.

The chai latte was good, it hit the spot. The decor is homey, feels very upscale barn inspired and seems like a good place to study. They get an A+ for best transformation of an old fast food joint. 

I definitely will not drive to Green Hills to get a drink here but if I am in the area, I will absolutely stop by.

The view is great, but the drinks are absurd. I understand paying $10 for a good vodka drink because of the location, so I got a vodka Sprite. What I got was a Dixie cup of straight Sprite. I even let people around me try it, literally laughing out loud that I paid for it. I went back and wondered maybe if she had forgotten the vodka, and the brunettes response was shrugging her shoulders and said "um, I never under pour" and walked away. Have you ever worked in customer service or at any bar? Maybe y'all should try your own drinks before you keep ripping us off.
We came here for drinks and music.  The bands were great so much fun.  We had a couple appetizer and they were good bar food.  Great place, lots of fun!

Went during lunchtime, the place was pretty much full, but didnt feel packed in like sardines like other places. Brisket Nachos were very yummy! Happy hour prices were good.  No beer on tap :-( but that seems to be a Nashville thing.   Band was really really good.  Went upstairs to play shuffleboard but the bartender wouldnt give us the pucks, saying there would be a private party coming in 15mins.  Helllllo, we couldve played 5 games by then!

Just spent Halloween at this location. $20 cover charge and absolutely ridiculous. It was hardly even packed and the costume contest was an absolute joke. They let the crowd judge the contest, which was fair, the only problem was the people that they introduced into the contest the crowd didn't even like. How they chose the contestants into the top three is beyond me. Nobody in the crowd even cheered as the contestants were called. It was embarrassing to the bar to say the least, if they were not embarrassed they should have been.  I will never return nor would the other five people I was with. After a $20 cover, you would honestly think it would be a pretty cool place. I think the only people who enjoyed themselves were the employees who worked there and the employees who won the rigged costume contest. I will definitely spread the word on how terrible this bar in Nashville is, especially when there are other top notch bars to visit. **Visitors be warned.

This was my favorite bar when I lived here a few years ago, and I was super excited to come back while in town for the weekend, but was kinda let down. Maybe because I felt way older than the rest of the crowd? Or maybe because the drinks we ordered were disappointing? Not sure, but it just wasn't the same. Maybe it was just an off night.
The band was awesome though. And it was never too crowded to dance or wait for drinks. I would go back for the band, but next time I will know not to hype it up as "the best bar ever" to my friends.

I don't want to be too harsh, the food was just OK, but fresh for sure.  best ranch dressing definitely homemade.  took a long time to get food but we didn't care. back patio is nice, love the pallet garden and lights.  I'm sure if you go to see the music it gets even better. glad you are in the neighborhood. the servers were very nice and attentive.
Several floors to bounce around on, each playing different live music.  I liked this place even though it was almost impossible to move around.
Good experience when in Nashville because of the history. Lots people, pretty crowded, and loud. Recommend going to the 3rd floor there was more space. Great musical acts!

The world famous Tootsies is a fun place on Broadway.  Beers are kinda pricey at $6 each, but you do get entertainment.  Each floor has live country music depending on what style you like.  The first floor was the most fun and can get packed.  Found this place to be most fun in the afternoon it's more of a laid back vibe.  The rooftop patio was nice but always packed.  A lot of good artist singing here, even the door guy rocked it out!  This is a must stop when in Nashville on Broadway.

Sooooo many good food places in Nashville, do yourself a favor and don't waste your time at this one. The bluegrass band was great and The bartender was nice. The mimosas transfer from bar to table so that's awesome and convenient But that's about it. The food comes out very fast because it is not fresh. The table service is also extremely slow and our server messed up our order and tried to blame it on the kitchen. If your priority is cheap mimosas and listening to music do it,  but there are such great food places nearby don't waste your time here if you actually care about food quality. 1 hour plus wait for a table, and not worth the wait.
Not a good place to watch football they play Justin's Bieber over the game. The food is pretty good, I let my girlfriend talk me into catching a college football game on a Saturday.
Great new spot in the Melrose area. Fun for a drink, live music and some new twists on Southern cuisine. Definitely a great addition!

Food is pretty decent; however, we had to approach the bar to get a server to our table and 3 people sat at the bar right by us and we're waiting for about ten minutes while the bartenders were standing in front of them on their phones not even willing to help. That's not the way to treat customers if you want their tip...

We had the best time at the bluebird! We caught the 8:00 show on Sunday. (Waited for 2 hours outside to get in but it was so worth it) We heard a ton of different singer song writers (Anne buckle was amazing!) and then had an hour of Victoria banks who told some really amazing stories and put on a great show. Food was good. Company was great. We loved the bluebird!!!

It's not amazing, but it does have booze, is staffed by hipsters, and most importantly:

A black velvet tapestry of Tom Selleck in his Magnum PI prime.

I don't think you need any other reasons to go here.
Great Beer. Cool, laid-back atmosphere with Live Music.

I had the fried chicken salad with sweet potato fries on the side. Delish! The fried chicken bites were amazing. My friend got the brisket sandwich and really liked it. The bartender was awesome and had us try the assortment of sauces. The Texas Ketchup was seriously good and I am going to buy some online because it was that bomb. I'd come back here for sure. Also had a Bloody Mary and the Bearded Iris IPA. Recommend both!

This place has a really good Happy Hour. Half off drinks! You can never pass that up. I tried my friend food she had the grill cheese and it came with some tomato soup. When I tell you that soup was sooooooooo good! I have to order it the next time I visit. The basement area is amazing and so chill!

How have I never written a review about the gloriousness of Paradise Park? It is, hands down, my favorite bar on Broadway. After living here for a few years, I tend to shy away from Broadway because of the massive crowds that flock there. However, a handful of times a year, I'll go there just to head to Paradise Park. Let me be clear: this is not a fancy bar, but it is a fun one! Lot's of delicious fried food to order from the kitchen next store (which is always great when you're intoxicated). Beer is cheap and served from old bathtubs. Music is always pretty good too. Tends to get crowded on the weekends so be wary of that but a really fun place to be regardless!
Cane here for St Paddy's and was disturbed by the treatment of the star spangled banner. If you love the flag of the USA, this is not a bar worth visiting

We really enjoyed our time at Woolworth, with the atmosphere being just what we'd hoped for. It's quite noisy inside -- we were there for lunch -- which, with an antsy baby, we liked.

The food arrived quickly and was tasty, with appropriately sized portions. We had no leftovers but didn't feel full.

The only negative is that the cocktail I ordered took awhile to come out and seemed to have been sitting in wait for awhile: Its large, square-shaped ice cube had begun melting and gone wonky, watering down the already small $13 drink. The trouble with the cocktail, called Baby Doll, is that it seemed to contain none of the rum or brandy it promised. I can't be convinced that there was alcohol in this drink. However, in retrospect, I shouldn't have ordered a lunch cocktail at a restaurant like this. It isn't their specialty, and it's possible they only offer cocktails because it's come to be expected of them.

When it comes to their actual specialties, everything was on point -- in particular, the peach cobbler. We will be back for it.

So much fun!  If you enjoy standing for hours in a tight crowd, then you won't be bothered by the sardine-like feel of watching the bands perform.  However, if you want your own "party-space" with your own security and cocktail waitress, I HIGHLY recommend reserving the Third Floor Private Area.  It's worth the price and makes your time at Tootsie's all-the-more enjoyable.  Joel was easy to work with, Emily was an amazing cocktail waitress for us, and Daniel, our Security Guard for the evening, was AWESOME!  Absolutely amazing for our group!
First time in Nashville and we heard this place had really good food , it didn't disappoint the ambience was great had a great burger and BLT
The female fiddle player is insanely good! Her blonde singer counterpart, however, is not. She's the one who demands money even though her fiddle-playing colleague deserves all the money.

What a great spot for experiencing a show!  It's small and very intimate and I really liked the unique set-up of enjoying a performance in the center of a bar/café/restaurant.  Every seat is a good seat in this place.

It is very popular and very tough to get into...we planned ahead and I thought it was worth the time spent in trying to make this happen.  The staff is friendly just adds to the great experience here.

Before revamping the entire menu this place was awesome. The old menu offered a different and delicious take on basic comfort food. The new menu and new decor make the sutler more generic and honestly reminds me of a "western Applebee's". The new food isn't terrible, it's just definitely not what it was.  I used to recommend this place when people would visit Nashville, but not anymore. There are so many better places with better food.
Great place to hang out and listen to music in the afternoon or party at night! Has the Nashville Honky Tonk vibe you would expect and comes highly recommended by anyone who's been there.

Went around 1030am on Saturday morning.  Got a table on 3rd floor.  Was pretty empty then but was packed by noon.  The group playing on 3rd floor was awesome. The waitress was very good and we were happy to get there early enough to get a table.  Was a mix of older crowd and younger crowd and the band did well with that.  Bottle beer was $7 for Mich ultra but I guess that's how they afford the bands since there's no cover.  We happily stayed for 3.5 hours before heading to the airport to fly home.  Definitely worth checking Tootsie's out.

If you are visiting Nashville, you go here. Doesn't matter if you want to go, if it is your scene....this is just one of the places you go.
It is crowded, expensive, and loud (live music!!). But it is loads of fun!
But it is basically one of the quintessential places to go out downtown.

I can't believe I've lived in Music City for all this time without having visited Tootsie's Orchid Lounge.  After all, it is a Nashville institution.  We stopped in mid-afternoon, and the place was already packed.  We never did find seats, but the drinks were cold, and they had good live music on every level.  And the view from their rooftop bar was awesome.  Tootsie's is definitely going to be added to my list of places to take out-of-town guests.

Not a bad greasy burger for A bar that is not a pub... I was a bit afraid because I saw someone eating us chicken sandwich which looked like a Scooby snack but the burger was bigger and better than I expected.   I would stick with cocktails and live music and eat elsewhere.

Last night I walked into the sutler to place a togo order, it was my birthday(8/22) and I wanted their delicious burger dripping in cheese sauce. It's my favorite burger in town. It was busy, so I patiently waited for the bartender. She asked me what she could get for me. I said burger, mac and cheese, and collard greens Togo. Then she blatantly stops me with a traffic cop hand, asks me if I'm with the person next to me at the bar, I said no but I just need a burger, greens and Mac n cheese Togo. She proceeds to wave her finger at me as if to pause our exchange, doesn't take my order, and proceeds to take two more drink orders from other people at the bar. 3 minutes later she's back, and she's acting like she still doesn't have time or patience for me. I had to tell her 5 times in all, because apparently I was talking entirely too fast for this fast-paced short-order bartender to comprehend that I wanted a burger, collard greens, and Mac and cheese Togo. She offered fries, and I obliged. When I came back for the food, there were no napkins, utensils, or ketchup offered or included in my $30 order. I asked for them, and she gave me this look like I crapped in her cereal. She warns me it could be a few minutes because they ran out upstairs and she would have to go to the downstairs bar to get them. This is when I started getting upset, because the last time I was there I tried to order a burger in their downstairs lounge, and got denied my food order because food was only available upstairs....while I watched some other guy at the other end of the bar eating a burger!!!! Why would you need Togo cutlery as far away from the exit as possible?! It's for people that exit your establishment with their uneaten food! So she sends a bar back down to get them, 3 minutes later he's back, and she  still doesn't have the time or the ketchup for me. Now the exchange is complete, and I walk out the door. I'm still confused as to why food can't be delivered downstairs, it's like they don't want to profit, they'd rather tell their guests No. Let's talk about the food. 
    I wasn't aware that they had changed their Mac and cheese, no more broccolinis:( I wasn't aware that they had stopped putting fried chicken skin atop their collards:( they do their fries like five guys, except it's like their fryer can't handle it so we had like 3 pounds of oily/soggy shoe string fries. Or the best soft McDonald's fries you could imagine attempting to enjoy. Don't sacrifice quality to satisfy your bubba guests.
     The burger, the burger, the burger. I asked her for an extra side of cheese sauce FOR THE BURGER twice during our altercation. I'm giving her the benefit of the doubt, because she might be new. I haven't seen her before, and she was kind of moving in slow motion. She might not have ever had the chance to try the glory that was their burger, that deity-like cheese sauce and those wickle pickles on there, oh my god it was so good. I found the order ticket from the computer in with the French fries and she ordered an extra side of cheese sauce for the Mac and cheese....which wasn't in the bag. Neither was the burger I wanted. The burger I got was this little ratty cheese burger with melted sliced cheese on top of peppers on an old moldy bun. I'm not one to complain about mold on bread, but this was an ugly looking burger. In their defense, in regards to my photo, I ripped the burger in half and then took the picture.  I still ate it, fearing a 20-30 minute wait, or the attitude,  If I were to step back inside their establishment. Ive spent around a thousand dollars in that place since they opened, and I'm starting to lose appreciation for their inconsistent standards of service and food quality. It's a great tourist trap, I'll give them that.
Amazing bacon. Ok fruit. The potatoes are abysmal. The sausage is cold. Cold sausage isn't edible, its trash. The margaritas are good here.
Guitarists and fiddlers dancing on bar tops? YES PLEASE!! Tootsie's is the best bar in Nashville. The music were amazing, the patrons were friendly and the beer was cold. Great place.
If you only go to one place on Broadway, go to Tootsie's!!  The bands are great and it.s lots of fun! And there is a 2nd band upstairs.

Great location. Not a quick meal. I ordered a hot dog and fries and I waited a while. My 4 other friends got their food quicker than I did. They said the hamburger was outstanding. Great flavor of food!

Was visiting from out-of-town and our host suggested Woolworth on 5th.  Absolutely loved it!  The former downtown dime store interiors are still partially visible and the main restaurant has an inviting vibe.  No one in our party of four was disappointed.  The fried chicken was crispy, as noted, and very tasty; it was accompanied with southern green beans (which they were), corn pudding (very good), and mashed potatoes (meh, just ok).  Another one of us had the fried chicken livers, which were excellent, and it came with weird-sounding "grits with bacon & kale", which turned out to be outstanding.  The other two had dinner salads and both ate every bite.  Dessert was shared and it was the bourbon caramel pecan pie, as good as it sounds.  I would strongly suggest this place and I hope to return on our next visit!

This place is amazing! We actually never made it upstairs, only staying on the first floor, but we had the time of our lives there! The music was awesome, the beers were cold and the atmosphere rocked! If you don't like crowds this probably isn't the place for you but we loved it!

Very disappointed with this place. I was soooo excited to do their "bluegrass brunch" and even though it was on the other side of town, even though the locals tried to persuade me to a different place, I wanted to try this place. The restaurant was really cute and pretty busy on a Saturday afternoon. We were seated in Emma's station and we ordered the bottomless mimosas for $15. I asked if we could have ice in them and it seemed to baffle her. I said, can you just bring 2 pint glasses with ice then and we'll dump our mimosa in there. Her response was "I cant serve you 2 drinks at once". Um...what? 1st of all, yes you can, but thats not what I was asking. We decided to share the brisket hash with sweet potatoes, peppers and greens. It was served lukewarm and the brisket was overcooked and super fatty but the rest was really flavorful. It really had potential. I got a side of the andouille sausage as well and that was really good. Emma kept up on our mimosas but they were super weak. They mix them in a pitcher to make it easier on the servers but the oj/ champagne ratio is off....big time. We basically paid $15 for bottomless oj. We also got a side of biscuits which were very good with a sweet butter and grape jelly. I wouldn't come back here. Food and service were pretty forgettable. Ohhhh yeahhh....AND...they say Bluegrass brunch on Saturday and Sunday but thats a big ol lie. There is only live music on Sunday. See pic...totally makes it sound like the live bluegrass is on Saturday as well. This is the reason we came here in the 1st place. Very deceiving.

The Stone Fox is a wonderful, wonderful place. They have some of the best shows in town. They are great because of the art they provide to the community. You can see a killer band, watch a funny local comic, check out the local short film night, play bingo, buy goods from local vendors at a pop up shop, or shake it down to some vintage disco. You can't really find another place that is doing that here. 

That being said, their cocktails are hit or miss, but they are a good price. They have a couple bartenders that know what they're doing. I have never been impressed with the food. The portions are small for the price, and the food itself is mediocre in general. I love chicken and waffles, but theirs missed the mark. I had about five tiny piece, almost nuggets, of chicken with a very basic waffle. I liked the spicy syrup, but they are other places in town that do chicken and waffles much better (namely, The Southern and Tenn Sixteen.) 

So if you treat the place like a bar/venue instead of a restaurant, I guarantee it will be one of your favorite, unique places.
Worst system EVER!!!!  Never waited in line so long w/ no communication. NOT WORTH IT!!!!!

This place is known for being just across the alley from the back door of the old Ryman Auditorium that used to house the Grand Ole Opry.  Performers would come over between acts, have a few drinks, and then head back over to perform.  Thus, many, many famous people have visited this club, and the pictures on the wall bear the proof.  But, there is more than just history being served here.  

We came in to check it out, and ended up enjoying the cuisine.  Tootsies actually has a pretty decent Black Bean Burger for the vegetarians in the crowd, and both my wife and I found it to be very tasty.  It was a good value, too.  The burger itself had a good texture, a good flavor, and it really hit the spot.  It comes with seasoned fries that are pretty good, too.  Just note that all the condiments come in little packets instead of bottles, so, if you like a lot of catsup, mustard, and mayo,  you're going to have to open a lot of packets.  The prices is pretty good, too.  

If you like dining in history, and you like eating vegetarian, this place fits the bill.  We also enjoyed the friendly, helpful staff.

RUDE, we didn't even get to eat b/c when we walked in with our babies(us and our friends had their baby too) they practically rolled their eyes. When we went to the hostess to ask for a table she said "we don't have high chairs" then put our name down. She said it would only be a few minutes wait, then she disappeared and reappeared to tell us that they were not seating anymore people b/c they were too full.
WHAT?! what kind of restaurant turns  waiting customers away? Needless to say we WILL NOT be going back. So if you have babies or a kid(s) don't even think about going to this snobby place.

Maybe it was just the time and day I went (Fri night, midnightish) but the place was packed  shoulder-to-shoulder. It was so crowded you couldn't do anything. I didn't get what the hype was, but maybe it's cooler other nights of the week.

Wow. After a few suggestions to try out Tootsies, I'm here. On the roof deck, listening to live music...which sounds all great except for the fact that the vapid blonde waitresses have yet to acknowledge that we've sat down, even after asking the bartender if there was wait service outside...15 mins later (not at all busy btw) I go inside to get my own beers. No corona light, that's disappointing. So, crap service, doesn't have the one light beer I like, and I've inhaled more 2nd hand smoke in the 30mins I've been here than I have my whole
Nashville trip. How very disappointing.

So if you're in Nashville, you HAVE to stop at Tootsie's at some point. Its a little dive bar, with crazy loud, fun country music! There are two areas with bands, one downstairs and the one upstairs or right when you walk in. Make sure to check both out before you leave and move on to the next place. 

Definitely would come here again.

First timer. Went with a couple girlfriends for brunch on a Sunday and it was fairly busy. Our waitress was nice. She disappeared for a bit, but she came back and apologized for it. 

We started off with mimosas and they offer $20 carafe that serves 4 people. Always a plus when they have some kind of special on drinks. 

I just had the biscuits and gravy and deviled eggs. I'm not a vegetarian, but none of the other items seemed to pop out at me. (I was hoping for either some kind of salmon or turkey sausage dish, which there was neither) The biscuits were fluffy and the gravy was tasty. They offer unique topping deviled eggs, but today they were only serving the traditional kind, I was a little bummed about that, but it was still good. 

My gf's had the chicken and waffle and the biscuits and jam with chicken. Neither complained about the food, nor raved about it, so I'm just assuming it was decent. We were busy catching up about other stuff so that could be why the food was never commented on. 

Everything was just okay.

One of the best places in Nashville. The hot fish tacos are the best thing I've had so far, although the grill Bologna sandwich is is close second. And the sweet potato hummus with a side of pickled onions and jalapeños is also excellent. Very cool space, too.
With local recommendations- we went for breakfast. The staff was SO friendly and personable! The meal was great!! (Jalapeno bacon especially) we will be back!
Their chill is amazing, but everything else isn't anything too special. Their mac and cheese is plain, and not creamy enough for my taste. Their Nashville nuggets aren't too bad, but super spicy.

Finally made here and was not disappointed. Went with a friend and posted up at the bar for dinner and a few drinks. Both bartenders were great and very attentive. We both ordered cheeseburgers, which came out quickly. Burgers were tasty and fries were great. Band started about halfway through our meal and they were pretty good. The sound wasn't overwhelming and you could still carry on conversations easily.  Really enjoyed our visit and will be back. Fun spot.
Visited from Chicago last April. The staff at Toosies really stood out and set the bar higher than other bars on Broadway. Overall, It's a great city and I can't wait to visit again.
Stopped by for a drink and to enjoy the live music.  Staff was friendly...  Atmosphere was Trailer Park themed.  LOVED IT
Slow slow slow. 1pm Saturday.  Food ok. Good band.  Get ur chit together.  I dont mind waiting but it appears that the cook is in need of some help and a better mrthod of orded delivery

Tootsies was so much fun! Came here on a Wednesday night just to get a taste of the night life in Nashville. It was packed! 3 floors of music, top floor has an additional outside balcony and NO COVER. If you can't get to the bartender on floor one, head upstairs! We enjoyed every floor! The music was fantastic. I also got to enjoy my Yuengling which is unavailable to me at home!!! Either way, good place to dance and have a beer!
Always a great time!  Bands have been consistently great every time we come to Nashville.  Absolutely,  a place to have a few drinks and enjoy the music.

This place took a solid 15 minutes to get a drink on a slow Thursday night on the more quiet bar. Didn't stay too long past that -- due to the change in venue that we went for. 

The overall feel for this place was good though. Seems like a decent staff as long as you don't mind waiting awhile did your drink.
If you're visiting from out of town and want a fun bar this is it!!  Three floors with a different live band on each floor, rooftop bar, bar food and drinks!

UGH! Why didn't someone call me and TELL me this was a non-profit. I would have put my 'non-profit judgy-ness' hat on instead of the usual 'Grr...I'm a grumpy consumer'  hat on. I'll totally give the place snaps for warm/weird vibe but really, do I need the crazy lady in the corner making laps around the place pan handling while we are working? 
I'm sure this is mecca to the Hillsboro High students who are a block away and, in fairness, the hot chocolate was bad arse...warm and spiced with I dunno what? Crack? Vanilla? Cinnamon? At least two of three anyway.  But seriously nutty chick, if I can't get my work done, we're both gonna be homeless so lets give that stuff a rest.

Cool atmosphere, neat history, food is over-priced + over-rated. Service is average. 

Example: $15 cheeseburger. 

Grass-fed = good. 

Previously frozen + sliced American cheese + tasteless pink grocery store tomato + huge bun = are you kidding? So what if there is a (average) fried egg and half a (average) sliced avocado? And no way did this patty start out at 8 ounces, as the menu claimed.

I love this place for beer! It is a great place to hangout and relax with a great beer selection. As for the food, it is just mediocre. It isn't bad but isn't great. I have only been for brunch though.

The Bluebird Cafe is a listening room and it's well-reknowned for a venue for a songwriter's performance.  I thought it was amazing that we were able to hear the 'heroes behind the hit' perform their own songs, and song that have been recorded by chart-topping artists in all the genres of music.  It was cool as they have 2 different setups, dependent on which artists you see - they can either perform on stage or do an 'ITR' (In The Round).  We had the latter, so the songwriters actually sat in the middle of the cafe, and the tables were placed all around them.  Technically, there are no 'bad' seats, but I wished we were a little bit closer to the singers (we had Table 20) - for anyone who is claustrophobic, this can be a little challenging!  We got to see Thom Schuyler, Fred Knobloch, Jack Sundrud, and Jelly Roll Johnson (best harmonicist EVER!) - they played either as a quartet or as an individual.  The songs were just plain awesome, and the vibe was more of a laid-back atmosphere.  The guys had a great sense of humor, shared stories, and played their bits.  The only 'downside' is that you have to make reservations online (can be quite stress-ridden as I almost fainted from trying to navigate the site and it was slowed down as I'm sure hundreds of other people were trying to get a spot), and you are required to spend a minimum of $7 per seat on drinks/food - I just had a ginger ale and their housemade chips with chipotle mayo sauce - pretty safe, and it was pretty good (the chips were cold, though, but the combo was good and salty).  Our server checked up on us and was was very sweet.  You line up to your left, and the right of the entrance are for people who don't have tickets and who are offered any available seats for no-shows/cancellations.  When you walk in, you pay with cash and are seated.  I really enjoyed the experience here and I'm so glad I was able to check this place out! :D

+purchase tickets online (high anxiety!)
+highly suggest 'ITR' (In The Round'
+$7 minimum on food/drinks

I am a coffee freak.  Seriously, I might have a problem.  And the biggest problem for purveyors of my beloved caffeine addiction is that I drink my coffee black.  With my love of this fantastic beverage, I would be about 500 pounds if I added cream and sugar, so oil sludge it is.  So to give me a good cup of coffee can be challenging.  Most coffee tastes burnt.  

But one day while out and about and wanting desperately to enjoy coffee I happened to spot this little place in Green Hills, and I cut someone off (sorry random person) to turn into the parking lot.  First of all its adorable in here.  Kind of like a barn.  Lots of people studying (as coffee shops are good places for that) and friendly people behind the counter.  And a wishing wall for people to post about raising money for charities and mission trips.  Overall really cool just from the visual.  

And then came the coffee, which was utterly fabulous.  Buttery delicious not-burnt-not-crap coffee.  I was in heaven.  And they have great little food options as well.  It's a little pricier for coffee, but I promise you its worth it, and I can't wait to have an excuse to go back.  I recommend grabbing a delicious beverage from here and then going about your shopping in Green Hills.  Way better than Starbucks.

I keep giving this place a try.  I have dined at the bar and been seated at tables with small and larger groups.  Regardless, I find the service to be horrible.  The food and atmosphere is good, which keeps me trying again.  Out of 4 times that I have been here, my order had been "lost" twice, once when I was alone and the other time when with my husband.  The larger group experience was the best. Those aren't good odds which should be a concern for the owners.  Things are not improving. Both time there were issues with service, the same manager visited me to apologize. She was sincere but acted like there was nothing she could do.  Once she comped a dessert, but we didn't want one, so she basically said "bummer" and left it at that.   I hope they figure this out since the place has potential.  There are a lot of great places in Nashville with solid service.  Something is wrong here. I have reached a point where I have stopped suggesting it to people.  It is a shame.

It might be 3 pm outside, but people in here are partying like it's 3am. Holy bachelorettes. If you're looking for a fun, loud, honky-tonkin good time, this is the place. People complaining about crowds, bouncers, and bathrooms must not go out all that much, or maybe don't know where exactly they are. It was packed inside and in the mid 90s outside, but somehow thanks to fans and AC, it wasn't too hot. The bathroom was actually really clean when I was there. Yes, the beer prices are steep, but you are paying for a full experience that includes awesome live music and being in a Nashville institution. We had the most fun on the third floor. The crowd was drunk but happy, and the band was a blast. We saw tourists, college kids, 30-somethings, some people in their 60s, and packs of bachelorettes. After dancing, it was nice to go onto the roof top and look at the people on the streets. It's a must-do for tourists.

Beautiful woman left and right at this place. Went there Friday and Saturday. Awesome band was playing. It's packed and when I mean packed u could hardly move, that was the only downside but that means it's a popping bar. I loved the outside balcony too u can see all of the bars on Broadway. I loved this place!!!

We went here on a Tuesday night and it wasn't hard at all to get a reservation about a week ahead of time. It is a cool little location. We went on Fat Tuesday (Mardigras) and got some free beads and saw Les Kerr play. There was a very diverse age range in the crowd. The food was quite expensive for the quantity, but it is quality! I ordered Fish & chips, which were three little fillets with maybe 25-30 fries for $13.00. It was very tasty, but not as filling as expected. My fiancee ordered some type of nacho dish, which was full of cheesy and beany goodness. 

DEFINITELY a must stop in Nashville! They have some cool merchandise there as well, we brought home a magnet for the fridge for only $3.00! I also got a hat.
Great bar ! Gets crowded as it can get ! Always has some good music  Get their early and head to the top floor snag your self up a table fast and enjoy the night away !

Came here for Sunday Brunch.  I got the enchiladas & they were SO SO GOOD. Cheesy deliciousness in a skillet. Perfect hangover food. My date was eyeing them. He was Super jealous. I tried his Hash which was a mixture of sausage & peppers. It was just meh.  I also loved their biscuits. Excellent to have munchies while you wait for your food. However, fair warning. They sat us RIGHT by the stage. While they were great...It was fairly loud & quite the opposite of what I expected from a chill rainy day brunch. I had a bit of a hangover & in hindsight would have chosen a place without live music. Only in Nashville is this normal  Oh also our server was outstanding.

You must go to Tootsies in Nashville! If you go on Thursday Friday Saturday or Sunday from 10:00 to 2:00...say hello to Jake Loban ! He and the band are awesome! Country music at its best. Jake is the sweetest and awesomely entertaining. Rodney and the rest of the band are flat out good country and great human beings! Don't go here if you're looking for fancy decor but only if you want great people and good music. After listening to Jake , check out the other 
floors for Taylor or Rachael or TJ!  You might even get to sit in Willie Nelson's section! Some of the greats of country have sung here! Jake is sure to be one of them! See you there!
Was a really cold day, we waited on line for over an hour but got in and it was well worth it... Very intimate way to see great music

Bluebird Cafe is an interesting place.  Famous for live music, Bluebird Cafe is great under the right circumstances.  The venue is entirely context dependent on which artists you see and whether or not your have reservations.

First, if you want to visit Bluebird, get reservations.  It's a pain, I know, but it's the only way to go.  On the night we attended, about 90% of the venue was filled with reserved seats.  The remaining 10% went to the line outside, which was at least 50 people deep.  Needless to say, the vast majority were left out.

The tight seating had one great side benefit.  I watched with glee as multiple people tried to sneak inside the building before being caught and escorted out.  The woman who "wanted a quick picture" suffered the same fate as the dude who "just had to go to the bathroom" - the host politely escorted them out and dropped them at the back of the line where they belonged.  It was the most entertaining part of the night for me!

Our group had a reservation, so we were seated quickly.  We had a great view of the stage, and ordered some food and drinks.  I know that most people come to the Bluebird for the music, but the nominal per-person minimum makes food a small part of the experience.  I had a black bean burger that was excellent, but the rest of our table met with less success with the pork sandwich and other items.  The food was underwhelming, but again, that's not the big reason why you come, so it's a minor demerit.  The staff continued service during the performances, but it was more difficult to get the staff's attention (as you would expect).  My suggestion is to arrive and eat early, then sip a drink during the music.

The reason people come to the Bluebird is to hear live music.  I've heard all of the legendary stories of epic performances in the "listening room" setting.  However, on the night I visited, the artists left something to be desired.  I don't want to criticize anyone who performs and puts themselves out there for others to listen to.  However, I will say that the group we saw was not up to the standard that I expected from the venue's reputation.  The other guests with me had visited the Bluebird multiple times, and all agreed that this was the worst performance they had seen.  Without going into specifics, the music was more juvenile than I expected, and the constant pandering to "Nashville" TV fame was extremely annoying.  I get it,  you're on the show... You don't need to remind me every 5 minutes!

I read an article online that described happiness as someone's expectations minus her reality.  Under that framework, Bluebird Cafe didn't measure up on the night I went.  However, I would go back and hear a different set of artists perform.  To summarize, only visit if you have reservations, and hope that you hear a strong artist or two.  Without the good music, there's nothing to fall back on.

Hashtag; Serena, I'm sorry. 

This 5 star rating is a rating of my actual experience here, factoring in alcohol,  and not an overall assessment of the establishment as a whole. As i was in no position to do so. 

Let me preface this by saying this was a 2am,  3 sheets to the wind, stumbling home stop for a burger after partying down for a few hours. 

The joint is done up real cool, I like the divey feel, and how the band's stage is situated so you have to walk past it to get to the rest of the bar. Feels like you've got a rock'n soundtrack to the beginning and end of your time there. 

The Staff:  In all honesty I don't remember much, BUT I do remember the lovely bartender Serena (sp?) being galacticly tolerant and gracious to me despite my drunken jackassery. Seriously, I was a L7 wanker. Serena,  let me publicly apologize for whatever rude or absurd ramblings I subjected you to. (I was able to recall your name because one thing I do remember is going ON AND ON about how your name reminded me of the show FireFly and Serenity).  

The Food: The bacon cheeseburger we had was AMAZING! .. and i think there were some tater tots, but I can't be sure. 

Overall, it's totally worth stopping in and trying it out.

This is a pretty good meet up spot. The food, its average. The atmosphere, I really like. I came here to meet girls for drinks one evening. The cellar was super loud and difficult to hear people across the table. I ordered the trio guac. The pineapple one was my favorite. Like I said, good not great. 

Brunch was definitely the better option for me personally. I'd recommend asking for a table not next to the stage is available. They do have $15 unlimited mimosas. Not super strong, but hey! They're $15! I ordered the enchiladas. My friends ordered the breakfast tacos and the chicken biscuit with gravy. I didn't try the tacos but she said they were pretty good. I liked the biscuit and enchiladas. Brunch also comes with biscuits and a jam or sorghum butter. I wasn't a fan of the jam but the better was great!

Overall, I'd come here again. Not my first choice but they have a decent happy hour.

Your luck with getting a reservation isn't too high! I was online in the queue waiting long before 8am, randomly placed in line at 8am, and by 8:08am the tickets were completely sold out. So sad! I know it would have been amazing. It would be better if the site recognized and honored who first was on the page rather than randomly placing people. Oh well!

Reservation process is ABSOLUTELY AWFUL. Don't waste a minute with these guys. I rearranged my flights to make sure I was online at 8am CST and got into room at 805 - May 10 was already SOLD OUT!! So frustrating. It's one time my wife is in Nashville and I did everything they told me about to get tix. The game's rigged. Don't waste your time.

Went to this place with my wife for an evening meal.  We were not greeted by anyone, even though there was only a small crowd that night.  Still, we decided to give it a try.  After a lengthy wait for some sort of acknowledgment that we were there, I went up to the bar to get some menus.  The bartender ignored me and continued to flirt with several young ladies.  Two young couples came in and were attended to very promptly.  At that point, I decided that we were too old for this place and got up and left. 
We will not be back.

They claim they have the best burger ever. I didn't think it was anything special. The decor is cool and the girl at the register was really sweet. The burger wasn't bad and it was a good late night snack. I just peeked into the bar half, so I can't really judge that aspect of this place.

Aaahhhhhhh!!!!! Now this is what Country's all about "Ya'll"!!!!!  Unbelievable....can't believe I'm witnessing what I'm seeing!!!!  This place is INSANE!!!!!  Wall to wall people on all 3 floors!!!!!  I LOVE IT!!!!!!  Amazing place in glorious Nashville!!!  .  As someone local told me...."Nashville's got such soul...I love it!!"  I couldn't Agree more!!!!

Hands down the worst experience I've ever had in a bar. Bartender stood, leaning against the wall, watching the band, while chewing on a straw, and ignored us. When I asked if we could order drinks, she said "Yes, what do you want?" However, she never took a step toward us. We had to ask for a beer list, which was placed near us, but not given to us, while she looked every where but at us. I asked her if it was too much trouble, and she just said, "No, I asked what you wanted." We just left, and didn't get to enjoy what sounded like a great band. We have been touring the state, eating and drinking, and tipping very well for good service. Not here, though!

Honky Tonk/Bar.
This place has a special place in my heart because it's the first Nashville-bar I walked in to. And I was not disappointed. It's divey with great music and bartenders.
I prefer the first floor but it can be really crowded.
Don't forget to try their applepie shine!

One of the best local spots in Nashville! Regardless which day of the week you are looking for a good time, check out the original Tin Roof on Demonbreun. Live music most days of the week, with another side ("Green Room") that has DJs on the weekends. Bartenders and Servers are great, and will ensure you are taken care of! Don't miss out on the hot wings, some of the best in town. Happy Hour is 2-7, and my go to when I visit is a chicken quesadilla and a side of cheese dip. Great spot to watch sports, especially the local teams. They will put the sound on for most big games for Vols or Preds, which is not always the case for sports bars. 

Also, Sunday Funday has become a big thing in Nashville with everyone starting at brunch and spending the afternoon doing some day-drinking. Tin Roof has been one of the best Sunday Funday spots for several years with a DJ starting mid-afternoon. You're guaranteed to have a good time at Tin Roof on a Sunday... don't miss it!

This review is for Bingo and cocktails--we had SO MUCH fun!!!  The bingo guys made our night!  Thank you so much for putting this on!  The music was great and the calling was a colorful delight.  We were never thirsty and the trip home (yay, Uber!) is a happy blur, so the staff is aces in my book!  I'm certainly not sporty, so I had no idea we had cruised into Nashville during the Music City Bowl, so this trip had more than it's fair share of surprises--This night was a GREAT surprise!  The Stone Fox's bingo night WAS right up my alley.  Thanks everyone!!!

We stopped here mainly because it was one of the few places on the strip that our 14 year old daughter could get into after 6pm.

We all ordered burgers, I got the double wide of course. There was no line to order, which I guess we got lucky because not 10 minutes later there was about 15 people in line waiting.

We were also lucky to be able to grab a booth on a busy friday night.

The burgers were very good. Thick patties, and perfectly sloppy. Cooked perfectly.

The live music was also nice to have while we ate. The place is separated into a bar on one side and eats on the other. The walkway between the 2 makes it easy to eat and also hear the music.

Very fun place.

Well worth the wait. We got there Monday for open mic and although we were 1 1/2 hours early we didn't make the cut..............to our great fortune. Later we arrived 2 hours early for a 2 hour show (haven't done that in quite a while) having no idea what a treat we were in for. This place is tiny and they will find a way to cram up to the limit of allowed by law.
It's "Blue Monday" and the house band is playing out of this world. I recognize a bad ass bass player that played for Ashley Cleveland when she was down here in Austin (the live music capital of the world) and in the back I see someone familiar. HOLY SHIT, it's Joe Bonamassa on a guitar in the background. He just happened to "pop in" and join the set. The band later asks a couple of other famous musicians to come on stage and play too.
Sometimes miracles happen and you happen to be in the right place at the right time.

I ordered the catfish tacos and a side of fries and they were both delicious!  The slaw they had on the tacos was second to none, and the catfish was fried to perfection. Service was fast and attentive. The bar downstairs looks like my new favorite place, can't wait to come back and try it!

This is a place that I've never thought of eating at but it was AMAZING! I will definitely be returning. The food was well prepared and the service was excellent. The ambience was southern and lovely. 

Our group of four enjoyed  the humus and hot chicken bites. I ordered the grill cheese dunk with the tomato soup, savory and delectable. I cannot say enough. 
The cocktails were creative and love just about everything about this great gem of a spot!

We went here for brunch yesterday.  We ordered chicken fried chicken with biscuits and sausage gravy.  The gravy was watery and had no sausage in it.  It was ready too quickly to have been prepared in any way other that microwave.  The chicken was dried out and tasteless.  My husband was served eggs that were full of cracked shells.  Very disappointing meal.  Bloody Mary's were great but for a bill of over $100 with drinks we should have gotten edible food.
Amazing singers, I actually prefer this place than the ones on Broadway. The songs they played have a wide variety. I love how everyone was sitting in circles, It really feels like one big family.

Stone Fox: I wanted to like you! I might try coming back for another show, but I'll just order drinks from the bar.

I try not to judge a place from an experience with 1 bad server. However, ours informed us he was leaving so we would have to close out, and did not change us over to another server. This is after he took 20 minutes after we ordered a pitcher and he informed us they were out of PBR drafts so essentially we were SOL. 

Uh...couldn't he just have given us over to another server? 

When my boyfriend went up to pay at the bar, the bartender was snotty & informed us we would have to chase our server down (God knows where he was at this point; even though he had conveyed quite the sense of urgency that we had to pay RIGHT NOW). 

I completely understand wanting to leave at the end of your shift, but that doesn't mean taking the frustrations of the day out on your customers.

This will now go down in history as one of my favorite venues in the country. The acoustics are incredible. Such a warm, intimate environment. We hit up the Bluebird for Open Mic Monday and Mike Henderson band. Open Mic was fantastic. The talent in this town is unbelievable. Then Mike Henderson band was phenomenal, playing blues covers and getting the house rocking. I'm so happy we stopped here!

Tootsie's is a very lively place!

I only had a short stay but had a fun time. Tootsie's has 3 floors of live music, so get the benefit of choosing which you like best! You can also duck out onto their balcony, which was my choice to just converse with friends outside the crowd. Drinks were expensive, but you are paying for the experience.

I visited on Monday, April 2, 2018 around 2:30 in the afternoon. I have known for a while this is an iconic place in Nashville, and I have always wanted to go and say I have been.  I love the history that artists used to play a set at the Ryman Auditorium, and then use the alley entrance to come and drink and sing at Tootsie's. 

There are 3 floors. We entered through the front.  The bottom floor was very full with patrons at the bars and tables listening to the band. We didn't see the third floor.  We ended up sitting at a table on the second floor. The guy who was singing was very good, and provided great entertainment. 

Our waitress was nice, but it was obvious she was tried and pretty fed up already. 

My mom and I ordered the Philly Steak Sandwich with fries and split it ( $11.00). She ordered a Diet Coke, and I ordered a Jack Daniels and Coke. I believe our total was somewhere around $24. The fries were really good.  The philly was good.  Pretty much what you would expect from a bar. 

The building is showing its age...run down a bit and not very clean. But, that is part of the charm. It is a very old bar, you just have to realize that before you go. 

With all of the patrons, televisions, and the bands, it can get pretty noisy.

I would go back for drinks and to hear some bands.  I would probably try some of the other food next time.

This place was the worst dining experience I've had thus far in Nashville. I'm a little bit of a food snob, but it's hard not to be when you have so many great restaurants around you. The Sutler is definitely not one of them. It took us 3 HOURS from start of meal to checks, mainly because our server was non-existent throughout the meal. We waited 45 minutes at the end because we couldn't find her to ask for a check. The food is absolutely awful and it's a shame they get away with charging what they charge for it. I've had better meals at Roberts on lower broad. About the only saving grace was that the bands playing from Belmont we're really great. Still, I'd never come back and don't waste your money on the horrible food.

Well, this was certainly an interesting spot on the Nashville Broadway tourist trap...err... bar circuit.  I visited Tootsie's over Christmas when the weather was unseasonably warm.  I had a good time and got to experience what brings people to Tootsie's.

To start, Tootsie's is a multi-level bar that features live music and a large upstairs patio that overlooks the Bridgestone Arena and Music City Center.  It's part of a strip of bars that feature music and cater to tourists in the area.  

The interior of Tootsie's is unremarkable.  The decor is what you would expect, and the place has a more run-down vibe than some of the newer bars across the street.  I don't mean that as an insult - Tootsie's has a dive bar vibe, and that's a good thing because it is a change of pace from a lot of the other bars nearby.

The top floor is where I spent most of my time, and the deck offers a great view of the street below as well as the Arena across the way.  I enjoyed being on the patio, and there was a live band that played on the top floor.  It was a lot of fun to hangout, to the extent that the rest of the bar was a bit of a letdown.  Because of the unusual weather, Tootsie's was crowded on the day I visited, but the staff handled it well.  There wasn't a problem splitting tickets, but the waitress did forget one beer.  She apologized and gave it to us for free, which was great.

The food and drinks at Tootsie's are about what you would expect for the area:  They are serviceable but overpriced.  I understand that you are paying for the music and atmosphere, but it was a little too touristy for me.  Some of the bartenders were trying way too hard with their appearances, while the guys were lackadaisical unless a pretty girl needed a drink.  My whiskey shot came in a sad little plastic cup that was *barely* half full.  For the exorbitant price, I expected a little more liquor or at least a shot glass so I would feel l like I was getting my money's worth.  My beer was too warm, which is probably a problem with the lines from the keg to the well. The food was bar quality.  My only complaints were the price relative to the quality.

Overall, I enjoyed Tootsie's for what it was - an overpriced bar with a great view.  I would recommend it if you are in tourist mode, but there are far better places to go unless you just want to be on Broadway.  It wasn't my scene, but I can see why others might enjoy it.  It's certainly better than some of the alternatives in the the area!

I was worried about seeing a show here with all the negative reviews but it was awesome. We went about 2 hours early to do the free whiskey tasting and the $5 wine tasting before eating at café fontanel. Nothing was overly crowded and we were able to get right in all three. Cafe fontanel was just ok for me but nice to have a place onsite all within close walking distance. We took our beach chairs that sit on the ground into the music venue. There really was not a bad place you could sit. We were there to see Trampled by Turtles. The music was fantastic and the background of the stage was gorgeous. We stayed till the very end of the show and getting out was no problem at all.

As much I love the music- NEVER AGAIN-the staff is SO UNEDUCATED!! The bar staff is SO rude and professional. !!!! The MOST unprofessional staff I have ever met( 20 + years in the business)   Tootsies - teach your staff cuz last night was a $hit show and u allowed it. Tonight- sober but wanted to see (Anthony orio) amazing.  18 yr old told me to leave.  Wasn't even drinking.  But last night- the bouncer- at 1am apologize to me cause it was a $hit show and would not remove the drunk bumpingon her boy and crashing into us!!!.  No CONTROL just a ton of ego!! BBB next ( hire better staff) EVERYONE ELSE- REDNECK RIVERA  BETTER ALL AROUND!!!  Guarentee no response or a delete!!

The history, the atmosphere, the nostalgia... The service exceeded my expectations. I had goosebumps just knowing the history. My lunch was delicious. If you're into history, good food and great service, you should check this place out. Sit at the counter for the full experience.

I hadn't been to The Stone Fox in a little while so I ventured across town and had a meal. And I was disappointed to see the King Rabbit Bowl was gone. It was an extremely tasty dish for someone, like me, trying to be a little more vegetable conscious. But alas, I got the fantastic cheeseburger with the house pimento cheese and was flabbergasted with the taste. My side salad with the citrus vinaigrette was also a fine substitute for the King Rabbit. I also got a free coffee for literally just waiting a few minutes. I've always loved the place and will continue to visit!

I wanted to wait a couple of days to see if my anger subsided in regards to my treatment at Tootsies.  I came here with a group of friends expecting to have a good time on Friday February 12 2016, not expecting to be singled out because I am African American.  We got into the line that was set up outside the bar, and the line seemed to be moving fairly quickly.  As I observed the security person outside, he seemed to check a person's ID and then let them in the bar without any type of trouble.  Once I got to the front of the line, I observed more of the same, the bouncer was letting everyone in without being searched with a wand.  Once I got to the front of the line, he asked to search me with a wand, when he had not searched anyone else ( with the exception of the guy standing right in front of us ) previously.  The thing that incensed me the most, was that the person he searched was in a group of four, and he only searched the one guy out of the group right before he asked me to dump everything out of my pockets.  It seems like he was making a scene about searching the guy right before me, so I could not say that I was being singled out, when it was obvious that I was being singled out.  How could he explain that he let the other three guys in without searching them?  Was it the way I was dressed?  I hope not, because I was wearing tennis shoes, skinny jeans (that fit), and a grey Chicago Bulls hoodie.  I am sure that I appeared to be thugging out in my group of mostly Caucasian friends.  I am seriously angered, hurt, and upset that I was treated this way.  No one deserves to be singled out to be searched, especially on the basis of their race.  The other people in my group ( who were mostly Caucasian, one was Hispanic ), were not asked to be searched at all.  I will never go here again, and will recommend to anyone in the Nashville area to not support an establishment that uses such practices to single out people due to their race.

Beer was cold and the live music was great!
Good times ! Keep your expectations low and enjoy!

This place is a Nashville establishment. Each floor has different music (live bands) and it is packed - even during the day there's people in there. It was super fun though and the music was great. We didn't end up staying that long just because it was so, so full, but it's worth checking out, definitely. Fun place, good tunes, tonnes of people.

Came for lunch at 11:50am it now 1:40pm... we ordered french fries and buffalo wings the moment we sat down.... Slowest service on Demonbreun for lunch. Make sure you have a few hours to blow if you decide to go to Tin Roof

Went there a couple of weekends ago. All right place. Only commenting here because I've been trying to track down a credit card I may have left there. After a few voice mails, someone did call me back and was courteous and helpful. Amending my review accordingly.

A friend and I (we both work downtown) decided to try Woolworth on Fifth for lunch a couple of weeks ago. We started with the corn fritters with peri peri sauce, which were delicious. My friend got the Southern Caesar (country ham, fried okra, and black strap), which was mediocre at best. It was just pretty bland and very underwhelming. She also got a side of the bird pepper mac and cheese, which wasn't spicy at all and was just okay. I tried a bite and I was fine with just trying a bite (if that mac and cheese had been good I'd have been pointing at things around the room and sneaking bites of her mac and cheese). I got the brisket sandwich, which was okay but nothing to write home about. Generally my impression of the food is that it's fine but overpriced. I'll be honest - the messaging and imaging of this restaurant confuses me. If you go to their website, you'll find a history page that tells the stories of sit ins at Nashville lunch counters during the civil rights movement, including violent counter protests (to the sit ins) at this Woolworth on February 27, 1960. I guess I'm glad that they're acknowledging the history of the restaurant, but it begs the question - given the history of lunch counters in the South in general and this Woolworth in particular, why open a retro, vintage lunch counter that glamorizes the period? If the food were good, I might spend more time exploring my feelings about this issue. As the food isn't really good, I'm excused from having to think about this further as I probably won't be back.

Lived in Middle TN all my life, so I have fond memories of Starwood (and now Ascend). Fontanel has a lot of work to do before they begin to meet expectations..

Good: Didn't take that long for us to get in and out of the venue as others experienced. But, we did get there an hour + early.

Meh: Based on the number of people filing out early, we left before the encore to ensure we didn't sit in line forever. There's one way in and one way out.

Bad: The GA seats suck. They are not only on a slight incline, but also to the left of the stage. Literally all we could see was stage equipment. If anyone stood up, and I'm talking many feet down the 'hill', you couldn't see a thing. The best view of the event was over near the porta-johns. 
'Bathrooms' had very little lighting. It's hard enough to use a porta-john, but in the dark it becomes downright treacherous. 
Food was expensive, tall boys were $9 and a small mixed drink was $11. 

We paid $50 for these tickets and it was the worst venue we've ever been to. We will definitely not be back. I don't care who it is. No bueno.

I agree with some other reviews, when you try so hard to look like you're not trying, sometimes you end up just not trying at all. Love the menu and venue and also like that it's in the nations... but Geeze Louise they are slow, generally inattentive, and often screw up orders.  All for a fairly steep price. I hear they are good for live music though, so maybe just go there for a show and some drinks?

I couldn't believe how small this place was. We got there an hour ahead of time and luckily made it in on a Thursday. We actually got better seats because we were the latest ones in. The talent is amazing. It was a great experience. I definitely recommend it if you're visiting Nashville.

HORRIBLE PLACE!!!!! I had to talk to the manager twice and NOTHING was done. Service is horrible and the bartenders are B's I had one tell her coworker not to sell me anything because she didn't like me RUDE..... manager's did nothing. Don't bother

Pop up Brad Paisley performance on a Sunday- bouncer at the top of the stairs with long beard and glasses was incredibly rude and letting people leave while letting no one else enter. Understandable that it was crowded and could have been a fire violation, but don't treat others differently and make special exceptions for them (which he did multiple times and was probably why they went over capacity, and this was not only noted by myself, but everyone else that was patiently waiting). Terrible experience, which is sad for such a true Nashville establishment. Poor event planning and rude staff.

I've only been to the Woods Amphitheater at Fontanel once so far, for the Barenaked Ladies/Guster/Ben Folds concert.  Having grown up with an outdoor amphitheater in St Louis, I've had lots of experiences with outdoor concerts.  Woods at Fontanel was fine--there were pros and cons to the theater that made the concert we saw there both great and not as good as it could be.

The Pros:
-Nice variety of concerts and performers--there really is something for everyone.
-It's a small space compared to the amphitheater I'm used to, so there's really no such thing as a bad seat
-The sound was great throughout the entire concert.  Consistent, loud enough but not too loud, and a nice balance of instruments and voices.
-The vibe.  Everyone is relaxed, easy-going, and there for a good time.
-Free parking.
-Food trucks and fun contests on the way into the concert space.

The Cons:
-If you purchase actual seats, there is no slope to the grass to allow for stadium-style seating.  If the people in front of you are standing, there is no way for you to see the stage.  That's a major problem in my book.
-The seats are placed VERY close together, uncomfortably so.  I need some space, particularly when it's hot outside and the concert is sold out.
-Getting out of the parking lot after the concert was a mess.  There was no one directing traffic, so it took us 45 minutes to finally leave the venue.  
-Porta-potties instead of actual bathrooms, and running water sink--without soap.    Gross, especially in the summertime heat and humidity.
-High-priced snacks and beverages.  This is to be expected at a venue such as this, so it's not a huge surprise, but it did keep us from buying dinner or a beverage during the concert.
-The delicious Cafe Fontanella is closed by the time most concerts let out; given that they serve pizza and alcohol, the restaurant would make a killing if it stayed open later into the evening on concert nights.

I'd return to the Woods Amphitheater at Fontanel to see a band I love (like BNL), though I'd think twice before attending a concert just because.
What a cool place, well worth the 1 1/2 hour wait outside. It was quaint,  food was great ,and so close to Sons n Britches, the great group performing that night!!!!

I came in tonight with a group of 15 ladies; I was over charged an extra drink, when I wrote that on the check my entire party was kicked out. I was love to talk to a manager about this, so I don't have to go through my bank to clear up the misunderstood.

Having moved to the nations recently, I was really pumped about this place and have given it chance after chance.... Tonight my husband and I got the 'meatball with macaroni ' .... Meatballs seasoned with Greek seasoning (they put this is everything) and macaroni in red sauce. It was terrible and I give up on this place. We left and got White Castle. I give it two stars because it's a great atmosphere. They need to find a new chef.

Entrees were excellent.  Dessert was lacking...I would skip it.  Potted smoke was delicious and odd at the same time.  Service was decent but needs some fine-tuning.  It was a little slow and our Asian server was using a horrible fake southern accent.  Would go back.

I like to think that the Stone Fox is an upscale dive bar. It's an old repurposed house (like many other fine establishments in this city) and has ample seating, indoors and outdoors. The patio is a nice place to enjoy an evening drink. A rich collection of local craft ales, and regular beers, tantalize the tippler at their tiny bar. While their food selection is quite good, I was left hollow at their brunch choices. The portions were tiny, and nothing to write home about. There is a place for a live band, and dance sessions erupt periodically. The crowd that hangs out here is "different", by which I mean no suits or pretty clothes.
DELICIOUS food, good atmosphere and great service. Best French fries. Private party option.

Brought in 2014 at this place and had one of the best nights during my visit to Nashville by far. The place was rockin' so ordering drinks was a bit of a thing, i let my much more attractive friend Marlene stand at the bar in my place to get attention first (i'd like to think it worked).

Everyone there was hella cool, very nice to me although most people are nice to you when they find out you're from New Orleans and they're all just as drunk as i am, i got an incredible amount of compliments on my attire from people left-n-right. There was one guy who liked what i had on so much he asked if it was cool for him to put on my jacket, hat and scarf and take pictures (drunken good times). 

I liked the fact that there was nice space for a dance-floor, a stage plus an outside area that was perfect for taking those much needed breaks after straight minutes of drunken boogie-ing inside. 

And whoever the DJ was there on NYE 2014 was wreckin' it! He was playing oldies but they were hella groovy and kept everybody moving! I really enjoyed the vibe of the place that night, i'll forever have those good memories to hold.

Wowzers that was a damn good burger. Probably the best burger I've had. Like ever. Seriously. You want a good burger go here. I don't know about the rest of the menu, but why try anything else, really. Just get a burger. It's magic meat in your mouth.

I came during the day when I had a break during a conference I was attending. It was hotter than the sun out and the bartender quickly came and asked what we wanted to drink. Since I needed a minute to look over the drink menu I said I would take a water for now. Little did I know they only had bottles and you would be charged. I've never been forced to buy bottle water in the US, only abroad so it already set me on the wrong foot. The place was cool, but I just didn't get the hype. I think the waitress/bartender was a bit rude and it just overpowered my true feeling of this place. I'm hoping to check it out again and maybe have a better experience.

This place is a complete joke and a rip off. Bachelor parties beware, we reserved the space behind the stage and they took advantage of us, ripped us off and the bouncer attacked the bachelor when we were just trying to settle up our bill. We were a group of adults that not bothering anyone, but they just went crazy on us. 

Also FYI, they do not treat their employees well. They take advantage of their customers and of the waitresses. 

Bottom line, go somewhere else. This rat whole urinal cake smelling bar sucks.
