Best place for live music good food and best craft beer & cocktails. Not to mention their serious collection of aged scotch/whiskeys!
When you visit head down stair for a game of pool in the parlor or a lounge cocktail in the speakeasy. Something for everyone!

I was really excited to try out this cool new spot for Mother's Day brunch yesterday.  The place seemed hip and right up my alley food wise, with some innovative and different things on the menu.

My family were the first patrons to arrive and besides us, there was one other couple there for a good 30 minutes before anyone else showed up.  I expect great service when there are more wait staff than there are patrons.  Our waitress was nice enough, but not too quick on refilling drinks.  I sat there with an empty water for quite sometime.  I'm willing to overlook an empty water glass.  What I'm not willing to overlook is waiting 30 minutes for food in an empty restaurant and then getting served freezing cold breakfast tacos and petrified iceberg cold potatoes.

I wish I could say that was the worst of it, but that came when a kitchen staff member walked out, plunked down my food (cold) and walked off with no food served to my husband.  We sat there for 5 minutes before the waitress walked over to ask how everything was (I guess she failed to notice my husband had no food at all).  We mentioned the fact that we were missing his food and she walked back in the kitchen only to come out and inform is that the waffle machine was broken and he would have to order something else.  There was no apology (she did take it off the bill but never offered any apology).  It was unbelievable especially since the food had already been served.  He ended up ordering something else and it was fine, but the experience was already ruined. We were treated like a complete after thought.

I usually give restaurant more than one shot. But they blew it so bad here that I definitely won't be back.  It's sad because I love local, fresh, and innovative places, but the food was mediocre at best and as I said before, COLD...and the customer service was atrocious!  Happy Mother's Day to me!

Had Sunday Bluegrass Brunch at The Sutler and it did not disappoint! Awesome service staff; ours (Rachel) was incredibly friendly, attentive and kept our mimosas full. Food came out very fast and was exactly what we ordered, despite some picky vegetarian substitutions on my part. The biscuit Benedict was amazing. The bluegrass band was top notch and added to the super authentic honkey-tonk atmosphere of the place. We wished every restaurant/bar in Nashville were more like this!

The food has been great: Tasty, seasoned well, served hot, on time. 
The food has been bad: Bland, cold, sloppy, slow.

The service has been perfect: Friendly, timely, professional.
The service has been terrible: Short, slow, forgetful, careless.

Sometimes a 5, sometimes a 1. 

Consistently inconsistent. 

Good luck, when you go.

Tootsie's is a legend in Nashville, so you sort of have to take it for what it is. Live music, unfinished wood floors, people every-freaking-where you turn, and crappy beers. It's fine, but not my scene. Our friends in town were excited to visit, and it seemed they enjoyed singing along to the music. The many bachelorette parties and hook ups on the prowl around us also seemed to be enjoying themselves. 

I hopefully won't be back, but only because it's not my scene. If you like a dive bar and live music and don't mind insane crowds, you'll probably dig it!

After asking around for must have a beer at during out crawl in downtown Nashville, we made it a point to go in here. Walked in, walked right out.. Not because it sucked, but because it was SUPER busy. Didn't want to become sober waiting for a drink. Haha.  They must be doing something right! Maybe next time:)

If it were not for the wait in the hot sun before we were let in I would give this place 5 stars.  We went on open mike night.  I loved hearing all these aspiring stars.  No stars showed up to play.  I wonder if that really happens.  But this is a must do in Nashville.
3 Hughes floors of great food and drinks. Some of the best musicians are always here as well

On the plane ride over to Nashville I sat next to a local who told me that her #1 must do for visitors was a trip to to the Bluebird Cafe. Sadly I hadn't made a reservation beforehand, so I convinced my friend to take a chance on the no reservations show on Sunday. 

The Cafe, a 90-seat music club that opened in the early eighties, is famous for intimate, acoustic shows. Some performers are established singer/songwriters, and others perform hit songs written by other artists. We arrived about 45 minutes early for the show to a SUPER long line, but luckily we made it inside right before the cutoff (seriously -- we were numbers 88 and 89)!! There is no cover but there is a $7 food and drink minimum per person. I ordered a few beers. The food that I saw and tasted was nothing special. I'd eat beforehand and stick to drinks.

The space really was intimate and people were nearly sitting on top of each other. Groups were sharing tables and some people were seated up against the walls. We were just a few rows back from the band, Two Story Road, a husband-wife duo with some amazing credentials. They played a mixture of covers and original songs and were pretty incredible.

The shows are only an hour at The Bluebird, but it is for sure worth the wait. If you are going to Nashville I would see if there's a show you can buy tickets for ahead of time (I think they release them 1 week in advance and they sell out almost immediately). Otherwise, get there about an hour before and be prepared to wait for a great show!

Thanks be to the chef/s at Woolworths. The chicken was skinny and tasty. My spouse had the pork chops. Truly great food. The price was what I expected, but the quality service and great food will make this a great date night for the Ryman. The history of the building was enough to fill my heart. I only have two thumbs to hold up. Bravo.

I have found my new neighborhood bar! The Stone Fox! 

I have been hearing a lot of great things about The Fox over the past months, but have never made it in. All I can say is that I shouldn't have put it off for so long. 

What I like about it so much are the two patios. One in the front and a larger one out back. Great for these nice Spring/Summer days. The smoking policy on the porches can leave you gagging while eating dinner, this knocks my rating down at least half a star. You shouldn't be able to smoke where other non-smokers are eating. Just saying. 

For a place I consider mainly a bar, their food menu is solid. They also have a few vegetarian options that are quite good. I chose to skip it dessert, but it sounded damn good. Maybe next time. Their draught beer selection is...alright. About 10 rotating taps, but not nearly as beefy as it could be. Though I am never disappointed in the limited selection. 

Also, check out their music calendar. Tons of live music almost every night. 

Solid neighborhood pub. I cant wait to get to know you better Fox!

What's NOT to like about the Bluebird Cafe? Other than the fact that purchasing tickets is akin to an Olympic event where time is of the essence, which I didn't deduct stars for, it's a fantastic listening room with a calendar of A+ performers. As mentioned, it's a listening room, and the audience respects the performer/s (who they are in close proximity to considering the limited space) by not talking when the performance begins.

P.S. Try the coconut cake. You'll thank me later.

What a sh*thole.  Took 45 minutes for jalapeño fritters that tasted like a homeless guys as*hole.  They call out food numbers in no discernible order.  There are at least 3 people in front of me that got the wrong order after waiting 30+ minutes.  Stay away. Save yourself time and morning after diarrhea.

$5.50 for yuengling?  Big deal, I'm on vacation!  Stick a few bucks into your pocket for the restroom attendant (and I love this), very European and keeps things nice and tidy!  Absolutely LOVED the music, the crowd and was everything (and more) than I expected.

The crowd danced, sang and had a ball!  I do love a crowded venue!   DH had a great time and he's not a country music fan!  Cannot wait to return!

My favorite bar in Nashville. There's always something going on, happy hour is everyday from 2-7 and has really cheap beer! Also if you get a chance, the cheese fries are amazing!!!!! I'm obsessed. Only complaint is have of this place is that they run out of their draft selections quite often but for the price, you can't beat it!!
It's worth the wait to hang out on the first floor with the live music! Get the fried string beans!

Love the rooftop- been here multiple times. But this last time was a little different... We had a friend in from our home town. And when the boys bought their drinks the waitresses gave a stink about no tip, loudly to each other, then up front to our friends. I'll tell you- it was a Tuesday afternoon- girls? With that attitude? That's why you got no tip, and that a why you work the weekday shift. So don't come to my out of town friends for money when you chose bartending as your current profession. Thanks for the first impression. Good day.

This was such an awesome experience. Got tickets to the Friday night songwriters round and it was amazing.  Dennis Matkowsky, Mike Reid, Emerson Hart and Lucie Silva each took turns playing their music and sharing heartwarming stories. It was truly magical. The service was excellent and it was the best experience during our trip to Nashville.

Gourmet food with a come add you are ambiance! ! However,  I would recommend to tell them to go easy on the salt! ! Awesome and unique menu! !!!!!! Delicious !! Highly recommend the trout! ! However tell them to go easy on the salt,  all of my friends loved it,  but it was a bit salty,  other than that,  great atmosphere! !!

My friends and I were SO happy to get lucky enough to snag tickets online for a Sunday songwriters night here! It's quite the online process and kind of luck of the draw to get tickets, so we were pumped.

The place is very tiny inside which I wasn't expecting to be AS small as it was, but the tables are laid out with enough room to get by. We were seated at table 1 which was a 6 person high top and not the most comfortable, BUT - we had a great view of the stage.

Service here was phenomenal. Even though it's a listening room and you have to be super quiet, the servers did a great job of staying on top of if you need anything while still respecting the singers on stage.

Food is sub-par, but I kind of expected that. I would recommend grabbing dinner somewhere else beforehand and just ordering a drink or two to meet the $10 minimum required on a Sunday night show. I got the chicken tenders with fries and they were just...meh. My friend got the quesadilla which didn't look too great either. Other friends got a salad, and it was just nothing exciting.

The experience was great and the songwriters night lasted pretty late - it was about 8pm-11pm. 8 songwriters playing 3 songs each plus a special guest at the end. They start on time and move through without breaks, but expect to be here for a while!

Good place to bring guests from out of town. There is live music, a bunch of cowboy boots nailed/glued to the wall, decent cocktails and bunch of southern style foods. They recently started brunch which is pretty good - the biscuits are the best part. The main meals are OK but if you focus on the drinks and the music they'll make you feel good. The downstairs lounge is hip and full of  post grad people, mostly normcore not super hip but people that are cool to be around.

We were not impressed with this spot as we were "honky tonk" hopping down Broadway. The band was mediocre and constantly asked for tip money. Let your music do the talking! Also, the drink prices were much higher than other locations. 12 bucks for two miller lites!

A very casual spot.  So casual no one is in a rush, not even the service.  I think our server was related to Phoebe, from Friends.  "Do you know what you want to drink?" 
"No, do you have a drink menu?" Booze arrives 15 minutes later.  I'm sitting 5 feet from the bar. 
"Do you know what you want to order?"
"No, do you have a food menu?"...Oops, again!  Brunch was very good.  Get the deep fried French toast!

Waited 2 1/2 hours to get into the cafe - such an amazing atmosphere. I have been dying to visit this place ever since the show Nashville came out. The staff was fun, and the open mic night was very entertaining. I think we saw a few stars in the making!!

Stopped in here for a concert on a Friday night. What a gem this place is! It looks like an old house - very inviting. The interior is very relaxing and felt right at home. We opted for dinner & drinks as well - which were all fantastic. Especially loved the unique pimento cheese hushpuppies. And of course the show was superb. The sound and vibe of the concert was great. I will recommend this spot to all I know! Will be back for sure.

The tamales I had here were very good, whole ingredients instead of unrecognizable mush.  Chunks of chicken beans and corn with a side of salsa verde over sour cream.  They also had some great rum I've never tried before called Afrohead.  The service is great and I felt welcome immediately.  I will be back.

Tootsie's is the most notable of the bars on Music Row. That shouldn't mean overcharging for beer. 2 beers coming to $14.00??? I expect that in high priced city bars. Not on Honky Tonk row in Nashville. Other than the drink prices, the music was great, as was the atmosphere. Unfortunately, we went elsewhere after 1 drink. Drank for cheaper elsewhere and heard great music elsewhere also.

We loved our evening here! The atmosphere is wonderful, the service was so great and everyone we interacted with was kind, and the food was delicious! Every bite!! I had the braised short ribs and it was delectable, my husband had the burger and he said it was really good, our friends had the ribs and the pork chops. We started with a Brussel sprouts app and ended with the pecan pie for dessert. Our friends got cocktails, and they were really pleased with them and said they were unique. Oh my goodness- the cornbread/biscuit basket. We all just melted in our seats over those. Excited to try this place for breakfast!
A great honky-tonk full of history. It's a must whilst in Nashville

I'm so glad I got to experience the Bluebird Cafe. It's a small place situated in a random strip mall you would never expect it to be. We went for the Sunday night writers show. I was a little worried beforehand that we wouldn't get there in time and make the cut. But luckily we got there about an hour and 15 minutes early and got a spot in line. I believe we were around number 50 at that point and good thing because they were only allowing in 75.

As others have said you don't come here for the food, not that I can speak to it as we didn't order any. But what seemed to be coming out of the kitchen were some simple sandwiches and your standard fare of fried snacks. Since there is no cover charge or tickets they asked that we spend at least $7 on food/drink which was easy enough to do with a glass of wine.

It is very intimate inside and we got the last two seats in the place together at the bar. Everyone else's party had to split up into single seats situated throughout. But that doesn't seem to matter too much as you're there to listen to the music and not socialize. I thought all of the writers/performers of the evening were fantastic (probably because they have to audition to even perform there). It was a great way to hear some new and upcoming music. Definitely check it out if you have the time!

I loved this place. the history behind it the atmosphere the food all enjoyable. I got the pot roast and it was delicious! we also had their burger which they make their own jalapeno bacon. I will definitely be coming back

Wow. If I could give a half star I would. What is up with this place?! Horrible. I have been twice. The first time it took about 20-25 minutes. The second time we watched our drinks sit at the bar while our server walked by them 3 times and a total of 7 servers walked to the bar and still left them there. It took over 30 minutes to get a drink. Then there is the food. BOTH times our orders came out wrong. BOTH times there were issues with what was delivered. Very hard to understand why this place is getting the ratings it did. I literally cannot explain why we had two bad service and food experiences. 

Please believe me when I say that I wanted so badly to love this place that I went back even after a bad first experience. The atmosphere and vibe of the place is so adorable and cool, like the downstairs with the big band, and just in general- the concept is so cool. I will not take any of that away from them, but it did not overcome our overall negative experience.

I really believe this restaurant as not being effectively run, either in front or in back of the house. I think if they can find the right leadership to organize everyone, it would make a huge difference. I wish this place the best, but I will not be returning.

Great!! Chris Young dropped by and ordered a Few drinks and was in the back listening to the live music. Our waitress was on top of the drinks as well. Great spot, good music and laid back, friendly staff. A good place if you're not trying to be too fancy.
My bar drink was very good - it was just TOO freaking loud and crowded for me .... so I drank one and off I went

This is my second attempt to get reservations.  I got in their queue 12 hours before tix went up for sale, waited patiently for 14 minutes(once 8am rolled around), still sold out.

Both times were to see an old friend from out of state perform.  I'm sorry, but this ticket/reservation system is a joke.  It says it's a lottery/random spot in virtual line.  So, even with getting in the virtual line 12 ours in advance, I probably lost my reservation to someone who logged in minutes before 8am.

I don't think I will ever attempt to go the Bluebird again.

Not the greatest grilled cheese like we'd been told. Oh well. The sweet potato fries were gross too. 

The bartender was sweet and helpful. She helped me pick a beer that was pretty good since I'm new to beer. It was cool that there was live music. The guy was pretty good. 

Dive bar for sure. But cool.

Sutler's Bluegrass Brunch was a request from out of town guests. We had a great experience when we went last year, however, the $15 bottomless mimosas you are better off getting one off drinks. After I saw several other customers with lighter mimosas, I asked our server (Jenna) for a splash of champagne she went to the bar and added soda (vs. champagne) as my two bartender guests watch her do. Highly recommend the food, but maybe a more understanding waitress than Jenna...

This burger joint was expected to be better but I give it two stars. 
Probably was one of the worse places to come and it in Nashville. The only thing that was good was that I came with a group of friends and it was empty, so it was perfect for us to sit together. 

Needs to somehow make a major change or i believe it's not gonna make it.

Proud of the history established in the Woolworth in 5th for Desegregation by the "sit-in"! The restaurant portions are large, our food was good - just be aware the blacked ribs are very spicy! Very attentive wait staff! I would recommend and I would return!

We had so much fun here for open Mic night NYE week 2014. The getting in process is out of control but once you are in the music is great, the service is good and it's a fun and iconic experience. Go for it if you are in town!

Such a horrible place to go too. If you like to have fun and enjoy yourself, don't go here. Was relaxing and drinking water (it was my birthday) and was somehow kicked out yet had nothing to drink. Anyway, shitty people working there and the manager Wayne was even worse.

For all the hype, I was not impressed.

A small group - seven of us - went for a friend's birthday. The birthday boy summed it up - the place needs less hipness and more service.

It started out well enough. A couple of people had ordered drinks when we arrived, and encouraged us to try the Babs on a Budget. The waiter came back after a few minutes for our order, and my husband tried it. Boring Me had some ginger ale. Drinks took a few more minutes to get there, but came in cute mason jars, and everyone was happy.

20 minutes later, the waiter finally returned. He seemed annoyed that we ALL needed more drinks by that time. He brought them back, and seemed to need reminded that we might want to order food. We were getting hungry by that point, so we indicated that we would get an appetizer, but we would order at the same time. As soon as we mentioned the appetizer, he ran off to put in the order without getting our food orders.

A little while later, the pimento cheese appetizer arrived, delivered by the bartender. Pretty good. A little pricey for something served on saltines, but I guess that's part of the hipness of the dish.The cheese itself was tasty.

We were pretty hungry by the time the waiter returned to get our order. And then we waited and waited for the food. We all kept trying those little tricks you use in a restaurant. "I know when I come back from the bathroom, they'll be bringing the food out." 

We had been there more than an hour and a half by the time dinner finally came to our table. There were some apologies muttered in the meantime, but they didn't seem that sincere. Especially since our drink glasses kept getting empty. 

And everything was a mess. He didn't seem to know who had ordered what, or what sides came with each person's main dish. The girl to my left got the kale salad instead of the house salad. There was an unclaimed dish of macaroni. The birthday boy's burger arrived, with a promise that the fries would be out soon. And everything was cold as though it had been sitting, waiting to be delivered.

My husband's gumbo was okay. Really more like chili, and a little cold, but there would have been few complaints had it arrived in a timely fashion.

I have to say that my marrakesh kale salad was the highlight of the evening. Good flavor, good texture. Quite nice.

But my burger, my poor burger. I think Elsie would have been disappointed with her "favorite." It was cold and positively squishy where the juices had soaked into the bun. I ordered the BBQ sauce on the side, and it came on the side - and on the burger. I had ordered the burger medium - I know that's always a risk - but as I finished the last couple of bites, I realized that part of the squishiness was meat that hadn't gotten cooked at all. I scooped out some pink paste, closed my eyes and finished the rest.

The Chris Scruggs band lightened the mood at the end of the night with some killer classic country and western swing.

We walked out feeling better. Until we looked up on the back deck to see our server smoking and having a boisterous cell phone conversation. Which explained a lot.

wow... I'm so glad I drove over to Green Hills today to check out The Well Coffeehouse! First of all, the place looks awesome... huge, lots of room, but cozy and comfortable and welcoming... 

They use Square, so checkout was fast and easy... a few taps on my iPhone and I was done.  And I got 20% off for my first visit... And prices are super reasonable... $2.85 for a 12oz latte.

Now, this is what really impressed and appealed to me... they are non-profit, christian based, and focused on helping people around the world... 100% of profits go to their mission... I love it! 

Oh and I almost forgot... how was the the coffee??? It was fantastic... I had a latte... it was smooth, creamy and delicious... They use Just Love coffee beans which are great... and I'm pretty sure they use whole milk unless you ask for something else...

Great Job guys, keep it up! Be Blessed! I'll be back soon!

Tootsie's is overrated. Been here a couple of times with my friends and it's nothing special. Was once escorted out because my friend misfired a mayonnaise packet and the group behind us that it hit asked the bouncer to escort us out and he did, even though we apologized and explained it was an accident. Staff isn't friendly or understanding, bands really aren't very good. Check out ANY OTHER bar on Broadway.

Don't bother... Besides this place probably won't be there in six months anyway. Great concept but the idea got lost somewhere before execution.  Drinks, food and bluegrass, what could go wrong? Well let me tell you... parking is limited but that's not their fault, however everything else was... We waited for an hour for brunch on Sunday at 11:30am which is fine and for a good restaurant I understand that's primetime and that's also not the problem. Bloodys were bland, never saw the hostess seat anyone unless she knew them(we ended up sitting at the bar), people come for the bottomless mimosas and camp at the tables both inside and out but order no food, hmmm, bartender took my half drink and silverware away while I was still using them and the food was completely uneatable. I had the standard breakfast, my most favorite things in the whole world (eggs, bacon & fried potatoes with a biscuit and gravy) eggs and bacon were so greasy you couldn't eat them and the potatoes had some kind of mystery spice that made have no taste at all. Oh and btw gravy was from a jar...disgusting. Sorry Sultler, I was looking for more and was very disappointed. I won't be back.

Great drinks. Food. Music..  The tater tots are out of this world. My friend had hers smothered in cheese and chili. Mine just plain were good.  The bacon cheese burger was very good for a pre fixed burger but all the fixings were fresh and awesome

We stopped by for drinks at Tooties.  The employee at the door would not let my 63 year old father in because he did not have his license with him.  I sincerely appreciate that establishments need to check IDs for liability reasons and for safety.  However, this employee showed a complete lack of common sense.  I am 30 - if I didn't have an ID I would completely understand being turned away.  But, 62...  I feel sorry for this business because they lost the money we would have spent and ended up using next door.  Again, I fully appreciate safety but this person at the door was ridiculous.

Good spot to stop if you need to get a late night fill up. Tried the 5 alarm burger one night and bacon cheeseburger another night. The jalapeno puffs were the best thing we had. Can be a bit of line depending on the time you stop by. Once you order food comes out pretty fast. Staff was hit and miss, 2nd night seemed like they were less than thrilled to be there. I get it a bunch of drunks stumbling in to eat is less than desirable but I think I would expect that during the shift. Good food, not great but not bad.
Big crowds very tight. Several floors of music.  Very pricy for drinks.  Music and history was great.  Great to visit once.  Many other great ones down the hill

Went here for bluegrass brunch on a Sunday - waited about an hour, but for a brunch place, that's a good sign that people like it! I got the breakfast tacos which were delicious. Service could have been better but it was pretty busy that day. Nice live music while dining. :) Would definitely return!

I've lived in Nashville 8 months and tried to go to the Bluebird Cafe without a reservation twice. Once, the line was quite literally about 120 people! Needless to say, we didn't get in. 

Last week, my brother was visiting and I decided to make reservations. Do this. We went to the early "Round" show on a Saturday. Much like some reviewers have written: it was an experience truly beyond words. Powerful. My brother and I were moved and awed. The 5 musicians' that evening were musically and lyrically diverse. And, they were all fantastically gifted. The setting is intimate (our table was right next to the round) and quiet (it's all about the music here). 

There were only a handfull of Nashvillians in the audience, as the place has become a tourist go-to spot. No doubt, the ABC series Nashville, that regularly features the Bluebird, is partially responsible.  No matter though, the music and setting are real and authentic.  

If you are looking for a night out with drinks and chatting with some music in the background, this is not the place. This is a place you come to pay attention, be grabbed, and moved by the songs.

Live music on top floor great!...over priced drinks ($5 bud light, $8 well) eh guess that's ok...warm beer????!!?? Plus rude top floor bartender who would not take it back right after we bought it??...No thanks. Luckily most of us had a good buzz going by this time and it was our last stop of the night. I talked with another friend who had been there before and apparently warm beer is common at tootsies because they get so busy. They should really take care of that for the price they charge. Plus I should mention it was 24 degrees out, no reason for warm beer that night.

While the bars around Tootsie's are always bumping, even in the middle of the day, only one consistently has a line. And for good reason. Now while I spent at least a few minutes in more bars than I can remember in Lower Broad, there were some things that made Tootsie's stand out:

A giant fan on the top floor - it was humid as hell that weekend. Like, actual Hell. That fan was a lifesaver and us guys spent time rotating in and out of its blast.

A big open balcony, just to chill out at and people watch.

The best bands I'd heard all weekend. Not sure if we just got lucky, or Tootsie's really gets the best performers, but I was thoroughly entertained whenever we were here.

It just felt like a legit party on the top floor. Like I was at a concert that I didn't have to buy a ticket for.

Yes, it's crowded as hell, but for good reason. Sometimes it's just right to go along with the crowd.

Amazing experience and hands down my favorite part of Nashville so far. The listening room setting is incredibly intimate, the artists were so talented and truly engaging with the audience. Very cool to see where and how some of the songs I hear on the radio everyday come from. Definitely reserve tickets and keep in mind that it is a bit outside of Nashville (we were expecting it to be in downtown and it's not). The food was okay--we had the nachos-not bad but nothing special. The wine list was pretty decent and each glass was 7-8 dollars-very reasonable. A can't miss experience and I wish we could go back tonight!
Started out a 5 then my husband got ripped off in the third floor men's room by two guys charging people to use it !sucks check your rest rooms more often

This place is a great listening-room. I have been here three times so far. I always come here when someone is visiting us from out of town. 

First off, the lines here are ridiculous. Unless you have a reservation (which by the way, always opens and fills up to the brim by Monday morning), good luck getting in.I think after the third time being here though. I see people making reservations and flying in here all the time, but I have simply no idea as to how to make it happen. Sad. 

I have finally figured out what to do if you are unable to make reservations. Get here at like 4:00 p.m. (they open at 5:30 p.m. on somedays and 5:00 on the others, check the website!). Bring your iPad/iPhone/gadget of choice with you. Park your car and wait. Once you see one or two people showing up, go line up with your friendly gadget. Either remain on the gadget until doors open or talk to to crowd of people who will pile up around you. We have had some amazing conversations here with people from all over the world (Russia, New Zealand and Nepal! YEP.). 

Being seated is the biggest deal here. I felt like the next morning I was so proud to throw in "so I was at Bluebird last night.." in every conversation. (Ok, maybe not...)

$7 minimum on drinks and food. It's easy to meet. Their carrot cake is to die for. The biggest piece in the world and really, really, outrageously good. Nachos were good too. Overall, great experience. If I have the time and patience to wait, I'll come back again.

My friends and I were killing some time downtown before the Titans/Packers game a couple weeks ago and decided to stop here for a couple hours. Considering it was a Saturday afternoon on Broadway, it actually wasn't too busy inside. We were able to grab one of the booths that they have, which was nice. This is definitely more of a dive (although I've been to some places that were more dive-y than this) but it's not terrible. The beer is pretty cheap, and the bartenders are super friendly.

I went to the bathroom and there was an employee in there giving people soap and paper towels and stuff. That was definitely unexpected in this type of place, but I can appreciate it. I would definitely come back here again, and possibly try some of the food that people seem to think is decent. A good spot downtown if you're trying to avoid the crowds at some of the more popular bars.
Great atmosphere of tourists listening dancing to country and rock standards at this historic honky tonk bar. A hefty Jack Daniels on rocks in plastic cup is  $7.
Good old fun. Go for the music and crowd. Pass on the food. Make sure to floor hop. Great service!

Lousy place. Bartender would not put Masters on tv. Instead played a Condeleeza Rice interview on Golf Channel. Talk about clueless. Food was also crap. Chicken quesidilla special was terrible. No chicken in it. If you got a variation then it was 3 or 4 bucks more. (for onions? really?) Waitress was fair at best. Lots of other choices nearby. Never again. This was the only crappy place we went to in all of Nashville.
Best place on Broadway St.  During three night we try almost all the bars and Tootsie's had the best bands and service.
We were told that there would be a 15 min wait for brunch then the manager immediately sat his friends that were in line behind us.  It seemed extremely rude.  We won't be back.
Super cool space. Fried cheese curds were the bomb. Cocktails were yummy. Definitely worth checking out.

Sunday night, got in line at 4:55 pm for 6 pm show. Didn't get in to that show, but were 20/21 in line for the 8 pm writers show, which was amazing! Well worth the 2+ hr wait! Food is mediocre bar food but great service in a packed house.

This is a much appreciated addition to the Nashville downtown food scene. Finally, a place that is large enough and staffed to handle the business lunch crowd. I have been coming here for lunch since I work in the UBS tower...

I will have to say that the breakfast menu is by far my favorite. Bacon, eggs, sausage, potatoes... very delicious. 

The atmosphere in this place is what really makes it a step above. It seems like most restaurants have been going with the modern, semi-industrial converted look these days; while I like that alright, I have to say it has been a long time since I've visited a place and had a "wow" moment. This place does an outstanding job of preserving the 50's - 60's style while working in some modern conveniences. I hate walking into a place that tries to be "retro" but ends up looking like IKEA's interpretation of vintage (I'm looking at you, re-modeled Frisch's). This place really feels like a throwback done right, and I tip my hat to the owners for making that happen.

Came here for lunch & had fantastic service food was great too. Being from OZ needed a bit of a hand with directions & the young lady was so helpful & friendly. Wen in Nashville nxt I'd def come by here again

We have been hearing about tootsies, so we decided to get in, the bouncer on the door said that I can't take my camera in, so I had to go back and leave in the car.
The place is crowded but you can stand or sit comfortably, they have 3 stories, we have been to the first 2 stories, each one had a live music .the drinks are reasonably priced
$7 for a beer. I think you should give it at least a quick visit

Tootsie's was full of life and very crowded but I definitely recommend stopping in. They have live music on just about every floor. It is definitely an atmosphere you want to immerse yourself in if you are ready to party. The band on the top floor was high energy while the band on the 1st was more mellow. They were both playing covers that everyone could sing a long to and they even took requests from the crowd. Either way I had a great time and would recommend you stopping in for a drink. I did not eat there but saw others eating there on the 1st floor.

Gonna start off by saying I am a tourist. 

This was the first place I walked into on the strip.

I went straight to the third floor which has an outdoor roof.  

It definitely isn't the classiest place, but if you are a tourist you will soon realize there isn't much class on the strip of bars in nashville.  There were a lot of bachelor/bachelorette parties going on.  Every one was trashed, really friendly, almost TOO friendly if ya know what i mean, and the music was great.  

Being from new york, I'm not really a huge fan of country music, but I surprisingly knew a lot of the music that was playing by the band.  

Place gets CROWDED.
I could see why the locals would tire of this place but it's great for visitors who like a packed scene with multiple floors of music. Be ready for the heat in Summer.

Truly a neighborhood gem!
I could rave for days about the original decor but then food was put in front of me! The cracked corn is not to be missed! I know you're going to think it's just popcorn but it's so much more! Brussels hash is another don't miss item. Everything I had was so good! I took a little bit of everything from all of my friends plates. In no way is this low calorie food but throw caution to the wind and try everything. Then go down to the cellar speakeasy for a drink! Super vibey down there and a great spot for a party.
Seriously people...this place should be on everyone's radar!

Great music and great times. Very chill and a lot of fun. Always something going on and the bands are great. The shots are expensive but what isn't on Broadway. Just stick with beer and you aren't breaking the bank.

I have never taken the time to write an entirely negative review about any place I've been but I had to share.

They say it's the people not the place that make your experience - well my experience here was ruined by the horrible attitudes behind the bar. As a first time visitor to Nashville I was really excited to visit Tootsie's - while the space itself is nothing to write home about, it's a true classic. However, disappointment is an understatement.

From the second my boyfriend and I walked in, the bartenders had the worst attitude I've ever seen. We had just come from having a blast at the Stage and decided to head into Tootsie's for one last drink before heading home. We walked in and sat down at the bar on the first floor - we weren't sure if they were still serving drinks as it took at least 10 minutes for anyone to even acknowledge that we were sitting there. A bartender (blondish hair) finally gave us the time of day and we had to ask if they were still serving as she just stared at us and didn't say anything. She finally got our drinks and barely looked at us, throwing our change onto the bar. We still tipped thinking maybe they were all just tired and cranky because it was the end of their shift.

Last call was announced soon after (we were probably there around 25-30 minutes total) and we finished our drinks. People started making their way out and I went to quickly use the restroom; I was gone only a few minutes as there was no line. I came back to find another bartender (short with long dark hair) screaming at my boyfriend "GET OUTTTTTT" and was immediately taken aback. I asked her what the problem was, and she proceeded to say "he's been sitting here with an attitude when we told you to get out." He calmly replied that he was only waiting for me to finish using the restroom. I asked her why she was being so rude towards us (I had truly never seen a bartender act like this before, and I've encountered my fair share of bartenders) and she said that my boyfriend had been "talking shit" about "all the employees." Okay sure, whatever you say, girlfriend.

She was referring to the fact that my boyfriend and an older gentleman seated at the bar had commented about how the guy screaming at everyone over the mic to "drop their drinks and get out" was a bit aggressive and they'd never seen anything like it. This girl happened to overhear the exchange and I suppose it caused her to become even more rude and unprofessional than she already was. 

I sincerely tried to give the bartenders the benefit of the doubt at first because it was the end of a Friday night and I'm sure they all had long days; but their behavior was completely off putting and inappropriate. I don't care how tired you are, it's not an excuse to speak to customers like that. It really sucks having to write this about Tootsie's of all places because it's such a Nashville staple. But I will never go to Tootsie's again and will advise any friends or family traveling to Nashville to avoid at all costs. What a shame, I hope you reconsider some of your hires.

Really enjoyed The Bluebird Cafe. Went for the early show on a Tuesday and was excited to realize that our table was on the stage where Martina McBride would be performing later that evening. Go for the entertainment, we only had nachos which were just ok.

Awesome hamburgers, terrible cover bands. Enough said. I tend to eat and run because the cover bands are always garbage (and I simply hate cover bands). When the bands aren't playing, this is a cool place to hang out, drink beers and eat.

For you Predators fans out there, they will give you one free beer prior to the game if you come in wearing Predators atire.

I was visiting Nashville and didn't choose to visit the Bluebird for its food.  I went to see some good music and I got it.  The fook is just OK - which is why I gave it three stars.  I went for the Sunday free show.  Get there early and the early show will be better chance to get a good seat.  However, it is the later show that has a variety of artists who are trying to make it big.  If I had a do-over, I would go to later show on Sunday instead of early.  Eat dinner before or after.

My first couple visits to The Stone Fox had me singing their praises and spreading the good news to my friends, co-workers, and social media pals.  Finally, a restaurant that is quirky, interesting, AND delicious.  Every time I visited, I would order something different, and it was always outstanding.  My favorites were the burger and a kale & quinoa salad that has since disappeared from the menu... Yeah, yeah - you can get a burger nearly anywhere, but I had declared The Stone Fox's burger the best in town... and while simple, I kind of liked the curly fries that came with the burger.

Recently, I had a friend come to me and tell me that they visited The Stone Fox per my recommendation and had a terrible experience - Bad service, bad food, and an all in all bad visit.  I did my best to defend my recommendation, and chalked it up to a bad night.  However, about a week later I paid The Stone Fox a visit after a long work day and a much needed meal out and found myself equally disappointed.  I ordered humus and pita bread as an appetizer, and the pita bread had obviously been microwaved.  I was going to let it slide, but I have a strong objection to microwaves being used at a restaurant - if I wanted to eat a microwave dinner, I would've eaten at home.  For my entree, I ordered the burger and was equally disappointed.  I had ordered it medium, however it came a dark gray color, chewy, and lacking flavor.  Not to mention, my beloved curly fried were replaced with generic frozen streak fries.  Lastly, I ordered a peach basil hand pie for desert, and it was served EXTREMELY hot and mushy, and quite obviously microwaved.  I thought to myself, "Maybe they're having another bad night...."

Well, all that to say, I returned a couple nights ago and had another disappointing experience.  The highlight of my visit was that it was 2-4-1 beers, but aside from that, the food was bad, the service was worse, and The Stone Fox just wasn't what it used to be.
Great place to drink hang out and listen to music. We will return on our next visit to Nashville

First time I ate here it was great so I was excited when my boyfriend suggested going for dinner last night. I ordered the same dish I loved on my last visit - the zucchini tacos. Unfortunately, they were pretty awful this time around. The zucchini was covered in such large globs of beer batter that it didn't cook through all the way, resulting in a crispy outside and raw doughy inside. Not good. Our server did remove it from the check, thankfully. My boyfriend's smoked meatloaf was ok, but the jalapeño Mac and cheese was disappointing... it was just regular Mac and cheese with a couple jalapeño slices on top. Overall, the service was ok but the food definitely wasn't worth the price point. Probably won't go back.

Can't comment on the food, but my bar experience was very very poor. Ordered a cocktail which had little to no alcohol in it, when I commented on it to the bartender, my partner and I got a very rude response rather than an apology. Shouldn't have kept drinking there but ordered another drink to give a second chance. Same scenario next time... When I politely asked for a little more alcohol in the drink I had, the bartender charged me for a double and almost wouldn't speak to me the rest of the night. I attend bars regularly and know what constitutes as rude behavior from both customers as well as servers... Being extremely polite and borderline apologetic for my preferences, the bartender was extremely negative and generally unpleasant on top of the poor service provided. Will likely never return, especially after reading negative food reviews from other customers.

Amazing experience. 3 Floors of fantastic live music. All the bands were exceptional and fun. Crowds like you wouldn't believe, but even that was not too stressful as everyone there was well behaved and courteous.

Huge age range, anywhere from 20 somethings all the way to couples in their 60's having a great time.

Great roof top!

Paradise Park Trailer Resort
We decided to grab a quick meal here. One side is more of a "trailer parked themed" bar. The other side has a tacky diner theme where you order at the counter and then pick up at another counter in the back. There are several booths and tables. I got a grilled cheese with tater tots and my husband got the single- wide burger with tater tots. It was all very good. It was a good place to grab a quick bite to eat if you are walking down the Broadway strip in Nashville.

Awesome spot to grab food after the bars, the jalapeño cheese fritters are amazing. The staff is very friendly and the crowd is usually heavily intoxicated so it's cool to see the staff so calm and patient when dealing with customers.

I'm giving 5 stars for the show. 
It's worth it.
We went on a Saturday 6:30 show, with out reservations. There was no cover, but there was a wait... Like we got there at 4:30 and were the last people to get in. I know the website says 28 seats that "no reservations". Can get in on, but they only let in the 1st 20-24, then you can wait for cancellations and get in at 6:15. If you don't have reservations it's all a maybe. So your best bet is to get them (good luck :)) if you don't, show up early, and hour at least.

Nothing outstanding to say about the service or food/drink.  But the show was great, ours was artists in the round.
We sat in the back pew, but it's so small there isn't a bad seat.
Don't forget about the 7$ min, even if there is no cover. Cover is for the artists, 7 is for the house.

Fine selection of coffee and tea.  Atmosphere is friendly, chill.  Lots of space to sit and work or catch up with friends.  Staff are easy going and show that they care about the customers, the shop, and the community.
Brisket hash was not great. Chicken fried chicken biscuit was described by my friend as "About as good as KFC". Service was great.
The worst of the tourist bars on broadway, 7$ for a bottle of pbr . Directly next door they are 3$. Seems like greedy ownership as this deters the average folk from tipping the band accordingly
The brisket Mac and Cheese was amazing. Perfect portions. The waitress, her name was Cat, was so personable, fun, and made the experience even better. Will definitely be back.

The Bluebird Cafe was by far my favorite experience in Nashville! The bartender, Martha was so friendly and knowledgeable. She recommended food and drinks and discouraged us from food that a lot of other customers had been unhappy with in the past. She was the second person to welcome us and we were lucky enough to sit at the bar. If you do not have reservations (which cost $15/person) you have to wait in line. We chose to wait in line 4 hours before the doors opened on a Saturday. We got in line at 130pm and doors didn't open until 530pm. The next people that came got to the line at 230pm so we started waiting way too long, but, we were the first people to be seated. They only have 10 seats at the bar and they have 14 pew seats. The bar is a far better area to sit than the pews. Obviously, the tables would have been better if we had gotten reservations two weeks plus prior. The setting is very intimate and we had all of the songwriters and singer sign our Bluebird Cafe merchandise. Overall, the most amazing experience!
Loved it! We had a blast. Great music and the food was pretty good too. Fun to go in the back alley entrance like the old performers did. Follow the white footprints.

The Stone Fox is the first of what I hope are many places to call the Nations home.  A restaurants and live music venue, the Stone Fox is a great place to enjoy some great food and drinks and see some great up and coming local bands.  I have been here for everything from brunch to late night shows to Nashville Outlines, a day-long music bonanza showcasing some of Nashville's best.  

Considering all this place has to offer, it's a bit small and the staff a bit thin, but if you have patience its not an issue.  Some items on the menu are definitely better than others (great sandwiches, but brunch isn't my favorite) but they do make great drinks.  They don't have a lot of parking so be aware of that when coming to visit, and there really isn't anything around the Stone Fox (yet) so keep that in mind when coming out here for shows.  However, again, this is a great live music venue to see some really great new acts before they hit it big.  

The Stone Fox is basically an all-day kind of hangout, and I hope to see more of these in the Nations soon.
Had a blast here. Very loud, crowded, youthful scene. If you like quiet, laid back bars- don't come here. Definitely a scene for bachelorette parties and college kids. Three floors, live music

Great bar for music and people watching.  They have multiple floors with a roof top seating area.  Each floor has their own act playing.  Music was very good, but the food and drinks were not good.  Drinks were served in plastic cups and food was terrible.  Service was very slow.  My advice would be to eat elsewhere and come to Tootsie's for the entertainment later.
OMG THE BURGER WAS TO DIE FOR! If you want a good burger please go here first! I think that's all I remember though LOL

The Good:
1. The potted smoke- though, note this terrine is a smooth texture which I know bothers some people.  I loved the flavor.
2. The wait staff had terrific recommendations.
3. Great, creative Cocktail list
4. The Burger (dunked in cheese soup) - This might be my favor burger in Nashville.  The Ciabatta bun was crispy providing a great contrast to the soup dunk.

The Ugly
1. To be fair, this is more like the mediocre... I had high expectations for the Speakeasy downstairs, but the space is too big.  It feels more just like a bar/holding room for those waiting for their table.  I'd prefer to see something akin to the Office in Chicago if I'm going to a "speakeasy"- small room, no windows, comfy seating for a few, not for 50.
2. The Brussels Sprout Hash- This should be called mashed potatoes with 3 sprouts on top.  I was surprised given the hype around this dish which was sold to us as one of the most popular on the menu.  It was delicious, but did not meet expectations.
One of the best music venue's in town . We go often.  We also love bluebird on the mountain

Average at best.  Too many better options in Nashville.  

Brought friends from Boston and was embarrassed with the service

It is total bs to stand in line for over and hour and still not get in to just buy a souvenir and this is at the early show. Do better and have someone to sell that stuff. RIDICULOUS. I realize you need reservations for a guaranteed table but to buy something? Incompetent

I was in town for a conference and decided to check out the famous Tootsie's.
It was a short walk from my hotel and wasn't too crowded.
At first glace I thought it was packed but soon learned they have multiple levels with live music on each.
I enjoyed some wings and beer while listening to some great music.
The food was good and HOT for what I would consider bar food.
It was overly loud and practically had to shout to the bar tender to order.
I have to say it's a great place to kick back and listen to country music.

It was our favorite place as far as hanging out and listening to good music. If you get a chance to catch Beth Beighey and Laurel Taylor, do it!! They were wonderful and seem to be regulars. The food looked good, but we didn't eat there. It was nice to sit on the top floor and have the view of the town. Can't wait to go back soon!

The name is deceiving. 

We went here before the Maroon 5 concert, after we couldn't wait for one hour to get food at Rippy's Bar-b-que. Bad decision.

This place indeed looked very nice outside and they also had a band playing inside the restaurant, but that's about it. We had the burgers and fries. They were so greasy and have been fried to death. I thought McDonald burgers tasted better than these craps I just ate. Although I was starving, I took 2 bites and threw the rest in the trashcan. The food was definitely a foodie's nightmare. 

Please spend your hard-earn money somewhere else.

2013/#52
By far my favorite honky tonk bar in Nashville.   The staff were great and the live music was even better.  Fantastic venue.   I will always return here every time I'm in town

So, this gets a 2 for the music. I'd give a zero for everything else. It's just a nasty bar. I read the review from 3/18/18 regarding a blonde waitress, same day I was there. I wonder if that was the one wiping her nose when in the bathroom to remove the white powder. The same one that charged me $3 for a nonalcoholic drink & when I paid with a $20, she pulled out change from her wallet (never rang it up in the bar's system; therefore, she made the money). I was really looking forward to going here, but was surprised by how disappointing it is!

There are no words to describe this place. I've never seen such a pitiful excuse for a concert venue. I've been to many amphitheaters and never seen anything like this. Highly disappointed. Would never recommend.

I'll give this place a 4 overall but it flirts with a 3. First off, it's a very cool music spot and vibe and the band we saw was great! Played a lot of fun crowd songs and the singer had an awesome male voice. The food I would rate a 3. I ordered the pulled chicken sandwich and fries and it didn't blow me away by any means. Not bad but nothing to tell mom and dad about. Had a few beers and 1 Moscow Kentucky mule that was good but at 9 dollars quite expensive. I would come back but it's not at the top of my to do list.

Pretty cool space, despite being divey and louuuud. During the day there is plenty of room to stand and sit. The drinks are pricey, but the bands are good and they seem to have a lot of fun. There were some very cute and endearing Texan girls playing when I visited - they rocked!

Perhaps my favorite bar on Broadway, Tootsie's was definitely a highlight of the music side of Nashville. On each level of the bar there is a different band performing, and were were lucky enough to experience an absolutely killer band on display on the first floor this past Friday night. The band was great and the lead singer was on fire. She had an amazing voice and absolutely brought down the house - this experience was the highlight of my Nashville trip. 

This was one of the top rated bars when I researched Nashville before making the trip and I'm glad it didn't disappoint. I would definitely recommend making Tootsie's a priority when visiting the city.

Heard good things about this place before I visited Nashville. Looked at Yelp on the night we decided to head over, mainly to get the address, but started reading the reviews. Was alarmed by the negative ones which claimed service was awful, but there were so few I figured, "Eh, let's give it a shot." Should have listened to them. We were seated and then not waiting on for a while. We finally ordered and got our drinks pretty quickly, but took over 20 minutes to get the one small appetizer. Took another 5-10 to get our meals. Three veggie burgers and fries and one order of the house chili. All of the veggie burgers and fries were cold and seemed like they'd been plated and left out for quite a while. My fiance wasn't thrilled about the chili but at least it was the proper temperature. The waitress apologized for the cold food and the long time it took because there was a meeting in there and "they told us they weren't going to eat, but then ordered food and there was only one cook so he got slammed." When we arrived, the meeting was over and there were people milling around having drinks and talking, and definitely not eating. In fact, it looked like they'd had maybe had some group appetizers or something, but there weren't signs of a large group having eaten dinner, let alone having JUST eaten dinner. 
The server was nice enough but service was just dreadful. They really didn't seem to have any idea as to what they were doing. Also, the veggie burger was the worst I'd, personally, ever had, and the other 2 on the party weren't crazy about their burgers, either. Would definitely never make the trek out to this place again.
Live good music, delicious food at one of Nashville's oldest and best venues. Kinda small so get there early to get in line so you can enter into a Nashville dream!

My favorite Honky Tonk that we visited! I did not even know this one is "world famous". We arrived right after a Titans game let out down the street so the place was packed. There was a band on each of the three levels and we enjoyed sipping our beers and listening to the band on the third level (and the 3rd floor patio overlooking Broadway). This place is a definite must if you are in town and visiting Broadway. 

I guess Kid Rock (and various other musicians) is (are) known to hang out here a lot. But not in a pretentious "you must be seen here" kind of way. This place is way too cool / laid back (but also crowded) for that.

I was pretty excited to check out this famous Nashville spot and even though I only got to see it during the day, I loved it! I feel like you can really feel all the talent that has come through this "lounge."

I love the live music scene on Broadway and this was no exception to the greatness that one would expect! The prices were pretty standard for that of a Broadway bar. It can get pretty crowded, but that is also to be expected anywhere on Broadway. Overall, I love Tootsie's and I can't wait to go back!

This bar was pretty cool but definitely a tourist trap. I honestly had more fun at other bars but you really can't not go here. The downstairs band was hands down better than the one upstairs and so was the crowd. Great country music, few mash ups, and cheap drinks - I mean really, what more can you ask for?

Get there early!

Not a club-goer. Ate there for lunch on a whim while downtown. Staff was decently friendly. Waiter was just going through the motions basically. Salad was FAR too small for cost of 8.95. Food was ok. It's a live music bar in actuality so I wouldn't recommend it for lunch.

On the plus side they have pretty good soda. Fairly confident I could have died of asbestos poisoning by playing the pop a shot game. 

Food is disastrous. I'm guessing that the last time this place was cleaned was Pre 1990.

A recently updated menu with great food choices. The atmosphere is a perfect Nashville look. The stage provides an absolutely beautiful backdrop with live music and a unique boot wall. A must have picture! 
We started with the guacamole trio. Three healthy portions with some outstanding chips for dipping. For mains my wife ordered the smoked brisket tacos and I opted for the chicken fried chicken. The tacos were really good with a bit of a spicy kick. So good you couldn't stop eating through the heat. The chicken was moist with a perfect crispy breaking. Served with greens and mash, YUM!  
We enjoyed the music, dancers and the drinks before heading downstairs to the speakeasy. 
Be sure to get the camera out for another picture opportunity when walking down the steps. Looking up to the ceiling you'll see boots covering the ceiling!  The secluded dark lounge speakeasy is something to behold. Grab a seat at the bar and enjoy the mixology specials. This place was a real treat, we enjoyed every minute of it. Can't wait to go back.

I had high hopes for Woolworth. The history is draw to this place, and when first walking in the building is stunning. That's the peak. It's pretty much all downhill once you get to your table. We dined on the ground floor. The lighting is so oddly yellow tinted and uncomfortable. The acoustics of the building weren't well thought out when planning decor and furniture and as a result it was difficult to hold a conversation across a table and converse with the server. Our female server gave off the aura of bored hipster and most of the evening couldn't be found. Her dull demeanor set the mood for the meal. My party ordered a variety of dishes which all fell flat. The menu aims to be upscale southern but translates to the palette as bland, devoid of identity and soul, and overpriced. Dessert was even more of a letdown - $8 for vanilla ice cream with fudge syrup? I wish I had passed on dessert and saved my $8 for two separate visits to Jeni's. Cocktails were adequate but nothing special. Overall very disappointing. Do not recommend and will not return.

If you're a visitor and can get tickets, it's a must do in Nashville. If you're a local and haven't gone, go. A great intimate atmosphere with live song writers and has such great history, not to mention a great tshirt selection. If you can't get tickets you can get in line for first come dibs which is cool. Seating is kind of communal so you get to know the people around you and have a good conversation. Full bar, and food is simple but really good. Not a place where you can go and gab away all night, so if you want a nice first date spot, super intimate choice. Been there 3 times, and going in a few weeks.
First time visiting and had a great time. The bands were great and the crowd was a lot of fun. I would definitely go there the next time I'm in Nashville.

I had been to the sutler a few times before for drinks downstairs or Monday night writer's nights, but I hadn't eaten there. This week, I met my dad there for lunch and we were overwhelmingly impressed with the food and the whole lunch vibe. We both live and work near the 12th south/Melrose area, and there just aren't many places for lunch that you could find easy parking, bring a big group or have a business meeting. The Sutler will now be a go-to lunch spot for me, and I'm excited to try dinner!

Being gluten-free, I also generally find my lunch options a little limited. All of the sutler's salads and meat and three plates sounded like delicious gluten free options. I went with the mustard tarragon chicken, and it was fabulous! Filling but light, flavorful and fresh. 

My dad got the hot catfish tacos and I bet he's still talking about how much he loved them. They were basically like nashville's hot chicken in fried catfish nugget form, served in a corn tortilla with some fresh slaw and whatnot. I was really jealous not to be able to try them (for fear of flour in the batter), because they looked amazing and dad was overjoyed.

This place is a hidden gem! 
Don't let the location scare you away. It tucked away off of a few sides streets and on a corner. The decor keeps your head turning and looking throughout the whole restaurant. I loved the USA sign. 
A few of my favorite things: awesome seating on the front porch, mason jar drinks, large bar, amazing outside seating, cool pallets with flowers and greens and friendly service. 
I came with a group of girls for brunch and were very please with food and service. We loved the bloody Mary's! Breakfast tacos all the way! Our food was fresh and delicious. Don't pass up this little gem!
Step back in time where college students sat in the first lunch counter protests against segregation in 1960. They serve breakfast lunch and dinner. The service was excellent.
Every floor had a band and drinks flowing.  It was like A Vegas strip but on floors. Super fun place!

Way too expensive and overcrowded. We wanted the rooftop bar and there were hundreds of people packed in upstairs that we could not get through the crowd. Huge disappointment my well rum and coke was 9 bucks for a very tiny plastic cup. Bartender was rude and unfriendly. Would not recommend unless you're 21, obnoxious, and want to spend a fortune on mediocre watered down drinks.

I was in town visiting Nashville for the first time and got the recommendation to come here for their bottomless mimosas. I ordered the fried chicken biscuits and it was AMAZING. The service was excellent as well as the atmosphere. The band was great but not too overbearing (it was brunch after all that wasn't what we were in the mood for). We were so happy with our decision to come here!
Such a fun bar with great music and atmosphere! Didn't give 5 stars due to bartenders being slightly rude. Definitely a great time though!

We came here for lunch. Had the Woolworth burger and gumbo. The burger came with fries. The fries were over cooked. The burger and gumbo had an average taste to them.  The total cost for lunch was $23 including drinks.

The restaurant was designed to look like the finer Woolworth store, and had a man playing the piano throughout lunch. We enjoyed listening to the music. The customer service was good.

Up until a few weeks ago, this would be a "six star" review. The bar downstairs was our new favorite place in Nashville. The 3 stars here are purely for the environment. It used to have the best, creative, well made drinks rivaling any place like the Patterson House in Nashville. And the pork rind nachos were one of the most unique things in town to recommend. However that has now been removed from the menu (which I understand there will be changes of course.) But the most disappointing things is that they have changed their drinks to be more generic. Gone are the wonderfully creative mixology drinks full of flavor and character. All we are left with is generic drinks mad to look fancy but that you could get anywhere. Such a shame. Very sad.

My girlfriend was so excited to come to nashville because she wanted to see where some of the greatest country music stars of all time had got there start. We went to the open mic night at 630 and were told we would not be allowed in and that there was another open mic night later that night by the staff so we came back at 815 for the "open mic night." The first open mic night was free but when we showed up it turns out it was a 12$ cover charge at the door plus 7 dollar food and drink order minimum and it wasn't open mic night but rather a blues band that in my opinion was not good at all. The cafe was in terrible shape and falling apart and we were all stuffed packed into this small cafe. I wouldn't even call it a cafe. It had no theme there was no real selection for food or drinks. The waitress we had was very rude and disrespectful. I was very disatisfied with the entire night and me and my girlfriend ended up leaving early. Will not return to this place in the future.

Probably the least touristy place to take your true friends in downtown Nashville. 

If you want to hear the latest Kenny Chesney or Blake Shelton song then PLEASE go to any other place in downtown. Paradise Park always seems to have a very skilled rock band that never ceases to amaze me. 

Cheap drinks and a very friendly staff go along way when every other place on the block charges $6 for a Busch Light draft. 

This place has great music but also plenty of space for sitting and talking with friends. 

Yes, it's a little dreary and dirty looking; but to me the benefits outweigh the disadvantages.

It was way too noisy to have any kind of engaging conversation. Our server was  rushed. The main dishes came out too fast, the food was good. I found it strange and disrespectful that there was no information on the civil rights history that took place there.

This is the place to be in Nashville. We got two seats right by the band on the second floor. The bands were great and talented. The beer is a little on the expensive side with $6 for the Bud light but you are downtown and listening to music so you can't complain to hard.

Great tunes! Great drinks! Great times! Don't let the crowds scare you away, Tootsies is a MUST! There is nothing like an afternoon spent soaking up the environment, music, friends, laughter in Tootsies! Don't forget to bring your sharpie so you can tag your name on a wall or table!
Thanks for not letting us in! Just joking! Thanks for taking a picture with us. Will see you in the daylight when teenagers can enter.

My friends and I ate here as soon as we got to Nashville as it was suggested by our Airbnb host. The place is really nice, I dig their decor, and they seem to hold a lot of shows, smaller acts from different cities, which is super cool. Our server was prompt and pleasant. We had Mint Juleps but it tasted too strong. Although we haven't had Mint Juleps before so we weren't sure if it were supposed to be strong.
I love this place. There's several floors and live music all week long. It's a Nashville staple.  The bands are fantastic. You have to try this place if you're here and looking for a good time.

I can't comment on anything inside the restaurant.
As a fan of the tv show Nashville, I made my husband stop here while we were driving through town.  We were unable to stay for a show, but I did want my pictures in front of the sign.
It's odd that it's in the middle of a strip mall.  It also looks a lot smaller then I would expect it to be. There are a lot of scary signs about copyright infringement all over the doors.
However, it does look like a great place to see some great talent.

While out searching for apartments, I was in dire need of caffeine, a bathroom and internet (in that order).  The Well delivered and then some.  (OK, bathroom wasn't great, but it was clean enough and it worked)

I had an iced soy chai - it was lovely.  Much better than Sbux.  Plenty of seating, although some was less than comfortable.  Service was a bit slow, but I appreciate that they took the time to make drinks right.  

It wasn't until I read the other reviews on here that I even knew about the religious slant.  But I appreciate that it wasn't pushy.

Drink menu was pretty big - I look forward to returning!

Bottomless Mimosas?!?!? Done and Done. The wait can be long on the weekends, but you get to drink while you wait, so who can really complain? Plus, they have live bands playing so that provided a great atmosphere for people to sip on their bloodies or mimosas and chat! 

The biscuits were light, fluffy and delicious! I don't know what was in that honey butter, but it was divine. I ordered the chicken fried chicken biscuit and it  was a bit too salty for my taste. My roommate ordered the biscuit benedict and that was bomb! The ham was perfectly smoked and topped with creamy and rich gravy. MHHHHMMMM 

Overall, I would definitely recommend checking out the Sutler if you want to have a good time chilling to live music, while sipping on unlimited drinks !

Stopped in for dinner and a drink. It was a Tuesday and kind of quiet, but I can see how this place can get hopping. Food was good, decent bar fare with a little twist on things. Service was good and drinks were solid. Affordable solution to the overpriced tourist traps on Broadway.

It's all about the history and atmosphere 
Came here for some jack, music and look at the pics ...wasn't disappointed !!
This is a really cool place! (Though I was it was cleaned up a bit) The food/drinks are reasonable and the talent is unmatched. Get the baked Brie and whatever dessert they have that evening.

My wife and I visited this cafe this evening and saw a very good show put on by the Sweethearts of the Rodeo.  We enjoyed the entertainment as well as the venue which was made popular by the show Nashville which we both enjoy watching. We would welcome doing a return trip to this location during another future visit.

I am a Hispanic male from Southern California. Thursday night, I visited Tootsies with my GF and  some friends. As I approached the entrance of the bar, I was asked for my ID. I pulled my wallet out, and pulled out 2 ID's (drivers license and State ID) I handed what I thought was the bouncer, my Drivers license and then he asked me "Is the other ID your Green Card?" I turned to him in disbelief and asked him did he really ask me that. I immediately walked in and asked for the manager. We were approached by a dark haired man with glasses who said he was the manager. We walked down to confront the bouncer only to find out the bouncer was a Sheriff. In the midst of speaking to the Sheriff and manager, a large black man (real bouncer)walks up to me and pushes me. I tell the man to keep his hands off me, and the manager proceeds to tell me I am no longer welcomed in the bar. The Sheriff had to separate the bouncer and manager from me. This is the first time in my life that I have experienced racism directly and wouldn't imagine it would occur in an establishment of this magnitude. I've been to this place a couple times on other visits to Nashville and even attended the bar earlier in the day before the incident! I know this incident is a sign of the times and this will no way effect their business but hopefully the "management" at Tootsies will consider some training on how to handle these types of situations in the future, as I am sure this won't be the last time this happens here!

Nice little place in green hills. It really beats going to Starbucks. The coffee taste natural, and brewed right. The staff is friendly. Great place to go and study/get some work done. There is plenty of room to either lounge around and talk to your buddy or to sit and open a textbook. The coffee could be a little better, but overall I really love the atmosphere and the staff which is why I will be coming back.

Over rated place. We got in quick and bartender was very attentive as soon as we walked in, but too crowded due to the hype of it being the "spot" to go. We ended up at Legends and Layla's which was less crowded and music just as good.  Not a bad experience but def a place to stop me say you were there. Nothing incredible.

No matter how much time you have in Nashville or who is performing that night make sure you get out to the blue bird cafe. This was my favorite place in Nashville. I came on a night where they had a round circle of singer songwriters performing. They were all friends and chatted between each song giving some background about what they had written. It was so cool to get up close and get a better understanding of why a song was written and what it means. I think they have a lot of variety in the styles of their performances and whether or not the evening is ticketed so check out the line up ahead of time. I can't wait to come back again!

I was so excited about coming to Nashville and Tootsie's was on the top of my list. My husband and I went on a Wednesday night and I was shocked of how packed it was. It's a great venue with three stories of live music. The entrance and bottom floor was much smaller than I expected it to be. We spent most of our time on the third floor which had the roof top bar. Drinks are reasonably priced and my husband said the beer was nice and cold. 
The reason I am giving Tootsie's 3 stars is for the service and attitude of the bartenders. I have never met more rude woman behind a bar in my life! The three in particular on the roof I wish I had gotten there names but they were horrible. I wasn't drinking that night and I ordered a water and it was like I was a bother to them for ordering water. Some people don't drink!!!!! I live in Los Angeles and have been to some of the best bars and restaurants LA has to offer. I never received service like that. We eventually went back downstairs because those girls were just miserable. Rolling there eyes when people ordered drinks! Come on now! If you want a great honky tonk on broadway with great friendly service walk right next door to Legends! That was our favorite on all of broadway

2nd honky tonk bar that we chose to visit during our mini vacation. This was as good as it gets! Rowdy! Great band! Awesome service! We were packed in like sardines! Everyone was happy! We grabbed two open seats right in front of the band. We just slid in there when someone got up and met all kinds of tourists from around the globe. There were folks my age, folks 20 years older than me and folks 30 years younger than me. We all had one purpose - party like it's 1999! And party we did! Always had a beer in our hands - bartenders raced about making sure we were all satiated. I never smiled so big! We clapped! We sang! We cheered! We swam in a bowl of happiness!

WooHoo!

Went Saturday 17th, great historic spot my wife recalls from her youth.   Fantastic service, good blood orange mimosa.    Burger and fries were very good, very tasty.    Wife had poblano pepper dish, also a solid example with good flavor.    Lunch was good, will go back for dinner next.

This place is not worth the wait and the service is absolutely terrible. Waited an hour+ for a table that we were told would take 30 mins. Server didn't come until 20 mins after we were seated. Even then they got the food order wrong. One star because they didn't charge me for my order, which was the right thing to do. Don't intend to return.

Look, if you're a tourist, I understand that you have to check this place out. It's not a bad place. It's cool because they added a balcony on the second floor recently. Beware though! During the weekend, it gets SOOOOOOO packed upstairs. I mean, you literally cannot move. Like I said, get ready for that!

Music is always good. They always have a live band and they play all the country songs you typically would hear in Nashville.
