Drinks are horrible. horrible and expensive. Look, I get it's a bar drink. I'm not expecting anything fancy. but they're just horribly made. They get SO busy upstairs that they really don't pay much attention on their pours.

Tip: if there's a long line in front, there's a backdoor. so go behind the alley and you can get into the place through there too.
Great band...very crowded but a must see while in town!
fun place. crowded. all good singers. have a good time!

There is truly no better drunk food that a double bacon cheeseburger and cheesy tots from Paradise Park at the end of a long night on broadway. This food will cure even the worst hangover and is absolutely delicious. 10/10 would highly recommend.

Had a great time at Tootsies!  We loved the 3rd floor bar and outside deck!  We visited your establishment on Friday night and felt right at home.  We came back on Saturday night because we loved the bartender!  She was quick and friendly.  Very good personality.  Love her!  Thank you, Chelsea for being so good to us!  You are a great bartender!  So glad they gave you the chance to sling drinks two years ago with no experience!  You're great at it!  If we ever get back to Nashville from Chicago again, we will certainly stop in to see you!
Service was subpar, food was underwhelming and took awhile to come out. Will not be going back

Went for a brunch on a Saturday morning. Of course we expected a long wait for a group of 4 at 11:00, and we were lucky to have bottomless mimosas to accompany us as we waited. The bar staff was very diligent and friendly to refill our mimosas very promptly! I'm not going to say we were drunk by the time we sat down, but... well... crap happens. 
Anyway, we ordered the big ole biscuits and gravy and the sweet potato pancakes with some coffee to sober us up. The food was incredible! The wait staff was so friendly and they continued to fill our mimosas as the bluegrass band played.. This place was amazing and we had a great time!

I am not sure whether to review this place as a bar, or as a restaurant. My wife and I went here on a week night and while as a "bar" it was good to very good. The atmosphere I think was fun and it was lively enough...but not so packed you couldn't move. Probably the only thing that brings it down from 5 to 4 stars is that the band that was playing was ok, but not as good as some of the others on Broadway. As a restaurant it was very good also. The hot dog wrapped in bacon was probably the best hot dog I have ever had. Their Frito and chili was very good also. The hamburgers looked great...but I will have to come back another time to find out.

Super fine touristy spot! We stopped in during the day on NYE. It was cold but they still had the rooftop open with heaters of course. It was busy but the bartenders were very quick to get drunk orders. The beers were cold and drinks were super yummy! The music was loud enough to jam to but not too loud you couldn't hold a conversation.  I would for sure go back if we were in town! The only complaint I have is we ordered a vodka red bull and they did not inform us that it wasn't real red bull and my husband who is allergic to artificial sweeteners had a bad reaction.

So, I had never been inside of Tootsie's and my beau felt like I needed to experience it.  I will say this...it was a Friday night and super crowded.  I think for some that would be a plus, and for others it may be a deterrent.  I was mixed on how I felt about this place.  The live music was good, but they should work on overlapping the set times so that there is never a time when all the stages are empty/on break.  That happened to us and we were waiting for the music to start back up for half the time we were there.  The wait time on getting a drink was super fast, especially since they have beer tubs with bartenders set up around the bar areas.  I most enjoyed listening to the live music in the front room and also checking out all of the pictures on the walls of people who have been there in the past.  
I should mention that it was free!  :)  That is always a plus.
Overall I am glad to say I have been to Tootsie's even though heavy crowds are not my favorite thing in the world.

We went for Sunday brunch and there was a 30 wait which was no big deal.  We finally got seated and our order was taken.  Didn't have to wait long on the drinks (the only plus was the Bloody Mary!). But the wait for the food was ridiculous and then to get it cold made it even worse!  I got the breakfast tacos and the cheese was hard as a rock since it had been melted and then cooled off.  The potatoes and bacon were cold too.  When I let the waitress know she was extremely rude about it and said that's not possible bc all the food comes out immediately. When the waitress came back out with our bill they did take our meal off and she asked that we would give them a second chance when not so busy?!? Um, we won't be going back anyway!

Five stars.  Initially it was a 60 minute wait and they turned it into a 20 wait.  We came here with the kids  and food was delicious and came out super quick.  Definitely would recommend anytime but the Sunday brunch with live music is hard to beat.

Wow, where do I start, I should have left after I saw the red flags but I really wanted to have lunch on their patio, so after struggling to get a seat , no one ever acknowledged us, waited for 10 - 15 min.  Finally just got up and left,  it was not busy,  saw bartenders / waitresses just standing behind the bar. Never again

So I was not even let into the bar for no reason. He said I was too drunk to come in (FYI I have a PhD and they also denied entry to a trauma nurse), and neither of us were actually drunk. This dude had a chip on his shoulder and was a total jerk and should not still have a job after this weekend. We did not deserve the treatment we received. I will continue to call until I hear from a manager.

Here for a work related function. Had family style dinner. Was fantastic. The fried chicken was the best I have ever had. Excellent bar and great service. Check this place out. Very cool atmosphere. Old Woolworth store made into a restaurant.

Look... This place aint bad, it's just not my choice of places to grab a drink and listen to live music. My fiance and I went based on it's popularity and so did everyone else in the area from out of town. Im not big into the tourist traps so... Yeah.

PRO TIP: Dont bring stools away from tables and sit in the middle of the room. Im talking to you man in the green shirt (he'll never see this)!
Got into town for the first time at 11am on a Thursday and went to Tin Roof for a beer and good live music. Had a great time

What was once a classic gem of Music City is now a sticky-floor beer pit designed to sell as much alcohol as possible. All the historic adornments on the wall are vandalized and during peak hours it's too crowded to move inside. If you must, poke your head in to say you did but please I encourage you to find something more genuine Nashville has to offer.

I came here for just a casual lunch with my significant other and it was a great time in my opinion. The place looked a lot better in the inside than I had initially expected. The food was fantastic and the service was pretty good. They are a little proxy though. Also My SO is pretty picky and and tends to be an "difficult customer" and he was still able to find something on the menu to his liking which is amazing in my opinion. The servers did seem to get annoyed with him but I can't really blame that on them.  They also have souvenirs which where pretty nifty. They have different menus throughout the day if just depends when on when you get there. Over great place to eat.

What an amazing place to visit and the bartenders are always nice especially gunner and avery and the waitress scarlett is very nice, just kinda on the shy side. Oh btw what time does Deacon Claybourne play? I would love to see Rayna James and Deacon sing on that stage!

Oh gosh, if you really had just one day in Nashville, where would you go that evening for live music, the Grand Ole Opry or the Bluebird Cafe? That's a tough call, but since neither Jamie W. nor I have ever been to Nashville before, we went with the Opry with no regrets. An excellent concert that turned out to be the pinnacle of time management as the show was done at 9:15PM sharp. Did we dare try to traverse the city for a half-hour to attempt to catch the 9:30PM show at the Bluebird? Why not, what did we have to lose? After all, we were leaving town in the morning.

So off we went to discover that the Bluebird Cafe is in a strip mall off Hillsboro Pike. Like Joseph and Mary in baseball caps, we were hoping there could be room for us. We wouldn't have minded standing next to the restroom, but alas, there was a handwritten sign taped on the glass door that said no one else would be allowed in since they were sold out. It reminded me of that scene in "Hans Christian Andersen" when Danny Kaye got locked in the closet by Farley Granger, an ironic point since both actors were in the Hollywood celluloid closet if you know what I mean. Danny was put in the closet to prevent him from giving the slippers to his beloved ballerina, the subject of his unrequited love.

I didn't have any shoes on me to give to performer and well-regarded composer Gary Burr, but we were able to peek through the window and see a bit of his performance that night. The owners were kind enough to have speakers out into the parking lot (photo:  http://bit.ly/1IL4WQ4). I know who Burr is because he's now in a country trio with his wife and my old favorite Kenny Loggins. "Even though we ain't got money, I'm so in love with ya, honey." Burr has an almost-as-pleasing voice. All we needed were a couple of naugahyde recliners from Bradford's Furniture next door except they were closed. Too bad there was an agitated guy on his cell thoroughly upset that he couldn't get in. Chill bro, this is Nashville. Good music is everywhere.

Suggest reservations went on a Wednesday night and had a 30 minute wait. Dinner was fantastic the Beef Tenderloin was 5 Star. I would highly recommend this restaurant and piece of Nashville history to locals and tourists. Only negative thing I would say was the valet service. I am sure this is contracted out.
Holding people at the gate til about 30 minutes before the concert starts seems silly.  Food and beverage vendors inside could have been selling a lot more if we were allowed to walk in.

I had a really great time here as a solo traveler! It was a fairly low key Sunday night, but the bands were fantastic and it was easy enough to snag a single seat on each of the different floors. My favorite spot was the second floor- there are seats behind the stage that are perfect for someone who wants to quietly observe and enjoy!
The sign said it made the best burgers in Nashville. They may be right. Technically great burgers, but I like Fat Mo's better.
What a fun evening!  The bands were awesome!  It was crowded but we were there to mingle.  The drink prices are way too high.  $7 for a Yuengling beer. And $11 for a G&T plus tips.

Awesome venue with great bartenders and the best music on broadway.  My favorite time to go is Sunday afternoon when it's nice out. Head upstairs and enjoy the sunshine and listen to some fabulous music.

Not really what we expected.  Caveat that I'm not into modern country music, and there was lots of that, but it was also a bit crowded and there were Kid Rock posters everywhere (I have no idea why).  Lots of white "bro" guys and the women who like them.  But maybe that's the Nashville demographic.  Not a bad experience, but don't think it lives up to the hype and there are other bars in the area that are just as good. We were there last Friday night, and I was particularly impressed with one very good male singer on the second floor.
Cool bar, good live music, packed butts-to-nuts though, so expect that. Pretty sure the place was over-capacity. However, really historic and lively.

The Stone Fox is one of the best additions to W Nashville. They have a wide array of different things going on each night (from bingo, trivia, old school hip hop, country, dance contests, etc). The service is great (John is a really nice waiter) & the food is wonderful. & also the drinks are very innovative. The only complaint I've had with the food is that their fried pickles are spears instead of chips. I thought I'd enjoy something different but they were so hot that eating them in that form wasn't pleasing (I burnt the roof of my mouth). But, very small flaw...in a nutshell, this place is one of my fave spots in Nashville.

Disgraceful attitude from the staff. They refused to give my card back and denied they had it. I showed them my credit card statement that had the transaction, they told me that "it wasn't in their computer system". I won't ever come back.

I had the shrimp basket...time they opened up. The shrimp were extra crispy and a bit overcooked. We were the first orders to come out. The fries, I added cheese on them for .75. They apply this white, thin cheese sauce on the fries that you barely see and barely taste. So it's not smothered or what you think of when you read "cheese fries". The waitress was short and uninviting...not very welcoming at all. Dropped our food off and went to go sit back down. I thought she was going to get our silverware, not realizing they have plastic ware on the table, but I wanted some ranch so i had to wait until she made her way back to 'check' on us. First time here...not that pleasant. I'll leave this to the college kids and night life.

Worth the wait in line. Sunday morning brunch was so good. The sweet potatoe pancakes are perfection. The basic well bloody mary is also very good. It's a tight fit on a crowded morning so be prepared to squish in with everyone. 

I thought the chicken and waffles are just ok. The chicken itself is bland, average. The corn bread waffle is tasty. 

Cheese grits have amazing flavor but are far too watery, you need a spoon! 

Staff are fantastic, shout out to Kelsea. 

Definitely go, take your out of town friends for. Good Melrose area experience.
Food was amazing for a bar! Burgers were awesome! Great vibes with the live band and trailer park themed decor!

Had to check this place out as it is one of the more popular places in Broadway. There are several floors and each floor has a different band playing. 
A bit older crowd but fun to have a drink.

I had been curious to try this non Starbucks coffee shop in Green Hills and came in on Sunday for a pick me up. 

I really enjoyed the decor and that there is PLENTY of space to lounge and read, study, or work. Finding out it used to be a Burger King made sense! The counter top is long and definitely fast foodish, but they have done a great job giving it a make over. 

I decided to order differently and had an iced Fireside; a vanilla and cinnamon latte. I was pleased to discover they offer both soy and almond milk, I love variety! 

My drink was..odd. I'd get random patches of sweetness mixed with a bitter espresso flavor. It was different, and in a way that I would not order it again. I'm thinking the drink was set up that way, but it just wasn't for me. 

I wasn't blown away by my first experience, but maybe I had an off drink. I will come back and order my regular latte and see how that goes!

One of Nashville's original Honkey Tonks.   Just loved the place.  Tons of pictures of people that have played there in he past.  
2 bands playing on 2 different levels and both filled with talented musicians.  Couldn't sit still on the bar stool.   Random stars' band members showing up throughout the night.  The night we were there a member of Tim McGraw's band sang a song and Frankie Ballard's drummer who preformed as well!  Can't imagine the talent that shows up on CMA weeks or on the weekends.  
Crowded?! Absolutely, and I can't imagine what it's like on weekend night as we were there on a Tuesday night.   I will say however, that we rarely waited long for a drink there.   The bartender, Chelsea, was on it!!!  
The bathrooms were completely horrible.   Especially the one on the lower level heard that the one upstairs was better though. 
It's definitely a must visit for anyone coming to Nashville!

Just the most history rich honkeytonk in Tennessee. What I love about this little music shack is that it always has a great crowd. You find yourself singing along and if you leave without a smile it's your own damn fault. Drinks are expensive, seating is limited, cover bands galore- and I still love it.

Paradise Park is the place to be! Their food is a 5 EASILY! My boyfriend and I came to Nashville for the first time, and Paradise Park was the first place we went! Bacon Cheeseburger with fries is what I got and he got tater tots! Mouth watering. Our ticket number was2, so I'm thinking we may have been the 2nd order of the day, but the customer service was 5 as well! The perfect welcome to Nashville! 
So we decided to go Saturday night after a fun night out (to also see if we were just hungry and to confirm our thoughts on how amazing this place is) well, the customer service was not very good. She was short and rude, which is why I have to knock it down a star because you have to beware if you aren't going when they first open! But the food was still a 5 nonetheless. The venue is a 5 as well! It's a trailer inside the building, which is pretty cool, and at night the side where they play live music is pretty awesome! I would definitely go again!

Tootsie's is overrated. Been here a couple of times with my friends and it's nothing special. Was once escorted out because my friend misfired a mayonnaise packet and the group behind us that it hit asked the bouncer to escort us out and he did, even though we apologized and explained it was an accident. Staff isn't friendly or understanding, bands really aren't very good. Check out ANY OTHER bar on Broadway.

We came to Nashville for a bachelorette party and we found ourselves on the doorstep of Tootsies. I cannot express just how fun this bar is. The people are super friendly, the band was great, and the atmosphere was awesome. I would like to give a special shout out to the door man David. David is a genuinely sweet guy! He is charismatic and warm and knows how to make people feel safe and welcome!

Love the indoor and outdoor seating! They also usually have the best bands playing! It's one of the original spots on Broadway and deserves a visit! Drinks are a bit pricey due to the large amount of tourists. There was also an older crowd since we came in during the early evening.

All I can say is so much fun! Out of all the honky tonks my friends and I visited, this one was my favorite!

Every level had a band, and the top floor had a gorgeous deck overlooking Broadway. It was packed, but we still had adequate room to dance and sing with the band. 

Great time!

Always one of my favorite honky-tonks to visit when I'm in town.  Top-notch music any time of day.  Fairly-priced drinks.  The old bearded guy who plays bass in every band.  Lovely girls playing fiddle.

But seriously, the talent here is some of the best in the city and you're missing out if you don't stop by.

Went here for Sunday brunch. A fun eclectic little place off the beaten path. Small menu but with good stuff that runs the gamut from Southern /soul (biscuit and gravy, chicken and waffles) to a little Mexican (huevoes rancheros) to traditional eggs,  french toast etc) 

Sides were also tasty including cheese grits, andouille sausage, etc. Also a good bloody mary (depending on your love for a lot of horseradish....) 

Special mention goes to dessert.... Homemade pies... By the owner's mom according to the server. They had a dense chocolate mint as well as a sort of key lime/lemon pie.   Both were super good. 

Decor was open... Looks like they knocked down all the interior walls of an old house and they has a DJ spinning real vinyl of rock music (not too loud.... It was brunch after all) 

Great service also... Knowledgeable staff and very helpful 

We went for brunch but it looks pretty good for dinner as well.... Recommended if you're close to Nashville

My husband and I truly loved the Bluebird. Maybe partially because its iconic, but mostly because it was a quaint, low-key, intimate venue. The performers were incredible and you felt like they were playing just for you. The food was ok, nothing to really write home about, but they had a good selection of drinks and it was very reasonable and they were all extremely nice. It was a great experience. A little tough to get in, but if you are on the site at 8am Monday you can get seats .

The music in this bar was absolutely amazing. I loved every artist that we listened to. The bar tenders were very fast and very nice. The atmosphere was very authentic and gives you that old time country feeling

The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because it's hard to find any room to stand when on the first floor. You can go up a few more floors but the artists tend to get worse the higher up you go. The first floor is where to be if you don't mind a lot of people!

I would highly recommend this place if you are visiting Nashville!!
Great place....worthy of coming to support such a historically significant restaurant.

A disappointment. This new restaurant/bar is actually two doors down from where the original Sutler was. We were seated and no one came to our table for fifteen minutes. Several servers walked by us but no acknowledgment of us even being there. The place was half empty and I couldn't manage to wave anyone down. My husband and I sat another five minutes until I had to walk up to a passing server and ask for assistance. He said he'd tell our server. Ten more minutes went by with no sign of any one to take our drink or food order. We gave up and left. The hostess looked surprised we were leaving. I told her that no one came to the table. She just gave me a blank stare. Won't be back.

Tootsie's is a damn good time with different live music on every level. It has a hole in the wall feel with a lot of personality. Great live music, friendly staff, and as always you'll definitely walk out with a few more friends than you arrived with.

There are so many great places to eat in Nashville sad to say service and food was adverage at best and way over priced. I went there for the nostalgia unfortunately I would have to say the decor is a 21 centry version of what wonce was a place where average Nashvillians gathered for lunch and a on February 13, 1960, a group of mainly college students from historically black universities walked in sat down at the lunch counters and asked to be served.This is lost in the glitz

Being a huge fan of the show, Nashville, I couldn't wait to get tickets to see some songwriters and singers.  As everyone has said the process for getting tickets is daunting and frustrating.  We had 5 in our party and that wasn't possible so just two of us were able to snag tickets.  I have to say the pain was worth it.  It was an amazing experience from start to finish.  The singers did not disappoint.  The venue was cozy and inviting!! The atmosphere is just heaven.

Things to note: I had 6 tickets for tonight. One person in my group was running late and they still let her in after the singing started. The waitresses will still take orders after the singing starts too. I was at the 6pm show and it ended around 7:45.

This place is amazing! We went here for apps and drinks and everything we had was amazing. We had the loaded nachos which I highly suggest if you are going. We also had the fried pickles which were very good! We had some sort of quesadilla that everyone liked. And I can not remember what it was called, but there were corn pancakes with chile on them that were very tasty!

Had an absolutely terrible experience here.

Attempted to watch a game with some friends this weekend, so we got in, got a table and asked the bar to put the game on. Sure, no problem, they put the game on. So we ordered food and started drinking.

Just before our food came, they changed the channel and refused to put the game back on. The bar gave us some excuse that they are unable to change just the one TV. They refused to put it back on. We received our food and left.

The food was absolutely mediocre. I ordered a chicken and been quessadilla, which was bland, not crispy, and not worth the hassle.

The waitress seemed sympathetic and friendly enough, but had no sway over the bar.

Great atmosphere. Stopped in for an IPA and some band listenin'.

Lots of TVs for the hockey game viewing.

Has a patio if you want to sit outside.

Great dinner.  I travel to Nashville periodically for work and often eat alone.  I will definitely come back here.  The restaurant is a beautiful homage to the old Woolworth lunch counter and honors the civil rights history with the restoration and historical photos.  Music is soul, nice change up from country.  Tonight I ordered meatloaf, it was amazing.  Also real mashed potatoes and roasted Brussels sprouts were excellent.  Everything was GREAT. Nice atmosphere.  Nice bar.  Nice service.  Highly recommend.

It was my first night after officially moving to Nashville and I figured I would try a bar nearby.  It's a dependable local bar.  Bartenders are chill and helpful.  Prices are good..with great hh deals from 2-7pm!  I love whiskey and one of the bartenders recommended a new whiskey to me called Angel's Envy.  4 stars just for that.  Happy that this bar is literally across the street from me.

Some friends and I came to this establishment and were told at the door that we were not welcome because this was not a bachelorette party type of establishment. We all came from different states and were very excited to come here! Yes we were on a bachelorette party but this was our first stop because we wanted somewhere low key. We were instantly judged and not welcome and told this was not the place for us...what kind of establishment turns away guest. We were also told there was no seating but as we glared through the glass there were open tables. The group in front of us was let in (with no reservation). Welcome to Nashville!

I waited to get back home to write about my awful experience at your establishment.  The events of Sunday 2/12 have shaken me up and not only made me feel embarrassed, violated but for the first time I've felt singled out in discrimination.  My only crime that night was to place my knee on a bar stool. 

I am a petite 5.3" woman, 115 lbs., sitting at the back of the bar enjoying the band and only to get a better view of the band I placed my knee on a stool.  I was asked not to do that by a tall bouncer, and I removed my knee, only that the music got the better of me and I placed my knee on the stool a second time to get a better look.  Just seconds after the bouncer reappeared and said I had to leave, I said "fine I will go, let me wait for my husband" who was at the bar ordering drinks, at that point the bouncer forced me out by grabbing my arms behind my back and dragging me out, when I tried to resist his abusive manner of grabbing me and I was pleading with him to stop and asked "what did I do wrong" begging him to let me go, he grabbed me by my neck and violently dragged me out to the sidewalk. 

At this point I broke down, I was in disbelieve that this is how I was being treated as a patron that was paying good hard earned money at your establishment.  I am from Miami and in my many years of visiting bars, restaurants and clubs in Miami, I have never in my life been treated with such disrespect and abuse.   Sad to say that when the manager came out her response was "he was doing his job".  Well everyone has a job to do, but mistreating someone is not the way to do any job. 

I want to thank the kind people who came to my defense, they saw the way I was being treated was not right, and spoke out of their disgust.  If something positive is to come from this, I hope no one else should endure such horrible treatment. Tootsies needs to evaluate this bouncer, no one who feels they must grab a woman by her neck should be a bouncer and they must find another approach to properly remove someone.

Food is great. Whatever time it is the food is consistently good! The prices are super fair and the food is super fresh. Def a place to eat before you go out drinking or after a night of drinking. The place itself is a little dingy but the food is top notch. Would come back for the hot chicken and the cheese burgers.

Love the food and the atmosphere. You just never know when this place is open or when they are changing out the menu. The last 4 times I've tried to get food I have been unsuccessful on different days and times, so I'm afraid I will not patronize The Sutler. It's unfortunate, it could be a great place to hang.

Always a great stop for a scrumptious burger.  Nothing fancy ... Food is served in paper food trays and kitchen roll towels serve as napkins on the table.   Don't pass up the sweet potato fries, though mine weren't as hot as they could have been.

Darn?!?XO!

This should be a 5 star review!  After all I showed up in Nashville for one night and was able to get into the famous fabulous Bluebird Cafe with no reservation!  

But we saw an old blues guy, who insisted on just playing 12 bar blues songs and he wasn't very good.  I hope, he was having a bad day or I was not in the mood.

There was a reason why we were able to get in without a reservation.

That said, I loved my experience......  even waiting in line in the rain wasn't too bad.  The food, drink, and the service were very nice.

But the tip is look at the website and make sure it is worth waiting in line.

This a great spot for a party. So many stars have played and sung here. The bar is a little cramped and when it's busy it can be impossible to move around but if you go in the afternoon for some day drinking there's always a good local live musician playing! Make sure you leave a good tip for the bands on the way out!

This place has a super cool set up: upstairs - was the traditional dining room set up; downstairs was more suited for lounging.  I came during happy, so it was half off their signature/specialty cocktails as well as some other drink specials.

I had two of the specialty/signature cocktails: Don't Ask Rye & The Gambler.  They both were pretty good but if I had to pick the Gambler was the better of the two.  To snack on we tried the wings and the mac n cheese - green chicken chili.  The wings were better than average but nothing spectacular.  The mac n cheese was a very unique combination that went together well.  Usually I steer away from restaurant mac n cheese unless a trusted source gives me the ok but I'm glad I took a chance on it. **The menu did not indicate that the mac n cheese  had tomatoes on it; so if you're allergic or don't like tomatoes be mindful of that.

My husband and I visit friends in Nashville on a fairly regular basis, and our hosts scored Bluebird Cafe tickets for us (which is no easy feat, as others have mentioned), on Friday night. It was such a great experience! The setting is very intimate, and the music was great! 

We did not try any of the food, as we had pew seats, but did have a couple of drinks, which were nothing to write home about; and quite expensive. 

Don't come here for the food or drink though, come for the music. Inside you can see pictures of many greats who have played there in the past, and it just feels like a special place. I cannot wait to go again! 

Oh, and one last thing, get all of your talking out before the music begins, as there is a SHHHH !policy that they are pretty serious about.

100% worth the wait.  My husband and I decided fairly last minute to try to get into the early show on a Tuesday.  We waited in the 90 degree, sunny weather for a little over an hour and barely made the cut, but it was soooo worth it!  

Pro tip: you can make reservations a week out, do that.

Food and drinks were decent and the music was fabulous.  This is exactly what we wanted when we came to Nashville, not the craziness of lower broadway.  This place is a must go.

Also, if you watched the TV show Nashville this might now be what you expect.  But in a great way (in my opinion).

A great bar on Honky Tonk Row. Great scene on even a Monday night! The live music was spectacular! The bar service was speedy. The vibe here was a lot of fun, great scene with a small stage right in the window. This place was packed, selection was good they even had cider.
Is this my favorite Nashvegas spot? Could be based on my past experiences. Two bands, one cutting up with Merle Haggard... Drinking @lagunitas..yup my favorite #ipa and bar!
We had a delicious brunch here, made even better by our hostess Leticia and our server Damian.

Food options are as reviewed previously. Lots of fat, salt, cheese, etc. I ended up choosing the grilled veggie plate, which had a nice variety of different things, but was a little oily and salted. Service was fine. Tables are pretty close together. We went very early (5) and it was half-empty, so we didn't experience the crowded, loud part of the deal. Table liked the spicy fried pickles (you can order all pickles instead of sampler), steak, trout. I won't rush to go back based on ambience or food. The "speakeasy" (sigh) downstairs looked like a cool space, but it's hard to get into it when you're in a strip mall off Franklin Pike.
The queso is a must have, gotta have!!!! We ate it with chips, put it on our sandwich, pizzadilly, and everything!!!! OMG amazing!!  Service was a little slow, prices were moderate

Hands down one of my favorite places on Broadway. Although it's just a hole-in-the-wall, it's a great bar environment - especially before a Preds game (if you wear Preds gear, you'll get a free beer ticket). $6 Natty pitchers, fun bands, and spectacular service makes for a great time. The food is pretty good too.

Food-
Normal bar food, nothing special. 
HOWEVER: get the sweet potato fries and you won't be disappointed. I like to call them "crack fries" yes they are that good. 

Music-
The best sounds I've heard! You have to go at least once!

**SO worth the wait, if you can't get a reservation a week in advance to sit at a table be prepared to wait outside an hour to an hour and a half prior to show time to ensure your seat at the bar or in a pew.

From the moment we walked in we felt like we were home. Great food, atmosphere and staff. This place steeped in history as a counter where sit ins occurred in 1960. The hostess's parents actually were at the sit ins. Wonderful experience!

My wife, I and our wheelchair bound daughter went to the Bluebird for the first time last night for the Monday night "Open Mic".  Although we had the obligatory wait outside for over an hour before they opened, it was actually enjoyable and gave us a chance to speak with and hear the stories of musicians and others who had come from all over the United States and beyond to visit Nashville and the Bluebird. The Bluebird staff of Elliott, Britton, John and others were absolutely fantastic. They checked on us outside periodically and got us in out of the rain and seated as soon as they could. Although the small 85 seat room was packed, the service was very good, the drinks very reasonable and the beer extra cold.  We did not order any food, so can't speak to that.  There was no cover charge or minimum expenditure for the 6:00 open mic show, and the show was quite enjoyable - certainly can't beat that!  By the end of the night, we were on a first name basis with the staff and many others who were there.  Certainly an evening well spent. Highly recommend it to others.  Recommend that you do your research regarding the procedure for the night of the week you plan to go (as they all differ) and follow it carefully. Get reservations if you can and be sure to arrive extra early to be safe. Enjoy your memorable evening at the Bluebird and say hello to Elliott, Britton, John and the gang for us.

Loved this spot! Definitely my favorite bar in downtown. Came here on my first night in Nashville and had a great time. Being a fan of rooftop patios, this place was a must and the views of downtown are great. It is multileveled and has live music on each of the levels. Only downside was how packed the rooftop was when we were there. Ps... The moonshine is strong- watch out!
By far my favorite honky tonk bar in Nashville.   The staff were great and the live music was even better.

I decided to get the sandwich named after the place. It was the first time I had a peanut butter and chicken sandwich. It was great. No idea it could be done and I was definitely surprised. They have mastered this combination and if you're curious about the Tin Roof special you should definitely check it out.

What an amazing place! First time here. Big heart's for change. Plus 20 different coffees to choose from and great sandwiches. All their profits go to ending poverty around the world. I will visit here every time I'm in green hills. Check them out!

Really enjoyed this bar. Bartenders are attentive and fast and make a great drink. Band was awesome and the atmosphere was great, my entire group had a really great time. Those who wanted to dance could dance and those that wanted to chill had room to do so. I also loved that the band didn't just play country music like every other bar on Broadway. Great bar, I will go back when I'm back in town.

Loved everything about this place. From the moment you walk in there's a fun energy throughout the 3 floors of this bar/restaurant/live band venue. The bar is great and the food options are pretty good. But I think a lot of people go here for the historical significance more than the food 

With such a rich history in country music, you've got to visit this spot if you're anywhere near Nashville.
By far the best Honky Tonk in Nashville.
Fun atmosphere, cheap food, cheap drinks. Worth stopping in, although - like most spots on broadway - not worth staying all night.

Finally!  A great latte, I'll take it!  It is so right, I could keep going but you'll totally understand when you come.  Go read their wall, find out about their mission.  

Because giving adds to harmony, oneness, satisfaction, and happiness.  meh debatable.  you can only give from a heart that knows love.  #philosophical #volunteer #youareloved

When you come in you'll find Respectful social people, gosh I love this city!   Winnnnnn  #sotrue

This was probably one of the funnest bars I've ever been to! I loved that it had 3 levels with a different band on each! So fun to go to and listen to live music. I also was a huge fan of the rooftop bar overlooking downtown Nashville and the rest of Broadway. 
This place was also very dirty though. It's not one of those bars that I would bring a child into to listen to live music, I would only go here if I was with my friends. 
I will be back though because it was so much fun!!

I'm a huge fan of the show "Nashville" and it was a dream come try to get tickets to the elite Bluebird. Yes the process of getting tickets is awful and difficult, but once inside it is worth it. Food and drinks are very good. Staff is friendly and helpful. The atmosphere is very welcoming and it is great to see new songwriters. I could spend every night in here if possible!! Can't wait to return for a third time(: Hopefully I'll run into "Deacon" one day there (:

Tootsie's is always a great time!! With three floors of music, you can move around just to hear a different band play. The best part is that each floor still seems pretty intimate so you feel like you're really jamming out with the performers! They try to get you involved which is nice compared to the other bars that have one band and a huge dance floor. Yes beers are a $1 or 2 more expensive here than at other bars but it's worth it to me because I think they have some of the best acts. And you never know which celebrities can pop up on stage!

Won't be back. Was very disappointed...they took up chairs at 1047. I went to the bathroom and the guy took up m chair...as my friend was sitting there and my beer was right I front of my table. I could understand if it was packed and they wants to keep the flowing but it wasn't.  They made the people next to us get out of their chair. Im confused???

I cannot say enough about Rachel and the staff working tonight. I have never been to a bar that started out with 20 people and turned into 120 and the bartender executed her duties as diligently and as balanced as she could behind a bar by herself. Watching her fill pitchers and serve shots at the same time while calming the natives was nothing short of phenomenal. I would recommend this bar and Rachel to anyone who has patience and can see the momentous amount of hard work and dedication it takes to be an amazing bar tender. I cannot say enough about Rachel and her bar skills. We're from small town Ohio and she made us feel right at home from the first moment we arrived.

After Stevie Wonder concert went here and the bouncer didn't let me in to wait for the Uber surge to end.  Am writing this just after the surge ended and want to express the disappointing end to what otherwise was a good night.
Great fun! First visit to Nashville have to see the world famous Tootsies and you just may see the next great CM artist !  Just like Willie and many others!
Terrible venue.  Hard to see stage. Worst venue I've ever been too.  Paid $50 for lawn seats and for a show that starred an hour earlier than advertised. At least the sound is decent.

Just went here for drinks (prior to dinner). It was OK. The place was pretty dead but I'm sure it's a hot spot at nights. Customer service was not bad, bartender was nice and drinks were fine. But that's all I can really say. One thing I wasn't a huge fan of was when I was there, at the bar, the garage or windows were open and people were smoking outside -- I could definitely smell it while hanging out at the bar indoors. 

Can't say much about the food, didn't have anything.

It's really sad to say that I will not be coming back here for their food. It just doesn't taste good. I've been here at least 4-5 times and I am always disappointed. I only come because they are the only
Place in this side of town that has a happy hour until 7.

The ambiance is really nice. I love sitting at the bar and their cocktails are pretty good. So cocktail wise, it's great! But man, their food is not good at all. 

So come here during happy hour to drink since the ambiance is so cool! But that's it. Don't come here hungry.

I've been to the Tin Roof in Charlotte, NC many times, so it was kinda fun to go to the actual Tin Roof - as I imagine this was the original.  It looked identical to the one in NC.  It was fun, good music, dancing, busy yet still places to sit down and converse.  I'd come back for sure.

The only reason this bar is not slammed on a Saturday night is because the service sucks.  Literally disappointed everytime.  Leroy Powell is the only reason we come here. Amazing music, poorly managed.

This place was PACKED. It's legendary in the area so we had to go have a beer there. I suggest stopping in and checking it out, if you're with a large group you'll have a blast. A few other places I'd rather go if I was looking for a place to sit and chill and have a beer and listen to music.

Absolutely yummy buffalo strips!  Flaherty and got and the handcut fries were great also!  Love the trailer park theme and three live band was really funny. It's great that you can go to the restaurant area listen to the music but still have a conversation

I have driven by this establishment a few times and I was looking for a change . I went in solo and looking forward to a extensive menu . For my taste it wasn't that extensive and kind of pricey . I had the burger and it was tasty but I am not sure that I would revisit it again . I felt like I was paying for a different vibe that involved bourbon not food . I know it's busy quite a bit so this is one mans opinion

Tootsies definitely lived up to its famous reputation! Great cover band playing on this Sunday night. The bar was jam packed with a lively crowd, and the singers gave a great finale singing and dancing up on the bar.

John was really great. He was friendly, attentive, and probably cool with the Oxford comma. I also can't believe the great bands that play there. I really wish I would have bought a house closer so this could be my neighborhood bar. Did I mention the food? So much to choose from and I haven't been disappointed once. I can only hope to get snowed in while visiting so I have an excuse to take up a longer residency.

Was so great for breakfast we went twice. Best sweet potato pancakes hands-down ever had in my life. Hope I can replicate them at home. Service was top-notch. If you're from the north and you remember the old Woolworth store and diner counter this is just like it. Surprisingly great experience what a fab find

This is a hard review for me, because The Sutler has such highs and lows. 

The highs? 

1. Great happy hour. Upstairs (The Saloon): M-F 3-7 - 1/2 off draft beer, wines by the glass, and signature cocktails. Downstairs (The Cellar): W-F 5-7 - 1/2 off draft beer, wines by the glass, and signature cocktails. Downstairs (The Cellar): W 7-10 - 2 for 1 wines by the glass. Also - the Cellar is pretty big, so it's not as crowded during happy hour as lots of other places in Nashville (where you walk in at five and half the tables are taken)!

2. Good drink selection. Good beers on tap. Good cocktails. 

3. Decor. Especially downstairs in the Cellar, the Sutler is really cool. Comfy couches, big chairs. Definitely a great place for happy hour with a lot of people (I've gone with groups of 7+ and we can always find seating). 

The lows?

1. The parking. It used be bad (when you could park behind the McD's and walk over), and now it's even worse. With all of the construction and building on 8th, they have about 40 spots for The Sutler, Sinema, and everything else in that shopping center. If you're going after 4, good luck. (I have Fridays off, so I went at 3 last week and parking then was a breeze.)

I haven't ever eaten, so I can't speak to the quality of the food. The menu looks pretty typical Southern (burgers, fried chicken sandwich, steak sandwich, tacos, nachos, queso, meatloaf, but they have a salad or two if you're looking for something a bit lighter. 

I'd also like to try out the Bluegrass Brunch sometime (Saturday and Sunday 10-3). 

If it weren't for the insane parking situation here, this would probably be a four-star review for the happy hour alone. Seriously, where else in Nashville does the happy hour last until 7 and has plenty of seating? Nowhere, that's where.

Ein muss für alle Nashville Serien Fans.Ist bloß etwas schwierig Karte zu bekommen zumal man von Deutschland aus bei der Zeitverschiebung gut planen sollte. Mit dem Onlineausdruck aber unproblematisch.
Es ist eine sehr spezielle Club Atmosphäre.Wir hatten nur Getränke weil die Veranstaltung um 9 pm losging.Aber alles ok

Music was awesome. Food was hot and tasty. Pretty much self-service after you get your food and they leave you be which is nice. It was a nice place to grab a quick bite and it was quieter than the other restaurants near by. Wait was only a few minutes and staff was decently friendly. We would stop by again. Decor was ok but nothing special.

I was so excited to have lunch here due to the rich history of the building, but honestly I was disappointed. My brisket sandwich was not hot and was dry. I had to drizzle hot sauce all on it just so that it'd have some flavor. The sweet potato fries weren't bad though. They were sweet and crunchy, but just needed to be be hotter. (My food had obviously been left out, just sitting there for too long after being cooked). But the worst part of the meal was the coleslaw. It was absolutely disgusting. I might've gone at a bad time and heard their breakfast is better. I will try again. Hopefully with a better experience.

Went in prior to the bowl game and it was the wrong Tin Roof. However we're glad we stopped in. Ladies working were very nice and helpful. Tried the hot wings and chicken quesadilla. The wings were very good and my wife liked the quesadilla. Would be a regular if I lived in Nashville.

Came to Tootsie's for a bachelorette party bar crawl. Despite it being a larger bar with 3 levels, it was still incredibly crowded!? We were wading through crowds to move around, to the bar, from the bar, away from the bar. 
Aside from that, it has live music, which is always fun. The bands playing that night were fun, and we spent most of the time on the third floor. It was annoying though that they said that it was $20 to make a request...seems a bit steep. The venue itself is a total dump. The floor is sticky and grimy. I didn't end up paying for any of the rounds of drinks at this location, so I can't comment on the price, but it seemed have a a lackluster selection of drinks: mostly cheap beers and well drinks. 
The bouncers were also a bit annoying. They opened up the patio area behind the band, but were oddly (and obnoxiously selective) about who could go to the patio. We were standing on the raised area besides the roped off patio area, and they told us that we had to step away. However, there was a couple standing beside us, also outside of the roped off area, and they were allowed to stand there...seems a bit arbitrary. The clientele also was a bit obnoxious. They seemed completely oblivious -- and even a bit rude -- to people trying to pass through. I know that it can be a bit annoying, but just be courteous and move out of the way so people carrying drinks can get by...
Overall, it was fun and part of the quintessential-Nashville experience, or so I'm told, but I don't think that I'd go back if I visited Nashville again. It's a one-and-done deal for me: been there, done that, and it's time to explore some place else.
Cool hangout. Food is nice craft burger style. Interesting flavors from local goods . The Stone Fox burger was nice. Overall the experience was nice for a weeknight. I will go back
Great brunch on Saturdays, the food and atmosphere are great.  Friendly staff, great wait staff.  Loved the Nashville Hayriders, get them back!

The space is very cool. The night I was there, there was a funk band playing in the club downstairs, and it was a fun vibe. Upstairs, the huge screen playing classic music videos also set a retro feel that matched well with the classic 60's era building. 

The service was great. Very friendly, engaging, and helpful. I would give five stars for the space and the service staff.

Unfortunately, the food, on our visit, didn't live up to the promise. 

The biscuits and corn bread that came out first were one of the best parts of the meal. I heard from my table mates that the cocktails were also spot on. 

The appetizer were of marginal quality. Pickled shrimp were fine, but the first plate came out without the piri piri sauce, and the next plate did have it. Taste was good, but presentation inconsistent. 

The lamb meatballs were inedible in my opinion. To me, they were clearly underdone in the center, and the flavor was unpleasant.

The entrees suffered form the same inconsistency. The gumbo was inedible due to a pronounced burned flavor...it has been on a low burner too long between stirrings and had scorched.

The salmon was a good portion and cooked well but with mediocre flavor. The succotash it rested on was scant and no lima beans were to be found. 

The Blue Ribbon salads were topped with over fried plantain strips, measly portions of chicken, but otherwise not bad. Not great, but not bad.

The short ribs my table mate had were also lackluster. He said "It was basically pot roast". Not bad, not great. Consider the price tag of the entrees is significant.

So the kitchen was having a rough night when we were there. They were out of the vegetarian special and also the chicken breast. How does a restaurant run out of chicken breast?

Anyway, cool vibe, not very good food.

Place is terrific, the food is decadent and delicious.  The fish was my favorite, but burgers were very good too.   I particularly liked the music teach of the Saturday nighs I wentt.  Glad to see the old Melrose area coming alive.

So today is the 21st of March, one day after my 24th birthday.  I made the trek out from Chicago with my girlfriend to visit friends and family.  I used to live in Nashville and had passed this place on my way into the pool hall many times, so I decided to drop in for a cocktail with some dear friends of mine.. But the staff at Sutler decided that both my girlfriend's and my id's were fake.  I presented the manager with my debit card and my insurance card.  He then quizzed me as to what astrological sign I am.. You've got to be shitting me. Thanks for the warm welcome guys, the beer that my buddy bought for me was delicious!!

This place is AMAZING.  Was a first timer here and had a BLAST.  Walked in on a Saturday night to a VERY BUSY bar.  The bartender waved immediately and took our drink order.  Luckily, three people got up from the bar and we scored three barstools!  We stayed there the ENTIRE night.  The band was amazing, friendly and engaging with the crowd.  I absolutely loved this place, and cannot wait to go back to visit.

Never in a million years would I have walked into this place but it was after 11 o'clock on a Thursday night and we were starving with few options on Broadway that were still open. I asked one of the bouncers where we go could to get food at this hour and he pointed to Paradise Park and I was still skeptical. He assured me the food was decent so in we went. The place was the strangest bar we encountered throughout our four day stay in Nashville. The floor looked like a putting green near the stage area and the band was odd. I'm not sure what they were playing exactly but it was chaotic. The people near the stage were wild, it was a very very interesting crowd. The bar towards the back was as divey as it gets, I mean DIVEY. Stool seating, not the cleanest, HUGE sink filled with beers behind the bar. If I wasn't starving beyond belief I would have walked out. We ordered a hot chicken sandwich with french fries and I got a grilled chicken sandwich with sweet potato fries. The food was served on a tray and we walked to tables next door that seemed like it was part of another restaurant/bar, we still aren't positive. I don't know if the food tasted amazing because we had been drinking since noon or if the food was actually that good, but regardless, we were very very happy in that moment. The bartender as busy as she was had no problem running to the back to get us extra honey mustard and blue cheese. The meal soaked up whatever we had in our system that day and we were able to stay out another 3 hours so for that Paradise Park, I thank you.

I don't get why this place is so dang popular.  It's ok but I've been to better rooftop bars with live music before.  It's got a cool view of the strip so worth checking out the upstairs patio.  The live music acts are pretty alright and there are about 3 stages.  This place gets soooooo crowded that it's not enjoyable after awhile.  Drinks are mediocre and it's kind of dirty.  But you gotta visit there once to see it and then move on to other cool bars on the strip.

Rude bartenders there. They look bored and don't make you feel welcome. Just horrible!  Wanted to get the first time experience, but very disappointing.  Note to owner:  too much competition out there to let this happen.
Fun bands. Games. Multiple bathrooms. Multiple bars. They serve food on the other side of the building. Huge place and awesome for a Saturday night party

What a cool ass place with great history behind it. It was cold out and not too busy on Broadway but this bar was still packed. Really nice staff with some great music. If you go to Broadway street you have to make a visit to Tootsies. I didn't  know the history behind the place until a friend messaged me on Facebook after I tagged myself there.

Waited in line 3 hours tonight to catch the 9:30 show.  IT WAS WORTH EVERY MINUTE. Don Schlitz was on stage and was joined by some random "union" picker.  Mr. Schlitz put on a heck of a show and the picker just might have a future in Nashville. 

Special shout out to Joe Salvo.  He is professional, good natured and one great doorman, as well as, being the most "photo bombed" doorman in Nashville.  Also props to Vonda ---- quick, professional and efficient service. 

The baked Brie was awesome. 

Folks -- the "picker" was Vince Gill. The Blue Bird Cafe is a must see.  I can't put it any other way.  I just can't think of where else you can see such superstar talent (Mr Schlitz and Mr Gill) for only $12 in such an intimate setting.  

We stayed in Nashville (on our way home to Texas) because we wanted to see the Blue Bird Cafe ----- it was sooooo worth it and I am so glad we did. 

Also, I am happy to know that the reservation system is improving.  The current system is a bit of a pain (back to waiting 3 hours in a stand by line), however, they are fixing it.  

I can't wait to come back on my next trip to Nashville.

The food was good I had the BLT with home fries and a side of mac n cheese. I am rating this place a 3 because the level of service was poor from our server.  We went without refills of water for at least 45 min - hour.  My girlfriend contacted the manager and he did comp all of our meals. I was very impressed by his efforts. The atmosphere was cool and they had a live band throughout the evening. I would try this place again.
Homemade granola bowl was delish! Jalapeno bacon was really tasty. Service was good too. We will definitely come back when we are in town.

If this business was more geared toward customer satisfaction than assuring that they maintain a hipness that included aloof, rude,  and incompetent staff, I might enjoy it. I've sent many friends who've visited Nashville there, and always hear that the food is mediocre and overpriced. I didn't even get as far as the food because of how incredibly unfriendly the staff was when just trying to have a drink. Will never go again, nor would I ever recommend it.

First off, the service was horrible. The waitress was extremely rude, and we had to get up and ask for things like silverware, napkins, etc. because she didn't bring these things to the table, or come to check on us. On the other hand, the food was great. So we had fried okra and pickles which were tasty! Also had macaroni and cheese with chicken. Delicious! I enjoyed the local music night.

A must stop for all when In Nashville as a tourist.  It's more for the history and live music than anything else.  It's the perfect place to end the night as most of the older tourists were there and gone.  the prices aren't bad depending on what you're used to.  Some of the reviews mention it's tourist trap, well unless you live in Nashville you're a tourist too, and a trip to Nashville isn't complete without a stop at Tootsie's.

Ummm this place has beer. There's not much more to say. It's cheap -ish, it's very divvy, you can write on the table if you're bored, and the night I was there they had some mediocre live music. I'm not sure I would eat here, but if you want cheap beer, this is your place.

First time here.  Good start upon arrival...pleasant server and came to the table quickly.  Ordered drinks and reviewed the menu.  Server offered some good suggestions.  Unfortunately, we then waited 40+ minutes before our server finally came to the table and said they'd lost our ticket.  They said the meal was comped and would come out quickly, but others continued to get their food.

Food was good and I like the atmosphere, but wouldn't rush to go back.
Burger was really good. Bun to meat ratio a little off. Meat was seasoned well and good quality cheese.  A/C was cold inside. Staff friendly.

Born and raised in Los Angeles California. I visited this spot as it comes highly recommended for tourists to try out. This was my first time in Nashville and I actually really wanted to see people line dance, wearing cowboy boots and hats. Yes, I know it's stereotypical but c'mon I'm a tourist! This place was grossly packed, just like a hip club in Vegas or in Hollywood. I actually didn't even hear country here, it was all top 40's and stuff they'd play in clubs here. I totally understand that not everyone in Nashville oozes country, so this is a good spot for people who want to 'club' because this is prob the only one in the area for miles.

Okay, so as a tourist, I HAD to go to Tootsie's, right? 

I tried to go at a quiet time, but apparently that time doesn't exist. The crowd was huge and the space is small, which led to many uncomfortable moments since everyone seemed to have been overserved. The band, of course, made up for the discomfort and played a slew of popular hits, and the crowd couldn't get enough.

All in all, I'm so happy I went, but I probably won't return.

I have lived in Nashville for 5 + years and finally made it to the Bluebird last night with our out of town family.  A member of our party has a disability and Bluebird staffer Kae-Leigh was super helpful in getting a table that would accommodate needs.  The service was great and the performers in the round were wonderful.  I have been missing out for years and will definitely return.
Kolby is the best! Hands down the best cashier this side of TN...maybe the world, but who is to say.

Meh. Had to do it because it is a legend in Nashville. Service was okay, drinks were a bit weak and of course it was a packed and kinda dirty bar. It would be a great place to get sloppy if you want to be able to say you did so in a landmark.

I would not recommend Sutler to anyone at all. We went in on a Monday night and the restaurant had only a few tables filled up. Our service was terrible - it took close to 20 minutes to get the drinks that we had ordered and about that same amount of time for the server to return and take our order. The appetizers we ordered came out with our meals. The meals were not good at all. My fiancé ordered the trout and was not prepared to spend the rest of the evening picking bones out of his meal before he could eat it. Several at the table also ordered the "grilled veggie plate" which turned out to be mostly grilled lettuce with a roll of thyme on top that was still on fire. No one finished their meals due to the appeal and taste. It took us approximately another 20 minutes to find our server and check out. Mind you this place was NOT anywhere close to busy. I was extremely disappointed.

This was one of the worst meals we have ever had.
Food, decor and kitchen make for a terrible 
Combination!
We would never return, ever.

Tootsie's is a Nashville staple and somewhere you should visit if you are doing the tourist thing on Broadway. I really like that they have added a rooftop bar area with live music and drinks. But eeesh. When I was there with out of town guests it was packed to the gills and they were only letting people go up if others were coming down. 

This now creates 3 levels of music which is nice, but man. Overall it's just so crowded that it can be difficult to enjoy the scenery. But... get there early and I'm sure it is much more enjoyable!

This is the real fuckin deal. Small bar with a tiny stage, country music blasting from a live band, drinks being slung and spilled, people singing along to every song. Oh shit yes!  John Stone and his band KILLED it the other night when my husband and I were there....  such a great vibe. Spent the remainder of our drunken night here and didn't regret it.

I REALLY want to like the Sutler. They have done a great job with the decor and I love the downstairs bar.We live in walking distance to this establishment, so I was very happy to see The Sutler reopen.  We have visited the Sutler at least 6 times, and each time find the staff to be on the "high-falutin'"  side (thats a nice way to say snobby).  We recieved better treatment at the OLD Sutler!  On our last visit, my 3 friends approached the upstairs bar at the same time, and once they got the attention of the bartender, was told by her "I need some breathing room". I suppose we had to wait for her to find her Zen before we could order drinks. Since there are no cocktail waitresses for the bar area, several of us in our party of sat without drinks for at least 30 minutes. Having been in the service industry a very long time, I looked around and saw other tables with empty glasses. Lots of lost revenue. This place needs some trained professionals behind the bar and hostesses that are not rude. The downstairs is great, but no one is in a rush to serve you if you sit at the bar. Too many garnishes to prep, I suppose. Other reviewers have commented that the staff is dismissive - We have had that experience as well.  I wish the Sutler would get it together - it may be growing pains but if you want my business and  more importantly for the high falutin' staff, my tip, you are going to have to earn it from now on.
Warm beer. Okay music. Too crowded too early and the bands in different sections blended together. Not all it was chalked up to be! Had much more fun at several of the other bars
Best stopping place for a beverage in Nashville. Service is hard to get, cause they are so busy. But for a great watering hole, Don't miss this well located bar. Go to the rooftop...

The food was freaking fantastic. Some of the best dive bar food I've had in a long time. My fiance ordered the hot chicken sandwich and was fully warned that it was extremely hot but ordered it anyway. Turns out, she was right. His eyes were watering, but said it was so good he still ate the whole thing. I had the hot ham and cheese which was fantastic. It was basically a BLT and ham and grilled cheese in one. I highly recommend it. I do regret not getting the tater tots. A lot of times tater tots are too greasy but these weren't. Luckily my fiance let me steal a few of his. Music wise, the band wasn't great but they were a good change of pace from hearing the same five songs that are played over and over at every other Nashville bar.

I'm so disappointed in this place! I went to Nashville on vacation and when I found out that there was a bar that was purple I was so excited to check it out. We weren't let in two nights in a row due to a backpack (okay that maybe understandable) and then for having a camera. This place is not tourist friendly.

I came here for a reunion event

The Good:
So I really liked the feel of this place - it has a very speak easy vibe to it and it was great for socializing in groups (the basement was of course super spacious) and there were plenty of great sofas to take advantage.

I also really liked the the glasses they served things with and their great drink selection.

The Bad:

- Parking for this place is a nightmare
- Definitely need more staff to help out (I only got drinks and that was an ordeal)
- The outside has horrible decorating - if I didn't know better this was a weird shop on a strip mall.
Excellent venue.  Small intimate performances but some really really talented musicians.  Space is limited and getting a comfortable seat will benefit your night.  Nice drink menu.
Not a huge fan of Stone Fox as a "music venue". Bartenders seemed nice, but made sure to take care of the regulars first.

Pretty cool place to grab a bite and some beers and listen to live music or watch sports!

Vegetarians, they have some options for us: cheese dip, cheese fries, jalapeno poppers, salsa, guac, three different kinds of quesadillas (and you could probably vegetarian-ize any of the pizzadillas), three sandwiches (pb&b, grilled cheese, and a veggie sandwich), and salads!  

Happy hour is Monday - Saturday, 2-7, with some pretty good deals!

One of our favorite places to eat brunch. 

First, bottomless mimosas done right. At other places you have to wave the waitress done to fill your glass--here they fill it before you even realize it was empty. All for $15.

Next, the food was delicious, the portions generous, and it came quickly. My blt ha probably a half pound of really crispy bacon on it. My friend had the green chicken chile and eggs and couldn't even finish her plate.

And they had a great bluegrass band playing on the stage. They just were just loud enough, but not so loud that you couldn't talk.

I give the venue 4 stars and their food 3. The restaurant itself is cool. It's very relaxed and there's a stage so they probably play music at night.

Came here for a Sunday brunch. Got there around 10:50 and there was already a wait. we got seated around 11:15 and left around 12:30. By the time we left, there was still a line waiting to get seated. Advice: call ahead of time.

I had biscuit with jam and added fried chicken with it. Honestly, it was okay. Nothing special. They didn't have anything on their menu that was unique. 

It's not a bad place. Decent food. Decent service. If I knew I had to wait longer than 30 mins, I would go somewhere else.

Being from the northwest I am probably a bit of a coffee snob.  Tough to get good espresso or cappuccinos in the south.  Service was nice.  Coffee was OK.  Atmosphere was OK except they painted the tile floors and walls.  The paint is flaking off.  Looks dirty and unkept.  Bathrooms were pretty disgusting.

Might have to try Dose next time.

I went here for happy hour and while I found the standard drink menu, I was a little taken back by their appetizer selections. Honestly, they charged a ton of money and served dip with some saltine crackers. Not homemade saltine crackers, no. It was straight out of the package from Kroger (or whatever). That was a turn off because it felt like they were charging me for trendy, and not really for anything truly different and cool. 

I'll go back for dinner but the appetizers were meh.

We really enjoyed the food and atmosphere here. The live music was pretty good. Jenn the bartender was fun. I had the grilled cheese and my wife had the 5 alarm burger. Both were delish. The tots were pretty good. It was not crowded but we were here in the middle of the afternoon. Good place to eat for cheap with good food and service.

Tin Roof became a go-to lunch spot for the BEST CHICKEN TENDERS IN ALL OF NASHVILLE. No foolies. The accompanying crinkle fries are just divine.

The service is pretty good overall, although there is a completely incompetent and rude b that works on Fridays and is usually on the new side. Brunette, ponytail, sour expression: avoid her at all costs.

The quesadillas are also amazing (the shrimp is very bland, so can't recommend that one). The Shroom is probably my favorite, but the Buffalo is good, too.

Do not order the nachos: TR does not have any ovens in the kitchen, so it's cold ingredients on chips. That ain't nachos, people! The hubs and I ordered them once and sent that sorry sh*t back.

Went to TR once at night, on a Friday. I was told it got stupid busy by 11, and that is a minor understatement. The crowd is young (I am not), so let that be your guide.

Again, best chicken tenders in town, if that's your thang.

Hole in the wall... it a crucial country music history wall...
Bucket list 
Thanks to The Lied To's for a great set!

Overrated is right.   Overcrowded because of the historical popularity.  Musicians are always good, but typically music is always good on Broadway.   The drinks are way overpriced.   They are taking advantage of the tourist crowd.

This place was packed. It has three different levels and great music. The drinks weren't too expensive and it was a lot of fun talking with the members of the band who came around to chat. They were taking all kinds of requests and wanting input from the crowd. The bartender was nice and always looking out for us when our drinks were almost gone.
Fun place to be without all those teenagers spilling the drinks in Nashville. It is fun. Nice music. If I can type it without error with all the drinks.

Another brunch in Nashville, The Sutler calls it Bluegrass Brunch on Sundays. I ordered a coffee along with chicken and waffles. We arrived a little after 10am, party of 8, and we did not have to wait. Always a plus! Chicken and waffles were delicious! Our server was very attentive. Check out all of their brunch menu with many options for food and beverages. I have not been there for dinner, but I have heard great things. Keep it up!

I will not go there... I went with 20 friends. Was not allowed to enter because I had a tank top.. So men can't enter with tank tops... I guess women can. Several walked in after I did with spaghetti straps... I thought Nashville was better than this...  I'll never enter that place
This was the best corn dog I ever had! The cheese on the cheese fries was delectable. The service was awesome and the environment was fun and social. Can't wait to go back for another corn dog!

Wait a minute--affordable pub style food in an unpretentious atmosphere that gets you in and out in a reasonable amount of time on lower Broadway?! Yep. Want a great burger, tasty chicken tenders, salty fries or a host of other satisfying options pre- or post-drinking or event you've found the right place. I'm always looking for good, quick fairly priced food in this area when I come to an event at Bridgestone or elsewhere in the neighborhood as there is so much of the opposite in abundance. Lower Broadway is tourist central and they know it--and hence charge for it. If I'm going to a concert or event of my taste I don't neccesarily want to get deafened by music I don't care for or go bankrupt for a sandwich and a drink prior to the show I came for in the first place and Paradise Park Trailer Resort had me covered.

I had the bacon cheeseburger with fries and a side of mac 'n' cheese---I know, a lot of cheese salt and carbs but I was starving and hadn't eaten all day (and this hit the spot). You can make that a double but after seeing the generous portion they served me I was thoroughly glad I had kept it to a single patty which is more than enough to suit a reasonable person. The patty was juicy, the cheese was melty, the bacon crisp---fresh lettuce, tomato, onion, pickle and a great bun with some good sauce and bam! The fries were super salty but tasty, fried up in peanut oil (ala "Five Guys") with a bottle of vinegar to coat them if you so desire. I added the mac and cheese which was delicious, real cheese with cheddar flavor.  My wife opted for the buffalo chicken tenders and was surprised at how meaty and good they were for bar tenders, they came layered on top of tots which were crispy and great. All of that for less than $25 (on lower Broadway)! So many places in this neighborhood charge twice what they would if located anywhere else in the city so it was refreshing to eat something good before a show and not be gouged for it.

There isn't a waiter service---we made our way in through the bar having passed up the actual restaurant entrance so it took us a minute to realize you placed your order up front at the counter but that works great here. They call your number (fast service), you grab your food and you're on the go after you take your time enjoying the meal. Gaze at the "mullet wall of fame" , velvet paintings and various trailer park motif if you want. There is (or at least was when we were here) an open mic style music thing going on in the bar area next door but unlike some of the neighboring joints it's not cranked to 11 drowning out your conversation and appetite. I realize this is "music city" but as someone very selective on what country music I can handle this is often a deterrent in hanging out too long in the touristy section of town. Thankfully we have Paradise Park right here for something different that locals can dig. I have a lead on similar such options in this part of town and will be checking those out soon as well.
Great homemade bloody mary! Brunch was OK, but baked cheese grits are worth a return visit. Service and music both great as well. I would go four stars, but the food was a bit sub par.

What an awesome, iconic spot in Nashville. If you don't know the history of this place, it's worth checking into - they have a good synopsis on the menu, which of course I neglected to get a photo of! This was one of the major sites of peaceful protest in the American Civil Rights Movement, and is really a famous place to visit for that alone.

Of course, the food is what lured me in, and it did not disappoint. We had our college-age kids with us over a weekend, and we needed a brunch spot on Saturday. The city was packed (holiday weekend), and we could not get a reservation anywhere. Fortunately, these guys had bar seats open, and it's a great bar to eat at so we took a shot. Good move! We had the corned beef hash, which was really tasty and had huge chunks of corned beef in it. My daughter had the fried chicken salad, which I didn't taste, but she said it was amazing (and it looked to be the case). I ordered the sweet potato pancakes, which I usually don't do (carbs-o-rama) but they were very likely some of the best pancakes I have had in my life. I'm not exaggerating. If nothing else, order one plate of them for your table and share - you will not be sad you did. 

We had a lovely brunch Bloody Mary (great) and Greyhound (also great), some coffee, and a lovely time chatting with the bar staff. Would definitely go back here, for sure. 

Only reason I took off a star is because I do feel they're just a tad overpriced. Coffee was $3, for example. Not grossly so, but enough to where I would not eat here that often if I was local.

This is a great casual place to get really creative and above average bar food. They have a decent beer selection, but their cocktails are just okay. The atmosphere is a little kitschy, but it works. The servers didn't really know much about food and especially didn't know anything about the cocktails or beer list. 

We ordered the fried pickles and okra, which was pretty standard but very good. I LOVED the bacon popcorn. 

The grilled cheese was good, but I was not a fan of how it came sitting in the soup. Next time, I'd ask for the soup and sandwich to be served separately. I also did not love the tomato soup because it was much sweeter than how I usually like it- this was just a matter of preference, since a few people at my table loved it. 

The roast beef sandwich was really yummy, but a little mild on the horseradish and blue cheese - some people may prefer that! 

Overall- I think the food is great. What this place needs is a ramped up cocktail program, and it would greatly improve the experience.

Great brunch guys! The atmosphere is a bit off but the food and service are great. I like the tofu options and the chicken and waffles are good too. I am excited about trying more of their dishes. This one is on the short list.

We've given this place a shot a few times now. Today confirmed that we will not be coming back. We were the only people waiting for a table, yet we still waited a solid 30 minutes (because it seemed the entire restaurant was just waiting for a waiter to bring them a check). When we finally got seated, we ordered right away because we were all very hungry. Our waitress never came by (not even once) to check in on our table or to apologize for the ridiculous amount of time we had been waiting for our food to come out.
