We were getting ready to just leave because we hadn't seen a single plate come out of the kitchen in over 40 minutes and the entire restaurant seemed to be looking around trying to figure out what was going on. In the end, it took about an hour for a food to come out, and nothing was ever mentioned of it. Our waitress did not apologize or give any explanation. The food was decent, but not great ... as always. Definitely not worth the hour and a half we spent waiting for a food. We will not continue to give our money to this business.

I gave the Bluebird 3 stars because the food and service was really great. The song writers, so disappointing! If I want to hear shitty pop country, I'll listen to country music radio. I was expecting my visit to inspire and show real country coming from people's hearts. Instead, I listened to overplayed pop songs about being "the girl next door" and "baby daddy drama" seriously. Shits weak! I saw better music at the local dive for free and didn't need to make reservations. All in all the Bluebird is unfortunately overrated.

I love this place but coming in for brunch is quite a hassle. It's always so crowded which is clearly great for the owner but there isn't much place there hang while waiting an hour + for a table. The food is fantastic and 98% of the staff is great but when it comes to the hostesses, it needs improvement. Theses ladies don't smile and have attitude when asked about things. 
If you're going have a community table please close the gap so you can get more people seated. Don't let the customer keep an empty chair in between them and the next person just bc they do not like sitting beside strangers! It's a community table!!! Also, can you please start carrying moscato wine? Brunch is perfect with moscato! 
Cudos to great food, drinks and atmosphere!

Definitely would not recommend taking your kids there after 6/7pm...but great live music & also GREAT food! My family and I ordered a few appetizers (potato skins and the nacho platter) and they were amazing!! Pretty unique atmosphere, and a perfect place to get the true Nashville experience!
I like the decor in this place, and the coffee was great. I didn't spend much time here, but nearly everyone around was smiling. A good sign, and after tasting the coffee, I can understand why.

We attended the CMA Fest last weekend and immediately saw Paradise Park upon our arrival. It looked entertaining and enjoyable but unfortunately, we did not have the best experience. Although, the instruction sign was clear on how to order and pick up food, there was a negative vibe with no greeting or further direction from the front cashier. Thinking it may have just been a bad day, we continued to pay and wait for our food. We realized the number display was not working and instead, the cooks were calling out numbers for food pick-up. We weren't sure how long it's been this way or if it was actually normal, but it seemed a mess to us. Food was being wasted from not being picked up or given away to other customers for free. Our order number did not match the order given to us and we had to wait for almost an hour for two hotdogs, and fries. The food itself was amazing, and the rooftop atmosphere would bring us back. Just hoping after the planned remodel, there will be a better experience.

Easily one of the top bars in the South. You can go there anytime of day and listen to some amazing music. You don't need to be a country fan to enjoy Tootsie's and Nashville. The staff is excellent and the prices are cheap. I had 3 beers and my bill was 9.00 on a Monday afternoon. Fri and Sat nights the crowd is having a blast.

Wow - this place is truly one of a kind! I'm so happy we were able to get tix and experience the Sunday night singer/songwriter session. All of the artists were phenomenal and I enjoyed the quiet, intimate atmosphere with everyone giving their full attention.

Bought tickets to the hot chicken and jorts fundraiser event which was really a good time and good way to say goodbye to the place. Only problem is the next day I noticed the bartenders had taken it upon themselves to leave a $20 tip on a $12 tab. Currently disputing with the credit card company. Hopefully these awesome people aren't hired elsewhere in the city.

nice service, good beer and top music!
the rooftop its verry nice! i love it! we go there on 11 AM and its play a live country band! thats cool!! i definitly come back!!

Giving 3 stars because i have attempted to eat here 3 times but haven't had the chance- worst parking situation in town.  The $3 for valet says, "yeah, we know it's garbage but we don't care"... It screams amateur for a restaurant that should average $50/cover.

If you are the landlord reading this- designate some parking for your businesses... It's a key to success with multi-use.

Two words: bottomless mimosas.

The food is priced correctly and the mimosas were strong! Bottomless for $17 is really quite the deal, and I'm so excited I found this hidden gem in Melrose.

I had the the andouille hash with their complementary biscuits and, OOH GIRL, the food was delicious! With great live music, amazing service, and reasonably priced food and drinks, I'll be back numerous times.

This place sucks!!! It's like being in a police state. There's bouncers in fluorescent yellow shirts lurking everywhere, sneering discerningly for someone to harass. I'll use my experience last night as an example: I was upstairs by myself (I'm here for work you see) paying inflated prices for mediocre drinks, and I approached a single woman and was immediately interrupted by some fat excuse for a human being and told, "don't disturb the ladies, leave them alone and move on." I could see this being necessary if I was drunk and being disruptive or making this woman and her friends uncomfortable, however this was not the case. After questioning his authority, and this is the part that makes my blood boil, he decided to put his hands on me and push me out of the bar. I'd like to see him again and put my hands on him. I don't need to be regulated while I'm out in a bar spending money and trying to have fun. Save yourself the hassle and go elsewhere!

Tootsie's is a must
Every floor is lots of fun
Rooftop is a beaut

Bit of an odd place.  Not sure why I paid $5 for a terrible country/random song they felt like playing cover band.  The real issue was the amount of extremely loud 40rd old plus people having no self control.   A plus is the bathroom was surprisingly cleaner than I expected.

We love performing at The Bluebird on our tours through Nashville. Steve Goodie is an amazing Sunday host and it's the best listening crowd in the country!
Watch our music video here:
https://youtu.be/X01MtEiuNP8

Whitherward
www.whitherward.com

Really cool for an end of the week Friday happy hour. The cellar has a very intimate feel, it's super dark down there. The melrose mule was delicious and refreshing and at half off price you can't beat it! The only thing that I didn't love was how loud it was there, not because of the amount of people but because of the building itself. 4.5/5 for sure.

Really cool vibe! They have different cocktails upstairs & an entirely new menu downstairs. Get your first drink at the bar and then venture downstairs for your second. If you're going for dinner, go early and ejoy the cool basement vibe. It's upscale but casual. Most weekends they have live music. So glad this great venue is in the Melrose neighborhood!

When it was much warmer, a group of friends and I came here to enjoy the Bluegrass Brunch, which features live Bluegrass music on Sundays from 10AM-3PM. We came around noon and the wait was about 30+ minutes but they had plenty of outside seating for us to wait at so it wasn't bad. 

Once inside, we were able to snag a booth right by the open window, which was perfect. Our server made great recommendations and was attentive. The live music was a nice touch and not too loud for us not to be able to talk to one another. 

Since I'm an unapologetic lush, I immediately zoned in the Bloody Mary Bar, which allowed you to pick your choice of vodka then have your gander at whatever fixings you want. I went with my beloved Tito's. The Bloody Mary Bar is located to one side of the stage and had a good variety of hot sauces, seasonings, celery, olives, and dried meats like pepperoni and salami. Honestly, the only thing else I wish they had was slices of bacon. They also offer $15 unlimited mimosas, which was very appealing. 

Honestly, I don't recall too much about the food. Let's just say we had a boozy brunch. I know I ordered an entree but by the end of finishing my Bloody Mary loaded with all my favorite fixings, I don't think I ate very much of my actual food. 

Overall, I would come here on a nice day to grab a seat by the open windows and enjoy an afternoon brunch.

I would give this less than one star if it was an option. This bar is super cliché, and while it could be a cool concept it is poorly executed. The staff here is terrible. The guys at the door are super douchey. Don't waste your time choose bar that better fits what you're looking for. If you want a true Nashville experience with live music go to tootsies. If you want bad food and bad service come here.

Great atmosphere with okay food. I ordered the Cheeseburger with Fries and it was okay but no where near the best burger in the world. After I ordered I noticed that the cashier did not ask how I wanted my burger cooked. That is not a good sign.
 But this place serves food late night and has live rock music which are a big plus.

This was my favorite spot to drink and see/hear live music in Nashville. Very happening place with very attentive bartenders and awesome live music. The bar itself looks old and kinda nasty but if you're here to have a good time it doesn't really matter. They have multiple levels with bands on each floor. Would definitely return if I ever come back to Nashville.

Place is filled with pretentious hipsters who are too cool for anything. I assume the chef is too cool to cook since I am sitting at the bar for over an hour for a glorified grilled cheese with turkey. But at least I am now getting 2 beers at a time? 

The Sunday Brunch gets great reviews. The Thursday sandwich dinner-not so much.

The bouncer shoved me for no reason last night after waiting in line to get food. Nobody should be treated like that. Sad that you can't go out and have a decent time without worrying about some jerk. Would not recommend going here. The owner of this establishment was put at tremendous risk by this fellow. Just think if I had gotten hurt from an unprovoked attack by this worthless employee what could've come from this!

Excellent music, so-so service- would have had more fun if there was more room in the uppermost floor where the band was. My group wasn't able to watch the band because the upstairs bar was at 100% capacity. Could hear it from the second floor though. Only got one beer and that was from the beer tub on the ground floor. Didn't start a tab upstairs as the bartender was down the shitter. Trying to give her the benefit of the doubt because it was a Saturday night- but second floor bar could have been run way more efficiently and my group would have stayed longer than we did.

We just stopped in for a quick lunch, it meets the perfect description of a dive bar. The bar itself had, of course, great live music. There is a separate dining area so you can enjoy your food in a quieter area. We were pleasantly surprised to find that the burgers were amazing. No complaints here!

This place was pretty rowdy and full of 20 something's looking to get drunk. I couldn't even hear the music over the screaming bachelorette parties. If you're looking to get bombed this is the place. Lol

Reservation system is the worst.  Waited online in the queue for 18 minutes (exactly as instructed) and when I was redirected to the site to make my purchase, was greeted with "sold out".  This is for a week night show.  VERY irritated.

We were so excited to go check this place out until we finally went in and were so repulsed by the smell of rotting grease? Beer? Something rank! We turned right back around.

Thinking they should replace the green carpet through out the bar with something a little more sanitary. :(

Had Donatello's Toast for brunch and was extremely surprised at how good it was . The atmosphere of this place was phenomenal. Extremely unique , free arcade games and board games while waiting . Very unique and food was delicious.
Ate a burger here yesterday and am now dealing with the WORST case of food poisoning ever. Seriously guys, if you're thinking of stopping in here, do yourself a favor...keep walking.

I.love.their.brunch.

The boy had chicken and waffles and I was so annoyed! You know when you order something and then realize after it comes that you should have gotten what your dining partner ordered. Yeah, that was me. I kept trying to steal his food. Not that what I ordered was bad, his was better!  What I ordered was the BBQ pork omelet. My problem with the item was that there was too much pork in the omelet and that they seemed disconnected. I think I would have liked it better if it was BBQ pork served with two fried eggs, eggs over-easy or scrambled. That way the items could mix in harmony. What ended up happening was that I unfolded the omelet and ate the pork out of the middle with the potatoes. Even so we were on the back patio and it was great. Relaxing, calming, and sipping on a mimosa in a mason jar, I was content. It's almost two totally different venues when you eat out back. Next time I plan on trying the enchiladas. I hear wonderful things about them!

Beyond brunch we went for the Kentucky Derby. The place was packed, the bartenders were hustling, and the ponies were racing. Mint Julep in hand I watched my horse not win. (wha whaa)

Overall I'm a huge fan of the Fox. I left feeling like, but why, why must you be so far away from me?? I would come here every weekend if I could! Instead I have the honey drive me. (It's on a short list of things I will drive too.) The prices are great and they really pack the schedule with things to do, see, or listen to!

We spent the weekend here with friends - finally decided to go to Tootsie's hearing that it was a famous place and fun.  We went up to the 3rd floor looking forward to having some fun.  The bartender "Taylor" that waited on us had attitude from the beginning. We ordered our drinks, one with just a splash of cranberry - she made it with a lot of cranberry.  then we gave her a $50 bill and she gave us change for a $20 -  when we asked her to remake the drink the way we asked and then corrected her on the amount of money she gave us back - she rolled her eyes and gave us attitude- and I don't mean a little bit of attitude.   She then started talking back to us being rude and obnoxious - we asked her name and asked to speak to a manager.  She proceeded to call security and they refused to bring us a manager - and escorted us out without hearing our side of the story and getting us a manager.   As a couple in our 50's and not trouble makers we've never been treated in such a manner and under no circumstances will we EVER step foot back in that hole of an establishment or tell anyone to go there.
Typical honky tonk. Bar goers say it's one of the best bars with live music on Broadway. It gets really busy on the weekends. And it has rooms with live music.

Great local hideaway.

Came in on a Wednesday had a pint,, $3 porter unheard of!

Live musc was just what I needed


4* just because of the $5 cover but hey, everyone has to eat !

We were lucky enough to score a reservation after about 3 weeks of no luck lol the ticketing system is terrible! Once we arrived, very easy check in experience. Unfortunately our waitress was rude and never checked in to see if we needed anything. I had to ask for a drink menu 3 times- I am a New Yorker and have no patience for sh*t like that lol The food is blah and overpriced for quality you get, my fries were freezing.

Now the performance was awesome and the band we saw "Wildeyes" was great! They went outside for a little preshow performance of "Jolene" as well, which was fantastic!

Overall fun time and if your able to get a reservation it's worth the trip but yes there is great music all over Nashville, so no fret if u can't make it in!

A cool place to hang out and listen to some music.  I wish there were places like this in Miami!  Alas, the culture is very different down here!

If I am ever in the area again, I'll be back.

I love the Stone Fox, and I especially love that it's in my neighborhood! I've visited twice now within a couple of months and look forward to going back again. 

Both times I have received excellent, personalized service. They're quick with suggestions and information, as well as explaining the different beers they offer to my husband. 

If you're there for happy hour times, be sure to ask for their Small Plates menu, because the flatbread pizza is where it's at! Their homemade chips are pretty much the best, too.

We're not much into the live music scene, so we make sure to visit when we know they are not performing. Our latest visit came during a sound check, and I know for sure that our choice of times to avoid live music was spot on, as you can't hear anything but the music when there. If live music is your thing, then you definitely need to go during those times, because the music we heard sounded great, but we were there to visit with family. The sound check didn't last long, so it worked out well for us. 

I hope to visit soon on a weekend for brunch, because I hear that they serve an excellent brunch. They serve chocolate gravy. Can it get any better than that?
It was a country music fan's dream come true. Long line, great acoustics, memorable time.

Awesome spot on Broadway! This place is small but was pumping with a great band on a Tuesday afternoon, female singer was standing on the bar performing!  Bartender was attentive, quick, friendly  as soon as we walked in. You share tables with other guests but it's fine bc everyone's happy!

Gourmet food with a come add you're ambiance! ! Nevertheless, I 'd urge to let them know to go easy on the salt! ! Amazing and exceptional menu !!!!!! Yummy !! Highly urge the trout! ! Yet tell them to go easy on the salt, all of my friends loved it, but it was a little salty, other than that, great setting! !!
Loved loved loved bluebird cafe!!! The music was wonderful, the group had such amazing chemistry. I am hoping to come back again soon.

Ok so this was the second bar I went to with my girls for my night out on the town in Nashville celebrating my bachelorette party. This place was amazing compared to the first bar we went to. The drinks were priced fair and the band was awesome. The bat also had a lot more room for standing, sitting, and dancing! Needless to say I would totally recommend going here when trying to find a fun place to party in Nashville. There was no cover charge and the bouncer was very sweet as well as the bartenders and band members. If your looking to get down country style, dance in a bar, or enjoy live music and yuengling, this is the place for you!
This was an awesome nights. The wait staf was great and ver helpful. They even moved our table for a better view. The artists were friendly and honest with thier stories and songs

Super cool bar off Broadway that is definitely worth stopping at. This place was absolutely jammed pack so it was super difficulty to navigate through it. The bands on each floor and the rooftop view were great. Would recommend trying the apply pie moonshine from here!

When I went here we heard really good things about this lounge from the desk clerk at our hotel. I was excited because it seemed a like a very cool place. When we got there there was absolutely no place to stand downstairs. The place was completely packed with people standing right next to each other. You could literally see the sweat in the person in front of you. It was hot and very uncomfortable. The drinks were pretty good if you could get to the bar. We only had one and then left because we couldn't handle the zoo. 
On a positive note however, the music upstairs was really good. The band was high energy and really got the crowd going. If we could have gotten our drinks amongst the mass amount of people we probably would have stayed to listen to them.

Entertainment was 5 Star. Dillon went above and beyond to make sure the group I was with was safe and had a great time! He was also the one that greeted and wished us a good night when the bar closed.

Anywhere that breaks the rules and stamps my hand at 7.00pm instead of the stated 8.00pm is A-OK, this meant we were paid and guaranteed entry in case it was a sell out but could go off elsewhere until 10.15pm.  A small but perfectly formed venue with tables and a lounge area.  The sound for Meadownoise was great as was it for Tristan's release party.  A packed venue with a front and back patio for a gasp of air.  The menu had enough to please the veggies including , Mac and Cheese $9, Bimibap $10 and Fox's Hot Chicken $12 and Fish and Grits $12 for the res of us, The cocktail list was lovely and   well crafted, I guess I am saying I had preconceived ideas that were way off the mark.  This was a delightful surprise, a young crowd on the whole but a good vibe is a good vibe, wish it was on the East Side.

Not as impressed as I thought I'd be! The atmosphere is neat but the entres aren't spectacular. Fried pickles & okra was delicious &the Christie cookie dessert didn't disappoint but I'm not so sure we'll be back. All our entres seemed to be infused with much more spice than the menu elluded to and had not much flavor since all my taste buds got so hot.

Hailey is the best server ever!!!!
Hailey is the best server ever!!!!
Hailey is the best bartender ever!!!!
The food isn't that great
Hailey is the best server ever!!!!
Hailey is the best server ever!!!!
Hailey is the best server ever!!!!

Came here for the fried pickles that other reviewers mentioned, only to find that they aren't on the menu. Ordered some cheese fries instead. They were ready in 26 seconds but I was eating raw potatoes. Also, the band was incredibly brazen, demanding $30 to continue playing the song they strummed a few notes of. Someone caved in to their incessant bullying, and then the lead singer announced that they didn't even know how to play the song and would wing it. He sounded awful - I feel bad for whoever wasted their money to hear "Africa" tonight!

Stop in for drunk food late night, otherwise keep on walking down Broadway.

Fast service, but drinks are really small - barely cover the bottom of the cup.  Maybe that's good, considering that most people around the area bar-hop, and it's not their first drink. Good fun music and fun crowd.

We made our way into the bar around 430 on a Friday afternoon. The band playing was excited to see our bachelorette party walk in, and immediately invited the bride up on stage. The main singer was encouraging the playful banter with the bride, but eventually flipped on a dime. He flipped after the bride took his hat and put it on her own head. Apparently that was a trigger point for him because he immediately put his hands on the bride and physically shoved her off the stage. Half of the bridal party left the bar immediately while the others finished their drinks. While the other half was still there, the singer told the bar "f*** those girls" as they were still standing there. While walking on Broadway to the next spot, multiple groups came up to show their sympathy for the situation. They had all left after watching that incident play out. Overall, the singer was a very poor representation of a bar that came highly recommended. Hopefully, the bar recognizes this and takes the appropriate action to address the disrespect of their hired entertainment.
A classic, but also a shit show.  I think there are three stages, one way in the back, one upstairs, and one near the entrance.  Crazy big and busy.  Definitely a must stop for an out of towner.

Great spin on corned beef hash! Best flavor with a combo of hot sauces (Texas ketchup and ones name I can't remember that taste like Tabasco). Has corned beef chunks, sautéed bell peppers and onions with skillet potatoes, black-eyed peas, 2 eggs cooked of your liking and I chose a corn muffin. Worth writing about.

Nashville 
Good sounding band. 
Awesome fiddle player who worked the room! 
Nice view of the area from the top floor,
Awful.  Ignored by bartenders for a good ten minutes.  Then failed to check I.D.'s.  First and last time we'll be in.  Nothing more left to say about this place.

We came in the other day as we always try to do when we come downtown. Love the food and the atmosphere and that it doesn't cost an arm and a leg to get a beer! But this time the bartender Tawny, was fantastic, she had such an outgoing and fun personality. I tend to be critical seeing that I'm a long time bartender (which is awful, I know) but her service was on point. I hope to see her again next time we venture out!
We were looking forward to a nice meal while in Nashville and unfortunately did not find it here. I truly cannot write anything good about the meal, staff, or cleanliness of restaurant.

This place is awesomeness except the seating 
Which holds 75 they turn away business 
Every 2 hours I'd love for them to find a bigger 
Place but from what I'm told they like doing 
Business this way anyways the band's are 
Always great and the service is awesome

Well, crap. I wanted to like this place, but it's really not worth it - at all. First of all, service is rude - from the get-go. We were in line, and dang if someone who works there didn't just cut everyone off and order a bunch of stuff. Here, you order up front (from someone who wishes they were anywhere but there), and then go find a table. We did that, and while my husband was watching our stuff, I went over to the other side to the bar to get us each a drink. So, instead of the usual 2 drink limit per person, there's a 1 drink limit per person. Each of us had to go get our own drinks - even though we're over 50. This is just a dumb business plan. Food was only o.k.. He had the chili, and I had the Paradise Patty Melt. There was supposed to be a "board" where your number would be shown to let you know your food was ready. Wasn't working, but the kitchen staff didn't seem too concerned. Customers were looking around - wondering whose food was up there getting cold. Unfortunately, this will go on my list of places to never go to again in Nashville.

Came here on the recommendation of the Blue Collar Comedy Tour Bus (or whatever that thing was called).  We were told that it was the best burger on Broadway, so we figured we'd check it out.

This is more of a fast-casual type of restaurant- you place your order at the counter in the front and then pick up your food in the back.  We went on a Saturday before a hockey game, so it was pretty busy.  We probably waited about 20 minutes for our food.

We sat down on the bar side of the place.  There was a live band, playing hard/classic rock covers.  While it was a nice break from country music, I wasn't really a fan of the band that was playing.  However, I did enjoy the meal.  My husband and I both got a singlewide burger with sweet potato fries.  This meal was a good value for the price and quality.  I'd definitely come back for the food.

I had to give three stars, however, because I just didn't like the atmosphere.  The band was too loud for a place that was more of a eating-type of a place.  And it just wasn't a very comfortable place to eat a meal.

I usually don't grade bars but after my experience at tin roof I feel it's necessary! THE WORST service from the bartenders (especially the tall bearded female). I love coming to Nashville and enjoy the town, but I will never go back to the tin roof (horrible service !!!!!)

The line scenario is a joke. Lie, cheat and steal to be in line 1 or you just wasted 2 hours of your life standing in the sun. There are plenty other places for great live music. Would not recommend the experience.

I have visited once before and had a great time.  Unfortunately your reservation system is crap and site does not process the demand adequately.  Half loaded pages, table selection, bogged down, etc.  Terrible experience that obviously causes frustration and now general disinterest in your bar.

Don't take your backpack, they won't let you in. Seems silly, being smack bang in the middle of Broadway you're going to get a lot of tourists popping in, some are going to have bags from shopping (what's the difference?) - we weren't staying centrally to drop anything back. It's a small backpack, no bigger than a large handbag really. I just use a backpack now because handbags hurt my back. 

Maybe next time Tootsies! I've heard great things about you!

I would give it 4 stars but I didn't really know the cultural and historical importance of this place. The place is very cool looking, and the music is excellent, but I personally didn't think it was worth waiting 1.5 hours. There was a $12 entrance fee plus a required $7 purchase minimum. I wish I was able to appreciate the venue, but it's hard when I didn't grow up listening to southern music.
Been waiting in line since 6pm. The band and friends got in us..   Yea  we still stand out here...  Awful place!!!

Nashville is full of great restaurants but this one tops our list.  My husband & I enjoyed our brunch there so much that we managed to squeeze in one more meal before we had to depart.  The food was delicious and the staff was friendly and welcoming.

They need to train these servers. The host/wait staff is a hot mess. The hostess grunted at us and threw our menus on the table. The server was incompetent. I asked what blancos tequila they had and her response was "I don't know, a bunch I can't pronounce." GIRL BYE. She didn't offer to go check or ask or even write them down so I could read them myself. She suggested I just order the tequila that someone else at my table had ordered. Still have no idea what it was. And when it came out, I sipped mine which was disgusting then compared to my friends which tasted normal so either my glass was dirty and still had sanitizer in it, they started pouring the wrong drink or someone just put something in it. Cool. I would have sent it back but we were ignored the rest of the night. This place sucks.

It's a very cool space that was renovated and is like walking back in time. We had brussel sprouts, chicken liver entree, farmers plate. All were great.  Will be returning. Make sure to check out the other floors after you eat.

Prepare yourself because this place get's pretty packed, but I can definitely see why. The talent is through the roof, this place has several levels. The view from the rooftop is absolutely amazing. This place pretty much represents what Nashville is all about. The entertainment, drinks, and the crowd equal a great time.
I had to wipe vomit off my shoe after leaving this place. Tourist trap. The music was descent but the bar staff were very rude and inattentive. Ew.

Had a ladies night with BINGO (mondays) at 9 and 2-4-1s til 10 and we had a great time. Although I didn't order any food, my gal pals really enjoyed the Pimento Sandwich and the chicken tenders basket. I was all about the drinks, well drinks to be exact for the 2-4-1 prices including beer. Both drinks I ordered, a whiskey & ginger and gin & sprite, were surprisingly strong :-) And at 2 drinks for $5 i made out pretty well! BINGO was really fun and with a packed house, there was definitely excitement in the air...who doesn't like prizes from Grimey's??? I'll definitely be going back for the food!

Totally divey, but cheap beer and the band actually had some talent to speak of. (Playing electric guitar with glass slide, good. Going around with a bucket and hitting patrons up for tips, not so good... just sayin)

Drank a local beer called "Jubilee" and chain smoked in the front window with some friends while listening to live music. I consider that a win.

The vibe of this place and I didn't mesh.  It had a hipster/preppie thing going on and there was a large party that was a little tipsy.  I got the impression from the look on our server's face it wasn't the usual.  The hot chicken was ok, and husband's gumbo wasn't anything exceptional.  Felt the beer was a bit limited given other options in town.  

Fun renovation and great location for the area.  Happy I tried it, but probably won't be back.

This was a great venue to visit for a night out. The three floors have all bars and room to dance and live bands that will make you shake rattle and roll. The bartenders are on it and you don't have to wait long and some bands even take requests. Such a good time and lots of talent
Food was great! Atmosphere was great! Bartender was awful. Not only not great at managing a busy bar but bad attitude! If you don't like your job DON'T bartend.  Especially in Nashville.

"You know it is a hot spot when you're the oldest person there" says my friend. Interesting eclectic 1950s Formica throwback. Great bar design. Food good- had to ask for fresh avocado because original guacamole tasted old- being an avocado adficiando I am picky! Chicken and waffles interesting and tasty with the spicy maple syrup adds a nice touch.

Woolworth was an interesting experience. I ordered the gumbo and deviled eggs for my appetizer. The eggs were great but my the rice in my gumbo was not fully cooked. The waiter replaced it in a timely manner. I enjoyed the short rib for my entree but it was a little salty. 
    Although the food left more to be desired, the service was spectacular.  I also enjoyed the facilities.  Don't forget to tour the mezzanine for some superb photographers of Nashville's history.

Definitely a happening place. Crowded, multiple floors, multiple live bands. It gets a little too noisy and crowded at times. The bar doesn't sell bottled water or iced tea, so if you don't want alcohol you're stuck with soda. 

There are girls all around selling beers, with not so subtle signs asking for tips.  

Definitely go up to the various levels to decide what band you like best.

Really enjoyed this place. They have a nice roof top bar that's great when the sun goes down and it isn't as hot. Very attentive bartenders and the music was good too. Good crowds and fantastic people watching

Went here with the family this past week.  Even though it was obviously busy, the service was fantastic.  Multiple levels with live music on everyone of them.  The only thing stopping me from a 5 star was the lack of an elevator for some of my family members to enjoy the rooftop.  Defiantly stop in for great music and great drinks!!

A coffeehouse with a mission. I  so thankful Green Hills has The Well as an option for morning brew. I was impressed with the spacious seating area as well as all the natural light it provided. Absolutely refreshing! I ordered one of their breakfast sandwiches & it was pretty generic. Would've been nice to see it topped with some fresh veggies. It felt a little "grab from the fridge & heat." Aside from that, I definitely recommend this shop! If you go make sure to check out their Wishing Well!

If I'm going to say anything I am going to say that the bread is absolutely amazing. Best bread I have ever eaten in my entire life. For my meal I had the fried chicken and it was OK as far as fried chicken goes. The drinks at the bar were delicious and the atmosphereis really neat! Our server was great too!.

I went with a group and was kicked out for no reason and offered no explanation other than a very rude "have fun somewhere  else" by the security. I was ejected so quickly I didn't have time to notify the group I was with that I had to leave. I have a few folks that can vouch that I was in no way being belligerent or doing anything to warrant the way I was treated. This was my worst experience on Broadway so far and I'll be "having my fun somewhere else" permanently.

A friend and I went to here on a recommendation while visiting Nashville. 
It was a few flights of stairs to get to the bar. On the Saturday night we visited it was JAM PACKED. Literally could barely move at all. Despite this we someone managed to get beer very quickly. 
We did notice the patio seemed fairly open. We walked towards it but were told by a bouncer they only let a certain number of people out there at a time. We waited in line and watched others make the same error we did it only took a couple minutes for us to make it outside. 
The view was incredible. It was a panoramic of the Nashville skyline. Across the street was where the Predators play so there were larger than life posters of attractive hockey players. 
There was a large bucket with beers you could purchase outside without going back in. I paid cash but I cannot remember if they accepted cards there. 
We couldn't hear the music outside (which had been very good) but we could breathe. Awesome place overall.
Good bands...couldn't really get over the no weapons sign on the door or being wanded, the chilly was good but drinks more than the competition.

I want so badly to like this place because I've recently moved into the neighborhood. I'm writing this review after my 3rd visit to the Stone Fox, so I will try to provide input from all 3. First encounter: We just went for beers and to listen to live music. Con - We ultimately had to sit outside because the volume was unbearable, and I'm no stranger to small music venues with Indy artists. Pro - They have a neat patio area. Second encounter: This was for a neighborhood function. I had an ok burger and again listened to live music with less than great acoustics and obnoxiously loud volume. It was difficult to converse with people at my table, and we were even sitting on the other side of the restaurant. Third encounter: A friend and I went for dinner on a Wednesday night; I had Elise's Favorite (it was just fine) and my friend had the BBQ plate (we both worked at BBQ places during high school or college and were less than impressed). By the time we received our food after sitting down at the bar to order, 45-50 minutes had passed with no explanation from anyone. This is unacceptable! Ordinarily I would pass the time with a bourbon or beer, but they charge $10-12 for a pour of Woodford Reserve. Some places might be able to get away with that, but this is not one of them. In summary, this place has a cool atmosphere and the food is fine, but it is certainly overpriced coupled with subpar service.

If the food was cheaper, I'd give it a 5. This is the place to have breakfast in Nashville! I'm not one to pay for "ambiance", but this place has it. The food is good, service is excellent, but I lucked out and sat next to a regular, who attends the place consistently. Also, there was piano playing in the background. What a treat. This place is a treasure. And read up on the history, so if you don't know, now you know.

If you're looking for a good time in a packed bar with great music and a rooftop, this is your spot. Service was on point and bartenders always seemed to be looking out for every customer, plus multiple cash tubs of beer available in other spots.

This place is a Nashville classic. They even have a location in the airport as you come in (definitely a place to be if you're early to your flight or waiting on a ride). 

Anyway, the location of Broadway is historical and always a hit on the strip. With three floors of live music and a rooftop view of the strip, this is always my first stop in Nashville. I usually go with a local IPA and a spot on the rooftop patio to look over the street and hear the band at the same time.

We go to Stone Fox nearly every Sunday for brunch and always take out-of-town company there and EVERYONE always raves about how good it is. 

The Bloody Mary's are made from scratch and could be a full-meal themselves. Coffee is from local roaster Drew's Brews (excellent!), and the atmosphere is very cozy inside or outside (outside is the best, take note.)

For food you can't go wrong with any options. We've been there enough to have tried nearly everything and we're always satisfied, however the best option is the Chicken & Waffles. Two breaded chicken tenders on a belgian waffle, with maple syrup on the side as well as a maple-syrup-hot-sauce infusion. Go with this one amply--SO GOOD! Add an egg if you're feeling particularly hung-over.

Proud to have this place as a part of the Nations neighborhood--plus the Outlines neighborhood block-party they've thrown the last two years now has been STELLAR!

Holy cow Paradise park is the place to be!! Regardless of the broadway craziness and being unable to sit at a bar, Tawnie the bartender found me and my person s place to sit it's a Sunday and the place is packed... she still made it a point to let us know who was about to leave and when she could accommodate us... I'm from CA and came back over and over while i was in town because of my experience here with her!  thank you for being so awesome!
Disgusting service and good. Do not eat here. I was recommended by some friends and it was a horrible experience. Absolutely awful.

I wanted to like Woolworth on 5th. I have been to every other Tom Morales restaurant in Nashville and Franklin and have liked them all. I hope tonight was just a bad night for Woolworth on 5th. The hostess was aloof. When we arrived 5 minutes before our reservation, she coldly said "Have a seat and we'll call you when your table is ready." The chicken was dry and the order was wrong. The manager stopped by and asked how it was. No discussion when I said "OK." He said "Great," so I guess OK is the goal. Fortunately, Nashville has many restaurants with loftier goals.
Such a great bar and authentic.  Bartenders are very attentive and musicians are great.   Bathroom attendant was aggressive and uncomfortable.  Drink there.  Don't pee there!!

The food was not good. The meatloaf has been thrown on the grill to be reheated. The mac n cheese was hard and not good at all. It was greasy and the brisket looked like dog food. The service was amazing, super sweet girl. She cute too. The food was garbage. Sorry sutler. Local Nashvillian not impressed

Tootsies rooftop is fantastic when the sun is shining! Live music was fun inside and the bartenders were helpful.  Friends got food and they really liked what they ordered - quesadilla egg rolls and chili cheese hot dog.  Classic place check it out if you're in Nashville for the weekend/downtown.

Loved this place 
Had the best time and great music.
I saw five or six bands here over three days.... all were great and the place rocks !

The wife and I stopped here on our way out of Nashville for some live music before lunch.  A nice guy was playing country western covers by request.  He asked people in the audience funny questions and the crowd enjoyed the show.  This bar has live music starting in the morning. I would happily sit here all day.

The beers here were not cheap. Market rate as opposed to inexpensive.

Love what they are doing with this historic spot. My feeling echo previous reviewers. As a Nashville native I'm thrilled that this spot and all it represents can now be enjoyed by everyone in the community. 
On the morning of my visit I went with three friends, we each ordered something different. There was fried chicken, pot roast, an entree salad and the sweet potato pancakes. All the food arrived hot from the kitchen, correctly plated. Our server was pleasant, professional and knowledgable about the menu. The menu itself covers the basics but not much more. Choices are limited. I can see the value of keeping things simple given the reality that Nashville has a shortage of cooks and wait staff. In the end, I was glad I went and I think most who care about this city will be glad to support their efforts.

Man did we love this place!

Ambiance- a 10! Eclectic, western, old time saloon wrapped into one. Just gorgeous!  Took my daughter for a special birthday lunch. She LOVES to try new places. 

We shared the sweet potato hummus and home made chips.  The pesto on the top made the hummus. When the pesto was gone, the hummus was just ok. But the chips were great. 

Then we had the bbq horseshoe sandwich and oh my it was so savory and amazing. Smoked brisket, homefries, cheddar gravy on Texas toast...with a fried egg on top. A bajillion calories but OH SO TASTY! 

After we ate,  we went downstairs (the boot sole ceiling staircase) to the basement bathrooms and discovered the 'speakeasy' room which I will definitely be going back to. (Without my daughter)

Annoyed with this place. Came for my bachelorette with 10+ girls and bought drinks for hours. On the way in and out the bouncers told me to go get a free bach shirt and after waiting 20 mins on the way out the manager told me the new promo ended 20 mins ago and wouldn't give me a shirt. When I told him his staff sucked at communication he agreed that they said that but that they were wrong and too bad. Changed my whole experience
3 great bands playing in one place (different floors). Rooftop was very nice also. Must visit if you're looking for live music

Went for brunch, have to say, food was excellent, music was awesome, our bartender (we sat at the bar) was super friendly. Met some nice people that came and went at the bar, great bloody mary's and think they have some special on mimosa's, I see on someone else post that it is bottomless mimosas!  I will definitely be back here, really had a nice brunch experience. Crowd was from 16-60, really nice energy, they really have a nice place going here! Much better feel for Nashville than the Broadway experience, great place to bring out of towners!
Best food ever!!!! I had the roast beef and it was out of this world amazing! The atmosphere was incredible. Also the history of the place was so inspiring! I can't wait to go back for breakfast.

I didn't eat here, but I was able to go inside. Very cool set up, great history, and awesome to get to visit in person....(I have seen it on the tv show Nashville). It was a must go and see while visiting Nashville because of the tv show. The manager was ridiculously friendly too!

The staff and chef need to eat their own food. Yet another Nashville restaurant serving crappy food at high prices. The Waldorf Salad was disgusting. Presentation was beautiful but I spit out my first bite. It tasted like a vinegar salad. I sent it back for one without the dressing and it came back tasting worse. They must have tossed the fruit in straight balsamic vinegar and it was also extremely spicy. The server acted like we were a bother so I boxed it up and threw it in the trash when I got home. My husband had a burger that tasted like it had  half of a bottle of salt in it but at least it was real beef and other than the sodium was tasty. The fries were great (salted to the extreme) but really, who can't cook fries? The server allowed me to have one glass of water and never offered to refill it until I finally asked for some more. The atmosphere is awesome but the greeting and seating leaves a lot to be desired. The music was the highlight and why we went but if I ever go back, I will not eat.

I've been here before but haven't had an experience like this until now. I ordered a round a shots then drinks and when I went back to ask for a water she handed me a bottle of water and said it would be $2. I asked if I could get a cup of water and she acted like she couldn't hear me and said 'what do you want?!' I repeated my question and she gave attitude which is when I told her she didn't need to be so rude. She then stopped pouring and threw the glass at me spilling on the people nearby. I just don't understand how you could be so rude working in a service industry. I asked politely and just wanted some water after ordering drinks. When I tried to ask for a manager to speak to I was given several different reasons as to when the manager would be in and when he would come talk to me. I thought I liked this place but I've never been so disrespected before for no reason.

Pretty cool place! I love the boots on the ceiling heading downstairs towards the "speakeasy" style lounge, which is my favorite area of the venue. Perfect for a chill night out with good music, food, and not too bad of pricing.

My friend wanted to start here for brunch and bottomless mimosas. In theory this sounded great I mean who doesn't love bottomless mimosas. Upon arrival the patio looked very sunny and inviting. We didn't have to wait to be seated outside which was surprising for Saturday brunch. So we sit and we already know that we want to drink of course. We get our mimosas and they look pretty heavy on the OJ and super light on the champagne.  I see everyone else in the bar ordering them so I assumed they couldn't be that bad right? However after number 3 I started feeling a cramp like a cramp you would get from chugging artificial orange juice. I asked my friend if she felt the same and she did. Finally we see that they are not making the mimosas individually to get the ratios precise, they are actually just pouring them out of a huge pitcher for the "bottomless" crews. Now this might be a normal bottomless mimosas thing that others are used to but I was completely thrown off and felt a bit ripped off. After the bottomless Artificial OJ no one really felt like eating so we headed somewhere else for food. I say 3 stars because the vibe was nice and our server was incredibly nice and attentive. Would I go back....probably not.

It's so interesting to me to see the revitalization of the 12 South area. From Sinema to The Sutler, the different condo buildings opening up, this place has turned the course. My first time at The Sutler was as a plus one to a filming for a show on The Travel Channel called Food Paradise. We waited at the bar before the cameras went up & I ordered a Royal Crown which is George Dickel in a RC cola bottle. I think they actually pour a little soda out of the bottle & then put the Dickel in. It's 6 bucks & not bad. 

The interior of the place looks common for Nashville, it's very western, Honky-tonk. They've got a stage that frames the backend of the restaurant. Lots of wood throughout. It's not a bad atmosphere to dine & have some drinks. I tried the Mac & cheese & the hot chicken nuggets they have on the menu. The hot chicken isn't too hot; more spicy to me. They've got a great aroma when they come to the table. The dipping sauce is an "Alabama sauce". The Mac & cheese is CHEESY as one would imagine. It's got pulled pork on top. The noodles are those ruote type that look like wagon wheels, I would prefer a normal macaroni noodle, but I guess I'm a traditionalist. 

They've also got a somewhat of a speakeasy downstairs, another bar & lounge area that you'd never guess was down there. I had no idea there was even a downstairs. Downstairs you'll also find the bathrooms. They're kind of tucked away. The stairs that lead downstairs have tons of shoes that line the ceiling. They look (& smell) like old shoes. Anyway, the food was enjoyable & so was the atmosphere.

Must try the sauces, they are fabulous. Had the carrots and roasted beets as well as the sweet potato soup...both were yummy. The squash sandwich was really good too. This all coming from a veggie. Not disappointed a bit.
Awesome venue. A must do if ever visiting. Atmosphere is so cool and so chill felt like we were all just hanging out at a bonfire (without the fire) playing music and telling stories.

Lol. Love this place but despise this place, ew.

This bar is so gross... but so awesome. Green carpet that has people's lost dignity soaked in it, beer in bathtubs, and the wood paneling on the walls makes me want to take a shower. However, the bands that play here know how to rock a crowd. This bar is one of a kind and my experience here is awesome. I also ate here two nights in a row around 2am (yikes). They have good late night food that's generally fast and priced well. 

Not sure if I'll be back, but this is a sober review now y'all

This was my must in Nashville and it was exactly what I thought it would be...fabulous! The food was just plain and decent food and the only ding of 1 star off the review.  I really didn't care too much for the food but it was just something to satisfy my belly while I fed my soul with a wonderfully curated set of fantastic music. Service was great and my Jack and Cokes always came just in time. We saw Becca Mancari, BrotherSister, Neal Carpenter and Jon Troast. They were all great and it was a truly magical experience to be in such an intimate setting surrounded by people who share great respect for singer songwriters. Will go back! It was the highlight of our 4 day trip to Nashville for me.
Great music and great times. I love visiting Tootsie's. Always a wonderful experience!

Such a cool bar. If you've never been in a trailer or trailer park, this is your chance. Service is usually quick and the music is the same as all over on Broadway. They give out free beer before the Preds games if you're going to the game. That's a win right there. I've never had the food here but I definitely don't go to Broadway to eat. From what I've seen, it looks decent. Just like the other bars on Broadway, this place fills up on the weekends. There's always room in the back area by the restrooms. Getting back there can be a challenge though.

The que system is a joke. The video they have posted a link to that shows you how to get a ticket is false. I reloaded the page at exactly 0800 and had the full page of possible reservations to choose from. I immediately clicked for a two person table and it says it's unavailable and then it's only has a few pew options so I click it and everything is sold out. Hey.... as long as they sold tickets I guess it doesn't matter to them.

I LOVED this place. Nashville bar/ music venue on one side and greasy diner burger joint on the other. Don't let the word "greasy" deter you, it is anything but lousy. I had the mini chicken sandwiches. AMAZING delicious little sliders cooked to perfection. My husband had the veggie burger and said it was one of the best he'd ever had. The bar was fun and live music was a mix of popular covers and an original here and there which I think is perfect for the scene. The baby faced bar tender said to me " wow, you're really chugging those [vodka &a club sodas] down. 33 year old me says I'm trying!

We had a great time and the food was delicious! The sweet potato pancakes are ridiculously good and the service was outstanding! The historical building makes the experience that much better! You definitely want to go for any meal that you can!
Walked here from the hotels a block away on a Sunday for a sandwich. Bouncer rude. Place crowded with drunken 20 somethings. It was loud and by the menu more bar than grill. Avoid this place.

Super nice place!   Stopped in for a business lunch.   Super clean, I like that! Food was outstanding, service was great, atmosphere awesome!  Left wanting to come back for dinner, music sometime in the near future!

I still love the Stone Fox for various reasons, but last night I came around 5:30 to eat dinner and whoever was playing that night was doing a very loud sound check for a 9 PM show.  If I wanted to hear a show while trying to talk to my friends, I would've came at 9 - not 5:30.  It was obnoxious to say the least.  Otherwise, the food & aesthetic of Stone Fox are great, but I hated listening to CHECK CHECK CHECK and vocal tune up over and over while trying to have a meal with friends.
amazing new find.  great coffee, happy staff, & charming atmosphere.  will be back - again & again!

The Sutler was the perfect place to host a high school reunion.  We had it in the Cellar in a sectioned off area which was perfect for about 100 of us.  Everyone had an amazing time! From the venue, the food and the staff who went out of their way to make sure our event was special, it truly was an ideal place for a reunion. We even had an impromptu dance party upstairs at the end of the night which was hilarious. We all look forward to coming back!

Came here Last Thursday from Dallas for a family Wedding and this place was (A Okay). If only they can remove people who smoke. But the rooftop was good and they could use an Upgrade!  I rate this place a 5/10.

Everyone has to visit Tootsies. The memorabilia and old records on the walls is worth the visit itself. The bands are always fantastic. My only complaint is the nasty bathroom with a strip club attendant and the airport bar prices. If you are coming to stay a few hours it's going to cost you a few hundred bucks.

Tootsie's is the go-to music venue on Broadway! Carrying years of distinguished historical provenance, you can feel it as you wander in past the tight first floor bar. With the walls covered floor to ceiling in photos and memories from years gone by, there'll be jaw dropping moments when you realize just how significant to this place is to Nashville.

It is old, it is dirty. Some of the employees don't seem very thrilled to be there... You chose the Service Industry.. cheer up a little.

Live music on the first floor. Make your way up the stairs to the second. Yep, you guessed it, live music there too! And one more set of stairs to the third. What's that? Yep - that's more live music! Three levels of live music and an ass-kickin roof top patio? Now that's a go-to music venue. What's awesome is you definitely can't hear the music on any of the other levels.

I guess we were lucky. I never had to wait in any of the long lines that several people talk about, and that I saw as we were walking around.. We just bar-hopped around and made our way back to TOL.

Digging this place. My one complaint is the  bleach blonde "bartender" working the third floor. I've never seen someone so lazy and avoid work like this girl has. Thrust me sweetheart, you're cute but not enough to get away with all the other bartenders carrying you.
I've eaten here once and will definitely be back. I liked the atmosphere and loved the food. Great location in 8 South. Everything we tried was great. Highly recommend.

Tootsies is one of my most favorite bars on the Music Row Strip in Nashville. This place gets a lot of hype and is very touristy, but it deserves all the praise it's been given. From the moment you walk in, this place is filled with such a fun energy, lively band, and friendly engaged bartenders and patrons. There are multiple levels to this bar and the first and second floors were open the day that I came. The first floor was playing more modern/contemporary country to a completely packed room, and the second floor was playing classic country to an equally packed room. My favorite part about the 2nd floor venue is that you can actually sit right next to the band. You get front row seats to a great show and some of the coolest people in the business.

I will say that it is absurdly packed nearly all the time, and I totally avoided it my first go round on Saturday afternoon and Saturday night. It only became reasonable to get in/hang out there later in the day on Sunday when the strip was less crowded. Despite the crowds though, it's definitely worth it to stick around.

Just spent over an hour there for lunch. The restaurant was maybe half full. You seat yourself, so I grabbed a booth. My wife was right behind me. As I was sitting down a server came by and said she would bring another menu. There was only one menu on the table. More than 10 minutes later another server came by and asked if we had been helped. We never got the other menu, but we ordered. I ordered unsweet iced tea with lemon. She brought the tea, no lemon, no artificial sweetener. My wife ordered tacos, so prior to getting our food I asked for some extra napkins, and a refill on the iced tea. We never got the napkins. Long after we had our food another server came by and refilled my tea. My steak sandwich was terrible. Tough as nails, and the bread was dried out with no taste. I never got a chance to tell our server that it was subpar because it was a long time before we ever saw her again. She brought our check, and another 10 minutes goes by, we are needing to leave, so I took the check and money to an inept bartender. She had not had a single customer since we'd gotten there, but she acted like I was bothering her. She asked the name of our server. I told her I wouldn't know that, because she never introduced herself. She leaves, finds our server towards the back. Our server proceeds to glare at me and is talking to the bartender. The bartender comes back, has a hard time figuring out that on a $31 check she owes me $9 change. Finally, she entered it on a calculator, and gave me back 9 one dollar bills. It was a tossup to go to this place, or back to ML Rose. Wish to gosh we had done the latter. Wow! What an awful experience.

Stopped by this place from a referral from a friend in Minnesota. He was right. This place is a blast! Bands on two levels, an outdoor rooftop bar, it's no wonder this place is packed with people. Had a quick beer, then went exploring Broadway Ave. We'll be back...
Always a fun atmosphere.  Just wish the bartenders would smile and say thank you when they take your money for the over priced 8 dollar drink.

This is my FAVORITE bar in Nashville!!!! It is so fun! The rooftop bar is the best, they have pitchers of beer for cheap, live music, greasy food and good people!!!!! The astroturf, lawn chairs, string lights and other funny decor items add so much character! I recommend it to everyone! It is a must!!

This place was an absolute blast. Now I'm not a big music person (blasphemous, I know), but listening to the performers on Song Writer's Night was very, very cool. I loved the impromptu songs and that family members were in the audience. It was great to talk to the songwriters after the show. What fantastic people! The wait staff was awesome. At times, the banter between performances was about awkward, but mostly it was humorous. 

The food is okay. I wouldn't come hungry. And beware, if you come to the later show they will sell out of popular food items. 

Also, be prepared to wait two hours plus in the scorching, humid heat before the show. It's definitely worth it, but definitely adds a particular smell to the experience. 

Overall, go here! Come really early. Eat a big meal before/after.

We had a reservation and we were on time. All the courses came out at the same time. We spent 300 for a table of 4 and we're rushed the entire time. When we wanted to finish our drinks and listen to the live music that was about to start we were a approached by a manager and we had to move to the bar since were finished eating. The food was pretty good. I really enjoyed the trout.  The brussels sprouts were not that great. It was supposed to be hash style but instead it was a few brussels sprouts on top of mashed potatoes didn't quite understand what they were trying to pull off there. $14 is a little high for a small Moscow Mule. In the end they are getting one star because the service was awful and I cannot believe we were asked to get up when we were finishing our drinks. In comparison the table next to us split an appetizer and got two beers and hung out longer than we did.
Really enjoyed the live music, good old country with a mix of current. Small menu but great taste!

The Bluebird cafe is truly magical. My boyfriend and I attended the Sunday night 6pm show. 

I didn't find getting tickets to be hard. I live in Philly, so the morning the tickets went on sale, I logged on at 8am and just kept my browser open. I was put in a line and once the tickets went on sale at 9 (eastern time) I was immediately entered. One thing that caught me off guard was picking your seats. I panicked and picked the first table I saw with 2 seats. I don't think there is any bad seat in the building though.

Day off: I read a lot of reviews about bad traffic so my boyfriend and I headed over early and went to a bar near by until the doors opened. There is a line for reservations and a line for non. We probably waited about 5 min until we were seated. This was around 5:30. 

The show was amazing and everything we thought it would be. After, we went to the bar across the street and talked with the band even more. I highly recommend the Bluebird to everyone

Nice atmosphere but very poor food value. I ordered the chicken horseshoe which was maybe 4 oz of chicken concealed by shoestring fries and an excessive quantity of gravy on a piece of toast for $16.

 I had such high hopes for the white chocolate bread pudding, but what arrived was a brownie like dessert that was do dry it was suitable to be used as a building material! 

The live local act was the only saving grace for the evening.
We're visiting from Petaluma, California and didn't want to miss an evening at the Bluebird Cafe!  We thoroughly enjoyed it.  Great atmosphere.

We went to a few places downtown on Broadway while waiting on the show at Ryman Auditorium.  We were on the way to see "Ghost Brothers of Darkland County" so we 
enjoyed this bar for a few drinks. I drank only soda..
There was a band there. . They were pretty good. Can't remember there names but they were pretty good. Better than some we heard in other locations. 
The Budweiser was $6 each and a soda was $3...too expensive if you ask me..but a definite Tourist spot..It was packed..standing room only...

This place doesn't allow smoking because they allow you to bring your kids in under 21 until like 8 or 9 pm...that is stupid to me...stupid...


All of these locations are small and narrow and they get crowded fast.  But at least the crowds come and go if you sit still long enough.   
I would go here again!  They love the Tourist here!! 
Remember the bands play by tips only!!!

"Dive" bar downtown on Broadway.  My best friend and I loved this bar.  We came upon it just wandering around looking for somewhere that looked cool and chill where we could have fun and drink but be able to hear each other talk too.  It was absolutely amazing and had so much character.  There's actually an ancient car parked in the front room.  There are booths if you want to sit and order food from the window from the place next door.  Lots and lots of memorabilia on the walls and so much character.  Old car seats to sit on in the front room.  Truck tailgate to sit on close to the back.  Beer in a tub behind the bar.  Love love love.

We were lucky enough to get tickets to the Wednesday, Aug. 31 with the Stellas. This was such an amazing start to our trip to Nashville. The food and drinks were great, and obviously the music was amazing. I did buy a t-shirt and got home (South Carolina) and it is entirely way too small so be careful!

Had the pleasure of stumbling upon this new restaurant and decided to give it a try for dinner. We're we're so glad we did! The historical ambiance was incredible. And the food was just simply delicious. We started with 2 appetizers -- the cheese curds and the Brussels sprouts (we loved both and would order again in a heartbeat). We shared a very reasonably priced bottle of wine.  Finally we shared the fried chicken plate and the pick four side dish plate (yams, corn pudding, black eyed peas, Mac and cheese) all amazing -- home cooking like a good southern mama would make. The service was outstanding and friendly. We're glad we took our waitress' advice and peaked upstairs at all the old photos hung on the wall depicting the old Woolworth's history. Then we checked out downstairs where a new nightclub is going in. I loved all the Art Deco decor, original flooring, furnishings, etc. -- all very true to the time. I felt transported back to the 60s. Kudos for whoever had the inspiration to bring life back into this old building!
What a blast this place is. Great rooftop bar and live music. It's a touristy spot but a must visit for the Nashville bar music scene.

Dirty  nasty urine and vomit stained sinkhole.   I understand  the place is historic but  the band was not even good.    Seems like they are falling back on their reputation  and coasting at this point.  Granted we were expecting  a rowdy honky-tonk  and not the Taj Majal. . . But everything was sticky in this joint.
Food is terrible and the staff is beyond rude. Will never visit this establishment again. Save yourself the money and time.

We ended up doing a walk-up for the 6pm show on a Thursday night and got to the Bluebird around 5:10pm. The line didn't seem that long, but apparently they had already let people who had been waiting earlier get in. After waiting for almost an hour, we were THE last three people to make it in (whew!) Note: Get tickets online or get there at least an hour early to wait in the line at the right (facing the door) which is the one for people without reservations. The one on the left is for people with tickets so you wouldn't want to get stuck waiting in that line only to find out it was the wrong one!

Since it was already jam packed, we ended up having to split up and our friend had to sit at a table close to the stage and my husband and I ended up sitting in one of the pew seating towards the back. The good thing was, there is no cover for the earlier show like there it for the late show, we just had to order drinks or food (same as the late show too).

The show we watched was "in the row" where the musicians were sitting at the "stage area" in a row. The music, banter and stories were AMAZING and it was truly a joy to watch these songwriters share their talent. There were even a couple of songs that I recognized that night! I would definitely bring friends who are visiting Nashville here and will be going back often!

The staff is absolutely wretched. Going to this bar was by far the worst experience I had during my entire trip to Nashville. If I could rate it zero stars I would. Came here with a bachelorette party which understandably can be annoying. They confiscated our flask (I get it..being a bartender myself I understand it is against policy to bring outside liquor) but the bartenders continued to take shots from my flask right in front of us. After calling out the bartender with the fake boobs , fake tan, and fake blonde hair she had security kick us out. Extremely rudely. For what? For simply asking her why she took my flask and drank my liquor right in front of me. She was so smug about it and the security guard was a dick who could not provide us with a reason for kicking us out. DO NOT GO HERE THE STAFF IS BEYOND TERRIBLE.
I could live off the iced coffee, so I frequent this place often. Works great for a casual meeting place and to catch up on work. Everyone behind the counter is always friendly.

We hit up Tootsie's again and again during our stay in Nashville.  Great bands and three floors of music!  The first floor is always packed so move upstairs to the second floor.  If that's packed you always have the third floor!  It's a noisy place but then again we went back again and again
This place reminds me of Sloppy Joe's in Key West. We had the luxury of hearing the most excellent band. Fun and lively vibe!

Waited 1.5 hours for the show which was completely worth it. However when they got to me and my husband there was only one seat left. He insisted I went in while he waited in the car. Only stayed an hour because of this but was grateful to at least have that time. Wish we would've went earlier. Truly an amazing experi

Just horrible. Menu leaves a lot to be desired. Food is average and tries way too hard to be hip southern with few choices. I ordered the trout which sounded really good only to find out that they were out of it. Would have been nice to tell us when we sat down. So I ordered the grilled cheese with bacon and was served the brisket. Never going back.

Unbelievable. The green carpeting was great. The natty light was cold. $6 pitchers. Need I say more? I mean, the place is exactly what you would expect. I thought it was a nice change during my stay in Nashville.

While waiting in line at the bar there were also hilarious stickers to read & kill time. Fun arcade games in the back in case you want to take a break from all the chatting. There was a live band when I went too, they were great and so fun!

The view from the top floor is priceless. Three floors of 80s rock and rowdy tourists there to party and have a good time. I loved it, and I get why it's one of the most popular places on Broadway. It's very crowded, but I didn't mind at all, because it's just such a fun bar to be at.

5* for the musical performance and for the fact that this venue is featured on the Nashville TV program, 4* for the food; 3 for the ambience.  The chumus, pita and fresh vegetable basket was surprisingly good for a music venue. The hummus tasted homemade and the pita was fresh (I was expecting packaged hummus and stale or defrosted pita).  It was a rare treat to be entertained UP CLOSE by wonderful singer-songwriters.  You must reserve seats a week or more in advance.  Do not go if you're claustrophobic; the seats are tightly packed in.

Words cannot express our gratitude to Brandon, Fantaicia and Danny. They went so above and beyond for my son my heart is bursting. He couldn't eat the meal due to his food allergies. We ran out to try to get a safe meal to bring back in and join the rest of our family. We struck out and when we came back in, just to sit and have a drink, the staff offered to drive to a safe restaurant to get him something! In 11 years of being an allergy momma, never have I experienced such compassion and action in a restaurant. Truly amazing people, will never forget. Thank you soooooo very much!!!
Pretty loud on any of the floors, staff was ok not the best attitudes. Bands were ok more geared for young crowds, stayed for a drink.
Location in the Nashville Airport. Worst food I've had in Nashville and worst BBQ iv ever had! Very disappointed.

I could totally see Guy Fieri barrel out of his red, open-top convertible and walk in here with his sunglasses pulled to the back of his bulbous head and his bleached hair in full spike, wolf down the burger and proclaim it as being "off the hook". Then the camera and lights go off, and he spits the whole thing out of his mouth as he moves on to the next generic diner, drive-in or dive. With its faded teal neon sign, Paradise Park looks like the perfect fit on Broadway with all the honky tonk bars, western gear stores and BBQ joints in the area. It turns out to have a split personality as half of it is a fast food spot while the other half is a long bar with a live band on a slightly elevated stage performing in front of an audience of three (photo: http://bit.ly/1OEDvHh).

We were here to eat because we missed the complimentary breakfast back at the hotel. Unless you count the post-hangover Frito Pie, there wasn't much on the menu that said breakfast to us (photo: http://bit.ly/1HTiuZw). At the front counter, we found the woman with the pony-tail and the Fireball Cinnamon Whiskey shirt a hoot (photo: http://bit.ly/1Dchlpn). When I asked her if she recommended the Spam Sandwich, she gave me a sideways look from her fashion-backward glasses and said that every time she passed by the Spam in the kitchen, it made her want to hurl because her momma made it throughout her entire childhood. So I assumed that was not a recommendation. Instead, I ordered the $8.49 Singlewide Cheeseburger.

It was a one-third-pound Angus patty with chopped onions, shredded lettuce, a couple of beefsteak tomato slices, and a slice of melted American cheese. In other words, it was your typical roadside diner burger, greasier than most, and I ordered a $1.99 side of Tater Tots instead of the fries (photo: http://bit.ly/1GhLrzd). Turned out to be a smart move because the tots were the best part of the meal with the burger having unfortunate side effects on me later that day. Jamie fared marginally better with the $8.49 Paradise Patty Melt, which took the same patty and saddled it with melted Swiss cheese and caramelized onions between two slices of rye (photo: http://bit.ly/1G5mfGw). The big orange naugahyde booths were roomy (photo: http://bit.ly/1GhLP0H), but it was starting to crowd quickly. Paradise lost, I guess.

FOOD - 3 stars...greasy fast food but the tater tots rock if you like them right out of the Ore-Ida bag
AMBIANCE - 3 stars...well, think retro-rockabilly
SERVICE - 2.5 stars...after the Fireball woman, not much except a number yelled in our direction
TOTAL - 3 stars...if you want to eat like trailer trash, be prepared to be treated like trailer trash

Awesome bar with great music - great bartenders but beware of the woman in the woman's bathroom peddling compliments and hairspray for tips this woman strong arms you to tip her - she is clearly making more money then the talent! I would go to the bar but avoid using the restroom!

This place has the best music! The upstairs patio area is usually pretty packed, but who cares? The music is better inside anyway:). I'm only giving this place 4 stars because I could have gone without the whole being carded multiple times crap. I was literally carded THREE times within 15 minutes of being there. Seriously? I'm 25 years old and there were PLENTY of other girls walking around who looked much younger than me--yet none of them were approached. It was just weird. Do you guys not trust the two gentlemen you assigned to card people at the door? Or do you just card any female under 40 that isn't wearing cowboy boots and a dress? I guess I should have worn my boots that night and joined the rest of the herd. (To be honest, I sort of regretted going straight here after my workout and not changing first... I was itching to dance!!)

All in all, it's a great place and I highly recommend it for the music.
Must visit during your Nashville stay! Super crowded but the the music live band, singers make it worth it! Loved each moment minute spent there. Can't wait to be back.
Best night ever, it was such a great time listening to the artist.  A must stop!!!!  Bartender was so nice.  Please be aware of the reservation policy, book way before you come to Nashville.

Loved this joint. Relaxed, fun and great music. So glad we got a chance to spend some time here. Plan to hang out here hard on our next trip. Didn't try any food, just enjoyed plenty of beer- had craft beer on tap, but could also get a pitcher of PBR for cheap. The music is what really made this place for me though! Loved the music.
Had an awesome time with my love and the bar maids Natilie and Nicole, then went to the roof top to hear some great music, then ran in to thi very rude b****.....the first and only rude person i met.
Might be a fun place but was extremely too crowded.  Back to back standing room only and it was early evening when we arrived.

Just a heads up if you are wanting to watch a performance your chances are very low on getting in or getting tickets.  I tried to get tickets for a Friday show.  They went on sale that Monday prior to the show and they were sold out within 1 min of starting sales.  The reason I give this place 4 stars is because I did get to go into the Bluebird on a tour.  The Manager gave us a history of the place and let us walk around and take pictures.  The tour that I went on was the ABC Nashville TV Show tour.  If I would have been able to get tickets to a show I would have gave this 5 stars.
