what a wonderful place.  you fund the building of wells in developing areas with no access to clean water with your purchases here.  

they also support awareness of other local non-profits serving those in need by allowing you to purchase those non-profits' goods (some made by women and children in the countries they serve).  it's truly a place where you can go and see how big of a change and how much help we as individuals can do just by choosing to spend our money at socially-conscious minded businesses--they have pictures of the wells they've funded with the individuals who benefit from the clean water posted in here.  

this place makes my heart happy.

Woolworth was an interesting experience. I ordered the gumbo and deviled eggs for my appetizer. The eggs were great but my the rice in my gumbo was not fully cooked. The waiter replaced it in a timely manner. I enjoyed the short rib for my entree but it was a little salty. 
    Although the food left more to be desired, the service was spectacular.   I also enjoyed the facilities.  Don't forget to tour the mezzanine for some superb photographers of Nashville's history.

I'll start by saying I definitely need to come back here to try more of the menu items and check out the live music. I stopped in waiting for a friend so I only grabbed a quick bite, the Root Salad. This wound up not necessarily being a "quick" bite since the portion was huge - definitely shareable. Basically, it's just thinly sliced root veggies with goat cheese and a light oil dressing. it was a refreshing change to a typical salad order. If I had my choice, I actually think I'd prefer this as a side salad (in a smaller portion) to the standard side salads filled with lettuce. I only stayed for two shakes of a lamb's tail so I missed a lot of the buzz surounding that nights performance. I showed up a little after 5 and was seated with no problem but by 5:30ish they were putting out reserved signs on the majority of the tables and people started showing up for the 6:30 show. The decor was attempting to be saloon like and used BALL® Spring Green mason jars from the Heritage Collection which I loved in contrast to the wood.

First time visitor to Nashville and fan of the tv show so The Bluebird Cafe was a must see. The band that played was a blues band comprising of older guys who have clearly been playing a long time as they were fabulous. I wish the guy who worked on the door at the end of the night was as well, but sadly not. Clearly he must hate that some people (you know, the paying and tipping customers) are fans of the show because he did not seem happy that he had to help and sell merchandise to any fan whatsoever. His attitude was a real disappointment, but I'm not letting it affect the fact that I'd travelled all the way from Australia and made a stop here purely as a fan of country music, the show, and wanted the experience. I'm so glad I could visit! It's just a shame there is no heating of any kind outside when you have to line up for over 2 hours to get in :(

We enjoyed my birthday dinner here on Sunday night. The renovation is amazing. I loved the old movies playing on the wall and the organic feel to the place. The food was OK. We had the pork belly, short ribs, ribbon salad (my favorite), cheeseburger and flounder. I was not overly impressed with the food as I usually am at most of TomKats locations. The service also felt rushed and the server uneducated on the menu. She kept asking us to order when we clearly wanted to enjoy some time visiting and catching up. I highly recommend the bushwaker type dessert. I can't recall the name of it, but an adult milkshake of sorts. Over all, a 3-4.

I loved this place!

Although I initially heard of Bluebird from the TV show "Nashville", this spot was verified as legit by some friends who are locals.  So on our recent trip to Nashville, my husband reserved us tickets to an "in the round" session.  Note on reservations- MAKE ONE.  They open about a week in advance of every show.  Even on a Thursday night, every seat in the house was taken.  Ticket prices were reasonable- less than $20 per person.  

First thing to note is that the Bluebird is not located in downtown Nashville.  You will need to either drive or get a cab/Uber/Lyft to get here.  Also, it's in a strip mall, so there aren't many pre- or post-show dinner/drink options.  But none of that matters cause all that matters is the awesome music going on inside.

Inside, I was shocked how small this place was.  But it added to the experience.  On the night we visited, the songwriters were a group of three men and one woman.  Although I had read up on them prior to arriving, I was surprised at the number of songs I knew.  The woman songwriter penned the Lee Ann Womack hit "I hope you dance".  It was cool to hear the people who actually write the songs performing them.

Seats are cramped and you will probably sit at a table with strangers, but it didn't feel claustrophobia.  If you can, get a seat at the bar--- you can see more since you are elevated.  Drink prices seemed pretty standard for Nashville-- there is a per seat minimum (maybe 7 or 8 bucks?).  They also serve food- I would probably eat prior to the show- the food just looked like standard bar food.

This is a must-visit spot in Nashville- make sure to get your reservations ahead of time- and get ready for some great music!
Fun atmosphere!!! Great entertainment!!!!!  Cold beer was very refreshing on a hot summer day!!!!

I've been there twice and today was definitely the last time I'll be coming here. I live in this neighborhood and was so happy to find somewhere that could rival east Nashville brunch spots. Boy was I wrong. Today they were OUT of juice for mimosas. WHAT ?! How are you a brunch destination that runs out of juice? The service there is also horrible. The staff is not friendly and act like they don't care. I work in customer service and I couldn't imagine having that attitude at my place of work We got the breakfast tacos and chicken n waffles. Both were mediocre. We left quickly and had breakfast at another restaurant. 40 bucks wasted. 100% won't go there again.

Stopped in for breakfast,  a very eclectic menu,  but still can get basic eggs. Had scrambled eggs,  awesome breakfast potatoes and bacon.  Husband had cornbeef hash,  and it was real cornbeef, also very good. Jalapeno bacon good and spicy.  Service was very good,  very friendly.  I would recommend!!

If you're a music lover, then The Bluebird Cafe is akin to an abusive relationship. You'll be the one who's apologizing - for what THEY (at least in part) did wrong. So if you're the type to become any kind of loyal customer to what in theory is possibly one of the best places for live acoustic music ever, then don't go here. Or maybe I should say don't "try" to go here. Much like any sort of beloved significant other, it sounds pretty and doesn't look bad either. The amount of talent featured is BEYOND incredible. You get to hear much beautiful music from so many unbelievably amazing (and often VERY successful, even well-known, at that!) songwriters/singers - and in a location where you actually can HEAR it. Unfortunately, it seems and feels very deeply as if any kind of care/regard they have for customer loyalty has all but disappeared over the past several years and replaced with letting absolutely anyone, who may or may not know who it is playing that evening, in. Some random individual who just happens to wander up and so therefore can take the seat of someone who 1) knows of the artists playing and the schedule to the point that they set an alarm JUST so they'd be awake in time to make the 1-minute sellout time reservations 2) drive for approx. 2 hours just for the show, 3) tried to call multiple times so they wouldn't lose their seats but got no answer and 4) had the audacity to be 3 minutes late when the business "policy" is that seats *may* be given up after 15 minutes of a no-show.

If you'd rather read a much shorter review than mine about a somewhat similar experience please read Kelli B's from 8/19/2013. Though she's not quite had the opportunity to be frequent, it seems the treatment is much the same.

*An important aside - several times when policies are officially stated it's said the pew/bench seats are first come/first served. However, the pew/bench seats ARE among those which can be reserved with the system. Umm..?? Sure that never leads to a reserved pew seat being lost.

Maybe being made even more "world famous" (though not really so much in their hometown) is to blame for this obscene mistreatment - but that doesn't make it a fair excuse. It is one reason why I hesitate to even write a bad word in any kind of public forum about them, however; because the likelihood of it affecting their bottom line is pretty non-existent. Nevertheless, what follows is a sampling of my very souring (to understate the situation) experience tonight. So please read below.

We HAD reservations for a show, my boyfriend had even used vacation time at work for it - with such a stellar lineup (I really had been looking forward to it for weeks) we eventually decided on the Bluebird over seeing Kenny Rogers at the Ryman. Well, anyway, even after my YEARS of loyalty (and more recently also putting up with new employees who had never seen me telling me rules I've known for years) when we got there at approximately 9:03 after the drive from Murfreesboro we were told "our" seats had been given up to someone without reservations. I know the Bluebird's supposed 15 minute policy but it hadn't even been 5. AND I had TRIED to call several times with NO answer, to say we were on the way. I miss the days when they would care enough to call the customer themselves just to check. So even with customer loyalty, so-called "reservations," a $4 nonrefundable reservation fee  - which is normally OK if losing the seats is actually at all my own doing - and the drive to and from Nashville I guess just a little bit of wanting to stay in and having a hard time leaving my loving cat has cost all this grief. Obviously, with all the tourists, especially now because of "Nashville," loyal customers who actually go there for the music mean nothing. Yet another situation that pushes me to just entirely give up on caring about music. All that said, I'm sure it's still a perfectly fine place as long as you don't plan to frequent it. Or have to drive any substantial amount of distance to do so. And don't have reservations. Or if you do, aren't a few seconds late. Oh, and hey, if you do get a table (probably one allegedly saved for someone else) or even a bar seat, don't forget there's a $7 food/drink minimum. Have fun and enjoy the music for me.

We went to see the Lewis Copeland Band. My girlfriend and her friend know Lewis from his hometown. We went for the music, but did have some beers while we were there. They have a great selection of beer and serve it in plastic cups. The trailer resort theme is cool and the stage is big enough for the bands. Some of the places on Broadway have tiny stages.

Three stories of hootin' n hollerin' and good times! Take s stroll to the back alley and enter through their neck entrance to avoid the line out front. Lookin' for a good time kinda night? Stay on the first floor and enjoy the live music and the party atmosphere. If you are looking for a bit more fresh air and open space, make a bee line to the top floor and onto the balcony. Live music is also blasting through the upstairs speakers, too.

Great atmosphere.  Bluegrass music added perfect feel for Sunday brunch.  Service fantastic.  Food and drinks pretty good. Had tacos, enchildadas, and both sangrias.  The place to go for weekend brunch.

Let me just start with this...there's a part of me that wants to hate the idea oftrailer parked themed bar in the epicenter of Hillbilly Vegas but the other part of me can't deny the food is VEEEEEE on point. They, surprisingly, have a great veggie burger and are also open late. Great size of food and cheap. Literally what more could you ask for in a chaotic shit show that is downtown Nashville? The wait can be a bit much but grab a drink and listen to a pop country cover of "Don't Stop Believin" a thousand times and you won't even notice.
Blond bartender serving on the rooftop on 8/4 is rude AF. She has no reason to disrespect a group of courteous, paying customers. Won't be returning.

Love this spot!  This is my neighborhood pub, so I usually come here for happy hour or last call.  I think I've only been to like, 2 shows here.  Bigger shows can get crazy packed.  Solid food and a decent beer and whiskey selection.  The burgers are easily as good as ML Rose and you don't have to put up with the aging bros;  just hipsters.  90% of the staff is super cool and I ain't even mad at the one that doesn't like me.  Also, 241 beers on monday is super clutch.

The food was okay, but execution on the cook fell flat. The speed with which I got my food was amazing. Probably indicative of the food all having been precooked. I got a hot chicken sandwich. The heat was good, but the chicken was over cooked. The fried exterior was too crispy that it took away from the bite and the chicken itself was dry. The Texas toast used for the bread of the sandwich was cold. The sandwich would have been better if the Texas toast had been toasted or at least warmed up a bit. The tater tots were overcooked, but otherwise good. 

Overall, the place was fine for food in a pinch. Might have been better if I was drunk and jonesing for a food fix. I'm on the fence about whether or not to come back.

This was a special experience. We had just come into town and we were  told  to go to the Bliebird Cafe ! we tried to make reservations in "the queue ". That was a bust. So we just got in line for the 1 and 45 minute wait. It was ok. We just bonded with everyone!  We were literally the last people in. They had to separate us but it was ok just to get in!  I was so close I felt like part of the band!! 
The gals at the door were very nice and the wait staff was fast!  It ended up being a special experience and one of our favorite places in Nashville !!!!

Love this place! It's great food and service...I love the old Woolworths atmosphere. It was happy hour til 8 on Friday. So cool...definitely recommended by us for sure. Swing bar downstairs is so classic.

I came here for beer and music and Tootsie's most definitely delivered. From what I saw they had 5 different bands playing on every level of the bar. I was amazed. Drunk, but amazed. The upstairs bathroom attendant was the shit and kept calling everyone "sexy sassy". My friend paid 7.00 for a rail gin and tonic with no lime haha but that seems normal in a tourist town.

Some say this is the heart of Nashville, every website, and everyone I talked to told me that this is a must visit. So there was no doubt that this was gonna be the first place we went  out to on our first night in town. Because this place is pretty packed it doesn't seem as big as it really is.  But there are like 3 floors of bars, stages and people singing everywhere. In fact thier even singing on top of the bars. The live music here is the star, its pretty much everywhere. This place is is deff a tourist trap, but not one you will regret. If you can get a table or space to sit at the bar its a good time. Not one of my fav places on broadway but deff set the tone for the weekend.

Went to see the Urban Pioneers and the stage, acoustics and venue were awesome. 

I ordered a brisket horseshoe and got about 70% fat on a piece of white bread covered with fries and some kind of cream sauce. I think the idea was to hide that there was really no meat. It was the most disgusting thing I have ever tried to eat. 

They should really not serve food.

Also how can you charge $16 for what is basically an appetizer? This should have been less than $10. Probably about $2 of food. 

The music was great and the setting was awesome. My suggestion is to eat before you go to the Sutler.

We made a point to stop in here over the weekend, glad we did - very cool place! It was super crowded when we arrived, but following advice from other Yelper's we made our way upstairs. Much less crowded and a great band playing! If I had it to do again I'd go earlier in the day to have a better opportunity to look around and hang out without the crowds.
We are visint from Jacksonville and popped by for a drink, totally affordable and GREAT live music! Happy hour deals are great and will be back in the future!

There's a bouncer at the door checking ID, ensuring that you are 21. Friday & Saturday nights are the most popular and it's wall to wall inside. ....just like walking on the street. 

Seems like the music is pop rock as all the 21 year old girls in the audience know the words and sing along with the band.

The norm is no cover,  and beets are about $5. Male sure you tip the band when they pass their Buckley around!

Always a fun time, and you might actually hear some good music.
My favorite bar in Nashville! Hate to see it have less than 5 stars.

Had a great time here. Their were so many different places to choose from, this one was packed but has 3 floors with 3 different performers. So don't let the crowd in the door steer you way. Go in and go up to one of the other floors. Kayla Woodson was performing she was amazing. Good times!

DO NOT GO TO THIS BAR!!!! I was charged $20,000. Yes, twenty THOUSAND dollars and they will not answer nor do they have an answering machine so there is no way to get in contact with them which is by far the worst management I've ever experienced.  If there were negative stars, they'd get 5.

Wife and I dropped in on Saturday to listen to music and have a couple drinks.  The guy checking IDs was very nice and professional. However, the hostess was the most dismissive and rude person I can remember encountering front of house.  She literally swiped me away with her hand to get to the person behind me.  The drinks were fine, nothing special.  The music, and really the reason we were there, was great.  Although the sound guy in the back had an old plate of food hanging out by him, which was a little nasty.

With so many music venus in town, and many known for world class customer experience, we probably won't be back.  Not bad for a quick visit after dinner at cinema though!
Features great talent! Small bar equals a lot of fun! Bartenders ARE ATTENTIVE (unusual for the crowded traffic but they are good!

Went here with a group of 8 for bunch. Food was heavy but delicious. I enjoyed the chicken and biscuits. Coming from the south, the white gravy did not disappoint. Live music was playing and the service was great. Bottomless mimosas were a hit with the group.

5 stars for entertainment but 2 for food, it's all about the show!! Was very good and it's a small venue so not a lot of people. We waited in line for 3 hours because we didn't have reservations. Definitely worth the wait

I was looking forward to visiting this establishment for quite some time having heard it talked up and advertised on local radio. Unfortunately, I was sorely disappointed. To start, the cheese curds are not cheese curds at all - they are mozzarella balls jazzed up with sauces. The dish itself was perfectly fine, but please don't call them cheese curds. I had the pulled pork sandwich and there was hardly any pork on it at all and the bun was just a regular old bun, nothing fresh or baked in house. The sweet potato fries were limp, cold, and lifeless. The coleslaw was... coleslaw. And I had ordered a side of their mac and cheese. Nothing life changing but just fine. My cocktail was good, but the whole experience was marred by the lackluster food and surly attitude from our waitress who even tried to remove my plate as I was still eating off of it. Honestly, I would save your money and pick up some quality BBQ at better local restaurants. This is for tourists who don't know any better and as a local I would not recommend it.
Didn't do dinner just drinks and for music.   Atmosphere and decor is awesome.  Band the night we were there was awesome!  Recommend!!!!

Looks like a local dive bar. Basic bar food but with a little twist. I had the pizzadilla and it was great. Spicy with the added jalapeños. Craft beer was only $4. Staff was friendly and attentive. Friends had chicken tenders with a honey buffalo sauce and it was great! Def a cool spot to have a beer and quick bite.
Went here for brunch , food was amazing , staff was very friendly . Make your own bloody Mary's . Highly recommend this place .
Pricy drinks, talented bands playing covers of crappy 80s songs and modern country. Was hoping to see some cool original stuff- found out you have to get off Broadway for that!

Met up with friends to enjoy a nice evening. The food was good and the specialty drinks were enjoyable as well.
The fried chicken was good as were the short ribs. The stand out was the BBQ ribs. Service was good. We had reservations and were promptly seated. Afterwards you can go downstairs to enjoy live music and dancing
It would have received 5 stars, buy the dining room is pretty loud for conversation.
All in all, you should give it a try.

$5 cover to get in. It wasn't even packed. -1

Reeks of barf. -1

Bros with tribal tattoos arm wrestling. -1

Dubstep JUST touched down in Nashville. -1

I literally spent less than 3 minutes at the bar. Walked to the back, made a u-turn, and walked right out.
Sat for 15 minutes without even being acknowledged. If you can't handle the amount of people on a Saturday night, hire more servers or train your people.

Very cool classic Nashville bar.  I've been here about 10x because all of my visitors consider this a "must do".  It's always too packed and difficult to get a drink. 
The employees are not very knowledgeable.  One employee checked my friends ID and let him in.  He told the guy he was going to stand by the door because he was waiting for his wife.  While he stood there the bouncer changed his mind and told him that he could no longer go in because his shirt didn't have sleeves.  In 100 degree downtown Nashville.  Nice.  
It's fine if you want to have rules, but don't let someone in and then change your mind. 
It's unfortunate because they always have fabulous performers.

My friends and I were visiting from Washington DC and were hungry and wanted to get some food. We went to Paradise Park at around midnight. However, they were experiencing technical difficulties and so there was a little bit of a wait. As the servers got back online, however, we were accused of cutting by the people behind us. The cashier was incredibly rude and did not even attempt to listen to our side of the story. I understand that there was a lot of stress caused by the technical difficulties and the assumption that we were too intoxicated and tried to cut in line because of our intoxication. 

Our exchange went something like this: 
RUDE PEOPLE BEHIND US: They tried to cut us.
US: We were waiting in line. 
HER: Ya'll need to get to the back of the line, or leave. 
US: We're not trying to be rude, but we have been waiting in line. 
HER: Stop being condescending. You can get to the back of the line, or we can escort you out. 

Legitimately, the only saving grace was the manager. He had a long beard and a tattoo near his eye (I believe it was a star. I think he also had gauges. This is not the other guy with a long beard who was the bouncer and also rude to us). He had seen the entire exchange and knew we had been waiting in line. He got us our order for us and said that he had hoped he rectified the wrongs the cashier had committed. I only wish I had gotten his name, as he was very sincere and genuine and seemed upset that we had such a poor, miserable time at his establishment. THANK YOU MANAGER. You truly were the only bright spot during this experience.

A dive may describe the atmosphere but the food drink and staff were excellent
Music was good for a Wednesday afternoon

I'll never go back to this place.  They're so disorganized they don't have a system in place for their 'first come first serve ' night.  Stood in line in 100 degree weather for an hour and a half and didn't get in.  This after the little punk running the door said he counted and said it was fine.  Guess those people I saw just walk up and be let in took our spots.  Oh..but the 'good news' was we were first in line for the next show....2 hours later!!  Ever thought of utilizing the deli ticket method morons so people will know if they're getting in and don't have to risk heat stroke?

Went shortly after it opened with a large group.  We ordered pretty much all of the sides, and many other items.  The corn was really good, but everything else was pretty much a let down.  Corn fritters, meh.  Cheese curds, not so great. Harissa chicken was a let down.  Also got something that's no longer on the menu---pretty bad, which probably explains why it's not on the menu.  The place has been nicely restored---looks like it's from the 1940's or 50's.  Service was good, but the food just isn't very good.  But a lot of people will say it's great because, well, there is a lot of butter, and salt.
This place is small but so much fun theres this band I'm not sure what they're called but they play all the hip hop hits
This place is a PARTY. I'm a northerner who didn't know what a "honky tonk" was, but this was a great place to learn. Nash Vegas' best.
Just because your closing doesn't mean you don't give a F.   Hard work will get you a good job of you make an effort!

Now I want to give the manager a round of applause because he rectified the situation immediately. I called the manager from my cell phone and he came to our table. He was outstanding and we are so grateful. Now let me tell you why I had to call the manager.

I came with a party of six on a Saturday night. We ordered drinks and food and settled in to enjoy the music. The wings were returned because they lacked flavor. The brisket macaroni and cheese is vinegary. But even with the few food flaws the ultimate flaw was the service.

Our waitress, Karina, took time with all of her tables but ours. She verbally checked in with them but not us. She would stare at our table. We didn't get a refill until the table finished their food. Not one refill and our drinks were all empty. I called the manager to let him know how our table was treated differently. He rectified the error immediately and comped the food for our entire table, apologized, welcomed us to come back, and said he would talk to the waitress. Thank you for fixing it. Thank you for acknowledging that this does happen and it's wrong. Thank you but I can't give any more stars.
Love this bar!!! First time in Nashville and it was awesome, on a Sunday too!!! Bands were AMAZING.

Date night at Woolworth on 5th. This is in the old Woolworth's building downtown where my date used to shop as a kid. It was also the site of the first sit-ins during the Civil Rights movement. There's a faux lunch counter as an ode to the past. The terrazzo floors are impeccably restored. The vibe is Art Deco and the background music Percy Faith.

This is another TomKats creation, so the menu has many a splendored thing. I had the predictable fried chicken with green beans (hint: they also own Loveless.) My date had Southern vegetables: okra, black-eyed peas, mashed potatoes. All in the name of comfort food.

Our server was from Athens, Georgia, and too young to realize our interest in the building (check the period wallpaper in the basement restrooms.) You step outside looking for Corvairs and Oldsmobiles. They have valet but recommend parking at the library (which has an impressive Civil Rights Room no one knows about.)

You'll leave Woolworth full--of food and righteousness.

I've been here for dinner twice and for drinks once. I won't be back. The food was OK at best the first time. The second time, it was even worse.  During dinner, the band is so loud that I wasn't able to have a conversation at all. I love music! I love loud music! But both times I went, it was unbearably loud.

I wanted to love Tootsie's but just couldn't.  It is a three level bar with a stage on all three levels.  It is one of Nashville's famous spots and we were looking forward to enjoying it.  Unfortunately it was just not for me.  It reminded me of a fraternity house and was absolutely filthy from top to bottom.  I would fear ordering anything from their kitchen.  Good looking waitresses with skimpy cut t-shirts and lively music keep the crowds coming in.  You can find space during the afternoon, but come night it is shoulder to shoulder.   If you are looking for a wild time on the strip and don't worry about contact diseases (lol) it may be your place.  The best thing here is the music, but we found many other little honkytonks up and down the strip that were clean and still offered a lively crowd and good music.

This is a pretty serious bar scene.  We couldn't get in on Saturday night but that's not saying much because we couldn't get in anywhere on Saturday night.  This place is right on the main drag and it was packed on a Sunday night.  There are three floors and each has their own bar and band.  The drawback is that it is pretty full of tourists.  But it is pretty cool to be in a place where so much history took place.  I saw one of the tables from this place at the Willie Nelson Museum.  They have a rooftop bar that boasts really nice views of the city.  It was fun but crowded and crazy.

I really enjoyed the music.  You are definitely not going to be attending this place for their food.  They have a very limited menu with nothing impressive.

This place is all about the music, which they do a great job with.

Word of advice on price:  beer is cheap, but a whiskey is $10 and a "double" is $20!  The liquor drinks are crazy expensive, but you are there for the music...

Good luck getting in.

I love this place!  Quintessential hipster hangout.  I definitely love the black velvet Burt Reynolds.  The place reminds me of a cross between the old Iguana and what 12th and Porter used to be like for those "of a certain age" who remember when Jodie Faison ran the best places in town.  Stone Fox has a great beer selection and I'll be back to try out the weekend brunch.

All I have to say is Bluegrass Brunch. Food is delicious, atmosphere is rowdy at 10am. Did I mention they have bottomless mimosas? Great place for brunch if you're looking to let loose on the weekend.

I have also been here for evening cocktails in the cellar a couple of times on the weekends. Very unique atmosphere, nicely designed and laid back. Vastly different from the party upstairs, but in a good way.
Save your money !  Extremely over rated and I have been in the restaurant industry for over 30 consecutive years.

My food was good ( peppered ribs) but the rest of our party did not enjoy the meal. Fried chicken was very dry, pulled pork can found much better around town. 
The atmosphere was very loud, and the acoustics in here allow you to hear everyone's conversation. Definitely not a quiet meal by any sense of the word.
Waitress seemed tired and annoyed right off the start. Not very attentive, nor deserving of the included gratuity.
Drinks were mediocre at best.
Really fun atmosphere! Loved that there were so many different areas of the bar with live music. It can get a bit crowded depending on when you are there- definitely worth checking out though

so fun- definitely a place to go for some fun music and dancing. the "hip hop" side is a nice change of pace for this town! just prepare to be surrounded by a ton of young college kids on the weekends.....
I just ate the best grilled cheese of my life. Also they have live music that is the PERFECT volume. Not too loud not too quiet. Definitely recommend!
Best burgers and homemade hand cut fries on Broadway! More than just burgers on the menu. Fast homemade affordable friendly service! Takeout or dine in!
Lots of bands playing, one on each level and we went on a Sunday! Service was great, we were waited on as soon as we set down and she continued to check on us.

Loved hanging out on the patio and having drinks but 2nd floor bathroom is a bit nutty...the attendant continually barked instructions to those using the bathroom and sprayed huge amounts of glade air freshener into the top "vent" area if she felt people were taking too long (fortunately I just witnessed this vs experiencing it --- guess I was quick enough)! My friends went to the bathroom after and I understand this round the attendant was demanding tips...Get rid of the attendant concept - it's 2017!

Our chicken fingers were served raw. They did make us new ones, but did not offer any concessions on the first. I was pretty disappointed. I would think food safety would be a big concern for them, but they just played it off like this was normal.

The Stone Fox is exactly that. A stone cold fox. Too good to be true!

I've been here a few times now. Haven't sat inside yet, because it appears that we only go to the SF when the weather is perfect!  The first time was mid-day, and we grabbed a beer on the back porch, which was fantastic! I love that there is plenty of seating and that there is a little mini garden growing on the fence. I also love that the beer selection - while fairly limiting - was very satisfying. Great options.

The second time I went here, I enjoyed a nice meal on the front porch.  The waitress was a little all over the place, but she was really nice and the food was great. Boyfriend and I split a burger + a kale salad, and both were more than I was expecting out of bar food. I really wanted to try the fried pickles, but I'll save those for another time.

If you're looking for a great porch, a delicious craft beer, and a fun bar (check out their events - super cool stuff going on here!), this should be your new favorite local pub. I know it's mine!

This is a shining beacon amidst what is otherwise a pretty bleak offering of cool hangouts in West Nashville. Lots of really great beer on tap at totally reasonable prices, and the food is damn tasty. The fish and grits was really fresh and just the right spice level to keep you coming back for more.

While the featuring of local talent is often fun, I do sometimes wish there weren't as many nights requiring cover charges as there are. I got stuck paying a $12 cover on a Thursday night of all nights, when all I really wanted to do was drink some beer. Of course, this was really my own fault. My advice: do your research and check their calendar before you go. 

I continue to be a Stone Fox fan and will be back soon!
Music was awesome! Food was tasty! Drinks were made stong. :-) Waitress was friendly.

Poorly managed line up process that leaves you wondering if they let people continue to line up so they can have a huge line outside. They truly give not one fox about the people standing outside because they are going to fill their club no matter what. 

Another reviewer called them pretentious and that is exactly what they are. Go late if you only want a t-shirt and sit in your car until the line disappears.  Not worth the waiting

We only went to the food side for late night burgers, did not venture into the bar.

After a day of drinking, those burgers really hit the spot! The single-wide is the perfect size (others who ordered the double were complaining it was too much) and everything was fast and fresh and delicious. I'd definitely go again.
Great crowd, music and $5 pitchers. A can't miss if you are in Nashville.

Any spot with a tribute dish to the all-vegetarian spot where my mom waitressed long before I obtained personhood (holla @ The Laughing Man) has a special place in my heart.

More recently, their veggie burger gained a special place in my stomach. The kale salad made a special place for itself in my wallet... not enough flair in that bowl o' leaves to warrant  an eight dollar price tag. The burger is definitely worth its weight in really good veggie burger worth, though.

Less importantly (but most distractingly), their staffcandy has an imaginary special place in my phone (seriously I want half your phone numbers) and the decor has equal hipster-appeal.

In a nutshell: trendy, tasty food, funky fresh interior, good-lookin' people, and a bonus kitschy venue. Bring your friend from Portland, your thick-rimmed glasses, and an appetite for beets and black beans.

We always have a BLAST when we come to Nashville and visit Tootsies! Every time we come in here we find ourselves stuck here until bar close because the atmosphere is so energetic and the music is seriously awesome. We usually make our way up to the 2nd or 3rd floor and stand at the outskirts of the dance floor. It is the best when the bands will play ANY song for $20...seriously they can play anything. We almost lost it completely when they played Sublime. It is always very crowded but it is worth the experience. Tootsies is the best!
Great live entertainment when you walk in and upstairs! Lots of fun and great talent. Best margarita in town :-)

A personal favorite. I LOVE TOOTSIES!! The bands were especially good this week. Got lucky with the weather and sat outside a few time on  the roof deck. This is one of the first and last places I visit when I come to Nashville. Stop by for a good time.

I would go here every night if I could. Made it to a 9pm show on a thursday night. It is great to see such a huge fan base at this place!

I had made a reservation 1 week prior to h
The show. Tickets sold about 5 minutes after they came available, which is crazy. I had never heard of the names of the people performing but after leaving, I will own some of their CDs now!

Cover charge at the door and a $7 minimum inside. It's easy to spend $7 by simply ordering a drink. The oven was broken the night I went, but they still had some food options available too. I wouldn't say it's worth eating here, especially if you are visiting from out of town. Nothing on their menu is worth while. 

The music and performances make this place great. Like I said, I would definitely come again and again.

Fun place during the week-- good place to spot celebs of all genres -if that's your thing. Way packed on the wknd and drinks are pricey but I don't mind paying for a good time once in awhile! And a must go when u have visitors in town!

Soooo disappointing! We went with another couple last night after we heard some good things about it. After all of the hype we were expecting to be blown away by the service and the food...we didn't get either. 2 appetizers, the Brussels sprouts and the pickled shrimp. The shrimp was not bad tasting but over cooked. The sprouts were no better than any local diner. Portions were small and taste was average at best. For all of our entrees, they were crazy expensive for no more food than you get. I had a 4 vegetable plate, each were crazy small bowls and the items were again, nothing special. All of us left extremely disappointed. Not to mention a rude bus staff acted as if we needed to leave as he cleared our dishes. Will Not Be Back!

The Paradise Park Trailer resort is located in the heart of the action in downtown Nashville. With so many venues playing great music, what sets this place apart is it's delicious bar menu. With bar classics like Burgers and Tater Tots, what caught my interest was the Corn Dogs and Fritos Pie!

While described as a Dive Bar, it was one of the cleanest dive bar I've been too. Even with carpeting, there was no stale beer smell.  On stage there was a cover band belting out 90s and Country classics.

Be sure to stop by and check the Mullet Hall of Fame and hit the picture booth!
The food was good! The services wasn't the best by far, and the place was like stepping back in time.

Great place for quiet study while enjoying a nice cup of coffee, EXCEPT Tuesday nights after 7-8:30 PM. They were holding some kind of presentation in the front room and it was EXTREMELY noisy. It seems they'll be holding it every Tuesday nights. 

Note: The presenter said there'll be Food Truck service at The Well at 7PM on June 19th 

The restroom here is only better than the ones in LA's China Town (if you considered it's a restroom and not a house of horror) 

Tips: Working outlets are in the front room. Wear a light sweater because it's always cold inside!


2013/#33

This is the only bar downtown where the tables and walls aren't sticky and old. Very clean, rustic and modern. They have two stages (front and back), and the brands that we saw didn't disappoint either night vs finding a hit or miss band trying to hop around all the other crusty bars. Yes, the other bars are vintage and have character- if it's your first time in Nashville you still should go check them out. However, ending the night at the Tin is probably the best way to go.
Very good food, but my wife saw a kitchen workers leave the restroom without washing her hands, we are never eating there again.

Worst place to go for Sunday Football. Not only is the service very poor, this locations "Green Room" was the only area open, and the staff was unwilling to change any of the channels to display different games. 
The fact that only the Green Room was open was not explained to any of the guests, which had many of them leaving upon arriving. No sign was placed on the entrance to Tin Roof so over 30 different groups tried to open the locked door and left while I was in the facility. 
In regards to the games on the TV and not willing to change channels. It is understandable if that is an established rule but about 10 minutes after we arrived, a different person asked to change a game to another and her request was granted. Needless to say, I was not impressed. I would recommend going to Tin Roof in Lexington/Cincinnati/Louisville before Nashville.

Love this place for Brunch.  Never disappointed.  I can say without a doubt that they make the best Bloody Mary in Nashville.  The back patio is perfect for a weekend morning or early afternoon cocktail to soak up some vitamin D.

We were nicely and very casually greeted by entering the pub with a great atmosphere. Live music was supposed to start a bit later but it was already a pleasant place to hang out. The waiter was kind and interesting and the walls were decorated with the most entertaining and interesting maps, pictures etc. Looks like a place one can easily hang out with friends, go for some live music and drinks.

We came for food as we got the place recommended while visiting town and I was sold by the different Gluten free options. The menu looked interesting and many/most items contained vegetable and herbs from their own garden and many dishes were partially or fully organic while it was still sharply priced. the dishes were not ordinary and from all around the world!

\The place would have received a 5 star review if the food didn't turn out to be that spicy - as if you ask in a Thai restaurant for the entree with the three out of three jalapeno pepper sign. We received some extra rice to cool it down and the waiter was very good about it.

Will certainly come back if we are around and recommend all our friends to come as well!

This place is huge. Great music and atmosphere, nice patio for enjoying the view of Broadway. Music and bars inside everywhere you turn. If you don't like the music inside, go onto the patio and enjoy the music that's outside.

I loved it... thanks to my hosts...I was able to book seats.... 7 venue..... the artists were so down to earth and made funny remarks / conversations an awesome form tof entertainment.  I felt the same vibes as well did watching Nashville ...and grateful thankfull for the chance to experience.  The waitresses were awesome.  The food amazing, though I realised that outlr sweet potato fries may have been slightly burnt comparing them to the lady next door.  Still loved the place,  look forward to some day visiting again.  Thank

One word: overcrowded!
I get this is a tourist stop but it is quite small indoors to house as many people who enter the building. Music is good, atmosphere geared toward younger crowd. Good place to stop if you're passing through
Nice venue.  I didn't realize there were stages on multiple floors.  Don't just stop at the door there is plenty of space upstairs and multiple bars as well.

This place is decent. Indeed, will return to explore the inside seating area that appears to be recently renovated.  The breakfast food includes a variety of options with plenty of ways to mix up your order do that you can try new things.  I am a northerner so after moving to the south I had to try lots of different preparations of biscuits and gravy and grits.  Therefore I feel qualified at this point to evaluate these dishes.  B and g were good but needed to be warmed up a little. Cheesy grits needed more cheese and pepper.  Omelet was overdone according to my partner; however I did not try it and he's really picky.  I will come again.

The outside patio was so slippery, ® cause of one little puddle. No sign to say it was slippery at all. The bartender and the bouncer were just on their phones doing nothing last night. I totally fell into a chair and hit my head HARD. Told them that they should clean it up, or put a sign. Again they sat and did nothing about it. Very disappointed in the service there. It was a great place, until they handed me a rag to clean it up for them....like excuse me....Maybe get off your butt and Facebook , and do it your self. Grab a mop. All they had to do was push it into the drain.

Så otrendig så det är super trendigt! Avskalat inredning med lite medvetna sunk vibbar är dekoren här. LP skivomslag från 70-tals pop töntar som Captain & Tennille och Eddie Rabbit pryder baren. Enkla bord och stolar à là amerikansk köksstandard utgör möblemanget här. De verkar ha glimten i ögat här och vet förmodligen att klientelet kommer hit inte för att titta på tjusig, genomtänkt inredning utan de kommer hellre för musikunderhållningen eller bara för att umgås med andra här. Kvällen jag själv besökte var för Jonathan Richman på den lilla scenen. Härligt trång konsertlokal med något hundratal besökare som bara njöt av musiken och showen här. Bra, trevlig och behjälplig service.

I am currently at the Bobby Jones Gospel show and this event was very misleading from the advertisement.  The tickets that my family & I purchased advertised the show from 1-3pm.  I traveled to meet family from Kentucky and be here by 12:45pm. Only to be told that the doors open at 1pm and show starts at 2pm.

Then once seated in the New Era Ballroom I Ordered the 2 pigs small bites only to be told by the bartender that she didn't know if any of the small bites were available.  She later brought me the small entree and it was ice cold.    Who in their right mind would eat ice cold pulled pork and ice cold corn bread?  

I am very disappointed in the overall service of the restaurant and also the food selection.  What a disappointment to an overly hyped up new restaurant in Nashville.

Go if you can get tickets! I was extremely elated to score tickets to a show. This glorious cafe is a must visit landmark.The club is famous (also featured on the hit show "Nashville") for intimate, acoustic music performed by some established ..some upcoming singers & songwriters... so you might be witnessing/hearing songs here for the first time before they go-on to land their record deal and become famous (Taylor Swift was discovered here).

The singers sing to a small audience (seats about 100 people) The Bluebird has two shows a night, dinner is available at both shows ..Monday nights are Open Mic...

Artists in the songwriters circle who performed that  night were Scot Sax, grammy winning songwriter his songs performed by Faith Hill and Tim McGraw... his wife, Susie Brown and Korby Lenker (who was my favorite... his songs my little life and forbidden fruit... OMG outstanding! ) and a newbie Anthony De Costa.

There is a cover charge of $10 per person for food and drinks... they have a great menu and desserts too.

It was one of the greatest experiences of my life!

Dive bars are important.  They provide a crucial role in the bar scene and can be among the best to hang out in.  This is not that.  The drinks are ok.  The band they had at the time was lousy and spent more time doing sound checks than Aerosmith does and the sound was still bad.  Only redeeming quality was the rocking chairs which were kinda cool.  Meh is a good work to use for this place.

On our trip to Nashville, every one kept telling us "you have to go to Tootsie's," and now I understand why. They had, by far, the best band we saw at any bar on Broadway that week. The bar was packed, but the bartenders were very quick and, like everyone else we encountered, incredibly friendly. The drinks were reasonably priced, the crowd was great, and we had a blast dancing the night away! I would come back to Nashville just to go here again!

This is a really fun bar that has live music all the time.  We sat in here for hours drinking cheap pitchers of local beer. I don't remember the bands, but it was mostly well done covers.  This bar is on my list for the return trip to Nashville.

The on-line purchasing tickets is an F. I was in line through Google, and when  it was my turn it came up a BLANK screen. Then I logged in using Internet Explorer, got in, but when it went to the purchase screen it went to a blank screen, then said it was sold out even after I had selected my tickets.
Such a failed system. :(

I met some friends here to celebrate a friend's birthday, and I just was not wow-ed by the experience. We went on Sunday for brunch, so the place was packed. Despite two people in our group arriving early, they would not let us take a table until the entire party was present. As a result, even once we were all there we still ended up waiting close to 40 minutes before we could sit down. 

The drinks here are really good! I would highly recommend the strawberry lemonade sangria. It is a nice, refreshing, summer drink and they are not shy with the alcohol. Just a heads up, it can take awhile to get your drink. I think I waited about 10-15 minutes for both rounds of sangria that I ordered. 

For my meal, I ordered the Andouille hash, which comes with potatoes, Andouille sausage, peppers, onions, two fried eggs on top, and a spicy hollandaise sauce. They were a little skimpy with the sausage; I only had about 5 or 6 pieces of sausage in my meal, which was irritating since it was supposed to be the star of the dish. The so-called spicy hollandaise sauce was also not spicy at all. The portion itself was also pretty small. For $12 I expected more. 

I would be curious to try The Sutler again for lunch or dinner, and I could definitely see coming back here for drinks. They earned 3 stars for having good drinks, a fun atmosphere, and live music, but lost points for small portions, less than stellar food, and mediocre service.

Definitely a fun bar! We came here because it was so well-known, and for good reason. They consistently have three excellent bands playing at three different sections of the bar, and the place gets so busy, but the crowd is a blast! Glad to have had the chance to check it out.

HORRIBLE MANAGEMENT!!! If I could give them a 0 star I would. Waited in line in the sweltering weather of 95 degrees with many other fine people, patiently for over an hr. To be told several times by security that we would be getting in, the line ended after us. All the while watching people coming in, being told that they were at capacity, turning people away, and watching grown women with their teenage daughters manipulating the musicians to let them get in early with them, even though they were NOT REALLY WITH THEM!! The security and management team let this happen even though, there were many of us that did NOT get in who communicated to them what had happened. They did NOTHING... they said we could go in and buy merchandise, take a few pictures, but not stay!! 
If they would have told us, we would not be getting in, we would have left instead of waiting. I would NOT support this venue for ANY occasion!! The management is horrible! Did not even offer to compensate or make things right for the 26 people they miscounted that should have been able to get into the venue!

My review is based on the band I saw here. SO GOOD!! They did rock covers with a female singer. Her voice was AMAZING. We went here towards the end of our night...before we arrived I was getting ready to go home, but just had to stay to hear her sing. It was on the second floor. It was pretty crowded but there was enough space to keep a bit of space between you and the next stranger. Unfortunately, I searched online and could not find the name of the band. I would definitely come here again if in town hoping I would see this band again!

First trip to Nashville ... So of course we had to check this place out.

This place packed 'em in like sardines. Way too crowded for my liking. Nothing was open up front, so we ended up going to the back upstairs. We liked the music in back much better as well. The gal on the fiddle was absolutely killing it. Very crowded bar but the bartenders did the best they could.

Had a few rounds but soon left after that to check out more of the Nashville scene.
Drawn by the music as we were walking on Broadway. This is a big venue and not too crowded inside. Service was friendly and band was playing mainstream music.

I only gave three stars since we didn't eat here.  We came to see The Band Oklahoma and had cocktails.  Our waitress was excellent.  She was also very knowledgeable in the beer selection.  What I really enjoyed was the sound.  Usually these places are so loud with bands however the acoustics here are great.  It was a really good atmosphere.  Can't wait to go back.

Here with a couple of girlfriends, a place I would never have chosen but glad they did, I just liked it the minute I walked in, an upscale saloon with a stage at one end.  The food surprised me, we shared plates and it was all good - hot livers and gizzards on white bread, sprout hash and a shrimp dish, enough.  The cocktails were tasty.  The mood relaxed.  I felt the waitress was a little over friendly, honestly I am just not that interested in listening to them witter on about themselves especially when there is food to be eaten but that's just intolerant ole me.  I really enjoyed my experience here.  We hit the bar downstairs afterwards for another cocktail.  It is large with sofas and more of a loungy feel.   They think it is speakeasy but seriously the music is so loud that is is anything but that.  There were very few people down there and after asking for it to be turned down we were finally driven out - just the totally wrong style of music for 8.00pm .  Price point was very affordable for upstairs and downstairs.  All in all a really nice surprise.

First time at a "dive bar" and loved it
Super casual and very fast service, the lady that greeted us at the cash was very friendly and the man at the pickup counter was also very nice. If you want some inexpensive messy food try the chilli cheese tots!

We were down in Nashville this past week and stopped at Tin Roof for lunch our first day. We went back every day after that. The bartenders were outstanding especially Ryan, JT, Josh, Ward, and Alex. I would highly recommend checking the place out. Drinks were awesome and so was the food for reasonable prices.

A dive bar, in a bad way. Pretty junky. We popped over here from Robert's and were nothing but disappointed. Pretty empty, but the bartenders were disinterested and difficult to get their attention. Music was on the low end for a downtown Broadway bar. The vibe tries to be cheeky but the place is so trashed that it ends up feeling actually dirty and not just pretend dirty.

Tried out Stone Fox on a Saturday for brunch. We enjoyed every aspect of the experience: the comfortable patio seating, the friendly server, my amazing dish called the King Rabbit (vegan), my husband's French toast, and the coffee with whiskey drink. Cool place. Will definitely return!
Biscuits were dry and hard, chicken was tasteless, don't get brisket hash and service was subpar. Not worth the money.
Really enjoyed our time here - great music and reasonably priced drinks. The band on the first floor was by far the best (I'm sure that is by design to attract the street crowd).

My wife and I went here on our date night and was not disappointed.  The fried chicken entree reminded me of Sunday afternoon meals after church.  The food was excellent.  The atmosphere was very relaxing.  They have done a great job with the place.  The service could have been better as it took our server a while to check on us after we got our meal.  It might not be the Woolworths you might remember shopping in back in the day but it is a very good choice today for a nice, relaxing meal.

Amazing! They were recording nashville song writers while we were there and they did not disappoint! Highly recommend anyone visiting but make reservations FAR in advance or you will be waiting outside. ..

This was one of the only bars I visited more than once during my trip to Nashville. The upstairs bar had an awesome rooftop patio that was fun to hang out on and catch fresh air. Definitely was a tourist bar.

Atmosphere: The back patio is a great spot to share dinner.  The smell from the smoker and all the trees is great! The only downside is the few mice my friend and I saw scurrying across the ground to get under the house. I'm assuming this kinda comes with the territory with it being in an older area of town. However, I will say its something that really needs to be taken care of.
Drinks: I had The Kate- which was excellent! Extremely refreshing! 
My friend had the White Sangria which was ok but we both liked The Kate better. 
Food: We shared the Stone Fox Cheeseburger with the Marrakesh Express salad and the Meat N Three with the Smoked chicken with Cajun Mac and Cheese. The Cheeseburger was awesome. The meat was fresh and the bun perfect! The Smoker chicken was not at all what I expected. I got well cooked chicken that was unfortunately drowning in some sort of Tabasco based marinade. It in no way had a smoke flavor- all I tasted was vinegar. They should call it spicy chicken not smoked. The Marrakesh Express salad could have been great but the kale was too raw- I would suggest cooking it slightly so it's not so hard to eat. I think it would actually taste better warm. 
Dessert: Coconut tres leches was absolutely wonderful. Would have loved the coconut toasted a little on top but not necessary. 
Service: Good. Not overly pushy but could have been a tad more attentive. 
Overall I'd go back- but maybe sit inside this time :/
Great bar with 3 floors and different bands. Very touristy inside with all age groups and mostly from what i heard rock cover music. It was a good time and fun place to drink and hang out.
Visited this place over the weekend. It was so nice and I loved the rooftop and live music.

Such a fun place! I came here as my first honkytonk experience and it did not disappoint! I saw two bands play and both were incredible. They play for tips so they were taking a lot of requests, but in general I liked all the songs they played. We didn't have to wait in line too long, but the place gets really packed inside. Try to grab a seat just to carve out some space for yourself.

I came with my girlfriends for drinks and a small bite to eat. We came during happy hour on a Wednesday evening so it was half off their signature cocktails, wine and I think draft beer. We got the cocktails and they weren't too bad for just $5 (happy hour price). I got the "don't ask rye" and the "Amarillo by morning". 

Don't ask rye - bulleit rye, peach, sour, red wine. It was surprisingly good. It wasn't too sweet, which is what I feared at first bc of the peach. 

Amarillo by morning - tequila, jalapeño-cilantro syrup, lime, smoked salt. I was told this was going to have a spicy kick, but I didn't taste any spice. I tasted more tequila than anything, which isn't always a bad thing, but I was looking forward to the jalapeño-cilantro syrup taste. 

We ended up eating elsewhere for dinner, but we ordered and shared an app while having drinks. We got the guacamole trio which tasted amazing. There was a classic guac, lump crab guac, and mango habanero guac. Each one had its own unique taste. The chips served with it were warm and crispy. I will definitely get this again. 

The menu looked good, but we just weren't in the mood for it. We mainly went there for happy hour. I'll go back for sure for an entree. I had my eyes on the different types of Mac n cheese. 

Staff were all friendly. The host greeted me with a big smile. Atmosphere was chill. They were getting ready to record something or someone on stage so there was some business going on around us, but it didn't bother us much. We didn't get to make it to the cellar, but that's on my to do list for next time.

What's not to love about this Restaurant?  The atmosphere is spectacular. I have had breakfast lunch and dinner and all meals were superb. I had healthy options like quinoa and unhealthy options  like fried chicken and they were all amazing.  Woolworths is located in the Downtown area right next to Pucketts on 5th.   If you are coming at night, you can valet for a small fee.  I just prefer to Uber or Lyft because their cocktails are too refreshing to have just one.  There are other parking options available during the day like street parking. But, like every popular city, parking can be tricky, so have a plan and leave your frustration s at the door. Woolworths should be experienced by every local and tourist in Nashville.

One of the many Honky Tonks you'll find on Broadway!  If you are in Nashville, Honky Tonks is a MUST visit and Tootsie's does not disappoint.

There is multiple floors...we mostly stayed on the 1st floor.

The music was great and the bartenders were very fast with service, despite the crowd!  

If you are up for it, try the Apple Pie Shine!  It is surprisingly DELICIOUS!!!

The venue/restaurant was nice, but I just didn't prefer the menu. Again, the food wasn't my personal preference but we still had an amazing time and the environment was pretty awesome. 

I especially love when you're walking downstairs to the bathroom and the top of the stairwell wall is covered with the bottoms of boots. Hundreds of them. 

Not to mention this place is gigantic. There's also a pool hall underground as well. According to my Lyft driver this place has a historic background, but unfortunately I can't recall exactly what it was. 

Definitely a spot to visit if you're in town for a few days.
Fun, did not kill you in the price of beer, and service was great.  Bands were very very good!
Tootsies is always a great time. This is the first time I've come on a weekday and you can definitely move around a lot better. They didn't skimp on the talent being slow, the band is fantastic.

I wanted Tootsies to be more, but found less is alright.  Been here a couple of times and have found it mildly entertaining.  A lot of urban "country boys" high on themselves, but need a mirror.  Next time Tootsies, when obnoxious, fat, New York asshats want to dominate the front entrance area and throw their life savings into the musicians tip jar for requests, stop them.  So many walked out because most of us cane to hear the budding artist do a set, not read from an iphone.

We went for brunch with a large group so we had to wait awhile. Luckily we snagged the waiting seats on the porch. However, since we waited so long many of us ordered the chicken and waffles, but they only had 3 left! I was confused how they only had 3 left when couldn't they just make more batter? However, I was one of the lucky 3 and the chicken and waffles was great. It would have been better if it was warmer though. Tiny tiny mimosas and bloody marys though for $6. It was almost great.

Super divey bar and pretty expensive. The music wasn't anything to write home about- although to be fair it was a Sunday night. Gets really packed with a fairly eclectic crowd- bachelorette parties to 70 year olds. All in all good to say you've been but not worth it to stay the night.

We came though Nashville and had a hard time finding a place available with seating.  We happened to come across The Sutler and was so glad we did.  The service was quick and the food was fantastic.  I'd highly recommend the chicken and waffles. Not too oily and the waffles were exceptionally fluffy.  If you get a chance. Stop on in!
You can't bring a backpack in. Purses and shopping bags are apparently fine. Feel free to buy a large purse and put your backpack in, because that's acceptable for some reason.

Full disclosure- I'm one of those people who only found out about the Bluebird Cafe through the TV show "Nashville," which has directly contributed to its skyrocketing in popularity. The history of this venue is remarkable. Countless famous artists played here when they were still unknowns, hoping to get discovered and signed by a record label. It's also common for prominent musicians to drop by and perform here, sometimes unannounced. In short, the Bluebird Café is LEGENDARY. 

Getting seats requires a bit of strategy and teamwork. Reservations are available Monday of the week of the show  at 8 AM sharp. They're very limited, and they go FAST. My friends and I employed a divide and conquer approach, hoping to maximize our chances. Only 1 in 4 of us got through. 

The website was impossibly slooooooooow . One guy was basically out within the first minute- his browser crashed. One girl decided to refresh the page because she wasn't seeing any progress. Never, ever refresh! It was down to me and one last guy, and alas, my wifi wasn't fast enough. The show was sold out within 7 minutes. 

There's a $2 online reservation fee, and a $7 minumum to spend on food/drink per seat. Some shows have a cover charge, but many are free. Don't give up if you didn't snag a seat. They hold a number of spots that are first-come-first-serve, so you can wait in line before each show  for those. 

I assure you, the effort is entirely worth it. This was one of the coolest things I've ever been blessed to experience, and I DON'T EVEN LIKE COUNTRY MUSIC (does Taylor Swift count? JK, don't hurt me). You don't have to be a fan of country music to appreciate the pure, unadulterated magic and raw talent at the Bluebird. We had the pleasure of enjoying a beautiful set from four writers, who have not only penned hits for recording artists, but are also gifted musicians who sing, compose, and play instruments. I felt so inferior in the best way possible. 

The café is cozy and intimate, with the artists in the middle and the audience circled around them. You're  here for the music, not the food, so I won't dwell on that. Their music overflows with passion and bleeds love. One of the songs was so real that it moved me to tears. They performed lively songs too, and had the crowd roaring with cheers. They just completely shut it down. 

We met the artists after the show and got pictures and autographed CDs. Carly Pearce, in particular, went above and beyond my expectations. I complimented her on one of her songs that wasn't on her EP, and she said she would email it to me. I scribbled my address on a crinkled receipt, not anticipating to ever hear from her again. Next AM, I checked my email and there it was- a sweet note from Carly and the song that touched my heart. I definitely have a newfound appreciation for country music.

As a history buff, I was probably going to like this place no matter what! I'm really happy that it didn't disappoint. My friends and I made reservations and were seated withing 5 minutes of our arrival. Parking is difficult because it's smacked dab downtown so expect to pay for parking. There was a Premier Parking lot nearby, not sure how much it costs as we had parking passes already. 

We went for dinner before a show at TPAC and were in a time crunch to make it to the show by 6:30 PM. Our reservations were at 5:00 PM and we had plenty of time to order food and drinks, consider dessert, and walk to the nearby theater for Wicked. Our service was pretty good considering our tie crunch.

I ordered the Fried Flounder and it was delicious. The tomato gravy came on the side and let me tell you, you need it! It ties the entire dish together! The grits are pretty bland without it but the collard greens were fantastic and the fish was fried perfectly. Because they serve complimentary biscuits and cornbread, it was plenty of food to fill me up.

As for cocktails, I had the Johnny Smokehouse and it is SPICY so consider yourself warned. It's alright if you like walking on the wild side, but it's not for the faint of heart. The Serrano pepper is so spicy and there's a sweet balance but when I go next time, I'll definitely try something else.

My friends ordered the fried chicken, pan-roasted bone-in chicken breast, and roasted poblano pepper respectfully. One of them loved the fried chicken and said the sides were delicious. The pan-roasted bone in chicken breast was described as pretty good and really light if you don't want something too heavy. One of my friends is a vegetarian and wasn't wowed by the poblano pepper, adn ended up ordered a side of mac and cheese that she said was great.

All in all, I'll definitely be going to Woolworth's again! I'm excited to try brunch! :)

This is what you need. Paradise Park is where you go when you've been drinking on lower broad all night and you need a sobering pick me up before the trek home. You can be as loud as you want and you will see fairly odd things Depending on the time of night you're there, but trust me you need this in your downtown adventure handbook. Myself and some friends stumbled upon the restaurant side of this place a few years ago and decided to give it a shot. It's been a part of our Nashville eateries ever since. The burgers there are fantastic! Not the best in the whole city, but way better than your average burger place. Always fresh tasting, always hot, and great tater tots to go with it. I don't want you to go here expecting to be blown away because you won't and honestly I don't even think that's the purpose of this place, but it's a very Nashville dive, and for that I thank them!

Perhaps this is a better place to visit at night, but I was not impressed with Paradise Park. The place was dead, even on a Saturday, and the atmosphere was dull. My sandwich was very sub-par, and though the sweet potato fries were good, they weren't anything I couldn't have fried up on my own. Not a terrible place if you're looking for a quick and relatively cheap bite, but definitely not one of the more prime locations in the heart of Nashville.

Bluebird cafe was such a fun experience; however you definitely need to know a couple things in advanced to make sure you get in.  We went during a writers night.  We had to drop someone off at the airport around 5pm.  We assumed this would be enough time to drop her off and then go wait on line for the 6pm show at the bluebird cafe.  When we got there, we couldn't find parking in their lot so we parked in the next lot over, no big deal.  We got online around 5:30pm assuming it was for the 6pm show...it wasn't...we apparently were online for the 8pm show.  It was unbelievable.  Luckily we had the coolest people in front of us and we chatted throughout the whole two hours.  Once the line started moving to get inside, we barely had seats (Yes, 2.5 hour wait and barely were able to get inside). Luckily, we got the last couple ones...We couldn't see very well because had some bars in front of us obstructing our view..it was really cool to listen to though.  The day we went, they had a $7 minimum food/beverage fee and no fee to get inside.  They have traditional bar food/drinks.  It was very good!  I think the whole experience was a lot of fun!  We saw a lot of people who were very good trying to make it in the music business.  We even were lucky enough at the end to see one of the writers who wrote songs for Blake Shelton and Tim McGraw.  It was such a great experience and I would love to do it again soon!

I thought it was nice that the people who didn't get in were able to come inside for a couple minutes, listen to some of the music and snap a picture.  They did for that the people who couldn't get in but were in line!  It was nice of them to do!  Keep in mind, this place is really small so it doesn't fit a lot of people! 

My advice to you is to get there really early, way earlier than you think, but definitely squeeze this in when in Nashville!

I loved the vibe here! The prominent counter contrasted the huge screen.
And I loved their Brussels sprouts!

Great music, good prices for drinks, apple pie moonshine was amazing. Definitely gets tight in there when its busy but it was a great little bar! Loved the pictures on the walls.

(This post is about a year old. Thought it posted...guess not)

Tootsie's Patio is the place to be during the summer if you're looking to be on Broadway while the sun's shining. The food isn't anything to write home about but the drinks are affordable, the music's always good and the stairs are a good test of how sober you are. 

Everyone knows Tootsies and you can't go wrong here.

Nestled among a number of chain establishments, The Well filled a long needed gap in the Green Hills neighborhood when it converted a former fast-food restaurant into a cozy, inviting local coffeehouse in 2012. Surrounded by margin-focused for-profit businesses down the street at the mall, The Well goes against the grain by operating as a non-profit that gives away any money they make. Not only can you help others through buying a cup of coffee at The Well, but you can also find help here. "The Wishing Well" is a place for people to write down needs or requests they may have - from car troubles to simply asking for a prayer - and for others to respond to those requests. 

Oh, and I almost forget to mention - the coffee and tea selections are solid and there's even a drive-thru!

Tootsie's Orchid Lounge is a Nashville bar with lots of fun for anyone who walks in the door. I hung out at an UYE during Spring Break and had a great time. The lowest level has a cool stage with a bar area that wraps around all sides! There was also some construction going on with the 2nd and 3rd floors. Thanks to an awesome Nashville Yelper (Mike G.), a group of visiting Yelpers got to the hang out on the top level of Tootie's even though the place was jam packed! The best parts of this place include the great bands they have playing on each floor (their was a country band on the lower level and a rock band on the top floor during my visit), great frozen drinks (the Piña colada is awesome!), and a rooftop balcony with breathtaking views of downtown Nashville and Broadway Street.

Food was good. But I liked the service more. The overall ambience was casual and lively with the love music. And you really can't beat the bottomless mimosas, lol. I had chicken and waffles and I liked they added curry powder in the dish. It made the dish different than what I used to have. And not too much or it would have overpowered the whole dish.

Awesome service, great food! The sweet potato hummus appetizers were amazing and the recommended Brussels sprouts with mash potatoes were a good balance. I like the fact that their shrimp is from the Gulf and they gave a good amount in the shrimp and grits.

We saw Old Crow Medicine Show here recently and had an amazing evening. It sprinkled, but resulted in a double rainbow over the woods - well worth getting slightly damp. The beer lines were long but there were plenty of purveyors wandering around on foot to make up the difference. Give yourself extra time to get in and out - one lane road.

Definitely one of the highlights of our Nashville trip. We saw Mystery Trip, a Beatles tribute. Their in the round format was very cool . It made for a very intimate setting. It was like you were sitting with the band. We reserved our seats, which I highly recommend. The staff was very friendly. Would definitely go back next time I visit Nashville.

Freakin awesome lil bar on broadway.  Music was alright... service at the bar was legit with cash in hand.  
Someone next to me ordered a Grateful Dead... 90's baby?  lol probably but better than an LIT.  Bartender was quick n knew how to make it, then boom!  My beer!  
Awesome job!  Place is a bit dirty, especially in the rest room but, besides that... awesome!

This dive bar was one of the best memories of my trip to Nashville! It was early afternoon. Not crowded at all, dinghy, my feet were sticking to the floor. I wouldn't want to go to the restroom there :/ but the music was good, the company great, the other bar patrons were fun and we interacted with multiple other groups. The redneck wall with the boat scene is awesome, took a super cheesy pic in front of it!
A couple of my friends went back late night and had some late night snacks and said it was pretty good. 
All in all, a must do when you are in Nashville!
This place has a great atmosphere if you plan on being there ALL day or night. The food is great but plan on it taking longer than an hour for you to get your food. The wait is absolutely ridiculous.

First time at The Sutler. Ordered the okra and fried pickles and the smoked wings. Might have been in the top 3 best wings I've ever had. Smoked then deep fried to get  crispy crunchy. Great with their homemade ranch. Excellent 90s rock band on tuesdays made up of musicians from several prominent country artists band's.  Highly recommend!

I've lived here in Nashville my whole life, born & raised. I can't begin to explain how saddened I am that this bar is a "staple" of Nashville. It's painful to even give it 1 star. 

My fiancé & I stopped into Tootsies only to have a drink & watch my friend sing. We aren't ones to get crazy at a bar. My fiancé was patiently waiting for me outside of the restroom before being pulled down the stairs & out of the bar... for no reason at all. The bouncer just didn't want him standing there I guess. I didn't even have time to wash my hands before I heard the commotion. Next thing I know 3 bouncers are pushing him out of the door. As I stand there & watch them then push him to the ground, I get angry. I ask them what were they thinking...and then I get pushed to the ground. Obviously my fiancé lost his cool over this, which made one of the bouncers mad... who then had to be held back by his fellow bouncer friends because he was threatening to fight my fiancé. 

I realize this is a bar, a lot of crazy things happen... But if you intend on being a "bouncer/security guard" you should be trained to keep your cool & treat people like human beings. You & your power trip are pathetic. I also realize that not every bouncer is this way... I apologize if this offends anyone. 

I've read several reviews & every single bad review is about the horrible staff. There have also been several lawsuits due to the mistreatment of customers. This place is a disgrace to Nashville.

What a cool place!
they have successfully reincarnated the Nashville classic "the sutler" the food and drinks are very creative and delicious!
You can see a live band, enjoy a craft cocktail and eat yummy southern inspired chef driven food.
The lamb ribs are amazing and the jalapeño popcorn is very cool!
Fired pickles and green tomatoes wow!
