Got early access to this throw back to a bit of Nashville history.  I'm a beer guy and the selection on draft and bottled was really well rounded, good local options too.  Everything we tried was really good. Get the Fried Pickles (the fried lemon slices are the best!).  Elevated southern food done really well; collards, mac n cheese, mashed potatoes.

If you like good old country but tired of the tourist trap that downtown check this out, love music and not too loud so you can still have a conversation.
Awesome joint in west Nashville. This one has a nice selection of cocktails... And the food is pretty choice. I like the veggie melt and the veggie burger. The items that have meant are great too.

Stopped in here during an evening on Broadway! We were nearby at the Honky Tonk Bar after an evening of traveling. The burgers were delicious! There were many variations of burger, sandwiches, salads and more. I opted for the Singlewide Cheeseburger with all the toppings, and added their fresh cut fries. For a quick burger joint we enjoyed our experience and would definitely go back.

Went in January was only packed downstairs, go upstairs there is another live band! 

Diverse crowd of all ages and I got to travel back I time to my college years with the divey decor, plastic cups and bottles bus or miller beers. 

The fiddler playing on our way out made this bar stop worth it plus now I can say I went to Tootsies!

Okay, I'll be honest. I love this place. The environment is fantastic because it is cozy and inviting. The coffee is wonderful as well. There are so many great brews and you can't go wrong no matter what you decide to order. 

However, the reason I only rated this place 2/5 is because:

1) This place is ALWAYS packed. If you want to just grab a cup of coffee and sit down for a while, good luck. There is never a place to sit down. This place is always crawling with people and, I mean, that's great but there is just never a place to actually take a seat and enjoy your coffee or get work done. 

2) Maybe it's because this place is located in Green Hills, but parents seem to think it is acceptable to drop their tween children off at a coffee shop to get caffeine high. This place is not just crawling with any type of people. It's crawling with tweens who are loud and slightly obnoxious. 

3) The line to get coffee and order is insanely long and you have to wait a long time to get your coffee. 

4) If you're not a coffee aficionado, good luck with the menu. Great brews but insanely confusing menu. 

5) The coffee is EXPENSIVE. I get why, your purchase is going towards a great cause, but still. just a heads up. 

Anyway, I would've loved this place had it not been for the above mentioned reasons.

I loved the (physical) atmosphere and think this would be a great place to see a show.  That being said...

The staff has perfected the toocoolforschool vibe.  From hostess to our waitress to various food servers, there was a distinct chilly vibe.  Whatever.

The beer list is subpar, though we've discovered that is par for the course in Nashville.  After suffering through a local IPA, I ordered a Bulleit and diet, only to be served a Coke and Bulleit.  I can deal with that, as I shouldn't be mixing rye whiskey with anything, but still...

The menu is interesting.  I ordered the GA White Shrimp and it was a prime example of presentation trumping taste.  It looked beautiful, but sadly, didn't taste as good as it looked.  It was significantly over salted (and I LOVE salt).  The carrots were primarily a PITA garnish and the corncake quite dense.  The shrimp were smallish and just ok.  

My husband ordered the brisket and only ate about 1/4 of his meal.  The saving grace to the experience was the brussle sprouts (I know, right?!!).  No, really.  They are served in a cast iron pan atop fluffy whipped potatoes and topped with friend onions.  Awesome.  I'd have been quite hungry after dinner if it weren't for them.

Bottom line:  if there's music you want to see, check it out.  If not, I'd skip it.

NASHVILLE,TN-Love this place...the rooftop patio gives you the best view of downtown Nashville. It backs up to Grand Ole Opry and overlooks the "Batman" building. I have to go back so I drink on the patio...counting the days!

Terrible service.  Sat ourselves a little after 10pm, waited 10 minutes, no server.  Went to bar to order drinks thinking maybe we had to order food through the bar, they said a server will come to the table.  Server made direct eye contact with me while she was chatting with her friends.  Server checked on every table next to us but never came to our table - I was starting to think her incompetence as a server was intentional.  We had to ask for our own menus.  Laziest staff and worst service ever.  We got up and left after 30 minutes of no attention - incredibly disappointing since they weren't even busy!! She has short blonde hair and is shorter stature.

I've been to Tootsie's a few times but I've managed to do it with the worst timing. Literally every time I've stepped in there it's been in between sets and musicians are either wrapping up or just unpacking, which means that I've held off on reviewing it until now. 

Unfortunately, my last visit was the same situation a band was literally wrapping up but it was still crowded from the Bridgestone crowd. What we did was do a couple of apple pie shots, waited for one of the ladies to head upstream to the bathroom and we decided to text her to let her know we'd be going down the street. A crowded spot, clearly popular with everyone but I've yet to hear anyone play here.

great location, nice seating outside.  However, I was finished with my sandwich 20 min. before my two guests were served theirs, then the server forgot one of their side salads...and for 3 sandwiches, one hummus appetizer, it was $65, incl. a 20% tip!  I should have expressed that this was a rip off to the server, but decided to just leave.  Afterthoughts, I did not help that restaurant get "better" by not telling them, so here it is.  Hope they get more efficient with serving sandwiches to 3 people at once.
I really like this place--but more than anything the mission it has! They have good variety of coffee, I'm not too crazy about the smoothies or the sandwiches but the coffee is on point!

At 8:00p.m., they ran out of the trout. No biggie. But then my friend's "hoe cake," was raw in the center. So, basically, uncooked Bisquick. My husband's brisket was 25% straight up fat. The rest was only semi edible. 

Service was ok, and the waitress was genuinely sweet and helpful when we told her about the two dishes that were undercooked. The manager took off 20% of the bill, which was very nice and appreciated, 


All in all, the service was good, but the food is over priced and nothing great at all. 

Best part was the fried pickles!!! That was yummy.

I wanted to like this place a little better than I did. It's got a fun atmosphere, a creative drink menu, interesting foods, and a unique flare. The Sutler has a lot going for it but I think it could easily be better. 

I went here for a business dinner with a client group. First off, we ordered the fried pickles, hot chicken, and Potted Smoke Jar. All appetizers were pretty good. I personally liked the pickles best. The portions seemed off on the jar and the hot chicken's breeding was too thin. However, the chicken had a good flavor with as much back-end kick as one of the horses festooned about The Sutler's western decor. One of the guys had a backyard drink and sang it's praises. 

Finally, I had the Short Rib Dog and it was okay. I really wanted to like it since the menu description had me salivating from the moment I walked in. It was blander than I'd like and could have easily brought in more of the cumin mustard and sauerkraut flavor. A big issue I have with The Sutler was the price. I feel like most things on the menu are 20-35% overpriced, especially considering the smaller portion sizes and proletarian featured ingredients. 

Pros-Fun vibe, interesting menu, good addition to the area

Cons-Price and the food misses on the wow factor. 

Overall-Definitely worth a visit. It could be better but I thought it was a good spot!

The Bluebird Cafe didn't bowl me over.  I'm sure if we'd seen an artist we really knew and liked, it would have been an entirely different experience altogether. We were just happy to have scored reservations while in Nashville.

I do think it's important to arrive early whether you have a reservation or not. We had reserved pew seats, but requested table seats (if any were available after all the reservations were seated), and sure enough, we got to move up to a table. Much better than those uncomfortable pews!

The venue is tiny and seating is extremely tight. We shared a table with two other couples. The kitchen burned my quesadillas twice, so I strongly advise eating somewhere else beforehand. I can't imagine anyone comes to the Bluebird for their food anyway. 

My best advice for the Bluebird is to keep your expectations in check!
Great fun..great bands. The place was packed upstairs because the singer was amazing.

My husband and I met some friends here last night for dinner and trivia. I ordered the veggie burger with a gluten free bun (#newyearsresolutions) and fries. I sadly drank water and everyone else had beer or mixed drinks. I like that the drinks were all served in mason jars. It was very fitting with the cute, vintage tables & twinkle lights. Our server was really nice and our drinks were never empty. I personally really loved the veggie burger. I've never had a veggie burger made with beets but I want more! The bun tasted great but was a little more dense than a regular bun. Still, it didn't have the weird taste of some GF breads. It was just impossible to pick up and eat without the burger squishing out onto my plate. I do wish I could have eaten this like an actual burger and not with a fork, but it was still really tasty. There were other things on the menu that were tempting and my husband's pretzels looked awesome. Trivia was really fun and we will definitely be back!

What is there to say, an Institution in Nashville. Lots of fun, great music, great people, great, drinks.  Great for locals and for tourists. Can get very crowded at times but Love this place so Proud of Tootsies

This place is my favorite place to eat while I am in Nashville. There single wide or even their double wides are awesome with tots. 
Lots of fun in this place!

Had a lot of fun here, music was great, Cassandra on that fiddle was absolutely amazing. Very small place and it was a packed house but great crowd, singing along and friendly. But again great music!!

Walked in on a Friday afternoon after hearing some good music coming from inside. The entire bottom level was packed with old couples. It was hard to make your way through without bumping into walkers or canes. Went upstairs to get away from that and ordered a shiner and my friend ordered a mixed drink. It wasn't as busy up there but the bartenders seemed to be more interested in talking to each other, rather than work. 
I ordered one more beer before we left and when I saw my bill was $14 for two shiners, I was pretty annoyed. 
Shiner is a very inexpensive beer so it was annoying to have to spend that much on it. It's way overpriced for what it is. Won't be coming back.

Went on a Thur night and the place was packed. A different band was playing on each floor, it was a lot of fun. As you would expect a lot of young people but was also surprised to see an older crowd (myself included!). Went with a crowd from work and had a great time.

We have been twice. The first time was to go have a drink at the bar downstairs. Such a cool atmosphere. The guys behind the bar definitely know what they are doing. Let's just say that because of the first visit for a drink and an appetizer, we wanted to come back. The second visit we started out downstairs. Again, the drinks rocked. Our bartender totally created a drink for my wife that she love. (He had to do this because they were waiting on fresh strawberries for the drink she had last time.) I also saw the prep work done for the bar. They actually washed the lemons before they cut them!
Upstairs for dinner was great! Our main coarse came out just a bit before the fried pickles and the beer cheese soup, so they took them off our bill. I like that. Shows that they care even if we did not. Good vibe, great staff. Wished we could have stayed for the show. (Yes, they have a stage with live music. Hard to find that these days with a dinner atmosphere.) Go. You will enjoy it.

It's three floors of shoulder to shoulder people.  Surely they're breaking fire codes in there. You would think for such a crowded  place that the only way to get good service would be to park yourself at the bar. Not so!  We were only there for an hour & had someone checking on us at least 4 times while we were there.

My family and I waited for 2 hours in the heat for a open mic at the bluebird cafe. the lines were very confusing and people were line jumping. The staff kept on changing the rules. It was a very frustrating experience overall. Then, after waiting for hours, they directed us to the gift shop. I would not recommend this to anyone unless they enjoy waiting in line.

I enjoyed myself
Halloween here was so fun!
Great mix of music

Great place to end a weekend night (ahem, around 2 or 3 am sometimes).  The band ALWAYS rocks, I don't know how they book these awesome acts, but keep em coming.
I've only been here once during the day, that was during the Nashville Oyster Urban Adventure Race.  They supported community fitness events, so that makes me super happy with them.
Despite the huge amounts of people here on a weekend night, it's actually not that hard to get a drink and the pours are enormous.  
The best part is dancing to the band.  Even if no one in your group wants to dance, the music is going to suck them in.  If that doesn't work, there's always folks to dance with already out on the floor.
A great Nashville spot for a party!

Been here many time and this time was maybe the last time. Ordered 9 beers...ALL were warm and when I approached a "manager" I'm assuming...he acted like he could care less and actually acted annoyed.  An apology would have at least been nice.   Very rude.

Love the Bluebird! It is pretty impossible to get tickets here now since the show Nashville, but it is definitely worth the fight if you can.  It is even worth standing in line.  If you are going the standing in line route, be sure to get there a few hours before. The history of this place is just amazing.  It is very small and quaint inside and you watch about four or five songwriters perform songs that they have written and tell stories about them. The talent here is amazing and the drinks are good.  I am a huge fan of the Bluebird.

Went with my friends and went outside because the bar was crowded, but it was freezing outside. One  of the the at lamps was off and we tried turning it on but it was broken and a security guard came out and told us to stop and we'd be kicked out. We said okay and smoked a cigarette and he came out again and told us to stop again, even though no one touched it. We said okay and a few minutes later he came out with police officers and told us we had too much to drink. Out of all the bars I've been to in Nashville, I don't think I've ever experienced bouncers as rude and ridiculous as this, and I will never go back.
Ok, place overall.  Went once, worth seeing if you've never been.  The bands were ok, not great.  Really crowded on a saturday night fyi.

I just stopped in for a quick lunch here and had some sort of pulled pork sandwich that was very tasty, and the service was good.  I was there mid-week at 1PM and was pretty shocked at how slow they were.  I guess lunch service is new here, hence the sign outside, but I'd go here again.
The atmosphere was great. The people that worked there were incredibly friendly! The food was fantastic. We ate there two nights back to back.

West Nashville hot spot!

This is an adorable house that has been converted to a hip restaurant.

Great for a happy hour hangout with friends, family, or co-workers. On Mondays they have two-for-one specials.

Beyond that, they have great apps and delicious burgers.

One of my favorite things? Owned and ran by a brother and sister, who both serve and bartend. They have created a local spot with great music and a place where you could become a regular.

Definitely a must!

Heard about the infamous Tootsies and knew we had to visit. The line was out the door every day we were there but looked quiet on a sunday night. However took us a while still to crowd in.

Discovered the upstairs, got a table and enjoyed some of their fine Apple Pie shots. The upstairs band suckes. Cared way more about their egos than e very other person in the bar. Couldnt finish songs. Also there was a valet in the men's bathroom?

After spending a few hours here it was already one of my fav Nashville bars. Then we almost got picked up by some swingers and now this infamous dive bar has a special place in my heart too.

This was my first bar I visited on my first night in Nashville last spring and I ended up staying here all night! The bands are great, but the bartenders are better! This is a must for anyone visiting Nashville!

It's nice to see bands under the stars, but the location of this venue is unfortunate. It's only accessible from one road. Expect to wait the better part of an hour to get out of the parking lot. Furthermore, the beer selection is mediocre.

My 2nd favorite place on Broadway..
It has 3 levels of fun!!
All levels have live music.
It gets crowded so be ready to get cozy when you walk through this bar of fun!

Rooftop is amazing! This is a must visit bar in Nashville. The drinks are reasonably priced and the Moonshine is a must! Be prepared to be in a popular venue. It is always crowded, but almost always has live music and for being as crowded as they are the bartenders are attentive and work quickly!

Couldn't get tickets, but stood in line for an hour and a half on a Saturday nite and got very lucky. One of the songwriters (Brian White) that entered while we were waiting told us it was worth the wait. He was absolutely right! The variety of music was incredible.  It was music in the round with five performers's all taking turns with different styles. We particularly enjoyed Lisa Carver.  And, the food was very reasonably priced with tremendous portions and it was delicious. I had a Turkey bacon club that was thick and juicy and came with the most yummy potato chips I have ever had! Service was excellent! We talked to the performers afterwards and even purchased their CDs which we are now listening to on our drive back to Ohio.
The food was excellent. Very hip and trendy environment. Relaxing place with friendly waiters and hostess. Went for Sunday brunch and loved it!

Four stars for the music and fun. I did not try any of the food so I'm not reviewing for the food or service. However we were here on a Wednesday night and there were two great bands. The one up front was playing country. The one in back upstairs played some 90s country and 90s singalong tunes that almost everyone knew. What a fun place. Just don't expect a lot of room for dancing or to get a drink easily or fast unless you are very aggressive about ordering on your own. No cover charge thst night. Can't beat that! There were about 15-20 bottles on the tables around us before anyone cleared them out too so not the fastest to clean-up. I was afraid to go near the bathroom because of this. I can't imagine what it looked like in there. But for sure a "must see" if you're on Broadway.
The bands were excellent. The drink prices were very high , and the bartender on the third floor were not attentive or friendly, all girls who were chatting among themselves and primping.

We thoroughly enjoyed our meal at the Sutler. The fried pickles were tasty. The gumbo was just right. And my husband loved his smoked bologna sandwich with Mac and cheese. Try the Don't Ask Rye cocktail. It was delicious. Even the sweet potato pie was on point. The service was really fast too. So, I don't have a single negative thing to say about this place. Everything was just right and we will definitely be back.

Went here for back to back shows on Valentine's Day. Had the pork sliders which were excellent and so were both shows. I just wished they had a more extensive beer menu.  When your watching music for almost 4 hours it leaves you a lot of time to try a variety which they didn't have.

Walked in here cynical thinking tourist trap and then couldn't leave because the entertainment was so good and the vibe ruled. I don't know the name of the group (four girls who sing on top of the bar, one with a fiddle plus a band) but they were so awesome. They did covers, country hits, hip hop, Led Zeppelin, TV show theme songs, you name it. Super talented and super fun.  Place was packed. They sang and played their hearts out for at least 4 hours. Didn't have any food but the selection of beer is decent from craft beer to crappy Bud/Coors Light.

Warning , coffee fiend review! 

I had been wanting to check out this place for a while since, like others have said, there isn't a good coffee place in Green Hills. I was expecting more ....yeaaa. The place always looks packed and I finally decided to drop in one day. 

The inside was busy with kids running around Everywhere. It seems like this is more of a place for soccer moms to bring their kids after school. At least this day was like that. The line was long and most people seemed like they didn't know how or what to order. A lot of time was spent watching people get all the way to the front of the line only to not know what they wanted. There was only two people working behind the counter and they were swamped ( don't get me wrong , they were working their asses off). 

I got a french press roast and sat down waiting for it to finish. I was surrounded by kids and tweens cracked out on caffeine with parents no where in sight. The decor of the place makes me feel like I'm in a Cracker Barrel!!  There's a whole gift shop area right next to where you need to stand in line. O, and for some reason they are selling books.......religious books are sitting right next to sexual southern romance novels !?!?Lol......I dunno. 

I mean I get the whole idea of helping out countries with severe poverty, I really do. I think it's super cool and I get behind that 100%. But I don't know why a place that's a coffee shop is selling Christmas ornaments , scarfs and stuff that you'll find on Pinterest if you ever go to peruse the website.

I think this place is definitely marketed towards people that live in the area and that alone. This is a place that I would not go out of my way to find or drive to. If you're coming from across the city, there are better places to hit up. Check out my reviews on places in Nashville, Atlanta or San Fran.

Great time till one of the waitresses on the rooftop got a little very rude with us. Over an hour of sitting in the same spot and then she suddenly got mad at us and shoulder checked us a few times then kicked us out. I'd understand if we were drunk. But we were listening to the music nicely. Horrible service and not well made drinks. Music is good service is bad. Tallest, big, unreasonable, blonde waitress upstairs, avoid her like the plague.

First time visiting Nashville and had heard great things about this place... They definitely didn't disappoint! It is extremely touristy, but the live music was great, the drink prices were reasonable and we had a great time. We went on a Wednesday night and it was still pretty busy, so I imagine on the weekends it must be totally packed. Would definitely go back!

Very disappointed.  Went to top bar with my wife and another couple we sat inside because of rain.  Bartender and waitress saw us walk in and sit down.  Sat at a dirty table for 20 minutes while bartender and waitress sat at end of bar and chatted, bar wasn't even busy up there.  We just left.

Great environment, 3 floors with a band on each one. Was very crowded for a Tuesday but was a great time! Not as "Honky Tonk" music playing as so.e of the other bars on Broadway, but bartenders were friendly and music was good!

The burger super grease and not the world's greatest burger. If u drunk and no taste buds perfect place to eat. The taters were extra salty and the chilly was also salty and no crackers. Chilly is all meat nothing else in it. First and last 4 me.

I was so excited to try this restaurant.  I'm a fan of Tom Morales restaurants and I know about the history of the building and knew he would create something special.  I think he did, but I was very disappointed in the service.  Our server and bus boy were inattentive and seemed stressed rather than hospitable.  The food was good but the presentation was sloppy.  We had dirty plates (appetizers, salad and soup) still on our table when they brought out main entrees and we actually had to ask to have the dirty dishes cleared.  I will give it another shot but they need some  improvements to service in order to live up to the hype.  Tom, I hope you are reading this.  (Also -- would recommend one more healthy, non-comfort food choice for both appetizer and main dish options)

This place is everything I expected and wanted a bar in Nashville to be (and to be honest, it's what I'd love a bar to be anywhere).  First off, the place has astro-turf and lawn furnature...genius.  If society wouldn't look down on me, I'd be barefoot in this bar because I love the way turf feels on my feet.

Next, $6 Natty Light pitchers.  Nothing like reliving the old college days and drinking beer that tastes like white bread.  They also had a variety of other beers behind the bar sitting in a bathtub full of ice.  

This is also the only place where I could fall into a lawn chair, break it, get punched in the face by a chick, and still keep telling myself how awesome this place is. 

Plus the bar has "trailer resort" in its name and the link on this Yelp page has a myspace address, how could you go wrong?

We went Tuesday night before a play at TPAC for a round of drinks and appetizers. The service was decent where we had 4 people check on us and gave us what we needed to dine, like small plates and silverware. The food was great, our favorites were the deviled eggs and the Brussels sprouts. Plus, the head chef Matt gave great recommendations on desert for the next time we go, as well as other places to dine in. The decor was nice and somewhat true to the history of Woolworth, and we really enjoyed the shelves with Black chef cookbooks!

My girlfriend and I loved this place.  We were told about The Sutler by a local and came the day before New Years Eve.  We were very impressed for a lot of reasons.  First off they offer a generous military discount and we were treated like first class by our waitress Kelly.  We enjoyed our drinks on our first visit and were again impressed with drinks on our second visit.  The musicians were professionals and added to the atmosphere.  Last I must say what really made our night was this; they were out of the chocolate jar dessert on our first visit and second visit, but went to the extra effort to go out of the way and make one of the lacking ingredients for us. It's full of people of varying ages and lifestyles that keep coming back because of their continued impeccable customer service.  For our brief time in Nashville for Bash on Broadway downtown for New Years The Sutler will be our most memorable experience in Nashville.

My favorite bar in Nashville. When my friends come in to town from out of state I bring them here. Staff is GReAT, drinks are awesome and I love the bar food. I can come here to catch a game, listen to some music or use it as a jumping point to go to the rest of the strip.

I can't comment about the venue or what the atmosphere is like but I can comment about the line you will wait in. The 3 stars is just me imagining I'd of had a good time. No previous yelper really let us know what to expect besides "you will wait in line". We decided to go on a Sunday night where no reservation is required. For the 8pm show we got there at 630pm. The line was already at least 80 people deep. Every one waiting seemed to be from out of town, no locals, so the conversations I got to listen to for an hour and a half were a little annoying. We almost made it in, only about 8 people left in front of us but no luck. As for parking forget about the front parking lot if there is already a show going on. We parked directly behind the bluebird cafe, possibly an employee lot. No signs saying not to and a lot of open spaces. So get there about 2 hours a head of time. Good luck!

I came here on a Friday night to meet a gal pal for a drink. The bartenders were really friendly and served me pretty quickly. I appreciated them being attentive and serving me right up. When my friend came, they let her try a few things before she decided on the cava. When I walked in, there were a great crowd dancing on the floor with a DJ. I loved the vibe and will definitely be stopping by a lot more than often.

a great experience in a beautiful setting! i got there 30 minutes before my friends and had the fried pickle app and a manhattan before they arrived. bartender was great- sorry i didn't get his name!! the food and drink were awesome.

then we moved to a table and Bluesy was our server- she is AMAZING!!! knows everything about everything and is helpful, personable, and professional. she told us everything we wanted to know. i ended up sharing the bc burger dunk with a friend, as well as the brussel sprout side and the pork fat fries. ALL WERE AWESOME.

besides the manhattan, i had the spicy margarita-style drink, and it was SO good. bluesy recommended it, and she was right, as she was about everything.

i'm not a big chocolate person but the friends i was with loved the brownie dessert they had! 

we then went downstairs for another cocktail, and i had one of the bourbon drinks- - brad, the bartender, told me it was similar to a manhattan, and it was, but it was BETTER than a manhattan. brad was awesome, super friendly as well. 

i can't wait to come on a live music night and check that out! bluesy says it's amazing. basically, GO HERE. and ask to be in bluesy's section !! she's AWESOME!

Attended a private morning showcase the day of the 2015 CMT Music Awards.

The breakfast buffet was great and the Mimosa's flowed.

But the best part was seeing and hearing the acoustic sounds of three top songwriters: Chris DeStefano, Jessi Alexander and J.T. Harding.

Hearing them perform some of the songs they wrote, which would be performed later by other "major" artists at the awards show, proved to me that most times, the original is better than the cover.

If you haven't been you need to go. A Nashville landmark and a great place to hear up and coming artists, and some you've heard before. Wife and went over the weekend and the music was great! The food is normal pub type fare but done well, TRY the hummus! It goes perfectly with a Southern Wit. Our server was kick ass and totally earned her tip, again great place.

This place is rad. I usually come here once a year just because I'm from out of state. I love the down to earth, Nashville feel. I usually never remember leaving this place!  
You'll also catch some of today's biggest country music singers or musicians in there. Awesome place!

The main thing holding me back from giving The Stone Fox more stars was our extremely poor service. I came to eat on a fairly slow afternoon with two girlfriends. We ordered our food & theirs was brought out first, which is fairly normal, but when the waitress messed up my order & brought me out something completely wrong I politely let her know, and she told me I could keep the wrong dish & take it home for free. I said sure why not & then expected for my CORRECT dish to move to the front of the line in the kitchen to be rushed out.... twenty minutes later (after both my friends had finished their dishes) I asked about my dish, the waitress went back & got it for me. It was wrong again. She sent it back a THIRD time & finally got it right. I ate my food alone & ended up having to pay full price for it. Service really makes or breaks a place and I can't say I got the best impression of TSF at all after this visit :(

So I've been to this place a few times, I've got to say I really like the food and the atmosphere is good, but every time I've gone they appear to be short-staffed. Now, the staff that eventually gets to me is friendly, but they might not get to me for a while and the wait time gets up into the not particularly acceptable if you went actually hungry.

Their drinks are stout, they have Fernet there if you want to punk a friend (image search Faces of Fernet if you want to know what it tastes like) and they make a pretty decent bloody mary.

If a food item's sauce has something spicy in it, they can't tone it down. I'll point that out as I went with a friend who green bell peppers can be hot to and she had to heavily modify some orders in order to not die of mouth burning from one of the items. They will substitute ranch, that's all I know that saved her.

Nearly everything there seems to have a vegetarian option, they've got tofu galore, but I'm not particularly a fan of how they make it. 29 years of tofu cheffary has made me a tofu badass, theirs is ok.

Parking is ok, there's a lot, nobody knows how to park, easier to park on the street and walk back some times. Your parking will vary.

I like it, every time I've been it's been fun, but every time I've been there's been lots of waiting and I've been hungry.

One random note - if you're sitting next to the closed off fireplace beware, there're nails or pointy wire or something that stick out at knee level (eye level to a toddler) - I somehow managed to perfectly hit my knee on one, although I had no idea looking at it how that was possible.
It used to be better. I ordered grilled cheese and it came out with 1 slice of cheese and 9 tator tots :(

Wow!!!  I didn't have tickets so I got in line for the 6 o'clock show at 2:30 and it was worth it!  Tickets go on sale a week out and very hard to get, but they take the first 20 people in line for the 6:00 pm show. The line started to form between 3:00 -3:30 and didn't stop even after the doors opened at 5:00. The show I was able to see was "a row" where the 4 artists say in a row and took turns playing and talking about their songs. It was incredible to hear these talented song writers and I felt so lucky to have been apart of the intimacy of the show. This is a must for a Nashville experience!

There is a good reason why Tootsies is such a famous and well-adored bar. It is truly one of the gems in Nashville. Located perfectly in the heart of the Honky Tonk strip, it is a short walking distance from most downtown hotels.

I went there on a Wednesday evening, not sure if weekdays would be a good bet, but was pleasantly surprised at how lively and full the bar was. I got there around 7pm and there was a good deal of standing room in the front area by the stage. There was a super fun band playing with a female vocalist covering famous country songs, from Johnny Cash to Miranda Lambert. It started getting pretty packed as the night progressed and I left around 10:30pm.

During my stay I had about 4 whiskey&cokes and the two bartenders were very attentive and prompt in their ways. I did notice and appreciate that the 2 girls kept a steady eye on the door and would greet people coming in. Even when the bar got crowded they'd make eye contact with folks trying to get closer to the bar and get their drink orders.

Each of my drink was pretty well made and only cost me about $6.50 for each. The whiskey and the music went great with each other and I can't wait to visit Tootsies upon my return to Nashville!

We went here for a couple of drinks. It was $7 per beer bottle which I think is a bit much. No beer on tap (we prefer draught beer). It was really busy but we went to the top floor and were lucky enough to find a couple chairs at a table right at the edge of the patio. The thing that stood out to us the most was that there was a live band on each of the 3 floors. I think its a great place to stop by, for the experience. Cool to be at such a historic spot!
Great atmosphere and I love that they contribute financially to the community. Even with live music playing, the environment was tranquil and the drinks were good quality.
Good beer, better bands, amazing food!!!  Me and this place get along better than Michael Jackson and Macaulay Culkin.

Went here with 2 work colleagues based on the reviews.  I will say the entrees were delicious but the 2 appetizers were terrible (lamb meatballs and pickled shrimp). The meatballs were so dry they crumbled like sand and were tasteless.  The shrimp was also tasteless - not even a hint of pickle. 

When we were starting to tell the manager he tried to say "Let me get a content card". We said we'd rather just talk to him.  He essentially said thanks for the feedback,  see ya later.  Didn't even offer to take them off the bill. 

We did try the desert and that was okay.
Food and service was great! I didn't give it a 5 star because the kitchen was very slow. The BLT has enough bacon on it i got a to-go box for. Mac and cheese and tomato soup was on point.
Beers only tonight. Good People on draft. Forget to wear skinny jeans, Chuck Taylor's and fedora so stuck out like sore thumb.

How does this establishment need reviews?! It's blow the top off, no reason to leave amazing!  Pick a floor, settle in, listen, be enlightened by the great music.   Did. Done. Would do it a thousand times over! You're welcome.

Fuck this place. We walked in and immediately smelled piss. Walking upstairs my shoe almost came off because of it sticking to the week old miller lite covered floors. I don't give a shit how its "part of nashville" and how its on the, whats it called? the "nashvegas strip"?. Drove 11 hours and the first thing I wanted to do was drink out of a plastic cup, said no one ever. Shiners were like 5 bucks and the food looked better on the way out. Again, fuck this place.
Live music all the time - cool. $4 yeungling - not. Filthiness - not. Mediocre service - not. Uncomfortable seating - not. Super-touristy crowd - not.

Goodnight. If you like crowded, loud, hot bars that smell like they haven't been cleaned over the years (years that no doubt included drunks puking now and again), then it's your place. If you don't like that -- particularly on a Saturday, midday, then stay away -- even with its history. There seemed to be only two types of people in the bar: 1) 20somethings looking to get drunk, and 2) 40somethings looking to prove they were still 20somethings. Call me a curmudgeon, I just didn't want to spend any more time there than I did.

Well, the booze and food were fantastic. Pretty good prices and I loved all the retro kitchen tables. Service was pretty lousy. The place wasn't that busy to have been ignored by our server, maybe she was having an off night. The door guy, on the other hand, was too preoccupied with chatting up his hipster cronies to even do his job. He wasn't very sly about bad mouthing customers either, we heard him loud and clear as we stepped on the porch to smoke. My travel companion and I are from Chicago where pretty much everyone is a jerk, but the staff here kinda blew us away. Stone Fox, get yourself a better crew of kids who actually want to work and you'll be an A++ establishment.

My wife and I just did lunch at The Sutler, for the first time.  We had a great experience.  Our server suggested the fried pickles and sweet potato hummus as being what they are known for in app's and the hot catfish tacos and pulled chicken for meals.  I wasn't interested in an app, so my wife tried the beer cheese soup and liked it.  She had the hot catfish tacos and really liked them.  I had the brisket tacos, and they may have been the best ones I've had.  They had a lot of great smoky flavor!  This place does have a stage for live music, and they have windows that roll up (think garage door), at the front, for when the weather is nice outside.  We will be back!

This place is made famous thanks to the show Nashville which is the only reason I know about it.  I am coming to Nashville with a group for my sister's bachlorette and we wanted to check this place out.  This means that I had to wake up at 5:50 a.m. my time to go online to reserve spots.  They say you can only reserve 6 people and we had more than that so my mom and sister were at home sitting in line as well.  I clicked in right exactly at 6 a.m. the time they were made available for the following Friday night.  When I got to the selection there was only a couple seats left at every table. How is this even possible if I was right in at exactly the time they said while my mom and sis are still in the queue.  Doesn't seem they make everything available.  I selected and then when my mom and sis got in they got sold out.  I sent them an email saying to cancel the reservation I made and that I'm sorry that because of their system we wouldn't be able to check out their place during our visit.  They wrote back - 
                     
              Thank you for reaching out to us. We are happy to assist with the cancellation of your reservations. Please remember that we are unable to refund the amount you were charged at the time of your reservations (Service Fees, Taxes, or Pre-Pays) but you should not see any additional charges in regards to your cancelled seats.

Awesome, so not only am I out of luck but you also charged me $3 to even try to reserve for a free concert.  What the hell?  People talked about pretentious - I think that is a perfect word for this place.  Get over yourself Bluebird Cafe.  We will likely enjoy great music at better places in Nashville.

Oh and thanks for making me wake up super early and ruin my Monday morning!  Not like you care one bit.

Came in as a tourist, to check the box and say I visited Tootsies. Live music in the back, open mike on a Saturday afternoon. It's exactly what I expected of a honky tonk, lots of people but not too crowded during the daytime. We were greeted right away at the bar for drink orders, and we found a couple stools right in front of the stage.  The rooftop patio was a little scary with its plywood floor but had a great view of Broadway.
I had to go here during my first trip to Nashville!  I mean come on it Tootsies right!?!?  This place was fun!  We were here celebrating a friends 40th bday :)

Went here for happy hour on a Friday, and had a great time! We started upstairs and then transitioned to the downstairs cellar, which was a more refined, chill space to relax. The cocktails were all a little sweet for me, even the old fashioned, but they were a great deal for being 1/2 off (making most of the cocktails $5). The manager and our server were both wonderful and went out of their way to make sure we had a good experience. Would go back again, but probably for happy hour only.

Bit of a wait, but awesome food and even better service!!! Our server, Santos was amazing!! She even got up and sang and blew us away! 10/10 recommend :) 

Also, the bottomless mimosas were actually worth it here. Quick and tasty.
hoenstly the live music is not very good and you cant really dance cause there are too many pepole around. they  also do not give free chasers which is a reall bummer.

Had never been to this part of Nashville and thought it was great. There was an incredible number of bars to hear some really great music. Everyone said to go to Tootsie's and I wasn't disappointed. The bartender Sarah was the nicest young lady, very pretty and sweet. She made the night for me. The band was great and I loved that the woman singing got on top of the bar and sang! It was a really fun place and I was even more impressed with my visit here after visiting other bars with much less enthusiasm and service. The view on the top gave a fantastic view of the street. Again Sarah was great and very thoughtful to make sure I enjoyed my visit. Definitely with come here again and bring friends.

This was the chosen happy hour spot today and let's just say I didn't do the choosing. I ordered a melrose mule first and it was forgettable. But the cucumber cooler was so outstanding that I dubbed it the most refreshing drink I've ever had. Imagine the perfect day by the lake with the sun kissing your skin ever so slightly and this is the drink that can take you there. I am giving this place two stars solely for the cucumber cooler. Go get one! Now the appetizer...the brisket nachos. Just say no to dry brisket. Just say no to broken cheese sauce. Just say no to under seasoned food. This place has potential to be a real winner but the execution and the need to cut corners in food prep stunt the potential.
Went on a Thursday night around 8, super crowded,    Average bands, drink prices same as most on Broadway... nice that they have heaters on roof patio.
Paradise Park is awesome. We split the double decker burger with tater tots and it was amazing. Late night snack stop that you need to try! We also had fun playing with all of their arcade games.

I went to this bar with a couple of coworkers and clients during a conference I was attending in town... I consumed $87 in drinks on my credit card. When I got home to look at my credit card statement I noticed that I've been charged twice, once for $140 and a second time for $35!!!
I had to file a dispute through my credit card company because it's just impossible to reach this joint by phone...

Never going back!
Great music but the beers are more expensive then anywhere else and the beers are warm!!!!  They need to put beers on ice or get colored working right. My service was good and polite

We went here for Sunday brunch a few weeks ago. FYI like every other brunch spot in Nashville expect a long wait. My absolute favorite part was a bloody Mary bar. Think about making your own bloody Mary with your own ingredients except they give you the vodka. I got the breakfast tacos and it was not worth the price. Three small tacos for the price of $12 and it was not worth it.

The key is to hop online and get "in line" for their ticket system. Definitely get on the ticket page a few minutes before the clock starts counting down. I was able to get 2 seats at table 9, which was literally touching the stage. It was perfect. There is a seating chart on the website if you're curious how seating works. Reservations are the only way to go. I can't imagine standing outside (especially in the Nashville summer heat) and waiting for a seat that likely won't happen. 

Food is nothing special, but it's nice to have a few options if you need a little something. They have beer, wine, and your standard cocktails available. Great prices too. 

Overall, such a fun experience and definitely worth it if you can get tickets!

Not great for vegetarians. Yes, there are two dishes on the menu that look vegetarian: my husband and I ordered one of each. Prep was fine (I liked the market special vegetarian dish; he was lukewarm on the poblano pepper), but portions were itty bitty, uninspired, and rather expensive. (He came home and made microwaved Indian food, and I had cereal!)

Only a few of the sides are vegetarian and many of the vegetable dishes are cooked with bacon. 

Our server was kind, but distracted and a bit forgetful. We loved the ambiance and the decor, but the restaurant has a way to go in working out its kinks.

I would recommend The Bluebird as a "must do" for anyone visiting Nashville.  It is a small venue (seats about 100 people) featuring great artists.  I reserved seats ahead of time. The tickets go on sale one week ahead at 9AM Eastern time.  The show I attended was an "In The Round" session, so the 4 musicians sat in a circle in the middle of the tables and took turns playing. It was such a fun time, with excellent music!  The Bluebird has a history of launching artists' careers and lots of country music talents got their start there.  The drinks and food are nothing special, but the music and experience are unforgettable.

I dragged my parents out here for my birthday brunch after having recalled reading an article about it in the Nashville Scene (and maybe because there was a really attractive shirtless bartender in said article). I was not disappointed!

I ordered the chicken and waffles, which was my biggest reason for being interested in the place. They came with a side of syrup and a side of hot sauce, and you decided how much you drenched your food in each. It was delicious. The Bloody Mary I washed them down with was mighty tasty as well!

We sat on the back porch, which has a few tables and overlooks a garden, where I think they might grow some of their own herbs. The inside of the place has a very East Nashville feel to it, a bit hipsterish, but also seems like someplace I could just cozy up with a book on a rainy afternoon. I think I recalled seeing a couch or two inside as part of some of the seating.

My only complaint was that parking was a bit difficult. Otherwise, this place is truly worth checking out!

(I also tragically never encountered that cute shirtless bartender, but I'll settle for the waffles.)

We were walking around Broadway mid afternoon and the band lured us in. They were very good so we decided to stay for lunch. Service was friendly but kept feeling like this place may be sort of tourist trappy but that's just what we were in Nashville so we decided to soak it in. Food was ok nothing to rave about. We had pulled pork sandwiches for about $14 each and had some chicken scratch beer. We were definitely there for the entertainment and the crowd wasn't bad either. We had a good time!

Beautiful small music venue.  We were lucky enough to get tickets for table 4/5.  We shared our table with a mom and daughter from England.   We listened to four really talented musicians playing "In a row".   They each took turns singing their original music.  The show lasted about an hour and forty minutes and then they stayed for pictures.  Great experience!!!  I wish they would have let us spend our $10 each mandatory fee on merchandise instead of food.

First time in Nashville in probably 20 years.  Also first time at Tootsies.  My father use to sing here years ago and I've always wanted to visit.  

My wife and I only wanted to stop in for a drink and then explore more establishments on Broadwsy; however,  we ended up ordering lunch and spending a couple of hours there listening to the band. 

I ordered the burger and the wife ordered the pulled pork sandwich, as both were recommended.   We had them cut in half so that we could share.  The pork was goid, but we both felt the burger was best.

Great experience.   Recommend everyone visit Tootsies.

This past Sunday, my wife and I witnessed a Cuban American mom (about 5' tall and under 110 lbs.) being dragged 20 feet in a choke hold by a large African American bouncer with a large diamond zirconia earring in his left ear - just for kneeling on a chair in order to see.

We followed them out with two nice men (whom were patrons for 10+ years) to ensure she and her husband were OK. 

This was clearly assault, the gal also appeared to be targeted. She said that she was willing to leave but wanted to wait for her husband to return as he had stepped away. This obviously put quite a damper on our Nashville visit. I don't like submitting negative reviews, albeit this guy should be facing assault charges. I feel obligated to warn others in the event this should happen again.

Love this bar!  Both stages always have amazing performers.  Drinks are reasonable, bartenders are friendly.

The negatives I have to give are:  the bathrooms!  So small and difficult to get to!  The other is a good/bad.  It gets packed!  So much so that you can't move and it begins to be hard to enjoy yourself.  If you need space, go upstairs and hang out behind the stange, it seems to have a decent amount of space.

Tennessee staple Honky Tonk. It was really busy and you have the option of three different floors and live music to pick from. Very top has a beautiful view of the NashVegas strip and heat lamps for when it's chilly!

Loved this place!!! Loved the history and looking at all of the pictures on the second floor. A nice restaurant with fantastic food. Very accommodating and friendly toward children. We brought our toddler during the weekend dinner rush (it was a gamble really!) and they made the entire experience so good even with a toddler. I got the fried chicken and an extra side of corn for the little one (so good!) all of their food looked fantastic!
We went back, it's under new management. Super nice and had a high chair! Thanks for appreciating all walks of life

I had heard/read so many things about the Bluegrass Brunch, so I decided to try it out when some friends from out of town came to visit. I read enough reviews to know that I should be prepared to wait a bit. Luckily, once we checked in we were able to go ahead and order our bottomless mimosas to enjoy. The bar area can get pretty packed, but with a mimosa in hand, I wasn't too stressed about it. Plus you have live music to listen to while you wait. I also like that they get your number and text you when your table is ready. You are also sent a link to a site that lets you see what number you are in line-SO helpful! When we got our table, the waiter was very friendly. He immediately asked us if we were planning to truly take advantage of the bottomless mimosas, to which we unequivocally replied YES! That being said, we managed to put down a serious quantity of mimosas, making it totally worth the $15. The food was also good. I had the breakfast tacos (you can't go wrong with bacon, eggs, and avocado). I also loved that we were never rushed, despite there being a wait. I definitely recommend the brunch! Good times were had by all!

upstairs rocks! expensive, but worth it. We actually had a sort of negative experience with my cousin getting us kicked out after punching some chick who pushed her mom and the band not playing our well tipped requests; however, I still don't have a bad thing to say.  The service was awesome (even while escorting us out like gentlemen because we didn't know someone in our group was asked to leave), there's always a band and it's a rooftop deck in the heart of downtown!!

Tootsie's is the place you have to go to at least once just to say you've been. I prefer the top floor, it has much more room. I don't like the first floor at all...very crowded and so packed you can't even move. Top floor is very cool and seems to be just slightly less tourist-y.

I am so glad I was able to have lunch here after reading about it in The Week. I was able to eat a variety of vegetarian dishes -- favorite being the butter bean hummus with sweet relish. The ambiance is way cool and the staff were just out of control lovely from Chef Kevin to our waiter and the woman who greeted us at the door and hugged everyone. Unfortunately her shift ended before we left so I'll have to return for a hug.

My girlfriends and I came to the Sutler on a Saturday for brunch. We were able to get right in around 1:30 PM and they immediately served us some fresh biscuits with sorghum butter and jelly. So good. I ordered the BLT. It was piiled with thick cut bacon and the usual suspects. I tried the hash that my girlfriend got and it was delicious. They offer unlimited mimosas for $15 and the sangria looked refreshing too. I'll be back to try that! 
Overall- it's a good brunch spot. Inexpensive and who doesn't like unlimited mimosas on the patio? Did I mention they have a patio? Yep.

This is totally a dive bar with great music, but they have a bathroom attendant.  I try to make it a rule to deduct a point for bathroom attendants.  I never bring cash with me when I have to tinkle and it makes me feel like I'm not entitled to the soap and paper towels when I wash my hands.

Do not go here if you are not comfortable with strangers pressed up against you en masse.  But if you can handle that (and I generally cannot) then you should definitely go to Tootsie's because it was an amazing time.  It may have been the company, but we actually went twice on our four day trip to Nashville.

The food here is standard "bar food"...the "smoked tuna dip" is not really all that great, but the rest of it was good.  The bartenders are generally very entertaining.  The first night we went there were singers and fiddlers playing on the bar.  The second night we discovered the upstairs bar that had a second stage. 

We had a great time and the music was all very fun.  At least check this place out, even if you don't stay.

One of the most iconic bars in the entire country. This is the place to be in Nashville, amazing bar, amazing people. I did not even try and got about five girl's numbers here just by being friendly. It is sometimes hard to hear in the place its loud but you have to have skills. It had a few locals but its mostly a tourist bar with legendary country music framed pictures on the wall. Southern women are easy to talk and this is the best bar on the Broadway strip by far. Only downsize is that it is not that big and its packed and its hard to move around.
Good food, but a little pricey. The old Woolworth building is really cool. The peanut butter pie was amazing!

Yes, the reputation is deserved.  

We went there on a Friday evening to the first show.  The songwriters' circle was excellent; there were some truly talented voices and I enjoyed hearing about their life experiences and how they factored into the song.  Food wise service was very fast and friendly.  The food is nothing special, but it's totally edible, reasonably priced, and fast (and you don't come here for the food anyway, do you?).  

It's a hole in the wall and a little bit of a ride from downtown, but it was totally worth it.

I had to write an update after coming back for dinner and loving it! I had heard not so great reviews about their brunch from friends, BUT I'm hoping that maybe its just they are busier at brunch and they were still new?

Either way, my friend and I came in for dinner before a show, and ordered drinks and food in the back fenced area. Our waitress was awesome and sure to keep our glasses full. I sampled a couple of cocktails that were really really great and I had a black bean bowl and my friend had a cheeseburger with curly fries. Both were delicious and we ate every bite! Food was seriously delicious! 

Seems like they change up the menu a good amount since my black bean dish is no longer on the online menu :( sad! However I see that they have replaced it with a couple other items that look pretty amazing in comparison. 

Maybe coming here for dinner is the trick, but I'll give it a shot for brunch too!

Stood in line for 90 minutes before anyone came outside to tell us what to expect. They only took the first 20 people in line and suggested that the remaining 40-50 people wait in line for the next show which was 3 hours away. What a waste of time standing in the rain for nothing. We did try to make reservations.

Had a blast here and rocked out until closing time. I'm not sure of the name of the band, but they could play any song requested and kept the energy up!  Beer prices were average $6 for a 16oz bottle. I'm definitely going back the next time I visit Nashville!

One of the best Honky Tonks in Nashville. 3 floors of bands. At least 4 bars. A lot of hooting and fun. The bands were all really good. The beer is cold. What else can you ask for in a party atmosphere (:.

Fun Stop In The Western Nashville Area

SITREP

I was brought here by friends for a nice evening of some munchies, great drinks, and Monday-night *BINGO!* and was not disappointed.

THE SETUP

Located on 51st Avenue, just a bit outside the Downtown arena, the Stone Fox provides some seriously vibes!

*THE FOOD

Delicious food that we had:

* The Kale Pizza; and,
* The BBQ Pork Chipolte Sliders

Each on their happy hour menus for just about $10-$12.

*THE DRINKS

I got myself the Paper Plane, which was a wonderfully refreshing cocktails consisting of Kentucky Bourbon, so it did not disappoint!

*BINGO!*

Monday is bingo-night, and the action was fast-paced as the participants tried to keep up with the "caller".  It makes for a great retro-fun experience, and the crowd was mainly a very hip cadre of 20/30 somethings.  So not your typical bingo crowd.

TOM SELLUCK

There's an oil painting of the man up there right in the middle of the restaurant.  I do NOT know why.  Next time I'm there, I will ask!

THE LOWDOWN

The Stone Fox is cold stone fun!

Well it was an early Sunday Dinner for myself, the wifey, my nephew and my passed out asleep son who had dominated the Nashville Zoo for about 3 hours earlier in the day we decided (after already eating Bobbie's Dairy Dip only 4 hours earlier) on the way home to have a nice meal.   1st choice was Kien Giang, but for a first time ever, I wasn't really in the mood.   

So I threw out the suggestion of trying the Stone Fox.   Of which none of us had tried.

Thankfully (for my sanity sake) it was not very crowded (sleeping toddler in stroller means we might get to enjoy our first damned meal in God knows how long).   I ordered a Brooklyn Lager that came out in a mason jar (nice touch hipsters, nice touch) and enjoyed my brew while some random music I had no idea of from probably the 70's played in the background.

I ended up ordering the Kimchee Reuben (which was fantastic albeit a little pricey at $12 bucks but worth it) and the Pimento Cheese Hushpuppies (I would skip these, they came out almost burnt, try something else instead, of which I'm sure there are good things on the sides list (my first choice was a kale and quinoa salad though they were out of quinoa so I diverted to hush puppies for some dumb reason)).  Wife and nephew ordered Elise's favorite burger, that avocado's and other random things on it.  I tried a bite and very very tasty.   They asked for it medium though it came out a little over cooked but it was still very good.

I can't wait to go back and try the brunch one day.
What can I say about a place that is that established... The drinks are good the beer prices a little high.. but the music and the staff are great. The chili dogs are awesome...
Fair food, fair music. Clean.  Burgers a little too well done for my taste. Lots of tv screens. Not very impressed overall.

After being unsuccessful to get show tickets once and getting on the website for the next night's show, I was THRILLED to be in the que immediately with less than a minute wait time....only to see the show was sold out. Really??? What a scam!!!! Disgusted

Well where do I start. I had the fried chicken and first bite took me back to my grandmothers house frying chicken in her kitchen. She would fry it in an iron skillet. The collards were equally amazing and let's not even talk about how good the Mac n cheese is. Thanks for taking me back 30 years!!!

Went on a Saturday night. Place was packed but be sure to take advantage of the several different floors including the rooftop.  They had a band with a sick fiddle player and they did a lot of popular stuff with a twist.  We only drank beers so I can't speak for the mixed drinks.

Tin Roof is tucked down at the bottom of the ever changing Demonbreun (street?) and has somehow managed to outlast a good number of other bars on this strip of businesses, so they must be doing something right! I find a good number of people planning to go here, but it's just never my go-to place. Drinks are about what you'd expect and I can't remember the food, so that tells me it's probably OK. Just seems rather middle of the road all around. They have a lovely patio area and a "green room" that they've added on that is nice. 

Tin Roof also has live bands and music and can be a fun night out. Maybe now that my BF lives in the Gulch I'll head over here more... we'll see!

Went here last night, St. Paddy's day, they had two local singer/songwriters and then two from Belfast, Ireland. We were able to get reservations in advance, you can only get them a week in advance on-line. When you get there, there are two lines, one for folks with reservations, the other without. You have to check in, there's a staff member to do this. I noted there were around 20 people without reservations and they all got in, and even saw some additional stragglers seated later.  There will be a ten dollar cash cover and they want you to spend 7 bucks on either food or drink. Food ain't that great, don't come here to eat is my advice! Place is very small and intimate, maybe sits maximum 125-150 and it's cramped. The artists sit in the middle and take turns playing, they played almost two hours, but about a half hour was crowd banter I could have lived without. Perfect sound and acoustics. Now, some song writers should stick to writing and not singing, a wide variety of the quality of singing was displayed. Even better than listening was gleaming insight into the history and process of song writing, the local
Guys had written some major hits for big stars and they didn't mind name dropping at all. Glad I was able to visit and experience this "listening room" experience. Anxious to give the Douglas Corner Cafe a try tonight!
First time here, in from Chicago for business. Great place to get a 1/2 burger with sweet potato fries. Sunday night visit about 7:45pm. Not a long wait. Definitely will ve back.
the tots are the best thing to ever happen to my life i wanna order 8 more orders rn. then i wanna roll in a basket of them and cover myself in tots and ketchup and never look back

The food was exceptional! I got a chicken and avocado sandwich with fries (probably some of the best I have ever had). The sandwich was large enough to take some for later. 

My only complaint is that I went during the lunch hour and sat outside. It was not very busy, and the waitress was not very attentive despite the meager crowd. The food was delicious if you're looking for a nice light lunch though!
I really like this place, the drinks the atmosphere and the random events I walk in on from time to time.

This would have been 5 stars. The bar itself is five! The vibes, the bartenders, the layout... all AMAZING. But I need this situation  to be brought to light. Tonight I went with two new friends my boyfriend and I just met at a previous bar. We were jamming, dancing, enjoying ourselves sooo much! The band was great! However, at the end of the night, the band's moral compass took a turn. It was the most unreal experience I have ever had in a bar, and I have been in the industry for 15 years, working in several bars that host live bands. we were on the top floor, Thursday night October 25, it was a girl with long dark hair as the lead singer, and a second singer who was on acoustic (there were three other members who did not seem to be apart of this rude disgrace of human behavior). She basically hosted an auction for people to pay to request songs. I get it you're working for Tips.... but she said "we'll play free bird for 100$" and some female audience member actually paid it! I was like ok that's a great song, 'do you' if you have that money, but then literally 2 bars in, she claimed she'll stop playing if someone else paid her 100$.. and someone oddly did.. so they switched.. I soon found out my new friends made a donation of 20$ for a direct song request that they continually ignored... and then after both those incidents, she started arguing with an audience member who took her drink off the floor of the stage by accident.. and a few of the band members chimed in to call out this girl and told her to "if you're gonna steal a drink,you better drink it otherwise get the fuck out!" over the microphone.. that girl in the audience clearly got upset and ran out.. the band (not all members specifically) clearly manipulated the audience for money.. took advantage of intoxicated people.. it was super disheartening .. and rude. I hope they no longer represent your company as I heard amazing reviews from your establishment overall.
Very fun, great night out.  The food wasn't very good but the experience was outstanding.  Very Nashville with great music, and very laid back crowd.
very cool 3 story bar/restaurant with live music. blackberry moonshine was awesome. Nachos just ok. But definitely a place I would revisit for drinks and music!!

We just got back from dinner at The Sutler and it was deeeelish!

My husband and I started with the Potted Smoke - a mixture of brisket and pork butt with some bread for dipping. We both thought it was a bit too fatty and the ratio of bread to meat was a little off. For $9 we both agreed we wouldn't order it again.

For dinner he chose the Brisket Horseshoe with and added fried egg ($2). I had the Chicken Horseshoe. The Horseshoes are $16 each and come with your choice of protein on a slice of Texas toast. There's a sauce and then shoestring fries on top. The chicken was SO good and really tender. The portion was definitely just the right size. We also shared a side of the brussel sprouts. The portion was good for an added $8 and split between us well. They're layered with mashed potatoes and have french fried onions on top. Not remotely healthy, but SO good.

We ended up sharing the brownie dessert. It comes with a maple ice cream and a nut topping. I thought it was too rich, but I'm not a huge chocolate fan to begin with. Also we got four brownie pieces and a scoop of ice cream which seemed a bit off balance. I'd have liked one less brownie since it was split between two people.

Their drinks are well priced - signature drinks run $9 and most draft beers are $5.50. My husband had two of the cocktails and they were really tasty. The Tennessee Brew Works Southern Wit is what I had and always a good choice.

Overall - $100 after tax/tip/drinks. We definitely wouldn't eat all that again, but before Nashville overtakes this place for the next few months it was good to try a little of everything.

The basement lounge area is really cool. It's open but with lots of little seating areas for groups. The bathrooms have a prisony vibe to them - but it fits with the overall theme of the downstairs area. 

All in all - four stars. The ratios on some dishes need a bit of tweaking but the quality was great!

Sitting here observing the cleanliness practices at the bar on the third level. Watching Sasha on Jan 28, 2018 at 730p cough repeatedly into her hand, braid her hair, and then eat at the bar. Never saw her wash hands and then she handled ice, cups, and alcohol. Now she's rubbing her fingers on her lips. Yikes.

Went for the first time a couple weeks ago. Have always heard good or indifferent things about this place and wanted to check it out for myself. I don't typically go out to bars much, but sometimes a girl just wants to dance. 

We got there a little early, I would say around 930-10. Was not super packed, took a while to get bartenders attention to get drinks. Sat at a table listening to the music. Not many people were dancing at the time. Once the time djs swapped, the music got better and brought a ton of people to the dance floor. By 11 the place was packed and we were having a blast. 
The other side wasn't packed earlier in the evening and I honestly forgot about the other side. On our way out, we walked through the other side. I stopped for about three songs. Loved the live music on that side.

I would come back.

This place is nice. Good food, good service, and as much history as they could bring back. For some reason, this place doesn't pop up on Yelp when searching for breakfast spots. It really should, because your food is delicious. To the owners/managers/employees, thank you for helping to keep history going. If we would have known about it earlier in our trip, we would have come here more than just this one time on our last day.

Seen some of the best shows since I've been in Nashville here. The interior is Twin Peaks(the show)with a modern kick which is awesome. The back porch area has a great atmosphere. I have eaten here once and the BBQ Nachos were layered with BBQ so every chip had some toppings, and the fried pickles were delicious. Very cool
Best joint on the Broadway! The bartenders are super attentive and nice. Food was on salty side and typical, but the and playing that night was golden!

This place wound up being my favorite bar on Broadway. It's totally a dive bar but the beer selection is top notch, the music was great and the staff friendly and attentive...and they have skee ball. Totally worth a stop when in Nashville!!
GREAT acoustic venue. Food is good and service is as well. It's a little small but that adds to the intimate feel. Great place to really go LISTEN to some great music.

I'm not a huge country music fan, but I had an absolutely fantastic time at Tootsie's.  I would consider some of the songs played as more main stream than Country, but Country is prevalent.  It's a simple formula, great music, libations and wonderful service.  Check it out before the crowds become too overwhelming.

We had a great dining experience at the Sutler. I was curious to try their take on the horseshoe, as it's a favorite in my home state of Illinois. I made a reservation online, which was an easy process, but was a bit disappointed to find that we still had to wait 10-15 minutes upon our arrival. They'd run out of the cocktail I was really hoping to try, but our waiter was quick to make an alternate recommendation. The food took some time to arrive, but I didn't think the wait was anything out of the ordinary for Nashville. The staff was very courteous and gave us frequent updates. I have to say, that horseshoe was well worth the wait! It was simply delicious. To make up for our wait time, they gave us a complimentary dessert, which was really thoughtful and spoke to their dedication to customer service. I will definitely return to the Sutler and would recommend it to anyone looking for a good meal (especially the elusive horseshoe!) in Nashville.

I don't know where to start on this review. Let's go basic: Food.

The food is good. Very good - if you're in the breakfast/brunch mood, pick the sweet potato pancakes with bourbon butter and jalapeno bacon. If you're in a light lunch mood, you can't go wrong with the fried chicken salad. It comes with white hominy and is amazing.

But actually you should come here because of what this place was and what it means now. This is where the Nashville sit ins happened and in the second seat from the end is where a black man was arrested instead of a black man having an opportunity to eat.

Sitting at that same counter, thinking about what all has and hasn't changed in our country, made me cry all the way through my meal. The history is palatable here. The staff knows it, the owner sure as heck knows it and no one is afraid to talk about it, share memories and stories and celebrate the opportunity to be a different place, in the same place, as part of a new time.

Go. Eat a meal. Ask questions. Think.

Sro. Standing to the side of the stage, got pushed into table to my right. Female singer very off key
 Left after 10 min. Should have a crowd control. So much for my excited anticipation of this wonderful legendary starmaker.
Victoria Nellums

Every time I walk into Paradise Park I get transported back to an era where 90's version of Billy Ray Cyrus rocked a mullet and sang "Achy Breaky Heart". Make no mistake, P-Park is playful with the redneck decor (i.e. there is a Christmas tree made out of tires spray-painted green) but it gives this bar a fun atmosphere with a Joe Dirt-like character. It is kitschy and slightly over-the-top but not offensive. I've spent hours here since the trailer park theme draws you in, the cheap beer in the bathtubs catches your attention then the bands get you to stay. The bands are some of the best I've seen on Broadway. Although I've mentioned some of the highlights and appeal there are even more things I enjoy about this joint.

The service is great. The bartenders are super nice and I've never had a problem with the service. The food is an intoxicated person's dream. They have all those foods you crave late at night--mac n' cheese, hand dipped chicken tenders and tater tots smothered in nacho cheese (yes I've tried all of them and they are amazing). On a night when the main bar area isn't completely packed you can order with the bartender and sit at the bar to eat or one of their tables in the back. They have a section of the bar that looks like the outside of a double-wide and you can order food there and eat on the restaurant side of P-Park as well. 

In summary, P-Park is a place that I recommend seeing if you find yourself on lower Broadway. I always take visitors here and they find it to be a "hoot". Grab a $6 pitcher with some friends, listen to their amazing artists and have a good ole' time.
Good night time bar.  If you are a smoker you can go outside and smoke.  You may see a country music star occasionally.  Big mixed drinks.  Cabs are always available.

So, this is a trashy bar. You should not go here sober. If you have a low tolerance for bachelorette parties or tourists, it's also not for you.

However, I freaking love it. For some reason half of the graduate students at Vanderbilt are always there. It's a particular favorite with the law school. 

The band is always great, there are $6 pitchers of beer, the bathrooms are always relatively clean and there is an attached restaurant for your drunk-food needs. (I recommend the cheesy tots and the award-winning corn dogs).

In short, it's a great place for a wild night out. Don't expect to sip a classy drink here though.

A MUST do in Nashville.  I am not a country music fan but that does not matter here, when someone has talent, the music has no boundaries.  This place is small, intimate and the talent that is show cased is never short of exceptional!!  If you have ANY interest in music, you MUST go.  Anytime I come to Nashville now, the Bluebird cafe is a MUST.  Now, getting tickets is another story but I would not hesitate standing in line for 3 hours for a chance to see another show!  And I typically don't do lines!  GO, you WILL NOT be disappointed!!

I am a Hispanic male from Southern California. Thursday night, I visited Tootsies with my GF and  some friends. As I approached the entrance of the bar, I was asked for my ID. I pulled my wallet out, and pulled out 2 ID's (drivers license and State ID) I handed what I thought was the bouncer, my Drivers license and then he asked me "Is the other ID your Green Card?" I turned to him in disbelief and asked him did he really ask me that. I immediately walked in and asked for the manager. We were approached by a dark haired man with glasses who said he was the manager. We walked down to confront the bouncer only to find out the bouncer was a Sheriff. In the midst of speaking to the Sheriff and manager, a large black man (real bouncer)walks up to me and pushes me. I tell the man to keep his hands off me, and the manager proceeds to tell me I am no longer welcomed in the bar. The Sheriff had to separate the bouncer and manager from me.
