This is the first time in my life that I have experienced racism directly and wouldn't imagine it would occur in an establishment of this magnitude. I've been to this place a couple times on other visits to Nashville and even attended the bar earlier in the day before the incident! I know this incident is a sign of the times and this will no way effect their business but hopefully the "management" at Tootsies will consider some training on how to handle these types of situations in the future, as I am sure this won't be the last time this happens here!

I finally was able to eat at the Stone Fox.

What I mean by that, is that every time I had stopped in before, my visit happened to occur between serving times. I do wish "bar food" options would be available throughout the day, especially because times that I have been declined for food have been awkward, in that servers let me walk around a bit before explaining the schedule. Maybe a sign could help to communicate the set up?

Food was OK, but service was way slow. There wasn't an explanation or check-in; I wish that our server would have offered us refills on beers (or even water), because I would have taken him up on that in a moment. Fried pickles were fine. BBQ nachos were greasier than usual, especially because flour tortillas were used. 

I'd be interested in visiting the Stone Fox again, but I'll be sure to triple-check their hours.

I like The Stone Fox. I do. The food is good and I love the cocktails. The major problem that has continued since they first opened is service. They are perennially understaffed and service time really suffers for it. The staff are really nice, but it takes forever to get anything. As someone who used to be a server, I try to be understanding, but it's also very frustrating.

Everyone kept telling us to grab a drink at Tootsies and I'm guessing it was out of nostalgia? Super packed and drinks were nothing fancy. Live music was awesome but after my vodka soda with well (Popov? I'm guessing) vodka we were ready to move on. Definitely a been there done that kind of place.

I have had some good, GOOD food at The Stone Fox. I regret to say I've only been there maybe twice in all the while it's been open, and with all of the excitement that has surrounded it since it did open.   The ambience is great and unusual.  The food really is the star, though. And the eclectic music, if that's what you're there for.

Tootsie's is a three floor venue with live music on every floor. Although it's crowded on the first floor as soon as you walk in, don't despair, go up to the third floor where it is most likely roomier and cooler. 

They take advantage of the fact that they have been around so long because their prices are higher than most in Downtown Nashville. $7 for bottle beer, but the entertainment makes it worth it. 

Thursday afternoon 7/27, beginning at 2:30, we saw perhaps the best band in the three days in Nashville. It was a 6 member band that was unnamed. Lauren on vocals and Katrina playing the fiddle. They were joined by various male singers at times. This group had more range and material than the other bands we had seen.

Music City USA. You have to visit this place.

I got their buffalo shrimp appetizer as a meal with a side of Mac n Cheese.  Both were outstanding.  I was a little surprised when shrimp lettuce wraps arrived because of the dollop of celery salad, which I did not expect, but it was a great compliment to the fried spiciness of the shrimp.  Also had a few happy hour drinks that were delicious as well.

We went for birthday brunch yesterday and it was amazing. Great fun atmosphere, good food, outstanding service, and the best part of all bottomless mimosas for $14.00.  And they gave me a free glass of beer served in a western boot mug.  It was so cute.  The only think I would have done differently, was to arrive earlier.  It gets crowded quick and we were hard pressed to find a parking spot and a seat at the bar.  But it was so much fun.  Annual event from now on.

Ehhh, it's ok. I've been twice, the first time for a black coffee and the second for an extra dry cappuccino. I wasn't impressed, and the place is definitely overpriced (a common Green Hills failing). I was a barista for more than eight years, and I know my way around a cup, but this place is drinkable at best. I'd honestly rather go to Starbucks, so that says something.

AVOID at ALL Costs-FOOD POISONING and Bad Customer Service

Me and my family arrived at Sutler Saloon on Monday afternoon. I was super excited because the website looked awesome. 

My family arrived 15 min before me. Once I arrived my family had their Apps, I looked over the menu and found what I wanted. 5 min passed and then 10min. I was thirsty even a glass of water would have sufficed..but no NOTHING!. I had to go find another server who stated that original server had been cut and but she could help us. He didn't check on his table or anything. Just did his side work while we sat with no server. That wasn't even the beginning. 

* It was so cold we had to bring in jackets into the establishment, we even asked for the fans to be turned off and our request was dismissed by the male server who forgot about us. Another lady came in and asked and it was turned off. HMMM
* We had to bus our own table
* Sangria was horrible we told original server but again who would expect him to do anything from the amount of customer care he has already displayed.
* The manager was whipping down tables, on his computer answering the phone and then was at the prep station placing food to the plates WITH NO GLOVES
* The server wasn't focused and messed up all the checks so we had to write down all the orders on separate pieces of paper to help. 

NOW HERE COMES THE DOOZY!

THEN 3 OF US GOT SICK FROM FOOD POISONING. My sister immediate had to use the restroom and was throwing up for 2 days. 
I had stomach aches but no biggie couldn't eat for the rest of the night no biggie right.. WRONG the next morning woke up THROWING UP! On the flight home THROWING UP on the PLAN. Had to take a day off of work. I am diabetic so when I get sick it is a different beast and I have to monitor myself so DKA won't occur. 
My other friend had diarrhea for 2 days

PLEASE DON'T GO THROUGH WHAT WE WENT THROUGH!  We even called and didn't they care UMM NO! Please the experience nor the food is worth the pain me and my sister are going through. I am just so glad my 5 year old niece wasn't effected.

Decent appetizers and lots of music choices.  If you don't like the first floor go to the second or third.  Surprisingly kid friendly (middle of the day).  Wanted them to see what a Honky Tonk was and they delivered.  Worth a hop as you hop in and out of the establishments on Broadway!

This is mostly for the Friday Night Fight event on 8/26 which was coordinated with JRCLive. 

We bought VIP tickets for the Mayweather v McGregor Fight Night Block Party at Tin Roof. The VIP tickets cost about $20 more than a standard ticket ($35 vs. $15 in advance) and had a number of alleged advantages. First, VIP ticket holders had access to a restricted area closer to the screen for "optimal viewing." The VIP area had its own dedicated bar and bathroom areas (more on this later), and were allegedly sold in "limited numbers" to keep lines for both short. The screen was "the biggest in Nashville." 

To put it mildly, the reality was a bit different than the expectation. For starters, the "VIP" area was absolutely jam packed. There was less room to move around the VIP section than there was in the general admission section. There were a few folding chairs in the middle, but for the most part, it was just crowds of people standing and hoping to get something resembling a decent viewing angle (not easy to do because the VIPs were in the front and the giant screen wasn't easy to see from most spots- actually better from the General Admission section). 

The lines for the bar were terrible. like 20+ minutes to get a drink. The lines for the bathrooms were worse. Also, the VIP "bathrooms" were 4 porta potties that got REALLY gross. Lines in the general admission section were shorter. We ended up walking further to go up there for drinks and bathroom runs. 

On the positive side, the screen was huge, it was fun to watch it as part of a big crowd like that, and the drink prices weren't bad. The staff remained friendly and helpful even though they clearly were overwhelmed (anybody in their shoes would be). Though to be fair, I'm not sure whether the outside bartenders were from Tin Roof or the event planning group (JRC Live).

After the fight we went inside (the bracelets got you in for no cover) and left almost immediately after because there was a huge fight on the dance floor and someone was literally dragged out. No thanks. I like divey and even a little rowdy, but this was downright trashy. Maybe it's better on a non-event night, but it was rough.

We went to Woolworth on 5th during a trip to Nashville and were pleasantly surprised! The selection is good and all of the food was southern comfort food. The staff was lovely, our waitress was very friendly and attentive. 

We got shrimp and grits, gumbo and both were great. The vegetarian options were really creative and nice for the vegan in our group.

Definitely worth checking out for the history when you're in Nashville!
Fun vibe.  We stopped by late night on Friday, and then returned again on Saturday. Really enjoyed all 3 floors.

Wow! What a awesome way to start off my Nashville trip. I'm glad I listened to everyone. Its a three level bar with live bands on each levels which includes a roof top bar. Drinks and bartender are wonderful. It's a must try experience.

They don't allow colored people into the bar. EspeciallyIndian (India) people. I was sober and still kicked out.

Cool but crowded venue with different live music on every floor. The outdoor patio was crowded (Saturday afternoon) but it was such a nice day that I personally didn't really care. The live band on the 3rd floor was amazing, glad I got to hear them play in this venue.

My husband got us expensive tickets to a Willie Nelson and Alison Krauss & Union Station concert. We went mainly to see Alison Krauss & Union Station. We are from Birmingham, AL and made the trip to Nashville to stay the weekend. We had dinner in Nashville before the concert & left a little later than we wanted, but still had plenty of time to get there by start of the concert. When we got a couple of miles away, as I could see on the map, traffic was totally stopped. It inched along for an hour. When we finally turned into the parking area, it was insane! None of the parking attendants knew what the heck they were doing. A few of the cars in front of us were directed to a lot near the street. We were directed to the very back of the lot, near the stage. When we got to that lot there were about five parking attendants all standing together and when they started directing us, one directed us one way and another directed us the other way! They were totally clueless! We then saw why it was taking so very long for all the cars to get into the lot. These morons! When we finally got parked & started walking to our seats, we noticed that we had to walk back, all the way to the front of that lot to get in. It was blocked with fence close to where we were. When we FINALLY got to our seats, Alison Krauss & Union Station were over an hour into their set. We got to see their last 40 minutes. During intermission to change the stage, my husband and I started talking about getting out after the concert and how terrible it was going to be to get out since we were parked in the lot farthest from the street. Then I started reading reviews on here and saw that we were right in thinking that way. We ended up leaving after one song of Willie Nelson so we wouldn't get stuck for another 2 to 3 hours in traffic trying to get out. I have been to hundreds of concerts at many different venues & I've never encountered something like this. Bad experience and a waste of a lot of money. Will never go here again.

Nice Nashville bar. The security was relaxed and that was nice considering some can be gun happy. The bartender greeted us right away and got us drinks quickly for the amount of people in there. The mixed drink was delicious and it wasn't watered down so thumbs up to that. Band was great. They took song requests and got right to singing the songs. They rocked that little stage.

Great atmosphere. We got here at 11 for brunch and it was already slammed. It gets pretty crowded really early.

I had the breakfast platter (w/bacon and biscuits) and he had the BLT with an egg. Our food was salty like clog your arteries salty. I left half my food on the plate because it was so salty.

Also, we waited almost 30 mins for our food and it was lukewarm-cold.

Maybe their dinner is where it's at because it's not the brunch.

I would come back for drinks or a show or to try dinner though and I'll review again.

Incredible dining experience from start to finish! We went for dinner last night, and we're already planning our next visit to the Woolworth. Allow me to give you a breakdown of our very memorable evening:
Ambience: As soon as you walk up to the building, you can feel the history this beautiful building has to offer. The owners did a remarkable job with the restoration, salvaging the original floors, the staircase, and the mezzanine. The aesthetics are top notch throughout, from the beautiful antiqued mirrors to the retro wallpapers. I spent most of the night obsessing over all the decor. The entire restaurant had perfectly dimmed mood lighting with a warm vibey feel. I can't wait to come back to have cocktails at the upstairs mezzanine bar that overlooks the downstairs. 
Service: From the second we walked in, we were greeted with friendly smiling faces. The hostesses were very kind and attentive. The bartenders were very knowledgeable about the beverages and quick to take our drink orders when we visited the bar. Once we were seated for dinner, we had very prompt and polite service from our server and SA. Benjamin was great to check on us and keep our table clean and free of empty plates. All of our appetizers and entrees came out in a very timely manner. Overall, we thought the service was great! 
Cocktails: The cocktail menu is very inventive, full of solid choices. I had quite a few of the rye whisky cocktail called 1930 and finished my night with the Love Pinot Noir. Both were very satisfying and paired well with our dishes. My table also ordered several cocktails off the menu, and everyone was very happy with their choices. 
So now the food: Oh the food! To start, everything on the dinner menu sounds amazing! I would label the cuisine as creative Southern comfort food, with a few dishes having a little Cajun feel. I wanted every appetizer on the menu, but we kept it to 4. The fried cheese curds and gumbo were my favorites, but all our starters were delicious! I'm dying to come back for the harissa chicken thighs and the Brussel sprouts! Then the entrees....sooo good! I ordered the braised short ribs and also tried all of my friends dishes. The short ribs were excellent and the portion was quite generous. The fried chicken was absolutely legit. Living in Nashville, it's not often that I get to have fried chicken that isn't labeled as "Hot Chicken," but I loved this fried chicken so much. It was authentic Southern buttermilk fried chicken that granny would make...if you're granny was a 5 star chef, that is. Not greasy, not too heavy, and perfectly breaded. Our table really enjoyed the fish and the ribs, as well! After our entrees, we were completely stuffed (due to the sizable portions) but could not pass up the dessert menu. So we indulged, and we were NOT disappointed. We tried several but my favorites were the chocolate pudding with the peanut brittle and the caramel pecan pie. They were amazingly decadent and were the perfect finish to a wonderful night.  Overall the entrees and apps were very flavorful and well seasoned, and the desserts were everything a Southern gal could ask for. I can guarantee you won't find anything bland or boring on this menu. I recommend you go make your reservations now before everyone discovers this new hotspot. It will definitely be a new staple of Nashville. 
PS Sorry there are no pictures. We dug in as soon as the food arrived. At best, I could have uploaded pictures of empty plates licked clean
Our first stop in Nashville. Great happy hour specials!! Bartender was awesome and live music.

Tried most of the honky tonk bars on Broadway and Tootsie's was easily our favorite.  The place was packed on all three floors and for good reason.  I'd suggest checking out all three floors and find the band you enjoy and go for it. The beer is ice cold and we found the bartenders provided really good pours on the mixed drinks.  Hey, it's not the bar at the Ritz, but it's not trying to be.  This is a honky tonk; expect that atmosphere and you'll get the most out of this place.

Love this place! Totally local flavor with a hip environment!  The drinks are great and they just added food.  Love that they offer gifts where the proceeds benefit different causes. The staff is always friendly!

Loved this place. I've been to Paradise Park Trailer Resort bar on two separate occasions. Its right down by all the action on Broadway in downtown Nashville. They had great live bands and a crazy crowd. We had an awesome time as this was one of our many bar stops me made in downtown Nashville. The drinks were ok, but a little pricey. I did not get a chance to eat, but they do serve good food from what I have been told. I would definitely go back when in Nashville..A+ good time!

Had a great time here last night! We were there for a blues show with the Mike Henderson band and they were awesome! No reservations for the Monday shows, so we started lining up about an hour before the doors opened and we were around 10th in line. Drink prices were reasonable and the service was decent. We ended up sitting dead center directly in front of the stage, so we had a great view of the band. Would definitely come back!

I really enjoyed brunch on a Sunday. There was a wait so I ate at the bar. I had quick, super friendly service and delicious food.  The scrambled tofu needed lots of help though, just a bit of seasoning would have helped. That's really the only reason I'm not giving Stone Fox 5 stars.  The homemade biscuits had great flavor with a perfect flakiness. The Tres Leches with coconut icing was beyond any I've had at the neighborhood Panaderia.  John at the bar was so warm and attentive. I'll go back for Monday night BINGO!

Terrible staff. Visiting town and with my friend who stepped outside to call über for our ride. I was just minding my own business and Was immediately started being harassed.... thinking I was abandoned. to their credit they were trying to line me up a hotel I just played along confused why they were bothering me to begin with. So if you want to be treated badly and put up for the night they are your place!

Ummm lose the attitudes dudes!

Fantasia was AMAZING!!!  She helped us with our heel situation and was able to offer us flip flops which made our night!!!  As well as the whole staff.  Fantasia was very patient and fun with us and all the customers that were there. We go there often and  enjoy the late hours and great menu!!

I'm not one for Honky-tonks, but the historical significance of this place in the 70's and 80's got me interested.  Not much by way of decor here -- walls are plywood with graffiti encouraged by the management, concrete or wood floors, and stools to sit on, and wooden tables.  The draw is the music, not the decor, and while every bar on the street has a live band, Tootsie's sports 3 -- one on every floor of the building.  Don't like the song their playing, hit the stairs ........ like tuning the radio.  Craft brews on this whole street are pretty hard to come by, but Tootsie's had Fat Tire in the bottle for $5 a pop, so we hung out for a while.  Conversation is quite strained, because the music is really loud, and the crowd is really raunchy -- country girls have no qualms about grinding up against you if they like the way you look.  The other thing that surprised me here -- although they aren't alone on Broadway with this -- is that after every set of songs, the band sends one of it's members into the crowd with a tip jar to "take up a collection".  While their conversation with you is friendly and good natured, the jar is being shaken right under your nose, and I did feel a little brow-beaten by the guy after his third trip around the bar during our visit.  Where I come from, the bars pay the band with the jacked up prices for booze, and you tip the musicians on your way out if they played a song you like, or requested.  Here, it seems that the bar jacks up the booze prices anyway, but the bands are forced to "sing for their supper".  "Gotta earn a livin' ", he said more than once as he rattled his pickle jar in my face.  Put me off a little bit, but not so much that I wouldn't recommend them.  Just know what you got as you enter.

We would give it more stars but they asked us to leave our booth unless we paid $1000.00 because it was after 6:30pm on a Monday night. So all 20 of us whose flight was cancelled will spend our money somewhere else in Nashville!! Have fun we will somewhere else where they want to make $$$!!

I love a great coffeehouse. This is definitely a cute gem in the heart of bustling and busy Green Hills. I came on a weekday afternoon, and it was quiet, but many people were there-- students, professionals meeting with coworkers, etc. The coffee choices are many. Very low-key environment.

The website says each reservation can be for up to 6 seats. We are at the front of the first come, first serve line. A party of 9 come through, which only 6 have reservations for. Of course, they let the 3 additional people in without reservations. The girls at the front seating and hosting were rude and dismissive. Disorganized seating. Unimpressive interior. You'd think with all the allure of its venue, they'd invest in a better set up to accommodate the people "keeping their lights on and their doors open". The experience was underwhelming. It's a relic that is barely functional. Take a pic in front of it and tell people you went. You're not missing much.

This place is a great place for brunch, nice vibe and a great bluegrass band. Rachel was our waitress and she was great!! Always made sure our mimosas were filled. I had the smoked brisket and it was pretty good. Also had the cheese grits...AMZING!!

Cool history. Awful business. Ive known several people to work and play here over the years and they have all said how horribly they treat people. Sky high prices. No room to move. This is a tourist trap plain and simple.

Fun college type bar. The place is HUGE! We came in after the live music and before the real clubbin crowd, which was great for us. 

We even had some fries which were really good. Nice way to soak up the booze before...more booze. 

They serve drinks in plastic cups, shots in paper cups. Not my favorite, but definitely fitting the type of bar and crowd. 

The bartenders were *lightning* fast and kept track of our tab perfectly. The music was loud, servers were quick and the beer was cold. No complaints!

Looks like a great setup for bands in the back. We'll be back to see some live tunes for sure.
I had fun. My boyfriend thought it to be a frat bar. But I meet some awesome people there. Service was friendly. I would go back.

I would like to preface this review by stating that I did not eat here, but only made this a stop during a night of drinking down Broadway with the wife. That being said- as a beer and moonshine drinking, NASCAR fan from Florida- this is MY kind of bar. Cheap drinks, trashy decor, and a fun-loving crowd of good people.
Went on a Friday night and the place was PACKED- but no cover and friendly bouncers. After wading through a crowd to get to the back of the place, we finally found an empty spot to stand. I was very surprised at the amount of draft beers available, and they had some great specials on bottled beers as well. 
We lucked out and grabbed a table as some folks left, and we were surprised to learn that we had a server who would take our drink orders for us! How awesome is that! You didn't have to get up from the table and wade through a crowd to order drinks, she just got our order, and was back within 2 minutes with a refill of delicious beer. I loved that.
We ended up inviting a few guys to sit at our table with us since we had the extra room, and made some new friends while sharing some drinks. The live music was pretty good, and the crowd was well behaved and having a good time. Pair that with cheap drinks, great service, and a laid-back trashy atmosphere, and it equals a fun night out on the town. I had a blast here, Highly recommended- especially if you can come out on a weeknight when the crowds aren't bad, but even when it's packed, it's still a blast.

The building is beautiful, and I really appreciate everything that the owners did to try to revive an important piece of Nashville history. The staff is friendly and the cocktails are good too. Here's the but... The food is not up to par. The first time I visited they were on a limited menu so I got a cup of gumbo and bussels sprouts. The sprouts were not cooked enough. They had a little char but we're hard as rocks and the gumbo tasted like they put too much filè in it. All I could taste was sassafras. YUCK. The second time I came for happy hour. The drink was great and the bar tender was a doll, but the cheese curds I snacked on were not cooked all the way. The breading was under whelming and under cooked, they were not warm inside and several hadn't melted at all. The sauce on top was only okay. Unfortunately, experience won't make up for bad food.
After catching a live act downstairs, plow through the crowds and catch a view on the rooftop.

Since I live around the corner, I am worried how successful this place is going to get and it will be a huge success, because it's absolutely wonderful!  The owner renovated the interior maintaining its historical significance during Nashville's Civil Rights movement.  And the food is fantastic - at least what my friends and I have had thus far!  Crispy fried chicken livers (light on the exterior; rich interior!), fried flounder (great sauce), hearty brussel sprouts (except can the restaurants not come up with something new!), and great biscuits!  I should also say their bar seems top notch; at least the Manhattan I had was!  Food prices are great; bar prices standard.  Enjoy!

So this was quite the throwbacks for me.  Stopped in for lunch last Sunday before leaving for the airport.  Sat at the counter and got fast and friendly service.  My server recommended the sweet potato pancakes and they did not disappoint.  There was live piano music playing in the background, which made for a pleasant backdrop.  There are TVs playing and ample space for diners, whether at the counter or tables.  The place also sells some souvenirs but it's a small portion of the place, nothing obstructive or intrusive.  

Overall, I enjoyed my visit and trip back down memory lane.
Lousy OVERPRICED food & drink, but usually great music. Whether it's worth waiting in line online to purchase tickets or outside the club to get in is still to be determined........

Had a blast here! The bar was crowded with people who were happy and having a great time! The bartender was extremely attentive. The band playing was fun and engaging...didn't want our time there to end!

I tried to make reservations a week before my trip to Nashville, but was unable to log on at the right time.  So on Saturday night, we took our chances and went to try to get into the 5:30 doortime.  We got there at 4:30, and it was just the right time.   They only were taking up to 20 people for the unreserved seats, and we were like 17 and 18!  We were so excited to get in!!  Had no idea who the performers were before that night...it didn't matter, because they were all excellent.  Such great songwriters....and really loved a couple of the performers.  They had one girl come up to do a song, who has just released a song that's being played on "The Highway" on Sirius XM....her name is Kelsey K, 16 years old, and could be the next Taylor Swift.  I'm not kidding.  Check her out....amazing singer.   I did not care for the food on the menu, ended up ordering some veggies and hummus and truly thought the hummus was about the most tasteless I've ever had.  The waitresses were attentive though with a full house, and drinks were fine.  I don't think anyone goes for the food...we were hungry though and wanted something.   I think they could improve on it a bit considering the profit they must be pulling in every night.   The intimate experience was well worth it...so glad we took a chance of getting in.

Tootsies is a must see while in Nashville! Awesome music on every floor. Drinks are still expensive however I am ok paying a little more when I am entertained. People and staff were friendly, crowd was a little older (very few college kids). We felt very safe there unlike some other bars.

This place had a fun atmosphere and lots of history had taken place there. This is one of the places we wanted to visit while on our honeymoon. The music was great and the drinks were reasonably priced. It was a three story bar that had a music entertainer on every floor and the crowd there was fun. The only thing that was not cool was the fact that one of the bartenders would come around asking if we needed anything, we let her know we needed water and she never brought them. She then came around again and asked what we would like to drink, well my husband and I were already drinking beer just needed water. We let her know for the second time we wanted waters, never brought them. She came for the third time and asked the same question. Guess she never got the hint we were thirsty and for the third time didn't bring them. It's not a huge deal but pretty annoying. Other than that we'd return again.

Point of service is critical to any business, and if you can't take an order every 30 seconds with a line out the door... well you suck.  

I waited in line what seemed over 30 minutes with about 20 to 25 people infront of me.  If someone isn't teady, just say "next" like Frau Farbissina from Austin Powers screaming "Scott". They should open another register.  

I also git cut by a bunch of groupie chick's who inserted themselves with their boy toys. I didn't want to say anything and cause a fight, but there should be some sort of security with a line like this.  Fights start this way.  

The food here is decent,  but not worth the wait.  I'm sure there's another place that can fill your arteries with grease at 2am.

Good music. Food.....Meh. Fun roof top with great views. Mercedes was a great waitress. Drinks were good, prices not horrific. Our only problem was with their rule that the outside heaters do not get turned on until 4:30! Well, iI'm sorry we were cold at 4pm!  EXCUSE US!   That is ridiculous.  Our waitress made it happen and we were thankful but the gentleman that turned it on did ask us where we were from and insisted that we shouldn't be cold because we were from a northern state and it was 55 degrees in Nashville.   As if there is a cut off for a certain time or temperature that we are allowed to be cold!!!!

The atmosphere was very hip, but the service was lacking. We didn't get menus or even a greeting until more than 10 minutes after we sat down... and it was not very busy. The food was okay for the prices but nothing to rave about.  But then again, I'm a little bit over the whole hipster scene, and this place is definitely more about being cool and trendy than good service and food. However, the biscuits with pear compote were good. I'm thinking this place might be better at night as a bar or music venue rather than brunch. Maybe I'll go back for a show and drinks sometime.
Roaches crawling around like they own the place! But other than that it is cheap, greasy, food you can get after a night of drinking in Nashville.

Mngmt has decided to change policy from FUN to RUDE. Staff security hassle anyone not sitting at bar or table yet they keep letting people in. Also, new bartenders offer 1/2 size or watered down drinks. I bring everyone who visits over past 5 yrs & have seen decline firsthand. Saw people leave for same reasons last nite. They came out grumbling about treatment by staff. We had one drink & left. Spent money elsewhere.

Music is great, but can't figure out why the board of health doesn't shut them down .  Ladies bathroom is intolerable, while some attendant helps a young patron who consumed too much get sick. Line out the door to use the facilities, but employees get to jump in front of everyone.  And some pseudo security guard watching all of this.  Go for the music.....but beware!

This past Friday, I gathered a few friends in hopes of doing something different and going to the Wilson County Fair. Well some of my friends were less than thrilled about the idea of driving to Lebanon to eat corn dogs and funnel cake, so I said "Ok, I'm in for something else if we pick somewhere unique and fun that I have not been." My friend Amber suggested Sutler and even made the bold claim that it was her favorite bar in town. 

Amber really needs to get on yelp, because I thought her raving review was spot on!  We started upstairs for a drink and dinner. For dinner, I had a delicious grilled cheese with tomato soup. The waitress suggested it over the other two sandwiches I was debating, and she was right! It had four kinds of cheese and bacon. But the tomato soup and pesto sauce were my favorite part!  My husband got the brick chicken and enjoyed it as well, but it seems those of us that got the hot chicken bite appetizers and grilled cheese sandwiches were a little more impressed with our meals. 

After dinner, we went to the downstairs bar where there was a totally different speakeasy type vibe. If you are just going for drinks, I would definitely recommend the downstairs. The drink menu is the same as upstairs just with a more unique atmosphere! I had the Melrose Mule and another cocktail with blackberry moonshine that were both excellent but also not insanely overpriced like many places around town have become. I mean you pay $8- $10 for a drink here, but it will actually be worth it in my opinion. They also have a great beer and wine selection.

Sounds like many of the complaints about this place come with the parking. We actually took an Uber from home knowing that we would each have a few cocktails, so it seems our $7 Uber from home was well worth not having to pay valet or hunt for a spot. 

I will definitely be going back to Sutler. I though it was the perfect spot for a group of friends. It had enough variety on the menu to please everyone, and the two different floors allow you to change up the atmosphere as if you are headed to two different places.

Rachel Baker is awesome. They took great care of us at Paradise Park. So much fun great music, great drinks, great food, and Great Times, I brought a friends bachelor party down and they were awesome  to us we had a blast everyone should come here when they go to Nashville. Broadway Royalty.

I LOVE that I finally fit in a visit to The Well.  I really enjoyed the coffee I had  - the Mayan Mocha, with almond milk.  I'm very looking forward to see what other concoctions The Well has to offer.  Especially because... they seriously have every Monin syrup known to man.  I am not exaggerating, take a look for yourself... they have EVERY FLAVOR in existence!

The Well has a couple of cute 'n attractive T-shirts I'd like to buy at some point, as well as coffee beans for sale.  I think a really big attraction of The Well is the ambience - it was so peaceful, comfortable.  I sat in a comfy couch, and there are plenty of tables and chairs.  There's no rushed feeling.  

Of course, I was there at 8p at night.  Oh! And that leads me to mention that they're open 'til 10.  Wish they were open right now (at 1a)...

I'll just say it - this place is weird.  I like the classic feel but not the modern pricing.  The food simply doesn't live up to it.  I had the pork chop, it was ok, not anything special.  We had multiple servers, multiple people stop by and ask us if everything was ok (before food arrived), even gentleman wearing dishwashing aprons came by to interrupt our conversation.  I get it, this place is new.  But I don't know, just an awkward dining experience overall that will prevent me from returning.

I attended a winter onsie party this place hosted and I had a blast! I appreciate the lively experience they facilitated. The drinks were good and the service decent. I didn't try any food while I was there so I'm not sure how it is.

I am only basing this review on on a server we had. My group was not here for the music or club scene so that doesn't count for me. This was our first stop in Nashville and we heard this place was great and honestly we were hungry so we'd go anywhere at that point. I do not remember the girl we had as a server but she was nasty. We ordered some appetizers. We ordered 3 waters and my other friend ordered an alcoholic beverage. The alcoholic beverage was wayyy too watered down so my friend told the bartender/server thinking she would either fix it or recommend something else. Instead the girl just said, "That's just the way it is." and walked away. We finally got our food - which took forever and it wasn't even busy there... it was 11am. The food was mediocre at best. Even after we got our food, we STILL never received the 3 waters so we were all eating and dying of thirst. This server would keep disappearing and finally she came back and we asked her if we could have our waters now and some napkins. So what did she do? She walked back to the bar and helped other people. Hello?!?!?! One of the girls in our group finally just got up and found some napkins and brought them over herself. What a terrible experience... I definitely would not recommend or go back to this place. FYI: We never got the waters. We went elsewhere for a soda.

Well I've been told by a few friends that this place has the best burger in town.  Well I tried it,  let me say it was a good burger and I would eat it again.  But it was far from the best Nashville has to offer.   The buns was awful though,  it actually broke in my hands.  (Very stale)  I did not go to the venue side, but the venue side smell came to me.  With that said I will probably give this burger another go, I'll just hope for a better bun and dive bar smells never scared me.

Beyond disappointed !!! I came here tonight to have a great time for my little sisters 21st birthday. I was ided, let in. Mind you I'm from California. My boyfriend hands them his id, also from California,and the SHERIFF had the audacity to say "Oh I know your type, are you even LEGAL, is one of those IDs your green card." Let me just say my boyfriend is Colombian. He is an American citizen. I can not believe this is 2017 and he is being labeled as an illegal because of the color of his skin. No! This is not ok ! I am half white half Mexican even though I look white. Why was I not harassed?  Because of the color of my skin? What type of establishment is being ran here??? The manager whose slim with glasses did nothing ! Instead when told how out of line the comment was, he had security push my boyfriend out to the street. If you are Mexican do not come here ! You will be discriminated against and have security used for the wrong reasons. The message was told to us loud and clear today what Tootsies REPRESENTS. So disappointed tootsies. You DISGUST me! I will NEVER be back!

A certain kind of woman's paradise for sure, but that woman is me. I came to Paradise Park looking for a relaxing evening for one after a past few days of too much honky tonking and networking. 

Paradise Park contains, among other things: gross carpet, a bit of a smoke smell, an old car, and some old  television parts. In other words, it's basically my grandfather's basement. I figured this would be a laid back, less crowded place and while I was right, this certainly does not mean it was not fun. I ended up having an unexpected blast, rocking out to the cover band  that refused to play country and watching people of all types dance like crazy with enough room to do so. I didn't try try the food but  Paradise Park had a decent amount of drafts and a super friendly staff. I was told it gets pretty crowded on weeknights, but on a quiet Wednesday, this disgustingly carpeted place was full of good times with plenty of breathing room.

But II hope I didn't breathe too much of the mildew from the green carpet. 

...I know. I'm obsessing. I spent the first portion of my night here alone-plenty of time to concentrate on the carpet. 

...I wrote a yelp talk thread trying to find out the name of this place, because yes, I had such a good time, I didn't bother to learn the name. Nobody remembers the carpet so I really hope I'm not dreaming it. How could I?

...I'll stop complaining. If the carpet does indeed exist, please don't get rid of it, I won't know how to get back otherwise. :(

Bar tender ignored me for over 5 minutes. No she wasn't busy with guests. I ordered a beer from tap. She pured a large one and charged me without offering the shorter one. Which I wanted. Trying to build her sales, but she screwed her tip!

Great place until security without no reason took my gf out by the neck, what type of place drags women out like that, I will make sure that place never does that to women ever again, that's abusive and discriminative.

I have waited years to go to The Bluebird Cafe. It needs no introduction. The intimate space and talent that they book converted my friend who does not care about music (I know who doesn't like music - well here is one) who came with me to buy the album on iTunes and listened to the album for days. Of course I bought souvenirs. The food is very average and the service from the server was below average. She knew what she was doing but didn't want to do it anymore; "it" meaning serving.
We stopped in on a Thursday afternoon for a beer. We loved the music playing and lively atmosphere. A great spot!

We enjoyed our visit!! There are 3 floors with 3 different bands even at 11a. The fried pickles were delicious but the drinks were kind of small for $9. Over all, enjoyed our time and the roof top bar, even in the rain!

A great experience for our group.  We walked and it was so packed you could barely squeeze your way through, but once you get to the second and third floors there is more space to breathe.  The second we walked in though, the bartenders were asking what we wanted to drink.  Everywhere we went there, bartenders were asking if we needed anything.  They have live music on every level and it is REALLY REALLY good.  Band's closer to midnight are so talented its unbelievable.  If you can't have some drinks and enjoy your time here their is something wrong with you.  TV's to watch games are on.  Did not try any food, don't even know if they have it, but probably do.  Drinks were expensive like every other bar on a weekend night in Nashville.  Totally worth it and a lot of fun.

Hands down best bar tender service (they WILL spot you and get you a drink ASAP) and stiffest drinks of all downtown (can't go wrong with a $7 "mixed" drink you have to choke down... I love it).  Double bands are great too, though the band in the front of the house always seems to be better.

Can get way too crowded for its own good, but still a fun spot.  Also, way too touristy.  But meh, what cha gonna do.

The iconic Tootsie's Lounge. It's a 3-story dive bar with a very unique crowd. It gets really crowded, it was packed on Saturday but was a lot better on Tuesday. 

It's a little pricey for what it is but so is everything on Broadway. 

One tip: bartender told us they charge the same ($9) for any whiskey and mixer, but if you just say whiskey and coke they'll give you house. I found that to be beneficial so we started ordering the good stuff haha. 

This place is really cool to come and check out and say you've been there.  The live music usually consists of 3 different bands, one on each floor which is really cool and best of all, it's free.

Great bar in Nashville! Truly lives up to its name. Three floors of live music. One night we went Kid Rock made a late night appearance!!!
Sub par bar food- but no one goes there for the food. However, I have heard there are a few items that are great after a few too many. People go there for the live music, lively atmosphere, and good times. This was the bar we normally started our night off and ended it at. Always packed, but a stop you must make when on Broadway!

Does a mans heart good to see such musical joy. Four song writers performing and raising money for an area hospice.  Good local IPA brew and tasty seasoned chicken fingers with fries.  Touching evening. Highly recommended.

Word of advice - be patient to wait in line, it will be a long wait, but it's fun.  If you're with someone, take turns going across the street to get something to drink/eat.  Also, if it's a first come, first serve night, hope you are within the first 100 to get in.

Once you're in, find a seat and take it! There is a minimum food/drink order, but that's no problem.  Enjoy the show, it's all about the experience and to say I've been there is pretty awesome.

Yes, if you watch Nashville, you'll see parts of the club where they shot.

Front door person was so rude!! "What you don't know you need a reservation!" She needs to be replaced!! Someone more friendly needs to be greeting. $50 later in Uber rides to be treated so rudely. You maybe popular, but doesn't give you permission be rude. Be grateful,humble & thankful!!

So much history here. We loved the musicians on each floor doing their own thing. Being there gives you such an appreciation for Nashville and all the musicians that have played there. I definitely recommend this spot when you're out there.

I don't think I will go out of my way to go to The Stone Fox....actually, I might go out of my way to avoid.  

Good: Seated quickly at the bar during a seemingly busy brunch hour

Bad: Food.  Bland and underseasoned.  I ordered a BLT with an egg.....underwhelming and was left thinking about my next meal.

Ugly: Sanitary practices.  I asked for a lemon for my water.  The bartender, who had been touching all of the random surfaces, dirty plates from other customers, and writing utensils......just reaches with her bare hands into the lemon container and just hands it to me (like a hand to hand transfer).  Needless to say, I was grossed out and didn't want the lemon anymore.
This dump is way overrated and over-hyped and not worth the effort of standing in line. You are far better off enjoying the various venues on lower Broadway!

The fox is an odd place... Trying entirely too hard to appear as if they're not trying at all. From the kitschy decor, to the apathetic staff gliding around oozing general disdain... This place wants so badly to be "authentic" it makes one almost feel bad for it.

We dropped in on Sunday morning and joined the small crowd gathered at the doors awaiting their opening. We were quickly seated at a repurposed diner table and promptly were assaulted with entirely-too-loud hank Williams by a hipster Lou Diamond Phillips look-alike manning two old record players on the stage. It's 10am and we struggled to speak over the din, having to yell out order to the server. 

We politely asked that it be turned down a touch so we didn't have to shout. Lou Diamond Hipster dropped it a hair, then slowly bumped it back up even louder. We eventually retreated back to the bar to get away from the speakers. It helped, somewhat. 

In general, the staff were very disconnected and borderline rude, harboring a "too cool to be bothered" attitude that doesn't jive with their choice to work in the service industry. 

The food... Solid but unspectacular. I had the chicken and waffles, and was served a couple chunks of dry white meat heavily battered and fried past done. The waffle was average, helped by tech yolk spilling from the optional egg atop it. My girlfriend's BLT was solid, propped up by a couple slices of their excellent local bacon. Another in our party raved about the fried french toast. 

Their Bloody Mary mix is house made, and excellent. 

The decor and concept has promise... But IMO it misses the mark. I've been to many places along these lines that execute the Idea much more effectively. 

I would be remiss to not mention the sanitation issues we saw behind the bar and around the main room in general. We were not afforded a look into the kitchen, but I fear it matching the upkeep of the bar area. 

We won't be back.

Out of all the Broadway bars, I had the most fun here and I'm not a country fan!  I like Division street way way more but this bar was so friendly and felt inclusive.  I know Broadway can be a total tourist trap but this felt so much more approachable and enjoyable than honky tonk.  Solid drinks and great crowd

I am pleased to report that Nashville has a truly interesting, affordable and delicious restaurant added to the downtown scene. I thought that the theme would be somewhat gimmicky: an old Woolworth's with an historic lunch counter now turned into a slick contemporary upscale diner. But I think they really pulled it off. The whole space is open and bright, but comfortable and warm. Staff was exceptional, from the bartenders, valet, hosts and servers. We had appetizers and craft cocktails, all reasonably priced and delicious. The deviled eggs are made with smoked trout and they are excellent. Salads were also excellent. We had fried chicken dinners and the fresh fish of the day, a blackened cobia served over succotash. The cobia received raves from our table mates and the chicken was what a fried chicken dinner is supposed to be: Very moist half chicken fried in pieces, very crispy and flavorful. The chicken was served with mashed potatoes, creamy and buttery (no gravy). It is also served with stewed green beans, great flavor with a nice peppery bite, as well as mac and cheese, pretty traditional with a little bit of heat from some red chiles. 
Although there were pricier items on the menu, including a couple of steak entrees and pork chops, the half chicken dinner is under 20 dollars. The menu is varied but not overly ambitious. There are several vegetarian and gluten free options, for those of you high-maintenance types (I'm not talking about you, Alex). 
It is clear to me that the chef is trying and succeeding at taking diner and bistro standards, cooking, serving and pricing them just right. Nice job!
This bar is so fun, bands are always on point, but beware of the crazy bathroom attendant!! She should be fired. She's nasty to everyone that uses her bathroom.

Hate to do this, but....it's no Red Rocks.  But nothing is, really.  I'm forever spoiled for any other outdoor venues.

However, this is a nice little venue and beats the heck out of a corporate mega-arena.  The grounds were really nice (would have loved to see them in the daylight) and there are lots of trees and cricket/cicada noises to add to "the woods" ambiance.  And hiking trails too!

When we were here for Sigur Ros, the entire grass area was general admission.  Because we were traveling, we weren't properly equipped with lawn chairs and the like but luckily had a blanket to sit on.  If you do opt to not bring chairs, be sure to get there early and get a seat where the ground is somewhat sloped.  Seating is also somewhat willy nilly (no defined rows) so make sure you have a landmark before you venture out to the restroom or you might not find your way back.  Speaking of restrooms, these ones were strange.  All porta-potties, but an oddly permanent inside sink set up outside set-up.  At any rate, your trip to the restroom is guaranteed to be an adventure!

Beer selection was surprisingly decent.  The food looked terrible, but that's par for the course at an outside venue with no actual kitchen.  Be sure to have snack in your car as you may have to wait a bit to leave (we were in the car for close to an hour afterwards).

Another nice feature would be a screen to better see the performers.  Because the ground is relatively flat and we didn't arrive as early as we had hoped, it was hard to see.  And finally, smoking seem to be permissible throughout the entire seating area.  I get that it's outside, but a bit of a shock for me.

But really, you can't beat seeing one of your favorite bands in "the woods."

Can't speak to anything at Tootsie's other than the awesome band that happened to be playing the night we were passing through Nashville. We made our way to the top floor where the band was rocking. Although it was pretty packed, we managed to push our way towards the stage and ended up right in front of the lead singer. Once we established our space on the dance floor, we had a blast singing and dancing to every song. The band did a great job balancing country music, which Nashville is obviously known for, with other genres. We only ordered one drink while we were at Tootsie's for fear of losing our spots in front of the band and the drink was average strength and average price for Broadway.

I always have a good experience when I come to The Sutler. The vibe is trendy-but-not-too-trendy. It's nice that this place isn't located in the hub-bub of hipster Nashville. The food is great and the drinks are delicious! I'm a fan of the Guacamole Trio (appetizer) and the Melrose Mule (drink). The tacos are great too! On Thursday nights, they have a "live karaoke" band where you get to sing with the band...lyrics are on a screen. It's fun and oh so entertaining! If you sit at the front of the restaurant (near the windows), the live music isn't obtrusive. The Sutler is kid-friendly, but don't worry, it's not ever packed with little ones! (I have a 4-year old and a 7-year old that come for the kids' mac-n-cheese!) Parking can be a challenge, but there's valet available at the corner.

So this place is famous, and a lot of people stop in because of that. And just like those other people, I was drawn in by the allure of fame. Once inside, I realised that they didn't have good drinks or good drink specials. Adding insult to injury, they had no (or at least no local) beer. Thanks, but no thanks. The music is good, but they have 2 live bands playing at the same time and that is confusing. There are plenty of bar choices on Broadway. Stop in, if you love the band playing, stay, if you don't, keep walking.

The Bluebird is awesome and worth the wait in the long lines to get in. I would give it a five except for the lines. It would be nice if they just sold tickets so people didn't have to wait for hours.

We arrived around 4pm for a 7:30 show (doors at 6:30) and the line was already about 10-15 deep. The walkway where you wait isn't entirely shaded, so it can be quite hot and sweaty. 

All that being said, once you're in, the Bluebird is charming and has a great ambience. The staff is friendly and fun. The music is excellent and you get a lot of it.

They have a nice drink selection. The food menu is minimal, but everything we had was good. Homemade potato chips are highly recommended!

Ok, honestly our server was the tits. We had a party of 10, waited for 2 hours like hey told us, but when we followed up, it was at least another hour to get a table. 3 hour wait is insane. So our bar / cocktail waitress told us we could eat in her section (on the couch). Back to the 2 star rating though...the food.  I may be kind of a diva but I HATE Luke warm food. The fried pickles were awesome, and their bacon was be best I have ever had. But everything else was barely warm. And again, we were a party of 10. So I'm sure it's hard to time it all. But I swear they didn't even try....Did I mention the waitress was amazing (blonde, cute up do, wearing black lipstick?), ....But if you've come here for great food it's not worth a 3 hour wait. It's not worth a 45 min wait. Drinks,atmosphere and a social encounter with the staff is our experience.

Food exists here. There are things you can put in your mouth and chew on.

Will you like that food?

No. 

Why?

It is disgusting. We got terrible chicken fingers and a grilled cheese sandwich. I sent my grilled cheese back.

Read that again. I sent a grilled cheese sandwich back. The reason, yes you guessed it, they forgot the cheese. 

You have to work hard to screw up a grilled cheese sandwich. 

Next, the buffalo chicken tenders taste like they were still using yesterday's fry oil. I think leaving this menu item there will suffice.

My advice? Go somewhere else your conscience and colon will thank you.
Awesome vibe. Terrific upbeat staff. Live music at brunch. What more could you want? Amazing food! Yep. They have that. And Bloody Mary of which one dreams!

My wife and I spent almost 6 hours here yesterday! We had a blast!  We are back today! Again same upbeat have fun vibe with great music! We particularly like the band that played in the afternoon with John Stone.   If you are visiting Nashville do yourself a favor and run to this place!

Voted by our entire family of 5 as the best meal in Nashville. Something for every person on the menu and the flavors.... oh my gosh .... my very picky tastebuds were super happy. 

It just tasted like the food was actually crafted with thought and love instead of cranked out for the tourist crowd. The chef has done an amazing job of keeping a simple menu with phenomenal tastes. 

The building itself is lovingly restored and the staff were all kind and attentive. Sivon, our waitress was so kind! Food runner Zack made sure the kids were fed first - so important! 

Sweet potato pancakes were AMAZING. The biscuits were also our fave of the trip. Husband said the fried chicken was also best of the trip (he ate fried chicken all over the state). 

Special note to the proprietor.... it was amazing and refreshing to see the love in restoring this special place. As the city gets more and more modern, it was beautiful to walk into a restored place of history that was obviously curated with love and attention. Beautifully done.

Place has great history went there for breakfast corn beef hash was great I really enjoyed the seafood gumbo the sweet potato pancakes were surprisingly very good we were unsure if we wanted them or would like them and when we got them we weren't disappointed I definitely suggest checking out the Woolworth

The food is pretentious and over priced. They've tried to make upscale diner food without success. The fried chicken was nothing special and the mashed potatoes were the worst I've ever eaten. They had a chemical taste. The green beans were also strangely flavored. The bf had the shrimp and grits and said the grits were bland. The only reason I'm giving 3 stars is because of the excellent and friendly service and my best friend's complicated order. .

As a fan of Nashville the TV show I was very excited that we were able to make reservations at the Bluebird! I read reviews as well as their website that tell you how small the cafe is but it was much smaller even than I expected! There is not a bad seat in the place and you better be ready to sit close to your neighbors. Fun time, good prices, and Sarah was a great server!

My friend found this place because of their $15 bottomless mimosas and wow are we glad!!!! The atmosphere of this place screams Music City!! The stage with a bluegrass band and the boots on the wall! Take a hike to the restroom and enjoy the country-retro mixed with bar-vibes decor!!! Everything is very well randomly put together and it's Amazing!!! 

After you freshen-up.... get ready for the challenge of deciding what to order! Everything sounds and looks delicious--- you truly can't yo wrong!! I had the breakfast tacos --- that salsa! My friend had the breakfast sandwich -- an oldie, but a goodie!! And my partner had the chicken fried chicken -- stick to your ribs yumminess!!!

The service was great! You rarely see the bottom of a mimosa because their constantly asking if you need a refill.... and trust me, ya Do! My only minor complaint is the tightness of the 2 community tables-- but people gotta eat!

Four of us ate lunch here yesterday after touring the Country Music Hall of Fame a few blocks away. The history of the place lured us there and we were definitely not disappointed. They did a nice job of updating the restaurant while honoring the style of mid 20th century Nashville. Our server was obviously quite proud of the place and seemed to come alive with information when we asked questions about the peaceful demonstrations staged there during the civil rights movement. 
Oh, and the food was excellent!!! Highly recommended.

Although it's a tourist trap, it still contains some magic. I recommend checking it out if you appreciate music. Just close your eyes and listen to the artists stories. Some acts are hit and miss, but if you get lucky enough to catch folks like Tony Arata or some other great writers, then you're in for a treat.... That is if you can actually get in.... 

SET YOUR ALARM BEFORE 8 AM AND WITH MULTIPLE DEVICES TRY TO GET A RESERVATION ONLINE FOR A SHOW THE FOLLOWING WEEK!!! There are thousands of folks just waiting online to snatch up seats, so be ready and be quick. Know the seating chart before hand!

Had the honor of catching an intimiate show at the world-famous Bird on my last trip to Nashville. Initially I was expecting more of a bar-scene, but was suprised when I realized it was just that, a cafe. A very personal setting where I got to literally sit right behind the performers. Now, I'm not a country music fan, but I very much enjoyed this. 'When in Rome.' Or at least 'when in the Athens of the South.'

Mo was an incredible server!! She gave the best local recommendations and was extremely accommodating and helpful with all of our questions. Mo made us feel welcome and made the experience even more enjoyable. Definitely recommend this place for brunch! Amazing food and awesome service!!

It's crazy how you keep a place open when you have an issue with a toilet leak from the 2nd floor pouring down to the first level where people were walking in and it just kept pouring down. After at least an hour of it coming down they closed the first level realizing that it was a sewer issue. Shane on the establishment for staying open and keep people walking through sewer water. It's all about making the money shame on you. I actually have video of this happening and they just kept the place going and the music playing. Totally disgusting!!!

I like to separate my Church and Coffee, and for that, and only that, I'll ding a star off The Well. Discounting that, The Well is a great place to experience some really interesting coffees from around the world, brewed in tender and slow processes (such as Aeropress) to maximize the experience. They have a nice sit-out which, on a cloudy Fall day, or a sunny Spring afternoon, makes a great place to hang out. Free Wi-Fi everywhere makes this an attractive place for students, but I also go there to write at times, and get a break in scenery from the Fido-Frothy Monkey routine!
Great bar with live music! Stays open late. I would recommend trying to get a table on the rooftop, the view of downtown Nashville is amazing! The history alone is worth giving it a go!

Walking into this place, it just feels like Nashville, and it feels good. There's a country band playing, but you don't feel like you have to yell to talk to your friends. We ordered some awesome appetizers, the popcorn blew me away! Great vibe in this joint, they have a super cool downstairs bar that is always packed. In fact, I would definitely suggest making a reservation, cause the Sutler is always busy! I went with my wife on a Tuesday, and it was crazy! We had a good time, especially when the food came out, I ordered the trout and it was kickass. Our waitress was super sweet too. Check it out!!

This was my 2nd time here, and I was definitely disappointed this time around. The first time I was here I had a ton of fun and had a great experience. This time, I brought my husband and it was terrible. First of all, they must've had a speaker wire loose as the music was cutting in and out - to top it off it was also blaring at max volume. So no one could hear each other to try to have a conversation which was disappointing. Secondly, they charged my husband $20 for 2 draft beers. Pretty sure someone else's drinks were put on our tab, it was so loud we didn't bother to have it adjusted. And lastly, it must've been closing time at 10pm on a Sunday because they flipped on the lights and then started turning TVs off with 2 min to go in the football game. I found that incredibly rude as it appeared that they were doing pre-closing type stuff. Waiting a few minutes so we could finish the game would have been appreciated. 

On the bright side. The atmosphere in the bar is really cool, and when they have live music it is really fun. It's a great little dive bar just really disappointed with my latest experience.

A must, must do in Nashville! Super friendly and funny staff - as a party of 8 arriving around 11 AM on a Saturday, we got seated immediately; definitely got lucky, though. When I had called about a week earlier, I was advised to have a party of that size arrive right at opening. 

Bloody Mary bar was fantastic; the bacon was great and all the fixings seemed fresh and continuously replenished. I loved getting to dress up my drink myself! A few at our table had bottomless mimosas which were a hit. The biscuit dishes were highly enjoyed, as well as the breakfast tacos and enchiladas. Smoked brisket hash sounded great but it wasn't a standout. I cleaned my chicken and waffles plate - they were so yummy! The brown sugar butter is super good. 

The live music made everything great and the decor and energy of the place were absolutely perfect! Will definitely come back someday!

(6/21/2014)  So apparently one of the more famous "honky tonks" in Nashville.  Reportedly, some of the early famous first customers were Willie Nelson, Patsy Cline, Mel Tillis, Kris Kristofferson, Waylon Jennings.  Place is right behind the Ryman Auditorium.  We had to stop in, just to stop in.  Got a rail drink and a Bud, for $14, would call that on the high side for prices, but I guess we were downtown.  It was Saturday night, it was crowded, it was loud.  All the surfaces were sticky with booze, as were the drunken and rowdy bachelors and bachelorettes (apparently if you're getting married in a 300 mi radius you have to blow your wad in Nashville??).  I guess all I can say is that I've been to Tootsie's World Famous Orchid Lounge.  Period.

I've been to Stone Fox twice now for brunch, and it's awesome. Every time I am visiting Nashville we make it a point to go to brunch here. There usually isn't a huge line, but it's typically full. This seems to still be a hidden gem brunch spot.

I'm not the biggest Bloody Mary drinker, but I love their Bloody Mary. Definitely worth trying out. They have good Saturday morning deals on mimosas and Bloody Marys.

The food is great, never had something I didn't like. They have a decent selection of items. 

The atmosphere might be the best thing about this place. The stuff on the walls is really cool, including a giant mental hanging of the United States. They have all different tables, chairs, plates, and cups.

I loved how a lot of things were the same like the floor and the counter looked. I took my mother for her birthday to relive old memories for her as a child. I wish we would have seen more pictures of how the place looked in the past on the walls upstairs however the upstairs was mostly about the civil rights movement than the actual restaurant itself. The food was also disappointing we went for Brunch and ordered sides. The gravy was cold the biscuits tased like the kind I make from the freezer section and they didn't have much of a brunch breakfast selection. I also got a Bloody Mary and it was ok. I think Dinner maybe the better choice on when to go for food. Our waiter was nice however he knew nothing about the history of the restaurant or the pictures upstairs only that there was some...

We came to Tootsie's after running the TN Ragnar, I had never been to Nashville before so I was very much looking forward to visiting a few bars in the area.  Tootsies was fun, it of course was packed with people.  We ended up on the top floor where we saw a few good singers but it was chilly from the fans or wind being blown.  We decided to leave because apparently the gentleman MCing was extremely rude to one of my teammates.  I'd probably give it another cautionary shot if I returned to Nashville in my life.

Maybe we came on a bad day but at least for breakfast, would not recommend this place. Service very slow, limited menu, sweet potato pancakes too sweet to eat. Not enough gravy on biscuits, jalopeno bacon burnt. Will need to eat again soon. Is cool for the history.

I cannot praise this establishment enough, especially the service. Shan, our waitress, was phenomenal. Our mimosas never once ran dry. The food was amazing and the attention to detail was impeccable. I definitely recommend the chicken fried chicken biscuits and the biscuits Benedict! Also, request Shan, as she is the best!!!

Freakin Fantastic Honky-Tonk Friday Fun!

SITREP

Something I noticed about the venues in Downtown Nashville along Broadway - they like their levels!

I mean, you can have a music venue on one level, then a full-blown bar on another level, and then a music venue AND bar on a top level.  Sheer size overwhelmnent!

THE BAR

Let's start with the easy stuff - I just defaulted to my go-to of Sam Adams which ran a cool $4, plus a buck for the tip.  After that, things got a lot more complicated...

THE SETUP

And to be honest, I may have been a bit buzzed to know at any given moment EXACTLY what level I was on since I was following my local Nashville buddies around, and like a passenger in the car, you may not be paying attention to where you're "driving to" and "how you're getting there" cause you're too busy looking at "the scenery" along the way!

A CROWD SURFING ADVENTURE

It was like a human ocean, and sometimes you'd get got in the currents and eddies head to the bar, or to the restroom (which is how/why I almost ended up getting sucked into the women's room because I was got into the vortex of 5 blonde rocker chicks - had to "extract" myself....).

IT'S A SMALL WORLD

Back to the stage, oh my god, the scenery!  I don't know why we eventually left the room where all the girls were dancing in front of the band, behind the band, and AMIDST the band members (oh wait, I was WITH girls, that's why), but that was just fun to see!  

And crowded!  It was virtual rainbow land of Asian women, African-American women, Caucasian women, all emblazoned in different dance attire, shaking their booties to Def Leppard, then Nine Inch Nails, and then the bands' own country tunes.  It was amazeballs! 

LOST AGAIN

This place is HUGE to the first-time stranger, with it's labyrinth of halls and stairs, kinda like an Escher Bach sketch where you may not really be leaving the floor you thought you were.  

When we were walking through 1st level (but I think, it COULD have been the 2nd Level if that's the level the bathrooms are on - and THEN if you're trying to orient yourself from the rear entrance - where we came in - that's not necessarily the same as the ground level from the front entrance), it was like a roller-coaster ride since we kept going UP, and then DOWN, and then UP, and then DOWN again as we were crossing over one dance pit, then to another .  See my confusion?

ADDITIONAL DISCOMBULATION

We would go outside after haggling with the back security guard so that we could be assured we'd get back inside.  [He was a bit distracted at the time too since he could not find his smartphone.]  The girls were taking a smoking break in the back alley and after an hour we corralled everyone back up, and mosied through the back door into Tootsies to THEIR back door where our awesome Nashville hosts - Chris, Nickie and Marti - worked their magic and got us in.

THE BANDS

I listened to 3 throughout my Tootsie adventures and they were definitely strong in the countrified rock and honky-tonk genres, but very gifted in parlaying their talents towards Heavy Metal and Industrial.  

THE LOWDOWN

A most excellent musical rodeo ride in Downtown Nashville!

This place was awesome to go to. Alex was probably the coolest bartender, and made our group feel welcomed to the city. Bob franklin really has a great running business. If you like a great atmosphere, and a staff that matches that you'll have to go there.

I'm a wing snob and approve of these! The sauce was spicy, tangy and the wings had a good crispiness to them. They were also super saucy and not dry, which I loathe! Most of the menu items sound delicious, too. Service was friendly and next time I am in Nashville, I'd come here at night to check out the live music!
Everything (Music, Food, Staff, Song Writers) about this place was phenomenal. We definitely enjoyed our time here.

Tootsies hires individuals who impersonate officers and carried concealed weapons without a license ?! What a responsible establishment you folks have been running. We were contacted by the "head of security" and were reinsured that "this officer" would be talked to after the incident that occurred earlier this year. How ironic that it comes out this man has been IMPERSONATING AN OFFICER and Tootsies continued to allow it! Justice has been served! May he gets what he deserves and may Tootsies step up and actually provide a safe establishment to their guests.

I am impressed by their commitment to their patrons experience. After having a less than acceptable experience I was contacted by the GM whom offered a sincere apology and was genuinely interested to know more about my visit. He was courteous and listened well. 

If you like cheap drinks, mullets on the walls, and live music to fill your ears this is the place to come. Did I mention it's also a great place to fill your belly full of tater tots?
Great variety of old country and classic rock.  Very fun place to hang out and get the party started.
I came because of the series Nashville but I would return on its own accord.. This place is amazing and quaint! Small and intimate it's the perfect venue and everything sold was very reasonable.

It's a very nice coffeehouse. It has a wide open space and a nice patio. I got the Mocha an it was very good. What makes the place pretty awesome is the profits from sales go to help stop poverty and underprivileged areas.

This is still one of the best places in Nashville.  Good food and good beer selection. Friendly service and the atmosphere is fun with awesome decor.  The parking is starting to be a problem though which sucks because that was always a big reason we would go.  Hopefully that gets fixed.

We decided to go here, like many I am sure, because the wife saw this place on that Nashville show.  

First of all....GET A RESERVATION!  We walked past a line of people that I am sure never got in because they did not have reservations.  During the shows I didn't actually see anyone leave.  So once again....GET A RESERVATION!  Getting a reservation is pretty easy.  Just follow the directions on their website for when you want to go and you are in.

They had a very nice drink selection.  We both had some craft beers that we enjoyed.  The food was good too.  I expected some gimmicky bar food, but it was much more than that.  Really good food options.  

If you have never seen that Nashville show, like me, and you just enjoy real people playing music so close they bump your table....this place is a must.  I thoroughly enjoy singer/ songwriter shows and the "in the round" show is just amazing.  This place is a must for music lovers.
Avoid the bartender who looks like she's on steroids, she becomes perplexed when it doesn't involve a juice a monkey concoction !

Hey-you know why you came... to see the walls, autographs and listen to the bands. Good in that respect. Kinda grungie and no way wanted to check out the bathroom but for 1 beer it was worth the experience

We went for brunch and were told it was going to be an hour wait, which it was. In the meantime we had bottomless mimosas, which are pre-made and honestly I had 4 and I don't think there was much champagne in them. The atmosphere is great, the bluegrass band was very entertaining. The food was nothing to write home about. Nothing bad in particular, but I probably won't be returning back here.

Not sure how I haven't reviewed Tootsie's yet since it is a Nashville staple. However, it's also a tourist trap and I cannot stand it. Every time that I've been there, it has been crazy packed (no surprise) and I can't even enjoy the fact that I'm there because I'm packed like a sardine in a can. The musical acts I've seen there are pretty decent, which is expected. However, the staff seems incredibly overwhelmed all the time, thus putting them in a bad mood. I tend to avoid this bar but I guess ya gotta experience it just once to say "I've been to Tootsie's"!
Obsessed!!! The food- atmosphere- and wait staff were amazing.  I can't wait to come back.

The service was very good, the food and setting was average. I was not happy when I got the bill and found out they were charging $2 for rocks (aka ICE) in my bourbon! Bottom line: extremely overpriced for what you're getting and I wouldn't come back.
Great food along with an amazing vibe reminiscent of the classic 1960s restaurant. Love the nostalgic video and movie screen showing clips from the era.
Great music and pretty good appetizers. Not amazing but a great atmosphere to grab a bite to eat and listen to live music. A good experience overall. Glad we found it.
Really great wide ranging music experience with heart.  It's on the strip and worth it.

This place has a really good Happy Hour. Half off drinks! You can never pass that up. I tried my friend food she had the grill cheese and it came with some tomato soup. When I tell you that soup was sooooooooo good! I have to order it the next time I visit.

We love The Sutler! We really love that it's off the beaten path. The space is really nice, good seating for all to see the show going on as opposed to all Broadway honkey tonks. Drink selection is really good. Do not recommend the nachos, too small. The walk down to the restrooms has a bunch of hanging cowboy boots which was really cool! Also connects to a pool hall downstairs.

The hamburgers at Paradise Park are GREAT!  Tastes like a burger you would make at home.  All the toppings are fresh and the meat is MEAT.  I highly recommend this place.  It looks like a dump from the street, but the food is so so good.  I am so glad we decided to eat here. as it was our last day in Nashville.
I went here for brunch today and the food was amazing. Crisp bacon, scrambled eggs, creamy grits, soft French toasted bread and a special complementary bowl of hash!!!!!!
