Great meatloaf!  Server said crazy busy weekend so they were out of mashed potatoes and ingredients for signature cocktails.   50-50 chance we would go back again.  Suppose the build up from reviews and recommendations from others set our expectations too high.

First time there and have to say I was not disappointed. My son told me that some famous artists occasionally just show up there. Boy was he right!  After Brad left I went upstairs and listened to this great band covering everything from Garth Brooks to Led Zeppelin to Sublime and everything in between.  It's a must visit if you're in Nashville.

I am not one for negative reviews and especially not one to put down a bartender or server of any sort. Last night was an exception. As I was waiting to get a drink for my two friends and I, one of the bartenders had to ask what I wanted three different times in a three minute time span. He was obviously intoxicated and I still remained patient with him. After the first drink he made he took a shot with someone next to me. Still waiting for my other two drinks he took two other girls' drink orders. He made the second drink and had to ask me again for the third drink order. As he was about to make my third drink (or so I thought) there was a man behind me who he knew. The man behind me was talking about how he has better hair then the bartender. The bartender then leaned over so close to my face where I could smell his vile breath and asked me obnoxiously who has "better hair" between them two. I asked where my third drink was (it has been atleast ten minutes now since I first told him my order.) He made me my drink and I gave him my card and told him to close out. He walked down to the cash register where I kept watching him and watched him swipe my card. He then found a bunched up napkin next to him and I watched him throw it at a guy in front of him messing around with him. He then started pouring them shots and I watched him take two shots with them. All during this time he had my card in his hand waving it around. I asked the other bartender to please have him bring me my card. The other bartender was no help and also seemed to be intoxicated. I then asked him where his manager was and he told me he would go get the other bartender. The other bartender came back with my card and I told him I wanted to speak to his manager when he then replied "Why are you in such a bad mood?" And I said "It has taken you 20 minutes to get me a drink." And as I was walking away he called me a "fucking bitch." This was my first drink of the night and it was also my last. I do not associate his post with the whole business as I have been here before and have had great experiences, but this one particular bar tender was very degrading to your business.

Tootsie's is Me and my boyfriends favorite bar in downtown Nashville. They have the best bands, especially on the top floor. It is small but it is wouldn't be the same if they opened it up more. It's very original. Love all of the pictures on the wall ! Katrina is a fiddle player that plays with most of the bands there. She's badass. Give the band $100 bucks to play the devil went down to Georgia & you won't regret it. She's the "best dam fiddle player there's ever been".

I wish I could give it a zero stars but we came here for a bachelorette party and we just happened to like the name and decided to try it out. We went to the third floor and started to order drinks. One of my girls in the group bought four shots and four mixed drinks (so 8 total drinks) as soon as we arrived , so she spent good money to then be treated like shit by a bartender when she came back to ask for a cup of water. The bartender slammed the water and was pissed she didn't want the two dollar bottle. Then when I went to grab a manager to speak with him about the incident the girls I asked were Petty and were telling that bartender what I was sayin and laughing at us. The manager apparently wasn't there so I never got to actually speak to him. I'd never go back and that's sad we are here for the weekend and that experience made us leave after we finished our drinks. I feel if you are a bartender or server of any kind should not be rude to a paying customer when we simply just asked for some water I don't care if you have a bad day or not your in the service industry and should be nice. Really petty to then all talk about it and stare at us not professional at all or a good time. Wish I could have talked to a manager as we were just trying to have a good time and wanted to feel comfortable at the place we were spending money at.

Their food has never been good. I was served a steak sandwich that was almost raw once, and a chicken sandwich that tasted like bad meat. The only reason I gave them any stars is for the good atmosphere

This spot deserves a solid five stars because it's a lot of fun, and an entertaining spot for a drink. 
=== === ===
This hopping spot is on the Broadway strip and doesn't look like its very big from the outside. However, there are a couple of floors and music and drinks on each. Much of the bar is standing room only, even though there are quite a few seats, if you're lucky enough to snag them. We ordered a drink each and pushed past people to the second floor where we were lucky enough to find a seat. 

Live bands play in each area which is pretty cool to experience. As it were, we sat down where they were holding Open Mic auditions. Basically, singers get up and sing with the band and if the owner thinks you're good, you might just get hired. That was pretty awesome to watch! So yeah, if you're in the area, stop in and enjoy some live entertainment and a few pricy drinks.

Green Hills needed a coffee shop.  It needed it bad.  Like an addict needs their fix, Green Hills needed a place for people to load up on Caffeine and chill out.  Finally, it seems, that day has come.  The Well took over what looks to have been an old Burger King.  In the hipster rating system, this gives it an automatic 10 points on a scale of whatever number is cool that day.

There is a lot to love about the Well.  From its truly reclaimed nature, to its altruistic mission statement and on to its smiling staff.  What is really great about the Well though is its location.  Located (finally something is) on the OTHER side of Hillsborough (or as the Green Hills locals call it, "the rough side") it has a sort of Zen that is lacking in the greater Green Hills area.  

Whats most important about a coffee shop?  The coffee of course.  It is good here, really good in fact.  The pour overs are good, but their house dark coffee is also astonishingly good.  Perfect temperature and well crafted.  The food here is an after thought, there isn't much.  Were they to add a set of artisan breakfast sandwiches they might win some kind of hipster award.  Think, guys in too tight jeans weeping, and girls with ironic makeup rocking back and forth slowly.  

I think the thing I like most about this place is their committment to be a not for profit coffee shop.  They donate (or so their sign says) all of their profits to charities.  It takes a pretty special kind of person to wake up this early and make coffee for people not to make any profit at all.  For this reason, and many more, I give The Well my stamp of approval.  It might not be worth a damn, but honest people, doing good work makes me a little warm and fuzzy inside.

An historic lunch counter and iconic civil rights venue in the middle of downtown serving classic southern comfort food.

We stopped in for dessert as a part of a food tour and took a little time to go upstairs to look at the photos from the struggle for equality in the 60's.  Downstairs we feasted on the chocolate peanut butter pie while admiring the classic interior.

The place was pretty busy at lunch and all the food going by looked really good.  If the decadent pie with its pecan crust, chocolate layer and creamy peanut butter center and crunchy candied bacon and brûlée'd bananas is any indication, you may not want to step on a scale after eating this indulgent treat or hearty southern chow.

Will have to plan a return visit to try more of the menu!

This has to be one of the dirtiest bars I've ever been to in my life. It has 3 stories, and each story has a different band or music. The floors are literally plywood and so are the walls. Everything is covered in dirt and dust. I looked behind the bar... yikes! I did give it 2 stars because the music was fun.
I enjoyed a very juicy burger that was excellent.  The service was really nice and prompt.

The Seafood Gumbo Was One Of If Not The Worst Soups That I Have Ever Eaten. Three Days Of Excruciating Heart Burn and Possible Food Poisoning.  The Braised Short Ribs Entree Were
Good. ( Reason 2 and Not 1 Star) Service Was Friendly and Good. Overall ( Except the Gumbo) Good Not Great.

Went to The Sutler for drinks and a show. The Sutler was clean and the waitress we worked with was very friendly. The drink specials are the way to go. During happy hour most drinks are 50% off. Very happy with them music, Alyssa Brown was playing when I was there. 

I ordered one of the dessert mugs. I was pleased with the dessert, but not super impressed will probably not order again. My friends enjoyed the cucumber drinks and the whiskey drinks as well. 

The Bathrooms are downstairs and the elevator is not easily accessible. This was especially hard if you had bad knees!
Had an awesome breakfast here. Sat immediately at the counter and loved it. Great service and even better hospitality! Hands down the best sweet potato pancakes ever.

This is a great bar! I had to stop in since it's a Nashville icon, and it didn't disappoint. We sat on the mid level, the music was great, service was great and the food was delicious! We didn't have high hopes for the food, so we were really happy when it was way better than the bar food we expected. Definitely a must see.

Who plans a vacation around a TV show? My wife. We don't even like country music. 

All I heard about was this Blue Bird Cafe and how hard it is to get into. We followed the directions on the website on logging in at a certain time. No luck, they went fast. I'm talking seconds.

My wife now just wanted to see the outside of this place. We roll up early the doors are locked and nobody to be found. Place doesn't open for another 2 hours.

Then we find out they let the first 20 or so people waiting at the door in. We're the only ones there. We rode it out and I'm glad we did. 

FYI the wait list line started to build an hour before the doors open. By the time the door opened there were more people in the wait list line than could possibly fit into the club. Get there early. Real early if you want in. 

4 musicians in the round. Food was better than expected and the drinks were reasonable, 

I'm a fan and I would come back to the Blue Bird. I think I might like "some" country music now.

We were in Nashville for a concert and were indecisive about dinner. A traffic cop on the street recommended this place and he was so spot on! The food here is delicious; I had the shrimp and grits which was awesome and sampled some of the fried chicken which was also excellent. We had an excellent server, Rick who was super funny and attentive. He made great suggestions! They have good cocktails too and we even had a celebrity sighting while we were there.  Would totally eat here again. Atmosphere and staff both great. Chocolate malt was wonderful too.

Every time I visit your establishment your bouncers suck. For the fight, I go back to the restaurant and they tell me I can't go in. I just want to leave and can't get out. They want me to fight a huge crowd of people to leave when I want to leave early. I paid for this shit. This is why I never come here. There is always a problem with your bouncers

We had a fantastic evening at the sutler good music, food and drink.  We ordered the sweet potato hummus (4/5 stars) the raw veggies (5/5 stars) the grilled veggies (4/5 stars) and the popcorn - which was the best popcorn I've ever had.  It was apparently popped in duck fat, rolled in bacon bits (and grease)' mixed with deep fried jalapeños, and then drizzled with honey.  The popcorn was so good...  I had a bourbon barrel aged ale that was really nice.   Compared to prices in my home state the meal was totally reasonable, especially given the quality of the venue, the service, and the music.

On one hand, its the Bluebird Cafe.  You have to go.  But on the other hand, waiting outside for 3 hrs in the blistering heat is no joke.  We were first in line (though others came shortly after us) so we got the best seats in the house, but I was pretty annoyed that the first show is not even the headliner and you don't get to stay for the second one.  But then to get into the second one you have to arrive somewhere near the end of the 1st show line, but somehow time it right so that you're first in line for the second show.  I dont even know how its done.  

I don't know that I'd do it again, or even recommend anyone else to do it.  But it was a very Nashville experience.  Food was decent at best, drinks were meh, and band was good but not my fav I saw in Nashville.
The food and service was great.   Parking is crazy,  just find a place and walk.  Little hard to find.  Sit at the bar.

Cool history. Awful business. Ive known several people to work and play here over the years and they have all said how horribly they treat people. Sky high prices. No room to move. This is a tourist trap plain and simple. If you want to see Nashville for what it really is, don't go here. If you are here to spend too much on drinks, not be able to move, support bad businesses, and get bad service then go here.

Great Happy Hour TIL 8 pm on second floor! $5 special cocktail and $6 wines plus $1 off beer. The food was good a little pricey but it's downtown. It's a cool old building completely refurbished so you feel like you're eating in Woolworths!

Have been to bottomless blue grass brunch twice and had a great experience 

Go early! It does get crowded - I found the golden time to be 10:30-11:30 - I have heard there can be an hour to two hour wait. 

Ordered the andouille hash last visit and it was very good!! 

Pros:
$17 bottomless mimosa
Live music 
Great food/great prices
Cool decor 
Parking in front (but if you plan on drinking, call an Uber!) 

Cons:
Can be understaffed at times and staff can seem overwhelmed 
Can have long wait times 
If you don't want to wait, there are limited other brunch options in the neighborhood 
Do not take reservations

TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE! WORST PLACE IN NASHVILLE!

I got inside the bar before my friends got in, and was inside waving to them through the window as they were standing out front, and then was kicked out because it was a "restricted area" even though the ropes were off to the side and made it very difficult to tell that I was not supposed to be in that area. They continued to let the rest of my group into the bar, and I was still not allowed to go back in with them. The bouncer had an aggressive manner, and even trying to reason with him, soberly, I couldn't get anywhere and didn't even get to explain my situation. We were there to celebrate a birthday, and this bar was first place on the list we wanted to go, and didn't even get to go in. Was very much looking forward to hanging out here for a bit, but will not be trying to go back in the future.

Had a blast at Tootsie's. The music was good, drinks flowed, and patrons were all there for the same thing, I good time. Like most other places, it gets busy and crowed, but you can usually find a space to hang.

What a atmosphere of comfort and style! Was captivated the moment we arrived. This place is overflowing with history and the way it has been displayed is beautiful. 
Everything worked on so many levels- the decor, the presentation, the hospitality of the hosting station and servers, the comfort food, music choices, etc. Will bring visitors here as a great representation of how Nashville vibes. Everyone is smiling, which is a nice change of pace.
Kassidy was the most awesome bartender we've ever had! She was a sweetheart and was the reason that we stayed.
It's a Honky Tonk. Multiple levels of live country music and overpriced beer. A must stop on the bachelorette party tour.

My favorite place on Broadway. Don't get me wrong. This place is a dump  (in the best way possible!)... it wasn't obnoxiously crowded.. drinks were well-priced.. live music... good beer selection on tap.. they have an AWESOME signature Green Tea shot... skeeball, popashot basketball, buck hunter (which actually all work)... clean bathroom... short lines for drinks... and amazingly greasy and wonderfully horrible for you food. Burgers were awesome, I had a killer spam sandwich, and the tater tots were crispy to  a t. We bar-hopped around Broadway, but ended up back here both nights. Get the Green Tea shots!!

It is what it is.  It's pretty trashy (on purpose) and smells like stale beer.  However, they have a vast selection of beers of draft, great live music and good food.  I wouldn't take my date's parents here or anything but if you are looking for a good time, this is the place.  It's got a fun decor and plenty of arcade games to play. Frankly, this place is a lot of awesome fun and if you aren't pretentious, you should make an effort to visit.

I have never heard the music or eaten the food upstairs. My review is limited to the downstairs lounge area, or the "Cellar."

We love coming here because of the speakeasy vibe and the friendly bartenders. The cocktails are also delicious, and they change up the cocktail menu from time to time so be on the lookout for new drinks. 

My only complaint is that the bartenders don't appear to have been trained on some signature classic drinks. I ordered a Penicillin, a pretty common cocktail, and the bartender had no idea what I was talking about. So that kind of sucked. But the drink he ended up making for me was absolutely amazing, so that made up for it.

What a great place to eat! We had sweet potato pancakes, avocado toast, and Bologna Eggs Benedict. I can't tell you which one I liked better, but I can say the food was amazing. The Avocado toast was perfect and unlike many places that offer avocado toast salt was not necessary. The pickled onions and juices tomato's were perfect. Couple the food with service and the history of the location and you have a must visit when in Nashville. Only regret was I didn't take a picture of my plate. Keep up the good work!

My boyfriend and I were wondering around downtown Nashville looking for somewhere to eat without a 45 minute wait, and stumbled upon this lovely place. The service is very prompt and courteous! We had a great server. I enjoyed my chicken and gnocchi, but the cream sauce it was served in was more soup-like than anything (except it was too heavy to actually eat as a soup). We were in and out within 45 minutes thanks to their quick service and cooking time. Very nice ambience.
This place is hilarious. Check out the mullet pictures on the bar.

I'll just say it - this place is weird.  I like the classic feel but not the modern pricing.  The food simply doesn't live up to it.  I had the pork chop, it was ok, not anything special.  We had multiple servers, multiple people stop by and ask us if everything was ok (before food arrived), even gentleman wearing dishwashing aprons came by to interrupt our conversation.  I get it, this place is nee.  But I don't know, just an awkward dining experience overall that will prevent me from returning.

This place is so awesome.  I came to visit Nashville from Los Angeles for the first time and everyone who had been recommended this place.

I was informed that I needed to buy tickets way in advance because they sell out fast.  Long story short, I wasn't able to purchase tickets (they do sell out within minutes) so we opted for the stand by seats.  The night of the show, my boyfriend and I barely made it in.  Our uber driver (who missed the exit twice), basically made us late but the second we pulled up, we jumped out of the car and the host was waiting outside to accommodate the stand by goers.  We were the last people in.  And by some strike of luck, we ended up getting some of the best seats in the house.  We didn't have to sit on any pews.  We weren't pushed into any back corner (although that's not a bad spot since the venue is small and intimate - any seat there is good).  We ended up sharing a table with a group that was just a few feet away from the performers.  It was awesome!  Sometimes it all just works out.  No tickets and being late equated to only having to pay a cover charge ($20/ea) and sharing one of the best tables in the venue!  So, if tickets are sold out, don't fret, you still have a great chance of making it in!

Once we were in the place, we were relieved.  The performers (true talented artists who write their own music) circled up and each took a turn to sing and play their hearts out.  Now, I am not a big country music fan, but I can appreciate good music and pure artistry and I witnessed it here.  Some of the music made me cry cuz it was just so heartfelt.  

If you want a relaxed and quieter atmosphere where you just wanna listen to good music and kick back, come here.  It's great!

Found WW5 when the recommended Puckett's had a 45 minute wait. Neat throwback of a place with interesting civil rights era history. Chaotic morning - delightful server had too many tables, our order got lost so we weren't served for more than 30 minutes after ordering a simple breakfast. Terse (new?) hostess. Vacated tables took forever (in diner/restaurant time) to be cleared, resulting in huge crowd waiting for a table. Owner - more of an investor, we were told - doesn't spend much time at the restaurant, and it showed today. With a more efficient operation, they could probably move 25% more people through.

I had heard about the Bluebird Cafe ever since I moved to Nashville. On a Thursday nite I stopped in to listen to the music. I had not even gotten to the door when I was stopped by an immature doorman who asked what did I want? He had been talking with several people who left as I walked up. I replied I had stopped to listen to some music. In a rather rude manner told me they were at capacity. Perhaps they were but the manner he communicated was not very respectful. I don't plan on going again.

Broadway is a tourist trap and a must do. You can listen to live music anytime between 11am and 3am at most venues. Kids are allowed in any place before 6pm so long as smoking isn't permitted (Tootsie's is one of these family friendly places.)

We went at 2 in the afternoon with our almost three year old and the first floor was full, so we took the first table on the second floor and had a view of the band. Food section is minimal, drink selection is wide. 

We ordered chips and dips (undoubtedly canned salsa and queso), chicken fingers and fries (delicious, though previously frozen), and the bbq pork sandwich which melted in my mouth and was smokey goodness. 

So why the four stars for what seems mediocre? Because it's exactly what we were looking for! Music, food and family permitted. 

Also, during our visit I had to go to the restroom which smelled fresh and clean with underlying bleach tones. I was surprised and pleased!

Cool place as far as the restaurant goes... neat atmosphere and cool bar lounge downstairs.  The food was average at best and the time that it took to serve our food was over 45 to 50 minutes after we placed our order and it was just my wife and I.  The manager came over to our table apologized and comp'd our food, which was nice. She took it upon herself to do this, we didn't ask for them to do this but it was right thing to do.  This place needs to work at getting the food out of the kitchen.  They maybe still working out some kinks back there.  I believe this is a newer restaurant.  It seems like they could not keep up with the dinner hour rush.  45 people enter the restaurant in about 10 to 15 minute time frame and got packed very quickly.  I would also say that it is slightly pricey for fancy BBQ type food.  I had the cheeseburger because the bartender said it was so good.  A lot of bread, over cooked burger, floating in a beer cheese dip sauce...I was disappointed to be honest.  The Potted Smoke was good. An interesting BBQ type appetizer & neatly presented.  If they can work the kinks out of the kitchen and keep up with the dinner hour rush, this will be a 4 out of 5 restaurant and a very popular place.

Even though it is a bit pointless to review the bluebird i will give my opinion anyway. The bluebird is what it is. A highly touted, famous, live music venue. While this makes me proud being a Nashville, green hills native, i do believe it is over hyped and over rated. At the bluebird fun is out. You will sit in these wooden chairs, no talking, you must buy at least two overpriced drinks and i would eat before you go. The thing is Nashville is loaded with live music venues, most of them showcasing artist who probably wrote the songs that made the bluebird artist famous. If you are visiting Nashville for sure visit the bluebird if you can, but dont believe for a second that this is the best and only place to hear live music ,and most are free.

When I told people I was going to Nashville, everyone said you have to check out Tootsie's for a view of the Honky Tonk (Broadway) aka the place were everyone gets lit, & for good drinks.  I was not disappointed!

I believe that this bar is 4 stories high?  & with a rooftop bar with a great view of the strip.  I do not know how the gals made it with their high heels!

Each level is madness, with bartenders serving too much alcohol & live music.  It was epic!  To be honest, I do not remember much but I remember getting fat shots, like half a cup full, & having a blast!

Tin Roof is actually a very cool place to grab a bite to eat and a beer. We got dropped off by Uber right in front and we were able to sit outside period ever very easy menu which is very reasonable. I ordered the Cuban sandwich and the tater tots off the starter menu which came with bacon bits and ranch dressing, pretty damn good. They have a good beer list as well as some good mixed drinks. Great atmosphere, kind of a younger crowd especially as the night goes on but it was fun to people-watch on their patio. Our only issue was our waitress seemed to disappear as they got a little bit busier and had to track her down to get a bill, which was screwed up, but we just wanted to move on by that time. Otherwise seem to be a good place and everybody enjoyed the food
Absolute blast! A Nashville must-see! Went for late night on a Wednesday. The band on the top floor was amazing. Great sound and music for everyone no matter the level you were on.

This place is petty close by to where I work, so we pick up food or drinks regularly, typically whenever I go to pick food up it's a male bartender with a bad attitude. I was pleasantly surprised with the excellent customer service today. It did take the girl a few minutes longer than it probably normally would to greet me, but I understand that she was busy. She was so nice whenever I was finally greeted and even gave me complimentary tea to makeup for my wait time! Thank you blonde girl working behind the bar today!!

Had their "Dime Store" burger and fries. Not a good homemade hand pattied burger like I expected but a pre-formed patty. Tasted like meat was from a restaurant supply company like Sysco pre-made. Fries were so-so. They ask you "how would you like that cooked".  I had very high expectations when paying this price. Fries should be hand-cut if they are trying to position themselves with an over-$10 burger in my opinion. It didn't taste good. Cost $13.00.

Beware of new doormen and bouncers with attitude. I stood up on bottom
Of stool
To get my sisters attention, and one of the security grabbed me and said "sit the fuck down". I wasn't even drinking. Then on the way out the door man said they were going to kick me out. WTF! The bartenders were awesome and band was great. Your a little to big for your britches sir.....

So I was warned that Tootsie's was not worth the hype.  But as I was at another establishment on Broadway, a new friend told me that you had to go to Tootsie's at least once as it was one of the original honkey tonk spots.  I wanted to explore so we went.

After entering, the ground floor was wall to wall people, my Aunt needed a bit more space so she suggested we should go up to another floor.  As we walked towards the stairs, I saw a black pouch on the ground and asked the woman standing over it, if it was hers.  She was so excited that she didn't lose it, she bought me a drink.  After getting my drink from her, I headed upstairs.  My Aunt found a table and we enjoyed the band up there.  We had a second drink.  The second floor was crowded but a bit more manageable than the ground floor.  There was a third floor but we didn't go up there.

The band was great, the drinks were well made (I don't know the prices as I was being treated to drinks for my birthday), and everyone in the joint was fun and nice.  I had a great time and am glad I hit this spot before leaving Broadway for the night.  So I say, come at least once to Tootsie's and you may have a great night like I did.

This place fucking sucks. This place is very bad. Very bad this place is. Do not ever go here. Such an incredible waste of money. I'm being completely serious, do not go here like ever. If you haven't noticed yet, I'm just trying to reach the word minimum and convey the message that this place absolutely sucks! Ok cool, thx.

This place is popular for sure.  Visiting Nashville for the first time and stopped by this staple bar.  It is busy and has great music and the staff is on top of it for the crowd size they are dealing with.  Recommended stop for sure!

This place is everything it's hyped up to be, and it better be considering how freaking hard it is to get in the door. This sentence could also be written like this:  Who do I have to befriend to get tickets to a 9pm show at this place? Who, who, who? 

We've waited in line outside the doors for 3 hours to get seats to a no-reservation show; we've queued in the website ticket line for 2 hours to land a reservation for a weekend performance; and we've even rolled the dice for fate and popped in during the week when the doors opened, hoping for a miracle. It is hard to get tickets to this place. Hard, hard, hard. 

Yes, three (count 'em, 3!) times, we've managed to get a seat inside these hallowed strip mall walls, but once there it's a little...um...anticlimactic. With super tight seating and full-to-bursting guest count, hearing a show here is a bit like listening to a concert from your seat on a Delta flight: enjoyable, but super uncomfortable. 

Of course, all that said, it's still The Bluebird Cafe. And this is still Nashville, and we still love good music and good songwriters. And Deacon and Scarlett and Rayna and all our pals on ABC's Nashville still tell us The Bluebird is where it's at, so I guess we'll all have to keep sucking it up and getting up at the crack of dawn to get in the virtual ticket line or stand outside the front doors hoping the first 100 people in front of us will just go home or drop dead or something so we can get inside. 

Yep, we'll do it, but that doesn't mean we're going to be happy about it. Just for the record.
Great little pice if Nashville history. Had bear burger and sweet potato fries! $13 bucks and I was full. Great family atmosphere- will go back.

Hm... not as impressed as I thought it was going to be. I LOVE comfort food and this didn't really hit the spot. We ordered the pork belly appetizer and for entree, ordered the pot roast and pork chops. 

Pork belly: Delicious! They did a great job balancing all the flavors - the fattiness/richness of marinated/roasted/broiled pork belly, with a fresh salad in a tart salad dressing, pickled pears, and goat cheese, plus watermelon chunks for a bit of sweetness. This was on point for $12.

Pot roast: Solid. The meat was very tender, the mashed potatoes were silky and buttery, it's a classic comfort dish that is hard to mess up. They did it well here for $32.

Pork chop: Not good. The meat was overdone and lacked flavor. The stuffing they put on top also didn't help add any texture or flavor. The black eyed peas and cabbage it came with were too sweet for their own good, and although did add flavor to the pork, then overpowered it. This was not worth $30.

All in all, the service was great, the restaurant feels a bit bare (albeit its historical nature), and the food was okay. Wouldn't say that this would be a place that I'd come back to if I were to choose another restaurant during a Nashville visit.

A Nashville must see.  As far as honky tonks go,  Tootsies sets the gold standard for others. Tootsies is a no frills watering hole, with a Wall of Fame, that includes a who's who of Country music stars, who have played or visited Tootsies at some point over the last 30-40 years.  Live music upstairs and down.  Lots of cold beer on tap.  Wonderful rooftop area to have a beer, enjoy good conversation and hang out while watching the scenes along Broadway.  If you only have time for one honky tonk, make it Tootsies.  Who knows you may experience an up and comer who will one of the next great country music stars.

We didn't think brunch was our thing until we came here this morning! The Bluegrass Brunch is a must go to! Great atmosphere. Great food. Great mimosas. Their biscuits are superb! I got the sweet potato pancakes and he got the chicken and waffle. Both were delicious. This is our brunch spot from now on. Others don't even come close to our experience here.

We loved this little bar. It was the only one on Broadway that wasn't playing country music. The band was playing nineties rock. Drinks were reasonably priced and our server Brittany was super friendly.

Tooties has some great live music no doubt, just like all the other legendary honky tonks on broadway. So this review is for the venue and the atmosphere, since you gotta choose which bar to visit by some criteria right? 

Tooties has two bars, one that you can see from the broadway entrance and one up the stairs in the back. That means double the music acts on a given night. You can really see the age of this place. It is ancient, and there is barely any place to move about even with two bar sections. Despite the lack of space and the throngs of crowds, the bartenders are like hawks. They target you and make sure you have a cold budlight in your hands at all times. If it wasn't for how cramped tootsies is, I would like it a lot more.

We went because the website advertised LIVE Karaoke Thursday nights.   We got there excited to participate and were told they stopped it.  The live band of two were good. Had appetizers and drinks that were good. Very disappointing.

The female at the front door was rude and extremely condescending . From Southern California and wasn't aware of needed reservation. I understand there wasn't room for our group 5, but that is not the person I would want to represent my business. "Everybody knows they need a reservation"... well shame on us I guess

This is by far a must stop for dining while in Nashville.  It has a friendly casual atmosphere and the servers always seem to care about you.

Our personal favorite is the bbq chicken tender sandwich.  The fries are hot and crispy and come with a wonderful queso dip.

Great place to relax and have a great meal!

I'm not sure what was going on when we first walked in, but it felt odd. Once inside the space, it was super cute! It is a very large space... it wasn't busy. The hostess was PERFECT! We were seated at the time of our reservation. Zach was attentive and was patient with our party of 8. The kids loved the macaroni and cheese. The meatloaf, shrimp and grits, and turkey were all good. The fried chicken was fantastic. Get the fried chicken! The kids got milkshakes for dessert and multiple people at the table said it's the best milkshake they've ever had. Several reviews mention the food to be underwhelming. This was absolutely not the case. It's southern fare. It isn't fancy. It was great!

Oh my! What an amazing time we had watching Scott Collier and the midnight special! He is so awesome with the crowd! The bar staff was wonderful! They were always ready to serve! We can't wait to come back!

This cute place in the heart of Nashville brings back memories of the classic mid century lunch counters (with addition of friendlier and less-discriminating staff).

Jeremy and Mike behind the counter were awesome. While here I sat at the counter and got excellent service and great food.

My only complaint was that the air conditioning unit above the counter appeared to condense the cold air and drip down on the seats and countertops. Not a huge bother though.

Would gladly come here again for music next time I'm in town!

My new favorite bar in Nashville! The cheese fries are so addicting. I met some other customers the other day who refer to tin roof as their second home. Bartenders were very outgoing and made my experience here awesome!

I came here on a Friday night with my boyfriend for the food as we were hungry and this place was empty. I didn't think any bar type of food would be any good, but it wasn't too bad. The place is run down but the customer service was good and the food was decent.
I don't remember what I ordered but the burger was dry and they're known for their tater tots from what the cashier said so I ordered that. Everything was mediocre at best. The sweet potatoes fries weren't good at all. Would highly recommend staying away from those. But definitely go with a juicy thick burger if you do get anything from here.

Ay yi yi.  This 30 year old is no longer cut out for the packed to the gills bars.  However, Tootsie's is kind of a big deal, with its historic list of big-name acts.  When in Nashville, it's a bucket list item.  The walls are littered with celebrity photos of all eras.  Simply put, it's the perfect place to spot great talent before they go big.  There was no cover to get in, but be prepared to wait in line.  Some girlfriend's and I waited about five minutes, and then we slowly worked our way through the masses to the bar.  Drinks are overpriced, but remember where you are.  We were lucky enough to grab a table while the former occupants were talking about leaving, so we parked for a while and enjoyed the music.  Because of the crowd, which leaves no room for personal space, don't expect to have a conversation.  Go for the experience.

This used to be my most favorite bar as a local but with the new reorganization and the band at the front it's hard to love. There's no room to swing dance and the flow of the bar is so messed up. Why change a good thing?? Now you have to walk through dancers to get to the bar. They also sometimes have a band that plays some sort of instrument on fire and it's just a screaming noise and it's God awful. I miss my old PPark.

Just visited The Stone Fox for the first time. We got there a little before opening at 11 and there were people already waiting. We were seated immediately and our food was delicious! Out party included adults and children and it was great for everyone. I will definitely be back!

5 Stars.   This is an iconic location with significant civil rights history.    Aside from that, the food is great!    It is not high end, but simply outstanding "comfort food".   The decor is super-cool retro and the service is outstanding.   Don't eat lunch on Broadway, go here!!!

The talent at this place was through the roof. I honestly felt like I was at a concert and could not believe the musical talent that was set before me. I was pretty much in  heaven because we ordered a delicious pitcher of red sangria, a chocolate dessert in a cup, and live music. It was the perfect evening. Also if you want to venture downstairs there is a Pool Hall Downstairs, and another swanky bar attached to this place. This place had me at Hello!

Wow!  What a great experience. The Thursday night we were there we saw Jessie Lee, Paul Sikes, Ash and AAron. I think I have that right. Sorry if I don't. Our group was split up because it is so hard to get the tickets on line -we just took what we could get. No one in our group cared once we got there. Every seat was great. My husband and  I sat at table 9. It was almost like we were part of the show we were so close to the artists. They even sat there drinks on our table. The music and background behind the songs they sang and wrote made it an once in a lifetime experience. The artists stayed after and we were able to speak with them and take photos.  Highly recommend!!

Bring lots of cash if you plan on a long drinking stay. Drinks are extremely expensive.  Alcohol drinks are a minimum of $9 a drink.  That is for non call booze. No food just liquor. It is truly a tourist trap bar with. name recognition. 
Have as rink and move on to the next tourist trap. All prices have really increased since my last visit. 
Only 2 stars because of pricing of alcohol and lack of value.

Came in for my first visit, and I was both HANGRY AND THIRSTY!!! Was Greeted by an attractive girl at the bar who seem to have a chip on her shoulder she never wants mild never watched big knowledge me other than what can I get you to drink I ordered my food and she put it in and then disappeared and gave respite to new bartender.... New bartender delivered my food to an empty beer which had been empty for probably 3 to 5 minutes somewhere in that area remind you I'm at the bar. A bar of 10 seats maybe. They delivered my food seven minutes ago it's still sitting in front of me ice cold as it was when I got here and I still haven't gotten anyone to come over and asked me about it. This will be my first and last trip here at the Sutler no matter how good the food would've been if it was hot like it should've been!!! HORRIBLE SERVICE
visited late Saturday night.  can the locals get any nicer!  funky atmosphere.  Younger crowd.  I'm looking forward to going back.  If you need a late night hot dog, they have you covered.

Plan ahead and order tickets & be patient when you still need to wait in line to get in. Great live music brings in the crowds. They're so well known, they'll allow you to have your photo taken inside if you're unable to get tickets & entrance.
Awesome spot!

Can't rate the food , but would rate business zero based on "security" / door detail.  My 37 year old friend was turned away as her ID was in the hotel room (with no plans / intention of ordering alcohol-if they even have it?   I was then turned away for a "bad attitude " as I thought it was bogus they wouldn't let her or I  in to order a take away burger......guess we aren't the right color or sex

So Weird.  Other Bartenders in the area said food was decent, but 2 girls couldn't get past the angry door men.

Went for a girls night out. Everyone's food looked delicious! I got the bistro steak with the Brussels sprouts and bacon! It was delicious! My friend got the filet and subbed the haricot verts for Brussels sprouts and bacon. Her filet was cooked well done (and it was dry when she cut into it) when she had advised the wait staff that she wanted it medium. The filet was sitting on top of mashed potatoes and barely had any Brussels sprouts on the plate and the Brussels sprouts that were on the plate had been mashed into the potatoes. We did call the waitress back and asked if she could remake it. The waitress of course made a remark that my friend could afford to be picky since she was paying for it (not sure if that was even necessary-I've waited tables for several years and would have never made that kind of comment). The second filet was cooked appropriately. Overall, food was decent for the price. I would be willing to give this place a second chance minus the snarky waitress.

Decent beer selection, mediocre live music at best and a lovely bartender lady who either can't count correctly or purposely gives you incorrect change hoping you won't ask her where your missing $2 went...
This place is fun! Super crowded downstairs but that's the place to be. Drinks served quickly and music was great. Saw a couple get engaged there actually! Fun stop.

Outstanding! Very cool place to hang out on a Sunday. We arrived around 1130 and were told by the hostess the wait time was 75 minutes. We left and hung out at the coffee shop, Fenwick's 300. The wait time was slightly longer than the estimate however we didn't mind since the coffee shop was equally enjoyable. Our service at The Sutler was prompt, courteous and our orders were accurate.  I had the Classic Breakfast and my friend had the Smoked Brisket Hash.  Our food was served timely and hot which was surprising given the amount of people.  The Bluegrass Band was decent, made for pleasant change of pace.  The atmosphere is very relaxed. Out of the 3 meals in Nashville, this restaurant was the favorite!

Catfish tacos and the fries will forever be in my dreams! The presentation, unique style and OH MY the taste! It is sad that I just now find this before moving away but anytime I visit Nashville...this is my first stop!

I gotta say, I love my dance bars and Tin Roof delivers phenomenally. But my review is not for a classic Saturday night out. I'm here to tell you about Tuesday night bingo night, hosted by Lightning 100.

First, I'll tell you to arrive an hour early for guaranteed seating. I arrived at 7 (starts at 7:30) with one other friend and had to share seats with another table. i will say that the fellow that we joined was extremely welcoming to a newly minted bingo player like myself which adds to my liking of the event.

Great prizes and plenty to go around. This is how I picture bingo nights going and I will definitely be back. Why  4 stars? The slow service. At one point I stood up to have my drink refilled. Not good. The bar is trying to make money off us right?

Other than the slow service, I loved the chill atmosphere and would definitely recommend.

What a day! Sitting in Tootsies in Nashville, listening to live bands with excellent musicians. We watched the new bachelorette with her 5 friends from Canada dance and sing Hotel California with the band. Met an AA flight crew in down time. Met  Michiganites masquerading as New Zealanders. And drank too many ciders. My wife and I had a ball. The star act was Natalie Spiroff an 28 year old on her way to stardom. Thanks Tootsie's for the best day

4 floors of madness. Just madness. The first floor was crowded, people were singing on the bar, but you just have to elbow your way through! In the back near the alley there is another stage with live music. We got a beer and got a spot behind the stage and watched them sing songs by request for a while. The upper floors were just as crowded and music was being played on each. It was cool to check out!

This is one of our favorite finds in downtown Nashville!  The first impression was with the hostess. Lateesha,  she was so amazing.  Her contagious personality is a rare find and we loved her!  Our waiter was on point, the food came quickly and was beyond our expectations!  I would highly recommend Woolworth.  We will definitely be back and will suggest this to everyone!  Thank YOU for an amazing Saturday morning family brunch !
Great local bar! Has a great happy hour and laid back feel! Their quesadillas and fries and queso are a must try!

This joint is over the top great! Don't go here for good drinks or food (or anywhere else on Broadway for that matter), but the music and liveliness will blow your mind. The talent in the city is amazing, but I kept finding my way back to Tootsie's on my visit and always wanted to stay. You also never know when someone famous will drop in;) Do yourself a favor and visit even if it's the only
place you go on Broadway. Tip the musicians well. And if you're going to buy a ridiculously overpriced beverage, be sure to tip the bartenders well, too.

Absolutely horrific. Music was AMAZING but the "manager" was rude, offensive, and ruined future business for establishment. I have never had a worse customer service experience. 

I walked in, ordered a beer and he came up to me and said "did you pay to get in? You shouldn't be standing! We are at capacity leave!" 

What?? We walked in, no one asked us for a cover, ordered a drink and this "manager" verbally assaulted me.

I would advise you stay away from this place and if you are an artist - You deserve a better venue.

I was excited to finally try Woolworths.  We were more interested in the history of the site than actually dining there. Unfortunately, the mezzanine with all the historical information was temporarily closed due to a construction project upstairs.  We might have selected another restaurant had we known this before entering.  I did not see a sign to that effect.

Our server was very pleasant and made suggestions of his favorites on the menu.  I should have listened to him.  I ordered the short rib pot roast which was a good sized portion.  The mashed potatoes were obviously homemade as there were chunks of potato. The green beans were crisp and good.  However, the sauce over the entire dish was way too salty, almost briny.  It was a disappointing dish because of it.  I had requested my wine be served with my meal but I had to remind our server to get it.  

My husband ordered the patty melt which came out prepared on a marble rye bread.  It was full of seeds which my husband cannot eat.  There was mention of the type of bread in the menu nor by our server.  The server apologized and offered a couple of other choices and sent it back to the kitchen.  Once it arrived on a nice brioche bun, my husband enjoyed his meal although he said the fries were over salted as well.

The portions were huge but that really doesn't matter if the food is sub par.  I don't think l'll go back for dinner but I might for lunch.  We still want to visit the mezzanine.

Their pour here is close to a double.  The bartenders know what this place is about.... heavy drinking.  I haven't eaten hear so I don't feel safe giving it a 5.  This is a prime pre-game spot before hitting downtown Nashville.
Great music and fun atmosphere. From looking at the outside and venue this wouldn't be my first pick but we had a lot of fun!

Fire hazard -----Too crowded to be fun.  


Not worth the wait in line to shove past throngs of obnoxious bachelorette parties to wait for a beer. Typical of all Broadway bars. Check it out during the day to say you've been there, spend your evening elsewhere, Nashville has better nightlife than Broadway.
Music and atmosphere were fine.  Drinks were terrible and overpriced.  I do not recommend.

Omg nothing on the menu under 15. The burger was bland and the fries were limp and cold.  Dim lights did nothing to enhance the evening.  Selection is better at lunch when prices are less.  Ok for lunch but a total miss for dinner.

AMAZING BAR!!!! This was one of the must stop at for the bar hopping down Broadway.  So many singers have made it big out of Tootsie's.  There is so much live music here with multiple bands playing. Yes the bar  seemed dirty and it was crowded, makes you feel like your back in college.
Oh how I love thee. Multiple bands, great country music, open windows and doors, great company, what more can one ask for? Heaven on earth.

Food was decent, only real reason i gave this any stars. 
1. Host had a bad attitude through the get go, and we werent sat for 6 mins. Take into account there was no line of people waiting to get sat. We were eventually told by some other employee that to just seat ourselves which we did.
2. Sat down and didnt get served for a solid 11 minutes. No waters, no anything. If it were busy no big deal, but half the restaurant was empty, so idk what was up with that. When our server finally showed, she took our entire order, brought just my drinks not my husband, and forgot our appetizer entirely. Burgers were actually pretty decent. We reminded her of our missing app when entrees were dropped and i could tell she just forgot to ring it in. Not a huge deal she said itd be out in a minute. That was a lie of course. 
3. Finished burgers which were nice, app finally came out but we were already full. Told manager to either take it back or just leave it, as it didnt matter. He did comp it so grateful for that. We received no refills on drinks didnt even ask. We could see our waitress paying more attention to the tables right beside us. Everyone else was helped but we were left alone. 
Overall: this was a truly disappointing experience. Wont be back again, even after it was hyped up to us.

I've been here twice now for brunch. The place is adorable, servers are friendly, drinks are great, food is pretty good. I just am THIRSTY throughout the entire experience. I feel like it's such a hassle getting a water refill in this place. Usually this doesn't bother me, but during my first visit I realized that when you've eaten a few bites of their super spicy chicken and waffles and realize you won't have any more water for 20 minutes, you start to contemplate putting your face under the bathroom faucet for relief. Luckily my brunchmate let me drink his water too. 

My second experience I wised up and went for the classic breakfast plate which was great. Runny eggs, flaky biscuits, sausage and hashbrowns...but no bev refills (coffee or water) for like 20 mins at a time. I think honestly they just need more than 2 servers on weekends. I hate to be so harsh, but seriously, especially for brunch, we need to rehydrate and caffeinate, Stone Fox! I will try you again, but maybe try for a less crowded time.

Tootsie's is always on my list when I'm in Nashville!
Crowded and loud - shoulder to shoulder ... exactly what I expect for a Legendary Nashville Honky Tonk!
Awesome experience!  MUST see!  Make a reservation FOR SURE!!  The baked Brie is off the chain and I don't even like Brie!  Good service, amazing music.  Recommend this to EVERYONE!!!
One of my favorite places on Broadway! Love all the beer on tap and the games they have available. Good place to day drink and play some golden tee. They did take out beer ping which is a bummer:/

Hmmmmm... I guess I didnt realize that this spot is a bit of a tourist trap before coming in. I just thought to the brunch drinks were supposed to be, ahem, "litty."

Food: Not lit. Sure it's been a month or so since I dined here, but even the next day I couldnt remember what I ordered. After some soul searching, I believe it was the chicken biscuit with gravy. Nothing was necessarily bad about the taste... I just despise lukewarm food. Ya can't really send it back, and unless it's got an amazing flavor... It's not appetizing. My dining companion had a sweeter option and I believe they enjoyed it. Meh. 

Drinks: Okay, this is what I came for... Let's be real. What's brunch without booze?? The sangria carafe is ice...and more ice. We got a solid two drinks out of it. The bloody Mary bar is what my eyes were set on. Admittedly, they had a nice spread of items. The drink prices just seem bumped up for the tourist. I get it, but even those bottomless mimosas seem like a well marketed trap. Meh. 

Service: Meh. 

Live music: Nice touch! No extra stars bc it's music city.

The Well has gotten massively popular since it opened around a year ago. Its perfectly located in Green Hills. The coffee is great (my go-to drink is a honey latte, very smooth and the sweetness balances well with the espresso), service is nice, seating is pretty easy to find, and it's not too loud (plus, whoever mans the playlist does a great job). There are certain times of day where parking can be really difficult (around 10am-11am on weekdays) but it's open everyday and for pretty good hours. They also sell pastries and sandwiches, as well as other merchandise like mugs, T-shirts, and household decorations. All profits are contributed toward providing clean water for regions of the world that need it, which is pretty awesome.

Super cute place, very trendy and hipster. 

But please. For your own good. 

Do NOT eat the chicken and waffles. They made my boyfriend so sick.
I did not enjoy my enchiladas- they were cold and tasteless. We paid almost $40 for a lame meal. 

Only go to this place to drink.

I don't understand why everybody is bringing up segregation. It is not segregated anymore! Can't u talk about the food, atmosphere, and the nice time u had? The reviews posted o here r supposed to b about recent visits to restaurants and other places; not about what things were like 50-60 years ago! Please America can we try and heal! Of course it wasn't right to segregate the old lunch counters, but this place is trying to just b a nice place to go for a night out.

Five stars. One of my favorite things so far in Nashville! 

The building is small, but it's history is huge. Some great musicians got their start in the Bluebird Cafe and I have no doubt that a ton more will play on that stage who will later play on much larger ones. It was a really fun experience with some excellent music and lots of jokes from Don Schlitz! 

There is a minimum food/drink order because the cover charge goes to the musicians. You don't go to eat though, especially at the late night show because the food is nothin special, so keep that in mind. It's all about the music. The beer was cheap and tastes just fine. They prefer cash! Keeps things moving quicker. Plan ahead too, apparently Friday night shows are sold out the Monday before!

The Well is my favorite coffee shop in town, hands down. I love the atmosphere and extremely kind people. It definitely takes awhile to get your coffee, but the wait is worthwhile. Just some advice if you're here to get work done- the outlets hear the front don't work....and if you're wearing yoga pants, don't sit on the prickly hemp-type chairs :)
Super cool bar downstairs. Food was great I had the wedge salad with steak. The bartender down there was really friendly and helpful. I'd certainly go back and try more.

This is my favorite place in Nashville.  It's so amazing to watch and listen to amazing songwriters and hear their stories.

You need to make a recommendation a week in advance.  Tickets sell out in less than 5 minutes and there have been times I didn't get a table when I refreshed the page right at 8am.

When the artists are playing, you're expected to be quiet and listen.  Because of this, you don't get to talk to the other people in your group very much over dinner, but you'll have a lot to talk about after. :)

As far as food goes, you're expected to spend at least $7/person for some events.  I've had a few items off the menu and they're good, but there is a lot of amazing food in Nashville and people come to the Bluebird for the music rather than the food.   If you're looking for an amazing meal, I recommend going out to dinner before or after the Bluebird.

Waiting in line in the heat sucks but if your lucky enough to get a seat it worth the pain and suffering of the wait. Music is awesome and room is historic. Not really any good options here so if you haven't ate plan on going somewhere afterwards.

Great place to see some music, big stage, open layout so there really isn't a bad seat to watch and good acoustics.

The drinks are really yummy interesting concoctions, and made well and consistently every time. 

Some of the food is pretty basic. I was not at all impressed with the avocado salad. But, if you explore the menu a little bit and know what to get, there are some really good options. The tacos are some of my favorites. 

All of the servers are really friendly. We had one server both nights we were there and she made us feel so welcome and so at home right away, even kept a smile after what was apparently a 14 hour shift.

Just one big reason for losing a star. Friday night, they forgot to put in an order and I had to ask three times and eventually had to get it to go, and still charged in full. But not a huge deal. 

The major issue with this place was this- 
Last night I went with a group of about 10 friends, some of whom were the band. We ALL ordered appetizers almost right away. At the same time. The kitchen was backed up, which the waitress told us..it happens. Understandable. The waitress forgot to put in the guacamole I ordered. Again, not a huge deal. About 30 minutes later, our apps came out. All together.
But at the end of the night, closing out, our waitress made a point to tell just the band that THEIR food was taken care of because of the 30 minute wait. If the band got to eat for free because they were playing, that is not unusual. But, if the reason all of their food was free was because it took 30 minutes to get appetizers, why was that not given to everybody that had to wait 30 minutes, and not just the band?

Overall, I've had a slight issue each time I've gone, but the friendly staff and good atmosphere warrant another visit.

I like the atmosphere and friendly service. Wonderful knowing this civil rights historic landmark has reopened, and with a nightclub downstairs. I love the black & white films being screened on the wall and the old R&B/funk background music . The brisket sandwich, served alone with bbq sauce, was very moist and tasty, though it should be served on a kaiser roll not a plain  hamburger bun. The thin sweet potato fries are deliciously crisp, the black eyed peas were okay. The price was reasonable and I'd like to go back to try their brunch.

Maybe the worst service we've ever had in Nashville 
Food was pretty good, but don't be in a hurry to go anywhere if you come to eat here, you will be late.

Hub and I dined here on our single night in Nashville recently. We chose Woolworth on 5th  based on a suggestion of my niece and her hub after they dined here on their recent trip to Music City. Ours was a very enjoyable experience. We had a reservation, and arrived promptly at the appointed time. We were seated on arrival. The restaurant is located in a former Woolworth five-and-dime. With the exception of the exterior signage and the preserved lunch counter, there are no other overt representations of the old store. The interior is elegantly decorated with a neutral color scheme and dimmed, atmospheric lighting. Service was timely and professional; our server was lovely. The food was very good and reasonably priced. I had  wild mushroom risotto while Hub had chicken and gnocchi. My risotto (pea shoots, pickled red onion, charred pineapple, citrus vinaigrette greens) was super tasty, due in part to the pineapple and the citrus vinaigrette greens, which topped the dish. Hub was enthusiastic about his choice, citing the chicken as being especially flavorful. In all, it was a lovely experience.

Getting a table here is a nightmare. You can reserve a table at 8:00AM the Monday before a show, but their website is not equipped to handle the traffic, so you just get locked out. So the people who get tables are just the ones lucky enough to get through the crappy website. They need to fix this.

Beautiful bar and restaurant. Had great drink specials, live music, and holy moly their food. Best breakfast in Nashville. I want to eat their fried chicken as my only meal for the rest of my life. Go to here.

One star is a bit of a stretch..... I had a terrible experience at Tootsies. I ordered a beer at the upstairs bar and was denied because my ID had an air bubble. The bartender denied me, then laughed in my face and asked where I got it from. I said it was obtained from the Department of Motor Vehicles and requested it to be checked by the manager. When the manager came upstairs with my license it had been destroyed. The small air bubble turned into the bottom portion of my hologram being ripped off, making it unusable for the rest of my trip. After this interaction I wasn't even offered anything to compensate for ruining my license, which I need to fly home. I was not even offered a cup of water while I waited for my friends to finish their drinks. I will never go back to this restaurant because of their disgusting lack of customer service.

We decided to check out The Sutler's opening night - headed over around 10pm, snacked on Potted Smoke (heaven on toast - best if enjoyed with the coarse mustard and pickle slices that accompany it), sipped bourbon and enjoyed the old-fashioned country & western music of Johnny Appleseed. Before leaving, we headed downstairs to The Cellar to check out their creative cocktails and friendly bartenders.

The Sutler is comfortable and friendly, just as we remember it. We hope to return often.

The menu and beer selection are electic. We started with appetizers, the guac trio and smoked wings. The guac was brown and the variation consisted of simply piling crab meat and mango chunks on top of very brown guac. The Costco chips were tasty though..
As for the smoked wings, they were not really smoked but instead had the soggy memory of being in a warmer..The Alabama White Sauce has the taste of mayo, vinegar, and ranch which some may love... However, these are not ingredients I find delightful.
The entrees have yet to come.. But we are hopeful..

Intimate venue with ive music.Songwtiters perform their work.  U need to make reservations online for all shows except Sundays and Monday's.  Parking limited.  7$ minimum but food not great so eat before or after and stick tyo drinks and sweet potato fries.  The music is fantastic so make reservations
GREAT FOOD/ Location/ Prices!!!  BBQ Bacon burger is the business!  Tater Tots are delicious!!! Right in the middle of Broadway!  Good people watching!
So. Much. Fun!!! Too crowded on a Sat night but thankfully we got in on Sun about 6pm - the place was still packed. The performers were fantastic & non-stop! Bartenders were awesome!

If you do not like crowds or standing shoulder to shoulder with everybody then do not go here. Do go here if you want to see some of the best musicians in the country playing for free. Two levels, two bands and one hell of a time! The memorabilia alone is worth the visit.

Yup, it's one of those places you just HAVE to visit if you are doing the touristy thing downtown. 

I loved they had the history of Tootsie herself on the actual menu. We didn't order anything besides beers here, but I loved learning a little more about the history. 

The walls of fame are covered with old, falling apart newspaper articles and pictures of some of the biggest country stars you know. Just having a seat at the bar makes you feel a little special, about being somewhere so many great things have come out of. 

It was about 2 pm on a Thursday, and we had a little more time to kill before we headed back to the airport. Yep, there was live music playing, and although it was more of a "pop" country kinda thing going on this day (not my favorite) it was still an experience. 

There is also another bar and was another band upstairs that suit our tastes a little better... so we grabbed another brew before we were unleashed back on Broadway.

Hostess was amazing!! The food was the only other thing that made me give this at least 2 stars
The service was greatly lacking. Our waiter was terrible. He took our order and we could immediately tell he was not very interested. He brought the wrong drink out. He dropped our basket of bread on the table with no plates. Our food came and we still had no plates to eat them with. We asked for plates and was told they would get the rest of our food first. One of our side dishes was never brought out and when I asked about it he said it was his mistake and just walked away. However this is after we had already finished our entire meal. He did not check on us one time throughout dinner. He finally stopped by and when he asked if we needed something we said he could start clearing off the empty plates. If it weren't for the food I would give this place less than 1 star. Service clearly needs to be stepped up.

We stopped into Tootsies a few times on our long weekend in Nashville. It was always packed and had bands playing no matter what time it was. The drinks were a bit pricey but it's a touristy place so that's expected. We always found a good crowd here and the best spot is to head up to the rooftop and grab a table if you can.
. We had the brisket tacos and the steak sandwich and they were both fantastic. Jasmine gave us great, super friendly service. Will definitely be back

Food was good, solid, but not amazing. Nothing super-exciting in the menu choices--about what you'd expect from a nice place down south. The drinks were actually better than the food! The place is also a historic stop and you can wander around and see photos of sit-ins and the Civil Rights history that happened right there. The owners have done a great renovation job--honoring the history while also creating a 21st century space.

Felt like a tourist trap. I'm ok with paying $7 for a light beer to be downtown and enjoy live music but it appears that Tootsie's does not subsidize the artist. We walked up and put a $5 tip in there tip jar and asked they could play a Tom Petty song. Only for the lead singer to pull it out of the tip jar and told the whole bar this is way too low and she was only playing requests for $20. I got to see Tom Petty live in concert before he passed for $30 lol, but she needed $20 for a song requests. It was kind of embarrassing and seemed like a tourist trap. The artist will ask for money after every song, which starts to get uncomfortable.  There are a lot of better bars we found that appreciated our tips and played great music. Very strange experience overall.  Not for me...

If you like bouncers who look like the lead singer of good Charlotte/ fallout boy/ Green Day/ or any 130 lb emo male this is the bar for you. They throw out loyal customers for having a fun time. The bouncers call the cops when they are too small and emo to deal with the customers who aren't doing anything wrong. This is an embarrassing showing by a bar to keep fun loving people happy. The bar needs to hire better/ more capable security instead of the 90 lb "bouncers" who get offended by the comments on his eye liner.

****By far, the WORST ticket purchasing experience I've ever had.*****

Me and the wife planned a trip to Nashville for our anniversary and wanted to catch a show at the Bluebird Cafe. Tickets go on sale at 8am on 07/04/19 so I planned ahead and put it in my calendar and was in their virtual line by 7:30am for tickets on  7/11/19. 

The ticket website goes down that morning and I reach out to the venue, the virtual ticket company and even the vitrual line company. (All different) 

I finally get an email an hour later that the page is back up so I IMMEDIATELY go back to the site to find that tickets for the 6:00pm and 9:00pm shows are sold out. 

The story doesn't end there.

I take the loss on that one and see that they have tickets hoing on sale at 8am on 07/08/19 for shows on 07/12/19. (Day after our anniversary)

I repeat by getting in line at 7:30am and finally get through for the 9:00pm show and its great because there are 2 tickets available at the bar and, since I know I only have one minute to pick my seats, I take the bar seats and click on the proceed to checkout link.

The link malfunctions and puts me back in line and then brings me back to the page to choose my tickets. Guess what happened next..... 

There is only 1 seat available in all sections. So now we don't get to go because their website ticking is HORRIBLY run. I'm completely disappointed and we will fine another way to enjoy our 1st anniversary. 

Thank you Bluebird Cafe for ruining our plans with your defunct ticketing service.

We waited in line for several hours to get in for the late-night show. IT WAS COMPLETELY WORTH IT! 

Our seats were front row center. The ambiance, music, and general vibe of the Bluebird was incredible. 

If you're coming here looking for a good meal, you will be disappointed. Come having eaten and be prepared to wait in line.
This place was the best part of Nashville, which was a great experience on its own. We had literally the best waitress I have ever had (shout out to Virginia) and she is the GOAT.

Worth the wait!

My mom and I waiting in line for 2.5 hours to get into the early show. It was 90+ out and really muggy. But, all that heat and sweat was worth it. Once we got inside the vibe of the venue was buzzing with excitement. Each and every person was excited to be apart of the upcoming show. 

We saw a songwriter association show. The music was better than most songs on the radio and that isn't an exaggeration. Each song was original and the singers voices were amazing. 

Next time I'm in Nashville, I'll make sure to go to another show here. If you have a few hours to spare, get down there and check out a show!

Dined here for breakfast on the weekend. The service was excellent. The hostess and wait staff was very attentive.  The food came out pretty quickly. I ordered the sweet potato pancakes. I should have taken a picture. I would have liked for my pancakes to have been warmer; nonetheless they tasted great. The atmosphere was really nice. Initially I anticipated a diner atmosphere because of the lunch counter. But it was more casually dining. Music and videos play on the screen, very tasteful. I've wanted to eat at Woolworth's on 5th for some time. Finally had the opportunity.

Good experience overall. Service was friendly but not particularly adept. We all liked our entrees a lot - salmon, shrimp and grits, and bistro steak. But the desserts all disappointed - fruit cobbler, strawberry shortcake, and bread pudding. Three people including desserts was about $150 with tip so it's not cheap.

Lots of fun the first night we went. It wasn't too crowded and the band was amazing. The bartender was right on top of things, asking as soon as we walked in the door if we'd like a drink. Tried to go again tonight but it was way too crowded. Couldn't even get in.
I love this place for the history, ambiance, friendly staff and amazing food and drinks! Woolworth in fifth is a must if you're downtown.

What fun to get a seat in this iconic venue for a live show!! We waited in line for an hour to get into a 9:30 pm Monday night first-come-first-served show. Those who arrived closer to 8:30 risked not getting a seat. 

Super cozy and personal inside - you fill every seat in the house, so the last ones in get split up to single spots. Nothing fancy, and mediocre single person restrooms. 

Beverage selection was ok, food choices were basic. The music was exceptional! Some apparel and souvenirs available. They prefer cash for admission, but could handle a credit card. 

Definitely a place to appreciate the significance in the Nashville music scene (moreso than the food, bevs, and ambiance).

Allow a little extra time to find a parking spot. The atmosphere was casual and fun, live music doesn't start till nine. 
 The potted smoke AMAZING! Boiled peanuts were deliciously salty and tender. The greens were so very good! The Mac was lackluster.
 The cocktails were very tasty but they were out of the syrup for the one we wanted which was disappointing.
 Going on a weekend? Get a reservation or be prepared for a wait. I will be going back to sample more of the menu!

Came here for a Bloody Mary and sat at the counter. Really neat history of what the space used to be. They were playing old time videos and music. They had a neat upstairs and kept a lot of the original fixtures and decor.

We weren't able to get reservations so my friend and I decided to stand in line to see if we could get in! We got there 30 minutes before the doors opened at 7:30pm for a Sunday night 8:00pm show and got into the pews in the back! It's actually small enough that you can still see well and communicate with the servers! You order food and drinks at the bar and they bring the rest to you! The music was incredible, Service was very kind and swift, and overall a wonderful place to spend an evening! Highly recommend!
Alex is the shit & needs a raise$$$ asap. Bob Franklin is a genius for this bar. Respectfully from the Shane Johnson's bachelor party 7/2917. Again Alex deserves a $$$$! Savage

Trailer trash.... Oh yes! 

This is the second time to the park, and I have had a blast every time! Live music and it's usually very loud! However, we stopped on a Monday afternoon and the music was fantastic and the performers were awesome. We chatted with them while we enjoyed ice cold beers. The bartender was great and attentive. Now that is a fantastic Monday in my book! 

Ok the decor is hilarious... Green astro turf, a pontoon, broken down car, beers are iced down in bath tubs, and you order your food out of the food truck. The bumper sticker that are posted are hilarious... Sorry not appropriate to write, so y'all know they are bad as I don't hold back much. There are old school box TV's with Jerry Springer or other trashy shows like that. Paradise park does not miss a thing. 

The food is good and greasy... Perfect place to soak up all the booze you have consumed on Broadway. 

Game day wear your predator's jersey and get a free beer. 

Love this dive and can't wait to go back!

If you are looking for a tourist trap, this is your place. Seriously, if you have the urge to say "I went to Tootsie's and had a beer", visit the airport location-less crowded, less dirty, better environment, but still expensive. Just don't let on your Tootsies was on the Gate C ramp and not lower Broadway.

Went in for a few drinks before the Garth Brooks concert, was extremely crowded but we made our way to back of the bar, got lucky and 2 were leaving so we got their seats. Bartenders were extremely friendly and very good at their job. Bands were ok, begging for tips . A fun 3 hours, would have liked to walked around and looked at all the history on the walls and went upstairs to check out but didn't. Will definitely go back on our next weekend trip

This place is pretty famous in that it is right next to the Ryman Auditorium. It has several sections including an alleyway entrance, a main entryway, and a rooftop section. 

We found a spot in the front section and listened to some live music while drinking a couple of beers. 

Every place on the strip has terrific live music from struggling but talented musicians who play for tips. The music is mostly country with some blues mixed in.
Such a fun place. It gets extremely crowded, so be prepared to be squished. The music is very entertaining, usually a very fun and friendly crowd. Good drink prices.
Kassidy was awesome! Made our entire experience even better. Great bar tender great service. Great music.

The Stone Fox is this weird little conundrum for me. I really enjoy the local musical acts they bring in, their involvement with the community, the fact that they're casual..... But jiminy crickets.... most every time I've been in there the service is pretty awful. There's been times when we were sat outside and forgotten about. Times when we were sat then completely ignored by staff who were very clearly serving the tables next to us. It's definitely a "grown-up hipster" kind of vibe... like the east nashville hipster crowd are growing up and moving to West Nashville to mate and procreate....
