Which you know.... would be cool if you're in their clique. If you're not it's definitely a place you have to be ready for the judge-y faces and occasional eye roll. Now, some of the staff..... once asked for service can be pretty friendly.... it's just weird that you have to bring attention to yourself after sitting there for 30min-1hr sometimes. Food wise... it's alright. I personally don't enjoy the food and find it relatively overpriced. But.... again - some of the events they host are pretty awesome. If you overlook the staffing issues and eat before you go...chances are you'll have a pleasant time. There's drinking so as long as you can have a good time without too many expectations.... it's cool. Though avoiding it all together won't destroy your evening.

I'd say it's more like 3.5 stars. After reading some of the reviews about how the wait staff was unfriendly and food often came out cold, I was a bit concerned about what my experience would be like. 

My roommate & I arrived around 7PM on a Friday night for dinner, and a friend of hers joined us shortly thereafter. The place was fairly empty, maybe only about half full, which was somewhat surprising. 

Positives: 

- Our waitress (I believe her name was Mariah?) was one of the best waitresses I've had at any establishment in a long time. She was incredibly helpful with her recommendations of beers on tap and was just an awesome, friendly person. Far from the poor reviews other patrons have given the waitstaff. 

- My dinner: I ordered the chicken tenders, which were amazingly good. They were tender, juicy and perfectly fried. I ordered honey mustard to go with them (which they apparently make in-house) and it was a great combo for both the tenders and fries. I'm STILL thinking about those tenders!

Negative:

- We ordered the sundried tomato & basil flatbread as an appetizer and I wasn't particularly bowled over by it. The cheese seemed to have a bit of a rubber consistency and I couldn't really taste much of the sundried tomato element of it. It definitely came up short. 

By 9PM, the place had filled up and was packed for the live music that was about to begin. We stayed for about an hour into the set and the crowd seemed to be into it, but it wasn't music I have much knowledge of, so I'll abstain from giving my opinion on that. 

All in all, it was a much better experience than I thought I might have, given the other reviews. If you go for dinner, I HIGHLY recommend the chicken tenders, but avoid the sundried tomato & basil flatbread. I'll definitely be back (and hope to have Mariah as my waitress again)!

The Blue Bird Cafe is incredibly cool and what a great vibe! It was really cool to be in a place that holds so much history of music legends. We had reservations and didn't have to wait outside in line too long. Our server was wonderful. Watching "in the round" was very cool and it really does feel like you are "sitting in your living room listening to music with family". Wonderful experience.

I am so happy I got to experience a show at The Bluebird. This is a must-do for anyone visiting Nashville. I never even liked country music but felt so connected to the artists due to the intimate setting and of course their talent. Fell in love with Bluebird and Nashville last night.

Stopped in for lunch for the first time. I love the historic authenticity of the place. 

The food was hot, fresh, and delicious. I tried the fried flounder with collard greens and grits. Loved it. 

I would have given them five stars but the service at the counter was disappointingly slow.  There were at least three servers behind the counter and it was past the lunch rush so there was no reason for it. Not sure if they all thought I belonged to the others, but it was a big downer to an otherwise positive experience.
We walked in to be part of the crowd appreciating the music and atmosphere there, live band is energetic, place is set up nicely, staff super friendly and no fee to go inside, highly recommend!

Heard this place is one of the most desired place in Nashville as well as REALLY hard to get into. Only 18+ place in MILES. Luckily got in here. Music was great and the guys were funny. Waitress Ericka was RUDE.  Got snappy with a few of us sitting around me as well as myself when asking for water. But good thing it's about the music I suppose.

I loved the atmosphere.Our server was nice but was not very attentive.
We had breakfast it was really good after a bit of a wait. My main Con
is that they need more Woolworth type foods on the Lunch menu.
Patty Melt, Chicken Salad, Soups and must have milk shakes etc.
I completely agree that evening is fine but lets really take it back to that era.

The historic value of this place is enough to get you in the door of this Downtown Nashville gem but the food and flair will easily keep you there for a great meal!! We started with the deviled eggs, then moved into entrees of Pork Chops and Fried Flounder, before topping off the delicious meal with an absolutely perfect Pecan Pie variation that complimented everything beautifully! Excellent service, welcoming atmosphere, and a delight for the taste, visual, and auditory senses. If you are a local or just visiting for a trip, don't miss out on adding this place to your "must visit" list!!!

I finally got tickets here using the tried and true method.  Basically I woke up Monday morning and had my browser ready to go before 8am.  I hit refresh and landed 4 tickets at a large table.  First of all, the venue is near the Green Hills mall.  I don't know why this never dawned on me but it didn't.  Why does this matter?  It matters because you need to account for traffic.  We were actually running a little late which was very stressful for me after fighting so hard to get the tickets but the girls at the front desk actually called me.  How cool is that?  I let them know we were close and they held our seats.  

It is true what they say about being a listening room.  You do have to be quiet.  That's actually a little hard for me - to sit still that long.  I'm not sure if I would go back based upon the fact that you have to be so still for a couple hours but I'm thankful I got to enjoy it.  The food was mediocre but inexpensive.  The music was very fun.  We had three artist the night we visited and I felt like we had a wonderful range.  We heard everything from Bluegrass to white girl rap.  Give it a try if you can!

I tried this bar twice during my stay in Nashville as everyone recommended it, but was unfortunately disappointed. Both times I walked in, checked out each floor and walked right back out because I could not move - which I guess is a testament to how good it is if so many people are always there! However, not being able to walk isn't exactly my cup of tea. I will say the second I walked in the second time the bartender made eye contact with me and asked if I wanted a drink - I definitely appreciated that. I'm sure the service is great. I only purchased one beer there unfortunately. If you want to be where everybody is (and I mean everybody) then it might be for you.

The food was delivered ice cold - the tacos looked like they had been sitting for a very long time. The hollandaise and ham on the benedict, along with the potatoes, were cold to the touch. The wait staff quickly returned the food to the kitchen and brought us a slightly warmer meal. The food was fine, but not stellar. All that was after we waited an hour to get seated, only to find that our space had been deleted. The app apparently had a glitch. Loved the bluegrass. Just not worth the drive out of the downtown area.

First word of advice: please encourage your staff to NOT ask patrons if they are pregnant. It's incredibly rude.

That was my first interaction walking into the establishment so I was immediately put off. We got a cute bubbly waitress, but she brought us glasses of water that were in fact just glasses of ice, to which later she realized her mistake. We then asked for sugar for our coffee since there was only sweet n low on the table. Our waitress said they didn't have packets of sugar but she could bring us some from the tub of sugar they use to make sweet tea. 

The food was decent so my review has nothing to do with the quality and quickness of the food, which we received soon after ordering and enjoyed. I mainly was very upset at the assumption that I was pregnant and a ditzy server who seemed very confused.

I really enjoyed this venue. My friend and I got there pretty early but sat at the bar and had a couple of drinks and the mezza appetizer. Despite incredibly small olives (we were just really confused by that) the food was good. The white sangria was delicious, I would probably come back just for that. Both the front and the back porches were relaxed. I've heard great things about brunch and I can't wait to go back for that!

This is a new stakehouse that I have never been to before but this is probably one of my favorites so far. I got the New York strip and so did one if the people I ate with. My stake what medium rare but the meat itself was surprisingly soft when you chew and the fat on the end was the melt in your mouth kind of fat.but the reason i give it a 4 star is because the other persons stake was not so soft and was not so medium rare but still good. If I ever come back to Nashville I think I would eat here again. 4/5 - 5/5

Okay - this place is right next to Sinema and I had no idea it existed until I recently popped in for a business lunch...IT IS SO GOOD! 

I ordered the sweet potato hummus and avocado salad. The avocado salad was just alright - a little too much dressing. But the sweet potato hummus was fricken delicious! I loved the overall vibe of the place and the service was fast! Parking kinda sucks, it is a small lot so if you've got a group, you may wanna carpool or uber there. 

I'd love to come back here for dinner or during a weekend night to listen to live music and get drinks. I'm stoked it's only 10 minutes away from where I live, I'll be back soon Sutler!

Edit to Add: I came back recently for brunch and was so so impressed. My fiance ordered the chicken and biscuits, I had the breakfast tacos....we also had the bottomless mimosas. The food was amazing and they had a bluegrass band playing. I will DEFINITELY be coming back ASAP - I'm obsessed with this place!!

Have never once written a yelp review so this is my first. Wow!! Okay so my wife took me here this past Saturday evening for my birthday, and wow! It didn't fail to live up to the hype. The music was amazing and so much fun to see live these songs we knew. 
The food was amazing, my wife and I ordered the chicken mozzarella sandwich and the caprese both so delicious. I NEED that ranch recipe it was the best I've ever tasted. (And I own a restaurant back home so I know) The food was far better than I had been thinking it would be. The drinks were local brews and all great beers. Great selection all around. Our waitress was amazing and so sweet to each of our needs. Thank you again nashville and blue bird cafe for the best birthday I've had in years. This is a fun and great night out, so happy to have been able to have come here.

Awesome experience! They do an excellent job of recreating the lunch counter/diner feel! Food was great, got the Egg Salad Sandwich with shoestring fries, wifey got French Dip with Sweet Potatoe Fries. Both were generous portions with my egg salad falling out perfectly! Wonderful staff and atmosphere with superb food. Highly recommended!!!!

Worth the wait! Got there at 4pm and just got in to the 6pm show! Ended up with great seats on the floor. Had the fried green tomatos. There is no cover charge but a $10 spending minimum! This is great place. The music was authentic and incredible to hear while in Nashville for a short time. Highly recommend! :)

Our server kim was exceptional!  She was extremely attentive and went above and beyond to give us a great dining experience. The food was great and very reasonably priced. I loved looking at the many historical photos throughout the building and the atmosphere is very charming.

My chips that came with my pulled chicken tacos were stale. Service was so slow and they weren't busy. This used to be one of my favorite places. The Sutler was out of Amarillo by morning. How do you run out of margaritas??? We had to ask for silverware and napkins after our food arrived. There was something stuck to the dirty menu too. I doubt I will return.

It's difficult to put into words how cool it is to go to the Bluebird Cafe if you're a country music fan. The venue is so small and intimate, and realizing just how many amazing artists got their start here is unbelievable. 

Yes, it's difficult to get tickets. We didn't get tickets so we showed up an hour and a half early and got in without a problem. The first 8 in line get seats at the bar and then next 10-12 get church style pew seats. From what I gathered, there is no cover charge for these seats during the early show, just a $7/person food & drink minimum. 

Honestly I can't speak to the food because I didn't eat it, but no one goes for the food. 

Do yourself a favor and make the extra effort to get in here. It's worth the trouble.
Angel was our bartender and she was amazing!!  Quick to serve and so friendly!  Tip well!!

I'd give tootsie's 4.9. We watched the NBA game 7 while listening to a great band...can't complain. The drinks were small and heavy on the ice for the price. Service was good. Restroom service was on point...bring a tip!  The line moved and it was clean!! Different live bands on all 3 levels. Outside seating on the roof.

This place was crazy!!! So incredibly busy. The drink menu consists of sweet alcoholic drinks. I left with a sweet belly after trying a few of their cocktails. Super fun country bar with a party atmosphere!!!!

I stopped at Tootsie's while staying in Nashville for one night.  I was driving from NY to Seattle alone.  

This place is probably better if you're with a group.  I thought that the crowd was kind of trashy (i.e. completely wasted on a Sunday night at 8:30 PM), the drinks were weak, and the music was meh.  There was a cover band playing country pop and it wasn't that impressive.

This place is incredibly difficult to get into to see a performance. Thankfully 6 of us were able to get tickets through the online portal and sit close together. It's a very cool and intimate venue to come listen to up and coming artists. They serve food and drinks immediately as you are seated and service is very speedy. However, the staff were rude to members of our group multiple times throughout the evening. Seems to be a theme as I've read from some previous postings as well. 5 star place if you replaced the staff with friendly people!

Wife and I were in town and decided to try and get into the Blue Bird Sunday night. We got there about 5pm and the line was just starting to form. We sat at the bar and had a great view of the stage. The Bartender Tim was awesome and made us feel right at home. Had the chicken quesedias (sp) and sweet potatoe fries, they were good, but we didn't go there for the food. The place was great, all the song writers were very entertaining, and the atmosphere was very intimate and personal. Loved it and would suggest you go if you love country music and the story behind the music.

Amazing. If you enjoy raw, live music, you will love it here. There are no bad seats in the house. The waitstaff was incredibly prompt and friendly. 

The food is...edible. That's about all I can say for it. We ordered nachos and they used "stadium cheese" or velveta and canned chilli, pretty sad. And the drinks were Very weak. BUT it still gets 5 whole stars because you are there for the music!

Didn't actually get to go, but wanted to say that you need to get there extremely early for the Sunday night writers nights to have even a remote chance of getting in.  I called 2 1/2 hours before show time and was told they were already at max.  I'd guess you need to be there 4 hours early.  For the reservation shows, make sure you log on and buy the second you are able to, the Saturday night show sold out in less than 1/2 hour.

The bartender went back and forth with me because I asked for my drink to be remade. I was not rude whatsoever but he was so rude for no reason that I honestly felt like he was racist. After my friend addressed his rudeness he replied " I can't wait for y'all to leave". Wow! I won't be back bc apparently I'm not welcome

Finding myself in Nashville again and wanting to visit Tootsie's . This time I climbed all the stairs to get to rooftop. It had a beautiful view and a lot of legendaries musicians have performed here. Everyone should check this place out when in town. The collection of pictures hanging and signed by artists is something to view.

Tootsie's is one of the most famous/popular bars on Broadway. 

Came at 6 pm on a Friday and it was pretty packed and full already.

Was at the top level, the bar was small. They have a big stage for live music. Luckily we arrived right when the band was going to start. Tips for request. 

Crowd was very energetic and sang to the music. Once the music starts, you are shoulder to shoulder with people. Very hard to move and gets really cramped. We found seats at the bar so it was not as bad.

Bartenders were good. Came around pretty fast. Drink prices were ok. Higher then normal but expected for such a popular spot.

Honky Tonk Mule - $10 - Decent mix drink, crappy whiskey though.
Jameson Ginger - $10 - Good, it was not drowned in the ginger ale.
Bud Light - $7

I'm not sure I have ever written a bad review for anywhere I have been before, but after my experience here I needed to share. A friend and I were so excited to get brunch here this weekend while in town and it was a complete let down. The first thing brought to my table was my coffee which had a bug floating in it when the waitress sat it on the table and somehow got annoyed when I asked for it to be replaced. Shortly after that our food arrived, but not a single thing at our table was even slightly warm. We tried to eat it because we didn't want to send it back understanding they were busy, but it was awful. We didnt see our waitress after food was dropped off for probably 20 minutes and by that point we just asked for checks, paid for the mostly uneaten food, and left. I definitely wouldn't recommend this place for a brunch outing.

Eh. I was here for a wedding party but you can only order food at the main floor bar (strike one - they have 3 bars (upstairs, main floor, and downstairs, but only one with food). So I go to the main bar to order food as advised, and the meatloaf sounded awesome so I ordered it. For $24 I was hoping for a portion size larger than two of your average chicken McNuggets. It was GOOD - but very very tiny: strike two. Strike three is the complete lack of decent parking nearby -- I did valet parking for $12 as that was the only option. So basically $36 plus tax and tip for two bites of meatloaf and some veggies. I'll be skipping this one in the future.

Four phrases: Come for the music, drink to get to the minimum tab required, avoid food, and order your tickets as early as possible. Just assume every night will be sold out (supposedly open mic nights are the only exception to this rule). You will have to wait in line for 1 hour+ in order to even find out if you get to go in and have a seat that went untaken from someone who did buy a ticket. It's a risk that isn't really worth it I think and I got lucky tonight only because I was alone and was very flexible. Out of our whole line of about 20 people, 4 people got in, all split into individual seats. 

Think of this place as less cafe and more "listening studio." You'll get intimately close to up and coming artists. You will feel exclusive, and almost secretive that such good music (even the early show was amazing!) could be in such a small, strip mall, nearly hidden venue. 

However, if you get food, you'll also be mad at the quality, quantity, and price. The hummus I got was $10 and was served with stale, cold, and occasionally crunchy pita. My friend said her BLT was disappointing. Others seemed disappointed in the BBQ Nacho plate. 

Beers are $4.50-$5.50 per beer in most cases.

I got online about 10 minutes early and decided what tables I would like for the two of us do I could pick when it opened at 8am.  I was able to get my first choice but you have to be online right then because it sold out in 5 minutes when I checked back. 
The music was great. Caroline Watkins and Parker Welling were awesome!
Food was awful. We had fried green tomatoes,nachos, roast beef club and chicken tenders. Drinks were good. I had a Cosmo. 
Go for the music and just order drinks!

I would do five stars based on the beer selection, great food, the bar environment, music, etc.

But, what I will say about my overall experience, cover the top of your glass.

Atmosphere galore.  Shrimp and grits great, fried chicken very good, gumbo very good.  Cheeseburger ordered medium, came out blackened, tough yet cold.  Fries meh and cold.  Chocolate malt, however, room temp.  3 out of 4 is a fair rating.

What I totally expected out of a bar in Downtown Nashville...

Lots of white people (I love white people, by the way), flannel shirts out of the wah-zoo, loud music and lots of drinking. I didn't realize they had multiple stories but somehow I ended up on the top floor where they had an outdoor patio. I felt like I was in the center of Downtown as a 360 view gave me a wave of all the Downtown buildings.

I continued my margarita binge and listened to some good ol' country music while enjoying the nice evening weather. Cool spot, I suppose!

It was fun to stop in for a drink at a Nashville institution like Tootsie's. There was live entertainment with the singer walking down the actual bar during her set. I only stayed on the bottom floor, but the place kept going up to the rooftop.
A must while in Nashville! They always have great music and strong drinks! The bartenders are a little slow but the pours are good.

Hands down the funnest bar in Nashville! There's a variety of music and live bands to choose from. There are 3 floors plus a little outdoor section. The vibe on each floor varies, I found that the first floor you can go and just hang out with friends or on a date and listen to music and relax. As the floors get higher, I guess so does your level of intoxication cause the 3rd floor was the dance party. So much fun, I totally recommend--And there's no cover.

If you are looking for a trendy  fancy place.... this is not for you. Now, if you are looking for a good old bar,  full of history , great live music,  and a good stiff drink at a decent price... This is your place! Their bloody Mary did not look the best, but I was Pleasantly surprised at how good they made it. Definitely recommend this place, lots of history, it's a must go to if you're in the area just to say you've been there.

Incredible location in the heart of downtown in a beautifully restored and historically rich space. Atmosphere had a really nice, simple elegance while still feeling extremely relaxed and familiar. Host staff were warm and inviting. Sitting at the bar was a great call as the bartenders were welcoming and knowledgable.  Mikey, Freddy, Adam, and Fletcher made sure we had an amazing experience, and the food and drinks were excellent! Can't wait to try everything! Hightlights: Five and Dime (cocktail), pickled shrimp (app), cheese curds (app), corn pudding (side), black eyed peas (side), fried flounder (entree), bourbon caramel pecan pie (dessert)

This venue is pretty terrible. I've been to many outdoor venues and this one is the worst. The gravel walkways are awful. If you wear anything other than tennis shoes,  it sucks for you. I wouldn't even try sandals because there a few steep places that make it easy to slip. There are no clear pathways to get through and once the lights go out it's practically impossible to get around. People will not move and the folding chairs all kind of link together and you can't get through. You will trip over blankets and stuff bc there's very little lighting. The stage is basically something they set up and break down for a fair. Ticket prices are too high for such a small venue and poor facility. Oh... If it rains anytime during the week... Bring your mud boots. The only good thing about it is free parking and great bands. If it's not someone you REALLY want to see. Pass on this venue. Wait for them to play the Ryman. #BringBackStarwood

Well, be assured that  the wait to get in or the hassle you survive to get tix is worth it. Of course, most folks go for the music which never fails to surprise, intrigue, and entertain, but the requirement to spend a certain minimum on food is actually a good thing because otherwise people would miss out on what is surpisingly tasty fare!

It's only appropriate that my 100th review be at a legendary place. And legendary it was. The bluebird cafe did not disappoint. It was the highlight of my trip to Nashville and one of my favorite all-time things I have ever done. that's right. Ever.

We basically winged it... and got lucky! We were told that without a ticket I(which apparently sell out in less than 5 minutes after ticket sales open 1 week before every show) , we'd have to wait about 2 hours in the waitlist line only for a CHANCE to get in on the about 25 bar and pew seats. Well we were enjoying a dinner, and at first had planned on going to the listening room cafe afterwards for live music but thought we were already all the way in Nashville.. there was no harm in winging it and trying our luck in getting in for our chance to listen to live music where legendary songwriters and artists perform or are discovered.

So we didn't get to the bluebird cafe until about 9pm for a 930 show and despite the warnings of FAT CHANCE, we STILL GOT IN and got great seats in the first row of the pew (which is way more comfortable than the bar seats)!!!!

Finally the show... what can I say... Don Schlitz put on an incredible performance. And to be able to sing along to Randy Travis songs that I knew from childhood from the songwriter himself was priceless. He was an awesome performer-- talented, funny, charming, and a great entertainer!

Got ourselves a bottle of Reisling wine and enjoyed it while listening to awesome music. Although any wine would have been just fine when we were already in musical bliss.
Nice view from rooftop,  multiple levels and bars on every section keep the drinks going.  Music was good with different acts on every stage but still overcrowded for me.

Typical college bar - I didn't think it was anything special. Came here with a large group for dinner and beers. Food was okay, nothing to write home about. There was a band playing in the background that was pretty terrible so it was somewhat annoying to have to listen to that while eating. Probably won't come here again unless I'm completely inebriated.
Loved it!  Great food and service.  Cool history too.  Recommend !!!  My first Nashville chicken and it was great!  HOT but, great.  Will return on my next visit.
We didn't get tickets but waited in line for 1 1/2 and scored two seats inside. Was worth the wait and really cool to see. Very small inside and they pack the house.
Super cute bar! Very old but has a lot of history behind the honky tonk. Great live music - loved the upstairs and rooftop. Fun place to go at night or during the day. I will be back!

LOVE this place!  Always a good show where you also make new (very close)friends. A Nashville trip is not complete without three things: Roberts Western World, Station Inn and The Bluebird...and Loveless, must have Loveless.

The first time I came to Tootie's I was really disappointed, there was an open-mic on but it was a bit slapdash and though my friends and I had been hoping to sing, we felt a bit discouraged by the loud crowd-- at one in the afternoon! But that's Nash-Vegas for you. 
Luckily a new visitor arrived into our group and she was dying to see the World-cam that they had set up, as she had told her friends to look out for her. We arrived back in Tooties and I'm so delighted we did! We had an incredible time here-- the band was just crazy and I'm sad I don't remember their name but they had Michelle Lambert on fiddle and she just blew the house out. Girl is hot sh*t. I didn't even care that we were in the cheesiest most touristy part of town-- we had an amazing night. 
The frontman of the band was also fantastic and was all over the bar getting everyone to sing and they were well worth a few tips-- they even let my amazing singer friend Cherry get up and do a number on stage and the crowd loved it. 
The staff at Tootsies  are fantastic, loads of banter and really quick to get drinks. Been there, literally bought the t-shirt. 
LOVE YOU TOOTSIES
Great prompt service for new friends in town before happy hour.  Hope you enjoy it here too.

I have lived in Nashville for 5 years and finally made it over to the Sutler. I've consistently heard locals rave about this place (particularly because of their bottomless brunch mimosas). My roommate and I were hungry, and decided to make our way on over to this notorious eatery. It was a bit packed, granted it was a Friday night, but we were able to snag one of the only open booths left. It's seat your self, so keep that in mind when going there!

Live music was playing, which is always nice on a weekend in Nashville, bonus points because it was a recent Voice contestant leading the live music. We started off with drinks, the strawberry-lemonade sangria pitcher was our choice, and it was pretty delicious, I would definitely order it again. My friend ordered a club sandwich and mac and cheese, she raved about the sandwich, but was a bit underwhelmed by the mac and cheese. I wasn't too hungry but got the whipped pimento, which was pretty tasty (nothing crazy amazing though). I have a pretty big sweet tooth so I also ordered the chocolate jar...it was huge--but hit the spot.  

The service was great, our waitress was so helpful, so attentive despite how packed it was. We ended the night by going right downstairs where they have a cocktail bar called, Rambler. They also have a billiards bar which we didn't have enough time to check out. So much to do in such a small space, I'll have to come back and check it out again!

Rachel was our waitress and she was AMAZING. Friendliest service, didn't rush us at all and had a wonderful time. Highly recommend this breakfast if you need to kill time and want to listen to good music. Rachel is the best, she gave us amazing recommendations of things to do in Nashville. Can't wait to explore this city

So worth the wait!! 

This cute little cafe is located in a strip mall and it is super famous because of the show Nashville (sorry never watched it but a friend dragged me along to this venue). We got there at 3:45PM  an waited in line close to 2 hours. It was a little hot outside and we were not exactly prepared but made friends with others in line and the time flew by. They even brought water for us as we were waiting (which was so nice). 

Once we got in we got seated in the benches in the back of the room. The venue was very small and intimate and we both absolutely loved the show. The food was not bad either - also very reasonably priced!

Love Tootsie's!  The band is always pretty good and willing to take requests.  

PSA: Bring some cash for tip money.  I like to remind folks to bring cash because so many people don't carry cash anymore but when going out to the Nashville bars, tips are often how musicians make their money!

Well, back to it!  If you don't like crowded places or people possibly bumping into you or touching you, this probably isn't the place for you!  

Tootsie's is often crowded at anytime of the day.  It is one of the original bars in Nashville and is iconic!!!!  I have never had a bad time, though have found it difficult to get in during busy times!!  If you are visiting Nashville, I would definitely say you should make a trip to visit Tootsie's!!
I had so much fun here! Great venue and live music was mind blowing.  Jackson, Courtney and their band were first class.  Crowd was a bit rowdy but added to the energy.

The food and music at Tin Roof is fine. My main issue is cleanliness. I live near this restaurant and six out of seven days every week there is a lot of trash in front of Tin Roof. Demonbreun Hill is home to many restaurants and bars and with the exception of Tin Roof and Two Bits all the other establishments clean the area in front of their restaurants daily. At best this is unsightly and rude to neighbors. At worst it's a health and environmental hazard. Please clean up in front of your restaurant and place a trash can in front too. That would likely help!
Stopped in just for a beer and music. Loved the place. Intimate setting and outstanding band.

Went on a Thursday night around 7pm and I was shocked how empty this place was.  We started off with almost every appetizer and the deviled eggs were the best!  I ordered the steak and it was cooked to perfection, awesome flavor.  This place is perfect, not crazy but great food.
The food was fantastic, and we received great service from our waitress Kim! I recommend getting the Patty Melt. Their milkshakes are handmade and were so good!

I enjoyed breakfast here, with friendly service and historical roots. I made a reservation for 10:15am but didn't need it. After getting our table we were forgotten about for 5-10 min but once the staff realized that error we were served quickly. 

The breakfast menu isn't huge but there are several hearty options. The only real gluten-free option is the eggs, bacon, and home fries, and pray the seasoning doesn't have wheat maltodextrin. Next trip to town we will stop for lunch or dinner.

Three of us had breakfast/lunch there today.  The cheese omelet was huge and delicious.  One of our party ordered two eggs medium with bacon.  The eggs came out well done with two slices of bacon.  You would think they would serve at least three slices for what they charged.  I ordered the corned beef hash with two eggs over medium.  My eggs were very well done instead of medium.  The hash was great and more than enough to fill me up.  It contained chunks of corned beef, onions, black eyed peas and potatoes.  The seasoning was just right.  We didn't have to wait too long for our food which was impressive as they were busy.

The interior is amazing, our server couldn't have been better and the manager checked with us twice even with a full house.  I would have given a five if our eggs were cooked properly.  We plan on going to dinner next.

Came to tootsies for a bachelorette party on a Friday afternoon around 4pm. It was absolutely packed!!!! Live music on multiple floors and different bars on each floor. You can get food on one of them. We spent most of our time on the top level because we loved the band there. Solid selection of beers. Walked down a few floors for some bar food...nothing to write home about but got the job when we were hungry.

It is a great place and a short walk from TPAC so you do not need to move your car if going to both. My last meal here in this building was about 1959 before I left Nashville for another university and was also working at Cain-Sloans on the corner of 5th and Church. My friend and i had jambalaya and the meat loaf for entrees. My jambalaya was fabulous and the meat loaf seemed to have been frozen before it was cooked and was very mediocre for this main dish. Definitely not the taste I remember when coming there for years before I was 19. There also was no bread with the  meat loaf and vegges. The dessert bread pudding with a warm whisky brown sugar sauce was terrific with ice cream. This had been suggested by our very friendly and efficient waiter. I gave it a 4 instead of a 5 as the meat loaf was such a disappointment, but try it and take your children and grandchildren for a history lesson as well as a good meal in a lovely atmosphere..

We had the BEST time at Woolworth before a TPAC show! They made us feel like special guests from the moment we got there. From our excellent server Rick to the great chef Martine! We got to sample the pork belly and deviled eggs (yummmmm) and loved our entrees (grilled chicken salad, fried chicken salad and meatloaf). All were incredible! Then Martine spoiled us with an amazing dessert (bacon, brûléed bananas and more!) 

Amazing!

Stayed at the Comfort Inn across the street and this was a great place to go if you were not looking for the chaos of downtown. It has indoor and outdoor seating and also 2 sections to the bar with live music.

We came here during the day and it was relatively quiet. Prime seating at the bar and everyone, including the bartenders, are super friendly. The guy sitting next to me even gave me one of his wings to try before I ordered my own.

Def worth checking out if you are staying across the street.

The food was great! However, our service was not. Once we got our food, we didn't see our server. We waited longer to get our check than to get our food. Once we received it, we waited another ten minutes to have it picked up with our credit card. We finally put cash on the table and left.

You can't beat the price on the endless mimosas! My friends and I went during brunch on a Saturday so of course it was busy, but we were able to start on our mimosas while we waited for our table. Our server was attentive and friendly. My mimosa glass was rarely empty because she was on top of the refills! My food was good, so I'll definitely be going back.

If I could give this bar a -10, I would.  This is by far the most overcrowded, hot, noisy, and annoying bar.  Everything is filthy, you can't move inside and you feel like you're packed in like sardines, it smells awful, etc.  There are three stories to this place, and each story is the same thing.  I stayed there for about 10 minutes and the whole time I got bumped into, couldn't move, and couldn't hear any of my friends. Oh, and the drinks are small and overpriced. NOBODY should be spending their time here while in Nashville, to put it nicely.

We went for dinner on Saturday night, and had absolutely wonderful experience. We had reservations, but plans changed, and we got there almost 90 minutes early. The girls up front, were totally accommodating, got us in right away. "Come on, we'll feed you!!" Is what we were told!!
Got immediately greeted by Eddie, who made all of us feel immediately comfortable and relaxed. He got us seated, introduced himself, made us all smile, and made it seem effortless.
He was attentive, fun and made great recommendations!
The food was amazing, everything came out correctly, and fast.
I had the bacon wrapped meatloaf, my wife the burger, and her dad, the shrimp and grits. It was all delicious, but the highlight may have been the pork belly appetizers!
Don't skip those!
10 out of 10 will be back
Great people and a historic location make this a must visit!!

The brunch menu was slim pickings.  But opted for the sweet potato pancakes and some biscuits-n-gravy.  Both were pretty good.  Want a fan of the bacon side... Might out for something else.  Standard drip coffee, but not terrible. so

Fantastic food, welcoming and friendly service, and a gorgeous cup of real coffee, I highly recommend this historical spot to anyone looking for comfort food. My only complaint is that the heavy, diner style mugs should be available for purchase.

What an amazing night. So happy and lucky to have got tickets on line. Wow. Sons of daughters playing in this intimate setting. A memory to treasure for a lifetime.  I'm so thankful and grateful to have sat with some amazing people during this experience. I really enjoyed the food and amazing music.
Had a great time there yesterday. Awesome music just an over all good time wit 60 plus of my new best friends

This place is the best. Are there really people voting less than 5 stars for the Bluebird? I'll be happy to house another French Dip while listening to amazing intimate live music in your place next time if you aren't into this place. I'm not even a big country music fan, but you'd have to be out of your mind not to love it here. Believe the hype.

We came here because it was walking distance from our Air B&B and I would say it was okay, they had one really refreshing and delicious drink that had cucumber in it. But he food was only okay, nothing really all that special, in fact, the experience was kind of forgettable. My fiance got a burger that he was really excited about and ended up getting another burger the next day from somewhere else because he didn't feel his craving for burgers was satisfied. I had the pork mac and cheese and it was oddly sweet. I was not a fan at all, half the noodles were crunchy and the flavor was just not pleasing to me. The girl who served us was pretty nice and we liked that there was live music playing while we ate, but, that's pretty much every bar in Nashville
I don't know how this place works but the door guy made fun of my husband for holding onto a tote bag we had just bought at a show at the Ryman. I was annoyed.
Fun place. Good music and signature drinks. Beautiful on the roof top.  Good service too.

Came here as part of a "pub crawl" that was anything but. Basically paid 20 bucks for a sheet of paper with a list of bars on it and told it was self directed. It was one of the lamest most cash grabby things I've ever seen. The organizer worked at this bar so I blame them. They even had inaccuracies printed on their piece of paper. It felt like such a scam. 

I ordered this sandwich. The B n C Medley or something like that. Described as beef brisket with queso and peppers. I basically got a bun with a little cheese sauce, some pepers, and probably a half ounce of meat. A half ounce of meat. A half ounce of meat. Another blatant ripoff that. 12 bucks for a sandwich with less meat that a single slice of cold cuts. 

I ordered the fried green tomato appetizer. This was actually good, and came with plenty of pimento cheese, but only 4 tomato slices. 

Drinks were pricy and not very strong. Service was fine. Not the waitresses fault her bosses are so greedy.

When it appears a business' number one goal is not quality or service but the extraction of the maximum amount of cash while providing the minimum in return, I definitely would never be back.

A must-see if you are visiting Nashville and love music (even if you are not as familiar with country music). I loved the intimate setting of the "in the rounds" setup--each artist took turns playing, and it was like getting to sit in on a group of talented friends/ musicians sharing their stories through music. My only complaint is that the online reservations ran out so quickly (within minutes of opening 1 week prior)! Thankfully, we got in after arriving early at 430pm to line up for a stand-by spot as the 13th,14th, and 15th people in line and were seated in the pews, which was still great. So glad we got in, because this was definitely a highlight of the trip.

My wife and I got here at midday and were able to cozy right up to the bar with a great view of the stage. The musicians, namely the lady lead singer, were quite good and very entertaining. I'd go back, but made a difference that we were able to get a seat and stick around awhile.
Fun fun fun!  Did I mention that this place is fun!  Be sure and check it out!

This place was mediocre at best! I understand it is an iconic place, it is a staple here in Nashville, but it looks and feels dirty. 

There are three levels. Which we didn't know at first, so when we arrived we thought it was so crowded we weren't going to find a place to sit. 

Once we walked up the stairs to the second level we were presented with another full bar, tables, and a stage. We decided to have a seat. We ordered appetizers: Buffalo Chicken Wings, Fried Spear Pickles, and Supreme Nachos with Chicken. 

There was nothing original about the food. The performances weren't that good, off key at times, and the tables and walls had lots of writings on them. As if it was 'a thing' to write your name down or a message. Before I could express my thoughts on that, my mother scratched BZ-PZ into the table. Well I guess they happened. Haha 

Sitting at the table I felt like I couldn't have gotten a sliver bc it was so worn down. I also felt like with the moisture sitting in the table the writings that were there could have gotten on my clothes and ruined them. 

Our food which was plated in paper plates, I get it but also....where does the money go? Clearly this place is profitable. However it doesn't show at all in the decor, food, or performances. 

Anyway, after finishing our food, I walked up to the third floor to see what that looked like. Well it was a lot of stairs and the nicest level at a quick glance. There was a patio which looked cool but I was 'Tootsie-d'  out by this point and just wanted to bounce. 

Overall, it is a 'been there done that, don't have to ever go again' kind of a place for me.
Nice idea.  Poorly executed.  Very average food.  Service kind of slow.  Seemed unorganized.

We had to go here! There is so much history here. I was with a group from work and this was a must stop for us.  There was live country music on every level, we went straight to the top.  They have a rooftop patio which affords beautiful views.  We had to make a mark...literally...wrote our names on the wall.

I loved the ambience here.  It was true country.  There were couples slow dancing, friends line dancing and the singer of the band dancing on the bar.  It was everything that I pictured Nashville to be.

Go there!
Great music joint...don't come here for the food...just drinks music and great ole time

Walked in expecting an eclectic take on fine dining. Has a kinda classy feel. Reminded me of the Merchant Tavern in St. John's, NL, a restored, classic brick bank building. Unfortunately, Woolworth's is still Woolworths. Uninspired menu, terrible wait staff. Rushed us from the moment we sat down. (Never bring a main when appetizers were only served 5 mins earlier.) Either poor kitchen coordination or intentional table turning. In any case, if looking for something with similar atmosphere while in St. John's, the Merchant Tavern is 5 star on all accounts. 

Not impressed.

Great place to grab a drink and listen to live music. Classic honkey tonk on broadway. The staff is very friendly and very attentive when getting a drink. Never had any of the food. It is always a bar I stop in when I am in Nashville.

Nothing screams True Nashville like the Bluebird Cafe! If you're lucky enough to score a ticket to their singer/songwriter concert series, it's a must-do! You can thank me later. The Bluebird sells out every night, it is a legendary venue that has reared many of country music's biggest hit songs. 
If you're in Nashville, get on their website to check for showings and to buy tickets. During each show, there are a few pew seats available on a first come first serve basis, but the line for those seats begins hours before the show. 
This was truly an incredible experience! I oils love to come here on a date, hopefully that will happen in the near future :)
Perfect down and dirty Nashville bar with flowing drinks and great live music! Liked having the option is explore a few floors of music/bar options and the views of Broadway from the rooftop deck.
The music is good. But the food is typical greasy bar food. Nothing amazing. The BLT the bread was greasy and kind of burnt. Also they need more gf and keto options.
Too crowded, lots of levels but so does everything else in Nashville, I don't get the nostalgia behind this bar but ok.

Seriously pretentious. Club is in strip mall. Acted like I was crazy when I showed up and wasn't there two hours early. Crowd was listening in parking lot. Go early or don't bother. Door attendant with mullet seriously needs a reality check.

Such an absolute pleasure to have been able to visit Tootsie's! When we came, it was jammed full of people, but nothing that we couldn't handle. It was an incredible experience to come watch live music for the first time in Music City! We only stayed for a few songs because we had other places to be, but I'm sure glad we stopped in! The decorations amongst all the walls were really neat and gave us a glimpse into the history that made Nashville what it is today. It's very cool to think about the artists that once graced the stage here and have made it big. A family member purchased a T-shirt here for me without my knowledge and that was a great surprise and great way to remember where I'd been. The building itself is beautiful inside and out, and has been very well taken care of. I can't wait to one day visit again!
Offered the band naming rights to my 2nd child for a Queen song (preferably "somebody to love" or "Bohemian" and they only knew "Fat bottom girls".  Not what we were looking for.

I go to Nashville a lot !  The only reason we go to Tootsie's is to get the VIP booth with the one of the most fun and amazing  bartenders! Angel makes our whole crew feel like family! We never have to wait for drink and she's constantly making us laugh with her amazing personality.!! I would highly recommend going there just to see angel!! Thanks Tootsie's for making our Nashville experience that much better !!

First time to the bluebird.  We went on a Tuesday night and got there very early and stood in line. It was a rainy night so we got in easily and sat in the pews.  We ordered drinks and some food to eat before the show began. The fish was hot and   very good, I can also recommend the nachos and the blt sandwich. We heard four writers / singers who was all very talented.  We enjoyed it so much, we came back for music in the round the next night and again stood in the line. This time we waited a bit longer but we were seated at a table, next to the performers. We were so close I could have shared our nachos.  Again it was some great music from some young artist.  Recommend highly.

I'm giving this place 3stars because the food wasn't too good, I ordered catfish and red beans and rice the fish was fried too hard,the beans and rice was dry ..the staff was friendly even though when the waitress asked me how was the food I told her and she didn't try to make it right, I will not return here again

Enjoyed our server Jordan! Friendly and happy! I am notoriously indecisive so I love asking servers what they like from the menu. Her recommendations were very delicious! Enjoyed the overall feel of this restaurant. I always have friends asking me where they should go when they come to Nashville so this will definitely be on the list of recommendations!

Went by The Sutler for a later dinner last night. As others have mentioned, the parking is always tricky. We found space in a deck to the right of the strip in which the Sulter is located.  Were seated right away since we agreed to a table close to the stage.  I like the atmosphere at the Sutler and the band was good.  Nice place to enjoy an evening.
Our server was pleasant and seemed attentive. They have a pretty good beer selection including some good local brews. We ordered drafts which were as expected.
I ordered a Saloon Burger, medium well. The burger was fine though not medium well. It was pretty pink inside (this often seems to happen when the kitchen gets busy and tries to get the food out. They don't seem to have the patience for a medium well burger request). This burger is listed as having charred green chilies, red onion and a red chili mayo. I guess given that description, I was expecting a bit more heat than I experienced.
My husband ordered the Reuben, which contained plenty of pastrami.  We both had the house chips with our meals. My chips were great, crispy and a bit on the well cooked side so they were nice and crunchy. His chips looked like they came from a different batch (maybe?) as they were lighter colored and some even a bit soft.
Overall the food was fine, though not outstanding.
Service was very friendly and kind. Food was horrible and we found a piece of plastic in the salad. Will not be returning.

Good breakfast spot but make sure to come early. The place gets packed very quick so if it's a big party try to be there when the restaurant opens. The food was good but a little cold by the time it came out. Overall it's a great place to have brunch!

I'm in town for a bachelorette party, and we have a member in a wheelchair and they claimed they were "wheelchair accessible" which basically means they meet the literal bare minimum for legal accessibility. Our friend could enter the place and that's literally it. The place is 3 floors and she could only enter through "the back" and then could go nowhere else. Didn't apologize and felt no sympathy. It's 2019 - be accessible for all people and quit being discriminatory.

This place was super busy and it's clear why -- the bottomless mimosas and satisfying southern breakfast brunch menu are a big draw. There was live bluegrass playing in the back and a fun saddle to hop on for photo opportunities in the basement.

Everyone enjoyed all the dishes (we shared smoked brisket hash, andouille hash, chicken fried chicken biscuits, french toast, and chicken and waffles) and had a blast taking advantage of the bottomless booze opportunity -- gotta get your ~$18 worth!

Expect a wait if you're there at a popular time, but this restaurant can support a fair-sized group if needed. Service was a bit slow at times, but the place was slammed and we got everything we needed eventually. One tip is to make sure you're aggressive about flagging down the server to refill your mimosas! ;) They come around with pitchers.

Time of visit approximately 11:30 PM
Date of visit 1-26-2019 

Where is the fire marshal in Nashville Tennessee?? 

 This place is out of control. They have no standards to the number of people they allow to come inside. 
On vacation and we visit this place, there were so many people in the downstairs of this place where the band was playing it was dangerously out of control. As my girlfriend and I stood in one spot for over 15 minutes getting pushed and shoved we felt completely helpless as we were yelling for help begging for someone to help us get out of this place. I kept pointing at the female bartender asking for help and they laughed and thought it was funny. Both she and I lowered our heads and shoved our way to the front door as we were getting hit by people and pushed we finally made it to the front door. I tried to speak to the man working the door that was an older gentleman. And he stopped letting people in momentarily but he was then told by someone to start letting them in again. We left this place and I told extremely large security guy working the door that led to the upstairs of this place that what they were doing was against the law and they are not allowed to do this due to various fire codes they are breaking. I told him this was not safe for anyone in this establishment and that I would be reporting this. He then asked me if I owned this building, I told him no. He then put his hands out and said arrest me then. 
 This is a message for the fire marshal of Nashville Tennessee you should get a hold of what's going on in this establishment it's out of control and someone is going to get hurt very seriously. This is unsafe, dangerous end it is only a matter of time before someone gets seriously injured or worse. 
 For the last time let's not forget this is against the law! 
I will never visit this place again. Pathetic is biz Int excellent description of this establishment. Unprofessionalism from the employees is an understatement.

Definitely would not recommend the food here we order a cheese burger and fries and dip trio which was a joke the dips were blah the salsa tasted like paste picante and the guacamole had no flavor the fries that came with the cheese burger were salted to death so I guess this place isn't famous for the food waste of money .

Went here for a bachelorette party dinner. The pineapple mint sangria was delish! Loved the fried pickles and fried ocra and cheese dip. The guacamole trio was really great too.
I ordered the Reuben and it was out of this world good (and I have had many a Reuben). However the best part of the meal was the collard greens. No joke. The BEST collard greens EVER!

We are very happy with our food and service by John. It's New Years Eve and there is w special menu. We chose the garden greens and Filet  mignon. Everything done to perfection. Dancing and drinking were downstairs in a large hall. Great music provided (big band). Lots of happy people, surprisingly many young people and some terrific dancers. The bartenders were on the job. Drinks flowed real quick across the bar. The only criticism of the night was too few chairs for attendees. Lightning valet as well. Good job Chris.

I love coming here! I work in one of the neighboring businesses and me and my coworkers can not resist happy hour or brunch. I recommend this bar to all my friends. Plus, any time Mo (Morgan) is making my drinks they are top notch! Never disappointed

Since we heard this spot is the main spot to hang out on Broadway, we of course decided to make it our first stop on a night out. From the minute we walked in, we were instantly uncomfortable. This place is packed to absolutely capacity and it's nuts to even move around here. The front entrance was so clogged with people waiting to hear the show down there, you literally had to shove your way to get to another floor. Once on the second floor, it was just marginally less packed but we were able to get a bar spot.

The best part of this place is how helpful the bartenders are, as they actually wave you down and ask if you need anything. Usually this is the opposite so its pretty surprising they were able to keep on top of that. There's a cop standing around eyeing everyone down and even though I'm over 21 the guy made me feel like we were doing something wrong. The band playing on the second floor was mediocre at best- I am not a voice coach or anything, but the guy was off key. I think the main attraction was on the first floor but there was no way we were able to squeeze in there.

Prices are OK but this place is just too freaking busy at night.
The fries are great but I'm not so sure how I feel about  the chicken tenders having purple everywhere

Visiting Nashville with a group of friends and we decided to go here because we heard great things about the brunch. Honestly we are all very disappointed. We all got bottomless mimosas and our waitress rarely came to the table to check on us. One of our friends arrived late and asked for a mimosa, and we had to remind the waitress twice that our friend needed a mimosa. We have watched other servers be much more attentive to their tables. Other servers would refill the mimosas before they were empty and our mimosas would be empty for 10 minutes at a time, and we usually had to ask her for a refill. The mimosas were not strong at all either. They were bright orange with barely any champagne. If they are going to offer $17 bottomless mimosas than they need to be staffed correctly and know how to make a proper mimosas
All of my friends who got breakfast food thought their food was less than mediocre and while at the table looking up where they were going to eat next. Our server never even checked in with us after our food was brought to the table. The reason I'm giving this place 2 stars instead of 1 is because the burger and live music was great. 
Would not recommend coming here to anyone. You can find a good burger and live music all around Nashville.
Bluegrass brunch... 10 out of 10, would recommend!! $17 bottomless mimosas is definitely a bang for your buck. Our waitress was Virginia and she was amazing! We'll definitely be back to see her!:)

If you are looking to go see some singer song writers there are far better places to go in Nashville. I would recommend The Listening Room Cafe over this place all day. This place is a tourist trap that over charges for a sub par product. You will end up sitting with people you don't and won't be able to see the acts. They put them in the middle of the room because it is "cool" but the acoustics end up being rubbish and you will end up watching the back of the performers heads the entire time. It ends up being over crowded and uncomfortable. The servers are very robotic and rude as well. If you want to go watch live music GO SOMEWHERE ELSE. This. Place. Is. A. Dump!
Horrible service!!! Don't come here. People are so rude. We are from California and people are so much nicer on the west side

I don't know what it was that turned this rabid former country-music-despising woman around.  Was it the incredible hospitality I encountered everywhere I visited in Nashville?  Was it the land of "no cover charge with talented musicians"?  I don't know but Tootsie's gets some of the credit.

I visited on a business trip in Nov, 2014 and it was their anniversary.  What a night to pick.  Kid Rock stopped by to play in the wee hours.

Returned home to Denver, looking forward to a return trip with my country-music-loving husband.

We visited a few times on our trip last week.  There's no mystery as to their popularity.  Three floors of live music at all hours of the day and night and no cover charge.  We paid $6 + tip for a bottle of beer and you tip the bands. The three times I've visited, I've heard country, rock and pop...all covers and all a fun crowd.

When we left at 9P on a Friday night, there was a long line waiting to get in.  We arrived at 7 or so and it was just starting to get busy.  By 8, it was packed.

Holy mother of perfect pancakes (insert drool emoji)!  The sweet potato pancakes with sweet bourbon butter were highly recommended by the hostess and they did NOT disappoint.  Service was relaxed and the food came out quickly. Menu tells you the history of the building and the significance of their lunch counter. Commune with the ghosts of the civil rights movement and enjoy the modern hospitality and awesome food!
Had a mixup with our cocktails being poured from a bottle of pure water that had been used to train new bartenders on....

HORRIBLE ACCESS.  60 minute line to get into parking lot.   Inept parking assistance and piss poor logistics.  Getting out was just as AWEFUL!   Spent more time in car lines than at the Boston concert.   Shame on the Fontanel.     Won't come back.

Love, love, love this place.  I was fortunate enough to get in 2 nights in a row.  The first night we got right in and the next night was about 45 min wait and got in barely but fortunately others stepped out of line.  Their prices are very reasonable and I have no problem with meeting their minimum requirement to spend toward food and/or drink (I believe $10 minimum).  Everyone was extremely friendly.  They are very strict with their rules but I get why they have to.  Someone told us this was a tourist trap, it couldn't be further from the truth.  It was a treat and make sure you add it to your bucket list.
Sunday Brunch: So they have "bottomless mimosas" until 3pm, but they "ran out" at 2:30pm. Food was ok. Bluegrass was excellent. Overall, wouldn't recommend.

First time to Tootsie's and it could not have been any better! We stayed on the first floor and Kassidy was beyond amazing, so kind, and an absolute rockstar of a bartender! Thank you! Also met sara and angel as well. All three girls were super cute and so friendly! Thanks girls for a great time!
3 levels of live band on a Tuesday afternoon, and crowded, but a great place to have a beer ($), and listen to live music. Bartenders were on it, so no waiting although it was jammed packed.

Look, the Stone Fox is great. We eat here every week. Everything on the menu is tasty, the specials are always good, and the drinks are well-done and well-priced. I've never been to a show here, but it's one of the best bars and restaurants on the west side.

Update: it's a pretty good venue.
New York City wishes they had a tourist bar as much fun as Tootsie's!! Great music, inexpensive, lively crowd! And I was there on a Tuesday afternoon!!!

I've been coming to this Tin Roof for a while and loved it, was happy when they renovated. The last 4 times I've been there, someone on the DJ side has tried to fight me or shoved me. I'm military and can't respond because an arrest would mean the end of my career that I've worked very hard for. Each time I've been an adult and asked the individual to stop. Typically I get a response like "get out of my face." I then proceed to tell the bouncer, who goes and tells the guy or girl to "stop." You can imagine how effective that is. Tonight it happened for the last time. I talked to the manager and told him, Morgan, who was very nice and understanding, that I couldn't come back for fear of an altercation leading to the loss of my job. He told me he gets it, he's sorry, several bars have closed that have led to a "rougher" crowd at Tin Roof. I get it, but to summarize this review: if you go here, it's fun, the bartenders are mostly great, but the clientele lately has been troublesome and you will run the risk of fighting someone. It's sad because I want to come back, but my friends and I won't be anymore. There must be consequences to being an aggressor...currently at Tin Roof Demonbreun, there are not.

Tootsies is not fancy but it is fun.  Where country music is at the heart of Nashville.   No better place to feel the soul and history of country music other than the original Ryman.   Friendly atmosphere and if you are fortunate enough to be able to rent the vip area behind the band you just might get to meet  some big names in the Nashville music industry.   I had the opportunity to meet Rhonda Forlaw Adkins and she was kind enough to invite us to continue to share the space when our time slot was over and hers had begun.  For my visits to Nashville I may visit other establishments but Tootsies will always be my favorite.

If you are into old country and the history of country music this is the place to be.  There may have been Murder on Music Row, but not at Tootsies Orchid Lounge.   Been there. Done that.  Bought the T shirt and I will be going back.

I would rate this place as a 5 for the band and a 3 for the venue.

There was nothing special about the venue. It could honestly use some updating. The bar itself needs some reinforcement because it was shaking a bit when a very light weight female was on top singing. They didn't have any beer on draft or the ingredients for specialty cocktails, that was a disappointment. 

The band that was playing was damn good! I was surprised for such a great performance with it being on a Monday afternoon/evening. The fiddle player could really get down and so could the lead guitarist, the best that I've seen live. That band has a great sound! They rock!

Well I thought i was too old for places like this but... apparently I am not. It's like a 3 floor bar with music on each floor plus big crowds and a lot of sloppy stuff going on. But that's sort of what the broadway area seems like on the weekends in general and you could do worse than Tootsie's where the bartenders seem to be able to hear over the din at near superhuman levels. Truly baffling.
Not too touristy. Lil dive bar with live music. Comfy. I liked it here because everyone is welcome and you can walk in in a t-shirt and shorts. Very comfortable.

It was a fun pre game bar back when I was in TN for a work trip! 

The drinks were pretty cheap, i think.. Lol, Mr. Boss Man paid. :P

My friend/co-worker and I did some dancing and singing and had a blast.

I remember the food being pretty good, especially for a "party bar".

I will return next time i'm in Nashville!

I was lucky enough to get a ticket for a show here that featured Chip Eston. All the musicians were great and approachable and friendly. With this is mind I really think the staff here can be judged unfairly. It's pretty hard clearing out the bar for another show when everyone wants to chat with the musicians afterwards. Erika the waitress was brilliant spotting who needed ore drinks and sorting out the checks. The door staff had a nightmare trying to clear out the place as well as selling the merchandise. If you are coming here, a simple google search will explain how to try and get your tickets. If you don't get tickets, get here early to get in line. People were getting here about 10 minutes before the doors opened then wondering why there was a big line

Went in at 10pm on a Monday night. No smile/greeting from bartender. He started by stating they had $2 Tecate and $5 margaritas. Had to pry information out of him. He was not listening to me as I ordered, so no surprise he messed up a 3 drink order. Acted as if he was doing me a favor by allowing me to order and bring back a pizza from a few doors down when his establishment had no food offerings at that hour. In just over an hour of sitting at the bar neither bartender bothered to check on us. Music was good, and we liked the decor.
Anthony and Andrew are the best! They made my first trip to Nashville a treat. Will for sure be coming back to Tin Roof! Be sure to check out if you are in Nashville

We got there at 1:00pm the hostess told me it be about an hour wait, we waited till 2. Still no call, then we went up to ask how much longer the wait would be got told no longer than 20 minutes, so we waited until 2:30  still no call. Then we saw groups of people who had been there way less than us were getting called. So we just left.

Their BlueGrass Brunch is awesome! Live music during brunch along with bottomless mimosa's...so you can't go wrong. Virginia was wonderful. She was so attentive and made sure our brunch was not only delicious, but served with a smile. This is a must brunch spot in Nashville...but it wouldn't be complete unless you have Virginia as your server.

I've tried to eat at The Sutler twice in 3 months. The first time they were closed for a private party. Today upon entering we were told they weren't serving from 3pm to 5pm. I wish they would put this information on their website. It's 42 degrees and Christmas time! I'm
Not happy & they won't get a 3rd try from me!

We did the hop on hop off trolley and they mentioned Woolworth which was a fun touch! I made the reservation early on Open Table for dinner on a Friday, but there seemed to be plenty of open tables. Food is pretty big portions, my parents were able to split the Caesar salad and chicken and it was tons of food for them- always good! We all got burgers which were pretty good- I love bread and the bun was really nice and fluffy. We had the Brussels sprouts, fries, and mashed potatoes sides- all good! The fries are the thin kind that look like steak and shake fries! We also got the bread pudding to split between the 5 of us and it was AMAZING! Made with biscuits- it was devoured:) The screen in the background and music definitely add to the experience as well.

This was a cool unique spot blocks away from Broadway street. It was quite empty on this Friday night and the ambiance is very casual and diner-esque, but our group of girls were ready for a night out. There's a cool projector area where they old time music videos too, so that was fun to look at. 

We ordered some brussel sprouts to start, which were not the best in my opinion. The sauce was tasty though, but the crispiness of the sprouts could have had some improvement. I also ordered the crispy pork belly and fried chicken salad. I didn't realize how big these portions were, so I definitely didn't need both. The crispy pork belly was delicious though! I wasn't a fan of the watermelon and large amounts of cheese in the rest of the dish, however. The fried chicken salad was also huge with lots of fruit in it- I wish I noticed this when ordering because I don't like fruit in my salads. The chicken was very dry and had to be doused in hot sauce and ranch. I had a good amount of my friend's rib dish, and this was delicious. The sweet potato fries were soft and addicting, and the cole slaw was also a tasty addition to the tender ribs. 

Overall, the food was a hit or miss, but very heavy and filling nonetheless. You definitely get your money's worth in portions! Service was quick and great as well for our large group.
This place has some great live music. It's very difficult to get reservations, so get to the door 2 hours before the show and you will likley get in .its become a iconic place to visit

So first I suggest arriving before 10AM, if not prepare for a wait. My group and I got her at 10:10 and it was already an hour wait. Good thing that they moved rather quickly so we weren't waiting for an hour. Their.sangria pitchers are at a great price but depending on who makes them depends on how strong it actually is. You can get a good 3 cups out of it. Their bottomless mimosas aren't bad, just make sure you keep the receipt. The food tasted great but was a little cold. Not sure if it was because of it being busy or if that's a regular thing. The biscuits and gravy are good enough to share if you're not too hungry. The live music adds a great element to the environment. It's not overly loud but keeps it entertaining, really gives it a great southern vibe. The waitress was a little rude but everyone else was pretty nice. I definitely recommend just make sure to tell them you want you're food hot.
I was afraid that this bar would be too touristy and not worth the hype, but it totally lived up to it and more!!! The band was amazing!!! Seriously wonderful!!!
Great live music and service! A Nashville must see!!! Cold beer!!!!!!!! True dive bar.

I came here for brunch this past weekend and we had a great time. We were originally quoted a 25 minute wait time but we ended up waiting a little over an hour. We didn't mind because we're pretty understanding that if people don't leave then you can't sit new tables. Plus the $17 bottomless mimosas helped speed that wait up. The food was pretty good. They had great southern options for brunch. The chicken fried chicken biscuits were decent. The white gravy is a little flavorless. The Benedict and chicken and waffles were delicious! 

I for sure recommend this place. The $17 bottomless mimosas and great brunch options make it a nice choice. Be prepared to wait on weekends though.

Went here for brunch and the food was amazing! Service was great and the place was clean. Really good ambiance. The place is historic. Included with the menus is a sheet that gives you some info on the history of the place so you can read through it while you wait for your food. The brunch food was really good and was very flavorful, fresh, and filling. My friend got the hot chicken and said it was the best he ever had! I definitely think you should check this place out especially if you're from out of town.

We have been here several times in the past year. Not overly crowded. Friendly service....a little slow at times. I ordered the catfish platter. It comes with a great sauce and Sutler fries. It's a large portion.  Very tasty. My husband ordered the catch of the day fish tacos. He really enjoyed them but not enough food for his hunger...shared my fries with him. 
Live music has been great each time we have been there. Will Dakota performed last night. He was great!
There is a great selection of drinks, beer and wine.

A Must Do

Waited in line for 2 hours to get in for the singer-songwriter show and it was well worth the wait.  From the outside the place looks like a dump in a somewhat worn down strip mall.  But you go for the music which is fantastic.  

It is very small and just a great atmosphere once the music starts.

I ate at The Sutler a few months ago. The atmosphere is great, the food is good, the music is awesome, and the drinks are yummy. My boyfriend and I were extremely turned off by the hostesses though. There were 3 of them at the front, yet it took a while for them to service us, and then they had poor attitudes. We felt unwelcome but still gave it a try. 

Today, we returned to try to have some lunch and drinks. When we came in, again there were 3 employees at the front. It took a bit to get their attention, and this time, the one who I was speaking with turned to her coworker to talk to her while I was asking about the wait. They were complaining about either a guest or another coworker. I was shocked that this happened, and we turned around and left. We enjoyed much better service at ML Rose down the street. 

The hosts and hostesses are the face of the restaurant. There are too many up there for this to be a regular occurrence; they should be friendly, welcoming, and helpful.

We live a 5 min walk from The Sutler and would love to have this be a go-to place, but the service at the front is so awful that we likely won't be trying again unless something changes.

Not too touristy. Lil dive bar with live music. Comfy. I liked it here because everyone is welcome and you can walk in in a t-shirt and shorts. Very comfortable. It is really humbling learning how many famous people got their start here. Ie: Patsy Cline

Tim and Sarah made our night!!! Loved their midwestern hospitality especially from some northerner gals! In town for #cmas and enjoyd chix tenders and leinies summer shandy!!! Find us on insta feed!! -#sarahandannietakenashville

I'm extremely saddened about this review. This restaurant turned had become a part of my top 5 places to eat for to the food and the history. Tonight, that changed. To my knowledge, a lot had changed since my last appearance which was in October. The menu changed. The MENU CHANGED. How and why, Sway?! They no longer sell their rich and flavorful gumbo. The small basket of biscuits/cornbread/ho cakes are gone. Even the peach cobbler was taken away. The Mac and cheese is no longer a side! Which is foolishness bc how on ear are you a southern restaurant. The fried chicken isn't even what it used to be. It's more "crunchy", which typically is a good thing for me but something wasn't right with it. They decided to add "Nashville hot chicken" flavor which is not something I thought they should have added. I originally order the friend chicken but couldn't even enjoy it so I went with the short rib roast. It was pretty decent. Tender but not much to go with it. Barely any mashed potatoes or green beans. According to the waitress, the menu was changed to alleviate some costly meals which I find to be false due to the chicken plate being the same price as before ~$16 and the short rib which by the way was a small plate around ~$16. I'm really disappointed that they changed things up. It's barely a year old and boom change menus. I don't think I'll be back. All that history.

Tootsie's was recommended by many friends, so I felt the need to check it out while visiting Broadway. Found seats at the bar and was quickly welcomed by the bartenders. The band that was playing was WONDERFUL (featured a full group with a killer fiddle player). I don't mind spending money on a good time, but the drinks were VERY expensive, even for the area ($9 for a TINY shot of moonshine, and I believe $8-9 for a Coors Light). Be sure to check it out, but watch how quickly you order your drinks!
