Love this place!! The vibes are excellent, it has interesting decor and cool live music in the evenings. The drinks are really affordable and happy hour here is ALWAYS full so expect to take some time finding parking. Pro-tip: their fries are the best in town.

Have been here twice now. Great food! Good prices. The first time here had a waitress that was rude and always seemed " bothered" when asking her for items. I believe her name was Virginia?  Then came back and had wonderful service. By one of the sisters.Her name was Brianna I'm pretty sure.  I think her and a twin work together. 100% a great place to eat and have a wonderful honky tonk time.

I've been here twice. The first time, the food and service were great. The second time, the food was mediocre & service was poor. Our server didn't introduce himself and barely spoke to us. We had the Brie and roasted garlic app, the meatloaf and the gnocchi. The app was amazing, 10/10, would recommend. The meatloaf was dry and the truffle mashed potatoes were more like cheesy smashed potatoes--they weren't bad, just not what was advertised. The flavor of the gnocchi was good but there weren't a ton of actual gnocchis in the dish.

Additionally, we had to pay $12 to parallel park in front of the restaurant because those are "valet spots." I don't mind to pay to valet, but usually valeting involves someone else actually driving the car, not just moving it two inches up once you get out. Also, the meal was $160... feels like parking shouldn't cost extra.

This place was very fun. Multi level bar with live entertainment on every level. Fair drink prices and pours. We enjoyed this place. The bartender had a Rangers cup behind the bar. Yeah!! Let's go rangers!!

Can't get tickets! I was buying tickets for my upcoming trip for my birthday. I was on the website, 2nd in line and when I ordered my tickets I was booted and then I kept trying 3 times but it kept kicking me out of the queue- very frustrating.  Horrible process!!!  I'm just enraged at how difficult this was.  I didn't get tickets.  Please think about changing your process.  Thank you!

Lost my credit card, still charged me for my entire tab.  I gave up after several attempts to get redress from management and staff.

Was towards the bottom of my list even when I was still a howling wildebeest of a Vandy grad student.  It's a bit like Fireball.  Terrible even when you were in college... now even less appealing.

I had pretty high expectations for Woolworth on Fifth, but not high enough. Yes, the atmosphere is both unique and beautiful, but the flavors are what I continue to think about. It was hard to decide, so I trusted the manager's recommendation, and he did not lead me astray. I had the Turkey Hot Brown paired with an Affogato Boozy Float. Honestly, I had no idea that a Hot Brown could be that good! The turkey had so much flavor and never hinted at dry. Gravy, bacon, Texas toast - Yum! I had been looking forward to trying a boozy float, and it was just delicious. We sat at the counter bar and our server was super sweet and helpful.

Good drinks. You climb a ton of stairs to get to the lounge. Half way up the stairs you will find the bathroom which was surprisingly clean. Upstairs there is nice live music. The band was ok. There is a nice outdoor patio. It was quite cold that evening but no one turned on the heaters so I saw folks start turning them on themselves. Drinks were just ok. Would recommend if you are into country music and just want a place to grab a beer
3 floors of quality live music and frosty cold beers. This is what I was expecting from Nashville and Tootsie's delivered fully.
Checked it out on a Friday night as I heard it was a place you just HAD to go.  Atmosphere was fun. But it was literally wall to wall people and could hardly move, or hear  anything.
Second floor is a real fun time. The Andy Gibbons band plays all your favorite country songs and they are a so personable. Nice band to chat with in between sets.

Sure, the place has history, but if you're really want to hear good current country western writers and singers visit the listening Cafe. Good food plenty of seating excellent prices great bar service and you're sitting right next to Nashville's next big stars
The world famous Tootsie's was packed on a Tuesday night. The band was okay on the second floor. The beer was cold and quick to be handed out. Another spot to see when you are in Nashvil

This should be on the top places to visit in Nashville! We were visiting from D.C and we went back for the 3 days we were visiting! The tuna melt is exceptional! The jumbo sundae was delicious! Hardy meals would be the fried chicken biscuit and the cheeseburger.

Clearly my favorite is the tuna melt! I should have gotten it every time we went. I would travel to Nashville just to visit this place again!
One of the coolest place I've ever been in my 66 years! Don't pass on the opportunity to go to this truly historic venue!
The bartender complete left the vodka out my vodka tonic. She was fun to look at but don't expect  any alcohol in your mixed drink if ordered after 10:00 pm. I recommend sticking to beer at Tootsie's

Absolutely a must visit if you're in Nashville. We sat at the bar, and Martha was great. We had the nachos, cupcake wine, Corona, and another drink and it totalled to be around $50ish dollars, which isn't bad.  You are sat very close to other people, but everyone is so polite.

Alright, first time in Nashville and I had to hit up the legendary Tootsies Orchid Lounge after hearing all about it for years and years and years.

Crowded? Yes. Loud? Yes. Fun? Yes.

Each of the different floors offers different kinds of live music which I loved. The cover band on one of the middle floors played everything from country to Fall Out Boy which had me reminiscing hardcore.

The rooftop offered a nice view.

I had one drink and called it a night, but I can say that I went.

I'm perplexed as to how all of these people on Yelp are complaining of the crowds but really I'm like, "What did you expect?" This place is an institution and tourist hot-spot. From what I experienced, Nashville wasn't the cleanest of cities...dare I say spots in New Orleans are cleaner. So just take this place with a grain of salt. Grab a drink. Take an insta pic. And be on your merry little way.

Awesome spot and not terribly expensive! The staff is REALLY what makes this place! You feel at home when you walk in and are grated by there hosts. Sandwiches are fab, filled chicken salad is awesome. The soups are bomb!

Bouncer put a crack in my legitimate drivers license by bending it back and forth, then told me it was a fake because it had a crease. I asked him to stop bending it (Maryland ID does not bend) and presented him with a credit card with my name and my teaching ID, both of which he ignored. Cop verified that it was real and let me in, no apology from the bouncer. I will be writing a letter to the manager and asking to be reimbursed for the cost of replacing my ID.

Update: the manager reached out to me the next morning and did agree to reimburse the cost of a new ID. He was very apologetic and agreed that the bouncer had used excessive force when bending it.

We had a total of 12 people visiting for Christmas and they requested a downtown day. I figured it would be difficult to make a reservation for 15 people during the holiday weekend but we were lucky enough to snag a table at Woolworth's. Parking was easy and they had our table prepped and ready on arrival.

Service was a little slow, but that was to be expected with such a large table. Fortunately, the food was still hot. 

We are a difficult crew to feed with vegatarians and one member with severe food allergies but everyone was able to find something and most everyone liked their food. The most popular and well-liked dish was the sweet potato pancakes.

Woolworth's also provides a nice jumping point for a downtown tour. When you exit the restaurant, you can walk through the arcade and then past some of the newer hotels like Noelle and Bobby. You can then turn to walk through Printer's Alley before making your way to Broadway. 

Great location, great food.
This place rocks ! 3 levels of bars & music ! Friendly servers music is live and rocks! No cover charge this place is creative & fun let your hair down spot ! Performers are great .
Great atmosphere and food. Good choice before TPAC performance. Loved the pot roast. French fries are awesome. Will definitely come back.

I get it and agree with the history and the music and all that. My only suggestion is close it for a couple of days and give it a good cleaning. It was a dump when we were in there with garbage on the floor... To be fair we were there on a busy Saturday night in August so prime time. I do think they can do a smart renovation, to keep the history in the walls and charm, so they can get rid of the 4x8 sheets of poorly installed plexiglass everywhere. Ole Red and Kid Rocks' place are just as fun, but modern and clean...

So, this one felt kind of like a tourist trap, but I actually left feeling really pleased with my meal and experience!

We ended up at Woolworth's for dinner with a group on Friday night. We had initially wanted to grab dinner in a trendy section of town but after being quoted crazy long wait times, we got on Open Table to see what our options were. We were able to snag a table for 5 at Woolworth's in 15 minutes.

When we arrived, there were only 4 other tables dining here. Not a great sign for a Friday night. Also, the place is huge since it used to be a department store, so the size of the space made it look even more empty.  The man who sat us was really friendly, and our server was also great.

The history of the place is really interesting and they include a print out so you can read about it which I really appreciated. 

After we ordered drinks, the server came back around and checked on us. Myself and a friend had ordered the Parlor Punch which I was a huge fan of. It had a huge sprig of rosemary in it to offset the sweetness of the prosecco topper and I just thought it was a really interesting and refreshing cocktail. Our server checked on the two of us specifically because she'd been getting mixed reviews of the drink and said it was either a love it or hate it thing. While I loved it, my friend didn't care for it. Our server insisted he swap it out for something he'd prefer even though he gladly would've taken the hit and finished it. She brought him a sangria and he was thrilled. I really appreciated not only checking back on us but insisting on doing whatever it took to ensure we enjoyed our meal to the fullest. Major kudos for that.

I had the short rib pot roast which was really delicious. The short rib was perfectly tender and fell off the bone by the forkful. It was atop a bed of mashed potatoes and green beans, both of which were okay. I had a few bites of my boyfriend's patty melt which was also quite good, as were the fries. Two of our guests had the meatloaf and they said it was really good. I will say that our friend who had 2 appetizer plates as her meal was not as thrilled with her choices, but those of us who ordered entrees were quite pleased.

Overall my expectations were pleasantly exceeded. Service was truly above and beyond in the hospitality department and we were able to enjoy a solid, southern meal for probably 1/2 the price of the places we had been trying to go that night.

I have not eaten yet but our server is wearing a Trump 2020 hat while working at a historic touch stone for black history.  I am very uncomfortable having this man serve us. We are a big group and they are putting a 20% tip to a man who supports our president who has demonstrated bigotry
Free Brad Paisley concert! Great music before and after the show - he even bought the crowd beer!

Loved every minute of this place. Great vibes, and good atmosphere. 
Mo, my bartender, was sweet and professional and on point the entire time I was visiting. Excellent drinks!  Every drink she made was more delicious than the next. Mixed perfect and delivered with a smile every time!  Thanks Mo for all the great recommendations from off the menu and also for around town!

Give this girl a damn raise!
Felt very much like a tourist trap. Way too crowded and nowhere to sit. There are other, better places in town if you want live music. It is worth a stop because of the history though.
Didnt try the food so I cant rate this place based off that, but loved the atmosphere and live music. Everyones friendly, no cover. highly recommend!

Coolest bar on Broadway Street. You could spend the whole day at this location going up and down three floors listening to live music. The rooftop bar is pretty epic as well. It's absurdly crowded most of the time but well worth the experience and vibe.

Went in for the bluegrass brunch. I can definitely understand some of the complains about parking, because with the spaces it shares from the nearby businesses, you had better be prepared to park a little way's away. None of that is a serious obstacle (if you're used to city parking), but plan accordingly, and I can definitely see why it would be tricky to get in here late at night.

Once you're in, I can see why this place is a community institution. There's a goodly amount of seating, the music is very enjoyable, the menu is affordably priced, the food tastes good, there's a nice drink menu, and the service is damned prompt. One of the things that struck me was that we were taken care of by multiple servers, meaning that they all just look for what needs doing it and do it (I'm hoping they share tips, too; they earned them). The biscuit benedict was extremely tasty, as was my girlfriend's chicken fried chicken biscuits. The bottomless mimosa was appropriately bottomless (I think they refilled it something like six or seven times) and there's a substantial whiskey menu to pick from as well. All of the brunch entrees seemed to hover in the $9-$14 range, and while the drinks were a little bit pricier, not unjustifiably so.

For starters, two of the plates we were brought for our biscuits, had bright green gum stuck on them. Part of my order was forgotten (but was brought out when asked for, for a second time) and I was never brought my change or receipt, after paying. The change was 20% of the total and therefore would have been left as a tip anyway, but it made me uncomfortable that no effort to bring me a receipt, or acknowledge that there had been change, was made. That being said our server was friendly and the food was good. The live music and happy crowds of customers created a fun environment.

What bothered me the most, however, was the service at the bar. While waiting to be seated, the hostess (who was also quite friendly), informed us that we could order bottomless mimosas ahead of time and just needed to hold onto our receipts and show them, upon continuing to order. The young woman with the braided pigtails behind the bar was SO unfriendly. I don't expect much, but she didn't even so much as smile, and honestly made me feel like I was somehow inconveniencing her with my presence. She had a scowl on her face when she approached me, took my card/ID and my order with barely a word, and brought them back with my drink, then turned around and walked away without a word and without giving me the receipt I had been previously told I needed. When I got her attention again, she seemed genuinely frustrated that I was asking for a receipt and brought it back, placing it on the bar, turned around and walked away. As I looked behind the bar, I realized all of them look upset. I work in the service industry and I know how frustrating and draining it can be, but your patrons are you livelihood and there's no excuse to take it out on them. It also made me concerned that maybe the work environment is not great for them, if all of them looked so unhappy. I do not believe I would come here, again.
The staff is so quick and friendly, the music was awesome too. Can't wait to come back!

Do not go.  Rudest waitress I have ever encountered. As I stood up to walk away because she scared my daughter, another waitress told us she is like that all the time. She threw menus at us, slammed down the water. The manager simply said he could give us another table. He didn't look too shocked either.  Why keep someone employed working there who is actually harassing and mean to your clientele.

Very touristy, but also a great experience! Incredibly packed and shoved in with hordes of humanity, but the music options are great with three bands at any given time (bottom floor, second floor, top floor indoors). Deck outside is also pretty neat in the right weather (got one day where it was about 65 and sunny).

Drinks are rather on the pricey side and no draught beers (just bottles and/or cans). Music quality is pretty good, with women dancing on the bar, etc. Also, try to avoid it evenings on weekends. If you go in early afternoons, it is somewhat reasonable, crowd-wise. Also try going through the alley in the back. Probably the most fun bar on Broadway (I like Tin Roof too but completely different feel).

Visiting from Michigan and we had a blast! Fun to see so much history on the walls. It ended up getting too crowded for us on a Thursday night. However, the waitstaff was really awesome and attentive.
The band member told my younger sister to take her shirt off. I will never be returning.
Service great and seat right away. Plate looked good but tasted horrible. Catfish was very greasy and red beans were salty/vinegary. Had two bites and couldnt finish it.
The filet special was absolutely delicious - 6 oz filet covered in savory bearnaise sauce over sausage and potatoes. They give you huge, shareable portions. Recommended!

Walking around the Melrose area on a Saturday night, we needed one last place to enjoy a beer and maybe a snack. With our trusty Yelp app, we found The Sutler and decided to give it a try. The parking situation did seem tricky but luckily we parked at a different location and walked here. Our IDs were checked when we walked in the door and we received a stamp on our hands. The place was fairly busy so we grabbed two seats at the bar. The restaurant is set up to focus on the stage. To the left is the bar and then there are high top tables in the rest of the bar. The stage is at the front of the bar. The whole place has your typical honky-tonk kind of atmosphere. Nothing fancy but has some great character. If you walk downstairs, they have cowboy boots hanging down from the ceiling. Fun to see some of the unique touches.

When we first got there, the bands were switching so we weren't worried about having a stage view. We decided to sit at the bar and we were given a drink menu pretty quickly. They have a nice selection of beers at a fair price. I picked out my beer and waited for the bartender to come back. There were two bartenders at the time and neither even looked our way for about 10 minutes. They were busy making drinks for the whole bar. We finally got their attention and ordered our beers. While drinking our beers, a new band took the stage. They were playing some country classics and a few non-country songs. We decided to stay for another beer and a snack just so we could listen to some music. We realized they had gone from 2 to 1 bartender (on a Saturday night) and after waiting awhile again, we decided it would probably be quicker to move to a table. This worked out nicely because then we could see the stage better. The band was a fun husband/wife combo and even though I'm not a big country music fan, I enjoyed listening to them. A server was over in no time and took our order. So my suggestion is sit at a table, not the bar. I ordered the chips & queso (of course) and my boyfriend got a PBR tallboy (classic). The beer was out quickly and was served in the can. My chips didn't take too long. The queso was in a small skillet accompanied by the chips in a basket. The queso is a white cheese combo with some peppers and onions. It didn't have a ton of flavor and after it was cooled down a bit became a weird texture. But it was ok. Not great, not bad. I'm not sure I would come here again for the food. 

It sounds like The Sutler has a nice brunch so maybe that would be worth checking out. We discovered The Cellar, a downstairs bar, when looking for the restroom. This space looked pretty cool and is definitely more my scene than the upstairs space. I would come back just to check that out. I also liked the connected billiards room. I think the building has a lot to offer and is a nice alternative to Broadway if you want to see some live music.

I visited "The Sultler" Thursday evening 1/3/19 with 3 other couples after an evening at a comedy show. The experience from the outset was terrible as we walked in and saw a sign that said seat yourself, we proceeded to sit at a table that sat 8 and after 10 minutes no wait staff came to us! We then decided to scrap formal dining and go downstairs to get drinks, play pool and eat finger food. When we got downstairs we approached the bar and watched the bartender while the bar down and ignore us for approximately 5 minutes. My long time friend (30years) went to ask if we could play pool on a table that was open? We were told that there is a list that you sign with your phone number so that staff could inform you when a table was ready. The same pool table was still empty after 5 more minutes! So my friend with his spouse asked a staff member why is this table still empty with a group waiting and as they spoke another table became empty! The staff member told us we had to wait and was extremely short and dismissive towards us, even laughing in amusement and walked away in mid discussion! The obvious thing is all 4 couples were of color (African American) And everyone who was being attended were white! The overall experience was shameful and embarrassing! I would strongly advise you not to spend your hard earned money in this place! They are stuck in an America that is long dead!

Disappointed with the food. We ordered the fried chicken and someone forgot or misplaced the order. Finally the waiter brought it after waiting for a very long time. It was overdone, almost burned and we send it back. We exchanged it for the meatloaf, which was not bad but nothin to write home about.

4.5

True story: the first time I lived in Nashville, I lived in Green Hills just a little north of the Bluebird on Hillsboro. It never crossed my mind to attend. Back in those days, despite the small space, it wasn't *that* difficult to see a show there if the intention was just to see a show.

Fast forward.

Getting a ticket to The Bluebird involves a Hunger Games-like online ticket system, especially to enjoy the as-seen-on-TV™ In The Round/In The Row singer/songwriter night. Well, as it so happened, I had some of my very best buddies coming in town and I was determined to give them a full on Nashville weekend. So, I studied the reviews of the lucky and unlucky, asked questions, poured over the website to find out who was playing when, scoured the seating arrangements to figure out the best place to sit to enjoy the show... and I waited. I plotted. Tickets for the In The Row show I wanted to attend went on 'sale'* at 8 am CST so I started stalking the site at 745. At 759 and 30 seconds, I refreshed the page, getting my ticket finger at the ready and when the page blinked, the show time was live. When vying for tickets, you need to know which table you want. I think this eats up valuable time. You're in a race, people. You're running to get the bow & arrow. You don't want to wind up at the circle last and only have the maracas to choose. With lighting quick speed, I chose the table and hit the number of seats I needed. 'Enter.' Yes! The payment page. I knew to have my credit card at the ready. Again, it's a race. Every second counts. I typed in my info, pressed enter and held my breath. 'Congratulations.' Yes, that's what I wanted. I couldn't believe my good fortune to emerge victorious in The Ticket Games. The clock on my laptop read '802 am.' The show was sold out.

Day of, I plotted the best route to Green Hills in rush hour traffic (doors opened at 530 for the 630 show) and... as expected, the parking lot was full of cars and people waiting in line to get in to the show. I was annoyed that viable parking spaces were sucked up by people who weren't going to patronize the venue but then I remembered reading about the back lot. I drove around and snagged the second to last parking place. Perfect. We walked back to the front and got in line (admittedly, with a smug attitude) to the left side of the door, waited our turn, walked to the host stand, gave the last name, and planted our butts in seats. Victory.

Our waitress came over to drop off menus and let us know that in addition to the beer, soda and wine on the menu, the bar was fully stocked. That's all I needed to hear. I ordered a Jack & Coke and BBQ nachos ($10+) and settled in to be entertained. One of my buddies is a (very skilled, former on-the-road- band) musician and I was eager to get his impression for what we were about to experience. The In The Row show was four singer/songwriters all singing their songs. Other artists may have bought/performed/released them, but these are the originators. Four guys. Four guitars. A ton of stories. It really is as magical as promised. Even if you're not a country music fan, the artistry and musicianship will pull you in. I was impressed with all of the performers but Bobby Hamrick blew me away. His song writing, guitar playing and versatility of his voice hypnotized me. It was just another reminder of the ridiculous amount of talent in this city. Forget New York, if you('re a musician and you) can make it here, you can make it anywhere... because the level of competition is downright insane.

The show ended around 8 and we milled about to meet some of the writers and to take some photos with Mayor Barry (she was there, enjoying the show like everyone else). I didn't want to delay too much because I knew the staff needed to turn the venue over for the next show which had doors at 830. Before leaving I took a mental picture of the small room, relatively few tables, the bar seats, the church pews (I think they seat 15-20), and Christmas lights and concentrated on my gratitude for having had the experience. I may not have appreciated The Bluebird as a younger man, but I do now and I am so very happy to have gone. 

*The show is free. You pay a nominal amount to reserve the seats and then, at the show, you're required to spend, at least, $10/head while there. That's, like, a drink. It's fine.
Amazing experience! From Iowa and I loved sitting in the roof top and enjoying the sun and a great view up and down Broadway.
Great choice for good food in a little historical spots.  Tried the shrimp and grits and it was fantastic!  Great service at the historic counter.
This place is awesome. Service is great and the food is delicious. It's an aesthetically pleasuring environment.
This place is fantastic! 3 floors + an outside patio on the roof all with different bands playing! One of those things you just have to see and experience
I don't throw around 5 stars very often but this place is definitely worth it. Pimento dip was great. Baked Italian eggs great. Woolworth salad great. Everything was great.  Highly recommended.
tin/tin Came here for a sorority date party. Reasonable prices for beer. Friendly staff. Bathrooms were clean yet vulgar. 2 ply toilet paper, ample paper towels. Very cold and refreshing water.
Drinks were made strong which is how I like them. Beer choices were ok and all bottles at least for the upper floor outside area

We had a GREAT time here on a Saturday!! We came mid day and wound up spending a few hours here! This bar is pretty cool as it has three different levels and a few different spots where live music is being performed. The vibe in the back bar on the second floor was pretty chill, but we really enjoyed that the bands had different local performers rotating in and out and performing songs. 

We ordered some fries while we were there and they were really good but some were cold and others were super hot. They came with a side of spicy queso cheese which was realllyyy good!! 

The top floor of this bar has a rooftop deck which was pretty cool, but we didn't stay out to long as it was insanely crowded and you couldn't really enjoy the views/the area bc there wasn't much room.

I love the Sutler! Between 90's Night on Thursdays to Bluegrass Brunch on the weekend and the weekday Happy Hour this is always a great place to gather with friends for drinks (I recommend the Kentucky Mule) and quality food. The service has always been wonderful and attentive, and they always seem to get great live music performances.

I had a great time at Tootsie's during our most recent visit to Nashville! We got there around 1pm on a Sunday and headed up to the third floor. The sun was shining and it was a great day with a slight breeze. 

There was a band starting at 1, Lady and the Gents, and they absolutely rocked the place for 5 hours. Getting there around 1pm we were easily able to get a table and we did not move from that spot until 6pm. 

They had the college games on, and the drinks were flowing. I would say the only drawback is that they did not have draft beer and that the drinks were on the expensive side. I can say my wallet did not like Tootsie's. 

Overall a great experience!

Yet another fun stop on the Honkey Tonk Strip! This place has no cover, just like all the other bars on the strip. There are multiple floors, but i ran straight up to the rooftop. It was a fairly cold night, but the heat lamps make it a comfortable place. There is a great view of the strip and Bridgestone arena. The inside just past the doorways to the roof was very crowded, so it was difficult to approach the band to tip them or request a song. People were friendly and having a great time, so it was no big deal to push through. This kinda affected being able to approach the bar as well. However, when I was outside on the rooftop, there was a waitress walking around and taking orders on the floor. There were plexiglass boards on the walls showing who had performed there in the past, very interesting, and a very fun time!
Amazing service and live music! Came on a Sunday night and it was awesome! 10/10  @carone

Talk about a great place in Nashville, this place is great to just go on roof top get you a coke or what ever you drink and just sit and watch Nashville.  
You can see for ever in that roof top, always a little crowded, but worth it.

This was my favorite bar to goto on broadway st. All of the bars have similar pricing so expect it to be $6 beer night at all of the bars in the area. What set this one apart from all the other honky tonk bars on the street was the live bands and atmosphere. This bar is three stories tall with a bar and a live band on all three. We found a nice spot next to the second story band and enjoyed the experience. They were playing country music and even taking requests. The third story also had a balcony that overlooked the whole area. Most of the bars on broadway st. are very similar, but this one is a little notch above the rest. 

~Bmo

This place has a cute vibe and great bluegrass music. We came here while visiting for brunch on a Saturday with a group of friends. They do not take reservations so be prepared to wait. Overall, the food was just ok. I tried the biscuit Benedict, a few friends got the shrimp and grits, and my husband tried the hash. The biscuit in the Benedict was hard and the food came out semi cold. The hash potatoes were the same way (cold). The shrimp and grits were apparently amazing tho!
Great neighborhood bar with amazing live music! Good food and good drinks! Cool staff :)
Had so much fun visiting Nashville and Tootsies was one of our favorite spots!  Great atmosphere, nice staff (shout out to Angel), and great entertainment.  Would highly recommend.

Okay, I'm perplexed. Cool space, rich history, pretty dang good food...what's missing?  Nothing we had was so special we couldn't get the same somewhere else. The crowd was light but it was a Sunday dinner so the room energy, both staff and diners, was at best, subdued. The wait staff is supposed to encourage and sell the menu at different stages of the meal...drinks, then apps, then entree, then dessert and then the check. I never felt compelled to stay any longer than the entree. We did try a couple of apps but our server brought the entrees before removing any of the used plates and that made for some awkward teamwork to clear and make room for even more plates. Two things they need to work on, timing, attention to detail and representing this place with pride and a higher level of passion. If this doesn't happen Woolworth on 5th is sunk. 
I think they should have returned it to its former glory and capture what it really was, a southern lunch counter instead of some crafty southern gourmet trendy bar restaurant and event space. More chrome, sweet waitresses in dresses, southern style plates, amazing pies and coffee, a place to gather, a place to meet up and dine. Woolworth is none of that in all its redefined trendiness.. a little more authenticity rather than austerity would go a long way in making it successful for the long haul.  Right now it's just another trendy restaurant in a town full of them...and it's clearly not the leader.

This place was great. We went with a group for a friends birthday and they were very accommodating and the food and drinks were great. Above all of that our server, Keena was maybe the best server we have ever had. EXCELLENT.

When coming back to Nashville I try to avoid the touristy spots and attractions. My boyfriend had never been before so on this last visit we hit many of those said spots and it was actually fun. With that said, I've never considered Tootsie's touristy. I mean of course it is but it's also a local institution, iconic  and legendary.

A really fun place to relax, have a beer and enjoy some of Nashville's finest local performers. Employees (including the bartenders) work for tips only so it's important to be generous.

This honky tonk is epic and a must visit whether you're a tourist or a Nashville regular. Always a good time.

***Tin Roof is an okay casual bar and grill for nearby residents or workers, but there is much better food elsewhere in Nashville that is more reflective of the local cuisine and ingredients***

Tin Roof looks like a garage from the outside with all of the aluminum/metal (lots of aluminum/metal on the inside too), but it is actually a spacious dining establishment for casual food (sandwiches, wraps, pizzas, and quesadillas) and live music.  The restaurant has kind of a kitschy feel with all kinds of retro decoration on the walls (not sure if the decoration is authentic or not).  There is even a Breathalyzer on the wall.  At lunch, Tin Roof draws a young, hip and casual downtown Nashville crowd. 

As mentioned, the restaurant features casual food.  It is American bar and grill food with mostly bar and grill ingredients integrated with each plate of food (even quesadillas and pizzas).  Tin Roof appears to specialize in sandwiches and they have a great variety of them including standard, found-everywhere sandwiches like an Italian sub and a turkey club as well as more hard to find items like a Reuben made with turkey. 

All of their sandwiches can be made into wraps so I took their buffalo chicken tenders sandwich and turned it into a wrap.  The kitchen tosses chicken tenders in your choice of sauce and I opted for the traditional buffalo style hot sauce.  I had them remove the cheese and add lettuce. 

The wrap was good.  It did not feel full enough though.  I would have preferred a tighter wrap with not necessarily more chicken but more crisp and cool shredded lettuce to provide a satisfying contrast to the hot sauce chicken.  Still, the lettuce was fresh and the tortilla was not dry or stale. 

I thought the chicken tenders were nicely prepared.  The batter had a great crunch and was not too heavy.  The chicken itself was moist.  The hot sauce was nothing particularly unique, but it was satisfying enough if you like this type of heat.  They generously applied the hot sauce so it was a hot sandwich.  Ranch sauce was provided on the side for dipping.  I would have preferred a blue cheese sauce, which I think would have been a more satisfying compliment to the chicken.

Sandwiches come with fries, but they are the crinkle cut, Ore-Ida style fries so I had them substituted for tortilla chips and salsa (the menu indicated that their chips and salsa are made fresh everyday).  Unfortunately, I found the chips and salsa to be disappointing.  The salsa did not have much heat or spiciness and while the chips were thin, they had kind of a stale crunch (it might just have been from how the chips were fried).

Service was very pleasant and the food came out quickly.  Unfortunately, servers were hard to track down at times--understandable perhaps given the size of the restaurant and the huge plastic cups used for water, soft drinks and such. 

Prices are reasonable though it is not a significant amount of food served at lunch. 

Tin Roof is a decent and quick lunch spot and a good option for people who work or live in the area.  If you are visiting Nashville though, you might want to seek out other options because there is much better and more local food elsewhere in Nashville. 

I believe free street parking is available.  I do not know if Tin Roof has its own parking lot.
Enjoyed putting our feet up and listening to some good music. Bartender seemed less than thrilled.

This is a great place to experience a lot of different things. The atmosphere was very nice and retro. I love the different food selections and even the lunch promotional that they had. The food was seasoned and had good portions. My only change would be to ask for the chicken to not be as fried as much to the point where it is dried out. Definitely worth another visit!

I was in Nashville to celebrate a birthday and asked my hotel for a recommendation to take a group. Made reservations in advance and received a text alert the day before and day of as a reminder. Great so far.....

Then we got there. Atmosphere was good, place wasn't very full for a Friday night so didn't need to worry about disturbing anyone. But I have to say, we received the absolute worst service I've ever repay a restaurant. The waitress was young and very inexperienced. Took our wine order then disappeared for 10 minutes because we had a question about on if the wines. My group finally flagged another waiter down so they could at least order drinks. 

She finally comes back with two bottles of wine but no wine glasses. Then tells us it took her all that time to determine that they didn't even have the wine we had the question about.

She didn't bus the table hardly at all throughout the entire meal. We finally gathered them up and stacked them in a corner of the table and even that wasn't enough of a clue for her to take them away.

At least the food was ok, but in talking to others after that night, this place is getting a reputation for poor service. With so many other great choices in Nashville I'd recommend you eat somewhere else.

Very embarrassed and disappointed. Suffice it to say, I won't forget this birthday.....

So glad we chose Woolworth for a late breakfast. The food was delicious and the staff were attentive. We sat at the counter where, as you will be reminded by the pictures displayed around, others made their mark in history. A "must add" to your list of places to experience while in Nashville!

Wow,First when I walked in it was great with the service. They wanted my money, okay..... How RUDE multiple staff members were to my son because he was eighteen (had nothing to drink) and at the strike of 7:00 out he and all went and we understand the rule, but to be that cruel. We only went to listen to the music and spend time with friends and family. Lost any future business...you suck!!!

This manager of this restaurant, Woolworth on 5th, who worked the night of December 11, 2019 is discriminatory. I did not get a chance to eat because of how poorly they treated me before I was even able to order. I live at the corner of 5th and Church so I walked there last night wanting to have a boozy milkshake & eat dinner. I was not feeling well all day yesterday and I pretty much stayed in bed all day. I had received some pretty upsetting news earlier that morning so not only was I feeling under the weather but I had spent the day crying. I don't know why this gave the manager the right to tell the waitress not to serve me based on the 5 seconds I had been in the restaurant & the fact that he had not even spoken to me nor did I even see who this person was. The waitress came to my table poured water for the table then asked if I would like anything to drink? I responded, "Yes I would like to try the Affogatto." She then said, how about something else like a juice or something non alcoholic? I responded with, "Why?" She then tells me that her manager told her not to serve me. I'm completely confused now because I have no idea why I could not be served unless the kitchen was closing, but then she interjects with, "You haven't been drinking?" At this point I'm absolutely baffled at why she or anyone would even make this assumption. I respond with "No, why would he even say anything like that?" First of all, I rarely ever drink, and when I do it is normally no more than 2-3 drinks because I do not like the way alcohol makes me feel after any more than that. I did not have anything to drink that day nor the prior 4 days to the date this event happened. I have an alternative style of dressing, so was because of the way I looked any reason to start making assumptions about me? She said she was going to get the manager, but whoever this person is, is not someone I want to waste any of my precious time on this earth on. Not only that but at that point I'm upset about being judged unfairly, so I get up and walk out of the restaurant.  I'm not going to give business to someone who makes a bad decision based on the way a person looks to determine weather or not they are to be served or not. Sorry but my friends & I would rather eat elsewhere then to be subjected to this type of discrimination.

Great Experience

It's not the original Woolworth's (from what I understand) but the history is still present. As a history nerd, this was a definite stop for me while in Nashville. I expected the typical tourist trap but the food was actually quite good. We had a group of six and everyone said their food was good. Not typically the case for a "tourist trap." Service was also very good.

The reason for the four stars is for a few reasons. I think my expectations were tempered thinking it wasn't going to be good, the competition around it with so much great food in Nashville hurts it a little, and the food really wasn't quite at the level of great. I still think it's worth the trip and the stop, especially if you like history like me.

My friends and I went to Nashville for the weekend and decided to get brunch before we left Sunday. We found The Sutler on google and I'm so glad we did! This place was awesome! We got there about 5 minutes after they opened and that was just in time because it was already full. If we had more than just the 2 of us we would have been waiting a while. Now that I have been there I would do the wait. They have live music and great food. The complementary biscuits were to die for; I could've eaten 20 of them. They also have bottomless mimosas. We opted out because we had drive. I got the beef Benedict and my friend got the avocado toast and I can't say anything bad about either. Delicious, she also got a side of hash browns which I wish I would've gotten instead of the grits. The grits were ok but were a weird consistency for my liking. Not to mention, the place is cute as heck! 12/10 recommend!!

Super Divey Bar with a great crowd and great music. Exactly my kind of place. Bartender was on top of her game getting everyone a drink in there hand as they walked in. Packed on a Monday so you know they are doing it right.
The food is amazing but Kristin and Virginia are the best parts of this place! They work so hard and make sure you're taken care of! We loved them!

I am not a native of Tennessee.  However, I am an African American.  As an African-American, I would have thought that I knew a bit of Tennessee relevant black history---unfortunately, not.  Thanks to my white Uber driver for telling me the history of Nashville's Woolworth and its relevance to lunch counter integration for the entire state of Tennessee...and thanks to the same Uber driver for telling me about the recent opening of the original Woolworth's as a restaurant.  Prior to a Valentine's Day concert at Polk Theatre, my fiancée and I had a nice dinner at Woolworth's.  Upon entering you can see the counter tops area to the right.  We were seated close to the kitchen area to see a peak into the bustle of the kitchen.   We decided to share an appetizer and entrée.  We ordered the roasted brussels sprouts as the appetizer and the blackened catch for entrée.  The food was very good and well prepared.  The entrée was served with a brilliant succotash.  We are suckers for roasted brussel sprouts and get them at almost every restaurant we go to.  I must say that it left us wanting more--in a good and bad way.  Good because they were delicious, but bad because we felt like the serving was a bit smaller than appetizer portion that we have had elsewhere.  

The wait staff was bit distracted at times, but I think they were in the mist of training.  We did not have a chance to visit the Mezzanine but I am assuming that is where more of the historical artifacts showing are stored.  Without knowing the history, no one would go there to learn it, especially if they knew nothing of Woolworth, the Civil Rights movement, and only visited the entry level restaurant space.  Without acknowledging and sharing the importance, wouldn't the owners just be taking advantage of the historic significance?  Just a thought.

This was the dive of dives! Smelled of pinesol and puke!
This may be a historical bar, but it was dark, cramped, filthy and overall nasty.
Don't waste your time coming here to eat. Beer was not cold, server was not at all friendly and the food was sub par. The bar has some cool decor and a decent patio but that's about it.

Came here with friends and their small child. We got a booth by the window in the front one Saturday morning so we could listen to the music. The menu was somewhat limited and our waitress seemed really bothered that she had to take our order and bring us our food. I wouldn't come back. Also, this place seems popular with large parties (like bachelorette parties).

Attended a Buffalo Bills pre game party here 10/4. I have never seen such a poorly run cluster fck 2000 fans arrive pretty much ON TIME for a 5:00 show/party. No separate line for prepaid tickets or even VIP. 2 people attempt to scan and sign in a line that was down the block does not make for happy fans. Once "in" to a dirty parking lot behind building scattered with old trash, the VIP area is a joke. Literally...shitty well brands of booze is the only choice...and blue light cans. Took longer to wait In line at the VIP bar for a drink than the general admission bar.  Not a chair to be seen anywhere. When the sun went down it was impossible to see the uneven grounds and steps making the area unsafe for anyone attempting to use the pitch black porta potties.   I was one of many that had no idea this was going to be held outside and judging by the shoe choices and clothing of others, clearly this wasn't stated . For a place that was entertaining 2000 people it seemed like there would be SOME food/snack choice offered over the 4+hour period. Happy to say the 1st band was great but after standing in the pavement for 3 hours and drinking no name booze In the " VIP" area  we headed out to a see more of Nashville than a parking lot.

No visit to Nashville is complete without a stop in to Tootsie's!  This is the original and it's still serving up drinks with the best of them!  Sure it crowded and loud but that's part of the fun!  We didn't wait long for all our drinks all night!  Great fun and great band.  They've even got a rooftop bar and patio!

This is where Taylor Swift was discovered. Bluebird is an iconic and legendary Nashville music venue. I really loved it here, the wait can be long to get in and its crowded most nights but you can catch some really great talent playing here. I would recommend this place to anybody visiting Nashville. The staff at the Bluebird are super cool and have a very laid back vibe. I would visit again when I am back in Nashville. Two thumbs up for the Bluebird Cafe, hopefully I catch this place when T Swizzle comes back to Nashville.
Food and service was awesome. Great selection of brunch items. Will definitely go back for the sweet potato pancakes!

Yes, it's a Dive bar- astro turf, plastic cups on the floor, empty pitchers on floor and I even found a wooden bracket on the ground because I stepped on it walking by! The tat tots are good and if you are drunk the food is awesome lol but not bad for a snack of tots or fries:) if you want a packed dive bar with live music GO here! There is only one huge problem for me about this place- the shots (served in small plastic cups) are $8.50!! If you are with three people that adds up fast! This place should have no shots over $6...it's a dirty dive bar!!  The bartenders aren't super friendly but with pitchers of beer selling at 6 bucks - they probably are over it! When I was there I noticed 3 bartenders so it was super easy to get a drink but shocked when I learned three small shots were $30. If you are with a lot of people and you feel like shots find another place- a dump like this serving in plastic cups is not worth it.

First time in Nashville, wanted to discover all good stuff I heard about this city and bars with live music ...And YES, I confirm that I had a great experience there. They do have multiple stairs with a live band in each...plus a roof deck. I am
Not a real country music fan but I loved it!!! Strongly recommend to hop there and have some good time!!!

Located in a strip mall. Stop in here for a drink before heading out to an event. We had 45 mins to enjoy a drink but it took 30 mins to get our drinks. One of the drinks never came. 
Our waitress seemed overwhelmed. We believe she didn't put our order in until one in our party went and asked her.
3 of the drinks we wanted were not available. They ran out of the beers. It was Friday around 6:00pm.

The music was good. The wall behind the stage is really cool- it made with cowboy boots. 
This place has  potential- the management need to evaluate if there is enough staff to meet the needs of the customers.

It pains me to write this. My husband and I ate dinner here back in December and had a 5-star amazing experience! We LOVED the fried chicken, and I decided then and there to bring my mom for dinner after seeing a play at TPAC in mid-March. I made the reservation several months in advance, and I was so looking forward to having this dish again and treating my mom to it as well.

I was shocked when we were seated and I saw that the menu had changed since three months prior. I understand restaurants change their menu, but I couldn't believe that the fried chicken dish had 1) gone from $14 to $26 and 2) came with haricot verts and fries instead of mashed potatoes, country green beans, and macaroni and cheese. Not only did it almost double in price, but it comes with less sides... one being fries. I was so disappointed. The fried chicken dish with the original 3 southern sides was EPIC and reasonably priced. I wouldn't have even cared about a reasonable price increase if the dish had remained the same. It was such a classic southern dish, and I was so bummed to find that I wouldn't be able to enjoy it again.

My mom and I decided to leave before we were ever even greeted by a server. To be honest, the place was not very busy, and I am surprised looking back that we hadn't been greeted since we were there for several minutes discussing if it was worth it to stay or if we wanted to go somewhere else. In reviewing the menu, it looked like everything had gotten more expensive, and I just wasn't willing to pay more when I knew it had been more reasonably priced (though still not cheap) just a few months ago.

I don't think the menu changes were positive, and it might explain why the restaurant only had about 10 tables full on a beautiful weekend evening when the SEC tournament was in town.

One of those gotta go to places when in Nashville.  Just try to avoid it during prime weekend times as it gets crazy crowded here (unless you enjoy being packed in like a can of sardines).

There are four (or five) levels with different bands playing on I believe three of them.  It is fun to drift around enjoying the different music.  

Make sure you hit the rooftop level which has a great view of Broadway-

Unbeatable intimate setting. It absolutely doesn't matter if you are familiar with the performers.  It will be an amazing experience that any true music lover will treasure for a lifetime.  Gary Burr & Georgia Middleman had me laughing & crying.  Their song writing skills & delivery are amazing so I was a little disappointed when they announced that they were bringing their friend Kenny on stage.  I was so enjoying them that I didn't want the vibe to change.  Their "friend" stepped up from a nearby table to play a few tunes with them.  "Kenny" turned out to be Kenny Loggins.  You absolutely never know who you'll see at the Bluebird Cafe.  Just go.  Reviews on food & service are completely unnecessary.  It just doesn't matter how good either of those things are.  You're there for a musical experience like no other.

Restaurant is good but it's way overpriced. For the price per plate and the look of the restaurant we were expecting amazing food and that didn't happen. We ordered wine and cava by the glass and neither one was good. It was just a big dissapointment.
Great food, drinks, service. Creative southern based menu with a strong well thought and creative culinary influence. This is a must go place.

Was recommended as this bar has been around for a very long time. Faded photos of stars cover the walls. We walked in off the alley and found seats on a Saturday at lunch. This was CMA weekend. The bar was comfortably crowded. The band played. We learned that the band get to play for one hour, then a different band sets up and plays. We ordered from the simple menu--pulled pork sandwich and fries--very good, delicious chili, and pimento corn fritters--hot and crunchy, but there was no green tomato jam served. I couldn't get the waitress's attention. That jam would have been good. The beer list was extensive, but there were no stouts. As we left we realized that we were on the middle floor. A stairway led to the third floor. We walked down steps and left through the front door which was the first floor. That room was smaller and a band was playing. This is a three-floor hole-in-the-wall bar, and popular with the music scene.
Went into this bar to bar hop. Didn't stay to long because there isn't much sitting area in this place. To crowded which is cool but the place is to small....
Worth waiting in the cold!!! This is a must while in Nashville!!! So intimate and priceless to be in a room listening to such talented people!
Good food, nice atmosphere.  Worth a visit for sure.  The fries are awesome!  If in Nashville you must come and sit at the counter where it all happened.  You get to eat and experience history.

Can I give it a minus 1 star? 
The hostess was extremely rude. I have never experienced someone at the front of the house treating not only only us ( but another group who was next to us) so poorly and disrespectfully - HUGE ATTITUDE! The message was "go away we don't want your business" ... said in so many words. Management alert !! Train your people! Regardless of how packed you are today, your success tomorrow is not promised!  I was shocked and disappointed at how we were treated. We traveled from California to attend. I am in the entertainment business and no one in our town would get away with treating guests like this and still have a job. I unfortunately don't have the hostesses name but if your interested in following up we attempted to attend Friday July 12th late show. She could have cordially explained the way it "works" there and invited us back another time. Just saying... :-( Maybe put a sign up on the door after your full ?) There are simple solutions to avoid uncomfortable situations in the future.

Came here for the first time tonight, my friends wanted to smoke a cigarette so we started to walk to the patio and there was a barricade saying that section was closed. We asked the doorman where we could go and still have our drink in our hand without having to go out the front(without our drinks). He said we could go past the barricade to smoke. As soon as we walk past the bait cafe one of the bartenders said we couldn't do that, we said sorry but the door man said we could to smoke... he said OK no problem. As soon as we got to the door another long haired bouncer came out cussing and saying "are y'all FUC*ING stupid or can  you not read??"
Then preceded to come out and grab our drinks and thrown them in the trash because we did not appreciate being cussed out as PAYING CUSTOMERS. Will NEVER COME back here.

Woolworth used to be so delicious. However, the recent menu changes and assumed recipe changes were obvious to our table of locals. The pancakes tasted microwaved instead of straight from the griddle and there were brunch items we just could not find on the menu. We asked if anything was different and it was confirmed that the restaurant had gone through a few changes. I feel like tourists will love anything, but it's disappointing when most of my local friends have stopped coming here as the food is just NOT the same. It's even more sad considering the historical relevance of the location. I would hate for this restaurant to go the way of so many places that have a short life span in this city due to tourists moving on to the next "hot spot in Nashville." Just a heads up, the locals do not like these changes. When suggested I'm often met with "they're just not good anymore."

Get there early if you want to get in. For most of the shows the doors open at 5. I got there at 3:45 and I was already number 55 in line. They only seat 90-100. If you don't get in you can wait in line to step in the entrance and take pictures. It was awesome, a must-do, but it takes planing and time! 

If you get there past 4:15 your chances of getting in are slim. It is a very small, intimate venue. You are crammed in there. We didn't have a cover charge, but there was $7 minimum food/beverage charge. 

The menu is small but you should be able to find something. We ordered Mozzarella Breadsticks and Sweet Potato fries for an appetizer. They were both amazing! I would recommend the mozzarella breadsticks (only 3 of them, but they are big). 

I ordered the pork sandwich and chips. The pork was very tender but I like mine with a little more BQQ sauce. I was full I didn't even eat the chips. Music was great! We saw Kevin So.

NOTE: just because you get in for the early show that doesn't meant you get to stay for the second show. They kick you out after and make you stand in line again. Basically there is no way to see both shows.

This was a must visit recommendation from my friends who have visited Nashville prior. This was my first trip to Nashville and I will add Tootsie's to my must visit list to tell others. Though each floor is small the atmosphere is amazing. All the bands were amazing and so much fun to listen to. The bartenders were amazing and so patient even though each floor was packed. It is fun to see the history and pictures all over the walls. This is definitely a place I recommend visiting even if it is for a short time or a drink or two.
The entertainment was amazing, there was a different band on each floor. Very friendly staff and great atmosphere.

Great atmosphere. The bluegrass band was a nice touch during brunch time. I had the shrimp
and grits which had a subtle Cajun flavor. The grits were creamy and the shrimp was seasoned to perfection. Also, they have bottomless mimosas. Bonus! Overall, great experience for brunch and the downstairs bar is a vibe in the evenings. Check it out.

Fun!!!! Great bartenders fun band!! Sheldon Road played and kept the crowd entertained all night! The security did a great job as well getting everyone out safely at the end of the night. My friends and I will be back!

Great atmosphere, had the fried catfish with red beans and rice, delicious. Kevin the chef is great. The pimento cheese with chips to die for . Great service. I would definitely go back. Fun place with a group.
I found the bar on yelp seems to me is a popular local place. There are two set of artist playing in the bar..i don't know the artist but enjoy the atmosphere.. it's loud but lovely..

My kind of bar. It's where the locals go. I have my favorites back home in Los Angeles and San Diego. Tinroof reminded me of home. They have live entertainment on most nights it seems. 
Most of the staff greets you with a sweet smile, i'd like to say the others were probably just too busy working  
The drinks are yummmy and the queso fries were pretty tasty   
When in Nashville you have many options as far as the nightlife, entertainment bar life go...I'd definitely check this one out!

This place is authentic and definitely not fancy. Great musicians make this place the best Honky-Tonk in Nashville. The bartenders are great too.  Hey when you look up Honky-tonk, this place is used as an example. Seriously, its painted a pinkish purple color on the outside. (only the outside..thank God) look it up. 

Bottom line, you go there for the music. 
Many Greats have performed here, Legends have been discovered here, and tomorrows Legends just may be performing there tonight.
The food is terrible. Chef can't even cook an egg. The drinks suck too but at least the mimosas are bottomless if you get drunk enough anything is edible right?

This is a pretty great brunch place!! This was another great recommendation we received on our trip. He cautioned, you will need to wait at least an hour. Come prepared to wait. They do not take call ahead sir reservations. 

Once you put your name in you can look to see how long you've waited and how many more parties are a head of you. 

They had some pretty good deals, such as bottomless mimosas. This is especially great if you are waiting. You can eat at the bar, but it is crowded so be aware. 

The food was great. I recommend anything with their biscuits!!!  The food came out surprisingly fast as well. I felt like we ordered, blinked our eyes, and the food was out. 

The bluegrass music they have playing is probably one of the biggest draws. It was so relaxing to listen to live bluegrass while eating. The restaurant itself had such a nice vibe to it. I can't wait to go back on another trip!
Great burger and fries served within five minutes during busy Saturday night. We had just left Rock Bottom restaurant after waiting an hour and not getting order

I came here twice during my Nashville trip and I didn't even realize it until afterwards! The first time I went in through the front and had a great time listening to some live music on the first floor. The second time I went through the back and had a great time listening to some live music on the third floor!

Both times I went the live bands were playing both old school and new school music which I liked because I was able to sing along and get into it with the band and I had a great time. The second floor was a bit more chill and didn't have a band (at least when I went) but the top floor also had a rooftop bar. It was definitely a chill night and no one was going crazy or acting too drunk. Everyone was just sitting around and listening or dancing to the music. There was a mix of younger and older folks.

If you're planning a Nashville trip and plan to bar hop, definitely put this place on your list!
Go to place when in Nashville. The rooftop bar was awesome with live music downstairs. 25 bucks for 3 drinks. Worth the visit.

This is the best restaurant in Nashville! The barbecue sauce is to die for! For reference, I do not like bbq sauce but what they have is completely different, a much lighter and liquidy sauce. Everything was cooked expertly. Probably the best breakfast/brunch I will ever have in my life. Our waitress topped the experience off with great service. 

Corn cakes: So good and filling. The bacon on top had something on it (jalapeño according to the menu) that gave it that extra crispy oomph. And just like bbq sauce, I don't like bacon either! All the elements - perfectly poached eggs, pesto on top of the corn cakes worked harmoniously together like a love song for my tastebuds. 

Corned beef hash: This dish had the bbq sauce! The beef was so tender, it was like pulled pork. I wish the corn muffin was bigger because we were fighting each other to get more of it. 

Sweet potato pancakes: Very tasty and cooked just right. The maple syrup was exceptional, not too sweet. I would ask for a different side because the bacon was the weakest link out of the whole meal. 

This is a must try that I always recommend to anyone I know who may be travelling to the States! If you appreciate good food, customer service like it should be done and history then do visit! I want to go back...

I'm so happy we decided to eat here for brunch. The food was delicious. Our server Kim was outstanding. She was pleasant and made our experience 5 star. Kim was friendly, knowledgeable of the menu, and had a smile from beginning to end. I highly recommend this restaurant.

Great music but don't go on Friday night if you expect to get your food. Settled in and waited 45 minutes for chips and cheese and a second glass of wine so definitely check to see if they're too busy to handle you. If not that it's a great time Great music but don't go on Friday night if you expect to get your food. Settled in and waited 45 minutes for chips and cheese and a second glass of wine so definitely check to see if they're too busy to handle you. If not that it's a great time
Husband decided to stop here, after sharing a flight at the Tailgate Brewery.  Meet some really nice people here and bartender was quite knowledgeable. Nice Dive bar.

Trying to find a breakfast spot on a Sunday morning in the heart of Nashville is a challenge especially on game day. We wondered into Woolworth and not sure what to make of it. The potato's were finely cooked. Eggs were perfect and service delightful.
Alabama fans not welcomed.  Got a big FU BAMA from the band.  Moving on to better bars in midtown....

The atmosphere is fun, open floor plan and the historical nods are present everywhere, from the music to the decorum. I really enjoyed the projection of classic movie and music clips on the wall above the kitchen that can clearly be seen from anywhere. The hostess was exuberant, funny, and knowledgeable, but my server wasn't as personable. She seemed a bit overwhelmed. The food...was fantastic. I had the shrimp Po Boy and a refreshing cocktail. The best Po Boy I ever had. Will definitely be returning soon!

As we were aware, this place gets cramped REAL quick! My boobs rubbed against so many backs trying to squeeze through  I should have gotten  a couple drinks or phone numbers,at least! 

Front room was not even possible so we worked our way to the back room after being served our drinks crazy fast. The band in front really had the crowd going. The band in back (wish I remembered their name) had a female vocalist with a killer hair-do. The girl could sing! We enjoyed ourselves for a bit and chatted with several people. The place just has a great, friendly vibe to it. Never did make it upstairs. Looked like a good size crowd for early afternoon enjoying another band.

We went here on Wednesday night to the 6 o'clock show. All reviews and word of mouth really built it up. It was a great time. The drinks were a little on the weak side but that's the way they are at a bar. We also split an order of nachos and they were fantastic!! A pleasant surprise!!!They also had nice big napkins, very absorbent. The show we saw was "In the round" and the main guy was Lucas Hoge with three other guys who have wrote songs with him , Eddie Killgallon( from the 90's band Ricochet), Drew Powell ( it was his first time playing at the BlueBird Cafe), and JD Wood. They played lots of real good songs some we recognized and some were brand new. We had a really great time and would definitely go back!!!! I gave it 4 stars because the young guy at the register where they sold T-Shirts at the end of the show was an A$$Hole with ATTITUDE. That is not the way you want to end the experience. Kind of a bummer. I hope the Blue Bird reads this but they probably won't  and probably don't care because this is a gold mine for them  that people everywhere want to experience. If you like both kinds of music Country and Western you gotta go. I highly recommend it.

I traveled to Nashville and this is the one spot I wanted to spend my birthday at. Tickets sold out online super quick so we decided to go and wait outside in hopes of getting it. I was super excited and got the chance to go in.

This place is a cute cafe that caught my eye when watching the show Nashville. Seating was good because anywhere you sit you can see the stage. They also have drinks and food where the waiter/waitress come around to you. Drinks came out quick and food was good. 

I loved watching all the people go up on stage and perform there own songs they have written and really liked the positivity in this cute place. Staff and owners are super friendly and genuinely love there jobs.

Perfect place to enjoy great music where a lot of the top
Notch artist have performed at! This place is a must when traveling or living nearby!

The filet steak is AMAZING! I will definitely be back to enjoy it again. Also, Jordan and Sam were amazing bartenders. They helped out with our large party and made sure we were taken care of at all time. They were kind and attentive. Definitely go see them and try the steak if you have the opportunity.

My mother is a history buff person. So coming here was on her list of things to do. 

I am not always comfortable talking about things that have to do with the segregation or desegregation between people. 

The reason I'm giving this place a 5 is because of the extremely cool lady who was our waitress. She had the most beautiful name (Zakira) and was really friendly! 

I know I can be a weirdo but she was cool with it and even told us how her mother came to naming her. Which was also a really sweet story. 

So thank you for your kindness and letting me add your name to my 'baby name list' (even though I'm 75% sure I'm not going to have kids-LOL)!

Very crowded for it's size (it's huge), and kind of dirty. But it's Nash-Vegas, can't really expect perfection. Come here just to get drunk and hear some good live music. It's one of the first bars you'll notice when you get to Broadway.

I will never come back here again. We had an event booked here until 10pm and they shoved everyone out at 9:00 despite all the money we paid. Very violent.  Do not give them you money. Very rude and a lot of other bars worth your money.

This place is soo trailer park that it lives up to it's name! Lol I gotta say though the food is good and it's the best for your 2am munchies! Tater tots a must! Sliders a plus! The music isn't so bad!!
Very eclectic place! Where u can see the Xmas tree made of green colored tires! And AstroTurf with rocking chairs!
The set up could be better to listen to the music near the band!

Tootsies was everything they said it would be and more! We had a blast! The musical talent on stage was top notch. They really owned the crowd. Our servers were amazing they literally ran back and forth hustling us drinks and were super gracious and it didn't hurt that they were gorgeous. The only thing Tootsies could improve on is their bathroom situation. Everything else has me looking forward to going back next time I'm in Nashville.
You can drink beer and listen to music all day here.  What else could you ask for?  Beers are reasonably priced and music is great!

Great bar and have had a blast here but the band playing right now is not as awesome as they think they are. Refused to take a request for less than a 20.00 tip. Not that talented. Playing Sunday around 7:00.

You want to love this place. Great location. Fantastic history. And a wonderful wait staff. But after going there multiple times, over a long timeframe, and sampling different menus and dishes, you can't get past the mediocrity of the food. Which in Nashville - packed with some of the country's most amazing restaurants - is a shame. It's not hard to ruin avocado toast, but somehow they managed it, by saying it's on focaccia but really putting it on tasteless wannabe Texas toast. It's not hard to ruin "baked eggs" over grits, but then you get a mess of scrambled eggs. And if you've got only one steak option - at steakhouse prices - make it a better quality cut, and learn to cook it. Medium rare isn't brown in the middle. Just constant sloppiness all around. You might be more forgiving if it was less pricey, but not for what they charge. The best you can say is, the food is hit or miss. Some dishes are OK, most are meh. When you can get a reservation any time on OpenTable, you know people must not be fans. (Scroll through the reviews and you will see similar commentary.) Really hoping they can turn it around, but until things improve, recommend booking elsewhere.

WARNING!!! If you think you really are in the que to get tickets, you're fooled!  So is everybody else!  In the matter of seconds, the seats were disappearing before I could even hit proceed.  I have been waiting for months for the day to purchase tickets and NOTHING! YOUR SYSTEM SUCKS!!!
Great experience while visiting Nashville for a concert. Authentic diner experience. Great burgers!!!

Fuckin racist! Please tell me why me and my bridesmaids just got kicked out of the bar after some 50 year old bitch tried to push my friend off a stool??? My friend sat on the stool that was EMPTY and this women kept shoving with her butt..we asked her to kindly keep her space. ...then we asked her to stop and she shoved my friend then the security guard insisted that we must leave. Mind you.... im fucking sober!!! This 50 year old C*NT HAD THE AUDACITY to tell me she was going to punch me in the face. . But doesnt get kicked out??!?!! My group which was a mix of indian girls and white girls get kicked out for what??? The bartender... told us he doesnt give a shit and there were other bars we could go to... ya no fuckin shit!! We came here thinking the environment would be fun! The security guard who had to escort us out understood but the prick who kicked us out wouldnt even listen...nice job you prick.

Yes, it's real. And yes, it's as good as the hype. If you're lucky enough to secure a seat, GO!

Did not have food, but the music was outstanding. And why people, I'm looking at you, 50 year old women in front of me, can't follow the "no cell phone use" rule during the show is beyond me. Really? You're THAT important that you can't go 90 minutes without checking your texts?? I was "this close" to ratting them out to Don Schlitz!

A Fraudulent charge from Tootsie's appeared on my credit card and their phone has been disconnected.  I couldn't even dispute the charge with them!  Calling the Nashville non-emergency police proved that even THEY don't have a phone number for Tootsie's! Use caution when charging here.... I recommend paying with cash only!

We very much enjoyed the band here - the music was excellent!  A great crowd and lots of enthusiasm The beers were $6 each and were icy cold.  Lots of fun!  We didn't have a problem getting a drink at the bar or at a table.

This is a beautiful venue. It wasn't as large as I was expecting which was a pleasant surprise. There are food trucks and beer vendors but make sure you bring cash! Parking is free but it's field parking so try to beat the rush at the end of the night if you can.

Bar, music, good service. Just as overpriced as the rest of the bars on the strip. Turns out this place has some history, they didn't mention that at midnight on a Saturday. Anyhow, service was great for the bachelor party I went down with. Cool joint, definitely been there a while and has the scars on the building to prove it. This was my favorite joint I went to.

A strong 2.0!  We decided to dine here because of Nashville Cares, where the proceeds from your dining experience would help the charity.  We asked our waitress, Mo, what were her recommendations since it was our first time and she recommended brisket anything. Well babe and I are brisket enthusiasts and we know good brisket so we gave it a go.  We decided to order the brisket nachos and the cheeseburger to share.  Lord why was there hair in the nachos??????!!!??? Of course we sent that back. Turned me all the way off but by then the burger had come out so we decided to eat it with caution.  Babe had to send her tea back bc her glass was dirty. My glass had water spots. This restaurant doesn't seem to take pride in cleanliness at all.  You know when you see one thing out of order you see everything and we had ENOUGH. Take home message: If you're looking for a grundgy, live music spot to get sloppy drunk at and don't care about food quality, this may be the spot for you.  All others, don't waste your time!!!
Yes, it's real. And yes, it's as good as the hype. If you're lucky enough to secure a seat, GO!!!

This really is the place to come on Broadway. There were 3 separate stages, no wonder there was so much good music. I liked hanging around the second stage on the second level until I got up to the third level and saw that band. They were awesome and singing all the latest country hits which I really appreciate seeing as I'm newish to country music. 

The drinks were average price compared to the rest of the bars on the block too.

This place has great history around civil rights era. We walked in and felt we went back in time. Sat at the counter and ordered breakfast. I had a biscuit with gravy and a fried egg.  The biscuit was different - not your typical white floured biscuit but it was light brown and fluffy, not heavy or dense. I wonder if folks here are judged by their biscuits?  . Needless to say, it was very very good!  Husband had corned beef hash that was great - nothing we ever had in Boston.  This hash had chunks of corned beef, caramelized onions, crunchy potatoes and black eyed peas. Northeast corned beef is more like consistency of canned dog food - odd.
