The waitress, Kara was so kind and sweet. We chatted about foods from the South and foods from the Northeast. We clued her in on korean fried chicken. She laughed when I told her I struggled with really good homemade fried chicken. She was adorable!

I would go back again in a heartbeat

I keep coming back to the Sutler for the mimosas, the music, and the service. Cat is a great server who always makes our girls brunch dates so special. They are updating the menu and the additions are FIRE. The sutler is here to stay and has wormed its way into my heart forever.
Food was great, drinks were good. Loved hanging out here. Our server was the best part, though! Super nice and helpful. I think her name was jordon?

I moved to Nashville 31 years ago.Ever since I've lived here I have had food catered from businesses that I worked for.I also worked in Brentwood for almost 19 years.Not one single client ever said a bad word about Pucketts food or service either.This place and Lovelace Cafe are two of the best home cooking places I've ever eaten at.I'm born and bred in Tn.and was raised eating awesome Southern Food.My only issue is I live in Cheatham Co.and its a long drive to go there.
We had diner there which was very good. service was also good. It has a nice atmosphere and a long bar with many barstools.

My trip to Nashville was a therapeutic one. The past year was riddled with deaths, terminal illnesses and the end of a 20-year-marriage. I came to create new, positive memories. The Bluebird visit was a sentimental one. I attended the charity event show on Tuesday 1/22. The show was fantastic. I was not disappointed with the music or merchandise. I was, however, extremely disheartened by what happened after the show. I dropped my wallet near my seat and when the waitress brought it to me (at the merch table) I realized $1000 had been removed. The thief left a $20 bill inside. The waitress became defensive and was unempathetic. I spoke with the manager/bartender who was rude, condescending and unapologetic. He did call the police for me but refused to give a statement or have any involvement in trying to rectify this situation. He stated that the Bluebird has no cameras in the venue and I was just out of luck. It was really disappointing and created a terrible memory for me. My takeaway from this is patronize this establishment at your own risk. The talent is phenomenal but the employees just might have sticky fingers. This was an expensive night at the Bluebird and a lesson in human nature and greed.

Visiting Tootsie's was one of my top bucket list items when visiting Nashville and to be honest it fell short. Maybe we went at the wrong time of day (Sunday, Memorial weekend) but it was just not what I expected. We were promptly served on the first level, which was nice, and bee-lined it upstairs where the vibes matched that of a standard corner bar, with less charm. The band was mediocre at best and reminded me of bad karaoke. I guess I just envisioned much more from this Nashville icon.

What a fun brunch!! Live bluegrass, bottomless mimosas for 17$, amazing brunch options, and fast service!!! Loved the brisket hash, but my favorite was the shrimp and grits with the Cajun creme! The monkey bread is a MUST! Great coffee too!! Would definitely come here again on a trip to Nashville!
The hype of this place!!!   Asses to elbows and can't even get a drink or move.  We said nah and moved along.  Would try again if it's ever not that packed.

Nicole was a great waitress! She took care of our whole party (over 10 people!) and made sure we had an amazing time. We did the bottomless mimosas and she always made sure our glasses were full. We loved getting to know her!

Worth the wait didn't have tickets waited for hours outside to get in and was well worth the wait. Environment is good music is awesome just to say you been there is cool. Worth the stop and is a must when in Nashville.

Great Happy Hour! You can get a craft cocktail for 5$ and experience live music. It has three different environments. Upstairs there's a typical Nashville bar/restaurant atmosphere. There's also a patio outside. Downstairs, there's a wannabe speak easy downstairs, it's a speak easy decor with modern music. Downstairs, there's also a billiard room with a ton of pool tables. There weren't as many people in general as I thought there would be, but it started picking up after happy hour. It was quick service and they were very friendly as well! There's also a parking lot which is a plus!

I called then at 11am Sunday  8/27/17 talked to this rude bartender on the phone. I asked for the owners number because I wanted to let him know I am calling the health dept on there San Diego location but this idiot says why are you calling me on a Sunday to complain to me about a issue with are San Diego location insaid can I speak to a supervisor non there manger non there I asked for his name won't give it he needs to be fired

Love this place! The music and bartenders are fantastic lots of fun. We had no problem ordering a drink the bartenders practically flag you down as you walk in and made our drinks fast. All of the performers were engaging and so much fun. It was neat to see all of the old photos of celebrities on the walls.

"Doors open at 5:30pm" but if you don't have a reservation, you will be waiting another hour at least before all the resos swagger in (we didn't have a reso, and got in at 6:45pm after music started). Actually you may be waiting for 2 hours in the walk up line and not even get in the building. This information was not communicated well enough I thought. 

Also, the doors didn't open at 5:30pm. They opened at 6pm because everyone had to wait for the bartender to show up before people could go in.

The music was quality. The food was decent, but I won't be back again unless I'm hired to play :P

My husband and I would not describe ourselves as country music fans, but everyone we know urged us to check out the bluebird when they heard we were visiting Nashville. We reserved tickets online in advance and went in with an open mind. We knew nothing about the singer/songwriters when we got there but left feeling like we knew them. The place is very casual and intimate, and the songs and stories were beautiful. The only downside for me was a few songs were really sad and I lost my dad recently - I didn't see them coming (should have, its country music, lol) and I was a bit blubbery and embarrassed toward the end. Definitely evoked a lot of emotion, which is great when you're not so sensitive! Looking forward to going again, prepared with tissues in my purse next time!

This was a great surprise. We we out Sunday night and couldn't find a place that didn't have a 2 hour wait. Found this nostalgic, historic little gem. Food, service and price were all good. The atmosphere was just plan fun. BTW our wait was less than 15 minutes.

Fun bar with a cool vibe, really enjoyed the lighting & doesn't seem to get as crazy busy as other bars in the area. I went during an open mic competition and enjoyed some live music which was a nice added touch. They have decent happy hour deals and good prices outside of that. A good spot to grab a drink, only critique is that the service could be better/faster. Aside from that, pretty good overall!

So I finally made it out to the Woods Amphitheater at Fontanel. All I knew is it used to be one of the Mandrell's place and it was now a concert venue and it is like super far away. Super far, to this in-town snob, being anything over 15 minutes. I know, spoiled!

Kid Rock is the man that finally got me out to this place for his first Fish Fry concert. So I am not sure how it is normally set up. But for this event they had it set up kind of like a festival or fair really. There were food trucks lined up around the perimeter. Picnic tables, standing tables, and hay bales around to sit on and eat. Carnival games and a ferris wheel. Cornhole boards set up throughout. Fire pits when it got later. Behind this was the actual stage/amphitheater. And plenty of beer stands and liquor stands. For this concert the beer was $5 for a big beer. THAT'S FREAKIN' REASONABLE. I suspect that was Kid Rock's doings. Mixed drinks were $7.

The actual concert area was interesting. Seats were available in front of the stage but all around and behind them is just grass and you get there early if you want to put a blanket down and get a spot. Otherwise you will do like I did and stand the entire concert. But that's ok since it was Kid Rock and what else do you do except rock out and get your redneck on when he's playing? The VIP areas are kind of cut into the side of a hill but damn, they seem pretty far away from the stage to be VIP. But at least you have a little seating area. Concessions are to the side and the back of the seating and it is kind of dark walking over there so be careful. AT LEAST the bathrooms were ACTUAL bathrooms and were clean and there were a ton of stalls. SO that's nice. Concessions line wasn't too bad I don't think but I'll be honest - I don't remember some of those details after being there since 4 pm.

Other things to note...security did a legit thorough check of my bag. I mean, she was digging in there and feeling all around. It must have been the yelp shot glass I happened to have in my backpack. Luckily she didn't find the fireball!! But if you are trying to sneak in a little nip just know that they may get really serious about searching you.

The other thing is...man, when you first show up you are shocked at how much other stuff is out here. There's an Inn? And a restaurant and wine bar? WHO KNEW? Certainly not me since in my mind this place was like an hour away. But really it was only about 25 or so minutes away.

That brings me to my last tip. If you are going to drink - and why wouldn't you? - you shouldn't be driving and you certainly shouldn't be driving up here. You can taxi or Lyft or Uber but your problem will be the lack of rides home AFTER the show. We planned ahead for this by booking a car service to take us out there and then pick us up at a specific time to bring us back. This was the way to go. We had people asking if our limo was full up quite a few times as we were leaving. Get your friends together and pitch in for a ride if you are going to drink. Or draw straws to see who gets to be the DD.

Basically I thought this was a fun event. I am not sure if that's because of the fun festival vibe that he put on or if all concerts would be as fun. But if you get a chance to go to Kid Rock's fish fry next year then you know what to expect!
This place was a quick stop stumbling outta another place. Awesomely divey... I likee !!!

I came here with a small group just after 10 on a Sunday for brunch - it opens at 10, and it was already pretty packed! They don't take reservations so you just have to get there early and plan to wait a little bit. The hostess told us to expect an hour wait, but it was really closer to 20 minutes which was a pleasant surprise! We ordered bottomless mimosas and didn't think they were terribly strong, but the price was definitely good ($17 all you can drink). The Bloody Mary bar is also pretty cool. The live bluegrass music was so so so good! They were really talented and we enjoyed them a lot. The biscuits before our meal were a nice touch and super yummy! I was a little surprised at the menu - the breakfast portion is about 10 entrees, and the "Benedict" comes with fried eggs (it's traditionally poached) which was odd to me so i opted to skip that one. My cousin got the breakfast sandwich and she was not impressed at all. My breakfast tacos were awesome, but the potato hash was a little plain. Overall it was good, music was fantastic, service was a little slow but a cool vibe.

A fun place to listen to live music and eat a basic, bland brunch. The band wasn't too loud and was very fun to listen to! The hash browns were mushy and unseasoned. The eggs Benedict was fine but nothing to rant about. Bottomless mimosas for $17 was a great deal!
Loved the nostalgia! The hot chicken was good, but hot! We had the most awesome ice cream sundaes! Great service!

My girlfriend and I heard a lot of good things about Tootsie's from friends who had been to Nashville before.  We decided to listen to them and give it a shot, and we had an awful experience.  The music was subpar, the bar was too crowded, and the drinks tasted bad and were rather heavily priced. They even questioned my ID - we had to deal with the bouncers.  I would not recommend this place to any one of my friends, plenty of other fun bars on the same street to go to that are much better.

An inviting theme meets live music and credible pub grub in the heart of Nashville. 

If nothing else, Paradise Park Trailer Resort wins the most unique concept of all the Clubs/Bars/Honkytonks on Broadway. The setting is simple - your local trailer park. Faux wood walls, disgusting Beer soaked astroturf, even Christmas lights up all year long... Paradise Park Trailer Resort has the trailer theme on lock down. All you need to bring is a dirty undershirt and beaten wife to complete the experience. Throw in live country music and reasonable drink prices and you are in double wide heaven. 

I stopped in with a good friend to sample the trailer park life style along with a nice IPA and a Burger and was impressed by the friendliness of the Bartender (and yes...he has all of his front teeth). He recommended the #4 which is a Bacon Cheeseburger served with a side of Tots. The food arrived between the time I finished thinking about growing out a handlebar mustache but before I considered options in homemade neck tattoos.  

Paradise Park's Bacon Cheeseburger is a simple, honest, and tasty affair consisting of a 1/3 pound medium cooked patty topped with molten Cheddar and 2 slices of thick cut Bacon, Lettuce, Tomato, Mustard, and Ketchup. A large Sesame crusted White Bun acts as the delivery mechanism and does it's job splendidly. The Tots were an admirable bunch coming out piping hot and seasoned simply with Salt. Wash down with copious amount of a hoppy and floral IPA between bites for maximum desired effect. 

For dessert I tried the Kodiak Chewing Tobacco sampler. Just kidding - that doesn't exist but maybe it should.

Went for happy hour with some girls from work and we ordered drinks. Music and environment was good and we were feeling the vibe. I ordered the Big Ol' BLT and fries. Food arrived and tasted good until I discovered mold on the bread of the sandwich. Brought the concern to the attention of the waitress and she responded by taking the moldy bread off the sandwich and proceeded to leave the remainder of the food. I let her know that I had no interest in consuming anymore food that remained. Waitress replied, "we are going to check the bread". We proceed to exit the venue for an after meal smoke and she approached the table,  asking a fellow coworker if we dipped on the tab? Very poor customer service and food that is at best out of date. No manager ever visited our table to extend apologies or to offer a token gesture. Last trip to the Sutler.

Addendum: After making the request to the waitress to speak with a manager, Shannon, came by our table. He apologized for the issue with the food and comped the meal as well as drinks.

The process of getting tickets is what is the most frustrating process of this website. A huge turn off making people wait like they do and not get anything. You could be waiting in line for 30 minutes and when its your turn it would be sold out. If you aren't going to get tickets why would you still make people wait?

Good luck if you are trying to acquire tickets!
Such a cute place! Great simple food w such character. Great cocktails too!

This place is AMAZING! The brunch is soooo good. Grits are to die for. Mo is the BEST bartender I've ever had and I'm from Vegas. She was SOOO cool and accommodating and suggested the best food. We had bottomless mimosas and never saw the bottom. She was so kind and recommended so many places around Nashville. Best place I've been in a long time!

i would have thought this would be one of those places with 500+ reviews. this place is one of those once in a lifetime type places in their sense of entertainment. especially their wednesday and saturday night shows.  just happened to be there during a singer/songwriter circle session.  2 hours of songs they've written in constant rotation.  i'm blown away by the talent i was able to witness for a mere 10 buck cover and buying a drink.  i don't know when i'll be able to witness such a collaboration because it's one of those "for one night only" kinda of deal.  

anyway, the place is small - it legitimately is just a cafe that happens to have assigned seating when you get there.  it happened that there was a mix up with the seating and they accomodated our seats to be together and that's awesome.  they have decent local beer selection and a pretty full bar and eat your heart out with standard bar food if you'd like.  you come here for your show though.  don't be picky about who you're gonna see and you might be surprised like i was.  i'm glad i got to witness a bit of history here.  pretty neat.
The Back When 80s/90s Night is beyond fun. The DJ spins all the hits and takes requests as well. Don't miss it. And dressing up isn't required but it does add to the fun.

This is truly a once in a lifetime experience and if you find yourself in Nashville, I would recommend this over any tourist attraction that you may be drawn to. It is a short drive away from the city, but totally worth it. I pre-planned this and reserved tickets online before we came, so I don't know how it works to just show up for a show. Judging by the popularity - you'd better get in line early. However, I had been on standby a week prior to the show and reserved seats the second they went on sale. Because of my willingness to do this, we got a table so close to the performers that I could have licked them. It is a small venue that holds about 100 people - very close together. However, once the show starts you will be grateful for the intimate nature of this spot. They have food, beer, wine and soft drinks only. I didn't come for the food and I only ordered a slice of homemade chocolate cake to meet the minimum $7 that they ask you to spend per person. The cake was fine, but nothing food-wise to write home about. I went to a "in the round" show, which is basically four singer/songwriters singing their own songs - some which have been published and some not. They tell you stories about the songs, about the business and it really is a very cool experience. Being as close as I was, it felt a little awkward to take photos, but they do allow it - just no video. The whole thing lasted about two hours and I could have sat for another two because it was just that great. I paid a measly $15 for this experience and it was by far the highlight of our trip. Don't miss this one.

Great, fun place to see a show and spend an evening, but there are just too many issues that keep it from being more than 3 stars.

The good: it's beautiful.  Can't imagine a much more pleasant place to spend an evening listening to music.  The employees were friendly.  Food and drinks were pricey, but not as bad as expected.

The meh: if you shell out a ton of money for the VIP section or for seats (for a seated show), you might be able to see.  Might.  If you're on the lawn, good luck (though we were to the side of the stage and the performer seemed really aware that we were there, so we actually had a better view than expected).  For an ampitheater, it's really flat.

The ugly: the traffic/parking situation is pretty awful.  Other reviewers have covered this pretty well, so I won't harp on it, but yikes.  I mean, if you get a "good" parking spot (near the venue), good luck getting out within an hour of the show ending...  And it's a total crapshoot where you're going to park when you arrive - depends on the random pattern that they're using.  We left early and avoided much of the mess, but our friends were not so lucky.

Old school honky tonk with three floors of bars and bands. We had a blast, although the first floor band was tops. Not to mention the two bartenders downstairs killed it all night. They were awesome! Not many bartenders can serve such a packed house and still make every customer feel like they are the most important in the room.

The Sutler provides a true Nashville bluegrass brunch experience with live music, bottomless mimosas, and delicious southern food. The atmosphere is authentic and gritty Nashville style, which is a refreshing experience versus the fancier brunch spots around town. Expect to wait - they don't take reservations and this is a popular spot.. you'll have more luck with a smaller party, but even so, it's worth the wait! Especially since you can enjoy bottomless mimosas and live bluegrass while you wait. 
We tried the Breakfast Tacos and the Smoked Brisket Hash, and both were delicious. We were so excited to eat that I forgot to take a picture until we were almost done! Also, our waitress was on point - she never let us see the bottoms of our bottomless mimosa glasses. 
I can't wait to go back again! Two thumbs up.

The new express lunch is fantastic! It was recommended by Mo the main bartendress who is always super helpful and conscientious of customers. You never have to wait if she's working she's full go all the time! Best service!Love the turkey avocado wrap and chili combo!

Nashville resident who spends a fair amount of time downtown, so I'm always looking for a different place to try--tried Woolworth on 5th Sunday and couldn't be more pleased! It wasn't overly crowded, so the service was excellent. I ordered a fairly complicated drink from the bar and it arrived timely, made perfectly and priced fairly. Going out on a limb giving 5* after only one visit but the food I had deserved it. Somewhat more upscale than most other restaurants on the block, but the food prices are not much more. Worth the climb up the hill and I definitely will return!
If I could give a 0 stars, I would. The bartenders are very, very unfriendly. I asked for a double and the poured half a single. They charged me $10 for that. DO NOT GO HERE.

Visited with a few girl friends before a concert and I really enjoyed my experience. The restaurant was beautiful and I loved how they managed to keep so much of the buildings history intact. I sat at the lunch counter while waiting for my friends to arrive and had great service from the bartender. Once we sat down, we ordered cocktails and more wine and Brussel sprouts with bacon as a starter. They were amazing- the bacon was thick and flavorful and the sauce was sweet and complimented the Brussels perfectly. 

I ordered a chicken salad which was good but kind of boring, but what really impressed me was my friends food- one ordered the fish and it was awesome. The collards were the best I've ever tasted, the fish was flaky and crispy, and the corn bread and biscuits on the table made me want more. I definitely want to go back to try the rest of the menu/ those hot pots are calling me!

Wonderful place to eat, which is also full of rich history!

We stopped for brunch (I highly recommend reservations!) on Saturday, and wasn't disappointed.  We all ordered different cocktails, and different meals, which ranged from sweet potato pancakes to the steak and potato Hash.  Every entree and drink we ordered was amazing! Cooked to order and fresh. 

Service was also on point/outstanding.  Our server was attentive, knowledgeable of the menu and made some great recommendations for us to try.

Highly recommend a visit while in Nashville!!

I came in with my boyfriend on our roadtrip from Texas and LOVED our experience. Krystal was very friendly and so was the security (maybe Mark was his name?). Beer was served promptly in a very busy bar which was appreciated a ton! The music in the front and in the back was a great touch as well!! Mark quickly emptied the bar at closing time and suggested we go to The Diner which was a wonderful suggestion! Thank you Tootsies, we will be back!!

The food and ambiance were great. The building is beautiful and the fact that the location has a historical significance made the experience even better. We shared the fried pickle and tomato appetizer, which was great. I wish I could remember the name of the waitress because she was amazing!

In town visiting Nashville for a long weekend. Was looking for a place to grab a couple of beers and food and Tin Roof was awesome. Hot chicken sandwich was amazing. Scott was the manager on duty and greeted me right when I sat at the bar. The staff was attentive and the food came quick. Also pretty sure country music star,  
Luke Combs was in visiting which was cool! Tin Roof was great.

Tootsie's Orchid Lounge es un clásico de Nashville, un bar enorme donde bocha de locales y turistas se juntan a beber, escuchar música en vivo y bailar un poco los distintos ritmos de la región.

El lugar es bastante grande, tiene varios pisos en donde en cada uno tocan distintos músicos y bandas a la vez, hay buena onda y mucha gente en cualquier horario del día.

Sí, el lugar es copado pero -a mi gusto- ofrecen tragos que no son para nada buenos, aunque -como imaginaran- la onda de este bar es ir a tomar birra de botella y escuchar música en vivo a morir, por lo que si ese es su plan, Tootsie's no los va a defraudar, ya que es todo un clásico de la ciudad.

Apparently this was a place we "had" to go to since we were in Nashville.  I was unimpressed.  There was a rooftop bar, so that's awesome, but the drinks were insanely expensive ($9 for a vodka soda?!) and we had to wait in line to get in but they didn't seem to be actually keeping track of how many people were inside because it was still too tight to move at times.  The line moved extremely fast- we were almost a block away and got in in like 10 minutes- but I would have rather waited a little longer and actually had some breathing room when we got in.

Tootsie's is whatever right? Just gotta day that they hire the most unreasonable/square minded bouncers I've ever ran into.
Couple friends and I were denied entry due to one friend "not having sleeves"
My friend then continued to put on a long sleeve t shirt and the only thing anyone could regurgitate was "FUCK YOU GET ON THE SIDEWALK BITCH!"
Absolutely absurd in my opinion.
Never going to any place who talks to other people like that...
1 star is entirely appropriate for that type of behavior

The Bluebird Cafe is a must see if you're planning a trip to Nashville. Thought it does take bit of planning since it's not always easy to get tickets.  It's a small place with only around 20 tables available.  Most shows go on sale a week in advance and sell out FAST. 

PLEASE read the reservation instructions, have your credit card ready  and review the seating map prior to making your reservation. Once the reservation process starts you only have a minute to complete it. Tick tock!! There are also limited seats available if you want to stand in line for a while before the doors open. 

Fees vary by performance but normally include a $10 minimum order per person. We both had a sandwich and a couple drinks so there was no problem with that. Everything was reasonably priced. Food was ok, typical bar food.

All that being said it's a great experience. We were lucky enough to get seats right next to the stage.  There is no talking allowed while they're singing. Even one of the performers mentioned how different it was to be playing in a bar where everyone was listening!

We visited Tin Roof twice in our short visit to Nashville. To me, that says a lot considering the many great places to go! Tin Roof is two stories and has a small balcony for smokers. It's nothing too special or fancy but the live bands were great each visit and did a wonderful job interacting with the crowd.

Very popular location and a great spot for good live music. The bands at any location  in downtown are not shy for panhandling but they deserve it anyway. Be prepared for the band to ask the crowd for free drinks too , I found that to be very forward lol. The bartenders were laidback and fairly attentive. Love that this place has multiple Floors with multiple bands playing. Definitely going back after dark to get more people watching and band listening in.

I read that Tootsie's is one of the must visit honky tonk bars in Nashville so that was the first one I stopped at. To be honest, it was just ok. The band that was playing was fine, not good or bad, and the atmosphere was like any other bar. I found much better live music down the road at Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville.

Came here for bottomless brunch on Fourth of July with a group of seven. We waited for an hour or an hour and half to be seated but I was surprised that we were even able to get a table as there was a ton of people there. I had the breakfast tacos with a side of potatoes which were both pretty bland even after topping it with the salsa that it came with. I doused them in hot sauce to make them edible. The servers were pretty prompt about refilling our drinks and there was a live music so overall it was a good time.

While at times it can be hectic at the Sutler when Mo's working you don't need to worry. That girl is on it! She recommended the express lunch and it was delicious and a great value! They have a great brunch on the weekends but I started coming for lunch and happy hour. Mo has to be one of the best in the industry and makes my day when she's working!

It's the best of the best on Broadway.  We came on a Thursday night thankfully so we did not have to wait in the half-a-block-long lines that were formed there on Saturday night.  Tootsie's has 3 floors each with its own bar and live musicians.

We headed up to the third floor where the rooftop bar was at, in hopes it would be a little cooler and we could get a view.  It was packed so obtaining a coveted spot along the rail was challenging but we did find the sweet spot in the middle of the floor directly beneath the AC vent.  (:

The band performing that night was incredible, taking requests from the audience, sometimes odd requests, but managing to pull it off.  The crowd was a real mix of ages.  Good vibes.  We had a great time.  Only wish I could have stayed longer.

Paradise Park is a perfect place to go on a weeknight before a show at Bridgestone. While everyone else is jamming up Rippy's or Brewhouse, you can be left in peace (relatively) at Paradise Park.

Standard divey bar on Broadway. Some interesting features include:
- Live band (ok, no different than the other bars, but worth noting)
- Photo booth right up front when you walk in
- Skee ball
- an old beat up convertible demolition derby car that you are more than welcome to sit in and take pics and look redneck
- basketball games in back
- crane games (my favorite)
- decently strong drinks

They do have bar food but...I don't really recommend eating here. There's better bar food in town, so just go there. Keep this one for drinking.

You will want to come hungry to Woolworths, the portions are huge & the staff are fantastic. We had the reuben & mercy me it was incredible. I am a hearty eater but thank goodness we shared this sandwich. 

The food is reasonably priced & a great value for the quality of food. The extraordinary history of the Woolworths is not to be missed & the pictures throughout the restaurant highlight the fight for equality. 

We liked it so much we are returning before we depart Nashville, a must stop on your tour of Nashville.

What an incredible, nostalgic breakfast at the counter of Woolworth's on 5th. Wow. Just wow. 

We were fairly concerned with parking availability, but easily found a parking place at the public parking lot around the corner, not even a block away. We made the mistake of trying to park in the parking garage across the street, but were kindly instructed that was for business parking only. Oops. Lol! 

Upon walking into the building, it was exactly like I thought it would be! We were immediately in love with the history and felt a little bit transported back in time. 

We had table reservations but decided to sit at the counter. Jonathon was our server and he was such a dream! He was so knowledgeable and ultra friendly with such a beautiful smile. 

We ordered from the breakfast menu and selected sweet potato pancakes with jalapeno bacon and the Hoppin John omelet. All was delicious! After a second cup of their awesome coffee, we took a few minutes to tour the downstairs area where they feature live music and a second bar area. Theres also another area upstairs, but it was rented out for a private event. 

Such a wonderful experience and we will definitely go back! Highly recommend.

Stopped in for dinner on a Saturday night and immediately found a place at the counter. I think they're doing a great job representing the historic significance of this location. It leans a little toward the upscale end of options as far as downtown Nashville offers, but not so upscale that you felt uncomfortable wearing the jeans you wore to the Honky-Tonks. 

The menu has the perfect amount of options. I ordered the pot roast and a cup of the seafood gumbo. Both were excellent and I devoured them very quickly. Woolworth also has a nice drink selection. Everything was really good and the staff was super nice.

Oh Tootsies.  I don't know why but I found myself here on 3 separate nights in Nashville.  Why?  Well probably because of no cover, 3 floors of live music and a super cool roof top lounge that you can easily escape the crowd and people watch the hustle and bustle down on Broadway.  Each time we had a good time, and saw good music and talked to good people.  TIp, enter from the rear though the alley on a weekend to avoid the line and super packed downstairs room!

So, this is The Nations, huh? Interesting. After being gone for so long, I have a hard time remembering if certain areas of the city (or, outside the city as this area technically is) had names/designations or if this is an outgrowth of population explosions, search for housing and what not. Whatever the reason, increased interest/activity in urban renewal* is usually a good thing. So, The Nations... and The Stone Fox.

I'd heard much about this out-of-the-way spot long before coming here and am pleased to note that it lived up to its billing. It's moody, interesting, fun, and full of potential. Kudos to the owners for having the vision and concept. And kudos, also, for having a 2 for 1 beer special going on with Bingo on a quiet Monday night. I can dig it. And, I should dig it, given the '70s throwbacks throughout the air and on the walls. $3 well drinks made things go down pretty easily, as well. Being that I was hungry as well as thirsty, I studied the menu for some choice eats. I almost went to town on the black bean chicken chili nachos (right? how good does that sound?) but our waitress talked me in to the comparatively healthy chickpea/beet veggie burger... which I, then, proceeded to make unhealthy by 'Elising' it with bbq sauce, onion ring, pickles, cheddar cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion, and avocado topping. Of course, it was magically delicious. How could anything *not* be with all those amazing toppings. The veggie burger itself was a bit crumbly but that's par for the course with homemade veggie burgers.

Food coma starting, I got my second of the 2 for 1 beer and walked around a bit. The dj was spinning '70s tunes on vinyl. The bartender was doing some interesting things behind the bar. But my attention was held by the deck. This wooden charmer was made for warm weather and cold beer. I'll be back for it. There are a lot of good things going on at The Stone Fox. Regardless of where you live in the metro area, hop on over and give it a spin. 

*Let's keep it responsible.
Awesome place.  Stopped by on an early Saturday evening with the family and we had a great time.  The band on-stage was really good and the food was awesome.  Highly recommend.

Unfortunately, not as good as I'd hoped. I think I must have been here on an off night, as almost every interaction was a bit askew. It started from the very beginning.

Parking at The Sutler isn't easy. The lot is shared with two other businesses and the back of the lot is (I believe) reserved for residents of the mid-rise. With so much interest in this neck of Melrose this equals congestion. There may or may not have been a valet. I thought I spied some attendants on my first pass-by but they were nowhere to be found upon my second. After circling the lot a few times, I lucked out and found a patron leaving. I slid into the parking spot she vacated with a few minutes to spare for my reservation.

Yep, reservation. I knew the interest was high, so I didn't want there to be any confusion about seating. Rather than stick me at a two top in the dining area, I was seated at a high boy in the front. Despite noting that I had a reservation (for one; I didn't want to bring anyone to a place I hadn't yet vetted) and pointing out a two-top was available, I was seated at a wobbly high boy... directly in front of the music board, in the corner. It was, easily, the most uncomfortable seat in the venue... and I had a reservation. 

Sigh.

In an attempt to balance the table, the host almost spilled my beer (more on that in a bit) on me as he worked on the table. His adjustments helped slightly. I was beginning to get in a foul mood. Wanting to turn things around, I ordered a cocktail and appetizer. Surely some food and booze would turn this night around. Yes and no. The queso app was pretty delicious. Any time you add chiles to three cheeses and spread it on a bread product, you have a hit. I found that the number of crackers didn't keep up with the amount of queso but that was easily rectified. My cocktail, was not as successful. I ordered the East Bound -- a vodka concoction starring strawberry soda. I am the demographic for this drink. Unfortunately, the strawberry soda was more reminiscent with cough syrup than Crush or Nehi and the cocktail was overly-iced so the balanced was watered down very quickly. 

Pressing my luck, I decided to get dinner. I ordered a beer and a Horseshoe. My beer preference changes seasonally. At the time of my visit, I asked my waitress about what reds she would recommend. She suggested an IPA and a porter after telling me they didn't have any reds. I ordered a Highland Gaelic Ale. A red. It's not the end of the world but I'd rather someone say they don't know the answer to a question than answer something with authority and be wrong. The beer came... without a glass. The server came, dropped off my beer and kept it moving. Again, not the end of the world but certainly not the expectation for a venue that has an active beverage program. Always offer a glass. Getting ahead of myself but when a manager stopped by my table, she noticed that I didn't have a glass for my beer and offered one. At that point, I'd already been drinking it and turned the offer down. It was nice, though, that someone noticed the error. Also, it was between the time to beer was brought and the manager came by that my beer was almost spilled on me when the host attempted to adjust my weeble wobble table.

Keeping up? Okay. The saga continues...

I lived in Chicago for eight years. A group of my best friends in town were all alums of the University of Illinois. What am I getting at? I know from horseshoes. There are bars that do nothing but specialize in the comfort sandwich which is helpful during six months of winter. What I had delivered to my table (already a shock at $16) was not a horseshoe. I took a picture as it arrived to my table because I was in shock. Again, at $16, the sandwich was already way overpriced. What I was served was shameful. I won't go in to detail. I don't need to. The picture says it all. As luck would have it, I was sitting close to a twosome from Illinois. The gentleman at the table looked at my plate, as I took my picture, asked if it was the horseshoe. I answered that it was and as a former Chicagoan, I was shocked. It was then that he revealed that he and his gf were from Illinois and they agreed. In fact, they decided not to eat at The Sutler after seeing my plate. They had drinks and kept it moving. I discussed the plate and my concerns with the manager. She mentioned that prior to working at The Sutler, she'd never heard of the horseshoe sandwich and what I had before me was the chef's take on the Midwest staple. I... don't know about that.

Despite my sweet tooth, I was eager to get my check and leave. I came to The Sutler anticipating a fantastic evening. Unfortunately, I experienced a series of disappointments. I'd hoped to have the same experience others yelped about. I did not. After my evening at The Sutler, I don't think I'd return.

Loved this place! We visited on a Friday night. We had drinks, pimento cheese, meatloaf and pot roast. Everything was wonderful! Our server was attentive and gave great recommendations. This was a lively spot for a Friday night dinner, not too loud though. We had the most fun, we loved the decor, and history. Overall everything was fantastic. We will be back. Thanks Jordan!

I am sad to say this was a total and complete disappointment.  The historical significance of the building is the ONLY thing that gave it that second star. If you take this concept and do it RIGHT then it will last for years....but at this rate I doubt it will last another year.  We sat at the counter and there were maybe a total of 20 people in the restaurant.  The service was SUB PAR at best. They handed us the cocktail menu, which looked pretty good, but when I went to order they were "out of" two things on the menu.  After my obvious look of disappointment the bartender brushed it off as "meh, new management....i don't know...". I ordered the fried chicken which wasn't terrible albeit a little dry but I struggled paying $15 for something I can get for $10 and tastes MUCH better at Swett's.  Much improvement needed,  Woolworth.

It is what it is, super cool! A very popular place in Nashville and very packed, but fun. We had no problem bellying up to the bar for a drink, our bartender was quick and efficient. I was impressed with the service.  

We went up a small set of steps, up to the 2nd level, which was nice and of course equally packed, lol. There is a rooftop level which looked like a great area to hang out in. 

No matter where you are in this lounge you can hear the live bands playing. Gotta love Nashville, great music at every turn.

I will definitely return. Next time though I just might plant myself down in this place a bit earlier in the day, for a load of great country music and daytime drinking! Ha.
I love this bar so for how old it looks and feels like i am your at a bar from home. Such good music and old Decor. The drinks are reasonably priced and the bartenders are nice.

This legendary place is a throwback to all the Woolworth's that used to fill every city where you could shop 5 and dime items and eat at the diner counter. There is no longer a shopping area, it is now just a restaurant but it brings back memories of sitting at the counter and enjoying a great meal at Woolworth's. And still great food too, had breakfast there. Very creative southern and soul food items on the menu. Apparently this place was famous for some civil rights stuff and was gone for a while and they brought it back. But I just love the nostalgia of being at Woolworth's, especially since there are only a few left in some cities most of which are not restaurants, just landmarks at this point. Cool architecture too, I think the building was built in the 1890's and went through several changes in 1913, 1925, and finally 2017.

This tiny venue is not only the backdrop for the hit show, Nashville, but also boasts performers such as Taylor Swift.

Reservations fill up weeks in advance and by a stroke of luck, we got tickets to an open mic night, just the day before. Because there were only two of us, they put us right against the stage. We got to watch 18 solo musicians stand up on the tiny platform and sing their heart out for a few minutes. A few got called up for a second round. 

We enjoyed fries and beers and loved the intimate feel of the venue. We truly got to know the crowd and singers. Such a magical night!

The food experience in Nashville has been superb. Spot after spot, I am delighted. The Sutler did not disappoint!! My meal was absolutely mouth watering and The Gambler (drink) was made to perfection!! 

The space is huge... There's a billiards room downstairs as well as a lounge. Seems like a pretty decent spot for nightlife. I will have to revisit when they have live music. The happy hour is great, the food is great, service great... Get on down to The Sutler ASAP!

This is one of my favorites! Treat yourself to the Smay and enjoy the scene. This is a great place to go with friends when wanting to grab drinks, listen to music and talk. They have live music events and always a great place to see the up and coming! The fishbowl is always a fun drink too, but the Smay is my favorite drink in all of Nashville

Historic Tootsies!  While this place reminded me of some of my old hole in the wall bar haunts from college - we had a great time at the 3rd floor bar.

Quick service, cold beer, yummy pretzel bites with cheese and really fun singers on stage.  

Great visit.
Wow!  This HAS to be someplace you visit!  Great historical value!!!  Everyone in this place was polite and talkative.  Great food and service!  Sam made some amazing libations!!!

You've got to put Tootsies on your "must see" list.  Great atmosphere and they get the best talent.  We loved new comer Rachel Curtis.  Watch out for the pimento cheese bites ... my mouth was on "fiya!!!"

Happy Hour review: 
When looking for dining options downtown, it can be difficult to find something that a local would want to visit, but I am happy to report that Woolworth is a really nice option! This diner-style open concept is unique and gives a feeling of art deco. The projector showing old movies and background music adds to that feeling I'm sure. I love the giant long bar and stools; the overall vibe of the place is really nice. We grabbed a seat around 5:30 for happy hour. They offer drink specials with a daily cocktail for $5 and wine, mules, and martinis for $6. We ended up ordering a bottle of wine for $25 or so and split it between us. For food we ordered the fried pickles, okra, and jalapenos plus the soup of the day which was broccoli cheese. It was a nice snack and everything tasted really good! It was a perfect way for 2 locals to kick off a fun night out (cheaply) adjacent to Broadway. I'll definitely be back to sample more of the menu!
VERY cool dive bar. Decent prices. Large beer menu. Cool atmosphere. Definitely would return.

I wanted to like this but it was nearly impossible. The hostesses were extremely friendly and we got our table immediately.
Off to a good start! Started flipping through the drink menu and noticed there was just wine. Asked our waitress- who seemed less than thrilled to be there- if there was a beer list and she informed us that there were pages missing from the menu we had- she brought us a new one.
My husband and I both ordered the blood orange IPA. The waitress left and 5 mins later came back to tell us that they were tapping a new keg and it would be a few mins. No problem. Came back 5 mins later and said they were having trouble finding the keg. I ordered a new beer- Wicked Weed sour, only to find out that they were out of that one too. I decided to not have a beverage. Later I noticed all of these yummy mixed drinks being ordered at tables around us-- our menus must have been missing the mixed drinks page, too. 
I ordered a bowl that included root veggies and eggs. Decided to pay the extra and get seitan added. Found out they were out of that, too. Clearly some restocking issues. Received my bowl. Not bad. It was supposed to come with an herb hollandaise but of course mine didn't have it.
Told our waiter and she told the manager and came back to our table to say, "it should be on the bottom". Well, it wasn't... but I don't understand why it had to be questioned. 
Overall the food was okay. The service was mediocre and they clearly need to update their menus. It's really disappointing to go somewhere and be out of nearly everything you order. We won't be back.

Bridal party came here as a result of a recommendation and were wearing matching tanks. Male bridesmaid attempted to join and was denied because men in tanks are not allowed as a rule. Fine. Put a woman's top on him to allow him in as most of our party was already inside and asked to speak to the manager (picture attached). He said he really didn't care what the rules were as long as he got paid by the owner. So.. TO THE OWNER... stop living in 1854 this is bachelorette central and we want to support your business within reason. Your manager made it very clear that there was no discussion to be had and was Borderline homophobic in his responses to my questions regarding the bars policy. All experinces with this jackass were rude, condescending, and fake. Would not recommend this bar to anyone looking for a GENUINE Nashville experience as this bar only values numbers and revenue.

Note- manager refused to provide me with a real name. Pictures attached to ensure accountability.

Our server Levi was amazing and very attentive. The drink special was strong and delicious. The restaurant was very cute and they even had an old movie playing while we ate. I ordered an appetizer of fried pickles, jalapeño and okra and it was BeRY good. 

We went for happy hour on a Friday and the place was not very crowded which I personally appreciated at 4:30 after work. It is downtown so it is going to be garage parking unless you want to walk a ways. 

I'll go back!

My experience at Woolworths on 5th was good, I had the half fried chicken and it was very flavorful (well seasoned) and crunchy! The side dishes mac &  cheese, sweet potatoes and collards greens were on point as well. My only suggestion, based on the theme of the restaurant would be to play music of that era.

Honestly, we didn't go here for the food, but the lure of seeing upcoming music artists perform. We didn't make a reservation a week out, so we got there at 4pm, braved the cold weather and stood by the front door to get "first come" seating in the overflow church pews for the early 6pm show. We got in and were delighted with the front pew seating we were given. Most of the bistro sized tables were packed with 4 chairs and squeezed into the small performance area. I'd choose bar seats or the tables around the outside walls if I made a reservation. 
My 5 star rating is hugely an indication of the "music experience" provided by this intimate setting and the four fabulous entertainers we saw tonight. I would highly recommend this venue to experience the journey aspiring artists follow in search of making it big.  We actually enjoyed this performance better than our Ryman concert earlier this week!   
Don't miss this place! I wish I was a local so I could come here weekly.
So, food? Fish/chips, burgers, salads and nice selection of beer.

This place was pretty cool but was way too crowded, even more than the neighboring bars. When I mean crowded, there was so many people that it was hard to get a drink from here, so we didn't even bother. However, the scene was pretty fun active here, which was kind of funny because the other side of this establishment was a fast food joint, serving up casual eats like corn dogs and tater tots. In this area, it wasn't as crowded but still kind of lively like at the bar side of this establishment. Would I come back? Probably, hopefully I can easily get a drink next time I do!

Tootsies is a Nashville treasure! The legacy of this bar and all the great talent that has walked in this place is legendary. The bar in its self is a wonder for the eyes. Both the food and the music is a feast for your soul. The place is filled with happy music loving people with a great staff, strong drinks and an even better story to tell written all over. You can spend hours here just looking at all the priceless memorabilia! If you are coming to Nashville then you must stop by for some true Southern Comfort! As Always, Enjoy!

This place is so tiny. It's booked as the best honky tonk. But it really looks like a dive bar the walls are old and hard to see what is behind plexiglass. It just isn't kept up well. And somebody please tell me why kid rock has his face on the front of this place?  He's a yank and a suck up.  Hes got his own embarrassment of a bar so I think tootsies could take down his picture. This place needs to be shut down for a couple of months and fixed up to be the bar that they claim to be. I definitely would not recommend this place as it is now.

"The Stone Cold Fox Jumped Over the Quick Brown Dog" (possibly not the actual name)  certainly has that family feel.  The fact that I ordered Elise's favorite FROM Elise may tarnish my Yelputation for honesty, but it was kind of neat.

Overall I can see that this is one of those places where they want you to come and hang out.  They have a large space for live music, and where else can you go for a Velvet Tom Selleck? Nowhere *I* have ever been!

Parking is no problem, they seem to have plenty of spots for the overall amount of space inside, 

Elise's Favorite was quite good, (I assume it is her favorite for this reason) and unique. I'd never had an Avocado on a Burger before.

One complaint of mine is that (I believe) the soda is from cans, and it wasn't very cold.  But I suspect soft drinks do not represent the bulk of the beverage sales here.  They have a pretty decent bar, and quite a selection of Beers. I didn't imbibe but none of those that did seemed disappointed.

Its a bit off the beaten path, but I certainly recommend it!

3 levels of live music
no cover charge
BUT must tip the bands that play
Nice character of the bar with old pictures all over the wall and thousands and thousands of notes handwritten on the wall.
Have a patio out on the 3rd floor with a nice view of the broadway
Drinks are cheap
Crowd is fun
Busy even on a Tuesday evening.
If this is your first time in Nashville, a must drop by for a drink and listen to some good ol' country music

Most lively bar on a Tuesday night. And I mean lively. Rooftop was packed shoulder to shoulder. Singers here were really, really good (and we didn't love EVERY singer on Broadway). 

Walls on floors 1-2 are littered with history. What's really cool, unlike Legends beside it, is that a lot of the photos are of country music legends of old actually singing INSIDE Tootsies. Most authentic bar on Broadway for sure. 

As a male, must wear sleeves after 7pm!

We came to the Monday night showing at 9:30pm. This show didnt have tickets you could reserve in advanced, but was first come, first serve. Knowing this, we arrived at 8:15am to stand in line. We were the 1st people there. While we were waiting outside, the earlier open mic show was still going. We knew that the cafe would be cleared out after open mic to make way for those of us waiting for the next show. While waiting, a couple walked up and asked if we were in line for the show and we said yes. They asked when the doors were supposed to open, so we told them 45 minutes from now. The woman got upset because it was raining and cold, so she went inside and the staff allowed them to get a table but also didnt make them clear out before the next show. Meanwhile, the rest of us stood outside in the rain. The staff should follow their own policies about who gets in at what time.

Secondly, I asked the door man if the cover change could be paid with a card. He said " we prefer cash. We will run a card if that's all you have, but we won't be happy about it". Nowhere on the website does it say cash is preferred. They finally let us in and I go to pay my cover and the cashier woman says "I can't take your card, you need to pay cash". I told her the other guy said card was fine and she replied "well, I have no mechanism to run your card with. There's an atm at that bank over there." I asked her if we could choose a table first and then get cash at the atm since we had been standing outside in the rain for an hour to guarantee a good viewing spot and she was pretty exasperated at this idea but let us do so. Apparently the card machine stopped working right before they let people in, but she never explained that or apologized. She was super rude

Lastly,  apparently on Monday night they have a reduced menu. This is not mentioned online. The choices of food are limited to 1/3 of the menu that they have on their website. We didn't eat dinner in preparation for being able to eat at the cafe and based off the choices of food they list on their website, so to limit our choices to chicken strips or fish n chips was just misleading and annoying.

The band gets 5 out of 5. They were funny and incredibly talented. The best musicians we heard during our time in nashville. The cafe staff however could use some customer service training and learn that the patrons are the ones who keep you in business.

The Sutler definitely has a saloon-like atmosphere, with reclaimed hardwood and cowboy boot decor.  It's located next to Sinema, another pretty new restaurant, all in the up-and-coming Melrose neighborhood.  You wouldn't expect this super-cool restaurant across the street from a pawn shop, but it's there!

For my drink, I had think what I had was the East Bound (didn't get a menu pic!), described as a strawberry soda with a kick.  There was another drink I'd wanted but they didn't have the ingredients for, and what I ended up with was something strawberry with a very interesting finish.  We asked about it because it felt like a spicy floral, and it was some kind of liqueur or bitters that gave the effect.  Not bad for a fresh-tasting beverage; not sure if I'd get the same one again, but I like the creativity and would be into tasting more concoctions.

For starters, we had the Sutler Queso Spread jar, which was chilies, cheddar, gouda and belle chevre, spiced peanuts, and saltine crackers.  There was also a really delicious jelly served too.  Overall, we wished the queso was more like *queso*, vs. a spreadable cheese.  Dipping not spreading.  The jelly was probably our favorite topping for the saltines.

For our main meal, we decided to split the Brussels Sprout Hash and a Bear Creek Brisket Horseshoe, which was brisket, Texas toast, house fries, and a cheddar ale gravy.  I love eggs, so we topped it with a fried egg to boot.  Awesome!  This was definitely the highlight of our meal.  I don't like vegetables, but the Brussels Sprout Hash proved itself to be tasty (and a happily less healthy version of the green stuff I'd expected).  But our absolute favorite was the BBQ stack.  The cheddar gravy was thick but a great complement.  We dug in with forks and cleaned the plate.

Overall, I'd come back to The Sutler.  The service was great, and even though not everything blew my mind, there's enough good there to keep me curious.  I'd love to try their pork fat fries, and maybe one of their "dunks", a sandwich literally served IN a bowl of soup.  Interesting, right?  This place has a great ambiance and pretty solid eats.  Oh, and PARKING!  :)
Great food, excellent service (Juliet is amazing!). Atmosphere is great for a history buff like myself. Huge portions! Will come back for sure!!

Band was great, room was packed. The atmosphere was awesome! That was until it came to interacting with the employees. I sat at the bar and it was literally impossible to complete my order with bartender, Tony. Initially, it took quite a bit of time to get him to even acknowledge me. As i began to order I was cut off and he walked away. Then, a few minutes later, came the first thing I was able to say. Then quick walk away. This continued for another 30 minutes until I was finally able to order to other items of food. When I noticed the people next to me who ordered a similar item get my food before me, I waited a beat, then had to ask for my food.. which apparently was never prepared. After this I went to the merch counter to get a couple items. The best way to describe Molly at the merch counter starts with a C and ends with a T. I have never had anyone be so blatantly rude to me by asking a simple question about a t-shirt style - to the point where she wouldn't even look at what shirt I was talking about. She rolled her eyes at me, gave me serious attitude and snarky responses. 

This place would be great if they restaffed with polite, customer service driven individuals. I don't plan on ever going back to this place.

We visited Tin Roof based on a recommendation from a friend who went to college in the area while visiting Nashville. The bar was incredibly welcoming to tourists. They have live music inside and a standing and seating area out on the patio. The bar was well-populated for a Wednesday, but was by no means overcrowded. 

What we enjoyed about our visit was their Wednesday $3 drink special on a wide variety of draft options, including several craft beers that would cost 2-3x more at other local establishments. Thursday had drink specials for "Big Gulp" Budweiser products.

If you're looking for a perfect brunch place, this is the one. I absolutely love their bluegrass brunch, it's such a cool atmosphere and everything is absolutely delicious. We try to come any chance we get!

Keep your wallets as far as possible from this place. I got charged 10€ for one orange juice. The waiter also put ice in my orange juice...who the fuck puts ice with orange juice? Like shit in a strawberry shortcake.

Been here a few times with my fiancé. This time she had friends with her, and she was going ahead of me to meet with them. When I get there, she said that she was hit by the bouncer. (She passed through one bouncer, and didn't realize she needed a stamp. The second bouncer literally stamped her face in an aggressive manner.)
She had the stamp on her face to prove it.

So, ladies, be warned. 
The manager said that there wasn't anything he could do right now with the bar being short-staffed. 
If it was my bar, and I had someone assaulting women, I'd fire him on the spot and do the job my damn self.

Naturally I had to visit one of Nashville's most historic spots. Woolworth lived up to all my hopes with its rich history and delightful food. If you don't know this is the location of the Nashville sit ins during the Civil Rights movement. Those original stools are still there today.

Woolworth gives you a great experience with interactive service and food that will have you coming back for more. I tried their salmon and it was perfectly cooked and came out in 20 minutes. They also have a great drink menu so be sure to check that out as well!

If you were planning to go to Nashville I highly recommend you put the Bluebird Café on your itinerary.  It's one of those places that you drive up and go, "this doesn't look so special", however it had to be one of the most spiritually wonderful and intimate cultural experiences I think I've had traveling in the US. 

It combines all the great things about Nashville into one place, wonderful music, spiritually enchanting, pretty good food and all-around soulful fun time.  It is very much a great date night, but will be great cultural experience for the kids too. It is what Nashville is all about, not to commercialize country music you hear on the radio today.

Be sure to book your tickets weeks before you go. As we were told we completely lucked out being able to get in the same day we thought about going. The place is always booked up, but the secret is to getting there early on the day you want to go. Be sure to look at the website for times  http://www.bluebirdcafe.com

They take a total of 10 extra people, first come first serve after for the 6 o'clock show (Doors open at 5 PM). There's also a later show.  The trick is getting there around 3:30 PM and getting in line.  Dori and I got there around 3:50 PM and we were number 9 and 10, however 11 through 15 got to come in as well sometimes they make special accommodations. However by 4:30 PM there were 50 people in line.  

The folks that showed up to play, were accomplished musicians as well as accomplished songwriters for some of Nashville's greatest singers. I have to say, John Scott was there, and was absolutely fantastic. I have paid hundreds of dollars for tickets for other singers, that do not compare to him.  His presence and his music was incredible. Be watching for him I think he's going to be big...
I literally just had the best chicken sandwich of my life... in fact I'm only halfway done eating it and had to stop to leave this review.

This one of our last stop on our first trip to Nashville.  
This was a horrible ending and horrible experience and this place.
A great nice gentleman bartender greets us and get us our drinks - we met some fun people at the bar on our right and on our left -- Having a great time. 
The TORY a female bartender appears. She asked us if we would like more drinks and I looked around and I replied " I think we are OK -I'll let you know when we are ready"
As I turned around I thought I heard here call me an asshole. I asked the couple on my left is she did and they confirmed she did and heard it. Well we were all shocked that TORY would do something like this for no reason. So I went to ask for the manager and ask TORY why she would cal me that for no reason and she starts screaming at me on how she is the bartender and she deserves more respect - and I could not believe as the customer I was being publicly berated by TORY- We were not intoxicated - I ask for the manager - them manager invites me into her office -I explain to her the situation - She replies TORY is on of our best bartenders and must be having a off night. I said your best bartenders calls customers assholes for no reason and publicly berates them? She continued to apologize and offered a round of drinks which was very thoughtful.
When we return I return to the bar - TORY is still not pulled off the bar or moved to other side - continues to throw us evil stares and bad looks and huffing under her breath -- So we took our money and spent in a much more classy establishment that TORY has probably never been exposed too. 
I never need to see the Honky Tonk again !!

If your a different ethnic group...I wouldnt't recommended this lounge. Tonight we brought over 20 people in a bar to enjoy a drink. The staff are rude and non cordial to people of there on type. I'm so appalled that this place even being on the road map for places to go. The hospitality is far from welcoming. I highly wouldnt't recommend this place. Nashiville this is NOT worth my 1 star. I didn't know a place like this even exist. Words can't endure what i felt tonight....Ronda Yoon

Attended a networking event at the Sutler. This was my first visit. We partied downstairs in the cellar.  I was thoroughly impressed with this setup.  A cozy little gem I've been missing out on.  The bar is huge. It practically stretches the length of the room.  The bartender is fantastic and pleasant. He can make anything you dream up. I didn't get his name but he was cute :-) The wait staff was wonderful, friendly, attentive to the large group, and provided great service all night.  We ordered I think every appetizer on the menu and they were all delicious.  Our event took place on a weekday night during happy hour.  As we wrapped up, there was a bad setting up to perform. I was so in love with my new discovery that I hung around to hear what the band was all about. At least I tried to. The band never played and it was almost 2 hours after their supposed start time. A little disappointed I finally left but will definitely return to try and catch the next one. The Sutler is a beautiful and inviting hang out for great libations and spirited laughs.
Eh... overrated. Three floors. Expensive drinks. At least the bartender was super friendly and pretty!

BOUNCERS SEXUALLY ASSAULTED MY GIRLFRIEND!!!! 

!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

If its friday night and you and your friends are looking for a night out, I beg you avoid this place at all cost. I can not stand for a business that hires employees which such vulgar, demoralizing, rude and sexist attitude towards its customers.  First of all, my girlfriends breasts were touched and frisked by a large black male around  6'3" (seemed to be a bouncer, very beefy man with a beard). This all happened while we had first entered the building. We walked through a group of bouncers who had the smell of alcohol on their breath. They proceeded to catcall at my girlfriend, which infuriated me. While walking through their group one of them grabbed my girlfriends left breast. Fuck them There is nothing more unprofessional than employees being intoxicated on the job. Apart from employees being drunk and having wrapped their hands around my girlfriends breast, they also threatened and insulted me when they accused me of  having a fake ID and I argued in my defense. After all this, I tried to leave and as I did the employees tried to "kick me out".  On top of all this the venue is shitty and gross. Do not give your money to these scumbags. Friday night was ruined.  An added note, this place does not mess around with fake ids, but they do take bribes if you are trying to get your Fake back give them 40 bucks. -- ILLEGAL

A really fun opportunity to see small and local artists as well as big songwriters performing for a small and intimate crowd.  Definitely advised to get reservations online ahead of time!  Also know that there is no talking allowed during the show.  As far as the food, it was a bit overpriced but all very tasty.  Ordered the black bean burger (spicy and juicy) with homemade chips (come out hot and perfectly seasoned).  Loved the chipotle mayo it is served with and the whole grain bread is a unique touch as opposed to the usual hamburger bun.  Also got the chicken and bean quesadilla - huge portion with lots of chicken, black beans, and corn.  It was spicy and not overly cheesy.  The salsa that it came with was fresh and very yummy.  Chocolate cake is also a good ending!

Everything on broadway blends together after a while. But I really liked tootsies and here's why

1) great music-- I liked their variety better than some of the other places on broadway 
2) great service! The management found my wallet that was stolen the next day and were very helpful and cordial dealing with me 

Otherwise, be warned this place is quite popular so it DOES get very crowded so weigh that when choosing a place to go on a typical Nashville night. Overall a great time

Definitely a dive bar but it's legendary so you have to at least stop in. It's pretty crowded. The roof deck was poached. 

The trick to getting in is to go in the alley way. 

There were three live bands playing.

This place is off the hook (over) crowded! Great music and a good time! One of the bartenders was a b*tch to myself and my friends on two separate occasions. TRULY's is NOT the same as White Claw, instead of throwing it away you could have communicated that you don't serve TRULY but the girl outside just 50 feet away does. She threw the White Claw in the trash. I paid for my friends drinks and I walked away with nothing for myself! Just because you work in the most popular bar in Nashville doesn't mean you should treat your customers badly. She doesn't belong in that bar if she can't handle the crowd.

This was such a fun spot to visit.  We had walked by a few times but did not get to stop for a bite to eat until this past weekend.  We went on a Saturday around noon and were seated within 10 minutes after we arrived.  The restaurant is really large--very deep space with an upstairs mezzanine and a lounge area downstairs.  There is a cafeteria-style countertop that is really long and is good place to sit if you don't have a large party and don't want to wait.

Everyone at my table really loved their food.  There were six of us and we had a little bit of everything at our table - brisket sandwich, corned beef hash and eggs, fried chicken, eggs with sides, salad, collard greens, corn pudding...oh my!  Everyone really enjoyed the food.  

The service was mixed.  Our server had no personality--I don't think she spoke.  But the woman who delivered our food made up for our server's lack of personality.  She was hilarious!  If she was a server, she would clean up in tips every day.

The food was great.  The prices were very reasonable.  I will definitely be back.

Bring lots of cash if you plan on a long drinking stay. Drinks are extremely expensive.  Alcohol drinks are a minimum of $9 a drink.  That is for non call booze. No food just liquor. It is truly a tourist trap bar with. name recognition. 
Have a drink and move on to the next tourist trap. All prices have really increased since my last visit. 
Only 2 stars because of pricing of alcohol and lack of value. As I walked into the door I and other customers are instantly chased down to get a drink order. Appears they have been trained to make sure everyone buys one of there small expensive drinks. 
Buyer beware of this property.

Now you can't just walk into this place without taking a few minutes to learn its history. This place has seen everyone from Pastry Cline to Waylon Jennings to Willie Nelson (who got signed after playing there). Being open almost 60 years will do that for you. It's named after the owner and it still has her friendly charm. When we stepped off the downtown sidewalk into this place there was a crowd of people with a beer in one hand and giving us a high five with the other. I knew this was a place to have fun. The first floor is a little tight on space, but you learn to make it work. The second floor was just as rowdy and fun. On the rooftop, you get half covered and half open air space. Your view is of all the neon lighting up Broadway. A full bar is ready and serving the first two floors and bottled drinks are offered on the rooftop. There are pictures of anyone who is someone in county music on those walls. And it feels like your neighborhood bar, where you could hang out all night singing and drinking. It is a Nashville must.

*Insider's Tip
-Take the time to hang out on both floors and the rooftop. They will all have a different band playing.
The worst. Save yourself and go to Kid Rock. Tootsies music stinks and the place smells like piss

Really probably about a 3.5. We were here for the bluegrass brunch. Was initially quoted a wait of an hour, but got seated in about 10 minutes. 

Pluses: Bloody Mary bar was $12 for making your own bloody mary with as many ingredients as you want. Waitress was quite friendly.

Minuses: Food wasn't that super (basic breakfast was OK; eggs were fine, but biscuits were undercooked a bit); Breakfast tacos were solid though.

Overall, go for the drinks and bluegrass more than for the breakfast. This was a worthwhile experience though, I suppose.
I love the Sutler.  Best late night food! Good music. Fun pool lounge downstairs.   Mac n cheese is yummy

You guys, this is a Nash must!! If you don't get reservation tickets ahead of time get there at least 2 hours before the show starts. To stand in line for the first come seating. We got there right at 5, for a 6:30 show and by the time we got closer to the door, there was only 1 seat left in the whole place. My hubby wouldn't let me not go in so I went in solo. They let him come in and out and stand at the door to watch a few songs, which was nice. It was definitely a cool experience and the baked Brie was super yummy!

Shout out to TomKats for keeping the historic flair of this cool building. Love the vintage terrazzo!! While most new places in town are trying to be more sleek and modern than the last, this space makes no excuses for keeping it old school. The historical Significance related to the Civil Rights Movement in the South is felt as you look at the lunch counter where black residents staged a sit in to make their case for equality. 
Aside from that.. if you just want to have a really good southern meal, this place is great for that too!
Park at the 505 building across from
Puckett's or park at the city library if you are arriving before 5. Valet after 5.

F minus.  Where do you start?  They have taken what used to be an authentic honky tonk that played traditional country music and turned it into a cheesy nightclub playing hick-hop. They are complete sellouts.  I remember thinking when they started charging to sit in the booth by the window downstairs that things were going to go down hill.  I would complain about the beers here costing either $7 or $6, but that seems to be the going rate at most of the places.  The cheapest beer downtown is at Robert's.  Robert's has not veered from its original mission of playing traditional country music.  It's the only place worth going to on Broadway now.  I think Tootsie's got jealous of all the young people pouring into the Stage a few doors down, so they changed.  It is truly sad.  BTW, if the line is long up front, go around back and enter from the alley.

Lower Broad doesn't always seem the most local-friendly of Nashville locations what with the endless woo-hooing of bachelorette parties and boot stores but, as things grow, Broadway becomes a place locals will flock to even when not hosting out-of-towners. The draw for some may be the views. The draw for some may be the music. At Paradise Park, you'll wander in because you're drunk and in need of delicious, greasy food that will right your ship. Lucky for you, there are some additional benefits to take in.

But, first and foremost, get some food and sober up, willya? After winning a challenge to drink all the booze, I didn't think it was a good idea to get in to the first Uber I called. I'd like to be able to keep using the service. So, being in the area, I used my handy dandy app to figure out where to get a greasy grub on. Paradise Park, it was. One of the first things I noticed was that the venue is a lot larger than it seems from the outside -- and there's a lot going on. They've gone all in to/for the trailer motif and it works. It's self-referential. It's funny. And, it's local. In Boston, I'd want to torch a place like this. Here, I shrug, admit to some truths and keep it moving. I stumbled to the counter and started talking to the young lady who was posted up there. This wasn't her first time at the rodeo and I'm sure I wasn't her first drunk of the night. Despite all this, she treated me with nothing but kindness and patience; I don't know that I could have done the same in her shoes. She walked me through the menu (there's more to choose from than you might think) and I settled on what had to be done: bacon cheeseburger (no mayo) and cheese tots. Cheese.Tots. Done.

As I waited, I a.) washed my hands in the men's room (very clean; this is a major plus) and b.) got to listen to the band that was rocking out. Un-ironically (I think) they were having a go at an '80s hair band thing and, screaming aside, I was impressed with their musicianship. There's so much talent in this city. It's a shame what you hear on the radio. There's business and there's talent and the two don't always meet up.
