No longer did I ponder the inequities of the entertainment biz because my bounty was ready. I settled up, smiled & thanked my counter-lady and went on my way. One Uber ride later and I was ready to dig in.

Oh.Yes.

I don't eat bacon cheeseburgers all the time (not that you can tell) but when I do, I want them like this: juicy patty, gobs of melty cheese, crisp (not chewy) bacon, lettuce, onion, tomato, pickle, ketchup, and mustard. As the perfect accompaniment to my burger, my cheese tots were just what the doctor ordered* to keep me belly-licious and sate my drAnkin' needs. PP is what it is and if you treat it accordingly, it will treat you right back. I have no doubts that this dalliance will happen again.

*No doctor would ever order these.

This is a Landmark in Nashville.  

A lot of country music stars have preformed here over the years.    And you never know who will drop in unexpectedly 


The rooftop area is awesome and a place to hang out.   You would be disappointed!    We will be back for sure

Went here on a Friday night.  It was a really great vibe!  The performers were top notch and the drinks were pretty good.  The acoustics are fantastics and the band honored requests (for a small, reasonable donation).  The only thing I'd criticize is that the stage is by the door and that makes the entrance to the place get extra crowded as people are coming in and out, but also standing around to listen to the band.  So other than the narrow cramping, it really is a fantastic place for music.

Who wouldn't love Tootsie's? It's one of (if not the) oldest bars on Broadway in Nashville and a must-visit place! It's not an upscale place, food is bar food and servers don't seem overly happy to help, but I that's part of it's charm. The music is completely amazing, and the next group is always better than the last (or you think they are because you've been day drinking since 10am). Make sure you have cash for the bands--they aren't paid by the bars to play, they make all their money from tips. A few will take Venmo, but most only take good ole cash. The tables and chairs all wobble and there's not always a place to sit (always packed on every level--especially on weekends). The later it gets into the night, the better the people watching gets, but once the large groups of bachlorette parties start coming in, look out. For reasons unknown, they can't seem to hold their liquor and it turns into a bit of a shit-show--but again, if you know what you're getting into, sit back, watch, giggle and have another drink and enjoy the amazing music. Try to catch one of the groups with a fiddler--they are truly fun to watch and have so much talent! Will visit here every time we're in town!!

Lunch Box, the Paradise Park manager on duty, was more than helpful when I was asking about the ingredients in their chili (I have a food allergy and thought the chili would be safe for me to eat). Lunch Box then informed me of the ingredients and how the rest of their food was made- he was awesome, incredibly helpful, and very informative; he was more than willing to accommodate my food allergy and make sure what I was eating was safe for me to eat. I could not recommend this place more. Yummy food and awesome service. Letty, one of the kitchen staff, also went above and beyond to help me out and find a manager for me to talk to. Without her great attitude and willingness to help,  I could have easily wound up sick. Thankfully the staff at Paradise Park is incredible.

We came here for brunch on a Saturday. What a waste of a meal. We were on vacation in Nashville and you only get so many meals while on vacation, I definitely do not recommend wasting one of them on this place.

Wait was an hour, which can be expected for getting brunch at noon. 

We ordered the Strawberry Sangria which tasted like syrup. We both took 1 sip of it and could not drink any more.

I ordered the chicken and biscuits. The gravy had little flavor to it. Just very bland. My friend got the egg sandwich and she said it was alright but really not anything to brag about.

Waitress was very sweet and took the sangria off of our bill since we hated it.

The atmosphere was cool, good Bachelorette party watching, and the live bluegrass music over brunch was fun. We had high hopes when we walked in because of the atmosphere, but sadly the food and drinks were so bad that I would never recommend.

The best part though? We went to Walgreens while we waited and remembered the South has BLUE BELL ice cream, omg, so we came back to Walgreens afterwards to pick up a couple pints. 2 stars for being close to Blue Bell.

I ordered the fried chicken with pickled vegs, mashed potatoes and mac and cheese. It tasted like salt or seasoning was nowhere the kitchen. I expected more flavor for a $18 chicken plate. My friend ordered the roasted chicken with white beans and fennel. Meh. My cocktail was weak as well. I ended up ordering a beer a few hours later (in the ballroom) and felt that more than I did the rum drink.

The rating is a 3 and not a 2 because the service and atmosphere was nice. They had clips of old school music and dancing playing on the wall (Jackson 5, Otis Redding, etc). The Motown dance party that took place in the downstairs ballroom was FREE; the band was great. 

I will return for the music shows only. I'll make sure to eat and drink before I go.

The bartender threw out my full beer while I was using the restroom. I get keeping things clean but if you cover your beer that means I'm coming back for it. Plus the bathroom had roaches. Dont fall for the tourist trap much better places on Broadway to visit than them.
Always a good time here. The music is always on point and the bartenders make the atmosphere fun.

You know what I really love? History. I love learning about what went down, where and with whom, and when I actually get to experience a part of it? Yeahhhh buddy. Bluebird Cafe opened in 1982, and since it's inception has been a source for songwriters to find exposure and fame. 

I'm a New Englander, now New Jerseyan. Although I can get down on some bluegrass or Americana style country (read Dolly Parton, Johnny Cash, Willie Nelson), I haven't ever really gotten down on country. And guess what? Bluebird Cafe isn't country. It's countryish, but it's more. It's rock, it's folk, it's acoustic, it's country, it's a lonely man pouring his heart out on a keyboard. It's magical!

The Sunday night singer songwriter night was such an amazing experience, this review can't properly convey how much I enjoyed my time. You sit quietly as you laugh at the MC's hilarity and listen to some of the most talented people (did you know Taylor Swift was discovered on a Sunday night session at Bluebird Cafe?). 

This is where the real people (the people behind the people), who make music try out there stuff and have an opportunity to share. See, Taylor Swift, Tricia Yearwood, Mariah Carey, you name it - they all don't sing only the songs they write, they often sing songs that were created by others. Sunday night at the Bluebird Cafe is the others.

Intimate, small, dark. It's a very cool experience if you love live music. Or, if you happen to be a fan of that new show Nashville, I guess the Bluebird Cafe is a reoccurring venue and you definitely see some hardcore fans.

Read up on how to get tickets for any day of the week. For Sunday, you do have to wait in line, as reservations are nil.* Depending on the day, I hear sometimes you should probably get there hours before**. However you get 3 hours + of free live music and it's all good. 

They do ask that you spend at least $7 per seat and although the food is mostly bar food, grab a few beers and enjoy. Don't order the chocolate cake, or if you do, I warned you unless you like flavorless, stale cake.

A wonderful experience for those who appreciate music and those who make it. It will be hard to top this wonderful experience. 

* I have some friends in high places who work in the biz and we were able to bypass that line.
** Sunday night at the Bluebird Cafe is the most coveted time slot. I highly suggest attending this.

We were in Tootsie's on a Friday at 3 p.m. in the place was packed. Jam-packed. I mean call the fire marshal there was 6 lb of crap in a 3lb bag packed. However that didn't stop us from getting some beers and listening to some good country music.

For six beers it ended up being $42. I don't mind paying a little extra but $7 a beer for Bud Light? That's how you know you're on the strip I guess. Be way it works and most of these Honky Tonks is they will play pretty much any song you want one if they know it too if you're a hot looking cowgirl in 3 if you have 20 bucks

We were enjoying ourselves and having a pretty darn good time when all of a sudden Here Comes a bartender who is about 5 foot nothing and came out and yelled at all of us were standing in front of the stage. It's not like we had any place to go we really couldn't move the only way for us to go without she was trying to push us back into the bar and there was simply no place for us to go. She went and got mr. Bouncer man who also came in and try to get us to move back and once we showed him there was simply nowhere to move he kind of shrugged his shoulders went back outside and took care of moving the Beggars out from front of the store. After the song we were listening to is over we decided to leave. We found it there is a couple more cost-effective Honky Tonks Off the Strip.

The Sutler is our place to tag up with friends around Berry Hill/8th Ave. There are some big booths and lots of big tables so it's easy to have a large crowd meet there and hang out. It's kind of a fun/wide open place that's interesting from the time you walk in. The decor is worth taking in- creative, fun and makes you look twice. It's a comfortable place that just feels familiar.
The food is really great at The Sutler. Most typical bar foods are available and service is usually great. It can be loud, but the staff is used to handling it. There are two levels, with the downstairs offering a slightly different feel, pool and other diversions. It can be more relaxing when things get too jammed upstairs. 
I love the boot sculptures and other little touches here. It's a fun place and a good hang. And there's parking!! Go, enjoy live music and great food! On a nice night, the walls are rolled open and it gets even cooler.
PLEASE COME BACK.! We miss you.! I need some late Mac n cheese and chicken strips and tots and a great mullet wall.

If you are going to the bluebird for the menu then you have completely missed the point. Not that it is bad, but you go for the music and the vibe. It feels like an absolute Nashvilles staple, with a writers-in-the-round set up, reasonably priced drinks, and a fine food menu. It is great for couples or small groups, or if you just love music.

Another Tin Roof! This is by far the most unique Tin Roof I've been to. It's in a great neighborhood, not too far or close to the Broadway bars. It's got two sides with very different vibes to them and I think it really helps draw different crowds in! Decor is on par with the Tin Roof theme and food is good and drinks are cheap! It's always packed here!

let's get real - who could give the bluebird less than 5 stars? LOL. anyways, it's just as they say it is. small, intimate, and dreamy! nothing better. the food isn't great, but no one goes for the food. the music is what is REALLLYYYY good.

Love at first sight......This is my kind of place!!  My friend and I rang in the New Year here with some new friends.  I loved the atmosphere and unique decor.  Being NYE it was obviously busy but the service was still top notch!!  I defiantly will be back to enjoy some PBR tallboys next time I'm in town.
Really enjoyed the food and ambiance of this historical place. Staff is very nice and courteous (the hostess is the bomb).

We loved this place! We came here for my daughter's birthday for brunch and just had a fabulous time! The music was great, food was excellent, and the whole ambiance was wonderful! I can't recommend this place any more! Rachel, our waitress, was the cherry on top! She truly made us have the best time! Thank you!

The Brisket Tacos are excellent for Taco Tuesday ! The service was fast! And my bartender Morgan was friendly  and down to earth! The delicious food and Morgan's friendly smile and attentiveness to her customers makes the Sutler a number one stop for lunch!

My review is based solely upon standing in line and not actually entering the Bluebird. We came on a Sunday at 5 pm when they are due to open according to their business hours, and the line was 20 people deep. Our fault: we didn't realize you need to make a reservation to stand a chance of getting in. Neither did everyone else in line. There is no one from the Bluebird corralling people or providing any kind of direction, so after standing in line for 45 minutes in the blazing sun with zero movement in the line (literally, no one went inside that didn't have a reservation) we decided to leave. I would highly recommend making a reservation to avoid this situation. The staff could also make some improvements by coming outside and educating people on what to expect with the line.

Really enjoyed our brunch here. They band was great and despite sitting directly next to the stage we could still hear each other. The food didn't blow us away but we were all happy enough with our orders. I'd come back for the music and mimosas!

Pretty disappointed to write this review as I really enjoy the bar and it's live entertainment. We have been several times with great service in the past. But last night an incident happened with the employees that clearly is no mistake.  As I purchased my beers, on the 2nd floor from one of the beer buckets, I handed over $100 bill, she commented "$100" and looked at it in the light to check if it was fake (you know. The usual). Than proceeded to get me change and the two beers I ordered. Got to my table to realize I was shorted on my change. I walked up to let her know, and within 5 seconds 4 security guards where booting me out the back door. 
    I'd love to believe that it was an accident on her part, but after talking to another patron that this happed to, and the way I was quickly forced out of the bar, I'm thinking this is a scheme they pull off on drunks all night long.

Made the trip to Nashville to attend an "in the round"  show at the Bluebird Cafe: John Cowan, Bill Lloyd, Pat Simmons Jr., Jonell Mosser and Tom Brit.  At $15 per person, plus a two-drink minimum, this has to be one of the best entertainment values I've seen in recent years.

Tiny storefront in a little strip shopping center - definitely nothing special from the outside.  Next door is a hair salon, I seem to recall.  

Food and drink options are average bar fare (but service was brisk and professional).  We looked over the menu online before we went, and decided to have a nice dinner elsewhere before the show.

But this isn't about the menu:  it is all about seeing a show in a very intimate, iconic venue.  Some seats are so close you could reach out and touch the performers (but don't - that's kind of creepy).

This is definitely a "plan ahead" place.  Most shows sell out in minutes, since venue is small, I'd guess it seats maybe 50-60 people?  You purchase tickets online, and generally need to be ready to make a reservation the minute tickets go on sale.  And you only have a minute or so to complete the transaction, so have your credit card out, and print out the searing chart and be ready with a list of your preferred seats.

You -can- show up the day of the show - they set aside a very small number of seats to sell at the door, and there is the occasional no-show for a reservation, but the night I went there was a line for last minute seats, and I don't know if everyone got in.

One of a kind place.  I can't wait to go back.

Ticketing process is a joke. Don't waste your time.

Its pretends to be democratic but is presumably rigged for friends because their technology makes it impossible to actually reserve a ticket.

You get up early, you wait in a virtual line, your turn comes up, and then the site breaks...EVERY time.

Lot of great music in Nashville so don't start your trip getting frustrated with this disaster of a process.

On vacation in Nashville and Tootsie's came highly suggested. My group & I decided to check out Tootsie's on a Saturday from approximately 11-5/6. We had a table on the rooftop. The view was perfect. The heaters by the door helped us to remain comfortable and it was November 9th. Drinks were great & ice cold (just how we like it). The food was wonderful; we enjoyed the sampler, nachos, and a pulled pork sandwich. The service was a bit slow as the bar was packed so this was understandable. If we wanted our drinks faster all we had to do was go to the bar which was completely fine. The only dilemma was the traffic to the bathroom. Its location was not ideal and caused traffic to back up on the stairs. Overall a great enjoyable experience for all.

Slow service over priced food. Good service = Good tip. Crap service and the bar tender had a crappy attitude and playing on your phone half the time does not warrant a good tip. 10/10 would not go again. Stay away.

Wow! If you are a native to Nashville you are truly lucky to be in a location so rich with talent and music. If you are not from nashville and looking for a great time or place to plan a trip around i strongly suggest nashville. Tootsies is a staple of the night scene and has been there for years. Many of artists have gone and performed but the atmosphere is so great. They have four floors of live music each better than the other is how i felt. The night was full of good people and staff to make the night fun and enjoyable.  With four floors there is no issue with space and the drinks are reasonably priced. The experience is one you have to jave and if you have some cash request your favorite song and get out on that dance floor. It is a full bar and they can make you almost anything (of course it has to be something real). There is no cover and the night life ends a little after 2am. Must travel place.

WILL NEVER GO BACK! went at night for a few drinks and both women bathrooms were apparently closed. The bouncer told us to pee in the ally way behind the bar and when we said absolutely not he called the cops and grabbed me by the arm to the point where I now have bruises on my arm.

This is perhaps the worst tourist traps out there.  Dirty, crowded, overpriced drinks in plastic cups, and the most rude and biased staff.  The music was ok and mostly cover bands begging for money.  The bar was dirty and not sure what kind of disease you would get if go to the bathroom. It's sad that they are listed as a place to visit in Nashville. This place brings Nashville down a notch or two.

If you have never been to Nashville, you have to come here just to say you did. I like it best during the day, it tends to still get pretty crowded. You don't come here for the cleanliness, that is for sure. We were able to snag a bar stool at the top floor bar, right near the stage which was great. Bar staff was very attentive and friendly however the prices are a but ridiculous. $10 bucks for a SMALL vodka soda and $6 for Miller Lites. But I guess they know what they are doing! Music was great as usual and all around a decent time.

This is a must visit for those visiting Nashville, as well as those who live here and remember the lunch counter sit ins during the 60's. The restaurant is very clean, and the staff are friendly and on point. 

Breakfast and lunch can be ordered until 3pm, but today I opted for the Southern Caesar Salad. I ordered it because I had never heard of this type, and had to see it for myself. The salad is a classic Caesar, with the addition of country ham, fried okra, and molasses drizzle. Sounds strange I know, but it was a great combination of sweet and salty to compliment the Caesar dressing. The portions seemed to be above average for everything that I saw at tables around me. 

This place is good, but a little overpriced for lunch. I plan to go back and try out the breakfast.
Great place to eat!  The historical value is wonderful and the food delicious!  Good service staff and knowledgeable about thee menu  Highly recommend Woolworth on 5th if you're in Nashville!

Definitely a unique place at a central downtown location. Prices are reasonable for food portions. Skip the tea as it has a very unique burnt taste. Prompt service, waiter needs not be so serious all the time, it makes you feel like you are a hassle for them. I hear the fried chicken is the best thing on the menu. None of us ordered that. The turkey sandwich was amazing. Patty melt not so much. I would not order that again.
Definitely a unique place with a lot of character and history. If not for the location and the music scene, we would have never considered visiting it.

The bouncers literally shut down the hallway twice because they couldn't properly escort a drunk guy out, overcrowded and nothing special from what I saw. Three or four floors of shoulder to shoulder sweaty southerners, no thanks.

Literally the worst service ever! Everyone is so friendly in Nash & working as a bartender, I would never treat my customers as an annoyance. Bartenders are too busy looking at their phones & computers to give you the time of day. The worst place I have been out here. Seriously disappointed!

I've tagged along for a few nights out on Broadway during my trips to Nashville and a stop at Tootsie's comes through every time.

The place has 3 levels of live music and a couple of bars to grab drinks. Yes, it's busy, but the energy is great! The musicians are good and they play a lot of covers from country to old school classic rock. 

The house band on the second level is one of our faves and they rotate out a female singer for some of the songs - super entertaining. Be sure to tip! They're working hard to give you a good time so give them some love back.

The bar staff is great - speedy! They're always keeping an eye out so they can get folks a drink despite the crowds.

Definitely went just straight for the food so I have no idea on what to say about the bar (bar hopped elsewhere). Five alarm burger is pretty good but reminds me a bit like I'm eating buffalo wings in a burger rather than hitting that heat wave. 

THING TO NOTE: For people with allergies like mine you're going to be the awkward step child. Asked them if their tots or sweet potato fries were made with peanut oil since they're pretty visual on telling you their fresh cut fries are...They are. So if you've got a peanut allergy... just hope you only wanted their burgers + dogs.

It was great to visit this piece of Nashville's civil rights history. I enjoyed the photos of the famous sit-ins. However, I was very disappointed by both the food and service. We arrived at 5:00 so they were it crowded. We ordered the fried green tomatoes appetizer, and when it arrived they served it with no plates. It was good, but not hot. I ordered the sirloin. It arrived cold and undercooked. My husband ordered the jambalaya, which was also room temperature. The food was foodervice quality. Service as inattentive and lackadaisical. I had to grab the waiter every time I needed something- he was not pro-active at all. We will not return.

Tin Roof Demonbruen is easily one of my favorite stops when I'm going out! It's been around forever and arguably has the most inexpensive drinks on the West side. Live music almost every night of the week! It's nice that they have three bars fully staffed, so you're not waiting too long to get a drink. Chill atmosphere, lively band and cheap drafts -- what more do you need?
The food and service upstairs is great. The 1 star is for the bartender downstairs. I've been twice and both times this bartender has been rude and inattentive. Bad service.

I give it 5 stars. It's pretty rare to have speedy service and amazing food the first week a restaurant opens, but the Sutler did it!  
Upstairs- The menu is perfect. The chef put his own spin on some classic dishes, so it's familiar, but like nothing you've ever had.  My husband and I had wine and beer with our meal, and we were very pleased with the selection.  
I would recommend the fried pickles, popcorn, grilled cheese dunk, horse shoe brisket, and the brownies... But I honestly doubt anything on the menu is bad. 
FYI- I think the price-to-portion ratio is spot on.

Downstairs- I love the atmosphere and the way they arranged the seating. It's the perfect place to go and have a relaxing drink with a small group of friends. The cocktails are creative but not too "crafty". Everything we had was delicious. My only wish is that they would serve dessert downstairs.

I am only giving two stars because it is a cool looking place... Even though it was very hard to find parking there were only a few people in there. We had the idea to try the sutler after going to two other places that were too long wait because they were packed... We were excited to go there and looking forward to trying it out... we got in immediately were seated and waited about 10 minutes and no one came to our table... My wife got up and asked the bartender if we could order appetizer and two drinks while we waited but they told us we had to order from a waiter... We waited 10 more minutes... No waiter. We were hungry so we decided to leave and go across the street to a restaurant... It was packed but they found us a table and we had a good dinner. I was disappointed I really wanted to like that place... I think they need to step it up if they're going to make it with all the great places popping up...it's too easy to go somewhere else where you know that they are glad to have your business and want you to be pleased. A night out to dinner like that is too expensive not to have a good experience...
You served us lukewarm beer. You knew it wasn't cold when you grabbed the bottles. I think this place is overrated.

We came here for brunch because a guest at Hattie B's raved about how it's a must for brunch. I had never been before and have been meaning to try it because it's just down the street from my house. The place is really cool.. but we sat outside because the boyfriend and I don't like anything cooler than 76 degrees. What's brunch without booze? It's not one I'd want to participate in... so we ordered some Bloody Marys. It's not the worst and definitely the best I've had. I had the breakfast platter: two fried eggs, bacon, potatoes and a biscuit. Maybe I had high expectations and possibly ordered the wrong thing but this was mediocre at best. The potatoes were just cut up in small pieces and then fried...where's the seasoning? Oh... just the ketchup/salt or tabasco from the table. Eggs were just a regular fried egg - no seasoning on it either. The local bacon was crispy and the star of the plate. 

Verdict: meh, I wouldn't go back for brunch....
Had the quarter fried chicken. The Mac n cheese was delicious! Love the vibe. It was definitely an experience

No sitting room for anyone dining in because everyone with one drink takes up the available booth seating. Literally had to eat my food on the floor. How hard is it to put "reserved for dining customers only" signs on the tables. On the other hand, seems about right considering how short sighted the downtown sporting club concept is. Just really shouldn't be that difficult to see people sitting on the floor with food and fix the issue.

happily checked off my bucket list. I made it! I couldn't get a reservation a week before (forgot to get online until the afternoon...) so I got there around 5 and stood in line.  there were already about 20 people in front of me though, but I was one of the last few people that made it in!

you don't pay to get in, you just need to spend $10 a person on food/drink. the wines were great, and may I strongly suggest the baked brie?  it may be one of the best ones I've ever had.  

musicians were GREAT.  I did not know any one of them, but they were all awesome - funny when they chatted, genuine when they played, and the songs were so good that they brought me to tears a couple of times.  

anyone, that's into the music, has to go visit if you ever visit Nashville!  thank you bluebird - thank you Nashville ABC!

I've wanted to visit the Bluebird for about eight to ten years now, since I was in college to earn my music management degree. The Bluebird is in a nondescript strip mall next door to a dry cleaner; you could easily drive by without realizing it. It's a tiny place, but it was a great show. I know now they take reservations online; I was there the week before this was rolled out. Hopefully that will be a benefit to people. I visited with a coworker when we were in town for a conference. We stopped in on Tuesday night and got there about an hour before the early show began, so we may have gotten lucky just because of the day of the week. We didn't have reservations or anything but were able to sit in the pews, and since we were at the end of the line got a spot in the first pew.

There were others there who had reservations, but I couldn't find how to do that for this show--it said that they didn't take them. Luckily, it was fine. We were there for an In The Round session, so we heard from the four artists in the round plus a bonus song from a collaborator of one of those artists. The night I was there those in the round were Vee Lasher, Madison Marie Armour, Paul Sikes, and Tony Zavitson. Vee's song plugger was in the audience too (who, judging by surname, is mother or other relative of one of the artists), so you know industry people stop in too. The show lasted an hour and a half or so, I think; long enough for each of the artists to do 4-5 songs each. It was well worth it: The music was great, the show was intimate, and everyone had a good time. I think some people might turn their nose down at the early show, thinking that it's going to be subpar; keep thinking that if you want. It'll make it easier for the rest of us to get in.

I don't know about any of the tables, but the sight lines from the pews were perfect. Use the restroom before going, if you can; there are two single-use bathrooms here, one for each gender. There's a $7 minimum per person but that's an amazing deal to hear such high quality music. If you're sitting in the pews, be careful what you order since there's nowhere but your lap or hand to put your food.

My wife and I attended the 2018 Kid Rock Fish Fry and let me first say that we attend many Kid Rock events and know what to expect.  The event itself was good, we had VIP access so it was nice to have the separate area to hang out, separate bar and a/c restrooms.   Prior to the event, I read some of the reviews and became concerned about the venue but tried to stay open minded, thinking maybe this was just folks that weren't used to the crowd and just had a bad time.  I was wrong, very wrong...this is an absolutely horrible venue....

As I mentioned, we paid extra for front row, VIP tickets, thinking that we would have a great view.  Luckily, we had seats 15/16 which was as far to the left as you can go without just looking at speakers and amps, I felt bad for the folks further left because they could barely see the stage.  That aside, the absolutely worse part, which was totally unacceptable was that the event staff allowed people to use the front row as a walk way!!!  During the concert!!  I did speak to a couple of the attendants and they blamed it on the way the seats were set up....not my problem!  They did make some effort to stop it but overall it ruined our experience.

It appeared the grass seats were not much better, unless you get there really early and camp out all day, there are few areas where you're actually going to see the stage.

I thought the entertainment was great so my boyfriend and I went for our last night in Nashville as we thought it would top off the trip, instead I had the most frightening and aggressive bouncer physically grab my boyfriend and I for trying to finish my drink on the side before heading out onto the streets (no open container law). I have never been more terrified by a man in my life as my boyfriend and I are both very passive and understanding people.. i've never experienced something so terrible in my life.

good luck trying to get tickets. the website is way below par, and pretty much blocks you from even having a chance. The Bluebird needs a massive site upgrade, to support thier fan base. disappointed for sure going to website to tickets and the door can not even handle the request.. I did get lucky and for past the select a seat page only to be rejected at the checkout page.. FAIL..  call your web/IT admin or get a new one..


Update 5.31.2018
So I FINALLY got tickets it took me a week of trying to get tickets but i got some. if you can get through the web process... going there and seeing an in the round live... unbelievable... 

would be 5 stars but getting tickets will possibly drive you crazy

Holler and swaller! This place is awesome every time. We went today with our luggage right from the airport. We thought that it would be too crowded, but the nice guy outside told us to come on in. We perched on the stairs and tucked our rolling suitcase on the top step. Perfect view of the entryway band. There were 5 people on the front window stage and one girl on the bar. There was a woman playing a violin that was fantastic! She was boss and killed it.

A great and truly unique addition to Nashville's many dining options. The food was excellent- my blackened salmon was maybe the best I've ever had. Our waiter provided excellent service and we loved the setting and appreciated its historical significance. Check out all three floors. It's fun to walk around. We'll be back.

Saw a Sunday writers round last week. The girl I sat next to was one of the performers. I noticed they force the performers to pay a minimum of $10. It was an okay show but I don't like that the performers have to pay to play even if it's only $10. Seems like the bluebird is more about money than quality performances.

Flew in from good ol Htown (that's Houston for you non Texans) and decided to stop for lunch, great vibes and atmosphere in a Friday afternoon. The Chili wasn't the Texas chili (our mistake, wasn't even thinking about it). Anyone know who the solo artist is here on Friday's?? Awesome upbeat chill acoustics. I wonder if he has a soundcloud....

If I was able to give 3.5 stars I would. 3 would not accurately portray since The Sutler isn't "average," and we'll likely return. 

First off, the venue was cool. The restaurant area was very stylish, but that "speak-easy" feel to the bar downstairs was awesome. 

The service was a letdown. Although our waitress was upbeat and helpful when she was at our table, unfortunately, she consistently let way too much time go between checking on empty drinks...from the time we sat down to the point we got up.  Another note on the service was the bartender downstairs. After dinner we grabbed a drink. I'm going to chalk up his recommendation off the drink menu as not hearing me correctly because the drink I received was not remotely what I stated I wanted. Great selection of craft beers which I ordered to help get the drink down. 

Food was very good. The four of us got something different (fish, burger, pulled chicken and pulled pork). All of us enjoyed it. I felt the pulled chicken portions were a little off. I received LOTS of fries (which they're very good) but not as much chicken as I would've liked. It was delicious and I would've paid more to have a larger portion. The burger was great and "fun" in the dunk. The pulled pork was also very good. It may have been an optical illusion, but it seemed like there was more pork on that plate than on the chicken plate. Lastly, the fish was raved about too. Order it without the head if you're the faint of heart as our person was. 

Overall, it was a good time, not great. I'm hoping it was an off night regarding service. It was definitely good enough to give it another try.
Overpriced, Overrated, Overlook it! 2 beers, a Miller High Life and an Angry Orchard was $14. Music was subpar. Do yourself a favor and head To Roberts next door.

Probably the worst place I've ever eaten.. There was mold on the bread on my egg sandwich... didn't bother telling the managers they were too busy or just not in sight. Really liked this place when it first opened but now it's just started to get ran down. Won't be returning

If you are a fan of the show, Nashville, Bluebird Cafe is a must visit!

Located in the outskirts of the main Nashville area in a small strip mall. Very tiny parking lot. The actual venue is really small as well. Inside also looks like it only seats a limited amount of people.

They open at night only so I did not get a chance to come see any live music during my visit. Seems like you need to plan ahead if you want to actually get inside.

Great music has come out of this tiny cafe, worth a visit!

Pretty much hands-down my favorite place in Nashville. Period.  And I don't even like country music.  I've been able to visit three times now (two were in the round and once was in the row).  I love the "in the round" option and how the songwriters sit literally "at the next table away" from you and just have a blast sharing songs, playing off of each other, harmonizing spontaneously, and telling stories.  A lot of times they play familiar songs and it's cool to hear the story behind the songs you've heard on the radio and to get to hear them performed by the songwriter him/herself!

It's very cozy inside and the food isn't spectacular...it's not terrible either.  But, you don't come here for the food anyway.  During the early shows, there's usually no cover and there's just a $7 food/drink minimum which is really nothing when you think about the amazing concert and experience you are getting while you munch on your food.

Reservations open up 8 am the week before so you want to make sure that you reserve early!  Seating is very limited so you have to plan in advance!  But, it is seriously an unforgettable experience and most definitely worth it.  A Nashville must see.  I love this place and I miss it so much now!

Thank you ABC for bringing this gem to the main screen! Yes, I am a fan of the show Nashville and yes I knew this had to be on my lists of stops. 
Unfortunately I was not able to secure tickets to a show but I was able to get on a Nashville TV Show inspired tour which took us to The Bluebird prior to it's opening one night. It was amazing walking in, I felt like I was on the show. They did an amazing job in replication. 
Hearing the history from the owners was such a treat, the place has started the careers of so many, the concept is amazing! 
I hope to come back into town and get to see a show but even walking in and seeing it was a great experience!

Absolute best part of the trip! Luckily I planned ahead and was able to get tickets ahead of time. Picked table 23...which I highly recommend bc it is out of the way and sits up a little higher so you can a good view of performers. The songwriters (Gary Harrison, Carson Chamberlain, Michael White and Rick Huckaby) were excellent and a very talented group of songwriters. I would pay to see them again for sure. The bartender was very friendly and quick to make our drinks. The food was delivered quickly and was delicious. I definitely will visit again in the near future.

A must if you go to Nashville.  We enjoyed a night "in the round," where four singer-songwriters​​ took turns playing their songs for us.   A very nice server brought us drinks and nachos while we listened.  Service was amazing.  The experience​​ was even better.  Get tickets a week ahead online.

I think it's a little strange and unfair that they don't do ticket sales for Monday evenings when they do for pretty much every other day of the week. I knew I wanted to make it here when I booked my first Nashville trip, and we even planned to go on a Monday night knowing that a weekend night would be pretty much impossible to get in. I had read online how the first Monday show is open mic and thought that'd be more interesting than the later show, which was a local band we wouldn't have known. We like a mix of music so hearing several
Musicians would've been right up our alley. We planned to get there by 4:30 after reading the reviews about how the line starts early. A huge thunderstorm rolled in right around 4 and it made driving through downtown a mess. We ended up getting there around 5 and the line was already almost down to the end of the plaza. Shortly after getting in line, one of the workers came out and told us where the cutoff point was and that we weren't making it. We got out of line because we weren't going to wait around until 9 for the next show--like most tourists, we had a few other things we were hoping to do before we left town since this didn't work out. 

I know that half of the appeal of the Bluebird is that it's small and has remained traditional and unchanged over the years, but it kind of stinks for people who only have so much time to spend in Nashville and then find a way out to the Bluebird, since it's not near downtown, just to be turned away. Again, we would've bought tickets ahead of time to guarantee our entry if we could have. I feel like they should know the place will be drawing a crowd regardless of the day of the week, so it wouldn't hurt to add on presales to all days so that people don't have to get turned away. I'd try again on a future visit, but I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a tad bummed this time around.

This will be a short post. Buy tickets in advance- that's a must! Go to the website and it will tell you when they go on sale for the show you want to see. 
Other than that tip- there is nothing like this place. You have to experience it to understand- there are no words to explain it.

Only giving one star cuz I have to. My friend tried to sit down and she was pushed off by a lady standing. We got kicked out when we had just gotten there and we were all  sober and had done literally nothing but try and sit. . It was clearly racial Discrimination and the employees decided to kick out the only Indian people at the place when the lady was trying to take my friends places. We left and continued our night but these people are clearly racist.

Cute hangout close to the gulch area of Nashville. I went during the day for a quick drink so it wasn't insanely busy. It just happened to be right across the street from my hotel. I did see it get packed at night however. The drinks are pretty cheap and so is the food if you're looking for a snack. We happened to be there during happy hour and they had $4 well drinks and $3 drafts which is awesome! They also had a $5 chicken quesadilla. 

It's in a good location next to a line of other similar bars and hangout spots. This location is less busy and more low key than the location on Broadway I would say.

Not your mothers Woolworth cafe.  Expensive with mediocre taste.  I had Mac and Cheese.  A side order sized portion was $13.  Lots of cheese but no flavor.  My wife's turkey was a very salty turkey roll.  The waitress tried to tell us it was Southern flavor.  Doubt it seriously.  There is a reason why other places have waits and this place has empty tables.

Listen, I heard this was the hardest place to get into, on Nashville! We were lucky enough to get in without a reservation. Cute place. Small, but man, it's The Bluebird Cafe! Bucket list checked!!! But, we were very very disappointed in the fact that after an hour, our food never came out. I only ordered a salad and my friend ordered a tender basket. 1 hour and still no food. The excuse was they ran out of Caesar dressing. I don't think that actually happened, not after an hour with out any food. The 4 other people at our table got their food within 15-20 after they ordered. I'm definitely not disappointed in the music because, hey, it's The Bluebird Cafe!!! But very disappointed that they couldn't get our food out. Or at least get my friends food out. We waited 2 hours outside to get in (5:45 time started) we got in at 8:00. We were definitely starving when we left at 10pm....

Saturday night 
Approximately 11:30 pm 
3-16-2019
I came to this place a couple years ago and had such a good time I remembered this place so decided to stop by again and check it out. This time my opinion is different. 
 Nasty, broken beer bottles all over the floor. Bathrooms trashed. Toilets overflowing in the floor. I'm Surprised the health Department still lets this place operate. And to top it off they charge a $10.00 cover to get in.
 TIN ROOF HAS TURNED INTO THE WORST AND MOST UNSAFE PLACE IVE EVER BEEN.
Disappointed in entertainment 10/19/19, lack of country vibe, and warmth we read about and expected. Staff and food was as expected.  Advice, double check entertainment before committing.

We were thirsty and trying to kill time before a show at the Ryman. 

Go to Tootsie's they said, hey Legend's looks ligit. Turns out my husband and I aren't really "bar" people. We walked in and right back out of both of those places. Too crowded, too loud, no southern charm.

Well Paradise Park is lacking in charm but it was definitely more peaceful than the other places because we actually got to sit at a good size table and have a drink. 

We decided to come back to grab a bite to eat after the Ryman. They now had the bar fenced off from the concession area which helped reduce the sound a little.

I ordered a corn dog and a New York dog. The hubs ordered the 5 alarm burger with cheese fries. 

Corn dog is hand dipped and very good, crispy crust that's not too thick. That's all I should of ordered because I was stuffed after eating it.

I tried a couple of bites of the New York dog. The bun was fresh but did not hold up to the steam and sour kraut. I didn't care too much for the weenie as it lacked any flavor. Good thing I wasn't all that hungry because I wasn't disappointed that I couldn't finish it.

Hubs really enjoyed his burger. The patty had a good crispy edge. He thought the cheese fries were really good too.

So, probably one of the least fancy places on Broadway but this is where we felt like we fit in the best.

Our first stop checking out the honky-tonk scene on Broadway was the "world famous" and historic Tootsie's Orchid Lounge. Honky-tonks are bars with live country music and Tootsie's is one of the most well-known of these. The business has been around for decades and is named after one of its former owners, Tootsie Bess (now deceased), and the color of the building - orchid. Tootsie bought the place in 1960.

Like several of the venues along Broadway and in Nashville in general, Tootsies has multiple levels with multiple bars and multiple stages plus a rooftop patio. We visited shortly after 11:30pm on a Friday night and the front of the house was jam-packed. Instead of entering through the front, we went through Tootsie's back entrance which is how many of the country music stars used to come after their shows at the Ryman Auditorium (former Grand Ole Opry House) next door. A cool neon sign out back calls it Tootsie's Alley.

It's a narrow little alley with just enough room for a vehicle to squeeze by. It was just our luck, during our visit, that a garbage truck was making its round to all the businesses behind Broadway, Tootsie's included. Therefore, it absolutely stunk. The heat and humidity at the time didn't help either.

We spent most of our time on the second level in the back. There was no stage back there so it was one of the least crowded parts of the building. All of the other rooms were pretty full. This part of Tootsie's had its own small bar with three TVs, two arcade games (golf and boxing), and a decent amount of seating (about 25 seats, maybe more). I would describe the space and decor as divey and kitschy. It's old, but it's got character. The air was smelly, the floors were sticky, and it was loud -- admittedly, not my scene, but lots of people (many of whom were tipsy or drunk) appeared to be having a good time. I had more fun at our next stop, the now-closed Paradise Park Trailer Resort across the street. It had a more comfortable and enjoyable environment.

A lot of celebrities have performed at Tootsie's. Garth Brooks popped in unannounced and sang on a fairly recent Thursday night (August 2, 2018). Kid Rock performed, along with others, to celebrate Tootsie's 58th anniversary on October 10, 2018. Both performances were free.

Tootsie's also has an offshoot at the Nashville airport as well as another multi-stage honky-tonk in Panama City Beach, Florida.

Mo is the best bartender/waitress I've ever had. I'm from Vegas and I've met many waitresses and bartenders where I'm from. She is so damn nice and puts her customers first. My bottomless mimosa glass was never empty! She is so kind and respectful. I would HIGHLY recommend sitting at the bar. She's the best! And the food was AMAZING!

This place seems popular and I'll give 2 stars because the menu made me want to come here for an early Friday HH.... BUUUT... I couldn't even manage to get a drink because our waiter was so darn rude to the rest of my group and when I sat down was told "hope you don't want separate checks because you all moved around and it really messed me up"... nobody had asked for separate checks in fact I was going to pay for everyone but we never got the chance... so instead we added about 5 more friends to our group and chose to relocate to Sinema to get better drinks and better service in the bar upstairs. 

*the rude waiter did apologize to my friends but I had already left because I don't take 'tude on Friday's... bish don't kill my weekend vibe!

One of those "famous" dive bar places to check off the list. Aka tourist trap.

Expensive beers. Check
General Filth. Check
Long lines at the bar. Check
Cover bands. Check

Walk in. Have an overpriced beer and say you have been there. Then find another less crowded bar in the tourist zone.

The legendary Bluebird Café Is located outside downtown Nashville in a very unassuming strip mall. Reservations are a must not available for the Saturday show until the previous Monday.  

Two lines form outside the café before the doors open;  those with tickets and those who are hoping there are seats still available. Someone from inside comes out and asks how many are in your party and allows only those folks in at time. 

It is highly recommended to have cash to pay your cover charge, this night it was $20; it helps with crowd control as the clerk inside seats you after payment, before the next party enters. 

Songwriter Don Schlitz performed his songs including The Gambler and When You Sat Nothing at All, and encouraged the audience to sing along throughout his performance all night.  Jellyroll Johnson, accomplished musician on the harmonica,  accompanied Don. 

If you're going to Nashville this place is a must see!

Food, beer and wine are available. The waitstaff does an amazing job keeping track of your orders; separate billing us an issue

You must go here and you must order the shrimp & grits.  It was so over-the-top delicious that both my husband and I declared it to be..........(drum roll)..............THE BEST THING WE'VE EVER EATEN.
I'm serious.  You have not lived until you have eaten their shrimp and grits!  

And while you're living large, order a boozy milkshake.  I had the peppermint one and it was fab.  And after that order a shot of bourbon because they have Pappy, Weller, you name it....fabulous collection of tippy top shelf bourbons.

We sat at the famous counter and service was perfect.  Will definitely be coming back here.

Awesome service, food and music! Went for a Saturday late brunch around 2pm. My favorite was the chicken and waffles. Hostess was honest about wait time and very friendly. We were able to start drinking the bottomless mimosas at the bar while waited to sit, which was neat. Also, they have this cool waiting list program that texts you a link and you can see what # you are on the list. Pretty neat!
Great atmosphere and cool venue for music, however the drink prices are high and the good is overly spicy without any warning

Visited Paradise Park after a two hour Pedal Tavern and bar hopping, so our group was really hungry and Paradise Park was exactly what we need to get rejuvenated for a night out on the town. 

- Food: A friend who went to school in Nashville recommended that we had to go here at least once and try their tater tots. I ended up getting the Cheese Tater Tots, Jalepeno Poppers and their Veggie Burger. 

The best part of the meal was the Jalepeno Poppers hands down, it was so tasty and perfectly cooked with the right balance of a spicy kick, oozing hot cheese and went great with the accompanying Chipotle sauce. The Cheese Taters were also really good and delicious! What really killed the meal for me was the Veggie Burger, although I know Paradise Park and Nashville in general isn't the best place to get vegetarian food, the burger ended up being really terrible. 

Either way, I'd recommend going here before/ after a night on the townand getting their sides which are fantastic from the two I've tried. 

- Service: The employees here really take the cake for the nicest staff in any food establishement I've visited. Everyone from their cashier, kitchen staff to the cleaning staff, they were just really friendly and caring. 

The one down part aside from the Veggie Burger was the wait to get my food, although most of my friends got their food pretty fast so it must have just been something in my order that had the long wait. 

- Atmosphere: This is a super casual place that I imagine most people go to after drinking. They also have an attached bar/ clubby area with live music next door, which seemed like a lot of fun with good music. 

Overall, Paradise Park did its job and we enjoyed our experience/ food there for the most part.

I loved the egg salad sandwich here for lunch. Two days later and I'm still thinking about it! Next time I'm there I'm definitely trying a boozy milkshake. Sad I missed out on trying one of those the first time!

Expectations dramatically crushed!! I've lived in Nashville now for 15 years and this place "Set the Bar" for the worst service ever!! Mixology and arrogance don't have to go together. Service at the upstairs bar was awful. We moved downstairs and the decor was great the service was worse. NO REDEEMING QUALITIES!!!!!! Zero

We love Tin Roof on Demonbreun! This is our go
to spot when we're looking for some quality live music and fun environment. We always make sure to bring friends here when they come into town.

Stopped for breakfast and did not have to wait over an hour like other local spots. To our surprise, got seated quickly and the food was really good. Service was great too. Friendly and personable. The atmosphere was neat too, great history. Would recommend!

Visited The Sutler on Saturday for Brunch. It was extremely, busy the wait was going to be 30 minutes. I asked the hostess if we could sit outside and she said sure there isn't a wait for outside. We had the pineapple orange Sangria, which was very refreshing. Elle was our server and she did a great job informing us on our food and the wait time for drinks as the bar was backed up. She politely brought us some water while we briefly waited. The food was served nicely and the Chicken Biscuits and gravy were over the top! This should be one of their signature dishes!  We will definitely be back!

I got the Dime Store Burger, which is basically a cheeseburger. I ordered it medium well, but it came medium rare. When we got a medium well burger it was charred and unseasoned. I also tried a bite of the fried chicken,, and it was also very dry and had little seasoning. It is not worth the expense, and I would not recommend it to anyone.

historic, cool, comfortable , classy.   Woolworth on 5th presents a wonderful dining experience.  immediately greeted at the door, you look around to see what they created.  either a table, booth or bar seating each authentically   relaxing.  a southern influenced menu. we enjoyed the outstanding oven roasted Brussels  Sprout starter.  now the challenge which wonderful item to order.  the fantastic Short Ribs were so delicate with the most amazing sauce.  the truly southern Fried Chicken was crisp, tender and awesome.  sides dishes of mac & cheese, collard greens, potatoes paired perfectly.  ended with Chocolate Pudding served via jar.   combined with an attentive waitstaff ,  such a pleasant meal !!!!!!!!!!!!!!

1. The place is a in a funny little strip mall outside of Nashville, across from a mall and suburban hell - as I like to call it. 

2.  I didn't eat here. I might have had dessert, I don't honestly remember. I had some beers, don't remember what the beer list looked like. Really, who *actually* comes here for the drinks and food?!?

3. Getting tickets/Getting In: You need to get online and get the tickets two weeks ahead of time at like 8am. I'm serious. We forgot and waited til 4pm and it was sold out. They do have a waitlist though, so call and get on it. We were told that there were often late cancels and no shows and there are pew seats that are first come first served. We were prepared to get there at like 730 for the 9:00 show, but around 2:00, they miraculously called me with two open seats at an awesome table ( I could have touched the one guy)! Once you get there, the line on the left of the door (when looking at it) is for people with tickets. The line on the right is for people without tickets. Do it right and get tickets, and you'll be happy you did.

4. Music: We came on a Sunday which is Artists in the Round. It was 4 older song writers who sat around in a circle and took turns playing songs they wrote. They were AMAZING. They told stories of getting their songs "cut". Some of the ones that I recognized were cut a bunch of times by different artists before actually getting recorded or on an album or something. Seriously, these guys were *LEGIT*. I recognized a bunch of them, and every. single. song. was AMAZING. These weren't up and coming song writers, they knew their country music. 

5. I officially love country music. This is my MUST DO/MUST SEE/MUST GO in Nashville. No ifs, ands, or buts.

I waited one week and then got on your website to buy show tickets 2 hours before the sale started. I then waited in a ten minute line and was redirected to the page to buy tickets. Then it says SOLD OUT. This is ridiculous. I couldn't have done anything differently. Every show was immediately sold out and now I can't go. What a waste of time.

In regard to the atmosphere, I tip my hat. Walking into a very fun, friendly, and classic saloon feel. The food and drink menus were interesting. The beer selection is okay, mixed drinks were good and the food was so-so. Dishes ordered were the burger, Mac and cheese, boiled peanuts, shrimp, salad, and mashed potatoes. Of the food ordered, the shrimp and burger were good. Everything else was C- at best. Dessert ordered was bourbon pecan pie and was delivered fresh from Kroger's freezers. 

In regards to the experience - it was terrible. We called 3 days in advance for a 10 person reservation. We're given strict guidelines of "if entire party isn't present at the time of the reservation then the reservation is cancelled/bumped." We abided by the guidelines, everyone was present and accounted for 10 minutes before seating time. When seated, they crammed 10 adults at a table plated for 6 comfortably, 8 pushing it. We were sitting on every corner and with drinks, waters, and plates, it was like a Tetris game from hell. Food was overflowing on the table and no one was comfortable. 

The seating arrangement we had probably impacted my enjoyment of the food. However, if reservations are made, seat your patrons appropriately. The wait staff was even frustrated with the seating because it impacted their ability to place food, drinks, and maneuver around the table because we were stuffed in the middle of the floor.

This review references the dining experience - did not stay for music.
Got there before 6 on a Saturday. No parking. Waited a bit for Valet ($3). 
Had two beers (which they were out of both IPAs advertised to be on draft), served with warm glasses, before we had to ask for a food menu, then had our food before we had silverware, but service aside....
The food was supremely disappointing. 
Fried pickles for appetizer, they were only about 25% cucumber pickles, the rest were peppers, green tomatoes, maybe a green bean or two, and several fried lemon slices??? so bizarre and just a taste people would want. 
We also saw an appetizer come out with a mason jar of spread and a sleeve of saltines. Come on. Try harder Sutler!
Hubby had the brisket "horseshoe" which was grossly messy - he ate it, and paid for it the next day with several trips to the bathroom. 
I had the brussles sprouts and the mac n cheese - brussels were too burnt/crispy where they left a bad taste in my mouth for hours, the dish was mostly mashed potatoes for $8 and the mac n cheese was just way too rich. Not in a tasty way.

I hate to be such a hater but, I have much higher standards than this place achieves. I don't know what it's trying to be but... it's not winning. 
Later went to Treehouse for drinks and definitely wished we had done dinner there!

Tootsie's really is one of my favorite places off Broadway. Each floor has a stage and a band playing on it. It was a packed house, but we found a spot on the second floor by the back entrance behind the band. They band was a lot of fun and played a lot of country faves. 

The bathroom attendant was the greatest! She was so funny. 

This place is a must if you're headed out to Broadway St.

Stone Fox is a home run for me. The atmosphere, the food and the service were all top notch!

My supper club and I went for Brunch one Saturday afternoon and although it's located out in the middle of no where, it's well worth the drive! I had the breakfast tacos with dill sauce and I have to admit I was a little nervous for a Mexican breakfast food to have dill sauce on it. Never fear though, Stone Fox knows exactly what they are doing and it was absolutely delicious.

If you like a kick of spice, their take on the Bloody Mary is the right brunch drink for you. Not only is it ascetically pleasing, but it packs a lot of flavor in that tiny mason jar.

I seriously can't wait to go back and try their lunch/dinner items.

Go, go, go, go, go. Quit waiting around. Go.

Awesome venue, superb eats, very quick/friendly service, great prices, and very enjoyable ambiance.

The wife and I stopped in for a special holiday-date and could not have left more pleased and impressed. We had a reservation, were seated promptly, and immediately greeted by a helpful server. We ordered a drink and appetizer, and those were whisked out very quickly.

I opted to try their fresh seafood gumbo. Stupid delicious. Getcha sum. Honestly some of, if not the best seafood gumbo I've had in a long, long time. The wife got a cocktail that she enjoyed, but thought it a bit overpriced at $14.

We then turned our attention to dinner, and opted for the quarter-white-meat chicken with green beans, mashed potatoes, and mac-n-cheese. It was probably not more than 10 minutes after we ordered before our food arrived at the table. I had JUST finished the gumbo, and out slid our food!

At the end, there was not a morsel left on either of our plates. Each item held its own with deliciously prepared and seasoned flavors. I must admit however that the mac-n-cheese was a star. Something was just spot on with the dish that made us both want to carry home VATS of the stuff. The chicken was also a bright spot. Perfectly cooked, tender, juicy, and lightly-battered deliciousness. Needless to say, the bone was licked clean (as it should be). All for $11.99? Yeah, we'll be in again soon... mouth watering.

Well done, Woolsworth. Can't say enough good things!

All I need to say is that I got too messed up to even check in properly until later on the next day...Yup, Tootsies was a great host to us Phoenicians for two insane nights... who is ready to get your crunk on?
~The Good~
Woof. This place gets slammed, and for a good reason. Already half buzzed; I went into this huge joint viewing multiple levels of bands strumming live tunes. Dazed and having fun, I knew it was time....time to dance. The dance floor on each level is actually just widened space adjacent to the bar...and it's always packed. Packed with bachelors/bachelorette parties galore, this place is Party Central. It felt like a Vegas club- Nashville style. On the top level you can also go outside to a party area with tables which outlook Broadway. You can see all the hijinks going on down below and inside ;-) You can also see the Johnny Cash life-size doll on the building off to the side, looking like he's ready to jump. That was a trip, especially whilst drunk as a skunk. Drinks are served appropriately; the bartenders are relatively attentive and did a good job serving me in a timely fashion. The music was up to the bands, but they delivered great tunes and did a wide variety of hits from country to pop to even some rap. I can't honestly say I remember everything about those couple nights...primarily because I was too busy having fun ;-) This is definitely a place you must hit up, when in Nashville.
~The Bad~
STEPS.... GAH! Steps at the entrance are god-awful. It's unfortunate, but since we are talking about a multi-level club servicing a ton of people, let's just say there will be steps. Drinks are served out of small plastic cups...I get it; they have a ton of customers. But couldn't you spring for some glassware and save the environment a tad?  Those are my two major complaints, other than that this place his hella-fun
~The Downlow~
When in Nashville, come here on a packed night and get ready to party. No cover! I love it! No cover and tons of rocking live music. There will be crowds of people, but nothing that will overwhelm you. This place would get 4  1/2 stars, but will be rounded up for being such a good host to me and the other Phoenicians...plus no one died, that's a plus right? 5 stars for the great and unflinching live music, fast bar service, overall atmosphere and for no cover whatsoever!

Fairly typically greasy, college bar, with an odd mix of middle-aged women wearing very little clothing.  We came after a conference for a social with other attendees; there were supposed to be drink specials, but weren't, although beers were pretty cheap anyway.  There's a decent amount of seating, but we encountered some broken chairs and dirty tables.

Online ticketing system is ridiculous... how can 4 different shows all sell out within 3 minutes of the 9am opening window? Why keep people waiting in a virtual line if the tickets are sold out? After this experience, I will not bother again... a waste of planning and time.

Beware if you are visiting!

You can't throw a stick without hitting a bar with a live band in downtown Nashville, but we got lured into this place and instantly loved it's chill charm.  The bartenders on Friday, October 27th were FABULOUS!  We liked it so much that we spend almost $500 on drinks and snacks and generous tips.  So, why not go back!!  Right??  We LOVED it there.

So, yes, we returned on Saturday and everything was going swimmingly.  Much busier on a Saturday, lots of costumes and insane energy.  We headed straight to the bar to be greeted by a bartender who remembered us from the night before.  Of course, she was awesome.  I wish I was better at remembering names.  

THEN, my brother accidentally bumps into some young twit with a nasty mouth.  She told him "NOT to touch her!"  As if.  She was nothing at all.  She was throwing such ugly attitude and acted like she was going to get in his face so I stepped in.  She then started insulting my age as if we didn't belong there because we were too old.  How did Paradise Park Trailer Resort respond?  They kicked my group of 7 out!  About $700 later.  

Every place in Nashville had such lovely southern charm except for this place.  Makes sense.  They only want trailer trash there.  Got it!   When we return, and we will, we will spend our money elsewhere.

Saturday 9/16/2017 for my 40th birthday we rented out the "VIP" area on the top floor of Tootsie's.  We paid $900 to rent out the are from 10 pm -1 am, as it is $300 an hour (CASH ONLY). We had 20 people in our party and there was room for at least 40 people. Our waitress was very nice an attentive. After about an hour my friend tried to bring a few people up to our space unfortunately this is where things took a turn for the worse. There is an off duty police officer posted at the entrance to the VIP area. He told my friend that absolutely no one else was allowed up in the VIP area. I thought this was odd (as we were paying $300 and hour to be there) and asked the waitress who said of course you can have more people up, the officer is "new" and was incorrect. When the waitress informed the officer you could tell he did not like being told he was wrong. Throughout the next 2 hours the officer would come up and badger us about silly things like our balloons were too close to the stage (they had been in the same spot the entire night). At 12:55 he decided to clear out the VIP area and that our time was done. I took out my iphone which clearly said it was not 1 am and he said he didn't care our time was up. The bar had at least another hour until it was closed but he decided he wanted us to leave. As we walk out he grabs 2 bouncers to escort our entire party out of the building. Once again we had just paid $900 for this VIP area, had a $700 tab with the waitress (which of course we tipped 20% on because she was great) and now this person is kicking us out for no reason at all. We asked several times why and he never could give us an answer, his only response was  "I want you to leave" No other reason. As we are walking out  the head bouncer starts to push me and say I was trespassing?!?!. At this is point I make sure that one of my friends starts recording because I could see where this was going. When I alerted him he was being recorded he no longer touched me just kept saying we were trespassing and we needed to leave immediately. I want to make this clear, we did nothing wrong, no one in my party got in a fight, no one was over served, no one did anything. If we had done something wrong  I would not be wasting my time writing this review. We were a party of 20 people (all doctors, lawyers. police officers, school teachers) celebrating a birthday. I honestly can not believe they treated our party with such disrespect, I know Tootsie's is an Iconic bar but please take your money some where else.  Tootsie's if you care (I highly doubt you do looking at your other reviews) I have videos and pictures as proof.

I've been a frequent regular to this place since May 2018 when I moved to Nashville and made a million happy memories. Sadly, the way I was treated and brushed off tonight ruined every experience. 

My car keys - after having dinner at around 8:30/9pm here were snagged from inside the establishment and I walked all around the entire property and bar area looking for them. When I approached bar tenders at both the Tin Roof and Green Room sides they hurriedly said they did not have keys and ushered me away so they could take drink orders. I waited in line just as everyone else to politely ask if they'd seen keys. Not ONCE did they turn around or ask others if they had keys turned in or reported. 

I'm in the customer service industry and yes I know Fridays are busy but when someone loses a piece of their personal belongings and safety equipment such as keys/protectants you'd think they'd try to help?..

I'm sadly disappointed and will not be visiting again. Items are replaceable but when you are basically treated as a nuisance there's something else going on.

This place is a classic Nashville stop for a reason. I strongly suggest going up to the 3rd floor - it has a different vibe than everything else. We went out here after going to grab some delicious BBQ at Martin's. We ordered a bucket of beers and hung out listening to the music. 

BRING CASH! (There's also an ATM on the 2nd floor.) You can pay for your drinks with card, but you'll want to be able to tip the band. They're amazing musicians and all of them are working so hard. I felt awful that I didn't have cash or a bank card. Make up for my mistakes!
Had the most amazing food on broadway and the band was amazing, fell in love with the place and would highly recommended!!

The Bluebird is definitely a must for any fans of the show Nashville. Although a very small music venue in a random Green Hills shopping center it is amazing inside. It is a listening room, so it is meant to enjoy the music not to carry on any conversations after the music starts.

My friend and I got tickets on a weeknight for 'In the Round' where songwriters/musicians sit in a circle in the middle of the room and take turns playing original music. 

Although it was free to reserve the tickets online it was a $15 cover the night we went and they require all patrons to purchase one item (my friend and I ordered wine). Tickets are available at 8 am exactly one week in advance from the date you are planning to go. You can expect that any given night may sell out in minutes, especially if it's someone well known. It's possible to show up the night of to get one of their few seats for first come, first serve but you would need to show up pretty early to do so. 

Overall great experience and I highly recommend it!

If you are going to the bluebird for the menu then you have completely missed the point. Not that it is bad, but you go for the music and the vibe. It feels like an absolute Nashvilles staple, with a writers-in-the-round set up, reasonably priced drinks, and a fine food menu. It is great for couples or small groups, or if you just love music.

When I read about the history of Woolworth on 5th, I said to my wife that this is a restaurant that we have to visit.  This restaurant location and particular the counter, is forever linked to the Civil Rights Movement.  It is at this location where protests occurred in the form of sit-ins that made it possible for all Americans to be able to have a seat at the welcome table of restaurants across the country.  It felt good to be eating in a place, where those who fought for my freedom, protested.  The restaurant now serves as a testament to their efforts to overcome racial injustice with racial equality.  By the way, and I have to mention that the food at this place tastes awesome!  I highly recommend Woolworth on 5th for any occasion.  I also highly recommend it as a place to visit to connect with those who fought for our freedom!

If it's a weeknight and you are looking for a bit of a crazy crowd,  you might want to go HERE.

If you like to breath, you should still go here - but you might not want to stay too long.

This place is tiny. The stage is tiny. The singer was actually standing on the bar, while the band was on the tiny stage. There are some tables with stools. You should probably just drink PBR. It was a serious blast, with the whole place singing along. Very different than The Stage and Honky Tonk Central. It was our last stop of the evening, and I really had a good time here.
A nice experience. Our table ordered the blackened pork tenderloin, shrimp and grits, a filet. Brussels and caramelized mushrooms.

So we never actually made it through the door, but did get up to the body guard and were immediately turned off.  As you can see from photo's this place looks pretty cool - so we were excited to visit, but after waiting in line for over an hour and just about to get through the front door - we were very disappointed in the way were treated, I understand it was busy! But have some respect, the guys in the front spoke to us very rude and disrespectfully which I did not appreciate.  Made me think twice about entering the doors and giving them my service.

Crowded and loud which both made it great.  Bouncers were cool and some of the bartenders were too.  Best part was the bands though.  We were there on a Sunday night and the band on the 3rd floor was great. At one point two great looking guys were invited on stage with the band and did the best version of "Jackson" by Johny and June Cash that I have ever heard.  Possibly better than the original, they followed it up with "Save a Horse Ride a Cowboy" and the place went off!  Those guy should get signed immediately and that band should get a raise.  

Bottom line is you have to go to this place when you visit Nashville!

This was a place we were told not to miss when headed to Nashville. Was surprised how far from downtown it was and in a strip mall on the side of the road, but everything about it was well worth it.

We came in for an In The Round fundraiser for the local hospice program and got tow witness the round robin of top of the heap acoustic artists and songwriters including Pat Alger, Kathy Mattea, The DonJuans, Jelly Roll Johnson and Bill Cooley. Wow!! Stories were traded and songs sung individually of shared by all. 

Service was good and drinks done well. As live venues go, it is small and intimate and makes you feel as part of the show. Make sure to make reservations as they will sell out quickly.

Walk into tootsies for my first drink and to open a tab. 

"No, I don't have time to get you a water." 
                                - x blonde bartender on 2nd floor on 1/28

My thoughts, "guess I'll just find a bar that cares at all about its clientele."

The appearance of people spending their money on Nashville soul. 

18$ doubles of house liquor

 Impossible ripoff with no soul or humanity.

We went on Saturday 8/26, it was also the night of the big myweather- mcgregor fight on tv (which they had on the tvs upstairs and downstairs). Im not sure if this was why I had the experience I did (unusual volume due to the fight), however nights with risks like this should never occur anywhere at any time. While we were there at about 11 pm, the bar was so crowded it was literally the most people you could possibly fit within the space, ie, people standing upstairs in rows of persons like almost like in lines of people shoulder to shoulder breathing on the necks of those in front of them. No way to even WALK through that area! Downstairs was similar, perhaps a hair less crowded - however as we were standing there after getting our beers it became more crowded to resemble the upstairs. 

I hesitate always to leave a bad review, from what I could tell the service (bar) and bouncers were polite and provided good service. I write this review because this place is a death trap, and the management needs to change policies immediately to protect the lives of their staff and the people visiting. My friends and I had severe anxiety while inside of the bar and we skedaddled as soon as we could tell it was unsafe. Situations like the station night club fire could have had many less losses of life had the establishment practiced safe fire code and not overpacked their capacity. As a patron, always be aware of safety and overcrowding and visit bars that have your safety in mind.
