Very nostalgic, but more than that, the food was outstanding. I had a jambalaya and my wife had the pot roast. Both were great. We sat at the counter (you have to, its Woolworths), and Mike the bartender made a very good old fashioned. Overall, the atmosphere, the history, the food and drink, made this a must go spot when in Nashville. When you're there, take some time to walk around upstairs and down and look at the history in the building.

The history was interesting here, and it's in teeny tiny print on the menu if you want to read about it. The food was just OK, I had the hash. The place was pretty empty for Saturday morning no reservation was needed even though I made one. I parked on the street. I don't know what the parking situation was other than that, I think I got lucky. This didn't really amaze me and I don't think I'll be back.

I was here for Cinco De Mayo & the Predators were in the play off's. such a huge scene & the staff was still speedy & accommodating. We even managed to wrangle a table on the roof. Such a shame we had dinner reservations & had to give it up but boy howdy it was a blast & great views of the hysteria below.

Welcome to Nashville! Let me guess, you came here to "be discovered and get a record deal"?! Well, you should probably just stop while you're ahead and go to DSC and get a drink from Tyler Bennet, because you're gonna need it with those kinds of hopes and dreams!

My husband and I went for lunch. I ordered a Caesar salad and a cup of sweet potato and black bean soup. My husband ordered the burger and fries. 

Everything was really good . I loved the Caesar dressing and the soup was good. The soup is more like a chili though. 

My husband said his burger was good. They bring you their homemade sauces to try. All of them are good. The fries were good nothing special. 

I like the restaurant will definitely go back to try other items.  The staff is very nice too.

Cool. What an experience.

Having done the whole loud Broadway for a couple of nights, we were looking for something chill to do. That's when Bluebird cafe popped up on my yelp search.

Situated randomly in a plaza (across from the Whole Foods and other stores), Bluebird cafe sits. We went on a rainy Sunday night for songwriters night, hosted by Steve Goodie. No reservations are taken for the night-it's a first come, first serve.

We parked in the furniture store lot next door and walked over to stand in line. Almost two hours we stood and luckily, when the time came, the line started moving.. And the doors closed right behind us.  We were the last two people to get in for the night!

We were seated in the pews in the back (most people got tables, but I think it's because we were the last ones) and were served right away. We got some local brews and nachos to share.. And sat back to listen.

Steve Goodie is an awesome host- he's hilarious, musically talented, and full of charisma. And then the songwriters came up to stage- from young to old, to guitars to accordions, to singles to married folk, the range was endless. And it even ended with a famous songwriter (who wrote songs for Faith Hill, Keith Urban, etc) But overall, they were all solid and great. The crowd appreciated the music too (much different than what you see on Broadway) and it was just overall a great night. 

If you're looking for a chill place in Nashville to hear some great singers/songwriters and are willing to wait in line for it, definitely check out Bluebird Cafe- what a gem in Nashville.

Nashville's venerable music hall and bar is a must see for any visitor to the Broadway scene in Music City. 

Chances are it won't take long for you to find your way to Tootsie's Orchid Lounge as the lines are usually the longest, the music the loudest, and the crowd the most heavily served. 3 floors worth of music await you, each featuring their own band, long bar, and mass of revelers. In fact, it almost feels like 3 separate clubs in one building. Sure, the drinks are on the expensive side for the locale but I would argue the ambiance is worth the extra coin; especially on the open rooftop located on the 3rd floor. Oh, and watch those steps ladies - I witnessed a few close calls on my visit. 

I should also point out that Tootsie's Orchid Lounge seems to attract the best talent in Music City. Every act in the area competes for stage time thanks to their seemingly always packed house. Don't forget to tip - the house doesn't pay the bands whatsoever. 

You haven't truly visited Nashville without the stop at Tootsie's Orchid Lounge so you may as well get it in early since they are the bar set for the nightlife scene on Broadway.

The great thing about Tootsie's is the fact that it is right across the street from the arena so perfect for before and after concerts. There are three different bands on three different floors, plus a rooftop outdoor venue to enjoy. By far, the live music here was the best compared to the other honky tonk bars we stopped in. There were also ample places to get a beer, so that was a nice option too. The only downside, the popularity of this place means that it is crowded any time of day or night.

We got to Tootsie's just as lines had started forming at all the downtown bars. We went in and downtown was pretty crowded so we headed upstairs. We found two seats at the bar and sat down. Sitting at the bar is always hazardous because you always have tons of people coming up behind you to order their drinks, but most people would chat and leave so it wasn't an unpleasant experience. The bartender remembered our drinks after the first round and I thought that was pretty impressive, thinking of all the drinks she must have made in between. I am not sure how long we stayed but it was a while. We had several drinks and a shot before we finally peeled ourselves away. I'd come back for a drink (or two or three) at Tootsie's!

To begin, this place is filthy. Ask for plastic silverware if you dare to eat here; the rolled silver actually had dried food on it. Plus the glasses were cloudy, so I am fairly certain that they were unwashed as well. 
The quality of the food was poor. My husband got the cheeseburger and was thoroughly disappointed; the patties were thin and significantly over-cooked. I tried two of their specialty cocktails and both of them were ultra-sweet. Its like they were syrup- instead of spirit-based. That might have been fine if whatever syrups they had used were even slightly well made; they weren't. My husband loves bourbon and, from the look of the menu, the Sutler carried many of his favorites. Yet this too proved deceptive; three of the bourbons he requested weren't available, in spite of them being listed on the menu. When my husband finally found a bourbon that they did have in-house, the price on our bill was $4 more per drink than the price listed on the menu. We might not have noticed had the server not left the over-sized menus on our table throughout our entire visit - long after we had ordered. The giant things were in our way all night. 
Most of the staff we encountered were as distasteful as the food and the lack of cleanliness. The manager was actually standing near the food window and shouting expletives at other staff members. Some staff seemed to deserve to be shouted at, as they didn't seem to care much about their customers or the restaurant in which they were working. While our server fell into this category, there was one brunette server that was kind to us. Sadly, she wasn't assigned to our table. 
Avoid this place. Even with a cool-looking stage that we thought world be appealing, we found the music to be an afterthought. The artist playing made us think we were anywhere other than Nashville. Nearly all other music venues in town offer outstanding music; the Sutler not so much.

Here's another bar worth checking out because it's iconic in it's own right & I get it, if you are being a tourist it's fun to check out the "popular" places, why not!
First time we stopped by was during the day yes it was jammed packed but I think this is mainly due to the fact that the location is pretty small specially the first floor. we made our way to the roof top since it was a nice day, drinks we had the Frozen jack & coke ..yesss this was great can't go wrong nice & cold good taste & amount of alcohol. 
Second time around on a Friday night & it was insane gesshh can't believe they let sooo many people inside but we wanted to grab another frozen Jack so we decided to brave the crowd, the roof top is not very big & with all the tables it's incredibly annoying to try & stand any where with so many damm people around it is just way to much hard to enjoy your drinks when u are constantly moving back & forth because of so many people.
Decent service at the bar considering the crowds, the frozen Jack & Coke was $11 not terrible would be great if the cup was bigger but not bad over all, worth coming to check the place just for the Jack.

I love music and am not exactly a country fan per say ...but this place was amazing. 

 Four people sit in a circle/square (let's not be technical) and take turns singing songs they wrote. There is great dialogue between them and the crowd and the songs sung were absolutely fascinating/impressive on the evening I went given the atmosphere/vibe. 

I think this place is a must visit if you are ever in the nashville area.

4.0 - I experienced The Sutler for the first time during their happy hour. Honestly, when we arrived we were we had no idea that happy hour was going on but it was definitely a good surprise. The happy hour was 1/2 price draft beers, select cocktails, and house wines. 
The atmosphere was very welcoming and inviting when we arrived. There was live music playing on the stage inside and the large windows were open out front. There is a small patio out front, but all the seats were taken, so we sat inside. 
I went downstairs to the bathroom and saw that there was a whole downstairs space. There was a large billards room and bar. This area was much larger than expected. 
I was only at the Sutler for two rounds of drinks, but I could have stayed all night. Can't wait to go back!

From one loud... sweaty venue to another, the thing I remember about Tootsie's is on one level they had rockabelly ZZTop looking dudes cranking... and on another floor up front more C&W music. Both areas packed with glass eyed locals and tourists blending into an amalgamation of humanity all seeming to have a good time. That is except for a bar maid standing over a bucket of cold ones yawning uncontrollably, even tho the clash of both bands had to be driving her eardrums crazy in her strategically placed area about mid way between both on the stairs. 
After a few Yuenglings it's a blur irregardless. Wednesday night in Nashville! I liked that while many were tourists or convention participants, many locals were hanging keeping cool and hydrated with many beers around their tables listening to, who knows, maybe the next big break out band. Either way, I'm pretty sure they have spent a good part of their down time here chillin and watching all the crazy out of towners happily drop serious coin into their vibrant city making them much more tolerant of the many who... just can't hold their liquor!

We planned to get tickets for this but they are elusive. We arrived around 7:30pm to line for the late 9:30 show. It was worth the 2 hour wait. We chatted up with others in line.

We got really lucky and was seated right next to the performers.

The bluebird has had so many song writers come through over the years. This is a very intimate setting. The performers are seated in the middle of the room and small tables form around them and it fans out. 

There was a $15 cover charge, but well worth it. The food menu was also decent with a wide selection of appetizers, food and salad options.

If you're coming from out of town this is a must visit.

I had a GREAT time here and would go back in a heartbeat.

This place was great for local music and felt like I wasn't on Broadway. I got there right as a new band was setting up and ended up staying through the whole set. The set up was great and a good amount of room with attentive servers and bartenders.

I could not stop drinking the blueberry Moscow mule, definitely one of my favorite drinks I had while I was in Nashville. I also ordered the candy pig mac & cheese and thought it was delicious. While it definitely tasted a little plain the jalapeno queso was delicious and make the mac and cheese delicious. Also had to get a side of fried pickles!

Overall, I had a really great time at this bar and would suggest it to anyone visiting Nashville.

Woolworth on 5th is a must s when visiting Nashville, simply for the rich history of the Civil Rights movement and counter sit-ins.  

The building and restaurant has expanded and completely been renovated, but they preserved the stools and the markings of where the counter and stools used to be (before they were moved) are still there.  

They've got a nice menu, but we shared a chocolate malt while sitting at the counter and taking it all in.  

Great malt, lovely service and something everyone should experience.

Though not my favorite Honky Tonk on the NashVegas strip, it's up there. It's a must-stop bar blasting country songs that needs to be a part of your bar crawl.

Sureeeeee there are some cheaper bars and sureeeeee it's way crowded, but c'mon! It's right there smack dad in the middle of the action! You'll stop here - whether you like it or not!

First of all the name needs to be changed ASAP... When you think of Café, you think of good eats, Southern style comfort foods. How about going with Blue Bird Joint! Went on a Monday night to see a band and no reservations were allowed. Being that this was my first time EVER there, I had no idea that if you can't make reservations, you need to RUN... Stood in line 48 minutes, only to get to the front and overhear the guy saying, I just got two singles left. Well it was 6 people in line. After 48 minutes and it was cold.. So the people in front of us got pissed off by the cavalier attitude of the door dude- He was king ,and we were peasants. I mean somebody from INSIDE could have come OUTSIDE and did a quick little count and said, ALL of YALL aint getting in.. GO HOME NOW.. don't waste your time, energy and dedication because you AINT GETTING in.. NAHHH nobody warned us.. IF the people in front of us had not gotten pissed, we would have been turned away.  After we were graciously allowed to pay the fee to get in, we were led right next to the band.. I was so close I could have been IN the band. The speaker box was reach out and touch close. I can barely hear a day later. I was so close, I could have unplugged the guitar, and overtook the stage and belted out my own songs. OF course I am talentless and my feet was still frozen from standing out in the freezing elements for 48 minutes. 
Inside of the place is small.. I mean like itty bitty. Tables on top of tables, hardly no aisle space. Certainly a fire hazard. Service was spotty.. One minute you saw her, next minute it was time to go home. The bathroom was a mess. Mr. Door Dude  had free time after filling every lil nook and cranny with people to get a Clorox wipe and clean up in there. My wine was watered down, my cranberry and vodka was overly iced and the zips were straight out the bag, served with refrigerator cold dip.  I think the menu was limited, I ordered sweet potato fries and was told they were out. Then I was told I had until 10 to order food, and it was 9:52. 
IF your going cause you're a fan of the show Nashville, don't bother. IF your going because you're a fan of music.. don't bother.. it's a crappy little stage with bad sound and cramped sardine style seats. And to think they charge a fee to get in there. SHAME!!!!

You gotta check out Tootsie's if its your first time in Nashville. Located right on Broadway it is near all of the other dive bars in the vicinity. Tootsie's is famous because of its early customers including Willie Nelson and Patsy Cline, and its right in front of the Ryman Auditorium. 

Pros: Fun live music from local bands and cool rooftop bar

Cons: This place is always packed, not the cleanest, and it can be hard to move around because of the layout of the venue. 

Plan to stop by early before it gets packed for the experience then go hit up other places on Broadway that are better.

Walked through this historic Nashville watering hole as part of our "Walkin' Nashville Music City Legends Tour". 

As it was a hot day, I saddled up to the bar for a quick Jack & Coke.

The bartendress asked "Who is that guy?", referring to our tour guide. "He comes through here every day at about the same time with a bunch of people just to use the bathroom."

I explained we were on a walking tour and he was our guide.

She said out of all the time she has worked there, I was the first on the tour to ever buy a drink.

I told her it takes a New Yorker to break the ice.

I made reservations for last night, and it did not go well. After a long uber ride, we were sat down and given menus. We waited. And waited. And waited. Then a woman comes over and tells us that due to a flood in the basement they are unable to feed any other people, then asks us if we wanted drinks. We say yes... And wait. And wait. And wait. No server came over the entire time we were there. We go to the bar to order drinks there, the bartender tells us they had let call 10 minutes ago.... So we leave. I understand it was a poor situation, but they could of handled us properly and appropriately. Big let down.

Obscenely crowded and cramped dive bar. Luckily we snagged an open area of the bar and flagged the bartender down to order drinks, which were watered down but the same price as a decent drink. $23 for a vodka tonic and rum and coke. The rooftop is pretty cool, with good views, but that itself doesn't merit a visit here.

It's famous and well known for having patrons such as Willie Nelson and a documentary about the bar, but if you didn't know any better, it's just another crowded bar. Our tour guide mentioned Tootsie's and its original name "Mom's," which was changed because, according to the tour guide, who wants to go drinking at Mom's?

I ordered the Chicken Fried Chicken burger with Sweet Potato fries and a Sweet Tea. I then proceeded to the pick up counter, where literally a minute later my order was ready. I was pleased with the fast service as I was hungry, but didn't question why it was so fast for a Chicken burger. I filled up my drink and sat down to eat and I noticed the food looked like leftovers, it wasn't until my boyfriend tried some chicken and fries and mentioned how it looked like it was old, had either been sitting in the kitchen or refried and was pretty cold considering a few minutes had only past. I wasn't going to return it as I don't like making a big fuss but my bf said he would since I paid for it and shouldn't get leftovers. 

When he politely told the lady at the pick up counter about it she turned to me and yelled 'I gave this to you 10 minutes ago of course it's cold' (definitely wasn't 10 minutes ago) then she told me 'I got you' and went to the cook at the back who then came out and stared me down. After he re-made my food, he came out with it and then had a go at me telling me that if I waited 10 minutes then of course it would be cold and continued to basically tell me I was wrong. I didn't argue back, instead I looked at him as I was already uncomfortable with how they were acting.  

The food this time, was great. The Chicken was more golden then brown, cold and burnt and the fries were steaming hot unlike the previous bunch. Obviously they thought I wouldn't notice if they just sent out an order already made, which was ready in 2 minutes from ordering, compared to when they remade my food which took more than that. 

As a server myself at a great brunch restaurant located in downtown, I have never been so appalled by such service. If a customer pays for a meal and they are not happy with it (in my case not because I'm picky but I don't appreciate leftovers) you don't come out and yell at them for your idiotic mistake, you re-make the order and get on with your day. 

I get its stressful, I'm in the same environment but if a customer is unhappy with a meal you fix it and remain polite. 

The food was actually great when they cooked it fresh but sadly the service from the back of house was disgusting from both the female and older male, therefore I won't be returning and will spread the word about my experience so no one else gets treated such a way for a mistake the cook made by serving leftovers.

Because the food was good they get two stars, otherwise I would've rated it Zero.

This was one of my favorite spots. We waited 2 hours for breakfast only to be told once we were seated that there were no more hash browns or grits. With such a limited  brunch menu there wasnt a lot of choices. We left after an hour drive. Total waste of 4 hours of our day.

This experience was very unique and enjoyable. My wife surprised me with this little Cafe and it was my favorite outing we did. It's a very personable experience to be that close to upcoming artist and there successes. I would recommend this place for anyone that is a party animal on the inside and a laidback gent on the outside.

Venue - Cool bar, smaller than most, not as modern as others. 

Crowd - Good looking crowds with good vibes.

Drinks - Outside has a cart bar that has good deals on drinks.

Prices - Very fair prices.

Location - Great location with great views from the patio.

Staff - Very nice and friendly. 

Overall great place and would be back.

The Sutler Saloon has it all. It has delicious food, fantastic music, atmosphere and well crafted cocktails. We took a friend, from out of town, with us and he loved it as well!! 

We had reservations at 9 and got there at 8:40 and thought we were going to have to wait a bit and magically a table opened up about a minute after we arrived. Our server was very knowledgeable about everything on the menu and loved his job! The band was a local act that had just won the Nashville Blues competition...:they were amazing! 

The most amazing part was the food! There were so many yummy things on the menu, that it was hard to decide. We ended up ordering too much and we were stuffed! We had:
-French fries with with BBQ sauce ketchup, I love ff and these might be the best I have ever had!
-Georgia shrimp dish-tons of shrimp!
-Loaded Macaroni: creamy deliciousness 
-hamburger dunk: might be the best burger I've eaten. The dunk means it comes on a thick bread and is dunked in a creamy sauce of some sort. It was a sopping good time:).
-pinto Poblano soup: spicy goodness!
-friend pickles-this was our least favorite dish, but it was still good.


We cannot wait to return for a Family Supper on a Sunday and listen to some live Bluegrass!!!

First off their bottomless mimosas are only $17 and there's no time limit! There was a long wait when I got there but the bar downstairs let's you start the bottomless while you wait and you can play all sorts of different games in the bar. Live music and the staff was so sweet! Food was also delicious! I got the chicken fried biscuit and made it hot (because it's Nashville)  Also I'm assuming there's always a wait on the weekend so take that into consideration!

What a cool place! I came here on a Friday night with my date around 10pm to grab a couple drinks and they had a really great cover band playing an eclectic mix of songs (including their own renditions of Red Hot Chili Peppers and R. Kelly). It's called a saloon, but it's not really a saloon. I liked that it wasn't just another honky tonk place.

What surprised me most about this bar is that they have two more bars downstairs underground - one's a lounge and one's a pool hall! The DJ at the lounge was doing a fantastic job playing a great selection of music. I was also really impressed by the cluttered cowboy boots hanging down from the top of the stairwell on the way down toward these two underground bars.

The Sutler gets Five Stars in my book for its live music, the lounge DJ's music downstairs, its overall atmosphere, its many eclectic surprises, and its awesome decor!
But I give the Sutler Three Stars for its service and food quality. I had to wait an unreasonably long time for a waiter to come to our table at the saloon part of the bar. And our drinks down in the lounge took an unreasonably long time to make and/or come to our table. Additionally: We wanted to order dessert at the Saloon, but they were out of their (only) two dessert options, and the potato hummus appetizer we ordered instead was not that great. The chips were oily and hard, and the dip (which wasn't anything to rave about) needed a bigger bowl for the size of those chips!

I still had a lot of fun there and highly recommend people check it out, at least for the fun of the music and the exploration of the underground bars. I also want to come back on a Sunday for their bluegrass brunches!

Right in the heart of downtown Nashville. This place is very spacious. We didn't go upstairs and just stayed in the dining area. We got seated immediately. The service was very slow. And the food was nothing to brag about. I would go back to try their breakfast. Seems like it  would be better. And I would love to see what the other levels are about as well. Still a pretty new spot so it probably has to get some kinks out. It has a lot of potential though.
Great spot! We visited on a Thursday night, probably a slow night for them, but a lot of people out & about. The bartender was quick, they had a great band playing!

I love the painstaking effort to restore this historic space. But the love stops there. This is a new place so maybe they just haven't worked out the kinks. I ate breakfast at the counter and experienced painfully slow service. Coffee came, no sugar no spoon and it took forever for the server to find those things. The sweet potato pancakes were really good once I was able to get them to bring the special butter promised on the menu and then she had to go find some utensils. The utensils were at the hostess station, (not behind the counter?).  Overall the place felt disorganized, chaotic, and slow, and I was there at a time that wasn't crowded.   I also ate lunch there a few weeks prior and had a similar experience with service so slow a really began to think they had forgotten about me,  very average fried chicken, and undercooked green beans by classic southern standards.
Went and had lunch on the top floor on a Monday afternoon. Food was great and the  bartender was super friendly. I'll definitely be back on my next trip to Nashville

Slooow service. Wish I knew what the new menu tasted like? Went in at 4 on St. Patty's day.  Seating was slow. Despite what appeared to be an abundance of staff service was sad. We told waitress that we were not interested in drinking but were looking to eat. After 10-15 minutes dropped some cash and left. I am not Suttling for poor service. 

Returned for another try at lunch on 9/14/16. Service was still slow despite an early start at 11:30. However, this time I got to try the food. It was worth it. Brisket tacos were muy bueno! The included a spicy sauce base.  Light weights beware or skip the sauce. Presentation was appealing and included a unique radish shaving on top for color. I will be back to try other things.

We came here for brunch on a Saturday and were SO impressed. I ordered the BLT (added avocado) and shoestring fries with a side of jalapeño ranch for dipping. OMG SO GOOD. The best BLT I have ever had, stacked high with bacon, big beefsteak tomatoes and crisp lettuce. The biscuits with honey butter that they bring to the table we're gobbled down by our whole group they were fantastic. Oh and live music and bottomless mimosas for $16 and some change? Yes please!!!! Love this place.

We had heard of the Famous Tootsie's in Nashville many times and it did not dissapoint. We ordered some beers and then listened to some great country music by up and coming artists. We stayed for an hour or two and just soaked up the ambience and nostalgia that is Tootsie's and you should too.

For the history and nostalgia a 4. Food is really closer to a 3. 
Yes there is a lot of it. Yes, it's your basic deviled eggs, fried green tomatoes, craft cocktails, LOTS of red meat choices but none really execute that well.
I had the salmon and it was 'ok.' I subbed the mashed potatoes (perhaps my mistake?) for Brussels which mean broccolini (undercooked and very tough-forget el dente-this was closer to raw and not a bright green), and Brussels that we're rather bland. (Maybe I'm spoiled by the bath of balsamic you normally see them cooked in, with pork belly!) but I'd Simeone it up by saying try the appetizers: deviled eggs were yummy, the cocktails (Diners Delight was perfect) or the NY Strip (which hubs had and judged 'good.'). 
Nice concept. Food is ok. Service was excellent (Ayanna) and the old dance movies on screen were fun!
It was our anniversary and they comped us a peach cobbler ala mode which was just all batter under ice cream and maybe two peach slices. No fruit flavor at all...super sweet. If you like tart cobbler like we do this will be a disappointment. But quite nice of them to give this. (Lit candle included).

Yeah, I expect live music to be played here. I didn't really care for it. Plus it's crowded which I can't stand. Maybe that's a good thing for the bar because it keeps the place going. But hey if you like feeling as though you are stuck on people and loud live music then this is your place. My friends and I went to the next bar.

I was hesitant about eating here because of the history that's associated with the restaurant but as soon as I walked in, I noticed that they preserved the history and are willing to discuss the history.
I ate with a group of 9 and we were accommodated with a booth that was perfect for a birthday celebration. Our waiter was very attentive to our orders; drinks, apps and food and everything was correct.
I had the burger and it was delicious. We were kidding about the description because it sounded like a Big Mac but far exceeds that fast food. 
According to the table, the shrimp and grits were delicious. The pork tenderloin was fantastic. The deviled eggs were a surprise, bacon makes everything better.

Tootsie's has a lot of different levels with a different band performing on each, which means you're bound to find something you like. It also has a great rooftop access that overlooks Broadway Ave - perfect selfie and panorama spot. I've been on the weekends and weekday and you'll always find this place bustling.

In town visiting from NYC and heard about comedy and live music happening here. I heard it was a very nice establishment and that a nice selection of food could be ordered. 

Upon arrival, it appeared very nice. The show was held downstairs and I was shocked that the downstairs area was not as nice. The furniture did not match and I'm surprised that the couple sitting on the sofa didn't tip out, as it was leaning. 

The service at the bar was great. The band and comedian were awesome! 

I was bothered by the fact that they served my salmon with plastic ware instead of silverware. . That is just unacceptable to me...especially for a 4star restaurant. They get 3 stars for mediocracy. And, the salmon tasted microwaved. We need more pacific and Alaskan wild salmon at restaurants charging $20+. Farm, Atlantic salmon is not worth it.

There is a reason why there is a line to get in!  Tootsie's won't disappoint.  We enjoyed music on all three levels, from the rooftop to the lower level.  Of course it was crowded, but the music was fantastic and the service was very efficient.  

This is a not to miss stop on Broadway!

This one is tough to rate. Depends on what type of night out your into. 

If you love jammed packed live music bars this is certainly the spot for you. 3 very narrow floors of live music , you will not hear anything but music. The energy here was jamming. 

If you are claustrophobic pick another place.

Three stories of honky tonk!  Yee haw!  Tootsies was the only one of the Broadway bars I'd ever heard of before coming to Nashville and it lived up to the hype.  It's purple.  They play good country.  And they have a great rooftop patio to look out on all of the bachelorette parties lining Broadway.  It was crowded and touristy, but it was also exactly what I had in mind for my Nashville experience.

Wonderful experience here 

We were like the other 50 people who couldn't get reservation so we waited outside for over an hour. But - it was so worth it. There is no cover charge but each person has to spend $10 on food and drinks and that was easy. 
Music was great and the performers were so wonderful. This was a great intro to country music for me and I like it!!
Green fried tomatoes: first time trying and decent taste. After awhile I didn't care too much for the breading but the tomato was food. 4 stars. Wait a little before eating or you may burn your tongue. 
Nachos with queso blanco: decent - jalapeño spiced things up and the accompaniment of salsa and. Sour cream on the side was appreciated. Chips were so thin. 
Hubby tried the pineapple cider which had a great pineapple flavor- if you like pine apple you must try. 
I got the Tennessee Wit: white ale. Smooth and delicious.

What a cool place!!! The vibe when you walk in is so cool! The lights are dim and the dining room is open. You can see the kitchen from your seat and the decor is very Nashville. The bar has great happy hour specials until 6:30, which is what we went for on my birthday. I got the watermelon margarita and it was refreshing and amazing, went down a little too easy, that could get dangerous! My husband got the moonshine and root beer, which was excellent!! I would definitely go back for happy hour again, great 1/2 price specials are totally worth it!!
While we were standing at the bar we were looking around to see what people were eating, it all looked amazing. We even ended up talking to the table behind us about what they were eating. Next time we go, I'm definitely getting food!!! 
I keep hearing about the downstairs bar and how awesome it is but unfortunately it was rented out for a private party when we were there. I was a little disappointed but I'll go back and hopefully then it will be open!

One of my friends brought me here because some of my other friends are obsessed with this dive and told me I absolutely had to check it out. It's definitely got a grungy feeling to it, but I accepted it for what it is and really liked it. It wasn't overly crowded when I went on a Thursday night and I do remember the night ending with Sweet Caroline so all in all, I had a great time.
The music here is so good, but the venue is way too narrow. I could barely see the stage. We stayed for 30 minutes, but left because we needed some air and room.

I don't do reviews, but I had to share my story. My friends and I visited Paradise Park before the Preds game free beer. I got home and I realized I lost my phone at some point. I for sure thought it was a goner never to be seen again lost in the black abyss that is Broadway.  But today I get a text from some random Racheal. Turned out she was a bartender at Paradise Park and she went out of her way to charge my phone, text, call, and message me to let me know they had found my phone. Talk about customer service from a bar, would've never thought that would happen. It gets better: I tried to tip her for her troubles and she wouldn't take the money! She said she was just paying it forward and if I wanted to say thanks write a Yelp review. So here ya go Rach, thanks for saving me a couple hundred bucks!

Hmmm. When I was at Tootsie's I felt like I morphed back to dirty 6th street in Austin. I am glad we checked out a honky tonk while visiting Nashville but 45 minutes was enough for me. This is the scene: $5 bottles of Coors Light, rambunctious bachelorette parties, large crowds even at 2pm and a band playing mostly covers. 

Tootsie's has a downstairs and a rooftop bar. We stopped in for a round and to experience a honky tonk while in Nashville. We first tried downstairs but it was packed so we ventured upstairs. The large mostly drunken crowd was having a good time. It truly is a fun atmosphere. However I would prefer a dark room with a singer songwriter and an attentive crowd.

The Bluebird Café has the best new music in town! I love going and hearing these singer/song writers perform in the round. There is something special about hearing a songwriter perform their music live. I've been three times and each time has been wonderful. Now the food is not that great....but hey, it's a music venue. I was there to hear the music.
Great food, awesome music and AMAZING drinks! If you haven't been to this haunt, you need to travel south and try it out!!!!

Excellent place for late night food you won't feel guilty about it because you won't remember it. Burgers and cheese fries are sooo good. Live music nightly, like everywhere else in Nashville, and a fun vibe throughout. The place is danky but huge, plenty of room to hang out with friends and sober up while you wait for an Uber. I definitely recommend this place.

Went to Woolworths before a show at TPAC. I called ahead of time to make sure I didn't need a reservation to sit at the bar and have a drink. When I arrived it was packed- that's a great sign! Then I sat down at the bar. It took almost 15 minutes for anyone to come and take my drink order much less just drop a water to me. I've worked as a bartender and I know they were busy- but it almost felt like they were avoiding me.
The bartender was extremely rude to the couple next to me- I get it- busy night, lots going on. But there's really no excuse. Perhaps Woolworth should add more bartenders? Not sure. The fried green tomatoes were great. However, it's not good enough for me to return any time soon.

Did not care for the music being played in this establishment. Too new country for me. Packed with bras hanging over by the bar area. 
Alot has changed since Patsy Cline used to go in here and just chill after the Opry, only reason i went in. I walked straight through to the back and walked out to the ally.
People push you, bump into you. 
Dodn't care for it.
I know its World famous but, I didn't like it.
To loud. Too busy. New country music. Young performers.

The Sutler has some promise. The layout upstairs is great for live music or socializing in the bar area. There's a good selection of drinks and smoky scents waft from the kitchen.

I came with a group of five and met some other friends coincidentally at the bar. Parking was a pain - the valet was massively backed up at 5:30 one a weekday - and while waiting I lucked upon a lone parking spot behind the valet line. Most of my group parked pretty far away or waited 10+ minutes to valet.

Once inside we (mostly) forgot about the parking situation as the group trickled in. Most of us had a beer from the good selection of craft beers on tap. The cocktails were getting good reviews too.

Service was minimal at the bar, so we decided to move as the smell of food made us hungry. We got seated in the bar area across the aisle from the actual bar because there was a wait for the main dining room - which was 2/3 empty during most of our visit. The hostess promised we'd get service "as soon as we sit down" but after about 15 minutes we had to go ask politely for service. Another wait ensued. Just as everyone was about to leave, a friendly waitress showed up and apologized. She helped us navigate the menu and suggested her favorites. Note: most items on the menu have pork or pork fat in them.

The potted smoke was richly flavorful but a bit too salty. Share it with at least four people. A little more bread to spread it out more would have been nice. The Yes Dammit burger had a tasty beer cheddar dip but the beef was over cooked and over salted. It has promise but underwhelmed. The fries were amazing (pork fat does wonders here) and the pig braised collards were good and had a nice kick.

Service was very friendly but slow most of the time - probably a function of being understaffed.

Work out the kinks and I can see this place getting a good rating. Until then, there is a lot of competition nearby.

I gather this place is historical? I don't know the history but this must be why the place was so jam-packed.  We could hardly get in the door or even enjoy the other floors.  Upon opening the front door we were greeted by an overwhelming "toilet" smell.  Not pleasant.  We fought our way through the crowd and made it all the way up to the rooftop.  None of the floors caught our attention and the vibe just wasn't working for us.  We stayed for only a short while.  Out of all the bars we stopped in on "honky tonk row," this was our least favorite.

I really enjoyed my time at Paradise Park. It's a super electric bar with AstroTurf for flooring. I loved the live music playing during both of my visits as well as the smells coming from the kitchen. They serve a variety of food that I didn't try. There's plenty of space to roam about as the bar was not overly crowded. Buyer beware - This is by no means a classy spot for a date or romantic evening, but for a small group of tourists, this worked out just fine.

The Bluebird Cafe has been on my list for some time! Its history, its intimate setting, its obscure location.... all adding to the appeal. 

Getting tickets online is a cluster, but not getting tickets in advance is a bigger cluster, or should I say huge line with limited chance of making it inside. We had three of us, and online ticketing split us into the tables. No biggie but not ideal. 

We arrived 40 minutes before the show and the staff was frazzled and not friendly. I am docking a star for that. It's intimate and they seat 75 guests for two nightly shows. Most of which are preassigned online. So why are you frazzled and short with us?

We ended up in the very back at a high top; the only seat that they don't have a waitress assigned to. Also annoying but the bar was close.

Now....onto the good stuff! The place is so cute and even in the far back, it was so intimate and enjoyable to see such talent on stage. It is clear that those on stage appreciate the Bluebird. As an audience member, being able to hear their music and stories in a lovely acoustic setting is very unique. I love live music and many genres, however "newer" pop-country is not one of them. The band we saw was a male/female country duo called Sons of Daughters. Because it was acoustic, it felt less country-ish...and I really enjoyed them! The male lead especially! I'm always rooting on these musicians working to really make it. 

Overall, the music and intimacy was excellent! And that helped ensure that the unsteady service didn't sour my long awaited night at the Bluebird!

I visited Nashville for Memorial Day Weekend and knew I had to pop by the Bluebird for Writers Night. Since Monday was a holiday, there was only one that weekend, and everyone had the idea to go early. I got to the Bluebird at 5:30 PM and was one of the last to make it in for the 8 PM show (even though during the initial count, I was #60 -- I think people saved a lot of spots for their friends to jump in later and the performers also had some guests). The wait was pretty long and hot, and there was no shade so bring a fan and parasol and something to do! I'm sure most nights aren't quite as bad.

That being said, the wait was worth it -- especially for 3.5 hours of music and stories. The Bluebird is truly a songwriter's venue. Steve Goodie was a hilarious host, setting the stage well and even performing the most hilarious song. All 8 or so performers were good singers... but truly amazing songwriters. I felt so many emotions that night from writers of diverse experiences, ages, and hometowns.

Just as I thought the show was over, they bring on a featured songwriter -- Don Schlitz! He was gracious enough to entertain us for hours with hilarious stories and songs he wrote, including "The Gambler," "Forever and Ever, Amen," "When You Say Nothing At All," "You Can't Make Old Friends," among others that the crowd sang along to together.

The inside is rather crowded, and I would strongly recommend against getting the garden salad (veggies were plain and chicken was nasty). I would gladly pay $7 and a couple hours of waiting for one of the most memorable musical experiences!

This quaint little Blue Bird Cafe recommendation get there early and make sure to reserve your tickets way in advance. This place had people waiting at the doors hours before the doors opened. Different people, famous and not come to this historic cafe to entire all who pass or travel to Nashville. It's small, original and oh so intimate. The wait staff is amazing shout out to Bobbi and Anna- don't forget to tip them. Be prepared to buy some souvenirs to take with you. I purchase a very cute truckers hat and shirt from the Bluebird. Nashville must see.

So disappointed. It started with the hostess. We came in around 2PM and it wasn't busy. The hostess had to look for us a table before she could seat us which wasn't a big deal. When she sat at us at a booth I said thanks for the booth and I meant it. She basically sneered and said well that's all she had that would fit our party of 5. Okay... so maybe I interpreted that wrong. I'll let that slide. Our server was so nice & pleasant but that didn't mean they knew anything about being a server. Food was delivered sans silverware. We asked our server for that when she brought us condiments. She left and was doing something else besides bring us something to eat with. We sat there for about 5 minutes until another server realized we were looking for her and he brought it to us. Another negative was running out of tea and I hate to run out of drink. She was nice so I hate leaving a bad review but she was just inattentive. Now to the food....eh. Nothing special. I had corned beef hash which it looked great and the description sounded good but it was just boring. Thank goodness for chipotle ketchup because I had to douse it pretty heavily. My husband had curried cauliflower that he said was boring. My 7 year old niece said the Mac & cheese at her school was better. Her & my brother n law shared fried chicken and just gave it an ok.  My sister had a burger and she was the only one that said that her food was good. So basically I give service a 2 and food a 3. I would not go back. Too bad because of it's interesting history with the civil rights movement it should be a place to stop if you're visiting Nashville.

It's very unusual that I like the food but don't like the restaurant. I try not to be a curmudgeon but sometimes it's warranted. I've been to the new Sutler twice. The first time I had the grilled cheese and tomato soup. It was wonderful. What wasn't wonderful was the hostess who looked down the length of her nose at me and made a face like she'd just stepped in something made by a dog. I had to get her talking just to see if she would actually insult me so I asked her if she'd ever been to the old Sutler to which she replied "No" with the attitude of "as if." I decided then and there that regardless of the food, I wouldn't give them anymore of my business.
Jump to New Years day, 2019. I considered my options, (price, selection, location, parking, etc,) for brunch and rested my hopes on my favorite all around brunch - Lana's Copper Kettle. No-go, not open. Then my thoughts turned to Fenwicks and their lovely sauerkraut corned beef hash - also not open which led me by proximity away from Sinema, (too fancy/dressy,) to the Sutler.
This time there were two hosts, one male & one female who also both regarded my presence with a fair amount of distain. I was eating alone, I'm not twenty-five anymore and apparently not sufficiently hip or cool enough to be greeted warmly. Whatever. I sat myself at the bar and had the Andouille hash. Pretty good. The bartender was nice as they usually are, (tip dependent.) 
As I ate I considered what bothered me about the place besides the cold welcome and I narrowed it down. I knew the old Sutler, I wasn't a regular but I ate there infrequently and saw a few excellent shows, (Victor Wooten solo no less.) It was a dark, comfortable place even as a brooding portrait of Nathan Bedford Forrest glowered over everyone from above the bar. They welcomed business AND working folk, young and old alike.
The new Sutler is a Disney-fied version for the young & hip crowd that offers a carefully crafted veneer of Southern sans the hospitality. When you've been on a pirate ship then ride the Pirates of the Caribbean you feel more than a little cheated. The wait staff all contrived in flannel and jeans, yee-haw y'all. Nothing sours a southerners mouth like a disingenuous pantomime of ourselves. I'd bet a thousand dollars not one person in the bar could guess what a sutler was or more to the point would even care. It's pretty good food but it's an insult to the memory of the real thing, a genuinely comfortable neighborhood bar. Gone but not forgotten.

This is a really fun place to visit with numerous options for listening to bands, one on each floor. It is well known of course, and it is worth visiting. I only got a coke with the intent of listening and we enjoyed our time there. It was busy, but because of the multiple levels and listening choices, we felt that there was lots of room for lots of people.
They have a selection of clothing products, mostly shirts, Ts and sweatshirts. My wife found one she liked and the price was fair.
Overall, I would encourage my friends to try it.
It is not a family venue. It is a bar! But if you like music, I don't think you can go wrong. There are many choices in the area and we felt it was worth our investment of time.

This review is not a reflection of the amazing performers that we saw at bluebird. The musicians were absolutely phenomenal and I don't even love country music- they were soulful and had wonderful voices! I am in awe of their talent and being so close to them was really cool! Musicians get a solid 5 out of 5. 

This from start to finish gets a solid two or three would be too generous. To begin with the ticket process is as people say another reviews completely annoying. You logon before 8 AM and are in this online queue- that randomizes people at 8 AM and hopefully you get in to buy a ticket but you only have a minute so get your credit card ready.  So you're better off just trying a bunch of dates and hoping for the best!

So we went to a 6 PM show on Thursday night. We arrived at 5:30 PM parking is impossible and you are likely to get towed if you park illegally in someone's life. When you walk up there is a line of people waiting to get in if people don't show up and if you have a reservation you can go in and hostess would check your name on the list. This is where it gets a little aggressive the hostess has an impossible job I do believe that her job is very difficult to try and get as many people in as possible while also Keeping to code regulations etc. I think that bluebird may need to take a page out of Starbucks book and revisit their customer service policies and invest in some training for their staff. So yes take this with a grain of salt this is a stressful situation for the staff they only have a small amount of time to get people's orders before the show starts etc. but with two shows at night every night of the week you think they'd have a better system down. Our waitress downright seemed annoyed by our existence she was short with us and disinterested. She would be halfway across the room before I could answer for ask for one more drink. 

Food: you come here for the music not for the food. My husbands "Nashville dip" sandwich was fine and nothing he would write home about- we ordered chips and salsa as well - chips were cold and stale and salsa was ok but kind of tasted like a cold soup. I then had the caprese salad which was acceptable. I had two drinks he had one and we had an app and two entrees all said and done it was $63. Not bad but not great for meh food. 

The pineapple cider was legit- I loved that!

All of this to say you're cramped in with people you don't know it's a little warm- the staff is rushing around- it's all kind of a mess to be honest. That said it's an hour and a half show and you're on your way- cool experience if nothing else.

If The Sutler didn't have bottomless mimosas this review would be 3 stars. Yes I said it. The mimosas are the highlight and the reason anyone comes here. No way I would be coming back again and again if not for those delightful orange breakfast drinks. Ok, the free biscuits are good too and there is live music on the weekends. But the food is just ok. It does not blow my mind and by the time I get my food I am quite a few mimosas in because I have been waiting around an hour for a table. Even then I am not blown away and the food is just ok. My brunch companions always tell me I'm crazy but hey I am not impressed. 

But brunch doesn't always have to be impressive. Sometimes you just want to get drunk, listen to country and eat a questionable breakfast on the weekend. That's ok and that is what the Sutler is for. 

Parking is a nightmare but circle for a while and you will find a place in the lot out front.

I was excited when i heard about this place and googled the website. I saw some " magic words like " grass fed beef " onthe menu and local fare...and maybe organic amd thought oh great a safe place to eat. The decor is adorable! Things spiraled down hill for me when our sweet server knew very little about the food's prep or whether or not any of the meat on the menu was local. I have learned to ask certain questions when i go out to establishments that boast local fresh fair. None of the meat was local. As usual i found it odd that the server had to go ask to find out basic info about food origin...Indiana..i read the website and found it is mostly veggies tht were local...i stopped asking questions i was making my friends uncomfortable . We all ordered burger..they were somewhat tasty..bun was dry..house hips were no thrill...but kale and brown rice side was original and tasty..they were setting up for a show so i think our server couldnt count on any of the other people i saw near our table but not offering help. Overal not a place i will be burning to revisit for some reason i was the only person to recieve ice less water in a suspect glass..none of us got straws and when we requested one the server was a little to handsy with it..so it went unused. All this too say..worth one visit but not two and the local fare was either misleading or the servers needed to be trained better to support the unique claims the restaurant made or to clarify what is worth bragging about.

For me this place rocks country! Three levels of bands and bars (a different band on each level). The roof top is a nice view of Broadway and downtown Nashville ... Fun to relax and enjoy some loud country music!

Has a wonderful time at the Bluebird. The staff was very helpful, the music was enjoyable.

It is a small place, so get reservations early and expect it to be crowded. 

I love the vibe, so much better than anyplace on Lower Broadway, it is like an acoustic set for writers rather than cover bands playing so loud you cannot tell if they are good or not.

Late night, it's hard to find food options, so we headed to Paradise Park Trailer Resort.  We tried the chicken fingers (Ok) and the frito pie (don't get the frito pie).  The live music is worth visiting, but the food is just fair.  If back in Nashville, I'd probably skip this spot.

Too hip for my trip.  I've been craving a cool music place on this side of town since moving here 7 years ago... and sometimes the music IS cool here, but nothing to rave over.  .    I prefer places where i don't have to float a second home mortgage to have drinks and a nice meal.   But I'm not giving up on this place.....I'll continue to frequent for a drink or too and see if i like it more.  OH....and please Fox....don't turn this into another 'writer's night' music place......Nashville has enough of those for eternity.  But DO pull in some cool, independent, rock and roll acoustic females.....there are a bunch out there if you look.
Tootsie's is historic, so I made sure I went by.  After a couple of​ days all of these places somewhat blend together.  No complaints.  Neat place.  Upstairs was great.

Gotta say I was pretty bummed to give this place one star. I would definitely NOT RECOMMEND this business to family and friends.

Well I stopped by here because it was recommended by some people that live in the area. A total wash.
We showed up and were very optimistic because you can tell from the street that they have an awesome rooftop bar. And as a bonus the band that was playing was sounding real good.
Unfortunately I wasn't able to get ANY service. The staff acted like I was invisible. They weren't super busy either. Such a bummer!
For some background information, the building is 3 stories with a bar on each level and a live band on the first and 3rd. I'll include some pics as well. I want to give this place a rating because it was cool being there with good music and awesome views but unfortunately I can't since I wasn't actually able to order anything. Poor showing all around.

So. Very. Crowded. Do yourself a favor and get to the rooftop as soon as you can...for air! Music was good, drinks were quick, but overall not for those wanting to relax and enjoy anything other than pushing crowds and drink slamming.
Colleen told me to say she is a great server and I did because she is

We went here for a friends birthday dinner and it was the worst dining experience I have ever had. First of all we had a large party, so we made a reservation. After waiting for almost an hour after our reservation time we were seated at a large booth. They had placed 13 table settings around the booth. There was absolutely no way 13 people could fit even sitting shoulder to shoulder. After being told, very rudely, that they were trying to find stools for us but there were none. Someone from our party went to the bar and took stools from people who were leaving and brought them over. 

The manager offered to comp appetizers since we waited so long even though we had a reservation. Which seemed nice at the time, but doesn't make up for the rest of the experience. 

Next, after the food finally came out one girl was missing her food. My sandwich and soup came out ice cold and I had to ask for it to be heated again. 

When it came time to pay the checks, not only did they not split them correctly (one guy had to pay for all of our bottles of wine we ordered for the whole table), but the waitress actually yelled at the person who's birthday it was. Apparently there was a HUGE misunderstanding with what he said and she was very insulted. But there is absolutely no reason to ever yell or be rude to a customer, and he didn't even mean anything rude at all!

I had had it at that point and went and to speak to the manger. She said she was thankful I spoke up and she would go do something and she disappeared. But I don't think she ever actually did anything and my friend wasn't apologized to for being yelled at.

Like I said this was the worst dining experience I have ever had. All of the staff were rude and acted like they were better than everyone else except for one woman. I would not recommend this place to anyone.

Definitely not worth the hype.  Worst Management and Customer Service I have seen. 

On a Sunday, my 3 friends and I arrived at 5:40 and waited in line for the 8:00 show.  When we arrived, the staff assured my friends and I and several people behind us that we would definitely make it into the show.  On numerous times, the staff came out to assure my friends and people behind us that we would definitely make the show.  Their assurances were the reason why we took the time to wait for the show.  However, once it came time to get into the show, and after over a 2 hr wait, that was not the case.  The "bouncer" told us that only 1 person could get in from our group because they "ran out of seating."  We were the first group to get turned away.  

Suggestion: why not give everyone in line a ticket so people do not have to mindlessly wait?!  There were so many people who did not wait in line but still got through the door.  

The "bounder" told us that he could let us in to take pictures and purchase merchandise.  So we waited.  From the door, we could hear the stand-up comedian.  I'm sorry, but isn't the Bluebird Cafe known for its music and not comedy?!  When the first act started, we could hear the music from the door the music was anti-climatic.  We were not impressed.  That's why we decided to not stick around even though we could hear the music outside the door.   

After talking to my uber and lyft drivers about the Bluebird Cafe, they were not excited about the experience, I should have been warned about the experience.  They specifically said that Bluebird Cafe was only hyped up due to the show, but it's not worth the wait.
Loud and fun. Crowded in its peak times and a blast. Terrific live music. I couldn't do it every night, but love to go on occasion.

I love what they've done with the place. Cool stage featuring live music, shoes hanging from the ceiling on your way downstairs to the bathroom. There is even a cool speakeasy bar downstairs. My husband remembered going to a pool hall down there years ago. The drinks were good. I really enjoyed my watermelon drink served in a solo cup. 
The food to me was rich and heavy. The fried pickles were very good, but beware they include fried lemons, okra, a bunch of filler. I actually preferred the fried okra best. Their pickles were a bit too spicy for me. My husband and any man on the planet would love the heat of those things and the spicy dipping sauce, too. So you can tweek the dish if you want to omit lemons or whatever. I seriously would ask for more okra next time. Those things were very tasty!
Moving on to main dishes, my husband and I split the burger and brussel sprout hash. The burger was served sitting in a cheese soup. It was a bit bizarre and made for a super messy eating experience, but it did taste good. I mean, you slap some melted cheese on anything it's good, right!? The burger itself was ok and the bun was massive. It was like some thick, hard brioche bun. It was ok.
The Brussel sprout hash was quite misleading and disappointing. As you can tell from my picture, it's a pile of mashed potatoes with some roasted brussel sprout flakes on top and a ton of those crunchy fried onions. While tasty, it was sodium overload and not what I was hoping for. I'd rename it potato casserole. 
Overall, there wasn't a healthy option on the menu and only one pseudo salad. Need salads, people!! I'd go back knowing it's more of a drinking, live entertainment type place. Not somewhere I'd recommend as a dining destination.

My brother was in town for a few days so I made a reservation for him, my boyfriend, and myself on a Monday evening. Parking in the area wasn't too clear, but we were able to park out front without any issues (the street signs say valet during the week however, when I asked the host he said they no longer had valet). There weren't too many people inside so we were able to get seated right away. 

Service was good, our waitress came by just enough to make sure everything was going smoothly and tasted okay. The boys ordered hamburgers, I ordered the meatloaf. The meatloaf portion I received was generous, 2 large slices. It came with green beans and mashed potatoes- I would have liked to see a little more potatoes though. The boys said their burgers were good, and they definitely looked delicious. I do wish they had more menu options, it just seemed a little limited. 

Overall the ambiance was nice (there's a ton of seating so if busy I could see it getting pretty loud) and the food and service was good. More clear instructions on parking as well as a larger menu would boost the stars!

RIDICULOUSLY OVER-RATED! We stopped into this place on a Friday night and it was packed to the brim. I MEAN.. CLAUSTROPHOBIC PACKED. I was afraid Id get trampled. Getting a drink was next to impossible and that was a problem because it was at least 95 degrees in the pace because of all the people. I waited for a half hour to get a drink before I just gave up. The band the night we were there seemed fun, but I just wanted to leave because I was really hot and really thirsty. Trying to leave was equally as hard because the front area is soo packed with people listening to the band. There needs to be more structure. Its a fire hazard FOR SURE.  Yes.. this place is famous because a bunch of famous people have played/hung out there. Well.. they are not there now and I dont understand why you would want to smash yourself into this tiny and dirty place. Sorry Tootsie's... im not a fan.
Good music and fun rooftop area. 2 bands playing during the day. One upstairs and one down. Good scene during the day, not so crazy as the nighttime

I've been coming to this bar for years (10) it's my favorite bar downtown.. however... I don't like how they have moved the stage bc it makes it hard to get into the bar.. and it was just far too crowded. Maybe we were there at "prime time" but my group stayed for 1 drink and left

I don't think I've ever had so much fun at a prime tourist location as I had for several hours at Tootsie's. A true tourist mecca, if you're not having fun here you might as well get out of Nashville. It's an institution, a legend, and a true good time. This place has three levels and each level seems to bring a different vibe and attitude of crazy - in a good way. By the time we hit the third floor it was an all-out party on a Sunday at about 2pm. Highly recommend.
Tried to come just now and you are closed early......HUGE MISTAKE! This was the worst idea you had all night.

Dream Girl and I dropped in on a Saturday night, which we knew might be a mistake, and in a way it was. The place was so noisy that we planned to move on, but the hostess told us we could go upstairs. Then she said that upstairs was only if you "knew someone", but we went on up anyway.

Service there was slow though there were few customers when we arrived. It filled up and we saw several orders returned as they weren't right. My Manhattan was first made with Scotch and returned. The second one was just boubon and water. I just kept it as that's an OK drink for me, but it seems strange that a place like that doesn't know how to make a Manhattan.

The food, when it arrived, was good. I had the Baked Eggs Southern Style and DG had a cheeseburger. We ate it all and were filled up.

It's hard to rate this place, but I gave it 4 stars for its excellent renovation and the history. Food is fine, but service - at least upstairs on the balcony - is 2 stars. The noise seems to be what new restaurants and their customers want, but conversation is tough. The mezzanine was quieter espeially back by the wall, so we were OK in that department. We enjoyed the videos with music from the past.

I was in that building many times as a boy when it was Woolworth's. The tuna salad sandwiches for 35 cents and a nickel Coke were excellent!

It is a Nashville classic but... Although they usually have a couple of great bands playing, you are definitely going to pay the price for sitting there.  The drinks are definitely expensive and can require some effort to get if they are busy.  On that note, understand that it can get VERY crowded in there and you have to work your way through the crowd to move from area to area.  The rooftop is nice if it is a nice day and you can get a good view of Broadway, which can make for some fun people watching.  Of course people always want to go there when they come to visit, but we generally tell them to go have one drink and then move on to some of the less touristy places.

What a cool unique place hidden in a strip mall. I would read about the history before coming here. It's a must do in Nashville. If you can't get tickets online get here super early. The show started at 6:30 on a Saturday, doors opened at 5:30 and I got there at 3 and was 8th in line. Only the first 12 people to wait are pretty much guaranteed in. But it's worth sticking around for no shows. For the late show it seems like you only have to be there at 7 for the 9 show to get in. There were people in line there since 12:30 which seemed a bit much. The show was free with a $10 food or drink purchase. All the food looked really good and I got the queso and chips with a hot choc with baileys! Perfect for a cold day. The setting is very intimate and special with almost every seat in there being a good one. If you can't get in I suggest still visiting it when the doors open and running inside to get some merch!

Love love love this famous bar! The only downside is that it's very squishy inside - it's not that small but so many people go in that it's almost hard to move around. I love that everything inside and out is purple, it's so fun and festive. I actually visited on the day of NYE so it was decorated with tons and tons of purple balloons. The drinks are reasonably priced and no different than any of the surrounding bars. They are nothing special and come in plastic cups. They do have a rooftop which I didn't go up to because it was freezing outside when I went. I believe they have three floors in total. They also have live music playing all the time and the bartenders are really friendly. Located on Broadway in the middle of everything! The line is always super long at night so get there early or plan to wait awhile.

We came on a Tuesday night for Lightning 100's beer, bands, and bingo. The green room was pretty deserted when we got there a bit early, but people trickled in as the night went on. They had a $3 leinenkugel special and a $5 blue chair bay rum special. So not bad prices for the promoted drinks, but I didn't look at the other options. Our server was attentive and made sure we had what we needed, but if it weren't for the bingo, we probably wouldn't make a habit of coming here (mostly because we're not really bar people).

Absolutely loved this place! Live Music on all 3 levels, of course bars on each level too! Raw, fun, great drinks. Happy people, perfect gathering place to catch up, laugh and people watch. This is Nashville at its best

The BEST place for live music, which also has a awesome rooftop to see Broadway!  The view is fantastic. We heard an awesome local band who took customers requests (for a tip). Their talent was very impressive and gave Tootsie's a great vibe! This is a must see in Nashville!

Place looked small from the outside.  But when you walk in, there was more space in the back.  So much space that they had to music going on... one in the front and one in the back.  

I was in the back with my coworkers.  It wasn't too bad.  Had a lot of fun listening to live music, and they were good.

Huge party scene with loud, great music.  The levels and the atmosphere reminded me of the Garment District in the mid 80's - without the smoke and drugs, but with the zoned-out happy people.

Drinks were great, as was service.  

This is the sort of place you need to be in the mood for.  If you are it will be a night to remember!

Sheesh. Waitress was on drugs. Didn't talk for some reason. "Do you guys have White Claw?" "Sometimes..... we run out all of the time" 
Cool. Order more? 
Wait.... Your sign say "A live music joint" Nah.... no live music. Food was actually good. Everything else sucked.

Stopped here with the boo after the Kevin Hart show...this food is seriously some of the freshest and tastiest late night food we've had in a while. I had the Singlewide Burger, he had the chicken tender basket...you can't go wrong with either option, in my opinion.

Reservation process was stressful but relatively easy. The weekend shows go on sale at 8am Monday the week of. I had my calendar set and right at 8am the tickets were released. They went fast! I tried to get a pair of tickets 3 times before they weren't snatched up from me by someone else. All tickets sold out by 8:03 am for the Saturday shows so you have to act fast. They require a deposit of $4 for the free shows. 

On the day of the show, I'll have to admit, it was kind of fun walking by the people waiting in line to get in. Be sure to get there on time or they will give away your reservation! My friend and I were at a 6-top and were seated with a lovely couple, their mother & grandmother. We got lucky to be seated with such nice people and had enjoyable conversation prior to the show starting. Once the show starts, shut yo mouf! They like to have no conversations or whispers while the artists are performing which makes sense as it's all about respecting the artists & their music.

We were fortunate to have four wonderful songwriters the night we went - Jenn Bostic, Sarah Darling, Emily Shackelton and Michael Logen. They would play various tunes citing them being used by professional artists and various movies & TV shows. They are not only all great songwriters but great artists themselves. I believe all of them had CDs they were selling post show. Bluebird is a very small venue which is great because you can hear every word the artists sing and are very close to their circle in the middle of the cafe where the performing happens.

The Bluebird Cafe was one of the best experiences I had throughout my whole trip and I'd do it again next time I'm in Nashville. It also turned out not to be expensive at all. They ask you to spend $7 each (random number) which is easily met by getting a couple of drinks. They had specialty pops like Diet Black Cherry - yum! I heard the food can be skipped so we ate prior to our show. Our server was so nice & beyond attentive. The show run exactly 2 hours on the dot and boy did it fly by! People then hang out to get CDs signed and have little chats with the artists. 

Parking can be rough but check out the secret spots in the back if they aren't any in the main lot. 

One of the artists I saw is now on Rising Star on ABC!

The Bluebird Cafe is a must do for music fans while in Nashville!

Sometimes yelpers just get it wrong... 3.5 stars?? Paradise Park is like having 5 guys or smash burger with a bar and live music in the back & bar. Perhaps it's just Nashville in general, but the musical talent even on a Tuesday afternoon was incredible. 

The burgers are big and juicy -- perhaps a bit on the salty side. But hell, this is supposed to be a fun time with greasy burgers and fries and cheap beer, not gourmet. Would come for a quick bite or a casual night out anytime.

Went to the Sutler for brunch one Sunday morning and it didn't disappoint. We went around 10:00/11:00 AM with a party of 4 and were immediately seated. The inside of the restaurant is very laid back with a country feel. There was a stage with 3 men playing some folksy tunes. Such a great vibe! 

My friends and I were treated to some complimentary biscuits while we looked over the menu. I ordered the BLT with avocado and a side of fruit. I was so happy to get strawberry, pineapple and blueberries vs. apples and melons. They offer bottomless mimosas for $17 and a Bloody Mary bar, but I didn't catch that price. All prices seemed to be very reasonable. Service was a bit slow but overall we still had a good time!

Five stars all the way. 
This place was one of our favorites, and we visited a few times during our week long trip. 
They do get a bit busy, but the crowds were manageable and we were still able to get a table for our group. 
During two of our visits they had the same band both nights in the back, and they were awesome. 
Also had some fun conversations with the back door guy and security guard. 
Overall we had a blast and will be making a trip back.

Exceeded my expectations! We made reservations because it was Labor Day weekend but it still wasn't too crowded. The service was friendly, attentive, and quick. We started with the baked pimento cheese dip which was so addicting! I got the fried chicken which comes with two GIANT pieces. I got one piece with Nashville hot sauce and one plain, which I'm glad that I did because the hot sauce was VERY hot (even compared to other places in Nashville). The breading is the crispiest breading that I've ever had without being burnt at all. The chicken was so moist and juicy and tender that it just fell off the bone when you bit in. It was some of the best fried chicken I have ever had (which is saying a lot after having lived in Louisiana, Alabama, and Georgia). Being at an old soda counter, I felt like I had to get ice cream! So I got a brownie sundae which was pretty standard. They also had unique cocktails and local beers. We loved the historical aspect too. It is in a old department store soda counter where there were Civil Rights Movement sit ins.

We're having an amazing brunch here right now. My friends hot chicken biscuit sandwich is delicious. My breakfast taco's are perfect and my boyfriends waffles are light n' fluffy. The waitstaff has been extremely nice, funny and friendly and the overall vibe is excellent. 

We're looking forward to coming back and checking out some of their live music. Great coffee and home fries too.

What a great musical experience! The musicians we saw were fabulous. They told stories that took everything to an intimate level. Staff was just OK and the food was not great at all. All of our food came cold. I understand you attend the restaurant for the music, but cmon! Cold food? That's the only reason I give it 4/5 stars.

Our second visit to the Bluebird Cafe was in October, 2013. The first time we tried this place, we couldn't get in after standing outside in the rain for hours.  This time we showed up REALLY early (sometime after 4pm) and waited in line (we were 1st in line this time) for the 6pm show. We didn't go online to get tickets because you really need to do that on Mondays from what I understand...and they sell out super fast due to limited number of seats.

But, this time we actually were able to get inside. we ate, drank, and enjoyed the "in the round" music. It was very enjoyable. The food was "okay"...nothing great and ditto on the drinks. But, we had fun and enjoyed our PACKED (yes, it was crammed inside) show.

For people who are coming in from out of town (like ourselves), expect to stand in line outside in whatever type of weather it happens to be that evening, and if you are lucky enough to get inside for a show, then plan to be packed in every seat. However, the staff handles the capacity pretty well once you're inside.

I still feel that the owners and staff could do so much more to make the events more enjoyable and less stressful for the customers. They need to get on top of their notoriety that the Nashville show has given them and get some help with crowds.

I'm glad we were finally able to get inside and see a show!

Stumbled here on a Thursday night around 12am and the place was still jumping. The bartenders were fast and courteous, huge dance floor and live band that played an eclectic mix of music. Dare I say, I don't even care for country music, and even I had a good time.
