There is also an upstairs if you want to sit and people watch the drunken patrons below. There were 9 people in our party and we all had a really good time.

Room had weird smell. Had to open windows to get rid of deodorizer smell.  Breakfast/ restaurant was just a closed off dark and dingy conference room. But the bar was very good. Comfortable seating good food and snacks!

I was a little scared to check in here after reading some of the reviews but good news y'all: the place has been renovated and is nice now. It is located in a beautiful area set off from everything which worked for me. 
The only complaint I have is the doors need soundproofing - I could hear the light bulbs in the hall! 
My room was newly redecorated and had everything you would want in a room. Nice comfy bed, big TV, etc etc. I didn't spend much time in it because I was here on business and we were out and about most of the time.
I dined in the bar area and enjoyed some chicken fingers and waffle, peach cobbler, drinks, and also had the breakfast buffet in the restaurant and that was nice.
Overall, a very nice property, friendly staff and I would stay here again.
Four stars only because of the door situation.
Bouncers are rude and racist.  There are plenty of other bars to give your patronage to than this place.

This place has the best sausage in town. Great flavor and a crisp skin. The rest of the menu is good too. The singer on Friday nights, sets a good atmosphere. The beer is cold. I recommend stopping by this place for the food and atmosphere. Get a combo plate so you can try it all!

This place is a little too old and used to be four stars. Spending four nights here. After night one, I paid to upgrade to a suite on the third floor. Much cleaner and quieter. I can't hear my neighbors coughing and chatting at 1am anymore. It's pretty worn down and it needs an overhaul, so don't expect much and you'll be fine. No sign of bed bugs, just generally "been around for awhile". That all said, the staff is tops! They act 5 star and have been accommodating and professional; which makes up for an 1990's place on the cheap.
Not really much to write about here just stopped in for a drink while walking around town and the use the restrooms, the music wasn't too bad
Went during the day to enjoy nice weather on the balcony. They had a good live band playing. I would probably only come during the day if it's nice to enjoy the outdoors!

My husband and I stopped here on a Thursday afternoon to get something to eat. The food was amazing and the service was great!  This is a perfect stop for live music if you don't want the crowds of the big name bars on Broadway.  To top it off, they have happy hour M-Thurs. $3 domestic bottles and 1/2 appetizers. I highly recommend the meatballs.  Delish!
Place was pretty legit differently stick to broadway street for chill hip hop music and dancing, this place was awesome

This place was fun!  We were here celebrating a friends 40th bday. We stopped here our last day in town in the afternoon and a girl was the laying. I bought her cd and both he and the guitar player sounded great and were friendly :))

This was one of the cleaner, most comfortable bars on the block. 

It is dark in there, which keeps it much cooler than the sweltering heat outside. 

The live music was better than some of the local competitors and the drink prices were comparable. 

This place is probably closer to 3.5 stars.

Burgers were great, sriracha mayo was amazing, the little guitar they served my two year olds fish sticks on was awesome and staff was super friendly. Appetizer was cold but I still enjoyed it. Food came out quick. Valet guy was incredibly nice, should have caught his name.

Excellent hotel!  Very friendly service, clean environment, fast service. Room was very clean and housekeeping was friendly. Great value for the money spent on the room. Convenient for commuting to downtown. Less than $20 can ride from downtown

I was here for CMA fest over the past week and spend quite a few hours in here a few different days. We had Jackie as our server and let me tell you she was OUTSTANDING!! The food was decent but the service was incredible. :)

Some of the nicest staff in the Starwood family of hotels. I have stayed in this location on several trips to Nashville and they never fail. I wanted to stay an additional day this trip and use some of my SPG points. They had no more rooms on the club floor that I am used to, but they happily offered me a deluxe room on another floor and still gave me club access with me even asking along with comps for the bar and dinner. Overall great experience. Had some noisy neighbors on this floor, but that's what happens on a Saturday night in Nashville!

I wanted to not like this place, knowing that it was the tourist place on the main drag with the biggest stage and a huge dance floor. But this was my favorite stop on my whole trip! At first it was pretty overwhelming. But a few tequila shots and dance moves later and I was hooked. I went here a few times on my trip, and each time they had a great band that played a variety of popular music. The crowd was super friendly and fun and there was never a wait for the bathroom. Combine that with decently-priced drinks and you've got yourself a good time!

Let me just start by saying our waiter Allen was AMAZING! He was very nice and was always there when we needed him. And he had only been there for 4 days! We've never been to hard rock and let me tell you it was great and we will be returning!
Great waitstaff! Very friendly & attentive! Loved the entertainment!! Nice place to get out of the sun & enjoy an adult beverage!

I love the comments about it being a  dive bar that is smoke filled and the music is too loud. Well, yeah and if that is not what you are looking for, you will not love this place. It does have a great space for live music, the bartenders are great and I can't say I have ever had a bad time here.

Really awesome spot with GREAT booze and great music. The have different flavors of sip-able moonshines. I personally loved the blackberry moonshine - it was delicious -- it tasted like a very, very strong cocktail. The bartender on the night I visited (Friday, July 29) was awesome. She was friendly and made great suggestions. She talked to us casually and really seemed like she was having a fun night at work. I would definitely return to this bar on future trips to Nashville.

Freaking love this place. Always a good band, a pretty mixed crowd age-wise, great drinks, and a cool interior. Lot of wood and antlers, and the "moonshine" list is awesome. It's a nice break from the douche bag spots scattered down Broadway.

I have been to Nashville a number of times ( I live about 2 hours away) and every time we hit the bar scene to listen to music, I seem to gravitate here for a few hours.  Why, because they country musicians and the talent.

It is relatively small narrow bar, similar to many on the strip.   No cover charge and bands will come around with a tip bucket since they play for free, which is common along the strip. 

They serve no food, only mixed drinks and beer.  Prices are about normal.  Two Jack and cokes and a beer (no draught, only bottles) came to about 18 dollars.  There are maybe 4-6 tables and seating along with wall and the bar.  There was a small area upstairs in the back, which I did not go up and see.  It was crowded on Saturday afternoon around 6 and we had to stand in the back for about  1/2 hour until bar seats opened up.  Some small area for dancing... everyone was friendly and no "rough stuff" so brining your date is safe .... Just get some cowboy boots... there are numerous stores to get the boots and hats to be a real Nashville native 

Waitresses were friendly and fast.  They also sell a number of souvenir T-Shirts with the bars logo and various slogans; which cost 20 each.  Great place to wet your whistle, cool down and listen to some great country music.  For what the venue is and comparing it to others on Broadway I would give it a 4 or a 3.... A three, only because they could put in many more stools along the wall land the back.

The stage is one of my fav bars in downtown nashville. I'm not a fan of country music. There is only a few bars downtown that play other music than country. The stage is one of them. The people here range from young to old. Monday-Sunday the place is crowded. Friday,Sat and Sunday are the busiest. Expect to be pushing through a crowd in a shoulder to shoulder atmosphere. This can be avoided if you get to the stage early. The beer here I think ranged from $3.75-$6 bucks I think bud lite was 4.50. 

The bands on the weekend are better than the weekday bands. I have never eaten here just bought drinks. The stage has a full bar with everything. I have gotten patron, beer and I even ordered a quad shot of vodka with 2 cubes and the barmaid got it right. I sat at the bar for a bit and just people watched for a bit and I saw a lot of guys scoping the place out. I guess they were looking for girls. There were more guys to girls in the place. I prefer a different atmosphere for meeting girls. But the people  that did talk to me were friendly. I do like how there are hand painted custom murals on the walls it is really cool they have willie Nelson to haggard on the wall. I'm not a country guy at all but I knew who was on the wall and that it was a great painting. 

Overall. Great music. But can get crowded on the weekends. Get here early to grab a table. People are friendly. 

PROS:
- great atmosphere 
- full bar good beer selection

CONS:
- gets way to crowded on weekends. Get here early to avoid crowds

Will not stay here again. Working WiFi is a bit of a bare minimum expectation nowadays. I was having WiFi connection issues and was transferred to Sheraton tech support where a nice agent spent 45 minutes trying to troubleshoot with me. That was unsuccessful, and when I called back to ask if I could be moved to a room near the lobby to utilize that internet signal, I was told that the internet outage was a known issue all day and "had been going in and out". If that's so, why did I end up spending time on the phone with tech support? They also did not accommodate my request for a room change to move closer to the part of the building that did have internet. 

I am a frequent business traveler on multiple continents and this is one of the worst customer service experiences I've encountered, mostly due to me wasting time trying to resolve something they already knew about. I ended up leaving to go to a Hilton and am happily eating a Hilton Doubletree cookie and will turn to my work now to make up for all the time I lost to this issue. Hooray for working WiFi.

Always packed. It's become a staple of downtown honkytonks...basically, you have to go here if you're bar hopping in town. Usually a good band, though sometimes there's a miss, but never had a bad time here. As a local, it's really fun going here just to watch the tourists drink and dance. LOL

Went for the weekend, second time there.  First time was great and we loved it.  Terrible service this time.  No towels at the pool, everyone had to keep asking them to bring some out.  No one comes out to the pool area to take drink orders - they are losing ALOT of $ there.  Many people were complaining.  Went to the restaurant to get beverages, restaurant was empty and staff was in the kitchen chatting.  Waited 10 minutes for someone to come out.  Another couple got tired of waiting and left.  Friday they repaved the parking lot and there was nowhere to park.  We asked and were told to park in the back BEHIND the employee entrance, quite a walk.  Restaurant opens at 11:00 for a few hours then they close until later in the day.  Bedding and pillows are HORRIBLE. We each had 2 flat pancake pillows and could have used 2 more each.  Sheets are so stiff they weren't even comfortable.  There was a piece of toilet paper under the sink from the prior guests and still there when we left.  After housekeeping changed the sheets, they were nice enough to leave the used pillowcases on our couch for us.  They do have balconies so you can sit outside if you wish.  We will stay somewhere else next time.
The new owners replaced American hard working Veterans with illegal immigrants!

Went here after a work seminar. ...they had Nashville hot chicken sandwich on the menu..
Hot chicken, hush puppies,  and a few Yazoo DosPerros. ...nice..
The music was super loud, so no conversation possible,  but the band covered some decent tunes.. :-)

I went to see a famous musician here, during the Songwriter's festival and I have to say, it was not the best place to enjoy music.
Whether it was the line outside, the way they take the tickets, the way they herd you in and everyone fights for a seat.....
Nah........  I didn't like this venue, in fact, I left early.

I wouldn't go back. I would avoid this place for watching performers.
Great bar!  The night we were there Jared Gray played.  He and his band were fantastic.  Great crowd, easy access to bartenders and others selling beer.  Everyone dances and has a good time.

This is a very cool place. It's in east Nashville but its not to hipster. It's got tons of space and plenty to do. While I was there we played pool, darts, and some awesome game called drunk Jenga. Very worth checking out.

This place is unbelievable on a Monday. I'm an out of towner and this place was recommended by my musician host. I loved it!! Great music, dancing and just plain fun. Drinks we're not expensive and the bartenders were attentive despite how busy it was. I Definitely would go there again.
Stop in to say you went to the bars on broadway in Nashville, but there are better places to see live music and have a few drinks. Most people in Nashville will tell you the same.

Nice music venue. It can get a bit too overcrowded which for me takes some of the fun away. They have a full bar with awesome beer choices. The prices are nice too. I've never paid more than 10 dollars to come inside and that's a plus for me. I go to the monthly Boom Bap party and I always have a great time. Be careful at the bar because the bathroom is tiny and almost always occupied. Ha! Any party here, I would most definitely go.

Another awesome bar in Nashville, with great music....very busy but worth checking out.  Memorabilia everywhere and cool to listen to some talented live music.  Friendly service....didn't eat just had drinks.

I love Nashville, we'll go ahead and get that out of the way right now. 

This hotel is one of the reasons I love Nashville so much. First, it smells so good. What is that? I need it. 

Second, the rooms are huge, have balconies and allow my dogs for free (well, with a $75 cleaning fee). The parking is free, the room service is top notch and management will bend over backward to make you happy. 

There is no other place you should stay in Nashville, this place takes the cake. Hands. Down.

We went bar hopping in Nashville, and made a pit stop here. 

The music was great, as were the drinks and the people. The rooftop patio is awesome and the weather was perfect so I very much loved that! 

Unfortunately everything closes at 2:00 in Nashville so the night ended pretty quickly considering we got to Broadway around 12:30.

Great artist here, left a Paul Simon T-shirt and they saved it for us!!!
Great people highly recommend and not shoulder to shoulder!!!
Pretty good meal. Nothing spectacular but nothing bad either.

Always another good bar spot for Nashville! I haven't run into one that I don't like. Only came during the night time hours for entertainment and for drinks. I always enjoy the bands that are here downtown, no matter which bar you are in. This one is no exception to the norm. Definitely make a stop in here, at least for a drink and to listen to one of the many bands that perform here.
Best bruschetta I've had anywhere! My cousin and I always make it a point to hit up the Hard Rock in every city. Staff was very friendly. Great location!

Dive Bars thy name is Home.

Meaning, like many cool dive bars I would move in and live in this place except for one major, glaring, awful, horrific issue with The 5 Spot:  cigarette smoke.

I love all things hipster (GQ magazine once referred to The 5 spot as "Nashville's Best Hipster Meat Market") I love all things rock and roll and seedy and cool and stuff but for the love I hate cigarettes and cigarette smoking.  It's nasty.  It smells nasty.  It causes birth defects and cancer and a host of other dark afflictions and at The 5 Spot you can still smoke inside meaning the rest of us are stuck sucking in the cloud of noxious chemicals while you smokers get your high.  Ewwwwwww.

Otherwise welcome to a very cool place!  I don't watch the TV show Nashville but I heard that The 5 Spot is featured a lot.  In the world of reality there have been some great acts that have received their start here in the past decade that they have been operating, and in homage to older, golden days gone by there are some pretty neat vinyl albums scattered across the walls.  (There is also a massive Elvis mural in the ladies bathroom that you don't want to miss).

The 5 Spot doesn't just host up and coming musical acts.  It also hosts fun dance parties (images of my friend Matt slamming a pretend sledgehammer down to Peter Gabriel's "Sledgehammer" on the dance floor come to mind) that are themed such as Monday 50s and 60s groove night and the night I went which was Friday 80s dance party along with popular cover acts like a recent Sunday night's tribute to the 1973 Watkins Glen summer concert that had tons of Dead songs, Allman Bros songs and of course tunes from The Band.  Standing up on the bar stool (choking in ciggy smoke) and singing "The Weight" with fellow bar patrons made for a really great Sunday night in Nashville.  My bar stool neighbor that night was from NYC and works in the music industry doing stuff for bands like Emerson, Lake and Palmer.  The kinds of people you will find in The 5 Spot will range a huge gamut from young to old.  A very cool, mixed crowd.

The Jameson on the rocks I ordered was the biggest one I've ever held thanks to the massive cocktail glass it was in and it was a cheap price.  They have great local beers on tap that sometimes run on awesome happy hours, plus loads of ice cold beer in bottles in their coolers.  You honestly can't go wrong here, just remember to bring your gas mask for those times when it gets crowded and everybody is lighting up.
Was here on July 4th! Live music jamming, beers were flowing! Must see spot if visiting Nashville. Yee Haw!

True to it's name, this part of Nashville definitely does have the Vegas vibe. Confession: I'm not a huge fan of Vegas (sue me). So, given the choice I choose a Vegas that comes with an abundance of cowboy boots, sparkly belt buckles, country music and southern charm. 

A few tips when making your way to The Stage (which was recommended to me not only by Yelp but a crew of locals I met at dinner):

-Prepare yourselves for the crowds, but it's worth it. 
-no cover
-drinks may or may not get sloshed on your getup. Dress comfortably. Nashville is casual.
-It'll take a bit of pushing to find yourself a spot at the bar 
-great sound and you're able to get right up to the stage
-again, no cover, so, rest assured, if you're not a fan - you can pop in and then make your way to the next honky tonk joint on the strip

First, I go to check in, and they've oversold the hotel. Because I'm a gold SPG member, I at least got a room. The hotel also advertises that they have a pool and hot tub, but they are mysteriously "closed for renovation"; however, the water in the hot tub is bubbling and lights are on. Everybody at the hotel was super friendly and my room was very clean.
I went there on a Saturday night and it was fun. It was pretty low key when we arrived (~10pm) but things started to get heated about 1 hour after that. I think I paid $5 for the entrance.

I love Sheraton. Beautiful hotel, well kept and even though it was big enough to get lost in, they have good service! Got a great rate for the night and I love how they offered cheap shuttle service downtown on the hour! Impressed!

We took a stroll down Broadway over the course of the weekend, trying to hit up every bar we passed. For some reason this was place was absolutely packed out. Maybe the band playing was a bit Nashville famous? Not a fan of country music so I couldn't tell you. 
There wasn't a spot at the bar nor a single seat in the house was open. The upstairs was also closed. After our group of 4 split up, standing at different spots at the bar, the one on the side & the main one & unable to grab the attention of a bartender, after 15 minutes, we left.

Great atmosphere. Cheap drinks. Great Band.

We came here on a Friday and had a great time. We started off on the first floor with one of the live bands. They had a lady on the fiddle who was very fun. Later on that night we moved to the 2nd floor and stood by the windows. Prime people watching location.

On the 2nd floor, it was pretty easy to get a drink from the bar and they also have a large dance floor. The band takes requests by tipping in the jar and also the band takes drinks too. Just bring the drink up to the stage and set it down. They will toast to you. 

Great first time here. Def worth checking out.

My brothers and I came to this spot during a guy's trip.  It's a dope spot; HOWEVER, the food is not good.  Grant it, I wasn't expecting much but sheesh! On the brighter side, our bartender was great!  She definitely made up for the horrible food.  Maybe we came on an off night.  DJ is decent and the rooftop is great.  Overall, not too bad.....just don't order food.
Elevators suck, breakfast food is not good. Staff was great, accommodating, friendly and willing to help!
Had the hickory barbecue bacon burger and it was very good. Fries were seasoned nicely. Wife had a combo appetizer and her wings were great. Service was average or I would give it 5 stars.

Sweet Tea shine with Lemonade was amazing. As was the coffee shine. Brandon and Jennifer were such awesome bartenders. Left with a a new fave ball cap. Loved the chandeliers too. Great place. Must check it out!

A great dive bar for all the degenerates.
Pool tables, darts, mexican food, flatscreen TVs with DirecTV, and live music and DJs.
Staff is friendly, but they're not gonna put up with anyone being a jerk, either. I like that.
Only things I would like to see improvement with is parking, it's kinda rough, and making some DJs who play there that think the people outside the building need to hear them turn down the volume just a little bit. Gets frustrating to have to scream at each other and say "WHAT?!" back and forth all night at the bar to your buddy sitting on the barstool directly beside you.
Other than that, this is my number one watering hole.

I first walked in at 4pm on a Sunday afternoon and there was literally no one on the first floor(no band, no guest, and a bartender drinking a beer) we went up to the second floor and no one was there, the third floor had a good amount of people but there was no bartender.... We waited a little and still no one came. It was really awkward

If you've not been to The Judge's Vinegarroon in a while, the new management has made a lot of changes, and they are not for the better.  The first thing you'll notice is that their parking lot is chained off.  There is no parking, so come on foot.  You know those amazing chunky, fresh, hand cut french fries they used to serve?  Those have been replaced with thin shoestring frozen fries that aren't nearly as good as McDonald's.  The fried corn on the cob was chewy and cut on the diagonal, which made it pretty, but really hard to hold.  Prices have been substantially raised.  The regular sauce has also been changed.  It's now thin and runny, but I thought the flavor was pretty good.  Fortunately, the beef brisket is pretty much unchanged, and it's still really good.  Unless the new management addresses these unwelcome changes, I wouldn't recommend going here, unless you want to pick up an order of brisket to go.

I like it here. There isn't anything that stands out but it's reminiscent of my early 20's. I love live music and I'd say anything goes but I'm not a huge country fan (yea, I know it's Nashville). I like the diversity here and the staff might be indifferent but I've never thought them to be rude. The patrons are pretty relaxed and clearly out to enjoy themselves. The booze is pretty standard and at a place like this I'm fine with that. It's not fancy or super hipster and it's not "dirty" but it's not spotless either. I love how the customers vary depending on the band. Overall, I'm not a regular but I enjoy stopping in to check out the atmosphere for the night.
Fun time. Stopped in for a quick drink. The bartenders were a lot of fun to talk to. I would go back. next time for dinner.

Do not stay here! Absolutely horrible customer service! This was my second time staying, both for conferences, and although I wasn't impressed with my first visit, the second was awful. All in all, the hotel staff seemed unconcerned about helping guests. The front desk staff treated me as if I was bothering them. After a long day, I returned to my room to find it freezing and no way to fix it. Turning on the heat, made colder gusts of air come out. Fortunately, maintenance responded within 5 minutes even though it was after 11pm but the maintenance guy's comments made me somewhat uncomfortable. But the problem was fixed. Unfortunately the next morning and all throughout the day, I had the opposite problem--I could not stop the heat and my room temperature was 90+ degrees. I called the front desk three times between 12 and 5pm, each time I was told someone would be up. No one came and when I returned to my room on a break before dinner, it was 94. I called the desk and again no one came. I went to the front desk and spoke with the manager who was less than helpful and unconcerned about the inconvenience I experienced. He spoke disrespectfully to me and acted as if I was over-reacting. He said that maintenance was heading up to fix it but did not acknowledge my dissatisfaction or offer to fix it. Only after I said that the hotel had failed me did he ask how he could fix it. He offered to sign me up for the Rewards program of which I was already a member. How does this make things right?!

This was a great hotel and I'm glad we stayed here. We were in town for Yelp Elite spring break and decided to stay here because the downtown rates were crazy expensive. We got a rate of $139 per night before taxes, with the Yelp rate. 

Pros: pool (looked beautiful but we didn't use it), big and nice rooms, lovely lobby. They also have a 24-hour indoor pool and hot tub. 

When we arrived around 330pm, our room was not ready, so the hotel gave us two free appetizer vouchers. 

Cons: I really would have liked at least 1 quick-service place or a place to buy juice or essentials. We mostly ate snack bars for breakfast and headed downtown for lunch and dinner. 

I would definitely stay here again if in the area, it was convenient enough to take Lyft or Uber everywhere.

This was my first visit to a Hard Rock Cafe and had my doubts, but I was very, very surprised at how good the service and food was. It was my sons choice and we had a great time! Remember this is a very loud very busy place to dine! If you are wanting to kick back and relax this is not the type of restaurant for you! But if loud music and good food are go! My son had the cauliflower burger and raves about it still! While In Nashville I wanted to try Nashville Hot Chicken and this one was flavorful and not to hot! Aleta our server was great and a big shout out to Sam "Stone" for stopping by twice and not only checking on us, but talking to us and making us feel welcome!!!
Had a good time here everyone friendly good music and cold beer. Multiple floors with different bands and a nice roof top with nice view and more music .. A must if ur ever in Nashville

Have been here several times always good and good value for the money , but this last time 8-23-14 was very disappointed . The special that was 3 meat choice for 10.00 with large portions went down to 2 meat choice  @ 10.00 and small portions ?? What's wrong with that pic ? Was very disappointed , we won't be back ...
Waited more than 5 minutes for service at the bar, was ignored by two different people, and they weren't even busy!

This is a really cool bar. The bartender was nice and did a great job. She was pretty busy but that did not stop her from speaking to people and getting drinks promptly.  If you are looking for a great local place this is it. I will be back.

Nice hotel. Attended a conference and it was a host motel. 

Not really near anything other than the airport. 

Have to drive everywhere. 

Room was nice and were remodeled. Flat screen tv etc...  Staff was very attentive and friendly. 

If not attending a conference there, I would prefer to stay closer to Nashville sites / restaurants.

This was a great venue for listening to some great music.  We didn't eat here.  The place got packed, but there was an upstairs that overlooked the band and dancing going on downstairs- great spot and music was fantastic!
Great live music scene! Not a big moonshine fan, but the relaxed atmosphere and prohibition decor were a nice change from the rest of the strip.

We came by here in the middle of the day and started drinking. We intended to do a little bit of bar hopping but, we liked the atmosphere too much to venture too far. We had a couple of beers here, left for dinner, hit another bar around the corner, then decided to come back for a couple more beers. The music was great, I liked the atmosphere of the bar, and the bartender Sarah was very nice and hospitable. 

I definitely would come back if I were to ever head into Downtown Nashville again.
Lovely place to stay. Short Lyft drive to Broadway and Opryland. Pool was beautiful and our room was spacious and had a balcony overlooking pool
Moonshine and music.  And beer.  Great spot, nothing fancy, just a great bar and terrific acts.
Was super excited to see Nashville's Fourth of July fireworks at their rooftop party. But it was not a full viewing of them.  The building obstructed nearly half of the show. Very disappointing.

Nashville is just a fun place to be. The Stage is a lot of fun. Good music, live music, drinks and fun people. The bartenders are quick and the drinks are strong. It's a pretty large venue so is definitely great for bigger groups! I would say this is one of the bars you need to check out when you're in Nashville.
We absolutely love this place!!!!!!!! Great beer, staff and music!!!!! Can't wait to go back!!!

Ok, I must admit after booking this hotel through a third party website I was a bit skeptical. I read the reviews after booking the room...I know, silly me. Anywho, the room was a great rate compared to all other hotels in Nashville...even the two star hotels...so I had to book it! Nevertheless, I read some of the most recent reviews on here and I was fearful that I would get a nasty, outdated, smelly room, and the front desk folks were going to be rude! Omg, y'all...complete opposite! I wish I would have gotten names, but from the beginning the customer service was excellent. I checked in at about 5:45p.m. on 10/26. First, the door greater was very friendly and even offered to carry my bags. Next, the woman that checked me in spoke to me as soon as I walked through the door. Check in was easy, she was helpful with suggestions of things around Nashville since she's a Nashville native (though I didn't need it since I'm a native as well :)), and she was genuinely nice! Again, I was shocked since this is not what I expected. Next, I got on the elevator and headed up to the second floor. The entire time I'm worrying just a bit because I remember reading how nasty the rooms were from several folks. Y'all!!!!! My room was updated and beautiful. Do you hear me?! I totally did a happy dance right there in the hall before I even stepped into the room. 
Now, the only thing I will say that I did not like was the fact that due to the construction, it is a bit of a pain to get to the indoor pool and the gym. It wasn't awful though.
All in all, I don't know, maybe I was just lucky. I was certainly pleasantly surprised by this hotel, and I had to make sure to write a review.
Good times here. Had a couple beers here. There were so many places with all good music, we couldn't decide. So we had a couple beers in each place. lol.

Faith...seriously. Any. Other. Words. 


Best service. Best drinks!!! and she is beautiful

We had lunch here as we were passing through and the staff were extremely accommodating. We had a large party with a lot of kids in it and not only were they friendly but they were also extremely generous with my children. Great beer on tap made from a local brewery wish I could remember what it was called.

We had a great time in here! My fiance and I rolled in around 4:30 PM on a Monday afternoon after I heard one of my favorite songs  being covered by the band playing at the time. They were completely solid and we rolled in where we had a quick beer a piece before heading to Jack's BBQ for dinner. 

The Stage, I assume, has to get crazy crowded during the nights, and I can totally see why. They have plenty of table top seating and bar seating where you can sit and enjoy the music being played by what ever band that is serenading the crowd. Drinks are reasonably priced, and not overkill like a lot of the downtown Nashville strip tries to knock up prices. Not Stage though. 

Bathrooms were clean -- I felt that was worth mentioning. 

Anyway, solid place and would love to return for a night out on the town.

I'm updating my review now because my original review is from four years ago, and a LOT has changed since then. Before it was a solid five stars, but since then, WBS has taken a turn for the worst. The drinks here have always been overpriced, but I tolerated it before because 1) it's downtown, and all the downtown bars are expensive, and 2) the atmosphere, management, and music more than made up for it. However, the prices have still increased, even though they were already too high to begin with. Last night, I ordered a Shiner Bock, and it was $6. SIX DOLLARS for ONE beer. I can go to a bar in another area and get a fancy cocktail for that price. Heck, I can go to the grocery store and get an entire six pack for that.

The management has suffered as well. Four years ago, the bouncer always knew my face and didn't need to ID me every time. Now there's a new bouncer who still sees me nearly every Sunday, yet he still has to ID me every time. I understand that they may have changed their policy since then, so I won't knock them too much for that alone, but the bouncer is still incompetent for another reason. A few weeks ago I went in and used my global entry card instead of my driver's license as my ID. I've done my research, and this is an acceptable form of ID under federal and state law, as it's a photo ID issued by the US government. However, the bouncer would not accept this ID. I explained the above to him, yet he didn't believe me. After about five minutes of arguing (I didn't have my DL on me at the time; I'd left it at home), I called a friend who was inside to come out and help me. She's the wife of one of the band members and sees me nearly every week at WBS, so I figured she could talk him into letting me in. It eventually worked...after another 5-10 minutes. But the bouncer said that I had to use my driver's license next time, or he wouldn't let me in. This guy needs to get retrained on what a valid photo ID is. Now I'm wondering if people without a driver's license can get in with a passport or a state ID. If not, I feel sorry for them.

The bouncer isn't the only incompetent employee here. When I first started going to WBS over four years ago, there was a wonderful bartender there every Sunday named Sarah. She was friendly and prompt at getting my order as soon as she saw me. She was also very attractive, if that matters . She would even come out and dance with me when she wasn't busy. I don't know if she left or got fired, but she hasn't been there for several years now. The current bartenders are just crummy. When I went last night, I sat at the half empty bar for several minutes before getting a morsel of attention from a bartender. I made eye contact with them several times, and they just ignored me completely. Eventually after about ten minutes, one of them finally noticed me and took my order. It seems like they're always in a rush, even when there's only like four people at the bar. When I do finally place my order, I feel like I'm being rushed. WBS seriously needs to hire some competent and friendly bartenders like Sarah was.

The final thing I'll bring up is the band. The only time I come here is on Sunday nights for live music by one of my favorite local bands, Hushpuppy's Daddy. Recently, I heard rumors that this band may lose their gig at WBS. If this happens, I will be very disappointed, as they're the only reason I even go to WBS anymore. They're one of the few bands that plays classic country, rock and roll, jump blues, and oldies music downtown anymore. Walk down Broadway, and you'll mostly just hear 2010s pop country.

Whiskey Bent Saloon, y'all better step your game up. If you fire Hushpuppy's Daddy, I will not be back, even if you do hire more competent staff. The only reason I'm rating you two stars instead of one is because the venue itself is still nice (it's still very spacious with nice hardwood floors and cool decor), and Hushpuppy's Daddy hasn't been fired...yet.
Another music bar on Broadway that had talented musicians. It wasn't too crowded and the bands were great!

Not a super loud and obnoxious bar like the others on Broadway. Love the music here, a little toned down. We were here during the day so things could change of course. There seemed to be more polished music acts. It was one of the few that we stopped into and stayed for the quality music.
If you're on yelp looking for a bar, do not come here. It's not the place for you and you won't like it. Locals only
Just try the Atomic burger medium rare and you will be hooked.  If Alexsis is your server you will have a great experience!

I'm not sure why we went here or why we stuck around. One from our group found this place on Yelp so I'm blaming the other reviewers for taking us here. We showed up on Saturday night and nobody was there. The staff was hanging out around the bar and in the front, with nothing to do. Given our unfamiliarity with the area and hunger, we decided to stay.

As we start to order we are told they were out of mac 'n cheese. Really? Did the staff eat it? Because you have no customers. How does a place like this run out of such an essential side? You don't run out of a dish if no one is eating it. More so they didn't feel like making it. At least half the table would've ordered it and that didn't sit well with us. One of us even joked that we should run to a local store and pick-up some Kraft. We ordered our dinners and drinks. One of us got the The Dirty Brendon that came with brisket filled olive - when she got the drink, the olives were your regular pimento filled olives, no brisket in sight.

My pulled pork sandwich was decent, I heard the brisket was meh. A few people felt sick afterward (me included). Plenty of other restaurants in the area we should've gone to. I recommend you skip this joint.

Our server Mary, who is a newbie, ROCKED IT! 
We had a party of 7 and are demanding.  The manager Faith was also phenomenal... I traveled from St. Louis and expect excellent service and food.  This place did not disappoint. Well done Mary!!

No cover, live band, I'm in! This was probably my favorite bar in downtown Nashville.  The band they had playing was entertaining and diverse in their music selection. There isn't much room to sit or anything but who comes to these places to sit anyways?! The drinks were pretty good and about 10-12/drink so pretty standard. Would absolutely recommend this place to anyone visiting Nashville and I certainly can't wait to return!

Cool dive bar in East Nashville. Went on a Saturday night. $5 cover. Chatted a bit with the door guy, was a friendly Australian. The people here are eclectic. A little bit of everything. No one bothered anyone and just enjoyed themselves.

Food and service was fantastic.  Steak was cooked perfectly and the nachos for an appetizer may have seriously been the best I have ever had.  All of the other restaurants we tried were booked up and needed reservations.  We were happy with only a 15 minute or so wait and then pleasantly surprised by the food.  Good choice if you don't have reservations at another local place.
It's 26 degrees out and this bar refuses to close the door as guests sit in winter coats, hats and gloves. The drinks are overpriced but the current band is incredible.

Well, this started well. The hotel looked nice and our room was clean as well. We stayed 2 nights. 
About 20 minutes into our stay at the hotel on the first night, the power for the whole neighborhood was cut due to weather. Understandable. One can't predict these things and it's something that could happen. The hotel had no generator of any sort, no way to have any light inside the room. No candles or anything of that nature either. So, between 7pm and 4-5am on the next day we basically stood in complete darkness, using our phones as flashlights... Until the phones died too. Not only that, but the air conditioning was obviously not working either. It was miserable. I was, however, prepared to let that go. 

On the following morning, after a long concert the night before, I thought I'd sleep in and check out right before 11 am (the set check out time). I was awaken by knocking on the door and the door suddenly opening. I had the inside latch on, therefore whoever was trying to come in was not able to do so. I jumped up in a panic because I thought I overslept and I was late to check out. I found my watch and, to my surprise, it was only 8:50am. I couldn't go back to sleep since my heart was pounding out of my chest, so I started getting ready and getting my luggage together. It wasn't even an hour later when the knocking on the door continued and someone, once again, attempted to walk in. It was 9:45am, over an hour before the set check out time. At that point, I was quite upset. Why on earth would anyone, housekeeping or otherwise, want to come into my room when I've paid good money to be there until at least 11am... Without being asked to do so?! 

I then packed all my stuff and left. So, I stayed the two nights, of which I sat in the dark on the first, and the next I was interrupted by staff and was not able to rest. I could have slept in my car and probably had a better and more relaxing time. 

Once I returned home, I wrote customer service an email and described my experience. I had to provide a condensed version due to the 1,000 symbol space constraint. It's been almost three weeks since then and I am yet to receive any kind of response. The fact no one contacted me and at least apologized was even worse than the actual experience. 

I used to like Sheraton and would seek the hotels out anywhere I went on vacation. After this experience, I would not pay another penny to stay there. If you have the chance, find somewhere else to go, you probably would have much better time!

Had THE pleasure of stumbling into The Stage during the day while shopping with my boyfriend on Broadway. It was very early on a Sunday (maybe noon) but there was already a fantastic band playing and we sat at the bar.

Bartender was a sweetheart and our beers were cold. What more can you ask for? Also, this place is like a music history museum. Just gorgeous and rich.

My favorite of the places we hit up on Broadway for my bachelorette party.  We heard 3 different bands on the different levels, and each one was great.  I loved the rooftop bar, and the drinks were reasonably priced.  Keep in mind there is no cover, so the bands only make money off teh tips they receive - tip them well and make a song request!  I definitely will be back next time I'm in Nashville.

You can't come to Nashville without experiencing the live music. That would be sacrilege. Jamie W. and I always attend a show at the Grand Ole Opry when we're in town, and on our last visit, we pressed our noses against the window at the Bluebird Cafe. This time, we were determined to find a place on Lower Broadway despite the armies of party-hearty drunkards that stood in our way at the doorways. This one appealed to us the most because there was no cover charge and there was a lot of space where you can get a view of the band (photo: http://bit.ly/2N9liIC).

We ended up on the mezzanine where we could look at all the activity below including all the couples doing the two-step without falling down. This was one of the rare times that we ordered bottles of Bud Light as we swayed to the twangy tunes though they alternated with more urban pop songs to make everyone happy. We went upstairs to find yet another stage of musicians and another bar but with a vista view of Lower Broadway down below (photo: http://bit.ly/2Jeltjt). We ended up hanging out for a couple of hours like we were Nicole and Keith or something.

I booked our summer vacation through Booking.com here . As the hotel is under renovation and they didn't tell the third party we were woken at 7 all week . We would not have booked there had we known about renovations. They blamed third party . Third party said they were not informed. Manager offered us a meal which was ridiculous as we had spent a lot of money staying for a week .third party gave us a 15% discount to make it right as they could . Vacations were meant to relax when you work 60 hour work weeks .

Once our food arrived, they were not too bad but the service was lacking. It took about 45 minutes or more for everyone to get there food. Also, they were running out of sides at 5:00 pm. Certainly not on a list to hit again.

I saw a super star yesterday at the Stage Anna LaPrad is the real deal. At 3 in the afternoon the joint was loaded. Really cold beer and good whisky. All the bands we  saw very very good .As far as playing for tips nobodies putting a gun to their heads to play there. Relax and enjoy!
Loved this place. Went to several places on Broadway and heard the best band and fiddle player here. Wasn't crowded but so much fun.  I will definitely return. Give it a shot!

If I could, I'd give the hotel even more stars for one simple reason: Ashley. Ashley made my stay amazing through her exemplary customer service. She consistently went out of her way to lovingly accomodate all hotel guests; she is customer service at its finest. What a pleasure.

My brother suggested I check this place out on my trip and I'm glad I did!!  The 3rd floor is a cool place with the rooftop bar.   We were there on a weeknight and it was rockin!  Definitely put on your places to go!

For BBQ, you can find much better in Nashville. Everything was oversmoked, from the meats to even the Bloody Mary, to the point of being nearly inedible. The smoke level seemed like a gimmick that ultimately failed. I've had some of the best BBQ in Texas, and let me be clear that this "Texas-style" joint is not anywhere close. The service was slow and at times not present, and the menu was overpriced.

I came here once for Motown Monday night. I wanna go back! It has an interesting mix of demographic here at this dive bar. Doesn't feel like a weird dive though it was lively especially as it got later. Love the throwback music and the fact people actually dance. (Some of it really entertaining. Great people watching here.) you can't beat the happy hour prices! Seemed like a good beer selection too!! The bartenders were on top of it and friendly. Major plus. Didn't try any of the food but I'm assuming that's just like any dive bar food? Maybe next visit. They have something going on almost every night it seems. There was a line out the door as it got later, clearly a popular thing to go to on a Monday night! My friend and I got there early like 9ish, no line and not crowded at all yet. I'll be back! Duh.

We went here to eat on Saturday June 9th at 11:30 am and got seated right away. The restaurant wasn't very busy at all. So didn't think there would be a problem getting waited on. But I was wrong we set down at the table and was looking at our menus and another couple got seated and waited on right away. Then they got their drinks and still nobody waited on us. Plus their waiter walked right by us 4 times and made eye contact with me but nobody ever waited on us. So after 20 to 25 minutes we got up and left. I told the waitress setting there doing nothing as we walked out she lost our business because nobody waited on us. Mind you our menus where still open on the table and we left them there as we left and I told the hostess as we left that we never got waited on and you lost my business. She acted surprised but as we set at our table waiting to get waited on she walked by us 2 times.

I really want to love this place because it is so popular, but I think that is my problem with it.  We had a hard time finding a space where we could really go to just enjoy the band.  I love Nashville for the country music.  The night we were there, the band downstairs was playing a lot of rock n' roll, but upstairs was my problem, the band was playing backstreet boys.  I know the musicians get tipped to play songs, but the terrible music continued, which I hated, because both bands were excellent.  
Our bartenders were great, very attentive and friendly.

I had an absolute BLAST in this outstanding Broadway club during a recent visit to Nashville. The Amanda Daughtry Band kept our group rocking until the early hours with covers that ranged from Garth Brooks to Queen -- and the country band playing the main stage wasn't bad, either. 

The third floor bar may seem like a long walk up, but the open-air patio, great music and spacious dance floor makes it worth the exercise. The beers were a little pricey, and the selection fairly weak, but with music this good, who cares? Hard to imagine a better place in Music City to rock out to great tunes.

I chose this hotel because it was the cheapest on Expedia without being super sketchy. It was definitely a good choice! About 15 minutes from downtown, it's easy to uber or take their shuttle. The shuttle is actually run by a third party so you do need to call the front desk to arrange pick up. It comes to the hotel on the top of the hour and it costs $10 round trip per person or you can pay $15 per person and have unlimited for the day. 

The room was super nice, plush pillows and beds, plenty of space. We had a room with a balcony over looking the pool which was nice. We tried to go down to the pool one night because we thought there was a jacuzzi, but it turns out the small circular pool is actually a children's pool, not a hot tub. They may have a hot tub at their indoor pool, but we didn't go looking for it.

I ordered room service my first night in the hotel. I ordered the chicken piccata and a glass of Riesling. They said it would take 45 minutes or so, but it actually came in about 20 which I was pleased about. It was arranged nicely and came with everything I needed, including a glass of ice water. There is a $7 room service fee FYI that is not annotated on the menu. The chicken was a little salty and not the best I've ever had, but it was decent for room service.

Check in was super easy when I arrived and there's plenty of free parking. This hotel is a great place to stay when you're visiting Nashville!

Stayed here for my recent training in Nashville. My room was closer to the pool elevators, which took some finding. It's a large square, so the more expensive room have balconies or patios facing the courtyard, the less expensive have balconies facing parking lots. Still a decent view. The outdoor pool is open until 9, and there's a nice gazebo and plenty of outdoor seating around. Beautiful. the bar serves food late if you miss the restaurant closing. If you are a Sheraton member you get access to the club on floor 2 for a free breakfast, otherwise, you'll be spending $17 in the restaurant. OUCH. 

My coworkers and I had the privilege of meeting Sarah in sales, who was hosting an appetizer and drinks thing in the lobby. It was awesome, and Sarah is the best around. I would definitely recommend her for your business or private function needs. She recommended all the great places we went while in town, and more that we didn't get to. She's a gem. 

My room was clean, but the maids didn't come the second and third days-weird. clean sheets, fluffy towels, I was happy. Bathroom was spacious, more than enough hangers for my work clothes. The iron worked- a major plus- and my balcony had two chairs and a table for my outdoor needs. 

The shuttle driver was AMAZING. He liked playing trivia with us, and made sure we were to work and to the airport on time. He was a wealth of information and made our stay complete. 

I can't wait to come back. Wi-Fi is free in the lobby, paid in your room unless you are a club member-then it's included.
Hard Rock Cafe Nashville has the best veggie burger in town. Add grilled onions and pepper jack and it's on!

Stop by last night after hearing how nice the place was and was not disappointed. The staff was super nice and attentive to us. Love the chandelier, tables, bar tops  as they all seem to be a good balance in the room!! The whole place seemed way to nice for Broadway but I'm not complaining. Finally a place to listen to music without stepping in who knows what. Wish the best for them, me and my girls will return this weekend!!
Typical.  If you want the typical Hard Rock chain and to get away from Nashville, stop in here.  You won't even remember you are in the Music Capital.

Ah yes, the hotel in which we stayed during our trip to Nashville. It got the job done, but we were left pretty disappointed by our stay. 

It's worth saying first, that this hotel is super pretty. There's a pool and a courtyard that's just lovely, and the lobby is very elegantly decorated. 

Our room was nice too, for the most part. It was clean when we got in, the bed was soft. There wasn't a fridge, which was a bit of a surprise since that's a pretty standard thing, but it wasn't a huge deal.

The issues at this location had to do with the service. It started out with television problems. None of the channels had any volume. Irritating, but alright. Naturally, we called. The person who picked up the phone seemed bothered by the fact that we'd called the desk.... When that is their job? Not quite sure why talking to us was such a big inconvenience. Anyway, they sent someone up to fix it eventually. The volume worked, but then we didn't have any local Nashville channels. Kind of annoying when it's storming and we're trying to make plans, but can't get any weather forecasts or alerts. 

Then, we didn't have a welcome book. You know the one. The one that comes in every hotel room, that tells you about the hotel, what services are available, places to eat nearby, etc. There wasn't one. No big deal. So again, we call the annoyed desk. They were ridiculously condescending and tried to tell us it was on the desk, like I was not in my room staring at the desk as we spoke. I mean, it's a hotel room. It's only so big. And my stuff is all in a suitcase. It's not like it's a quest for the lost ark to search for a damn book. Eventually, the guy on the phone fluffed us off and said "if another book turns up, they'll send it over", because apparently there's a welcome book shortage in Tennessee. We left a note for the maid to ask for one, and like magic, one was on our desk when we came back the next day. 

So much for Southern hospitality, eh?

We were here Labor Day weekend and the band was fantastic.  I'm not a big Country fan but my husband is. However this band made me dance. The bar is not huge but everyone was nice.  Thankfully my husband is good looking bc the women bartenders definitely head more towards the men. :-) the bathrooms could use a deep cleaning. We would definitely go back.

Absolutely terrible. Food is gross. Watch for huge spider webs on the ceiling. The food took over an hour.  If we knew there was one hr wait for food, we would not have stayed. The manager stated our food was only in the system for 26 minutes.  There was no solution just bad food.
One of my favorite Nashville bars!  Great bands and no cover.  Bathrooms are clean too.

Not the service I expect from a sheraton.  Check in was smooth, room was decent,  nothing spectacular.  No fridge.  When we got there we had some issues with the tv, no volume on most channels.  After a conversation with am obviously annoyed front desk clerk they sent someone to the room who then fixed the volume but managed to make all local channels disappear.  Normally not a big deal but as it was a stormy weekend full of weather warnings would've been nice to know about them.  There was no property guide in our room, you know the one with amenities, room service menu,  local attractions, etc.   The same inhospitable front desk clerk told me I must not see it and insisted it was on the desk.  It was not.  He pacified me and did said he'd look around for another one and send it to the room. That did not happen.  Though a note for housekeeping on the first night accompanied by cash and the guide appeared.  All in all pretty property,super comfy beds,    just be advised the staff could use a refresher course in guest services and hospitality.  When I return to the area I'll try the other sheraton in Nashville before trying my luck with this one again.

Front desk staff at Check-In (August 3, around 2:30pm) did not smile, I don't even think they gave us a greeting. Even though we were SPG members and booked directly and VERY early in the year, we were given a ground floor, handicapped room, and no, we couldn't change it. When I told the lady I had a tax-exempt form so I could have federal taxes removed, she said, "it's already been charged to your card". Luckily the manager overheard her and said he could take care of it. But no smile or greeting from him, and he made it seem like a chore. The hotel is EXTREMELY outdated, and has a stale smell throughout (think of the hotel from "The Shining"). The room was very outdated except for the TV, which is newer and big. The only staff who was nice was the bellman. If you passed any staff in the hallway, they did not smile or say hello to you. The toiletries are extremely cheap and no good. Luckily, we brought shampoo and conditioner from the Marriott and used those. The food at the Old Hickory Grill was outrageously priced and had no taste whatsoever. The quality of it was the same as the free breakfast buffet at a Choice hotel. I was waiting to be seated for a good 5 minutes on the last day of my stay, and NO ONE would help me. A server went past me THREE times, completely ignoring me. I will NEVER stay here when I visit Nashville again. Please don't think I'm a negative person. I have NEVER written a bad review for a Marriott hotel, but unfortunately the conference I was attending was held here. Please take a cue from Marriott and do everything they do. In fact, I just stayed at a JW Marriott the week before, and you all charged the exact same room price. This is utterly outrageous.

This is a very comfortable bar for dancing or just kicking back with a brew. We caught a bit of two sets and found it to be an energetic space. The servers are very attentive and the decor is pretty funny to see.

This place is the ideal stop along Broadway!
There is no cover so that in itself makes it to the top of my list!

The bands are always great and the drinks are fairly well priced and always taste wonderful.

The bartenders are quick and friendly.

The bathrooms are clean.

I am not sure what else you could ever want from a Broadway bar, but this is about as awesome as it gets!

This is a smaller and more laid-back bar on the Broadway strip. It has pretty unique touches to the inside like mason jar chandeliers. I have to say that this place is unusually clean, compared to all of the other bars on Broadway. As like much of Broadway there is live music playing all day. 

It's a really narrow and long space so it's really easy to start a dialogue with the performers, which is cool. Seating-wise, the bar is looooooong, and there are several tables that can accommodate four people each. 

The bar's specialty are moonshine drinks. Not really my cup of tea, but they do have several different flavors that you can choose from. 

This is a great place to sit and relax for a few hours with a group of friends.

My favorite spot in Nashville. Out of all the bars, we always came back here. The bartender, Brandon, was so nice, especially to us out of towners. The greatest sweet tea moonshine (with lemonade), my new drink of choice. The music was great, the service was fast and great, even when it was so busy, restrooms clean and a nice crowd. I will have fond memories of this gem. And can't wait to go back!

The bar is well staffed and well stocked. The music is right on.  This place is a gem among a multitude of similar joints but somehow, they really have their act dialed in.  Tip - Hit it up on a week night as the entire downtown area is a massive throng on the weekends.

I go to Nashville for a lot of things....but BBQ isn't one of them.  In that category, Nashville's ugly sister to the west (yes, I'm talking about you, Memphis!) usually has more to offer.  Well...that was BEFORE I had been here!

Happened upon THE JUDGE on a Friday around noon while I was showing someone around town. They had a legit smoker going in the back, so I thought, what the hell, maybe this place is legit.  I was not disappointed.  Although this place is more of a Texes BBQ slant, I went for the pulled pork sandwich.  It was awesome.  My buddy got a brisket that just about fell apart because it was so tender.

They have a nice deck/patio and the service was on the spot.  The new owner (as of April 1 he said) stopped by to check on things too....always a good sign.  Next time I'm looking for some 'Q in BNA, I know where to go!
Great spot for drinks and great music!  Ambiance was rustic and the bartender was nice.  Merch was overly priced, $22 for a low quality trucker hat ...did I mention great drinks though?!

Stayed here for 2 nights on a marriage retreat. The food was absolutely terrible! Everything was stale, dry or just completely lacking flavor! Most of the rooms don't even have a mini fridge. The only good thing I have to say about this place is that the beds are comfortable and the rooms seem relatively clean.

This place is a blast. Had zero problems the entire four hours I was in there. Doorman was cool. Bartenders were cool. Security at every level were polite and helpful. Don't know if security were the Vanderbilt offensive line but they could have been. Every floor had live music and multiple bars. Top floor opens up to a rooftop deck. Great views and great place to hang. Not the cheapest place for a drink but you get what you pay for. I recommend Tito's or Shiner Bock. Spend some money and have a great time. Stage stands out as the best bar on Broadway.

Got the brisket which was very good but the fries were cold and not good. When the check came lots of extra charges were added. Even after review, when the check came back again there was still extra drink charges. Waiter did not want to fix the bill. I wonder if he gets extra money by adjusting checks after customers pay. Looking back I regret leaving him a very good tip and wish I would have contacted the manager in case he had a thief working for him.
Great place.  Randomly found it off the beaten path. Good food and fun atmosphere.

Went to Motown Monday but all we heard was swing, which was a total let down. Also bartender was a complete weirdo, refusing to serve me a club soda along with my bourbon on the rocks. Waste of a $5 cover charge.

The main reason I gave this hotel 2 stars is because it claims to be a 4 star hotel but it's more of a 2 1/2, 3. The room we stayed at was very old not updated at all the wallpaper was peeling off in places. The shampoo, conditioner and soaps were all Sheraton's generic brand. The sheets and comforter were also very old. The only good thing about this room was the location which was near an exit and our patio led right to the pool. No fridge or microwave. Also we had booked a 2 bed bedroom and they gave us one with a king size bed which we had to make work. Very disappointed, next time we will stick with the Hyatt hotels.

It was my first time ever going to a Hard rock cafe even though there was one in Memphis but never bothered to go. This hard rock cafe is located downtown and it's very lively. Going in the restaurant, music of original Nashville roots are played and its quiet unforgettable. 
I ordered a grilled salmon from the menu and our food took a while to come out but I have to say...that that was the best salmon I've ever eaten and to this day, I still want to make another trip just for the salmon.
Sweet bar with a great covered outside area. Reasonable door cover, drink prices and GREAT music most nights of the week.

Stayed here last night. Nice hotel. Check in easy. Friendly staff. Good location. The problem with this place is the people that stay here on weekends. If you are trying to get some rest ...,forget about it. Drunks, parties, loud people at all hours of the night make me not want to go to Nashville on the  weekend again. Not much security presence.  People making a lot of noise down by the pool also way after closing time. Rooms are clean and nice and they are pet friendly.
The drinks were great but the food was cold when it arrived at the table aside from the onion rings.

Very sub-par. We went for Sunday brunch and it took about 20 minutes for us to get seated and over an hour for us to even get drinks. The place wasn't even crowded, there were only 4 other tables full. The band was okay but the server was very nice but very slow. My friend got a drink from the bar but they ran out of orange juice so the cup was only filled half way, but they still charged him full price. We were told after we got our food that they ran out of fruit for one of the orders but then a half hour later the server came out with a mini cup with a few sliced strawberries for us. The food wasn't very good and was way over priced for how much we got. The only reason I am giving it 2 stars is because the roof top view was pretty nice. You can see the river on the left and the rest of Broadway on the right. Unfortunately we won't be going back.
We had fajitas and burgers that were very good we had a great server Braz. He actually got on stage and sang with the musician that was playing.

I like to go to the hard Rock Cafe in different cities to see the differences in decor and memorabilia. I just like the vibe of the place. There was a live singer when I was there--it is in Nashville after all. I had the Guinness bacon cheeseburger--it was really good. It had a sweet sauce that I enjoyed. Server was very nice.

Came here with a large party and they were accommodating. Everyone ordered different type of mixed fruity drinks that they offer that were all extremely good (try the pineapple or strawberry mojito). The food was extremely good. Had the tres fajitas that came with chicken, steak and shrimp. Next time would stick with the chicken and shrimp which were both very flavorful. The steak was a bit tough. They were accommodating to my allergy and gladly offered corn shells in place of flour shells. Service was great and for our waitress to handle a party of 11 plus 3 other tables at the same time, she did a great job. Would definitely return and if you are coming with a large party would recommend a reservation to cut down on wait times on busy days!
Like the decor and the long L-shaped bar.  Did not go upstairs, but the seating and view of the band looked to be good from up there as well.

Really good onion rings.  
Everything else was a bust. 
Dry meat is a bummer and Sutter Home wine. Really guys?

We stopped here to listen to some live music in downtown Nashville. I liked the ambiance of the bar. Very laid back and casual setting! The band was very good! Amazing guitarist! Bartender was very nice. I'm very picky with alcohol so asked her to make me something sweet. She made a Raspberry Lemon Drop; it was delicious! Nice place to chill for a minute after trekking downtown!

I love the stage for the live music but after being told by a bouncer that they "didn't need any more business" I don't think I will return. Rude and disrespectful thing to say to people waiting in line to just get inside your bar in 30 degree weather. I won't be taking out of towners here anymore.

This hotel was terrible.  We stayed two nights as part of a group staying for a hockey tournament.  For starters, it took a full week and a half to get a hold of the person in charge of booking the room for us through our group.  I left four messages before she finally called me back to accept my reservation.  When we arrived, they had us in a room that was not what we reserved.  That part worked out, but again, not what I had reserved.  The hotel is in dire need of updating.  The carpet in our room was worn, and the entire hotel had a musty, old smoke smell to it.  The staff was not helpful or friendly.  I was hoping for the southern charm that we experienced the night before in Memphis, but it was not to be found.  We made multiple calls to the front desk for items we needed to have brought to the room.  I had to call three times for blankets, and housekeeping did not leave us any clean towels when they made up the room after the first night.  Breakfast was included in our package, and it was inedible.  Cold, rubber eggs and tasteless other options.  Overall, very disappointing experience, especially considering the fabulous experience we had a the Sheraton in Memphis the night before!

Apart from it being a smoking bar it's a great place to enjoy some great live original music on Thursday night at 7pm and a moonshine. Most popular flavor is Sweet Tea. Good location on lower Broadway Nashville. Lots of girls enjoy having their pic taken against the wall of moonshine American flag.
This place was pretty terrible. We went on a Saturday night with a group of people. The food was subpar. The majority of our group felt sick afterwards. Maybe it's better for lunch?

My favorite bar downtown. The music is always amazing, and it is never too crowded that you can't enjoy it. The bar staff is great and always welcoming. I come for the jalapeno moonshine bloody and margarita. They don't serve food but will allow you to bring some in.
Very fun place to go watch and listen to live music in Nashville. Great staff that was very friendly. Def worth the stop on Broadway!

This is one of those must hit places when you're on a bender on Broadway. It's always packed with good music and good people. I find it pretty amazing how well the staff keeps up with the orders given the volume of people that they serve.

Very bad service and rude workers. The kitchen was slow but rather than a polite apology after waiting well over a half hour, our server was extremely rude when we asked for the status of the order. Would not recommend.

I've only been here once, but I really liked the atmosphere. It's a very chill place, with lotso moose heads on the wall as if someone likes to go hunting... Other than that I like the stage, but more importantly the music was THE best I've heard on Broadway. If you ask me, it gets old pretty fast listening to all the country singer wanna-be's. Don't get me wrong, I appreciate country but I'm not a die hard fan so it was nice to hear an artist singing more alternative songs. 

About the beer... yeah, nothing's on tap, and a bottle of beer will run you about five or six bucks. Meh. Not the greatest deal but what the hell I go there for the music, not the beer.

Always solid music and what you would expect of a Nashville honky tonk. The weekdays more acoustic shows are much better than the crowded weekend full band in my opinion. Prices R above average but that's what you can expect from a popular Broadway honky tonk.

They must do when visiting Nashville

Two words: Motown Mondays!

I travel in and out of Nashville for work during the week and I typically ask locals what's fun to do in town. Based off their feedback, I was recommended to check out Motown Mondays at The 5 Spot, and in all honesty, this place does not disappoint. Drinks here are cheap like $6 for a PBR can and a shot of Jameson; $7 if you're looking for a little more craft. The music starts around 10:00 pm and the crowd gets bumping around 11:30 pm.

Disclaimer: If you're not a dancer, enjoy classic hits from the 50's to the early 70's, or like a good dive bar, then this place isn't for you. Also, if you have work the next day, you probably will have a hangover.

Hands down the best bar on Broadway. Get there early as the place gets packed with limited seating. Each time I go I spend most of a long day sipping at the bar listening to some of the best music in Nashville. I have yet to be disappointed with their performers there. Great place and decently priced
Stopped in here for a quick drink as we ventured.  Ordered a vodka redbull for 9.75 and watched her pour skol vodka and use energy drink off the gun,   Not worth it

This place is where its at! The staff are a loveable bunch and the atmosphere is what a club should be. This is where the sound of east Nashville is cultivated...I highly recommend a 2 dollar tuesday.

By far the worst hotel experience I have had.  So many bugs.  Bugs and hair in first room and roaches in second "Club Level" room.  Front desk staff telling me to just take some Benadryl for reaction to 1st room.   Told us they wouldn't charge us due to our experience then Charged us for both nights even though we left after one night, when disputed charges on credit card they denied giving any money back then credit card company pushed the issue and they refunded us one night.  Awful

I love the FooBAR. The bartenders are great, the people are chill as hell (especially the ones on the back porch), and I've never had a bad time, just good ones, a handful of great ones. I love the FooBAR TOO. It's always something interesting going on in there if you like to rock. People bitch that it's loud, but it's a rock bar, so ah, yeah, it'd better be loud. It's cheap, it's nearby, and it's as East Nashville as it gets.

LOOOUD but fun!  I was bewildered by the fact that the singer on a Saturday night was using her phone to remember song lyrics.  Moonshine was great.  I know because I can't remember.  That's how you know.

I love this Honky Tonk bar in downtown Nashville! I had the BEST time here!

Since we were only able to spend 1 day in town, I wisely chose 2 spots to get my "country" on. I wanted a good ole' dive bar with great music, cheap beer and a rustic atmosphere. Whiskey Bent Saloon met all my criteria! We arrived at 1230, shortly after the music started, when it was pretty empty. That didn't last long because the band was fantastic and quickly drew a large crowd. Even though it was busy, the bartenders were great! For some silly reason I wanted a bloody mary (what the heck? It's not Sunday!) and she made a really good stiff drink. WooHoo!  Mike was enjoying his beer and we moved to a table on the floor. Who was playing? I didn't know but they played great music! We laughed, we swayed, we drank! 

Whiskey Bent Saloon is as good as it gets!
Great little bar on lower Broadway to grab a beer and listen to great music.   Such a fun bar.
Jenna is an amazing waitress. She is a true professional of the craft. Her service alone will make me come back!

Strolling down Broadway and killing time before Tim McGraw we popped into this place to check out some live tunes for a few minutes.... prices were good, bartenders were attentive... the music wasn't too loud so you could hear yourself think and when it was time to settle up they were quick with the tab... can't ask for much more than that...
Great service and an amazingly broad selection of whiskeys and bourbons. I wish my liver could stand to stay here all night and try them all.
Came in with some girlfriends, so fun!

Rock Til The Drop New Years Eve 2018-- paid $150 per ticket, 9pm-1am. Plus: Fun crowd and good choice of premium liquors. Minus: stood in line for 45 minutes to get to the prepaid rooftop, 7 tables--standing room only, one bar with three bartenders, and limited snacks. The Hard Rock did not seem at all prepared. The shoulder-to-shoulder action was much like any other on lower Broadway. Note: the note drop and NYE show is now at Bicentennial Park. Nothing new to see from the rooftop.

Came here with a group of friends while visiting Nashville, and we had a great time. The drinks were decently priced and it was easy to get served (aka not overly crowded, which can be a big issue at some Honky Tonks). The band that was playing was actually good, and they drew us in with country music, but it was clear that they were not actually into country, so they kept covering old rap and hip hop. Not my style, and not what I expected, but the rest of the group was pretty into it, so we stayed for at least an hour.

When it's warm outside, it's REALLY warm inside- the further to the back you go, the hotter it is. There's a small upstairs area that I would imagine gets roasting by the end of the night, so I'd stick as close to the front (and the open door) as you possibly can.

If you're looking for different kinds of moonshine, you have found your place! They serve old Smokey Brand moonshine in many different flavors. The first time I had the flavor called "hunch punch" and the second time I had the strawberry. Both were excellent! This is such a fun little bar that I wish it was bigger. The first time we went, we saw the Justine Blazer band and she was absolutely phenomenal and her guitar players were the entire show! Second time we went we saw another band that I did not get their name. Both were awesome bands and the waitstaff here and bartenders are excellent! This was my favorite bar on Broadway in Nashville so I had to get myself a T-shirt to wear back here in San Francisco California where you have to look for live music with a magnifying glass. I already miss Bootleggers Inn! I'll be back!
I went here on a date, it was nice, the food wasn't bad! :)

They only have one bartender who has to wait tables. Three other girls came in and are behind the bar but doing nothing. People come in sit for a while, but the bartender is overwhelmed with people at bar. We watched a group of 6, a group of 5, several groups of 2 and one lady walk out without service. A group of 3 ladies who had on drink at a table left. When we left and went next door 3 of the groups were there drinking. One of the 3 girls doing nothing should have taken care of the tables. They could have made good money. It is a nice bar/club to listen to music at, but with only one server who works I would recommend going somewhere else.
