Also, when calling the hotel to request the shuttle at the airport, no one answered the phone for nearly 20 minutes. I had to keep calling repeatedly.

Let me start by saying that the people here are AMAZING! This has nothing to do with service or hospitality. I give one star for the infestation of Stink Bugs in the hotel. Our room was infested. We were offered a new room that was also infested. We opted to stay in our room and had to have maintenance come four times to remove close to 30 bugs. Still more emerged this morning. We love this hotel but will think twice about staying in the future. 

Our room was comped for the night. Thanks to the management and staff for quick decision making and quick service. Ashley was outstanding!

THIS PLACE IS AWESOME! My husband and I came here for "Motown Monday's" and danced all night. It was hard to leave! Drinks are good, music was awesome, interior is a bit small but nice and clean, and the staff is friendly. Don't miss this local spot if you're in the Nashville area!

We did the self-guided Ryman Auditorium late morning & wanted to eat somewhere on Broadway. The music sounded really loud at some places & the parking was too far for a one-legged fat boy like me. Hard Rock has relatively quiet, had valet parking & since my name is Rock I've always wanted a Hard Rock baseball cap. 

I knew going in that the food wasn't highly regarded. We split a half-pound burger with fries & a smoothie. It was plenty for two. A souvenir pint glass came with the smoothie to add to our collection.  

It was not bad at all, but other than the destination has & the valet parking it was unremarkable. I don't regret doing it, but I've got my hat & my pint glass so I don't need to go again.

My must visit bar when I'm in Nashville. After a night at the Ryman what could be better. Nashville downtown is tremendous and the big guitar outside leads you to the Hard Rock Cafe. You will love it here. Even though I've never been disappointed at a Hard Rock Cafe in any city, this one in Nashville will always be my favorite.

I went here on a Wednesday evening to hang out and have some dinner. The band was enthusiastic, but the country was a little too old school for me. I enjoyed their gummy bear shot (which was the special of the day) and got a really good veggie wrap featuring some kind of spinach dip in the wrap. The Mac and cheese was mediocre and the place was a little on the emptier side for Broadway.

One of my favorite places in Nashville.  Sunday Funday with Shawn Mayer and Mark Dooley (12-3) is some of the best live music around.  Shawna Hornbeck bartends every Sunday with her faithful partner Molly Bird.  They always make my cocktail just the way I like it, and are super fun.  There is no place else to be on Sunday afternoon!

My first time bar hopping in Nashville and wandered into this place. The bar was ok, but honestly the band was just awful. I'm a musician myself and after all the talk about how great the Nashville music scene is, I was appalled that they let such a crappy band on stage on a Friday night. However the place was pretty empty so maybe the person booking will realize the error of their ways. One beer and we were gone.
I had a great time at this venue. This the drinks were very delicious and not water down. The pricing is not that bad.
Service was good but the food was lackluster. Luke warm, wilted fries and a tasteless club sandwich. My daughter did not care for her salmon salad as well.

2.5

The good things to start: the employees are wonderfully nice. Everyone from security to the door guys to the bartenders... super nice. I think many of the problems I had/have with The Valentine are due to the fact that it's new. BUT if it's open to take my money and is located on Broadway (ground zero in the tourist traffic game), I think it's fair to expect that it would have its act together from the very beginning.

I came here with a good friend in late spring. I was excited to spend time with her and to show off a new business. She, being from TN, was dubious about going out on Broadway but she indulged me. I left with egg on my face. We walked in to find a, largely, empty huge space. 'Well, it's Sunday so maybe it needs some time to amp up.' Thing is, even though it may be Sunday, it's still Broadway. Most establishments weren't hurting for a crowd. We walked in and thought about getting a bite to eat. The menu, at that time, wasn't quite ready. We'd thought about having salads and sandwiches. At the time, though, all they had to offer were chicken tenders and pretzel bites. Hmm. Okay. Drinks. We're in a bar. We'll get drinks. I got a Stiegl Grapefruit and my friend ordered a white wine... which came in a plastic cup and was a small pour. Hmm. Okay. We tried to make the best of it (the bartender was very sweet as she apologized about items that were unavailable) but as we started talking, the band started up. I hate to yuck someone's yum but this band was not the most talented. But they were loud. Very loud. The emptiness of the bar didn't help the noise or talent level. Wanting to escape the madness, we tried to salvage our time there by going to the roof. Since it was such a slow night, the venue was closed past the second floor. I get it. I do. But rooftops are Broadway bars' bread & butter in food weather. After the first floor, the rooftop should always be open. My friend, patient and sweet as she is, was nearing her breaking point. We gulped our drinks and took off to see what else Downtown had to offer.

This honky tonk saloon had great live music 12:30 in the afternoon. Greeted with smiles from the bartender who quickly took our drink order and welcomed us at the bar while we enjoyed a piece of Nashville. We listened for a few songs and continued on our saloon shopping g escapade but quickly came back to this one because of the music.

Absolutely spectacular! Sheraton hotels are always top notch but this one in particular was special.

Aside from the normal exemplary service, we had the pleasure of meeting Michael Self at their hotel bar. I simply cannot put into words how amazing Michael's service was throughout our entire stay. Truly an expert within his craft, and an amazing resource for narrowing down what to do/not to do within the Nashville area. In fact, his impeccable service and spot on recommendations were the entire reason we extended our trip by 2 days. 

10/10 the only place to stay in Nashville by a landslide. Great people, multiple professional shuttle services for downtown and the airport. This will definitely be the only place we stay during future visits. Be mindful that certain room discounts exist and the hotel is happy to accommodate almost any imaginable requests.

Michael, if you're reading this at some point then thank you for turning our vacation into a once in a lifetime experience!

Another quality stop on the Broadway tourist trek. This place was CROWDED, but super fun once we got situated by the stage with drinks in hand. It was a little tough to get drinks and make our way through the packed bodies in this space so be prepared for that. The band playing that night did some country covers and played a few of their originals. Prepare for sloshing drinks and rowdy fans - there was a big group of folks there who knew the band and were singing along to everything, even the original stuff. Pretty entertaining to watch. Worth a stop in! No cover, remember to tip!

I love a good dive bar with live music. However having a unfriendly bartender is the worst. Came here after dinner to see live music, paid cover, came to bar for drinks. Bigger guy with red hat and glasses was the rudest  dud of a bartender. Asked how his night was going, his response was what do you want. Ordered 4 drinks, including  a dos amber, brought me a dog fish where I responded is that for me. His response, well not anymore....ummm wtf smile and listen. Band was boring, crowd was not entertained. Moved onto next venue....keep trying.

Ok let's paint the picture here. It is 10pm on a Tuesday night, with the restaurant being pretty barren. I am here eating my dinner with my dear mother on a night before a well anticipated college tour of Vanderbilt University. Upon arrival, we were seated immediately in a booth. For drinks, mother ordered a glass white wine, laughingly the waiter carded my mom, an adult over 50 years. Then we ordered a green salad which had wilted spinach. Unremarkable but rememberable because it was so bad. A round of chilly beef nachos came next. As a result of the cold temperature and discoloration of the steak (not fresh), we had to return it. After that the waiter made sure that our nachos were fresh but that still did not redeem the kitchen's mistake, for the nachos, despite having freshly cooked steak, were still cold! It appears that they just cooked the steak off and stuck the nachos in the microwave for about 20 seconds just to get the edges hot. In addition to this, the waiter forgot to give us the salsa that comes with the nachos on the second round which made us have to ask again. When the salsa did come, we couldn't help but notice how discolored it looked too. It looked almost brown. All in all, this chain has let me down. In my younger days I thought they held their qualities to a higher standard, tonight they proved me wrong. I do not recommend this place because they appear to just not pay attention to detail or listen to its customers.

With so many great places on broadway why end up here. First they have drinks, delicious, yummy, in a cute cup drinks. Also it's open all the time, any day, like Christmas Day. Typically I stay home on Christmas Day but being on vacation this was the spot. The food is good, Mac and cheese never disappoints. The service was great and we had an overall great experience.

Terrible service. Took 20 min to get served when restaurant wasn't even busy. Plates missing items listed on menu, no designated server assigned to tables, manager drinking at the bar instead of assisting guests. Very disappointing compared to other experiences at Hard Rock Cafe restaurants.

Love going to this club! It's clean, open and friendly...No food here, but you can bring in your own. Bartenders are great and attentive. Our favorite local band is The Randy Nations Band. They play here most Tuesday (classic rock) and Thursday (classic country) nights. Highly recommend!!

This is a fun place to stop by to check out the historical cafe, to sit by the cool bar and listen to music. 
We ordered two virgin drinks and a dessert. Our bartender was quick and very sweet. The drinks tasted great and the cobbler was decent. The videos are fun to watch on their flatscreen TVs. The place is clean and has various historical pieces (outfits, guitars) saved on their walls.

This is one of my favorite bars on broadway, but tonight made it clear that this is a terrible place to go if you want to have fun. Security attempted to keep my dad from coming back into the bar after smoking a cigarette, even though he had drank only two beers at this bar. People were falling asleep on the stage and falling off of their stools, but apparently my dad, coherent and put together, was the biggest threat. He was calm and collected throughout the entire night, and to have him be treated like that as a REGULAR is insane. I will never recommend this bar to any of my customers again; tonight was absolutely absurd.

Hung out here late on a Friday night and Sunday night (Jan 15th and Jan 17th). This place gets packed, packed, packed! We got lucky both times and snagged a table and chairs in the small upstairs area near the back. Otherwise, I think it would have been really unenjoyable. The dance floor is shoulder to shoulder standing room only in the evenings. 

Both times the live music was outstanding. They played a great mixture of cover songs, both country and pop. We had a great time listening and singing along, definitely a place not to miss when visiting Nashville! 

Be aware, they do not serve any wine at this bar! Beer & liquor only!

Security threw me out because I've been there for two hours hanging out and they took the chairs away at the bar and I complained!  They literally grabbed me and threw me out!  Not worth it! Don't go there.  Go somewhere else!  I will also be filing a police report.

I can't say much about this place because we only happened to stop in when we walked by and heard my BF's favorite song playing. The bar on a Sunday afternoon was pretty empty, more of an older married crowd, but the guy playing music was good. We stopped in for 5 minutes and stood by the bar listening to music and the bartender didn't ask us if we wanted any drinks.

Bourbon Street?  Is that where I ended up?  For surely Broadway in Nashville has much of the same vibe as the New Orleans iconic bar street with plenty of the same drunken patrons, loud mouthed yelling and bachelorette parties galore.

The Stage had come recommended to me by people who obviously like cover bands that play great songs in a mediocre way.  But the crowd doesn't seem to mind as they cheer, dance and drink their way to oblivion!

There is no cover charge (for most places that we went to along this stretch) and there is also no smoking allowed in this bar, both of which were a plus in my book.

As for the drinks, they pour a strong one and if you have a place at the bar, know that people will be putting their empties on it all night which makes for a lot of jostling for position.  Also be prepared to have people spill on you as it is crowded and often reminded me of frat parties back in my college days.

You may have to stand a bit in the line out front, but never fear . . .it moves fast and you will find yourself inside in no time at all.  The bands vary from night to night so you may get lucky and find yourself a decent one when you visit.  But even if it doesn't start out strong- they vary about every 3 hours so just pop into another place on the strip and come back a little later.

I love live music . . . .and of all the places on Broadway, this still is my favorite.  Just know that it's a party first, and a music venue second.

They book some of the best up and coming local bands for all the patrons to enjoy. It gets very crowded when the bands are playing. Lots of funny people watching from the dancing drunk people to the groups of friends on a weekend get away where, "what happens in Nashville, stays in Nashville."  Their drink prices are pretty much the same as all the other Broadway music venues. The girls/guy behind the bar looked very busy with organized chaos but they got drinks served quickly and occasionally had a second to hit the floor and pick up the empties. The security is friendly unless you do something stupid to piss them off. I would not want to be on the end of their walk out as they are very big guys who have a business and vacationers to protect. 
BTW, If the line is long at the front door, take a little walk around back as there is a quieter entrance there. Love the Stage!!!

This place was tons of fun! My group went bar hopping on broadway on a Friday night and we stopped at the stage just to explore and to our surprise we were very pleased! This was the only bar on broadway that wasn't packed wall to wall with people. The live band was fantastic and the drinks were very affordable -- I'd definitely recommend it!
The location was nice, but you've seen one Hard Rock, you've seen them al. Bartender was great, though, so one extra star.

We were next door and I stepped out to smoke and I heard the music coming from here. It was fantastic!! I went back next door and told my husband to chug it because we were going next door. As we stepped outside my husband heard the music and said "Wow!". We walked in and the place was beautiful and clean. We sat in front of the stage at the end of the bar. The bartender was super friendly and helpful. We decided to order something small to eat. Our food came out fast, hot and delicious. Overall, I would have to say this was our best experience of our bar hop. Just great vibes!
Not a favorite. If you're young looking, the bartenders are very attentive. If you're not, good luck getting a drink.

Our experience here was not good.  Honestly, it was so bad our party joked that we felt like we were being "punked".  Most of us ordered Sweet Tea ... they were brought to the table in warm glasses containing warm tea and remnants of ice.  When I made note of it to our waitress she said, "Yeah, it's fresh."  - Okay.  I asked for a side of ice.  My husband ordered Ginger Ale... when he told the waitress it was flat (seriously, not a bubble in it) she told him, "Oh, it always is; everyone returns it." We really should have left then.  While the restaurant was not busy, our meals took forever.  I ordered the California Cobb Salad...the  pomegranate seeds were mush (probably previously frozen), the diced avocado was brown and mushy, and the lettuce looked like it was going bad.  - before the waitress had left the table, I gave her the dish back.  The manager came over and offered to get me another salad on the house.  I was honest with her - I didn't trust the produce after seeing what had come out of the kitchen.  Mine was the only dish that had to be sent back, but only two in our party finished their meals... the others were just blah.  The two that did finish had burgers ...and one of them chipped a tooth on a hard, bone-like object.  We knew he had bitten into something and put it on the side of his plate, but didn't know about the chip until after leaving the restaurant.  I had never been to a Hard Rock Cafe but was really looking forward to it ...never again.

Total dive, but in a good way. "Motown Monday" swing dancing is super fun. Starts a little slow but many locals come and almost everyone is there to dance (vs drink and watch). Would definitely come back!

The most average experience from start to finish. Our appetizer took over 30 minutes to get to the table, and it was incorrect. After the appetizer was corrected, it only arrived about 5 minutes prior to the meal. Despite that, I was still charged full price for the appetizer. The pulled pork sandwich I had was very bland and the bun was soggy. 

If you're looking for a place to spend $50-70 dollars for 2 for overpriced food and be underwhelmed, look no farther.

I really liked this place and the band we saw last Saturday, they had a bad ass female fiddle player which I adore. They had plenty of drink selections and plenty of room to hang out.
But I have to share this story which would horrify Jon Taffer. My friend ordered a beer, but the bartender misunderstood him and made him a gin and tonic (thats what he had previously). The bartender agreed to correct the mistake and gave my friend the beer, but he proceeded to strain the already made gin and tonic off the ice and place it on the top of the fridge behind the bar to presumably sell to someone else! Imagine if your bartender tried to serve you a cup of mystery liquid over ice after you order a gin and tonic, NOTHANKYOU!!
All that being said, I will definitely come back to The Stage, but watch your bartender or get a beer or straight shot, apparently they have no pride in their cocktail game!
The older bearded bartender made fun of my stutter so myself and 10 people left. It's untasteful and rude.Maybe get a attitude check!
Spent the evening with an awesome bartender named cass she is excellent check her out!

DOESN'T DESERVE A STAR!!! We complained about a cranberry/vodka served that tasted like straight juice. We were told bartender didn't have ice (which would have diluted the beverage to begin with...) We are from out of town and have never been to this location before this weekend. We went to the bar on a Friday night and had a blast... then on a Saturday night we had the complete opposite service. We have a complaint about a 2nd floor female bartender: we were 'served' a Cranberry/vodka with no ice because we were told she had no ice (although I personally ordered a Long Island Iced Tea with ice and was perfectly fine) In no way did we ask for a refund or another drink... we simply were bringing attention to the staff and bartender that she made a terrible drink. We came around 1:55 am on a Saturday, and asked for a vodka cranberry and she said she didn't have any ice. We asked when the club closed and she said, "She was done by 2:15, and everyone needs to be kicked out by 2:30." (When the club closes at 3 am according to online) You can tell she wanted to go home and was in a hurry to leave and get home. Another "assistant manager" stepped in and mocked us as we complained to the bartender to tell we didn't have alcohol in the beverage we were served. Not only were we treated poorly and charged for a drink we didn't receive properly... we have a poor representation of The Stage in Nashville as tourtist. As we left the "body-guards" treated us poorly and made us feel like we were in the wrong by saying, "As if she had any reason to do that to you..." they made us, as paying customers, feel like we were incompetent and lesser than. As a server in my home town, I would never treat a "guest" like this. We never ONCE asked for a refund, nor another drink we just asked the bartender why the drink only tasted like cranberry with no vodka. Multiple people tasted the drink (with no ice) and said it was purely cranberry juice and told us to ask about it, we were treated like absolute dirt. We have never been to this city, and never this bar... and we will never recommend this bar to anyone after this. We had people who don't even drink, taste the beverage, and tasted no alcohol. As a server and person who works in customer service, I would have taken the beverage and thrown it out-- and made a new one. I would have treated the guest better than we were treated. It's about the principle and treatment we received.

We had a great stay at this Sheraton on the way from TX back to DC. We were traveling with a 65# bulldog and the pet accommodations were great... No pet fee and the rooms were wonderful! The rooms were clean and spacious with great amenities within the hotel. Michael who was a server/bartender was superb! Very pleasant and helpful with recommendations on areas to see downtown. Overall great experience, great price and very pleased with the dog friendly atmosphere.
Checked in for a work conference.  Landed at the Nashville airport and took the shuttle to the hotel.  Check in was quick and easy.  Rooms are decent, nothing fancy, just a regular hotel room

I dislike leaving bad reviews but this was such that I at least needed to have it stated. 
we went last night for a memorable trip for the girls unfortunately that was not the case. The good was we had a pretty decent server, Michelle. she even got us a great table. The reason why we needed a new table though...I'm a bigger girl its obvious you can see that so when you put me in a booth that's fine if the table moves but I couldn't even sit in the booth. so ok whatever we get moved to a table. Then it was a 40 min wait on our food. that's fine. my kids were complainy but they can learn patience for good food. but it wasnt that. we watched them place our food under the headlamps and stay for about 15 or so mins one of my daughters dishes the twisted mac and cheese came out cold. I know this because I took a pic at 8:06 and at 8:14 when I took a bite it was so cold, not even room temperature. which was disappointing. my friend who was with us ordered a burger medium well. theres a wood fire grill which is fine but it was so burnt. ya know that acidic burnt taste that you get. ya that. so badly she couldnt even eat half of it. It really put a damper on a once in a lifetime experience for my kiddos.
Good music and great Tennessee Moonshine.  Service is pretty good too.  Placed was packed on Sunday afternoon.
Decided to eat at the hotel and listen to some live music. Ordered the burger asked for mayo and have been sitting waiting for it for over 30 min. now. Hope this $17 burger is worth it cold.

This, like all the other nearby juke joints, is quite the scene. 

There's a bouncer at the door checking ID, ensuring that you are 21. Friday & Saturday nights are the most popular and it's wall to wall inside. ....just like walking on the street. 

Seems like the music is pop rock as all the 21 year old girls in the audience know the words and sing along with the band.

The norm is no cover,  and beets are about $5. Male sure you tip the band when they pass their Buckley around!

Always a fun time, and you might actually hear some good music.

We went to the Hardrock last night for dinner before heading out for my bachelorette party. I'm giving 5 stars strictly for the serving staff alone.

We got to there and had to wait for a table, no big deal. They told us an hour and a half, also no big deal. We actually only waited about 40 minutes but as a former hostess and FOH coordinator, telling someone 90 minutes when it's actually 40 minutes is how you lose business. While most are happy to be sat early, I know this means a mistake was made or an over estimation was given. We also spent our wait time at the bar upstairs where a second set of hostesses were extremely confused about our wait time. There were a bunch of tables open because we were there around 6:00 which is how we eventually were able to be sat. (I understand saving tables for reservations, former hostess still here). The upstairs hostesses ended up confirming our wait time with the downstairs hostesses and assured us it wouldn't actually be much longer. (Hostess with short hair, working upstairs on 10/22 with a nose ring maybe? You're doing it right.)

We were sat and our server was Brandon! He was great and I wrote his name down in my phone specifically so I could write this review later - something I never do. Brandon was great! He took great care of us, was happy to enable us to be silly and bachelorette party-y and it was so much fun! At the end he asked about my wedding and told me about his own marriage, giving me the nicest wedding advice I have received the whole time I've been in Nashville! Brandon didn't do any magical server tricks, he wasn't exceptionally fast or anything astounding. He was just genuinely a great server. I've been to the Hardrock in Nashville before and I remember the hurricane I had and that's it. This time I will remember Brandon. 

Additionally, the rest of the serving staff was so friendly and fun, one server was singing, another server was doing a Z-snap about how much she loved my friend's dress. All of the serving staff was really on point. 

The food was the best we have had so far in Nashville and I am happy to recommend we and everyone else come here anytime we come back!

Came to Nashville for New Years.... Very impromptu trip so our hotel was booked very last minute. We were pleasantly surprised with the hotel considering  the price we paid per night. Hotel look clean, well maintained and had great customer service. Front desk was very friendly and informed us of all the amenities we had. Room seemed clean
Until we saw our comforter.- MOLD! We went to the front desk and they said they've gotten complaints/ concerns before regarding the comforter. They said it's the feathers in between the comforter that make it look like mold. (I still feel unsure). Although they said that the "moldy" looking substance in the comforter is actually the feathers In between, they changed all the sheets in our bed. They had the head of housekeeping contact us to explain to us that it's the feathers not mold and then they had the front desk call us in the afternoon to let us know that they've further looked into the comforter to make sure it wasn't anything bad. Regardless of what this "substance" may be, the customer service  this hotel has is impeccable and not seen often. Even thought this hotel may not be very central, I highly recommend it just because of its customer service, friendliness and attention to detail!

Also- breakfast was good at the restaurant. And the bar at the lobby is great also.
Excellent music, great service. What more can you ask for in downtown Nashville. We will return.

This is one of my all time favourite places to go when on Broadway. The atmosphere is amazing with the live entertainment outstanding. It's a real mixed crowd of young and old and the vibe is top notch. Service is fast but mixed drinks are hit and miss.
Fantastic spot on Broadway. A gem! We came to hear J. Edwards play and he was marvelous. Get the oatmeal cookie moonshine. Out of this world. So much better than the huge bars on broadway.

My life is like a series of ADHD moments. You got into one thing with a good intention and then it snowballs into something completely different than the direction you were going for. This is exactly what happened to me on Monday night when I was sitting in the Starbucks near my home where my complete was open ready to do homework. 

The guy next to me at said Starbucks started talking to me about one thing and we landed on the subject of swing dancing. He told me that dancing was going to take place that night at The 5 Spot. I had never heard of it nor did I know of its dancing. I had only been swing dancing at one spot so far here and though I enjoyed it, I was looking for something that offered something more. I considered going to Brentwood, but it is my understanding they are a bit of a more babyboomer crowd. I love dancing with them, but I enjoy a mix of all ages versus it being lopsided in the aging of dancers.

I packed up my laptop, ran home to change and off I was to The 5 Spot. I arrived before 9pm where I got free entry. After 9, it costs to enter and dance. They call it Motown Mondays, but truly is a mix of all genres from the 50s to 70s. They offered more traditional swing and rock n roll until 10:30pm before turning it up to some other stuff. I loved it. The crowd evolved with the music. Once the swing dancing music concluded, many of those people dispersed and a new type of crowd appeared. It was extremely lively and fun. Everyone had a great time, especially me! I didn't leave until nearly midnight. This was on a Monday, too, as I said!

Drinks were reasonable. I didn't have anything, however, after talking to a few fellow dancers and getting to know them - they vouched that the bartenders served up some booze heavy pours. All drinks are under $10.

Parking might be a bit painful, but if you get there early like me - you won't have any issues. Just leave all valuables in the trunk of the car or leave them at home since they really do not have a place for you to store them. 

What to wear - wear comfortable shoes! Ladies typically wear weekend attire or period clothing of the era of swing dancing. I personally always wear a dress with leggings because if I am spinning around, I sure don't want any of my stuff being shown. Guys wear jeans usually or slacks along with a casual shirt or button down. Again, this vastly depends on how deep you are into the swing dancing scene. People later in the evening wore clothes that were more suited for going out than for deliberate dancing like the earlier crowd. 

This particular night I went, they did have a DJ. This would seem pretty obvious from the above statements, but the 5 Spot does have live music as well. I look forward to when I will have the chance to check that out and dance to them.

5 Spot, I look forward to you becoming my weekly habit!

Service terrible.

Food cold.

Server was in the bathroom on the phone the entire time.

I have very few words about this experience.

Stopped in last Thursday afternoon because we heard the great live music while walking down broadway. We had two beers each while we listened to the band play. They were really great. The venue is very pretty and is two floors. It has a very pretty large chandelier in the center of the ceiling and had a large bar downstairs and one or two bars upstairs. 

The only reason I am giving this place three stars is because when I came back on Saturday night they did not have live music. They had a DJ and a girl playing the violin. On Broadway with so many venues playing live music they should have had some kind of band playing. I was a little disappointed because on Thursday afternoon it was great!

I had high hopes for this place, but was very disappointed.  I did not like the ribs at all, they were way more tender than ribs should be (literally fell off the bone), and did not have much flavor to them at all.  The ribs were so bad I didn't even bother finishing the portion I got on my sampler platter.  I've never had ribs before that were so bad I had no desire to finish them.  The only fairly good thing I had in the sampler platter was the Texas sushi- a jalapeno popper wrapped in brisket, and the brisket was fairly lackluster.

We chose this hotel during our few days stay in Nashville. The staff are friendly and kind. We loved every day of it!

Ashley, in guess services, is so great! She was helpful and always very understanding. 

Maria,the resturant manager was very friendly and helpful too. As well as Shanooda in the resturant. He was so helpful and our morning breakfast was on time every single day. 

The American Breakfast is very delicious. Those hashbrowns though. So good!! Totally recommend. 

Housekeeping was on point. Room was very clean when we arrived. It was spotless! Thanks to Shanooda, in house keeping. He did an excellent job every single day.

I really enjoyed the facility and the pools. There are two. Indoor and outdoor. Parking is free and internet is free for SPG rewards members only. If you're not a member it's ok, just become one and start racking those points too . 

Overall, the staff are what made the stay better. The hotel is clean and the location is excellent. We will stay here again in the future.

Probably the worst hotel that I have stayed with.
We booked rooms months in advance with the request of side by side rooms since it was my mother's first trip to the hotel and we would be sharing supplies for the weekend.
Our first room was dirty when we checked in. There were marks and spots on the bedspreads, toilet was not wiped down, and everything just felt pretty gross.
It took them several hours to have our next room ready and it was on a completely different floor. We got them to switch the room to the same floor but had to wait several more hours.
We had also talked to the reservations department about a week before the stay because we needed ground level rooms because we have a person with an elevator phobia. We were put on the 3rd floor.  This led to most of the party taking the stairs all weekend with an infant.
Also,  the elevators we did take are a nightmare! We got stuck for a solid minute without any movement and the doors would not open.  They are also very jerky and feel unsafe. 
When we asked for a manager, the one on duty refused to come out of the office according to the front desk.  However once we called the customer service line, we were told the manager was "helping shuttle buses."
We've spoken to several different levels of management and all they say is that they can not do anything because no matter how early you reserve a room or ask for a request, that it is only a request. 
So if you need anything outside of,  "Hey here is your key to a dirty room," then I would find a better hotel.
All this for 215 per room, per night. 
I've stayed at more accommodating hotels for less than half that price.
Also keep an eye on your credit card statements, they send multiple "pre authorizations" out that can lock your card up until the ghost charges fall off.

Don't go to this place with a large group.  They struggled with the service and timing of the meal.  I don't know if it was the size of the group or what, but they cook their steaks way too fast.  Rare to medium rare is the best you'll get.  Medium  to well doesn't happen, even if you send it back.  Drinks, like all other places in downtown Nashville are way overpriced and not much of a selection.

Another five stars for another Music Row bar!
They were all so much fun for our crowd. 
Definitely a great place to visit, and we will be traveling back. 
We hit every honky tonk on those few blocks, and each one was just as fun and more unique than the last. 
Whiskey Bent was awesome! Even with the crowds we were able to get a table for our group and enjoy ourselves! 
Thanks for a great time!
I went there during the day and it was only about 25% full. But, the lack of people made it even more fun. The band worked hard to get people involved and they were a lot of fun.
We came to visit for the view and get a drink on the roof. Nice view but not worth paying $5.50 for a bud light.

Came for a Lightnin 100 event. It was filled with tons of people, but they have plenty of standing room and a handful of tables with stools to choose from.

Tons of beer choices to choose from with good prices. The downside was that the female restroom was flooded.

Not really a fan of eating at Hard Rock but it was close to the strip and we needed nourishment so we dined in.  The food was decent enough and the service was good.  Food isn't particularly fresh or foodie worthy at all but it was a big clean restaurant.

First time in Nashville and it was late in the evening on a Friday night, last month. We were not sure where to eat. We saw Hard Rock and thought, "ok we will go there, Hard Rock always has decent food". Boy were we wrong. We should have realized... no line like everywhere else... run. But.. its the Hard Rock, cant be that bad... We went in and were seated right away. I think we were one of five tables. The waiter was great, excellent service. The music was great as well. The drinks were horrible and very overpriced. Still, no big deal. We ordered three huge fajita nachos and two burgers with fries. The burgers with fries were just okay, a little bland. The Nachos, thats where we went wrong. By the time they got to the table they were very cold. One plate had nearly raw fajita meat on it, a little brown on the outside, red and dripping with blood on the inside. They did not ask how the meat was to be prepared. We sent it back as the person would not have been able to eat blood-soaked chips. The second person ate a few chips off the enormous plate and stopped eating. The third person, She started eating and went to get her fork from under neath the edge of her plate and felt something odd. When she lifted her plate there was food literally baked on to the half of the bottom of the plate. It had been there for a bit. We still had not gotten the third nachos back from the kitchen. We showed the waiter the dirty plate, he was pretty embarrassed and apologized. We told him to cancel the third one. As he walked away he was telling a coworker about the dirty plate and showing it to her. The third plate of nachos was coming out as he was walking back. When they arrived at the table you could clearly tell the kitchen did not appreciate the food being sent back. The meat was burned and the whole top of the stack of nachos was burned black. I am guessing they were just making sure that the meat was done and not raw, right... So the waiter apologized and said he would talk to the manager. As we were waiting for the check I needed to use the ladies room. I walked in, it was appalling. There was wet toilet paper strung across the bathroom floor. The stall itself was not even hover-able. I could understand if this was a busy establishment, but it was pretty empty. Staff was just sitting around at the bar pretty much doing nothing. Someone could have easily checked the conditions of the restroom. The manager never did come out. The waiter advised us that the manager took the nachos off the bill. Our bill for two burgers and fries and about six cocktails... $120 before the tip... Save your money and stay far away from this nasty establishment.

A big bar but usually full, not uncomfortably busy but about right. The bad was good and this place has Dickel so I was happy.  As we were walking in the singer was in the middle of something about George Strait and a drunk voice in the crowd yelled, "If you don't like George Strait- Get the F**k OUT"..I had to laugh.

 They have this big mural on the wall and I could identify all but one, the old chubby guy on the bottom. I was told he was a Grand Old Opera star back in the day, probably before i was born. I've been here a few times and have always had a good time.

Great place to stay. Very clean, polite staff. We did have an issue with our room when we first arrived and it was a bit of a headache but the manager took care of it and upgraded us to a room across the hall and everything was great. The pool area was super nice and has been very well kept. The restaurant was great, great food and service. Our server Tessa was amazing and Andrew at the front desk was so very helpful.

The night started out with such promise.  This place seemed like the "IT" bar. It was packed wall to wall with handsome young men in my age range.  Sadly the glow of promise turned out just to be a cheap neon sign and in reality the place was huge disappointment.  The drinks were overpriced.  Paid $1.50 more for a mixed drink than we paid at Legends the night before.  However, I could withstand a hefty price tag if it was attached to a bar with amazing musicians on the stage.  Alas, the stage let me down in this aspect too.  Two bad musicians in a row.  Both seem more concerned with making noise than making music. Unless your looking for a little eye candy to rub shoulders with (and chances are they will leave like I did after having their ear drums assaulted), I'd skip this bar.

I am disabled and tried to use the elevator, and it turned into a huge ordeal. The bouncer who was in front of the elevator was incredibly rude and dehumanizing. He wouldn't let me up because I looked like I could use the stairs. I explained that I have a disability. He said I had to use the stairs unless I have a special VIP card. I even showed him a card I have in my wallet that shows I am disabled. His tone was super rude even after I explained my situation. He kept saying the elevator is for those who can't walk up the stairs. And I was like, yes, that's why I came to the elevator. After about ten minutes of trying to get upstairs, my friend asked to speak to a supervisor. At this point I was almost in tears because he kept insulting me. Just because someone doesn't look disabled, doesn't mean they aren't. I look "normal," but exertion can cause my heart to pause and then I pass out, but I shouldn't have had to explain that anyways. I also have autoimmune issues that affect my joints. But again, that shouldn't be their business. 

The supervisor came over and almost didn't let us up. He finally said, fine go ahead. But then he said, "I'm being nice; I could just kick you out for having a bad attitude." My "bad attitude" was me almost in tears because of how badly I was treated. Do you want me to bow down to you for letting a disabled person use the elevator? Your bouncer was treating me like a criminal before you came over, and your tone was just as rude. There was no apology or anything remotely close to it. Some illnesses are invisible. What you did is not only illegal, but incredibly demeaning. I will be filing a complaint with the ADA.

I can't begin to explain how great of a time we had hanging out at the bar listening to Brandon Holden sing/play his guitar on Saturday. First of all, this place looks like a small bar from the outside and very unassuming. It is anything but that! There are some bar height tables against the wall and a pretty long bar top with bar stools plus enough room for some dancing while enjoying the music. They have like 30 flavors of moonshine which could easily make hundreds of different combinations. The drinks are reasonably priced and they have a big variety of everything from Bourbon to Vodka and plenty of very cold bottled beers. The insides are a little dark but it gives off that saloon feel like the old country days. As for Broadway bars, they have the cleanest bathrooms and that is a plus when you drink a few beers.
The daytime girls behind the bar serve up more than just drinks. They are super friendly and totally funny to talk to. While we were there, we got to know Jess since it was not very busy. She is the best. The other girl, Deanna has an amazing voice and it is a special treat when she gets on stage to sing a duet with Brandon. On Sunday morning there is a musician who plays his own original music and though he is a bit loud, his music is very good. Glad we visited here and can't wait to return in 6 mos. for our next vacation.

I went to Nashville with friends for the weekend and of course popped in and out of bars all day. We decided to go in to the valentine and I'm glad we did! We went to the rooftop area, there wasn't many people at first, but there was live music the whole time (awesome bands btw), Sean was the best bartender I've had in a while and the others were also very attentive. My friend and I try nachos everywhere we go and there's were some of the best we've had. Once it came closer to game time it started to fill up but the staff was still just as awesome, they even brought out a table and chairs for a disabled vet. By far one of my favorite memories from that weekend, we stayed pretty much all day! Only downside is that it's a Georgia bar. GEAUX Tigers!! 12/10 recommend

Got the sampler plate.
1) brisket was really good. texture was excellent. tender. nice flavor, good smoke ring.
2) sausage. good. garden variety smoked sausage.
3) wings. good. 
4) ribs. ***  they gave me a butt end that was like shoe leather and inedible.
they gave me 1 meaty rib from the middle of a slab.. it was downright tasty and pull off the bone tender. It's really too bad they didn't throw the butt away - instead of putting it on a plate and expecting someone to attempt to eat it.
5) onion rings.  I'm going to guess and say that they use gluten flour to batter. The batter stuck to my teeth and was gummy..  I literally had to scrape it off.  
6) smoked green beans.  I once had a mother in law that thought that opening a can of green beans and cooking it in a sauce pan for 45 minutes constituted a vegetable.  These green beans were just as bad.  They need to change up the recipe and the cooking time.  They were awful.
7) They gave me two jalapeno's that were stuffed with sausage, some cheese, rolled in sliced brisket and toothpicked.  They were two large to shove in my mouth, and difficult to cut up...  Think they were a waste.

I had a dark ale called "The Special."  Quite good.  I highly recommend.

Would I come back here?  I think I would do take-away and just order the brisket.  
Maybe stick around for a beer.  The brisket is worth ordering.. 

They need some fixin..  They have a good anchor, they just need to fix some recipes.
Atmosphere is comfy.
Plenty of seating.
Good for groups.

* Call them up, order the brisket, have a beer, leave.

A MOOSE ..... My favorite wild baby & lots of other animals on the walls plus a polar bear greets you at the entry !!
The drinks are good... Especially the whiskey !  Remember, this IS Jack Daniels country !!! Charley R. Is a great bar tender... She made me a super Jack Daniel's lemonade!  A very talented country band performs & mixes with the patrons !
It makes for an enjoyable evening in Nashville !

BI had maybe eight people in the entire bar when we walked in (and that included the musicians and bartender), but I've never been to a bar that makes its own moonshine, let alone a multitude of flavors (Sweet Tea? Apple Pie? Grape? HELL YEAH!). And I sure haven't been to a bar that has a jalapeño flavored moonshine with a Bloody Mary chaser ... DAMN was that good! Washed down with an ice cold IPA while listening to some damn good live music ... yeah, sounds like a great way to spend an afternoon.

Would have been great but the lead singer in the band made 2 demeaning gay "jokes" within 5 mins of each other.
Took the fun out of being there. Music was good but just couldn't support them with those attitudes:(
Great music bar on Broadway with no cover charge. I'm used to paying for anywhere with live music so this was a nice surprise. The music was great and the crowd got really into it which made it fun.

This little bar on Broadway is one of the best for live bands.
They must be very picky about who they hire because I have not seen a bad band here, in fact some of the best pickers in town will be on stage any day of the week.
The bar is comfortable and the bartenders quick to serve and very polite.
A highly recommended stop on a trip down Broadway.

A little far from downtown, but a very nice hotel to stay at. Ample parking, friendly front desk and our room came with a cute little patio. We booked through hotels.com and got a fantastic deal! We will definitely stay here again if we get the chance.

MOONSHINE, MOONSHINE, MOONSHINE. That is literally all you need to know.  The bartenders are awesome and very friendly.  Casual, laid back bar.  One of my favorites on Broadway.  Is pretty small so can get fairly packed on the weekends.  And the bands they have playing there are top quality, and play lots of older country.

The Stage is great! The locals that play here are fantastic! I hit a lot of bars while in Nashville and by far this was the best place for me. Outdoor patio with great views, ground floor bar, acoustic bar, and top floor bar. Staff was very quick and friendly. Definitely a place to stop into when in town and check out.
Extremely slow service and overpriced food. Never asked if we wanted refills and saw server only twice entire meal.

My husband & I came to eat here for our first wedding anniversary & the food was VERY mediocre for the expensive price. Our server was great, but again, the food, yucky. Very bland & small portions. We tried it, didn't care for it & will probably never eat there again.

This is a review for the 4th of July VIP and Parking area that is held as an event. The charge for VIP roof view was $65 per person and the parking area was $10 per person. I paid $50 for 4 adults and 2 children. Needless to say, both tickets were a hit and the area was packed. HOWEVER, NO one was able to see the fireworks. Many people like myself waited hours to enjoy the fireworks and were not made aware of the blocked view. When I asked for my money back, I was told that I signed a "contract" saying I understood the view would be blocked. I never signed anything of that sort and simply walked in and bought my tickets and that was the end of it. There was NO mention of the very limited view. I have pics of the "view" or lack thereof, and plan to post them on tripadvisor. I encourage you to go there and see it. Hundreds were ripped off on July 4th. I am very upset all my out of town guests were so excited to experience the 4th of July in Nashville, but were left with a bad taste in their mouth for the treatment at the Hard Rock Cafe. I wasn't the only irrate person that night. A couple dozen VIPs walked out very upset!
Got a renovated room on 4th floor just by asking for one. If you concerned about all the reviews of smelly carpet rooms it's true until they finish renovation going on now. Ask for renovated room.
Spent a few hours here enjoying live music and bourbon. Staff is friendly and the prices are good. Nice atmosphere and a good view of the stage from most tables.

This hotel was one of my favorites I travel there every chance I get.  I'm an spg member and have exhausted my attempting to get the corporate or general manager to acknowledge  or remedy the situation...Don't ever take the transport company to downtown Nashville Monarch transport...I was touched inappropriately by one the drivers...the hotel could give no info on company and Sheraton management lied when I asked if they receive any money for steering unsuspecting tourist with families onto this transport.  In fact following my own investigation that Sheraton receives a 1.00 for each person referred to them.  I thought management would at least pretend to care but no such luck...don't stay here and if u do call Nashville moves they pick up if u Google them and they won't molest you or your children

Loved this bar so much, but came here on my birthday. Bartender accidentally poured me a different drink. I politely told her I do not drink pop. She poured my drink out and cut me off. .. won't come back.

This is the type of place to grab a drink, not eat dinner. 

I came here with a large group, so I understand that there will be time delays with wait staff. But our waitress took over 30 min to take our order. Not sure if they were short staffed but then it also took a long time for drinks to come out and food to get there. And when the appetizer came out, we got the spinach and artichoke dip which I sent back because it was cold. Even the second time around it was still cold. I just gave up. 

On another note, I went on a Wednesday which are live karaoke nights. That part is a blast, and since it's Nashville majority of the performers can actually sing pretty well.

Don't Do It!

I have been to Hard Rock Cafe's around the US in most major cities. This one is the worse.  

There was a large party with at least 10 kids in it. Instead of seating them all together, the parents were seated in an elevated section near the door and their pre-teen daughters were seated next to the kitchen..and our table.

Not only were they running around and overall barely supervised but the manager just walked back and forth as though it was no big deal.  I love kids, but on a Sunday afternoon on Labor Day weekend, we just wanted a simple meal with a normal level of activity for a family resturant.

Lastly, our waiter put an asterisk on the bottom of the recipe...next too the 18% gratuity recommendation.

That gave us a good belly laugh!

As for the food..nothing special.

When you see this sign run! Best I can tell, they committed a federal offense tonight! It would appear they created a charge on my credit card. I've ask that federal government step in, shut this scam down, make arrests, and enforce federal offense laws. To me they have committed an act of OVER BILLING! I have contacted Chase as well as Visa networking in efferant to avoid such auctions. They don't seem to understand it's a federal offense. Subsequently, hasn't a statute of limitations. Each instance is three to five years in prison and $10,000 in fines. Stay clear unless you plan to be hustled!!! They won't even use Vaseline!

The rooftop was my favorite spot. Great live music, talented band, cheaper drinks, and the ability to escape from the crowd as needed makes this a great place to start your night. The lower levels were a bit crazier, but still awesome as a whole.

My wife, son, and I have used the long term parking/shuttle service a few times now. It usually is running behind a bit which isn't normally a big deal. But we waited 30 minutes for a shuttle and when it arrived they took southwest employees over us. The southwest people had just walked up while we waited that whole time. "Sorry we have to take them first." Cool, I enjoy waiting. This will be the last time I use this service.

Had a super fun Sunday night here the music was great, the band mixed it up with rock & country. The lead singer that night (6/16) was super sexy had a girl crush on her. 
Delicious moonshine infusions, tried a cherry margarita & grape on the rocks with a side of club soda which I suggest so you can really taste the yummy flavors. The white lighting is deadly. If you have an early flight the next day be careful it makes for a painful ride home as I found out today. 
Don't run out when the tip jar comes around it's noticeably rude & $ 2 won't kill ya. Your`e going to have a great time here

Food was bland and overpriced. It's hard to mess up chicken tenders, onion rings and salad, but they nailed it. Makes me not to ever want to go back to any Hard Rock Cafe in any city. Waiter was very nice but service was a little slow as well. First time to Nashville. I have to do better next meal.

We got a burger here with jalapeños and my fiancé got bbq sandwich with Mac and cheese and beans. Everything was tasty any my fries were delicious. Service was quick and my waitress was pretty funny kept us entertained throughout the evening. I would certainly come back again.

The hotel is very nice and well kept. The bed is extremely comfortable and the room was large and extremely spacious. Had the king suite with a view of the pool! The staff were all very nice and every time we came in contact with staff they always asked if we needed anything and if all was good. Would book here again if ever in the area!

We stopped by here on a Friday afternoon and the place was packed. However, the music was great. We were trying to decide which club we wanted to stop in, and the great music lead us here. 

They do serve some food, but it's primarily a place to drink and listen to the band. Billy and Keri were playing, and Keri was awesome on the violin. She's very talented. All the songs they played were great. 

Every time we walked by during the weekend, the music was great. I believe this place brings in some of the better up and coming bands 

It's not that great inside, but it's good music and good drinks.

I had a very strange experience here. Due to flight delays, I didn't arrive at the hotel until about 2:30 am. When I walked up to the desk, I stood there for a long while before someone heard me in the back room and came to the front. I said hello and that I was checking in. The person working looked up at me with super angry eyes and didn't say a word. She shuffled through some papers then went back to the back for about 30 seconds. Obviously I was confused. When she came back she asked if I had ID & a credit card. So I handed each to her and she didn't say anything but walked into the back with both. She came back about one minute later and handed me a room key. Still saying nothing. I asked how to get to my room and she said I turn right and go down the hallway. I said thank you and went to my room, excited to relax, after a long day of flying and traveling alone. I open the door to find luggage and a men's suit on the bed and the bathroom door was closed. I was so confused and realized I was potentially alone in a room with a man at almost 3am. I immediately went to the front desk to tell her about my experience. This time I was helped by another woman who kind of tried to laugh it off and gave a crappy reason for the mistake. I was so tired from traveling that I just wanted to get to a room without anyone else in it. However, I had a hard time sleeping after realizing this is an establishment that gives out multiple room keys to different guests for the same room. I woke up early the next day to check out and asked to speak with a manager about what had happened. The morning front desk staff seemed mortified for me, but said no managers were available because they were in a meeting. They referred me to someone else, but not a manager. To ease my terrifying situation of being a lone woman traveler in the middle of the night who goes to find a mans things in her supposed hotel room, he asked me if I wanted a coffee... or maybe a bottle of water, because he sees I already have the water they carry, so why wouldn't I want more. I tell him no, thank you, and by this point I'm clearly shaking from being so freaked out by this weird situation and his lack of understanding how scary it was for me. He told me there was nothing they could do but apologize. I obviously was not impressed and was going to leave. He offered to sign me up for the FREE rewards program to make me feel better. I travel frequently and I have been meaning to do so, so I agree to sign up but let him know it doesn't really make anything better. So they added some points into the account. Not enough for a room though, which is fine because after that, I would have a hard time trusting another Sheraton. I left right after, and don't see myself returning here anytime soon. 

Also, the room smelled musky, they put me on the first floor with a back door leading right into the pool area, and the shower flooded. No thanks.

We stayed on the club level which is a great bargain that includes breakfast and even appetizers. You also get a room that faces the courtyard with a usable balcony. Start your morning with a cup of hot beverage over looking the beautiful landscape and pool. The room was very clean and pleasantly quiet. You know how hotels these days fill the bed with pillows, well here they do too but they are a variety of firmness. In the bathroom were not just the usual shampoo, conditioner and soap but also a scrubby puff, shaving lotion and other specialty items. It's little touches like that, that sets this hotel apart from the crowd.

I was overly optimistic when going into the restaurant after hearing that this one had "a ton" of Beatles memorabilia. Super disappointed when I went upstairs to see mostly just posters. They did have some Ringo & John Lennon items, which were pretty neat. But being a fan of them, I was happy to see they had any Beatles stuff at all. 

Onto the food! 
I had ordered a BBQ bacon cheeseburger and a sweet tea to drink. I wasn't expecting it to be great, seeing as the restaurant chain seems to be declining of popularity and quality more each passing year. Luckily, because of the low expectations I had, I wasn't too disappointed. The burger was cooked well, however, it was FULL OF HOT GREASE. So much grease that when I brought into it, it squirted all over my hand. I was wearing my 7 week old daughter in my baby carrier at the time. If I wasn't leaning forward when I took a bite, it would have burned her precious head. The burger ended being so greasy and messy that I had to take the bun and toppings off and eat the meat with a fork by itself. It was a let down. The fries and the sauce on the side were the best part. My 2 year old LOVED the sauce and stole all my fries to dip them in it. 

My 7 year old ordered the cheese pizza and fresh fruit. It came on a guitar platter, which was probably the highlight of his meal. The pizza was so thin, it could probably be a wicked good frisbee if you tried!

Our server at first was really upbeat and excited because they were doing some sort of competition between them. If we bought a Hard Rock Cafe glass, it helped her reach a goal. But when none of us did at first, she seemed annoyed. My mother in law ended up buying one, though. Do hopefully she wasn't bitter about the rest of us not buying one. I'd rather find one in a value village or goodwill for $.50.

A nice, smaller bar on the strip. A little less crowded (at least on a Tuesday night), and that's how my old bones like it. The bartender was nice and helpful when selecting a drink (they don't have a drink menu, no biggie). The music was good, but again I never mind turning it down a bit, but hey, it's Nashville I get it, so they certainly don't lose points for that. Overall, nice place that I would certainly recommend if you are looking for some whiskey and music, and little less of an early 20s party scene.

We are Nashville natives and are always looking  for something that is not centered around country music. The DJ  here rocks! He reminds me of clubs we visited in Las Vegas.  Whoever the DJ Is on Saturday nights ....keep him!!

I'd like to write there was something special unique and exciting about going to the HRC here, but I can't. On Broadway, there is one restaurant after another, each with unique atmosphere or menu. At the HRC, I don't find that. The burgers and sides were about average; certainly not the best burger I've ever had. How 'bout this: toast the bun, melt the cheese, and jack up the flavor a bit in the patties. Grill them to a good medium, less so we'll-done. Give me a reason to WANT to come back; give me a reason to satisfy my taste buds' craving. Don't let it be just all about buying drinks at the bar.
One positive: the music. Perfect for Nashville (not like the loud, ear-bleeding music at the HRC in Philadelphia.)

Having a ball. 
Love their moonshine drinks. Moonshine Margaritas to please any taste. We started with the mildest and worked our way up. 
My favorite was the apple pie, which in spite of the name is  cinnamon and tasted a lot like fireball.   I think it's my favorite. 
The music is very good. 
We listened to Randy Moore and the music was a mix but most 60s- 70s Rock. I was enthralled, he is very good and after walking up and down Broadway and passing up bar after bar of terrible music we were hooked. 
Stayed all night and really had a great time

Lefty Vergeson (not sure of spelling), band was amazing. Visiting from Denver.  
Reminded me of Kenny Chesney.

Where to start? Ok, the staff is very friendly, albeit uninformed. The rooms not only need to be renovated but they NEED TO BE CLEANED. Not exaggerating, I wouldn't touch the light switch in the bathroom with my bare hand so I used a tissue each time. I took pictures of that and the carpet. Really disgusting. So many things combined. The TV on demand only worked about half the time, the clock radio was flashing and I could not get it to reset or to change the time so I just unplugged it, the side lamps by the bed emit an electrical buzzing sound so I just didn't use them...The room service WAS SO SLOW and the night before I had to wait 90 minutes just for someone to find a room service menu to bring to me as for some strange reason they don't keep them in the rooms. I think they mean well but the hotel itself is not managed properly. Silly things like no butter on the toast or on the tray so when they bring the butter later the rest of the food is cold. Then they have "Adagio Spa" listed on their website. Well, I left a message and never got a call back. So I went online and found another number for them and it was some clueless girl who wasn't even sure there was a spa at the hotel at all. Then when she figured out there was it comes out that they don't really have "a spa" there, but a room where THEY CAN DO MASSAGES. But as there is no staff on site they will send whoever is on call and therefore, no appointments were open. Really annoying and badly planned. Trying to see how to attach photos as the photos I looked at before I reserved were much better than the real thing. AND I paid twice as much for my room as I should have given the CMAs were this week and I guess some people were still here.  But seriously, out of all the airport hotels I could have chosen, this was not the best choice. I think if I ever had to stay at an airport hotel again here I would just go with something like an Embassey Suites, at least you know it is low budget and probably better managed.  Really disappointed.
The Stage is a subpar bar with the best looking staff on Broadway. Go see those fellas for yourself.
Fun, party bar with the right level of laid back. Bartenders were great, music was great and they had a great variety of drink options.
One of the best dive bars in Nashville. Music is sweet! Not loaded with crazy kids. Love this place. Bartender is one of the rising stars of the country music scene.
UNDER NEW MANAGEMENT! All the service and quality is out the window, it really used to be a great place.

My family went to Judge's on 08/30/2014 and it was very disappointing  the food was cold the ribs were small but cook nicely the brisket was half fat and the mac 'n cheese dry and cold right out of a box. The staff I don't know what to say it was bad bad and more bad.

Don't use the ATM machine. For the second  time now it's given me a receipt and no money. Worst part is when you ask the bar manager about it he tells you he'll give you a number to call. Really doesn't give a shit. He finally gave me my money and said, "Here. Now get the fuck out of here". Is that the professional way to handle the situation? Note: it was only $20 that I took out in order to pay the cover charge at the door. I'm sorry but if it's a repeating issue then it's no longer the ATM company's fault it's the club's wrong doing for keeping a faulty machine in there. More so, if you're going to charge cash only cover charges then you need to provide an ATM that works and doesn't dispense invisible money. Why is it still in there? Is it owned by the mob and there's nothing you can do about it? Get a new frickin' ATM. It's really not that difficult. And fire that belligerent, apathetic asshole of a bar manager and hire someone who takes customers getting ripped off seriously. Way unprofessional on two levels.  I expect more class from an establishment that's considered a staple of the music East Nashville scene. As a result I didn't stay, didn't spend money there, will probably never go back and now I'm writing this shitty review. Congratulations. Not giving a shit is so worth it.

Went here while on vacation in Nashville because my sister heard it was the place to be for a little swing dancing on a Sunday night.  The place was pretty crowded, but we were able to snag a table in the corner with front row seats to the dance floor and the band.  The band was excellent!  It was nice not to have to listen to country music, as they played some old school songs from the 50's and 60's.  Quite a few people were swing dancing, and other just drunkingly. 

The drinks were fairly cheap and the staff was friendly and helpful.  I stupidly tried to pick up too many drinks to carry back to the table and the wet beer bottle slipped through my hands and fell right to the ground.  Luckily, the awesome bartenders helped me clean it up and gave me a brand new beer!  

There was no cover to get into the place, which is always a huge plus to me.  The crowd was eclectic and is a great place for people watching!  Definitely a fun vibe and would go back here again if in town.
The Stage  my first time here nice place to have a drinks with friends listening to the band play country music having a appetizer  this place has air conditioner for those hot summer days.
Clean room, nice staff, got extra tea bags. Will definitely be staying again.

Don't go here. The bouncers, security, and front door ID checkers are violent and abuse their power. I watched a guy (patron) get punched in the back of the head as he was leaving the venue  by a bouncer standing outside of the door. Then when the guy turned around to defend himself, three people from security took him to the ground and tased him... twice. This was excessive use of force, especially for people who aren't even police officers, and an abuse of power. Outsiders tried to help but were confused as to what was going on. Multiple people saw this whole encounter, but these bouncers think they can get away with it because they're attacking drunk people. It was really messed up. There are plenty of other bars on this strip with professional security. Beware.

Also, the drinks were awful and overpriced.
Very very nice beds and pillows and rooms. Really sweet staff. But the walls are so thin that any noise from next door is going to keep you up all night.
No complaints. It's a live music spot which I like. Patrons seemed to be nice enough. This particular night, there was no cover charge. They have alcohol too.

Hate to be a party pooper, but total bummer night. The sound in the venue totally destroyed a couple of my favorite bands. More than half of the songs would have passed wonderfully as a shreds video. (Google it) Waiting over 15 minutes for beer and then having the bartender first whisper in his coworkers ear and then give me completely incorrect change kind of feels like a scam. The dudes on the street selling newspapers are running a better business.  I pray to all the gods of music that neither a band I love nor a friend's band ever have to play here again. Amen.
This is the second hrc i have eaten at food was as good as expected and so was the service. Granted not busy at all while their. Prices were on point for a vacation spot.

Great atmosphere. Sat out on outdoor 2nd floor area. Service was good and very friendly. Bad part - food horrible. Ordered nachos and spring rolls. I could have gotten better at Taco Bell (I don't even like Taco Bell). Very disappointed in the food! Will not go back. The band was country. I know we're in Nashville but we're at the "Hard Rock" cafe. Expected rock band.

Great atmosphere, good food and great service and staff! Definitely enjoyed my first time here with one of my best friends. Our server, Cody, kept our drinks refilled and was always nearby if we needed anything! Definitely going back

Went on a Sunday around lunch and it was dead. Radio played bizarre music, including children's dinosaur sing along something. Food was ok (not bad, not great). Service was good. Felt like the items on display were minimal and boring. There was nothing exciting about this location. Even though its chain, I was hoping for something special. VERY small gift shop area. For the price, go somewhere else for your meal.
Awesome service and great music. Highly recommend the moonshine drinks. Get there early as it seemed to get packed around 7pm.
Unfortunately I wasn't moved by the burger here. Our server was nice though and we received great service.

My guy took me here on the first night I arrived. When we arrived, we were told the Kitchen closed early. The Night shift didn't show up, what a bummer. We decided to just have one drink and eat somewhere else then.

The two girls working the bar were funny and told us about this Smoked Dulce Vida Tequila they had smoked in house. I was so intrigued, we had to try it. She brought us a taste and it sold us on those drinks. Like a fine cocktail in a BBQ restaurant, it impressed me enough to want to come back the next day. 

So for lunch, we met at Judge's and sat at the bar again. We ordered a 2 way and a 3 way so we could try the different smoked meats. The flavor is beyond smokey and delicious. I'm a fan of brisket and loved the portion they gave me. It was so good, I barely added any sauce. 

Food was on hit. Those smoked margaritas are great and we loved this spot. Although I didn't finish it all, I took my leftovers back with me and finished them later. ;)

Had the fajitas at the bar. Not bad, not great. Bar staff is great. Drinks are good. Music is good. Not as crowded as Acme Feed which is where I really wanted to go but there was no seating. The brownie sundae is huge. My treat after the Rock and Roll Half Marathon.

Sheraton Music City Hotel is a good location for our last night in Nashville. We have a 6:00 AM flight and we need a hotel near the Airport. It is only around 5 minute drive and they also provides hotel shuttle starting from 4:00 am.

Rooms are dated. Still the old layout like most of the Sheraton in North America. Hopefully some renovation in the near future as it is just depressed to stay in a dated room.

No free wifi unless you are with their reward program and for Gold members and up, high speed connection is complimentary.

Since the weather was bad, so we ended up having a drink and a light dinner in the lobby restaurant. The price is reasonably for hotel meal and the food was a lot better than I expected.

This used to be one of my favorite places on broadway and we were headed there last night to show our friends this spot! It was pouring and had been for hours. We were wet and cold. My husband was at the front of the line of all of us and he put his foot up on the stair at the entrance. He then tried to shuffle me under the awning to get out of the rain while we got our IDs out. The man checking IDs told Justin to step back and he needed to see his ID. He was trying to get it out of his phone case and the employee kicked his foot off the stair. He then shoved him back. We are in our mid thirties, and we understand the importance of the IDs and also how establishments can be liable if someone underage gets in. However, kicking someone's foot and shoving them is absolutely inappropriate. He could've asked us nicely and we would've obliged. I'm sad that we won't ever go back here due to this interaction. :(

While in these trying times I can appreciate that clubs wish to maximize profits, still, at $8.50 for a whiskey drink, the customer would surely expect a decent pour in the Jack Daniel's & Coke he paid for. Total rip off; won't be coming back here. Ever! But the music was great!

I like this place, but I've been lied to on two recent occasions when getting a drink there and getting served something that is not what I ordered. Red Bull never comes on a gun. I shouldn't get charged for Red Bull if I'm not actually served it. Since I do know that it's not served on a gun I asked for a new drink with actual Red Bull. One bartender was cool about it. A different bartender through a hissy fit telling me it was Red Bull, then telling me it was sorta the same thing and then angrily remaking my drink. The bullshit was that he was actually drinking a Red Bull himself at the end of the night during last call. Clearly that dude doesn't even want what's on the gun.

Memorabilia was alright, though I expected more from the Nashville HRC...

Food was basic. Nothing exciting, and overpriced, if anything.

Waitress wanted to sell us stuff; said she'd get some accolade if we bought more stuff. She seemed to lose interest after only one person in our group said yes.

I had never been to a HRC, but always saw the shirts and figured there must be something special. After the Nashville trip, though, I feel that is a serious error. I wouldn't go back to the Nashville HRC. And frankly, I have no interest in visiting another one anywhere.

I LOVE Bootleggers. So many moonshines to choose from. I'm not a huge moonshine guy or flavored liquor guy, but for some reason the atmosphere here makes me love it. They are seriously really good. But watch out because you can tend to drink a lot without realizing it! I also love the smaller stage. It provides a bit more intimate setting and never outrageously loud like a lot of other places on Broadway. If you're in town when Rocky Bottom is playing, he's a must if you love anything folky, americana. he does Tom Petty to John Prine to Prince without missing a beat and his originals are great also. I've bought one of his albums recently.

Let me explain my low review of The Stage on Broadway. Of all of the live musical venues I got to visit last week in Nashville, The Stage on Broadway had the -best- sounding mix and PA with a GREAT group of musicians playing on a stage located near the bar's entry. All of the staffers I encountered were ultra-friendly and ultra-helpful, and the whiskey I got to drink was tasty and affordable. The no-cover, all-ages until 6 p.m. venue was wonderful for the early time slot we attended on a Friday afternoon. The band of unknowns played classic-country cover tunes VERY well, with a few acoustic solo tunes by the singer while the band took a break and a few classic-rock tunes while the singer took a break. There were ample tables, great crowd/band interaction, generally clean restrooms, and a multi-floor environment in which to enjoy the music. Under normal circumstances, I'd highly recommend other tourists to stop in for a few beverages and some GREAT performers. 

My low rating comes strictly from the fact that I was told the band ONLY gets paid tips to perform for the day.
