Let me remention this: the band ONLY makes tips for their efforts, just like the buskers on the sidewalks outside of the venue do, but instead with a wonderful stage and sound system out of the elements. I don't know about you, but for the high-level of talent I got to hear last Friday, I really feel awful knowing the incredible-sounding band got nothing but tips for their time playing their hearts out. I realize this is a free country and such, but I also believe that artists should be compensated for their work--without the excellent-quality of musical entertainers I got to hear, I doubt many would stay and buy the affordable drinks served here and instead go elsewhere to hear music and drink. 

I would be willing to revisit this low rating if given evidence otherwise, but I find establishments who do not pay their entertainment (especially with it being as good as it was here) to be the lowest-of-the-low of pond scum in an uncleaned septic tank of fecal matter and therefore give The Stage on Broadway the lowest possible rating I can give it ONLY because of this.

I came here recently and haven't been to a hard rock in probably 6 years. They are always over priced for quality of food. I was very satisfied with our experience the wait wasn't awful the bar was so damn slow though. I know they were busy but they did not pay attention to all their paying customers. Their menu selection seemed smaller than the last time I visited. But it was over all good.

Finally. I finally had the chance to check out The 5 Spot. I don't know what took me so long. Actually, I do. I kept hearing so many people rave about it but I was dubious that it could live up to the hype. I mean, it's a 'dive bar' in the 5 Points area of East End. *Obviously* this is going to be a hipster nightmare wrapped up in a pretentious pita. Obviously.

Obviously wrong.

The 5 Spot is as fun as advertised. It's one of the few places in Nashville (sadly) that welcomes all types at once and endeavors to have a great time with everyone present. The easily navigable website let's you know who's playing (or, spinning) when so you can come check out live music in a wonderful environment on your time. My out-of-town buddies and I stumbled into the Spot on a Saturday night when a band a couple of my friends were excited to see was playing. $5 a man is all it took to walk in and enjoy ourselves. While it has a dive bar aesthetic, I wouldn't call The 5 Spot, a dive bar per se. For one, I wasn't afraid of catching hepatitis or getting a staph infection from a seat when I sat down. Hygiene goes a long way. Secondly, the folks behind the bar are nice. Like, they're *really* nice. To wit, I saw (and, received) non-ironic smiles. Plus, they serve $2 draft beer (Honky Tonk) and $5 hooch (Peechy Keen). Done and done. But, the door girl was pretty rude (like, scary mean) so maybe that helps the dive cred?

There's plenty of tables, shared and perimeter seating so post up where you please. One of my musician buddies took some umbrage with the sound set up. He complained that the performers couldn't hear themselves but I am much too far away from that world to remember whether or not I agreed. Plus, I don't know if that's an issue with the venue or with the band. The good thing is that if you get hot, bored or the music isn't too your liking, you can venture outside. The 5 Spot has a brilliant, enclosed outdoor space with food truck-adjacent realness, patio benches and a bar. *Some*body was thinking ahead when s/he planned this place and I thank hir for it.

The 5 Spot is as good as advertised and if you haven't been, you're wasting time. I know. I was. Check the site, find an act you want to see/hear and get yourself over to one of the more enjoyable venues in the metro. You'll dig it. Promise.

Nashville, the home to country music.  This city was wild, and it was fun to visit.  So, we visited almost every bar on broadway.  So much to see in a short period of time.  However, employees and I stopped here.  I'm from bay area california, and I am not familiar with country music.  Never listened to it.  Not a fan of it.  But I had to try it out, since I was in Nashville.  

The place was semi-packed.  There were plenty of spaces on the dance floor, but no one was dancing.  But everyone was just drinking and enjoying the band.  

Rating:
Food:  n/a
Price:  3
Ambience:  3
Service:  bartender
Overall:  3

For the experience, it was worth it.
Sucks. Sucks sucks sucks suck. Bartenders are a complete joke who think very highly of themselves and over price drinks.

I hadn't been to a Hard Rock Cafe in many years so my husband and I decided to try this one while in Nashville. It was awful, from the food to the drinks. The music was not rock at all it was pop music which threw me off a bit.

We signed up for a pub crawl. Which was more just a wrist band that allowed us discounts on certain drinks at specific bars. The Valentine was one of those bars, after verifying with the bartender that the wrist band did give us the discount, I thought we were all set. Instead at the end of the night when my bill was nice and big, the bartender called the manager over to enter the discount code. 

Well the manager came over and told me I was wrong. The discount code only works for drinks on the 3rd floor of The Valentine. I told him I We had no idea, and that the bartenders have been saying all night that we were good to go. Well the manager didn't care, instead he started calling me a "fu*king idiot" then threatened me and threatened to throw me out of the bar. Then laughed when I said I was giving a bad review. 

Listen I totally understand if you can only honor the discount on specific levels of the bar. It's kind of silly but whatever. But for the Manager to act the way he did, to make threats and to use such disrespectful language... that's just nuts
I won't be booking here again after the experience I had with the reservations agent.
Drinks aren't made well. Staff is rude. Music is the only good thing. Give it a miss!
Amazing service! Ask for Nixon he's awesome! Atomic burger was perfect! NY strip was cooked to perfection! Presentation was great! Amazing hard rock atmosphere!! All in all great place!

I didn't know this place existed, as I don't frequent Broadway that much. But it was a pleasant surprise for our friends night out celebrating a birthday. 
4 floors of dancing.. what?! It looked bumping from the outside and I was ready to see what it was all about. There were 3-4 door guys checking IDs so it made the line go quick in the cold. We headed up to the rooftop and people were dancing along the way at every level. There were a couple different DJs playing on different levels, too. It didn't take long to get a drink and bathrooms were conveniently located. There were tables to sit/stand/hang out at if you didn't feel like dancing and would rather watch. Everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves and there weren't too many creepy drunks to ward off. Would recommend going with a group of friends if you're on a level and want to dance!
Our last day, we spent here. Dropped a ton of money, but there were four of us. Hoping to go again when I'm back in November. Good music, good people.

I had an awesome gig at the Opryland Hotel on a Friday with a paid room so we decided to come in a day early on Thursday and stayed at the Sheraton Music City Thursday night. 

We liked it so much we decided to come back on Saturday and Sunday. 

It was our 10 year anniversary so my wife called and they gave us an amazing upgrade to a suite plus $40 in food credit.

On Saturday Night a couple of locals who portrayed themselves as prostitutes, got very obnoxious hitting on all the men in the bar. Then they got into a confrontation with the bartender Tessa, who handled everything very professionally. She called security twice who never showed up, at least not while we were there. So after the obnoxious women who weren't even staying there insulted my wife and cussed out the bartender, we bolted upstairs.
The incident ruined our night and put a damper on the whole thing.

The next day we spoke to the manager Olivia and she was beyond understanding and empathetic. She felt so bad she bought us dinner and drinks to make up for it. We didn't even ask for that. We just wanted her to know how well Tessa handled the situation. 

Olivia told us to ask for Michael at the bar and he would take care of us. Boy did he. He's very friendly and engaging. We had several nice chats with him and he never let our drinks get below half-way. 

We want to thank the entire staff who all conducted themselves with class and friendliness. I would recommend staying here to anyone wanting clean rooms and impeccable service. Good job y'all!

Eric & Kim-Cara Stone
www.IslandEric.com

This is my favorite bar in Nashville!!! Great happy hour and good burritos (If you like spicy food you must try the Green Chilli Burrito). The bartenders are awesome and pour a strong drink! The best thing about this bar is that it's never the same...the eclectic mix of people and ever changing genres of music always keeps the place fun. People think of it as a dive bar because of its location but it's actually a big bar inside with a seperate room for live bands. If you want to experience the East side of Nashville, make sure you stop at Foobar.

This place is so much fun! I came here with friends on a Saturday night during a weekend trip to Nashville. I'm not a country music fan, so I wasn't sure what to expect, but I ended up having an amazing time. There are multiple floors with different live bands on each. They don't just play country, but an eclectic mix of Bon Jovi, Journey, and Tom Petty - I even heard an Uptown Funk cover. Bands come around for tips and will play whatever you want if you tip $20. Crowd was friendly and not overly rowdy, plenty of bathrooms and room to dance. Would highly recommend it if you are on Broadway!
Very cool place. Bartender Jordan was awesome. Music was really really good. The place is spotless and brand new. We will be back.

Food was great! The service was better. We went during cma fest and it was very crowded but being able to make a reservation we were seated quickly. Our waitress was very friendly and the drinks were good too!

Went here with my two friends last night. We had one drink each and then the douche at the door came and put a rough hand on my female friend's back and said to us "you guys need to leave." We were super confused and asked why because all we had been doing was sitting peacefully at the bar. He wouldn't answer and just kept saying "you three need to leave now." He was creating a scene and it was super awkward. Even the live music stopped playing and everyone was staring! We left immediately because it wasn't worth arguing and the guy was being weirdly forceful with my friend. It honestly soured our one night in Nashville. We wondered if it's because we look young (just graduated college) but he saw our ID's when we arrived so it just didn't make sense. Ridiculous, embarassing, and so so rude.
Fantastic music and service. Moonshine is great. Try the Oatmeal Cookie. Worth the visit.

Why doesn't this nearly brand new place have more craft beer options?! Fingers crossed that there will be more the next time around. With us visiting during SEC time, I understood the craziness and the major lack of seat options. And the fact that everything seemed to be tossed around. Hopefully during my next visit I'll have an all around better experience. :) And I'm sure I will. It just honestly wasn't very "ohh ahhhh" for it being listed as hot and new. So .... to be continued!

Bartenders aren't the best. We were the only two people in the bar at the time and we were non existent. She was more worried about the bouncer maybe try and hire people that don't date or screw each other .
Great vibe! Fun music. Dancing bartenders. Loving it! Band is awesome! Getting the crowd totally into the music!

This place was awesome! The DJ (I didn't manage to get his name) played a nice mix of Top 40, throwbacks, and country songs. He welcomed requests and was very open to all of the bachelorette parties. The bartender at the mini bar Christian or Kristen (it was really loud so I'm not sure which one I heard!) was absolutely amazing. Even though the place was packed she managed to remember me and my friends drink order every time we came back. It was our first ever night out in Nashville and this place did not disappoint!

We' were in town for a festival and stopped at the hard rock for a bottle of wine and delicious nachos. Amazing service by our server Krystal and supervisor Anna who made sure to accommodate us and made great convo. We had our dog with us and he became a little sick from the heat, the staff came out with ice cold water and a wet towel to put over himself. They went above and beyond to make sure all of us, dog included, were comfortable. Thank you ladies!

Looking for a classy yet casual Cocktail Bar with a rooftop option on Broadway in Nashville? The Valentine has you covered in spades.

The Valentine is a self-described 'upscale saloon' boasting three interior floors of food, drink and live music, along with a rooftop patio located in the center of all the action in Music City, Tennessee. I found myself at the bar thanks to a corporate event complete with open bar and appetizers and would argue there isn't a more distinguished or well appointed interior on the Broadway strip thanks to the giant chandler, prohibition era vibe, and illustrious service. Thanks to the open floor plan design on the second level it is easy to watch the nightly live music without blowing your ears out and the 3rd floor begs you to belly up to the bar to catch your favorite sporting event. The rooftop bar and patio closes any argument on what Bar is the most elegant and chic in the area.

I had a wonderful time at The Valentine and suggest that this is the spot to start any Broadway Bar Crawl.

Sat at the bar with two friends and we were completely ignored. Blonde waitress with tattooed arms (I looked for a name badge but she didn't have one on) seem to not want our business. Never came to take our food order. Took food orders for people who had been seated AFTER we took our seats. I annoyingly had to find someone to ask her to give us the check for our drink, even though she was at the bar and we were at the bar. Even with eye contact, she continued to ignore us. Also decided to take her sweet time with the check. I'm a local and used to bring family here sometimes when the came into town. Never again.

Extremely rude staff. Would not recommend if you want to have an enjoyable evening. The service, starting at the bouncer who takes your cover fee, is sickly. Unfortunately, once you are inside there is not much to make up for the fact that you are down $5 and have been talked down to. 12/10 would not recommend.

$2 Tuesdays yass! A featured band plays in this intimate location. In and outdoor seating. Food truck in back.

Other special featured musical nights.

The 2 window fridge filled with a happy collection of ciders and beers, in addition to the taps and hards.

If a good band is playing, like Jesse Caine, this place can be a lot of fun.  Most bands are pretty decent, but there are a few bush leaguers too.  The bar has a good sound system, although the sound guy tends to push way too much bass.  The beer is usually really cold, so that's a plus.  Not crazy about paying the bathroom attendant a buck with every visit, but I suppose it does keeps the bathrooms cleaner than most on Broadway.  Definitely worth visiting.

Our first stop on Yelp Spring Break was checking into the hotel! This was one of the hotels that offered a discount if you were attending the 2014 Yelp Spring Break. Because it was one of the more inexpensive places, my friend and I decided to book our stay here! 

Such a convenient location to the airport! It's literally across the street. So close that the hotel offers a complimentary airport shuttle. When you approach the hotel, you're taken to the top of a hill and kind of given a dramatic entrance. The hotel is beautiful! You walk in and notice a computer area to the left, separated by partitions. On the right is the check in desks. The staff was super personable and really nice. Next to the check in desk and computer area is a hotel bar for your convenience. With a discounted rate of $139 a night, this really set the tone for the trip!

A couple of mishaps that happened in the hotel were as follows. Keep in mind, they didn't ruin the trip at all!

-After getting out of the shuttle from the airport, the shuttle driver grabbed my telescope handle to my rolling suitcase and ripped it completely off of the suitcase. He took me to the front and asked the front desk agent to take care of me. After looking at the damages, one of them mentioned that they had duct tape to fix it! I was like, "oh heck no." I clearly needed a new suitcase and duct tape wasn't going near that. Thank goodness the company I bought the suitcase from completely exchanged a new one out and sent it directly to the hotel. The hotel staff was awesome enough to bring it directly to my room!

-Along those same lines, I was required to send the broken suitcase back, so I sent it through the hotel. Shipping was completely free so all I needed was tape. When I called the front desk, the agent told me that they are too busy to look for tape now. I gave her a couple of hours before calling back and she mentioned they did not have tape at all. That was kind of a turn off as I hoped a hotel of this magnitude would have something as simple as masking tape. I ended up going into the city to buy some tape of my own. 

Once again, I would like to say that these hiccups did not at all ruin the trip. Overall, they were great hosts and the hotel was awesome! The cool part is that the pool area was in the center courtyard and the setting of a previous Nashville episode! This hotel wasn't too far from town and super convenient to the airport. If the price is right on my next trip to Nashville, I will absolutely stay here again. Thanks so much for the great stay, Sheraton!

A lot of reviews are very dramatic about the worst ever HRC. I thought the employee policy and procedures were followed well. We arrive and was created and she said give her a minute, which means she knows I'm there; a half a second later she seated us. Same thing our waitstaff came by said I will be right back and take your drink orders. She came back quickly and we ordered just a few easy water, tea and spiked milkshake. And some of their famous nachos with steak. I got the toppings on the side, kids don't like that stuff. 
So the staff is managed well but just a few things could be better on attention to detail. A waiter delivered the spiked milkshake and this thing is big and the way he set it down hard and walked off made the brownie fall over in her lap. So thanks for that touch. 
The nachos came out... I was a little Disappointed they were not the mound of nachos I have ordered literally all over the world - from Rome, London, KL, NY, Dallas to LA .... on and on you get my drift. 
It should have been more than enough for 3 to split. Sparse on chips the beans and cheese. We quickly finished the nachos and me and the son needed a little more. We got the classic sliders. Very well presented and tasty. Ground meat with cheese and onion ring and coleslaw. It was good. 
Again the manager helped when we returned the dirty plates - again not a big deal but if you pick up plates and deliver them to a table you should look down at them before tossing them on the table and walking away. 
The manager tried to make light of it and apologized. 
It's a well run HRC. 
I will be back
Came for a long weekend.  Great place to listen to live music.  Friendly and attentive service.
Awesome food awesome service.  We a very nice waitress.  I will come back and recommend this to anyone anytime.

We stopped by here twice while on a weekend getaway to Nashville. Our first night, Friday was a much more pleasurable experience than our Sunday stop in. Maybe everyone worked the whole weekend and found themselves tired, but we did not find the same hospitable atmosphere. We wanted to buy shirts to remember the first place in Nashville we stopped. Every server passed us off to the next and we ended up leaving empty handed.

Let me start by saying I had a bad day and the cause of it was once again a Hilton property. I decided I was going to stop subjecting myself to bad customer experiences at Hilton and go back to Marriott SPG. 
I arrived at the Sheraton and Meagan greeted me from the entrance. Asked how I was, I was honest and she treated me better than any of my past 67 stays at Hilton did all year. It made my day bad to better just by being nice and customer centric. 
I just got here but if everyone here is like Meagan, this place has it goin on.
Sincerely, a Hilton Diamond member that just switched from Hilton to Marriott.

LOVED our stay!  The bed was soo comfortable.  If exploring Nashville wasn't the point of our vacation, I would have spent the whole weekend in bed.  Staff was nice and helpful.  The location was great.  No complaints - I highly recommend!
The brisket and ribs were excellent and the service was great.  We'll definitely be back.  Watch out for the Shrmp Diablo......its VERY spicey hot.  Very friendly staff and patrons.  Live music.

We visited  numerous bars on our recent trip to Nashville and this was definitely my favorite! 

- Not too crowded but busy
- QUALITY live music each time we went (3 times over the course of the weekend) which was a bonus as some of the bars on Broadway had terrible bands.
- Friendly staff
- Very cool country decor, lots of animals
- Clean and not as divey when compared to nearby local spots

Will go back if I ever return to Nashville!

Came here Saturday for brunch. Bloody Mary was really tasty-- loved having smoked brisket as BM garnish.  Food was quite tasty as well (I had an omelet w/ brisket). Only complaint was the wait time for food. We were one of two tables (arrived and ordered food at same time) but the second table finished their meals and left before our food even came out. Regardless, servers were nice and food was good, so I'd definitely come back again

This was where my Nashville Night begun.

A beer, amazing live music and a famous venue.

I especially liked the Keith Urban mural.

I will definitely be visiting here again

I started to book this location in the spring, but the availability soon filled up and before I knew it, I'd waited too long to decide. Fast forward a few months forward and I found myself in the area, looking to switch hotels. I always play the Hotwire roulette and Nashville is the only place that I've been burned, and it was in the spring. 

When I called and looked online, I found that the cheapest Saturday before Christmas rate was $129. I mastered Hotwire for the first time in Nashville and scored this place for around $100.

I was able to get a slight bit of an early check-in, at around 2pm. It was hard to believe, but they must've been sold out the night before... at least that's the way that they acted when I asked for an early check-in. When we arrived there were several people checking in too, so they must do their early check-ins all at once. The only thing I received for being a Starwood Preferred Member, was free wifi, no upgrade that was mentioned in another review.

The location is not near downtown, it doesn't seem near anything actually. It gives you an office park environment feel. As long as you know that ahead of time (which I did) then there's no need to knock it for that.

A huge plus is the $10 round trip, third party shuttle company that was mentioned while I was checking in. I was prepared to pay around $40 each way for an Uber... so that was a pleasant surprise. 

The room itself was outdated. The decor reminds me of something from the 80s. As long as it's clean, I don't have any issue with the decor. That was a bit of the problem though, the wallpaper it the bathroom was on the verge of nastiness though. Again, I'll make an excuse; I'm not sleeping in the bathroom and as long as the bed is clean, I'm good.
Spent the evening with an awesome bartender named cass she is excellent check her out!

Really fun music venue!  I also found out after the fact that one of my friends from college was here in Nashville at the same time and was just across the street. So crazy! Wish I would have known so she could have joined my party and me. 

Good music, decent drinks, crazy weirdo crowd. (A lot of drunk tourists, but we had fun laughing at their antics).  We had gone to another music venue earlier in the night, and this one far exceeded the former.  Love Nashville.
Motown Monday's after swing is five stars dance party. Be prepared to twist. Nice crowd and mid priced beers.

This Hardrock is just plain bad.

You set expectations for a national chain in the music capital of the world, and this has to be the worst Hardrock experiences in all food, service, and venue.

Unfortunately we won't be back.
Hair in food and waiter seemed to be in a perpetual state of highness.  I wish i had 4 hands So i could give this place 4 thumbs down!

A great little bar on Broadway! Delicious drinks, great live music and a more local bar vibe. My boyfriend and I stopped in a few times on our trip to Nashville and they remembered us from the night before. Will absolutely be back next time we're in town

I like Sheraton hotels. I was concerned about being near an airport, but I honestly didn't hear much from outside.

The slamming doors from other guest rooms is what is my biggest issue. I must have several neighbors that have been in and out of their rooms all evening, and at time I can actually feel the noise in the floor when that door closes. This is what woke me several times, hence the 3-star rating.

Otherwise it was a nice stay. The room was clean, check-in was easy, and the gym is a nice size with great equipment.

Absolutely awesome.....brisket AAA+ - sausage incredible - pork ribs holy mother - cole slaw is the bomb!!!  If you're in Nashville do NOT pass this place up. BBQ lovers unite. Guy Fierre - food network dude  - you have to come check this place out.

Great place to stop in for a beer and great music. Saw a very young and extremely talented girl perform - it was incredible! It's definitely a popular bar but doesn't get as claustrophobic as other bars on Broadway, in my opinion. Nice staff as well.

Confession: In 33 years of living, I'd somehow never been to a Hard Rock Café.  Talk about a deprived life.  Then again Hard Rock has lost in 80s/90s cool back when everyone wore the t-shirts.  Nowadays it's more along the lines of a rock 'n' roll Applebees or something.  Anyhow, we hit it up whilst day drinking on Broadway.  Beer was cold, bartender was friendly, and the rock décor was kind of cool/very kitschy.  I can't say that I'm dying to go back, but I'm glad I checked it off the bucket list.

On top of great music and reasonably priced drinks, the place was super spacious and I didn't feel over crowded listening to bands the way I did at other honky tonks. Was so great we went back to end our night

Another Nashville spot I was at a few times and feel I can write a review. Every bartender we had was amazing and their choice of bands or musicians was amazing. Every bar on broadway has music, but this place has exceptional talent and great bartenders. I was at countless bars on broadway but I have this place saved to make sure I get there again. Do yourself a favor, save the time and stop in here.
12/27/19: Service was SOOO SLOW! Food was cold and chips for spinach dip were stale. WORST experience! DO NOT GO TO THIS HARD ROCK!

Great bar. Had a group of friends for NYE in Nashville and went into Valentine the night before NYE and had a great time. The bartender Katie was great and our group had the best time. Will go back here when I am back in Nashville. Also there was another bartender on the rooftop that all my friends were raving about how she was so great but never made it past the 3rd floor.

Wonderful time had at the Stage. The music with all the bands was just incredible to say the least. We visited in the afternoon and late evening. Surely less crowded in the afternoon. The drinks were good but little on the pricey side. That's expected with the bands playing. Had a great time with friends.

The live bands that played here all weekend were awesome. We kept coming back! We did not care for the rooftop entertainment. The drinks were spendy, but I think that is the case everywhere on Broadway due to the liquor tax. It was crowded on Friday evening but we found a table and stayed for hours. Sunday night was not as busy but Chris Ferrara was amazing with The Common Good. Make sure to stop here on your next visit!
One of the best Honky Tonks/ Bars on Broadway! Great music and even better drinks. Molly Bird kills it behind the bar! If you're looking for a fun place with a friendly staff, look no further!

So I used to be a Hard Rock Fanatic! Anytime I was in a new city I would get the same thing Nachos and a Hard Rock Collectors mug.  Times have changed.  I am now a diabetic and I have to watch what I eat and drink.  With that being said, it was my birthday so I decided to lax my diet for the night.  

This was my first time to Nashville.  So I wanted to see what Hard Rock's contribution to Nashville's role as being the Mecca for us country music fans were.   Not impressive. It was more like all the other hard rock hotels where it was more about rock and roll than country.  When I got to the restaurant, I had to go to the rest room so I went right in and the toilet was disgusting. Somebody had diarrhea and clogged up the toilet.    I went out and informed the lady at the podium and she gave the illusion that she knew it and they were just leaving it there asking me "well is it overflowing?" What difference does that make?!?! Do you think people want to be thinking about somebody's bowel movements while they are about to eat in a restaurant? Like get real!  

Going back to the diabetes issue, I can't believe with every body moving toward healthier choices, Hard Rock still decides to hang on to 2,000-3,000 calorie dishes still. NO healthy choices at all.   I mean I was laxing my rules a little bit but I couldn't in good conscience eat that many calories.   So I just got chips and salsa and a hurricane. Now I usually have a hurricane and am able to get a buzz.  Not here, I got nothing!  It was like 95% juice and 5% liquor.  I tasted the vodka at the very end  which means the bartender didn't mix it up right.    

Will never return to this Hard Rock again! and until Hard Rock gets healthier choices,  will probably never go to any hard rock again.

Valentine has lost its appeal on Broadway. They built a solid group of locals with plenty of money to spend with a great place to gather and turned us away. They have let go of great bartenders with a great customer base and brought in new security that do not know the regulars and treat all of us like out of town strangers. 1 star for effort and great atmosphere but they are going no where quick

Small place to listen to music and drink, which is most places downtown. The bartender was very nice and the musician was very good. Since it was a Monday night it was quiet and perfect place to relax. I don't think it would be that way if it was a weekend though.
It's a nice place with friendly staff, good drinks, and it's located right downtown.. We were in from out of town. Try to stop at hard rock in every city we visit

My review is based on the gift shop in front of the Hard Rock Cafe...the building is very small but stocked full of Hard Rock collectibles and shirts and all kinds of other souviners.

 There is a section on the floor where it used to be the silver dollar saloon. There are several silver dollars in the floor. It really is cool to see it.

The staff is fun, friendly and helpful.

Highly recommended..

Hands down my favorite bar on broadway. A great place to day drink. It's smaller and it definitely gets busy as the night goes on. You'll always hear some great music in here! Drinks are great as well.

I think this place is wrongly listed as a cocktail bar. It's just a bar.. and while it is a fun bar with a fun atmosphere, if you come expecting a "cocktail bar" you'll be disappointed.

It's conveniently located right on Broadway with a nice rooftop patio. Inside they have live music all day, but the rooftop is quieter and you can have a conversation. 

Drink options included your standard array of bottled beer, liquors and some standard cocktails. I ordered a gin and tonic but got gin and soda water, both drinkable so I didn't complain.

I did order the Pecan Feta Salad, which was really fresh and tasty! It had a good potion of candied pecans & feta cheese and the balsamic dressing was the perfect topping. I got it with shrimp meaning it comes with two large pieces of shrimp, which really added some flavor to the dish... but 2 shrimp left me craving more! 

Altogether fun patio, few cocktails and fresh salads!

I absolutely love this hotel! It's beautiful, has a full bar, restaurant, indoor pool, beautiful outdoor patio and a large pool. 

The hotel has recently been updated and it is better than ever! 

The customer service is top notch! Ebony (I think that is correct) is amazing at the front desk! 

The rates are fantastic! I honestly don't know why anyone would want to stay anywhere else when visiting Nashville. It's about 15 minuets from the crazy traffic and downtown area; with free parking and WiFi! 

Every time I stay there I have such a good time.

My wife and I have been heavy rock fans since we first got married. We travel to Hard Rocks all over the country, Las Vegas being one of our favorites. Of course that was until we came to visit the Hard Rock Cafe in Nashville the other afternoon. We live in Knoxville so we visit the Nashville cafe quite a lot, maybe 3 times a month, but one thing really stood out this past time and it was our server, Ali. Besides the exceptional service that she provided, she took the time to actually have a conversation with my wife and I about our travels and life as well as her goals, ambition, and passion for her job. While having these conversations and making us laugh our socks off, she also managed to run around making sure everyone else outside was well taken care of. Being in the food industry and working at the Hard Rock cafe myself years and years ago, I was more than impressed. By the end of meal we were ready to adopt her ha! This being said, our new favorite Hard Rock cafe has now become the Nashville Tennessee restaurant. I highly recommend everyone to go there and request this young lady and listen to her stories, you wont be dissapointed! We will be coming back more than 3 times a month now and with friends and family. Thank you Hard Rock Cafe for making my experience well worth it.

We were in Nashville Oct 11-14, we were on the roof top, ordered a round of drinks, paid with $100 bill and the female bartender gave us change for a $50, we called her out and she laughed and said oh yea I owe you $50. 
Fun bar and good entertainment.

Watch your money in Nashville!!!!

I've lived in Nashville my whole life and have never been to the "honkey tonks". I went with my hubby and some friends to the Stage in Saint Patrick's day and we all had a great time. The band was really talented and played all sorts of songs, not just country, and the environment was welcoming. Felt like a modern saloon. It was nice to find that they had a second bar in the back so it didn't get too crowded at one. A bonus of the night was having a group of firemen come in and play drums and bagpipes for a few songs for Wounded Warriors. It was a fun night.

I stopped here for a drink, and to hear the band, on a Wednesday evening in early June 2019, which happened to be during the CMA Country Music Awards Festival.  I am a senior citizen and a tourist, visiting Nashville for the 2nd time.  The town was crowded.  I walked into The Stage and immediately a good cover band was playing!  It was easy to get a drink, listen, and dance.  Fun!   No problems!  Easy in, easy out, and ready to visit the other bars on Music Row!

In my opinion five spot is the only place to be on Monday! If you want to go out and dance you're face off and just have a great time then look no further! Only reason I didn't give five stars is because of their door guy. He's a rude ***hole on a power trip that starts off you're night terribly! Always wears white glasses with no lens. Thought it was just me maybe but everyone I've talked to says the same thing. Besides this douche the rest of the staff is awesome. Super friendly and helpful. If you're going to Motown Monday then you're going to have a great night!

This place is by far one of my favorite bars on Broadway! It has four different rooms, all with different vibes and all with live music and their own bar. Everyone seems to love the bottom floor (main room) but I love the roof! You are right in the middle of the strip and the view is awesome- one of the tallest roofs on the row. They don't have a great craft beer selection, and  they make you wait in line to get to the roof after you've already waited in line to get into the bar. Thus, four stars. But, the bands are always solid, the dance floor is fun, and the bathroom line is always quick, so i'm pretty sold.

The pool area and lobby are nice.  The room we stayed in was a little dated, but no major complaints.  The room was clean, but I did see a centipede and a millipede in our room.  I understand these things will happen, but I still don't like it.  This hotel is very convenient to the airport, but if you have an early flight you will have to find your own way to the airport.  They should start the shuttle service earlier in the morning.  

If you are looking to swim, the pool area is awesome.

On Thursday, August 23rd, a hotel employee used an off duty employee's card to access my room and steal over $300 from my wallet.   This happened while I was at the hotel pool area during a 30 minute time period. Manager Korrie was great in helping take care of this situation and reimbursed me money.  A police report was filed. The night before,  I called the front to check the AC because the room wouldn't cool to the setting I entered on the thermostat.  The front desk sent maintenance, who changed the filter and said that since the heater is behind the thermostat,  the room wouldn't cool any further.  That didn't make any sense to me.  The maintenance person offered another room,  but said the we would probably have the same problem there as well.  I was comped a night's stay for this situation. On a positive note,  the outdoor pool area is great, and front desk staff are very helpful.

Wow, what a great venue and rhe best on the block.  Came to hear Natalie Brady who currently is on Adam Levine's team on The Voice.  And what a voice she has.  Rivals Ann Wilson or Grace Slick.  Stayed until 1 am.  Opening country band also excellent.

The Sheraton was the last of several stops on our cross country drop your child off at college trip! It was a great time and his hotel made the last day simply perfect! Close to the airport, excellent customer service, timely shuttle service but most importantly this hotel has Ashley! She is the 5 star representation of the Sheraton Brand! She was friendly, warm, kind and knowledgeable! She welcomed our tired and stressed family and made us feel relaxed and at home! Ruby ended our trip with a beautiful soul and smile!

First, our waiter was great and amazing food. My friend and I shared the jumbo combo appetizer which was more than plenty. But we went to the bathroom and one of my rings fell off and went into another stall. When I asked the waitress that went into the stall she said she didn't see it when I clearly saw it before she went into it. Very upset that she took my ring. Ruined my whole night.

I just got back from staying two nights here. Even though our stay was corporate-paid, let me say that this hotel is NOT worth the money. I have literally stayed at 2 - 3 star MOTELS that had cleaner and nicer rooms than this. First off, the customer service was lousy with our reservations. A standard double room was reserved with a 5 pm complimentary check-out (because of the seminar timing), free breakfast for all guests in the room (total of 4), AND we would receive our AAA discount. This was all handled over the phone. When it actually came time to checking in, the front desk said that no, breakfast was not free and that no, the latest we were allowed to check out was 2:00. But, they said with our AAA, we could upgrade to the "Deluxe" room which was 300 sq. ft. bigger (?) for the same price as the standard. But, after wheedling with them we got the complimentary breakfast as well as the deluxe upgrade. We should not have had to wheedle to begin with, not after having everything confirmed and worked out prior to our visit. Then, we get to the room and find that they GAVE US THE STANDARD ROOM ANYWAY! It was way smaller than we were promised with the "deluxe", it was the same size as your typical "motel" room - barely enough to squeeze a suitcase through. The bathroom was so tiny and cramped you literally could not shut the door if you were sitting on the toilet or even standing at the sink. And we are not big people! 

The room was also aged and very worn out. Again, I've been in nicer motel rooms. And then, the room itself was kind of dirty. There was a used bandaid and rubberband floating in the toilet, dental rubberbands (braces type) on the carpet, a pistachio on the carpet, and get this....a dried up DOG TURD under the curtains. Needless to say, I found the turd as I was getting ready to check out and just happened to peek under the curtain to make sure my kids (who were with me) didn't leave any hotwheels lying under there. I complained to the front desk and thankfully, they knocked off $100 from the bill. 

Another thing, they put a bottle of plain cheap Nestle TAP WATER (that is what filtered water is) and had a $5 price tag on it. Who pays that for a single bottle of water!? Either give it complimentary or don't put it in there at all. People can go to a vending machine or buy a 12 pack for less than that! Thank goodness they offered Starbucks & Tazo free....but that was the ONLY thing worth the stay in that room. They also charge for their WiFi. Who still does that!? This is 2017, and everyone (even Super 8 Motel) gives you free WiFi. 

And lastly, it was our experience with the cleaning crew/housekeeping. My kids were taking their nap and I was sitting on the balcony reading. I got up to go in the room and check my phone when I see housekeeping in the bathroom. The girl looked up was startled and acted guilty, like I had caught her doing something. She very quickly took our dirty towels and left. I went in the bathroom and she had literally taken two of our dirty towels, folded them back up, and put them back on the rack. I know they were the same ones because they had peculiar old stains (who knows what) and were still damp from our showers. She never brought us fresh towels our entire stay. Never. We had to RATION our towels. When I complained about it, the front desk just ignored me. They were more concerned with me finding poop than anything else. 

So for customer service I give a C, for room cleanliness and quality I give a D, and for housekeeping I give a whopping F. The public areas of the hotel were very nice however, and what you would expect of this caliber hotel. Everything else about our visit soured me on ever wanting to stay at this particular hotel ever again. I'm hoping and praying that next year the seminar is held at a different location!

This is one of Nashville's best kept secrets.  I have been to Nashville 3 times recently and the talent here has always been the best.  Staff is so friendly and it is the place to visit for those of us that prefer something outside of the tourist traps.

I'm a 10yr bartender and high volume regional manager in the industry. The music was great at the venue. Keep in mind the acts are not paid by the bar and work for tips only period. On a home NFL game (09/30/18) the ground floor had a single server serving 14 tables and the bar top. Not acceptable. Server was great. Overworked while leaning on southern hospitality and failing on service and quality isn't the way to grow or sustain your business on Broadway in Nashville.  After a round of Nashville hot chicken it was obvious this is a place to avoid as there is other amazing options. I attached a few photos of my "micro" chicken. If you want amazingly underwhelming food and overworked staff from management worried about cutting costs and overhead versus succeeding and fighting for business in one of best locations in USA to run a bar. Come here!!!! Shoutouts to Valarie on the rooftop who killed it, made every trip up to the roof worth it each time. She made this a 2 star review instead of a negative 2. Pick it up management. If you want input I'm right here

After reading reviews I knew this had to be our first stop. No better way to start the day that with a jalapeño moonshine shot with a Bloody Mary chaser. It was so good I had a second one. My hubby opted for a beer the second round as he has a healthier fear of death than me. 
The bartender was really friendly and was right on it. The man singing was very good! We enjoyed listening to him. He did the usual crowd pleasers and also added a few of his own songs which were very good! 
We went on our way but decided this would be our last stop as well. Another great singer, a doorman now on duty and  it was surprisingly not that crowded. I did another jalapeño  shot and he had a beer. Now this is really important. I believe the 3rd shot is the one that caused flames to shoot out this morning. It had a definite molten lava feel to it. I'm just saying, by all means drink 1 or even 2 but then move on to something sweeter like the moonshine your grandma used to brew. You'll thank me!
Nice spot, live music was okay. There wasn't a cover when we visited. The bathrooms were clean.

Do not eat here if you're a tourist!! This place will ruin your whole vacation.. After eating the chicken cobb salad I have horrible FOOD POISONING and can't leave the hotel room. 
Narrowed it down to the salad causing this because my mother and I had shared and ate the same food all day until dinner where I got the salad and she the veggie burger. My mum is totally fine.. I can't leave the hotel room and explore Nashville which we've paid thousands to come visit. 
Chicken and greens are some of the most common carriers of food poisoning bacteria, so clearly Hard Rock is not washing or cooking correctly which is disgusting to me. It was extremely busy but that is no excuse and one of the waitresses kept yelling in the restaurant which was strange. 
Will never eat at a Hard Rock again.

Three words: Apple pie moonshine. This is the best shot of hard alcohol I've ever had! Bootleggers has many different fun flavors which go down easy. Their shine carries on the legacy of Popcorn Sutton, a moonshiner from the Appalachians. The atmosphere is lively and fun. 

The venue on lower Broadway does not look like much from the outside, but once indoors it has an old saloon sort of vibe. The bar area is nice and the lighting is very fitting as there are makeshift "chandeliers" made out of old moonshine mason jars. 

Even on a Saturday afternoon when they were busy there was good service. The bartenders were great! 

Overall, not the sort of place my liver can handle on a weekly basis but should be a must for tourists. I brought three friends here who were visiting Nashville and they loved it. We unfortunately didn't get to go upstairs and hear live music but I'll be back to check it out!

DONT USE A CREDIT CARD HERE!!! My tab was 82$ and they added on a 97$ tip. I called the manager when I checked my balance and he was completely sketchy and never did anything to help me. So many other cool places to go in Nashville. Don't give a place like this business when it takes  advantage of  people just having fun with their friends.
Cool spot on Broadway. Large selection of moonshine cocktails and fun live band the night we went.

One of my favorite bars on Broadway. Docked them one star because they don't have food, and sometimes you're just drunk enough you don't want to walk anywhere else. I realize this is probably limited by their access to a kitchen, so if you're not hungry, this shouldn't matter.

 Service has always been good, although the bartenders tend to take a little while to notice new patrons when it's slow. Good beer selection, full bar, decent prices, and great music. It's rare that I come to Whiskey Bent and leave dissatisfied.

I had the absolute worst turkey club of my entire life here. I attended the CMA music festival, which is a busy time for all restaurants in the area, but that is no excuse for the pathetic slop of a sandwich I received. First of all, when ordering I was straight up ignored at the counter for a solid 10 minutes before the staff even looked my way. After I finally got service, I was given a barely toasted two pieces of bread with a disgusting amount of mayo, one slice of tomato, one piece of browning lettuce, and dried out chicken. There was no bacon at all. If I wasn't so hungry I would not have even touched this overpriced garbage sandwich. I will never eat at this chain again.

Took some friends from Missouri out for drinks and dancing. It was Friday night, so it was expected everywhere we went would be busy. Waited in line to get in, but only about 5-10 minutes. We got beers as soon as we walked in. First floor was super crowded and the band was still setting up. We made our way to the top floor, every floor had different music and bands on them. We ended up staying on the top floor next to rooftop patio. The band was great. Range of music and interacted with crowd.
Pleasantly surprised at how collected lead singer was when a rude bride to be tried to take money out of tip jar and said his tip jar sucked.Glad he had patience, because she sure was on my last nerve.
We decided to go to another bar down the block and immediately regretted it. When we left the stage it was really packed with a bigger line out front. Will definitely be back, we all had a good time.

The manager Terry was amazing!! She gave my party of 12 her undivided attention when we had a slight issue with our waitress. The way she handled the situation was more than we ever expected. I work in the restaurant business and was so impressed by the way she took care of our party. I cannot say thank you enough to Terry and how she handled her manager position.

I'm a Nashville local, and a friend hosted a wedding get-together here last weekend. Another friend and I rode our bikes to Broadway to join them. We were rudely told not to lock our bikes to the sign on the sidewalk by a staff member. I told him we would be happy to move the bikes, but I did argue that it was legal for us to lock them there as it's a public sidewalk. I wasn't ugly, but I felt the need to defend myself. We moved our bikes and started toward the door. 

The bouncer then told us we weren't allowed in because we had backpacks. (Small, commuter bags.) Meanwhile, three women entered with purses the size of a carry-on bag. I argued we were bike commuters and backpacks were necessary. Then, he told us we couldn't come in because we were being argumentative. I was absolutely shocked. I never once raised my voice, and I never used ugly language. Of course I argued because I felt I was being wronged. I felt completely discriminated against and targeted. If backpacks were an issue, that should've been stated before we moved our bikes. If us standing up for ourselves was reason enough not to allow us inside, that too, should've been stated earlier. It seemed clear they didn't want us in the establishment and they found ridiculous excuses not to allow us inside. 

As a Nashville local, I was completely disappointed in the business. It was disheartening to say the least.
Had a blast at our first visit here! Key is a super fun and awesome waitress! She kept us entertained while we were waiting for our food.

This location has to be one of my favorite Hard Rock Cafe's I've been in. Smaller than most I've previously seen, this location has a very modern look. Not nearly as much memorabilia as other locations, but still has the typical feel with guitars, clothes, albums, etc as décor lining the walls.

Hard Rock has an extensive drink and food menu, so it can be easy to get lost with what you want to order, but is a great place if you have a group of people and a variety of tastes.

For my drink I went with the Hurricane. Hands down one of the best that I have ever had. Not too much liquor flavor and just the right amount of fruity taste. As with all Hard Rock locations you can opt to get the drink in a regular glass or you can choose to upgrade and get in a collectable souvenir glass.

For my meal I went with the Guinness Bacon Cheeseburger (new on the menu). Topped with Jameson bacon jam and Guinness cheese sauce and also comes with lettuce and tomato. Includes fries on the side ($16.95). The burger is the perfect blend of beef and bacon and the cheese sauce is amazing! This is one of the best burgers I have ever had. 

I was in a hurry tonight, so I ended up grabbing a seat at the bar. Best decision I could have made. If you get a chance to come to this location see if Lisa is the bartender. Best bartender ever! Made sure I was taken care of the entire time I was there and checked in on a regular basis, while juggling upwards of 12  - 15 people at the bar and handling all the drink orders coming in from the waiters and waitresses. Extremely fast at making really good drinks and one of the most friendly I have ever seen. Sets the bar for any bartender at any Hard Rock locations (and most other locations). 

Great location! Great food! Don't forget to check out the Hard Rock shop before you leave for apparel and Hard Rock signature items.

A few of us decided to take a self guided scooter tour from Bearded Iris back to our place in the South area of Nashville. We planned to make a couple stops and when we hit broadway, we needed a watering hole ASAP. Luckily we rolled into Whiskey Bent and got a few seats at the bar. It was early afternoon so it wasn't super crowded. This definitely worked in our favor because the two piece duo was amazing and once they really got going the bar started to fill up quickly. Whiskey Bent was a quick stop for a beer that turned into a great experience. Definitely one of the better Broadway spots.

By far, my favorite spot we visited in Nashville!  I loved everything about this place and can't wait to visit Nashville again.  I loved the live music, the atmosphere, the bar and even the crowds.  My favorite band during the 4 days I visited was the Harold Allen band with Amanda Allen on vocals (they aren't related).  
Will definitely visit again on our next visit to Nashville!

I'm gonna be plain honest - I'm really not a fan of country music/honky tonks. When I stepped out onto Broadway, I tried to listen for a place that wasn't playing country music, and wasn't too crowded. I stumbled across The Valentine. The building has really lovely architecture, from the prohibition era.

I caught Steve Cunningham and the Cunninghams, a good cover band. They played Prince, Journey, Jackson 5, Queen, and more. I got myself an Angry Orchard cider and swayed along. There are people of all ages there having a good time dancing. It was one of the few venues that didn't get too crazy on Friday evening, and I appreciated it. Staff was very pleasant. Do stop by if you get a chance.

My favorite "honky tonk" of the trip.   Fun and friendly staff.   The bands that played the night we were there were all fantastic.  Any one of them could be the next discovered big star!  

Drinks were generous and fairly priced.   Security staff at the door was a kick..  Carded everyone regardless of age.   They. made this gals night

Stayed there for a meeting in summer 2018, and it was fine.

Back for another meeting end of July 2019, but this time it didn't go so well.

Pros: friendly helpful staff and comfortable, well appointed, spacious room.

Cons:
1. I arrived around midnight to discover that they had no rooms available. This despite me being a speaker at the meeting and my room having been reserved by the meeting organizer well in advance. I get it that people sometimes don't show up and a business doesn't want to leave money on the table. But a last minute no-show is charged full fare (so no money left on the table) and a room reserved by a meeting organizer (especially when that meeting is bringing in a ton of business) maybe deserves some special consideration before giving it away.

2. Internet connection spotty everywhere--guestroom, lobby areas, meeting rooms. 

3. Electronic door locks malfunctioning. While I was checking in (finally) the 2nd day of the meeting, a guest needed assistance because both of her key cards had stopped functioning. I didn't think much of it, until the same thing happened to me the next day. Staff were polite and helpful but not surprised when I went to the front desk with this problem. Seems to be a routine issue for them lately.

I stay in 5-10 different hotels every year. This property is well below average.

It seems to me that they minimally need a substantial investment in modern technology (at least the door locks/key cards and internet bandwidth). Management staff might need some retraining or replacing, too.
Hole in the wall, disrespectful and disgusting. Treated me nice but I watched them, I mean security and manager being rude and mean to others and that hurt me, we all left and never coming back.
Super fun and friendly place and they get good bands. I always stop here when in town.

I tried to bring in my personal water bottle (every other bar allowed me to enter with the bottle) and this particular bar/bouncer did not let me enter the bar. I was excited to visit this particular bar and meet my friends/I have had 2 drinks throughout the entire night. Unfortunately I will not recommend this bar to anyone I know and or this bouncer ruined the experience due to his own personal feelings against me.

An employee pushed me out of the way very aggressively because I "was not moving" so I nudged him with my elbow and was immediately manhandled by security. This place abuses authority. DO NOT SUPPORT THIS ESTABLISHMENT.
Nachos were great and beer made me happy... our server and new friend key, is awesome!!!! Worth the visit especially to take a look at the memoribilia

Had beers here.

Watched music here.

Beers did not end.

Music did not end.

I.....vaguely recall leaving?

I like the outlets on the bedside table and in the arm of the chair
Nice dimmer on the lamp (i am afraid of the dark in hotels)
Super comfy bed
Nice size bathroom 
I can hear people walking in the hallway, don't like that at all
I peeked outside and saw a really nice outside pool all lit up but it's a bit chilly out for all that
Would like to know where this inside pool or Jacuzzi is, haven't seen a sign yet
Restaurant serves breakfast$15.95
Wi-Fi is not free
There's a Jack in the Box down the road I almost went to eat there instead of going to a real restaurant, I had to fight the urge, people. 
10 minute drive or so from downtown. Grand Ole opry isn't far, airport also maybe 20 minutes. 
Their website says today and the next 3 days are$215-304 a night. Everything after that is less than$160
I used hotel tonite and paid$151 , fair enough price for a comfortable bed and clean room.
First time in Nashville and this bar is my favorite! Great live music and bartenders are amazing! Venue is perfect for loud music!

This place is soooooooooooo much fun!!! 
I swear I've never had as much fun as I've had in the bar. The bartenders are super nice and the drinks come out great. I happily paid my $200 tab because I was thoroughly entertained . I will definitely be coming back to this place every time I'm in Nashville. Thanks for the good time 5spot

Nice enough place. Only complaint, when I ordered a bourbon on ice they charged 8.50 for the bourbon (fair enough) and another 2 dollars for ice cubes. Really now? I posted that receipt on Facebook cuz I found it so unbelievable.
This place is great. Lots of good moonshines to try. Jalapeño one is definitely my favorite. There's always good music in this bar.

Despite the London Fog-style smoke hovering at all times and the super small and kind of stuffy space, I love the 5 Spot.  Seriously, I do.  It's some sort of hidden gem of musical amazingness and I have yet to go here and leave having not enjoyed myself immensely.  The first time I went was when a friend asked me if I wanted to hear this awesome new band called the Alabama Shakes.  I don't regret that next long day of work at all.  

I have seen so many fantastic acts since that remind me of everything that is amazing and fun about living in Nashville.  From a guy quite literally standing on while playing his upright bass to a drummer practically dancing into the audience while playing, the 5 Spot has provided me with the opportunity to see some of the most fun musical acts I would have never heard of otherwise.  And they have so many other special events, like 80s dance parties.  Seriously, can more places do that?  

The bartenders do a great job trying to stay on top of the orders of demanding patrons, so be patient.  It's always inexpensive to go (like the time it was a $10 cover but I got the bands new record as part of my admission) and always a good time.  Be prepared to sweat and reek of smoke and not care because you're having a blast.

A great place to listen to music.  They specialize in great acoustic acts until 6pm, then good bands.  Tuesday night is 80's Rock night - "Twang Free Tuesday" with Randy Nations - terrific guitarist.
No food, but a super friendly bar staff, and a great sounding room.  The animals on the walls and floor (bear) were all killed by a bow, if you want some trivia.
Sunday Funday starting at noon with Shawn Mayer and Mark Dooley is a must see - Shawn is an amazing singer/songwriter.  Try to catch Kinsey Rose when she sings here.  Brin, Laura, Shawna, Molly, Charley, and Sara are great bartenders!
Great bar for music and whiskey!

If you are looking for a low key day with live music, I'd recommend this little gem! By, little I mean big! This place is really big compared to what it looks like from the street! We stopped in on a Monday during the day and had a blast! They are dog friendly too! Who doesn't love that? The only thing I was sad about, they don't have draft beer! Seems like that would fit the vibe! They do have bottle though so things could be worse! Cheers!

We stopped in for drink and to listen to some good music. It was just an okay experience. The band was pretty generic, honestly. And then they were passing the tip bucket around before even finishing the first set. Just not a lot of personality in this one.

It's a very sad state of affairs now at the Hard Rock Cafe Nashville. For many years it was a great downtown neighbor, and a community staple. In 2010, they helped downtown Nashville recover from our worst disaster ever. The volunteering and community outreach with HandsOnNashville & The Ronald McDonald House was unlike any volunteer effort I've ever witnessed&become stronger throughout. We could always depend on The Hard Rock Nashville to stay strong in our small community. I guess you could say it's always been 'home base' for us.   Now- recent transplants from corporate HQ who know little about the neighborhood, and seem to care even less about what made Nashville cool, are charged with running The Ship. Unfortunately, they have no apparent respect for tradition. Again, not their fault; they are just scaling the only corporate ladder they have in front of them. These new chickens don't seem to give an honest frack, but even if they did-It's an EXTREME corporate directive: to make money- and these good people work in fear. Sadly, the ship is going under now. And there's your travel trouble. Stay away from Hard Rock Nashville. Powerless, pricey pain on display. It's a damn shame Elise.
Came here with a large party and ordered a cheeseburger. Service was quick and the burger was good. Would recommend.

We stopped in here for dinner because we wanted to get away from the strip and the bar scene. We picked Hard Rock because we've always gotten good food and service at any location we've stopped in to. The service was very slow and it wasn't because they were busy. The food did not look or taste fresh. It tasted like something they had sitting on a burner in the kitchen for hours. We ordered ribs and they were almost inedible. It was so difficult to get our server's attention, we gave up on complaining, we just wanted to pay our bill get back to our hotel. Summary: We spent almost 100.00 for 2 people ordering just a meal each, an appetizer and a couple of non alcoholic drinks - A high price to pay for disappointment.

Was visiting Nashville over Labor Day weekend and we tried to use the elevator in this bar to get to the rooftop. Stairs can be too much exertion for a friend in my group because of a medical condition so we actually picked this bar BECAUSE it had an elevator but we were initially blocked from using it. The bouncer at the elevator said we had to take the stairs and when I asked why he said it was because the elevator "was for people with disabilities." She was even told she didn't "look disabled."

Even though it is illegal to ask, we tried to explain she did have a disability and showed a medical card and needed to use the elevator. Why would we make that up? Around this time, the elevator doors opened and 2 bachelorette party girls in sky-high heels and dresses get off the elevator. They didn't "look disabled" and I'm sure they actually weren't but were taking the elevator for convenience. I asked to speak to a manager who ended up being the same bouncer who checked our ID's at the door, who eventually did let us use it, but told my friend something along the lines of we had to "be nice about it or he'd kick us out" when he should have been saying "I am so sorry we treated you this way." Be nice about it? That was NOT the right thing to say. Both of these employees I interacted with were rude to both me and my friend. 

Not all disabilities are seen by the eyes, and why shouldn't everyone be able to enjoy life and have access to things designed to make it easier? I hope this bar will learn from this and train their employees appropriately.
The most rude, arrogant, bullying door staff of any venue on Lower Broad. Stay far away from this place unless you enjoy being assaulted for simply asking them a question.

This is really an airport hotel, but you wouldn't know it by it's amenities, food venues and size.

It's huge... and the employees are top notch.

There are a lot of large group events held here, but don't let that scare you away. They have ample staff to assist at a moments notice.

Rooms are nice and big, as is the lobby, restaurant and bar.

Good choice if you don't want to trek downtown.

So far my favorite spot on broadway! Band on the first floor was sooo good last night we didn't want leave to check  out other spots! We are definitely will back tonight! Drinks and crowd were good too!

My complaint is in regards to reservations.  They are the worse to deal with. The reason for my travel was because my father had a stroke and I'm driving. I made a reservation and called back to cancel within less than an hour. They will not cancel and are charging me the full rate of $189.  This was a family emergency not a leisure family time.  I realized when I arrive it will be at 5am in the morning arrival and would have to leave a few hours later.  There customer service along with management is extremely poor.  I will never do service with them again.  Extremely poor management and waited an hour to deal with a supervisor and still no feedback.  Amazing how they stay in business and being so heartless in this time.  If I could give them no stars I would.

Location - Slightly off the main strip here on Broadway. 

Vibe - Place is slow and just feels more of a straight up restaurant. 

Patio - Doesn't have a big patio or areas to chill like all the other spots here in Nashville. 

Service - Staff here is really nice and good at making sure you have everything needed. 

Parking - Its all hard to find around the area unless you pay to park in the parking lot here. 

Wouldn't be back cause I dont think it lives its name to be hip and chill place as all other Hard Rock Spots. Will be going to other spots instead with more hype.

Probably my favorite spot on Broadway! Went on a Thursday afternoon and they had AMAZING live music on the rooftop (s/o to Spencer Jordan Music!) The bartender was super sweet, it wasn't overly packed, and the drinks were yummy. Stayed till the band left and had a blast!

Ordered my burger well done and it came out rare. For the price they charge here you'd think they could cook your food correctly. Also wanted to sub Mac and cheese for the fries and it came out with fries.  The nachos were okay.
Great patio overlooking broadway and the manager, Molly, was extremely friendly! I would recommend coming here for a meal or casual drink to anyone looking for a fun spot!

As a resident of downtown I hosted a group of friends in town at The Stage. There was a huge crowd, a lot of pushing and 2 of our phones were stolen. We asked a bartender who proceeded to tell us that was the 6th time that night a phone was stolen. I went to buy a drink and found my ID and credit card were stolen out of my purse attached to my body. The person went immediately to GH mall and spent $10,000. I mentioned this to my neighbors who said The Stage is known for pick pocketing. As a resident of downtown I want to make tourists aware of this as it is a known problem and The Stage has not addressed it. BE CAREFUL!

We were unaware there was some sort of "dog show/convention" going n during our stay. So between the allergies (we are allergic to dogs) and the constant barking, our stay was less than pleasant. It would have been nice if the hotel had both notified guests of the dog show/convention since they would have known in advance, and kept the dogs in a specific area of the hotel in consideration of the rest of the paying guests.
Rude!!! Dont go here, waitresses are rude and snobby. Drinks are watered down. Go next door to Tootsies.

On Sunday night, their Valet came flying out of the driveway in someone's car without stopping and almost hit me.  I honked my horn, and the guy jumped out of his car screaming!  He called me a "FAGGOT"!  He's lucky I didn't shoot him when he leaned in my window screaming at me.  He told me "FUCK YOU FUCK OFF!"  Then started mocking my southern accent.  This guy has some serious anger issues and needs mental health treatment.  He needs to be fired before he gets your business into some serious liability by crashing a patron's car or assaulting someone.  I mean, he easily could have hit a pedestrian and killed them the way he was driving.

Great place to go if you are heading for a night on the town. The patio on the second floor and live music is great. They generally have good artists. 

You can valet here for a reasonable price, eat, listen to music, visit some spots and go back for your car when finished. They are in a prime location. 

There are vegetarian options which I love. Service however, is hit or miss. But.... it's broadway in Nashville and a busy area in general.

We have been to many Hard Rock cafes and will continue in other cities but I will never go back here again.   Visually we had twenty plus tables open and yet waited 35min to be seated.  Once seated our server ignored us for another 15 minuets walking by twice.

I was on a long weekend trip to Nashville from Maryland (13 hour drive). While my wife and I were walking Broadway on Sunday, we stopped in Whiskey Bent Saloon. Not only was it one of the nicest bars we walked into in Nashville, but I found a tshirt that caught my eye and I just had to have it! Unfortunately they didn't have my size and we returned home with no shirt :( I was hooked on that shirt though so I emailed them and asked if it would be possible to order one and have it shipped to me. It was a long shot but I figured, why not try?

The next day I received a phone call from the manager Zeke who couldn't have been more accommodating. I paid for the shirt and shipping and got it in the mail 4 days later! However, when I opened the package, I was slightly disappointed when it was the wrong color. Could have easily been my fault as I didn't specify a color to Zeke on the phone, but non the less, wasn't excited about it. 

I contacted Zeke again and BOOM!, he comes through once again! Another 4 days later and the right color arrives in the mail! I know, it was a stupid tshirt and he could have said he didn't have time or not even returned my message. But the customer service I received from Zeke and the Whiskey Bent Saloon was second to none. Hard to find that nowadays. HIGHLY recommend!! Can't wait to get back to Nashville next year and enjoy a cold one at the Whiskey Bent Saloon.

-Ryan

We were staying for an event on property. We had booked 2 double beds for our room, however upon arrival we were given a King room. When we stated we booked a double, the response was we're completely sold out--which explained why while we were waiting to check in we were hearing the FD staff calling for roll-aways to rooms, and then also stating it was their last one. So they had oversold our block--not our fault, shouldn't have been our problem! Thank goodness the other 2 people that were to be traveling with us had stayed home or we would have had 4 people in a King bed! This agent did the best she could, apologized, and even told us to help ourselves to anything from the shop before heading to bed. It was very late at night, there was no manager on duty, so we requested that they call us in the morning about this matter. That never happened. Due to weather conditions when we were leaving our flight out was canceled, so we called the hotel to see if we could book another night. The front desk girl who answered was so rude, I don't know why she would work in a hospitality position or customer service, she clearly doesn't like helping people. She said there was no way they could get us another night under our group block rate--even though the block was still going on. When I explained our already unpleasant experience at check in, she gave me an attitude and when I asked to speak to the manager, she said there was one, but that I couldn't speak to her! I work in hospitality and in hotels and this is the kind of employee who should find a new industry. Here we were stranded in an airport needing another hotel night and she had the opportunity to be helpful and compassionate and instead made sure to give a loud sarcastic "Have a Nice Day!" before hanging up when she heard how dissatisfied I was and that I said I'd be sending a letter to Sheraton about our experience. Our group had more than exceeded the block of rooms and brought in a huge amount of revenue to the hotel for the weekend and this was the final experience we had with them. I gave it a 2 because the event staff were very friendly, and the bed was very comfortable. However on our last day when we were exhausted and wanted to sleep in after a busy weekend, housekeeping started knocking on our door at 7:30am!

Not going to lie, I've never been a huge fan of Hard Rock Cafe locations. The food is always mediocre and I rarely find that I'm raving about the service. Sadly I wasn't "wowed" by this location either. The bartender didn't know much about their beer options and, well, a bartender should at least know a LITTLE about what they're serving. I need options! The atmosphere was just so-so ... nothing super special as we were all crammed in the doorway as we were waiting on a table. I don't know - I don't want to be a Debbie Downer for all Hard Rocks; they've just never impressed me all that much. I'd suggest checking out the NUMEROUS other bars and restaurants sprinkled along Broadway. You'll have more fun!

Great music, fun servers. There was about an hour wait, which we expected on a Saturday night. When you first walk in, it's really hectic and the staff seemed to be really scattered and flustered- They even forgot to give us a buzzer at first! 
We waited at the bar and probably should have just ordered our food to eat there, because it was a little longer than an hour wait.
Once we were seated, our server was fun and gave us really good input about the menu. our ONLY complaint about the menu was that the brisket was sold out. (it was only about 7:45) 
They then ran out of glasses- just as I had ordered another drink. I was almost done with my meal by the time I got my new drink. You would think that a large restaurant like this would be prepared for a huge rush. 
Other than that, the atmosphere was fun and it was a good place to start our night.

The Stage is a fun, casual bar. We stopped in on a Friday afternoon for a reprieve from the heat. Apparently there is a bouncer checking IDs at the door, but I walked in without getting my ID checked. Since I didn't have my hand stamped they still checked it at the bar, though. The beers are about $5 or $6 a piece, even for domestic, which seems a bit ridiculous to me. I guess that's what you get for going downtown, though. 

The live music is what really sets this place apart, though. While we were there, the band was playing some well-known country songs, but based on other reviews it seems like they play other genres as well. The only drawback of the music was that it made it difficult to have a conversation with the people I was with. 

If you are looking for a fun, casual place that has a definite Nashville vibe, I would recommend The Stage. Whether you're a local or a tourist, you are guaranteed to have a good time.

Worst customer service I have ever received from Sheraton Music City Hotel and I haven't even made it to the hotel yet. I booked it through priceline.com and made a mistake when it came to the dates. I booked for 1 day prior then what I needed. I called the hotel directly to make the change and I was first told that I was out of the window to make any changes. This was strange to me because I booked not even 5 minutes prior to calling. I was put on hold and was then told since I booked through a third party there was nothing they could do for me. So I called Priceline and their solution was to call the hotel and have them move the date or authorize refunding the reservation so I could re book the reservation. The priceline representative told me the manager Kate was rude and said that they would not authorize a refund and would not allow me to change my reservation. I asked the priceline representative what could be done and he forwarded me to the customer relations department that was going to try and help me as well.
