She spoke with another front desk manager who said they would have to speak with the revenue manager Mike. I had to call back to see what the resolution and Mike offered to move my reservation for a mysterious amount that they couldn't tell me what it would be until I got to the hotel to check in. I'm hoping this is just a bad dream and someone from priceline.com or Sheraton Music City Hotel will contact me and help me get to a resolution that makes sense. If not this has by far been the worst customer service I have ever been subjected to.
A 4-star dive bar!  Not smoky inside, which is a huge plus.  No country music here, more of a place for local jam bands/punk.  Drinks were cheap and staff friendly.  Not a bad time.

Terrible service. My friends and I waited 20 mins for a table at lunch time, which was great, but waited another 30 minutes for a server to take our drink orders. Even after flagging someone down and being told it would be taken care of, we were left waiting and eventually left. Would not recommend.
Great music nice rooftop bar. I had the Music City Mule, which is a blood orange flavor and it was delicious!

A friend and I went to the 5 Spot on Motown Monday; however didn't stay for the Motown bc it didn't start until 10pm and it was 8 pm when we arrived. We did, however, get in some free swing/jive dance lessons before the crowd arrived at 8:59pm. (Cover charge after 9pm) The place was jumping and we had a blast! Food from the "permanently parked" food truck outside was very good and hit the (5) spot!!
A place worth going to. Great live music. And it's just fun.

My wife and I love the Stage. Always has great music, and for the most part actual country music and not the fake twangy Florida Georgia Line wannabe's. Drinks are great. Servers are amazing. And it is a SAFE place. I've seen several drunk guys thrown out by security for being A-holes. This place let's you have fun, but be safe too. I hit the stage every time I'm on Broadway. And, if you happen to be there when Chris Ferrara is playing, you're in for an amazing show. Seriously the best band on Broadway. Period!
Great music! Relaxing and fun atmosphere! Another popular Broadway destination bar! The second floor was my favorite because it was more calm and had a comfy couch!

Lots of floors to enjoy music on, fantastic rooftop patio and although the bars are always packed the bartenders take care of you quickly. 
While in Nashville for 2 nights we ended up here both nights. 
Lots of fun, good bands, great time. Loved the rooftop!!

Two might seem harsh, but nothing about this place was above expectations, and there were a few things that were below expectations. The bartender was nice, not complaints there, but the cocktail/drink menu had approximately 10 drinks. Of those 10, only 3 contained whiskey, I would have guess if there were 10 drinks on the menu that at least 7 contained whiskey. Anyway, of those 3, the most appealing was variation of a Moscow Mule... which came in a styrofoam cup...really? For $14 I get a styrofoam cup?

It was a decent venue, not too crowd (and I sort of understand why). Music was good, but nothing any better than anywhere else on the strip. Overall, I'd say it was a decent place if you don't want a large crowd, but overall certainly nothing special.

Let me disclose first that hotels are more alike than different to me - I'm pretty much in-and-out of my room to sleep & shower and spend more time exploring whatever city I'm in. Okay, Las Vegas hotels are a little different.

But as far as Nashville hotels go, this Sheraton Music City is pretty solid. Since I knew I was renting a car, I didn't want to double my room price and pay for overnight parking by staying downtown. Having said that, I left the car at the downtown Omni a couple of times since Melissa & Shannon were staying there, and Daniel of the Omni staff took good care of it each time. Cool.

Back to the Sheraton: This place is huge, it took me a day to get my bearings, and every room has a balcony. The only hotel amenity I actually care about is WiFi, which is free in the lobby here but also free in the room if you're a Starwood member. And the entire place is smoke-free & dog friendly. 

And finally, this Shearton is really quiet, the hallways are really long, and returning really late one night I'm pretty sure I saw two little girls down my corridor holding hands and beckoning, "Hello Danny. Come and play with us." For one brief moment, I wondered why Daniel from the Omni was parking cars at the Sheraton. But then I went into my room and called it a night.
Bar was nice. Band was great. Bartender was preoccupied with his phone and didn't seem to realize he was working in a service industry. No conversation or eye contact.
a dungeon of hipsters who really need to get over themselves, and the space is pretty gross and crowded.  I wanted to give it 0 stars but Yelp does not permit that.

Moonshine bar!! This bar is a must for a night out on Broadway in Nashville!! They have a full bar but what makes this bar special is the moonshine selection!

A COUPLE TIPS FROM A LOCAL!!!
-There are two floors to this bar, on weekend nights the second floor is much less crowded, has a full bar (same as downstairs, and has live music too! You can also smoke on the second floor...I don't know of many bars on broadway that you can smoke in.
-When you come in, try the moonshine!! My tip for anyone I bring in from out of town is to try any of the fruity flavor moonshines with Sprite, you get the flavor without the burn from drinking it straight!! Then you can still say that you drank moonshine when you were in Tennessee

Pure dive bar with live music. Had a great time watching some pretty good talent. The older guy regular band that was on when we got there was just okay, but the rest of the acts were pretty good. Of course, this is just lucky, but Jewel showed up and sang with the Cordovas in the last set. The cordovas really rocked, little folkey, but none the less the guitar play was great.

Ever seen the movie Country Strong? I haven't, but the look on my husband's face when he realized we were in the bar where one of his favorite movies was filmed was priceless. 

The Stage is located on the main strip of Broadway and boasts one of the largest stages. They always have incredible live music playing and it's a type of bar where people visit to truly enjoy the songs. 

It's a classic and must-visit if you're bar-hopping down Broadway!

Oh, and there's no cover fee and reasonably-priced drinks.

Hello, I come here regularly sunday evenings to listen to Brian Wayne band and dance. It really has not disappointed me. I am a dancer and its a good place to dance. The people are friendly and the band is exceptional. I recommend Whiskey bent to any swing dancers or music lovers.

I thoroughly enjoyed my night out here.  There were two bands that played. I can't remember who they were.  The only recommendation I would have would be to figure out how to switch bands faster.  The service was great and it was easy to get a drink quickly the way it was set up. For the amount of people in and out of the bar it was very clean. The bathrooms were clean most of the night. Up until about 1am. They constantly had staff walking around picking up empty drinks and taking out the garbage.

I tried. Really, I did. I just didn't get it. #simoncowellshrug*

I knew what I was getting into. It was Saturday night. It was Broadway. It was a honky tonk. BUT. I had friends in town and that's what one does when one has friends in town. One goes to Broadway and hopes that one doesn't have too terrible of a time. When I am in these situations, I try to hit bars I've never been to so that I can get an experience as well. So, The Stage it was... along with every other tourist in Nashville.

The crowd wasn't so much the problem. This isn't my first rodeo. I know to expect crowds on Broadway. The problem was that it was boring. The elements were there (people, music, booze, roof top) but there was no excitement. It seemed as though everyone was going through the motions. I am fully aware that places are within their rights to have off nights. I suppose that I was there for one. To be even more clear: I'd say The Stage is more Texas than Nashville so if that's your thing, you may enjoy it more than I did.**

Not wanting to fight the mosh pit downstairs, my friends and I made our way to the roof. It was just as crowded but the roof cut out allowed for more air and a bit more room. For a Broadway bar I was surprised that the sound was so bad. I couldn't hear the band on the stage behind me. From the hoots and hollers, I got that they were a cover band, but I couldn't tell you the style. From the way the singer was slinking (at one point, bent over), I have my suspicions. The bar wasn't as chaotic as I feared. We got up to the bar fairly easily and the bartender did his job without rolling his eyes or grunting. That's a win on Broadway. But, that was it. It was a full bar of out of towners doing what they thought they should do in a Nashville bar. As a local, it wasn't my thing. We stayed for one drink and left. No cover (thanks!) made that an easy decision.

*Because Kanye shrugs -- like Kanye ' are cancelled. 
**Whereas Layla's is more Kentucky than Nashville and I enjoy it more for that reason.

The best bartenders .. Coldest beers ... And the best bands on Broadway. I have been here several times and each time it keeps getting better! This last time charley and Laura were my bartenders and made my experience amazing! I would recommend this bar to anyone visiting Nashville! Keep up the great hospitality!! Thanks!!!!

NOT ADA COMPLIANT. we could not get around this hotel, there are steps to the main restroom, carpet that makes wheel chairs extremely hard to use. there are steps leading to the first floor rooms. there is a ramp but it is way too steep and when we went down the ramp my friends who were in chairs went to fast and got stuck. going up the ramp is a whole other story. also the only way to get to the indoor pool is to go down a set of steep sets. we had to carry our friends wheel chairs down the steps to get to the pool. if you have any type of disability do NOT stay here!

This is a really cool bar. They have multiple levels with different themes. When I came I hung out on their rooftop. It was pretty busy but my friends and I got our drinks pretty quickly! The rooftop had a great view of Broadway. I enjoyed my time here! I'd definitely come back. I would suggest coming early (9pm) because when we left around 1030/11 there was a wait to go to the roof.

I have driven past The 5 Spot several times while looking for a parking spot in East Nashville. It never looked like much from the outside so the need to go never popped into in my head. However, on a Friday night I finally had a reason to go. One of my friends was doing a show there and I'm always down for some live music. Like most places in Nashville, parking can be tricky. We parked on the side of the street and it seemed to be fine. If you drive around the neighborhood long enough, you'll usually find something. Like I said, the venue does not look like much from the outside. Kind of your typical dive bar feel. Their was a person right inside checking IDs and collecting money. It was a $5 cover (cash only) for the night. There were 4 different performers so $5 seemed like a pretty good deal. When we got inside, it was pretty much what I had expected. The outside matches the inside. It's a dive bar which I'm totally fine with. I love a good dive bar. The place was busy but not too crowded. We were able to get drinks quickly and find a seat. There wasn't exactly service with a smile but I can understand this considering the noise level once the music got going. They have a good selection of beer both on tap and in bottles/cans. I had a Guinness and PBR on tap and then a Fat Tire bottle. One funny note. They have a jug behind the bar labeled "Stripper Sweat $5". It scared me how long that had been sitting there but of course people in my group had to try it for a good laugh. When they asked what was in it, the bartender replied "It's a lot". I don't think I need to try this but I'm all about other people taking the plunge. Like I said earlier, this is your typical dive bar. It's dark. The seating is at the bar or some high tops. It's nothing fancy. There is a patio outside that I forgot to check out but my boyfriend said it was pretty and had a food truck. The best part about this bar is that it is smoke free. Also, the sound is pretty good. The bands were loud but not deafening. If you want to listen to the music, you can sit up front and jam out. If you want to chat, you can hang out in the back. Overall, it was a fun night out with great music. The crowd was a good mix of people so anyone can feel comfortable here. You can check out the music schedule on their website.

My husband and I are HUGE Hard Rock fans, whenever we are traveling, which is often, we always go into Hard Rock it is our happy place because we can ALWAYS count on good food, good drinks, good service, great merchandise. So, we ducked into Hard Rock Cafe on Broadway, to have lunch, a drink and pickup our memorabilia... NO ONE even attempted to seat us, we had to hunt someone down to purchase a T-shirt (1 of only 8 available), and it was hard to identify a designated "bar", good grief this is Nashville. We expected SO MUCH MORE!

I went to The Stage this weekend while in town with some girlfriends. We were there on the early side, arriving around 8 on Saturday and the place was PACKED. The band was playing covers of semi-recent hits, which was really fun and they got the crowd engaged. It only took a couple minutes to get attention at the bar, and the woman who served me was amazing. I watched her prepare the 2 drinks I ordered while also opening 4 beers for someone else and communicating with other servers - it was like watching a beautifully choreographed dance. My G&T was solid and served in a heavy duty (reusable) plastic glass. It was a bit crowded and I felt like I got (unaggressively) touched by ~150 people moving about the place during the 45 minutes we were there (which might be normal for the Nashville night scene), but was still a good place to stop for a little honky tonkin.

A total blast!!! My friends and I headed down after dinner for Motown Monday looking for some fun to get into.

I did not know what to expect walking in- I just knew I wanted to dance the  night away. Thankfully, The 5 Spot got the message and we were on the same wavelength. Arriving around 10, the place was already packed. Early arrival is highly suggested for this very reason. 

Snagging drinks from the bar (Mondays feature 2-4-1 drinks, haaaayyyyy). Though it was packed, I felt the bartenders moved quickly to get orders taken and drinks out. i think I waited about 3 minutes for my drink and the bar was 4 deep. 

We made our way to the dance floor where we danced our asses off. Mondays feature music from the 50's, 60's, Motown, Soul, the list goes on. A nice refreshing break from the trill, ratchet music flooding every club, everywhere. The dance floor was filled with people dressed in period attire, which was pretty cool. Regardless if you think you are a good dancer or not- just lose yourself in the music, the moment (ok, almost quoted Eminem there, ha!) Check out their back patio to cool off, meet people, and enjoy your drink.

The 5 Spot features a different theme each night so there is something for everyone. I would suggest bringing cash with you for the cover. Also, keep your eyes peeled for Riddim n' Spice Food Truck. This chromed out, slick truck slangs Caribbean cuisine, blasts fun music, and a gaming system featuring the classic, Mortal Kombat. I ordered the smoked jerk chicken tacos. DANG! Fresh corn, smoky meat, and hand tossed tortillas made for perfect bar food.

An overall great experience, unexpected for a Monday night. Will definitely be one of my hang spots when I make Nashville my home!

Out of four bars we hopped into on out night out this place was the busiest. In fact it was so busy, I'm surprised the Fire Marshall hasn't closed it down. We literally could not move there was so many people in this place. 

That said, the band was one of the better bands we saw. They were your standard cover band mixed it up quite a bit to keep everyone happy. Their  fiddler jump up on the bar at one point and was really ripping, which was pretty cool.

Very mixed crowd here, but I'd say more over 30 than under. Again, super busy, but when you do finally get to the bar, the bartenders were very quick.

Only three stars because it was just too crowded.

Service was abominable.  We should have known we were in for a disappointment as soon as we walked in - the host was nowhere to be seen, then we noticed her just lollygagging around even though we (and multiple other people behind us) were waiting at the host stand for TEN MINUTES.   

Finally taken to a table.  Introduced to server.  Waited 15 minutes to get our alcoholic beverages filled (mind you, the restaurant was only at about 1/3 capacity with plenty of servers to be seen....)  Then inexplicably, our server got switched out (we thought it was a shift change... no... he was still seen in another section of the restaurant).

Server barely checked back on us, so when our meal was delivered totally incorrect (and I would blame the kitchen.... except when we mentioned it to the server, you could see on his face he messed up)... then we waited TWENTY MINUTES for the new item to come to the table.  Folks... it was a SALAD.  Brought over with ZERO apologies, my guest's food was well-consumed by then.  Still charged full price despite the huge issues.  Ugh.

As far as a Hard Rock goes --- not nearly as much memorabilia as I've seen at other locations, which was a huge disappointment in a place billed as MUSIC CITY.    hmm.

The worst Sheraton hotel we have ever stayed in. We arrived on a 90 degree day and the A/C in our room was broken. The room temperature was 75 and after 3 hours of the room set at 60 it was 78 in the room. 

After taking a shower to cool off, we discovered that the tub drained at the slowest rate possible. Took almost 3 hours for the tub to drain and it only started at my ankles.

The entire hotel looked like it was put together by 3 year olds. Moldings were not caulked, drywall wasn't finished, wallpaper was peeling. 

Do your self a favor and stay somewhere else. SPG should be ashamed of ranking this as a category 4.

Have you heard of Motown Monday's? 

Well if not, let me tell you about it... you may have been born in the 90's, maybe even the early 2000's but let me tell you, you know a LOT of Motown and it's the best music for dancing. 

Yes it's a DJ, and yes you're in Nashville, but this place is worth it! You'll see amazing dancers pick up and jive with folks they never knew and your jaw will drop to the floor. How did they do that move? How are they so well coordinated? Impressive doesn't begin to describe the dancing at 5 spot. 

If you're in need of a break, head to the back patio for some fresh air and a moment to think to yourself, but then lace up your shoes and get back up there because this will be the best Monday night you've had in a long time!
Much like Hard Rock in other cities.  A solid choice. A little bit on the pricey side, but consistent and flavorful food.  I'd recommend sticking to the burgers.  They have never let us down.

I loved this little venue. It is not in the chaos of downtown, but also not so far away from lots of things going on. The night I went was a 90s coverband. There was a cover at the door ($10) but it supposedly was a fundraiser to get women into music, so I was fine paying it. 

We got there moderately early and there was plenty of space. I can imagine it gets packed for more popular artists. The drinks were shockingly cheap and bartenders were super easy going and nice. 

Bathrooms weren't the cleanest, but what do you expect from a divey venue. The venue is small enough to feel intimate, but not too small that it holds enough people. Would recommend catching a show, even if you don't know the person playing.

I flew in from Maine to Nashville to get my first Hard Rock Cafe experience and it was also my last. From the moment we walked in the door the bartender, Lindsay, was aggressive, pushy and completely unprofessional to us. If I could give her no stars on this rating I would have. She was complaining to other bartenders and customers about us right in front of us. She had a lazy work ethic and to top it all off we were trying to leave and she gives us a dead pen so we had to wait even longer to get out of there! The drinks were not satisfactory and when we told her about it she huffed, puffed, and rolled her eyes. She exclaimed "what was wrong with them should have made them myself, what do you want now." AND her breasts were all over the place. I don't know what kind of business the Hard Rock Cafe is trying to bring in, but I will make sure all of my family and friends do not go there even if it is the last resort. Trash experience.

I wasn't sure what to expect after reading other reviews but overall very happy with our 3-night stay.  

Lobby - looks great and nicely decorated - see pictures. The only drawback was that the sitting area closest to the door meant that there was a permanent draft if you sat around long enough. 

Rooms - included a safe and mini fridge but no microwave. The safe is on the top shelf in the closet -  which is tough when if you're vertically challenged like me! Our room had a balcony overlooking the front entry which is a nice option if you want fresh air circulating. Starbucks coffee available in the room, includes 2 bottles of water. $5 extra for the larger bottles of water. 

Pool - great option for the kids after a long day of sightseeing. Adults, bring your suits too if you want to relax in the jacuzzi. 

Location - about a 10-minute drive to downtown which is about a $10-12 Uber ride if you don't want to deal with parking meters. The Sheraton shuttle is $10 (per person!) and leaves on the hour. I've stayed at Holiday Inns that will take your family anywhere within a certain distance for FREE so I was really surprised with this rather high per person rate. There's plenty of parking on both sides of the hotel and it's well lit so I felt safe going to/from the hotel at night. 

Dining options within 2-5 miles: 
- Monell's on the Manor (southern comfort food served family style). Highly recommend! 
- E. Milano's (Italian/pizza) Check in on Yelp for free cheese bread 
- Homegrown Taproom (local brews + food/sandwiches) Nice nearby option if you don't want to head downtown. 
- Jack in the Box (if you want fast food)

Otherwise, if you prefer to stay in, our friends said the breakfast buffet ($15/person) and pizza at the hotel was good. 

Overall - this hotel is a great option if you want to save more than half off the downtown hotels. Kids like having a swimming pool to end the day but the lack of a microwave and the high per person shuttle charge keeps me from rating the hotel as a 5. These are a couple factors I consider when traveling with kids. 

TIP: Sign up for the Starwood Preferred Guest for free WiFi.

Our group had a plan to hit every honky tonk and bar on Music Row, and this place was just one of those stops. 
Super fun! We had a blast. 
Would love to go back and take it all in again.

It's impossible to have a bad time in this bar!!! Tons of friendly people singing along with the incredible band, which when I was there was led by a singer named Michael.  He was highly engaging and entertaining, I'd go back just to hear him!  The guitar player, Billy, was a shredder, serious chops!! Great selection of whiskeys and bottled beers.  Super friendly wait staff!  Go and leave your inhibitions at the door!!!!

If you are looking for Classic Country from the 80's and 90's, this is the place to be EVERY THURSDAY night from 6:00-10:00! The Randy Nations Band, featuring the vivacious and extremely talented vocalist Taria Long, will not disappoint!! While you are there, purchase her CD full of original songs! We moved to Nashville in July and make it a point to go as often as we can!

This place is one of my favorite bars in Nashville!  Bartenders are very friendly and attentive, the lighting is cool, and the love bands are always great!  I love how many floors they have and that each floor has a different feeling to it. The rooftop is awesome, as you can see the Broadway fully from it. Love this place!

Best hotel experience I have ever had, and I travel A LOT. I've never experienced such caring, attentive staff in my life at a hotel. Given my choice, I'd stay at the Music City Sheraton every day, but that might add up! 

5/5 100%

Food is amazing, too!

I decided to book this hotel because it was close enough to the city but far enough that u didn't have to worry about all the craziness of the downtown area, good value & close to the airport. 
Once we arrived & checked in, we get to our room but it was the wrong size bed, I got a King size bed but ended up in a room with 2 beds useful if traveling with friends/family not for us. I called the front desk & spoke with Hailey who apologized & fixed our issue initially we got a room on the 4th floor after she fixed the mix up we ended up on the first floor much better with the right size bed. 
We got room #1062, it had a nice comfy bed, good toiletries & a mini fridge along with the open terrace & easy pool access, nice outside pool area, they also have an indoor pool. 
We happen to be celebrating a birthday after our mix up Hailey was nice enough to offer us a free drink ticket for one day & ended up giving us breakfast vouchers, sweetttt .. breakfast is buffet style for the vouchers or u can order from their menu for a price. 
The buffet is not bad at all u have the basics, typical fruits & yogurt, breads, bagels also biscuits, some sausage, bacon & eggs enough food to satisfy a quick meal before heading out to explore the city. 
my only complain was house keeping it was not quite on point, we had our drinks one day & the beer glass was left in our room the entire time, toiletries were not changed everyday. I also found a cheeto in one of the folded towels. we did get bed changed & towels daily, they also replaced the free water which was very helpful. 
The hotel grounds are nicely kept, nice lobby area & the staff was nice we enjoyed our stay.

I still have not gotten my food as I am sitting here waiting for it and writing this review. It took us 20 minutes for our server to come say hello and ask us what we want to drink. Water or anything. 40 minutes later, she came back to check up and see if we needed a refill. We did. 

I would get it if the place was busy but it's empty. There are a total of 6 tables upstairs and rarely do we see the staff helping other guests. The only thing that is enjoyable is the entertainment. 

Also, I understand that the servers have no control over the kitchen and when they have the food ready, but they can certainly check up on us and check up on our drinks. They haven't. The only reason I gave them 2 stars is because of the entertainment.

When in Nashville.....came for vacation from Richmond, VA and are staying in a B&B in East Nashville and were told to walk down and try this place. After reading so many great reviews we had to try it. No wait on a Sunday at 11:30. Awesome pizza and friendly service. We sat at the bar and Stuart was fabulous! She serves pizza and drinks with a friendly smile and great attitude. The pizza has a wonderful very thin but slightly crispy crust with homemade sauce. I ordered the prosciutto and fresh basil pizza....mmmmmm!

On our last night in Nashville, my wife and I stopped by The 5 Spot on $2 Tuesday to check out some live music. 

All of the staff at The 5 Spot were really friendly and the drinks were reasonably priced. We showed up at around 8:30 since that was when the music was supposed to start. In reality, it was more like 9:30 - 9:45, and I get the feeling that is how it normally goes. I would probably recommend showing up around then if you want to see the live music. 

In the mean time, we had some drinks at the bar and ordered some food from the taco truck they have outside the venue. The food was the only disappointing this about this bar. We ordered some chips and salsa and what we received in exchange for our $4 was basically a small handful of cheap store-bought tortilla chips and a thimble's worth of cheap store-bought salsa. You should definitely get food from somewhere else before coming here.

Despite the music starting late and the food being underwhelming, the excellent music performances made the whole experience at The 5 Spot worthwhile. All of the acts that we saw were incredibly talented and fun to watch. We would highly recommend checking out $2 Tuesday. Just show up late and eat somewhere else.

We went last night, Thursday, at 10:30pm when Jesse Cain band came on. They check everyone for ID at the door. We found seating right at the bar. The band played everything from Johnny Cash, Charlie Daniels, and Garth Brooks. The dueling fiddle players were crazy good. The band was really entertaining, very talented singers and musicians.

The patrons were a lot of fun, and the $8.50 Captain and cokes were good.

First, the hotel is pretty nice. The customer service is what I have issue with. 

When you pay for a hotel, you pay for certain aminities. When I arrived, after a 6 hour drive, I had 10 minutes if AC before a citywide blackout. 

Now, I know that is an act of God which is unpredictable but our first night in the hotel was sans air in July. It was miserable. The only thing my best friend and I could do was open the balcony door to let some night air in the room. By doing this, we could hear (all night) a group of very loud men in the pool/balcony area. At 1am, I went down to complain and ask the status of the outage.  I was told that they would find the men who were keeping us awake and have them hold it down. I was also told the outage was being resolved.

At 5am, we just couldn't take it anymore. No one had resolved the loud guest problem and we were so uncomfortably hot, we decided to go find breakfast somewhere.

About that time the power came back on.

Today, when I checked out, I asked if they would discount the room. Let's face it, it may not have been controllable but you had guests that didn't sleep and paid ahead of time for amenities that we didn't receive.

Instead of being polite, the front desk guy rudely told me no, I would not receive any discount. I was merely asking a question. A reasonable question. And I wasn't being a jerk. I paid money that I worked hard for and was uncomfortable an entire night to the point that I did not sleep.

When I told the guy that I planned to contact his corporate office, he said "Well you do that. You weren't the only person inconvenienced. 23,000 other people were affected." He said it snarky. Again, I was simply asking a question and as a paying customer, I expect better service than that. I do not appreciate being talked to like a spoiled brat. 

I do NOT recommend this hotel to anyone. It might be okay if your trip is uneventful... But should something inconvenience your stay, don't expect Sheraton to do anything about it and surely don't ask the guest services people about it or risk being treated rudely.

This is one of my favorite places on Broadway because they have a roof top and you can see all downtown. BUT you have to walk up those stairs. 
They have music downstairs. There are a few levels. I don't know if they have music on each level at the same time. 
We had a really nice time on a Friday afternoon listening to nice music on a bright sunny day eating hummus and vegetables while the teenagers had chicken nuggets. Yes, they let them in during the day. 
They serve the wine in a plastic cup to remind you that you are on Broadway. They have several vegetarian options which are good for the Gluten intolerant friends. Drinks are very reasonable too. 
Put on the list to visit and you WILL see a bachelorette party.

Not sure why this hotel isn't ranked higher. It is at minimum a 4. 
The lobby and building was in excellent condition with 5 star customer service. The room was exceptionally clean and the workout room was the best one I've been to in a bonvoy chain. 2 pools and a hot tub, free parking, 12 noon check out. 
My only complaint is I could smell cigarettes . Not sure if I was near smoking rooms or a break room but it was distinguishable

Dinner last night was slow being served. The pulled pork meat was very good but dry not much sauce. I asked for a lemon which I never got. The cole slaw was without taste. The fries you could get anywhere. Buy the shirt and take the picture but eat dinner somewhere else. Disappointing they used to have such good food and menu choices.

I don't know, maybe some people like dark, smoked-fill hipster dungeons that wreak of vomit and STD's, but not this guy. And if that weren't enough - let's turn the heavy metal up to 11 so that the patrons have to scream at each other. And make sure the bathrooms doors don't lock, people love that. The live music venue may be the only redeeming factor here, but the sound guy must be deaf - again, way too loud. In a place where I could've easily caught something worse, I suppose I should be thankful I only left with tinnitus.

I tried. Really, I did. I just didn't get it. #simoncowellshrug*

I knew what I was getting into. It was Saturday night. It was Broadway. It was a honky tonk. BUT. I had friends in town and that's what one does when one has friends in town. One goes to Broadway and hopes that one doesn't have too terrible of a time. When I am in these situations, I try to hit bars I've never been to so that I can get an experience as well. So, The Stage it was... along with every other tourist in Nashville.

The crowd wasn't so much the problem. This isn't my first rodeo. I know to expect crowds on Broadway. The problem was that it was boring. The elements were there (people, music, booze, roof top) but there was no excitement. It seemed as though everyone was going through the motions. I am fully aware that places are within their rights to have off nights. I suppose that I was there for one. To be even more clear: I'd say The Stage is more Texas than Nashville so if that's your thing, you may enjoy it more than I did.**

Not wanting to fight the mosh pit downstairs, my friends and I made our way to the roof. It was just as crowded but the roof cut out allowed for more air and a bit more room. For a Broadway bar I was surprised that the sound was so bad. I couldn't hear the band on the stage behind me. From the hoots and hollers, I got that they were a cover band, but I couldn't tell you the style. From the way the singer was slinking (at one point, bent over), I have my suspicions. The bar wasn't as chaotic as I feared. We got up to the bar fairly easily and the bartender did his job without rolling his eyes or grunting. That's a win on Broadway. But, that was it. It was a full bar of out of towners doing what they thought they should do in a Nashville bar. As a local, it wasn't my thing. We stayed for one drink and left. No cover (thanks!) made that an easy decision.

*Because Kanye shrugs -- like Kanye -- are cancelled.
**Whereas Layla's is more Kentucky than Nashville and I enjoy it more for that reason.

OK I have to admit it was the music that drew me into this place. A guy named Ryan Tolson was playing and his band. He was absolutely phenomenal. If you could've seen him sing "the devil went down to Georgia!" you would have thought you died and went to heaven. He was an amazing guitar player! We thought that the food menu looked good and we needed some food in our stomachs because we were drinking so this looked like our place. I have to admit the poor girl who was the bartender, the waitress, the cleanup person, and God knows what else I felt sorry for. We sat down and ordered drinks right away. It was happy hour and they said domestic beer was three dollars we ordered a beer that was made in Nashville and we were charged six dollars. I said isn't this domestic and this waitress said no. How could it not be domestic if it's made in Nashville? Whatever, it's what we wanted so we got it. We ordered the soft pretzel appetizer and it took about 45 minutes to get. We knew there was no way we were ordering any other food! I waited for Ryan to finish his set and the new band came on and we stayed around for a couple songs. We never saw this waitress again. She was so busy working the bar and whoever owns this joint has a lot of explaining to do. We literally could've walked out the front door and no one would've been any the wiser. However we are not that kind of people so we walked back to the bar with the latest bill that the waitress gave us and she tacked on the last few drinks we had and we paid our bill. If I was her I would quit. She is totally overworked! We couldn't even leave her a good tip because we never saw her! Yeah you might have good music, you might have good food even though we wouldn't know, but the service is horrific!

Really great staff, good food and not far from the heart of The District in downtown. I really enjoyed my meal here and I didn't feel rushed to eat and leave as you do at several other downtown restaurants! I will definitely come back here

If you want to eat here so that you can say you did, then go ahead. Otherwise, I would eat elsewhere. 
The service was good. Our waitress was really sweet. 
Food wise, it was average. I've had just as good or even better at any cheaper chain restaurant like Applebee's. 
Sadly, I didn't look at the price of a soft drink and was shocked when I got the bill. $3.79! Maybe in NY City, but Nashville?!?! That's ridiculous. I got the sweet tea. It was actually terrible. I don't mean just average. I mean terrible. 
Husband got hamburger and said it was good. Not great, just good. I paid extra for flavored fries. A complete waste of money! I could barely taste the difference between the regular fries and the "flavored" ones. 
So go buy  a t-shirt in the gift shop and eat somewhere else.

I had a good experience here.  Just one visit, so I'll keep it short - but I liked it and will be back.

The Southwest Salad with chicken (an add-on option) was really excellent.  The chicken was very well seasoned and full of flavor.  I'm not sure what the dressing was, but I supplemented with some of their hot BBQ sauce and it worked really well.

I liked the atmosphere (sat outside) and laid-back attitude, and our server was friendly, quick, and professional.

We checked into this hotel the night of my birthday. It is a very beautiful establishment, close enough to the city (15 min cab ride to downtown nashville) and far enough from all the craziness.

The check in process was quick and easy, my lady booked a king sized bed room and it was quite a ways from the elevator. Once we walked in our room we realized we got a double bed room, which was not what we asked for, we called the front desk and were told to speak with Hailey.

Hailey took care of us and gave us our king room with an outside deck entrance to their outdoor pool. She also gave us complimentary breakfast buffet passes for our entire stay for the inconvenience, very cool! I told her it's my bday so she also gave us two free passes for cocktails at their lobby bar.

The room was big, great amenities, good working a.c., everything was clean, up to date and also had a mini fridge and a big TV. The outdoor deck was an added bonus, being able to walk to the pool from our bed is always a great way to spend a lazy day. 

This hotel is definitely large, they have cool Johnny cash memorabilia, great amenities like a jacuzzi, an indoor pool past their gym, the outdoor pool, a bar, decent buffet and they also have shuttles to and from the airport. As well as a friendly and helpful staff.

This is definitely a great hotel to stay in even if you want to spend most of your stay in downtown Nashville.

It is a Hard Rock Cafe in another city. Good for Tourists looking for Nashville stuff in the gift shop. Nothing stands out that I have to say because I live in Nashville. The Hard Rock Cafe in Vegas a different story. I can get collectibles at Walmart in Nashville..so really the tourist location loses it luster here on me. Prices are a bit pricey for average chain food grub. If not a local, maybe stay away. Why pay for parking when you can get average food down the street for free parking. NOW this is NOT to say this is not a place to visit when you visiting Nashville. It has COOL stuff only Nashville will have. If I had someone come to visit and ask specifically about the Hard Rock, of course I would take them. Otherwise, not so much. Not against this place, just not for it as a local.

To the bouncer that decided to man handle my sister tonight.  What an eye opener that things like this truly can happen to anyone at anytime.  To most a simple, please don't do that would do.  But for him he seemed it necessary to grab her arm and pull her out of the bar with force.  Trust me I am not naive and understand drunk patrons do a lot of things.  But I'm one of many witnesses that will say she was doing nothing wrong.  So I could cuss them out and I could raise my voice but what's the point.  All I ask is for people to realize it's NEVER okay to grab a woman the way he did and I'd say the same thing If he was a man being mistreated.  It's 2018.  Get your shit together.

The best service ever Chevy was our waitress, she was the bomb!  Very personable,  the Manager was running his Bum off ,  i guess there was a grease fire the day before and so the food was running slow but the Manager on Monday the 26th night wasn't, LOL.  I told my husband i bet when he started this Morning He was 400 lbs. Now Hes just a string bean.   But We spent our 2nd Anniversary there!!!   It was perfect

Awful carpet that smelled up the entire entrance. This hotel would not be on my list to stay at again when I visit Nashville. From the outside it's quite large and appealing from the sheer size.  The parking lot get's quite filled up easily so parking can be an issue.  When you walk in the main entrance it's very dated.  Old world style decor.  I did happen to see some signs saying pardon our dust why we renovate so maybe they are revamping the whole hotel.  They need to. 

The weekend we came in they had a super large convention going on for sorority sisters.  No not young college students.  This must have been some kind of reunion after 40 plus years cause the average age was 60 and up. They seemed to be having a great time.  So due to this our first night we had two full size beds instead of a king.  The next day they did give us another room with a king size bed but it was a hassle to pack, leave our luggage downstairs until the room was ready later.  The front desk staff seemed as if they were at their wits end of having much patience.  Not the most friendly.

The beds had nice comfy sheets, comforters and pillows, and the bed luckily was comfy.  It looked to be fairly clean until I saw streak marks all over the shower and bathroom mirror.  Not to happy with a quick clean job.  For the money you pay here, I think we paid $160 a night, I guess I just expected much cleaner rooms.

The pool was pretty and they had a nice bar downstairs.  I just think you can find nicer hotels than this one in the area.

I love the Stage for its large main stage and the artists that appear on it. Also, I've heard of surprise visits by some big names which has got to be an amazing thing to see when you're just there hanging out. 

The place is always pretty crowded and it's difficult to get to the bar. That would be the biggest negative about The Stage. But the quality of live music and - this is important after all those beers - the gigantic bathrooms which can accommodate lots of ladies are clutch. Definitely a must-visit while in Nashville.
Simply a really great bar.  Always fun, different music.  $5 beers and drinks ( a la 5-spot name).   And staff that clearly enjoy their jobs...

Review your check carefully. I ordered a flavor moonshine and a coke and vodka for which I was charged $21 excessive. When I reviewed my check there were 4 items listed. I questioned the check and 1 item was removed but they had an additional charge for the "rock" which I was told was sue moonshine had an additional ounce.  I never asked for additional ounce. Musician accepted request and was pretty good

I found this Saloon the last time I passed through Nashville on a cross country motorcycle trip to Arizona in April of '18. I liked this place so much then I left with a shirt. I knew when I planned on stopping through on my way to Ft Hood, TX I would be making my way back here during the night and I certainly did. I tried out two other bars before I ended up back here, I couldn't stay away. Again, this place had the best live band of the three bars I went too that night. They engaged the crowd, played all their songs well, and were happy to take requests free of charge. Another bonus here is the bartenders are very good at making the drinks and look great doing it ;).

Wouldn't let me and my husband in the door bc he had ripped (buckle) jeans, then let the girl behind us in with ripped jeans. When I asked why he said girls could go in with ripped jeans but guys could not. Go somewhere else. They suck.

Got drinks here with the hubby up on the second floor. Prices were great compared to the rest of the bars on broadway! Cheap actually. It has a great view from the second floor balcony and is a nice place to sit down and sip on a cocktail (while people watching). I honestly couldnt believe how disappointing the music was and how dead it was inside. Those were the only downsides. While I would guess that most people don't come to HRC to have an 'authentic' Nashville experience, I expected for a country-esk band to be playing at least and for there to be more than one measly bachelorette party and another table filled on the floor. 

In short, don't go here if you're looking for a real Nashville honky tonk place. Go hear if you want some cheap drinks, good people watching from the balcony, and some rock music (I guess that is what the name says).

I see that this place receives mixed feelings from its customers, so I'll throw a mostly positive one into the hat.

I love the fact that the hotel is away from the hustle and bustle of downtown, even though I spent my weekend there (distance wasn't bad at all). The lobby, restaurant, and bar were absolutely beautiful. I did stay in the midst of a renovation, but could hardly tell except for when the elevator stopped on the 2nd and 3rd floors.

My room was quite spacious and accommodating. No complaints there.

I was accidentally given a key to an occupied room (no accidents), and the lady at the desk seemed shocked and told me that their system does that from time to time. It was resolved quickly. I also had to walk quite a ways to get to my room, though. I guess that just comes with being a large hotel. Not much they can do.

P.S. - I booked through Expedia and got a rate about a third of the usual rate.

Literally left my baby's carrier inside at closing time and asshole security on Tuesday, January 2nd 2019, wouldn't even let me in just to GRAB IT so I could carry my child to our car and home. NEVER COMING HERE AGAIN! Can't believe the guy at the door was such an asshole he would't even look for me. He just sat there shaking his head. I had to run my freezing child to the car with my family because he was to lazy to help. Screw this place they are NOT family friendly!

Touristy places like this are often over-priced, and nowadays can be found in almost every medium or large sized city.  This location isn't a must go to place for locals, and probably gets most business from out-of-towners.  The food is decent, and they actually have some parking (which is rare for most downtown Nashville restaurants).  My biggest issue I have with the Nashville Hard Rock is the volume of the recorded music.  They sometimes have live acts, but their recorded music is played so loud you literally can't have a conversation with others unless you're almost shouting.  You might actually become nauseous.  For this reason we've only been here a couple of times. Don't think we'll go back any time soon.

We stopped into numerous "honky tonk" bars along Broadway and this was my favorite.  It might be because I was totally in love with the band performing on the top floor.  They were great!

Three total floors, with a heated rooftop bar as well.  Despite the very chilly temperatures we could comfortably stand right by the open garage doors.  There was plenty of room on the second and third floors to enjoy the great live music - no fighting through a jam-packed crowd, finally!!!

Staff was great and the beer selection was better than I expected.

Definitely the highlight of my bar-hopping!

It is my first time in Nashville, absolutely love "Whiskey Bent Saloon"!! Great energy, awesome live music entertainment. The entertainers will take any music request at no charge (if they know it then they will certainly play it). Guns N Roses hands down my favorite. My drink was made pretty good too! Now this is my kinda bar. Fun, upbeat, lots of good vibes, and just really good engagement. I'd definitely recommend! Thank you for a great time Whiskey Bent!

We came and visited from out of town because a friend of ours was dj'ing. We figured we'd give it a try. 
It was a great place, but not what we were looking for on this trip. 
The dj was great, the staff was overly friendly, and the crowd wasn't too bad. 
Had this had been more of what we were seeking out for this trip we definitely would've spent some more time here!
Each floor has matching powerful energy. Lots of talent and fun! Only downside is finding the restrooms or what room your friends are in.

Ok experience , staff somewhat indifferent but will try again.  Food was good, took a minute but satisfied upon arrival.  Parking a bit of a chore, but it's downtown and expected.  Street performers a bit distracting but once inside felt more comfortable .  Looking forward to some brunch another day.

First I loved this bar first time I'm in Nashville.  Was enjoying myself listening to the Chris Weaver band until this woman in a hockey shirt and braided pigtails with a baseball cap decided that she wanted to pick a fight with my girlfriend and I.  All we were doing was dancing and she accidentally elbowed my friend several times.  It happens the place was crowded.  We are patient people.  But of course she was highly intoxicated. All we did was ask her if she could try to stay in her own personal space with a smile.  She came after my friend, she moved so she decided to come after me.  Luckily there was a 6'6" man with his wife watching the whole thing.  He intervened and talked to her husband and then she stopped.  Well I thought until she threw a beer bottle at my legs.  We left and told the bouncer on our way out.  He was very nice and listened.   I would of gladly given the bar 5 stars but your local drunks ruined it for us.  Very disturbing.

Ordered a mixed drink here that had pineapple juice in it. I watched the bartender make it & she used the entire can of pineapple and a little more from another can. All it tasted like was juice. I had to ask for another shot on the side to go with my juice. Lol. I bartended also so I know the pours and this was definitely under the standard. It also took a few minutes to get service because she was on her phone before realizing we were there.
Great place for live music and a drink! The cover charge has taken me by surprise a few times, but it's worth it.

What? You live in Nashville and don't have allergies? You want to know how it feels to have rheumy eyes? Come here. I'll give Foobar this much - it lives up to its name! I'll also give it this - if you aren't from around there, you really have no business hanging out there. It's a strictly locals only place that is as inviting as an oyster with its trap shut. I saw people (it could be the light, but I only saw white folks) walk in, slap each other on the backs, hug, dance and have a great time. A supremely loud band was banging out on the nearby stage in the adjacent room to an audience of about 6 people. Suddenly a health inspector walked in with a cop in tow, and went about pointing his flashlight everywhere, looking for something. Then, a bouncer came in and yelled, "Who has a black Acura?" One dude raised his hands, and the bouncer said, "Someone rear ended into your car." After half an hour, I went out to take a call, and I found the place swarming with cops, a dude being arrested, and cop cars going up and down the road. That's when I figured that this place must be Magic Kingdom to a bunch of people for they see something in here that I don't, and I need GTFO.

By far the BEST bar in Nashville for awesome-old school- country.  Filled with memorabilia, simply but tasty menu. Service is busy.....with location being popular, but they were very friendly and attentive.  We stop in every night we are here just to listen to the music we love.

Hard to say what hasn't been said about the Ryman. It's literally one of the best places in the country to hear live music as it was built as a church before the days of amplified acoustics.

A few tips: the first two rows of the balcony are some of the best seats in the house. The first two front rows on the floor are folding chairs. When seeing a show the merchandise area is on the second floor; get there early if you want one of the limited edition hatch print show prints of your show as they sell out quick.

Super Fun!  Went to Roberts on a Thursday night, after being at the Wildhorse Saloon.  What a fun surprise!  The crowd was a blast, the music was great! Wish I'd spent my night here instead of the Wildhorse.

We started our Nashville weekend at Roberts. It was supposed to be one of many stops on our first day! Problem is we never left. Great music, great drinks, fantastic $4 Fried Bologna & Cheese Sandwich and the best bartenders ever (Rachel & Shyann)!!!!! You must stop here while in Nashville; stop for one or stay 5 hours like we did!!!!

This is my favorite bar downtown. It's the vibe and the music. Lots of room to get around and they play great bands. Quick to get drinks as well. This bar feels like more of a 30's and up crowd where like tootsies is more 20s. Now don't get me wrong there all all ages everywhere and there is always a mix it does tend to fell this way.

This is a gorgeous convention center that is well located in downtown Nashville.  It's right by all the Nashville attractions, and there are a bunch of upscale business hotels nearby so that conference goers can wrack up their points.

It is so big that there are pockets where cell phone reception is rather rotten.  I'm glad that there was sponsored free wifi for my conference.

Also, there's a huge capacity in the 4th floor ballroom, but there aren't a ton of escalators or elevators, so it becomes a cluster f getting out of there.

Great place for original country music!!
Listening to John Shepherd. They have great bar food, like fried bologna sandwiches!!

Good drinks, probably good food but we never received our order. We loved our waitress but she had way too many tables for a Friday night and we had awful service. The whole staff looked miserable. Wasted our whole Friday night sitting waiting for drinks, food that never came and for our checks.

Couldn't have asked for a better brunch experience. We went on a rainy Saturday so we sat inside but I did notice outdoor seating. They had live music and the singer was really good, sometimes we even forgot that it was live. Because of this live music we read that it was a two hour limit but it wasn't too busy and we stayed a little longer than two hours. We didn't get kicked out so don't let that be a deal breaker. They had a bunch of cocktails to choose from including coffee ones. The coffee ones were 9 dollars on the menu but when we got the check we found out they were only 6 dollars and it was happy hour! My friends raved about the Bloody Mary bar although I didn't try it. The server was very attentive with refilling our drinks and keeping us updated on the food ETA. She strongly recommended the coconut mojito and we were glad she did. The server even gave us recommendations about where to go to watch the Predators game.

I was here for a large party,  limited menu,  company dinner. The filet was great as was the pork chop. The salad was a great mix of greens and a sweet dressing. 

The place is in a cool neighborhood and the locals say was all warehouses years ago. Service was good and the restroom was tidy. The band was fantastic. I was worried I would hear all country music and when the played Sinatra and other standards it made for a great atmosphere for dinner.

Birth of the Bluegrass, 1945! The history in this place is incredible. I was only in downtown Nashville for 12 hours and experiencing this venue was one of the funnest nights of my life. I've learned my lesson and will purchase tickets early next time because there is no general admission, which might be obvious for some events but not always the case when a rock band is playing.

What a great place for a concert, if you don't sit behind a column, or tall people.
We had a couple of rude people in front of us that wouldn't stop talking and wouldn't get off their cell phones... 
But other than that little burp, what a splendid place to see a concert. 
I was fortunate enough to see a Legend tonight.. Miss Loretta Lynn.
Sound was good, nearly every seat is good, is small enough that it's comfortable, not like a big cavern...
It was a little warm, A/C was not cranking as much as it could have - in order to make everyone comfortable, so sitting next to someone in very close proximity makes it a little warm.....

I would definitely go back to see another performance, and I would also wear lighter weight fabric.
Bottled water was $3.
Tickets were reasonable.
Bathrooms were ample.
Isles were spacious so you didn't feel like you were in an airplane, all squished up.
I was actually able to extend my legs underneath the next row..

This was definitely an experience, and it was truly awesome to see Miss Lynn.
I was like a kid in a candy store.

I will post photos when I get a chance.
Them popsicles are poppin. Your friends are fake asf if they haven't dragged you here yet.

We tried to eat lunch here today, but were turned away because we had our water bottles in our bag.  We are here for CMA fest and it's over 90 degrees.  Even the music venues let you bring them in and encourage you to keep them filled.  So no burgers & beers for us.  We went to another place down the street.
We went to the Gulch for a nice meal.  Sambuca had great entertainment, nice food, and great drinks.  We had an excellent time.

If you are a music history buff, and especially if you love all things country, the Ryman Auditorium should be a definite stop on your list! This was where the Opry began and the home of bluegrass. We took a self-guided tour ($20/person) and spent as long as we wanted strolling through the auditorium and soaking up the energy of musicians who made the place what it is today. There's an eerie kind of energy that permeates the place - sort of spiritual. I especially liked seeing the displays of costumes on the lower floor in the back of the theatre. I opted to get my picture snapped on stage and for ten bucks, it's a great souvenir. For a few dollars more you can get a guided tour which takes you backstage to dressing rooms and the like. We thought the time we spent was plenty.
I almost - almost - opted for my own private studio recording time. For an extra $20 you can sing one of several songs and get it recorded in their studio. I just didn't see any songs that I thought I could adequately sing! (That's my story and I'm sticking to it).
They are back to live performances here - if you get the chance to see a show, DO IT! I'm told the acoustics in this theatre are some of the best in the world. And who knows, you might just sit next to Dolly for a show or see the ghost of Conrad Twitty...

Loved the atmosphere here!  We saw The Silver Threads perform and they were terrific...covered Linda Rondstadt, Patsy Cline...we bought a couple of their CDs.  I love that they serve fried baloney sandwiches!  (It's something I hadn't had since my childhood.) Definitely worth a visit!

Really frustrated by this visit, planned months in advance for my birthday. The food quality was decent though the filets our party ordered were average at best and served cold. The salad was excellent. Also, I ordered a side is asparagus not knowing the filet was served over asparagus. The server should have mentioned this. Also, I couldn't get my drink refilled until my meal was almost done.

But the biggest issue was the 70s rock band who, in the middle of a Springsteen song, stopped and the lead singer said bourbon was more important than Springsteen as the band did double shots. Then they laughed they forgot the lyrics and took a break. If you were planning a break  you couldn't wait until the song was over to snort up the booze? This is really unprofessional when you have a room full of dinner guests subjected to juvenile behavior by grown men. Felt like they cared more about their drinking then the paying customers.

I cannot even fathom how this place has anything less than 5 stars. 

The first time I came here was about 4 years ago on a family vacation to Nashville. All of us absolutely LOVED it. The atmosphere, live music and food were all amazing. I don't typically remember meals but I remember those scallops perfectly because they are truly the best I've ever had. 

Fast forward 4 years and I'm back visiting Nashville with my boyfriend. I hyped up Sambuca and said it was one place we HAD to go to while in town. After checking Yelp and seeing 3.5 stars I was nervous it had gone down hill. We got to sambuca at about 8pm on a Wednesday night. We were told the dining room was reserved all night but could grab a seat in the bar area. We had great seats with a perfect view of the amazing funky blues/jazz/soul band that was playing. Our bartender, Clayton, was incredible. Such a nice guy and gave us outstanding service. 

I didn't even have to look at the menu because I had been dreaming of having these scallops again for the past 4 years. They did not disappoint!! I was sooo happy that they were as amazing as I remember. Seriously worth a stop if you're in the area!!! You will not be disappointed.

Review as a music venue: I just went to my very first concert at the Ryman this week, and it was everything I thought it would be. It's an amazing experience to hear an artist perform in this 100+ year old church turned music venue that has heard and seen the greats of music and film and theater and politics and everything else on the stage. Great acoustics. Great seating - hard to find a bad seat in the house (I think the worst seats may actually be the very first rows on the orchestra floor, because you might have your view blocked by people ahead of you and you have to look up at an angle to see the stage)! We sat on the balcony, and our seats were great. We had a great view of the act we were there to see (Elle King). The pew/seats were more comfortable than I thought, but (no biggie) you do have to get up and out of the seats to let people through, because the pews are a bit too close together to allow someone to walk in front of you. They sell beer and wine and cocktails (and let you take them into the venue), but they're pricey. My advice: get a drink at Cafe Lula (just outside the Ryman - just before the metal detectors at the back entrance where you go in for concerts)! Their beer and other drinks are cheaper (my beer was $5, rather than the $8+ inside at the Ryman), and they let you take them into the Ryman. All in all, seeing a show at the Ryman is such a cool experience! I know I'll be back!

Review of the tour: When my friend from Austin came to visit me in Nashville, I was looking for activities we could do around the city. Touring the Ryman was at the top of my list! We went on a Saturday afternoon for the self-guided tour. It was so worth it! I didn't know anything about the history of the Ryman, and the self-guided tour starts with an entertaining and informative video. I had NO idea that the Ryman was almost torn down and was vacant for years after the Grand Ole Opry moved from the building! After the video, you can walk around the Ryman, sit in the pews, take photos of the amazing architecture, including the gorgeous stained glass. In the stairwell of the auditorium, there are several panels that detail the history of speakers and performers at the Ryman over the years! Once you get down to the first floor of the auditorium, they have dresses, guitars, hats, etc. worn by famous performers at the Ryman. The self-guided tour is $20 - but it's worth it! It's one of the most fun things I've done in Nashville! I learned a lot about the city, the Ryman, and country music! (There's also a guided backstage tour that is $30.) Tons of fun! Highly recommended!
Awesome time portal to the Golden Age of music. What a treat. Filled with memorabilia.

I came to Nashville one weekend for a bachelorette party!

This place had good reviews so we tried it out.

Their drinks were pretty great. I drank a Naked Margarita and it was perfect. I sampled a few other drinks that my table ordered and nothing disappointed.

We ordered mostly tapas and it was perfect to just have a few bites of everything. We ordered the Chicken Samosas, Shrimp & Crab Dip, Chicken & Beef Satay, Tomato Caprese, Goat Cheese Stuffed Artichokes, and Margherita Pizza. None of these dishes disappointed.

My favorite by far were the Goat Cheese Stuffed Artichokes. They were absolutely delicious. 

The atmosphere of this place is also pretty cool. The decor is very trendy. We went on a Friday night and they had live music. Can't remember the name of the band but they were awesome.

Definitely would recommend this place to anyone visiting Nashville!

All around a wonderful experience. We walked in on a Thursday night without a reservation and were seated right away.  Started with a delicious naked margarita and beet appetizer.  The server was extremely friendly, helpful and knowledgable about the menu.  i tried the blackened red snapper and maple sweet potatoes and ate every last bit!!  I was too full for dessert although I imagine it would be as good as the rest of the meal.
Amazingly enough this great little dive bar with a good band had the best fried green tomatoes I've ever had... I cannot come back to Nashville to come to this place!

Wow. We just asked the server if she could bring us drinks. Direct quote "I'm sorry, I don't have time. I have 5 people waiting at the bar". I get it - you are busy - but you don't EVER tell a customer you don't have time for them. Especially when you just brought drinks to the table next to us. #worstserviceever #wontcomeback
The Arcs are going to rock the church tonight. Always venerable venue keeps us coming back. Love love love the Ryman.
Without a doubt, the best, most genuine honky tonk in town. Always cheap, always amazing music. ALWAYS take your family or friends visiting in town here.

Great vibe and wonderful service! A very chill place for great live music. Attracts an older (wilder) crowd, which adds to the charm and appeal of this place. Hope, our bartender was very attentive and made our night with a steady flow of good drinks.

Came with a group for a late night dinner, ambiance outside was nice, I had the crab and shrimp scampi (minus the shrimp) and it was pretty good. I went to order a 2nd drink and was told the bar was closed, yet I noticed another server coming out with a round for the table next to us, not to mention some folks at our table joined us after, with drinks they bought at the bar. They closed early for a Friday night. Felt like our server was just done, and wanted out.

SO fun! this bar was the first bar we went to while in Nashville. The live music was awesome and the drinks didn't cost an arm and a leg. The giant Jenga they have in the back was really fun along with the photo booth. We had such a good time here. And their QUESO was AMAZING.

My brother and I decided to go here for some food and drinks before a show at the Ryman a couple weeks ago. Read the reviews on here and decided it looked like a pretty decent place.

The atmosphere is AWESOME. Everyone else has described it, so I don't think I can really add on to it that much. I'm not really a country music fan, but the bands that they have there really know how to play, and there's no cover charge, which is always a plus. I also loved the decor, it was great. There were a ton of cowboy boots and dollar bills on the walls and it just seemed like a really fun place.

They have a great amount of beers available (even though I only got a Blue Moon) and everything was decently priced so that was great. My brother and I did get some food as well. I had the Mushroom Swiss burger with onion rings, and my brother had the Cheeseburger with fries. The food was decent, but it's something that they obviously don't really focus on so I didn't expect it to be of really high quality.

The bartenders and everyone there was super friendly and always had a smile on their face. Overall, this is definitely a must visit for anyone that's not from here or new to town. Even lifelong residents would enjoy this place!

If you come to Nashville and get down to Music Row don't you have to stop in here? I think so because it is such an institution. Always good live music playing its a real honkytonk. They are famous for their $4 fried bologna sandwich. I had one this week and will tell you it was very good and well worth it (4). With lettuce and tomato and a lot of bologna it brought back my childhood days when we would make these all the time. You also get a bag of chips so you can make a meal on it or just a good snack. 

With all the pictures and posters on the wall there is a lot of history here. Come in and enjoy.
OBSESSED. Was one of my favorite bars in Nash. Suuuper cheap drinks and great live music!

Took my boyfriend here for his birthday. They sat us two tables from the stage.  The jazz band playing was great. Definitely set the mood, and they were also taking requests. We ordered the shrimp and crab dip for starter and it wasn't anything special but was good. Our entrees were really awesome though. The waiter recommended the Blackened Red Snapper and is was incredible, the flavors were spot on! My boyfriend ordered the Shrimp and Crab Scampi, another winner. But by far the dessert was the best: Cheesecake Sopapilla. I would go back just based on the desert alone. Are waiter was awesome, very friendly and definitely directed us to the better choices on the menu. Definitely plan on returning!

Went here for a concert last night. Planned to get inside early, hit the merch table, visit the bar and get settled before the concert. Got to the venue a few hours early to secure a place in line in order to do so. No ropes, no one directing the line even though there were already over a thousand people in line at that point. In fact the line just kept growing with no one to manage or direct it. As the area filled up no security was present until a lone man came to tell those of us with tickets we had to move to the back of the line. This resulted in missing most of the opening act and not getting to visit the merch table at all. Why was I punished for buying a ticket? Further, let's talk inside. Poor acoustics, no screens, uncomfortable seats. Never coming back.

There are a lot of things going for Sambuca: free valet, really hot music, and arresting visual displays. The food, however, leaves me perplexed.

Food is my primary measure for evaluating a restaurant, but I have to take a moment to comment on the ambiance of this place. With its generous use of draped red and purple cloth and weird light fixtures. The interior design is sort of how I would imagine what an upscale Turkish brothel would look like. I can't say that that's either a good or a bad thing, but it's certainly interesting. I have to say, though: I am all for mood lighting, but this place is exceptionally dim. At one point, I watched a waiter forced to identify a soup by using a flashlight. If the lighting is bad enough to interfere with your employees' ability to do their jobs, I think it's time to go back to the drawing board.

As for the food, I was pretty optimistic after the first course: the bisque was well-balanced and quite tasty. Furthermore, their side-dish, prosciutto mac&cheese, was remarkably light. I thought I was headed for a thoroughly 4-star meal, but alas, it was not to be. I admit that I broke one of my own commandments of restaurant eating, which is "Don't order a chicken breast or a pork chop unless someone has specifically recommended it." As punishment for my sins, I spent my evening chewing through an overcooked, though relatively well-seasoned, pork chop. Remarkably, they managed to pull off the opposite feat with their vegetables. Now, I prefer many vegetables, like broccoli and carrots, to be on the "al dente" side. However, bell peppers and onions do NOT fall into this category: it was remarkably bitter. I will say, though, that because they were undercooked it made for good eating the next day after I nuked them in the microwave. I didn't try too much of my tablemates' food, but at least two folks commented that the lobster enchiladas were not particularly lobster-y and that the portions were a bit stingy.

This meal showed some moments of promise, but I was expecting a bit more. Perhaps one should only order items with cream in it.
I got a greasy burger like I like it with some greasy fries.  Listened to awesome music and had great service.  Best part was I didn't hear one song by Luke Bryan or any of his cohorts.

As Northerners who are relative newcomers to country music, it was great to visit the holy cathedral of the genre.  It was like going to a living historical museum.

I would say that unless you are a die-hard Grand Ole Opry or country music fan or historian, the backstage tour (which was good) really isn't necessary.  I know I probably would have gotten as much out of the self-guided tour.

The movie they show is very well done and educational.  You can get that with the self-guided tour as well.

Saw Judah and the Lion last night, show and venue are fantastic!   Be aware of 2nd hand ticket seller SeatGeek.  Many of the tickets to the show were available on their website.  We purchased 2 tickets 2months ago and had to call seatgeek the day of the show to get them to send us the tickets.  We then had scramble to print them (they had to be printed) and they came out blurry which caused issues getting in the show.  Would not recommend using SeatGeek to purchase tickets.

Second Fiddle had a great band playing on Friday night and attentive bartenders. Drink prices were standard, the place was not crowded, which was nice because we were able to move around. Their decor is really neat; they have musical instruments behind the bar, a lot of attention to detail in here. I love the brick wall and there are tables throughout. It's a little empty in the back of the room and you don't have a great view of the band unless you're up front. It was a fun stop to listen to some good music.

This was the first place we checked out on Broadway street while visiting Nashville, really liked their Southern Sangria. The energy is great, people always dancing around the stage. They have different bands so it's not always country. We came back a few more times for their drinks.
my favorite honky tonk on lower Broad! the best! best music! a must for anyone doing the tourist thing that wants to hear great music.

Tonight at Sambuca I had the filet Oscar. The filet was cooked perfectly, medium rare, as I requested. The size of the filet wasn't bad. The Oscar part of the filet was a bit of a different story. There wasn't nearly enough crab on top. The filet had to much béarnaise over the top. Although the béarnaise was tasty there was just to much of it. Don't let me forgot the asparagus. It was a huge disappointment. Very undercooked. Had to use some muscle and a steak knife to cut through it. Damn. But because of the perfect cook on the filet and a decent tasting béarnaise I'll give them a few stars.

This is our first trip to Nashville. The music playing was great, the bartenders were awesome. They were on it!  Keeley and 
Chad were awesome!!!!!   They made the evening. Thanks again.

Great experience at this place! They accommodated a party of 15 for a bachelorette party with a special prix fix menu because of the size, and the food was delicious! One of our party got dripped on from an AC unit and they re-sat us in a private room and comped some of our meal. It was handled immediately and professionally. Our server Jesse was great, he humored us and made sure the bride had a great time. We were all very happy!
Love the blues??? You must go.  And for a blues joint the food was decent.  I'll be back.
Great bar, gets super crowded though. the band was awesome, the drinks were great. I will definitely be going back here. Definitely not a place to go if you are looking to have your personal space.
Amazed at the history here.   Did the tour and back stage pass.  So glad we did.  Highly recommend.

This was my favorite and last stop on Broadway. I would have loved to stay longer if my friends weren't ready to go home for the night. The band played a medley of 80's-00's hip hop for most of the time I was there. It was very nostalgic for me. Reminded me of middle school and high school dances. There was a much younger crowd here. Didn't hear any country music. It was a Saturday night. Didn't catch the name of the band. Only crowded on the dance floor. Plenty of places to sit in the back.

It was average. Was in Nashville for the weekend, we have a Tin Roof back home but we still decided to check it out (we actually mistook it for another bar.) But nonetheless, we sat upstairs because it was nice out, they had opened windows & half of the roof was open. Not sure it was open on purpose, the half that was covered, was covered with ply-wood. It began to rain which scattered the half that wasn't covered. Stayed for a few beers & mules & left.
Loved seeing the place where the Grand Ole Opry started!! Emerging artist and those tried and true! Don't miss this when checking out Nashville, from music, comedy, square dancers, young and old!!

Great location for this one.  Much better than the other Tin Roof on D street.  Came down to Nashville to watch my brother's band play here during the first week.  What an atmosphere Nashville has at night.  Really love the girls wearing cowboy boots.  Don't see that at all back in Ohio.  

This place was great.  Really giant and long (that's what she said).  Placed was packed and the crowd was fantastic.
