Came here for lunch, absolutely wonderful!!! The food is awesome, server is so nice, he split our meals into two and even gave us an extra cup of soup. Great place and great food. Turkey and Brie sandwich and red snapper étouffée are some great recommendations
Definitely a crowd for the older folks or those who like the oldies. Not a typical Nashville bar. Cheap alcohol tho but not much room.

We had an amazing experience at Sambuca! We loved the goat cheese artichoke appetizer! My friend and I split the scallops and and an order of the havarti dill tots- both were delicious. Shout out to Emerson our waiter!! He made our night so much fun! Rachel Rodriguez has an amazingly beautiful soulful voice and we were lucky to hear her perform. She was great about taking requests from the audience and provided a lively atmosphere to the night. From the P-Pod Posse thanks for an amazing evening!!

We ended up going here several times during our trip to Nashville. Every time a great band was playing. Even at 6 or 7 pm we stood around and waited by the bar for a seat but the music was worth it. I wouldn't eat dinner here but the fried pickles were delicious-we got them all 3 times we visited. It's a dive bar but every tourist should be going here at least once.

This place was pretty cool. The live music here wasn't my favorite and my first drink was not great but it was a cool experience for about 30-45 minutes. We stopped in while waiting on a table for dinner across the street. Upstairs bar has the perfect lighting for selfies ;)

Unfortunately we were unsure when we'd be arriving, so OCMS shows on and before NYE were sold out, so we just went for a daytime tour by redeeming 1/4 of our Access Pass. Beautiful space, but they really need to include a demo of the acoustics as part of it. Will certainly attend a show if back in Nashville.
Always a good time, fantastic live music...drinks are a little pricey, but I would choose going here over quite a few other along the strip, because the layout feels less cramped.

This is not just any historic venue,  this is hollowed ground for country music!  It's THE church!  The pews,  the floors, the ceiling is all original which provides amazing acoustics.  Now I know why bands still play here and find it an honor in doing so.  The video introduction is amazing and educational for the self- guided tour.  When you come to Nashville, you must see this place along with the Grand Ole Opry.

Great place. Great location. Very good live music, they have a very good variety of live music unlike all the other places in Nashville where it is always country music. Food was awesome, the portions were huge. Great place for hangout in the Gulch. All the staffs are super friendly. Max treated us great. Definitely will be going back.

We were told by multiple Tennesseans that Robert's was the best bar on Broadway so we had to check it out for some day drinking. We scored a table right up near the stage and were lucky enough to catch Eileen Rose and her band playing some great country hits. We had the best time, sipping our beers, munching our fried bologna sandwiches (order immediately as they take an hour to arrive at your table!), and singing along to the wonderful music. Great energy and atmosphere at Robert's.

Most of the time, when we visit a new city with a classic music venue, they end up having bands we have no interest in... not this time. Rufus and Martha Wainwright rolled into town for their Christmas show, and we enjoyed every minute of it.

The venue itself definitely has character and some obvious flaws (that are probably unavoidable for such an old spot). Roughly 75% of the seating in the lower section is under the balcony and doesn't get a "great" view of the stage, but they aren't really obstructed either. The acoustics are amazing, so much so, that Rufus sang without a microphone for a rendition of "O Holy Night" which was worth the price of admission alone.

The only downsides are the concessions, in terms of what items are available, and the location of the restrooms as the doors were open most of the night for smokers and it was frigid outside.

We went to a Grand ole Opry performance here and it was an unforgettable experience!  We had balcony seats and still felt so close to the stage. The seats resemble church pews so not the most comfortable but the sound of music in the auditorium more than makes up for it! Had such a wonderful time and would recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville and likes country music!

Horrendous. Took TWO HOURS at lunch for a party of five, with only two other tables in the restaurant. Forty minutes to receive one round of drinks. Wrong bill amount was brought, card was charged the right amount (twice as much) with no notice or mention. It's too bad that this restaurant continues to go downhill more and more.
Fun place, great music and drinks. Funky, and historic decor. Came here from Reno, Nevada with my honey and we had a great time! Our first stop in Nashville was a 10!

Horrible horrible venue. Came for a show November 21st to see the 1975. Still outside at 8:12 with a line about half a mile long. They couldn't open the door sooner! The opening act is all ready on stage and performing. This place stinks.

This was the last dinner I had during my trip to Nashville. We had a reservation and were sat on the balcony above the stage. A jazz band played some light music starting at 6:30pm. It was a really awesome set up and had such a trendy cool vibe. I had a couple of Dirty Martinis (best ones I had in Nashville) and we tried a few of their apps to start. the Mac and Cheese with prosciutto, the buschetta and 2 orders of the Buca Beignets. All fantastic. We order the right about for the 7 of us to share. 

I had the special which was sea bass wrapped in bacon with risotto. Different but delicious. A very unique dining experience. We had a great time!

Best sound in Nashville  Every show I've seen here has been great. We came and did a self guided tour and the attendants were really friendly and excited to tell stories about artists and bands who have come through. If you haven't done the Ryman tour it's actually worth it to learn the history.

this would probably be cool if you were into old timey country music. we paid for the backstage tour. you should do that if you want to see shitty dressing rooms built in the 90s and hear kind-of stories from a tour guide who "doesn't know for sure, but probably." taylor swift MIGHT have been in this dressing room.

the old costumes are pretty legit, and this place would be cool for a concert.

Really enjoyed this place. Menu is small and simple. I went out on a limb and tried the fried bologna sandwich and was pleasantly surprised! From the locals I spoke to there, one being a musician himself, this is a great place to hear some of the best local music, which I was able to do while there. Definitely worth a stop in.

Nashville...lots of guitars in various incarnations on the walls.

Plays Adult Contemporary versions of songs while still having a C&W vibe.

Not too crowded.  Friendly service.

Corner of the busiest street in Nashville.

Besides my friend Cat loved it !
The mixing for the live band is incredible. It sounds like you're listening to a record. There's a nice selection of beer and a full bar. I didn't get the food, but it looks good.
It took over an hour for our food...which was mediocre and cold at best. Definitely don't come here to eat.

We rolled into Robert's Western World after a morning trip to RCA Studios before touring the Hall of Fame. We had the fried pickles, two bologna sandwiches & a Yazoo Pale Ale while listening to an old fella paying some traditional country tunes. 

Great service. Tasty, cheap & greasy food. Laid back, Nashville atmosphere.

Definitely come check this place out.

Stopped in here based on a recommendation and we weren't disappointed. Drinks were nice and cheap and service was nice. They ran out of Yeungling, which was kinda disappointing, but they have a good selection of other beers. 

The live music was really fun and upbeat and VERY loud. The crowd was positive and enjoying it as well. There was nearly an hour gap between when one band went off and the other band went on and I wish they had put some music on the speakers while they were swapping to add to the ambiance.

The place itself it pretty cool decor. Really interesting posters and such all over. We were on the lower level and the only table we were able to grab was under the A/C. It was cold under there, but the A/c kept dripping all over the table. It was musical drinks to make sure it didn't drip into the drink. 

Probably wouldn't stop in here again, but glad I can say I've been here.

I'll give 3 stars only because of Alden (she deserves 5 in customer service skills), Otherwise I would have given a 1. She went out of her way to turn around tonight's visit from a pretty bad experience, to a more bearable one. It's my second time at Sambuca, I come to Nashville for business, and I made it to this restaurant/bar again due to the great previous experience I had the first time (I like exploring new spots but loyal to the good ones). Since the beginning, from trying to use the valet parking, everything went down hill: valet was about to close, they did not take my car. I had to find parking at a nearby garage. I made it to the restaurant at 9:40pm (supposedly it closed for dinner at 10 and the bar at 11, plus the band was playing still upon my artival and till I left, and the place was at least half full inside), after explaining upon arrival the parking issue, I was informed by the hostess that not only dinner was not available to order, but when asked about bar appetizers, I was told that it wasn't available either, just "sorry, no food". At 32 degrees Fahrenheit, I was not willing to walk elsewhere, and decided to sit for a drink and calm down the disappointment with the band's music... It only took a good server, Alden came and graciously managed to get me at least a lobster bisque and suggested a great cocktail to try, so she somehow made up for the horrible experience from earlier... It's sad to admit that although she was awesome at providing just plain and simple good old customer service, it's very unlikely that I'll be back there or that I'd recommend this place to my colleagues... Note to the business management team:  In general, if you are closing earlier (or you make exceptions due to weather or whatever the case is) please make sure that your website information is up-to-date, that way your customers don't get disappointed and don't waste their time or yours with an unnecessary trip.

Recently went into Nashville and stumbled across here for car parking.
Great rates non event time and easy underground structure with great payment options.
We walked through the centre and it is massive and seemed clean and welcoming.

The Ryman Auditorium was another stop on our tour and I really enjoyed the introductory video on this music venue which was apparently done by Disney and super informative.  I never heard of the Ryman before stepping foot in Nashville but it has a great history and is apparently still a very coveted venue due to its intimacy factor.  Don't skip it!
I mean, seriously, a can of cold Busch Light and a fried bologna sandwich for $5!!!!  Awesome deal, and the sandwich was great!!! Friendly staff
Always a good time at legends...always a great band on stage and though it may be packed 99% of the time, it's worth it..
No service at the bar. Eventually moved to a table and got service, but came with an "I don't wanna be here attitude" from the server.  Band only covered Chuck Berry songs. So we were outa there....
Classic joint where there are as many false starts by the band at the door as there are patrons. Solid grub if you're feeling peckish, and $2.50 for some domestic cans if you're feeling parched.
Loved the band they had the night I stopped in here with friends, we danced so much!
Not very crowded.  Nothing special to speak of, therefore, stop in, drink and hear the band.
Good food & drinks, great service, even better band! Went with a group and were seated immediately. We had a great time. If I lived in Nashville, I would most definitely come back!
Good food and really fun to go there. Beer was very tasty and live music was awesome. Get the catfish sliders they were the best!

Robert's Western World es un clásico de Nashville, un típico bar americano donde siempre hay música en vivo y, por supuesto, es el lugar ideal para bailar Honky Tonk.

Onda que este lugar es súper turístico y se llena de gente, pero -así y todo- tiene un encanto particular que lo hace más que especial y sumamente pintoresco. 

Sí, acá podrán escuchar a grandes músicos en vivo tocando country o rock en cualquier horario y los que gusten también podrán bailar el clásico ritmo sureño. Respecto a las bebidas tiene una gran variedad de cervezas industriales y artesanales en botella, distintos tragos, como también una buena variedad de comidas para acompañar lo que puede ser una muy buena noche de tragos y buena música. Posta que este bar es un clásico de Nashville de visita obligatoria.

Classic Nashville establishment.  Drinks are decently cheap, music is good and the food smelled and looked very good, I just didn't get to have any.  Not too many seats, so be ready to stand on the weekends which is not a big deal if you're not eating.

Best burger on Broadway. Amazing live music. Lovely staff. Always lots of old timey  dancing and fun. Always filled with people of all ages and lots of locals. Most authentic Nashville bar on Broadway. You are missing out if you pass up on Roberts, it's a rate Tennessee gem!

The venue for opry country classics is awesome! The theater is nice and intimate. The 2014 fall series started with really nice show. The sound is perfect and crowd was super. It's strange to believe a live broadcast is happening during concert. 

The gift shop had a nice collection of items. The t shirts are a little much but you're talking a 100+year place it's paying for. 
I thought I was getting bluegrass but I'll take country gold in perfect place. One of best musically experiences I've ever had. At home I've seen almost everyone overt last thirty years but nothing compared to this place. Halls built for sound and nothing comes close, the ghosts most help.
I typically hate country music, but this place is legit. Great snacks, a genuine and amazing bar vibe, and a great time overall!
Great ambiance and a classy vibe.  Perfect music for dinner and drinks.  Outstanding service and hands on attention from a super friendly general manager.
Awesome place great music great people fun place to hang out.  The food is ok the service is great!!

Great ambience, had dinner reservations stopped in hot happy hour before dinner. Ordered the crab and shrimp dip, and a Sambuca 75. Happy hour is 11am-7pm but happy hour with small snacks is 4pm-7pm. My dip was $5 or $6 and my drink the same either $5/$6. I sat at the high top bar where I could view the jenerators, who were awesome! The seat for me I felt I needed to be taller because the bar stools sat low. Closed out my happy hour tab and headed right to dinner. For dinner I had a Caesar salad and the ink squid pasta. The salad was a little salty to me but tasty and the pasta was lightly flavored but satisfying. For dessert I ordered the berry cobbler. The pastry part was sweet. The berries were warm and comforting with ice cream on top. Sweet but not too sweet.  I love The restaurant the vibe is great. Around 7:30 they dim the lights inside. They have a second floor for additional guests or large parties. They also have outdoor seating it's also a close walk the Nashville wings mural. If you're curious.

This place is so amazing! We took the guided tour and Tom, with his mellifluous voice, took us through the dressing rooms backstage and described the history of this amazing theatre. It's awesome to be able to step on the stage here. I wish had been able to see a show and experience the acoustics.
Amazing food, great atmosphere.  Our waiter, Tyler, was very helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. Love this place!

My favorite music venue of ALL TIME!  Every show is an amazing experience and it is truly a magical place.  Artists aspire to play the Ryman and I have not attended a single show where the artist has not commented on how special it is to have the privilege.  

There really isn't a bad seat in the house and the sound is amazing.  Hatch Show Prints are a Ryman tradition and they add a special touch to each show.  If you want one, get there early!
Doesn't get much better in Music City than the Ryman...it's a beautiful building with a terrific history. Sit in the balcony or front of the floor for best views.

The new Music City Center is incredible! The space is unique, beautiful, has great views, and was built with extreme thought to being environmentally friendly. 

I attended the Greater Nashville Association of Realtors conference here shortly after it opened, and it blew our conference experiences at the older Nashville Convention Center out of the park. The rooms are all super nice and parking in the garage is very convenient. Our lunch, which in years past had been borderline awful, was prepared by the MCC's chef and was really impressive, especially for a big catered event type meal. Dessert was very tasty too, which was chocolate mousse and one other option served in martini glasses. 

For your coffee needs, Bongo Java is right next door inside the Omni Hotel. If you're not a local, the center is right downtown so you can take advantage of everything Downtown Nashville has to offer.
We've been twice so far and we love the atmosphere and good food/drinks. We plan on making this a go to spot!

Went here with some girlfriends while we were in town for the weekend.  Not only was our waiter extremely helpful, our meals were amazing!  Patton James was playing and we all found the band very entertaining.  This place made me wish I lived in Nashville.
Great place. Tables on the balcony are definitely the way to go. Food was excellent, as was Tiffany Johnson. Nice show. And lots of bachelorettes...

Maybe I just came here on an off night, but the Tin Roof is on a long street of bars and live music venues- and this place wasn't enough for me to stay for a drink. On a weekend night, the place was 3/4 empty, and full of a older (50-60 y/o), drunken crowd. The bright lights are cool, the name is catchy, and people seem to like it, but I wouldn't spend more than 30 minutes here.

If you're looking for a great atmosphere, live music and a fantastic house band with some of the best country musicians(great guitar and bass player), friendly venue and the best fried bologna sandwich ever, then this is the place. Be forwarned, its small and crowded, but fun and they dont get in a hurry; if you want beer or liqour or snack for a fair $ step on up, cuz they aint gonna ask ya.

I was in town for a conference and after checking Yelp, decided to stop in. My only regret is that I had already eaten by the time we decided to visit this place, so no fried bologna sandwich for me. It was, however, a charming little joint with a great band and positive atmosphere. It felt like a real Nashville experience. Of course, I'm from CA, so I may be way off there, but still... I enjoyed my experience..

Finally getting around to reviewing this place, last concert was the XX.  Third row seats, sound and vision was good.  Interior is of course lovely, the ushers super efficient although a day not under 75 which adds to the charm.  For all its charm I have heard more bad audio here than good depending on where I am sitting.  Upstairs does not work for my ears at all or far back under the balcony, so advise always spring for the closest downstairs tix.  Take in the tour of the place during the daytime $17 and make your CD recording for $15 and the experience is complete with a final trinket from the gift shop, everyone from Elvis to Coldplay and more have played here so its a slice.  My friend even named his son Ryman a few years ago.

How very cool it was to be here. I love, love, love live and country music so stopping here to walk around the venue and sit on their wooden benches where many folks got to see so many legendary singers perform. Think of the young kids of today going crazy for One Direction or whatever and go back in time and think that the same energy and excitement and happiness was felt for Elvis Presley (my meant-to-be husband), Johnny Cash and Patsy Cline when they graced that stage. Some people usually just see a band once or twice.This is where so many once in a lifetime memories were made. 

It cost $14 to get in. You're asked to sit down to watch a 10-minute video about the history of the Ryman with Trisha Yearwood and can wander the venue. There are tickets for a guided tour as well and you can go back stage.  Sing and record a song for $20. My cousin's girlfriend sang Patsy Cline song and it sounded amazing. I was going to do it. I sound pretty amazing in my car.  Also, you're able to take a photo on stage. There were people dressed in their best country outfits having their photo taken with their guitars and boots. Head on upstairs and see how massive this place is. Pretty amazing that it originally was a place of worship. The cases all around the venue hold clothing and photos of past performers. The rear wall of the beautiful arched windows definitely reminds you of church windows. Around halls outside the main area, the walls paint you a timeline of events as mentioned in the video. And there are signed Ryman posters that were signed by the artists - Kid Rock, Robin Thicke, and dare I say it, The Jonas Brothers. These posters reminded me of SF's Fillmore. It was a great experience. Next time, I'll record a CD just to say I sang "Live at the Ryman!" But I would love to see a live show here sometime.

I was here for a work event and it was a wonderful space for it. There were 25,000+ of us and most of the time it never seemed that way since there is so much space inside the MCC. The building was clean; inside and out. All the staff I encountered were friendly. The bright natural light from all the big windows was wonderful; and I loved seeing the decorations, especially the rocking chairs, nice southern touch!
Great band tonight, Smoke and Guns. Danced hard!!!

Great atmosphere, great band, friendly waitress, so-so food.   The chicken and waffles were not very good in my opinion. The waffle is legit an eggo frozen waffle.  The maple bacon syrup just didnt taste right. I tried some of my daughter's brisket Mac and cheese and it was interesting with a smoky flavor.

I was amazed to see such a historical place in person. Learning about how the Grand Ole Opry came about and the numerous musicians it helped to showcase was great. I loved seeing Johnny Cash's black suit and June Carter's pink dress on display was the highlight for me. I loved being able to walk around on my own and see the space for on my own. The price is pretty decent too for what you get, I'd recommend for a very informative and fun tour.

Beth's Aunt and Uncle celebrated their 50th Anniversary here. We drove up from Atlanta for an overnight trip. Had a super time with excellent food and drinks. 
Staff was friendly and delightful. Really made us welcome.

Music and beer are good but the service was atrocious.  Waited almost 20 min for the waiter to come so we ordered at the bar instead and then waited at least another hour for the food. When we asked about our food they said they have other people waiting first and the people who arrived an hour after us got their food within 5 min.  The people next to us left because the waiter said someone else ate their food.

We were on the honky tonk tour of Broadway in Nashville, couldn't bear to miss this spot. Exactly as the other reviews have highlighted, likely very crowded as the evening marches along (we stopped in rather early). Definitely a destination on the strip!

Started out my night at Robert 3 out of the 5 nights I was in town. Amazing musicians, very friendly service, and an unbelievable cheeseburger. I was told their fried pickles are life changing but the fryer was down all week so I wasn't able to try them. Next time for sure. 

I hit up at least 12 bars this trip and Roberts easily  stood out as my #1.

Went to the Awe + Wonder Conference here.  It's obviously a little older building, but seemed like a great place to hold an event.  Located right in downtown Nashville, it's a great place to see a conference, concert or sporting event
The atmosphere at this place is awesome. Great concept for a restaurant with amazing booth seats. Service staff not the most responsive, but otherwise a great place to eat and hear live music.

The good, we saw a great band on Memorial day.  Great female singer and band.  The bad - no drink service.  This was not too annoying since we weren't craving a drink but you had to fend for yourself at the bar if you wanted something to drink.

Our server was Amazing! I think his name was Jesse. He was very friendly and helped us through the menu. The food was amazing. I had the goat cheese stuffed artichokes, which he recommended. He also brought out a birthday cake for my friends 21st! I have nothing bad to say about this place. Atmosphere was great with the live music they had playing. Thanks for a memorable experience in Nashville.

I'm not sure how to feel about this place. I know how other people feel about it and it makes me feel like there's something wrong with me for not enjoying myself while I was there. 

We went to a show and they're doing some sort of construction. Most of the lobby was roped off and this meant the entire lobby was packed full of people to the point where you couldn't move. You couldn't tell where the lines for food and drinks were vs the lines for the bathrooms. 

Once I got to my seat, I was a little dismayed by the pew seating. As someone who doesn't know much about the history of the building, even after I was told, the pews aren't my idea of comfort. Especially when I'm sitting elbow to elbow with a complete stranger. They really pack those seats full and you have no personal space while there. 

I may have been cranky because I had basically been on my feet for 12 hours prior, but I was ready to leave before the main event even began. During the opening act, I went to the lobby to stretch my legs, since it was no longer packed like a sardine can. I paid, I believe, $9 for a small box of stale-ish popcorn and a can of sprite and went back to my seat. 

There was an encore, but we chose to duck out before it began so that we could leave the building without having to deal with the mob of people we experienced on our way in. The valet parking was worth every penny of the $20 I paid for it. No hassling with finding someplace to park and they got our car super quickly after the show.

If what you are looking for is a straight up honky tonk on Broadway, this is your place. Entertainment is twangy goodness. Fried bologna sandwich special was an exceptional deal and good when trying to absorb a bunch of liquor.

You just gotta see this place. Its just a small little place but there is so much musical history here. If you go to Nashville this is a must. They have some Hatch prints on display and different memorabilia on display. It was cool bc we just saw Loretta Lynn that morning getting her star on the walk of fame, then we came here and saw a couple of her dresses.

For me this was a breath of fresh air. We had been on the road for a few weeks and just wanted some good music. Jesse did the job! I could have stayed there forever just listening to Jessie Lee Jones Brazilbilly band crank out the oldies of Bob Wills and Marty Robbins (Roly Poly!). Loved it. Went around 3:00 pm so can't say what the night crowd is like.

Honky tonk what??? This was our first stop on our "authentic" Nashville night. I'm not sure if it's really authentic, or just sold that way, but it seemed pretty legit to me. Walking in, you almost feel like you've entered a time warp, where it's totally a thing to wear hats and tight jeans, bring your young children to the bar and sip on PBR. But the band was pretty good and even us city slickers couldn't help but move to the beat.
Just go. It's amazing. Best bands, went 3 times the week I was in town. Great service too.

Don't let the fact that this establishment looks like a trendy upscale bar and lounge keep you from coming here for dinner. Their food is actually amazing. It only took me at least five years of coming to Sambuca to figure that out! 

My friends and I used to come here to hang out for drinks after dinner usually somewhere else in the Gulch. Sambuca has a great ambiance and amazing drinks. I loved their pomegranate martinis! One night we were hungry and got a few tapas/small plates and thought, man this is good food!

Fast forward a few years later and we're now all married. My husband and I decided to make a dinner reservation for one of our birthdays. We were blown away at how good the food was! My husband had a really amazing steak here. The live music was a nice added romantic feature. 

I would definitely say this place is worth checking out whether you are looking for a place to hang with friends or for a nice dinner.

Spacious, conspicuous, under bldg parking..

Went here for the Women's show and parking was ridiculous.
They don't tell you you can't pay with cash. Instead, when you get to the pay station, you have to leave your vehicle and go pay inside.
Otherwise, be credit card happy.

Restaurants... what restaurants?
Some pizza place at the front of the bldg on Shelby Ave..
Nothing healthy. Everything pre-made.
Otherwise, there are donuts next door.. Again - really healthy!

Eat before coming here.
Make sure you have your credit card.
Make sure you have your temper checked at the door.
A lot of frustration, to say the least.
Cheap beer, solid diner food, calmer than the insanity of broadway and had good old school country.  Take a load off here between nashvegas bars and you'll be glad you stopped by.

We visited while in town in a bachelorette. Everything was fantastic!  Our sever Matt really brought our dining experience to the next level. We couldn't have asked for more!  Food was delicious. Great entertainment. And awesome service. Next time I'm in Nashville, we'll definitely visit again!

This place is a GEM

Great professional service

Excellent menu

Very welcoming ambiance 

Even the customers here were nice/friendly

I've been to a few extremely large convention centers now. Nashville wins for the prettiest I've been at if it does feel a little small. This said there're some really big problems with the staff.

Got there on Sunday morning for a garden show, just wandering from the world's smallest and best hidden Dunkin Doughnuts (very good, nothing to complain about,) and as I'm strolling aimlessly as I'm lost I wander up to an ask-me desk with two employees trash talking Asians, loudly to the one person at the kiosk, or perhaps at each other who were just hanging around there. I get my directions from the one person who's working (not the two who are just leaning there,) head off, more trash talking at volume that can be heard quite a distance.

I'm not Asian nor part of an Asian defense league as a note. Just loud unsolicited random racism was uncalled for.

3rd floor, sit down for a few minutes as I'm hauling a baby and otherwise tired. There's an employee sitting in the sitting area looking disgusted. I don't know what his problem was, but he was taking a couch and glaring. Eh, not at me or mine but dang. He glared for as long as I felt like sitting and when I left he was still sitting there sprawled out.

Walked past some rocking chairs, there's a large coffee spill.

Two hours later I'm done with the event, walk back to the seats, oh hey coffee spill. I mean, it could be a new one...

All this said, nothing bad happened, there were people there on it, I don't know what's going on and perhaps the casual racism was directed at a group of asians who were there, perhaps the guy glaring at the world had just had his family murdered by asians, I don't know. The only not on top of it was that coffee, unless that was two spills.

I can't put into words how awesome of a venue the Ryman really is... This was my first show there and it far exceeded my already lofty expectations. It's such a beautiful place, and there's really not a bad seat in the house. The acoustics are perfect as you'd expect, and the layout of bathrooms and concessions are awesome. The gift shop in the downstairs lobby is worth checking out as well.

Came here with a large party for a bach party. Most of our food was excellent, one order came out a bit messed up, but they eventually fixed it for us. Our server was adorable - though maybe a bit too chatty and friendly, making it hard to get his attention from other tables when we needed him. The ambiance was pretty good. Fun to see a live show while eating non "bar food" food. Would def recommend and go back if I'm ever in the area again!

This is a great addition to South Nashville. Don't let the exterior fool you, the interior of this plaza will surprise you and make you feel like you are in Mexico! Everything is bright and clean, with a few delicious dinner options. My favorites are El Ceviche Lock and Tres Gauchos. Order the shrimp ceviche from El Ceviche and the grilled shrimp and plantains from Tres Gauchos. Polish it off with a mangonado from Paletas Tocumbo!

The Tin Roof was just okay. We came in on a Friday night and the band that was playing wasn't playing country so we were a little disappointed. They were playing Blink 182, Justin Bieber and some other pop songs. People enjoyed them but we didn't and it was kind of hard to hear them from upstairs. Upstairs they did not have any music, just a balcony to watch the action downstairs. For us, it wasn't anything special. Maybe we caught the place on an off night.

My girlfriends and I ate here for a girls-night-out. We split 5 or so plates among the 7 of us, and had one person pay and we split the bill later. The food was all delicious and it was really fun to sample a little bit of everything on the table. It was fun to have live music on stage behind us.
This place is awesome!  The fried bologna sandwich is great.  $2.50 for beer and great music to boot.  The staff is very nice and quick.  My husband has a hamburger and fries which he enjoyed.

We stumbled upon this place on our last night in Nashville. . . Wow!  The Mad Hatter band playing was absolutely amazing.  Very entertaining.  Staff was very friendly. Drinks were reasonably priced.  Highly recommended stopping by if you're in downtown Nashville.

Even on a Tuesday afternoon at 4 there was live music.  It was absolutely a hoot!  There is a definite dive bar atmosphere, bottled beer only.  We had the yucca fries which were very thick cut and softer than french fries, but quite good.  A great venue.

Loved the red walls, and the overall atmosphere of this place. It was a little disappointing to have such a great environment but not the best service. The server in the bar area was less then attentive, I would have loved to have tried the green brûlée but never had the opportunity to order it.
LOVED IT!!! Came here on a recommendation and had a great time. Nice late night bites and live music, will return!

We stopped in for the live music.  No tao beer, only bottles was disappointing.  The service was even more disappointing.  The location (kitty corner from Bridgestone Arena), the live music and the atmosphere bring it up to three stars.
Great honky tonk bar! Fun live music. Delicious fried bologna sandwich!

Amazing, as usual!

We weren't expecting the Music City Bowl (yes, I live under one very un-sporty rock) so we were surprised to find Broadway even crazier than usual upon arrival.  No worries--we hit up Robert's around lunch time, snuck in the back door, found a few stools at the grill, and had the best beer and breakfast in recent memory!  Even my food snob companion was blown away by the recession special--it is practically all he talks about when asked about the trip!!!

Great music and unbeatable, tasty bargains!  The lady working the bar was super nice and they have the cutest can cozies of all time.  You totally need this in your life.

Thanks for the great time!
A true Nashville honkey tonk. The fried bologna sandwich is a my favorite and wash it down with a PBR

This was the first place I fell in love with when moving to nashville.  There is a bass player named Joe that plays there often.  It is a must see.  This is a great place to start and end you night when going Honky Tonkin.  Oh...and they are a bar!

This was my favorite tourist attraction in Nashville!  The history and architecture are fabulous.  I definitely have great respect and reverence for such a spectacular historical place.  We went to a show and the acoustics were incredible!  It was great to walk around before the show and between acts.  The gift shop was also a fun spot to visit for souvenirs.
This is one of our favorite Nashville bars.  They always have a great band playing.

Arguably the best honky tonk downtown, and the preferred choice of many locals when we dare venture to Broadway.  I've heard they serve food, but I wouldn't know anything about that, as I don't make a habit of eating whilst honkeytonking, which seems counterproductive to me.

The place is small but if there's a line it's worth it. Great beer prices and the fried bologna sandwich is awesome. Depression special is the way to go for lunch or if you need something to soak up the beer. Traditional country music playing at all times and the servers are very nice.
Fantastic music!!  Good food and a great atmosphere.  I will be back the next time I am in Nashville.
This place is such a good time. The food is great and it's such a fun atmosphere with live music and friendly staff and cheap beer and eats! My fav thing is the fried pickles. Can't wait to go back!
Excellent concert venue.  Very good view and acoustics everywhere.  Enhance the guests' experience by adding real cocktails to the bar, and more food selections.
Great country music!!! Drinks priced right and best sweet potato fries served. Room to dance and plenty on seating

Came here with a group of friends and had a good time.  The food was enjoyable, atmosphere was nice, the only downside was the really loud volume of the live band.  I felt bad for my friends and other patrons who were seated by the stage.  The music was fun and entertaining, but the volume of it was almost a bit much as evidenced by the faces of the people stuck to sit around the stage (before the live music started up).

The food was pretty good!  The Buca Beignets were delightful and the Shrimp & Crab dip was tasty.  I really enjoyed my chili-rubbed scallops.  The cheesecake sopapilla was awesome!

The fried bologna sandwich was fantastic and the beer was cold.  The servers were friendly and the band was talented.  The place is a dive but part of Nashville history.  A definite must stop while you are in town.

Good food, good music, nice staff. A lot of space for groups and nice ambiance for date or group night out.

Artichoke appetizer delicious
Chicken Somasas- pretty good
Artisan pizza with sausage- tasty
Mango pear drink-pretty good

Will definitely be back!

The inside is beautiful! We walked around the building for about 30 minutes before we went to get food. When we went for food, there were a ton a really good options. The food, and amount we paid for it, was great! I had the chicken kabobs with vegetables. It was so well seasoned and the chicken was super tender.

I was here on my birthday and by fortuitous happenstance, we were seated front center to see a group called "Mood Ring", which did 1970's Adult Contemporary style music. Odd, but awesome!

The food nd service were impeccable. Top flight experience!

Mary Coul is the best bartender in Nashville! And that is saying something bc this town is AWESOME. capital A capital W capital E capital S capital O capital M capital E. The live band is super rad too. They play a lot of the older (read: better) country songs, but they aren't snobs. Had an amazing time here for a friend's birthday. Wish San Diego had as many outside bar, and more Mary Couls! Love! Love! Love!

Absolutely 0 air in this bar. The bathroom had shattered glass covering all 2 stalls. Line wrapped all the way down the bar. 

As far as bars on Broadway - the music was mediocre but the experience was not worth it. No standing room unless you want to breathe down someone's neck the whole time.

We decided to walk the line and ended up in this establishment. A local tour guide told us this was one of the best honky tonks in town. Most canned beer were just $2.50 and there was great live music. Ample seating for a large crowd and memorabilia many decades back, made us feel like we were there with Johnny himself.
If you like museum type things you'll probably like it.  They actually had a really good video presentation instead of the usual shitty ones you get.  It looks like a church on the inside.
Great music.  Thank you John and Lois Shepard for your 40 years of entertainment and making our visit so special.  Bologna sandwich highly recommended!

Salmon Oscar with crab meat, asparagus and hollandaise sauce. Salmon was good, not enough crab meat to even taste; asparagus was almost to the point of being tough.  Did 3 sides. Brussell sprouts were too large to be tender but still tasty, sweet potato was very sweet. Overall about the same dinner we would have had in the hotel restaurant but twice as expensive. No return business from us.
#PorkMcElhinny is an awesome entertainer. Fun atmosphere. Friendly wait staff. Stopped I because of a reference on Yelp and glad we did!
A lot of fun. Good bands. Ole country. We couldn't find a table and it was packed. Good service and food. Value.

Great food in a great location! Close to downtown if you are wanting to go out after dinner. Great patio seating as well. I would suggest making a reservation if you have more than 2 people. But if you have two people it's easy to find an open table by the bar with no wait.

Firstly, the music deserves 5 stars. The band that played was fantastic and nothing short of entertaining. They were everything I wanted from a jazz bar.  

However, the food was not great. The shrimp and crab dip was the best thing we ate, but it still wasn't phenomenal. I had the Oscar salmon. It did not have much flavor at all. They do have salt on the table, but when you charge that much for an entree why do I have to season my food? My husbands steak was fine, but again did not match the price. 

Overall, I would not come back for the food. The only reason I give it 3 stars is because of the amazing band!

Love, love, love the Ryman Auditorium!!!! You must absolutely put the Ryman on your list of places to visit when you are in Nashville, TN. The 11 minute video prior to entering the auditorium offers the audience the experience of being a part of history. The information and exhibits tell an amazing story, and at the end of it all, you can stand on the stage where so many talented singers have stood and have your picture taken. This is the soul of Nashville, you must check it out!

We made a reservation for a bachelorette party and the first issue was they couldn't make a reservation for our party of 13 so we had to have two separate tables. The next issue is that when we showed up for our reservation one table was seated and the second table was seated 25 minutes later. The second table received AND  finished their food before the first table received their order. The manager finally showed up to give us our food but the only excuse was that "a lot of big parties came in at the same time". The only saving grace was that the food was actually decent when we finally got it and the band was entertaining. The waitress was knowledgeable about the menu and did make good recommendations.
Absolute garbage. Wouldn't let me bring my backpack in and didn't provide any accommodations for it.

Hands down the best concert venue - not only in Nashville, but I believe anywhere! Seeing a show here is like being in church... there is a reverence in an audience for anyone who plays here. Maybe it's Nashville, maybe it's the building... but there is flat out respect among the crowd at a concert in this place.  I can't even recall who all I've seen here... Mumford and Sons, Bright Eyes, NeedtoBreathe, and Nickel Creek are some of my more memorable shows here. If you get a chance to see a show here, take it!
Nashville at it's best.  Good bands.  I just wish they didn't move out the tables and chairs.  Very limited seating so it's difficult to stay here very long.

I didn't know what to expect when walking into the Ryman Theater.  It was a beautiful experience.  Be careful where you park.  Prices vary widely.  BEWARE of Premier Parking.  Their logo is a script font 'P' on a blue background. You can see the logo above the pay station as you drive by.  They are not required to post the prices, so you won't know the cost until you park, unload the family, and are standing in front of the pay station.  If you think you'll add more time later, think again. A: You can't add more time like a parking meter; your time just starts over again. B: they can engage in "rush hour" pricing.  There are many low cost municipal options.  Plan before you go.  I ended up paying $40 for 5 hours of parking at a Premier Lot.  I called them and was told I should know better.  According to online complaints they will easily ticket you, too.  Do yourself a favor and just stay away from their parking lots.

It was a great backstage tour of the place. You got to see the entire place and learn about the history of the auditorium.  The new video was really cool. I've never experience something like that before.  It is something that you have to experience.  It would come here before I would go to the country music hall of fame,  there is more history and information here to see and experience.

Had such high expectations and was sadly disappointed. Ordered medium rare filet. Sent it back. Still came out medium to medium well. Tough. Tasteless. Only offered free dessert. Creme brûlée was less than desirable as well. Service was poor. Will not be back. I prefer filet from Stoney River or J. Alexander's as a comparison.
Another Nashville staple.  Crowded and loud.  Go in for one drink and band set, then move to another bar.
Amazing food, talented musicians and fabulous and friendly staff. Couldn't be happier with our second stop in Nashville.

My passion on the weekends are great music, service and cold beer!!! This particular gem of a bar provides exactly what I am looking for. If you want to grab a bottle of water during the day/night  and listen to live music or throw down shots and a beer; this clean, always nicely staffed bar will satisfy your need!!! 

I travel 12 hours from Northern WI, and have been coming to Nashville for over 15 years. This is an amazingly bar every time; that fits all ages and personalities you will walk in and out with a smile on your face!!!

We had stopped by here for my cousin's birthday a few weeks ago. The place was pretty packed on a Tuesday night and we managed to order food and beers at the bar before snagging a table. The Chris Casello trio was playing the majority of the night and I absolutely loved them! They are such an amazing and talented band! My cousin had a great time for her birthday and her man even got the band and the bar to sing happy birthday for her. Also, the cheeseburger with chips I ordered was very tasty and delicious, I'd come back just for the food alone but everything about this place was awesome. Being from Seattle, I was definitely out of my element, but the people and the environment are so dang inviting, it's hard not to start stomping your boots around after just a short time! I'd love to come back!
Came here hoping for a little but above par food and music. Both were disappointing. Food was cold and pretty bland overall.
Best deal on Honky Tonk Row. A fun, divey place. The special was $5 for bologna sandwich or hot dog and a beer. Live guitar player was good. Just had fun.
Food was absolutely amazing, our server was great as well! Music was fun, you will be charged a $2 "entertainment fee".

Our visit started off poorly when the hostess said "I need your drinks" immediately after greeting us (referring to our empty coffee cups that we would have thrown away had they had a trash can outside). It just seemed extremely rude. 
Once we were seated, our server Robby greeted us and he was amazing from beginning to end. He made great suggestions and never rushed us. He was very laid back and knowledgable in the best possible way.
The food was very good but the difference in portion sizes between the flat iron steak and the salmon was kind of odd. 
The band playing the night we were there was unreal! A lady named sissy was singing with them but I can't recall what the band's name was. 
The only other thing I found odd was the fact that a restaurant this nice has paper dinner menus. 
Overall, great experience!
Solid honky tonk on Broadway with cheap drinks, great live music and no douche bags. Seems there's a reason this is the spot locals say hit up if you must go to Broadway. And you must!

We selected the Self guided tour for $20 on a Tuesday morning. It took our party of 4 around an hour to make our way through. There was a defined route to follow with informational booths and videos along the way. The Ryman is a rich piece of musical history in the Music City and our visit there completed our trip. I really enjoyed the video at the beginning of the tour that explained the history.
Really enjoyed it here. A must see if you are downtown. Part of history. I love the Minnie Pearl tribute too. She was one of a kind.

The food court was awesome! Everything we ordered was delicious. The guy at the juice bar was really friendly and let us sample a couple of things before ordering. The tapas place was awesome, the worst part was only that they had sold out of two items I wanted to try! We went on a Sunday and there was a Mariachi band playing, a kids story time, two different acrobatics shows, and another three piece band. That was all just in the 2 hours we were there. I look forward to going back for more!

Don't hesitate to hit this bar.  It's not the commercialised bar with high priced food and drinks.  $2.50 PBR and MHL.  Simple burger and fry menu, but who cares.  

Highly recommend coming to this "dive" bar.  As always, they usually are the best.  Great place to sit and chill with a band.  

The only drawback is that it's not great for large groups.  Tables are pub style meant for only a few people but you can push them together.

To whom it may concern - The atmosphere of your establishment was acceptable for Broadway standards however, your tacos make taco Bell seem like a 5 Star restaurant. Whose bright idea was it to ruin beef tacos with a crunchy nasty crusty meat type thing. It takes an incredible amount of effort to make me hate a taco, in this instance you succeed in every aspect. I can now continue my life with the knowledge that the worse taco ever created was created in your kitchen. I think it would be acceptable for a trophy to be displayed somewhere for such an accomplishment. Sincerely the guy that from now one will always be in fear of what's hiding between the tortilla shell.
Food was ok passable. Service was slow and inattentive. We had cheese burgers. Music meh next door at orchid was better. But this place has so much potential to be awesome that is why we stopped.

One of my favorite music venues in the country. Incredible acoustics, unique decor and vintage Americana atmosphere. The seats are similar to church pews. Staff and security here are very friendly and don't take themselves too seriously. I saw a concert here last night and thoroughly enjoyed the entire experience.

Beer and mixed drinks were $9, which is insane, but whatever, the Ryman is so cool that they can get away with it.

I doubt I have anything to say about the Ryman that hasn't already been said. It's just a great place to see a show. I haven't done a tour as we try to stay away from downtown until dinner/showtime.

Many folks say that balcony seating is the way to go, but I've never been up there. I've been under the balcony a couple of times, and for the last three-night run, I was in section 2, row J. Those were great seats but I think I'll shoot for balcony next time just to have that experience.
Pretty standard honky tonk that has good music every once and a while. The coolest thing is that they serve a poor boy special- a fried bologna sandwich, a bag of chips, and a PBR.

A great convention and event center, in a great location in downtown Nashville. Parking is the only negative. $15 on a Sunday to park in the garage for the Antiques and Garden Show in the Music City Center is a bit much.

It's hard to miss this building downtown as it kind of looks like a UFO.  It's home to concerts, roller derby matchups, our indoor football league (didn't know we had one?), the annual Beer, Bourbon, and BBQ fest, as well as other various shows and exhibits and events throughout the year.  It my not be the most aesthetically pleasing venue you've ever been in, but its extremely spacious and conveniently located right downtown so it makes for a good place for many social gatherings.  There's a lots of parking nearby too which is a plus.  They have lots of spots for food and beers ad its exactly the kind of food you'd expect at a place like this.  I've never had any issues with the staff and everyone's always helpful.  It's essentially a little dome, like a bite-size Bridgestone.

Wow, I can't believe I have been in Nashville for three years and just got around to coming here! The drinks were great, service was excellent and then there was the food. I ordered bruschetta and three sides, asparagus, au gratin potatoes and carrots (I don't eat much meat) and everything was amazing. The bruschetta especially since they serve it in a dish with warm toast which prevents it from getting the bread soggy. I honestly don't remember what my bf got but he loved it as well! The atmosphere is fun and laid back while maintaining a level of classy elegance. Will definitely be going back!

My wife and I are big fans of Nashville (the city, not the horrible soap opera). Once a year, we make the 925 mile trek to Nashville for music, food, and the fantastic scene. Our first stop is always Robert's Western World. There's nothing fancy about this place. The menu consists of fried bologna sandwiches, burgers, and various tasty fried snacks. Heck, there's even a veggie burger on there. Though they have a full bar and a great selection of bottled beer, that's not what you want. What you want is an ice-cold can of PBR for $2.50. The music is as good as it gets on Broadway. I'm talking fantastic musicians playing old-time, bluegrass, classic country, and honky-tonk. You will not hear any obnoxious bro-country/pop-country. I recommend keeping an eye out for Rachael Hester and Don Kelley Band. Also, no trip to Nashville is complete without catching a set by John and Lois Shepherd. 

As great as the music is at Robert's, the element that holds this whole thing together is the fabulous staff. As soon as you walk up to the bar, you realize that you're dealing with people who like their job. Though we're just tourists on our annual vacation, they immediately make you feel like locals. It's people like Hope B. (not to forget Teresa and Hank) who make your Nashville experience fun and welcoming, as opposed to feeling like just another anonymous patron. 

Nashville is a great city. As much as we love going to The Ryman, or eating at Husk and Rolf and Daughters, it's Robert's Western World that keeps us coming back. Hank you.

How can anyone NOT like The Ryman?! Been here several times for concerts and love coming every time. The stain glass windows are beautiful, I love the layout of the venue - very intimate.  They recently re-did the entrance and added a cafe, which is awesome. My only complaint is the parking situation. Valet is crazy expensive and if you want to park your car yourself, you still have to pay to park in a lot nearby. No free parking, boo. If you live in Nashville or are visiting, you MUST attend a show here. It's historical, magical, and awe-inspiring!
Great place great music and good prices on drinks and food. Thanks for a really good time.

These people were super rude and racist!! I have never encountered such a disgustingly gross and mean spirited group of people in my 46 years of life! This bar is appalling and I can't even believe how sad and mean they are to minority's and women. They should be ashamed of themselves and learn tolerance and respect for others. Sick WHITE TRASH!!! They deserve MINUS STARS!!

This p[lace has a definite old school vibe. The band plays pre 1980 country music. The décor is very vintage inside, as is the menu and the small grill in the middle of the bar that they cook it on. Drink prices seemed a bit lower here than other places on the street. The staff was very nice. I enjoyed my stop here.

I loved the look of this place as we walked in. It was a Sunday night and a great four-piece band was playing music onstage.
We were really well taken care of, with staff that was attentive but not overbearing. 
We shared an order of Buca Beignets, and they were really great. I had a good, not great, Caesar salad and then the 7 oz filet. The steak was prepared to my liking. It wasn't an amazing cut, but it was good. We enjoyed sweet potatoes and Mac and Cheese as sides, both very good.
We finished the meal with a piece of white chocolate cheesecake. It was rich, but not too rich, which made it a little too easy to eat.
I would give it a 4.5 if that was an option. On the strength of the service and great live music, I'm rounding up.

Great live music and cool decor make this place stand out from some of the other places downtown. This bar had a good vibe going on a Thursday night and we could have shut this place down if not for our Friday morning plans. Next time I'm in Nashville I'm paying a visit here
Good conference center. Clean, convenient, and newish. The staff is helpful and friendly. The food is above average when compared to other conference centers.

The night we visited a 70's rock cover band, Mood Ring, was playing. I loved it and sand along with every song! My nephew knew one song. Lol. The service was a bit slow but the place has great ambience and the plating was phenomenal, it makes you feel like someone really took the time to care about your meal. We started with the shrimp and crab dip appetizer. It was excellent with freshly cooked tortilla chips. We had the pork chop, Mediterranean veggie lasagna and the lobster ravioli. The food was good but not as phenomenal as the plating. The creme brûlée for desert was excellent. During the bands break the lead singer stopped by our table to chat and ask us if we were enjoying the music. This was a very nice personal touch. We sat at the back booth which was great because we could all mostly see the stage but not too close that we couldn't have a conversation. Nice place!

Came here with my co-workers. What an awesome experience! Our bartender Hope, was the best. Her service was first class. 

The music was old school country. Bob Kelly band were the best. The decor on the wall is cowboy boots and pics of old country western signings. 

They have typical bar food but you need to try the fried bologna sandwich, which is killer!  

If your visiting Nashville you must come to ROBERTS Western World. I will be back!
While visiting I was brought here and absolutely loved it. A great place to eat or hang out and listen to the live jazz band. Service was great. Will definitely come back upon the next visit.
So so so delish!!! Shared a bunch of appys and they were all amazing.  Highly recommend

Great food in Nashville!  Started with this wonderful ginger & vodka spiced drink called the "cock n' bull" and then had goat-cheesed filled artichokes for an appetizer. So good!!  The entree was squid infused linguine with lobster, scallops. Really really good. Not to mention the service

AMAZING! Great food and great atmosphere. Somewhat pricey, but 100% worth it. We were seated in front of the live band. Our waiter was great and recommended what he thought was best, which turned out to be perfect. Went with a group of 5 and it was great.

We had heard great things about this place and the happy hour in particular so we were excited to check it out when we got a gift certificate to go there. The venue is very nice with a large bar area. We placed ourselves at one end of the bar which was a little bit behind a pillar. The food and drinks were good, but we had pretty bad service. I don't know if it was because of the pillar, but we literally finished our drinks and food and nobody checked on us for 20 minutes. We were all set to order more drinks and more food, but because we had to wait so long, I just couldn't stay. 
The food itself was good; we had a great margherita pizza and some good satay. Wine on the happy hour list was among the better we've seen at local places. We would have gotten more, but like I said we just couldn't keep waiting around forever. Maybe we'll try again at some point, but pretty disappointing.
What a cool place. Great for families. Came on a Sunday night and it was a full night of entertainment and food.

Of all of the bars located on Broadway, I'd have to say this was our favorite!  We always enjoyed the bands and the bartender's are friendly and provide great service.  The drinks seemed to be slightly less expensive than the rest of the bars nearby, although everything on Broadway is pricey.  Can't wait to come back!!!

If I could rate it higher I would.

Went there for the tour during the day followed by a concert by Steve Miller that night. The atmosphere is incredible and the sound quality is right up there with the other iconic performing halls like Carnegie Hall.

It is a must for all music fans.
This place is so fun and you can actually move inside. The band is fantastic, the pizza is good and greasy and the drinks are a good pour! A must visit as you do the pub crawl down Broadway.

Only went in for drinks. Bartender was good.

I understand wanting to entice everyone from the street to come in, but the music was a bit loud. We left after just one beer.
Constantly asks u for tips and make fun of u if you don't give it. Awful. Music may be good but attitude sucks big time. Won't come back here again.

Legends was a blast. It was packed, but it wasn't so packed we couldn't move. The music was great and the bar service was great. By the end of the night (130) some people were pretty sloppy drunk, but it was still a great time with good music! It was a lot of fun. I definitely recommend it and no cover!

Not a very busy Saturday but there was a 30 minute wait for a table. Ordered fried chicken with mashed Good which was delicious. Ordered the Kobe burger medium well which came out rare. I sent it back and they just took it and seared it bun & all. Not my preference it should have been taken off & redressed. Will not come again, slow service and mediocre food

The Band was fun . Bartenders on the most part ok. Drinks over priced. Staff and bouncers SUPER RUDE!!  Went there with another couple all in our 40's, enjoing the Tim Mcgraw look alike band. Spent alot of $ on drinks and food, we were all standing up by the bar next to a smelly garbage can, so we moved it aside (3x). Busboy kept moving it back. Then he went and got an over weight (B Team Bouncer) to kick us all out. Is that how you treat your clientele? People come to Nashville to enjoy the Honky Tonks and listen to bands. They should not be treated like 2nd rate citizens. Alot of the reviews for Legends say the same thing. Maybe if an owner or a good manager would be on duty, this place could be better. What would happen if word gets around how bad the Bars in Nashille treat the folks who travel from far away places. What if your business starts slowing down and its not a $ maker anymore, would the Owners pay attention then? WHAT HAPPENED TO THE CUSTOMER IS ALWAYS RIGHT?     Time to train customer Service!!

Came in with my mom for lunch and got the spinach and goat cheese omelette, which came with breakfast potatoes and fruit.  The food was really good, but even better was the build your own Bloody Mary bar!  They bring you a glass with vodka and you add your own bloody mix along with olives, pickles, bacon, and anything else you can think of!!  The atmosphere was also very cool with a live band and our server was very friendly as well!!

The Ryman is a beautiful place full of history that is well worth a visit. Nothing wrong with the building or tour. 
We went on a $20 tour. 

Neat video. 

Here's what I don't like:
This is Nashville, Tennessee, and 6 of the 10 people in our group had basic pocketknives. This is the SOUTH. 

The utterly stupid security rules don't allow for any kind of pocketknife. You go through metal detectors. My belt buckle set off the alarm. One of our group members had to walk back a mile to the car to drop off our "weapons". (Swiss army knives and a leatherman) 

He missed the tour, at least they refunded his ticket money. 

But that's just ridiculous. Again, this is Tennessee. 

Oh, and they will charge $20 for a photo on the edge of the stage. You can't use your phone. 

I loved the bulding, but the policies really made it feel uninviting and were 100% unnecessary.
Bologna sandwich !!!!  WOW !!! Never thought I would enjoy it as much. Sweet potato fries and onion rings also very good.

A colleague wanted to try out Sambuca since it was nearby and was a bit different than the other restaurants in Nashville.  The menu looked delicious with items ranging from lobster enchiladas to a red snapper étouffeé.  However, the food itself was just "meh" and wasn't really memorable.  We happened to be there on a night with live music and were seated right in front of the stage.  Although a conversation may be possible if you were seated further back, I could barely hear myself up front. 

One highlight of my experience is the Tennessee Mule, which is served in a pretty big glass (maybe it was more surprising to me since I'm used to those little copper mugs).  The dinner was okay; I might try to come back for their bar and see if they have a happy hour!

Sadly, I have not had a chance to hear any music at the Ryman.  Instead, I did the next best thing and took a tour.  I loved learning all about the history of this auditorium.  For $20, you can take a self-guided tour through the venue.

You start out watching a short video that goes through a high level history of the auditorium.  I typically am not a fan of these types of videos, but this one was actually engaging and entertaining.  After the video, you are on your own to go through the self-guided tour.  You get a map that clearly shows where you need to go.  They do a great job of roping things off so you don't wander in the wrong place.

I loved being able to just sit down in the balcony and the lower level.  It was cool to see the differences in your view.  I'd definitely buy a balcony seat if I ever get the chance to check out a show here.

My favorite part of the tour was being able to see all of the signed posters from Hatch Show Print.  They make the best posters!

Beautiful venue for shows-  rumor is that Led Zepplin's Robert Plant has named the Ryman as his favorite American venue.  
It kept a lot of the church feel with pretty stained glass windows (during summer shows the sun lights them up as it's setting) and worn, almost comfortable wooden pews.  They also have cases of country music memorabilia, really neat to see it up close.
I love watching the Grand Old Opry here on Thursday nights, Larry Gatlin is a great host and I like the crowd better here than on Saturdays at Opryland.  The concession stands are nice, the acoustics are beautiful and the whole experience of watching a show in Music City at the Mother Church of Country Music is one of the best things about living in Tennessee.
Not the best place for day drinking.  Food didn't look good, really small / hard to get a table, and the bands were so lame when we were there. Will not return, not sure what the hype is about?

Didn't eat or drink here. Walked in, started to go upstairs and was told no one's serving up there. Went to bar downstairs but waited a few minutes and no service. Moved on. Band seemed ok. Typical country band. Crowd was tame and around age 50. Went on a Wednesday around 5:30 though.
First time here. Waitress wasn't the friendliest, but my food was amazing! I would definitely recommend the brisket and shrooms quesadilla.  The live music was great too!

Came here for lunch, absolutely wonderful!!! The food is awesome, server is so nice, he split our meals into two and even gave us an extra cup of soup. Great place and great food. Turkey and Brie sandwich and red snapper étouffée are some great recommendations. Would skip the dessert though, tiramisu and creme brûlée were disappointing. But after all, food and service are great.

Don't go to Robert's for the food or the service.  Go to Robert's to hear great country music and for drinks.  Among all of the bars in downtown Nashville, this one had the best ambience and feel about what Nashville is all about.

Was there for 3-day conference. I got lost almost everyday because it was very different to see which floor I was on. It's very confusing. I wish there was a big or a visible sign showing floor level. It was huge, nicely designed and clean but something simple like the floor/ level sign should be easy to read/ find.

We are vegan and try to find adventure in the many restaurant experiences in Nashville. Madera in the Plaza Mariachi did not disappoint . We had the corn cakes stuffed with vegetables , the jicama salad and the jackfruit entree.
So much flavor, fun, and excitement. all were colorful and full of unusual flavors.
We will return to repeat the experience .
Thank you, Madera.

Best venue in Nashville, without a doubt.

Best venue in the US?  Quite possibly.

So blessed to live half a mile away from The Ryman.  Every show is an experience that you'll never forget.  I honestly could see anyone there and enjoy it... even if I wasn't too familiar with the artist.  The acoustics are one in a million and the building is absolutely stunning.

Tip:  While buying tickets, if you can't get up close... the balcony seats are much better than the far back floor seats.  Definitely!

My flatiron steak was gristly and tasted like a whole bottle of spicy rub was poured on it. I couldn't taste the potatoes or the cheese in the au gratin potatoes for the copious amount of garlic-I love garlic, but that was was too much. My stomach hurt an hour or two after eating, then my guts-still 15 hours later. I would have sent it back but for two reasons- 1. I didn't want date night to be ruined. 2. Courtney, asked if everything LOOKED good, after I had had only one bite of green beans. Then nothing. The coconut mojito was good, though overpriced. The band's selection were decent, but the vocalist was sick, so he sounded bad, which the restaurant manager pointed out to us. Too bad he didn't stay long enough to ask what I thought of my meal.
My wife and I had a wonderful time the food and service was great. The jazz band was awesome, this is my favorite new place to come to in Nashville. If you are in Nashville this is a must visit.
Pretty good, 5 star on check book, however, treat yourself and the food is excellent.

What a nice addition to south Nashville! From the outside you'd never know how upscale, classy and cool this place is (as you know it used to just be a shopping center Kroger). Inside is beautiful, great art and architecture. A lot of great Latin and Hispanic business, food, drink, snacks and desserts. Great customer service, friendly folks everywhere including guest service coordinators making the rounds and introducing themselves.

Live music that is of excellent quality, clean and new, original and creative. We strolled through many of the stores, my friends grabbed a margarita at the Cuban restaurant, we chowed down on some delicious ice cream at the Paletas Tocumbo.

Stop in next time you are in south Nashville!

Must go if you live near or are traveling to Nashville. This is a small and old building, but offers the best, most intimate availability for music that you can partake. A true Nashville staple, inside and out. Highly recommended. (Nashville tip: ALWAYS sit in the balcony. Don't complain about being put behind a column in the back bottom, the balcony is better anyway.)

While the band was great, they were playing Purple Rain when we walked in, I witnessed a bar tender upstairs, begin to mix a round of 5-6 shots, shook them and then when about to strain them into the cups the strainer fell in the garbage.  He proceeded to pick the strainer right out of the garbage, not rinse it nor wipe it off and strained the shots into their cups and served them.  Thankfully the shots were not for me.  I was appalled and left abruptly.  Drink at your own risk.

Even if you are not into country music, you have to take this tour. It's self guided and will teach you about the history of how music made its way into Nashville. The Ryman embraces all. The 15 minute movie at the start giving the history of the Ryman is very interesting. Very reasonably priced way to learn some Nashville history.
I'm not even a country western music fan, but I loved it. The tour was worth every penny!!!!!

Hot Saturday afternoon and we were looking for music and cold drinks.

We immediately found a booth even though the place was pretty crowded.  Quick service.  Amazing $2 tea and soda in huge cups.  Attentive service and free refills.  Great music.  Fun place!
While the facility was nice beware of the conference food.  I was served raw chicken at lunch. The breakfast muffins tasted like they came out of a jiff box.
Legends corner is awesome! tell the cabbie to take you to 5th and Broadway. Every time I go to Nashville I start here, if it's busy use the side entrance on 5th, The music is always always great

Wandered in and found an amazing place. Good drinks (had the moonshine margarita) and snacked on the chicken 'n waffle nuggets. We were fighting over those suckers. Did I mention bacon? 
Music was loud and great to rock out to. A must stop as you walk down Broadway.

Robert's Western World was exactly what I needed after a long flight. It was the first bar I went to in Nashville, and it had live music and an open kitchen.

It's a long bar with a lot of seating, but it gets crowded (especially with the dedicated cowboy boot rack on the wall). I watched the Don Kelley band here twice, and both times they rocked the house.

The bar takes up more than half the side of the place, which is both good and bad. It's good because there's a ton of bar seating, and it's bad because it's tough to get a bartender's attention.

That said, I ordered the Recession special - a fried bologna sandwich, bag of chips, and a PBR for the low, low price of $5. Was it worth $5? Definitely. Would I order it again? Probably not.

The grill man was doing a great job, but the waitstaff was a bit backed up and food was just sitting on the counter for a while.

The fried bologna sandwich is a misnomer. No part of it is fried. The bologna is grilled. The bread is grilled. But it was definitely a bologna sandwich.

My husband and I are a bit older than the younger crowd around Nashville.  It was difficult for us to find a bar with CLASSIC COUNTRY MUSIC, until we peaked into Robert's Western World.  Dave Cox was on stage and we were happy to sit and just enjoy the music.  Our bartender was friendly and joined him on stage with a Patsy Cline tune and that was just fine too.  Thank goodness there's still a bar on Broadway that caters to classic music.

The ambience, atmosphere and the music make this place truly unique. It's never a dull evening at the restaurant. The food has always been great. I've personally only had the pizza, but what great pizza it was. 

The wait staff were exceptional. Even on a day when they were busier than usual r waitress provided just amazing service in the bar area nonetheless.

Very positive experience and i can't wait to go again.

This place was one of the best spots I checked out while in Nashville. The band "Casello Trio" or something like that was the best band we saw. Three older guys playing rockabilly with obvious talent and skills to spare. I had a few BPRs and was really tempted to try the "fried bologna" deal for just $5 bucks. Its the sandwich, a bag a chips and a PBR for just $5 bucks! Amazing! In NYC this doesn't exist. PBR alone is at least $4 bucks. 

This is the obvious stop for anyone's honkytonk tour ..

My significant otter and I decided to do the Broadway touristy thing during our stay in Nashville and I'm so glad we selected Robert's Western World. Great burgers and fried bologna. Excellent service - one woman was waiting on everyone and making the drinks on our Thursday afternoon visit. She's awesome! Great band!! They played all the classics and sounded fantastic on each.

My wife and I stopped in late one afternoon after hearing the music as we explored Broadway. The band was playing bluesy covers and sounded great. We grabbed a local beer (Mantra Saffron IPA), found a table and enjoyed the music. It was before the evening rush so the timing was perfect for us. We had a great time. I'd definitely go back.

This is absolutely my favorite spot ever. It has live music and fantastic food! I've been several times and every time I like it more and more. The music is fantastic! Great Cocktails and ambiance! So far for my Nashville spots this is my favorite!

The Ryman is beautiful.  Nestled in the streets of Nashville, it's a well kept, beautiful building full of so much history.  It's so clean and well cared for, you could almost believe it was built today with the throw back style.  It's small - which we loved, and made for a very intimate show (and we were in the back row!).  I'll admit, the whole church pew thing freaked me out a bit.  I worried what if I was next to some seat hogs, or people who were eating popcorn and throwing it all over the place, or what if the seat numbers weren't really numbers.  But, once I sat, the seat was comfortable, I had plenty of space, and most important, we had a great view of the stage.

The sound is amazing - and I am sure that's why it's been used by so many stars.  Hands down one of the best venues to see a concert.

And, I'd suggest the balcony- unobstructed views.  It looks like the orchestra (aside from the first few rows) has a less open view.

Just got back from the Chicago concert at the Ryman Auditorium-it was amazing!! I had wanted to go to a concert after touring a few years ago and this was my first opportunity. We sat in the balcony near the center and had a good view of the stage. The seats are church pews with nothing separating your space with your neighbors, but that was not an issue.
