The sound was wonderful, I really enjoyed the show as did my husband. I hope I get to back again. If you have the chance, I would recommend going to see a show there. The tour is interesting and gives a great history of the building and the Grand Ole Opry.

Oh course you have to stop by Robert's. Classic country music, cheap beer, and a must see bar. The great things about the Broadway honky tonks is that you just walk next door to see what's up there once you've had a beer or two at the first (or fourth) place!

This place was amazing. First time there and came with group for my boyfriends bday. Cory was our waiter and was great. Food was amazing and drinks were so good too. The only Thing I could say is it seemed a bit like we were rushed. But live band was great and I would absolutely come back.

I think this is the only bar on Broadway I actually liked. Beer and drinks are reasonably priced. The security was super nice. They threw out a guy who was incredibly inappropriate with my friend. The music was great, and I loved the vibe. Really liked this place!

Great place, whether you come in for a few minutes or stay a few hours.  Friendly staff, great burgers and beer selection.  Prices are fine, food a great value.  Don't miss the onion rings and the grilled cheese is perfect, gotta try it, don't mock it.  The band is great, their play list speaks to the history of country music, what a talented band.

"People are wantin' to know who you've been sleepin' with to get on the Opry so quick." -- Coal Miner's Daughter (1980)

Oddly, with all the concerts I see in a year, I've yet to attend one at The Ryman. It's still on my bucket list, but it's bound to happen sooner than later.

On my recent trip to Nashville, we decided to take the tour and I'm so glad we did. The price tag is $20 and well worth it as I learned so much history is just a short time. I was in awe. You start by watching a fun movie that explains the beginnings of the place and how it was the Grand Old Opry and how it was then resurrected - it was fun and was more than just watching a bland and boring VHS tape - I won't give anything more away. As you leave, they give you a numbered map and then you begin the self-guided tour.

I'll admit, I suck at self-guided tours, but I prefer them to having someone drone on about a place to me - unless they are really engaging. So this was probably best for me. I just don't tend to follow instructions. First, I was distracted for a long time by the posted from previous shows that were signed by the artists, framed and hanging just outside the main auditorium. I spent a lot of time looking at the posters, and being sad I didn't see these shows. Shout out to Dave Grohl. 

We wandered for a long time and read everything there was to read and sat in the balcony and lower level (this is awesome because now I know where to sit for shows) and just took it all in. I resisted the urge to buy any schwag in the store as I know I will be back for a show soon.
We're from Detroit, and one of the locals at dinner recommended this place for good honky tonk, and it was so good we just stayed here the whole night. Both bands were awesome, and no cover!
One of my favorite spots we crawled to during our vacation to Nashville. And bonus it was St. Pattys day!!:)

I attended Walker Stalker Con April 9 and 10, 2016 with my son Brian.  This was my Christmas present, and I have to say it was an awesome experience.  There was a lot of walking, but they had tons of seating along the way, and accommodated us with seating inside for anyone who needed a break.  The Whole Walker Stalker experience was awesome!  We had VIP tickets which got us in early, into events early, and early entry for meet and greet and photo ops.  I have to say that I have read reviews on other Walker Stalker Conventions that were not good as far as organization, but not this one!  Everything was organized.  Even with a ton of people we never felt as if we were standing in a huge line forever to see someone and all of the stars were so friendly and awesome to talk to.  I have new favorites just from going.  Ross Marquand, and Tom Payne are so very nice.  If you watch the Walking Dead, and you have an opportunity to go, do it!  It was so fun, and Nashville, is a C R A Z Y party town.  Go to the Opry Mills Mall as it is gigantic, and check out the Opry Center.  The whole area is just beautiful with tons of things to do after you get your zombie fix.  And the Barbecue is great.
Standard Nashville bar, pop in if you're walking by but nothing to rave about (or complain about) from my experience.

My go-to for real honky tonk music in downtown Nashville. Do my best to go 5-6 times a year. My last visit came a week ago, and my usual cheeseburger and fries were spot on. Swear they are best fries in downtown. The beer is good; the waitresses are attentive, despite the chaos, and music is great. What more do you want?!

A quaint place that hosts a rich history for those with an affinity for country music and just love the simple lifestyle. A good attraction for those that enjoy live music and rustic food that is really cheap in comparison to most others. Service was responsible in their timing dispute being over in with so many customers. Enjoyable bar scene for those that enjoy the most barebones type of experience.
This is a great place to watch a football game and have some great food and drinks. The atmosphere is good and the staff friendly.  There is always live music.

The atmosphere was great. Our server Jade was awesome and sweet. She made sure our drinks were filled and our food was prepared right. We had no issues with our orders. The band they had last night Paulina Jayne (6/26) was amazing. We will definitely be back.
If you are looking for a real Nashville feel come here! Luke Nickles and his band are fabulously entertaining. Great place for a drink and here great music. Don't want to leave.

I went to Nashville for a friend's bachelorette party. The night we all went out we decided to start by having dinner at Sambuca. The service was terrible. It took them 45 minutes to figure out our checks. Due to the time it took us to eat and the check debacle we started our night out very late.

Delicious food, super swanky sexy live music in the background and Jesse our server absolutely killed it. I'm a bartender of 10 years and have super high standards and I've never been happier with a server, really ever. Love the atmosphere and good time attitude. Thanks Jesse for a kick ass meal.

Went to see the Black Crowes while we were in town and the show was phenomenal.  The acoustics were a little sketchy but I'm not sure it was the fault of anyone specifically.  When inside you just FEEL the music of days gone by.  The vibe is fantastic.  I wish we had done a tour to see the venue in daylight to really appreciate it.  Next time!

I got a sandwich with Andouille sausage and shrimp. It was delicious with a kick and I couldn't stop eating the crinkle fries. I also tried my friend's southwest quesadilla and loved it! We chose Tin Roof based on the music and a picture of the sandwich ordered. The bartender was friendly and I felt like I made the right choice stopping here.

I really enjoyed Sambuca, the food was great and the entertainment was very good. Defiantly one if not my favorite place to go to. I would highly recommend you trying it out. You will not be disappointed. I look forward to going back.

I went here to get a late lunch (3pm on Saturday) to go, based on Yelp reviews and the fact that their menu prices seemed reasonable for something simple.   Sorry to disagree with so many other Yelpers on this one, but my experience clearly was different than theirs and I wasn't looking for music. 

The place was extremely busy and it took me a while to make my way to the bar/register area. One of the bartenders took my food order, and said they could do it to go which was great. I ordered, paid and waited. And waited...while other people kept getting their food. 

After 25 minutes I got her attention again (after she helped several other customers) and she didn't recognize me at all just asked if she could help me with anything. I asked if she could check on my food order, she asked what table I was at, I said it was a to go order and I'd been standing there. The look on her face told me she had forgotten about it. She brought me the food, and said it had completely slipped her mind. 

The food itself was okay...grilled cheese sandwich was decent but soggy (due to sitting around I'm guessing), the fries I got as a side were crinkle cut fries clearly from a bag and they were undercooked  the fries were definitely not worth the up-charge for getting them instead of chips. 

I might try this place again, but more likely to go elsewhere.

The Ryman: The Mother Church of Country Music. You walk in this place and you can feel the history. The seats are wooden pews, it's great! I've been here a few times and every show has been great!
My two favorite shows have been Elle King and Kacey Musgraves "A Very Kacey Christmas." I'm pretty sure Elle King married a couple on stage and then Kacey Musgraves put a beautiful Christmas show on!

Sambuca is chic with lavish decor, made for the young and hip professionals of today. A great place to go and unwind, grab a drink and listen to live music. For you with a immense palate, the food is amazing.

A visit to the Ryman is nothing of a religious experience for music lovers, and considering the building's history as an evangelical church, that's an appropriate analogy. The history of this incredible venue overpowers you from the moment you walk in, and really comes alive when you take a backstage tour. You'll stand on the famous Ryman stage, see the dressing rooms that honor the building's rich musical past, and hear fascinating anecdotes about the famous performers whose careers were launched in the Mother Church of Country Music.

After the tour, take time to linger in the auditorium and see the displays recounting its colorful history. Run your hands along the wooden pews where thousands of music lovers have sat for more than one hundred years, and soak in the atmosphere that makes the Ryman one of the most memorable places in America. 

Then make time to come back for a show, where the space comes alive with miraculous acoustics, the thunder of more than 2,000 fellow music lovers stomping their feet in unison, and the wonderful call-and-response between musicians and their fans. I took in a Bluegrass Legends show, and came away with a new appreciation for the essentially American style of music that was born on the Ryman stage.

Like Preservation Hall in New Orleans, or Carnegie Hall in New York, the Ryman is a shrine to the music that makes America great. If you're ever fortunate enough to be in Nashville, be sure to make it your first stop.

I was in Nashville for a national convention and decided to break away from the pack and explore this on my own.  Sure glad I did, they call this "The First Church of Country Music" and it's A-MAZING!  Any fan of music, not just country music, will appreciate this living museum.  I wish I would have more time to just walk around and explore and just learn and soak in the vibe.  I got there the last tour, want to say it cost around 15 bucks for the tour.  The tour was cool, we were lead around by some old-school codger who knew his history.  I enjoyed going backstage, getting to peak into the dressing rooms where some of the best musicians ever have graced the stage.  You get a sense of the tradition and importance of this place hearing the stories and seeing the sights, the spirit is still there.  Seeing a live show here is definitely on my bucket list, I hear the acoustics are perfection and it's such a beautiful stage.  In a city known for music, this is one place you have to hit, it's the real deal you all!

Great place...so much fun. We ate great food and watched an excellent mariachi band!!
We will definitely return!!

Great atmosphere!! Love the energy on a Saturday afternoon, watching college football and listening to some great music! Ben Matthis and Taryn Papa are crowd pleasers! The bartenders Tony and Vince are super friendly.

This is the only Tin Roof location I ever been to that I enjoyed, it has a great location right in the heart of Nashville on Broadway. The food is not the best but the atmosphere is lively and the service is good, friendly people. After visiting other US cities I am glad Nashville has really friendly and welcoming people for the most part especially in hospitality they know how to do it right.

In the sea of honky tonk's and chaos on Broadway, there is the heaven of Robert's Western World. A savior for the hungry patrons who are looking for some great music and delicious food. The fried bologna sandwiches (and I hope I wasn't just intoxicated) are FREAKING AMAZING! The fried pickle spears (although they burned my mouth horribly) were unforgettable, and the crowd was perfect. This place definitely stands out to me from the 20+ establishments we visited that night in Nashville.
Excellent meal.  We ordered the scallops and sea bass and both entrees were awesome.  One suggestions if u wanna talk try and get a table away from live music.  Music was very good though.

This place is awesome, perfect for any history or country music buff. We came here on Friday might to see Chris Young, Ashley Monore and Michael Ray. What a great show! We had such a good time and all the hosts were so funny! A must do in Nashville if you can get tickets to go. Concessions are allowed in the theater, so feel free to buy wine or beer at the concession stands to enjoy during the show.
Decent music. The bands are entertainers not just musicians which is fun. Similar to most spots on Broadway, it has walls covered in albums and cool stuff. Only serves pizza but the pizza was good.

Great music, if you sit in the back you can carry on a conversation, and hear great music. Waited awhile for our food, the Sweet Tea, delicious, nice big cups. We are from Chicago Illinois, and have been here for a week and have been here twice. Fried pickles great.

I thought the architecture of the Music City Center was pretty cool-looking, with it's curvaceous outward appearance!  It's a convention complex that offers a large 1200000 square footage of meeting space and exhibit options.  You can check out their website's calendar to see what events are coming up.

+cool architecture!

Really really good service and a very attentive waiter. On the weekends (Friday and Saturday) they have a live band. When I went it was Al Green and the hard times. Lol. They were really in good though and had the whole crowd enjoying themselves.

If you don't want to be close to the music there are quieter areas or a patio outside. The place is really nice. The drinks are on the more expensive side but totally worth every penny. They don't cheat you on your alcohol and they have really taken their time to come up with a creative and satisfying drink menu. 

Food was great. They serve small plates and larger meals. I ordered a small plate of Chicken Samosas. They were a tad greasy but the flavor was on point. In will definitely be going back there my next visit.

The vibe of the Ryman, Holy Church of country music was great. The visibility however was less than optimal especially if anyone of any size sits in front of you. The beer selection was not very good but prices were typical of the stadium concession . 

I would definitely come back to the Ryman for another show, just need to choose the upper balcony first row or main floor towards the front

We bought the combo Ryman/Grand Ole Opry tour.  This Auditorium in downtown Nashville has stunning architecture and beautiful details throughout.  You can see everything at your own pace and enjoy the history.

I've held several events at Sambuca and have usually had a pretty good experience. However last week my husband I went in for dinner on evening and I was really disappointed. The restaurant was extremely slow for a weekday evening, yet our server didn't seem to be particularly interested in serving us. I ordered the filet, and it has to be the absolute smallest filet I have ever ordered. Considering the price point of the restaurant, I was extremely disappointed in the portion sizes. The filet only came with asparagus making it a lot more like a small plate than a true entree. 

Beyond the portion sizes and service, the place was a wreck. The women's bathroom was absolutely atrocious- see attached photos. When we left, the valet line was about 10-12 people long. I realize it's handled by an outside company, but it reflects badly on the establishment for such a long wait. Probably will not return for a private dinner.

Difficult review to write - really was wanted a good experience but disappointed in terms of food quality, cost and frankly service. 

I would equate the food experience equivalent to that of a mass produced event type quality.   The restaurant was filled to capacity (not a bad thing) but the food fit - was somewhat lukewarm, dried, and lacking any serious flavor.   I had the red snapper étouffée- again, fish was overcooked and a bit dry.   My wife had scallops with risotto coins - very small serving and a bit salty.   

Derive was adequate at best - appeared understaffed for the amount of people.  B coffee came after dessert - annoying.   

Drinks were adequate at best as well.  

For the cost ($150 for two - three drinks and normal dinners with dessert) just left feeling like we could have gone to a dozen other local new places and had a much better meal.   

Good place for large parties I suppose.

Very nice convention and event space.  Some of the best food I have ever had on a trade show floor but then again when I saw that Chef Elaine Taubin former of Lowe's Vanderbilt Plaza is there, it was no wonder.

Needed a perfect place for an important business/fun dinner.....could not have found a better place.....
1) our waiter "Price" was incredible.....great recommendations...sincerely wanted us to have a great time.
2) the band was amazing (thx Nashville!) but not too loud.
3) appetizers, wine list, entrees, and dessert were all awesome!
The chef is incredible......an epic evening!!!

I got here on a Sunday afternoon for some brunch with my buddy. There was live music playing, western swing country music to be specific. Very good ambience owing to the fact that the band was hitting some real nice chords. 

I got the recession sandwich. It included a fried bologna sandwich with chips and a PBR for $5. To me this is/was a steal. I get started on my beer while waiting on the food. Now the sandwich was too salty and I did not like it one bit. I don't know if this is common with frying bologna but I'm not getting it again until proved wrong. 

My friend got a turkey sandwich and he seemed quite happy with his food. A basic nod of the head is what I got when I asked him about his sandwich so I cannot really tell you much about his sandwich.

I will go back again for some beer and live music, but it's not on my goto list for sure.

WOW. This is easily the largest building I've ever been in. This place is massive! 

I attended a conference here recently and I thoroughly enjoyed my time roaming the halls of this place. Everything in this building is super clean, clearly organized and "green."

By "green," I mean that they use reclaimed rain water in all their bathrooms. At first glance though, it looks like every single toilet in the building needs to be flushed. It honestly looked like each toilet had pee in it and no other bothered to flush it. It wasn't until you go into a stall and read the sign on the back of the door that you realize it's not pee, it's reclaimed rain water. So don't worry when you go into the bathroom!

Speaking of bathrooms, every single one I went into had an attendant. There was also a huge bottle of Listerine mouth wash with tiny, disposable cups, hair spray and lotion to use. It felt like a really fancy hotel - but it was a huge convention center. 

During the opening ceremony of my conference, I couldn't go 20 feet without someone offering complimentary (came with registration) food or drinks. The food was AWESOME. They had mini brisket and pork belly tacos that were to die for. Two or three bites of food that packed a ton of flavor! And the drinks were amazing too. I couldn't turn around with being offered beer or wine. And the bartending stations (they were scattered all over the place) offered a full bar of items. The specialty drink of the night was called The Red Carpet with watermelon moonshine and some other stuff I can't recall. It was really sweet and it got me really buzzed. 

During the expo hours that food was phenomenal. I was expecting simple things - finger foods during the expo hall hours, but I got food you would normally get at a higher end restaurant. We had pecan crusted chicken, sweet potato tater tots, quinoa vegetable mix, teeny salads with fennel, argula and house-made dressing, pork tenderloin with risotto, baked potato gratin,  cake pops, house made pecan pie, teeny tiny ice cream cones with Jack Daniel Bourbon Honey Vanilla gelato and branded white chocolate bars. So much good food! I don't recall the names of everything I ate, but I everything was delicious!

Major props to all the staff at the MCC - I kept seeing staff constantly moving. Servers, chefs, attendants - everyone was great. There was always someone there to point me in the right direction, offer to show me something, grab my plate, serve me food, even talk to me in the restroom! 

If you're ever in the Nashville area, I highly recommend stopping by this place to check it out! It's right next to the Bridgestone Arena, the Omni and the Country Music Hall of Fame.

This review is for the tour only, I did not have the pleasure of seeing a show here when I visited.

As first timers to Nashville, we decided to get their city pass that allowed us to get into a bunch of attractions for a discounted price. Our first stop was the Ryman. I knew this was the Opry previous to its current location, but didn't know much else. I must say, I absolutely LOVED the self guided tour we were given. The video you see at the beginning is really like a mini theatrical production, and it was PHENOMENAL! I'm a history nerd, so I was relishing all the facts that were thrown at me. The little showcases throughout the auditorium are very well put together and gave me tons of insight into the true significance of the Ryman. My grandma, sister and I got our picture taken in the circle on stage, since my granny has always been a huge fan of the Opry and I think this was part of the Old Lady's bucket list. Overall, a great venue to tour, and hopefully one day I'll get back for a show.

I have been here a few times and every time it's been amazing! The food and service is always amazing followed by great live music. 

*Now the menus are hard to read due to the lack of lighting

Not a huge fan but I keep going back!  The food is overpriced for what you get. The ambience is upscale as is the decor but I always leave feeling like I was pick pocketed.  The guy who wrote the diatribe below is right so far as mixed drinks go; order straight liquor or a bottle of vino. 

Last nite I had the tuna tartare and a salad. Both were good. Th fam had champagne chicken which they enjoyed but were still hungry when they finished it. Again, can't really knock the place but.......

One thing for sure the hostess is a sweatheart, the service is excellent, and the valet parking a must. I'll be back. 

One thing that drives me NUTZ in Nashville. I have been to five restaurants in the past month who say their espresso machine is broken. FIX IT! When I pushed the waiter at Sambuca he said we don't carry it because no one orders it. 

Hey Nashville - Wake-up and smell the coffee!!!!

Very cool show but be sure not to talk quietly, act excited, or show any form of life because the man clientele is 75 years old or older and we got scolded for enjoying the show....just don't move or sing along or clap and you'll be fine.

Great place to watch Sunday football and hear local music at the same time! Our server, Livi, was great and attentive this past weekend. Would definitely recommend this place to anyone visiting Nashville and exploring Broadway.

I was here for a concert on ST patty's day.  What a great venue.  This is the ultimate place for a concert in Nashville.  The sound is amazing, and the building is just gorgeous.  I always love coming to the Ryman for any event.  If you've never been I highly recommend going!  You will not be disappointed.  Oh and I had the cheap seats up in the balcony and truthfully.  I think I would prefer to sit there because you have just a good a view as any where else.  And it will save you some money!

Second to the time with our Granddaughter in Nashville our experience at Sambuca was the highlight. Don't let the $$$ scare you - it's very reasonable for what you experience. We started with their meat and cheese platter and an adult beverage and shared a cup of their fabulous shrimp  and crab bisque. My husband had a filet, I had their sea scallops for dinner along with a glass of wine. Both were excellent. The live music was energizing and well done. We closed our evening with a shared dessert and a night cap. 3.5 hrs later we ended our night on the town for less than $175.00 including tip and valet cost. So worth the money for a memorable experience.  We will return the next time we are in Nashville.
Rainy Saturday afternoon, they were open! Got the "dis" from next door octopus, just rolled in here.  Amazing duck, great appetizers.  A little slow on service - but good place to chill.

You really can't give this place a bad rating.  We got into Nashville, and were starving and did not want to spend time going place to place.  One of the guys in the group had heard about the "recession special" so we went for it!  $5 for a bologna sandwich, chips, and a PRB.  And served super quick.  That is hard to beat! Other than that, similar to the other older joints on Broadway.

Happy to experience the legendary Ryman Auditorium in wonderful downtown Nashville. Located right in the middle of downtown, you can grab some drinks, dinner, or whatever before or after a show.  The auditorium itself is clean, but still had the old feel to it... you can just feel how much talent has passed through this venue. :).  There is seating on both the balcony area or in front of he stage and to be honest you can see clearly no matter where you are seated.  The seating on the balcony area is like bench style seating (no individual seats) so you have to kind of shimmy into your seats since you can really tell how many people will be in the row.  We have some fellows that we're mad we were sitting inside... they were like "how many people do you think can fit here?" lol I'm like "I don't know but we're about to find out since they sold us these tickets in the same row as you." Lol grumpy old men. Lol

All and all, we are So glad we came! If you haven't been to Nashville before, this is a must for your to do list.

The place was packed, but I listened to an AMAZING band and had a ton of fun. I liked that I could sneak my way up to a table and sit and enjoy the great live music even on a Friday night. What a fun place for some music and drinks!

Drinking in Nashville will lead you to some interesting places.  While wandering down the strip, I saw a busy-looking bar with a bouncer in front sporting a ZZ Top beard, and a drink menu promoting a recession special: PBR and a friend bologna sandwich for $5.  I was sold. We clawed our way to the back and got seats at the bar where the bartender made sure my drink was always full.  She poured with a heavy hand (which I will never complain about) and the Don Kelley Band rocked my f'n socks off, which was an impressive feat since I was in boots.

So, we took my visiting BiL downtown to play tourist.  We had some time to kill before meeting the folks we were going to dine with, so we stopped in at Legends Corner.   I guess it was too early in the day for waitresses, but our beertender did a pretty good job of tending bar as well as waiting tables.  

The beer selection wasn't very extensive, but we found something suitable to quench our thirst.  My wife was pleased with the Cosmo that she got.  And my beer was good and cold.

Megan Ellis and her band were providing the entertainment.  She's got a great voice, and we liked her a lot.  I know this city is chock full of talented people looking for that one big break.  I hope she gets hers.

Wrap me in red velvet!!! Yes the walls at Sambuca are a bright red fabric to match the Beetlejuice themed design, love love love! The welcoming laid back attitude of staff makes this a Nashville staple. Live music, check. Dancing, check. Well executed cuisine, check. Drinking, HELLO!!! The charm of a place that serves cheese sticks a la cranberry sauce, calls it something fancy and makes me love to pay for it, has my vote!
Nice atmosphere.!!Great Steak!! It is worth the buck!! Great music!! The waiter was fab!!

When an old buddy of mine let me know there was a fantastic show coming up, that just happened to be on my birthday... there was no doubt in my mind what my plans would be. Within the hour, tickets were bought, flight and hotel booked, and finally the day came when I returned to the Ryman Auditorium for the best of birthdays. 

It wasn't my first trip to the Mother Church, sure as hell won't be my last either. This has to be my favorite all time venue, EVER. There is not a bad seat in the house: I've sat right up front, all the way up in the balcony, and a few times somewhere in the middle, and have always had a great view... and the sound...the sound. Almost acoustically perfect, if not perfect, even with just one person on stage or a whole mess of folks. 

Back in another life, when I was hitting up the concert scene across the Midwest pretty heavily, I had the ultimate pleasure of getting in backstage. To see all of the signed photos on the walls, the dressing rooms, and even smoking a cigarette out back on the iconic back exit stairs to Ryman Alley.... you just feel the bigger than life energy of all the phenomenal stars that have played here.....

Some of the best times of my life here. ALWAYS an experience that will create a sweet, sweet memory.

Only there for a beer and a half on 4th of July.  Bartender wasn't too friendly, but it was find for a quick beer and a fun environment.  Also the live music was a little on the loud side for conversation.  At any rate I would return as it seems to be a Solid honky tonk and at good for some beer!!

Sambucca was great for a large meal. We had a group of 12 and they made the reservations easy. Our table was right by the stage for a great Latin rock performer. She was great! Our waiter was very nice and helpful as well. A couple of our steaks were over cooked, which can be hard in a Party but also basic at that price point. We were freezing! The AC was cranked and we asked numerous times to have it adjusted.  My uncle had napkins all over him.
So much fun!! Great music and great bartenders!! Corone served the best drink I had all weekend!! I don't mind paying for quality drinks as long as it's " quality"!! Very professional and FUN!!

Amazing venue and history here. The complete package that can only be found in a building that dates back to the 1890s... take the guided tour of the place for sure, worth the $ to know the history that the building has with the town.

Also, watch the movie, a great history in 12 minutes.

Came to see Jason Isbell. I love the idea of pew seats but sometimes I don't want to be crunched with a stranger. There just wasn't enough room for the amount people on our row. But every single employee was insanely nice. And the show was great.
Good music, cold beer, great atmosphere. Doesn't feel hokey like a lot of the other bars on Broadway.
A great day at the Ryman! A well polished tour guide, with lots of information, and lots of freedom to tour and take photos.

While waiting to enter witnessed a very aggressive foul mouthed female door employee push a woman to the ground and then claimed the customer pushed her first. Need better quality of people at your door

Would give this place 5 stars if it wasn't for the beyond loud music that makes it impossible to even think. They have both gluten free and vegan options Great waitress and good vibes. I'd suggest if you want decent prices and a place to start your night off.

We went here 8.4.18 to celebrate our friends 27 Wedding anniversary. We have never been before.
The atmosphere was charming and relaxing..The venue is wonderful. They had a live band "Grant Garland" wow!!! 
  The service was excellent!! 
We had the crab & shrimp dip and shrimp  ceviche  it was delicious and fresh! 
For dinner I had the salmon Oscar- fresh and cooked perfect
The others all had the Jumbo Chili rubbed Scallops and rice pilaf- OH EM GEE!!! They melted in your mouth and so flavorful!! 
We had the most enjoyable time and will be back for sure!! We are still talking about it 2 days later.

This is not the first time I've toured backstage at the Ryman Auditorium, but the last time, it was still THE home of the Opry.  After a Saturday night show, my buddy and I wandered backstage to look around.  He and I were both involved in college theater, and we fascinated by all the props and sandbag counterweights.  I'm sure that kind of self-guided backstage tour would get us in all kinds of trouble today, but . . .   

This week, my son was visiting, so we spent a day downtown checking out the local sights, and this time I actually bought a ticket.  When I got to the ticket booth, I asked if they had a veteran's discount.  She not only had the discount but thanked me for my service.  I really appreciated that.

The tour itself was fun.  The dressing rooms may not have been all that impressive, but our tour-guide was very knowledgeable, and she had a truckload of stories about the building and all the people who have played there.  Her stories were worth the price of admission.  However, I was a little disappointed that I didn't get to actually tour the back of the stage again.

The Ryman has always been a fantastic venue, and the acoustics just can't be beat.  I never understood why they let it sit vacant for all those years.  I am delighted that it has been refurbished and is in use again.

In the endless search for a place with a later ending happy hour, I find Sambuca!  Yes, there are actually some people who get off at 5 pm and can't make happy hours that end at 5 pm.  If you are like me, then you need a happy hour that goes beyond 5 pm.  Sambuca happy hour ends at 7 pm.  The drinks are succulent and they offer some decent happy hour bites.  My drink of choice: skinny margarita!  My favorite bar bite: the shrimp and crab dip.  Yummy plush lump pieces of seafood--I almost ordered another for our table.  We also ordered the bruschetta.  It was bit deconstructed in presentation but another decent choice.  The service was prompt and waitress was attentive.  Sambucca, you've made the list and I will be back!

Another one of those "If you are visiting town, you just go here" places.
Also crowded, expensive and loud.
Absolutely worth it!
Every time I have been, there is fab country band playing.
This last time, I learned about the rear entry that goes out to the alley and provided easier access to a couple other bar.
Absolutely worth a visit.

Tin Roof es un simpático barcito que se encuentra en el centro de Nashville, el cual es ideal para ir en pareja o amigos a tomar algo y escuchar un poco de música en vivo.

Este es el típico y clásico bar americano donde encontraran distintos tragos y cervezas industriales, ya sea en botella o tiradas. También tienen un poco de todo para pedir para comer.

La onda de este lugar es ir a escuchar música en vivo y en este espacio podrán presenciar shows de distintos artistas que generalmente tocan distintos covers de clásicos de rock. El lugar en sí es bastante amplio y pintoresco.

Let me tell you about the happy hour! Sambuca 75 and Frose are the clear winners. Cheap, strong, and tasty just how I like my drinks. I brought a friend here that was visiting and she has not stopped raving about it. Well worth a visit and they have live music. Come get some!!!

went here on a sunday night on my first trip to nashville after reading all the glowing reviews on yelp and trip advisor. despite going in with high expectations, i couldn't have been more pleasantly (i'm far from someone that knows his way around country music) surprised. i know that i'm sounding like a broken record in saying what's already been said about this place dozens of times, but it bears mentioning again, and once more for every good experience that a person has in going there.
- great honky tonk, country, rockabilly, and old school 50's and 60s' rock n' roll
- great fried bologna sandwich and decent selection of local beers at more than reasonable prices
- everyone there, including staff, had an unfazed smile the entire time

it's a quintessential nashville experience

We went to the Ryman last night to see the group "Home Free".  While the concert was great, the valet parking situation was HORRIBLE!  We are seniors not familiar with the area (we traveled from Ohio for this show).  We opted to use the "valet parking" option, offered by The Ryman (hence the 4 star rating), thinking at $20 it would be worthwhile since we had no idea where to park.  After the show we had to wait 1.5 hours (yes.....1.5 hours!!!) standing in the pouring rain and freezing cold (Nashville weather in April - who knew?) before the valet brought us our car!  What a huge mistake.  My advice to anyone who is going to The Ryman is to not use the Valet parking option.  Their entire process sucks!   They had only two runners working last night and lots of people were required to wait this ridiculous amount of time.  Several folks were in wheelchairs waiting.  It was the worst mistake we have ever made and the most miserable time we have ever spent. It completely ruined the joy of having seen the show. We were absolutely soaked and freezing by the time we got our car.  Don't repeat our mistake!

Perfect after the zoo place to unwind with live music, bar, tacos, playground, arcade and more! Everything is super affordable and the building itself is brand new, clean and has security also! We had such a good time, everything was delicious especially the tostadas and paletas!!! Can't wait to come back with friends and family.

Hey y'all, there's a reason the Ryman is called the Mother Church of Country Music. Located in the middle of downtown, it looks like a God-fearing cathedral from the outside, and it's hallowed halls definitely reflect the spiritual heft of its history. No coincidence there as the auditorium started life as the Union Gospel Tabernacle in 1892 and housed rafter-raising revivals. Its program was broadened by a woman named Lula C. Naff who booked a wide variety of performances in the theater for over half a century.

She's the central figure and narrator of the ten-minute, multi-screen video you see in a separate room at the beginning of the $21.95 self-guided tour. Obviously inspired by similar featurettes at Disneyland and other theme parks, it provided a highly engaging overview of the Ryman's history. Once you exit the room, Jamie W. and I were free to peruse the two floors of the theater which includes quite a few exhibits and a historical timeline (photo: http://bit.ly/2ltIlC6). Lots of spangly costumes and elaborate musical instruments with accompanying videos narrated by familiar country music stars.

It was like a smaller version of the Country Music Hall of Fame (photo: http://bit.ly/2K9o835). Of course we took advantage of the photo opp where we stood on stage in front of the Grand Ole Opry barnyard backdrop (photo: http://bit.ly/2lxF7xa). This was where the Opry resided until 1974 when it moved to its current cavernous home to the east of downtown. But I could well imagine seeing Hank Williams or Patsy Cline perform their familiar hits In the more intimate setting found here. We would love to come back for a real show, but the tour gave a strong sense of how potent country music can be.

This was a referral from the hotel concierge. There is a live band so if you want quiet don't come here. We say way back to reduce noise. Started with free fried pickles thanks to the concierge. Really good thick pickles. We had the hot chicken sandwich which was good. The best macaroni and cheese ever with some brisket in it. Overall awesome food

Stopped in before the Preds/Bruins game. Not very crowded. Band was good. Drink prices were on the higher side, but at least they had the beer prices on the menu (most other places didn't). Will come back next time wer're in town.

We came to Sambuca for a bachelorette party and made reservations a month ago and it was very easy. We called day of to confirm and they said they had our reservation up on their second level "rooftop", which is more of an dining area with retractable doors, but when we showed up it was gorgeous! We were seated right away with a beautiful view of the Gulch and when our waitress Ariel (I hope that's correct) she was right away amazing. She gave us honest opinions of what to get, the red snapper and the flat iron steak were both amazing, she was able to split our checks up with no issues and she just made our experience great overall. Thanks Ariel and Sambuca!!
Decent mixed drinks, good live bands, and plenty of space to move. Glad we stopped here, out of the many bars on Broadway!

i've been to several shows here, and have never  had a bad seat.  it's true, there's not a bad seat in the house (except for like 3 which are behind those columns...). 

most recently we say patty griffin, and it was just an incredible experience.

Great venue with fantastic staff!! I'm still recovering from a broken hip so I was using a wheelchair tonight. The ushers were unbelievably friendly and accommodating. 
Because of the church pew seats they wheeled me to my seat then guarded the wheelchair to insure it wouldn't roll away. We weren't sure what to expect and found the experience better than we had even hoped for. 
I'm not big on giving 5 stars but the Ryman completely deserves it!!

Sambuca is perfect for a special night out. It's a tad on the pricey side, but the food is outstanding. The decor is pretty swanky and hip so be sure to wear something stylish. Don't miss the sea-bass and soapapia cheesecake - it's seriously one of the best meals I've ever had.

This was hands down my favorite bar in Nashville. I'm honestly not a huge country fan (had I not been in town for a business trip, I doubt I ever would have made it there), and I loved that their live music included a mix of all genres. Lots of great 80's and 90's covers! The drinks were fairly inexpensive, and the atmosphere was just right. Everyone was super friendly for the most part.

I come here for lunch any chance I get because the staff is amazing and the food is fantastic! Even though you cannot go wrong with anything on the menu, I highly recommend the Sea Bass, Brussels sprouts, and best salad!

Great stop if you want a quick bite to eat on your way to a concert. 

My friends and I took the train from Mount Juliet to downtown Nashville. The stop for the train is at the end of Broadway. The tin roof Broadway restaurant/bar is a perfect stop in between the train stop and Bridgestone arena. 

The restaurant has live music, which is great for an authentic Nashville experience. It is quite noisy up in the front of the bar but there's several tables and chairs towards the back that is perfect to be able to chat with friends and still hear music. 

My two girlfriends and I Shared an order of loaded tater tot's and chicken tenders w/ fries, it was perfect for the three of us to munch on with some drinks before the show. The food did not take too long and it was a nice upbeat fun environment.

I am here now on a Wednesday evening. Been waiting an hour, and the waiter still hasn't brought anything. No soda and not a single dish yet. If I knew I'd have to wait this long, I would have gone grocery shopping myself and cooked at home.

It's been years since I have seen a gig at Nashville Municipal Auditorium. From what I hear this was the premiere spot for larger-drawing acts prior to Bridgestone but even years ago when I first came to a show here it was more for raucous acts and a more "engaged" floor audience.
I really enjoyed the show I caught here recently. So why only 2 stars? 

It's just a bit run-down and I don't see them doing anything about that. That though is manageable. What does suck are: (a) if you pay for a seat and are anywhere close to 6" tall you will be crammed in knees bumping the person in front of you; (b) check in through the line is nowhere near as efficient as at comparably sized (or larger) venus (e.g. Bridestone); and (c) concessions are ridiculously priced with little to no variety. You want a beer? Your options are Bud, Bud Light, Mich Ultra or some crappy lime-a-rita Bud, all in 25 oz cans for $11 a pop. Any other music venue in Nashville you can get a quality beer for half the price.

But...I'd come back for sure if the right act is here. There's a reason some acts are going to opt for Municipal over Bridgestone (if they're too big to play a fantastic venue like Marathon or the Exit/In)...and that's because they let folks act like they're at a concert. Plenty of security and good checks to make sure you're safe when entering but they let you mosh in the pit. It's grungier and more run-down but there aren't too many bad seats in the house (view-wise) and it suits a lot of shows.
Love the show at the Ryman. To be sitting on the church pews in the same place that Johnny Cash first met June was amazing. Great place a must check out when in Nashville.

My daughter was here for a volleyball tournament this past week in Nashville and this venue was perfect for this event. This venue is big, beautiful, and clean. Also the seating is patted chairs which were comfortable. This is the best venue I've ever been to!

Our other favorite place on Music Row!
We loved it here!
The bands were awesome, the staff was great, and while we were there the few times we went the crowd wasn't too terribly bad. 
Found out our last night there that they have the perfect little patio in the back. Great place for smokers. 
This is one of those places we'll be heading to again on our next trip to Nashville!
Easily the best bar on Broadway. Cheap beer, great music, and simple food. Getting a grilled cheese like your mom used to make for $4 a bit tipsy is amazing.

Loved this place. Cheap beers and great live music. Saw the Don Kelley band on 6/17 and couldn't leave until they were done playing. Did a slammin' version of Ramblin Man by the ABB. $2.50 Miller high lifes? Are you kidding me. The sound was mixed perfectly for the cozy environment. All good. Question-Who was playing lead guitar that night?
Eh. Music was too country and too loud. Drinks were ok. Best part about it was that there were seats and could sit down.

Fun fun fun!!! That's what I thought about Robert's Western World! So.....I had a layover in Nashville and brought my bf along. It was Christmas night and I Yelped and found Robert's! I used to avoid the Nashville layover, but now I can't wait to return because of this place. I don't know if it was poppin' because it was Christmas, but it was a blast! The drink specials were great and so was the food! Love the hotdogs!!! They had live music and people dancing and some were wearing rhinestone cowboy suits too! Too cool!  People were dancing and just having a grand ole time. I can't wait to return to Robert's Western World!
Great venue with impressive acoustics and big headliners! Great location and close to all the best restaurants Nashville has to offer!
Capped off each night of our trip to Nashville with a fried bologna sandwich. Amazing snack after a day of drinking.

In late July during a heat wave, we walked up and down Broadway and Second street twice trying to find great music that did not blow your ears off and decent air conditioning. 

Then we heard Rachel Hester at RWW and we spent the afternoon there. She and the band were both very impressive. Classic country, but not too twangy. We were able to dance on the small dance floor and that made it even more memorable. I made a few video clips and after listening to them back home, I realize that they were all extremely talented musicians. I especially liked her rendition of "No one knows my name". I had never heard that song before, but I could not get it out of my head after hearing her sing it. I think she does a better rendition than Gillian Welch.
Go on a guided tour with Bob, you will be laughing the whole time! Can't wait to see shows here, I have tickets next month.

I went to Nashville for a bachelorette party, which I'm pretty sure is 60% of the people walking through the city.  It is crazy the amount of people in this city that are celebrating bachelorette parties, and just in the restaurant alone were 3 other parties.  We took an uber to dinner, and the driver told us a little about this area of Nashville known as The Gulch.  The atmosphere as soon as you walk in is very nice and welcoming.  It has a L.A vibe to it, and I loved that about it.  It is two stories and has a great bar area as well as a smaller restaurant seating and large outdoor seating as well.  The lights are dimmed pretty low and made my 28 year old eyes feel much older than they are!  

The food was decent.  A bit overpriced for the flavor, but several people I was with loved the seafood carbonara and the salmon Oscar.  I wish I had gone that route instead.  I went with the filet which came with asparagus and a bordelaise.  I love bordelaise usually but this one just lacked the flavor it was intended to have.  They were out of asparagus so I opted for the sprouts.  I LOVE sprouts and they are very difficult to cook and getting them right is an art.  These were decent, but since getting them right is so hard, I'm usually not too picky on the sprouts.  I just expected for the price they would be perfect.  The band was amazing and I really enjoyed having some music in the background while we ate.  It was hard to hear at times, but we were seated so close to the band that is understandable.  Drinks were great and overall a decent dining experience for the city.  Great location and we really enjoyed walking through the Gulch after dinner.  Best part of the entire meal was the fried cheesecake.  That is a MUST try!
This place has amazing service, and such great live music! It is a really cool atmosphere for day drinking or night life! Would bring anyone there!

Older crowd of 40s/50s living it up at Robert's. Band playing authentic old-school honky tonk and got people dancing up front. So crowded that I couldn't even find a seat, but no wait to get in on a Friday afternoon. Appetizers, like sweet potato fries, were your typical bar food: greasy yet comforting.

I wasn't expecting that this place would be as good as it was.   Thursday afternoon and a decent country singer performing who'll probably never succeed big time but put on a good show.  Good enough that we stayed long enough to want food. I didn't expect much from the cheeseburger but was surprised as it was well prepared and pleased not only me but my wife who's really a far tougher judge.  For a street full of tourist traps this place may ruin that image.

I really liked this place. It's something new in the city of Nashville. They have something going on every night on stage such as salsa night and so on. However it still needs some improvement but overall it's a nice family hang out when an event is going on

Gotta say, we love country music, but we sure learned a lot on this tour. We both remember watching The Grand Old Opry as kids along with Hee Haw, but I didn't know Bluegrass music started here. And, I really like Bluegrass too! 

The Ryman has a wonderful history that is presented exceptionally well through a back stage tour. Our friend Anne told us it was a must and we trust her opinion. She hit a home run with this recommendation! The transition The Ryman has been through is quite a story told very well. 

I must say I had my reservations before going to The Ryman since we were scheduled for a show at The Opry and a back stage tour the following night, but Wow... it was awesome! A piece of history that everyone should experience, including those not in love with country music! 

Our tour guide, I think his name was Justin, was outstanding and provided so much insight and character into his presentation! I highly recommend him for your tour. This was my favorite part of this trip to Nashville.

I saw Alt J here in September. I was in the second row of folding chairs. Not only were the seats incredible - minus the fangirling drunk 20 year old guy in front of me - but the sound was better than most venues I've been to and that's saying a lot. The staff is nice and gets the crazy girls who run up to the stage out which is also nice because no one wants to see you twerking.

Stopped at Tin Roof last night and had a really good time. Only went for the drinks and music. Live band was really good. I made a song request and they actually sang it (unlike the previous bar I was at). Met some people there and really enjoyed the evening. They have a nice drink menu and the food smelled and looked good.
They also have happy hour until 7pm with good drink prices. If you are looking for a good time with great music you should stop by the Tin Roof.

Definitely a must-see. It's the mother church of country music for crying out loud! You can honestly feel how special this place is when you make your way into the auditorium. Being a former musician and singer (... for my high school band and chorus...), I definitely feel and understand the special place this landmark has in music, country or otherwise. It's very small, making for a more intimate environment. The "balcony" comes down pretty far, so I don't recommend sitting in the back section of the ground floor area if you actually want to see a show, but if you care more about listening to the music, I don't think it matters where you sit. Just walking around you can hear how different it sounds.

I recommend getting the Total Access pass at the visitor's center. You can visit 5 attractions for a fixed price, and you have a choice of different places (technically 4 because the Parthenon is a preset choice). This pass is $50 as of today, and a great deal if you use it correctly, especially if you want to see a lot of major attractions.
Good band, nice bartenders, good service on a thursday. Try the ring of fire as a shot. Yum.

Honky-Tonks, Live Music, Boot Stomping and Yee-Hawing are the crux of Nashville's historic downtown center. Broadway Street is like the Times Square or Fisherman's Wharf of Nashville; so yes, it is the 'tourist' area; but one needn't say it like that's a bad thing. As a visitor, you have to visit the tourist areas to get a feel for what I think of as the 'origin' story of a city. In San Francisco, it's the wharf; filled with ports and history, fresh seafood right off the boat and sourdough bread. In Nashville, it's Broadway; filled with honky-tonks, live country music all the time, history and legends. Our second stop in Nashville, was Robert's Western World, a fantastic honky-tonk with walls covered in memorabilia, cheap drinks and my first basket of fried pickles!

The Don Kelley Band was our 'band du jour' and they were amazing. They have been playing Roberts since the nineties. With an authentic country sound and unabashed honky-tonk vibe, they will make you want to get up and dance--or at least stand up and holler. Either way, they are a party waiting to happen.

If Shaun White and Stevie Ray Vaughn had a love child, Daniel Donato would be his name. Like a thunderclap from a clear blue sky, this 19 year old guitar player will bowl you over.

For a complete review with tons of photos, visit my site at: www.TNBTA.com

Cheers!
Not too exciting but great if you are looking to rest your feet, this is the place. It has a Dunkin Donuts inside and was perfect for us to grab a cup of coffee and wait for the rain to let up.

Great restaurant great music
Service average 
Food less then average 
Appetizers Cold we ask the server to make sure the entries would be served hot.
They were also cold,
Had to send things back and half of the food never came back.
Don't think I would go back

Best place in Nashville to listen to live music. The history, the acoustics, and the atmosphere was amazing. We saw Mary Chapin Carpenter, she was as excited to play as we were to see and listen. Will be back. Thank you For a Great Show!
If you want Mexican ambiance come here . I love here . Makes feel like I'm at my family Mexican parties

Great bar in the middle of Broadway.  It filled my impression of a Nashville bar.  Great music, packed to the back and awesome friendly feel!  Some may call it a dive bar. But it was the night I wanted for a Nashville trip

The mother church of country music does not disappoint.  Every seat in there allows for the perfect musical adventure.  It is a cozy venue as well and you are immersed in the history of the place .  It is an amazing place to catch a show and you need to do so if you have yet to have the opportunity.
What an amazing experience! It was like stepping back in time - to a better time! Love this place!
Best Honky tonk in Nashville! We had a blast dancing with all the single old men. It was a little crowded,but a fun joint to take out of town folks!

I had my first experience at the Ryman last night to see the X Ambassadors. First of all, WOW, the X Ambassadors were amazingly good. Second This is my new favorite venue! It was very intimate but still exciting. I love that the pews give you space and no one judges you if you sit down. ALSO since the seats are at an angle, you can sit and enjoy the show with a view. I also want to note the range of ages, you had the 19 year old hipsters allllll the way to the 60 year old man on the balcony jammin! Also thank you Clark for forgetting your sisters birthday and giving me the tickets because you couldn't go!!
Acceptable bar food at a reasonable price. Not much choice...basically burgers and fries. Music was good given it was lunch time.

Went there this past Saturday and was very disappointed. First off my friend and I waited hours for this place to open since it opened at 5. Once we got in, we sat in the bar area which was nice. After ordering our first round of tasteless watered down drinks and an appetizer that came with frozen shrimp and dollar store saltines as opposed to cocktail crackers or at least Ritz, we soon determined that we would not take the chance of ordering an entree. The band was mediocre at best. In fact if the band wasn't actually sitting there I would assume that it was just cheesy elevator music. Do yourself a favor and find somewhere else to spend your time and money...totally over-rated

Great bar, artichoke appetizers was awesome, meal went down from there, Spring chicken was very dry, Red Snapper was also over cook but cold, strange
Would not return except for drinks outside

I did the self guided tour because it was close to closing and it was anticlimactic.  They charge for pictures on stage in addition to the tour cost.  

I'm sure if I had made it there early enough to do a guided tour it would have been better.  The place is beautiful in it's historic way.  I have a friend who is a songwriter and had a song played on the show Nashville in the Ryman so it was nice to view the auditorium from that prespective.  I'd go back again with others, but probably not on my own.
decideyournight.com kept recommending me to go to Robert's Western World and I'm glad I did. The fried pickles ARE TO DIE FOR!

Sambucca is a solid place for a night out. On my last visit there was live music. 

I ordered the pasta and my companion a steak. Both were tasty.

I had the sticky toffee pudding for dessert...it was a solid decision.

Pros: pretty decent cover band played some classic country tunes. Lots of old timey country music decor. Much fun for a tourist like me.

Cons: too many buffalo bills fans. Also, whiskey on the rocks was a ridiculous $9

If you are visiting Nashville make sure you stop in for a burger and listen to some great country music. The night we were there the band was great. They had a 17 year old guitar player that was amazing. Food is cheap and the place is just plain ol' fun.
I had an amazing time here!  I enjoyed a fried bologna sandwich, sweet potato fries some kind of local beer and listened to a great band.  For a first time visitor it was a perfect experience.
Really quirky place,  even for a place on Broadway. This has an older country feel and was my favourite spot in Nashville. The food was okay and drinks were cheap.

Overall terrible experience. To think we had a group of 20 to 30 people at a private event and the management lady was just unprofessional and completely rude. Not to mention had terrible communication skills. Complete waste of money and time. Stay away.

We had a great time here. The music was fantastic! Hope was our bartender and she took very good care of us while we were there. No cover charge to get in, just don't forget to tip the musicians and bartenders. This place is honky tonk legit, I would recommend going here before one of the touristy bars on Broadway.
Lots of fun! We had quick service and the music was great.

Save your money. Not worth it. And if you have a party greater than 10, they will have a set menu for you and have you all pay a high amount. There are so many better places in Nashville to try for a better price. The lasagna was dry and cold. Please guys...save your money. Side note, the music is way too loud.

DISCLAIMER: My review is based on my OWN personal experience and opinions ~~it has NO bias intent towards the company/business, the owners/managers or their employees. Please let YOUR OWN experience and views be your guide for enjoyment !!!!

Just got back from the Chris Daughtry Concert on Nov 16th, with my daughter Noel celebrating her 19th birthday. We had such a great time. The opening act was Bobby Church Band and then Daughtry put on a 2 hr show with encores..it was amazing..Rushing out tomorrow to buy his new CD/Album  "Baptized"...if you don't have it yet....GO BUY IT !!! Amazing entertainer...the best concert I have been to in years..
The food was GOOD, the beer was COLD and the music was GREAT!  It is a honky-tonk and it is FUN!   Nothing fancy...  but a GREAT honky-tonk dive bar.  Stop in and enjoy life!
Not a bad place seats are just uncomfortable and narrow. Definitely a every now and then event place.

Hot mess! This is a great alternative to the honky tonks up and down Broadway. If you're looking for a place with live music that plays a little bit of everything, this is your place. There's plenty of room to dance and the bar is pretty accessible.

There's also an upstairs area where you can enjoy drinks and food without all the chaos that is taking place downstairs. From here there's a great view of Broadway. 

Back in the day, their location on Demunbreun was my favorite spot for live music. It's nice to see they can bring the same good times to other locations.

I was excited to attend a work function here because I'm familiar with the Tin Roof in Franklin and LOVE their food. Huge fan of their quesadillas. The name is where the similarity stops! The quesadillas barely had anything in them and when I mentioned it (half was biting into plain tortillas, only the center had the yummy goodness) they mentioned that everything was measured and that was standard Portion size. Umm....ok? Not anything I would ever want to order again. I understand now that they are all individually owned and managed, have their own menu but Taco Bell charges les a than half the price and will fill my belly better. Music was so loud I couldn't hear anyone in my party talking and we were sitting upstairs. Seeing how I work in the downtown district, and constantly have out of towners asking for recommendations, the nonchalant attitude didn't win me over at all. 
Unless I'm going to listen to friend play, I don't see me making a special trip to go again.

Authentic honky tonk surrounded by tourist traps, apparently one of the few places on the strip still frequented by locals.  Fare is simple but good and more than reasonably priced.  Service is friendly if not always fast. Good for a late night but and some music.

The Tenn Lizzy was amazing, if you're into cocktails! The person I was with had tacos, and he said they were great too. It was crazy busy, and even with a band at the front and one at the back, we still had pretty quick service. The prices were absolutely reasonable, and the decor kept me captivated throughout.

This place is awesome for big groups. It is off of the main drag so we were able to get a reservation last minute for 15 people. The food was very good and the setting was awesome. We sat outside and we loved it!

What a great spot!  I am not a Nashville native, nor would I consider myself an authority on country music, but I definitely know what a good time is!  I went to Roberts in the middle of the day on a Monday, which I highly recommend.  The bar was busy, but not overly so.

I went up to the bar and ordered a PBR and a fried baloney sandwich, which happened to turn out to be one of their regular specials (The Recession Special, $5).  Not the best fried baloney sandwhich I've ever had, but it was good, and came with a beer, and for $5 plus live music, so I certainly am not complaining.  Bartender was also waiting tables and they probably could have used one more staff member, but she was doing a fairly decent job of keeping everything moving along.

I also really enjoyed the music.  I was able to hear 2 different musicians before I had to leave for the airport, and they were both very good.  I liked that the music was more old country style than the other honky honks I went to where the music covered a wider variety, including very recent songs.  Overall a great spot, and I will definitely be visiting again next time I'm in Nashville.

Pretty mediocre live music on a Saturday eve...almost 30-40 minutes without any music when bands switched...cocktails were decent but nachos not upto the mark..either too soggy or completely bereft of any topping...so what could make this experience  worse? As we munch on the badly done nachos in a no-music background at around 11pm, the staff comes and makes everybody at the bar stand up since it's  supposedly  their time to pack up the bar stools..so highly unprofessional!
Fantastic food, service, and atmosphere. Great live music too! I will definitely be making a trip back next time I am in town!

Now this was one  the one stop in Nashville where I found the outlaw country that we were looking to find. On top of that, their cheeseburger was killer. Anyway, best bands that I saw the weekend I was there were at Roberts. Felt old school in a town where I wrongly expected to find a whole lot more old school. Loved Roberts. Solid.
Live band.  Great bartenders.  Can't ask for much more in a bar.

This place was packed! Typical bar scene. Drinks were cold and refreshing after walking around Nashville on a 95 degree day. Band was good and up beat. Would probably stop by again. 4 stars since we didn't try the food.
This is my favorite restaurant in Nashville for a classy night out. If you're in the mood for wine, good food and a soft jazz band, Sambucca is perfect.

Went to see JOE & Fantasia for Valentines weekend.....

I absolutely hate this venue! It serves its purpose for hosting large sold out events but staff wise and seating are a hit or miss everytime. Price wise, well it just depends on who is going to be there and what day the concert falls on. Ours was on a Friday. Once we got inside  we headed to the concession stand to grab a hot dog and nachos. The girl behind the counter made our food with NO GLOVES on! which we were not having! So it took about 20mins to get our food. Seating is pretty much whoever gets there first if your not sitting in the floor section. Any higher seats are first come first serve.

The staff knew nothing about helping you find your. Plenty of security there so no drama. 

Will i return..?? probably not, i just think there are better venues for artist to show at.

I'm really surprised there aren't more reviews for this place. Maybe it's new?

While walking through the crowds on Broadway, we were drawn in here because of their unique band/stage set-up. There were windows people could climb in to and be behind the band... some of the singers obliged people with selfies, etc. That looked fun enough, so we went on in.

The fun continued with pretty great bar service downstairs, and shots served in paper cups labeled "Medicine Cup" and with dosing lines. This was especially awesome because we were in town for a health related conference. The fireball shots and mixed drinks helped us have a reallll good time.

The band was awesome and played a mix of country and classic rock songs, and the place was crowded pretty early, which seemed like a good sign. Restrooms upstairs were large, clean, and simple. 

If I ever make it back to Nashville in my life, I'd be sure to hit this place up again.
Really like this place, great music, pretty good food, friendly waitstaff... out of all the options on Broadway the Tin Roof is a great place to stop

This review is on the Ryman as a historical landmark to tour during the day.  We were only in town for a few days, and wanted to take in a show at the famed venue, but the only act that was performing while we were there was standing room only, and my bad back keeps me from being able to stand straight up for more that half an hour at a clip, so we took a pass, and came back the next day just to look around. Even if you aren't a huge fan of country music -- like me -- you have to have a healthy respect for the building's history and historical significance to American music in general.  It's part venue, part museum (gift shop included), and you're permitted to either look around on your own, and read the plaques in the cases, or take a guided tour, where the docent gives you some anecdotes about the Grand Ol' Opry, and the decades of entertainers that have graced it's stage.  Absolutely worth a stop, even if only for an hour.

Great venue for music. The people who go this bar are really friendly. I also get a hot girl's number when I come here so it could be my place. It is one of my favorite bars on Broadway other than Tootsie's and Robert's Western World. I would recommend you to visit if you come to Nashville, the entire street of Broadway just walk it and find the bar or music venue you like I would recommend checking this place out it always has good live music.

What is awful about this rating is the food was excellent. But we came with a large group and they were not ready for us. The bartender took over 30 minutes to bring our drinks. From the time we finished our dessert until we got our checks it was at least 30 minutes. Our ready to party crown is looking to go to bed because they waiting and the mellow music was putting us to sleep. No bueno Sambucca and I blame the manager for not stepping in.
Awesome place! My wife & I are visiting from out of state & two different friends recommend this place. The bartender Carolyn was very attentive & had a great attitude. Highly recommend!
Came here for a conference event.  The live music was great, service was awesome and the hot chicken and jalapeño mac 'n cheese were really good!

Not much to say here that others haven't said, other than, it is definitely a tourist trap, but the tourists are those in their mid-50's who want to be in their mid-20's, and think they still look like they are in their mid-20's. I went in, since our taxi driver said it was somewhere "everyone goes". he must get a lot of soccer moms and grandmas who want a good time while they visit Nashville, because this place was a hot mess!

Albums cover the walls and the bar doesn't serve any good beer. There is a mini stage in the corner where a live band plays. The band was decent, but that's about it.

I stopped here on the first night of my stay in Nashville. It was such a cool experience! A true honky tonk dive bar filled with people dancing, talking, live bluegrass music, funky wait staff and life.

There is never a cover charge but the band does come around with a bucket collecting tips. 

I ordered the garden burger and the fried pickles. The fried pickles were out of this world! The garden burger was stinky but i mean who orders a garden burger at a bar anyway?? In retrospect I would have gotten the fried bologna sandwich (as part of the $5 "recession special"). (See update below!!!)

Def check this place out! So much fun!

Update: I went back here and this time I got the fried bologna (the $5 Recession Special) and all I can say is WOW. Tasted like a grilled cheese but instead of cheese was cooked bologna. So so good. Highly recommend!

We went to about five honky tonks on Broadway on our trip to Nashville.  It's kind of something that I think you need to do when you visit Nashville. I had read somewhere that this was the best and most authentic of them all. And it was one of the best. The band was good and interacted with the patrons well. I liked all the boots on the wall. It was a nice touch.

This was my favorite honky tonk bar... On a Saturday night, Legends was filled with young and cute country boys in dirty jeans, cheap drinks and great live music. On a Tuesday night, it was filled with elderly couples dancing and romancing to country music... with cheap drinks. It was a great time, and I'll definitely be back when I'm in Nashville.

Great, fun time! We went on a Thursday night and there was plenty of space. Service was very friendly and fast and the BBQ brisket nachos were a hit with everyone at the table. Amazing band and fun atmosphere! Would definitely return and will recommend to anyone that also comes from out of town!
Awesome. Beautiful space, lots of food and drink options. Excellent place to watch World Cup.

Awesome venue to see musical history! We saw Ryan Bingham in concert and enjoyed the experience of Nashville history. We thought the view was good in orchestra under the balcony. Not the most comfortable seats but you pay for the history and acoustics were pretty good.
Great atmosphere! Love sitting in the patio when it's warm or enjoying the live music inside. The pizza is delicious and happy hour frosé is a fun summer drink.

Our food was excellent.  There were four of us and we ordered the Sea Bass, Fillet, Scallops and the special was Trout topped with crab.  This is a supper club.  The band playing was really good.  The best part of the night was our server Scott.  He knew the menu extremely well and was very helpful and enthusiastic with choosing our dinner.  He knows his food and beer. We were visiting from out of town and he gave us lots of ideas on what to do and he went out of his way to write down a list of recommendations based on our conversation.  All in all a great night!

This is a great bar to hang out for good country music, some drink and a simple meal.  They don't offer draft beer but have fine bottled beer.  The Recession Special which includes a small sandwich, a bag of chips and a RBL for $5 is a good deal.  The inside is cool and dark.  The vibe is nice.  The bands performed there were the best we had on Broadway.  Some customers went on the stage to sing and boy, they were good!  We recommend this place to spend an afternoon and/or night.

This was my favorite bar in Nashville. The music is the best. It's real honky tonk, old school style country music. Many places claim to be a honky tonk but they only have terrible cover bands playing pop music and modern country music. Places like that are a dime a dozen in Nashville but, Roberts is the true gem of downtown Nashville. Awesome and attentive staff that chatted us up during our visit and some damn fine sandwiches on the menu. Can't beat the $2.50 Miller High Life either. Make sure you go early and check out the house band. They really get everyone dancing and singing. 

Bottom line, I spent a week in Nashville and should have just went here every night. You should do the same. Do not go to the other over crowded bars just go to Roberts!

I made reservations for this Sambuca outing in honor of my friend's bachelorette party. This restaurant has special meaning to her because she went on several dates with her fiancé there while they were dating. We had a really special night. Some rad blonde girl was belting out some killer tunes with her band that were totally mood appropriate. We had calamari and the shrimp crab dip for appetizers and both were pretty good. The bride got the salmon dish and she LOVED it. The other dish that seemed to be a hit at the table was the filet with the Gorgonzola walnut butter. YUM. I (and one other pal) got the ribeye and it was unremarkable. The other guest got the lobster enchilladas and she wasn't all that keen on them. So to sum up, we had: excellent appetizers, a few solid entrees, good cocktails (apparently there is a berry dragon cocktail that everyone loved), and killer tunes. The ambiance rocks. Worth the trip for sure.

My husband and I just happened upon this place over Labor Day weekend while visiting Nashville. We were so pleasantly surprised - finally a place with elbow room, a delicious looking menu and music that wasn't making us deaf. As you can tell we were over the bar scene but still wanted to take in some music. The Chris Weaver Band was playing the night we stopped in and they were a delight. Think Joe Cocker voice but definitely interacted with the crowd and got people up dancing. While there we both ordered steaks. I had the filet and my husband had the ribeye, both were some of the best steaks we've ever had. Delicious and cooked to perfection. We also enjoyed a couple of glasses of Cabernet Sauvignon. That too was excellent. I highly recommend this place and would go back in a heartbeat, if I'm ever back in Nashville.
Loved our server. Cumcumber pineapple drink was delicious. My entree was the scallops with risotto -- So perfect. Scallops were cooked perfectly and paired great with the risotto and asparagus.
We left this evening before ordering. We refuse to dine in a restaurant next to a group loudly using foul language.

A fun honky-tonk with cool decor. The drinks are cheaper next door at Robert's however. But if you don't mind paying a little more and listening to covers of less traditional country, it's a good time.
An Absolutely great place to visit.  The tour was really very informative and filled with an energetic video before you walked through the auditorium.  Really a great place to visit.
Great music. Packed venue! In agreement with everyone else = the fried bologna sandwich with a beer and some iced apple moonshine = fantastic. Had a blast!!!
