Disappointing. I was looking forward to the Miso Sake Sea Bass but the fish had no hint of miso or sake in/on it. Served dry with no sauce, the jasmine rice was also dry, flavorless and cold. A beautiful restaurant with nice ambiance, but the food is lacking flavor. So for the price I definitely would not come back.

FYI buy a beer do not buy a mix drink.  They Do not now how to pour a mix drink.  Do yourself a favor and go down to the whiskey bent saloon for a real drink.  $7 for a coke with no alcohol.  I wonder why no one was drunk when I was there at midnight.

we were wrongly kicked out of this bar. We were a party of 13+ 50 year old people and their children having a great last day on vacation and our experience here with a bouncer was unreasonable and rude. Will never come back, nor would we recommend this bar to anyone who is visiting or living here.

For me, while the food was fine and the wait staff attentive, the atmosphere was just weird.  Dimly lit with blood red accents and one of the worst bands I've ever heard.  In 'Music City' of all places, you don't expect (or I don't expect) to hear the 'easy listening' top forty sounds of the '70's delivered in the most bland way possible. Think Seals and Crofts, Bee Gees and ELP played by a band in a nursing home.

My favorite sandwich of 2017 is the grilled cheese sandwich. It wasn't made with beurre noisette or raclette cheese and it didn't contain lobster or truffle oil or pancetta. It is, however, perfection.  My best-loved sandwich contents are simple: white bread, butter, American cheese. It's grilled on a flattop, cut in half on the diagonal, served in a basket with a bag of plain Lay potato chips.  However, because I always seem to eat it between 11pm and 1am, standing up, shoulder-to-shoulder with a hundred others, I have to assume ambience is as important an ingredient as any. 
As the undisputed home of traditional country music, Roberts, with it's live music, cheap beer and inexpensive food is all you need when you want to run away for a weekend.  The people-watching is the best in the country and I always have a story to tell the next day. But it's the grilled cheese sandwich I crave always.  While most eyes are on the band, I love watching the fry cook balance the grill.  Between fried bologna sandwiches and burgers and fries and fried pickles he handles it all with a trucker cap and a bored-as-f expression. His grilled cheese is nothing short than luscious.  It's soulful and gooey and crispy and hot and there is an obvious seasoning in that grill that flavors it so it's unlike any other. 

There's no doubt that atmosphere is a huge influencer in my choice. However, if the end result is a memory that all of your senses recall as pure perfection, it shouldn't matter.
My second favorite sandwich of 2017?  The fried bologna sandwich from Roberts Western World...

Not my best experience. The band seemed in the bottle for a Monday night and my wife and I got sick from there French Onion Soup Special. Sorry but thumbs down all around on this one!  Should have known better.

Tito's Playland is hands down the best thing here as my 5 year old was kept busy for more then an hour (5 hours in equivalent adult time). 3 story indoor climbing structure is free!!  All the games work and it is clean and noisy as an arcade should be. 

The rest of the plaza is just ok. Nice musicians in the food court. Some empty storefronts but very limited shopping options would only be 2 stars if not for Tito's being amazing.

A fun bar with great talented musicians. I was pleased to pick up the menu and see they had a veggie burger. I ordered it and it was good for bar food. My only problem with this place is that the bar was packed, and the grill is maned by 1 person, and getting your food takes forever. They definitely need a bigger grill and more staff to get these order rolling. By forever I mean at least 45min to get my order. 

Fun spot to drink and listen to great tunes and eat if you have a lot of time.
First home of the Opry and amazing history!  The video at the start of the tour was very entertaining and informative!  Awesome spot!!
Live music all the time! The bartenders are super sweet and the burgers smell amazing!

I visited the Ryman on a venue tour because there were no performances that we wanted to see while we were in town for the weekend. And while the tour was interesting, this really is a place that you need to experience, not just go look at. Therefore, I'm going to make an effort to see a show at the Ryman the next time I visit Nashville. Its acoustics is suppose to be superb making it one of the best places in the world to see a show. 

The museum tour starts with a video with the history of the Ryman and how evolved from a gospel tabernacle to the Mother Church of Country Music. The rest is a self guided tour of the auditorium, where there are selected artifacts from its history. It's fascinating and this place is full of history and stories. Definitely worth a visit, especially if you can't get in for a performance. 

Really looking forward to seeing a performance at the Ryman the next time I visit Nashville. Review will be updated, and I'm confident I'll be changing my rating to 5 stars!

This was our first trip to Nashville TN and it definitely won't be our last. We had a great time Roberts Western World is the best place to go. We went there everyday of our trip. The music is great and we had 2 exceptional servers Karen and Masha we're awesome. They were very attentive and personable and went above and beyond to make sure our 1st time experience was exceptional. The food was great!! Highly recommend the Fried Bologna Sandwich and the burgers!!

Went in on a Friday night and the band was bloody brilliant! The double bass player (which in my opinion is a dying art in this electronic world) was amazing. Unfortunately, I didn't catch the name of the band, but they played proper old school country honky tonk...which was just what this uncountry, english girl was looking for while in Nashville!

Not only that, the $6 burgers were fantastic. One of the best burgers I've had in years. Beers are $4, and there is no cover charge. However, be prepared to fork out a few dollars every hour when the band comes begging. I quickly learned that if the bar didn't charge a cover you're going to pay about $5 per hour per table of 4 people (less if you don't love the band, but you still have to remember that these talented musicians don't get paid a penny to work in these bars because the competition is so stiff). The band on Friday night (later on) recommended a tip of $10 to $20  per hour, but I think that was wishful thinking!

We went back on Sunday night, which was much quieter and the band was good, but not as good as the Friday night band, but the burgers and service were just as good. This was our favourite bar on Broadway without a doubt.
live music at lunch time, Chicken tenders are amazing... Best lunch downtown

The food looked better than it taste!! If you are not a fan of dill be careful ordering the dishes with dill, it can be over powering. The drinks and Appetizer's were very good! Our server Jordan was excellent and he did everything within his ability to assure that we enjoyed ourselves. 
My future visits will consist of Appetizer's and Alcohol. Can't go wrong with this combination.

Every time I come to Nashville I have a great time at The Second Fiddle. This trip proved no differently. I was in town with my husband in mid September. Brandi Thorton was awesome on Thursday night, her voice is unbelievable. The bartender had a really big fantastic smile & she was very nice to us. We've been coming in for years & we were pleasantly surprised to see Megan when we went back on Friday. All the staff is friendly & kinda silly (one guy behind the bar was hilarious) and seem to get along well (cutting up, working hard, laughing and smiling all night) which makes it an even better place to be. Seems more like a family working together. This is not a Honky Tonk anybody should be skipping past when visiting Nashville.

This is the tour to go on while in Nashville.   It is a beautiful former church turned concert hall.  A film starts the tour to tell the history.   And what a rich history it had.  Walking through the building feels thick of spirits of the fine country musicians in time gone by.

There is an opportunity to get on the stage for a photo.  I didn't look to see how much that cost but many in my group did it.  The gift shop is very nice and full of treasures. 

The Ryman is still used for concerts and events.  It seems like a very nice venue for music.  If you are in Nashville check it out.

The apps were delicious! Buca Beignet, Shrimp and Crab Dip and Chicken Samosas were our favs. Our server was so sweet and nice! She gave us suggestions and informed us what other places to check out....

We sat close to the stage, Live music while we ate was a plus although my partner didn't care for it bc you really could not have a conversation bc it was loud.

I don't love the new construction (just doesn't fit with the aesthetics of the previous design), but this is my favorite place for a concert. With the exception of the last 6 or so rows on the main floor, there's not a bad seat in the house.

My family and I went on a Friday afternoon.  It was not busy at all.  My card was overcharged by the bartender when adding the tip.  It could have been an honest mistake or it could have been skimming.  I had to call the establishment.  They apologized, but should have offered compensation for the error in my opinion.  The overcharge was not excessive, but it's the principal of the matter.
quick service. friendly staff. great music. one of our favorite venues during our time in nashville.
Good ole music and good cold beers. Cheapest beer on the Broadway strip. Come and cool off and sit for a spell ya hear...
Great drinks with the best server named Evan. Happy hour more than worth it here. Great  music by the Jacob Reynolds band.

We went to Sambuca to celebrate our daughter's 16th birthday.  The food was all very good.  The place is expensive but we knew that going in.  All of the entrees were great:  Shrimp and Crab Scampi, Filet and Lobster tail, Salmon Oscar, Blackened Flatiron, and regular Filet.  The only thing we found underwhelming was the side of Dill Havarti Potato Tots. The ONLY warning: be aware of the live music, and ask to be seated away from the stage if you want to me able to chat.  But if it's just my hubby and me, we will probably want to sit there and enjoy the live music.

The Ryman is a great place to go see a show. My brother and I had tickets to see Lewis Black here (he was hilarious) and since moving to Nashville, it was my first time here. Everyone told me about the nostalgia and how it's a pretty historic place so I was pumped to check it out. They have a few historic pieces throughout the venue which are really interesting and give you a pretty good idea about the history of the place.

Since it used to be a church, it offers pew style seating. This is good because it gives you a pretty good view, regardless of where you're sitting in the auditorium. However, they are pretty uncomfortable, especially because that day I happened to be having some back issues. And the fact that there's no dividers means that you hope you're sitting next to some skinny people, otherwise not everyone is going to fit. Luckily we didn't have that problem.

This is a historic part of Nashville that anyone should come see if visiting the area. Be prepared to pay for parking at one of the nearby garages. The night we went (since it was a special event) I think we paid $15. But, it's in close proximity to Broadway so it's close to everything else you could do downtown. Definitely a place you have to see!
We loved the folky live music here. There were locals that were doing some awesome dancing. Favorite bar of the evening.

In my opinion the obstructed view could really be a lot worse. I mean it's something I will avoid in the future, but if I found really great ticket prices for a show I really wanted to see I would definitely not have issues purchasing them because of this fact. The Ryman's amazing acoustics more then make up for the lack of being able to see who is playing fully. The place  is unique and definitely a must for any person who appreciates sound. Plus it's old school, no usher was under the age of 60. 

My only qualms are with the weirdness of live music crowds in Nashville. I still cannot get over it.

This is the best venue for amazing music...if you're in the right seat. There are a lot of limited view seats in this place, which makes it a bummer if you don't get your tickets quickly enough for the hottest concerts. But you really can't go wrong with the sound in this place. The acoustics in here are phenomenal.
I've seen people bring their own seat cushions because the pews can be hard after a couple hours. But all the more excuse to stand up and DANCE!!
Had an awesome time at Robert's the band blew me away. Service is good everyone is super friendly
I'm sure this is a great place to see a show, but the hour tour for 25 bucks is a rip off.

If you are looking to experience everything that is Nashville, you have to stop here. This is the root of what all the rest of the bars wish to imitate. 

My fiancé and I went on an overnight trip to Nashville(spur of the moment). He had been to Nashville once, while I never had the pleasure of going. I love country music and was enthralled with the idea of going to the heart of it all. We got to Nashville and started hopping bar to bar at 3pm on a Sunday. Robert's Western World was the fourth bar we walked into and it was as if we stepped back into the time when country music was in it's prime. The Tennessee Walkers were performing and the smell of the fried bologna sandwiches hit you in the face when you stepped in. That smell was so enticing, but we had just ate so we just settled for one of the cheapest beers in town, a PBR. When I say it's the cheapest, it truly is and we couldn't find another place that came close to a $2.50 can of beer. We drank our beer and enjoyed the music for a bit and then continued on our way to the next bar on Broadway. It was after many bars later that we returned to Robert's Western World because no other bar had the atmosphere that they did. We surely worked up an appetite and we had to order the "Recession Special"- fried bologna sandwich, bag of chips, and a PBR for $5 I believe.  It took me back to my childhood. The service was quick with the "Recession Special".  I loved everything about this place and the sandwich topped it off.

We ended our night just they way any night in Nashville should probably end, dancing to some classic country in the front of Robert's.

After walking around Broadway for about a good hour to find a place to eat, we landed here. They had good live music and the servers were cool. 
My friend and I ordered the Mac and cheese, hot tater tots, and chicken and jack quesadillas. My favorite of all the 3 was the Mac and cheese (soooo good). We also had A shot called "F-n-8", not that good, it was too sweet. The bathrooms needed a touch up. I'd go back to have the Mac and cheese again !

Another must stop when in Nashville... If you want to stay away from the tourist trap aspect wait until later in the night to go... Start on Lower Broadway and work your way up.   The history and great live music is worth the stop.  Plus, you never know who will pop up and jump up on stage.

Food was good, but nothing over the top. Favorite order was onion rings & mozzarella sticks. However, the atmosphere was excellent!! Definitely a great time to enjoy a local dive. The staff made you dee right at home, and the music was fantastic. Traveling through Nashville, this was a perfect stop.

The food was so delicious and our sever Matt was beyond attentive. Matt answered any questions with the smile gave us great suggestions and made our dinner that much more memorable. The restaurants ambience was romantic with a jazz band that was playing in the background. The food was cooked to perfection! We didn't have one bad experience with Sambuca's from start to finish, it really was special. Next time we are in Nashville at the Gulch we will definitely be going back!
I just love this place. Never a bad experience. Sat on the patio and enjoyed terrific music, service, food and cocktails. Can't beat that.
The best honky tonk on lower Broadway.  The food is great and the music is always top notch. Unfortunately, it has become very crowded.

Tyler and Clayton are amazing bartenders. Come see them!!!
Amazing drinks, food and live music

Great service. Try the goat cheese stuffed artichokes! Amazing. We caught a great blues band, and got sat right away at 7pm in Saturday night. (Although to be fair.. The entire city of Nashville is out waiting for fireworks in the rain)
Great venue for music. Lot's of history. A must when you are in Nashville!

This review is for restaurant. Had Calamari Fritti and Cheesecake Sopapilla while listening to live band. Food was okay nothing special and fancyish atmosphere. What was not okay was seeing the way staff handled other customers who were not happy with the service they received. Instead of addressing this away from dining area, the staff continued this feedback session with the customers to the point where the customers were loudly cursing. Intimate atmosphere ruined. Gets worse. I guess there was some mix up with receipts among waiting staff. Guess where they have their arguments? Right in front of customers. Get your act together!

While deciding what to eat ( my wife has cranky spells when she gets hungry) we popped into Roberts, ( heard they have fried bologna sandwiches) and who doesn't love that. While we agreed we would split one to "tide her over", she ate it all but one bite! It is def a cozy place, but then again most of the bars are on broadway........ but hey, that's what we are here for !!!! 
Cheap beer, and the bologna sammich was ALL OF THAT!! - def worth popping in on as you try to figure out what your gonna do next ..... only to look up and realize you spent the whole night there! Caelin was the best .... she kept us in drinks we never got parched!

Best place around! Where else can you buy boots in the afternoon, listen to great music and then nosh on a fried bologna sandwich (a must - soooo yummy). Their country music is more traditional and wonderful, so much talent on the stage. I also want to give a BIG shout out to Hope who served me yesterday. I forgot my purse, called them later and they put it in a safe place. Thanks Hope!

Don't forget to tip the band!

I don't think there is a better place on Music Row and certainly one of my favs in the US. If you have a bar/music bucket list, make sure you put Robert's on it.

It's kinda one of those places you go in Nashville because it's so iconic.  It's in the hub of all things touristy on Broadway, but this place itself is as authentic as it gets.  Great live music.  I would definitely recommend it as a must-stop if you're doing the Broadway Street Circuit.  This and Acme Feed & Seed may be the only two places I recommend on Broadway
I have always had a great time here - the choices of love music are great -- and they have one of the better wine lists around. There is room to dance a bit and the outside seating is really great.

Seen the Gatlin Brothers and toured the behind the scene dressing rooms where johnny Cash and Minnie Pearl would hang before the show. The original 1892 and great restoration plus don't forget the movie they show it was fun.

Arguably one of the best places on Broadway! Upstairs is semi-open so you can smoke. Plus no matter which bar you went to, you got quick service. Nothing beats that. The staff there is great and be music was even better. A great mix of country and classic rock. Cannot recommend this place any better.
What an amazing piece of Americana history. This is a must see, even if you aren't a country music fan. The amazing names to have graced this stage is bigger than a phone book. Really a gem.
Great atmosphere and beer. It was also nice to find a place playing something other than country on Broadway. I know I know it's Broadway,  but I still love it

Color me impressed with Robert's Western World!  I came in here with a friend as we were both eating dinner next door at the BBQ joint, and could hear what was going on inside of Robert's and we wanted to be part of it.

Being a fan of music, mainly ROCK music, I was hesitant to walk into a place that had the words "Western World" in its name, because I'm not a huge fan of country music and I think of Western country music as being the twangy music that I just can't stand.  However, my perception was dead WRONG.

When I walked in, there was some young kid, maybe about 20yrs old or so, wailing, and I mean absolutely wailing on his electric guitar that was behind his head.  I was like 'what the...??"  This kid was a wizard on that guitar and what I was hearing wasn't twangy at all...the kid was shredding it.  Come to find out the house band is legendary and the band leader is known to mentor up and coming guitarists and plays with them live in this bar.

We didn't order food here as we had just eaten, but those fried bologna sandwiches looked fantastic.  Also, were I'm from, you put down a $20 on the bar for a couple of beers and any change you get goes to the bartender.  Not here.  I ordered two beers and got $15 in change...WHAT? 

Then I thought the fun was over.  The band announced they were going to play a George Jones song....I was like, "ok, here comes that TWANG that I can't stand!!!!!!!"  I was wrong...that band made that song their own, updated it, and it was awesome.  The musicians were fantastic...then they put their take on a Merle Haggard tune....and it was AWESOME.  

What a wonderful experience here...the decor is fantastic, and this place qualifies as a DIVE...but one you never ever want to leave!!!  

Highly recommended.  Don't forget to tip the band!!  (and the staff!)

Your average bar with live music.  I chose this place since it had 4 star reviews.  IMHO it did not live up to the reviews.  We ordered BBQ sandwich and quesadilla.  The BBQ was cold and the quesadilla was average.  We went in the mid afternoon so perhaps they were not staffed to meet expectations.  The service was average with only one server.  The music was live.  Don't think I'll return here unless I just want to drink beer.  Suggest you skip the food.

Still wondering how this place got so many high ratings.
We just left...band was playing Purple Rain and other Prince tribute songs....there was also a Black Lives Matter documentary playing on the TV's. Not the Nashville I know...not going back!

The atmosphere was quite amazing for live country music bands and an energetic audience. We loved the finger foods as that was what we mostly ate. Our server was a hot little college chick who forgot about my wife's quesadillas, but altogether we still had a great experience. The kiddos were dancing to the music and cheers of "whoo hoo" came from our group. Three stars for the food as it was average. Also, the bar ran out of draft beers, so that sucked because I didn't get my Goode Island drink, lol! Overall, a memorable event with some family

My parents and grandparents used to go to shows here, and my spouse and myself have been attending for around 15 years.  This used to be hands down the best place to see live music in the state; but thanks to its proximity to the bars on lower Broadway and the recent push to attract tourist dollars, it's now more a place to hear the drunks behind, around and in front of you whoop and holler instead of letting you see or hear the show.  People drink all day on Broadway and then show up here for the concert, where they buy more beer and mixed drinks to keep their good time rolling.  The venue is now way more about booze and drinking than actual music.

It's really too bad.  People used to be respectful and you felt you were getting your money's worth (tickets here are NOT cheap).  But now you'll be treated to the people nearby screaming, "singing" along, and having loud conversations about whatever they had for dinner or what they plan to do after the show.  Heaven help you if you actually ask them to talk a little more quietly, keep hands/feet in their own space, or whatever - "they can do whatever they want," "this isn't a library" (actual quote) and the kindly older folks who serve as ushers here have no real power.  There are usually one or two security guards, but they won't do anything about the obnoxious behavior of others unless one of the drunks actually takes a swing at somebody.

The worst thing, though, is when you spend $$$$ on seating near the stage only to have security let the people who've bought cheap tickets at the back of the floor flood down and stand in front of you.  This may be why many folks prefer the balcony.

No way I'd even consider going here on a  Saturday night anymore, under any circumstances.  It's heartbreaking to see this place turned into just another tourist commodity, but so goes a lot of Nashville these days.

A venue of American musical history in a City that is defined by music. A must see in a must see City. Located right around the corner from the strip of Honky Tonks. Tours are available. The Ryman is Americana.
We stopped by to sit at the bar and didn't get any acknowledgement from 4 men behind the bar. After 15 minutes of waiting, we just left. Very disappointed! Definitely won't be going back.

Friendly bouncer at the door, nice staff, beautiful honky tonk/blues country music by the house band, unique wall décor made up of legendary records, and an older more chill, quiet crowd during the day and a younger livelier crowd at night. It's a small space, so you'll have to work to find seats!

I've been on a mission to catch as many great shows as I can this year (2017) and though I've caught some great ones all over Nashville from large venues (Bridgestone) to tiny (The End), I've somehow missed the Ryman completely. I've seen shows at the Ryman in the past but not since moving to the area a few years back. Partly that's been avoidance because I hate the parking situation at the Ryman, part of that is the artists I've been wanting to see simply haven't played the venue. However, a favorite artist of mine was set to perform here and I bought my tickets as soon as I could and the performance reminded me of how great this venue can be.

Pros: (1) Historically significant spot that every Nashville visitor (or resident) should visit at least once--do the tour for the history, see a show for the experience; (2) Acoustics are phenomenal--the sound here is just perfect--no distortion, no fuzz, just clear bright sound that sounds great at a sound level that is totally audible at every note but that isn't so loud you need earplugs; (3) for the most part, not a bad seat in the house--if you're not directly behind a post you can see the stage from everywhere you may sit. Toward the end of the show I recently saw  we were near the back of the bottom level but with the way the room is angled we had a clear view the entire time. Toward the end of the show many of us began walking down the aisle to catch the encore from the front which showed just how great the view is from the center front but those tickets are typically noticeably higher; and now (4) valet parking that is only $20 (free if you drive a Nissan due to their sponsor). That sealed the deal but though drop-off was seamless and painless, pick up of the automobile after the show took a bit long.

Cons: (1) Pick up time for valet as mentioned could use some work, there is some confusion as to what the official process for pick up procedure is as well since what we were told at drop off was not what we were actually supposed to do; (2) concessions as they are at any of the "name" brand venues of the city are a bit ridiculous ($12 for a beer, $8 for a soda); (3) seats are a bit hard after awhile as these are old school church pews without a cushion; (4) this venue while perfect for some styles of music isn't suited for everything--if it's an active show with dancing, moshing, movement at all this doesn't work

So check it out, it's worth a visit!

Another superior spot on Broadway, Legends Corner is a little louder but a little deeper. I loved that we found a table on the "mezzanine" where we could see over the folks on the ground level but the music was still clear.

I'm not quite sure why the band had to cut out at exactly 10:15, but okay.

Best traditional country honky tonk on Broadway. Hands down.

With a house band and upright bass player, the play all the best of traditional country music at its best. Merle Haggard, Buck Owens, George Straight would be proud.

An old boot store converted to a honky tonk, but the boots are still on the wall. 

Enough room for dancers. 

You shouldn't leave Nashville before you visit this place. It's Epic.
This place is amazing! There is such a great variety of shops here! I found chicha morada, which made me very happy. I can't wait to come back on the weekends for live music.

Stepped in here before going to see a show at the Station Inn which is across the street because they only serve beer over there and I'm more of a hard liquor kind of girl...
Very nice live band playing but didn't catch the name. Female lead singer and female backup were both great. Again with the cover songs tho...

Shimmied up to the bar. Ambiance is chic and dark... The crowd was a little off-putting, maybe a tad too snotty for my mingling taste. Angie the bartender was great tho and did me a huge favor by making me a slammin' espresso martini. I was on the road all day and badly needed caffeine to perk up. Espresso martinis, when done properly are probably one of my favorite things in life. I don't usually order them tho because being a bartender myself I know what a bitch they are to make. She glady obliged my request and it was delish!
My bf got a fancy $12 beer and then had major martini envy when he saw/tried mine. Place wasn't cheap but I guess that is to be expected in this part of town. Only had one round and left but it was a good one!

I cannot be judgemential with only one visit but we were there at saturday night so; 
Good music venue. Definitely not a food place. Hot dog was ok, but burger was horrible. Friendly staff is a huge plus.

First, let me start of by saying the architecture is phenomenal. An absolute beauty. The convention center has great seating if you need to rest between meetings, sessions, etc. The layout was confusing. Ballroom was on the main floor. The meeting rooms were limited and strewn out. If you are a handicapped or someone that has difficulty getting around it will be difficult. 

I have been to many convention center such as ones in Boston and Chicago and they offered a variety of food services and places to dine. This convention center lacks those amenities. The line for Dunkin' Donuts and the tiny restaurant, both in the convention center, where a mile long. I normally would not say anything about the food services, but they were lacking considering the number of people the convention center can hold. Also, due to the enormous amount of hotels surrounding the convention center, there was not much choices for food. So, pack your lunch. Once you pay the $15.00 charge for an event parking fee, you cannot exit the garage and come back in. You must repay, so no going out to eat. I would suggest the MCC Parking give out tickets of different colors for each day, that way it would allow you to come and go as you please.

Overall, the experience was a great one. Fantastic new facility. Other than that, nothing sets it apart from any other facility in a larger city, except for the culture.

Went to the Ryman last night to see Sam's Place, hosted by Stephen Curtis Chapman..... One of the best events we have attended.!  We felt like we were joining in a small gathering of some of Steven Curtis's close friends, singing their favorites and enjoying just being together!   Such a special place and a wonderful series....can't wait for the next one. We bought the whole series and gladly would have paid twice the price for this event!

I honestly don't remember going to this place till i saw my check-in on Yelp. Yeah yeah I was a little drunk in Nashville- what can I say? Anyways, after my hangover cured, my memory started to come back. 

This bar was a blast! I don't remember the band that played, but they were awesome and got the crowed involved. I came here on a Monday night. It wasn't too busy, but had enough people inside  to have a good time! Plus they didn't charge a cover. I would definitely recommend stopping here in order to have a good time, but avoid a lot of the tourists. This place seemed a little more "local". 

They do have a "bar food" menu which we ordered pizza from. It was pretty good and helped me escape a little bit from my drunken haze ;-)  

Yeehaw
Walked up and down Broadway and chose the best sounding band. The female vocalist on 9/8/17 blew us away! The food didn't.

Sunday 5/14/2017 Had an amazing dinner out on the patio on a perfect early evening to eat outdoors, which happened to be Mother's Day! From start to finish, it was a lovely experience. Our hostess sat us promptly when we arrived at our reserved time. Our server took our drink and appetizer order, then came back to take our dinner order. All four of us had a glass of wine and the table shared two appetizers. Dinner arrived in a timely manner and was delicious! A nice variety is on the menu for both beverages and food.  No dessert for us this time, we were stuffed. Nicely sized entree portions for your money. Service was very good and the manager came over to our table to introduce himself and make sure our experience was on par. It was!  Live music was happening inside, but since it was so nice outside, we opted for the patio this time around. We will definitely come back. With so, so many in town vying for our food/entertainment dollar, everyone has to keep their game up and stay on their toes. So far, Sambuca is doing just that!

This was a pretty cool first time to Nashville spot to visit! True honky tonk and lots of character. I had the $5 recession special which was a pbr, bologna sandwich and a bag of chips. The sandwich was actually pretty good. It was 3 thin slices of bologna on a buttered toast with lettuce and tomato and a mayo packet. Definitely worth my stop in. I would suggest you sit upstairs in the back of your in a group so you can hear each other talk. Band was loud but not to loud. Enjoyable.

This place is amazing and as all the businesses open it's just going to get even better! Awesome child fruit cups, live Latin music, restaurants, and fresh hot tortillas. I'm so excited to see such an awesome development in the area!

We visited today and chose a guided tour at $30 each verses $20 for a self guided tour (includes the self guided tour and a movie explaining the history of the Ryman). We are glad we did. The tour was interesting and informative. We would have been disappointed to pay $20 each just to see the movie and walk around the seating area. 

Our experience was very good, but this is not a cheap visit. It cost $14 for two hours of parking and $60 to tour. 

We look at us as a one time thing, although seeing a live show there would be awesome, and a charitable contribution to keep this place going for generations to come.

Robert's was recommended to us by a local as the best honky tonk on Broadway and they were right! We got prime seats upstairs and had the best bartender, Hope, she was awesome and both bands that we listened to were great! This should definitely be a stop for anyone visiting from out of town!

Robert's is a fun Broadway stop for Nashville visitors. It's more accessible for all ages(meaning not a ton of young wild kids), and great for enjoying live music. Drinks are also really affordable. Most hover around $5-9 which is great for this busy street. It does get packed so you may want to try and beat the crowds before 10 to get a seat or be comfortable.

DON'T GO TO THE RYMAN!!

I went to a see Tedeschi Trucks Band Concert there (or so I'd hoped.)  

When I entered the venue, my ticket was denied and I was told to go to the box office. 

The box office staff were rude, arrogant, disrespectful and completely unconcerned that I'd paid $120 for a ticket that they'd already sold to someone else.  They told me that I was "out of luck" because someone else was already sitting in my seat.  No help to find me another seat, and when I expressed frustration, they called security.  30 seconds later, a Metro police office and 3 beard security guards surrounded me.  All the sudden, I'm a criminal.

The Officer lost his temper, put his hands on me, and escorted me off the property. He actually threatened to arrest me. 

Until they find box office staff and security who respect human beings, DON'T GO THE RYMAN!!  Oh, and STOP DOUBLE SELLING TICKETS!

This is our "go to" place on lower broad to bring people visiting Nashville. The music is always good and so are the burgers. It gets very crowded but if you're  lucky you can grab a bar stool or a table.

We had the guided tour which last around an hour, we went backstage and our guide was informativ, after the guided tour, you do self guided one because not all the stuff is covered in the guided one. The only thing that made the visit unpleasant, is the girl that was taking the photo( that was 7/8), we approached her to take a photo for us, she didn't talk or greet us, so we had to ask her to take a photo for us, she said ok without a single smile, it felt awkward like we came on wrong time. no smile, no talking.
Anyway, you can get a parking close to the auditorium on the weekend for $10.

The Ryman was the greatest music venue I've ever been to. The intimate setting and the church style set up makes for such a unique concert experience! I caught a Leon bridges show, and even from the back of the room I had great view of the show and the acoustics were great. The story behind this place takes it to the next level. Even if you only have a day in Nashville you have to stop by here.

A very nice, all around experience for the entire family.  A great food market with fresh seafood, meats and a bunch of other goodies.  It also has various shops, a nice restaurant and a killer food court area featuring vendors offering an interesting variety of other foods.  The venue is spotless, the live entertainment is incredible, the food we tried at various vendors was excellent.  There is also good security throughout the plaza.  I am especially addicted to the ceviche at El Ceviche Loco.  It is soooooo good.  It's an overall fun and delicious experience.  Check it out.

we went here for happy hour drinks and they were incredible! the atmosphere was really nice and this would be a great place to go for drinks and music, unfortunately none was playing at 2pm on a Thursday (obviously). the only reason I'm giving this 4 stars is one of the girls received her drink with green leaves in it and the waitress sat it down and said to disregard them that they were from another drink the bartender made.. they should have never served that but remade it. with that said I would still go back and try their food with hopes they take more pride in making sure its served without other ingredients.

A gem for tourists, this place has cheap fried food, fireball on tap, accepts credit cards, and awesome live music. However, my first trip was also my last since it definitely reads tourist by way of the customers, crowds, and location. Broadway is a must see, so don't let this review deter you from going in just keep in mind that you might have to wait for a seat  to sit next to what appear to be frat guys from out of town. But hey, the bartenders are lightning quick and the live music is likely better than anything you'll find in your hometown.

Behold! The future of eating is here and it is GLORIOUS!!!!!!! The place is huge and the dining options are extravagant. Also the entertainment is something akin to a Disney experience. My family and I ordered a meal of shish kebabs and steak fries then we were beset by music on the stage and fire dancers performed for us. All for free. THIS IS HOW U EAT!!!!!!

Easily my favorite bar in Nashville for the following reasons:

1) The live music was amazing every time we went

2) It's the only bar in Nashville that sells beer for less than $5

Great place for your first Honky Tonk experience.

A pretty typical conference center. 

I wasn't crazy about the main ballroom being on the top floor, but ended up working out. Everything was clean and organized though cell service on Sprint could get spotty. There was free WiFi provided by the conference. 

The location is great- close to Broadway and all the hotels and I'd pick Music City over Opryland any day.

First time at this great honky tonk. Had 3 kids with us and got a seat upstairs no problem. Food service was slow but staff was very friendly. They lost our food order initially but ended up giving us another order on the house. Great music and atmosphere!
Definitely a must on broadway, they always have good bands and great bar tenders.

This is a great place for trainings and huge gatherings. I am here all week for training and conferences for a huge company. I am excited! Here is so much room. You would never know from the outside. 

Everything is super clean and bright. Who knew they could cool down such a huge building. They keep it nice and cool inside. There are plenty of stands for snacks and drinks. The bathrooms are not as big as I would have expected. The lines are long.
I love Robert's!  Karen is by far the best bartender I've encountered in all my years of coming to Nashville! Great bar, great music and excellent service!

Nothing bad to say about this place. Fried bologna was so good I wanted to have 15 of them but I held on because my wife would have killed me, or the bologna. Yeeehawwwww. Great live music, great drinks and with great prices.  Would recommend this place to anyone looking for a good time in Nashvile.

Very cool to walk in the steps of the greats. We did the self guided tour. Ask for AAA discount and save about $5. The video part during the beginning of the tour was awesome. Very entertaining. The tour was a little rocky. They just basically let you lose in the auditorium to roam freely. Was kinda lost and didn't know where to go when let lose. Pretty cool experience.

Good place for dinner while enjoying live music... (Jazz swing on my visit) More upscale and has really good food.
Very comfortable seating in dinning area and great bar area that is still in viewing and listening distance from the band. Outside seating also available.
Fun with great music and a good greasy burger and fried pickles and delicious sweet potato fries!
Our favorite joint on Broadway!  Cheap beers!  Great food!  Also one of the few places downtown that still plays all the traditional music!

Used to LOVE going to Ryman to see all these brilliant musicians.  These times they are a changin'.  We saw the Tedeschi Trucks band last week at Ryman.  The band was FANTASTIC!  What an incredible group of musicians!  Love them!  Cannot say the same for the venue. We sat in the front pew so had a great view of the band... if the people wandering around in front of us would have sat down or gone back to their seats.  They were all drunk, screaming, and jumping up and down.   No reason to pay for premium seats because you can't see the musicians anyway and have to put up with screaming drunks.  And they just kept going back for more beer.  Ryman was once a church and a venue where the audiences were polite, responsive and enjoyed the evenings.  Not so anymore, it appears.  On the way up the aisle as we left, a drunken male almost ran into me.  I guess the bar in the Ryman could monitor their sales a little better.  And remember, this was a church.  It is a true institution that deserves more respect from the staff, security, and those responsible for serving alcohol.  But loved the Tedeschi Trucks Band!

There is a Tin Roof in Memphis so I had to see what this one was all about. Well... I really enjoyed the food here. I ordered street tacos and corn on the cob. The street tacos were pretty good, but the corn was out of this world!! It was sweet and salty. It had cheddar cheese and some other type of sauce on it. I never had anything like it. The bartenders were nice and the door attendant was kind enough to get my friend a seat to sit at the bar. It was crowded because of the Superbowl viewing. There is a second level for seating as well. I enjoyed my time here.

Cool corner bar on Nashville's Honky Tonk strip- crowd gets more lively later in the evenings.
Next touristy gift shop.

If you're looking for the authentic Honky Tonk experience in Nashville, Robert's Western World should be one of your first stops. Like a great jazz club in New Orleans, Robert's is the perfect spot to hear country and bluegrass music on Broadway. The house band that was playing when we dropped by was as good as any I've heard, and had the audience locked in throughout the entire show. 

The long, rutted bar that runs along one side of the narrow space beckons visitors to pull up a stool, order a whiskey or a beer, and soak up the music and the atmosphere. The beer selection was nothing to write home about (they at least have Lagunitas), but that's not really the draw here. Nashville's wide-ranging music scene offers dozens of great choices, but Robert's Western World is one of the truly unique places that makes this town the center of the country music universe.

Husband and I wandered over here on a Friday afternoon in June. We'd already eaten lunch, so we walked up and down Broadway, past all the bars, before we picked one that was playing the best music. To us, that was Tin Roof. It didn't hurt that a friend had also recommended this place!
They had reasonably priced beers, but the best part was definitely the live music! When we were there, that was a band playing all different type of country music covers, from those popular in the 60s and 70s to more current pop-style country. They harmonized well and also did a good job of keeping the crowd interested & participating. They genuinely wanted people to make requests. 
I know a lot of this review is of the band, which changes, but I also noticed that Tin Roof had great acoustics! Likely, any decent band will sound as good as they can in there!
We had a lot of fun spending a few hours here! They had a decent selection of beers - local and otherwise - on tap. We tried a couple local beers from Little Harpeth - Yum! I preferred the Chicken Scratch, my husband the Iris IPL. We had one of each, so it was perfect.
Next time I visit Nashville, this place is at the Top of my list!!

Blew into Nashville for a little country music and stepped off B'way for a Mushroom & Swiss Burger @ Robert's Western World based on several Yelp reviews that talked mostly about the music. 

You gotta love the live country music here in the Mecca of country jams. Great country-blue grass here at Robert's today. Dark, cool air conditioned atmosphere was a nice backdrop for my burger & IPA...and tasty fries...very nice. 

Definitely lived up to Yelp's 4.5 rating.

This was my first time at the Music City Center. I'd previously been to the Nashville Convention Center a few years ago for the Nashville Auto Show and I have to say this place is a needed upgrade. We stopped in on a Saturday afternoon for the Antiques and Garden Show of Nashville (we scored a couple free tickets from Yelp). We parked over on Lea Avenue, a few blocks away, free parking, woohoo. We'd at at Bakersfield then made it over to the center. 

We entered down at the 5th Avenue south and Demonbreun entrance. I figured that the antique and garden show as going to be so big it wouldn't be a too hard to find, however, I think I miss judged how large this place was. This place actually takes up 3 blocks. They've got 2 streets that run underneath the building, pretty neat. We randomly entered down a hallway that had a few rooms with a multi-level marketing company. We realized we weren't in the right place and asked one of the information desks where we needed to go. We needed to walk pretty much to the other side of the building, to level 3. The stairs leading up to the 3rd level have small, little terraces. The were locked that day we were there, maybe because it was only 20 degrees outside. 

We made it up to the show, the room was pretty large, it wasn't the biggest in the place, but I did peek though some open doors on the way to the show and some of the rooms are HUGE. I really like how they have so much natural light. The windows on this place are vast and the ceilings are so tall. The design of this place is very futuristic on the outside, with some of that filtering though inside. This place is a a true asset to Nashville, no matter how much they had to spend on the place. It's sad that the bees on top of the building died over the winter.

Giving 1 star because my wife's purse was stolen right from our table.
We stood up to dance a song RIGHT NEXT TO THE TABLE and her purse was gone.

Staff was sympathetic, said it "never" happens, but it does.
Stay on guard.
This is one of the spots I hit when I have out of town visitors. It gives a good taste of the town in a venue with good music and good service.

I love the Ryman!! I've been here probably 25 times, for both tours and shows. Every time it is more expensive. I took a six year old to tour it last week, it cost us $50 to do the backstage tour, with a coupon! I've done the backstage tour before and it included going on the stage. This time we got to see three dressing rooms, listen to a man speak about the photos on the walls and give some history on the place. There was also no photos allowed backstage. Why? Don't want people to know that it's a ripoff?  It was not worth it!!! What happened to the big backstage tour?  Also, I wasn't allowed to take the child's photo on stage, but I could buy theirs for an additional $20. Total rip-off, but I expect nothing else from Ryman Hospitalities/Gaylord. If their name is on it, then know they're going to over charge and nickel and dime you for everything. 
I won't be back, which is sad to say bc I love the Opry, it's history and country music history. 
Ryman Hospitalities needs to stop exploiting the Opry and actually honor it, make it affordable instead of a ripoff, we're the ones keeping you in business, remember?   
* Side note, isn't it ironic that all of the reviews that basically say the same thing I'm saying are "not recommended"?

I can't believe I've never written a review for the Mother Church. This is one of the best venues ever, seriously EVER. The nostalgia of the place itself is enough to keep me coming back. Seating is church pew rows and it's not the most comfortable but it is well worth it. I've seen countless artists here, from country to indie artists and the Opry during the winter months as well! The interior is beautiful and there are no bad seats in the place. Lines for concessions usually go pretty quickly and they offer a good variety of beer and liquor. They also offer tours during the day if I'm not mistaken. Staff is very friendly and helpful with finding seats and accommodating guests. I will definitely continue to come here for shows and I'm excited to see the expansion they have begun working on!
Good place for lunch & live music. Rodeo burger was great! Deep fried pickles were awesome. Plus, the one of the best Bloody Marys I've had in a long time.

Such a wonderful, classic bar on the strip. Everytime I went past Legends while I was in town last weekend, it was was either full to the brim or had a line out the bar. Great classic country music with a fun, welcoming atmosphere. Good drinks, friendly bartenders and a friendly, engaged crowd. This is one of the most important spots to check out on your next trip to Nashville.

Disappointing to say the least. I came with a large group and we had a limited menu due to the number of people. We waited over an hour for somebody to take our order. Our food arrived over another hour later. Servers ignored us and nobody acknowledged what was happening. When we reached a breaking point and complained, the staff mocked us and were not told to stop. The food probably would have been very good if it were not cold after sitting out. I would not recommend this restaurant due to lousy customer service.
Music is the best.  Service is the worst.  Have been a patron for over 10 years and just can't take it anymore...will not go back.  Rude...

Came here 2 nights in a row while I was in Nashville.  Came here first on Christmas Eve during the day.  It was pretty empty as expected, but still had a decent amount of people there.  That didn't stop Buck McCoy (the performer at the time) from being so much fun and incredible!! We had a blast.  Then the next day (Christmas Day) while walking up and down Broadway trying to find a bar that was open, we saw that Legends was only one of 2 bars that was open.  To our delight, Buck McCoy was there AGAIN and this time the crowd was double the size.  We were still able to get a seat and a drink no problem.  Definitely a fun environment there.
This is an amazing venue. I've been to a couple of shows and also did the tour. Yes the acoustics are great. Choose your seats carefully so as not to be behind a pillar.
The best honky-tonk for more traditional country (not new country) music. The drink prices are better than the neighboring honky-tonks, too. And the service is always great.

Went here on a Saturday night with a friend and my boyfriend. All of us have out of state IDs. The bouncer gave all of us a hard time, but especially my boyfriend, who has a Florida ID. The skinny, scruffy bouncer then proceeded to break my boyfriends ID without looking him in the eye or admitting he had made a mistake. This is a ruinous and disrespectful way to treat first time customers. We would've forgiven this transgression for good music and a good atmosphere, but we were instead greeted with a terrible cover band and worse patrons. Would not return.

History is there, music is good. Beers are expensive, as is typical of a tourist trap. However, the shortest, bearded doorman has Napoleon complex. Tread lightly on Titans game day when around as a fan of opposing team. 

Update. This guy is still not nice.

Disappointing experience. Previously visited the Tin Roof by Vanderbilt, which lead us to visit this location - however, much different experience. Took 45 minutes for nachos and a quesadilla. The nachos were cold. Waitress never checked on us - so we had to get our napkins and silverware. Huge disappointment. 

The bathroom doors, while having a lock, don't lock. And the music is so loud you can't talk to anyone.
Great food good service always live music a must go excellent atmosphere always lively

How could you not give this place 5 stars! Heart of Nashville, great place lots of amazing talent and fun. I travel to Nashville on business often and always pop into here, Honky Tonk Central and of course Tooties. 

Definitely stop in if you are doing the Broadway crawl!!
Awesome experience!  Masha is the best waitress ever!  Of course it is just a fried bologna sandwich, but tell me where you've ever had a better one!

My friends and I enjoyed our dinner here almost 3wks ago. Although, the live music was a bit loud, but they sounded great. The steaks were cooked per individual temp request, accompanied with a side of our choosing. We also ordered appetizers which we devoured! The cocktails were on the strong side but tasty according to the ladies ;) our waitress and her assistants did an okay job serving us. As a note, it is not as dressy as they claim it to be, most customers were dressed casually. However, you won't be out of place if you decide to dress semi-formal. One more thing, it is very dark in the restaurant, tables were only lit with 2 small candles, therefore, making it hard to read the menu.  They brought a special dessert on the house to celebrate our friend, which was a very nice touch!

Great new spot, they have it figured out!   Live music, kid friendly, porch upstairs, and games on the TV's!   Something for everyone in the family......I live downtown and it's great to have a spot to take the whole gang!!

Beer- Ice Cold
Food- Simple and Good
Entertainment-  Icing on the cake

Had a great time. The music was the best in downtown area. Food was great and really reasonably priced, even if you have to order at the bar(they'll l bring it to your table). Drink prices are fair  and people are friendly. Get a spot upstairs for a secluded spot to watch the show.

This is a 'must visit' during a trip to Nashville! It's a classic bar with a good beer selection and an intimate music atmosphere. I'd recommend going during the day so you can get a table up front close to the live music.
Very cool, vintage place to see a concert! Loved all of the old concert ticket posters that were hanging. Bathrooms were clean and staff was friendly ( both a plus for me!) I will definitely go back
We didn't attend a convention here, but we walked through the building.  It's a nice convention hall.  Right next to Country Music Hall of Fame and Bridgestone Arena.

The bartenders may be fast, but they also like to pull a fast one on you. I paid for two mixed drinks ($7.25 each, not terrible considering the place) with a $20, and the Britney Spears wannabe took my cash and pocketed the change. I stood there a minute, expecting her to get in the change drawer as quickly as she greeted me and made my drinks, but no. She disappeared, evidently under the impression she deserved a $5.50 tip. She tried to do the same thing to another girl in our party with a $7 order. No, you don't get a $13 tip, sugar. Maybe this is standard operating procedure nowadays, but it's not cool and would keep me from tipping at all on subsequent drinks. 

The live music was decent and the crowd wasn't obnoxious. Go in there with ones and quarters and you should be all set.

If you visit Nashville, you have to visit the Ryman Auditorium. Yes it is old and yes it is a bit pricey, but hey it's a part of Nashville history! There isn't a bad seat in the house and it is kidn of neat being part of a live radio show. We might have lucked out with some great performers, but I could see this place being a great time any night. It's a bit refreshing/odd to only have each performer play 2 songs, but at the same time, you get a good variety. I enjoyed both the imported and regular talent (btw how are the square dancers still chunky after all those moves). Overall, a great experience!
Enjoyed this bar alot. Had a great time with my wife there. Great live music and a great spot to end my date night. Lots of dancing space and not as crowded as some of the other bars.

This place is gigantic, it is beautiful, and I like its modern design. I still don't think it was a good use of taxpayer money though. I hardly saw the old convention center used, so we'll see how this goes. Hopefully it gets put to good use. I was here for the Nashville Comic Con that came in. Maybe more fun things will come to town because of the center is here.

Pretty cool place! Stopped here for lunch during our trip to Nashville...nice atmosphere and a little less hectic than other honky tonks/bars. Overall, decent food...but great live music! Waiters/waitresses were also very nice and helpful. Would go here again!

Went to this place for a birthday. I will say it has great atmosphere and that night they had a really great live cover band playing.
This place is great for accommodating groups. We got the top floor and the decor and atmosphere is nice. Felt like I was in a private LA style bar.
They do valet so keep your receipt when getting your car.
If you want to take a date, a intimate setting with that special someone, this is the place to take them. 
Do not come here looking for a big meal. You are paying for more experience than a full stomach. Though I will say the food I did order was tasty and full of flavor. I did enjoy the Shrimp & Crab Bisque. I also ordered the Chicken & Shrimp Tostadas. Paid 9.50 for 3 small chips. You are going to pay more for much less on a plate.

I would say this is a great place to get drinks, have fun with friends, listen to live music and just enjoy the Gulch area. If you are tight on budget, prob find a place to eat first than come here for drinks. But they have a full menu and great choice and if money isn't an issue than this is a one stop shop!!

This is a perfect place to experience Nashville dive bar.  This is among the many bars on Broadway.  It's close to the Ryman.  All the bars have live music.  No matter which one you pick.  So now you have to pick one you want to chill out in.  This is the place.  During the day you can have kids there.  Now it's a bar. So don't think it has a kids menu.  Basic bar food.  But they have one special that is what I had to get.  It's a fried bologna sandwich and PBR for $6! It was the coolest thing.  They have cheap beer.  Basic beers for $2.50.  They have the air conditioner on high in there and since it was the summer it was welcomed.  Nashville has weird weather.  It was a hot day and sitting inside and watching some players on stage was well worth it. 

I'm sure at night it's a happening place.  So maybe I'll go at night.  But it's well worth it to stop in and have beer.

two and a half stars is what I'd really like to give because this place in a certain way is a 5, but in another way it's a 1.  or maybe I'm just a jackass.

I'd been here for a few private parties, which were fun, but then again I usually have fun when snacks come floating along and my drink is refreshed by a smiling face every so often.
This is a great place to have a private party.  It looks and feels like something between a restaurant and a club.  Sort of like on a cruise ship, but right here in the gulch

My friend invited me to see his wife sing here.  They're cool so I went.  There was singing.  The waitress smiled.  It seemed like a nice place.  I, being a jackass, ordered a French 75.  I thought that this nice, upscale-seeming, place would whip me up one of these delicious classic cocktails and the Katy Perry covers would wash over me like icy seawater from a penguin.

After about 20 minutes I was worried.  When something showed up in a martini glass I knew I had made a mistake.  Sambuca, I'd like to say I'm sorry I misjudged you.  But also, I feel misled.

In this day of craft beverages and pretentiously knowledgeable bartenders I thought I was ordering something of the relative obscurity of an Old Fashioned.  Again, I'm sorry.  It's never happened to me before that I couldn't drink my drink.  It might just be my age.  
Did I mention that I was really tired?

The nice and smiling waitress asked me how it was.  I didn't want to tell her, but I was making a face while trying to think of some gentle but true words and she didn't need me to say anything.  "Just a glass of bubbles please," I asked the second time she offered to replace my drink.

After another 20 minutes peppered with spontaneous group dancing from each of the seven bachelorette parties around the room I was planning my escape.  I had been working all day, surely my friends would understand.  But then suddenly the article of slender glassware I had been waiting for arrived, appearing just in front of me the way I had imagined it two hours before when I was leaving work.

A champagne flute can really change things.  The Proseco tasted like an old raisin, but I didn't care.  I had to reach into the glass to pull out a half inch of spaghetti that had dried to the inside of the glass, but I laughed when I showed my friend.  It was then he told me just to order straight liquor.  I'll remember that.

Maybe this was all just a case of mistaken identity.  Maybe we just don't quite understand each other.  I appreciate the space and accommodation, but as I sat there averting my eyes from the lithe bodies bumping in to things as they sang along to Christina Aguilera I had this feeling that it wouldn't work out between us.
Really, it's not you.  It's me. 

Good luck in the future, I'm sure you'll do fine.

This is another must do!!! $20 seems a bit much for a self-guided tour, but it is definitely worth it to keep this huge piece of country music history around. They offer AAA discount which was 10% off. We went on a Sunday morning and it wasn't crowded at all.

Reviewers are right!  Definitely worth a trip to Roberts--good music, cold beer and you can't beat the recession special!!  Fried bologna, chips and a PBR for $5---lol.  Only drawback is it's a bit tight, but that's the price you pay for a great place to hang out (as all of the bars are the same way)

A fabulous experience and birthday dinner! Our service was excellent, not a thing was overlooked. We had the hot shrimp and crab dip appetizer as well as the bruschetta, both very tasty! I had the margarita shrimp which was perfectly fresh and light. Others at my table enjoyed steaks, pork chops and pastas. Everyone was very pleased with our meal from start to finish!

This one on Broadway is pretty reminiscent to the one in Birmingham with the only major difference being no outdoor stage. They do have two floors so it has a more restaurant feel, although the second floor was closed off by the time I got there around 1:00am. They open everyday till 3:00am which has it's advantages. The Mad Hatter's performed a mix of Top 40 and 90's music.They serve the best amaretto sours and a little too strong for my taste Vegas bombs. I'd definitely like to come back on a Friday or Saturday night and see how different it is as opposed to a Monday night.
I went to Sambuca during a Bachelorette weekend.  The food was great and the atmosphere was upscale yet fun!

Great atmosphere.   Made an evening dinner.   Great music.  Fabulous meal.  The blackened red snapper et toffee is off the hook!!!    Great service , the staff is fantastic.   A new Nashville must visit for me!!!   Loved it!!

I came here on a Sunday night for a late dinner. Food and service did not disappoint. The drinks were great - I too went with the pineapple, cucumber drink and that is probably one of my new favorite combinations. The food is pricey here - so I went with a couple of the small plate options and dessert. I had the bruschetta, Mac and cheese and the duck breast. I did feel like it was a little crazy to pay $15 for three bit size pieces of duck breast, but they were delicious. The Mac and chest was good and you would love it if you love goat cheese. I don't like goat cheese, but I still liked it enough to eat it. The bruschetta is pretty standard here. I really wanted the creme brûlée, but they were out so I settled on sticky toffee pudding with ice cream. That was pretty amazing. The night I came they had an amazing blues singer that I could have listened to for hours. This would be a great date spot for anyone looking to impress.

I can't say enough. Boots everywhere. This place is Nashville, Nashville, Nashville. There is always music and it is always good. It's a great place to stop if all the pop-country cover bands on Broadway are starting to feel like a little much. Robert's is old school. 

If you show up on a weekend night, it's going to be packed. It just is. Still, the staff is great. But you might have to strong-arm your way through the crowd to the bar. I prefer the random Tuesday. More room to sit, dance, etc. and the music is just as good.

Had dinner here with a large group last night.  Great ambiance/music.  The food was really good, other than one issue with a steak not being cooked to perfection which was corrected.  The only complaint would be the slow service, like extremely slow.  By the time our entrees arrived, we were ready to leave and one person did not receive his entree until most everyone else was finished and ordering dessert.  All in all good place to go, but not with a large party.

It's no wonder this place has stellar reviews, it is a one of kind bar, super unique with some incredible musicians, cheap drinks, a bartending staff who has clearly been working there for years and people inside who are just looking for a good time. Apparently their food is fantastic but we showed up a little too late to try anything. We took a seat by the wall and listened to an incredibly talented group of musicians for a while. This is such a divey vibe, nothing really clean about this place  but it's about the country music experience, right? If you choose to skip this bar, you're not doing it right.

Of all the places in Nashville that we discovered, and there were many, this was by far our favorite venue for awesome live music and good, cheap drinks. We went back at least 6 times in a four day trip. I also loved the grilled cheese sandwich - great "blotting paper" when drinking!
We love old county .. Exactly what we were looking for .. Great music And simple food!!

While in The Gulch recently we were wondering where to go for dinner and stopped in here.

The positives were that we got right in without a reservation and the server was friendly.

The food was overpriced and while it was well intended, lacked in terms of flavor.   I had the Lobster Enchiladas which were dry as was the tortilla/potato side, while the "kale chips" were overcooked, nearly burnt and just bad.  My wife's steak was o.k.-a flat iron.

Drink menu was large, focusing on wines and cocktails as it's the theme of the place with a jazz bar/dancing/dining concept in that order.   I realize what the place is going for, but an example of it being off was the band played the songs "Tears in Heaven" followed by "Knockin' on Heaven's Door"...kind of a downer in my opinion.

New favorite place.  Good atmosphere, football on every where and the beer is cold.  Wings are a must try.  Also, have to, absolutely HAVE to sit in Victoria ' s section!!!  Outstanding service....be back Sunday for football!
Had lunch there today.  Burger was okay; nothing special,  but the music was AWESOME.  Pork McElhinny is a very talented and fun as well

Visited here while on a business trip to Nashville. It was a Monday night, so it was pretty dead. They did have some live music and a bit of an older crowd. I proceeded t grab a seat at the bar, and ordered a drink. They dont have any draft beers which was what I was wanting. Settled for a bottled beer and ordered the shrimp and crab in lemon butter sauce with linguine. The shrimp was very plump and flavorful. Was a little disappointed by the crab in it as it was more of a crab puree then actually getting crab meat. I told them light on the lemon butter sauce which is the way to go. Too much it may have been swimming in it since it is a very rich dish as it is. I wish they gave a little bread or maybe a side to go with it, but I think you have to pay for that. For the value I would say average, but thankfully the meal tasted pretty good. Barendar was nice, and they had TV's with some games on so that kept me occupied. If I go back may try someplace new, but if you are staying in the gulch this place isnt too bad.

The music is great! Good beer selection, try the Yazoo pale ale. It's local to Nashville and really good. The tacos were great, but the Mac and cheese was runny. I'd pass on it next time. Overall, great bar pick!

Oh my gosh, this place is amazing and has some of the best bartenders.

I would like to start off by saying, we asked for a mixed drink which required root beer.  The bartender let us know they did not carry root beer, but instead of making us order another drink, she offered to go next door and BUY us some root beer!  Um, coming from Chicago, this was a once in a lifetime thing and Second Fiddle will forever receive five stars.

The band played excellent music - not one song we didn't know or want to learn because they were such great performers.  The band was so engaging, and the people in the bar were just as much fun.  

The drinks were pretty cheap compared to some other spots on the strip, and the bartenders really know what they are doing.  Great spot.
Fun bar right in the thick of Nashville. We like to go in the daytime. Less crowded and not a lot of drunk people. The bands are so good. Old time country mixed with new music.

This place is my second home. I've been a resident of Nashville for 10 years but I don't think that Robert's will ever get old. There is history in those hallowed walls. The music and acts they feature are real, genuine country. I love the dance floor. The food is great and fast. The wait staff are kind and helpful. This joint cannot be missed when you're on Broadway.

This place is BIG!!!!!  Built in '13 it's fresh and ready to go.

Pro:
*Big and broken into sections
*Easy to find bathrooms and their big!
*Staff: helpful, friendly and eager to help!! 
*Location!  Across from country music hall of fame and TONS of nearby restaurants  snd walking distances to hotels. 
Multi points in/out. 

Cons


Meh:
*Food was ok based on the convention I was there with.
Minus one star for the pillars the 19 pillars that will block your view if you're seated on the 1st floor ...not cool

Absolutely wonderful!  Our waiter was the best. He was attentive and very knowledgeable.  We tried several of his recommendations,  and he was spot on. I enjoyed the Sea Bass and my husband the Rib Eye, both of us had a great meal!  The band was very good and tried to keep the crowd involved. (Too many talky people, that evening) we also enjoyed the atmosphere.  High Fives all the way across!

This is the original home of the Grand Ole Opry.   The building this is a former Church, and you will be sitting on hard wood seats with very narrow Aisles.  Bring a seat cushion.   The show is for a radio program, so there are commercials as breaks.  We enjoyed the show, but HATED the seats.

Simple litttle gift/touristy spot to get everything with Nashville, country, music, southern and more with a theme or name on it.


Staff is nice and friendly.
Place has stuff stacked to the gills.
Greet for drunk buying...

Music was great! The service and food was a lot to be desired though. We had a group of 10 girls and the waitress was nice enough to put the bill on two separate checks, but the food for the first check came out and then the second check 20 minutes later. The food was mediocure: the fries tasted like frozen bag fries, the hot chicken was very bland, nachos came when we were finished eating.

Went here with my in-laws for my fiancé's birthday dinner. We were expecting great food and atmosphere. Bottom line: food is way over priced, the service was average, the restaurant was very loud. I wouldn't come back here unless I had a discount.

What a cool place!! The atmosphere is just amazing. Nice big bar area, dining area with a stage and live music, and if that's not your thing, then you can sit outside on their patio and people watch The Gulch. Love it!

Hubby and I got drinks at the bar and I must say, I was not a fan of mine. I got a lemondrop martini and it tasted like pure lemonade. Ok lesson learned, stick to wine...

The beignet appetizers were AMAZING. A puff pastry ball stuffed with cheese, prosciutto, and I think even basil with balsamic drizzle. Just do it. 

Dinner was not great.... I got the scallops. They are served with risotto which I love but this stuff was either over or undercooked (hard pieces) and seemed as though it had been sitting around for a while and someone just popped it under a warming light. 

Husband got the lobster tacos and he was also very underwhelmed, very little taste he said. The meals are not cheap, but we chalked it up to the price you pay for the great atmosphere. 

We got desert on the house since we were celebrating his birthday - berry cobbler and it was delish!!!

I do want to comment on the service also.... not good. Our waitress never came to check on our drinks the entire time we ate dinner and both of us had empty glasses sitting out hoping she would notice. So instead of ordering from her when she brought the bill, we just decided to get drinks elsewhere. 

Overall we loved this place because of the atmosphere and we would be back, although next time I think we would just sit in the bar area, get wine & apps, and listen to the band.
Rambling layout.  Poor access for disabled. Expensive. Wide range of space.  Lots of stairs and climbing.
Worst bar on Broadway. As a local I can say that this is the most unfriendly bar in Nashville.
Saw Josh Turner here and I must saw that this is one of my favorite music venues. Even if someone has a "bad seat," you're so close to the stage where it feels like they're singing to you.

I like seeing historical landmarks when I'm traveling and this is certainly a must-see in Nashville! 

We did an unguided tour and I really enjoyed taking in all of the historical value in this place. In particular, I really liked the clothing exhibits. Something about that is just so fascinating and eerie to me.

If you have a spare hour, definitely sign yourself up for a tour of the Ryman!

If I could give the Ryman 0 stars I would. Horrible experience. Treated poorly by the staff, no one seemed to care except for the events manager Trevor. Ushers Damien and Carol (who are apparently married according to her and take up for one another) were completely vile and I have never been treated like this in my entire life. Did not get to enjoy the show due to their rudeness and persecution. When I complained to the ushers manager I was asked if I "wanted free tickets." I explained that I didn't care about the money I cared about being treated like a human being.

A classic Nashville honky tonk. The music was loud and pumping. The crowd was dancing and having a blast. The drinks were cheap and strong. I was there on a Monday night. The strip was pretty quiet overall. But not Robert's. Just as fun and wild as a weekend. 

I wouldn't regularly spend a lot of time on Broadway, but I would definitely want to get my fix each time I'm in town and I would totally be okay doing that here.

Maybe it's because I used to live in Austin and Nashville reminds me of it-- but I found Nashville incredibly intoxicating and RWW was the cherry on top.  A friend and I capered from establishment to establishment despite the frigid springtime air and we ended up staying at Robert's Western World until it shut down.  I already had some penchant for country music, but my time at Robert's Western World and watching the talented band (and hunk) on stage only intensified my liking for the genre.  The crowd was incredibly diverse and riddled with foreign tourists who drank and danced gleefully to the tempo of the music.  A very happy place for happy people (or inebriated people) :)
Cool little venue with some great history. Lots of local bands walking through their door and the bar staff and food a great.

The best! An absolutely must-stop, must see spot in Nashville. Every bar in Nashville has a great vibe, and fantastic music, but this is by far the best spot.
