Every performance was amazing, and the energy is fantastic. The bartenders are sweet and sassy and so welcoming. I will most definitely be going back to Legends any and every time I'm in Nashville!

Came to Nashville from Chicago for an Anita Baker concert. The auditorium was huge and beautiful. The church pew seating was nice and  gave you a communal feeling. My sister complained about sitting on hard wood so bring a pillow seat cushion or something if this is your issue. The Ushers were kind and helpful. It would have been nice to had gone on the tour of the auditorium to gain more historical knowledge of the venue. Great place.

My wife and I were in town for an Avalanche game and this was the first of many bars that we visited. We stopped in late on a Monday night and it was lively...but not packed. The drinks were very inexpensive from what we are used to paying. The food was good for a late night bar food...but the band was GREAT!!! I don't know if the music is that good every night...but if it is...don't miss it!

We had a great time here last week celebrating a birthday and holiday family get together. The band was absolutely fantastic. We had a table night next to the stage and it wasn't loud at all. Food was great, drinks were flowing, and our server was attentive and wonderful.

the hubs and i were here for comicon (not dressed up, which put us in the minority...oh how the tables were turned!), and had a great time. 

the venue was super clean, with helpful attendants, informative signs, and CLEAN BATHROOMS! hallelujah! the dunkin donuts attached is super small and cramped, but, the worked efficiently, and our experience in it was good. 

there are several parking lots that surround it, and we were able to park less than a full block away for $10 in a smaller lot. 

large venue, clean bathrooms, nearby parking for reasonably cheap. all around, a good addition to nashville.

Probably my fave broadway bar. I like that you can be on the second floor and still enjoy the live music playing  on the first floor. 

Also Tara, our waitress, was amazing! Just the right balance of attention. Nice  to Find a place in Nashville that values god customer service!

One of my favorite restaurants in Nashville. The food is always amazing and normally the music is great too. Great atmosphere and the service is always on point. Definitely make a reservation because they stay busy. The patio is great during the warmer months, but the main dining area is the place to be to see the nightly band.

You could feel the history in the Ryman auditorium. We saw the grand old opry there last night and what a treat it was to hear the old sounds if country mixed with the new. The seats are like church pews adding to the spirit of the old world. I could pretend I had gone back in time 90 years when the music first started. The mood was jovial and peaceful despite the presence of numerous gun toting patriots. The black lilies were great and I loved it when Larry Gatlin danced with audience members. We were disappointed that there was no mention of Stringbean Akeman and no Stringbean memorabilia in the gift shop. No Stringbean overalls no Stringbean harmonica or Stringbean pens. The gift shop was severely overpriced and you had to show your ticket to get in or out. We enjoyed watching the bossy little singer of the black lilies direct the musicians as she belted out harmonies.

By far my favorite bar in downtown Nashville. I've been here both times that I've been to Nashville, and have had a blast both times. There's always great live music, especially Friday afternoons with Buck McCoy! There are two bars, the main in the front near the stage, and one in the back where the bartenders at both are always amazing.
Omg! Bologna sandwich. Just get it and thank me later. This place was packed for very good reasons. The musicians were great and had many people on their feet!

Dont have any other honky tonks to compare to, but great ole timey country music with fiddle and lap steel enjoyed alongside my fried bologna sandwich and PBR.

Mix of locals, sport coats and cowboy hats... good time for all. Drinks arent dirt cheap, but no cover for a great band, so no complaints at all. 



sidenote... Nashville seems to be the friendliest place on earth!

A GREAT band was playing (Rachel Hester and the Tennessee Walkers).  The place was lively and hopping on a Sunday afternoon.  The pickle fries were good and the beer was cheap. ($2.50 Miller Highlife bottles).

This place is superb. The atmosphere is elegant and music is wonderful. Not country but more blues and other crooner music. The staff was super friendly and helpful in selecting food and drinks. Our Server actually stuffed some olives for one of our martinis. Food was perfectly prepared. I had the pork chop and mac & cheese. Both were great and perfectly served. This is a great date place and can't wait to return.

This is a true Nashville bar.  There was a great band playing when we were there.  Good place to chill and have fun drinking cocktails with friends.   Good for watching games too.  They have a huge big screen downstairs.

Where to begin...lets say a great visit gon bad. The Rhyman sold us two $20 tickets at 11:04. Because there was a special evnt that day they were pretty clear that they would be closing in an hour. 

What wasn't clear was that self guided tour would be herded into a line to wait 15 minutes to watch a intro video. Once through we had 20 minutes to see the actual auditorium. 

It wasn't long into our final minutes that the lights began to flick off and the guards/etc began to shoo people along. 

Once to the lobby I took a moment to register my feelings on a comment card an then use the facilities. The guard drew the stantion tape across the entrance as I was entering and then began to argue with me about how we had enough time...should have known the place was closing...and to leave now! Oh.. But spend as much time in the gift shop as you like.

I'm very disappointed that the Rhyman would sell tickets so close to the time they needed the building empty and then not have the decency to allow your final tour of the day to take in what they paid for. We weren't overstaying our welcome. 

Also I'm not okay with picking a fight with your guests.

One of the parts of the welcome video that stuck with me is that the guests and fans of the Rhyman are what kept the place from being razed and kept vital.... If what I experienced is any sign. You've clearly lost sight of that.

Final analysis...great history here, but you'll be treated like trash once your money is handed over. Would not recommend.

We really enjoyed Sambuca! They have live music every night, and the night we were there featured a Latin Jazz band that played some original songs as well as covers. They were really good. Staff was great! Very helpful and professional. We had fried artichokes stuffed with goat cheese. They were good, but average. The crab and lobster bisque however was some of the best I've ever had. Sweet and creamy, the way I like it. For my main entree, I had lobster enchiladas, which were also fantastic and very tasty. My fiancée had crab stuffed salmon. I had a bite. It was good, but paled in comparison to the superb flavor of my entree. We couldn't resist getting a side of prosciutto Mac & cheese, which was good, but next time I could resist. For dessert, I had the tiramisu, which was different because the marscapone layer was very thick. Personally, I like it that way. My fiancée got a Heath pie, which was exceedingly rich, but he ate the whole thing somehow! My only criticism would b the cocktails. They were paltry and expensive. I swear I could have sucked down my entire margarita in one slurp. My guy ordered bourbon on the rock - hard to mess that up. Perhaps it would have been wiser to order wine, but alas I'm a tequila/vodka lover. Rim salt was excellent. Very Limey! But that's not supposed to be the best part of the margarita! Lol

Wish I could give this place more than 5 stars as they deserve 10!! Being from NY I'm not used to such a welcoming environment so Legends Corner is always a favorite spot to be at when I visit! 

The music is great, the company is great the bartenders are awesome. Even before walking inside you get greeted by such welcoming people! 
This past time when I visited Legends Corner ( weekend after Thanksgiving ) my friend and I were greeted at the door by the kindest, funniest and most inviting bouncer I've come across! ( Ray ) 

When you go into any bar your first impressions are usually with the greeters/bouncers and for me Ray definitely made a FANTASTIC first impression and was a definite influence on our decision to go inside! --- if the bouncer was that friendly and welcoming we were sure the rest of the staff would be too! ( and they were :) ) 
Can't wait to come back and visit again, it'll be my first stop!! -- and hopefully Ray will be at the door again next time! :) 

-Alexandra
:)
If you're going to Broadway, this is the place to go; don't waste your time going elsewhere. Great music, great food, and an overall great vibe. They even have a veggie burger!

Yummy cheeseburgers, great bands. Hope, our waiter today, was fun and terrific, just like the others when we've stopped in. Go for lunch, enjoy talented bands and relax! Don't forget to tip the bands :)

I love that so many businesses are made accessible by inclusion in one building! Plaza Mariachi has everything from a market, restaurants, shops, a small gallery, an attorney's office, a radio station, a live music stage, etc. It's definitely a cool spot. My only real problem with it? It looks a little too like Epcot? I wish they hadn't tried so hard with the decor, because it appears more like a theme park than a great shopping center with a number of great businesses.
Awesome old school venue that is a must see in Nashville.  We went for bluegrass night and saw Gibson Brothers. Fantastic show. Parking lot right there next to building for $10.

I haven't been to Sambuca in years, but joined a friend at the bar on Saturday night. Our bartender was amazing. He ran the bar like the ultimate pro- cool and collected while sweeping in to take orders and refilling drinks as we enjoyed the jazz band. We enjoyed the small plates and I cannot wait to go back and check out the bar upstairs which was closed for a private event. Until then... I'll be dreaming of those Goat Cheese-Stuffed Artichokes :p
Best place in Nashville for blues and Jazz. The steaks and seafood were delicious. I would say that the quality of this was the very best that you will find. We will definitely go again.

Robert's completed our solid first night in Nashville! After too many cocktails and gorging on high class food at Rolf and Daughters, my friends and I decided to end our night on a high note with $2.50 bottles of Yuengling. While the idea of Broadway isn't really my thing, obviously I couldn't come to Nashville without at least checking it out. With the street performers and endless groups of bachelorette parties, it felt a little like the Vegas Strip, minus the ability to walk down the street with a beer. 

I'm not really into country music, however, I wanted the true honky tonk experience, and I got it at Robert's Western World. The music was great, the bar was crowded but lively, and people were friendly. We made friends with multiple groups of people, most of whom were all in Nashville for the same reason - to persue their music. Definitely different from what I am used to in DC, where everyone works for the government or is looking to break into politics. Refreshing.

I had heard that Robert's was the best spot on Broadway, and while I don't have much to compare it to, I would certainly go back. Cheap beer, good music, and friends. What could be better?

My wife and I went to here last night. 

It was pretty dead and the restaurant was very dark, like hard to read the menu dark.  Yes, I get it's the vibe, but still. 

The band was average at best, much better performers elsewhere. 

The was was definitely good.

The video at the intro was a good history of the building. Fans of country music will enjoy the tour more. Balcony seats for a show would be absolutely amazing but be careful on the first floor towards the back,  visibility is limited.
So much fun!!  Bands are great and the staff is awesome!!  Loved every minute there!!!  My new favorite :):):)
Great drinks and awesome atmosphere.  they were gearing up for some live music.  too bad i couldnt stay.  i would go back in a heartbeat

The ambience is geared toward a more mature crowd, with classic country being played by live bands. The night we were there brought in an older crowd. Definitely some talented musicians. 

Drinks were a little slow, but it was a busy night. Maybe staff one more bartender to increase efficiency.

Overall though, a good time and would come again.

Being a fan of country music, seeing the Ryman was pretty awesome.  There was some construction but seeing all of the old architecture was amazing.  I went there for a concert and the acoustics were very nice and knowing all of the legends that performed on that same stage made the place that much more amazing.  We also had a great time in downtown Nashville!!!

As a music lover, I'm fortunate have lived in this great city for over a decade now and have the opportunity to see so many shows at the Ryman, the "Mother Church of Country Music." There is definitely something special about this place. The history, the pews, the stained glass. There is just so much to love about this place. The acoustics are great. Some great shows come though Nashville at this venue, because really,  who WOULDN'T want the opportunity to play here?!

Seeing a show here should be on every music lover's bucket list!
A good place to grab a beer and watch some great entertainment on Broadway . Nashville is an extreme party town but watch yourself as their are a lot of cops on the Broadway .

Well we had a bad experience at Layla's (see review) so we decided to cap the night off here. Walked in and got a bartender fairly easily. Ordered an Irish carbomb and a Jagerbomb. The bartender looked annoyed to make them and minute later we had our drinks. We finish those since they are bombs and she walks off to apparently not take another order. Stand there and get ignored for a couple of minutes. Screw this just gimme the tab so I can back to Georgia. Bartenders in this city lack personality and seem to hate their jobs. The bartender at this establishment was no exception.
Rude rude rude bartenders!!!  Our mixed drinks were straight up soda and the blonde hag said I have a shot in my drink if I paid for it.  Don't bother with this hole.

So I'm not a honky tonk person. I don't listen to country music. I haven't worn cowboy boots seriously since childhood. So obvs Broadway street is not really my scene, but it seemed ridiculous to not try it on our first trip to Nashville and of course go to Robert's Western World (or Westworld as we continued to call it all night #themazeisnotmeantforyou). We came in at maybe 11:30ish on a Saturday night and found a table within like 15 minutes. Music was great and drinks were only $6 and suuuuper strong- what a deal. Though I probably will never come back, it was definitely fun and worth trying.

Thank you to the gracious staff members who found my wallet and made every effort to return it to me! Our party had a fantastic time here and although it was a busy Saturday night for every bar in Nashville, I appreciate the staff taking the time to help me! We will definitely be back, the music was awesome!
If you are looking for a place to eat, play games, shop, and hear live music, then go here.  Several restaurants and lots of different shops, even a grocery store.

Robert's Western World is a Nasvhille staple. The music is great, the beers are cold and the food, well the food is greasy. The food is great to soak up the day. We went on a Sunday night, it was hard to get a seat at the bar, but after a little while we were able to get in. The band was great and well worth the wait. Make sure you check out all of the memorabila behind the bar and people watch while you are there!

Cool visual experience and fun to walk around but it kind of got old fast with their lack of food options, and lack of shops to go in and visit. But it is definitely cool to visit if you find yourself on a weeknight with nothing to do and you want to experience something new.
First bar we went to once we got to Nashville! Great music and fun on a Wednesday night! Very attentive and friendly bartenders! Very welcoming to us Washingtonians!
Great place for authentic live country music and cheap food and drinks. Had a wonderful night here during my first trip to Nashville.

We wanted a true Nashville honky tonk experience. We got it! It was Saturday night. The line at the door didn't take too long. I can't believe there was no cover! After we got inside, it was crowded and noisy, but a ton of fun! The band was awesome! The cocktail waitress managed to work the entire room. It was a great night!

What can you say, it's the Ryman. The walls breath good vibrations. The history in here is unprecedented. To think of all the artists that have graced this 125 year old church is staggering. We brought in the NewYear with Old Crow Medicine Show and they didn't disappoint. If you're ever in Nashville, make it a point to at least peek your head in this old school house of country music.

My favorite Honky Tonk in town. Along the Broadway strip, your typical night can be very hit or miss-- but not Roberts. Always fantastic music with a crowd actually interested in listening. For a proper Nashville experience, it's a must.

OK, I know. I sang my praises about 5 years ago and I was basically breathless at the end of my review. Here I am, knocking a star off of Robert's and it kind of hurts, but change is part of life, right?

I really do still love this place, but the Broadway strip has taken a turn in the past 5 years. I think most can agree that this has become a tourist destination for bachelor/ette parties and it sure does show if you're visiting on a weekend. It was impossible to get into some of the bars, including Robert's, and I feel like the noise of the crowd here was louder than the music. Very few people were dancing and taking in the atmosphere and it was just altogether a mess. 

I'd really like to come back on a weeknight and see if it's a little more focused on the music, which is what Nashville is all about.

We just celebrated my bachelorette party in Nashville this past weekend and had a blast! However, my Maid Of Honor has some severe food allergies (dairy and beef) and we had a difficult time finding a place that would accommodate. I can't tell you how excited we were when we saw online that Sambuca can accommodate any allergy and they re-assured us of that when we called to make the reservation. So fast forward to dinner - the place was beautiful, the waiter was super nice, and the wine was delicious. The waiter even brought out the chef who spoke to my MOH and even further re-assured us that there wouldn't be any issues. So it's going to be a good night, right? Well about 15 minutes into our entrees, my MOH calmly announces that she is going to take a few Benadryl because she doesn't feel right... Long story short, she went into a full allergic reaction which required an epi-pen and we ended up spending 3 hours in the Emergency Room because the kitchen somehow screwed up her food. Luckily, she fully recovered and is feeling great, but the worst part was that the restaurant didn't even have the decency to take anything off our $300 bill - including the contaminated food that sent my best friend to the hospital and ruined our night.

Was doing the Broadway thing and slid into Roberts after starting out at Silver Dollar. The band was serving a serious slice of blues with a young lad on lead guitar slaying his axe. They went into a long Allman bros. song with an incredible solo. After the tip jar went around they started a C/W set. Before I could lament the loss of the blues, our fine young lad was tearing up the licks. Please don't miss Roberts - it's the real deal. Oh yeah - cheap beer too.

Great place to see some country/western music in Nashville!  (Less of a tourist location compared to the other spots close by) Since you didn't come here for the bbq get a fried bologna sandwich and enjoy the great music. Tip the staff and the musicians(there is no cover)! Will definitely go back if I am in Nashville.

Really fun place. Great band. Not sure her name but i had a blonde bartender that was great and really attentive. The fried bologna sandwich is the thing to eat but I didn't love it. Just my preference. I still recommend trying it just for the experience.

Man, our bartender 
Really jacked up our drinks so
No thanks to Legends

We had a fun time checking this place out.. the beginning video is excellent!!! Honestly, whomever did this video on the history of the Ryman should go HELP the Country Music Hall of Fame - that place is so boring - this was NOT boring.. the tour is quick (about 30 min for us) but we saw a lot of history and you can just "feel" everything they are speaking of!! Def worth a check out if in Nashville!!

I am not sure why this place has 3.5 stars. In my opinion, it's a guaranteed good time with fab food! We had a bachelorette dinner there for 18 girls who flew in from several different cities throughout the country. I wanted to make sure the bride to be and the other gals had delicious food, good ambiance & service, and great live music. That is exactly what we got. Since we had such a large party we had to choose one of the many pre fixe options. We were able to adjust the menu we selected since we had a handful of vegetarians, to two veggie entrees (veggie lasagna and Portobello quinoa- YUUMM) and two meat (the steak was perfectly charred). Each dish was so unique and worth every cent (which wasn't much!). To top it off with the trio dessert, let's just say we were craving more. The toffee chocolate ball was to die for. Tiffani, who helped arrange the menu was a pleasure to work with and even personalized the menu for us! Natalie served us the entire evening and put up with our antics. :) She was such a great server.The band was fun and entertaining as well. The bride got to go up on stage and chat with them, it was a riot.   I am giving it a 5 on every level! Made our Nashville experience all that much better!

During our Broadway bar crawl this spot hands down had the most consistent line up of amazing live music. 

Every time we stopped in we were completely blown away by the singers on stage. 

It's a great bar for people watching as well. The bartenders here are very polite and actually pour pretty great drinks. 

This should be a stop during your Nashville adventures! Cheers! 

Stop in and request some of your favorite county songs!

Horrible experience. I don't even know where to begin. The building is at least beautiful but in a nut shell they couldn't care less bout YOU the customer.  To top things off we were trapped in the parking garage for over an hour because they don't know how to manage the traffic on their own property. THEN the machine to pay for parking doesn't work the first ten times you try to pay even with the employees trying to do it for you. I was shocked that they still wanted us to pay... At some point waiting over an hour to escape a parking garage is insane and you should cut your losses and just let people out. Everyone was freaking out honking and yelling. Kids were crying in cars. God forbid if someone got sick an ambulance would never get to you. I WILL NOT BE VISITING AGAIN.
Beautiful venue, excellent sound. Only issue, never purchase tickets under the balcony. The view was seriously obscured. Great bar setup, plenty of options for getting drinks. Staff was very helpful.

Great night, food was great with a wide selection. The entertainment on the night was awesome. Only problem was we never booked a table and had to sit at a bar area, a first come bases. Had a great view of the band however so wasn't to bad!
Cheap beer.  Great atmosphere. Live music in Nashville is awesome  and Tin Roof keeps the vibe going.

F*ck every other bar on Broadway after coming to Roberts western world. Bartenders are always amazing to me, bands are amazing and no BS country, just the real sh*t. Fried bologna sandwiches, makers mark on the rocks, with some killer live music and you have me sold.

Mine and my boyfriends favorite place to go to in nashville for a special night out. It's great food and always love music, only thing I dislike is I feel like the tables are on top of each other, if you're looking for something a little more private or romantic I would suggest somewhere else
First place we stopped in on our trip through Nashville.  Great music, no cover charge, cold beers, good service and good crowd.  What's not to like about this place.  Didn't have any food.

Tonya and Issac was behind the bar and slinging drinks, the band was entertaining and fun, met some really cool locals. Overall a great experience and will be a regular stomping ground whenever i am in town.

The bartenders are amazing here especially Becky at the far end. I didn't even watch the band I just watched her work. Bands are really good. The bar has a lot of energy. And a lot of people eat here From what I can tell.
My wife and I really enjoyed the music here today.  Harold

EW, EW, and more EW! So was there for a military ball, and I get it you probably gave us a discount. . .whatever. Food was HORRIBLE chicken was raw, NO not undercooked, not to "our" liking RAW. One piece was still bleeding and when it was brought to manager? supervisor? S attention we didn't get any concern or care, just oh want another piece? UMMM no thanks dying or getting sick on raw chicken and who knows what else it touched not my idea of a good night. Couldn't even enjoy the veggies those were also undercooked and had a bad vinegar sauce on them. so left early and had tacobell for dinner. Really thought we were in for a great night at a great venue, boy was I proven wrong.

Good time.  Good music.  Food was served fast.  Limited menu.  Cheeseburger just right- nice and greasy.  Fries and onion rings also good.  Like a little hole in the wall- just what I was looking for.
Had a great time. chose the guided tour and our guide was not only witty but very informative. amazing history and a must see by any fan of music period. LOVED coming here.

Playing tourist, I wandered in here.  Found a table close to the performers.  The music was great, if you don't mind the commercials.  They ask for money all the time.  I felt they should be offering a tote bag.

Waitress finally noticed me, and I got a fried baloney sandwich.  I regretted it a few hours later.  Tasty at the time, it was a real gut buster.  Still, it was a touristy thing to do, and most of the honky tonk meals I had in Nashville made me queasy if I didn't drink enough unsweetened ice tea.  You don't go to Nashville for the food.  I don't see how anyone can trust their gut instinct when their guts are rebelling.

The decor was interesting.  Boots, old timey instruments and signs, etc.  The second floor was empty when I was there, but the place could be hoppin' at a busier time.

I only went into a few of the honky tonks in the area, of which there are many.  All are a little different in terms of decor, menu and music as they vie for your tourist dollars.  Robert's seemed a good place to hang out on a hot day, and less of a blatant tourist trap.  But next time, if there is a next time, I'll have one of the burgers.

This was one of our favorite stops during the Bachelorette weekend. We had fried pickles, chips sampler, and chicken Caesar salad, and a bunch of beer, and the waitress was very sweet BUT the music was the best part. 

This was the perfect place to go on a Sunday afternoon and swoon over the music duo Matt Marinchick and Ben Mathis. They are adorable, talented, and funny.  I didn't get a chance to sample any of the other bands that play here, but if this is a taste of what else the venue serves, I'll be back again.
Great food, great vibe.  Just don't get the lobster.

Overall disappointing. With all of the AMAZING places around Nashville, Sambuca has to step it up. Service was wonderful and the manager was very apologetic, but the food took nearly 2 hours and arrived cold. I don't recommend it, honestly.

Loved this auditorium. Just being there, I could understand the whole country music history.
Hope I can watch a show there. Introductory movie they are showing at the Ryman was impressive. Well done movie.

Umm 11a-7p happy hour in the Gulch!? Yes!! The drinks here were so great, as was the food & the ambience.  Best part of it all was our soft spoken super kind & helpful waiter..what a nice & funny guy! Drinks: Sambuca 75 (95?), blueberry margarita, frose, and mojitos...all made well & not too sweet...& at $5-7 for HH, try them all! Food: crab dip, salmon salad, chicken sandwich...all good again! There was nothing we didn't like about this place!
Band is kicking a$$. Love the atmosphere.  There is a lot of room and the drinks are great.  Looking at the menu...  Live the bar food too

This place is super fun. We stopped by here on the YSB UYE bar crawl this past Friday, I believe it was.

Apparently the musicians don't get paid, so make sure to tip them well - their only payment is tips. 

We all congregated on the top floor, which was a *tiny* bit quieter than the bottom floor, which was nice.

I'd come here again if ever in the area!
One hell of a bloody mary. Great music too. We went around lunch time too. Bartender was nice too.

I've been here multiple times for my favorite shows in town. The Ryman is legendary for a reason. I've never been to a place where the audience respects the bands and which holds a communal reverence as well as the Ryman.

For example, in comparing the Ryman to the Tabernacle in Atlanta, the venues are about the same capacity and have about the same-level acts come through. However, shows at the Ryman have a way of capturing the audience's love and respect that makes you feel like you're face-to-face with the performer paying them their personally owed respects for their time and efforts. It's a really unique feeling that I only get at the Ryman.

I could go on and on about the details of the place but you really must go experience a show here if you haven't already. Yes, the pews aren't super comfortable and they pack the audience in but you don't care about those things once the show starts.

Pros:
Best concert venue I've ever been to. The sound, atmosphere, history, and audience all add up to the best concert experience you can imagine.

Cons:
It was under construction when I went to see Ben Howard so it wasn't quite as pretty as it normally is.

Overall:
Go. Just go.

You cannot find better music! The food (for bar food) is great. I had a wonderful hamburger and fries. They make real drinks. You do not have to wonder if the bartender really added alcohol to your rum and coke. Back to the music, if you do not want get up and dance it must be intermission. The crowd is fun and oh did I mention that the music is the best on Broadway?

I scalped some tickets to a show.  The venue is a historic place that must be visited.  For seating, dont sit in teh lower level, GET BALCOLNY!   As any old venue, the seats below are obstructed.  But great place to see and great sound.

Walked in and sat at a booth. The band that was playing was alright. We waited for five or six minutes before finally being given menus. The waitress dropped the menus on our table and walked away. 
We ordered drinks and chips and salsa. The water tasted like sewage water and the shots were served in medicine cups. Later that evening all of us that drank the water were feeling really sick.
Service is great! Burgers are ok but the fries and grilled sandwiches are on point. Live music is one of the best on Broadway!

Good music, quick snack. 

Stopped in here towards the end of the night for a baloney sandwich.  Comes with a bag of chips and PBR but we upgraded to whiskey.

We enjoyed the bands here. As you may surmise from the name it is on the corner of Broadway and 5th Ave. It is a popular place and was busy night and day while we were here, always playing good music.

This place was a lot of fun. Was it the best ? Not for me but it was still a good time. The music can vary from each night but most of the bands on Broadway are very good (at least in my opinion). The beer was cold and that is what means the most to me.

Awesome venue! No matter where you sit you have a really good view of the stage. I actually prefer the seats up top. Seems like you get a better view (plus those seats are cheaper ;p). All the great artists want to play here so there's no lack of shows coming through. Only thing I can find a complaint with are the seats. They're way hard on your backside, but what can you expect from church pews haha.
Saw Little Big Town here and it was awesome! My first time visiting Nashville & the Ryman and I cannot wait to come back. Amazing night!

Was there last week. Great bands. Good food. The bands I listened to I ended up buying their CDs. Awesome time. Highly recommended. If you need to check off "get drunk at a honkytonk" on your bucket list, this place fits the bill to a "T".
Great location.  Across the street from the Bridgestone Arena.  Great music and fair selection of beverages.

Historic? Yes. Great sound? Yes. Great acts? Yes. But, it is hands down the most uncomfortable venue to see a concert. They oversell the church pew benches so you are smashed together. I'm not a big person, but it seems like everyone else is - and I prefer a bit of personal space, especially if I'm sitting for hours. I've seen a dozen shows there, but I give up. I will not go back until they update the seating or stop overselling the venue.

I don't like being touristy but mom wanted to do the tour here. WOW! I was surprisingly impressed! tour was very well done & the place has a history that would be interesting to ANYone. go for it while you're visiting!

I would return to Sambuca based off of service alone. Tyler, our server was beyond attentive and was definition of southern hospitality. The food was amazing as well. I had the Shrimp and Crab Scampi, it was delicious and filling. A few people in our group ordered the scallop dish and it was devoured by all. You should definitely get the creme brulee, it was SO GOOD!!! If you're visiting Nashville and need a good spot for food and music add this spot to your list!
Wow! I love this place. I make sure I stop in when I am in Nashville. The show tonight was fantastic and the food is good. Simple, delicious bar food straight from the flat top.

With many music choices in the live seeing, they have two bands playing alternatively through the night. While the food was decent the chicken sandwich was more like for food but the salad was very good the music more than made up for it

This venue has a pretty old and musty feel to it.  I'm definitely not a huge fan.  For as old as it is though, it's clean and the drink prices are a a dollar or 2 less than Bridgestone Arena.  I wouldn't not go to a show here due to the venue but it's not somewhere I'm dying to go back to either.

First night in Nashville ever. Wandered in for dinner with the kids because the vibe sucked me off the street. Good service but very casual. Band playing were solid and tolerating a few annoying drunks. NFL games playing on a number of screens which is a bonus. Good price, serving Mexican mostly. 
Wished the kids were at the hotel so I could of enjoyed this place a lot more!
Drinking a Hop Perfect IPA...Great beer and listening to the Don Kelly Band. When in Nashvegas, one of many places to visit!

Another great bar on Broadway. A lot of good energy and good music. There's not much which separates this one from the others, but for no cover, good music, and a nice atmosphere you can't go wrong with Legends.

Stopped back in this place just for a night cap and dessert -- the bar area upstairs is open seating.  We had another phenomenal time.  Great music, great service, great drinks and dessert.  I'd recommend this spot to anyone looking for great live jazz and a fun atmosphere to celebrate something.

Just FYI, if you don't do valet the pay lot up the street is now $15 for the evening.

Awesome dive-ish bar on Broadway! 

Yes, Broadway is the tourist-y strip in Nashville, but it's worth checking out, esp. if you're a tourist.

(Make sure you check out the rest of the city though, too.)

Legends: live music, strong drinks, ample space, fun/kitschy "Music City" décor.

Nice ladies' bathrooms! Solid bartenders. 

Not too much else to say, really.

We stopped in here to grab some drinks before lunch. Overall it was a nice place to grab quick food and listen to music. I will say that the music was very loud, so if you plan to have a conversation with the people at your table, this might not be the best place to go. We ordered drinks and appetizers, and sat on the second floor since the first floor was packed. The food we ordered was pretty standard bar food, nothing spectacular.

I haven't been to every music venue in Nashville, but this one takes the cake hands-down. The Ryman Auditorium is historic and is a respected institution of the city. The Ryman got its start by hosting evangelists as a tent revival then became the Grand Ole Opry and almost was destroyed before being restored. They do host tours which I would love to do sometime, but this review is just as a music venue. 

The acoustics in this place are amazing. My friend and I went to see Brandi Carlisle, and she really used the venue to her advantage. Brandi, with one guitarist and one backup singer stood in front of the microphones to sing and the whole venue could hear her. It was one of the coolest things I've seen someone do at a concert. 

The seating is still reminiscent of church pew style seating. The big long wooden benches do make it an interesting arrangement for watching a concert, but somehow it works. 

The staff are all friendly and would walk you to your seats. They have a few concession stands to buy wine or beer. 

If you get the chance to see a concert here do it! Its one of the most interesting places in Nashville.
We did a self guided tour here & it was really nice! This was a great place to see! I'd recommend a visit.

Came here with my family and girlfriend during Christmas leave from overseas.  They do have a military rate and the Ryman is an attractive building...... Although I was sorely disappointed that we were rushed through a "self guided" tour.  The security people were very rude and pushed us through the walkway like cattle closing the doors behind us each section we barely viewed.  I understand that you may have an event to setup for but we were there well before closing time.   My money would of been better off supporting the Country Music Hall of Fame Museum.  


Congrats you get One Star!

We came for the drinks and dessert and we were thoroughly delighted with both. Cory, our waiter, also let me "make my own drink"--the strawberry purée mojito....with no mint. It's called The Brooke, and it tastes like a Sonic drink so be careful; it's a bit too easy to slurp those suckers down with no inhibition. Cory was awesome. We basically became friends by the end of our stay. Loved this place. When I'm back in Nashville, this will be a place I come to.

We attended the late Opry show at the Ryman on a Saturday.  We showed up at 9:10pm and were left out in the cold night until 9:30pm.  The show was suppose to start at 9:30pm but started around 9:45pm.  There was a fine mist and around 33 degrees that night.  We had my elderly father with us.  Standing in line to get in the door in the wet cold air.  I was extremely worried about my father's health.  I think they were waiting for everyone to get out from the early show.  I have no other explanation on why we were out in the cold air for so long.  I wish I had known we would have to wait outside and would have made different decisions.  Thankfully, to date my father hasn't gotten ill but I have.  I know it is from standing out in the cold mist for so long.  Next time we attend Opry in the winter months we will go to the early show so not to be in the cold so long.

The show itself is like stepping back in time.  The seats are pew style and as Americans are getting bigger they are tight.

We returned later in the week for the back stage tour.  I don't know if we would do it again.  Really the self guided tour gets you everything you learn on the back stage tour.  The tour allows you to see the dressing rooms and stand at the side of the stage.  The entire tour was about 30 minutes.  Everything the guide told us can be read in the self guided tour.  The closest parking lot cost us $20.  I am sure there are other places to park but again with my Dad we wanted to be as close as possible.

The history here is special.  Worth a visit.

What a waste of money. Nothing printed on my tickets about limited view. I went to guess services and the gentleman looked at a seating chart and replied that my seats were fine. I showed him this photo and he still wouldn't assist me. 

Sounded like a great show and I bet most seats are a great view. Shame.

This place was a little odd, but I liked it.  It's located on a corner (hence the name), right next to Tootsie's and down the block from the Ryman.

My husband and I stopped in for a few drinks on a Saturday afternoon after escaping the 24/7 bachelorette party of Tootsie's.  It wasn't very crowded, which was a nice break.  We were able to settle in at a table and drink some cheap Miller Lites.

The entertainment when we visited was this guy named Buck McCoy.  I guess you could call him a Tim McGraw impersonator?  Musically, he was just ok, but he put on a decent show and was very entertaining.  He also brought on this TERRIBLE Elvis impersonator... which was kinda weird, but again, entertaining.

If you are on Broadway, I'd definitely check this place out.  They have all sorts of country music memorabilia on the walls, which is cool.  It's also a long, narrow space, so you can be all the way at the back bar and still see/hear the band.

used to be my favorite place to come. the last three visits have not been good. service awful, food bad, warm drinks from the bar. the only thing this place still has going for it is the atmosphere. its completely overrun with bachelorette parties now.

This place has a cool western vibe. Live music, plenty of bar space, staff is very friendly and knowledgeable of the menu. Drink specials are awesome. Fried bologna is very good as well as the onion rings. If you're looking for a place to grab a drink with some friends, I would recommend this 100%.

The Ryman Auditorium has some interesting history and the tour is a must! They bring you in a room and a presentation plays that is very entertaining and educational! The building has so much history! Highly recommended!
Love this place, it's beautiful and a must see while in Nashville but the stage performances and advertising push seems a bit dated, which was sad to see.

Our favorite bar on Broadway - this coming from a girl who has trouble listening to any country made after 1995. We came here for fun after my wedding, and it was the perfect place for a little after-party dancing! What's more, I was wearing my great-grandmother's bracelet (priceless) and after getting home that night, realized it had fallen off. With little hope, I called RWW the next morning and, lo and behold, they had found it and kept it in a safe place until I was able to come get it. Needless to say, I'll be a patron for life.

The Mother Church! Amen. What an inexpensive no frills tour that takes you back in time!
 
Arrive on time, make it safely through the TSA-style Security checkpoint and head up stairs.
You file into a small room with multiple benches and a large screen surrounded by old school concert posters. This room - packed with tourists - definitely needed a fan or air conditioning as it got a bit toasty during the opening film.

I learned so much about The Ryman and it's beginning during this video. So, pay attention! It's very well done. Next, you'll move through the double doors and WOW there it is ... the iconic auditorium! Amazing and breathtaking.

It's an easy self-guided tour that will take you as long as you want to spend admiring The Mother Church and the displays donated by artists and their estates.

This was one of the last music venues I had left to go to in Nashville. 

I had the opportunity to come here with some girlfriends to see darrin criss and leah Michelle a couple months ago. As I mentioned, I had never been to this venue and wasn't sure what to expect. We went on a weekday and upon walking up there was a huge line outside. We were even early, so I was a little confused. They didn't open doors until right before the show and the lobby area was small; hence the line.  
It's a smaller venue, but very much like the grand ole opry. The lobby area is just as cute and quaint as the opry. 
We had pretty good seats, but let's be honest the seats at both locations kinda suck lol. They're church pews, which are super cute, but not comfortable for a long show. 

I liked the venue all in all.

We had a late lunch at Tin Roof on the first day of our first visit to Nashville and it was a wonderful experience of the Nashville, Broadway music scene.  The food was excellent.  We had a great burger and yummy beef and mushroom quesadilla.  The frosting on the cake was the band, a trio that did a mix of older and newer country songs.  Pedal Steel Guitar, Bass and Guitar were perfect in this space.  It was quiet at lunch, the band took requests and we almost stayed all day.

Nice old fashioned mom and pop operation with good music, tasty fried baloney sandwiches and disgusting wine in a plastic cup.....and our bartender was proud of it when she proclaimed "y'all ain't gonna get no fancy wine in this town"
Cheap beer and good bar food!  Second floor patio is great for people watching. Nice place for happy hour on a week night.
Again, just fulflilling a few items on my bucket list. It was a marvelous living, breathing memorial to a cultural form.

This place is great! 5 star food, live entertainment, arcade games, mall stores, grocery, you can even buy a car or a house. Everyone we came in contact with was really nice. Great customer service. We will definitely be back.

omg... $2.50 domestic beer
great live music 
fried bologna sandwich, burgers,  pork chop sandwich....great food at reasonable prices.
don't miss robert's!!!!!

This place was pretty good. The music was very loud (which I think is typical for Nashville). It's almost hard to hear yourself think. We stopped in for
A snack-we had the loaded tator tots. They were to die for! We had the ranch dressing on the side which was a good idea as there was a lot of cheese on the tots. The service was good and the people were very friendly. I would definitely return for drinks and a snack.

My wife and I had our Valentine's dinner on 2/13/16.  All the food except our dessert was exquisite.  For starters we had chicken samosas in puff pastry and buca beignets, and for dinner had red snapper bouillabasse and scallops.  The first two drinks we ordered were also exceptional - Sambuca 75 and coconut mojito.  All the food and drinks to this point were creative and delicious.  Less exceptional were the other two drinks we ordered because we got things that were way too sweet, and the cheesecake sopapilla dessert was nothing to get excited about.  The ambiance is very cool and romantic.  There was live music at the front with tables laid out theater-style. We're not fans of loud music where we can't talk to each other, so this was perfect for us - very talented musicians, Tiffany Johnson & Soul Confidant, with a great sound balance that was loud enough for us to be fully engrossed in the music but not so loud that we couldn't carry on a normal conversation.  The service was also very good.

So some friends asked me to go on an adventure to this new place on Nolensville Rd for lunch today. I had no idea what to expect but was surprised off the bat when I showed up to the old Kroger and saw what they had done to the exterior! It looked great! When we went in there were little shops and kiosks everywhere selling everything from absolutely beautiful Quinceanera dresses to International trinkets to cell phone cases. The food area is set up like a food court with a stage at one end. There were about six walk up food stops and one sit down place at the other end. I went to the place that serves esquites street corn naturally and also got carnitas nachos. All I can say is yum! And as I looked around It looked like all of the portion sizes are great!! They have live music every night! Wednesdays they Wine and Rewind night where they play live 80s and 90s music?!?! Um, sign me up!  Check this place out! It's worth it!

I'm really glad I didn't write this review a week ago.  This place really grows on you.

It always smells like onion rings in here.

I haven't been here a whole lot..probably about four or five times.  If I'd have reviewed this place last week, I would have given it two stars.  If I'd have reviewed it after the first or second time visiting Robert's, it would probably only be one.  I would almost give it four stars, but I don't think it's grown on me THAT much just yet.  Maybe someday.

Anyway, enough rambling...let me get to the point.  The first thing you'll probably notice when you first come here (if you're like me) is how small and compact it is.  This is no Wildhorse or Whiskey Bent Saloon.  There's a small stage and a small dance floor in the front.  From there on back is the bar on the right, tables on the left, and the bathrooms in the very back.  There is very little walking room between the bar and the tables.  So don't come here on a busy, crowded night...you won't find a place to sit or even stand.  I typically come here on Tuesday nights, and I can still hardly ever find a place to sit.  I usually end up sitting on the ledge by the piano.

The name "Robert's Western World" can be a bit deceiving.  When I hear "Western World," I think of an Old West saloon.  This is not an Old West saloon...it's a Tennessee honky tonk.  The only thing really "Western" about the place is that there are cowboy boots lining the walls, which, I will admit, are kind of neat.

I've never drunk alcohol at the bar here, nor have I eaten the food, so I can't really review the food or drinks, but what I can tell you is that they must make lots of onion rings here because the bar ALWAYS smells like onion rings.  Every.  Single.  Night.

Now, on to my favorite part...the dancing!  Like I said, there is a small dance floor in the front.  I would say it's about big enough for two and a half couples to dance at a time.  So, as I said, don't come here to dance on a busy Friday or Saturday night.  But if you come here on Tuesday, Sunday, or another non-busy day, you should have enough room to dance.  I would definitely recommend Tuesday nights though.  Harry Fontana, a great local rockabilly singer, plays; and his music is excellent for swing dancing.

Also, the bar smells like onion rings.

The men's bathroom here makes me want to regurgitate.  I wouldn't know how the women's bathroom is, but the men's smells like rotting corpses.  I have to remind myself that I'm not in a morgue every time I use the bathroom at Robert's.  It doesn't necessarily LOOK gross or even FEEL gross...but do yourself a favor and wear a clothespin on your nose whenever you use the bathroom here.

The bartenders here are mediocre.  Not great, but not terrible.  If they're at the other side of the bar, you'll have to wait a few minutes to get to you.  But once you place your order, they'll get your order out in a jiffy.  They're not particularly friendly, but they do their job and get you your food and/or drinks in a pretty timely fashion.

However, if you want to meet an EXCELLENT employee of Robert's, just talk to the bouncer.  Okay, maybe I'm a little bit...or a lot...biased.  She is both gorgeous and flirty.  She always smiles and calls me "handsome" when I come in.  So yeah, if you're a man, you'll definitely get a kick out of her!

Oh yeah, did I mention that Robert's smells like onion rings?

It's a great place, just make sure you're outta there by sundown. At sundown, they basically just turn the amps up to screaming levels and pretend they are as good as the afternoon band, which is not true. The afternoon band plays with purpose and sensitivity and is very tight. The feature band is not tight at all, although they are loud as hell, which apparently is all you need to be to fool this generation of morons.

The tour itself was great and worth the $20. Our tour guide, Leslie, did a fabulous job. But the customer service upon entering the theater was lackluster at best. Every employee just looked at us with "deer in headlight" stares. We needed assistance retrieving our pre-purchased tickets. The one guy literally said, "can't help you till you have your tickets!" Really? We can't get our tickets, that's why we need help!! There was a line for an upcoming concert at the ticket sale office, where our tickets were being held. It was confusing and frustrating.

Great live music for a low key dark dinner. Wine list and service was fantastic. Food was average at best with value. Pork Chop was dry, apps needed some more flavor and ramped up presentation. Just average for Nashville. Expectations were higher
This place has great fried chicken. The tater tots smothered was delicious. And had great live music.

This is one of our favorite places to visit for fun drinks, good food and great music ALL of the time. Their music starts earlier than most bars on Broadway and they play a mix of everything including some Country Rock n Roll. Our server Maggie was friendly and brought us our bar drinks pretty quickly. She took our food order and brought out everything just as we wanted. We shared some food and we tried some tacos and sandwiches. The burger was juicy and the toppings were fresh. The Pulled Pork sandwich was just sweet enough and not too stringy for a pulled meat. We really liked the street corn and wished the portion was a little bit bigger for a side order. Nothing gourmet but we just wanted good bar food while we listened to the singers/bands. That is exactly what we wanted. 
This is a chain restaurant/bar and they are opening a location very close to our home. We mentioned to our server how excited we were to be getting a Tin Roof soon and asked if she had any other information for us on when it would be opening. She actually sent over to our table a gentleman named Wes (corporate guy) who gave us some great information. Fingers crossed that we will become regulars to the new Delray Beach, Fl. location and still enjoy our Nashville getaways and visit here when we are in town. 
Thanks for the fun times this past weekend!

Dont think Awesome can sum it up. Gorgeous. And very well centralized downtown. Came on a conference and was able to see the Music Hall of Fame, Bridgestone Arena and all of Honky Tonk within a 2 block radius. Restaurant inside as well as a Dunkin, no crazy prices, but walk outside and prices skyrocket. Wish there were healthy food alternatives nearby or other coffee shops not charging $6 for some specialty super branded type. How about some tea?
Views from fourth floor are amazing. Ballroom is huge. It is centered on two blocks with the parking lot entrance and shuttle pick up in between under enclosure.

In Nashville Memorial Day weekend with some girlfriends and had to check out Robert's Western World.  One of my good friends from college is an Okie who is old school country to the bone.  He assured us that Robert's was the ONLY real honky tonk on Broadway, so of course, we had to oblige.

The house band was incredible.  The lead singer knew every word to EVERY requested song by heart.  He was the only one all weekend that did NOT have any sort of reference to cheat from while he sang (ipad, iphone, etc).  Of the many bars we checked out, EVERY other singer had an ipad.  Clearly this band REALLY knows their stuff.  Plus they were legit.

Drinks were made well and affordable, and the friend pickles were DELISH.

What a fun afternoon, we had a great time and made some awesome memories.

I'll start with the positives:
1) atmosphere was awesome. The lighting was sophisticated and romantic. The live band was also a great touch and not too loud. We sat upstairs so we have a really nice view. 
2) the service was great. Our waiter was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. He made some great recommendations to my husband for his whiskey drink and beers.  

The negatives: 
1) for the price, the food was UNDERWHELMING at best.  We ordered the calamari as a starter and it was bland. I'm not sure if Applebees has a calamari dish, but if they do, I'd imagine this would be it. No flavor and rubbery. At this point I was apprehensive about ordering dinner, but we proceeded. My husband ordered the ribeye and I ordered the seabass. Both were pretty bland, and again for the price, I was expecting to be blown away. 
2) our food took close to 40 minutes to come out. A group of six women that came in at least 25 minutes after us got their food before us. 
3) the drinks, while tasty, were WEAK. Again, for the price I was expecting much much more. 

Overall, if a friend was having a birthday party at this establishment I would probably go back. With that said, I'd eat before and just order wine.
Of all the honky tonks I visited on my recent trip to Nashville only Robert's lived up to my expectations for authenticity. It's free to get in, so why not give it a shot?

I planned my best friend's bachelorette party dinner here and it was more than I could ever ask for. The hosts were so sweet and knew the bride by name, and they put us by the stage and the singer honored our bride to be. Our server, Maxfield, was perfection, recommending so many incredible dishes-- the mozzarella beignets and the shrimp and crab dip were amazing, and the ribeye was the best I've ever had hands down. We came for the ambiance but left happier than we ever could've imagined.  It's a must-try if you're looking for a great night on the town that's not the over-done Honky Tonk stuff!

Perfect in every way.  This is the real deal, people.  Awesome, storied venue with solid vintage country music live starting at 11 am.  The service is impeccable.  The prices are very reasonable.  Brendon (?) waits tables on the first floor.  Dressed for the part in his cowboy best, he is also a very nice person.  We were there for 5 hours on a Saturday and watched him work. We started timing our beers.  The longest wait was 14 seconds.  He should give lessons.  We loved it here.  Nothing else on Broadway compared all day and all night.  Seriously awesome time.  Fried bologna sandwich was simple and delicious in the best way. Giddy up and go!!!!  You will feel like a regular in 5 minutes because of how they treat you!  It's like being in a friend's basement.

Great food and the service was great as well. Sophia, our waitress was super friendly and attentive. Live music playing in the front of the restaurant, but if you sit in the back, much quieter but still able to hear the music playing.

We did the backstage tour of this place and it was amazing!!!  A must in Nashville!!  It really settles you into the history of country music!!!  After the tour yesterday, we saw Josh Turner & Little Big Town in concert and what an experience!!!  There not joking when they say they have the 2nd best acoustics in the country!!!  WOW...this is an extremely special place to see a concert!  What an honor!  Definitely see something here if you can, you will not be disappointed!!!!  It seats about 2,100 people.  We had lower level tickets, but I think I would try the balcony next time.  There definitely isn't a bad seat in the place, but I would just change it up!

Amazing music and great vibe.  Been here twice in a 2 day period.  First time was great food, great service and great vibe on a Friday night.  Music was perfect and they were very accommodating for high top table and joining them together. 

2nd time was not as pleasant. It was over 1hr and 15min wait for food with little to no explanation except over hearing an explanation to another table.  At first I thought it was just a large table ordering before us.  But as we saw two tables leave we realized there was a bigger issue. 

All in all it may be a one time issue but unclear and no explanation provided. Might consider amending with an explanation.

I had a really terrible experience here--the bartender took my order two separate times, then got people's drinks but not mine. When I asked her where mine was & why I hadn't gotten it yet, she told me that she wasn't going to serve me because she didn't like my attitude. I am NOT the type of person who is rude to service workers, ever, nor was I belligerently drunk, so for her to behave so unprofessionally was appalling to me. I would submit a formal complaint to the bar, but let's be honest, they're an incredibly popular tourist trap that will do business no matter how rude their bartenders are, so I doubt they care about losing one persons business. I can only hope that others will see this review and take it as a warning--there are much better places to go on Broadway with a much friendlier staff.
The first Honky tonk we encountered on Nashville's famous Broadway. This one is on the corner, kitty to Bridgestone arena. Decent cover bands,  pricey beers, nice staff. Time to hop to the next bar.

I had to hit this spot up multiple times on my week-long vacation. The platter....oh the platter! I with I could find sausage like that where I live. And the pulled pork was, of course, amazing. A shot of crown is cheaper than a shot of Jack Daniels because "It's the best whiskey there is"...this is clearly a Tennessee thing.

This honkytonk was listed as a recommendation on the Grand Ole Opry website so it was the first stop for me and my family for lunch upon arrival. I was very disappointed considering there are so many other honkytonks to choose from. Immediately upon walking in I was approached by waitstaff but was not greeted w/hello but told I could not bring in outside drinks (I was holding an empty soda can). I disposed of the can & ordered a few items off the menu. The food was basic fast food. Nothing spectacular at all. Tried to enjoy the music but the band playing was horrible. They were not even playing country music and were not shy about passing a tip can around in your face even before we heard them play. Wish I had gone somewhere else! Don't waist your time here when there are so many other options.
A really great place to stop and take Nashville in. Grab a pop, a fried bolognese sandwich and listen to the live music. Go there if you're walking around downtown Nashville.

Took my gf here for her birthday since it was the only place that could accommodate a large party on a Friday night.  It was my first time here.  First, the ambiance is something I think everyone should experience with a live band, sky bar with a lounge type feel. Drinks were ok. Had the starburst which tasted like unset jello but was good.  The tigersblood was good also but was a little too dry.  For dinner I had the cosmos pizza which was decent.  Gf had the beignets which were ok....it was my first time having those as well.  She wasn't impressed with the desserts which were fried cheesecake and creme brulee. I would go back but not really for dinner. Maybe just for an appetizer and drinks and to listen to the band.

Even as a local this is a really fun place to get away for a night on the town dancing to great fun music.

Cheap beer .  fried balogne and burgers after a long night make it a must do anytime were downtown.

Also, generally less crowded than some other popular honky tonks too.

If I'm feeling extra wild i sometimes even end up coming home with a brand new pair of boots!
Great spot that wasn't too crowded and music was great. Good bartender service and band not to pushy about tips.

Amazing venue. Historical, reverent, and rockin'.   We had side seats for a concert, which were fairly pricey, though cheaper than some better seats. (130/ticket).  The disappointing thing was the sound. There are speakers pointing at the sides of the auditorium, but didn't seem to be on. We were only hearing an echo off the back wall (I guess).  Couldn't hear anything but the bass (drum and guitar) and hints of the lead.  I walked around back and heard the full amazing sound. Real bummer.
Best band experience I enjoyed on Broadway. The band with pappi on the fiddle made for a great time. Everyone dancing and enjoying themselves. Will gladly return on my next visit to Nashville.
Cheap beer and some of the better live music on Broadway. Happened upon Tin Roof my first night in Nashville and I keep coming back for the fun atmosphere and good music.

What a great little destination for family fun or date night, shopping, beauty parlor, Maz Fresco fresh market with some good looking meat, fish and veggies, singing dancing and restaurants all in a nice save environment.  Worth the wait and it did take a long time coming. Vegas/Epcot feel and all affordable for everyone.

I completely love this venue and have been here probably over 10 times since moving to Nashville in 2010.  This venue is where I attended the open funeral for legendary banjo player Earl Scruggs. I have been two times in March- once to see Tommy Emmanuel, and the second time to see John Prine. The acoustics are awesome, and if you close your eyes it is total paradise on the ears. The only drawback I could even see is if you have a lot of people in your row that are larger and take up more of the pew seat, but I have never had a problem enjoying my time there and the attendees have always been very friendly to me.  The snack bar has gone up a little bit over the years. I enjoy getting the caramel corn- it is 5 bucks a bag... and very filling... but if you think about it... it is reasonable compared to a movie theater... and the value is much higher than a simple movie. I will always cherish this place. I think it is perfectly comfortable and I really like sitting on one of the front rows or in the balcony.  Highly recommend this venue to everyone!! Don't come to Nashville without checking out a show!

Ambiance was great -- music was a tad bit loud, but the band did a good job of playing for 45-60 minutes and then breaking for about 30-45 to give time for both conversation and enjoying some great live music (jazz, soul, etc).

Bill for two entrees, app, dessert, and bottle of wine was $120 plus a tip, which I thought was quite reasonable.  Our dessert was absolutely to die for -- I will return again if only for that dessert.

Definitely a fun place when you need to celebrate and splurge.  Two pay lots right up the street ($5 for 5 hours), and also valet.

It can accommodate groups, but don't plan on being able to have across the table conversations while the music is playing... best for an intimate night with one other person.
Food and service horrible but good vibe in music, and it is pretty chill in here compared to the big boys on Broadway in Nashville

Plaza Mariachi opened about 2 miles from my house and it's now my favorite spot in town! It's such a great option for flexible dining or large groups and a great way to kill a couple hours. Their entertainment program is slammed each week with Mexican Bingo, Salsa Lessons, and much more!

EXCELLENT food. Well balanced, fresh, and full of layered flavor. Yes it's pricey, but worth it. Environment was low key and classy. The wait staff, manager, and host were very friendly and accommodating. The band was fantastic. Happy hour is 4pm - 7pm Monday - Friday during which the drinks are about half the price.   You should make a reservation early even on a Monday.
This was a great place to sit and have a beer and listen to some live music. The food was just ok and the fryer was broken when I visited for lunch. The beers available are of a good range.
It was so nice to see a performance in a smaller venue rather than a stadium. The Ryman is legendary, but the pew seats are sort of uncomfortable and it was very hot for the first half of the night.

Loved the vibe in this place -- quite hopping for a Saturday afternoon in January so we found a place to set our beer and listen to some excellent country tunes --wish I could remember the country singer!!  He was very good.
The best honky tonk in Nashville.   Try the fried bologna sandwich and drink lots of beer while heRing the best western music of all time!
Was in Nashville on business and this place was recommended to us. The food was totally amazing, the service was great, the music was even better. I loved the atmosphere. I will definitely be back!

My favorite spot in Nashville. It's all about old time country and blue grass and the house band (Don Kelley's) is just the best. Between the crazy talented bass player Joe Fink and guitar prodigy Daniel Donato, you are in for an amazing night of fun music. The Don Kelley band is there Monday - Saturday from 6 to 10pm. Be sure to tip these talented guys what you'd pay for a great night of music, because all the bands on Broadway Street only get paid in tips. They'll pass a bucket around regularly and remember to fill it! Oh and be sure to try the fried bologna sammich - it's the best on the planet. YUMMY!
Fun bar lots of good music.. Not a overly crazy crowed.. Which is nice if you just want to sit back and enjoy music and cold beers..

This is actually a fun place. It's pretty small and they had a good band playing which strangely didn't bother me. There's an upstairs which isn't big but you can carry a conversation over there. Tragically I didn't try their food which I know it's what you have to try. I was surprised to the bar and the grill located next to each other. I would recommend this place as one of the bars to go to if you are ever in Nashville.

This place is amazing!! In Nashville from Michigan and we had the best time!! Had the caprese appetizer, crab and shrimp bisque (OMG), the lobster enchiladas, and my friend had the margherita pizza- all were soooo so good. The absolute best part was dessert- cheesecake sopapilla. The best dessert I've had in my entire life!  Not exaggerating! The band was amazing too- The Chris Weaver Band, so great!! Loved the atmosphere of this place too, great decor, classy but not snooty!
We didn't eat .  We came for the music, and it didn't disappoint.  Nathan Belt and the Buckles.  Need I say more?

Nice place to grab a drink & listen to live music. 

There are many bars on Broadway in Nashville, Second Fiddle is one of them. It was not as populated as other bars, say like Honky Tonk and Tootsies but it was fun. Will go there again if I visit Nashville.

Pros:
Music: Nice live bands. Good music.
Crowd: People seemed to be having fun. Not overpopulated like other bars in the area.
Staff: Bartenders and servers were friendly and fast. Don't need to wait long to get your drink(s)!!!
Ambiance: Real cool. Liked the pictures of classic country singers on the wall.

Cons: will tell you when I think of one :P
I hope I get this right -- we walked in on a Saturday in late January and Jake Maurer was playing -- really enjoyed his voice.  Good venue!
Super nette Country-Music Bar mit non-stop Live-Musik. Es gibt günstiges Bier und einfaches Essen. Authentisch und sympathisch!
Very fun bar, good music, multiple levels. Food was better than expected. Our only complaint was the A/C was not working well. Hope they fix that. Otherwise, great fun!

We at 8 pm on a Saturday night. Bar was crowded but managed to find a table. Sweet potato fries were on point! Great authentic Nashville bar feel. Note - there is a back entrance through the alley behind Tootsies.

I wasn't going to get the food but decided to have a mushroom burger while I listened to music. I have to say it was the best burger I have ever had. The band was great. Get there early because it gets really busy.

I really want to like this place because the ambiance (both before and after it's reinvention) is cool and the bands are pretty darn good.  However, both times, the service was slow, the food was just 'eh' and the drinks were like TGI Fridays.  The could get a Jack and Coke just fine, but anything requiring more attention than that came back either too sugary or simply wrong. 
We've thrown a few dinner parties/group gatherings here and it's difficult to keep everyone fed and with a drink in their hand, even when the rest of the restaurant wasn't crowded.  Great location, great atmosphere- but if they revamp the drink list and hire more staff they'll have a real winner.
It was the 2nd fiddle but the 3rd honky tonk we stopped at. Same deal as all the others with some kitschy-er decor.

This place is INCREDIBLE. 

I planned a bachelorette party weekend away in Nashville, and this was the first location I attempted to call a week in advance to make a reservation for eight. Sadly, they said they were booked at the time we needed. So I made a reservation for a different place. The other place fell through so a friend called Sambuca and asked again, and this time they said they had availability! I was really frustrated by the fact that we had been given different information, but my elation at eating here overshadowed it. 

They were so helpful and accommodating. Some of the most friendly service I've had. The waitress talked with us for a good while and provided great recommendations. We were seated on the top floor on the terrace overlooking the city, and it was such a lovely view and a lovely night. They had little candles on the tables and all these couches around the room and really ambient lighting. There was live music in the level beneath us and people were dancing. It was just such a beautiful atmosphere, everyone was so happy.

Prices are high, but the food was worth it. We all got different drinks (around 11 dollars each) - I got the Tennessee Tornado which packed a punch, and was so delicious. My friend and I split a pizza, the name evades me but I know it had goat cheese, italian sausage, and prosciutto. It was AMAZING. And it was only 15 dollars and provided a great meal for two. Many of the girls commented on how amazing the shrimp and crab bisque was, and I also heard the beignets were to die for. 

Overall, this place was top notch. Great location. Great food and drinks. Great service. 
If I go to Nashville again, this is definitely going to be a must go.

I really loved this place!  Robert's Western World is my new favorite bar in Nashville.  Ha!  Not that I have a lot to compare it to but this place was so fun.  It was crowded but not overly so.  The music was fun, live, honky tonk ish stuff!  The decor is very fitting of an older style honky tonk bar. 
I most enjoyed listening to the music and dancing with others in the front.  They also have a short order food menu.  The grilled cheese is pretty tasty, I must say.  

Oh, and it's free!

Go check this gem out if you are in the downtown Nashville area.  :)

CCA Convention was here this week. Great venue, very clean, plenty of restrooms, nice people and easy parking. It's in the middle of downtown, very accessible, with plenty of restaurants in the surrounding area.

No need to wear your best duds. Burgers and fried bologna. 
Can't miss. Western Swingers the bomb. Fun conversations with other tables. We're coming back the first Monday we're back in town. Wednesday night the Don Kelly Band performs. Great musicians lots of fun and terrific customers. You'll be hand clapping and foot stomping and singing along. 
There is no cover charge but about once a hour they pass the tip jug. It is a fair deal. Throw something in so you don't feel guilty.

Stunning. Absolutely incredible. From all of the history involved in each room, the stage, and the back door to Tootsie's in the alley where the Everly Brothers were discovered. The Ryman is a MUST SEE in Nashville. I upgraded to the backstage tour and every moment was worth every single penny. My tour guide, Christopher, was fantastic as well. He had so many fun stories, along with the bragging rights of performing with his band at the Ryman as well. I can't wait to be back in Nashville to do this tour again!!!
One of the old classics.   Nice bartenders with good service even when it's packed.  Great music and classic atmosphere.

This was the first bar on Broadway we ended up hopping into, solely because the music coming out of it was stellar. While this bar doesn't have as much room to dance as others, I felt that each night I visited the music was miles better than anything around - and isn't that the whole point of Nashville? 

Great bar, great music, great atmosphere. One of the top spots on Broadway.
Great atmosphere! Great service despite the noise and sheer quantity of people! I'd definitely recommend this spot on Broadway!

History is there, music is good. Beers are expensive, as is typical of a tourist trap. However, the shortest, bearded doorman has Napoleon complex. Tread lightly on Titans game day when around as a fan of opposing team.

I am so thankful that we have such a nice convention center. The only reason I gave it three stars is because of easy parking. This is the second year that I went to a hair show at this facility. Last year was worse than this year. There are plenty of bathrooms. But 3 hours into the show , they are nasty. It is embarrassing to me because people come from all around to be at this show. And this is what we show them? And I know there is a lot of body heat in 1 big section. But people were walking around fanning themselves. Come on???

I spent several weeks in Nashville recently and stopped by Robert's quite a few times.  They have great music, great burgers and fries.  My only complaint is most of the waitress staff is less than friendly.  None of them seemed like they wanted to be there, let alone get you your next drink.  other than that great place.

Went here last week on a recommendation from our hotel. This place is perfect for a date night out. NO COVER and great live music. Beautiful decor inside , nice and classy.

Menu was easy reading and tasty. Kinda pricey but expected with upscale ambience and free live music.

Drinks were super tasty. I had the Tigers Blood.

Service was great and speedy. I think our waitress's name was Natalie.

Do pass up this spot if you like jazz and good eating.
Rockabilly/country vibe. Place was fun. Beer was cheap.
This is the honky tonk look that you've seen in the movies with the boot wall and all that. I know beer is cheaper in other parts of the city but you have to roll through this at least once.

First fried bologna sandwich ever. Pretty good. The burger was good for the price. The music was fantastic for the price. 

Good crowd. Great musicians. Friendly service! Come for the music and a drink. If you like anything else, it's a bonus.
