My wife and I were so excited on our first night in Nashville but Sambuca truly underdelivered I'm sorry to say.  It's all about perspective right?  My college kids would have loved it.  My foodie wife and I found the entire experience average at best, though our waiter was kind and attentive. Tuna special came out cold, twice.  Hanger steak was comparable to something I could whip up in short order.  Oh well, live and learn.

Roberts Western World! What a place! Cheap beer, friendly staff, and great music. If you get lucky you can catch Dave Cox strumming his many strings. His voice is electric and gets the crowd going. Beer is served in a can just like home, and quite cheap if the wallet is light. Haven't had the food, but the aroma fills the air and keep the mouth watering--that's what the cheap beer is for. Great vibes at Roberts!

Loved loved loved this place! I liked it more than Tootsie's. There's something so charming about this honky tonk that makes it stand out in my mind. Perhaps it's how cheap the food is ($5 Recession special - sandwich, chips, AND PBR - unheard of in Chicago) or maybe how great the music is or how wonderful the service is. I don't know. Something about this place helped to make my Nashville experience!

Try the fried pickles! They're delicious and the best fried pickles I've had (also less than $5?!)

My family and I went here in the forth of July.  Loved the live music.  The band played country and rock covers and added their own flair.  

The chicken and waffles appetizer had a nice presentation but the flavor was a disappointment.  My daughters enjoyed their chicken strips and fries.  My son had a chicken quesadilla with queso dip that he raved about.  The brown sugar and chili dry rub wings were impressive.  The house special spicy chicken sandwich was great.  The food, band, atmosphere and staff made this a great spot to enjoy a lunch in Nashville with the family.
Went there on Sunday morning. Perfect ambiance, relaxed music, great drinks! Will be back!
Fine cheeseburger and sweet potato fries and ice cold beer. Can't get any better than that!!!!!

This place is incredible! It is such a vibrant and entertaining place to go not only just to enjoy some live entertainment but also enjoy really great food too! The prices were very fair and there was a wide assortment of food available. There were even a couple places that served delicious desert foods! We were very impressed with our visit here and we loved the live band performing too! This place is great if you want to just grab something to eat or if you want to shop around. Plaza Mariachi truly brings something unique to Nashville.
There are better places to go, with courteous staff.  Try not to let one employee ruin my view of an establishment, but very poor customer service will do that.
Food is mediocre but the beer selection and great service make up for it. The atmosphere is very fun and great for groups.

Incredible acoustics! I've been to a ton of music venues in Chicago but this was incredible.

I went to the Grand Ole Opry at the Ryman and it was a great show. A bunch of artists went up and sang a few songs. I loved the musical variety - all types of country music went up on that stage.

I definitely recommend stopping by here if you're in Nashville. Catch a show of something if you can!

What a great bar. The band was playing some great Johnny Cash. I am not into country music, but I really did enjoy it. The bartender was great. Reasonable drinks and the food was good. I had the BLT. A definite must when in Nashville

"They say the neon lights are bright on Broadway
They say there's always magic in the air
But when you're walkin' down that street
And you ain't had enough to eat
The glitter rubs right off and you're nowhere"

So the song may be talking about the other Broadway, regardless, the neon lights *are* blinding on this Broadway too. We headed there in hopes of catching some live music at a honky tonk during our stay in Nashville. Figuring we'd end up on Broadway, I bookmarked a few places that interested me. I've gotta say what caught my attention at Robert's was mentions of boots and bologna - a combo you don't see everyday.

Broadway was madness when we arrived; we quickly abandoned our plan to hit Tootsie's and The Stage after seeing the line. Robert's, fortunately, had a very reasonable line around 11 and even better no cover, so we popped in. The bar was crowded, not so much there wasn't breathing room. It wasn't long before we scored seats at the downstairs bar, with the grill in front of us and the boots lined up behind. 

If you're like us, and not country fans (at least not contemporary country), Robert's might be your speed. Robert's bills themselves a traditional country venue; they played some originals, but much of what Nathan Belt & the Buckles played we recognized and liked - covers of Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis, Peggy Lee, Roy Orbison, and Buddy Holly. As an added bonus, Robert's didn't seem as crazy as some of the other bars.

If you're not picky, the best drink deal to be had is $2.50 bottles of PBR, High Life and I think Bud Light. If you're into bologna, which judging by the cook, lots of people are, the fried bologna recession special is for you. It sounded weird and kind of gross to both of us, but after watching a bunch come off the grill, manfriend was quite tempted to try one.

A little divey, but a lot of fun; I'd recommend Robert's if you want to hear some good music, drink and eat on the cheap, and not have to scream or play charades with/at your companions.

I loved this place! It was one of my favorites in Nashville. The bands were pretty decent and fun. I don't understand the complaints about drunk people and shitty music. HELLO! It's a bar! And it's Nashville! No complaints here.

For what this is - essentially a Latin American food court in a Vegas-style atmosphere, this place is top-notch! Don't come here expecting fine dining, fancy wine lists or white table cloths. Rather, dress casually, bring your friends and family, and come hungry! The standout options on this visit were the spicy mixed seafood ceviche, street corn in a cup and cold Dos Equis lager. You have to visit different vendors for different foods, but the potential hassle is avoided by just sitting back and enjoying the varying entertainment at the huge stage at one end of the food court. On our visit , there was a Mariachi band followed by fire breathing dancers. Very family friendly in a creative environment.

Where to take my musician brother-in-law and his wife on their first visit to Nashville.  We researched the music offerings available at venues with more upscale food ( limited) and chose to return to Sambuca for the second time ( been here about 2 years ago).  We were not disappointed!  

We ordered a bottle of wine and some appetizers to start.  The signature calamari was ok, the tuna tartar was very good, the humus -unique as it came with three pots of humus, garlic, roasted red pepper and one that tasted like red beets.  Off to a great start.  The Amancaya Gran Reserve 2011 Malbec/Cab blend was very good and reasonably priced at $50!  Nice to see one we have enjoyed before! 

Since we were full from the appetizers,  hubby and I decided to each get a salad and share the margarita pizza!   The bib and gorgonzola salads were both above average -we got dressings in the side!   Our pizza was generous enough to share and very fresh!  

Brother-in-law and wife shared the red snapper as a main as well as the roasted vegetables-both gave excellent reviews.   The kitchen split the entree for them as well. 

It was a great choice for our evening and we will be back!

Great place for old school country! If you want to dance a little- don't plan on it on Friday or Saturday night! Gail, the bartender, is fabulous! She's on top of things! Shes friendly, attentive and takes great care of her customers! If in Nashville, this is a great place to check out!

Limited menu but I think they do everything well that is on the menu. Ordered a bologna sandwich with fries. Very good! A friend ordered a cheese burger and said it was also delicious. We also had fried pickles which were very good! Service was pretty good also.

Great place to see a show and soak in American history. A few tips: The address says 5th Avenue, but the entrance is on 4th. Park a block or so away and pay $1,  rather than $20 right next to the Ryman. If your seats on on the second floor, odds are you'll be walking up some steep stairs, If you aren't a fan of stairs, go for first floor seats. Seats on the far left or far right do keep you from seeing the entire stage. Peace y'all.

Really enjoyed the dimmed lighting and cozy booths. 

The menu is diverse with something for everyone's tastes.

I had some sort of crab pasta dish and a few glasses of white wine and the whole meal was very delicious. 

The live music was also good. Will definitely be returning.

This was such an awesome place to hear local music. Drinks were cheap, everyone was friendly and the band was really good. I just wish I had enough time during my Nashville trip to come back and try the fried bologna sandwich.

Even in a packed room with only two servers, I felt like the only guy in the room. I wasn't spending like crazy, either. $2.50 beers, fried bologna, live music. This will be my go-to from now on on Broadway. Thank you ladies

Great restaurant! Loved the live music, loved the food and loved the drinks. We also had great service from the waitstaff which was much appreciated. The only thing is it was a bit dark and loud so it was tough to talk or see the other girls in our group but it certainly put us in a good mood for celebrating!

Great staff here and nice place, but banquet catering leaves something to be desired. Chicken in buffet was lukewarm and passed appetizers were odd. One was some type of sliced beef on Melba toast with a pickle relish and wasabi. Tasted good but just seemed cheap. Who uses Melba toast in an appetizer at a nice restaurant? The other was a scoop of Caesar salad in a crispy parmesan cheese cup. Again, tasted good, but seemed odd and cheap. Neither of these felt very sophisticated or upscale--they felt like something someone came up with at home and brought the idea into work.  Their house salad in the buffet was good, as was the salmon over rice.

Although I'm not a country music myself, this place was pretty cool. We took the self guided tour which started off pretty cool. It was this high tech presentation that talked about the history of the building and how it came to be. Pretty neat stuff.
After that we were free to walk around the auditorium and check out the surrounding. Then you have the option to take a photo on stage, it was $20 for like 4 photos. We didn't buy it, but not a bad deal, I guess.

Overall, it is a pretty short tour, unless you are a huge country music fan and want to spend more time. It is a neat experience, plus it's right in the downtown area, so if you are there, check it out. The tour is about $20 a person, no backstage access.

This is a must if you're in Nashville. A true "HonkyTonk" and you won't be disappointed with the live music that generates from this place nearly 24/7 with some of best musicians in town. Oh, and they have beer and booze too !
Stopped in for a couple of beers and to hear live music. Eileen Rose was playing and was awesome!
Total tourist here. Went in around 6 on a Friday and loved the singer and band, as well as the $3 price tag on drafts. Hung around for a half hour before moseying on.
Touristy at night. Better to go during the day. We saw a great country band here. Lots of beer and Marshall tucker. Great place to spend the afternoon.

Been coming to this bar for 5 years now and tonight I had the worst service since I've been coming to Nashville. All three bartenders were very rude and cold when ordering.  If you pay almost 10$ a drink you would think the servers would be friendly. One bartender rolled her eyes when my wife let her know their sprite was out.  Sad I've seen a lot of bars go down hill and close because of bad service.  Hope this one doesn't get to that point.

I'm really glad we checked Yelp as we were coming out of the Country Music Hall of Fame. For cheap eats and great music, this place was perfect at 1pm on a Friday). The bar had a good selection of craft and domestic beers including Lagunitas IPA. I was very happy to see a veggie burger on the menu, and it was good, served with cheese, lettuce, pickles and tomatoes. Frozen commercial crinkle cut fries rounded out my order. The bartender was pleasant although not chatty and remembered lemons for my water.

I am all about getting more for my money, so the recession special is where it's at.  

$5 for fried bologna sandwich (what else would you want after a day on Broadway, anyways?) with chips and a PBR.  Granted, we upgraded to include cheese for another $1 each per sandwich, but it really did make it taste even more delicious.

It's a dive, but for a beer and a bologna sandwich, it's the place to go.
Excellent food.  Excellent drinks.  Excellent live music.  I was very impressed with the entire experience.  Located in the gulch, very modern setting.  I would definitely recommend and come back.

This was a great place - suggested by a local businessman.  We walked in - NO COVER and listened to great music on a Friday night.. Lots of great dancing.  Beer was cold but they did run out of water.
This place is amazing. The history, the sound, everything! And you know what makes it better? Home Free Vocal Band. Or Ashley McBryde. Or Home Free Vocal Band. Did I say that twice? Oh, yes, I did.

What a cool place to see a show!  Just saw Sturgill Simpson here last weekend.  This is an older building/venue with church style (pews) seating.  It's pretty intimate with a small capacity.  Because of that, every seat feels close.  The volume is perfect - not eardrum splitting, but still loud enough that you know you were at a show.  There is a full bar in the lobby area and beer/water stands inside.  16 ounce tall boys (Bud, Lite, Fat Tire Amber and Coors light are $8, bottles water is $4) are nice and cold and served with a friendly smile.  The ushers are helpful and friendly too.  They have a souvenir shop near the entrance with lots of great stuff - shirts, hats, CDs. and all the other trinkets you would expect.  Again, this is a fun spot to see a show.

This is my favorite music joint on the Music Strip.  
I am most happy when I stumble upon any Rock-a-billy band playing there.
With over 160 reviews, no need for Juicy to wax on.

The place is cool, laid back and has a welcoming vibe (if you're cool). 

It's not your cleanest, but not the Dive as some light-weight reviewers would have you believe.  It's a bar people! With live music and no cover charge... you do the math!  As a lover of dive bars, this joint would not rank. 

It's a true-blue Honky-Tonk. It is not a Barrelhouse. 
I usually go between Noon and 8 pm.  I don't like crowds.

Where else can you get a "Recession Special" meal for $5 ??? (see photo)
It's PBR + Fried Bologna Sandwich + your choice of Goo-Goo Cluster or Moon-Pie.

Does life get any better?

Always bet on black.

When given a choice between touring the Johnny Cash Museum and the Ryman Auditorium, go with The Man in Black.

Since I've never caught a show here, I can't rate this as a venue. I've heard the acoustics are amazing, so I'm inclined to believe my rating would be higher. I'm not the churchgoing type, but was looking forward to touring "The Mother Church of Country Music"; unfortunately, it was a letdown.

The Ryman offers two types of tours, self-guided tours for $15 and backstage tours for $20. We opted for the backstage tour, which worked out to around $50 for both of us when you include the stupid service charges. Reserve your spots in advance, tours do sell out and I don't believe they're offered when there are scheduled shows.

We were cutting it close and arrived right on the dot for our tour; it felt like we were late, our tour guide had already done introductions as we walked up to the group quickly pointing and asking where we were from. Maybe our disappointing tour was the result of our guide's style or maybe that's how they all are. 

True to its name, our backstage tour was just that - backstage, for the most part. Aside from the old pictures, nothing in particular makes the dressing rooms stand out as Ryman dressing rooms; after seeing two, we got the picture. Our tour felt rushed and sometimes confusing; our guide talked fast, had my parents been with me that would surely have been an issue. Even more annoying, our guide started talking the minute he starting moving toward our next stop; if you're not right next to him (impossible since most spaces required being single file), you're missing stuff. 

As quickly as our tour began, it ended. I don't think it could've been more than an hour, but our guide noted we were well over the allotted time. It's not clear that it's the intent, but I think it would make sense to do the self-guided tour immediately following the backstage one; since you're already in the theater, you don't have to pay for it. That will expose you to the Ryman video and the timeline of artifacts and historical moments associated with the auditorium.

Bottom line: Beautiful auditorium with a rich history, mediocre tour.

Great location, great sound. Great bands. Smaller venue with big name bands. What more can you ask for. Oh, Christmas lights! they should have up lights for ambiance and decoration:) Love the location. If you want to go out before or after there are tons of places.
Cool auditorium with a nice self-guided tour.  They show you a video at the beginning to give some context, then let you walk around inside on your own.

0 stars! We went on a Friday at 5 just to get a table by the dance floor then to have table and chairs jerked from under us at 6:30 to "make room"  for more drunks instead of quality people. Beware they remove all tables and chairs even chairs from the bar on lower level for night time band! Poor business practice!!

Great atmosphere, good music, decent burger, cheap beer. Burger, fries and 3 beers for $15. Cannot beat that for a place on Broadway. Probably going to start the night there again to get going without breaking the bank.

Of all of the options on Broadway, this is consistently my favorite.  Everything about it is perfect.  No pretense, just fun, great live music, friendly bartenders, cheap and delicious food, all in an incredible party atmosphere.  Get the fried bologna sandwich and a basket of onion rings.  Eat, smile, rinse with a PBR, and repeat.

The venue itself is a ten! I would like to say that your security officers could use a lesson in hospitality. The pudgy, mid forties, brown haired, guy you had working outside this evening was less than desirable and treated the group of people I was with terribly. Instead of asking us to not take photos he flashed his "ego" light vigorously at us with no explanation and upon us asking why it was not allowed he became very hostile and shouted at us. All he had to do was say, "ladies, photography is not allowed". Then again, he's a forty year old security guard- probably used his "aggression" to compensate for his lack of character.
So not worth the money! Atmosphere is nice, but the food is just ok. $35 for a cheap Flat Iron steak is just insulting. You can get much better food for a lot less money.

Spent my 6 year anniversary here at Sambuca. We had a gorgeous view from the skyloft and an amazing dinner. Our waiter Matt was great. He made our special day very memorable. Both the service and the food here are worth it. I do recommend to come in before the dinner rush. I am not sure how service is when it gets busy.

The music was fantastic and the drinks were great! the bar staff was friendly and professional and prompt considering how busy they were. We came to town to celebrate a friend's 40th birthday and this was one of the better places we stopped.
Great food ....great service....great atmosphere!!!   Enough said !!!  Ask for Teresa...she is the bomb !!!

They say when in Nashville ya gotta stop here and try the fried bologna sandwich 
So of course we had to try it yesterday 

It's a cool little place 
We set at the bar ( right after the opened ) 
You can see them make your food right behind the bar 
Service was exceptional ! 
We got the fried bologna sandwich with fries and split it ( had a late lunch date later ) 
Man I had no idea a fried bologna sandwich could be so good !

If you haven't been here. Do yourself a favor and stop in get the bologna sandwich. You won't be disappointed !

My boyfriend and I went to Robert's Western World a Tuesday afternoon in January. It was really quiet but the staff was extremely friendly and there was good music. I got a  cider and a hot dog and they tasted as expected.

Beautiful convention center. My Dad was teaching a class at the Firehouse World conference. We walked around a bit and admired the architecture. Facilities were extremely clean. Awesome location for a conference.
This place is a dump!  Why would any self-respecting musician agree to perform here?  Especially someone of Sting's caliber!  Last time I buy a ticket to come here.

This was a great place to have a beer and listen to some great music.  I think it was the Don Kelly band. They played classic country, a little blues, and a little southern rock.  Very nice bar tender and a good crowd for a Saturday night.   We will definitely come back when in Nashville.
Loving Nashville. Food and drinks...oh and the music...fun place.  Very accommodating for burgers...see why it has a great review

First bar we came to while in Nashville for a very short weekend. It was PACKED on a Friday night and the band was playing a bit of country and some top 40s hits. They were phenomenal. The drinks were reasonable and the service behind the bar was pretty quick considering the amount of people that were tightly squeezed into this small venue.

Definitely preferred this place to Robert's Western World, and would love to come back if I am ever in Nashville again. Just another one of the many gems on Broadway. Yeeehaw!
Great live music atmosphere, chicken tenders and tots were awesome. Fresh chicken, not processed. Fun times.

This place Rocks!!!  What a great venue to see a show. Do yourself a favor and see whatever band is playing.  It won't matter who it is.  You will have an amazing time.

Quick tip:  Buy your tix at the venue to save extra fees.

Quick tip 2: Bring ear plugs.  It can be really loud and they don't sell ear protection.

Quick tip 3: Save your money on the backstage tour.  The one at the Grand Ole Opry is much better.


Rock on Nashville...this place made my trip!
Impressing building , modern , clean , spacious , green roof with bees but i dont feel free inside ...

I am a Nashvillian, and this is my favorite place in Nashville to see a concert. I see a lot of concerts, averaging about 15 - 20 a year at the Ryman alone. The Ryman only seats about 2,300 people, and I love the aspect of seeing huge names at a relatively small venue. I am not a big fan of giant arena shows. The sound is amazing, and the building is full of history. I am not a country music fan (at least not what is called country these days), but I really appreciate all of the historic touches. The bathroom/merch/bar/gift shop area was recently renovated and expanded and looks excellent, and there is so much more room in that area. Anyone who visited previously knows how crowded it could get out there. I haven't tried the new cafe but I have heard good things. Some people complain about the hard pews, but they honestly don't bother me. I am not such of a sitter at shows anyways. You can't find a bad seat anywhere in the balcony, and the only seats on the main floor that I don't like are the back 6 - 7 rows. The balcony will often cut off your view a bit from back there. You definitely should put seeing a show in this venue on your bucket list.

My first concert at the Ryman was John Mayer in 2003 before he was big, and I loved every second of being there. Music has never sounded better or more authentic. My husband and I went on our first date to see Bon Iver here and we return for multiple concerts every year, bringing family and friends to experience this wonderful place. It's my favorite spot in all of Nashville to listen to music.

A National Historic Landmark and Mother Church of Country Music, the Ryman is a Nashville icon. It is such an intimate venue with its church pews and close balcony. There are truly no bad seats! The building itself was a church so it has a kind of aura about it. Couple that with the people that have performed on that stage and it's humbling to stand there. I walked back by after dark and even more stunning in the lights. There is a reason this place is known around the world. It was a great place to see a concert. It really shows you the history of the Grand Ole Opry and what it was and what it meant to people and the building is beautiful. Worth a visit even if you are not a country music fan. Don't leave Nashville without visiting the Mother Church of Country Music!

History Comes Alive
The tour only takes 1 hour, but it is like stepping back in time. The tour starts with a 10 minute historical film. You are then free to roam through the theater/auditorium. If were to come back to Nashville it would be to see a show at this intimate setting. Book your trip to Nashville around a show!

Couldn't wait to get to this place when we arrived in Nashville. Had heard a lot about it and mostly favorable. Only worth 2 stars. Band was great- they're worth 5 stars. Waitress- 1 star- took 15 minutes just to get a drink and acted like we were a huge inconvenience to her. Had a coupon for free fried pickles- that took another 45 minutes- (although they were good when they did finally arrive)Didn't get a bill- waitress just rattled off a number of what we owed- had taken her so long to come back around- we just paid it- figured it out later and she charged us wrong- I'm sure it's not the first time- plenty of other places on Broadway that have good food and much better service.

Roberts is fun little bar with live music of course, good service, plenty of bar stools line the bar and there's a good amount of tables as well. We only had a beer and left but only because there's so many spots to see.

Quintessential Nashville! The real give away is all the locals and older folks who come in here as regulars. I was with a big group on a packed Saturday night; we were in the back and had great service. Music is always good.

I loved this place! It's a classic honky tonk and it was packed when we stopped in on a Monday night. There was a band playing, of course. The service was really great and the food was so cheap! This is where I tried fried pickles for the first time and they were SO GOOD! And only $4.50! It was a fun stop!
Great history and worth the visit.  Get the guided tour for the added stories and insight, look for groupons deals and if not, AAA discount (HOF too)

We visited on a Wednesday night 2 weeks ago.  A super-fun cover band was playing downstairs so we sat down for a beer and appetizer.  Ordered the chicken and waffles app - it was good bar food.  Nothing extraordinary but decent experience all around.

I love the Ryman. It's easy to buy tickets at the box office. They'll let you park in the lot for free to run in and purchase. I like that the Ryman is small. You don't have to arrive early to wait in line and trek 4 miles to your seat. Concessions move quickly and are located on both floors. Bathrooms are big and clean. Seating is comfy and acoustics are great. Everything about seeing a show at the Ryman is convenient and pleasant. I look forward to my next experience there!
Cool venue. The band was really fun. Great prices and they even make it easy to charge your phone at the bar.

Simply fantastic.  In my opinion, the only place on the strip worth visiting for live music and ambiance.  We caught The Western Swingers, and their stage presence was dead-on.  Surgically accurate musicianship and casual, fun-loving showmanship.
Small bar on Beale. Cheeseburger was dynamite. Pork sandwich was a little dry. Love the atmosphere. Live band always playing. Bar servers were very nice.
Since the seats are pews it can get cramped just FYI. Staff was nice and show was good.

This place is in the Gulch section of Nashville and is worth the trip from downtown. The atmosphere is really comfortable and we were lucky enough to have a live band play the night we were there.  The sound is just right where you can hear your friends and enjoy the music without having to scream to them.  We were dressed in shorts and nice tops and fit right in, so I'd say business casual attire is fine.  We sat in one of the side booths and it was perfect to see the stage and room, while still feeling a little private.

The food is fabulous. The menu is really diverse and well priced.  We had the smoked salmon and fried calamari to start and then scallops and red snapper with a side of tater tots.  Everything was delicious. The tater tots were a little bland considering there was dill & havarti cheese in the potato mix...  for drinks, I had the frose which I highly recommend if you like a slushy type drink on the sweet side. 

The dessert menu didn't really jump out at us, but we tried the Creme brûlée which was just ok. The presentation was really nice (same for the apps and dinner plates).

Our server, Natia, was really sweet and informative. She helped with suggested recommendations and didn't rush us in away.

Food-4.5 
Price-4
Atmosphere-4

This place is amazing. $20 gets you a self guided tour, once again this is all that you need to spend, the lady at the ticket window told us to not spend the extra money...Sweet right. As the tour starts you are guided into a movie theater, this part is a great way to start the tour. You are then free to roam around the Ryman. A great step back in time, tons of music, you can get a picture on the stage. Bonus, they even still have concerts in the Ryman. Nice gift shop. This is a must do in Nashville.

We walked in and sat down at a table somewhere between the stage and the bar. There were only a few other people there so quite easy to find a seat...there was a guy on stage singing, he was pretty good but not country. 

The server came to take our orders, when asked what kind of beers they had she didn't know nor did they have a beer list. So after playing the do you have this game we finally found a beer to order. 

We sat and listened to the band for awhile, but when he started singing "Don't Worry Be Happy" we decided it was time to move on.

A few hours later we passed by and the same singer, seemed like better music though, was still playing and the place was packed. Maybe it was just our timing but then again it was getting later and all the bars were filling up.

One of my favorite music venues in Nashville. The house band rocks! (or should I say countrys!)  food not so good, unless you like balony between white bread. Tip the waitstaff, I think they don't get any hourly wage, so depend on you to tip, and I guess the owner becomes even richer that way.
Our first time to Nashville; we headed to Robert's on a recommendation and I'm so glad we did. Music was awesome, staff was nice - we had a really good time here.

This was the first time my husband and I have been here. The show was awesome the acoustics wonderful. We took the guided tour and the history behind the "mother church of country music" was sensational. If you come to Nashville it is a must see.

My friends and I were in Nashville for a weekend bachelorette party, so we visited many bars and restaurants during our stay.  The food at Tin Roof was by far better than any other place we went.  For appetizers, we had the loaded nachos, which were covered in some pulled pork and other goodies.  Delish.  We also had some fried pickles.  They could have had more breading, but still tasted great.  For my main meal I ordered the Pollo del Sol Quesadillas.  MMMMM!!!  It was literally a party in my mouth.  The avocado, queso blanco, and chipotle bbq each stood out with bursts of flavor.  I'm not kidding.  So good!  

On the service side, there were 9 in our party, and our server said she was new to the restaurant.  I couldn't say a bad thing about her.  She was friendly, prompt, and got everything right in our big group.  Such a great experience!
Tried some really good local Bourbon called Old Hickey. To bad it's only sold locally. I would buy this at home. Has a cream/caramel smell and taste.

Had the onion rings at 2:30 this morning and they were awesome! Heartburn has unfortunately set in quite heavy, but was well worth $3.75 after Makers and great music all night, it was a good way to cap off the night.

I am so excited to have finally visited plaza mariachi! It's definitely a cool place and a great experience. There are lots of boutique shops, a hair salon, market, and even an art gallery! The food court is definitely the center of all the activities. We went on a Saturday and walked in to a full on show with arial dancers, jugglers, and a full band. We really enjoyed the show and the atmosphere just enjoying a little slice of Hispanic culture. We tried several of the food places but was slightly disappointed, otherwise this would be a 5 star review. The food was very mediocre and actually priced a bit more than say Mexican food trucks or other restaurants. We had gordidas and quesadillas from the hildago stand, this was probably the most average taste. The carne assada was extremely chewy. Although I did appreciate the three sauces they put out self serve style. The tres gaucho place had more pricier fare, we got some potatoes bravas which actually was the best part of the meal. We also got a side of corn but was very disappointed that for $4 we only got half of corn. We also tried the churros place, but the churros were too over fried and the chocolate sauce was just Hersey's syrup. Lol.

I like to go to Robert's for two main reasons.  First they have super cheap miller high life bottles for downtown.  Secondly they usually have the most talented bands.  Robert's atmosphere is a little more family oriented than a Tooties or the like, but you can still throw back a few.  It's an ideal day drinking honkey tonk for stop number 1.

A legendary venue. We used to joke that you would buy the album of the opening band, only to find upon listening when you got home that they didn't sound nearly as good outside of the Ryman.

If you have any chance to see someone here, do it. You won't regret it.

Friendly folks for sure (Caron is awesome!). The food menu is very very limited. Ordered the chicken fingers with Honey-spicy sauce. The chicken was authentic, but the sauce was pretty water-y. Shots were pretty expensive, but the band was ok.

Will I go here again? You won't have to twist my arm, but I won't twist yours either.

LOVE LOVE LOVE! Must go here for a fancy night out in Nashville. We had reservations for my birthday and they sat us within our reservation time. Everyone that came over to our table wished me a happy birthday which was so sweet. I had the burrata which was SO GOOD. The flavor of the balsamic tomatoes was amazing. I then had the shrimp and crab scampi, which I shared with a friend and I am glad I did because it was super filling. They even split the dish for us which was so nice. My friends all enjoyed their meals, mainly ordered seafood and no complaints. We had the fried cheesecake for dessert which they decorated beautifully for my birthday which was so nice. The best part about the place was the friendly service you received from everyone there. The live music was awesome too and not too loud for dinner. The only negative was the place was super dark and it was really hard to read the menus. My friends are I are all 24-25 years old and I felt like my parents when we had to take out our phones to use the light, but other than that, I had an amazing time and the food was delicious!

Enjoyed a great meal, the live music was great and the speakers throughout the restaurant were mixed perfectly for sound. I sat at the bar and still felt like I had a great seat for live music, good drinks, and the food was fantastic.

I was alone on a business trip. The bouncer actually sold me on coming in! I still wasn't convinced until, while standing near a table, the bartender came out from behind the bar to take my order!!! Amazing!! Band was great! At least as good as next door at tootsies is not better. 

Keep up the fantastic customer service!!! You'll have lines out the door in no time!

The band was great and the food was amazing! It was the perfect night out for a girls weekend away. Our server absolutely went above and beyond for us and was very attentive. He forgot one of the appetizers, and comped it for the table. I will be back if I'm ever in Nashville again!

Sooo I blacked out here
Which means it did it's job, folks.
Good music! (I think)

My favorite music venue in Nashville by far!! The acoustics of the building itself were amazing and it felt like such a personal/intimate experience. The seats are wooden pews but they really weren't bad to sit on. The view was great. The concession stand lines weren't long. The prices for food and beer were not outrageous. I would love to go back in the future!

A really impressive (and huge) facility right in the middle of Nashville's awesomeness.  I went to the Opening Weekend festivities so I haven't been to an actual conference yet, but this place could handle even the largest of events.  MCC is big-time.

Hands-down the best place on Lower Broadway to hear traditional country music. On any given night you will hear great young talent, such as Josh Hedley & Sarah Gayle Meech, along with well-seasoned Nashville session musicians. The beer prices are the best on the strip, the bar food isn't bad either. You are also likely to strike up friendly conversation with many music fans from Europe, Australia & others parts of the world. If you're in Nashville and want to hear the "real" stuff - take in an evening/night at RWW.

Great place on lower broadway. Wandering in at midday on a Saturday to find an entertaining young lad called Lefty Ferguson doing his thing. Very friendly crowd. I found it to be a better daytime place to go rather than nighttime, but I would certainly recommend a visit.

Nice bar with live music. We stumbled upon this new place while exploring downtown Nashville. There was a free Gin Blossoms concert that night as a grand opening. We stood feet from the stage and met some awesome people while waiting for the band. The only downfall was you couldn't get to the bathroom or the bar due to so many  people. This was to be expected with a great band though.

I've come to this venue for multiple events, and multiple times. My favorite event is Wizard World comic con. The hall is huge! Lots of room for vendors and convention visitors. The structure stands on several levels as it was built on a hill and can be a little confusing at first. It's important to note where you are going and ask someone if you get confused. Otherwise, you can wander for a long time in this massive building.
SEC Tourney Weekend and officially THE bar to hang for UK fans! The queso is addictive!

From start to finish, this place was top notch. Had some French Martinis to start, then apps. EVERY dinner was fabulous.  One had the scallop with orzo, another shrimp and crap scampi, the sea bass (OMG), and the salmon. Not one complaint from our table. The service(from Jesse was great) was impeccable and the waiter attentive and entertaining. Don't miss it if you come to Nashville
Just got to Nashville first time down on Broadway went over to the Tin Roof  had the shrimp and a baked beans and it was awesome will have it again

In an oasis of new age country music cover bands and Sysco box food this place may be the only venue reverent enough to claim the title of 'Home of Traditional Country Music'. Burger was what it was suppose to be and the Traditional music was exactly that.

Came here for drinks and the live music and boy did this place deliver.  They had this guy Tyler Gordon with a kickass band who not only do country, but also pop and rock tunes.  Guy played for 3 hours straight without taking a break.   The bartenders were great, attentive and friendly.    The atmosphere is great.. people dancing, having fun.   Great place and right in the heart of things.    Wish I'd had a chance to try some of the food... maybe next time.

My wife and I went on the tour. It was amazing to learn the history of such a historic building. I highly recommend the guided tour. It was worth every penny. Going backstage shows you many things hidden from the public either expected or unexpected. Don't miss the movie they show, it's worth the 5-10 minutes. Note: There are many steep stairs in the Ryman with low ceilings in places. May not be easy for people with mobility issues.

My favorite bar in Nashville. A fun mix of locals and visitors, the bands are awesome and play a great mix of old and new songs, but mostly the classics like Patsy Cline, Johnny Cash and similar. Friendly bar staff, and beers range from $2.50 up, with Fat Tire and similar only $4.50! Cocktails were mixed nicely and very reasonable. I loved the bacon cheeseburger and onion rings, and their special is a 7-piece fried bologna sandwich. Fried pickles are delicious, too, with ranch dressing, of course. Simple food and inexpensive food and drink, but really good food that's affordable. Great bands play for tips, so bring your $5's for the tip jar. I'll be back again soon! Possibly tomorrow! Saturday night can be a different kind if crowd, mostly tourists, but other nights everyone is friendly.

Went to Nashville for the first time on a whim and stopped here based on good reviews. Smells kind of weird when you first walk in, but you don't notice it the longer the night progresses. Took a hot second to get a drink, but it was decently busy and the bartender was real nice. Didn't try the food, but the beer was decently priced. Women's bathroom was clean and tidy, which is always pleasant. The band was entertaining and talented. Not only did the band play, but the fry cook, bartender, and door girl all got up on stage and performed, which was surprisingly awesome as well. I had heard that Nashville was a place where everyone is talented and this proved to be true. Overall, it was a real good time, and I'm glad I got to experience the many talented aspects of Nashville' very popular Broadway street at this place.
Spacious honkey tonk. Live music was great. Drinks were cold. Crowd was fun. There is room for dancing and prices were reasonable.
Great venue for solid country music. I didn't eat anything but we had a great time drinking and listening to music. Hope upstairs is the best bartender !!

We had a private event here and everything was delicious, meats, sausage, pasta, salad, desserts to die for, appetizers, everything was so good and tasty and flavorful. They had a band as well that played all variations of songs from different eras and languages as well and the upstairs had a great view as well as patio to lounge on, overall this was a great spot to enjoy a nice dinner
Great wonderful place to enjoy great drinks, great food, and even better live performance by a band each night. I can't believe it took me so long to come here. Had a great night.

The best place for honky tonk!  Whenever I am in town I make a point to spend time here. I have not had a bad experience yet. From a packed Friday night, to a relaxing afternoon, to some amazing Sunday morning worship, this place showcases some amazing artist.

This place was great!  We went twice on our recent trip to Nashville and the music was phenomenal both times!  Good service in spite of the large crowds.  4 stars just because you're in there for awhile listening to music and it would've been nice to have a snack, but they have only have bags of chips.

Great place! Loved the rockabilly country band they had. Drinks were reasonable, atmosphere was warm and friendly. It was a great place for us out of towners to experience something different. We had a good time. Would recommend to anyone going to Broadway.

Robert's Western World was our first stop in Nashville ahead of our long girls weekend.  At first we were a little unsure about this place, the crowd tends to be a little older, but you MUST look past that because it is a really good time!  We went upstairs (the downstairs was crowded) and managed to sit at a small little bar table.  The bartender was cute, friendly and very attentive.  We all wanted a quick snack so decided to go for the burgers, and they were SO GOOD!!! I love that the burgers are served with a good ol' bag of lays chips. Such a nice touch that I don't see very often.

The bands they have play here are amazing too!  I was jamming out to almost every song that was played, and they definitely knew how to keep the crowd engaged and having a good time.

Stop by Robert's if you want some cheap beer & burgers & good live music!

Fun place!  Great music and the staff is awesome.  The food:  burgers.  Really good burgers.  Don't expect a quiet experience.  This is a place where you will be lucky to find a seat at the bar and enjoy your greasy burger along with some live music.   As far as your options on the strip, this is probably the best.

Went in for lunch, we were only ones in there due to weather. Waiter was super friendly without being overly intrusive. Bisque was delicious, grilled chicken sandwich was good, would have enjoys it more if bread had been toasted.

I've attended Beer, Bourbon, and BBQ a couple of times at this venue.  It's ok, but not my favorite place ever.  It very much has a "warehousey" feel to it...and also smell.  Parking is a little rough, especially since it seems that Nashville has taken to covering many of its downtown meters with red 'no parking' bags.  It was appropriate for this event, but still not my favorite place to hang out.

Perfect lunch spot! Super inexpensive compared to other local restaurants. App, burger, and two beers for under $20!!! I had a burger which was good- it's nothing special but it's delicious! We tried all the apps- none disappointed. Mozz sticks were my fav. $2.50 PBR's and MHL. The staff was super friends and accommodating for our large group. I will definitely return!
Amazing food really nice service service loud music and active crowd! Country my favorite!!! Nice place and friendly staff! I'm from Michigan and I loved this place!!!!!!!    :-)

Well, I'm reviewing the tour of the Ryman, not a concert in the Ryman, so if you want to keep reading, feel free...

I was in Nashville for the first time in April, and knew I had to visit The Grand Ole Opry, The Ryman, and The Bluebird Cafe (yep, I watch Nashville on tv!). After touring the Opry we next visited The Ryman and got the backstage tour. It was worth the extra money, but the tour wasn't as great as the Opry tour. Probably because the venue is just so much older smaller - I think if I had it do over again I'd do The Ryman first, then The Opry. 

At any rate, this is the home of Country music and the tour helps explain all of that. From the radio shows to the live concerts, The Ryman is the 'Mother Church' that gave so many young musicians a venue to share their music (Little Jimmy Dickens, Minnie Pearl, Johnny Cash, Elvis, etc.). It is pretty inspiring to stand on the stage they all performed on, to walk through the dressing rooms they used, to feel (just for a moment) what it must have felt like to be them.

I would definitely recommend this tour to any music fan - country or not. The history is far too rich to pass up, and it is right in the heart of downtown Nashville - just off Broadway.

I tend to avoid downtown but if i have friends in town that insist on going to Broadway this is one of the few venues we will be sure to take them by. Realize what your getting... It is a honky tonk for tourists. you will see some locals, like me they are usually entertaining guests. It will likely be crowded. Dancing is limited, although late night when it thins out a bit and the stragglers are well and truly drunk you can see some interesting "two stepping" attempts. Beer and booze prices are in-line with downtown and the service is usually surprisingly good.

Saturday brunch favorite Sambuca did not disappoint. The live music by Garcia and Scott, coffee alcoholic drinks and the shrimp and grits made this a brunch favorite. I like to bring guests to Sambuca because of the ambiance and great drinks but I brought a date to Sambuca for brunch and that was a sure way to win mega points. So save this one for a good date spot. Our waiter was phenomenal and took the time to explain the menu. We ordered shrimp and grits and chicken and waffles. The shrimp and grits were spicy and the sauce had layers of flavor. The grits were whipped and creamy with little pieces of sausage mixed in. The chicken and waffles were huge! The chicken was juicy and covered in gravy that is homemade goodness. The waffle has the right mix of fluff and crisp edges to make this a masterpiece. The live music was lively and they engaged the crowd with commentary and original songs. Five stars for the service, food and the talent on stage. I'll be back!
Great tour! Must see in Nashville. Our tour guide Kylie was very knowledgable and had great energy!

I personally dig Sambuca, but I agree with others in the sense they are a bit expensive, which is why I only go for happy hour. 

I had the chicken samosas and the shrimp and crab dip. The samosas were terrible, I mean whoever even came up with that recipe needs to be slapped. They were drenched in grease and had some wierd cheese mixture on the inside. But the shrimp and crab dip, now that was delicious. Now I know what Im going to order next time. 

The drinks are expensive but very good. 
My only disappointment was the fact that despite most of the patio area being empty, only one teeny tiny area was available for happy hour dining. Whats up with that?

In the first place this bar has a really cool name, my name is Robert so I could be bias but it what it is. This place rocks man, one of the better bars on the tourisy Broadway strip of honky tonks and bright lights. If you are Nashville you must come to this legendary bar its awesome baby.

We loved the Ryman!  We paid extra for the backstage tour, which was basically a tour of the rooms and stories about the pictures.  You couldn't take pictures, which was a bummer, but this is the only way you can see backstage which is absolutely worth it.  The tour itself paled in comparison to the one we got at the Grand Ole Opry, but the building is just awe-inspiring. 

You can imagine the women and men sitting, fanning themselves and unfolding dinners as they watched the early shows, and hear the laughter and cheers resonating in the wooden pews.  This place is a treasure.
Love this place, one of the oldest honky tonks on Broadway is that hey have a dance floor. So, if you love good, live country music and want to dance, this is the place to be.

Now I know why those boots are made for walking because that's all you're going to do in this place. It is huge complex that takes up over 1 city block.

I was here for a work convention for work. The backdrop and architecture and interiors are clean and aesthetically pleasing but the food is terrible. Perhaps they have a price variation and it was my job that ordered on budget or there is only one quality of food option. Either way the food was miserable so in conclusion looks great but go eat at a regular restaurant after you're done with your work event

Great great place!!! Came in for some music, appetizers, and drinks.  Did not disappoint!  
The live band was great.  We ordered popcorn shrimp that was tasty, the chicken and waffles was sweet but good, and the nachos were my favorite. We ordered beer and I had jack n coke... Let me tell you, my drinks were stiff and tasty .  This place is definitely a good time.

I've had nothing but positive experiences at this place. I'm not a huge fan of contemporary country pop, so it's great to find a place on Broadway that gives a nod to more traditional, country swing music. I've been during the day when there was hardly anyone there and had a fine time chatting with patrons and the bartender. I've been at night when it was packed and the whole place was rockin' with high-spirited locals and tourists alike. I love the range of people and ages Robert's attracts and the fun Southern atmosphere it exudes.

Gotta check this place out for the best talent in music in town! One of my favorite places on broadway!
I rate this place on the top of my list because of the entertainment. Seating is limited. It had great fried foods when you've been drinking!

Had the best time here last night! Awesome live music, great divey scene, friendly staff, and a gem on the Broadway strip. Stopped in on a music crawl and we never left. I'll absolutely be back next time I'm in town.

Interesting bit of history. Nothing terribly exciting to a non-country crowd. The intro video was informative and would have satisfied my curiosity (without spending too much time here). Pricey, considering it is about as expensive as the Hermitage. We were done in about an hour. Not a good place for rambunctious young ones at all.

Phenomenal first experience at a honky-tonk.  Service was decent, but tough to get the bartender's attention or a table.  It was all worth it though; their regular Monday night country swing band was great.  We also loved the recession special (fried baloney sandwich, Lays chips, and a PBR to wash it down).   We tried the fried pickles and hot dogs as well.  As a true inner city kid, I wasn't sure how I'd fit in however, I think I've found a new niche!

Really enjoyed all the Honky Tonks on Broadway.  Legends is on the corner and seemed to be less busy than some others.  There is also a side entrance that seemed fast. 

Music is country of course - but a little bit more rock and roll - at least the weekend we were there.

Got snow delayed traveling home and ended up wandering into this place because it seemed lively despite the city being pretty much closed. 

Beer was cold, music was fantastic and service had a smile. What more can you ask for?
Great live music and local beer! Not too crowded either! Perfect spot to get started on a Friday night!

If what you are looking for is a straight up honky tonk on Broadway, this is your place. Entertainment is twangy goodness. Fried bologna sandwich special was an exceptional deal and good when trying to absorb a bunch of liquor.

We were told that this place you can buy a pair of boots and listening to some music. Well we had the music, booze and food but no boots. It was a fun place to hang out, the singer was in his 80's and was very entertaining. They had typical bar food, drinks were decent but no table service. You have to order at the bar.

This place is brand new. I think this they have had less than 10 conf here. Very nice. Big, clean and the staff is very nice. Our conf had about 800 people and you could not tell. Easy in and out. Hope i get to go back. Its the new standard in Nashville.

Oh my gosh! Such a fun honky-tonk. We stopped in for beer, music and lunch (in that order) and OF COURSE ordered the Recession Special: A fried bologna sandwich, chips and a PBR. This was literally the best fried bologna I've ever had - I know it's been years since I've had bologna, let alone had it fried but there are simply some things you just don't forget.

Like I'm not going to forget that for just $5 I had a great lunch and listened to a great local singer's gig. Sit at the bar for a good view and plenty of attention from the staff.

This place is legit.  If you want to hear good honky-tonk and the classic country hits instead of the top 40 leanings- you have to come down to Roberts.  

The place just oozes vibe and I can imagine the greats spirits lingering in a place like this.  There's beer on the floor, half-empty in the hands and folks feel comfortable enough to let it rip on the dance floor.

I witnessed two great and I mean talented bands on two separate nights.  Wonderful renditions of the classics that I personally love.  History keeps rolling with every drum fill, guitar lick and song sung at Roberts.
A bit overpriced, and in our party all of the proteins were highly overlooked. That said, the service was good, drinks were decent, and the food was pretty good. Great atmosphere and music.

Let me start by saying my meal was delicious, but my family didn't have the same experience. First off, our server gets to our table by saying we're out of a lot of things. Not a way to start your meal at a fine dining place. 
 We both ordered filets and mine was medium and my aunt was medium well. Mine was more well done than hers and it was supposed to be less cooked. They had to recook her steak longer, and her Brussel sprouts weren't good, so she ordered spinach instead. They ended up charging her for spinach which I think was pretty distasteful especially since THEY messed up her meal. Who does that? For dinner we ordered the berry cobbler which is supposed to come with ice cream. Half the reason you order it. It came out without ice cream (non of which our server forewarned us about) and they were out of ice cream. Had we known we would have ordered a different dessert. How do you not tell your customer that? Lastly, the bathrooms were DISGUSTING. I went in a couple times and there was water all over the counter. The toilet paper was never in the holding or it was sitting on the ground with toilet paper all over. Personally, a gross bathroom at a steak house speaks volumes and is awful. It should have been well kept. Overall, the place is beautiful and the music is fantastic and the food is tasty, but for a fine dining experience what did they do to keep me as a customer? Not the best.

i whent there last night. I've always had a decent time however last night was different. The band publicly harassed my friend for not tipping him. I approached an employee and explained what had happened, not expecting any recourse however, i would have appreciated some kind of apology. To my shock, he stood up for the band. Haha the funny thing is, there wasn't anyone it the bar. I explained that if they stopped publicly harassing their customers they may actually have a business. Im definitely not going there again and by the looks of the crowed, it seems other people have made the same choice. There are a lot of other bars on the ship that will show you a good time and appreciate you as a customer.

Packed almost every night and if you get in you'll understand why.  
Go early and have a kicking hamburger. Go late and listen to any one of the bands.
Best country music spot in town. Good music every night. Food is ok but, the music is great.

Had dinner with a friend on 02/05/13 and enjoyed it.  I had the flat iron steak with a Caesar's salad and it was tasty and a good portion.  The service was not spectacular, but the jazz band was pretty good and not too loud.  It was pleasant in it not being too busy as well.

Similar to Roberts...tight, good beer and good bands.  Place was rocking.
We'd go back!

Great time we'd. July 3  2013 in the afternoon one of the best Acts on the strip ... An afternoon of great talent and a cold beer or 2  great female singer with a great as well as comic guitar player ( he had us chuckling a few times) .. Drummer good voice great chops .. Unfortunately having sound issues but the bass player worked through it to give all a great show... Add the fact the server was very attractive young lady right on the ball with our drinks... We did the bar crawl Sat,Sun, wed afternoon and saw some great acts but this had to be the best highlight of the week for us ...Legends will be on our favourite list on our next visit...  Recommended to add to your stops ..

Sooo Sambuca, where do I start.The staff was super friendly, helpful and nice.You have to make sure you make reservations for this place, we came a hour late because of traffic but they were extremely helpful and was able to seat us, they wanted to make sure they took care of us because it was our anniversary. I didn't know my husband  had called ahead time and requested a bottle of champagne we didn't get it, we supposed to be in the balcony viewing the stage that didn't happen, the dessert he requested wasn't right(he wanted them to replicate our chocolate cake). The food was ok nothing to right Home about, it wasn't really season as well. My husband was really disappointed and because of that his night was ruined and because I didn't know these things until later now I'm disappointed.
Love this place!!  always my first stop when I'm in Nashville. Great atmosphere, nice people and good music.

Great atmosphere off the beaten path in Nashville. We went with a larger group and sat right next to the stage, but everywhere in the place has a good view of the band. Great service - friendly staff & most importantly, delicious food! I would definitely return for the champagne chicken. :)

There was a 70's band playing last night which was fantastic. The appetizers were delicious- buca beignets being our fave. The filet was cooked perfectly and the berry cobbler was oh so nice- the ideal bite to end the evening. We'll definitely be back.
Coldest cheapest drinks in Nashville! Nicest servers! Just go you will love it the Sammie's are interesting!

This is a nicely laid out bar, plenty of room inside, nice and clean, wee decorated. The service was good and the bands are great. This one was a bit less crowded than some of the others on the street.

Love their food!!! The atmosphere is so fun!! The only problem is that if you're on a date, you can't really have a conversation Bc you can't hear anything but the loud music! When it's warm, we love sitting outside! It's our favorite spot for date night!

Awesome restaurant, awesome band, awesome environment! Our waiter perfectly spaced out our wine, appetizers, and entres. Everyone was very nice and the music is the right volume. The food is a little pricy, but overall I do not have any complaints. Make sure to get a booth; it makes the experience much better...hope this helps.

Great experience On a Tuesday night ! Awesome music, awesome vibe! Definitely a lot of tourists! Bar prices are typical I guess, I'm not a fan of paying $6 for a beer, but the bartenders were super friendly! Overall great crowd and the band was AMAZING!

We went on the tour and it was my favorite thing I experienced in Nashville. So interesting to learn the history and see all the memorabilia from the stars I loved growing up and newer artists. I would love to be able to see a concert here next.

We had a nice time at Sambuca for my best friend's bachelorette weekend. For 9 girls, they sat us in a great table next to the balcony, overlooking the stage. The music was really fun and  a nice added bonus to the dinner. The food was really tasty. Our only issue is that we waited forever for the entrees- about an hour after our appetizers. The kitchen obviously did not time out their large parties appropriately and the kitchen was backed up. But they were apologetic and offered us dessert on the house. Would recommend!

There is nothing not to love about "The Mother Church of Country Music" As a true fan of country music I am still in awe of this place after my third visit. 

One of Marty's guests, Dale Jett, a relative of the Carter family, absolutly brought the house down IMHO singing the Classic Carter Family song, "Will You Miss me when I'm Gone". This old guy cried his eyes out listening to every word of that song. 

Oh yea, that Stapleton guy was pretty good as well . ;)

Amazing chefs combine surprising yet scrumptious flavor combinations! My absolute favorite restaurant! The gourmet food is served at incredibly reasonable prices! If I could give a "10" I would!! Ask for Maxfield he is an awesomely attentive server!! My brother thought he was eating his ahi tuna in Japan! Now that's doe gooood food!!!

BLUF: Friendly staff, good music, not a bad place to hang out.

I spent a day wandering around downtown Nashville and ended up spending a good deal of that time at Tin Roof. I came in around 11 to hear Kevin and Luk play (I'd never heard of them prior to this). Despite a little bit of construction work being done on a new stage at the front of the restaurant, they weren't hard to hear at all. They played well and were more than willing to take any requests anyone could throw at them. Unfortunately for them, I was the only one there for the first couple hours and I couldn't think of a single song to ask for, so they were stuck trying to come up with more ideas themselves. 

After just sitting and enjoying the music for a bit, I decided to order some lunch. I had the Rodeo Burger and fries. Everything was good, but nothing to write home about. If you're at Tin Roof for a show it's worth getting something to eat, but it's not a place I'd tell someone to go specifically for their food. 

At around 2:30, I got up and left (Kevin and Luk were still playing, though by this time there were plenty of other customers to hear them) to wander Nashville for a bit. Despite how long I'd been just sitting around with nothing but my water, none of the staff ever seemed impatient or unpleasant with me (probably partially because they weren't particularly busy), which played a large role in why I decided to return later that same day.

I returned around 4:30 to hear the Lower Broadway Band and take advantage of Happy Hour. I don't recall exactly what the discount was, but I know drafts were all cheaper, so I had an Angry Orchard Crisp Apple and a Little Harpeth Brewing Chicken Scratch. I think I paid about $4 each for those, not sure what the normal price is. The bartenders I interacted with were all helpful and quick to offer me another drink when they noticed me finishing up mine, despite the place being packed and extremely loud at that point. After finishing my drinks, I headed out to get dinner elsewhere rather than eat a second meal there.
Nice little divey honkey tonk. Nothing fancy here. Just basic food done right and good music for a good price.
Saw Wrable, Andy Grammer and Gavjn Degraw concert last night at the Ryman.  It was awesome!!!!!  Great seats, cool place, amazing show!!!

How can one simply review the Mother Church? The history here is rich and the sound, flawless. Highly recommend catching a show here and having a good look around. Also, buy a limited Hatch Show Print upstairs!

If you venture into the 'honky tonk' district, and nudge your way through the tourists downtown, then you may find yourself near Robert's Western World.  Here's the deal, most of the nearby honky tonks are pretty miserable for people who really are into music.  I've heard enough fake southern accents from performers in downtown Nashville to turn Hank Williams Sr over in his grave.  Robert's is the rare exception.  The few times I've been here it was crowded with people of all ages, but somehow it didn't seem that hard to get a drink.  The 3-4 different artists Ive heard play here ranged from 'pretty damned talented' to 'holy hell, that guy's about to go viral'.  
  If you don't really give a damn about good music, then there are plenty of downtown options for you and your group of tanked up knucklerumblers.  But if you want to take a chance on hearing that rare performance from someone before they make it really big, the Robert's is your best bet on Broadway.

Easily the best music venue in town, one of the best in the world.  The acoustics are incredible, and the history in this venue is unbelievable.  Do yourself a favor and get there early to take a walk around if you've never been before.  Only complaint is that the seats are pretty uncomfortable, but that's just part of the experience.  10/10 would recommend seeing a show at the Ryman.

The food was good and our waiter was lovely, but those were the only redeeming parts of our experience at Sinema.

Dinner took almost three hours and the manager seemed unwilling to accept any blame, and only came over to apologize to us after we asked for him. Drinks were extremely overpriced (seriously, $12 for a rail drink?) and dinner wasn't exactly affordable either. The main dining room was extremely dark and the place was practically empty on a Saturday night (not a great sign). There are way better places to spend your money.

Ghost  brothers of Darkland County by Stephen King and music by John Cougar Mellencamp..it was AWESOME!!!!
First of all the seats were FREE...normally $75 each but thanks to AEG and Yelp.. we were able to attend for free...AWESOME!!! Tony and I had never been here before for a live show so it was truly amazing to sit there and imagine the many glorious stars that graced that stage..the likes of Loretta Lynn, Patsy Cline, Kitty Wells, George Jones, Porter Waggner, Dolly Parton, Lester Flatts and Earl Scuggs..just to name a few..I grew up watching the Grand Ole Opry and the Hee Haw show ...like many others...and it was just an overwhelming feeling sitting there in the front in the INNER CIRCLE!!!
We had Section 3 Row G seats 11 and 12....Amazing Amazing Amazing...is all I can say..

The show was amazing. I can't wait to go back there again!!!

One of the worst experiences of scheduling a group company outing for a tour of the Ryman. I had to call about 3 times to finally get confirmation that they had availability of the dates and times.   The girl said she would get back to me but never would (should have been a pretty good signal at that point).  Secondly after she finally confirmed after about 2 weeks, she wanted my credit card information immediately, with little consideration that I was currently traveling and in the airport.  But the last piece that broke the straw, and I absolutely hate to put such a negative review in for such a signature place in Nashville. I have lived in Nashville for over 30 years and love my town, but the Ryman called me with less than 48 hours notice that they were canceling our tour, it left me speechless!!!  Evidently someone came in and threw a bunch of money at them to hold a private event so my 20 person group that I had scheduled out weeks in advance was left high and dry.  I just hope this is not an overall indication of how landmarks are treating their customers or we won't have to worry about the growth we have seen in our city the last couple of years!   I would not recommend scheduling anything with these folks!!!  Buyer Beware.

A group of 8 girls on a bachelorette party landed here on a Friday night for dinner and it was one of the best foodie decisions of the weekend!  IT is a perfect place for a date night or with a large group.  I started with the beet salad then I had the shrimp brochette and Brussel sprouts--amazing flavor!  I ate every crumb off of my plates and got to taste some of the of the fish and steak. Everything was cooked to perfection!  Also, I loved the idea of having the band in the restaurant. The atmosphere is so much fun, but you are still able to chat with your friends and have a delicious meal.  Will be going back!
Bands on both Friday and Saturday night were mediocre at best...Crowded and no room to even walk

This is the first bar my husband and I went into on our first, but not last, visit to Nashville. Mike Silas and his Short Notice band were playing old George Strait, the walls were lined with old records from famous artists, and I knew then and there that my heart will always belong in Nashville.

Ok....I was invited to sambuca for a surprise anniversary party which was amazing I have been previously before and it was just as a amazing so you can't got wrong with this restaurant the live band is nice and the restaurant itself is very intimate once I got there I felt a little out of place with everyone having a significant other but I made it work...I ordered the Blackened red snapper etouffee which was delicious and some wine which was great as well our server was very knowledgeable about the menu and very attentive to everyone needs we sat upstairs in the balcony where you can look over the stage it was really nice this is a good place for a perfect date night and enjoy some good music .

Went here for dinner, drinks, and a live band with my boss and supervisor after work. We got to sit on the main floor in front of the live band and enjoyed a great cover band of country music. Still surprised most of these musicians in downtown live off of tips, so please tip them well. 

Now on to the food and drinks that we ordered. I had the local brewery's beer, Yazhoo Hop IPA, which was a good craft beer that I've had in the past. But please note that all the beers served here are in bottles. NO DRAFT BEER. Not a big minus but I do prefer draft over bottle. The price of the beer was also good for bottle beer, ranging from $4 to $6.50

The food menu was very short and simple but good selections of western traditional food. My supervisor got the burger, which he noted was really great. And my boss and I ordered the fried bologna with cheese. Wow! was it great. The guest who's table we took after they paid, made the recommendation to order this sandwich and glad we listened to them. In order to have a reference of what this sandwich would taste like think of a grilled cheese with bologna or ham. It was a really great blend of flavor. For the three of us with two beers each we paid only $30. Order this and enjoy!
Love this place! Great music and drinks! Will definitely be back. John Karl sang while we were there. He was awesome!

One of our many stops on our bar crawl through downtown Nashville. We walked in, not too busy. Live music (of course) on stage. We happened to be lucky enough to get there when Buck McCoy was playing (he's a dead ringer for Tim McGraw). He was fun to watch, sang good songs and engaged the audience quite well.

Service good, but had to go to the bar to order our drinks. They had the local Yazoo brew and it was cold, so another big plus! This was one of our favorites on our bar tour. Would've loved to come back again when Buck McCoy is playing again.

This was a unique experience. If you're looking for a casual, cheap place to go, this works. I dont mind the cheap cups (that adds to the uniqueness) but bad service is an issue. We got our drinks and didn't see the waitress for 15 minutes. We finally walked over to another and she helped us from there. Food was only ok. Loud country music, which would be cool in the right group.

Appetizers: 
- Smoked Salmon
- Shrimp & Crab Dip

Entree: 
- Sea Bass

Dessert:
- Cheesecake

One of the best meals I've had.  Couldn't stop eating.  The music was a nice backdrop to the meal.  One of the more expensive places that I've been, but certainly worth a visit.  I visited on a business trip, so I got my money's worth!
Awesome atmosphere here!  The band was amazing and the drinks were delicious!  I will definitely go back next time I am in the area!

Food is a bit pricey for what you get, but the ambience and live music make up for it. I had a very enjoyable time. Ordered the beignets (wow! what a contrast in taste and I forgot they were filled by the time they arrived), the crab dip (awesome), and 2 other appetizers that I can't remember now. For entrees, I got the sea bass, while my friend got the chili scallops. Both were quite delicious, although the portions were smaller than expected.

First time in a long time I ate at Sambucca. It hast changed much which is both good and not so good.  I had the scallops which were good not great.  I did like the artichoke app we had but not so much the lobster app. Our server was really good considering there was 8 of us.  He stayed on top of the drinks and was there when you needed him.

I ordered the brisket and shroom quesadilla.  I opened it and this is what I found .  Where's the beef? Very disappointing.  My sister ordered the chicken  quesadilla it was not much of an  improvement but it did at least have a few tiny pieces of chicken  in it but it was also pretty pathetic. The waitress did comp the bill but for just mine but  I would of rather had what I  ordered.  Im a local and don't think I'll be back to eat there but the band was good. To many other options on Broadway.

It's clean and nice enough, but WAY overpriced. Get over yourselves. As a statistic test sample I bought 7 Dewars White Scotch and this one was $11! 

By far the highest, and the environment was just ok. Go to Tootsies or Crazy Town. Much better prices. Get over yourself Tin Roof
Music is great here. Friendly staff. You have to get a cheap beer and soak in your surroundings. I really enjoy their fried pickles. They're the spears, which I prefer.

Food was great especially the stuffed artichokes. Sat at the bar and the hot blonde behind there served me well!!!! She's great at her job and works hard!!! I will be back just to have some water maybe!!! Great place

I have now experienced the Ryman as a concert venue and as a tourist attraction and it is amazing as both.  The tour of the Ryman was truly remarkable; I had no idea how much  history this relatively small building housed.  The sheer number of famous people who have stood on that stage is mind-boggling: presidents, orators, musicians, entertainers of several eras and genres have graced that unique stage.  Even the introductory video is not your average tourist attraction video.  The way that it was done was distinctive and entertaining.  I don't want to spoil the surprise, so you should go see for yourself.  If you want the backstage tour, call ahead and make sure there are no performances scheduled for the day you want to tour the Ryman.  If there is a performance scheduled, you will not be permitted to tour the back stage area so check ahead if that is something that you really want to do.

As a concert venue, it is an intimate set up with great acoustics.  I can stand a little discomfort for such an awesome venue (hard, wooden pews, anyone?),  but  the Ryman's  acoustics can be a huge disadvantage: I missed great chunks of the performance I went to see because I couldn't hear the music over the din of talking and whispering, combined with the shushing from fans who actually wanted to HEAR the music (and no, I do not shush). 

All that being said, the Ryman is a wonderful Nashville attraction that should not be missed whether you are a country music fan or not.

Average bar venue, with entertainment,  to get a "quick" (*see below), bite to eat for lunch downtown. Busy place, nothing fancy, nothing real special. Seating on bar stools at small tables, or at the bar. Their fried bologna sandwich is their signature. They were training a new cook, and it took almost 45 minutes to get our food. This may not be the place to go, if you are in a rush! Or I just caught them on a "bad day."
We are visint from jackaonville and popped by for a drink, totally affordable and GREAT live music! Happy hour deals are great and will be back in the future!

Great food and service but pricey. Buca Beignets are amazing (had 2 orders with a group) as was the Pizza. But was surprised for a Saturday night the band ended at 10PM. Overall not bad Nashville...not bad.
