This music is what we came to Nashville to hear!  John England and the Western Swingers were playing. Oh my gosh, what a great group. This place is the real deal.
Food wise - okay. We had chicken strips and onion rings. The O rings were great, chicken strips were okay. We did not come for the food, but it was okay. The music was awesome!
What a great venue! We really enjoyed it. Don't think there is a bad seat in the house.  Staff was very friendly and helpful.

Ended up here while in Nashville.  We ordered the lobster on the menu and the pork chop.  The lobster plate was "just okay" but I can't say the same for the pork chop.  I ordered the chop  rare but got it well done...horrible.  So well that while using the steak knife trying to grab bites I jiggled the table spilled a bit of our lovely drinks. 
Aside from that, it was a great atmosphere, the drinks were on point and the music was awesome.  
Do plan to revisit bit will skip dinner.

This is one of my favorite bars on Broadway. Came here last night for the first time in a lonnnng time and was reminded why I love this place so much. Great music, two story bar (which is awesome and you don't feel trapped like a sardine), and awesome drinks! We popped in and were all able to order our drinks in a timely manner, which was surprising because it was a busy Saturday night. Beer is super cheap and overall, a really fun place to come with visitors and friends!

Visiting the "Mother Church Of Country Music" was a must for me on my to-do list while in Nashville. That said,  it was definitely fun to see all of the back stage dressing rooms where legendary artists like Dolly Parton, Elvis, Johnny Cash spent their time getting ready before the show, having the opportunity to take a picture on the stage (which came at an extra fee I might add) but it was certainly not the highlight of my trip. Fun? Yes. Rich in history? Sure. 

I suggest you visit the Ryman to watch a show and get a real Country experience rather than touring the place. 

$20 admission.
Music was  great and crowd was fun. Get the loaded tots! I also had the Pickers blueberry which was like a pie without the crust. No crust means less calories!
Robert's was a blast! Fun live music and an amazing fried bologna sandwich. We have never heard of a fried bologna sandwich but we would come back just for that! Good mozzarella sticks too.

This is my favorite spot on Broadway. 
Best music and friendly staff.  First time to Nashville and Robert's band was the best !

Mixed feelings about this one. Great entertainer- had a more fun approach to his singing than most of the bands on Broadway. Nice atmosphere. Food was very slow. We ordered onion rings and chicken strips and it took a while which was disappointing. They were hot when we got em though! Only had one or two cooks so I get it but unfortunately we stepped in to Robert's for something fast. Our mistake. But like I said, fun atmosphere
Hot damn! This place is so action packed! Great food, uplifting music, and entertainment everywhere! Must check this out. Something for everyone!

Stoped in for some quick dinner on a Thursday night. There was a nice jazz duo on the stage and the drinks and steak were above average but nothing to write home about.. especially with so many other great options in the gulch area.

I can see this as a good spot to catch a drink later in the evening but would definitely prefer one of the other hip options in the area.

While this is iconic venue, it is no place for a person in a wheelchair. The staff treated us like we were a bother rather than a guest. The aisles were too narrow for my wheelchair to get through, these oils would be too narrow for some children wheel chair to get through. I have seen my first and last show at the Ryman Auditorium.

I toured the Ryman about a month ago and it was very informative! Last night I went to my first concert there to see Bryan Adams bare bones show. The venue is amazing and the acoustics are second to none! Will definitely try to see another show there in the future!

Located steps from the famed Ryman Auditorium, Robert's Western World is the quintessential Honky Tonk where many up and coming Country Music stars have cut their teeth, Upon a recent visit, I had the privilege of watching studio musicians jamming to some classic country numbers - some of which they actually played on during the original recordings. A highlight of the evening was witnessing one of Elvis's background singers step on to stage and sing a rendition of Suspicious Minds which elevated the already high level of quality music. Check Robert's Western World out on the Broadway strip for good beer, good people and great music!

Ja var börjar man sin beskrivning angående denna legendariska konsertlokal. Kort är det i den här f.d. kyrkan som country musiken utvecklades och frodades under flera decennier (då Grand Ole Opry höll till här).

Alla klassiska country artister som hade karriärer under 40-50-60-70 talen har spelat här och oftast själva varit begaistrade av det faktum att de platsade att beträda denna anrika scen. Om man tilläts framträda här, så var oftast en country musik artists lycka gjord. Ett bevis på att du och din musik var accepterade, beundrade och älskad.

Men något regelrätt museum har det lyckligtvis inte omvandlats till och att leva på gamla meriter duger som bekant inte i dessa dagar. Så desto mer glädjande att man fortfarande har världsartist bokade här. Akustiken och intimiteten är rena lyckan för både artister och vi i publiken.

Om du har möjligheten så se gärna en live konsert här. Annars kan man besöka under dagtid och bara gå runt och se både de underbara lokalerna och diverse montrar med historiska material. Möjlighet finns även att få en guidad rundtur i logerna bakom scenen och själv få stå på den klassiska scenen och låta sig fotograferas bakom mikrofonen (de lånade t.o.m. ut en gitarr till mig för det ändamålet).

En original bar - det er her legenderne opdages, en fantastisk stemning og man bliver nemt revet med. Vi var 3 gutter der havde en fantastisk aften, den går aldrig i glemmebogen. De bands der spillede var både autentiske og gode (vi var andre steder hvor kvaliteten var knap så god) - stemningen kunne få selv den ringeste drink til at smage godt...

We were really enjoying ourselves last night at The Legends until the lead singer started making crude comments and changing words to songs that also sounded crude. We left at that point. Disappointing. Up to that point the classic country music was good and the lady fiddle player was awesome. Wish I would have gotten the name of the band.

Very nice steaks but still a bit pricey. Service from Dimi was excellent and personable. We had no alcohol and split a dessert and saved some money. Trying to avoid sugar and carbs. Rachel Rodriguez and her band started playing and she was incredible. We should have stayed longer but headed back in the rain to the hotel around the corner. Most of Nashville seemed out of town for the Christmas holiday. We may come back but there are so many good restaurants in Nashville, it really had to be outstanding to want us to come back. I would come back for drinks and music.

FANTASTIC RESTAURANT!! We sat upstairs on the balcony with a georgous view of the Gultch!  Matt our waiter was so interactive, attentive, and created that extra special touch that made or night memorable!   Thank You Matt!  The food wasn't only fabulous, it was a work of art! No one was disappointed.
IDK, overproduced band didn't know what they wanted to play. Pop country at it's best prefer the other places on the block.

The music brought us in this place. We ordered a drink each and kept the tab open thinking we would stay for the music and have more drinks. We closed the tab and left after one drink. The drinks were not good, don't think there was any vodka in my vodka soda. Bartender was on his phone the whole time. Go somewhere else! Lots of other choices with good music and better service and better drinks.

Flight Cancelled...you're stuck in Nashville for a night.  Get in a cab, tell them you want to get your honky tonk on and arrive at Robert's.  Then have a fantastic night!  So goes my story. 

Good music, cheap beer, good music, limited food selection, good music,. 

I don't even like country music and I had a great time and thought the music was great.  I would recommend it and go back in a second if I were in Nashville.

Very nice lunch.  Cool place to come on a nice Saturday spring day in Nashville.  Atmosphere is great & vibrant.  We sat upstairs by the window so we caught some good sunshine & a faint breeze while watching the activity on the street.  Music downstairs was great.  Being upstairs muffled some of the sound so it was not too loud.

Food was good.  I had a burger with a roasted poblano pepper & Cole slaw.  Beer selection was good.  Had a local Wit from Southern Brew Works.  I would have it again.

Overall a good place to stop for lunch,

Cold beer, burgers, fries, amazing onion rings, good band.  

Touristy for sure, me included...but a lot of fun!

Food took a bit to get but the crowd was huge. 

This place is everything that I expected and hoped for for my first trip to Nashville

Went with friends before an evening at TPAC and it was delightful!

We started with the goat cheese stuff artichoke - a combo I have never had but really enjoyed!

My table companions had the shrimp, the veggie lasagna, and the chili-rubbed scallops, and they all munched way quite happily.  The scallops were a very pretty dish - with risotto "discs" under each scallop that had been shaped and seared to resemble scallops too. fun.
I went with a Gorgonzola salad (sooo good) and then the 3-side combo because the sides all looked so good.  The crunch broccoli was good, but I wish they said onions and peppers in the description (not my fav), the prosciutto mac and cheese was creamy goodness. but the BRUSSELS SPROUTS - oh my, wish I'd gotten 3 of those.  If you like Brussels sprouts, you must try! and if you don't THINK you like them, this might just change your mind.

For dessert we shared the Sticky Toffee Pudding...and wow, it was amazing.  Not too sweet, almost a savory bread pudding with warm toffee inside---man, out of this world.

Great service from Matthew and we made it to the show on time.

The was a light rock band (sorry did not catch the name) that was really excellent as well.

Don 't hesitate ... Just walk in find a seat and order your favorite beverage!  Place is old school and not commercialized.  Great cheeseburger and make sure you order the onion rings.  Music was off the charts... Highly recommend if you are on Broadway !!

This is a must on any Nashville bar crawl. Awesome live band, strongest Jack & Cokes (I guess they splash some Coke in there) around, and greasy grub if you need to soak up some of the spirits. You're gonna be packed in like sardines, and that's OK. Go.

Ryan at the door was so welcoming! We had just had a bad experience at Tootsies. No water bottles no backpacks, etc. Anyway two doors down Ryan is like "Welcome'! It was awesome. His smile was great. Inside, great band great drinks and friendly people! My kind of place. Keep it up! You've got my business. Local couple with visiting family.
Need a quick burger. The burger is good enough  but the band was a pleasant surprise- for somebody who visits Nashville for the first time and has her first full meal in the city. Lovely posters too
Good bar with excellent band. Not too crowded. Drinks reasonable.  Good service.  Highly recommend.

This place is a such a great addition to Nashville. I was very impressed when we went here for lunch with some friends. They have a large food court area with lots of different food options. I loved the live music and rich culture of Plaza Mariachi. You can tell that a lot of time, money and care went into building this place. My favorite part would definitely be the the popsicles. No explanation needed - they are amazing! This is a perfect spot for friends and families to go and enjoy good food, drinks and music!

What a great venue. I've been to a view events here, most recently being the auto show. Now it does suck they jack up pricing for parking for "special events." It's normally $6 to park, but they charge $15 for anything going on. It was convenient parking in the garage and we didn't have far to walk to go inside. It's really a spacious place with tons of light, cool light fixtures and state of the art facilities. The main space is HUGE! Hence, the auto show was there! Now, I didn't see any food options. We were so thirsty from walking around and when I went up to the concession stand, they were "closing" at 3pm when there were 2 more hours of the show left. Just know that going in, bring your water bottle! Convenient to Omni and Country Music Hall of Fame. This place has really cleaned up that side of Broadway and put Nashville on the map in terms of attracting good shows and conferences. 
Great place!

This place is a cool divey Honky Tonk Bar and Grill! It stays packed, does not charge a cover, considers itself to be the "Home of Traditional Country Music". Keep in mind it is very popular and stays crowded. Be prepared for a wait to get inside. Robert's Western World is a unique Nashville treasure that boasts great live country bands, cheap but decent drinks, ridiculously low priced food at the Honky Tonk Grill with beer specials (such as the $5 Stimulus Package - all beef hot dog, chips, & Miller Lite and $5 Recession Special - a fried bologna sandwich, chips & PBR), and an array of interesting people mingling with each other. 

The coolest feature for me was the upstairs area that overlooks the entire bottom half of the bar and stage. The dim and red lit area has plenty of seating and standing areas that have great vantage points of the entire place. I also learned that the top floor has a back exit that is less congested than the front. I was surprised to find that most bars on Broadway have back entrances and exits. As the folks in Nashville say, "Always leave out the back door when your bar hopping downtown!"

First time seeing a show here.  Not even a CM fan but man, this was a very cool experience.  I enjoyed every minute. Even the dude doing the radio commercials was pleasant to listen to.  Very professionally executed.  Congrats on 90 years GOO!  And Cheers to all the amazing staff that give people great entertainment for their hard earned money.
Almost forgot to mention, when you purchase your tickets be sure you avoid obstructed view.  Happened to be a live screening this past Friday evening and cameraman was blocking 50% of our view.   Staff gladly moved us to the front pews and we were very pleased.  Thank you for that !

Horrible venue and I'm from chattanooga tn!!!!Im 6'2" and my knees are literally in the back of girl sitting front of me. I especislly love the smell of burnt popcorn on vomit that fills the entire arena. Next time i will go to Atlanta  given the opportunity.

Great band with an awesome variety of songs; friendly staff ready to make your experience great; good, affordable drinks; awesome atmosphere on Broadway. A fabulous find on our Friday night out exploring Broadway in search of bars with live music. A must do for all on broadway. No cover- so tip the staff & musicians!

The wife and I sat near the stage area. The band they had was totally amazing! The band's name was the Chris Weaver Band. The food was decent. The drinks were okay as well. But what got us was the air conditioning seem to be out when were there last Friday night! It was extremely hot inside. We don't like eating hot food when the thermostat is set to Hell. We were sweating profusely! We only come here occasionally and parking is valet tip plus $5.
Here on s Friday night. Overcrowded. Took well over 30 minutes for any  music and the and the band to come on....awkward silence for a good amount of time

If you want to hear quality, traditional Western Swing and Country (the music on which Nashville was built), this is your place. 

Always a good band, and if you don't like them, a new one will take the stage in about an hour. 

But you'll like 'em all
Fun fun fun! We just stopped in for a beer and stayed for 4 hours! The music was awesome, and the service was spot on.,we will be going back today!

I'm definitely glad I went in and saw the building although it didn't really feel like I got my $20 worth for the self-guided tour. The movie was entertaining and interesting and seeing the building was great. I would have liked to learn more on the tour in general.

Probably one of the finest acoustic settings in the country. Unique seating on wooden pews (surprisingly comfortable) that stretches wide so there are many great seats. A formidable lineup of outstanding acts. The snack stand had some terrific popcorn prepackaged fresh in boxes. And they also had cocktails, beer and wine, as well as other treats that you can take into the theatre. I would look for an excuse to come here again!

Remember when spending your hard earned money on an overpriced beer granted you a smile from a friendly bartender? Nah. This place doesnt either. 

Never experienced a more miserable, uninterested, arrogant bartender in my life.

Maybe you've forgotten how fortunate you are. That you have a bar full of people all day, seven days a week, just because you're in a tourist trap? But you have to figure it out girl! Your service was embarrassing. Only to every patron though, as I noticed your entire character changed when coworkers arrived. 

You're not the only bartender. Other people exist in the service industry. And treating everybody like a miserable, hard-done-by-server just screws your chances of better tips.


All that lipgloss you apply behind the bar surely warrants a smile.
Just embarrassing.

I was invited to a reception at this restaurant, and we were put in the sky room on the second floor. The food was outstanding and the wait staff was not only extremely attentive, but they went out of their way to accommodate special requests. Not to mention that they were extremely friendly.

The entire ambiance of this place is comfortable and extremely amenable to social gatherings. Big thumbs up on all counts.

This place books some great bands. They were consistently at or near the top of the best music on the street. They have a dance floor that gets real busy. Our drinks were served well at the bar. Love the retro furnishings inside and the fun crowd.

AMAZING! Best venue I've ever been to for live music. Beautiful, historical building with gorgeous stained glass, great views from pretty much everywhere. Cool church-pew-like seats, not much legroom but whatevs, it's a cool and nostalgic form of seating. We sat in the balcony, which I had read had the best views, and I definitely agree -- even the back seats would be fine. Awesome acoustics as well. Just an overall great musical experience with some Music City historical charm thrown in. 
[Boring info: There's a gift shop on the first floor with country music/Nashville stuff, and refreshments for sale somewhere that I didn't use. I can't speak to the restrooms as I didn't use them either. No parking that I know of; we took a Lyft.] 
LOVE IT!

If you're visiting in the winter as we are, then the Opry is held at Ryman Auditorium and you're very lucky. The sound is amazing and the intimate vibe of the place, incompatible. 

We've never been to a show like this and we've been to a lot of show. The line up was great - four sections each with two acts and a host. In between acts there are announcements as it is after all a radio show and they have to plug their sponsors. Bill Anderson was a brilliant host for the second quarter, very charming.

We feel very lucky to have seen the variety of talent we did. From artists who've been Opry members for 30, 40 years to artists on their second Opry bill. The standout was Chris Jansen who I wish if heard more from but will look him up. He had fantastic energy. Artists feel very honoured to play this show and you can tell, this is one of the highest accomplishments you can have as a country performer. That makes for a brilliant vibe, the fact that they all want so much to be there.

What an amazing show. An absolute joy.

Great location for a drink and country music. Never know who may show up on the stage. Food service is minimal pizzas from a warming oven. They get 4 stars only for the history and music that they provide. All entertainers play for tips which is common for the area. Many of these performers are looking for a start in the music industry. The ambience is the draw that will grab you when you visit. 
Evenings get very crowed so go during the day.

We visited Robert's on a Friday night in Nashville over Spring Break - it was packed but we had a great night, watching the house band Brazilbilly and soaking up the atmosphere. Will definitely return if we're back in the area, This is a Nashville must-see.

The beer is ice cold and the servers are friendly. It's a very limited menu even for a bar so I wouldn't plan on a full "meal" here, more along the lines of "snacks" with my drinks while I'm listening to the live music. 

With my cold beer and the live music I grabbed the Pollo Del Sol Quesadilla which was really good - just because the menu is very limited doesn't mean that what it does have on it will not be tasty! 

Thumbs up!

Although we do not hit the night life as much as we used too...we love swing dancing and Sunday night is the night to go to Sambuca!!! Our favorite band is Patton James and the Synchromatics but every Sunday night the place has a group of regulars that go to all the dance stops around town and Sambuca has a great swing band on Sunday nights. If we are up for dancing and an evening out and wishing to catch some old dance friends, we go to Sambuca.

I was visiting for CMA fest 2015. This place had great music, beer, and friendly staff. I would definitely recommend this place to a friend. We had a lot of fun at The Second Fiddle and look forward to going back when we come back to Nashville.

History alone makes this auditorium neat. There are natural acoustics, clean bathrooms and a bar on the first and second floor. Those accommodations make this place get a three star rating and not two. I feel like even writing this review is going to give me bad lucky with the music industry in Nashville, but I cannot help it. 

While the acoustics make this place a fantastic venue to see your favorite musician take the stage, the seats and comfort level while trying to watch the musician is a miserable experience. Every single seat in this place is a church pew, not an individual seat. There is not a bad seat in the house, but if you have a boney butt, no butt or a bad back, stay away because you will not be able to sit long without discomfort. Sure, you can stay during a 3 hour concert like some people do but even then you will be uncomfortable. They pack people into the church pew rows like sardines. While I was sitting in my seat, (and I am no way above average in body type) I had to sit or stand at angle the entire time otherwise I would be sitting in the lap of a complete stranger. He was equally uncomfortable and could not get his arm up to his mouth for a drink without standing up or leaning forward. 

So, if you are looking to tour this place for history purposes, or have to see a concert here for the bucket list, cool...do you. But just be aware that you might not be comfortable which will take away from the fact you are seeing great music.

Do NOT sit on main floor unless you are in the first ten rows. Acoustics are great in balcony but nowhere else. The view was majorly obstructed by the balcony
Hanging low overhead. The seats were very uncomfortable church pews and I sat next to a large person. Felt crushed the whole time. Plus they didn't turn the house lights under the balcony  all the way down after the main act started which it made it near possible to see what was going on on stage. Also, maybe due to another concert getting out about the same time but it took over an hour to get out car out of valet.

This classy plaza is basically a mini mall with essentially an upscale food court (Greek, Latin, coffee shop, juice bar) and several shops (boutiques, grocery market with fresh meats/seafood, hot food & small pharmacy, restaurant, art gallery, spa). Looking forward to more shops here.

Live entertainment in the food court - Latin music, fire juggler, and aerial dancer. You can have a beer and walk around the plaza.

The outside is well landscaped with seating areas in center green space and awesome outside bar off the main restaurant. Plenty of free parking.

Kid and stroller friendly. Tito's is in the plaza too which is an arcade and has kid slide. There is a private event room there also for parties.

Happy to have this addition to our neighborhood!
Pretty ridiculous place, cheap beers and alot of fun.

Just had appetizers and drinks for happy hour, both were very good.  We recommend the cheese beignets and the shrimp/crab dip.

Wish we had found this place earlier would have liked to catch one of the weekend bands.  Great stage & dance floor area.

Love, love, loved it! I stopped by with my girlfriends on a Sunday night, and we had the best time. 

As a 30-something Nashville visitor, I felt overwhelmed by a lot of the honkeytonks with their long lines and cramped spaces. Legends was roomy, the people were friendly, and the band was awesome. I couldn't get enough of the singer's voice and she fulfilled as many requests as possible. She even dealt with a drunk heckler who was on a mission to hear "Sweet Home Alabama."

I would absolutely return on my next visit.

Great music and food it was expensive but I think it was better than Ruth Chris! Our waiter knew the answer to all my questions and had recommendations on what food was best. Would love to go back soon. I had the sea bass and my boyfriend had the pork chop we had the chuterie  appetizer. Highly reccomend!
Ordered a drink, the waitress never came back with it and ignored our table for a good 30 minutes. We left. I'll never come back
Favorite honky tonk on Broadway. We caught Buck McCoy on Saturday afternoon and loved it so much, we went back and saw him again on Sunday.
Awesome place for beers and traditional country music with good food for less than 10 bucks.  Music was great

We took the backstage tour that was excellent!  Our guide really knew his stuff!  This place is amazing!  I could feel the presence of all the old acts that used to grace the stage.  It's kind of how you feel when you go to Arlington Cemetery or Little Big Horn!  Don't miss the video either...it was fabulous!  I am so glad we got to go in. I wished we could have seen a show there. Do not miss seeing this place!

Made a reservation for 8:30pm and arrived at 8:10pm to check in and have a few drinks. They did not seat us until 9:10pm. Conclusion: a reservation means nothing here. Very unprofessional to be 40 minutes past the time of the reservation w|o any hostess even communicating with us. Oh and when we talked to the hostess at 8:45pm they were so carefree and acted like it wasn't a big deal... Again, very unprofessional. If you are paying $50+ per a head you should absolutely have better service.

Hard to believe this place was recommended as one of best live music dinner clubs. Band was terrible (off key easy listening covers of every overplayed song in the universe) sea bass was very disappointing, small filet swimming in a sea of watery quinoa, cooked cucumber (who cooks cucumber?) and tomato on a few lousy leaves of of kale. terribly overpriced, can't believe I'm paying $40 for this meal and a drink. Won't return.

Great place for live music and entertainment. Not so great place for quality food. We were looking for a quick lunch to have on our last day in Nashville and wanted to soak in the live music one last time. This is certainly the place to do that. The live music is continuous and all the time and the bands were great. The singers sounded so authentic and the band wasn't too loud around lunch time that it was still easy to hear the people sitting at the same table. 

The food menu isn't huge here, but there were some good options. I chose the el Jardin quesadilla that had a lot of veggies like mushrooms, zucchini, tomatoes, peppers, and can't forget about the cheese. The quesadilla was served with a side of chips and salsa which was something refreshingly different than just the usual French fries (and I love chips and salsa)! The quesadilla was huge, and it was good, but it did taste a little greasy. Everyone at my table got a different quesadilla and the consensus seemed to be that we all liked them while eating it, but our stomachs were a little upset later on in the day. 

Overall, this place is great for the live music and nightlife. Next time I think I would skip the food or just order an appetizer.

Great!  Great suggestion from the folks at museum.  I've been to tootsies before but this was an entertainment pleasure.  Now, I did arrive just after lunch on a Tuesday so the crowed was think.  Enjoyed a hot grilled cheese and a nice turkey & Swiss sandwich.  

Entertainment was great.  Had some kids walk in off the street and be invited up on stage for a few songs.

Very cool bar with really good live music. Right in the start of the heart of Downtown Nashville this is a great place to stop and check our all the photos and history on the walls and have a good drink for a great price!
Always such a great atmosphere.  Live jazz music which is never to loud and the food is delicious.

Absolutely FABULOUS!  Went to see some friends' band play.  The first floor was booked for an event so we sat in the balcony.  It was great.  Of course we love the band but the sound was exceptional.  Dinner was amazing.  I had pizza and a caesar....yummy.  May husband had a steak with potatoes and green beans.  I got a bite of his and it was really good.  I ordered dessert on the waiter's recommendation,  it was ok.  It was chocolate something...not memorable.   Had their signature drink which was tasty.  Great place.  Definitely not for kids.  Saw a previous review comment about the bathroom being unclean.  She must have hit a bad night.  It was very nice.  The music from the band is piped in the restroom too. Sort of odd but nice so you don't miss your favorite song.  Will definitely return!

Attended a cocktail gathering in the Sky Loft for a business conference. There were many heavy appetizers to choose from as well as beef tenderloin and desserts.

The beef tenderloin melted in my mouth, so delicious and tender. 
The crab cheese dip and chips was good, but my favorite had to be The sticky chocolate toffee bites for dessert. So dang delicious, I ate several (oops). 

Great atmosphere and wonderful place to meet! Would definitely go there again.

A must see in Nashville. We picked this tour over going to the new Grand Old Opry location. So much history here. It was $20 each and was nice and cold inside! Well needed on an August say in Nashville :)

I love this place. It's so small and squished and smells like grease and beer. True classic Nashville spot. I have found myself here multiple times as their beer is cheap and they have cheap food too! 

I'm all about the Miller High Life's for $2.50 and there's something called the "Stimulus Package" which is a MHL, all beef giant hot dog, and chips for $5.00. Lol . Absolutely awesome. Love it so much.

There's always decent bands in there as well. Bands in Nashville can be annoying sometimes when the lecture customers on tipping. We're all grown adults, we understand you work for tips. We get it.... makes me roll my eyes. I found that happening here a few times and if I was a server or owner would not let the band make my customers feel like that. 

This place is definitely one of my faves and I will be back next time I'm in Nashville.

This place is pretty cool and I really hope that they can make a go of it. When you walk into it it kind of reminds you of walking into a Mexican themed at Disney World. There was obviously a lot of thought and effort that went into the look and ambience of the mall. My friend and I decided to eat at The Madeira Cafe that is located inside the mall, and a separate review has been left for them. They had very interesting food counters as well as little retail stores, and a small Grocery and bakery that was located in the front of the mall. We got to see a live Mexican band which was very entertaining, and if I hadn't eaten and painful I would have loved to have gotten something from either the ice cream counter or the bakery. If you are in the Brentwood area this would be a cool place to check out if you're looking for something to eat, a place to rest for a bit, or place to pick up some snacks or groceries.

We stopped by late Saturday afternoon for a snack and to listen to the band. The Southwest quesadillas was a large portion with chips, salsa and sour cream and the chipotle bbq sauce and roasted tomatoes made it unique. Nice spot to rest upstairs and enjoy live music with reasonably priced food and friendly service.

Hands down, my favorite bar on Broadway. We drunkenly wandered in on Saturday night and have gone back every night since. We tried other bars, but the music just can't be beat. Every band we've heard has blown us away! Also, the beer is cheap... Like, really cheap compared to other bars. I will definitely be recommending Tin Roof for years to come. 

The only thing I dislike is the women's restroom. It definitely takes a beating every night, but we had to be careful for broken beer bottles and a clogged toilet. Regardless, a great bar that guaranteed us a fun time, every time.
I love this place. This is my 2nd convention here and both of them were a blast. Wear comfortable shoes because this place is huge.

We were In Nashville for the 1st time. We found our self surrounded by many bars on Broadway as y'all know...  Thanks to the good reviews on Yelp! we made our way to Robert's Western Word. We loved it. Great easy going atmosphere. Great live music. The food was simple, good and good prices. Staff was friendly. I would most definitely recommend this place and will return again when in town.

My favorite place in the Gulch! Great atmosphere and entertainment. My waitress, Ariel was fantastic! She recommended some delicious appetizers. The fettuccine carbonara was amazing and the coconut mojito was refreshing. I highly recommend this restaurant.

We stopped in here on a Tuesday around lunch time and it wasn't busy. They had live music talent that's actually talented. Why aren't there more reviews here ?!? I would've taken a picture of the Hot Chicken Torta sandwich but honestly it was too good and I inhaled it. My wife had the same problem with the Chicken n' Waffle nuggets. They have a children's menu also.

This may have been my favorite place while visiting nashville. The music was out of control amazing both nights we went here. The bartenders are fantastic and pour great drinks. Cool Atmosphere and while crowded, it didn't seem too crowded which is good since I don't do crowds ha

I've heard terrible things but now it's official. Some guy named Anthony Cunningham wouldn't let me in because I reminded him of his ex girlfriend?!?  Super weird. Guy needs to be fired. If I could recommend either The Valentine or Famous to newcomers, those are a great time! Nashville is about love not hate and this hateful man clearly hasn't gotten over his ex unfortunately :/

Fun little place on Broadway! Enjoyed the music, definitely a little older crowd. The drinks were very reasonably priced and wish we would've tried the food. It was pretty busy but we still found a place to sit and got our drinks pretty quickly. Really enjoyed all the fun decorations and authentic atmosphere. Not bad!

We went here on a Saturday night, it was pretty packed as was expected. We waited for 25 minutes for a table, while we waited we sat at the bar and had drinks and listened to the live band, both were excellent!! We got to our table on the 3rd level and it was so dark up there we had to look at the menu with the flashlights on our phones!! lol (no joke) The server was great, had a real upbeat attitude, the food was delicious as well!! I would highly recommend this place , and plan on going back...

Cheap beer...we went to a few places downtown on Broadway while waiting on the show at Ryman Auditorium.  We were on the way to see "Ghost Brothers of Darkland County" so we had some time to before the show...

The only thing I don't like this bar...they allow tourist to bring in their KIDS...I just don't enjoy listening to music, drinking and watching other kids babies while they drink..not healthy environment...not talking babies..talking 10 yr olds...not right people..not right!!!

There was a band there. About five in group...They were pretty good. Can't remember there names but they were pretty good. Better than some we heard in other locations.  The Budweiser was only $5 here where everywhere else $5 or more.

All of these locations are small and narrow and they get crowded fast.  But at least the crowds come and go if you sit still long enough.  
I would go here again!  They love the Tourist here!! 
Remember the bands play by tips only!!!
My favorite spot on Broadway, no bro country here. But don't take it from a guy from the south side of Chicago, go yourself.

I have so often heard "what a great venue" applied to the Ryman. If you like paying $16 for 12 ounces of wine, sitting in church pews, and waiting in a ridiculous line for a bathroom then that may be the case. But start to finish this was a rip off and a hassle at every turn. I've learned my lesson seeing shows at the Ryman.

It was Friday after Thanksgiving, 2014.  There were 4 of us and it was our first time in Nashville. We wandered into Robert's, and instead of staying for one drink, we stayed for a few hours, and had a great time! The music was great, the drinks were cold, and the food was outstanding!  Especially the burgers and fried pickles!  The bouncer was great!  He made sure we were seated in a good spot to enjoy the live music, and checked on us periodically to make sure we were happy.  And WE WERE! Excited to go back next year!

This 5 star review assumes you are not constricted by sitting anywhere under the balcony. Make sure and get a seat in the first 10 rows or anywhere in the balcony.  Sound and sites await. Super venue. ..the sound veritably echos through the ancient timbers.

There is no substitute for Bennys bologna..  The man is a walks on water next that grill.  

He was not in this visit, but sandwich was still okay.  Not the usual great

We had been here about 5 years ago and decided to try it again. It was excellent the first time and were a bit hesitant about going back....afraid we would be disappointed from our first experience.......WE WEREN'T!
Kenny was our waiter and everything he suggested was excellent! From the filet to the wine pairing, dessert and the music. We will be back!!!

Not the original home of the Grand Ole Opry (this was actually the fifty place the Opry called home in its first 18 years) or even its longest home (the Grand Ole Opry House at Opryland holds that distinction) but it's undoubtedly the most famous home the Opry ever had and one of the most historic theatres of any kind in the country. 

Full disclosure:  I worked here for a few years in the 80s, so a bit of history.  Built in 1891 as a house of worship by riverboat captain Thomas H. Ryman, the building was originally called the Union Gospel Tabernacle and renamed for the Captain Ryman upon his death.  For years, it was the primary performance venue in the city of Nashville and the list of names that have appeared on the stage include Will Rogers, Sarah Bernhardt, Charlie Chaplin, Harry Houdini, Enrico Caruso and Presidents Theodore Roosevelt and William Howard Taft.  In 1943, the National Life and Accident Insurance Company purchased the building as a home for the Grand Ole Opry and renamed it the Grand Ole Opry House.  Every Saturday night (and later Fridays as well) until March of 1974 the greatest names in country music, from Roy Acuff to Faron Young graced its stage.  It was hot in the summer and cold in the winter.  The old wooden pews were uncomfortable to sit in and Cokes spilled in the balcony would often drip down on the audience below.  Conditions for the performers were worse with only 2 small dressing rooms and stage lights that made the stage feel like a bake oven in the summer.  When the Opry left for a new home at Opryland, fans continued to flock to the Ryman to stand on the famous stage and see where so much country music history had been made but the auditorium largely stood empty and in disrepair with the balcony completely off limits to the public.  Some nut at National Life suggested tearing the building down and using the bricks to build an interdenominational chapel at the (now defunct) Opryland theme park.  Cooler heads prevailed and the building eventually landed on the National Register of Historic Places.  

Fast forward to 1994, when Gaylord Entertainment restored the auditorium, added air conditioning, modern dressing rooms, sound and light systems and a new support building and reopened it as a concert venue.  For nearly 20 years the Ryman Auditorium has once again become one of the top performance spaces in the southeast and the Opry itself returns each winter for several weeks.

I've seen a number of shows here over the years and must say that it is a great place for live music.  The Ryman's acoustics were legendary but the remodel did away with much of that.  However, modern audio systems make up for that.  The first 10 rows on the main floor are great but once you get under the balcony, the slope of the floor becomes very steep and in the back rows you can only see about 10 vertical feet of the stage.  The posts that support the balcony also create obstructions.  This actually makes the balcony seats the best seats in the house.

The wooden pews are still just as uncomfortable as they've ever been and the number of seats in each row assumes that the average patron is incredibly skinny...which, of course, isn't usually the case so you'll get to know your seatmates very well.  On Opry nights, the crowd will stretch around the block waiting to get in for the show and there is no protection from the elements.  The ushering staff hasn't mastered the art of getting one audience out and another one in in the 30 minutes between shows so you run the risk of missing a substantial part of the second show.

During the day, the Ryman offers self-guided and guided tours.  Unless you absolutely can't live without seeing the dressing rooms I would skip the guided tour.  For the money, you don't get much and the guides don't seem to know much more about the building than what they have to memorize to guide tours.  Since the building was pretty much gutted during the remodel nothing in the backstage area has much historical significance to it.  The dressing rooms are nice but a dressing room is dressing room.  A better sense of what the Ryman was like during the Opry years can found in the display cases and video presentations out in the auditorium.  The Ryman is really a living museum but is still very much a modern performance hall.  Self-guided tours are available daily and there is a small gift shop on the lower level.  The entrance to the building is on 4th Avenue and ample (if expensive) parking is nearby.  

You don't have to be a country music fan to enjoy a visit to the Ryman.

This place was recommended to me by a friend - and I'm so happy I listened. Nicest staff, great drinks and food and amazing music. It was definitely one of my favorite stops in downtown Nashville. I was very impressed by one of the waitresses especially; in a completely packed bar, she couldn't have been better or nicer. I will definitely be coming back here next time I visit Nashville.
They had a great band playing tonight. Lively crowd and very fun!

Stopped into this bar, restaurant while visiting Nashville during the CMA fest. Saw the band playing I. The front and thought we would have a drink. This places really surprised us. Two band areas one in the front and one in the back, it also has room upstairs and the inside is amazing with character. We ordered a couple of drinks and an appetizer. You must try the loaded tots. Truly delicious, they have queso bacon, onions and more. So good. Our waitress "Anna ". Was very friendly and was able to suggest a few drink items that we enjoyed. You can pass right by, but don't pass it by, good value, great music, delicious drinks and tasty eats.

Wayne's Western World was one of the highlights on our visit to Nashville! The honky took atmosphere was contagious. We planned to hop around to a number of bars but were having so much fun we stayed the evening! Our waitress was amazing in keeping up with all the folks and she kept us well supplied on drinks.  The Recession special of a balongna sandwich or hot dog....plus chips AND a beer for $5 has got to be the best deal around. But our best time was the entertainment which was fantastic. The Don Kelly Band which features Don and the incredible stand up bass player Slick Joe Fick is amazing to hear and watch! Highly recommended for a great time and small hit to the wallet.

Uptown funky chic...this micro chain is located in the Gulch section of Nashville ...far from the boots and ball caps of Nashvegas. Situated adjacent to two upscale competitors (Watermark and Octopus restaurants ) Sambuca carves out  amazing jazz club atmospherics with succulent menu choices. Salmon , scallops, filets , chops and some thoughtful apps/ small plates will nourish most discriminating palates. Signature cocktails, such as a basil infused vodka mojito makes early or late night rendezvous' on couch sided tables très bon....
Try the southern inspired tomahawk cut smoked pork chop with prosciutto mac and cheese ..enough for two.
But tis the quality of exceptional musicians that make this hallmark unique. Jazz combos playing crossover R&B, funk, motown at a listenable level makes for a full evening out, including dancing.
Our friday was graced with the the silky vocals of Herchel Bailey, grandson to Country Hall of Fame member, D. Ford Bailey,  who crooned his way through renditions of Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, James Brown and Bruno Mars...
Sambuca is more than an apertif, it is an entrée of delish
My son and I were on a road trip,family golf, etc. stopped in here for a drink. This is the most authentic fun place you can go in Nashville. Don't miss it. Went back several times

Stopped in on a Sunday afternoon and are upstairs. I had my 14 yr old with me and the atmosphere was great. Band was awesome! We thoroughly enjoyed the food! I had the chicken n' waffles - pretty good!!! And she had the Smashville burger that was surprisingly super awesome! Shared fried pickles... They were good and not too salty! Definitely stop in! The place looks so cool inside!

Hostess was efficient (not warm), and the server was nice enough.  We should have researched a bit more before going in and sitting down.

The menu was limited and the prices outrageous for what we were expecting.  It seemed like a minimal effort menu for a maximum $$.

We opted to get up and leave, because we could not see paying over $20 for roast chicken!  Our son was ready to order the $50 prime rib, but we informed him we would get this at J. Alexander's, instead.  Really, this place is no Ruth's Chris (and certainly not Jeff Ruby's).

After reading some other's reviews (mind you, after the fact, on Open Table), it was hilariously summarized as a place to go if you're having a mid-life crisis, and trying to rekindle something with your spouse, except since it's so loud, you won't succeed in having any worthwhile conversation, due to the odd smooth jazz renditions of Michael Jackson.

I suspect the reviews are high because people probably feel embarrassed that they went there and spent far too much money, trying to look like they know upscale dining and entertainment.  Alas, Tin Angel was our more than satisfying back up plan.

I attended a great show at the Ryman Auditorium. It has a great layout balcony sitting which I prefer. It gives their shows a more intimate feel than being at a large arena or coliseum. I had won tickets online to the show so me and a couple other friends met even more friends at the Ryman. The place is amazing. I would recommend taking the tour they have during the day of it. There's quite a bit of history in this place.

Good music and fun atmosphere but I asked for about 4 drinks from the bar after being turned down the 4th time bc they didn't carry an extensive cider and beer list I gave up and settled on wine. I got the champagne chicken I thought the food was ok. It sounded way better on the menu than the food actually tasted. I would go bAck but more for drinks apps and the band rather than a nice dinner. On a plus note they advertise gluten free options clearly on there menu and it's nice having options.

They where super accommodating for our 7 month old at nearly 8:30 at night! Relieving since many restaurants in the area don't even have high chairs. The food was good! But the service was meh.. We asked for a Cocktail menu for another round of drinks and extra salad dressing and never got either... But it was tasty. The buca begneit (spelling?) was the best!
One of the best steak I ever had. Miso Seabas was insanely good. It was a perfect Valentines dinner date indeed. We'll surely come back soon...

This place is just amazing ! The food is great , the drinks and everyone is so nice. Such a fun place 
I highly recommend to anyone who wants to enjoy the Hispanic culture. Date night would never be better !
Presently surprised at how good the food was for a bar. Excellent Mac and cheese - creamy and hint of jalapeño. Really like the street tacos-especially the fish taco.
Didn't get to see the live music but they have some local favorites all the time from I understand. Stuffed artichokes were incredible. Get a Sinless Strawberry Mojito. Quite refreshing.

The bartenders were fast and the music was good, but that jackass of a security guard out front ruined our night. Me and my friend step out for a smoke and start to come back in. The security was supposed to stamp our hands as we came in, but didn't stamp my friends hand hard enough or something. He told my friend that he wouldn't let hit back in. I tell dude "he came in with me the first time." He turns around and tells me if I don't calm down, he will kick me out. What a jerk. The bartender said his name is Steve. I won't be back.

We were greeted at the door by an incredibly snarky hostess who told us we had to be away from our table within a certain time as they had a second booking.
The food was tasty, sadly cold!

On the upside, Jesse our waiter-- absolutely lovely and the wine selection absolutely fabulous! 

Our tip-- ask for Jesse!

My friend and I hesitated about this tour because we know very little about country music. Decided to pay for the self-guided tour (which by the way was discounted with my military ID). The movie before the tour , the history about the Ryman and the musicians all over the auditorium were incredible. I was actually surprised by how many people I actually knew. Not sure if the backstage tour is worth the extra $10, but the self-tour was worth every penny!

My go-to for real honky tonk music in downtown Nashville. Do my best to go 5-6 times a year. My last visit came a week ago, and my usual cheeseburger and fries were spot on. Swear they are best fries in downtown. The beer is good; the waitresses are attentive, despite the chaos, and music is great. What more do you want?!

We made a 6:30 reservation to listen to music and have some drinks for a girls night. They sat us right in front of the stage. The music was good, but loud if you wanted to have a conversation. We were waiting on our one friend and wanted to have some drinks and hang out before dinner. Our waitress kept coming over to see if we wanted food every 5 minutes and we told her we just want to drink and will order food later. Around 7, she came over again to see if we wanted to order and said we are booked solid tonight and have a 13 top VIP  table coming at 8:30 and will be sitting where you are. She said if we weren't done we would have to move to the lounge area upstairs. I don't think we should have been warned about being kicked out an hour and a half before another table was coming because we weren't as "important".  After that I didn't even want to give this place our business and that comment immediately ruined our night. Anyways our food wasn't good for how expensive it was. My friends chicken was dry and the beignets were cold in the middle. Our waitress was nice, but pushy and I do feel bad for her that she was the one telling us we would have to leave at 8:30. That comment should have came from the manager and not been put on her. So if you plan on listening to music and enjoying your night...this is not the place unless you are a "VIP". I would never recommend this restaurant!
You come for the great country music, but it's hard to imagine a better fried bologna sandwich.

Traveld from Chicago for friends birthday and they took away my 22 year olds friends I'd because "it didn't look real". We are all clearly of age and why would we travel 8 hours for nothing... Asked to talk to manager and they told us we weren't allowed to speak to a manager without police supervision. This was on the last day of our trip (Sunday) and it was 6:30. We were just trying to get dinner. Will not return ever again. I suggest going to the tin roof on demonbreun..
Great bands but no draft beer. Service is great and fast, even in a Saturday night. Be prepared to tip the band if you like them, Legends doesn't charge a cover so you can too the band!

Pretty descent spot on Broadway. Good music and a fun atmosphere. I would have preferred better beer but still a 4 star establishment. There is a pretty good amount of seating down stairs and some fun bar sports up stairs. I'll probably hit up again next time I'm in Nashville.

They offered a Mother's Day brunch.  Being from out of town we didn't know any better. Well, I could tell they don't normally offer Sunday brunch because it was poorly done.  First of all once we were sat it took a good 15min before anyone approached us for drinks.  It was not very clean. The restaurant looked like it was trying to be a fancier place but was struggling big time.  Lots of little and big things that needed attention. Food offerings were only ok.  There was barely ever any fruit out and what was out was picked over.  Two pluses were that the orange juice was very good and they had a band playing that was very enjoyable.
AMAZING brisket Mac n cheese! Great vibe and got to listen to some really awesome music from Blue Honey! We were visiting Nashville, but will definitely return if we are in Nashville again!
Chicken waffle bites are rediculous! Great bar food and service. Live music! Definitely worth a stop.

The Legends Corner is pretty damn literal. The bar is located on a corner, and many legends have played here.

The place is on a slope so there are two entrances on two different floors. There are two bars, but when I went, the upstairs bar was closed. The downstairs bar was crowded as a result.

The stage is small but there's tons of room to stand, and some tables.

There's also great memorabilia everywhere, from said legends. There was a signed acoustic from Johnny Cash, a 5-neck guitar I can only assume was from Rick Nielsen, and lots of other cool things.

Loved this place.  Spent three nights in Nashville, visited many places, ended up here all three nights.  Great old school country music, my understanding is they play all pre-1979 music so no bro country - you can find that just about everywhere else.  Great bands, great music, friendly waitresses, the Johnny & June mural next to the bathroom is awesome.

We ate here for lunch on a Monday afternoon after visiting the country music hall of fame/museum, you can take a short walk up to honky tonk row on Broadway. 

We had the recession special which consisted of a fried bologna sandwich, lays potato chips in a bag and a PBR in a can. I love PBR, but the can was not super cold when it arrived at our table. 

The fried bologna sandwich was really good. Served on toasted bread with lettuce and tomato. It was several pieces of thinly sliced bologna. My kids got the burger and fries and there were no complaints.  The onion rings were also very good. Fried in a tempura type batter and super crunchy. 

The best thing about this place was our very nice and attentive waitress and the atmosphere.  Lots of old decor on the walls, a long bar and an old, but talented country western singer on the little stage up front. 

We really enjoyed our stop here. Check it out for a friendly honky tonk experience!

This happened to my friends husband who happens to be a poplar country band drummer! 

On January 30, 2018 my hubby and I was at a charity event with our friends from out of town. I left the group to go home I had to get up early. My husband stayed with the group ( pic below ). @ 11:03pm, They went to the Second Fiddle on 420 Broadway all of our friends were allowed to enter but my husband wasn't. When my husband asked for a reason he was told they do not have to give him a reason after several times of wanting to know why with no answer my husband asked is it because of his race and again was told they don't have to give him a reason.  Our friends asked and they were told the same thing. The manager came to the door and also told him he couldn't enter but our friends could. When my husband questioned he was told I don't owe you a reason and you can't enter (they all left) This was total RASICM!!!!!! DO NOT GO TO THIS PLACE RACISM, SEXISM, RELIGION RACISM WILL NOT BE TOLERATED.......THIS IS A NEW DAY AND THE SECOND FIDDLE WILL HEAR FROM US AGAIN.......IM ASKING ALL MY FRIENDS TO POST THIS ON YOUR PAGE....let's shine a light on the practices of The Second Fiddle....this is not the first time this has happened check Yelp 

facebook.com/wandalee.ho...

Photo of Second Fiddle - Nashville, TN, United States

This is a great place to go for dinner, drinks, or just a night out with friends to listen to live music. The band during our visit played jazz, and appeared to be very talented. (The music is a little loud for conversation, so request to sit away from the stage if possible.)

For appetizer we ordered the Buca Beignets. They were delicious. As our meal, I ordered the Salmon Oscar, with a side of sweet potatoes. Both were very good. The salmon might be the best I have ever tasted. Nice, crisp outside but very moist and flaky in the middle. My wife ordered the pork chop. She stated it was well prepared and tasty. 

Overall, a very nice choice if you're looking for a higher rated dinner establishment. I think the drink prices are a little high though. In my humble opinion, I don't see a need to charge $12 for a standard margarita. Let your food fare warrant the high price, and treat the guests to average drinks. Regardless, we had a great meal and will probably be back. A solid 4 rating.

Ambiance, entertainment, service and food were amazing! Jesse went above and beyond and provided us with exceptional service. The filet mignon melted in your mouth and the lobster tail was cooked perfectly! I would definitely go back!

We were mainly here for a local live band that was performing over dinner time. The speciality cocktails, spicy blueberry margarita and strawberry basil lemonade ware both refreshing and tasty. The goat cheese stuffed artichokes we're prepared perfectly over crostinis. We split the sea bass, unfortunately it wasn't very good. The fish was over cooked, chewy and fishy. The brussel sprouts weren't anything special. They were mushy and didn't have any flavor to them. For dessert, we tried the cheesecake sopapilla. The outside was burnt and the cheesecake inside was over cooked. Overall, the meal was disappointing but the atmosphere, live music and drinks were great. I'd recommend it for drinks and apps but definitely not for dinner.

This bar is awesome as I was just in here for about an hour in Nashville. They had an awesome bartender. Plenty of standing room and decent prices on beer. Love this place, definitely one of my more favorite places on Broadway

Idiots bar backs are druggies. Pay for your food wait an hour and they kick you out before you get your food. Bouncers are clueless. Bouncer and manager backed the drug addict cook thank god I can afford to walk away with out my 50 dollar food. Idiots. .

This place is a must see if you are in Nashville! The food is amazing, the people are very friendly, they always have live entertainment....its so great. They even have a kids play area, fun little shops, and a full grocery store complete with a bakery and butcher. You will not be disappointed in this fun place!

Classis country. Hank and more.  Great atmosphere- wall of signed pictures on one side and shelves of cowboy boots on the other. Truly old school.  Had lunch as music played. Burgers and fries were good and hot as it's cooked right there on the grill.  Enjoyed lunch and the classic country music!
Great music and tasty food. Quick, friendly service. Loved the chicken and avacado quesadillas. Great spot on Broadway.
Best damn $4 fried bologna sandwich ever, and even though the fried pickle spears are out of a freezer bag they still are very good! A must while bar hopping broadway!

This place was so fun! My husband and I spent a Monday night here and it was awesome. There was a great cover band playing and we ended up staying till close. There were good vibes, good music, and a lot of fun to be had...the drinks were a little watered down, but it was a fun spot.

Started w queso and chips. Chips were thick and cold. So probably not made here. Queso was just ok (not world famous).  Chicken tacos were spicy hot. Removed jalapeno and still very hot. Nashville chicken sandwich was awesome. Good flavors. Tator tots hot and crisp. A little heavy on salt.
Music awesome!

Great music, fun crowd! This was my favorite place that we stopped while in Nashville! Although $9 for two PBR's is the most expensive price I've ever seen anywhere. Not too bad considering there's no cover charges in the area though. We will definitely be back!

Not sure what the hype is about at all. There is a lot of drunk tourist and the drinks are over priced even for Nashville. I went there multiple nights in attempt to hear decent music and never did. Cover bands playing crap versions of crap songs. The bartenders are very good at ignoring people. The security guards or bouncers are very good at throwing random people out. I'm being sarcastic. The bouncers are a joke and are the douche bag over assertive type. 

Seriously there are so many better places in downtown Nashville for a good time. Try Roberts or Tootsies. Avoid this place unless you are a drunk tourist.

Legends, along with a few other honky tonks, on Music Row are FUN!!!!  We had a the best time ever in Nashville!  We had so much fun at these honky tonks that play awesome live music, that we never made it to any other place that we had on our list!  And, I don't even drink alcohol!

As one of the very talented singers stated as some folks left the joint "don't leave, they don't understand you out there, we understand you in here." She couldn't have been more right. You will not be disappointed by this classic honky tonk! Cheap drinks & eats (and delicious!). The live music could not have been better or more authentic Nashville. My husband and I kept coming back for more and stayed as long as we could. It was a knee slapping good time!

Great place to stop. The atmosphere and food is great. The reason for the four stars is it was  a little understaffed for lunch. The place was packed and they only had one waitress who was also the bartender and one cook. So the drinks and food took a while to get.

Best moonshine margarita in all of Nashville!!!!! I enjoyed this place of all the bars on the "nashvegas" strip. The bbq brisket nachos are amazing and made me almost miss Southern California for a minute. The owner and waitresses were friendly and had good vibes. I would definitely go back and recommend that you try it out. I can't get moonshine margaritas and live country music in SoCal on a Tuesday afternoon!

FUN!  We walked around Nashville for 2 days and kept coming back and checking in here.  I love the atmosphere and the friendliness.  I love REAL Classic Country music and it doesn't get any better than this.

This is without a doubt one of my favorite places! One of the most historic places in Nashville (that we almost lost!) period. The building to me has a heartbeat. I've seen at least 100 shows here and it is always a great experience. The pews are hard church pews and there's not much room but it is just part of the experience to me. If there is any music act or artist you really enjoy and they are playing here you MUST go! They will never sound any better and will never forget the experience. Only bad thing is seats are hard to get so you have to be ready when they go on sale.

your average broadway, neon signed, country music cover band bar.  not complaining since it's everything you expect on this street, just hard to give it 4 stars.  congrats to tin roof for getting many small things correct, good drinks served quickly to a well behaved crowd.  you should probably eat somewhere else then head here for music and drinks, but if someone in the group is starving, they can definitely find a decent meal (stick to the quesadillas).

Here right now - ordered scallop risotto - the scallops were good but the risotto were gummy balls of rice. Considering it was $36, s bit disappointing. My friend got veggie lasagna - oddly sweet and grossly crispy! We also got calamari - chewy and gross! The goat cheese artichokes were extremely yummy- best thing we had! Would not recommend unless you are just having drinks on the outdoor patio. The "risotto" ball is pictured below.

Tin Roof is where we kicked off our bride to be's special bachelorette night!

We found a table on top and ordered dinner.  The menu was pretty big.  Heads up, food portions are big as well so if you're with a group, maybe share or you'll for sure have leftovers.

The drinks are cold, the servers are friendly and once our food was consumed, we partied hard to get the night started.  This is one of our favorite places on Broadway!

Ryman Theatre: 

$25 to enter just to look around is a little ridiculous without live entertainment. It's cool to see--once. The theatre is beautiful with a lot of history but wasn't worth the $25--each. I loved all of the history and photographs with descriptions on the walls. My daughter took about 20 steps into the theatre and was ready to leave when she saw everything. It's definitely a must see but like I said--once. We love country music so we had to go to the heart of it, we were not disappointed with the ambiance.

Went to Roberts Western World last night for a quick bite to eat ... service was ok but it was slamming in there, burger came out hot and fries also hot. It was exactly what I expected, decent food very edible...limited menu but really the ambiance was what was killer. Great music great time !

I have been to many concerts at the Ryman and absolutely love the acoustics, vibe and history. However, the pews are horribly uncomfortable and the sardine can effect makes it difficult to enjoy the show. Last night I attended the Tedeschi   Trucks performance. They were fantastic! Unfortunately the woman next to me was over served and fell asleep and half of her drink ended up on me. She was too drunk to care. When I told the usher he said he would have someone come and clean it up. Never happened. Her very large husband should have bought 2 tickets as should many people who attended. Very unfair to those of us who can actually fit into our designated space without encroaching on our neighbor. Amazes me how many people feel entitled to space that isn't theirs. It will be a very long time if ever that I attend another concert at the Ryman. Makes me sad.

Awesome, awesome, awesome music!!!! Absolutely love this place.  Is it the cleanliness??  No!  Do the bathrooms suck?   Yep, pretty much.  
Friendly staff, great band and nobody here cares!!!  
Tons of TVs for the sports fans and did I mention awesome music on a Sunday night?!

I can't tell you what the food was like cuz I didn't have any. The women at the next table had the fried baloney sandwich (think BLT) and loved it. On the other hand the beer was cold and the music was hot (western swing). Robert's has a fun vibe. Come in the afternoon, or after dinner, and swing your ass to some great live music.
Grill closed. Gospel music playing live on stage. Guess that's ok if you are into it. Wish I could of tried the food.

We had an EXCELLENT time at Legends, the live music artist, Buck Mccoy was excellent!!! I can't say enough good things about this singer from his song selection, to his stage presence to his cd of original music. 
As for the bar itself, the girls behind the bar are quick and attentive. You don't have to wait long fir a drink and the album covers and discs on the wall brought back memories. I'm old enough to have played a lot of them when they were new.
All in all a great experience!

We ate here while passing through the Gulch.  My wife and I enjoyed the place.  Our waiter was very nice and informative when it came to the food and the local scene.  Our lunch was good and so were the drinks.  My wife really loved the strawberry mint cocktail they had for lunch.  We will be going back for sure and would love to try their dinner menu.  

The staff was even nice enough to split our lunches so we could share.

This was recommend by a friend who grew up there as a great little Honkey Tonk to get a drink, something to eat and listen to some music. And, we did. 

Cool place. I'm sure many musicians pass through each day. The one that was playing when we were there was pretty damn good. 

The decor is what I expected in a divey place like this. A lot of local signs, stickers and cozy-quaint with the grit of a good ole place. 

Had a burger and a some vodka sodas. Burger was great...flat top grill greasy. Yum!

Our bartender was awesome. I love a bartender who has worked so long in a place that you feel like you're walking into their own house. 

Definitely stop here for some good music, cold drinks and great service.

Atmosphere. Good music. Great good. Yes. Yes. Yeah, sure. You're going here for a chill Nashville place to hang out, and to listen to good music. Nothing wrong with the burgers, and we fed 4 people for $40 (including 2 beers and a side of fried pickles).

The music is alway great. It's a fun bar to hang out. People are there to have a good time.  Drinks are not pricy,  staff is friendly. And u can eat if you want. It's right downtown next to a lot of other places.  I always.  Always come here.

I did this tour on the same day as visiting the Country Music Hall of Fame and the Historic RCA Studio B tour and I thought the Ryman tour was far better than either of those. If you do the Ryman tour, spend the extra $5 and choose the guided backstage tour option.

I understood why they wouldn't let you take photos in the dressing rooms, but it was still disappointing not being able to.
Great pickles and burgers at a great price. All with some great live country music and down to earth atmosphere.

One of my favorite Nashville restaurants, 
The food is always on point, The service was JUST RIGHT, and the ambiance so perfectly romantic
And they have live Jazz at night
I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone in the Nashville area!

It is however, a LITTLE on the pricier side... My group of 4 ate for $170 + $30 tip and we all had immaculate entrees, several drinks, TWO appetizers, and TWO desserts!!!
Not bad AT ALL, and completely worth every penny :)

Will return!!! OVER AND OVER AGAIN!!!
My favorite spot on Broadway. The honky think band playing on the weekend and the regulars dancing make it an experience not to be missed. To me, this is what Nashville is about.
Great music. Food was pretty decent for bar food.  But heck, it's Nashville and folks are here for the tunes.

We had such an enjoyable experience. Loved the hostess that sat us at the table. I think her name was Alicia? Maybe Ashley? She deserves a raise either way. When I informed her of my girlfriends medical condition she went above and beyond to make sure we were accommodated. She even helped us find some fun nightlife!! Definitely recommend!!

The four stars are for the amazing wedding that I got to witness happening in the upstairs party room and the great live music that we got to enjoy from the balcony seats where we ended up. Food was alright- our waitress was sweet, but like they say.. you aren't going to the same place for live music as where people send you for the food. We loved that we were all able to talk during dinner and really enjoy our couple of hours at dinner but you're here for the music and the location. But you already knew that

I enjoyed the food and vibes here. I got pork tacos and they had this really good peach salsa kind of thing on top which was easily my favorite part. The reason I can only give 3 stars is that the layout is not good for listening to / seeing the live music. The venue goes back very far but is very narrow so only the few people at the front can really see the musicians.
This place has an incredibly chill vibe.  Everyone is a mixture of ages and just there to have a good beer, burger, and most important time. Go!

This place was recommended by a friend so my boyfriend and I stopped in one evening while checking out Broadway. The band was playing covers of pop music (not old country) which was okay but I liked the old country band at Robert's Western World better. The interior of Tin Roof is really cool with Christmas lights, neon signs, a comfy lounge area with couches and an overall retro vibe. That's where the charm ended for me. Our bartender wasn't very attentive and seemed much more interested in flirting with the girl sitting next to us (her boyfriend was NOT amused). We had one drink and then headed out. Overall I felt very "meh" about Tin Roof.

Robert's is unique in that they are devoted to traditional Country while other places on Broadway play new country.  We spent a Wednesday afternoon listening to Rachel Hester and the Tennessee Walkers.  She/they were outstanding. She rarely took even a short break yet her voice stayed very strong. The place was busy with SEC fans yet there was only one bartender.  She never stopped moving yet stayed very friendly. The decor is exactly what you want to see in Nashville--tons of photos and boots everywhere. My one complaint was the smoke. There was very little ventilation and one ceiling fan that barely moved. I can't imagine how it must be on a busy weekend.
Awesome music, lots of food choices., family friendly. This a a great place for Sunday afternoon in Nashville.

My favorite bar on Earth

Visiting Nashville and this was the gem on Broadway.  Non stop live music.  And every band we saw was fantastic.  Loved the setup with all the boots and murals on the walls.  People love to dance here and I don't blame them one bit.  
Drinks on this street are brutally expensive but RWW has you covered with $2.50 PBR & Busch beer.  I was also a big fan of the $4 grilled cheese and the fried pickles.  
We went every night and sometimes during the day.  I wish I could go back.

Great new place just opened!  Terrific for families and kids complete with live music playing & a game room for kids.  Variety of restaurants and choices and shopping all in one area with free parking.

Good authentic Mexican, Cuban and even Greek?? Food.

Tried this place for lunch due to the high reviews. Fun dive bar/honkytonk atmosphere and dirt cheap food. Got the recession special which is a fried bologna sandwich, chips, and a PBR for 5 bucks. Nowhere else in downtown Nashville can touch that. Only one server working the bar when I was there so it took a little time to get her attention and place my order as it looked like she was struggling to keep up with the pace of business. Might want to avoid it if you're in a rush but if you wanna sit for a while, listen to some music, and eat cheap food there's no better option in the area.

too pricey for what you're given- starter side salad is $9 with no protein. came for the live music but the singer took a break for over 20 minutes and we finished our dinner in the mean time....service is fast. The dill hollandaise for the Salmon Oscar was really tasty but the salmon itself was way too salty and the portion was so small for the price.

Another trip to Roberts, and another 5 stars. Band was just hot... 3 piece band blew the socks off anyone else on Honky Tonk row. If you are looking for eye candy or a pickup opportunity... this is not the place for you... if you are looking for great music in a fun divey atmosphere... this is it.

Absolutely the best place to enjoy live music! The acoustics are incredible. The atmosphere is wonderful. Sitting in the pews is so fun! My only complaint: do NOT, I repeat, do NOT, use the valet service to park. It is so poorly operated, under staffed, and a huge disappointment. It seriously took them 55 minutes to get my car after a show. No exaggeration: 55 minutes. Do yourself a favor and park in a nearby garage and walk to the Ryman! But don't miss any opportunity to see live music at the gem!

An absolute must see, even if you are not a country music fan! It boggles my mind to think about the amazing talent that has graced that stage,what a great representation of American popular culture, my family throughly enjoyed this tour! Don't think about going, Just Go!!!

Went here for a bachelorette party. We had an amazing server. So that wasn't what got the three stars. It's all about the food. It was just not in line with what you expect to get for that price. I suppose you are paying for the ambiance and live music. The risotto under the scallops was very dry. The lobster enchiladas were also just dry and bland. No one at the whole table finished their plate.

This place has a wonderful, hip hot spot atmosphere, talented artists and impeccable service. We sampled a couple small plates which were delicious, and then I had the most amazing pizza I think I've ever eaten. 5 stars for ambience, service, talent and tasty food. If you want the best service, ask for Tyler. He was the best!
Try the recession special. Best fried bologna you'll ever have (except for grandmas!)

Such a fun atmosphere. The best performers around, good drinks, and fun service. It's a party all day everyday. This is where you want to go on your bachelorette parties. Dare I say it, my favorite place on Broadway. Did I mention how good the music is?

This was my first time going 1/18/13 for my bfs bday. We did a reservation through the opentable app so we got there an was seated in 10min. Looooove the atmosphere an band that was there that night.
