So the food was good but highly priced for the small portion. I got a Caesar sald an champagne chicken my bf got the filet. It was good but we left hungry. I'd go back probably just for cocktails though. Very sexy place though.

This is what was Nashville was missing. I LOVE the ceviche and their nieve de garrafa. They always have cool performances. The only downside to this is that more and more people are coming here and so parking isn't enough sometimes. 

They have a little "cantina" booth in the corner. Their Drinks are a little expensive in my opinion.

Place is always clean and very presentable.

Amazing cultural place!

First time for us at the Ryman and we will definitely go back but next time we'll try for the balcony area.  The main floor isn't sloped so hard to see around people in front of you.  Usher's very friendly, drinks will cost you $, as they usually do at these venues.  Valet very friendly and they know what they're doing.  If you drive a Nissan, valet parking is free! Yes, we drive a Nissan (though it's old as the hills!) and saved $20.00!

So really should have asked to see a manager to give them a chance to correct our experience, but when 5+/- things go badly right from the get-go, you're just kinda over it and want to get out of there. My husband and I came to dine here tonight. We are out of towners and did not make a reservation. It was after 8pm on a Sunday evening however, so it really shouldn't have been too much of an issue. We were greeted by a hostess who was presently snacking on something. Not professional but we all get hungry so no big deal. She promptly asked if we had a reservation which we replied no. She then stated they did not have availability until 9pm but that the bar area was full service. We were more than happy to sit at the bar, order an app and some drinks, and wait for a table. I then inquired if we could have a table on the patio when it became available (which there were several empty already but I understood they may be reserved). Here is when things really went wrong. The hostess stated no because "we wouldn't get proper service" and that they are "very particular with their patio seating". I have never in my life been told we couldn't sit somewhere because we wouldn't get service, nor did I ever tell anyone that in my 10+ years in the restaurant business. Stunned by her response, we took a high top table at the bar. It was a good 5 minutes before we were greeted and then it was very apparent that the bar staff were overwhelmed and we weren't going to get good service anyway. We went ahead and ordered drinks however and she brought my drink but stated they were out of one of the key ingredients and never even asked if I would maybe want something else. Then we went to order the calamari which she stated they were also out of. She did not offer or suggest anything else so we just ordered a salad, had our drinks, and tabbed out. Very disappointed as this is our 3rd year wedding anniversary trip and this place had great ambiance and music.

This is a living, breathing piece of music history.  Johnny Cash, Loretta Lynn, Elvis, The Band, you name it, they've played The Ryman (which played host to the Grand Ole Opry program for decades).

It's a great building with church-style seating.  The museum tour is interesting and - for a fee - you can record a song (either from a list of options or an original of your own) in a small on-site recording booth.

Recommended for any music fans, casual or serious, or for anyone generally interested in a slice of American history.
Greasy burger deliciousness and outstanding old school country. Loved this place maybe my favorite in Nashville. Can't wait to hang again.
Great Honkytonk.  Not your biggest not your smallest but the beer is cold and the music is great.  It is a great place to start or end the night

This was my second visit to Sambuca and it was amazing! We went on Saturday 10/4/14 and the band Minnie Murphy was playing. We made reservations for 6 o'clock (only availability unless we wanted to eat at 9:30) I dined with my husband and our two children ages 1 and 3. Yes it is very kid friendly! We were seated in the far left booth in the main dining. Perfect view of the stage. We were promptly greeted by our fabulous server Jordan. We knew we were gonna take the dinner slow because we wanted to see the band (they started at 7)! 
First lets talk about the food. We ordered the bucca beignets, bruschetta, garlic cheese bread, caprese salad, and the house salad to start! All was very very good. The kids enjoyed is all as well. We asked Jordan about the pinot noir selection. He suggested a few but pushed one more so based on our palate. We tried 2 tastings both were good. We trusted our server and order the Meomi Pinot Noir he suggested. He nailed it. It was a delicious bottle! My husband also order a sweet tea, where Jordan told us they didn't have any but could bring some sweetener. A couple minutes pass and he returns with the iced tea and fresh made hot simple syrup! He went above and beyond to get us our sweet tea! He just set the tone for the rest of the night. We were quite stuffed from all our apps but shared the Miso Sea Bass (another suggestion from Jordan) It was Fantastic! I seriously don't know where we put all the food?! 
Once the band started our kids hit the dance floor! They were not a disturbance to any of the guests dining. I actually think those around enjoyed their entertaining. We sat in our both listening to Minnie Murphy who was just as fabulous. The whole night was perfect. The service, the entertainment, the food! We will definitely be back when in town and ask for Jordan!

Yes the venue is loud. Yes the food is yummy. Yes it is kid friendly. Yes theres a patio. Sambucca is at the top of my list for favorite restaurants.

I used to love this place, but this time it was awful:( the service was slow, food was not good, especially for the price, and they cut their portions, and music was so loud my throat hurts from trying to talk to the guests at our table over the music. Used to be a nashville fave, I won't be sad to never return!

The music is alright. Not too loud that you can't hold a conversation towards the back, which is nice. The service is great! Our server made sure our drinks were never empty and our plates were cleared quickly. The gator tots are amazing! The smashville burger was just alright.

The Mother Church of country music! Need I say more?

To see a concert in the Ryman is to be part of history. This is a must do in Nashville. We loved every minute of our Country Classics show.
Wonderful place! Great food, great deserts, friendly atmosphere. Highly recommended and whole family fun!
Great spot for live music! Out of all the bars I visited on my first trip to Nashville last weekend, this bar had the best band playing. Vibe inside is cool and loved all of the boot/wall art!

Visited Nashville for the first time and stopped by this bar first. Band was great and played a variety of music. I'm not a country music fan so it was refreshing as I assumed I'd hear country all night. Fair drink prices and good atmosphere!

This was pretty cool. We did the backstage tour, it was neat to see the rooms, hear some history and get to go on the stage. The displays around the venue are cool, wish we would have known that you have to reserve the make a cd ahead of time, that seemed like it would be fun.
Nice life music. Great margarita. The only bad thing was how to u run out of local beer???!! Such a shame!

I came here on a friends recommendation. She said they have really good burgers. This was definitely true. The burgers were fantastic and fresh. We had appetizers and sides and all were great. Our waitress was friendly and very attentive despite the crowds. They had live music while we were there too. If you have a big party, I'd recommend getting their early.

I took a client to Sambuca for lunch and it was phenomenal! The service was precise and the food was outstanding from the beignets to the sea bass. The flavors were so precise and the ambience was great for lunch. I will be back!
One of the most immersive, memorable multimedia experiences i have ever attended. Fine staff, great story, and even better music history.

I have been to two concerts at the Ryman so far, and both have been great experiences. As a venue, you can't beat it. It has great acoustics and loads of character. When bands play here, it seems like they're really at the top of their game and put on the best show possible.

Ryman Auditorium is an awesome experience with amazing history...I mean Elvis once "left" this building!  Saw two shows here, one comedy show with Fluffy (Gabriel Iglesias) and the other was a kids show.  Great experience and great venue for shows.

During the Gabriel Iglesias show I sat in the upper balcony and it felt very tight.  I am 6"2 and this comedians fans tend to be larger folks... so I was very uncomfortable there between my knees touching the bench ahead and being squeezed by large people from the sides.  

During the kids show we sat towards the front and it was a much better experience.

We went to Nashville for our first time and found this bar on Yelp so figured we'd give it shot. The line was kind of long but it was worth it! Great bartenders and a great atmosphere. The music was really good and just a great time! We found a seat at the bar and stayed for a couple of hours. Will definitely be going back!

This bar on downtown Main Street was a nice atmosphere and had a live band playing on Thursday night. Things I enjoyed about this bar were decent prices for beer, the live band, and a huge big screen playing the NFL Thursday night game. In order to get a 5 star they would need to keep their kitchen open later than 9-10pm and have better customer service. Overall it wasn't a bad experience.

Music and staff were great - location, decor, very good. Food was blah. Macaroni was garnished with brisket, not a lot of meat as implied. Also had the pulled pork nachos and they were just OK.  Overall a good experience but I wouldn't recommend this as a place to eat, especially if you're trying to squeeze only the best into a long weekend. I would gladly go back for drinks though!

Hmmmm... In Nashville for an event or live in Nashville but can't decide where to go?!? I recommend here!! Much different than other Broadway locations they truly pull off live music & sports well.  They have a good TV setup and their bands are decent.  With two floors, multiple bars, outdoor smoking section, plenty of bathrooms, full bar, happy hour, and a decent menu they hit all my top categories!  We have tried multiple places as a "sports bar" all over Nashville and this is in the top 5 and its downtown as an added plus! Come here for your favorite game and you'll not be disappointed!

What I liked:
1. This is phenomenal music venue.  The acoustics are strong and even the back of the house is closer than most shows.
2. The line-ups- whether it's the Opry or an up and coming band, there's terrific variety and I've never seen a bad show there - my first was OCMS and several of the Nashville stars- they were all just terrific.

What I didn't like:
1. Many of the seats are partial view- just beware.

The Verdict:
If you like music, any music, it would be a shame not to have seen a show at the Ryman.

Saw Gabriel "Fluffy" Iglesias here. Great acoustics and very close seats even though we were in the very back. Only gripe is on the lower level in the back, you better hope the performer is shirt. Thankfully Fluffy was! I will be back, but will be sure to get closer seats or balcony!
Loved coming here on our vacation. Fun, food, music, etc. Good times. Will be back. I recommend the fried pickles.
Love this place! The food is excellent, the music doesn't blow your ears out (for those of us tag grew up in the 70's) - can't wait to come back!
We come here just about every time we're on Broadway.  Have a PBR, kick back to some of the best music you'll here anywhere and if you get hungry have a fried bologna sandwich.  Great honky tonk.
Horrible management, completely rude and unmanageable. Never going back- worst place in Nashville. Two thumbs down.

Even though we don't drink, we still stopped by this place to experience Nashville's nightlife. This place was packed on a Saturday night. People were wild. The live music was not bad but I did wish that the band member didn't come around with a tip jar.

Great Happy Hour!! Some of the best cocktails I've had in Nashville. Dinner was delicious. I rarely order a chicken dish but I couldn't pass this one up and I'm glad I didn't! The Shrimp fettuccine was very flavorful! My husband doesn't care for sweet potatoes but he liked the whipped ones here. The Mac and cheese was so creamy! The giant tots were awesome! We will definitely be back. No pictured, the goat cheese stuffed artichokes. Not your typical stuff artichoke, it's the hearts with goat cheese filling.

One of the best places we ate in Nashville. Our waiter, Cory C, was awesome. The red snapper was absolutely incredible and the cheesecake rolls were to die for. The ambience of the place was perfect, good for a romantic dinner or relaxing night on the town. One of the few places we went to that had a live band playing super chill jazz music as well. Overall great atmosphere, great service, and great food.
Love this place! Best music in town, and the fried bologna sandwich and PBR (though not gourmet) is a classic rockabilly staple.

Currently, one Canadian dollar is worth about 89 cents in the United States. So one Canadian woman is worth about...

Actually, I am not going to deliver a punchline. If it's mean (and potentially derogatory) towards Canadians, my fans (my mom, my sister, and that random girl on Facebook who likes my photos that are 37 weeks old) will say I hate Canadian women. 

And if it's nice (and potentially derogatory towards Canadians), my fans (my mom, my sister, and that random girl on Facebook who likes my photos that are 37 weeks old) will I say hate American women. 

Moral of the story: Women are (usually) never happy.

But when it comes to Tin Roof, women can be happy all night long. I saw plenty of them smiling, laughing, and dancing the night away in Music City. Just one quick glance around the room and I knew I wasn't in "Man Jose."

To put it simply, Tin Roof is a small place with a good vibe, strong drinks, and live music. So much good stuff in one place that I ended up drink and dancing with two Canadian girls at once. And that's what it's all "a-boot" in my book. Two is usually better than one. Well, except when discussing the peso and the dollar. 

Anyway, this place was fun. It made me want to move to Nashville. Or possibly the exotic land of "Canadia."

My mom and I came here after our tour guide George from the Country Music Hall of Fame recommended it. We're from California and it was awesome to get some southern hospitality here. We liked it so much that we came back the next day, and both of our bartenders (Hope and Teresa) were AWESOME. I got my fried pickle fix and the drinks and music were great. For anyone visiting downtown Nashville looking for a great, laid back place, this is it!

Went in for the first time, drawn in by the live music.  

Music was great but bar was a little too cramped for me.  We were also really hungry and it took forever to get some pretty basic food.  

Not sure if we'll be returning here when we venture into the city.  

Depending on your taste in country music, this might be a good place for a couple of beers.  Not the place to grab a meal.
Cold cold beer....great service.. KAREN thank you.. Live Music and we enjoyed our Apps.. Just the way we want to start off the night..
Nice little bar on Broadway.  It was not crowded and the people were pleasant. Nothing really stood out making me want to rush back to this bar.
Beautiful convention center! A well designed downtown where it is centrally located. Great things to do in walking distance.

This was my favorite honky tonk that we stopped at. I love dive bars, the band was great, and the bartender made great drinks. We did not order the famous fried bologna sandwich but I have heard great things. Definitely worth a stop while you are on Broadway!
An authentic honky tonk (especially compared to some of the new bars on the strip). Good music. Smells kinda weird inside. The staff we encountered were pleasant.

Hope, you are the most fantastic 'tender of the bar in Nashville. How do we love thee? Let me count the ways.

1. You showed my parents the time of their lives as we spent one night--and one night only--cruising the Broadway strip.

2. Can bust some chops, and bust a move!

3. Is quick-witted and even quicker on the tap.

Seriously, go here. Find Hope. Party on.

This was such a cool place to visit and I highly recommend it. Of course, it's very well recommended and is therefore a tourist magnet but that's ok - they still deliver.

A Honky Tonk band play in the corner at the entrance with several instruments. The room is pumping. People are dancing in front and having an awesome time. The bar is spread out with people against it watching the band. All the tables but one are taken. We grab it and order a beef burger each, $6. These burgers are excellent, my husband said they were among the best he's had which means they're pretty good.

The bad sell CD's for $15 and will sign them or you can just tip at the end of a set. This is so important to do as they're not getting paid by the bar to perform. You don't pay to get in so think about how much you've enjoyed it and tip accordingly. $3 gets you a beer so no big deal, right?

Check it out.

Great music venue. Music sounds wonderful. Hardly a bad seat in the house.  Church pew seating does require the 7th inning stretch. Concessions and meals available. Will be returning to this historic place in downtown Nashville

Not all Honky Tonks are created equal and after coming to the Second Fiddle I began to understand the differences. 

It seemed like this place catered to a slightly older crowd. The band playing when we came on a Saturday night left much to be desired. The lead singer looked so unamused and there were points where she turned her back to the audience or where she was texting during the song. It was really sad to be honest. 

There were a few people dancing on the dance floor but the music wasn't all that entertaining. 

We left at the end of their set for a larger Honky Tonk to listen to good entertainers and better music.

Amazing!!  You have to try the shrimp and crab dip!  The best I've ever had.

My fiancée had fish tacos that she loved. I had shrimp and crab Bisque with a pulled pork Banh Mi which was delicious as well.

The entire experience was great and we'll be back.

On a side note,  ask for Tyler, hands down the best server I've had in years!

Great...  well worth the trip
Stopped by for a drink after a concert , was easy to  get in, ordered cold beer, found A bar ranks to rest a few, staff was friendly. Could see this as a fun place on a busy night
ロンリープラネットで紹介されてた所。4時に行ってもめちゃくちゃ混んでる。朝から常に音楽が演奏されてるらしく、いつ行ってもいい。演奏も上手でカントリー調。店員さんが驚く程美人。

Really great honkeytonk atmosphere in there with the live music and southern feel but WAY too small of a venue. May be good if you go by yourself for a quick couple drinks but if you don't get a table you'll end up cramming up against someone sitting at a table/bar making it awkward. I also found I was moving out of the way a lot for people. Not to add this was on a Monday. It's worth checking out but not a place you'd wanna stay at for too long.
One of my favorite venues in the country. Great history and just absolutely gorgeous.

There's clearly a rich & worthy legacy to this venue & it's obviously well-deserved.  Nashville is after all, widely regarded as "Music City," & this is one of its most famous concert halls.  However, that's not to say there's no room for improvement.

Obviously, the acoustics are outstanding.  But as an audience member, there are issues with comfort & site lines.  As the seating is church pews, I didn't know whether to clap between songs or tell the person seated next to me "Peace be with you."  This seating also leads to the unfortunate habit of "manspreading, which wouldn't happen with individual seats.  

Also problematic were the support beams that obstructed the view for many audience members.  Obviously, had the balcony above come crashing down on them, their view would really have been obstructed, but it seems a design flaw that could be remedied.  I suspect at this point nothing can be done because the building is a landmark? But that's unfortunate.

Finally, their camera policy.  I was there recently for one of two Paul Simon concerts.  Prior to the performance, an announcement was made that CLEARLY stated that photography was allowed, as long as it was no video & non-flash.  So, people began taking photos, until ushers started telling them not to.  So, which is it?  If photography is allowed, inform your ushers prior to the show.  If it's not, don't play a pre-recorded announcement confusing 2000+ audience members.

Otherwise, it's a lovely venue inside an out & the Ryman should be part of your Nashville experience.

Hi, I'm Matt and I don't really like country music.  Why on earth did the wife get us a backstage small tour of this place?  Almost all of my country music history came from the Graceland and Sun Studio tours in Memphis, but you know what?  This tour was interesting and our tour guide was knowledgeable and passionate about the Ryman.  I loved hearing about the follow up from stories we heard in Memphis about Elvis and other country singers.

Frequent stopping point for us each time we're in nashville. Fried pickles, bologna sandwiches and cheeseburger on Texas toast can't be beat!! Quick, tasty, and entertaining as well. Definitely recommend.
Great atmosphere, great music, friendly staff. We stopped in during a bachelorette trip this weekend and ended up staying until closing time. Loved it
An absolute must even if you are not a Country fan. Nice video presentation on the history of the building as well as familiar exhibits. Good fun for the family
The bartenders were goofing off & not paying attention to the customers the doorman called my wife Grandma, the band were poor. This was easily the worst club on Broadway!

The venue in itself is not bad. It intimate. However there are several support columns that will block you view. Now the issue I had was the valet parking. After the show, it was well over 2 hours before we were able to retrieve our cars. And that was because we walked (a group of about 20 ppl) and followed the valet drivers to get our car for a garage a block away. I would so recommend this auditorium but not the valet parking.

Best honky tonk on Broadway, hands down. I tried going to other honky tonks but the music was never as authentic and the crowd was never as lively like at Robert's. I went there on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday night, and every single day the bands were just as good and the crowd just as rowdy. The bands they showcase are always extremely talented and put on an awesome performance. 

The beers are dirt cheap too. I haven't tried their food but it looks good! The service is also very friendly and attentive despite how loud it is in there.

This place is the only honky tonk you should go to. And ALWAYS tip the band and the servers, it's only common courtesy. It's just plain rude for you to not tip the band performing their hearts out.
very nice auditorium and explanation of history. country music stuff such as minnie pearl's hat and shoes and plenty of country/western outfits that stars wore over the years. - pretty good

This place is one of my favs on Broadway if you're looking to just hang out, have some drinks, and listen to some good music.  The past two times I came to Nashville this was the bar we hung out at before we went out to get wild.  The staff is super friendly as well.
Great spot, tons of history, random memorabilia throughout (check out the hallway on the way to the restrooms), reasonably priced drinks & approachable bartenders.

Okay, these five stars come with a bit of a caveat. It is not 5-star food. It's not really 5-star service either, though the staff is impossibly sweet if you treat them the same. These five stars are because when you go to Nashville you have to experience something truly honky tonk -- like really, really honky tonk. 

If you're lucky enough to be in town on a Monday, definitely go check out John England & The Western Swingers, a staple at RWW. They're super genuine, mega-talented, and worth the effort.

While you're there, order a fried bologna sandwich (and while they're making it for you, try your best to dispel what you think this amazing treat might be -- it'll be worth it!) ... We also had the chicken strips which were pretty much of the generic drop-and-fry variety, but good nonetheless.

Again, nothing about this place is 5-star, but if any place should get 5 stars on Yelp, it's this one.

This place was crowded all day and night...but what else would you expect from one of the original honky tonks in Nashville,right? We were still able to find a table way in the back, which suits me just fine since we only want to hear the music no need to "see" the music too...my first ever fried boloney sandwich washed down with ice cold beer and surrounded by great music and musical history was just perfect.
the food was really good, the service - justine - was really, really good and the entertainment was over the top.  a great break from the cma's.

$2.50 PBRs and live country music made our Monday afternoon in Nashville. Our server was busy but beautiful and sweet. This place was recommended to us by a local as the only authentic bar on the strip.

Beyond expectations! If you are in Nashville, this is a must! This place has the best of everything! I can't tell you how amazing the food is here. Martin makes sure that you are taken care of and that you leave happy!

Hands-down one of the most acoustically perfect venues I've ever been in. It's an old space, so choose your seats carefully. But you'll be surprised to discover the old pews are remarkably comfortable. Parking is in garages and surface lots - do a bit of research to find the best deal. But overall, once you arrive, sit back and enjoy the show. It will be WONDERFUL. I promise!

This place is like Candy to a fat kid, Crack to a druggie or rubbing alcohol to Kitty Dukakis. 

Amazing time watching Greg Allman. I had side seats and thought it would be troubling to see but it wasn't. 

The acoustics, the lights, the shear fact of being in the Ryman made this one of the best places I've seen a concert. 

Staff was great (will call and greeters), place to get a drink was very convenient and the people was a great mix of young and old. This was, and IS, the place for me to get a music groove on.
We visited from California this week. Such a fun bar. Great bands both times we stopped in and loved the fried bologna sandwiches and onion rings!

This place is embarrassing. The door guy didn't let me in on Friday "because I was stumbling" meanwhile he let some bachelorette party girls in who could barely walk in. I guess it didn't help that I'm Latino. This place is off my list. I guess racism is still alive and well on Broadway.

This is a GREAT place to come for a bach. party or fun night out with a group. It is almost like being at a wedding reception. You can run up and dance with the band, go back and forth to table. The service was excellent! Food was very good. Price range is great for a group. Pizza is $12 and main dishes are around $30. I thought it was such a fun atmosphere. It is loud, but less than what I imagined. I wouldn't go here to have a serious date night or with a serious group of people. I will recommend this to friends.

Came for lunch while in Nashville, and it was by far the best meal I've had in months! You have to try the shrimp and crab dip...I honestly wasn't expecting much but this blew me away! For lunch I had the fish tacos and the portion was enormous! Highly recommend them, they are beyond stuffed and the shell doesn't fall apart. My fiancé had the soup, salad and 1/2 sandwich. It was a full sized salad and the sandwich was overstuffed with goodness! Our server Tyler was the best, he couldn't do enough to ensure we had an amazing meal. He also helped us plan out the best places to see and things to do for the remainder of our visit and made some great recommendations. Can't wait to come back!

Horrible experience. We were actually having a decent time until two new bartenders showed up. One was just nasty. Mean!  I guess that's why he is where he is. I can't believe he hasn't had his ass kicked. The cute blonde was great and witnessed this asshole being rude. It was 4/21/16. I'll be interested to see if anybody gives a crap. If they don't fire that dick I'll never be back. Actually,I don't care what they do. If the manager is stupid enough to allow somebody like that to serve drinks than they don't care if anybody comes back. Huge tourists trap.

I will never return to this bar, solely because of how my group was treated by a bartender. He was messing around with a female bartender, spraying her with the water from the fountain drink gun. He got out of control and sprayed a few of us standing on the other side of the bar. I was visibly upset, but before I could even say anything he arrogantly barked, "Get over it, you're in a bar". I informed him that I was aware of where I was, asked for our check and left. Wasn't looking for any freebies or anything, just a simple "sorry about that" or some sort of apology, whether genuine or not.

The best place to see a concert IMO and i have been to lots of venues, including many in NYC. The only negative is the seating, as some people don't really fit in their seats and might hang into yours.
Great fried bologna sandwich! Good drinks and fun music. This isn't one of the super popular places so it's a little easier to get into. Loved it!
Recession Special = PBR, fried bologna, a bag of Lays, live honky tonk in the morning and smiles!

What a fun place to eat some junk food, drink beer and listen to an old style country band with a fiddler!!  I had the fried bologna sandwich with onion rings and loved it!  The drawback, it needs a good deep cleaning!
Great music. Food was than acceptable but the service was absolute horrendous. Unless you went up to a bar you were blatantly ignored.

Came here a few nights ago with a large party.

Let me start with the good - essentially, the only reason why I didn't give this place 1 star. Those at my table who ordered a drink said that the drinks were good, and the atmosphere at the place is pretty cool as well. 

First of all, we sat down around 7 and it took over an hour for our salads to even come. We were starving by this point, they refused to even bring us some bread or chips. The server was VERY rude, giving everyone an attitude when they asked for something simple, like a refill.

By the time our salads came, I didn't even care that there was barely any dressing on it... I ate it anyway. We waited another hour almost for our meals to come.

I ordered the chicken and beef skewers, which were disgusting. They were extremely cold and absolutely tiny. The "vegetables" were sad mushy squash and zucchini. Some of my coworkers ordered the steak, which was good. I should have ordered it!

Dessert came - I skipped it, but my coworkers said that it was fine.

Definitely would never come to this place again by choice, which is unfortunate, because the vibe is cool and it seems like they might have better food if you're in a smaller party. But if you have a big group - don't come here unless you want to spend 2 1/2 hours for dinner.

Came here for a work dinner with approx 100 colleagues. We had rented out the sky loft and had a fixed menu. The service was great, however, the food was cold when we received it. I understand that there were quite a few of us, however. I ordered a steak medium rare but it came out well done. Will give this place another shot when I come back to Nashville (without 100 other colleagues:))
Great service and food! I had the sea bass and half of my friends prime rib that was humongous! Definitely would recommend!
Why is that bologna sandwich so good? It just is! And it's even better to have it with a brew while enjoying some great music! Of all the spots on Broadway, this was easily among my favorites.

We loved our self-guided tour of the Ryman! The video knocked our socks off, we were definitely not expecting it to be as amazing and interesting as it was! This venue has so much history and it really is a fascinating spot to wander through. All of the staff people we encountered were very friendly and helpful as well! Especially the gentleman who took the time to explain all of the photos outside the theater room! Loved it!
Wow! Loved the atmosphere. Came here late night on a Sunday night - had really good small plates & the live jazz was so awesome! Definitely returning

I really liked the timeline in the Ryman telling about the history of the building, it's occupants, and the Opry. It helped piece things together. This and a few other exhibits are part of the self guided tour. 

The guided tour add on is way to go - it is only $4 more. You can do the self guided museum before and/or after the guided tour that allows you to see backstage. Granted the views are not amazing - and you can't take  pictures behind stage - but the guide is full of knowledge. Each dressing room you visit is themed and full of pictures and the guide goes through all the pictures with you telling you the story of the singers pictured.

The venue is classic. it's a wonderful building and the acoustics are great.

The only thing that I am not a fan of is some of the acts they book. Rock concerts are not meant for this venue. There are pillars obstructing the view and I felt awful listening to some of the lyrics of these rock bands coming out of their mouths as I stood in a church pew. If you are to buy tickets, your experience would be well worth your money if you bought closer to the stage, for sure.

Went here for a girlfriend's bachelorette party. They were super nice even though the bride got stuck in traffic and was a half hour late. Our food was all really good. My favorite part was the upstairs bartender, Eric! He made the whole night better. We had a few drinks and an app. upstairs with him while waiting on the bride and the rest of the party. He was a lot of fun, very helpful with the menu, and made the night great!  Thanks Eric!
Great place for an inexpensive meal.  Limited menu but really good food and entertainment.  Yucca fries were the big winner in our group.

I would have rather stopped in for a drink to listen to the band and gone elsewhere for our meal. The bartender paid no attention even when drinks were empty and never checked in once the food arrived. There were only two others at the upstairs bar so the beer got restocked instead. The food was just ok. If I would do it again I would stick to an appetizer at best and move on for better food.

Petty cool experience on a Friday night.  We ordered the Fried Bologna sandwich and Mozzarella sticks.. mehh nothing to brag about there.
If you take the cool atmosphere and live music into consideration, overall, we had a fun time.

This is a review of the backstage tour. We did the backstage tour because everyone said is wast "AMAZING." So, of course my expectations were high. I didn't understand my tour guide. I should have asked for a refund but I didn't. If you make reservations ahead of time you pay a premium with service charges. There is a $3 off coupon in the "whereMAPS Nashville" brochure (it has a pair of cowboy boots on the front). If you don't have one, you can pick one up at the Ryman. When you walk into the first set of doors at the Ryman, there is a section where you can pick up lots of brochures. In my opinion, I didn't think it was worth $49 for two people. For that much money I was expecting something more. While I think the Ryman has history I would have much rather bought tickets for an actual show instead of just a tour.

Exactly what I was looking for. Great aspiring band, friendly and observant bartender, and delicious low-priced food. Basic sandwiches, appetizers, and domestic/import bottles, this place is an easy stop along Broadway. A beer and burger will run you just over $10.

This place was fun!  We were here celebrating a friends 40th bday. The service was reasonable considering it was busy :)). The bday girl got on the stage to sing and the band was awesome and super friendly. We'll be back next trip :))

First time here and very impressed. The food was amazing, the atmosphere awesome, live music very entertaining, and Jordan our waiter was attentive. World class customer service and quality restaurant. Would definitely come back and recommend to anyone in town!!! 

Appetizer- shrimp and crab dip! (Great taste and portion) 
Meal- pork chop (flavorful and well made) 
           Flat iron steak (quality meat with taste) 

Today is a Friday night and the band is keeping everyone engaged!

My favorite place on Broadway! We don't venture to Broadway often, but always bring visitors to Robert's when they want to do the tourist thing. By far the most laid back, fun, live music environment.  Plus they have decent drink prices.

This facility is beautiful.  I've been spending the past few days here for a nutrition conference where there are 10k of us and the space accommodates us nicely.  The facility has a very friendly staff and well maintained restrooms.  Many conference centers are confusing navigate around but this one is not. All rooms are nice and easy to find.  

The one downside is that food on site is kind of pricy but that's expected.  Loved that the country music hall of fame is across the street and it made for the perfect lunch break.

If you are looking for an event space in Nashville I'd definitely suggest looking into Music City Center.

The Mother Church of Country Music! We really enjoyed this being unfamiliar with the history of the Ryman. The video with holograms that you start out with was the perfect length of time and detail in my opinion. The building is beautiful. We did the self guided tour and enjoyed being able to listen/read as much as we wanted. 

They do have a AAA discount I think it's 2$ off per person. 

We went soon after opening which it wasn't crowded yet which I'm sure led to such a positive experience for us. 

We chose to go here over the country music hall of fame museum and glad we did!

Came here for dinner on Wednesday night. What a disappointing evening. As noted in Alex's review from 2011, you can't ignore the band because they are completely in your face. I don't wish to complain; they weren't bad but if I had wanted to go to hear a band play, I would have gone to a bar. I went there with a large group, and was supposed to have a set menu but a few of us went off piste and ordered appetizers. I'm so glad that we did. The beignets were lovely and creamy and the lobster and crab were seriously tasty. The fried oyster had been obliterated by the cooking process and was just a hard lump of batter. The chicken samosa was good. The entrees were not so good. The steak came with a weird sauce and no sides. I would have ordered something had I known. i didn't even touch the set menu dessert.
Service was good and friendly though. Wine was quaffable.
No thank you to the rest Sambuca!

Food was a 1 star
Service and bar/band was 4.5 stars

By the reviews of this place maybe I just ordered the wrong item. I had the crab and avocado sandwich and it was not good at all...2 bites was all I could eat. Basically they opened a can of crab meat and used a half of a slice of avocado on ciabatta bread--no effort was put into this sandwich 

The drinks and the band was great and it's hard to beat their location. Next time I will try something else just not that sandwich
Hands down best honky tonk on Broadway. Superb musicians, cold beer, and hot grilled bologna sandwiches.
Nice bar. Was in Nashville over the fourth and went here a couple times. Fun band, friendly staff, yummy food. Pretty spacious and good upstairs 'outdoor' area that's unique.

I've gone on a quick tour in the Ryman when I first moved to Nashville, but I never came here for a show.  The Ryman showcases all kinds of music that Nashville has to offer like bluegrass, blues, country, classical, folk, gospel, jazz, and other types.  I came to see the Americana Music Awards this year and it was really entertaining but I gotta say, a 3 hour special sitting in hardwood pews is not great for the derriere. Aside from that, it seemed like a great location for a show, especially since its the "Mother church of country music" and supposedly the birthplace of country music and Bluegrass.  So much history.  If you're a fan of Nashville, you gotta at least know a little bit about the Ryman.

Music was good. Food was fair. I had a chicken Cobb salad. The chicken was bland. It needed more seasoning. The other couple shared the teriyaki chicken wings. They said they were tasty but smothered in sauce. The fish and chips were also only fair. The chips came out ice cold and undercooked. They did make new fries which were hot but a little on the hard side. Cole slaw was inedible.

The worst food ever. I had to actually spit out the coke slaw it was rancid! I have never spit out food before! I ordered the Mac and cheese with bacon... came cold and trust me I LOVE Mac and cheese. I did not even eat it! Worst Mac and Cheese ever! Hubby got the voodoo hoagie and average at best! Don't spent your money on food here. The server did not even ask why we did not eat the food....... totally bummed! Skip it!!

This was one of the more fun spots on Broadway that I visited recently, mostly because I felt like the crowd here was better than at some of the other honky tonks. Like others, Tin Roof had great live music, strong drinks, and a cool atmosphere lighted by strings of Christmas lights across the ceiling. Didn't eat anything, but enjoyed the strong dranks!

Not a very kid friendly place. Didn't have access to silverware- to cut a hotdog for my baby. Also, no changing table in bathrooms.   Hamburger was less than good. The group playing music made the place earn my stars.

Delicious food but their reservation system is currently not pulling open table reservations so call to confirm. Thankfully we had out reservation confirmation so they helped us out and found a way to get us seated in a full house! Server had a little attitude but overall did a good job. Trendy and enjoyable ambiance, good was delicious and they have a little something for everyone!
Great place to start your downtown experience, we went on a Saturday afternoon the band playing was great.
Always love coming here and seeing the history of this place even beyond the country music!! Recommend coming if your in town!!

Great Spot to stop into for some live music, drinks and food. Drinks are fairly priced and the food is cheap. I had a bologna sandwich "Delicious", my boyfriend had a burger with onion rings. Onion rings were so good, we had to order an additional basket. The Service was great and the atmosphere was friendly. Definitely a "GoodTime". I'm hoping to stop by before my visit ends.

We stopped in for a drink and appetizer on a Sunday afternoon while visiting Nashville. Aside from being sat on the patio and then not being waited on for 10 minutes everything was good. I had their version of a moscow mule, which wasn't served in the typical copper mug but was still good. We also had the Bruschetta, which was good.

What can I say about this historic building that has not already been said? This place has the vibe of greatness. Everyone who's anyone has performed here over the last 100 or so years. It's updated at the entrance and in the lobby but the theater itself still has the old pews. We saw Jeff Foxworthy here and I want to come back to see a music act and hopefully the spirit of Minnie Pearl!

Nice upscale place for jazz brunch! Loved the venue and location, and the live music was great. We had a large group and they did a great job accommodating us. Drinks were great, and the Bloody Mary bar had a lot of fun add ins. I didn't love my burger or dessert, and service was super slow - 3 hours for brunch. I originally rated this a 3, but my friends argued for a 4 so I went with mob rule.

Was craving a hot dog and live music.  Many other places stopped playing at 10 pm and kitchens were closed, but not here!  Place keeps going strong.  Good band selection and vibe.  Hot dog was good too.
The food and drinks are SO good. The entertainment is free and Tito's play land is great for the kids. Definitely a fun spot to go to! Gauchos is my favorite. Anything you order is amazing.

Great live music bar.  We ordered the chicken and waffle bites (they were life-changing), fried pickles were good, brisket nachos were to die for and chicken fingers were spicy similar to Cajun.  

Great music! Also for a bar, this is an impressively clean bar.

The music is outstanding. The bartenders are friendly, and the food is awesome. There are decent vegetarian options, and the fried cheese sticks rule. The atmosphere is fun and the crowd is always diverse, made up of  many generations from all over! This is not a bar to have a conversation at, it's perfect for listening to great musicians, people watching, and drinking!

Amazing place to visit if you're a country music fan. Standing in the auditorium where country music became what it is today is an amazing feeling. The Ryman is well kept and the exhibits were great to see. The introductory video was very cute. Everything was very clean.
Great for hanging out and getting drinks. The food wasn't very good. I'd go back for a night out but not for a meal.
This place was fun,  lots of great cheap food & drink choices.  We are here and had a fried bologna sandwich.  It was very good.  Sweet tea kept flowing and the live music was perfect.

Eclectic environment, live music and amazing food! This restaurant exceeded my expectations. Staff was attentive and courteous.  Highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great place to eat in Nashville.
Pretty much the standard crazy bar on Broadway. Band playing the night I was there was awesome which made the place. Get the wrong band in there and it wouldn't be anything special.

A co-worker recommended this place for dinner on Friday night and it was a great recommendation! The restaurant was packed and we didn't have a reservation so we grabbed a table in the bar area. Almost everything we ordered was really good:

- Bianca flatbread (5.0 stars): This was not low-calorie, but was worth every calorie!  The crust was thin and crispy, which is partially why I liked it so much.
- Grilled Polenta with chicken added (4.0 stars): I thought this was good (enjoyed all of the veggies and different flavors together), but the polenta cake was a little too dense and dry. I'm glad I added the grilled chicken as it was hard to eat all of the polenta.
- Spring Chicken (5.0 stars): This was really, really good.  Who knew cauliflower puree with brussell sprouts could be so good?!

The ambiance was nice (live music), but I'm docking one star as service was really slow.  Our appetizer arrived and was consumed before our bottle of wine did.
Hands Down one of the coolest spots I have been to. This is the epitome of the Downtown Nashville experience. Cant wait to go back

Strange stadium set-up. I went there to watch a Queens of the Stone Age concert when I immediately realized this was not the preferred design for a rock concert. This place is much more suited for conventions, as a roller rink, or sporting arena. The acoustics are not great and the dome from the inside is off-putting and makes the entire place look run-down.
Beautiful, historic, legendary. Do the tour and see a show. Then head down to Robert's for a "stimulus package."

Two stars: 1 for quality napkins and 1 for guacamole. 

Everything else I could have definitely gone without. From the service to the salad, this place fell short in so many ways. If you're looking for a tourist trap with crappy service and mediocre food at best, then look no further! 

Seat yourself at a table that has yet to be cleared and then wait 15 minutes for a staff member to finally notice your presence. Sound great? But wait, there's more! After ordering, be prepared to suffer a solid 45 minutes for your food. This better be good right!? Well not to burst anyone's bubble, but once your order finally arrives you'll find that the $10 citrus salad you ordered is actually side salad proportion and that the kitchen didn't take the time to seed any of the citrus...fantastic if you ask me (not!) 

Do yourself a favor by avoiding Broadway altogether and look into more local favorites for a true Nashville experience.

PS the quesadilla made my mom violently sick.
Had 4 tickets to see a show on Thursday, October 25, 2018 and they had moved the show to Grand Ole Opry without any notification. Who does that in this electronic communications age?

I have been to Sambuca several times and each time the food has been amazing! The service is almost always amazing as well, although we have had so-so service on occasion. 

The Chicken Samoas are amazing but I do wish they came in a larger size. Their cocktails are unique and fun, I love the Mojito! 

The vibe is what keeps me coming back again and again; it's the perfect place for a date night, a celebration, or to wow out-of-town guests!

Just got back from a Nashville trip, and this bar was the most fun we had while we were there.  My boyfriend & I are NOT country music fans ("Then why were you in Nashville?") but we popped into Robert's and listened to The Silver Threads play and they were INCREDIBLE.  Not only were they a solid band, but they really knew how to work the crowd.  It's not a 5-star establishment by any means, but I wouldn't call it a dive, either.  We ate the fried bologna sandwich, and that was quite tasty :)

Came here last weekend to celebrate my friend's upcoming nuptials. Everything was amazing! Our table was waiting for us when we arrived so we did not have to wait. The band, ambiance, drinks, and food were all up to par. Loved this place! I highly recommend the crap dip, it was soooo good! If ever, in the area check this place out!
Just go sit, eat, listen to live music, watch acrobatics. For kids, teens, and adults. FUN

The architecture was stunning.  You can tell people really took the time and effort to make this place special. Live music all day. Fantastic food. And the popsicles were amazing. Most food was tapas style so u can try many things.

Honestly this was not the best experience. I planned a dinner for a 14 girl bachelorette party. I had worked with the manager to setup a pre fixe dinner that was 38 dollars each. I also had arranged for the brides aunt to have a round of drinks sent over. The service was good but the food was absolutely terrible. Myself and a few other girls had  to have their meals sent back as they were not edible. The meal i got as a replacement was not good either. I sent the manager two emails to explain my frustration and have yet to hear back. I expressed my frustration to our waiter and he did take off a 4 % gratuity charge but that really did nothing for us, as it wasnt his fault and we all still tipped 20 percent. I will be back there soon and based off  the way they handled this, i will not be returning.

I'm not used to going with a place that has great food and great musical acts. You usually get one but not both. But given it's Nashville which is all about live music it's all very possible. This is a great venue for music because you can sit and have a full meal or just hang out at the bar. It's even more awesome they pipe the music into the bathrooms so you don't miss anything!

My girlfriend and I did the tour. We were able to walk right up and purchase tickets for $22 each. She had been dying to go and I obliged and actually had a really good time. 

It starts with a 15-minute interactive video that was my favorite part. It is truly a unique experience. 

After that we toured the facility on our own and there was a lot of cool memorabilia to see and take pictures of. The whole feel in there is like you're in a church, with all the seating being like church pews. You could tell there was a lot of history in the building. 

There isn't really that much to see and you shouldn't need more than an hour to do the entire tour. At $22 I think they are priced too high for how small it is, it's worth about $15. However, it was really a lot of fun!

This was a stop on our Nashville City Tour.  I was not familiar with it until we showed up on the bus and went in to see it.  It is best known for being the home of the Grand Ole Opry from 1943 to 1974.  And if you are a fan of County Music and Bluegrass, and who isn't, you are sort of making a pilgrimage when you visit.  As we walked around we saw a lot of pictures representing a lot of history of the Nashville sound.  We were told it is still used occasionally today to host the Grand Ole Opry at certain times of the year.

When it originally was completed, it opened as the Union Gospel Tabernacle, and Christian revival meetings were held there.  Although it was originally intended as a house of worship, through a sequence of unforeseen circumstances it eventually came to be used for speaking engagements, concerts, boxing matches, etc. in order to be able to pay for the upkeep on the building.

After moving in and having a long and successful run at the Ryman, the Opry moved to its new and modern location at Opryland and the Ryman was almost demolished.  But because it was such a key part of the history of Nashville, the community and a number of investors raised the funds to have it restored and it is still in active use today.  I thoroughly enjoyed being able to go inside and learn about the history and importance of this building to Nashville.  Check it out if you are in the area.
Great Music! Fabulous onion Rings! We popped in several of the bars along the strip in Nashville. This was our favorite!!

Clearly a great place for visitors and locals. Cheap beer  and tastey food.  Just wish the bartenders would stay off their phones. Never seen a bartender at  a busy bar ignore customers to get on their phone.

Had a business dinner here and it was fabulous. Corey, our server, was warm, informative and provided excellent service. The menu offered a great selection of unique entrees. I was the only vegan in the group and my dinner that started with roasted beets and followed with the polenta dish was delicious!  The snapper my associates ordered was flavorful and beautifully presented. Add a great wine selection and you can't go wrong. Highly recommend and I will add this to my new favorites.

We did the regular tour at the Ryman (not the backstage tour) and I really enjoyed it. They explain the entire history of the Ryman (I didn't know any of it) in an entertaining way. The video at the beginning of the tour was my favorite. I loved the parallels between the origins of the Ryman (as a church) to present day (as some people hold music in a similar regard), and as a place where anyone can gather and enjoy the spirit of music. The facility itself is not much to look at, but the history is pretty mind-blowing when you see who has been there and what the stage has held... Helen Keller, Charlie Chaplin, Harry Houdini, Jackie Robinson, Johnny Cash, countless rock stars and country singers, the birth of bluegrass, the list goes on and on and on. It was really amazing to think about. 

The perimeter of the Ryman includes some exhibits with old costumes, video, and artifacts that were pretty cool. Overall the video at the beginning was my favorite, along with the hallway full of old Hatch Show Print tour posters (amazing!) and the area with the display of all who have graced the stage at the Ryman. Super cool for any history or music lover.

Legends Corner is a fun bar located on Broadway, however it can get a little bit crowded at times. I stopped by twice while visiting Nashville and both times there were live bands playing on the small stage located in the front of the bar. There is an open area which was pretty crowded with people listening and drinking both nights, however there is an area up a few stairs near the back of the bar which was less crowded and even had its own bar. This is where I spent most of my time as it was easier to relax, while still hearing the music.

Another plus is the side door, which makes entry much easier during peak times. The Broadway entrance can get backed up pretty quick on busy nights so the 5th street entrance usually had much lighter lines which made getting in much easier. I recommend a stop on your visit to Nashville, who knows you might see a rising legend before they become famous!

Our service was impeccable. I ordered the ribeye with scalloped potatoes and asparagus. All cooked perfectly; my only complaint is that it wasn't /quite/ hot enough, but so much that it was offensive. Our server, Robbie, dealt with 9 ladies--each with substitutions--and two drink returns (us not knowing our own tastes) without even a hint of irritation. His suggestions were spot-on, and his service timely and thorough.

The worst bar I have ever been in. They totally made my husband and I feel unwelcome. No service. And while my husband was away from his chair the bouncer came and took it.
I told him my husband was sitting in it. He told me that he had to move it to the back because they had to keep a certain amount of chairs back there. He also took a chair from the people sitting behind us. They also told him someone with their party was sitting in it.  We will never set foot in that place again.
Solid upscale dining/live music combo! The blackened snapper was perfect and the scallops were cooked just right. Bottle of pro secco was reasonably priced and the service was great!

If you love country music and history, this tour is a must!  We really enjoyed the guided tour and were able to go backstage.  So much wonderful history here.  Also saw a top notch evening show  here.  Seats are wooden church pews, which are not all that comfortable, but they rent cushions if you wish for $5.  The food at Cafe Lula, just outside is also very fresh and good.

Took husband on Friday for a surprise date night...what a wonderful evening out! From Shevar (the gentleman who greeted us) to the excellent service of our waiter, Aaron and bartender, Frank. Aaron was fantastic walking us through the menu and helping us decide on one of the best meals we've had in awhile...btw, the beet appetizer was incredible. Can't wait to get back there SOON! A+++

Great space, food, and hospitality. Attended a conference here as a Nashville native and loved every moment. The food, drink, and rooms were superb. Definitely come check out music city center if you get the chance, the environment is unlike any other in the region.
If you expect to eat here then grab a snack before you go.  We have been here 30 minutes and still haven't had order taken.  Thank goodness the music is good.  Will go to another place to eat.
The Heartbeat and the Soul of Nashville. America's Greatest Bar! This bar makes your favorite bar look like Applebee's!

This is my go to lunch restaurant. I love the atmosphere inside, and their patio is equally marvelous. The lunch menu has lots of options, you can mix and match a variety if salad, soup, sandwich options. The best part? Apparently no one else in Nashville ever thinks to stop in for lunch! I have never had to wait for a seat, and the restaurant usually only has a few occupied tables. Makes it a fantastic place if you need something conducive for a conversation with clients or colleagues. 
I'm not as big of a fan for dinner - still love the atmosphere, but the menu just isn't my style at night. If I could rate lunch and dinner separately I would give them 5 & 3 stars respectively.

I used their catering service for a work luncheon.  Delivery was very prompt and friendly.   Their food (boxed lunches) were good no doubt, but what stole the show for me was the chocolate chip cookies (very addicting!).  When I asked everyone on a scale of what they thought, they rated Sambuca a 7 out of 10.

Wow,  Great food!  Is it a bar? a night club? a restaurant?  We were a little concerned with the live music every night, thought it may be too loud and drown out conversation, but we were right up front and the music was to a perfect level so we could carry out a nice conversation.  And the music was great.  Perfect blend between Jazz, blues, and piano bar.  Very fun and a different dining experience than anywhere else in Nashville.  The only reason it's only 4 stars is because you can't do 4.5 stars and the service was a little off.  The server was great, but the food came out a little quick before the wine, so we felt a little rushed, maybe they are turning tables??  I noticed that when we made the reservation on open table, that the restaurant said there was a two hour limit for our table??  a little weird, but still great fun!  Will go back for sure.

A Nashville must see. The Ryman is full of history, from the steep staircases to the stainedglass windows, this place is legit. We opted for the self guided tour, but spend an extra $11.00 and take the guided tour.

Wow! This place is so much fun and they have great food. If you're into Spanish music like salsa and mariachi, this is the place to go. I definitely recommend this place. Will come back for salsa night and lotería night.

I come in town for work regularly and found this place not knowing it was a chain. I thought it was an original. The service is usually great, the beignets are delicious, drinks are made well and a nice variety of them. I usually get the caprese salad or beignets and sometimes a filet, and filets are cooked perfectly. Service was slow this time for things I requested- pepper, steak sauce, check....but I sat outside so I'll go with that. Nice location in The Gulch, but a little pricey depending what you get. They do have a happy hour and live music...when I'm not sure. Even with all the good restaurants around, I'll be back.

I visited this restaurant while in Nashville for a conference. Great atmosphere, amazing food, the best service (ask for Matt). Matt did an incredible job at recommending apps, entrees and desserts. Everything was so good. We were so stuffed! The music was nice as well. I highly recommend this restaurant.

FIRST:  request Jesse as your waiter. 
SECOND:  order & enjoy
THIRD: the music (if they keep  it at an enjoyable volume) is a highlight. 
FOOD.  Miso Sea Bass.  Filet Mignon.  Duck appy  Roasted Beets  veggie lasagna  polenta - enjoyed all
Great dinner. Had the scallops, was expecting creamy risotto and it was firm only downfall. Service was great.

This is a great bar with some really good folks working there and great live music.  Drinks are reasonably priced and served up quickly.  It has a good vibe and is worth a stop if you are in Nashville.

My husband really wanted to go here and listen to some "not pop country". It did not disappoint. I'm a little sad that we had already eaten because the fried bologna sandwiches looked really good. The atmosphere was great and we'll totally be going back during our visit.
Fantastic! Great service, great music. The burgers were good and the atmosphere was terrific. I liked it so much, I went there twice in the same day.
Came here based on a recommendation for some people on the street. It couldn't have been a better welcome to Nashville with the fired pickles and friend bologna. The live entertainment was great too!

Overall, I had a good experience. The restaurant itself is very nicely decorated and has a great atmosphere. However, I think the live music kind of cheapens it/makes it difficult to actually have a high class dinner. The music is good, but it's really loud and is only a few feet away from where everyone is sitting.

The food was good- the chicken puff pastry appetizers were wonderful and I highly recommend them. The margarita shrimp entree was a little lacking in the flavor department. The snapper was very well-liked by my boyfriend but it was a little too strong tasting for my liking. The berry cobbler dessert was also delicious.

Overall, I would go back but I would go early, maybe around 5:30 when the band isn't playing. I think the band starts around 7, so if you don't really like listening to it while you eat, you should get there early. It's a very good restaurant but just not great!
So much fun!! Great music and great bartenders!! Corone served the best drink I had all weekend!! I don't mind paying for quality drinks as long as it's " quality"!! Very professional and FUN!!

I did the backstage tour and I do not regret it. You go through the dressing rooms and walk across the stage while a guide gives you some valuable info. Afterwards you are free to walk around and see the exhibits around the walls. It is beautiful perfection. What a piece of history. You do not want to miss this.
Robert's is my favorite Honky Tonk in Nashville! They have some of the most talented country performers on Broadway street.  For under $4, the baloney sandwich is a solid deal.
Best honky tonk in Nashville! My husband and I always have a blast here.   Carolyn always provides great service for us!

M- yes we had a good experience here the food was pricey but it's quality was appropriate. I did have a fall down on the bisque it was flat needed a bit of chicken base a dash of sherry and a sprig of dill. Also a bit of meat may have justified the price. The music was also very good and added to the atmosphere. Filet and lobster were very good as the scallops. Service was stellar
Tasty enough but biscuit sliders were not biscuits and very small for the price. The tater tots were good but small again

Legends never fails to entertain. The bands are always good and know what to play for the late night crowd. Always super fun and upbeat.  Drinks aren't that expensive and it is a staple of the downtown scene right across from Bridgestone and Rippys.  I do not think they have food, or if they do, I am not sure that is where I would eat with so many other options.  But again, always a ball and a must stop spot on Broadway.
By far the most fun we've had.  No need to go anywhere else. The music was great. We will definitely make this a regular stop. Nothing else on the Strip came close.

An awesome find on Broadway! Cheap Busch Lights, live music, and a dive bar atmosphere in the heart of the city. This place was much more laid back and affordable than anywhere else I found on the strip.

My wife and I saw Alanis Morissette here last fall. The show was awesome, and the venue is absolutely incredible. It's such an intimate setting, and the acoustics are amazing. The Ryman is such a beautiful place, and attending a concert here should be on everyone's bucket list.
One of the best experiences while we were in Nashville recently! Amazing talent! The friend bologna sandwhich was also amazing. I can not wait to visit again!!!!

The MultiMedia presentation at the start of the tour was phenomenal, I would enjoy watching it again.

The Ryman has soul, there is an energy that one can feel. It is a beautiful place, I would love to see the Grand Ole Opry there. 

So much history, I'm glad it was restored.

This place was AWESOME!! It was our first time visiting Nashville and if anything made an impression, it was this joint! We walked up and I saw a kid singing on stage through the window, then saw another kid on the drums. When we asked if there was a cover charge, we were told "there's never a cover charge!" and had a friendly exchange with the bouncer before going inside. The atmosphere inside was exactly what you would want from a bar in downtown Nashville. People were happy and engaged, and the kids on stage with the band that was playing was just the coolest thing to see. Definitely going back next time we visit!

Typical Nashville atmosphere. We were able to bring two kids in for late lunch weigh my parents. Managed to bring the stroller too. I should add this was a Saturday afternoon before any eric church concert at the arena. Food was average for a broadway street bar. If you want good bbq go to Martin's about a half mile away.
Nice small intimate bar if you get there early. I found this to be similar to the other smaller bars; good band, good drinks, lots of memorabilia.
Awesome music but only giving this bar 3 stars... rudest bartender I have ever encountered!  Management really needs to re-evaluate her employment status!

I stood in the presence of greatness watching Luke, an 18 year old guitar prodigy. His guitar licks were magical as he poured his soul into that thing. He played some Stevie Ray Vaughn and gave it his own flavor--I shouldn't have left, but thinking I was missing out on some great music on Broadway, I left. Every other place we went to was filled with people acting a fool dancing dreadfully to empty cover music. When I stopped back at Roberts to get more of Luke, there was a verrrrry long line. I'll be back tomorrow!!!! This is Real Great Music at its nitty gritty best.

The best place on Broadway.

The best music if you like old country, Cheap Drinks, even cheaper food.  
Get the "Recession Special" and enjoy Bologna, chips and Pabst Blue Ribbon.
This is the absolute classic dive bar with great bands and great staff.

This place was fun, not too crowded and the bartender was fun. Upper level area was overlooking the bottom floor and was substantially less crowded. The bathrooms were clean despite how busy they were on new years day. The only drawback was the female singer they brought in, her voice was not that great.

Great place, especially after 1am the music was amazing & the fried Bologna sandwich with cheese was outstanding & under 4 bucks. Soaks up the moonshine just fine. Don't miss out on going here when in Nashville. Tip the musicians ppl. Don't get itchy butt & run out before paying for your entertainment it's rude.

This bar was a lot of fun. Kinsey Rose was playing. The band sounded so great outside we stopped in for a couple beers until her set was over. We've been listening to her on Amazon since then. 

Service was quick, beers reasonable priced. Good selection.

Robert's is awesome! I was in Nashville with my boyfriend for a 2 day stop during our roadtrip, so we weren't really looking to go hard on Broadway (the bachelor/bachelorette parties were too intimidating). We went into Robert's on a Friday afternoon and it was pretty packed. We managed to get seats at the bar and enjoyed our cheap beers and the band playing. This place is absolutely perfect for anyone - there was a bachelor party there being rowdy, but tons of couples too, of all ages, just looking to have a fun afternoon and listen to some tunes.

Have to give a special shout-out to Gail, our waitress/bartender. She was a gem. We are from NYC and you basically have to wave $100 in the air to have a bartender even consider coming over to you. Gail kept checking on us (and remember, it was fairly packed) to make sure we had everything we needed, and made us feel so welcome. She is amazing and so representative of why Robert's is such a nice place to be.

Looking forward to my next Nashville visit, where Robert's will definitely be a long stop!

Simply epic. Ate there two nights in a row and had two different dishes...both were excellent. 

Service was great, ambience was nice and the three-story setup was pretty cool. 

Definitely will be back.

Robert's is a great place to experience Broadway! I had quite a bit of fun here-really decent old school country music, boots lined up against the wall, and cheap (enough beer) It's exactly what I pictured a Honky Tonk to be like. A little crowded for my taste but hell, great things draw the masses. I don't know anything about authenticity, but if you want to experience Nashville like you pictured it, then please come here!

This was our new "treasure" on this second visit to Nashville.  It's a for-real Honky Tonk.  First the beer is very cold just the way I like it.  The waitresses are super friendly and most attentive.  Even with large crowds, I NEVER had to wait for a drink.  These gals are ON IT.   Discovered from Caroline, Keri,and Hope that this used to be boot store.  Very interesting.  I cannot complete this review without giving a shout-out to their fry cooks.  One guy in particular --can't remember his name--but he'll know I'm writing about him because I specifically told Caroline and him (the fry cook with black rim glasses)  that we were so so impressed with his cleanliness and his work ethic.  I thought he was a part owner the way that he was always busy, stocking, restocking the cook station and wiping and cleaning up around the station.  He cooked and he delivered to tables.  He must have changed gloves about 10 times in the 40-50 min period I watched him.  Now the food was not outstanding but tasty for bar food and I know it was prepared in a sanitary setting and the prices were great!   Now--the bands and musicians they had were OUTSTANDING.  We enjoyed watching them and their talent was unmatched on the stip.  We will visit again!!

Exceptional live music and a nice staff--these are my qualifiers for Nashville bars and this one meets the test. 

The bartender did charge me for my club soda and lime, but he kept them coming as long as I was there. He also didn't give me a hard time about not drinking. 

The live music was great and the band was top notch. I think I am only giving this 4 stars because I enjoyed another bar with live music on the strip more, however this is a great place to stop while in Nashville. Give it a try--I ensure you won't regret it.
Excellent venue.  We had front row seats to see Simple Minds.  The sound was amazing and the atmosphere was awesome.  They could use more help with the concessions,  that would be my only suggestion.

Just okay and overpriced. The staff is not really that friendly. My drink was watered down but server never came back to check on us. It is very loud with a sports pub feel yet with Ruth Chris prices. We had to ask for silverware and then for napkins. Server only checked on us once and never asked if we wanted another drink. Got a Ribeye and it was chewy with no flavor. I have had sirloin better than this...all around disappointing and with all the choices in Nashville, I say keep moving; not worth the price.
Good tour, just sorry we couldn't catch a concert here while on vacation.  Loved all the costumes from entertainers who sang at this venue.
Great atmosphere!! Loved the music too. However, the drinks are very expensive compared to what I'm used to paying in Charleston. Drinks are twice as much. The atmosphere is worth the cost though.

State of the art facility. directly in the downtown area, LEED certified, visually consistent with the feel and vibe of the city - this convention center takes the cake. 

The directional signage is clear, prominent and readily available. "Ask Me" kiosks with personnel manning them round the clock make it easy to find out where to go and how to get there. 

There are also many opportunities for marketing signage via led screens and tv screens throughout the building. A nice option for local venues, Restuarants and attractions. 

This is a building that makes you want to look up and not down as you get your steps in. There are design features, historical gems, music references and city secrets all through out the center. 

Whether you are hosting an event or attending an event you will not be disappointed with all the Music City Center has to offer.

Went here on a Saturday evening around 7pm. Had no issues getting a table for 3 people without a reservation. 

The band was excellent; kinda loud for a good conversation. 

Drinks -- awesome! 

Food -- eh. I ordered the pizza and caprese. Not the best food I've had. The drinks and music made up for it. 

Service was really good.
Dive bar with great live music and personable/speedy bartenders...ended up here on NYE bc the line was moving fast. Out of all the honky tonks we went to on Broadway, we had the most fun here.

This was a cool multi-story bar on Broadway. We stopped in to hear the band playing and had a few drinks. We got some queso to hold us over until dinner time...it was okay. The service was pretty bad though, and our waitress was MIA. The band sort of made up for that, and they did have TV's on with the games. There were also Bud Light promo people working this bar so we ended up taking their survey and got free beers. Fun spot, just need to work on the service!

Let me start from the very beginning:
I was trying to make a dinner reservation for a group of ladies the Monday before the Saturday evening that we wanted to dine here the same weekend of the Music City Marathon. The lady that I spoke with on the phone to make the reservations was extremely nice and helpful with ways to get around the city, things to see, shuttle services, etc. I requested to be seated on the patio if possible (wish was granted, & awesome by the way). 
So, we arrive at our dinner reservation right on time, we were escorted to the patio near a lovely fountain. We all ordered some fun drinks. If you get a cocktail, expect to pay $12.50 a pop for it. I got the Sambuca Sling. Worth every penny. 
Apps, we ordered the beinets and crab dip. They were both fabulous. I ordered the champagne chicken entree with havarti tater "tots", that were actually more like potato logs. lol. Everyone ordered something different & everything was fabulous. Service was very friendly & quick. We were given a complimentary dessert for my friend who was celebrating her bachelorette party. 
I mentioned that the cocktails were a little pricey, but my bill ended up only being around $50 before tip, so as a whole it really wasn't a bad price for the quality of food/drinks/service they have.
If you are planning a trip to Nashville, you must come to the Gulch & go to Sambuca for dinner. Sit on the patio if possible!

It was lunchtime and we decided on stopping here. The hospitality was the best on all of Broadway. Karen, our server was always on hand if we needed anything. Nina, cooked my wife and I two delicious cheeseburgers. The wait wasn't too long at all. The music was the most honky tonky of any establishment we stopped at on our journey in Nashville.

5 stars is 100% due to the bologna sandwich.  Hands down the best grill man (Benny) in the USA.  

I come downtown just for this late night post drinkin pleasure

Robert's Western World was excellent.  No other place on Broadway held our attention so long or made us so happy.  The music varied each night, but all acts were top notch and entertaining.  We saw both rockabilly and country acts over three nights.  It was fun to see folks dancing and having fun.

The service is relaxed and friendly.  The food is surprisingly good too. It's a small menu of fried and grilled items, but we ate there more than once.

We tried other places, but nowhere came close to Robert's for us.
