I think this is my favorite place on the strip!  We've been to Nashville twice & both times, I saw the same band.  I was glad because I loved them the 1st time!  It is hard to find a seat sometimes, so wait your turn.  High top tables with stools are all you will find here!
I remember from the 1st time, how good the food is too!  You will see some great locals dancing their tails off almost every song!
Don't miss this stop!
Bartenders seem a little uptight.....not a fun bar....plenty of fun bars....keep walkin......

This was a great place to hang out at!  The music was fantastic, and the staff was prompt, and very friendly.  No matter how busy it got, someone always walked around to check on people sitting at the high top tables, including myself.  I was really impressed with how friendly the staff was.  Since this was my first time here, I have no idea if the music is always this good, but the band they had tonight was absolutely amazing, and it was a fun place, with great energy.  Everyone around me appeared to be having a good time as well.  I had a burger, and it was your standard bar burger.  It was good.  I didn't get to try many of the other more exciting items, but the next time I am Nashville, I will for sure visit Robert's again.  This is a great spot for experiencing the great music that Nashville has to offer, in a great environment with a super friendly staff!
Best sliders!!!!!! These were a nice surprise- we stopped for a drink and bite and these were some of the best I've ever had! Brisket, cheese, Burton peach jam on a fried biscuit! Crazy good

What I wouldn't do to go back to this Honky Tonk bar at 1am. I went on vacation roughly two weeks ago and wanted to visit a little slice of home. Robert's Western World was the perfect reminder of why I will always be a Tennessee girl at heart. The deep-fried pickles with ranch dipping sauce...delish. Absolutely delish. I'm a sucker for fried pickles and I'm ever-so happy we decided to her them. I got the mushroom swiss burger with a side of sweet potato fries, and if you're looking for a great place to walk into for a night of boozing or just wanna visit some nostalgic Nashville...this is the place. The food was amazing, the people were great, and the live country music was the perfect charm. Even if you aren't a country music fan, this place is a must-go. You won't be sorry!

Really fun dive bar with excellent bands playing classic country and bluegrass. Good prices on macro-brews, and they have plenty of other beers available too. Friendly and hard working staff. If you go to one honkytonk on Broadway, this is the place.

We did the Backstage Tour of the Ryman and our tour guide was Mamie. She said it was only about her 5th time giving the tour but we thought she seemed like a pro! It was awesome to go through the dressing rooms-- it was definitely worth the $10 more than the self-guided tour. The video they offer to watch is very well put together and a fun way to learn more about the background of the Mother Church. The only bummer part was that the stage was being waxed so we couldn't walk on it and get the full view that the artists get. Still a fun time!

We didn't stay long enough in my opinion. 
The first thing we heard when we walked in was the band explaining to a customer that they wouldn't play Zac Brown band - only old country. It was one of only a very few places that gave me the flavor of the old Nashville - or at least what I imagine it as. 
It's nothing fancy, no roof top bar, and not named after a star (Kid Rock, Jason Aldean, Luke Bryan, etc) but that's what will make me go back.

Great to see part of the home of country music. The venue is amazing and nice to see a historic building. The displays are informative and I like that you can walk though at your own pace. Very low key experience. Wish you could talk photos on stage with your own phone- feel this is one area that they take advantage of people. $25 for a photo just shows part of how they really feel about guests- it's all about the money and not the person....

The Ryman Auditorium is the best place on the planet to hear acoustic music.
The tour is nothing really to write home about but the sound and the gut feeling you get when you walk in this venue is something that will stay with you forever.

A really solid bar with a gorgeous theme and great music. We stopped in here on a rainy Sunday to listen to a "Hangover Special" band that was all acoustic but pretty good. We sat at the bar and the bartenders were pretty quick at helping us out. The beers are pretty cheap and we also got quite a few $3 jello shots. The second band that came on were lively and we ended up staying a lot longer than originally anticipated. We ordered the loaded tots and my god, the queso melted over these little tot nuggets were amazing. Highly recommend if you want an unhealthy snack.

Love the vibes here, love the food here, love the bands here!

Awful experience. Bartender basically stole money. I went to the ATM bc I had no cash at all. I got myself and my wife two drinks for $19. I gave the bartender two $20's so I could I've a good tip and I got no change.  When I told the bartender that I gave her two 20's, she replied with "no you f'n didnt, you gave me a $20 and a $1". Do ATMs give dollar bills now? That's the only way I would get a single.  She then slammed a $20 down on the bar and yelled "here". I told her she clearly needs it more than me. I wrote to the website, don't intend on hearing back, as if they employ scum like that I can't imagine owners or managers are much better.

Robert's Western world is everything you imagine it to be and more.  The dive has great live country music.  It's crowded, it smells like a dive, the music is awesome. Everyone is packed in like sardines yet somehow people still find enough area to honky tonk and square dance in the front near the live band.  

Cheap drinks, super friendly clientele, and free live music, what could be better than this!

I'm reviewing the ceviche and pallatas food court restaurants. There are others... Très gauchos look amazing.

Ceviche: Pretty robust menu. I ended up going with the ceviche de pescado. All I can say is... For 12$ you get a massive quantity of food. The ceviche itself is okay. I would rate that a 3. It's mostly shrimp with raw cut up vegetables. It doesnt have a lot of flavor... Not something super authentic.

Pallatas: There was a huge line for the pallatas... And there's a reason. The pallatas were amazing. I got a strawberry pallatas and it was just the perfect blend of sweetness and flavor. Why this review is a 4.

Overall: I'd go back for the pallatas and to try out très gauchos. I would probably not try the ceviche again..  it's just not that great
Tasty enough but biscuit sliders were not biscuits and very small for the price. The tater tots were good but small again

Well I have walked up and down the street most of the night. I just flew in from Dallas this evening. For the most part I would have to say the live music isn't very good. But right here at Robert's Western World it is the best music I've heard all night. I would definitely come back here if I was ever in Tennessee again. But I doubt I ever will be. Robert's you rock!
Great food and music! Just don't expect any service! So and I had to get up and asked for water, then waiter apologized for not waiting on us due to staff gave him too many tables! Save ur money!

Sambuca is one of my favorite restaurants in Nashville. I won't lie I've always stuck to my favorites on the menu, but once I find something delicious, it's hard to try anything else. The shrimp and crab dip for an appetizer is a must for everyone! It is soooo yummy. Also if you want a perfectly done steak, this is where you go. Every time I've ordered my steak they have prepared it correctly on the first try. The same for the rest of the people I have dined with. I personally love the Filet! It has great seasoning and a delicious sauce. The wine is tasty here too. Finally the ambiance is always great with the live music on the weekends. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone in the Nashville area.

Is Sambucha's er "Sammy's" the best food I've ever had - nope.  Best drinks - probably not.  Best atmosphere - it's up there.

Is Sammy's the best experience I've ever had at a restaurant?  You better believe it.  Here's the thing - you are family the second you walk into Sammy's.  Whether it's in need of great service at the bar, a recommendation for a night on the town - or just the family you've never had - Sammy's is the ONLY place is Nashville (make that the south) that you need to go to.

Some say George Washington's crossing of the Delaware is this country's greatest quest.  Well I'd beg to differ.  That stumble down to Sammy's on Friday and Saturday during our Nashville vacation will forever be written in the history books.

Only difference - GW crossed the Delaware a third time - and if my wife lets me back into that city again, a third crossing shall commence at the one and only "Sammy's."

This place treats patrons with unforgivable scrutiny. The "gatekeepers" at the door are both unreasonable and uneducated as it applies to the validity of a drivers license. Apparently, they are not concerned about their business and give a different face to southern hospitality ~ it's ugly.

You don't really come to a Honkey Tonk on Broadway for the food, but if you happen to be here when everyone's hungry- the tacos are way better than I thought they would be. Especially the fish tacos that tasted very fresh. But beyond the food the live music was amazing - even mid afternoon on a random Monday, and the staff was friendly and attentive.

While walking up and down Broadway, I knew I had to chose a country western bar and listen to honky tonk before I left town.  I really don't like country music and knew that these bars wouldn't change my mind.  It didn't.  But country music is Americana and I had to experience it live, love it or not.  The bar was long and the live band played at the front with their backs to the window so patrons walking by could see and hear them.  Because they were playing some Sweet Home Alabama when I walked by, I thought it would ok to come in here.  Bartenders were not very sociable and the crowd really didn't seem to get into the music.  Maybe they don't like country either?  Nonetheless, I'm glad I walked in and stuck around.

We were lucky enough to snag seats up front on a busy holiday weekend and stayed for a few hours because: the music was awesome (think Johnny Cash) and the beer was a couple bucks (we decided to be less high maintenance and go for PBR & Busch). My only regret is leaving to check out a couple other Broadway bars just to find bands playing...Third Eye Blind? Yuck. This place was the best and the people watching was top notch.

Went there for my husband's birthday while I was pregnant with our first child. Service was incredible. My husband drink was delicious and they were able to make a mocktail version for me as well. Our appetizers were the duck breast, absolutely mouth watering, and the calamari, not my favorite but my husband devoured it (I'll blame the baby). For our main meal, my husband got the scallop risotto and I got the black ink pasta with scallops, lobster, and shrimp. My husband dish was made perfectly. The risotto was soft, fragrant, and melted in your mouth with the sweet taste of truffles. My squid ink pasta was heavenly and the seafood was cooked to perfection. For dessert my husband inhaled his white chocolate cheesecake and practically licked the plate. I had a chocolate dessert (pregnancy brain is failing me) and practically drilled over the empty dish. The live music was incredible and my husband and I finished our drinks and hung out for a bit before continuing our birthday night out. We can't wait to go back!

Been twice. Received awful service both times, treated like I'm not good enough to be there or an inconvenience when I order. Food is meh. I ordered something that was not what I was expecting at all, and as much as I hate sending food back, I did ask and the bartender was infuriated. It's very clique-y here, which if you read any of my other reviews, I don't really like. I think this would be a nice place to go on a date if you had reservations and didn't care about blowing money on small portions...the décor/vibe without people is really cool and swanky, somewhat romantic...I just think there's better places to go.

Really enjoyed this place until I sat next to an article, which I read, about the rags to riches story of the owner.    That story I love.   But, his band played tonight and they are talented, to pass around a tip jar like you are a struggling band  is a fraud.    To make matters worse, Mr. Come from nothing asked who went to the Ryman tonight and further crapped on what he called pop country.   Yes I went.   Music is about acceptance and while I understand the want to maintain traditions there is no need to put down an evolution in music and alienate half the folks patronizing your bar.    Crushing to the soul that you aren't open armed to anything promoting country and music and solid paying clientele.   Any stars from me simply for good wait staff (Ramone's  t-shirt) and a good bologna sandwich.     Overall, the place is worth the visit.   The attitude I got on my visit just sucked.

This is where locals go IF they go to Broadway.  Don't waste your time going anywhere else, Robert's has the best music on the strip.  Catch the Don Kelly Band on a Friday or Saturday night to see the best guitar player in Nashville (19 year old Daniel Donato).  You won't hear pop country here, it's all old school country, Southern rock and blues.  You might get REAL lucky if the band happens to let the Robert's staff sing - they are all amazing.  The guy that cooks your fried bologna sandwiches has moves like Jagger (and a great voice/presence) .  The cute blonde bartender just wrote a song for Willie Nelson.  Incredible people behind those counters.  Brazilbilly is great if you like old country, think Marty Robbins.

Don't bother waiting in line out front, go to the back and get onto the balcony.  You can scope out a seat below, especially when the bands change out or take breaks. 
The place gets really crowded, but have some patience - a server will come around to you if you have a table or you can always ask someone sitting on the bar stools to let you in to order, chances are they are regular barflys and will be more than happy to oblige.  

Try the Recession Special, a bologna sandwich, chips and beer for $5.  Or the Stimulus Special with a hotdog instead of the bologna.  The fried pickles are awesome!  And for anyone visiting from Louisville, they have Falls City beer!  Don't see that much outside of Kentucky.

No cover. No smoking. No pop-country.  Usually drunk, college kid free (changes as the night goes on, but nothing like the other Broadway bars).  

Robert's is true Nashville.

Don Kelley and company were terrific. We watched them on Fourth of July weekend. 

The lead guitarist, Porter McClister, was simply the most incredible player I have seen in some time. He works incredibly hard and gives his all for the audience. 

Kelley, meanwhile, is really funny. He entertains the crowd with a good sense of humor. 

The bass player's bass was really cool. He was extremely talented.

The bar, itself, was jam-packed with patrons. A host of them were dancing right there in the front. Others were drinking PBR and eating hamburger and fries at the bar. Good experience.

I had a great experience here, and look forward to returning to this particular place. Lot's of fun!
Obviously a place for tourists. Short wine pours. Mediocre food. High school type band too loud for dining. Not a be back.

If you like live loud music (you can literally hear it from across the street), friendly bartenders, good beer selections, and lots of seating, then Tin Roof is your place. The music isn't quite Honky Tonk when I went, though. Think more college music.
I ordered Breakfast Tacos.. Very good!!  I like the atmosphere  and the blueberry margarita

Dirty, cramped, smelled of pinesol and puke, bartender female ignored me and kept serving the males. 
Got no service at table, and finally left!

Not only were the drinks delicious and light, the food was fresh and exceeded my expectations, but the service was unlike a typical dining experience. Our waiter Kenny, went above and beyond to make sure our group had an unsurpassable experience. The manager also helped created a unique experience for our bachelorette party! Thank you, both! We will be back next time in town!

Sit outside on the upstairs patio. It's gorgeous. If you're in the mood for a live band in a lounge setting, sit inside. The shrimp and crab dip was delicious. Also great cocktail selection! The items are pricy but you could fill up on appetizers to ease the wallet.
Great food and service. Centrally located near downtown. Prices are reasonable. Only negative is the parking. I would go back!

Excellent venue for the Grand Ole Opry! Saw old Crow and the Gatlin Brothers play the last show of 2018 there.  Big Historic Church converted to a performance auditorium.  Four sets with a variety of unannounced performers makes for an evening full of surprises.  Certainly a "don't miss" event if you visit Nashville.

Note: original wooden church pews still the primary seating.  Bring a cushion as the 2.5 hours can be hard on the backside!

I had to leave a review for this because it was absolutely amazing. I wanted a nice dinner for my birthday and I found this place and decided to check it out. I got the Filet and Lobster and was one of the greatest meals I've ever had. The waiter told me to get it with Gorgonzola Butter (I don't like Gorgonzola cheese but figured to try it anyways) I don't think I'll ever have a steak that's tastes as AMAZING as that one did. The person who was with me even said that may be the tastiest thing I've ever tried.

What is there not to love about the place? Outdoor seating, live music, delicious food, great service and a nice drink menu. My husband and I just happened upon this place. We were actually walking to a restaurant next door, but because their patio was booked for a private event we decided to check out Sambuca. So glad we did!! We had the cheese and prosciutto beignets, and calamari to start. Then my husband and I split the sea bass with lump crap and each enjoyed a glass of red wine; I had the Clos de Bois Cabernet and my husband enjoyed the Luna, a red blend. Oh, and our entree arrived split on two plates for us to enjoy...very nice of the waitress to have done for us!

Sooooo much history here.  Where everything on Broadway is new and so commercial, Robert's is Old Nashville.  No hipsters in here.  Just good country music fans who appreciate the local musicians.  It gets just as crowded and crazy on Friday and Saturday nights like all the other Broadway joints, but Robert's is pure history.

Someone told me that "there's not a bad seat in the house," and so far I've found that to be true.  I've been to a lot of shows here and sat in various parts of both the floor and the balcony, and I've never had trouble seeing or hearing the performers.  I like the pew seating, but I suspect that's partly because I'm on the smaller side, as people go; I've gone to the Ryman with people who are taller or broader than I am, and they seem a little less comfortable.  Concession prices are in line with what you'd expect.  But the history, the aesthetics, the acoustics-- they all combine to make this my favorite live music venue in Nashville, and one of the best I've been in anywhere.  I hope to do the tour one of these days.

This place is a lot of fun. You can find more authentic places (Robert's, Ryman, etc.), but this place just feels like a good time. The bands that at Second Fiddle were very good with involving the crowd and making it fun.

Awesome burgers!!! Fresh soft bread, the Angus beef is SUPER DELISH! And there is live music. 

We got there at noon and it got pretty packed shortly after. Great ambiance and a good low budget and local menu to choose from!!! Definitely a place to go

I have nothing bad to say about this place. My boyfriend and I stopped in pretty early one night during our stay and had a blast. Broadway certainly isn't for everyone (touristy!) but Robert's Western World felt less touristy than the one other honky tonk we checked out. The band was great, playing old country and interacting with the crowd. We knew we had to try the fried bologna sandwich because everyone on the Internet told us to. It didn't disappoint. It's not gourmet by any means, but it's salty, perfectly grilled, crispy and delicious. Basically like a BLT with thinly sliced bologna instead of bacon. We washed it down with some $2 MGDs and tossed our cash into the band's tip jar. The bartender was attentive and polite. It wasn't too busy when we were there but I imagine it (like all the others) can get packed on weekends and later at night.

This is my second concert at The Ryman. And any chance you get to see and artist you like...DO IT! 

I love shows at the Ryman because the venue is small and intimate. There aren't really bad seats in the house. The artists that typically perform here aren't huge on lights, smoke, and/or pyro. Just stripped down performances with the vocalist and his/her band. The Ryman will always be a Nashville staple and you have a chance to make it, you'll definitely see why it belongs in Music City.

My wife and I live locally, and have heard and read pretty good reviews so we decided to give it a try. We quickly found out that this is a bad Nashville tourist trap. The food/drink were priced on the high end, but they have done a good job with their menu descriptions. Unfortunately, the food quality and preparation were both terrible. I would expect this quality of food at your average wedding or cruise. For the record, we got 2 appetizers: dumplings & Brussels, and the flatiron steak and salmon for our meals. On top of that, our wine (by the glass) came out skunked. The service was great, but the live band was below-average (for a Saturday night in Music City). Really felt like we threw away $150 after that night. The first restaurant in Nashville that my wife and I will never go back to.

Do you like the smell of overwhelming body sweat? Have you ever secretly had a dream of being strangled by a sea of people? Do the words "personal space" sound like some sort of ridiculous new age hoo-hah to you? Well then, the Second Fiddle might be the place for you. 

The Second Fiddle is a bar on Broadway in Nashville. That should tell you all you could ever want to know about it. It's gonna be crowded. There will be lots of beer. Constant country and honky tonk music to either soothe or assault the ears, depending on your particular view of country music. Really, it's pretty much the same as any bar on the street. But if you're looking to have a night on the town in Nashville, well, the Second Fiddle is as good a bar as any other to drunkenly stumble into.

My friend and I went here last night.  It was "ok."  I enjoyed the live music, and the bar tender told us they have different bands almost every night.  The atmosphere is nicer than some other bars in Nashville and its geared towards upscale (I said geared towards..not it IS upscale).  
     The food is somewhat greasy and salty, but I guess that goes hand-in-hand with beer.  However, I'm not a beer drinker.  We ordered the lobster tempura (if you want to call it that).  It was a disappointment.  The 3 small lobster tails were dipped and fried in what looked like onion ring batter with panko bread crumbs.  That my friends is NOT tempura.  I ordered the margherita pizza, which was beyond salty.  I could only eat 2 slices...I gave it a second try incase I just happen to eat a salt patch.  My friend ordered their striped bass with vegetable couscous.  The fish that came out was a very sad less than 4 oz filet that had soggy skin.  However, the 3 cups of couscous they piled on her plate was ok o_O.  That is not worth $32 dollars.  About the drinks.. I've "heard" around town that this place makes the 'best' drinks.  If you like mixed drinks that are sweeter than southern sweet tea, you found your place.  I ordered a strawberry mojito, and my friend ordered their 'signature' pink lemonade..blllaaaahhhh!  They should write in the description these are sugary drinks with a pinch of alcohol.  
     I gave this place 3 stars because I enjoyed the environment.  However, the service and the food are not worth it for me.  I forgot to mention..my friend and I had the "dinning experience" at this place.  In other words, we were here for about 2 hours waiting for service and food.  This is not the place for that..maybe I will come here just to listen to the bands?

I thought one of the best places I visited on the strip. Had room to move around still and the bands hey had were good. Also didn't seem like over the top begging for tips like some other bars on the strip.   The bartenders were friendly and always had a drink fast   This place is a must visit

If you are in Nashville to hear good live music instead of the same 5 contemporary pop country songs being karaoke'd by every bachelor/ette party, you need to find a way to get into Robert's Western World. This place had hands down the most enjoyable music/band of any bar that I was in on Broadway. 

I can't speak for the food (although I don't know that the grill and fryer have ever been cleaned based on their appearance), but the fried baloney will always peak my interest. The music was great, the other patrons were friendly, and everyone seemed to be having a great time despite being packed in pretty tightly. 

If you want to dance and sing to songs you hear on the radio, go somewhere else. If you want to enjoy good music by quality musicians with others that also have an appreciation for the music, this is the place to be.

Stopped here for drinks and live music. The live music was awesome! This particularly night their were three guys that sang individually and together. One was actually from NJ. It was a fun night! I enjoyed beer while my sister had their sweet tea (so good!). My boyfriend had really expensive gin and clubs. I suggest sticking to beer when coming here.
But its a fun little venue. Didn't try their food but I am sure it's good too!

Visited for a show. We bought tickets online and the line up of artists were not what we purchased. But we made the best of it since we were there. The singers and musicians sounded great. The comedian was very funny. We went there mainly to see Dustin Lynch.  He came out at the end and only sang 3 songs. We were expecting more of a concert type of event. The seating is in wooden pews and our backsides were aching sitting in them. Seating was tight, we were all squished together. Made it a little uncomfortable. It is a live radio show so there were a lot of plugs for the sponsors of the show. That seemed alittle odd, but guess that is how it works there. Probably wouldn't return there for a show.

With a night to spend in Nashville, I thought it would be best to find a place with live music and food.  Sambuca came up a few times on google so even with an average rating on yelp, I decided to try it out.  Long story short, I am never listening to google again.

Sambuca has a stage on one end with various performers almost nightly.  Tables and booths are facing the stage giving it the proper attention.  My server was super attentive and sweet.  Service was the only "wow" factor I got from Sambuca.  I ordered the beignet appetizer and filet entree, and while they weren't bad, the food in general was only average, to say the truth.  The filet was a bit soggy to the cut.  The butter sauce was not complimentary to the steak.  The drink (sambuca sling-back) was strong with no particular flavor.  Food is overpriced and I was not satisfied from the food to the drink to the ambiance.  This place was unbelievably dark!  Everyone around me had to use their phone in order to read the menu.  Maybe I was expecting too much.. But I'm sure there are other restaurants that can better represent Nashville.

I did not know this was a chain but I'm happy to hear there are  4 other locations. Sat at the bar, I always ask for recommendations. Bartender said the beignets stuffed with prosciutto and mozzarella, soooooo good. Also had a filet and it was cooked perfectly and not a bit of bad meat. Drink was strawberry basil something cocktail and very natural ingredients. So good!

Very disappointed!  We couldn't eat there. They would not allow us to stay due to my brothers back pack. They have a No Backpack policy. My brother has to carry this due to the chemo that he is going through right now. When he told the man at the door what he had in there, he said come in you're fine. We were maybe 5 steps in when a woman came up to my brother and said that he couldn't be in here. He started to tell her what he had in there and she said " I don't care you can't come in here with that back pack, you need to leave!

If this is how they treat people with cancer, shame on them!  No compassion!  

My mom taught me it's all about how you say something.  This was cruel. 

So disappointing!

Very lively crowd. Great live music. Friendly staff. It's not overly crowded so you can actually grab a seat of standing isn't your thing. Unlike a lot of other bars in music city, they don't play all country. So if you're looking for an upbeat bar to come and listen to great music, this Is a great joint.

I love Legends.  Lefty Ferguson is the best entertainer and his band is awesome especially the keyboard player.  Lefty has a great voice and is the best guitar player.  What a great musician.  He plays on Friday Saturday and Sunday from 10 am to 2:30 pm.  Love him.  Every time I'm in Nashville I never miss going to Legends.

This place is the real deal country! They play all real country music not the stuff you hear on the radio lately. The staff was friendly and attentive and the beers were cheap! My boyfriend got some food and wasn't impressed but it is just a bar so can't hold the food to too high of standards. The live music was great and we will be coming back.

This WAS the Grand Ole Opry where history was made. It was fun hearing the stories and taking the tour, seeing backstage, the dressing rooms, etc. The video showing the history of the Ryman was interesting and the spots featuring Minnie Pearl were priceless. They still have concerts there and I would love to attend one of those.

This place is something you definitely have to see, it's an amazing experience, however once you've seen it, or been here, you really don't have to see it again. It's cool that it is still a live radio show, and the acts change from time to time.

There were a lot of people I had never heard of, but are or have been a huge part of the Country Genre Community. The closing group was Alabama, and I actually knew songs they had sang, but a member was sick, so they ended up not performing. That was a bummer. 

My mother went on a tour of the location earlier in the day, I didn't, and when we went to the "show" she told me this was everything that was on the tour besides the performances. So she felt it was a waste of like 30 dollars. Which I would have agreed with if I had gone on the tour. She was also bummed there wasn't a discount for Senior Citizens. Which my mother always looks for and as a 65+ Beautiful lady, she deserves to ask, and should be given one. All Senior Citizens should get a discount here, but sadly they don't. 

Anyway, go, if you haven't been here before, or decide do you like country? Yes, then go see the "show" but don't waste your money on a tour earlier. Are you not the biggest Country Music fan, and/or do you know the acts that are performing while you are there? If not, then book a tour, but don't waste your money on a "Show". That is how I would have decided if I knew what we knew when we visited.

This is a must especially if John England & the western swingers are performing. ( every Monday night). The group is the best we've heard this week. Gets the crowd right into a good time either singing or dancing.
 The bar is great and friendly with great weight staff

Ice cold beer and hot honky-tonk music, what's not to love?  

We may even go back for the bar food sometime.

This was my favorite bar on Broadway. It was a small enough space to feel close to the stage but you are not packed in like sardines. . . like at Tootsie's. The band playing was old school, felt like Elvis era country, I loved every second of it. As one of the oldest bars on Broadway, this music seemed fitting. They also have amazing grilled cheese to help with the drunk munchies.

Since we had an hour until our hotel reservation, we thought we would spend some time on Broadway. We walked by a few places, but Robert's Western World sounded like it had a great band, so we wandered in and took two seats at the bar. After a few songs (all classics of course: Loretta Lynn, Patsy Cline, Johnny Cash, etc.), we knew we had to stay. One hour became four and before we knew it, the band's set was over and it was dinner time. We didn't want to leave!

First, the atmosphere is great. Don't be shy about coming inside -- the stage is on your immediate left when you enter, so it can feel like you're interrupting. Don't worry about that! People want you to come in and sit down. Speaking of the people, a few of them came up to talk to us. They asked us where we were from, what our plans were in Nashville, then gave us great tips about which bands were playing where. Also, a shout-out must be given to the women behind the bar. The one who served us was always available and super sweet. Tip these ladies well! And the musicians, too! The bands that play are paid by your tips, so be generous if you like what you hear. We liked the group that was there on Fridays from 2- 6 PM and found that the time of their set was perfect for drinking a few beers before dinner. 

Final tip: order a Yuengling if you can. I was so happy to be in a state that served them that I had more than I probably should have.

Fun place to listen to great music and have space to dance. Worth a return!
Great shots as well!

One of my favorite bars in Nashville! Got to this venue around 1am and it was still hopping! The band there played a wide variety of music, including classic rock, country and even some 90s hip hop! It's one of the cheaper bars when it comes to purchasing beverages, so keep that in mind! There are a couple of bars, one up front with the band and one in the back that's not as crowded. Overall, a great time!
They had the perfect drinks. The live music was good. And the bartenders were great and fast! I'd return!

Reading Marcia's Yelp and I want to say about the same thing except I was the tourist and we got a taste of the Nashville Country Culture.  We were recommended by Danny at Gruhn Guitar.  No Cover.  The band folks canvas the joint for tips and we bought the CD.  Read later that this is the best souvenir to buy when in Nashville.  We can check that one off.  Great bar service as well.  We got extremely lucky and got an actual table with a seat thanks to a kind fellow that had some extra room.  On the pricey side for a couple beers and 2 shots of Fireball Whiskey but again, it was very worth it because this is exactly what we wanted to experience.  And we were able to do it at 7:30 when Broadway was not full of drunks yet.  Perfect for our taste.  Good old Honkey Tonk music.  A must visit for Tourists and I know Marcia is right when saying probably not an everyday place as it would get pretty monotonous but this Yelper and my wife really loved it.  The eclectic crowd also made for amazing people watching.  All kinds.  Crowded and loud and we loved every minute of it.  A real must see on Broadway!
The band was good and the beer was cold, but seriously... How does a bar named second fiddle hire a band without a fiddle???
We enjoyed great music, very reasonable beer prices and of course the famous sandwich was fresh and tasty.

The Ryman is must see for any country music fan or historian. You will not be disappointed. Take your time and soak in the smells and aged architecture that they have preserved. Well narrated and lots of artifacts and information available to view.

Roberts Western World was recommended as a must visit in Nashville from many friends and other authorities in the area. It's no secret it stands out among the other honkey tonks as classic and old school country music. For full disclosure I don't consider myself an expert in country music although I do enjoy it. I can say it was a relief to visit after becoming fatigued with drunken tourist and overall madness of nearby bars. They are famous for their recession special sandwich and beer combo which you absolutely should order and enjoy. The bar is unique and something I've never experienced which is always a pleasure. The sites and sounds give an insight into the inspiration for how the genre has changed and where it came from. The sounds coming from the stage are ones that you don't typically hear much of anymore and I can always respect a trip down memory lane.

The Mother Church--a force to be reckoned with. Did you know that up until about 30 years ago, drums weren't even allowed in here??

I took a tour of this place with my Music Business program in college, but didn't see a show there until last night. 

The atmosphere is quaint, but charming. Stained glass windows, church pews for seating, incredible acoustics and not a bad seat in the house! It was so intimate, I literally felt like I was on stage with the artist.

Overall, a great experience and a Nashville must-see. Will definitely be back soon and often.

Great venue! The sound is terrific and the staff are very nice.

Drinks are on the pricey-side.

During the encore, they had security guys come to the front... Which was disruptive... And sucked 'cause they took audience members' spots. I was a total bitch to one of them about it and he just took. So I guess that was nice.

LOVE Plaza Mariachi and all the local goodness it brings to our neighborhood! There is always something fun happening, from live music to salsa nights to soccer or hockey games on the big screen! Try the ice cream shop in the food court- the coconut flavor is to die for!
This was a pretty decent bar. I didn't love it and I didn't hate it. I got an amaretto sour which ran me about $10. I enjoyed the music but it was a bit too packed to find a table.

we stopped by for lunch this week and tried a bunch of things. i had the falafel plate from kouzina cafe and hubby had steak and fries from tres gauchos (he's from argentine and said their red chimichurri sauce is "the real deal"). then we both got coffees at madera cafe and did a little grocery shopping at mazfresco market. everything we had was great (and also cheap!) and everyone we interacted with was so friendly and nice. the facility is bright, clean (including the bathrooms!), and family friendly. and apparently they also have live music and dancing on certain nights! =O we will definitely be back. i already decided i want tacos and paletas next time. i also noticed that they still have some empty store fronts available. can't wait to see what else moves in! =)

This place was amazing and located perfectly by so many other touristy spots.  We saw the Grand Ole Opry here and the surroundings really teleport you back in time (those pews are over a hundred years old and the original pews!)

So much rich history in the place - very much recommend doing the tour afterwards so you can see the dressing rooms and get a chance to learn more about the history and past.
We had a lot of fun here! The band was very inviting and adventurous (they were willing to try any recommendation). We just got drinks and sat near the band.

It's a honky tonk, it's a bar, it's a western wear store!

Iconic spot in the heart of Nashville. They've got a great collection of memorabilia. If you're in the market for gear then you're sure to find a pair of boots or a ten gallon hat to fit your style.

Grab a bite, grab a beer, grab a boot and scoot.

What a great place and a real asset to Nashville! You could spend several hours browsing the shops, sampling the delicious food, and listening to guest musicians. Get authentic groceries there. And don't forget to visit the coffee shop. My favorite new spot in Nashville!
Nice. The real deal. Really great deep country charm music experience with heart.  It's on the strip and worth it. Way cooool. Way cowgirl.

We love this place!!! Miso sea bass and shrimp crab dip are to die for! 

Staff is always friendly but you need to make reservations in advance (more than 1 day).

Love the romantic atmosphere and the music sounds great. Highly recommend for date nights and birthdays. Birthdays get a free dessert too ;)
Cool spot with 4 levels, live music, excellent food and cocktails. I had the spicy blueberry marg, ceasar salad, scallops and the cheesecake sopapilla. All excellent!

I would not normally take time for this kind of crap, but the security didn't do them self any favors. 

For my sons 21st birthday we came to Nashville, great time! But the security Gaurd decided to judge my son and thought he was a bum, and told him he pissed in a trash can and kicked him out. Even though he was with us the whole time. Then they let us know that he wasn't allowed into 3-4 different bars 

As far as I'm concerned if somebody  pissed on a trash can they should be reprimanded. My kid didn't and and legends should piss off. Bummer for them.

We went back to the Ryman Auditorium to do our tour using our Total Access tickets purchased online. Those tickets are only good for the self guided tour so we paid an additional $10 each to get get us to the backstage guided tour. 

Make sure you don't have any Swiss Knife or whatever...it's like going through TSA without removing your shoes...yes they take safety seriously which is good. No drinks or food either...it's already enough that they have multiple bubblegums underneath their pews (part of the history told during the tour).

The tour guide told us a very good timeline of how the Grand Ole Opry got it's name then renamed to Ryman  Auditorium then the people who maintained The Ryman and how the legends in country music started. It was very interesting and very informative. It may seem expensive for a tour but hey sitting on an 1892 original pew and wood floors...that's amazing! You can feel the history.

Then after the tour you get to watch this short clip called Sounds of Nashville (if I remember right) which is retelling the story of the Ryman through the narration of Lula C. Naff...this was really entertaining. 

Take as much pictures as you want without the flash and of course no video recording. Too bad we were only able to see and get into 1 dressing room and not even on stage since Amos Lee's concert preparation was going on.

You may either visit the Rayman Auditorium once in your lifetime so I suggest immerse yourself with the history. Then if and when you get the chance to catch a good show at the Ryman Auditorium just go for it. It's worth it!

On the strip of broadway, in downtown Nashville - where the bars are kind of like the houses in any major city suburb - cookie cutter, but the superficial accents separate them slightly - Tin Roof was set apart the night of Wednesday, Feb. 27.  

Myself and a handful of coworkers strolled in because of the band's teaser - mashup of jazzy reggae - that spilled into the streets.  They were awesome and friendly - if I lived in the area I would make a extra effort to see if they were playing at Tin Roof again.  

The service as received was lovely compared to other locations on the strip.  They were kind, attentive and the drink prices were ok.  

Didn't get food.  The bathroom looked moderately clean - but my judgement was after a few drinks. 

Overall - nothing orgasmic, but I'd check it out again.
Fried Green Tomatoes, Tots, Biscuit Sliders, Chicken and Waffles all delicious and fab service!!

Live music on a Monday afternoon?  You betcha...Great atmosphere and cold beer. The cook was a little busy but the burger was cooked perfect and fries were super hot and stayed warm until I finished them off.

Sometimes I give 5 stars rating because the place is so in a class of its own.  Robert's Western World is such a place.  
- It has a long music history.  
- There is live performance of old country music from eras before I was born.  
- The all day beer special is $2.50 a can, tax included.  
- The simple pub menu is headlined by fried bologna sandwich (hint - the bologna sandwich was salty and delicious). 
- The interior hasn't seen a decor update for eons.  
- The place is so divey that the ceiling lights in the ladies washroom don't work; the washroom is lited by a contractor work lamp.  

I think this was the way it has been since a long long time ago, and the way it will be for a long long time.  And I enjoyed it.  I loved that John and Lois still perform here after 40 years.  I loved that they were transparent about their service level/style during weekdays, as they put a note on the menu to tell customers to order at bar themselves.  We did get waited during our visit because the business was slow.  I Ioved that the waitress didn't watch over my shoulders for tips.  She just let me put the tips in a big jar on the bar at my time, because who wouldn't when she ate a completely full filling Recession Special for $5, unless she has indeed been hit by recession, then the waitress would be completely understanding.

If all the nostalgia doesn't make you think Robert's is in its own class, it is the only pub on honky tonk that has a Pokémon Go gym named after it.

P.S.  No cover charge.  Ever
Very informative tour! You get to see a few different dressing rooms that the artists still use to this day. Also get to learn about the history of the ryman, the mother church of country music!
History, great acoustics, intimacy, basically every ingredient for an amazing show here. Go!

Attended for a three day convention.  

Place needs more food and beverage options.  

Rooms were comfortable temperature wise.  

Bathrooms were clean.  

Workers were friendly.  

Omni hotel right next door.

This was our second year taking clients to Sambuca for dinner. It's by far our favorite. The food is phenomenal. We have never ordered even a mediocre meal. I've ordered the scallops twice now, which are super tender and well seasoned with risotto and asparagus. The snapper was a hit with our group, as was the prime rib. Remember to save room for dessert, too. The drinks are also excellent, with many containing hand-squeezed juices (the the Victim for a sweet pineapple-ginger treat).  The music is excellent. The singer sang old standards with a trio of musicians accompanying her. The music wasn't overpowering but great for the ambiance. We had a large group (12+), and they were able to accommodate us easily. The waiter was excellent and had a great personality.  

Even though we had a big group, the location is also popular for dates. It's perfect for a romantic dinner. As a parent, I wouldn't necessarily take children--not because they wouldn't be welcome but more because the menu is more sophisticated.  By the way, the menu is changing soon, and we can't wait to try their new offerings. Enjoy Sambuca!

Oh my lord these acoustics are insane!  We went to a Grand Ole Opry show in December at the Ryman. Most of the year the show takes place at a venue at Opryland. We scored some amazing seats for under $50 a pop for lower level. We got to see LoCa$h, Mike Snider, Béla Fleck & Abigail Washburn, Riders In The Sky, and a handful of other artists. Since it was the Saturday before Christmas, everything had a holiday vibe to it. The beers and mixed drinks are overpriced, as can be expected at a Venue like this. I recommend having a drink somewhere nearby, you can get it for half the price. For any tourist reading this review, you haven't experiences Nashville until you have experienced the Ryman.
Service is crap in the middle of the day! No matter if u sit at the bar or a table!  Music is good.
Classic spot on Broadway for some honky tonk music before you leave the city. It's old school and classic country. Great price for drinks and friendly service.

If you're looking for a place that has great drinks, food, live music, AND is great for groups, this place is a winner! Went here on a girls trip to Nashville (actually went here every day we were here!!) and was very happy with our visits.  During the day or night, there was always a crowd and music!

Experience:
-AWESOME taco options! We had one vegetarian in the group and Tin Roof had great options for her.  Fan Favorite were the Avocado Tacos...everyone loved them!
-Friend Pickles...need I say more?
Drinks- strong and cheap! Great cocktail menu.
-Nachos - great for sharing and great flavor!
-Music was also great, we were never disappointed! Look forward to returning here on our next trip!

So sad this was my favorite in town ! But they removed two tables to make a dance floor well after we were sitting and ordered round of drinks.  The manager who was also serving at the bar and not managing the floor or customers could have cared less. She basically said too bad for you . Would not have been a big deal if it was just me. But I had brought in a group to show them my favorite bar. Well as another bar sober in town said you need to manage your business keep your customers happy . Tin roof has forgotten that they could care less if you come back

Great cultural place for live Latin Music but most of the food is WAY overpriced for the quality served. Colombian empanadas one order of 8 are $13.95 and they pull them frozen out of a bag. You can go to Cucharitas and get the same thing for half price. The juices are made from concentrates that come from a jug and they charge almost $7 each. I had three juices empanadas and an order of Yuca fries and it set us back $33. If you know anything about Latin food that's rediculous!  The Argentine place Tres Gauchos is cool, but again super pricey for what they serve. I'm not paying $20 for a steak in a food court on disposable plates. I would definitely go back for the music and a beer but don't think I will he taking my family there to eat again anytime soon. There are much better choices for most food options within half a mile for most stuff they serve there at other restaurants up and down Nolensville Rd.

Love this place.
Great place to come and eat, listen to live music and have some cocktails

Fantastic cheap Mexican food that I was treated to for lunch by my boss. The food is freshly cooked and perfectly prepared I had the chicken sofrito with rice and beans and it was spectacular. This area of Nashville is an ethnic enclave with great international food.

Really! How insulting can you be? Shrimp and  crab bisque came. There were onions and celery. No crab or shrimp. We sent it back. Our lovely waitress brought us a new serving; telling us that they had added an extra scoop of shrimp and crab. It must be a 1/4 tsp of something, mostly onions and celery. DON'T spend your entertainment dollars. AVOID. Very high priced entrees, no problem if there was a value.

We toured the ryman this morning. We did the self guided tour as well as the guided backstage tour. The guided tour was good, wish it was more informative and our tour guide was a little more articulate. We had trouble understanding her at some points due to her mumbling. The video that started the self guided part was the highlight! Absolutely exceeded my expectations. Great job ryman.

Must see in Nashville.

Take the backstage tour to get the best feel for the amazing history and talent that had passed thru here.

My wife is not a huge country fan but even she was impressed with the tour and history.

Only thing better would be attending the Grand Ole Opery show here.

Tip leave enough time.  We went on the 3:30 tour and were pressed for time on the self guided portion if the tour.  They close early if there is concert/event scheduled which is Friday and Saturday.

My (awesome) job hosted our annual Holiday (Christmas) party here this year. The space is nice, but not amazing. The service was alright. And the food was.... blah at best.

Unfortunately this just isn't the place I would recommend or spend my time. I got a three course meal - started with a crab bisque - the cream wasn't cooked down enough and wasn't really edible. The second course was pretty good though- medium rare filet was seasoned and cooked well. The side of asparagus was ok, lower quality veg and the au gratin potatoes were salty, cold and were over cooked. 

Nashville is an awesome city- and there are so many places with great food or music. Dont waste your time or money going here. Sorry!

This place has one of the best burgers on Broadway! It's super cheap and you get to listen to great live music while you're there. There's just something about Robert's that draws you in; we ended up staying for more than 3 hours. The crowd tends to be older but everyone is usually really friendly and fun. We sat upstairs and had a great time drinking and dancing with everyone around us. The bar tender was nice but not the most attentive, we often had to ask several times to get something. But, I would gladly come back.
We really enjoyed the tour!  It was around 45 minutes and very informative.   We are not huge history bluffs but this was interesting!  Great history on The Grand Ole Opry.

Bit of an atypical place for Broadway; has some country music, but just as much of rock, reggae, and other things. So the music variety is pretty good. There is an upstairs level (not sure if there's music there, but I believe there is a second bar). Drink selection is pretty good, with very good happy hour prices ($3 PBR, $1 off draft beers, $5 for well drinks I think?). Didn't get a chance to try the food, but seems to have a fairly wide-ranging menu by Broadway standards. Also has pretty good range of drink options (brain freeze types of drinks).

Service was a bit better than the typical Broadway standard, but I was also there kind of mid afternoon (maybe 3-4:30 or so), so it wasn't that crowded.

Came here based on the rave yelp reviews and I have to say, was disappointed!

Very divey and quite dirty. Hard to get drinks at the bar as extremely overpacked (yes, many bars are overpacked in Nashville on a Saturday night, but this one was moreso than others, no elbow room whatsoever)

They had some very disgusting deep fried food with an open kitchen in front of the bar, so you could see the guy removing frozen nuggets from a fridge and deep frying them in front of you. And frying up bologna sandwiches at the same time. Bizarre.

Waitresses were friendly and drinks were quite cheap though. Live music was good.

We live in the icon across the street and have always enjoyed sambuca's until the last visit. We had a birthday celebration and several preteen kids. They ordered from the small plates and we chose outside since they were with us. It was a very large group and several ordered drinks. I did not see the bill but when I reviewed later we were overcharged 60 something dollars. I wrote a letter to the manager and have been ignored. I enjoy the food there and the atmosphere but cannot believe I had no response to my communication. Will NEVER go back

This dive honky tonk bar is the read deal! We came during the afternoon and listened to live music and are a recession special of a PBR, fried bologna sandwich and chips for 3.50. They also have burgers and hot dogs. This is s music institution. The food is mediocre but the atmosphere and music are five stars!

This is a true gem of a honkey tonk on Broadway.  It was recommended to me by both visitors and local's.  Great music and standard bar, cheap eats too, burgers, etc.  I'm rating it only 4 stars because I found the evening bar staff to be a little bitchy and neglecting.  I'm sure they are all jaded by the constant tourists, but it wasn't the most welcoming of service.  Overall great experience though!
Great place for live music and a great bite to eat. Very very good food, and they have a great variety on the menu. Great location in the gulch and great staff. Definitely recommend!
This is what a bar is supposed to be like. Great, simple food, awesome drinks and servers. Awesome live music! True, old school dive bar.
Enjoyed an excellent lunch with live music here. Food and drinks were both fresh and delicious. Most importantly, our server, Kenneth, was outstanding!
Great music bar, right off the main strip with great food, beer, cocktails and service.  Places in Nashville can get packed, so be ready for a busy bar on the weekends.

Robert's Western World is the only honky tonk worth checking out on Broadway. Seriously, don't even go anywhere else, cause compared to this place it's just not worth it.

There's no cover, and they always have live music. Be a good person and tip the band!

The prices here are SO CHEAP. The $5 Recession Special (fried bologna sandwich, Lay's, and a PBR) might be the best deal in Nashville. I had two different locals tell me about this fried bologna sandwich and it definitely lived up to the hype. I might have just had one too many Miller High Life's (only $2.50 here! $7 for MHL at Tootsie's two doors down), but that fried bologna sandwich was sooo good. Yes, it tastes like something you would make at home, but when you're drunk you want that buttery bologna comfort food and it really hit the spot. 

Loved this place, it's the real deal.

This s*cks to choose "a-ok" (3 stars) v. "Yay! I'm a fan" (4 stars). Yet, based on our experience... :( 

I was SUPER looking forward to traveling back to Nashville and trying the fried bologna after seeing it highlighted on a Food Network show. And how perfect - getting to do so while listening to some live classic country after a weekend in Brentwood. 

The fried bologna was okay; just not as great as it had gotten built up in my mind. There was a little too much bread v. the amount of bologna. Hubs' burger was evidently also okay - although it looked really good!

Perhaps what most negatively influenced the experience - in turn generally impacting the overall experience - was service. Our gal was nice, just not the most attentive server in the world. Had it been a shoulder-to-shoulder Friday or Saturday night, I'm confident it'd been less of an issue (we'd have understood); however, it was an early Sunday afternoon with many open tables and spots at the bar. That being so, I don't want to have to carry my arse across the place to ask for refills. Get your "bar eyes" on and take care of your guests! 

We'll try again. It's Robert's Western World in d'town N'Ville for God's sake.

We had an 8:30 reservation and were able to be seated early, 8:00.  The five star review is fir the food and service.  Our waiter was great.  The veggie lasagna is amazing, different than a traditional lasagna.  My husband enjoyed the ribeye, but it only came with one scallop. The waiter offered to bring one more scallop, as the dish only comes with one scallop.  The downside is where we sat.  We sat upstairs in the glass rooftop room. It was unbearably loud.  I could not wait to leave because of the noise.  I was hoping for a more intimate experience for an anniversary dinner. They do have music, bands that play. If you go, make sure you ask about seating if you don't want to be in the loud rooftop room.

I went and saw John Mellancamp or John Cougar Mellancamp, as he was known back in the day, at the Ryman Auditorium the other night. I must say, it was an excellent show. It started off a little slower than I expected it to, with what was almost like a 20 minute documentary that played before he came out. It was long, but gave a great history of his music career 

I was astonished however when I started looking around the auditorium. I felt like one of the youngest people there. It was like every one in there was 60 or 70 years old. And then I thought about it for a minute and realized that I'm almost 50 myself. Crazy, but true.

Man, this guy was popular when I was in Junior High and High School. His music was very popular in the late 80's when I was in High School. I'm telling you, it really took me back. I don't think I've ever sat in a concert that took me back like this one did. Don't get me wrong, I can listen to a number of songs that stir emotions and make me reminisce, but that's what was happening to me during this entire concert...it was a trip. I was almost in a daze. It felt like I was almost transported back in time. I know...I shouldn't have partied so hard back in the day...LOL

I made my first trip to Sambuca on 12/10/14 and loved it. I met a group of ladies for happy hour and had a great experience.
First, it was not busy on this particular evening, so we had a very easy time finding seating. The bar area has several couches and over-sized chairs and tables in addition to regular tables/chairs and seats at the bar. The entire restaurant was very clean and decorated very nicely. The atmosphere was very warm and welcoming; all of the staff I talked to were extremely friendly and seemed happy to be there. This being Nashville, you can always find someone singing/playing and this place is no exception; a singer with a nice selection of Christmas music. Parking is also ample and very easy to find; there are 2 pay parking lots 1 block away - I paid $2 for 2 hours - completely reasonable. 
Good happy hour specials with a fun selection of drinks and appetizers; the food was excellent. I had the mac & cheese with prosciutto - a small plate but was more than enough for me and it was delicious.
I will definitely be back to Sambuca!

We spent three days in Nashville and experienced great service...until we went to Tin Roof.  Absolutely terrible service from the bartenders.  First of all we sat at the bar for several minutes then people sat next to us and she walked past us to serve them first. Then...we are happy to pay higher prices for a cocktail but expect it to be more than water which is exactly what we received. We had to ASK her for a full shot.  Very disappointing.  Great band but unfortunately we left and went to the next bar.

Three words: fried bologna sandwich! I'd eat this dirty little beast everyday if I could. It's the best sandwich in Nashville. Wash it down with a Miller Lite while listening to great music and you'll be in heaven. 

NOTE: the boots are display only. I was excited to find a pair of red cowboy boots for 20 bucks and then completely heart broken when I was advised they were part of the décor. Sad thing is, I've been in this place no less than 15 times and never paid attention to the boots. But I was sober the last time so that's probably why.

I am not a country music fan so the history of the Ryman doesn't thrill me as much as it would someone who loves the music. I did enjoy the movie that started the tour as it gave great background information. I wish the backstage tour was available today, but it wasn't. Worth a stop, whether you are a country music fan or not. Oh, and one of the best part was that they have a Tennessee appreciation deal going - by one, get one - for their regular tours.

I came here for a Melanie Martinez concert and let me just tell you that it was a very overwhelming experience. I had purchased the VIP package and found out that there had been a huge mix up with the VIP seating. I will say that the employees were doing their best to handle the situation and I really appreciate that. They were calm and courteous, but were not able to help that much until we kept badgering them. It would have greatly helped to have been updated more on the issue. We ended up having to sit far in the back but we got refunded. The place was nice and clean. The main drawbacks were in that it felt sort of unorganized. There didn't seem to be much streamlining, although it is a pretty big place, but the lines for purchasing merch from the artist and other lines were all over the place. Overall it was fun and there isn't much else to say. A lot of this will depend on the artist performing and their personal team, so the employees handling the events here can only do so much, but they could step it up.

Great bar in Nashville. This place is more dive than tourist trap and was recommended highly by our local friends. It's a railroad style bar, so narrow area by the bar with a small stage up front, but a nice upstairs that has a few tables and a bar, that is where we congregated.

The band that night played non stop, for maybe 2 hours? They were wonderful, played a solid mix of music and got the crowd having fun. The bartenders were all friendly. Prices were pretty solid, no draft beer, which seems to be a thing around Nashville.

They also serve up fried bologna sandwiches, old school. I would definitely visit here again.

Went to celebrate our wedding Anniversary & it couldn't have been better. 

From our waiter, Jesse, who went beyond the definition of server to make our night special, to the Stacy Mitchhart Band, playing us a funny song for the occasion, the entire night was fantastic. 

The Bucca Beignets appetizer was a perfect way to start along with a glass of wine & a Cock'n'Bull (their take on a Moscow Mule)

The Spinach salad and the Crab/Shrimp Bisque really wet our appetite for what was to come. 

We had the Miso Sea Bass, which had an Asian zing flavor with the bed of apple & cabbage stir fry & the 7 oz filet with the Brussel sprouts. Both were prepared to perfection. 

We finished with a White Chocolate Cheesecake that really topped off a perfect night.  

Overall a truly superb evening out. Thanks to the Sambuca team for making this Anniversary dinner a tough one to top for years to come.

Hands down my favorite music venue we visited in Nashville! I am not a huge fan of modern country myself, but as someone who has switched from classic violin to country fiddle, I've definitely found an appreciation for honky tonk and that's what you're going to find here. 

The bar itself is small and long, pretty no frills, and lots of quirky, fun, and unique decorations adorn the walls. They have a bottom floor/bar as well as a top floor/bar. Lots of tables for seating and room to dance up front near the band! We found it was easier to get a seat on Wednesday night than it was on Thursday night and one of our Uber drivers said that was pretty true to his experiences as well. When we arrived on Thursday, the place was packed (shoulder to shoulder) and we couldn't move in or out. Kind of just got stuck in the flow of traffic. Wednesday was great though! 

Food is bar food. I had some french fries. Friend had a burger, chips, and mozzarella sticks. No one tried the fried bologna sandwich- we didn't realize it's like THEIR THING. I guess someone will have to try it if we ever head back. I'll update and let ya know. Otherwise, it looks like there's 600 other reviews... someone has probably tried it ;)

It's all about the people !

My wife and I were exploring the Gulch on our last day of vacation in Nashville. It was extremely hot out so we stopped in to have a couple of iced teas when we were greeted by Dawn. She seated us with a big southern smile and within minutes we were sipping our tea and talking with her about how great Nashville is and why most folks who live here never leave.

Time had slipped away through pleasant conversation about travel experiences when I realized we had a flight to catch and asked Dawn if she would call us a cab to get us back to our hotel. She gladly made the call but almost 30 minutes had passed and no taxi in sight. We were running out of time and were stressing about the possibility of missing our flight.

Without the blink of an eye Dawn insisted on driving us back to the hotel in her car. My wife and I were shocked by her generous offer and took her up on it. I tried to offer her gas money, but she refused and said it was karma. We have been around a little but never experienced kindness and generosity as we have from her. 

We were in a town full of celebrities, but never knew what it was like to treated as one.

Kudos to you and your great city, Dawn !

My client suggested this place for dinner after our work meeting. Much to our surprise Red Bow records was having a party with live music being performed by Rachel Farley. Not only was the live music great the dinner was excellent. For appetizers we had the Goat Cheese
Stuffed Artichokes and the Shrimp & Crab Dip both are definite must haves. Then for entrees we had the Hickory-Smoked Prime Pork Chop, Filet, Miso Sea Bass, Crab-Stuffed Salmon and the Chicken Parmigiana. All of our entrees were superb!  I would recommend this place to anyone for a romantic dinner (the ambiance was great), client meeting or just to have a drink at the bar. With excellent service and food, who could ask for anything more? I will absolutely go back next time I am in Nashville.
Well with five stars says it all .. great music great drinks and great food .. trifecta all at one location ... I highly recommend this restaurant for you and the spouse....

Honky Tonk music that is fabulous! Packed, but we had no problems getting served. Bartender walks thru the crowds and is amazing how she remembers who is drinking what! Very divey... loud, but fun. Difficult to get seats or move. Gotta make it here to see the house band at least once on your trip.

As you can see from all of the other 1 star reviews, Sambuca has a service and management issue. How is their food? I have no idea, here is why:

Reservation was made for 12:15, we were seated promptly. Some chairs were broken, odd start, but we switched them out and were ready to order. 

12:20 - Waitress stops by and does the usual 'I'll be right back for drink orders'

12:50 - Yes THIRTY minutes later she's back to take our drink orders. She said sorry it was swamped in the kitchen. Odd comment from a waitress... this is when we started suspecting our waitress was doubling as a line cook. We place our drink and food orders at this time, the hanger is beginning.

1:00 - Band finishes and we realize we've been here nearly an hour and don't see food on anyone else's plates. We chat with the table behind us and they explain they've been waiting 1.5 hours and haven't had food. We worry, we had a 2 o'clock appointment to be at.

1:01 - We see a manager, let's call him Brad. Brad just got done talking with a couple who was very disappointed with the service. Brad explained that the kitchen was understaffed and offered to take their names and talk to them later.

1:02 - We flag down Brad. Explain that we've been waiting a while and haven't gotten anything besides water yet, and are fearful we're going to miss our appointment. Brad says when is the appointment? We say 2. Brad says 'you might get your food by 2'. THAT'S NOT GUNNA WORK Brad. We got here at 12:15 and at 1:02 you're telling us our food MIGHT get here in an hour? I would understand if we ordered a freaking paella with a molten lava cake, but we just got breakfast basics.

1:03 - We explain our concerns to Brad and he offers to check in with the kitchen the get an estimate. At this point I should mention we were told our tip was included so they didn't really seem to want to please us.

1:10 - No sign of Brad returning to our table (but we do SEE Brad, boy is he dodging us). No one is eating around us. we went and got our waitress and explained that we know it's not her fault but we have no confidence that our food is coming and that when it does it will have been worth waiting for and missing our pressing appointment. We leave and go to ADELE's up the street who sat us immediately and fed us - which is all we ever wanted!

In sum, how is the food? Unclear. Is it cooked by double agent waitresses? Potentially. Is it worth finding out? Nope.

Placed our order.  Waited for 45 minutes and still no food as a table next to us came in after us and was finished eating.  Waited more than 20 minutes before anyone even noticed we were out of water.  I cannot tell you how the food is but the service was awful.  Placed our order at 12:30pm and walked out at 1:15, still hungry.  No they were not busy.
When everything else is too crowded you can get a place in Roberts, however, not the first choice for prime music And Nashville and honky tonk atmosphere!

I've been going to this place for years! It's always spot on. I had my husbands birthday dinner here (upstairs, overlooking the Gulch) and we just recently went for Mother's Day Brunch. The food is always delicious and the service is GREAT! We opt'd for Sambuca because our kids had never experienced dinner with LIVE music and luckily we were seated right up front, that was a real treat for them to watch.

Happy Hour: I haven't been to HH in a few years but it was always great Martini specials and good food, I'm sure that hasn't changed. 

Parking: this is the reason for the -1 star! It started off with free valet, then it was 3 bucks, then 5, then 10 and now it's 12 or 13. Really? It's not the most expensive restaurant, but it's not cheap either, I think they should validate your parking or at least subsidize the price.

Overall, very nice place anyway of the week to listen to some good music (outside of country music, thankfully...since you can get that anywhere in the Ville) and good food and drinks.

We were told by quite a few locals that this was the bar to check out on Broadway. sure Tootsies (and another big one across the street) have all the fame, but we wanted to go where locals recommended. 

It's a relatively small but cool place, and like most bars in Nashville you'll ALWAYS find live music happening here. Most of the groups that play here are skewed to the "Honky Tonk" subtype of Country music, so if that's your thing this is the quintessential place to visit (at least on lower Broadway). It's located in the thick of things so there are plenty of options to jump around for sure. 

Beers were well priced (listen, I'm from NYC originally so $5-$6 is well priced for me!) And they had a bunch of food options (we didn't partake in the eating though). This is definitely a cool place to chill with a group, have a few drinks and listen to some live music. It's Nashville so who knows.. You may just be listening to the next big thing...

What can I say that hasn't been said.  We took a self guided tour which was just perfect; it wasn't crowded which was nice to really look around 
The ticket purchased included a photo on stage.  
Beautiful theatre rich in history.

The best honky tonk in Nashville! Here you'll find a friendly atmosphere, world class musicians,  and a solid cheeseburger. My husband and I love coming here and have had countless great experiences watching the talented musicians who play here. Even if you aren't interested in country music, you will enjoy yourself!

As far as alcohol goes, the selection isn't bad. Domestic, premium beers and even a few locals. They have fried-bologna sandwiches and fresh burgers. The staff is fast and never impolite and try to get you a drink asap (the place is usually packed so that can be difficult so have a little patience). 

Robert's is what I consider to be the quintessential Nashville experience, and I think anybody who visits should go there at least once! A great place to dance, have a cold beer and hear some great country tunes.

Bang for your buck: 7/10
Quality: 10/10
Service: 10/10
Ambiance/Location: 10/10
Overall: 9/10

A Nashville staple! This is a must see when visiting the home of country music. Our only critique is the price. It's a bit on the pricier side for a self-guided tour, but it's worth forking over the cash to get  this slice of history!
Bad experiensce for us. Limited food menu is way overpriced. Ignored by our waiter. The only thing we liked was the music. Never again!

There are only two types of music I hate! Country and western! Fortunately for us, we had to squeeze and push through to the back in order to find a clear area to hang... far enough that the squealing whining drawl did-not puncture my eardrums. There we spied 4 ladies all happy to celebrate one of theirs 51 birthday. There were a couple of seats and I politely asked if we could borrow a couple. 
Oh no...you may hafta sit on Tina's lap...that's her chair. Said one. Yep you better not she may not be happy another warned. I'm thinking Tina must be 6'10 and 2 fiddy! 
But the Yuengling was talking. I saw they were all drinking what looked like pink lemonade and figured Tina had to be diminutive based on those girly ass dranx. I said nope I'm sitting and when she gets here she can sit on my lap! 

Tina all 5 foot nada and 100 lbs soaking wet shows up. I introduce myself and explain the status of the sitting arrangements. To which she says I can't sit on your lap cause of my enormous set of Balls! 

We all hollered laughing! They said they were from LBC and I'm like where exactly? They said they had to go over a bridge and I'm like ah you are San Pedro homies! (Not that I lived in SP)  that got Tina so excited she swore one of her other girls told me. But that bonded us Cali folks for a couple of sets. Even my client lived in Manhattan beach and we had a good ol time chatting about So cal. 

Of course they never heard of Yuengling so I educated the crew who unanimously agreed "best f-n beer evah! 
But Tina was insistent i try that girly drink. So we got a round and I asked the bar tender what's in it. Apparently ruby grapefruit flavored vodka and tonic... damn if it wasn't very refreshing and good! Like Fresca! Tina corrected me no this drink is called titanium balls!  More hollarin! 

We pushed off to the next bar saluting the bday girl who got a tribute song cause Tina spent a bit of coin to have them do one in her honor. Another climbs on the bar stool to permanently etch their names on a vacant strip of woodwork on the wall. 

Country western is much more palatable when you are in the back of the joint with 4 cool ladies from So Cali!

At the Ryman for Live From Here with Chris Thile, courtesy of a Christmas present from my hubby's younger son! 
It's a classic old auditorium with seating resembling old wooden church pews, 4 people to a section. Although we couldn't see the far right of the stage, but there doesn't appear to be a bad seat in the place!
Tonight's guests are David Rawlings, Courtney Barnett and comedian Neal Brennan. We had a great time!

I stopped in to ask the hostess some questions, and she was incredibly rude. If the first person I encounter as soon as I walk in the door was that unpleasant, I'm not too keen on wanting to come back.

This place hosted my favorite night on the Honkey Tonk strip! on Wednesday nights they always have a named "Reckless Sidemen" and they are amazing. So, enjoy some food, drinks l, and dancing here! Have a good time! Now, when I say dancing.. this place wasn't packed and rowdy, but  there was space to  could bust a move. I really enjoyed the jalapeñorita A LOT! The cool cucumber taste with a hot finish was actually subtle and the most sophisticated drink i've been served in a plastic cup.
