The hot chicken had a great spicy flavor, but was a little too hot to enjoy for me personally. The hotness actually made the nachos taste sweet! I think there is another band upstairs, but I didn't check it out. I highly recommend coming here!

Lucky for the one star, should be a big fat 0. It's 11 am and we just got off the flight and can't check into our room until 4. This place has a whopping 5 other people in it and they say we can't bring out carry on in. I get it if it's busy but it's not. Shitty rule for a tourist town

I would love to give Sambuca a 5-star rating, but our server (I think his name was Keith) was not good. He gave us a 20-minute explanation of the menu (a few highlights/specials would have been sufficient). He only came back everyone once in awhile to check on us (and didn't look like he had many tables). All of that could have been overlooked, but the way our dining experience ended was just completely rude. Booking on Open Table, it was clear that we had a two hour limit. He pulled my friend aside and said "I need this table in 5 minutes, so you need to pay your tab." We had already got the tab and were paying. I understand why the policy exists, but between the 4 of us we spent over $300 for dinner/drinks. It seems a bit like a money grab to turn tables quickly versus having an enjoyable experience. The band (Patton James) was AMAZING!! I would go back again, but would likely sit in the bar area where we wouldn't be treated so rudely. Sad, it's a great place, and the food was amazing! I hope the manager takes this opportunity to teach the staff how to politely turn tables...especially those spending a ton of money.

This IS Music City. The heart of Nashville can be found beating at Robert's Western World where locals and tourists mingle together. Come during the day, and you'll hear singers and song writers. Come at night, and the band will be playing some of your favorites and some of their own stuff. I heard the food is good. Drinks are basic but good and rails are strong. People are dancing and talking and all having a good time. We went at night and the next day because we loved how authentic and genuine this place is unlike some its neighbors. You can't miss RWW.

This is by far our favorite spot in Nashville! Small, crowded, dancing & most importantly GREAT honky tonk music! This place brings in the characters so it's great for people watching and letting your hair down.
We always creep our way to sit at the bar in Becky's section, they are crazy busy but she makes sure to take care of you no matter what if she can see you! 
If you can't find a spot, there are stairs in the back righthand corner that lead up to the balcony... not a lot of service happening up there usually, but a trip up and down the stairs to grab another beer is worth it! 
Oh... the food. I am about to tell you the food is not good.... but I'm also gonna tell you that we end up eating here every time! haha! Its kind of like the burger you used to get in the school cafeteria.. I don't know if they have anything but a burger or not.... but we always stay long enough we NEED that blah hamburger and let's be honest.... who cares at that point, I'm just glad we can get food without leaving!

Free live classical and quality honky tonk bands with no cover charge, no minimum drinks, inexpensive fried foods ($5-$7 for entrees, $4 for sides, $5 for beer). 

Service and ambience are great. Don't expect much in terms of food quality. $6 for their famous fried bologna sandwich with a beer, can't be beat.

The mother church. Amazing Experience - You should go anytime you get a chance, regardless of the act. Not a bad view from the balcony, look carefully if you are in the back of the lower level - some seats (very few) are blocked by structural beams.

Weekend trip to Nashville brought us to staying in the Gulch and I have been very impressed. Sambuca has a great vibe. Dim lighting made for a elegant evening but the live music was worth it! The band and lead singer was phenomenal! Food was incredible and was worth every penny! We had the popular appetizer, salmon, and the polenta entree! Fantastic evening!

My BF and I had stopped into a bar further down Broadway that was definitely a trap for tourists with overpriced beer. We made our way to Robert's Western World after and it was, in my humble opinion, a genuine honky tonk experience. Cold (cheap) beer, great live music, friendly staff, awesome company - sign me up! 

Everyone is smiling and enjoying the music here, and you'll likely see a number of folk on the dance floor - even in the early afternoon. 

If you're visiting Nashville and have time to only hit one place on Broadway, pop into Robert's Western World.

This is one of the best meals that I've had in a long time. Robbie absolutely killed it. The service was perfect, his suggestions were on-point and the food was incredible. For a great date night, I'd suggest sitting outside upstairs as we did. Do yourself a favor and order the shrimp dip app and chili-rubbed scallops for an entree. Unreal.
Favorite bar on broadway!!  They have the best music for sure and the staff is very friendly.  I also love to end there for a burger and fries :) You really can't beat it.

Very beautiful convention center and a great experience with our show this week. Bring comfortable walking shoes; there's a lot of square footage to cover! Skip their catered food (it's just 2 out of 5 stars).

Our waiter at Jimmy Buffets Margaritaville told us not to miss stopping in to Roberts and he was right. Best music on the street and I popped into every honky Tonk.  Crowded, everyone dancing, the Don Kelley band was entertaining and talented- bought a CD, worth the visit to hear them play.

This is a fun place for the family. The food selection is great, the free entertainment even better. This place is definitely an experience plus the stores in the Plaza are worth checking out as well. I personally love going to the Mexican Market, I always find new treats in the store with every visit

We had came here on a Friday afternoon as our first spot. I really enjoyed the music but the service was not the best. The waiter we had was attentive to every other table and left us hanging a majority of the time. However the live music was awesome and I would come back for the music.

Great place, so glad I found it...
I had the BLTAE. Bacon lettuce tomato avocado and egg

Stopped in for cocktails . The Sambuca 75 was very intoxicating and delicious. The service was great. We were the first to open the place so it was very quiet, which was nice. We did not eat so I can only speak for the cocktails and the service. So try the drink next time you are there. It is like a cosmopolitan in a way but with a kick. Enjoy!

We went in for a  late night fried bologna sandwich and ended up staying for the music. Broadway is overflowing with hokey honky tonks filled to the brim with drunk tourists, but Robert's Western World seemed different somehow. Of the four or five bars that we went to, this was easily my favorite. Not a bad sandwich, either! The fries weren't great, though. I'd say skip 'em for a second sandwich.

My husband and I went to Sambuca for a laid-back night out. The jazz band that was playing live was great to listen to! Lots of people were out dancing and having a great time! We sat at the bar watching the NCAA tournament and talking to the bartender and local patrons. The bartender obviously took pride in his work and the bar was kept very clean. He also checked on us often (but not too often) to see if we needed anything.

If you go, I would definitely suggest the creme brûlée! It was fabulous!

My only complaint is that the drinks are pretty pricey.

Great show with Michelle Obama & Stephen Colbert. Only complaint is that after the show started, there were pics on the large screen behind Michelle that did not come up on the smaller screens we looked at . We had to duck our heads  if we were gonna see those pics. Only people in front area and balcony I guess  got to see those.  I think this was a mistake made on Ryman's  part.  Guess they couldn't fix it once the show got rolling.
But still a great show in a favorite venue.  Always. I love my Ryman outings and always forgive  the little things. We are so fortunate to live near here.
Not only was the food beyond exquisite, but Jessie Rice (waiter) made this experience priceless. His attention to detail and service was absolutely exceptional.

Show was fantastic.. 3/21 great songs ..Got carry away with music
Unfortunately the post show tour was terrible
Tour guide , 1, was incoherent, spoke to low and unable to hear.--' ,wantred to learn more about singers   .Showed dressing rooms to a few people  ,Also had trouble with  Free souvenir photo camera
Tour 1,order# 3296768
Feel adjustment should be given.

Sunday around noon. On the stage a good mariachi band is playing. There are boutique stores and restaurants, some just beverage joints. There's a Latino market on the north entrance and inside you can get Mexican food from a steam table -- it's pretty good. Attached to the market is a Colombian restaurant called La Sobrasura Colombiana. The lady speaks no English but I manage to order the Picadas. I am surprised at the $19 cost, but when I get it I understand -- it's huge, way too much for one person, and it's almost all meat -- four kinds of meat! I imagine it's an inexpensive alternative to a Brazilian steak house. Plaza Mariachi could use more restaurants serving food, and fewer boutiques. It will probably grow, but right now it's mostly the curious walking around not knowing what to do with themselves. I'll be back and check out more of the food options, especially at La Sobrasura!

This place has a great atmosphere and the live music is awesome, however, the service is so slow.  My table waited over an hour and a half for our food and it took around 30 minutes to get our drinks. We were there early lunch and the place wasn't that busy so I am not sure why it took so long.  As for the food, it wasn't anything that special.  The fried pickles were great and the brisket taco and pulled pork taco are good.  However, my friends got the turkey club and they couldn't even eat it.  If your visiting Nashville, which is full of amazing food, I would skip eating here.  If your looking for a drink and some music it has a nice atmosphere.

Recently I was at the Ryman for Marty Stuart's Late Night Jam on  a Wed. night in June 2019.  It was wonderful.  I love that the Ryman is so close to Music Row, where all the honky tonk bars are located, all with live music all the time.  This historic theater has good proportions and a good, small-to-medium size, allowing for lots of connection between performers and the audience.  It feels intimate.  One thing to be aware of:  seats on the ground level, in the rear, have vertical posts as obstructions, detracting from one's enjoyment of the show.  So try to avoid getting a seat in the rear half of the lower level.  This theater embodies the history of country music.  It's a national treasure.  Highly recommended.

First stop on Broadway this afternoon. It's a loud venue, but they sound mix to the back of the bar. So fight your impulse to sit up front and center if you're a true live music fan. 

I have a standard amaretto on the rocks, so I can't tell you if the bar tender is any good. This is a place to have beer / shots. Maybe don't expect anything classy. 

Had a bathroom run... no toilet seat covers and the toilet seats make you feel like you need them. But that's pretty standard for most popular bars.
Lots of fun and authenticate environment. Great food and definitely recommend. Can't wait to go again. Shop the markets and enjoy the shows.
Great girls weekend to celebrate a birthday. Amanda was so helpful with the menu and drink selection. Service was on point! Definitely a go to place when you're in town!

I came early on a Saturday night so I didn't experience the "Sardine Experience" people were talking about. I got a local beer (Yazoo Hef) which was awesome and so reasonably priced. They have PBRs for 2.50. Coming from the Bay Area, that price is pretty unheard of. The band I saw was extremely talented--they apparently had an original song that was featured on the show Nashville. I don't watch the show so I don't know much about it. 

Anyway, I know folks say this is touristy but I enjoyed my experience. You can't deny the great music, cheap drinks, and awesome vibes.

This happened to my brother who happens to be a poplar country band drummer! 

On January 30, 2018 my hubby and I was at a charity event with our friends from out of town. I left the group to go home I had to get up early. My husband stayed with the group ( pic below ). @ 11:03pm, They went to the Second Fiddle on 420 Broadway all of our friends were allowed to enter but my husband wasn't. When my husband asked for a reason he was told they do not have to give him a reason after several times of wanting to know why with no answer my husband asked is it because of his race and again was told they don't have to give him a reason.  Our friends asked and they were told the same thing. The manager came to the door and also told him he couldn't enter but our friends could. When my husband questioned he was told I don't owe you a reason and you can't enter (they all left) This was total RASICM!!!!!! DO NOT GO TO THIS PLACE RACISM, SEXISM, RELIGION RACISM WILL NOT BE TOLERATED.......THIS IS A NEW DAY AND THE SECOND FIDDLE WILL HEAR FROM US AGAIN.......IM ASKING ALL MY FRIENDS TO POST THIS ON YOUR PAGE....let's shine a light on the practices of The Second Fiddle....this is not the first time this has happened check Yelp 

https://www.facebook.com/wandalee.howell/posts/1021403

We ate here March 25. Loved it. Our waitress was great. The Buca Beignets are excellent! The Shrimp & Crab Bisque was excellent as well! I also had the Chili Ribbed Scallops over risotto which, truth be told was good but I could have eaten another round of beignets and bisque because they were so good! Loved the atmosphere. The band was jazz that eve and I don't really care for jazz but liked the fact there was live music.

This place is just magical! Only place I'm willing recommend on broadway. Gives you the feeling of old Nashville when everything around is changing so much. The live music is always fantastic. Just read the incredible life story of JesseLee Jones (the owner), he is truly a Nashville legend and you can see him play! Also had the pleasure of checking out Sunday Morning Gospel--a church service on Sunday morning with a gospel band, no alcohol is served from 10:30am-12pm. They even had free coffee and coffee cake. Very special experience, I will be back!

Terrible service just like the Orlando location. They weren't busy but just ignored us while we waited for a drink. Music was great and fun but the staff here has no business on Broadway in Nashville.

I didn't really know what to expect going here. My brother, a Nashville resident, took me here for my birthday and introduced me to the Grand Ole Oprey.  I didn't even know that was a show kind of thing, so this is for anyone wondering what to expect if you go to the Ryman for that. 

Seats are bench style, and not terribly comfortable for long sits, unless your ass has more padding than mine, in which case it might be fine, but then harder to be between the lines on the bench designating your assigned spot.

This is a very festive event, with lots of cheery white folks of all ages having a very good time judging by all the wiggling and smiling.  The show is done in segments, with each having a host. That host does a little music that everyone seems to know, and then introduces other artists for a song or two, followed by the Grand Ole Opry square dancers, and a commercial break where a live guy at a podium reads the commercial old radio style like from the fifties, usually sponsored by farm equipment or the like. I only realized when the commercial came on that this was being recorded as a show. (My Uber driver later told me that he was listening to that show live while driving around.) After the commercial it starts all over like a new show, but with different artists. After the show you can visit the gift shop, but try to do that before, as if there is another show after yours, the crowd will make it difficult to get there. 

I'm not a county music enthusiast, but I did have a really good time doing this, and would recommend the experience to anyone. Oh, not to forget they sell alcohol in the lobby.

Sunday Brunch here was fantastic!!

Stephanie Athington(sp?) band was unbelievable. Highly recommend if you like the classic Sinatra,Bublè and others. 

 Highly recommended! Stephanie's band is unreal! Well done, please bring them back Sambuca!
For a Thursday at 2PM, this place was poppin'. The band playing was awesome, cold beers, and fun crowd.

My husband has been talking about this bologna sandwich for YEARS. I finally got a chance to try it and it was perfect way to end a night on Broadway. The music and crowd were great, and overall the bar was a fun experience.

It's the Mother Church of Country Music-that in itself creates feelings of history and reverence. We visited last night for the Alabama Christmas show, and were incredibly disappointed when Alabama cancelled due to illness and they did not replace them with another headliner. Also-the Christmas show was only 3-4 Christmas songs. The church pews are of course, appropriate, however hard as rocks! The Humana advertisements were absolutely ridiculous in number-we all should have left with refunds from them since there was no headliner. Anywho-it's the Mother Church of Country Music.
Such an awesome venue.  Been here three times in the last couple of years for different events.   Beware of the Dublin Donuts located inside the center.   Staff is very very very very very very rude.
Great drinks, great people, great music! First time in Nashville & this is a must stop. You will not be disappointed grabbing a cheap drink overlooking the best view we've seen so far.

This arena is used for concerts, sporting events and exhibitions. In fact, the weekend we visited there was a National Volleyball tournament, a log home show and a concert! The space is open, clean and visually appealing. Great venue in downtown Nashville.
Great music & great beer; atmosphere is worth coming to & is a spot that hasn't been commercialized. Would recommend as a top 3 spot

As far as convention centers go, this one is one of the best! I've been to the ones in downtown Denver, Houston, New Orleans, Memphis, and Los Angeles. It's the newest in the country!

Since it's so recently built, it's a lovely fit for the hip young town and such a short walk from the incredible food, culture, and music on Broadway. As a 20-something, there's a lot of appeal to me!

I love the exterior of the building. It's huge and glass so there's a lot of natural light filtering in and there are plenty of ideal spots to market your convention. The rooms are fairly large. I haven't been able to determine how the walls change to change room sizes. 

I'll comment that the convention center could use more standing table options for hospitality suites.
Cool place nice music drinks a little week. Great roof top in the middle of downtown.
Honestly if you want to have a good time, don't come here. They are nasty, awful, bitchy bartenders.

A great place to escape the summer heat on Broadway. There's always great live music and the staff is super friendly. Don't miss the balcony / second floor. There are more seats and a separate bar up their with a view of the stage. It's not fancy, but definitely fun.

You won't find a bad seat in the house at the Ryman.  You can see the stage from wherever you are, and the sound is great each and every time I've ever been.  It's a smaller venue, so it's perfect for people that don't care for a massive amount of people or have anxiety issues with large crowds.  
The only negative I have about the Ryman is that the old wooden floors underneath and in between the church pew seating was very thickly covered in filth.  They were swept--but desperately needed cleaning.  If large people are in the pew and women have to put their purse on the floor,  it's just nasty.

When my friend from Austin came to visit me in Nashville, I was looking for activities we could do around the city. Touring the Ryman was at the top of my list! We went on a Saturday afternoon for the self-guided tour. It was so worth it! I didn't know anything about the history of the Ryman, and the self-guided tour starts with an entertaining and informative video. I had NO idea that the Ryman was almost torn down and was vacant for years after the Grand Ole Opry moved from the building! After the video, you can walk around the Ryman, sit in the pews, take photos of the amazing architecture, including the gorgeous stained glass. In the stairwell of the auditorium, there are several panels that detail the history of speakers and performers at the Ryman over the years! Once you get down to the first floor of the auditorium, they have dresses, guitars, hats, etc. worn by famous performers at the Ryman. The self-guided tour is $20 - but it's worth it! It's one of the most fun things I've done in Nashville! I learned a lot about the city, the Ryman, and country music! (There's also a guided backstage tour that is $30.) Tons of fun! Highly recommended!

We visited multiple times while we were in Nashville, and Robert's is definitely the best music venue in that area. Free cover, cheap beers/food and good music. Service can be slow, but everyone is nice and it wasn't a problem. Tip the musicians because it's free cover.

Pretty cool place. I came here today for the Inter-Nash-ional Food Crawl, but as one of the sponsors. While there I enjoyed the live musicians, as well as the acrobat dancers. I also had a chance to try the "elotes in a cup," and it was quite tasty. I'll return with my family to explore more next time, especially Tito's Play-land!

I was in Nashville for a few hours and this place was POPPING on a Tuesday night at 2am. The band was amazing and the drinks were good! The crowd seemed too wasted to respond to the music though - otherwise it was great to be at this iconic place. Just felt a little sorry for the talented musicians.

DID NOT SEE A SHOW. ONLY DID A TOUR. 

The tour starts out great with a well done video of how the Ryman started and became what it is today. After the video, the tour takes you around the auditorium to look at memorabilia and watch a few videos. The costumes were neat, but the price of admission was too high for how little there is to see.

If you're not a huge country buff and know little about the Ryman, my recommendation is to save your money for a better attraction.

I. Love. This. Place. 

Such a amazing venue, the history here is incredible. For shows, I would suggest getting balcony seating unless you are looking at the first few rows.

I was so disappointed in Sambuca this trip. I've been several times before and enjoyed it. However, this time was awful. Our waiter, while nice, seemed like he was yelling at us and called my parents "brother" - my mom was uncomfortable. The drinks were probably the highlight of dinner. We ordered and when our food arrived it was so average. My salmon was barely warm and the Brussel sprouts were almost raw. The rest of the table ordered steaks and they were so over seasoned no one could finish. The band was fun as usual but seemed too loud for dinner. I have no plans to return to Sambuca unless under new management or chef supervision.

The Good: Quality of food; experience; service; selection.

The Bad: notta

The Rest: One of my favorite stops in Nashville. They have a great selection and I never had anything   On the menu I didn't like. I dined as the host of a party of 11 and the service was exceptional.  We had several appetizers in addition to main courses and desert and everyone was pleased with their meal. Following dinner, we stayed for a while to listen to the live music and were made to feel welcome. Final bill was under $1k for a party of 11 with appetizers,  main courses, deserts, and drinks. Great vegetarian selection as well.

We've spent 2 days up and down Broadway and by far the BEST atmosphere and service was here at Robert's! Karen took such great care of us yesterday, we came back for more. We will definitely be back here each visit and this is my most recommended stop for live music, beer and that fried bologna sammich. Find Karen! She will take care of you!

A solid 4 stars.  Friendly, attentive service and live music at 11am on a Monday morning!  They lost a star for food...it was solid, but I could tell my hot chicken was not the best you can get in Nashville.  I also loved the decor...picture attached!
Happy hour is the bomb, bartender was a stud. Get the basil lemonade cocktail and the crab dip. Half price from 4-7 I think
Best venue I've seen a concert at even though its pew seating so if your row if full it's pretty tight.
This place is in a great location and the music and live band is top quality, however the price on food is outrageous and not very much food, for a drink and an appetizer is a great place!

I'm a big fan!!!! So far, my favorite stop on Broadway. We had a lively band of live music. I super duper enjoyed the music, the drinks, and the fun! There was line dancing friendly atmosphere and tons of fun. 

The bar is pretty long, so there's plenty of seating that allows for a view of the show. There's a second bar in the very back. Not super inhabited, but nice to have the optionality. They also had a screen showing the show in the front in case you aren't far enough forward to enjoy the show!

We came here on the last night of our week in Nashville looking for a bit more upscale date night and Sambuca was everything we could have asked for and more! 

Very few places combine such stellar food and ambiance with a staff as invested as our waiter, Jeff. I would have eaten anything he suggested to me - and we basically did! 

Appetizers: Buca beignets were FABULOUS. Deliciously Seared Ahi Tuna portions were sizable, which was welcome. Accompanied by A Victim and Red Apple Spritzer cocktails - so fresh. 

Entrees: Filet and scallops cooked and seared to PERFECTION, and a Miso Sea Bass that was OUT OF THIS WORLD. The apple and cabbage stir fry won't leave my mind!!! Jeff gave us great wine pairings as well upon request. 

For dessert, the creme brûlée was amazing - and Jeff once again went above and beyond by making it all just a touch more special for us. Give that man a raise!!!!!

Also, the band? Charismatic, professional, and soooo talented. I hope they're regulars!

Excellent music, fantastic burgers, and outstanding service by Rachael R.!  I came to town for the Jimmy Buffet / NFL draft weekend.  All of downtown was packed and the energy was great. My friends and I went to more bars than I can count and found ourselves visiting this establishment the most.  We were served by Rachael on our last two visits on Sand we were equally amazed each time with her lightning speed, friendliness and accuracy! 
I highly recommend this place to all who visit the Nashville downtown area. The singers were incredible and every visit was memorable.

I'm a Tin Roof groupie and not afraid to admit it. I definitely prefer the Demonbreun location since it's more of a traditional Tin Roof feel but I'm glad TR has another location that is aligned with all the rest of the Broadway bars - represent! Due to the location and name, you will rarely find this spot empty! With that said, beware of when you come as some don't like to fight crowds.

The Ryman is such an exquisite and beautiful place to go enjoy a show. The acoustics travel through the auditorium with such grace and the rows/pews are well arranged. 

I do not necessarily agree that there isn't one bad seat in the house, as I would not want to be all the way in the back of the main floor due to the balcony blocking half the stage. Again, that may not "block" the performance, but it's not as visually appealing or welcoming. I have never sat in the balcony or sides to comment on those seats. 

Merchandise set up for shows is a bit chaotic and does not easily allow patrons to preview what is for sale before waiting in line...but I do not see anywhere else to set this up better. And the entrance is a bit hectic, but they do a good job for such a small venue. 

Price of food and drink are to be expected for a venue. 

Love the intimate setting and will be back for more shows in the future.

AMAZING. If you're going to Nashville this is a must visit! We saw a Tuesday evening show and it was amazing. This venue is smaller and we had seats that were "limited view" but it was still amazing and I would definitely go again in those seats. The venue is small so I don't think there is a bad spot in the house. Plus this is such a historical site you don't want to miss that!

My sisters and I had dinner tonight on the patio at Sambuca.  Drinks, appetizers and dinner were fantastic!  We started with the beignet and garlic bread appetizers and then had scallops, shrimp & crab scampi and salmon oscar.  Everything was fresh and delicious.  Sambuca was the perfect place for a fun evening in the Gulch.  We'll be back!

Legends Corner left me sorely disappointed my last visit. I was rejected at the door with a valid I.D. of age and in addition to such, the bouncer at the door was extremely tacky and rude at me. He proceeded to yell rude remarks at me as I walked away frustrated with the establishment that I used to deem as a favorite because I had in fact been before. Overall, management needs to shape up and get a better system in place of ID checks if that's what the issue is. I will never be returning my business to this bar in Nashville again.

Everyone said this is a must but I found it overpriced for what you got.  Definitely need to take the back stage tour otherwise your just roaming around a theater on your own.  There's interesting stuff to look at but I wanted more info on the artists.  Ok to visit but not a must in my book

My fiancé and I have gone here for special events 2 years apart. It was the same experience each time - incredible. Because of this last experience, I feel the need to do a review. Tonight our young server was above and beyond. Halfway through the night of great live music, we started to notice an older gentleman making appearances at the tables. Eventually, our original server was nowhere to be found. The older gentleman, who we assume was the manager, had taken over and covered for the server who had fallen ill. At no point did the server disclose he didn't feel well, and continued to give 5 star service. We thought it was very honorable that his manager took over all his tables and sent him home to recuperate, with a seamless transition and continued great experience. We can't wait for the next time. Twice I've had the best steaks I can find in Nashville. 5 stars, only because I can't give 10 stars on Yelp. The food, live music, location, and staff are top notch. Thank you Sambuca.

Ryman is one of the famous stages in Nashville. The history of the Auditorium dates back many years.

Did not come for a show but I wanted to see the site itself.

Huge auditorium, all brick. Built like the historical sites in Philadelphia and Boston. 

Great place to see even if you do not come for a show. You can hear and feel the historical vibes.

It was graduation day for a couple of universities so they were booked up. In light of the fact that all were reserved parties, they were incredibly under staffed. The service was very slow, the Bloody Mary bar was not maintained, the food was mediocre at best.  Oh, and they ran out of one of the appetizers within 2 hours of opening. They were ill prepared for what they most certainly knew was going to be a busy day. I was embarrassed that I chose this place to celebrate our sons graduation and will not return.

I love this place with a fiery passion.  The tour can be interesting, but I really suggest going to see a show at the Mother Church. Any show, any artist, it doesn't matter.  I went to the Chris Stapleton show this past Friday and was blown away.  This venue is spectacular and Chris was as well.

The acoustics will blow you away.  It is almost as if you don't necessarily 'hear' the music as much as you feel it.  That is what makes this place truly special.  Crowds are usually fairly tame as the church Pugh seating makes it difficult to get up and move around too much, although some will try.  

The new renovations go very well with the venue and have only added to the charm.  Go to the Ryman for a show, you'll be glad you did.
A big shout out to Rachael. Great time the 2 nights we were there. Onion rings and bologna outstanding.
Only true authentic place on Broadway. Cheap bar food that is out of this world. Cheap beer and cool place to meet the locals!

I'm in awe of the line cook on a Friday at 1:37 on with a dozen tickets hanging and she is pumping out burgers , fries,  bologna sandwiches, dogs and onion rings 

Impressive.! I don't think she broke a sweat 

Watched her for 30 minutes.  It was methodical annihilation of the tickets with a detail to the timing of making sure all the food was hot and came up at the same time.     If your burger was cold it wasn't her fault. 


The music was more my husbands taste.  Talented but a little cheesy ( think Floribama)

To me the entertainment and true talent was the line cook and the bartenders juggling everyone 

Cheers to the line cook -   Impressive and know you are appreciated !
This is my favorite bar on broadway. Classic honky tonk style country music. Bands are great and the bartenders are fun. The loft is a secret treasure.

If I could split my review in 2 I would. Here's why. The music is phenomenal. It's a great venue for enjoying live, talented musicians. On the other hand, the food and service leave a lot to be desired. While our server was kind, he was also wildly slow (but not in the weeds at all). Appetizers came out well ahead of drinks, and entrees all came out at different times. This may also be a kitchen/bar issue, hard to tell. We ordered calamari, beignets, and civiche to start. The calamari was tasteless and cold. The civeche came with a side of Frank's hot sauce poured in a plastic tumbler. Meh. For my entree I ordered the flat iron mid rare. It was cold, over cooked, and so incredible salty my mouth hurt trying to eat it. The green beans were canned and the potato side dish was bland. I'm also pretty certain the flat iron was not an actual flat iron steak but it was hard to tell because...salt. Anyway, enjoy music? Go here and just stick to drinks.

You can honky tonk this place and experience the "old" country music . The country music with the twang. 
The environment is pleasant , homey, and a mamma and poppa store. 
The hamburger is basic and fries the same. 
What's bonus of this place is its environment.
Def worth the visit .

A little disappointed with this place. The music was okay, we found much better music in some of the other places on Broadway. As for drinks, the selection is not that extensive for hard liquor. I wanted some johnnie walker black and they didn't have any. Overall, it was just okay the night we went there.
Authentic Nashville! The only place we locals go on Broadway. Some of the best music and cheapest beer in town. Make sure to get the "Stimulus Package." You won't be sorry.
Great bar tender upstairs! Better service with $3 beer in plastic cups than down the street.

I don't do crowds. Few things I hate more than being somewhere that feels like being packed in like a sardine. I'll make an exception for this place. Slap packed, but some of the best country music you'll find in town. Don Kelley's band played last night, and they were phenomenal. Skip the big name hype at the other bars, and come here.
Cool place! We just walked through quickly because we were in a hurry, but would love to go back. Lots of shops and food.

One of my hands down favorite bars I've ever been to! We got a recommendation to come here and were really excited as we heard its pretty old school Honky Tonk. On a Saturday night there's dancing in the front and it's absolutely packed so be prepared to be packed like a sardine. We managed to get a table near the bar but it was really hard to 1) find the one bartender and 2) catch the "waitress" as she would come at completely random times since she was overwhelmed. 

The old school music makes this place. The fiddle solos alone are great enough to make you swoon! I'm not even a huge fan of old school country but these bands had me tapping my feet. I also loved how cheap beers were- 2 beers were only $7 (PBR is $2). My only regret is not getting a recession special (fried bologna, chips, and a PBR for $6).

Absolutely love this spot! Stop in!

I don't think there's much more that you could say about this bar that hasn't been said already. It's a necessity to stop in here when you go to Nashville. It is just old country kind of bar it has good music and you can hear yourself talk and you can still dance. The beer is cold and the people are fun You need to stop here at least to get the experience.
I went with some work colleagues and had the grilled red snapper ettoufee and the sopapilla cheesecake. Both were delicious! The band was excellent fun too!

Saw Shinedown there this week....seating leaves a lot to be desired (too crowded in the pews) our seats were under the balcony ( it was like a scrunched dugout), that with the warm temperature in the place made me so claustrophobic I had to go stand in an open area at the back. Probably won't go back.

Excellent meal, service and music.    Everything was cooked to perfection.   Service was at our pace.  Never rushed nor slow.   Our server, Emerson offered great selection and was very attentive.  Chris Matthews band was a nice variety and relatable with the audience.

Plaza Mariachi! I have been holding out on this review for a minute and chose it to be my 2,000 REVIEW!

I frequently come here for dining, window shopping, or to dine. It is a multipurpose space in a strip mall that handles an array of Latin American and South American owned businesses. I love that I can come here for Argentinian or Peruvian cuisine just as easily as I can Mexican.  They also have a spot for bubble tea! Granted that is not Latin, but the diversity exists here.

I love salsa dancing. The Plaza offers it Thursday through Sunday night weekly starting at 7:30pm and ending around 1am. At 7:30, they offer free lessons. The dancing is free as well unless they have a band. Sometimes they will have a cover charge. 21 & up are only admitted after 9pm. 

The space where salsa dancing happens is huge. It is basically in the food court if this was considered a mall. Some dining options stay open late and the bar is also open until Plaza closing time. There is always a huge turnout every night it is held. 

Worried about dancing alone? Don't be. Come here alone and someone is always willing to dance with you. I often come alone and find it more enjoyable since I do not have to entertain friends who might be apprehensive to dance with strangers. I feel safe coming here alone as well. They have security. Plus, they will walk you to your care if you request it. They're generally professional, too, minus the one guy who asked my friend for full body pictures when they exchanged numbers. She cut that off quickly, but I digress...

Plaza Mariachi always has different activities going on. Daily, they have musicians in singing from all genres, not just Latin music. They also do a lot of community events.

I love it here. Come check it out and see what it has to offer!

So I felt I was in the world of Mexico in the Plaza Mariachi. It was a happy feel good vibe inside and the best night life I have encountered in Nashville and surrounding area. It was the perfect end to a busy day at the The 21st Galactic Expo. Watching the dancing     was supremely fun.  I loved going inside the little dress shops too. I really want to visit this place in the day time and go to the little restaurants and boutiques with friends.

Went with a group of 8 the evening after Thanksgiving.  Were promptly seated at the table that had been requested days before.  We were upstairs with a view of the stage.  
The band was good and did get loud at times.  However, they were very entertaining. You are charged $2.00 each on your tab for the entertainment.
Our waiter, as well as back up support, were perfect.  Waters immediately.  Waiter knew the menu and he also advised of the specials.  He was good with keeping up with each tab.  
Food was good for all.  One or two even said theirs was great.  Linda Lou had the Sea Bass and loved it.  I had the ahi tuna seared with a bowl of the shrimp/crab bisque.  Ahi was perfect.  The soup was bland.  
Good selection of craft cocktails and craft beers.  
We will go back again.

Tried to go to Tootsies but it was so busy I couldn't even get a drink so I ended up next door here at 2nd Fiddle.  That was the best decision made.  This place is great. Good music, good drinks and great bar staff (Jessica et al). I came in here on my own and was soon talking with a bunch of people. Everyone was super friendly and just made you feel welcome. It became my go to place on Broadway and is now easily my place to go and hang when in town. Thanks all for a great time!

3.5 Experience 
Nothing Spectacular. We hit this place for Happy Hour. 
Half price drinks and apps! 

The wait time was a bit long for drinks, but worth the wait! Aloha Sunrise was super delicious the only thing better would have been drinking this on the beach! 

I ordered the shrimp and crap dip- it was tasty! I didn't taste the shrimp, but overall good! 
It was very fresh.

The band was interesting- not what I had pictured and played a range of music. Not to loud either. 

Running a bit late to meet the girls, I grabbed a parking spot on the adjacent corner ($20). Good if you are going to be in the area til midnight, but you may wanna cruise if you are just popping in.
Really good food and excellent experience. They had a lot of good performing acts. Authentic Mexican food too
I loved the atmosphere and how quickly we got our food!! The live music was lovely and the food was good. Didn't necessarily like the Mac and cheese but the shrimp and crab soup was lovely
Love love love this place!!! Tuesday nights with Vince Moreno is a country music blast from the past - he's fantastic! A definite Nashville must!

4.5 stars.  It's a pretty cool indoor plaza.  It's like, a big Hispanic shopping plaza.  This was my second time at this plaza.  I came when they first opened and thought it was pretty neat.  You walk in, and it's like, a big food court with different vendors from different places.  There's also a game room, and a bar.  There is live music, and entertainment in the middle of the food court while you eat.  There is also a grocery store inside, and different kinds of shopping stores inside this plaza.  There's even a radio station in there.  Great plaza to check out if you're in the Nashville area.

The Ryman is an event unto itself and not to be missed.  Steeped in music history, the Ryman is the birthplace of bluegrass and the heart of country music.  If you're visiting Nashville, put this at the top of your to do list.  It doesn't really matter who's performing the night you're there.  Consider it a bonus if the performer is someone you actually want to see.  They're all good (they have to be in order to get a date at the Ryman).
Live band music! Delicious food and wine.  It will be my go-to place when I am in Nashville.

I hadn't been to this place in years and now I have stopped by twice in a month for happy hour. Good special on their drinks with some good prices. They also have some good music. One time with a live band and the other with a DJ.

Celebrated my wedding here with a few friends and they made sure to make us feel extremely special. The live music was amazing and dedicated a song to the bride and groom. The food !?? Fantastic !!!!!

Truthfully I had higher hopes for Sambuca. The music was great but the service was awful and the food wasn't particularly good.

The drinks were served after appetizers, and they came in intervals. I was with a party of seven and they brought out two drinks...then after 5 minutes another drink...then after another seven minutes they brought another...you get the point.

Overall, it has a great vibe because you get dinner and a live music show, but I guess people don't come here to eat. Perhaps it's a better date spot or "just drinks" spot, but certainly not for a culinary experience.

A good upscale date night restaurant. Live music starts at 6.30pm. Nice bar area with upper level seating area as well as an outdoor patio area. Bit more on the pricey side but it's worth the splurge. Food was very filling and delicious. Highly recommend the ribeye steak entree as well as the shrimp &crab linguine.
Terrible bar. Music was decent. Blonde server with dreads needs to go... the table next to us said he was an asshole as well. Won't be back.
Great dive bar with good music and reasonably priced beer. We loved the music enough here to stay for a couple of beers.  Would definitely go back!

Here for chinese new years celebration plenty of food options that look good havent chosen a place to eat yet but asking people about their food options everyone says all the food is great and good portions...would recommend this place because it has plenty of options...

The Good: Music and people watching.

The Bad: Beer was not cold; area behind the bar was dirty.

The Rest: stopped in after dinner at The Southern for an after meal beer and music. Had a bottle of Laginitus IPA and it was warm :( Music was good. Crowd was moderate. I left after one drink.

It is with the deepest sadness that I have to give Robert's this terrible review.  Robert's used to be the best bar in downtown Nashville.  It is now a shell of its former self and I will never go back.  I've been going to Robert's for 25 years and it's just a shame that this bar is now one of the worst on Broadway.  The old Nashville is gone and sadly the real Robert's will just be a memory in our past.  Sic Transit Gloria.

This place is great.  Cheap beer, grill at the bar and awesome music.  Great small bar where everyone was friendly. The staff was super even when slammed. $2.50 Busch lattes and good music..best in town. We will be back!

Legends is always a great spot to stop for live music. We always try to grab a table by the railing in the upper bar - great view of the bands. As with many of the spots on Broadway, Legends looks a little "worn" but it's a classic and the music's great!

My wife and I started out here, music was great but a bouncer (named Chris) was on a power trip or it's just shady practice to keep people out after they order drinks. Luckily we went to the stage on broadway right after and enjoyed the rest of the night.

The best part of this meal was the biscuits and gravy! I could eat a whole meal of this. I shared the turkey brie and fried chicken sandwich with someone and both of them were good. I think that only having a half of each sandwich was perfect because they were both a little rich. The chicken wasn't completely white meat which grossed me out a little. Also I didn't love the combo on the turkey sandwich. I would be willing to try other things the next time though.

I had the pleasure of visiting this fantastic American city for 6 days and had a beer (Or three) in almost every one of the honky tonks on Broadway. For a number of reasons, this one makes the top 3. The quality of the musicians and the standard of the bands was immense. The bar staff were friendly and knew their stuff. I didn't eat here but the food that I did see arriving at tables looked amazing. Very clean toilets. Another bar upstairs and a cheeky little smoking area. Good screens for sports fans as well. All in all a great place on the strip. I indulged in 6 visits in 6 days! Enjoy live music? Enjoy The Tin Roof.

My mainstay watering hole during my trips to Nashville.  I try to avoid Broadway with the exception of a few places. Roberts, Second Fiddle, Layla's, and Legends. Sometimes Tootsies.  All at the corner of 5th and Broadway.  The place has all the charm you'd expect from and old school music hall and bar.  Go there for the early shows to see real Nashville. Stay later to see the house band, Don Kelly, cover some outlaw country classics. While the food selection is limited it is awesome. THE BEST fried baloney sammich or an awesome cheeseburger with all the fixings. No fries, chips! Good selection of beers but it really is a PBR kinda place.
Amazing live music. Their ocean water is great. The Broadway superstar is good too but the raspberry was a bit syrupy.

Love this place!!! Jessica the bartender is so sweet and fun. Always have a terrific time. Steer clear of all the gimmicky places. If there is a big time country singers name on the door u can pretty much know it's crappy. Places like this are what makes Nashville amazing. Thanks Jess!!

From my understanding, this place is not always open, but I was here in early December and was lucky enough to see a show. The music was great and the energy of the performers was fun, positive, uplifting, and just made you want to dance. Surprised by the performance by Luke Brian at the end of the night. This experience really turned my NY/NJ daughter of an immigrant attitude toward understanding the love of country music! The establishment is actually quite active on social media, surprising! The whole of the building was not as much as I had anticipated; I thought to show up an hour early to tour the building, but you definitely do not need to do that. Also, the seats are mega uncomfortable, but it's fine. All seats are not created equal, some places do not see all parts of the stage. And don't even think about sneaking to an empty seat mid-show, they will find you. It was very interesting to hear the live radio advertisements being made.

We were looking for a place to eat dinner before the Pink concert.  We stopped in to the Tin Roof and found an empty table... there are no signs that say you can seat yourself. So we asked a passing waitress, and she said we could sit but the kitchen was closed until 7. I thought that was weird but we don't go downtown very often.  The waitress was Amanda and she was wonderful! She brought over menus and asked if we wanted something to drink.  At exactly 7 she came over and took our order.  I got the south southwest quesadilla and fries. Yum! Unfortunately they were out of French fries( so weird) but ordered the tots instead and I'm so glad I did.. they were golden brown and came in a big basket.  My husband ordered a combination of tacos.. unfortunately they were out of the fish.. but he loved the chicken and ground beef.  Our food came out quickly and hot... Amanda our waitress was super sweet and on point!!! I wish I knew what band was playing because I would come back to listen to them again.  They played some 80's songs!! Overall, we were very happy with everything and will be back!!
This place was just incredible the live band was amazing the drinks were good the atmosphere was awesome. Would recommend coming here if you're a outer Towner like me.

This is for sure see on anyone Country bucket list. However don't expect more, by paying for guided tours than self guided. Yes you get to go back stage. However it is very rushed, and for what you pay, I felt like you should be able to soak it all in. So much history and wonderful music I wanted to share with my 15 year old, but was off and running and back to self guided in less than 30+ minus I would guess.
Giving a little more info to what you get for your money would be s great thinf.
Just a great hangout for classic country music - lots of fun - dancing - packed - fun decor - you gotta swing by just to say you did!! It's a great spot come on in!!

The $18 tour is definitely the one to do. For $4 more you get the backstage tour and someone who guides you through the history of the venue which you would otherwise not fully get due to the normal tour being self-guided with reading stations that leave a lot of be desired.
If it wasn't for the tour, I likely would've given this just 2 stars. But the tour allows you to learn about a variety of other things about the Ryman that you wouldn't get.
Very enjoyable tour of the historic theatre. We paid extra for the guided tour, and it was worth it for the behind-the-scenes access.

Robert's is one of the last standing true Nashville homes for all. If you visit here from out of town, be respectful, tip the band, and tip your bartender. We are living to work here in your vacation town and must pay our rent/mortgage. Caroline behind the bar is as close as you can get to a real life guardian angel and deserves every ounce of your kindness just like the rest of Robert's staff. Please patronize this long standing amazing business, have fun while you're at it and most importantly BE RESPECTFUL.

So much history at the Ryman! The exterior and interior still resemble the church it originated from, giving it a lot of charm. There is something comforting about sitting in a church pew and listening to some great music. 

I rate the Ryman a 3 because you have to be careful where you sit. The main floor has many pillars holding up the balcony that can directly impede your view if you didn't choose your seat wisely. My suggestion is to  sit further up on the main floor or get balcony seats because if you sit under the balcony, your view will be impeded at some point during the show. 

Despite this, the Ryman is a must and it has never disappointed me!

I honestly was expecting a lot more. From everything I heard, I thought there would be more variety in good options - the pizza and gyro/kabab places just make no sense to me here. Why not have a pupuseria or some type of other latin based food like paella from Spain. The taco place was such a let down, I assume they were heated in a microwave because I didn't hear or see a griddle. The tortillas were cold and not heated as in grilled or fried in any way. To me this place is about the shops, live music, and snacks like palettas or the crazy corn in a cup (which was delicious). The grocery store is awesome. To me there are far better places to have an authentic meal on Nolensville Rd. Maybe I have higher standards coming from Miami. I'll give it another try for sure, maybe the Argentinian place (Tres Gauchos?)

After reading some recent negative reviews, I almost didn't go to this great place. But since I was staying at the Thompson Nashville a half block away and it was raining intermittently, I decided I'd rather walk than drive. The place was excellent, from ambience to service to food and live band. Anastasia was our server and super pleasant and helpful. The steaks and seafood and desserts were so good. I'm a bit of a foodie, but not hypercritical, and they did a nice job, about $80 per head after tip and that included entree, several drinks, and dessert but we didn't do appetizer bc we didn't want to be too stuffed. All in all a satisfying, enjoyable visit. Thanks, Sambuca!

Attended a private party on second floor provider by a vendor at a conference that I attended.  I really loved this place.  Good apps (loved the chicken & waffle nuggets), cold beer, attentive staff.  Great live music by a talented singer Mary Todd & a young man whose name I can't recall (sorry)!  Good vibes at this place!
Best place in Nashville, a must , great live music , great atmosphere, amazing comfort food ...

Great atmosphere!  The service was very good & attentive. Food was AMAZING and the accommodations they made for my dietary needs were second to none. I had the salmon and will for sure have it again. One thought - hire a professional sound person because we couldn't hear the lead singer for much of the first set.

Came here on a Friday evening with a friend for dinner. The drinks were awesome (happy hour was still going on and the waiter was good at notifying us when happy hour was ending so we could order more drinks.) the live music was awesome as well - added to the cool ambiance of the restaurant. The food was ok, we split the shrimp and crab dip, beignets, shrimp and crab bisque, and macaroni and cheese sides. Would recommend getting a reservation before coming here. But definitely come for the happy hour deals!

The live band and loud chatter make this a cool spot to hangout and drink with friends, not so much for a date with intimate conversation lol 
The food was good, not great as aspected with the price...overall you're paying for the ambiance, which was great. 

Side note*our waitress was EXTRA attentive which was mildly annoying...barely half way through my meal she was asking if I needed a box to go...then followed up with no rush...which made me feel rushed‍

Had the chicken sandwich. Only okay, analytics nothing special.
Service was very friendly but getting the good was slow.
Live music was entertaining for a Sunday afternoon.
Not sure I'd eat here again.

The Madison Square Garden of Country Music, such a great and historic place. The tour is outstanding and I highly recommend to everyone who goes to the Nashville area. We went on the self guided tour, and saw everything that we wanted, including going on the stage. Have to get back there to go a show.
Was fun visiting there. Music was very good.  Food was ok and i guess one doesn't go there mainly for the food. All said and done, go there and enjoy a beer and the music. Staff was very welcoming.

So I'm giving Sambuca a 5 star rating because of our server (Tyler). Here's the story....we had drinks at Sambuca in the afternoon. After leaving, one in our party realized she had lost her credit card. We called Sambuca. The person who answered the phone seemed un-interested in our plight so we got back in a cab and returned to Sambuca. Tyler ( who had not been informed of the phone call) looked through all of his receipt books until he found it! He then refused a tip! Thanks Tyler!

This place was recommended by friends. However, the service was AWFUL!. Our waiter, Ken, neglected us all night. After bringing us our initial drink order, no one checked on us for over a half hour. With long empty drink glasses, I had to flag down another server and ask them to find our waiter for us. When he finally came by, he apologized for the delay, took our second drink order, and assured us our food would be out soon.

After being seated for over an hour, he brings out -- our entrees. I asked what happened to our appetizer? He apologized for forgetting and offered to get it for us. But, it was too late by then.

Since it was my wife's birthday, I asked for some cake with a candle (which another table near us had received earlier). And, we also ordered another desert to share. But another half hour later, it still hadn't arrived. I flagged Ken down from serving another table and signaled for him to bring my check. He offered to bring our desert boxed up to-go. But, I just told him to cancel it and bring the bill.

Viewing the bill, they at least didn't charge for the appetizer they forgot or the desert that never came. But, considering the poor service, I would have expected some kind of consolation, such as comp'ing a round of drinks or something.  

The experience ruined our birthday celebration. I will never return.

What a wonderful event we had at Sambuca in Nashville!!!

We had a rather large party for dinner - a gathering of family in town for a wedding - and we couldn't have been happier with the setting, the food, the music, and the way we were taken care of by our server Jesse.  (Everytime someone left the table, Jesse would fold up there napkin into a beautiful rose :) )

We had a variety of four appetizers and each one was better than the next.  I don't think you can go wrong there.  As for dinner - it was the best sea bass I've ever had.  My husband gave me a bit of his scallops and they were awesome too.  All 15 of us loved our dinners.

A special thanks to the manager Casey who visited us to be sure we had everything we wanted, which we did.

Thanks Sambuca!  You will be on my list whenever I visit Nashville!!

The Roman Auditorium is the true birthplace of the country music variety show...that is before the Grand Ole Opry was completed. The round stage, in fact, was donated to the latter to provide some continuity when the music moved elsewhere.  A great tour and colorful history should be on any Nashville list.  It's well worth it.
The Ryman is a must see if you are in town! I do wish we booked the guided tour to hear more about the history.

Fun bar with great music other than country. This was one of our favorite bars in Nashville. Country is not really our music. They played some great rock and roll old school music. Friendly staff and a great time!

This is the Broadway honkey tonk you want to visit.  

It is as old school as it gets in the land (street) of new neon bars that us locals recommend.   

Go in for the classic country and stay for the grilled food -- grilled cheese, fried baloney sandwich -- you must check out the food menu! 

**you can't miss the "recession special" on the menu for $6 - PBR + chips + fried baloney sandwich

Stopped here for lunch while traveling through Nashville with family. The food was good bar food. The pork chop sandwich was tasty and hot, and the onion rings were outstanding. It's no-frills food and the menu is pretty small, but that wasn't a problem for us. The service was fast and extremely friendly. It's definitely got a cool dive-bar type feel. The live music was excellent, authentic classic country (shout-out to Rachael Hester and the Tennessee Walkers, who were nearing the end of a 3-hour set when we got there). It's relatively small inside, but there is a small balcony if you can't find a place to sit on the ground floor. I would highly recommend this place and would definitely come back if we're in the area again.

Such a great experience to visit this bar. The band (on the night of 8/7/13) played classic country songs, and the singer was talented, yet funny enough to entertain the crowd. He came off the stage and walked around, partly to collect tips but also interact with the people in the bar.
The bartenders were friendly, and prompt in serving drinks and snacks that we ordered.

With numerous Honky Tonk bars on Broadway in Nashville, The Second Fiddle will surely be my first recommendation to anyone that is in town and wants to listen to authentic country music. There is a little dance floor for those of you that are looking to swing the hips. The interior is cool, with antique radio receivers and instruments decorating the walls.

Want an authentic country music bar that seems to have bachelorette party repellant hanging over the door? So did I, and that's exactly what I found at Roberts. Reasonably priced, good crowd of all ages, and great old country tunes. Loved my time here.

Yes to the Bologna Sandwich!  Simple...but delicious. My husband ordered the turkey and Swiss.  He regretted not getting the fried bologna...like I suggested he should. I let him have a bite...but I didn't share. I wanted it all to myself. It was so good!
Don't make the same mistake my husband did.

Plaza Mariachi is a great concept and i was very excited to come here for the first time on a Friday night. The interior is very nice, new and clean. I wasn't able to fully explore but spent most of my time in main food court area. Overall, I wasn't blown away by my experience but will highlight the hits and misses. 
The food court is really nice with a big stage and live music. I really enjoyed the ambiance and the music was fantastic. That was definitely a highlight of the night. 
Our first stop (obviously) was to grab a drink at the stand set up in the food court. They had wine, palomas, margaritas and beer. We ordered a margarita and a paloma, and I liked the paloma a lot more than the margarita but unfortunately the grapefruit juice was out of a can and not fresh. The margarita was also missing something... I can't quite put my finger on it but I really didn't like it. 
Everyone was raving about Tres Gauchos and it had by far the longest line in the entire place. We were pretty hungry so we stopped at the tapas place to get a snack, Las Tablas. Unfortunately they immediately told us they were out of most of the menu so we were limited on what we could order. Luckily we were able to get some manchego cheese with honey and patatas bravas. Both were very good. 
I decided to skip the slow moving line of Tres Gauchos and opted for Botanas Lokas instead; the Mexican snack stand which had tacos, street corn, candy and other small bites. I tried the chicken, pork, and barbacoa tacos and liked them. The street corn was fantastic and I liked the pork taco but the other two were just OK. Honestly, I would have much preferred the taco trucks that are right down the street on Nolensville Road. 
I sampled some of the meats from Tres Gauchos, and wasn't a fan. Not only did you have to wait in line a long time to order, it took another 20 minutes or so for the food to come out. Expect to wait if you eat here! The chimichurri options were good (especially the spicy one) and the steak was definitely better than the chicken which was overcooked and didn't have much flavor. The street corn was not good either, but the empanada was delicious. They aren't on the menu and may have been a special of the night. 
The pistachio ice cream was very tasty for dessert and overall I still like the concept and think it has potential, but some of the food was a definite let down. I'd come back but would make different selections.

I was really excited to go here for our nice dinner out for my bachelorette weekend but was left hungry and extremely disappointed. Our server was the only bright light in the whole situation. 
We sat down ordered drinks, and received them quickly, our mixed drinks were delicious. Then we ordered our salads, soups, apps and entrees. Salads and soups came out quickly but after 30-40minutes our apps (bruschetta and the goat cheese stuff artichokes) still were not out. When they did arrive after we complained on not getting them, the artichokes were room temperature at best but we were hungry so we ate them.
Then our entrees didn't make it out until almost an hour after we ordered them. Once they arrived we were ready to dig in only to find that they were cold. The flat iron wasn't cooked and was raw, the Au gratin potatoes were totally uncooked. My risotto was tasteless and was hard and room temperature. We were so hungry but we all barely ate our dinners because it was cold and frankly inedible.
We complained and after going back an forth they comped all the food but we still left hungry and disappointed in what was supposed to be a nice dinner out to celebrate my bachelorette.
We paid for the drinks we ordered and took good care of our server because it was not a fault of his.
They really need to get their kitchen together, the kitchen will be the demise of this place.
If I were you I would think 10 times before going here for dinner.
If you want blues and Country music, you must come here.  It is a dive bar with a grill.  My top two of bats if you are coming to Nashville.  Well unless your not a country fan.
Excellent restaurant!!! I went on a Saturday night. The food was excellent and the band was awesome!

The best chicken & waffles EVER! The chicken was crispy and juicy and complemented perfectly by gravy and a very spicy and unique syrup. The waffle was golden and delicious. Very generous serving.

Bonus - there was also a great live band playing!
Our favorite place on Broadway - Rachel was fabulous as a bartender and server - we had a group of 13 and enjoyed every minute -- the music, cold beer, onion rings and bologna sandwich!

2 stars instead of one because of the amazing history. But otherwise to me this place seems totally overrated as a music venue. Very uncomfortable seating for a longer show. Better places to see music in Nashville IMO but the history is indeed amazing.

Had one afternoon in Nashville and wanted a Hinky Tonk experience.  Had the bologna sandwich, which somehow tasted better than any bologna sandwich I've had. The live music and cheap beer completed our experience.

Had an ok time here. Stopped by to have a few drinks and enjoy music. Music was good, food and drinks were good. But service was everything but. The bartender asked if we wanted to keep and open tab and when we said no he replied "so this is your last drink?" Almost pushing us out of the establishment. Overall just an OK experience. Especially on Valentine's Day.

Just like your favorite local bar back home!  We stopped in for a quick burger and beer and we were not disappointed.  No issues finding a seat on a Tuesday afternoon a few hours before a hockey game.  Only bottled beer, but a nice selection.  Burgers were good and so were the sweet potato fries.  And the live music was fine too!

This bar has to be by far my MOST favorite bar that I experienced while in Nashville for a 5 day girls trip. The managers, bartenders and especially the barbacks were nothing but nice. We were quite the rowdy group and probably a bit annoying if you ask me, but they always spoke to us with patience and respect. I do have to give a big praise on the bar backs Dustin and Dylan. They were constantly working, cleaning and still managed to keep a smile on their face, while having to deal with us talking to them NONSTOP. I mean when have you ever met a bar back that finds you food close by & gets it delivered for you? 
Chad and Haley were great bartenders, always quick with our drinks. We even came back for a 2nd day and noticed Chad wasn't feeling, but still busting his butt to keep customers happy. I had the pleasure of chatting with the managers Desi (Drake's Twin) and Brad (Jason Aldeans dad) who were also very visable at all times and didn't mind us being ourselves in the bar. At the end of the night we were gathering our things to find our Uber the manager, Brad helped us find the right Uber which was awesome. Highly recommend going here if you are looking for great staff and drinks. The music was great too, but once you have enough drinks in you, what music isn't Good? 
I will be back soon to Nashville and visiting Second Fiddle!

This is a great Nashville experience- highly recommend to start your evening here. Just don't sit too close to the stage as conversation will be hard... as it is in most live music venues. Service has always been great- food is a 4/5- usually good but not the best I've ever had.

Love love this place.  So much history, good music all the time and a great staff.  It's a shame bars like this are being taken over by country music "name" bars that are all the same machine.    Don't let these gems disappear!
Amazing time and a definite must if you have not been. The staff is friendly and the acoustics sound was amazing!

Great place with the affordable drinks in Nashville. Bologna sammy is delish- try it with cheese!  2.50 Busch lights kept us coming back every day. Karen and Katie are the best! Super friendly and sweet and even recognized us each day!! Sending much love from MN and we plan to come back to see you guys!!

Was in town for a get away and decided on Sambuca based on yelp reviews. I must say it did not disappoint ! It was in a great location in the Gulch area of Nashville. Valet was super easy and we walked in on a Friday night and promptly seated. I would recommend reservations though. If we hadn't had reservations , it looked like a 30 minute wait that grew as the night went on. 
We had a super professional waiter (Keith) who was very knowledgeable about the wine and food selection , helping us pair just the right food and drink. The stuffed artichoke appetizer got things started and was delicious. The spinach salad followed and was proper size and flavor. The seared scallops were the highlight though , simply out of this world! The BEST scallop dish I have ever had ! Finished off with the chocolate tote which was absolutely wonderful. The music was live and super good we really enjoyed our entire experience. Will definitely return !!

Very unique venue.  I went to see Jill Scott and had great seats.  However, after sitting for very long, the seats were starting to get uncomfortable.  I loved the intimate setting and the production was great.

Two bartenders told me that Nashville was no longer a country music town. One of the bartenders even said it and then "dropped the mic". Then had two security guards stand behind me after I said this bar was more of an LA bar than a country bar. Perhaps they were right that Broadway was no longer a country location, but I walked 10 seconds down the street and was in an old school country bar and happy. This bar is just like any other bar in any other city. Don't go here if you're looking for a country bar. It sucked. If you want an LA bar with bartenders who are obnoxious and willing to call security guards for zero reason then this is your place. Drop mic and the 20 something douchebag bartenders can promote more candy pop music for $10 a pop and make Nashville less country and more MTV. Johnny Cash (if these loser bartenders have ever even heard of him) would roll over in his grave. This place blows.

Im ganna start this review in a weird way but who cares...i just gotta start by saying that their cheese queso is some of the best queso ive ever tried. Came here for a quick lunch and had a nice time. Got the loaded tots to start and they were great. A little small but a very nice app with amazing queso lol. For lunch got the pulled pork sandwich which was average id say but got queso on the side for the fries which was a great call. 
Bar is cool and has a unique look with stickers and sharpie everywhere. They had some live music which was very loud so we sat in the back. Bartender was a little nasty but she was the only one bartending and had a pretty full lunch crowd. 
Overall a decent spot to stop for a bite to eat at a reasonable price.

The birthplace of the Grand Ole Opry!

They close at 4pm but you can stay until 4:30pm if you get in before they close. In total it takes about 45 minutes to go through the self-guided tour. An adult ticket costs $24.95.

At the beginning they have a very cool interactive presentation about the history of the Ryman Auditorium. It was also a bit creepy as if the person narrating is haunting you. When you walk out of the presentation at the other end of the building there's a wall that has the history of the auditorium that you can take your time and read.

After the presentation you can take a tour of the auditorium and take pictures. You can even take pictures of yourself on stage. They also have a photographer there to take pictures of you and is included with your ticket! At the end of the tour you get a physical copy when you leave which makes for a nice momento.
Kate is such a wonderful bartender! Friendly, personable, attentive- highly recommend checking this spot out for a brewski and a fried bologna sandwich!

When I was visiting Nashville, I heard some good live music coming from this bar so we decided to walk in for a few drinks. Unfortunately the band was taking a break about 15 minutes after we got there but the drinks were good and there was a good vibe here.

I am giving this place a 4 star - not because the food is anything special or tied to the unique Nashville culinary scene, but because we were a group of 12 women for a bachelorette party and they provided nice ambiance, and service.   It is hard to go all-out foodie when you're a group that big, so I think for what we got, it was good.  

They have a huge dim-lit space, a stage with live music and even an area for dancing. Our server was a sweetheart; answered a lot of questions, was attentive, was fun, took a ton of photos of us, split the bill without issue based on what we each ordered (this must be uniquely Nashvillian because they do not do this in NYC- though I never mind splitting evenly).  He greeted us with bottles of champagne, provided by a female not in attendance, so they do, do bottle service. I feel like they made my bride to be friend special which is what mattered. We go ta big comfortable table in the middle of the room.  Menu is big and has variety.

I shared food with my bestie girlfriend to the left - we shared a fresh shrimp ceviche (could have been better but wasn't bad, was fresh.. just lacked some flavor and usually ceviche complexity)...I ordered the blackened snapper etoufee which was good - good portion of blacknened snapper, shrimp, and crab dip.. which was super creamy. Kind of wished they had less of this and more of the dirty rice, which was little but a bit small for portion.  They dish also had crunchy French onions (like the salad topper) which gave what would have been a mushy dish some texture.  It was good - and great for if you are hungry. In highsight, I also would have tried the scallops which they recommended. 

Lots of girls were getting a mixture of sides, or salads - my gf got the portobello mushroom, asparagus and salad... The one scallop she ordered was $7 though which was a bit ridic. She was told it was an add on order for surf and turf.. Idk. Anyway, boo.  I guess being this kind of entertainment place you can expect prices to be in the upper 20s to low 30s for meh to good food. 

They also had an extensive drink menu, including some drinks that were... lol.. "naked" aka less calories.  I guess they try to target women. 

It was great for our purposes (seating a large group) but if coming to Nashville just to eat, I wouldn't go. It's in a nice neighborhood though. Amazingly, the server did not add auto grat also.. which was a kind gesture but that was a surprise with a group so large.

Four of us on a girls trip stopped in for a cocktail.  Travis waited on us, gave us a great recommendation, the strawberry lemonade cocktail and took great care of us.  After we left I realized I was missing my credit card.  We called them but they claimed they did not have it.  Went back  there to double check and as soon as Travis heard I was missing the card,  he started searching all the black bill holders.  He found it!  He made the extra effort and saved my vacation.  What a fabulous employee.  Thanks Travis!

Very disappointed from our evening at Sambuca tonight.  Food was good, atmosphere was good, music was good but after drinks, appetizers, dinner, desert and spending nearly $1000 on family and friends from out of town (7 of us total) which we had invited for the night, we were asked to leave because "they had reservations for our table and the people were waiting."  This after the manager and server had been hovering by our table for some time while we were eating our desert.  My family from out of town which has experienced many nice restaurants throughout the world said they had never been treated like this in any restaurant.  Very embarrassing for me.  I realize you want to turn tables but we tipped very well, we were not loud and we were not there longer than any other tables around us.  Very poor decision on the manager that asked us to leave.
