He then didn't even want to talk about it and walked away from us.  I just hope that you don't treat all patrons like we were treated tonight.  If you do, you will not succeed in the very competitive market in the Nashville area.  What was a nice evening for us was completely ruined by a Manager's actions.  Disappointed!!
One of best bars in Nashville.  Authentic Honky Tonk.  Jessica and crew are Best Bartenders in Nashville.   Always great artists.
This is one of the best options in downtown Nashville. Our waitress Amanda was amazing please ask for her when you make your reservations!

Robert's Western World is by far the best place to spend a night on Broadway. It's the perfect spot for kicking back and listening to some classic honky tonk. 

It was super crowded before 1:00am, but as the night wore on, the crowds dwindled and we finally had some breathing room to post up at the bar for a bit, and later, scoot our feet across the small dance floor for a couple songs.

Every staff member we interacted with was exceptionally welcoming. Becky especially is such a sweet soul! You don't typically connect with the staff at a bar, let alone at a bar in one of the busiest night life scenes in the US, but the staff at Robert's is so friendly! They treat every customer with respect and dignity, and want to ensure everyone has a great time. If you have been to Nashville recently you'll understand why this was surprising. It's an absolute zoo on Broadway! 

You're not going to find a better bar for classic honky tonk music, cheap beer and friendly people. Be sure to stop in for a drink and a song or two at this special place!

This was a great stop when checking out the bars on Broadway. The beers were cold and there was good music which is the main thing. We unfortunately got there when the the band was just ending and it was between sets but still a good time.

The food here is actually atrocious. The charcuterie board was embarrassingly overpriced and the cured meats were disgusting. The carrots were inedible and extremely burnt. Their cheese sticks were fast food level. It seems as if it's only redeemable quality is there is always live music. DO NOT come here for dinner or appetizers. You will be disappointed.

Going to 5 seconds of summer concert and the line was very disorganized and just a mess. The concert began and there were still at least 200 people still waiting and there's trash everywhere and barley any security. I don't know if I would come back.

People who actually write bad reviews for The Ryman astound me. They're really just whining.  The acoustics are great. The venue itself is great with lots of character and history. I feel Nashville is lucky to have it. 

Yes, there are church pews. It is the Mother Church, after all. They add to its character. Many say that they are uncomfortable. I don't really find them to be so, but you can take in cushions like you would to a ball game. I saw one guy say he didn't like them because he felt he was at church. Really?  Are we looking for things to complain about?  I've never really felt like a packed sardine in the pews, but I am neither overweight nor were any of the people in the rows I've been in so far. Maybe I've just been lucky. 

The columns are there to support the balcony. I have not found them nor the balcony obstructive of my view. When I saw Weezer I supposedly had an "obstructed view" according to the seating chart, but I saw everything fine. The columns aren't that big. 

I highly recommend seeing a show at the Ryman. You should at least once in your lifetime.  And keep your cranky pants at home. 

Tip:. Free valet for Nissan owners!  They even leave bottles of water thanking you for being a part of the Nissan family in your car!

Not sure what to say other than going to Nashville without an evening at the Ryan would be like a day without light, or going to Chicago and not going to Wrigley Field. I can't imagine not making this the number 1 thing on your list to do. It was without a doubt the best part of our trip and something we will always remember.

I will admit your experience may depend somewhat on who's performing and we so fortunate to be there the night they handed out awards for the songwriters. We saw Blake Shelton, Darius Rucker, Jewel, Jamey Johnson, Old Dominion, Thomas Rhett and several others that I had never heard of but thoroughly enjoyed.

Regardless, this place is special.

In Nashville - So many bars and honky tonks, so little time...

If I had one afternoon/evening in Nashville, this is the place!!

Music from Wendy Newcomer and her band was fantastic!!  

Service was warm and hospitable, ambiance is everything you would expect in a dive bar, we did not try the food offering so, no comments on food. 

Even the patrons were nice - met people from Canada, Indiana and some locals, too.  

Highly recommend.

We attended a show a few nights ago at the Ryman.  I love the history of the venue and love the venue itself.  The wood church pews were actually more comfortable than I expected.  Midland put on an amazing show!  Unfortunately a very inconsiderate couple chose to stand the entire show.  We were in the balcony where no one else in the area was standing.  The 4-6 rows behind the couple could not see the stage at all. People around them asked politely several times if they would sit down. The guy was drunk and extremely rude.  Ryman staff was notified and would do nothing. They have a policy of not interfering with attendees. Really disappointing After driving 4.5 hours for the show.

Definitely an older venue. My first time here was earlier in the year. 
The usual security check. However, not very many vendors for food and drinks. There are some, but not like the other venues. Sound was not great during our show. Wouldn't say I'd be thrilled to go back.

Comfortable venue and plenty of space for 12 or so people to go enjoy a meal and great music.

Pros:  
Food is fresh
American sized portion
Waitstaff is attentive
Water glasses kept replenished
Dirty dishes kept off the table
Music is good
Menu has plenty of variety.
Chairs are comfortable

Cons:
Lacking BAM! in the dishes.
Expensive
Waitress suggests the most expensive wine on the menu, and doesn't tell you.


I agree with everyone that said that the dishes sounded good, but lacked ooomph.
I had the salmon Oscar tonight and the hollandaise sauce had dill in it, but I didn't taste it.  I saw it, but didn't taste it.
Asparagus was cooked perfectly, salmon was cooked perfectly, portion size was more than ample.  In fact, half the size would have been perfect.

Dessert:  I ordered the bread pudding with a syrup on it, and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.  The bread pudding was so dense, it definitely needed much more syrup than what they put on it... It needed all the bites to be wet...  They were not.
But that's just piddly stuff..
I think flavor  is lackluster.  It's like someone is afraid to create art with herbs, spices and salt....

Wine:  I asked for a Pinot Grigio.  Waitress suggested a brand. I accepted, and then when I saw the price on the check.. I was surprised she suggested the most expensive Grigio on the menu...  When I looked at the wine list, there were 3 Pinot's... and the one she suggested was the most expensive.
I wished she had said out loud, "This ** Pinot is a good one, and it's $15/glass."
I think that would have been more honest.

The place was just less than half full at 6:30 on a week night.

All in all..... 
there is at least 2 new restaurants opening a week, here in Nashville..  Not sure when I'll get back to this one.  Nothing was memorable.

This place is one of those that you want everyone to know about but you don't want it to change. Great musicians, friendly staff and just the feel like you are in a place that knows it's a honky tonk without having to try

This place is awesome! Was here a few weeks ago for a Thursday night get away and had a blast. The food is great, the music is great and the people who work there are amazing. 

The band, The Cosmic Collective performed that night and were fantastic! Definitely will come back again for some more fun.

I just got back from my dinner here. We are here for a week visiting and this was the greatest first night place. We are celebrating my 30th birthday and we were lucky enough to have Emerson as our server. Not only did he give us a recommendation on an amazing drink he was great through the entire meal. He helped us know the good places to visit on our trip in Nashville. I am so thankful for him he was funny and so personable and so helpful! He really made our first night in Nashville extremely memorable! We would come back just for him let alone the food and drinks! This place is a must go and definitely ask for Emerson if you want a one of a kind experience!!!!!

This is a Broadway joint that you imagined and hoped all of Broadway to be. Tremendous "classical" country and rockabilly bands. I had a bologna sandwich for the first time in like 15 years as part of the Recession Special, and I didn't regret a moment of it. It's the one place I demanded to go on multiple nights.

We came here for a late lunch early dinner on Saturday a little after 5:00PM. What really was a turn off when we walked to the hostess 2 of them standing around and asked for a table for 2 ... they looked at us like we came to their house. Then they said ohh are u having drinks or dinner we are not ready so you can sit at the bar. Just a little tip if you are in the restaurant business weather you are ready or not you should always be welcoming and accommodate your customers. The people that walk in your door don't want to hear anything, they want to be seated and served. Focus on providing them the experience they expect and deserve. 

However our server George was wonder and made the experience great. I had the salmon with asparagus and my husband had the pork chop with Brussel sprouts and everything was delicious. Id say the portions were on the smaller size. The manager came by to make sure everything was good.

Service and food were very good but the Don Kelly Band really made it a poor experience.  They constantly berated the patrons for not applauding enough and aggressively panhandled for tips.  A better performance would have made both unnecessary.

I've come here a few times. It's nice to see that each time I come here, it looks just as clean as the last time I saw it. The staff is always nice and helpful. 

It could use a few more food options, but there are plenty of options outside of the venue.

This is the only REAL honky tonk on Broadway. Robert's has great music, a fun atmosphere, and cheap food/drinks.

If you want to see what Broadway used to be like before it turned into a giant frat party of the exact same bars, serving $8.50 Bud Lights for an endless supply of bachelorette parties... 

Robert's is your answer.
If they have the same caliber entertainment every night awesome. $$$ Drinks tough to find a seat but I guess thats a good thing.

Walking down Broadway - came across this place after few stops. Ordered 5 drinks and paid in full. Ordered another round of Jell-O shots and hold-behold! Bartender was rude with a 'TUDE!!!! Looks like "Hunter" the bartender even "pocketed" the "amount pay" for our Jell-O shots, after we told him their Jell-O shot tasted like a year old. He was rude and beyond unprofessional!  To top it off, manager and just repeated the same thing he said... didn't even apologize for saying "sorry the Jell-O shots were awful.". Never again. Would never go back! And he claimed "oh good" ... that to us is BS for sure. If he only knew who I am ... visiting his little old bar.
Good place to visit if you are not a police officer.  They will not allow you in if you are armed off duty.

Sambuca is just never my first choice. 

After a horrid NYE experience years ago, I am slowly giving it a chance again. I've only stopped in for cocktails my past couple visits, and I'll admit they are a bit few and far between. The cocktail list is pretty decent and they have a variety of liquors to choose from. Most of the drinks looked quite sweet and I ended up having a plain mojito on my last visit. It was made well and I was pleased. Our bartender was friendly and the place wasn't very busy on a Tuesday night, however we couldn't sit in the upstairs patio due to a corporate event. There seem to be quite a few corporate events that happen here.

The jazz singer and band downstairs was VERY loud and not very good. They must bring out their C squad on non busy nights of the week. I love the atmosphere and the dim romantic lighting. The giant Buddha on the second floor is pretty bitchin as well. I honestly haven't eaten in here in so long that I can't go into detail about it, but I remember it being decent but nothing blew me away. 

Overall an upscale fancy place to stop in for a drink. Not too bad.
Lovely place. First time in Nashville and tried this place out. Great ambiance. Amazing service. Delicious  food!

I came here on a Saturday night over Labor Day weekend and it was a poppin' time! There was no cover when we went on a Saturday night which makes me think there's probably never a cover for this place which is really cool since they're a popular spot on Broadway.

The band and the music were great, the people inside were super friendly (via the act of receiving and giving shots). Isn't that what happens when you and your group of friends are having a good time and you talk to people who are also having a good time? Good vibes always make for a good time!

I saw the deal for the recession special which is such a good deal! For $6 you get a fried bologna sandwich, a bag a chips, and a PBR. If you're hungry that's a good way to soak up those adult beverages.

The RyMan was an amazing facility unfortunately the Larry Gatlin hosted Country Music Show was horrible LARRY IS WAY PADT HIS PRIME AND TRYS WAY hard on songs especially high notes ! Lee Ann Carter was great but that was about it ! The show was really bad some people left before it was over ! The gospel part was actually the worst ! I would never go to another one of theses shows . They will be artist specific like Dwight  Yoakum

My first time in Nashville and after going to all the fancy restaurants ie Kayne's Prime this was a surprise. We spent our 27th anniversary here and actually went with the recommendation from the hotel driver as opposed to the concierge recommendation from the Omni hotel.  Keith our server was awesome and recommended the best food the shrimp and crap dip is to die for has a little Cajun/ chili flavor the filet Oscar with grilled shrimp was not on the menu but was better than the filet I had at Kayne's the night before, my wife's salmon Oscar was perfectly cooked. The music was the best jazz even compared to the best from DC.  Hands down go here if in Nashville a great alternatives to the honky Tonks!

A fun, loud, great honkey tonk right on broadway next to countless "country music clubs." Amidst the massive amount of bachelorette magnet bars, this place stands out as a true country music destination. It can get rather crowded and still have the occasional bachelorette party crash the scene, but hey, this is Nashville, that's bound to happen. 

The drinks are inexpensive and ice cold, and the music is ALWAYS phenomenal. You should definitely make this a stop on your trip to Nashville, or make it your regular bar if you live downtown, the music never disappoints.

The food was good but unspectacular.  The calamari appetizer was the most disappointing part but everything else was tasty.   I expected more based on all the hype.   The staff was friendly and brought us a free desert for our anniversary, which was much appreciated.  We got the sopapillas which was probably my favorite food for the evening.    We were disappointed after making a reservation very far in advance to be seated nowhere near the live music and instead being in a very generic dining area watching the music on a TV.  The prices seemed high for what we got which is the main reason I would not recommend.  I think people would enjoy the food but frankly could get the same or better for less cost elsewhere.

I love seeing concerts at more intimate venues.  The Ryman has to be one of my all time favorites.  There is not a bad seat in the house.  I love sitting closer because you feel like the musician is singing just to you, but I have sat in the upper level in the last row too and enjoyed the concert just as much.  I find each time I go to The Ryman I am usually on the younger side of the other concert goers.  

My most recent concert was Jason Isbell & The 400 unit.  He is one of my top 5 or so favorite singer / songwriter. I was excited to see that his extremely talented wife, Amanda Shires was also performing that night with his band.  They are a force together on stage.  They at times had me mesmerized.  

If you happen to go to The Ryman, not for a concert / show, but just to see the history of The Grand Ole Opry and country music you will have plenty to see.  They even give tours and allow you to stand on the stage and even have a photo op like you are the one performing on stage with the iconic microphone stand.

I just love visiting this historic space, being there and thinking of all the legends that have been there before me.
Great place to have a beverage and listen to great music.  The food is fun and reasonable.  Had fun and great place all around

Best Honky Tonk on Broadway. Unlike some of the other bars, this one is less crowded and chill. We enjoyed the live music and the bucket of beer deal - probably one of the best deals on Broadway (five beers for $25). I also loved looking as all the random country artist memorabilia - old records, guitars, juke boxes, etc. next time I come to Nashville this will be my go to spot.

great music, i was impressed with the audio set up, i know i shouldn't be cause its nashville and everything, but really, sitting in the back and being able to hear the band perfectly, impressive.

 they have a good basic menu and the food on their is really good, the prices were all over the place, somethings were cheap, and somethings were prohibitively expensive: example $4.5 for 8 HUGE mozzarella sticks (delicious), but $5.5 for a 'premium beer' ( Shiner Bock ). basic french fries were 4.50... so just kinda odd.

 also this doesn't really bother me so much but worth pointing out, even tho the bar was not busy the service was poor, sub par. i didn't count off for that, just really the pricing is what impacted the score.

Where do I begin with the Ryman? From Bright Eyes to Broods to John Legend to Hurray for the Riff Raff to Broken Social Scene and to the most recent show, Local Natives... I've seen countless bands at the Ryman over the years. 

This has to be one of the top music venues this side of the Mississippi. I might go as far as labeling it in the top 10 in the country. I love the Ryman! My only complaint is that it's not in Louisville! When you look at the ticket giants selling you tickets for certain venues in cities like Livenation... if those companies ever wanted to franchise a venue, they should model it off of the Ryman. There are a few things I'd modify but overall I can't complain too much as every show I've been to has been an amazing experience.

The history is cool. Being almost 192 years old is nuts! It was originally built to be a church but that didn't last long. It quickly became a community and event space. Once it became the Grand Ole Opry, I think the rest is history. The Opry eventually moved in the 1970s, but the amount of talent that has been on that stage... breathtaking. As far as I'm concerned... let's convert all churches to music venues.

The upstairs and downstairs lobbies are awesome. They have multiple bars and it's spaced out in such a way that it's never a hassle when seeing a show. Plenty of toilets to make a quick restroom run in between acts and the place has been clean every time I've attended. One peeve that usually comes up anytime I go to a show are the drink prices. While the beer on tap here isn't in the early teen prices.. it is still in the $8-10 range. With that being said, you're in downtown Nashville so make sure to drink cheaply somewhere else before arriving.

The seats are pews which can be uncomfortable, but like most venues... people normally stand up once the music starts. The floor is also wood. Every time the crowd goes nuts, it's dreamlike to hear everyone stomping their feet and clapping their hands on the pews at the same time. It never fails to place me in a trance every time.

The only thing I'd suggest is if you're further back on the floor and your seat is to the right or left of the stage, you might want to reconsider your ticket purchase. There are beams that can get in your way in certain spots. You can still see, but it can be annoying. Most people say there isn't a bad seat in the house. Well... that applies here(except for those few seats that are right behind the beams). 

You can also tour this place and if I'm ever in Nashville during the day, I'll certainly give this place a tour. 

If your favorite musician tours here, make the trip. You'll be glad you did.

Second Fiddle is a must stop for Sunday Bloody Mary's.   Bartender Jessica went above and beyond again.   

Band (Buck McCoy) was great and very interactive with the audience.

Second Fiddle still has feel of authentic Honky Tonk you don't get with the new bars. Always a great place to relax.

Fantastic Food! Elegant atmosphere! We expected the menu to be overpriced, but the $25-$35/plate was priced well with a great house band that allowed you to socialize and enjoy the music at the same time.

This is a must do when in Nashville, great history, architecture, acoustics, and character. We were lucky enough to be there for the Gatlin Brothers and Crystal Gale, along with several other great singers...it was fun to be a part of a live show and so much history.

A friend was physically assaulted here by the bouncers trying to defend an African American friend of ours that was being racial profiled and asked to leave the bar. He truly didn't do anything wrong and was being told to leave without being given a real reason. Although, after over hearing them making inflammatory racial statements we have a pretty good idea as to why. Let's do better Nashville. Just cause we are in the south doesn't mean we have to act like we're still fighting the civil war.
Awesome band and music. Stopped by on a Sunday night and place was packed. I enjoyed the experience. Only complain is shots were too light. Not enough etoH. Didn't pack much of a punch.

Unexpected date night as we just jumped in the car and headed downtown! I made some calls and was able to secure a table upstairs for dinner! 

We were the first upstairs in the dining room, but it quickly filled up. Our waitress, Brandy was great! She was very knowledgeable and helped up make some decisions. We ordered drinks and the shrimp ceviche for appetizer. My husband made the comment about them not having a "great" beer selection, but we were told they were working on getting beers on tap to be able to offer local brews. I had an extra dirty martini and it was very good! I ordered the chili scallops and my husband ordered the red snapper dish. It was very good! Service was very good as well! 

We were very glad we were seated upstairs! The band was very loud downstairs. We will always request upstairs when we go back!

Old-fashioned honky tonk bar.  We tried to go early Saturday night but it was way too crowded.   We stopped in Sunday after brunch and it was not crowded.  We saw local legend, John Shepard.  Nice, corny, old-fashioned country show.  Beers are reasonably-priced, they even have some local microbrews.

I was at a conference here for a couple days. It was a typical, but really nice convention Center. I didn't have much time to look around the area, though. A project fir next time. I thought the best part, was $12 parking for all day and $7 for half a day - but free with validation. The lunch food was better than the usual rubber chicken. I stayed a few miles away and found the traffic very manageable.

I travel to Nashville on a regular basis. I have had the opportunity to spend many nights on music row and have had a lot of fun. My favorite place to go is Legends Corner. Good atmosphere, cold beer, laid back compared to most places on the strip and more traditional country music. Give it a try, if you don't like all of the crowds at Tootsies etc. you will like this place.

Our concierge recommended this place. The food was absolutely amazing. The bread pudding was the best I've ever had. Service was spot on and the entertainment was great. You will not be disappointed with this place.

You can't do Nashville right without going to Robert's. I'd give up all the rest for this honky tonk! I really like that they play old/classic country (the good stuff like Johnny Cash). They have a small dance floor by the band and encourage guests to dance! The bartenders are nice, and while it's often busy, it's never body to body like some obnoxious places (cough cough... Tootsies). I love that it's historic and classic Nashville, but not obnoxious and overly packed. Go to Roberts for a great time, you won't be sorry!

The hostess was so rude and utterly incompetent.  When we got there she insisted that we sit at a couch for a dinner reservation and refused to move us to one of the many empty tables in the restaurant. Tyler, the bar manager, was nearby and very quickly resolved the issue and kindly moved us to an ACTUAL table and provided us with the utmost customer service and was so personable and friendly. The food was absolutely delicious, and our group was thrilled in the end with the restaurant overall. Thank you Tyler!!!

Great food, great service, great music. I read a wonderful review so I had to try it myself! I had a burger with fries and it was delightful. I thoroughly enjoyed all aspects of the atmosphere provided. I will warn you, there is no cover charge to enter so tipping the band is a MUST. I would definitely visit again. Rock on, Nashville, TN

Unprofessional staff. Made inappropriate racist comments against people in our party. Kicked them out for being black and couldn't provide justification for forcing them out of the bar. Take your business elsewhere.
Place was just dark, dirty and not real inviting. Only thing noteworthy was the graffiti on the walls which were more interesting to read than the band or crowd.

My church. What can you say about one of the finest music halls in the world? All the seats are great - even the back row of the balcony. Wish i could move to Nashville and buy a season pass to the Ryman. That would be heaven.

This is the real Honky Tonk grill!! We felt right at home here. This joint reminded me of the joints you stumble across in our hometown in Pennsylvania. It's a laid back ambiance with good eats, friendly staff, cold drinks & ear catching entertainment. We snagged a table right up front near the cowboy boot lined wall. I loved this!! The entertainment was what you come to Nashville to enjoy, down home old school country. 

Our cheeseburgers were on point. The best we've had in a long time!!

Great live music! Ambiance is a little dark on the inside. Staff was attentive, with great personalities. I give the review three stars cause the brunch menu was extremely limited. They only had about 8 items if I am remembering correctly. I got the chicken and waffles and they were good. Huge amount of chicken so you could split with someone if you got an extra waffle. Extra syrup was key.

Nashville is Music City. The sound quality at the Ryman could & should be excellent, and it is not, in my opinion. At the recent "I'm With Her" concert, each band did their last number acoustic with no mics & the sound was clear. The amplified vocals had been muddy, hard to get the words. 
Are the sound techs unfamiliar with this very good acoustic hall? Do they just turn it up too loud? Is it the microphones? I really would appreciate having an excellent sonic experience in this fine historic auditorium.
The general ambiance is pleasant. The church pews are hard. You can sit on your jacket or bring a small cushion. If you are tall, you might reserve an aisle seat to give your legs room.

What a fun place! I was told that sometimes celebrities pop in and perform. While we didn't experience that, it was still cool. The band that performed played great music. They went back to Johnny Cash and some great classics. Truly a wonderful experience!

Spent 5 days in Nashville enjoying ourselves.  Everyone was extremely friendly. I will recommend Nashville to all my friends and family.  I have but one complaint.  Until I reached this store our trip Was flawless, but the sales help in this store could kiss my ass in Nashville.  Fire the little bitch that was rude when we were spending our hard earned money.  Unfriendly and rude.  Didn't want to help get a shirt off the top rack.  I said I'm sorry to bother you and that little brat seemed annoyed and bothered.  Remember who pays your salary you brat.

Loved this place. It's hallowed ground. This is the Grand Ole Opry downtown. Took a self-guided tour. Signs about its history, performers, costumes, instruments are everywhere inside, and it's easy to get around. The country musical history here is phenomenal. This is where professional country music and bluegrass began, and stars were made. The Ryman was saved by the performers and fans as money was raised to restore the old building that was crumbling. We learned about the 3 p.m. performance and purchased tickets. We sat in the original wooden pews.  Boy, listening to Announcer Eddie Stubbs, hearing the humor and the songs of Larry Gatlin and his brothers, listening and singing along to award-winning songwriter Don Schlitz, and watching the dreams come true of some young performers, THEN being entertained by 85-year-old Charley Pride who is still jiving was one of the best days ever. We couldn't help but smile. This venue is a must-see.

A great concert venue. This is the home of the Grand Ole Opry. Much smaller and more intimate than the new Opry the venue is a grand old church. The place rocks with a massive sound system. 

Ticket prices vary with performers.  I don't think there is a bad seat in the house. 

Guided backstage tours.

The bartender was AMAZING! She had a great personality, was attentive, and definitely was someone every employer would pray for. Her manager; however, was not. My father ordered a drink "neat" -- you know, a drink without ice. Somehow that warranted a 40% upcharge on the "regular" drink. But wait.. if it's between "neat" or "on the rocks" is there a price difference? No. Apparently, in this tourist-focused town you're expected to know that you will be charged an additional $2/drink NOT to have ice (or to have ice). I live in Los Angeles, I've traveled around Europe & Asia, and I'm born and raised in Cleveland, Ohio. No matter how cheap or expensive a cocktail is, I've NEVER been charged EXTRA for requesting a drink without ice! Hilarious.

In all honesty, what was more upsetting was the condescending tone the manager took with me when disputing a $4 upcharge!! $4! That's how much their MANAGERS do not value their CUSTOMERS. I will never return to this establishment, nor will I be paying the amount charged on my credit card--you better bet I'm disputing that $4, nor will I ever recommend this business again. Congrats! You "made" $4 on 1/8 "extra" alcohol without ice with ZERO customer loyalty and ZERO return business!!! This company needs to hire managers that understand customer service.
This is the ultimate dive bar.   They have great entertainment and pretty reasonable drink prices.  Nice happy hour.

We went to Opry at the Ryman.  What can be said about such a historical place that hasn't already been said? It struck me like there wasn't a bad seat in the house. The acoustics are great, the gift shop well stocked. 

The only criticism I have is the entrance process is chaotic. Essentially, the crowd gathers in one big mass in front of the doors until they open. It's not really safe.
Nice small intimate bar if you get there early. I found this to be similar to the other smaller bars; good band, good drinks, lots of memorabilia.

Hate to write a bad review but - drinks were extremely watered down, talked to people around us, everyone agreed. Wings were alright, def not worth the price. And ceaser salad was something you would get at fast food chain. Food took roughly 45 minutes. Service wasn't very good either. All around go somewhere else. Waste of the money
Great historic gem. At first I was hesitant about going thru because of the price ( my bride says I am cheap),but after seeing the theater I was amazed. This place is a must see in Nashville.

Whoever you have controlling the "aisle-way" was a dick. He was walking through a packed house bitching at everybody and even told my friend and I to "suck it in" as if we were fat. Get me out of here I'm not about to be treated that way with so many other live music venues to be at. Straight up rude.

So, I had no idea that this Tin Roof was sister bar to Tin Roof Cantina in Atlanta. I totally walked in there with that in mind. They had live music like every other bar on Broadway and it had a real comfortable dive bar feel. I love stickers and signs everywhere. Definitely one bar to make sure you pop in for a round just to check it out. I went June 2nd, the Sunday/Monday leading up to CMA Fest.

Located right in the middle of Downtown Nashville with so many places to choose from.  What drew me here was the live music that was being played.  It was modern music with an attractive looking band.  The bar itself was nice and had plenty of seating.  I ordered a drink at the bar and I love that the bartenders were really nice.  I sat down at a booth and when a table closer to the band opened up I moved up.  

The vibe of this place was so fun.

I have to admit I wasn't too excited at first about touring the Ryman Auditorium but I do like visiting and hearing the history of historical buildings.  This tour didn't disappoint.  We had tickets included with our City Pass that we upgraded to get the guided tour.  Our tour guide was very knowledgeable and shared a lot of stories about the building and the artists that have played there.  Lucinda Williams was performing the night we visited so we were only able to see a couple of dressing rooms backstage, but we did get to go on stage and take our souvenir photo.  I also enjoyed the Sounds of Nashville movie that they have you watch before your tour, it was very creative and informative.  The Ryman is definitely worth a visit.

This place is THE BEST!! I never been somewhere so unique, different, but quality in every way.

Food: it's a good court styled place, so you have 4 or 5 different restaurant options. El Gaucho Argentinian food is my favorite, but all are delicious. I think my favorite thing about El Gaucho is the sauces. The chimichuri is killer and just makes everything you put it on 'pop.' Bright and fresh, it's delicious! The nacho potatoes they have there are very different but in a good way. I think of them like potato braves (from a Spanish tapas spot) on steroids. The potatoes are perfectly cooked but have the sear and crunch on the outside that seals the deal.

Entertainment: wow oh wow. This place has it all. Salsa lessons. Fire dancers. Aerial dancing. Singers and bands. Truly a sight for sore eyes, no matter when you go. 

People: the kindest. Everyone is friendly and wants you to have fun and experience something new.

I beg of you all, please check this spot out. You will not be disappointed.

Things I love about this place:
1. SALSA THURSDAYS! Come early on Thursday evening for a free salsa dance lesson and stay to continue dancing all night long!
2. This place is a huge mall full of everything that you could possibly need: food, shopping, groceries, performances, etc. 
3. THE POPSICLES. The popsicle shop is cheap af and they serve delicious popsicles of all kinds of flavors.
4. You can just grab a drink and walk around the mall! 
5. THE CULTURE! Everything here has Mexican culture in it (clearly, by the name), and everyone is incredibly friendly. I had a really great time at this place.

Things I was meh about:
1. The prices of food (not the popsicles). I ordered some pork belly and oysters. The portions were small (but delicious) and our bill came to like $40. It seems a bit over-priced for the area.
2. It seems as if there is still some construction going on in the building, as they continue to fill it with new stores. So you may notice some unfinished work on the opposite side of the building as you walk around.

Overall, I had a great time, and I definitely plan on going back here for some late-night dancing! Excellent space!

I felt like the menu was limited for gluten free.  They were accommodating to alter some of the items. The atmosphere was great with the live band. I will say the band was a bit loud to where we couldn't have a conversation with my family.

It's been a few years since I came here and recalled it being very nice. Even tonight,  the band is awesome. We were promptly seated. The restaurant was less than half full. However, the promptness in which a server came to take our order was not good. Our party waited 30 minutes for our drink order to ne taken. Jeez...

1889 Captn Tom Ryman and
Sam Jones corraborated to create 
the (Union Gospel) Tabernacle.  Great care was put into the acoustics of this building.  Upon the death of its creator the building was renamed 
Ryman Auditorium in 1904.

Ryman was the original home of the radio program known as the Grand Ole Opry (until 1974).  It was also the home of the Johnny Cash Show (1960-1971) and home to multiple performances by an all star list including Ray Charles, Stevie Wonder, Charlie Pride.

In spite of hosting many African American speakers at the Ryman and many performances by notable African Americans since the 1930s including Louis Armstrong (1958)...
The audience remained segregated until the 1960s.  Only after two boycotts from the African American community did the end of segregation at Ryman begin. 

The Grand ole Opry moved its home to where it is now in Music City, Nashville.  The Ryman closed its doors and was almost demolished until many performers and the city in collaboration with private investors began restoration and renovation in 1989.  The Ryman reopened in 1994 and has even hosted the Grand ole Opry back on special occasions. 

The Ryman is still renowned for it's beautiful sound.  This beauty has bean voted  the 2nd best venue in the whole country for its acoustics.  It's been an honor to meet you Ryman!

The food - they are not kidding when they say their steak and seafood is really good here. Arielle is the best waitress ever. If you have a chance to request her - do it. She's wonderful. The filet is so awesome - I added shrimp to mine and the Brussels sprouts and the Mac n cheese. The appetizers we had were also amazing. We had the shrimp and crab dip and artichoke with goat cheese and beignets. Everything was incredible but Arielle made the experience all the better.

Second visit to Sambuca. First time was amazing. Second time was no different. Bartender made great drinks while we waited on our table. Waitstaff (Jessie and George) went above and beyond with everything. The band (The Dantones) was entertaining. The food was stellar. We had the crab dip, to start. The scallops, steak, and lobster tail for main course. 

Absolutely no complaints. Highly recommend Sambuca.

If I could give this bar a zero stars I would after the spinless way they fired the best band in town! How do you do that by a text with no explanation?? Adults don't conduct themselves
 like that! How unprofessional!! I can only say it was a huge mistake to get rid of money makers like Eileen Rose and the Silver Threads!!! Hope they can eat stupidity! I can see business going down hill!!

Was there for a couple for my birthday dinner on a Saturday night. The atmosphere was great. Had a live band while we was there & they were wonderful. Definitely a date night, laid back kind of place to go once in a while. I would recommend this place for anyone that just want to enjoy some good floor and live music.

Great vibe. Romantic. Sexy.
Decent food. Definitely not of the highest quality but good enough.
Excellent music. Phenomenal band.

Primary complaint: Very slow service. The waiter purposely asked everyone in my large work party of 12 if they wanted soup or salad prior to their order (after we had already ordered several appetizers). It felt manipulative and as a strategy to stretch our wallet when we wouldn't ordinarily a soup or salad in addition to a bunch of appetizers and entrees.

I *think* I'd still come back. But what started off as an excellent night ended up being a very long 3+ hour very
 expensive dinner --$1300 w drinks. When we asked him for the bill, he told us that we "stressed him out." Get it together guy--not good to show your stress publicly.

Don't get me wrong--I pay top money for amazing food and service but although the entertainment was excellent the service missed the mark.
Food is great and the atmosphere is amazing. Great hospitality. I would recommend the street corn and the southern biscuits.

Very friendly staff, good music and a really good cheeseburger for 6:50. It's almost impossible to find a burger this an expensive in Downtown Nashville. Especially one that's good. It's a honky tonk so don't expect fancy furniture and China. But I strongly recommend Roberts.
This place is way cool and especially on a hot day. Old school flat top behind bar serving delicious fried bologna. Very nice only bottle beer selection.
Classic..loved the music and atmosphere. So Nashville. The band was awesome. We just got drinks there

Good music, decent food - very affordable. Long history 
Went on a Monday, so kind of quiet.  Decent cheeseburger- good beer selection 
I bet it's hopping on a weekend

Great music & always amazing bar service & food!!!  My husband & I visit every time we come to Nashville!
Karen gave us awesome service!!

A bunch of us had lunch here when visiting Nashville. It was really good food. It took a while for the food to come, but our waiter checked in on us and kept us updated. The wings were really good and most of us got tacos/quesadillas and all of it was good. Good music and TVs had football on so we could catch the game.

What a fun place to hang out during the SEC tournament ! We came during the KSR show and had so much fun. The bar was pretty well inundated with UK fans but the staff kept things moving . The Bloody Mary's were spicy and delicious . We smacked at the bar during the show and had the hot chicken tenders which was very good .
Good old country music. Enjoyed every second of it. Nice crowd!!! A must while in Nashville.
True Country and nice staff! Saw Brazil Billy the other night and the fiddle player was amazing! Back in here again as I loved it so much!

Did a little bar hopping in Nashville while in town for a brief visit last week. Second Fiddle was our second stop downtown. This was our first visit in this bar on lower Broadway. I'm sure it won't be our last. The band in the window drew us in, and right away we found seats at the bar. We ordered beers and settled in for a set with the excellent band playing classic country, originals, and contemporary commercial country music. Hub had Sams (Adams) while I stayed local with Hap & Harry's Tennessee Lager. We stayed for about an hour taking in the atmosphere, imbibing and digging this expert band. A visit to Second Fiddle is a fantastic way to enjoy Music City!

We came for lunch on our first stop in Nashville thanks to the Yelpers for the suggestion. The menu is small - burger, sandwich, corn dog, fries and such. Perfect for lunch!  The food was good. The prices were unbelievably low. The service was great - friendly, attentive, and smiling. Plus there was live music - talented musicians!!  Personally I think every restaurant should have live music this good. What a great start to our Nashville getaway weekend!

Roberts Western World is a dimly-lit, no-frills, real-deal Honky Tonk. It's the perfect place to pull up to the bar and let the fantastic (and loud) live music carry your cares away. This is my favorite Nashville bar.
OMG! Have the fried bologna sandwich! So good. This is a relic, one of the few left in  Nashville! Good food and good drink!
We dined here for lunch and the service and food was great!  The live bands were excellent.  The bathrooms were clean and tidy.  Really nice experience.  Would definitely eat here again!!
The garden burger and sweet potato fries were delicious! Enjoyed the band and the prices were reasonable! Will definitely return when we visit Nashville again!
Ryman has a  very interesting history. But, not much to see. The price is ridiculous! I would say if you don't mind paying way too much to be on the Ryman stage, go for it.
Bartender HUNTER was rude and unprofessional. He was sarcastic and gave smart a** answers when approached with feedback regarding orders.

Sambuca has a great menu selection! We visited for a a birthday dinner. The food was fabulous. The service was not amazing. We had to wait 30 minutes to get our checks. Also the music was very nice but almost too loud to be able to have a conversation. I will be returning however, the food was really that good!

So much fun! If you're lucky enough to catch beyond wings circus you are in for an absolute treat. There always seems to be something entertaining going on. It's very family friendly, but wouldn't be bad for a date night either!
The food there is so delish. There are a lot of options, but I'm a big fan of tres gauchos. It would be difficult to make a bad food choice there!

This is a hidden gem!  We were in Nashville with a large group & we bought the 7 attraction city sightseeing pass......had no idea what this place was; but it was on the list & close by so we thought we'd check it out. It is a beautiful auditorium that has so much history & they still have music acts that perform here in the present day.

It starts out with a cute multi-screen film detailing the building's history with lots of great video clips & photos of famous  performers.  There are lots of displays with photos & memorabilia from former performers.  There is also a booth where you can record a recording keepsake.  

The auditorium is beautiful with church pew style seating.  You also have opportunities for photos with instruments right up on the stage.  Cool place!

Your rating will largely depend on what you see. If it's a performer you like, you'll likely overlook the uncomfortable seats, but if you see a variety show that is more schmaltz than substance, you'll likely be disappointed.

This was a very cool bar recommended to me by a barista at Marchant's. Naturally I came on by once I finished my dinner and drink there. This place had a live country band which was very talented and I'm a fan

Came here again to celebrate our one year anniversary together. A year ago today, we came here for our dinner reception after we got married and I couldn't have been any more excited and happy to come celebrate again! The food was amazing. The music was on point. It was such a emotional and romantic experience with my husband. Our server was the best ! He made sure to make our night extra special. This place will forever be a special place for us.
Great line up, great atmosphere, best place in downtown Nashville if you're looking for good music. Don't expect sophisticated cocktails. Fried pickles and Voodoo chicken fingers are very good.

If you want to see a place rich in history that by grace of some wonderful people was kept alive so all could enjoy then don't miss the Ryman. We did the self guided tour and took away a deep appreciation for all who brought this gathering place together and revived it after many years of neglect.

Nice outdoor seating in the thick of it. Over-priced menu for the average quality of the food. We did enjoy the seared tuna appetizer, but were so disappointed that the ice machine was broken and they could not make some of those tasty-sounding drinks on the menu. I had a very overly sweet passion fruit Mojito. The mint was not at all muddled- which drives me crazy. Yo, bartenders: MINT MUST BE MUDDLED IN MOJITOS!! Over-priced drinks, too. The Havarti tater tots did not taste as if they had any cheese in them, nor could I detect any garlic, as promised. Too bad, they have live music and a good ambiance....but the food does not deliver.

The cost of the food vs the portion size was unfortunate! Although what little we got tasted good I would have much rather went somewhere else where I could pay less and receive more. I ended up paying for another meal to supplement. 

The restaurant itself was nice and has a very relaxed atmosphere.  The live band was nice but it was a bit more laid back than we wanted to be.

Went here to see Shinedown. 
Great place with a lot of nostalgia 
Sound system was very good. Could here them singing even without the microphone 
Pews were a little cramped. But once you stand up you can spread out some.

Due to a last minute trip for valentines weekend, we didn't have a dinner reservation. We went to the tin roof for a couple of drinks and some bar food. The service was great (and fast)! The food was okay. You have great music to listen to while you're here too!

Was physically assaulted by racist door staff here after defending my African-American friend who was asked to leave without any explanation.  The staff kept saying, "get rid of the black guy with dreadlocks".  I was dumbfounded.  I'm 5' 8" / 140lbs, pose zero physical threat to anyone and have never been removed from a bar or public place in my life.  I have bruises and cuts on my body from being thrown to the sidewalk outside for absolutely no reason.  I had had 1 Amstel light.  The bar tending staff was nice at least.

This place had great reviews and then a few horrible ones and that worried me a little. Had a 7pm reservation on a Thursday. Got there at 6:45 and were immediately seated. Service from that point on was excellent. I had a couple jack/cokes and my wife did 2 fruity girly drinks which were both good but upon getting the bill they were definitely expensive ($14-$15 each). The food was amazing. We got the shrimp/crab bisque and it was the best we've ever had. We also split the scallops and sea bass. Wow. Once again the best we've ever had. Service 5 stars. Food 5 stars. Band 5 stars. Only negatives would be the price of the drinks and it was a little dark inside. My old eyes don't do well in the dark and a little extra light would have been great.

On Friday November 8th my group & I sat down at a table and enjoyed a couple drinks while listening to very talented singers. It was perfect. The food was delicious, I especially loved the cornbread. It was a perfect location downtown. A place I would highly suggest.

As someone who enjoys fine dining, I searched for a restaurant that would fall in this category, coupled with live music, during my short trip to Nashville. 

From the moment we set foot inside the restaurant until we left, the entire experience was remarkable. The hostess that seated us was pleasant and our server (I wish I remember his name) was fantastic. It was a Sunday night and the band that performed was The Steve Roper Band. Excellent performers!!!

Everything we ordered tasted great. The portions were just right. Leave room for dessert!

The food here is actually atrocious. The charcuterie board was embarrassingly overpriced and the cured meats were disgusting. The carrots were inedible and extremely burnt. Their cheese sticks were fast food level. It seems as if it's only redeemable quality is there is always live music. DO NOT come here for dinner or appetizers. You will be disappointed.

On Friday November 8th during the evening my group & I stopped by second fiddle to have a couple drinks and listen to the talent. The band was very talented and also knew how to entertain a crowd and was excellent at involving the crowd. I even purchased a beer koozie which saldly I had forgotten to take home with me that night. The next day I stopped by the bar, explain my mishap and they gave me my koozie which I was relieved to have again. They are adorable beer koozies. The only downfall to second fiddle is that they did not serve food. We ended up having to leave this establishment in search of food. Just a suggestion for the future. Overall great time, great atmosphere, and great music.
Great food and atmosphere a must visit in Nashville.  Music is awesome, your girl deserves to be treated to this!

This "mother church of country music" is a sensational place to see a show. I attended an Opry at the Ryman concert, which was great fun and very much enhanced by the venue. It does feel somewhat like a church, with the stained glass in the back of the auditorium and the exquisitely uncomfortable pews for the seating. It positively oozes with history and the acoustics are incredible. Also, for a building seating over 2300, it feels quite intimate. There's a modern lobby with new and clean restrooms and a bar. A gift shop is attached. (Tip: If you enter the gift shop at intermission, you will need your ticket to get back into the show.) Price depends on where you sit, but the view is fine even towards the sides where the tickets are less expensive. (It appears they don't sell the most extreme sides for most events, where the view would be obstructed.)

Seeing a performance here is a must-do Nashville activity.

We were not sure if we were going to enjoy our visit here but it was a pleasant surprise. This is the original grand old Opry location. It includes a video of the history of Ryman Auditorium and they have a display of items that our favorite country western singers wore. You too will be pleasantly surprised

Called Sambuca days prior to see what they do in terms of a 'birthdays.' I was told that the band can do a 'shout out.'

Reservations were made for the wife's birthday and to just simply 'acknowledge' her birthday, no expectations.

Our waitress and the band, Patton James & the Synchromatics went above and beyond.  The band not only did a 'shout out,' but did a customized version of 'Happy Birthday' for the misses. 

Our waitress, Cody, was attentive, pleasant, and when we ordered dessert; she came back with a lit candle in the desert with 'Happy Birthday' in chocolate icing along the plate.
 Something they didn't have to do.

Also, a lot of the reviews state the food is overpriced?! Compared to what? Applebees or Ocharleys? I guess you would call it overpriced if those restaurants are your frame of reference. The free live music/show is easily worth the price of the food.

My only gripe, is that all the patrons around me, were so self-absorbed in their conversation is that they couldn't appreciate good music or the saxophonist killin' it.
Bar was ok but food was low quality, might come back to listen to music but never to eat

The Mother Church of Country is a musical institution in Nashville that is unrivaled in beauty & soul.  Originally built for the Union Gospel Tabernacle, the Ryman eventually became well known for the live Grand Ole Opry shows and radio broadcasts.  Even if you are not a fan of country music, you will be hard pressed not to be inspired by the historic significance of the Ryman. So many talented musicians have been proud to step foot into the circle - My first show at the Ryman was Sturgill Simpson and I will never forget how excited I was to finally be living in Tennessee.  Some of my favorite bands have played there and it is always an amazing experience.  My favorite shows have been - The Wild Feathers, Jamestown Revival, The Head & the Heart, Jason Isbell, Margo Price, Tyler Childers, Lucas Nelson, and Lucinda Williams. I'm so excited to see Josh Ritter tonight and Ray LaMontagne in October!  Honestly the only show I was disappointed by was the Vince Gill Christmas Show.  Otherwise I highly recommend seeing your favorite band or trying someone new! I would like it if ushers (and some concert goers) would not talk so loud during performances.  Sometimes the sound can vary in quality but usually is very good. I saw the I'm with Her acoustic show and would like to see more of that style...The valet parking is hit or miss- I wish you could reserve a spot in advance because if it is full then it can take 10-30 minutes more to find a parking spot (there is a garage right next door but sometimes with traffic it can be a long wait to exit). I would just recommend being careful when purchasing tickets because some seats have restricted views or are tighter on actual seat space.  And of course sitting above is a much different experience than sitting below (you just have to try both to figure out what you prefer) Tickets can sell out quickly so I recommend getting the email or FB alerts to see when new shows are added.  I wish they would allow refillable water bottles - they do not recycle or compost! And all entrances should be made smoke free!

I was able to get the last seat available to see an acoustic Shinedown show and was blown away by the character of this place.  As the old venue for the Grand Ole Opry, the auditorium has a special meaning for the performing artists and because it is small, there is a special connection with the audience.  It appears as a small modern building in the front, but upon entering, you realize you are in a for a unique experience inside a piece of history.  The acoustics are perfection and allow for musicians to perform potentially with no plugs.
Ashley is a fantastic hostess with friendly hospitality and kindness. A great restaurant with great customer service. Thank you!
History rich and quite an experience. Hard to describe the reverence in the air. Enjoyed our time here!

What a beautiful space! 
We took the backstage tour of the Ryman and found it interesting. I think the backstage mostly just brings you in each dressing room (and they show videos in some), but other wise you see the same as a self guided tour. 

Don't forget to exit through the gift shop ;)
Perfect location and really good food. You're in the best spot for bar hopping in Nashville (without being on the overly populated touristy spots). Music is great too.
We came here for drinks and music and were not disappointed. Beer was cheap, music was great, and it was packed enough to be fun, but not overwhelmingly so.

I won't be dining here again. Rachel was our server and the service was almost non existent.  The restaurant was not very busy but the other waiters had to cover for her. The food and wine is mediocre at best.

I can't believe it took me this long to finally see a show at the Ryman. We went to see Jenny Lewis in February, more for the experience of the auditorium than for the choice of musical act (though she's great, too). Now, I'm super excited to come back for another concert soon.

You already know it's an old church with wooden pews. The acoustics, as advertised, were phenomenal. The history just seeps through the walls, and I was impressed how the crowd really respected the atmosphere and the music throughout the night.

If there are any drawbacks, it's probably the lack of more restrooms. But the Ryman can elevate a good performance into something almost mystical. There's no better place to see a show.
This was by far our favorite spot on Broadway!  It's worth braving the crowd even if you're not a broadway lover.
If visiting Nashville, this is a must see venue! The beginning of the tour alone is AMAZING!
Great place for dinner and very enjoyable live band in the Gulch.  Also cheap parking nearby

This is Nashville. Mother church of country music. I wish I saw a performance here but I was only able to do the tour and that alone was amazing. 
You can feel the history. The old wooden pews, the amazing acoustics its chilling. I really enjoyed the video at the beginning of the tour, I had no idea there was so much behind this place! I history on how it came about was amazing, really tells you the true significance of the Ryman. 
So many picture opportunities but I really had to take my photo "in the circle". It's tradition right? 
To think the Ryman was almost demolished! Thankfully it's history inspired the community and a number of investors to keep it going & have it restored.

Here from out of state for concert. It's 8pm and we can hear that they've started on time... but because of HORRIBLE organization well over half of the seat ticket holders are all still standing outside! We were lined up, rearranged, then rearranged again in a courtyard beside the venue. General admission tickets were let in first, understand that! But we won't be inside for another 30-40 mins... and the concert started 5 mins ago!
$320 in tickets, travel and hotel just to see this show... and we are still outside furious!!
Won't come to another show at this venue

I have one thing to say and it is awesome. The band flying  buffaloes is out if control and really the best band I have ever seen in years in the bands  in Nashville bars   The base player drummer and lead guitarist are fricken awesome
Beer was cold. Only thing they got going for them. Food was no good and got kicked out of upstairs for private party so we had to rush eating never going back.

Although i loved the theater itself my trip was based around a concert here.   When we'd arrived we'd noticed the Ryman was hotter then outside and more humid inside!! 
It was a very uncomfortable experience and i had to leave my seats several times to go put east on my face.  The 2 couples in front of us left 3 songs in as they couldn't do it anymore!!
Not cool.... literally and i was o so excited for the showi don't even remember it...i only remember the heat

Such a fun bar to come to for live music and drinks! They have their specialty cocktails, but I opted for a beer. We also ordered chips & queso for a midday pick-me-up. The staff channels their southern hospitality by being very friendly & attentive. Definitely will be coming back here.
One of our favorite Nashville restaurants--every dish is terrific, service is friendly and wonderful, live music is always fun! Will return, highly recommend.

You have to check this one out when you are on Broadway. This is the best bar that Nashville has!  This is a place that has seen a lot of stars. The walls are lined with pictures and memorabilia. There are photos above the stage of many famous classic country music artist. You will not hear anything but traditional country at this bar. Any of that new stuff on the radio is definitely not welcome at Robert's!

This is classy, low vibe restaurant in contrast to the other places in Nashville, especially on Broadway. High end menu for both eating and drinking and also along with the prices.  With a small band, they entertain guests with easy listening music. People dress up for this place too.

Great place on busy Broadway. The waitress was super friendly, nice and attentive. The music - two older men that were in their 80s probably - did a great job entertaining the crowd. It was so much fun seeing how much they enjoyed singing and entertaining the crowd. There was a special New Years menu so not as much to choose from as normal. We had fried bologna and french fries. It just sounded so funky we had to try it and it was not bad at all. Good place to hang out for a while.
Great movie and great AC.   If grew up on Grand Oe Ovary, it is a must visit.  Very educational about its history.
This was a cool place in the plaza. We came at night and they were doing salsa dancing on a Thursday night. We ordered in the restaurant..

Great and very interesting tour! I probably enjoyed the history of the Ryman video the best before the self-guided tour. It was also cool to see all the memorabilia worn by the many celebs that played at the Ryman, both past and present!

We stumbled into the Tin Roof after hearing some of the music outside. They had great bands and there was actually room to walk around and breathe in contrast with tootsie's next door. Drinks are reasonably priced, would come again.

I went to Tin Roof with my friends. We were all 21, and the bouncer kicked us out because he said "we didn't look 21". We showed them our IDs and told them to scan them but they said they didn't care. I bought a drink from there and they took my drink away from me and kicked my friends and I out even though I paid for my drink and showed them my ID. This is the most disrespectful place I've ever been to. I will never go here again, and I recommend never going to this bar.

Was seated at a nice table on the patio. Waitress was very friendly and attentive.  Drinks took way too long to come out.  
Apps were the cheese balls and the fried cauliflower.  Both were average.  We were then told there was a 15 top and an 8 top that are blocking up the kitchen.  Food wouldn't be out for a while.  30 min later we got our food.  The greek bowl was awful.  Raw cauliflower, chick peas and artichokes straight out of the can.  Didnt even take the time to add salt.  Side of carrots was literally 8 carrot chips.
Offered us a free dessert we chose the toffee pudding.  10 min later she comes out and says they are all out.
Check please.

Mike Hayes band and the best food we have had this entire trip has made this the best #1 in a long year of travels! Outstanding performance-An exceptional talent and a great night all around - THANK YOU.
Very interesting to be in the spot where the core of Music City originated. Beautiful place where so many legends performed.

Parking tonight at the MCC was awful. Normally after a Preds game police direct traffic to empty the parking structure.  Tonight, the police officer was not letting anyone out of a jam packed structure. He was on Demonbreun not helping at all.  Not sure if there is some fight between traffic control and MCC, but it was terrible. Eventually we were allowed to leave via a different exit after idling in place for 45 minutes. Terrible effort. Terrible logistics. Avoid at all costs.  Cannot understand how the Preds' sell parking there.  Everyone should be embarrassed at an extremely poor effort and execution.  Refunds should be honored.

Wow. Few places in America have as much impact, as this little auditorium does.  The birthplace of the Grand Ole Opry, this place has a lot of significance to the history of Country music. I didn't make it out for a show (I have been here 2x and haven't had the luck to take in a show) but I did take the self guided tour and it was definitely a place that feels/smells like it has seen a thing or two.
Love the old stained glass, the intro movie was informative and I really  love the old Hatch posters of all the bands who has performed here. Anyone who is anyone has performed here. What a great venue. I love old performance venues and I'm glad I made it out and took the tour. It is a magnificent building and really a cornerstone to making Nashville into the Music City it is known for today.
A must see for anyone looking to explore the history of this glorious City and the artists that inhabit it.

We chose to come here based on their website, which was pretty misleading. The decor is outdated and not in a cool "vintage" way. It is just old. We arrived early for our reservation, so we decided to order drinks at the bar. Service was slow, and the drinks were the absolute worst cocktails we have had anywhere. Stay away from the Sambuca 75 cocktail. It tastes like strawberry dishwater. Happy Hour prices are good, but that did not make up for the awful drinks. When we went to the hostess stand to check in for our table, management was moving around a bunch of furniture. They never said "excuse me" and my wife kept having to move to get out of their way. Might be a good idea to take care of these things earlier in the afternoon and not to make your customers feel like an inconvenience. The hostesses were disorganized, as well. However, once we were seated at our table, we were well pleased with our server. Matt was super attentive and knowledgeable of the menu. The food was pretty good and reasonably priced. Stay away from the tater tots, but the prosciutto mac and cheese was really good. Scampi entree and the scallops were both good. Nice dessert options. We will not be back, but we hope they can turn it around.
Could not love this place more, attentive wait staff, great prices ($2.50 Miller high life), great music, awesome mix of clientele.  This place is the best!!!

The self guided tour is as long or short as you want it to be. The Ryman Auditorum is a cool place to visit but we thought the extras you get to see on the tour are not worth the money. Mainly, just a few cases of artifacts that are covered up during the performances. We would recommend attending a concert there instead.

This place essentially defined the Nashville experience for us.  We were lucky enough to catch Brandon Holder perform and grab a table on the mezzanine with a great view of the stage.  The atmosphere just screams Nashville with all of the music memorabilia decorating the walls and guitars hung behind the bar.  They had a decent beer selection with your cheap standards and some local craft bottles.  All in all a good time out to grab a drink and listen to some music.

My all time favorite happy hour spot in Nashville! Great prices, menu, and atmosphere!!! Kaycie is hands down the best! She always delivers incredible service and very kind. She is the reason Sambuca's hang out spot. She feels like one of the girls.

This place is huge! And beautiful. The building itself is said to be shaped like a guitar (I didn't see it). There are plenty of places to sit down and get some work done, individually or with a group. Indoor and outdoor seating, even on the second and third floors. My favorite part was that the exhibition hall actually has some natural light! I came in December and there were lovely Christmas decorations everywhere. There are a few art installations and the country music songwriters showcase.

Completely ignorant and spiteful server. Asked my daughter three times for her ID just so she could drink a lemonade. Sent the manager over to check my daughter's ID when we, again, explained to her it was just lemonade. Asked about our food after waiting for fried pickles for 45 minutes and the server's response was "I have no idea." Definitely will not be coming back here. A shame for the performers that the wait staff is doing nothing for the atmosphere.

I love this place. It always hits the stop. The only reason it doesn't get the full 5 starts is the bathrooms, yucks! They are honestly smelly, even on a good day, they always smell like sewage. They definitely need to redo them, keep the old dive style decor but just make them clean and sanitary, that's all. I'm sure you make enough to upgrade and care for the customers making it all happen. Ok last one... not pleasant.

Burgers? Why do I want them?!!! Delicious... I do ignore the bathroom situation because I can see the kitchen. I cannot believe such a place with awesome burgers have that kind of cleanliness standards for their bathrooms. The staff have for the most part had been nice even on the busy days/nights.

New thing on a Monday night for me was a server to the table. She came and got our drink and food order and it was a nice treat. They were busy as most times I have been there so we got lucky to get that table. They have a upper level as well but the thing is to get as close to the stage! 

Overall you definitely need to check them out!

Fun,, Fun, Fun!  Yep, TIP THE BAND....Let's keep everyone coming back so we can hear the great music!  Great place to buy a pair of broken-in cowboy boots as well.

Popped in to check out a band and have a quick beer.  Ended up staying for the entire set.  Couldn't get my husband out of there, lol!  So M U C H   F U N ! ! !  I am almost loathe to share the review of the band (Silver Threats), I'm afraid the place will be so crowded next time there won't be room for us.  They are A M A Z I N G ! ! !

The bartender was on point, husting her butt off!  Kept the beers coming!
My first ever fried bologna sandwich was a memorable experience. Great bar with a very different vibe from the rest of the Nashville strip. Stop in here for some old school country western.
Cool place with good live music.  Very nice setting.  Bartenders were awesome!  It's not cheap, but the drinks, food, and service were excellent!
Stopped in for a drink last night, our last night in Nashville. We had fried pickles and a fried bologna sandwich. Yummy! Great band and a really fun place

Walked in and to the back. Looked around, listened to the band for a couple minutes, looked at the staff who all looked sad or mad from being there and we left to find a happier place to blow our money.

Wow, brought our family here to see the tour and they had so many people on the tour you couldn't get inside the rooms, or hear anything. The guide was speaking at the front of a long line each time, and although we complained that we could not hear she did next to anything to address the issue. Then the guide left us (we had someone with a wheelchair) and didn't explain that there was a video we should be seeing. As it turns out, the video should have been the first part of the tour. Total waste of time for us and such a shame as we were excited to show our family the rich history of the Ryman. Our tour guide's name was Adele. I hope the management addresses her performance as a guide. Apparently there's also a souvenir picture that comes as part of the package. It would have been nice to have that clarified as we are just now getting those details from another guide after 1 hour 45 min here of a 1 hour tour. 

After speaking with the manager regarding our experience, they refunded our ticket price. We paid parking twice to avoid a ticket in the process of clearing things up with the manager.
Just got to Nashville and this place pulled us in. It was a blast! Food was good service was great and the band was fun. We felt welcomed as soon as we walked in.
So much fun! Came here on a random Sunday night, live music was fantastic, the vodka was strong, the fries were cheesy and Brandon, our waiter, very accommodating! Fun fun times :)

I have never been to a venue so poorly run as this. One magnetometer for a venue this size. Several block long line because of this. The entire mass of people funneled through one set of doors. Ridiculous. 

Ryman, learn from the other venues in the area.

great music, i was impressed with the audio set up, i know i shouldn't be cause its nashville and everything, but really, sitting in the back and being able to hear the band perfectly, impressive.

 they have a good basic menu and the food on their is really good, the prices were all over the place, somethings were cheap, and somethings were prohibitively expensive: example $4.5 for 8 HUGE mozzarella sticks (delicious), but $5.5 for a 'premium beer' ( Shiner Bock ). basic french fries were 4.50... so just kinda odd.

 also this doesn't really bother me so much but worth pointing out, even tho the bar was not busy the service was poor, sub par. i didn't count off for that, just really the random pricing is what impacted the score.

The thing I love about Robert's is, you're not going to here fake twangy Florida Georgia Line music. You hear real honky tonk country. We come to Robert's a lot! If you're in town when the Eskimo Brothers are playing, we highly recommend. They're a blast to watch and play really good traditional music.

We stopped in for lunch during our trip to Nashville. The band was great, and we loved checking out the cowboy boots all over. Our only disappointment was when we ordered our food-cheeseburger and fries/onion rings. After putting in our order, the lady came back and said that their fryer wasn't working. We wished we had known that when we arrived as we could have gone somewhere else. At that point, we were stuck. I guess I should be thankful that we saved the calories! I hear this a great spot to visit at night, and I will have to go back and try it next time!

If you only visit 1 honky tonk THIS! is the one to go to!!! While on our honeymoon this was the place we visited again and again. The music was ALWAYS amazing and old school country, none of that Florida Georgia Line bull crap! The staff was fun and attentive. And the prices were right! $2.50 Miller High Life's! And ya gotta get a fried bologna sandwich. Holy delicious! Get here ASAP!

first bar we went to because of reviews whilst having girl's trip in Nashville. great vibe and music. pretty packed and there was just one bartender, she was very quick and attentive. tried the recession special - fried bologna sandwich with moon pie & potato chips. really delicious. definitely best bar around that Broadway strip.

My family and I went to the Ryman Auditorium for the Amy Grant and Vince Gill Christmas Show in 2017.  Of course Amy Grant and Vince Gill were great, but the Rymzan  Auditorium is a great place. It was my first visit, and I would return no matter who was playing! I like the historical aspects of the building, and it appears to be well maintained.  Entrance was well organized, and it appears that all seats are good.  I think no it's a must to visit while in Nashville.

"Roberts" is definitely a place to have a good time. I did feel that the bar itself is a bit congested and tight on space. Besides that, everything else was pretty cool. Good drinks, great music, positive vibes. Staff were friendly and attentive!
The music venue is wonderful and they have a lot of varieties of local beer which I loved !

The Ryman was one of my favorite things we did in Nashville. We did the self-guided tour which starts with a short video that details the rich history of the Ryman and how it has evolved through the years.

You can can walk through the auditorium and see the beautiful architecture, stained glass windows, posters from shows in the past, and artifacts from artists who have performed there. It is such a cool feel for a concert venue - such rich history and i love the pews for seating. Oftentimes they are setting up for a show on the stage which will happen that night which is cool to see. We ended up being able to see a show and it was amazing! Great acoustics!

Not a bad seat in the house other than being hard church pews which were very close together. We saw LeAnn Rimes one night and Sheryl Crow the following night. Sheryl Crow was great. LeAnn Rimes was awful! Gospel group opened for her and they were not great either.

What else is there to say, a true classic in Nashville. Loved this place, music was excellent, atmosphere was spot on, and last but not least, we all ate our share of fried bologna sandwiches this past weekend. Went back to Roberts WW at least four times. I will be back!

THE GOOD:
the vibe was awesome. great atmosphere. newly married and the live entertainment really made our time there special. the singer (Chloe Dolandis) came to our table and interacted with us so nicely. made my wife cry. (good cry). the staff was friendly and easily accommodated our party of 15 with no reservation.

THE NOT SO GOOD:
