we were there for brunch. the food just wasn't good. i ate off of 3 plates. i ordered chicken and waffles for myself, my wife had the BLT, my mom had the eggs benedict. NONE of them were anything to write home about. my chicken had soggy breading and the massive chicken pieces tasted like large processed, genetically engineered fake chicken breasts...
luckily the environment was awesome enough to make it worthwhile to come back. next time i'll just keep it simple with a cheeseburger and enjoy the vibe. please revamp the recipes.  5 stars for the atmosphere, 2 stars for the food.

My favorite so far

Real bartenders who do a real pour 
Friendly and All business at the same time 

great music on Saturday at 2pm.    A mix of country and .....Neil Diamond ..... who would have thunk it 

We plan on making this our first stop tomorrow due to the excellent service and great music

My first time visiting this spot. I loved this jazz club when it was in Atlanta. The bartender was a great happy hour host. I ordered the buca beignets and chicken and waffles! The food was good! The chicken needed some seasoning but over all it was a great experience! 
Fyi! Park behind the building because parking sucks!

Our waiter at Jimmy Buffets Margaritaville told us not to miss stopping in to Roberts and he was right. Best music on the street and I popped into every honky Tonk.  Crowded, everyone dancing, the band was entertaining and talented- bought a CD.

To be honest, I didn't research the Honky Tonks before I headed to Nashville. I was shocked to find that PBR bottles were $10 at each of the better known tourist packed places. My friend saw my sticker shock, took me to Robert's Western World and heavens gates opened. There sat the $2.50 PBR my little heart desired.

I didn't know all of the classic (50's-70's) country music they played, but it didn't matter. Live music, AFFORDABLE DRINKS, and good food. This was my favorite Honky Tonk, it reminded me of all my favorite Pennsylvania dive bars back home in NEPA. 

Coming back for a fried bologna sandwich ASAP.

Had an amazing night at Sambuca! Keith, our waiter, was great! We came for a date night/birthday celebration and had a great experience and were able to take our time. We had great drinks, loved the music, and food. We spent a few hours enjoying ourselves and the atmosphere. Even got a birthday dessert! We are definitely looking forward to coming back once we are in Nashville again.

My fav spot to be on Broadway. Can get a crowded. Simple old fashion country music, cheap drinks, friendly staff and good cheap bar food. The fried bologna sandwich is really good. Definitely a fun place to be!

Because there are already forty million reviews, I won't bore you with my typical in-depth review. However, it's good to know that this is an older crowd, real country/bluegrass unlike the other whiny/rappy junk you'll find on the rest of the strip and, the drinks are cheap.

Let's be honest, nobody gives a good goddamn what a review of a honky tonk bar says so I'll just say this much: on a hot summer day, when you're looking to get out of the sun and suck down something cold while listening to something hot, jump in here, sidle up to the bar, order up a bourbon on the rocks, take that little beauty upstairs and sit with your face six friggin' inches from the A/C vent as I did and listen to some twangin' guitar music.
Awesome Sweet Tea. I ordered the cheese burger and Onion rings. AMAZING!!!!!! Very reasonable prices, would recommend this place if you are ever in Downtown Nashville .

Ended it up here as of our barhopping spots  downtown, glad we did. The bartenders were extremely friendly, made good drinks, and the live music was really good. Not only did they play today's popular country music but also country music from back in the day , they played a mix of everything. Another's place I definitely recommend if you are downtown Nash!
Good music, fun atmosphere. This place had musicians playing originals, which we enjoyed. Acoustics definitely weren't amazing, and the stairs are a death trap. Still, I'd go back for the fun.

Not really sure why this place is getting such a great review.  My girlfriend and one of here freinds stopped there last night. We sat at the end of the bar and all ordered a bottle of beers .sitting there for 5 minutes when a bouncer came up to us and said he wanted are bar stools, they both got up, and I asked why?  A second later the power trip head bouncer tips me out of my bar stool from behind while two others grabbed me by the arms and another took my bottle of beer out of my hands and practically drugged me outside and kicked all of us out!  I have never been disrespected at a establishment like that! And I was not resisting in any way ,shape ,or form!  I will never go back.

Robert's Western World was everything I thought a Honky Tonk would be... a tad edgy, dark, filled with nostalgia and history, crowded and absolutely rockin'. It took a few minutes for us to find a seat which was made a little awkward as everyone was staring me down because I had the kiddos with me. Children are allowed to enter, stay and have a ball until 6pm, then it's strictly 21 and over. Honestly, this was THE best way for me to show them first hand what Music City is all about!! People wouldn't think Nashville would necessarily be a destination for children and I'm here to tell you that's absolutely false! We all equally LOVED honky talk hopping and Roberts was at the absolute top of our favorites list! A must stop! The girls LOVED Eileen Rose & Silver Threads who played while we were there. They were incredible! I highly recommend trying to stop by when they're there. They are regulars! Check the band schedule on Robert's site. They played it all....Janis, Patsy Cline, Cash (obviously) and some fab originals such as "Rose Garden" which is one of our favorites. They were so insanely talented!! That guitarist blew my mind!! He could've easily been Stevie Ray Vaughn, Kenny Wayne Shepherd or Satriani. Wowza!! 

Make sure you bring cash to drop in their artist's bucket. They live on these tip and it's the least you can do as there's no cover charge. The girls begged me to purchase the CDs the band was roaming around selling. I think I paid $5 each! It was the best souvenir we bought our entire trip! We still listen to them daily!!  

The bartender was a doll. You can place order at the bar and she will bring it to your table. I had some local drafts, Yazoo for about $6 each The girls split pickle spears and sweet potato fries they gobbled up in two seconds as well as moon pies for $1. Typical bar food. PBR & fried bologna sammys are the supposed "thing" here however. 

Definitely put Robert's on the very top of your Broadway stops list!! It was an absolute blast!!
Poor layout! Needs more eating establishments/coffee stops.  Stairs are awkwardly placed and too spaced out! Not my favorite!

My husband surprised me with tickets to Ray LaMontagne! The concert was awesome! We enjoyed to opening show as well--Kacy and Clayton.

I knew The Ryman Auditiorium was the original Grand Ole Oprey but I didn't know it was an old church. It was very cool to see the old wooden pews that were curved toward the stage. The back of the auditorium was stain glass windows. 

What a special place to visit. They offer tours as well as concerts, have a snack bar (you can bring food/drinks into the concert), and hold holiday services.

Ambiance: Excellent, you should go!

Vibe is an upscale classy feel. 

Staff is professional. 

Live entertainment 

The restaurant Accepts reservations and great for large parties 

Emerson is the best waiter ever!!! He was able to customize drinks, offered good food and drink recommendations and was able to accommodate substitutions for sides.

We went for or 9th anniversary brunch. We had the 
Seared Ahi Tuna for appetizer. I got a cup of chicken tortilla soup. Entree I had the shrimp and grits and my hubby had the Beef & Lamb Gyro. For dessert the Cheesecake Sopapilla. Everything we ate was amazing. Our server Amanda was great. She always came to check on us to make sure everything was ok. The live music was great entertainment.

I was curious why this place had such a high rating compared to the other bars on Broadway, but now I think I see why. Robert's does everything you expect it to and does it well. The music - mostly traditional country, from what I can gather - is great and just loud enough, and the decor is very well done. Drinks are cheaper than a lot of other bars around the area, especially if you take advantage of one of the meal deals. I mean, you can't beat $2.50 domestics. Their kitchen, located right behind the bar (literally) seems to be running all night and spits out simple, tasty bar bites. I have no complaints. Glad we stopped in for the night.

Solid choice in the Gulch for a nice meal out. I was here for my friend's birthday dinner and they delivered! 

Service was phenomenal. Our lady was so attentive, was able to make recommendations (great recommendations, btw), and even brought out a complimentary dessert for my friend for her birthday! 

They have live music all the time. The Chris Weaver Band was there this particular evening, and while I didn't care for them they seemed to be a hit with most people dining.

Food was good. I got the filet, medium rare. It came with a blue cheese butter and asparagus. I asked for the butter on the side as I'm not a blue cheese fan. Tried a bit, not terribly overwhelming as most blue cheese infused things are (to me). The filet was a touch over cooked, but still very tasty. Asparagus was perfect, great flavor with a snap to it. Ordered the bruschetta as a starter for the table and that was definitely killer! I would order it a hundred times over. 

Ambiance: lovely. Thanks for a nice evening Sambuca!

I finally got to attend a convention at this gigantic new center in downtown Nashville, and it was an overall positive experience.  The new Music City Center has completely changed the downtown landscape, bringing in new hotels, restaurants, shops, everything.  It's amazing to see how much has changed in that area.  The new convention center is on par with venues like the San Diego Convention Center.  It's huge, open, and bright with lots of window  and a prime location.  It has some of the cheapest parking available downtown, though after attending my first event there, I'm not sure they have enough parking if they have a large conference there.  The staff were very friendly and helpful and there are lots of signs to help you get around.  It can get congested in that area very quickly so give yours led time if attending anything there.  Overall I'm glad it's not proving to be giant sinkhole and that they seem to have things progressing well over there.
Maybe I don't go at the right times, but it's never lively. The food is just meh at all the restaurants. The stores are highly over priced. I do love the market and the selection they have.

Excellent music, fantastic burgers, and outstanding service by Rachael R.!  I came to town for the Jimmy Buffet / NFL draft weekend.  All of downtown was packed and the energy was great. My friends and I went to more bars than I can count and found ourselves visiting this establishment the most.  We were served by Rachael on our last two visits and we were equally amazed each time with her lightning speed, friendliness and accuracy! 
I highly recommend this place to all who visit the Nashville downtown area. The singers were incredible and every visit was memorable!

Honky tonk at its finest. One of the only places worth going to on Broadway. Guitar solos that will give you goosebumps and live music performances that fulfill Nashville expectations.

There's usually a line to get in because it's popular, but it's worth the wait. I've been a couple times and both times only had to wait 30min max. If you have a couple beers elsewhere before you go, you'll barely notice the wait.

Once inside the stage is to the left in the front of the venue and bar on the right hand side. Grab a PBR (yay!) and soak in the music.

They also have food here - it was late and I was itching for 4th meal and ordered a burger and fries. Actually quite good late night bar food! Worth it!

Yee Haw! Going out with your boots on. Local favorite. Top rated live country music with good quality beer and and drinks and burgers and fries. Great afternoon joint to stretch the budget and Honky Tonk.

Super fun place and an excellent array of choices in this food court type setting. Prices are very affordable and the live music and entertainment make this family friendly setting even more enjoyable.

Really cool place.  They also show you videos of Ryman (the old and the new).  Really cool to see the original flooring and seating. It seems like no matter where you sit you'll have a good seat of the stage!  Very clean and awesome experience.  A complimentary photo is included with the ticket
Absolutely LOVE Roberts and our Kick Butt waitress Rachael!! She is the best! Make sure you go and spend an hour or 7

Great crowd, great music, and great bartenders. This was by far my favorite place on Broadway. We went to Tootsies, Second Fiddle, Big Bang, The Stage, etc. Enjoyed the people watching, the drinks, the live band, and did I say the bartenders here were the BEST!
A okay honky tonk bar where the drinks are poured strong and the bands play for tips. No complaints.

This was one of my Honky Tonk Bar stops in Nashville. The decor was great with vinyl records placed everywhere. 

Great band, great drinks, great people. 

Restroom had easy access as well, which is a plus in my book!

All I can say is amazing!!! We had a happy hour group of 10 people all coming in a different times  ordering food and drinks at different times but the service we received from Sydney was amazing, she did not miss a beat! You must ask for her next time you're in.

If you want to see the real deal, you have to go here. LIve music, done well, with lots of gleeful dancing by all ages. This a good venue for a longneck, even if you're not a beer fan. It's just the thing to do here. Expect it to always be very busy, very loud, and a lot of fun.  We were doing quite a bit of bar-hopping, it being my first time in Nashville, and this is one of a few places that would remain on my list for a must do repeat visit. Even if it looks too crowded inside, squeeze your way in. The drinks are served fast and friendly.

Had an important business scheduled with a confirmed reservation for over a week. Got an email the afternoon before that simply read - your reservation has been canceled. Called restaurant and couldn't find out anything or get any info except "we took a larger group reservation". Pathetic customer service. Will never go there again. Be careful if they tell you that you have a reservation. They don't honor them.
The true birthplace of country music.  The mother church. A must visit in Nashville.  Amazing the place has so much history you can feel the vibe as you walk freely through the auditorium.
Very fun atmosphere in the middle of the day. The band was very talented and engaging and my wife and I had a very good time.

I have been to Roberts a hundred times. This time they deemed  we  had had too much to drink. I think it was more that we didn't fit the criteria for their audience.   I will just go around to the back door and avoid the asshole in the front.

I love this venue. When we went this time, we sat on row H in the balcony to see Gregory Alan Isakov. It was a good view even being pretty far back on the balcony! And the sound was great up there, know sometimes that is a concern with balcony seats. We would purchase balcony seats again in the front couple of rows if possible for our next concert here.

They do provide valet parking for some shows, but there is plenty of parking for 12-20$ everywhere around the venue. The place is classy and easy to navigate. Overall we had a great experience!

An absolute must. Building is a time warp. So very worth the price of tour. Starts with film that's is so cool. Really enjoyed this stop on our trip to Nashville. Disappointed at the tours ending I and others didn't realize pics on stage  included in price. Person standing next to camera (I thought she was with the people setting up) stood on floor looking bothered and annoyed.  Her job is to take pics so I feel like that was a crappy ending to a beautiful day.

I am honestly not one to leave a negative review but I am beyond frustrated at this point. I have gone to the box office multiple times to purchase tickets for an event and have never had problems until this week. Today was my 4th time arriving at the box office during the listed hours of operation. Each time I have gone in the past week have been at different times between the hours of 10:30am-4pm. Each time I have arrived at the box office, all of the doors have been locked and no one was in the box office. I arrived today at 10am and spent 20 minutes on the phone trying to get ahold of someone to see if they would be open during their listed hours. I finally got someone on the phone who was helpful and kind but told me that the box office would not be open until 2pm. I understand that hours change, but the least management can do would be to post their correct hours, or take them down completely.

My favorite spot in Nashville. It's all about old time country and blue grass and the house band (Don Kelley's) is just the best. Between the crazy talented bass player Joe Fink and guitar prodigy Daniel Donato, you are in for an amazing night of fun music. The Don Kelley band is there Monday - Saturday from 6 to 10pm. Be sure to tip these talented guys what you'd pay for a great night of music, because all the bands on Broadway Street only get paid in tips. They'll pass a bucket around regularly and remember to fill it! Oh and be sure to try the fried bologna sammich - it's the best on the planet. YUMMY!

If you're looking for something different in Nashville, check out Plaza Mariachi! I went on a rainy day so it's nice that everything is indoors especially with unpredictable Nashville weather. I went on a Friday so it was super lively. There was even an aerial dancer, someone who danced with fire, and loud live music. Like others have mentioned there's also a dance floor and things seemed kid friendly (around 7-8pm at least).

On to the food: Lots of food choices from Mexican to Argentinian to sandwiches. They also have a few places that sell desserts like churros, ice cream and boba. I got three tacos and all were awesome! Overall a fun experience and something pretty unique for Nashville.

A historic gem in downtown Nashville. This was the one thing I wanted to see - so glad we did!! 
Enjoyed every minute of it. $24 for a self guided tour. I did want to do the guided tour but they were sold out for the day. Actually glad we did the self guided so we could take our time and just enjoy the Opry. It was nice to sit and soak it all in. We got to go on stage and take a photo. The photos are included in ticket price. We got 3 - 5X7 photos. There is a great gift shop. So much music history here.

Excellent venue! 
You can tell all the attention to detail.  

The food court has lots of options. 

The stage is beautiful with lots of room for dancing or other events. 

Shops and a market also round out the space.

This is one of the best bars on this street. 

Awesome vibe, cheap drinks and people just having a great time. 

This place is the definition of Nashville to me. 

Strap on a pair of boots, grab yourself a beer and enjoy this western world. 

4.8/5

Yummy yummy dinner, they helped me throw the perfect bachelorette party dinner. Everyone was raving about how delicious the food was for the rest of the weekend! The steak was cooked perfectly, the salmon was pink and flaky, the potatoes and veggies were delicious, down to the drinks and shot included with our specialty menu, fantastic! Would recommend for parties and couples a million times over and would come back to Nashville just to eat here!

My girlfriends threw me a surprise birthday dinner here and it was a great experience!  It was just three of us, and my friend that called ahead of time said the lady that helped her was very accommodating over the phone.  We sat upstairs on the little balcony that overlooks the stage.  The decor was very elegant and I'm surprised the look and ambiance has remained so nice considering how long this restaurant  has been open (note: it's been at least 5 years since I visited here last).

We had some cocktails and ordered appetizers.  Everything tasted yummy.  But the BEST part was that the live band serenaded me by singing "Amanda" by Waylon Jennings for my birthday!  They were great!  

Our server was very friendly and made sure we were taken care of.  There is valet, but the restaurant does not validate the valet tickets because they are a separate company.
Oh, you don't want to go to Plaza Mariachi.  There's way too much going on there for you.  Stay home.

You have to go  !!! Many things to do there. Impressive boutique shops, reasonably priced. Very clean.  Great eat in restaurants.  But, the food court and bar have great live music,shows. You order from whichever places you want,  they notify you when all is ready. They will seat you or pick your own  table...Never a dull moment. We went on a Sunday, we spent 4 wonderful hours there, very reasonably priced. Hopefully  to return this weekend.
This is the perfect Honky Tonk. The gold standard. If you don't like Robert's Western World, then f*ck you.

Frozen hamburgers and fried bologna sandwiches are the limited menu options. $2.50 Busch lights and an assortment of other beer at around $5 each are on the opposite side of the menu. 

All ages until 6 pm and the servers are very friendly to children and adults alike. 

The men working the door are inviting and the have hour long stage sets so you are bound to hear something you like. 

The bathrooms are surprising clean and overall this was a huge highlight to my weekend trip in Nashville. My pre teen asked to return the next day. So we did!

Would have like to see one thing on menu that wasn't frozen or fried.

I had read good things about Robert's Western World and I am happy to say that the reviews are true. Robert's is just what one might imagine a honky tonk should be. Excellent musicians, we especially enjoyed Rachael Hester & The Tennessee Walkers, friendly staff like Kate and good drinks.  We will definitely make a point of spending time at Robert's whenever we come back to Nashville.

Unable to get in concert before opening act came on.  Long lines poor organization.  Been to concerts all over the country and have never seen such a disaster.  I feel sorry that The Aces didn't get the exposure they deserved because more than half of the ticket holders were still in line outside.

I have been to Plaza Mariachi a few times now and will definitely keep going back. Every time I got there it's a different experience and I think that really adds to the fun of it. You never know what you will find at Plaza Mariachi! 

Plaza Mariachi is a shopping and restaurant venue (mall?) off of Nolensville. It is pretty new and you can really tell a lot of thought went into the planning of this place. The outside and inside are beautiful and very well kept. Parking is never a problem because the parking lot is pretty big. When you first walk in the door, you forget that you are in Nashville. This place has so much culture and personality. It's described as the style of traditional marketplace streets of Old Mexico with Latin history weaved in. In the plaza you will find retail stores, a grocery store, restaurants, a small arcade, and a food court area that transforms into an entertainment center/concert hall. There has always been live music when I have been there. The mariachi bands are incredible. They also have various performing acts. When I was there last, there was an aerial show performing with the mariachi band. It was so much fun to get some delicious food and watch the show. All for free! Well, not the food but you get what I mean. I have reviewed the food places separately but just know that you won't be disappointed eating here! The prices are fair, the food is fresh and oh so good. There is also a full bar if you fancy a drink or two. I've heard of some other fun activities that occur at the plaza so I NEED to get in and try them out. For example, they offer free salsa lessons during the week. I want to say it's every Thursday night. I also have heard that the time to go is on the weekends at night. The food court area turns into a sort of night club with more live music, dancing, and drinks. Where else are you going to get a cool experience like this in Nashville? It would definitely make for a fun night out full of great food, drinks, and music. 

So basically what I'm saying Nashvillians is Plaza Mariachi is an experience to be had. This is Music City and Plaza Mariachi delivers nothing but excellent live music every time.
Loved this place. Great music and great service. Had a much better experience here vs tootsies. Beer is cold and the ac was cranked.

Fun place to be at. There is a lot of things going on from grocery to live music, mariachi and ping pong table.

I've been here a couple times now and it's a great atmosphere. Love playing ping pong with the family and got some churros and tacos.

Note: most places have a 50% military discount.

Great band. Great drinks!

We went on a Friday night and it wasn't near as crowded as expected due to the large floor and table spaces both upstairs and down.  Bar service was good. 

We will party here again sometime!

We dropped by on our first night in Nashville. It was rainy and cold, but we were determined to try this spot and were so happy we did. 

This place feels real authentic. That may not mean much coming from the guy who lives in NYC.

As we crossed the threshold we were greeted by the twang of the south, with a live band jamming immediately to our left. And what the lead singer proclaimed at one point held true for the rest of the evening there, "there no pop country in this bar!"

I ordered the cheeseburger with fries, and the fried pickles. This is the quintessential barfood in a divey Nashville pub and I was happier than a mosquito at a music festival. The food was tasty and cheap and filling and just a wonderful experience washed down with an ice cold PBR.

Def recommend this spot. Take the time, try it out!

Good for what it is. A honky tonk type bar true to its name. Drinks were cheap but nothing impressive. It was relatively dirty but I guess there's only so much you can do to keep the bar clean when it's packed. There were a bunch of creepy guys around.. my friend had her butt smacked by a random guy while walking by.. but I guess there's nothing the bar can do about that. Not my cup of tea but okay to check out for 10 minutes tops.

This bar is great 
Music and staff was on point.! 
And prices are good,good amount is seats and nice dance floor. No cover,great looking spot.
Can't wait to go back on my next Nashville trip.!

This was my favorite place that we toured in Nashville. I would highly recommend it. This is also one of the 14 stops on most of the hop-on-hop-off tour trolleys if you are a tourist. 

The outside of the building and architecture is incredible once you find out when it was built. We did the self-guided tour, cost about $25. They also have a guided tour were you can go backstage. All tours start out with a video that explains the history and start of the Ryman. The video is presented in a really cool way and not just a video on a screen. I learned a lot about the history that I didn't know. 

Once the video is over they let you wander through the building and look at all the donated mementos of people that have performed at the Ryman. There are also little tv's at some of the displays showing past shows and acts. There is a large display on the opposite side of the entrance doors on the second level that explains the entire history of the Ryman. It was neat to see all the famous and incredible people that have visited. 

There are more display cases on the ground level and a little recording studio that you can test out your singing and guitar abilities at. There is also a little roped off area at the front of the stage where a worker will take a photo of you, the photo is included with the ticket purchase. Most people were just having him take photos with their phones anyway. The tour itself is pretty quick and you can finish it in under 1 hour easy, depending on how long you stand and read everything. The seating is two levels and there isn't a bad seat in the house. 

We did learn that the building was going to be torn down in the '70s but the singers, with the help of Emmy Lou Harris, rallied together to save it. Walking through there I couldn't believe that anyone at any point would want to tear that building down. They still have concerts and acts performing at this location half the year and the other half they are out at the Grand Ole Opry. Everyone that we talked to said the sound quality is unlike anything else. We will be back to see a show on our next visit.

We spent an afternoon getting our honky tonk on at Robert's and we had a great time. The music was great, the place was chill, and we loved the decor and the feel of the place. With lots of places on this strip to choose from, Robert's felt authentic with first class music acts.

I went to the Tin Roof 3 times.  Food was good. 

Wait staff awesome. Friendly, helpful and provided get service.
Nice shop. Lots of trinkets to choose from. I was looking for another shop that had some interesting memorabilia. No real country music here. I thought with a name like ledge DSS I might get that.

In the first five minutes* following a snaking through the dense crowds to a miraculously emptying two top by the main bar, we:
- ordered two Miller Lites and two Fireballs for $16. Because honky-tonk.
- saw the dude who played Ginsburg on Mad Men. Both nipples intact.
- tried to order a grilled cheese and a fried baloney sandwich, but were told they were out of bread.
- watched as a sloppy drunk played grab-ass with an unwilling female near the stage.
- watched as the band stopped playing, and the lead singer lunged at said grabber-of-ass, jacked him the face a few times, threw him out the front door, jumped back on stage and... finished the song a cappella.

Is this real? Are we on set? Nope. Just another day at Robert's Western World. This Broadway stalwart seemed to attract locals and tourists alike. It's not indie, it's not underground, but it's still the real deal.

*In the last five minutes, we ate a found bag of chips and dumped beer on each other while dancing to the stone-faced delight of a front row grandfather most country. Check please!

Robert's is my favorite, must stop on Broadway.  This bar is old school.  It is a classic, some of the best country music on the strip.  They serve PBR's for $2.50 a piece and they have a fried bologna sandwich on the menu.  In fact if you want to pair the two together they have a menu special called "The Recession Special" for $6.00 which is a fried bologna sandwich, chips, a moon pie, and a PBR.  Talk about a deal.

Every visit I have ever had at Robert's has the same ingredients; great, fast, friendly service from the bar, foot stomping good ole live country music, and cold beer.  Robert's just makes me happy.  I can sit back enjoy my beer, listen to the music, and just relax.  It is like I leave life behind at the door where they card me every time to enter.  Stop in and try it for yourself.

For Plaza Mariachi to only be a few months old, it's very impressive what they've put together. Obviously, something on this scale... with this vision... took a long time to execute and produce but from most all who have been here, the wait and effort was worth it. For purposes of this review, I am reviewing PM as a destination/venue/center. I think the various businesses that make up PM should be reviewed and rated on their own.

From the minute you pull in to the lot, you'll be impressed. PM stands tall on a hill and its imposing character demands respect. Walking past the cool landscaping and in the main doorway, look up to pay some mind to the impressive chandelier. There are touches like that throughout the venue. From the textured walls to the paint choices to the lighting to the architectural choices, no detail was left untouched. The various hallways bear names of places and add a nice conversation piece to the exploration you're bound to do.

What impresses me most is the diversity of options at PM. Yes, there's a large food court with plenty of South American, Central American and Caribbean styles from which to choose but there's also a grocery store, ice cream shop, radio station, jewelry store, art gallery, a kids' playground, dance studio, sports shop, and other stores to patronize. You could make a day of shopping and eating here. And, being Nashville, there's live music every day in the food court. From emerging artists to local favorites to big names, there's all manner of entertainment to be had. And to the diversity of stores, add a diversity of people. Glencliff's population has been predominantly Latino for a little while now and PM celebrates that and invites people from throughout the metro to come in and see what's happening. Perhaps now Nashville neophytes will finally stop exclaiming that 'there are no authentic 'fill in blank' in Nashville' once they come here. 

There's a ton of potential at PM and it's very cool to see what they've accomplished in only a few months. As more tenants come in and the plaza becomes more of a neighborhood staple and metro destination, I am eager to see how it settles in and cements itself as a fixture of Music City. A couple of final thoughts: PM management/ownership is thoughtful and forward-thinking. This will serve the plaza well. And if you stop by Nina's Nieves, ask for Daniel. After I had an atrocious (review to come) experience at a PM restaurant, I was bowled over by Daniel's enthusiasm, professionalism and fantastic attitude. Plaza Mariachi powers that be need to do what they need to do to hold on to this young man. He's an asset to the organization.

Hot licks and honky tonk in Nashville's premier rocks off joint, Robert's Western World. Hell, tourists will flock here, don't let that discourage you. Locals are engrained into their bar stools here. Seriously, they don't budge even for a dollar!

One of the coolest live music venues I experienced in 2018, hands down. The music was firing on all cylinders. Upright bass, a child prodigy riffing on the electric guitar, and the crowd energetic as can be. 

Things of note that may sell or not sell you on Robert's:

1. Doesn't matter what time or which night you visit, the room will be packed like sardines. Expecting a seat? Yeah, fat chance.

2. Bands in Nashville are notorious for making their living on tips. Confrontational encounters with band members storming through the crowd looking for a quick buck are imminent. 

3. Going to the bathroom will take every bone in your body to power through the audience. Maybe just hold it?

You know I'm a cocktail and craft beer enthusiast. When you come to Robert's, order a High Life or PBR, and maybe a shot of Wild Turkey. You're here for the music and the music only, not pizzazz.

I'm itching to return!!

With so many spots to choose from in Nashville, especially on Music Row, it's hard to say which ones are the best of the bunch. It really depends on the band that's playing, and the crowd in the joint. 

Legends stuck out because it was thoroughly entertaining in the middle of the afternoon and we were still recovering from the previous night out on Music Row. We were able to grab a table and a few chairs in the back, and stayed for a few hours. The decor is a bunch of old album covers on the walls and other memorabilia. 

We got there during the last couple songs of a band playing, so we had to wait for the next band to set up. This next band had a lead, who was an entertainer. Good musician, but also told stories/jokes between songs and really engaged the crowd. The band was good, the music was fun, and the beers were cold. We had a great time! Though it's pretty hard not to have a great time in Nashville.

I had my first visit to Sambuca last night. I can not say enough good things about this restaurant. The music was good, the food was amazing the cocktails were great but most of all the personal service given to us by our bartender Aaron was nothing but exceptional. He recommended our food and even our drinks. He went above and beyond to make our experience unforgettable. I will definitely visit Sambuca. Kudos to Aaron for making my first visit a unforgettable experience.

Last night we attended the ICMA reception at the Tin Roof.  The food was good and a nice variety.  But the 5 stars goes to Justin.  He worked that bar like a well oiled machine.  There were at least 150 attendees and there was never a line for drinks.  Hats off to you Justin!

Went to see Stephen King.  Got there thirty minutes before show and line wrapped around building.  15 minutes to get in.  Had to stand in trash in alley.  Other than that it's the Opry and worth seeing a show if you have never been.

This was a pretty cool find on Broadway. 
Smaller than I expected as far as a roof top goes. Not having much seating and feeling a bit crowded with no where to go. There isn't a band up on the roof either but there is a bar next door with live music that you can see and hear pretty well. The people watching of the street below is hilarious. There are some choices for drinks up on the roof too but not a full bar.

Me and a large group of friends went here for lunch on our weekend trip from Georgia. We were there for 3 hours before we got our lunch. The amount of time we ended up spending there ruined our day. Overall, bad experience.

Such a fun place to visit! We are from California so we miss the culture that state beings! This place is awesome! Mariachi music, salsa nights, great safe environment and a judgment free zone! Highly recommend this for a family and a date night

Open to all ages until  10.00pm. That makes it great for those 19 year old boys that are visiting.  No smoking, cheap burgers  and bologna sarnies in a basket and a cold beer circa $5.  Plus good ole fashioned country music without people falling down drunk like some of the other notable bars.  Home of Brazilbilly and a rocking good time.
Always a stop when we have out of towners.

Pretty messed up being a first responder and veteran being treated like a criminal for wearing a motorcycle vest.  We are a riding group not mc was treated like a criminal.  Let you bogus bouncer see in my vest. Proved no weapon but still treated like a criminal.  Nothing like putting your life on the line every day and being treated like a criminal. You people are joke and should be ran out of business.  We voluntary left business after being treated bad.  Shame on you. I did as you ask and still complied with rental cop. Tried second time to come back without Scarry vest still deined.  Bouncer were good but supervisor horrible.  Demand apologize
Love this place a Nashville classic. Great grilled cheese. They sell cowboy boots too. Always good music. Long honky tonk style bar.

I love this bar....BUT, they need to play old country between bands. 
It is what they do and their are some people who still want to listen to that type of music.
This is the only bar on Broadway St in downtown Nashville to experience real Nashville rockabilly live music! Cash only and prepare yourself for a great time. Upstairs level has its own bar.

Got recommended by hotel concierge. "Only" time they had was 6:30 Saturday we were told so off we went.  Walked in to a basically empty room that never did get more than half full the entire time we were there.  All I can say is it was the worst meal of our recent visit.  Don't go, run away. Eat at Cook Out if you are desperate.  Food was expensive service was slow and two out of four orders were cold when they arrived to table. Sent calamari back "we will re-make that right away", about 5 min mater the same microwaved plate came back to table - now a bit warmer but totally inedible.  When they cleared our table we could tell server was embarrassed but they still charged us for the food.  The place can't decide what it is - if fine dining then why TVs on walls?
We had great meals the entire rest of our visit at a variety of spots - avoid this one if you are in town.
Definitely a place that should be on your list if visiting Nashville! Great entertainment although seating is on pew benches. So can get a little uncomfortable

Stopped in here as I was touring Broadway and taking in the sights. They had live music in the window and I thought I would give this place a try.

Place is dark and smells like a bar upon walking in. The band playing wasn't too loud, but plenty loud enough that they could easily be heard in the back area of the bar. One of my buddies flagged down the bartender and ordered a few drinks. 

I am not sure what my friends got, but I got a 7-up and strawberry vodka. It was not very good. Very likely it was cheap liquor that was used, although the small drink was $9.00 on a Wednesday night. To be honest, I don't really care much for the taste of alcohol, so I'm a poor judge of what a good alcoholic drink should taste like. I have had alcoholic drinks that I like, so it is possible, but this one wasn't it. Even my buddy said he didn't think it was that good and cited the cheap liquor used in it.

The bar has a floor section closer to the band and a back section with a few steps to a raised area. We sat there and the band sounded great from there. The bar's back area is like a museum of sorts, with an older jukebox encased in glass. I know jukeboxes are terribly common, but it was like being in Back to the Future Part II and Marty looking at every day 90's gear like it is a museum item.

We left after the single drink. We were probably there 20 minutes. It is a quaint place. Probably worth stopping in at least once to check it out. Not really a place I would hang out for long periods and continue to drink, but it would be nice if you were short on time and wanted quick entertainment.

Amazing. that's what I have to say. Huge venue, we went to see Comic con and they had tons of space. On top of that all the rooms hat were provided made it massive. Wife and I like stairs and like walking so we took those instead of the elevator or escalators. The parking around it is tough, especialy when heirs so many events in town but that's to be expected. What makes it 5 stars is the location. Theirs so much to do around it that you cant go wrong.

Recently moved here from San Diego and seriously missing good Mexican food! I was so excited when I found out about this place. I've never seen anything like it. I came here during the week so it wasn't busy at all. The shops were fun to look at and got to see two performances. I think it's really cool that they do that. I want to go back and check out more events. Can't remember the place I ate at but it was pretty good. Definitely need to try out the other places.

Sadly the rave reviews didn't meet with reality.  The Fried Bologna Sandwich was a huge disappointment.  My husband was very let down as it wasn't fried, it was more steamed (barely hot).  Frankly the sandwich was the reason we came here and it along with the excruciatingly  loud band, mediocre burger and cheese curds made it a definite ONCE & DONE place to visit.

Great venue to see a show. You'll want to be there on time because the seating is not specifically labeled so if you are late someone might be sitting in your seat and everyone has to shift over.  The VIP was a little bit underwhelming. First of all the staff were very generous and helpful. The food was not well-maintained and just sort of over cooked as the evening went on. The desserts were delicious. Drinks are much smaller than you get if you are not in the VIP so in order to have a conversation you have to keep walking across the VIP to get a drink and walk back and get a drink and walk back. I think they're trying to control people taking drinks out to give to someone else but there would be many ways to do that without making the service for VIP worse than the service for other people. It is not a lounge it is a hallway. The doors to the hallway say emergency exit only. To make it worse they want people to walk across the entire building and then back to get to the lounge even though there are simply doors and stairs to the area. They have this completely wrong. When you exit at the bottom of the stairs there are two staff members standing there. When you enter at the top it is strange but nobody is standing there.  They need to put a VIP lounge sign on the upstairs and the downstairs where staff were standing and just pay attention to who goes in through those doors. It is absolutely ridiculous to think a person downstairs on the same side as the lounge would cross the entire theater go up the stairs cross the entire theater go in the door get a drink then when they need another do the whole thing again. Four trips across the entire theater to get a single drink. There are no chairs in the VIP lounge.  I rate locations according to their primary purpose and in this case it is music and music presentation was fantastic and the staff were very helpful. But I won't give the same rating about the lounge.

This is one of the best bars in Nashville hands down.  The servers are excellent and attentive even when its busy.  The live music is always good, though I would recommend going when Buck McCoy is playing as he is exceptionally talented and funny.

All in, this bar shows an authentic Nashville bar experience that is only a stone toss from the Reiman Auditorium.  Go now, thank me later with an appropriate drink.

Roberts Western World is 5 Stars.  The best of broadway, an old school honky tonk that has great music, loose women and amazing fried bologna sandwiches. You cannot beat the Special Doggone for $6.50. Premium Hot Dog, Chips and Buuuuusch Light. The service is second to none and Justin was amazing. Also he is super best buddies of Jason, Josh and Leif.
Amazing acoustics. Only bad seats would be behind a pole/column. In that case the seats would be cheaper for abstracted view. I was standing near the FOH boards/audio for the Janelle Monae show.

This is a great little marketplace in the heart of Nashville off of Nolensville road not to far from the Nashville zoo.

It's kinda in the hood, but I love that area because it has so many of my favorite Asian, Arab, and Indian markets. It's a melting pot of ethnicities which makes it very special in my opinion

Plaza Mariachi is a huge complex containing little shops, restaurants, and Hispanic markets. The live music and entertainment is also special. It's a great place to go and try food and shopping from many diverse Latin countries. 

Go check it out and make a day of it. I'm sure you'll enjoy it as much As I did!

I need to warn everyone about the overpriced Premium Pass Lounge at the Ryman Theater.
I bought my Home Free Tickets  & have been anticipating this trip every day since. I missed out on the uvip/vip so settled for the Ryman upgrade to the Premium Pass Lounge as I was bringing my disable Aunt & Uncle with me. He is a 91 year old veteran who is almost completely blind and partially deaf  needing a cane to walk. She suffers from cronic pain, fatigue and anxiety. It has taken me many years to get her to travel with me. The way the lounge was described as a private entrance with pass holders only allowed sounded as if it would be worth the extra $100 plus taxes & fees EACH so they could enjoy the evening with minimal stress. 
I had called Ryman customer service the morning of the show to ask details, confirm time lounge opened, handicapped accessibility and if here would be signage or direction to the lounge as we had never been to the venue. This was the beginning of our miserable and disappointing evening. I was given so much wrong information by the Ryman Staff, our evening was a complete and utter disaster until the Home Free guys took the stage, that is.  
I was told the lounge opened at 5:15 but it actually didnt open until 7pm, so we ate then waited in cold outside Cafe Lulas for over half an hour.  The start of the choas was my Aunt collapsing near main security line while trying to go out to the private entrance. The wheelchair I was told would be available wasnt there. At least a dozen staff & security watched us try to carry my aunt through the crowd only speaking to us when directing us to move out of the way for other guest to get inside. Where was OR is there even medical staff at Ryman events? Finally a sympathetic security guard brought us the wheelchair and pointed us in the direction of the Premuim pass entrance. The signage I was told would be there was non existant. I was so stressed and upset that I didnt even realize I was standing next to Austin, the adorable high tenor of the band, who was on the phone! We found the lounge which was upstairs on the complete opposite side of the theater from the entrance. It took some time to reach it fighting our way through the crowd, so much for that private entrance which brought us right into main entrance and the stream of a thousand people.  The stairs were not an option so we waited in line for the one elevator. Once reaching the lounge, We only had about 20 minutes before show started. There was no place to sit in the lounge wjich is actually the emergency exit hallway and appetizers from Cafe Lulas consisted of cold hard chicken fingers,  chex mix and cheesecake bites. It seems as if they shopped at Sam's club. After using the facilities and skipping the apps, we headed for our seats with much difficulty. The aisles do not accommodate the large size wheelchairs the venue has. The ushers were useless and just pointed in a general direction instead of assisting in finding our seats. Finally reaching our MF seats and getting my aunt & uncle settled after the show had already started,  I just broke down and cried. I completely missed the 1st 10 minutes of the show sitting there sobbing uncontrollably until the guys voices finally broke through that fog of disappointment. The music and the guys enthusiasm was the only bright spot to the entire trip. A Home Free show, being at the Ryman in Nashville and spending time with my family should have made some good memories. None of us had been to the Ryman before and they had never seen Home Free. We still feel as if we havent been to this historic theater because with the chaotic dash to try and get to the overpriced so called lounge, then to our seats, we do not remember anything positive about the theater itself. If it wasnt for some other fans helping with my uncle & with the wheelchair, my family getting seated, we would probably just have left before the show started.
Thank-you so much to the several Home Fries who  helped us, I'm sorry I didnt get your names. 
I blame the entire evenings disaster on the Ryman customer service staff, less than helpful ushers, lazy rude security staff and the disorganized chaotic system used for entrance to venue,  specifically the Premium Pass Lounge. This lounge was the biggest waste of money!! Take my advice to anyone considering it in the future, use the money to purchase more swag from the bands merch table. I didnt even make it to the table or signing line for which I'm even more disappointed in than the lounge. We were just too exhausted and needed to get my family out of the crowd.
I plan to send a formal complaint letter to the Ryman Management company and to copy the Home Free management too. I feel artist should be aware of these flaws as it ultimately effects them by creating poor fan experiences for something that they recieve no financial benefit from and even loss of merch sales. I really wanted a sweat shirt.

I was really impressed with the Ryman. I'm not necessarily a country music fan, and had never heard of the Ryman before arriving in Nashville, but I took a chance on the tour and really enjoyed myself. The introductory video was awesome and very well done (and I never ever say that). I really wish I could have caught a show here. If you bring your ticket stub from Ryman to the Johnny Cash Museum, you get $2 off. My only complaint is that I think $10 would be more appropriate than $20 for admission... but I'd vote you visit this over the Cash museum, if short on time.
Lots of activities, beautiful vibe, looks like little mexico vacation spot. Lots of parking, beautiful design

What a great place to check out while in Nashville. It's a great historical spot and a must see if you have time to tour the area. I found it to be a little pricey but then again it's a touristy place. You start out going upstairs to watch a little video on it. Then, you get to walk around and check out different memorabilia that is showcased. You can even get your picture taken on stage. There is also a gift shop as well.

I have been here twice with a large party of work friends. The place is huge and can accommodate any size group you have.  We even got a special menu for my party of 18.  The service is great and the dining room is set right I front of a really cool stage. Music acts have been really good and play a mix of country and rock and other styles. The food is pretty good but the larger groups I've been with usually stick to shareable appetizers and they were great.  A good place to take a large group from work or a large party celebrating

Interesting, but small venue. They do a very nice job with the multi-media presentation at the start of the self-guided tour. Great to see the interesting memorabilia from the history of the Ryman. At the end take a turn standing on the famous stage!

I had really high hopes for Sambuca, but it failed on all fronts.

Our waiter was extremely knowledgeable but he wasn't present after we placed our order.  We waited over an hour to get our food, not once did he ask if we needed anything or even asked to refill our drinks. 

Once the food finally came out it was all cold. Every single plate in a group of 10.  One of us ordered the shrimp and crab linguine but had to send it back because it was completely inedible. It smelled and tasted like pure onions.

Don't order the potatoes au gratin either. Everyone who ordered it complained about how overcooked and dry it was. You couldn't cut it with a knife.

Maybe this was just a bad night, but we won't be back. This is the worst restaurant experience I  have had and we paid a lot for subpar service and below average food.

The waiter didn't even apologize or seem to care about how unhappy we all were.
Great music, especially after 10:30, great drinks, and great service. Rachel is the best waitress we've had so far in Nashville!

What can I say - this is one of my favorite Honky Tonks.  The music is consistently good and well mixed.  You can have a conversation while it's playing, which sometimes is key.  The barstaff is the friendliest in town.  I know if I try to list them all I'll miss someone, but Brooke, Kara, Casey, Nicole, Nikki, Tara, Mary Coul, Barbie, are awesome!
There are two spots to see music - floor level and upper floor.  Try for a seat in the upper level to see and hear great.  It is mostly acoustic music in the morning until 2:15, then bands until 2-3AM.  Tip both the bands and bartenders - that's the Nashville way, and how they earn a living.
My favorite days and bands - Monday afternoon, Kinsey Rose, Tuesday afternoon Hali Hicks, and Thursday nights don't miss Becki McLeod.  Kids are allowed until 6pm

Solid venue for a show.

My love and I attended a David Byrne concert at the Ryman and had a great experience. The entry was fast and easy and the concession lines moved very fast. I believe the Ryman is and old church that was converted in a music venue. By the layout you can definitely tell but the acoustics of this place are amazing. My only recommendation is to definitely get seats either on the balcony or far enough up on the floor that your view isn't blocked. I dodged the columns but would have liked it more if we were further up (we were row M). But still solid  venue, with friendly employees and super clean bathrooms! Hands down one of the best shows of my life.

When we got there around 10:30 on a Saturday this place was super packed. Come to think of it it seemed pretty crowded in the daytime too. Anyway we were told to go to the side entrance the lines wasn't too bad. The band playing had a great violinist and we were all awed by her because she was definitely rocking it. It was a nice to touch to have the TV screens showing the band as well so those of us at the back had a nice view. 
There were a couple of bars at the back so getting drinks was  not hard at all. They also have outdoor area at the back where you can take a break from the crowed and get some fresh air.

Nutshell:  Simple, well done food, great prices, and friendly service.

Our group stopped in after the Blues v. Preds game on a Tuesday night.  The music was going strong and they had a full house.  We headed up to the balcony to find a place to sit.  The whole place has an old time honky tonk feel, unlike some of the newer establishments along Broadway.  We were starving, so we headed back to the bar to order drinks and food.  The menu is surprisingly really good, they have way more than just microwave burgers (unlike some other places I've been to)  I decided on the hot turkey & swiss sandwich with chips and a soda.  All in all it was under $10, which was great.  They have a grill behind the bar and then delivered it up to us.  I was expecting a very basic sandwich...I was wrong!  It's a simple sandwich, but super tasty.  The bread was toasted, the turkey was juicy and flavorful and piled high, and it was well constructed and not sloppy.  It hit the spot, which is the main thing.  It's worth a stop in for the music aaaaand the food.

Another rowdy bar on the Broadway strip, one of the smallest with just 2 levels both have bands playing. the downstairs area is kinda cool with the lights it was crowded so we made our way up. 
another band playing we stuck around for drinks, had some Lagunitas beer not bad. 
band playing was decent, they seemed to be doing some cover songs not too bad a good break from all the country music. 
Bar below was less friendly with the service, it was easier upstairs to get drinks.

Even if you're not a huge music fan, this is a must if you're a tourist in Nashville.  I would imagine seeing a performance here is the best way to experience this unique space, but i give five stars for the self tour!

The space is so uniquely intimate (in the age of stadium tours, its tiny!), it's amazing to walk around it and imagine how cool it must be to see your favorite band here.

The building is a microcosm of the history of Nashville, American culture, race relations, all focused on what happens when you bring people together.  The historical exhibits make you stop and think a bit about all of those things. And that it's still today an active concert spot is amazing!

And from a wow perspective, don't skip the movie intro to the tour. It will delight you!

Par-Tay with the G's!

SITREP

My yelp-buddies Chris G. and Nickie G. (NO RELATION!) organized a wonderful outing to Robert's Western World (RWW).  Little did I know I would lose my Nashville-Virginity at this wonderful den of iniquity!

THE SETUP

As you walk down the hill along Broadway, and head into the "strip" where RWW is amongst many other equally notorious & delightful establishments on both sides of the strip, RWW is easily identified by the neon-illuminated guitar sign.

And even though it says Honky Tonk on the sign, when you walk in the concept is REALLY brought home to you as your skirt right by the front of the stage where any one of a number on Honky Tonk Bands is playing for the enthusiastic crowd.  You can hang around a dance a few numbers like I did, or head straight-away upstairs where the darker, more secret bar is located with great domestic bottle deals!

THE CROWD

I swear I felt at home in this crowd even though I clearly sounded too much like the Peter Jennings & Tom Brokaw dialect of generic North American-speak.  And when girls here call you "dahlin", my heart melts automatically.  [Here's looking at you, Ms. Marti M.!]

THE ALLEY 

Right behind this second bar is the alley where you can step out and enjoy a smoke, have a chat with cute girls in black jeans, and then amble back in, or go next door to any number of other establishments that you can also access from the back (like we did with Tootsies).

THE LOWDOWN

RWW is THE stop to get your Nashville Honky Tonk on!
Exceptional Bourbon mule. They make their own finger reduction!!  Outstanding!!  Get the beniets. You will not be disappointed and I never leave reviews. H

Great location! Great food! Great live bands! Great ambiance! What more can someone ask for? I had the lobster bisque, chicken fried oysters. Scallops for my entree with a side of brussels sprouts. Two drinks which consisted of the Sambuca 75 and Cherry sour. The cherry sour was right on time! A little bit too much salt for the food which was why I didn't give 5 stars (I realize that's my NY/NJ palate talking so I'll let it slide). Other than that definitely good eats. I will visit again the next time I'm in Nashville! :-)

The second Fiddle 
Kelcy was the barmaid today and she was so kind and really fun.
"Big country & The Hee Haw Rejects".  We walked in as they were playing a 
song called Tennessee whiskey.

Well we ordered some whiskey on the rocks and she gave us two beers to back that up, lol, it's only 3 o'clock in the afternoon, it's going to be either a very short evening or a long night.  We were there for a couple hours, turns out it has to be one of our favorite places that we've been in Nashville! Acoustics were fantastic and love the decor, I WOULD go back.

What a fun place to hang out. Came here with my hubby and young son to check out the live band. The band playing Eileen Rose and the Silver Threads was so good! They played various country songs and they were excellent. My son had so much fun and he even started dancing to the songs. As for the food we ordered fries basket and drink. The fries were huge and crispy. The prices were definitely good. Great live music in a fun environment. Highly recommended!

It had such high ratings we stopped by and really liked the bands music. We ordered drinks and dinner. We both ordered the brisket and shrooms quesadilla's. They were really pretty good, only bad thing was the tortilla chips that were served with it were terrible they were fried in rancid oil. We couldn't even eat them. I told another waitress as we were leaving asking for the manager, she didn't seem to care. The band was great!

I can't imagine how good the music is during the weekend or evening because we are here at noon on Monday and it's fantastic!   Really didn't think it would be any good on a slow Monday.   Crazy.  As far as the bar, it's a bar nothing special.   But if you want to have a drink and listen to good music it's worth the visit.

I was here for QuiltCon and found it to be a terrific venue. 
There were clean bathrooms easily found near every room I was in.
The signage was great, employees were friendly and it was bright and clean.
I would come back here in a heartbeat, it made me love Nashville even more!

This is an amazing auditorium!  So much history goes along with this Building, and what a privilege to get to enjoy a concert here.  We came to Nashville to see Tommy Emmanuel in concert here.  We actually had 2 sets of tickets, so we decided to do the tour the day before to see which seats we wanted to sit in, and also I wanted to know more about the history of the building. 

The tour starts out with a quick 10 minute movie that explains everything about the building.  It's actually a very entertaining movie.  Then we got to tour the auditorium.  It's so cool to sit on the benches that are the original benches that were used when the Ryman was a church.  The hardwood floors, ceilings, and even the beautiful red bricks on the building are original.  When it was restored, they did an amazing job.  

The concert was WONDERFUL!  Tommy Emmanuel was awesome and the acoustics in this auditorium surpass any place that is built now.  They have a lot of concession stands to go to during intermission.  

I can't wait to come back to another concert here.  It's also nice that only a little over 2,000 can attend.  It's much more personal.  I HIGHLY recommend coming to a concert here.

Great service and drinks. 
Blackened flat iron steak with buffalo trace bourbon. 
Our server Kevin was great and the king of up-selling ( in a good way). We pretty much ordered anything he offered. We had the crab dip appetizer and additional drinks most likely because of his stellar service. He should be recognized for this as he is definitely generating increased revenue. 
This place was great. The food was amazing on all counts and the live music was great. Not too loud. 
And of course the service tied it all together. Great place.  Definitely 5 stars.

I recently walked to Legends Corner after the Elton John concert at Bridgestone.  It was about 11pm on a Saturday and the streets were full, so we ducked inside.  A band was playing, and they were really good, but my ears were still sensitive from the concert, so we got a drink and sat on the patio to people watch as they went by us.  Although we were the only two outside most of the time, a waitress still came out to check on us.  We could still hear the band and we even clogged to Rocky Top.  There is absolutely NO WAY that my feet will be still when I hear it.  

The most interesting thing that we saw all night was when we sat on the patio on Legends.  A woman, walking all by herself, was very intoxicated and holding a $20 bill in her hand, very visibly.  She walked down the alley next to Legends, and a man kept eyeballing her, clearly ready to take her money, and who knows what.  It was a gut feeling I had, I guess.  I called her to come over to the patio railing and started a conversation.  She explained that she'd been with friends, but she'd gotten too drunk to get into the next bar.  Bouncers said no, and her friends went in and left her to fend for herself.  

The man that was stalking her had turned and went in the opposite direction.  My husband and I told her about the man following her and told her she needed to put her money away, and try to walk closer to a group of people.  Although she was highly intoxicated, she was cognizant enough to realize what we were saying.

Women, don't walk the streets of Nashville at night by yourself.  It's not smart or safe.

All of the food was reasonably priced and the burgers were yummy! We got to listen to John Shepherd and he knew every old country song that we threw out at him! He was very entertaining and listening to him prompted me to check out the history of this place. I found out he had been playing there for over 40 years! This place is always busy at night and everyone is always entertained! A must stop in downtown Nashville!

Our office just had our staff Christmas party at Sambuca! What an amazing place.  We were greeted immediately upon our arrival and taken to the private room we were having our party in.  The decor was very festive.  Within minutes the staff proved to be very accommodating and friendly.  They remembered everyone's name and what they were drinking and we had a group of 60 people.  Everything we asked for they made sure we got it.  I haven't even mentioned the food yet! Everything we had was delicious and with the variety of appetizers everyone had plenty to choose from.  We have been going to different restaurants for Christmas for 16 years and this was by far the best place we have ever been too!  Thanks guys for a great experience.

Fantastic live music and fairly uncrowded for a Friday Night. Had so much fun there!

Only thing is that the drinks were pretty expensive, but definitely worth it for the music!
Great beer, great atmosphere, GREAT MUSIC!

Every other review talks about the acoustics in this place and yes, they are fabulous and yes, you feel up close and personal with the artist no matter where you sit. Going to a show at the Ryman is truly a must if you're in Nashville for any amount of time. 

I came with a few girlfriends just to experience the Ryman, and we bought tickets without even knowing the artist because the reputation for this venue is seriously that good (turns out Jake Bugg is quite good too). There is parking on the backside of the building for $15 or you can brave downtown and try to find street parking for less. 

If you're looking kick up your romantic evening to the next level, the Ryman does sell food items like chicken strips and hotdogs. They have a good drink selection with a full bar and one of the highlights of my night was a 16oz pour of red wine. 

The seating is sort of in pews, but you do have an assigned seat. The waits for food and drink weren't too long and the staff were very helpful and accommodating. Also its convenient that the Ryman is within walking distance of Broadway if you wanted to get your drink of before or after the show. Looking forward to more shows here!

I loved "Legends Corner"! It was nice to walk into a bar and hear country music in the heart of Nashville of course. Loved the energy, the bartenders were fairly quick at getting everyone's drinks which was pretty awesome given that the bar had been pretty packed and busy for the most part. The bar itself is super chill and laid back for sure. Loved spending my first night in Nashville with you guys!

Probably the first honky-tonk that many people in Nashville go to. Has a somewhat modern selection of country music, and has an older clientele (mostly age 40+) compared with many other places on Broadway. Patrons here some quite friendly and were having fun with the music. Unlike Tootsie's there is room to move around on the main floor. Drinks are somewhat expensive, as is the case for most places on Broadway.  Had some of the better music on Broadway though. Not the best on Broadway, but a good time if you don't know what the other places are like.

I don't think i fully understood or appreciated the fact that I was going to a performance at Ryman Auditorium. Arriving early and getting an opportunity to walk around the outside and start to take in some of the historical markers.....Birth of Bluegrass for starters. Going on to explain that in 1945 Bill Monroe and his mandolin brought to the Ryman Auditorium stage a band that created a new American musical form. As you start absorbing everything that has happened here the realization sets in that this is going to truly be a unique experience at one of the most historical venues.

As you walk in there is an amazing gift store with all kinds of commemorative items to satisfy almost any collectors souvenir needs. 

The staff was phenomenal and eager to help any way they could. From the aisle attendants to the bartenders to the souvenir stands they all were happy and smiling throughout the night.

As Paramore took the stage to close out their tour in their hometown and Haley Williams leaned down to kiss the stage before performing, it became very evident that this place is also very special to the performers that come through. 

I had a seat in the upper balcony, and couldn't have been more pleased. I think it's safe to say there isn't a bad seat in the place! Sound quality is amazing and the stage is plenty large enough to accommodate elaborate band set ups.

So glad that I was able to finally come to Ryman and attend such an amazing performance. Wouldn't hesitate to come back and attend another event in the future. If you haven't been you really need to add this to a list of musts....it's something that should be experienced by everyone!

A must see in Nashville! Amazing live music...the band was so good I almost converted to country music :) great decor also...boots showcased on one side of the wall and country music memorabilia all over.  Best part of my trip to Nashville! I wanna come back for more and walk down Broadway to check out all the live music bars and venues!

Classic honky tonk. If you like old school country music - think George Jones and Buck Owens - hit this spot late night. The house band is really fantastic and knows about any paid request you put in to them. Dance your heart out with anyone nearby - know 'em or not. Great service you won't go thirsty. Good bar food. 

Oh, and be sure to tip the band as well as your server! Nashville is a no cover town. Tips are how they make a living providing great country music entertainment.

Yes, the Ryman is historic. Yes, it has hosted many many musical legends. Yes, the place offers a lovely aesthetic that many other musical venues in Nashville hold, but despite all this, I wasn't crazily impressed by it. 

From the perspective of a concert goer, I felt the way they have us congregating into the place is a bit disorienting. There were no defined lines. The person checking purses did not do a thorough job of inspecting them. They do have a metal detector, but I just didn't feel the security of the place was very strong. That makes me nervous when going into large scale venues in this day and age. 

Again, this is just personal preference, but the pews inside are painful to sit in for long extended periods of time. I value the originality to maintain the integrity of the venue and being that it is what came with the Ryman when it was first established. As someone who loves historical architecture, I value this very much! But, my back wasn't having it at all and it really sucked sitting there for 2.5 hours. Take an anti-inflammatory before you roll in there if you also have back issues. The entire venue has pews for seating. When the Ryman was first built, it was created as a tabernacle. 

Expect price gouging. A soda or bottled water will run you $5. Sorry, but not sorry and no thanks. I am cheap when it comes to that I guess. I just can't justify it in my mind. 

Parking around the venue is rough $10-$20 in parking garages or paved lots. I parked a few blocks away in a free spot and walked in the cold wet rain to get there. I just wasn't going to do that. Next time, I will likely uber and save myself the pain altogether, but at the time this seemed the most practical. 

On an ending note, the Ryman really is a pretty place. It is a historic relic to downtown Nashville and has cemented itself into the fabric of the music scene of the city. I value it for its history and integrity, not practicality.

horrible service. literally stood in front of a male bartender as he served at least 4 men before finally asking for my order. and the 3 of the men had just walked up. the area where you stand to listen to the band/dance is SO small. the indianapolis location is better!

The Ryman Auditorium is filled with a tremendous amount of history. I was honored to be able to have the opportunity to see Norah Jones, one my favorite artist perform here.

They are on point with their security check in process. Safety is very important in Nashville. 

In case you didn't know, the Ryman Auditorium used to  be a church and is located right in the heart of broadway/downtown Nashville. 

Our seats were 10 rows from the stage. Ryman has a very intimate settings. Honestly it doesn't matter where you are seated, the view and experience will be satisfying. 

Considering the Ryman used to be a church that means the seats would be benches and that can be an issue with some people who aren't used to this type of seating. Just be mindful and wear comfortable clothing to protect your cushion :-)

Remember the concert usually last for three hours. 

Overall I had a beautiful experience and was extremely moved and pleased with Norah Jone's performance.

We love coming to Plaza Mariachi with friends to enjoy the music, atmosphere, and the food.  Our one gripe is the price of the alcohol.  My friends ordered two shots of tequila, and almost fainted when the waitress said $26.  Of course, they paid as requested, but it sure put a bad taste in their mouth for ordering alcohol while enjoying the other things offered at this wonderful venue.

Best bar on Broadway!  Make sure Slick Joe Fick is playing, he's the show!!!  Great bologna sandwich too!  Drink prices are the same as the other bars -- high -- considering the bar isn't paying the band, they work for tops.  Kind of a sweet deal for the bar owners!  Regardless, it's a great place with great music!!!

Sure, this is where the Grand Ole Opry started and where many country acts play, but for any music lover this is iconic - over 100 years old and the seats are still pews (it was a church).

The tour through the Ryman is an experience you don't want to miss if you are at all interested in Country Music. The history of the building, even the stage posters of the folks who have performed there are fascinating. You can get onstage for a picture for a price. You go back stage and see where the stars get ready to perform. 

All in all, I must say our "Ryman Experience" was 100% positive. The church pews lend to the air of intimacy- after all you are side by side with your neighbors on left and right, and very close to those behind and in front of you.

OMG. Such good food! Kinda pricey but totally worth it! My son and I were starving and had nachos, steak tacos, chicken tacos (we both liked the steak better but they ran out), and burritos. After he ate, my son enjoyed the arcade. I enjoyed the live music while he played. Awesome family atmosphere, and great adult fun at night. There were dessert and gyro vendors too, although we didn't try them yet; too full off the Mexican food!!! They also had some shoppes where you could buy trinkets and t-shirts, etc. Way better than the Kroger that used to be in this retail space!!! We live close and will be back!

I have been to legends corner a few times. This is the smaller less crowded version of the actual legends bar on the road. The bar is located off of Main Street and it does have two entrances. One entrance is on main street and the other is on the side street. There are two levels in the venue and upper level and a lower level. If you go into the main entrance you will be in on the first level. If you enter down the side street you will end up on the second level automatically. They do have bouncers at both doors and they will stamp you. 

I do prefer The upstairs over the downstairs. The bar is a lot less crowded you can actually have Conversation with the bartenders without having to scream at the top your lungs are point to what you want. There is a jukebox in a lot of really cool guitars on the wall. 

Legends corner is a good place to drink I've never gotten anything eat here but I have purchased a good amount of drinks. They do charge five dollars for pretty much every standard bottled beer.  They have a full bar drinks are a little bit more expensive here than some of the other venues so do you have buckets of beer. They have a happy hour and of course live music.
