Just remember that this place only plays country music.  

Overall legends corner is a smaller less crowded version of the actual legends down the street it's a good place to come and get a drink and stare at all the cool guitars and artwork on the walls.

On a recent trip to Nashville we were looking for a good Honky Tonk to bring kids to in the afternoon. Robert's Western World was perfect. It had a different feel than many of the shinier bars lining Broadway.

John Shepherd, who has been performing for decades, was on stage taking requests, with encyclopedia knowledge of country music. We sat next to his wife Lois, and enjoyed the show.

Beer is cheap, and the food is surprisingly good. I had the recession special, including a fried bologna sandwich. The sandwich was actually really good. 

I would come back, just a comfortable classic atmosphere.

Of all the places I hit up on Broadway, Tin Roof was my least favorite.  

At risk of sounding like an old lady, this place was just too loud.  The band was both bad and deafening when we went on a Friday afternoon.  We opted for the bar upstairs in order to avoid losing hearing at a premature age.

Once we got upstairs, the service pretty much sucked.  I'm not sure if the bartenders were in between shifts or ours was just plain disinterested.  At any rate, getting our beers from him proved to be a lackluster experience.

The one pro for Tin Roof was surprisingly the food.  The pork nachos were very solid bar food.  You can't really mess that up I suppose, and after hitting up several other honky tonks before, they were just what the doctor ordered.

Tin Roof wasn't the worst bar I've ever been to by any means, but it was definitely my least favorite of the honky tonks I visited on Broadway.

Wow what a place. Went to the Grand Ole Opry at the Ryman and loved every min of it. Sat in the upper part dead center. Great seats. The music was just what i thought it would be. Its so cool being there and soaking in the history of the building. If you have a chance go while at the Ryman. Little Jimmy Dickens came on and had the eveyone rolling in the floor. He's a funny guy.

visited in Nov 2011

Very busy, slow service and average burgers. Great music and party environment. The entertainment is more of a reason to visit than the food. Amazing people and if you just want to have a few drinks with friends and experience true Honky Tonk Nashville then this is the place.

If you truly want to experience Nashville, this spot is pure gold! My companion and I stopped in for all of 20 minutes prior to heading to a concert at The Ryman and it was overwhelmingly my favorite part of the whole evening. (And that's saying a lot). We had already eaten at some utterly forgettable tourist-trap restaurant down the street (take a look at my other reviews if you're curious to see which one), and I would've given my kneecaps to have sidled up to the bar and ordered an anything-but-fancy burger and a beer here instead, if for no other reason than to soak up the atmosphere. The music was some of the best live music I've ever heard (and it was a Wednesday night!) and the ambience is unbeatable. It's a dive, but a dive with some serious soul! It will be a "must" for any pilgrimages to Music City I make in the future.

I feel like the Ryman and Opry are a must see for any country music fan visiting Nashville.

The Ryman is smaller and has less comfortable seats than the Opry. But the smaller venue makes it feel like a more intimate show.

I was lucky enough to see Vince Gill in the Bluegrass series on my first ever visit to the Ryman. He put on a phenomenal show.

I was unlucky enough to be sitting behind a tall guy with a broad frame...glad my husband didn't mind me invading his space because I was really excited to see Vince.

It's a great experience, beautiful building, fun atmosphere. Worth your time and money.

Would have loved to tour it but they weren't offering any guided tours on the weekend we visited. You don't get as much from the self guided tour plus Nashville requires a lot of walking and we were pooped.

This is fantastic venue..... historic, intimate, great acoustics, lots of reasons to come here. But I gave Ryman 1 star to get their attention and possibly spare others from the same angst we had. 

We travelled 500 miles to Nashville to see Ringo and His All Star Band for nostalgia. We were stunned by the unexpected exceptional musicianship. These aging top notch performers haven't lost their touch and are still incredibly at the top of their game!!! I'm in my 60's and this was the best concert I was ever at!!!  

The reason for the 1 star..... my companion forget the tickets she bought on stubhub. Though we had photos showing the barcode in our phones, we tried to avoid a potential situation by calling the theater and even going there in person prior to the concert to ensure they would let us in. We repeatedly offered to leave should anyone else claim our seats (of course that couldn't happen unless the stubhub seller scammed us). The Ryman staff was downright unhelpful and insisted that we had have the stubhub tickets physically in our hands to get into the theater. This soured my companion's mood for the day as they could easily have made this a non-event. As it turned out, we got in line at show time, showed the scanned tickets on our phones and went right in without a getting any attention. 

Shame on you Ryman there was no reason to treat us this way!!!

This is a great meeting space. The parking garages are vast and the spaces aren't smushed on top of each other.. well, most of them anyway. I have attended several events here and have always been pleased with the organization and execution. The surrounding hotel rooms seem to multiply daily! The Omni is the closest. But the massive Residence Inn is nearly completed. There are many restaurants within walking distance.  It's also an easy walk to the Honkey Tonks. If you are attending a meeting here from out of town, you will not need car! Check out the concert schedule at the Ryman or the Bridgestone, because you will be right next to them. 
My favorite feature is the architectural design. Take a look! It is shaped like a guitar. I love it when builders get clever ;)

Here in Music City we are richly blessed with an over abundance of fine restaurants, but just as people mistakenly think of Nashville's music scene as Country, it would be similarly egregious to overlook the wonderful ethnic eating experiences on offer by focusing solely on the fine dining establishments. 
Plaza Mariachi promises to make a party from an evening of casual dining. 
The moment we arrived live music was playing throughout the parking lot from the stage inside hosting Songwriters Night. 
Stepping into this converted grocery store you're virtually transported to a cozy village square with cafe hemming it's edges much more so than a food court. 
They're still filling in a number of the mall shops with tenants but you can already tell from the early entrants that they're committed to making your visit an enjoyable one. 
I'm looking forward to my next trip back there to pick up some special items from the MazFresco Market & you have to stop by Paletas Tocumbo for some of their homemade ice creams, just be sure to leave some Coconut for me.

I would give no stars if I could! We were there last week and they had NO WORKING BATHROOMS and people were still going in the bathrooms and the men were using the women's because the men's was horrible!! The staff was told and shrugged it off and said the manager was notified and not doing anything about it. I can't believe in such a touristy area they would allow such filth and unsanitary conditions .

Great food and amazing customer services.  The restaurant's atmosphere was very classy and the music performance was beautiful with a mixture of Blues and Jazz. We ordered a lot of food and drinks. The Scallop dish and the shrimp/crab dip were amazing! Their drinks were on point and we ordered two rounds of drinks which doesn't happen often. The only downside was some of the shrimps were slightly overcooked. Even so, our server and manager were very attentive and they didn't charge us for the specific dish. Their desserts were delicious! I highly recommended this restaurant and we will come back again!

I came here on a Saturday night around 7:30 pm and it was packed. We couldn't find a seat, but were able to stand around and chat. They environment was super fun. They had live music, dancers and salsa lessons. 

The interior of this place is super cute. It's basically a latin mall, with a bunch of different stores and restaurants. They have carts that sell margaritas and a big dance floor. The salsa lessons were free and lasted for about an hour. And then it turned into an open dancing floor. There were all types of ages, but I imagine as it gets later the kids go away. 

Overall liked the place, and I'll be back.

Aside from the overtly dilapidated building itself, this place has the most ridiculous, rude, and invasive "security" staff I've ever seen. 

I'm fine if they require bag checks... but this woman pulled out my medication and required me to provide identification to PROVE that it was my prescription. Which, is an absolute violation of privacy.

I understand a bag search for weapons, but the fact that my medication was scrutinized illegally, yet my friend's bag containing A KNIFE passed thru without a problem seems extraordinarily backwards and counter productive. 

Also, she was extremely rude. Also, IT WAS 100% MY PRESCRIPTION, OF COURSE. 

SCREW THIS VENUE... ILL NEVER GO BACK.

Ryman Auditorium is a beautiful theater right in the thick of things, right off of Broadway. It started as a church in 1885 and is still called "The Mother Church" by those from near & far.

After a renovation a couple of years ago, they now have a little cafe connected to the building, a big box office & gift shop plus a new area for the tours they do. I'd love to come back for a tour at some point. 

The night I went, all my dreams came true as I saw Andy Cohen, a man I love and adore, along with one of his besties Anderson Cooper. The show brought me to tears (literally. i have problems.) but the venue was pretty magnificent, as well.

Ryman wasn't quite as a big as I envisioned and that actually made it seem like a very intimate environment for a show. Google tells me it seats 2,362 which is surprising because it felt like there was just 500 people! haha I had to google Grand Ol Opry because that felt way bigger to me and that seats 4,400. 

I feel like most seats on the main floor are fairly good however there are a bunch of pillars and one such pillar was right in my view-line. That kind of sucked and I wish I would have known so I booked a different seat. 

Ryman itself is a gorgeous place though! Lovely venue and every worker I encountered was pretty friendly. I was also impressed with their local draft beer selections. They had a good variety and prices weren't too inflated for a music venue. Bravo!

I would definitely see future shows at the Ryman!

I absolutely love the Mother Church of Country Music! This is my third visit to the Ryman, and each time, I am more in awe. The acoustics in the building are absolutely amazing! Since this was previously a church, you sit on church pews, which isn't the most comfortable, but the music certainly makes up for it. If you are in Nashville, I would recommend going to a concert in the Ryman.
Amazing place to visit. It was more than the Grand Ole Opry to us. The history and back stage tour far surpass the GoO. If you get a chance take this tour while in Nashville.

Singers on Monday Oct 17 was ok... birthday boy was the keyboard player.
Drinks were skimpy and watered down!
Not a good idea if you want to keep customers and no one ever came to tables to see if we wanted anything.

Walking on Broadway can be an overwhelming experience. You wonder which honky tonk or bar is the one worth visiting? Some are full, some are empty, do you go where the crowd is, or are the underrated ones the best kept secret?

Thankfully I did my research, and was recommended Robert's Western World through a few different sources. Mainly, because of its history which I can't quite remember the details of, but one feature I read about was back in the day you could order cowboy boots at the bar!

While it wasn't particularly an out of this world evening, it was in my opinion, the quintessential honky tonk experience and something you'll be glad you did. I really enjoyed the live band playing old country music and seeing what I assume were real life cowboys. 

After that stop of the night, I didn't feel like I needed to go to any other place off Broadway.

do not go here...I
. repeat do not go here. The bartender on the roof top floor was very disrespectful and had vulgar language and an attitude when I asked for for service after waiting 15 minutes. when I approached management for the bad service they did not apologize but simple asked me to go to another part of the bar for service and pointed me to a server on another level. I felt as my business was not appreciated and not welcomed. I left after the verbal abuse and continued down Broadway and had a great time, if you have a choice please skip this bar and enjoy yourself among the other great establishments.

Robert's is right in the midst of the Broadway party chaos. You probably won't get a seat, the dance floor is small and close to the door, and the drinks are expensive. 

However, it has a nice vibe to it, and the house band is fantastic. 

Saw Reese Witherspoon there the other night.

I did a self-guided tour which was informative and fun. First you get to see a 10min film which was great. Then you walk around the theatre to see displays and videos filmed with famous people talking about history of Ryman. Price is a bit high given how small the place is but I enjoyed learning all the histories about Tom Ryman and Sam Jones, Lula(I admire her intelligence and toughness), and the renovation.
Legends is a must see spot in Nashville! It's a tight space like many others with good drinks and live music. You can't miss it!

I only came here for a tour and not a show, but I loved it. Tip, they have a AAA discount, so don't forget to use it. 

The very best part of the tour is the interactive movie and I loved every second of it. It kept my attention and left me wanting to learn even more about the Ryman. While I was visiting, they were setting up for their New Years Eve show and there was a lot of hustle and bustle on the stage. I enjoyed seeing how they pull everything together and thought that was an extra special perk. 

I loved touring such a legendary place and I vowed to return next time and to see a show. 

There are endless picture opportunities and people were taking thousands of selfies. No pictures were off limits, except during the movie. 

In total, I spent about 1.5 hours here, but I could have easily spent more time.

I haven't been to a Sambuca in years.  Went to celebrate 3 birthdays, mine, my mom's, and my sister's.  We had a great time.  My sister and I started with the shrimp and crab bisque.  It didn't come out as hot as we would have liked hit it was very flavorful.  My husband is vegan so they were very accommodating for him.  Our waiter was amazing! He went over and beyond. Everyone enjoyed their meal.  It will not be years before I return back.

This place is a joke. I don't understand how it has so many positive ratings. I booked a reservation on OpenTable based on the positive reviews here and there. The band that played was onstage maybe 20 minutes of my dining experience (I arrived at 7 pm, not a tall ask at that time), the service was atrocious, and the portions were laughably small. If your portion size is small, I better at least think it was the best few bites of food I've ever put in my mouth. 

They care more about presentation and aesthetic than the food itself. Save your money, please go somewhere else.

It's hard to specifically nail down what is being reviewed at Plaza Mariachi since it only contains the businesses.  What is obvious though is that a great deal of care has gone into creating a fun environment very reminiscent of what you might find at Epcot in Florida.

They generally have a Mariachi band playing, and one of the time they had a show with women and rings of fire. I don't know what this act was called, but it was hot (Ba-dum tish).

I highly recommend it to anyone who is curious. There is almost certainly something here to suit your fancy

If you are anywhere close to this place you are doing yourself a disservice by not coming in. The food. The ambience. The staff. The Music. I'm a Worldly traveler and believe u me this is a top notch place on my List.

Absolutely a great place to tour, we took the self guided tour & could not have been happier. The staff are extremely helpful & it was a dream come true to stand on the stage. 

It is about a hour & a half to see the site including the initial video which is very informative. The costumes, photography's & atmosphere make it a must see when you are in Nashville.

Entertainment was a joke. This guy has been singing to his wife sitting in a booth since approx 1974. One waitress for the entire restaurant and entire bar. She was nice enough but completely frazzled. Cheapest PBR we found on Broadway tho. Reg cans for $2.50. Watched several bologna sandwiches and burgers being made on the grill. Did not look appetizing at all. Quickly finished our beer and left.

We went here just to check the place out. 
Not too bad. Nice set up, friendly staff. 
We didn't buy anything, but we did take a look at some of their merchandise. Lots of cool boots and clothing. A little pricey, but nice.

Was in Nashville for a business meeting and ended up having a team dinner here.  That was 13 people at 7:30pm.  The place is large enough to accommodate as there were a lot of large parties having dinner that night.  

As with every place in Nashville there was a live band playing...older band, but sounded great playing the 70's ad 80's. My back was to them so I could not watch, only had to try to talk over them.  

The food was good and the staff was fantastic.  

The only reason they are not getting 5 stars...the valet closes at 10pm so if you don't get your car by 10pm you have to pay a $30 overnight charge and you can't get your car until 5pm the next day.  I mention this as it caused our group to call it an early night and split up.  It would have been great if they would have mentioned this prior to dropping the car off. Especially since the parking garage was across the street as it turned out and I could have parked it myself.   Take a Ride Share program instead of driving yourself.

When yelp hands you lemons, the Nashville yelp community made lemonade for us!

Coming to Robert's with a million other amazing yelpers was hands down, no questions asked the BEST part of my Nashville experience. I loved talking to every single person I met! 

The bar itself is awesome too. Beers were very reasonably priced, and the live music was unreal. I wish I could import some of their sound in to DC! The staff was super nice, and for the most part it was pretty clean. 

I was worried the Broadway area would be a tourist trap much like Fisherman's Wharf is in San Francisco, but I was happy to be completely wrong. Really cool music poured out of every bar and people were just enjoying life. 

If you're from out of town, don't miss this place - you'll really enjoy it!

This was a cool place! I'm not a huge country music fan, but I do enjoy it. I liked most that you get a good history lesson and it's very cool that this place honors the past. I would certainly recommend this to all who visit Nashville.

The is a very nice restaurant. Feels classy and up scale. Very nice staff. Nice waiter. Low light. Live music. Located in the Gulch district Nashville. Cloth napkins. Moderate prices. Real glass glasses to drink water from. Pretty clean. Nice bathroom.

I paid a lot of money for 3rd row floor seats to see a concert and was greatly disappointed when security allowed 100 or more people from the back and the balcony to stand in front of me and block my view. At one point there were two woman sitting in the seats that I paid for. There were several complaints throughout the night and nothing was done by management or security. This venue ruined a great show. Also, the cleaning crew practically kicked us out of the venue less than 5 minutes after the show ended and were very rude. I will never see another show at this venue. I would rather pay to travel further distances to see the show in another city. Not honoring or respecting the seats that customers paid for is unacceptable.

Show was great. Attendants were rude upon leaving. As we saw the exit door was headed directly outside we headed for a different door to use the restroom and were told no re-entering. We never left! The two women said to go to a nearby cafe. Disappointing as the tickets were pricey.

I never like giving a poor review, but there are so many fantastic options in Nashville and in the Gulch area.  We went here for a date night to celebrate our anniversary and I was underwhelmed. 
If you want to dine here, make a reservation.  We made reservations a month in advance and still had to wait about 30 min.  We didn't complain, just ordered a drink in the bar area and enjoyed.  
Our first negative was our server.  You could tell that she was disappointed that we ordered drinks at the bar vs at our table.  Servers can truly make or break a restaurant experience.  The meal prices were high, but expected with this restaurant.  I loved my husband's snapper and would get that again (rated 5/5).  However, I wouldn't order my scallop entree again (2/5). 
This restaurant has live music and the band was great, but the volume was extremely loud to have dinner conversations.  I assume they want the music to carry throughout the bar area and second floor seating, but for the tables in the front, it was too much.  We were seated in the front, and it felt like we were trying to eat at a concert or in a club.  
If you are looking for a fun place to hang out in the Gulch, I'd recommend getting drinks in the bar area and enjoying the music, but I'd grab dinner elsewhere.

Yelpers you let me down. That is really unusual but this place was walk out bad and y'all rate so high.... Why???? 

Picture this come in off the plane looking for all broadway has to offer. I go to Yelp (of course) and find this. My wife has that look on her face like "I don't know john" but we are pretty excited so we go in and sit down. And wait 

And wait and wait... Mind you only like 5 patrons in the place. So I get up and go to the bar cook on the grill says someone will be right with you. I'm checking out the menu I guess they are famous for a baloney sandwich and have hot dogs burgers etc with lays chips. 

Back to the story... I wait and wait and wait. 

I almost never do this but I tell my wife lets go. We went to another place with just as much nostalgia and got served right away. 

Music was cool; you can expect that in Nashville on Broadway where many places have like 3 bands. Yes sure I bet they have lots of history there but it looks like it's kind of dirty too.

Food. I don't think baloney sandwich, hot dogs and burgers with lays chips is ever an event! Now I like a good burger as much as anyone else but by the looks of it this would not have been one of those "oh my god" burgers. Not all calories are created equal so make em count!!!

I had never been to Nashville and decided to make Robert's my first stop on Broadway. The food was cheap, the music was loud and fun, and the place was packed despite it only being 3pm on a Thursday. After hopping around to other places on the strip, this place had a more dive bar feel that I vibe with while the others felt more upscale. I imagine Robert's hasn't changed much since they opened and that this is what Nashville felt like decades ago. Definitely a must stop and a great value. I had the mushroom and swiss burger with chips and my wife got the "Recession Special" (fried bologna sandwich, chips, a PBR, and a Moon Pie). Our total was like $12 which is insane to me considering you're downtown in this area. Keeping prices reasonable encourages crowds to show up and makes it easy to be generous throwing money into the tip jug for the band.

What an amazing place!! The history of it all sends chills up my spine!  Love that you can take your time looking at everything you want to at your own pace.  The downfall is parking.  Really hard to find somewhere to park and there is no designated handicap parking??!!!

So this is what they call a "honky tonk."

We caught the tail end of the set of what I can only assume is the Nashville's equivalent of a boy band (the man on bass had one of the most impressive beards I've ever seen). And they were not half bad.

We witnessed a pint-sized girl pour a full beer on, spit on, and then slap a very large gentleman who was exhibiting remarkable restraint.

We made friends with some nice ladies, and then ran away from their massive cowboy man friends.

We had many drinks for not that many monies.

And it was good.

I took my husband here a few years ago for his birthday and we had such an amazing experience! Boy how times have changed....and not for the better. 
He surprised me for our anniversary tonight and took me here for dinner....let's just say that after a few cocktails ( that we're made incorrectly each time....not hard... bourbon neat and a vodka martini each round) and two terrible appetizers we left. The prosciutto was sliced so thick it looked like country ham....not to mention everything else wrong with their "charcuterie board"! Their satay was like chewing on a rawhide....at least from what I have seen from my dogs. 
When I slid into the booth my finger nails were filled with crumbs of who knows what from the cracked pleather seats....not to mention the throw pillow that was stained and had chunks of food on it. Never again! This used to be a very cool place with a sultry romantic vibe with great food.
Sitting in the lot for over an hour and now have to try to follow the direction of ONE person. Poor lady.

Among our stops while on Broadway was Roberts. I was relatively sober here....relatively being the optimal word

~The Good~
This place gets slammed harder than...well you take it from there on that one. It is a much smaller space that its neighbor Tootsies off to the side. It has two floors, both of which serve, and allows for passerby to congregate listening to jams. Drinks were decently priced out. I had a couple shots to get my night going and it was actually a tad cheaper here compared to other spots. The space up top allows for you to exit, as well as re-enter, rather than using the upfront line. This is helpful when all the tourists start flocking in. Music was loud but not to the point where I am screaming, which was nice. Overall a fun little spot... Oh oh, and NO COVER!

~The Bad~
It's just so small! I was elbowing people, people were elbowing me...even my shot glass was elbowing a beer bottle. Maybe that adds to the flavor of this spot.. not sure. Really small and cramped space led for a relatively quick exit for my gang after about 45 minutes of messing around. The music was also not as strong...I love most music, but old-school style country music in a bar seemed a bit off for a Friday night. Wasn't really amping me up like Tootsies louder bands did. 

~The Downlow~
This is a fun, albeit smaller bar on Broadway. Still, drinks are priced well, no one wanted to deck me for dancing like a fool, the atmosphere was still pretty chill and heck... NO COVER on a Friday night. Overall that adds up to 4 stars. Perhaps if the band was a bit better I'd bump it... Maybe next time Nashville ;-)

My girlfriends and I spent the weekend in Nashville for my bachelorette and we wanted to go to at least one really nice restaurant while we were there. Sambuca did not disappoint! Our server was absolutely amazing. (Shout out Emerson! Thanks for everything) He took the time to explain the menu and all of the drinks. I had two cocktails: The Cock 'N Bull which is their take on a Moscow Mule, and a Royal Basil lemonade. Both amazing. My friend and I split the chili rubbed jumbo scallops and the salmon oscar with brussels. Both were incredible. Perfectly cooked seafood and seasonings. The crispy rice cakes under the scallops were also a nice touch. They also surprised me with an announcement from the band with my wedding date and an amazing flourless chocolate cake with a candle for dessert. The live music was wonderful. I couldn't have had a better experience at this establishment. I've already recommended to a few of my coworkers heading to Nashville next week!

Great center with delicious food court and in my opinion the best live music in Nashville!! The 5 person mariachi band is excellent -- better than the ones I've heard in California. They've definitely made me appreciate Mexican music that I've previously taken for granted and never really noticed. And the stage is impressively well displayed/built. 

We loved tasting the various Spanish/Mexican-influenced cuisine in the food court. Unfortunately we didn't love the churros at the "Hot Churros" booth (because as Californians we're forever spoiled by Disneyland churros). 

The atmosphere and decor all create a really nice cultural vibe that's refreshing to find in Tennessee. Also, every employee here is so friendly & courteous. 

Worth checking out! Especially if you're tired of hot chicken or the crappy inauthentic Mexican food in Nashville!

Serious such a wonderful place, it's a hidden Gem that much people doesn't seem to know about. I love the food court the food is 10x better than the food court at the mall.

I'm honestly not a fan of the regular " stores " that inside just because the prices are ridiculous. We stopped at one of the stores that sold beautiful evening dresses for special occasions and outing and we asked how much for one of the dress & she said $220. Trust me that was NOT worth $220 & it's not even a name brand you know. But anywhooo I just said thanks and kept on walking. 

Now back to the food. Worth it. It was from "Guachos" I think that how it's spelled. In one of the order with the fried steak they brought it and it had a huge slice of ham & I don't eat pork so I went back and told them & they fairly told the chef about it and he said he would change it and make a new one, but honestly I was paranoid that he was going to give me back the same steak and he was only going to take the pork off so I stood and watched and he told me not to be worried that he threw the whole meal away and I didn't believe until he went and get the garbage can to show me & with all this he was smiling and being kind apologizing & I was so happy to be recovering that energy. 
 Well we enjoyed everything and I left a nice tip for them. I will definitely be going back. Also the gyro spot is very affordable & their fried Wings are the Bomb !!!!

My wife and I were on a week vacation to Nashville, in what was the coldest week they had seen in a decade. This is why we came here in January!!! But I digress. It was New Year's Day and a lot of the places on the main drag were closed, but Robert's looked fun when we went in.

Dave Cox was the band, he plays covers of old country hits, really good. They all play for tips here, so I bought his CD for $10 and thought the hour we spent there listening to him play was well worth 10 bucks for 2 people.

Kind of a narrow place, but an old time bar. No draft beer, which is my only fault, but the waitress was nice and the prices for a Bud were reasonable. The food looked like regular bar food, but we didn't try any.

If you like old country hits (Nelson, Cash, etc....) Check this place out!
This place was great, the bartenders were a lot of fun and had great recommendations

Worst staff we have ever encountered. Patilyn that works there doesnt do anything except stand around and then says after my husband exited to the gift shop that he couldnt reenter. She saw him go through and didnt say to him he couldnt get back in. He wanted a shirt from the show. We had paid tickets as proof that we attended. SHE SAW HIM GO THROUGH! there are no signs that say that you cant reenter. Patilyn was supposed to be doing her job and telling people that they couldnt reenter. Yet she didnt. Then called security to kick everyone out. Rude and nasty employee.  Contacted the ryman 4 times. 3 through email and once through phone. No answer on anything yet.
I love this place!!!  Great spot for dinner or even just drinks and live music.  When I'm in Nashville, this is where I go for guaranteed enjoyable time.

I LOVE this place! So much so that I went twice in one weekend!

My husband, four year old daughter, and I decided to give this place a try on a Friday night (then revisited on a Sunday morning).  It was a cold night and we decided to venture away from our usuals.  Upon entering Plaza Mariachi we were pleasantly surprised!  First of all this place looks great!  It has the feel of a Mexican marketplace with authentic stores, food, kids area, bar, grocery store, and even a radio station.  

On our first visit I decided to eat grab food from Tres Gauchos which is listed as an Argentinean steakhouse.  This restaurant is located in the "food court" but don't let that fool you the food is very high quality.  I knew this place must be good because the line was long.  I placed and order for the flank steak with a side of Mexican street corn.  My husband decided on Chisme Cafe and ordered nachos and street tacos which he enjoyed.  Everything was delicious and my daughter danced to the Mariachi band while we ate.  After dinner we went and grabbed a Margarita at the bar and headed to the play area.  My daughter was highly entertained by the large play structure and we were entertained drinking our margaritas watching. Upon leaving we stopped at Botanas Lokas and grabbed some delicious churros!

Sometimes living in Nashville I feel like there is not much to do for families.  I am so happy to have found Plaza Mariachi.  It is an amazing place that I will be visiting again very soon.

My review specifically goes to my overall experience here. Our waiter was the best waiter I have ever had! He was so funny and helpful when it came to deciding what we wanted! It was my friends birthday and he definitely made it special! I would suggest you go here if you want a calm/fun nice dinner! Plus the wine selection is awesome. **The food does come in smaller portions.

We couldn't visit Nashville without seeing a show at the iconic Ryman Auditorium. Located right in downtown it's super easy to get to as a visitor to the city. We saw Penny & Sparrow and Drew Holcomb and the Neighbors and had an amazing time! The venue itself is smaller and more intimate and the performers were very personable. When they would break from the music and talk to the audience it was really engaging and not something that would work as well in a huge stadium. The energy of the audience was also something special. My only complaint is the wooden bench seats start to get pretty uncomfortable after a while. We ended up standing in the back to finish off the show, which turned out to be great because I could move to the music!

My husband and I went in on a Wednesday night...which Sambuca says has a happy hour from 4:30-6:30. We had reservations and had a nice spot right next to the kitchen (sarcasm because there was NO ONE HERE) and could hear the band warming up. When we asked about the "happy hour" we were told that only applies to the "Cocktail area." Are you kidding me?!?! The happy hour is displayed on their menu being served to me in the restaurant area. After inquiring about this, the waitress told us we could get the "happy hour" special only on our drinks, but not on the small plates and acted like this was doing us a favor. So by now we know that there is a happy hour which applies to drinks and small plates, but not to the restaurant area. What a joke! We walked out without ordering and we will NEVER come back here to this pretentious, expensive restaurant...and we didn't even try the food.

If you're going to go to one honky tonk in Nashville, it pretty much has to be Robert's Western World. Don't let the name fool you, it's not some shop full of cowboy boots and hats for purchase. No, no, it's a dive bar right on the NashVegas strip with live music, cheap beers and where fun times are abound!

Robert's encapsulates exactly what you'd want from your honky tonk experience with beers that aren't at overly inflated prices, good music and a nice upper area for big groups. Thanks to my fellow Yelpers for bringing me here in perhaps the biggest UYE I've ever attended.
Absolutely amazing place of musical history!!! Thank goodness they didn't tear this place down. A Southern treasure that should be seen by any music lover of any genre!

Good food, good service, good drinks... Came here on a Friday night in August and encountered no wait to sit outside on the patio. Our server was attentive and offered a great suggestion as I was in between the salmon and the scallops. I took his suggestion and did the scallops and was so pleased I did. The flavors of the scallops, the tomato sauce, and the seasoning used paired with the risotto cake was out of this world. I encourage you to visit The Gulch and Sambucas. Oh and did I mention the $5 valet?

There's a bouncer at the door checking ID, ensuring that you are 21. Friday & Saturday nights are the most popular and it's wall to wall inside. ....just like walking on the street. 

Seems like the music is pop rock as all the 21 year old girls in the audience know the words and sing along with the band.

The norm is no cover,  and beets are about $5. Male sure you tip the band when they pass their Buckley around!

Always a fun time, and you might actually hear some good music.

When it comes to reviews, I have three things that make up my ultimate 5 star rating. What brings my rating of 5 stars to Sambuca?  Well, ultimately it was the overall experience my party thoroughly enjoyed. This enjoyment is courtesy of your incredible server Molly. 

I found myself working in Nashville temporarily for 4 months, and some of my dining experiences were truly not up to par. When we sat down, I was coming off a rough work day and needed a lift. Molly arrived at our table with a smile and uplifting positive attitude. This was exactly what I needed. There is nothing worse than a server who seems like they despise their job. Having served before, I can appreciate and respect everything they have to deal with during a shift.  I informed her of the lousy day that had preceded us walking into your establishment, and that we wanted to have a couple of drinks to get the evening off to a better start. She suggested margaritas, and she was right. It made complete sense, of course margaritas inspire a fiesta in life. 

Molly's suggestions for dinner worked out perfectly too. I was in the mood for some seafood and her recommendation of the red snapper étouffée was just what I wanted.  

First part of the 5 star rating is atmosphere.  Second part was the food and beverage quality. The third part was customer service. Honestly, to me it is the largest contributor of the dining experience.  

I am not sure if your business recognizes its employees for its receipt of positive reviews, but if they do please recognize Molly for making it an experience for us, versus a simple dinner after work.  She is the primary reason I will refer business to Sambuca in the future. Thank you!
Great atmosphere, not ear blasting loud if you are in the back part of the bar. Had a wonderful time as the band was so engaging. Friendly bartenders and staff.

Went into Roberts to have lunch with my wife on March 27 and despite it not being very crowded sat at a table across from bar and 10 minutes went by without anyone in the place approaching our table. Finally a bartender comes from behind the bar and walks past us before my wife asks him "pardon me do you work here?" He responds with Do I work here? Yeah I work here! Can someone serve us we wanted to have lunch here. He responds with " if you want something to eat I guess you better go to the bar and find someone to take your order", and walks on past us. There are way too many bars on Broadway to get something to eat and for me to spend money money in to deal with this wise guy so we got up and left. Thing is a table of 5 next to us with a handicapped woman in a wheelchair tells us as we go that they had been sitting there for about 5 minutes before we got there and they hadn't had a soul help them either and also decided to leave. Can't imagine how much money walked out the door of this place from these rude ignorant employees. Never again folks!
Don't eat here if you want to stay past 2 hours for dinner. They will politely ask you to move to the bar. So disappointed!!! Won't return.

Hands down my favorite place in Downtown Nashville! I've been three times, each time a year apart, and it continues to be my fave. You can listen to fantastic country here and I'm not even a country music fan. The place is always packed with all ages but does tend to skew more toward the older crowd. The little dance floor in front of the elevated stage is usually full of all ages dancing and two stepping. The servers have probably worked there a long time and take care of their customers. It's filled with old memorabilia that looks legit. I like going to other popular places on the strip as well but this place is just different in a really good way that I hope does not ever change.
Legends Corner is a solid choice for a beer on Broadway.  They have live, interactive music and cold beer (they must keep it in a freezer or something).
Great music! Food was good and service by Brandon M was awesome! I would highly recommend.

Loved the ambiance and the live music. We had excellent service but the food could use a little more punch or flavor. I had the Sea Bass, it was cooked to perfection but the vegetables underneath were almost indistinguishable, almost muddled.  Our husbands had the pork chops , unfortunately they ordered them medium instead of Medium rare so although the taste was fine the cook of the meat made them tough. The Mac and cheese it came with was a bit dry and not enough cheese flavor. The bread pudding was over cooked on the edges making it too dry, the chocolate cake was the tables favorite, very good

Had a very nice evening(12/16).  What a way to celebrate with my employees and friends. Thank you so much service was fantastic.  If they would have me, I would definitely have another party there next Christmas.

Thanks Again,

Scott Baker
A must experience and concert experience. Love the history the, the vibes, the Holy Grail of Country Music. Concerts are fabulous, go when you're town a must see!
Did the tour today.  Very informative would recommend this to others touring Nashville.  Worth the time going

I absolutely adore Plaza Mariachi, and I hope Nashville as a city sponsors more cultural endeavors like it. My friends and I went on a Saturday during Dia de los Muertos this year. In the food court, there was a joyously raucous band, the well-known and well-loved Stephanie Urbina Jones and the Honky Tonk Mariachis. Stephanie made the whole food court feel like family as patrons swayed dancing to updated classics and children were serenaded by dedicated songs on stage. Afterwards, there was also a brilliant circus performance involving both fire and acrobatics. For an additional fee, patrons could enjoy a 9pm boxing match in the food court as well. This is certainly a hub of culture and the place to be on a weekend night.

In terms of the atmosphere, I felt like I was back in San Antonio. Patrons stroll through pueblo-esque small shops and a marketplace before entering the food court. While modest in size compared to similar Texan experiences, Plaza Mariachi is definitely a new Nashville landmark everyone should make time in their schedule to frequent.

The actual strip mall outside Plaza Mariachi hosts a slew of intriguing restaurants, like Win Bubble Tea and several other specialty dining experiences. I am personally partial to Taj Indian Cuisine where the owner also specializes in Indo-Chinese dishes on the menu. 

With a prime location amongst other dining experiences and a truly fantastic marketing/planning director, Plaza Mariachi is a must-see in Nashville.
Our server Matthew Was incredibly friendly until he realized that we were just ordering wine and appetizers and then his entire demeanor changed. He was short dismissive and borderline rude.

This is a really good little hide-away bar on Broadway. The frontage is deceiving since the building goes clear back to the alley. There is really quite a lot of room. And there is a second bar on the second floor so getting seated upstairs is not a problem.
The real surprise here is the food. They have some very interesting choices and the prices are extremely reasonable especially for a tourist location. We heard some really good things about their "fried baloney sandwich". I am not a real big fan of baloney, but we were strongly encouraged to try it by some fans of the establishment.
The music is a little milder than some of the groups on the row, but I would recommend musicians earplugs for those sensitive to loud music. I thought the mix was a touch off, way too little vocals and too much guitar, but to each his own.
Overall, this is a real gem. Delightful service and food with free entertainment. What else can you ask for? And if you come in with a holier-than-thou attitude, lose it before you come in. This is a good old fun county place!

I went here for the first time this past weekend. Had it in my list but hadnt had the chance. Was not disappointed! I had the blackened filet with the bacon sauteed green beans and the prosciutto mac and cheese-it was all amazing. I wanted the sticky bread pudding for dessert but it is a very popular choice so they were out. Ended up ordering the Sopapilla; it was really good. The portions were on point. Definitely going back.

The Don Kelley Band was fabulous. Joe Fick is SO good on the bass, and Luke McCreary is an incredible guitar player--and just 19, I think they said. 

We didn't eat here, but the food looked good. Decent beer selection.

We decided to walk around the Gulch one Saturday evening. I had never been and wanted to explore and try new places. We asked around and people suggested either Sambuca or Burger Republic. We ended up walking over to Sambuca.
We got lucky, we didn't realize you had to make a reservation. We sat at the last open table in the bar area. Place was packed and had live music. 
Once we sat down, it took a minute to get greeted; which was fine. Servers were very attentive once we got greeted. We ordered wine and beer and looked over our menus. Server suggested a couple items and helped me pick my dinner. I ended up getting the hickory smoked prime pork chop with prosciutto mac & cheese. Oh my gosh, it was DELICIOUS. My date got the  Filet over the bed of asparagus with an extra side of maple bourbon sweet potatoes. Neither plate disappointed. Everything was so good.I am typically not a fan of sweet potatoes, but I couldn't keep my fork out of them.
Our server kept checking on us and was so glad that we liked what she had suggested. We stayed and listened to some music after dinner.

If you haven't been, I suggest you do. AMAZING food and ambiance.

Whoever knows me knows that I'm the farthest thing from being a night crawler, but Robert's Western World sucked me in for a couple of hours last Thursday night! 

My friend and I made our first visits to Nashville, and Acme really wasn't cutting it for either of us. I wanted good ol' traditional country music, and I'm so glad that we checked out Robert's!! It has a great mix of younger and older customers, and I met quite a few people who were easy to make conversation with. I'm also not a dancer, but Brazilbilly and Nathan Belt got me dancing up front like mad until 1am.

It's not your typical dark honky tonk like many of the other places are on Broadway. The atmosphere is not pretentious at all, and while being someone who gets anxious in large party crowds, I can see myself hanging out there alone. People are nice, especially since it's not just groups of younger people, so don't be afraid to ask others if you can sit down next to them if there are open stools. Do yourself a favor and check out Robert's!!

Go. Doesn't matter who's playing. Just go. The Ryman is an American institution and if you have a chance to see anything or anyone play on that stage, do yourself a favor and just go. It is, in so many ways, a truly religious experience.

Great place for music, maybe not so much if you're hungry. Breakdown of my review. 

Atmosphere and music: 5/5
The music was amazing as this is part of Honky-Tonk "row" with Tootsies Orchid Lounge and others. The band was fantastic and really set the mood with skills and amazing showmanship. 
They got the crowd dancing and bobbing their heads every time they played.

Drinks: 4/5
Good drink specials and the service for drinks was pretty quick. PBR for $2.50 is pretty unbeatable. 

Food: 2/5
Took over 30 minutes for orders of sides to come up. And when they did, the chicken tenders were overlooked and dry, while the yucca fries were not died enough. The yam fries were okay but nothing spectacular.

My expectations may have been too high for this place. Great concept, poor execution. Took my boyfriend for his birthday. Showed up at reservation time but waited 15mins for our table even though the place was half empty. Gluten free options. Food was just fine nothing remarkable. Salads and salmon. They gave a free dessert for the birthday which was nice. Music was good not stellar but the band took a very long break which dampened the atmosphere.

The 4 out of 5 star review is based on The Broadway scale. I will admit, I only go to Broadway when I have visitors in town. It's hard to rate them on the same scale as other bars because it's obviously a very touristy place. Everyone knows that. So my expectations are real for this area. I surprisingly had never been into Tin Roof before. I usually pop into the well known bars and then my friends pick where they want to wander into. We heard some fun music coming from Tin Roof so we ventured in. I was digging the inside of this place. We were here on a Monday night so it wasn't packed. This is the best way to experience Broadway in my opinion. The weekends are a bit too crazy. I'm not sure if it's always like this but they had colorful Christmas lights hung up on the ceiling. It added some fun colors to a usually darker scene. What I really appreciated most about this place was the fact that they had drink specials. Broadway can be so overpriced because hey, they can. My friends were a little tired of paying $10 for basic rail drinks so when we saw a $5 rail special at Tin Roof, we were excited. We hit it, and we hit it hard. Maybe the deal was actually a little dangerous haha. We just ordered vodka sodas so they were as good as rail drinks can be. Served in a plastic cup but that's what you get on Broadway for obvious reasons. Glass + Broadway does not end well. We were able to get a table right up front and the music was what also kept us here. The band was really fun! They were doing a mash up of different pop hits from the 90s and early 2000s. A blast from the past! I'm not a country music fan (don't kick me out of Nashville!) so I appreciate when bars mix it up. I can't comment on the food because I would never really order food on Broadway, but they have it if you need a bite to eat. Overall, it was a fun experience and I will no longer pass by this place when on Broadway!
Really cramped but I liked the environment and live music. The guy on stage was kinda preachy though... and the food was just burgers and hot dogs. Nothing special.
Very authentic music in a pretty inauthentic stretch of bars.

It's the best place on Broadway.  BUT, it used to be better.  The Don Kelly band is the 6-10pm band wed-sat.  Don Kelly is a legend and surrounds himself by the best musicians anywhere.  His now stable side kick, joe flick is the best and most exciting bass player anywhere!  A must see and hear!  Always has a great drummer too.  He's also had the best guitar players.  Most recently Porter McClister played lead for Don Kelley.  McClister is the most talented creative guitar player anywhere!!!  However, the Don Kelly band shuffled musicians not too long ago and McClister is no longer with Kelly.  New drummer too.  Unfortunately, the Don Kelly band isn't what it used to be.  Good, worth seeing, but just not the same professional talent.

The house band from 10:30 - 2am can be great or not so great depending on the collection of musicians.  Don't miss sarah gayle meech when she plays, she's the real deal!  Eileen Rose is another must see, she's awesome!

Sambuca is one of my favorite place to go after work for happy hour. I'm normally in a small party of 3 or 4, but yesterday I went with a group of 22! I was not expecting them to be able to seat us together, but we were able to slide some couches and chairs together so that worked out well. 

I almost always choose the shrimp & crab dip. It's cheesy warm goodness with chips is exactly what I need to hold me over until dinner later. 

My new favorite drink is the Cock N Bull, which includes vodka, lime, and ginger. The ginger is what makes the drink so delicious so of course I got two! 

I've always had amazing service here and never had to wait long for food or drinks. There is also plenty of street or garage parking in the area which makes coming to this location a no brainer!

Super cool! The band playing there on Tuesday night played some old country classics like Hank Williams and Conway Twitty. I didn't like the food a whole lot but that is the atmosphere, it's not supposed to be 5 star dining! Very affordable food and drinks. They do only bottled beer, no drafts.

I have NOTHING bad to say about this place. Great atmosphere, great music, and great specials. We stumbled in here and got the recession special... $6 for a friend bologna sandwich, a bag of chips, a moon pie, and a PBR. You can't beat it! Normally I never would have tried a fried bologna sandwich but now I'm ready to try and recreate it at home.

Overall Nashville is a really fun town to visit but is getting really really expensive to go. Although it's on the Strip, Legends Corner Bar still seems like it's true to its history. The bar actually a little bigger than it looks it has an upstairs and a downstairs but they had a really great band playing and they took request as well but as we found out the next night when we went back it was the same set over and over again which is okay.

The bartenders were attentive and friendly even though it was getting pretty busy they seemed to enjoy their jobs and had fun. They were pretty quick I'm getting the beers out to you and it seemed they liked to serve the beers in six-pack form which pretty much is going to separate you from 40 bucks so it was still kind of pricey.

They had a lot of memorabilia up on the walls in the bathrooms did not seem nearly as run-down as you would expect them to be in a restaurant that gets his kind of volume. They had quite a staff of bouncers I think I counted six which was a lot for a Friday afternoon. However seeing as how we just got kicked out of tootsies maybe they had the right amount after all lol

This was one of my favorite stops during my week in Nashville! Great live music on every floor, and a great place to hang out. It WILL get crowded as the night goes on, so we got there a little earlier in the evening since we wanted stools

Truth be told, I was skeptical that this somewhat snobby LA girl was going to fare well in a honky tonk, After all, I've never owned cowgirl boots and only know a handful of mainstream country songs...Carrie Underwood, Keith Urban, and anything else that makes the LA radio waves....you get the picture.  Anyway, I walk into Roberts and I'm blown away, not only by the diverse crowd (age, gender, race) but by the super cool old school band that was playing!  Tons of people dancing (old and young and both really good).  The availability of seats and the super sweet waitress.  I went ahead and ordered two Recession specials, one for me and one for my boss, because I was being funny. ($5 for bologna sandwich, PBR and a bag of lays). Our waitress advised me to upgrade and add cheese and grilled onions, so I did just that.  I don't think my boss and I have ever scarfed down something so quickly!  That fried bologna sandwich was scrumptious!  The music was fabulous and the atmosphere was sheer fun for a Wednesday night.  
I know this side of Broadway is not the "cool" side, but it was a great time and when I come back, Robert's is on my radar!

Sambuca without a doubt has one of the best happy hours in Music City! My friend and I decided that we needed to try it based on the prices alone. Many of the happy hour cocktail prices are between $5-6 each. I had the Sambuca 75 for my first cocktail which was a mixture of vodka, champagne and a fruit puree. It wasn't too sweet which I liked. For my second cocktail I got the Tennessee mule which was also good and not overly sweet. My friend and I split the bruschetta which was a light appetizer with a tomato mixture and crostini. 

If I had to pinpoint the patrons here I'd say mostly a 40s and older crowd but the atmosphere is nice. There was live music which wasn't too loud and we could still have a conversation. The food and drink was all good, the atmosphere was pleasant and the service was excellent. The server knew her drinks and I liked her recommendations. 

I'm not sure if I'd come back here just simply because it wasn't exactly my type of scene but the happy hour is very very good!

This bar is still great 2 years later. 
Music and staff was on point.! 
And prices are good, good amount is seats and nice dance floor. No cover,great looking spot inside and out
Can't wait to go back on my next Nashville trip.!

It's a cool place to hang out, but the drinks are way over priced. I'm from Southern California, so I am familiar with overpriced drinks, but these are way too expensive for the pour that you get from the bartender. The atmosphere was fine, and the band on the night that we were there was really, really good. But at $24 for a bottled beer and a rum and coke, its a little unrealistic to remain there for any length of time and get your buzz on....

Just shy of being a dive bar (imo) I'm giving this place 5 stars for what it is. Awesome cheap food (grilled cheese, grilled bologna sandwiches, fries, etc.) 

We had a problem with our food being given to another table? And then not getting all of our fries, instead getting too many bags of chips. Their method has no madness to it with different servers bringing different things instead of a server to a table. But that doesn't really impede your experience if you have the time to wait, because they're more than willing to fix their mistakes and really nice about it! 

Live country music! I'd definitely hit this place again next time in Nashville!

This would be an absolutely brilliant place to go to lunch. Their recession special is a steal. Unfortunately it requires you either be unemployed or have an hour and a half lunch break and work right next door in order to obtain it when there are 21 other people in the place.

They will keep you in beers until your food heats up in the fryer, and there's generally a good musician playing, although you could luck out like I did on my last visit and have the epitomy of "guy just trying to make it i the music business" who would be charged with murder if any of the singers he was covering were still alive today.

Slow, music, good divey place. It's the sort of place you like to dislike, and like to prove your dislike by patronizing. Or something.

Probably my favorite place in Nashville just because they have cheap beer, old school country music and fried bologna sandwiches. 

The quality of the music is always off the hook. Simple place, but simply awesome.
Adam stone rocks! It's a bar. It looks and feels like a bar. The live music is awesome though! The service is slow, at least the blond is slow. The brunette is awesome!

A must stop on your Lower Broadway barhop.  Since there are tons of reviews about this place, here's my brief thoughts.

Free admission.

Decently strong drinks.

Cowboy boots on the wall, perhaps for sale?  I couldn't tell.

Always a good band, usually with a upright bass which is, of course, festive.  Tip the band - no admission so go ahead and give them some bucks so they can pay rent or buy some beer.

Totally packed out on the weekends but on weeknights much more manageable.  Plus if you are a tourist you don't have anything to do the next day right?  Drink up!

That's all you have to know.  Then you can stumble out and hit up another honky tonk.

This is the worst bar ever. My friends and I went here and we just turned 21, and the bouncers after a long while of us being in there kicked us out of the bar because they thought we were faking our age and thought our ID's were fake even though they were very much real and the bouncers thought we looked "too young" to be in there. I explained to the bouncer that what he said to us about looking too young even though we were of legal drinking age was "discriminating" and he kicked us out because he thought we were lying and because he got called out. He then towards the end proceeds to snatch out drinks away when we paid good money for them. I felt extremely disrespected and I'm very disappointed my friends and I were treated this way. Do not recommend and do not go here.

I walked in by myself on Sunday evening October 20th at approximately 8:48 p.m. the bar was full so I sat at a bar seat at a counter facing the stage to the left of the bar. I waited patiently as no one came to help me. Then 3 men sat down next to me; I saw a waitress motion to them they'd be right over. None came. They waited, got tired of waiting and left. For giggles I sat there to see how long I could go being ignored. It lasted at least 20 minutes from 8:49 p.m to 9:09 p.m. (probably a tad longer but I only started paying attention at 8:49).  At 20 minutes I finally went to the waitress station to ask if someone was actually assigned to serve that area. The two girls said yes and they'd send someone over.  I informed them that I'd been sitting there for 20 minutes being ignored and 3 other people had got up and left after being ignored. They looked dumbfounded and confused.  Good grief, pay attention people. It isn't that hard.  I can see from other reviews service is a major issue in this place.

A genuine Honky Tonk bar with live music and quick serving bar keeps. The cheese burger probably saved my night, as it's hailed as the best burger. It was good for the record. Music was great and the environment was fun. 

Visit this place if on the Boardwalk.
Great burgers and sweet potato fries! Live music playing all the time. We went for lunch, so good crowd...not sure if sorority scene comes at night. You don't want to miss this stop!

As a music lover, This has been a bucket list 'to do' for me. So finally on my trip to Nashville I made it happen. Unfortunately I did not have the opportunity to see a show, so I just did the tour. 

You have the option of the self guided tour, or a guided tour for extra $. As I said above, I have been waiting for this moment so of course I did the guided tour. I was looking forward to seeing the backstage areas (which is not included in the self guided tour). We head upstairs and head to some random dressing rooms. The 2 tour guides speak about some of the history of the building, the grand ole opry, some of the historical performers and their legacy. Where are the pictures you ask? Well for some unknown.... ridiculous reason... you are not allowed to take any pictures in the dressing rooms. Extremely disappointing.  We then leave the area and head downstairs into the auditorium itself where we again get given a bit more information about some things. All very interesting information, and things you wouldn't have known if doing the self guided tour. They then thank us for coming and wish us a happy visit. We spent about 30 minutes total on the tour. 

But wait.... when I was buying my tickets at the window I specifically told the lady I wanted to see backstage, so she told me to pay extra for the guided tour. So why are we being given our farewell? Well I asked our tour guide about seeing the backstage area and he told me that on certain days (and depending on concerts/performances) the backstage area is off limits. Now, I understand how that may have been a factor....... but why was I not told this before buying my ticket? The lady knew that's what I wanted and she failed to inform me. I honestly felt like she had pulled a fast one just to get those extra dollars from me. 

Do I think paying the extra money to see the dressing room upstairs and a little info from the tours? No. Did I still enjoy my visit and seeing the auditorium? Yes. Just paying for something I didn't get left a bit of a sour taste in my mouth...
Everyone should see a show at the Ryman every time they visit Nashville! It's amazing! The setting is so small and intimate. There isn't a bad seat in the place. It's a truly wonderful experience!

I, along with my husband and teenage daughter, attended the Paramore concert at the Nashville Municipal Auditorium on September 7, 2018. The concert was absolutely amazing. Immediately following the closing, the cleaning staff entered the floor area with large broom sweeps and literally began chasing people out of the auditorium with the brooms. It was absolutely pathetic. We had a staff member follow us pushing his broom wherever we went, trying to push us out the door with the broom and telling us to go to a particular door. My family and I because of his extreme rudeness began to run to another door to try to escape this man, as we didn't know if his actions were going to turn violent because of his attitude. As we did, we saw another staff member yelling rudely at a group getting a picture after the event to stop and leave the premise. The group was doing absolutely nothing wrong. They were not causing a disruption. They were simply getting a picture. We will not be back to this Auditorium. Rudest venue staff I have ever experienced. Ruined a great night!
Cool concept, nice temperature, inviting atmosphere, and very good food.  Not may cool shopping options.  I love the food market also.  I will come back with family and friends on the next time.

The Holy Grail of music venues. The nostalgia, atmosphere, and acoustics were just unbelievable. It sounds so good here. We came here to see the Local Natives and they sounded exactly as they do on the album. It really was as if I were listening to them on my music playing device! The staff here is awesome. They do not police people around like I have seen at other venues. They have ample restrooms and bar areas. I never waited to use the restroom or did I wait longer than two minutes in line for a beer. The ushers were very helpful by making sure everyone knew where they were going. Seating was by old school church pews, but they were surprising comfy and they are well spaced so no elbow touching and shoulder grazing with the creepy unknowns. This is hands down the best music venue I have ever attended.

***The Grand Ole Opry and Ryman Auditorium are two very historic parts of the Nashville music scene; while a lot of the music is old-fashioned, the Grand Ole Opry is still a must experience if you are a music fan***

Ryman Auditorium is one of the country's most historic and well known music venues.  Ryman is located right in Downtown Nashville (next to bar and lounges that explode with live country rock music).  It is also the original home to the nation's longest running radio show the Grand Ole Opry and even runs the Grand Ole Opry for a select few shows of the year before the Grand Ole Opry relocates to its newer and bigger home--the Grand Ole Opry House.  The Grand Ole Opry House is near the Gaylord Opryland Resort (a few miles outside of Downtown Nashville).

I went to the Ryman Auditorium for a Grand Ole Opry performance and it is a unique experience.  You can purchase tickets at the box office the night of the show.  If you get there early, the Ryman Auditorium has a small and very crowded gift shop, which sells lots of Ryman Auditorium and Grand Ole Opry souvenirs.

Ryman has a few concession stands that sell reasonably priced food with generous portions though the quality is mediocre.  The concession stand here serves hot dogs, chicken tenders, popcorn, various candies, caramel popcorn, bottled water, soft drinks, and alcohol.

The auditorium itself has a lot of history.  With the decor as well as the memorabilia on display, you can feel the age and the history of this venue.  You can feel it in the seats too.  The seats are actually long hard wood benches.  They are not very comfortable and they can be a little tight depending on who is in your row and how many layers of clothes they are wearing.  The venue has a mezzanine section (some seats have obstructed views) and a balcony.

The show has a fairly interesting setup.  The show is broken up into four parts/acts and each part is hosted by a Grand Ole Opry member, who also performs the opening and closing song for each act.  The host then introduces performers for each act.  The hosts tend to be more well-known than a lot of the other performers, but there is an incredible variety of performers as at least eight different artists/groups perform each night at the Grand Ole Opry.

Since the show is a radio show, there were also sponsored ads performed live by the show's standard radio announcers.  The ads featured brands like Cracker Barrel, a dollar store and a boot retailer and some of the ads were even unintentionally kind of funny.

The show was interesting even if you are not a fan of country music (there was a mix of more modern country music as well as some very old timey country music).  In addition to the wide variety of acts that performed, the hosts and the performers had a very familiar camaraderie that resulted in a lot of comedy as well as a very casual, intimate and family feel.  The familiar and jokey banter made me feel that like I was just spending a weekend with these artists at a large gathering.

In terms of the live music, the venue was nice.  The acoustics were very pleasing and the music really fills the big space.  The acts themselves were good too though how much you like it depends on how much you like this style of music.  Still, for non-country music fans, it was fun seeing country music legend Vince Gill and American Idol star Lauren Alaina perform.  It was also a unique treat to see Tennessee's state song Rocky Top performed by the artists who originally recorded that song.

Service was very good on my visit; the staff was friendly and polite.

Ticket prices are reasonable and can be a real value depending on who is performing though there is very short notice on a lot of the performers.

Live music is a major part of the Nashville experience.  There are definitely more contemporary and exciting music elsewhere in Nashville, but Ryman Auditorium and the Grand Ole Opry are still very signature elements of the Nashville music scene.  Though this style of music as well as some of the commentary that occurs throughout the show is not for all tastes, the Ryman Auditorium is still a very unique experience and a must visit if you are a music fan.

There are several pay parking structures around the Ryman Auditorium.  I believe the parking structure adjacent to the Ryman Auditorium is $10 per vehicle.
A beautiful and intimate venue. Beyond classy. Always a great time.

This isn't fine dining, but its fun and has a great atmosphere.  The food is pretty good and they usually have a pretty talented band.  Its a fun enough place, that it should be more crowded.

My only complaint about this place is that the mgr. has the waitress seat people in some of the worst side tables, even when the place is nearly empty and the other tables were not reserved.
The table was so bad, we dined at the bar and watched the band.  I won't go back if they don't start changing this.

No Passport Needed

From the time you step out of your vehicle and walk the few steps from the parking lot to the main entrance, you begin to feel there's something different about this place. Perhaps it's the neat decor in what was once a run-down food store in a strip mall. Perhaps it's the lively music constantly being piped outdoors...and that music continues indoors as you step into a beautifully decorated mini streets scene. Maybe it's the alfresco cafe with its enticing aromas just to your left before you enter.

Questions? There's an Information booth right inside the main entrance. And there are plenty of assistants and Security Personnel throughout the area to guide you to ... to wherever or for whatever you need ... the bathrooms perhaps? (Located in the street--hallway to the right of the large stage in the Food Court.)

Walking into Plaza Mariachi, I was immediately transported to some of the tiny villages and small shopping areas I've visited all over the world. The lighting, the ambiance, the sights and smells are both subdued and vibrant at the same time. The decor is absolutely spot-on with gaily decorated wall art, plants, and paisajes (landscapes). Please take time to look and admire the effort that went into the planning of this amazing venue...a little slice of Latin America - Mexico right here in Nashville!

Entertainment? They've got it. Live music much of the time with acts ranging from Mariachi Bands to solo performers to trios and more. The acts are ever-changing and also include daily performances by jugglers and acrobats performing above the Food Court... maybe right next to your table! (Check the calendar on the website.)

Food? Yes they've got it. Try some mini tacos (teeny 3-inch bites reminiscent of tapas style) at Botanas Locas (Crazy Snacks). Or, walk across the spacious Food Court area to the Tienda Bar for a cold cerveza. Maybe you're in the mood for a steaming cup of hot Madera Coffee? If so, go ahead and grab a Cuban sandwich while you're there - they're located near the back (or is it front?) of the Food Court, opposite the stage.  

Maybe you're in the mood for a cold, refreshing, and healthy, fresh-made Zoomito Juice (I had a tantalizing apple, carrot, and cilantro) or a bowl of cold ceviche or... tapas at Las Tablas Tapas? 

I grabbed a generously filled, lightly spiced Gyro with Lamb and Chicken and grilled onions at Kouzina Café, then sat down to listen to a rising Colombian star, Marcela Pinella....oh my!

Maybe you'll want to play with the kids at Tito's Playland (arcade)? I'm sure they will!

The side hallways (aka streets) are filled with an eclectic collection of stores: an Art Gallery, a Cellular Provider, a salon, Insurance Company, a Radio Station broadcast booth (Activa 1240), clothing stores, ice cream (oughta have something sweet to sustain you on your journey), along with many, many, many more.

On your way out, you might stop by MazFresco Market, the International Grocery Store, and pick up something to take home - fresh fish or meat, while choosing from a wealth of Latin American fresh baked goods and packaged products. 

¿Listo? Ready?

Púes, ahora tienes tu oportunidad de hacer un viaje a América Latina justo aquí en Nashville. ¡Cierto! 

(Well, now's your chance to take a trip to Latin America right here in Nashville. Really!)

By the way, the Mariachi Band today played a full set of lively Mexican music...and ended with their version of "Rocky Top!' How appropriate for this marvelous mix of cultural creativity.

Had an early Sunday dinner at Samba recently, which was an altogether enjoyable experience. Live music was very nice, service was good and the blackened red snapper étouffée was off-the-hook tasty! Will be back.

We had so much fun here! We met up with friends at the bar and had a good time. Drank a bunch, got some snacks, listened to good music. I live the Christmas light hanging and just the whole vibe of the place. You wanted to just get a drink and stay awhile, and that is exactly what we did. We will make our way back there next time when we visit.

Loved this place!!! Super old school country music & great simple food.   they have live music, bar & a great little menu. When you first walk in, it's like you are being transported to a different era. There is a wall of boots, that are not for sale lol. I made that mistake ‍. Most of the boots have autographs of country singers. That night they had a great three man band that played old school country and some fifties music. The food was great! Supper simple menu like I said, but so good. They even had recession combos that included fried bologna sandwich, potato chips, moon pie & beer. Combo 2 was a corn dog, chips, moon pie & beer. The food was great the music was great. It was great seeing everyone have a good time. Love it!

Perfectly average! Not too loud, decent music, plenty of seating, a kind bar tender. Literally everything you would want out of a Honky Tonk! The best part is beers are actually the cheapest here out of anywhere on the Broadway strip, at just $2.50 a glass. Not being a beer fan myself, I just had a glass of water, but the bar tender still stayed and chatted with us for a while and wanted to hear all about Chicago. When a girl spilled her drink near us on accident, the bar tender quickly whipped up another one for her, free of charge, which I thought was so kind and out of the ordinary. Definitely worth a trip for some genuine service and laidback country tunes.

Bouncing between a three and a four.
I came her for Lizzie concert and initially I loved the scenery, the organization the building looks great and very beat and clean. However for the actual location being for a concert i can't say it was the best experience.

Bathroom are always going to be long lines however, these bathrooms were cleaned frequently they were nicely designed and truly felt safe.

The bars were horrible. Over priced drinks for poor and slow service. Minimal options, the bar service felt like I waited for an hour for a bootlegger

We weren't looking for super loud, obnoxious party crowds. This was perfect! The price is right, the AC is strong, the classic country music was spot on, and the crowd and staff was down to earth and sound. Also--I can eat a recession special every day for the rest of my life... $6 goes a long way! #friedbolognasandwich

My husband and I were heading back to our hotel when we decided to stop in for one more drink. The bands were switching out so we got lucky and scored a table right on the rail of the upper level. Amazing atmosphere and we totally enjoyed the energy of the place. There's no table service, so you do have to go to the bar for your drinks, but that was fine, we were only coming in for one, right?
