Nope, ended up staying for a couple of hours! Clean bathrooms, friendly bartenders, and an excellent band.

When I am in Nashville I always make it a priority to stop at the tin roof. Located right off Main Street the tin roof is a really small place and has very good music. The bands that play here don't just play country music they play a wide variety of country rock I've never heard metal but it's definitely a good variety of music. It's also a change of pace from just hearing country had every other place on Main Street. The tin roof reminds me of a hybrid between music venue restaurant and bar

A friend of mine actually knows the owner here and he's very nice. I have had two conversations with the owner and he goes out of his way to make any accommodations needed. The venue itself is very small but it makes for a good show. They do have an upstairs area. Out of the four times that I've been here mostly it's older individuals that I've seen here  A lot of husband-and-wife just dancing or just sitting having a drink listening to good music. I have seen a couple younger people stopping but they're usually there for one or two drinks and then they leave. 

The tin roof does have a full bar. They do have specials every once a while on fireball shots which is a Nashville staple. Not my cuppa tea. They also have buckets of Bud light. And every other fruity girly drink that you could think of. The bar itself is a big L-shape. they do have multiple bartenders behind the counters. They also have food here and it's very good. One of my favorite things about this place is when you do order a shot they give it to you in a medicine cup. 

I do like the fact that every time I've come here it has not been shoulder to shoulder crowded. There has only been one time that I have not been able to get a table. I have also never been disappointed with the music. If you do decide to bring a car here there is a parking lot not far away but spaces are very limited unless you have a reservation. Otherwise it's all street parking or you have to park five or six blocks away. 

Overall the tin roof is a great place to come. I highly recommend coming here if you do like to see live music and a good variety of music and not just country. Also it's less crowded. You can also get a table and actually sit down and enjoy the night. I will stop at the tin roof every single time that I come to Nashville. 

PROS:
- owner is a great guy
- staff is friendly 
- they have a good happy hour
- you can get a table 
- not crowded like the other bars
- good variety of music

CONS:
- parking is tough if you drive here

Beautiful building rich in history and nostalgia!
Many pictures and items displayed throughout the building!
 This is a must see and do while in Nashville!

They only let in certain people they only want in. 
The bouncers will pick people out of the line they are scared of and will not let them in for whatever reason. Call it racism call it being scared of actually having to do something but it is a fear they have. As a native of Nashville to be told your friend is not allowed after going in EVERY bar on broadway is a little stupid to anyone trying to talk up their city. Because if the city is talked up and gets positive reviews the club or whatever it is that is being positively reviewed is making more money because of the positive reviews and in this case should not receive positive reviews. 

Workers will turn down any guys they think might actually be as strong as them and will mess up their little lie of a story to get them a better tip so ignore

This is the worst concert venue I've ever been to. The opening act has already started and we've been waiting outside for hours. HORRIBLE organization.  No ropes or anything to keep people in lines, just a bunch of garbage and wood pallets. Everyone else around me is equally pissed about this situation. I will not be attending a concert here again.

Very cool looking venue. Waited 15 minutes at the bar and couldn't get service. No band even started setting up in that time. So we decided to leave. Everywhere else around there has more accessible bars with live music starting more frequently. Somehow this place is slightly hipper, which means more crowded and less customer service focus.

The experience of the Ryman theater cannot be simply put into words. There is an energy that fills the place. Not sure if it's the history of the legends that have graced this stage or the emotions that the place brings in each person that walks through these doors. We've came here about 3 years ago before the updates. The transformation is pretty amazing! 

We have sat on the floor seats and balcony and both views are fantastic. They do offer drinks, and they are very expensive. But hey you are not there for the drinks. 

The best part of this place is when you can take a tour. Just DO IT! It's such a fun experience. The tour includes visiting back stage and on stage access.  

This is a memory everyone needs to experience!

We loved it! Not as loud as the other honky tonks

Brought our toddlers and they seemed happy

They card you as you enter so be prepared 

Clean

Great cheese curds
Lovely workers

Good solid music

Highly recommend

If I could, I'd give them 0 stars. And if I could, I'd take away all the stars they already have. 1 group of my friends walked in before we got up to the door from the parking lot. Didn't charge 3 of my girlfriends. When I walked up they said everyone was $15. 

I explained I already knew they hadn't charged 3 if my friends they denied it. 

I watched them not charge 3 people who walked in while I waited on the side. 

Then when I walked up with the rest of our friends from the parking lot (I only decided to go in because it was my friend's birthday) they charged everyone $15 (including a friend of mine who is a VERY attractive professional cheerleader so you know this wasn't completely about looks) except my 1 guy friend in the group who winked at the girl at the front they charged him $10. 

The woman at the checkout had heavy makeup. Curly brown hair she parted to the side - with some sort of partially striped top for her costume. And worked with the short security girl in front who wore glasses who "backed up" her story. 

Lucky for them it was my friends birthday.

Absolutely awful service and disrespect. Needless to say - if you don't look Spanish or Hispanic you might get charged. Never again.

Homophobic owner announced that girl on girl dancing was allowed and encouraged, but  boy on boy dancing was prohibited.
Dave Tanner, a regular guitarist and vocalist there, has also written a homophobic song about Tootsie's, which he calls a gay bar. This is Southern discrimination at its best. Stay away and don't support. It's a shame because the music was amazing until all the homophobic slander started.

Sambuca looks like a Las Vegas lounge transferred to the down to earth town of Nashville.  It is the epitome of incongruity.  As we are not particularly enamored with Country or Blue Grass, the opportunity to listen to Stephanie Adlington, an accomplished jazz crooner, was exciting. Entering into the bordello like ambiance of Sambuca was odd, but great seating was available on this Sunday night and we thoroughly enjoyed the music. Drinks were light on the alcohol, service was spotty, the food mediocre at best, but the music was great.  The surprise of the evening was when I asked for bread.  Sambuca does not serve bread.  No bread? What restaurant doesn't have bread.  I asked them if they had croutons, but the server didn't get my joke. I offered to go to Piggly Wiggly for a loaf, but that didn't go over well either. As Marie would say, "Let them eat cake."
One of our two favorite spots while visiting Nashville. We went every day at least once. Saw some good bands. All the servers were friendly. Prices reasonable. Would definitely return.

Love the Ryman Auditorium. Yes, the acoustics are superb, but there are some tricky sight lines at the ends of the balcony and under the balcony. I recommend paying a bit more for the better views of the stage, but you'll hear well from anyplace in the auditorium. The place is steeped in history and deserves all the accolades. Enjoy!

It's the Ryman. What more does one need to say? If you are a music lover and an artist you follow is performing here, I can't imagine that you'd have a bad time. Coming here just for the sake of coming here, however, is a bit more of a mixed bag. It's nothing about the venue; it's just sitting through a performance (or, performances) you'd never attend otherwise. That's what happened to me for my Ryman experience.

I had friends coming in town and they (well, really, just one) were on fire to go to the Ryman. Sheepishly, I admitted that I'd never been. I'd meant to. There were shows I would have seen. But I don't make it out to live music venues as much as I once did so I never quite got the spirit to commit to coming to a show. But this would have to be different. On a Saturday in mid-November the show was... the Grand Ole Opry. Hmm. I can appreciate the history and kitsch but this was wasn't my first choice of first show to see at the Ryman. But things were what they were so I attempted to buy tickets and... gone? Really? Three weeks before the show? Hmm. I called customer service and somehow the rep was able to find five seats together where there weren't any before. Magic. Not only was she incredibly helpful but she was quite polite as well. It was a wee bit shocking for a customer service interaction, sadly enough. We were to be seated up top but that was fine with me. Sound travels up and I was there for the sound, not the sights.

We arrived 25 minutes before the show and... chaos. Pure chaos. There were no stanchions. There were no discernible lines. There was only a crush of humanity without the ability to form logical ways by which to enter in to the auditorium. Making things worse, I had to pick up my tickets at will call. Thing is, people were just standing around, not moving. Taking initiative, I started asking who was waiting to pick up tickets. Then I started push... making my way to the counter. I devised the brilliant idea to ally with an older woman. I was the muscle, she was the sass. People parted for her like the red sea and I kept her moving. #teamwork We got to the counter (passing many people who weren't waiting for tickets; they were just blocking the way), got our tickets and resumed waiting. 

The doors opened at exactly the posted time (I can appreciate that) and we made our way inside and to our seats. Once inside, the process was pretty smooth. There's no excuse for the mess outside. None. Drinks are overpriced and weak but you know to expect this. The venue is as stately as advertised. The sound is the stuff of legends and the energy is palpable. I just wish I'd come to see an act I was pumped about. It was cool (read: kitschy) to sit for a live broadcast of such a long-running show but (for me) the novelty wore off. Plus, I think I was one of 10 locals (including the performers) in the building. The Titans-Patriots game was the next day and the Mother Church was full of Patriots fans. Maybe the locals knew better?

I'm glad I came. I'd come again -- but next time I'd come see an act I really wanted to see. Last tip: back row on the upper level had padded seats. As anyone who went to church in the south can tell you, church pews + sitting for a long time =/= comfort. Go for the padded chairs.

Sambuca has a great atmosphere, location, service, and menu (food + drink). 

It has multiple levels and two great outdoor seating areas, a stage with great live music, and an overall cool vibe that I'd recommend as one of my "go to" spots in Nashville. 

You can't beat the filet with added toppings but they have other great dishes and seafood options which seem hard to find in Nashville. 

They have a very professional staff that is helpful, friendly, and knows the menu front to back.

Serious such a wonderful place, it's a hidden Gem that much people doesn't seem to know about. I love the food court the food is 10x better than the food court at the mall.

I'm honestly not a fan of the regular " stores " that inside just because the prices are ridiculous. We stopped at one of the stores that sold beautiful evening dresses for special occasions and outing and we asked how much for one of the dress & she said $220. Trust me that was NOT worth $220 & it's not even a name brand you know. But anywhooo I just said thanks and kept on walking. 

Now back to the food. Worth it. It was from "Guachos" I think that how it's spelled. In one of the order with the fried steak they brought it and it had a huge slice of ham & I don't eat pork so I went back and told them & they fairly told the chef about it and he said he would change it and make a new one, but honestly I was paranoid that he was going to give me back the same steak and he was only going to take the pork off so I stood and watched and he told me not to be worried that he threw the whole meal away and I didn't believe until he went and get the garbage can to show me & with all this he was smiling and being kind apologizing & I was so happy to be recovering that energy. 
 Well we enjoyed everything and I left a nice tip for them. I will definitely be going back. Also the gyro spot is very affordable & their fried Wings are the Bomb

No matter what you do,  you have to check out the madness of Broadway at night,  it's very entertaining. We decided to check it out at night and it was crowded and the lines and people were spilling out into the streets.  Legends didn't have a line so we got there in time for a band to start playing.  They were really good and sang some recent country hits. It can get hard to enjoy the music because it gets crowded and unfortunately we were trapped between two Bachelorette party mosh pits. There was a lot of broken glass on the floor but it reminds me of a college bar with live country music. I would definitely give it try again but maybe earlier in the day.
This place is a must stop in when in Nashville.  The entertainment was rocking, fun and well, entertaining!  Interactive and just the right amount of loud!

All I can say is wow! 
I came on a Friday evening and had good Mariachi musicians providing us a wide genre of songs in the traditional Mariachi style. Then we were entertained with two very talented aerial Acrobats (I think that's what they're called.
Eating out with a vegetarian couple can prove challenging in an Hispanic area, but this place provided options and everyone was happy.
I enjoyed the decor and cute shops. I could imagine my students really enjoying taking selfies and learning about quinces and first communions.

This place is so steeped in history that you almost can't help but get caught up in the nostalgia. I had no interest in going here but my wife insisted. She really got this one right. 
This building is over 100 years old and anybody who's somebody has played here or wished they had. The list of singers, actors, shows, etc. who have occupied the stage is amazing. The Grand Ole Opy is only one of many who called this the ultimate stage.
The acoustics here are incredible. The only thing I have seen like it is the Hollywood Bowl. You can barely see the person and yet you hear them very well. A photographer was barking instructions to her subjects at stage front and we could hear her clear as a bell walking above the balcony seats.
We tried to book a show after our tour of the theater, but they were all sold out. So book ahead and rest assured it will be a treat!

We went to the Ryman on our visit to Nashville, and it was incredible and memorable. Great live show. Many acts included in a series of four mini shows. 

In addition to seeing the show, we also took the self-guided tour of the auditorium and really enjoyed it. The Ryman offers a very interesting tour highlighting the history of country and bluegrass music with numerous exhibits housing artists' costumes and instruments. A movie shown in their theater, traces the history of the building. I'm very fond of country music and enjoy listening to the greats-- Johnny Cash, Merle Haggard, George Strait, Patsy Cline, and while this is our very first time visiting this venue... sure this won't be the last.

No tour is complete without dropping by at the gift shoppe. All things Mother Church (the Ryman was originally built as a church, hence the reference) and Nashville. From collectibles, records, décor, and clothing they've got it!

"Country music has become the music that best represents the reality of American life." --Brad Paisley
On of our favorite stops on Broadway always great talent on stage. Beer cold, atmosphere fun..downside bathrooms downstairs can be tricky after a few brews..so pace yourself!

The butcher in the market alone deserves 5 stars. Excellent meat and seafood selection and helpful.
All of the plaza (except the cell phone store )is a great place to pig out and dig into some varied cultural experiences.
We got both the hot and cold platters from the tapas place and it was a good variety, then sampled the pizza, and then hit the ice cream/popsicle shop. Very good all around.
My friend took some of the ceviche home and raved about it. We tried the flan from the market and it was delicious as well.
Great concept and execution. I can't wait to see what moves in to the other spots inside the plaza.
While you're there, get your next meal to-go from Taj Indian Restaurant in the same parking lot. It's the best in town.

Great honky tonk on Broadway. The only bar in downtown we actually met some locals! 

We came in for a Shiner and their fried bologna sandwich with mayo and tomato. The bologna is actually grilled though not fried.  I saw this place on diners drive ins and dives and glad we made it in.  I thought the sandwich was very good. Not every meal has to be gourmet, sometimes a simple meal can hit just the right spot. Especially when there's some good live country music playing in the background.  I hope this place sticks around for ages.

Absolute hands down one of the best meals I have ever had! The Prosciutto mac and cheese just melted in your mouth with all the blended cheeses! The Brussels sprouts w/ smoked bacon was awesome the layers of the sprout were soft and tender and the smoked bacon just made the sprout come alive with flavor!  Flat iron with green beans is a must! It was cooked to perfection! Oh and the entire staff was attentive professional and very efficient!!

An excellent place to visit. The original home of WSM's Grand Ole Opry is still as lively as ever. The tour guides were very  friendly and informative as they showed us around . Later in in the week, we went to a show at the mother church of country music and the acoustics were superb. Two thumbs up! :)






friendly

All in one place, good food, good dessert, good cantina for drinks, live entertainment, and if you want a variety grocery store they have it too and some stores to buy cute nicknacks! Tacos, churrasco, churros, margaritas, salsa music on Thursday!!!! Beautiful plaza filled with color and Mexican decor makes you fell like you're in a another country!

Review of the tour...we didn't see a show here. The tour was kind of lame and super expensive. We did the tour with the guide and while it was nice and more informative than the self guided ones. I am glad to check this off our Nashville bucket list, but I wouldn't go back. I would, however, love to see a show here!

This might be one of the oddest bars I've been in but that's what makes it amazing.  Most of the servers were older ladies (which I loved) and is refreshing from all the T&A on the strip.  Reminded me of an old VFW.  All of the photos on the wall are old and crumbling but that adds to the charm.  They had a great band when we were there an old country band with an upright base.  They also sold boots which was a bit odd but again added to that charm.  

We didn't eat while we were there but they had fried bologna sandwiches which had I been in the mood would've been exactly what I would've ordered.  This place is a real gem in Nashville where everything is being taken over by the singer of the moment mega bars.  This is a throwback!!

I wanted a true honky tonk experience. Cowboy boots, southern accents, big hats, dancing that do-si-do, cheap well drinks, and all those other stereotypes. Because when in Nashville, see the Nashville sights, right? While I was on the search for that on Yelp, Robert's came up. 

First of all, you won't find southern charm here from the staff. I just thought I'd let you know, in case it was something you are looking forward to experiencing. The wait staff here was rude af. And I don't mean just one person, but everyone we encountered. Perhaps it was an off day... For all of them. If you're constantly at capacity, and that makes your workers cranky, maybe management should hire more people to accommodate surging numbers in the summer. Or perhaps increase their pay since they have to deal with a bunch of drunk tourists. Just a few thoughts. 

Other than that, it's a pretty entertaining dive bar. Live music is played here, every day. I love that, even if it isn't really my kind of music, it's still fun to people watch and enjoy the company of your friends. It's extremely small, and no doubt constantly beleaguered by drunken people, no matter what time of day it is. They pride themselves on their well-known "Recession Special," which includes a fried bologna sandwich, chips, and a PBR. PBR here is consistently cheap in general, at $2.50, and most of the food is as well. While the food is cheap, you'll find that the quality is also cheap... Definitely lower than typical bar fare. You'll find mozzarella cheese sticks for $5, French fries for $4, and even a hamburger for $6, all very affordable and incredibly greasy; perfect for soaking up a bit of alcohol before you go on with the rest of your night and drink more. 

THE VERDICT:
Cheap food, cheap drinks, live music, centrally located in downtown Nashville. It's an entertaining place to go at night with a group of friends, but not really the place to be if you like tasty food and friendly bartenders.

We visit Nashville about 5 times a year. And every single time we dine at Sambuca. We were there this past Saturday night (11/11) This place has it all. Great food. Wonderful entertainment and top notch service. Arielle is an awesome server. Friendly and knowledgeable efficient and attentive!! The entrees were delicious ! Miso Sea Bass is a must!! Wonderful array of flavors!! The flat iron steak is cooked perfectly any way you want it!! The entertainment the Pearl played very upbeat and fun sets!! We can't get enough of this place.  Hats off the the entire establishment!!

Absolutely love this place! The grocery store bakery makes the BEST chocolate flan I have ever had - a whole one ordered was $25!!! The people are so nice - I love heading over to Plaza Mariachi for lunch during the week or even on weekends (and I don't live close...lol).

Great entertainment - love the live music and Mariachi band!!

Overall, a great place that I hope stays around for a long while!

I have been to Sambuca several times and it never disappoints me and my friends. The food is great and so is the band. The music has a wide variety of genres so it appeals to a diverse crowd. The dance floor is very very small that to me is it's only flaw. 
This time I had the stuffed artichokes, roasted Brussels and a house salad. It was all delicious and more than I could eat. 
This time the place was full of women, there were only maybe 5 couples in the whole place. 
Me, my friends and all the other women there had a blast dancing. 
It's a sexy,  fun,  safe place and a night there won't set you back financially like some of the other places around Nashville. 
They also have valet parking!!

I visited on a Saturday with live music. The featured special included steak, shrimp, scallop and red mashed potatoes, but I don't eat beef-the chef graciously agreed to substitute salmon or red snapper.  We also ordered the beignets, crab dip & brussel sprouts.  Everything was wonderful and the waiter & manager provided great customer service. Definitely plan to visit again the next time I'm in town.

My friends and I were so excited for a night on the town in Nashville after getting off a rough part of the Appalachian Trail. We heard good things about Tin Roof so we went there first. 

THE BOUNCER WAS AWFUL TO US.

He wouldn't let us enter. All of us are 22+, so this came out of left field. We were patient in our response, because we all are of age and have been for a long time. We pulled out many other forms of identification, but he refused to give us the time of day. You might be thinking that he had to help the next people but it was early on a Monday night- there was no one else in line.

It was a terrible way to start the night, and we felt so disrespected and belittled. He was awful. 

Thankfully, Tin Roof is not unique. We still had a great night, enjoying other bars nearby. We will NEVER go back to Tin Roof.

This is the home of TRUE country. Stuff you can only hear on Sirus XM channel 59
LOVE this place. Brazillabilly band is awesome!!  So much history in this establishment.
Gets packed...wonder why... Lol ...that tells ya something.
A MUST see!!! If in Nashville stop in.

After hours the shops close down and the dance floor is open. They play all types of music, although the music is mainly Spanish, but they play all types and it is amazing. The dance floor is large and there are plenty of tables. Me and my friends had a great time. The security is also really good and lines move by fast. The drinks are expensive, but that is gonna be the case in most places. I would definitely come back and recommend it!

I did absolutely zero research on the honky tonk scene before coming to Nashville and I just randomly popped into RWW because I liked the music. I'm not really a fan of C&W, at least not "modern" C&W. I prefer the sounds of slide guitar from the '50's through the '70's and since I heard those delightful notes wafting through the open window of RWW, I figured it would be as good a place as any to have a beer and and a listen. 

The band was great and the beer was cheap. Seriously cheap. A PBR was $2.50. The bathrooms were clean enough and while the downstairs was really crowded, everyone was friendly. All in all, a very enjoyable time!

This was by far my favorite place. The music was absolutely perfect for a Sunday afternoon. They had football on tv and I had a few tacos and a beer while watching the game. Service could've have been a bit better - but that's not the reason you go to a bar on a Sunday.

How cool is this place? My friends and I happened upon Plaza Mariachi after eating dinner in Nashville. We heard the music and were way too intrigued to pass it up. 

Plaza Mariachi is a spot split up into a lot of smaller other spaces. I spotted a dress shop, car rental kiosk, insurance agency, and a clothing store. This section is laid out like a mall. The decor is mesmerizing. The ceiling is painted like the sky and the lighting brings a nice ambiance. 

For food, this is a place I would frequent if I lived nearby. There are fresh made churros, a whole grocery store with unique Latino foods, a taco shop, a popsicle shop, and a bar for drinks. This part of the plaza is super cool. It utilizes the big space and tall ceilings to create a roomy dining area. It could be just like a food court, but a stage with performers adds to the experience. Apparently on Thursdays and Saturdays you can enjoy salsa night. I would love to come back to dance. 

Everyone there, security, servers, clientele, were all so very nice. I haven't been to a place with such a great experience in a very long time. 

Oh! And my favorite part was probably for the kids. There's a nice arcade and play place where kids can win prizes in arcade games. Everything was really updated, Time Crisis 5 and a four player air hockey table. 

Plaza Mariachi is a family friendly place that I look forward to browsing around again.

Best value and most authentic classic country venue in Nashville.  Reliable series of quality musicians that play old time gems as well as a few songs of their own.  Check out their music schedule for what acts they'll feature and when. 
Also: All day every day deal of $2.50 PBR & MHL plus delicious burgers.

Wow what an interesting place! I have never seen anything like this. It's a combination of a local mall, Mexican version of Eataly (many restaurants and stores in one place), community talent show- type stage (with a host), and an indoor playground.
I went there with some friends and they ordered bunch of tacos, steak kabobs, and margaritas. I had ceviche, popsicle (strawberry and cream), cappuccino, and concha (sweet Mexican bread). 

My friends really liked the "carne asada" and shrimp taco from the taco shop. (Not the sit down restaurant) The potato and fried plantain I took from a friend's plate were very good, too. 

My ceviches (shrimp and fish tostada, $4-5) were good, too, but they had so much cucumber (which I  hate)..

Cappuccino was also very good - they even have a coffee roastery! Not bitter or sour, and it was much better than the cappuccinos I had at The Wells or Red bicycle on this trip. 

Popsicle was great -very creamy and lots of strawberries! (About $2.5, I think)

There were acrobatic performances, fire show+mime (@.@?!?!), some Irish dancing, and some band singing. 

It was too loud at times but what a fun place! I will definitely come back next time I'm in Nashville! It'd be fun to bring kids here, too.

This is one of the oldest bars out on Broadway & really is a must stop if you want to experience downtown Nashville. The band my girlfriend Julie & I saw was great & if you get hungry they have a grill where you can grab a bite.

Robert's was one the Honky Tonks I wanted to visit. Since I was in Nashville for work, my boss & couple other people recommended that Robert's was one of their favorite Honky Tonk in Downtown Broadway. 

One thing I love about all the Honky Tonks, there is no cover charge but make sure you have cash on you because the bands will walk around with their tip jar (tips is the way the bands make their living). 

Food: We ordered their Fried Bologna Sandwich served with chips ($4.00). You can order their Recession Special which is their Fried Bologna Sandwich, Chips & PBR Beer. Since we didn't get to go to the breweries in Nashville, we got to try a few beers at Robert's. Tried Tennessee Beer Works, Southern Wit & Yazoo, Hop Perfect IPA. They were both really good! 

Entertainment: I forgot the bands name but the gentlemen who was sitting next to us told us they were the best band that performs in Downtown Broadway & he was right. We were able to go to Robert's twice during our trip & both nights we caught the same band. 

If you're in Downtown Broadway, make Robert's your first visit & make sure you order their Fried Bologna sandwich. Happy Eating!
Great drinks, great music, and great service. What more could you ask for? This is a chill spot in a hot neighborhood. It draws all sorts of people, which always adds to the experience.

The butcher in the market alone deserves 5 stars. Excellent meat and seafood selection and helpful.
All of the plaza (except of course the cell phone store, law office, and money changing place) is a great place to pig out and dig into some varied cultural experiences.
We got both the hot and cold platters from the tapas place and it was a good variety, then sampled the pizza, and then hit the ice cream/popsicle shop. Very good all around.
My friend took some of the ceviche home and raved about it. We tried the flan from the market and it was delicious as well.
The art gallery has some really beautiful things to look at. Make sure and check out the rope art.
Great concept and execution. I can't wait to see what moves in to the other spots inside the plaza.
While you're there, get your next meal to-go from Taj Indian Restaurant in the same parking lot. It's the best in town.

One of the BEST venues EVER!!!
The music sounds soooo good in this venue it's unbelievable. I was here back in 1976 when I was a young gal and I wanted to go back since we are in Nashville alot.
We got Excellent seats, Sec. 3 row G
Amazing!!!! 
Country artist pop in all the time here. We had T Graham Brown pop in and sing a couple songs. Loved it. 
I felt so much closer to the artists and felt their heart pour out when they sang here.
I was however thought the gift shop could have had more things/variety and could have been bigger.. I did not see the GOO GOO bars anywhere. 
I would highly recommend this venue!!!

Walked in because I heard "A Boy Named Sue," stayed when they started playing "Copperhead Road."  Food was solid.  Beer was cold.  Service was outstanding.  My favorite Honkey Tonk on Broadway, or tied with Legends.  People were great.  Service was better.  Beer was cold.  Bologna​ sandwich?  Corn Dog?  YES PLEASE!!!

One of the hardest venues I've ever had to work with. 

I've dealt with this venue for several different events, and they do not make life easy. There are always roadblocks for something that should be an easy fix, or some crazy hoop that has to be jumped through to get things done. 

It's size and convenience to downtown are great, but over all i try to never work there if I don't have to.

The Ryman is one of the best venues to hear live music in the country.  It's the home to more country music stars than I can name and if you ever get a chance to go make sure that you do. There is also so much history there that it is fun just to look around and read about all the interesting facts. 

It's a must do if you are in Nashville, TN.

We stopped in for lunch.  It is definitely nothing like the typical Nashville restaurants we went to.  It is dark and mysterious, more like a lounge, with really neat bold colored décor that pops out at you.  (We went on a Monday, so I'm sure the weekend/dinner experience is different) The lunch menu was very diverse and was reasonably priced for the area.  I ordered a soup and salad combo.  The shrimp and crab bisque was very tasty, although I wish it had more pieces of shrimp and crab in the soup.  I ordered The Bib salad, which was very fresh!  I also decided to try a Pale Ale from Yazoo, a local brewery in the area and it was also very flavorful.  Our waiter was new, so the service was a little choppy and slow, but the manager came by twice to see how things were going.  Overall, we had a great experience and I would definitely go back.

***REVIEW FROM AN EXPERIENCE IN JUNE 2015: I just wanted to let everyone reading my review know that even though this review was written in the beginning of 2018; I went to this place in June 2015 (however I am sure if I went to this place again the review would be similar). A few days ago I was talking to someone about places visit in New Orleans because they are interested in visiting the city. I realized that when I went to New Orleans I went to a lot of amazing places but I never wrote Yelp reviews for them because I did not start writing Yelp reviews until the beginning of 2017. I enjoyed many places on my trip and I wanted to share my experiences with everyone  even though they are a few years old. So I decided to dig up some old pictures and write the reviews.

I would also like to add that most of the experiences I am writing about are places I went to while I was on a guided tour for my trip. I went on a Collette Tour called America's Music Cities. Most of the places we saw and ate at were planned because of the tour. During the tour we stopped at 3 major cities New Orleans, Memphis, and Nashville (and few other stops along the way). I just wanted to let everyone know that since I was on a tour my experiences may have been a little different compared to those who went to these places and were not on a tour (they went on their own) It was an amazing tour and I definitely recommend it.***

I went to the Ryman Auditorium for a tour. The Ryman is a beautiful place with a lot of Nashville history. I loved learning all about it and having the opportunity to see a piece of history. It is known as the Mother Church. The Ryman was a church before it became a home for the Grand Ole Opry (until the Opry moved however some Opry shows still perform here). The is also a mini Country Music Hall of Fame in the Ryman Auditorium where you could see some costumes people wore when they performed there. If you can, definitely visit the Ryman Auditorium especially if you like country music. 

I hope to go back someday and see a performance there. 

Enjoy!
Simona

We went to sambuca for our first meal in Nashville. 

Environment: excellent. Live music, great lighting, wonderful service, overall excellent ambiance. 

Food: for the price, it was okay. We got everything that was highly recommended by our server as being the very best, and it was decent- but not worth the upscale prices. We liked our cocktails and local brew, but the appetizers, salad and main course simply did not match the lovely environment. Although, desserts looked amazing, we were too full!

Love the tour and being able to learn the history of the building, of Nashville history and the history of the Grand Ole Opry. Seeing tonight's show (12/23/17). Most of the year the show takes place at a venue at Opryland, so we lucked out coming here midwinter. The posters and photos of past performers here was eye-opening. This old tabernacle is now referred by many as the church of country music. Taking a tour beforehand really is worth it. I had no idea of how close it came to be being torn down. Nice to see how they're preserving their musical heritage.

I'm glad I made it to this beautiful theater.  It's such an awesome piece of history.  I wish I could see a show here sometime.  
The self guided tour was best for me but you can get a backstage tour, get a picture on the stage or make a recording.  
You can see concert posters, suits & dresses worn by stars, guitars, walk through the theater, and history on the wall after watching a brief movie that gives the history of the theater.

I love Tin Roof!!!

I just got back from visiting my brother Nashville and while I was there I stumbled across this gem. I had been recommended to visit Honky Tonk Central, which I did, but I actually preferred Tin Roof. The environment at Tin Roof is casual, relaxed and fun. I also thought they had the best bands!

The bands play a lot of country but it isn't exclusively country. I went on a Wednesday from about 5-9 and on a Thursday night. You need to go and watch the band that plays every Wednesday from 330-7. I have never seen a band that was more relaxed, fun and was able to laugh at themselves. It is a trio and they are super chill and fun. It was the first and only band that I saw in Nashville (or ever, really) that was able to laugh at themselves if they made a small mistake (ex -- singing 90s song and voice cracked a little during a high pitched part...ha!). The mistakes aren't major but it is just refreshing to see 3 young guys having fun and just doing what they love - it is clear that they love it. They were funny and did a mix-up of 90s music when I was there -- Third Eye Blind, Blink 182, Incubus, etc. I had walked by earlier in the day and they were playing country. Overall, they were awesome!

The band that played after them from 7-11 (I think until 11) was also great but very different. They were much more intense (the other band was more relaxed and low-key) but these guys knew how to rock out. They were also really fun but very different energies. They played all country but I wasn't familiar with it all -- I would say it was a mix of older and newer songs. They were definitely talented.

The band two bands on Thursday were also great (one from 8-11ish in the front and the other in the back after 11). There was good dancing in the back when the second band set up for the rest of the night. 

The drinks are nothing fancy, so I am not looking for a craft cocktail when I am here. They do have happy hour specials from 3-7 and it is $1 off certain drinks (wells, etc.). I didn't try their food so can't speak to that.

The reason I took a star off is because of the bar service on Thursday night -- my mom ordered wine and it came in a plastic cup (which is fine) but the bartender only poured about an inch of wine in her glass. Really?! It was about $7 for an inch of wine...lame. I ordered a mixed well drink and it was fine. We switched bartenders later and he was better, however, their shots looked under-poured too. But, the 2nd bartender was friendly and attentive. Our waitress the day before was nice but I had walked to the bathroom and saw our drinks sitting there while she chatted w/other waitresses and they were still there when I came out - she brought them over right after that.

Overall, this is a great spot if you want to have some drinks, dance and listen to good music.

I was fortunate enough to see the CMA Honors here at the Ryman.   It was a great show and the experience of seeing anything at the Ryman is well worth it.  

There is nothing I can say about the Ryman which bring anything new to the equation from what all of the other reviewers have already stated .... so I won't even try.

What I will say however --- that as a boy from New Jersey who is not really experienced in the ways of County Music or Bluegrass (the Ryman certainly isn't the house that Springsteen built) I nevertheless could feel the history of the place and recognized the love which the people of Nashville have for it.   

If you get an opportunity to see a show at the Ryman, please don't pass it up.  This is a truly historical theater the likes of which are rare throughout this country.

This place is top notch from head to toe. We were seated right away when we arrive. All of the staff was extremely friendly and professional. Our waitress was timely to our table, asking us if we would like anything to drink. The entertainment for the night with setting up as we sat down. They begin playing around the time that we got our food. The entertainment was fantastic! All of the food that myself and two friends got was absolutely divine. We had a few small plates(buck beignets and duck breast), Gorgonzola salad, a pizza, and the filet mignon. Not to mention the cheesecake for dessert. The steak is one of the best I've had in my entire life.  We also had a few Tennessee mules, which were very light and refreshing. The waitress was even able to separate our checks, which made it very easy to pay. I highly recommend this establishment!!!! I came all the way from Florida to have a great experience in Nashville, and this place did it. I am going to have to definitely come back.

Fun to tour and learn the history. A place were souls were saved and bluegrass was born.  Sat in the old wooden pews and took in The Grand Ole Opry.  So cool to see so many stars from different era's and the fun they had interacting with each other and performing in a place that they love.

My oldest would give Plaza Mariachi 10 stars if he could! We were looking for a fun place to take our boys the night before the new school year. I found an amazing review about Plaza Mariachi and we were hooked! 

It was a Monday night and not very busy. There was still live music on stage in the food court area. There are halls that portray streets that run off of the food court. In these hallways are shops and art studios. Such a neat place!! 

For food we had a feast of oysters with a chimichurri sauce, salmon atop veggies, and an amazing dish that had potatoes, pico, steak and cotijo cheese all mixed together. 

After eating and listening to the lovely lady on stage (Luna Morena), our boys wanted to go to the arcade. They had a blast and blew through their $15 arcade card. The two oldest split the card and they got about 8 games out of it. The youngest played in the jungle gym.

We are all looking forward to a return trip!

This place is awesome; I love Nashville! Having read the reviews, I was hesitant to come here. After the conclusion of Vanderbilt Commencement 2017, we had lunch at Bricktops and ended up at Sambuca for dinner. 

As you walk in, you are met with a lively crowd which is ready to listen to some live music. Luckily for us, the Chris Weaver Band was in attendance and played everything from TLC to The Band. They absolutely killed it tonight!

Anyway, the Tennessee Mule drink was awesome and fairly alcoholic. We shared an order of the beignets filled with prosciutto and mozzarella cheese. For our entrees, four of us had the blackened red snapper on dirty rice. This dish stood out immensely! It was perfectly seasoned and a substantial portion. 

Come here for a good time!

This place is pretty magical - especially when you see the history and see how close it was to closing on a few occasions. 
We took the self guided tour through the Ryman which was the original home of the Grand Ole Opry. 
The space looks like an old church with bench seating and stained glass windows. 
Big names have played the Ryman for decades. It is not only blue grass or country music - it is The Pretenders, Jack White, The Foo Fighters. I think that can be a common misconception. The Ryman and Nashville in general seems to embrace all types of music. 
It's interesting to walk around the building and think about how many stars have performed there. If you are a history buff this is the place for you. I'm not sure that it's great for kids - not a lot for them to do. But if you are a music lover - you'll love it.

Man, I love Tennessee. Two things people here don't mess around with are their BBQ and their blues, or music in general. 

I insisted we come here, and so glad that we did. No cover charge, and the place was pretty big. We happened to come through on a Saturday when there was a pre-season game against the Falcons and a car show in the middle of downtown. Broadway was hopping and so was Robert's. We grabbed our beers and waded through the crowd to the upper level. 

The band came on shortly thereafter, and 18 year old Daniel from Memphis was guest starring with the band. Holy cow! I've been playing guitar for YEARS and this kid made me wanna hang up my strings in shame. The whole band just rocked. I sang along to Johnny Cash and other favorites. I was hoping for some Folsom prison blues, but ah, next time. 

Decent prices for a drink and a recession special for $5. I don't eat bologna but if I did, hell, I'd be all over it and a bag of chips. Which it comes with. And a PBR. What?! 

I mean, I don't think you're coming here for the food anyway, but if you were, you could eat a fried delight for a Lincoln. 

Amazing music, amazing vibe, amazing Nashville.

The building is great and the architecture is superb.  Place has plenty of room to have multiple events and nice views of downtown Nashville is nice!
Only pitfall is with all that great architecture there are people SMOKING outside on the patio areas and they are dropping cigarette butts all over the place - NASTY! 
It would be in there benefit to make the outdoors area a SMOKE FREE ZONE!  Bad when you try to sit at a table out on patio and about 25 cigarette butts are all around you; STINKS!

Stopped here for some drinks and music around noon on a Friday.  We were able to sit at the bar and order some drinks.  The drinks weren't cheap but they were good!  The singer that day was amazing and I could've easily listened to her all day.  The bar staff was great too...very friendly and offered their suggestions with no problem.  I would definitely come back next time we're in Nashville!
Solid breakfast. Very good biscuits and jam. Average coffee. Nice people and interesting history.

Loveless Cafe in Nashville has been cooking up their famous biscuits and southern food since 1951.  They now serve over 450,000 guests per year.

The Loveless Cafe serves down-home country food.  Their comfort food will remind you of grandma's house.  In 2005, USA Today named Loveless Cafe as America's "Top Down-Home Dining Spot." Loveless' famous "Biscuit Lady" Carol Fay became famous for her biscuits.  She has been on many television shows including the Ellen DeGeneres Show, The Today Show, the Martha Stewart Show and Late Night with Conan O'Brien.  The video below is Carol Fay the "Biscuit Lady" with Martha Stewart.  The Loveless Cafe serves their biscuits with amazing homemade preserves.  I was so excited to see they made and served my favorite preserves, blackberry.  It was perfect and delicious on their homemade light biscuits.  I do not get a commission for sending you to their site.  I truly just enjoyed The Loveless Cafe.

Loveless was a cute quaint little joint. It looked like your typical family style sit down restaurant. We heard that we had to have the biscuits and the ham. I ordered biscuits and gravy, bacon, and the chicken biscuit. The biscuits and gravy were phenomenal! They were just like mom's homemade stuff. The bacon tasted like it was fresh from the farm. The chicken biscuit was a complete let down. It was super tiny. Honestly, if you want a chicken biscuit, Chik Fil A is a much better choice. The peach, strawberry, and blackberry preserves were AMAZING! The waiter was super helpful and friendly, along with the rest of the staff. The BBQ guy, Eddie, was friendly and gave us the scoop on Nashville. The thing that was the biggest disaster is that we were initially sat on the patio seating area, after 30 seconds of siting there, we started to smell what we could only guess was vomit, so we asked to be seated inside. We were at this place on a Thursday morning and the wait was 10 minutes. Not bad considering the rest of the reviews on here mentioned much longer waits on the weekends.
Incredible southern cooking. The chicken gizzards and livers were the best I've ever had and the moonshine Marry was an amazing drink. Enjoy!!!

In town for the weekend so gave this raving place a try because everyone I spoke to in the area said "its amazing" or "you HAVE to try it".

The biscuits and jam are delicious and served as a free appetizer. It was SO good, I had 4 in one sitting! It comes out fresh and hot (you can see the area where cooks are making the dough and baking it). The jams are also homemade which pairs perfectly with the biscuits. I had peach, strawberry, and blackberry-all which tasted superb.

I had the veggie omlette with hashbrowns which were okay. Nothing spectacular. My friend had their fried chicken and says that it was tasty but nothing crazy. 

Service was over the top. I will definitely be back when I visit Tennessee!
Although the wait is long, the biscuits and jams really do live up to the hype! It's a Saturday well spent! I highly recommend the fried chicken and macaroni and cheese.

It's like eating at grandma house.  The first item they bring out is the biscuits. They are DELICIOUS.   I tried the blackberry preserves with them and it was my favorite. 

I ordered fried chicken with mashed potatoes and fried okra. Overall the meal was good but not overly special. The outside of the chicken was really tasty but the actual meat was bland. The mashed potatoes were good and you could taste the butter in it. Don't bother with the fried okra. It tasted like the frozen stuff.  

Service was excellent once we were seated.

Although it may seem like a tourist trap at first, Loveless Cafe is definitely a must-hit restaurant. The food is true southern cuisine, and the biscuits are to die for.  The service is exceptional.  They are models of southern charm. Truly wonderful experience overall.

i'm afraid this restaurant is losing its edge.  I will begin with the positive.  The cole slaw,  mac and cheese and the hash brown casserole were pretty good.  However, the green beans were sour, so I had to substitute something else.  The turnip greens were not very good, either.  If you order hoe cakes, they will charge you for them, but the server did not tell me that.  I thought the hoe cakes came with the meal.  Wrong!  The sweet tea was not good at all.  
This is about the third time we have eaten here in the last few months.  We kept thinking it would improve, but it hasn't.  Their breakfast is probably better.  The pecan pie was good.
I hate to see the quality of this restaurant go downhill.

I have live in the Nashville area since 1979, but have never ventured to the Loveless Café. There is a ton of hype out there about how this is the "be all - end all" mecca of Nashville country cooking...hmmmm

Party of 8 and none of us have ever darkened their doorway. It's a Thursday night and it is past 7:00 so seating and waiting was not an issue. Below I will list items ordered and the general consensus of all:

Fried Chicken - good - not great - good. In another lifetime I was the manager of a chicken restaurant. It takes at least 13 minutes to cook chicken fresh - we received ours in 10. Due to moisture content the dark meat was good. The breast - a little dry, but not bad - time to change the grease...

Meat loaf - good
Chicken livers - good, not great - slightly over cooked - time to change the grease...
Chicken gizzard - general consensus was that the breading was too sweet - again - time to change the grease...
Pulled pork - very good - huge portion!
Grilled pork chop - good
Biscuits - good - really don't understand the hype and the "top secret" recipe. Great starter to the meal, but definitely not "OMG!"
Mashed potatoes w/gravy - good - gravy seemed to be from a packet...
Cole slaw - very good
Cream corn - EXCELLENT!
Mac & cheese - very good
Turnip greens - too sweet - somewhat disconcerting...
Slow cooked green beans - "unique flavor" not necessarily good...no one wanted to take them home...
Caramelized sweet potatoes - meh...
Fried green tomatoes - good, but mostly breading - sliced too thin...
Cucumber and onions - excellent
Fried okra - good - again...time to change the grease...

Personally - I won't be back - too far and to me not a "destination" restaurant. Better - or at least equal - food can be found closer to home.
Great food and excellent service. The aroma was very good and cool shops to walk around and see while waiting. Definitely make time for the wait!
Wonderful breakfast! I had the Chicken & Waffles (so good!) Others in the party really enjoyed the hash brown casserole and omeletes. The biscuits and jam are 5 star!!
Country ham is not edible.  It was so salty even for some one that likes salty food. Biscuits were good but not great as others have mentioned. Grits were super rich from the heavy use of butter.

Absolutely the biggest tourist trap in Nashville. Just awful. Flavorless pork pounded flat, fries, worst Rueben ever, and two beers. $87 including tip. If you are into dropping substantial cash and having instant diarrhea from the low quality grease, then this is your dream restaurant. Enjoy!

The Friday special was hot chicken and it was the best we had in all of Nashville! Creamed corn was very good, and hash brown casserole was what you'd expect. Super nice waitress gave us a ton of biscuits and jam to go. Worth the special trip to eat here.

Great environment and great old fashioned food.  Portions are great and the biscuits are FANTASTIC!!!  They are very friendly and when we asked for orders to go they were very accommodating and did not skimp on the extras that would have came with the dishes if we were eating in house.    Yes the wait is long because it is that good.  We sat on a picnic benches and walked around the shops... we even played a little game of cornhole/bags.  It's a great way to spend an afternoon.

The biscuits are sometimes good, sometimes not. It used to be consistently amazing when the biscuit lady was around. Good fried catfish. Good cocktails with moonshine. Good fried chicken gizzards with gravy.

This was located off the beaten path. About 30min away from downtown. It is a drive but well worth it. If you're looking to feel like home and really get that warm feel, then this is the spot. Upon entering in the late afternoon, we were quickly seated. The server Owen was the best. Super attentive and helpful. He brought out warm fresh biscuits. It came with 3 different jelly spreads. Blackberry, strawberry, and peach. It was so good. The biscuits were hot and fluffy. with the homemade spread was a match made in heaven. Then we ordered the sweet tea as drinks. For our main dish I went with the half order of the loveless country ham, scrambled eggs, grits, and bacon. The country ham had a nice smokey taste to it. A thick cut and it was delicious. Better than any ham I've had before. Finished this off with the made from scratch banana puddin'. It was served cold and was a great way to end the meal. I'm so full yet so happy. The service here was also amazing. 

Recommendation: Country ham, biscuits, and banana puddin'
Best Biscuits I have ever tried in my life! Simply exquisite! And they make sure they bring plenty for everyone in the table! The staff was very very nice as well! The whole experience was very nice!

This has to be the best Listening Room I have ever visited.  I have been twice and now I I am hooked.  The small plates and Flatbread are outstanding as well as the acoustics. My next move is to become a Vino club member.The short ride up from the Huntsville area is well worth it

An exceptional cafe with a really homey feel, I felt like I was coming home, and I don't feel that way often enough. Very homey and down South interior, our waiter was highly attentive and incredibly sociable and kind. I was really impressed with the service. The meatloaf tasted like it was made straight from my family's secret recipe, it was incredible. The fried okra tasted amazing and the pickled salad I had was delicious as well. I was in a hurry to get in and get out this time around, I'm looking forward to returning and relaxing for the full experience. 10/10, would absolutely recommend.
Had terrific service from JaDee and of course the biscuits were amazing! You can't leave without a quick trip at the market and store they have on property.
If you don't eat here you will regret the fact that you are alive. Food? Perfect. Service? Perfect. AMBIENCE? Perfect. Love u, loveless.

Beer was good - or else it would be 1 star. Nothing else was, which is a bummer bc it seems like it has a lot of potential.  Not only were they playing the most horrendous dance music (this is a German restaurant, not a club), I had a hair buried in the bottom of my very bland Spaetzle.  The beer cheese was very watered down, and the "spicy" mustard was just yellow mustard.   As a Donelson resident, this bums me out bc we are already lacking restaurants.
Soooo good! I couldn't stop eating the catfish and I don't like fish. Everything you'd want southern food to taste like! Make sure you ask for Susan. She'll take care of you!

If you want to go to a hole in the wall tiny dive and listen to live music at any time, go here. The seats are ripped up, the people on stage will have a beer with you and the people in the crowd are musicians or locals having a brew with their girlfriend. We came in the middle of the day and the bartender was the sweetest person on Earth, but not pushy. The lady on stage almost seemed offended when I gave her money - there was no tip jar out which I thought was a bummer for them. Maybe people just try their stuff out here and don't expect money.

This place is set in a mall - close to the grand ole Opry house. It has a great bar and good, hearty food. 

On the night we went, a woman was singing, playing music and having a grand time on stage. She was good - kept guzzling her beer and was a terrific entertainer. That's what Nashville is known for - their entertainment even in the bierhouse. (No she wasn't singing country)

I have been to loveless several times now and it has never disappointed.  Their biscuits are absolutely amazing and we always eat up all the preserves that come with them.  Before I leave I always make sure to buy a couple jars of their peach preserves because they are my absolute favorite.  I've had the biscuit sampler breakfast, the meat sampler breakfast, and their fried pork chop breakfast (epic sized pork chops).  I always love everything.  Their ham and sausage is some of the best I've ever had.  The hash brown casserole is cheesy and decedent.  We always have a great server.  If you can get over the wait and enjoy the experience as a whole it is a great one.  It is an awesome place and I know we will be back many many times in the future.

Had to stop here since it's known as an iconic place to eat in Nashville. I was already expecting the wait to be 2 hours long, so that part didn't bother me a whole lot. Except that our dining experience wasn't really worth the wait. 

The food was good. Most of it was pretty basic that you can find anywhere but there were a couple of dishes that were done really well. However, the sweet tea was not sweet at all and was actually watered down horribly. After a few minutes when some of the ice melted, it tasted like you were drinking straight water. My biggest complaint though had to be all of the bugs. We had an outside table and I kinda knew to expect some bugs since we are Tennessee in the middle of summer. But we couldn't even enjoy eating at all because of all the flies, gnats and mosquitos. There were 2 yellow jackets that even flew into my purse! I'm really surprised that being such a busy and popular place, they don't put a screen around their outside dining area.

That being said, it's definitely a place to visit at least once. They have a little country store, complimentary lemonade and water set up outside, and other little shops to visit while you wait for a table. Our server was very friendly and the food was good. But probably a place to just visit once.

The food was awesome! We ordered the fried chicken and the meatloaf and it was the best fried chicken and meatloaf ever! All of the sides are good also! The biscuits and the preserves that come with every meal are so yummy!! Highly recommend buying more from the store behind the restaurant. The service is very friendly and food came out in a timely manner. I would definitely go back next time we were in Nashville!

We've walked by this beer joint several times since it opened and haven't checked it out even though I'm a beer nerd.  So, we went in today while out walking the mall and sat at the bar, I got a German beer and my wife a cider, which she said was very good and they said was exclusive to them.  After some discussion we decided to snack on some fries, these came with "beer" cheese, and "bacon".  Well, the fries had obviously been cooked hours before our arrival and kept in a warming tray which made them limp and lukewarm, the so called beer cheese was, as far as I could tell, cheese wiz out of a can, and the bacon was bacon bits out of a jar.  The server after checking in with us approximately ten minutes after they were delivered by the kitchen runner offered to replace them, needless to say we did not eat many of them, he did not offer a comp. Since we live across town from OpryMills I won't be disappointed that I'm not close by this place as we won't be back.
Loved everything Beers, pretzel& beer cheese, sausages, schnitzel but the MUSTARD is outstanding!!

Our bartender was awesome, so friendly and personable, as well as the host and concierge. We didn't make it in to a show, but I've heard great things. I just wasn't interested in the performer unfortunately. 

They have totally customizable flights from their wines by the glass menu, which is really nice. I do wish they'd have a few suggested flights on the menu as well though to keep the tastes complimentary.

We ordered the brussel sprouts, which were pretty good. We got sold on the wild mushroom flatbread. He said it was award winning. It was fine, lots of rapini and pretty salty. Another guest gave us the last couple pieces of his margherita flatbread and I liked that one more. I wish we would've tried the duck pizza instead, to be honest.

There were a lot of enticing menu options. I'll definitely be back.

I came here last year and knew that this was my favorite place in Tennessee. The biscuits are worth the hour wait, but the rest of the food is amazing too. The staff is excellent, everyone is so friendly even when it's super busy and I know how difficult that can be. I had the lunch special, which was chicken fried chicken, and it was fabulous! The breading was crunchy but not burnt and the chicken was moist which is hard to get perfect in the first place. Overall, this place is super cute, super fun and super delicious! I'll definitely make it back!

The gourmet's Cracker Barrell. 

This place is tremendous Southern cooking.   Bring a heart monitor.  If you're a Southerner, you'll swear your grandma is in the kitchen.   

The ONLY reason I don't give them a 5 star rating is that they're just so hard to get into.  Hour, 2 hour waits are common.  You may have to hike a quarter mile to get there from the back of the parking lot(s).  On the weekends, there's no good time to get in.   The first time you come the shops are enough to keep you occupied, but they lose their charm after a few times.

Such a cute place with gift shops to adventure in while you wait for a table. Their biscuits are sooo good with a wide selection of jams. They offer a good breakfast, lunch, and dinner menu. Kid friendly with loud positive atmosphere.

In my global pursuit of the best fried chicken, I was very pleased with the birds from the Loveless Cafe - crispy, well seasoned, not too greasy. And the biscuits rock! In addition, the place is kind of a time capsule from the past - worth the drive from downtown and not too bad of a wait at dinner time.
Really good onion soup! Very nice staff and people in general. Beer was tasty and cold. Can't wait to watch the music. I'll be back.

I was not impressed. I decided to park on the street because I don't mind walking instead of paying the $5 valet. The atmosphere was great and we were seated immediately. Out of the six items on the menu (it seemed) they were out of half of the things on the menu. I wasn't very hungry so I got the brisket taco. They were $11, micro mini in size, little flavor, cold, and the brisket was tough and dry. The risotto balls were great. It took forever to get our checks. I won't be back. There are too many decent restaurants in Nashville to choose from.

Live close by and eat here frequently. Occasionally can be seated quickly but usually a wait. It's just home style COOKIN and typically good for when you want fried food and country veggies. We like seeing all different people and visitors from out of town. Occasionally will see country music stars as we have a few times who also live close by. Miss the biscuit lady yet her recipe lives on...

What an interesting and picturesque place. Attended with a work group, and was happily surprised at how much variety is on the menu and as advertised, a great wine selection.

3 stars comes from a bit of a bar issues and the seating arrangement.  When ordering $15 scotch, the bar should know the difference between 'neat', 'on the rocks' and 'one cube'. Several of us had to send back our drinks due to being served incorrectly.  Note to the bar, I can tell by the taste and aesthetics when you just strained the ice out vs pouring the drink correctly, neat as ordered.  Secondly, when you have 8 full size grown men sitting shoulder to shoulder, it makes for an uncomfortable night.  It would have been nice to have a larger and more comfortable table for our group size.

The food was great, everyone loved their orders, and service was prompt.  Overall a good experience.

I spent a day in Nashville and was going to head out of town and grab breakfast along the way. We saw the sign on the highway and decided to check it out. So happy we did! The biscuits and jam were the best things ever!!! Out waitress was so sweet. The food came out fast and had generous portions. They even gave me a coffee for the road! Everyone should definitely check this spot out.

Loved having bbq and eggs for a classic southern breakfast. The biscuits here are absolutely jaw dropping as well! I do wish I could just get one pancake off the menu rather than only stacks of 3, but the great food makes up for that. Service was outstanding as well, and it really is a good southern dining experience

So you wait an hour and a half, big deal!!! The food is absolutely worth it. Hands down the best friend chicken and biscuits I've ever had in my life. 

I seriously can't think of one complaint that I have, other than the wait. But again, it was worth the wait. Put your name in and then walk around. The Pumpkin Butter is to die for. The honey unbelievable, the blackberry preserves NOM NOM NOM.

Honestly I can't wait to go back, and if I'm ever traveling even remotely near Nashville again this is the first pit stop I will make.

Ok Folks, listen real close. If you're visiting Nashville, you have to put Loveless on your list. This place will not disappoint. Tonight I had the smoked pork chops, caramel sweet potatoes, and turnip greens. And it was just like Mom's. The biscuits are life changing, so leave plenty of room for them (they come out as an appetizer). There is plenty to see while you wait for your table, so stop by and enjoy Southern Hospitality at its finest!

We decided to try out Loveless due to all the hype.  Honestly, we all wish we had the 2 hours of waiting we lost from our lives back.   Its a quaint little place - I suppose it's good we tried it once.   

The food is decent - but not worship worthy as many have claimed.   Overall, we (party of 3), would say if you have a 20 min or less wait - it's worth it - but if you have to wait more than an hour, skip it.  You can do better.  We had the biscuits, fried chicken, fried green tomatoes, mac n cheese, turnip greens, fried okra, breakfast eggs, bacon.   

Service was great - it's just the balance of the time you have to wait for the quality of food you get....medium food - LOOOONG wait...nope - not worthy.

Why is this place famous?

The biscuits are good, but they're not magical. Butter and salt. 

We had biscuits and gravy, and the sausage gravy was standard, boring fare. Nothing to it really. 

We'd heard that this place is always crazy busy, so we came first thing in the morning. We were here 15 minutes after they opened - third family in the door - and the service was still terrible. The server brought gravy and said he was going back for a fresh batch of biscuits ... and then got distracted or something. So we got warm biscuits and then had to ask for fresh gravy. My husband ordered a side of cheesy grits that came out later, and sans cheese. 

The side of fresh fruit was good. 

All in all, if you want to check off a tourist destination, fine. (Be prepared: it's priced like a tourist trap.) If you want a good breakfast, go somewhere else.

Breakfast review...Pricey, have to say that right off the bat.  We ordered a la carte for the most part, to try different menu items.  My scrambled eggs were good, not overcooked, the in-house, smoked bacon was really delicious, grits were smooth and the hash brown casserole was tasty but I thought it had a little too much cheese in it.  I know, I know, can there ever be too much cheese?  I  would have like to taste onion, maybe even some green pepper.  The biscuits were very tasty and personally I'm glad they are small.  The country ham was thick (we like it on a the thinner side though), not over-salted and had a great flavor.  The service was excellent, waiter friendly, bringing out a plate of biscuits and 3 servings of homemade jams. We arrived at 7:15am and the cafe was half full.  When we left at around 8am they had a wait.  Though the line was moving, I would suggest making a reservation, even that early!  There are cute little shops surrounding the cafe.  All in all a good experience and we will go back again for other breakfast items and for lunch/dinner.

A family tradition that never gets old. Loveless is a timeless classic in Music City and receives frequent visits from the local country stars. 

Make sure to try their famous loveless biscuits and fried chicken. It's stick to your ribs good!

Visited November 2013
Great food, service, ambiance. Wat there at least once every 10 days. Staff is the best. Have to wait a bit? Just visit the cool shops on property!

This place is so cute and cozy! We was welcomed with a very friendly staff that showed true southern hospitality. The country fried steak was massive and some of the best I've had. You'll definitely not leave hungry!

Awesome little authentic slice of the South from food to the moonshine to the little stores around the restaurant. The biscuits and jams are worth a trip alone. After you visit make sure you take a little drive over the Natchez Parkway and take in the beautiful countryside of Franklin and Leipers Fork.

Best pulled pork I have ever had.  The sides were amazing too...  I highly recommend the hash brown casserole and mac n cheese, which were both excellent.  The biscuits were good but nothing special, although they bring them out complimentary so no complaints.  The jams they serve with them, however, were very good.  Expect a long wait...my wife and I waited 2 hours, but planned ahead and took a scenic drive down the Natchez Trace parkway so no big deal.  Probably not someplace I would eat often but worth at least one trip.  Good place to bring friends or family visiting Nashville.

First, it has to be hard to do live music AND good food in the same space, so my expectations were not that high. It was a good time, and the music, environment, stage and service were all good. Food was decent, not excellent and pricey for the quality. Here's the problem: You're forced to Valet ($5 + tip) and they have this LBDT tax; (as far as i know the only establishment in town that does.) Sales Tax + LBD Tax + Food Tax = 20%!!!!!!! Add another  20% tip on your bill and be ready to add 40% to your bill. (A $7 beer will cost you $10. That $22 Trout entree? $31. I'll be back, but will fill up somewhere else before hand......

We really wanted to like this place since they are getting some music on the books that we like, and want to see, but I will be hard pressed to return. We have been to City Winery twice now. The first time we went, we did as the website had suggested which was to come between 6-7 for dinner before the show. WAY too early, as it was awkward to be in the music venue with all these empty tables around you. It just felt weird. The food wasn't that great either. The only thing we ordered that we liked was the truffle fingerling potatoes. The flatbread was soggy, and the cheese plate was underwhelming and expensive for the stingy portions.  We were disappointed that a winery boasting such a large list doesn't sell any bottle of wine for under $40. 

The second time we went, we ate dinner beforehand and decided to just have some wine during the show. We ordered a 2010 Malbec that she opened right when she got to the table (in the dark - you can't see!) and poured for us to taste, BUT we were never shown the bottle until she had poured it out and walked away. It was 2011. Not a big deal for inexpensive wine, but if I had been buying a $200 bottle that was wrong, I would have been incensed.

When we got the bill, (it had slipped past us on our previous visit) we noticed that they charged the Liquor By The Drink tax that EVERY other restaurant in the ENTIRE STATE builds into their pricing, but City Winery charges it ON TOP of your already overpriced drink. So a $40 is really $46, a $15 whiskey is $17.25 plus sales tax etc...it is in small print on the menu, but you feel gouged already, and then that tax just seems like a big F-You. 

Paying for rude valets who don't even unlock the door for you, much less open it, plus overpriced food that isn't good, and really overpriced drinks just made us feel nickeled and dimed. Unlike others, we did have good service inside the venue. Again, I wanted to like this place - the upstairs patio has beautiful views of downtown and it's a nice space, but we just feel like it's not worth what you end up spending for an evening there.

I'm from California. There no place like this back home. This is one of the best meals at the best price I've ever had. Had fried chicken, mashed potatoes and gravy and creamed corn. Trust me if you are anywhere near this place, get over here.
Bier selection is great.  Food is very authentic.  Had the Leberkase brotchen and it tasted just like what I had for breakfast every morning when I lived in Germany as a kid.  My new favorite place.

What an awesome place! Cool decor, great fiod, fast service! A must go to!!! My best friend and I started our roadtrip here and it was a Friday morning. I was surprised at how busy they were but the service was fast. The food was phenomenal especially the biscuits!

I met up with a friend for lunch on a weekday and was so surprised at how big the restaurant was. Their food was okay, nothing that made me feel like I needed to come back. I was a little surprised that you couldn't substitute side dishes but it wasn't a big problem. The service was great and I'm sure their beer menu is awesome!

Absolutely a blast for fun, excellent German cuisine! Group of 6 enjoyed the in Opry Mills Mall dinner with live music and great beer and food. Very open and loud! Great service and servers all dress authentic. Food $15-21.00. Would highly recommend! I had Black Forest schnitzel! Yum

It's a good venue. I've been to both the main room and the little white building across the street. The main room is amazing. I went for a CMT taping of Crossroads so they definitely had a great setup. Many times venues overdue it or even under do it so the sound quality of the bands is very mediocre, but not here. Excellent.

We visited the Loveless (again) during one of the busiest times of the year for Nashville! CMA week. We even arrived at 9am. Waited ZERO minutes for a table and was promptly served those amazing melt in your mouth biscuits that I crave the other 364 days of the year when I can't visit. Our meal was perfect! I always recommend the Loveless to anyone visiting Nashville. Most folks go the "long way" there but it is quite a bit nicer to drive Broadway away from Nashville to see some beautiful homes along the way instead of freeway. I've sent hockey teams to the Loveless in the past and they are still talking about it. And hoping to have another tourney there this year (me too! I wanna come back). Thanks for consistent excellent customer service and food quality. I never fear recommending the Loveless to folks! See you soon!

Best home style cooking you can get! It seems to always be busy but it's worth the wait. Plus they have little stores to keep you entertained while you wait. Everyone is very friendly and have southern hospitality. After getting seated and ordering, the wait for your food isn't that long. And if anything is wrong they will make it right. Pies are to die for! And FYI the moonshine are very strong!

Just freaking good. I had the fried chicken (1/4 white meat - amazing), turnip greens (amazing), and mashed potatoes (really, really good). And of course, biscuits with blackberry jam that was to die for.
