This is one of those places where you just have to stop caring temporarily about things like calories, sodium, etc., and simply go for it.

Brunch this morning. Good food huevos rancheros and build your biscuit. The decor is awsome and concert venue looks great. It has a warm fire place right in the middle of the room. Will return for dinner and drinks.

To begin, the food was four stars. We had the fried chicken and catfish, with creamed corn and caramel sweet potatoes. All of it was very good. The jam was also delicious! 

The reason I rate loveless three stars is because of the hostess and the lady working the cash register.  Not only did they lack southern hospitality, they lacked any hospitality. I am hoping it was just an off day and not a usual occurrence.

Biscuits are heavenly, sides are flavorful and fresh. We had the fried chicken, I felt that the crust was a bit dry, but overall, a great meal. Great atmosphere and a cozy gift shop. The jams and jellies are to die for!

The single best biscuits I have ever had in my life. In fact the only downside to the biscuits themselves is the fact that I don't live in Nashville and they have ruined all other biscuits for me. 

The atmosphere of the restaurant is quaint and clean and the service from our waitress was fantastic. Unfortunately there is quite a long wait on the weekends but it is well worth it and they do have outdoor seating for you to wait on and some neat little stores nearby to peruse. 

In conclusion the biscuits are so good that I will someday return to Nashville just to come get these biscuits again.

Went for lunch, arrived quarter to 12, around 15mins wait then people started to arrive. Friendly staff esp our server Mark. The biscuits are really good. Too much food, we brought home some. Love the strawberry preserves.

Be prepared to wait a long time with a lot of tourists on weekends! But then be prepared for some of the best southern food ever. I have never had anything that I did not like. This place is definitely worth all the hype, and the biscuits are delicious.

I love the atmosphere and we always eat here before seeing a movie at the opry mills regal. The fish and chips are my favorite. I prefer sitting in the bar area because it can get really loud. I prefer the guy entertainment over the girl because he sings du hast by Rammstein and we always request it. Love it! Lol!

Just WOW! From the moment we arrived, everything was perfect. The decor is modern, but homey. The venue has wonderful sound and allows for the most intimate feeling. The food is....ahhh, simply delectable. They have a wide variety. Ask about the specials. I bet you change your mind five times trying to pick the best item. 
I have nothing but praise for every aspect of City Winery. Don't miss a chance to dine here, and if at all possible, take in a show.

This place was fun and all of the food was reasonably priced and good quality. The chicken was top notch. The biscuit sampler was good. The fried chicken tender batter (for the biscuit) tasted like panko and left me wishing i'd gone for something different. The pork, bacon, pimento cheese and fried green tomato biscuits were really nice. The tea was perfect, not too sweet. We all shred everything. My 7 year old who hates everything loved the macaroni. She also loved watching the biscuits being cut and the chicken being fried. 

We will definitely be back the next time we are near Nashville!

Having spent nine years of my military career being stationed in German, I got excited seeing this in the mall. Ordered a .05L beer and giant pretzel, both were delicious and exactly what I remembered. Ordered the jagerschnitzel and my wife had the currywurst. Both were so far from what I remember. My meal was bland and soggy, the spaetzle had an odd texture. The kitchen manager said that the currywurst came premade and wasn't sure if the frying oil for the schnitzel was hot enough. Both meals were a bust. Not to mention no brotchen or cucumber salad which traditionally comes with a meal were available. Unfortunately, this was a huge letdown.

One of our good friends who LOVES food came into town so I brought him for a taste of the Loveless Cafe!  This is an update so check my first review for more details.

When we sat down at 6:50pm, we learned that their daily special (Chicken and dumplings on this particular Wednesday) was out already.  My friend wanted to try it so that was a minor disappointing start to our meal but with so many other delicious options, we weren't sad for long.

Some updates on the food experience:
Pulled pork - tender, flaky (shreds apart), smokey and flavorful.  It was much more moist this time!
Fried chicken - crispy, moist but lacked flavor inside with good seasoning on the outside
Fried catfish - squeeze a little lemon on the top, a little dip into the tartar sauce and yes, the bombness in your mouth.

A lowlight was having undercooked hush puppies served to me but the server quickly replaced it with another requested side (creamed corn).  Fried okra, Mac 'n Cheese, and sweet peach tea rounded out the meal.  Note to self for future orders, I don't like their turnip greens - a bit bland with a kick of pepper/spice.

Tip: It's always good to call ahead for a shorter wait time.

Extra: my friend is really into smoking stuff so we stopped by their smoker and were allowed to take a peek into how they make their smoked meats.

The berry jams were great. Biscuits are soft, think dinner roll more than biscuit. Ham was super salty, if you like that, this is your place. Lines are long, visit the shop while you wait. Our wait was 1.5 hours. Service was good and friendly.

Big birds flying across the sky
Throwing shadows on our eyes
Leave us...
[Loveless], [loveless], [loveless]

Having read of "bottomless biscuits", we were disappointed by a lack thereof, apparently not part of the slow service and separate charges for a change in teas (but not for refills after the switch, but given the speed, it wasn't worth mentioning because our time is valuable) despite no mention originally.
$37.79 before tip for:
biscuit sampler with chicken and hashbrown casserole (satisfying)
breakfast sampler (tasty)
two sweet teas, and a peach iced tea (the latter was excellent, the former eh)
fudge pie (tasty but nontraditional)
No creamed corn until 11 (foolish)

If we hadn't also planned a Belle Meade visit as part of our morning, I would've been a bit disappointed about trekking out here (if this is still considered Nashville, you folks really take some liberties with the zoning). Apparently they were on Throwdown, and management changed at some point recently, causing the commercialization that kinda ruined the charm for me.
This place was really good. A colleague told me about this place and I gave it a try. The food and the service was superb. The hash brown casserole was my fave

Oh the hype...these poor biscuits didn't have a fighting chance to stand up to such praise. Maybe I'm too much of a biscuit aficionado or too critical. Either way, these biscuits were good, but not nearly the best I've tasted. 

Driving into the Loveless parking lot around noon on a Saturday, we expected the 2 hour wait for our party of nine. We browsed the little village off shops that Loveless has going on for you while you wait. And 1.5hrs and $60 spent on merchandise later, we made our way into the restaurant. 

Even before all of our butts were in our chairs, they set down two plates teeming with dozens of the infamous biscuits and jam. With our tummies rumbling like they were, of course they tasted good. As famished as I was and as warm as these buttery biscuits were, I still instantly acknowledged that they paled in comparison to the biscuits I've fallen in love with at a pie shop back in Chicago. 

I found the texture of these biscuits to be too uniform throughout. These guys lacked the exterior toasty crunch that only makes you appreciate the soft and crumbly insides that much more. You need that contrast in texture in a top notch biscuit. I was also saddened by the lack of moisture in the biscuit and the much too dry crumb.

Biscuit disappointment aside, the omelettes were impressively large and stuffed with ingredients. The pancakes were hearty and the maple syrup was somehow exceptionally tasty. I felt the need to try a half order of their country ham and was surprised by my dislike. Ask anyone, I am a huge fan of ham but this was salty to the point of being inedible. Honestly, I took two bites of this $7 slice and didn't go for more.

While overall on the disappointing side, I'm glad to have experienced the institution that is Loveless.

this cafe has a super cute location. i expected to find the restaurant by itself & in a remote location. but it along with it, there's a gift shop & fun games. i had to wait for a little while but it was okay because it gave me time to explore the area. once i got my food, i was so excited. i got a waffle with fresh strawberries & hash brown casserole & it was SO GOOD. i dream about the hash brown casserole constantly. the waffle tasted like any other waffle but i would definitely go back when i'm back in nashville. highly recommend!!
Great venue. Food options aren't great in choices or pricing. I'll be back, but I'll eat first.

The best service and breakfast food you can eat north of Alabama!!! Brisket and Eggs makes you want to come back everyday of the week.
And Have I mentioned the biscuits.... Well, you will never want to leave! If you visit Nashville, it's a must for breakfast & stop by "The Halal Guys" for lunch or dinner! Not far from each other, you are on the west side of Nashville

This is the perfect place for a good brunch, especially if you are from out of town. The atmosphere was so pleasant, and the customer service was perfect. We had to wait a few minutes to be seated, but our waiter was extremely attentive, and our food came out quickly. Food was fresh and correctly prepared. No complaints here, and would definitely recommend.

One of my all-time  favorites and a must for out of town visitors! Average wait is about an hour but the shops on property will help that pass quickly. I have always preferred breakfast here but I've never had a bad meal.

Good Food, Great Staff, can be a little oud and overwelming at times though. The first time we went in we ate at the floor table, community style, and the place was rockin. The 2nd time, we ate a wall table, hightop, leggs dangling. The last couple of times, we have sat at the bar Hightops, and it's quieter, more comfortable, and enjoyable.

Recommend for a date night for sure.
Very good food.   Service was phenomenal.   Sophia was so nice and helpful with the menu and recommending drinks.  We will be back.

Traditional American breakfast options, nothing spectacular. They are famous for their biscuits and homemade jams and I have to say they didn't disappoint, which for someone who's never liked biscuits is saying a lot. The steak, eggs and home fries were okay but under seasoned. The French toast was also pretty bland and traditional.
Possibly the best breakfast restaurant I have visited. Great history, atmosphere, and traditional southern breakfast. There was a wait but well worth it!
Best biscuits we have ever had.  Food was definitely worth the wait. Real friendly atmosphere.  Ask for Owen the waiter,  he will treat you like family.

Loveless Cafe takes you back to the 1950s when Lon and Annie Loveland first opened their roadside restaurant. We drove from downtown Nashville (about a 20 minute drive) and arrived around 9:00am on Labor Day to a 20-30 minute wait. During our wait we walked around the Loveland shops. They sell so many different gifts- sweets, jams, biscuit mix, shirts, postcards, jewelry, magnets, home goods, etc. across a few different shops all adjacent to one another. They have corn hole and other games too. All of these things help keep you busy while you wait for your table. The biscuits are amazing, try the darkest jam and request honey. We got french toast, bacon, eggs, fried steak, and hash brown casserole, all worth trying.

HOLY MOLY, now this is some DAMN good Home Country Cooking.  I had some great Fried Chicken, wonderful Catfish and amazing Country Ham.  

Our Server was the best, he was on top of things, funny and didn't miss a beat with anything we needed.  

The best thing, we happened to see Billy Ray Cyrus and Johnny Van Zant while we were there...Hell, if it's good enough for them, it's good enough for me.

I was really thinking about going back there for dinner every night....it was that good.
This is how you do country breakfast, and it doesn't help when it's at the end of you road.
Amazing authentic German food.  Shintzel was great and get the pretzel and Bier cheese as an appitizer

Ate here the other night.  Still being on ny time we get that about 5:45 and we had no line.  There were 4 in our party, 2 adults and 2 kids.  My youngest eats nothing so be ordered macaroni and cheese with a side of mac and cheese from the kids menu which was delicious.  The rest of us ordered different dishes and sides to taste everything.  Nothing disappointed us.  Keith, the manager, stopped at our table and when he learned that we were from ny and tasting all southern food, he brought us samples of some of the things we did not order.  Keith also brought us a molasses/agave type of spread that is available to all but you need to request it.  Keith taught us to mix this with butter and spread on a biscuit.  This was amazing!  So was the hasbrown casserole, creamed corn, fried chicken, hot chicken, stringbeans, pork and catfish.  We liked the city ham better than country ham.  Skip the fried green tomatoes.

We had a great time last night at the City winery . We enjoyed the music with Andrew Ripp and the food we had was really good . We had the risotto balls , hummus plate, flat bread, chicken, and slaw with cranberries, almonds and Brussels. Everyone enjoyed their food. My only complaint is hard seats which is an issue when you are sitting for hours.

Iconic. Classic. Consistently good on all levels. What's not to love? There are places that do individual things better, but few that pit out a comparable total package. Just be prepared to wait a bit on most nights, or use their take-out or catering services.

Get there early, the other reviews are right on about that. It can take a year and a day to get a table, but that's not why I rated it so low. I anticipated the end all be all breakfast when I looked over the menu, and what I got was a glorified Cracker Barrel. I can get eggs, biscuits, and meat anywhere, and these biscuits aren't even close to being the best metro Nashville has to offer. Not worth the wait, not worth the hype, not worth the money.
We stopped in for $5 double shots. All delicious. We left because it was like 7pm and empty. But definitely good for a start of the night double shot!
Long wait. Huge portions. The Sunday special was smoked brisket. Simply the best I've ever had. The creamed corn side was similarly memorable. Great food at a modest price at a Nashville institution.

We came here mainly for the biscuits because they were advertised as The Best biscuits in Nashville, or maybe all of Tennessee. They were very good, they were buttery and soft, but our first batch wasn't that hot. They were probably sitting around for awhile. Also, I would have liked it a little browner and crispier on top. We asked our waiter for more and the 2nd batch was a little hotter. The preserves they give you with the biscuits were the best part of the meal I thought. We got some to take home. 

I was debating between the country ham and the smoked pork chops with the peach preserve glaze. Our waiter said he loved the pork chops, so I ordered them. They were good, but a little on the tough side for me. I loved the peach glaze on it though. Maybe I should have got the ham. 

Overall, it was a very good meal and we are happy that we visited this famous Nashville restaurant. The service was very attentive and friendly. If we are ever back in the area, I would like to try to come back for breakfast.

This cafe is awesome.  Cute decor, polite servers, amazing biscuits. We loved it so much we came back the next day for breakfast round two.
I loved the peach jam, pulled pork bbq, biscuits and hash brown casserole. 
Loveless gets pretty busy somehow we beat the crowds both days.  A must see if you find yourself in Nashville.

I've been here now 3 times and have been consistently impressed with the food and the service.  From great appetizers like the giant pretzel to the cheese fries, you are in for carbohydrate heaven.  The sausages, the sauerkraut and schnitzels have all been great.  
The Bierhaus is very open and nicely draped with hops and murals.  It seats over 600 so you should be able find a seat, but may share the table with others.  The restaurant is set up as a proper beer garden.  
They have excellent German beers from well known German breweries with a variety of glass sizes.
Don't come if you're on a diet.  You'll leave stuffed and happy.

After moving to Nashville & hearing all the raving reviews about loveless, I was really excited to try it. Unfortunately, loveless did not live up to my expectations. The food was average. They wanted to charge over $3 for an 8 oz (maybe 12 at best) of Apple juice. The biscuits were ok as well. However, the staff was nice. IMO, you won't miss anything if you choose not to go.
Fourth of July visit! We had to wait to be seated but the food was every second worth it!! :)

I love loveless cafe because of the history and atmosphere, but recently it's gone a little downhill. The biscuits and homemade jam are always good and the chicken n dumplins they serve on Wednesdays are delicious. Unfortunately everything else is just average.

The bad:
White corn grits were soupy and tasteless, even with cheese. 

The good:
Fried chicken was yummy, but missing something.... Salt? Heat?
Fried green tomatoes were good. 

The great:
Love the biscuits with peach preserves! The pork was yummy too.  
The hash brown casserole didn't blow my mind until I got home and reheated it. 
Peach tea, half sweet and half unsweetened was pleasantly flavorful without being too sweet. 
The moonshine bloody Mary was good and the tiny souvenir Jar was a nice touch. 

If I come back, I'm going to the store for peach preserves and biscuit mix!!!

Very cool venue, but it has the absolute worst layout of any music venue I've ever visited.  The bar is tucked away in the back corner, and it's damn near impossible to get a drink.  The layout dictates that the bar line cuts straight through the middle of the venue, inconveniencing the people trying to watch the show AND the people trying to get a beer.

Incredibly awkward and counter-intuitive layout, and not a very comfortable place to watch a show, but four stars because of the cool vibe and the incredible bands they book.  The mix on the music always sounds great, too.

We enjoyed our visit very much everyone was very friendly the place was very neat to look at all the pictures of the famous people there it was fun just sitting around the area they told us 45 minute wait it took about 55 pretty good on judging time just a little disappointed there was no really big gift shops it looks like they had plenty of room but they just weren't there otherwise we had a beautiful day and would definitely go back

Fantastic southern food, huge variety, and great drinks to boot. It's just a shame that so many people know about this place; there's always a huge wait (I've never waited less than 30 mins, and sometimes as much as 2 hours). On occasion I find it worth the wait, but usually I'll just go elsewhere.

My boyfriend and I drove over to see Steve Hackett in concert (so rare to find progressive music in the south) - went to the show with my brother who lives in Murfreesboro. The sound & stage were great, it was excellent to hear some old Genesis music and to see Hackett live again.

We really enjoyed our visit & this venue. We had excellent seats to see the stage, enjoyed the wine we ordered and the cheese tray. We didn't order any dinners or desserts, so I can't speak for anything else (I intend to come back and check it out though). My only real complaint is that our server did take a while to get to us originally & frankly we didn't see her again until near the end of the show. In fact, I had wondered if she stopped at the table and I just didn't hear her - but boyfriend and brother said no (which we had ordered a carafe and no one was trying to get lit, but I would have ordered one more glass if she had shown up again). However, I saw other servers constantly at their tables, so in this situation it was the server assigned to us. I didn't take off a star for that because it really didn't unduly affect us....though in most cases, that definitely would put a damper on your evening.

We opted not to use valet parking and drove around to a backside area where there was one other parked car - which made us a bit nervous since we didn't exactly know what it was like in that area. We weren't far from the venue though - and walking with two guys I felt more comfortable (by myself would have been a bit intimidating). I think valet parking is fine (and at our show it was 5 bucks, so easily affordable) - however when the show ended there was quite the wait & line for valet parking to return cars, so in that instance, not using it worked out better for us.

They've had several people there I'd like to see - but most of the shows have been on weeknights and it has to be somebody really special and rare to get me to take off work and drive 6 plus hours. Though I do have family in this area, so now I may schedule my family visits around who is playing. ;)  I greatly prefer small venues and being able to order food and drinks that are a step up from the usual "bar food & drinks" is nice. Once I've had a chance to go again, I'll update this review.

Biscuits for dayssssssss. Their peach and blackberry jams are just scrumptious. 

On the other side of breakfast, my entire family went savory - eggs, bacon, sausage, grits, hash brown casserole, etc. Overall, everything was super salty. But our wait was only 20 minutes... If we had waited the two hours that a lot of people say they wait, we probably wouldn't have been as happy.

It's been 6 months since I went to the Loveless and I'm counting down the days til I can return. Everything we ordered amazing: Southern sampler, country ham, fried chicken, fried green tomatoes and of course biscuits and jam!! As an NJ resident, dreaming of returning, keep up with Loveless Cafe on social media, they are very interactive and post beautiful food pictures that have me checking the prices on flights to Nashville on a regular basis!
It is solid and the biscuits are perfect, but the wait can be a bit tedious after a certain hour in the morning.

From one meal at Loveless, I can see why this place has the reputation it does. 10:00 am on a Thursday and the wait was 35 minutes long. Luckily, they give you a buzzer so that you can wander the multiple gift shops on the property while you wait. Before we knew it, our outdoor table was ready and a huge pile of biscuits was plopped on our table. Holy hell, they are addictive! Served with unbelievably fantastic peach preserve, as well as strawberry and blackberry preserve and sorghum syrup...honestly I would have been happy just eating these as my meal! 

But then our gigantic plates of food arrived, meats and eggs and grits and cheesy hash brown casserole. Everything was excellent and we stayed full and in a food coma until 6 pm that night, I kid you not. The Loveless staff was excellent and a few servers came by and chatted with our table. We loved the food and hospitality!

Honestly I would have given loveless cafe a 5 star and they should get it for there food. However, the reason I'm giving the 4 stars is for the rude hostess, Brittany. She had ruined the experience at first because she was giving us attitude from the beginning when we walked in. However the wait was worth it because the food was amazing. Large portions that were made to perfection. Our waitress Cindy was amazing and suggested great entrees to try. I had the bbq breakfast and it was so savory an delicious I highly recommend it.

One of the best breakfasts I have ever had. I really enjoyed my pork chops, but the highlight were the biscuits. LOVED THEM!!!  Great friendly service too. I can't wait to visit again. Too bad I live in CA.

Overall, I had a very pleasant experience at the Loveless Cafe last weekend. I was there on a double date with old friends. The wait (starting at 5 PM on a Saturday) was an hour and a half, but we had planned ahead and showed up well before we were hungry. We killed the wait by playing corn hole and checking out the shops. 

The biscuits were solid. They didn't beat the homemade biscuits that my southern family makes, but the blackberry, peach and strawberry jam that they were served with was delicious. 

We each got the drink special of the night, a Strawberry sipper. It was essentially lemonade with strawberry rye whiskey and was fairly sweet. It was perfect for my taste, but not for the guys'. 

Our waiter was friendly and hilarious. The service was fast and each of us enjoyed our meals. I got the catfish sandwich with grits and it was certainly well done. 

If you go there with good company and expecting a long wait, the Loveless Cafe is a good place to grab some southern food. I'm not sure I would go there over the summer though because most of the waiting areas are outdoors and a long, hot wait would have made us miserable.

Addition: We did not feel rushed at all while we there. In fact, we actually felt that the restaurant did not have the focus on volume that other places had. While we were there, we commented that we appreciated how much space they had put in between the tables.
Biscuits are amazing. Best I have ever had. Every time I come I wonder why I don't come more often. It is great. Best pulled pork anywhere!

If you take the time to go anywhere to eat in Nashville this should be your number one choice! The biscuits were the best I've ever had and they are free!! There is always a long wait, but if you go during nonpeak hours it's not too bad. Plus they have a little shop to look around in while you wait.
Make sure to take some of those golden biscuits home with you...great for heating up in the microwave. This place is famous for a reason.
Great service and amazing sides. You will have to wait most nights, but you know what you are getting into and the food and staff never disappoint.
You can get better food at a chain restaurant. Not worth the over an hour wait time. Neat place to see, but eat somewhere else.

I wish I could of just gotten the biscuits.  We were driving from Chicago to Orlando and my wife insisted we stop at Loveless for dinner so I humored her.

It is in the middle of nowhere but thankfully it was during the week and we had no wait.  I was excited as my wife and kids had been there before and my daughter always wears her 'Got biscuits' shirt and now I know why.

I wasn't sure what to get so I order the sampler which was fried chicken, ham and BBQ pork.  My wife got Fried chicken.

Thankfully, they brought out the biscuits right when you sit down and they are 5 star delicious.  They were hot, light fluffy and I could of ate 6 of them but I saved room for dinner.

The ham was insanely salty, the pork was tender but drenched in a just fair sauce and the fried chicken was juicy but tasteless.  My wife agreed that the chicken was smoking fresh out of the frier but truly was missing any really seasoning

The mac n cheese side was good also.  Unfortunately, it wasn't worth the traffic.
I've only ate here once, and it was good. I think cracker barrel is better though.

Not as great as I expected! Hot chicken was hard and very dry. Fried green tomatoes were awesome I must admit. I grew up on southern food and I've had much better biscuits. Would say it's a place to visit but don't have high expectations!
A favorite for us. Chicken tenders are some of the best and we always get decent to great service. Our out of town visitors love it here.

Uhhh... biscuits, biscuits, and more biscuits! Took about 45 mins to get seated, but you have the chance to wander around the place and check out all the cute little shops in the area.

Once seated you are promptly give delicious, buttery soft biscuits with a variety of jams. My fav jam was the peach one. 

Per the recommendation of the guy at the BBQ pit place, I got the BBQ pork omelet. It was just perfect! Usually I find omelets to be too filling, but they had the right ratio of eggs to meat in there. Super tasty. Everyone else thoroughly enjoyed their food and we were even able to pack the rest of our biscuits to take away.

Service was nice and friendly and the place was very clean. You can even take a look at the kitchen through windows on the way to the bathroom. 

Defo make this a food stop if you are in Nashville.

All the notoriety surrounding this restaurant is true...it is worth coming to because the food is excellent, the atmosphere is great, and the service is top-notch.  The store they have in their compound has a lot of cool souvenirs and provides and opportunity to kill some time if you have to wait in line which is always a possibility here.  I've been here once and surprisingly only had to wait for 15 minutes which I'm told is unheard of.  Anyways, do yourself a favor and check this place out if you're in the Nashville area!
Really awesome food and a fun atmosphere. The service was great! Loved the chicken schnitzel sandwich!

Believe the hype!!!  This place is wonderful.  The Country Ham and Fried Chicken are so good!  Evan was our waiter and he was funny and never let the glasses go empty. I would recommend this fine establishment to all who venture to Nashville looking for a local treat.

The Loveless Cafe was everything I had expected and more.  The food was fabulous and plentiful.  You will not leave her hungry.
http://yallcomeoninthedoorsopen.blogspot.com/2014/08/cousins-gather-at-loveless-cafe.html

DEFINITELY worth the hype.

I had no idea about this amazing place UNTIL I checked Yelp and found this fantastic brunch location.  We were in Nashville for a fun weekend. The Loveless Cafe is a drive from downtown, but totally worth it. Be prepared to wait for your delicious, eating experience. No fear, they have already anticipate this, and LC has an entire tourist town for you to explore and shop while you wait for your buzzer to go off.

Finally. We are seated. The interior of this cafe is suuuuper charming. I got the signature plate with the "red eye gravy." Definitely an acquired taste, but I'm glad we were able to try it. I had meal envy over what the hubs ordered. A pulled pork masterpiece (photographed).

The buttermilk muffins that are served while you wait for your entree are reason enough to some here. And the Bloody Mary's made with moonshine are great (if you like Bloody's).

Since we had already made this 'south' drive outta Nashville, we continued down to  Jack Daniel's distillery. An entire day of amazement.

I live in the area so it's great to have a new options. This place is sort of neat, but it also feels kind of like an amusement park. Just not authentic. Some of the foods are interesting, as are some of the beers. I find the tables and chairs to be cool looking, but quite uncomfortable.

If my only choice were inside Opry mills, this spot would land towards the top of the list. Other decent options in the area include Chuy's, Mission barbecue, and scoreboards over across the street. The hot chicken at scoreboards is worth the trip.

Tuvimos que esperar una hora para sentarnos a comer, pero valió la pena! La comida estuvo deliciosa y la atención muy buena. El café tiene tienditas a los lados donde te puedes entretener mientras esperas.

Had a very enjoyable time here after shopping at Opry Mills.  Set up like a traditional beer hall in Germany it is one of the few places to experience German food in this part of the country.  Had a pork schnitzel and bier cheese soup.  Both were very good.  A little disappointed with the apple strudel compared to others I have experienced.  Choice of German and local beers was good.  Entertainment was touristy but good.  Servers were excellent and attentive.

My wife and I had the fried chicken.  The chicken was great.  I would compare it to White Fence Farm in Illinois.  The biscuits and jam were fantastic!  Best biscuits I have ever had!  We had creamed corn, fried green tomatoes, grits and mashed potatoes as sides.  Best creamed corn I have ever had.  Fried green tomatoes were great as well.  A must try in Nashville.
Love this place.  Great food and service.  Awesome biscuits and homemade jellies.  Very homelike feeling.

Positive: The atmosphere is great. Table and venue decor is great. Love the way it looks! Server was very sweet. 
Negative: Food! The offer a $20 very limited and sub par buffet. I went the route of ordering off the menu = rock hard inedible biscuits, cold food that seems like it sat on expo for a little too long. Extra well dome crispy burgers. 

I really wanted to love this place because of it's great atmosphere, but just didn't do it for me!
Our family loved the fried chicken, fried green tomatoes, collared greens. But the smoked pork chops with peach jelly stole the show. Everyone is so friendly down here we took home souvenirs too!

The Loveless Café was the most disappointing restaurant I have been too. We have been looking forward to going there for almost 3 years and we finally got the opportunity and were disappointed at every turn. The place is cute, quaint. and has a lot of history but the waiting staff is rude and you feel like you're inconveniencing them by just being there.   The food is absolutely nothing special nothing that you can't find at a local Cracker Barrel or mom-and-pop diner.  We have no reason to return

A cute, clean, well maintained Ma and Pa kinda feel, restaurant. Cute little stores that sell their homemade jams and jellies, bbq and of course their biscuits. It is worth a morning drive. 30 minutes from Nashville. Have a great little bbq smokehouse right on property. Busy but keep
Things moving. Excellent, friendly service.

My husband and I went to dinner and a concert here and left unimpressed.  We ordered a good sampling of the menu.  My lobster chowder was overly smoky and salty, with very little lobster.  The bread basket (which was $6!) was completely stale.  (I am talking, crumbly, need a drink of water stale.)  My husband's cheeseburger was quite good (that was the highlight of the night) but my duck confit left a lot to be desired.  First, the presentation was completely unappetizing.  Everything was brown and drab looking.  The taste wasn't much better.  Everything on the plate was salty and heavy.  There was no brightness or "pop" to the dish, and it sorely needed one.  It honestly reminded me of a chicken dinner plate at Denny's!  (But at least at Denny's it would have cost me $10, not $24.)  Finally the chocolate stout cake was small and stale.  All in all, a very disappointing, very expensive meal.

The concert venue was also disappointing.  While I found the acoustics good, the chairs were incredibly uncomfortable. They were like the chairs you'd find in a cheap office lunchroom -- metal and plastic and stackable.  Except instead of sitting in them for a 10-minute lunch, you sat in them for 90 minutes or more, constantly shifting to try to find a comfortable position.

I had high hopes for City Winery but left disappointed.  I think this is a great concept for a restaurant and music venue, so I hope they'll improve their menu and get some new chairs!  :) If so, I'll be back to give it another shot.
Used to be great but food quality has went way down. More of a site seeing place now.
Weren't allowed in with kids during lunch on Thursday cause it's a smoking bar.  Headed back another night when we had a sitter.  Love music.  Drink specials.
The place is nice but the food is sub par at best.  Small portions for big prices and nothing leaving you with a reason to come back.

The biscuits were buttery, but I put some more butter on them just for fun. The pinto beans had some ham in them, and they were just right - soft and creamy. I also got fried chicken. It needed salt or brining ahead of time. Maybe dark meat would have been better? The raspberry peach cobbler was divine. Our waitress was very attentive and friendly. Go if you're in the area!

I'd have to agree with others that this cafe might not necessarily be worth the wait time. My friend & I came on a Sunday (before Memorial Day) around 6:30pm and didn't get seated until almost 8pm. We walked around the little store and checked everything out. Two separate weddings were going on so it was neat to see the brides posing under the Loveless neon sign out front while we waited. Our waiter was real friendly and attentive. He brought us their famous biscuits with 3 different flavored jams right when we sat down. Now if anything, the wait was worth these biscuits with butter-n-jam! My friend & I both ordered the fried chicken with mashed potatoes and gravy. She got the collard greens and I opted for the green beans. Both were really good. I honestly thought the white meat, fried chicken could've been more moist, but I don't really eat fried chicken like ever, so I'm not the best at deciphering from good/bad fried chicken. All-n-all, it was a decent experience. Our waiter comped our desserts which was nice. My friend just had a slice of the apple pie and I had a small portion of their banana bread pudding. My friend said the pie was so-so. The bread pudding was decent, but I was so full from my meal that I couldn't eat anymore than a few fork-fulls of it!
This is a unique gem just outside of Nashville. Everything I have tried has been wonderful Nd always filling. Take  look at the pictures your eyes will it lie!

Delicious!   Our family of four ordered 3 entrees and we still had leftovers!  Steak and eggs, southern ham and eggs, and the southern combo platter.  We all had the hashbrown casserole, which was cheesy and tasty.  The ham was a bit salty for my northern palette.  The sausage gravy, the made from scratch biscuits, and the homemade preserves were all excellent.  

Don't forget to stop by the cute shops to pick up a jar of preserves for home or as a gift for a loved one!  Biscuit mix also available, along with cute souvenirs, home decor, t-shirts, and stuffed animals.  Wish we could bring home cajun bacon that we saw at the shop.  They do have a shipping option.

Nice breakfast spot, definitely a tourist destination. Make sure you walk in the back past the restrooms --they have two windows that let you view into the kitchen and watch them make biscuits and flip eggs. Pretty cool! We waited about 25 minutes for a table on a Sunday morning. They gave us a buzzer so we could walk around the property and explore all of their little shops while we were waiting so it didn't seem quite that long.

First thing, you get a basket of fresh biscuits and jam. They are pretty small so you don't feel guilty eating more than one :)

Service was excellent. The food is good, nothing special, and the prices are quite expensive. You'll spend $10 for 2 eggs, meat, potatoes, and toast.

I saw August Burns Red here last night and I liked how there wasn't any alcohol sold at the venue and foul language wasn't permitted either. However, later on in the show I was afraid I was going to end up really disliking this venue because of the crowd rules. I noticed a guy crowdsurfing and I immediately waited for him to get kicked out (which never happened, to my surprise). I then noticed there was actually a pit in the center of the crowd away from where I had been standing and the rest was history. There was even a guy in a power chair in the pit with us and that made it even better. I really respect this place and I love that a fellow West Virginian originally started it. I drove over three hours from my house in Jefferson City and I'll definitely be back.
This was an ok bar. I did not notice this was a smoking bar. The service was decent. The drinks were blah... there was no music playing. They have drink specials but nothing that was all that great.
The biscuits were great.  The chicken so so and the fries the typical frozen type.  Very average.

I have not eaten at the restaurant proper.  I ate Loveless food at a business function in the Loveless Barn.  Hopefully the food inside the restaurant is better than the catered food, or is at least hot.


Barn Facility: a very nice space for a company, organization, or large gathering.  There are outside areas and a stage.

The service:  Servers were assigned to large tables seating about 10 people.  My water glass was never refilled. She refilled my husband's water; he was sitting right next to me, but I just had to be thirsty.   She didn't inquire if anyone wanted anything.  All she asked was if we were finished with our plates so she could clear them.

The food:  Seriously?  Is this the famous Loveless Cafe food??  We were served family style.  Nine people at our table were given serving dishes that would have maybe fed four people (see the above note about the server not asking if anyone wanted anything else).  On the Loveless catering link, it says "All You Can Eat" on the page that describes the family style menu options.  All a 3 year old can eat would be more accurate.  We left hungry.  Our event chose the Fairview Family Style catering option, $35/person.

Our menu consisted of:
Chef's seasonal salad--typical salad.  I didn't eat mine.  It had gorgonzola cheese and fresh apple chunks.  At the time, I wasn't sure what kind of cheese it was, just white and crumbled; I assumed either bleu or feta.  I don't like any of the soft cheeses like that, and I'm allergic to apples, so no salad course for me.  Husband said it was alright, and the pralines were very good.

Macaroni and cheese--it was cold.  It tasted like elbow noodles with melted Velvetta.  Stouffer's frozen mac and cheese has better flavor
.
Green Beans and Carrots-- I don't like green beans or carrots, so I have not idea if they tasted good.  My husband ate them. He said they were cold.

Fried Chicken--it was almost cold, barely warm.  The flavor was good, but these were some of the most scrawny pieces of chicken I have ever seen.  Our dish of chicken had more wings than anything.  At least 2 people at our table were stuck with one chicken wing as their entree.  I have no idea what part of the chicken I ate; the piece was too small to identify
.
Biscuits--If these are the famous Loveless Biscuits, then someone did a tremendous PR job.  The biscuits were about 1 1/2 inches square, flat, dense, chewy and COLD.  Not light, fluffy, tender and hot from the oven like biscuits are supposed to be.

Dessert--Banana Pudding.  I can't review the quality.  Of the nine people at my table, I and one other skipped dessert altogether because we don't like banana pudding.  One girl had never eaten it before and tried it.  She didn't like it either.  Another lady knew banana pudding wasn't her favorite but ate a small spoonful out of politeness.  Hubby isn't a big banana pudding fan either.  Please, just because we're in the south, and banana pudding is the signature southern dessert, do your guests a favor and pick something else for the dessert course, preferably chocolate.  Loveless doesn't have a chocolate dessert option, which is ridiculous.  

Overall, Loveless Catering was absolutely not worth the price.  Rental prices for the Barn facility seemed reasonable judging form information on the website.
Live music & the best jello shots of my life!! What more can one ask for?!? Just go and enjoy a blue raspberry jello shot for me! Oh and don't forget to shake it on the dance floor me too.

I live down the street from this place but I don't go all the time (I wish) but I can't! If you like to wait in line this is the place for you! If you go during brunch hours just be prepared for a two hour wait, minimum BUT, it is well worth your wait time, during your wait there are a lot of things to do. There are a few gift shops and there is a local artisan gallery, and corn-hole! There is a theater too but I don't know what happens in there, they probably do stuff at night. 

Anyways we finally got seated and our waiter was great, very cheerful and respectful! The food came out promptly, it was hot and delicious! I really have nothing bad to say other than the wait, but it is a Nashville icon! Hope you enjoy it!!

I have been here four times with hope each time we would have better service. Each visit has been made at lunch time so there has only been maybe 10 parties dinning at the same time so not that busy. Each time it's has taken about an hour and a half because the service is soooo slow. On one occasion we gave up on telling the waitress what we wanted because it would take her 10 minutes to get back to us and I hope you aren't thirsty because that is not a priority. If I were rating on just the service this would be a one star. The food is wonderful I haven't ordered anything I haven't liked and the large pretzel is huge enough to share. I do suggest you try it just be warned that the service will be slow!!
Not close to downtown, this iconic spot still serves it like food is the main business. We love it.

Wasn't worth the hype IMHO. We waited almost two hours. Sides were really bad (e.g. mac and cheese was runny as soup and had zero flavor). Fried chicken was great and biscuits were too. Other than that, I thought the food was blah. Service wasn't very friendly either. You go here once, post your pic to Instagram and probably forget about the food. I liked Hattie B's chicken better (sorry!!!).

This place meets all its reviews!! It is amazing by all standards. I recommend all of their preserves, I even bought some. The gift shops are really cool they sell some of their products. Definetly order the biscuits they are amazing as well. I bought a sample preserve jar set from the gift shop because I liked them all!

If there was ever a destination restaurant- this is it! What a great place to visit!! So many adorable trinkets and souvenirs, even the drive from Nashville is enjoyable!
I wish I would have known about this place before.. I can't wait to go back!
The food, the service, the grounds, literally everything about this restaurant is awesome! Down to the crossword puzzle place mats!
I should mention that we went with a large of group of about 15 people and they literally stayed open for us to eat, they were extremely accommodating and gave us about 40 of their heavenly biscuits to go!!! I truly cannot describe what a great experience we had at the loveless cafe! All of their preserves and all of their homemade honey and jams were to die for, I strongly recommend spending an evening there and support their amazing locale!

The drive to get here made us wonder,the food removed all concern.our waitress Susan was fantastic we were served quickly and correctly.
Every dish was fantastic from the jams and biscuits to the country ham. Portions were large and all tasty.
  The biscuits were endless and waitress gave us what we didn't it to take home.
Everything was great

We only did a drive-by for take out biscuits to see what all the rave was about. I feel like I just had biscuits and gravy for the first time in my life! Throw out your mother's recipe, it means nothing compared to this gravy! And the jams were quite impressive, especially the blackberry. YUM!
Horribly annoying performers making racket the entire time we were there... nearly impossible to even relatively enjoy the average beer and food they have available.

My first breakfast visit when I moved out here. The cafe is quite a drive (25-30 mins). Upon arrival you will notice quite a bit of people waiting or outside eating..I advise you to put your name on the list and look around their little shops. I have to say the wait was awful but the food was worth it. We ended up ordering our breakfast ToGo and eating it outside on the tables. I've only ever had breakfast here so I cannot speak for the other dishes but man their biscuits are good! I cannot wait to come back and revisit the Loveless Cafe! Maybe next time I'll try breakfast inside :)

AMAZING!!!

We were visiting from out of town for the CMA music fest. We drove 45 min in the rain to get here and it was worth it! We only had to wait about 20 min for a table and our waiter TALOR was awesome. He got us set up with mimosas and bloody marys, and  the food was the best breakfast food I have ever had!! The hash-brown casserole was delicious and the biscuits, well they are famous for a reason!

I suggest everyone go there if you get the chance! I will definitely be back again as soon as I can.  xoxo
As advertised! Wonderful food and great service! Might be a little wait to get seated but you can walk the grounds and visit he gift shops while you wait so it passes fast.

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE everything about the Loveless!  The food is outstanding and the atmosphere is so charming.  A must stop for us every time we go to Nashville.  Great little shops surround the restaurant so time passes quickly if there is a little wait to be seated.  The food is SO worth the wait.
Some of the best German food I have ever had. Outstanding atmosphere and service. Huge place with great vibe...fun, fun, fun....
This is the sweetest place and our server Jeff was wonderful and accommodating! I would highly recommend the spot, go for a Natchez Trace drive afterwards, and make sure you ask for Jeff.
Ham heaven. Biscuit heaven. Preserves, hummmmmm. Wonderful relaxed atmosphere, even though the place was packed. Two trips while in Nashville, need I say more? GO

Insane waits on the weekend. Waited over an hour on Friday for a take-out order (including the 30 min drive over there). Can't see what the fuss is. Will have to try to make it out on a Tuesday or Wednesday and see if it's actually possible to get a table. Not impressed with the food I got- have definitely had better in the area.
Can I give this 6 stars? The food is delicious, plentiful and excellent value for money. The service is efficient and friendly. This is maybe the best Southern cooking I've ever had. We'll be back!

Disappointed-Heard such great reviews and that this was a landmark restaurant. Ordered chicken tenders and they were overlooked and tasteless. Fried green tomatoes were undercooked. Not good at all. Seemed like a dingy old restaurant that needs some major Clorox wipes and a clean up. Flies were all over the place and hair was in my menu. Overpriced greasy spoon. I've had better chicken at KFC. Will not be returning.

I came here for a concert, I saw Hey Monday and someone else. It was a big open area, there isn't much to say...it seems fine. Will I go here again? Sure why not. It wasn't a very closed in space, I liked that

Awesome place, the biscuits were delicious and all you can eat. I had the bbq Sammy and my wife had the fried chicken and waffle.  Both were great and at a reasonable price. Our server (Morgan) was excellent.

Man do I want to hate this place.  Everything about it says TOURIST TRAP.   And some items aren't as good as the others, but they do so much well.  I know that the blackberry jam is suppose to be the item, but the Peach is soooo Good.   In a way, it does kind of remind me of what Cracker Barrel was like in the 70's when the staff wore red bandana shirts.  I have gotten into a habit of taking co-workers from out of town out here to eat.  So far, everyone has gone on and on to others about it.   I just wish I would quit ordering the sampler plate with 3 meats.

Growing pains... I was in Munich last fall for October  fest, and if you come here to get a taste of that experience you'll get it. But they are working out the bugs that come with opening a new place, staff knowledge of menu and bar items were most noticeable. I have no doubt they will get it all worked out, I'll be back! The attention to detail inside is impressive.

I cried when I found pulled pork that I enjoyed more than my own.  George rolls in at 3:30 and starts smoking meat, for the love of god.  I know this because that's when we showed up...and waited until they opened.  George was real friendly to three random men showing up at the smokehouse before dawn, looking for BBQ.  He was cool with us napping in the car and playing catch in the parking lot.  

We were the first ones in the door and they throw biscuits in your face when you get inside, served with homemade jams that makes Smucker's look like Suckers.  BOO-YA.  George swears by the biscuits and I won't say he's wrong.  They were excellent.

The exact moment my life changed is easy to recall, it's the second the pulled pork hoe cakes arrived; heaping, steaming, and screaming at my soul.  People, the pork melted in my mouth.  Has that ever happened to you?  Be real here.

Oh, the service was good and the staff was friendly.  They hooked up a free plate of biscuits and jam to go as we left.  We also shared a nice conversation on Chicago style pizza which they adore; I think after the food and service a frozen za should find it's way to Loveless from "the boys who went camping."

A true labor that is not without love produces a product that fills my heart and tummy tum tum with the truest form of adoration.

I know it's touristy, but dammit I don't care! Loveless is a cute place with tasty, bad for you food, that is moderately priced and generally fun to visit. The stores are nothing too exciting, but the restaurant was nice with great service. We had a party of 6 and had no problem getting a table right away on a weekday morning. We started with some of their wonderfully light mini biscuits with a variety of house made jams... so good, I could have just kept eating those. I had the biscuit sandwich sampler with the fried green tomato, bbq pork, fried chicken, and sausage gravy options. This sounds ridiculous, but each biscuit was small, so calm down. The best by far was the fried green tomato.... super tasty with pimento cheese. The bbq was a little sad... not terribly flavorful. The fried chicken was your run of the mill chicken, but not bad. The gravy was tasty and added flavor to the less flavorful of the sandwiches. I also split some cheese grits and hashbrown casserole with someone... cheese grits were just ok, the casserole was delish.... definitely recommend that for your side option (cheesy, oniony potato goodness). I wanted to try other things so bad, but I literally hurt from the amount of food I consumed. Check this place out while in Nashville, it's worth it!

PS We beat the placemat, hooray!

Wow. I'd been to this place twice before and was just as satisfied as I was this time. I was visiting Nashville again with a friend and she said she wanted a hearty southern meal and we ended up here! We both ordered the quarter chicken with cheesy smashed potatoes (amazing). The biscuits are great and I was so completely stuffed when I left, yet we still contemplated the desserts. Great place.

Was in town for business, thought I'd check out the Loveless again as it had been a few years.   The biscuits were incredible, as were the 3 jams.  Had the fried chicken plate (dark).   Quarter chicken was generous...2 legs and a back/thigh.  Came out very hot and fresh.  The crust is not overly salty nor greasy, but the chicken was cooked just a few minutes too long.  Even the leg meat was a bit tough.  The turnip greens with pot liquor were excellent, as was the pot liquor.  The fried okra was disappointing...the coating too thick and bready.   I remember having this several years ago and it was a different cornmeal coating that was much lighter and crisper.   Have they changed the recipe?   Came around 5:30 on Monday night and the restaurant was pretty empty.   Used to seeing this place being packed.   Service was quick and friendly.  I ended up walking out full but feeling a little let down...not the same as I remembered.

My first and only visit (so far) at this place was nothing short of amazing. For Christmas my friends and I traveled from Memphis to see John Waters' Christmas show. Initially we had balcony seating. Upon checking in we asked if we could upgrade our seating. The gentleman helping us was extremely helpful and friendly. He upgraded us to stage side seating at no extra charge. We literally got to sit mere feet away from John as he delivered a hilarious show. 
Our server was attentive and polite and answered all of our questions in a knowledgeable and helpful manner. 
I ordered the house Rosé and amongst the three of us we split Wild Mushroom & Risotto Balls, the Hummus Plate (this is a must! It was so delicious and fresh!), the fried Brussels Sprouts, and the Margherita Veggie Flatbread. The entire experience left me feeling completely satisfied and overwhelmed with joy. I know it had a lot to do with how giddy I was from meeting John Waters and being in his presence for the duration of the show. But the food, ambience, hospitality, and wine,  exponentially added to our experience. I was left with a glow for a few days afterwards and dreaming of the tapas and wine. 
I would most definitely like to return to experience the food and another show.

Amazing biscuits, definitely the best I've ever had! Their blackberry jam is outstanding. Service is great as well. Watermelon ribs, fried chicken, fried green tomatoes, and mashed potatoes with gravy are some of our favorites!! Definitely  must stop here when you're in Nashville!!!

"Biscuit Poisoning? YES PLEASE! "
5 of 5 stars Pending review
If you are visiting Nashville, make the drive to this wonderfully taste of history! But be aware they bring you a plate of the most buttery biscuits with an assortment of jams, preserves and honey. Stop at one...or you will get too full of the yummy goodness. Then make sure that what ever your family orders as the main dish you all order a different side, because there is ALOT to share. From Mac and Cheese to the BEST turnip green and mashed potatoes. My husband had the house chicken, I had the meat loaf and my daughter had the roast beef we each got 3 sides, we took so much home, so good, And we each ordered dessert to go. You could of rolled me out of that wonderful place!!! But don't leave till you visit all the shops and learn about its origins. It's a very nostalgic place. After dinner.... Take a drive through the parks. Truely beautiful.

Visited August 2015

We came for brunch, so it wasn't very busy and we didn't see a live show.  The inside is very nice and spacious.  I love the staircase of wine bottles !   The food wasn't great.  I had a salmon salad wrap, which was salty n bland at the same time. The potatoes were seasoned well, but also salty. The flight (wine samples) were all good. I like the display of them.  Honestly, the best part was the fire place we sat next to.  They lit it up and we were so warm ! Thanks !!

Typical country cafe with adequate selection but exaggerated pricing and an insane popularity (i.e. Wait times). We waited 2 hrs to eat a $40 + tip meal consisting of a V8 and hot sauce Bloody Mary and an overdone chicken fried steak with Hardee's quality gravy.  If Commanders Palace Bloody Mary's are a 9/10, Loveless barely ranks a 1. The creamed spinach was tasty but heavy and the green beans were overdone and tasted like a porkchop more than garden veggie. 
Service was very good and the quaint little country campus with gift shops were well maintained, but being from the South it was absolutely NOTHING special.
Awful food.  Service was amazing and biscuits but that is it.  Our food was cold and just not good...breakfast was a bust
Only had two waitresses. They were good and very helpful, just not all that satisfied!  The waitress we had kept getting lost and we had to wait way to long for everything!!!
We loved loved loved this place and our waiter on our trip to Nashville. The wait was long but our bellies were not disappointed. Good food, service, and plenty to do during the wait!

Loveless was a ride outside the city but worth the trip.  They have built their own little community where you can shop at stores while you wait and even ship home your items!  We had an hr and a half wait to eat so we did shop and enjoyed their own community.  Their chicken and waffles was good.  But their gravy was even better!  Their biscuits were good but it was really cool to watch them make them through the glass window on your way to the bathroom. If you have kids make sure you check it out!  The mashed potatoes were delish! Worth the trip outside town and the wait! I have to say it was the best food we had the whole trip.

Wow wow wow. I love the biscuits. I love the preserves. But most of all, I love that Southern hospitality, ya'll. We waited over an hour for a table on a Saturday for brunch but it was so worth it. The venue itself is an attraction alone - a little bluegrass was being played by an endearing small group of musicians to patiently waiting customers in the 90+ heat (many of us were waiting under shady trees and sauntering in and out of the air conditioned gift shops full of Loveless goodies). Once we got our table (inside, phew! Too hot out!) we were treated so well by the gorgeous Susan- she was genuine and sweet; took the time to talk through the menu when we asked questions etc. Our coffee (filtered) was delish and never ran dry. Hot chocolate was the BEST! I was totally overwhelmed with the well-priced menu and quick pleasant service too. If you are a tourist visiting Nash, you gotta just do this- it's a rite of passage- those biscuits alone smothered in peach preserve will make it worth all that long wait in the summer humidity.

When near Nashville this is a foodie must!  

Excellent biscuits and other southern favorites including fried fish and chicken gizzards!  

We have had both breakfast and dinner and no complaints!

Great local diner/cafe for a hearty meal. They are definitely famous for their home made biscuits and preserves, which are really delicious! The service was good and friendly, and Amanda did a great job taking care of us.

If you're looking for tasty local eateries, definitely add this one to your list!
What a great place really enjoyed the food and a few shops adjacent to the Loveless Café their hash was the best I've ever had I don't know what was in there but it was food fabulous!

Super cute with delicious food and drinks. Everyone loved it and it was such a great atmosphere. They closed early but did not warn us of that when we made a 1pm reservation (closed at 2) which was a little frustrating. Overall good experience.
The most Amazing biscuits!!! Cute place and the food is great. Service was quick.  The ham and jam store right across is great to find cute little gifts to take home.

We waited for an hour and 45 minutes. Not worth that long of a wait. Under an hour, do it.
The service was pretty good, they were obviously very busy.
Right away they will bring you biscuits. Dig in because they're famous for a reason. Try the peach jam. They will bring you more so keep them coming and you can take some home to go!
We had omelets which were yummy. The pulled pork one was fun and good. Cheese and garden omelets were standard.

It has always been about the best breakfast or lunch restaurant in Nashville. Fried chicken is best ever. Breakfast is always perfect. I just wish it wasn't so far away and so tourist-infested. And kinda pricey.

Worst. Meal. Ever. 

My mind is blown. I've been so excited to see Nashville's food scene become on par with larger cities. However, in my 30 years as a Nashvillian I've never had a worse meal. It was like a middle schooler plated our charcuterie plate with store bought Bologna. The aioli was neon yellow and bread was like wonder bread. On to the cheese board that had one particular mystery cheese no one wanted. The food allergy we told the waiter was subsequently disregarded causing a plate to be sent back. 

The food was terrible and waiter blissfully unaware. I will never be back.

Took the 1 hour drive from Lebanon just to get some biscuits and it was very much worth it. Our waiter was the best. Super quick and friendly even though we got there only about 25 minutes before they closed. Only had dessert (pie) and biscuits, and then stopped at the store. Eat the biscuits. Take some to go. The preserves they are served with are excellent as well, especially the strawberry.

This place is good, but super rich. We came here for breakfast, and it's typical, heavy, American fare. They start you out with a pile of biscuits and jam. The biscuits are super tasty, but I guess they are about 50% butter. I impulsively bought the chicken and waffles, and they were also super rich. The chicken was great and had a nice crispy shell. The waffle was also good, not too much to say about it.

The service was amazing, my dad spilled coffee everywhere and they were quick to help us out.

Overall it's great food in a casual southern atmosphere. It's just a bit too rich and they don't really serve lite fare, so I'm going to give it a 4.

We loved The Loveless Cafe! The food was great, everyone in our group enjoyed their meals and the biscuits were great. The server was so sweet and super nice! If I'm back in town I will for sure be back. I wish we would have gone here sooner. A must try!

We had our hopes to high for this place but we weren't impressed. Their biscuits indeed are one of the best we've ever had!! They bring four biscuits and three different jams and WOW... really delicious. We had ham and eggs, the ham was very salty. We also had chicken and waffles, the chicken was really dry and the waffle was ok. The service could be a little bit better. Our waitress was not friendly ( kinda rushing us even though it was our first time there) and didn't tell us about the daily specials but she did tell other tables the specials. Other waiters/waitresses were nicer than ours (tall guy). The place is kinda cute.

We found a lot of love at the Loveless Cafe. We shared the sampler choosing fried chicken, fried catfish and pulled pork BBQ. Our sides were creamed corn an hash brown casserole and we added fried green tomatoes.
Everything was wonderful including the service. Tammy never rushed us answered all our questions and even gave us a small sample of the red eye gravy the south is known for. We both agreed with her that coffee should be in a cup and not in gravy. It was very different than I expected and when I described what I expected she said that sounds like our other gravy and she brought us two tastes - sausage gravy "for the biscuits " and white "for the chicken ". Those were both great. 
We left happy and full and with leftovers. 
I wish we could go back often, but we live in Los Angeles and that's a long way to go. It would be worth it if we could.
Fantastic food, charming decor, friendly service (thanks, Katie!). I now see why it's on everyone's "must" list when checking out Nashville's sites.

We came here for late breakfast on a Sunday. The wait for two if us was not bad. we walked around the property while we waited.  The biscuts were great along with the hashbrown casserole. Lucas chatted with us and gave us good recommendations for the area.

This place was only so-so.  Food is no better than any of the run-of-the-mill breakfast chains (not even the biscuits). The service is absolutely appalling and just skirts being downright rude.  The wait was ridiculous and I can't help but think that it is grotesquely overestimated in an effort to get people to shop at all of the other little shops on the premises.  The grounds are pretty decent though and the hostess was at least thoughtful enough to suggest ordering takeout to eat at one of the picnic areas.  Would advise against using the app to order takeout. The front end staff admittedly have no idea whatsoever about any takeout orders placed via app. They only know about any app orders when/if the back end staff bring completed orders up front.  Would also advise triple checking pick up orders (before leaving) for things like having complete meals, drinks, syrups, sauces, sides, utensils, etc... In a nutshell, I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again or consider it a must do event if family/friends are in town.

I might rate this 3 stars if it weren't for the 5-star hype. It was all "OK" cafe food at best - NOTHING special.

Biscuits? They were good - but very small. If you want a real biscuit, get off the trace at Hwy 72 and go to Corinth, MS for Abe's or Lloyd's - nothing to see here. Preserves were pretty good and the sorghum was good.

World's best fried chicken? Hardly. Dry and over-cooked and - that poor thing musta been a chick - littlest pieces I've ever seen.

Meatloaf was cold. Not stone out of the fridge, but not warm. Taste of it was average.

Green tomatoes were too thickly cut and got soggy fast.

Mashed potatoes? Stirred potatoes. Like from a box? Red eye gravy? Mix?

Wanted to try some pie, but $33 in for very "eh" food - I didn't wanna risk it.

This place is evidently surviving on past reputation. I didn't get the hype.

Loveless Cafe has gone through several ownerships, but the place stemmed from Lon and Annie Loveless, who were known to pass out fried chicken and biscuits to travelers who were traveling on Highway 100.  They serve items such as the country ham, pork bbq, omelets, fried chicken, catfish, pancakes, sandwiches, salads, and desserts.  My sister and I shared the 'Famous Loveless Country Ham,' which was a 7oz sliced ham that came with 2 eggs and a side of red-eye gravy.   You also have a choice to have homefries or hash brown casserole, and the platter is also served with biscuits (sorghum and honey are offered upon request).  The ham itself was tasty, but way too salty (even for my taste).  Even without seasoning the eggs and eating it with the ham, it still didn't balance it out.  I really enjoyed the hashbrown casserole, as it was wonderfully cheesy and creamy - yum!  I could have eaten this all day!  We also tried the Pimento Cheese & Fried Green Tomato Biscuit - it came with a nice generous dollop of pimento cheese with a perfectly fried sliced green tomato, all in their homemade biscuits - it was delicious!  I also really enjoyed their biscuits as it had a nice little crispy top with a lovely soft interior; great on its own or with butter - you can add honey, sorghum, or any of the jellies that they also provide you with.  There are plenty of parking spaces, and there's also a cute gift store that you can check out across the lot - they sell the Loveless's strawberry vines decor on platters, cookbooks, kitchen accessories, home decor, etc.  I'm glad I was able to check this place out!

+DELICIOUS BISCUITS!!!
+hashbrown casserole
+Pimento Cheese & Fried Green Tomato Biscuit

We stopped here as a must see and it didn't disappoint. The service all around was some of the best and the food was sooo good. Moonshine drinks were STRONG - but tasty. 

I had the pulled pork omelet and my husband got the biscuit sampler.

Where do I start?  Ok, the biscuits with three different jams. I thought it couldn't get better until the fried catfish came out, piping hot, crunchy outside, flaky inside.  Garlic mashed potatoes and fried green tomatoes finished out the meal. My companion voted the fried chicken as good as it gets. My daughter had the gigantic pancake. We finished by sharing the fudge pie.  Worth every calorie. Even though we arrived late afternoon on a Monday, there was still a wait of 40 minutes but don't be put off. Spend the time imagining a flaky, hot biscuit.  Our server was friendly and full of information. He made us feel as if we were old friends stopping by for a chat and getting a meal as a bonus. It might seem as if you are driving to the middle of nowhere but when you leave, you'll be planning when you can return.
My husband has not stopped talking about those biscuits now 8 months later. It's a bit out of the way if you're downtown, but worth it! Yum!

Grounds are lovely and lots to do while you wait - and you're going to wait. Biscuits are overrated. They're more like buttery dinner rolls. Service was excellent, they had lots of friendly and attentive staff. But I wouldn't come back for the food. Fried chicken was underwhelming, and the pancakes and waffles were very sweet. However, the pork was really good. It tasted like sweet, smoky pork - it didn't need a sauce or any other cover up.

Biscuits are no kidding great. Loved the chicken the pork and the pies look great. Too full to order pie. This was some good cooking. Worth the extra trip. Great wait staff lots of enthusiasm from everyone there.   
A little touristy but still lots of fun. I will be back for the biscuits!!!

Biscuits with the homemade jam are to die for. 
We came at a good time, no wait and sat on the patio. 
Everyone was friendly not only at the cafe but at the shops surrounding it. 
Ordered the southern platter sampler that had catfish, country ham, fried chicken and for the sides fried okra and has brown casserole. I would order the catfish and the sides again. The piece of ham I had seemed a little over cooked.  Also got the special drink - Blue moon (pictured below) it was refreshing. 

Definitely would make the trip out here again!

Loved this new restaurant in the Opry Mills Mall. The food was awesome and the entertainment was so good. Our waitress was Allison, she was so cute and very knowledgeable of all the beers and the food!!!! We will be back!!!!

Absolutely adore the Loveless!  Best biscuits ever and tasty jams with the blackberry being my favorite!  Always get the fried chicken biscuits which are just perfect little packages of pleasure.  Breakfasts are great too! Outstanding, friendly service.  Picnic tables outside make it easy to have a meal with your pup traveling companions. Give this wonderful cafe a try if you're nearby.

The food was outstanding, service was impeccable and the entire place was such a great place for dinner and a show. This is a one of a kind destination for people to go to. To top it all off, if your a wine lover, then there is no better place to go. You can even buy wine on Sundays. My wife and I will be going back.

Loveless is known for their biscuits, which is why we came. And they were in fact DELICIOUS. But I can't get over how good the country fried steak was. I went with a group of 3 girls and we shared the country fried steak, the breakfast platter with ham and fried chicken. The country fried steak was by far the best dish--you can tell they gave you a good cut and the flavor was out of this world. I've had a lot of country friend steak and I think that's been the best I've had yet.

Meanwhile, despite reviews otherwise, the ham was too salty to eat, which was a shame. We got scrambled eggs to go with them, which were very standard. Finally, the friend chicken was good but I eat a lot of fried chicken and it wasn't really standout. Service was pretty good, especially given a (surprisingly busy) Wednesday lunch time. It's nice that you can shop around the complex while you wait for your table and our buzzer went off much sooner than they said it would, which was a plus. 

Net net, come here for the biscuits (+ homemade jam) and country fried steak and you'll leave a happy camper.
By far the best biscuits. Top them with the peach jelly and you have a winner. Overall great southern food and that friendly southern service you hear about.

We stopped by at 8:30 on a saturday morning and it was perfect timing as we got seated right away. Our server was friendly and attentive and gave great recommendations since we were first time visitors. I got the bbq pork eggs which came with 2 buried pancakes. Helpings were generous and the food was tasty too. My friend got the chicken biscuits which were delicious. The house biscuits lived up to their legendary status. This place is well worth the drive!

If you are a first timer to the Loveless be advised that the food is great but the wait is always long. I'm not sure there is ever a "slow" time - we arrived around 1:45 today and still waited a long time. We did notice when we came out around 3:30 that the parking lot was less crowded so that may be a better time. It took about 30 min for our food to be served after ordering so don't go if you're in a hurry or you are an impatient grumpy old man! Definitely the best things on the menu are the fried chicken, biscuits and fried green tomatoes.

4 stars for events
1.5 stars for food.

I swear, I don't understand why the food is so bland here.  Does the chef not taste his food?
We were here for dinner, the other night and both of us made faces after the first bite.
I swear...  I don't understand why the food is so bad, here......

I like the concerts. 
I do not like the food.

I usually have to ask the bartender/barmaid to put a little more sweetener in my mixed drinks..
They're bland, too..

I don't know how this place stays in business with the food part of the establishment.

It was delicious. We waited 45 min for a table. So we were starving by the time the food came. The service was fast. We ordered fried chicken and sample platter. The meals come with endless biscuits and jam. Both bbq pork was a bit dry. The pies were too sweet for my taste. The fried catfish and fried chicken were yummy. Will definitely visit again.

The Good:
- The biscuits and preserves are great.
- The steak biscuit platter was excellent.
- The side dishes are generally good. The grits left a lot to be desired.
- Our server was very nice and attentive.

The Bad:
- We ordered two moonshine drinks, and only one had any alcohol in it. 
- The Bloody Mary tasted like moonshine, water, and a splash of hot sauce mixed together.
- Flies. Everywhere. There were at least 20 flies buzzing around our table from the minute we first got there.

I was in Nashville for work and several co-workers mentioned this place was great for a weekend breakfast.  We arrived at 10 am on Saturday and waited about 1:15 for a table. The food was good, but heavy. All of the homemade jams were delicious with the fresh biscuits (try mixing the blackberry and peach jams together for even more deliciousness). We ordered a side of sausage gravy as well, in order to try that with the biscuits, and I almost liked that more than than the jams. 

I had the pulled pork on top on cornbread - it was huge! All of the entrees were a good size so you may want to consider sharing, especially if you want to enjoy more than one biscuit. 

This place is worth driving out for, but make sure to allot some time for the wait. You can entertain yourself at their shops while you wait or relax at one of the many tables they have around the restaurant.

All the hype really had me believing the biscuits would melt in my mouth, they were good, tender, not really a flakey biscuit. We ordered the beef brisket special & it was delicious, had we known we would have ordered one platter between us there was that much beef ! Reasonably priced for Nashville area. Had a 45 min wait time but it passes quickly thanks to their great marketing i.e. Shops, cornhole. 
Enjoy, it's eclectic & kitschy. Staff is incredibly upbeat & friendly.
