Okay...I always try to say something good about a place...it has nice...hmmm...nice chalkboards. I have been to brunch twice and both times the service and the food were striving to be average. The only reason I went back the second time was because someone gave me a groupon...still felt like it was a waste. I have not been for a music event, so don't use this for anything other than a brunch review...but a $15 Manhattan for brunch is way too much $$...go to Sutler...much more fun and much better food, value, atmosphere...albeit not chalkboards.
Biscuits. Fried chicken.  Homemade fresh jelly. Loveless lives up to the hype. It's worth the trip whether you live in the Nashville area or are visiting from out of town.

The biscuits and preserves live up to the hype! The biscuits are small but very tasty and especially delicious with some preserves slathered on top. I loved the peach preserves so much I picked up two jars from the gift shop to take back home. 

The breakfast is pretty good as well. I tried the steak and eggs and the steak was just okay, nothing to write home about. The hashbrown casserole that accompanies breakfast, however, is divine. 

I would say the only downside is the wait. Thankfully I knew from experience to get there early and was happy to say we were first in the building. It's definitely worth getting up early to have the first taste of those biscuits.

One of my favorite places for fried chicken.  Wait time is crazy long, but you have lots of stores/activities on the property to keep you busy.  Definitely worth the experience.  We also tried the salted ham for $70+ and when we opened it, we found lots of mold.  Pretty scary, but I think that it's normal and I just cut it off.  We split the ham 3 ways and it would have been nice if they could have cut if for us.....but they said they could not.  For a restaurant, you would think they would have no problem.  So we ended up hacking at that thing in the back of our minivan with a knife.

I enjoyed my meal at the Loveless Cafe. Fried chicken and biscuits! I loved the strawberry preserves and bought a jar! Arriving at 9, the restaurant was not as crowded as shown on the many travel and food shows that feature the place! However by noon a tour bus full of senior citizens pulled into the parking lot and the place quickly became packed. I purchased some items from the general store and walked around the grounds stopping at all the shops in the back! The waitress and hostess were courteous and cheerful! I liked looking at all the celebrity pictures and reading the articles throughout the restaurant. The strawberry rhubarb pie was good but in my to go container the strawberry juice spilled out.   Next time I am in Nashville I will return to the Loveless Cafe!

For $3 + tax, I was able to get a grilled chicken biscuit and two additional biscuits with their jams. And I was full. The biscuits deserve a 4/5.

The restaurant is not technically in Nashville proper - I think it took me 25 minutes to get there and if it wasn't renowned, you probably wouldn't stop here. It's a cute restaurant with super sweet staff and service. The restaurant is more sizable than I expected and since I came here on a Monday, I didn't have to wait. I did hear a tip - if it is packed, get it to go and sit on the picnic tables. 

There are two shops with their jams and some adorable lunch sacks and pot holders.

Ventured down 2nd street a couple of nights ago and finally had the pleasure to attend Big Shotz. They have the best alcohol deals in Nashville, in my opinion. Haven't had a chance to enjoy their food, but heard its a good bang for your buck. 2 dollar drafts, 3 dollar bottles, 5 dollar double shots are some of the deals that popped out to me alcohol wise. One of the biggest problems about this place is that it is a smoking bar. Two, the night i went in there it was more rock and roll instead of a good mix in music. Looking forward to giving this place another chance in the future. Especially, to get my hands on some food.
Just go... always great and such a cool one off. Liked it better before the gift shops and performance hall but food always a winner
Luke was our waiter and his customer service was spot on!! So friendly and helpful, food was delicious, chicken biscuit was one of the best!

Awesome chill cover band here when we visited . They played some good jams. Our friend we were with says this place normally has legit bands, so we'll go with that statement.  The 5 dollar shot menu on the screen flashed so fast that it took me 10 mins to stare at it and try and decide which ones I wanted to try because before I got to read one, the screen changed !  Bartenders were friendly but I think one was new cause she was slow and got my gals order wrong when she went up and ordered

They had me at biscuits and mimosas! My husband and I brought a large group of family and friends here for brunch while everyone was in town visiting for our wedding back in December. We knew there would be a bit of a wait before we got there since it's a Nashville staple so we warned our group up front. No one seemed to mind much because they are all still talking about how delicious it was and insist on revisiting during future trips to see us! Btw, you must try the CHESS PIE! Even if your stuffed... it's so worth it!

Six of us went to The Loveless around 1:00 February 15th for lunch on a Friday afternoon. 
The waiting list was long. We got our names on the list and were handed a pager so we could roam around the shops or sit outside until a table was available. 
We were seated about 45 minutes later. 

I haven't been to the Loveless in years, so I was hoping it hadn't changed too much. 

Complimentary homemade biscuits and homemade jelly with butter. CHECK
Quaint dining room and friendly server. CHECK
Good food. CHECK
Eat until you're uncomfortable. CHECK
Very reasonable. CHECK

Nice experience...YES. We'll be back more often!

If your from the South and want a taste of home cooking then you've come to the right place. If you're not from the South then bless your heart. However, great news, you've come to the right place as well!! The freshly / home cooked food is phenomenal. Every bite puts a smile on my face. Anything you order at any time of day will be great and will exceed all expectations. If you've saved room after your wonderful meal then dive into the desserts. Dear God are they good. My personal favorites are the cobblers and pies. Oh and final warning it is very easy to get full on the homemade biscuits and preserves / jams so pace yourself! :-)

Was invited to this venue for a friends surprise birthday party and my husband was also playing in the band for the r&b brunch. The parking was very confusing and there seemed to only be one valet outside which caused the already jammed parking lot to get even more backed up. He was a nice young man though and offered to help me unload the cupcakes from my car. 

Once inside I loved the atmosphere. It is very pretty. The selling of individual seats seemed unnecessary and very confusing for the hostess...it took a few minutes to figure out what area had been reserved for our party but the young lady was very kind and helpful. 

When I ordered my food I got the burger with fries. Easy enough...right! Can't go wrong with a burger. I heard the waitress tell my friend (who also ordered the burger) that their medium rare was more like rare so she recommended ordering up a temperature. I got my burger well done, plain with no cheese. Mayo, mustard and ketchup only. When it arrived it was so charred I couldn't even finish one half of it and it was smothered in cheese. I also had no condiments so it was even more dry. I would have asked for some but never saw the waitress again. The fries were delicious but I was very disappointed in the burger. 

Overall my two stars are solely based off of the room decor and the fries. 1 for each.

Our experience was wonderful!!
Food was amazing  as was the wine.
Our server Jared was a pleasure, he was friendly, polite and very helpful. The service was OUTSTANDING!!! If we ever return to Nashville, we will definitely dine here again!

Went for our anniversary dinner and Tammy was the best server we've ever had! Entire Menu was tempting and the biscuits were, of course, amazing. Can't wait to go back for more brinner (breakfast for dinner)!!! Love the ambience every time.

Last night my boyfriend and I landed in Nashville for a Bonnaroo vacation, and immediately wanted a classic Southern meal to kick off our week. Loveless Cafe is our favorite spot when in town, but last night our server, Owen, truly made the experience exceptional! Not only was he kind and courteous, but his recommendations and introduction to molasses butter was to die for. His customer service and attention truly made us feel like we were over a friend's house for dinner. Thank you so much for another great experience and for the mini mason jar as a little token to take back home to Los Angeles! XO

Excellent food, the German Potato Salad was amazing. A true German dish. I had the chicken schnitzel sandwich. The chicken was so tender and delicious, the Swiss cheese and ham a nice compliment. The prices are excellent.
The location is great for a business meeting. The atmosphere and character seems a bit forced. Food is mediocre, with some items much better than others. Beer selection isn't as expansive.

Great food, great quality, good service once inside makes this a staple for nashville. My only issue was the 90 minute wait to get in! So,many people wasn't to try the chicken that theirs almost always a long wait. Luckily they provide iced tea and seats for the wait. He chicken gizzards! Haven't had those in years!

Best f ing biscuits ever! Trust me I've had lots of biscuits! Jams really fresh. We had a 45 min wait. But they have little shops to check out. Food was worth the wait. It's one place I've been to that I wish I live closer to so I could go more often.

Fun experience. The entire location is cute and have a great ambience. 
There was some wait in the morning on a sunday, but go early to put your name down then walk around the area. Great selection of southern brunch items. Staff was attentive. Would go again for the amazing biscuit and jams!

Yep, this is the destination as a go to in the Music City area. Kinda out of the way and a long wait, but interesting southern food, and breakfast all day. Go ahead and have the country ham, it's southern and good. Visit the shops and converse with the other waiters from all over the country. A classic place that goes with the Opry. I understand that you might see a country singer there at times. You'll love more not less!!

Welcoming at the door was warm and inviting. Our bartender was very knowledgeable. We had the Bavarian Bierhaus light Helles beer to drink. We also ordered the Bierhaus Wurstteller to eat. We subbed the sauerkraut and red cabbage for green beans and German potato salad. Everything was excellent and perfectly cooked.
Biscuits are amazing. The food was really good. There is a very long wait but I would definitely recommend the wait.
Got sick from the crab bennedict which tasted stale and they didnt seem to care.  Will not be going back.  I have an iron stomach and it still took me down.

Nashville Iconic Landmark!  The food is pretty good, and they have some neat things.  It is a tourist trap, but worth going to (at least once if you are from out of town), and occasionally if you live in town.  Fried Green Tomatoes, jams, and or course the Biscuits.

The area now has other goodies around it... arts and crafts places, entertainment venues, and the terminus of the Natchez Trace Parkway, just a hair down the road!

The biscuits are the best I've ever had and I now know why people actually eat sausage gravy.  The homemade preserves were excellent as well.  My only regret was that I couldn't try everything on the menu.  Will definitely be back.  Be prepared to wait during peak meal times, but they do give you a beeper so that you can shop in their stores while you wait.
Everything here was good prompt service yummy sausages wonderful pretzel, decent sauerkraut good potato salad and felt like  German  the big beer houses in Germany fun place

It was a hour and 10 minute wait to get a table for 7 people on Sunday at 11:30. At least we could kill some time by browsing the small shops nearby but the selections in the hams and jams shop was pretty small but they have jams, honey, peanut brittle, popcorn, nut mixes and some souvenir items. 

The food was average, which is why I rated it 3 stars. It was nice to get complimentary  biscuits and jam. I ordered the French toast with a cup of fresh fruit. The French toast was thick but there wasn't anything "extra special" about them. My friends had the omelette and pancakes and they rated it 3 stars. Good food but nothing special for foodies.
Happy hour 5-7 were great although possibly need some sort sauce on duck sauce rest was great! Wine selection tasting was great

Headed for the Natchez Trace Parkway, we had to stop and try a meal at the iconic Loveless Cafe.  My wife had the fried chicken, dark, with a side salad.  I got the barbecue plate with pinto beans and fried okra.  The chicken was perfect, full of flavor and moist without being greasy.  The barbecue was very good as were the beans and okra.  The biscuits were outstanding.  The service was very good, very prompt and efficient.  Reasonable prices.  This was a good start to our journey on the Trace.

Like the Terminator, I'll be back.

What can you say, it's The Loveless. Is it the best "homecooking" food I've ever had?.... no. But it's darn good and it's VERY Consistent. Your going to be happy, you're gonna be full.... EVERY-TIME!  The staff is the absolute best anywhere around. Exactly what you would expect from a true veteran establishment. They're even serving up a small menu of moonshine cocktails now.... BONUS!  Take out here is great as well. Super convenient, fast, and consistent as well. Try the smoked boneless pork chops.... you can thank me later.

4 people for a 7:00 reservation.
As I got out of my car at Valet, I was informed that CITY WINERY was charging $5.00 for parking, and that did not include the tip. When I asked, the valet person told me I could pay them on the way out.  
Arrived about 6:40 and had some great cocktails at the bar. We were seated at 7:00 and informed that the restaurant was closing at 8:00 for a private function..WTF!!  That information could have upset somebody on a date or out for a nice evening, but we are long time food service professionals, and figured out that the event probably started at 9:00.  Nobody ever pressured us to "order up," but at 8:15 they started moving tables and chairs around us.
We started with the cheese board and the Falafel.   Both were about as predictable as tap water..it's good when you are thirsty(hungry), but not very exciting.
Around the table for dinner we had:
The trout---apparently very satisfying.
Chicken fricassee--the grits were bland
Waygu beef tartare--over processed, DRY, flavorless beef.  The sweet corn and charred scallion relish didn't help. I think they forgot the mustard seed aioli and the cured egg shavings.
Hummus plate--nice hummus.   I'm positive that the peppadew feta was replaced by the peppadew ricotta because it had none of the sharpness of feta cheese.  I did not see the pickled eggplant, and it was replaced with some kind of sweet honey like concoction.
Buratta---it was a glob of bland watery fresh mozzarella, with none of the buttery flavor you might expect.  It did melt nicely.  It was in a small cast iron serving dish, with halved cherry tomatoes and some mild green peppers.  it lacked the pickled garlic and sunflower seed pesto that the menu promised.
Speaking for myself, nothing came to the table piping hot, even in the cast iron serving pieces. 
Nothing was an assult on the taste buds (except for the tartare) , nor was anything memorable.  The menu reads a lot better than the actual food tastes.  I am not sure if the missing food items would have helped.
I realize that the weather has been bad, but if something is on the menu and not going to be on my plate, let me know and I can work around that.

We were asked about seeing a dessert menu, but it was difficult to think they were being sincere about offering it as they picked up tables and chairs around us.

When I picked up my car at Valet, I was never asked for the $5.00.  Not sure what that was about.

It was a pleasant evening because the people I was dining with made it pleasant. 
The food was stunningly adequate.

This was my second time at City Winery. I was disappointed the first time. But since I had to go to an event next door my friends and I thought we'd give it another chance.  Well to bad so sad. I ordered the most expensive think on the menu the ribeye, thinking there was no way to mess that up. I ordered it medium. It came out rare. I sent it back and it came out rate in the center again. I sent it back a third time. To the credit of the management he was embarrassed at the experience we had and  didn't charge me for the steak  or my cocktail. 
But I don't think I'll be back.

Amazing restaurant/wine bar/concert hall. 
Food and wine list A+.  Service was best in Nashville. We will be regulars

So I had been recommended Loveless Cafe for their 'amazing biscuits.' Let me just say: they're good, but not amazing. I definitely wouldn't come and wait in line in the morning for them. The blueberry jam though was TO DIE FOR. And fortunately you can buy it on site! 

The coffee is decent, the omelette was good. The veggies in it were fresh and still had some crunch, which I love. The country ham, which they are also famous for, was really good too. 

The service was excellent. My waitress was very friendly and helpful and always made sure I had just enough coffee :)

Overall, giving it 4 stars because it was good but not quite amazing.

I thought this would be a really kitschy place, but it was actually pretty authentic to food in Germany! The ambiance is really cute, service was good, and there was live German music on a Friday night. It's a tad expensive though, minus the one star.
Good music. Nice atmosphere. The "double shots" are made from cheap liquor.

I am and always will be obsessed with Loveless Cafe. The preserves, the biscuits, what's not to love? I visit it every single time I am in Nashville and I never regret it. I love the Loveless fried chicken with a side of mashed potatoes and macaroni and cheese. I am not a huge pie fan so I have not tried the pies, but everyone has told me that they are SO GOOD. I am also a fan of their waffles. Really, you can't go wrong with anything at Loveless Cafe. I drag every person I know to eat there and they never regret it.

It was excellent food!!! I loved the biscuits they served and al l of the things that they put on them!   The chicken was very good as well!  The service was great to!   It is a must go to place if you are in Nashville!

Wow this place was impressive.We ate a great breakfast of eggs, generous portion of crisp bacon ,hash brown casserole and of course the biscuits. What I enjoyed the most was the fresh preserves . Loved all three, but the blackberry was great! This is not your ordinary cafe!
Hash brown Casserole, homemade biscuits  n homemade jam, country fried steak n eggs w sausage gravy, biscuits n gravy, all amazing!!!!!!!

We're in town from Texas, so we used our phones to find somewhere to eat. This places is about 35 minutes from where we were staying but 35 minutes was nothing compared to the trip from Houston, so we decided to give it a try. We will for sure come back.
Biscuits amazing.
Fried chicken amazing.
Hash brown casserole amazing.
Did I say chicken was amazing?

This is classic southern food, if your visit the Nashville area you need to go. The breakfast, lunch and dinner are great. The biscuits are the best! They are a meal in themselves. The service is awesome as well.
So much food on that plate. Chicken and dumplings were delicious tonight as were the sides. Only wished we had room for dessert. Ate too many biscuits before the meal.

This place deserves 0 stars. Warning to Tourists and Locals. This place because of lack of manners by The Owner and 
One Male Manger is the worst place l have ever been in.  
The Monday night l went to the bar and was thrown out-3 others got the boot too. 
Read the reviews on The Facebook page called "Hot Shotz." As l was writing my review for HS on their Facebook page, l read a review from a lady tourist from Mississippi. She was reporting what happened to her the night after l was there. She was with her boyfriend and was grabbed in the Arse while she was sitting at the bar. She complained to the bartenders. They said they could do nothing because it was their boss who had grabbed her-The Male Manager on duty. He has a glass in his hand. He dropped it on purpose and glass went everywhere. 
The night l went to the bar it was not busy. I accidentally bumped into A Blond Lady who was built like a football player. 
I could have gotten hurt. I did not know 
l had run into Owner- "The Queen of Nashville." The Queen said to me-"Do You Always Run Into People and not say excuse me?" She had a extreme attitude and did not say she was The Owner. 
I thought she was a mean drunk. I said are you drunk?" Because it seemed like she was taking it to far over me accidentally running into her. A normal person would have let it go. She said  "l am not drunk, l am the Owner." I have never said this to a Woman before but l said exactly what l thought. I could not control what automatically came out. I said like Bette Davis-"What A itch." Her reply- she said 
"l can kick you out for anything since l am The Owner. " She set me up and wanted to let me have it. Then she said get out. 
I said are you kidding-I am not drunk (only had 2 small Cokes.) Then l said let me talk to someone and l will leave."  She said "NO." The Queen grabbed my plastic cup of Coke out of my hand and throws it into the bar area. She had lost it-could have hit the bartender. Then The Queenie als her good Old Boys- her Posse. Get her-The 2 Bubba's come up on either side of me and both grabbed a arm. They were throwing me out. I thought is this real? 
Or am l in a Hollywood Movie staged in The Old West? I started to fall-they continued to drag me out as fast as possible. The whole bar stopped and watched. I was thrown out into Freezing 19 DEGREES weather. I tried to ask the  guy at the door to help me. He told someone he was lucky he was deaf in the ear l was talking to him. So l went to the his other side. 
Then The Queen calls the police. She told me you can't stand there-you are still on my property. I wanted to call the police but Of course my phone was dead. Not one person coming out of the bar would call the Police in my behalf. 
One lady who came out did talk to me. Her advise was to leave. She knew the owner and was afraid she would press charges and l could be arrested. 
I have reported this Bar to The Nashville Mayor's Office Assistant /Claudia H. 
She is sending a report to The Nashville Tourist department. The tourist Dept does not Nashville to appear like this. 
I filed yesterday this business?? with 
The Better business bureau, posted a review of the bar on their FB page, and last Twitter. You do not treat Customers like this. Especially a Virginian. 
Too bad the bartender and The 2 Musicians were great. I went in because of The Music.  
Another review from 2015 from Yelp,        a Customer review said The Owner started a fight with her Girlfriend at the bar while she was there. The police and a ambulance had to come. The picture is still with among the pictures posted here. 
Be careful where you go in Nashville on Broadway and nearby. Read the reviews of places. The above could happen. Some bars are old. Somehow they pass the safety code. But watch out for tiny steps that are not marked well as you go in. 
I am no longer a local-No more Broadway bars for me. They like their money and could careless about the safety of their customers.

It lives up to all the hype.   If you want a down-home, country dinner, this is the place.   I had the fried chicken and it was amazing.  The biscuits and jam were out of this world.  It was soooo good.   I ate so many biscuits I had to take most of my meal home with me.

It is worth the wait, seriously, it is that good.

Best biscuits and jam ever. The turkey and swiss sandwich with grilled onions was divine along with the fried okra.  And the virgin Bloody Mary really packed a spicy punch.  To top it off, our waiter Matt had a fabulous personality.  I would definitely come here again!

This year for Spring Break, with the kiddos, we decided to take a two week road trip to the Grand Canyon from DC. We started planning the trip in November and when we looked for places to stop on the way, Nashville and the Loveless Cafe were both high on the list. The Loveless Cafe is not what I would consider a tourist trap, it's a great experience!  The restaurant is a nice old house that has had some updates but has a lot of character. The service is great and the people are so nice. The food was great; I am a coffee snob and the coffee was less than ok, but my husband said it wasn't terrible. To help me forget about the coffee, I had pulled pork and two eggs over medium and it was some of the best pork I have ever had. My husband had a pork omelet and the hash brown casserole and he said it was better than great!  The kids had pancakes and sausage and although they didn't finish their food (a huge plate of pancakes) they loved them!  The biscuits were really good! You can view the baker rolling these out in the hallway behind a window.  Definitely the best biscuits I have eaten at a restaurant; it's difficult to make delicious biscuits in bulk and Loveless can/does!  It was a great experience and we will definitely visit again when we're passing through. A+ 
Lastly, we arrived at 0730 on Sunday morning, by 0817 there was a wait to be seated!  Everyday is a great day!
Great breakfast today and the service was top notch.  The biscuits and country ham make it worth the trip over from Smyrna.

Great restaurant. The biscuits a awesome and they just keep coming. I have only eaten breakfast there but the rest of the menu looks great as well. It is a tourist attraction so I recommend going early or be prepared to wait.

Absolutely the biggest tourist trap in Nashville. Just awful. Flavorless pork pounded flat, fries, worst Rueben ever, and two beers. $87 including tip. If you are into dropping substantial cash and having instant diarrhea from the low quality grease, then this is your dream restaurant. Enjoy!

Speaking to the owners degrading comments, please let me apologize for forgetting about the horribly expensive, dripping (literally) with grease, Rueben Egg Rolls we had as an appetizer. So sorry. Hope the math adds up for you now since you called me a liar.

A local friend recommended this location for Sunday lunch, boasting about the ham and gravy.  What she didn't tell us was the average 2 hour wait.

We spent some time running in and out of the shops.  Samples were amazing and we got some pumpkin butter to take home.  We still had over an hour to wait.

Once we were seated, service was fast and attentive.  We all loved our homecooked food and didn't eat again for the rest of the day.

If you are coming here, be sure to have plenty of time.  We would have preferred to not take up so much of our limited Nashville time...but we have some great memories of this unique place.
Kimberly is the most amazing server I have ever had her kind attitude and over all demeanor made my night! Loved the half chicken as well

Second time here and as good as the first time! Virginia helped us celebrate a birthday by totally embarrassing my 21 year daughter by asking her to come to the center of the restaurant and having the whole place sing to her.  Eggs, biscuits and Hashbrown casserole is perfect after celebrating 21st birthday on Broadway!

I was only in Nashville for a short time, but managed to swing by the Bierhaus for a great dinner. The pretzels with beer cheese were a huge hit with the whole fam. As for beer, I had the Hefeweizen and it was cold, spicy, and just right. I went for an appetizer as my meal and chose the Rueben rolls. THEY WERE AMAZING. Get them.

Food is good but we have had better. We actually prefer Monell's food for both breakfast and dinner overall. 

But no one can compare to Loveless biscuits and preserves! They are simply the best. 

3 star for food. 5 star for biscuits! 4 overall.

Ok I still love seeing shows here. Seriously. It's a great listening room, and still a great place for intimate shows. But wow has the service gone downhill. 

I've had odd experiences with the valet service the last several times I've been to City Winery.

At a show in December, the valet left a phone charger in my car. Why were they in my car long enough to charge a phone? Or if they weren't in my car while the phone was charging, why were they using my car as a mobile charging station?

At another show in December, I got the, what I've now learned is common, speech about tipping. It's insulting and unprofessional to ask for tips, especially at the beginning of the evening, when the service hasn't been completed. The valets are the first people we encounter at City Winery, so to start the evening with a lecture about the importance of tipping is off putting to say the least. I've always tipped, so it's just weird to start the night with such an accusatory speech.

At a show this month, I again got the terrible, off-putting tipping speech.Tips (which I have always, always given) are optional based on service - they shouldn't be requested at the beginning of the evening. 

Lastly, what is wrong with the plumbing at this place? Two out of the last three times I've been there, the women's restroom was closed because of plumbing issues. Get it together, City Winery.
Trendy, infesting menu, I had the pork steak,  great taste proportionately though I found it lacking, generously sized just a little out of balance with the accompaniments.

Really enjoyed Loveless Cafe. I ordered smoked turkey, mashed potatoes and corn and all of it was excellent. We received our food in record time and was in and out in thirty minutes or less. The famous biscuits lived up to the hype with strawberry, blackberry and peach jam. 

This is a must restaurant if you like southern home cooking and a neat atmosphere. I would highly recommend and look forward to returning soon.

I can't say enough about this place. We came here for New Years Eve and saw Marty Stuart. We had a table in the VIP balcony area. Upon checking in we were immediately escorted to our table and then greeted by our waiter. We were seated at one of the bar top tables, which are not nearest the railing. Our view was slightly obstructed and when I mentioned it to our waiter, Patrick, he moved us to a closer table and our view was fantastic. 

We ordered the cheese plate appetizer, a bottle of champagne. I had the trout and my girl a steak; everything was delicious. The show was phenomenal and the crowd respectful. 

Overall, the whole experience was tops and was the highlight of our trip.
3.5 stars, really.  My country fried steak was quite tasty.  Can't say the same about the mashed potatoes, though.  Hour wait on Sunday at 3 PM was odd.  The blackberry jam was quite awesome.

Prepare to wait a long time for southern food. This place is always crowded. Yes, the jams are tasty. The chicken tenders are huge. The mac n cheese is pretty creamy. The green beans are a bit too spicy for my taste but still flavorful. The prices are a tad steep but I expected that since it's such a popular tourist attraction. I recommend ordering takeout to avoid the crowds, but your food is probably going to be cold.

The food wasn't that great.  Beer was good.  We had higher expectations for a flavorful meal.  It's a really nice restaurant though which should do well in this very touristy area.  Two beers, two meals, tax and tip about $72.
So fun and delicious!! Staff is so friendly!! Highly recommend the Chicken friend steak and chicken and waffles!
Great selection of German beers. Love the atmosphere. Not many options for those who only eat fish.
Sooo good! Worth the drive if staying in Nashville! Great staff and fantastic breakfast.  Plus some fun shops right there when you are done eating.
Awesome for a glass of wine and maybe some cheese. Wouldn't recommend for dinner. Cool venue.

I really wanted to love this place.Unfortunately, it missed the great mark for me.

Let me start with the pros...
Beautiful ambiance, happy hour specials, great event venue, solid menu
The restaurant itself is gorgeous. There is an upstairs event space, a spacious bar area and a great stage set up. A group of 6 of us ordered dinner while watching the Marc Cohn show last week. 

Dinner: Everyone enjoyed the food. The service was less than impressive though. The server seemed to be overwhelmed by the tables he had. It took forever for him to take orders for cocktails. Then an even longer forever to come back with cocktails. Then add on some more forever to take out orders.

Nothing ruins a beautiful dining experience like subpar service. You can correct an underwhelming dish, but underwhelming service can ruin an experience for me. Having been a server/bartender for a number of years I am both very critical (internally) but also forgiving (externally) when it comes to service. I am never rude, even if the service is subpar. That being said, it is an absolute pet peeve of mine when a server cannot keep up with who ordered what at a table of 6. In an establishment as nice as City Winery that just should not be the case. It is a complete moodkiller for the server to have people at the table check off what they had on a printed out receipt. It is even more annoying when the server encourages the table to split the check evenly because "it's easier that way". Unless there is a policy against separate checks that is indicated to a party at the outset, it is the server's responsibility to separate checks. It is a pain in the a** to do so, but that is what is expected. 

Ultimately we ended up splitting it evenly because after the 2nd return everyone was irritated. I will note that the show was over completely before we even got to the even split of the checks, though everyone was done eating before that. All and all, I would go back again and hope that this experience was an aberration from the norm.
Love the Loveless!  I've never had a bad meal here.  It's taken time, but I've finally learned to NOT visit on the weekends or holidays.  The wait can be incredibly long.

Absolutely the worst restaurant I have ever eaten at
Bugs in my silverware and terrible service doesn't even start to explain it
The manager when informed did nothing at all!!! 
They wouldn't even return my phone calls!!

We knew them before they became popular, just a tiny little shack with closed motel rooms around them. Thought they were amazing then, and think they are amazing now with shops all around them now. The service and food are all amazing! You won't be disappointed if you love good country cooking. Everything we are in the area, we always go there for breakfast.

The place to go when you come to Nashville! Great country ham, biscuits, homemade preserves, and all things Nashville. Wonderful gift shop.  Friendly people and good outdoor spots to wait for a table where you can sit around a picnic table and talk with friends and family just like you would on a front porch, and they have one of those too! Wonderful!

For our breakfast stop on the way out of Nashville, this really was a great spot. Biscuits are all they're cracked up to be, with either gravy from our platter poured on top or the housemade jams. Sausage patties crumbled in your mouth, ham was nice (although a little salty for my taste), plenty of scrambled eggs, and beans. Needless to say, we left full and very satisfied.

Also, whoever is in charge of the merchandising and gift shops are "on point". Fantastic collection of shirts, souvenirs, etc including the brilliant shirt that says, "Taking care of biscuits" haha
So glad I stopped here. Good food and excellent beer. I sat at the bar and the service was great.
Two dollar beers, bartenders are friendly. If this bar was in Dallas it would be packed every day and more likely in Deep Ellum. I really liked this bar I would definitely go here againg.

We stopped by for a late lunch after spending some time at the Botanical Gardens. We were told the wait would be 45 minutes and it turned out to be 30 minutes. We walked around the grounds and sat in the shade. We were given complimentary ice water and lemonade. Our waitress Nancy(?) was very pleasant and helpful. She made us drinks off menu. The biscuits and preserves were excellent. The chicken and sides were very good. The amount of food was incredible. In retrospect we should have split a meal and just order extra sides.

Pace yourselves. Is all I have to say! I overdid it! The biscuits are so good. Ridiculous good. So good you could eat them plain, but why would you when there are the best jams ever on the plate? The peach jam is like eating the best peach cobbler on a biscuit. The blackberry still has pieces of the blackberries intact?? How do they do that?? The strawberry is good, but not as noteworthy as the other two. Oh, and they will bring more biscuits, but cut them off after two plates! 

I prefer the turnip greens at Arnold's, but hey to each is own! They were really the only thing I wasn't over the moon about! The sweet tea is perfectly sweetened. Not too sweet, not too bitter, just right! I had fried chicken and it was sublime! Would definitely order it again. The string bean casserole was a little taste of thanksgiving in may...score! 

I also had the chicken and bacon soup chowder which was delicious. Not salty at all, perfectly seasoned! My friend and I both had pie, the strawberry rhubarb and steeplechase ( derby style pie) and they were perfect slices, not too big and not too small, definitely too small to share, but perfect when you already regretted ordering it!! Delicious both of them!

Well worth the wait, and theres plenty to shop before you eat! Oh and ask for Virginia! She's the best waitress!!!

Good country grub at a very "hot" stop in Nashville. Plan on spending over an hour to wait.  The food is good and the prices are reasonable. I guess it's the type of place you have to go to once.  Everything we tried was really good, just not great.  I had far better meals during my trip.
It's good. It's fun. Just not worth the wait.

Enjoyed the food, beers and atmosphere.  Felt like we were back in Munich.  Maddie was an awesome bartender!
Prost

My friends love this place and said its a highlight of their city. I thought it was just okay. 

The property is pretty cool. An old inn converted to a restaurant and shops (too bad the shops were closed by the time we got there). The interior is country kitchen. It was cute but nothing spectacular. 

We started with the complimentary biscuits and preserves. These were marvelous. Probably the highlight of the meal. 

I ordered the fried chicken with creamed corn and mac and cheese. The mac was okay. The chicken skin was good, but the meat itself was a little dry. I was disappointed. The creamed corn was amazing! I would eat a ton of that. 

The service was good. All in all, it was okay but I wouldn't say it was one of the best parts of my Nashville experience.

I've only come here for shows and it's not some place I get excited about when someone comes to town I want to see. I don't like how you get crammed in to tiny tables where you feel uncomfortable to even eat. The food is awful. I tried several apps on the menu and was unimpressed. The only reason I gave this place 2 stars was I really enjoyed the bottle of wine we ordered.. so I guess thanks for having it on the menu? The service was HORRIBLE. I sat for 20 min before the waiter even came to my table. It then took him 10 min to come back to take my order. Then he just completely disappeared. It wasn't until the end when he was anxiously wanting the bill paid that i saw him on numerous occasions. It was infuriating. I'll go here again I'm sure for shows, but I will never eat a meal here and will know what type of service to expect in the future.

My 1st time in Nashville & this cafe was highly recommended by my stepdaughter. It was very hot that day & the cafe had a wait of 1 hour & 15mins at 2:00 pm. Wish they had a waiting room for the overflowing tourists & locals willing to wait almost 2 hrs to dine. Thus the 4 star.
They're known for their biscuits.I agree. It was very moist & savory.Choice of their 3 exclusive brand, BlackBerry,Strawberry  & Peach. Peach was my personal choice.
My husband & I split the three meat + 2 sides. Fried chicken (1 thigh) Fried Catfish & pulled BBQ pork. Quite small portions for $17.99. Sides were cream corn pickled cucumber/onions,both were okey. 
The staff however has the Southern hospitality. Great waitstaff. 
The dining area is bright, clean,& well decorated with a local artist's paintings which are funny & beautiful.
I will go back to Loveless & try other dishes.

Ate breakfast this morning at the Loveless Cafe with my fiancee.  Thursday morning, 7:30am, so no wait for a table.  Our server, Bruce, brought us two biscuits.  Not sure what all the hype is about, they didn't taste like anything special.  Also, my fiancee was miffed because she wanted to order a Bloody Mary, but Bruce said it was before 8am, so she couldn't get one yet.

So things didn't start off well, but they soon improved once our food arrived at the table.  I had ordered the Pit-Cooked Pork Barbeque & Eggs (One to the Left and One to the Right), and my fiancee had ordered the Fried Chicken & Waffle.  Our meals were good, I had a hard time finishing the generous portion of pork on my plate.  Wasn't really crazy about the red BBQ sauce on top, but it was OK.  Hash brown casserole was tasty, I liked it.  My fiancee liked her Chicken & Waffle quite a bit, the waffle itself was very good, delicious.  

And Bruce had brought us out more hot biscuits and a Bloody Mary in a mason jar for my fiancee.  Overall, a good experience this morning at the Loveless Cafe, we would like to come back again, but it is about 85 miles away from where we live, so I imagine that won't be happening anytime soon.  I recommend giving them a go if you are in Nashville.
if i just ate the schnitzel and drink the beer it would be a 5 for sure. the sausages are good but everything else i have tried isn't 5 star stuff.

The peach preserves are a masterpiece!!! Great southern cooking - tastes like homemade! Fried chicken is incredible - how do they make that crust?!! Mashed potatoes are the real deal and the macaroni and cheese makes you want seconds. Don't worry about dessert - the biscuits with butter and peach preserves are dessert!

Plan your trip carefully - the wait time can be long. We waited 45 minutes.

We stopped in while visiting Nashville and  were impressed with the Bavarian Bierhaus from the moment we walked in. The ambiance immediately makes you feel like you're in Munich. They young lady who greeted us was warm and friendly. The bartender, Shawn, was our server. He was thoroughly knowledge about the impressive German beer selection, as well as the German food that is available. We had several questions about both, and he seemed more than happy to thoroughly answer each of them. The beers were terrific and each of us LOVED our meals, which were authenticity prepared and delicious. Nashville has a lot to offer with regard to restaurants and bars, but next time we visit we'll most certainly come back to the Bavarian Bierhaus.

Gotta start with the biscuits. After all Loveless makes about 7500 a day! Usually tender, flaky, fresh as fresh can be, right out of the oven. I often pop them into my mouth before I even have a chance to smear on the strawberry, peach, or blackberry preserves. (Honey and Sorghum are available on request.) All you want-all day long. But save a little room for a delicious breakfast. You name it they'll make it. Today I had a gigantic Barbecue Pork  with 2 eggs over easy (cooked perfectly). Honestly, I think there was nearly a pound of meat not he platter...no kidding! But wait. Can't decide what you want for breakfast? How about a sampler several meats and sides.? If you brought friends and family...they got you covered--Family Style Breakfast includes most of the above and sausage gravy too. Be sure to try the Hashbrown Casserole or maybe the BBQ omelet - 3 eggs and enough stuffing to fill a suitcase...(well, maybe not quite that much). 

Oh, you're here for lunch? Fried chicken, meatloaf (better than Mom's...sorry Mom), and finger lickin' good Pork Chops. So much good stuff, I never have room for dessert...but you might, and they got it too.

Service is alway top-notch and extremely cordial...but a slight misstep today (entered the wrong order for our breakfast in their computer system and brought us the wrong plates. .... They apologized profusely, but dampened our enthusiasm inasmuch as we were there with friends visiting from California.

Can be a bit noisy.

Be patient...the wait for a table can be anywhere from 20 to 40 minutes or more. But take heart, the wait is worth it for a special experience...at least once.

Delicious good ol' southern comfort food. Their fried chicken, catfish, pulled pork, okra, fried green tomatoes, and biscuits are all amazing, and that's just the food that I've tried. If you've had Monell's, Loveless is similar (in terms of food) to Monell's but with a more intimate setting because you get to sit at your own tables. They have options for ordering a single order as well as ordering a buffet-style meal. The only real downside is that it is a bit far out from downtown Nashville/Vandy.
Very overpriced for breakfast.  catering to tourist. I am local and quit eating at Loveless.

Thursday night at 7...no wait!  Triple choice with chicken, meatloaf and catfish was outstanding.  Cream corn and green beans were excellent sides.  Endless biscuits with various jams are always amazing.

Listed on Open Table but unable to make reservations. Called the restaurant and the woman said they didn't take reservations on weekends but it's a weekday and they would be taking reservations period. Terrible system to try and eat there. Probably never will.

Been here multiple times and I have loved my trip EVERY SINGLE TIME!  They have the best biscuits on the entire planet; warm, flakey, buttery, melts in your mouth and with the choice of three of their home made jams! (Peach, Blackberry, and Strawberry) The food speaks for itself and is absolutely delicious. I would suggest the Southern Sampler because you can try some of their best meals all in one in decent sized portions. They also have gift shops that you can explore while you wait, that sell some of their special ingredients to little fun knick knacks! Highly recommend trying this timeless, classic out!

WOW. I mean the reviews are clear...it is definitely a tourist trap..however, well worth the wait. We arrived and waited 45 minutes for a table, they have little shops and such to visit while you wait. Biscuits biscuits and more biscuits - their peach marmalade was amazing! Their sampler platter was the best - however I had hoped for more of each meat and less biscuits...but alas..5 biscuits later...darn good food! 

And of course...couldn't leave without dessert...their steeplechase pie and banana pudding...amazing! 

Great value - prices are very reasonable.

Location is so/so - not much in the area, but the Checkwood Botanical gardens are nice.

No love for the Loveless Cafe. We waited about an hour to be seated for dinner and after eating there, I figured this had to be a tourist trappy type of place. The drive to the cafe was beautiful as we passed by large homes with acres of property. During our wait, we were given a buzzer that would work at their different gift shops. My winning find was the piggy popcorn cooked in bacon grease with bacon bits at the Hams & Jams Country Market. I will definitely order that online. 

All of the workers were super friendly. Their specialty fried chicken was bland and dry. The fried catfish and fried green tomatoes had the same batter and were both bland. Yes, even the biscuits were kinda bland. Maybe that's just the way it's supposed to be so you can smother gravy on everything. I honestly enjoyed the food at Cracker Barrel better... and that's not meant to be an insult.

I had catfish it was just ok, the hush puppies and slaw were not good at all. The biscuits and jam are good. This was my first trip to loveless and I am local and see no reason to return.  Tourist love it!

I thoroughly enjoyed the Loveless Cafe except for two small things: the distance from downtown (thank God for Uber!), and...don't kill me, but...I didn't think the biscuits lived up to the hype. Maybe it was just an off night. 

Everything else, however, was great! I had the fried chicken with a side of green beans and mashed potatoes. Even the smaller portion of the chicken was more than enough. The alcohol was a little expensive, but my cocktail was good. We went on a weeknight and were able to make a 7:45pm reservation the day of with no problem.  It's very cute inside, and the service was quick. I'd return if I go to Nashville again.

Bought a Groupon on 8/24/16 City Winery  -- Valid Monday-Friday: Lunch for Two. On 8/29/16 we walked to have lunch there. When we walked in we noticed that the area surrounding the bar was completely empty. The hostess just looked at us and I explained that were there to have lunch. She informed us that they were no longer open for lunch Monday through Friday. I then told her I had just recently purchased a Groupon (5 days earlier) 

Obviously exasperated by the situation I explained to the hostess that we had walked to the restaurant and I asked if she could give us any ideas on where we could go have lunch. She sarcastically mentioned that there was a hotdog stand nearby and gave no more information. Her behavior was unnecessary and rude. I should've known better then  go to a chain restaurant.

My first trip to the Bavarian Bierhaus rated a five because the live music really made the experience unique and fun. The second time I dined here there was no live music, so it was somewhat of a more ordinary dining experience. (But still fun)

The prices are in the higher than average midrange for the food and beer. If you're like me you probably don't mind paying higher than average menu prices for a fuller experience, so it's definitely worth your while to call ahead to see if the live band is playing. It think live music makes the beer taste better. LOL

The menu selections include authentic German cuisine, and everything I tried was excellent. They have a lot beer choices to compliment the menu, and I recommend trying the beer sampler at least once just for the experience. 

I can say that even though this is a mall restaurant, it's separated enough from the mall area that you almost forget you're in a mall. I can imagine that Oktoberfest at the Bavarian Bierhaus is probably a riot, so we'll be sure to plan a visit around that time.

Final tally.... four stars without the live music, and five stars with it!!

I was lucky enough to win a tour of the winery with three friends. We had a wonderful time! Our sommelier (I think his name is Evan) was personable and informative - and he had answers to all of our questions. The venue is lovely. We didn't have dinner there because it was a little pricey for us, but the menu looked terrific. I think I would like to go back again to  hear some music. Something to look forward to ...

Really fun atmosphere to walk into, very loud and fun. Staff was very nice and welcoming, the waiter helped my husband pick out a delicious beer also. I only really had one complaint, it was our first time coming here and the waiter offered us some apple sauce for our baby. We thought it was just a polite gesture, but we were charged 3$ for this apple sauce. Had I known it was a "side item" I wouldn't have gotten it. Our baby is 8 months old and only ate like 5 bites off of it. Either way we told him we didn't mind paying for it but I wish I had known before hand we would be charged 3$ for something I thought was just complementary. I got the Oktoberfest chicken which was pretty tasty, I didn't like the red cabbage that came with it but that's just my opinion. My husband loved the red cabbage. He got the Rouland and he said it was delicious. We ended it with the apple strudel dessert. OMG so delicious. I will probably get that dessert everytime I go back. It was a pretty pricey place but it wasn't bad for an occasional visit. We enjoyed it overall.
Great place! Food was good. Biscuits were hot and fresh. Waitress Joni was super! I recommend it! Gotta have the homemade banana pudding!!!!!

I attend the Taste of Nashville event here. It was a little of an annoyance to try & find a parking place. We parked in a pay lot. The event space is large area that has a stage at one end. At the Taste of Nashville, they had tables set up on the sides of the event space and also in the center. This allows for people to be able to walk around the space and partake from the different venders. 

The space is large, but I think Taste of Nashville overshot the space size, because to get through the event you had below & bump into people. The bathrooms at Rocketown are located under a catwalk that extends along a part of the building. The bathrooms were large enough to accommodate people in the large group without have to wait in line. I say that about the men's restroom, I think the woman had to form a line.

Overall I had no issues with Rocketown, other than I'd like them to have a little more parking. The space is pretty bare, allowing you to decorate how you'd like. At Taste of Nashville they had colorful paper lanterns hanging around. The event space is great if you're looking for a place with a stage. I have to say that I like City Winery & The Bell Tower better as an event space, Bell Tower being the front runner. Both are also in the same area as Rocketown.

I love, love, love the Loveless Cafe! I highly recommend their biscuits and gravy (their the best I've ever had)! Their scrambled eggs with cheese, hashbrowns (they have cheese in them, too), and fruit preserves are great, too! 

The atmosphere is so cute and country with their checkered print table clothes and farm-y feel. I also loved the shops that are located on their grounds which is a great way to kill time (as the wait is 1-3 hours). If you're on the go and don't have time to wait, I recommend getting it to go and dining on the benches in front of the cafe. I'll be sure to go back!
Great food, super friendly service...biscuits, chicken, bbq, country fried steak were all ordered in our group.  All very happy & full!

Such a cool music venue! I have not had their wine or their food, but I am happy City Winery brought this unique music venue to Nashville. From what I observed, the table service was very professional and nice. 

Only concern: the venue is not in a location with a lot of street parking close by...or in an area I would feel comfortable parking in. We were pretty much required to use valet for $7.
We have been here a few times. It is always fun, the music and shows we choose have been great. The food choices and wine are just top notch. The over all atmosphere of the place is fun and relaxing.

Best breakfast ever! Worth the wait. We waited about 45 minutes. While we were waiting we walked around the property where we samples peach cobbler hot tea- so good. Hashbrown casserole is an absolute must. Biscuits were amazing. Everything was delicious.
Went Fri night around 5, got seated right away.  Ordered breakfast.  Was good but nothing to brag about.  The biscuits and preserves were the best part.

We've heard so many great things and people told us we had to go. So we stopped by on our way back home from our Nashville trip, even though it was 44 minutes out of our way. Got there and there was an hour and 10 minute wait. I was told there would be a wait so it was expected. They have little shops you can browse around to kill some time. We were seated and staff was friendly. I ordered the Loveless Fried Chicken (half chicken), green beans and mac n cheese. They brought out biscuits and I tell you i took one bite and it threw me back to being a little girl at my grannies table. The chicken, in my opinion, wasn't all that great. It was dry and didn't really have much flavor. The green beans were good and the Mac n cheese were mediocre. But, honestly, I will go back just for the biscuits alone.

The Loveless is a great place, with sprawling grounds formed from the bones of an old highway motel.  Nowadays, it houses a music venue, gift shop, tourist items and... authentic southern food.  
If you like biscuits with preserves like your grandma from the farm made, and fried chicken with okra, mashed potatoes and hush puppies, this is your place.  I've visited a few times and I'm personally not a fan of this style of food - pretty much everything is battered, breaded, fried, and carbolicious.  However, it is a fun place to take some out-of-town guests who want to live the southern comfort food life for a couple of hours and don't mind going a bit away from the city.  Treat your arteries to some real gravy, butter on your biscuit, and fried catfish while you're here.  It's not good for you, but it's tasty, authentic, and worth a trip once in a while.

Beer was good; food was not. I was very exited to see a new German restaurant in town especially after my trip to Germany. Although the food choices were familier the quality wasn't the same as what we had in Germany. The pretzels just didn't quite match up, the schwinebraten was dry, and the kartoffelsalat was cold (usually served warm in Germany). I'd be able to over look all of that because the space is huge (great for large parties), the staff was friendly and attentive, and the beer was delicious, but it was soooo expensive to not have excellent food too that I doubt I'll be returning.
Best breakfast I have had! The biscuit are so darn good! Loved the stored. The jams, meats and chicken are the bomb!

If all you ate here was the fried chicken and biscuits every day of your life, 3 things would occur. #1, you'd be happy and full everyday of your life. #2, you would give it a 5-Star review every time. And #3, you would die young of a heart attack.  But you'd be very happy (and weigh about 400lbs).

This was the first time I have ever waited 1.5 hr to eat at a restaurant.  Service was great.  I had the fried chicken which was very tasty, crispy, and juicy.  My husband had country ham (which was too salty for his taste), scrambled eggs (which tasted like fluffly foam), and hashbrown casserole (which was too cheesy and heavy).  The biscuits were different, but I wouldn't say they're the best in the world.  I really liked their peach preserves.  The food came out very quickly.  So many people were turned away after hearing there was now a 2-hr wait, but more came to wait.

My wife and I came here back in the winter for the first time and absolutely loved it.  We came back to experience the great food and atmosphere but were severely disappointed.

They have changed chefs, which means a new menu and the food is lacking (to say the least).  The cheese plate was good but not enough bread.  We also had the Brussel sprout salad but it is bland, very bland.  Anytime we see bone marrow on the menu, we order it but this was nothing of the sort.  They loaded it up with saved lemons (really?) and the bread was soft, big and purple.  No capers, no garlic, no sea salt - do not order this dish.  We finished up with the duck flatbread which was the best thing of the night we ate (and that isn't saying much).  

With all the local, incredible good choices in Nashville, we will mark this place off our list.  Don't waste your time and your money; we came on a Tuesday night and there was literally 4 other tables filled in the restaurant - no one at the bar, no buzz and nothing to be desired.

Exceptional food, comfortable country atmosphere, friendly folksy service...what's not to love??? The biscuits haven't been topped anywhere - smooth and silky. The gravy, jams and jellies were all homemade and complimented the biscuits well. 

We'll definitely be back!

Loveless Cafe is absolutely delightful and one that shouldn't be missed by anyone visiting Nashville. The restaurant is located outside of Nashville on Hwy 100. The restaurant sign is clearly visible from the highway with its blue color and neon lighting.

There are several building structure within the "compound" which houses the restaurant, the market, bbq pit/smokehouse, local arts store, and other buildings. The restaurant itself in nondescript and unassuming with a short flight of stairs leading to the main entrance. The inside of the restaurant is warm and inviting. It feels like visiting a Southern home where you are always welcome. The walls are decorated with pictures of famous celebs (country music stars, I think but not too sure since I didn't really look too closely at the photographs) with autographs. 

The servers were friendly and accommodating. We came around 10 in the morning so it was not too busy.  Our server was quite attentive and didn't need prompting for any refills.  My friend ordered waffles while I ordered fried pork chop. The biscuit was complimentary along with the different jams and preserves.  The food that we ordered was amazing but the biscuit was exceptional.It was not greasy but soft and flaky...delicious.  I wasn't fond of biscuits before but their biscuit turned me into a believer :) Such a great example of how good Southern cooking is and a reminder of how much I miss it. If there was one thing that I regret though is that we didn't order the fried chicken liver :(

I heard that wait time can be long on the weekends so it might be better to schedule a trip during the week. Overall, this was definitely worth the drive over from Nashville.  If I am back in the area, I will definitely come back to eat.

Prices were okay and reasonable. They have a parking lot that offers free parking.

Kimberly was a wonderful, attentive server for our large bachelorette party for dinner and drinks. She took great care of us and never grew impatient! 
Also, the Brussels sprouts here are FIRE!!! The barrel-aged Sauvignon Blanc hit the spot and the Cabernet Sauvignon was also smooth.

When in the #Nashville #TN area, this quaint little place tucked away in the burbs is a fantastic find if you're after country style dining. The old charm of family meals is reason enough to venture out yonder. I brought my wife and two grandkids here for Sunday brunch on our way back to #LittleRock #AR after a fun-filled #FourthOfJuly #roadTrip in 2014. A cultural icon, the Loveless restaurant is built into a vintage 1950s motor-hotel complex. Far from a tourist trap, Loveless is a local favorite. We make the extra effort in our travels to find places where locals eat. We had our usual favorites: chicken & waffles, bacon, eggs done to order, fresh fruit, buttermilk pancakes, sausages, and (of course) freshly made grits with lotsa butter. The Bride had #mimosas and I had #MoonshineMary (#BloodyMary w moonshine) -- both served in  mason jars. The servers were fun, attentive, and very friendly. This is home. Plenty of free on-premises parking. Prices are reasonable. You may wait a spell but with customers trekking from all parts #USA and the World, it's worth the wait.

Full of love cafe!!!!! We came here for breakfast and had the best experience.  Love how attentive our handsome waiter was to our every need.  He was also very quick to recommend other items on the menu that he felt we would enjoy more.  He was right and we left full and in high spirits.  Till next time!

I found this German joint by accident, and have been there couple times. 
First time I went the place was dead. Our group of about 10 were the only customers, quiet, nothing much going on just some noise from the big screen TV. 

Then second time...the place was packed and live band was signing some German music like no tomorrow, no way to have any conversation. 

So this place serves German beers...in 1L size, which is cool. Or you can try the tasting. 

Food quality is...boring and nothing special. I'd rather eat at mission bbq next door and then head to this bar for fun.
Very nice music venue! Not a bad seat in the house! I love being able to pick my seat when ordering! The food is equally good! Service great as well!

Does it get better than Loveless Cafe? No, probably not. 

When I lived in Nashville this was one of my absolute favorite places to go for breakfast. Sure, it's sort of a hike from the city, but the drive is scenic and the biscuits are worth it. So are the preserves. I still dream about the preserves actually. I could totally go for some right now...

Anyway, everything is really good here. I won't lie to you, dear reader. You will probably have to wait. You may have to wait for a very long time to eat at the Loveless Cafe. But trust me, it's worth it.

Everything I have had there has been wonderful. I've had omelets, I've had pancakes, I've had breakfast ham, and various other side dishes. They're all good. And in Nashville, we know our food. If Loveless Cafe is that busy, it's for a reason. 

You can always check out the nearby shops when you wait. Pro tip: the preserves are sold there. Buy some.

Oof. This place was just terrible today. We asked for a table outside, and stood three feet away as the manager (?) loudly explained to the hostess to take us to a table outside and tell the sever they "don't have the option to say no to taking a table outside" (sheesh, we'll just sit inside.). The hostess seated us at a table outside and said "Devin will be right with you"... I'm not sure if this Devin person exists, we never met. Luckily, about fifteen minutes later, a confused server walked out with a plate of food she thought was ours. This gave us an opportunity to tell her that we hadn't been served yet. After sorting out the mistaken food (presumably), she eventually returned and took our order. We had some mediocre drinks (not worth trying), and some below average soft pretzels with some questionable cream cheese dip, which we consumed with some silverware that showed up as we were finishing and no napkins.

This is one of my favorite places to take out of town guests to. It's cute, quaint and just one of those Nashville places you have to experience. I will continue to go but I have to say the last three times I have been my fried chicken has been dry and overcooked, like it had been sitting under the heat lamp to long.  I still love you Loveless so please start frying smaller batches of chicken so they don't sit to long! I would rather wait a little longer for my meal and have it fresh and just right! The sides and biscuits are right on point so I'm hoping I just went on a few bad "chicken" days :)
Pretty tasty but, a touristy type of place. Things are the way they are, kinda mass produced. A lot of down home vibe.

Came in for a late lunch and was told it was an hour and 20 min wait. Almost left but got sidetracked looking in the shop and we were actually seated much sooner. Biscuits and preserves were delicious and brought promptly. Food was amazing. Delicious fried green tomatoes. Everyone else had fried chicken and I had BBQ. I could only eat half of mine as it was a large portion with the sides. Delicious coconut cream and peach pie for dessert! Worth the detour!

Love this place! Menu, food,service, atmosphere and history make for a great meal and experience. Biscuits are awesome and the asst Jams are amazing!!!! Love places like this......they get it all right!!
My wife and I are both vegetarians so coming here I thought would have been a little difficult but I was wrong!!  So many options for everyone!!!! I've been twice and I'll definitely be back!!

So couldn't go to Nashville and not visit the infamous Loveless Café - even though it's about an hour and a half outta town but sooooo worth the drive! It's so much more than a restaurant - cute little shops, etc. which make it worth a visit. 

AND of course, the biscuits. Oh the biscuits.... these are hands down the BEST biscuits I've ever had in my life. Fluffy, light and buttery...they literally melt in your mouth. The rest of our breakfast was also really good although the biscuits are the real start here. They bring 'em to your table like bread so you'll get to try them if you eat here. :) It's also kind of cool to walk towards the restroom where there is a little window where you can see them making them. Yu can even buy the mix to bring home and try your hand at 'em too! 

Service was great and friendly. Prices are fair and parking is ample. Definitely recommend you pop by especially if you're a biscuit lover like myself. ;)

My wife lived in Nashville and introduced me to this place and it did not disappoint! We were immediately seated, greeted by our waitress and given warm, fresh biscuits!! The biscuits were THE BEST I've ever had!!! I was blown away by the service, friendliness, and high-quality food! This is a MUST while visiting Nashville!

Such a cute set up with the little shops surrounding the cafe. The wait was awhile but there was also a lot of people there as well. Very good food and service. I ordered the BBQ and eggs. I recommend it. The bisquits and jams was so delicious. Worth the stop.

One star because this review is not about the food or wine, but the venue itself.  The seating is awful! The chairs are the most uncomfortable seats I've ever sat in besides bleachers! I have a stiff neck from having to duck under the balcony railing because it was right at eye level. It was freezing, so if you go take a pillow to sit on and a blanket to wrap up in! Concert was fine!

We had a wonderful afternoon here today! We were seated right between the bandstand and an opening to the patio,  so enjoyed a lovely breeze while we ate. We sampled a flight of beers,  then my husband had the pork schnitzel and I had the wurst plate with jalapeno cheddar wurst and smoked bratwurst, sauerkraut and rye bread. The beers were good and the food was delicious, but the atmosphere was outstanding! We'll definitely be back!

AWESOME!  Although the wait was an hour- after the amazing meal we were all happy.   
Danielle was our server.  She made the meal as special as the biscuits.  Patiently explaining her recommendations-sharing cafe history & famous sightings.  The food and the experience were awesome!

I gave this place two stars for the following reasons.

I want to emphasize that the food tasted good. The pretzel was amazing. The server was somewhat irritated by the loud music and translated that frustration towards our party.

I feel that the prices are way out of line for the amount and quality that you receive. I do not understand why places like this cannot prepare authentic food. They always Americanize it in same strange way.

I will not return, simply based on the prices.

This the private response from the manager. I have changed my review from two stars to one.

Mark, we are sorry especially that your server conveyed her sense of irritation to you. That is unacceptable with a server. As for the prices, they are comparable to the region and given that we prepare everything from scratch and import all but one of our beers, they are the lowest we can get them. We try to keep them as low as possible.

We wanted to give this a try and we are so glad we did! Emily was fantastic! We sat at the bar and she was very busy but she moved right along with it. We are only here a few days but will be back at least once. It is so refreshing to see someone who loves their job and makes every customer feel welcome!

This was one of my favorite places I stopped at while in Nashville. Yes, the wait can be insanely long, but I promise it is so worth it. If you are tight on time, be sure to call ahead and see how busy it is. If you have to wait, there are cute little shops surrounding the cafe to kill some time. Those biscuits are SO GOOD! The staff is so friendly! They even sent us with water and biscuits to go to bring back to our hotel room. I was more than pleased with my experience. I'm heading to Nashville again soon and will be making a stop here again!

I was so looking forward to this meal but I'm terribly disappointed. It was average (or below) in every way. I don't believe the chicken was even brined!  So sad. We have better southern food in Minnesota.

Any restaurant that brings in Usingers sausage is solid in my book.

POSITIVE:  
+tasty sausage
+tasty schnitzel
+Good biers 
+I dig what looks to be like a locker room for beer steins.  
+traditional looking uniforms for the wait staff
+went at lunch.  Was happy to see the waitress point out the meterwurst as an option for 2 people to split for $10.  Guess they understand that they're in an outlet mall filled with cheap MFs like me


IN BETWEEN: 
-/+  spaetzle seemed a bit off.  I get that it's mostly flour and egg yolks, but these seemed closer to scrambled eggs.  Still buttery goodness though.

NEGATIVE:
-Waitress was attentive I guess, but she seemed like she hated her job and wanted to blow the building up.  Look, I'd hate my job too if I were still in food service, and I hated working at an outlet mall back in the day, but at least throw on a fake smile.
-Maybe I missed it on the menu, but how bout some veal as a choice for the schnitzel?

BOTTOM LINE:
Hope this place sticks around.  I'd like to come back next time I'm in town.  Hopefully when they've got some live music or during Oktoberfest

Our first plate of biscuits were cold and tasted old. It wasn't till our waiter brought us a plate of hot fresh biscuits did I discover why they are so talked about. I'm a Yankee living in the south so a lot of my critiques will come from that. My wife for the ham, the waiter smartly suggested to get the breakfast sampler bc the ham is salty, it was a good idea, the ham was way too salty for my taste. She had the hashbrown casserole as a side. I had fried chicken which was good. Sides were taste as well. Not the best meal of my life don't wait for hours like some do, go at an off time. Overall I'd recommend

We managed to get ticket for 2 of the 3 sold-out Jason Isbell shows here in December. We were really pumped, because I managed to get great seats on the first night (4 seats back from the stage). The wife is a huge fan, so she was incredibly happy about the seats and the show. 

Unfortunately, we happened to be seated next to a VIP investor in City Winery, who didn't happen to know dooku about the talent on the stage. Typical bloated businessmen with trophy wives (one of which was Googling Jason Isbell during the show and blurted out that he had "Played with the Drive By Truckers"). You know these kind of businessmen: hang out at cigar bars, eat at Mortons, and live in the Governors Club. Thankfully however, they realized that they didn't really care for the artist on the stage (other than the fact that someone told them how "great" Isbell is, and they had to see him for prestige reasons), so they left half-way through his set. Bonus for us, we ended up front row!

Onto the place itself!

1) Service. Our server was great! In fact, I don't think there is a bad server in the place. They manage to be unobtrusive yet attentive at the same time. They also manage to maneuver through the seating area without disrupting the show (the same can not be said of bloated businessmen!).

2) Venue. The venue is really classy, clean, has a great feel and even better sound. Given the tasteful use of recycled and new wood both inside and out, the backdrop for the stage is a bit corny (City Winery logo on plywood set against a gray Corian panel),  But who cares. You get a great show!

3) Food. This is where they need some help. We just had a few appetizers. Risotto balls and truffle fries. Neither was all that tasty. They weren't bad. They just lacked flavor. Maybe the entrees are better? But the prices aren't that bad. You'd hope they have some better stuff to go with the great wine options. Speaking of which...

4) Wine. Well, wine is their schtick, so let's talk about it. We tried a few of the "on-tap" wines. The Syrah was good. The Malbec is better. They sell by the glass, by the carafe or half-carafe. The prices aren't bad on these, UNTIL YOU SEE THE CHECK!!! This may only apply to the the house wines which are dispensed from barrels, but they charge you separately for the Liquor By The Drink (LBTD) tax, which is 15%. I'd like to say I KNEW if it only applied to tap wines, but our server (who was otherwise great) served us tap wine on our second night instead of the bottle wine I ordered. To do the math for you, if you order the $42 carafe of Malbec, you'll be paying $53 after 15% LBTD tax and another 9.25 % sales tax. ANYWHERE else in Nashville, brewers, servers and distillers include this tax into the price of a served drink. There's a tiny footnote on the back of the menu that mentions this tax. So, if you don't like surprises, be sure to ask your server if the tax applies to all beverages, or just barrel wine.

If I could sum it all up under pros and cons:

Pros: Great wine, great service, great venue, excellent staff all around, good prices on food.

Cons: Wine taxes are brutal, food needs a bit more flavor, valet parking when the show gets out looks to be a real CF. But I don't see a solution to that last issue.


I'll be back for sure. It's a great new place!
The food was good and wait was short.  The only thing overrated was the bisquits.  They were still good, they just didn't live up to the hype.  Definitely a Nashville must.

Really famous restaurant but I don't really think this could category in Nashville restaurant since it take 25 min drive to there. Food is good and fresh but kind of too salty especially the county ham. It is a nice place if you don't mind the drive and get some beyond average brunch.

My third time here and still the parking problem ruins the experience.  I don't feel safe parking anywhere but valet (it's a long walk to other lots) and don't mind paying for it.  However, last night I spent 20 mintues getting into valet and 45 minutes getting out.  Since there was a late show scheduled, the actual show, while magnificent,  was 75 mintues.  I spent almost as much time waiting for my car.

This is quickly becoming one of our very favorite restaurants in Nashville. The portions are gigantic. We have had really good service each time we went and they have a great bar with tons of beer choices. I love the beer  cheese soup and of course the Jager schnitzel is amazing. There is nothing that we have had here that was not good.

Beer and food were both excellent!! Holly was a great server. Was very knowledgeable on both beer and food. My wife, daughter and myself had a great experience. She was extremely kid friendly, taking pictures of us there. We will definitely be back!!
