I normally eat healthy and cook a lot, but when I travel, I want to try places that serve delicious food no matter how much the increased risk of stroke or heart attack it posed. So, of course I put those thoughts behind me with this restaurant and I don't regret my decision. Yup, the biscuits and preserves were dang delish. I had the sample dinner platter of fried chicken, catfish, and country ham while my friend had dinner platter consists of fried chicken, meatloaf, and pulled pork so that way we can taste all of them. We had sides of fried green tomatoes, cream corn, sweet potatoes, and grits. The chicken and green tomatoes were the best, the rest were mediocre. Service was fast. Quaint little place, enjoyed the atmosphere and seeing the adjacent shops while we waited.
If you are in Nashville, this is a must.  Best biscuits and homemade jams in the world bar none,

Where country ham and eggs are the norm, I found it to be very good but not exciting as expected. The biscuits are hot but not flakey nor tender, I would call them mediocre at best. This place is a solid breakfast or lunch venue not sure if I would take the trip out of Nashville to hit it again in the future.

This was our last breakfast of our trip in September 2016 & it was a great finale. It was a Sunday & we got there around 9, so we knew there would be a wait. This is more than just a restaurant, it's a destination. There are several cute little shops where you can get some preserves, meats, knick knacks & souvenirs. The time passes pretty quickly while you wander around. There are even cornhole boards & other games to pass the time. We waited around 45 minutes. 

We had a great waiter & I hate I can't remember his name. He greeted us immediately & pretty quickly, we had a giant bowl full of these amazing little biscuits that Loveless is famous for. The biscuits were great & a perfect size so you didn't feel bad eating a ton of them. The preserves were delicious. A couple of us ordered the biscuit sampler platter, which is your choice of 4 biscuits. You can choose between fried green tomato & pimento cheese, bacon, sausage, fried chicken, barbecue, country ham & steak. I had the chicken, barbecue, country ham & sausage. They were incredible. I don't always love country ham, but this was great. Not too salty or tough. I'm obsessed with the idea of barbecue &/ or fried chicken at breakfast, so I think those were my favorite. Our friends tried the bacon & said it was great too. One of the guys made their own omelet & the other had the barbecue omelet & both said they were delicious. I can't imagine going & not eating the iconic biscuits, so I will have to take their word for it. 

This place is amazing m, but come prepared for a wait. By the time we were being seated after our 45 minute wait, the wait was up to about an hour & a half. Have a snack before you come, be prepared to shop & hang out for a bit & then stuff yourself on an insane amount of delicious biscuits. It's worth it.

Visiting the Yelp Spring Break Nashville 2014, we went off the beaten path for this experience on a Saturday morning. Told that there would be a wait of over an hour, I had no qualms. Travelling all the way from Alexandria, VA, I had a hunch it would be worth it.

It has been a long time since my childhood, growing up in Florida, that I tasted truly authentic southern cooking. Ham steak, sausage patties with biscuits and gravy, grits...mmm.

The bonus is there are many things to keep you entertained while you wait. It's a village of family fun to entertain everyone. Antique and boutique shopping, complimentary sweet peach tea, quaint areas to bide your time while playing bean bag toss (AKA the "corn hole" game which made me blush). And Pumpkin Butter samples!

When we were finally seated, it was by the general manager, who enthusiastically made us feel welcome. The waitress was also a sweetie. Service is key here.

I can vouch for the:

Complimentary Biscuits and (3) Jelly Sampler
Ham Steak
Pimento Cheese
Biscuits and Gravy
Omelets
And Creamed Spinach

If I were to visit Nashville again, this would be a destination!

My besties aunt and uncle stopped and ate here and said we must go try it! And I'm so glad we did the server was awesome and the food was delicious! I got the fried catfish with greens and fries best catfish I've had in along time not fishy at all! Next time I go I'm definitely get their chicken tender they make them fresh I tried my friends and like everything else it was delicious I highly recommend this place!

I visited City Winery last night and was very impressed. We only had apps and wine (which were very good - risoto balls, anyone??), so I can't speak to the concert hall in the back, but we did get a tour and it is beautiful. Some folks have complained about parking; our tour guide mentioned that as soon as construction is complete they are going to add a parking lot with space for about 60 cars, to alleviate that "forced valet" option. Which I have to agree, was probably the worst part of the visit. We also got to see the private dining rooms which would be great for small events, and we saw the room where they will eventually make their own wine. Multiple outdoor seating areas have great views of downtown. I also heard a rumor about adding brunch to the menu sometime soon?? This place is a great addition to Nashville!

If you are visiting Nashville, you have to come to the Loveless. The food is fantastic (country grub) and the portions are large. Definitely get a side of biscuits. Coffee isn't the best but it's what you'd expect. It's a bit off of the beaten path which makes it all the more fun to visit. There's a shop where you can buy Loveless items and some other fun little knick knacks.

On a road trip down to the gulf coast with my sister and her husband we decided to stop by a place we had read lots of good things about, the Loveless Cafe. This place is absolutely fantastic, even with a 35 minute wait (this place is popular) there was plenty of things to make the time go by more quickly as their campus features multiple shops and corn hole games to entertain and distract. 

The food was amazing, I am not sure I've had better fried chicken, and the creamed corn and slow roasted green beans were delicious as well. A main feature of the Loveless Cafe is their biscuits which they make sure you get plenty of, served with various preserves, sorghum, and honey it was impossible to finish all of the food I had ordered as they kept bringing out hot plates of biscuits. Truly a taste of the south and a great stop for anyone going through the Nashville area.

This place is an experience.  It is located in what I can only describe as Middle of Nowhere, Tennessee.  It is around 30-40 minutes outside of Nashville, however as soon as you see the sign, you notice the huge parking lot full of cars and tons of people hanging around the restaurant.  The wait was pretty long, but Loveless does everything possible to keep people entertained.  There were guys playing corn hole, some kids drawing pictures on the ground with chalk, and a cute elderly couple enjoying the day in a set of rocking chairs.  There is also an array of small shops that you can check out.  Once we got in, the food was absolutely amazing. It lived up to the hype of every previous review.  I practically was rolled out of the place because my ambition got the best of me and I went for a platter including ham, meatloaf, fried chicken and a couple sides.  I probably shouldn't have eaten so many biscuits before the meal.

Amazing true southern food. Great priced and wonderfully kind wait staff. You can't visit Tennessee without stopping here. Prices are very reasonabke, portions are huge and best of all moonshine and chess pie are on the menu!

What I liked:
1. The biscuits- I wish I could give 100 biscuit stars.  Living in south I feel like somewhat of a biscuit connoisseur  at this point, and it's safe to say these are my favorite- extra buttery and only made better when loaded up with Loveless homemade jam.  And, get this, they are unlimited! 
2. The atmosphere- Yes, it's touristy and a little cheesy, but worth the visit if you're in town for the weekend.

What I didn't like:
1. Very long lines on the weekend.
2. Per above, tourist hell on the weekend.
3. The rest of the breakfast is average and very greasy.  

Overall Verdict: Go if you're in the mood for biscuits or doing a quick trip to Nashville.

My husband and I just got back from the Bavarian Bierhaus ~ and we were extremely pleased. It was a lively night with the lovely Lynn Marie playing her accordian. The food was excellent - the beer even better.

I've been wanting try Loveless since moving to Nashville back in December but have been deterred by the long typical long waits for one of Nashville's most famous breakfast foods location. However, I recently figured out that the secret is getting there before 9:30 on the weekends prior to the rest of the crowd. I had the Famous Loveless Full Country Ham platter and soon discovered it was famous for a reason! My girlfriend eyes lit up over the enormous portion as our server delivered my country ham to the table. The slice of ham was very thick and cooked very well, i preferred my country ham a little bit saltier and cured a tad bit longer but this is nothing I couldn't solve with a salt shaker. The biscuits and homemade jams were served to us before our meal came out and were the perfect fix to settle our premeal hunger. I will be ping back to try their cured bacon and smoked sausage in the near future.
Great food... well worth the wait would defiantly come back !!!! Great waiter Luke...drink was really good not strong Lynchburg lemonade with souvenir mini mason jar :)

Betsy was our bartender or as we call it our social chemical engineer in Vegas. Thank you for the great recommendations based on the beers we like. We weren't hungry and you recommended the beer cheese pretzel. The mustard that comes with it is not spicy not too sweet and perfect with fresh warm appetizer. The people are so nice in Nashville. We met a regular Anthony. Very welcoming to this city and friendly. Everyone knew the locals and good to feel like your at home. Great hospitality! Thank you
Great place!!! Such a cool atmosphere. The biscuits are to die for. The wait was over an hour at 9:30 AM, but it was worth the wait!

We went for brunch today and were not impressed. They messed up 3 out of 5 orders. I ordered a build your own biscuit with andouille sausage and the sausage tasted like greasy jimmy Dean breakfast sausage you buy at the grocery store. The server was not attentive. I will say the beignets were good and the wine taps are very cool, I would come back to try that but would not Return for brunch.

Let me just say, sure the wait is long if you go on the weekend because it's a popular spot.
The food though, was awesome!  Service was a little slow, but we were in no hurry and our waitress was great.  If you haven't read it by now, the biscuits are amazing!  The jams are amazing!
I got the chicken and waffles with a side of sausage gravy.  The chicken was juicy and crispy.  The waffle was great.
It was so good, we had to back and eat again!  I can't wait to come back to Nashville and go back to Loveless!!!!!
Best biscuits ever. Fried chicken would delicious. Grits and corn meal was Soo good. Would do the 3 hr wait again for this.

The is my favorite tourist attraction in Nashville. They are famous for their chicken and their biscuits. Unlike at most southern restaurants, the chicken is not dry. They have comfort food and a cozy atmosphere. They also have a store that sells their fresh preserves. All of their food is made from scratch. It is also historic, as it used to be a motel. The Loveless is great and I would definitely recommend coming here.

Ate Sunday brunch at City Winery with an online Groupon deal. It was worth every penny! We had 2 breakfast cocktails (delicious), French toast entree, and the CW breakfast. Everything was over par. Definitely recommend !

Great food, great wait service! 



My four star review is in relation to the snide remark made from one of the host personnel about "another bachelorette party". While I understand that some of these groups may make a bad name for themselves, my own group was there for a fine dining experience. I do apologize sir, but last time I checked my money was as green as everyone else's.
One of my all time favorite restaurants. I have not been here for a few years and it is good to know things haven't changed. Same great food!

We had a little bit of everything at our table: pancakes, chicken fried steak & eggs, and fried chicken, fried fish, and pulled pork with sides of turnip greens and Mac and cheese. Started off with a plate of biscuits. Wow. We may not eat again today. Everything was great. The waiter was very good.

The Best!  Just moved here and have already been there 3 time.  Chicken, gizzards, livers are outstanding, sides are homemade and the biscuits are world famous! 
Staff is super friendly (say 'hi' to Susan!) and attentive AND it's reasonably priced!

I have to say that everything was fantastic from the fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and mac and cheese that my girlfriend ordered to the chocolate chip and pecan pancakes that i ordered. The sweet tea was delicious, the service was quick and polite. and the prices were fantastic. I really enjoyed the building it was located in as it complimented the southern cooking that they provided. It had a lot of nice boutique shops on property but did not visit them due to time restrictions. The only negative is they used fans to cool the dining area which was near the kitchen sot it was very hot. I wish they had some air conditioning. Overall i would return there if I am in town again cause the food and service was great.

What's left to say about the Loveless Cafe that hasn't been said already? A staple of the area and an absolute must visit every time I'm in the are. Had the smoked turkey with cranberry BBQ sauce and a side of hashbrown casserole and fried green tomatoes. All were excellent. And still the absolute best homemade jams I've ever tasted (try mixing peach and strawberry.) The wait sucks, and I don't blame anyone for skipping a second-trip because of it, but there's enough to stay busy in the area if you're with friends or family.

My wife had an early dinner at the Bavarian Bierhaus. We both had the pork shank and it was over cooked, in our opinion. The outside was very crispy. The meat did fall off the bone, but it was pretty dried out. Hence, it was very chewy. We order some dumpling as well and they were OK, not great. The red cabbage was very good. I was disappointed to learn they didn't have any dark beers available, per our waitress. The place is located in a mall with some outdoor seating. In general, it has the feeling of a cha

Very nice place! Great choice of German beers! Great atmosphere too! The food was good. I had the schnitzel n dumpling which was great. My boyfriend had the pork shank. Which was awesome! Definitely need to be super hungry in order to eat that! It was huge! Definitely a must try if in the area.

We were visiting Nashville and had read about this place, so made the drive before heading home. SO glad we did.

The biscuits themselves are out of this world, warm, fluffy, and straight from the oven. Served with a couple of housemade jams. YUM.

I ordered Loveless' famous salt-baked ham with red eye gravy, cheese grits, and two eggs. And several glasses of sweet tea! The sweet tea was so good, we went to the shop afterwards and bought a gallon to take home with us!

I already want to go back and visit for the biscuits alone.

Insanely popular and worth the trip 
BUT
The wait can be likewise insane (we waited 2 hours).  My suggestion: Wake up, eat breakfast, then send one person to put your name in.  If the wait's a half hour, join them.  If it's not, judge appropriately.  We were told 90 minutes and it took over 2 hours.  TAKE THIS INTO CONSIDERATION IF YOU ARE TAKING KIDS.  There are some distractions there, but not 2 hours worth.
The food is fantastic, but if you're overly hungry from waiting to have your first meal there, it clouds your enjoyment.
I had the biscuits and t he biscuit sandwich platter and just about licked the plate.

Time goes fast while waiting for a table here.  We waited 45min and it was entirely worth it.  Free coffee in the gift shop, free tea and lemonade by the artist studio.  Chairs on the porch to enjoy the weather and touristy yet safe family atmosphere
Incredible fried chicken, Mac and cheese is nice and cheesy.  Very fast and friendly service.  Secret biscuit recipe biscuits are wonderful!  Our food got to our table in amazing time.  Our server Gretchen, offered her suggestions and answered all our questions with genuine care.   
The out buildings offer a market, a gift shop for kids, a few artist studios and some activities for kids i. e. blowing bubbles, side walk chalk, bean bag throw.
Definitely worth a visit!!!
Amazing atmosphere and pretty good food- check out the Reuben rolls which were great but really tasty.

Southern hospitality at its finest! Everyone we ran into here was so sweet and helpful. The food was great. You have to try the cheesy hash browns had the meatloaf and turkey breast. Both were excellent! We were sat right away and our food came our quickly.  We played corn hole after dinner! It was perfect. A must in Nashville.

Just as good as I had dreamed it would be. We went on a Monday which was a holiday and waited about an hour but it was worth it! Biscuits and jams are incredible, wonderful ham and pulled pork, amazing side dishes and incredible service. We had Jessica waiting on us and she was just lovely! Thanks Loveless Cafe!
Food was alright, service was awful. Stay away from the lemon aioli, tastes like lemon curd. Also my friend had the burger and it was SUPER dry.

Food was great - no complaints! The only thing that soured our trip to Loveless was the hostess "Brooke".  Totally unfriendly and a really poor first impression of the restaurant. Watched her interactions with other guests and it was the same. Rude and unwelcoming. They could so much better! 
Enjoyed the food though! Would definitely recommend.

I had to go w 3. Just bc your name is famous doesn't mean you can give slow and almost snail paced service. The wait was 25 minutes but once seated the wait was an hour. Sitting here w an empty glass and haven't seen server since he first came to take order.
Excellent food and great service!  We will defiantly be back for the fried chicken and homemade biscuits!

I have been 100% satisfied from the first visit to the last!  One time an order didn't  come out correct. Hey it happens, I mentioned it to the staff and they went above and beyond what would have made me happy. 
Beers are HUGE.. and tasty, wait staff is knowledgeable, chief is worth his salt and management are on top of things. A winning combination!

Loveless Cafe is a terrific country cafe with good food and lots of interesting memorabliia. Service was also excellent.  I had barely opened my newspaper when my omelet and biscuits were delivered.  I have been here 4 or 5 times and the food has always been great.  One note, there can be a long line on weekends as it is a popular place.
My wife had the turkey breast with cranberry barbq sauce and I had the smoked pork chops, both were excellent. Best turnip greens I've ever eaten. Trust the staff they know what's good!

I have been to the Loveless Cafe quite a few times, and it never disappoints. This time, I took a few friends with me that wanted to experience some southern breakfast foods and they fell in love! The wait staff was wonderful, the food was great, and the mimosas topped it all off. If you're showing someone around Nashville, don't miss out on this awesome place.
This is a wonderfully unique restraunt!Our server whose name was Madison was friendly,and fast with our food and seemed to really love her job!the atmosphere and food is exceptional!

This place is a great stop food was amazing service is great everyone was friendly it's always packed with people we were lucky to only have a 30 minute wait . Our table ordered fried pork. Hops fried chicken kids cheese burger and kids chicken strips every thing tasted great the sides were wonderful and there biscuits are some of the best I have had and always served hot ... If your going through Nashville stop in they have shops you can walk through while you wait or you can sit on the front porch

After a year of living in Nashville (and 5 minutes away) I finally decided to dine at the Loveless Cafe. 

While I had a positive experience at Loveless please be prepared to wait at least 40 minutes. I've attempted to dine here 3 times but finally pushed my impatient-ness aside. While waiting for our table we perused the gift shops and sat on the property's front porch. I was literally taken back to being a kid visiting my grandma's house and various other small towns in the deep south. Yes, my friends if you dig Southern charm this is your place!

After much anticipation we finally got in and promptly order sweet teas which were perfect. The superstar of Loveless is supposed to be biscuits however I found them just good not great. But you still have to give them props considering how many they make from scratch everyday. The homemade jams: apricot, blackberry, and strawberry are some of the best I've had and definitely elevated the biscuits.

My friend and I both ordered the fried pork chops. I ended up getting the home fries and she got the hashbrown casserole. I wasn't a fan of the home fries, it tasted like the potatoes you got in grade school but the hashbrown casserole, my God was so good! I was totally envious of my friend. Portions of meat were massive, there's no way you'll be able to finish it all. All in all very tasty.

Looking around the rest of the joint, the other food looked so delicious. I definitely would love to come back and try it all. Waitress was super friendly but was scarce due to the place being packed so I can't be too upset about that.

Great restaurant if you're craving true old school Southern fare but come hungry!

I recently went to Nashville for business purposes and was very eager to go to the Loveless Cafe after seeing them on the Food Network.  The service was excellent! The wait staff was friendly and made us feel warm and fuzzy.  The biscuits are definatley to die for! 

I ended up ordering the sample platter and was unfortunately dissapointed.  The fried chicken lacked adequate seasoning in addition to the fact that the wings were extremely small.  The pulled pork was blah. The catfish was pretty good though.

Overall it was okay, but I probably wouldn't go back.

First, the biscuits are made from scratch and come with delicious jams- and they just kept coming.  I was pretty full by the time my breakfast arrived.  Others in our party were  equally impressed with their lunch meals.  

Everything was wonderful and our server, Kramer, was excellent.  Highly recommend the Loveless Cafe!

I had a friend visiting from KC, and we both love live music, so we got VIP tickets to City Winery last night.  Wonderful venue, great music, very entertaining, but then there was the service....... We were sitting at our table for over 20 minutes before we were approached by our waiter.  And that was the one and only time he came to our table.  My friend and I had to track him down to get service the rest of the evening.  And the venue was not sold out, actually is wasn't crowded at all.  When we finished with dinner, we had to track him down to get coffee and dessert only to be told the kitchen had closed.  Bigtime thumbs down on service.  Won't be going back any time soon.

If you need carbs, this is your place. 
I always end up eating the country fried steak for a few days because the portion is just huge. The wait is going to be long and make a holiday reservation for a large party. Parking is rather plentiful and there are places to wander while you wait. The blackberry jam is... well my jam and the biscuits... oh the biscuits.

Bavarian Biernope...

I had such high hopes for visiting this place. I had reviewed the menu before going and hoped they had even a little of the good German taste I grew up on with the German Sausage Festivals with the German Communities back home.  Sadly, I was seriously disappointed.

The interior of the establishment is ok for a German/Bavarian Beer Hall. It is a bit more modern than the old world style I would expect from the exterior theming and the costuming of the staff, but it is light and comfortable for the most part.  The benches are a bit narrow, but that is ok.  The menus are straight forward and easy to order from, the selections fairly simple and not a lot to it. It's about what one would expect, and a one page menu does well here.

To start, my friend and I ordered a giant pretzel with beer cheese.  The pretzel was indeed massive and more than enough for two hungry folks. The cheese however was lackluster, but the mustard that came with it was awesome. Kind of sweet, and fantastic with the good and soft pretzel.

My friend ordered the Kasespatzel.  She said it was a safe choice and was ok.  She ate about half of it and got the rest to go.  She also ordered the beer cheese soup and also said it was good.  Her favorite dish however was the potato salad.

I ordered the Bierhaus Wursteller.  I won't ever do that again.  I had high hopes and we both wanted to try the various sausages, plus the sides sounded good.  We were wrong.  We both tried all of the sides and the sausages and agree... the sides, all of them, were bland and almost flavorless.  The potato dumpling and bread dumpling were both cold and looked to have been scooped with an ice cream scoop. The potato dumpling was almost gelatinous in texture and congealed.  The red cabbage was bland, and the sauerkraut was terrible. A good sauerkraut is strong and bold... this was the complete opposite and I was afraid I was eating coleslaw instead.  Then there was what was passed off as sausages.  While they weren't so terrible as to inedible, I have honestly, no joking around, had better sausage from Jimmy Dean and cooked in the microwave.  There is no way one could say this was anywhere near authentic.  I know it was at least cooked in a grill since two of them were heavily charred almost to the point of burnt, but the taste was nowhere near my expectations or hopes.  For the most expensive dish on the menu... epic fail.

We both ordered desserts hoping they would be the highlight of the meal.  To that end my friend ordered the Pretzel Pudding and I got the Strawberry Tort.  She indicated the Pretzel Pudding was good.  The Tort meringue was entirely too sweet and too hard. Though the strawberries were delicious.

If, and that is a strong if, I ever come back, I am doing nothing but a beer flight or two and praying the beer is better than the food.  After spending almost $100 this evening for dinner, I feel we'd have gotten far better food from McDonalds, and I freaking hate McDonalds.  I'll give it two stars being generous because the staff was nice and courteous, but the food was terrible.

This is our second visit to The Loveless.  The food is great, but the service is even better!  The people here are genuine, kind, and actually care about your dining experience.  The sweet tea glasses were always full and the hot fresh biscuits and jam kept coming throughout the meal!

The bbq pork was delicious. The chicken salad sandwich was too according to the Mrs.  Our server, Barbara, made us feel like we were old friends and every employee we passed on the way out sincerely thanked us for our patronage.  It's wonderful when everyone you meet understands the value of excellent customer service.

I really loved this place - it was my first time at a City Winery! I'm a music teacher and love attending live concerts but not so much the types where I have to stand the whole time, or deal with screaming crowds, jumping up and down to get a glimpse of the performed. PLUS - I love wine! 

This was the perfect setting for me: delicious wine, cheese boards and flatbreads, and an intimate concert. We saw Josh Kelley, who I was obsessed with in college, so it was a nostalgic night for me. Great venue and inexpensive. I love that they have a decent wine list, too. I wasn't a fan of their own wines, but opted for a much nicer bottle that was totally worth it.

I'll hit a couple of highlights and two lowlights.  First, they serve great southern food and you'll leave full! Lunch/dinner food is what they're best at.  Breakfast isn't anything special as you can get the same thing most places and for a little less cost.  Breakfast is not worth waiting for if there is a line.  We've been going there for about 13-14 years or so and have always enjoyed our food.  They used to can their own jams on site and jars were about $7.  Not cheap but as an occasional thing it was okay.  However, they now outsource their jams and they don't taste nearly as good.  Plus you're paying over $10 for a jar - OUTRAGEOUS!  Wait times are terrible. Rarely will you go without having to wait, maybe later in the evening.  We've had wait times over 2 hours. Because of this we just go a couple times a year.  I've always wanted to try their watermelon glazed ribs, but it's a specialty item they serve only on Wednesdays (maybe Thursdays but I can't remember).  We've been three times on those days but every time they've run out before we got there.  Overall they have really good lunch and dinner fare, great hashbrown casserole, giant portions of chicken tenders, yummy fried green tomatoes......

Strong coffee, cheese grits (why don't more people talk about these? I LOVE good grits, and these are some GOOD cheese grits!), hashbrown casserole, ham, biscuits, eggs and zero wait - a really great way to start a Southern morning. Clearly the trick is to get to Loveless Cafe early on a weekday morning. We ate beyond our fill and were ready to hit the road for 8 hours without another food stop. So very glad Yelp led us to this place.

We arrived at 7:15 on a Tuesday morning. It was like a ghost town. My 4 year old nephew didn't understand why I was so shocked to not see anyone there. We were seated right away as we were the first ones there. It took a while to order, even saw an employee get their meal before we ordered. 

We got the kids pancakes and the sausage, egg, and cheese sandwich. Of course we also got biscuits. The kiddo loved his pancakes which were way too big for a toddler. He barely put a dent in one pancake. My sandwich was odd. The eggs were served on top of the sandwich of sausage and melted cheese. I had a hard time prying the bread open to get the eggs on. The server said that's always how it's served. I've never seen that anywhere. 

The service was slow. This was evidenced by the next diners coming in, grabbing menus, and seating themselves. 

It's not a place I choose to go, but would rather stay local.

After visiting the Hofbrau Haus in Vegas, I was leery, but the food is delish! Great place! Loved the Jaegerschnitzel. The mustard served with the pretzel is fabulous. Didn't want to stop eating. Oh yeah, and there's German Bier! Very happy!

We decided to try Loveless as it is a huge tourist attraction in Nashville.  It is about a 30 minute drive from downtown Nashville, but the view is pretty.  Loveless is quite the complex- the restaurant, gift shop, shipping office and barn for events.  We went on a Monday morning and the wait was about 30 minutes.  The service was great, but I found the food less than exciting.  I had a garden omelet, and the mushrooms were canned and the veggies chopped very small.  The biscuits were more greasy than dry and crumbly.  I was glad to check out a major tourist stop, but I would not go back.

Biscuits and jam. Enough said. 

Completely amazing. Such a fun thing to do in Nashville and always worth the wait!

The quality and quantity of reviews speak for themselves. There's nothing more I can add without being repetitive.

Some of the best scratch cooking I've come across on my travels.

The venue is amazing, but the food and wine recommendations (keyword: recommendations) was not so great. 2 appetizers, 2 glasses of wine and we were out for no less than $60. Ouch. 

Will go back for music, but not for food or wine.

Jam/jellies are amazing and some of the best parts of the meal. You can buy jars if them and some good jerky in the store on the property. Food's normally great, but if the wait seems too long, might want to try a slower time, since a longer wait time means they're getting slammed, and the fried chicken can seem a little rushed and the kitchen overwhelmed/backed up because of large parties with large orders. A close drive from the local cemetery, which can cause rushes, as good southern food like they serve at the loveless is often called comfort food (which I agree with!).

Well.......


Not sure how long they will last with the restaurant concept.
Place isn't busy..
Waiters are hungry.
Interrupt conversation when they come to the table.

Didn't have to use the valet as there is plenty of self parking.
Food.. I'd say 3.5 stars.
BUT.. their music venue seems to be strong.

I did not partake in a music venue.  Instead, friend and I went to dinner and 
were not swept up with any excitement over our food.

Doubt we'll eat here again.
Would like to check out some entertainment, some time.
The charcuterie board was one of the worst and the burger not only was a hockey puck but came with extra calcium added bone fragments. The bun easily classifies as freeze dried for astronauts.

Stopped at the Loveless Cafe on our way from Lexington, KY to Dallas, TX. The cafe was warm and welcoming with good home cooking and friendly service. We loved the complimentary fresh baked biscuits with homemade jams. The bacon burger with pimento cheese, the catfish fried in cornmeal batter and the hash brown casserole were all delicious. Although the soup and fried okra were served less warm than we preferred, our server (Mark) was delightful and attentive which made it easy to overlook a minor temperature issue that was not a deal breaker.

The food is really great! The truffle fries, risotto balls, hummus and tacos were all bomb.com! Can't really go wrong here and the bartenders are super attentive. Love the atmosphere and would like to go back for some live music!
Legit Southern sides and the best biscuits and homemade jam. Friendly service. Great experience every time!

This is one of our faves to eat at since moving to Nashville. Food is tasty. Service is always good. Being a local we can go at less busier times unless we want the "to die for" brisket which is only on Sunday's so we have to wait 2hrs with the tourists. But if you try it, you'll understand why we wait. Our last visit though was disappointing. The fabulous biscuits weren't so fabulous. They had a "medicine" sort of taste to them. Texture was off too. I asked the waiter if they changed the recipe and he said no. It's almost like she added too much water or something. I'm hoping that was just an off day biscuit wise. My only complaint is pricing is high, and call ahead seating all hours would be nice. We will ofcourse be back soon. Can't be without that incredible hash brown casserole. Try the brisket people! YUM!

What a neat environment! The food was fantastic but I was more impressed with the grounds. The Loveless seems to be an old multi-building motel and they've turned it into a down-home restaurant with neat little shops and games.

The small biscuits beat everything else to your table and, if I were a cheap-o, I could see myself just eating those!  Not sure which made them taste better: the biscuit recipe or the jams that they come with.  Amaze-balls!

Loveless is definitely not a "touristy  trap". Yes, it has the gift shops and all of that but the cafe...the cafe was probably the best breakfast I've ever had. My boyfriend and I frequent breakfast joints at home (Chicago) as well as where ever we travel. The breakfast at Loveless was awesome. The biscuits... warm, fluffy, tasty. The jams/preserves made the biscuits even better. I had the Southern omelette- and I'm pretty sure it put all other omelettes to shame. My boyfriend had the waffles with sausage...and the sausage isn't the typical bfast links, but legit patties of delish that were thrown on the grill. 

But honestly, the best part of the visit was our server- Luke. He was fun, friendly, just the right amount of chatty. Coming from Chicago, we aren't used to servers being so awesome.

Being from the "north," biscuits aren't a go-to dinner or even breakfast staple, but they should be. Oh my goodness, these quick-bread kings were probably loaded with saturated fat and lard but they were some of the most delicious pieces of bread I have EVER tried in my life. And the jellies and preserves they were paired with made them even more amazing. 

What goes best with lard-based biscuits? Fried food, of course! I even took my fried quota to the extreme for this meal because I ordered fried catfish AND fried green tomatoes. Both to die for! I washed it all down with a southern-style lemonade cocktail with nothing other than moonshine. Even if it were brewed in a bathtub it was still very, very yummy! I applaud you because I didn't taste a single trace of soap. 

The one question I have is how can food made with so much love be made by a restaurant named "Loveless"?  Even though you probably caused me to gain two inches on my waist and three on my hips with your delicious fried Southern cuisine, I have nothing but love for you!!

Have you ever wondered who would drive 30 minutes out of their way for a delicious homemade biscuit covered in homemade jam? Hi- that's me. 

My sister and I were visiting Nashville and the last time I was in the city was about 2008... I had Loveless for a rehearsal dinner. I can't say that marriage lasted terribly long, but the memories of those freshly baked biscuits and homemade jams held a place in my heart. So we had a little bit of time on our last day so we drove about 20-25 minutes south to Loveless Cafe.

The drive is beautiful. So don't let that detour you. We came from the Vanderbilt area, and truthfully it was so pretty and green, and we had Taylor Swift in the background playing... time flew. But Loveless is perched on the side of the old highway and it is an old side of the road motel that now serves as a restaurant and gift shop area. We had called ahead, so our biscuits were ready on the spot. A dozen biscuits were $6. Steal. 

After purchasing those delicious goodies we lusted after plates of comfort food and then made our way to the gift shop. They have all things southern comfort. Candles, jams, house decor, sauces, tea... and Bacon. A personal weakness of mine. That specific day, they were buy 2 get 1 free- so for the low cost of $24 I got 3 slabs of thick cut flavored bacon (peppered, jalapeno and cajun). My mind was thinking about bacon biscuit sandwiches, and bacon breakfasts, and marrying the love of my life and being Mrs. Bacon. I couldn't say no.. 

So I left with bacon and biscuits, a picture in front of the old sign, and a sweet tea to go. It is truly a southern experience and I would advise anyone to go if they want to sit outside on a pretty day or feel full to the max. It looked like there was a wait and it was about 2 oclock.. but again, people seem to wait a lot in Nashville. I can't say I tried any more of the food, but it looked and smelled fantastic. I would go back -again- and probably get more biscuits, and jam. They are the bomb.

This place is like heading home and being served food by your mother after years of travel. Warm. Welcoming. Wholesome. We had to wait a couple minutes to be seated. Almost immediately, we were met with the famous biscuits, which were just as delicious as the articles suggest. I ordered a barbecue pork sandwich with a side of okra. The okra went fast. The sandwich was delicious and tender. Our server was incredibly attentive and kind. 

I'm don't live in TN, but absolutely imagine myself going out of my way in the future to come back. Is this the best food I've had in my life? Probably not. But the combination of the atmosphere and hearty food create such a content aura, it's hard not to give this place 5 stars.
Rissoto balls are excellent. Scallops are fantastic. Great place to be able to have good conversation due to the dining area being small and quaint.

The Loveless Cafe is amazing!!  For a number of years now, every time we drive anywhere close to Loveless, it is our dining spot!!  The quality of the food (texture, flavor, variety, etc.) would be hard to beat - and the menu (including breakfast all day!) is filled with a wide variety of some of the best down-home 'Southern cooking' to be found except at yo Mama's table!!  The Loveless is famous for their biscuits, and a plate of these, along with delicious jams, is brought to the table soon after customers are seated.  The meals are not inexpensive (but not very expensive, either), but the helpings are HUGE!!  Very easily, two could share one meal and be quite full.  Actually, this might be a good recommendation, for this is the only way to have any room for some of their delicious dessert items!!  The only 'detraction' for the Loveless Cafe is that this place is so popular that there usually is a wait (up to an hours) for a table, but that is a great compliment on what they provide their customers!!  Try to arrive between 2:00-4:00, and you usually can be seated immediately.  Oh, yes - spend some time checking out the very numerous autographed photos of celebrities who have dined at the Loveless!!  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!!

On our last day in Nashville we rented a car (must have since Loveless is about 25 min from downtown).  When we got to the cafe, I was expecting a wait but not a 1 hour and 45 minute wait.  Usually I do not wait at any restaurant more than an hour but since we could drive around we left our name.  When we came back we got our table and we are glad we ate at Loveless.  Our waiter was really good.  First he brought a plate full of biscuits and jams which are amazing.  He recommended the blue plates special which every Saturday is a BBQ chicken and also the fried chicken for which Loveless is famous for.  Both were really really good.

For a vegetarian there are very limited options. I ordered the dumplings and I didn't love it. I didn't eat the dumplings which are like squishy undercooked bread.. to be fair I have never had this kind of food before so I don't know if this is the way it's does to taste. The service was good and the environment. Is fun. I did like the sauce the dumplings came in though.

Kim was an amazing waitress for a party of 20! She explained the menu amazingly. She split carafs of wine between 5 people.we had a pretty delicious margherita pizza and asparagus. The shining star of the dinner (besides kim) was the brussel sprouts. I didn't even know I liked brussel sprouts because they smell like farts but these were glazed with balsamic vinagarette and cooked to perfection.  Prices were a little steep but I would suggest City Winery to Nashville visitors and locals.

Beware. This place has got have have the worst service ever. We were there for a concert and literally had to wave our waitress down every time we wanted something. She would just ignore the tables until you stood up and stopped her. Then she would bring incorrect orders to the table and act like it was our fault. Management didn't seem to think this was a problem.  We have been there 3 times and each time the service got worse.  Three strikes. We're done!

As many years back as I can remember, I have been frequenting the Loveless Café as I have travelled on I 40 east to Nashville TN and sometimes Charlotte NC. Famous for deceased employee Carol Fay's secret biscuit recipe, this place has tripled in size through the years. Biscuits, preserves, and gravy are still good as ever. The breakfast eggs cooked perfectly. The salt pork ham perfectly aged and prepared. The Southern grits extra creamy and also cooked to perfection. But the star of our breakfast table was the tender, crispy Southern Fried chicken half. Oh my goodness, what a wonderful place! Perfect service and plenty of space with the friendliest employees you'll ever meet.
Love Loveless, wish I could visit there more often, but alas my wife doesn't like the wait.

My oh my! This place is worth making a trip to. Be prepared for a wait, but it's so worth it! I couldn't decide what I wanted so I got the Sample Platter and chose, Fried Chicken, Catfish and BBQ Shredded Pork with a side of green beans and macaroni and cheese. The biscuits are also perfection! I washed it down with an Apple Pie Sunshine.....amazing!

The food was very good. We were there for breakfast The biscuits  are heavenly with the jam. The prices are a little  on the high side, but there  they do serve large portions. There is usually  a long wait, but the property has several  gift shops  to go thru while waiting.

Please... it is so commercialized and far from authentic that whatever it's roots were are long lost.  Better off finding a little diner with big fluffy biscuits and great eggs than waiting an hour and a half for mediocre food and a big bill.  If you want the branded stuff they sell you can find it in downtown Nashville all over the place.

The beer selection was good. I liked being able to order 1L of beer like you're able to in bavaria. The food was a 5 out of 10.  My weisswurst was decent though it didn't taste like they had actually made the sausage itself and the gravy on my potatoes tasted just like the kind you get out of a jar at the grocery. The potatoes themselves tasted a bit like chemicals...fake garlic perhaps? My husband's meal was better. So you could find something good there if you were willing to endures a few misses first. I would go back to drink but not to eat. Our server was friendly and the atmosphere was fun.

OK.....drove way out of our way to eat here, and then before we left we just HAD to go back....

The biscuits, well, after eating there's no one else tasted anywhere near as good....with butter, with jams and preserves, and then, oh yeah, with their incredibly delicious fried chicken.

The chicken.....well it is do good it leaves you wondering if its some special breed raised just for them.....

My advice to anyone going within 100 miles if Nashville.... Find a way to end up here for both breakfast and then lunch...if you have to drive into Nashville and do stuff...whatever!!!
YUM. To everything. Just be prepared for a really long wait unless you go at an off time of day.

Yep. It's as good as everyone says. I don't think I can even add to the information. 
Awesome biscuits, jam, chix fried steak, veggies. Friendly folks. Worth a trip.
It's kitschy. The pretzels are good. The bartender hates her life on mug night and lets it show. Meh. Overpriced and attracts the tourists, I won't be back.
Place is overrated and lame. 2hr plus waiting and the food looks average.

This Winery is incredible. They have live shows 5-6 times per week and it's all played in a sit down for dinner and wine setting. I was a little bit intimidated walking in at first because some of the tables are shared tables, but the hubs and I were able to grab a side table! They have a nice selection of food  and wine  for everyone. 

I would definitely recommend the Nutella pizza for dessert! IT HAS HOMEMADE MARSHMALLOWS ON IT THAT MELT INTO THE CHOCOLATE. Then after that you cry happy tears! Then you listen to fun music...and then cry a TINY bit more because you remember how incredible those homemade marshmallows were on top of the pizza.

AMAZING biscuits! We decided to stop here due to the great reviews and it did not disappoint. As we checked in we were told it would be an hour and 15 minute wait for two but we were seated within 45. In the meantime there are little shops to pick up some souvenirs and browse to kill time. The biscuits were awesome along with the peach jam. Our waitress Virginia was also very kind and provided the BEST service we have ever received. Must try if you are ever looking to explore Nashville.

Have you ever fallen in love? Felt your heart race, and excitement course through you, and all you can think about is your next encounter with the object of your affections?

That is how I will describe the truffle fries at City Winery.

I will be honest, that I can only speak to the truffle fries and wine, but, on the basis of truffle fries alone, I am granting this place four stars. They are perfectly cooked wedges of potato, seasoned with truffle, parmesan, and prosciutto; they are a culinary romance of the tongue, so much so that, after splitting an order with a friend, we decided to promptly order a second order. Following that, we started plotting how we could get the waiters to bring us additional free orders.

And therein lies the problem. City Winery is somewhat like a beautiful gold-digger, tempting you and asking for everything you have, all at the same time. It is so pricey that you (at least if you make a teacher's salary) are left wanting more. More free parking spaces (valet is $5), more alcohol (the cheapest wine glass was, I believe, $8), and more food (one order of fries was $8). The vibe is cool, the servers are great, and the truffle fries are absolutely worth the trip; however, don't come here for a quick and cheap rendezvous.

I love it! Hands down! The only con; it's a good drive outside of the Nashville city limit and there is a wait. I had breakfast alone and the wait was about an hour and 30 minutes.  Will return regardless

Service was fabulous after our 35min wait (which is not too bad considering it was going to be nearly 2 hrs last weekend!).  The food was standard southern classics like fresh biscuits (ok - but the jam was great!), fried catfish (just ok - good hash brown casserole) and bbq (didn't try it).  The food was good but didn't think it was anything special and not worth the 30 min drive out of Nashville or the wait.

Wait!! I just had a slice of their coconut cream pie that we took home. The whipped cream is light and not too sweet. The custard is creamy and the roasted coconut flavour is just right. I'm going to grab another slice right now!

Went there for the Walter trout concert and he put on an incredible show.  Our waitress, Kimberly, was very sweet and her service was spot on.  The apps menu could use a bit of work.  We ordered a flatbread and it really was not happening in the flavor department. The crust was nice but the toppings were bland.  We ordered one desert too, the banana  tiramisu.  That was not very good either.  We left it on the plate.  We did not have dinner there so I can't comment.  The City Winery is well appointed, very nice bar and restaurant area and the show seating is very nice also.  Every employee we encountered was polite and friendly.  Parking is a breeze with the valet and we enjoyed our evening very much.

Came here for dinner. The line is long (but they give you a buzzer thing that tells you when you are next). There are gift stores around and cornhole which help pass the time.

Food: biscuits, fried chicken, catfish, ham, pulled pork, pecan pie. Bad: pecan pie, just pass on the desserts. Amazing: biscuits. The outside is almost crunchy and the inside is so fluffy, but not flakey. The fried chicken was really good (not hot chicken).  Also was a huge fan of the catfish. Looks like it was almost deepfried and had a lot of dry rub around it. The ham was pretty salty, but that's just cured ham. I didn't think it was that special. Overall, my favorite meal at Nashville. Some really good sides as well.

Fantastic service, and the food is AMAZING.  People always mention various things they've had, but if you're not there for breakfast you're not doing it right.

Do NOT go through N'ville without stopping here.

Stopped in for breakfast before we left Nashville. Nice decor and cool history on the place. Their biscuits were SO GOOD and their homemade preserves were awesome. I had the biscuit sampler with fried green tomato (so good but I passed on the heave pimento cheese), fried chicken (so good), bbq (pretty good), and sausage for my son. Hubby ordered breakfast sampler, he really liked it too.

The food definitely stuck with you.  We were so full from all that food we skipped lunch.

I wouldn't say that this place necessarily lives up to its hype. But it's still a lovely place to eat. The biscuits are def overrated. The fried chicken is good but overdone. However the catfish and hash brown casserole are out of the park good! That's what I would recommend from here. They're delicious and the staff is friendly. The place is just lovely if u sit or wait outside on a nice day. There is a country market belonging to it as well right next door that u can buy groceries from and a farm behind it. It's just a pretty neat place.

We've been on the road and was looking for some authentic southern comfort food that didn't taste like it was sitting in the deep fryer for the last month...this met every single expectation! Shout out to our waiter Owen who helped us make decisions when we couldn't choose what to eat and had a true passion for the food. It was well worth the 45 minute wait.

Once upon a time - oh, 30, 40 years ago - Loveless was a secret place I took people to when I wanted them to get a taste of the "real southern cuisine." Unfortunately, no longer. It used to be terrific, homey, everything from scratch.
It may be all from scratch now, but it's really become nothing more than a tourist joint. If you haven't ever had good fried chicken, you might think this was acceptable, but you'd do better at a gas stop Krispy Krunchy. 
If you want the real deal, ask around for old-fashioned meat & threes. Sorry to be so brief but there's not much more to say except that it's also quite expensive given what you get - poor service, low quality. If you want really great southern cooking, take the time to visit Lynchburg and go to Miss Mary Bobo's, former home of Jack Daniels. Just make sure to reserve in advance.

Had our team dinner here and it was a fun experience.  The German two person band was good and very entertaining.  They played throughout our dinner with two short breaks during the night.  We shared pretzel appetizers and what looked like egg rolls, but being German, I am sure it was called something else.  Their beer selection was good and the service was excellent.  I ordered the jagerschnitzel which came with mushroom gravy.  It was pretty good, but I prefer more flavor in my food, so German food tends to be on the bland side.  We all shared the dessert which were also tasty.  I would recommend this restaurant for good German food.
Great food. Great wine (both red and white... and I don't typically even like white). Great service. Kimberly is the best. True story.
Being German, we were sceptical but this is real German food in a real German beerhall. Amazing, decent prices and very good food.

Yes it was Saturday of July 4th weekend. But a 2+ hour wait?? Come on. That's insane. We found out the to-go orders were only about a 30 min wait and decided to do that instead. I got the biscuit sampler, BF got the BBQ pork omelet and biscuits and gravy. Food was ready in about 40 mins. We walked around a bit while waiting but didn't go into any of the shops. Place was mobbed. Ate in the car. Honestly, Cracker Barrel and Biscuithead in Asheville have better food and better biscuits. My fave was the chicken biscuit. After that, the pulled pork biscuit. BF said omelet was just good, not great. Won't be back. Went once to say we were there and tried it.

3.5 stars. I really want to give it more, because the biscuits are unbelievable and the service is lovely, but I just can't. It's like one of those Nashville places that took off and suddenly the demand was far greater than the capacity. AKA you're stuck waiting more than an hour for weekend brunches, every time. When I visited, it was typically closer to two. Granted, while you're waiting, you can walk around the cute grounds and visit their awesome little market store to pick up some delicious goodies, so that's a bonus. But the inevitable wait, combined with the average and arguably overpriced (excluding the biscuits, mind you) food, just sort of takes away from everything. I'd highly recommend just picking up some to-go biscuits and calling it a day.

Am glad to have had such a great place to join with friends and family to celebrate my birthday.  I would surely go back and encourage those who maths w read so
E unfavourable reviews to go to this
Lace and form your own opinions; city Winery gets my vote as a nice place reasonably priced to enjoy yourself with friends and family   I am especially pleased to be able honestly to give praise for the winery as so many others have denied them the kudos they DO deserve.  I recommend giving the city winery a shot. Is it the best .food I have ever had -- no but it was still fun to try a new place and ignore some of the bad reviews which seem grossly inaccurate. give the City Winery a chance.

Simply put, my mother told us to go there, by the time we were done we all decided it was the best chicken, chicken fried steak and creamed corn we've ever had. Oh and then we topped it all off with a slice of coconut cream pie. Did I mention the biscuits with the different jams? Yeah, we'll be back!
The food was amazing but the wait is crazy. The staff is really nice. I ordered my food to go and sat outside on a picnic table. The corn hole is a lot of fun too.

Definitely a tourist destination, while I'm glad I went to check it out, I probably wouldn't venture there again.  The food was simple, but good.  Biscuits were yummy, but not the best I ever had.  Truthfully, I was happier with the atmosphere than the food.  We went this past Sunday and the wait time was 90 minutes, so instead we ordered take out, had it in less than 30, and ate in one of the other buildings.  It was perfect and much more efficient.  We got some of the Cajun bacon as well, and had BLTS that night, and they were outstanding.

Southern breakfast ? Check ! Biscuit platter lets you taste their famous biscuits AND delish BBQ and three other choices. At 830 on a weekday, no wait and totally worth it. Also- check out the shops :)

When I am asked for suggestions to take guests from out of town for a true Nashville experience, the first place that comes to mind in Loveless Cafe. It is a true staple of the Nashville cuisine. I have to admit, I am NOT a lover of fried chicken, biscuits with gravy etc,., but something about this place changes all that. The staff and service is all polite and adequate. The food is prepared nicely and my guests have always said that the fried chicken is cooked perfection. The appetizer are the infamous Loveless biscuits with a side of there jams and preserves (my favorite). This is not just a restaurant either, the cafe is surrounded by neat little shops selling antiques, souvenirs, and a bike shop. Definitely cannot get bored if you are waiting for a table. If you are looking for a great dining experience and to experience Nashville (Southern) culture, Loveless Cafe is a great place to visit.

I attended this restaurant for a work dinner recently and was sorely disappointed. I was in a group of about 8 people and there were maybe another 10 people there total. It took nearly an hour for our table to be served our orders. I got so hungry I asked the waitress to please bring some bread out to the table to which she replied, "we don't do that". This is extremely bizarre to me and I've honestly never been told this when I've inquired about bread for the table. When the food finally did arrive, I got the scallop ravioli, I was disappointed to find it came with only four measly raviolis. Keep in mind, this dish was about $25. When we finished, eating the waitress then took another 20 minutes to process our payment. I will not be attending this establishment in the future and if anyone is looking for prompt service and a filling meal, I'd look elsewhere.

Beautiful cafe and surrounding shops. Bisquits were good, a little too hard for my liking. The best platter is the sampler with (choose 3) fried chix, bbq shredded pork and fried catfish they all were great! The BBQ sauce was phenomenal! We had the sides corn casserole, sweet potato side and the hash browns. The only one that was ehh was the corn casserole or maybe because it was not too hot.  Overall the shredded pork takes the prize with the hash browns and sweet potatoes.

The Loveless is off the Natchez Trace Parkway a few miles from Leiper's Fork/Franklin TN.  There's not much around it, so it's definitely a "destination" trip.  The café is in a house surrounded by the original 1940's era Loveless roadside motel (the rooms have been turned into shops selling Loveless memorabilia, pottery, antiques, etc).  

If you go, it'll be to say you've been to one of the south's well known attractions and not necessarily for the diner-style food.  The famous complimentary biscuits are "okay".   I ordered a well done cheeseburger, which came burnt and very dry with melted slices of plain American cheese.  The crinkle fries were good, though.

The presentation of the brownies we ordered could use improvement, as we sort of expected they'd be on a plate, slightly warmed, with maybe a dollop of whipped cream or something.  Instead, they were tossed onto the table wrapped in saran wrap.  Fortunately, they were good. 

The Loveless isn't somewhere I'd go on a regular basis, but will take out of town guests who want to see an iconic southern sight.

Noticed this restaurant upon leaving the mall last night. Had no idea it was there but then remembered some small indication of it while walking the mall. My nephew and I decided to try it and ordered the reuben and fish and chips. The reuben ($11) was very good and came with regular fries. The fish and chips came with steak fries which we did not like as much as the regular fries. I love fish but probably would not order this dish again. It was $15 and came with one piece of fish and a lot of steak fries. The fish was ok. Jennifer was our server and we found her to be very nice. We were told the restaurant opened last Wednesday. Unless you park in the side of the mall you probably would not know the restaurant was there. One suggestion I would make is to have better signage in the mall. The doors leading to the restaurant are just plan exit doors that the general public would not use anyway.

While out of town visiting my boyfriend's family for the holidays in Tennessee, we all came here for a good ol' Southern breakfast on Sunday. Come for the biscuits, stay for the friendly service. And seriously, put peach preserves on those biscuits because holy crap, that's delicious.

Country fried steak and eggs with cheesy grits was really good. The eggs were slightly overcooked, but honestly, not by too much.  Definitely not enough to dock a star.  Those cheesy grits, though...man. SO GOOD. I want more right now.

Don't wait - get yourself here TODAY for the deliciousness.

I'm going to give this 4/5 stars just because it took some effort to get seated. The girls thought I was invisible for about 5 mins, then they suggested take out, then I was seated in the corner next to a large loud table before seating myself... 

Everything looked up right after being seated. My waitress was very friendly & the food was delicious. I ordered the watermelon ribs which were full of sweet zesty flavor, which was covered in BBQ sauce. The meat came off the bone with little effort.

I had a TOTAL blast at a special event at City Winery last Friday! As far as I know, the restaurant was closed to the public that night. We had the entire front area bar, as well as the large venue room. 

There were at least 4 bars placed around the room, which was really convenient, and there was never a long wait in line to get drinks. I enjoyed the cab that they offered that night for the party, as well as one of the "holiday martinis" which was reminiscent of an upscale bushwhacker ;). 

The food was SO impressive. I sampled a little of everything, and found myself saying "mmmmm" on every single item. My favorites were the cheesy grits topped with a shrimp gravy (omg), and there was also a mushroom option which I sampled from my sister's plate that was delicious. The shallot dip with the homemade potato chips was crave-worthy, and the strawberries and cream creme brule hadh me "mmmm'ing" at every bite. 

I can't wait to go back for another show and for another delicious dinner!
Food was spectacular and the service was good.  Blackberry preserves and biscuits with gravy were amazing!
Great bar, under a great music store! Been here several times. Good music, and good service. Clean bathrooms.

Of course the main draw is the fact that, well, it's the Loveless Cafe. So, I wouldn't call the food amazing, but it is pretty darn tasty. Especially their biscuits (of course!), of which they are thankfully very generous with. Everything else is yummy and your dining experience here might remind you of eating dinner at your grandmum's kitchen table. :)  The staff were very friendly and attentive.

This place is overwhelming with southern charm and to be honest, I'm pretty sure its overdosing on all aspects of cute.

However, the options for vegetarians are limited outside of the regular Denny's staples. I ordered the french toast because some variation of eggs just didn't seem like it had enough umph.

And see, I love biscuits, Perhaps more than my biscuit loving, meat eating friends. And their biscuits contain lard. While I appreciate my server mentioning it, he did so with a bit of unnecessary sarcastic zest.

And while I understand I'm in the south and perhaps the vegetarian lifestyle hasn't quite made it down here in the last 20 or so years since I've been a vegetarian, I was a bit underwhelmed by the food and overwhelmed by the charm of the Loveless campus.

A great place to watch a show, but for the love of Pete, eat somewhere else before or after. This place cannot get itself together on service. When the food arrives, it is forgettable. I've been here at least four times in two years, always with the same result. Unfortunate.

This review is for the restaurant.  Worst food I have ever experienced.  I love Dolmas (Grape leaves traditionally stuffed with rice and lamb) so we ordered the dirty rice dolmades with Shrimp.  They were so dry they were falling apart and they tasted like dirt.  Hummus plate was ok.  They piled on the one kind of hummus that was the worst and dotted the plate with the others, which weren't too bad.  
The braised duck tacos were terrible.  We all agreed.  The only reason I am giving this a 2 star instead of 1 is because of the pumpkin gnocchi.  If you like gnocchi, this is a MUST.  Delicious...but it did not make up for the poor quality of everything else.  Do yourself a favor and eat elsewhere!

Potato dumpling tasted like instant mix along with mashed potatoes. Potato pancakes were good as were the sausages. Apple strudel was soggy (probably microwaved). Funny there is NO German music playing.  Would not return. I've eaten better food.
True Southern cooking.  A spot not to miss when in the Nashville area.  Now serving beer, wine and cocktails.  The vegetables are as close to "home cooking" as you will find these days.

Perfect place to see local music. The vibe was cool. Seating is tight, but it's all a part of the experience. They have valet which is great, but prepare to wait a while after the show, as everyone has to get their cars from valet. Also, it's best to order all of your food the first time you see your waitress. We ordered an entree after our apps and it never came. Service is very slow, but for a music venue I thought the food we had was tasty!

We waited an hour for eggs and biscuits. It was ok. It was touristy and fun and so very Nashville but as far as quality food is concerned, I'm not impressed. The biscuits were good and I understand why the place is SO busy but there are better places for breakfast. Of course, if it's the experience you're after, you won't be disappointed. Just get there early!! Like, before they open if you'd like to avoid the wait. I will say the giftshop was cute and there was plenty to enjoy during our 1 hour wait (which is clearly mild based on other reviews). Come here knowing what you're getting - a touristy, famous spot with average food.

We came for Valentine's Day lunch.  I would not come again for dinner due to the slow service and no compensation from the restaurant for running out of items that came with the meals we ordered, getting one order completely wrong AND waiting a very long time for the food.  The nice couple sitting next to us had their meal paid for my the restaurant because they waited so long for their food to arrive.  That same couple felt so bad that our meal was not also paid for by the restaurant...that THEY paid for our meal!!! Gratitude for the nice couple and shame on the restaurant.

Ohhhhhhhh the biscuits! Everyone is saying it, because it's true! I got the friend chicken and a bunch of extra sides and split my meal with a friend. It was plenty of food plus some! I didn't love the sweet potatoes (just seemed like they had opened a can of yams) but otherwise, everything was so amazingly good. I really loved the green beans! Our server, Jason, was awesome! It seems like he's been there for a long time and you can tell. He knew his stuff, he was super friendly and helpful and added to our positive experience. I'm always grateful when a server will engage a little bit with the table and he did just that! The food is everything people say it is and ask for Jason if you want excellent service to go with it!

Had about an hour and ten minute wait. It was worth it. The biscuits were very good. But the chicken and waffles were to die for. Service was exceptional. Price was on the high side but the quality of the entire experience as well as my very full belly didn't seem to mind.

This might be a good place as a music venue, but as a restaurant- skip it. In a party of 4, 2 of us ordered steak. The plating was very nice but the steak was room temperature. The waiter apologized and took them back to the kitchen. In 2 minutes he brought 2 new dinners, again cold! A vegetable side that came out with the first steak, was still warmer than the 2nd entrée. When I called the manager about it the next day, she offered no solution other than if we came back we could have a drink on the house. I would NOT recommend this restaurant.

I am so surprised that I have not reviewed this place earlier! 

This is the place where we bring anyone and everyone who is visiting us from out of town if they say they want to eat "southern food". 

This place has a great ambiance. The decor is awesome. It's vintage-looking with the pictures of 101 famous singers/dancers/musicians/senators/presidents/mayors/etc. Amazing how many people have been here! 

Everything is delicious, so where do I start? Their biscuits are the BEST in town. The fried catfish is great. I have tried the pork chops as well- ah!mazing. 

The prices are great and you get A LOT of food. I can literally eat my left-overs for 2 more meals the next day. 

When people say the food here is to DIE for, I think they mean it literally. After all that cholesterol and fat, you will be very near death. If you want a meal that will keep you full for the next 18 hours, go here! 

Love it!

I've dined here multiple times, and I loved it when I first ate here, but each time seems worse. This time, the service was just awful. There seemed to be only 1 or 2 servers responsible for all of the tables, and everyone in the restaurant seemed to be doing everything - running food, delivering drinks, bussing tables, refilling water, etc. I don't blame the wait staff; there's probably a management breakdown. Our simple, 3-person dinner at 8:30p turned into a 2-hour ordeal. All of the tables around us seemed to be having the same experience. They also greatly reduced their menu. Good luck if you're a vegetarian.

To top it off, one of their events let out around 10:15p, just as we were preparing to leave. You'd think they'd have a dedicated valet for the restaurant patrons, but alas, we had to get in line with the hundreds of people who had attended the event. It seemed to be the final nail in the coffin for us.

while you may have to wait a while to get in that should be your first clue that it is that GOOD!!! have eaten there for the last 42 years and  it is just as good now as it was when i first went there. every meal has always been great as well as the down home service. it is a must if you are in nashville.

I love this place it's just a really cool place to go, if you have eaten here and you are close by do yourself a favor and stop in. It's good food, friendly staff it feels like grandmas southern cooking! So yummy

Love this place.  Breakfast is amazing.  The jams are delicious.  And the smoke master gave the kids a little tour and a tutorial on how he smokes the meat.  Very nice man .. We all enjoyed talking with him.  Awesome morning!

Love this place! If you go to Nashville you must stop. Didn't have to wait too long when I went but i wouldn't have minded if we did. The fried chicken was great. Also got mac & cheese and cheesy potatoes. They have a store next door and they sell family size food to go!

"Breakfast at The Loveless Café?"

I had been in Nashville less than 24 hours, and this was the third time I had heard of/and been instructed to eat at The Loveless Café. So, we did!

Since the 1940's, Lon and Annie Loveless have been serving chicken and biscuits right from the front door of their house to travelers going to and from Nashville. Eventually, their 'home' became a regularly scheduled stop of travelers, and as such evolved into The Loveless Motel and Café in 1951.Today, they serve 7000 biscuits a day, and once you've sunk your teeth into the creamy, buttery goodness, you'll know why. They are amazing. They also bring an assortment of fresh made preserves to the table. Yum.

I watch a lot of cooking shows, which is ironic, since I don't cook. Our stove is used to store things, suitcases waiting to be used and shoes waiting to be worn. However, from the myriad of cooking shows, I have gleaned that Tennesseans know bar-b-queue, and after visiting, I am convinced.  Ribs, ribs and more ribs. Ribs slow cooked in a pit. Ribs smoked dry, baked, boiled, broiled, rubbed, doused, simmered and oh so good. The Rib Special of the day at The Loveless, were slow cooked with watermelon; the meat literally falling from the bone. The keys to good ribs, I'm told, are some 'fine swine' and lots of time.

Throughout the ages, The Loveless Café has been a much cherished piece of Nashville culture. In 2004, for the first time in Loveless history, they closed their doors for renovation. When they reopened a few months later, 'folks were standing in line thicker than sausage gravy'.

Today The Loveless has been featured on many shows, including Ellen DeGeneres, Today and Good Morning America. For a downhome  southern food experience, this place makes the cut.

Visit my site at: www.TNBTA.com for cool photos and more reviews....

Food gets 5 stars, service was 3.5...

Our meals consisted of fried chicken, chicken strips(giant..the biggest I've ever seen), garden salad, hashbrown casserole, green beans, mashed potatoes, creamed corn, mac & cheese, and fried green tomatoes. All were very good. My favorite was the creamed corn. That alone is worth the 3 hour trip. 

Biscuits were excellent. I loved the buttery flavor topped with even more butter from the table. The jams were PERFECT. Not overly sweet, fruity chunks of peaches, loved the consistency of the blackberry. Our table of 5 ate 13 biscuits before our food came. We couldn't stop!

We were told an hour and 15 minutes to wait for our table. It ended up being an hour and 30, which is fine. There's a lot to see and do in the shops and grounds. Free coffee in the Hams & Jams store. 

Our waiter was kind of odd, for lack of a better word.. He was attentive at first but then he disappeared from the area for a good while. We were waiting on drinks to be filled and more biscuits. Several different people brought out our order and we asked one of them for more biscuits but they didn't come, so then we asked our waiter when he finally reappeared. He offered the next table more biscuits before they were even done with their plate so not sure why we were skipped over. Plus he offered them honey & sorghum, but not us. 

All in all, it was worth the trip and I can't wait to go back.
Great local place with lots of history .Best biscuits anywhere. Always crowded. Their food is worth the wait.
Always a great experience here. Friendly people, good food, good shopping while you wait. Be sure to stop by the smokehouse. If you're not hungry by then, you will be.

My meal got off to an amazing start with the biscuits and preserves; it was very good. Other than that, your money would be better spent at your local Cracker Barrel. I ordered the pulled bbq pork with turnip greens and mac & cheese. The mac & cheese was beyond disappointing, the turnip greens were decent but below average, but the meat was actually kind of tasty. Overall, my experience was very disappointing considering the hype that surrounds this place. The Loveless Cafe is definitely nothing to write home about.

This is the dive-iest of dive bars a midst a row of other dive bars.  The music was great.  The beer was cheap (like $2 for 6oz).  The tables were really sticky.  The smoke was thick.  Anything that wasn't beer (I can't do gluten) was crazy expensive.  My very weak dixie cup of vodka/cran was $7!!   In retrospect I should have just done a couple of jello shots.  Great fun though.

The brunch menu was hilarious. The PB&J is very disappointing, I couldn't even finish half of it. Our server could of cared less about our table. We were out of town guests and it was our first time and he didn't help us with the menu or drink recommendations at all. He seemed in a rush. I was very excited to go there and ended up very disappointed.

I had read reviews and some weren't favorable so I didn't know what to expect. I was not disappointed!! I had the fried chicken, hashbrown casserole, pinto beans and fried green tomatoes and everything was so good. The downside was the 1 hour wait, but the food and service more than made up for it. In fact, I'll be back!

Caution: Tourist trap. Biscuits were warm and were good but not the best I ever had. Food was mediocre. Wait time is ridiculously long and I think they do that on purpose so you can spend time in their shops purchasing needless merchandise.  Our service was great though.
Great home style comfort food. Really loved the the cream corn and mac and cheese. Chicken was also really good.

I will start by saying I hope they make it and I am surprised they are not more together being a chain(4) in major metropolitan areas.  So to start there was a bit of confusion upon arrival due to the fact that we had a reservation in the restaurant and not the music venue.
