Some how within 10 minutes (time it took us to be taken to our seats in the music venue side only to find out that is not where the reservations were for) our reservation for 8 was lost and we were now going to have to wait 3o minutes to get seated.  We finally got that worked out so the wait was only 15 minutes, ok.  The server was very nice but not overly attentive.  We waited for our food for 1.5 hours, then it came out over a 15 minute time frame and for some it was cold.  The food was mediocre at best, the pizza was cold, the duck tacos were gamy and the burger was just ok. Oh did I mention we had to ask 2X to get some silverware for 2 of the people at the table.  After dinner and coffee we waited another 40 minutes to get our bill.  Parking was not an issue for us as we took a lyft but I have to say upon departure and trying to get a taxi the people at the Valet stand were very, very rude.  So my experience was not fun, I did not feel like a patron but more like a nuisance.  I have to say the experience inside the music venue may be better but I do not think I will spend the $$$'s to try again.

We decided to get outside of Nashville for a day on our recent trip, and knew we had to stop at Loveless for breakfast! We were able to snag an 8:45am reservation on a Friday morning for 6 people. The table was ready for us upon arrival.

Our waiter was really nice, funny, and on top of it! The coffee was terrible...it had to be some of the worst coffee we had ever had. I got the chicken fried steak with the hashbrown casserole... when in Tennessee!! The chicken fried steak was decent but un-memorable. The hashbrown casserole was the best part. Cheesy goodness!!

This was a fun stop. Okay breakfast, southern hospitality, cute gift shops and grounds. Nice stop, but don't feel a great need to come back.
Nice place great food and excellent service!!! Gemmall was our server and he was fantastic!!!

I'm on vacation staying at downtown Nashville and my daughter recommended Loveless Cafe. The drive was 30 minutes and well worth the trip. The homemade biscuits and homemade jams was amazing. The breakfast was good but my ham was a little salty. The waitress was very attentive and gave us extra biscuits, jam and coffee. I highly recommend this place.

Biscuits: 3.9 out of 5

That's perhaps the most shocking result of my recent trip to this iconic property west of Nashville. I decided to embark on a mission to find the Top Ten biscuits in Middle Tennessee, one of the many foods for which this area is known (hot chicken, barbecue, pork chops, Goo Goo Clusters, pies, etc.). So why not begin my investigation at the most quintessential place to get a biscuit in Music City?

The Loveless Cafe and gift shops have become quite the noteworthy destination for tourists and locals alike, a charming enclave of shops so rustic it's almost kitschy. It had been years since I dined here, long before I was a Yelper, so this time I came prepared to take careful mental notes on the food, especially the complimentary biscuits. Despite their underwhelming size, they come out hot and fresh with a delicious buttery top that's slightly salty and rigid. Almost perfect! And then you consume the interior which becomes sticky, not soft, as you begin to chew and lacks that classic buttery taste. My father the chef developed a 5-star biscuit so perfect it required no condiments. The biscuits at Hominy Grill in South Carolina are a 4.5. Thus I have high biscuit standards, and these unfortunately are nowhere near that caliber.

PROS:
Loveless offers tasty comfort food of reasonable quality and tourists will certainly enjoy their visit. The service is fantastic, in fact the waitress kept my water glass as full as the wait staff at a top-rated Beverly Hills restaurant. The mac 'n' cheese was simple but very, very good and the fried pork chop batter was almost perfect!

CONS:
For a restaurant so lauded by the media, there were many disappointments beyond the mediocre biscuits. The fried okra was mushy and tasteless when it should be flavorful and just as crisp as fried chicken. Okra is currently out of season, but there is no excuse for such a lack of crunch. The pork chop itself was dry. The gravy, supposedly one of their specialties, was perfectly peppery! But the consistency was extraordinarily gelatinous, certainly the type of thickness you don't want in gravy. Perhaps the biggest disappointment of all was the slice of pecan pie, a staple for Southern diners. At $4.29, the small portion I received was terribly bland and tasted like flavorless Jell-O with a hint of pecan. In fact, it is the only slice of pecan pie I've been unable to finish in my lifetime, probably the worst pie I've ever had.

Yes, Loveless is good and it's worth one visit, especially for tourists looking for that classic Southern meal. But compared to the burgeoning restaurant scene that has overtaken Nashville, Loveless simply cannot keep up. I understand how it achieved iconic status. I just don't understand how it maintains that distinction.

Items Selected:
Coffee
Unlimited Buttermilk Biscuits with Housemade Strawberry, Blackberry, Peach Jam
Pecan Pancakes with Maple Bacon, Sorghum
French Toast with Housemade Sausage and Sorghum
Biscuit Sampler - Fried Chicken, Pulled Pork, Aged Ham, Pimento Cheese & Fried Green Tomato with Cheese Grits
Pecan Pie, Chocolate Chess, Banana Pudding
Chess Pie

Conveniently located just off the route from Nashville to Memphis, Loveless Café and the small village of stores around it are nothing short of a Tennessee Landmark, and fresh off the redeye from LAX our arrival at the former hotel preceded its opening by a mere fifteen minutes, a line of six already formed with the sizable restaurant nearly 100% full by the time we left just after 8:15.

Featuring concepts of sustainability, scratch-based cooking, and a menu of Southern diner classics spanning from breakfast through lunch to supper, it was almost immediately upon seating that water was poured while coffee was readied and although the brew itself was a bit acrid without sweetener the refills were spot on and spontaneous, though food did take a bit longer than would be expected as our server was spread thinly throughout the largest room in the house, at times even drawn to the al fresco seating to assist others at a table of twelve.

Sipping coffee with orders placed it would not be long before a plate of Loveless' signature buttermilk biscuits was delivered, and paired with a trio of housemade jams plus requested sorghum and honey it goes without saying that the fluffy golden rounds are indeed quite delicious, though for my money there are better to be found not only in Nashville but also parts of the Carolinas as well as at Yardbird, still the reference standard, though admittedly theirs are not refilled freely on request.

Moving on to entrees, another piping hot cup of coffee poured, it was largely a matter of sampling widely that led to an order of even more biscuits and with each of the four golden rounds topped differently one would be hard pressed to name a winner amongst the group, the crispy chicken and tender pulled pork rousing curiosity of just how good a full plate dinner at Loveless might be while the tart green tomato topped with spicy pimento cheese was as 'Southern' as it gets, certainly not the sort of stuff you see served for breakfast anywhere back home.

Moving next to the French Toast and Pancakes, suffice it to say that both are competent takes on classic American breakfast staples, and with the buttermilk fresh plus the bread homemade the only real question is whether to indulge in Maple Syrup, local Honey, or thick amber Sorghum as the topping of choice, from my standpoint a decision that entailed a little of each before deeming the decision a tossup, the Sorghum almost a bit *too* sweet on the vanilla and cinnamon dipped toast but absolutely delightful when mellowed by the ample amount of toasted pecans added to the pancakes for just a buck.

Unwilling to forgo desserts, 7:45 in the morning or not, what started as a sampler of three miniature pies and puddings quickly expanded to a quartet when the server brought chocolate chess instead of original, and with a pure butter crust serving as the base to both reference standard iterations it speaks volumes that the pecan pie was actually the best of them all, a dearth of 'filler' allowing the caramelized nuts and brown sugar to shine without being overly sweet - a similar degree of subtlety offered by banana pudding that used house whipped cream and softened vanilla wafers amidst thick chopped fruit and a smooth yellow base to deliver an experience that was not only texturally pleasing but also shockingly natural, a quality far too infrequently found in a dessert where boxed pudding is far too frequently meant to suffice.

AMAZING does not even begin to describe the meal I had while here.  The biscuits are out of this world, the food is all homemade and the service was exceptional!  I would give this cafe 100 stars if I could.  Thankfully, I live states away or I would be in trouble  FYI you might have a long wait to get in but let me just say it's well worth it!  They have little stores you can visit and shop while you wait to make the time go by.  I'm wanting some biscuits now as I'm writing this....lol.  Enjoy everyone, you won't be disappointed I promise.

Love this place! Food is amazing and the staff is the best! There 3-4 different shops you can go to if you are waiting to be seated, they offer so many things. You definitely need to try this place if you haven't already and if you have go back they are still great!!

Wonderful food and nostalgic atmosphere. You can browse the store and surroundings while you wait to be seated. You WILL wait. World famous biscuits. Good country cooking. A lot of history in this local and tourist favorite.

I was here for an event during Music Biz 2018. The venue is BEAUTIFUL and the service is phenomenal. I ordered the rose cider and wow it rocked my world.  I would have ordered another but it was a bit pricey for me (recent college grad so definitely out of my price range). Because things were a bit more expensive I was hesitant to buy any food but my hunger quickly grew as the man next to me ordered a margarita flatbread. I decided to #TreatYoSelf2018 and order one as well. I'm glad I did. It was huge portions and tasted amazing.

Overall I really enjoyed the place. I will say it is definitely on the pricier side so I won't be returning unless some fancy man is taking me out. But, it was still amazing. If you're looking for a place to make an impression this will for sure make the mark with their amazing selection and well crafted menu options.
Worth the wait! Best biscuits, best fried chicken, love the atmosphere and friendly staff. Always enjoy my time there. Thanks Loveless Cafe!
AMAZING! Food is great, service is great and the place is adorable! Every time I'm in Nashville I make sure to grab some breakfast!!!

Made the long drive out and although it was neat to see the food wasn't overwhelmingly great. I had the fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and Mac and cheese. The Mac and cheese was very good. I almost think the potatoes were instant at least they tasted that way...not a compliment. The fried chicken was plenty good but not amazing. Now the biscuits were very good but the preserves were the best part of it all. I'm glad we didn't have to wait. I wouldn't say it was worth waiting for. All in all not sad we went but wouldn't go back again.
The biscuits alone are reason alone why to go to Loveless!  I've had chicken fried steak and both were amazing.
if you want to feel like absolute shit after, eat here.

This is quite literally the most popular meal stop in Nashville. Locals and tourists alike flock to Loveless. The bulk of them in search of the famous biscuits. 

Upon arrival, you will be handed a pager (it's a given, there will be a wait). But no fear, there is plenty to keep you busy while you wait. These folks sure have taken space utilization to new heights. Gifts shops, bookstores, deli, arts and crafts; can't fault anyone for maximizing profits. But I wonder if the food has suffered in the process. 

The food :
The biscuits - Served bread basket style, complimentary as you await your order. I will say they are very good. The best? Probably not, but quite satisfying. 

Grits - pretty mediocre 

Waffles - good thickness, texture, and flavor, but becomes stale after about 5 minutes 

BBQ pork - arrived a little cold. Not exactly how you like to enjoy your food. Otherwise ok flavor 

Country ham - touted as one of the specialties; kinda fell flat. The ham itself was on the cold side, and very tough/chewy. 

Unfortunately the name is pretty befitting, loveless cafe.....After my visit, I love them just a little less.

The biscuits and preserves are definitely what keeps me and my family coming back. The breakfast is good, but nothing special. My kids love to watch them making biscuits in the window and play on the grounds. We usually go on the weekends but we make sure to get there no later than 8:30am to avoid a long wait.

You just has to know what you are getting into. It is a tourist stop, so it is busy. (we waited an hour) While we waited there was some drama with a bachelorette party, which there seems to be a million of in the nashville area. The food was solid to very good, the service was very friendly. I would stop back if I know the wait would be less.

Yes, the hype is real -- the biscuits are ridiculously good. Paired with their strawberry jam, I swear I felt like I was 8 again. Homemade as it gets.

Everything has that authentic, made in your grandma's kitchen taste. Very traditional. Seasoned well, but not overwhelming on the salt. So far it's the best comfort food we've encountered.

Got here at 7:00ish on a Saturday and only waited 10 minutes to be seated. Will definitely come again! Bring your parents, they'll adore it.

We were visiting from out of town for the NPAA (Nurse Practitioner American Association) Conference at the OpryLand Hotel, and had great service on a Tuesday at around noon even though we waited 15 minutes to sit.  

I had a country fried steak with white gravy, Hash-brown Casserole, and two eggs over medium.  I combined the eggs and the gravy to top the CFS and it was great.  The CFS was about the size of my hand, or about 10 inches round.   Very very tasty.  My wife had a fried chicken salad, and my daughter had the old faithful chicken wings.  Everyone was very pleased with their meals.

Not a fan of places that Nickel and dime you. They make you valet, as there's no parking lot, and charge $8 for it. They also have a separate wine tax. Additionally, we ordered the roasted red pepper ricotta dip as an appetizer. It was delicious, but they only gave us four chips to eat the whole dip. We asked for extra chips, and the waitress said no problem. When we received the bill, we were charged for additional chips. I have to say, I'm not impressed with their customer service model. That being said, everything we ordered was delicious. However, we won't be returning. I don't enjoy paying fees for every little thing.

We were eager to go here and were sadly disappointed. To be semi fair, we have had real German food IN Germany before so of course we got our hopes up to have some good real German food. 

The pretzels were good, but really that's not a hard thing to get right. My husband got the beer sampler and you are only aloud to choose 2 of the beers that come in it, and their Radler isn't aloud to be in it. That doesn't make sense to me considering radlers are beer and lemonade. I mean you're using less beer so why not add it to the sampler if a customer wants it?

I was pretty disappointed in my food. I ordered sausages, bread, and sauerkraut. Which all of those things are amazing if made right (and in Germany). The sausage was good, best part of my dish. I was disappointed that my bread was just simply sliced bread, instead of a roll or something. And the sauerkraut.... don't even bother with it. It was horrible. My husband got mini burgers and enjoyed his food. 

The service was sad too. I'm not sure if our waitress was having a bad day or what. You never know. But it wasn't good while we were there. She hardly smiled, spoke too softly, checked on us only once (and she wasn't even the one who brought us our food). Additionally, the place wasn't even close to busy. 

So...
The good: pretzels tasted good (but kind of hard to screw those up). Beer is good. Sausage was good. Decor and atmosphere is cool. The waitresses and waiters attire is cutely German.

The not so good: sliced bread? Lol. Stay away from the sauerkraut! Service was sad. If you have been to Germany and like real German food, stay away all together.

The defining example of a tourist trap. Yes the buns are good along with the jams, but that is it. The food is of poor quality, and barely warm. Add this to a long wait, high prices, and an overworked wait-staff and you have a poor dinning experience.  I was very disappointed.

We went two days in a row, it's that good. For breakfast we had the country ham and pulled pork omelet. Both were very good along with the hash brown casserole and biscuits and gravy. The best sausage gravy I've ever had. On our second visit we had the fried chicken with fried green tomatoes, mashed potatoes and gravy and Mac n cheese. For desert we had the key lime pie (the best I've had). Everything was excellent and both times the service was good and very friendly. I will go back every chance I get.

Southern cooking at its finest. It is worth the wait to get some down-home goodness right here. I would give it 6 out of 5 if I could. Lots of celebrities have been here, it has been in business for more than 60 years (that says something), and the diverse mix of people in there was nice to see. I had the chicken fried steak along with eggs and grits; super well prepared with the buttery stone-ground flavor made me perfectly satisfied. Great wait staff too. The wooden floors and windows are reminiscent of the Old South. The biscuits are the best thing I've ever had!!! There is a heat and soft tenderness to them you cannot get anywhere else in my view. Perfect jams as well. Overall tremendous experience. Worth the long drive down Highway 100. Don't forget the sweet tea!!!!!

We had my company's Christmas party here and it was wonderful. I was nervous because I'd never been (my usual haunts were all booked) but we were very pleasantly surprised! There was a harp player, which made for beautiful ambience. Everything from the drinks, apps to the entree were amazing. The service too! I will definitely be back for a date with my boyfriend.
Amazing food! Had the biscuit French toast!! The seating on the outside patio is so peaceful and delightful!! Will be back before we leave Nashville!!
Service was good. Was a unique setting. We visited for a group event so I can't give a fair review on the food.

Came here for brunch with my girlfriend following church. We had a groupon for basically 2 brunch drinks and 2 brunch meals. The Bloody Mary was good, my gf ordered a drink with pecan vodka and ginger ale that was really good as well. I had the eggs Benedict that was pretty good and my gf ordered frosted flakes French toast. The food is good and service wasn't terrible. Just not my ideal brunch spot. Food meals are a la carte. I can't speak for music venue wise but the brunch here doesn't do it for me.
Not bad at all but nothing to excite me about coming back for brunch. Maybe I'll try dinner/a show next time.

Being the only really solid breakfast place in a large radius, Loveless Cafe is always crowded--that's the downside. The upside is pretty much everything else: melt-in-your-mouth fluffy biscuits, solid breakfast food served all day, and friendly service. My wife and I come here every time we drive through Tennessee.

I took off a star because they discontinued their call-ahead option.

Been to this place a few times and it's always great. Food is fast, fresh, delicious, and always on point. Our service from Charles tonight was flawless, You would think we were at the Catalina Wine Mixer! The live music and the energy it creates is the cherry on the strudel.

This place became my favorite, for its atmosphere and amazing service. 
We came here 2 times during my short visit to Nashville. We had breakfast and supper. 

The place is very cosy and welcoming. It was a 45 min wait for a table on Friday morning, so we decided to check out the gift shops. Staff everywhere is so friendly! Coming from California, where the only thing is served is attitude . 

Lots of cute souvenirs and home goods. They also ship their food anywhere in the country, which is awesome, because they home made preserves are delicious. 

For breakfast we had country ham and eggs, with side of grits and hash brown casserole. I haven't had southern food in so long, so I enjoyed it. I also got a moonshine shot, which came in a cute jar, that you get to keep. 

Famous biscuits were also good, however I was more excited to try the famous chess pie. And if I could sign up for a monthly delivery of that awesomeness I sure would! That pie is so good! As full as I was after breakfast, I still ate almost a whole slice! 
Susan was our waitress and she was amazing! Very friendly and nice! Thank you Susan!  

Next day we came back for dinner. I had to have some fried chicken before I leave. I got a half with a side of mashed potatoes and green beans. I died and went to a fried chicken heaven! Comfort food at its best! To drink I got a harvest moonshine(?) , it's mixed with sweet iced tea, and so so good! 
But the best part of the dinner was our server Owen! I would like to thank you so much to make this dinner experience so special! Now, every time I will think about southern hospitality, I would think of you! Thank you for great service! You made us feel so welcome! 

Overall, i fell in love with this place and I think it's gonna become a tradition, while I'm in Nashville! Thanks y'all!!! Can't wait to be back!

My wife was born and raised in Bavaria and I was stationed there in the military, so we love eating German food.  We took five friends and two relatives to the Bavarian Bierhaus on our week long trip to Nashville.  None of our friends/family had eaten authentic German food, so our expectations were high that the food would be excellent.  Unfortunately, we were extremely disappointed in the quality of the food, as well as the lack of authentic German entertainment.  When the food finally arrived, it appeared to have been sitting under a warming lamp for an extended period, as the surface of the red cabbage, spatzle and rouladen were extremely dry.  The food was only luke warm and there was no flavor to it. Everything tasted very bland, which is the same response that I got from our friends and family who joined us.  My wife had the Black Forest Chicken Schnitzel and thought it was very bland and dry, as well. The facilities are second-to-none, which led to our high expectations that the food would be the same.  After spending more than $300 on food, we all agreed that it would be our last trip to this venue, unfortunately.  We would have sent the food back or called for the chef to come to our table, but we had a 2 year old toddler who was getting cranky and my niece just wanted to get home to put him to bed. It is a great concept, but they need to seriously work on their food quality and flavor.

Well worth the 40 minute wait (if you do have to wait they have a few little shops you can walk around to)!!  Had their breakfast, pork brisket and eggs with their biscuits topped with their preserves (blackberry was my fave).....delicious!  Mark served us and he was an amazing server.  You can't go wrong stopping in to this place.

Okay, so I finally made it to Loveless for breakfast. Waited an hour and a half was expected, and there was enough to keep me busy, so that was okay. People were friendly. 

I had some trouble with the menu, ultimately I couldn't find anything I really wanted which is usually not a problem I have. The biscuits were good, but let's be honest, this whole show is about the jam -- which is delicious. 

Waitress was rushed, kind of harassed, but mostly funny about it. 

The breakfast with friends was nice, overall the experience was good. Not really sure why people are so obsessed at this point, aside from the fact that the place IS AN INSTITUTION. Definitely worth it for the history, I suppose.

This place is definitely worth the drive out of downtown Nashville! The staff is very sweet and accommodating and the manager came over and was a very friendly, interested guy. The biscuits are AMAZING, but that is what they're famous for! The pancakes are huge and are sweet, making them special. The biscuit sampler platter is large, and more of biscuit-sandwiches style than biscuits with various ingredients cooked into them. Definitely try the home fruit preserves on the biscuits! Lots of free parking available and there's a cute market to mosey on over before or after! Interesting history to the place and adorable decor. A great stop!
A fabulous brunch - grits with shrimp, French toast, frittata- yummy. Full bar. The perfect Sunday morning

Came here some time ago, and I have to first say it was the best, most tender, juiciest bbq pulled pork I have ever had. Another thing - the wait time was ridiculous, nearly 2 hours. I ended up having a snack at the shop that also sells the bbq pork, where I had a small preview of the delicious bbq pulled pork. I wanted a second and third helping and just to eat that, but my friends wanted to eat at the actual restaurant.....

And yes, it was worth it, for those dang biscuits. MAN THEY'RE GOOD. I needed extra strawberry jam for them, TWICE. These, along with the bbq pork, are what I remember most. I had dessert too, it was delicious, but nothing comes close to these babies.

Overall, AMAZING, but WAY too long of a wait when its busy. ALTERNATIVE: get BBQ sandwiches next door and buy goo clusters for dessert!

This place is a Ten!  Wonderful southern food with great service.  Neat little compound of shops too. Chicken fried steak was best ever.  Biscuits were incredible. Not to mention the decadent all handmade desert menu.  Fudge pie?  Only in the south. Do not miss this place!  A bit of a drive from Nashville but so worth it.

This place is tasty - the biscuits are top notch! However, I'm not sure I'd wait the 2 hours on the weekend. I tried the sampler - the pork bbq one is the best!  The tomato and pinto cheese wasn't my favorite.

great food! the biscuits are amazing, and you have to have them with the blackberry jam...delish! great service, and a really cute gift shop next door with equally pleasant people. I highly recommend!

The minute I walked in I was so disappointed in the atmosphere. If you've been to a a real German-style bierhaus the atmosphere is rustic and lively. This was more like a cafeteria; white-walled with a few checkered swag valances hanging from the rafters.  The so-called oompa band was playing country; I didn't hear polka until I was ready to leave. Nashville doesn't give you a pass to play country at a -theme- restaurant. (Volkfest has a more authentic band.)
We sat at the bar which served several authentic German beers. The bartender was dressed normally but at least the barback was wearing a German dress. Sitting under very bright lights at a white bar felt like a blandly sanitized environment I wouldn't want to experience again. 
We didn't bother bother staying for food.

I am giving this three stats because of the quality of the pancake and the wait time.  We were told the wait was 45 minutes, but it was more like 1 hour 15 minutes.  The best part was the biscuits and jams they bring out, they were amazing!  I ordered pancakes, plus a breakfast with egg.  The pancakes were extremely heavy, not good at all, I was quite disappointed for a place that is known for their breakfast.  The eggs, bacon and  were very good.

I did enjoy walking around their little (overpriced) shops during the wait.

This place is nothing short of heaven on earth. I just found this place today and I have yet to leave. We came for brunch which was delightfully fresh and flavorful. I had an omelette and a side of potatoes with biscuits. The blackberry jam is simply Devine and has a hint of wine and whole blackberries. The highlight here is the superb customer service with Darrell and Sydney. The wait staff was attentive and I asked a million questions since I love wine and this was my first time. Hayley the bartender treated us to drinks and lovely conversation so come see here. The icing on the cake was when Mike the manager came and asked us if we wanted to see the wine operation. Of course we squirled with excitement!! We have had a magical day of wine, food and great customer service.

Wow! Tonight I came in with a large group and Kimberly served us in a phenomenal way. She was attentive and fun! We even took a photo! I felt at one with this lady! She got our orders 100% correct and we had a blast. She knows everything about this menu. What a star! Can she come home with me?

We had a fun and wonderful experience at Loveless.  The atmosphere was very cozy- Felt like it was dinner in a family home. Very friendly and great service. The fried chicken we had was delicious and the sides were delicious and generous. Had to wait for about an hour but it was well worth it. We live quite a distance away, But would return and would highly recommend a visit here.

This review is just for the front restaurant, not the venue. Besides the fact that our server wasn't the most attentive (even though he was knowledgable and personable), we had a great time. The food was great and reasonably priced, the wine flights were delightful, and the atmosphere was really neat. We had a great time!

I was driving through Nashville and meeting a friend. She suggested this place. It was a Friday night and was a little shocked when the hostess said it would be a "2 hour wait". We walked around while we waited and checked out the gift shop, the jam shop, and the grounds. Our buzzer went off after only about an hour. Pleasant surprise. 
Biscuits, jam, and butter were delivered immediately and our drink order was taken. I had the fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and mac-n-cheese. It was delicious. Everybody else enjoyed their food as well.
Our waitress was great. Very attentive and prompt. Asking if we needed anything, refilling drinks, etc. I would recommend this place and let them know the food is worth the wait.
This is a superb place. I always love driving out of the way to dine here! The food is down home comfort goodness

We went for Mother's Day Brunch ,,, 2 hr wait,,, drive was beautiful , worth the wait . we got Omletts and French toast ,,, AWSOME biscuits,,, with To die for Jam . Ordered another dozen biscuits to go. 
Friendly service. Love this place.
Remember to look for Bobby flays pix near the door to ur right as u come out .

Loveless Cafe is a half hour away from the center of Nashville, but it warrants a visit! When you pull up to the location, you know you're about to get a real southern experience just from the look of it. The small town, old school motel sign, and location inside a small house set the scene perfectly and then the staff inside executes with that classic southern charm. I came right when they opened on a Thursday so there was no wait.

The waiter immediately started us out with a plate of six biscuits for the three of us along with some peach, strawberry, and blackberry preserves. I don't even have to say it, but I will: the biscuits are phenomenal (I ended up eating six by the end of breakfast). I'm usually not one for jams/butter/other spreads on bread, but I decided to try each of the preserves they provided. Boy am I glad I did! They were all delicious and I couldn't decide which was my favorite so I kept alternating between the three.

For breakfast, I was able to try the french toast, the fried chicken & waffle, and a chicken biscuit. Everything was well made and tasty - a solid 4 stars all around with nothing more to say than that. Also, our waiter brought out a second round of biscuits with the food so we got to keep indulging in their fluffiness as we enjoyed our main dishes.

In the end, I say you've got to stop at Loveless Cafe when visiting Nashville because of the classic Southern feel, top notch biscuits, and tasty food.
I've never eaten anything here that wasn't delicious. Service is fast. If you don't want to wait go during a down time of the day because it gets busy.

This former hot sheets motel turned BBQ pit and restaurant is a must when you're following the Natchez Trace and want some solid Southern cooking. Their turnip greens with pot likker are the best you'll ever have. I also recommend the country ham, which I will be ordering from them next Easter, with their biscuits and fried green tomatoes. Put some housemade jelly (buy it from the gift shop, too -- the peach is especially good) or pimiento cheese on it and get back on the 100.

Not sure how anyone could complain that there was a wait for here.  You'd have to be from Mars to not know you would have a wait.  2-3 hours is the norm on weekends, people!  Grab some bean bags and play corn hole and chillax!  By the way, you CAN CALL AHEAD to be put on the waiting list.  Get ready to leave the hotel, put in a call, and then by the time you get there, you should just about be ready to be seated.

I lucked out and had a 10 minute wait last Wednesday between breakfast and dinner.  We were seated exactly at 11, so we had dinner.  Son had the pimiento cheese bacon burger which was FABULOUS.  I couldn't decide on which sides to get, so I got the side dish platter.  I had black-eyed peas, green beans, mac and cheese, and the best creamed corn I have EVER tasted.

Biscuits?  Yes, they're wonderful.  Peach preserves were delectable.  Next time, I'll try some biscuits and gravy.....and I'll buy some mix and peach preserves for home....

We decided to follow a friend's recommendation while in Nashville for a quick trip for a wedding - I am SO glad we did! While it isn't in the downtown area, it was certainly worth the drive. We sat outside and just loved the atmosphere. I'm GF so I couldn't try the biscuits but the rest of my group had 3-4 each (our waiter, the lovely Trevor, gladly kept bringing us more!) Their omelets are DELICIOUS. Just go - you won't be disappointed!

So this place is definitely out of the way if you're staying in the city (my friends and I were a few blocks from Broadway when we went), but if you've got wheels and a burning hunger for the kind of southern food you came down South for, then Loveless is your place. 

The meal started with a basket of biscuits with homemade jam (on the house) and my friend and I shared the Pimento Bacon burger and the BBQ sandwich, then finished the meal off with some pie. The service was super-friendly and the food was all good.Totally what we wanted out of a Nashville dining experience.

My husband and I stopped here after finishing the Natchez Trace around 4:30.  Perfect time to stop as we had to wait only 20 min before being seated. The biscuits were very good as everyone says. Of course we had to have the fried chicken after hearing so much about it.  We both got the 1/4 fried white meat. I got the green beans and Mac and cheese after finding out the vegetable of the day was already sold out. My husband had mashed potatoes and gravy and the white beans.  I thought my chicken was a little dry. The beans were salty and I wasn't fond of the Mac and cheese which seemed like boiled noodles with cheese sauce. My husband enjoyed his mashed potatoes but was a little surprised at the sauce on the white beans. I guess we were expecting a lot better meal because we had always heard what a fantastic place this was. It was ok. I'm just glad we didn't have to wait as long as I understand most people have to.

This place is a Nashville staple. Great for getting groups together and heading out for a good meal (my recommendation - breakfast) in the "country". It is a little stretch from Nashville, but not a bad drive.

The food: this is just a good meal. The portion sizes on some plates may make you want more, but you do get fed. You WILL wait a while to be seated. Come prepared. They do have a little shop off to the left to keep you occupied while you wait.

Prices: for the amount of food you get, I do find the prices a tad more than they should be, however, if you have as many customers as Loveless does, why not charge more? They are obviously getting it!

Bottom line: Go, you like it, and it's like going to a more local and homemade cracker barrel. Great biscuits and jam!

I went to the City Winery during my one day Nashville whirlwind. I went into town for the glaad concert for Love and Acceptance to see Meghan Linsey. 

As others have said parking is pretty impossible unless you do valet - which is $5. Don't try to park in the adjacent lot unless you want to be stopped by security in a golf cart.

Since I had a ViP ticket, I was escorted to my seat. I don't know if the tables are always that close together, but I am on the lower end of a "normal" weight range and I felt like it was a tight squeeze. Not just on each side but even scooting my chair out. The person at the table behind me could not have pulled his chair out simultaneously with me. We were that close.

The bathrooms were okay. They ran out of paper towels and they stayed out through the evening.

The wine list is not as impressive as the name would lead you to believe. No Moscato anywhere on the list if you can believe that... Not even available by the bottle. I am such a Moscato fanatic (my dog is named after it if that gives you any indication), I would have bought a whole bottle despite being a two drink max girl. But alas it was not meant to be.

I wound up getting a burger with those truffle fingerlings with some Chardonnay (sweet, but moscato you were not). 

The food was... Ok.

I hadn't eaten all day. All I had had was caffeine. Caffeine and adrenaline. And somehow I didn't even manage to eat half the burger. I don't know...

And I love truffle oil. Truly do. On fries. Tater tots. Grilled cheese. You name it. But, I found these needed salt and some (gasp!) ketchup to go with as they lacked seasoning. 

Service during the show was good. And quiet. She literally managed to get me my bill without me noticing she had placed it down.

I also love the water at the table - reminds me of Bailey's Chocolate Bar in St Louis. It also saves the waiters time.

But after the concert, the service was not so nice. A hostess came up to me to ask me where I got where I was wearing. She said another hostess absolutely loved it. I told her it wasn't a dress but a top and skirt but that only the petticoat was still available. She huffed off. Told the other hostess and not so nice commentary ensued after as if they didn't believe me when I said it was no longer available - it sold out circa 2013... Not making it up.

The same girl didn't recognize Jamie O Neal later and it wasn't until someone informed her of who it was that she let them up the stairs... Whoopsies! 

They were quick getting my car out from the valet too.

We really enjoyed this place!  When you're headed there, you're going to swear you took a wrong turn, but just keep going - trust me, you'll get there if you follow Apple Maps or Google Maps.

So their biscuits are really almost as good as everyone says they are.  We got some to go, with some of their preserves, and it was great!  As for their food, it was also really good!  I went with the Country Fried Steak with Mac & Cheese and Mashed Potatoes, and thought that everything was generally really good.  Definitely not the absolute best I've ever had, but more than worth it.

My wife had the Fried Chicken, and it was also good, but same report from her - good, but not the best she's ever had.

We also hit up the Country Store while we were waiting (be prepared to wait, btw), and bought several things, including some preserves to take home.  That was nice, because their Strawberry Jam is really freaking good.  Like, maybe some of the best I've ever had.  So good, that I really want to have it with a PB&J, but don't want to run the risk of wasting it on a sandwich where it might be overshadowed.

We also ended up with a free pound of their peppered bacon, which we ended up giving to my sister.  She cooked it up several days later, and said it was some of the best bacon she's ever had.

So, I'd recommend coming here, if nothing else, for the biscuits, preserves, and the experience; you won't be disappointed!

I love going to City Winery when one of my favorite alternative musicians comes to town. My husband and I recently saw Eric Hutchinson and AJ Croce. We purchased our tickets early online and got seats at one of the tables closest to the stage each time. What a treat to be so close to the artist while they're performing! I haven't tried the food. I'm grateful to live in Music City where I can enjoy incredible talent throughout the year!

Fried chicken that was done perfectly. Turnip greens and grits!  Peanut butter pie!!! Tooo good!! Absolutely deserves the longstanding reputation of great food...oh I almost forgot...butter my butt and call me a biscuit.
Great homestyle cooking. Can't go wrong with a place that gives out biscuits and preserves while you peruse the menu.
Biscuits and jam are awesome. My favorite part! I've been here lots of times with my boyfriend, which he loves it as well. Service is always great!!! And I leave happy and full each time!!

YUM!! So good! I went last Saturday and had the "Blue Plate Special" , which was a half smoked Honey Fire Barbecue chicken. It was SOO yummy!! Great homemade biscuits with yummy jam! 4 stars instead of 5 due to an hour wait and soggy fried green tomatoes. All the other sides were great and the corn my niece got was the best corn any of us had ever tasted!

Food was excellent. I ordered a country fried steak and it was massive. Biscuits are fresh and fluffy. Staff is super friendly. Only negative was we had to wait over an hour to be seated but there are some shops to walk around in and cornhole to play.

Drove 20 miles from my hotel to eat here and would do it again.  The chicken was crispy and moist but not greasy.  The collards were excellent, grits cheesy and tasted great.  Service was excellent.  I'd make the drive again.
Very good staff.  Food was good, well seasoned vegetables.  I would eat here again.

We were visiting Nashville and some family who came last year said we had to check this place out. Its a 20 minute drive out of the city, but it's a beautiful drive. We waited for maybe ten minutes to sit down on a Monday morning, not a big deal at all for such a popular place.

Our waiter was a gentleman named Mark, and I hope the owner reads this, he was the most genuinely nice person we met in Nashville. He answered the few questions we had about the menu and offered his recommendations. He really did a fantastic job of making us feel welcome.

The biscuits were great, the blackberry jam was amazing!

I ordered the country fried steak and eggs with a side of the hashbrown casserole. Everything was really good, portions are huge. The casserole was AMAZING! So good!

My wife ordered the bbq pork omelet. I had to taste it, and the pork is delicious. I can only imagine how good it is on their dinner menu.

After we ate, we went through their gift shops and got some recommendations from the staff on areas to check out while we were in town. Again, very friendly and helpful employees! 

I will definitely come back when I find myself in Nashville again!

Entertainment is an A+ ...they like to get everyone standing on the benches having a good time. Rouladen was a disappointment because it was more like a cylinder shaped meatloaf instead of rolled meat as in the traditional way.  They also wouldn't substitute side items which didn't seem reasonable. Service was a little slow during this visit too.
Dont expect 'Southern Comfort' if you are a party of 8.  It took them 1 hour to seat us.  It was a Thursday at noon.
We met friends here for dinner, wine and an Ambrosia concert. Full of song writers and who knows who. Great food and fun! We will be back!

Dined at the cafe and the food was excellent and it had a very friendly service staff, hosts and hostesses. Our part of three arrived at 12:20pm on a Thursday and we were seated with no wait on their covered outdoor patio. They are famous for their biscuits and I quickly understood why. Hot and fresh served with homemade jams and preserves they are clearly the best I've had. I had a sampler of catfish, meatloaf and pulled pork bbq with fried okra and hashbrown casserole. I also tried a taste of my wife's grilled pork chops with peach preserves and my son's breakfast pork sausage, bacon and country ham which were all exceptional. My favorite was their pulled pork and I have had many through the years and it is surely now near the very top of my list. Also specifically our waiter Lucas was friendly, attentive and anticipated our every request. I cannot say one single negative thing.

What a great atmosphere! The fried chicken was not the best I have ever had but it was good... The biscuits were for sure the best thing about this place! I ate five of them before our meal was served...

The food was amazing, the decorations are very neat. Service was quick and efficient. The only complaint was that my $21 Jägerschnitzel was the same size as the schnitzel on my wife's $12 sandwich. The only difference was she had a bun and mine didn't. That's only a minor complaint. Like I said, food was amazing, fast and fresh!

**edit** I had to edit the price for the Jägerschnitzel, the menu listed it as $19, but once we got the check it was listed as $21

First, the good:   We loved the atmosphere.  It is open and airy.  There is plenty of seating.  We are fans of eating in the bar area of a restaurant and were happy to have had that option.  The service was great.  Our server, Joey, was excellent.  He was stationed behind the bar.  He gave us a few moments to check out the drinks menu before coming to take our drink order.  Personally, I am not a beer person (hubby is) and I asked about ciders and he pointed out two that were available.  Hubby ordered the "Munich Hell"and I got the "currant rose cider." We we're both happy with our selections. 

The rest:   We ordered the giant pretzel and beer cheese based on Yelp reviews.  Save your money.  For $12 we received an obviously previously frozen pretzel and a very basic cheese dip (with no hint of beer).  It might have been better if the pretzel was at least hot....it was barely warm and I definitely felt some cold  spots.  It was what I would equate with store-bought frozen pretzels.

Our entrees:  hubby ordered the jagerschnitzel with spatzle and I ordered the pork schnitzel with fries.   I was concerned that my schnitzel came out with a small plastic pick indicating that it was "rare."  Rare pork concerns me to a great extent, but it was actually cooked nicely.  It was tender juicy.  My main complaints were 1) the pork should have been seasoned before breading; 2) something should have been done to make sure the breading stayed on the pork; and 3) the schnitzel should have been drained better before service, because of the oily flavor.  Also, I would have liked the fries much crisper.  

Hubby ate all of the jagerschnitzel but did comment that it tasted like it had been fried earlier and then reheated, again another indication of old oil.  Also, the spatzle looked like the same spatzle I buy from GFS.  

Final thoughts:  we may be back.  I would like to give this place another chance.  Perhaps trying the sausages and potato pancakes.  Overall, the food is what I would expect of typical mall/chain food.  It was definitely not worth the $99 we paid (including tip).

One of the most hyped restaurants in the USA but it definitely lives up to it! The biscuits are incredible and I can never decide which preserve (strawberry, blackberry, peach) is my favorite. Fried green tomatoes are crisp and tangy. Meatloaf is nice and juicy, perfectly accompanied by BBQ sauce. Fried chicken is tender and succulent. Banana pudding is creamy and smooth. Southern deliciousness!! Explore the grounds and shops while you wait for your table because chances are good that you'll wait an hour or two (or more), especially on weekends.
Cool place, great service, but the food is just good southern style food. Its very similar to almost all small town diners. But the atmosphere makes it a must see place!

The staff here is horrible.  We bought $75 VIP upgrades to our already $35 ticket a piece x 3.  I have two friends who drove from Michigan.  We are being treated horribly.  I'm a Vino VIP member and have never been treated this bad.

Let me tell you a little something about Loveless Cafe, y'all. A friend and I decided to ride our bikes there one day from West End. 13 miles. Bad Idea. 5 hours later when we got there, and the biscuits finally came, they literally saved my life. I owe those biscuits MY LIFE, I tell you. If you are gonna do Loveless, just forget about the calories and order the Fried Chicken with all the fixins (or you could burn it off with a bike ride). Also, try your darndest to save room for Steeplechase pie. To Die For. The wait can be long, so go at a weird time and you should be ok. Otherwise plan on waiting at least an hour. Luckily there are little shops in the same complex to keep you busy. A must visit in Nashville!

50 minute wait but well worth it plenty to see and do while you wait. 
had southern sampler breakfast plate. Country ham bacon and sausage were good but not the best I'd ever had. Browning's Country Ham in Kentucky has better tasting  
Eggs hash brown casserole and biscuits and jam were awesome. 
Pancakes were excellent. 
Friends got omletes and were happy with them.

Our time at Loveless Cafe started out with a bit of a hiccup.  I thought I had reserved us a table for a Saturday and when we arrived I was informed I'd made the reservation for Monday and the wait was going to be an hour and twenty minutes.  I take full responsibility for my screw up but I was really hungry and really upset with myself.  Fortunately, there are a few quaint shops on the premises where I was able to get a GooGoo Cluster and root beer and forget that I was starving and also managed to buy lots of cute kitchen decorations, preserves, even a pair of earrings.  Our wait ended up being around 50 minutes (thank you so much for your hustle or whoever ate their food quickly, my stomach and girlfriend are forever grateful).  Once seated we were greeted by the sweetest server who took care of us like a pro.  She got our sweet teas (a must), and a plate of the most divine, buttery biscuits and preserves you could ever dream of to nosh on while we waited for our lunch.  I had the fried chicken tenders, hashbrown casserole, and macaroni and cheese.  My girlfriend had the chicken fried steak, fried green tomatoes, and cucumbers and onions.  Everything was exceptional, well seasoned, and just downright delicious.  Plan to take home leftovers as the portions are huge.  I took home enough to make an entire second meal.  Despite being absolutely stuffed we decided it would be a sacrilege to leave without pie and we were absolutely right.  A slice of coconut cream pie and peanut butter pie was the perfect ending to a perfect meal.  

If you're staying in downtown Nashville, allow yourself about 30 minutes to get to the cafe but it is worth the drive and then some.

Went to see Steve Earle and Elizabeth Cook last night. The show was great and the food was fine. It's expensive but that's what I expected. They advertized an after show in the upstairs lounge that sounded nice. Go up after the show, have another drink, and listen to a fine local artist. What I didn't expect is that the after show was another $12!!! I had just dropped close to $200 on the main show and dinner and I just didn't expect to get charged again for basically another ticket. Sure, the guy's upstairs deserve to be paid, but I would think the establishment could cover a guarantee for that plus put out a tip jar. It just sort of cemented in my mind that the City Winery is about taking money from its patrons any way they can. I'll go back and in fact I have tickets for another Steve Earle show in a couple of weeks. It's a nice, comfortable, upscale venue but I'll be keeping my hand on my wallet.

Dess styrka av att vara både en restaurang och en konsertlokal är tyvärr också dessa svaghet. Den gör båda sysslorna lite halvdant, och ingendera helt bra. Börjar med min (hittills) endaste besök här. Insläpp två timmar före musik showen börjar, ljusen i den stora lokalen är så neddimmade så att det är omöjligt att läsa menyerna, ens för de med perfekt syn. Resultatet blir att alla som vill beställa något tvingas lysa upp menyn med sina mobiltelefoner, en del genom att tända foto led belysningen. Andra tvingas ta hjälp utav serveringspersonalen som får ta fram sina mobiler och fungera som ambulerande ficklampa. Rätt komiskt! Jag kan förstå att under föreställningen vill man ha nedsläckt för att framhäva artisterna på scenen, men det här är timmar innan uppträdandet, när dessutom ingenting pågår på scen (allt är färdig riggat och sound checkat). 

När jag och andra här beställer öl så får vi varsin ölflaska men inget glas att hälla upp den i och dricka ur. Och det här är definitivt ingen billig honky-tonk sylta utan en restaurang med $20 varmrätter och $10 öl (en hygglig ansenlig summa här). Ber man om ett glas för sin öl så bär de gärna fram ett. Borde kanske vara standardutrustning?

Den förstärkta ljudanläggningen här verkar vara av fast karaktär som är permanent uppriggad och inkopplad för alla artister. Det sparar visserligen både tid, besvär och pengar men betyder också att du som ensam trubadur här får ungefär samma ljudbild som en hård rockade heavy metal band. Kompromiss är inte alltid optimalt! Kvällen då jag var här var mycket tung blues-rock gung ifrån scenen (Leon Russell). Men ljudet var, om inte direkt dåligt, så iallafall underdimensionerat för musik typen.

På plussidan så påminner man här, på flera ställen, om att man som gäst inte skall prata under föreställningen av respekt mot både artisterna på scen och sina bordsgrannar. Det budskapet applåderar jag!

Great bbq, fried chicken, and biscuits. Got a smoking education from the pit master. He suggested the smoked pork chops and they were awsome. I found I new favorite. Keep the good food coming loveless.

This place is amazing! 

I will preface with I suffer from a peanut & tree nut allergy. I called the restaurant to see if they would be able to accommodate this and the hostess said they could not. She said nothing in the kitchen would be safe since there is a chance of cross contamination. She then said the fried chicken would be safe since it only gets put in the fryer and they cook with soy oil. I still took the chance and went since this was one of the things I was looking forward to on my trip & boy am I happy I went! I spoke to the waiter and he said everything was pretty safe to eat. The biscuits, fried chicken and sides were definitely nut free and were safe to eat. I ordered the fried chicken (amazing!), grits with cheese (hands down the best thing I ate during my trip) and mac & cheese (so-so, I wish I ordered the mashed potatoes instead!). The biscuits are everything I hoped they would be - they were fresh, soft and oh-so-buttery! I would suggest asking for another plate of biscuits before your meal is over so you can take them home for the next day. 


I regretted not purchasing the biscuit mix the next day, but was luckily able to purchase it at the airport before leaving. 

Anyone visiting Nashville must go to the Loveless Cafe during their visit!!

Went to the Loveless Cafe on a recommendation from a local friend as one of their families favorites. Of coarse I first still checked yelp for reviews prior to goin,g so I knew I was in for a wait, which was helpful. It took 45 minutes to be seated at 8 pm on a Monday night.  The drive to it was very scenic and the gift shops kept us happily occupied.  Once seated though our fabulous waiter named Owen promptly took our drink orders and brought my party of 5 an enormous plate of the famous biscuits and jellies. I thought we would never eat all of them but within a few moments time Owen said, " I did bring you a plate of biscuits didn't I?" with a warm smile on his face.  We each ordered different meals and not one was disappointed with their choice! As we sampled each other's side items....the cheese grits and Mac and cheese were big hits.  Not only was the food scrumptious but the hospitality of our awesome waiter (Owen) mixed with the cozy environment made it a night to remember! It will be a definite stop for us next time in Nashville.

I am absolutely in love with everything about Loveless Cafe. It is one of the most popular Southern breakfast diners in the U.S, and it doesn't surprise me one bit that it made that list. 

  It is pretty out of the way from downtown and other tourist attractions in Nashville, but I think that adds even more to it's hometown - type background.So in other words, expect a 20 minute drive out, but it is totally worth it.

  The restaurant looks like the inside of your grandmother's house. You can also tell that their staff know how to treat their customers with true Southern hospitality. 

   They've got a huuuge selection on their menu, it was so tough for me to decide what to order. Everyone gets free biscuits, which were perfect and fluffy, also given a choice of four types of jelly. I went for the Southern Sampler breakfast, which seemed to be like a bit of everything. 

   With my meal including ham, eggs, sausage, bacon, AND fried potatoes, you can guess that I didn't leave there hungry. The portion size was overwhelming! But everything was delicious, especially to someone like me who normally doesn't care much for breakfast food. 

  Anybody and everybody has to experience this cafe at some point in their life.

Shawn at the bar was extremely cool. The Reuben was probably the most amazing sandwich ever created. Every bite was better than the last, it was just perfect. My wife and I would probably drive from Chicago, just for that! The atmosphere was authentic German and the place was packed, so the food quality is apparently not a secret. I'm hoping I can find a sandwich of that caliber in Chicago, though I won't get my hopes up. Thank you for being one of the best parts of our trip, we'll be back!
The best biscuits and moon shine Mary's ever. Love this place even though they are always packed and the wait is long, but that's okay, the wait is worth it and all the shops are super cute.

Come here for the experience! I've found that country food in Tennessee isn't all that different from what we have in Texas, with the exception of never hearing of "hot chicken." Either way, Loveless has all the awesome breakfast offerings, even becoming a bit overwhelming! 

I stuck with the chicken and waffles and it was just fine. The order comes with a bunch of syrup on the side so you can add it to your liking. 

What did stick with me - their drinks! The "Blue Moon" isn't the beer... instead it's all sorts of goodness with blueberries, lemonade, and a souvenir mini mason jar with mason jar, also so you can add it to your liking. Since I was planning on taking the souvenir with me, I went ahead and dumped all of the moonshine given to me, only to later find out that they give you a lid for it. 

We had two servers for 30+ people and they did a superb job getting everybody's orders right and getting control of such a large group. 

When you're done eating, step out to their many little stores for some shopping! I snagged a gift for my niece's birthday and Olive & Sinclair chocolate bars for everyone else who can't fit in a 12 month old onesie.

Fun idea but flops. Benches uncomfortable, benches too far away from the table and had to wait for beer flights for a ridiculous amount of time. The server did a good job but I think he was overextended. He was very polite and helpful. It is what you would expect from a German restaurant as far as the food goes. Also a very loud restaurant!

Cheap drinks and quick bites, I happened to see a fantastic band whose guitarist was playing mad notes on his Tele.  Awesome band!  
Definitely a dive but good service from the bar.  Small and dark, don't be intimidated.  Dirty, stinky, sticky...yeah that is true but it's a fun place.  The bathroom walls have no lack of jokes about you manhood, so don't take it personally!
Cool place to unwind and get started hitting the rest of the scene. Let your hair down, just don't take off your shoes.

Amazing food and service, and the beers were great we had two flights! The Schnitzel -that was amazing and the noodles were some of the best I've ever had! The Pretzel was delicious and huge, of the newly addicted to the Apple mustard.  The only reason they got 4 out of 5 stars is that the children's meal was really not good at all pigs in a blanket... I tasted it and it was really greasy. I kind of like that kind of thing so I was really expecting to be wowed by something new on the kids menu! Ah well... overall, for me it's the best pick of our three weeks on the road.  I really wanted to go back and get some of that Dunkel beer or whatever that was :-) try it if you can figure out what it is!
Very good and great service.The food wasn't bad we had a sampler plate. Some was great some wasn't

So after a week in the smoky mountains getting fat, happy and not so fulfulled on southern cooking I find myself a loveless on the way home. 

One of the top 2 meals I have eaten in the last week. The deference in quality from the places in the smokies was apparent from the first bite. 

I ordered the breakfast sampler and a bowl of gravy. Three meats two eggs and a bowl of hash brown casserole. Oh don't forget the unlimited biscuits. I didn't. As I tried to single handedly eat them out of biscuits this night. Between smothering them with gravy or lathering them up with butter and jellies. Yum Yum 

All the food was great. It's hard to do great breakfast and this place does it. Most place breakfast is good and the is it. I am so glad I got a top notch breakfast before heading home from vacation. The one thing I would pass on next time is the Banana Pudding...got some to go but it was just okay. 

Oh and can I have another plate of biscuits....some of the best you will ever have.
Horribly slow service (40 min to get appetizers, then another 20 for entrees!, it wasn't a busy night too). Ambience was nice but no live music. Waiter was friendly. Food was OK, nothing special.

Of course you have to eat at Loveless while in Nashville, it's an icon. The fried chicken is unfortunately a tad dry...but, the biscuits, jams, fried green tomatoes, and desserts more than make up for that offense. I highly recommend the fried green tomatoes (crunchy, salty, and delicious), the homemade peach pie (with spiced peaches for the win), and biscuits with sorghum.

Loveless cafe was a special stop today! The property is so cute, with a gift shop, antique store, art store, and bean bag tossing pits in addition to the actual restaurant itself. I can see why loveless is so popular! Great staff and authentic southern vibe going on. Had the chicken and biscuit side for breakfast, it was delicious but tiny (I ordered another!) Lots of southern sides and dishes! Yum.

I've been here a couple of times and the food is consistently good, but it is definitely not worth a long wait if there is one.  We only had to wait 20 minutes, but it was on Thursday at 1pm.  It's your typically southern fair menu.  The quality of the food is good the jams are excellent, but biscuits are nothing extraordinary.  My fiancé had the Southern omelette.  It was packed full of country ham, cheese, and veggies.  His daughter had a waffle with chocolate chips and bacon.  I had a bite of her bacon which was really good.  I had the fried chicken with green beans and mash potatoes.  The fried chicken wasn't greasy and was moist.  The sides are good, but nothing special.  The portions are big, so come hungry or dishes can be easily shared.

Every time I come here always get great customer service food always good it is a must if you like good country food come hungry the portions are plentiful biscuit light & fluffy it's like no other in Nashville been here many times & will be here many many many more thanks

If you follow me on Instagram, you already know how I feel about this place. 30 minute drive and a 90 minute wait, but it was worth it. Man was it worth it. 

So Loveless Cafe is surrounded by a handful of little Loveless shops that well a variety of items such as jams, preserves, bacon, trinkets, tourist souvenirs and clothing. I bought a rather awesome "Taking Care of Biscuits" t shirt but one wash turned the large into a Small, so I actually never got to wear it. I'll frame it and hang it on the wall or something. 

We perused the shops and enjoyed looking at their paintings and souvenirs (mini mason jars are just the darnedest cutest things) and my friend bought a canvas painting of a rather happy looking pig. We named him Wilbur Darnell. Don't ask. 

But the food. Ohhhhhhh man the food. So the policy is that as long as you stay on the first round (it's all you can eat), you're allowed to take the leftovers home. But once you order seconds of Anything, you are not allowed to take anything from the table home. Luckily, we never even made it out of the first round. Just look at my photo. Hilariously huge spread.

But I want to talk about the biscuits. These biscuits make you question your life, the world, the Galaxy and Mother Nature herself. You question religion and the science behind it. You question your upbringing and the girl you decided was worthy of your first kiss. That's how magical these biscuits are. 

Small, fluffy, chewy, yet airy and buttery (you must butter it--it's phenomenal), these are worth the hype and the rave reviews. Served with four preserves (the blackberry was my personal favorite), you must always order more. 

The fried chicken. Best. Skillet. Fried. Chicken. Ever. Skillet fried chicken is something every single one of you (even you strange vegan and vegetarian folk) need to try at least once in your life because you will be shocked at just how different it is from regular deep fried. Juicy while maintaining the crisp skin, Loveless has it going on. 

The pulled pork with corn cakes. Okay the portion was absurd. We each had two helpings and it looked as if a family of six could've enjoyed it afterwards. Needless to say we took it home and enjoyed some delicious leftovers.  Man was the pork great. Tender, sweet and tangy, with a hint of smoke, it was a favorite of ours. 

The fried okra was delicious (god I love fried okra), but it could've used a pinch of salt after frying as it was a bit bland. 

Fried green tomatoes. Best I had the entire week.

Mashed potatoes were excellent as was the gravy that accompanied them. 

I can't stop thinking about the biscuits. I haven't stopped since I left the place. To the wonderful staff, thank you so much for the lovely experience and meal! I'm sorry I can't wear the shirt!

It's a dive bar that has it all; no cover, cheap drinks and great live music.  I stopped here on Memorial day weekend with some friends and it was our favorite bar in Nashville.  We would definitely recommend if you're looking for a good time without emptying your wallet.

Truly as good as it gets when is comes to home cooked country food! At our table of 3 we had, Meatloaf, Ham, Pulled Pork, Squash Casserole, Hash-brown Casserole, Mac N Cheese, Banana Pudding, Cherry Pie, Peach Cobbler, and a plethora of Sweet Tea and Biscuits! There was not one thing that was mediocre. Everything was hot, fresh and flavorful. And I would personally like to give a shot out to Ms. Barbara who made sure that we had all our left-overs to go and a few extra biscuits for the road! I cant say enough good things about the Loveless Cafe!

I had the chance to go to City Winery in Nashville for an event, and I absolutely fell in love with the atmosphere. The service was excellent and the servers were careful not to interrupt during the event. 

I had the Margherita flatbread and the Cabernet Sauvignon and was not disappointed. I can be picky about my wines, but this was excellent. It was a little pricey, but I kind of expected that with this nice of a venue!

I really hope to attend events here in the future and try some other items on the menu!
Awesome wines. Great small plate. The dinners are tiny and just ok. Dessert was awful. Really expensive for what you get. Felt like NYC. Really??
Had lunch there today.  The service was a bit slow but the food was excellent.  Lunch is easy to get in and out of because it is quiet and not many customers.

I ate decent breakfast here.  The biscuits are a signature dish, but I didn't think they were very special.  They were not flaky or interesting.  Had the texture of a dinner roll with the shape of a store bought biscuit.  Adequate, but I expected more and was told by my airbnb host that it was better years ago.  I really liked the country fried steak.  Very tasty with the sauce and very crispy.  Best part of my breakfast.  I also had eggs and potato casserole.
Best fried chicken ever! Be ready to unleash your inner fat girl if you eat here! Everyone is super nice and wants to feed you! Beware of the biscuits! They are like crack on steroids! Soo good!

This was a fun restaurant and a good introduction for my students for German style foods. The service was ok. Portions were fine and everything came to order. Prices were high IMO, but it may be due to location. That's the reason I rated this place a 3, that and the servers were uninformed about the specials.

Recently moved to Nashville and one of my friends told me about seven times in the first week we needed to visit Loveless ASAP (no exaggeration). We showed up at 3:15pm on a Sunday afternoon and couldn't believe there was a 45 minute wait for two people. And supposedly the wait is usually two hours long so we were "lucky" (okay we can roll with it. Good thing there were a few shops on their property to waste some time so we walked over there. My bf bought two jars of preserves for his family (on recommendation from said friend) even though we hadn't actually tried anything yet. Im so sad now that we didn't get a few jars for ourselves! 

The wait seemed to be over pretty quickly and we sat down to our late lunch. We got our first plate of biscuits and they were AMAZING!! There was a sampler of preserves to try out: blackberry, peach and strawberry. My favorite was blackberry and his was strawberry. They were all so good that there really was no way to rank them higher than the other. 

I ordered the fried chicken livers with the sweet yams and corn. He ordered the pork chops, hash brown casserole and corn. Our meals came out piping hot and I actually had to wait a second to eat because it was so hot (something I really appreciate --hot food is the best!). We also got the banana pudding even though we were so full. Took the dessert home but took one bite first and it's some of the best banana pudding I've ever had. The vanilla wafer is obviously homemade and has such a nice crisp to it. The service was fantastic and we'll be bringing our family back here when they visit us for the first time in the city. 

Highly recommend. Wait is worth it. Buy some preserves for yourself and some holiday gift goodies when you're here. We know it's a down home southern cooking restaurant but you really can't go wrong when they're stellar at their job. Can't wait to come back!!

We were lucky to walk in tonight and have no wait as this is a well loved restaurant. You get biscuits when you arrive, essentially, served with their outstanding jams. We liked the blackberry and strawberry best. The biscuits live up to their reputation that's for sure. We ordered and our meals arrived very soon thereafter and the service was professional, helpful, and pleasant. My mom ordered the watermelon ribs which is the Thursday night special. The meat was falling off the bone, juicy, satisfying flavor as they should be. My sister had the fried half chicken and thought it was good. I had the grilled catfish which was pretty flavorful if a little wet. The hush puppies that came with it were excellent with just the right sweetness and flavor. I ordered fried okra as a side, which was a mistake but what can you expect from okra I guess? My sister and I both ordered the caramel sweet potatoes which were as advertised - very sweet but good. My sister's second side was the turnip greens and they were a little more spicy then expected. My mom's two sides were definite hits with the beans - flat and green beans - my sister did get some grit twice while trying these though. The creamed corn my mom got was so tasty. We finished it off with the peach cobbler which did not disappoint. Made with peaches that were frozen when they were fresh a dumpling and good French vanilla ice cream. We were pretty impressed!

Me & my husband were driving past Nashville & checked out this place. Yes it is a bit of a drive from the interstate & yes there was a long 1 1/2 hr wait but the wait staff were super friendly & the biscuits oh yea made the trip & wait worth it. I'm not into biscuits as much as my husband but let me tell u I ate 3! All with butter & their strawberry, blueberry & peach jams all delicious! Next I had the blue berry moonshine & it comes with a shoot keep sake that the moonshine comes in. Boy my first time having some I would say don't throw it all in cuz that stuff is strong but good. We couldn't decide so we had the sampler platter with fried chicken, meatloaf & ham. All were great but ham was a little salty then I would of liked. The hashbrown casserole & Mac & cheese were on point! This is must stop!

My Loveless experience was more love than less. True to all other high regarded reviews, I do actually have nothing but love for this roadside joint. It boasts some tall orders like homemade banana pudding, biscuits, and pretty much if it's on the menu it's made from scratch. Places just don't do that anymore. Not like this and not for these prices. All my respect to places that can manage good food on a budget and more. With that said, I enjoyed everything I ate. Was it the best ever? Probably not .... But it was most definitely solid hand made fare that for Nashville, is a force to be reckoned with. There are a LOT of southern fare joints we discovered in Nashville. The Loveless Cafe is a must visit. There is no negotiating this. Oh and yes....even with that crazy long wait. All you foodies must know by now, the longer the wait .... It must be worth it.

Want commissary food that is the same as any truck stop on the interstate? Welcome to the Loveless.  The tourists come because of a reputation left over from the fifties. Pull over, have your picture taken out front, then go get something good to eat elsewhere.
This is really great food. If you come here you have to try the hashbrown casserole! It is the most amazing version you will ever find in a restaurant.

This company is taking customer service seriously, that is important to me! Please consider giving them a chance. I will be giving them another chance since they have graciously offered me the opportunity as a result of my dissatisfaction with my dinner. A real commitment to customer service is an amazing thing to find in a multi-state company but looks like City Winery is making the extra effort to get it right! I debated about three or four stars but decided the music/listening space gave this place the extra boost. Great space, fun concert and amazing (amazing) sound My waiter could have done better and the food was not above average but I am giving them a second chance! You should go - some amazing concerts are planned! Oh and $5 for valet is so reasonable in this town!

Loveless was such a fun experience! We went on a Friday, so it was not busy at all. There was a small wait, but the shops and grounds made the wait go fast. Walking around was quite enjoyable. There were plenty of vegetarian options. The pimento green tomato biscuit was the best. I ordered the cheese omelet as well, which was not great. I rectified that by making my own biscuit sandwiches with the endless biscuits we kept getting. The biscuits and jams alone I would give it a 5 star! My fiancée loved the bbq - he said to pass on the ham. My only regret is not going back while we were in town.

Great country breakfast.  We ate here twice while in Nashville last week.  The first morning, I had the fried eggs, ham and red gravy, which is more like aus jus where I come from.  It came with hash brown casserole that was quite tasty.  The biscuits and homemade preserves were divine.  Overall a very good breakfast.  The second visit, I had the port BBQ and eggs and my friend had the country fried pork chops and eggs.  The highlight was the country fried pork chops!  The BBQ pork was delish as well.
The service and atmosphere are great. The prices are reasonable. The food could use more seasoning. We had the pork shank and the schnitzel, they were both bland. Not much taste....

Hands down the best restaurant for Southern food for me! I am not actually a big fan of southern food, but I enjoyed every bit of experience at Loveless cafe. The friends that came with me that night came from different states in the country and they all enjoyed everything they ordered. But one thing stood out: their BISCUITS! The biscuits were so fluffy, buttery in a good way and melt-in-your-mouth soft! The different preserves on the table were so good but I love the blackberry the best. You could just have as many biscuits you like and I think I had more than 10 on top of my big meal (the servicing size is huge too!). I just can't stop eating their biscuits, it was that good! To add to the wonderful dining experience, the servers were very friendly and they have a store where you could buy their biscuit mix and homemade preserves/jams. A definite must-try in Nashville!

I mean, come on, what can I say that everyone else hasn't said?

Yes, their biscuits are pretty rad.
Yes, I have had better country cooking (hailing from Alabama, and all).
Yes, the staff is very friendly...especially for being crazy slammed all day long every day.
Yes, I only go here for special occasions (i.e. Out of town guests).

We drove over from Nashville (30min each way) and there was a 75 min wait, which was super accurate. There are all kinds of things to do and see on the grounds, though, so it made the wait go by quickly. The food was great (worth the wait); I had the jumbo chicken fingers, the meatloaf was amazing; my favorite was the green beans, brown gravy and definitely the biscuits!

Why LoveLESS? This place should be called loveMORE! Hands down the fluffiest biscuits I've had in life! And the waitress was very generous about  bringing out a second hot basket before we even finished our first.
