Though I wondered what did she do with the leftover buscuits that she took away with the first basket? o.O

The fried chicken was executed to perfection. You can tell the recipe has gone through decades of tradition and years of perfection. The chicken however  lacked a bit of seasoning. Good stuff but I've also had better. 

I was somewhat disappointed by the hash brown casserole, especially after reading raving reviews about it as I was waiting for our table. The proportion of cheese to potatoes was nearly 50/50.

The location is a little out of reach, but definitely worth a short drive if you are in town.

My dad visited here a few years back and loved the food.  He was so impressed he got me a care package shipped just so I could try some of it.  Their black pepper bacon was really good, not overly peppery and a good smoke on it was a perfect combination.  Their jelly was also good, sweet but not overly sweet.  The blackberry was our favorite.  We are suppose to be moving to Tennessee in the next year, so this place is definitely on our list of places to visit once we do!

Don't waste your time trekking out to this little club off the beaten path in Nashville.  Aside from the clean bathroom, there wasn't much else I liked about this place.  The bartender was rude in ignoring people while chatting with his friends at the bar and what appeared drinking on the job.  Pretty unprofessional.

Music wise, maybe I hit it on an off night but there couldn't have been a bigger mish mash of conflicting acts and sounds.  Clearly they need to look into a new booking agent.

Overall I've had much better experiences elsewhere in Nashville.

I've been eating at Loveless Cafe since 1978. The current owner is acclaimed, well known caterer, multi-restaurant owner & Madison, TN native. Unfortunately Loveless is very poorly managed & the ladies handling front & phone are rude, frustrating & not knowledgable about how "call ahead seating" works at every other successful restaurant in the USA. If you call ahead & are given a range of times to show up you will learn that they were lying to you & your name doesn't even go on the waiting list UNTIL you get there! Then you wait another 45min - hour & a half to even sit down. Ours was not a single, isolated experience & we live just 3 miles from Loveless. Ray Danner would be ashamed of how far from his training Mr. Morales has allowed his crown jewel to go.

The food will be served hot, most often by well trained servers who are ALWAYS over worked, have to bus their own tables & run back for the simplest of request. Loveless needs to hire back waiters to support the fine front waiters that work very hard to provide the guest with a great experience. 

The red eye gravy is good & standard Southern style while the white sausage or chicken gravy lacks much & should be reworked using the recipe of any Nashville Grandmother. The meats are very good & the fried chicken well prepared. All egg dishes will be enjoyed. The biscuits are certainly not the same recipe as the McCabe family used in the 70's & 80's when a Senior White Southern Lady made them from scratch but the current owners lead all to believe they bought the historic recipe & process...NOT, but most guests will be delighted by the taste & never know what they are missing unless they grew up in the South eating Gold Medal Flour made from scratch biscuits.

Final words, when you visit ask to sit in the dining room to the left of the front counter. That room is original & where the true Loveless past still reigns supreme! Finish with a piece of one of the exceptional pies.

Yelp demographics says I asked for directions but I didn't. Just wanted to see if any other long-time Loveless customers were having the same experiences my family has for the last 7 years. 

E.P. - Nashville
Madison, TN Native

Can't say enough how delicious this place is!!!! If you love biscuits then this has to be a stop on your way through Nashville. We went on a Monday night and there was a small wait but it was well worth it! The best fried chicken I have ever had not to be out done by the amazing BBQ pork and fried catfish. Our waiter was extremely friendly and made the experience even better. Truly like having dinner at grandma's!!!
This is a great place to visit. Plan on at least an hour wait. Their biscuits are made on site. Jams are delicious. I preferred the peach.

The service was amazing! The biscuits, homemade biscuits, and the hash brown casserole were all delicious. The coffee is just so so and the omelette wasn't very good. I'd definitely come back & try some other things on their menu.

So we finally made it to the Loveless Café! Definitely not disappointed. Everything was delicious. We had French toast, southern omelet, hash brown casserole, bacon and the famous biscuits with a side of gravy and homemade jam!! Everyone is so nice here too! Virginia our waitress was superb!! Do not pass this up! We can't wait to come back to try out their dinner menu!! If you like what you eat they have a store that you can buy biscuits, ham and jam!! Oh...and if you leave hungry something is wrong! Portion sizes are large so come with an empty belly! :-)

This place oozes rich history. My meal was lip-smacking delicious. Biscuits. check. Jam. Like no other. Menu. Limitless possibilities. What to eat was the hardest choice I had to make all summer. The menu has every rendition and combination of breakfast food you can think of, and some you cant. We waited for a good hour, so I had ample time to rack my brain over what to eat. In retrospect, the wait was perfect, because I have a feeling I would have gone with my gut (no pun intended) and chosen on impulse versus deliberation. I ended up choosing the smoked porch chops w/peach preserve with creamed corn and cucumbers & onion in vinegar. The porch chops were moist, the creamed corn was the best I have had next to my friends mom. I am a creamed corn fanatic. 

Like they are a marketing power house. You get there and there is a crazy wait... I was there on a Friday and we waited for about an hour. However, the location is an old trucker motel turned gift shop emporium for you to occupy your time while you wait. They put all of their jellies and jams, dishware, and merchandise into the rooms of the old motel. 

One really random downside is that the drive is like 25-30 minutes from Nashville. I was driving with my friend and we were just like really confused that possibly had the wrong address, but alas it popped up literally in the middle of nowhere.

Came here for the famous biscuits and was disappointed. The biscuits are good but do not live up to the hype. They aren't any better than chain breakfast restaurant biscuits. The jams and jellies were pretty good but didn't make up for the lackluster biscuits and other breakfast food. I wouldn't come back and I would say you can skip this place if you are visiting from out of town like me.

June 2017 - interesting place with Great Southern Cooking and Good Beer.  It's located near Hwy 100 and Natchez Trace Parkway, a wonderful way to drive to the restaurant.  Breakfast is served all
Day.

After reading some of the reviews I had a few doubts that our meal here would not be as good as some places closer to the downtown area. I was very very wrong, we had a wonderful time, waited about 15 minutes to get seated but enjoyed relaxing on the front porch until our table was ready. The portions were huge and every single thing we ate was delicious. We ate too much, and after lunch went and visited the shops around the property. Overall a need to visit if you're in the Nashville area :)

We came here because my husband was really wanting some chicken fried steak and fried green tomatoes. It was over an hour wait but we figured it was supposed to be worth the wait.. We walked around and shopped until our buzzer went off. We enjoyed the biscuits and the jams were delicious but they weren't the best biscuits I've ever had as they were a bit dense. We ordered the apple pie moonshine and it was pretty good, but definitely not worth the $11 price even with the take home shot glass. Our food came out so quickly we were shocked so we asked the waitress if it always comes out this fast and she laughed and said no we were lucky. Well, the reason it probably came out so quickly is the main dish was cold but the sides were hot so we can guess it was sitting and waiting. The flavor and texture of the chicken fried steak was just okay. The table next to us ordered fried chicken and it looked like it was probably better. The mashed potatoes were also a little disappointing because I thought they would have more flavor but were lacking. Maybe I just like rich potatoes. The Mac and cheese was pretty good as were the fried green tomatoes. Being from Texas, we have high standards for southern food and Loveless was just mediocre.

Set up is nice. Music is too loud. Waitress didn't know what kind of meat was on the burger. Enough said. The wine bottle table numbers are cool, but not cool enough. Waitress didn't check on us the entire time we ate. No courtesy stops. Food was less than average at a higher cost. Added taxes of $10 other than sales tax? Table#62 on 1/24/15 didn't meet expectations
Food was good. Pretty place. People where friendly and helpful. Only downfall was prices way too high....20$a plate was the average.

Joe was SO AMAZING. We arrived early off a flight before we could get into an air BnB for my friends bachelorette party he let us in 4 hours before hand and surprised us with cannolis. I have worked in the hospitality industry for years but he goes so above and beyond he truly is amazing at what he does. Thanks joe!

Stopped here while traveling on vacation and IMO it is one of the best restaurants you will ever encounter.
Short wait, fast service, fresh baked biscuits with toppings to enjoy while waiting for your meal in a super friendly place.
I totally enjoyed the chicken and waffles while my wife had eggs smothered in tender BBQ pulled pork, there was enough pork left to take home and make 2 sandwiches.
When your there look at the list of celebrities that have enjoyed this place.
Awesome hash brown casseole.  Great biscuits and jams.  Jadee was server and did a great job!
Food was pretty good but the music was really loud, so beware. Not quite what I was looking for. Service was good, however.

Some people may see this as sacrilege but I would say that the most exciting things about Loveless are the facilities and the drive there. The dining room is cute and very open, and there are cute stores in the campus. The food was solid and the biscuits very good, but the latter didn't live up to tall the hype is heard. The preserved on the other hand were pretty awesome. What I was most disappointed about was the service. In a place as iconic as this one I expected some good southern hospitality but it was all just rushed. I don't regret going, it was a good experience. That said, my visit was during the week. Had I waited the typical 2.5hrs on the weekend I may have been a little disappointed, only because of the hype.

Went in early afternoon on a Monday and was told the wait was 30 minutes. There are several shops to look in, and we were signaled in less than 20 minutes. My wife had the eggs with ham and the ham slice could feed 2 people. Had to bring some of it back home. I had the pimento cheeseburger with the bacon (yep, 5 slices) with fries. One of the best burgers I ever had. Oh yes, not to mention more biscuits and soda refills. I will definitely recommend this cafe to others.
The biscuits are what this place was supposedly about, but truthfully, the biscuits as Bob Evans beats Loveless hands-down. Nice place here, though.
Oh God the food here was outrageously good. Everything we tried with better than the other. Worth a half-hour Trek from downtown Nashville. They close at 9 so allow time.

Growing up in the south you know a good place to eat good food.  The biscuits were great right out of the oven with the jam.  I ordered from the breakfast menu with the country style steak and eggs.  I was a bit disappointed in the steak.  Too much breading but a very large portion.  My husband got country ham plate.  It was nice and thick.  Would go again if nearby.

We were staying in downtown Nashville and had heard about this German Restaurant. It was about 5-6 miles from downtown and worth every mile! The Bierhaus is attached to the Opry Mills Shopping Mall. The inside is very traditionally German decorated. They have the traditional long wooden tables and benches. We ordered the onion soup as appetizer and it was delicious topped with a pretzel covered with an abundance of cheese. We ordered the King Ludwig platter to split. It was $27 and plenty for the two of us. Afterwards, we had the Black Forest Cake. OMG!!!! Delicious!!! And a huge piece. My husband and I couldn't finish it!! Our server was Kelse. She was AWESOME!!  We highly recommend this restaurant!!

Good quality food for the experience but pricey. Long wait but we toured the grounds. Delivered a plate of biscuits and jams when we sat down made me change what I ordered. Country ham is a speciality but try it with the red eye gravy. Fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuits was weak on the tomato.

EVERYTHING we ate here was really good--even the leftover meat and biscuits the next day! We'd only wrapped the biscuits in a paper napkin--16 hours later they should have been hockey pucks. Instead, delicious! 

Our excellent waiter brought us a basket of steaming, golden-white puffs (ah, those biscuits), pots of jewel-bright, fruity-fruity strawberry, peach, and blackberry preserves (we finished them off with a spoon), plus the sorghum we'd requested. I suspect Annie Loveless developed her biscuits with sorghum in mind--their pairing beats all I've had in the south. 

A couple unique items on Loveless Cafe's beverage menu are its moonshine offerings. The watermelon moonshine comes in 2 mason jars, a large one, pink with watermelon juice and chunks, and a mini-jar with an ounce of clear moonshine. Poured together, they produce a refreshing drink, no cloying sweetness.

Our orders of watermelon ribs and fried chicken both came with 2 sides, so we ended up with creamed corn (double), macaroni and cheese, and the pot liquor greens. It's good we didn't have to share our sides of the creamed corn--wow, it's light and lovely and (woot, woot!) the recipe is available online. 

The watermelon ribs are dry-rubbed and smoked, then braised with the nicely tangy sauce and watermelon chunks, a process that gives the chunks a great tomatoey taste and texture. The fried chicken, though, proved why the Loveless Cafe has such an enduring reputation. Make sure at least one person in your party orders it, and make sure he or she shares!

And save  room for dessert. We ordered the chocolate pecan pie, a not-quite fudgey, highly successful Loveless treat.

The service was great, the atmosphere is fun, and the food is terrific. Yes, you oughta eat here.
We shared fried chicken, mashed potatoes, sweet potatoes, chicken fried steak, mac n cheese, and greens. Everything was so good!! And their biscuits were to die for!!! Best food we had in Nashville!

It's definitely a tourist trap but well worth a visit if you're in Nashville.  Biscuits were great and portions are very generous. Servers are very friendly.  

When you're heading to the restroom, you can see them making biscuits.  :D

Went for their Mother's Day Brunch and this time, was very disappointed. They couldn't seem to keep the buffet full and the quality of what was put out was poor. I'm assuming that the people that ate earlier than our 1pm reservation were able to sample all the options, but we weren't. Many items were not replaced while we were there. We had to ask for salt and pepper and was told there were a few sets floating around the room.  There were a lot of empty seats so it wasn't because they were packed. They must have not planned well for this event - or it was a staffing issue.  The music was great and the one glass of wine that I was able to order was good. Not worth the $42 per person

I lived in Bayreuth, Bavaria, for three years, so I know German when I see it.  What a surprise and delight to find this place in Nashville!  Our server, Charles, was attentive and tireless, ensuring we had  our food delivered hot and delicious and our beers cold and flavorful.  Definitely, we're coming back!  Great place, great times, great food, great music!
The only complaint I have is that at times they are very busy and the dining room gets rather loud. However, all those customers is a good thing.

The reviews on the biscuits hold true! I ate a few (I'm afraid to admit how much lard I actually consumed). If you love the biscuits you should go to the gift shop and buy the magnet that says "praise the lard and pass the biscuits". 

Aside from the biscuits I shared the sampler meal ( BBQ, chicken, meatloaf) with the mashed potatoes and sweet potatoes (I apparently love lard and starches). The mashed potatoes were great (had little potatoes chunks that made me think they were homemade). The sweat potatoes were nothing I would try again ( semi sweet with a hint of Carmel).  I also tried my friends fried ocra, it tasted average. 

I loved the meatloaf.  It had great flavoring and consistency. The chicken and BBQ was good but if you've had great BBQ and fried chicken it's about average. 

I gave 4 stars because our waitress only came to our table 2 times the entire meal and pretty much rolled her eyes at us. She would just walk by and not offer refills or ask if we needed anything. We finally waved down another waiter who gladly helped and brought more biscuits, drinks, and even made sure we liked our food.  We left a tip for Kramer and he ended up running outside to thank us for the tip- so kind and sincere of him! 

Worth a shot but planning on waiting!
This place is a solid 5 stars.  The food was great, shops were cute and we got in quickly although it is a Monday morning.  The homemade food and jams are worth the trip down from Nashville.

We were very impressed by the decor and set up of the winery.  It was a pleasant evening with friends, amazing food and even better music.  I would recommend the City Winery only to those who want a low key evening though.  I wore jean shorts a tank and a kimono with boots for a bachelorette party.  I felt underdressed and would have felt more comfortable in a summer dress and sandals.
Reminded me of beer fest in Munich, great pretzel! Great beer, especially the helles!

Perhaps the worst food I've ever had in Nashville....maybe even Tennessee.  The steak was 2 small pieces and was not even remotely warm when it arrived.  The chicken was marginally edible.  Out of one of their tap wines.  Will not be back and will spread the word to avoid this place.
A Nashville classic - perfect country food just like your grandma makes  Biscuits and pork chops are to die for.

City WInery where you been all my life!!

This venue is nice! Decor of wood dining tables with candlelight makes for a romantic evening. The stage and lighting were on point! meaning very professional , we sat at the first table next to the stage and didn't need to cover my ears not once due to it being too loud. The food..eh its a hit or miss,..recommend you eating before you arrive and just selecting from the vast selections of wine (half in which i couldn't pronounce) 

Valet parking was not a hassle as i thought it would be, price was 5$.
Entertainment wise, R&B artist TANK was there!!! my favorite singe/producer of all time sonnn!!! so my night couldn't be any better!

Heck ya i'm a fan!

Giant chicken tenders, people!  Seriously, they are the largest chicken tenders I have ever seen in my life AND delicious too.  This would be a great meal to share for sure.  Our server was very friendly but just a little slow (in moving).  They weren't all that busy so I'm not sure what was up?

Great little spot to stop on a road trip!  Cute little shops around the place too.  Obviously I liked the shopping because I easily spent 50 bucks on stuff I really didn't need.

I don't understand why people are so obsessed with this place... it's mostly new comers, but I've met some lifetime Nashvillians that love it. It's just good southern food. It's about on par with what I can cook at home... there's nothing special about it and the biscuits are just lard biscuits. Look up a recipe and make them yourself. Honestly, I think it's about the same as Cracker Barrel only more expensive and you have to wait for 2 hours to get in. Notice I'm not saying it's bad food, because it's not. It's just not worth the price, wait, or hype. 

If you want wonderful, impressive southern food: find a good hole-in-the-wall Meat and Three or go out to Monell's.

This is my first time visiting Nashville and my second day in the city. I am in loveeeeeeeeee with this winery. So much so that I could cry from how kind everyone here has been. The wine is great. The decor is sexy. The people make it all worthwhile! I was helped by Mike, Hayley, Daryl and Sydney. I want to pack them in my bag and take them with me to Atlanta! The mimosas are divine, KEEP them coming. I will be back! I will bring people with me!
Just waited an hour and a half to be seated and it was worth waiting! Wonderful southern menu,exceptional food, excellent service !  Southern hospitality at it's best!

We went to Loveless Cafe on our way out of Nashville. We arrived at approximately 8:30 and had to wait about an hour before we were sat. They have several shops, games and areas to sit so it wasn't a bad wait. You get a plate of biscuits as you sit, which was nice be has there was a wait after ordering before we got our food. The hashbrown casserole was my favorite. Definitely will return next time we go back to Nashville.

Great Southern food.  Good biscuits and preserves.  Blue Plate Special was ribs...excellent.  Baked Beans had nice kick, and sweet potatoes were delicious.  Finished meal with a peach cobbler a la mode...perfect.

Always a great meal. The biscuits are dynamite( obviously) and the pancakes are my absolute favorite.! My husband gets the brisket omelette and swears it's the best breakfast place in Nashville. Tip--!get there before 8 to get a table, otherwise the wait can be very long, but totally worth it!
Breakfast all the way! Great service, fun atmosphere. Loved every minute. Not to mention the biscuits were AMAZING!

As far as Southern cooking goes, Loveless Cafe isn't even in my top 15, but the experience was enjoyable and it's definitely something you should do at least once when visiting Nashville.

Biscuits:  Decent. Don't know why everyone is so crazy about them. Pretty small, so plan on eating at least two. The housemade peach preserves are awesome. Overall: C+

Fried Chicken (white meat):  Light, crispy, flavorful crust. Meat was tender and juicy. Overall: A-

Hashbrown Casserole:  Sizable portion. Thick and rich. Slightly better than what you'll find at Cracker Barrel. Overall: B

Collard Greens:  Relatively bland. Lacked a traditional saltiness from the ham hock. Pot liquor goes well with the biscuits. Overall: C-

Green Beans:  Same issue as collards. Overall: C-

This revue is for the concert venue only. 

I like City Winery as a concept and venue. There isn't a bad seat in the house. However, show tickets are pricy for Nashville and the menu is also inflated. I also need to add that the acoustics are terrible, which is sad for a room that was built for the specific purpose of performances. It's also the most expensive ticket in town for a show (more than the Opry). 

The food:
I have no problem paying a premium for excellent cuisine, but I've been there three times, and the entrees just aren't exceptional, nor are the wines (and they will add TN liquor tax to your bill instead of including it in the menu price, so that glass you ordered went from marginally reasonable to rather pricy). Expect 25% by the glass tax (between TN liquor tax and regular state and local taxes). The next time I go to a show at City Winery, I'll eat first and have a glass of wine when I get there instead of dining in. 

Parking:
Parking is VALET ONLY at night; be prepared. Make sure you understand the time on your ticket; it may be when the concert venue opens for dinner, and you could have an hour or an hour and a half before the actual show. 

Bottom line: as a local, I wouldn't go to City Winery except for a show, the performer would need to be someone exceptional, and I would to go with the expectation that the sound is going to bounce all over the place.

So so so good. We went Monday around 9 and didn't wait at all. Hash brown casserole is amazing. Pancakes are amazing. The biscuits though. Beyond words. So good. Pace your self! They bring those out first and by the time you get your food you're stuffed. Adorable venue great staff.

A pretty long wait to get in on a Saturday morning, but boy am I glad we got there when we did, because the line only got longer. You cannot call in to reserve a table. We toured around the buildings while we waited and once we were seated, the wait was well worth those delicious biscuits and home made spreads itself! I really loved the peach preserves...yum! Breakfast and coffee were average, hubby's chicken fried steak was pretty good but my ham was very salty. Those biscuits..I would go back just for them.
Great wine, really delicious filet, and a cool atmosphere. We had a great time here for a low key dinner during a bachelorette. Service was excellent.

The food is excellent. Never had a complaint. Not very handicap friendly for wheelchair patrons. They have all the parking and ramps but the inside is tight and hard to negotiate. We are one in wheelchair and one who is blind.

Definitely the highlight of our trip.  Went on a Monday around 10 and there was no wait.  Best biscuits we've ever eaten.  Friendly staff and even solid gift shops.  Recommend anything involving a biscuit from this place.

Tourist trap. Interesting concept and if you want to just say you've done it, then go for it, but don't expect anything amazing food wise. Pricey for what you get. Our group had both breakfast foods and lunch foods and we were all underwhelmed by it all. The waitress was nice and the place was packed, but I can only imagine it is with other tourists as you can get the same food at Cracker Barrel (and it would probably be more tasty). Not a fan. 
BLT didn't come with any condiments, you had to ask for mayo. Fried okra was good. Hamburger with pimento cheese was subpar. Fries were typical, nothing special. Fried chicken was disappointing. Eggs and country ham were to be expected. Biscuits ok and jam was fine. 
Been there, done that. No plans to return. Too many good food options out there to fall for this tourist trap again.

OMG!!! I want to live in their kitchen! This is real southern cooking. Not only is the food AMAZING but the staff will treat you like family...the members you like :-) I will most definitely be coming back to Nashville just to visit them again. Don't leave town without visiting these guys. Yes it's a bit out of the way, but the drive is well worth it. It really is a hidden gem.

We loved it! Is it the greatest restaurant in the South, no, but it was a perfect stop for my first trip to Nashville.  I ordered the smoked pork chops and Mac and cheese and it was OFF THE CHAIN.  Sooo good! The preserves with biscuits were generous and super tasty. I am also a sucker for a road diner with a history! Oh, and the artwork was awesome!

The best thing that we ate was the Ruben roll and that was even over fried!  My husband's beer he describes as creamy, but I don't like beer so I can't comment.  The bad of the meal:  everything else ... which includes the over cooked and under-salted smaller pretzel which the Manager wouldn't take off the bill after a few bites!  My Pork (as they don't offer veal) schnitzel was OK but was tough, dry but don't ask for extra gravy cause that's additional!!  The crispy-fried pork shank was just OK too, but barely ANY gravy with that either!  I tasted the pork shank and thought it was tastier than my schnitzel!  It is enough to feed 2 people I would say.

Other reviews of this place say negative things about the sides -- we agree!  The spaetzle, kraut and potato dumpling were not worth the time nor calories ... and of course, no gravy!  So I'll go there and say that the German place could be considered the gravy Nazis!  Sorry guys...

If we came back, and that's a BIG if, we'd just have the big pretzel, beer, and Ruben roll (requesting that it not be over cooked).

A friend who's a local told me that if you have one meal anywhere in the greater Nashville area, that the Loveless Café's the place. He was absolutely right! Pork barbecue, fried chicken, catfish, and the sides (especially the creamed corn) are just spectacular and the staff was so accommodating I even took a few biscuits home.

Flaky, soft, freshly hot biscuits? Crunchy crusty, yet moist fried chicken? Perfectly cornmealed and seasoned fried catfish? Tucked away next to a gas station out of the Nashville city? Yes, definitely the best way to start my New Years resolution of 2014!!

This place was poppin' late afternoon of New Year's Day. Screw your New Years resolution when there's food this delicious around!

We loved the biscuits, fried chicken, and fried catfish. Sides were okay. We weren't too pleased with the overly cheesy hash brown casserole, but we loved the cucumber salad, fried green tomatoes, and hush puppies.

An amazing place with that southern charm that makes you feel like you're eating in a local home, just be ready to wait at least 30 min to and hour if you haven't called in before hand. No worries, you can stroll around their cute stores and get some loveless souvenirs!!

Second time eating here when visiting Nashville. It's a fun setting and the shared tables are authentic to what we experienced in Germany last year. The food is very good. The service is good. The pork shank is amazing and enough to feed a small army of humans. Loved the potato salad. Make sure and come on an empty stomach.

3 stars because I like the vibe of German restaurants. Service definitely could be better since we were sitting at the bar. 

Food was good and authentic. 

Of course, great beer too 

20% chance I give it a second try
Slow slow slow .... I have been waiting for my credit card for more than 10-15 minutes. Steak was to hard.
It's famous for a region. Plan to drive out of the city a bit, wait awhile for a seat, and eat stunningly good Southern food. Order anything--it will be excellent.
We went here for a bachelorette party!! The place was perfect. The service was great and the atmosphere was so unique. The food was AMAZING!!!

Came on a Thursday morning at 9am no wait to get in super fast service had our food very fast as well and it was insanely delicious! Had the moonshine Bloody Mary comes with cured bacon and a souvenir glass! Southern sampler, biscuit sampler, and biscuits and gravy! Everything was delicious and cooked to perfection!

The venue is beautiful! This is a great listening room. Service was a bit slow. I cannot comment on the food, but the wine was OK. Not the best wine, yet not unpleasant. I would return for another event.

Every time I visit Nashville this is always my first stop. Being from Chicago, I don't get good southern food often. I always get the Southern platter with a choice of three meats and two sides. The complimentary biscuits are amazing and so are the berry preserves it comes with. The catfish is perfect, turnip greens were delicious. I can't find anything to complain about except for it being so far away from where I live.
Best meal I had in all of Nashville. The people here are so nice as well. You need to put it on your list of places to visit if you are in or near Nashville!

Upon approach one might think this place is "cute" or "nice"... boy looks can be deceiving. Let's start with the highlights, although they over work their waiters (a grueling 17 hour shift... yes you read that right 17 HOURS) Jason was incredible, a true glowing star in a dark and cruel place. Also they had the worlds best beverage, you know it and you love it... rootbeer. We had to wait for an hour to get seated and the place is sooooo out of the way. Everyone think the biscuits are soooo great but the true winner was the hash brown casserole. Not a very child friendly place.

That cafe is located like 30 minutes from downtown, and even though it is on a highway.
There is always a line. We had to wait 40 minutes on an afternoon on a weekday to get in. Once you got seated, you are served biscuit and jam. Their biscuit is from heaven!
I ordered the country ham with egg ( perfect) and fried chicken liver and gizzards ( so so). Their prices are good and the service is good as well.

It's good! It is not great. The atmosphere is awesome,  great wine selection. The tartar appetizer is spectacular,  but they were just short on the rest. Don't get me wrong everything we ordered was good, again it's just I've had better.  It's decently priced and service is very good! It's worth trying.

First time stopping for dinner. Hit the spot. Was craving country cookin without having to go to Cracker Barrel and they did not disappoint. We sat with Owen and he did an amazing job. Great server with great personality. Food was amazing. I had a vegetable plate and he ordered brisket.  I had to get hash brown casserole, it is to die for. There was so much brisket on the plate. Great value.

Omg! These people know how to make biscuits! I have to say the recommendation to mix Sorghum Molasses with butter and dip the biscuits in them was a delicious idea. The service was incredible. And if you haven't been here yet, their Hash-brown Casserole is OUT OF THIS WORLD! The wait can be grueling but I've never felt so rewarded than after eating at this place. Love, love, love Loveless Cafe!
Great food! Good beer! They are still working on kinks with service but overall good!

This place is extremely popular...after having read about it and seeing it featured on a variety of shows for years, it was crazy to actually experience it.  I didn't think that a place could be so popular that people would actually drive out to basically the middle of nowhere and enjoy great food...wow, this place was great!  

Loveless Café isn't very close to downtown Nashville and really is in its own spot.  This place is so popular that it's actually its own amusement park.  We arrived somewhat early on a Sunday morning and the wait wasn't bad (about 20 mins).  The food itself was incredible...very rich and very Southern.  Well known for their biscuits, they are definitely incredible...rich, decadent and extremely buttery.  The accompanying jams were great too.  I had chicken fried steak and thought it was excellent...definitely a heavy meal that will keep you satisfied for hours!

If you can make it out here, definitely visit this spot...great food!

I've been wanting to eat here for several years and finally came today. I was a bridesmaid for a friend who got married at the beautiful barn there also. We arrived around 2 and the wait was around 30 minutes but that was okay since you can walk all around the property and know when your table is ready. The market and gift shop were nice too. The hostess were very welcoming and friendly. Susan was our waitress and she was so great! Please tell her that! She was so happy to work there and spoke so highly about the homemade food!! I got the cinnamon raisin French toast, bacon and hash brown casserole and ALL of it was amazing!!! The food seriously stayed hot the entire time I ate! My hubby loved his pancakes and sausage. Tell Susan this is Noah's parents writing the review ( she said she'd remember him lol) she was a sweetheart and we enjoyed having her take care of us! We'll be back for sure :)

Let me start by saying that I am an AVID lover of beer. While I have yet to visit Germany itself, I haven't yet come across a German-beer that I don't like. Their brews are SO MUCH BETTER than the American swill we all suffer down on hot days around here.

That said, Bavarian Bierhaus delivers the goods with supremely delicious offerings and imports of a vast selection! We've yet to try it all, as we've only been 2-3 times, but what we've sampled and had, we love it. Each time, I opt for their most massive stein (generally about $13-14) but it is SO worth it.

On to their food: I will come clean, each time we've been, we've only shared their pretzels and biercheese fries. The apps have so much food and the beer is so filling, we can't get to an entree! We decided last time that next time we go we'd get our usual beer, but then split an entree. I'm excited to try their food, as I've heard it's wonderful and each time we're there, everything I see come out of the kitchen looks tasty.

Overall, we'll keep coming and enjoying every sip! Well done, Bavarian Bierhaus!
Great night last night...tons of energy in the building to watch Yacht Rock Revue.
Tasty food if you don't mind heart attacks. Very long wait. Very busy. Cool shops and buildings all around it. Fun experience. I'd go back, but it wouldn't be my top choice.

Amazing venue for some music. The menu is a bit pricey but whatever. House made wine is fantastic! Couldn't ask for any more honestly. Service was spot on and on top of everything! Going again for the Marc Broussard show.

Loveless cafe is a must if you are in Nashville. Yes it's touristy but the food was well worth it. I got the country fried steak with hashbrown casserole. The steak was giant and amazing! Had to take half home. Biscuits come warm and with three delicious jams. Drinks are pricey though. Not sure if they were with it. 

I hear it gets pretty crowded though and there can be a huge wait. We went on a Friday morning around 9am and got right in. I guess all the wild and crazy partiers from Broadway were still asleep so try a weekday and early if you can.

Ok, this place is worth the out of the way drive. We were a party of 4 and had an 1.5hr wait. We considered going somewhere else but then found the cornhole stations (you check out the bags at the little postal office store, leave your ID with the clerk in exchange). After shopping for jam in the adorable Loveless themed shops, playing a few games of bags and sipping on some cream sodas our buzzer went off and we practically squealed with excitement. 

This down-home diner didn't disappoint. We were immediately served a plate of buttery biscuits and jam (pro tip: skip the jam and butter up that biscuit!). I ordered the waffle and everyone at the table agreed it was the best decision. The waffle seems to be somehow made of the same delicious dough used to create the biscuits, it was delightful. Highly recommend. 

We were heading out on a 6hr road trip post visit and our sweet server loaded up a to-go box with MORE biscuits without even asking. If you don't buy the biscuit mix at Loveless you can buy it at the airport on the way out of Nashville. Get thee to Loveless and bring your appetite!

Waited over an hour but it was SO worth it. Food comes out very quickly! Creamed corn and coleslaw are my favorite sides. 

Skip the coupon mentioned, it's for online orders only.
On vacation from California and came here for breakfast. Best biscuits I've ever had. Hash brown casserole was my fav. Service was awesome. Highly recommend.

Delicious biscuits with preserves.  Well worth the 30 minutes wait on a Sunday afternoon.  The blue plate special, smoked brisket with two sides was ginormous and so was the barbecued pork.  My daughter enjoyed the moist and well seasoned meatloaf.  Will have to come back for the pies someday.

This place is fantastic! The People are friendly and brings the customers back to "service with a smile". Country fried steak, eggs, cheese grits, bacon and biscuits. All great! Loved the grits...
Came on a Monday morning around 10am with 6 people. Did not have to wait...
Also loved the Peach Jam.. Bought a few bottles to take back to NJ!
If you're able to go... Definitely go and have some breakfast here!
It good, not any better than Cracker Barrel at twice the price, which makes it not as good.  Enough said!

Did nothing for me a popular place to go? Maybe because it's off the Trace?
Wasn't worth the wait the food was cold and the biscuit's were hard.
Just finished my birthday dinner here! Everything was fantastic! Jamal took excellent care of us. Will definitely be back!

AMAZING experience!! Kirsten was an out of control AWESOME server! The food, drinks & pie were crazy good too. Wish we were local so we could pop in whenever. Definitely check it out if you're in the area!

We had a phenomenal time last night at the Greg Brown show at City Winery. This was our first time there and it will not be the last.  The food was amazing and the service top notch. I have to specifically call out Kim for being so helpful with our menu choices and never letting our drinks run dry. Kim was also so sweet to my mom and a huge thank you goes out to her!

Certainly a solid breakfast option and one that stood out among the plethora of breakfast-centered restaurants in town. The whole place has a very home-y, comforting feel. The biscuits are amazing - my only complaint is that they are too small! But no worries, they will bring you another plate if you ask. The food was good with generous portions. Perhaps not the BEST omelet I've ever had, but I would definitely return next time I'm in town. Be sure to check out their gift shops for cute (if somewhat overpriced) souvenirs to take home.

I think this venue is going to have a successful run. It's quite lovely. There is a bar out front so you can go even if you're not watching a show. There's also additional space upstairs but we didn't check that out.

We didn't dine with the winery; we started with dinner at the Omni and walked over. I will say that I was surprised to see the valet charging seven dollars. I do not believe that there is parking available anywhere else, so if you drive, you will likely be paying to valet.

We had wine and cocktails in the concert hall as well as at the bar afterwards. Both were very good. Pricey, but I've come to expect that in the new Nashville.

The concert was Joan Osborne and she sounded fantastic as always. The acoustics were fine to my ears. Be careful when choosing your seats because some in your party will likely need to crane there necks a little to view the stage. The seats are regular chairs, not stools that swivel. Still, the space is nice, and well presented. 

I'm very impressed with the lineup they've been able to book thus far. I think that the ticket prices are reasonable and I'm sure I'll be attending shows at this venue for years to come. As a matter fact, I've already bought tickets to a second show.

Paid for a "premium table," which unfortunately came with less than premium service. Ordered a bottle of wine upon arrival which took several reminders and more than 20 minutes to arrive. Food was average and expensive. All this would be a wash if the music listening experience was top notch, but it wasn't. Wedding DJ music bled in from the adjacent private event space, so for the first half hour of the show, the live act on stage was competing with Cool and the Gang.

I had high hopes for this place but it fell short on all ends. We made a reservation for our bachelorette party to come wine and dine. Our table was not ready (or thought of) when we arrived. After 15 minutes we sat down to eat. The truffle frites held us over before our entrees arrived. The flatbreads were HUGE, definitely shareable. I enjoyed the margarita flatbread to kick things off. I also ordered the burger which honestly sucked, it was bland & blah. Though we were sorely inconvenienced, the server and manager offered nothing to offset the burden. The server asked several of us if we wanted change after gratuity had been included on our bill. Asking if a patron wants change is an industry 'no no'. The restaurant was freezing cold and hard to sit in as well. I wouldn't return or recommend City Winery based on this experience.

Must visit for tourists! We visited on a whim right after we arrived in Nashville but were too tired to search for a place to get dinner. We must have hit a good hour because we got seated right away. We were taken care of by Owen, who was EXCELLENT. We split the sampler plate with pulled pork, fried catfish and fried chicken. Everything was delicious. We ended up trying their breakfast later in the trip and it was also good. The biscuits really are as great as they're made out to be. We checked out the gift shop and brought some preserves home with us. We will definitely go back next time we're in the area.

This place is huge!! We sat at the bar for some quick biers!! The liter is humorously huge but hubby got one. The bartender was great and gave mine in smaller glasses( same liter)as I'm not a fast drinker and also don't have the muscles for the liter!Lol! 
We had sausages, fries  and the pretzels as we watched soccer( US vs Martinique)...
Great atmosphere, friendly service and awesome servings.
We shall be back obviously!!
Every time we come to Nashville we stop here to eat. The service is great and the food tastes so good. The biscuits come with an assortment of preserves and butter

MY pastor came from this neck of the south so I went and visited his best buddy there who took me on some country bumpkin road out to this place! I loved it,talk about good ole hometown southern fried cholesterol! You got it here.The waffles were huge,fried chicken steak great.It's old school,dixie do it right! Wear a checkered tablecloth and go grits and pancakes too! It's been a long time but i have a book of matches from this place right here on my desk....sort of brings a little "Earl Pitts" tear to my eye.....if you get my drift! Every food lover should eat here once! It's a tradition! I salute you Dixie!

"I just want his dignity, that's all. I want him hopeless, loveless, finished off! I just wish him ill, very very ill." -- Addicted to Love (1997)

I love a good biscuit - small, large, fluffy, flakey, sweet or buttery. Bring them on. Loveless has been on my bucket list for ages and until recently, I've never been able to get my group to drive the distance/time it takes to get there - because truly, it isn't really in Nashville. It is on the outskirts and takes time to get there. Thankfully, my fellow biscuit lover and bestie, Tanya C was on this trip with me and she knew this was the place to go!

Be prepared to wait, but know that the wait is well worth it. Not to worry, there is plenty to do to pass the time. This is a converted motor hotel and they have converted the buildings into different shops - so there is so much to see (and enough places to spend money). Art, cookbooks, food, clothing, tchotchkes, and then some. If you aren't in the mood to shop, then there are chairs, picnic tables, more chairs, benches.

We drove in and parked (parking is plentiful) and got a pager. They gave us a wait time of an hour 40 - wow. Okay, let's wander! If you don't want to wait, you can place a to go order (yes, they have an app) and eat at the picnic tables (no seriously, this is brilliant). 

We were seated before the allotted time had elapsed - excellent - and were seated at a table close to the front door. Wow, the place is massive. Much larger than I had originally realized. During our wait, I looked through the menu too many times and had a hard time deciding what to eat. After much internal debate, I opted for lunch. Knowing that they just bring you the biscuits for free (with the jams), and that was the main reason I wanted to eat here, my entree was second fiddle. 

First the biscuits and jam - blackberry, peach and strawberry. That's the order of my love of them. Why did I NOT buy some? WTH, Lindy? I could have eaten my weight in these little tiny biscuit gems. And they didn't weigh anything - light and fluffy and no bigger than a 50-cent piece. YUM. I ordered the friend pork chops - delicious. Crunchy, while juicy on the inside. I had the hardest time deciding on my sides - I opted for mashed potatoes with gravy and creamed spinach. I also ordered a side of country ham. Everything was amazing and somehow I ended up with all 3 gravies (brown, white and red-eye).  I think the creamed spinach was my least favorite thing I ordered and it was not bad.

Unfortunately, there was no stomach space for dessert, but based on the other tables it looked good. Next visit, I'm getting the fried chicken! Did I mention I'll be back?

This place was good, but I sat at the bar and the service wasn't that great. The bar tenders talked to me to grab my order and that was pretty much it. I probably would have had another beer or meal (only got an appetizer), but by the time they talked to me again I was done.

Very cool venue.  You can have the full menu in the dining room or in the actual concert venue itself.  They have select wines that are on "tap" which are prepared especially for the winery, as well as a decent selection of bottles as well.

We split a couple small plates, which were tasty (went with the arancini balls our server recommended, as well as the brown butter pumpkin gnocchi).  Our server in the dining area was great, but the server in the concert venue was a bit frazzled and hard to track down.

Be aware that the concert time that's advertised is actually when the doors open,  not when the concert begins, and there may be an opening act.  Our show was advertised as 7pm, but we had to leave at 9 to get to a show at the Opry, and the main act hadn't even come on yet.

Good service. We had about 25 people and they were helping us when we needed anything. They weren't very interactive with us. Like they wouldn't talk with us. But they are very busy so it's understandable. But that could be improved with just a small conversation and some jokes.

Food was great! Biscuits were the BOMB. And they just kept bringing them back. We took 4 dozen back and they were gone in 30 minutes. Cream corn, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and many other sides to a great country brunch.

This is a great place to go. I'd love to go again if possible.

I will never return here again. I have only been three times, but will never go again because our last experience was so awful. The food is good, but the wait times can be long and service can suffer due to the restaurant's popularity.

Great beer, authentic German food served in a big beer hall. The staff is friendly and attentive. My fav is the leiberkäse sandwich and the Flammekuchen. You can't go wrong with any of the selections. It's also a welcome Oasis within opry Mills Mall.

My hubster found this place on the food network about famous places to eat. We stopped in from taking pictures at Percy Warner park ( separate review). Super cute cafe located on the same lot as a quaint old school loveless motel and loveless famous ham gift shop. 
It was cozy and super friendly. Down home cooking at its best!! The biscuits were 
A. M. A. Z. I. N. G!!! They serve 3 home made fruit preserves that were yummy as well. 
Hubster ordered the 1/2 fried chicken, fried okra, green beens and turnip greens. I ordered the French toast and bacon. Now I L. O. V. E. bacon. The bacon was slap your friend good so were the green beans and I had a food-gasm from the turnip greens. They were perfectly cooked with ham hock and vinegary goodness that make you want to suck the juice out of the greens then chew!! I could have eaten a whole pot of those. The French toast was perfect, the eggs were done right. My daughter ate a ton of the okra. So if a 1 yo eats it then you know it's good. The biscuits, OMG. ( I'm hungry now). 
Cool thing too was a Antique car club came by and chatted a bit. Saw an old dodge and a couple of model A's and T fords. Amazing food and experience. A must go if you can.

We moved to Nashville a year ago. Loveless is where we take all of our guests visiting us in Nashville for the first time. Last Saturday (8/27) I brought my entire family (10 of us) to Loveless. The food was great as usual, but it was really the personal touch of our server Diane who really made the visit special. 

Diane: You made this daughter proud to live in Nashville. You also made my 88 year old dad feel so welcome and special with your wonderful attention and service. Thank you so very much!!!!!!

The quick story-go anywhere else, anywhere.  The house wines are overpriced and watery. The service is beyond horrible, and the food is so overpriced and overlooked you're gonna want to hurt yourself for not following this review.   The long story, we dined here in the summer for the first time for dinner.  Anticipated to view the city while, if not dining, having drinks.  The upstairs, outside was closed for a private event, no one was allowed.  The downstairs where the main Restsurant was wine barrel themed. Noisy as noisy could be.  One server for the ENTIRE large set of tables.   He was pushy and we felt pressured and rushed.  That time in the summer we vowed NOT to go back.  Unfortunately, we ended up there the other night because someone in our group forgot how terrible it was. Hoping it would be better, DISAPPOINTED again!  The server was so busy, we felt like it was a hit and run accident.  He suddenly appeared, asked if we were ready to order.  We were ready to order but weren't quick enough I guess and he fled to do something else.  He didn't return.  The hostess took our order.  The truffle fries ( they were short cut and few) were good, risotto balls over cooked.  Flatbreads were overlooked and the duck flatbread was barely edible.  Cavatelli pasta was undercooked ALOT and lacked any flavor really aside from hot pepper. The bill for the extreme basic meal for 4 was 200 dollars.   And he poured water on my ring and hand!!! How do you miss the glass 2 inches away!!!!! Thankfully it wasn't coffee!!!  Never going back.  Will go to The Butcher in Germantown (fabulous duck and you can buy it and cook it at home additionally if you like) or go to Bobs steakhouse at the Omni.  You may pay more but everything is perfect .
Food isn't all that and our server was a complete weirdo and is probably in the wrong business.

We've been going to City Winery since they first opened and enjoy the music venue set up. Service is good, the food is usually good. The only problem is the ladies restroom. Each time there has been some type of problem: toilet overflow, lack of TP, and always problems with paper towels. Went last night and still no TP and the paper towel dispenser was hanging open, no extra towels in the shelf and a big wet roll on the counter- thought I was at the local gas station!
Doesn't a manager or attendant ever check the ladies room for problems or cleanliness?
Come on folks- for what you charge for parking, food, and beverage, you can afford to fix the paper towel dispenser or hire an attendant to hand you towels like House of Blues.

The biscuits, oh, the biscuits!  We had the fried chicken, biscuits & gravy, and pork belly biscuit with egg and everything was amazing.  The aroma of the smoked pork belly was fantastic.  I also highly recommend the fried green tomatoes.  The mac & cheese was good, but not stellar.  The place was packed and they were very efficient and personable.  I will be back for sure.
Homemade biscuits and jams, slow cooked & smoked brisket...uuuummmmm....uuummmm...good!

The last time I ate here I was a kid but it still looks just the same.  The place is a tourist trap in a lot of ways but it still has some charm to it.  The biscuits are still great while my steak was less than acceptable as it had far too much gristle in it.  The rest of my food was just good Southern food and the staff was friendly and attentive.  This is much more than just a Cafe as it was also a motel that has since turned all those motel buildings into different shops and art displays along with a big ole barn in the back they use for different events.  This place provides a lot of Disney level ambiance and while you can find some better Southern food at other places this spot is still worthy of a visit just to experience the grounds and the biscuits are usually among some of the best in the South.

WOW. I used to hate biscuits until I visited Loveless Cafe.
This is a restaurant in the middle of nowhere but it is DEFINITELY worth the drive. You come in and they give you your wait time but while at it, there is a bunch of things for you to do around. From many boutique shops, to Loveless very own products shops and they even provide free coffee. After a long wait, we were finally seated.

The biscuits were brought to the table continuously and the jams that came with them were as good. For food, we ordered the famous Country Ham (which was incredibly salty but the waiter does warn you but once you pair it with the gravy and even some jam it complements it beautifully), the Chicken & Waffles, and the plate with all meats (sausage, ham, and bacon). NOT ONE PERSON in the table was unhappy with their meal.

On top of that, the service was friendly and the atmosphere absolutely enjoyable. This is what I call a 5 star restaurant. :)

Had to wait, but well worth the wait in my book. Once seated, they were quick for drink orders, brought out the AWESOME biscuits, and then took food orders. I had a hard time deciding on breakfast or hot chicken (the special)...I ended up trying the hot chicken, mashed potatoes, and mac n cheese, and it was fabulous!

First time visit to the Loveless Café as part of a wedding rehearsal dinner.  Very unique southern-style restaurant surrounded by shops to purchase jams and jellies, meats and souvenirs.  The southern atmosphere and charm was wonderful!  The food and customer service were excellent!  They made you feel right at home. Next time I'm in Nashville, I'll go back for breakfast.  Highly recommended.

Worth a 20-30 min driving detour from the heart of the city of Nashville.  Loveless is located off the 100, and this is what you would picture when you think of Tennessee.  The idyllic setting of the countryside, the large homes, the serene road and nothing but green.  Not too many cars in sight, until you get to Loveless. 

Loveless itself is a quaint little tourist stop, and it is complete with activities for the family, little shops, and even a post office in case you don't want to lug all the things you bought here back in your luggage. 

The cafe itself - be prepared to wait. We were told about 1.5 hours on Sunday morning at 1030A, and I think the wait just got worse as the day went on.  Now, is it worth the 1.5 hour wait?  I would say yes.  There is plenty to do while you wait, and the beeper for your table works anywhere on the grounds.  

Now, onto the food. The biscuits are really quite delicious.  The jams are jar licking good, and I had to refrain from eating too much biscuits so that I could enjoy the rest of the meal.

The fried chicken is quite crispy, and the breast of chicken was a tad over done, but still good.  The fried catfish was also breaded nicely.  The bbq pork was juicy and saucy - just the way I like it.  The country ham is also not to be missed.  Juicy and tender.  

All in all, the wait staff is what made it for me.  They are all so nice and chatty - some of that southern hospitality for you.  Something you definitely miss in LA where the people are all rude and vapid....LOL.

All in all, Loveless is a great place to visit if you're in the area.  Eat as many biscuits as you can!!

Unbelievable food.  Fried chicken, country ham/biscuits, fried green tomatoes and creamed corn were fantastic, BBQ pulled pork was good but just okay.   The service was even better, Meagan was probably the best server I've ever had, and I eat out a lot.  A lot.

Quite the ways out but I had nothing else to do since I got in so early. 45 mins from the airport. 

First thing you smell when you walk in is their biscuits. You can smell the slight greesed and savory biscuits. That's also one of the first things you'll taste and it sure is a great first bite I'm the morning. Their biscuits are a little different in texture than I've had at other places but they are great. They come with some very tasty preserves. 

I got pork chops and eggs. They are not regular sized pork chops! Definitely a splitable menu item. Pork chops were really good until I got to the second one. They are breaded and fried so you get a nice taste of savoriness coming from the breading alone. By the second one, I was taking on a little too much grease.

Server was amazing and enthusiastic. I would say it's worth a trip if you have nothing else happening.

We visited on Friday afternoon, around 2.  There was plenty of parking around the back of the property (I can see how it could be challenging at times or for handicapped).  The wait was estimated at 35 min, at that's what it was.  Greeter Michelle was smiling and friendly.  Our server Lucas was very nice and easy to talk to, and his service was excellent.  We ordered 1/2  fried chicken and 3 side order plate.  The food seemed to take a little long, but the biscuits (4 out of 5) kept us busy (don't eat too many), and jams were great!  Everything was very hot and delicious!  We will return.

Great home cooking. Try to eat there often. 
Can get breakfast anytime. 
Wait staff very pleasant. 
Feel like u r on a mini vacation when to go there. 
Great jams and biscuits.

Greeting- yes
Vibe- farmhouse tourist attraction
Price- nice
Service- good
Parking- free lot
Food
 best biscuits
Great jams
Fried green tomato sandwich is tasty
Fried chicken is good
Fried okra was dry
mashed potatoes are cafeteria style
Banana bread pudding is very southern
WIGB? yes

One of my go to places when in Nashville

I attended a concert at City Winery on July 9,2015. The layout, decor, and overall space is promising for a concert. They of course have an incredible wine selection, upscale bar food, and descent amenities to offer you during your visit. Although the positives for City Winery are plenteous, I would say there are a few areas they kept me from giving them 5 stars.

The first opportunity I found was with the valet. Although I read previous post about the price, which is $5, my concern was simply with the staff. These people are your first experience with the venue and they were very unfriendly and uninviting to my wife and I. Yes, you took my car and brought it back to me at the nights end but try and be as upbeat and excited as the workers inside the facility. Secondly, would have to deal with the food. I will openly admit that these opportunities fall solely on personal preference and not solid data but I believe there were some concerns. First, if you are offering a special, only allowed for the restaurant and not the stage area, don't put it on the projectors and show it to me every four minutes. Secondly, 98% of the food offered was not sharable but was also too large. I understand I'm at a restaurant but at the same time I am not. I have experienced in other locations shareable, medium size dishes worked better. Lastly, I didn't enjoy my food. My wife and I purchased the truffle fries and risotto balls for an appetizer then a hamburger, which was a burnt on the outside and raw in the middle, and a chicken dish which my wife enjoyed. The dining is attempting to be upscale and new age but seemed to miss the mark with each selections. The fries come with a garlic mayo which does nothing except take away from the fry. The risotto ball, which should come with marinara sauce, is accompanied with BBQ sauce and spicy mustard. Both offering nothing to highlight the flavors of their counterparts.  You can see the definite potential with City Winery but these are just a few areas where attention could be shown. 

Lastly, on a side note. If you are going to a concert and truly care about your view and sound quality, I would definitely recommend forgetting the front sections of sits. Although this is usually my section of choice, the venue and atmosphere of food, wine, and conversation with your neighbors really demands you sit in the second section and back. 

Thank you City Winery, Victor Wooten and friends for an amazing night. Honestly, despite the few comments here in this review I look forward to returning and recommending your venue to others.

Might be my favorite restaurant. Absolutely wonderful. Be prepared for a long wait but there is lots to do while you cool your heels. The biscuits are exquisite and the hash brown casserole is legendary. Just goooooo!

Not trying to be negative but I was not impressed with this restaurant.  Thought it was overpriced for what we got.  Waiter tried to push more and more drinks on us and seemed to be on a schedule of turning tables.  Food was good but experience was not as good.

Let me start off by saying that our server, Matt, changed my life. Not only was he friendly and easy to deal with, but his meal choice has altered my view on the world. We started off with biscuits. I've never been a huge fan of anything that doesn't involve meat. I feel like eating biscuits are a waste of time, but not these biscuits. They were amazing. I crushed about 2 of them before we even ordered. Anyways, I attempted to order fried chicken off the supper platter. My boy Matt, said that they offer a spicy version of this dish. Hearing that Nashville's all about hot chicken, I jumped on that opportunity. After destroyed about 2 more biscuits, our food arrived. I gave it a once over and decided it was too hot to eat, so I started off with a dab of the mac n cheese. My mind was immediately blown. The noodles were soft and the cheesiness of the dish was perfect. Pleasantly surprised, I went after the chicken. It was an explosion of flavor in my mouth. It was euphoric. My immediate reaction was to rip off all my clothes, jump in a deep fryer, roll around in the breading and pour the spices all over me so that the chickens could see how good they taste. I reluctantly gave my wife a piece, so she could enjoy a little bit of heaven. This is by far the best fried chicken I've ever had. Dear Mr. and Mrs. Loveless, I love you.

Edit:
One thing I forgot to mention is that you must take the excess breading and spice from the chicken and mix it in with the mac n cheese to complete the experience. God Bless the USA.
Had the sampler platter. Wasn't fan of fried chicken but meatloaf and catfish was really good. Caramel sweet potatoes side was amazing!

Being an Iconic Cafe in Nashville, we had to try this out. We even watched a video about Loveless, it's history, and "the power of biscuits" prior to heading out. I was expecting a long line to wait for mediocre food that only has good reviews because of the nostalgia. My assumptions were pleasantly incorrect. The wait was 45 minutes but with the shops to meander around it went fast. The aroma of the place was tantalizing, a combo of fried chicken, barbecue, and biscuits which wound up being exactly what we ordered. The barbecue was the biz-omb and my favorite. No need for barbecue sauce. The other half loved the fried chicken though I wasn't jumping out of my seat for that. The biscuits- well-are pretty darned good and the peach preserve was our favorite or the three they serve with them. Ooh, the creamed sweet corn was delicious. The banana pudding was the best I've ever had (aside from our Aunt Red's). Basically everything we had we'd want to eat again and now we'll have to take our friends here just because it lives up to the hype.

Nice atmosphere, mediocre food. My wine drinking friends sermed to enjoy the wine. Excellent service.  We sent a salad back that was soo horrid I'd be embarrassed to serve my dog. But they took it back with no hesitation and without charge. My "medium rare" lamb was so rare it was barely lukewarm.  Again...they took it back for more fire. When it came back...hardly more cooked... it was only tolerable. An attempt at some "interesting" flavor combinations was mostly unsuccessful.  Someone is trying too hard. 
Sapphire Restaurant in the Factory succeeds in the style in which City Winery currently fails. 
I won't be back for the food.
Biscuits were good and so was the food!  Enjoyed the hash browns casserole was the best!!!
You need to go here and you need to eat the biscuits!!!! Definitely one of the best meals we had while visiting Nashville. We had to wait a little but well worth it. You will not be disappointed :)

This place was great! We received a recommendation from a local to definitely check out this cafe and we are so happy that we did so. The people there are so friendly and the cafe is very quaint and has a lot of charm. The food is sooooo good, we can't stress that enough. We aren't from around here and we loved getting to experience some of Nashville's greatest foods. Also, they give you a lot of biscuits and jams to eat with it and it was amazing. If you are coming to Nashville or live there and have never been, definitely check out this place! It is so worth it.

When you order a draft flight, BB designates 4 beers (Bavarian Bierhaus, Hofbrau Dunkle, Paulaner Hefe & Spaten Munich Hell)  and you get to select 2 others for $15. That was a good deal. I ordered a Reuben and subbed German Potato Salad for the French Fries. (I just could not order same old FFs at a German restaurant-to wrong.) The meat, was lean and very good just not as much of it as I expected. This is NOT piled high, NY style. :-(  There was more sauerkraut than meat on the sandwich so the bread was wet (soggy) when served. Not soggy good, soggy bad. I pulled the soggy bread off.
We went for lunch, around 11:30AM so the place was quiet and still empty like. It's a large place. You eat family style (long tables) like in Germany at Oktoberfest. 
I would eat here again. The beer list is extensive and worth more investigating.:-)

The Loveless Café is a legendary establishment in greater-Nashville, and one at which Hub and I dine on most every trip we take to Nashville. The ride out to the Loveless is about 25 miles from downtown, but it is worth every mile. After exiting the interstate it's a short and lovely ride through the countryside. While the drive out and the location and the quaint little building that houses the café are all pretty swell, those are just ancillary considerations for making the trip. At the Loveless, the food is the star. It's excellent, delicious, southern comfort food. We've only ever had breakfast so I can't fully attest to the deliciousness of all the menu items, but I'm gonna go out on a limb and say that based on everything I've ever eaten at the Loveless, you can't go wrong with anything you order. The biscuits are pretty renowned, and they live up to their reputation as one of the Loveless' signature items. They're smallish, but wicked tasty, and when you finish the complementary plate of biscuits, your server is more than happy to bring another plate over. Speaking of the staff, we've always found everybody, from the wait staff, hostesses, managers, and gift shop personnel to be super friendly and accommodating. Most importantly we've always left fully sated and happy.  The Loveless Café more than lives up to its legendary reputation. It's a swell joint!

My office is just around the corner from Loveless. I get by about once a month. My favorite is the half order of country ham plate with eggs, hash brown casserole and eggs. ALWAYS a winner--with the unending biscuits! Makes for a great morning!

For the weekend we stayed in Nashville, this was by far the best food!
Great fried chicken, awesome banana pudding and service that was like eating with close friends.
Go to the gift shops, buy some jam(we did), and then get a few gifts for all your friends.

Nice to visit with out of town guests.  Aside from the biscuits and jam, the food is mediocre at best.  The wait staff is always so pleasant and kind.  Wait time for a table is ridiculous.  Needs to be a larger waiting area for people waiting on their table

The biscuits!!! The biscuits I say!!!! Simply amazing, baked to a warm buttery perfection topped with homemade jams...I could eat 1000 of them!

I had the eggs and BBQ breakfast, scrumptious! The BBQ had a little rub on it and the sauce is near drinkable! 

The property is really cool too....get ready for a coma!
Came here today for the first time. The steelhead trout was amazing. Jamal, our server, was very friendly and knowledgeable. Highly recommend this place.
Go here. Eat here. Drink here. Wow. Everything was tasty. Great service and the food... can't say enough. Wish we had one of these in Dallas.

I just love this place!!  I was coming here for 10 years before I moved to Nashville and now I live only a hop skip and a jump away!!!  The Pork Chops are Wonderful....the Biscuits are GREAT....and I love love love the Coconut Cream pie!!!  10 stars!!!

Good, typical southern food. They give you huge portions. However, I am a girl who loves my seasoning and this place is just kind of bland. Everything is cooked to Perfection but just needs a lot more Salt and seasoning. The biscuits, on the other hand are delicious. The reason I'm giving it a 3-star instead of 4 is because of the lack of seasoning And there's always an incredibly long wait, for which I can't quite understand. of course, the wait is not the restaurants fault but it still makes the experience less than enjoyable.
If your staying in Nashville and deciding if you should drive all the way out, the answer is yes. The biscuits alone are worth it.

One of our favorite places to go.  They get pretty busy on the weekends, but they have more seating then you'd expect.  The breakfast biscuits and lunch fried chicken are legendary for a reason; they're the best you can get.  Service is always awesome.

Unfortunately, our meals were all disappointing. The fried chicken dark meat pieces were cut strangely, yielding mostly bones. The drumstick was very small. The fried green tomatoes were thin & limp & bland. The cream corn had an odd texture. Our guests were quiet during the meal - no comment about the poor quality. To finish my meal, the banana pudding was also disappointing because the serving was tiny, the pudding was flavorless and the bananas on top had turned. The cafe is cute & the service was great.

BISCUITS!!!Very superb southern food! Just take a second and look around while you are eating and you can see how much the staff goes out of their way to create such a great restarting environment! The chicken was very yummy, portions are huge and prices are very fair! Did I mention Biscuits?!

Home cooked, Southern style food. Good food, good service, good moonshine drinks. Ordered the blue plate special, which at the time was hot chicken with fries and mac and cheese. It was so good! The chicken was juicy, yet crunchy. Had a little kick of spice, and was delicious. I was in a big group and they got everyone's order right. I had a side of ranch and others had small sides or little extras, and they never missed a thing. I ordered the Blue Moon drink, which was delicious. Had blueberries, lemonade, and Sprite (with moonshine). The Loveless is such a popular dining location that people wait hours to eat there. There was a big crowd of people when we arrived and left, and I can see why. I highly recommend visiting the restaurant and shops behind the restaurant if you want something to take home.
Had a great time amazing service from the wonderful, large hearted, and amazing bartender Mattie. By far best service. Everyone needs to come and see her.

Worth the wait. I'm full, I'm happy and I'm going to sleep.

That should say it all. Love it.

The best The South has to offer: the biscuits, the blackberry jam, the bbq omellette, the chicken fried steak. You can't go wrong at this place!!!

http://notquitegrownupguide.blogspot.com/

One star for good biscuits and a bloody mary. Another star for the gift shops to walk around in during a very long wait. 

I expected at least a 20min wait for brunch Friday for a group of 9. Hour wait seemed long and I would have left except the place is far enough outside of Nashville it wasn't worth it to relocate. 

Finally got seated and ordered our bloody Mary's which were good and came with a piece of bacon. But they took a very very long time to come out. Actually everything took a while. Service is not a strong suit - but rarely is with large parties. 

Now for the food. It was just bad. We ordered various things across the 9 of us and no one liked their food. Hash brown casserole? Sounds great but it's more just strings of soggy potatoes covered in melted velveeta. I thought it'd be like a crispy cake with some onion and peppers and bacon fat maybe. But nope. The country ham? Foul. Super grisly and way to salty. 3 of us ordered the ham and all felt that way. 

On top of the food just not tasting good, we all had some hurting stomachs afterwards. I was looking forward to coming here since I heard great things. But it was a major disappointment and I will not be returning again.

My wife and I hit City Winery last Friday to see Matthew Sweet play.  This is already one of my favorite music venues in Nashville.

First off, it's just awesome to be able to sit and have a drink while watching a concert.  I think I'm getting too old to stand throughout a show.  The service was very good and I was impressed with the wine and beer list.  We were told that they would actually have wine for sale that they personally made (as any winery should) within a few months.  

We weren't sure about the menu because the show started at 10:00, but they were still serving.  We had already eaten, but did order dessert.  It was a peach dish and was very good--reminded me of creme brulee a bit.  The menu appeared to have an excellent selection and you're probably looking at about $20 per dish.  However, there are appetizers and desserts if you don't want to a whole meal (or, you could just drink).

This place is great.  Check out their calendar as they do have a diverse list of acts.  I look forward to trying their food on the next visit and could easily see myself adding a fifth star.

I do enjoy a loveless day once in a while, provided it's here.  That being said, Country Ham is touted as the go-to at the LC and, well folks...to me, it tastes like a belt that's been brined overnight.  And I was born in this state.

And I don't even mean LC's take on it...I just have difficulty eating anything that proves someone hybridized a pig's glutes and Lot's wife.

So, I opt for other things.  It's hard to find a restaurant that serves gizzards and my first try here left me taken aback, for the soaking of same in buttermilk or whatever renders them indistinguishable from livers (which I am capable of ordering, should I deign to).  Nevertheless, I return periodically and occasionally delve into the livery gizzard plate.

Someone labels LC a tourist trap, I see, and it's a little more that than it was formerly...something about having the extra space making it seem a bit less down home and more commercially comfy.  It was more fun to fight for for seating.  You could barely walk through the place to the bathroom.

Best thing there?  Blackberry preserves, then biscuits...as if you'd have either without the other.
