It remains a pleasant stopover.  We occasionally come here before visiting Chaffin for a play or two, since they're neighbors.  Recommended, but if you've got other plans, it'll be there when you get back.

I'll probably be dethroned of my yelp elite status for leaving anything less than 4 stars for this Nashville staple, but honesty is the best policy, right? I'll start by saying that for me, the best part was the experience: the gift shops, decor, and southern hospitality from the staff. 

When we put our name on the list, we were told it would be a 1 hour and 45 minute wait. There are plenty of gift shops to spend money at while you wait on your buzzer to go off. It ended up being about an hour wait. I spent $30 on a ceramic berry carton, a tea towel, and foot cream. All very cute and I use them regularly so I don't regret any of them. 

As far as the food goes, (don't judge me, we hadn't eaten anything and my eyes are larger than my stomach) I ordered two eggs sunny side up, a fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit, home fried potatoes, a piece of fried catfish, & biscuits and white gravy. My husband ordered a few of the same things, but also pancakes. 

The good: the pancakes were huge and good. The biscuits and homemade jams were tasty. Not drive 30 mins out of my way good, but definitely the best thing I had. The catfish was tasty and I wish I had ordered the catfish supper plate. 

The bad: the eggs whites weren't completely cooked. I know a little is expected on sunny side up eggs, but I scraped more than I'd like to the side of my plate. The gravy was... weird. My mother-in-law also ordered the white gravy and we both thought there was something about it that was off. I had a couple bites wanting to like it and just couldn't eat it. It didn't taste old or like it had gone bad. It just had a really different flavor than anything I've ever tasted in white gravy. 

The meh: fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit. This was a 60:30:10 pimento cheese:biscuit:tomato ratio so I really only tasted the pimento cheese, which was nowhere near as good as my own homemade pimento cheese. The home fries were cut up in little squares and deep fried, probably frozen, potatoes. Similar home fries are available at Nashville biscuit house down the road from our house. 

I guess what I'm saying is that we won't go literally out of our way anytime soon to go back, but if we have friends visit who want to go, we will go back with them and I will try the catfish plate. Otherwise, I'm not in a hurry.

We decided to go here for brunch on a Sunday and the wait was 1.5 hours. We killed time by walking around and visiting the cute shops around the cafe. Ultimately we found out that it would be quicker to order carry out. We found a picnic table in the shade and ate outside. I had the two eggs with bacon platter with a side of hash brown casserole. It was amazing! I will definitely revisit on my next trip to Nashville!

Absolutely amazing!!!!  The drive from Nashville was absolutely beautiful.  Wait was about 45 mins but they have cute little shops to keep you entertained. Went in the middle of June so it was hot and humid. Once you are seated they bring these delicious biscuits and jam. If you arent a big eater than i recommend sharing a plate. Had the chicken fried chicken.. perfectly crisp with gravy on side. Mac and cheese wasnt anything to right home about. Cream corn was quite tasty. Over an amazing dinner. Definitely worth the drive!

This is my second time at City Winery, the first time was last year when we had a company luncheon event. And the last night to see one of my favorite bands, Parachute. I fell in love with venue itself with its rustic charm, high ceilings, and intimate setting. I knew I had to see a show there one day. So I was pretty excited about last night. Valet was available for $6 which was great for a rainy night like last night. We checked in and was showed to our seats that we were able to pick out when purchasing tickets. The tables were super small and we definitely cozied up to our neighbors. We ordered the risotto balls for our appetizers, margherita flat bread and duck tacos for our entrees. The risotto balls needed more flavor and the rice was way undercooked - my pizza was good, but was a tad bit oily, the duck tacos were decent - but also needed more flavor. Our server probably had way too many people to serve, she never brought me crushed pepper, but did check up on us a few times and was really nice. Parachute was incredible and they put on an amazing show and so did their opening act, Johnny Balik. I just loved the intimacy, setting, and sound of an acoustic show. I definitely cannot wait to see another show. May even give dinner another chance.

Great place to catch a live music show! Fair ticketing and great prices....cheap valet parking. Eats and drinks are somewhat overpriced but getting a great seat for your favorite musician makes it all work out.

Pros- fair ticketing, clean, lots of drink choices, pretty good menu of food, they don't give you grief about taking a vid.

Cons-sort of pricey drinks, they pack you like sardines at little tables and its reminiscent of "family style" seating in fact you share table water, sometimes hard for servers to hear you.

So the seating is 3 tiny tables (if not more!) pushed together and 6 seats at those tables. Just hope you sit next to someone nice! As you will be VERY close, actually its ridiculously close. End seats are the best I think.

The shows never seem to drag out like they might at other venues. They seem to stick to the time very close.

Disappointing experience. We came to the winery with high expectations. The setting and wine were good but the food took over an hour and was less than impressive. The server did her best and comped one of the meals that came out cold and desserts but our bill was still over $300 for four of us. Don't waste your time here.
Tourist/mall German...much better at other places in town....Beer and Onion soup were standouts...wife's Reuben was 95% kraut..no meat...not horrible but one and dobe

Okay. So many things i want to say but really just go here.  The biscuits are obviously the star of the show.  The blackberry preserves are next level.  And to top it off , the waitresses are outstanding.  Danielle in particular made me feel like I was just part of the family.  She was absolutely awesome. Seriously guys.  Forget a birthday cake next year, I just want biscuits.  Okay that was too far...I'll take both.  GO TO LOVELESS CAFE!

Iconic location.  You could stand and look at the pictures in their main room for an hour.  Incredible menu as well.

I went in and picked up some sauces and spices for my father's birthday and they even put it in a little package with a card for me.

Worth stopping in!

This place is an event that everybody should do at least once. Yes, it probably is out of the way. Yes, there will be a wait. Trust me though, it is all worth it. There are cute little shops to check out and free lawn games to play while you wait for your table; and you can make the detour worth it by going for a stroll down the BEAUTIFUL Natchez Trace Parkway after breakfast/brunch. As far as the food goes, prepare yourself for mountains of the most delicious biscuits you are likely to find anywhere unless your grandma has been making them for as long as you can remember. I highly recommend ordering the pork barbeque breakfast platter, but you probably can't go wrong with anything on the menu. If the weather is nice, try to get a seat out on the side patio to further increase the experience.
Delicious fried chicken. It's so worth the wait to eat here. Don't forget to visit the cute gift shops.

I give them 4 1/2 stars - dinner last night was excellent for the 4 of us at an early-Mothers-Day celebration.  Service was welcoming, friendly and fast.  Three of us had the sampler platter and I had the BBQ pork with sides of sweet potatoes and green beans - fresh and flavorful!
Great first visit and they honored our reservation for 4 on a Thursday weeknight.  
Thanks - we will be back !
Amazing food and the friendliest staff I have ever met.  A must eat when in town.  The pimento cheese burger is great.  Everything home made
very country. been twice. first time was good. second time feel like being rushed by the server.

Such a great restaurant - a can't miss place when visiting Nashville! Yes there will probably be a line when you visit so check in and spend the next hour or two walking the property, play games, do some shopping, or rock away your hunger in one of the many rocking chairs! Once you get seated - prepare for a feast! Don't miss the fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit sandwiches. Everything on the menu is great. And I mean everything! Take dessert to go ;) Service...best in Nashville!

This place is amazing!! I can't even fully describe the atmosphere here. Live music, great food and amazing huge beers! Access to the mall from the back. My family highly enjoyed this place on our stay in Nashville. This is a MUST stop!! Recommend this place to everyome
This place is very unique and must be experienced. When you come,  ask for Kimberly as she is the most professional and thoughtful server we have seen in quite some time. The food rocks too!

Cute little restaurant. As a tourist, saying it is in Nashville is misleading. It was about a 40 minute drive from broadway.  But the drive was relaxing and worth it if you are not in a rush to eat like my mom was lol. 
We had watermelon ribs, ocra, cream style corn, fried green tomatoes and mashed potatoes with gravy. It was all good. We also had a three dessert sampler plate that was delicious. Coconut cream pie, pecan pie, and the banana pudding. My favourite was the banana pudding. They need to turn it into a pie because they do a great pie crust. 
The server Mark was excellent.
The BBQ is great and the biscuits are some of the best I have ever had. I had a sample plater it came with meet loaf fried chicken & BBQ a side of green beans and a side of cucumbers with onions.

I live about 15 minutes from the LC, and honestly I'd suggest finding a Cracker Barrel instead.  The biscuits are flat and dry and everything else tastes about the same as a Cracker Barrel (if not sub-par), but has a much higher price tag.  This is not a spot where locals eat (often).  Every time I pass by I shake my head at the tourists lined up outside.

It wasn't bad but wasn't good either. Just saying for a place that prides itself on biscuits I ordered the pancakes thinking they would be awesome and I was wrong. My pancakes were dry, flat and tasteless. If I would have known that it was going to taste like this I would have not waited ninety minutes until we got a seat. My husbands country fried steak and eggs were good but nothing to write home about and my father in-laws ham and eggs were really salty and not good at all. Very disappointed in what we had. When I come back to Nashville this wouldn't be a place I would choose again. I just hope the jams I bought as gifts are better.

So even though I've lived in Middle Tennessee for quite a while, I've never been to the Loveless Cafe until now. Some relatives from Cali came in to visit so we stopped here after picking them up for the airport. 

We arrived there at a time that most restaurants aren't that busy; smack dab between lunch and dinner. However it was still an hour wait here, and I'm actually shocked it was *only* an hour given how many people were there. 

I really liked the building(s) itself. For anyone who doesn't know, the Loveless Cafe and surrounding shops are a converted motel from the 50's. I love places like this; you can tell just by looking at it that it's a relic from the golden age of highway road trips. You almost never see such things anymore, as they've either been torn down or are in complete disrepair because they went out of business after the interstate system was built. 

The little shops were cool. Touristy but charming. They had quite a few interesting items, as well as some food such as jams and cured meats. I had plenty of time to check them out while waiting on my table.

Once we were finally seated, I was quite impressed by the service. Despite being packed to capacity, our server was extremely attentive and very sweet, taking plenty of time to explain the specials and whatnot. I ordered their blue plate special for the day, "Honeyspice" chicken or something to that effect. It was a half chicken barbecued with a spicy honey-based sauce. It was absolutely fantastic, as were the turnip greens and okra that accompanied it. The biscuits, for which this place is apparently known, were quite good as well. My girlfriend and I shared a slice of fudge pie for dessert and it was quite delicious. 

All in all it was a really fun experience, but the wait is long enough that this isn't the sort of place I'd want to go to regularly. However it seems to be a fantastic place to bring visiting family or other people who have never been, and it's definitely a place I think everyone should experience at least once.
Went back for fried chicken oh my! Have the green beans and fried green tomatoes for sure!

This is really a 3.5...bit given the history, 4 is a safe number.

My stars...(5=epic "best of") (4=really tasty and want to go again and again) (3=good and will go back once in a while) (2=fair, might return for a visit if there was some glimmer of hope) (1=avoid at all costs)

Go or No?  Go

Tease:   The Loveless is known for their famous biscuits.  They are amazing...but everything else is just good.

Why I went:  For the biscuits!
When:  Summer 2012

Food:   I was in a group of 6 people.  Everyone enjoyed their meals.  We had a late breakfast/early lunch.  The BBQ was OK.  The fried chicken was good, but not "Gus's good", and all the fixings were tasty.  However, the biscuits were amazing.  They taste different than any I've ever had.  No gravy...just jams and marmalades.  The biscuits are super light and fluffy...and highly addictive.

Service:  Very good.  Our waiter was good.  Friendly enough, but not all that attentive.  He took the order well, but didn't frequent the table enough for refills, etc.  They were super busy...but they should be used to that and still give ridiculous service.  Not bad mind you...just not as good as we were hoping.
    
Hints/Final thoughts:  This is a tourist trap.  But it's a good one.  Just know the biscuits may not please every palette.  It doesn't taste like any others.  But, take them for what they are and they are amazing.  Everything else is pretty much just good.  Also check out the store...there are lots of cool foodstuffs, shirts and trinkets.  While their BBQ was a bit disappointing, they BBQ sauce isn't!  Grab a bottle!
I don't need to  add to  the other great reviews.  Do yourself a favor; just go.   And be sure to stop by the gift shop for jams, hams & biscuit mix. You'll be craving these within days.

As a music venue, very nice. Great sound, physically spacious yet intimate-feeling. Except for my first experience, for Sturgill Simpson in August which was a crowd of Americana fans and a private event, I have never yet seen the place full, however. it's early, though, and I'm sure it's still getting its footing. It's about a 300-seat venue, which really helps you feel connected with the artist, but a lot of that has to do with the act, as well. It's not really great that you have to share a table for eight with people you don't know for dinner and a show; it'd be nice if there were more tables for two and four, as there are hardly any in the whole house.

The menu, however, is less impressive. Pretentious is okay if you can back it up with taste, but it's just not there. So, it's a pretentious and pricey fail. Since City Winery is a wine venue, it thinks it has to offer only complicated dishes, and I enjoy the occasional highbrow reduction or unusual flavor combination. The friend who was with me, however, does not, and that's okay, too. Sometimes wine is best when it accompanies something simple, and there is not even one menu item that might be qualified as uncomplicated or unfussy. Not one. Take a look at your menu, Chef, and relax it a bit. Give us a variety of options, to appeal to a variety of diners, in the way the sommelier offers the wine list. Everybody will win.

I will say that our server, whose name was Matt, I believe, was very patient and was happy to take time to explain every description and answer every question we had. I ended up with the beet salad, and when that proved too spicy because of the cayenne pepper, I ordered the cheese plate and made that work, although I did not enjoy the horseradish spread that was one of the accompaniments. 

Also, when we arrived, the seating staff said that we were to sit at separate tables, and of course, I wasn't going to have any of that. Our arrangements had us seated together, and I was polite, but had to insist that they check their seating chart notes again. After just a few minutes, we were led to one of the few tables for two, off to the side but still well in view of the music. I was happy that they made the effort to correct the error without any attitude at all. 

I did attend a private event at one of the smaller upstairs rooms that also had a little stage and a bar. I was helping at that event, so did not experience it as a patron, but I did notice that the bartenders were friendly and helpful, and the waiters seemed prompt at the tables. The hors d'oeuvres trays, however, lacked variety and imagination. Anyone can put crackers and cheddar on a plate with strawberries, but to be fair, maybe that is what the client ordered from the catering staff.

The parking is what everybody else says it is, but I have had great luck with the valet staff being exceptional every time. I've never waited more than a few minutes for my car. They really ought to offer the valet as complimentary, however, since there aren't any other real parking options. 

So, it's like this:

Main Music venue: B
Dining Menu: D
Service: B (Matt was a little slow, and rushed us on the check)
Private events: B
Parking: B-
Overall: B-
Meh. The food is good, but not so good that it's really worth the wait. One in our group got french toast and it arrived cold. Checked it off the bucket list and will probably not be back.

The BISCUITS!  Enough said.  If you order nothing else on the menu, you will come away more than completely satisfied from these delicious, warm, buttery morsels.

First of all, they keep them coming....as many biscuits as you would like. (Meaning we got to take home a box full as well)  In addition, they are served with a fabulous assortment of seasonal jams/preserves.  The most recent time I went we received strawberry, peach, and blackberry  all of which were delicious.  

Besides that I got the meatloaf for my meal.  The meatloaf was very good, exactly what I would expect if I visited my grandma for some home cooking.  What I really enjoyed were the fried okra on the side though.  And the best part was, when the waiter brought out my dish he exclaimed that I had been "shorted" on my okra serving and so brought me another bowl!  I

Overall the staff is very friendly and the place has great southern country feel.  The wait may be long, but stick it out because it is definitely worth it!

My last review was less than favorable.  I would still caution anyone to ask what something costs when the wait staff offers you an alternative, as they will always up sale you to the most expensive wines and liquors they have, but I will say my last two visits (yes I continue to go for the music acts) have been far more favorable.  The last two times it seems the food quality is back up.  This does make me happy because the acoustics are better than any other venue for music.

While some locals told me the original owner passed away, fried chicken and biscuits wasn't as good as it used to be.  I think they have the best fried chicken.  Crispy outside but not full of breading. The chicken cooked just right, not rubbery but fully cooked.

Husband and bro in law love their biscuit and home made Jam.

A must visit for us every time when we are in TN.

I'm going to go with a 4 star because of the cheap drinks. From the Chicago area and we didn't anticipate the "Chicago Bar Prices" so this place was a nice break from the rest of the "Nashvegas" strip prices. But we also were wanting to grab some food and were told they are redoing a lot of things and aren't serving any food, so disappointed. Also, the bartender seemed like she didn't want to be there. On her phone and not super friendly. Great band though!

Even though I've lived in Nashville for nearly a year and am a huge fan of live music, I only recently got the chance to go visit The Basement. We went for a Saturday night showcase which included a range of genres from indie alternative to spoken word rap. Needless to say, it was an experience like no other. The total showcase only cost 5$- and the music was so good they could have charged more but I appreciated the price. It was packed as the artists played and the drinks flowed. Speaking of drinks, they have a very impressive beer selection including a lot of craft brews and domestic drafts. Being that The Basement is more divey than most music venues, I was surprised and grateful for their selection. I recommend going to The Basement for any of their showcases as well as just random night shows. From what I gathered, there's always something going on here. Also, the space is great as its intimate and cozy without being crammed.

There are no words! Everything is made from scratch they are kind of out of the way off the beaten path but we'll worth the trip. My husband had the gizzards he loved them the biscuits with sorghum and butter omg a must do if you are in Nashville

This place is no joke and worth the effort. Go. Doesn't matter how far you need to travel to get there, just go. Eat the biscuits, order the fried chicken and cream corn. SO good! All of it was amazing... you'll leave full, happy, and ready to come back for more. I will definitely be coming back to Nashville just to eat here again. Instant favorite!

We had to wait on a weeknight, but that's kind of expected with the Loveless Cafe. The biscuits are delicious, and our service was awesome. She was very helpful and friendly. Everything on the menu sounds so great and well-priced. The homemade creamed corn was top-notch! 

I'll have to go next time for breakfast!
Oh my goodness, if you are looking for a hearty (and wonderful) breakfast, the loveless cafe does not disappoint! The peach jam was my favorite, and the pulled pork was fantastic.
Best breakfast in Nashville no matter what time of day. Great food, great service, great experience. We try to go once a week.

I walked in for a quick biscuit and jam experience around noon on a week day. While the blackberry jam was outstanding, the biscuits were a little on the chewy side for my liking. And YES I'm from the south. ;) 

The most disappointing part of my experience here, though, was service related. Our waitress was incredibly rude and snarky. I overheard her making ugly remarks to the cashiers about my party in the next room. We were all extremely nice, but she was not. If you're looking for "southern hospitality" I'm afraid you won't find it here.
Food was simply amazing! The pulled pork is a must try. And ohhhh those biscuits. The place is extremely clean and service is very friendly!

It may be unfair to compare this establishment to the numerous restaurants I've visited in Germany and normally I would let this go. However, the Jagerschnitzel I ordered was the worst I've ever had. I sat at the bar where i was served by Kira, a lovely and very personable young lady. I ordered the Draft Flight and the samples were very nice. The Jagerschnitzel arrived less than ten minutes after ordering which is strange. Preparing this filet properly should have taken longer. The crust was almost impenetrable and the gravy/sauce coagulated. I mentioned my opinion to Kira and guessed that this meat had been prepared prior to my visit and was microwaved for quick service. She checked with the kitchen and indicated that this may have been the case. This place has the feel of a Munich beer hall and groups will have fun here, but the food needs to be stepped up.

Caught a free Fruition and Dead Winter Carpenters show while here in Nashville last night at The Basement. What a treat for an out of towner to catch a couple of my favorite bands at a free show! The basement is as exactly as its name suggests. This little spot feels just like an unfinished basement, only there are great sounds emanating from it making the experience unique. The beers are reasonable and you can't help but drink them just as you would in your own basement. The other great aspect is that the musicians are accessible - luckily the members of Fruition and DWC were friendly! Thanks for a great experience!
We just had lunch at this establishment.  Good food and GREAT wine!  :)  The place is really clean.  The bar tender and server was really nice!!  We could not have asked for better!!

I love this place.  We love Biergarten in Epcot and this reminds me of it.  Fun, festive, good food, good beer.  The food is not very gourmet, but I do not believe it is supposed to be.  I got weinershcnitzel the first time, it was very good, spaetzle was a little bland but I liked it anyway.  I don't like that the lingonberries were served in a plastic shuffle cup, it cheapens the place.  The pretzel and beer cheese app is awesome.  Potato Pancakes are like my polish mom in law makes.  We brought her home some sausages and she asked us to bring more next time, which says a lot considering she is polish and eats similar cuisine.  The pretzel pudding is heavy but delicious!!  The band was great, my daughter had a ball.  We went back again for lunch and loved it then too.  Our waitresses on both occasions were excellent.  We will be back.  It's new, has a little ways to go as far as the food but it's got a ton of potential and could turn out to be a new fun favorite place to go.
Food is awesome and so is the service.  There is always a wait but they at least provide distractions with the multiple shops!

Firstly - be prepared to wait for a table on weekends for a long time. We waited for nearly 2 hours to be seated and even though there are little nooks and crannies to explore whilst you wait, we'd exhausted them by the time we were seated. It's very popular!

Breakfast though was GOOD. I had a plate with different biscuits on it which was delicious. The jams and condiments were all outstanding. Would like to return for lunch or dinner one day.

Biscuits & jams were so delicious we visited twice in a 1 week trip (and bought biscuit mix & jam to go!). It lives up to the reputation and is worth the wait. (Just make sure you call 24+ hours in advance for reservations, especially for large groups, otherwise they won't take em).

BBQ pulled pork breakfast platter was huge and tasty. Fried chicken and waffles were okay (waffle was on the heavy and bland side), I subbed in dark meat fried chicken and it was super good. I'd order just the plain fried chicken dish next time.

Blueberry vodka drink with a souvenir shot glass for $11, it was really good... Maybe too good! 

If we lived closer, I'd be 400 lbs. Can't wait till my next trip to TN to return.

This review is strictly for the food at Loveless cafe. We waited more than an hour to eat. I ordered an omelet and home fries and a fried green and tomato biscuit. The food was good but probably not my favorite breakfast I have had in the area. That being said, I think I ordered the wrong thing.

The biscuit was good but not the best I have had in the Nashville area. My favorite thing I had was actually the blueberry cupcake I had for dessert. So delicious! The service was great and our waiter was very friendly. My mom had the chicken fried steak which I tasted and it was pretty good. My husband had pancakes, eggs and ham steak and he really loved his meal. I don't think I will rush back but it was fun walking around the property and shopping in all of the little stores.
Decent sausages but not great sides. Come for the beer and pretzels and not much else.  NO substitutions allowed.  Super slow service.

In love with loveless! What an adorable place! Had to checkout loveless while in Nashville and I'm so glad we did. Didn't  get a full meal as we had dinner plans but we HAD to try the biscuits and jam which were AMAZING! They were so buttery and delicious along with the 3 samples of jam: strawberry, peach and blackberry, all delicious. We also tried the hash brown casserole and key lime pie. The hash brown casserole was so good, along with the key lime pie. I don't normally like key lime but this was delicious. I wish we would've had time to go back for breakfast or dinner. We did go to the gift shop and picked up BBQ sauce, jam and a few other goodies. Super adorable gift shop and grounds. Definitely worth going. Best biscuits we had while in Nashville.

The best fried chicken , home made biscuits, & toppings in the south-The best fried chicken , home made biscuits, & toppings in the south-The best fried chicken , home made biscuits, & toppings in the south

Great services , good fried chicken. Mac and cheese and creamed corn were amazing , get them together and try to have spoon mix of them - tasted even better to me. Long wait lines but you can grab free coffee from the gift shop while you wait or just go for a drive on the parkway near by.

If you want a look into the true local music scene in Nashville, look no further than the basement. There are a lot of great places in Nashville when it comes to locals, but I love this place because it has a wonderful vibe. It feels like the hangout you chilled at in high school or college at that one friends house, you know..the guy who had that room, garage or whatever perfect for throwing back a drink, smoking some stuff and listening to dark side of the moon. Acts are hit and miss, just like a lot of places, but if you catch a great band, then the basement will feel like magic.

There's too much against this place for me to give it a higher review. I want to like it more! 

My first time was confusing-I didn't know where I was supposed to go, and no one greeted me when I came inside. I had to go up to a hostess and ask, and she was not the friendliest. Seemed like I was inconveniencing her for not knowing how things worked. It wasn't crowded, otherwise I would have watched other people.

Things I like: environment is very nice. Love the Isle of Printing piece on the wall. Acoustics were good (not that I'm a pro). Service was attentive. Spicy pork tacos were tasty.

Things I don't like: Paying for parking. Encountered a rude hostess (Won't get into that story). Tacos were good but had to be eaten w/ fork & knife, which kind of defeats the purpose of tacos... Also, SO not worth $12.  Very pricey overall for just ok items. TINY tables, uncomfortable chairs.

We went to the Loveless Cafe on a Monday mid-morning. We had a 45 minute wait, but it was nice because we got a pager and were able to walk around the campus and go into the different shops. Some people in other parties were becoming edgy due to the wait, but the staff does not keep it a secret that you will be waiting. 

They have delicious southern cuisine! Must haves= biscuits, hashbrown casserole. It was literally the best hashbrown casserole I've ever had! Loveless Cafe is definitely a place you should experience when in Nashville!

My only complaint would be that it was pretty cold inside. I ended up wearing my gloves while waiting for our seat and our food. By the end of the meal my toes were numb!

My family and I visited this Cafe after going to Cheekwood Estates.  It's on the side of the road and use to be a motel.  The service is very friendly.  The biscuits are delicious!  The meals are well portioned and priced.  I would encourage anyone that stop by for a bite if in the area.

The all-you-can-eat biscuits are tempting, but definitely not the best. They're not bad, but seriously, just a standard biscuit. The 3 jams they serve are apricot, berry & strawberry. All are very sweet. Again, nothing special. The food was beyond disappointing. Please, do not order the southwest omelette. It's a basic omelette that they ruin by dumping an atrocious amount of pace picante salsa on & inside before bringing it to your table. Of course, it's stone cold from the large amount of cold salsa that was just poured inside. For the price they charge & the crowds they draw in, it's completely ridiculous that they're serving such mediocre food. Sorry we wasted our time & money out there when there are so many other great places in Nashville.

Oh I adore The Basement. It's such a great place to see local and upcoming bands, and I can't wait to see the artists that I've been 5 feet from make it big. I love that it's musty and dark. I love the grungy nature of the bar and that you really feel like you are in a musicians basement checking out a show from a friend. I'd highly recommend just stopping in on a random night when you feel like hearing a live band that will be vastly different than the artists you'll see on Broadway. 
Of course you need to park on the street and might have to walk a tad and the drink line gets long, but those are minor annoyances when you consider the experience you are there to have.

Decided to stop here on the way out of Nashville after it being recommended by several friends. From what we had been hearing regarding its popularity, we expected to wait for a table. Luckily, with it being a Wednesday morning, we were seated right away. The host was extremely welcoming and made us feel right at home. The decor and atmosphere only furthered that feeling- inside is a quaint, country dining room, one that you'd expect to find in grandma's house. 

Our server, Ashley, was an absolute delight. She was extremely friendly, prompt, and completely made the experience for us. We feel very lucky to have had her although something tells me the rest of the service staff are just as warm and kind. 

The biscuits! I will dream about the biscuits the rest of my life. Ashley brought a few plates out for us during our meal, which we happily inhaled.

I had the garden omelette, which was honestly not any better to me than the ones I get at IHOP or Denny's. not bad by any means, but nothing special. 

All in all, will definitely be visiting Loveless next time we are in Nashville.

I would probably leave 2 stars except for the fact they have a zillion 4 and 5 star reviews and I've only tried one dish there.  Maybe people think the place is cool and the staff is friendly.  They're right.  The menu is fun too.  

I ordered the biscuit sampler with fried chicken, pulled pork, fried green tomato and country ham.  My side was grits and my wife ordered the same main with a hash brown casserole side.  You get 4 biscuit sliders.  The fried chicken is dried out white meat.  Needed maple syrup or something on top.  Dry.  The pulled pork was excellent.  No sauce?  Dry.  The fried green tomato was cold and mushy and buried in pimento cheese until you couldn't taste the tomato.  The country ham should have been topped with an egg or something.  Dry and salty.  The biscuits are average at best.  A little overmixed and not really flaky.  They're nothing special for sure.  The grits were good but the hash casserole was frozen potatoes buried in a ton of fat and cheese.  Disgusting.  

The coffee was from the 1950s and served with packaged 1/2 and 1/2.  Neither is ok by me.  Time to move on to something better folks.  The plastic 1/2 and 1/2 is really bad for you and most coffee service in the U.S. has made great advances.  

I took a look around the room and saw lots of food and wasn't bowled over by the frozen bagged home fries and the griddle top omelets.  I think if you order the right thing here you might have a decent meal but I'm a little concerned about the level of food knowledge overall.  I would come back and try lunch perhaps or just get something different for breakfast skipping the coffee!

Best biscuits and jam ever!! Well worth the drive, it's truly an icon. Also super super yummy chicken. What more can I say you have a wait ours was 45 minutes but well worth it waiter was super nice I also loved the apple pie drink we shared yummy and I don't usually drink alcohol we shared one because of driving I repeat best biscuits and best Jam ever we brought blackberry and strawberry to take home

Holy biscuit what a delicious experience! I highly recommend visiting Loveless Cafe, as a visitor from Southern California I was excited to see what all the hype was about and I was not disappointed at all.

Everything about this restaurant felt kind of meh. The space is huge and sitting at the communal style tables was fun, but something about the environment seemed kind of sterile in that "this is what Americans expect a German beer hall to be like" kind of way. That is to say, I kind of felt as though this was the sort of take on a beer hall you might find in an amusement park along the lines of Disneyland. That being said, if you go into it with the right sort of expectations, I think you can still have a great time. They have passably good pretzels, all sorts of "traditional" German fare, beer in big cups, and servers walking around in Bavarian attire. Everything seemed to be a little on the pricey side, but I suppose that really is to be expected from a place in Opry Mills. All in all, if you want an entertaining place to go watch a game, drink a lot of German beer, and eat some grub with some friends this spot is not a terrible choice if you don't mind paying for the novelty. There are certainly many other probably better spots to do that around Nashville, but this one's a beer hall!

Nice happy hour deals before the show time - flat breads and wines for $7.
The wild mushroom flatbread was pretty good, unique combo.

Smiling, friendly and knowledgeable staff everywhere! The food knocked our Washington state socks off! The BBQ is pure talent and the prices were fair. Great little set up to keep you busy while you wait for a table and it was well worth the wait! We'll be back!
We went on a Tuesday night for "new faces". It was free, the drinks were pretty good and the music extremely fun.

Awesome,awesome place. Fantastic food, friendly staff, retro feel. Pitmaster Steve gave us a  wonderful little tour and lesson on smoking meats. Gift shop was great. Biscuits melt in your mouth. Bought the mix to make them at home.

Stopped in to meet my mom for a lunch 1st time going was impressed by the building and set up inside (it does have a strange location) had their selection for Nashville burger week the KLD far burger it was good but didn't get my vote they did offer s smaller portion due to the promotion which worked out fine for a hot day added on the zucchini fries and they were the best I have ever tried will eventually go back to try out some other items

For what we thought was our final Nashville area breakfast we chose to go to Loveless even though we were staying literally right near the Nashville Biscuit House and the drive there with a packed car-well it was definitely out of the way. As soon as we got there there wasn't a parking spot to be had-which was the opposite trend of what happened during our trip since it was so cold and hardly anyone bothered to come out.

The breakfast is served all day, and the cafe is basically its own little universe of commerce. The cafe, the shop there's a smoker. I was thinking maybe we hit on the tourist spot of all tourist spots. Instead what I got was a really classic place serving really good old fashioned food. 

The biscuits were buttery, soft and the jams were all a great accompaniment to the biscuits. They brought 9 for the four of us. We cleared it and then asked for more. My friend asked for a side of gravy to go with it and I don't know why they don't advertise that more often. Biscuits and gravy here should be announced on loudspeaker here in addition to it written in big, neon lights.

I ended up ordering the steak biscuits and realized I made a mistake. The steak was a little tough and I should have just gotten one of their breakfast plates. I mean, if I can get as many biscuits as I wanted then I should have gotten something without biscuits in it. 

The shop also is touristy but fun. My flight out got canceled as we were eating and I spent 45 minutes on the phone there trying to rebook flights then extending the rental and finding a hotel. The staff there occupied my friends' time by talking about the weather and generally entertaining them until I got off the phone.

The next time, I need to come with 3 other people who are down for that all you can eat deal.
Awesome food, friendly service and outstanding atmosphere. Do leave room for desert, the chocolate pecan pie was well worth the belly ache from eating too much :-)

Loveless Cafe is a classic southern little diner that never disappoints. It's a perfect southern eatery. The workers are so friendly and really make the experience even more enjoyable. Never had bad service here. The fresh homemade biscuits and jam are what I really look forward too, everything else is a bonus.
This place is awesome! The staff were friendly, the food was delicious and I especially enjoyed the seating arrangement. It was very communal and casual.
The biscuits and jam were amazing, the food was top notch, and the waitstaff were all super friendly and laid back and made our time there truly enjoyable.
Great service, but the food really wasn't worth the wait. Granted we went on a sunday after church let out, but the food was just ok. Nothing that left me waiting to come back.

11:55am on a Sunday the day before the big eclipse so take that into consideration.  Hostess quoted 2 hour wait.  Yikes.  It's a long drive and we had nothing else to do so went for it.  It only took 1:15 and like all the other reviews will tell you, there's stuff to do as you peruse the small shops.  

Biscuits come out as soon as you sit down along with fresh jam and soft butter. Coulda stopped there.  Really fresh and soft.  

If it's summer when you visit, the watermelon crawl cocktail is total summertime drink. 

Ordered the Southern Sampler which is a choice of 3 meats and 2 sides. 
Fried chicken - A+.  My favorite of the 3
Pulled pork - A+  served on a thin pancake.  Awesome 
Country ham- C. A bit dry. 
Wife had fried catfish, also and A+ super tender.  

Waitress was no doubt slammed the entire time she's there but was one of the best I've ever had.  Great service.

I went for breakfast yesterday.  I was alone which at some restaurants means you get poor service, but not here !  My friendly waitress made sure I got hot coffee with plenty of refills, a plate of plentiful right out of the oven biscuits, and made sure I was happy with my order.  I ordered the pork chops.  The order comes with eggs and the hash brown casserole.  My goodness what a plateful of good food.  I ate plenty and packed the rest in a big container to take home.  I had the rest of the pork chops and biscuits for lunch.   I think their biscuits are better now...more buttery...than they used to be.   I had not eaten here in about five years.  My visit here yesterday was much more pleasant than in the past.  So I think everyone should revisit again !
AK

The beer hall ambiance tries to be authentic and most people here look like they're having a good time. The costumed staff are fast, friendly and appear to enjoy their jobs. The drink menu had several German white wines to choose from and hubby liked his beer. There's even entertainment starting at 6pm. However, the food is bland, dry and cold. The schnitzel tastes like it was made days ago and reheated. The Reuben rolls burst with so much grease I had to jump up and step back to not stain my clothes and several napkins needed to wipe our faces. The sausages and mustards were tasteless. And the fries were like eating strips of cardboard. Yes, we lived in nearby Holland and eaten at many German restaurants in the US, but sadly this was the worst.

Sehr gut fixings, as if I was back in Deutschland.  Great lunch; with my wife, we always enjoy good German cuisine.  We had the Bavarian Onion Soup and split a Currywurst plate.  Joey our server was spot on and of course our meal was topped with Spaten lagers.  All said...highly recommend.

I was sold when I discovered they offer wine on tap! Yes please! 

I actually came in on Saturday night for dinner and then returned again yesterday. I was impressed with this place, and have only gone to the restaurant area. It is cozy and welcoming with wine barrels directly built into the wall above the bar. They also have a private room that can hold 10-15 people. 

When you sit down, you are greeted with a taste of white wine that is delicious and the perfect start to the meal. The wine list is crazy long and separate, but I stuck with the smaller portion of the wines on tap that can be found in the food menu. The syrah is delicious and you can get it in 3 different portion sizes. 

For food, I sampled the risotto balls and the Mezze plate with multiple dips. I liked them both, but probably wouldn't order them again. Luckily there are tons of other appetizers that look delicious and will try next time! For entrees, I sampled the fish specials, and they offered barracuda which was unique and delicious! Last night I had the lamb loin and my SO had the flat iron steak, both were great, but I enjoyed the lamb best. 

They also offer cheese and meat plates and flat breads as well. Everything was very delicious and reasonably priced too. My lamb was only $26.00! 

City Winery is fantastic and I haven't even seen a show yet! There are a few things that could use some improvement; the $7.00 valet is pricey, and I think some of the appetizers need some slight tweaking, but overall I very much enjoyed it and know I will be back and soon!
Great food!  Excellent wine!  Good place for dinner and a show!  Love the atmosphere!  The staff was very helpful and friendly.  Can't wait to go back!

I have to chime in to give a different perspective. Coming from a restaurant lover  from Chicago now transplanted to the south, the food isn't that special. You are coming here for the experience, the eclectic Nashville tourist trap. The biscuits and jam are great along with the fun little shops. But the wait is pretty awful all the time and the food is basic country home cooking. The meat was just strange. Great service though!

We went really early since we have a baby and made it out by 9am. At that point they were quoting over 1.5hr wait on a Sunday. Honestly not worth it, in my opinion.

Quaint place to visit. We took a detour to visit, as we'd gotten their coffee and blackberry preserves on our last trip and fell in love with the product. 

Well, when we read "cafe" we expected a small Mom n' Pop joint, and not the grounds that greeted us. 

We visited on Labor Day, around 2:30pm and it took us an hour and a quarter to be seated. The hubby ordered fried pork chops, and I grabbed the fried chicken. We figured with the rave reviews and the half chicken only being a couple dollars more than the quarter, we'd order up and munch when we got hungry on our trip home. 

Pork chops were juicy, but hubby says they were too greasy and he wouldn't order again. Fried chicken was the same but there was no flavor. Maybe some salt in the breading, but that was all I could taste. Fried okra was soggy. Caramel sweet potatoes was just ok. The hash brown casserole was good. Biscuits were also good, and we loved the peach and blackberry preserves. First cup of coffee was decent, second tasted burnt. 

Based on all this? We were still blown away with the blackberry preserves and coffee, but wouldn't go out of our way next time. Cracker Barrel, sorry to say, tastes better, is closer, and is also a tad cheaper. 

Friendly staff though, with that southern charm that we all appreciate. Just didn't love anything else unfortunately. 

Based on those
Near my house but I don't go often because of the long wait. The biscuits, yes, are to die for. The salads are pretty awesome - ask for the creamy peach vinaigrette dressing!

Best biscuits. Was visiting for a marathon and came across this place. Not your healthy California fare, but if you like biscuits (these were the best I have ever had) and fried chicken stop here. Fun place and friendly wait staff.
After well over a dozen trips here I had my worst experience at a Nashville restaurant in years. Mediocre food every time I've been there. Terrible service. I won't be back.

This is always a favorite place whenever we visit Nashville. Delicious food, great service, and a beautiful location. Their homemade blackberry jam is out of this world, their biscuits are delicious, and I have never eaten anything that wasn't good.

Delicious and worth the wait! The compound with the stores around the restaurant is entertaining and it's always simple to find a good souvenir for both yourself and your family or friends! Highly recommend a visit, or two or three or more!
Perfect spot for a cold beer with a sausage snack.  Don't forget the pretzels. Enjoy a relaxing afternoon with friends and fun music.

I went to City Winery for the first time the Saturday before Valentine's Day this year. The ambience was very nice except you were sitting 2 feet from tables on each side of you. There was no privacy. The wine was very good, however it was pricy which was expected. I chose to go with the special of the day, "Cab and a Slab". They brought out my steak and I waited 10 minutes for them to bring my guest's meal out as well. When we were finally checked on we were told they had lost the ticket and it would be another 10-15 minutes for them to cook theirs. My plate was then taken back to be kept warm until the rest of the other was finished. I have never had this happen before. The steak was good except it was 6oz's and the sides that came with it were very small portioned.  After a $40 meal I was still hungry. The waiter Ryan was very personable when we first sat down and explained the menu, however we saw him maybe 5 times the rest of the night. I think he was overwhelmed! The table next to us had their plate taken back twice before she was finally served a warm piece of chicken, so we were not the only ones unhappy. We weren't able to experience dessert because by the time we got to dessert we had already been there for over 2 hours and had other arrangements we were late for. When we got the check there was an added alcohol tax on top of the food tax and subtotal. I was always under the impression that the restaurant was supposed to take on that responsibility. To top everything off, there is no parking and valet will make you pay $5 up front, and expect a nice tip afterwards. Just another way this place can nickle and dime you. I have never been so upset with an experience before, especially on a big night like Valentines, where you would expect them to have it all together. I would not recommend this place for anything other than drinks. There are too many other good restaurants in Nashville I'd rather spend my money.

As good as advertised! We had to wait almost 2 hours on a Saturday afternoon, but the time flew by because they have plenty of casual seating areas and free iced tea to sip while you wait. And of course shopping :) 

Once we were seated they instantly gave us biscuits, and the food did not take long at all to come (we were afraid it might, since the table wait was so long). Everything tastes genuinely homemade, and the environment is friendly and cozy. We will be back!
A bit more than a tourist trap! A must stop for any nashville visitor. Scenic area.  Historic site.  Ridiculously delicious down home southern cooking!

I had a blast here. The wait was just under 2 hours, but there is so much to do on "property" of the restaurant that it was nothing. The experience was great and I can't wait to go back to try more of the menu.

The drink menu look fascinating, but I at 10 am and didn't want to partake in the moonshine cocktails that early in the morning. :)

We came in to be seated and the hostess was busy conferring with a waitress about what tables were clean, I could understand that if they were busy but 80% of the tables were empty. We were a party of four and seated in front of their stage where a three or four piece band was playing some German music. The music was mediocre at best, this is Nashville, how hard can it be to find decent musicians? We decided we wanted to sit outside rather than talk over the mediocre music so we were reseated on the patio. The food was OK, we ordered the Ruben roles as an appetizer and they were greasy. brats were OK, onion soup was good.

I won the Bushel and a Peck gift basket and was blown away at how fast it arrived to my door and everything was packaged to perfection (nothing broken, bent or damaged) .  Now I can't wait to try all the goodies in the basket. 
Oh by the way,  I am not just down the street or in a neighboring town.  I am about 30 miles West of Portland, Oregon.

Even on Sunday night there was still a 40 minute wait but it was worth it.   Waiter was friendly and came out with food right away when we told him we were hungry.  The best friend chicken I've ever had with sides of greens and green beans.   The biscuits were really good too.  I'd go back next time I'm in town.

Great food, sommelier David was awesome! Very interesting venue, Joan Osborne was singing in adjacent room and sounded good! Overall delicious food and great atmosphere, the room got a bit loud but it was lively and fun.

The biscuits were fantastic!! Service was good. I wasn't crazy about their pork barbecue. I could've done without the cornbread hoecake they put under the BBQ. Id rather have it on the side. I'd also appreciate a choice of BBQ sauces.  They don't have any at the table so you have to ask for it. Their sweet potatoes had way too much brown sugar for my liking. I can't cay I was crazy about their coconut cream pie but I like the idea of the mini pies.

THE BISCUITS!!!! I could just eat them for the whole meal!! Delicious! But, I did order an omelet and hash brown casserole and it was delicious as well. Be prepared to wait at least 45 minutes for a table on a good day. But it's not bad because they have a bunch of cute shops for you to visit and they give you a little pager to carry so you know when your table is ready. Definitely not the place to go for a quick bite, but a great place for a leisurely, relaxed, fun breakfast/brunch.

I'll echo what some other reviews have stated as far as seeing shows at City Winery.  The tables are absolutely small and the chairs are way too close together. If you want to actually see the stage you'll have to sit uncomfortably sideways while packed in there like sardines. Sitting at tables that small, and in chairs crammed that close together while seated at tables with strangers isn't my thing. At all. I'll reserve attendance here in the future for those very few things that I absolutely can't live without seeing. 

The valet thing. The not-free valet. Annoying. We were warned beforehand and parked on the street in the neighborhood. Not the safest feeling neighborhood at night but it sure beats waiting in the huge line we saw after the show. If you valet you're gonna have to wait a while to get out of there. 

The food isn't cheap. The drinks really aren't cheap. I think the beer list consists of 8 choices? That's total. That's not just the draft list. Or the bottles list. So when I ordered one of the beers off the list (a stout) and something other than what I ordered showed up I questioned it (after several minutes of trying to flag a waiter down). Supposedly they had run out of the stout I ordered and sent this other stout as a replacement. With no explanation. Or apology. It was weird. If you're going to have a beer list that small at least make sure you have the few that are on the damn menu. And ask if it's ok with the customer before sending out a substitute. So for that...2 stars.

We always make time to stop at Loveless when we come to Nashville. The prices are fair and the atmosphere is so down-to-earth. Servers are friendly and we've never had a bad experience. Definitely give this place a try!

It was suggested to us by a complete stranger at a resort in Crossville, he said if you go anywhere in Nashville the Loveless should be at the top of the list, well it was # 3, What a wonderful experience, we were warned that there are sometimes a long wait,We waited approx. 30 mins. After that we were seated promptly on the side patio and greeted a very friendly bearded waiter wish I could remember his name! He took excellent care if us! The food was amazing! Very sizable portions! I would highly recommend this to anyone visiting Nashville that us looking for a home cooked southern style meal! Two Thumbs Up! Can't wait to visit again nex

It feels like the house party of the year in your neighbor's basement.  I make friends every time I go and always feel welcome.  I can't get enough of this intimate spot and love checking out the talent that comes through.

Food menu selection was decent, we only had a few appetizers, including the risotto balls (based on other Yelpers recommendations). House red wine was tasty, but a bit pricey at $41/bottle. Concert experience was uniquely awesome and an intimate setting. We sat at the table next to the stage, at the far left, from a facing the stage vantage point.

Maybe the hype is about the history of this place and the country store/farm house/home style cooking charm. The food isn't really anything spectacular, not even the biscuits. Maybe just not my types but they're pretty sad to me. Tiny little pieces and no texture but loaded of baking power. Definitely don't come here for biscuits. We had breakfast here, nothing special, meh! pretty salty ham and country fried steak was big, but you tasted so much fried grease after 2 bites and full. 

Came here again for dinner cuz some friends who's never been and wanted to visit this joint. We had the smoked pork chops, although tasty, the texture was a bit funny. 

Friendly staff and food came out pretty quick. But not a place I'd come for the food, especially seeing all the magazine covers on their walls.  I didn't grow up in the south, but surely had plenty share of southern cooking and this is just not the place, but it's pretty cute with the country store and all.  But for food lovers, don't come here for the food.

I visited Loveless yesterday with a party of 7 around 10:30am and despite the crowd we were seated promptly. I was excited to visit the restaurant and really enjoyed the service and atmosphere of it, but the food fell just a bit flat. My omelette was overcooked and the cheese inside was hardly melted and tasted just like craft pre-shredded cheddar. I couldn't finish it- and that was a $8 omelette. The grits I got for another $4 and the complimentary biscuits saved the meal, however. The owner (I'd imagine?) came out to talk to us for a bit and wished me a happy birthday which was very nice. 

Overall, I would probably not return because of the high price that did not match my food quality, but I still had a nice visit. The little shops around it are cute and my friends bought me a set of Tennessee drink glasses to remember the trip.

This was our first time. The service is still a little green but only 3 weeks opened. The music was really nice and interactive. 5 stars. We got the giant pretzel w all sauces. The beer cheese was our favorite, a must try. The food portions are large. I'm not a huge German food fan but I really liked everything. The decor is traditional and very noisy. Overall a winner in my book.  Defiantly go when the musicians are there. I can't say enough about them. We will defiantly be back.

Although I'm only giving this place 4 stars,  Lucas, my server gets 5 stars.  As I'm revamping my star system, a five would be hitting it out of the park (a home run)!!! The food was good just nothing incredibly memorable.  As far as it is location-wise, I just would go somewhere closer.  I am glad that I stopped in though. Lucas was a definite highlight.  Service is great, food is good so give it a try!!!

My family had breakfast this Sunday morning and I want to update my review from seven months ago as well as add a fourth star for Loveless Cafe.

We arrived around 8:30am and had only a 20 min. wait. It was in the low 40's outside and we were able to wait inside right across from the pie cabinet. People watching is quite good from here and it amazed us how many guests place themselves direct in the single doorway after checking in, making it terrible for those leaving or entering. Not Loveless' fault but certainly a fire hazard and rude.

Once seated at a clean and well set four top table in the largest dining room on the East side of the building, our delightful and knowledgeable waitress greeted us and took our drink order. I want to reiterate a point I made in my previous review that the wait staff at Loveless is the absolute best you will find at any Nashville restaurant. Certainly a reason to eat here!

Very quickly our drinks arrived along with the biggest plate of hot biscuits, three flavors of preserves and plenty of real butter we remember receiving in many years. Our Waitress took our food order and we chatted briefly. Today we learned that Tom Morales and TomKats Catering no longer has any involvement with Loveless. I noticed a Senior Manager that appeared very professional and maintaining a regular, close review of the wait list. Bravo!!! The lady that seems to always be handling the wait list when we visit Loveless is the weakest link at Loveless so I was thrilled to see a General Manager regularly overseeing her work, asking questions and staying very familiar with the info on the list. Please keep doing this Management!

Now to the food. Chocolate chip pancakes that my daughter always orders were perfect and so large she brought some leftovers home. The breakfast steak and eggs my wife ordered were served hot and cooked to order. The steak could be a better grade meat and actually a bit smaller. My guess is the steaks are coming at average grade from a Sysco type supplier and a local area grain fed beef supplier would be a nice improvement for Loveless to consider and make a highlight of the menu. Today I ordered the half-order country ham meal with red-eye gravy, eggs & grits. All cooked just right, served hot and plated perfectly. I got chocolate milk for my drink, a first, and was very pleased that it came in a carton from our local (sadly now owned by Dean) Purity Dairy. This is the same milk I grew up drinking in Nashville from weekly home delivery 50 years ago and it is still the best anywhere! Great choice for your dairy products Loveless. 

I still want to encourage first time visitors to ask for seating in the original small dining room to the left of the hostess stand. This room gives you the real feel of the original and later the McCabe owned Loveless of the 70's - 90's. Most of all don't be afraid to ask questions and try different foods at Loveless. It is a true Nashville treasure.

Some people might love this but I found it horrid! Maybe because I have had real German food, but this is not even a close replica. Now I do love German food but my stomach hurt immediately upon eating the fake cheese sauce.  There was nothing real about this food, the potato dumpling was out of box paste, the noodles had no flavor at all, then that same fake cheese sauce was placed on top. With those canned onion rings in top. I tell you this food was bad, bad bad. Even the Hot Dog has a strange flavor the only thing that tasted okay was the pretzel( no sauce) and the sauerkraut.  Maybe the food would have been better had we 5-6 beers, but because we were driving it was not a good idea. Sorry we should have just grabbed a burger somewhere. The music was fun but loud as well.  Should have checked the reviews first
This is in response to owner asking when we went
Wir kamen am 15. Juli 14 um 15.30 Uhr und es gab kein Salz im Sepatzle-Wasser. Der Käse war nicht das, was wir benutzen, also wer auch immer die Soße machte, vergaß den echten Käse. Prost

Stopped into here during a business trip through Nashville because they're supposed to be famous for their biscuits and gravy. While I did really enjoy my meal, I wouldn't say the meal was much better than I've had elsewhere.  I don't get how the biscuits and gravy are famous.  I wouldn't advise you drive 30 mins out of Nashville for the food. Perhaps the nostalgia of the place is worth it?

I would say that the staff were all super friendly!  Southern hospitality at its finest!  The place does have a nice southern charm to it too.

This restaurant boosts on how all of the food is homemade southern cooking and I'm here to tell you it's absolutely not. Most of what we ordered was frozen or out of a can. I think the best thing about our whole dinner was the preserves and biscuits although the biscuits tasted like ones I've gotten from Sysco. 

My husband ordered chicken fried chicken, garlic mashed potatoes, green beans and fried green tomatoes. I ordered the meatloaf, mashed potatoes and fried okra.  My husband did eat his because he hadn't eaten today but I ate only about 1/4 of my dinner. 

I was so disappointed because I had heard so many good things about this restaurant since its revamping several years ago and I thought this would be a meat & 3 with true homecoming. If that's what they call home cooking they need to come eat with our family to see what real southern home cooking is all about.

Loveless Café is super well known in Nashville...correction...in the US. 
I thought it was an over glorified diner. I come from the state with diners in every town. So LC didn't wow me. It's super popular therefore it's super busy. 
We had virtually no wait. Our waiter was super nice. 
Each day there is a special. We were there on a Sunday so it was smoked beef brisket (we passed on it). Everything is made from scratch. They are known for their biscuits, which quite honestly, was the best part of the meal. They were indeed delicious. 
For a meal we decided on:
Southwest Omelet (3 Eggs) - Diced Onions, Peppers and Salsa with Cheddar Cheese
Southern Omelet (3 Eggs) -Diced Country Ham, Bacon or Sausage with Onions, Peppers and Cheddar Cheese
Add an extra side of sausage and more biscuits (you can request honey or sorghum). We decided on just butter. Their coffee was quite good. Prices are super reasonable. 
A nice stop on your trip to Nashville. 
They have some boutique shopping stores near by...stop in for a T-shirt.
The country fried steak here is amazing. We love it here & the service is always awesome too!!  You can't go wrong eating here.

Best fried chicken and biscuits I have ever had!  Loved the not overly hard fried chicken with just the perfect crunch.  The biscuits that are delivered to every table are light and fluffy.  As they are warm, the butter melts into the doughy goodness right away.  Then add their fresh made preserves and you are in heaven.  We had peach, strawberry and blackberry.  The peach preserves were the clear winner of the three.  I was let down though with the sides.  The hashbrown casserole was only okay.  It wasn't very hot and ended up just tasting kind of bland.  Daughter's mashed potatoes weren't mashed well and she ended up with a very large piece of whole potato in her scoop.  The creamy coleslaw wasn't very creamy and was completely unremarkable.

Our waitress was just as nice as can be and make our experience here just peachy.

Didn't expect a lot since this is inside the mall. Food was relatively pricey. I've spent time in Germany and this was a bit disappointing. They are trying very hard to make it feel like an authentic beerhaus. We had a good time and the food was decent. Probably won't be back.

My mom came in town to visit and we made a day trip out to Loveless.  I don't think we realized that it would be as busy as it was.  We parked and went in to the restaurant and got our buzzer thingy and were told it would be an hour and a half.  Normally I would have gone somewhere else, but there is so much to do there!! We spent time walking around and visiting the various shops around the restaurant.  The employees were all nice and helpful, and they ship your items for a flat rate--and you can buy items from any store and they just walk it over and put it all in one box!  Really convenient for my mom, who ordered some holiday gifts!  When we got to the restaurant it was hard to decide what to get because everything looked great!  The fried green tomatoes were crispy and delicious, and my chicken fried steak was the best I have ever had.  It was enormous.  The sides were fantastic and the biscuits--out of this world.  The nice little blueberry and lemonade drink with the moonshine shooter was a nice touch as well.  I will definitely be going back!

This place was the bomb! The only thing that bombed it down to four stars, was the ladies bathroom was worse than any roadside truck stop I've ever been in to use the bathroom. I actually rolled the legs of my jeans up to use the bathroom. Besides that, this place was the bomb dot com!!! They have drinks/beer/shots ranging from $1-$5! They also tap a keg at 8pm and you can buy a glass for $5 and have as much beer as long as the keg lasts. They had amazing live music. The crowd seemed to be a little older, but it was hysterical watching them drunk dance! Their $1 shot was called a Demon Drop which is a shot of Fireball with a cherry in it. The staff is friendly and helpful and the best part NO Cover (which was most places on Broadway). If you are someone that needs to use the bathroom, I'd only use this restroom once and pray that you don't catch an illness.

SOUND:  Honestly it sounds great!  

CLEAN:  No, it always feels sticky like whatever you touch or graze by, maybe bring some wet-naps haha!

DOOR:  I don't know, I've only ever been "on the list" with a guy that plays drums with bands.

SIZE:  I think it can pack a lot of people in, and there are some random tables and chairs.

TIP:  Go early if you want a SEAT. 

DRINKS:  I feel like they are pretty affordable, usually $5 or more. I haven't had a liquor drink, I usually get a beer and it's always been great.  Not sure how good the liquor drinks are and how the pours are.  Not sure I could recommend anything other than a bottle of something.

Overall, if there's someone you want to see here you should definitely come by!

[TLDR]A former roadside motel converted into a country-style restaurant serving stick to your ribs entrees, breakfast all day, and the best biscuits I have ever had [/TLDR]

I have been reading about this place for many years trip reports and local assessments on Roadfood.com, most especially about the biscuits, and finally made the trip down here this past week

The food there is very good.  Not great, not mind blowing, but good.  In terms of what is available on the menu, it is very similar to Cracker Barrels; but I think most every item (except the mac-n-cheese, which was surprisingly meh) here is a notch or three better than what you'd find there.

The option to dine family style is available here for groups of 4 or more

While the food did not blow me away, the biscuits most certainly did.  Moist, fluffy, delicious -- perfect.  These are served as the free bread basket and you can ask for as many refills as you'd like, and every plateful includes three different homemade jams - strawberry, blackberry, and peach, and all three are wonderful - plus real butter.  For the best experience, I'd advise ordering minimally - a little protein of your choice and a veggie side or two, or maybe a bowl of sausage gravy, and just let those biscuits be the focus of your meal.   A little tip: ask for extra jam with your biscuits, as they tend to be a tad stingy with the portions on the jams, and trustme, you'll want more.

If a place like this existed locally, we'd absolutely be regulars there.

One caveat - this place is VERY loud, even when not filled to capacity.  It is very popular and you should expect a wait to be seated even during non peak hours

5+ stars for the biscuits, everything else was 3 to 4, so overall 4 stars

Recommended

The staff is awesome. They are super friendly and will take good care of you after waiting so long for a table. Expect to wait 2 hours or more for a table. Have no fear. They have things to keep you busy while you wait. Like a couple of gift shops to explore, a huge barn to hang out in on cold days and the property is enough to enjoy the scenery. Your table will be ready in no time.

The food comes out fast. EVERYTHING IS AMAZING! The fried chicken is my favorite with cheesy hash. I love this place. If I am ever near the Nashville proximity I will make the trip to Loveless Cafe. This place is made for foodies. Must go!

I have had this on my "to try" list for a while now- my hubby HATES to wait and was hesitant to come.  We got here at 8:30 on Saturday morning and we got a front parking spot AND were escorted right to our table as we walked in . 

My 2 year old got milk, pancakes, and bacon- which he refused to eat.  Hubby took them home and said they were great.  Hubby got the sampler platter and said everything was great.  I got the city ham with egg whites (and didn't really care either- my ham was burnt and my eggs were wet and not very appetizing), but the biscuits and preserves were amazing and so was that hash brown casserole.  

We had a great breakfast and would come again for sure.  We also enjoyed walking around afterwards.

I really wanted to like this place but unfortunately I was very disappointed. Our service was lacking. The waiter barely checked on us and we had to ask other servers for wine and water refills. The sides were lacking in flavor. The fried zucchini needed salt and a dipping sauce or something. It was extremely bland. The entrees were okay but nothing special. Very over priced for what we got. We took some out of town friends here and we're really upset that we wasted a night going here. I definitely won't go back and would not recommend. We only went for dinner and didn't see a concert.
Decided to try this on a whim and so glad we did.   Incredible biscuits and homemade jellies.  Great food and service.

Amazing southern comfort food. Good service. If you are visiting Tennessee this  is a must!!! Highly recommended. Will leave you stuffed lol. The biscuits are sooooo good and always served warmed. Freshly baked out the oven. Do not forget to ask for honey. It has to be requested. Big menu to choose from. #carbNation

Lots to love at the Loveless Cafe. As the Mrs. noted, the bowl filled with pats of butter is a great harbinger of good things to come. As in, good things to spread that butter on. As in delicious biscuits. Also accompanying those biscuits is their signature strawberry, blackberry, and peach preserves. And when we finished those off, our waitress Robin brought us more, which we boxed up and took home with us.

Mrs. ordered the pork chops, which came with three, two of which went home for a future dinner. Her caramelized sweet potatoes were quite good, and the creamed corn may be the best side they make. It's certainly one of their most popular. I had the grilled catfish, none of which survived to go home in the doggy bag. Wonderful seasoning. Mac and cheese was fine, the southern grits outstanding. 

Adult beverages are available. Their featured drinks center around local moonshine which comes in a little take home souvenir mug. I opted for for the sweet peach tea moonshine and loved it. There are also many dessert choices. Mrs. had the Blueberry and Peach cobbler, of course warmed and served a la mode. I had the honey chess pie. Both most satisfying. Robin took good care of us. We had a minimal wait time, maybe 10 minutes, but there is a gift shop and general store to occupy your time which beats just sitting on a bench. 

The only knock against the Loveless may be that it's just so far from the city, you really have to go out of your way to eat there. But it was undoubtedly worth the trip.

Worth the trip and the wait.  Plenty to do while you wait with shops, etc.  Lots of places to wait.  The biscuits truly are amazing.  You'll get a big platter of them when you are seated.  I had catfish sandwich on texas toast.  It was good but the star is really the biscuits.  Had 2 sliders, a fried chicken biscuit and a pulled pork biscuit.  Pulled pork was a+++ .  Definitely go check this place out.  Wait was about an hour on a rainy saturday for brunch.

After reading the Wikipedia entry on this place, maybe my expectations were too high (read it sometime), but the biscuits were not that good.  The country ham was way too salty (I am from the South, I know what biscuits and ham are supposed to taste like).  It was pretty much standard Waffle House fare.  One saving grace - the preserves that go ON the biscuits were great.

OMG!!!  What an amazing breakfast!!!!     Came on a Wednesday morning at about 10 AM and had just about a 15 minute wait for a table of 6 which I didn't feel was very bad at all!!!  Waitress was very nice and the food came out in a very timely fashion considering it was somewhat busy.  
The biscuits came out and were the best I've ever had.  Warm and moist. Served with sides of fresh apricot, raspberry, and blackberry.  
The little country store was soooo cute.  
A must stop when in Nashville!
Definitely try the cheesy hash browns and the BBQ, so yummy!!!

What a ridiculously amazing place! I had researched Nashville prior to my vacation and the biscuits at the Loveless Cafe were one of the top foods to try on everyone's list. We hopped off the plane, got our rental car, checked into the hotel, and drove straight here and boy were we glad we came. 

We beat the evening rush by coming a bit after 5 on a weekday and were immediately sat. The menu is very extensive and it seems like they make a bit of everything. We both ordered the fried chicken (we did come to the South after all) and our biscuits arrived in the meantime. They were absolutely and utterly perfect biscuits and they came with 3 homemade jams: peach, strawberry, and blackberry. All the jams were fantastic and worked really well with the biscuits (they sell them in their gift shop and at the airport). The fried chicken was perfect and very juicy and our sides (mac and cheese, fried green tomatoes, sweet potatoes, and mashed potatoes) were top-notch. Our waitress even brought over some carrot pudding for us to try for free since she wanted us to like it, which was really nice (and tasty!). We also got a slice of coconut cream pie, a local brew, and a moonshine cocktail (complete with tiny souvenir mug), which were all great.

Bottom line: this place has amazing food and great service. It really is worth the drive out from Nashville (or other surrounding towns) and try to come on a weekday on off-peak hours to avoid the huge crowds!
