Best fried chicken and biscuits. We've gone for breakfast too and had the best experience. The environment is nice and cozy - especially in the smaller dining rooms. I can't wait to go back for a quiet morning with a warm breakfast. The shops are fun too. I had to buy some jam to take home.

While the food and staff were both very good, I was here to see a show. I was surprised that a venue in Nashville would have such poor acoustics and that the sound would be so poorly balanced. We had seats on the raised level, right on the rail, and the sound was like we were a mile away.

I happened to see Marc Cohn at the City Winery in Nashville and a couple days later at the City Winery in Chicago. The sound in Chicago was so far better that it seemed like we were seeing 2 different artists.

The Nashville location looks great but the sound would keep me from recommending this location.

I think this place is a little over hyped. The biscuits and jams are good, I'll give it that. The rest that we ate were ok (chicken & waffles, pulled pork, fried gizzards, red velvet waffles) nothing special about it, wasn't worth a 45 mins drive just to come here and eat. Now I can mark this off my list of places to eat.

Delicious! We went on a Wednesday around 9 and there wasn't a wait. We made reservations just in case! We had friends in from Germany so we ordered the all you can eat breakfast so they could sample so many things.  The biscuits were hot and very good... the preserves were excellent!! We visited the general store that sold Loveless items and more... really neat experience as it had been years since we had gone but still just as good!

First time in the south and the family took me here because I needed some fried chicken. I just have to say Owen definitely showed us what "Southern hospitality" really is like. The fried chicken here was MOUTH WATERING. The biscuits I craved the morning after. Owen mixed their good ole sugary jam with a pad of butter, turned it into "liquid gold" and let me tell you it tasted like it! Owen also gave me a metal coin with St. Anthony, saint of lost articles because he said my name is a holy name! Only in the south! Server Barbara came by our table a few times and she was so sweet. 

I'm coming back when I'm in Nashville again.

The biscuits were amazing! Our server brought us a plate of warm biscuits, which were great, but then brought us a plate of MORE biscuits straight out of the oven... heaven! Especially with butter and preserves. I had the catfish dinner plate with fried okra and fruit. I thought the catfish was well done, as well as the hushpuppies. Unfortunately, I was not a fan of the okra. the breading was very thick and heavy. My boyfriend got the pulled pork sandwich and fries.... (of course I had to try!) and both were delicious. Loved the fries. Can't wait to come back and try the breakfast menu and the desserts.... they look amazing!

Don't order the pancakes unless you like dry thick pancakes then the waffle was a beautiful golden brown as it should be but it was so thick and Doughie waffles should be airy and crispy really a waste of my money and time

I would definitely put this on par with a Cracker Barrel with larger portions and an extensive  history.  Being that we went midweek in the evening there was little to no wait.  My food was decent.  The biscuits were quite tasty (I may have evaluated about 4...)  I was not blown away by my overall experience but I am open to going back again to try the breakfast.

There's a lot of good things going at Loveless Cafe, to start, let's do a list:

1. Southern hospitality. We asked our server what's sorghum and without explaining she went ahead and brought 2 containers of plain sorghum and then a bowl of butter and sorghum and mixed it on the table to show us how it should be eaten. Try it if you like molasses or just try it for the sake of trying. Always courteous, shows up at the right time, and splitting checks - no problem. 

2. History and photos.
3. Kitsch and charm.
4. Overall good showcase of southern food: my picks were the butter and fruit jams, biscuits, fried chicken, creamed corn, hashbrown casserole, and slaw.

Country ham (as warned by our server) is VERY salty and a bit tough. Something that I thought would be amazing would be the Banana Pudding was just ok, not much vanilla wafers. Pulled pork was said to be smoked for over 12hrs gave me too much of a high expectation. Fried chicken was good, moist and lightly battered.  Food was on the salty and sweet side. 

The souvenoir shops always leave a slightly bad impression. It's a double edge sword. It's hard to take it seriously as dining, when it is part tourist destination. A long sleeved t-shirt printing of bacon striped jacket - that is pretty sweet!   I know it's all part of the show and indeed they looked like they were doing pretty well selling overpriced goods, so good for them!

Thankfully, we're given a wait time of 35min, just enough time to explore the grounds. As a package, LC should be experienced at least once: 3.3 stars.

Bbq was very good. The biscuits and gravy were very delicious and the people were very nice. I bit of a wait for the table but worth it. There's shops around while you wait so there's something to do. They also serve moonshine drinks and beer, wine and tasty stuff. Its also very pretty around the restaurant lots of roiling hills and nice trees. I recommend going there.

This is an excellent place. We went on a Saturday and, honestly, did not expect to get in anytime soon, but we were up for the wait. We have wanted to go for some time now. While waiting we toured the little shops on the campus and found several very cool Christmas presents for friends and family (NOT the corn pone stuff at that Country yatta yatta joint). The service was excellent. The food was wonderful and the biscuits to die for. One of the 10 best breakfast joints EVER!

Definitely worth the drive from Franklin.  The complimentary biscuits were the best biscuits I have ever had and if I wasn't trying to watch what I'm eating, I think the biscuits and gravy or the fried chicken would have put me into a food coma. 

Food was great and walking around the little area while waiting for our table was a lot of fun.  It was an hour wait around 1:30pm so it's nice they have stuff for you to do.  There is cornhole out front and 4 cute little shops ranging from Loveless treats and meats to souvenirs etc.

Would definitely recommend as a place to check out!

Ok,,,,, what is there to say about grandmas home cooking??? How can it be topped. I just went home in my mind with the fried chicken, green beans, Mac and Cheese, sweet potatoes, ham and pulled pork! Service was outstanding and as friendly as I have ever seen!

Yesterday was our third trip to the loveless cafe and it won't be the last.
It was all great as usual
The biscuits were so heavenly and I love the peach preserves
Fried chicken was excellent
My husband got the combo plate chicken, fried catfish and meatloaf.  The sides were all great
The pie so many choices we got the chocolate cream and pecan Excellent
The store was also great
Lots of choices love the biscuit mix , country ham and all preserve choices
Until next time dear friend

Gemaal, was the best waiter. Very attentive and always on cue with all our needs. We did the five course meal with the wine pairings and it was incredible. I will make this a must do meal every time I'm in Nashville.
This is my favorite restaurant for good comfort food. The bbq is good and love everything on the menu.

So I wanted to love this place so much since my Nashville friends talked about it. This is way far out from the downtown Nashville scene. We arrived at 8 am on a Friday morning and it was about half full (look at that, eternal optimist). We started with biscuits. The biscuits were delicious...For about 30-45 minutes. We then ordered biscuit sliders since we couldn't decide what to pick. The hash brown casserole was really tasty! 

So after our meal, we shopped at the cute stores, which I highly recommend checking out. However, it was about 5 minutes into shopping when our stomachs exploded. Luckily, there are bathrooms on site! I'm glad we tried the food, but I think my stomach isn't equipped to process it.

There should be a yelp page for the biscuits alone... Best ever!

Found this place on yelp while on a trip to Nashville. 
The food was delicious but the biscuits... oh... Em... gee! They bring plates full out to the table. They even sell the mix online.

Great place and great experience!

This place is extremely busy and has had over an hour wait every time I have been here. Which is not too often because the food is really not that great. Yes, it's cute and I like the gift shop, but it's a restaurant. Good food at a good price should keep people coming. On a positive note, servers are really friendly and sweet.

Fantastic.  Can't wait to go back.  Expect a long wait.  We showed up at 1pm and it was still a 45min wait.  Split the Southern Sampler Plater with my wife (fried chicken, catfish, and ham as meats/hash brown casserole and marinated cucumbers and onions for the sides).  Also ordered side of sausage gravy to go with the amazing free biscuits and a pimento and fried green tomato biscuit.

Ignore that guy who said the sound sucked for Psychedelic Furs. I imagine he must have been smoking something gone bad. The sound was perfectly mixed, the seats were fabulous, the ambiance on point, the food was spectacular- risotto balls, pasta and steak had our whole table gushing with every bite ("This is SOOOOO good!"), and the wine, wow, the wine. This place has a sommelier and he knows his shit. The recommendations were perfect. Thank you Nicholas and Josh for the stellar service! And to those whining about the price, all I can say is "duuuuuh!" It's an upscale joint, y'all. If you want to pay less for your food and drink, go to a honky tonk.

We asked "the locals" for breakfast recommendations and this place took the cake, hands down! We were not disappointed!! 

My husband and I and another couple ordered Family Style. This was an all you can eat family style plate table service that included: hash brown casserole, sliced ham, bacon (too smokey for this Northerner), eggs, grits, and the most delicious homemade biscuits and preserves!

I could have eaten a plate of biscuits and preserves all by myself or at least wish I could have if I wasn't filling up in all the other deliciousness! 

Now, there was a wait but here are little shops to visit and free lemonade stand...to be cont...

I took my mother here for Mother's Day and we ate dinner there before the show and watched Citizen Cope perform afterward. I read on help before that the food wasn't very good and it was true. My mom and I both ordered the burger, which was just okay. However, it's the safest option on the menu so if you're going to eat there then order the burger. We ordered the potatoes Au gratin and they were undercooked. It was disappointing. My mom ordered the Chardonnay on tap and it was just okay. Luckily mom is happy about anything and liked her food and wine. I just expected more for the price. Also, the $20, 2.5 glasses of wine option consisted of maybe a typical glass and a half of wine. It was not much at all. The food overall was a 2.5/5 stars. 
    The waitresses and staff were fine. They could step up their customer service skills and friendliness just a tiny bit more. 
     The music was the best part. Excellent artists. We sat in the middle on the floor and it was still hard to see. Not great acoustics in the place. 
    All the negativity aside, it was a beautiful venue and great concept. If they could improve their acoustics, rewrite their menu, make some staff changes, this place could be the talk of the town.  

 All in all I suggest
1. Bringing $5 cash to valet
2. Order the burger if you're gonna eat there 
3. Save money and eat somewhere else
4. Drink wine there 
5. Sit close so you can see and hear (it's worth spending a bit more) 
Enjoy your time
A little bit of a tourist trap but pretty darn good food, awesome location and really nice people. I'll definitely go back.

Big breakfast, chicken and BBQ menu!   All the food and service was superb.   Plan on a short wait but there's plenty to see and do around the complex.  Smoke house and shop have lots to see.  Several shops with unique gift items from the area, or Loveless recipe products!   Our meals were all very good and large portions.  Fried chicken is to die for!  BBQ and even breakfast all day met everyone's desires.   A cool stop when around Nashville, highly recommended!

Worth the 40 minute drive from where we were staying. I fugured there would be a wait but,  we got right in.  Very friendly staff. The place just makes you feel like you are eating in someone's dining room, so welcoming.  Hot biscuits the minute you sit down and they were amazing. Breakfast was great too though tourist prices. Everything was fresh and well prepared. Cool grounds to walk around too in order to get rid of a few calories before the trip back. Highly reccomended.

I've eaten at Loveless many times, and have had quite a few different dishes, but I'll try to touch on some highs and lows. Long waits are to be expected, especially on weekends and at traditional meal times.

I'm a meatloaf connoisseur. It's one of the dishes I use to judge a restaurant. Theirs is good. Not the best I've had but far from the worst.
The mac n cheese is pretty standard Velveeta and elbow macaroni. 
The creamed corn tastes more like a corn pudding to me...a bit too sweet and custardy. 
Fried green tomatoes are not good. Thin and tough.
Mashed potatoes are good.
Hash brown casserole is decent.
The BBQ pork is good. Not great, but not bad. 
Fried chicken is very good.
Breakfast is always good, though the grits are a disappointment. And the biscuits just haven't been the same since Carol Fay died a few years back.

They have a liquor license. Try the Bloody Mary, then go over to the store and buy a jar of the mix for $10. It's worth it.

Breakfast review.  We went on a Monday - no waiting and no crowds.  I hear the weekends can be crazy.

Breakfast was good, tasty and fresh.  Scrambled eggs were some of the best restaurant scrambled eggs I have had.  Biscuits were light and fluffy.  Probably not too much healthy food on the menu, but then it is southern cooking. 

The cafe itself is very cute.  The history of the cafe and motel is cool.  Glad Nashville rallied to save it.  Clean restrooms are always a good sign and at the Loveless Cafe they were clean.

Well.....It's not really conveniently located.  But I am so glad we took the time to drive out of our way to visit this long time, old fashioned flash from the past café.

The drive out is interesting, we took back roads and enjoyed the scenic drive.  Once you arrived, it was clear from the parking lot, Loveless is very popular, the parking lot was packed.  Surprisingly, the wait for a table was not long.  But making a selection of what to order was difficult.  The bf got the fried chicken.  I ended up getting the pulled pork.  It was delicious.  For my sides, I got creamed style corn (win) and mac and cheese (good, too).  The biscuits were a nice surprise, the are actually fairly small, so you can't feel too guilty about eating them.  Service was very friendly.  Even so friendly, we ended up with biscuits and jam to go for later.  This place really is great.

Went back after a poor initial visit. Sat down on the main floor for Steve Earle and had a much better experience. The service was attentive, and while we didn't have a full meal, the apps we did order hit the spot. Most importantly, the sound in the room was fantastic, especially great for Steve's solo acoustic set. Will definitely be back.

Best breakfast I have had in years! We went during the week so the wait was only 15 minutes. I ordered the sampler and everything was perfect, the gravy was great, but the highlight was the biscuits and preserves. Service was incredible, the staff friendly, and the atmosphere homey. It was so good we bought a pie to go, some preserves, and a dozen biscuits (they gave us the biscuits). Only problem for me is they are near Nashville and I live in California but they make Tennessee very tempting!
This is a very fun atmosphere, the food and booze is great. Its a bit pricey but makes for a fun night out. Get the pork knuckle.

So for the first time in a long time I can say these words: believe the hype. This place is as good as every one says it is. If you're in the Nashville area you must stop by to have a meal here. 

Yes, the wait will be incredibly long -- so don't come starving or you will give up and leave. We had over an hour long wait, but it was well worth it. Plus. there's an entire property to explore, which includes two gift shops (one featuring free samples of food items and appetizers), cornhole games, picnic tables, and more.

The food is absolutely delicious. Tastes like a meal at grandma's house. I went here for breakfast/brunch on a Saturday. However, I really really wish I had a chance to experience for dinner. I look forward to making this one of my regular stops when visiting Nashville.

So, we really like the food at Loveless, particularly the biscuits and jam. Anything I've had on the breakfast menu (French toast, pancakes, chicken and waffles) has been great. The bbq is also top notch. Desserts are also amazing-- especially the blackberry pie and banana pudding. I would not recommend the BLT, even with the fried green tomato. Nothing special. My favorite side surprisingly is the creamed corn and the broccoli salad (when they have it). Yum!

This would be a five star restaurant except for how busy they can be and the so-so quality of the servers. Most have been good but we've had a few who haven't been (and when we were there at off-peak times). We live close so we never go during busy times because it's really not worth a two hour wait.

The Biscuits!!!! Ahhhh!  I could just eat a whole plate of them!  This place is ALWAYS busy, be prepared to wait. Food is fresh and service is friendly.  Just good old fashioned comfort food!  Don't miss the hash brown casserole!

Ya gotta love the Loveless. The wait is worth it! The food is perfect, every time! The offer up amazing food, great service and a fun atmosphere. I've eaten at The Loveless countless times and I'm always impressed!

Another place we went to after seeing it on the Travel Channel. It was pretty far out of town, $20 uber ride. The building and surrounding area was pretty cool. Little tourist trappy but nice. The food was good, not sure I'd make the trek out there again

A must see for Nashville. Gift shops, restaurant, resort, and breakfast all day! Moonshine shots, unlimited biscuits with three types of jams, and outdoor seating if you want. Service was good and prices are great. This was recommended by a tour guide and although it's in the mountains, it was worth the trip!

First off, I'm a southern boy through and through.  I love good southern cooking more than damn near anything else around. That said, I'm no stranger to good food and most of the time, they're not reinventing the wheel when you eat at southern food joints.  When my friends picked me up from Nashville to head to their home in Alabama, we stopped here for dinner.  Their biscuits, oh dear god, their biscuits.  Damn.  I ended up getting smoked pork chops/loin that was glazed in their homemade peach preserves.  This is damn near holy divinity.  As my chef says "god spoke to me".  I really do think, if there was a god, he'd tell you to eat here.  I had enough leftovers that I took with me, I had breakfast for two days straight with the addition of a couple scrambled eggs.  When you walk in, you see a wall/walls of autographed photos from the Nashville scene in there.  I'm looking forward to my trip back to Nashville just to eat here......at least once.

Be prepared for a loud, lively experience! Unfortunately, I went there thinking I was going to have a nice, relaxing diner! (Not the restaurants fault!) I had the fish and chips and wasn't pleased - but hey that's what you get when you order non-German foods from a German restaurant. My hubby had a good experience though!

This is a great concert venue . They have great sound so you can truly hear the music! However DO NOT EAT here!! I've learned my lesson after giving it TWO tries!! I was hoping to give them a second chance after my first experience wasn't so great, but unfortunately they failed me again . Both times we had terrible service and both times the menu was not full of great options. For instance there was not a single steak or chicken dish on the menu . There was " bone marrow" who wants that?? Call me a redneck but no thank you ! I ordered the Napa Slaw( that's right , slaw) for dinner because there were hardly any options. They had pizza and my husband got that , it was over cooked . Here's the deal, go, drink their amazing wines, but go to dinner somewhere else first!!!
We loved this place. Great atmosphere and the Giant Pretzels are a must. The staff was very friendly wearing costumes and our food was very quick. We went here twice on our trip

Good music, cheap drinks, and great employees. 
$3Drafts $4Bottles $5DoubleShotz 
When in Rome....you know the rest.
Stop in I feel like you'll love it.
Operating on the very real premise that a real trip to Nashville must necessarily involve biscuits from Loveless Cafe, we scratched that itch this morning. It's still the same, wonderful!

A beautifully created night spot. It's a perfect 10 on the "cool" rankings. However I probably won't be back and here's why. I went to a show there recently in the upstairs portion. For "regular folks" like me, drinking the the basic house wines are plenty adequate.  That way you can get your cost per glass under $10 and not feel like you're getting ripped off too bad. Well, the waitress explains that they don't offer their house selections upstairs. You have to order from the rest of the wines starting at $40 and going way up from there. This is BS and they know it. They don't offer their cheaper menu to patrons of a show because they know those people are a captive audience. They aren't going anywhere and they are going to order something, so why not put the screws to them and remove the cheaper portion of the menu? Great business sense! Well, you got me once but that will be the last time. Additionally, my tab came out to $59 after I ordered only the one $40 bottle of wine. They were trying to run us out of the place the second the show ended so I didn't dispute it. I just signed it and left. Too bad because it's such a neat place. They won't miss me as I'm not their target customer. The whole thing was a racket.

If anyone has ever given this place less than 5 stars, YOU A LIE!!!!!

Incredible experience - went on a weekday for dinner. No wait. Drink orders were delivered with warm, flaky biscuits and a trio of preserves (blackberry, peach, strawberry - ranked in that order). Server was so polite and helped me and my elderly father navigate the menu/side options and offered to bring us another side if what we ordered was not to our liking. Pa ordered country fried steak, greens, and hashbrown casserole (a must) while I got the BBQ pork atop cornbread hoe cakes with coleslaw. Cannot go wrong with their BBQ! We passed on dessert because Pa couldn't stop eating biscuits and wanted to drink the blackberry preserves. Left stuffed, well worth the stop!

Walked in at 10 minutes to closing without even realizing and they still sat us, the hostess was a bit begrudging and so we finally figured it out. The waitress was wonderful and still super helpful. It's definitely a cute little kitschy spot and certainly novel. There's two gift shops and two event spaces. There's a cornhole game for the kiddos and face cutout picture props too (no idea what those are actually called). To get the last star: get rid of the funky odor upon entry, don't be snarky when taking Mamés but kindly alert patrons you close soon, and maybe moisten the biscuits a wee bit. They were good but so dry. Overall: if you love kitsch and history, check it out.

Just went there last week . I have been eating there since it was really a cafe , over 30 years ! It has always been great until now .My server was a white guy with a shaved head and husky build . When he dropped off my water after a 15 minute wait , I was ready to order . Obviously , he did not want to take my order . I asked him a question about the sides when ordering and he literally just turned and walked away from me without saying a word . He proceeded to do what he wanted to and came back after several minutes . He was extremely rude , at a level I don't think I have ever seen with a server . The fried chicken came and was good except that the breast had an area of blood inside about 1 1/2 x 1 1/2 inches and was raw . The server did not ever return to check on anything or fill my water . I asked the hostess as she passed by for the manager . He was an older white man working in the kitchen area . I told him the situation with food and server . His only response was "do you want another piece of chicken?" in an annoyed manner . I said "no" and asked him not to send the server back to my table .  He said the server was the only one who could take payment and walked away . That was it , no apology for anything or any caring for the situation in any way . I regularly take groups there for business related meetings as well as family/friends . The server made no comment whatsoever when taking payment . He never at any time asked me if I needed anything or gave me more drink . I will never go back . By the way , I did not say anything to the manager until after the meal was eaten . I also told him I did not want free meal or anything like that . I did not want anything free or anything like that but the offer was never given . I paid full price for everything . I think this is the first time that I have not tipped a server . I am also in the service business.

Among the many delicious things that are on their menu, the thing that stands out most is the biscuits which is what they're most known for.  What stood out to me about these biscuits was fluffiness of the biscuits and the buttery taste that is well complemented by the jams they serve.  Everything else on the menu is generally cooked well, but the typical southern fare.  As far meats go, I have had their quarter dark fried chicken, pork chops, and pulled pork barbecue and was not disappointed.  However, I have heard that the chicken has been hit or miss from reliable sources so order the fried chicken at your own discretion.  I find the best time for a meal here is breakfast.

Another thing that stands out is that even though the place is a restaurant, they also have a barbecue pit and a souvenir shop where you can buy their jams, biscuit mix, bacon, and other tourist trap souvenir items.  

Service overall is generally pretty good and friendly, the food arrives fairly quick, and they are kind enough to give you a small plate of biscuits as a complimentary appetizer.

The only downside here is the wait because after 10AM on a Saturday, this place becomes very packed and an hour wait is not uncommon.  Easter Sunday is the worst since wait time typically exceeds 3 hours by 9AM.  

Food: 4
Service: 4
Price: 4
It's the Loveless!!  It's sooooo good!  Best friend chicken in town.  And the biscuits!  Oh my the biscuits.  Don't eat before you go so you can load up on them.

This place was one of the places recommended by magazines/sites and trip advisor. We didn't think much of it because it just seemed like any other southern eateries, but I am so glad we went there. This place was recommended by every local we met, they couldn't stop talking about it and after we ate there we understood why! The place is very homey and cozy, though casual. I loved the ambiance and it's set up! Our server was extremely nice and he suggested pretty much our entire menu. As soon as you sit down he brought us some fresh biscuits and jams and they were both delicious! The biscuits were fresh, warm, soft, and creamy! Jams seemed like they were homemade. Everything we ordered on the menu; fried chicken, grilled and fried fish were fresh and so so tasty! (we all liked the fried chicken better at Hattie B's but here it was delicious too). Sides we ordered were fried okra (YUM) and creamed corn (again YUM)! I am so glad we went there and it's definitely a place to visit when in Nashville!!

This place is quite a drive and for a pretty disappointing end. The weather was beautiful so thankfully we could order "to go" and sit on a picnic table to eat instead of waiting the 2.5 hours to eat inside. Yes 2.5 hours. The chicken and waffles was ok. The eggs were delicious and the homemade preserves were wonderful. I would skip this tourist trap in a heartbeat.

What stupidly good fun: Proust, everyone!! 
The food here is actually pretty damned excellent for a small chain and the vibe is like 24/7 Oktoberfest---this German lass is officially smitten! The authentic dishes/beers/sauces are expertly executed and laid out and the service here was quite superb from start to finish. 

And hello, there's fun entertainment too!! Yes indeed, I'm the cheeseball who will gladly do the chicken dance while chomping on a big sausage and slurping a boot of the good brews. It's family friendly while still being good all-aged fun too, which is truly tough balance to find, but somehow this joint manages to do all that in spades.

Also, if you're LUCKY....and if you're a lush like me....you'll get called onto stage to do a complimentary shotski. So you've been warned, fellow party people: come here to get sauced and bossed and stuffed full of schnitzel! Das all good!!

If I could give them a 100 stars I would. In February I decided to have a small and intimate dinner party to commemorate a milestone birthday. I sent my inquiry and Alex responded. I went down, looked at the space and fell in love. It was quaint and intimate enough for what I wanted to do. Alex was amazing from start to finish. She saw my vision and helped me achieve exactly what I wanted. I was working on a budget and while I went over, $700, it was definitely worth it and the ideas that Alex added, made a super classy and more special touch. On my actual date, this past weekend, Alex was out of town, however, from my arrival to my departure, from valet, to the Sommelier, Blake and our dedicated waitress, I can't find one complaint. I opted for buffet style, southern style dinner and when I tell you the food was amazing, hot and tasty. Delicious, is definitely an understatement. I will definitely be visiting the City Winery more often and I am also planning a wine tour and will be joining their wine club. Never have I been blown away, by such professionalism and their attention to detail is and was unmatched. THANK YOU, City Winery, Alex, Blake and Ms. A for making my 40th, one of the best moments of my life. There isn't anything that you could have done to make me any more happy, satisfied or make this experience any more enjoyable.

First time reviewer and what a great place to begin with. I travel for work a lot, and I tend to use Yelp to find those can't miss places. This place however, was based on a recommendation from a local.  And thank goodness she did. 

I went on a Tuesday evening with a coworker. The service was great, our server, a young college aged man, was very helpful, funny, and extremely polite. He quickly brought us some biscuits and wow, they're as good as anyone can advertise them to be. The jams are just great too. I ordered the friend chicken (half) with mashed potatoes and mac n cheese. I'm a little ashamed that I licked my plate cleaned, while inhaling a few dozen biscuits. I did leave Loveless with an overwhelming feeling of joy and shame. 5 stars no doubt.

Love the Loveless.  It's a great slot for locals. S tourists.
The wait can be daunting so come early or later.
Best biscuits in the area.  Amazing breakfast and just as good lunch and dinner

Be careful your bill can add up quickly.  I've lived in Germany 3 times so my view might not be fair.  I have a hard time paying $3.50 for 2 slices of Rye bread when it always came with the meal in Germany.  
The Schnitzel was large and tender, pretzels large and hot, potato cakes yummy and Bier cold.
Oh my gosh what a fun experience and great food!  Loved the friend chicken.
This place just doesn't have good food. I've been here three different times and each time I've been let down. The skinny........wait 1-2 hours and have bad food.

We had a great breakfast at Loveless.

The biscuits are perfect! Tender, buttery, salty. The home made preserves are delicious. We may have left with a pint of the blackberry preserves.

I had fried pork chop breakfast. Don't get this is you plan on eating again that day. It was great. Two well seasoned pork chops with gravy on the side and two over easy eggs. Comes with a side of your choice.

My wife got the ham and eggs. The ham was a bit salty for my taste but with the gravy and egg yolk it was delicious. 

The service was good and friendly. I really can't say enough good things about this place. You should go too!

Totally worth the ride and wait. Biscuits are amazing. I ordered the fried chicken with cream corn and mac & cheese. Incredible. I'm not a big cream corn fan but the waitress, Tammy (who was super sweet), suggested we try it and it was great! We LOVED it. The barbecue sauce was so good that we all bought our own bottles to take home from the gift shop. The fudge pie was tasty as well. Oh and the Hams and Jams gift shop is adorable and full of great items. If I ever come back to Nashville, it's to come eat at Loveless Cafe.
Average food, super slow service, overpriced for the tourists.  Nothing to see here.

Love me some Loveless!! Always great food and customer service! They have every kind of mouth watering southern soul food you can think of. They serve bloody Mary's & fun cocktails as well. It's definitely a family style restaurant with lots of fun gift shops. Restaurant still fantastic after all these years. Be prepared to have long wait time if you go at certain times & days of the week. Lots to do on grounds tho while you wait so just make sure you have a snack or are tithed over. Thanks Loveless for all that you do!

Yes I am a fan of Loveless and get silly when walking in the front door. Could be the checkered table cloths that triggers instant salivation. Mmmm we're talking fresh made biscuits and peach and strawberry preserve as starters and lots of down home meat and three to follow. Yessireedy Yesindeedy I love this place. While on a holiday from Australia I came saw and ate here and I love it for its down home vibe. It's usually crowded and it's typical to wait for a table to be ready. No problem cos there's a grocery and gift store perfect to kill time and stock up on some neat gifts and souveniers. While waiting to be seated I got me some grand souvineers that travelled well from Nashville to Sydney and back again. Got a nifty red guitar-shaped fly swatter and an oven mit. Still got em and have swatted a few Australian and Nashville flies too so these work just dandy. OK back to the food. Delicious. Smoked ham, turkey, fried chicken and all the usual suspect sides. Got tourists and visitors? Take them to Loveless.
Fabulous way to lose a lot of money quickly. Staff seems too cool to help you and everything is overpriced. It's a necessary evil given the great acts that come through.
Delicious and wonderful as always. The biscuits and blackberry jam are the best ever!
Great food & great history. Be able to eat here and understand the history behind the place really made the experience better. The biscuits are sooooo addicting but worth it.

Holy smokes, everything was so delicious that I ate too fast and had to go to bed after :)

I got the biscuit sampler with bbq, fried chicken, country ham and sausage as my four options. On top of the biscuits they brought to the table, I had a lot of bread in a short period of time! My boyfriend got the chicken and waffles, which were huge, full of flavor and completely worth the trip outside of Nashville.

Make sure to check out the various gift shops on the property and the barn. It was set up for a wedding and looked gorgeous!

A must visit in Nashville and worth the hour and a half wait! If you have to wait there are lots of little stores in site to visit. The food is delicious... I mean the biscuits.. THE BISCUITS! To die for. You can even see them make them! 

...if you're lucky, you might spot a celebrity. I heard they frequent this cafe.
BEST Biscuits, Fried Chicken and Creamed Corn I've Ever had!! I stayed in downtown Nashville and drove nearly every day to go to the Loveless Café.  It's worth the drive.  INCREDIBLE!!!!!
Joe was an amazing host! City Winery made our bachelorette weekend start off with a bang

This is one of my new places to frequent. The food is really good and the place is huge with a great atmosphere. They have fun musical performances. The woman who sings and plays most days is really fun and talented. Kevin is one of the managers and he's a really nice guy who cared about our experience. All of the servers we had were quick and helpful. Check it out! Get a brat!

This review is for their mail order store only. We ordered their ham slices for our Easter dinner. Amazingly, they could be shipped unrefrigerated which really cut down on shipping costs. They have flat rate shipping no matter how much you order which is nice. In addition to the ham I couldn't resist the Piggy Pecans which are pecans smothered in pancake syrup with bacon bits! Those were incredible. The ham was nicely marbled but way too salty for my taste. Served it with biscuits and red eye gravy (recipe was on the ham slice package) and black eyed peas. A nice meal. Very reasonable prices!

The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because there is always a 45 - 90 minute wait for a table. With that said, I have yet to have something on the menu that wasn't delicious!! Worth the wait but be prepared because you will wait. The place is cozy and has cute shops to look in while you wait. The fried chicken is my favorite and the biscuits are amazing!! I am a local and have been several times.

In my first visit to the famous Loveless Cafe I went with the Southern Classic that is Country Fried Steak, mashed potatoes, and fried okra. The breading was somewhat different than I was used to and this was a good thing. It made the dish set itself apart from the standard. It was a bit lighter breading that was just about perfect. The mashed potatoes where the perfect consistency and the fired okra was great.

The biscuits that come as a starter before the meal where absolutely excellent. They are from an original recipe of the Loveless family from the 1950's. They come with homemade blackberry, strawberry, and peach jelly as well as local honey.

A little bit off the beaten path from downtown Nashville but well worth the drive.

5 STARS JUST FOR THE AMAZING BISCUITS

I don't care how long you have to wait, how many hills and weird turns I had to take to get here, AND HOW FREAKING COLD IT WAS. These biscuits made it ALL worth it.

It's a Southern institution that I am shocked is actually not more popular than it already is. 

That said, I would skip the fried chicken (it was tasteless) and just go for the fried catfish, the creamed corn, the baked beans. Although the pulled pork was great too.

YUM.

I've seen a lot there over the passed decade. Great shows, good people. This Saturday night at a show with Weekend Jimmy we noticed a male gay couple that was being very publicly affectionate. About midway through the show, they started frenching...Now I'm no prude, but any self-respecting bar would put a stop to anything like that ; gay or not. But, that didn't happen. It just got worse as the show went on. Rather than make a scene, we left. Sent Mike an email and his response was basically "we'll miss you; or not".

So there ya go. Nashville's gay scene would be embarrassed.

My family and I went here for breakfast on a weekday. Love the experience; the store owners are very nice, the decor inside the cafe is great and the staff is very friendly. The biscuits were delicious and we all really liked the hashbrown casserole side, but other than that the food was pretty standard - and a bit pricey for your average breakfast. All in all, we were happy with the stop, but would probably try a different breakfast spot next Nashville visit.

The food is spectacular and the service is outstanding. If you are looking for good homestyle southern food then look no further. The price is a bit steep but you get what you pay for. You get to keep the moonshine side car jars, and the portions are huge. And the 14 hour slow roasted pulled pork melts in your mouth. Don't go to Nashville without eating here.

Such a cute place!  Friendly, helpful service.  We are from the west coast and had no idea what sorghum was until we ate at the Loveless Cafe.  The food was good but I have had better.  The chocolate pie was amazing.  We purchased their dessert cookbook and everything I have made from it has been outstanding.

This place is a bit of drive outside of Nashville but the place has a lot of charm. Food is made from scratch. The biscuits and jams are awesome. There are a lot if little shots around the restaurant as well to visit.

You can't go wrong here...southern cookin at its best. 

The hospitality was spot on. 

We order family style (fried chicken, grilled pork, fried okra, Mac and cheese, and hash brown casserole)...you know...health food...for the soul. 
The dessert was coconut cream pie and apple pie...oh then there's the biscuits. OMG!!!

We also tried their country fried steak...really good. 

So that's it.  If you want real southern cookin, then you need to go here. 

Don't debate it...just go. 
If you have a long line just stay; that means it's with it.

I know it is comfort food and mostly fried and sauced but it is southern food done well. When I want to splurge on calories/indulge or take out of town friends to a place with food they won't get at home I go here. It is worth the (usually) long wait, i.e. from the fried chicken, to the fresh out if the oven hot biscuits with local jams, made on site blue cheese dressing, and sinfully satisfying pies (if you have the room). They serve amazing brunches too but I usually go later for the fried chicken. I enjoy browsing in the various stores while I wait.

Yes, the biscuits and jelly were amazing but that's about all for me! Both are def made fresh. I've never had anything like them. They're complementary with some orders but you could enjoy them by themselves with coffee for breakfast- filling. I ordered the chicken and waffles. The waffles were too thick & that made them hard to enjoy. The chicken was huge! It's definitely a good choice if you have a huge appetite that early in the morning. 3 stars for the biscuits but I wasn't impressed by anything else. The drive is out of the way even if you are driving into/out of Nashville. The staff was decent. Stopped by around 9am  on a Friday morning so there wasn't a wait.
Enjoyed the ride through the local area via GPS too.  The food is superb. Pimento cheese and green fried tomatoe biscuit is awesome.  Sausage omelet was also excellent.

I loved the winery when it first opened up.  But I think it has gone down since then.  I have never felt like I was a cheap person, but their focus on trying to nickel and dime you to death is glaringly obvious.  $5 to self park yourself in their lot?  Who does that?  Then there was the food.  I've been to a number of shows there and thought the food was good.  Ordered a burger the other night and the bun had to be at least 3 or 4 days old.  I worked in restaurants for 15 years.  No self respecting kitchen would send a bun out like that.  And if they couldn't tell, they should seek another career path.  The thing was as hard as a rock.  Next is the wine.  Even buying their cheapest house wine by the carafe comes to $10 a glass.  I hate to tell them but BOTA box wines are better than what they make. Then to further their cause in pursuit of eeking out money, they've started making some shows like this one a Vinofile only show which means you have to pay $75 to be a member to even buy tickets.  I had to laugh because the venue was only 40% full.  

It's sad, because this place could be so awesome, but it appears whoever is running this place can't see the forest for the trees.

This place is awesome.  On our first visit, my husband took a picture of the sign and fell in a gulch (LOL).  He had (and finished) the sampler platter, I had the fried chicken.  You really can't go wrong with anything here.

The second time, I drove straight here from the airport (ok, I picked up my daughter) and headed over.  They knew I wasn't from here because I ordered iced tea (not sweet), but food is great, everyone's nice.

I will be back there in a few weeks - can't wait!!!

This place is definitely a Southern experience! The biscuits are amazing, and I loved the peach preserves in particular. There's also a Loveless store where you can grab some preserves (and more) to take home with you! It's a great place for large groups, though of course expect a wait in the evenings.
Worth the wait...and be prepared to wait.   Best breakfast in the middle of nowhere.   Bon apatite.
Awesome biscuits, great wait staff, nice atmosphere.  Try the blackberry preserves.  Watch out for the long lines Saturday morning.

I have been coming to Nashville for 6 years now and I always come to Big Shotz every single time! If your looking for a fun and friendly environment with great life music this is a great place to go. This year I went and I had more than a great time. My favorite bartender Brin was truly amazing . Very helpful and kind! I will def be back because of the staff! Drinks weren't pricey and the music was great! If you want to dance your butt off upstairs is a lot of fun to. That opens later in the evening ! I will be back in two months and this will be my first stop! Thank you Big Shotz for making this trip so memorable! Thank you Brin! I'll see you for my birthday in 2 months

I'll start on a positive note; the venue is beautiful! There is a huge wine selection, including 450 bottles, and several wines made in house that are on tap and served by the glass. The cocktail list is also good - I have the La Fleur and it was wonderful. The server was attentive and friendly and knowledgeable about the menus. The food, was very subpar. We were really excited about the menu, so we ordered lots of apps - the burrata, duck tacos, charcuterie, pork belly. All were mediocre at best. I ordered the filet and it was less than average. I didn't have the highest expectations, because it's not a steakhouse, but for $35 I expected a little more than average. The filet was not tender, little flavor, and appeared to be  less than the 7 oz advertised (not confirmed). Overall, I would go back for drinks (it's a winery, it's what they're good for), but not food. 3 stars because the server was great and drinks were good.

Biscuits.  Don't even question giving them a try with their blackberry jam/preserves - what have you.

The portions are fairly large.  I had the fried chicken salad with ranch.  It didn't even look like I made an attempt after my attempt.

I drove across the country for my bucket list/birthday/I bought a new car/hey why not and stopped here on the way from Raleigh NC to Los Angeles.Spent half my budget on gifts and food. Well worth it. Everyone was really nice, the biscuits were delicious, coffee hot and I just might make the drive out again. MMM. I love you, Tennessee.

Good food and fun destination. Love the little shops surrounding the diner. And it's a good thing, because you will wait a bit for your table. Nice to have the shops to browse, and they have corn hole games set up on the lawn.

Food was good, but no "WOW" factor. Just a good meal well prepared. The raves about the biscuits are a joke. They are indistinguishable from frozen store biscuits. 100% Pop-N-Fresh.

Be prepared to get rushed, they are ALL about table turnover, and will attempt to hurry you along. And will get very snotty if you linger.  Our waitress was very attentive, and friendly, but got chilly very quick when we pointed out she got our order wrong. I also asked for hot sauce, waited a long time, and had to remind her, which got me some eye rolling. 20 minutes after seating us she was so adamant about moving us along she practically handed us our coats. 

Frankly, the homey vibe feels like a sham, they are all about volume, volume, volume, and turning tables as fast as possible. Sadly, this place has the "Too famous to fail" attitude many successful places have, that they don't need to take care of you because the sheer volume of business they get makes the quality of the dining experience irrelevant.
Excellent southern food! Plan to spend all your calories for the day on the biscuits! It's worth it.

This was my first time trying German food and it really didn't wow me. Maybe it wasn't authentic I don't know i never had real German food but I ordered the Wurst Plate which had 2 sausages that you can pick from and a side of sauerkraut and potato salad. It wasn't that great. My boyfriend ordered the Pork Schnitzel which was pan seared breaded pork and it just tasted like fried unseasoned pork. If I had to come here again I would just order beer and an appetizer.
The most delicious food in Nashville! Great service, warm welcoming, feels like home! Biscuits are out of this world and the food is fast and delicious!

Lunch, desserts and service were all very good, 4+ stars, I'd say. The reason I'm docking them 2-stars is their posting of No Weapons signs. It seems to have been proven over time that a good guy with a gun is not a threat to anyone. I'll not return for that reason.

I went to Rocketown for a  rock/metal concert, which was placed in the white building across the street. Room was spacious enough for the number of people there and everything sounded good. There's a good bit of parking nearby.

My husband and I have been here several times since they've opened.  My husband LOVES the pretzels. I will have to agree - they are REALLY good. The other food we've tried has been great too. They had a chili on special one time that was the best.  I wish it was on the menu regularly. The beers are great and the Bavarian Mule is my absolute favorite drink there.  The majority of staff are awesome, too!  The only things keeping me from giving 5 stars are the prices are a tad high on SOME of the items, and the last couple times we went in it was super warm inside.  (No one likes to sweat while they eat....OR work!)  Definitely give this place a shot if you want a fun German experience!!!

Authentic German food. My wife and her family came with me here and they have all been to October fest in Germany and said that the food was spot on. I highly recommend the Black Forest schnitzel. It was delicious. Also happy hour is from 8pm until close daily. Get a 1L beer then. It's a good deal. Service was great too.

I love this place! Our waitress was extremely friendly and helpful with recommendations. 

While waiting you can walk around and visit their little shops and take cute photos. 

The food was fantastic! 

It does get busy though so be prepared to wait for a little bit or go at a off time.

Biscuits, peach preserves, blackberry preserves and grits were delicious. Country ham has the fecund farm flavor which was great, though unexpected. Cheese grits and scrambled eggs were not that good. Great ambiance and history. Store had lots of menu items for sale. The bisquits are so good that I could easily gain weight by eating them everyday.
I love this place! Our waitress is always so nice and helpful. We never have to wait because we go on off hours, early dinner/late breakfast.

We love the food here. They have the best biscuits you will ever eat.  I always order the fried chicken and hashbrown casserole and my husband always gets something different and has never disliked anything.

Really enjoyed this venue , food, and service. We will definitely return! Had 1/2 carafe of wine, the risotto balls and a flatbread. All were very good, brought out promptly and reasonably priced. Didn't mind the $5 valet as that seems cheap to me and love not fooling with parking, worth the money everyday. It was slightly odd sharing a table with people since we had 2 tickets but it was a table for 4. However, we chatted and had a lovely time. Think we may have found our go to date night spot especially when a favorite is in town. Love living in Nashviile!
Cracker Barrel if it did not go corporate. You are a fool if you pass up a visit here.

This review is solely about the service observed and received. This has nothing to do with the food (see last review). We came on a Friday morning. The wait for 2 was 1 hr 20 mins. Okay, not surprising. The staff was minimally friendly...I hate to give that much credit but I don't know what else to say. We ordered to-go again to sit outside on one of their (now) few picnic tables. As we sat waiting we noticed a lot of people wouldn't wait almost 90 minutes for a table, also not surprising. This astonished me as there were 7 empty tables in our line of sight...maybe they were short staffed? Almost every time someone came in and wouldn't wait, the host staff gave smile and then an exaggerated roll of the eyes. Anyway, our food was quickly delivered and I was surprised...I was even more surprised when our steak was well done (we asked for medium), and one of our entire meals was missing. My spouse went back in to tell them what happened. The girl at the counter unapologetically denied that I ever ordered. So...I order our meal but I don't get myself anything?? By the end of the interaction she was noticeably annoyed and upset that we would even suggest that she made a mistake. I'll tell you one thing. If I had made a mistake like that I would be thrilled because it means I'm a human being. Though, I wouldn't be confrontational about it. It seems obvious to me that they need more staff members who can work well under the pressures of numerous customers. 

PS: I am a Nashvillian, not a tourist. I was sadly disappointed and expected much better service than this.

My boyfriend and I took a trip to Georgia for Thanksgiving and we made a pit stop in Nashville. I was looking up some cool places to check out and the Loveless Cafe was one of the top places to visit/try out.  

When we first arrived, we parked in front of the Loveless Cafe country market where they had specialized gift, hams, and signature jams. As we walked to the cafe I spotted "The Loveless Cafe" neon sign...I definitely had to take a few pictures of it. You know me :) 

As we entered the cafe (which is the white house)  there were photos of famous musicians and actors all along the wall they even had stockings hung from the fireplace welcoming the holidays! Right as we got in the waitress right away showed us to our seats. I was amazed by all the decor and art on the walls. They had a lot of cool Johnny Cash portraits and pictures. The table covers were blue and plaid patterns and the place  mats gave you a little history lesson on the cafe and how it got started. 

Looking at the menu there was a variety of things to try. You got your fried chicken, sandwiches, salads, homemade size dishes, and much more. Since we were in the south we had to try the ice tea! It was bombacious! I had read on the travel blog that the Loveless Cafe had amazing biscuits so we asked our lovely waitress to try them. We saw that they were small biscuits and they give you little cups of jam.

Loveless cafe is definitely comfort food for the soul and a place you should stop by if you're in Nashville!

Service was great. Everything was delicious. The biscuits were amazing, especially with the preserves. I highly recommend the peach glazed pork chops, fried chicken, catfish, and country ham. The pork chops had grill marks so the charred taste balanced perfectly with the sweetness of the peach preserves. Everything was cooked perfectly and had excellent flavor and the portions were very filling. We would definitely eat here again if we were in the area.

First off, our server was great, that's it. Let me start off by saying, I have always wanted to try this place. I am a huge foodie and eat out a few nights a week, City Winery has been on my list of places to try out and is a convenient drive from my house. 

A few weeks ago I decided I wanted to go to a great brunch to bring in the New Year. I looked around at all my options and decided on City Winery because of their menu. I made a reservation and my boyfriend and I were so excited to check it out.

When you walk in, it's a nice environment, what made our 4/5 star experience into less of that was the buffet. The $30 per person hotel breakfast buffet....it was decent and mayyybbbe worth $15.....

The thing that really got me though, was that I had no idea it was a buffet until we sat down. No where online did it say it, nor when I made the reservation...or even when they called to confirm the reservation the day before!!! They only had the buffet option and no actual menu. 

I came here to try the menu, not a buffet and am very upset I was not told beforehand. Every single person in the place was just as upset as me and it ruined the way I think and will talk about this place....and my first day of 2016! 




UPDATE - A manager contacted me today and issued me a refund for the buffet. I will go back & review this place again when I am able to have a true experience there.

The schnitzel was decent but the spaetzle needed flavor. I was also disappointed in the potato salad, it was served cold. Everytime I have had German potato salad it was always served hot and delicious. The atmosphere was nice with lots of room. They had a wide selection of beer which is a good thing for a beer house. Highly expensive just like any German restaurant.
I had some pretty bad biscuits while in Nashville but this was amazing!! So good! And I bought the BlackBerry barbecue sauce without even trying it and it was amazing

Been in Nashville four years and finally I decided to drive 40minutes to try the talk of the town. I had the southern omelette which taste amazing. The biscuits is definitely a plus too. Now I can see why it is a place you have to visit if you are ever in Nashville.

Fun music venue but the food is just alright. I absolutely loved my food the first time I came here, but I just went back and I wasn't impressed. Try burger was overcooked (what I loved last time; maybe just an off night?). The goat cheese tart had great flavor but is so incredibly rich and doesn't come with and chips l/bread/crackers to eat it with so it's just like eating spoonfuls of cheese (ended up leaving half of it on the table). 

Positives - The duck tacos were very good Andy drink "Once Upon a Thyme" was excellent. I would definitely order that again. We did the wine tasting to a Prince cover band that was really fun too. 

So, 3 stars overall.

Most disgusting place! As everybody we came hungry and had grate hope that we will have a good time and good food . Our experience started with short waiting time which is we used for working in facility. Actually cafe was pretty empty, but I understand they may be just cleaning or any thing in that nature. After 20 min I got table, we had a party of 4 and with us was 10 y old child, order drink, servant bring for child cup with hole, as a result all table was sticky, I clean mess with napkins which was giving to me with fork. Some other employee not our servant took empty cup and bring new one - no apology, like it's ok ok, servant bring biscuits and saying not asking, just saying we good now , I sad will be nice to clean table . That was forgetting... ok , We are order food , so new disappointment- now I was serve chicken with feathers! Common now! It's not ok! Big time disappointment! So, they exchange and bring bill after 3 min of me eating ...  Never will return ...

I really enjoyed the Bavarian Bierhaus. Tried the flight of beers and the brats platter (Werstelier?) and the cheese and meat plate app. On top of great food they had a great act playing. I'd definitely go again soon. You've got to check this place out!!

The food was forgettable, and it's not exactly in the middle of town. They do have decent biscuits, if you're into that sorta thing, but don't expect much from the rest of the menu. My eggs were over cooked and it was probably the worst "steak" I've had in 10 years. Pretty much a tourist trap. Meh.

Bacon!
Bacon!
Bacon!

Wonderful, flavor-ful bacon and eggs.
Pork chops, brisket, ham!  Truly wonderful fresh foods abound at this cute little historical eatery.
Several of us went here because they were advertising buy 3 pkgs of bacon and get one free. How could we resist?
Cute place, very crowded, no reservations, you have to wait for a table.  In the meantime, walk around, take photos, check out the gift shop.. plenty of parking.

I will give them 5 stars - the day they start offering gluten free biscuits.
It is time to get with the times and realize that thousands  and thousands of people cannot eat wheat products.

My friend brought me here when I was visiting  Nashville, and wow this place is a gem! It was pretty far out of the way (it felt like we were in the car for 20 minutes from midtown?), and the wait was long (she said that it's usually longer), but it was worth it. I could make a meal out of the biscuits and preserves alone!! This place had amazing customer service, and even though it seemed everything on the menu was basic, everything just tasted better here. Even my scrambled eggs were the best I've ever had! I liked this place because it felt like I was sitting in my grandma's kitchen...you know, if my grandma hung up hundreds of autographed celebrity photos on the walls! I recommend this place to everyone visiting Nashville, just because you have to say you've been to the Loveless Cafe at least once, right?

Me and my friend go here about once every few months because we love the beautiful  ride over for the coffee and biscuits.. I always order catfish... Although I am from the MS delta where catfish is our middle name, I still enjoy their catfish... The turnip greens are great with pepper sauce and the crinkle fries never disappoint nor satisfy. The okra is out of a box... Server told me that one! 
I just don't get what the hoot is all about... I guess you say it's a Nashville thing but I've been to shacks on the side of the road with better home cooked food. I have a love/hate relationship with this place. I want to love it because of the beautiful location and home feel but it's just becoming to "franchisee" without being a chain.. People come from all over to see this place and celebrities as well... I don't get it... Like I said I come every few months for the scenery and hopes that the food gets better... Service is for the most part lovely

THE BEST meal we had in Nashville.  The fried chicken was amazing, homemade biscuits and jams, chicken fried steak, the mac & cheese.  This will be the first stop on our return trip!  There are also cute little shops you can walk to while waiting for your table.  Crafts, foodie stuff, etc

Heard about this being the "go to" place when in Nashville.  Waited for 45 min with great expectations.  The biscuits were fantastic and the gravy very nice.  Had a moonshine Bloody Mary which was good.  The fried tomato biscuits were also very good.  However portions were disappointing in size.  At the end of the day the food was good. But nothing to write home about.  The service was very attentive and friendly.

I came here during Nashville burger week. Their special was the porcini pork burger on a squid ink bun. It was good but my friend ordered the regular burger on the menu and it was even better than the special. Our server was Gemaal and he took care of us. He knew the menu inside and out. Most of all he was one of the most attentive servers I have had in Nashville. I will be back if only to have his humor at the table again

I rarely give a place five stars but this cafe is amazing.  It is a bit of drive and worth it. Everything I order was great tasting. They start you with you a plate of biscuits, which they're famous for. The plate comes with three Jelly's, peach, strawberry and blackberry.  Their all made in house and you can buy them or ship them. With the meal you get more biscuits and grits, which I love. Theses are the best grits I have ever had. The gravy is good with sausage in it. I had bacon, sausage and ham with eggs and a hashbrown casserole (excellent). I cannot tell you how good this place is, once again everything is awesome.  You may have to wait in line but it is worth it. You will love this place, you must go. I highly recommend it and will be back.

This is not fine dining German food and it's a kitchy Oktoberfest theme, but it's a fun night out. I came here with some family and we had a great time.

The beer selection is really good and they go great with the giant pretzels. Can't stress enough how good the pretzels are. Really hit the spot.

The waiter highly recommended the Jaegerschnizel which is a breaded pork cutlet with mushroom gravy on top of noodles. It was not bad, the pork was a little dry and it would have been much better if they put the mushroom gravy on the noodles as well as on top of the entire thing. But it was decent enough. 

Now the highlight was the entertainment, a lovely woman playing the according and keyboards and just making it a fun night. There are plenty of TVs in the space so if you want to keep up with the Nashville sports, this is a great place to watch the game.  Also has a huge bar so you don't even have to grab a table. 

So if you're looking for a great meal and that's the focus of dinner, skip the Bierhaus. If you're looking for a fun evening out with friends that revolves around beer and kitchy entertainment, this will do nicely. I had a lot of fun here.
Been here on many occasions. My first time for breakfast.   As usual,  worth the drive. Love the Loveless!

We drove 30 minutes from Nashville for brunch here, and then waited 35 minutes for a table (they told us an hour).......an it was worth it.  We had the ribs, brisket, creamed corn (the star of the show) and of course you get the biscuits with their homemade jam to start........i would just eat the biskets all day with the jam if i could.

it's worth the drive and the wait.

Worth the long drive and wait for a table!! We had a large group and being our first time at Loveless we ordered a little bit of everything! The biscuits and gravy where to die for and the fried chicken was amazing!!! Also had the fried green tomatoes, grits and hash brown casserole and I would recommend them all!! Staff was fast and friendly!
This place is awesome! The food tastes authentic, and the live entertainment is amazing.

This place was recommended to my hubby and I by our Airbnb host and let me tell you! Their biscuits were to die for and they serve them with three different types of preserves-peach being my fav (I actually bought some to bring home). Everything we tried was delicious and one of my favs was their fried green tomato biscuit with pimento cheese. I also got some pimento cheese to take home because it was SO GOOD. The service matched the excellent food and was provided with a smile every visit. We went three times while we were in town and were warmly welcomed and fed til we were stuffed each time. It's a must try when in Nashville! We will most definitely be back!

The hype over Loveless Cafe is fun and all, but their food seems is inconsistent and nothing mind blowing . Each time I've been, there's been at least one part of my meal that is just off. First time the fried chicken was extremely dry, and the second time the mac and cheese was salty and not very tasty. 

Their biscuits and preserves are AMAZING. The customer service is also great. 

I would go back if I'm looking to show off a Nashville staple or was in the area, but as a Nashville local there are many other restaurants in the area that will serve my palette better.
I asked for some yellow mustard with my biscuits and they brought it to me......umhumm.

Not a bad place.  The atmosphere is not quite as cool as the New Port, Kentucky location.  And it is a fat cry from the real one in Munich. The entertainment was not up to par.    But it is new and has potential.  

My waitress, Jennifer was very friendly and did a great job.

The food, I ordered the wurstellet sampler, was good but not great.  

I have dietary restrictions and was not happy to find a rule against substituting one side for another even though the sides  by themselves are all the same price.  

Will I be back?  Probably, but I will give them a while to become better established first.
The biscuits are the best!!!! It is sooo fresh, it is still hot and steamy when u break it in half. I would definitely go back to this and eat biscuits all day.

Outstanding southern fare and super friendly server made this such a pleasurable breakfast stop.  Biscuits are to-die-for and the jams are delicious (bought some in the shop to-go).  Chicken and waffles were outstanding, as were the cheesy grits, and sausage gravy.  Country ham was incredibly more salty that it's city cousin we're more familiar with.  Well with the visit, not at all over-hyped by the food channel spot.

Loved Loved..would go again.  We were lucky to sit outside. Staff was great 
food was good.

Thank you Food Network / Travel Channel!!!!

The biscuits were to die for.  The server was so nice and he knew we were from California right from the beginning.  This might have helped because he kept giving us biscuits and the jelly (amazing).  When we got to the food we weren't even that hungry.  The food was average, but the real reason this is 5 stars is due to the biscuits and especially the jelly.

Please treat yourself and order something small or split a meal and just get the biscuits and jelly.  The biscuits were soft and good, but it was the jelly that was superb.
The taxes because it is an event venue....hard to pay if you're sitting at the bar for happy hour.  Bartender needs to put a smile on her face.  My husband was totally turned off.  Won't be back.

I went to see Art Alexakis lead singer of Everclear and a special guest Leigh Nash from Six Pence. Great Venue. Based from New York this is the 4th location.
They will start making their own wine in a few months. They just been around since October 2014.
This was dinner and music and great atmosphere. I found this show through "bands in town" app on my phone and popped up. Glad I did and glad Art picked this place.

My server was great. Connor. Seemed all the servers that night were on it, when looking around. I actually came in with my wheelchair and they accommodated me. Staff was nice.
I was greeted and offered a beverage. That came out fast and he had knowledge of wine and suggested. Food came out fast and flat bread was plenty big!! Enough for 1 or three to share. But for a 2 hour show it lasted me the night. 

They do serve Sat and Sun brunch. Burgers look amazing and will have to try next time I'm in.
Their regular menu is different than their "Show menu" so keep that in mind.
You won't find a burger if you're craving during a show. Save that for lunch or dinner time on a non show night.

Pros: 
-great for friends, pop in and have a glass of wine, or something to eat. great atmosphere and cool hang out.
- Great artists too they have playing there from all around big or small.
-State of the art sound system, digital and Line Array speaker system. 
-You can see no matter where you sit.

Cons:
-parking limited. Valet is $5. Nice its cheap to park but if I'm already coming in to spend $10 on a glass of wine or more plus a meal walking out paying over 50 bucks. At least cover parking if you're limited!!? But again, 5 bucks isn't much.

-Food looks great but flat bread I got was bland. I had to spice it up. But don't get me wrong it was great, just needed little more flavor!

Over all great experience and will be back!
Except for giant dumpling everything was great.  Great selection of German beer on tap, and great sausage.  Going back for the Pork shank which was sold out.  Interesting place to eat.

We stopped here on our drive from Nashville to Memphis. I liked the experience here,  but didn't absolutely love the food. If I could just rate the biscuits, they would get 5 stars. 

Even on a Monday around 10am, this place was still pretty crowded. Our server was very nice, but the service was super slow. We got two plates of biscuits, one before our food came and one when our food came. We split the Southern omelette and country ham. The omelette was average and the ham was flavorful, but a little dry. The biscuits were perfection - not too big or buttery, and just a little flaky. Melt in your mouth deliciousness. 

They also have some shops on site, where they sell some of their preserves and mixes. 

Worth a visit for the experience for sure!

Primo southern cooking... My friends and I trekked it here from Nashville and waited an hour and a half but it was worth it. The food and service was amazing, I am still full a day later... Worth checking out at least once. 

I would suggest the BBQ and eggs!!

Pimento cheese and fried green tomato biscuit was interesting...

Raisin French toast was perfect, not too sweet, light and fluffy!

Decorated in the style of Hof Brau in Munich. Had the schnitzel which was very good. Spaetzl was soft and I remember it being more firm and fried in Munich. Had the Dunkel beer and liked it. Similar to beer in Germany, still has that American "bite".  Service and music was good. I would come back again!

Loveless Cafe brought me back to my life that I lived with my families in Abilene Texas back in old days.  GREAT Southern food!  I love fried chicken with waffles, Thanksgiving dinner with turkey, stuffings and oh yes, biscuits!  Biscuits are to DIE for!  

Ham, eggs, bacon, hash brown casserole and all that jazz are delicious, cooked to perfection and perfectly resembles what southern food is all about!  If I ever travel past Tennessee from one state to other, this place is recommended for those who pass by, you will not be disappointed, guaranteed!

If it's out of the way, make the drive.   If there is a line,  wait!   So glad we took the trek from downtown.   We got the sampler with chicken,  meatloaf,  and bbq pork.   The sweet potatoes were what sweet potatoes were meant to taste like.   The mac n cheese was OK.  The hashbrown casserole was delicious.   The biscuits. ....we went to the shop and bought the mix and preserves to take home. ...so good.  We were happy we took the trip  out and wish this place was back at home.

This is is awesome! Long wait but lots of seating and plenty to see. There is a BBQ shack in the middle that hands out free samples that are to die for! Also lots of cute shops! Bring a bottle of champagne and ok to drink mimosas while you.
 Worth the trip!
Unreal breakfast! Amazing biscuits and jelly and jams. Great service a must stop if your in Nashville

The environment is great and the staff is friendly. The food was good and there was a variety of beers offered. I felt the prices were okay, but may be biased against them due to the fact that I went to another German restaurant recently which offered more for the prices that were offered here. Great environment to meet up with friends and there were many children here as well. There was no wait time when I came but the staff still took a while to get to my table. I would go back if someone else suggested it, but I wasn't blown away by the food as much as I had hoped.

Showed up mid morning on a Sunday to find out it was a 3 hour wait. Urgh nobody wants to wait 3 hours for breakfast. But we noticed you could order online and carry out. There were plenty of picnic tables scattered around the property so we decided to go that route.  Instead of 3 hours we had our food in 25 minutes. While we waited the shops & cornhole occupied us. 

The service from the younger girls at the hostess stand/counter was probably the least appealing about the whole place. Asked for forks & napkins for our carry out order was like asking for the world.

Food was decent, nothing special or worth a 3 hour wait. But I can now say I've been to the Loveless Cafe!

Great venue for shows. Very intimate and awesome acoustics. The wait staff was very pleasant and helpful. My only qualm is the food. We got the trout, but felt like the quality of the food did not match the price tag. Still a great place, with great shows and staff. Would definitely go again.

I have loved Loveless Cafe since I was a child!  The biscuits & jams have always been phenomenal!  The ham..well, it's the best!  The character of this landmark is such an integral part of the "Nashville Experience!"

Music venue is great

Service was way off again! Party of six, 2 meals come out lukewarm, the other 4 plates start to trickle out 17 minutes later. They tried to deliver plates that we did not order three different times. Ordered espresso and the cookie plate, espresso comes out Luke warm and cookies come out 14 minutes later.
It seems like the kitchen really let the wait staff down again. We left 20% because we know how hard servers work but we will not be ordering anything to eat here again
The people that were crushed next to us also had the same horrible service. We were all laughing about it by desert.

Six different main courses ordered and the standout was the shaved kale salad....big miss on the food but it is hard to get a clear feel for the food when all the plates showed up lukewarm or cold

Super disappointing! 

Saw one review stating "best food in Nashville" my advise is go to City House, Sinema or Adele's and then recant your statement respectfully

This is one of those places you must carve out time to visit if you are in the Nashville area.  We arrived at 1:00 pm on a Friday and had about an hour wait.  They give you a pager that will allow you to walk around the grounds and still know when your table is ready.  My blog review can be found here:  http://pennyspassion.blogspot.com/2017/10/weekending-october-6-2017.html.  The fried green tomatoes were my favorite!

Cute place to check out if you're visiting Nashville! Biscuits are good, food is decent. I'm admittedly not the biggest fan of Southern food, but when in Rome...er, Nashville...

I had a beef brisket sandwich with green beans and Mac and cheese. The bf had a southern omelette with country ham. Everything was pretty good. Portions are HUGE. Consider sharing a meal if you don't want to walk out hurting!

We arrived to another country,  Germany. Waiters are all dressed appropriately :). My husband enjoyed the beers got one in all sizes .03, .05 & 1ltr. Nice outside area! Really enjoyed the band who spoke and sang in German. Will be back.  Enjoyed our food he got the sausage platter, & pretzel. I got potatoe pancakes and donor kabab!! Not sure of the bread but the meat and salad but was great and flavorful. Spent about 2hrs there..
