Had dinner at the Bavarian Bierhaus tonight, food was great, and Terry's German music played on an accordion and other cool instruments, was the perfect compliment to a really fun evening! Thank you Terry!! If I ever come to Tennesse again I will definitely stop here again

I do not believe there to be any affiliation between Loveless Cafe and the Oregon based company Nike, but regardless, my only advice for anyone deciding whether or not to make the trek out to eat at Loveless is to JUST DO IT. We sort of went ham on this meal and ordered a whole lot because we couldn't decide. The best were the melt-in-your-mouth biscuits, the hashbrown casserole (!), the creamed corn, and the peanut butter pie. The waffle is better than the pancake, but both are very good. The fried chicken biscuit was good as well, just a bit small on the portion size. Key Lime pie was also very good and the mac n cheese was solid. This was definitely our favorite meal on our visit to Nashville. Highly recommended.

Don't let the wait discourage you from this place. After all good things come to those who wait! :-) Excellent feel of being local and the food is simply amazing. Everything from the chicken waffles to the homemade pie was worth it. If you're in town don't leave this place off your list!

I have been to Loveless Cafe twice. Both times I have been extremely pleased. They have wonderful staff and quick service! Now don't get me wrong, it might take an hour for you to get a seat, but when you're seated you get served real quick!

The biscuits and jam alone make the restaurant worth going to eat!

This place is in the mall. You walk through a gift shop before you get to the restaurant, so you can probably imagine it's pretty cheesy. Waitresses are wearing costumes, pretty generic Herman beer on tap. We only ate a pretzel and it was pretty good. The one thing that was nice was the live accordion player and singer. That was a nice touch. Otherwise it's a tourist trap and I'd skip it.

While in Nashville three weeks ago we dropped in for a late lunch. The food was fantastic. Our server was not attentive. We both remarked how we wish we had been seated in another section as the other tables were getting amazing service. 
Back to the food. I ordered the BLT (the T being fried green tomatoes). It was very good. The bacon was just right and the fried green tomatoes had a nice crunch to them. I had a side of mac -n- cheese which was good (not great but good). The biscuit was wonderful and the strawberry preserves were fantastic. So good that after we ate we walked over to the Loveless market and each picked up a jar to take back. 
My mom had breakfast, two fried eggs, sourdough toast, bacon, hash browns, and the city ham. The ham was great. 
I was surprised on my way to the bathroom to pass two open window kitchens, one that show cased biscuit making. That was very cool. 
I would definitely come back and I highly recommend going. I would have loved to give 5 star but I just couldn't with such poor service.

Our family visited Loveless Cafe on a recent trip to Nashville.  We had heard many positive reviews of the restaurant and they were all correct.  After waiting a bit for a table, it was totally worth it.  Each of us ordered the chicken dinner with 2 sides and everything tasted great.  The chicken was cooked perfectly and the portions were more than enough.  Dinner was topped off with a slice of apple pie that according to my daughter was the best she had ever had.  Our waiter, Owen, helped to make our meal even better.  His service was excellent.  We can't wait to visit again.

A Must if you are in Nashville!!!!! Everything was exceptional the food the service there is a reason they are on a wait but believe me it is worth it!!!! Please say hi to Keith what a nice guy. We enjoyed this place so well we had lunch and went back the next morning for breakfast!! I will definitely be back!

Excellent food.  Great biscuits.  I had he fried chicken on a salad (can't remember the name of the salad).  Hubby had the fried chicken and waffles.  Service was great. atmosphere was cute.  Worth the drive to get to!
Virginia was an awesome server very good food and it is the first  stop on the Natchez Trace.. Very one stops and takes their picture at the sign...
Never got a chance to try because I was in this valet line for over 45 mins. I am literally writing this review in the car because I am stuck in the line. FML
Loveless Cafe is amazing. The biscuits are out of this world and the fried chicken and fried catfish are delicious. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Ask for Virginia - she is a great waitress.
Cool place! Owners seems to care about his business and puts the customers first.

We were in Nashville on vacation and my wife's friend told us to check this place out. Her husband said it was the best chicken he had ever had and the servings were huge. The place was a 45 minute drive from where we were staying and they said there would be a 40 minute wait I was not happy about it but went. One of the best mind changes I have made. Because it was very much worth it all. The chicken is great and the biscuits are the way you would expect them to taste in the South, mouth watering! The staff was full of southern hospitality and the place just gave you that down home feel like you were sitting in grandma's kitchen. A wonderful place and we will come back when we are in the area!

Loveless Cafe was awesome! Everyone I knew recommended I go on a recent trip.  The food was amazing and though there was a wait, as expected, it was only 30 minutes and gave us time to check out the little shops they have there which we enjoyed as well!

Our waitress was a doll and the biscuits was great. Some of the very best cheddar grits I have ever had. We come for the first time on a Sunday & it was a 2 hour wait so we left. We returned the following a Tuesday at 11 and only had to wait 10 minutes for a table. This place is worth the drive but not a wait of 2 hours on the weekend.

The Hofbrau house in Cincinnati is much better.  I ordered the Jager Snitzle, honestly the ones I make at home are much better.  If you plan on having a conversation in the place forget it.  There is a singer and the microphone picks up all the conversations.  Horrible echo throughout the place.

While visiting Nashville, Loveless was one of the top places on my list to visit. It was about a 20 minute drive from the city but it did not disappoint. We came on a Friday late afternoon and there was still an hour wait. Not to worry, there's a very scenic drive near by and you can kill time that way. Or just explore the grounds, there's two different gift shops with lots of goodies to buy. 

When we were finally seated, we noticed there was moonshine on the menu. How could you pass up on that? I had a Watermelon Crawl (watermelon, Lemonade, Sprite and a Moonshine Sidecar in a Souvenir Loveless Mini Mason Jar). The little souvenir mason jar was too cute! The moonshine did kick my butt!

For food we ordered the Loveless Fried Chicken (Quarter Chicken) with a side of macaroni and cheese, slow cooked green beans, fried green tomatoes, and hashbrown casserole. Before our meal came out they brought out their signature biscuits and they were buttery and light, just the way I like them. Everything else was really good. I loved the fried chicken, the batter wasn't too heavy or oily. The only side dish that I didn't care for were the fried green tomatoes. I've had better and they were so small.

We were so stuffed after our meal that we skipped out on dessert but now I'm regretting that decision! If I'm ever back in Nashville I'll have to make room for their desserts!

Great music venue. Had their personal pizza which was very good. 
Wines are over-priced. This is the first establishment I've been in that triples the retail price of the bottle and then adds the TN liquor tax on top of that making the bottle four times the retail price.

Every thing we had was awesome. The fried chicken and the country fried steak are  of this world delicious. The fried green tomatoes with their special sauce is great. The hash brown  casserole was better than Cracker Barrel.

Q: How far would you travel for fresh, homemade biscuits?
A: 393 miles.

Well, that's partly true. We decided to travel to Nashville just for the hell of it and because it was cold in Chicago. Next to the sunshine and warm temperature, Loveless was the biggest selling point for us to come on down.

We knew what to expect in coming to Loveless. We knew it would be packed and we would have to wait, but did we care? Absolutely not. Good food is worth waiting for, especially when it's on every major list of things you need to see in Nashville. We called ahead which I highly recommend. Once we finally arrived, they were telling people an hour but they only quoted us 30 minutes since we had called and our name was already on the list. (By the time we were leaving they were telling people an hour and a half, so go as early as you can!) Although there's a few shops on the property, it's not enough to kill more than 20 minutes. 

Loveless is primarily known for the biscuits and they didn't disappoint. I especially loved the peach jam that came with it. I also ordered some sausage gravy for the biscuits, but that was a waste of money -- the free jam was the way to go!

Breakfast was great, especially the jalapeno bacon. It wasn't too spicy, but the jalapeno gave it a nice flavor. Also, whoever said their hashbrown casserole was better than Cracker Barrel's wasn't lying. I kept eyeing my husband's hoping he wouldn't eat it. I should have just stole it from him :(

Our waiter was so welcoming that it almost made me wish I lived in Nashville so I could hang out with him. When he saw my ID (carded me for my mimosas) and saw that it was an IL license he recommended his favorite places in Nashville for us. I absolutely love southern hospitality!

The only reason for not giving 5 stars was the fact that I dropped $40 on breakfast. Do you know how many hours I had to work to earn that? Of course -- it was totally worth it.
Went for a show with the Americana Music Fest. Excellent service, good food. Limited choice of beers in the menus though. Seemed like 50% were IPAs, and I'm over those. Not many other choices.
Another great breakfast option in Nashville. Wait can be a little annoying but it is usually worth it. Excellent for a morning after a night on the town.

Have you ever had a food experience that you still remember to this day?  Loveless Cafe created that experience for me.  It's not fair to other comparable restaurants.  Oh wait a minute there no comparable restaurants.
The food is always amazing here! The staff is always nice and warming. The prices are great and the amount of food is very generous!
This place is epic. If you looking for a place with a home town feel you have found it. The biscuits are the best and the service is amazing.

Great atmosphere and decent service. One particular part of the menu is disappointing. They advertise vegetarian dumplings but use animal products to make them. This is seriously false advertisement, and can make people who can't have animal products sick, like myself. 

Not a great place for vegetarians.

I visited this amazing place on my first trip to Nashville because I read that this was a must-see. I was visiting from Florida to see the Vandy/UF game and felt so at home while dining here. The southern vibe was amazing and Loveless Cafe hands down has the best biscuits (mmh, homemade jelly!) and fried chicken that I've ever had. Whoever tells you to consider coming here on your next trip, please listen. Although the place is a few minutes out of town, the drive is very scenic and worth the time.
Points off for miserable sound system with scratchy noise; band was screaming.  Food was good.  Server very inexperienced.  He forgot our rye bread.

Biscuits were yummy!  Love the three different types of preserves that came along with them.  Also, enjoyed the rest of my breakfast: 2 pork chops, grits, scrabbled eggs with a mimosa. Had enough left over to eat later in the day.  Definitely glad we stopped here while we were in TN!

The hype is valid... (Although a bit out of the way, well worth the drive).
We only came for dessert and coffee since we had had dinner before heading over to Loveless.... (Big mistake).  Our party of four ordered the chess pie, fudge pie, banana pudding, and strawberry rhubarb cobbler... Everything was fresh and delicious. I only wish we would have tried some of the food.

Martha Stewart wasn't kidding when she said it's the best breakfast in America. I'm not sure why they call it the loveless cafe because all I felt here was love. I don't think I have ever had better breakfast food than what I ate here. The service was amazing and quick. We were in and out in about an hour. 

The biscuits came out first and I didn't think anything else could live up to those biscuits. Then the food came. I ordered the chicken and waffles and it was the most perfect meal I have ever had. The waffle was fluffy and light while the chicken was fried just beautifully. If you are in Nashville or even if you aren't I highly recommend making the trek out to Loveless Cafe.

Amazing place. We walked in expecting a long wait because the place looked super busy. The hostess said you two follow me.  We were sat and greeted immediately with a plate of biscuits. The best biscuits Ever. Everything we ordered was amazingly good. Highly recommend this place.

Always enjoy coming here when I visit my sister! The wait can be extremely long so don't come starving, because you will have to wait! But there are little shops and games you can play while waiting! Food was delicious! So anything on menu is amazing! I had grilled chicken sandwich with green beans... Delicious!! The biscuits they serve you before your meal is to die for! Love the jam that comes with it!!

On our last day in Nashville, we visited Loveless Cafe. My mom and I both had a great breakfast, but the biscuits were by far the best part. I loved the jellies and could have easily had an entire breakfast of just biscuits. Would love to go back the next time I visit Nashville!

To die for!! Well worth the 30 minute wait. Adorable setting with cool 
Tennessee hill breezes in the middle of July.  Shopped the four shoppes while we waited. Games of corn home on the front lawn. 

Food consisted of amazing biscuits and jams. I had the grilled catfishes with mashed potatoes. Cream corn and hush puppies !!! Amazing !!

Kat...Great waitress!! Looked like a rockabilly angel with big blue eyes :)

This place is famous for their biscuits and it seems to be a big place because all the country music stars come here. Personally, I've had better biscuits. The food is good but you can get the same food at any diner that serves breakfast. I think you're really just paying for atmosphere and reputation here. The service is great! Everyone is so friendly! Lots of autographed pictures of the music stars line the walls.
These are the best biscuits I've ever had. When I think of southern eating this is the place to be. I would recommend this place, it's a great atmosphere.

When you google places you must see/do in Nashville, The Loveless Cafe comes up as one of the top 5.  With it also being our last name, we were excited to see what it was all about.

We drove from St. Louis to Nashville for a weekend and came hungry as this was our first stop once in Tennessee.  We were greeted by an associate, very friendly, who was eager to take our pictures around the grounds esp with our last name being highlighted.  We put our name on the waiting list and looked around the shops, the Barn and other parts of the grounds.

Our waiter was extremely helpful and knowledgeable and excited that another Loveless namesake had stopped in.  We started with sweet tea and their homemade biscuits with the various jams and preserves.  I got the fried chicken with two sides and my husband got the sampler with 3 meats and sides.  Needless to say we were not disappointed.  They were advertising national dessert month and their homemade goodies so we had a piece of their turtle pie...not to miss!

We did get a little something to remember our time there and have already started thinking about our next visit whenever we're in Tennessee again.

I don't even know where to begin. I guess in the order it happened! Blueberry pickers: something we'll try to recreate at home. Biscuits and strawberry jam: perfection. The other two flavors were good, but the strawberry was phenomenal. Macaroni and cheese: best I've ever had in a restaurant. Cucumbers and onion: a little too sweet for my taste, but still good. BBQ pork: tender, flavorful. Good sauce. Meatloaf: delicious. I haven't tried my fried chicken yet, it's in my to-go box for later (with half of my meatloaf and most of my pork). There were three of us, and we all loved everything. 

This was out of our way, and we couldn't be happier that we made the side trip. It's fun like this that keeps me sticking to my motto on road trips: why not??

A co-worker recommended this place. What a great treat! We had their peach rub BBQ chicken and pulled pork. We also had creamed corn, cheese grits, turnip greens and sweet potatoes. Every bit of food was amazing! Definitely stop by!

The atmosphere feels like someone's cozy grandma's house to me (not mine though, I didn't have cozy grandmas), which is nice. The food is good when you're craving some country cooking. I've had various things here, from the pancakes (love) to brisket (pretty good) to a cheeseburger (a bit disappointing, but okay) to salad with fried chicken (good salad, the fried chicken is really good), and more. The biscuits are great of course...love the creamed corn, which isn't one of my usual go-to choices. We tend to go during non-peak times/days, so we don't usually have to wait very long. We wouldn't go there if we had to wait more than 20-30 minutes, but that's because we live near by and can go any time. I think it's worth a bit of a longer wait for a fun little tourist experience, if you're on the fence about it. The service is pretty good, sometimes things have to be sent back to kitchen for being cold or something but the servers always handle things well. In summary, I recommend eating here...because it's good and quirky and like (someone else's) grandma's house...in a good way.

Great little quaint place for breakfast. Service was fast and efficient. Food was excellent and truly southern comfort food. There are also gift shops and areas to buy jam and they will even ship it to you. Overall highly recommend this Nashville staple!

First meal in Nashville this time. My daughter brought us directly here from the airport.  Had to wait about 55 minutes no problem-we walked around and visited a few of the gift shops nearby-well worth the wait!  The biscuits have not been over rated. The problem is to stop eating them before your meal comes so you don't wreck your appetite! Delicious jam, too! I had 2 pieces of chicken which were absolutely delicious, so moist, cooked perfectly. I chose the beans ( didn't really like them) and the Mac and Cheese (which was very good) for my sides. Highly recommended!

Excellent food. Pulled pork was excellent   The biscuits to die for. Service was very good. Due to popularity there might be a wait but worth the wait.  We also went on a Saturday which didn't help.  The hash brown casserole is a must as a side!

So I surprised my wife with a trip to Nashville to celebrate her inexplicable love of country music and visiting the Loveless was high on her to-do list.  

Thank god!

You may be able to get a breakfast this good in New York, but I couldn't tell you where and I'm sure you'd pay a small fortune for it.  Despite the ridiculous wait (1.5 hour) and vertigo inducing pitch of the floor (a bit uneven) the meal was phenomenal with a capital "PH."

The biscuits were unique, even by Nashville standards.  Small and light, they didn't require any condiments to satisfy, though that didn't stop me from drowning them in the best Sausage gravy I've ever had.  My wife had the Chicken and a Waffle and declared it the single best piece of chicken she'd ever eaten.  I had to dive into the "Pit-Cooked Pork Barbecue & Eggs, One to the Left and One to the Right" which came with a pancake and the greatest iteration of breakfast potatoes created: the Hash brown Casserole.  Besides being some of the best pulled pork, the remainder of the meal was equally exquisite.  The eggs just seemed fresher and the pancake fluffier than any I'd ever had elsewhere. 

Know going in on a weekend that you will wait and wait and wait to be seated.  This is partially due the tourist destination nature of the establishment and partially by design as there are multiple souvenir shops on the premises. You've been warned.

In love with this place! We decided to eat here before attending a show at the Grand Ole Opry. We arrived at 5:30 and seated right away as this is a humongous restaurant! The waitress greeted us and took our drink order. She was attentive and polite the whole time. Out of our group, beer was ordered and enjoyed but I had a glass of Riesling which was also good. For appetizers, we had cheese fries, pretzel and beer cheese soup. We loved all of it! Everyone enjoyed their meals and agreed we would definitely be back. The polka band started playing around 6 and they were really fun to listen to! I would definitely recommend this place. Although we left our kids home on this trip, we plan on returning with them because we know they would also love the food, music and atmosphere:)

I'd always heard of this place and much like an old ex boyfriend, expected it to be bigger. But as they say, size doesn't matter. Because this place packed a wallop! Enjoyed the biscuits and jams, and my moonshine and sweet tea drink. I ordered a pimento and fried green tomato biscuit and side of yummy, cheesy grits, while another at my table had country fried steak. Can't wait to go back here!
The family style breakfast was awesome. The food came out hot. The coffee never stopped. The famous biscuits and homemade jelly were to die for. The waitstaff was great, friendly and attentive.

This place was alright. Definitely a good spot for drinks and appetizers with friends, however, it's very overpriced. It's 10 dollars per person for a wine tasting, and on top of that, if you buy a bottle, they will only wave one fee (all the wineries I have been to.. which have been a lot... they will wave the group tasting fee.) Also, their wine was good.. but I've definitely had better. Especially when one of the cheapest is 25 dollars a bottle. Again, it's a really really cute looking place.. it definitely has a fun vibe, it's just way over priced. We didn't get any appetizers while we were here (because of the price) so I can't attest to how good the food was. I will probably try some next time, but you definitely need to be prepared to spend a pretty penny.

Food was decent at best. Beer selection was fairly good, for German beers that is. Certainly not as great as the German food I was accustomed to back home in the Midwest, but for Nashville it was pretty good. Certainly not a place I would go to all the time, as the prices were a bit high for what you get, but for a quick German fix i would prefer this place over Gerst Haus.

Having been to City Winery for several shows now, I thought that it was about time to give this place a review.  
Sitting snuggly, a block or so, behind the Convention Center on Lafayette, you can, as I have, drive right past this place but once you find it, it is a lovely space to spend an evening.  Parking is valet only, unless you are savvy at finding street parking nearby (which I am and no I won't give away my secret locations).  If you can't find street parking, no worries, the cost to valet park will not shock your wallet.  It's a lovely building with a wine grape vine growing around the front.  The inside is spacious and has an open, welcoming feel.  
I thoroughly enjoy the variety of performances that this venue books.  Initially, I thought that it was just going to be yet another "Nashville-esque" venue with the same talent popping in and out but I've been introduced to a number of acts that I would probably not have found otherwise.  Kudos to them for this!  The prices for the shows are extremely reasonable.  The more popular the talent, the more the ticket will cost, of course, but even the priciest ticket that I've purchased has been reasonable.  
I love the ambiance of the performance area, wide open with plenty of seating.  I will say choose wisely for the shows, I'm not a fan of passing waiters/waitresses during a show but this is not a deal breaker.  
I am absolutely a wine lover but for whatever reason, I'm never in the mood for wine when I come here.  I have perused the wine list and it's nice.  The mixed drinks are decent and are priced maybe a little less than some of the trendier spots in the city.  If beer is your thing, they do have a small selection.  The food is good.  It's not the best in the city but it's on par with other restaurants.  So far, I've had the risotto balls, the duck flatbread, and the caramelized pork belly.  None have disappointed.  
The staff has always been attentive and very professional.  It can be a challenge at times, to get another drink once the venue is full and the show has started but I will not hold that against them.  If a drink is needed as soon as your glass is empty, there is a bar in the back.  
FYI - If a show is ever cancelled, they go above and beyond taking care of you for the inconvenience.  I received a personal phone call when they realized that I hadn't checked my email to alert me to a cancelled show.  In the email, they offered me a full refund or City Winery credit and 2 complimentary tickets to another show.  I mean seriously, how many other venues would do this!  
I'm thinking that I need to start ordering the wine and finally become a vinofile.

Loved it! We showed up on Monday around 2 and were advised that a 40 minute wait was head of us. Really we only waited about 20 minutes and during that time there was plenty to check out on the property. I ordered the fried chicken and my fiancée got the pulled pork. Both were absolutely amazing. The biscuits and sides all were just great. I got a sweet tea and a shot of moonshine. Go big or go home right. Portions are large and our waitress was super nice. I have nothing but good things to say about loveless. My only regret is I won't get to try everything.

This was legit authentic German cuisine!  And the atmosphere was great. Had a lady playing an accordion and singing Bavarian music. I got the 6 beer flight and was not disappointed. The food was tasty. The wait staff were awesome. Give this place a try. You won't regret it!

This place was given a lot of hype. I was looking forward to tasting the fried chicken I have heard so much about. Don't get me wrong the chicken was cooked perfectly but it was lacking flavor. The green beans and mashed potatoes were awesome though. The sweet potatoes were bland and the mac and cheese was subpar. The peach and strawberry preserves were awesome but I was disappointed in the biscuits. For a place that advertises their biscuits like crazy they were just ok. The sweet tea was not sweet which is shocking from what I've experienced so far down here in the south. Prices were a little pricey but not over the top. It's pretty much what I have come to expect from Nashville food. Lots of hype but really just ok. I might go back to try some of the other dishes. I am a sucker for country cooking. I'm just hoping another dish will blow me away. Where is the mouth watering food Nashville?

I have never had a more delicious breakfast in my life. Never. I would like to swim in a pool of their preserves, then take a nice nap in a bed of their biscuits. Well, after eating a bunch of them. Yeah, the wait was brutal, but we knew what to expect, brought a Sunday paper and did some poking around at the shops. The wait was worth it. Great service, too.

It was good, but was a bit too hyped up... We came for a late lunch, but even though, there was a line and a LONG wait. 1 hour and 30 minutes to be exact. Luckily, they have a number of stores around the restaurant and corn hole to keep people entertained while waiting. There is a country store-type store that sells Loveless Cafe souvenirs and an store that sells locally made art. The stores are cute, but a bit on the pricey side, which is expected. 
FINALLY our buzzer went off! I was absolutely starving by this point! They brought out a large plate of biscuits and damn, those were really good! I really wish that I had thought to buy some biscuit mix. They were butter, fluffy and warm. They also brought out a dish of preserves. I liked the strawberry best, but that might be because I really like strawberries. I liked that the jam wasn't too sweet, which sometimes happen. 
I split the 3-meat sampler with a friend and got an extra side. Our 3 meats were the pork, fried chicken, and fried catfish. Our sides were the okra, fried green tomatoes, and the grits and cheese. The grits really were cheesy. In fact, it was more like melted cheese with some grits. It was good, but a bit rich for my taste. I think that I prefer the grits to be in a broth rather than just slathered with cheese.  The catfish was good as was the pulled pork. I was less of a fan of the fried chicken. The batter could have used a bit more seasoning (pepper?). I think that my favorite part of the meal were the biscuits.

I was raised in North Georgia in a poor family in the 1970's. Every night Mom would cook supper and Dad, my three brothers, and I would enjoy what ever Mom was able to put on the table. It was traditional food cooked by the southern poor for over a hundred years. When I was tall enough to see the top of the stove she started teaching me how to cook the same way. Over the years I have tried to change and cook healthier while using the basic knowledge I learned. 

When I first heard of Loveless Cafe I was a bit skeptical and thought it was another place that served food that people "thinks" is Southern food. I was quite surprised.

I ordered fried chicken meal and a fried pork chop as well just so I could try it. Mashed potatoes with gravy, and creamed corn. My wife ordered her goto favorite  fried catfish with mac and cheese and fried okra. The only thing that appeared not completely from scratch and hand prepared was the okra. It was pre-breaded but still tasty. If anything served was not prepared in their kitchen it would be an extreme surprise to me. 

This meal transported me back to that dining room table with 6 people surrounding it. Mom that was there to take care of us daily, Dad, the hard working man that worked sometimes three jobs to make sure we had what we needed. Not always what we wanted but always what we needed. My three brothers and me. We never really knew we were poor but we always knew we were loved in good times and in bad. No matter what we knew where home was.... and still is. 

As I sat there with my wife talking and laughing with our server that first night, a tear welled up in my eye as I realized I was as home with my family as I could be....

Yes, it's that good, it's home.....

Our favorite place in Nashville! Barbara is such a sweetheart. She is always so friendly and the service is amazing. The southern fried catfish and the fried chicken is so delicious!! Oh and the warm buttered biscuits YUMM!! Always 1-2 hours wait during the morning weekends and nights but only 20-30 mins of wait btw 2-4ish during the weekends. Can't wait to go back again next month! 10% military discount too! :)
Excellent service and the food was outstanding. Our party got the garden/vegetarian omelette and the southern omelette .   Both were solid choices
Really busy at three in afternoon .  Nice staff.  Clean.  Great flavorful food.  Worth the wait.  Portions  are huge
A great place for comfort food. My wife and I ordered the meat loaf and fried pork chop dinners. Great homemade flavors and the portions were humongous. A definite stop if you are in town.

I had truffle fries for an appetizer.  Great stuff with cheese and bacon.  My meal was pork braciola and that was tremendous!  It is a rolled tenderloin stuffed with spinach, cheese and a white bean.  All covered in a marinara sauce.  Sides were potatoes augratin an a brussel sprout warm slaw.  The brussel sprout was done perfectly.  Really good meal that was unique and flavorful. 
We had stout chocolate cake which was good but not an OMG experience.
Atmosphere is very pleasant and service was excellent.  Waiter was knowledgeable and interacted with us on a personal level.

You are here for the biscuits! That being said, the rest of the food was a big southern mass of tasty awesomeness. 
You do not go here if you are on a diet, worried about unclogging your arteries, or planning on running a marathon that day.  The portions are big, covered in classic southern gravy and very very delicious. Eating to the point of explosion is a likely experience (especially because the biscuits come first!) 
Stopping by the gifts shops is very necessary. Do it

2nd visit to loveless cafe in about 6 years. Not sure why we dont go more often when we visit our family in Nashville.  Sad to learn that the biscuit lady had passed, but they are still going strong and the biscuits continue her legacy.

The wait was about 1 hour, but they have multiple shops , free lemonade and water and coloring activties, and cornhole boards for the kids.

the gentleman in the smokehouse even let my young niece and nephew come inside and see inside this work area and showed them  where the bbq comes from.

The foods was delicious,  we I had the country fried steak with hashbrown casserole,  with 2 eggs.  others had bbq, country ham, meatloaf and pork chops.  Everything was so good and the service considering how busy they were was outstanding.

An interesting place to try in a touristy area, but not a restaurant that would be in our regular rotation of places to dine. Mom had the goulash that was not like the Hungarian which we typically encounter. It was not a bad dish though, but a tad too salty. I started with beer cheese soup that was not anything to write home about. I ordered the pork shank on the recommendation of the waiter that was a huge portion, but somewhat lacking in sauce. The Black Forest cake is not baked in the restaurant according to our waiter who seemed devoted to serving the customer but was a good way to cap off the meal. I ordered a liter of authentic German beer from the tap which was a decent value at $13 and shared it with Mom. If we are out in Donelson or at Opry Mills, I might go back but won't drive across town on a special trip to eat there.

Came to the loveless this past weekend.  I have mixed feelings on this place.  First, the good.  The food was good.  I've had better but this is certainly better than average food.  The biscuits they bring out first are really good and the preserves were good as well.  I had the Half-Fried chicken.  The breading was very good however, the meat was a little on the dry side.  Good flavor just not as moist as I like my fried chicken.  The slow cooked green beans were good and my favorite part of the meal was the hash brown casserole.  The staff was very friendly.  

The bad, this is Tennessee and the Sweet tea left a lot to be desired.  I've had better Sweet tea at McDonalds.  The wait, yes I know the wait is long most days at this place.  I don't mind waiting but the shops just weren't much to look at and after about 15 minutes we had pretty much seen everything.  They had some corn hole games around but couldn't find and bean bags to play.  The snacks in the shops are way overprices.  My advice, if you need a little snack to hold you over while you wait for 2 or more hours, there is a Shell station next door.  Pick up a small back of pretzels for $1.  

Overall, probably a 3.5 stars in my book.  i would certainly recommend going for the experience and the friendly staff.  Expect the long wait and just be prepared.

We didn't have tickets to last night's show, but I decided that a "scouting trip" was in order before we return to City Winery next month to see Leon Russell. I also wanted to try out my VinoFile membership to see if it worked in person as well as it did online (no fees for ticket purchases - I've bought tickets in Nashville and Chicago already!).

First off - FREE VALET is a wonderful benefit at the Nashville location (it's discounted in Chicago).

My husband and I didn't have a reservation, but were seated at a high-top that gave us a good view of the bar and the lobby as folks were arriving for the evening show. We got a tasting-sized portion of a house white blend as we were seated - nice! The wine list was a tome - but we weren't really interested in a whole bottle of wine, so we just ordered from the "on tap" selection. Unfortunately, the first two "on tap" reds I tried to order were out of stock. But we ended up with two other "on tap" reds, which were fine. (Side note: Husband noted that Jack Daniel's on the rocks costs $8 at City Winery, which meets with his approval. $10 or above gets him hot under the collar.)

Our food orders (lamb shank flatbread and burger-and-fries) were promptly and correctly prepared, and very tasty! I intended to take half of the flatbread home, but promptly left it on the table. Cost for the evening (before tips) was $62. (Looking forward to hitting that $500 spend mark and earning free concert tickets!)

Service was friendly, but not overbearing. After we ate, we were allowed to wander around (the show hadn't started), and we thought the performance area looked spacious and lovely, and the upstairs bar/lounge was cool (but deserted). We're really looking forward to our return for Leon Russell, and I'm also excited about visiting City Winery in Chicago next month!

Friendly staff with mediocre food. Each time I come in the sausage is cold. Good is now overpriced but what do you expect from a town attraction? Biscuits no longer taste like they use to. Great location but underwhelming overpriced food.
Loved it. Food was pretty good. Soccer on tv so that was a plus. Polka band was awesome. Would have given five stars but it was pretty expensive. We will come back though.

This place is really cool. It feels like you're eating food someone's grandma made in her old farm-house. 

The menu is overwhelming and everything sounds awesome. And pretty much everything is. The pulled pork was great and the different flavored BBQ sauces were pretty unique. Mac and cheese was solid as were many of the sides. 

Next time, I'd go for breakfast, it looks amazing. But no matter when you go, GET BISCUITS.
Blane was awesome! This place was truly amazing. Our waiter was phenomenal. You MUST try the Brussels sprouts.
The food was amazing and our waitress was incredible!  Great atmosphere.  Worth the drive.  If I'm ever back this way is for sure come back!

Can you please expand the business to New York? I miss the biscuits there! So buttery, so fresh, absolutely delicious with home made jam! We had more than enough food to take home for the next day breakfast! I definitely will go back the next time I go to Nashville.

Five stars all the way. There is a wait and a hike to get there, especially from where I was staying by the airport, but it is well worth it. If you are looking for excellent southern, comfort food, this is the place. I had the country fried steak which was good but wish I would have ordered the fried chicken after tasting my dads. I would definitely go back if I'm passing through Nashville.

I've only called Nashville home for a few months now, and this was the first place my wife and I went to see some live music. 

I must admit, for a first timer, we didn't know what to expect. The Basement's website doesn't really give much info about the venue, but thanks to other Yelpers, we had a heads up about getting there early and hitting up the Free Tuesday night show.

We love this place. The small space forces an intimate vibe, and like many others have already said, this adds to the experience- so does the wallpaper of concert flyers and posters.

Tuesday nights (New Faces Nite) are when we frequent this place. Not only is there no cover, but you have the ability to see anywhere from 5-9 performers/bands ranging from local singer-songwriters to traveling Americana bands. Whomever is performing, the talent has always been phenomenal.

First time here and had a lovely evening. The upstairs venue is very nice, acoustics are fantastic, food was great and the service was excellent. There were some people at reserved tables but that wasn't an option for us when we purchased tickets online.  The smallest table size is for 4 so we were seated with two other people.

Valet parking was $6.  Surprisingly, there was only a 5 minute wait to get the car after the end of the show.  Our show was sold out so it was full but, rather than everyone stampeding toward the door at the end, at least half the room was just hanging out still eating or drinking so that helped regulate the flow.

There is a public lot immediately adjacent that was charging $10 - so not much difference considering a tip for the valet and we may do that next time.

Based upon some of the other reviews, it sounds like it's hit or miss but we will definitely be back for another show.

Honestly, Loveless never disappoints and on each of my three visits I've left here as happy as could be!

Once you sit down they'll bring you a plate full of biscuits and jam, and this could be meal enough on its own! The biscuits are always hot and buttery and delicious!

You won't want to fill up on biscuits though because you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. I'm partial to the chicken and dumplings, which is one of their blue plate specials on Wednesday. All of the sides are super tasty, but the creamed corn is really special.

I can't say I've ever made it to dessert... or even finished my meal! I always get caught up with the biscuits, which gives me plenty of leftovers!

Believe me when I say a trip to Loveless is worth the stop. Your stomach will thank you!

Take advantage of the whole experience. Browse the shops, take photos, and play some corn hole. The biscuits were perfect and the country ham is wonderfully savory. We think the fried potatoes are better than the hash browns casserole. I could have sipped on drinks all day. The Blue Moon is so smooth that it's dangerous.

Since City Winery opened, I have experienced many great performances there. As far as venues in Nashville go, it is one of the most intimate and one of my favorites. That's the good part. However, I find the food quality/service to be inconsistent. 

A friend and I attended the Labyrinth screening last night. It was General Admission, and my friend arrived a few minutes earlier to secure our seats. I gave the lady at the door my name, and told her I didn't need an usher since my friend was already seated and I knew my way around. One of the ushers started to walk with me, and I said that I was okay to find my seat. She seemed agitated and asked if we had menus. I said my friend probably had one. She started to walk with me AGAIN, and I simply said "can I just have a menu?" Then she huffed, said "fine!", shoved one in my hand and I walked away. Later I realized she only gave me a drink menu, not the dinner menu.  I should have spoken to a manager then, but I didn't want to cause a scene. I don't understand the big concern/rudeness over showing me to my seat!

Next, the food. The event ticket came with a prix fixe menu, which was fine with me. It was posted on the FB page and sounded yummy. However, the pasta entrée was pretty bland. The dessert, a crème brulee, was great...except for the fact the restaurant didn't have enough spoons to go around and we had to eat it with a fork. I usually enjoy the appetizers here, but you never get what you pay for. $3 for a flat soda (which was never refilled) was the icing on the cake. 

I wasn't going to post anything, but this type of service is ridiculous. I think this could be a top-notch venue if servers/management would just be polite and listen to their customers. I know several folks asked questions on the event page about times, menu, etc that were ignored. I will continue to see shows here if I like the artist, but I'll make sure to eat before!

My family and I recently went on a trip to Tennessee, and during this trip, I made it my personal goal to eat as many Southern biscuits as possible. The Loveless Cafe was my first stop on a trip to severe heatburn that was worth every painstaking moment and choked down Tums.

So let's start with the biscuit. Warm buttery and flaky as any good biscuit should be.  To accompany it, I also ordered the fried catfish, okra and sweet potatoes, along with a bloody mary made with the cafe's own bloody mary mix. I have to say it was the spiciest bloody mary I have ever had. My husband had an iced tea drink with moonshine that came with its own, little moonshine glass you could take home. Very cute.

But what the Loveless Cafe is known for is their banana pudding. Now by this point, after eating all of the above, I had no room for it. But we ordered some to take back to the hotel, and having never had banana pudding before, I have nothing to compare it to, but it was delicious with chunks of real banana in it. Overall, I was incredibly stuffed and pleased, and the only reason I am not giving this five stars was because I'm not sure it was entirely worth it.

Yes, the food was good. Yes, the atmosphere was awesome. But there was an hour wait. They have some cute little shops in the compound for you to bide your time, but so does Cracker Barrel, and honestly, I'm not sure this is THAT much more delicious than Cracker Barrel, so I'll leave that up to you. If you feel like checking it out and don't mind waiting, go for it. If you're just jonesin' for some quick biscuits, go to Cracker Barrel.

I couldn't decide between the fried chicken or bbq pork so got the sampler- good choice! Chicken was very good but pork bbq was absolutely the best! It was served on flapjack cornbread and was a meal in itself. Highly recommend taking the time to find this gem.

Outstanding food, friendly service.  Biscuits were amazing, I see why folks come back here again and again.  I was visiting some friends that live in Franklin and they took me here for lunch.  Large servings, tasty food, it was all good.  We didn't have to wait very long, maybe 20 min for our party of 4, so we had fun playing corn-hole in front of the restaurant.

The 10% off coupon is for their online store not the restaurant :(

I went for breakfast and ordered the country fried steak, hashbrown casserole and coffee. Breakfast was good but not memorable. Hashbrown casserole:  I expected something different. It was just hashbrowns saturated with cheese. I did enjoy the biscuits but was not blown away. I actually enjoyed the jams more. $17 for breakfast is a bit much but the portions were so big that it was 2 meals.

I cannot say enough wonderful things about this venue, the team of amazing people behind it, and their "leader" Mary Virginia Settle. Everything I needed was taken care of! Mary Virginia even took care of some things I didn't realize that I needed. Amazing venue and even more amazing people running it! My wedding reception was perfect! Easy! I was able to hand off a lot of decisions to them without worrying. They know what they are doing. I highly recommend Rocketown! Oh, and tip these wonderful people well. They deserve it for their hard work and attention to detail! Love!!

My friend and I were visiting Nashville for the first time and taking the Belle Meade Plantation tour about 15 minutes away. They have a restaurant at the plantation but we were looking for something local in town. 

The Loveless Motel/ Café came highly recommended and was said to have some stores to shop while you waited for a table. We were not disappointed! The wait was an hour and 20 minutes but there are three or four shops, and you can get a small snack while you wait; sometimes they're even giving out free samples of salsas or dips that they sell in the stores. The food is well worth the wait; it's basically Cracker Barrel, but fresher, local, and more friendly. Of course the history of the motel is nice to read about, too!

This is definitely a "must see" if you are visiting Nashville or even just live here. Great place to take friends visiting from out of town. You'll definitely have to wait a bit but I went around 9:30 am on a Saturday and it was less than 45 minutes. So not bad - plus, there are a lot of things to occupy your time while you are waiting. Mainly little shops to walk through which sell biscuit mix, jams, Loveless Cafe branded shirts, etc. The staff at the cafe is really nice and the service is good. You are greeted at your table right away and the service is quick and consistent throughout. Water and coffee are always filled. The star of the menu is definitely the biscuits and jams that come with it.
Delicious! But at the end of the day it is just a cafe - the eggs and bacon and other breakfast items taste pretty similar to what you'd get anywhere else. I got the veggie omelette which wasn't amazing but also ordered it without cheese so that may have been part of it. But I am not sure if people are really coming here for the food, but more for the experience at an iconic place in Nashville. And of course - those biscuits! Definitely worth checking out.

MAN did I love this spot! We stumbled on it by chance and I'm so glad that we did.  One of the manager's at the Johnny Cash Museum suggested it.  The fact that he threw it out there despite the fact that there were other eateries much closer that also provided down home Southern cooking said a lot.  It was well worth the almost 30-minute drive and the additional 1.5 hour wait.  Fortunately, you do not have to sit around idly while you wait.  The property was an actual farm and each of the buildings has been re-purposed.  So it is fun to walk around and explore the property until your table is available.  The barn is a nice venue for private functions like wedding receptions, parties, etc.  One of the other buildings is not a country store reminiscent of a Cracker Barrel but better! They keep your cup full with free coffee over in the country store and some samples of some of the food products made and sold on-site.   One building is the main kitchen and dining building.  Another is a store where you can purchase Loveless paraphernalia and other items.  There are also games like the cornhole beanbag toss and horseshoes to keep you occupied while you wait.

For breakfast we had the pancakes, waffles, biscuits, grits, eggs, bacon, and sausage.  EVERYTHING was soooooo good.  I wanted to try some of the lunch and dinner items but I simply didn't have enough room in my stomach.  Not only was the food great but the service was also excellent.  I forgot my server's name but he reminded me of Ashton Kutcher and even had a sense of humor as he helped me to decide on my food options and continued to check-in as we were eating to make sure that everything was to our liking.  If you are in driving distance of Loveless around breakfast time (or you just love breakfast food), do pop in for a bite.  It will NOT disappoint! I can't vouch for the lunch or dinner items yet but I WILL be back next time I'm in town!

If you love to eat, this has to be one of the best places to go.  Today was our second trip back to this restaurant and it was every bit as good as our first trip here.  This is definitely going to be on our list of restaurants every time we come to Nashville.

William

What a wonderful restaurant! Loveless Cafe is a favorite among Nashville natives and tourists alike! I have been frequenting Loveless since I was a young girl, and I just love taking our out of town guests for an unforgettable brunch!

Loveless is probably 30 minutes away from downtown, so if you are planning to travel from anywhere in the city, plan for a drive. Loveless is EXTREMELY popular, so you must get there early in the day to avoid a lengthy wait. 

If you must wait, Loveless Cafe has taken some steps to keep you entertained. There is a gift shop for browsing, Cornhole boards for playing, and lovely grounds for walking with loved ones. Sometimes the wait for a table can be as long as two hours, so plan for that possibility!

However long you wait, be prepared for the southern comfort food of your dreams. Small fluffy biscuits served with butter and 3 homemade jams are served first. And for the main course I recommend going with a table of at least 4-5 people and sharing one of their family style breakfasts. 

I would also COMPLETELY recommend the hashbrown casserole. (This is my favorite side, and my mouth is watering just thinking about it!) 

I have only been for brunch, but if dinner is anything like their breakfast food, you are in for a treat!

All in all, I would wholeheartedly recommend Loveless to friends and family! You won't be disappointed!

I was not impressed with the Loveless Cafe.  Most items on the menu are fried or heavily buttered.  We couldn't find the waitress with a Geiger counter, so trying to get a refill on our beverages was an exercise in futility.  I understand the "down-homey" allure of the joint - they broadcast a country music radio show in the barn adjacent to the restaurant.  I have been told the radio show is hit or miss - unfortunately, it was a complete miss on the the night I was there.  They had some decent local beers available, but aside from that it was only cheap domestics.  The wine selection is not very good at all.

Everyone raves about the biscuits - I've had better.

It's probably just not my scene, but I found the Loveless Cafe to be wholly overrated.

My spouse and I were excited to bring our in-laws for dinner and drinks someplace none of us had been before.  The restaurant appeared relatively busy, though there were no patrons that appeared to be waiting for a table.  We approached the hostess to ask about a table for 4 and what the wait would be.  The hostess did not look up to address us for several minutes, and when she did stared at us blankly.  She asked if we had a reservation.  We did not and inquired about the wait for a table for 4.  She stammered, stating that she truly had "no idea what the wait would be" but that right now, they were full.  I asked for any sort of estimate.  Again, she could not answer.  I noted that several seats were open at the bar and asked if we could sit there as an alternative.  The hostess struggled and appeared reluctant as she followed behind us to the seats.  Again, most seats were unoccupied at the bar.  After being seated for one or two minutes, I noted a table for 4 that was empty but assumed that there was likely a reservation for it.  However, after enjoying a flight of red wines and some parmesan truffle fries with lemon aioli (quite unique and delicious) an hour and a half later, the table continued to remain empty.  We left disappointed with that and many other tables empty.  Very upset and disappointed that the hostess (the primary job of which is to welcome and seat patrons) was so unwelcoming and unwilling to offer alternative options to us.

This place definitely lived up to the hype. Have always heard about it and had never tried it. Finally got around to it. The biscuits that they bring out are to die for. The jellies that they bring with them were probably my favorite part of the whole meal. The blackberry was incredible. The main course was great, as well. The creamed corn was probably the best I've ever ate- home or on the road!! Hashbrown casserole usually has onions in it, but not theirs. A refreshing break from everybody else's. The mac n cheese was exceptional. The meats were good, but the veggies were really what impressed me. The service was impeccable. Never had to wait on anything. We plan on coming back this trip for breakfast. Can't wait for those biscuits and blackberry jelly!!!!

Went to see Cracker here last night .  While the venue is beautiful, it is not a good place to see a show.  the tables are to close together and there is room to spread them out a little.  We ordered the duck tacos and two beers .  the duck was very under seasoned and the beers are a minimum $6 a piece.  the vocals cut out during the opening act, and the vocals during Cracker were awful.  Cracker brought out two female back up singers for a few songs and their voices were muddy and anything but crisp.  Johnny Hickmans backup vocals were muted and muddy all night.  Then the service.  What a mess.  I had to get the attention of a floor manager  after waiting over 15 minutes to place an order.  Then the waitress came along about 10 minutes after that.  Then during the show, our friends we went with were trying to get her attention, 4 times, she never came.  My wife got so fed up, she went to the servers station bar and ordered beers.  Then when the waitress came back, she seemed annoyed we did that.  Its a mess of a venue really.  Really pretty , great acoustics, but the whole premise is clunky and awkward.  Will not be back.

This place doesn't disappoint. Came from Southern Indiana to eat here and stay a couple of days in Nashville. I recommend the Sampler Platter. My wife's garden salad with fried chicken looked delicious.

Wait, are you kidding me? We drove 30 minutes outside on Nashville for this place for a Sunday 10AM brunch for 3 people. I already grew suspicious when I noticed that the parking looked like a parking lot for Disney, with cars with license plates from all over the south and college football decals. Disclaimer: I'm from New York City. Needless to say, we go through what feels like an amusement park filled with gift shops, jam shops and families having makeshift picnics on the trail to the actual restaurant. We go inside and were told that for 3 people, the wait would be 2.5hrs. Ha! We just left immediately, judging all the poor souls that came from the heartland of the country to a place that feels like a glorified Cracker Barrel.

What an awesome night to conclude our Nashville trip with friends.  We took an Uber there and killed some time upstairs in the record store, Grimey's.  The drinks were  heavy pours and delicious.  The venue is small but really does give a feel of a basement.  I loved the decor and the vibe.  The cover charge of $5 gave us a very full entertaining night of four bands all with their own unique sound.  My particular favorite was Craig Haller.  Make sure to check this out if you are in Nashville. It is definitely more enjoyable and relaxing than the crowded Broadway Street venues.

Been here a couple times when in Nashville.  Both times they had a great band playing mostly metal.  I was on a Wednesday.  I had to sit in the back because it was so loud - but that didn't bother me - because they were SO GOOD.  Wait staff and band were friendly and interactive.  Nothing is cheap on the main drag in Nashville - so I didn't have a problem with the price of my beer.  I like country music as well - so it's nice to be able to mix it up when I come to Nashville and get a variety of music.  I'll be back.  If you're snooty or tend to be judgmental - it's not the place for you.  It's a dive bar - and a lot of people like laid back atmosphere.  I pay cash for my drinks and never been over charged.

Food & service is really great. Worth the long lines? Not so sure.

However, if mom & dad are coming to town and you need to fill the schedule with some good country cookin, this is your spot! Plenty of kitschy shops to browse and buy jellies or trinkets while you wait. Toss some bean bags outside or just enjoy a chair under a shady tree. 

Once inside, you won't be disappointed. They're known for the biscuits, which I assure you are the bomb. My wife & I ordered the breakfast pork chops & country fried steak respectively. While both were good, the pork chops blew me away. Juicy & delicious with an awesome crunch. There was enough food to feed 3 people on that one plate. Plenty of leftovers for dinner.

Perhaps the best part of our visit was the service. These are the most efficient (and super sweet) servers I've seen. Never waited in anything. 

Would I cruise out to this place from Nashville for breakfast? Probably not. It's a pretty big time investment with the drive & wait. With that said, it'll be high on my list of places to visit when I have guests in town.
Simply delicious. The biscuits are to die for. The environment is welcoming. Don't be surprised if you have to wait for a table. The food comes out fast though!

The service was horrible! Our waitress was very slow and NOT friendly at all. We went at a slow time of day. There was hardly anyone there. I had ordered a burger of some sort. I took 1 bite and didn't like it at all. I waited several minutes until I saw her to tell her because she was no where to be found. She rolled her eyes when I told her. She asked if I wanted something else. I got the Rueben, only because my sister had ordered it and said it was good. It was much better. We waited several minutes to get our check. She had put our orders on 1 check. We knew it was going to take several more minutes to get it fixed and to pay. So, we went up to the hostess desk and proceeded to tell her how slow and rude our waitress was. At that moment, the waitress grabbed the bill right out of my hand and stomped away. She returned with 2 separate bills. NO tip for her! Kira was her name.
Biscuits are a must to take home. Great barbecue pork and fried chicken. Very family style and nice service. Quickly seated and served.

Not impressed. Bisquits are ok, pretty average tho. The wait time was long. They ran out of bisquits, had to wait 30 minutes to get more. The ham tasted like pure salt. KFC still has the best bisquits.

Jason was our server and absolute delight! The food was delish!!! Best biscuits ever! He warned me on the country ham and he was correct it's very salty. Thank you Jason. He did bring us a sample to try and it was very good but yes salty. If you like smaller portion I must say share a plate as portions are huge.

Biscuits and blackberry jam, yummy! Great home style food, recommend any of the chicken dishes and the hash brown casserole is a must. The wait for a table is worth it, and wait can be minutes or over an hour. Stock up on jam in the store while you wait!

This place has some amazing food but be prepared to ware for it. In my opinion it is worth the usual 2 hour wait. They have just about everything from ham and eggs to chicken livers. The biscuits are amazing and make for a memorable experience. You have to try the Loveless at least once. It's a Nashville landmark.
The breakfast is so great!  I love their biscuits!  I feel like I was in the old time at the former motel.  The place is perfect away from the big city.

Great food, awesome service, Best biscuits and gravy I had anywhere. Went on a mid week mid morning and still had to wait to be seated. That says a lot about a place when people are willing to travel and wait to get something good.
The breakfast was awesome. We went back a month later. I had the watermelon ribs, they were not that good. I will go back for breakfast but don't think I will for dinner.
Their breakfasts are lacking but I LOVE their lunch and dinners. Make sure you have plenty of time because it could take ages to get a table.

While the food was delicious, I was very underwhelmed with the service. For a place with wine in the name, you would think that the servers would be able to answer questions about the wine. Our server was not, and dd not even offer to go ask someone else. My appetizer came out with the entrées, which is a huge pet peeve of mine. If I order something to start with, I don't want to get it at the same time as my entree, having to choose which to eat first while the other gets cold! Our server also asked our table if we wanted separate checks literally five minutes after bringing our meals, and no one in our party was close to done. We felt very rushed. When our checks finally did come, one member of our party's wine was $3 more than it should have been. He asked about this, and was told that the wine she ordered was out and so he brought her a different one. You would have thought he would have run this by her first, but she was not even made aware that she received something different than what she ordered, and something more expensive at that! I was really excited to try this place because I had heard so much about it. I will not be going back to City Winery.
Went to Boca two weeks ago with my uncle and family for lunch.  We couldn't be happier with the food, atmosphere and staff. Anyone in the area should run not walk to Boca.

On vacation with 10 friends from Chicago.
We are foodies and have all worked in the food industry as servers so we have tolerance and yet...

We had researched where to get great fried chicken, great smoked brisket and great biscuits.
Loveless was decided for biscuits.

We drove 1/2 hour from our resort because of the recommendations.
We came in the evening on our first night (a Monday) and waited about 1/2 hour. Perfect. Really a fine wait time for a popular place. 
A few people went to the gift shop.

They seated us at two different tables a 6 and a 4. Not ideal for our first night together but we were hungry.

Our server brought out the biscuits. Meh.
I don't get the hype. It was bread with the jam on the side. Maybe biscuits just aren't my thing.

I ordered the sampler which was one egg, ham, sausage and bacon. DRY salty ham, dry sausage and overdone bacon. It *did* come with a hash brown casserole that I LOVED. I ate it all (I was starving. I'm pretty sure I make the same potatoes at home with frozen potatoes, dream of chicken soup, onion and cheese.

The fried chicken was underwhelming and not what I expected  from southern fried chicken . It was more the texture of shake and bake.

In my opinion, not worth the wait or the drive. 
There are MANY other wonderful places to eat in Nashville.

I just don't get this place.. I truly don't.

4 stars for entertainers.  0 stars for venue seating. 0 stars for food.

They have mediocre food, the tables are situated such that you have to block the aisles with your chairs so you can see over the heads of the people in front of you...
They turn the tables sideways - not straight on in front of the stage...
So all the people looking east and west have to pull their chairs out to face north, to watch the performer...

Terrible layout.  Terrible food.
Good artists.

Caught Damien Escobar, last night....   probably my 12th concert at City Winery...
I enjoy the venue, but just too much wrong with it...
It's really too bad that this place is so mediocre.

I totally enjoy this place.  We have visited here the last two trips to Nashville and have had a great meal both times.   Both my wife and I really thought the catfish was outstanding and I loved the hot chicken which I understand is a down south favorite. Side dishes were plentiful and the biscuits with preserves were awesome as well.  Save room for the peach cobbler and ice cream.  You will have leftovers for sure to take home with you ..
Great German Food and atmosphere. Try a bite of everything especially the beer and sides

My girlfriend and I tried City Winery for a Griffin House show in mid-November one Wednesday night. Mostly we wanted to see the new concert behemoth of SoBro (I still hate the name SoBro). 

First off, the atmosphere. This place is beyond superlatives beautiful and tasteful, all at the same time. They've made it obvious it's a nicer place without overwhelming the concert-goer seeking to just enjoy a show with a nice glass of wine. They'll start making their own wine here in 2015 so we'll be interested to go back and see even more of this gorgeous venue.

The wine. I'm just starting to understand different types of wines and an amateur at best in describing what I want in a wine. The waiter was well-trained and did not lead us astray when we were making our selection from the multiple wines on tap, available for a glass, and those available by a bottle. We tried a couple of these before we left and weren't disappointed. 

The food. It was good, not great. I had the leg of lamb pizza, which was tasty with a good mix of spices, crunchy pine nuts, and melty cheese. She got the Chicken Fricassee which was good but reminded me of much less expensive items I've had elsewhere. The food was tasty and good to munch on during a show or for dinner. I'm probably going to have dinner elsewhere the next time we visit City Winery, however.

Pros: Amazing building and predictably great wine selection.

Cons: Food was kind of expensive and didn't blow me away. The parking was pretty terrible. They offered paid valet or you can park on the streets, which is not the best option in this neighborhood.

Overall: This a relaxing, romantic place to take a date for a concert. You will win friends  and influence people if you bring someone from out of town in for a concert. If you can stand the parking situation and high-priced food, you'll be elated to make this spot one of your regulars!

I celebrated National Pretzel the best way possible.  I visited Bavarian Bierhaus on their open to the public night and they met my lofty expectations.  German beers and restaurants are among my favorite things and this is the most legit place in the south east.  The restaurant has an awesome gift section, oompa band setup, German beer hall seating, German beer menu, and, of course, food.  The menu is very comparable to the now extended Hofbräuhaus franchise but with more beers.  The waitress and hostess were attentive, and the GM paid our table a nice visit.  For food the giant soft pretzel was baked as good as any Bavarian bakery.  I ate the schweinshaxe (pork shank) which was the best I've had in the states.  The wife had the schweinbraten which was basically a pork loin.  She was ok with it but other things on the menu would have been better.  She was a big fan of the apfelstrudel.  If you like German beer halls this is the best around.

If you're in the area - drop everything and go here!
We were driving cross country and I read about this place online and got a recommendation to try it out. 
The biscuits are great, I'm not a big fan in general but these were really good and their homemade jams area amazing (bought some for home in their store next door while waiting for our table).
I had the pulled pork platter with the cream of corn and some potato side that were just incredible, the best meat, sauce and sides I have ever had (it's sad, i know).
My BF had the chicken tenders with fries, also great dish though I think that trying the local favorites is always best in these places. I asked our waitress what to order and went by her suggestion and I was happy I did. 
We will definitely be back next time we're in the area.

By far the best restaurant in Nashville. Their biscuits are AMAZING. I actually wanted to take their biscuits and gravy to go, they were that good. If you are only in Nashville for a day, this is the restaurant to visit. Definitely worth the drive.

Far and away the most gorgeous small concert venue I've ever seen.  Worth it just to see the room. Acoustically perfect and not a bad seat in the house. And they're also a pretty serious restsurant, catering to oenophiles and craft beet lovers. The  flatbread pizzas and the desserts were outstanding. And if they were any indication, I've got faith in the rest of the menu too. This ain't your basic bar grub....they'd do just fine as a restaurant even without the music.

But who am I kidding, right? Toss Buddy Miller and Jim Lauderdale out on the stage, and you've got yourself the moral equivalent of doggie heaven.

This place will ruin you for seeing a concert anywhere else ever again.  As the old saying goes, "How you gonna keep 'em down on the farm after they've seen Paree?"

Truly enjoyed this delightful surprise and Opry Mills Mall! Not at all the usual cramped, crowded normal Mall restaurant types. Very open spaces, large seating on benches,  German style seating so you were placed at tables with different people giving you the opportunity to make new friends. The pretzels are absolute heaven so light and fluffy and crisp! The food was delicious with very generous portions! Most definitely worth the venture to find this delightful place ! The night we were there they even had a polka band that did a fabulous job! We went on a Friday night, and due their communal seating they were able to seat us very quickly,  which was very refreshing on a Friday night in Nashville!

You can't miss this place on your visit to Nashville! This landmark features classic southern comfort food - and does not disappoint! The biscuits are the best ever and the coconut Cream pie is heavenly.
Great food, fun watching biscuits being made, and an interesting store to browse. Fun for the whole family.

On our way to our distention we saw a sign "Loveless Cafe" so I yelped it, checked out menu, & called in a take out order.
The order was ready when they said it would be ready. I bought a jar each of the peach & blackberry preserves 
We're on the road again. Car picnic dinner. We had the fried cornmeal catfish sandwich,okra, mac & cheese. All was good. Their biscuits were scrumptious, light & airing. Their peach & blueberry preserve were spot on. Glad I bought those jars.

We came on a Friday morning around 9:30am and there was NO wait at all, which was really great (the last time I came, it was a Saturday noon-ish time and we had to wait about 2 hours). 

Our waitress was really friendly and attentive and we were served their famous biscuits with three flavors of jam right away (strawberry, blackberry and peach). This kept us happy while we perused the menu. I ended up ordering the "City" ham and eggs with cheesy grits and their savory creamy white gravy with sausage (Delicious!!) and my friend ordered the fried chicken with hashbrown casserole and friend green tomatoes. We also asked for some red eye gravy to try and our waitress brought it out right away - not my favorite, but it was interesting to try.

The City ham was a nice thick cut and it was done just right. I had the Country ham last time and it was way too salty for my taste so I'll be sticking with the City ham going forward, which is cured in sugar but still salty too. The eggs were also done perfectly, not overcooked/burnt and the gravy with sausage went really well with the ham and eggs as well as the biscuits. At the end, we couldn't finish everything so I decided to doggy-bag it and had asked our waitress for a couple more biscuits to take home and she brought me four :-) The service is definitely awesome and the homey feeling of the place completes the experience. 

For the times when you do have to wait to get seated, there are plenty of shops to visit in the lot and there's also free lemonade/iced tea around somewhere. I'll definitely be going back and bringing friends to Loveless!

Expensive - $5.50 for a 11oz beer, $7.50 for a pint, liters start at $13, a flight of 6, 4oz beers was $15.  They have some signature cocktails $8+ Food was ok, had the burger, it was ok $11 came with fries.  Environment was loud, difficult to talk.  Music was German style polka with the chicken dance song being performed live, it was too loud and got old quick.  Service was average.  Easy to get a table and find parking.

My feelings about City Winery are kind of all over the place. I've gone there some times when the service is perfect and it's a wonderful evening. Other times I've gone and the service leaves a lot to be desired.

For concerts, anywhere on the floor is a good view. The tables get a little cramped, but that's no big deal. 

City Winery prides itself on being a "listening room" and I feel like they've been emphasizing "shut up and listen to the show" a lot more recently, but I went to one show where some Vinofile members were loud, drunk, and rude in the front row, and when people complained to the management, nothing was done. They never approached the couple, nothing. They just let everyone else's evening be ruined. 

Very recently, when I dropped off my car for valet, they reminded me that I need to tip on the way out because "the $5 goes directly to the building and the valets don't receive any of it." It was just offensive - were they saying I look like I don't usually tip? Or if you feel your valets aren't paid enough, well... pay them more appropriately? Of course I was going to tip, and of course I did tip, but the lecture about tipping to start off my evening was very off putting.

The most recent show I saw there, the waiter would not stop interrupting us during the show. I'd never had this problem before, as the service is usually super discrete. This show, however, the waiter would come over and hover about the check or talk to us while the artist was singing. It became very annoying. Every other time I've been there, the waiters have been awesome about waiting for applause breaks or encore breaks to handle checks and refills.

Having said all of that, though, it's still a nice place to see an intimate show.

I was raised in a family of good Southern cooks, so anytime that I eat at a meat and 3 I have high expectations. Loveless exceeded them. The biscuits were perfect. They were light and fluff and buttery. Everything I love in biscuit. Everything my friend and I had was wonderful. I especially like the hashbrown casserole. It was was full of sharp cheddar cheese, but not greasy. The green beans seemed to have a little vinegar i them, just like my Aunt Rita's green beans. 

We went on a Thursday night and there wasn't a wait. I imagine on the weekends its really busy. 

The service was great. We got our food in about 5 minutes and our glasses were always full. 

The Loveless isn't the kind of place I would go all the time, but it was fun. It is a little out of the way and kinda touristy, but it was good. The biscuits are so good!

Mediocre.  Food was not bad, but service was poor.  Partly bc of speed, but more it was just done poorly.  Plates sat while empty, not cleared before next course arrived, tried to cram too much on table.. And they seemed to have no clue that this wasn't good service.  Not sure if they didn't have enough servers, or what, but it made it not as enjoyable as it should have been.

Most of the staff was rude and incompetent. The place smelled like fish. Convenient parking, I have to admit. I think that this would be a good place to see acoustic performances or poetry reading. It's a strange place to see a rock show, and the staff acts like they're annoyed that you're there. Since this is a chain, is it like a slightly more upscale Hard Rock Cafe, just without the memorabilia?

This place was fantastic... We came here on a Tuesday night  and it was perfect... We were able to experience 3 different music groups and they were all amazing! The service was great! The space is very small but everyone was super friendly and it didn't feel awkward at all... People of all types, personalities and styles... Awesomely eclectic group of people!
