Was missing one star only because it's a bit out the way and you can't walk to anything else from it, but it's only a $5 cab ride to downtown which was totally worth it.
Beautiful venue. Came for the Dave Barnes concert. Incredible selection of wine, including wine on tap. Great date night!

This was one of the best places we went to in Nashville!! Unbelievable friend chicken, tasty sides, and the most delicious deserts. Out waitress, Susan, was just the best!! Cant wait to come back next time I visit!
Excellent sausage and biscuits. We had to get ours to go. Sunday 11 am had a two hour wait.

My favorite place in the Nashville area. Warm friendly service. Warm biscuits with Loveless jam to start are not to be missed. Chicken fried chicken was great but to get the most for your visit try the sampler platter. And take home some Loveless bacon from the shop!

The 35-40 minute drive from the Opry area to the Loveless Cafe was so worth it. We were a party of 5 and had made reservations for 8:00 pm. With only an hour left on service this place still had a good number of people eating. Our server was Barbara who was a pure delight and generous in helping us pack our leftovers. We also knew they were closing up as we were finishing and Barbara assured us to take our time and enjoy. Most of us ordered the sampler plate which allows you to pick three meats and two sides. Combined we had the pork, fried chicken, country ham, fried catfish, and meatloaf. Everyone enjoyed all the meats ordered. I had the chicken, ham, and pork and all were delicious. We had a variety of sides including creamed corn, mashed potatoes, fried green tomatoes, fried okra, french fries, and hush puppies. We all loved the creamed corn; all the other sides were good but the corn was exceptional. We failed to save room for dessert but will definitely try again if ever in Nashville.
Nice spot to eat breakfast. Biscuits were great. The rest of the meal was good. Will go back.

The Loveless Cafe was an amazing experience! My mom and I toured the entire place and had a blast. The food was also very good! The hot biscuits you are severed were amazing!! I had the cinnamon raisin french toast which was good and my mom's omelet was good as well, served a little too cold for our liking though. The hash brown casserole is a MUST try!! Overall good food and I would go back!
This is mediocre German food at best, and for the price point it's just not there. I guess if you're drunk enough you'll give 5 stars to anything.

Loveless Cafe earns its right to be Nashville tourist stop. However, I still can't get over the close-to-two-hour waiting time over southern food. But I also don't think you can find a truly southern comfort experience anywhere else in the Nashville area. So, it is worth trying at least once.

They now do reservations on OpenTable, which helps with the waiting time.

I personally wouldn't go back unless I was taking an out-of-towner here. However, I have gone back just to buy food and the other local gifts they have in their shops.

Protip: Eat there close to closing time. They give you the remainder of the biscuits they made that day.

Great biscuits! Peach jam taste like cobbler, so of course I loved it! The grits are sooooo good. I can only review the breakfast, and it was pretty good. Definitely worth a visit at least once. FYI: we waited an hour to be seated and was told it would be an hour and 45 minutes, so be prepared to wait.

Actually love this restaurant, however service was off today.  

Biscuits were served cold, the red velvet pancakes were cold and the sausage omelet was so-so.   Don't know if our waitress forgot to pick up our order or what, but it was not the best service today.  

Need to watch that!

Small venue with great talent. Grimey (owner) somehow finds some of the best local and touring artists around to come and play. 

Tuesday nights are NEW FACES night. You can see up to 10 acts covering several different genres in one night. There is always something for everyone on New Faces. AND IT'S FREE. 

Make sure to check out their calendar, there's generally an early (6pm) and late (9pm) show every night. 

Be sure to head upstairs before 7pm and buy some records and memorabilia from Grimey's and Grimey's Too.

Our first time here....OMG!  This is comfort food at its best. They brought out fresh hot biscuits and jam the minute we sat down, and they were deeliciouuusss!  The fried chicken strips, mashed potatoes, cucumber and onion salad were perfection. Chess pie and pecan pie were just average. They arrived cold and would be better at room temp. It's priced a little high and it's a 30-40 minute drive from downtown but worth it. Nashville treasure should be tried once by all; you won't need to eat again for 24 hours!!
Amazzzzzing fried chicken!!! I can say the best I have ever had. This place is a must go/see when in Nashville. Everything we ordered was amazing and everything we didn't order looked amazing too.

Don't go expecting the a best meal of your life experience. If you're local you probably know not to waste your time. I would mark this more as a tourist attraction. There is always a wait, so don't arrive hungry. The biscuits are made fresh, but I wouldn't call them amazing. I would call this an average southern style restaurant. You can go to Cracker Barrel and get the same food.

Ahhhh the Loveless! A Nashville landmark situated just off of the Natchez trace Parkway. Awesome daily specials... Most every jelly, jam, condiment... Is homemade. They have their own smoker! Everything is very very fresh. 

Breakfast is amazing. Huge menu and the biscuits and all the different flavored jams are part of your meal whether it's breakfast lunch or dinner. Friday nights there is a band in the barn which is actually a lot of fun as long as you plan for it. Just don't go most evenings thinking that you can walk in. Friday night and Saturday night is generally at least a two hour wait. That said, there are lots of games outside for kids and adults while you are waiting...as well as some really great local artist shops to poke your head in, browse, or chat for a few minutes!it is totally worth the wait. 
Being from Nashville, I believe I tend to take this wonderful nugget for granted. Additionally I pass by it every day to and from work. It's kind of funny to me seeing people standing in front of the sign taking pictures! But I guess that's part of the Nashville journey!...and don't be surprised on any given day if you see Mr. Vince gill or Allison Krauss ..or any number of country or rock 'n' roll legends when you look around at the tables next to you!
A total favorite among Nashville locals and visitors, alike!

This is by far one of the best places my family has eaten at. Very eclectic and charming atmosphere. Mark has to be the best waiter we have ever had. The food was great and Mark was memorable. We will never forget our visit to Loveless!!
I eat at city winery for brunch. It was the best brunch i have ever had. I had the biscuit Oscar!! So good cant wait to come back.

When we walked in the place was empty except the bartender and three other people. It was dark, dank and dingy, there was writing all over the walls, smoking allowed inside, dirty and disgusting...a true dive bar. I just love dive bars for many reasons but mostly because you can still get a great drink at a cheap price. 

While we were able to get cheap drinks, there was barely a choice of drinks to choose from. I am hoping they just had one hell of a night the night before and sold out of everything, but either way every beer I tried to order (first tried all of the local TN brews, then my favorites) they were out of almost everything, the bartender just opened the refrigerator so I could see what they had and end the guessing game. I ended up with some basic not so great warm beer.

They had a variety of shots...we tried the cherry soaked fireball $1 each, it was just what it sounds like, a cherry soaked in Fireball Whiskey. I thought it was pretty good.

The live band was playing 90's cover music, he was really good and we enjoyed it, but we were there to experience the country vibe...so after our drinks we moved on.

If they were playing country music and had a decent selection of (cold) beer this place would have been so much better.

Yummy!  Good ole Southern cooking. Fried chicken was delicious, peach jam excellent, sweet potatoes delightful. What can I say about the Hoe Cakes?  Unfortunately, they sat there while I ate my whole meal because I thought they were pancakes (I was with a tour group and didn't know the menu). Not to shabby.  Nice environment. Would visit again.

We had breakfast at the Loveless cafe and loved it.  We had the "breakfast #2" and it was a wonderful choice although a bit pricy for five of us.  It aloud us to try the things they are know for, cheese grits, ham and the hash browns. Our server was pleasant and the hostess spot on in her estimate.  This helps because I drove out early to place our name on the list before returning with the group.  Great food!

There is only one place better (in the entire world) for fried chicken and it's very close with the Loveless Cafe.

There isn't a time when I'm not in Nashville, where I don't make the time to stop and get some chicken.  The skin is nice and crispy but the meat stays juicy and moist.  You'll never get bad chicken here.

Biscuits, biscuits, biscuits! That's all you need to know- moist, buttery, absolutely incredible. If you want more go for the sides: mashed potatoes, coleslaw, fried green tomatoes. The restaurant has a whole plaza of little shops to visit while you are waiting for your table or for a takeaway order. To save time when the wait for a table is long, get takeaway and eat on the tables outside.

Good food, good service & a great atmosphere. The Fried Chicken, Meatloaf, Catfish & Chicken Fried Steak are all superb. The sides are wonderful & don't eat too many biscuits before your meal, trust me, its hard not to. Can't wait to go back a 7th time. Oh, the breakfast
Is great too!

Food was absolutely GREAT! Huge portions of homemade food, biscuits are to die for! First time and will definitely will be a repeat customer. 
Our waiter Jason keep us in biscuits, butter, sweet tea and we never had to wait on anything!!

This place is a MUST if you are visiting Nashville! It's a bit off the beaten path but is super quaint and features homemade goodness throughout the whole menu. We were so impressed, we are here twice during our short visit. The biscuits and fresh preserves are amazing, the chicken and dumplings was the best I've ever had, the chicken strips were juicy and mouthwateringly good, and all the sides were fabulous! The service was prompt and full of southern charm. After eating we walked the property and visited the little gift shop, which is full of mixes, preserves and sauces that they use in the restaurant along with a lot of cute little souvenir type items. Make sure to stock up while you're there and if you forget anything you can always order it later from their website. Overall, I would definitely recommend this cute little slice of southern charm to anyone looking for amazing food and a fun memory!

The biscuits were the joy of my visit to the Loveless Café, paired with the bowl of butter and jam varieties to put on them.  I ordered the country ham which was a little too salty for my taste, but everything else was delicious.  My husband ordered fried chicken and waffles which he devoured.  Luckily, we arrived right when it opened, so there was no wait for us, but our friends who live in Franklin said they once had to wait 4 hours!
Best biscuits I have ever had.  All three of the preserves served were delicious.  Had to wait an hour to get it but more than worth it.  Boyfriend had the pulled pork and eggs...fantastic!

My god. Worth every second you wait for this place. The biscuits change the game there.  Best biscuits I've ever had, hands-down.  The peach and blackberry preserves were out of this world.

Sausage gravy was really good too.  The pancakes are so-so, but to be honest, this isn't a place you go to for their pancakes. So many better things on the menu.

This place was a pleasant surprise! Great beer options, fun atmosphere, and friendly staff. Totally legit German food! Items on the menu prepared the authentic German way and small "American touches" like beer-cheese dip for the pretzel appetizers! Short 10 min walk from Gaylord Opryland.

Loveless Cafe is way on the west side of Nashville.  It has a storied past and is still a great place to eat!  They have a wide variety of traditional southern fare.  The service is great and the atmosphere comfortable.  My brother, who is a notoriously picky eater, ate everything on his plate!  I'll definitely be back the next time I'm on that side of town (or I might even make a special trip if I'm not there soon).

Great biscuits!! It's fun to watch them make them and boy are they good. Small in size and served warm so it allows you to eat too many! We had the pimento cheese omelet, added mushrooms and ordered hash browns as our side. It's very cheesy and filling. We couldn't even finish the hash browns. We also ordered the four biscuit combo plate. The fried chicken was amazing!!!!! The fried green tomatoes and pimento cheese are good but very rich. The bbq was also flavorful but again it's a lot of food. The cheese grits were delicious and I should have just had those. The staff was efficient and sweet just like the tea. It's fun to visit and it's a place to mark off your "restaurants to try" list.

We've been coming to Loveless Cafe when in town after discovering it 42 years ago-- before it reached landmark status. It has stood the test of time. Yes ,there are long waits occasionally , but if you go with that in mind you'll be rewarded with an unforgettable meal. Today I ordered the fried pork chops. They are crisp, tender and sooooo huge I could only finish half of one ( you get 2). Comes with 2 bowls of gravy, white and brown ,on the side. I had mashed potatoes and thin crispy fried green tomatoes ( superb) with it.

Been here several times. This was my worst and most disappointing experience so far. I ordered eggs and ham and fruit. My eggs were supposed to be over medium but they came out pure water. The whites weren't even cooked it was all liquid. Not even close to over medium. I end up not wanting eggs. The ham was so salty I couldn't taste the flavor besides the salt. I didn't even eat the fruit but it looked good. Anyways, they ended up taking the eggs off my meal which was originally $11.99. But they still charged me $10.50 for the ham and fruit which really I think is DISTASTEFUL considering they messed up my meal. They asked my mother if she wanted toast not telling her that it wasn't included and charged us $2 for that. Just stuff like that I don't think shows well of the business. $90 is a lot for three people for breakfast, especially since a few of our meals were messed up and they didn't take care of the bill. Sounds cheap to me.

Love the wine, ambiance and music venue. Food is really hit or miss. I tend to have better luck with appetizers and dessert than entrees. My last dinner there was so salty it was inedible. But the risotto balls were to die for. So, I think from now on this will be an apps-only place for me.

Reservations are a must for breakfast. The ham, biscuits and blackberry preserves are enough to make me fly back to Tennessee. The country grits tasted a lot like my mother's.  Lots of memorabilia all over.  Cute little shops around the property.

This place is awesome! Long wait but lots of seating and  to see while you wait. There is a BBQ shack in the middle that hands out free samples that are to die for! Also lots of cute shops! Bring a bottle of champagne and ok to drink mimosas while you.
 Fried chicken and biscuits were divine. Worth the trip and the wait!

My friends and I were closing out a trade show and needed a place to get food and relax. We walked in with low expectations given we were told they only opened a few days before, only got their liquor license at 4:00 that day, and were a German place in Tennessee. Maybe it was the hand drawn traditional artwork along the walls, the staff in authentic regional attire (for Germany, not Tennessee), the menu full of amazing options, a great selection of beer simply priced by one of three sizes, or possibly the three guys on stage rocking out crazy train on a drum kit, upside down employed saxophone, trumpet, and accordion (yes, three guys - four instruments, you do the math) but we were floored. Staff was awesome, beer was awesome, food is literally something to write (or Facebook) home about. Go there. Repeatedly.

Foods pretty good. A very busy tourist attraction, so the wait is always pretty long. They have really good fried pork chops, the steak and biscuits could use some more flavor. Daltons has better steak and biscuits for sure!!!
Cool venue.  Very small and cramped, but cool vibe for sure.  Not a wide alcohol selection, but got the basics.
Went and saw Marty Stuart last night,  the place is top notch.   Sound ,service,food was top notch,  we will be back.

I absolutely can not say enough great things about this place !!!! Mary Virginia and the whole staff was amazing ... We had our wedding and reception in the main room there in sep and they accommodated us in every single way imaginable and beyond ... It really is a very unique and cool venue . We have received sooooooo Manu compliments on our wedding and how fun and different it was . There was plenty of parking and space for all our guest (about 200-250 ppl) and no vendor restrictions so that was very helpful ... However they have suggestions for almost any vendor you could need and are more then willing to share the info with you .... I would recommend them to any and everyone looking for a venue not to mention it supports a great cause .... Love rocketown and I the  staff ... Can't go wrong here!!!
Great beer, awesome pretzels and bier cheese! Red cabbage is very tasty. Great restaurant feel. One of a kind place. Best place to eat dinner before an Opry show. Will be back!!!

This place was on my must do list when when we went to Nashville.  It was a little out of the city so it's a good idea to have a car to get there.  The drive was very pleasant, we saw a different side to Nasvhille.  I had no idea there would be such a huge crowd when we got there.  We went on a Sunday around 10am and there was an hour and 20 minute wait.  The nice thing is there are little souvenir shops in the complex where you can shop while you wait.  I loved the souvenir shops...it was probably the best souvenir I got from Nashville in general...very unique!  While we were going to the different stores, they had free lemonade and water that you can grab.  I really liked the lemonade.  After all that, we still had about another 20 minutes to wait, so we just sat in our car for the remainder of the time.  

Once we were finally called in through a buzzer that was vibrating, we got seated!  The service was outstanding!  They kept coming over to make sure everything was okay and to refill waters, coffee, etc.  We got the complimentary order of the amazing biscuits and they were great!!  I ordered the fried chicken...it was okay but I would probably not get it again from here.  Hattie b's makes it way better!  Everyone else felt the same way about their food!  I definitely think this is more of a place to get the experience as opposed to actually come for the food if that makes sense!

All in all, it was okay.  I definitely think you should try it at least once if in Nashville, but maybe not much more than that (unless you are really into biscuits)!

My boyfriend and I tried out the BB today for the first time. We started off with an appetizer of potato cakes that were just the right size and delicious. Good flavor and not greasy. My boyfriend ordered Jagerschnitzel and I had the Schweinshaxe. I know he really enjoyed his meal. It was crisp and loaded with layers of flavor. My meal was AMAZING and large enough for two people to share (next time!). My pork shank was crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. The side of purple cold slaw was a perfect balance for the rich meat. Our server, Noah, was especially delightful. He was friendly, efficient and made excellent suggestions..it helped that he is also from Germany and added to the authentic feel of the place. We can't go back on another night to catch the live music and try a few more of their beer selections.

Had to wait at Sunday lunchtime, but wow, was it worth it... Every bite was delicious southern cooking, like my grandma used to make. Now that we have gorged on chicken & waffles, fried chicken, numerous delicious sides, and some pie---- we are rolling out to car to nap... :)

My friend and I met up at City Winery for the Hotel Nashville show. This is a super vibing place from outside. 
They do have $6 valet parking, a good sized parking lot out front for $10, and apparently free parking somewhere around the back? I didn't drive around to check. I got there right at 6pm and the parking lot was full but it started to clear out rather quickly. 
Walking inside you definitely get hit with a great ambiance. We had to go upstairs for the showcase. The staff was very sweet and helpful. We sat down and I went to look at the menu... well that's kinda what made me unsure. I do get that it's more upscale and the food and most of the wine prices didn't really bother me. What I don't understand what makes the wine from city winery so expensive? I guess whenever I go somewhere I like to try what comes from the area. This case I didn't and settled for a beer, in which case I got a German import at the same price as I could have gotten for a PBR... to me, that's milking it. ‍
It's a very cool spot and I will at some point go back back for a tasting. The food is delicious, and definitely worth what you pay. 
The sound is great, every artist illuminated the stage. 
As for a winery, well I'm still trying to figure that one

Adorable space, great story, good biscuits. But the catfish, oh my god, was it disgusting. It was chewy. The texture was so off putting but I didn't want to send it back and wait any longer than I already had so I tried to suffer through it. I ate a third and had to stop before I got sick. The fried okra also had no flavor.

This place is more hyped up than it should be. It's a cute, southern place but the food, especially the sides, were not good. They didn't taste like homemade southern food, they tasted like beans out of a can and I was very disappointed in the Mac and cheese. Very bland. The food tasted like it came from a can then got microwaved. I got the hot chicken the first time and it was average, nothing great. I got the catfish sandwich the second time and was not impressed at all. It's a thin fish stick between 2 big pieces of bread with a ton of sauce. It was ok, not terrible, but I'm not sure what all the hype is about. The biscuits are great of course but that's probably the only thing that is made fresh.

Although we had to wait over an hour to be seated, the food was worth the wait!!  The hot biscuits are delicious and all of us raved about our meals (hot chicken, fried chicken, fried catfish) and all the side dishes were well seasoned and tasty.  I had the specialty pumpkin cupcake with cinnamon maple icing. It was so good!  I had gotten it to go and after I ate it back at the condo, I wish I had bought two!

We were told by family members we just had to eat here. Boy am I ever glad we did! Hands down the best turnip Greens I have ever had. And then biscuits melt in your mouth. I have the fried catfish and it is to die for!!! Stop here, it is worth the wait time!
Favorite restaurant in the known universe. Been going for 50 years and go every time I'm in town since I don't live here anymore. Love this place!

This is at the back of the Opry Mills  Mall  where we were able to find a parking spot so we said let's give it a try -- hubby as in the mood for a beer-- nice atmosphere like  German beer garden with long tables and a large bar area .  Our server Megan was very polite and attentive asking often if all was ok with food and drink.  I had the Reuben which was awesome and hubby had chicken schnitzel sandwich with ham and cheese which he really enjoyed. For dessert we shared a warm apple strudel with Carmel sauce and whipped cream it too was awesome . Although passing thru Nashville( tourist) I would recommend this place and would eat here again for a future visit ..fun place great atmosphere good food moderately priced

All restaurants go through the whole, we've just opened we have learning to do, thing. So that's pretty much what this is based off of. I will go back once they get themselves a little more together.

As we're walking in, first impressions are everything right, there is a couple complaining to the hostess about someone never coming over to take their order. The hostess apologizes and say's they can do something about it. The couple was so over it by then they declined and went to eat else where. This happened and we haven't even sat down yet. GREAT......

Hostess was very friendly. When we sat down the benches were very awkward. I'm a small person and I had to sit on the edge of the bench to even reach the table. It wasn't very comfortable and the table and chairs didn't move. My beer was great. My mother ordered the Reuben sandwich. She said it was really good and it looked really good. My Dad and I both ordered Brats. The brat was great, the bun was meh, and the fries were awful. The fries were actually awful for all three of us. They were cold, soggy, and really looked like they had been sitting out for a long time. I ordered a side of the german potato salad. It was wonderful!! Our waitress was ok.

I think I would prefer just to grab a group of friends and drink some beers at this place. Maybe that will change though in the future.

Made it to the Winery on a visit to Nashville. First, we were definitely surprised to see the restaurant was not packed as most restaurants in Nashville are on a Friday night. The waiter was good, attentive with drinks and stopping in to ask if we had questions. We ordered a variety of appetizers for our family: Mediterranean, house bread with butter, crab cake, mussels, and cheese board. The hummus, Mediterranean dish, and cheese tray were delicious, but the other food was sub par....the house bread was cold, and the pickled veggies had so much vinegar they were painful to eat. The mussels were bland and had no juice. The crab cake was stringy and had a blackened crust. We also ordered a chocolate cake that was dry, so I assume it was old, but the chocolate icing with crushed coffee beans were tasty. Overall, we were not impressed. Will not be returning.
We were in from out of town and looking for something different.. We found this cute little place and loved it! How cute! The food was great and staff was extremely friendly! Highly recommend it

Loveless??? More like Love MORE!!! This place is incredible!!! Biscuits up the wazoo!!!! I could eat their biscuits for every meal, every single day, even if I lived to be 95 years old. It would never get old. The staff is very friendly. It is as if I walked straight into my mamas kitchen and all my friends were there to serve me and make me feel like I was part of the family. This is a good place to bring the ones you love and love the ones that you see. If I was a man, I would propose to my wife here and then get married in their event space.

**Overall, this is an establishment that has changed the course of my life.

I went for lunch with my wife. The food was very good. it's traditional southern fair. Portion sizes are large. I had the fried pork chops and my wife had the turkey sandwich. Everything tasted good except the fried green tomatoes. They were breaded with a cornmeal and flour mixture that was heavy on flour. I know they are difficult to bread with a heavy cornmeal mixture but they are so much better that way. We will be back.
This place is incredible! Worth the drive and worth the wait! You must try the pie! So save room!

It was a great place for some acoustic music during the day, cheap drinks. 
At night it got smokey so for a non smoker it wasn't enjoyable.
Overall it was a decent experience
Very nice area to get away from the crazy city atmosphere with some great southern meals.

This place is amazing. Plenty of traditional German bier and amazing traditional Bavarian food with an American twist. Definitely a do not miss kind of place. If you haven't been, you're definitely missing out!

Great biscuits.  Friendly service.  Amazing biscuits.  Good breakfast.  Everything was enjoyable, and if it were near where we lived, it would be on our everyday to-do list.  Our cholesterol is glad it isn't, but this was some good good comfort breakfast food.

I hate to say this but this is a very hyped up place.

First I had a choice between hot chicken at princes or loveless. I chose loveless and took an extra 30 minutes to get there.

first it's been made pretty commercial with every possible piece of made in china memorabilia stamped with a "loveless cafe" including $12 bacon that is $4 in a price rite etc that put me off right away as did the $45 gift baskets you can mail yourself for another $12.

The biscuits were pretty similar to pillsbury pop open buttermilk biscuits. the blackberry preserved and butter made the biscuits otherwise it's not all that.
gravy tasted like Campbell's cream of mushroom soup with a handful of pepper. 

fried chicken was low on seasoning and salt. it was all crunch and no flavor. I have a corner grocery afghani place near home that makes infinitely better chicken for $1 a piece. the hash casserole and catfish came out cold and had to be reheated... the casserole was good but you can put that much cheese, butter and heavy cream on paper and it will taste good too. 

the fried gizzards and liver... were awesome. Saved the meal for us. my wife though the same on all points. overhyped and under good. 

I'd give it 3 for a random place but 2 for my overhyped expectations.

this is a made in China and mass produced version of what was probably an authentic piece of Americana even 20 years ago.

Very disappointed. I ordered the sauerbraten. It was a tiny piece of over cooked meat on a pile of red cabbage. There was so much cabbage on the plate it was in everything. My wife had the rouladen which was ok but it came with over cooked spaetzel. Very unappetizing. We ordered the sampler desert for $10. When I got the bill it was $13. I was charged $3 for a scoop of ice cream that I hadn't ordered. With a glass of wine and tip it was$73 for a very disappointing lunch.

We kind of stumbled into this place by accident. What a great accident. This gem is off the beat and track and is just so cute. We had a 25 minute wait but killed time walking through the little shops on the property. Such fun all American trinkets. The food was delicious and service was with a smile. The biscuits are so yummy with a variety of jams and the ham was so fresh.
Food is like eating at Mom's kitchen. Tasty and all is fresh!  We had meatloaf, waffles, and pulled pork and they were all tastyyyyy!  Get to them early and shop around the shops..

Fun place outside Nashville. They have made it into a bit of a tourist destination. The creamed corn is great. Biscuits are rockin'. Had the "special of the day" creamed chicken & dumplings. Good, wouldn't call it great. Excellent service, nice atmosphere. A little pricey, but worth a visit.

I love Joan Armatrading, but was disappointed with the sound quality (tinny & echoed) on the balcony - the a/v guy was told, but it didn't seem to make much difference - I've been before  downstairs and had no complaints re the sound........so my suggestion is to book downstairs (I like that one can pick your own seats)

Normally I don't rip restaurants, but passing your cost of business on to your customers is WRONG! An excise and lbtd tax on top of sales tax? This is a joke, right? No, it's not...mediocre food and paying for another meal in tax? Don't think so, never again!

Average breakfast with a 2 hour wait no matter when you go. This place has a great reputation, but I was unimpressed. The ham was too salty for me and the sausage patties were dry, but I guess that may be how country ham is supposed to be? Whatever the reason, it's rare that I will leave food on my plate, but I just couldn't eat the ham. Biscuits were good, but "best biscuits in Nashville" is a stretch. It's a cool location with a few things to do (like giant Jenga, free lemonade, and some gift shops), but its out of the way. I would recommend other breakfast places closer to downtown Nashville (Fido, Tavern, Jacksons, Noshville, or if you're looking for more of a low-key country breakfast, Pancake pantry whose wait times are comparable to Loveless).

Let me start.
Could not find the place from inside the mall.
Sat at the bar took 15 minutes for bartender to serve us.
Beer selection and quality excellent.
Food so so ,wifes burger overcooked.Fries ice cold bartender brought out some new ones on a different plate.not much better.Plates sat a long time before they were removed.
suggestion get a pretzel and drink the great beer and forget the food.

Eat here every time my parents come into town because my mother is obsessed with their southern food! Have waited no less than 1.5 hours for a table on Sunday afternoons but well worth the wait. The biscuits alone are worth any wait! They are to die for!!!! Pretty sure I could eat the whole plate of them myself. I've only had fried chicken which is so good. The breading on the chicken is so darn crispy! Banana pudding is good, but can't say I love the other desserts. Definitely a fun atmosphere and have always had excellent service. It's one of those iconic places you have to try when in Nashville!

So lets start off with the fact that this was my mother's birthday. We walked in and greeted the first person we saw. He told us to go by the concierge desk. They were not warm at all. The immediately directed us back to the initial desk. At this time the awkward gentleman said that he would be giving us the tour. The sommelier was extremely lack luster. He had the wine already picked out.He also seemed forced to have convo and not very personalable. We paid for a wine tour I definitely expected this experience to be a tad more elevated and exciting. I'm not exactly sure why they charge so much for a tour that lands you only between the wine cellar and the front door. Having been in service industry for many years, I find this experience and level of service to be underwhelming. I honestly only gave it 3 stars because my sister was able to talk to the staff about our experience same day. They did their best to make it right.
Friendly and good service. Pretzel was to die for, onion soup was amazing. Worth the trip.

We absolutely loved this restaurant! It's super busy on the weekends, but if you catch an early brunch or lunch during the week, it's perfect. It's definitely a place we will continue to visit throughout our lives.
Great place food was great. It's pricey so be ready for that. Glad there's something different restaurant wise in middle Tn.

Definitely yummy food but the wait is just insanity. I think we waited an hour and a half and there's not much to do to fill that long of a wait. There's gift shops and fun little history areas to learn about the place but those don't last you over an hour. Not much seating or places to wait either so you kind of stand around for a while. But once you finally get seated and get to eat the food is really good and the staff is all really nice! As always, don't pass up the biscuits.

Loveless Cafe... it just does not get much better than this. A Nashville staple, this place has got it all- music, biscuits, and out of this world chocolate milk! If you have a more adventurous spirit, do not fret they have quite a selection of breakfast/lunch cocktails. 
The biscuits are amazing- you can choose from an assortment such as fried chicken, ham, sausage, fried green tomato, etc they also have a biscuit sampler where you can pick four kinds of mini biscuits... it does not sound like a lot of food but man it is so filling! 
My friends ordered variations of eggs/ omelettes and said they were cooked to perfection. Out of nine people, not a single one of us was disappointed with our food nor had orders remorse.
Oh my gosh and do NOT get me started on their hotsauce. Being a hot sauce fanatic, I am normally not impressed with restaurants if they do not carry some form of hot sauce other than Siracha/Tabasco. So obviously, because Loveless Cafe was marketing their own hot sauce, I was quick to write it off. How wrong I was. This hot sauce is AMAZING. It's spicy without being overwhelming and adds a unique flavor to any dish without overpowering the original. I was such a fan that I bought a bottle for myself and my family. Two months later I went and purchased three more bottles. Mark my words, it is some of the best hot sauce you will ever have.
The only downside would be the wait on weekends, but if you go early enough you can avoid this. And the actual wait itself goes by pretty quickly except on holidays. Otherwise, when going to Loveless Cafe, you're in for a treat!
I was terribly disappointed w dinner tonight. Service was super slow. Food was mediocre, and I'm being kind. Loved the atmosphere and decor. Wine was good. But I won't go back.

The biscuits here rival anything you have ever eaten! They are incredible and they never stop bringing them to the table. Served with homemade peach, strawberry and blackberry preserves. As my cousin so aptly put it as she bit into her third biscuit "this is my church"!!! The coconut cream pie is my all time favorite from anywhere I have eaten. The custard is thick, rich with just the right amount of coconut and sweetness. The meatloaf is juicy and the tangy sauce they put on it is so yummy. Not a ketchup paste at all. Loved the green beans and the white beans too. And the pulled pork. This is a must go for every one

We opted to get take out and eat at nearby picnic table rather than wait the 1 1/2 hours. It was a Saturday, so I suppose that explains the long wait. We waited about ten minutes for our food.

The biscuits were really good. I wouldn't say they were life-changing, but I really enjoyed them and could have eaten about a hundred. I got the sampler plate with two orders of fried chicken and BBQ, with creamed corn and fries on the side.

The fried chicken was awesome, not the best I've ever had, but definitely in my top 5 all time. I wish they would have served it with honey, but that's just me being extremely picky--I'm sure I could have asked for it. The outside was super crispy, the fat had been rendered down, and the inside was moist. The BBQ was really good as well, with a great smoky flavor. I really liked seeing the open kitchen around the BBQ pit.

The creamed corn was delicious. The cashier recommended it, and that was a good call. It was creamy, flavorful, and better than any other cream corn I've ever had before in my life. The fries were your standard fries.

We were able to visit on a weekday, so we didn't have to wait in line which was a huge plus. The biscuits were delicious, complimentary and hot - plus three jams to try. I had a typical breakfast - eggs, bacon and grits and my friend had chicken and waffles with a side of hashbrowns. Personally, I love grits and I thought these were amazing. Everything else was great too and the store was cute. That being said, I gave it 4 stars since it is so far removed from Nashville and it did feel slightly overrated.
Awesome bar I came across while I was in Nashville for my birthday. Cheap beers and great entertainment. They have awesome Jell-O shots there! I went to this bar a few times while I was there!

I cannot believe I'm just now reviewing the loveless! Such a great place to eat if visiting the Nashville area. The biscuits and jams are incredible and the perfect starter (free) to any meal! The fried chicken, creamed corn, fried green tomatoes, sweet potatoes, and turnip greens will make you slap yo'mamma! ;-) very good! And I hope to visit again very soon!
Great comfort food. Great service. Cute little place! While waiting for a table we explored the shops and buildings around the property.
Loveless is the perfect country cafe! The hash-brown casserole is a staple. The wait will be long but there is plenty to do while you wait. They have corn hole boards and shopping!
Fantastic food. Great service. Friendly. Loved the biscuits and gravy and cheese grits. No crowd on Tuesday morning. Wish I lived closer

This is second time we visited this place with same great friends.  First time we thought they had some things to tweak.  Today all the details have been figured out.  Phenomenal service by Jeremy.  Food was awesome,  potato pancakes were as good as my moms. Beer is the best in town.  Music was authentic.  Thank you for a great time and the personalized service we received from the waiting team at our table of seven.

This is a great place just outside of town. Most of the food is greasy, fatty, and pure goodness. If you're looking for healthy options, this is probably not your place. But if, like me, you occasionally like to eat way too much fried food and wash it down with sweet tea, then this is worth a stop. 

I've found that it's a nice place to bring out-of-town guests. In fact, that's the only time I ever go. But there's lots of country music references and decor, which is very Nashville. 

The wait is normally long (an hour on average), but there are shops and corn hole boards, etc to pass the time, especially if the whether is nice.

I mean the Lovelace Cafe....  How can you go wrong!? There is a reason people drive 25 minutes outside of the city to eat at this place.  I have lived in Nashville for almost 2 years and had yet to eat at the Loveless Cafe.  I have had the food catered but never at the restaurant.  When my parents came to visit I decided this was my opportunity.  

We came here for lunch on a Thursday and the place was packed! The hostess was telling people that there was a 1 hour wait.  I only had to wait for five minutes because I made reservation (you can make reservations on weekdays, and I strongly encourage doing so!). 

The Loveless Cafe is actually a small house but it is bigger than it looks and the decor is very old fashioned farmhouse.

I mean their food is amazing!  It is the food that you wish your southern grandma made if you had a southern grandma.  I had the fried chicken, coleslaw, mashed potatoes and gravy.  Lucky for me they brought out green beans instead of coleslaw (which they quickly fixed but let me keep the beans) and the green beans were amazing!!  My mom had the smoked turkey and my dad had the fried chicken and waffles.  They also bring you a plate of biscuits and jam which are out of this world!  

When you walk to the bathroom you can actually see them making the biscuits which is a treat!  There is a reason this place has been around so long and if your making a trip to Nashville you won't be disappointed!

I'm not normally a fan of German food, but I am a fan of this restaurant and the options on their menu.

The long tables will accommodate a family of any size and the staff is attentive and don't mind answering any questions you may have.

If you're a beer fan, you will love the selection here. Also, ask about the beer club.

Last night, we went to our favorite restaurant to have a small celebration of life. Just four of us. As always, we were greeted by 3 smiling faces and, quickly put on the waiting list. (At that time, it was 35 minutes.) 30 minutes later, our buzzer was buzzing.  We were seated and greeted by our server, Owen. WOW!!! They were BUSY. Owen is an amazing server and we were delighted to be in his area. Each of us discussed how the food placed in front of us was perfect. Absolutely perfect. Yes, we are regulars. Yes, I notice everything. I have worked food service for over 35 years. Everything was perfect but, we wondered why we were not greeted by a manager. They always greet each table. Well, I got my answer. After leaving the ladies room, I passed the kitchen. The tension was visually clear. The manager we were hoping to come by our table was in the kitchen, yelling at the staff. I wanted to tell her how much we loved our night and thank her. She had no idea I was even there. Cristy truly let me down at the end of it all.

Great food and service for years, but just not worth the long waits. Their seating scheme is far too egalitarian. Owners should consider giving priority to locals who've been patrons for years. I'll be back, but less often due to the excessive waits.

I was surprised with this place! I didn't expect it to be anything great, but it was good! The atmosphere is amazing. Inside is beautiful, wood tables, pretty bar, & then they have a neat music venue where you can eat & listen to music. They also asked you if you would like to try a little of the wine of the night when they seat you, which I thought was a nice touch. 
Our server was great when it came to picking a wine. He asked what I liked & then suggested one, which was very good. He did get a little overwhelmed with other tables & forgot to check on us a couple of times, but hey, it happens.
The food was good, but not as good as it could have been. We had the Crispy Risotto Balls & they were not that full of flavor. Somewhat bland, as well as the sauce that came with them. The Alfresco's Cavatelli was good, but it seemed like it had been sitting out for a minute because when it arrived it was cold & the pasta did not seem cooked well. Also, it most definitely could have used more flavoring or sauce. 
The menu is somewhat confusing & all over the place. I think I need to go back & try a few more things & speak to the waiter more about the menu options. I most definitely will be going back for the atmosphere and wine selection!
By far, worth the drive! If you're visiting Nashville this place is a must be in your To-Do list! Very good service and fabulous food!

This place is a bit overrated. I love the decor and the history behind loveless cafe, but the food was sub par. The service was excellent though. I had the Country fried steak and to be quite honest, i've had a lot better. I hope this was an isolated expierence.

I don't know why it's taken me so long to write this review. You'd think out of all the times that I've been and had to wait an hour and a half before being seated that I could find the time to write one up! But no, I've usually found something else to do. They do give you a little disk that vibrates when you're ready to be seated. The Loveless has a few gift shops around that you can browse in. Some of the gifts are really cute but touristy expensive. Now...good lawd the food. Biscuits are made from scratch and are light and fluffy. They come free with your meal along with 3 preserves. If my memory serves me correct they're strawberry, blackberry and orange marmalade...or peach. I don't know. They're all tasty though! I ALWAYS order a side of cheese grits! I'm telling you I drive clear across town for their grits. So freaking good. They serve breakfast all day. I keep telling myself that I'll try something else then never do...because cheese grits, yo. We've tried a variety of things and have never been disappointed. They have excellent bbq, hashbrown casserole, fried potatoes, country fried steak...it's all good. This restaurant is the epitome of classic southern food. Service is kind of hit or miss. You've got the servers that have been there awhile that found their niche and are on a roll. Then there are the newbies that shuffle through things. They're all right but don't give you the "Loveless experience". Parking can be a bit rough depending on when you go. I've never NOT found a parking spot but you might have to walk a ways. No biggie. After eating all that fried food, a bit of walking might do you some good!

I've heard wonderful things about Loveless Cafe so finally made it out there. We went on a Friday morning to avoid the weekend rush. It was a beautiful 20min drive outside of Nashville and managed to get in after a short 10min wait. It was busy on a Friday so I can imagine the craziness on the weekend. Good news is of you did have a wait there is a outdoor area to walk around and buy keepsakes, souvenirs, etc. 

The biscuits were good but not as I had imagined. I had such high expectations. The trio of preserves were delicious and paired nicely with the hot biscuits. We didn't order anything special--eggs and bacon/sausage. Very average or typical to any breakfast joint. I would have been happy with my coffee and biscuits. Service was good!

The biscuit mix you buy in the store is quite good and you only add buttermilk. Very similar tasting to the real thing. 

I will return--and try lunch but during the week.

Loveless is a tasty treat after (or before) a ride down the Natchez Trace.  The food is okay, but not spectacular.  The wait is long, but worth it if you want the Loveless experience.  For my money, Monell's in Nashville is better on food, but lacks the experience of a nice drive and a shared "It's Loveless!" experience.  While you're waiting, go over to the shop area, get corn hole equipment, and toss the bags.

Great place to eat and walk around and do some short shopping. The jam with the biscuits is amazing. The hostess and waitress were both knowledgeable and employees loved their job. The chicken and waffles was perfectly cooked the skin on the chicken was to die for a must try! I also had a blue moon it came in a mason jar and was super smooth.

I took my folks here for brunch while they were in town visiting.  The biscuits are incredible (and bottomless) -- well worth the wait and drive.  I had the fried chicken and biscuits and will definitely be back.  Be ready to wait at least one hour, but there are some shops to browse in while you wait -- we brought a deck of cards.

Very reasonably priced given their demand and the food was very good.  Friendly service, great spicy, strong bloody mary's.

Food is good.... More of a tourist spot
Had dinner sampler ( catfish, ham, fried chicken with hash brown casserole n Mac cheese) 
Catfish-- great light batter
Fried chicken- crispy. Could use more seasoning
Country ham- salty 
Biscuits - great with the blackberry jams

Drink
Blue moon -- great with the moonshine 

Is it worth the wait? Depends

WOW.  Don't go anywhere else in Nashville for breakfast. Or lunch. Or dinner. Every little thing we had here was incredible. Tammy, our waitress, was a total pro!  She was so sweet and I never ran out of coffee or water once!  Service was quick but we were never rushed and had a great relaxing breakfast with plenty of leftovers to take for snacking later.  What a gem!

Had to do it, too many friends recommending the biscuits etc. 
Flew into Nashville and went straight to the Loveless Cafe. They clearly have this thing figured out - multiple parking lots, mail order hams, a general store, and an art store. All are there to keep you entertained during your looooong wait for a table. 
We arrived at Loveless around 1100 and were told our wait would be 70-80 minutes for a table. No problem, figured it would be worth the wait. Like everyone else, we cruised the stores and wandered around. After 45 minutes, we were buzzed. Yes, they have buzzers to let you know when your table is ready - and they work anywhere on the compound. 
We were seated and quickly met by our waitress. Service was good, fast and efficient. Drinks, biscuits and jams were on our table in 5 min or so. We ordered and had our food in 10. Everything was good, not spectacular, but good. 
Would we go back, you bet. Would we wait another 45 min for a table? Ummm, doubt it. But, again, the food was good and you have to go once to check it out.

Amazing southern cuisine! We dined at Loveless for breakfast, which was absolutely delicious. I ordered the Biscuit Sampler Platter with cheese grits. It came with 4 slider size biscuit sandwiches of pulled pork, fried chicken, medium rare steak, and ham. All deliciously seasoned and cooked perfectly. The cheese grits were also really tasty. This meal really hit the spot.

My boyfriend ordered the half order ham & eggs with hash brown casserole. After he tasted my pulled pork, he wished he'd ordered the pulled pork & eggs. Regardless, he enjoyed his meal and I couldn't help but sample the delicious hash brown casserole.

We were visiting from out of town, so we were excited to buy their cookbook, available for purchase in their gift store.

I'm still thinking about just how tasty this meal was & can't wait to make some of the dishes at home!

Great food, great music, great fun! Our family ended our reunion vacation with 19 of us eating here on Friday night. Kids and adults alike had a great time - and we now have a 2-year old who yells "oy, oy, oy!"

Great food and atmosphere. Takes you way back in this awesome setting. Depending upon when you get there there is usually a wait, but there is plenty to see and walk around the grounds. Biscuits were fresh and amazing, food came out quick and everyone enjoyed their selections. A must do while in Nashville.
Grilled smoked pork chops are to die for.....  Biscuits were not as good as the hype.

Everyone raves about this place,  however I wasn't impressed.  The famous biscuits were OK.  I have definitely had better.  Our waiter wasn't really friendly and some of our food was burnt.  We were kind over the place and didn't bother to say anything.  We ate less than half the food.  The shops are a little over priced but a cute set up.

I was skeptical when a friend first suggested that I check out Rocketown as an event venue... and boy, was I wrong. 

Rocketown is the jam. 

With room for up to 1500 of your friends , the main venue space has fantastic built-in lighting and sound system so that your don't have to outsource for these additional costs. The attached complimentary parking lot and available surrounding street parking are a luxury to have for a venue space, especially one that is located Downtown! 

I love the expansive and industrial space that makes up the main room. It just beckons you to make the space your own whether you're producing a concert, wedding, conference, fundraiser, or really, the sky is the limit. I planned a community outreach fundraiser for 1000 here and had the best experience! We brought in food sponsors, adult beverage sponsors, and various nonprofit booths into the massive space and it felt and looked fabulous. Did I mention Big Wheel drag races out in the parking lot? Only for Yelp Helps, folks....

Throw in the fact that there is a generously sized stage, up to date bathrooms, and multiple entrance points and you have a ton of room to spread out your own event concept. You also have the option to rent out the smaller "White Building"which is across the way as it is more suited for events 500 or under. The Skate Park is also available for rental and use too.

A cozy "living room" setup greets when you walk into the front doors and you may be surprised to see a fully operational coffee bar filled with java, snacks, and other refreshments. I should set up my "office" her once a week because it's a nice environment to get some work done or relax. You'll see anything from students and creative types to professionals sipping on a latte and working on projects here. They also schedule art exhibits, open mics, and other events within this space from time to time.

And, I can't say enough about Mary Virginia Settle who is the dedicated Director Of Operations here. From the first time I reached out to inquire about using the event space to the cleanup of our event, this lady is nothing short of fantastic to work with. She's always looking out for everyone's best interest and not afraid to roll up her sleeves to help ensure that your goals are met. I wish that I could work with people like her every day!

TIP: As if there isn't enough wonderful things going on here, the work and community outreach that Rocketown does for the youth in our community is admirable. They have afterschool programs, summer camps, and other events throughout the year that help kids off the streets. Rocketown is a 501c3 nonprofit so you may also make donations or contribute to this wonderful place!

One of the best places to grab breakfast in Nashville, TN (breakfast is served all day). This place is a little further outside of downtown Nashville, but it's worth the extra drive. Be prepared to eat when you arrive because the portions are massive. All meals come with complimentary fresh baked biscuits and jams.  

The first time we came here we ordered the country ham (with 2 eggs and hash brown casserole) and the country fried steak (with 2 eggs and fried potatoes), both were excellent. The country ham and the country fried steak was as big as my face! 

This place was so good that we came back a second time. I decided to order off their supper menu and got the fried chicken gizzards (with a side of gravy, turnip greens, and cheese grits). They did not disappoint, everything was delicious. 


Not only did this place have awesome food, the service was great and friendly.  I highly recommend coming here on a weekday because it gets super crowded on the weekend and the wait can get up to 1 1/2 hours. However, if you decide to wait for a table on a weekend it is absolutely worth the wait. Just outside the cafe there are little shops where you can pick up jams, hams, and souvenirs.

First impression: really cool space. Warm and inviting---intimate for a concert setting, but not too shoulder-to-shoulder, if you know what I mean.

I won tickets to a Lord Huron secret show today, and we ventured here for the show and lunch. My boyfriend and I both ordered the burger and substituted sweet potato fries and zucchini fries, respectively. Service took a while, our burgers came out lukewarm and flavorless... and the substitutions were not made. I was supremely disappointed--the burger looked AMAZING... and the taste didn't match. The show was amazing, and that was the saving grace for the afternoon.

Valet is $5... mostly, the experience was meh. I wouldn't mind going back fo ra show, but definitely won't plan to eat here.

This was on our list of places to visit while in Nashville!  Even though it is out of the way it was so worth the stop!  Quaint setting and amazing food.  I could not choose what I wanted so I got the biscuit sampler!!!!!  Best decision - the chicken was amazing!!!!  Their hash brown casserole is a must try!

This place is all about country BBQ, but the food does not deliver. My husband ordered pulled pork and fried chicken, with sweet potato and fried okra sides.  I'm vegetarian, so I was there for him; the menu had no veg entrees, although it did mark the side dishes that were flavored with meat. I ordered a speciality salad and sides of fried green tomatoes and mac and cheese. Salad was a pile of lettuce, overpriced at $9, fried green tomatoes were good, the other sides were mediocre at best. I thought perhaps my husband was at least enjoying some really great BBQ, but he reported that although the chicken was perfectly cooked, it lacked flavor, and the pork was nothing special.
We waited forty minutes in sweltering heat to get a table, and we had a reservation. There are great restaurants in Nashville, I can't imagine why anyone would choose to go here.

Wow. The biscuits were as amazing as all the previous reviewers stated. And I got a salad, which seems a sin at a great little cafe such as this... In my defense, my husband and I have been visiting Tennessee for almost a week and the good southern cooking is starting to give me more of a souvenir than I want. The salad was only so-so. The peanut butter pie I had afterwards made me have an audible "mmm" with each bite. The pie alone would warrant a plane ticket back to Nashville in a heart beat. Worth the wait. Worth the hype. The Loveless Cafe is wonderful.

Sunday evening @ 7. Very few patrons. We had a party of 6. 20 minute wait. I assume they were short servers. Our server was in a rush to get our order. They were out of fries, cheddarwurst. Sauerkraut was cold and tasty like the can was just opened. We are from an area with a Genuine Hoffbrau house. These people should stop pretending. Waiter explained nothing and obviously in a hurry to leave.

Cheap double shots that taste great, fantastic music and service! If you're visiting downtown Nashville for the first time like I was, this is a great starting point for Broadway night life. It's a quiet, small dive bar with a large variety of drinks and shots (particularly if you love fireball). Wish I'd found this place sooner in my Nashville journey!

Fantastic service. We went in on a slow night because there wasn't a show scheduled for the evening. We had a fantastic wine flight- Classic CW flight- and enjoyed their happy hour Margherita flatbread. 
The bartender and Sommelier were extremely personable and knowledgeable about wines. They were also very friendly and great conversationalists. Excellent experience.

Hey look, this was a great venue for a great band-- the psychedelic furs. The band played great, but their performance was squelched by the incompetent sound person. The bass was way too boomy, and the whole sound was a pile of mush! I don't want to be hypercritical, but this was the worst sound that I've heard at a concert since i played at my junior high. On a positive note, the hummus plate and the duck tacos were delightful!

Fried chicken OMG. Biscuit OMG. Definitely the best biscuits I have ever had and top 5 fried chicken. The biscuits were so warm and fluffy and add their homemade preservatives and you have biscuit heaven. The fried chicken was so good, the skin was crispy but not too oily. The meat wasn't dry, and it tasted really fresh. So good!

Absolutely off the charts.
Got the pulled pork plate.. With baked beans and slaw
Everything was awesome!!
The only thing that would've made it better was corona light.. Had to settle for bud light
Mmmmmmm biscuits.....and killer jams (blackberry is my favorite). A must stop for breakfast and cute gifts!!!
Wow!!! Most amazing biscuits ever! I got the country fried steak with fried green tomatoes, and it was the best I have ever had. Our waitress was the nicest person!
Waited an hour and a half only to sit out on the patio and be extremely hot. The saving grace was the hash brown casserole.
Best place to go to in Nashville!! The bartenders are awesome and they have great deals !!

One word: AMAZING. Outside of downtown Nashville but worth the trip. Everybody was super friendly and even though there was a 2 hr wait because of the 4th of July holiday, we were patient and it was worth the wait. Highly recommend it.

In regards to City Winery and their concert menu, it doesn't make sense that they have such a limited menu compared to their dining room. The cheapest wine is $8 for 5.5 oz. with tax it comes close to $10. That's ridiculous for such a small glass of wine. 

A friend and I tried the beet & bacon flatbread because we didn't have much money to spend. The combination of the cheese, beet, bacon, arugula, balsamic vinaigrette and some other ingredient just wasn't quite right and we weren't up for trying the mushroom and something other gross combination. 

The seats in the house aren't too bad, we were sitting in the back. Their sound guy had the instruments up louder than the vocals making it hard to hear the 2 bands that played. Their lighting was alright. 

The server at our table didn't show up very often and so we had to sit a while longer than we wanted to just to wait for the check. 

Also if you don't want to pay $20 cash for valet you have to park on the street and walk a while. 

Overall I think this is a great space for intimate shows, but I think it's outrageously overpriced when you're already paying a large amount for tickets. This place is obviously just trying to get every penny squeezed out of you.

Lives up to the hype! We happened to be in the area, starving and much to our surprise the food is as good as they say! The place was covered over but we were seated quickly and our food was delivered quickly. The meal was amazing and the portions were large and could have shared a plate. We will be back!

Just landed in Nashville and this was the first place I went. Entered the business and immediately felt the local vibe.  The menu was amazing and I decided to go with red velvet pancakes, eggs, bacon and potatoes.  Perfect breakfast! The velvet pancakes were like a piece of cake. Oh yes the biscuits were served as appetizers with jam and honey, a must.  The only reason this place is not a 5star is because the prices are a bit high for breakfast. Maybe I'm just cheap, this place is great!!!!!

Worth the drive. Made the mistake if eating 3 of those wonderful biscuits BEFORE breakfast and was stuffed afterwards. Great food! We had a 25 minute wait but there are other buildings/shops to look around in while you wait to be paged. Very homey place. It's like eating at home and being served by your mother.

Don't buy the hype. 
The wait is too long and it's nothing special. You can get the same experience and quality of food from Cracker Barrel. If the wait were less than an hour and a half and it wasn't outside town, then I'd say go for it.

What's not to love? If your a fried chicken and southern hospitality fan...this is the place for you. It gets a good crowd, but it's a big place and there is plenty of parking. The service is always welcoming, quick and pleasant. The food is plentiful and delicious. I am getting a hankering for some chicken just writing this review! It's a nice drive in the country to get to Loveless. Overall a pleasurable dining experience.

One word (that has been said a million times before): BISCUITS!! Worth coming here alone.

My chicken fried steak was fine...nothing amazing, but hit the spot. I also liked the biscuits and gravy that my sister ordered. Service was super friendly!

Didn't love the desserts weirdly enough. Expect a long wait, but there's lots of fun little shops on property that make the wait bearable.

I'll be back!

Two guys making out in front of the stage this weekend. Mikes reply when my wife brought it up was very put-offish. Something to the effect of, if you don't like it leave. Enough said Mike. We won't be back. Too bad, we've seen some good shows there over the years. But, there are many places in Nashville to see good original music without dealing with rude owners and the gay scene.

OMFG the biscuits. THE BISCUITS, PEOPLE! 

I went here for breakfast on Sunday with my husband and two of our friends. We arrived around 8am and there was already a wait. We only had to wait about 15 minutes for a table for 4, but we must have just barely beat the rush, because while we were waiting to be seated I overheard wait times of up to 45 minutes for other small groups.

Moral of the story, if you are going on a weekend: ARRIVE EARLY.

The first round was biscuits with homemade preserves. The strawberry and blackberry were the true standouts here; we all agreed the peach was just okay, if only because it is more mild in flavor. I could have only eaten biscuits and left a happy customer.

Honestly I ate so many biscuits that I couldn't finish my cinnamon raisin french toast and sausage. Our breakfast entrees were good, but again....THE BISCUITS.

Come here for the biscuits, maybe even take some to go. You won't be disappointed.

Had not heard of this place until they had a Groupon.  You don''t need one to get a great meal for a great deal.  The roasted broccoli and beet salad was great.  The turkey with blackberry aioli sandwiches are great.  The server was excellent. And they have valet parking that I'm a great fan of. We didn't go for a show or concert, just for lunch.  That's enough for me to go back again.

Food was great, However, we just had apps, cheese N meat plate with jalapeño & cheddar brat.  the atmosphere was off the hook, and great beer.... however, the service was a little slow, however they were slammed since it was the first weekend in OCTOBER, so i should have expected it.   Looking forward to my next visit to see an improvement!    I will let you know more.   PS. The beer flights were great!

I had no idea this was even a thing. I must admit when pulling in I felt like I arrived on the set of Bates Motel. Walked in at 2:10 in the afternoon and was told we had a hour and 20 minute wait!  I thought to myself, what is this place and why is is so busy! Then I found out they have been featured on the food network. Once we got in and ordered our food, it came out quickly. But before that we got biscuits and they were so good! The food was really good and worth the wait. If I'm in Nashville again and have the time, I'll definitely go back.
Had a flatbread and was really chewy and tough. My friend dishes didn't look good either (trout and steak)

It's all about the biscuits and the preserves. That's why you go, that's why you have to wait and that's why you'll say it was worth it. Make no mistake about it, there will be a wait. Dad and I waited almost 2 hours. We walked right in to the old house front and put our name on the list. She handed me a pager and off we went to check out the rest of the grounds. There are a few shops to browse through. One with Loveless Cafe souvenirs, from their cook books, jars of their preserves, to handy guitar shaped wooden cooking spoons. Lots of neat stuff in there. One with t-shirts, caps and more gift shop goodies. The barn on site is used as a venue for weddings, parties and music shows. If there's nothing scheduled, you may look around inside of it. There are several other boutique shops on the place to pass the time. The BBQ Pit is a screened in area that you can watch the staff prepare their pulled pork or smoked turkey. When Ya get tired of looking around, sit a spell and compare wait times with the other patrons and before you know it, your pager will buzz and light up! After ordering your drink, she'll bring you a plate of hot buttered biscuits with 3 preserves: Blackberry (with seeds), Strawberry and Peach. All three are absolutely delicious. The biscuits are melt in your mouth smooth. It don't get any better than this. Dad ordered the Pulled Pork and I got the County Ham. Now just so ya know, BREAKFAST is served ALL DAY. SUPPER menu is available from 11am to close. Our food was hot and very tasty. Did you know the front is the original house that the Loveless Couple originally sold Fried Chicken and Biscuits right out their Front Door? Look around when you come in. Can you find that Original Front Door? Enjoy!

There honestly isn't a bad thing I can say about this place. The wait was long - an hour and a half- but they combatted boredom with outdoor games, lemonade, shops to browse, and free snacks. The wait breezed by, and it was worth it. Once inside, our waiter was very friendly and attentive. The walls are decorated with thank you notes and signed portraits from Oprah to George Strait. Our biscuits were excellent and the preserves only made them better. All of my food was well seasoned and delicious - I had mashed potatoes, beans, greens and creamed corn. Everyone enjoyed their food and we plan on going back. Definitely stop if you are in Nashville.

BEST THING I ATE EVER.  My husband quoted on Facebook, "Lord, If I could eat any more, I would!"

This is a must do when visiting Nashville.  However, we need to pace ourselves better because we're always too full for dessert.

This new place is great. Wonderful staff and managers making sure your experience is superb. Wonderful food that is traditional and plenty of it. And the beers on tap are the exact selection a German joint should have. Can't beat four varieties of Hofbrau. Highly recommend making this a lunch or dinner stop soon!

The Basement is an intimate (code word for tiny) bar and music space below Grimey's records on 8th avenue. If you can't find a spot in the small dedicated parking lot, there is plenty of street parking in the residential neighborhood that surrounds it. One important thing to know about the Basement is they typically book two main acts a night. The good thing about this is if you're going to see the first act, you know the show will start and end on time. As the wife of a musician, this is big. It's a huge annoyance to think a band will start at 8 and they end up not starting till closer till 10 and before you know it, you're not leaving to come home till well after midnight. The bad thing about this two main acts a night is if you've come to see the first one and paid your cover, you'll have to leave and come back in, paying another cover for the second show. But, I also understand they want to pay the bands. There's not a lot of tables and chairs, so unless you're there super early, prepare to stand. Again, not a big deal as it's a small venue so there's really not a bad area to be.

I've been to City Winery twice now, once for a movie screening and once for a live show. The atmosphere is really cool. The food is good, though marginally overpriced. I'm no cheapskate, but when I compare the tab to the overall food/drink/service experience, the equilibrium feels off. I think this place has a lot of potential though, and I hope they continue to improve.

Everyone was hyping this place up so I figured I had to try it. I'm from Chicago so when my friends and I came down here for a roadtrip, we were staying in Vanderbilt. It took us about 30 min to drive there and the wait was an hour and 20 min. Not too bad because we got to walk around the cute stores they had and bought a few things.  I was looking forward to the biscuits but honestly they were just good. Not as amazing as I thought they were going to be, but just plain good. The strawberry and peach jam were my faves. I had the pulled pork and eggs. Not that great. The pulled pork didn't have any taste to it and they barely put any BBQ sauce on it. Would I order it again? No. I'm sure they had other good things on the menu but when I asked my friends what they thought about the food they said it was alright. 
I give it a four stars because they had cool little shops around, their food was okay, and the service was great. Our waiter took the time to explain everything on the menu, what was popular, etc.  I was definitely expecting some amazing southern BBQ breakfast and I mean if it wasn't for the service and stores I would of given them 3 stars. Overall, I tried it once and once is enough for me.

My coworker used Rocketown to host his wedding and reception. Before coming here, I was worrying if this place would have enough parking spaces for 300+ guests, considered its downtown location. The groom convinced us not to worry about parking and he was right. Parking was plenty for 300+ guests (don't leave any valuables in your car). Rocketown itself, was a large and spacious venue. I went to several weddings before in different venues and this one was probably the largest.

Since the Chinese/Vietnamese food in Nashville is below to average. My friend hired Happy Valley (chef and servers) from Atlanta to come down to serve the guests. I've never thought they would have a kitchen in here, but they did. All of the food came out fresh and steaming hot! The stage was spacious and great for playing live music (He hired singers too). The sound system was awesome. It was like watching a mini live concert. In addition, this place is well-kept and clean, even the restrooms were so clean (A++++). They had more than 5 rooms so we didn't have to wait in line. This was the first time I didn't have to wait in line to use the restroom at a wedding (I went in more than twice. Blame it on the alcohol!). 

My only complaint is the place was a bit too dark for a wedding. I'm not a fan of eating in the dark. It was hard to enjoy the food. I couldn't tell what dish they put on the table until I took a closer look. Also, most of the photos came out very dark (with flash!) like we were at a club. Other than that, I think this is a great place for hosting weddings and receptions. I would recommend Rocketown to friends and family for hosting big events.

2013/#69

Read about this cafe as one of the must things to do while in the vicinity. So I trusted the reviews and blogs and drove for about a half hour out of Nashville to find this place. I had been warned about wait times and being a Friday visit, I didn't want to take chances. Also the owner had just mentioned that they now take reservations in non-peak periods through OpenTable. So got a reservation and its a good thing I did, cause when I arrived, there were a lot of people waiting outside. For me, didn't wait long, about five minutes and I had a table, thanks to the reservation. So definitely consider making a reservation.
First impressions, its off a highway, and sort of like a small neighborhood with gift shops all around the restaurant. Its definitely popular, found a ton of people there.
When the server arrives, they get you a biscuit sampler, and three different kinds of jam. My favorite was the strawberry, but the biscuits were really wow, just delicious and so soft. Had to leave in a rush, so got the pancakes and left in a hurry, but the biscuits definitely make it worth driving over.

My original rating was a 2 star with the original post below.
However, I received an amazing email response from City Winery management. I had emailed them immediately after leaving the venue. 
The management addressed each one of my concerns with an honest, straight forward response, which is rare. They didn't make excuses. Instead, they thanked me for the feedback and detailed the steps they were taking to improve.

Wow!! We will definitely be going to another show there soon!
Way to go City Winery management! We love live music and wine so we want you guys to be a success!


Original post below:
City Winery Nashville has potential! The space itself is gorgeous and a great place to watch a favorite artist.

There are several areas that need improvement.
- Forced to use/pay for Valet parking, which was slow, unorganized, and unsafe. 
- Our waiter didn't even know how to open a bottle of wine nor possessed any wine presentation skills.
- The food was eatable, but nothing special. If I had it to do over, we'd have eaten somewhere else before the show.

Eh. If you haven't been you have to go. It is a tourist thing to do in Nashville. Overall it is overpriced for ok food. 
100% for tourists. 
Cute grounds though. Decent amount of things to do during the 2/3 hour wait for breakfast on the weekends.

Every time I travel to Nashville, I come eat at the Loveless Café.  It's a good atmosphere, the food is always good and I love the atmosphere.  I travel down the Natchez Trace Parkway often and I don't know which I like the best!  They're both at the top of my "good" list.

I enjoyed my time at the City Winery. The menu is limited, but nice. Also, the items are a bit pricey for dinner. However, there are more affordable items like the appetizers.
