We ordered the Margherita Flat Bread, and it was delicious! The portion size was large enough for a dinner portion. The parmesan truffle fries were yummy as well. I was disappointed to see they did not have sangria on the menu. However, when I told the bartender, she whipped me up something on the fly, and it was incredible!! They need to add it to the menu!!! The service was great. We also saw an improv show that evening, and it was a great time. I would love to go back for another show. It was a great venue and nice place for a date!

Worth the wait!  My fiance and I were in town for one night, and a Food Network junkie friend recommended the Loveless for breakfast.  We were warned ahead of time of the wait, so we were mentally prepared.  They have a great system using a pager that works all around the grounds, which include shaded benches, gift shops, coffee and sweet tea stations (complimentary).  We were pleased that our wait time was actually about half of the quoted time.

We were greeted by a very friendly and enthusiastic waitress named JD.  My fiance is from the Midwest and knows his way around a carb-laden breakfast menu.  The SoCal native in me doesn't know red-eye gravy from grits.  JD was more than happy to educate me.  With her advice, I decided upon everything "southern"; cheese grits, biscuits and sausage gravy, fried green tomatoes, and eggs and bacon.  

My review may not be truly qualified, as I have no basis for comparison of southern food, but, oh my, was it delicious!  It was a bit of a fluke for me to be in Nashville in the first place, and I will probably never return.  With that knowledge, I savored every bite, plus about five extra bites that I should have resisted. 

My fiance enjoyed his chicken fried steak, hash brown casserole, and plenty of warm biscuits.  

Make your way to the Loveless if you find yourself in Nashville.
Was excited to go here. It felt rushed,the food mass produced and bland and the seating was in really tight quarters. The service was friendly however. Go somewhere else

What can we say that hasn't been said?  This place is amazing and still serves up a true southern specialty of good food and hospitality.  The chicken is a must with its crispy tasty exterior.  The sides are home made and delicious and the biscuits are fluffy like pillows.  Stop in, order it to go and eat outside or in the car or take it home. You will be glad you did.

Biscuits, biscuits, biscuits! This was my first stop during a trip to Nashville due to many recommendations and we were not disappointed. I ordered the country ham with fried eggs and grits, which was great, but let's be honest, it's all about the biscuits here. I could eat 6 of those puppies with every meal. 

The only thing we didn't like was the location. It's far from the city center and took a long time to get an uber but we passed the time in the restaurant gift shop.

The best breakfast ever!!! We had the country fried steak and eggs with the hash brown casserole.  The steak was so amazing and fried perfectly and the hash brown casserole was Amazing.   The biscuits were the best biscuits ever served with their homemade preserves that were so good you had to use all three flavors. It was worth the drive while we were visiting in Nashville !

This place was great!!!! Friendly staff and if there is a wait, and I'm sure there will be, you can walk over to their market and gift shop to look around. 

Biscuits are served with every meal and they are yummy! I ate so many I barely had room for my meal. 

I had 3 sides as a meal and they were all very good. My husband had the smoked boneless pork chop and it was delicious. 

If you are in the Nashville area- you should stop here for sure!

Prepare to wait, then prepare for cholesterol city! 
If I were to return to loveless, which I hope to one day, I will prepare by starving myself for a day or two before hand just so I can enjoy all the delicious delicacies without the insane guilt. 
Yes there will be a wait but there are retail opportunities to bide the time and if the weather is tolerable, there is outdoor seating to enjoy while you wait. 
I had the catfish with creamed corn and Mac and cheese. There are so many sides, I would recommend your party orders a variety along you in order to sample all. Everything was delicious, no exceptions. Even the Bloody Mary! 
This is a must-try when visiting Nashville.

The best thing that we ate was the Ruben roll and that was even over fried!  My husband's beer he describes as creamy, but I don't like beer so I can't comment.  The bad of the meal:  everything else ... which includes the over cooked and under-salted smaller pretzel which the Manager wouldn't take off the bill after a few bites!  My Pork (as they don't offer veal) schnitzel was OK but was tough, dry but don't ask for extra gravy cause that's additional!!  The crispy-fried pork shank was just OK too, but barely ANY gravy with that either!  I tasted the pork shank and thought it was tastier than my schnitzel!  It is enough to feed 2 people I would say.

Other reviews of this place say negative things about the sides -- we agree!  The spaetzel, sour kraut and potato dumpling were not worth the time nor calories ... and of course, no gravy!  So I'll go there and say that the German place could be considered the gravy Nazis!  Sorry guys...

If we came back, and that's a BIG if, we'd just have the big pretzel, beer, and Ruben roll (requesting that it not be over cooked).

We decided to try Bavarian Bierhaus because of beer, brats, and beer cheese soup. We first saw this place in September while randomly going to Opry Mills but decided to go at a later time. That time was two weekends ago on a Sunday afternoon. 

We didn't wait long to be seated but for some reason, waited a really long time for service. Like, really long time. 15-20 minutes for someone to come by. We could only see one server and she wasn't coming anywhere near us. I finally flagged down the hostess and asked about our server. A couple of minutes later, she came by.

We decided to get a beer sampler and she explained to us what beers it came with and answered any questions we had about beers we were thinking of adding. I got the Bier Cheese soup and a plate with two different sausages and Chris got the schnitzel. 

While we waited for our food, there was a polka band that we enjoyed. I genuinely like polka music, so I was really digging them. They did some rock covers as well as played actual polka songs. I enjoyed them already but as I drank the beer (really good beer, by the way), I enjoyed them even more.

I haven't had Bier Cheese soup in years, and theirs was amazing. Of course the sausages were good. I was really digging everything: the polka, the beer, the food, the boyfriend. Speaking of Chris, he rather liked his schnitzel. 

As we were leaving, the hostess apologized to us for having to wait for our server. Honestly it only felt like a hiccup in an otherwise pleasant experience. I told her everything was amazing other than that.
Going the extra mile is what sets you apart. Thanks for letting us in and grabbing a drink half an hour before opening!!

When a hostess tells you it's going to be a 1 hour 45 minute wait for breakfast on a Thursday morning the normal reply is "no thank you" except for when your looking to sit and eat at a historical landmark like the Loveless Cafe. Well 90 minutes later we had our table and we hit the ground running with hot biscuits right out of the oven. Along with that came a potpourri of delicious jambs and sweet butter. We all had something different and each raved more than the other of how good the food was. 
Don't leave Nashville without putting this off the beat and path on your list.

This place gets 2 thumbs up in my book! I'm in Nashville for a Nutrition Conference and after a long day of learning, our group needed some delicious wine.  We stumbled in during happy hour which was legit--7 dollar glasses and 7 dollar apps.  Worked out great!  The wine was top notch and the apps were delish--especially the fried risotto balls (every dietitian deserves a treat!).

We hung out at the bar because there were not enough tables for us but after enjoying happy hour for over an hour, a table opened up and we enjoyed some more wine and apps.  

It is a little pricy but the quality of the wine and food, in addition to the cozy ambiance and wooden walls, would make me come back if I was local to Nashville.

Yup. Down-home cooking. We had a huge party and they accommodated us easily. Jason our server was friendly and professional. And my chicken was delicious! Cucumber salad was the absolute best - I recommend that to go w/the chicken. It is as good as others say!

The lunch started with biscuits and homemade jam. Great stuff. They told us the wait would be 1 hour and 15 minutes, it actually only took 45 minutes. While waiting we got a chance to explore the shops on the property. I had the smoked turkey breast with cranberry bbq sauce. Large portions low price. The wait staff was friendly and kept my ice tea filled. 

We had a good time..
Skip this is place!! The food was BLAND and the wait staff was less than friendly. There are so many other places to eat in the area - choose one of those!

The 3 stars is more so for the amazing show we enjoyed last week. The winery is beautiful but sadly I wasn't impressed with much else. I've heard so many great things about the food/chef and having eaten before the show, we decided to grab an appetizer, The Salt n Vinegar Frites. Upon placing the order, they came out faster than our drink orders. To some, this would be great. To foodies/food bloggers, this only can mean one thing. This was not made to order. The fries were seasoned to perfection with a less than accommodating side of another perfect garlic aioli. But they were cold. This baffled us. There could not have been more than 150 people at the show and upon glancing around to see if others had ordered food, I did not see a food order within the surrounding tables. There's actually preparation that goes into complete dishes with components. We only ordered the fries.... and they could not be made to order? In efforts to not disrupt the show, for our sake and others, we ate our fries that probably would have been the best fries we ever had, had they been prepared properly. Upon entering the restroom at a later time, I noticed a white table napkin on the floor of an occupied stall. That white table napkin was then picked up by a server from the floor, placed on the sink while she washed her hands and then taken with her when she exited the bathroom. I didn't want to even imagine....I think between the two, this was enough for me not to return. Sadly.

We visited 6/29 around 11 am, we thought we were hitting it early and during the week but when we checked in it was an hour wait, we had come specifically to have lunch so we waited. There are some small gift shops, a postal shop to ship goodies home and a local artist shop with something for everyone. They also had some corn hole games set up around the area as well as picnic benches so that did kill some time but not a full hour. When we were being seated the wait was up to 1 1/2 hour wait!!! So be prepared for the wait! Once seated we were approached immediately and given a plate of fresh homemade biscuits and preserves, quite genius way to stave of the hangry's! My husband ordered the biscuit sampler, they had many choices, he went with bacon, sausage, pulled pork and fried chicken, he thought they were all great but the pork and chicken were his favorite! He also wasn't able to finish as the portion was large. I ordered the catfish dinner with okra and hash browns and can't brag enough, the catfish was probably the best I have ever had and I am a southern girl who has had some catfish! I ate every bit and it was a large portion, it was so light and crispy, not greasy at all. The sides were delicious. We would definitely go back, I would order the same thing too! The food was definitely a 5 but the wait really is a consideration. Definitely a tourist favorite but you will see the locals for sure!!!

This is a really fun restaurant! My Fiancée and I stopped here a few weeks ago while at the mall and we were very pleasantly surprised with our meal overall. The staff was attentive and our food and drinks were brought out promptly. The drink selection is good and they have a variety of German brews and wines. The menu is what you'd expect from a German restaurant and the pretzels, sausages, and schnitzel were very, very good and quite filling. It was a great meal overall and it will be our go-to if we ever want German food!

I went to Loveless Cafe around lunch time for breakfast. The wait was initially forty-five minutes, however, since we were coming from Chicago that was no big deal. We decided to wait and peruse the gift shops that were filled with delicacies and kind of  pricey apparel. We were buzzed back into the restaurant before the estimated time. It is very chilly inside so make sure you bring a sweater! The menu was simple and easy to navigate; I ordered the biscuit sampler since they are known for those. The platter came with biscuits that were shared with the rest of my table as an appetizer. A sweet and decadent plate of blackberry, peach, and strawberry preserves... as well as honey (which you can ask for). The biscuits were scrumptious to say the least and my favorite was the strawberry preserve, but all of them were tasty! The coffee accompanying my meal of my choice of the 4 biscuits (fried chicken, green tomato and cheese, and steak) and grits. The grits were the best I have ever had. I added honey and butter even though it came perfectly flavored already. Out of all of biscuits, chicken was my  favorite because of the moist and crispy texture that complimented the warm soft biscuit. All together five stars for the great service even though it was a long wait, the enviroment is very southern inspired and the story sheet they give you provides a great back story. Very great experience, do not forget to take a picture with the sign!!

Great atmosphere and vibe.  Plentiful wine list (among the deepest in Nashville) with many reasonable choices.  Have been a couple times now and while the menu is limited, there are some stellar items on there including the Napa cabbage salad and burger.  Staff has been friendly and knowledgeable thus far.  Have been to one concert and looking forward to going back.

This place must be some institution because you wait like an hour and half, there must be something going on. Luckily they got multiple shops on the property, but it'll only last you so long. Then they offer complimentary lemonade and water out front, while they got some guys playing music. I guess that'll pass the time while I wait.

I heard from some others that normally wait isn't that long, no more than 30 minutes. But I guess this is what happens when you go on a long weekend.

The service is really nice. Though the guys must be running all over the place as their a bit sweaty. The food was decent, good home style southern food.

Best part, get the Lynchburg lemonade with souvenir mini mason jar. You get a good Tennessee drink with a souvenir!

Fun experience. Expect to wait ~ it's always busy ~ but worth the wait. The food was very heavy but very good! I enjoy the a la carte breakfast menu options. The bloody mary with a moonshine sidecar was awesome! The little shops are nothing to brag about and the service was slow but it was a fun experience nonetheless. Just be patient!

Went to Franklin and Nashville to visit family.  The first morning, they took us to the Loveless Cafe.  The food was great and the portions were HUGE.  They are famous for their biscuits and, of course, the gravy.  I had pork chops and eggs.  It came with biscuits and gravy, and it also came with their hash brown casserole.  Everything was delicious.  I would say you must go here if you are in the area.  You won't be disappointed.

For once DD&D had it right on!  The chicken is awesome, the biscuits like none I have ever had before, and the fried green tomatoes divine.  

The only caution I would have is to get the EARLY.  We got there around 1pm and had to wait an hour for a table but it was well worth the wait.  Wouldn't mind going back to try the bbq some time.

Absolutely hands down best home cooking/soul food whatever you prefer in the greater Nashville area. The chicken and biscuits is what they're known for but everything is awesome. And that's really all anyone could ever say about this place...awesome

I love this place. I've been here a few times and it's really quite delicious.  It's tasty comfort food with the best biscuits ever.  Typically, there is always a wait so be prepared.  The vibe is country comfort and the food represents that.  Today, I had the fried
Chicken and some pork chops with peach jam-mashed potatoes and Mac and cheese.  The crispy skin on the chicken and the moist tender inside was simply delicious. I forgot to take pictures because we were so hungry and the food smelled so great.  If you find yourself in Nashville and looking for good comfort food, come to the Loveless.......the biscuits, try and eat just one!

I was so excited to try this place, but now I wish I hadn't.

The good: 
- our table was ready at our reserved time

The bad:

- Server was not knowledgeable on the wines, which seemed strange since winery is in the name.

- Everyone at the table ordered wine flights and they came all jumbled up, the server was trying to figure out what was what by sight and hand them out that way. Some of them were not as described, i.e. a red instead of a white. The wines tasted fine, but no one had any idea what they were drinking or if it was what they ordered.

- Food tasted fine other than the steak was way overcooked. It was not a cut I had heard of before, and was not something I would describe as a steak. The cauliflower puree that came with the steak was the best thing I ate while there. We tried the charcuterie as well as the cheese board, both were fine. The baked ricotta appetizer came out with ONE slice of bread. Not sure how you would share that. I do feel like the menu is overpriced for what you get.

- When clearing the table the server dropped a dirty knife into my friend's purse. I understand accidents happen but after everything else come on!

- After several rounds of incorrect checks, we were ready to get out of there but one person's credit card just didn't come back to the table with her check and had to be hunted down.

- I thought it was strange that no one asked how everything was, and we never saw a manager checking in with tables. We would have liked to tell them about our experience.

I wish I had read the other reviews before trying it. Save your money and go somewhere else. Anywhere else.

I cannot say enough good things about this place...the food and the service are amazing!!!  The pancakes and biscuits are out of this world!  Their biscuits are as close to my grandmother's homemade biscuits as I've ever had anywhere.  The pancakes have an amazing smell and are so filling you can't eat them all.  The homemade jelly is so good too.  The pace is always busy.  If you go on a weekend, go early because the wait will be over an hour.  When I went during the week there wasn't a wait for breakfast.  The shops where they sell some of their jelly, bacon, pancake and biscuit mixes is great!  They have some unique items and a catalog for mail order.  Definitely a place you must try!
Overrated. Great biscuits and ambiance but slow service and waaayyyy too noisy and a long wait always. Prices higher than expected. Not too impressed.
This would have to be one of my favorite restaurants. The food is fresh and good. The atmosphere is great. I would definitely recommend this place.

Good: 
A beautiful space, located in an up-and-coming area you wouldn't have wanted to visit 3 years ago. You walk in and immediately feel at home. The whole club, from bar area to bathrooms to the showroom, is intimate without being cloying. 
It fills a huge gap in this city, which has needed an upscale club inbetween tiny 75-100 seaters (eg Bluebird Café) and larger halls (Ryman). 
Very clean, great bathrooms, nice bar area. Lots and lots of wood.
They're making their own wine next year, and the gigantic barrels are eye candy if you like good vino. The wine lists (there are 2) are comprehensive. Some very reasonably priced , but that's because they charge YOU the liquor tax. Be forewarned.
Food is better than expected. Risotto balls, recommended by our waitress, were excellent (though I'd go for spicier mustard). Pork tacos ditto. The steak was two lovely pieces of meat - though the chef has a heavy salt hand. (Maybe they're salting and letting it sit to tenderize? Still, it shouldn't be that salty.) I don't recommend the mussels, and the cheese tray is absurdly small for what you pay, but the ravioli was gorgeous. The burgers are very good, and there's a vegetarian option too.
I'd recommend the meze platter, except that we had it our first visit (opening night) and it was large enough for four. Last visit it had shrunk considerably. 

The bad: 
Five dollar parking charge? Really? The attendants make it clear that your $5 goes to the venue, so you're expected to tip on top of it. But there's NO street parking!!
Getting seated is a work in progress. I've been here 5 times so far, alone, with family, with business associates. Each time, we arrived at 6 pm, when they opened. Each time, wait staff weren't ready. Each time, there's a meaningless cluster of hosts and hostesses? standing by the entry doors, doing anything but paying attention to the customers. Each time we were sent to the "concierge" for tickets and information. Forgive my being snotty about it, but how many City Winery employees does it take to seat someone? If it happened once, all right. But every time? 
Food service is slooooow. Don't come hungry. I don't know if the wait staff are over-loaded or what, but when you go out for an expensive evening like this, you expect better service. My waitrons have all been nice, but far from the kind of competency I experienced at the NY or Chicago clubs.
Food is expensive for what you get. (Online menu prices changed?) Our party of four had a bottle of inexpensive wine, 3 Tito's vodkas, and two beers, plus mains and 2 appetizers) was $310 before tip. I think that's expensive. Portions aren't big enough for leftovers. If this were The Palm, I'd expect it, and I'd be satisfied knowing the quality would be wonderful AND I'd have enough for another meal next day. 
The wait staff are friendly, but scattered. Ask for salt and pepper. Ask again. And again. Finally ask a bus boy, who brings it eventually. My wife's burger arrived with fries, everything looked great, but by the time salt and ketchup arrived everything was cold. This is not unusual here, but I can no longer excuse it as growing pains.
And they don't pay the liquor tax?!?! This is the only restaurant in Nashville charging the customers for it - even Kayne Prime, home of 50 cent charge per blue cheese olive in your drink, doesn't charge liquor tax. Really, between food prices and liquor tax, I would not suggest eating here.

The ugly:
Sound problems. It carooms off the back wall so you can't hear vocals at all if there's a band - of the 3 we've seen, this was a problem with all of them. It's all right for an acoustic act like Taj Mahal, but something needs to be done. Who opens a club in Nashville without consulting a sound engineer? Everyone in my party, each time, was disappointed in the sound quality.
Seating is, to put it bluntly, horrendous. At first glance, it's very pretty - until you realize that a) no matter where you sit, you're not facing the stage, and b) chairs are tiny, and tables are about a foot shy of the standard 2 or 4 seat table length. What this means is that no matter how much you pay, or what you reserve, you're going to be miserably uncomfortable. My wife is petite, our daughter is likewise, but even they complained that they couldn't eat without elbowing one another. 
The sideways-only seating means you don't get to enjoy the show the way you would with concert-style. I understand you can't do the concert-style and serve dinners, but I'd love to see this place change up so half the table is facing the stage. The other half could just turn their chairs around for the show. As it is, no one was happy with the seats.

All in all, I will continue to attend when I'm in town, because they're bringing in a lot of acts you wouldn't normally see in Nashville. But I'll dine elsewhere. And I'll try to get validated, even if I'm not a "vinofile" (because I resent paying $75 a year for what I would get), and I'll avoid ordering liquor.

Got there at the end of the night which was a bonus becaise we didn't have to wait long. Service and food was good. Biscuits were so delicious. Had breakfast for dinner ham amd eggs with redeye gravy. Noce place worth a trip.
This place is amazing. Owen was probably the best waiter I have ever had and really made you feel at home. The food is affordable and absolutely delicious!!

The biscuits are melt in your mouth good! For breakfast I had the southern sampler and the country ham was really good. The hash down casserole was yummy as well. Service was incredible and really fast! Loved it.

I should have known better....huge restaurant in tourist area.....red flags I ignored. Four of us ate there for Valentines Day.  One of four entrees was acceptable. Other food.....dry, no flavor. My Reuben had virtually no sauerkraut, and the meat was dry, tough and stringy! Looked like it had gone into the oven and left far too long. Go careful when considering this place for a meal. Settle for Black Forest cake and have your meal elsewhere.

UPDATE:  The on line customer service associate followed up immediately after my above review was posted and asked me to contact the restaurant's GM.  I did so today. He is DEFINITELY interested in providing a quality dining experience and was disappointed to hear about my experience. I'll now gladly give them a second chance.

This past Saturday 22 of my friends and I went to the Bavarian Bierhause for dinner, beer, and dancing to an oom pa band.

It turned out to be an overall terrible evening all the way round.  Service:  Terrible - 30 minute wait to get the first beer - it took 45 minutes and  two servers with two different orders to get more beer.  To add insult to injury it took an hour to get a check
  The server had to go around and ask each person what they had! Then she processed each check one at a time some people waited almost another hour to pay!!!

Food some sausages over cooked and even burnt.  Some fish raw on the inside.  Many mixed up orders.  People would say this is not what I ordered.  Waitress would reply "this is what they made you".  You won't eat it????

Atmosphere way way way too much back around noise.  You could bafely  talk to the person next to you and no one else. 

Entertainment:  Band played some German songs them mostly US pop oldies.  Sound mixing was terrible band sounded very bad. 

Over all the evening was over the top bad.  22 people  have said we will never  go there again.
Alex Stillwell

Not good for a new restaurant in Nashville where people have high expectatioms at new venues!!

What it is:  A Munich Brew/Beer Hall in the U.S.  It is loud.  It is community seating (tables for 8-10)  Yes-you may be seated with someone you don't know.  No-you can't have a table made for 8-10 for you and your date.  Did I mention loud?  You go there for the atmosphere, to talk with friends and family, to laugh, sing, and drink beer and eat.  It's a place to hang out for a long time and enjoy the experience.
What it isn't:  A place for a quiet romantic dinner.  A place where the food is quickly prepared and served so you can eat and leave and they can turn over the table.  It's not a place to grab a quick bite on your way to the movie.
Seriously the food was great.  Enjoyed the Rouladen with red cabbage and sourkraut.  Sometimes rouladen are prepared differently in different regions.  I prefer mine with cubed bacon inside.  These seemed to be wrapped around a pickle and a carrot slice.  But very good.  Served warm-could have been hotter, temperature wise.  The Jagerschnitzel was good.  Now, wienerschnitzel is a breaded and fried pork or veal cutlet.  I remember Jagerschnitzel being fried without the breaded coating, then the mushroom gravy.  This seemed to be a wienerschnitzel with the mushroom gravy.  The beers were great!  
The band was tolerable.  I'm hoping they'll eventually find a "real" German band and have a long-term contract.  This evening was a guy with an accordion, a guy playing sax, and one on drums.  Some German drinking songs.  But-even Queen and Rammstein played on the accordion isn't German music. 
A flight of beer, a radler, a .5 liter beer, 3 entrees=$110 with tip. Opry Mills rent has it price. 
I will go back.

I visited Loveless with my mom on a trip to Nashville recently. The location and spot itself is so cute and fun. They've got a property with a lot to look at when you wait for your table. The staff is nice as can be and the atmosphere is great. 

The food itself was good. They have their own brand of biscuits, which are piping hot and pretty tasty, although there are better biscuits to be found in Nashville. We had the fried chicken and a BLT and were both pleased with our meals.

Let me tell you a little story about Loveless Cafe, y'all. A friend and I decided to ride our bikes there one day from West End. 13 miles. Bad Idea. 5 hours later when we got there, waited an hour for our table, and the biscuits finally came, they literally saved my life. I owe those biscuits MY LIFE, I tell you. If you are gonna do Loveless, just forget about the calories and order the Fried Chicken with all the fixins (or you could burn it off with a bike ride- but seriously--dont.). Also, try your darndest to save room for Steeplechase pie. To Die For. The wait can be long, so go at a weird time and you should be ok. Otherwise plan on waiting at least an hour. Luckily there are little shops in the same complex to keep you busy. Recently, I went to the Loveless Barn on the property for music city roots. If you have not done this, you need to go as soon as humanly possible or, move away from Nashville . k thanks. bye.

If you want great food and service, in a quiet and peaceful place this is worth the trip. After spending Friday and Friday night in the Broadway area, Sat night demanded us to be somewhere more quiet and less smelly. :-) City Winery had first class service, they were all so nice and attentive. The atmosphere was wonderful, calm, intimate. Food was unique and flavor amazing. It's worth the trip, don't miss.

Would of given 5 stars if they wouldn't of forgetten my preserves with my biscuits in my to go order. Being as the preserves are a staple I can't give 5 stars without trying with my biscuits! We're from Texas so I don't know if we'll ever eat here again. Hopefully so we can give them a try

Always always always a superior meal. Staff there, including the managers that assist the staff in serving, the wait help, the store cashiers and attendants, everyone is helpful, happy, and engaging.  I've had the fried chicken, so far can't be beat, the chicken fried steak, always juicy and tasty, the biscuits are so good...jam, awesome, cooks nail the eggs the way you order them. Give the Kitchen the Kudos for always great flavor, fresh ingredients and how when it arrives!
Biscuits best I ever had. Pulled pork was tender however pork chops dry fried chicken very good. people were so nice and the peach jam WOW.

We really enjoyed the setting and the "to do" surrounding this place, including the remote location and the campus like setting. We had to wait about 40 minutes, at around 11am on a Thursday, which wasn't a big deal. 

While the food was tasty, it was overall pretty underwhelming. Good, but not great. I would have given it 4 stars if it wasn't for our server. She wanted to take our order right away and rolled her eyes when we asked for more time with the menu. Then the fried green tomatoes that I ordered to go with my eggs never arrived, so I inquired about them and she went to fetch them. 10 minutes went by, by which time my eggs were cold, and eventually she dropped them off with a "here you go". A simple "sorry about that" would have been plenty, but the southern hospitality was somewhere else today. Otherwise, we enjoyed our time at the Lovelace and would likely visit again in the future.
German beer,brats,bar at the mall. Overall food and atmosphere is good,great place to hang out while others are shopping.

This place was awesome. The service was absolutely wonderful. Our waiter had a sense of humor and made sure we were taken care of. (I wish I could remember his name!) Even in the outfitters shop, the girl was super sweet and helpful. The biscuits were heavenly!!! I ordered the country fried steak (which was as big as my face, no joke!) And fried okra and mac and cheese. Everything tasted perfect and that mac and cheese is so creamy! My husband ordered the meatloaf and was probably the best meatloaf I've ever tasted. For dessert, I got the fudge pie. It's served chilled, which in my opinion, makes it taste better. The whipped topping is so thick but not too sweet and it pairs well with the sweet fudge underneath, best chocolate pie ever!! I would definitely go back!

We have been to City Winery three times, each time for dinner and a concert. The food is fine. The service is fine. The building is fantastic, although directly beside the homeless shelter. It's nice they have valet service. The sound is fine.

Here's my problem...We saw Robert Earl Keen and he was introduced as "Robert Keen Earl." Last night we saw Mac McAnally, 7 time winner of Musician of the Year award, and he was introduced as "Mac McNally." City Winery is getting great acts and there are more shows I look forward to. I wonder how may times they can insult the artists and keep the talent coming.

Chris Knight is playing the venue soon. Please be aware the K is silent.
Nothing to say. Everything is fantastic. Don't think you'll like chicken and waffles. Try and be amazed

This is a must if you are in Nashville area. The wait will be long but do yourself a favor and wait. There is the smokehouse to spend time in and the gift shop. So unique and a treasure. 
The food is amazing too

For breakfast, the biscuits and blackberry jam are superior.  For lunch, the fried chicken is exceptional.  Everything else that I have tried is great.  Add to the great food the amazing history, the iconic location and the associated store nearby, and you've got an excellent eating experience.  To me, it's a "must try" for anyone visiting Nashville.

I loved this place!  The food was great and the staff are welcoming!  We happened upon live music night which was very entertaining.  The gift shop is small and reasonably priced. 
Highly recommend!

Wonderful service and wonderful food.  Worth the extra drive if you are in town. Prices are pretty reasonable when you factor in the amenities.  Beautiful drive on the way!  The manager came out immediately to great us and help with food allergies.  The bbq omelet was perfect!  Enjoy!  Easy 5-stars!

Where in the world can I begin to write a review? I guess it has to be the biscuits-tender, flaky, fresh as fresh can be, right out of the oven, popped into my mouth before I even have a chance to smear on the strawberry, peach, or blackberry preserves. All you want-all day long. But save a little room for a delicious breakfast. You name it they'll make it. Today I'll just stick to some savory Southern Country Ham and some sunny-side eggs, of course with creamy, cheesy stone-ground grits. Mmmm. But wait. Can't decide; how about a sampler? Or if you brought friends and family...they got you covered--Family Style Breakfast includes sausage gravy too. And be sure to try the Hashbrown Casserole or maybe the BBQ omelet. Oh, you're here for lunch? Fried chicken, meatloaf (better than Mom's...sorry Mom), and finger lickin' good Pork Chops. So much good stuff, I never have room for dessert...but you might, and they got it too. Try some pie and make a note to come on back, y'all.
A must when in Nashville! Great food and service!!! Highly recommend.  We times it just right and was seated with out a wait.

The people who work here are amazing, the food is incredible. I'm from Nashville I typically hate going to touristy locations ,but for this amazing food I'll go any day. The sides are my favorite part, but they also make a mean Beef Brisket and Hot Chicken.

I'm not even done eating and I'm giving it five stars. This place has the whole package. Take note restaurant owners, it has an original and consistent theme, it's clean, the waitstaff is super friendly and pleased to help you. The fried chicken is up there with the best. Were the biscuits the best I've ever had? No but they weren't bad and they'll give you as many as you want and with awesome homemade preserves. I've had better Mac and cheese but it's still really good. For the price, this is as good as it gets. I'm waiting for pecan pie right now but I'm confident that they won't fuck that up.............and they didn't. Win!!!!

Food was delicious! My husband ordered the country fried steak and it was massive! The biscuits are definitely the best biscuits we've ever had. Such a cute little place with shops around back. We bought the biscuits mix to make at home, doubt they'll come out as good but it'll serve its nostalgic purpose. Wish we could have gone again before we left but couldn't make it back. You have to go to Loveless when you're in Nashville.

Worth the drive!
It is absolutely worth the hype! 
Their fried chicken, catfish and dumplin's keep me crawling back for more and their biscuits!!!!

It's a Nashville must have! You will never eat at a CB again. The prices are great too for such an amazing meal. 

Yes, go and you will thank me. Seriously.

Everything was amazing!!! The service, food and ambiance was perfection!! Catfish was not to be believed!! Our service was some of the best I've ever had!! Biscuits and jam of course were the best I have ever had and they are free!! You must go here for best southern comfort food in a laid back atmosphere:)

This place has GREAT potential. Authentic beer and food. Staff seems well trained. Performers are very talented... they do modern hits and classic hits with a German style. BUT! THE VOLUME WAS ABSOLUTELY OBNOXIOUS. I COULDN'T EVEN THINK MUCH LESS ENJOY THE COMPANY OF THE PEOPLE I WAS WITH. THE ACOUSTICS OF THE MAIN  AREA DO NOT WORK FOR SUCH LEVELS. ESPECIALLY THE DRUMMING (the all caps reflects how I felt the whole time). Honestly only posting this to help the staff and the business because they're right on track to be amazing! My party of 14 was very close to leaving and not ordering food because of the sound levels alone. Turning it down will prevent this.

I've eaten here since 1996 wouldn't give it 5 stars due to the popularity of the restaurant and the wait times most encounter, food is pretty good but very overhyped. A must try for non-veterans but go on a weekday.

True southern hospitality and great southern food! We stopped by for a late lunch/early dinner. Our server, Robin, gave great recommendations and excellent service. Amazing biscuits! The best ever. Served with strawberry, peach & blackberry jam. My fried chicken was crispy, perfectly seasoned. Delicious sweet creamed corn. GREAT hash brown casserole. I highly recommend.

The Loveless Cafe has a nice concept for a restaurant, neat way to turn a motel into something else.  Came here on an afternoon so no wait for us, sat on a side patio, our waitress was slow and didn't really seem to want to be there.  We each got a drink with a sidecar shot in a souvenir mason jar.  I got the Harvest Moon with moonshine excellent and we also got a strawberry lemonade one too, good as well.  The biscuits with jelly were good, liked the different flavors of jelly.   We then tried a ham on a biscuit basic but good.  The best thing we had was the chicken and waffles, chicken was moist but crispy and the waffle was fluffy and crisp, a must try if you come here.  One of the best experiences was a group of southern women sat next to us and it was a riot listening to them, great people.  They have some nice souvenir shops in the rooms around the restaurant.  Overall it was a pretty cool place.
Our first time and everything was Fabulous!! The best food. You can't go wrong here no matter what you order. We will be back! A Nashville landmark and gem

This place is massive and has a very fun atmosphere. We shared a platter that included a porkchop (which basically tasted like ham), a roast beef with gravy, one of their sausages, red cabbage, sauerkraut, and mashed potatoes. Everything was tasty and had a unique flavor to their seasonings.

Service was really good here tonight. It's the first time we stopped in here. They have a live polka band and had I thought about it, I would've requested to be seated away from it because it was so loud we were trying to scream at each other so it really put a damper on any kind of conversation. I ordered the Reuben  and it was decent. Not the best, but still good, my husband was really excited about the beer!

Been a few times and always loved it. Went shortly before Christmas for dinner and we were not happy with our dinner. Even messaged them on FB about it and no response. We had 2 Jägers and they were not like the times before. Overcooked and the gravy was not right. We will come back and hope the food will be better. Glad we have a German restaurant in Nashville now.

Really fun casual German beer hall. It's connected to the mall, but it boasts more of a touristy feel rather than a quick "dine and dash" mall spot. 

Unfortunately I was here for a work lunch and didn't get to sample any beers, BUT I highly recommend the reuben sandwhich. The marble rye and sauerkraut were good (a little strong but good), and the corned beef was nice and salty. 

Clearly a spot for good heavy German food. You can tell this place must get packed. It had rows and rows of bench style seating. Not the most comfortable, but hey, it's a beer hall.

We were totally unable to book online for an upcoming show. Then, show was sold out and still it was impossible to be placed on a wait list because of problems booking online----we even tried to set up a new account which rejected us and stated, "invalid password ". So, tried calling the venue to see if we could be placed on a wait list. No---not possible---can only be done online. Seriously? We won't bother w/this venue again.

Unexpected disappointment!! We came in a big group so we were placed in a separate room with 2 long dining tables away from the restaurant. The air conditioning was on very cold and there was no ambiance. No greetings when we entered. The food had been pre-ordered. Not what we thought it would be. The meat was very dry. Couldn't tell the difference between pork and turkey. Sweet potatoes looked and tasted canned. The biscuits and green beans were the best. But overall sad to have this represent Nashville or Southern cooking. You've lost the spirit of why you became famous!

The experience was definitely European. The service was outstanding and the food was excellent. An excellent choice of German beers both on top and a bottled. A great place together with family for a good meal or friends for a Saturday football game.
Best biscuits and fried chicken I've had in my life. There should be no contemplation about this place; just go!

I love the loveless café. A lot. My only complaint (and I probably wouldn't even call it that) is that their Hot Chicken is only available on Friday. :( Their hot chicken is the best around....and I would know...I am kinda a hot chicken snob. lol Seriously though...it is UH-MAZING.

Beautiful venue! The food was amazing and the service impeccable. Daryl and Mark went out of their way to make us feel welcome and answer any questions we had. The wine flight had four selections of wine that were all very good. We climbed the curved staircase to see the beautiful outdoor decks and seating area upstairs.
We made a reservation for brunch on Sunday, July 16, and it was a slow day so we pretty much had the place to ourselves! Highly recommend the eggs Benedict, the roast beef calzone with au jus, and the BLT. All were absolutely delicious and good portion sizes. Our appetizer was recommended and didn't disappoint. The food is high quality as is the service and the restaurant/venue itself is beautiful!
Good drinks, good music. Double Shotz are $5. I was hoping for munchies to snack on, but the only food is Jello Shotz. Smoking is allowed, but it didn't get too smokey. Overall, not bad.

This place is amazing! I highly recommend everyone to go and see this place and have a meal. While you may have to wait, it worth very second of your time. The staff are so friendly and accommodating. The food is out of this world! The hash brown casserole is to die for.

When I die I want to be buried under the foundation of Loveless Cafe. I've been to Nashville probably 10 times over the years and I finally tried this place with my friend on a Thursday morning around 11a. There was no wait. I strongly recommend you go on a week day so you can get in quick. The staff were extremely friendly and the restaurant itself has that Southern home charm so you feel like you're eating at someone's home. They are known for their biscuits and if you order a plate or platter you get biscuits with it automatically. The biscuits are very good. I would say 4/5. They have a crunchy texture on the bottom and are soft and fluffy on the inside. Our waitress guided us to get the pulled pork and eggs which was the best of both breakfast and BBQ. The pulled pork is hands down the best I've had in Nashville. Their BBQ sauce is also really tasty and has that tangy vinegar undertone I love in my sauce. The portion sizes are HUGE! You can get at least 2 meals out of it. The coffee was delicious and they came around often to fill up our cups. My friend got the hash brown casserole as her side and I got the cheesy grits. The grits are the best I have ever had anywhere! You have to get the grits! Long story short, I love this place and didn't want to leave. It's a must experience if you're in the area.

Not a bad place. I can't complain since we only have two German restaurants in Nashville that I know of.

Stopped here after shopping. If you're at the mall, it is almost impossible to find this restaurant because you literally have to walk through an exit door. Once you're inside tho, this place is huge!

Food was decent. We only had their wurst when we ate here. They don't let you substitute your sides so FYI- you're stuck with your fries.

Kitchen was a bit slow for a not so busy place. Our server was nice tho.

I'd like to come back and try their main dishes next time. They have plenty of beer choices of course.

Holy biscuits! It's been a few weeks since our last visit and I am constantly craving their biscuits-so good! There's really just no place like Loveless. The staff feels like family and you never feel rushed. Take some time to walk around after you eat-the shops are all lovely.

We went around 10am on a weekday and the wait was 40 minutes. The biscuits and jam were delicious. However the rest of our food was not great. Def not worth a long wait. We got chicken & waffles, waffles, eggs & bacon and pancakes. The atmosphere was fun and the gift shops had a lot of cute things. Guess it is more of an experience place but don't think we would go back.

OK 511 reviews let me throw mine in there!

It is good great country ham, went on a Monday morning 8am so no wait.  would I wait for breakfast?

Can't go wrong though for breakfast.

When I have guests visiting from out of town, without fail the one place I always end up taking people is the Loveless Cafe. The wait was only for 45 minutes for two people on Saturday night around 6:30pm and it was well worth it. During the wait you can explore the stores and play corn hole in the various locations around the premises. 

Once we got inside, Sandy our server as busy as she was brought out our biscuits and brought us our Sweet Tea. I LOVE Loveless biscuits. I don't know how to describe it or explain it but the biscuits and their jams. Ugh. To die for. 

My friend and I chose to share the sampler and I'm so glad we did. We got the fried chicken, fried catfish, and the pork barbeque with Mac and cheese, creamed corn, and fried okra. I have never had fried okra or okra til I moved to the south but loveless has given me the best experience with okra. And the fried chicken was simply perfect, as was the catfish and of course the pork. 

Everything about our meal was delicious and I am never disappointed when visiting Loveless. Although the wait to get inside is extremely long, the staff is rather good about getting your food orders and your food out to you as soon as possible. 

Always a favorite restaurant of mine and always highly recommended to all Nashville visitors even if it's only for the biscuits.

We checked out this place while on vacation in Nashville and it was worth the trek. It is a bit off the beaten path of downtown Nashville, but the drive is somewhat scenic and was enjoyable. Upon getting seated, our server brought us two platefuls of biscuits and jams - and when I says platefuls, I mean stacked up in 5s and we immediately started stuffing our faces. They were so good. 

I ordered the pit cooked pork bbq plate and my husband got the fried pork chop plate. They came out and my jaw dropped, they were so big it was enough to feed me for lunch and dinner (possibly breakfast the next day too!). I thought the bbq pork was good, not the best I had during this trip however. My husbands fried pork chop however was so good. I could have eaten that all day long. 

They also had cute little shops to make this more of a destination to check out rather than just the restaurant - which after how much we ate, we needed the walk. I definitely enjoyed those biscuits and think this was worth the drive.

Absolutely beautiful ambiance. The food however is a different story. The performance was nearly over before we received our food. My husband ordered a pizza. We also ordered the truffle fries and a Kale Caesar salad. The salad was delicious until I pulled a long, stringy red hair from the salad. At that point, I was done! The venue is beautiful but the food service is lackluster. Eat before you go!

Just finished a great lunch here.  It's an authentic and fun German restaurant.  The food was fabulous and the service even better.  I couldn't recommend more.  Andrew was my server and did a fabulous job.

I had high hopes when I first walked in because of the restaurant design, but I was really disappointed in the food. Don't go here if you're expecting real German quality food. This is the worst Jagerschnitzel I've ever had. Bier cheese was terrible too. I definitely won't be back

Love the venue -- classy, intimate, good wine -- great shows.  I have not had food here, so can't comment .. But since I really think Nashville in general is missing the mark on classy places --- this gets a 5 star for me.  Nashville is a strip of 'bars' and beer drinking joints -- so this is a really great option (one of the few) where you can see a show and drink some nice wine.

I went here for breakfast this morning, and it did not disappoint! We arrived at 9:45 AM and got the last open table before they went on a wait. For a Monday morning, that shows you how popular this place is. 

The child in me was craving some chocolate milk, and their chocolate milk is wonderful! Very creamy and chocolatey. 

The biscuits come out first with blackberry, strawberry and peach preserves. They were all delicious, but I think the blackberry was my favorite. If you fall in love with one, they sell them so you can enjoy them at home or bring back as a souvenir or gift if you're traveling. 

I ordered the bacon and eggs with a side of grits. I've learned that you either love grits or HATE them. I'm a true southern girl so I love them! I must say the grits at Loveless are some of the best I ever had. 

The serving of eggs was huge! I got them scrambled with cheese, and I swear there had to be about 4 or 5 eggs on my plate. I only got half way through before I threw in the towel. The bacon was cooked crispy, just like I like it. That makes a big difference to me when choosing a breakfast spot, as most places never listen when I ask for crispy bacon. 

This will definitely be a go to breakfast spot for me from now on!

I struggled between 3 and 4 stars on this one. My girlfriend and I attended a concert here two nights ago and I had mixed feelings. As far as our food went, it was amazing. We had the burrata, which was out of this world, and also the Brussels sprouts. They were cooked perfectly and seasoned just right. There were no complaints there. However she ordered a glass of wine that she received after our food came out and I ordered a beer that never showed up at all. On top of that the doors were supposed to open at 6 and the show started at 8. We showed up at 6:45 so that we would have plenty of time to eat before. We weren't seated until after 7:05 because we were waiting in a line that wasn't moving at all. Just seemed a little poorly organized which caused the wait on the drinks and wait to be seated. I would go back just for the food and get take out next time.
Pretty good, honestly don't understand what all the hype is about.

We've been back several times since my original review, and I still love it.  Every time we have out-of-town guests, we take them to the Loveless.  We make sure they all get a chance to try the Rise & Shine (moonshine & OJ) if they want to.  I've had it once, and that was enough for me.

We went back this month, and I ordered a bowl of sausage gravy for the table to share with our biscuits, and it got me to thinking about Bobby Flay's biscuit throwdown at the Loveless.  Now, I'm certain that Bobby's gourmet biscuit and jam were outstanding, and I'd really like for him to come fix my breakfast sometime.  But the biscuit that he made is not the kind of biscuit that anyone can make by the thousands, every day, year after year.  And I'm not sure how his biscuit would be with sausage gravy.  I may never taste a Bobby Flay biscuit, but I'm certain that I'll be having a lot more of those wonderful Loveless biscuits, either with gravy, jam, or as a ham/bacon/BBQ sandwich.

I don't understand why this place is so praised for their biscuits?? They have this awful chalky aftertaste. My husband can confirm. Have tried them on different occasions and always taste off. Is it the kind of thing where no one wants to disagree because it's so famous?? Disappointing.

The food was amazing. The biscuits were unlike any I have ever had. Waitress was so kind, and service was speedy. Can't wait for my next trip to Tennessee. Loveless will be on the list to visit again, because of the current biscuit withdrawals :)

Went in early on a Friday morning, had a omelet and biscuits and gravy. Biscuits and gravy were good but not the best I have ever had. The one pet-peeve that I have is un-melted cheese, which the omelet had, and under cooked onions and green pepper. The ham in the omelet was excellent. Prices are a little high, since this place is a tourist trap.
Excellent food and service Lucas (luke) awesome server ....best breakfast near nashville

This is a fantastic place and a must if you are in Nashville at any time. I had ordered the BBQ over eggs which are over pancakes. It was one of the best things I have ever eaten. The biscuits where the best I have ever had. They even have a cute little shop where they sell the biscuit mix and was so good. Later on our trip we went back for lunch and had the BBQ pulled pork sandwiches. It was soooo good. Be prepared to wait because this place is always busy no matter what time you go. However, you can check out the little shop or play bags while you wait. Thats right I said this place had bags that you can play while you wait. This is definitely a must go!

Went during the week with my dad and we both loved this place.  We waited only about 20 minutes,  I heard the wait can be up to 3 hrs on the weekend.  There is a window where you can watch them make the biscuits from scratch.  The food was amazing, I would go back.

The gift shops are super charming too.

Needed to catch a meal at the Opry Mills mall before a show at the Grand Ol' Opry. The number of tourist traps at this mall are unbelievable. I was walking to the food court when I see a sign for a Bavarian Bierhaus down a mysterious hallway. We decided to walk down it and came to a restaurant decorated like a beer hall. Super loud, with a band playing, people yelling "oi oi oi" and "we want beer" to the music, and also chicken dancing....yikes. Anyway, we decided to sit at the bar to the side to avoid all that noise. They have a reasonable selection of german beers which you can get .3, .5, or 1 litre potions. Also tried the 2-sausage platter with the original and cheddar jalapenos sausage. It was nice and juicy, and the place had a good selection of a few mustards for dipping. The sauerkraut is unfortunately really plain - needs more pickling!

Overall, a good place to park, drink, and eat, before walking over to the Grand Ol' Opry for a show.

I feel sacrilegious writing this but I am not the biggest can of loveless.  Sure, it's a staple for taking out of town visitors.  They have good food and cool shops and that adorable bar on their giant complex out there...but the food isn't that spectacular.  It's good, in that traditional breakfast way, but it's nothing you can't make in your own kitchen.  And (please don't hurt me for this!) this biscuits are just not my favorite.  Again, good, but not shout-from-the-hills good.  The wait on the weekends is always insane and I always feel like we are rushed out.  It's a place to go once at least, especially if you have visiting relatives, but I don't go out of my way to go there on my own.  I'll go if invited, but it's never a case of "gosh I'd love Loveless for breakfast right now."
My boyfriend and I have been here 3 times after moving to Nashville a month 1/2 ago. Constantly good food, homemade biscuits, and friendly staff. Cool gift shops, worth the wait for home cooked food!

OK so you are driving into Nashville from Memphis... BANG you see Lovelace Cafe's sign! STOP at this restaurant! You will not be disappointed! If you have ever listened to some rando on the Internet, listen to me now! The Lovelace  Cafe is amazing, flavorful, and spazmatic!

Definitely will have to come back and take in a show.

Atmosphere:
The entrance reminds me of a theater hall - which it pretty much is. We went the day after Christmas so the crowds were extremely low - like maybe 1 or 2 other groups with ours so we were able to enjoy an empty restaurant. You should be able to park on the street but it can be sketchy. (This place is next to the Nashville Rescue Mission - I think they tow if you park there.) Valet is available as well.


Service:
Since there was not a crowd we didn't have to wait. We didn't even have reservations so I couldn't tell you how the peak hours are.

They sat us near the bar but we could still see everything happening.

The food came out promptly.

Food:
We decided to go with the prefix menu with the wine pairing. I would highly recommend doing so as it was delicious, and the servings were surprisingly large. (Make sure to ask if you've got food allergies as they may substitute some dishes for you.)

However the wine pairings you can leave out. I would suggest if you're familiar with your wines that you just choose yourself. Some of the pairings were a bit overwhelming.

Overall:
I enjoyed the food very much. I was hesitant when this place first opened because it was next to the Nashville Rescue Mission but knew eventually I would have to give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

We were given free pretzels by the lady standing outside the restaurant (a card to get a free pretzel). They have a gluten free menu for those that need it and a vegetarian menu as well. Amazing. 

I got the potato dumplings with mushroom sauce which were delicious and the wonderful pretzel with honey mustard dipping sauce. 

The apple strudel (warm) is a must. 

The accordion player was excellent. 

Recommended

Omg those biscuits! And they're complimentary! 5 stars just on that. The other food was good too. I never imagined a pulled pork breakfast dish with eggs and it was excellent. The gravy was ok compared to other places in the South. But those biscuits....

I live right down the street from the Loveless so we frequently get carry out because the wait is too long. Expect a long wait, but there are shops that you can visit while waiting. 

As for the food, it's all the southern food that you would expect. The biscuits are delicious and I am not even a biscuit fan in general. The fried okra is great and the breakfast menu is recommended.

I've been here several times the staff are 
Always professional and I love their 
Southern food it's hard to leave the 
Table I always enjoy coming here
The food was just okay, nothing special. The service was terrible! So slow and they just didnt pay attention. Don't waste your time or money. But the whiskey 101 class we took there was great!

Great breakfast at the Loveless Cafe.  My wife had the Chicken Fried Steak breakfast, which was melt in your mouth delicious.  I had the country ham, which I had not had before.  It was a bit salty for my taste, but surely was exactly what you would be looking for in this type of ham. The endless biscuits were a hit with the family, and the homemade jam was worth the trip alone.

This is my new favorite place to go! Had the pleasure of seeing Los Lobos at City Winery a month or so ago. Just getting around to writing the review...

We used the valet service when we arrived which was fast & efficient. Walked in through the beautiful entry into main lobby and were greeted by several friendly staff along the way. We made our way to the podium to check in and were immediately escorted to our awesome seats for the show. Honestly though, there doesn't appear to be a bad seat in the house. We were on the side, second row of tables....

Our server came by within 30 seconds to get our drink order. Since our group was interested in wine, she brought over the sommelier to assist. He was very knowledgeable and recommended a great wine for our party. We ordered food and enjoyed the ambience and said hey to other friends who were attending. 

Food arrived quickly. Everything was really delicious - I loved the mussels and had the steak for entree. It was very tender and tasty...everyone in our group enjoyed the food very much!! Our server was excellent as well so the dining experience was 5/5 overall for food quality as well as service. 

The show began and this was amazing for many reasons. (a) I love Los Lobos - they are an old favorite and they never disappoint. (b) The sound of the venue was first class - excellent PA system was rich, warm and the mix was perfect...you could hear everything and nothing was either too loud or too quiet (c) Having a excellent meal while experiencing this made it over the top great!!! Add in the fact that you have plenty of "elbow room" makes it really fun to kick back, relax, and just enjoy the show!

I love City Winery and will go out of my way to see concerts there again and again!

Danke Bavarian Bierhaus! This place is amazing and you just feel you are having a beer and a sick pretzel in Germany. They have 1 liter beers, Giant pretzels ( you got to have one) and their apple strudel is delicious. So far, The giant pretzel is the most delicious I have ever tried.

Hubby and I came here in October to check out their fried chicken.  We were pleasantly surprised to be served complimentary homemade biscuits and jams which were all delicious!

The chicken did not disappoint either ... the coating was golden brown crispy and juicy.  It's a very popular place for tourists so there was a wait to get seated but they had many shops to keep people entertained.

Very friendly service!

I've been here countless times and have never had a bad meal or experience. The staff is wonderful and the food even better. If you want good home cooking then this is for you. There are options for everyone and an all day breakfast menu. They smoke bbq all day long on the property and it's to die for. The price is more than fair too. The bbq omelette in the picture was $8 and is huge. You can't go wrong with bottomless biscuits with a variety of jams.

This is a German themed restaurant, not an actual German restaurant. The beer is the delicious, but the food is not. You will enjoy this best if you have never been to Germany or even an authentic German restaurant. Diuble check your bill, our waiter added the $3 beer cheese sauce to our order, without us asking for it. And for some reason, after i filled out the check, and added the tip, the receipt that I sign had been rounded up.  I will not be back.

My friends and I had brunch here on a Sunday morning. The wait time was about an hour and a half, but we were able to order take out to eat at the picnic tables outside and received our food within about twenty minutes--worth it! While waiting for our food, we wandered around the shops. I loved the concept of this cafe and the way that the motel property has been re-purposed. Very popular with bikers, hipsters, families, retirees...this is truly the type of place that brings generations together.

I had a tough time deciding what to order, but after smelling the barbecue roasting I went with the pulled pork barbecue with eggs. This could easily feed two people...so much food! The barbecue was delicious, as was the hash brown casserole that I ordered on the side. I had high hopes for gluten free biscuits, but alas. I tried the peach preserves and they were great.

Everything was very good! The biscuits were great, the jumbo chicken strips, Mac n cheese, fried okra, mashed potatoes and has brown casserole were all so yummy! We got there at 5:30 on a Sunday and waited about an hour. Worth the drive!

I'm not one of those people who gets up early to eat breakfast or that person who just can't get started for the day without a heaping plate of sausage and eggs first thing after I wake up. Hell, most days, by the time I've done my morning routine (check emails, read the latest Cracked articles, read the news, shower/dress), it makes more sense to eat an early lunch and just skip breakfast (unhealthy, I know). This is not to say that I don't enjoy breakfast. I loved chowing down on the dining hall's breakfast on weekends when I was in college. I'm always up for a late night trip to IHOP (or WAHO, if I'm south of the Mason-Dixon). I've even been known to whip up big Sunday breakfasts if the mood suits me (homemade pancakes are my go-to, but I've made crepes and ebelskivers and omelets and more). I'm not a fan of early morning breakfasts, but I adore brunch and I enjoy leisurely breakfasts, and when I'm traveling, I'm much more inclined to fit breakfast into my schedule.

While visiting Nashville a few weeks ago with my best friend from home, trying out breakfast joints was near the top of our list of things to do. The South knows how to do breakfast and Nashville has a collection of well known breakfast places and diners (including Noshville and Pancake Pantry). The Loveless Cafe is perhaps the best known breakfast place and it's famous for a reason: they serve a delicious breakfast. 

To be completely honest, we didn't actually dine in the restaurant...we drove out there on a Saturday (after being defeated by the long lines at the Pancake Pantry) with high hopes of finding a seat. Unfortunately, everyone and their mother had the same thought in mind, so when we pulled in, it was a struggle just to find a parking spot, let alone a spot on the restaurant's waiting list. After hearing the wait could be well over an hour, and unable to handle the increasing grumbles of distress from our stomachs, we opted for the take-out option (having been reassured that it would only take about 15 minutes). 30 minutes later (which was not too bad, because the waiting list time was now almost 2 hours), we had two Styrofoam containers filled with breakfast and, as the weather was unusually warm for January, we were able to to take a seat at one of the picnic tables in front of the restaurant. The food was delicious: the eggs were light and fluffy, the biscuits were airy and buttery, the sausage had a nice snap to it, and the jam was sweet. My friend had some sort of concoction of pulled pork and eggs and hash browns and more and enjoyed every forkful. After dining, we roamed around the property, visiting the little shops scattered about (I happily purchased a bag of biscuit mix and apple butter--both ended up being delicious). 

So, while I can't review the actual dining experience in the restaurant, I can say that the food was excellent and, with its reputation and that whole "the owner was friends with Paula Deen and a bunch of country stars have eaten there" thing, it makes sense that it's a busy little place. If you want to dine in, be prepared to wait for a long time. Take-out is a great option and it definitely is quicker than waiting for a table--there are picnic benches around the property, or you could always take it to go. The employees I spoke to were incredibly friendly, despite the craziness going on around them, and they were quick too. The restaurant is a little bit out of the way, but parking is pretty decent and it's not too far from downtown. 

If you're looking for a great breakfast, definitely drop by...just be prepared for the fact that you may just end up eating breakfast for lunch due to the wait time.
This was so amazing and totally worth the wait. My server Skye was super sweet and friendly. The food is so yummy!!!

We got here on a Sunday morning around 10 am the last day when we were in Nashville and there was a 2 hour wait! Wanting to get on the road, we ordered to go and it was ready in 15 minutes! The pimento and fried green tomato biscuits were recommended by the sweet hostess and they were out of this world! We enjoyed all the staples as well. Stopped in the gift shop and purchased a cookbook and some biscuit mix and we were on our way. 

To summarize - if you are in a pinch for time, order to go.

Best biscuits and preserves I've ever had!!! The endless supply of deliciousness will get you in trouble. :) The breakfast was pretty good. The bacon could have been a bit crispier, but the sausage & ham were good. The house fried potatoes were amazing - also the best I've ever had. There was an hour and 15 min wait on a Monday, so I would call and make a reservation. But there was plenty to do and see all over the rest of the property, so our wait went by quickly. Such a cute & cozy southern atmosphere!

Hmmm....that really sums the whole experience up. Everything was amazing.  The location, the service,  the selection, the food! Oh the food was amazing.  Again, traveling through the south and found this little gem. Biscuits,  life will never be the same since I've had the biscuits from the loveless cafe.  I will shamelessly say I ate 5 and then the awesome waitress sent me home with another 9! And I ate the rest during our drive back to new england. I had the catfish and it was perfect! My husband had the country sampler and the fried chicken was amazing.  Overall best meal I had on our road trip. I would make my next trip circle around being able to stop here.

Wasn't surprised that we were told the wait would be an hour and 45 minutes at 11am on a Saturday morning. But we were pleasantly surprised when our pager went off after only 62 minutes. And it's not like there isn't enough stuff to keep you busy while you wait! Food is outstanding! Well worth the wait. And our server Mark was outstanding as well! This place gets 5 stars for sure - I'll definitely be back again!

Not what I expected.  I thought they would have a good chicken fried steak.  Unfortunately I got what was in the pic.  Anyone who is a chicken fried steak lover knows that the cfs in the pic is not the real deal, its the variety with that strange school cafeteria taste.  I'll still rate it a 3 because it was a nice place and the staff was friendly but don't come here expecting top notch southern cooking.  I am sure at one time the food was supurb, but this has now become very popular and commercial since.  I do understand, it is very hard to serve so many people when cooking everything scratch, but i have to tell it how it is.

This is a small place out in the country.  But it is definitely worth paying a visit.  It is a down home atmosphere, clean and friendly service.  But it does get busy, crazy busy on weekends.  I'm normally not a huge breakfast person. But the sausage patties and cheesy hash brown casserole here are simply amazing.  If you have a party of 4 or more, you can order 1 or 2 family breakfast meals where they keep restocking the food at your table until you throw up the flag of surrender.  

Summary:  Great down home, country dining!

The scenery was beautiful the wine was equally as pleasing. Unfourtunatly I came foR THE FOOD! Disappointing... The waitress was a darling about my dissatisfaction. 

Ok I just gave another star because of the waitress alone.

My wife and I visited this restaurant today.  Kelsee gave us some wonderful recommendations and took great care of us!!   The food and beverages were well prepared and tasted great!  Thank you Kelsee for taking great care of us!

Our gang of 4 enjoyed our breakfast at Loveless Café. Attentive and friendly service. Southern hospitality practiced here.

We drove nearly an hour based on recommendations from local friends. It is out of the way, and you have to seek it out. Fine Southern Cooking.

Tip I: Some seating is better than others. We asked to be re-seated to the front room, left of the greeter. Much better choice.

Tip II: Time your visit for non-peak hours to minimize wait to be seated.

Good value, and tasty food. Excellent choice for a local dining experience.

Ordered the double sausage plate with original bratwurst, sauerkraut and replaced potato salad with spaetzle. Brats- spot on; kraut- cold and meh; spaetzle- lacked all flavor whatsoever. Good news/ environment is SUPER chill and relaxing and Sean the bartender was excellent. Would try again if in town, if not for the food, definitely the beer, music, service, and atmosphere.

One of my favorite places to eat in Nashville! I also love the entertainment aspect. City Winery does a great job of booking desireable talent, and it never fails when I'm in need of showing my visiting friends/family a good time! I would recommend this to anybody. A little higher price point, but the experience and quality food are so worth it!!!

We are spoiled because we live close to this Nashville treasure. That means we can come during the week and avoid the two hour wait times during nearly every Saturday and Sunday of the year. 

But, if you're visiting Music City and want to try some famous biscuits and fried chicken, then this is a great place to put on your list. 

Located in West Nashville near the scenic Natchez Trace, it is an easy, scenic drive from downtown Franklin, or conveniently located off I-40 and McCory Lane. 

Come on the weekend and prepare to wait. The time will pass quickly as you visit the gift shop, take photos by the famous Loveless sign or play a round of corn hole or two. 

By the time you're done, you'll be ready to eat. This converted motel turned restaurant has charm. The entry is covered with autographed photos from country singer, athletes and local celebrities. 

The staff is friendly and many have worked at Loveless for several years. 

We've enjoyed many meals here as a family, friends and even a couple of business meetings. You can't go wrong. While the biscuits may be what bring you in the first time, it's the charm of this local institution that will bring you back.

Good and bad. Good: atmosphere, personnel friendly, clean, new, music. Bad: 28% tax on food and drink, plus $5-6 parking. So total of extra 50% of our experience was on taxes and parking. AND, extra 20% fees on top of event fee. Plus plus plus...this place nickel and dime's you to exhaustion. Boo!

After a long drive from NH we made a quick stop in Nashville and a local bartender told us we couldn't continue our journey without stopping for brunch at Loveless. I had the fried chicken and waffles with a bloody mary and my bf had the pulled pork and a moonshine drink. And let us just talk about the biscuits for a second, warm and buttery magic. Coming from New England, this exceeded our expectations as to what Southern food should be. The portions were huge and well priced. Our server was an absolute sweet heart! In a whirl wind trip, they left a lasting impression on us!
All I can say is OH MY GOD. The best food & service I have ever experienced. An extra THANK YOU to our waitress Jess! She was absolutely amazing and made our experience at the cafe a 10/10!!!

We came here at the recommendation of a friend. Let me start by saying to go online and make a reservation. We went at what I would consider an "off" time (2pm on a Tuesday in Mid-October) and there was still a 30 minute wait. But because we had a reservation, were were seated right away. We had a sample of items. Meat loaf, ham, fried chicken, and BBQ chicken. It was all delish! Like others have said, the ham is a bit on the salty side, so don't order that if you don't like salty foods. But otherwise you can't go wrong here! I also had the pumpkin cupcake, which was almost dense enough to be called a muffin. But still delicious.

Not only are their biscuits ahhhmazing (and jellies) but the place is also iconic! I love the food, but there's so much history there too. Feels like I'm eating in my memaws kitchen! And there's even a gift shop for tourists passing through!

I went here for lunch on my last day in Nashville. I AM SO GLAD I DID! They have to die for fried chicken and mac n cheese. The biscuits that come with your food are perfect, best I've ever had. They give you a selection of preserves with the biscuits as well...the peach is amazing. It's a bit of a drive outside of the city but if you are going to Belle Meade or Cheekwood, it's not too far from there! Totally worth it!

I've been to City Winery about 7-8 times. I've had a review on here before but they removed it because it of something to do with the reason I was here was for an event, which I feel most people come here for an event. I digress. This wasn't my first time. 

We arrived around 6:15pm on a weekday for an event. The event stated that valet parking was free for us, it's normally $6. Usually you can find parking in the back of the lot. This night there was two lanes, a valet lane & an Uber/Lyft lane. We decided to park in a spot down the hill from City Winery. In front of where we parked, it said "IR-G Customer parking 7am-5pm Monday - Friday". It was a Thursday, so we thought we were good.
