We were parked in the car for about 3 minutes when a valet attendant came down to speak with us. He said that we weren't able to park there as they park the valet cars. We could valet up front or park on the street along & behind City Winery. If you've been to City Winery, the whole place is fenced off. To park on the street & walk around is probably a block walk. This part of town isn't somewhere I want to walk a block in the dark when we left. He asked what event we were there for & we told him. He said that valet was free. We asked if we had to drive the car up there to then have him drive it back & he smartly said "yea" and shook his head up & down. 

We asked him about the sign that said IR-G parking & he said that "we have permission to park here".  So it's not even City Winery's property & they're dictating who can & cannot park there. I even looked it up on the property records & they don't own it. So we move the car up to the parking lot proper. There was a ton of open spots & cars that weren't backed in, which made me think other "regular" people parked there. Also because in the past we'd parked in the lot without issue, even when the valet was in force. 

We parked in the lot along the patio & got out. As we locked the car, a different valet ran over to tell us that we couldn't park there. He also asked what event we were there for & he told us valet was free. I asked "if the valet is free, can we not leave it here?". He said, "no". It then dawned on me, if we didn't have them park it & keep the keys, they would be out a tip. I asked him, "can I just give you a tip & we be able to leave it here". He agreed & I gave him $3 to leave it where we parked it. 

That situation put a slight damper on the night but it bounced back with the black bun pork burgers we had & some hummus. They also had some different wines on happy hour pricing, for $7. Not a huge deal, but better than the $10-$14 normal price tags. Two wines at $7 each, the bill totaled $17.40. I didn't think about it till after the fact, maybe some kind of tax? Liquor tax maybe?

They've got small plates on the happy hour menu (that runs from 5pm-7pm). We also had the crispy risotto balls, beer cheese stuffed, spicy mustard & adobo BBQ. I could've ate ten of those things, but instead I ate like 3 of them. I tried one of the duck tacos, I liked the flavor but the meat was a little dry, maybe an unlucky one. 

I've got no issues with City Winery expect for that exchange between the valet. I really don't understand how all these valet's in town can close down & take over public streets or other people's property for their parking. Next time I'll park on the street & pack a scooter to ride over.
So worth the drive!  Crispy chicken, tender gizzards, best biscuits ever!  Desserts were good, but we were really too full to appreciate them.  I'd skip dessert and have another biscuit myself.
Awesome lunch!!  It's not the same without the infamous biscuit lady, but still love to support local!!

My second visit in late August:

I made reservations for my meetup group of ten ladies here because of the amazing time I had previously at City Winery. I bragged on this place and the wait staff and could not wait to share the Nashville gem with the group. First, the reservation process...I made the reservation on open table and asked to have a tour and noted that I was a Vino file. I expected a call about the reservation which happens nearly every time I use open table but not this time. So I called the day prior and asked if we were touring and why no one reached out. I was told tours need to be made 48 hours in advance but that they would squeeze my guests in if it was not busy. We show up and it was busy with a Nashville Scene event. We were seated and waited for 14 minutes before anyone asked for our drinks and that was after I asked a server to find our waiter. Up walks Jared. SMH. I time everything when I get served in a restaurant like literally on my iPhone I time it. It took 15 minutes to get a round of mimosas so I asked for the manager to check on it and up walks Jared who tells me "oh they are sitting on the bar". Well go get them please Jared. At this point I snagged Darrell and remembered him from the amazing previous service and begged him to be our waiter. He quickly took our orders and was so pleasant to my guests. Thanks God for Darrell! I even had a guest celebrating a birthday and he even got her a slice of blue velvet cake. Jared however was aloof and spent much time with his other two tables. The food came out and all guests were pleased. I then asked the hostess about the tour and she said sure you can tour now it is not busy I'll send the manager. The manager never came. One of my guests stopped the manager and asked for the manager so we could tour and he replies oh I'm the manager. I explain the situation and he says we cannot tour. He said "I don't know who you talked to yesterday but we can't". I'm a vinofile and will not bring my guests here again. I was embarrassed to have talked to highly of this place. What a huge disappointment and disaster
The most amazing breakfast place in the WORLD. My favorite was the pimento cheese fried tomato biscuit! So so so so amazing! And the staff was extremely generous!

Oh man. If I lived in Nashville, I feel like I would be here ALLLLLL the time. It really seems like the go-to place for new and emerging talent. Talking to some people on the patio, there is also a fair share of accomplished musicians who decide to drop in unannounced, (I heard Metallica came once upon a time to randomly practice their set). This was our first stop when we got into town, as my friend was putting on a Texans in Tennessee showcase that included a bunch of singer-songwriters either living in, or originally from Texas. There was truly something for everyone - indie artists, country artists, a little bit of pop-rock...and everyone was more than welcome. 

I can't put my finger on it, but you just feel like you're kind of in the presence of greatness in this place. Like one day you'll hear someone on the radio and say, "Oh, I remember seeing them at the basement!" 

Drinks are reasonably priced and pretty heavy-handed if you go the liquor route. The bartender was super friendly and awesome. Definitely a place to visit if you're visiting - even if you don't know anyone who's playing, you'll probably still find someone you like.

Wow!  Such a great experience!  We had a large group so we had to wait a little while (but it WAS a Saturday night so we expected it). They did have shops and things to look at and check out on property though, so that was nice. Once we were seated there were no disappointments from there on!  The food portions were huge and plentiful!  It was a great experience and I would love to come back with my family!  Thanks!

OMG our first visit here. Drove in from Cincinnati on our way to Memphis and was strongly advised to stop here for lunch. The hour wait was very much worth it. I had the BBQ and my wife had the smoked turkey. Both meals were outstanding. Come very hungry is all I can say. The portions are big!!!!

After reading some other reviews I feel that Some people just want to complain.   $5 for valet is reasonable.  This is a intimate venue.  We watched Jason Isbell there last night and the crowd was 412 people.  I was amazed an audience could actually be quiet in this day and age.  The food seemed a bit pricey but it was very tasty.  No complaints about our service, as Ashley took very good care of us.  The wine selection was good, the craft beer selection could stand a few more options, but this place is called the winery....   If an artist you like comes to the winery, do yourself the favor and go watch them there.

Yummy! Long wait , but played cornhole and enjoyed our company ! Food was amazing!!! Pulled pork BBQ biscuit is where it is AT!!! I may have also drank a mimosa for two ... By myself.... Yummy yummy yummy !!!

At this point I could care less how good the food is. Sunday morning, arrived at 10:40. We were put on a list and told an hour and a half for a group of six. Because of the long prospective wait half of the group opted out. So we went up front and were told twenty minutes. We wait a half hour and then we're told it would be about her 45 minutes. So we are getting it to go. It's 12:30 and we are just getting the food. Totally unsatisfactory.

Southern hospitality at its best, and QUALITY FOOD!!! I could not believe my mouth! This place is everything it promised to be, always FRESH HOMEMADE ingredients is what we were told, and they delivered no problem... THE BEST BISCUITS ANYWHERE!!! Seriously folks... as a native Californian, i have never ever ever tasted biscuits so good. I've got a gluten sensitivity, but am not celiac, and these did not affect me at all. The pork loin was tender and delicious, the creamed corn is to die for, the service is friendly, warm, amazing - Susan was our waitress and she was generous with portions and her customer service - before we leave Nashville, we are definitely making the 30 minute drive back out to this place... IT IS WORTH IT YA'LL!!!

Got biscuits? The Loveless Cafe has you covered. Buttery, flakey and served with strawberry, blueberry and marmalade jam, breakfast doesn't get much better. Come early, or you will wait. As an alternative, you can also order takeout and eat at one of their picnic tables. Country ham, fried chicken, grits, sausage gravy and hash brown casserole are all not to be missed. We got a sampler of pies to go, and I'm already looking forward to dessert. Customer service and price ping both A+. Be sure to stop by their retail store on the way out for some merch, biscuit mix and jam.

I absolutely LOVED this place!!! They had AMAZING food and te service was great! Anytime we are in the Nashville area we will go to the Loveless Cafe. We have already told all of our friends and family about this place and cannot wait to go back!

Excellent !  Order exactly what u want, they will accommodate.
Passing thru, yelp score again!

This is a little diner out in the middle of nowhere.  We went based on the reviews.   We were not impressed.  The mac and cheese was decent.  We had the fries checked fingers and three sides.  We purchased one extra.  We had sweet potatoes which were too sweet, fries green Tomatoes which tasted like they were laying in the kitchen all day.   Not impressed.  Our waitress was super friendly and made the experience enjoyable but the food was mediocre at best.

Pretty darn authentic. Just a lot cleaner than a real Oktoberfest tent! The chicken was delicious (although the skin could be a bit crispier) and the currywurst was spot on, although you could argue currywurst has no business in Bavaria. This would make for a great night out with friends in the fall!

This breakfast is GREAT! Boyfriend and I got to Loveless at about 9:45 on a Saturday morning. We went in knowing we were going to have a lengthy wait, so when we were quoted an hour and a half I wasn't too perturbed. The grounds are really cute and we were distracted (or I should say I was distracted) by the shopping for about 20 minutes. Afterwards, we just sat in the car with the buzzer from Loveless because it wasn't a super nice day, and listened to Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows on audiobook. Highly recommend.

Our buzzer went off after about 45 minutes, cutting our wait time in half! This was awesome, and I don't know if they over-quote intentionally but I think it's a genius idea because I was so happy when the wait was shorter than I had gotten prepared to wait for.

The place is ADORABLE inside and our waiter was really nice. I had an omelette, my boyfriend had a sampler with a million meats and eggs, and we gorged ourselves on those biscuits. The omelette was really yummy and my boyfriend's plate was very good as well, but at the end of the day, I think people go here more for their lunch specials like fried chicken than a standard omelette, but OH MAN THOSE BISCUITS.

The biscuits are so light, so flaky and delicious. The jams that accompany them are delightful, and I had to tell our waiter to stop bringing them over because I was getting really concerned at how many I would be capable of eating.

This is a really fun, albeit kitschy, breakfast spot. Don't come here if you are a person who will be annoyed at waiting a long time for food that isn't THE BEST FOOD YOU HAVE EVER HAD. Enjoy the experience, and mostly those biscuits. Yum.
Amazing food!  We had the fried chicken, hash brown casserole, green beans, fried okra, mac and cheese and Biscuits with jam.  So good!!

yeah i know, i'm going to be boo'd and hissed at for only giving it three stars.  the biscuits were 5 stars though.  my husband and i are locals, and he has somehow never been here, so he insisted we go.  after the expected looooooooooong wait, we were seated and greeted by an exceptionally personable server.  

my husband had some friend chicken, i think....and i had the barbecue pork.  the portions were HUGE (and the server also gave us a ton of biscuits to take home with our leftovers...i'm not sure if he should have, so don't ask about this!)  we both had sides of macaroni and okra.  the macaroni was yum and the okra was good too.  

i know loveless is a nashville tradition, and there was nothing really wrong with our experience, but, take away the tradition, and it was just, food--except for the biscuits, they're magical, like they were made with unicorn tears. 

so here, get some neat jams and bacon from their gift shops, and tip well, those servers have hard jobs!

Not really much to say that hasn't already been said.

First of all, the fried chicken is the best around...maybe some of the best I've had.

They are known for the biscuits and jam, which are just ok to me.  I compare everything to my mom's homemade biscuits and jam, and nothing comes close.

There is one thing you can always count on with Loveless Cafe that may not have been previously mentioned...the music on their playlist is solid country gold.  Merle, Possum, Waylon, and all the hits from the 90's. 

I'd like Loveless so much more if it was a hidden gem.  It's popularity creates a long wait for a table.  If going on a weekend, arrive before 8:00 and you won't have much of a problem. After 8:00, and especially after 9:00, you should plan on at least an hour.

The Loveless Cafe experience was worth the scenic drive and wait!  Excellent, friendly customer service with every employee we encountered.  Jason made amazing suggestions! Thanks for a lovely Sunday!
Tourist trap meat-and-three.  Biscuits are mediocre...they mass produce them, so that they are just a "step" about fridge "grands".  My homemade baking powder biscuits are better.

After reading the reviews I decided to check this place out for breakfast before our ride back home to North Carolina. We, my wife and I, felt the nostalgia as soon as we pulled in. We were greeted and brought to one of many rooms; very comfy. The menu was loaded with a lot of nontraditional breakfast items, very non-typical of a breakfast menu. My wife got coffee and French toast, I got coffee and Southern Omelet (3 Eggs, Diced Country Ham, Bacon or Sausage with Onions, Peppers and Cheddar Cheese). While the omelet was good sized, the fillings were non-existent and the cheese was clumped in the middle. $10.00 for an omelette with no side like potatoes is way too expensive. $7.00 for three pieces of French toast, regardless of how good, is also expensive for no bacon or sausage. No way would I come back here again at these prices for NO reason... oh, and the coffee was weak and overpriced too...thankfully the Loveless Cafe is close to Interstate 40 and the Natches Trace Parkway.

This is my favorite Restaurant in Nashville! I came to this restaurant alone because I was visiting, and all the staff was so friendly and would stop and have a conversation with me. Their BBQ sauce is nicknamed "sweet and sassy" and it was to die for! I had the BBQ pulled pork sandwich with bisquits, and then some coconut cream pie and I was in heaven. I highly recommend this place, it's extremely cute, the people are amazing and the food is to die for.

Wonderful restaurant and service. I'm a vegetarian and was able to order a plate of 4 sides- grits, Mac n cheese, fried green tomatoes, and fresh fruit. Mac n cheese was some of the best I've had! Will definitely be coming back!

I had an awesome experience here. Great food and beer. Live entertainment and very entertaining. A real German feel experience. My server Holly was very helpful with recommendations for food and was able to find a beer to my liking. The desserts were delicious. Also met the manager Kevin who signed me up to have my own locker and beer mug! Overall great experience and a lot of fun for the family.

I have been here four times with hope each time we would have better service. Each visit has been made at lunch time so there has only been maybe 10 parties dinning at the same time so not that busy. Each time it's has taken about an hour and a half because the service is soooo slow. On one occasion we gave up on telling the waitress what we wanted because it would take her 10 minutes to get back to us and I hope you aren't thirsty because that is not a priority. If I were rating on just the service this would be a one star. The food is wonderful I haven't ordered anything I haven't liked and the large pretzel is huge enough to share. I do suggest you try it just be warned that the service will be slow!!


Update- so we tried again and was very happy this time! As always the food was great but, our server was very attentive and helpful.

The Venue is beautiful.  But the service sucks.  Management was not friendly at all.  I think I spoke to the GM about why the food was cold and he did not try to get me another plate or offer to comp my meal.   I think with this is going to have a lot of bad reviews if the management doesn't get changed.  
As the rest of the community has discussed the parking situation is not favorable.  I was their for a corporate party is how they handled where to go was not organized.

Oh my word. This place is hog heaven. Not for hogs, of course, cuz they're getting smoked out back. But all manner of cooked hog--bacon, sausage, country ham, pulled pork--is here for you. We also spent some time talking with Eric, the pitmaster. He brought us into the smoke house and talked with us about the process, showing us pork butts, briskets and chickens in the smoker. This dude loves his job and does it well.

Back inside, they gave us a mess of biscuits to start. After we were done they gave us another mess of biscuits to go, along with the preserves. Here's a tip. Ask for the sorghum for your biscuits. And while you're at it, mix a little in with your grits. Oh my word.

Went for Super Bowl party.  The wines for tasting were not good.  The hummus plate was not good. Some store bought hummus with pickled cauliflower and flavorless cracker bread. The mushroom pizza was AWFUL. Servers were great. The big screen TV was great.  Venue has potential but the food and wine were meh.
Road tripping from NY to TX and saw this on Yelp. Waited 1.5 hours and would do it again any day. Food was excellent and enjoyed strolling around the grounds while we waited.

I had the southern sampler plate. I enjoyed everything except for the sausage. My boyfriend had the biscuit plate with the bbq biscuit, fried green tomatoes and pimento cheese and the chicken biscuit. He really enjoyed them all. Service was great as well.

I wouldn't waste my time with the drive.  The biscuits didn't seem to be the greatest ever to me as they just seemed like biscuits.  They were warm and good but not great.  I think I had too  high of expectations for this place hence the two stars.  It probably is a three star place because of the various attractions around the store.  They also make their food themselves which makes it a decent place.

I ordered Biscuits & gravy which was good as the gravy was done right.  The coffee was a little weak for me and I didn't get a refill until my food came.  It sat empty for close to 5 minutes.  My wife ordered a Mimosa which was strong and she liked it.  It used wine instead of champagne.   My daughter has scrambled eggs which were blah with no flavor.   My wife went with a chicken biscuit that wasn't up to her Chick Fila standards.  All in all the food wasn't bad but it wasn't so great to drive 30 minutes out of ones way for.  The homemade jams are ok but my mother and aunt make it jbetter.  

The nice thing about this location are the little shops with overpriced stuff in them.  It is nice to walk around and see the places.  They have baby changing  stations in their handicap stalls.  The bathrooms were clean and all the workers we met were friendly.  I would stay in Nashville and try out another breakfast place instead of coming here.

We really enjoyed our visit to Loveless Cafe. There was about a 45 minute wait for dinner, but there is so much to do on the property the time just flew by. I had the brisket special, which was really good. It had a nice smoky flavor. My favorite thing was the fried green tomatoes.

Wow....lived in Nashville all these years and never ate hear. The peach preserves are off the chain. I had the Biscuit sampler. The pimento cheese and fried green tomato biscuit is a must.Everything was really good except for the sausage it had a funny seasoning.

Destination Restaurant! If you are visiting Nashville this place is a must... The food, the service, the grounds, the country ham and their preserves... Yum their peach preserve is amazing... I even thought of liking the jar :/ it was that good. Their portions are gigantic so you will be better off sharing a couple of dishes... Easy drive from Nashville and beautiful scenery on the way here...

Convinced my family to go while visiting Nashville.  Thought it would be "touristy" but made the trip.  WOW!!!  The biscuits with the preserves are worth the trip alone.  The hot chicken...definitely THE best. My son, who just got the fried chicken, said if he ever was on death row, THIS would be his last meal.  Spinach Alfredo soup, a must order! The service was AMAZING.  Susan (sp) went above and beyond and was friendly as could be.  Y'all need to go!
A great breakfast good service great food. Best biscuits and gravy ever. I will be back.
Overall, I had a really good experience. Loved the live music the day I went, as well as my food and my server Gemaal. Great service! Definitely would go back.

As if headed to a Winery was tough enough for a pregnant lady like myself who loves wine...the food situation was like a Abbot and Costello routine.
I ordered a bacon flatbread and was completely starving as we waited 40 minutes for food to arrive. The other couple at our table received 2 orders of their food within 20 minutes - so clearly an error resulted in a duplicate of their order but ours never came.
My husbands food came and I was told my flatbread was on the way.
10 min later no flatbread. Our waiter apologized profusely and comes back to say it's on the way.
2 songs later still no flatbread. My husband has now fed me half his dinner.
Our waiter again apologizes profusely and begins bringing appetizers, offers to comp a meal, and nearly had tears in his eyes that the kitchen can't produce food for the pregnant lady. 
Manager stops by and apologizes, again offering to comp a dish (needs to be the whole meal) and brings us some truffle fries.
After 2 more songs a flatbread arrives! 
It is the wrong one.
For fear it will be removed and I'll never see food again, I eat it as fast as I can.
Lovely atmosphere and wine selection. Delightful wait staff. 
Kitchen situation was pretty rough. Hope that is addressed.
We'll be back for another concert but won't order that flatbread again.

So, I had major expectations for this place because of all the hype from everyone. The best biscuits ever? No. And they weren't even warm. My husband & I agreed that the best thing about the biscuits were the 3 homemade jams that came with them. Those were fantastic. My cinnamon raisin French toast was good, but nothing fantastic. The bacon was great though & I'm not even a bacon eater, typically. My husband's omelet didn't have much flavor. It was a good breakfast, but we kind of expected a great one, especially after waiting an hour & 40 minutes.

Best biscuits on earth....(I'm not kidding). The biscuits are truly amazing, as is the rest of the menu. I bring all my visiting family members here for breakfast or lunch at least once during their visits. My favorite from the menu is the pulled pork omelet, as it has just the right sweet and savory combination to satisfy the palate. Do yourself a favor and take the significant other for a nice breakfast, or brunch.

Loved City Winery! The wine was fantastic and the food was even better. I got the grouper and my boyfriend got the steak. Both were delicious, we didn't want them to end! You can tell everything here is made with quality ingredients. We stopped back for brunch with family, it was also delicious. Make sure you ask for Kimberly, she was by far the best server we've ever had!!

The beer is absolutely awesome! Some very rare german beer and the food is pretty authentic for American standards :) I'm just in love with the pretzels hahaha but I'd definitely recommend to come here if you're in the area!

The biscuits alone are worth the wait that you generally encounter when visiting. Their fried chicken is excellent every time and the hashbrown casserole is a must! Try going early to skip the crowd- they're basically busy the entire afternoon on the weekends in my experience.

We took a group of 9 people Wednesday night.  Initial drink order went ok although water was a long time coming and red wine spritzer came as a white one.  Our 9 th party member was late to dinner.  She had to go to the bar for her beer.  Never did anyone offer to take her order.  We shared our meals with her.  My meal was lukewarm and pretty much tasteless, as was my husbands fish and chips.  It took a good 30-45 minutes to get the meals we ordered and the restaurant was not overly crowded.  Although the beer was really good I could not recommend the food or the service.  My husbands coke was only refilled after asking 2-3 times.

I would have posted a photo but the food didn't last long enough. On the one hand, I wonder if they make you wait so long (1.5 hrs!) to make you so hungry the food would be good no matter what. On the other hand...OMG THAT FRIED CHICKEN! And the biscuits. And even the coffee. The service was excellent as well (thank you Robin!). It's worth the drive AND the wait.

Yummmmmmmmmm

I suggest going first thing in the early AM to get a good table on a weekend- but that said- still worth the wait if you hit it mid church rush!

Love the pancakes here, the biscuits are delish and my husband loves the country fried steak that they have on the menu.

Really quaint little restaurant- like such that you might find the floor uneven in spots. :) Part of its character.

that said- the mini biscuits and the preserves are delish and they are very generous they do not skimp.
Worth the hype. Amazing biscuits, amazing jam... my husband got pulled pork and eggs and loved every bite! I got the ham and eggs! If we're ever back in TN we will definitely be coming back.

This place lives up to the hype. Great food, service and atmosphere. We only had to wait 20 minutes for our table. Definitely worth it. We'll come back again if we're ever in the area. Great fried chicken!

Went to City Winery for an event last weekend. Besides the sub par food, the atmosphere really rounds out your entire experience. Couldn't really see myself frequenting to this establishment if I didn't have a reason too. Examples, event/concert. The drinks were over priced and the food was just ok. My girlfriend and I decided to split a flatbread. The crust was exceptional. However, the flavors that were included didn't really compliment each other. Hopefully I can give this place another try because it really does have the potential.

Ordered the famous fried chicken (half) to see what all the fuss was about. Thankfully I wasn't disappointed. The fried chicken was incredibly crispy with succulent juicy meat. The marriage between the perfectly seasoned breading and skin was about as tasty as I've ever had. We're talking fried chicken so good you'd smack your mama for, if she didn't smack you first. The choice of two sides, which I chose mash potatoes and macaroni & cheese were also very good. Our waitress was also very sweet and patient. This cafe deserves all the 5 stars it gets.

I made a reservation on OpenTable two months in advance for a weekend trip.  I was notified this evening they are unable to accommodate my reservation for a party of TWO.  After reading other reviews it seems they've done us a favor!  They shouldn't offer reservations if they can't coordinate their seating.
Food is very good even though the restaurant is annexed to the mall.  Don't let that deter you if you have a craving for German food & beer!

Best biscuits! Biscuits with jams are complimentary. Be sure to get there early. If there is a long wait, there are several cute shops to peruse. Great place to pick up a gift. A game a corn hole is available as well as plenty of outdoor seating to wait on. You can also see into their kitchen where they make the biscuits from scratch.

Very homey decor and feel. Tables looked a bit squished together but I didn't notice this being a problem. Great friendly waitstaff. Breakfast menu had everything you'd want for a traditional breakfast. I decided to go with French toast with a side of bacon. Perfection on a plate! It was a great introduction to Tennessee home cookin for my first trip to Nashville. Great environment for family and kids.

Biscuits and preserves were the best part of the meal. Don't know if I would travel more than a few minutes for them though. Guest ordered the special which was peach-bbq smoked chicken with mac and cheese and mashed potatoes and his verdict is that the sauce was the best part. Chicken was said to be kind of dry and there was a shoulder shrug when asked about the sides. I ordered ham and eggs with hash browns and turnip greens. The hash browns were the best and came recommended by our nice waitress. The turnip greens had great flavor. The ham was a very large portion but was a little hard and chewy and was my least favorite part. The experience may have been better had we gone to the museum and the store etc. Maybe next time and maybe one more star. But it's gonna be a solid 3 for me.

Yelp never lets me down.  What a great place to come and eat if you are traveling thru Nashville. Expect a long wait, but lots to do on the campus and well-worth it. Our table tries the Barbecue Pulled Pork, Half Fried Chicken, the Green Tomato BLT and a bunch of wonderful and yummy sides - Turnip Greens, Mac & Cheese, Hash Brown Casserole, Cream Spinach and Cream Corn. All the food was delicious and Barbara our waiter was just a doll and very helpful to us. If we definitely will come back and loved your Southern Hospitality.

This is a stop worth the wait.  It's a great experience if you've never visited here.  We got there at 12:15 pm on a gorgeous autumn Sunday.  Ninety minute wait for a table.  We passed the time by exploring the interesting shops and walking the grounds.  Our lunch menu included hash brown casserole, hush puppies,ham, meat loaf, pulled pork, turnip greens and THE biscuits.  These Texas women didn't care for the biscuits at all. Tough, bland biscuits.  Turnip greens were cold and very stringy--no pot liquor as promised.  Meat loaf was bland.  High points-- hash brown casserole, ham, hush puppies.  Got the homemade banana pudding--made with sugar cookies instead of vanilla wafers--nothing special.  We're glad we took the time to visit, but I don't need to go back unless I'm in Nashville for extended time.  If you're traveling south out of Nashville, take the Natchez Trace.  Beautiful drive!  Have a full tank of gas before hitting the Trace...gas stations are few and have to ask Siri for gas locations.  The Trace has sporadic internet connection.  Go to Loveless at least once in your life!  No regrets!

I will find any excuse to eat here when I'm close to Nashville. The breakfast is amazing. For lunch the fried chicken and mashed potatoes actually taste homemade. This is one of my favorite places to eat.

While the location is nice and adds a little class to Nashville the training of the wait staff is underwhelming.
If you use wine in your name your people had better be the best they can be when it comes to wine and this is not the case. 
The staff were very nice, however, it is just that they have not been given the tools to be as aware and knowledgable as they should be.
The night was very quiet and the overall service was suspect.
Food quality was mediocre and not to the quality expected.
This is not the place to eat or drink until they learn to step up their game.
Too bad, we were initially excited and were let down on our first dinner in Nashville for NHL All Star weekend.

32 bucks for breakfast is a wee too high.

food was great, service was great.

just can't get over the price.

Best place in Nashville for country ham, eggs, biscuits, preserves.  Only wish they still had the homemade butter and a little thinner cut on the country ham.  Their lunch and dinners are fantastic as well. Meatloaf or chicken n'dumplings are both winners.  The homemade salad dressings are fabulous.

Great food, service, and location.

Good home cooking style food.  The staff is great, and I've never had to wait long for a table even though the place is very busy.

First time here. Fun. Good brats and awesome pretzels. Indoor beer garden tables. They have a live band in evenings. Outdoor patio. Kept it simple this time but definitely want to explore the menu more. Full service restaurant with Coke products. Everyone enjoyed their meal.

Loveless is (apparently) one of those Nashville institutions, and since breakfast is one of OUR family institutions, we decided to hit the place on the way out of town. Because we enjoy traveling while in a coma, we opted for the family-style breakfast, which, roughly translated, means "we come to your table and stuff you like a Thanksgiving turkey until you can't take anymore." Eggs, grits, hash brown casserole (very light -- not), bacon, ham (yummy, but WAAAY too salty), and the star of the show -- biscuits that will make you slap your grandma. At first taste, I wasn't that impressed, but after the 7th or so I concluded that maybe they were pretty good. And served with delicious preserves and sausage gravy. Needless to say, there was no lunch consumed that day. Good coffee and great service. Be prepared for a significant wait during rush times.

The Best Bisquits I've Ever Had

The place was a zoo on a Sunday, with nearly an hour wait--but worth it.  It serves the most amazing bisquits I've ever had--you take a bite, put your tounge up against the underside, and the bisquit just melts like cotton candy.  These bisquits are like crack.

I can't comment on the rest of the food.  It was good, but so overshadowed by the bisquits that even mentioning other food would distract from the real feature at this place.

The first thing I thought was odd was the $5 up front valet fee...I usually pay more on the back end and this really turned me off.
The location is beautiful and service was great.
I tried several items on the menu:
Beef bone marrow...just to say I've had it once...best thing I can compare it to is beef-flavored snot...one and done with this one
Hamburger and fries...excellent! 
Sausage pasta dish...tasted like a salt lick...even my sodium addict wife said it had entirely too much salt..very disappointing.
Flat bread pizza was great too!

Stopped in on a Wednesday evening for dinner and had the daily special of chicken and dumplings. Delicious is an understatement! The Loveless Cafe serves up southern, home style cooking with a side of charm. The biscuits were yummy, especially with the trio of jams for you to try. If she's working, ask to be seated in Ms. Barbara's section; friendly service that ensures your sweet tea stays full and that you've got all you need to enjoy your dinner. Don't forget to grab a piece of pie to take home with you (you'll be too full to eat it there). Ms. Barbara claimed the coconut cream pie is their best and she was right!

My mother and I first time Nashville. We just wanted some good ol country food. When we walked it was so cute with the wall of fame. We were ordering take out because the wait was very long to be seated. We didnt have time to waiting. So when it came down to ordering the hostess Hiley was sooooo rude. When she had to take our order, when we were sitting down (starring at us so ugly), and when we were getting our food. I never felt so uncomfortable. I was so mad but i didnt say anything because i didnt want to cause a seen. But they with be getting a call and a letter. Thanks Hiley for ruining our first time in Nashville.
Stumbled upon this place by accident but so glad I did. Had the smoked pork chops and the onion soup. Both food and service were excellent. And the brews, don't get me started on the brews. So good!

Not sure where I heard of this place, but I know I had heard of it. We stopped here on a road trip out west. It's a very cute place; was an old hotel, I believe. We ordered food on the phone ahead of time and then picked it up. We ate it in the car. The food was okay, but that may be because I ordered a salad. The biscuits are good, but I'm from the south, so I wouldn't say it was anything spectacular. Definitely think it's worth a shot, but I think I may have missed something about it.

From what I understand from well traveled friends, this is styled very much like an authentic German beer hall; very large with tons of seating. The bar also seats close to two dozen. I've never been in there when there isn't a live German band playing which is a blast. 

First, a warning: The large pretzel is an EXTREMELY large pretzel. And yes, you want the bier cheese with it (in case that was a question). 

The beer flight is great, especially if you're not well versed in German beers. They do, however, pick 4 of the 6 for you, which was the only downside. 

All the food I've tried has been very good, including desserts. I don't think you can go wrong on the menu.
Food was great, biscuits were hot and fresh out of the oven, and our server (Mark) was awesome! Highly recommended

Good food that did appear to be "scratch made" I have the biscuits n gravy.  The gravy did taste scratch made and not from. Mix.  
Biscuits were really tasty. 
The jams were good but the strawberry was
Extremely runny so not very jam like.  The peach really didn't taste overly peachy to me.  
The blackberry was By far my personal fav of the the 3.
Luke was our server. He was attentive And provided us with great service and just the right about of chit chat. 
Nice way to start the day. 
I'd return but might make reservation in advance.  We waited about 1 hour this sunny Sunday morning.

After shopping in a mall with an 8 year for a couple of hours a large beer was in order. We stopped in for beers and food. The decor was traditional bierhaus, with servers in costume, long tables and German music. A liter of seasonable Oktoberfest beer was $15, a little pricey in my opinion. The children's meals were well priced but the pigs in the blanket had a meat that was too seasoned for my daughters liking. The adults ordered a large pretzel with beer cheese ($13) because carbs and cheese are two of our favorite things... however the pretzel was blah and the beer cheese gross.  (Which before now I would have ever though was possible!) Honestly it tasted like a weird beer cheese soup...which is on the menu as well. The sweet mustard that accompanied it was just that, sweet. The best dipping sauce was the free Düsseldorf mustard on the table.

City Winery has been overlooked and underrated for far too long.  It's time to give them their props. Though this establishment is relatively new to Nashville the clientele who frequent are some of Nashville's finest.  And there is a reason for that.  The service continues to be exceptional.  Yes, truly exceptional.  Wait staff and bartenders take the time to engage and form relationships with diners.  The service is timely, accommodating and personalized.  Ryan Nelson is a staff member who goes above and beyond to make patrons feel not only catered to but at home.
  The change in Chef may have altered the menu, but this establishment has not skipped a beat as far as dishing out delicious choices.  Chef Garrett Pittler brings a much welcomed Buffalo flair to the Southern kitchen.  The Burger on Weck (Menu item: "Black Hawk Farm Burger") does his native town justice.  The Kummelweck roll is perfectly seasoned and baked (no small feat for those who understand this savory sandwich bread - which may be easily crafted but is temperamental to store - therefore, fresh is a must!)  This burger boasts beautifully grilled onions and a horseradish aeoili that tingles the tastebuds.  The Grilled Cheese goes above and beyond in a gourmet Texas Toast style - bringing comfort in a layered combination of two cheeses and fresh thick tomato. Accompany these choices with the Smoked Salt & Vinegar Fingerling Frites to add a tasty compliment.
Top these dishes off with the House Zin - a delicious, fruit and jam forward flavor with a lingering dry finish - and arguably you have a perfect lunch.
Another excellent option is the Kale Caesar flavorful and zesty - an anchovy lovers salad experience!
Much like their sister properties in NYC, Chicago and Napa, this location is now producing their own featured wines. Happy hour at City Winery is a quality experience for visitors and locals alike - a wonderful value!
Lots of food. Pulled pork and chicken were good, but we all left feeling sick because we ate so much. Glad we went once, but probably wouldn't go back again.

I've officially set my mom up for failure with a visit to Loveless Cafe two days before Thanksgiving!!  Friendly service, amazing meatloaf and delicious sides.  This little gem was the icing on the cake for our day trip to Nashville.  My only regret... Not saving room for dessert!

This place is VERY touristy -- for example, there are *multiple* gift shops -- but the food is absolutely worth it. The biscuits are, of course, famous, but their BBQ deserves to be equally well-known. The BBQ pulled-pork omelette was so flavorful, moist, and delectable. You can get a plate of biscuits with four different toppings for variety -- I LOVED the pimiento cheese and fried green tomato biscuit. Their country-style ham is excellent -- it tastes like a thick-cut slice of prosciutto. I'll also note that our server was very friendly and helpful. 
Pro-tip: one of the gift shops has a freezer with Jeni's ice cream in it. :)

I visited the Loveless Cafe twice on my recent trip to Nashville. This restaurant never disappoints. The pulled pork and Bloody Marys are wonderful. The granola (might be a side item) is good. I wouldn't recommend the French Toast. But, of course, my favorite part of the meal were the BISCUITS!!

While in town for a conference, I coordinated an evening event to be catered here. The food was great, and the staff were semi-helpful. I would like to have seen a little more hospitality and communication from there. Otherwise, a great experience.

I don't normally post reviews (actually, I have never posted one) but, maybe I should have. My wife and I have eaten at many of the newer restaurants around town and have enjoyed the majority of them. We went to City Winery last night to watch a show and eat dinner. Here are my thoughts:

First, the good: Cool place, nice outdoor seating for just drinks or a meal. The inside is really nice and the concert area is cool and spacious.

Now for the bad: No parking and forced to pay $7 for valet service--that is in addition to the tip. The food is edible but not special. Smoked avocado dip is just run of the mill and very thin chips that broke when we tried to dip with them. The entrées--my wife had bacon and beet flatbread and I had the chicken--were overpriced for the quality of the food. Chicken was very average and the side of grits was nothing special. The flatbread was just flatbread--nothing special. For the name--City Winery--the wine selection was poor and the beer list was also limited (Nashville has awesome local brews, but there were only two on the menu).

The acoustics were not good either. We were seated in the upper deck and couldn't even understand the musicians when they talked and sang (maybe the sound quality is better on the main floor); I was expecting much better in such a new and intimate setting.

Overall, this would be a decent place to go to hear a band or singer if you could be fairly close to the stage, but I would recommend eating elsewhere since there are many options nearby. I was dissatisfied to spend $100 to $150 or even more (depending on choice of drinks, appetizers, etc.) for tickets, food, drinks, and parking and not have a memorable experience.

Very delicious. Everything was good. Had the Leberkase. Eggs were cooked perfectly. Also had red cabbage and potato salad. All food was very tasty and they have a nice selection of beers but not extensive. I gave only 4 because I asked for a glass and was given a dirty one. I will return again.

UPDATE:  10/17/18. My husband and I attended the Bierhaus for a Yelp Elite event.  Our party was held in the back of the large dining hall in a separate room, which is good to know they have for any special events.  Being Oktoberfest, the main restaurant was pretty busy with a good oompah band playing on stage.  Like other reviewers have stated, you sit at long tables community style so there's a good chance to meet other diners.  We sampled three Paulaner beers, all were quite drinkable.  I'm not sure if they will always be on tap, it may have been for this week of Oktoberfest.  The pretzels are huge and the housemade mustard and cheese sauce were both tasty.  We enjoyed the Black Forest cake and apple strudel for dessert as well.  They have a stein club for regulars, which is a fun idea to have your own stein in a locker, and take advantage of drink and food specials all year.  Really a fun place to bring guests, they certainly won't be expecting a German bierhaus in Nashville!  

A nice addition to the Opry Mills mall, with an entrance inside the mall and once outside if you want to avoid the mall crowd.  Large beer hall with a stage for live music.  They have a reasonable selection of Bavarian beers with seasonal specialties added.  Food menu looked good and as is typical German fare, leaned heavily on sausages and meat.  We only tried a few small sides, the spatzle, roasted red cabbage and fries.  All satisfied that craving for German food.  If you're a meat eater I think you'd be satisfied with their selection of Usinger's sausages. Servers dress in authentic German beer hall attire, which lends to the festive atmosphere.  A nice addition to the Opry Mills complex.
Extra long wait during the weekend, but yummy chicken and biscuits!

I attended City Winery New Year's Eve and that evening KIM was my server and she was fantastic. I've been to City Winery a few times and by far Kim provided the best service of any visit. I am not a fan of the wine but the experience she provided certainly helped with that! :) Thanks KIM!

Though you may have to wait for a table it's worth it. The service is outstanding and the food is great. I had the sampler with fried chicken,country ham and meatloaf with hashbrown casserole side. Every dish was perfect. The meals come with dinner biscuits that are really good.

The long lines are for the famous name, but the food is actually delicious.  I'm not sure it was worth the long wait, but once we got in, it was good.  Service was top notch.  The breakfast was satisfying, with basics like eggs, bacon, hashbrown casserole, biscuits and gravy.  My favorite was the pillowy biscuits brought out first with the assortment of jellies.  My daughter got the chicken and waffles and she was not impressed.  I would go back, however, if we were in town again.
Good food and great jam but the wait is ridiculous! Regardless, my wife and I will likely return for the jam alone.
No.. just no. It's just all pre frozen food you could probably get at Costco. The beer was no good either.

Let me first say that this place has such potential and I'm really hoping they work through some  "growing pains" because the atmosphere is great. BUT...My family came here from out of town for a drink while simultaneously casually looking at the venue for a wedding as my sister just got engaged. When we walked in there was no one at the host stand and the two women at the ticket counter barely looked up from their phones when we asked for some guidance as to how to get a table.  It was pretty frustrating feeling like we were bothering them by asking a few questions. This is absolutely not how we would want our wedding guests to feel. Also, our waitress was great initially however once we were served we waited a little too long for our checks.  All that said, the wine was delicious.

Excellent news.. The $15 burger with potato chips was cooked to order and actually tasted good..   A lot of money for a burger, granted, but if you're going to eat there, it's good.  Take my word for it..   The rest of the food is blah.

Seating is still difficult.  You pull your chair out into the aisle, so you can watch the stage and you are up against the other person, at the other table, behind you... and you're fighting for the aisle..  That's still a problem.  A lady and I were practically in one another's laps, trying to view the stage from the aisle........  Thank God she didn't smell.

So.. concerts here are (on a scale from 1-10) about a 3-4 unless you're in the first seats against the stage.
Food (on a scale from 1-10) is a simple 1. unless you have the $15 burger with potato chips.  If you HAVE to eat, the burger is good.  The brussels sprouts have sugar.  Just be warned.

I'm thinking if you sit upstairs on the high tops, you don't have to fight people for the aisle to get a good view of the stage.  You won't be in someone else's lap.  You have more room.  
I'll try that, one of these days.

Going to the Burlesque show tonight....  Again, down on the floor. But I chose a seat that shouldn't have anyone in front of me and I hopefully won't have to fight over the aisle for a view.

This place really is mediocre.. Unfortunately...
Thank God the A/C works.

Found the Loveless Cafe online while looking for restaurants before my wife and I took a trip to Nashville and boy am I glad I did! 

While pulling up I didn't think much of the exterior until I walked in and saw a nicely renovated place with autographs on the walls from nearly 30 years worth of country music acts. We had a roughly 45 minute wait (a testament to how good the food is!) that we spent sitting on a bench outside watching a family play Corn Hole. 

Once inside our waiter Matt was attentive and really nice. He had a personality with out being overbearing and took really good care of us.

 Their signature item is biscuits - they are served with everything. The biscuits were good, not amazing but nothing bad to say about them. Their jam on the other hand was amazing!  For our main course my wife and I both ordered the fried chicken.  It was the best fried chicken I have ever had. It was AMAZING. 

If I didn't live a 13 hour drive away I would be a regular here.
One of my favorite places in Nashville. Great service, friendly staff, and good music. If you want great German food and lots of good beer, look no further.
I must have preferred the wrong thing. It was the pair of dumplings. One of them was inedible. The sauce was going s but the dumplings were too dense. My husband liked the fried fish.

We stumbled upon on Big Shotz on Friday and we couldn't get over how nice and sweet the Bartender was she took time to get to know us and our drink order! The band was really great! We felt like the Prices for drinks and shots was very reasonable! We made sure to make Big Shotz our first stop on Saturday night and as soon as we walked the sweet bartender not only remembered us from the night before but remembered our drink order as well! Before calling it a night we had to stop back in!! We truly felt like this place is definitely underestimated! We have been telling everyone about it! So if y'all out in Nashville stop by Big Shotz you won't be disappointed!

What an amazing dinner!  We where recommended to stop here for dinner. I do not even know where to begin ... the staff is wonderful and so friendly and the food holy wow!  We had spent the day at Graceland and then drove to Nashville so we where tired and ready to get to hotel but so glad we made the stop. It was my moms bday and we had on shirts to celebrate. Most everyone there stopped and wished her a happy birthday!!!  Both my parents got the country fried steak and I got the fried pork chops (pictured) ... and the biscuits where absolutely delicious. We all had different sides and mom had banana pudding. All where sooo yummy!  If you anywhere close, I suggest this place. We will be back!!!

Absolutely the best German restaurant we've eaten at! The portions are huge!!! The red cabbage was amazing. The service was excellent and the staff was so friendly and hospitable. We will definitely come back!!

Finally got here for a show--and there is much to like in that format. Good service--thanks Debbie. A solid Old Fashioned and hey put it in perspective--solid concert food. The farm burger with bacon: nicely done. But come here for dining? Probably not, too many better options just minutes away. Also not impressed with the welcome experience here. Never fun when staff are obviously bothered that you don't know what to do. Yet I enjoyed my evening and will take in more shows in the future.

I was visiting Nashville and I had to come here. It's a bit far, 25 mins outside the city but a nice scenery drove. The place was busy but moved quickly with service. The waitresses are polite and attentive. Food is pretty good and biscuit is a bit different then what I was expecting but still good.

They just made it on the tv show 36 where they shared their tip with viewers: put chunks of pink watermelon on smoked ribs and finish off in a 400 degree oven for 30 minutes. The hosts both raved. I will go soon.

Wine for days! Went to dinner since I'd never been. Had a couple of the small plates, pumpkin gnocchi, fries and kale salad and the beet and bacon flatbread. All good, but they are changing the menu, so there are a couple of things that are not carrying anymore. I would like to come back to see a show.

Adorable, iconic, and so tasty! 

Feels like you're eating at your grandmas house. The food was so yummy. Their known for their biscuits and for good reason. My favorite item was the pimento cheese breakfast (listed in the starter section) it was so strong and savory! 

A bit far out but it's a pretty drive so go for it!

My group decided that Loveless Cafe was a must visit on a recent trip to Nashville.  This place is actually about a 25-30 minute drive from Nashville so be prepared for a little hike. 

When you pull up, you'll notice that this place used to be a motel and they've converted most of the old hotel rooms into little shops.  Put your name on the list immediately.  We were quoted a one hour and 40 minute wait.  We got in about 10 minutes before the quoted time.  The good news is that there are plenty of shops to browse around as well as plenty of seating locations throughout the property.  Some people wanted to avoid the wait so they used the Loveless Cafe App (Hi-tech!!) to place a pick up order and they ate their meal at one of the picnic tables scattered throughout the property.

We finally got seated around lunch time.  This was perfect as you can order from both the breakfast and lunch menu at lunch time.  I ordered a grilled chicken biscuit and then a plate of 4 veggies as my main meal.  A plate of biscuits are brought quickly to your table as soon as you sit down.  

Everything was really good.  My least favorite item was actually the grilled chicken biscuit.  Everything else was fabulous.  The biscuits themselves are perfectly light and small enough that you don't feel guilty when you eat 10 of them.  I stole a bit of smoked turkey breast and it was really good.  My sides (mashed potatoes, hash brown casserole, creamed corn and green beans) were all really good.  I almost licked my plate.  

This place is good enough to merit a drive to Nashville alone.

The food was amazing!!!!! The best creamed corn I have ever eaten!  Peach and strawberry jam are excellent.  Peach jam was like peach pie filling! 
We ordered the fried chicken which was juicy and very good. Great mashed potatoes!!! Fried green tomatoes not that great.  We will definitely be back. The pancakes looked great too!! It's out of the way but worth the drive!!!!!!!

There isn't much to say. This place is amazing. We know that it is a kind of quasi- hipster concept. To bring a German drinking hall to Nashville, complete with polka, and lederhosen, but it isn't ironic at all. In fact, this restaurant is genuine. No weird east Nashville fusion fad recipes. Old school, German recipes like Grandma from the old country made. This is by far my favorite restaurant in Nashville.

My family ate at the Loveless Cafe on a Sunday afternoon. It was packed and we had to wait about 35 minutes before being seated. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit and hope to go back. The food was delicious!! Loved the biscuits and we were even given some to bring home with us. Definitely recommend.

I am a recent move to Nashville, and like other post, was suggested to go here. I like home style cooking as much as the other place, but this place missed the mark. I got the fried chicken. But, for me, it didn't have enough seasoning. I cannot remember what side I ordered, but I know I was not satisfied with it.
Holy smokes!! Jalapeno and Cajun flavored bacon! Who knew bacon could get better? Biscuits are delicious and the pit bbq pork is excellent!

Although very busy we had the option of carring out and eating outsidw picnic style. The wait for s table was 1.5 hours. Since the last time I was here the quality seems to have gone South, but not in a good way. The chicken fried steak was tasteless, the mac and cheese was mushy. My wife's fried chicken was not as good as a remembered.  I would only give them 2.5 stars on this trip.

I love love love their biscuits and homemade jams. If you come here expect to wait anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours. It is definitely a high volume restaurant. We enjoyed walking around the grounds to the little shops while we waited for a table (2ish hours). The food was pretty good but the jam and Biscuits were by far the star of the show. They had a ton of delicious looking pies on display though we did not partake in any of them. I'm not sure we'd go back unless an out of town family member or friend wanted to go because of the usually long wait times but it was pleasant enough experience. Nice attentive service and plenty to look at.

Nice strong coffee. After breakfast I wanted to take a nap in the corner. Homemade everything is hard to really dislike. The potato casserole rivaled my grandmothers and the biscuits. They were basically crack.
Of course friendly southern attitudes complete the experience.. Great breakfast spot. Can't wait to try it for dinner.

Maybe it's because I have been raised around Southern food that I wasn't blown away. Everything just didn't live up to the hype, and I am honestly a little disappointed that I got so excited to eat here. The service was pretty good, and our drinks were always immediately filled. That's probably the reason I feel bad giving Loveless Cafe less than three stars. However, the food... meh. I've had better food from local restaurants from my town (e.g. Beacon Light Tea Room). The biscuits were good, but again, Beacon Light Tea Room has better ones. The fried chicken I ordered tasted a little dry to me, and it caused my stomach to be upset that night. It was nice to say I've had the experience, but I probably will not be returning.

Biscuits are fantastic. And the jam/preserves (peach) are equally wonderful. This place is out of the way but absolutely  worth the drive for the biscuits alone. The food is pretty good as well! Fried chicken was a touch too greasy for my liking but still yummy nonetheless.

Fantastic pulled pork and fried chicken (the chicken needed salt, but had best crispy coating and moist meat).  Pecan pie was on point.  The cheese grits and Mac and cheese were both solid as well.  The free biscuits that come with dinner were flaky on outside and warm on inside, and came with a fantastic assortment of jams and apple butter, all house made.

Went there for a combined Father's Day / German World Cup match early on Sunday morning. They were unprepared for the crowd they got, but in spite of a few moments of confusion we were seated with the entire family and quite enjoyed ourselves. The staff (for the most part) was attentive and pleasant, but a special shout-out to the manager on duty - he ran a tight ship and took care of the initial issues like a pro. The weisswurst and knackwurst were a little bland, but the rest of the food we overall pretty good for a place this size.

Some of the best southern hospitality and cooking ever. Flavors are on-point, waitstaff is so pleasant. We got the chicken and waffles, chicken tenders, meatloaf, and chicken fried steak. Sides were potato casserole, turnip greens, creamed corn, fries, and bread with preserves and butter. Nothing healthy about this meal, but you'll have enough for leftovers for one or two meals to offset. Restaurant is settled in a mini "town" with gift shops, post office, and bakery... only problem is the wait. I get it - it is super popular and always busy. But a 2 hour wait for food is not always ideal, even with the shops and no matter how good the food is. We browsed for 30-40 min, but then sat for 90 just waiting out in the TN heat.

Seriously the best. Always a wait but worth it.
Biscuits and homemade jams to start.  Unfortunately you can't just eat those. You have to order food from their variety filled menu items. Chicken and waffle - chicken breast is bone in.  Waffle is hearty. I think it has wheat germ in it.  Don't hold me to my guess . Important part is fluffy means it is hearty and good. 
Southern plate I think it looked good. My friend had the whole thing ate by the time I poured my syrup on my waffle. Must've been good. . 
Biscuit sampler they are biscuit sliders. Choose four from the choices.  
Sausage gravy.  Not the best I've had but I would order it again.

Just drove 20 minutes out of the way and had lackluster fried chicken at loveless cafe. Famous for fried chicken?? Booooo.   No seasoning. 

Biscuits tough

Blueberry preserve was excellent, however

BBQ sauce too sweet (on meatloaf and pulled pork)

Paula Deen fried chicken in Pigeon Forge waaaaay better
The best biscuits ever!! Watermelon ribs are amazing and their jams are sooo good!! Everything we had was wonderful.

This place is such a pleasant surprise! We went to Husk yesterday and it can't compare to this place. You feel the southern hospitality not just from the way this place looks like home but also from the friendly staff: Owen our server. The food is the best thing about this place: DELICIOUS! I now love Southern cooking. The hot chicken was flavorful and the catfish was fresh.

I had been wanting to go here for about 2 years now. It did not live up to my expectations. The service was good until we were done eating, stacked all of out plates and 20 min later the server asked how we wanted out check. So it got real slow after 10am when a lot of other people came in. The food was ok, typical southern food. It was a little overpriced but I guess you are paying for the experience. I will not go back unless someone is visiting me and really wants to go. There are much better breakfast places a lot closer to Nashville.

A lot of hype and super long wait for an average breakfast. The biscuits and preserves are worth the hype, but not worth the wait. Order to go and sit at a picnic table on the property is the way to go.

The atmosphere was cool. They had a band playing some bluegrass. It was a pretty day to sit on the steps and enjoy. 

When I ordered, I asked for the bacon to be cooked crispy. The waitress said all the bacon is cooked crispy, but it came out limp and fatty. 

Overall, it was decent but been to better.
The biscuits!!!! Delicious! We ordered the family style "all you can eat"....the sausage was tasty, the jams were good. Good service..All in all, a great family place for breakfast.

3 shows under our belts here, supper club...dining, drinking, music and chit chat.  It is lovely, not a bad seat in the house.  Our preference is upstairs in what they call VIP area.  Great view and easier to chit chat.  Go downstairs if you want to make new friends as you sit close.  Food is good, me loves the Kale salad and risotto cheese balls.  Super satisfactory on all levels.

I would give this place 5 stars if I didn't have to wait two hours to eat...but I will say that it was worth the two hours!  The food was amazing!  We were from Chicago and wanted real country cooking and we got it. The staff is amazing too.  Only downside is I wish they had some more stores to shop in :)

Over hyped...my wife and I are visiting Nashville for the first time. Like anyone else visiting, this is an obvious must stop since it's a Nashville institution. This was definitely a place that we were both looking forward to. We got there around 9am, were seated right away. I ordered the chicken and waffle. She ordered the country ham. The chicken was crispy but bland, overall it was ok but not worth the price. I've definitely had better fried chicken before at a lower price. The waffle was good, then again you can't really mess that up. The ham that my wife ordered was quite salty and had a not so good barn yard flavor to it. The biscuits were good but does not live up to the hype. Overall, the service was good, the decor and ambience is what you would expect for a southern style restaurant. The food is underwhelming. We would likely not come back to this place if we visit Nashville again.

I went the night before opening, the German beer selection is incredible, the Weinerschnitzel is authentic. They've really done a great job re-creating an authentic German beer Hall. Lots of space for for big groups. I'm looking forward to seeing the changes when construction is complete.

Excellent. First of all, the space is incredible. It acts as a restaurant and an event space with two venues (one smaller, one larger). Got to see that they make wine in house, as well. There's nothing I love better than authenticity. There is ample seating here, from multiple patios to a main dining area. I came with a big party and we were accommodated very well. Also, I came for a birthday and the staff made sure we received a free bottle of champagne to celebrate. This kind of courteousness goes a long way. The staff handled our huge party very well and had everything out to us in a timely manner. This place is great for a date night, a birthday party, and event, or a wedding. Loved my time here.

What great venue for eating, drinking, and listening to your favorite music groups.  Last night we saw New Riders of the Purple Saga and they blew us away.  A trip down memory lane when I hung around San Fran in the early 70s.  Jam band elite, although the founding members are dead all but one they still got it.  They were working their way toward Chicago for the Greatful Dead 50th and last show over the 4th of July weekend.  We started with a Scottish Devil egg, Cobb salad split, peach n Beacon flatbread with a very young Vinhe Vino wine.  All in all. A great evening!  We will back!

So worth the wait (1.25 hours). Everything was GREAT!  Fried chicken, mac n cheese, creamed corn and greens. The biscuits are deserving of all the rave reviews! Everyone else in our party of 7 got something different and everyone left happy and full!
Great music venue!  I was lucky enough to catch Lucinda Williams there and it was fantastic.  The food was great, too.
Great food. Very fun atmosphere. Great staff. If you like good, authentic German food, I would highly recommend.

Loveless is a must stop! The bbq is amazing as is the fried chicken! Normally there is a crazy long wait but it's worth it! I got a sampler this past trip with catfish also but didn't care for it as much. The mashed potatoes are yummy but skip the turnip greens. They're known for their biscuits but I'm not in love with them. I guess I'm spoiled to Cracker Barrels biscuits and turnip greens. I'd say you definitely need to get the chicken or bbq!
amazing chicken and waffles. Never knew why people loved fried chicken before, but I do know now! Their waffles tasted like cake batter, and deliciously crispy chicken.

I used to like to say "don't treat me like a tourist",  therefore I really shouldn't complain when I get food of this quality at a very tourist sort of restaurant.
 Nonetheless four stars out of five is definitely not what we  experienced.
My cousin had the beer and cheese soup and a hot bacon and spinach salad.
 I had the Jaeger Schnitzel with spaetzle and a cucumber salad.
If the food prices were in line with the quality I suppose it would be a very slightly more positive review, however, $56 later I can say it was a truly bad meal.
These days I generally don't like to eat what I consider "factory Pig" .
Not only was this schnitzel Factory Pig but it actually tasted like a pig smells. It was horrible.
The brown, mushroom gravy was not even up to par with your standard Knorr packaged gravy it was simply awful.
The cucumber salad was at least edible.
My cousin's beer and cheese soup was just OK.
She said that her spinach salad with hot bacon dressing tasted moldy.
I did have one bite and I had to agree,  it wasn't worth a second.
So being locals,  I guess we got what we deserved for going to a touristy area, eating touristy food and certainly paying touristy prices ....but it won't happen again. I truly feared I might get ill from the schnitzel.
However if you're a Beer Drinker I suppose it's an okay place.
 The beer is imported from Germany,  to bad the food wasn't. The place was cavernous,  loud and the waiter,  who was very nice when we ordered,  disappeared after asking how we liked the the food and receiving an honest answer.
I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking authentic German food.

A lot of kinks to workout. Understandable, as they are only 6 days old. However, the staff was not able to answer basic questions; more than 6 different people serviced our table (with little knowledge of the food and which patron placed the order). This is basic training, folks. Management - please spend more time training your people. They have no knowledge of the wine or the food menu.

This is my first 5 Star rating!!
The food was amazing. The server (Shalimar) was wonderful! The manager sat down and talked to us! It was a great time!
The only negative is------ I live 1600 miles away
We live nearby and frequent this place for breakfast. My father law tried to order toast with his meal and I almost smacked him. If you go to Loveless, you get the biscuits!

Tried Loveless for the first time and absolutely loved it. I'm a little annoyed that I lived 5 minutes from here and I am just now trying it. Prepare yourselves, You will have to wait. We went on a Sunday at about 11:45 and waited a little over an hour. 
My sister and I split the biscuit sampler platter with fried chicken and country ham biscuits. We ordered an extra side of hash brown casserole and sausage gravy. Little did we know to start, they bring out a huge plate of biscuits with strawberry, blackberry, and peach jam. They will also bring out more if you eat all those and you will. I probably wouldn't have ordered a meal with biscuits had I known. Biscuits are made with butter and taste like it. The sausage gravy was delicious and the hash brown casserole came sooo close to my family's recipe. I normally HATE gravy at restaurants but I ate all of this one. The macaroni and cheese was also amazing, we should have gotten another side of that. Between the biscuits and our sampler, we were very full and didn't even finish some of it. 
If you want good southern food and your grandmothers not available, this is the place for you. Can't wait to go back!

Unique dining experience for the whole family. The service was exceptional. The food is all family style and arrived at the table quickly. Their signature biscuits and homemade jams arrived first and were outstanding. The barbecue with homemade sauce was tender, juicy and flavorful. All the sides (cream corn, green beans, hash brown casserole) were warm and delightful. Desserts were plentiful and delicious. The fried chicken was a little on the dry side and was the only disappointment. Did I mention that their biscuits were outstanding?

I visited City Winery on a Saturday afternoon as part of a series of events for a bachelorette party.  We were a party of 6 ladies and I can speak for all of us when I say the overall experience was wonderful.

Once greeted we were seated at a booth in the dining room right off to the left when you walk in.  The service was top notch throughout our visit. Our server even smiled when we asked him to take a few pictures.  

Drinks - I had one of their wine flights which was a mix of white and red wines.  Their flights are $20 which includes tax.  One of the other ladies had a bloody mary.  I love bloody Mary's so of course I tasted hers.  They use Zing Zang as their mix which, in my opinion, is one of the best mixes around.  They also have a small variety of beers. 

Food - The table ordered a few appetizers to share.  Everything was delicious and very flavorful. The brussel sprouts with goat cheese are a must. 

City Winery is a great place for a nice date night or a special occasion.  If I lived in the area I would definitely be back.

Good food, although the menu items (including both drinks and entrees) are more expensive at the restaurant than those listed on their website. Service was okay, although waiter seemed a bit sensitive.

We were driving to Memphis,  we looked for good breakfast places on yelp. Based on the reviews we stopped in. I told my wife when we arrived, this place was on diners drive ins and dives. The biscuits made this place famous. We walked into the restaurant. It has tons of celebrity pictures on the wall. We got seated, and a plate of biscuits and jellies came to the table.  The biscuits and jellies are incredible.  . The breakfast is very good. The waitress was Johnny on the spot.  We will be coming back, next time we are in town
What a fun find.  Fun atmosphere, great beer selection and authentic German fair.  I would come back next time we are In Nashville.

I was super excited to come here, after hearing great things, but it didn't wow me as much as I hoped it would. The food was good, the wine was delicious (as to be expected) but it was lacking the atmosphere I was hoping for. If you're really into wine though, this would be a great place for you to visit!
Thank you. Your servers and chefs say that their is animal product in them. What do you use to make your stock? They warned me when I ordered and also double checked with whoever prepares the food.

I have since tried this place 4 other times.
Each time ordering something different.
 All in all, the food is good, with the exception of the spaetzle.

After commenting about this place, a couple of friends wanted to try it.

They have also lived in Germany, so expectations were high.
I did not let them know about previous reviews, so as to not give a possible negative bias towards anything.

Each time, the negative comment was on the spaetzle.
Usually with the same comment....... it was like paste.

We did go one day for lunch (a Tuesday?) and a band was playing.
I will say it was playing MUCH to loud for the space.
4 adults could not carry on a conversation due to the volume.
Now we may of felt different if we were there to fest, but it was a working lunch and just had to fight to be heard.

I do like going here, but that may be due to my love of German food.
Is it the best? No, but is it good? YES.

Will I continue to eat here? Yes, just not on days with the band due to the volume level.

By far THE best bbq spot in all of Nashville! It's a bit on the outskirts of the city but let me tell you, it's worth the drive just for the biscuits alone. They said our wait was going to be 40 minutes but our buzzer rang after 15 minutes. The meat was smoked to perfection, and the sweet potatoes had just enough cinnamon and butter. They make their own jams to go with the biscuits; and did I forget to mention they serve them before your meal? The banana pudding is house made to perfection too. Food came super fast, and service was great. Everyone was super friendly; the hospitality lives here!

This place is fantastic, albeit a distance from downtown Nashville. Still, well worth the drive out to enjoy the scenery and the restaurant/shops. 

If there's one thing that stood out for me the most, it was their hospitality. I work in the industry and appreciated receiving the sincere friendliness and attention to our visit. 

The biscuits were ready for us as soon as we arrived and our order was received quickly. The food comes in large, hearty portions. But wow! Everything tasted amazingly. Definitely recommend the Country Fried Steak or the Chicken & Waffles. 

Make sure to take time and visit the nearby shops that were formally the rooms at the Loveless Motel. You'll find great stuff there with their logos - especially kitchen decor and items. 

I already look forward to my next visit to the Loveless Cafe.

Well worth the wait. We stopped in for breakfast before visiting the city. Highly recommend the country fried pork chops and the country ham. Portions are pretty big and they give you biscuits with their delicious jams to start, so come hungry.
We went here for Easter, it was fabulous...I am not a biscuit lover, but, these I couldn't stop eating w their homemade jams...all the dishes we got were worth the wait, and they have alcohol !!

A lot of folks drive out for the fried chicken.  Had the Fried Chicken, Hashbrown Casserole, biscuits & jam.  But oh my country crickets! I had one bite of the home made Cream of Corn and wanted to order a gallon of it! It's called Loveless but there is nothing but love for this cafe.  When I walked in the restaurant that looks like a white country home. The walls are covered with celebrity headshots. Leann Rimes and my boy Bucky Covington and of course Elvis! Tons of celebrities.
     There's other shops surrounding the restaurant and you can order some pulled pork sandwiches to go. There's a bbq smoke house too which is cool.  The chicken was good.
