I didn't have a chicken that people talk about. I need to try more items which is fine. I can't wait to go back for the corn. The biscuits are smaller but they have good soft texture with the jam.  The hashbrown casserole was ok.  I'll pass next time and try another side dish.  Loveless won me over with the corn and a photo of Bucky.  All kinds of people have made the nice drive out to the country side to dine here.  It is worth it. Just becareful at night.  Some country roads don't have lights.

One of our favorite place to eat whenever we visit Nashville. Hot biscuits, great choice of sides, and excellent variety of main courses. Something for everyone. We appreciate the full bar. Our waiter was excellent and on point for our large group.

Amazing. I wish that I lived closer to the loveless cafe- I would be trying the entire menu! I ordered the country fried steak with Mac and cheese and hash brown casserole. The steak was huge, great flavor and the sides were great.  The biscuits and jam were to die for!!  The service was top notch and I felt like I was at home.

First stop when we arrive in Nashville is to swing by the Loveless.   No matter where you are staying its worth the 20 mins out of town to eat at this historic gem.   45 min wait is easy with pagers that reach the entire property and 2 stores to visit along with the photo ops outside.  The food is tasty and comforting.   The biscuits come to your table in mounds and it's clear why, they are melt in your mouth.  Along with the 3 jams on your table!   Chicken tenders are the biggest you've ever seen.  One meal could feed three people.  Ham is smoked and salty.  The sides are interesting, delicious and you will want a meal on those!   My 8 yr old loved the fried catfish.
   Even if just passing through Nashville, Make it a point to stop at the Loveless!   Get yer biscuits!
One of my favorite places in Nashville. Good food. Great atmosphere. Everyone wears authentic German attire. Large variety of brats and sausages.
Really only one word comes to mind wow. They're homemade biscuits are just ridiculously good. The pic cooked pork is just like eating candy. I feel really fat leaving here now ate way too much.

I've been missing German food for quite a while and the city we currently live in doesn't really have any German restaurants. We were in Nashville for a couple days and I discovered this place. I was so excited to try it. What a huge disappointment. Our waiter was great, and the atmosphere was nice, but the food was absolutely horrible. I got the Jägerschnitzel and it was so salty I couldn't eat more than a couple bites. And that's saying a lot because I normally have to salt my food. 
With all the amazing restaurants in Nashville, I was super disappointed my husband and I wasted $75 on a meal here.

Drove an hour to this place, than waited over an hour to eat.... And the food was sub par. My bacon was like rubber. Save yourself the time and go to a chain restaurant for the same food. Not worth it.
Nasty!!!   Food was horrible, did not taste like schnitzel.   Save lots of money and go somewhere else.   They need to emphasize on quality of food instead of the lil German outfits!!

Being generous with 2 stars.  Food is OK, service is laughable.  
 I've been to Germany and the slaw and potato salad are pretty authentic to what we got over there.  Sausages are all made by a firm in Wisconsin (they're good), don't expect to get anything actually made on site.  

Now for the service....Seated at 6pm on a Sunday.  Maybe a third of tables occupied.  Probably 10 minutes for a server to come by.  Another 10 minutes for beers to be delivered.  Still very few people in the place. Had to turn away 2 different sets of food that were sent to our table rather than the proper table.  Once our food finally arrived, had no silverware.   So between the person that seated us, our waiter taking our order then delivering drinks and the person who brought our food, nobody checked the utensil stein on the table to see if we had silverware.  I went and scrapped up some knives/forks from another table.  FINALLY a member of the wait staff came over when they noticed we had 2 of the cutlery steins on our table to see if they could take one of them to use at another table.  It was comical.  

We had previously been here for their family style Christmas dinner and it was good.  Food was all tasty and service was decent.

Overall, it's pricey for what you get both food and service wise.

Won't be going back.
This place is a must!  The biscuits are the best I have ever had!  My daughter agreed and she is picky!  I got chicken and waffles, she got pancakes...delicious!!

I arrived to the venue and with all the information provided about the show. Did not see where it was gonna be set up where we couldn't even sit anywhere but the bar facing away from the artist. Employees were not nice.

From the outside it looks like a tourist destination. On the inside, it's different. Especially when you taste the food. The biscuits are fresh and so are the jams. Keep in mind it's just the warm up round. Then I got my food. Put Barbecue with 2 eggs. It was huge and it was great. It's clear they have a smokehouse and know how to use it, well. If you are in the area, you have to stop.
out of the way, but delicious and worth the trip!!  shows at the barn are top quality; however, fair warning, this is a very calm crowd who will keep grey tops in seats.

It's ok if you want traditional southern cooking. It's made its way on to internet lists so I think its become a tourist thing with long waits. I don't get what the big deal about the biscuits is. Its always just be ok when I have been. Don't be fooled by the BBQ you can see outside, they don't know what they are doing with that.
We had to wait for awhile and it was worth every bit. Food was delicious and plenty of it. Worth the trip here. Thanks for the good meal.

After the 1 1/2 hour wait, it won't be shorter even if you are only a party of 2, I can say it was worth the wait! Our waitress was super down southern sweet and the food did not disappoint. My hubby had the southern sampler choices were fried catfish, ham ( yes, it's salty but he likes that) and the fried chicken. Yum to all. Sides we shared were creamed corn ( to die for), fried green tomatoes (liked), caramel sweet potatoes (Yumo!!) and hash brown potatoes casserole. Tastes like the one I make so nothing special but it was good. Our food came out super fast but then it slowed waaaaay down on closing out our bill. Good place for southern comfort food!
Can't run a concert event to save their lives. Terrible organization and infrastructure. Staff lied about tickets to keep everyone there then turned over a hundred away empty handed.
Hands down best food in Nashville! I would rev comment this to anybody. A little higher price point, but the experience and quality food it so worth it!!!

I went to City Winery for the first time last night and it was a good time. Parking, as others have noted, is a mess. Uber/Lyft if you can. 

We went to a concert, and it was great. The artist (Ben Sollee) was fantastic as expected, and the venue offered an intimate feel and decent acoustics. (It is no Ryman, but I thought the sound was full and robust). Since the concert was not sold out we ended up with a table to ourselves, but you will usually be sitting directly across or next to strangers. You get to pick your seats when you book so you will know what you are walking into. 

The doors open about 2 hours before the show to allow for dinner service, but you can order food and drinks throughout the show, so don't feel like you must get there early. The staff did a great job of being incognito throughout the show. Our server was responsible for several tables, and he managed it well. I would expect they increase staffing if the tables are full. If not, service would have been terrible, this way, it was as attentive as you would hope for during a show. 

I had a glass of wine - Malbec - it was good. Nothing I can't live without. The food was ok. We got the Frites, Hummus, and Margarita Flatbread. Of the 3, the flatbread was the best. The others were non-impactful. Not bad, not particularly good. The prices are pretty high for what you get. For the above mentioned items and a coke it set us back nearly $60 (including the tip)

The chairs are not comfortable. I wished I was an old lady at a football game that brings along her seat cushion.

The concept is cool, the ambiance is great, the wine is pretty good, and the service was decent. I would attend concert here again. Next time I will eat prior to getting there and have a glass of wine at the show.

Stopped into Bavarian Bierhaus while visiting Nashville's Opry Mills Mall. If you are looking for a festive atmosphere for German beer - this is a good spot. If you are looking for really good German food, maybe not so much. Hubs liked his beer & sausage and that was about the only thing that felt just right. The other things we ordered just were a bit lackluster. Perhaps we didn't order "well" but that's our visit. 

Noting my child has food allergies I often visit/preview restaurants & menus prior to dining. The hostesses were beyond welcoming and confirmed we could find something for my son to eat. I will say his allergies are a bit difficult so most "normal" restaurants are not safe for him. After discussing again with our very nice & understanding waitress it was deemed that they didn't actually have as much food for my son as hoped - Gluten free burger & fries was the final choice we went with. It arrived at the table with what appeared to be a normal bun, so I asked if it was the gluten free version and it wasn't. Then they made him a new burger with no bun as they didn't have a gluten free option after all. The fries were deemed unsafe as well so despite my attempts to be prepared and find food for my son, he had a hamburger patty only for lunch. Obviously, this was disappointing to us. 

I gave them a 3 for the very kind staff they employed, atmosphere & beer but I personally was disappointed.

Stumbled upon this place after hitting up Yelp for a new place to try... I was I M P R E S S E D!

Entering into the restaurant, it felt as if I was entering into a beer hall in Munich. The atmosphere was so open and inviting. The menu features traditional German dishes. I tried the Schweinebraten, which is a pork roast. The meat was savory and the bier gravy was heavenly. The red cabbage reminded my wife of the recipe that her Oma used to make, it was amazing!

If you are looking for a truly German experience stateside-- or just comfort food, Nashville has it here! 

Oh, and beer??? Yeah... they got that too! :)

Maybe German food just isn't my thing, but I just didn't like any of it here. Was with a large group attending a conference nearby. Buffet had brats and kraut and pork schnitzel plus sides. It was all bland and over cooked. Ambiance and wait staff were awesome and there's fun little German market with lots of goodies near the entrance, worthy of a two vs one star despite the food.

Fried green tomatoes are excellent.  
Pork is really, really good, as are the biscuits.  Catfish is pretty good.  
Chicken was a bit dry.  
Waitress was friendly and accommodating.  
Overall positive experience.

This place blows. 
 
First, the sound is terrible.  How do you open a music venue in Music City and not take the acoustics into consideration?

Second, the management was completely rude.  The details are a dizzying display of childish manipulation not worth my time attempting to explain but infuriating enough to send me here in the hopes of sparing potential patrons the same treatment. 

Third, the valet asked me to find the drivers of cars who hadn't returned to claim their keys. A move the management appeared to endorse.  It was late and said drivers were no longer at the venue, a suggestion I made to him before going back in to retrieve my purse and husband who had just performed.  This request came after paying $7.00 for parking plus $10 in tips.  I'm thinking for $17 you can find out for yourself and chalk it up as not your customer's job.  I was there as loving supporting spouse, period, end of responsibility.

Musicians, if you are coming to Nashville, play 3rd and Lindsley, it's a bigger venue and it sounds better.  Spare yourself and your loved ones the headache.

Biscuits. You sit down and get biscuits. And once those biscuits are gone, you get more biscuits. How many biscuits consumed in one sitting could be considered obscene? I didn't care. Those biscuits were damn good. 

I kind of want to stop it there, but the rest was so good too, so I'll tell you about it. When I drove up, I just knew it would be good. There was a wait, but it went fast and when it was over, I was sitting at a table, with a plate of biscuits, strawberry, apricot, and blackberry preserves. Having eaten 2 of the biscuits before I had even started looking at the menu, I decided that an egg white omelet was in order, you know, just for balance. Of course, to throw it off again, I ordered a side of bacon. The omelet was superb and the bacon, thick and crispy. And at Loveless, an order is 5 slices. FIVE. And of course, there were more biscuits.

My waitress was awesome and friendly, as was everyone I encountered there. The atmosphere was nice and homey, with some groovy art on the walls. The memorial to the biscuit lady was my favorite. And they have a good, roomy handicapped stall in the bathroom. I like to mention this when it's true.

Go to Loveless. You will like it. I liked it. And now I'm really, really sad that I don't live anywhere near it. Although my weigh watchers points are OK with that part.

City Winery should stick with its namesake-wine. Their attempt at brunch was lackluster, uninspired, and left our party disappointed. City winery has obviously put a great deal of thought into its role as a wine bar, but brunch was clearly an afterthought that has yet to grow to maturity.  Nashville has such a great culinary community that we were sad we wasted Sunday brunch here.

Service- disorganized and confused. Two servers (one may have been the manager) approached us to take our drink order, and neither was very timely about it. Both food and drinks took a long time to order and come out.  The glass bottles of water on the table warmed quickly in the sun, and the server refilled the water only at our specific request.  Patio service seemed to be an afterthought.

Drinks- the spicy Bloody Mary is vibrant, but the glass was tiny and filled with ice, which made the $9 price tag a shock.

Food- when we first sat, we asked the waiter/manager what jumped out on the menu.  His response seemed to be that brunch was a way to let people try the food without the price tag of dinner.   His response made sense when the food came out much later.  Steak and eggs were well prepared, but with small portions and so poorly plated it was more akin to white plate Waffle House. Flavor was lacking, prompting the table to wonder whether salt/pepper shakers should have been on the table. Shrimp and grits were filling, but tails were detached and mixed in with the grits, which required some digging. All in all, at $18 and $15, respectively, the price was far higher than the value.

Ambience- great patio, and the venue is beautiful, but didn't meet its potential to entertain. For Nashville, we were amazed there wasn't some form of music, live or otherwise. Thankfully, the next door Rescue Mission had a live band.

Overall, city winery seems a classy place to grab a bottle of wine and cheese plate.  Otherwise, best avoided.

We were really looking forward to eating at the Loveless Café after reading all of the website and history of the food and heritage of the café. We thought we were going to eat such good food. Unfortunately, we did not. The food was just average. the biscuits were under cooked and not individually cut - but cut in one large square pan. The flavor of the biscuits were just average. The fried chicken was over cooked and dull in flavor. The blackberry preserves had no flavor at all. The pancakes were very dry and hard on the exteriors. Even though we knew it would be crazy busy, we were not willing to wait the 2 hour delay for breakfast, so we ordered it to go and ate I outside on a picnic bench. About 50 percent of the customers did this. To us, it was not worth it. We will not go back. I did buy a coffee mug in the gift shop. To be honest, this is nothing more than a tourist trap. Maybe when it was owned by just a couple who put genuine effort into the food, it was great. But now that a few high powered business owners have it, it seems to be just a marketing ploy to make "them" a lot of money at the expense of the customers and employees. Sad
One of my favorite spots in Nashville - a bit kitschy, but lots of fun and delicious home cooking.  Always a long wait, but also lot of things to keep you occupied in the process.

Loveless Cafe is the perfect place to go for a traditional southern meal and a nice walk around the grounds. I had fried chicken with eggs. My girlfriend had the breakfast bowl. Excellent meal with super friendly service. And the biscuits are delicious. The gift shop and apparel shop are also very fun to check out. Loveless is a great spot to walk around and check out some cool trinkets after a delicious meal.

Stopped in here for dinner with the family after a night of shopping. We are part-German, so we were excited to try the cuisine of our ancestors. This restaurant was all German including the long tables, and the attire the servers wore. All of the workers were friendly and helpful with the menu, which was partly in German.

Food was pretty decent. I had the schnitzel, which turned out to be huge, however, I was disappointed that it tasted like chicken parm. I love chicken parm, but I was hoping pork schnitzel would have a different taste! My brother & parents all tried different wursts's. They all had leftovers because the plates were filling especially with the yummy sides! 

This meal was a good change from some of the Southern food we had been eating the past week. I would definitely recommend it if looking for a change of taste.

I'm not a biscuit lover. I think they're usually too dry and crumbly, and I'd prefer a croissant or dinner roll any day. But I figured I might as well try again because this place was so highly regarded, and I was blown away. I was presented with delightful biscuits, the most delicious preserves (blackberry was my favorite), perfectly soft scrambled eggs, a giant heaping of barbecue pork, and the cheesiest, creamiest hash brown casserole. It's easy to make mediocre breakfast food; it's rare to find a place that does so many things so well.

My family enjoyed breakfast. We arrived early, 8:30am, and did not have to wait to be seated. We ordered a family breakfast. It was all you could eat, homemade biscuits, jam, scrambled eggs, gravy, sausage, bacon, and fresh fruit. The service was wonderful. The food was incredible. Totally worth the drive and would definitely return!

This is a great venue for a concert but the food leaves a lot to be desired.   I've been there a few times, and the risotto balls are good but everything else I've tried is unimpressive and expensive.   I'll definitely come back for a concert but I will dine elsewhere beforehand.

I understand why this place is an institution.  The ambiance screams southern cooking and in my opinion Southern Cooking is the best cooking.

I want to love this place because it has so many elements to love it, but the food in general is BLAH.  

My friend and I ordered the "legendary" fried chicken and a country fried steak to split.  We had a slew of side dishes to try and the only thing we both agreed on was the creamed corn was amazing.  

The chicken was no better than what I could buy pre made at a Publix and the white gravy for the Country fried steak had no flavor.  The mac and cheese was basic and the hash browns were OK.   Other than the creamed corn, my side salad was the best thing I had.  

The pie was average at best

Prices are great, service was phenomenal,  and the overall feel of this place is sooooo cool.  Like I said, I want to love it, but the food has to get better.

Opted to grab lunch here on a Wednesday as we travelled from Jackson TN back to Greenville SC.

It was worth the detour.

Biscuits were yummmmmy, as were the preserves.
I had the country fried steak, green beans and corn and there was more than I could eat. Huge country fried chicken piece!

My wife had the biscuit sampler and loved that too.

Shame we didn't save room for cobbler though...

It comes as no surprise that over 1000 reviewers have posted positive comments, but I'm not sure why anyone would post a negative one.

Long wait? Sure, anything worth having is worth waiting for...  We waited about 30 minutes and arrived around 11:30.  Service was fast once we were seated.

Edited: we got ahold of the manager and he was amazing! They made an effort to still give us the wine tour, which was the best tour that I have ever been on. Evan was so knowledgeable and fun. We learned so much. The wine was the best and most beautiful wine I've ever had and the food was delicious.  I was thoroughly impressed with the service last night along with everything else. 

They beyond redeemed themselves, and I would gladly go back to this place and recommend it to everyone I know!! 

I, for one, will definitely be going back!! Thank you so much to everyone at city winery last night. You made it a great night for us all! 



Old no longer relevant review:

If I could give this place 0 stars for service I would. 

My mother and aunt are coming into town to visit me and city winery has always been on our list of places to go in Nashville. 

A month ago we made reservations for dinner here, but they called and said they rented the whole place out and needed to cancel our reservations. Totally understandable. So we rescheduled and made a winery tour the next day. Well they just called and cancelled that for the exact same reason. 

Two cancellations was already a let down, but beyond that, the staff was incredibly rude and condescending on the phone, which makes me not even want to go to this place at all. They are not trying to accommodate us for their doings at all (and haven't reimbursed us for the cancelled tour) If you are going to cancel multiple reservations for paying customers then you need to have public and private times separate and only allow for reservations at those times. This is getting ridiculous. 


We're supposed to go to a concert there that night, but will they cancel that too?

Ehhhh... it was ok...super disappointed in the pretzels....hard as rocks...cheese dip was very watery and lacked flavor. My meal came with mashed potatoes that were barely warm. The waiter seemed like any enthusiasm would kill him... All that said I would go back to try other items...maybe we just hit a bad day...              Update: owner, Bob, read my review and was extremely nice and kind in ensuring that our next visit was much improved. He even explained what he had planned to do with mashed potatoes complaints etc..also different recommendation in place of the bier cheese... it was greatly appreciated... in light of the quick response and kind email I am bumping this review up....

There are not enough words to describe how amazing this place is. Brunch was outstanding. The service was great. And the food is delicious. We had the fork and knife BLT and the roast beef. So good. The mimosa bar at your table is also great. Check this place out!

Delicious! The biscuits are amazing, but the peach preserves are really what keep you coming back. I always get a vegetable plate, and from fried green tomatoes to creamed corn to mac and cheese, Loveless does it very very well. There can be a long wait, but when I visit at nontraditional times (like Tuesday night at 7:45), I am usually seated immediately.

Great homecooked meals, especially desserts. The wait can be long, especially on weekends and the parking can be challenging, but its a must-try if visiting Nashville. In short, its a better version of Cracker Barrel, but with lots of history and memorabilia.

My husband, friend and I got to enjoy this restaurant as part of the Yelp Elite event. We had never been to a restaurant like it, but I would definitely go again. We tried the sausages with sauerkraut, and delicious pretzels with beer cheese. I'm not a huge beer fan, but I did give a couple of the flavors a try! My favorite was the Hefeweizen. They have a huge stage in the middle of the restaurant where they play music and get people up to dance! It was a blast to watch; we even got to watch a stein holding competition! While we didn't really deal with the service, one of the owners was around for the event and he was super friendly! To top it all off, Kellie Pickler and Ben (from the tv talk show Pickler and Ben) were there and took pictures with us!

Delicious Southern Comfort Food!!!
Biscuits and Jam YUM!
The sampler plate was very good with three choices of meat and two sides.. Enough to take leftovers home to enjoy a second time.
The fried catfish and fried chicken are not to greasy. The meatloaf is as good as what Mamma makes and that is pretty darn good!!!

I come to Nashville every few months and have never been here. Until now! The biscuits did not disappoint. I got the southern omelette which was good and my fiancé got the country fried steak which was great. I must say the biscuits are the big hit. It is a little bit of a drive out of downtown but if you can make it I highly recommend it! Oh and our server Diane was just the nicest woman alive.

Amazing service and awesome food! Mike, Sydney, Hayley, and Daryl were absolutely wonderful and accommodating. I can't say enough good things about City Winery and their amazing staff. Food was great and the drinks were great. Came here for brunch, and I'm still here! Mimosas were great!

Thank you, Cass for turning on the lights for my selfie!

We had a good time - take it for what it is, beer beer beer and decent food, live music, just fun , if you're waiting for some kind of culinary experience that's not the point - staff was friendly and it was a fun place to relax, and did I mention have a beer! .... a little like polka
Can't beat it. Recommended to me so many times I had to try and it did not disappoint! Great for afternoons as it is not nearly as busy. Also had tons of shopping and things to do while you wait

Do not book a party at Loveless!!!  My fiancé and I decided to have our small wedding reception at the Harpeth Room at the Loveless Cafe.  We were unable to reach anyone by phone so we booked by email.  They said they'd get back to us about menus and pricing.  A couple of weeks went by and we didn't hear from the event team.  We tried calling again and left a voicemail.  They emailed us back stating that the Harpeth Room had been booked by someone else.  We called back requesting an explanation and to attempt to salvage our reception.  Instead of calling us back, they emailed us AGAIN stating that all venues on the Loveless property were now booked for the evening of our wedding.  Since we had no luck contacting anyone by phone, my fiancé went to the restaurant.  The managers apologized for the mistake and told us we could rebook for another night and that they would compensate by giving us a free dessert.  Like a free dessert would sufficiently compensate for their poor communication and incompetent event booking team.  The food is tasty, but you will wait for hours to get a table.  And clearly, don't send out invitations saying you're having a party at the Loveless Cafe because they will probably cancel your event with mere days to spare.

Not just a restaurant, but an experience! Played corn hole and shopped in the 2 stores while waiting for our table. You bite into a biscuit and it tastes like butter, it's amazing. The pulled pork platter was enough for me to eat dinner for a week. I got mashed potatoes and mac&cheese for my sides and they were great but I tried my sister's creamed corn and wish I had gotten that. It was yummy! Definitely not a place to go if you're on a diet, but it was fun to pig out on vacation :)

Placed a togo order yesterday and the amount of cross contamination in my food was a huge let down. I was unable to eat half of my vegetable plate with globs of chicken salad in my cucumbers and onions. Macaroni and cheese that tasted like perfume was in it? 3 stars b/c my boyfriends fried chicken and hash brown casserole were perfectly fine. 

*Clean up your stations on the line!*

This is my first 5 Star rating!!
The food was amazing. The server (Shalimar) was wonderful! The manager sat down and talked to us! It was a great time!
The only negative is------ I live 1600 miles away

This was my favorite meal during my trip to Nashville! The place is so homey and inviting and the food is to die for. 

We went on Monday for lunch and waited about 20 minutes to be seated. While you wait, you can check out their adorable country store with everything from jams to home decor. As soon as we were seated we got a generous plate of biscuits and jam, and these were the best biscuits I've ever had! Even better than a certain hyped up biscuit spot in Nashville.

I decided to order the meatloaf, and you get two sides with each entree. Its hard to make a decision since all the sides sound awesome, but I went with caramel sweet potatoes and fried green tomatoes. Everything was so fantastic. The meatloaf portion was easily enough for two people and it was moist and had a tasty sauce. The sides were excellent as well... along with my own choices, I loved my friend's cheesy hash browns.

Despite being so far out of the way in Nashville, this is a must visit spot.

Southern hospitality at its finest. I was hitting Loveless on my way out of Nashville with luggage in tow. The hostess immediately offered to stow my bag behind the counter and then led me to my table. I was then greeted by a helpful and wonderfully friendly waitress. I got coffee and water and she then brought out a plate of biscuits with homemade preserves (blackberry, strawberry, and peach). 

While the entire menu looked amazing, I went with the chicken fried steak, scrambled eggs, and cheesy hash brown casserole. Oh my word, ya'll...one of the best CFS I've ever eaten. It was a huge portion and I only wish I could have boxed it up and brought it on the plane. 

One of the best breakfasts I've had along with amazing staff. I'm glad I got there when I did though because it got packed real fast. The walls are a representation of the Music City. Paintings of musicians and signed headshots abound.
We split a breakfast plate and with the complimentary biscuits where enough to fill us up (2 people). Amazing biscuits!

This had to be the worst jager schnitzel we have ever had. My son & I got the Jager , his with fries & mine with some type of noodles, which neither of use could eat due to them floating in gravy. I could NOT even eat my dinner, the taste literally made me sick, my son did eat 2/3 of his meat & maybe 3 fries that weren't drenched (& that was only because it was almost 4:00 & we had not eaten all day.) NEVER, EVER would I recommend this restaurant. Our waitress acted like it pissed her off, when I called her over & told her to take it back because I just could not eat it, she never once came back & checked on us for refills nor to pick up our payment. The manager did come out & took my $21 meal off & left me a card for a free meal, NO THANK YOU....I don't want your free meal & after waiting 5-10 minutes for our waitress to pick up our payment, I decided to walk to the front & pay when my daughter realized a male worker had literally followed us from our table to the front, I assume to make sure we were paying & not trying to skip out. Very insulting!!!

Efter att ha gjort två stycken återbesök hit vid en ny vistelse 1 1/2 år efter min ursprungliga recension så tycker jag att man har gjort avsevärda förbättringar och finslipat rutinerna här. Det finns t.ex. numera tillräckligt med belysning för att kunna läsa menyn och maten här är riktigt bra nu liksom servicen.

This is my first time visiting the Loveless Cafe. I ordered the sampler plate with BBQ pork, meatloaf, and fried chicken. The meatloaf was good not great, the BBQ pork was just slow cooked pork with BBQ sauce, no smoke flavor whatsoever. The fried chicken was above average. My sides were mac n cheese and the hash brown casserole. The mac n cheese was just a notch above TV dinner fare, and the hash brown casserole was pretty average. What really let me down was the biscuits and preserves. I was dreaming about them on this trip before my visit on this trip. The biscuits were way below average, I might have had a bad batch as the waitress was taking to the table next to me about them and they said they never have seen them like this before. The preserves were below average for the peach and strawberry, but the blackberry were some of the best I've had. 

Overall for the price and hype I was expecting more. I wish I would have had breakfast for dinner as that's one meal that's hard to not hit the mark with. It's cool to say I ate here, but there are much better places in town to frequent. 

The service however was very good. Everybody here was warm and friendly.
Outstanding food and great ambience!  Reminds me of when I lived in Germany, just brighter on the inside. The food is on par with about any restaurant in Deutschland and the price isn't bad at all.

Literally everything I have ever ordered from Loveless Cafe is amazing. I love everything about this place, from the quaint interior to the friendly staff. If I could eat here everyday I would probably be hundreds of pounds over weight. It's that good. If you are ever in Nashville it is worth the drive to eat at Loveless Cafe.

We experienced City Winery last night as a restaurant (dinner) and also venue (concert).  I would probably give the restaurant one star and the venue four stars.

Restaurant was overpriced and underwhelming which is very Nashville-ish these days.  We came here for a 6:45pm dinner reservation before the show.  Parking is either valet or there is a pay lot.  The valet was $6 and the pay lot was a little bit less.  You could probably find street parking and walk, but we chose to do valet.  We ordered the Tour of Meat and Cheeses as an appetizer.  It came with three types of "cured" meats, but two of them were cheap salami.  You can't get that past me because I was a child of the 80's and I was fed that nasty stuff.  I couldn't even touch that salami.  There were three cheeses...one of them was a blue cheese that was pretty good, but extremely salty. One cheese was super mild and creamy, but almost taste-less.  The third was flavored of horseradish...even my cheese loving fiancee left some of that to be thrown away.  Beyond that, the platter was bread / cracker heavy.  They were fine, but the platter was very underwhelming for $30.  We then shared the Pulled Lamb Sandwich.  It was very much like a pulled pork sandwich although they put a large amount of plain old sour cream on it.  I thought that was kind of funny.  Sour cream all over the pulled lamb...?  Picnic-like maybe?  We ordered the Rioja Wine for $12 (pricey) and I like it.  We also ordered the Malbec for $14 (very pricey) and it was not a good Malbec.  Our service was lacking.  Our plates and silverware were pretty used by the time the lamb sandwich came and she asked...hmmm, do you want new plates?  Then she told us to take our silverware and she would take the plates.  We laughed about that...I mean take the silverware and plates and bring us new.  Again, for the prices at this restaurant, we expected better service.  We won't be back to eat here again.

As for the venue...it was very pretty!  It almost looked like it was set up for a wedding.  It was also large and spacious.  The service back there was MUCH better than in the dining room.  They were attentive and professional with us.  The only weird thing was that the band had big sound issues and the band seemed very unhappy about that.  The sound person just couldn't get it fixed and the band seemed frustrated.  I would come to another show here.

No more salami!

Second visit here, on a Sunday morning; waited 1.5 hours for a table for 2. Honestly the food is tasty but not worth the wait. It's a cool little country restaurant with a campus of different shops and such but the tourist hype has made this place overrated. 
Offers your typical breakfast items, but they're famous for their fresh biscuits and jams. The French toast was bland, and the Garden Omelet was also bland but had a nice assortment of vegetables on the filling. The hashbrown casserole was very tasty and the biscuits were great, as usual. Prices are reasonable. 
Would return, but only if no wait.
Best German food I have had! And being from Chicago I know good food! Kathleen our server was fantastic!

We were surprised the prices on our receipt from our drinks was more expensive than the written prices on the menu. We were informed the menu was an outdated version without old prices. Um...then update the menu? Or at least give verbal warning? Or even just cross out the old prices and write in the new ones? Absolutely made me feel like City Winery banks on people being too tipsy or drunk to notice what they're being charged for isn't the same as what's written on the menu- or that they know you won't argue over the difference while you're awkwardly getting your ticket while someone is performing. If they can get even a few extra dollars out of each person and know people aren't likely to be brave enough to make a scene at a concert over that, that's a lot of quick profit for the venue. Judging by a lot of similar reviews about food being over priced, service slow and not great I wouldn't come here just for the restaurant, and if I do see a show again here I wouldn't feel comfortable ordering from the menu. Surely with their prices they can afford to print new menus. Jeez.

The venue is a bit awkward in itself. Very cramped with not much room between tables or seats. It's not a very big space yet it doesn't feel intimate. The sound is good but it really feels like watching a show in a hotel ballroom. The neighborhood is historically a bad and sketchy area- definitely don't park anywhere around back "for free" or even near the street in the paid lot. The venue definitely feels out of place in the neighborhood; I always though it was an odd location for a more upscale venue(literally right between the greyhound station and a rescue mission...)

Believe the hype!! Believe the hype!! Believe the hype!! It can be a bit of a drive because of its location but there's other attractions near by such as Percy Warner Park that you can make a fulfilling day. Also, be mindful that you may have to wait in line but it's worth it. There's different areas you can visit to kill time or you can sit in the car. Treat yourself nonetheless!

Went to City Winery for the second time, I requested Kimberly because she was our server on my first visit. She DID NOT DISAPPOINT.... Kimberly was just as amazing as the first time that I had her! I was so excited when they told me she was working & hoped to receive the same level of service and WE DID! Great job Kimberly....you are truly a sweetheart & very knowledgeable! I will have to say again....she is the best server I've ever had in Nashville!!! I will be back and I hope Kimberly is working!!?

Hadn't been to the Loveless in 10 years or so and was glad to find the food is still great.  We arrived around 4:30 on a Saturday night and only had a 10 minute wait.  We spent the wait time browsing in the General Store gift shop and found many unique items tempting to purchase.  The wireless buzzer system allows you to roam the grounds while waiting.

My favorite meal of the day is breakfast and the Loveless is ready all day.  The biscuits deserve all the hype and with the jams and preserves and real butter are lovely together.   

Had never traveled to Nashville North on the Natchez Trace before but was tickled to find the Loveless is on Hwy 100 just off a Natchez Trace exit at its terminus or start depending on which direction you are going.

This place is the Most amazing and authentic southern food experience I have had and Nash Ville being there for one week

Came for lunch on a weekday and luckily was able to make reservations therefore no weight and the even seated us a little bit early

We each ordered the half fried chicken but opted for different sides.  The chicken is on point perfectly fried perfectly seasoned the sides were piping hot amazing the service is quick and hospitable with that perfect southern twang accent

My only regret is that I did not have enough room for dessert but we finished all of the biscuits and the amazing jams that accompanied them and these biscuits will change your life

The property has ample parking which was great and additional buildings were you can do some shopping for apparel accessories some kitchen stuff as well as their jams

I stopped supporting this place when they refused to let the band I was on tour with play at the venue. Simply for having the word "killed" in their name. Yep you're reading this right. They refused to pay our guarantee because of this. Oh, but remember that time they let DONALD TRUMP come here and have one of his rallies a few months back? Lol. It's actually true. So then, They let a bigot come and spew hatred and that's ok with them! Unbelievably hypocritical from a "Christian" establishment... 0 stars if possible.

To those well-read, methinks you've seen
the verse below with eyes quite keen;
and knowing whilst your vist next,
why City Winery makes Yelp's best.

"A Book of Verses underneath the
Bough,
A Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread -- and 
Thou"
     (These are the first 2 lines of a Quatrain by Edward Fitzgerald on Omar Khayyam's "Rubaiyat")

In our recent visit to City Winery we had all the above and more. Well, to be honest we had just one glass of wine, a delightful, light "house" Chardonnay. And the bread in this instance was replaced by a -- perhaps too well toasted--Lavash. Yet, while brittle in texture, it was fine in flavor when used to convey the sweet, creamy, "Smashed Beet and Tahini Dip" from plate to palate. And while the dip was creatively served in a tall mug, that made it difficult to scoop and serve, so-to-speak. Using my table knife was clumsy, but it accomplished the task at hand.

(Suggestion for manager: the addition of a butter knife or other utensil for diners to self-serve or share this thick and luscious starter would be very helpful.)

Our second shared item from the enticing menu was a perfect size for us: "Wild Mushrom, Goat Cheese, Béchamel, and Arugula Flat Bread." Not only did it satisfy in size, it wowed with its earthy, barely toothy mushrooms and slightly bitter bite of Arugula, mingled with the creamy and temperate Béchamel "mother" sauce. Simply a delight!

We chose to come early - just after the doors opened - out of respect for the performers whose show we did not want to disrupt with eating, clanking of silverware, and the like. But, just as the venue advertises, others who chose to continue eating during the performance were also considerate, paying close attention to the artists all-the while being served by a very polite, conscientious, unobtrusive wait staff. Kudos to the severs for their restrained, yet efficient, service.

Ostensibly, we came for the show in the Lounge, an intimate, well-staffed upstairs venue. The music of Kat Edmondson, a creative, gifted singer-songwriter and her band was a pleasing, well balanced evening of jazz, 95% Kat's original songs that touched on several styles of jazz plus blues. House acoustics were near-perfect and the energy level nicely sustained.

Thus, if you seek a venue
To sate your desiderata
'Check in' at City Winery
A place to Yelp; you gotta!

Be sure to check out their upcoming performers at both The Barrel Room Restaurant (downstairs venue) and Lounge (upstairs). The line-up is amazing!

Our server Kimberly was outstanding!! She knew her wines and was on top of the cuisine!!
You have to try the risotto balls, out of this world!! Lamb ribs were incredible but the roasted Brussels sprouts "stole the show"...Feta cheese on sprouts?!?! WOW!!!

Plenty to do during our 1:15 hour wait so it went fast. Preserves are very good! Biscuits small which is a good thing because I probably would have eaten the same number!! We Had the country fried steak, pork chops, and country ham. Eggs over easy cooked to perfection! All were outstanding! Bloody Mary also good. Grits different from what we usually get in SC but still very good!  Only thing I didn't like was the casual way the waiter addressed us: called the men (old enough to be his dads) "bro" and the ladies "girl..." as in, "hey, girl, what would you like." Would have preferred "ma'am" and "sir." But that doesn't seem to be unusual in restaurants today. But otherwise the service was good.

Why would the owners put all that money into a gorgeous venue with incredible sound and ruin it with horrible parking. You have no real choice but valet which is $7.  That would be have been fine with me except I waited 45 minutes and they were surly to me.   Let's hope they are still having growing pains.

Great sausage and German sides. Everything was delicious. Large beer selection. Portions are generous. Menu is full of selections and options. Fast and friendly service. Restaurant includes a small German market full of goodies. A rare find for a restaurant attached to a mall.

Very very good German food and beer. Very nice gifts reasonably priced out front. Very authentic looking beer haul that makes you feel like you are in Bavaria. Entertainment never made it to the stage while we were there. It would have been a 5 star with a little music.
Moved to 5 stars from 4. Reason - obviously they care. I got a prompt response from my review and honestly the place deserves 5 stars. I'll watch their calendar and catch a time with some live music!

From the description, we thought this would of been a great hangout for some wine and good, but once again seems the trend in Nashville over priced below average food.

The cheese and charcuterie plates were very mediocre and tasted very cheaply. And the wine was so so.  I do not mind paying a little extra as long as the food is good.

This place is nice on the inside but honestly the food needs to improve.

I know this place is known for amazing shows, but the restaurant stole my heart yesterday. I had a birthday reservation for 20 ppl. #1 they gave us a beautiful private room. #2 The staff was so amazing and patient as people trickled in due to the long valet line. #3 The variety of food. In my group I have vegetarians, vegans, vegetarians and gluten free. They modified dishes and more to ensure that everyone had a delicious satisfying meal. This place was AMAZING to me and my family. We will definitely be back

Delicious German food and great beer! Fun ambiance of the restaurant with live music. We sat at the bar, the restaurant was very busy and the service was great. Even being packed with people, the bartender got us our beers and food quickly.
Ate here for breakfast. Come early or prepare for a wait. We waited almost 2 hours. Service was fast friendly. Tons of choices serve both breakfast and dinner all day long. You'll leave full.
Excellent authentic German food. Even our waiter had a heavy German accent. The pretzel is amazing as are all of the sausages. The grapefruit Hefeweizen is delicious.

We went here on a Sunday and it was quite a long wait at 11 AM, but it was a neat area to check out  with a bunch of souvenir shops (I bought a ton of bbq sauce). The food was pretty good as well! Mine wasn't very picturesque because I just got eggs, hashbrown casserole and cheese grits.. but the person I was with got this cool biscuit sampler/sandwich thing, which he loved! If you're wanting to check out the place, the hashbrown casserole dish was suuuper yummy! Wish there was more of it! Overall, I'm glad we checked it out, and yes I loved the hashbrowns, but I'm not sure it was worth the long drive from Nashville and the wait.

The loveless cafe was lovely! We had the chicken waffle and garden omelet with a side of hash browns and they were amazing. Waffle was delicious, fried chicken was perfectly cooked, and the biscuits are to die for. They have a bunch of cute little gift shops and a shops where you can buy there homemade preserves and biscuit mix. Such a cute little country cafe.

Absolutely worth the wait time! Went in for the famously delicious biscuits (which they were scrumptious), but fell in love with everything we ate. Most tender pulled pork (try the BBQ sandwich), crispiest fried chicken (try the chicken & waffles), and melt in your mouth side dishes (hash brown casserole and Mac & cheese are musts). We ended up so stuffed that we had tons of leftovers which tasted just as good the 2nd time (we even just heated them up at our campsite that night over the fire - so good!). The wait staff was friendly and attentive. Just good ole' fashioned southern comfort! You can also explore the gift shops while you wait.

Really bad service on all fronts. Hostess, waitresses, and the manager. The most infuriating part was seeing the manager talk to other co workers casually in front of the kitchen while we were waiting for him to assist us..
Classic breakfast and complimentary biscuits & jam. Yummm. Super quick seating for a busy place! No complaints.

Pretty solid breakfast joint though not extraordinary given all the fanfare.   You'll wait a long time so be prepared. There isn't a place close by that sells adult beverages. Maybe bring a flask or a cooler to help pass time. Don't have a group of more than 4 to get seated faster.

Dont worry about the wait. They told us 1.5 hrs but we only waited 45 min. COMPLETELY worth the wait!!! The biscuits are to die for. We ordered the chicken fried steak with hash brown casserole. It was amazing!!!
Me and my wife came to Nashville for the country music. What a great surprise. Good food and tons of fun. The band was great. You won't be disappointed.

I'd give it a 4.33 stars if I could.  Yams we're great, enjoyed the biscuits and preserves, and the meat sampler was pretty solid across the board.  Didn't have room for dessert with all the biscuits I ate but it was pretty good overall.  Had a bit of a wait though so don't come starving.

This was by far the best breakfast that I have ever had. On our way out of Nashville we hit this place for some fuel for the long day of driving. There was a bit of a wait, but they give you a pager and you can go look at the shops on the property while you wait. Once we were seated, our waiter came by and was really friendly. He recommended a couple of things and I went with his recommendation of BBQ pulled pork and eggs. It was delicious! It came with a choice of sides and I had the hash brown casserole which were the best hash browns that I have ever had. My husband thought the biscuits and gravy were the best he's ever had as well. My only regret was that I didn't have enough room to have a piece of pie. They looked really good in the case. You can buy a half or whole pie to go as well. The shops on the property have a lot of their products for sale - jams, sauces, bacon, syrup, honey, etc. they also have a bunch of novelty items and souvenirs. A nice way to get breakfast and shopping out of the way.

I struggled when deciding between 3 or 4 stars but ultimately decided on 4 since it was a good meal but not mind blowing like all the reviews hyped it up to be. It is a solid 3.5 stars.

The atmosphere is homey and very welcoming. The restaurant looks like a repurposed home and I love that cozy feeling. Our waiter was also attentive and nice.

The food was underwhelming for me though. Which is really disappointing and sad for me. I ordered the Southern Sampler Supper Plate with catfish, fried chicken, and pulled pork, it came with creamed corn, mashed potatoes and hush puppies. The chicken was fried too much and just thrown on my plate that the skin was already half falling off. There was not much seasoning on it which surprised me. The cat fish was fried well but also not much flavor or seasoning. The pulled pork was also not tender or juicy like I was expecting. I did really enjoy the sides though! The gravy that accompanied the mashed potatoes was SO good. And of course the biscuits were deliciously buttery and fluffy. We also ordered the country fried steak, which was huge! It was tender but didn't have much seasoning on the breading. The white gravy that went on top was good! And again the sides were good, the hash brown casserole was good!

Overall the meal was good but I'm not sure if I would come back. The only thing from the meal I would come back for are the biscuits and homemade jams. Considering the glowing reviews my expectations were very high and the food was underwhelming for me.

Another must stop destination for those wanting to have the Nashville experience.  It is exactly how you would picture the South and it is situated in some incredibly beautiful country.   The service was friendly and the menu full of heavy Southern favorites.  

At the suggestion of the waiter I tried the Chicken and Waffles.  It was fairly good but within minutes I was down for the count and searching for the nearest hammock.  I've never understood that dish.  The biscuits were as good as advertised.  They were plentiful and came with plenty of jam options.
Not a good place for gay people and their friends: http://www.queerty.com/nashville-club-fires-staffer-wearing-i-support-same-sex-marriage-shirt-20130122/
Great place to eat.  Have eaten here several times and the food is always enjoyable.  The wait to be seated can be long at times but it is worth it.  Highly recommended.

Went here for the 10am Easter Brunch. Probably the worst experience I have had. The buffet was cold, and I mean cold. There was no coffee for the first 30 minutes, and when it arrived it was self service in paper cups. My wife ordered a tea and since it wasn't part of the menu it was $3 on top of the $42.  Mimosa's were $8.50 and were horrible. The desserts weren't marked and anyone with a nut allergy couldn't tell what was what.  The manager could care less about anything. Will definitely not return or recommend to anyone.
Best tap water in all of Nashville! I was very impressed by their ice to water ratio. It was SO worth the 50 cents!! I bought 10! :)
Loveless cafe has some of the best biscuits ever and there blackberry jelly is superb. Their food in general is amazing. It just taste great

Our server was a little slow, but she's only one person so I won't condemn the entire staff. Besides the long wait, our food was just ok. I've had better German potato salad, and the pretzel was really over rated. I was not expecting it to be so hard, so that threw me off. The jalapeño cheddarwurs is really delicious.

Let me say first thing that my husband is German, as in German, just came to America last year, German. So he is an expert on German cuisine, as I am merely a newbie, only really being aware of what it entails within the last two years. As with most German restaurants, the food is mostly from the Southern region which is Bavaria (look at me learning all this stuff). But of all of the places we've been, this one has been the most accurate (and delicious). The inside looks like an Oktoberfest hall and the staff wears dirndls and lederhosen. The food was delicious and authentic, though I'm sorely disappointed in the meat and cheese platter appetizer, which was a sad wilted miniature array of American cheeses and meats. Everything else, though, delish! They even have a beer stein club for those die hard fans. They also have a great gift shop, including some German groceries like spices and my FAVORITE chocolate. For an authentic American-ized version of an old time German classic, this place is your best bet!

Such a historic place around Nashville. First time there and it was a great experience. I loved seeing all the autographs from celebrities on the wall. Only downside to Loveless is the wait. My party of 3 arrived at 2pm and still had to wait an hour. The food and service was still excellent though once we were seated! Biscuits were delicious as well as the jellies. I got fried chicken and scrambled eggs with hash brown casserole and it was so amazing. The chicken was fried to perfection and felt like I was at home. A must when you visit Nashville!
First time at the Nashville location. I saw Anthony David perform. Everything was great atmosphere, service, our seats  and of course the artist! Kudos!

how do I even begin to review the best breakfast of my life. it was so good we went back during our trip. something we never do since we want to always check out and explore everything, not do a repeat. I found this place when searching best breakfast in Nashville and I thought it'd be our first stop after we landed, picked up our rental car and headed on the gorgeous drive over. shocked to find out there was a wait on a Friday early afternoon but it was less then the 45 minutes they said it'd be. we walked around and investigated the stores plus it was a gorgeous day out so it was fine. a wait is never a bad thing, means they are doing something right! 

it was so good, so delicious we came back Monday morning! no wait since we came around 8 am this time. just as delicious as the first time. first time I ever had grits and I am now spoiled for life.

Huge tourist-oriented restaurant near the Grand Ole Opry. The various sausages were decent, but the huge pork shank was a bit of a disappointment. The service was efficient enough, though. Prices were reasonable

We had a lovely Sunday Brunch meal at the Loveless recently. Our server Evan was great and our meal overall was very good. We started off with their great coffee and the famous biscuits with preserves. The biscuits are light and fluffy and lived up to the hype. I opted for the blueberry pancakes and eggs and my wife had the Music City Platter which consisted of French toast, eggs and hashbrown casserole. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal and recommend this Nashville establishment.

Biscuits were phenomenal, and they keep 'em coming! Fried chicken was absolutely delicious too, though 2 pieces of the dark meat was enough for me as I still preferred the biscuits with their peach jam. Ice tea is nothing special though.

Bought peach jam to go and their biscuit mix - I'd definitely go back if I'm ever in town!

This is an absolutely fantastic place! The food was amazing, and our server Owen was the best! All of his recommendations were on point, and he made us feel so welcome. I would recommend the Loveless Cafe 110%

Biscuits? Amazing. Food? Tasty. Service? Unbelievable. Our waitress Kirsten was the absolute epitome of southern hospitality and we had an incredible night especially because of her outstanding service. I will definitely be making my way back here if I'm ever in Nashville again!!!

From our table, I could see the biscuits coming out of the oven, removed from baking sheets and almost immediately put on plates for serving. They come to the table piping hot with little plastic containers of goodness called jam. Real butter on the table.

But this place is not really worth the hype. It's a diner. Cutsie diner, but a diner. Portions are huge, staff is friendly and fast. 

To take your mind off the sometimes long wait, you can mosey over to their shops to look at the same stuff with different logos you see in any souvenir shop in the US. Again, cutsie, but fairly high quality.

Southern comfort food at its best. Laid back and friendly. Great local eats. Do not pass this place up if traveling to Nashville. They are often busy so plan on waiting upwards to an hour. That said, the have corn hole on site. That's right, corn hole! Also, if they had a nice family friendly bar that would really help with the wait as well. Lastly, when you order grits ask for pimento cheese in them...you WON'T regret it!
Wonderful restaurant. So much food. Biscuits are the best. Great recommendation from our son.

Yes, the biscuits here are consistently tasty. No one disputes this fact. But is there a biscuit on the planet that is worth a drive out to the boonies followed by a 2 hour wait to eat what is essentially a glorified, overpriced Cracker Barrel meal? I probably won't do it again, but the tourists seem to think so. Aside from the biscuits, the food and service were decent, but certainly not worth raving about.

I had some friends visiting and decided to try city winery's brunch. 1) parking is confusing 2) our server was barely present. 5 people to eat brunch took over 2 hours. Food wasn't fabulous, I had a French toast which was bland and soggy. The drinks were decent but I wish there was more variety. Probably not my go to for brunch, but enjoyed our afternoon.

If you are in the area you have to stop. Food is fresh and hot. Once you sit down they bring you some hot biscuits with some fruit preserves. The peach preserves are delicious. I ordered the pulled pork sandwich. My husband had the biscuits and gravy. My daughter got the chicken tenders. The portions are huge. We took a lot of food home. Everything was delicious. Service was fast and friendly.

The loveless cafe is a fabulous restaurant for real southern soul food. I went here for dinner and I got the Southern sampler platter with fried catfish, fried chicken, and bbq pork(my choice of 3 meats). It also came with 2 sides and I highly recommend getting the hash brown casserole and the creamed corn. The portion sizes are very large and be sure to come hungry because there are free hot biscuits with homemade jams. Personally, the peach jam is my favorite. The only downside about the loveless cafe is that there is usually about a half hour wait, but once you settle down at the table, it'll be worth the wait!

couple of Canadians down to nashville for the weekend. We heard of loveless cafe after  reading many yelp reviews and hearing it is an institution we needed to go.
So too start off be prepared to spend your entire day waiting on lousy biscuits. Apparently supposed to be the best biscuits ever but we were quite disappointed in them.
We arrived and told it was an hour and 40 min wait. Although they have lots to do while you wait I recommend getting takeout and sitting outside.
We have the fried chicken white meat with Potatos and deep fried tomatoes. Our goal for the weekend was to eat no vegetables so tomatoes deep fried was the most I got. Also got chicken and waffles which was awesome.
Overall this chicken was finger lickin good and would recommend it to anyone!

An absolutely great place to stop and take a step back in time!!!! It takes awhile but worth the wait and there is plenty to do while you casually stroll the property!!! Creamed corn and BBQ Pork!!! Yum Y'all

Loved this place!!! The service and the food were excellent. We are only in town a couple of days and decided to go here twice. Jennifer was our waitress the first day, she was wonderful. The only reason I give it a 4 star is that the entertainment stopped very early

Loveless Cafe was definitely a treat, I would rate it 4 or 4.5 star. 

We arrived at the worst possible time (NOON) on a Friday. We ended up having to wait about an hour and 15 mins to get a table. It was definitely worth the wait but still a bit of a pain in the ass. You can kill time browsing the nearby Loveless Cafe shops and get a free coffee next door. 

We were giving some biscuits and preserves to start out (yum!) and I had fried chicken which was served with choice of two sides (I tried green beans and squash). The chicken was absolutely massive and I couldn't finish it. Definitely the best fried chicken I've ever had, although it's not a favorite of mine so I am no expert. 

Service was great here and the decor and ambiance are lovely. Prices were very reasonable (my meal was about $12). 

Overall very fun and satisfying experience :)
We stumbled on this one afternoon and it didn't disappoint. Having lived in Bavaria this wasn't 100% authentic but it was close enough to satisfy. The atmosphere and staff where great too.

Holy cow! This place is awesome!  The biscuits are divine!!! You might just get lucky and see a famous Nashville celeb!  We were lucky to see Alan Jackson on our last visit!  I've only ever gotten their breakfast, but it's been superb every single time!   We always stop in when in town. The atmosphere is great too!  Be sure to grab some apple butter from their store! You won't regret it!

Well it was no lie... next to Tennessee bbq, this is the next best thing.  Hot, fresh food at its finest.  Portions generous and delicious.  Homemade preserves.  Staff as friendly as can be. Great service!  Music playing ....Loretta Lynn., Johnny Cash. All Tennessee here.  Loved it!
My husband loves German food. His lunch was great, the wait staff was friendly and attentive. The pretzel and beer cheese is a must!

My mom and I were visiting Nashville from out of town and we had my 1 year old daughter with us. We were stuck trying to find someone to grab a bite, it was pouring and we were kinda lost. We coincidentally stumbled upon Loveless and we were blown away! The food is amazing. I ordered a plate of Catfish...to die for! They also serve up house jellies complimentary with a plate of biscuits to snack on while you wait on your food. My toddler was very pleased with the warm bread and strawberry spread. The service was great. I couldn't believe how many people they managed to pack into that place and still had our food out in a timely fashion. When I return to Nashville, I won't be eating at the overcrowded bar strip restaurants..I will be driving myself straight to the Loveless Cafe!

Awesome crowd and a very good variety of beers. You can get a beer sampler plate with around 5 types of beers. Being and Indian, Eating here would be a hurdle as most of Indians won't eat pork and beef. But still a good place to have some beers and enjoy some live music.

Yummy! We arrived just shy of 9 am on a Saturday (July 26th).  We were on our way to drive the Natchez Trace.  They only had a 20 min wait, so we had just enough time to shop before being seated.  FYI-The wait when we were called to be seated was 45+ mins.  The biscuits were delightful.  I loved the samples of homemade jams they brought with them.  I think my favorite turned out to be strawberry, even tho they are famous for their blackberry - which we'd already purchased a jar of.  Service was quick, friendly & efficient.  Our coffee never went dry.  Our waiter was never too far, and was very helpful to the more needy couple next to us.  ;-)  I had simple scrambled eggs, and half & half bacon & sausage.  The hotel had told us about their wonderful sausage.  It was indeed very good, but one can't pass up bacon either!  The hashbrown casserole was TDF!  Tho my husband didn't like it too much.  But he was not complaining when our waiter dropped off more super fresh out of the oven biscuits.  It was a fun place to visit with very good food & we'll definitely go back if we're in the area.
They had me at warm, soft, and FREE homemade biscuits. I got the pulled pork omelet for the sake of originality. I loved it along with my chocolate milk.

What a treat!  We bought tickets for the amazing Marc Broussard concert on New Years Eve.  This fabulous venue includes great wines, a fun and unique menu and helpful staff.  Our concert ticket included a dinner reservation so we came an hour earlier and had dinner before the show.  Our food was great, festive and our waitress was very attentive. On a very busy New Years Eve.  The Marc Broussard concert was excellent and the City Winery venue was the perfect spot to showcase this talented band and blues singer.  The size of venue made for a fun, personable evening and great memories!   Plus we ran into Delbert McClinton in the crowd and enjoyed chatting with him as well!

Food was incredible! Jared, our waitress, was absolutely amazing. So friendly, had great recommendations and felt he truly cared about us and our experience. Cannot recommend him or the restaurant more!

Perfect Experience from Start to Finish. Really neat nostalgic place to check out if in the Nashville area. Loveless Cafe was a bucket list item of mine and it certainly did not disappoint. We were there a little after 1:00 pm midweek so I was expecting a fairly lengthy wait. When we checked in, we were told 20-25 minutes. They took my cell phone # and said they would text me when our table was ready. I had enough time to go out front and take a picture of their old sign and use one of their restrooms located outside of the main building (I was impressed it was nice and clean). By the time I sat down on the front porch, they texted to say our table was ready so it ended up only being a 10 minute wait. We were seated and greeted with a plate of several hot, fluffy biscuits and three different kinds of homemade preserves. The menu is very expansive so I'm sure there's something for even the most pickiest of eaters. We all were pleased with our selections (see pics). We each tried something different and everything was spot on. The staff were all very attentive and knowledgeable of the menu items. We all had plenty of leftovers for another meal which was nice. They have cute little shops surrounding the main cafe and several photo ops around the grounds. They also have corn hole boards and plenty of things to do and see while you wait. It was worth the drive and I can't wait to get back and try something new!

Met a few friends for happy hour.  This was my second time at City Winery. The first one was Mother's Day Brunch and it was beyond amazing.  This time I had one of their specialty flatbread with shrimp and an amazing vodka sauce.  I also had the fried Brussels sprouts with feta cheese (to die for).  My wine selection was Riesling.  Our server was pretty awesome.

We had to wait an hour and a half on New Years Day but the food was well worth it. Our order came out really quickly once we were seated, the food was amazing (you have to get the biscuits) and the service was excellent.

I felt like I was in my Nana's kitchen. 8in the best possible way. Service was fantastic. Started with biscuits and homemade jelly, strawberry was my fave. I had the chicken n dumplings with Mac n cheese and hashbrown casserole.  All of them were perfection. I could have kicked the bowl of dumplings. Also tried a few bites if the country fried steak with white gravy. These are my two favorite dishes in the planet and Loveless did not disappoint. Sadly, I was too full for dessert. Until next time.

About 30 min outside of Nashville. Went on a weekday around 12:30pm and the wait was about 40 minutes. There were enough things on their property to roam around and purchase that 40 minutes ended up going by rather quickly. 

The service was phenomenal. Our waiter was so sweet, friendly and attentive. He must've kept refilling our drinks at least 3x that we had to kindly ask him we didn't want to keep drinking coke! Lol. The food is really good. My country fried steak was a bit salty but I ate it anyway. The ham though was the winner. They refill the biscuits so don't worry, if you want more, just ask! Be sure to walk around and purchase some souvenirs. Everyone there are so nice and overall, it was a lovely experience.

I love this place. Was here years ago and still as good as ever.  Can't decide what you want to try get the Country sample, choice of three meats and 2 sides.  and of course bicuits! they may look small but they pack a mighty punch.  Delish!

This place is pretty good! The biscuits are amazing and so is the chicken! If you aren't too full then the desserts are heavenly as well. Every time I've come here I've had a great wait staff. To avoid the long wait come on a week day after 7pm. Everyone knows this place is good so the wait to get in can be pretty long.

Probably our favorite stop in Nashville! We went for breakfast and made reservations just in case it was really busy, but we were seated immediately so that was great. The tables all have these adorable blue and white checkered tablecloths and there's lots of light and interesting art on the walls. Our waitress came up right away and took our drink order, and was super friendly. They served the OJ in mason jars, which I love! She brought a plate of their famous homemade biscuits out with homemade blackberry, strawberry and peach jams. Those biscuits were to die for! I got pecan pancakes, bacon, and the hashbrown casserole. My husband got the pulled bbq pork with eggs, hoecakes and grits. We split a fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit too. The food was out of this world! The hype about this restaurant is completely true and we will be back the second we come back down to Nashville!

Biscuits are really good but everything else is just fine. Nothing will will knock you out of your seat, but the history is interesting and the atmosphere is inviting. I've had breakfast and lunch food here and if you have the time it may be a fun stop.

Coming from California and specifically the Los Angeles area it's impossible to find a good German restaurant. I was delighted to see this beer house and was impressed with the food service and the beer. It looks like a beer Hall out of Munich if you like authentic German food this is a good spot down to earth good quality.

I was shocked at how awesome the biscuits are here. Melt in your mouth kind of good. And then you add anyone of their 3 jams and then it's like a symphony in your mouth. We had the fried chicken, barbecue with 3 sides and it was all absolutely delicious. Needless to say we have a family favorite restaurant here now. #myloveless #greatfood

Read about this lovely cafe on yelp and was not disappointed!! Loved the ambience, food, and service! I ordered the half fried chicken with mashed potatoes and mac & cheese...sooooo delicious!! Service was great!! Didn't have to ask for refills they were always ready with a new drink, super friendly, and just a great first time experience. Inside the decor is so lovely and makes you feel like you're inside someone's home..waiting as they cook you some delicious southern food! Also visited the market gift store outside and bought some goodies to take back home to Cali with me :) Hopefully we have time to come back here before we head back home! Lovedddd it :)

Yummy and delicious fresh biscuits with homemade jam to start.  
   Ordered the three item sampler.  The Country Ham was a little to Salty for my taste, but I was told that is characteristic for that type of ham.  The Chicken Breast came out hot but was dry.  Now the Fried Catfish was perfect and was so good.  I highly recommend it.
     Try the Apple Crumble with Ice Cream.  It is served warm and was definitely a winner.
      Pernell-Kyle (P.K.) Sylvester of the Nashville Predators Hockey Team was there with a film crew doing some shots.  Go Predators!

I have been enjoying this place with family for 2 yrs -usually I get pulled pork or meatloaf - this past time I tried catfish it was tasteless - hubby had chicken fried steak and that it was tough and blah - I will say despite this we decided to get dessert ( usually we are too stuffed ) he got chocolate cream pie , I got coconut cream pie we were shocked neither had any flavor really , the whipped cream could have used some vanilla flavor and a bit of sugar - in fact the pies themselves tasted like sugar was totally forgotten in both not to mention extract of flavors - whoever makes their cream pies needs some new re pies or baking lessons - not sure the drive is worth it anymore

Never eaten here before. The food is actually very good. Very different tastes than the normal. Food is a tad bit on the greasy side but it is good for the price. Staff is very friendly and the restaurant is set up beautifully. Would definitely recommend coming and trying it out. Don't go if your on a budget tho. $42 for two sandwiches and two teas. It's a bit pricey.
Very tasty. Had the chicken fried steak, creamed corn and hash brown casserole. Never had any bad here. A must when you visit Nashville

I went there last night with a group to see Johnny Swim play and it is a great venue to hear/see a band and sit down (the older I get the more I like the idea of sitting down).  The venue area is spacious but intimate and our seats were great.  

The wine selection was good and the pours were above average sized.  I didn't eat, but the food coming out of the kitchen looked and smelled great!

Valet parking is $5 and although most people valeted, the line to get the cars after the show moved quickly. 

It's a unique venue and worth going to to see a show!

I had to meet the head chef, Dennis, due to many food allergies, he had options for me and food was awesome. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone. Our waitress Erin was helpful and was knowledgeable about the food.

First timer. Menu is very to the point and priced as you would expect for mall/tourist prices. We were seated immediately. Our first table hadn't been cleaned so the hostess promptly found another without fail.
We were very excited about this and we were not disappointed. The Kartoffelpuffer appetizer was fantastic. The wurst plates , with 2 sausages(your choice), potato salad and sauerkraut( forgot our bread, no harm no foul). Great tasting grub and not as heavy as you would think.
They were out of the beer we ordered, so that's why a 4 star rating...

I think this place is a bit overhyped. Service was friendly and food was good, but not worth an hour plus wait. Fortunately I made reservations on Open Table, so my wait was only about 30 mins.

The property is nice and you can walk around and check out the shops while you wait.

The biscuits were good, but I've had much better elsewhere. I did enjoy the preserves--blackberry was probably my favorite. I had the Southern Sample Breakfast platter. The eggs, bacon, and sausage were pretty average. The ham was pretty tasty though (albeit a bit on the salty side for me). I will say the gravy and hash brown casserole were very good.

Bottom line: Food was good, but not particularly spectacular. It's a bit of a tourist trap, but it's worth checking out if you're in town. However, don't go without reservations. If it wasn't so touristy and busy, I'd maybe give it another star. Price wasn't bad. Maybe slightly on the high side, but pretty typical for this kind of place.

Food:           3.5/5.0
Service:       4.5/5.0
Price:           3.7/5.0
Wait time:     0.0/5.0
Atmosphere: 4.0/5.0
Cleanliness:  5.0/5.0

Well worth the wait. And when they say the wait is over an hour, they mean it. We visited on Sunday after the Fourth of July, which likely resulted in higher traffic levels.

The biscuits were truly amazing and they provide homemade jams. I had a spicy Bloody Mary with a shot of moonshine. I regret not selecting rum instead. The moonshine was too strong. 

The place is very touristy, and has many shops to kill time as you wait for your table. They even have a shipping center to send away things that you purchase in the shops.
