If I return it'll be during off hours. Not sure I enjoy waiting that long for food.
Food was good but the pork shank got all of us sick sooooooo that kinda sucked but overall it was good. The service was great.

Food: The server showed up pretty quickly to take our drink order and then food order once she delivered our drinks and four of their famous biscuits with a trio of their house made preserves which included Peach, Blackberry, and Strawberry.  The peach was good, the strawberry tasted more like sorgham to me but was good and our favorite was the blackberry. The biscuits were nice and hot! I mean piping hot! Fluffy, buttery and tender. I was impressed. I didn't eat much for breakfast as I knew I was going to want to eat well when we arrived so I was so hungary, I devoured two biscuits right away. I ordered the Fried Chicken and the sides I picked were Mashed Potatoes with Gravy, Green Beans, and Creamed Corn. Did you know Loveless Cafe has their own YouTube channel? They do and the night before visiting, I watched the video on how they made their Creamed Corn and it looked so good and it did not disappoint! I got the dark meat chicken. Two thighs and a small leg. It was good. Especially the crispy skin!  It is not heavily breaded. The green beans were good but I didn't eat much of them as i was too busy devouring the mashed potatoes and gravy! They mashed potatoes were lumpy, which I like, and I could have eaten the gravy with a spoon! It was delicious! We were impressed at how hot the food was when it arrived and how quickly it arrived especially for a place that is so busy. This tells me that they have a good system in their kitchen, well trained servers, enough servers to meet the needs of the 1500 customers they get a day, and that they care that the food gets to you hot. This way they can also turn the table around quickly for the folks that are waiting. We never felt rushed though. Our server was friendly, had that country charm you expect in Nashville, and she was patient with us as we asked questions about the menu items and desserts. For dessert, I ordered the cake of the day which was Spiced Sorgham Cake with a Lemon Cream Cheese Frosting. 

Our experience: We arrived around 11am on Saturday during Labor Day weekend. The wait was an hour and 35 minutes for two people. They give you one of those buzzers that light up when your table is ready. It will work all over their property so you can shop and walk around. There was live music next to the Smokehouse when we arrive but then the band moved around the property. It was a bit hot so we mostly hung out in the stores or in the shade. The main store with all of the food, confections and Loveless Cafe goodies was pretty cramped with people. The store with the clothing nearby was less busy and nice and cool. I found myself there cooling off and playing on my phone more often during the wait. There is also a store with artsy jewelry and pretty things to buy and though it was open, not many people went in. There are only two bathrooms outside that I saw. One person bathroom for men and one for women. There was a short line of women so we used the mens bathroom as well. It was clean and you would never know it was supposed to be just for men. It was funny how the teenage girl in line would not go in. I felt like telling her "honey, when you get to be my age, you get over being embarrassed about a lot of things". Haha. I finally ended up at the front of the restaurant where there is a small waiting room with some chairs and thankfully found an empty chair. I was there about 20 minutes and then the buzzer lit up and we got to got to sit down at our table. See above for food and service review.

I had pretty much decided before our trip that we would probably eat lunch items on Saturday and then come back on Sunday for breakfast if we liked Saturday's experience and food. They do serve breakfast all day, by the way. We went back the next morning early and got a table right away. The breaded pork chops with gravy were divine! I cannot wait to visit again. It's almost worth driving 3 hours just to come here again to eat breakfast!

"Better than sex biscuits" is not an overstatement. 

Damn, Loveless Cafe definitely has the best biscuits in town! 

The biscuits (6) came with the breakfast meal I ordered. They came with 3 different types of jams (strawberry, peach, and blueberry). After having the blackberry jam at Urban Grub, any other jam seems average to me. Initially I ordered the Breakfast Steak and 2 Eggs but they ran out of the Rib-eye (at 8:00 am!! boooo!!!), so I changed to Pit-Cooked Pork BBQ and Eggs instead. I had my eggs fried - medium and a side of hash-brown casserole. I wasn't a fan of the BBQ, however my friend loved it alot and ended up eating most of it. I never touched the hash-brown because of how cheesy it was. My fault, I should had gotten the potatoes instead. The only thing I like in this dish is the eggs, they were cooked to perfection.

My friend had the Southern Sampler Breakfast (Country Ham, Sausages, Bacon, and Red-eye gravy. The country ham was so salty that it was hard to taste anything after that. They should add this "country ham" to the hypertension risk factors list. The sausages were so dry. We tried to pour the red-eye gravy over it because we weren't sure what was the gravy for...it didn't help. I wouldn't order this. 

The portions are huge. I could barley finish half of my dish after eating all of those yummy biscuits. Breakfast for two people were more than $30, which is pretty expensive. I suggest share the platter with someone and order A La Carte on the side (for 2 people). 

I got here around 8 am and there were no waiting lines. I will be back for those heavenly biscuits and try the fried chicken next time! 

2013/#58

I was traveling from Los Angeles and wanted to try some real southern breakfast. My friend recommended this place and told me that it was the most famous breakfast/brunch place in nashville. After eating breakfast here, I was not disappointed and left very satisfied.
My friend warned me of the usual long wait so we came around 8:40AM on a Saturday. We only had to wait about 15 minutes to be seated.
I had the fried chicken with scrambled eggs and potatoes and my friend had the pork chops with the sunny side up egg and has brown. The fried chicken and pork-chop was bomb, super crispy and juicy.
Our meal came with complimentary biscuits and three specialty fruit jams which was the best part of the whole meal! The fruit jams were so good and went so well with the warm biscuits.
Service was excellent. My server kept refilling our waters and ice tea before we had to ask. They also offered to refill the biscuits and jam!
If I ever came back to Nashville, I would definitely return. I regret not buying their jams and will buy some to take home with me next time.

Thanks to Keely's Aunt Joanne for recommending this place! (Cool aunts rock!) We were here for lunch on Monday, so we didn't have to wait at all. Our waitress was a hoot, very chatty and personable. We were flipping through some of Marita's celebrity photos (she was a DJ, music director and record promoter in the country music industry) and she had a few stories of her own to share. Apparently Alan Jackson loves Loveless, and I bet he is a fan of the legendary biscuits. I'm not a big bread person, but they were very good...and fresh from the oven...yum! Keely once again tried the Nashville Hot Chicken and really enjoyed it. Marita had an ooey, gooey patty melt and I had a Southern Omelet, which was stuffed with more salt-cured Southern ham than I could handle. My dogs were glad! I wish we'd had more time to explore the shops, but we had places to go and people to see. Hopefully we'll be back someday.

Yeah, I lived in Fairview, for about 14 months not too long ago. First of all,
if you've never been to Fairview Tn., believe me you're not missing 
anything.
 
Anything at all. 

Couldn't stand the place. Went to Loveless maybe a total
of three times and was never impressed. 

The biscuits are not that good, the wait is just silly and the rest of the
whole ordeal made me think of the Bluebird here. Except you had to
eat with hicks instead of hipsters. Really don't want to eat with either.

A fun atmosphere and nicely decorated for Christmas. I can imagine it can be a hoot during Oktoberfest. The food is nice and tasty. We had a giant, hot pretzel served with beer cheese and an applesauce/mustard spread which was excellent.  For the entree I had the jagerschnitzel which had a good crispy coating on a bed of spatzel cooked perfectly. The potato dumpling I got as a side was a bit dry inside and the gravy unexceptional.  My wife had the Bavarian (French) Onion Soup and enjoyed it. We finished with the desert sampler and liked all three items.  Service was friendly and prompt. The gift shop had a nice selection, but unfortunately didn't have Ritter Sport Peppermint which I wanted to pick up for a friend (they did have about 6 other flavors).

A wonderful destination in Nashville. The food is authentic, the bier is excellent. The atmosphere is festive. 
As one who travels often to Bavaria, Bavarian Bierhaus gets my highest reccommendation.

Let me start by saying that I am writing this as someone who didn't grow up in the south and therefore doesn't have any nostalgic feelings for southern cooking. I'm writing this primarily for people that grew up on the east coast or anywhere other than the south.

First, the good: all the food is good and the biscuits are amazing. That being said, be warned: even if you typically like butter on your biscuit, do not do it. Stick with the preserves that come with said biscuits. That combo is absolutely amazing, but the biscuits themselves are so heavy that butter really doesn't work on them.

The breakfast food is generally solid, if a little unremarkable from the perspective of someone for whom the nostalgia for southern home cooking does nothing. If you expecting a direct correlation between how endlessly busy this place is and quality of the food itself, you might be disappointing, even though it's not particularly bad.

The somewhat disappointing: having had some great BBQ in Nashville at places like Edley's, and knowing Loveless' legendary status and seeing their BBQ pit as we approached, I went in expecting to be blown away by the BBQ at Loveless but it was quite the opposite. Not bad, but not great or even memorable - just ok. Main culprit is the sauce which is just sort of average.

I'd just say that it's worth going for the biscuits and for stuff like the art gallery in the back, but My advise would be to stick to the breakfast menu (including the chicken and biscuits) and don't go in with elevated expectations due to the long lines. It is largely just ok and there are certainly better BBQ options if that is what you are looking for.

I went here on a Saturday, so it was super crowded. The wait was about 45 minutes, so my friend and I ordered carry out instead. I got the half dozen biscuits. They come with three types of jams: strawberry, apricot, and blackberry. The jams were delicious! But I think the biscuits were a little overrated. Don't get me wrong, they were good but I'm not sure if I would travel out of the city and wait 45 minutes to get them. The coffee wasn't that good, and then I found out that they have complimentary coffee in the gift shop. 

My friend got the fried chicken biscuit and the pimento cheese n fried green tomato biscuit. I had a bite of both and they were pretty good! They seem small, but they're pretty hearty.

I cannot tell you much of anything about this national breakfast treasure that had not already been covered. We were lucky to have gone early and been seated right away. The small plates of tiny biscuits and there jams were phenomenally good. Good bacon, good ham even good grits for my resident grit expert. It was one of the better breakfast I have had anywhere. But you knew that from before. It's a CSU place I cannot wait to revisit.

Read the yelp reviews..and had to try this temple to southern cooking. Glad we did. You start with a plate of homemade biscuits and jam. 
After filling up on biscuits, breakfast show up and your stomach loosens up. We had a breakfast bowl and French toast. Both we fantastic! Service was amazing..if we ever in the area again..this will be on our list of "must do's"
WOW!!  Absolutely amazing food and a fun atmosphere!!  Loved the live band and watching people try to blow the alphorn. So glad we went in!!

oooooo-wwweeee! Call ahead and they'll cut 30 minutes off your wait time....which has lasted about 2 hours both times I've been here. The little shops that surround the Loveless Cafe aren't big enough to keep me occupied long enough so I sit and stare at my phone hoping they'll call and tell us the table is ready. The servers are friendly, food comes out fast. Most importantly, the biscuits and preserves come out fast. My god, those things are little pillows of flour and butter from heaven. They really are the best biscuits I've ever had. I've had breakfast and lunch at Loveless. Best fried okra/green tomatoes I've had in Nashville and I consider myself a seasoned expert. The place is a bit of a drive outside town but its cute, great for visitors and those enamored with the novelty of fattening, yummy southern food.

This is a quite famous cafe at the northern end of the Natchez Trace Parkway and for good reason.

The biscuits.
The biscuits.
The biscuits.

I still think about those biscuits. Wish they'd brought us more. Wish I'd eaten mine slower. Wish my husband had visited the restroom earlier so I could have nicked one of his.

The rest of our breakfast was great, too. I enjoyed their country ham (half a slice is plenty) and the cheese grits were not to be missed.

But those biscuits tho.
Everyone told us to go to Loveless Cafe.  The food is delicious.  We each had the special of Chicken and cornbread stuffing.  If your in Nashville you have to make the trip, you won't be sorry

Always a favorite for me!  All company I have visiting will go to Loveless after which I take them often down the Trace for a ride. Back to the Loveless, they have food for every palette of every age and culture. You will not be disappointed. Historic area with someone famous eating there most every weekend and sometimes during the week.  Great venue site for parties of any size and any occasion.
Fun spot and great food and service. Stopped in on a rainy Wednesday morning about 0800. Great coffee, biscuits, preserves, country ham, fried chicken, fried green tomatoes between the two of us.

Wow! We came for the German Christmas supper. The only thing I didn't like was that they didn't have rolling chairs and someone to roll me out to my car. From the start of the evening to the end was a great experience. The ambiance is great from the decor to the staff attire it is a welcoming and friendly environment. 
The food was great. From the pretzel we had as an appetizer to the strudel there was nothing that was not great. Roasted pork, ham, mashed potatoes pretzel stuffing, Brussels Sprouts and Red Cabbage composes the supper, and it was all amazingly good. I can't wait for my next visit, and since I joined their stein club, it will be sooner than later.

Being relatively new to Nashville, Loveless Cafe was one of the first places I was taken since I arrived.  I love the atmosphere of the entire campus, from the cafe itself to the Hams and Jams country store--it screams "Nashville!" in the best possible way.  However, even with the kitchy stores and atmosphere, I was put off by the 1 hour 45 minute wait and extremely grumpy by the time we were finally seated.  We ordered our dinner, a classic meat and three with the smoked turkey breast, mac and cheese, fried green tomatoes and green beans.  The turkey was freezer-burned and cold and so bad I had to send it back.  My boyfriend commented that his fried chicken was only lukewarm and the mashed potatoes had no flavor--he also said that the best part of the meal were the biscuits, the one thing we didn't have to pay for!  We left the restaurant feeling disappointed, with no desire to return.

I happened to have a business meeting here one weekday morning for breakfast a few weeks later, and I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious the meal was.  I ordered a vegetable omelette with grits and biscuits and enjoyed every bite!  The omelette was fresh and huge, and the biscuits were noticeably hot out of the oven.  I've since returned to Loveless with out of town guests for breakfast and have always been satisfied with my meal, particularly because the wait time is dramatically shorter than it would be for dinner.  I won't eat anything but breakfast here again anyways, so I'll be back on a weekday morning the next time I welcome visitors!

It's a long drive from Nashville for a mediocre meal served in what seems to have become just a money factory. Thankfully the drive is a pretty one. The hostess was absolutely lovely considering her job is to tell people they will have to wait more than an hour for under-seasoned, underwhelming food. Yes, there's history here and the setting gives you that southern feel, but you can do much better. Not one person at our table of 11 had anything to say about the food (other than the biscuits and syrup being good) and we had a range from the chicken and waffles, garden omelette, Pit-cooked pork and eggs platter, BBQ egg omelette (which was just folded eggs on top of dry BBQ pork, no cheese or sauce thrown on half a plate), and pancakes. The last time my mom was here she raved about the service, but our server was borderline rude and non-engaging and it was only 10am.

If I could give six stars I would! This stop was a highlight of our Nashville vacation. The history is great, there are celebrity photos all over the walls, the food is amazing, and the gift shop allows you to bring some of the goodness home. The hash brown casserole will change your life. The marinated cucumber salad was just like my grandmother used to make. And I loved that you can make a whole meal out of side dishes!
Don't know if you've eaten at the Winery for lunch recently but the menu is great, service exceptional and it's just a nice place to escape to in the middle of the day.
Loved all of my food! Great atmosphere and it was cool to see pictures of all the celebrities and their autographs. Staff is also really nice!

We read about this famous cafe in all of the Nashville food blogs, and it did not disappoint! It's about 30 minutes outside of the city, but the drive is pretty easy. The space is an old motel that expanded to have a general store, two eating venues and a barbecue pit. The vibe was so down to earth and family oriented! We went in on a weekday morning and were seated immediately. There was a wide selection on the menu, but the biscuits really took the prize! I got on with house made pulled pork, and my friend got a bunch on the side with her breakfast platter. They were hot, fluffy, crispy, and served with a great selection of preserves. After our meal, we explored the general store - it had a nice selection of preserves and ready made mixes for fried chicken, biscuits, etc. This spot is a must visit for anyone passing thorough Nashville!

A trip to Nashville is not complete without a detour to the Loveless Cafe. Be prepared for a wait, but the time passes quickly given all the cute gift shops scattered about the grounds. They have lots of cute trinkets and good souvenir material.

Every meal I've had has been delicious, but the absolute highlight for me comes at the very beginning of the meal in the form of flaky, buttery, perfectly salty heaven-cakes (other people call them biscuits). Served with strawberry, blackberry, and peach preserves, it's everything I can do not to fill up on plate after plate of them.

It's worth every mile in the car, minute of wait time, and calorie in your mouth!

The biscuits are definitely to die for.......the wait is far to long....the food is just ok.....i think back...back....back  in the day it was better but it is just average food at a small place with over crowded dining rooms ...the place is just tired......just to much hype....you can find much better in nashville....or you can be disappointed  and still  say you ate at the loveless cafe

As Tourists , someone suggested we try this place, as entertaining , with  great food  too. Well here we go again, They do have entertainment , as scheduled , ( Just Not Tonite )  anyway , we enter this massive biergarten  style plotz , The waiter " Fatjon " I kid you not, I inquired as to his nameplate,  he was very nice and made several suggestions. So I ordered the schnitzelspechzelschwine platter , along with katuffullpuffin , We enjoyed their large pretzel with a sweet style mustard, Onion soup was pretty good. But the meal, was lacking flavor, as well as the pancakes, very bland. I was not impressed. I was thinking German world in Epcot was better. Never the less, lest try the strudel. I am more accustomed to flaky strudel, not a doughy layering.
 But if ya like beer with your mediocre food, then is the place they have several varieties. You can even leave your own personal beer Stein here to boot ,
Great food and excellent service. Try to go during non-peak times to avoid lines, but it is well worth going to Loveless.
Great atmosphere, music, and wine. Service is a little slow but the food is worth the wait! Highly recommend this place for great live music and great food in one setting.

There was plenty of free parking on the nearby streets but the area did not look safe to me so I paid $5 for a valet parking. We came early and enjoyed our dinner there. The flat bread had a generous amount of goat cheese and mushrooms. I was glad I brought a mini flesh light with me because it would have been a challenge to read the menu without it.  Our waitress was very attentive and our overall experience was very positive.

I had been to the Loveless Cafe before, but this was my husband's first visit. He was a little concerned that it was so far away from downtown Nashville, but once he got there he loved it! We made a reservation through Google maps, but still had a wait of about 15 minutes. While we were waiting I enjoyed looking at pictures of celebrities on the wall and we looked over the menu. After we were seated, MawMaw came over and greeted us and continued to provide great service during our meal. My husband got the Southern Sampler Platter and thought it was wonderful. I got the fried liver plate and I could have fed a family of four with all of the livers on my plate! Everything was absolutely delicious! After we had stuffed ourselves we checked out all of the shops and picked up a couple of gifts.  The Loveless Cafe will always be a stop on our trips to Nashville.

Absolutely adore the staff here! We live in Nashville but it is totally worth the drive when craving home cooked food without dirtying up the kitchen! We've been several times and never had a bad experience with food or service. We love that every time we come in we feel like family. We will most definitely be back and will always recommend this place to everyone!

I absolutely love this Cafe!! I live in Texas and have driven cross country a couple of times and have ALWAYS made time to stop at Loveless! I found it by mistake once and it was the best accident that has ever happened. I make a trip every year and always stop to eat here. 

The different jams they make are delicious and I always buy a pack of them to take home and to gift to friends and family all over. The service is always fast and extremely friendly. The servers are so welcoming every time and are always helpful with questions or suggestions if you want to try something different. 

The food gives you that home cooked feeling. It reminds you of your childhood when grandma used to cook your favorite meal for you when you'd stay the night with her. I absolutely love and adore this restaurant and will always make it a staple in my cross country trips!

We had an absolutely wonderful time at the Bavarian bierhaus,  food and service was on point.  The entertainment was excellent and had the crowd involved.  We will be back when friends come back to Nashville. Brought back memories from my time in Munich.

This is my favorite breakfast place in Nashville Tennessee! I came here five years ago and couldn't wait to get back for their homemade biscuits and jams. Really cute and fun old-fashioned ambience. Wonderful staff. JaDee was our waitress and she did a wonderful job by welcoming us nicely and bringing out the nonstop biscuits and jams and with that sweet southern hospitality brought some coffee to go for a long drive. Great place for families! Delicious food and great conversation to be had! Don't miss this place on the way to and from your destination when you go through Nashville!
Dive bar with good music, but insanely understaffed. 20 minute waits for a beer. Was fun, but irritating.

Everything I imagined it would be. We had the family style breakfast and it was great, though I think we just did one go around with an extra basket of biscuits. The country ham is wonderful. People are really nice as you'd expect. It is very, VERY busy. We went on a weekday, late morning and waited about 45 minutes. The clerk in the shop next door said that wasn't too bad, sometimes it's 2 hours!

Great staff, great food, and the Blue Moon is sooo good!! I recommend the catfish, fried chicken, meatloaf, mashed potatoes, and the blue moon drink (alcohol). I would give 5 stars, but I thought the ham was too tough. I usually LOVE ham, but I wasn't a fan of the ham here. Everything else was amazing. Great place to bring the family!!

Well, biscuits and jam were brought to us when they sat us. That was the best part of breakfast. Scrambled eggs tasted powdered,  my 2 sausage patties were so dry and tepid I truly think they were cooked the day before....and the music pumped in was the Beach Boys........what?? At a Nashville "southern cooking" restaurant?? What a great disappointment.   And $71 for four breakfasts....yeee-ouch!!!!  Been there, done it, won't be back. Hello Waffle House?? Can you hear me....

The city winery has a fantastic ambiance. The food and drink selection are extensive and delicious. The only caveat would be the timing. The service was friendly and engaging, however the service was unbelievably slow. Our reservation was set for 6:00pm and we did not receive our bills until 9:30 pm. I would recommend the pumpkin risotto goat cheese balls for an app and the brussels were a hit. Overall a good dining experience.

Can't say enough good things about this place. The food is amazing. I've never had a bad meal here. The service is attentive and friendly. If you like BBQ you will love it. The pulled pork is probably the best I've had. 

Now as for complaints, and I wouldn't even say that it's a complaint, is the wait. Expect to be there awhile. I've never waited less than an hour. I can honestly say I believe it's worth the wait but I fully understand how this could be frustrating. What I do like is that there is plenty to do while you wait. Cute shops and lawn games definitely make the time go by. If I you have the time to spare it's worth the trip.

Fun fact. The Natchez Trace Parkway is right over by Loveless and it makes for a lovely afternoon drive.

Loved the food and ambience. I think our waiter had too many tables so service was a little slow but I still REALLY enjoyed our dinner. Everyone was super friendly. From hostess, to waiter, to bartender. Will definitely come again.

I thought I reviewed this already, but I guess not. That's ok, all you need to know about are the biscuits. They are amazing. They keep bringing them to your table, too! It's great!

I have been here two Saturdays - Saturday #1 - 30 minute wait. Saturday #2 - 90 minute wait. So it's a little hard to predict. I suggest going early in the morning. Like, 9 am. It's worth it!

Went for lunch during the day.


Having lived in Germany, I wasn't expecting much for a place in the mall.

Initial impression- trying to look like a fest hall/Guest House.

Seating is fest style, large tables you will share with other customers.
Atmosphere- kind of dull ( it was lunch, so no live music, but could of had some music playing)

Server- was courteous, but not very attentive.
 Drink glasses went Unfilled, did not check back to see if needed anything (or refills).

Food- I Ordered schweinebraten-rotwein., with a brotchen on the side.
Scweinbraten-rotwein was good, very moist, not over cooked.
The spatzle was like paste.
Brotchen was old, inside was as hard as outside.

Secondary impression- 50/50.
Staff was pretty "zombie" like ( going thru the motions).

Price was not unreasonable, but bordering on not worth it for what received.

Since this was my first visit, I will give benefit of the doubt. 
Maybe it was an off day.

I will try it again, and order another menu item.
Maybe Jager Schnitzel, and see how that compares to my expectations, and experiences from the past.

Did not have a beer, but did check out the selections.
I really expected more selections, at least bottle wise.

But in a bier garden in Germany, there is usually not a large selection either.

We unknowingly came to a landmark of a restaurant! I had the chicken friend steak with two eggs and fried potatoes....the meal was REALLY good and the biscuits were great! My wife got the ham with red eye gravy, potato casserole, and scrambled eggs. She wasn't thrilled with her meal but I loved mine. Glad we came and checked it out!
Food was good, service was great. Entertainment package is worth the $. Valet team was terrible. Couldn't help us get a cab, pretty much ignored us since we didn't have a car there.

The best breakfast/brunch in the Nashville area. The customer service was phenomenal as well. I'm in the hospitality industry and our server Mark was the best! If I'm ever in the area I will be back, also recommending this to our family and friends. You will not be disappointed!

Hands down, THE BEST food, beer and service we've had in Nashville while visiting!
Our bartender Betsy treated us like family, making sure we ordered exactly what we had in mind, and picked out the perfect beer selections for us. The Manager, Andrew, came to our table and had an actual conversation with us, not your typical "fly by" by management. Great overall experience!
Update: we loved this restaurant so much we dined there again tonight...two nights in a row! Kathleen took GREAT care of us, plus the entire staff is amazing! Food was perfect!! Thank you Andrew!!
BTW...the Apple Strudel and The Pretzel Bread Pudding is out of this world!
New Years Eve fixed menu...kinda blah to be honest. Food was a bit tasteless. Servers were polite and accommodating and the place is tastefully decorated and beautiful.

Unfortunately, the service was TERRIBLE and the food was way overpriced. The space is spectacular but our experience with the staff was not great.

The staff was rude, did not know a lot about the menu, and we waited almost 2 hours for our food. The chicken was about the size of my fist and cost over $30 after tax. Unfriendly and not trained. A shame because the layout of the place is great.

This is one of my favorite food places in Nashville. The country style village and smoke house are classic. If there is a line ... I always call my order in and then go visit one of the shops next door...

Waited about 2 hours to dine at Loveless Cafe. We ordered fried catfish, fried chicken, bbq pork, and country ham. The country ham was a bit too salty. The fried catfish has too much breading. The fried chicken was delicious though. It was very crispy and juicy in the inside. The biscuits with home made jams stole the show. It was very airy and fluffy. We each had at least 3-4 biscuits because it was that good! We ordered grits, fried okra, and cream corn as sides. The fried okra was a bit soggy. The grits and cream corn superb!

Love them. The food was great. Came out fast and the service was awesome. Dont go that much because they stay busy and it can be hard to get in. But the amazing server told us the best time to come so maybe we can go more often.
Great place, too busy most of the time, but a modern classic for country dining. The homemade biscuits and fresh jams are amazing.

Best place to bring friends and family for a good time..loved their seasonal beer and super friendly staff.. especially kudos to Fat Jon.. yes its actually his name.. super fun guy.. and if you are confused what to get... just ask him..

Totally recommend this place...

IF YOU ARE IN NASHVILLE YOU HAVE TO COME TO LOVELESS CAFE! Best home cooked southern breakfast we had the whole trip. The story behind the restaurant and the motel makes you fall in love with it even more! Our sever Virginia was such a doll!!!

First off, don't think you should charge people 9 dollars to park if they are coming in to eat and drink. Food was ok, prices are a little steep for what you get. Service was fine. Can't say I would go there again.

OK this is off the beaten path about 25 minutes from downtown Nashville. Once you get there plan on a wait. Ours was 1.5 hours however there is so much to do...we played cornhole, toured the various shops on property, relaxed, and enjoyed the day. Once we were seated we went through two baskets of the best homemade biscuits with fresh made jams. We could have made a meal of just that. We ordered the sampler (with bbq pork, friend chicken, and catfish), bbq pork platter, chicken tender sandwich, and chicken tenders. The tenders were the size of a small plate, and you got 3 of them (leftovers!), the meal was unbelievably good, so fresh, and tasty. We had leftovers we were so full. They packed it all up and a to go container of biscuits too. This was well worth the wait and we made an afternoon of it. The service was so great that we did not want to leave.  Go hungry and willing to relax a while. It will be the go to spot next trip.

Biscuits and jam were killer. 

We went for our honeymoon and it was perfect!
The food was mouthwatering. I was sad that I was too stuffed to keep eating.

A staple of Nashville culture and a definite tourist stop. I've been a few times before having lived here for 8 years now but brought my parents this morning. You have a wait, no matter the day or time. There's a wait. The food is good-Southern style and you can't go wrong with any of it. They are known for their biscuits and preserves. And for good reason.

Oxymorons of Tennessee: You cannot believe that  Jim Crow nightclubs of Memphis, which the bluesmen who played could not patronize -  were also 'great venues'? No 'great venue' maintains a policy of institutionalized bigotry.  Should the government shut Rocketown down? Nope. Yes, @Carrie G: Rocketown's rights to discriminate are absolutely protected by the  Constitution. Should everyone who believes in equality, freedom of expression, and, oh yes,  love and acceptance (Mark 12:31)(Luke 6:36)(Matthew 7:1).boycott Rocketown, and educate friends and neighbors to do the same? YES.  And that too is  absolutely  protected by  the Constitution.

I read an article that said the biscuits are terrific here. Since i am a biscuit lover, Hubby and I drove here from Chicago so I could try the biscuits out for my late December Birthday. I was not disappointed. The biscuits were FANTASTIC. The rest of the food was hearty Southern cooking and it was really good. We were not disappointed that we made the trip. In fact, on our last day in Nashville, we went back to eat at Loveless before hitting the road to head home.
Good food, plenty of it, in friendly surroundings and at a fair price; what more can you ask for?

Oh, the Loveless. How your name is a misnomer.

This place is great. The wait is ridiculous, but that makes the food all the better, and you can always bring a book or a game - you've now been warned! 

I brought my sister here when she was in town, so it was her first time and I wanted to have an awesome experience with her. I'd only gone there once before, and had an epic meal, so I decided to relive it and prove that my memory served the Loveless properly. Oh, it did. 

We had a hilarious waiter (they are all quite friendly there) who gave us crayons despite our age, and was quite speedy on the food delivery. I ordered the barbecue plate, because what else would I order?!?!? Got two eggs over easy and cheese grits on the side, while my sister ordered the country ham plate with tomato scrambled eggs and hash browns.

The meat was very good. Very flavorful and also wasn't so fatty that I felt sick. My eggs were a little undercooked, but such is the way with over easy eggs so I just avoided that part. The grits were suuuuper creamy, so if you like them that way, you'll enjoy these! My sister's ham was amazing, and we had so much food that we boxed about half of it.

Obviously, the biscuits were great. The first batch we had was not directly from the oven, so the biscuits were slightly dry and not wildly tasty. However, if you wait around long enough, a new batch is sure to get around your way and they are definitely worth the wait, served up UNLIMITED and with delicious jam. Yum.

After we drove on the Natchez Trace for a bit, and I'd recommend doing that if you're out this far. It tops off a great meal! I'd love to go again sometime soon - nice folks and nice grub.

Biscuits and Fried Chicken to write home about! Wow! This place is a bit of a trek from the center of the city but it is worth the trip. The service is incredible. The portions are big and the biscuits and jelly are out of this world! For anyone in town, this is a big time recommendation!

After our second visit at CW, I'm reminded to write a review. In our first visit, we found the food to be delicious, especially the roasted Brussels sprouts. The room is first and foremost one of Nashville's best listening rooms. It's like listening to a performance in the studio. Seating provides in intimate experience where you can make eye contact with the performer.

This used be to a great venue back at their old location. Now it is hypocrites pushing a Christian agenda. Allowing certain bands and nixing the ones they " deem inappropriate" and I honestly couldn't tell you based off what criteria. The people who work the snack desks are always polite and friendly, but the security is the most stuck up group of people I have ever met. I've sworn off going to shows here, even if it is my favorite band, I'll pass. Get back to your roots and learn how to run a business. I would give you zero stars if I could.

Love! This place is adorable and the food is delicious! I am not a fan of biscuits yet I ate the entire plate of the ones at loveless cafe! The hype is right and you definitely need to try this place! They also have a store and you can have goodies shipped home to you! It's a little bit of a drive to get to but definitely worth it!

Of course, couldn't drive by without stopping in. It's huge! You can't miss it. There was no wait on this Monday night. Just missed the 3-6pm happy hour. 
Customer service was on point. Very friendly, attentive, and they make efforts to make eye contact with every interaction. So put your phones down. 
Ample German beer with variety of sizes.
Only had the onion soup which was featured on the travel channel and the wurst platter which allowed you to pick 2 sausages. Wished they had sample platters to try all their sausages.
Many photo opts available. 
Fun gift shop area as you enter & exist. Prices in the gift shop are reasonable. 
Ample free parking because it's in the mall area.
A fun place to visit but they do cater to regulars and there's the stein mug club section with personal locks for each stein.

I can see why the world famous biscuits are so sought after! I came here with family after spending the last 2 days exploring Music City, and I'm so glad we stopped in. We drove a tour bus in and there was room to park in the very back so that was a huge bonus. When you walk in, there are a ton of photos along with the person's autograph adorning the front entrance. I ordered a southern omelet and I normally am not a huge fan of eggs and if there are other options I will order something else, but the omelet was incredible! I also ordered chocolate milk (my favorite!) and it came with a mason jar cup and two milk boxes. I ended up drinking it straight from the container, but I appreciated that they presented it with a glass just in case. When we left, our waitress had really made rapport with us, asking my grandpa where he had gotten his cane and what it was made from. She was very nice. I hope to one day visit again soon!

We stopped by for breakfast early Sunday morning. I had the fried chicken biscuit which was absolutely delicious.  Definitely the stand out.  My husband had the country ham, which was good, but nothing too amazing.  The hash brown casserole was very tasty and the little biscuit plate they give you is the perfect thing to tide you over until your meal arrives.  The shops are adorable and it's a very quaint little spot to grab a meal and wander around for a bit to walk off the biscuits.
Love this place, GREAT BRATS ! Also love the atmosphere... Certain nights they have live authentic bands/music

Good german food. Devoured the giant pretzel with cheese sauce. Tried the rouladen and sauerbraten. Good meats and red cabbage. Surprised the german potato salad was cold rather than served warm. Rather noisy so hard to hear a lot of the conversation. Advertised as kid friendly but probably wouldn't take the 1 and 3 year old again. Be prepared to share large tables. Rather pricey with appetizer, salad, meals, and drinks but it was like authentic german food in Wisconsin.

Just wanted to update my review. We have NOT been back yet because we live in a different town; however, the manager contacted me and stated "I want to apologize for your experience last night.  Of course we strive for excellence in every area, and we apparently fell way short with the food.  I am glad you enjoyed some of the appetizers, and that the service was good.  I can't change the past, but I would like to invite you back to attempt to salvage the relationship here, and to prove to you that your experience is the exception rather than the norm.  If you would be so kind as to take me up on it, I'd like to offer you two tickets to a show on me, to come back and give us another try." WOW..... I AM TOTALLY IMPRESSED AND WILL DEFINITELY BE COMING BACK!    #impressive #secondchances #appreciatecitywinery

Biscuits and Preserves to absolutely swoon over. Light and fluffy, with the perfect flakey texture. Preserves are fresh and sweet and flavorful. Service here is down home friendly and the pies are divine! Getcha some!!!

Perhaps my expectations were too high.  I think if you're new to Southern cuisine, you may think this place is the best thing since sliced bread.  However, I was just a little disappointed that it was like a more touristy Cracker Barrel (which I actually like better).  After reading the hype about the biscuits, I was absolutely convinced that eating at this place would lead to an unhealthy obsession with biscuits.  Negative.  I was completely underwhelmed.  The only thing that saved it from being bad was the delicious peach preserve topping that accompanied the bread basket.  

Service was kind of spotty - had to wait a long time for refills, the food had a weird timing issue (like I received my food well before the rest of the table).  I ordered a BLT w/ fried egg and a side of hash brown casserole (gag).  I don't think I have a lot of love for the Loveless Cafe.

Come to loveless cafe to experience the southern cooking and hospitality. I got the sampling dish to try out their fried chicken, pork chop and pulled pork. Their food is fresh, tasty and have a pang of vinegar and brown sugar as you would expected. This place is always busy as they have half a million visitors a year.

After returning from Germany a month ago I was having serious wheat beer withdrawals!! Bavarian Beerhouse to the rescue! 

Ambience : the whole ambience is exactly like the beer houses in Munich. Upon entering it reminded me of the world famous Hofbrauhouse. The long table and benches and family style dining is great to meet other diners and socialize. Even the waitresses wear traditional german clothes. 

Service : We went there on a late Sunday night and the place wasn't crowded. Service is quick and friendly.

Drinks: They have amazing German beers on draft and I had to have my wheat beer. We also got a liter of dark wheat beer which was delish! 

Food: Authentic German sausages and sauerkraut. We just had to get THE CURRY WURST!! it was just as it tasted in Germany. We got the LEBARLASE which is a meatloaf and it truly hit the spot. Got a couple of other sausages which were all great. Try the jalapeño cheddar wurst. 

Love this place and so glad we have an authentic beer house in town now
Love the atmosphere.   Food is delicious.  Portions are good and they menu is great.  Gotta keep going back and trying new things  Definitely recommend

We finally visited this Nashville landmark after living here for more than a year. Other than the unique down home feeling, not sure what all the hype is about. We waited about 40 minutes for a table on Friday afternoon around 12:30 pm.  Not bad. We were seated and a basket of hot biscuits and preserves were brought to the table right away.  A pleasant touch. They were good, but not great. They have a strange consistency on the top.  But still good.  It was the main meal that was disappointing. It was quickly brought out after we ordered. I ordered the "special" chicken and dressing with two sides. My husband had the smoked turkey breast with cranberry bbq sauce. He loved it, although he did say it was not very hot. My  meal was less successful.  The "dressing" was white bread with a few chunks (yes chunks) of onion and celery with a little poultry seasoning and chicken broth. The chicken was shedded chicken breast. It was all barely warm. The gravy was served in a side bowl and was cold. (The waitress did promptly bring me another hot bowl.). The sides, sweet potatoes and squash casserole, were slightly warm.  It appears they keep everything in steamers for fast service.

  All and all, I have had better meals at other "meat and three" places.

Cheesy atmosphere, food was good!

Got the giant pretzel and Rahm Schnitzel, both were good. I've had better pretzels but it was good. 

I like german environments but I felt like the singers were just trying to remind us to buy a beer with their songs.

So two people at our table of four were severely gluten and dairy intolerant and specified this multiple times. Our server even asked the chef to verify certain items were gf/df or would be made accordingly. When our food came out, the gluten free burger was served on a bun and the salad had a dairy based dressing on it. Two things that very clearly weren't even looked at by an expo person or the food runner. On top of that, the risotto balls were colder than room temperature in the center and very obviously had been sitting for quite some time - which makes sense as to why our order took so long. Every time we needed something we had to flag our server down. Not once did she come by to ask if everything was okay (which it was not) and an entire entree was completely forgotten. I've been coming here for over 3 years now and have never had such a sub par experience. I rave about this place constantly but I can see the quality of the service has declined. Very disappointing as I was just telling someone before the show that I was planning to sign up for their "vinofile" membership. Likely will opt for a different dining and music experience as there are plenty of others in Nashville.

Our server was a little slow, but she's only one person so I won't condemn the entire staff. Besides the long wait, our food was just ok. I've had better German potato salad, and the pretzel was really over rated. I was not expecting it to be hard, so that through me off. The jalapeño cheddar wurst  is really delicious.

We had high expectations for what we had heard about this place and it met every one of them! We went around lunchtime on a Saturday and had to wait for over an hour but there are a few shops and cornhole games to pass the time. The pork was everything we had hoped for and the biscuits are the best we have ever had! Highly recommend buying the jams and bacon in the little shop next to the cafe to take home!

Best comfort food in Nashville! Service and grub is always top notch!
Great cocktails  also!!!

A nice addition to the Opry Mills mall, with an entrance inside the mall and once outside if you want to avoid the mall crowd.  Large beer hall with a stage for live music.  They have a reasonable selection of Bavarian beers with seasonal specialties regularly added.  Food menu looked good and as is typical German fare, leaned heavily on sausages and meat.  We only tried a few small sides, the spatzle, roasted red cabbage and fries.  All satisfied that craving for German food.  If you're a meat eater I think you'd be satisfied with their selection of Usinger's sausages. Servers dress in authentic German beer hall attire, which lends to the festive atmosphere.  A nice addition to the Opry Mills complex.

I normally only review small businesses and try to stay away from chains, but this is an exception.

Valentine's Dinner at the City Winery was a pleasant experience. Seated in the back winery room excluded from the main dining area and the venue was a nice touch. There were several bistro tables for two, for couples that were dining as well. The menu was fixed for the night by head Chef Kristin Beringson was somewhat of a surprise due to the link on the website not working. It featured crab, a nice salad with cauliflower/beets, a lamb tartar, lobster/grits/roasted grape tomatoes, and finished with a fromage blanc mouse with pear dessert. 

Pros: Nice and secluded. Wine pairings with each course. Good service. Portions were perfect.

Cons: Handful of people bringing out dishes which created a few hiccups. Would have preferred fresh silverware for each course. Valet charge (though small at $5, I believe more people would be more generous in tips if it were free)

Overall. My lady and I both enjoyed our time there and would go back. I'd love to check out the full menu. This place is large and pretty unique. It tackles multiple feats and seems to do it pretty well.
The 45 minute wait is totally worth it for the fried chicken. I don't even like biscuits and I eat these!  In other words, it's worth a flight in!

What the what?!? The experience at Loveless started with a 20 min wait for our table which we gladly accepted and took the opportunity of extra time to take a photo in front of the smoke pit. While shooting our obligatory pics the smells from the pit were intoxicating. Jonathan (inside running the pit) invited us in for a sample. You didn't have to ask my husband twice! Thankfully no small children or animals were between him and the entrance to the smoke house or serious injuries could have occurred. Jonathan gave us an impromptu tour of the smoker and a sample fresh from the oven! Wow, he was as knowledgeable as he was hospitable and entertaining! Would have paid for this! THANK YOU JONATHAN! We hope you get to go to Hawaii some day :) ...oh and breakfast was outstanding!!

The food was delicious, the beer enjoyable but all this was overshadowed by the WAY TOO LOUD band. They played continuously for the time we were there making it impossible to hear any conversation. I don't mind music making the atmosphere fun, but turn it down and take a break every 20 minutes!
Not a music appreciation setting or sound. Very cavernous, and the sound bounces around the room, but seems hollow. The staff and service was quite good....friendly and efficient.

My initial review on 5.6.15 was very ho-hum. That being said, I was very quickly contacted by and apologized to by manager, Emilee. She explained the extenuating circumstances of the day I visited, and was clear, concise and very sincere.

This speaks volumes about the impression they're working on, and the relationship they're building with the Nashville community. I was incredibly impressed with the initiative and honest approach and am genuinely excited to return and experience City Winery once again. This follow-up had been truly rewarding for me to witness--I've told several people how impressed I am with the response from the business.
Charles is my absolute favorite server there. He's super friendly and kind. He's very attentive and he's the best! I would recommend him if you come in!
One of the spots around here that I'll refuse to return to if asked. I love a good dive, but this place really had no redeeming qualities, with faux promos that are perennial non-deals...

It is so unfortunate that this place has such a high rating on yelp (the main reason we chose to come here). The food was nothing to write home about. Most of the food was perfectly good but nothing spectacular or original. The only thing that comes close to being an exception is the apple pie that we bought and took home- if I were in the area and in the mood for pie I would certainly buy it from here! A classic done well and deliciously. 

My biggest issue besides the lack of excitement from the menu is the complimentary biscuits that come to the table. They come on a plate alongside three of the restaurants jams which were yummy. The biscuits themselves were dry and tough- not what I prefer from a biscuit. If you genuinely like a tougher biscuit then these are the ones for you. 

I ordered the meatloaf with coleslaw and green beans, all was perfectly fine. My meatloaf was covered in too much sauce which had a very strongest ketchup taste. 

Don't get me wrong, the service was fantastic and the food was good, but all home-style and done as boring as possible. 

To note, the atmosphere is very charming along with the exterior little shops that have cute boutique-style gifts and souvenirs. This is an absolute tourist trap and will attract a specific set of people but did not appeal to me and I would not come here again.

There aren't enough words to describe how good the food is a Loveless Cafe. During busy times get ready to wait at least an hour, but it will definitely be worth it. The staff is very friendly and quick. The food tastes amazing and the portions are big enough to have leftovers, unless you're really hungry. The biscuits don't stop coming and they taste amazing with either the butter or jams.

We drove 30 minutes from Nashville to go try this place and got there to find out there is an hour and 40 minute wait to even get seated. Didn't get to try the food because we were not willing to wait a ridiculous 2 hours after driving 30 minutes there. We drove back to Nashville to the tavern and we were seated within 5 minutes. WASTE OF TIME!

An incredible meal for our first night in town. We had a blast. The service was exceptional, the beers were good and obviously the wine selection was second to none. The Nashville Hot Chicken eggrolls were a killer starter, and very much got us in the vibe. I couldn't have been more impressed with the steak frites - perfect. We both enjoyed everything, and had a truly romantic and special night thanks to the City Winery team. Plus, was walking distance to our hotel - very nice bonus! Great meal, great time. Thanks for a fabulous night!

Oh my goodness. Loved the food here!! Not cheap though. We moved here from Texas so maybe that's just the prices here in Nashville. We went on a weekday morning and there was no wait. Very friendly staff!! Will return!!!

Shout out to Loveless Cafe for feeding my daughter while she's away at school in Nashville!   We love you guys and visit every time we are in Tennessee.  The food is as amazing as the people there! Thank you!!

Came here based on the high online ratings. The beer was really good. The food was not good. It wasn't bad either - It was just...there. Everything we had was bland. We started with the giant pretzel and bier cheese dip. The pretzel was so overdone, like a rock. The bier cheese had zero taste. Husband had a brat, I had the German mac 'n cheese with chicken. He said his was all right. To add chicken to mine was $6, and it was the tiniest portion of some of the driest chicken I've ever had. All in all, we were extremely disappointed to have spent $60+ on our dry, bland meal. Maybe we just didn't order the right things...Or maybe we just didn't have enough beer to make those things taste good. We won't be returning to find out.

This is a really good breakfast spot. Forewarning you will encounter a wait, but that just makes the food more enjoyable. I loved their bite sized biscuits. Gravey wasn't my favorite though. It wasn't bad it just was not my favorite. The blackberry jam though was pretty delectable. Definitely will return.

We were in town on a recent morning, early for a Predators game and decided to stop in. We hadn't done our homework so didn't realize the restaurant wasn't open for lunch, so decided to just do the wine tasting. The 4 wines - 2 white and 2 red - were of varieties not native to the region, which was refreshing. However, neither of us were enamored of the taste, though I'm not saying they were bad. When we went to purchase some (in order to defer the $10 tasting fee), found the 2 bottles priced at $50! Not competitive!

Off the main drag in downtown Nashville with less expensive drinks and shots.  Great live music.  Atmosphere is a bit rowdy and bathrooms are kinda rough, but it's the perfect spot to get the night started before frequenting the more pricey bars on broadway.  We always have a good time here.

Not worth the hype. The staff lost their friendliness when I made a comment that my order was wrong. Disappointed because I heard great things about their subpar biscuits. The jam and their sugar glazed ham were absolutely delicious, though.

Food was pretty good, but a totally disinterested staff, from hostess, to waiter, to valet.   Horrible service.  Most employees more interested in chatting with each other or tied to their phones rather than taking care of guests.  It took an hour and 15 minutes from the time we sat down to the time we got our food, and the place was only half-occupied.  The water was friendly, but didn't understand how to actually be a waiter.  Not attentive.  My wife and I stood outside of the restaurant for fifteen minutes  at the end of the night trying to find a taxi or uber.  There were SIX employees standing outside.  None of them offered to help.  They were all looking at their phones.  Wish I had a picture.  Bizarre.

Very disappointing. On a recent trip to Nashville, our Lyft driver suggested we try the place. We made the scenic drive to Loveless cafe and waited around for our number to come. The biscuits and jams were very good but the breakfast items we ordered were the worst omelette/waffle we have ever had. The salsa in omelette didn't feel fresh at all and we could barely get through half of our meal. Wouldn't recommend if you are a tourist and short on time

This place has been on my list for quite some time. I really wish I had gotten there sooner. It is a little pricey, but well worth it. I went for breakfast and everything was perfect and arrived exactly as I had ordered it. I had a couple mimosas that were also fantastic and served in Mason Jars. 

The wait was about 30 minutes, but it went by quickly as I explored the gift shops. I've heard about their fried chicken so I decided to order some of that to take home for lunch and dinner. The chicken was fantastic, but the greens were the best I've had other than those prepared by my mom or one of her sisters. If you're on a diet you will need the strength of a bull to not cheat on your diet here.

I was excited to see what all the fuss was about. Not realizing it was 30 min from downtown Nashville, we made the drive anyway. It must be worth it right? We waited 30 min to be seated and then about 45 to get our food, on a Monday at 10:30. Biscuits were pretty good. Ham smelt like a wet dog, eggs were touching the ham so I was not interested, pretty disappointed.

OMG the best fried chicken I have ever had in my entire life.  One of my friends shed a tear and the other licked her fingers and said "I didn't know people really did that! " it was so good.  They even have all you can eat chicken or meatloaf with great sides and unlimited biscuits.  The wait is terrible but there are shops to pass the time. Only disappointment was watermelon wasnt in season they said so I couldn't get the watermelon moonshine. Highly recommend.  Worth the drive and the wait.

Great service here. Amazing food. They serve breakfast all day too. The waiter was very patient even though we squeezed extra people into the table and separate tickets. A traditional place to go if you are in Nashville. It's nice to get outside of the city and see their shops. Only piece of criticism I have is the sweet tea was not very good and their pancakes are not to die for so stick to the steak biscuits.

If I could give this place 0 stars for service I would. 

My mother and aunt are coming into town to visit me and city winery has always been on our list of places to go in Nashville. 

A month ago we made reservations for dinner here, but they called and said they rented the whole place out and needed to cancel our reservations. Totally understandable. So we rescheduled and made a winery tour the next day. Well they just called and cancelled that for the exact same reason. 

Two cancellations was already a let down, but beyond that, the staff was incredibly rude and condescending on the phone, which makes me not even want to go to this place at all. They are not trying to accommodate us for their doings at all. If you are going to cancel multiple reservations for paying customers then you need to have public and private times separate and only allow for reservations at those times. This is getting ridiculous. 

We're supposed to go to a concert there that night, but will they cancel that too?
Been here for dinner and brunch and so good both times! And for some reason there was no wait both times. Great atmosphere and near downtown Nash! Highly recommend.

One word: Fun! 
Another word: Authentic!
The final word: GO!!!!

With a graduate degree in creative writing, I could go on and on, but I really said everything I needed to say above. 

So, here we go again. 

One word: Fun!
Another word: Authentic! 
Final word: GO! ! I

Don't make reservations here as the restaurant does not honor them.  The hostess will tel you to wait as if you had no reservation at all.  The food is good but don't be fooled by the reservations they offer.

We came for a songwriters night in the upstairs Lounge.  City Winery has valet parking or there's a pay lot close by. The lounge is a long open room with nice low lighting which sets the tone for an intimate evening. You can sit at the long bar or at shared tables. The menu was upscale and offered several vegetarian options, which you don't always find at a music venue.  We tried the burrata which was served with toasted ciabatta bread and marinated tomatoes. Also had the evening's special vegetable flatbread. The flatbread was served round like a pizza, and was flavorful. The stage is set off to one side at the end of the room and the sound was great. A great place to hear live music and enjoy dinner.
Pretty much blah blah blah food. Not tasty...just your run of the mill so called southern food...which is what?

Compared to all the food places Nashville offered, I wasn't a huge fan of this place. My food didn't come out hot, and the taste was mediocre. The chicken was overly dried, but the biscuits were definitely delicious. A cute spot, but would not come back.
AMAZING!!! Pimento Cheese & fried green tomatoes biscuit! I will just leave it there. Oh, and OWEN, our server, was AWESOME!

Best Home cooking yet. Friendly Staff. Fabulous biscuits..I can't say enough good things about them. The fried pork chops and meatloaf were amazing. They positively without a doubt make the best banana pudding I have ever had

Yummy! Authentic German dishes. Beer garden style seating. Just a great feeling to eat, drink, and be merry. I recommend starting with a giant pretzel. Reuben sandwich and a hot bacon spinach salad for lunch. If you like German beers they've plenty including a tasting tray. Good service too.

I bought a ticket for my dream Justin Nozuka! When I arrived I was super excited for his concert. I purchased multiple wines and pizza downstairs then I  came up to the venue. Once in the venue I ordered more wine and food. After a few songs I had multiple people coming by shushing me, come to find out it was management saying I needed to respect the other customers. What about me...I'm a customer too! I spoke with the manager I guess and she again said this is a listening room yet Justin wanted his audience to enjoy and dance and sing, this is a listening room so we have to be quiet and respect the customers. Again I paid like them and ordered food and drinks. I would not come to this place if you would like to actually enjoy the show. If you wanna go to a show and be quiet go to the library.

Taste: 5
Value: 5

When in Nashville, it was time to see what everyone was talking about! 

Expect to wait about an hour. You can roam around the little row of shops to find jams and things for home or little knick knacks. If it's not too hot, you can find the outdoor spot with cornhole!

Drinks were good. I had to try the moonshine drink which came with a souvenir shot glass. They also make their own bloody mary mix which tasted classic. 

The fried chicken was cripsy yet moist. And the breakfast plate and perfectly salted ham. The star of the show though were the free biscuits and jam! We took a huge box to go!!!

My husband was on a self~guided tour of the South and selected the well~known Loveless Cafe for supper. Splendid looking menu but in reality~~not so much. The famous biscuits arrived tough, tasteless, tiny. The homemade mashed potatoes were obviously from a box. The reference to the staff arriving before dawn to make the sides from scratch is puzzling. Opening a box of instant mashed potatoes shouldn`t merit early arrival. Squash casserole mainly overcooked squash, not a lot of flavor.

The fried half~chicken, however, was fabulous!

Made it out for breakfast with the parents.   Biscuits great of course but having them prior to meal is bad. I put away two before my huge plate of bacon, eggs and potatoes arrived!  Walked away stuffed and happy with excellent from the excellent service. Be back soon I hope.

They don't play German music. Instead it's a bunch of idiots trying to rap gangster songs and use an occasional German reference. In past was much better with polka music. This is the D- team. I've seen better music on a New York Subway. Make this place fun and authentic. Not a guy wearing a Green Bay packers jersey trying to be funny. He is not. Idiot.

This really is as good as it gets for German Food in Nashville. There's options for those that don't like traditional dishes and for those on special diets. If you like beer, food, and a great time, this is a winner. 

We prefer to eat in the cocktail area if there are only a few of us, but for a large group the main dinning area is perfect! 

Don't forget desert!

My family and I went to Loveless Café after a red eye flight from Los Angeles and immediately turned to Loveless Café after taking a peek at the reviews on Yelp. The reviews were definitely accurate! We walked in right as it opened, and the servers were incredibly kind and made us feel special. Loveless Café is known for its biscuits, so as soon as our server set them on the table, we dug in. They came with three different jellies: boysenberry, strawberry, and orange marmalade. The orange marmalade was personally my favorite although I'm usually not a fan. The biscuits definitely lived up to our expectations. The rest of the food was amazing as well. The servers and the wonderful food made our visit to the Loveless Café worth while.

Wonderful down-home food. Made sure we stopped after a recommendation from a friend. I wound come here time and time again. All 3 of our loved our food. Catfish, BBQ pork and Chicken strips. Creamed sweet corn, Wow! Hash brown Casserole, mmmm! Biscuits and jam to die for.  Make this place a must stop when in near Nashville.

We started with the Reuben  egg roll . Only complaint was that the thousand island dressing was a bit bland. Very good sauerbraten, generous portions.  Not too 'saur' medium tang. We were surprised that it was not served with spaetzel, but the cold sliced German potato salad was very good. Red cabbage also tasty. Monster sized yummy Black Forest cake finished us off.

Stay far away!  Dishonest people work and hang out there.  The place smells like dirty water and the broken beer bottles are all over the place.  If you go bring your own bouncer to protect you from all the low life in there.  It is not a safe place to hang out.

Service was great and food is fantastic. You feel like you've stepped right into Germany when you arrive. From the music, to family style table, to beer, and even the outfits of the wait staff; it's as authentic as it gets. Even the gift shop features all the German favorites. One of my favorites when I'm in town from Atlanta
Love the big pretzels. Recommend requesting spicy mustard or try the beer cheese dip. It comes with a Dijon/sweetish mustard.

ENGAGED COUPLES BEWARE! The advertised $15.9K "full service" wedding package ACTUALLY costs almost $70K after fees and charges (with NO 'upgrades')! SEE ATTACHED PHOTOS. 

We inquired here for their larger "full service" wedding package, It explicitly advertises for "80-250 guests" as read in the first line.  We are expecting around 170 guests and felt this particular package was appropriate. We communicated for weeks via email and booked a tour with the staff. We knew that the full service package did not include the bar/drinks which was fine. We chose none of the many 'upgrades' and opted out of extra costs for decor/lighting/drapes to see what the actual starting price came out to.

We thought there had been a mistake and were sent someone else's quote because the cost breakdown line items are completely different than what the package describes, and there was never any mention of a $10K admin fee. When confronted about the $50K difference in price although we chose none of the 'upgrades', their explanation is that each guest over the 80th is charged with the "additional guest" penalty fee instead of over the 250th, as written. When advertised as a 80-250 guest package, the number is false, and it is only priced *up to 80. 

This package called the "Flute" package is their largest package offered, using the largest room of this venue, as well as multiple others - Having only 80 guest spread around this large of a space would be laughable and makes no sense. They're trying to pull a fast one on families who are emotionally hyped. Shameful tactics. It's totally fine if $70K is the budget you have, but City Winery should be honest and transparent about the actual cost vs what they advertise. (Attached are photos of print ad vs official final proposal) 

Choose City Winery - One wedding, for the price of three!

We held a private company event here recently and it was a hit. The appetizers were enjoyed, the drink selection was good, and the staff were on top of their game. They gave us our own separate room and it was the perfect fit.

Hash brown casserole was amazing! Green beans and Mac & Cheese really good. Bought the strawberry jam to take home with us. Great experience overall. Kind staff. Cute shops. We are staying downtown Nashville and it took us 30 minutes to get here and that was at 1030am.

This was the most amazing breakfast I have ever had. From the welcoming smiles to the warm biscuits it was heaven.  I had the pulled pork with pancakes and eggs.  The pork was so tasteful and juicy.  The hash brown casserole is a must.   The wife had fried chicken and waffles and it was juice tender and packed with flavor. Take the ride and go experience this magical place.

Waffles and bacon hit the spot and were oh so delicious. The homemade biscuits are mouth watering and salted butter added extra flavor to everything. The jams tasted homey like my grandma was in the back making them. Mary, our waitress, was sweet and helpful with getting coffee to go after we finished. Would come back again!

If it wasn't for the big sign we still would have been able to locate Loveless Cafe based on the great smells alone. The wait wasn't too long, but they have cute little shops to check out while you're waiting anyways. The staff was friendly and recommended a lot of things. The Biscuits and Jam are a must along with the Chicken and Waffles. It was probably the most crispy yet juicy and flavorful chicken I've ever had. It was a little out of the way for me but worth it!

Great place to go with a wonderful atmosphere! Bar area is nice size and a very nice assortment of Beers from which to choose! My choice for the night was the Grapefruit Beer... YUMMY
Appetizers were really good as well had the pretzel and the flatbread between us and would definitely order again...
I tried some of the sausages my favorite was the smoked then the Jalapeño one.. red cabbage was not to sweet and the kraut was just sour enough!! 
Hubby had the pork chop  with the beef as well.
Tried the Dessert tray with small portions of 3 desserts favorite out of the Apple Strudel, Black Forrest cake and the Pretzel Pudding ? Definitely the pretzel pudding!! They make it in house

Visiting here is a unique experience that intertwines shopping and dinning, but my fandom for the food is fading  due to the decreased quality. We were there at 5:30, so it wasn't really a slow time, but there also was not a wait to be seated (which can be very common).  In the past, I have referred to their fried chicken as "the best I've ever eaten," but this visit was a sad rendition of a classic that came nowhere close to what it used to be.  I have a strong suspicion that the chicken was old because it was tough and dry. Usually, I would send food of this low quality back to the kitchen, but after a long day, it just didn't enter my mind.  There were a few food highlights like the peach preserves and the fried green tomatoes (which were very good, and we had to wait longer on those than the rest of our food, which should have given me a clue about the chicken). Service was very accommodating. I'll lay this one visit off as a "not up to their normal game" day, and give it another shot down the road.

With all the hype I expected better. Yes the biscuits are great. We had the chicken and waffles and basically it was a tasteless chicken breast with the bone on top of a waffle. Nothing special. I had better in MA!

We have been lovers of Loveless for 30 years. It's all about the biscuits and fried chicken. We made many a pilgrimage to the restaurant when we lived in the Nashville area for 20 years and make sure to return with each visit back.

The wait time can be substantial. It's best to arrive after 1:00 and before 5:00. If you can, ask for a table in the original house section at the front of the restaurant. The add on area is loud and rushed, resembling the ambience of a Cracker Barrel 

Order the fried chicken or better yet, the fried chicken livers. And don't fill up on biscuits and homemade preserves, you will need the stomach space.

What a lovely place! My husband and I took an Uber to visit here. This was the most expensive Uber ride that I have ever paid for and it was totally worth it! The cafe was a part of a farm. The service was excellent!

We had the biscuits with jams. I thought the jams weren't necessary. Biscuits were fluffy and yummy by themselves. I had the Biscuit Sampler Platter with fried green tomato & pimento cheese, barbeque, and fried chicken. They all tasted very good, especially the fried chicken! My husband got the country ham, which I thought it was too salty. We both had hashbrown casserole as our sides. It tasted so buttery and creamy, which was something I have never had before.

We also got the mini dessert sampler with chess pie, fudge pie, and coconut pie. I think my favorite was the coconut pie, which wasn't too sweet.

I visited City Winery for happy hour last week.  I thought everything about the place was lovely--nice ambiance, friendly staff, great happy hour specials.  There are just a couple weird things to note--if you want to enjoy happy hour, you must sit at the bar (not near the bar or at a table in the bar, but at the bar, proper).  This could quickly translate into you not getting a seat if you don't arrive early.  Another note on arriving early--I did, so I could park my own car, which was great.  My friends weren't so lucky, they had to valet for $5.00--not cool in a town where free valet is pretty much the norm.  I enjoyed the experience and will return for happy hour, for sure.

First ever review. I have been a couple times already and love the place, however, today (4-21 at 3:10) I walked in and sat at the bar only to be let down. It wasn't very busy, not not like I was expecting, and yet the entire 10 minutes I sat there I received no service. There were many open seats and the bartenders seemed to be more interested in carrying on in their conversation on the other side of the bar; I couldn't even wave them down. The few times they walked by, again the were deep in conversation and ringing up other tickets and didn't even acknowledge me. I'm sorry to sound so sour but this is the only thing that drives me crazy at restaurants. At least acknowledge me if you're busy. I'll try again some other time...

Just a pleasant experience every time. Fresh beer, surprisingly good German food for a place like Nashville, stereotypical but fun oom-pah music, and excellent service. Not quite at the level of my favorite German restaurants in other cities but much better than I ever dreamt of finding here, and I leave every time with a smile on my face. What's not to like about that?

Superb atmosphere and really good food! Cool little piece of Bavaria right in Nashville. Bier is great, food is superb. I had the Black Forest Schnitzel and the wife had the Bavarian Onion Soup. We shared the Brotzeitteller and all was excellent. Had a couple liters of Bier and she has the Spätlsse Riesling. Really cool experience and wonderful staff. Highly recommended!!!

My mom brought us here because of all the hype surrounding the place. With such fame, I expected a long wait but great food. We really only ended up waiting half an hour, and there were a lot of small shops to pass the time.

We ended up sitting on the outdoor porch, which was pretty serene, but the experience was somewhat ruined by the flies. Then, the biggest issue of the meal arose: the service. Nobody waited on us initially, and we actually had to ask for service. After taking our orders, we really only saw our waitress again once or twice, even though we requested more biscuits and needed frequent refills.
