The food was phenomenal. Every single thing we ordered was scrumptious, and the biscuits and preserves lived up to their legendary status. The food easily earns 5 stars, but the service was unbearable. Still, highly recommended for anybody in the area.

Loveless is fun & excellent quality.  Their fried chicken is very good, mashed potatoes and chicken gravy fantastic, biscuits great, BBQ brisket great, and the service was excellent.  We waited 1.5hrs and it was worth it.  BBQ. pit master and I talked BBQ for almost the entire 1.5hrs.  It was a great time.

Yes, it is a dive bar and off the typical Broadway Nashville beat. However, it is worth a stop. We stopped through on our "Music City Pub Crawl" tour and we came back multiple times after. The $5 "double shotz" are excellent and hit you unexpectedly - the "dirty pirate hooker" was definitely a fan favorite.

They should be a shame to call themselves a German restaurant. I was so looking forward to their sauerbrauten and i was very disappointed as to what i got. The meat was very tough and the gravy was nothing like gingersnaps. I sorry to write this, but is was not worth my time or money.

I had bought concert tickets here and decided to eat dinner here last minute, as well. First impression walking in: gorgeous ambiance. The lounge area is very open with lots of wood finishings and a round staircase surrounded by wine bottles. Very pretty. 

Our dinner included: fried risotto balls, chicken fricasse, pork belly, lemon olive oil cake, and a few glasses of wine. Overall, I was pretty pleased with the meal, especially the pork belly which was crisp and succulent. The risotto balls were also good and reminded me of falafel. The sweet jam that comes with the lemon olive oil cake was the best part of the dish, but next time I'll probably order the chocolate stout cake which I couldn't stop drooling over from looking at it from the table next to me. 

Dinner here is definitely not cheap. Our meal (for 2) came out to be $140 without tip. Plus, they charge an exorbitant amount of tax since they charge you liquor tax as well. Why the establishment (a "winery") doesn't pay it itself is kind of strange.  Also, valet parking is $5. Good luck finding parking elsewhere. 
 
The concert itself was pretty good, although considering that this establishment hosts many musicians and artists, the acoustics weren't the best. Maybe it was an off night. 

Overall, I'm glad I was able to have the full dining experience here although next time there's a show, I'll probably eat dinner elsewhere first; It's hard to justify the price.

Bavarian Bierhaus is fun!  The bench seating is unusual, but provides for conversation and sharing with others at the table.    They have an amazing beer selection, and I really enjoyed my flight.  And the pretzels are awesome (and huge).

My wife knows more about German food than I do, and she absolutely loved the Rouladen.  She said that it reminded her of favorites from her youth.  I had the Pork Schnitzel and thought it was excellent.  We took home some Appelstrudel for late-evening dessert.

The staff really added to the fun factor.  They are in costume, and are very knowledgeable about their menu.  And the live music contributed to the authentic German atmosphere.  I do not like going to Opry Mills, but the Bavarian Bierhaus makes it worthwhile.

Visited City Winery on July 10th to see the Bacon Bros. I was initially impressed with the upscale ambience and decor. After being seated and realizing our evening was to be spent sitting extremely close to another couple, it was downhill all the way. Our server seemed to get confused at every step. We ordered both the risotto balls and fried green tomatoes as appetizers. Only the FGT arrived... Cold and overcooked. I asked about the other appetizer and was told we didn't order it! They arrived slightly prior to our meal. We both ordered the pan seared grouper. It was overcooked, rubbery, tasteless and on top of what were supposed to be smoked bacon grits. The consistency was more like soup. Again, we were both disappointed. Sides of mac and cheese and haricot verts... again lacking flavor. I asked the server for unsweet tea and was brought diet Pepsi..... twice. Getting our car back from valet was another horror story as we waited in line for 40 minutes! All in all, a $300 very underwhelming evening at a venue I had been excited to experience.

Well I'm in town for work usually hit my "go to" BBQ rib joint before my flight in the morning. Thought I'd change it up and try a different place, lots of hype here. I didn't mind the food and the atmosphere was good live music from the German country side with the long horn.. LOL it's worth a shot if you want a different dining experience. Food was just ok.. nothing to put in a "must have" category first time here so not sure if I made a good dining choice although I did ask the bartender for suggestions. They are ok friendly and keep the beer full think I'll try again and get a different meal maybe.
Delish! Great service and food! Hannah was very nice and helpful. Their biscuits are what KFC biscuits are supposed to taste like LOL.

Biscuits were as good as advertised but, after hearing so much about this place, the rest of the experience fell short of expectations.

The fried okra and fried chicken were equivalent to any other place you can find in Nashville and definitely did not reside in the uppermost tiers of southern cuisine. The coffee was dry and bitter and the Bloody Mary was easily one of the worst I've had. 

Sausage and gravy was the only saving grace in this meal and I would probably stick to that and other breakfast entrees if I ever come back here (which I do not plan on).

This place is definitely worth the wait. Went with a party of 8 and it took approximately 1 hour to be seated. You don't even notice as they have 2 markets on site and cute photo ops. The actual restaurant has a very homey feel with pictures hung on the wall. The food is amazing and the portions are good to share. They're biscuits are great and they bring out 3 different types of jams. I would definitely recommend this restaurant.

No, NO, NOOO - a thousand times NO! I cannot vouch for what this place used to be when it was privately owned. Certainly quaint and a great setup - but the food (breakfast) was horrible. Given that this is a place for Country Ham, biscuits and all the fixins', they ain't up to it. Ham was not up to any other place that serves it, redeye gravy incredibly weak. Biscuits - doods - quit using baking soda with aluminum - like sticking an aluminum plate in your mouth. Plus, they had a terrible sweet afterbite when dipped in Redeye. Jelly and Jams were good, but ain't why you go out to eat. Interesting - asked for eggs over easy and was told that that meant the yolk would be close to hard. Let's try turning down the heat on the stove. In short - if you can't fix eggs right, where do you rise from. If you can't fix Country Ham right - then don't call yourselves Country.

Now, I know there are thousands of country stars plastered on the walls. Cool, but these folks know their mamma and grandma made better. I'd take my picture down.

As hard as it is to get Country Ham, I make it all the time - I beat this place hands down - which means they don't make the cut for a place I'd go out to.

Really sad part is that I was visiting from out of town and was told this was the place for country cooking. If you mean breakfast - forget it...

Absolutely a must if you visit Nashville. It's like sitting in your grandmas kitchen having breakfast. The food is great, all of it. The country ham is wonderful. The fried pork chops and gravy are my favorite. It can be a wait on the weekends if you don't get there early but there are things to see and do on the grounds and it's worth the wait.

Bland tasting food at an extortionate price. Incredibly small portions for what they're asking and the menu seemed confused.  I ordered the cheeseburger and was shocked at how small it was for how much they were charging. The milkshake tasted like everything else that was in the fridge. Just go to Hugh Baby's or Steak and Shake!

The biscuits did not disappoint! And I would eat the homemade jam with a spoon. Yum. Between the five in our party we tried the pork chops, steak, BBQ ribs, and the fried chicken. Everything was great! And the sides taste homemade as advertised.

I went to City Winery with 6 other girls for brunch today. After reading all the other negative reviews on yelp, I was a bit apprehensive, especially about the valet parking and the liquor tax, but I promised myself I would keep an open mind. I'm happy to report that I was able to park my own car in the parking lot. (Apparently they don't have valet parking at brunch so I was able to save $5-$8 there, according to varying other reviews.) I also did not order an alcoholic beverage, but the girls who did had double the tax on their bill. City Winery, paying your liquor taxes is a cost of doing business. Shame on you for passing that onto your customers!

I got the huevos rancheros. They were okay. Not impressive. Please note that they put hot sauce on several of their brunch items although it is not listed on the menu. Several of the girls had to send their items back because they can't eat spicy food. 

Once everyone was done with their meals, it took an hour for us to receive our checks. Yes, an HOUR. I'm not exaggerating. I timed it. The other girls were caught up in conversation so I didn't say anything but had I been alone or with my husband, I would not have let that fly.

The ambience here is nice. I love the decor and atmosphere, so I'm going to give it another shot. Probably for dinner next time.

First time visiting TN and was recommended to stop in at Loveless. Food was incredible and our server Barbara was an absolute angel. We ordered half of the menu and had no regrets. Everything was delicious.
Loved the chicken, i fell inlove with this place 4 years ago and will come back for sure everytime im in town!! People are very friendly

I had a friend in town and decided to show her the typical Nashville tourist experience by bringing her to Loveless. We came on a Saturday morning around 10am and had a 45 minute wait. To kill time we checked out their little shops and had a great time looking at all of the cute things. 

When we finally sat down we were greeted with a warm plate of their amazing rolls. The rolls ended up being the highlight of the meal. We ordered the red velvet waffle which tasted just like a regular waffle. I thought it needed some cream cheese icing or something to spruce it up. Then we ordered the fried chicken hoping to experience some of the classic southern cooking that they're known for. The fried chicken turned out to be so dry that it was hardly edible. 

Overall it's a place to try out once but I don't need to go back again, there are better places for southern food elsewhere.

I'm a local, and I rarely come here.  Shame on me, this place is terrific.  Cozy atmosphere. Great food. Friendly, attentive service.  Today I had the country ham, eggs over medium, biscuits, fried okra, and hash browns.  They were all on point.  Rachel was my server, and she provided thoughtful, friendly, attentive service.  Tip for tourists - come in the middle of the day during the week and you can be seated almost immediately.

Make sure to call and see if they're open. Uber'd all the from the city to discover we went on the one day a year they were closed for cleaning/maintenance. Was not advertised anywhere that they would be closed. Great way to start off the morning.

Thank you, Kim, for outstanding service tonight during our show! You were so attentive, sweet and helped us have the best New Year's in a very long time! Food, atmosphere and entertainment was spot on!

Really???? A place for Christian youth that cater to Satanic bands. I know Christians are called to go out and preach the work of the cross to the unsaved. But to bring in, not just the unsaved, but Devil worshipers to entertain the Christian youth? Where is the logic?

everything is delicious!!! i love this place. chicken  and waffles, country ham, french toast, steak and eggs and their aaaaaamazing biscuits and gravy!!! the homemade fruit preserves are a delight.  mmm...

Had a really good lunch here. The food arrived piping hot and very tasty. We had the fish and chips and an order of the rubin sliders. Both tasted great. The Rubin slider is more like a rubin egg roll than a small sandwich but it was very good. Seating is at a long table with benches on either side. Not the most comfortable seat but it keeps with the bierhaus theme of the restaurant. This is somewhere I will go back to again.

We always come to The Loveless when we are in Nashville. It's becoming more and more popular each year we visit. It's the best food breakfast, lunch or dinner. We always take home some blackberry preserves from their shop...so good!

Their bread pudding is amazing here. I was also pleasantly surprised by the chicken and waffles. Not only that, but the biscuits and gravy were pretty good. However, the country steak was meh; that is the only downside to this eatery. I also tried grits for the first time; it didn't taste good at all. Overall, it's a great place for breakfast/brunch. Be sure to get the bread pudding!
Excellent food, service, and environment! We ate early Sunday, before the after-church rush and had no wait.

I'm a fan! Such a cozy place to enjoy a glass of wine (their sparkling moscato is super delicious!!), and a live concert. Paired with the wine, I'd recommend the calamari, ravioli, and the pistachio cake. The pistachio cake has a very strong pistachio flavor which I love, and although it's a very dense cake, the blood orange marmalade and gelato make the cake extra DELICIOUS!! I'm such a fan! Outside of those few menu items, I honestly can't recommend anything else. If anything, try to grab a bite before or after the show!
As for the concert, the lights are low and romantic, there isn't a bad seat you can purchase on the floor, and you get to share a certain level of intimacy with the artist, which is the cherry on top. I love shows here! I can't wait until the next one!

Nashville institution. Not worth the trek for those only in town for the weekend, but certainly put it on your list if you're around a bit longer. The biscuits and jam are heaven! Cozy, down-home country kitchen vibe.

Had a wonderful, romantic dinner on our first night in Nashville - City Winery came highly recommended and fully lived up to and exceeded the hype. The atmosphere was lovely, the service was exceptional and the food and drink were fabulous. I'm not a wine guy, but my Lovely Dining Companion is, and she enjoyed both glasses she tried. Had we not been flying out she would have gotten a wine growler to go for sure. The beer list featured several local options, and I was glad to get to try a  few of them. We started with the Nashville Hot Chicken Eggrolls, which were fully delicious and not overly spicy. I followed a recommendation and had the steak frites, and the ribeye was perfect. My date had the seasonal farro risotto, which had big cherry tomatoes, asparagus, summer squash, spring peas and shaved parmesan. Really a lovely, different and not overwhelming take. While we were tempted by dessert, both of us were full and it was just the start of the night so we didn't want to overdue. Beautiful first meal in a beautiful city, very glad we got to enjoy it together!

Not perfect but I think this place has potential. The patty melt was tasty, though a bit on the small side for the price. The onion rings had too much breading and were on the border between well-seasoned and overly salty, but at least they weren't bland. The blackberry cobbler was delicious and the portion size was ample, but it was lukewarm at best. The music selection was superb and the service at the bar was excellent. And finally, while they're clearly aiming in a different direction with the focus on martinis, I think the addition of milkshakes (boozy or otherwise) and possibly even an adult take on some soda shop classics like egg creams and cherry lime rickeys would fit their theme nicely. 

In short, a mixed bag but there were enough good things to build on that I think this could end up being a decent place.

Beth is the best EVER!! Beth helped me all throughout the night, my boss was playing, so I had to go back and forth between my seat and backstage. Beth walked me around the back to get to backstage and even brought my wallet I left on the table to me!! The food was so good too!

3 of our 5 kids live in Nashville and we visit often so we will definitely be back! The food was delicious, the waitress was patient and friendly with our table of 13 and the kids loved dancing to Rocky Top!!  We had a great time and can't recommend highly enough!

Being married to a German, he wanted to go here since we moved to the Nashville area. He loves all the Bratwurst etc.  Me being a vegetarian always finds something on the German menus. I opted for the dumplings with mushroom gravy. The waiter suggested 1 potato & 1 bread, my husband told me to get 2 potato, but followed the waiters lead. Loved the potato one, the bread one wasn't flavorful or even warm on the inside. When the waiter came back I told him the bread one wasn't good & he just took my plate & said ok. Didn't offer to bring another potato one. This dish was $12.00!  So essentially we paid $12. for 1 potato dumpling. Definitely not worth it!

Manager has promptly contacted us, apologized & said they were planning on taking the bread dumpling off the menu anyway.  This apology went a long way with us & we will definitely visit this restaurant again.

just here for the skate park. brought my nephew here.  skate park is in good shape. there all about safety. staff is very friendly and helpful. they have a coffee shop serves burgers pizza dogs etc. prices aren't bad.  they also have a show venue here that is also a church on sundays.  great to have a safe place to take kids. being here makes me want to check out a show sometime.  Probably over rated the place but the safe haven for kids is worth it.

If you are looking for an authentic German experience, this place is pretty darn close.  Good food, good servers and good entertainment.  There are items on the menu for everyone - even a few choices for vegans.   The atmosphere is very electric when they have performers on stage.  You'd swear you were in a German pub until you walk out the door into the southern humidity.  Do yourself a favor and try it at least once.  I think you'll be back again.

Yes you can go back.
It's been 30 years and we returned.
It was expanded and almost unrecognizable 
from the original.
The food was just as good as I remembered.
We had the family style fried chicken and pulled pork.
The service was spotty but pleasant.
The little shops were a nice addition.

What a wonderful place, went there yesterday at 12:30 and was told would have an hour and a half wait, advised to come after 4 PM. Came back today at 4:30 and got right in. Our party of four had fried chicken meatloaf country fried steak and pulled pork. Everything was excellent and our server Kramer was outstanding. If you're looking for down-home cooking that is not real greasy this is the place. Got desserts to go, all homemade, and will enjoy later.

I've been to Loveless once, on my last trip to Nashville, from California and I was looking forward to another meal until now. I am coming out again for a visit next week and I will be skipping it and unliking their FB page and unfollowing them on pinterest due to the LACK of customer service and complete disregard of a person's holiday as displayed by the review posted yesterday. I am appalled how unkind the staff was. There are so many fabulous places to eat in Nashville that I am glad to say I can cross Loveless OFF my must do's list for future trips. Really disappointed. Disgusted is more like it. We have better Southern Hospitality in California than Loveless showed.  And don't worry, I'll share this on social media to make sure everyone knows how Loveless treats customers.
Amazing jewel out in the middle of nowhere. Great southern comfort food. Everyone was amazing. Great service.

Order to go on a beautiful day! They have a lot of picnic tables. Okay so it's Good food (especially the biscuits!) but I don't know about an hour long wait. It was our third attempt at coming for breakfast and we got smart and decided to Order our on the app. It was perfect we placed our order and walked around the cute little area and we got our food in 30 mins. My favorite was the biscuits!!! And meat loaf. My husband loved the hashbrown casserole! Overall it was good but next time we wouldn't make the drive out here we would go check somewhere else instead.
Like everyone else, was overcharged.  Server lady had bad attitude even though I was all smiles.  1 star for the attitude, nothing but remorse for overpaying.

I absolutely love Loveless! Every time someone comes in from out of town, I take them here! Their food is always amazing, and the experience is so fun! There is usually a wait on the weekends, but that's okay, because you can go through the shops or play corn hole.

This is a giant hostile gift shop rather than a restaurant. Wait is too long. Staff is not friendly. Biscuits are not delicious as advertised. Turns out the secret ingredient is non-dairy creamer. There's a reason people prefer real cream to non-dairy creamer. Actually some of the worst biscuits I've tried! Fried chicken was horrendous. I really wanted to like this place since I actually live nearby but had a bad experience here twice! Get ready to wait at least an hour before you get seated. Their business model seems to be making you wait a long time so that you buy stuff at their gift shops. This may have been a good breakfast place at one point in history but obviously they have let the quality of the food slide as it has become more of a tourist zoo. I will not be coming here again! 

Also when we finally were seated after waiting over an hour, over half the tables were open. Not sure why they are having so much trouble seating people!

Consistently good food. All the southern favorites like fried chicken, ham, greens, fish, and amazing desserts. Very generous portions and top notch sweet tea. It's always crowded so make sure you give yourself time.

The Good: A hidden gem in Nashville. Music was great; atmosphere was terrific; exceptional service. 

Nice food and drink selection. Wines on tap; other spirits. Great music and events. Looking forward to going back!
Today, we had Regan as our server. We had just gotten off of our red-eye flight and she welcomed us with so much hospitality. Food was also fantastic! Must-go location!

A bit of a tourist trap, and not inexpensive, but you gotta love those biscuits. Terrific handmade jellies and jams too. Very hard to get a bad meal here, and service is top notch. We always take people here when they visit TN. It's a guaranteed bright spot in everyone's visit to Music City.

Horrible service! Server had no idea what the Restaurant Week special was (on day 4). Ordered cheese dip, he didn't bring it. Checked on us for the first time after we were 99% done. 

The only reason they got two stars is because the food was okay. And I mean... just okay. Nothing special.

so, we drove almost an hour and had to wait about 90 minutes to be seated. 
no, pressure, loveless cafe. we only have a 13-hour ride back to nj ahead of us. nbd.

wait, actually- lots of pressure!!. the biscuits better be life-changing. 

THEY WERE. 
holy moly, these are some phenomenal eats. 

the biscuits. THE biscuits. oh em gee. i've never had a biscuit like this, and i can't stop craving them.  paired with the homemade preserves, they were AWESOME. and endless. (no, this is not a joke).

since this was our last meal in TN, i went BBQ... pulled pork over corn cakes, with sides of fried okra and cole slaw. it was SO yummy. i was pretty full from the endless biscuits (mmmmm biscuits), but the flavors of the bbq sauce and coleslaw to cut the richness were great. the fried okra was good too. it tasted good as a snack in the car a few hours later, too!

honestly, i'd go back and wait and wait and wait again. there are a few gift shops that share the parking lot, including a kitchen store that i believe sells some sandwiches (and they give out samples!). they have coffee and tea outside, which makes waiting even easier. 

5 stars for the biscuits. 4.5 stars for the rest of the food. and a definite drop to 4 stars for the service. 
our waitress was abrupt, barely made eye contact, and was almost impossible to catch. definitely not the southern hospitality i was hoping for from this place.

don't skip it. 
and if you're heading to or through the central nj area afterward, bring me some biscuits!! (pretty please?)
Best restaurant in Nashville. Not only is the food fresh and delicious, the service is friendly, fun. Overall a perfect experience.

Oh My! Just as good as advertised. We waited almost an hour but it was definitely worth the wait. Our group did the family style with country ham and sausage and it was amazing! As good of a breakfast as i've ever had. The biscuits and preserves were out of this world. I threw my low carb diet to the side to eat those biscuits! I will most definitely be back if ever in the area again!

Skip the bbq biscuit. It's $3.50 and TINY. Complete price gouge. Should be like maybe $1.50 if that. It's just the lack of respect for the customer. It was decent. (Honestly it was cold when served). The rest of the food was diner breakfast food, nothing crazy. It gets some respect for the location. But if they keep up the downward slide like this, it'll only be tourists coming and that will shortly fall of because of the drive.
We stopped here while in Nashville. We loved the biscuits!! But my meal was amazing smoked pork chops with a peach glaze. Delicious!

The service was good the location was nice and the beer was good.  With that said I will say I've had cheaper and better German food at other restaurants but this area doesn't really have many other options for German food.  If you have a craving this will do but don't expect anything spectacular.

This place is terrible!!! The bartender purposely overcharged us a beer because my mom left. When we received our bill and paid we told that he over charged us he didn't do anything and got super defensive. If you come here I would suggest watching what you buy and check your tab closely. I would not recommend coming here!!!

I've eaten here once several months ago with a few friends. I wasn't especially impressed. There food was okay and I definitely think it was overpriced. The service was good and I thought the "much touted" biscuits were so-so. Bear in mind when you read this, I am by no means a connoisseur.

The Bavarian Bierhaus is truly legit German food, and everything was amazing!

I'll start by saying that it is located in Opry Mills Mall.  When we entered, the band was playing and had about 20 or so people up dancing the chicken dance.  Whether you were dancing or watching, everyone certainly appeared to be having an amazing time!  The style of the restaurant is Oktoberfest themed, with the giant communal picnic tables.  It's so cool to meet and have conversations with people you've only just met.  We truly enjoyed ourselves, and made new friends we'll remain in contact with after this.

I'll start with the beer, and I'm not a beer drinker.  They provided 3 different samples for the Yelp Elites to try.  The Pilsner was the lightest. And to my utter surprise, it was delicious!  Way to go Bavarian Bierhaus!!  I'm super impressed    My husband enjoyed the hefe, a lot!!

The food....WOW!!!  The pretzels were amazing, and were great with the beer cheese.  Everyone else must've agreed also because there was only a smidgen of it left to try.  I heard the fresh mustard sauce was to die for, but I never got to try it.  The sliced brats in kraut......5star all by it self.  The were cooked to perfection, and the kraut~~~I wish I could've taken of order of it home with me.

I will most definitely be back!!!
I forgot to mention that Kellie Pickler and Ben showed up to visit and join in our stein holding contest.  I guess she was the prize for the three Yelp Elites that won the contest Yelp the stein holding contests.

Ok I ordered every single side from this place (in one sitting) and I can tell you they are ALL avery approved. Not to mention the biscuits- mmm mmm good. I had the peach pork chops- mouth is watering as I type. This place can do no wrong. 

Now, when you're driving there you're going to be thinking "Avery, is this worth it?" "Avery am I heading into a scene from Deliverance?" Emphatically yes and emphatically no, respectively.

It's a little out of the way, but so worth the wait. The restaurant has a little country store and what nots to do you can take some of that goodness home with you... you have been enlightened... you're welcome!

If you are looking for some delicious Southern food this is the place to dine. While there is normally a wait, there is plenty of shopping and seats outside for relaxing. The meals are always started with homemade biscuits and jam, and no matter what you order for your main course you will not be disappointed. The food is delicious and I've never had bad service. Whether you live in the Nashville area or just visiting this place is a must go for all.

We've been here before and yes, the biscuits were good and the honey bar-b-que chicken was fantastic.  However, the fried chicken was overdone and tough.  Some of our other food was just so so.  

That being said, I am glad we came back and ate here again but I don't think we'll stop in the next time we are in town.

This is a 3.5-3.7 star review for the food. We came at 10am on Father's Day and the wait was an hour. It was supposed to be 1:40, but we were not leaving until we experienced the food!

While we waited, we walked to the two stores. The clothing merch store was meh. However, the main shop was a tourist trap that we all were will to succumb to on this trip. I got the biscuit flour mix and snacks to bring home for the kids. 

Tons of shades for kids to hang around and grassy area for people to hang out and stay in the shade. 

The wait staff was friendly. The food was solid. I had expected more from the hype, especially the fried chicken, but it was just ok. 

Meats:  Fried chicken thigh meat--good but the breading was ok. I had expected more flavors. The grilled catfish was really salty. The fried catfish was ok.  You'll want to dip it in the pepper vinegar.c which is great. The pulled pork was the best protein there. Yum. 

Fried okre, green tomatoes--ok. Is it bad that I like the fried okre from Golden Corral in CA more?

Creamed corn--this was amazing. 

Casserole hash brown--ok. 

Fermented cheese with biscuit--meh

Buscuits--delicious with the jams.

I'd give more stars if I could! People are not lying when they say this is a must go to spot when you're in Nashville. I know they are known for their biscuits, which are delicious but the jams is where it's at! They are beyond words amazing!!! I'm not a gravy person what so ever but my boyfriend is so we shared biscuits and gravy (I figured I'd just eat the biscuits plain) the gravy was so delicious I was dunking as much of the biscuit as I could into the gravy until I couldn't eat anymore! We also shared the chicken & waffles which I might add was more than enough food for the two of us! Everything was delicious and I love that you can walk around the property while waiting for your table, it makes the time pass way faster and the gift shop with the jams and other cute decor is a must see!

City Winery was generic and didn't have that great of an environment.  We came for an after dinner drink, but couldn't get the attention of any of the waitstaff.  We went to the bar ourselves for service instead.  The wine was decent but nothing special.

I came for the biscuits and I'm happy to report they are as delicious as everyone says. I decided to try them with all the jams they come with and was pleasantly surprised at how much I liked the blackberry. I usually don't like blackberry anything, but this smothered in a buttery biscuit was a little piece of heaven.

I shared the garden omelette, which was stuffed with mushrooms, peppers, and onions and also more than enough to share. We also ordered the pimento cheese and fried green tomato biscuit. I'm not a fan of pimento cheese but was told the combination was amazing. I couldn't have tried it even if I wanted to because I'd already stuffed my face with two plates of biscuits. No regrets. 

Oh, and our server was awesome. Hey Lucas!

3.5/5

Probably the most decent place ever. Came around 6 on a saturday and while all the tables were reserved, we found seats open at the bar. Otherwise you would definitely need reservations to get a table. I was not a fan of their wine- the whites were all very sweet and the reds (cab sav and pinot noir) had this whiskey after taste. yuck. We ordered the cheese & the meat try which was $30!! It came with a few pieces of salami and 3 slices of cheese & bread. The rest of the things on the tray were just random fillers to make it look pretty (a slice of carrot, strawberry, blackberry, nuts, honey??). We also spilt a margarita flatbread- the mozzarella completely came off when you would take a bite and didn't have much flavor. I won't be returning.

Good southern cooking. Hashbrown casserole isnt all that good but the rest of the food we had was good. We had chicken and dumplings, sampler with fried chicken, bbq pork and country ham. Kate was very good as a server.

What an incredible experience... and surprisingly at a mall! It literally felt like a stand alone restaurant. Great atmosphere with great food. Much of it verified by the German friends we had with us. Ate the pictures posted (forgot what they all were) and loved every bite. I would totally suggest this to friends who are in the area that don't want BBQ!

We went off Yelp recommendation for a good breakfast place and ended up here. They give you biscuits once you order and there are delicious. I ordered fried chicken and waffles and the chicken was amazing! We enjoyed the atmosphere and the service was good even though it was busy we will return!

We had breakfast here on our drive from Nashville to the Natchez Trace Parkway, Franklin, and Belle Mead. I made reservations for a Monday but probably didn't need it as there were empty tables when we arrived. 

The restaurant is part of a larger complex of buildings that include lodging and a cute store that sells their preserves and biscuit mix. 

We had the following dishes:

* Chicken and Waffle - the white meat was drier than I like
* Fried Chicken and Two Eggs (dark meat) - the dark meat was nice and moist
* Pit-Cooked Pork Barbeque and Two Eggs

The meal came with biscuits, which were moist and delicious, and served with three types of yummy preserves: Strawberry, Blackberry, and Peach.  We loved the biscuits and preserves so much that we had them bring us a second helping!

I would bump the star rating up to 3-1/2 but it isn't an option. The Bier Hall is huge and very reminiscent of German Bier halls. I loved the Bavarian colors, the dried flowers, the Lederhosen,and the picnic style seating (much nicer than picnic tables). I loved the live music but missed the crowd interaction. The seating is too American which encourages people keeping to themselves rather than creating the European feeling of community, inclusion, discovery. The menu is promising offering some favorite staples of the local Ghasthaus in any German village. The execution however is disappointing. The best option we tried was any of the wurst, potato salad, schnitzel. I wish the spatzle was good but every dish of it in our party was mushy and salty.  The large potato dumplings were closer to mashed potatoes than a dumpling. The bread served is a pumpernickel rye instead of the traditional pumpernickel or brotchen and even worse it was served with American butter which is good but could never compare to European. The bier is served in proper glasses and mugs and the size options are nice. The bier selection was good not great but satisfies. I love the concept of this place but it is missing a few marks. I may be being a bit harsh because I have spent so much time in the bier tents at German festivals and many nights in German village gasthauses. I would go back but not for the food unless I was craving a traditional bratwurst. I went there is hopes of experiencing the German camaraderie and awesome food. I got a little of both so all in all not bad and even good, just not really good.

Good southern food at a good price in a good atmosphere.  There are so many good reviews so just ignore the bad ones.  Everyone else has discussed the biscuits and the rest of the food.  
  This place is trying to give you good southern food and does a dang good job of it.  Think about it this way,  I cook a better biscuit at home and they would make you swoon if you ate one....but I'm not cooking in the neighborhood of 10000 every single day!!  
  They are famous and have lasted a long time for just that reason.   Ignore the naysayers....I'm pretty sure they were simply not raised right,  and there's a rumor running around that they was raised up North somewheres.

Cute sign caught my eye to drive way out of the way to try on the road trip home.  What I found is a renovated restaurant that is quaint compared to Cracker Barrel. 

Unfortunately, the service to order is terrible!!! Takes too long to get there attention, they don't help you understand what's good here. 

After placing the order, it took MUCH too long to arrive. We should have just left after the 45 minute wait for our food but had hopes it would be good with all these reviews.. 

The Southern Omelet that Dad expected to be a Country ham omelette had a bunch of other things he did not want in it and the cheese was cold and not even melted from it's shredded state.  And this omelet made him very ill later in the day.  He was really sick after eating here. Somalia?

The biscuits are really small. The odd thing was when I ordered biscuits & gravy, the order came without biscuits.  I received a bowel of gravy with no biscuits. When I asked for some biscuits, they told me to use the 3 cold ones which sat on our table for the 35+ minute wait. I figured they were heading back to bring us some fresh warm biscuits while I ate these cold ones left on our table.  We needed biscuits for our 2 other plates of food. Unfortunately, after trying to flag down a woman for help of the 4+ women circulating next to the waitress station next to us, they finally arrived after our eggs were then cold. My daughter would then not eat her breakfast with cold eggs.

The waitresses need to brush up on hospitality and prompt service.  (Where is the Southern Hospitality?) They need to give more attention to the begining of a meal & during the meal. The best service was to get our credit card and back for payment. Which was odd after such poor service throughout the meal.

I am so sorry we stopped. This took much longer for expecting something better.

Literally only come here for the biscuits and jam. Her favorite is blackberry. My favorite is strawberry. We purchased 4 jars from the market during the visit. We also had other food, I think it was the daily special. Nice big  portions. We shared a plate with plenty of leftovers! Our waitress Susan was very animated and sweet. Excellent customer service was provided. We were greeted by everyone. What a great atmosphere. We will definitely be stopping back in for more complimentary biscuits and jam.

I was at the lovely Bierhaus for a Yelp Elite event this evening and it was a truly wonderful experience. Not something I would have imagined I'd really enjoy, but I did.

So, I'm not a beer drinker (cider girl here), but whatever they had was straight from Germany and it was legit. The food was good, but what actually stood out the most for me was the homemade sweet mustard for the fresh pretzels. It was amazing and you could taste the freshness of it.

Service was good. It was busy in the main area with a band and a little audience participation.

I would definitely recommend to others. Thanks BB, see you soon!

Think you need to be here for live music.  Big portions. Had sights on the pork shank but knew I wasn't hungry enough to do it justice. Had pork schnitzel and spaetzle.  Touch salty but good. Kids had bratwurst and loved them . Seemed to be a coarse meat grind so not like a hot dog which I prefer. Would go back.

Some warnings:

Located in a sketchy area

No live music in the restaurant -- must pay separate admission for the music. 

Parking is expensive - 10 dollars

Nice decor inside but the other problems make it less desirable. 

Many other better choices.
Excellent German Food.  The staff was wonderful, efficient and quick.  We enjoyed brats and corned beef as well as a fine German brew.  Definitely recommend.

We had breakfast here the other day en route to Memphis from Nashville. I'd read about loveless on blogs before leaving on our trip. It did not disappoint. We got caught in the trap of wanting to try things & really for us Brits it was too much food! We should have just had a plate of biscuits & gravy. Having said that it certainly isn't a criticism only a warning for any other non American visitors who aren't used to the portions! The biscuits (or scones as we call them) were amazing ALMOST as good as Granny used to make but not quite. Jams were great too. My husband had an omelette and I had French toast. Both were excellent. 
Make sure you have a peek in the surrounding shops. They have some cute stuff. Well worth stopping off or visiting if you're nearby. Really cute venue & the staff were great too.

We were headed from Nashville to Memphis and wanted to grab dinner somewhere before it got too late. We chose this place since it was near I 40, and as we drove there we thought maybe we had picked a place too out of the way. I fell in love with the place before we even got inside. Loved the decor, the bright neon side outside and the country market with hams and jams. They serve delicious, melt in your mouth, warm biscuits at no charge and they come with 3 homemade jams. Food and service was great and my drink was never empty. We even got to sing happy birthday to one of the waiters. This is a memorable, must visit destination if you are ever in the area!

Great new place near Opry. Music was a blast and food is fantastic!

Had the schnitzle and spaetzle. Band was a blast and German faire perfect.

This restaurant is a unique experience. The staff dresses up in traditional German clothing. There was live music. We had fair service. I think that the food is slightly overpriced for the quality. It was decent, though. The bratwurst was very good but other items were just okay, especially compared to other German restaurants that I have been to. It was fun to try but I probably won't be back.

Have eaten there a few times. Enjoy their barbecue chicken, green beans are great, and loved their cucumber salad. We also tried their breakfasts as well which was good. The only thing I wasn't a fan of was their biscuits (which is to be one of their signature foods). Texture was dense and they were greasy; other than that It was fair for my taste.
Good atmosphere but that is where the good things stopped.  Poor service.  Food was average at best. Prices was very high for the quality of food we received.

I LOVE this place! The greens are amazing!! They're definitely my favorite so far. The fried green tomatoes are good, the catfish is good, chicken fried steak is huge, the eggs are decent, the hot warm biscuits will fill you up before the plate even comes. Hash brown casserole isn't bad, but not worth raving over. I've been here twice and have received phenomenal service each time. I've been told there's a wait usually, but I have had no such experience. Was seated immediately! Overall, I think it's worth a visit.

What can I say great Staff make you feel right at home. Biscuits Biscuits Biscuits! So So Good I had Fried Chicken and Waffle Couldn't get through the waffle because too many biscuits lol Chick ws excellent though Others had eggs bacon etc.  Gravy was also to die for ! def try this place

Disappointed after looking forward to coming back here, but like all of rapidly growing, over-commercialized Nashville, it's not the same. The biscuits with homemade jam were the best part of the meal. The fried chicken was dried out and not hot, like it had been laying around for awhile. The country ham was a bit tough too. The prices in the shops were eye-popping...$8 for a small bottle of hot sauce, the same size Louisiana Brand gets $1 for. If we come here again we will order biscuits and some sides and skip the meat.

Came for a late dinner tonight and loved the food, the wine, and the ambience. Had the Turkish White Blend by the glass but they have an extensive wine menu for all tastes! We started with the cheese platter, which was the perfect size for 3-4 people. We shared the risotto balls which were dynamite and for desert had the chocolate stoudt cake.... Very good! I also highly recommend the waiter Chocolate Thunder... You can have him with every course :) 

Oh and the steak entree was pretty banging!

A great lunch stop on the way to the Natchez trace parkway.  Friendly service, great big salads with delicious breaded chicken.  Sweet tea and cute little gift shops.  We also took bbq & coleslaw to go for the next day. We will definitely be back.
Being born and raised in Germany, this reminded me of home. Food was excellent, our waitress, Ashely, was fanominal. Love the feel of it all. We will return!!!

Holy heck this place was amazing! My daughter and I both got the sampler as we couldn't decided. On mine, I got the ham, chicken and catfish. She got the meatloaf, pulled pork and chicken. We both tried a taste of everything and all of it was good. My one warning is that the ham, is very salty. We personally like it that way, but if you don't like salt, then avoid this dish. 
I can't not mention the biscuits and jams. I could make a meal off these alone. They were completely with our meal. They are served warm and to die for. 
If you are in the area, you need to try this place. It was lovely! We will be back.

Very good place for dinner - homemade biscuits and jam were super. Friendly waitress and good, prompt service. There were six of us and all of our food cans at the same time. Plus....they serve moonshine!

EVERYTIME I come here it's a good time. Bartenders are always friendly. However they sell many mixed drink specials that include 0 alcohol, only the decent bartenders are nice enough to inform you beforehand.

This is a true community hub. 

They have a multitude of youth-focused spaces and opportunities, including an indoor skate park, skate teams, and a snack bar/coffee bar which is often run by the young people too. They have a great ministry influence here, which includes "family dinner" on Thursday nights for all who are seeking to find community and deepen their faith. 

They also host lots of community events, which is how I have gotten to know this place. I go to a free weekly yoga class on Saturdays, and have attended a few different networking events and fundraising galas in the large event space. 

The staff here is really down to earth and accommodating, and the kids are always having fun.  Great work being done here.
Amazing food, service could be better. Biscuits are delicious. I love the southern environment feel. For it being a famous landmark the prices are super reasonable!

This famous cafe lived up to its standards. The service was amazing and the food was great. Also, if you like sweet tea and homemade biscuits this is the place to go. The prices were not too bad for the size of the portions. It was nice to walk around after dinner a explore the little shops.

Died and gone to heaven comes to mind when eating at the Loveless Cafe.  Biscuits that are fresh and home made!  Country ham and pit BBQ with eggs and grits for breakfast awesome!  Want delicious and cheesy hash browns?  Got it!  I can't say enough about this place except "Superb!!!"  Friendly staff with a southern charm.  This is worth the 25 minute drive from downtown Nashville.  Spend some time wandering around their shops, well worth it.  Crafts and food and an awesome BBQ kitchen.  Just stick me in the vat with the sausage gravy.  Happy to expire there!
Amazing food and staff ! So glad I stopped it was worth it ! I used the app and ordered since I was traveling ! The biscuits are amazing try them !!!

I think they try hard to offer real German food but in fact it is not. If you think what they serve is German food then please let me assure you, it is not. 
The sauce of the Jaegerschnitzel was too salty, the apple strudel super sweet and very chewy (I couldn't eat it). The potato salad had a garlic dressing - yucky_ and is light years away from the german version. We waited almost 30 min for our food. It is also over prized. I dont think we will come back.

Brandon, you're a rock start! Quality service. Food is ok, but what I tried wasn't not a signature dish so I won't judge them by that even though I believe everything should be amazing. I had the pigs in the blanket looking things. The sausage tasted good. They don't come with dipping sauce so if you are one that needs that, then you need to ask for it on the side. 

The decor is very medieval with the chandelier and the flowers on them. The staff dresses with German outfits. They don't seem to like wearing them, but they go very well with the atmosphere they are trying to create.

They have a big bar area where they have TVs  and differ wells, beers and wines. They have high top tables in that area too. 

They have a gift shop when you enter with different merchandise; key chains, cups, shirts, etc.

Go check them out, you won't feel you are in Germany but definitely will experience some of it.
Save your money for the better bars in the area. The drinks are cheap, but the poor service, warm beer, and overall bad management make the place not worth it.

The food is really amazing. The biscuits and jam are really awesome. Service was awesome down home service you don't see anywhere else

Must try when you are around Nashville Tnn

Nice job replicating a little piece of Bavaria 

Good selection on the menu ....nice offering of beers 

Service team takes on the Bavarian hospitality role with refreshing enthusiasm....as do many of the regular patrons

Wunderbar !

Noch ein Bier, bitte?!!

Got there just on time for the when the show was listed as starting on a saturday night. No one was on stage, and they didn't get up for a sound check until an hour after they were listed as starting. Then the sound guy says they sound good & he'll see them 30 minutes later. I just thought 'well I just paid for 1.5 hours of silence & a sound check, so its not like I'm being that much more wasteful if I just give up my cover charge' & I left. But! It was 10$ for 3 bands, & I checked out one on youtube before the show, & they sounded good, so I bet that would have been a good bargain if I had felt like sticking around! & parking was surprisingly easy to get in and out of. The set up is really nice for the stage & there's very little area where you can't face the stage, especially the bar which is almost up on the corner of the stage. That seems very convenient if you're waiting for your order to get taken and don't want to miss a minute of the show.

Note to self (sorta):  The smoked link and curry wurst are good, the jalapeño cheddar link has zero jalapeño flavor, the veal link is lean, but bland, too. The sour kraut is decent (it's sour).

The fries are batter-coated, the cucumber salad has an odd beer flavor and no dill flavor (we were told it would be dilly), the red cabbage is sweet (we were told it's not), the potato dumplings were sweet, with a bland gravy. The potato salad was not preferred, either.

Curry wurst is a preferred dish, but sometimes is totally drowned in ketchup.  It's also to be expected that we feel like we licked a salt block after we have eaten there.

These notes will help navigate our next visit, to fine-tune what we order.  This place is okay, and it provides an alternative to the same-old.

Note to Yelp:  it would be nice for y'all to add a private comments area for each restaurant, to allow for these sorts of personal notations.

Great service from very engaged manager and wait staff. Fried chicken sets standard for Nashville. Salads are good..not great..could use mixed greens and more variety. Corncake and biscuits excellent and jams outstanding. Fried okra had too much breading..lighten up! You can see why its top 10. No reservations so arrive early or late.  Year in and out a must.

We had a wonderful experience here! We booked a reservation via Open Table and put in a request for a table close to the front and when we arrived we were seated immediately and our request was granted!

We had a great server and he got our drink orders and brought out the biscuits very quickly. He was super busy and working a bunch of tables and yet he was attentive to everyone!

Our table had a variety of breakfast and lunch items. We had one Southern Sampler Breakfast and ironically, my dad thought the ham was the weakest of the meats provided and liked the bacon and sausage more. We also had an order of fried chicken and a variety of sides (sweet potatoes, mashed potatoes, white beans, and fried okra) and all were said to be really good. The last item we had was a Fried Green Tomato BLT with Fried Okra and it was fantastic. I did ask for a little mayo because none came on it originally. 

If you are in the area, it is so worth the trip! It's not fancy, but it's solid, authentic southern food.

I can't stand people that lie. We called to ask about whether the Predators would be viewable during the concert and two different callers were told YES! Absolutely!  We understand it is the finals and the Preds game will be viewable at your table. 
NOPE!!!  Not only that, they only had ONE TV in the outer dining room/bar. 
Seriously?!?!????
Even the band was huddled in the bar to watch.

Worth the wait BUT you can make RSVP online!
We heard about Loveless Cafe on a national morning show and made a point of going on our trip to the midwest, happily making a reservation for brunch. We followed the GPS out a lovely road, West End, passing elegant homes, and once there, checked in and were called rather close to the time we reserved. There are plenty of things to look at while you are waiting: cornhole boards, gift shops. Once inside, Mary was our server, and greeted us with a brilliant smile, happy eyes and welcoming us with a complimentary basket of fresh hot biscuits, several homemade jams, and drinks. Our meals were heavenly: my husband had delicious pulled pork and veggies, and I had waffle with substantial amount of melting chocolate chips and real butter, with FOUR slices of bacon. The service was great, she gave us a box and sent us out full and happy. We loved the Loveless Cafe! You will, too!

I want to love this place I really do. I came here 3-4 times now to give it the benefit of the doubt but  failed every single time. 
Nice servers, love the atmosphere, love the biscuits but the food just suck! The food taste very stale and mediocre !

I went to the Bavarian Bierhaus before a show at the grand ole Opry!  It's connected to the mall next door.  The beer was great, so I can't complain.  I ordered a pretzel to start, pretty tough, but the mustard was flavorful.  I wasn't in the mood for German food, so I ordered a salad with grilled chicken.  This is easy to make and simple but the taste was off, not sure if it was the chicken or lettuce itself.

I unfortunately found this place a bit overrated. Food was decent. Price was great and so was the service. I just found the flood a lil less than seasoned and the biscuits weren't as fluffy as I imagined. Plus there is a long wait since it's so popular

Very tasty!

We tried a lot of things... the BBQ pork, the bacon, the fried green tomatoes with pimento cheese, the fried chicken, the hashbrown casserole, and of course the biscuits. They were all delicious, but honestly I could have been happy with just those light and delicious biscuits!

The one thing I didn't like was the ham, and my daughter thought the pancakes were too sweet (which does seem like a weird complaint). 

I really liked getting to browse the little stores out back too. I got two really cute pairs of earrings made by local artists. 

I'd definitely come back again!

Wow! Two hour wait but so worth it. We came at 6:00pm on a Friday. We knew anywhere we went was going to be a wait. Waitress was friendly and knowledgeable about all of the menu. The biscuits reminded me of my Granny's biscuits. Pretty emotional moment in many ways. Brought back memories but also made you want to keep grabbing them. Jellies were very good and the waitress brought several kinds for us to try. They were all very good. The fried chicken wasn't the best I've had but was very good. Okra was lacking and kept this from being a five star review. Macaroni was good. I would definitely want to come back here but I would probably come much earlier.
Love, love, love Loveless Cafe!  So Nashville!!  My biscuits are better but Loveless is a close second!!

It is a famous cafe that's for sure, fun to see all the shops.  I would say that the food is good and the coconut cream pie is better!!  This is our second stop and while we had fried chicken this time I was a little under whelmed.  The food was overdone and dry, not very flavorful like our first trip here where we had burgers.  Our waitress was fun and very attentive so the service is excellent.  It is always an hour or more wait so be prepared for that .  You should definitely get the coconut cream pie to go!!

This review is based solely on a musical show we attended, not a dinner or food prep/service. We attended the Marc Broussard show on December 31st.  We like to sit upstairs as you can get a private table as opposed to sitting at the communal tables downstairs.  The downstairs tables/chairs are VERY close to one another and it makes me uncomfortable, especially if I don't know my dining neighbors :-).  The Somm at City Winery.  Just tell her wine type or flavor profile you like, and she picks a bottle just for you.  Prices are reasonable for tickets AND wine.  The sound quality is exceptional and it's a very intimate venue.  I highly recommend City Winery for the music alone, but I also hear the food is delicious.

It was a fun place! I go to Nashville once a year, and wanted to check this place out! The biscuits are so good. The has brown casserole and mac and cheese were delicious. The chicken is so crispy and really good! The sweet tea is a must in Tennessee!
Was not disappointed.. amazing food and good prices!!!! We shared a pretzel with beer cheese as an app. Split the reuban and the 2 sausage plate. Let satisfied for sure.

First time at City Winery. The service, food and wine were all amazing. The servers were prompt and courteous. The food was delicious and the wine was perfect!

We will definitely be back!

Absolutely delightful, and worth the drive. The service was amazing and they made you feel right at home. The drinks were fantastic too. Between 4 of us we had quite a few of the brunch items (pulled pork, waffles, biscuits and gravy, ham), it was all amazing!! Can i talk about there jelly's? The preserves were AMAZING!!! Blueberry, strawberry, all of them! The only thing we didn't get to try was the fried chicken. We wanted to try the banana pudding too, but we were so full after there was no room. Also, the wait was about 45 minutes but the time flew by as we looked in their little shops. They offered free coffee, and had cute little rocking chairs to sit in on the porch. I will be going back for sure when we return!

I love the loveless cafe!!! The assortment of jams, the sausage gravy, the hash brown casserole , EVERYTHING IS DELICIOUS! the service was smooth despite the large volume of customers. I wish they would open another location in the Chicagoland area

While on a business trip to Nashville, we had a chance to visit the Loveless Cafe for lunch on a weekday. Great timing because we only had a 20 minute wait and spent that time shopping in the cute little gift shop. Got a package of Piggy Popcorn which went over great at the office at home. Wearing my Praise the Lard T-shirt as I type this.
The food was classic Southern goodness. Delicious biscuits and jam to start the meal, and could have stopped there and been happy happy happy. Proceeded to have the BBQ sandwich and found it to be pretty tasty though not knock your socks of great. Coworkers had the fried chicken livers and the chicken fried steak smothered in gravy. I also had the sweet tea. Yum. I thought the livers were a little overcooked and did not get to taste the other entree. The caramel sweet potatoes side dish was wonderful! 
Loved walking around the property, especially smelling the smokey BBQ pit outside on a crisp, clear day. Everyone there was very nice, in typical Southern style. We felt welcome and left well fed and happy. 
If you cannot make the trip, do go to the website and buy up some of their tasty jams and hams.

Disappointing. That is the first word which comes to mind about my experience at City Winery. The service was uncomfortable. The food was an overpriced mediocre attempt at a la mode cuisine. The wine was good but not enough to overcome the other elements. Once seated, we waited approximately 20 minutes before our drink order was taken due to the servers each thinking the other was in charge of our table. As it was Sunday night, the restaurant was not busy. The first two things I ordered were not available. It took the server over 30 minutes to realize my second option was not prepared, and I had to fall onto a third choice. I understand running out of things on a busy night...or even her returning right after putting in the ticket to inform me they had run out of something, but this was odd. Food was eventually delivered with all the courtesy and customer service of the social security office. Food tossed on tables. Server awkwardly hovered but did not actually ask if everything was ok, then disappeared until we were pretty much done eating. 
Food ordered: 
Head of Romaine Salad: Boring, underdressed. Salad can be simple without being boring. This was not the case.
farro risotto was nice and hearty. Best thing we ordered. 
Shrimp piri piri: warm, mild flavored shrimp served on a bed on fridge cold couscous salad. The temperature different was offputting.
Pan chicken: underwhelming.
We did receive a complimentary dessert in compensation for the lack of available menu items. The olive oil cake was the best part of the meal, but was also tossed onto the table so that the forks slid into the marmalade (covering the handles of the forks) and the gentleman delivering the food seemed surprised when we asked for a little more marmalade (since the majority ended up sticking to the fork handles)
Our server was adequate, but shied away from our table.
Go for wine. Not for food.

Loveless Cafe is a beacon of southern comfort food for me, like it is for many others. Every time I'm back in Nashville, I make my pilgrimage to Loveless. The biscuits are always as good as they are in my memory, the preserves are so flavorful, and the hot food is delicious. The fried chicken is definitely above average, and all of the southern sides are a hit. 

I would recommend Loveless Cafe to any visitor going to Nashville. It will definitely be a hit. However, the 2+ hour wait gets old. This last time I went, my boyfriend and I played the "Guess Who" game with countless portraits of celebrities on the walls of the cafe while waiting 1.5 hours for our table. So if I'm in Nashville next time and had limited time and patience, I would take myself to Monell's for a comparably delicious and authentic southern food experience.

Good show venue , but it took 30 minutes for basic food.  Fries that cost 7 dollars should not be worse than fries I made in my oven at home from Kroger.  On tap beer selection has areas for improvement.

Hands down one of my favorite places to go! Their biscuits and fried chicken are amazing!!!!! It's an iconic tourist spot but even if you have to wait they have cute shops and games and things you can do in the meantime! I'd recommend anyone go there
The food is good, especially the biscuits! Decore and food is basically exactly like a Cracker Barrell. Still go for the experience of eating there.

A wonderful place to eat anything.  Great fried chicken with brown or white gravy. Unbelievable sides.  Great greens. Excellent coleslaw. Fried green tomatoes are definitely worth ordering.  One of the best bloody Mary's ever.  We loved the place   Our waitress. Cindy. Was amazing.  She was extra helpful and she was very nice.  Hats off to this wonderful place. Cute store. Impeccably clean bathrooms.

We were here visiting from CA and excited to try this new place.  My husband and I grew up with German Food and it looked authentic.  The food was AWESOME.  It was so good, we came back a few days later.  Love the beer selection!  Our waitress, Jennifer did a great job and was very helpful. Would definitely come back if we are ever in Music City again.

My guess is that I've had breakfast or early dinner at Loveless Cafe at least 50 times. I became a customer at the age of 16 as a freshman at the Vanderbilt University, and I continued throughout my wild days as a student and as a teacher at the university. 

Just went back and Loveless still serves up a lotta love.

Best biscuits and the best country breakfast I've ever tasted, What I really like about Loveless Cafe, besides the savory eats -- the customers cannot be put into a class, or party, or ethic group. It attracts truckers, artists, musicians, tourists, good country people, foodies, and no-nonsense Nashvilleans, and nobody cares, as the delicious food brings everyone together.

This is where politicians of different parties should break bread. Simple good food cures all.

I've had every entree on the menu & always VERY satisfied. Great folks & WORTH THE WAIT ESPECIALLY HOME MADE DESSERTS. 
 Country ham and biscuits awesome in the even know how to do chicken livers properly

I gave a star for the staff-- they were terrific. The food was simply not good. I had a garden omelet-- the vegetables were slimy. My husband had fried chicken and it was incredibly greasy. Everything including the sides was overcooked. Incredibly unsatisfying. We will not be back.
This place is way overhyped.  Save your money and go to Biscuit Love.  Food is blan but served in large portions.  Biscuits are mediocre but sauce was good.  Other than that not much else to say.

I hate to say this I think it's overrated. Don't get me wrong was food was good & our server was great but I personally I was expecting more. Still go & experience if you'd like but you won't be blown away. Sorry!

This place was recommended by 2 friends so we decided to give it a try on our way to Memphis.

It's an adorable little property with all sorts of cool buildings. You'll have time to explore those while you wait for a table.

Inside it has a real country diner feel with red checkered table cloths and rooster curtains. The servers are all extremely friendly and kind, they make it feel like home. 

My friend and I split the famous loveless country ham and red eye gravy breakfast platter, which was more than enough food for 2 people. I had never tried red eye gravy and it was basically like the pan drippings. It was fine, but hardly what I consider gravy. The ham was more tough than I expected and very meaty. It wasn't my favorite, but I'm glad I gave it a shot. The hashbrown casserole was incredible and I'm a sucker for a good hashbrown casserole. I definitely had trouble sharing! The biscuits were also fantastic, made even better by the accompanying homemade jam. The jams were all fantastic and I ended up getting a jar of peach jam to take home with me. 

I was happy we made the stop on our way to Memphis, but I'm not sure I would make the drive if I was just visiting Nashville. It is a cute property and the mountain of biscuits that arrive at your table are delicious.

Growing up, my Mother talked about how one day she wanted to go to Loveless Cafe if she ever made it to Nashville.  She passed many years ago and when I moved here in 1991 it was very emotional the first time I made it, I cried thinking how much she would've loved the experience.  I've been many times since then and Loveless Cafe is always a treat!  I love breakfast the best.

Where to start...Loveless cafe offers great value. The food is simple but done very well and delicious. Prices are very reasonable for the quality. We had eight in our group and all of the dishes without exception were excellent. Our server Kirsten, was truly a gem. Outgoing, personable, very affable and so helpful. An excellent example of what "friendly, knowledgeable service" should be. Will definitely return here if passing through these parts again. Highly recommend this restaurant.

Everyone told us we had to go here, which is 20 minutes outside of town.
It was so worth the trip. The Biscuits arrived (Warm) with three types of jam. One was yummier then the next. The portions were big and worth every over stuffed bite. Southern cooking, with LOVE at the Loveless Cafe.

I've been to both the upper venue room and the larger venue room in the lower level and they're both great. I went to two concerts: Greg Howe which was a three piece upstairs, and The Aristocrats downstairs which was also 's the piece band. Both rooms have great sound and the food menu is decent. I had the Margherita pizza which was good. I don't recall how much it cost, but it got the spot. I don't drink wine so cannot comment on that part, but the menu seemed large. Great venue

Unique restaurant in an old fashioned motel with gift shops in the sleeping rooms. I seriously could have just eaten biscuits and homemade jam and been totally content. Delicious! My hubby ordered a breakfast omelet (they have breakfast all day) and I ordered fried chicken with caramel sweet potatoes (yes, caramel) and coleslaw. The only knock is I felt that the chicken breast was on the small size and for the price thought there should have been two. Next time I'll order the fried chicken salad because it was loaded high with fried chicken and get the sweet potatoes as a side. Fun and casual for families.

Good experience, but a bit short of prior experiences here. I ordered the BBQ pork with eggs for breakfast. Pork was outstanding, eggs much less so, as they were somewhat overcooked for my liking. Biscuits were good but seemed less well done than is my preference. Dining partner ordered country ham with eggs, which she didn't love the ham, but I thought the ham was how it should be. Service was very nice; was quoted 45 minutes for the wait, but it was about 25-30.

Because of my past experiences would definitely come back although experience was a bit below par from previous visits.

Some of the best home style cooking I've had!!! We were a party of 4. Was about a 30 min wait on a Monday! The service was awesome! Lady was sooo sweeet and the food was amazing...the biscuits were beyond soft they were delicious! Get the sweet potatoes...soooo good!!! Who am I kidding it was all good! Well Worth the travel from Texas!

Love it here. It's kinda kitschy so I thought I was just buying into tourist hype (as I'm wont to do on occasion), but seriously everything was delicious. Nevermind that I don't understand the ham thing. I had the biscuit sampler and the hashbrown casserole and it was really great. I'm obsessed with the fried green tomato pimiento cheese biscuit. And the BBQ was surprisingly good. Two thumbs up!

I was excited to try this place after reading reviews and receiving recommendations from friends.  I was disappointed to say the least.  We had a party of 6 and all got different plates.  Not one of us said "I'd come back".  It was okay but not what I had hoped for.

Landmark restaurants are always tricky. Sometimes they're just good, but nothing to write home about. They're famous because the locals love it, or it's tradition and because it makes some people nostalgic. Other times, it's well deserved fame that makes you wish you lived there so you could feast on those dishes to your little heart's content- that's Loveless. 

Sweet lord, Loveless. I will fantasize about this place until I can come back. When people think of outstanding, southern home cooking this is it. This is stick-to-your-ribs, bad for your arteries but good for your soul food. I will never be able to have a conversation about Nashville again without mentioning Loveless. 

So what was so good that I am love rambling about this place? 

-THE BISCUITS. 
I'm pretty sure angels sing when these come out of the oven. In Pluto's theory of forms, everything on earth is a copy of the perfect form of something in heaven. And I'm pretty sure Loveless biscuits are the ones they have in heaven. They are fluffy, and fresh and perfect. Obviously you need butter and preserves, because you wouldn't want to cut corners on this delicious experience. 

-BBQ pork omelet 
(AMAZING. One of the best omelets I've ever had). I ordered it because I knew I couldn't get a BBQ pork omelet in NYC or LA or even in carnivorous Chicago. When in Rome, right? Best decision I've made lately. The pork is so juicy and flavorful, and there was just a hint of BBQ sauce, so the smoky flavor carried the omelet. It was perfect. 5 stars. Will order it again every time. 

- The hash brown casserole 
AMAZING cheesy, potatoey, fatty goodness. You couldn't dream up better breakfast potatoes. These are an absolute must. They are the cherry on top of each bite.  

-country fried steak 
My friend got this and it is the ultimate country fried steak with gravy. She couldn't stop smiling while she was eating. If this is your thing, you will be so, so happy.  


I thought the fried chicken was good, but I'm not a big fried chicken person so I probably wouldn't order it again, it wasn't  life altering, like the biscuits.  

The service was outstanding. You feel so welcome and taken care of. That Southern hospitality gets city people like me every time. 

This place is a must, an absolute freaking must. When I am old and gray and look back on all the delicious food I have eaten in my life, I will think of Loveless. 

Peace, Loveless & Nashville forever.

Bland Americana anyone could make better at home. Spinach salad came with a thick gelatin-like dressing that was full of sugar and inedible. Chicken for the schnitzel was not tenderized as is the procedure for schnitzel so it was tough. Sauce was bland with no Swiss flavor. Only the red cabbage was tolerable.

This place is a real deal german restaurant. I love german food but am a bit reluctant to try new ones because truly authentic german food can be hard to find.

I almost didn't go in because the entrance from inside the Opry Mills mall is kind of like a construction zone or a closed off area at an amusement park. When I got in there however, I found the decor and live accordion music very casual and inviting.

They had a dish called "leberkase" which is kind of like thick sliced bologna fried on each side or like sausage meat formed in a bread pan and sliced. Anyway, I got turned onto it in Munich and if I see it on a menu I gotta try it.

Fairly quick service in the bar area and the food was delicious and reasonably priced. Only reason I didn't go 5 stars is the purple cabbage was lukewarm but still very good.

Definitely will return to explore menu!!

Off the main drag in downtown Nashville with less expensive drinks and shots.  Great live music.  Atmosphere is a bit rowdy and bathrooms are kinda rough, but it's the perfect spot to get the night started before frequenting the more pricey bars on broadway.  We always have a good time here.
Great hidden treasure in Nashville.  The fish and chips were delicious and the service was quick.

From the moment I walked the atmosphere was good. Me and my boyfriend was impressed they had a live band but you didn't have to scream to have a conversation. The band was very interacting with the children. My waiter was good also always checked to see if we needed more drinks. The amount of food you get is decent but it cost extra to get bread. It's $1.00 every roll you get. The spaztle was overcooked I was not impressed I didn't even eat the extra spaztle I got. The schnitzel was dry. The gravy didn't really have taste. I think it took a huge turning point when the male manager told me I wasnt german. He said just cause your mom is Germany doesn't make you one. Do you speak German? Uhhh yes I am mixed with African American and German. I was born in Germany. I can speak, read, and write in German after that I was ready to go. I didn't even take my food home

I have only ever been here for shows.  And even though it hasn't been open long I've been to several.  I know there's a restaurant and bar space out front (the live music venue is in the back) but I haven't eaten there or even sat there so this review is focused solely on the gigantic slice of heaven that is the stage in the back.

Despite the large space the venue manages to be intimate, and the artists they book are not only talented but may not be your usual fare.  Many of them are older, classic performers, with amazing stories, or newcomers with some serious lyrical soul.  The acoustics are fantastic as well, and there's something about being able to just sit and enjoy some great food, drink, and entertainment without needed to dance or run around.  Its relaxing and enjoyable.

The staff is incredible in their ability to move around quickly without blocking your view of the stage or having to shout at you to ask if you want another drink.  And the drinks and food are just wonderful.  I am a huge fan of their beet and bacon flatbread and their burger.  They have so many delicious wines to choose from, as well as other alcoholic offerings, but if you love wine I recommend a bottle or two for a good show.

Most of the shows start by 8pm and are done by 11pm.  The servers are great at getting your tabs to you before the end of the show so you're not scrambling.  Its really just an overall fantastic dining and musical experience.

They offer free valet most nights, and even at soldout shows are great about getting your cars quickly.  The whole experience is just so laid back and enjoyable, and I've never had a bad time.  I highly recommend taking in a show here and coming early to eat.  The tickets for the concerts are usually more than reasonable, as is the food.  It's a great way to spend a Nashville night.
Unique place. Had multiple little gift shops to wonder thru while you wait. Get the breakfast! Great experience.
