Fantastic fried chicken and dining experience! I stopped in with a friend on a rainy Sunday around 3 and it was roughly a 15min wait. We were promptly greeted by our server with biscuits in hand. The biscuits and homemade preserves were to die for!! I ordered the friend chicken with Mac and cheese and fried okra. The Mac and cheese was excellent, very creamy! Our food came out very quick, maybe a 15 min wait. There is a reason this place had such a good reputation. Great food and great service!

We went on NYE for the Marc Broussard concert.  You can actually eat inside the concert hall if you want.  They open the doors well before the concert so you have plenty of time eat.  You will be seated at a large table with other patrons.  If you want to eat alone before entering the concert hall there is a small dining area and bar outside the concert hall.  It's small so you will need reservations.  

The beet humus was just ok.  The kale Caesar was wonderful.  Simple but one of the best salads I've ever had.  My wife had black eyed soup which was very tasty. 

The have one variety of most popular reds and whites.  We did a red flight.  It was acceptable but not what I would consider middle of the road.  They do have a large wine menu outside of what they produce.

Go here just for the biscuits....best biscuits I have ever had in my life ......fluffy tender buttery melt in your mouth amazing I lie to you not I think I ate 6 of them the blackberry preserve is just the perfect topping for the biscuits.....and the bacon is so full of smoky flavor ......the rest is ok .....but the biscuits  the hash brown casserole is amazing also

Where has this place been all my life? First of all, very cute place and excellent service. I had the fried chicken, top 3 fried chickens I have ever had and I have had lots of Fried chicken. Sides were mashed potatoes and cole slaw, both excellent as well. The only disappointment was the gravy, kinda bland. My wife had the fried chicken livers which were outstanding. I'm not a lover guy, and I even thought they were excellent. Very moist and tender with a nice crispy crust. She also had the fried okra and potato casserole, both were top notch. Hers came with a different gravy and it was bland as well. Finally, you get a stack of delicious little biscuits and jams as a starter, they are fantastic. Don't miss the Hams and Jams store next door where you can buy the biscuit mix, breading mix, jams and more. I will visit this place every time I am in Nashville, if I do nothing else. Dying to try the meatloaf, pork chops and Mac and Cheese.

Once seated, take your time and enjoy the biscuits (and accompanying preserves) while silently paying homage to the Biscuit Lady (may she Rest In Peace).....then order absolutely anything and be thankful ....IT IS ALWAYS DELICIOUS!

This place is a 20 minute drive from Broadway. A local recommend it. Glad we went. Great menu for everyone. Fried chicken is there specialty and I would definitely recommend. Lots of sides to choose from. Recommend the hash brown casserole. Shops outside to visit.

One of my favorite southern meals. Everything you want in a heart attack, I mean HEARTY meal.  They probably have the best biscuits I have ever tasted.  They come with three amazing preserves: peach, blackberry, and strawberry. Ask for more biscuits if you must. 

Meals: 

Smoked ham - get it 
Fried Chicken - honestly, what do you think? probably the best I've ever had. 
Hash brown casserole, Mac 'n cheese, and fried green tomatoes.  I cnat put into words how much I enjoyed this meal.  I'd love to return!

They have good food and biscuits. That comes recommended. 

My issue is that I have a dairy allergy, and unfortunately Loveless Cafe failed me with my dietary restrictions. I notified my server about my allergy. She went and grabbed a manager just to be on the safe side. 

He told me he would double check, but I could order pancakes or waffles as the batter comes as a mix and is dairy free. Skeptical, I agreed to a waffle. After I ordered a waffle the sever asked me if I was sure about that as she claimed it contained dairy. Contrary to what the manager told me. She went to double check and read the ingredients list. Low and behold, it DID contain dairy.

Not only did a manager lie to me, but things could have been much worse had I been deathly allergic.

I ended up ordering just 2 eggs and some bacon as almost everything on the menu was not dairy-free friendly. 

Naturally, they cooked the eggs in butter even when I was told they use oil. Within 20 minutes I wanted to die. 

I can say this, they really do live up to their name. Loveless...

Stopped in because my love of wine is strong!!! The winery is in a little sketch of a neighborhood but nothing terrifying.. the food and wine are worth getting in for! The service was extremely good from the start!! We got the cheese plate to start (exceptional) and recommended wines (a recommended cab sav and sav Blanc). We decided to do starters/ small plates to make up our meal. We had the deviled eggs (quite a unique but wonderful Taste), kale salad (nothing to write home about and not
Worth getting) and the spaghetti squash (a delicious starter). The ambiance is classy and enjoyable. A great way to spend a leisurely evening!!

From the minute you walk in, you're made to feel at home. This is my go to place every time I get to Nashville. The staff, the food, the down home, great feeling. Best food in Nashville. Makes you motneant to leave...the restaurant and the area itself. I LOVE the LOVELESS.

Good food, minimal wine selection. We sat outside on a Sunday, and were then notified that only one server was working. I believe the manager was the one who took or drink order thirty minutes after we sat. Wine was delivered fifteen minutes later by an employee who was technically off the clock. First appetizer arrived an hour after seating. Server's assistant was annoyed when I walked inside and asked for plates and silverware to go with our cheeses. We finally met our server when entrees arrived. He brought us a steak knife (upon request) after the filet landed, dropped two to go boxes when we requested, and delivered the check long after we had finished eating. I've never been more neglected during a dining experience. Hopefully my review can dissuade potential patrons from funding this establishment.
Dive bar that draws you in with advertised $2 drafts and charges you $3 per draft. Just be honest. I'll pay$3 for a draft but the false advertising makes people feel scorned and bitter.

Great food/service every time we go. 
Biscuits are awesome!
Go early for breakfast as there can be a wait for a table as you get closer to 8:00 am, especially o. Saturday & Sunday mornings.
Soooo good. Going back as often as I can!  Food hot and tasty. Fast service was seated. A lot of history hanging on wall. Take home desserts a real treal

Okay this places defines great southern cooking. Loveless is just like eating a home cooked meal, the staff is so friendly and made great recommendations . The owner even came over to the table, he was very attentive and accommodating to my nut allergy. Everything was just stick to ribs delicious! The property is also so charming to walk around while you wait for a table.

The Loveless Cafe is breakfast perfection. Seriously. I have never had better biscuits in my life, and I have a southern grandma! I could have made a meal out of the biscuits and housemade jam alone, but then I'd miss out on the house-cured ham, bacon, and eggs and cheesy potatoes that went along with my amazing breakfast. I was full long before I stopped eating. 

I loved the charm of the restaurant as well as the surrounding shops on the premises! I regret not buying the biscuit mix, but it just gives me another reason to head back. My only reason is for not giving it 5 stars is the price - our breakfast for two people was $47. FOR BREAKFAST. But you get what you pay for, I suppose, and in this case, I'd consider it money well spent.

PS - Don't tell my grandma what I said about the biscuits, ok? I don't want to hurt her feelings.

My wife and I were really looking forward to trying this place because there were not a lot of wine-focused restaurants/bars in the region in our opinion.  This one had a pretty good history.

When we got here, we walked in and while it was a visually pleasing space, it was really quiet which sort of takes the air out of your sails.  When you advertise that music is a focal point of your location, I would think having at least something playing in the Barrel Room would be part of the experience. It's rare when there is no music whatsoever playing even in the background in a restaurant.  It just makes it so that all you can hear are people eating, talking and clanging their plates.  That could be by design but it just kind of made us tired after 15 minutes.

We walked up to the bar and sat down and were greeted by a very friendly bartender.  My wife opted for one of their White & Rose' flights and I selected their Domaine Skouras.  Their wine list lacked some very basic options like a Pinot Grigio, Albarino and they only had one Chardonnay.  My wife tried all the wines in her flight and really couldn't connect with any of them so we decided to pull the plug and move on.  It could be that it was just an off night but we do wine places all over the U.S. and this one just couldn't hold our attention.

We came to Nashville for our Honeymoon.  This place was awesome after spending the day at the Belle Meade plantation.  Delicious southern cooking.  Biscuits did not disappoint! We   had fun looking celebrity pics.  The server, Owen was great. You could even see the cooks  working their magic!  Ha ha! 
Will return here again.

I am a local - 6th generation.  I know southern food when I taste it.  My family has released several published southern cook books over the years. The food is good!  The menu and the prices remind me of our local restaurant Arnold's Country Kitchen.  They serve food until 9:30 pm at Fat Kat Slim's, and this place is worth a try. You can get breakfast, lunch, and dinner. I am thankful this restaurant is so near by where I live.  I am glad to see another meat and three where they can get you in and out.  The service is friendly, and the owners (a husband and wife team) were present during our dining experience.  I appreciated their southern hospitality!  They have the best martinis in town...I had the spellbound.

If you are in Nashville you have to stop here just for the warm biscuits alone.  We were in Nashville for a conference and someone recommended this place and we were so satisfied with everything.  First you are met with a plate of warm biscuits with three different jams, butter is already on the table, before you even place your drink order which was amazing as we hadn't eaten lunch.  Everyone loved their entree from the BBQ chicken special to the pulled pork on hoecakes and their special fried chicken.  The only bad thing, if this is a bad thing, we had no room for dessert and staying in a hotel meant taking dessert home was out of the question.  If we are ever in the area this is one place we will not miss.

Fried chicken: amazing
Catfish: amazing
Smoked pulled pork: amazing
Turnip greens: amazing 
Hush puppies: amazing
Fried green tomatoes: amazing
Marinated cubes&onions amazing
Biscuits: none finer

The service was bright, fun and thorough. I never had to look around or hunt for it because it was there before I knew. 

They say road to disappointment is paved with expectations.   They are wrong.  

Whatever you expect, this place will exceed by a mile.

It is entirely possible that the Käsespätzle I've eaten at an Austrian restaurant back home is an outlier. If that's the case, my review is pointless.

But the Käsespätzle I got here wasn't even playing the same sport, much less in the same ballpark. It was glorified mac-and-cheese, and not even that glorified.

It came out in like 5 minutes, which was weird. There was nothing Bavarian about the seasoning. Just noodles... and lots and lots of cheese that looked like melted velveeta. 

Again, maybe the Käsespätzle I've had before isn't normal, but it had a very distinct taste and appearance, and this wasn't anything like that. 

Look for the reviews of stuff that was actually really good before ordering, and skip this item.

3.0 Let me be clear, this is a great place for a music venue (4.5) but the food is mediocre if you plan to make it a one stop date night.  They run out of wine!  Yeah...a place called City Winery runs out of wine. Back to the food, so we were excited about the braised duck tacos, but the excitement deflated at first bite.  I will pay for great food but it sucks to overspend on nasty food.  Let me sum it up in one word - Dry!!! Take home message: have a few drinks at home before you go, enjoy your show (truly not a bad seat in the house) and then go to dinner elsewhere!!!

This is a little hole in the wall bar off Broadway in Nashville, A good little hang out if you're looking for good cheap drinks and a not so crowded and busy atmosphere. They have girls going around selling jello shots, they sell moonshine pickles, their drinks are good and very reasonably priced.

I enjoyed this place.  I stopped by for an early dinner one night.  It was rather empty at the time so I was seated and served quite quickly.

The restaurant itself is really large.  Lots of room!  Be prepared for the German style long tables though.  If they are busy, I would imagine you would be seated beside others :)

They have a wall for beer steins, so I gather you can purchase them there and leave them there for some kind of drink discount.  Since I don't drink, I didn't look into this.

The food was good.  It was something that I would go WOW for but it was decent.  I would go back and try something different next time around I feel.  I think it would also be a good place to go with a group of friends.

Some of the waitresses tend to ummmm....hang out a little on the cleavage department.  Okay if you want to see that while you eat...me....it is not necessary and will not contribute to the size of your tip.  That all depends on service and food.   The service was good and she did get a good tip though haha.

Warning, to Tourists and Locals. 
Do not step foot in a lowdown bar called "Big Shotz". Today, l found out that the night l was kicked out, 3 more people were shown the door. Only l was drinking Soda-Coke. Never accidentally bump into The Blond Snobby Lady? "OWNER" there. 
All l did was turn around and accidentally walked into her. Maybe she was standing too close to me. Oh, my l did not know That l had been impolite to The Queen 
of Nashville. I did not know anything was wrong. Then she says with a attitude and raised voice "Do You Always Run Into People and do not say excuse me?" 
If l had been a regular, l am sure she would have laughed it off. 
She never said she was The Owner. 
So she was unplugged and ready to start trouble. But l was not the bad guy-l was the customer. I thought she was a customer also. So l said "Are you drunk?so l made her day and she said "l am not drunk, l am the owner. I can have you kicked out for anything." My mistake was saying the first thing that came to my mind-l have never said this to another female. Channeling Bette Davis l said "What A itch." True, not a good thing to say to a person built like a football player. Next the Queen says off with her head and you are kicked out. 
I said are you serious? I am not drunk. Have had 2 Cokes. I said no, please let me say something to someone and l will leave. She said NO-you are leaving now. Then she went nuts and snatched my plastic cup of Coke out of my hand. Threw it up in the air and it landed where the bartender was. Barely missing her. She was Out of Control. Next she calls her good old boys and tells them to through me out. The 2 boys come up on either side of me grabbing a arm. They were moving faster than normal - it was just like being in The Wild West. Only l was a lady. l started to fall and they just dragged me. So l was the Entertainment for the whole bar. I was kicked out into 19degree weather. Once outside, l still said that was not right. The Owner calls the police while she smiles. I asked people who were leaving to call the police in my behalf-my phone was dead. Not one person would help. 
I left after speaking to a lady who came outside and she said she knew the owner and l better leave. She was afraid the owner would somehow get me arrested. 
I have reported this Joke of a place to 
The Nashville Major's Office- Assistant/Claudia H., The Department for Nashville Tourism, The Better business bureau, FB, and last Twitter.
I worked for Dept of Defense. I know channels for action. Also to treat a Tourist this way?? You do not mess with a Virginian Tourist. I give a big Fat 0 for this bar. Too bad the bartender and music was great. Southern Hospitality is essential. 
I read one review by a Customer who said while she was at the bar, the Owner and her girlfriend got into a fight. The police and an ambulance were called. The customer took a picture of the police car and posted it here. Also-if you see someone wearing a Poncho over a Skirt please call The Fashion Police. Seriously-this makes Nashville look bad. So if you want to get beat up-here's the place to try.
Okay food average at best breakfast. The biscuits were delicious but that was about it.

My wife and two daughters dined at City Winery this past Friday and had a most enjoyable experience. City Winery is not top of mind to us when trying to eat downtown before a show but we wanted to try some place different yet close to our venue. We were seated next to the barrels which provided great ambience. All of our food was fantastic but what really made our dinner fun and enjoyable was our server Gemaal.  He was attentive, personable, knew the menu well and was overall outstanding. Nashville needs more servers like him. BTW, we weren't there to see a show. We just wanted a quiet, relaxing good dinner before another show downtown and City Winery and Gemall exceeded our expectations. We will be back.

Absolutely the BEST Chicken ever!  I've eaten a ton of chicken in my 7 decades, and this is the best. From the first bite, I knew it was special. The breading was light, the meat wasn't dry nor too moist -- just right. The portion size was ample.  
We did OpenTable reservations and so our wait was brief. The server was very friendly and attentive, made you feel as welcome as if you were family. The building reminded me of eating at Grandma's house... neat as a pin and decorated like a nice farm house.  My only complaint was the floor joists must be weak because the table shook every time someone walked through the room; it was a bit annoying (we sat in a room on the left side).
Will definitely go out of way to eat here again when passing through Nashville.

Out on a culinary adventure in the hills of Middle Tennessee to find a staple that is almost 70 years old. After a little drive, I am here at the Loveless Cafe off of State Route 100 in Pasquo (southwest of Nashville). You can't miss it because of the iconic neon sign that welcomes you. Wow this was like going back in time to the 1950's. As I walk in the front door of this home from 1951 I feel like a lonely traveler on the road that Lon and Annie welcomed back in the day. You can tell that there was a lot of love and generosity in the home which later became the restaurant. As I walk in the door the smells are amazing. The aroma of home cooking floating through the air invites you to have a seat and make yourself at home. As I take my seat the waitress walks up to the table like your mom coming to ask what you would like for breakfast. I find out that she has worked here for more than 20 years. She was the true example of southern hospitality. Now I am anxious and excited to try the food. Almost immediately after taking my order I see her coming back to the table with a plate of hand made biscuits that look like soft and fluffy pillows with a trio of homemade jams. The jams were the perfect combination of sweet and tart made with love. Even with it being a busy Sunday morning, my food arrived before I was done with all of my biscuits. I ordered the Famous Loveless Cafe Country Ham with two over easy eggs and red eye gravy and the hash brown casserole on the side. Would they pass the test for good southern cooking? OMG that's all I can say. I give the Loveless Cafe 4 guitars. On busy days be prepared to wait unless you have a reservation. Fortunately, you have stuff to do while you wait as you can explore the grounds and gift shops where you can even by the jams you get to eat in the restaurant.

Similar to other reviewers, we went a bit out of the way to grab brunch here. About a 25 minute drive from my place off West End in Nashville, we waited about 40 minutes to be seated. The biscuits and jams were DELICIOUS. The breakfast selections my friend and I had (French Toast, and Waffle) were good sized and tasty, but nothing extraordinary. 

Definitely a good meal, a bit heavy, and worth checking out if you have time in your schedule for the drive out and for the wait!
Ahh so good to have good German food the Jager Schnitzel was very good . The service was  as well thank you to our waiter  .  He was great.

The food was mediocre. This is a fun place for a photo op, but I cannot vouch for the food at the cafe. I will say that I enjoyed the nearby gift shop. If you're traveling and want to bring back goodies (e.g., jams, sauces) for your loved ones, this is a great place to find those goods.

Just a neat place to go.  With platters you can get a sampling but they are ridgid on swapping sides or up charging for things like ribs.  BBQ is smothered style but the watermelon and cranberry BBQ sauces makes up for it.  Amazing sides.  Banana pudding that keeps the local cardiologist in business and is the gateway to heaven.

A complex worth a visit when all the shops are open.

While City Winery is a great venue, the service in the concert room and the food are really disappointing.  I've dined here twice now, and happened to get the same waiter both times.  Nothing was as I ordered/requested.  The waiter seemed aloof and didn't follow up with me like he said he would when I had questions about menu items.  During my most recent dining experience, one of the people in my party ordered the duck tacos and she was disappointed because conceptually it was not like the duck tacos she's had at most restaurants.  Another person in my party was disappointed with the calamari because it was just warm.  Both dining experiences did happen to take place during holiday weekends (Memorial Day and Labor Day), and I would think the servicing and kitchen staff would be on point but that was not the case.

If you haven't been to Germany you wouldn't know the food is not quite the quality as real German food. We've lived in Germany for 9 years and I am European. 

Now the food is ok but since this is suppose to be German we left the restaurant a little sceptic. I ordered a Jägerschnitzel and we shared a Flammkuchen. Now don't get me wrong it's ok and it looks authentic but the flavor was wanting. 
The bacon on the Flammkuchen was too hard and it looked as if it was pre-made bacon. It's supposed to be Speck and white onions. The parsley garnish completely dominated the flavor. There's usually no parsley on Flammkuchen. 

Jägerschnitzel was fine if you don't know how it's suppose to taste like. This was just a pork chop with some tasteless breading. The mushroom sauce=Jägersauce was just brown gravy with seemingly canned mushrooms as a garnish. It didn't taste right and it didn't taste like mushroom. 

When you order a schnitzel in Germany the kitchen sounds like a construction zone because the chef hammers the pork down to almost hair thin so it cooks quickly and the breading stays crispy. The breading has subtle spices and full of flavor. The sauce is suppose to be more dark red/brown and flavored of  mushroom, wine and cream. Mushrooms are the key ingredient in a jägersauce not the garnish. If you have a German restaurant it would be important to an authentic German restaurant to at least get the schnitzel right- and unfortunately this wasn't right. 
The fries were great and had a subtle dusting of spices. 

The atmosphere is nice and I love the decor. It has the Hofbräuhaus feeling. 
However in Germany our bill would be half the price and the food twice as good and the beer as cheap as mineral water.

Loveless Cafe 
8400 Tennessee Highway 100
Nashville, TN 37221

We had a late breakfast here and absolutely loved it. This is the real deal, down home true Southern cooking at its best. The biscuits were genuine home made and you can watch the whole process in the back! Great food and service. All the bacon, sausage and hans are made right there. The jams and jellies are fantastic too!   I would recommend as a must anytime you come near Nashville. 

Urban Cowgill 
Dec 2015

The food and ambiance was amazing! The service... extremely slow. Wine glasses empty, never offering another round, dirty appetizer plates stacked on the table forever. Our reservation was at 7, we got our Che ha ag 9:30. Everything seemed to take a very long time. 
Everyone's food was so yummy ! I had the lamb sandwich, I can't wait to have it again! The risotto balls with punkin and goat cheese were a big hit, as well as the calamari. 
Another annoyance is when the music starts in the venue, and you're in the restI would go back for sure with hopes of a better service experience.

I came here back in July as a tourist it was highly recommended so I stopped in on my to Memphis.  Wait was an hour and half, I was hoping being a party of 1 there would be a bar I could sit at or something for a little faster service.  When I got seated it was for a table of 6, I felt bad for my server cause I was taking up such a big table but thats where they sat me and after an hour and half wait I was hungry lol

I was super disappointed in the biscuits and the country gravy being in the south I had much higher expectations.  The jams were all really good though.  I wasn't a fan of the sausage either but the ham was melt in your mouth hands down the best ham I've ever had in my life! 

The grounds have some outside games and several stores and galleries to shop at while you wait which helps pass the time as well.

Tough one. Love the idea...listening room with upscale feel and good quality talent. Enjoyed the show and experience overall.

Why 3 stars? The food was awful. The chicken saltimbocca was not good. The chicken itself was OK, but small. The sweet potato risotto around it was probably the worst risotto I've ever had. $22 for airplane caliber food. My sister had flatbread which was pizza and Chuck E. Cheese pizza at best. The wine was way over priced and the service wasn't great (beer bottles with no glasses, flatbread with no small plates to use, etc.). They had only 2 beers on draft that weren't sours or ciders. 

If u like the musician, go and it'll be good. Just skip the food n have low expectations of alcohol and service.
Great German food.  Fun music and very like a German beer hall.  Good beer and great dessert.

Simply, amazing food! You can not go wrong with anything on the menu. Favorites include the catfish, meatloaf, fried chicken (Chicken and Waffles!), and, well, pretty much everything I've ever had! Their seasonings at the onsite store are amazing, especially the seasoning salt! 

Oh, I can't believe I forgot their biscuits and preserves / apple or pumpkin butter! We keep a supply at home... I think y'all get the point.. only advise is call ahead to check the current wait time... Loveless is that amazing!

Went here because I saw the great reviews. Planned it into my road trip because I thought it would be the perfect stop. Sadly this place was highly overrated! Waited 1 hour for a table - which I expected. Once seated the side plate had cheese crushed on it which grossed me out. I pushed through got a new clean plate. I ordered the biscuit sampler with my choice being ham, fried green tomatoes, fried chicken and bacon side of hash brown casserole. Once the food arrived the only thing warm/hot was the hash brown casserole. I waited for the server to come to the table to check on us to inform her about the food but she didn't arrive. I finally flagged her down and she signed across the room do you want the check. I turned the signal for her to come closer to let her know about the food. She walked over and I explained the food was cold except for the hash brown casserole. She apologized and took the whole plate. Once she returned with all but one biscuit and it was STILL COLD as if nothing changed on the plate. She walked away before asking if the dish was to my liking. She returned shortly after with the missing biscuit which the meat was hot but the biscuit still cold. Still she walked away before asking how the food was the second time. Very irritated and disappointed at this point we never saw the server again until she dropped the check and left. Also no manager came to the table, the mistake didn't get fixed, and no comp meal (which I didn't want anyways). All I wanted was a hot meal done right. 

Needless to say this was one of the worst customer service places I have been. I won't recommend because of the service and food. For 40$ a meal I expect a little more.

If I could give it a 0 I definitely would. My parents (who live out of state) sent my wife and I a gift card for our 10 year anniversary so we gave it a go. What a mistake. The food was practically inedible. Our waters were never refilled. The whole experience was just ridiculous.  Avoid this place. Or spend 85$ on a fancy meal for your dog later.

We went 2 days in a row while visiting Nashville.  One of the owners was working and checking on the guest. He spent alot of time helping his guest and we had a great time. I really loved the jagersnitzel  and cheese  soup

Nice atmosphere but don't stop for a quick drink or bite! Stopped in on a Saturday at 3pm and sat at the bar. After going unnoticed for 15 minutes sitting AT THE BAR, my wife went to stand at the register to get the attention of the poorly trained (or managed) staff. The one girl behind the bar was far too busy running checks(?) to acknowledge patrons. The beer on the other hand was excellent (I had the Schnickelfritz). If management can train the staff properly this could be a nice experience. Use caution if in a time crunch.

If I could give negative stars I would. Came in to support a friend that was playing in the band. The bartender came up very rudely and says "yeah?" As he was biting his nails. Ok well hi. My husband and I ordered two beers and his response was "what?" Ok can we have "blah blah blah" walks away still biting his nails. Stops and keeps biting and spits his nail in the trash. So that's gross. Walks over to people at the bar does a shot while staring me down and still hasn't given us our beer. My husband and i walk over and say "just cancel our order" and his response was to just laugh and let us leave. I work in the bar industry and I have NEVER experienced such rudeness and unprofessionalism in my life!!!
This is a fun place! The pretzels were amazing! That alone would earn a five stars. I would recommend this place. That being said it wasn't my favorite food choice.

I went here for yoga class. Mitchell is amazing and very detailed. She makes you feel good and helps you if your form is not correct which is important to avoid injuries. You can't imagine how easy is to hurts yourself trying to improve yourself.

This class is on Saturdays at 11 but you can check their website for more information and other classes. This places is a fun place. They have a cafe shop inside as well. Parking and entrance in on the back of the building.

This was my second time visiting Loveless Cafe. The first time I had a great experience. Tonight I was extremely dissatisfied in the food and service I received. I ordered the country fried steak. What came out was a poor execution of a southern classic. The steak had little to no flavor. The breading was bland and soft. Country fried steak should have a crunchy and well seasoned breading. When Cracker Barrel has a better steak then that is a problem for a restaurant claiming to be a purveyor of southern cuisine. 
I took a grand total of three bites from my steak.  The waiter never questioned why I didn't eat my steak despite my lack of consumption. This is something that a trained waiter should look for. It seemed that the waiter was non-confrontational and didn't want to deal with it. I even handed them my plate with the almost entire steak still on it. 
I doubt I will return to Loveless in the future. Nor will I tell my friends to go as well. 
I encourage Loveless to rethink what they are serving customers and train their waitstaff to look for signs of a dissatisfied customer.

A little ways outside of Nashville but worth the trip! The drive to get to Loveless is beautiful. Expect a wait, especially on the weekends, but spend the time waiting browsing the 5-6 gift shops and beautiful grounds. The biscuits were to die for! We went with a group of 9 and everyone left satisfied, if not stuffed.
Food and service was amazing best german potato salad ever! I can't wait tonreturn just to try different items.

I was just abused by the bouncer at this location.  I'm no spring chicken and I questioned needing to see my aiD and walked away, he said "go F*** yourself ".  Needless to say this guy shouldn't be anywhere near the public!

Great food, unfortunately, horrible customer service....
I made a reservation for 12 people about 3 weeks ago. It was my birthday this past weekend, so I made sure that I made all of my reservations well in advance. We were about 12 minutes late for our reservation, however I called in advance to let them know. Once we arrived at the restaurant they had a table ready for us, for 8 people. I let them know that I made the reservation for 12, and they said that they didn't have our table in the system and it would be a 30 minute wait.. They then tried to blame us, saying that we were 20 minutes late for our reservation. Mind you, we were NOT that late, and I called in advance to let them know.  Once we finally got seated, we basically had no service. They switched waiters 3 different times, and no one came to our table. At the end of the dinner, we asked the manager for some sort of compensation for the inconvenience and horrible service, and he refused. He said that we should not have gotten there late and the general manager will not give us any compensation. I refused to tip them, and I let them know that I will not be back again.

It was very disappointing because we have been to the City Winery in Napa and we actually love it. I did not expect such horrible service in Nashville.

This place is very cute. The wait was around two hours for a party of five on a Sunday at 10am. Everything that we ordered was great and the little stores are a nice touch. Nothing was overpriced. Was a nice place to spend a Sunday morning.

This place is awesome! This is the 2nd time I've been. 

Great food! I went with a group and we ordered family style and it fed the 8 of us to beyond full. 

The service was great too! Friendly waitress! She was busy, but still was personable and kept our drinks full. I think her name was Rachel! 

The only down is they don't let you keep the left overs that are on the table, a lot of waste.

If you are in Nashville this is so worth the drive! Best breakfast by far! Biscuits, jam, country fried steak.....oh so good! It is so worth waiting for if there is a line. Little shops are very cute also! Was number one of favorite food venues while we have been here!

The 615 wine is excellent. The sound is excellent and there's not a bad seat in the house. Jose' and Caitlin were nice and helpful. I actually had an issue that wasn't their fault but they really bent over backwards to make it right. In the end I had a lovely time. 

The menu does not have a lot of basic dishes, so if you are picky or will have a picky person in your party, I recommend checking out the menu online beforehand.

Loveless cafe was on my list of places to eat while visiting Nashville. It's not far from Belle Meade so squeeze in a lunch or breakfast before your tour. My son and I LOVED the chicken and waffle. My daughter and husband like the spicy chicken daily special. He is still talking about the hash brown casserole a day later. With the wait!

As a venue this place is amazing. There's not a bad seat in the house and the acoustics are awesome. The food is mediocre and expensive. The wine can be hit or miss as well. Also, this last time we were here it was freezing cold to the point that we kept our winter jackets on for the duration of the show. I'm not sure if they keep it cooler on purpose on account of the wine but it was a little unbearable.

Had a wonderful breakfast!  We were seated within 5 minutes of arriving, around 10:30 on a Friday.   The country fried steak was bigger than my face!  The homemade biscuits and jams were outstanding. We are so glad we listened to the amazing recommendations for this place. We will definitely be back!!!

Biscuits, biscuits, biscuits. Yum!! The biscuits and preserves are the best part of the meal. Food is always hot and fresh. I love to eat here when in Nashville. I seem to keep missing the Nashville hot chicken special day though!!  This place is worth the short drive. The shops are great to browse in while you wait and the food is really good

Easily the best burger in Nashville. 
Our server Kim took care of us and she couldn't have been better. Spoke to our kids as soon as she came to the table, and had perfect drink recommendations for stressed parents. 
Will be going back for the burger ASAP!!!!

My favorite breakfast spot in Tennessee! Came here the first day I arrived and it was so good I had to have it again before I left. By far my favorite biscuits and preserves I had while on my trip. Even bought some jars of my own to take back home. I had their Music City Platter with the Ham and it was amazing! Massive portion was sure to keep me filled until dinner! I'll definitely be back on my next trip to TN

Waited 5 mins without evening being approached by a host. We were right at the counter, and finally told us 45 min wait for a seat. We decided to sit at the bar.She,bartender told us that quote" you're gonna be waiting very long for your food like an hour." That's without hi, what's up, ordering food or just drinking? And she clearly just had a cigarette. Gross and rude.  So we weren't concerned with ordering food and left..the thing is that it wasn't even packed, tons of open seats for a party of 2. Terrible service

Great venue. Lovely menu. The food has been the highlight each time I've visited. The wine list is extensive, although I'm not much of a wino. They also partner with a local shelter so I'm inclined to love their commitment to Nashville. This is easily my favorite attribute of the venue. 

During shows you're often seated with strangers. Not an issue for me since I love meeting new people. 

The service is so slow it makes coming here unbearable. I loathe coming to this venue based on service alone. They have table toppers as a feature to let your server know you need something. Unfortunately, it is extremely ineffective. Servers look past the table topper, ignoring your need for service.

While I appreciate their uniqueness as an urban winery and commitment to the local economy/people of Nashville, it pains me to say, don't come here expecting much more than a great show. Expecting anything more would be a disservice to yourself. 

Cheers!
Sadly had to walk out when told at 62 years old I needed to have id to order a drink. What??? Have had drinks elsewhere in Nashville without id. Silliness

We went for lunch today and it was our first time here. Everything was excellent!!! Fun staff. Neat atmosphere. Good prices. Great food and fun shops to check out. The portions are huge so we have leftovers for dinner tonight. A must see.

The service was very good  our server Micah made great beer suggestions. We split the king plate. The food tasted like it had been prepared hours ahead and just kept slightly warm   The pork chop was very good even being barely warm. Great atmosphere. Next time just beer and pretzels!

This is all I'm gonna say about this place. 

I was told my grand momma passed.  Nope, she's in the kitchen of the Loveless making biscuits and preserves. 

Yep, they are that good.
It's quite a ride out there but fun to bring family and friends when visiting. The biscuits are amazing. I wish they had more vegetarian options.

There's not a whole lot about Loveless Cafe I can contribute that hasn't already been said...but they are absolutely worthy of another 5-star yelp review! We came with a big party of 16 on a weekend while we were in town for a conference. It was hard to rally the troops to drive out to the middle of nowhere and commit to an hour + wait, but it was well worth it.  While we waited there was stuff to keep us occupied on the grounds.  We played corn hole and visited the shops. Side note: the people in the shops are just as nice as the wonderful staff in the restaurants. The girl at the gift shop let all of us try the different jams and was genuinely sweet at could be.  

We were seated in a back area where we had the whole room to ourselves. It was perfect! Our waitress was awesome and I can't say enough good things about every single member of the staff we encountered. I'm not sure how they did it, but every single order was right and came out at the same time. And of course the food was out of this world! You get a huge serving and everything is perfect. I'm glad I don't live in Nashville, because I would easily gain 20 lbs from eating there so often! 

We were the last diners in the restaurant that night, and did not remotely feel rushed out by the staff. They encouraged us to enjoy ourselves and stick around for dessert...which we gladly did! We had to hit the road to drive back to Chicago early the next morning, so they sent us home with a ton of extra biscuits they had leftover from the day.  Seriously, if you're ever going to Nashville, you HAVE to go to Loveless Cafe!!

Went on a BUSY Sat evening and decided to sit at the bar. It was a nice experience sitting there. The bar tender could have been a little more attentive, but they were quite busy. We started with the large pretzel, yummy!! I had the fish and chips and the fish is probably the best I've ever had! Light and crispy, I just didn't feel like the portion size was large enough, 2 1/4 pieces. The rest of my party had the chicken schnitzel, jagerschnitzel and wurst plate. They also tried various German beers, I was the DD for the night.
We love this place AND will be back!!

Biscuits, biscuits and more delicious biscuits. Honestly some of the best I've ever had. The brisket was pretty darn good too. My tip is to go early for breakfast to avoid the line. Luckily we arrived early enough and only had to wait 20 minutes. While we waited, we walked around the motel and country store.
I'd go back just for the biscuits, they were so good that I couldn't finish my breakfast.

Hands down one of my favorite places to go! Their biscuits and fried chicken are amazing!!!!! It's an iconic tourist spot but even if you have to wait they have cute shops and games and things you can do in the meantime! I'd recommend anyone go there.

After hearing about the famous Loveless Cafe for the past 3 months, I finally had the opportunity to try it out. And I must say, it did not disappoint. The Loveless is much more than just a cafe. There is a gift shop, gallery, and a few other buildings. It's like a mini campus. If you love it in the restaurant, you can buy it in the store.

The cafe itself is very kitschy southern comfort. Comfortable enough and if you go during the week, there shouldn't be a wait. On the weekend, good luck. The menu is full of southern classics. They have a good cocktail menu and my strawberry drink was delicious. I even got a little souvenir shot-glass mug thing. They only have 5 beers though, non that are tasty. I would stick with the cocktails, even though they run about $11 a piece. The best part is of course the appetizer of biscuits. Their jam is to die for. I could have filled up on biscuits alone. Will definitely be buying some of their jam. The main courses were also delicious. Lots of side options. You can substitute the fries for any side (and they suggest, almost demand, that you do). 

In the end, you will leave this place unbuttoning your pants so you can breathe. It's a great tourist spot if you have people visiting. Little too touristy for me just to go back on my own. But maybe for those biscuits...

We love Loveless!! Our first trip to Nashville and we ended up going out to the cafe twice for breakfast . The biscuits are dreamy. Ham was yummy!  This is a great place for kids also. You have to go to Loveless!! We also bought several bags of biscuit mix and jam for gifts.

We had a great meal and ate a lot of biscuits on this trip.  My wife got a nice smoked porkchop and I got the fried chicken.  The service was great.  This was a bit out of the way for us, but ultimately worth the drive from Nashville.  We enjoyed the jams and preserves, so we bought some in the local shops afterwards.
Solid menu and fast, efficient service. Decent German beer selection and reasonably priced.
Wait was not too bad but long since it was a Sunday, but ABSOLUTELY worth the wait. Biscuits and jams were Phenomenal! Service and hospitality was top notch! A must dine when you're in Nashville.

Absolutely mediocre. If you want a beer by all means I would have one and then leave and go get dinner! The pork shank pretty much was so over cooked it had a few tender parts and the rest were great toothpicks.

Fun place with good beer but if you love German food you might be disappointed.   The quality of meat was good.  The biggest disappointment was the run of the mill gravy and tiny portions.  $27 for a King Ludwig sampler should have more than a spoonful of kraut and red cabbage.  Overall not worth the money and I probably won't return.  Very disappointed.

The wait was long (1 hr and 30min) but it was worth it. To start, the biscuits and preserves were tasty but it was the fried catfish that earned the 5 stars!! Fresh and fried to perfection!! Server was good too. While this place is kinda outta the way, it is a gem worth exploring.
Waited 2 HOURS for a table. Food was good especially the biscuits. Would give 5 stars but for the wait. Seems like they could use more help especially for take out.

I wanted to like it. Recommended by a friend. Fried chicken was dry and over cooked. They gave me a new one but still the same. The gravy was cold and did not taste homemade. The creamed corn was yummy. The biscuits were also great along with the preserves. Service was great. Manager came and made things right but it was still very disappointing.

I'd never been to this (or any other city's) City Winery before until a recent show (Rickie Lee Jones) brought us out. A few artists I like had played the venue before but I'd never pulled the trigger on purchasing tickets. The price was right for RLJ and we'd wanted to see her for some time so we gave them a try. As a music venue it's pretty solid--we were on the balcony, which oddly had cheaper tickets and from what I could gather a much better view than anywhere on the floor save for the front row. In terms of atmosphere, it's a very chill/laid back show and I could imagine that some artists recede into background music material. Thankfully Rickie had requested no food service during the show and the audience was fairly involved so it felt like an actual concert not just an excuse to eat and drink with music in the background (she did a terrific set by the way).
The food was good+. A bit pricey for what it is, particularly portion size. For example, I ordered the shrimp and grits entrée which was $22; it was delicious. But, it was an appetizer portion at best. If they'd had 2-3 more scoops of grits with shrimp to match it would have been completely fair. The Brussel sprouts are really good, also a bit pricey for the serving size. And the desserts are really good (but again, very small serving sizes). Everything we ate was good but unless you order a burger you're apt to leave hungry if this is your dinner.
There's a good selection of wines but I honestly wasn't in the mood for wine. They have some house specialties, about $10-$15 a pour, and some fairly priced bottles to take home. I opted for 1 each of the 2 local craft brews they have on tap, both of which were good. My wife enjoyed the house white, though.

Parking is interesting--they do valet for very cheap (maybe $10 or less?) but if you go that route it takes an incredibly long time to get your car at the end of the evening, longer than the valet at the Ryman even. Pro tip--there's a $15 all night lot in the parking lot down the hill from the front doors--walk to it after the show and be on your way before the first person in line at the valet is.

Oh my.  Was I in for a treat.  I've been going to this place for about 6months and always ordered the 3 sausage plate until I came with my son and he ordered the Schweinshaxe. It was awesome.  Plus the Bartender Kathleen was very nice and knowledgeable. She sure made the experience better.  Definitely will recommend this place to my friends

Went for late night snack after the Opry. Really fun environment.

We had the "German" onion soup. Very good.

Had a few Wurst with German Potato Salad and Sauerkraut 

Also the Shnitzel which was moist and crisp the Spatzel was really too salty though. 

I would go again..
Great spot all around! Great food, excellent service!  Have eaten and experienced numerous shows here. Never disappointed. Reccomend to all.

I give this place a 2 star due to the hospitality Bavarian brieuhouse conducted. Food was wonderful but the staff wasn't something that I would call professional. My waitress Amy was astounding and very pleasant to be around! But the one flaw that I overheard was just rude and hateful. I can't remember the young girls name, she has short blonde hair wearing an ear piece, and wasn't in full uniform, she was speaking with another employee about another waitress. She was saying some awful stuff about my waitress. I felt that everything she had said was just mean. I feel like if they need to speak about anything not on the floor but in the back! Anyways, thanks again for the great food I doubt I'll be back.

The biscuits and the breakfast was good. Keep in mind we had to wait over an hour for breakfast.  We thought that the restaurant wasn't busy but it was because everyone was walking around the area waiting for their table. I'd recommend going earlier or bring a good book because you'll be most likely waiting a while.

(Biscuit & Gravy review only) Being born and raised in the south I've had some good biscuits but the biscuits here were not what I expected based on other reviews. Now don't get me wrong, they were good biscuits, but truly special they were not(8/10 at most). Their homemade jam was good(9/10). Gravy on the biscuits was only ok(7/10). I still want to try their other food.

By far my favorite restaurant! If you're new to the Nashville area, been here for a while, or just passing through you have to stop in and give it a shot. My family is from Germany, and this is the closest thing to authentic I've found it feels just like Germany! Outstanding service and great food puts this place far ahead of any establishment in the area. Great environment to experience for families, friends, and anyone honestly. If you haven't been here, you need to make this your next destination for a great time!

We were schooled in the delicacies of southern cuisine today when visiting the Loveless Cafe. Upon arrival, we were asked if we'd ever been here before and when we replied no, our server made sure to welcome us and explain everything. We were immediately served warm biscuits with three different housemade jams. I'm not normally a biscuit fan but these were light and tasty. Husband had the sampler platter with a pork chop, catfish, and pulled pork. His two sides were cheesy garlic smashed potatoes and the hash brown casserole. He wasn't a fan of the bbq sauce because it wasn't what he was used to but the catfish was especially delicious. We had to ask what a hush puppy was! The sampler platter was a great way to try different things but in hindsight, he shouldn't have picked two porks and two cheesy sides. Definitely filling! So what is a vegetarian to do in such a place? Loveless offers the chance to choose three or four sides to make a meal. I chose fried green tomatoes, cheesy garlic smashed potatoes, and marinated cucumbers and onions. Portions were enough to give a good taste and fill me up. The pies looked delicious but no room so I got peanut butter pie to go and our server threw in a sample of the banana pudding. I'm sure they will both be good! For some good old fashioned fun while waiting for your food, you can do a word scramble and word search. We tend to be a little competitive but we tied on the word search and did the scramble cooperatively! Just in case you want to bring home some jam or other gift items, there are several gift shops which used to house the motel. Fun stop! (And now we understand a little more about southern cooking!)

We had a private event here for my daughter's graduation from Vanderbilt.  We used the private room and patio and it was fabulous. We worked with Tianna and she was so helpful to me as I was trying to organize the event with 4 families.  The staff on the day of the party was wonderful (they set up all my decorations while we were at graduation) and the food was delicious.  I would highly recommend City Winery for an event!

Worse place I've been downtown and I live in Nashville. I'll never go back. I was there with some people I knew and the bartender was looking at them asking them what they wanted when it was me paying for myself. When I brought it to her attention to listen to me and not them since it was my card she replied with "don't get an attitude with me". I purposely did not leave a tip but some how got charged for a tip on my card.... I guess stealing is ok to her.

Came here for Easter Dinner and was very impressed! The space is beautiful, well-kept and the perfect setting for a relaxing evening. We couldn't decide which wines we wanted, so we ordered a few flights and were impressed by all the wines we had. They recently changed their menu but we loved the food we had ordered.  Their menu is (obviously) wine-focused so everything we tasted matched really well with our wines. 

What really stood out to me however is the service.  All of the employees seemed genuinely happy to be there and were eager to help with any recommendations or questions we had. It seems as though management has really created a great atmosphere for the employees and it certainly showed throughout our dinner.  At the end, we spoke with Rayna who was absolutely lovely and as gracious as could be.  Her demeanor and passion blew us all away.  We will definitely be back soon because of her!

First of all,
YES, YES, and YES! 

I came on a Friday night around 4:25 so it wasn't very busy yet and parking was not terribly difficult but I can see how it can fill up and become a challenge very easily. There are a lot of buildings on the property and if you don't look at the signs pointing you which way to go, it could be possible for someone to get confused as to where the actual cafe is. 
When walking in the main entrance of the cafe is plastered with autographed pictures of celebrities and country music stars who came and ate. 
It's warm and welcome. The decor is very Country but cute and fitting.

Once sat you get the choice of all day breakfast or lunch. They also have alcohol and some other specialty drinks. 
I got the Country ham platter. 
You can sub out the eggs for a long additional side if you do not want the eggs. I got the green beans "(delicious country bacon green beans), caramel sweet potatoes (not too sweet.. just right), and the creamed corn (good but definitely not what you would expect) 

The biscuits are to die for( softest, most buttery biscuits ever) as is every single preserve I got to try with it (peach, strawberry, and blackberry). 

My portion is huge. I got a huge ham steak, there biscuits, and three sides and I came alone! Haha!

The staff is fantastically friendly. True southern hospitality that makes the state of Tennessee proud.

There is a "motel" part of the property, as well as a barn, a "Hams & Jams" gift shop type, and then an area where you can have events such as weddings.

I see why this place is so popular and I highly recommend it for GOOD, SOUTHERN STYLE Grandma Sue's cookin'!

After mine and my husband's second visit to Tennessee, we decided to stop by the famous Loveless Cafe that my cousin had been telling me about prior to moving out east.  

From the outside it's not much to look at and you'd totally miss it.  We actually did and had to turn around.  But after going inside and looking up a bit of the story, we found out the cafe was built out of the Loveless family house and preserved to look as it did back in the early days, which made it something special.

The waitresses were all so friendly and attentive.  It really seemed as though they loved being a part of this charming time capsule.  Coming from California, I not my husband are accustomed to real Southern food which seems to be massive, deep-fried and delicious.

My husband ordered the fried pork chops which came with two large chops.  They were so tasty he literally made himself sick because he refused to not finish both singlehandedly.  If I were to have ordered the same this would for sure have been a 5 star review.  I however opted for the white meat fried chicken plate.  I never eat chicken skin, but this skin was fried so well that the skin was not fatty and instead was crisp and delicious.  The chicken however was so dry I could not eat it.  I loved the biscuits which come free as soon as you sit down complete with several homemade jams and jellies.  

I will definitely come back next time I'm in Tennessee and ready to really eat, but I won't be ordering the chicken.

Stopped in for a few drinks and ended up spending a few hundred dollars.  Bartenders were very pleasant and quick to make sure you had a drink.  At the end of the night, my friend, (male) and my cousin (female) had to use the restroom.  They asked the bartender if they could use the restroom, and she said yes.  As they walked to the restroom they were stopped by the manager of the bar.  He told my cousin ( female ) she could use the restroom, and told my friend (male) to get out of the bar.  We tried to explain that the bartender said it was ok to use the restroom but he was not willing to hear anything we were asking.  It ok, will NEVER visit this place again.

I stumbled across this place as I was walking through the mall next to the grand old Opry and the Gaylord Opryland hotel.  

Fortunately they have large signs advertising inside the mall or I would not of known about this place. There was a nice marquee in the mall that showed their menu and a girl dressed in a German outfit to answer all your questions.  She even gave me a coupon for a free pretzel a six dollar savings.  

I was torn between three items on the menu and chose the chef special called, Schweinshake.  It was basically a large hunk of meat on a large bone ..  it was unbelievably good and it came with some type of red cabbage on the side.

Everything was good I would probably order something else next time certainly like my free pretzel with cheese. I would highly recommend this place if you like German food.

Went here on a Saturday night while on a bachelorette weekend. Thankfully we had reservations because this place was packed. The inside is decorated nicely and feels as an upscale restaurant should. The menu has some different/unique options but I ended up ordering the Chicken Caesar salad which ended up costing me $20 plus tip. The salad was delicious and it was a very large serving; however, the amount of chicken that came on the salad was limited and I have a hard time justifying paying that much for a salad anywhere. A glass of wine was also kinda pricey, so I chose to forgo trying any of the wine. Also, service wasn't really all that speedy. We had reservations for 8PM and it was probably closer to 9PM before we even got our food. I will say it was a nice gesture for the restaurant to give my friend the bride a complimentary bottle of wine to take home. I've never been to a place that did that.

Drove 6hrs to this place as our first stop in Nashville. I'm only giving 3 stars bc the biscuits were worth coming here (the jam more than the biscuits.. kinda overrated and not worth over an hour wait). Waited 40 min to be sat (that's fine and was expected).. sat down and it took 30 mins for our order to be taken because our server didn't know how to multi-task. He was rude too when his tables (4 total) kept asking just to get their drink and food orders taken. He even gave one of his tables to another server because apparently he couldn't handle it. He kept doing things one at a time instead of all at once. I've served before and getting sat 3 new tables is no hassle. Very disappointed with driving all this way.

SO much fun! This German restaurant is located in Opry Mills Mall and there is tons of seating for however many people are in your party. Big wooden picnic benches line the large space and there is a big stage with live music. Large bar area as well if you want to sit in a smaller space. 

The beer selection is really good, especially if you like German beers! The food was fantastic as well. Large portions and everything was served piping hot. Yummy! I had a wurst platter and it was more than I could finish. Sign up for their email club and enjoy a free pretzel appetizer. Plus 15% off in the gift shop if you check in on Yelp!

Great experience. I would love to bring my family back here!
We had a wonderful time at Marc Broussard (my favorite) in New Years!! Jared, our waiter was AWESOME!! Made us feel so welcome and was just so sweet! Great time!

Good food, fun place to have meal with all family! We find some delicious German hotdog with red cabbage and potatoes salad with addition to meal of cause German sampled beer for my husband I ordered schnitzel for me, I prefer vine, so I give shots to German vine- it's ok, I may be next time will trying some ale, we have great time! People nice! Servant doing job, understand it's what they do and understand they are job part of entertainment business not only food chain.

Went for dinner at this place and it was one of my favourite spots in Nashville. The food is fantastic- I recommend the southern sampler. Our server handled our group of 12 like a pro. If you stop in take time to look through the little gift shops. I scored some candied bacon popcorn. Definitely recommend this place!
Band was awesome. Service is terrible. Place was full and had one bartender. Air conditioning is weak. Tons if other good bars.

Just had some bomb brunch at the loveless cafe.... let me tell you there is enough love to go around at this place. Virginia was our server and she was da bomb.com. I'm from Boston and bet your ass I'm coming back here to sit at her table. One of the best experiences I've ever had and I'm a server in the industry as well. Virginia you keep on rocking girl.... love ya! -Tony
I've eaten here twice and I have never done a review so here it goes. It's about the greatest comfort food on the planet. It's all good and the people are amazing. Enjoy!

Stopped for lunch on our way to The Smokey Mountains. Well worth the out of route!!!!! Loved the grounds and things to do and see while we waited. Best biscuits I've ever had and the chicken strips were amazing! Will come back the next time I'm in the area!

Wow!

My former roommate and I met here for dinner while I was in town for a couple of days. I am so thankful she suggested this restaurant! The food was exactly what I was looking for as an out of towner- down home, country fare. I ordered the pit-cooked pork barbeque. The pulled meat was presented on top of two cornbread hoe cakes with a drizzle of barbeque sauce. The fluffiness of the hoe cakes soaked up all of the juicy goodness perfectly. The dish came with two sides. I chose fried green tomatoes and coleslaw. In true Tennessee style, I enjoyed everything with a glass of sweet iced tea. With the portions being as large as they are, I left with a full belly and a nearly full container of left overs. 

Our server, Owen, was very friendly and accommodating. When he learned this was my visit to Loveless Cafe, he offered a few suggestions of their more popular items. He provided excellent customer service and his humor & hospitality made for a memorable experience.

We were in the Nashville area and were doing some exploring. We had heard that it was a great choice. We stopped by and were amazed by all the people hanging out in the area. Little did we know that it was due to the wait for seating. We put our name in the queue and explored for the hour plus. We watched the prep in the smokehouse. Explored the stores and played the games around. It was a warm day but time passed seemingly quickly. Once we saw the menu and ordered we knew that we had made the right choice. When food arrived we were amazed at the portion sizes. The food was fabulous and we had enough for snacks later in the day. The only drawback is that we did not plan for the very long wait. When we are in the area again we will be back.

Amazing!!!! The biscuits were unlike any biscuit I've ever had!!! We had a 45 minute wait, but it went smooth because of the shops/activities to do on the same campus. We hope our travels will bring us back!!!

I stopped in while leaving downtown to avoid the rush hour traffic and only planned on having a beer or two. I sat at the bar and right away felt welcomed by the friendly bartender who had some great recommendations of their draft beer selection. One of her coworkers had come in on their day off (which I always think is a good sign of the vibe) and I ended up talking with them for a solid 2 hours. At this point traffic had long died down and I could have made my way home with ease, but I was having a great time trying new beers and hanging with those at the bar.
I decided to give their food menu a shot, and quickly found several options that sounded perfect (although definitely not the $13 frito chili pie...$13 ?!?!?). I ended up settling on the patty melt with fries. This was an excellent choice and I will definitely be tempted to get it again even though I love trying different items when returning to new spots. Will be a hard decision next time!
All in all, Fat Kat Slims has a good beer selection, tasty food, and even better atmosphere created by their staff. I'm all for going back to check out their live music and hang on the nice big wrapping patio in the Spring and Summer.

Been here twice on our Nashville trips and I'm in love with those biscuits! They start you off with them at breakfast with housemade jams,amazing. Country ham with red eye gravy is my go to with eggs but whatever we've gotten has been great prepare for a wait especially on the weekends but well worth it.

Prost!

Ha!  What can beat a good German beer, pretzel or wurst?  Not much.  So we headed over to the Bavarian Bierhaus for Sunday lunch.  It was very quiet but you could tell from the souvenirs of the restaurant and all of the stein lockers when we walked in, that quiet is not the norm!

We had the currywurst and the sampler where you can choose two sausages.  We went with the waitresses recommendation of the Oktoberfest and the Smoked Wurst.  They were all delicious and each one had a little kick to it.  Not much, just enough to let you know it was there. Overall our firm favorite was the currywurst- simply delectable.

We finished off by splitting Black Forest Gateaux and it was everything a Black Forest cake should be.  Not too much Kirsch and just enough cherries to keep it moist and delicious.

Don't forget to take advantage of the Yelp15 offer to receive 15% off the bill.

Visiting Nashville for the weekend and was taken here by family as this is supposed to be a Nashville staple (plus I'm a sucker for fried chicken and biscuits). Dropped by on a Saturday around 1pm. We had to wait for about an hour before a table became available (we were a group of 6). Here's my take on this establishment:

1. Service: Our waiter was superb; friendly and explained everything to us. The lady who greeted us at the entrance and took our names down was not so friendly. 

2. Food: I got the Loveless fried chicken with two sides (turnips in liquor and caramel sweet potato). The fried chicken was yummy, but by no means the best I've ever had. The sides were mediocre. Sweet potatoes were way too sweet and soggy. Turnips were fine. 
Their biscuits are really good, but I personally preferred them more with butter or dipped in gravy. The gravy was great. Not sure what the hype is about their preserves... tasted good but nothing amazing?
Portions are good. 

3. Price: Good value. 

4. Aesthetics: Casual and cozy. Bathrooms were nice and clean. One thing I noticed when I first sat down was that there was some kind of food on my chair (and it was wet) which I had to clean up (and of course, I chose to wear white jeans just that day, haha). 

Would I go back? I personally don't think the wait is worth it. The food was good but not mind blowing and definitely not worth waiting 1 hour.

Left so full and satisfied! 

Definitely get their country ham, it's salty goodness on a plate! BF got the Famous Country Ham with eggs and I thought why not have a pancake too so I ordered that platter and boy what a mistake. Come hungry cause they start you off with the biscuits and it's all food extravaganza from there. 

Biscuits were interesting, tasted different and my BF told me that it's the buttermilk they must use. As I ate another one I was getting used to it and slathering on the strawberry jam they provided. 

Then our breakfast plates arrived and I saw my mistake instantly. 3 large pancakes along with the home fries, egg, and ham I ordered. The home fries were tasty, gobbled those up with the egg and ham real fast. When faced with the pancake though, couldn't even finish one and gave the other to my BF. I was defeated. Didn't help my BF asked for another order of biscuits after we finished the first. 

Great breakfast! Would love to come back.

Stopped in before shopping. Sat at the bar had a couple of beers, lots of choice on beers. Ordered Rueben tools and a pretzel with beer cheese, tasty but a little pricy for what we received.
Nice atmosphere bartender wasn't too friendly. We read you get a 10 discount out in the mall, yet she didn't offer it and knew he was a veteran. It wasn't a big thing but she should have offered it.
This might be a fun place to have a few beers and appetizers but their food is just mediocre. The waitstaff was extremely helpful and friendly.
Are you kidding? The best biscuits and homemade jam in the South! Ask Martha Stewart!

best southern comfort food. So happy we stumbled across this place. Did not have a reservation and only waited 45 minutes. Server Joni was polite and friendly! Yummy fried green tomatoes. Yummy bloody Mary's. Felt like being at grandma's house.

Love that we now have an legitimate Bavarian restaurant in Nashville! Great atmosphere, awesome German food and live music! Join The Stein Club!
Only thing I'd say is that I wish it was not at the mall!

German food you say- here's your go to!
Great food and beer choices and really cool atmosphere.

I REALLY, REALLY wanted to love this place. I'm from California and was in town passing through. We stopped here, looked around at the shops, and had lunch. I loved the people, our server, and of course the biscuits! I ordered breakfast with eggs, potatoes, and sausage. I found the eggs to be fluffy, but that's about it. I was excited for the potatoes but whatever kind of sauce or cheese was in them really turned me off so I barely touched them. The sausage was okay and nothing special to me. Maybe I should have ordered something for lunch. I would try it again if I'm in town.

Wow! What an experience! To begin with, our server was PHENOMENAL! He was incredibly friendly and. Knowledgeable, after we felt like we ordered what seemed like the entire menu, we get our drinks. I had the watermelon moonshine drink and it was basically summer in a Mason jar, the most refreshing drink I have had in a long time.
Our food then comes out, the best part of the entire experience were the handmade biscuits (you can see the kitchen staff rolling them out through a kitchen window). I am pretty sure I have had dreams about these biscuits and the amazing butter and jam they served with. I intend on bringing every guest I have that comes to visit me in Nashville here.

It's Historic. We have been here 5 times in the past few years from Florida South FLA in the 305 and only could enjoy breakfast and 1 lunch 3 of the 5 visits. It's worth the wait for the first or second time but honestly 2 plus hours to get seated, well that's a little long and qualifies for a Tourist Trap.  Go to say you have been and then go antiquing up the road. The food is OK but the biscuits are Great, and it's fun to watch them being made. There is a lot to look at on the property. Play Corn hole with the grand kids. Go once and buy a Coffee Mug in the Gift Shop.

Second time visiting the Loveless and it is a truly fun place to visit. Plan to allow a lot of time to get there from Downtown Nashville. The reason for my rating has nothing to do with the service - our server Bama was attentive and pleasant and did a great job. I started with a Lynchburg Lemonade - very lemony - not enough "Lynchburg" but good. I ordered green beans, fried okra and fried chicken. The beans were traditional southern green beans cooked with ham and great. The fried okra was really good as well. The chicken, which is billed as one of their great menu items = way over cooked. I ordered dark meat which has to be really overcooked to dry out and it was really dried out. It was seasoned nicely however. Since I had decided on fried chicken earlier in the day, I was disappointed and hence the 3 star rating. I will say that we took home the left over biscuits and I had biscuit toast for my breakfast the next day which made up a little for the chicken!

While it's a little bit outside of Nashville this is absolutely worth the drive! The sign is perfect for a photo op so make sure to take one!
The inside looks like a quaint house so it's very warm & welcoming. We had an amazing server, he was so friendly!
I went with the French toast and it was delicious! 4-5 pieces so it was very filling! But let's be honest the star of the show was the biscuits! They are fluffy, fresh & hot to serve! Have them plain, have with butter or spread some jam! 
Great breakfast experience! Make sure to check out the store and market next door for cute souvenirs!

Though I've been here many times, today I brought my parents to Loveless Cafe for the first time! Today's visit owes us nothing & my parents are sold on all things Loveless! The food was AMAZING and the staff was absolutely incredible! If you've never had the corn or the turnip greens... they are a must! Everyone was so kind, especially Mr. Keith who took a moment out of his busy schedule to give us the history of Loveless Cafe! The Loveless experience is well worth the drive! You won't be disappointed!

What I enjoy the most at loveless is the peanut butter pie.  I often want to buy a piece take home but I know this would be bad so I don't.  The fried chicken and the biscuits are other gems but always save room for the pie.  To avoid the long wait get food to go and eat it on the picnic benches outside.

I had heard so much about the Loveless Cafe and have been wanting to try it since the first time I ever visited Nashville. It was definitely so much more than I was expecting!

The Loveless Cafe is a great little restaurant with some shops surrounding the property. It was pretty busy when we went on a Sunday night, but they gave us a little pager that worked throughout the property. The wait was 45 minutes, but the time went by quickly as we were able to look around and shop while we waited. We ended up finding some birthday presents for my future brother-in-law!

When we finally got to eat, the food was definitely worth the wait. I got the fried chicken fingers with mac & cheese and green beans. The chicken fingers were so big--probably about the size of two regular-sized ones. I definitely couldn't finish it in one sitting.

Our server was excellent! He was very friendly and more than willing to accommodate our extra take out order.

It's quite a drive from soon-to-be mother-in-law's house, but it was definitely worth the drive and worth the wait once we were there. I can't wait to go again!

Such an amazing place. If you are on the fence, STOP, jump down and drive to Loveless. I ate at many, many amazing places in Nashville but this one just stole my heart. 

First, they do get busy because they are AWESOME, but do not dismay. To keep you entertained while you are waiting there are plenty of stores and things to keep you busy plus I love that you can chat with the grill master who is making the delicious meats. 

Second, the food is amazing. I had the BBQ Eggs breakfast. So fabulous and sooo much BBQ. I couldn't make it half way through and I'm no slight eater. We had melt in your mouth biscuits and all the sweet treats of homemade jams and jellies. Our server even brought out fresh sorghum. 

Last but not least, the service was just lovely. Truly kind and helpful people who just want to make your visit fun, memorable and especially delicious. Definitely worth the trip!

We are from out of town and heard so many good things about The Loveless Cafe. It more than exceeded our expectations!  The food was amazing and all made from scratch. The biscuits and jam were outstanding. The chicken and waffles (something I've always wanted to try) were phenomenal.  The service was wonderful and the general manager took a genuine interest in our experience.  Overall, a superb experience. Make sure you go when you are in the area. You won't be disappointed!!

Arrived just after they opened for breakfast and was immediately seated with a plate of hot biscuits and jam. Food was excellent and service was very attentive.  Great way to start our morning drive down the Natchez Trace.

This place is magic! Southern home cooking at its finest.  Fried chicken, green beans and homemade biscuits to die for.  But the best was our server, Megan, a truly kind, lovely lady with manners and a great smile.

THANKSGIVING REVIEW ONLY: so im slowly ordering from every reputable place in town for thanksgiving. monell's was last year and fantastic. loveless was this year and a 4. nothing more
