turkey was MOIST. but they give you a few legs with bone so not sure if that makes up part of the 60oz of turkey you get. would obviously prefer to forgo the bone for meat.

sides were all stellar as one would expect. i love the restaurant.

i absolutely love their biscuits but hard to bring back to life in my opinion. i wish they would actually just give frozen raw dough. you get a dozen in an order but they give you 3 tiny plastic ramekins for all dozen which i thought was complete BS. however they will cheerfully remind you "you can buy more preserves at our store!" you're spending $120 on the basic package so i dont think it would kill them to throw in one more set to make it 6 ramekins. you could probably squeeze out 2 servings per ramekin, if you have big folks, then forget that.

THE PIE IS NOT HOMEMADE. they dont state it is anywhere but just wanted to point it out bc its $11. SKIP THE PIE or just order one of their handmade ones. i wish i caught this but honestly, from a marketer, i think its bad for their brand to be selling mass produced pies. to be honest the pumpkin pie was not that great. it was more of a mousse texture. we didn't think it was done but the crust was 100% golden brown.

i would absolutely consider ordering here again for thanksgiving but didn't stand out that far from monell's. both are amazing so its just two amazing places against each other. 

the gentlemen who helped me pick up my order and take it to my car was the highlight of the experience. (not the dude who chimes in to tell me to spend $7 for more preserves)

We visited the Loveless Cafe for breakfast. We arrived at 10:00 am on a Monday and had to wait 30 minutes. The line was even longer when we were leaving. We explored the shops on the premises while we waited. We were given biscuits and jam upon being seated. The biscuits were light, fluffy, and delicious. They are small which we liked because it made it easier to try all three of the jams. Each one was great. We both ordered the fried chicken and eggs with homefries. The eggs were good. Nothing spectacular but still good. The homefries were just the basic previously forzen homefries but the fried chicken was very very good. The coating had great flavor, the chicken remained moist, and the portion sizes were large. The service was excellent. Our coffee was refilled regularly. We never reached the bottom of our cup.

The biscuit is aren't like classic southern biscuits I'm used to (although those are good in their own right). They're like little heavenly pillows of joy. I was expecting a touristy place so my expectations were low, but the food was just good, southern, homey, a little heart warming really. The service was the same.

What a tourist trap! It is not worth the wait. The only thing good was the biscuits. Everything else is fair at best. I was disappointed in the chicken fried steak and the gravy was plain which reminded me of Dennys. My friend's chicken was dry. You should go to Slow Burn Hot Chicken or The Country Boy in Franklin for some good Southern food that tastes like the region.

So being a German in the US, I admit that I am extremely critical of German food. I am of the belief that if I can cook it better at home, I've wasted my money. 

So let me start by saying that they did a decent job recreating the Hofbräuhaus, from Munich. This alone made me feel a little closer to "home". I opted for something that I don't make at home because I can either not get the ingredients or it's too much work. Meterwurst has always been a favorite of mine from home but not something that is easy to come by. It was so delicious! 

My husband had Jägerschnitzel - which I do make at home, so of course I had to sample his... I could tell the gravy was instant (but it is a restaurant), but it was good. I still make this dish better at home, but my opinion is biased.  As for my Meterwurst - I loved it!!!

I had a Colabier (coke and beer - don't hate till you try it), and my husband had some cocktail they tried to sell as German, but the only thing German was the gummies. Mine was GREAT! He had an Apfelkorn and I had a Kleiner Feigling to end the meal. 

Let me close this review by saying I will be back. I left feeling homesick and wanting more. I think that says it all.

I have nothing but love for Loveless Cafe. It's one of the few restaurants in the world I would wait over an hour for, but the wait was oh so worth it. I ordered the Southern Omelet with sausage (made and smoked in house). The omelet was huge and overflowing with cheese, peppers and onions. The sausage was very flavorful but not too salty with a bit of a spicy kick. The eggs were fluffy and did a great job of encasing the bulk of the filling. The side of hashbrown casserole was delicious -- creamy with lots of sour cream and cheese mixed in.

Of course, the biscuits were amazing. The preserves on the side were good, but I'm so glad I asked for some honey -- they elevated the biscuits even to an even more supreme level than I ever thought possible.

As long as our wait was, the shops around the cafe made the time fly by. The complimentary lemonade and coffee were great as well.

Everyone should go to Loveless Cafe at least once -- it's worth the drive and time.
Great atmosphere and bar. Love the 50's diner look. The staff is friendly and helpful.  I'll be back for sure.

Good wine selection, and enjoyed a show there last year. Gotta say it was a little weird being at a concert and eating but was lots of fun. Being front row is crazy good, actually touching the stage the whole time.

Endless homemade biscuits? What's not to love? Gets super busy. Now taking reservations on weekdays! Otherwise I highly suggest going between meal times. We tried at 11:30 on a weekend and were told it was a 2 hour wait for 4 people. Left and came back around 4:30 and only had to wait 30 mins. Totally worth it!

I had a wonderful experience at Loveless as a solo diner. The employees were friendly and efficient. The biscuits were divine. The CHICKEN was so freaking crispy and flavorful...I can't even. I had prince's hot chicken the day before, which was ok...but if you have the chance to eat this. Choose this! Broccoli and rice casserole was so comforting I wanted to curl up with it on a couch. Well with the drive out of the city. Perfect when coupled with a tour of Belle Meade!

We went here while travelling thru Tennessee. When we got here it was like travelling back to the 1950's. Walking up to the restaurant they had several seating areas. We were able to put our name down and we did not wait too long.

The dining room is old school and feels more like a home then a business. Our waitress was very friendly and was able to provide some suggestions considering it was our first time visiting.

We ordered the fried chicken and smoked pork chops. Both were excellent and we enjoyed two baskets of biscuits.

Overall we really enjoyed our meal and spent a little extra time walking around the historic property.

Worst German food ever. Wow. Left enough of an impression we had to write a review.

Spaetzle is limp, greasy and tasteless. Gravies are run of the mill, out of a can quality. Lacking in flavor, authenticity and value the owners should take stick in taking advmathe of the tourists. I mean $20 for a chicken schnitzel that is flavorless, small and not authentic. Even if you are a starving tourist, just pass this this restaurant. For this price go to the equally over priced aquarium restaurant but at least there uses higher quality ingredients.

Three positives, nice staff, a solid german and jaeger beer selection. And the chef who is on his game in that he actually came out to speak to us about our experience. If ownership goes back to its roots of a "german" experience and stopped sourcing low-grade ingredients they would easily hit the ball out of the park since they have one of the hardest things in the service industry under control -- good employees.

1. Grumpy bouncer sets your experience off to a bad start immediately.
2. Cheeseburger came out very dry and simply bad tasting. McDonalds or Wendy's has more flavor in their 99 cent hamburgers.
3. Same goes for the patty melt but add soggy bread.
4. Picture of the Mac and cheese attached in which the flavor was below average and the quantity was laughable. About 12-15 pieces of macaroni.

Bottom line: you will never go here for the food, maybe they have good music but eat somewhere else first.
Food and beer are great! The service at the bar not so much! I felt like we were bother them.

Love this place! Eaten here about 3-4 times and have never been disappointed. The schnitzel is incredible as are the pretzels and desserts! Great environment and lovely staff, whom speak with a german accent no matter the color tone of their skin A deffinate must for ppl who like food
Amazing food and customer service. Great atmosphere for night out with friends! Definitely recommend it!

My first attempt to eat here was on a Saturday, it was a cool atmosphere as it was a nice day and loads of people were sitting on the decks - playing cornhole or catch! But this made for a 2 hour wait! I decided to come back Monday since I was still in town.

Monday was a normal 30min wait - which you can easily wait by visiting their 2 Loveless Stores!

I wanted to try the biscuits, chicken, and pulled pork due to what I read on yelp - the waitress suggested the sampler platter - my 2 sides were creamed corn and potato casserole. 

They were not joking about how good the biscuits are! Amazing! Exp w the sausage grav. The jams were ok. The pulled pork I'd give a 8/10 - generous portions and had a great smokey flavor! I will say I was a little disappointed in the fried chicken as I don't add salt to very much but added it to the chicken - it was very crispy and moist though! The creamed corn and potato casserole were excellent too! Highly recommend those sides!

Great history, food and a very attentive nice staff - I recommend eating here!!
A staple in the Nashville area that every out of towner should experience! Great atmosphere and terrific Southern food!

After so many had told me to go check this "Nashville staple restaurant" out, I decided it would be a great opportunity to take my mother who was visiting from out of town. I knew this was a popular tourist attraction, so I wasn't surprised when we arrived at 9:20 there was already an hour+ wait. 

They have a few stores surrounding the cafe and some sitting areas and cornhole games. 

We waited around an hour and a half and then waited another 10 minutes to be greeted. Our server, Ethan/Evan, never introduced himself, never gave us a welcome, all he said is "what do you want to drink?" That was it. We thought that was a little weird, I guess we were expecting a little more from a restaurant that is so highly raved about. It took about 15 more minutes to get our waters and other beverages. We then ordered an appetizer and went ahead and ordered our food, again very little interaction with our server. They have little mazes and word searches on the tables (presumably for children) but thank goodness they had these to distract us from the almost hour wait for our food. The appetizer came out the same time as the rest of our food, always disappointing. Someone else delivered our food, not the server. But the server, NEVER ONCE asked how our food was, did everything come out okay?, can I get you a refill?, nothing. He brought over a few napkins. We asked for more biscuits and he told us when more came out he would bring them, he did this but again never saying anything to check on us. 

My mom ordered the Santa Fe Omelette, she was left very disappointed. It has very little flavor and had way too many onions stuffed inside. 
I had the biscuit platter as "an appetizer", the pimento cheese and fried tomato was my favorite! The others were good, but nothing I would drive another 45 minutes too again. 
I got the breakfast bowl and I was very pleased with my bowl, delicious, warm, plenty of food, great flavor. 

Overall, the loveless cafe was greatly overrated in my opinion and we were left very underwhelmed. I would not recommend this to people coming to Nashville, unless you are looking to spend your entire morning/afternoon for decent/good food with poor service. Disappointing experience, such a shame for what I had heard about the place. (Side note: I was a server for 8 years so I understand when a server is busy and overwhelmed, but this was not the case) 
I post this so that Loveless Cafe can help rectify the issue with their employees and remind them that service is key to a successful business, and that hopefully in the future no one else has the same experience.

I first visited this cafe about 10 years ago.  I had been thinking about it and wanted to return to it.  G and I decided to meet here for dinner one Friday night.  It's about halfway between his residence and Knoxville and mine in Memphis.  I got there, and it was about a 45 minute wait, which was fortunate, because he was 45 minutes late.  



The cafe started in 1951 with the Loveless family basically selling fried chicken and biscuits out of their house.  



They have a BBQ pit, so they obviously smoke their own meat.  



It used to also be a motel.  However, the motel quit operative about 20 years ago.  The old motel parts are used for retail.  You can buy plenty of souvenirs, some edible and some wearable.  



They start you off with biscuits and their famous jams.  The biscuits were great.  They also serve breakfast all day.  I had to restrain myself from eating too many before my meal.  



They have some drinks.  I had a whiskey and water.  One friend ordered a shot of moonshine.  It came in a cute mason jar cup.  He said it was "strong."  



I love combination plates, so that's what I got.  With as much food as I got, it was worth the price.  I think it was the most expensive item on the menu at $17.55.  The Southern Sampler Platter comes with your choice of three meats (Fried Chicken, Catfish, Country Ham, Meatloaf or Pork Barbeque) and two sides.  I chose the fried chicken, because that was one of their original items.  I also got the country ham, because it is proclaimed on their neon sign outside.  And finally, I got the pork barbecue since I saw the BBQ pit outside.  All the meat was just plain perfect.  The pork was on a cornbread pancake.  



I also got to choose two sides.  They have tons of choices.  I ended up getting the greens and the mac n' cheese.  Both were good and typically country.  I would have liked to try the fried okra, but I already had too much food.  



For my meat, I did't choose the meatloaf, because I knew G would order it.  he did, and it was good.  It was covered with a tangy tomato sauce.  He got the vegetable of the day, which was squash.  It was surprisingly good, too.  I wasn't tempted by it when I heard it was the special, but I was jealous when I tasted it.  



They have desserts, but there's no way someone could eat anyway after eating here! 

The other intriguing thing on their menu is their family style supper for groups of 4 or more.  It's all you can eat for $17.55 a person.  The table has to agree upon two meats and three veggies.  It also includes a regular drink.  

It is so good that it would be worth a three hour drive.  Seriously.

This place is kind of awesome, if you're in the mood for the ambiance it provides.  Big Shotz is located just off of Broadway, the touristy bar strip in Nashville.  Big Shotz is definitely a dive bar with live music, cheap drinks, and a grubby feel.  If that's what you're looking for, Big Shotz delivers.

When you first enter Big Shotz, be prepared for some cigarette smoke.  The interior is dark and looks pretty worn out.  Seating consists mainly of high-tops with some of the most beaten up stools I have ever seen in a bar.  These tables overlook two stages:  The back features a large stage and video projection screen, while the front has a smaller stage by the large doors and windows that open onto the street.

I visited on a Saturday afternoon and there was a small crowd listening to a duo play music.  Once inside, we discovered that the drinks were dirt cheap!  Beers were $2 for draft and $3 for bottles.  Shots were similarly inexpensive, though none of our group had the nerve to try the infamous double-decker $5 shots at 2:00 PM.  The bartenders were nice.  

Overall, this seems like a great place to kill some time if you are looking for a dive bar with ultra-cheap drinks.  I can't stress how inexpensive this place is compared to the competition around it.  It's a little dirty, but some of that is by design (I.e. the terrible barstools) in the so-bad-it's-good sense.  This is probably a great place to get hammered at night, too.

This is a great tourist spot! We love getting little souvenirs from their shops before or after we eat. We pretty much always get the chicken fried chicken, and the only one time it was undercooked, we were given replacements (cooked perfectly) and sent home with free dessert. It's a super friendly and welcoming environment and the servers are always warm and kind! The biscuits are to die for and we loooove the sides -- especially the creamed corn and fried green tomatoes.

Big Rig Blunder
We recently drove the Natchez Trace from Mississippi and I wanted to take my husband to Loveless Cafe. The only problem was that we were in a motorhome and were towing. I emailed ahead of time to ask if they had parking for a large rig and were assured that they did. Unfortunately when we got there the signage was unclear (and the road is very busy) so we ended up turning down the next street which had no outlet and we had to back up and turn around. When we got back out to the road we spied a dirt road across the highway and thought we could pull into that to get turned around. NO! It was someone's driveway and it was a dead end. Now we were stuck. Upon seeing our dilemma the operations manager ran across the street, hugged the very concerned property owner (not the first time this has happened apparently) and helped us to get turned around and into a back lot behind the gas station where there is lots more parking that you can't see from the street. We were assured that they were in the process of revamping their signage.
Once we got inside we found out it was 1 1/2 wait!!! I dug in my heels and told my husband that we were not going through all of that only to leave but after waiting 20 minutes I realized I was starving and not going to make it so I ordered food to go ONLINE (they have an awesome website for placing your order to go) and picked it up 20 minutes later and ate it in the motorhome. The Fried Chicken was just as I remembered it and my husband loved his brisket. 
The moral of the story: If the wait is too long (which it often is) go online to order and eat at one of their shady picnic benches.

This is our first visit to the Nashville location, but we have visit the City Winery in both Chicago and Atlanta.   

The concert we attended was upstairs in the lounge area instead of the main stage. It was a beautiful atmosphere, beautiful acoustics, and the food was delightful!!! You have to visit if you are Nashville!!

Tourist trap. Chicken was dry and had no seasoning or salt. Bbq was ehh. Chicken fried chicken was literally burned so bad we had to send it back and the gravy tasted like the jarred gravy you buy at the store for emergencies. The service was prompt but not friendly. Just cold. Felt no southern charm at all. 14.00 for a fried chicken drum and wing..mashed potatoes and a bowl of fried okra. Could have had the same meal at cracker barrel for 8.99 and had better biscuits and gravy.

We went to breakfast here on a Friday morning around 9 so we were able to avoid any major waits. We waited about 10 minutes for a table, which is not bad at all. I once tried to go for lunch and it was 1.5 hours (more common, from what I hear). The breakfast food was very yummy. I did love the biscuits and the jellies that they had. The hashbrown casserole that is raved about was also good. Overall, it was yummy food, but I am eager to try their lunch/dinner options. Good service, fun atmosphere. Worth the trip as a "bucket list" item!

Great brunch with dear pals. The crew at City Winery make every meal an event. Isaac took great care of us and we enjoyed his attentive hospitality.

Be sure to order the mimosa tray! It absolutely makes everything special. My friends and I really brunch - the food was perfect.

So delicious! The service was fantastic and the food was too. They ran out of some items but what they did have was sooo worth it. 

Definitely great home cooking eats!

Make sure you make a reservation!
Amazing dining experience as usual at loveless!!! Great food and drinks, I had the fried chicken , Mac and cheese and corn.
Food was good- I wished  it would have been served hotter but flavors were great - the Rouladen were dry :(

We loved the food, drink, music, and atmosphere. Our waiter was pleasant but extremely slow. We had show tickets, budgeted 90 minutes only to find ourselves 70 minutes into our evening and just getting our meals. Getting our bill was another endeavor. So we did feel rushed to eat and leave. Plan double your time.

Fun vibes, service is outstanding, biscuits were great. They serve breakfast all day and in hindsight, I should have taken advantage of that. The food on the lunch menu had too much gravy and cream sauce for my pallet.

Some true stick-to-your-ribs good Southern comfort food. We came here on our recent trip to Nashville after hearing rave reviews. In fact, it was the only must-do activity from our friend who had been here once before. We came during the early evening on Saturday and there was approximately a 40 minute wait. In the meantime, there were the little series of shops that we could browse through in the surrounding buildings.

Once seated, our waiter was super friendly. He promptly brought over their famous biscuits and preserves. While in the south, I've quite enjoyed my biscuits savory-style but these preserves tasted very fresh. They kept us occupied for a while until we decided on what to order. The soup of the day was chicken pot pie, which I couldn't turn down even though I was also anxious to try so many other things. Thus, my friend and I ordered the country sampler with fried chicken, country ham, and pulled pork. We opted for obvious sides of mac and cheese and mashed potatoes. The fried chicken drumsticks were delicious and the sides definitely hit the spot. The pulled pork was not my favorite though.

Someone else ordered the meatloaf platter with sweet potato and hashbrown casserole sides. He claimed the hashbrown casserole was the best he's had. Our other friend got the turkey platter with mashed potatoes and mac and cheese, which was good too. It was definitely worth the hype of classic down home southern cooking.

Well spent afternoon!
Laura, our sommelier and tour guide had so much information! 
Our visit coincided with their receipt of this year's grapes shipment, and so we saw a pivotal moment the very beginning of the fermentation process. 
Also, we tasted last year's Sauvignon Blanc, a Pinot Noir, and a Cabernet Sauvignon. 
We'd visited for music performances before, and it's always been a pleasure, but this time seeing behind the scenes confirmed it for us.  Classy operation.

I think Loveless is one of those one and done places. Definitely a must for tourists and locals alike. I stopped in for the first time this year after moving away from Nashville for 2+ years. Funny thing- Loveless was only 15 minutes from my former apartment. Anyway, we can around 10am and had about an 1 hour wait. This gave us plenty of time to explore the little (very small amount) of shops in the area. Nothing exciting, just biscuit mix and southern kitschy stuff. Make sure you put in your name for wait before you do this! 

When you are seated, you get a whole plate of biscuits and jam *with free refills. The biscuits are good but I still think biscuit love is better. The food portions are very reasonably priced and absolutely HUGE. The chicken is good- nothing exciting but like I said HUGE for a very reasonable price. We were able to split a platter just fine. Overall, its a cute, fun, historical place.

We were here a few weeks ago and have to admit that it was better than we expected.  We are German, so it's hard to come close to to the real thing when we're out, but since my parents live in a place that doesn't have as many German restaurants as we would like, I brought them here to try it.

The food was very good - filling, and although not exactly authentic, still really flavorful.  I had their version of French onion soup, some schnitzel and then a potato dumpling and all were very good.  The beer was really good and the atmosphere was very fun and enjoyable, with a duo (a couple, I think) who played while everyone ate.  

It was very convivial and I would highly recommend it, especially if you have a group, as you can sit at large long tables and share conversation easily.

A legend, and for good reason! I would go back here again for the warm, fluffy, buttery, perfect homemade biscuits alone. I wish I had taken a picture (not that it would have done them justice), but before I could remember to take out my phone I had already eaten all of the biscuits! Seriously, they're addictive and they will just keep bringing them to you. The homemade jams were also wonderful. 

But besides the biscuits, we also ate other things for breakfast. I had a half order of country ham with red-eye gravy and two eggs, which was plenty. Ham was nice and salty and the gravy wasn't like I was expecting. Being a Northerner, I was thinking Thanksgiving dinner but it was more like a thin sauce. For my side I had the best cup of grits I've ever had---definitely order this. My husband had the breakfast steak with a hashbrown casserole, which he had never had before and liked a lot. Prices are a bit on the higher side compared to similar types of restaurants, but they're justified since the food is so high quality. 

Around 9:30 AM, we only had a brief ten minute wait. Our waitress was super friendly, service was quick, and we were full until dinner. And I'm still thinking about those biscuits...

This place is highly overrated. The wait of an hour and a half led us to believe this place is going to be good. It was mediocre at best. My mother has chicken fried chicken that was overcooked, it was dry and crunchy. She enjoyed her fried okra. My aunt and I had country fried steak which apparently is the only menu item that is frozen. Huge disappointment. The mashed potatoes were good as well as the green beans. The biscuits with the preserves were good as well.

This place is terrible. I'm sitting in here right now and the service is horrible. I've been trying to get my servers attention for 10 minutes. He dropped the drinks off with no straws. On top of that, we ordered over 10 minutes ago and still haven't gotten any biscuits. I have tried stopping several other employees to get help but everyone seems incredibly busy, even though there are plenty of open tables in the restaurant. I won't be coming back here.

After a second trip here, I'm convinced my initial rating was too low. The biscuits and peach preserves were just as delicious as my first time here, followed by the exceptional cheesy hashbrowns... so good! I went a different route, and tried the french toast, and I was not disappointed! Cinnamon and sweet just the way I like it!

If your in the area, be sure you make the Loveless Cafe one of your stops !
You made need resets, so get that done !
Tim was our waiter and he could not have been any better!!
Fresh, hot biscuits with homemade peach, strawberry and blackberry jelly are delivered to your table as soon as you are seated .
You really can just stop there!!
Be sure and ask for some sorghum syrup too.
WOW
WOW
WOW
Very delicious!!
We did order, and this is what we tried:

Fried Chicken, cream corn & fried okra 

Fried fish, turnip greens & okra

Meatloaf with garlic cheese mashed potatoes 

It was all so good. To be honest, we were full from the biscuits.

They also have fresh homemade pies .
We had to try ! Lol
Key lime pie and also banana pudding!!!
You can't go wrong, just do it. 

When in Nashville, make that short trip to the Loveless Cafe!!
Go get Full
Great wine and atmosphere. Service was excellent, food was ok.  I will go back for wine and small plates.
Great brunch! Can't wait to go back! Had the Poke Bowl, Little Gem Salad...fabulous! Great service staff, never a bad time!

Wow!  Southern home cooking at its best!  I go to Nashville once a year and this is the best part of the trip.  The food and service are amazing and the cool little shops are a must to check out.  Also, it is right next to the best bike trail in the Midwest...the Natchez Trace Parkway.

Wow oh wow. AMAZING AYCE southern breakfast. The biscuits here are a must!!! The restaurant is on a huge plot of land, so lots of open space also to just hang out / roam around after your meal. There's also a gift shop where you can buy their biscuit mix.

Ok... at the suggestion of many, I finally made a trip (out of my way) to have a late breakfast here.  Yes, the biscuits are good, but not amazing.  Most breakfast platters are over $10 (a breakfast sandwich can be had for under $10) and you will get way more food that you could really want or need.

They have expanded into the retail game by operating a gift shop and a few other stores on site (former inn rooms).  Nothing that I just had to have, so I left without buying anything.  

It not overly touristy here, but getting really close to that level.  I will say the food is good but come with an empty stomach to get your moneys worth.

Must go. My friend and i got there when the doors opened sunday morning and were in and out within 30 minutes. (wait is usually around 1hr 30 at peak times) Complementary biscuits & their homemade jam are brought to your table and they are phenomenal- best i've ever had, especially paired with the blackberry jam. I got chicken, eggs, cheesy grits and bacon. All were very good except I do think the bacon could have been a tad crispier but I was so full I didn't really care. Chicken is cooked perfectly with crispy crust. If you love home cooked food you must go here.

When my fiancé and I had just started dating I was driving from Tulsa OK to Dickson TN nearly every other weekend to visit him. He brought me here one morning for breakfast/brunch and I'll forever remember it. 
I had the fried chicken and it was sooooo good. The biscuits they serve before hand w their jams are omg good! I do remember that the man had beans w some sort of chow chow on them and wow they were fantastic. 
The service was great too! 
One thing I also remember was that the wait was 1 1/2 hrs... but we didn't mind bc they have shopping all around and we could stare at each other!
Best southern food I've ever had definitely get refills on the biscuits service was lovely fast and felt like home. Some of the best fried chicken!
Biscuits and jams were great. Cheesy grits were the best I've ever had. Fried okra was perfect. The blackberry preserves are great so I had to buy some to take home.

Do yourself a favor and make sure you top here for breakfast, lunch, or dinner or all three.  To many amazing items to list.  So individually great and the opposite of all chains.  Has the amount of ratings and scores for a reason.  Loved it.

Once you have been served and eaten here at Loveless, you realize why there is a line out the door.   Phenomenal staff / service and the food is off the charts.    Loveless is so good, that I actually requested them to cater our wedding dinner for friends and family.   Huge hit.    Thank you Loveless!
Wonderful wonderful wonderful.  The southern corn was amazing.  Wish I had bought the peach jam when I there.  Get a chance buy some.

This has been my favorite grub spot since moving to Nashville. I had the watermelon ribs and they were to die for! I've eaten my fair share of ribs and these were some of the best I've ever had. Their desert was very good as well. 

Per the other comments, yes the wait time can be long, but once you try their food you'll understand why folks are lined up.

This is our second trip here. We stop to purchase biscuit mix. It is the best ever and easy to make. 
This trip we ate lunch. We both had breakfast fare including country ham. The food was great and the service was even better. 
Long wait times to get into the restaurant but they have plenty of shopping to help you while away the time and lighten your wallet.

I have been to plenty of shows at City Winery--Black Violin, Amel Larrieux, Les Nubians.  I love the diverse offerings of shows and the venue is quite impressive.  I have sat in the balcony...on the floor level...and close to the downstairs bar area in the concert room.  Let me tell you that there are no bad seats.  I recently went to the Wine Fest and it was very fun enjoying every area in the City Winery and the vast selection of wines.  The meals are always good.  I have had the blended burger project burger, which was blended with meat and mushrooms.  Delectable!  Not sure if they still have it as I believe it was a limited time menu item.  I have also had the duck flatbread which also is  very, very delicious (so much so that it is something that I have ordered on multiple visits to City Winery). 

Some times the service can be a little slow especially for packed show, but usually my experience with the service of City Winery has been positive.  One impressive experience that stood out in my mind was during Wine Fest.  Someone in my party spilled some wine and the first employee to walk by was the executive chef.  I would think that he would probably go in the back and tell someone to clean it up.  However, he put up a caution sign and came back and cleaned it up himself.  He even entertained our wine-fueled banter about how much we love the food and answered some of our questions.  For someone as busy as a top chef must be, I was impressed with the pride he takes in the restaurant (from the food to the floors) and making sure that everything is running smoothly and enjoyable for the guests.  

So overall, City Winery Nashville keep bringing great shows and doing a wonderful job.  Also, I am sure it is a great undertaking, but if Wine Fest could be offered every season, I would be a happy girl!

Man we were horrible road trippers this summed. Haha! We were always finding places to visit. We needed a place to eat and my husband found Loveless Cafe. He mentioned that it had great reviews. I completely understand the great reviews. We had to wait 1.5 hours for our table, but it was worth it. We shopped around at the stores they had. Of course I had to buy some biscuit mix. I plan on making them one Sunday morning so we can remember the good time we had here. There were some games outside to play, to help take away the feeling of being bored. Once we were seated we were able to take all the food and biscuits. Everything was amazing! The kids portions were big, which is great for my kiddos who eat like adults but, are old enough to benefit from prices on the kids menu. Ok, back to the biscuits, they melt in your mouth. We plan to return when we have more time to explore. If you have time to go here and are on a road trip, DO IT! It was worth setting us back 3.5 hours

This place was excellent it is a little bit of drive but nothing too crazy maybe 15 mins outside of city. The biscuits really are the best I ever had and the service was family friendly. Cannot recommend any more to check it out.
Incredible biscuits, country ham and sausage gravy! The jams were really nice too. It was neat and clean and the service was good. It's definitely worth your time.

Pretty cool area.  Bar smelled like piss...Literally.  Bathroom smelled like puke pie.  There were 2 other people there and the bartenders were not friendly at all.  You'd think that a bar with no customers would try a bit harder.  Walked in and stayed for 1 drink to be polite and the bartender wouldn't close out our tab until we tipped her first.. So yeah..... good work, guys...

Also,  I don't rate places low regularly if you look at all of my other reviews...
Bartenders are terrible. Very rude when you ask what's in a shot. The male bartender tried to fight the group I was with (which we are all bartenders)- he gave us koolaid as a shot. Do not go here.

Great food and drink, in a friendly and lively environment! The giant pretzel was fantastic, especially dipped in the relish or cheese. I've never had anything like it before, but the kasepatzle was amazing. The noodles were unique and the dish had a rich flavor and was very filling. The Munich Dunkel lager was refreshing as well.

Don't let the reviews fool you or think they're fake, the biscuits and jam really ARE that amazing. We love the Loveless Cafe. The food is top notch and the service is great. We love the gift shop and market too. Such a fun place to come. But if you plan to come, be sure to make reservations at least a day in advance. If you come as a walk in, good luck. It's always packed and backed up, no matter the time of day. But, it's well worth the visit!

The staff was throughly trained, but the food needs to be upgraded  I had the sautéed chicken, but they need to use better product.  Chicken was tough.  Suggest they upgrade to organic and/or brine it before cooking.  The ravioli was buried under mozzarella cheese and heavy sauce.  Too much mozzarella and too much sauce.

My boyfriend and I are only in Nashville for five nights and we've gone twice already. I want to go a third time lol. The food is so amazing and really is the definition of southern comfort. I've never had food so tasty before. If I could give it ten stars I would. 

The staff is so insanely nice and works very hard to get you to a table if there is a wait. The longest we waited was five minutes. The place is very clean and the wait staff is very on top of things. 

The location is very nice and the crowd that eats there is mainly families so it's a very comforting place. It's also wheel chair and stroller accessible! 

If you're considering going here, I cannot stress this enough. Do yourself a favor and go!!!

If you love a good, no a great biscuit, then look no further. Nestled deep in the hills of Nashville is this throw back to simpler times. What was once a family run hotel and cafe is now a delightful dining and shopping destination. From the outside of the Restaurant you would think it would be a long wait but walking in the doors you realize to how spacious it truly is. Did server was super friendly and welcoming. When I asked for a kids menu she was more than happy to oblige. She actually recommended it since their portions were so huge! Mom chose the chicken fried steak while I picked the kids catfish with baked beans. While waiting for our order our server brought out a plate of delightful tiny biscuits with a trio of fresh made jams. 
Everything was delicious! As we were walking out I made a u-turn back to get a mini coconut cream pie for later. Have to say i was not disappointed! Just wish I would have had a few more biscuits!
Wife and I stopped by for brunch Wednesday and were blown away. Service and food were great.

This place has great biscuits and jam! The hash brown casserole is amazing too! I think there's a lot of hype for this place, they can upgrade their menu a bit. Had the BLT with fried green tomatoes and it was plain, the bread was blah too.

This place is the bomb! My first time in the Nashville area and my daughter recommended it since her in laws are regulars. Omg, the biscuits were out of this world. Hands down the best country breakfast I have ever had in my life. I dream of the Applewood smoked bacon and grits and biscuits with blackberry jam. The eggs were so fresh. What a cute place! The gift shop was so adorable, I picked up a few gifts to take back home to Denver. Until next time, when we meet again.

This place is awesome...  best food?? Probably not the  "best," but pretty solid. The atmosphere is really cool...   Yeah yeah, I know it's hokie but it's still fun. I'm giving this place a high rating because of the total package and not just the food. Like I said, the food is good and they have some cool items like the big pretzels and the Speatlze (sp?).  Of course it's touristy....and that's perfectly fine unless you're holding an American German food chain restaurant to authentic German standards?? Honestly, I haven't been to Germany, and I'm sure it's not super accurate. But to hell with it, this place is fun!  do it!

Bury me in these biscuits! Yes Loveless Cafe may be a bit out of the way, but it is worth the pilgrimage as it is straight up a religious experience. During my first visit in 2014 my phone rang and my Rihanna "We Found Love" ringtone was blasting. My friends and I decided that "we found biscuits in a loveless place" were more appropriate lyrics (and subsequent Instagram caption, you're welcome). 

Expect to wait at least 45 minutes for a table on the weekend but take that time to venture around the property and shop around the marketplace. A little game of corn hole can help you pass the time until you get to indulge in some delicious food. Their dinner is also amazing -- we came for a team bonding meal and it was the perfect spot to soak up some southern hospitality. They also offer some limited reservations via Open Table which I didn't know until more recently. BONUS: you get a free piece of their scrumptious pie on your birthday!

This review is just for the restaurant part of City Winery. I didn't go see a show there, since I'm under 40, and their lineup makes me depressed just looking at it. 

Unfortunately their food made me even more depressed. The menu (like the music lineup) is straight out of the '90s: pretend fancy and bland, dating back to a time when people were probably just easier to impress. I'm vegan and only went to eat there because they had a promising-sounding vegan entree listed on their online menu, but our waitress explained that they took it off since nobody was ordering it. So I ended up paying $17 for a slimy portobello mushroom with a bit of couscous on the side.

I'm not against paying $17 for an entree when it's good. But there are much better restaurants in Nashville to spend your money at, and after picking up my car from valet (which you have to pay $7 for, by the way) I wished I had gone to one of them.

P.S.: Don't waste your time writing to management. They won't write you back.

P.P.S.: The Black Crowes? LOL.

Back home in Tallahassee, FL, we don't have any authentic German restaurants. So when my Mom and I saw the Bavarian Bierhaus restaurant while shopping at the Opry Mall, we decided to dine in. When you walk in, you are greeted by the sound of the live band playing Bavarian music. You immediately notice the staff wearing authentic outfits and the open beer-garden design of the restaurant. I was thrilled to see the menu and to enjoy their food. 

Boy, was it delicious! We split the Bierhaus Wurstteller, a plate containing 3 links of different bratwurst sausage, red cabbage, sauerkraut and whipped mashed potatoes. The food was just amazing. The bratwurst had so much flavor and the sides were a perfect pair. Our visit made us really wish we had one back home. When back in Nashville, I will be sure to stop in again!

Went for the soft opening, newly renovated with the appearance looking like an adult only Steak 'n Shake!  Love it.  Bartenders were awesome as always seeing a few familiar faces from their other business Hemingway's I believe grand opening is in couple weeks check it out !

I don't know exactly what it is about this place but I'm a huge fan. I suspect it's because of how much it reminds me of Biergarten at Epcot.

Be warned, this place is loud, by design. It's the only thing that I really consider a drawback. It wouldn't be the same if it wasn't, but keep that in mind. You aren't coming here for a quiet meal.

For starters I ordered the Spaten München Munich Hell based on the waitress telling me this was the most popular. Google would seem to tell me it's just an average German Beer, which is probably true, but I liked it. 

For appetizers we had the Pretzel with the Sweet Mustard. This thing is huge and was easily shared by two.

Dinner was München Weisswürste which is two sausage and ANOTHER Pretzel. (We had pretzels for days after this).

The food and beer were great and I look forward to coming back.

Where to begin?  This place is pretty cool as well as VERY loud.  It's connected to a large shopping mall, so our expectations weren't much.

They were B-U-S-Y when we were there.  Our server was stretched extremely thin.  Our drinks ran out.  He disappeared for long periods of time due to having to take care of so many other people.  But the main reason I'm giving them only three stars is because our food was forgotten.  Some other lady brought it out with an apology.  When our server finally did come back around, he seemed surprised we had received it.  It was cold.  Tasty, but you could tell it had been sitting up in the window for quite some time before it was brought out to us.  

Our fear was that had we complained, it would have taken yet another eternity to receive the remade portion of food.  It just wasn't worth it.

This place is neat.  It's touristy.  It just fell short for us,

Hear me out. 
Loveless cafe has some of the best bbq in Nashville. 
I know I know. 
I've read all the reviews too. Bbq is everywhere. They all say it's the best. But it's all so generic. There's just something about loveless cafes bbq that just keeps us coming back for more. Waiting up to 3 hours for it! Call us crazy. Or try it for yourselves.

Amazing amazing amazing. The wait is worth it, plus there's cool shops and corn hole to kill the time. Biscuits and jams are incredible. Had the pulled pork w/ creamed corn and Cole slaw and it was all great. It was so good we went back a week later and took the in-laws. This time I had the chicken fingers and they were just as good as the pork. If you're in town and can afford a few hours for some good southern food, this is definitely worth stopping by.

The Loveless Cafe did a fantastic job hosting our large family (32 people). We had a wonderful experience. The staff was friendly, courteous, and incredibly efficient. They took our order quickly, had a very short turnaround, and checked back frequently. Compliments to the kitchen staff as well, the food was excellent! Everyone enjoyed their meals. The biscuits are some of the best I've ever had. We were just about ready to order desert when a severe thunderstorm knocked out the power. The staff handled that well too. Quickly split the check and processed all of the individual payments. If anyone in our family are ever in the Nashville area again, we will be sure to return!

Great day for a meal.  I had the Catfish plate.  Four pieces of catfish with a couple hush puppies.  Then for my two sides I had their amazing sweet cream of corn and hash row. Casserole.  You also cannot forget their amazing biscuits as well.  I had a few with a mixer of butter and sorghum, yummy!!!   Washed it down with their freshly brewed sweet ice tea.  I also had a cup of their country white gravy for my catfish!!!!

This was some good country eaten today!!!!

I was so excited to try this place out. After living in Germany for 3 years, we were hopeful to find some familiar foods there. The portions were extremely small especially the schnitzel (husbands order)which is usually the size of a large plate, it was more of a kids size . So that made the high priced plate pretty lame. It was also the most greasy schnitzel I've ever had. 
My mom and I shared the roast and it was served with mashed potatoes that were very awful. To top it off, my mom and I got very sick after our meal!!!! 
Then there's the Kasespaetzle which was just okay. They topped it with dried French onion which honestly was what made it good. 

On a good note, the live music is always great! I might return for a beer and atmosphere, but I wouldn't eat there again.

I have been a customer of Loveless for more than 8 years.  I am grateful of my meal today.  My fabulous waiter, Owen was absolutely a delight.  Owen made my visit very special.   I want personally thank you for your generosity.

Despite the 1 1/2 hr Sunday noon wait at the cafe the visit and meal to the Nashville iconic cafe was a delightful afternoon.  The wait was made bearable by complimentary coffee and lemonade with plenty of shady porches to sit under.  There is a country store and gift store on the grounds.  They sell ham, biscuit mix, marmalade and other popular items that are on the cafe menu.There are a few other boutiques and and art gallery featuring local handicrafts.
The breakfast menu is available all day and dinner is served at 1100 on.  No reservations on weekends but they are possible by using an app during the week.
The food was delish.  Biscuits were free and probably the highlight for me. They serve alcohol drinks as well.

Never do business with this place. Owner has horrible business ethics. It's a newer spot and I guess they just haven't figured out how to treat people right. Save your money for a place that's worth it.

My sister and I dropped in for lunch. She lived in Germany for three years and misses many of the foods she came to love there. This restaurant scratched the itch for her! 

We started with the Bierhaus Wings. Since I was expecting pig knuckles, I was a little disappointed. However, they tasted really great. They just weren't what I thought they were going to be. We had jaegerschnitzel with fries, schweinbraten with red cabbage, sauerkraut, and potato dumpling, and black forest cake. My sister didn't like the sauerkraut, but I did. We agree on everything else that it was marvelous!

We'll go back for sure!

Music City Winery opened it's doors on October 2, 2014 with a private media party on October 1, 2014.

It was still under construction on 9/19/2014.  So any reviews in September have to be false..  Impossible for a place under construction to host any concerts.  There is a fake review from September, 2014...  
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


What a lovely venue.
What a big surprise!

Nashville is maturing into a stately, classy lady with glitz and glam and all these wonderful venues opening around town to host private parties, concerts, whatever you need, and it doesn't have to be in some stark windowless building.
City Winery opened their doors on October 1st.  They hit the ground running!

I came to this venue for a private party and the place rocked smoothly without a hitch.
From the moment we all walked in, took the tour of the building, met the owners, sat down to our scrumptious dinner and a variety of wines.

Everything was top notch.
The wait staff, the manager, the music, the food, the table settings, the wine..
Dear Gussy.....  what a magical night they made for my hosts.

I'd like to return for a concert venue and dinner.
Excellent place to have an event.. Christmas party, engagement party, Manager meetings..  what a great place to have it.

From their web site:  "We are a unique facility, combining a fully functioning winery with intimate concerts, food & wine classes, private events in a variety of configurations, and fine dining. We have created a compelling mix for our sophisticated clientele of foodies, and active cultural patrons--bringing the wine country experience to the middle of a large city."

Go check it out.
Atmosphere was great food was so so disappointing variety of entrees and some dishes were not really good

Awesome venue!!! We saw Phil Vasser here in October, 2019.  They are an urban winery that source their grapes or juice from California. So they offer a nice selection of wine including some cabs, francs, blends, Pinot noir, and more. They also offer a nice selection of craft beer. The food was delicious; pizzas, apps, and main entrees.

The venue has 200-300 seats that all offer a good view of the performer. The service was great, and we will definitely be back!!

The bar and food service sucked at the Leon Russell show last Sunday.  This is my 15 th show at the Winery and the food and service has declined steadily since I joined last year.  The Shows are outstanding but if you want the whole packages it misses. I love this place for music but the service and kitchen timing need to step it up.  We got our food during the last song.

Food was good.  Beer was good. I might go back for those items.  The service was a bit slow.  Friday night and not really that crowed.  The music was way TOO loud, or poorly projected.  And the room is not acoustically prepared for it. You could not talk at the table.  The waitress could not hear, and neither could we.  And there are lots of questions about the food and drinks.  Having music is nice, but get a better PA system and turn it down.

Every time I go it's an absolute treat. Delicious food (especially the biscuits---OMG) and fast service. Everyone is friendly and sweet. I highly recommend Loveless and even though there is always a wait, don't let that deter you. Enjoy the grounds, shop in their stores or lounge in the yard while you wait--it's worth it! Try the potato casserole and chicken salad. Both are EPIC!
First off the beer is delish. Atmosphere is amazing. Food is to DIE FOR. We're officially fans and will be back every weekend lol

This place is special to our family. Anytime we are in the Nashville area, we make our way to the Loveless for some good Southern cookin'. Breakfast, lunch or dinner, this place has it all. The Loveless Cafe is somewhat of a Nashville institution, so be ready for a wait during peak days and times. Even on a Friday late afternoon, we waited for 35 minutes or so. However, we did a bit of shopping in the gift shops and played a few games of cornhole while we waited. It was a nice to have alternatives to just waiting for a table. Once seated, the service was wonderful, and the food was even better! We had fried chicken, spicy fried chicken and a pulled pork dinner and all were fabulous. 
As a tip- this is off the beaten path. It is at the northern terminus of the Natchez Trace parkway, worth a drive on for a few miles as it is beautiful. It will take a bit of time to get to if you are heading from downtown. I'll be honest, I wanted to eat here so bad, I fibbed to my husband about how far off the Interstate it really was. I think if he heard ten more minutes one more time, I'd have been left on the side of the road in Nashville. But hey, I'd probably be working at the Loveless by now!

We have been lovers of Loveless for 30 years. It's all about the biscuits and fried chicken. We made many a pilgrimage to the restaurant when we lived in the Nashville area for 20 years and make sure to return with each visit back.

The wait time can be substantial. It's best to arrive after 1:00 and before 5:00. If you can, ask for a table in the original house section at the front of the restaurant. The add on area is loud and rushed, resembling the ambience of a Cracker Barrel 

Order the fried chicken or better yet, the fried chicken livers. And don't fill up on biscuits and homemade preserves, you will need the stomach space.

We had high hopes for this place....after living in Germany for 4 years we wanted to have a good German meal  Unfortunately The customer service was horrible and the food mediocre at best    Maybe stop in and have a beer ( albeit warm) but save your money and don't eat

Great place. Fun atmosphere. Good prices on shots. Mixed drinks still very expensive, but so is everywhere else near Broadway. Great bar tender this afternoon. She was friendly and working hard. Bartender this evening sucked. Dark haired guy. Played on his phone and talked with some blond chick while ignoring about 6 people at the bar waiting to order drinks. Then when he finally showed up his attitude sucked.
Cool space, good drinks, great staff!!! Breakfast served all day which is always a plus.

The grits, omg... the biscuits, omg! I swear in another life I was a southerner who survived solely on barbecue, grits, biscuits, and gravy. 

When I visited with friends during a Nashville vacation, I was more than excited to make the trek here for breakfast. We knew the wait would be worth it. Surely it was. You should also know that this isn't in the heart of the city, but rather on the outskirts -- about a 30min drive from the city. I shall remind you, the food is worth it.

We arrived, put our names in, received a pager that would work on the Loveless plot, which had a few gift shops and other places to sit and relax while you wait. For us, they said 1 hour, we got our table after 45min. 

Needless to say, we got a great deal of shopping done while we waited! The gift shops have cookbooks, biscuit mixes, kitchen decor and supplies, and so many other great items that are perfect for souvenirs or gifts to bring home for family and friends. Meanwhile, the hunger pangs started coming because of the irresistible scent of barbecuing meats wafting through the air.

Every table starts with a basket of biscuits (dreams do come true). They're small, warm, and fluffy. I loved the butter + blackberry preserves combo. I didn't want to overdo it so I had to cool off after 3 biscuits and save room for my entree. I had the pork barbecue with eggs over easy and a side of cheesy grits. I can't describe the comfort I felt as I devoured the tender, juicy pulled pork topped with a drizzle of extra BBQ sauce, which is more than enough to last another meal. Of course I had leftovers, which were great as a late night snack later that evening. The grits were perfect - creamy and cheesy and full of flavor. 

I could eat here for the rest of my life and be happy. Oh, how I wish I could...
Excellent food! Great friendly service!!! Would definitely come back next time we come through Nashville. Biscuits are out of this world!!!
Best breakfast in all ifNashville. Omelets are awesome. Biscuits fluffy and hot served with fresh made jams and jellies. Atmosphere is laid back. Love the specialty shops.

This is probably one of my all time favorite places to spend New Year's Eve. I have been visiting my family in Nashville for the holidays for the past four years. This year we spent the evening at the CW. Our venue waitress, Kim, was extremely knowledgeable about the menu, wines and enhanced our experience. 
Marc Broussard was the perfect entertainment for the evening. We shall return!

One of the best breakfasts I have had! Would definitely come back here!
Service and food excellent!

What we ordered:
-the country ham- their specialty - my friend thought it was alright and the ham was a little on the dry side
-Waffle- great flavor and crunch 
-biscuits- free for the table.  I loved the strawberry and blueberry jam.  I really wanted to love the peach jam, but wasn't impressed. 
-Chicken biscuit sammie- really good
-Granola- homemade they thought it was osme of the best granola they've ever had
- I got a side of gravy to try their gravy.  It's almost as good as mom makes! large pieces of sausage and great flavor. 

Although I was super full, I really wanted to try the Key Lime Pie, but sadly, they had sold out.  So if you go maybe you should try it and tell me what I missed out on :(

This ended up being the perfect destination for our last night in Nashville! Just stumbled on this place through Yelp, and SO grateful I did! 
Bought tickets online about 1.5h before the show. The ticket prices were reasonable, although I didn't understand the hefty service charge! You buy a ticket for specific tables and chairs so you don't have to worry about finding somewhere to sit. And once I was there, I truly believe no matter where you sit, you will have a great unobstructed view- even the balcony! During the show, they turn the lights off and just had the table candles- it was a very intimate show!
The reviews are very mixed for the service at City Winery. I ended up having great service- no complaints! The waitress recommended the Petite V wine and it was delicious, so smooth! They offer a menu of wines made at the winery, offered on tap! Besides their own wines, they have a long list of wines by the bottle or glass. Also a few beers! 
The food was good! I had the duck sandwich and subbed the fries for Brussels sprouts- great decision. I loved the Brussels more than the sandwich, although both were good! 
Overall, I highly recommend the City Winery! Loved getting to experience live music without compromising on atmosphere or food quality! It was nice getting off Broadway and away from the younger crowd. I highly recommend you give it a try!

Everything about this restaurant was amazing, what an experience coming to this place was! I went to Nashville for the weekend and of course looked on yelp and trip advisor on the best places to eat (The Must Eats) and well this place showed up on both so me being me and wanting some great food I took an Uber (about 15$ from downtown Nashville) and came to check this spot out. Let me star off by saying this restaurant is not only a restaurant it's the cutest motel with a restaurant and a couple gift shops. It's such a cute campsite area filled with such nice and happy people. The food at loveless cafe is everything ones taste buds can dream of. The biscuits are life changing!! I can almost guarantee they will be the best biscuits you will ever eat in your life, that's how amazing they truly are. It's hard to even save room for your actual meal because they're so addicting you cannot stop eating them and loveless cafe pairs them with four different jelly's so you have to try a biscuit with each jelly so you can determine which one you like the most lol. I could go on and on about how wonderful this place is and how delightful the food was but it's just an experience you need to try yourself.

I had the pleasure of being the celebratory guest of honor at Bavarian Bierhaus and all I can say is what a wonderful experience it was for myself and all 50ish guests that came along. My parents through me a graduation bash and the space and efficiency was unmatched. Despite all the hustle and bustle of the party, the servers in charge of us were more than capable of handling the many orders and requests that came through. From one order to the next on a blank check, every one of my guests was well satisfied with drink and food and no one's order was wrong. I applaud the staff or Bavarian Bierhaus for tending to both mine and my party's needs with efficiency and promptness. No one amongst us was disappointed in the experience despite so many of us and it was overall an enjoyable and pleasant time. Although there were many of us, everyone was treated as an individual guest and their requests met. If you're looking for an open space with exceptional service and fare, Bavarian Bierhaus has got you covered.

There are a few iconic places in every city that you just kind of have to visit, and in the Nashville area Loveless Cafe is one of them.  This place went "viral" before the internet, convincing people to head out to a former motel in the middle of nowhere to indulge in biscuits and jam.

I will admit that I don't like to wait in lines, so I've been avoiding Loveless as a result.  I've heard sometimes the wait is up to two hours, and they don't take reservations for small parties.  But when my friend Lindsey and I were texting at like 7am about breakfast, we figured we could go super early and beat the church rush on a Sunday morning.  We were right; we barely had to wait, and you get to wander around their little stores while you do.  It's like an original Cracker Barrel in that regard.

The biscuits were AWESOME.  I loved them!  I tried all the jams they brought with them too.  For my breakfast, I went basic with scrambled eggs and crispy bacon, plus a small side of their hash brown casserole.  That cheesy goodness was so rich and heavy, I didn't even finish half of it!  I ate very well and enjoyed it a lot.

I'm not sure if I will be back to Loveless, unless a visitor or friend wants to go... it's about 20-25 minutes from where I live, and nothing else is nearby.  I liken it to eating at Lady & Sons in Savannah; it's a haven for tourists after so many appearances on Food Network and the like.  But it was definitely worth checking off my Nashville "bucket list"!

First of all, this is the cutest little place! They have a little market store and novelty barn and hotel. But I came for the cafe! Cindy our waitress was so kind and wonderful! She was quick and had GREAT suggestions! I had her personal favorite: fried pork chops, they were mouthwatering! Not greasy, perfectly cooked! Grits were savory and butter filled, fried chicken was so juicy! The real star was the hash brown casserole! Cheesy goodness right there that makes your soul sing! The complimentary biscuits were warm and fluffy and their homemade butter and preserves were a perfect balance of fruit and sweetness! This will be going down on the must haves list when I travel to Nashville again!!

As a native Nashvillian one of the things that was severely lacking in my experience of town was attempted to be remedied last year with my first trip to eat at the Loveless Cafe. Unfortunately there was an hour+ wait and we got some to-go food, which was underwhelming forty minutes later when I ate it.

I'd been to the Loveless many times in the past, usually involving motorcycle rides or a charity event, or something at the barn, but I'd never eaten there which was quite odd.

I went again and was more impressed, but that experience was also nothing to write home about, especially since my home was about 20 minutes away and I was the only person who would be checking mail.

Third time however was a charm. We went with baby in tow, they were very nice to us and her, the food was quite good (those biscuits do *not* keep,) and I could imagine why some people dream of coming to this place.

There were a few vegetarian options available. I ended up getting an omelet and sharing it with my rugrat along with some cheesy hash browns and some biscuits. This place is baby approved as a note.

I never made it out there when the biscuit lady was still alive, so I don't know how they compare to the originals, but they were great fresh and solid as a rock unfresh, which may give you valuable clues and insights into how your arteries will fare.

Parking is a bit of a pain, always has been, it's a combo of not quite large enough, too much area, and slow exiting. If you're heading there just park and plan to walk a bit, you'll be happier parking further away, at least in my experiences.

Although off the beaten path, it was well worth the trip. Although it was lunch, we were seated quickly and our server, Mary, was at our table after was had settled in. After getting more biscuits than we could imagine, we placed our order. No sooner did our meals arrive then my wife knew she needed a "to-go" box. I had the catfish sandwich and my wife the BLT. Both came with fries and I cannot think of anything negative about the food.The catfish was lightly breaded and didn't cover the fish. The only negative we had was the location of the table which was next to a door and at a crosswalk between the hostess and dining room and the kitchen and a seating section. I have sat in worse locations, and it was a table for 2. Although this was our first trip there, it will not be our last.

Do yourself a favor and please eat here!

Hands down, the best Southern food around town!!

Free coffee is why they're getting two stars!

There is no way this place is worth the hour plus wait we were told when we arrived. Being on a time crunch we opted for take away and decided to eat outside. Our biscuits weren't really cooked. What the hell? The French toast was fine and happily my egg omelette was fully cooked. This is not a must visit and even if I lived in the area I don't think I'd go back.

Ok, so the biscuits get five stars! But the food only three. Loveless Cafe is a tradition in the Nashville area, having served their famous biscuits for over 40 years. 

We had to try it and they were some of the best biscuits I've ever had. The main course was good, but not out of the ordinary. My fried okra I make at home is better and I believe the mashed potatoes are instant. 

Still a good meal, but I would maybe go back for breakfast instead to try the biscuits and gravy.

4/4 people in my party don't know what the hype was. The biscuits were OK.  Mac and cheese was alittle worse than velvetta mac and cheese.  The fried chicken was dry.  The creamed corn was equal to Jolly Green Giant creamed corn.  And to wait a hour and 45?!?  NO.  We all said that Cracker Barrel would have been better.

My wife and I went on a Friday night. Half the tables were empty but they seated us with a group of strangers. We moved ourselves ONE table to behind the strangers. For over 10 minutes the wait staff and other employees ignored us.

We left.

We drove to the mall from out of town just for this restaurant.

I don't know if we will return.

They have lost their edge...no longer special, alright but nothing to write home about.

They have a system to maximize profit and that rather than charm and service trump customer happiness.

Well, would have loved to try this restaurant but, despite talking to a staff member and being assured that we could eat at the bar and not need a reservation, we arrived at 1730 and was told no seating was available and the restaurant was closing in 25 minutes.  What????

Along with Mission BBQ, this is arguably the highlight of the mall and I would definitely like to explore the menu some more.

The gift shop has some genuinely charming (though often overpriced) things in it. I found a stuffed a dachshund for only 12 bucks. The beer hall style is nice, as is the bar up front, where we ate.

The pretzel, which you can get for free if you stop at the kiosk outside, is fine for what it is - it's not terrific, but it's hard to really mess up a pretzel. The Bavarian Onion Soup was very good, with pretzel bits in it to differentiate it from standard French Onion.

We ordered the King Ludwig Platter to try to get a sampling of everything. The meats were all very good, with the Rouladen probably being the best part and the Knackwurst being the most forgettable of the meats. Meanwhile, while the gravy was excellent, the actual potatoes were kind of grainy (almost like instant).

Our server was very kind and attentive. I'd be curious to see this place once it gets more crowded. As is, I definitely enjoyed myself.
Looking for somewhere to eat in Nashville, this place is fabulous!!!  Food is great, hot when brought to your table.  Absolutely everything wonderful.

Five stars for the beers and three stars for the food! We came to try this place after missing Bavarian style beer after our trip to Germany last summer. The beers were absolutely on point! If only the food would live up to how good the beers were. I had the traditional schnitzel with fries and was really disappointed. Everything was almost cold when it was brought to our table and really lacked flavor. So I had to knock down a star. When we went there was also a live band playing! It really made the whole place feel authentic like any bierhaus you can find in Germany or Bavaria.

VIP means Very Impersonal. I purchased tickets thinking that I'd be close to the stage. Yet we're escorted to the back and because it's raised and less traffic. VIP ought to contain 3 elements closeness to stage, sectioned off and better seats AT LEAST. The tables are so small and uncomfortable. The design of the room really needs to be evaluated. I'm over it!

Let me tell you....the can make some biscuits! Some of my favorites! The peach jam is to die for and I always stick up on it when I'm here. I got the country ham, eggs, and French toast. The country ham is delicious, but the French toast was a little underwhelming. I got the Bloody Mary with Moonshine and my mom got the regular Bloody Mary and I'll just say, stick to the biscuits! Sorry but those were the worst drinks I've had in a long time. Tons of celery seed that you had to crunch your way through while drinking. Other than that, YUM!
The food was great! The staff were nice and the band was awesome. Totally recommend this place.

Came here for the first time and really enjoyed it. We ordered off the breakfast menu, but the dinner menu looked great as well. They also have some family style options for both. Biscuits were great, as was everything we ordered. Look for the cupcake of the month.

We were hear last winter and loved this place. Came back this summer and nothing has changed. Biscuits were marvelous! Service was great and prices were very fair. I love this place even if it is packed with tourists every day. Worth the wait any time.

What is NOT to LOVE about the Bavarian Bierhaus!? We met some friends tonite so the hubs, friends, and I could enjoy Oktoberfest! They have different specials each weekend night along with the Oompah Bands and Beer! Tonite I tried one of the specials they were offering and tweaked it. The Zwiebelrostbraten (pan-fried New York strip steak smothered with an onion reduction gravy) with REAL mashed potatoes on the side, but instead of the onion reduction I asked for and received their fabulous mushroom gravy! And oh.my.goodness this is by far the BEST thing I have eaten there yet! The hubs got the Grillhendl (roasted 1/2 chicken) and fries and split a bratwurst with his buddy. He said the chicken was a little dry, fries were fantastic, but the beer made up for the chicken! I'm not sure what my friends all got, I know 2 of them got the Rahmschnitzel (chicken schnitzel) and spatzle, they loved it! They participated in the FREE Bier until the keg runs dry which started at 8pm, the line was long, and the keg went quick! The beer was good and cold!
What a GREAT evening of live music, GREAT food, good bier, and FANTASTIC service!!

Wish I could put zero stars. I cant even go into everything that was wrong w our food. Every element was sub par to inedible. Absolutely no redeeming qualities to speak of. Over cooked, dry pork, mush cous cous overcooked to the point that it created clumps served ice cold under hot shrimp so half the shrimp was cold as well. Bland seasoning. Peri peri has spice, this had none. Was more like a bland butter chicken sauce from an old buffet. When paying 25$ a plate, salt and pepper should not be brought w your meal. So tacky and simple proof they dont know how to season properly themselves. Poured our own waters as there is a glass bottle full on the table and no one ever refilled them. Just an overall a amateur mess.

Reminds me of my Grandma's cooking.
The fried liver and gizzards were perfectly cooked, the biscuits were irresistible, and deserts were amazing. We also love the staff who sang happy Birthday to my wife.
Hope to come back soon.

Everything was rushed! 
I arrived and waited in the valet line, and from that moment on everyone was in a hurry. 

I got to the table quick service to see what I wanted, so I started with a menu.  Half price wine and appetizers. 
Everyone was getting their apps when I arrived. Three different wait staffers took my drink order. It was a bit confusing lol but they worked it out.

I got the mushroom and goat cheese balls. They were delicious. 
Prosecco was also quite tasty. 
I tried the hot crab dip.. not the best. 
Everyone at the table raved about the pizza! 

I would go back to check it out again. 

Beautiful decor!

The atmosphere alone is worth the visit. Even the staff are dressed to the German nines. Not nein, nines. Lederhosen clad servers and live polka music make you feel like you're in an authentic German bierhall. 

The German sausages are all sourced from my hometown of Milwaukee from a sausage maker that's been around since 1880! Usingers is synonymous with top quality. If you've never had a bratwurst that snapped when you bit into it, then you've never had a good brat. The menu has some seriously authentic dishes. I may be here every week. 

Make sure to wash it all down with a liter or das boot of the finest German beer before leaving to do some shopping at the mall while you sober up. 

Auf Wiedersehen!

A friend posted photos of biscuits and jam months ago - and I was like HOLD UP.... TELL ME WHERE THESE ARE.

So when we ended up adding Nashville as a stop on our family vacation, this got added to the list of places to eat.

Glad we did. Biscuits were yummy. Food was all tasty. Such a cute little spot with shops on the property, etc.

We left happy, and I bought a trio of the jams to take home with us.

This is such a cool place right in the middle of the hotel and mall. The restaurant is huge and there's an area when you walk in to buy all the German goodies your heart desires. We went a little crazy with the candies and imports that we had to think about how much space we had in our suitcase. There was no wait at all because we arrived during lunch. Our waiter was super friendly (and was actually German). He spoke with my boyfriend for a little which was cute. My boyfriend ordered the big meat plate and said it was quite authentic. He also said he was super full and satisfied. Being that I don't eat dairy, it was a little difficult for me to order but I ended up getting the chicken schnitzel anyways and asked for the sauce on the side. It was heavy but delicious. You're able to sub out whatever side you want so I got the red cabbage which was also really good. I'd definitely recommend stopping g by if you're visiting. I'm glad my friend recommended this place. I'd love to come back for dinner next time I'm in town.

They have a really nice selection of drafts. It was almost a little overwhelming but the bartender made great selections. While I was looking over the menu a host stopped by, I think her name was Rebeccah, and recommended the chicken fried steak. It was outstanding!

Get a picture with the classic sign at Loveless. A Nashville staple. Order the jam as gifts for Christmas and take tourists here for breakfast on Saturday. The atmosphere is cozy and the biscuits are to die for. If you need a pie to take to a special occasion, this is where to get it.

So I've been here 4 times, all said 45 - 55 minute wait...there is not that many small cafes that I would wait for, for that long...but the 4th time I decided to wait for 40 minutes....walked around the area and shopped at the other stores...very cool stuff...then we were seated...people talk about their biscuits...they ain't lyin!! Please all the food was delicious...so earth the wait, now i know how far Elvis felt after he ate there!

I would bump the star rating up to 3-1/2 but it isn't an option. The Bier Hall is huge and very reminiscent of German Bier halls. I loved the Bavarian colors, the dried flowers, the Lederhosen,and the picnic style seating (much nicer than picnic tables). I loved the live music but missed the crowd interaction. The seating is too American which encourages people keeping to themselves rather than creating the European feeling of community, inclusion, discovery.
