The menu is promising offering some favorite staples of the local Ghasthaus in any German village. The execution however is disappointing. The best option we tried was any of the wurst, potato salad, schnitzel. I wish the spatzle was good but every dish of it in our party was mushy and salty.  The large potato dumplings were closer to mashed potatoes than a dumpling. The bread served is a pumpernickel rye instead of the traditional pumpernickel or brotchen and even worse it was served with American butter which is good but could never compare to European. The bier is served in proper glasses and mugs and the size options are nice. The bier selection was good not great but satisfies. I love the concept of this place but it is missing a few marks. I may be being a bit harsh because I have spent so much time in the bier tents at German festivals and many nights in German village gasthauses. I would go back but not for the food unless I was craving a traditional bratwurst. I went there is hopes of experiencing the German camaraderie and awesome food. I got a little of both so all in all not bad and even good, just not really good. 
I did edit this and bumped it a full 4 stars. I LOVE LOVE LOVE that Bob replied! So listen, if you go to the Bavarian Bierhaus PLEASE PLEASE take advantage of the opportunity to interact with the other guests. People are interesting! You may learn something and it isn't like you have to invite them to the family reunion!  I recognize all of Bob's challenges in hitting all the marks. Thanks for the reply.

The food was amazing. I came for lunch on Saturday and breakfast on Sunday! The portions are HUGE! You will definitely take a meal home. The pancakes were buttery and fluffy. The omelet was cheesy and light. The hash brown casserole, oh my goodness talk about tasty! Overall I think this place is awesome and inexpensive. I love the atmosphere and the wait staff is super fast, efficient, and polite. Can't wait to come back!

City Winery has always been so welcoming and accommodating. I've seen different shows- from the Secret Sisters, when I got to experience the relaxation of sitting down and enjoying great wine and food during the show, to Brandi Carlile's surprise show, which was one of the most memorable nights ever. 

I've met the winemaker, gone to fabulous classes like a blind tasting class and Prosecco Masterclass, and finally got to do an event with them to open winery tours up to the Deaf community (I'm a sign language interpreter). From the get go, City Winery was enthusiastic and open-minded, and we all had the BEST time!!! It was fantastic to see a company be so willing to offer a winery tour and tasting to the Deaf community, and those who attended couldn't get enough. I'm so grateful for their proactive collaboration, and can't wait to experience more with them!

Iconic Americana at its best! this place, located outside Nashville is a tiny piece of yesteryear for us to enjoy today. On Sunday morning there was a 2 1/2 hour wait to sit inside and 35 minutes if you took it outside and ate a picnic table...which is what we did. Food preparation is excellent and their home made biscuits are the bomb, particularily with their homemade jams.  If your in the area you have to stop by!
EVERYTIME I come here it's a good time. Bartenders are always friendly. By far the best bar in Nashville. Drinks are dreamy

Ahh, yet another place in Nashville "renowned" for their biscuits that didn't deliver. Maybe it's my version of biscuits that they don't deliver on. They make 10k a day, and maybe that shows. While tasty, they remind me of the kind you bake yourself in the little metal tin. However, their preserves, country ham, hash brown casserole, & and country fried steak were very tasty! Very touristy and kinda cool. Worth the trip!

Restaurant is great. Big and spacious! The kids meal was cheap and giant portion and the giant pretzel  with cheese was the best appetizer. Our waitress Morgan was very nice and accommodating. We were with 6 kids and she was very patient and came back to check on us often. The pork shank was huge and crispy. Only thing I didn't like was the crispy noodles because it wasn't so crispy and my daughter didn't like the Mac and cheese but everything else was delicious. The French onion soup was really cheesy. The giant beers were super cold! Would definitely go back!

Lived up to the Hype. I have lived outside of Nashville my entire life and the first time I went here was the past Sunday. The grounds have nice little shops to browse while you wait, places to hang out in the shade so you really don't feel like your waiting. The food was delicious, the biscuits reminded me of my grandmothers. Quaint ambiance. Good food and friendly service made a great afternoon with friends.
This place was awesome!! Every server that came by rocked!! Virginia, thank you for the stories you shared with Tammy and myself Friday afternoon. We will be back!!

My wife and I stopped in yesterday based on all the great reviews we found online and they were NOT wrong.

I ordered the fried chicken (half size) with the fried green tomatoes. The chicken wasn't hot/spicy but well spiced and had a great flavor. The breading was crispy and not too thick so it stays on the meat as you eat. The fried green tomatoes are very thin, almost like chips so they're easy to eat with your hands. So delicious! Quite possibly the best fried green tomatoes I've had in my lifetime.

As far as service, our waitress was Virginia and if I could I would take her with me to every restaurant I go to. She was beyond pleasant, always smiling and was very attentive. In fact, all the staff there seemed to really enjoy each other and their time there. 

If you are in the area this is a must.

Great place and service was outstanding. Kristen was awesome and made our visit very enjoyable- had family style supper and did not disappoint! Not a fan of the Barbeque as it was a little dry but everything was wonderful

I visited City Winery last night for an event upstairs and already can't wait to go back. The food was amazing and the atmosphere was beautiful, but the service was enough reason to come back. Francesca showed exemplary service and went above and beyond to help my party and myself. I cannot express how happy we were with this place and the experience she created for us.

I have been enjoying this place with family for 2 yrs -usually I get pulled pork or meatloaf - this past time I tried catfish it was tasteless - hubby had chicken fried steak and that it was tough and blah - I will say despite this we decided to get dessert ( usually we are too stuffed ) he got chocolate cream pie , I got coconut cream pie we were shocked neither had any flavor really , the whipped cream could have used some vanilla flavor and a bit of sugar - in fact the pies themselves tasted like sugar was totally forgotten in both not to mention extract of flavors - whoever makes their cream pies needs some new re pies or baking lessons - not sure the drive is worth it an

Tourist trap with high prices, mediocre food and terrible service.  Inside the place is really cool and gives the vibe of a German bier hall.  Food is bland.  Draft German beer selection is just OK.  Service though at bar was terrible. Had lunch there at 1:30.  Bar had only a few patrons remaining and I almost walked out after sitting for 10+ minutes without anyone greeting me.  All the while, I was 4ft from the hostess station were two young ladies continued to chit chat without hunting down the bar tender who kept disappearing in the kitchen.  Go somewhere else.

I always enjoy eating at the Bavarian Bierhaus.
The pork shank was not only delicious, but it was also huge.  The red cabbage was also great.  We sat at the bar and service there was fantastic!  Everything I have eaten here is good.
Food here was good. Atmosphere and service is great. Decent beer. I'd definitely return. I'll go out on a limb and say of all the restaurants at Opry Mills, this is one you should go to.

Perhaps the cafe is overrated. Of course if you're going on the weekend be ready for a two-hour wait; it's quite smart of them to have a little village of shops to spend your time in while waiting. I bought their amaretto honey butter which is amazing (but so sweet only a dab will do ya). 
I ordered steak & eggs which were decent, but the side of hashbrown casserole was amazing (an LC specialty to be sure- don't go without trying it). I couldn't wait to try their oh-so-famous biscuits and ordered the biscuit sampler.  I found the pimento cheese/fried green tomato biscuit to be very good and the pulled bbq pork biscuit made me curious for their bbq dinners (the bacon and fried chicken biscuits are nothing to speak of). But the plain biscuits served with breakfast lack any flavor- Jim & Nicks' muffins cannot compare, even Red Lobster cheddar biscuits are much better lol. I certainly had enough leftovers for a second meal, but left the plain biscuits behind.
The service is friendly and all the famous Nashville celebs cover the walls as visitors but for me to wait two hours it's got to be outstanding.

The new Nashville. This place puts it all together.

Intimate setting, plenty of room, purpose built music venue, great food, great wine list, full bar and prompt service. 

What more could you ask for?

Here first time for Leon Russell. Quite surprised about this place. Like sitting in a restaurant with restaurant menu and servers only 50 feet from the stage.

The food was really good. Pan seared mackerel was a favorite for our table. Perfectly cooked and expertly paired with purple Brussel sprouts, lentils and a cranberry purée. 

The wine selection was ample and we never even looked at the reserve list. The sprits list was also plentiful with plenty of bourbon selections among others.

Once the music started the acoustics worked well and the sight lines were excellent. Everyone remained comfortably seated throughout the performance.

This place is worth visiting regardless of who is performing and can only be improved by the level of talent on stage.

Wish we could give 4.5 stars - it was almost perfection. Came with friends and we had a great time. Loved the atmosphere, the beer, and the food. The food was fantastic! Would love to come back on a busy weekend night with all the music. The one small complaint we had was addressed promptly by one of the owners. Would definitely recommend and be back!

German restaurants aren't easy to find, and it's even more difficult to find one that can accommodate gluten-free and dairy-free options.  So it was awesome to be able to eat here as they were accommodating and the food was delicious!  The hostess was also very helpful.  I ate there with people who had lived in Germany and they enjoyed it too.  Thank you!

I really enjoyed my experience at the cafe! The food was fresh, brought out quickly, and I had a very kind server. I enjoyed a waffle (which I could only eat half of because it was so big). The waffle was a bit dense, versus light and fluffy like I like them. I also had their cheesy hasbrown casserole (I could have ordered this alone and been SO happy!)... SO delicious!! I also had the ham and bacon, but they were both way too salty for my taste. The homemade biscuits were to die for though! Coupled with the peach jam (which I normally don't eat). Very very tasty! 
One last thing, be sure to eat before you go. Our wait was around an hour and 40 minutes, but there's plenty of shopping around to keep you occupied.
Best breakfast ever! Hands down, no contest. The biscuits and homemade jam were amazing! I highly recommend the BBQ pork and eggs. Good ol' southern hospitality! Our server Trey was the best!

As someone who has visited German beer halls in Germany I can say emphatically this place captures the feeling. From the hall design to the soccer goal in the urinals this place has it all. 

Kathleen, our server, was more than helpful. Even offering her last ibuprofen to my wife to alleviate her headache. I just wish her coworker, maybe a manager, with the gauged ear piercings had been so pleasant. When I asked if he could set the TV channel for us he held his finger up to me in silence without uttering a word as if I were disrupting him. Sorry to be a nuisance but you're in the service industry and I expect words not callous gestures. 

I can say I will be back, but I hope not to see this person again as they had no manners.

My wife and I stopped here because she looked up things to do in Nashville. It was a pretty cool place if you have time to kill a few hours. The biscuits you get before your meal were hot & fresh. You get peach, blackberry, and strawberry preserves to go on them. (We bought some biscuit mix & blackberry preserves in the gift shop while we waited to be seated.) For our meal we split the southern sampler (fried chicken, catfish, and meatloaf.) The chicken and catfish were great but the meatloaf was pretty average. Don't waste your meal on the meatloaf when there's plenty of other good things on the menu. The hashbrown casserole and mac&cheese were both really good for sides. This place reminded me of cracker barrel but with more history. Would definitely go back.

TWO WORDS - TASTELESS CAFE! I was as disappointed as a child on Christmas who didn't get what she asked for from Santa. 
When I learned my husband was coming to Tennessee for business, the first thing I did was scout out places to eat. He and I are both self proclaimed foodies. Anyway, Loveless Cafe was top on the list. I skimmed through the reviews and was impressed by what I was reading. 
When we finally arrived in Nashville, I asked the lady, who checked us into the hotel, what she thought of Loveless Cafe, she raved about the biscuits. She said they're like nothing she ever tasted before. At this point, I'm boiling over with excitement. 
On our way to the restaurant, the traffic was horrible; however, I didn't mind. I knew the payoff would be SO worth it - not so much. 
Lemme just say, my husband and I are from Alabama. We know some good, southern cooking. It's what we were raised on in grandma's kitchen. ... OK, back to the review. 
We arrived and were immediately seated. I believe the positives stop about there. Yup, immediately seated - the only positive. 
The waitress came over hyping the food up. The pork is smoked 12 hours... we're known for our pork, fried chicken and biscuits... On and on and on... Lemme just say, she played her role as the hype girl - give her a raise! 
I digress... 
I'd already decided on the sampler weeks before we arrived. I knew we'd want to taste a little bit of err'thang! 
Ah, I wish I'd taken a picture of the food. The chicken wings and hush puppies looked like they'd been cooked in old grease. You could clearly tell it was time to change it. If the looks weren't enough to make the determination, the taste sealed the deal. The fish was also tasteless. I don't believe any seasoning was used. The 12 hour slow smoked pork - all I can do is shake my head! It was cold, hard, awful and served on top of what looked like a pancake which looked and felt like it had been sitting under a light all day. All the moisture and life was sucked right out of it - poor pancake! 
Now, to the raved review biscuits... The biscuits at the Cracker Barrel in Alabama taste better. I'm sure they're the same everywhere, but I can't vouch for anywhere else since I haven't been... There's nothing special, or spectacular about these biscuits. In fact. I've had a better biscuit at Jack's - a fast food chicken restaurant.
Here's my advice - save your time, gas, coins, and taste buds! It's definitely NOT worth the hype. YOU'RE WELCOME!
Oh my I would come here just for the biscuits. Absolutely the best!!!! Service was great.

My daughter has lived in Nashville for almost 10 years so if don't do breakfast at Loveless it is not a good trip! We went during the week so we're seated right away. Before you even order out come the hot, melt in your mouth biscuits! You add a cuppa joe and you are in literally in  hog heaven! My daughter got the French Toast with bacon and I got my "usual" two eggs with bacon with hash brown casserole. We shared the two plates for the best of both worlds. They will refill not only your coffee cup but biscuits too!  They are known for their Country ham, takes one home to remember this epic visit.  They never rush you, even if there is a line out the door.  Sit a spell and enjoy a nice Southern breakfast.

Hewww weee honey! Bring your comfy crocs cause the line is looong! Oh and a crossword would be a good idea too. Ever heard of those Heavenly Hams they have at the fancy kroger or in the shoppin mall???? Well Loveless puts those hams to SHAME honey! They have heavenly ham, and boy oh boy did I butter my biscuit! But was it worth the 2 hour wait Yvette? Yes. Yes honey it was. Only thing I would say is, the bathroom isn't very escapable in a terror/hostage/tornada situation. For that I deducted a star, but, I'd put a step ladder in there to reach a window for old gals like me and it'd be a 5 star rating!!! A++++ food and service!

For me, the food was just ok, and barely that. The pretzel was great but very salty. The mustard it was served with was sticky and sweet rather than sharp and spicy like I was expecting. I ordered the meat and cheese board and the beer cheese soup. The meat was just awful. It had an overwhelming iron and geletin flavor and the quality was in par with Oscar Meyer. The cheese lacked flavor entirely. The soup had a gritty texture and should have been smooth.

They sat us quickly and accommodated us since we had a stroller. Our waters were brought out without being asked. We ordered our food and unfortunately it took about 45min- 1 hour to be brought out (2 cheeseburgers and 2 orders of chicken tenders). The milkshake we ordered was melted. We didn't receive one of our meals (we were sharing so we were all still able to eat). Our server Ian was rushing to help multiple tables with little to no help from anyone. He was very apologetic and never once was rude. We ended up returning our milkshake and never getting that 4th meal. I wish he had more help since it was a very busy Sunday lunch rush. 

5 starts to our server Ian, 0 stars for management.

We were charged more for two eggs and 2 slices of bacon than we would have been charged for an entire breakfast meal - why didn't the server tell us that? The prices are ridiculous, and for the life of me I don't understand why people rave over their biscuits - they're not even flaky! McDonald's and other fast-food places have better biscuits. Their chicken & dumplings taste like those you buy in a can at Kroger - not gross, but not homemade either. And their vegetable casseroles are too greasy. If people think the food is good I think it is because they can't cook themselves and don't really know what good home cooking tastes like. I'M NOT A FAN OF LOVELESS CAFE!

We visited Loveless for about the 15th time last weekend.  I learned a little more about it this time.  

Our first visit here was in around 1999 when Donna McCabe still owned it.  It was so charming then.  Like eating in a house.  This was before Loveless was expanded with more tables, professional kitchen, new restrooms, the stores, the barn, etc.  

It lost much of its charm when the McCabes gave it up.  But as I think about it, the things that have been done needed to be done.  Any business needs to make money or why have it?

A couple things I miss from the old Loveless.  They used to bring out biscuits in a round pan.  Now they are made in a large rectangular pan and served on a plate.  You just get a few and usually have to ask for more.  As I recall, the biscuits seemed better made the old way, even though it's the same recipe.  Also, the preserves used to be on the table in bigger glass containers.  Now they bring them out in tiny cups.  

Also, they used to grind up the ham for their omelets instead of chopping the ham.  Much better the old way.  Big difference.

But overall, I have to say the product is still good.  We waited for 2 hours last time.  It's not worth a 2-hour wait.  Cracker Barrel is not as good, but it's good.  If you have to wait more than an hour, screw it.  Come back another time.  

To me, this is a breakfast place.  They push the fried chicken at lunch and now have BBQ, but even when Donna owned it, the chicken was not that good.  Loveless is a breakfast place.

We have to give credit and a big thank you to the people who bought it from Donna.  I was told they are relatives of the Frist family of Nashville.  Good for them for saving this piece of our Tennessee culture.  

This place is not exactly as it used to be, but thanks to the new owners we still have it and it is very good.

Would prefer they use Tennessee-made meats, though.  Also, the sausage gravy here is less than spectacular.
Layne Mathis is literally amazing! It was extremely busy and Layne was able to really hold it down. Much love and greatly appreciated! Thanks Layne!

After reading all the great reviews on this place, I couldn't wait to visit! Very pleased. The staff is super friendly, and they look like they truly love being there! After talking with my server about the options, I decided to go with a sampler platter so I could have it all! I found the ham to be a bit salty but everything else was fine. The pork chop was my favorite. The complimentary biscuits are indeed to die for-- and I'm not typically a biscuit kinda gal! The various fruit preserves really make it, and you can buy these at their adjoined gift shop(s). I bought some souvenirs and a cute wrap for myself. Plenty of parking. No longer a motel but they do have function rooms available.

Wanted to try this place but decided not to based on the purposeful lack of organization. 

My wife and I walked in and were told if we wanted to sit in the restaurant there would be a wait, but if we wanted to sit at the bar we could right away. We elected to wait. 

Q: How long is the wait?

A: I really can't say. We're understaffed and have had a number of large parties walk in without a reservation. 

(There are several people waiting - looks like at least two parties.)

Q: Ok, can you put our name on a list?

A: Oh no, my General Manager doesn't allow me to make a list. I'd get in trouble if I made a list. You'll just have to stay around here. 

So while we're standing there, more people come in and are told the same thing. No no, we can't make a list. 

By this point it was clear there were going to be several parties, some before us and some after. 

Who's responsibility is it to keep track of who is first or second, etc? This young lady who hasn't given us a number, taken a name, didn't seem to be paying much attention at all to us or the other people waiting?

So we left. I'll go spend my money somewhere where the management is interested in providing for a reasonable accommodation of (gasp) logically dealing with crowds of customers in parties of varying size. You know - with something the rest of the restaurant world uses - a list.

We came to see the Opry and headed over to the mall to grab a quick lunch.  We stumbled onto the most authentic German/Bavarian  food we have eaten in the states.  

My wife had the Ludwig platter.  Tender rouladen made my wife remember her Oma's.  The spaetzle was light and fluffy and held up to our voracious shoveling.  The ham steak actually made her drop the fork and knife to gnaw every bit off the bone.  Red cabbage was deliciously mild, missing the high acidity I've come to deal with in other venues.

My currywurst (admittedly, the first I've had) was well seasoned with the "pop" one would expect of European sausage.  Pomme frites were crispy, but the curry ketchup made them amazing.

As we were wondering if this was a chain, the owner piped up from the bench next to us!  The manager stopped by to make sure all was delicious.  

My only negative is that we weren't closer to home in Maryland.  We ordered an extra entree to bring home for Oma, but I'm not sure the container will survive the trip.  I'll keep you posted if it makes her cry.
This restaurant should be on everyone's bucket list for authentic Southern food.  Forget healthy...forget cholesterol.  Just enjoy the awesome food here and eat a salad and workout tomorrow!

Why have a minimum? Why isn't one drink enough? No wonder it is dead here. Bad management/owner.
Out of business soon...go to a better bar. Lots to choose from.

This place is SO GOOD and SO CUTE. I loved, and I mean loved the southern vibes this place gives off. It's just really charming. 

The biscuits and preserves were dangerously good. I would've been happy just eating biscuits the entire morning. They're buttery and rich and delicious. I like how they were on the smaller side, too. And don't get me started on the preserves..they were out of this world.

I ended up getting a vegetable omelette and it was really fresh! They chopped up the vegetables into super tiny pieces which I loved because a lot of places don't do that. And the coffee was great too! There's also a really cute gift shop next to it as well. This was easily one of my favorite stops while I was visiting Nashville!

they handled a large (100+) group (with reservations) of hungry, tired, cranky guests and did so with grace and class...OH and the food was outstanding and everlasting ...did I mention the food was so very tasty and plentiful...because it WAS!!
A+++

My family and I visited during the 4th of July weekend. The wait was brutal, but with so many shops, there were a ton of things to look at. All of us loved our meals. I had the country fried steak and it was outta this world! Between that and the amazing biscuits, I was stuffed! The desserts looked so good that we couldn't pass it up and ended up splitting the banana pudding. Also very very good! 
It's now September, and I just went home to TN to visit my family. Mom made homemade biscuits using the mix she bought at Loveless. They were phenomenal. Some of the best biscuits I've ever had! Make sure to get some in their shop! (Expensive but so worth it)

Came here with a lot of family members - large family reunion. Good place with lots of seating and space. I ordered the schweinshaxe (pork shank). It was better than I expected. Most German fare I've had seemed dull, but this was very flamboyant: very crispy skin, tender meat, tasty lard, briny fried pork taste mixed with the sourness of the red cabbage and spice of the horseradish and creaminess of the gravy. 

Food didn't take too long to arrive. Price was a little on the high side for quantity and quality, but it is consistent with the local tourist area and shopping mall.

City Winery always has the  best events, tonight was the West Sonoma Coast Vintners...we did the VIP ticket which allowed us an hour early entrance to taste wine and the charcuterie board which was amazing, pictures will be attached!!! Some of my favorite wineries were Dumol, Ernest Vineyards and Peay Vineyards. Keep a look out for their events, top knot!!!

Came with the family for a nice German experience. Good beer! Giant hot pretzel as an appetizer was crisp on the outside and fluffy inside. Ambiance was cool, after the small bar there are rows and rows of tables with bench only seating. Perfect for making new friends if you're there during the dinner rush. Their food was good for the most part, would've gotten more stars from me if I didn't have to send my sliders back for being raw. When they came back out lo and behold they were still raw. The manager and server were super apologetic though and took it off the bill happily. The place also has live and festive music, complete with an accordion. Also bonus points given that everyone working there wore German costume. Would I go back? Maybe. Probably not my first pick though. Not too bad because the prices weren't awful!

This place is an event. There are multiple buildings for souvenirs, buying food to take home, and the smoke house. The restaurant is also massive and the staff so friendly; the manager personally reviewed the menu with my wife to discuss food allergies. The portions are massive, including the endless side of biscuits and jam. The amount of meat you get is the same whether it's a plate, or a dish with that meat! The pulled pork was good, not great, but I had enough leftovers for dinner and breakfast the next day! I'd go back.

Biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, jam, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, BISCUITS! 

Oh, yeah, they have other food, too, and a very friendly staff.
Loveless is a old Favorite It's Good Southern Cooling, Breakfast is Awesome and they do stay busy all day

New musician nights on Tuesdays! Free cover, good live music from new artists! This place was PACKED on a Tuesday. Like butts touching butts packed. This place must be doing something right if you can get all of these people to stay out late on a Tuesday and have a rough Wednesday morning. Small and dark inside, but a cool place to meet friends for drinks and tunes. Small outdoor area as well. 

How many blondes does it take to find the entrance? Well, there were two of us and we couldn't... so maybe 3? A nice man helped us out though. Like the big sign out front says, use the alley entrance. You have to go around back, and not down the wooden little walk that takes you to some other shop. Otherwise, awesome spot!

Stopped in on our way through Nashville.  It was a good choice. It was good food and quick.  Our waiter, FatJohn was good and funny. We enjoyed our meals.  The four of us had the giant pretzel with beer cheese for an app. The main courses were Black Forest schnitzel, curry wurst, wurst plate with jalapeño cheddar sausage, and spinach salad and onion soup.  All were good but here are some fine details...... the beer cheese was good but not great.  The jalapeño cheddar sausage was not spicy. The spinach salad dressing was a little gelatinous but still tasty. It was a texture thing. The sampler platter was ordered for dessert. The best thing on it was a toss up between the apple strudel and the pretzel bread pudding. Overall not a bad stop.
Great beer, food, and experience! Don't let the location deter a visit. Dishes are authentic, as well as the brews. Multiple visits have always been good.

With the drive and worth the wait. In fact I enjoyed the wait and took the time to tour the property and buy souvenirs. 

Owen made my day, he is a dream.

The food was amazing I chose a dinner sampler for brunch because it offered more choices. Chicken was well seasoned, catfish was amazing, and I always love country ham.  I wish I could have tried the bbq! Oh and the drinks were actually good I had something with whiskey, strawberries and lemonade...skip the mimosa and go for this drink it actually goes great with brunch.

The goods:  Beautiful bar, restaurant, venue.  The musicians that played were run of the mill singer/songwriters, but the sound was good (although it was really light, mainly acoustic music).  Every member of the staff I encountered was a lovely person.

The bads:  Overpriced.  Do you like paying $8-10 per glass of wine or beer?  Cause that's the lowest priced stuff.  Do you enjoy paying $9 for black bean dip that can barely be shared by two people?  Not to mention the chips that came with it were super thin and crumbled everywhere, and were gone by the time we were halfway through the dip.  All of the other reviews I've read here say the valet is $7, but it was $5 the night we went (Thursday).

So that's it. Everything was pretty much just okay.  I will probably stick to the smaller clubs with cheaper drinks and better bands.

Oh my goodness...seriously! I'm pretty sure the biscuits have crack in them...we just couldn't get enough! The best biscuits, hands down! The homemade jams that went with the biscuits (you get three to taste) were a perfect compliment to the biscuits. I had the BBQ pork and it was wonderful! And...since it's 'go big or go home' give the Mac and Cheese a try for a side! It was well worth the calories-absolutely delicious! And since no country meal is complete without dessert...might I suggest the coconut? It was delicious-even on a full stomach ! My only regret was not trying the banana pudding-I hear it's the bomb-diggety-I guess I will need to go back someday! We rolled out of the restaurant (literally) and was so glad we found this little gem on Pinterest! Give it a whirl!!

For a cafe that's named loveless, the place be showing us some mad love!

Loves:
+ Comp'd biscuits. They are def worth the hype OK!
+ I loved my chicken. Hopefully someone in your party will get some and share the wealth.
+ Owen was our waiter and he was an absolute delight.
+ Cute decor. I'm a fan.
+ Little shops for you to peruse while you wait for your table.

Not so loves:
- About 45 min outside of Nash.
- There'll most likely always be a wait.

Overall this place is wonderful and worth the drive AND the wait. Thank you to the cafe for delighting us with some good cooking and thank you Owen for being a kind soul.

The Loveless Café has the most amazing biscuits I have ever eaten! I mean seriously, I can make the biscuits my entire meal with their own preserves, honey, and butter. I cannot emphasize enough the biscuits alone are totally worth the wait at this place (my family has waited over 2 hours before for a table here - but there is plenty to do between walking around the on-site shops and playing cornhole by the picnic tables outside while you wait). 

Aside from the world's best biscuits, The Loveless Café services up all your classic country favorites. Their fried chicken is delicious - fresh, crispy, seasoned just right, and complimented by your choice of sides. I'd also recommend the fried catfish or the smoked beef brisket. Breakfast is served all day here if that's what you're in the mood for. 

The service is as top notch as the food here. Friendly southern hospitality at it's finest. And they've always been very attentive on refilling the biscuit basket - that's instantly 5 stars from me!

Just go and stay awhile. This little mini campus of country cooking and shopping is so much fun. It's something you don't find everywhere and they do such a great job of maintaining the grounds and providing a great experience.

-The hot sauce is very good, bought some to take home.
-The biscuit sandwiches are amazing! Got the sampler.
-The BBQ pork was so delicious.
-The jams are so good.
-The grounds have several buildings that offer different things.

Awesome experience that is worth staying awhile for to eat and shop. Very fun place!

Loveless is a solid 4 stars. Why is that, you might ask? Well, the biscuits are out of this world and they come with 3 different types of homemade preserves. It was buttery, sugary heaven. If I had those alone, it would have been 5 stars.

The food itself, however, was really just a 3. I got one of the omelettes and, although the portions were big (though not quite as big as the people there) it was a very average omelette. My friend got the pulled pork breakfast, which he loved. The meal was literally the day's sustenance for us. But i just keep dreaming about those biscuits...

The service was average. The waitress was not that attentive and forgot that I had ordered the honey and sorghum (which basically looked and tasted like just honey). Regardless, just go and order a plate of biscuits. You won't be sorry you did.

Friendly service and great rockabilly music, but that's where it stops. 
I had the turkey dinner, and the turkey was bone dry despite being drowned in gravy. I might come back for drinks and live music, but not to eat.

About a half hour drive from downtown Memphis but well worth it, wait was about 45 minutes but there other things to do like the gift shops on site.  The strawberry sipper in a mason jar with Rye Whiskey on side is absolutely delicious, hot biscuits with 3 jams are mouth watering, delish and addicting. I had the pulled pork meal with bbq beans, mash potatoes they have their own smokehouse on site as well for the dessert banana pudding is unforgettable, among the best ever. Lots of parking spaces available.  Im from the deep south (miami, FL)  & we have some pretty good bbq places (Shorties, Cracker Barrel, etc) but Loveless tops them all.

Perfect. I don't think anything could be better then breakfast Loveless. The wait may suck, you have to have most, if not all, of your party with you and then still wait 30+ minutes no matter the time of day. But with the gift shops and everything around it really is not too bad. Perfect pit stop if you are just coming through and tired of eating at Cracker Barrel.

Cute place and a must see if you're visiting the area in my opinion. It seemed like everywhere we went someone mentioned we should visit there. The kitchen store part had a lot of cutesy gifts that weren't overly cheesy which was nice. I got the pulled pork omelette my oh my was it rich but interesting and tasty! Pro tip - if you like sweet grits ask for the sorghum and pour it in your grits. So delicious! Went on a Tuesday afternoon around 1 and didn't have reservations. They said it was a good time where they weren't as busy and could take walk-ins.
Lots of good food and great service.  Had eggs, ham, pancakes and casserole .  All good !

Best breakfast I've had in a long time! First off...I wish I could remember the name of our waiter (tall guy with strawberry blonde hair-you know who you are!), because he was WONDERFUL and definitely made our experience even more enjoyable! 
The biscuits were to die for...Melt in your mouth! And the jams were delectable!
The waiter was amazing at giving suggestions! He led us all in the right direction based on what we were hungry for! 
The restaurant was so clean and well kept - but still had that historical charm to it. 
Loved every minute of my experience here! It truly felt as though I was having a meal with one big family

This place is to die for. Biscuits are just wonderful with their heavenly preserve. Also, they have brisket on Sunday. If you are there on Sunday, get it, or make a point to go on Sunday. Thank me later after your mouth dances with great meaty tasty brisket.

Reviewing this mostly as a music venue: This is one of those reviews that it's kind of painful to look at that two stars, but I'll try to justify it since there's no 2.4 star option.

Valet parking - despise it, despise it more when it takes forever in the freezing cold because of a valet issue, which it did after the show.

Friends bought us tickets to see a show there. We had front-table seats,  this should have been great. Unfortunately the assigned seating up there meant I spent the time faced almost completely away from the performers. I was jammed next to a couple I didn't know, had very little space behind me, so turning my chair was not particularly a feasible option. Very little room behind or to the sides.

I took a break from looking at the stage after a while because my neck hurt so much from craning it. I noticed there were plenty of free and open seats and tables, and the aisles they had constructed were huge so they could have given people a lot more space at the tables simply by not allowing 4 people to walk side by side in the aisles.

If we'd just had enough space to turn the chairs 90 degrees in the viewing situation would have been pleasant. We were packed in the sardine fashion, which was absurd because there were plenty of free tables.

Got up a couple of times to hit the restroom, just stayed standing off at the side of the stage until I felt like getting into the table pit again.

The food was alternately great and just ok, but the prices for everything were on the pricey side. I'll remind I was there for the performance, not for the food. My neck, back, and ears were annoyed by nearly everything at about five songs in.

Basically a slightly layout change to the tables would solve most of it, open seating after a certain point would have been nice, ability to get the car parked and unparked sans valet would be great.

By the time I left I was in a mood. For a music venue they could be so great, but it's just not set up for that and the way they have the up front seating. It was a very expensive, neck pain inducing night.

Maybe I should just say I'm old, this music venue made me grumpy. Get off my lawn. Food was tasty though. Not on my lawn!
AMAZING!!  The meatloaf and smoked turkey are sublime!  Let's not even get started on the biscuits and jams.

I was visiting Nashville with my boyfriend and we was told this was the place to go to! We went and put in our names, we ended up waiting 2 hours to even get seated. Once we WERE seated, our waitress, I believe her name was Skye, kept giving up glares the entire time we were being waited on. Did not seem very friendly at all towards us and we did not understand why as to she was being very well to the tables surrounding us. The food however was pretty good.. not sure if it was 2 hour waiting worthy, but it was decent. VERY largely portioned. I order the Music City Platter and everything was great except the ham is VERY salty.

I can't figure out what they are.  Is it a bar mainly?  Or Are they a 50's diner?  They have the decor but doesn't seem kid friendly or have shakes or malts etc and the menu has no real theme - kind of a hodgepodge and I don't recall seeing appetizer options but I could have missed that.  We were there for lunch.  One side of menu is all alcoholic drinks, martinis etc which doesn't rally seem to go with the 50's diner motif.  The acoustics are very bad and was hard to hear the person sitting next to me (and there was no live music etc).  As for food Onion rings were very salty.  Burger was average.  The chili frito pie lacked meat and was reheated but not all the way through even.  . It was also a small portion for $14 but that didn't matter since we didn't eat due to lack of flavor and temp.  The waitress did remove the charge from the bill so I will give them thumbs up for trying to keep us happy.  Am posting this mainly so Mgmt will see it and help them improve.  Would love to see them succeed and maybe the rooftop will do well when weather is nicer.  It's a great location - was hoping it could be someplace we could stop on way to Preds games with the family but not so sure unless some changes made.

While the music was great and that was what we were there for, the service is horrible to non-existent. This was my second visit, I've never been served worse food anywhere, twice! This venue is way overpriced on food & drink. I don't think anyone that works here cares about how this place runs. Food is a total mess. The seating is very misleading. Our VIP seats were NOT elevated as shown &  they were behind a barrier a short person (myself) would be unable to see over. Music is great, but, I repeat, the food is bad and shockingly overpriced. Eat before you come.

One of our Nashville favorites. When company visits, we like to take them here. Their homemade biscuits and jam are out of this world. The shops are fun and cute. And you will have time to shop because the wait is usually 1-2 hours. But it is worth the wait. We usually leave for Loveless Cafe before we are actually hungry.

I'd give zero stars if I could. 

First time here and it will be my last. Very low customer to server ratio but it still took over 30 minute to receive our pretzel app.  Beer cheese tasteless and my biergarten burger is like biting into a 1/4lb ground beef with zero flavor and very dense texture. 

Server was atrocious - did not offer condiments, drink refills and when given an empty pepper grinder, he ran off to refill it in the kitchen. I grabbed one off a nearby table so I could finally start lunch after waiting so long for it to come out of the kitchen.

My boyfriend and I loved this restaurant.   We had a wonderful experience. Nathan behind the bar was great!!!!   Morgan helped us get tickets to see a show and was a pleasure.  Hope to return to Nashville and visit again.

Would've given a half star if it was available.  This was the worst place ever!  Schnitzel was awful, you did not come with German potato salad or slaw it come with some buttery noodles that were just nasty.    I would never recommend this place to anyone.   If you are wanting German food in Nashville go to the Gerst house!
This place is so awesome. The food, the service, the warm employees make it perfect. Take the drive from downtown and eat here.
Large portions of made from scratch perfect comfort food with biscuits.  Enough said...

So there are those "spots" in Nashville. You know, the ones that ALL the tourists know about before they get here? And HAVE to go to in order to get an "authentic" Nashville experience. This is most certainly one of those spots. I can't tell you how many times I've been out and heard tourists talk about how they have brunch plans at Loveless the next day. 

Most of those "tourist" spots don't get high star ratings from me. They usually evolve with the rise in tourism and then loose their special local flair. This is not one of those places. I grew up about three minutes down the road from Loveless. I can't remember the first time I came here, because I was so young. But I do remember the motions. The delicious biscuits and crunchy fried chicken, the walk to the back of the property to look at the bicycle shop, and then over to the country cafe to buy some rock candy and a biscuit mix.

This place is Nashville. Its out in the middle of no where (Transplants and tourists.....you'll have to drive away from downtown). It's authentic, unique and special. The menu is simple for GOOD. The drinks are simple but GOOD. And the experience is actually and experience. 

Go there early. Play some yard games. Look at all the LEGENDS pictures that have dined there. Buy some freaking rock candy at the store. And do yourself a favor and get the biscuit mix. It might not be as good as they are at Loveless. But when your back at your non Nashville home....you'll crave a Loveless biscuit.

Southern cooking at its best!!!  Not sure how anyone would rate this place less than a 5-Star visit.  Food is great, atmosphere is great, and service was great.  Biscuits Biscuits Biscuits!!!  That is all I need to say, and don't forget the jelly.  I think I ordered almost everything on the menu because I couldn't decide what I wanted and everything looked good.  Great place for a tourist to stop by.

Very, very small... dark... FANTASTIC venue for live music... after you've browsed the used records upstairs at Grimey's. I paid just a few bucks to get in The Basement, bought a beer from a cooler tap, sat down 3 ft from where three outstanding, never-heard-before, blues bands played back to back. One was from Australia, the other two... were not. All three were remarkable. Don't miss a chance to check out this venue when you're in Nashville.
The food was fresh, delicious with a great atmosphere and rich history.  The biscuits are the best around

Wow, what an experience! The hostess, Rebeccah made me feel at home from the moment I arrived. The beer selection was amazing, almost overwhelming. Thankfully the bartender was very knowledgeable in helping satiate my thirsty palate. After a handful of beers, it came time to choose food from the expansive menu. I settled on the patty melt, and was blown away! The meat was expertly seasoned and grilled to a perfect mid-rare. All in all, Fat Kat's was a great experience, and I will be returning for sure.

Made reservations for 4 people one month in advance because I heard it gets booked really fast. It was easy enough to book the reservation online for my trip to Nashville. Heard it was a famous place to go for delicious food. If you're staying in Nashville, be prepared as it's about 25-30 minutes away. Staff was friendly and helpful.

Had a delicious strawberry cocktail and fried chicken for dinner. It was fantastic fried chicken but I feel like I can get really good fried chicken anywhere in Nashville. You get to pick 2 sides and the menu says they are handmade every morning. The cucumbers and onions were good. The mac and cheese was just ok. A friend's meal came out cold but the server fixed it right away with a fresh plate of food. They served us fresh, homemade biscuits to start and they were good. Again, nothing  so spectacular that you can't get in many other restaurants. 

I guess it's cool to visit/see if you really want to, but don't feel bad if you can't get there.

Stopped in to see what the talk was all about. I used to come in here when it was the pour house. I will tell you, the remodel, upgrade, stage and whole new vibe and atmosphere is fantastic! I can't wait to come back and hear some music and hang out.

This is a staged reality of a Bierhaus or real German restaurant. It's okay, and could be good, but tourism and the cheapness filter of Nashville have made it for the most part an overpriced, under-portioned mush palace. Nothing on the menu is exceptional or daring, and the desserts are pre-made and microwaved. Perfect for idiot tourists looking to hemorrhage money, in lieu of a quality human experience with loved ones.

Are you new here?  Are you of German descent?  Do you like beer?  Do you like great food and fun music?  If you said yes to any of the above, then this is the place for you!  My husband and I were at the Bierhaus last night for a Yelp Elite event but decided to go early to eat dinner as my husband LOVES beer, we're new here to the Nashville area and I'm of German descent (none of which matters btw).  We wanted to check it out prior to the event and let me tell you we weren't disappointed.  This place is incredible!  From the owners (thanks Bob), to the management (thanks Joe), to the servers and bartenders (thanks Joey) to the bands playing, you will think you're in Munich and will certainly meet people and have a great time.  But I digress... We arrived around 5 pm and there was ample parking (it's at the Opry Mills Mall, BUT not inside the mall).  We walked in and immediately found a place at the bar.  Noticed the liters of beer, the folks with their own steins, the live music and thought, yeah, this place is cool.  Joey the bartender immediately waited on us and my husband got his liter (happy boy brings me joy) and I got my Jägerschnitzel with a side of spaetzle (like a German noodle).  The pork was pounded thin with a nice breading, but the gravy made the dish.  It was deep, dark, mushroomy (that is now a word) and herby.  It might be a tad too much if the pork is covered in it, so I got it on the side.  My husband said the gravy alone could be a meal and I'd have to agree.  The spaetzle was light and fluffy, with a slight buttery taste, which also went great with the gravy. My husband then ordered a pretzel, as he's never hungry until I start eating.  OMG it was ridiculously massive, chewy, salty, and GONE!  It comes with a sweet mustard (which is typical German), but we love the hot/spicy mustard, which is already on the bar.  There is a full bar by the way, so if beer is not your thing, they have you covered.  Also, if German doesn't sound good, they have hamburgers, fish and chips and sandwiches, but when in Rome...or Munich...as they say...  They also have pretzel bread pudding, yes, you heard me, PRETZEL BREAD PUDDING!  You need this in your life...salty yet sweet and oh so decadent!  Trust me, you will want to save room.  Onto the dining area, which is a replica of an authentic German beer hall.  Communal benches and lots of room, with live music and people having a great time.  The chants from the band "who wants beer" and the crowd answering in delight "we want beer!"  But wait, there is a large group holding a ski-like board and taking beer shots at the same time?!  I'm in bar heaven!  Or is this a college flashback??  This is MY kind of place!  They have stein lockers!  Yes, you can purchase a stein locker to keep your stein locked up and safe until your next visit.  What more could they offer??  Open Table reservations, brewery tours, birthday parties, private room, dance parties, senior discounts, etc.  It goes on and on and on!  Honestly folks, this place is incredible!  Please come visit and make a few friends, drink some beer, eat great food and dance/sing to your hearts content.  Oh, and don't forget your lederhosen...you get a discount for that too!

My husband and I were in Nashville and this was about 30 minutes from our hotel. We had to check it out after all the great reviews and it didn't disappoint. The food, coffee, and the service was excellent! The biscuits were the best we've ever had. You get a plate of them for the table while you're looking over the menu and they are served with 3 different preserves. The blackberry was our favorite. My husband ordered the Pit-Cooked Pork bbq and two eggs. It's served over two pancakes and comes with a side, he chose grits, which he said were amazing and also more biscuits. It was $13.99 which is more then we typically spend for a breakfast entree but he said it was absolutely delicious. It was so much food he got a to go box and ate the rest later! I got an omelet which also is served with biscuits. It was $7.49. Needless to say we left with a to go box of biscuits! Right next door they have a little market called Hams & Jams and they also have a gift shop. That was fun to walk through when we were finished eating. Next time we are in town we will definitely go back!

20 minute drive, 1 hour 45 minute wait time. SO worth it. Came hungry, got hungrier and could've been rolled out afterwards. I tried the Pulled BBQ and Eggs, the rest of the table got the Brisket special. So much food! You could definitely share a plate. Amazing BBQ sauce and preserves for the biscuits.

Decent. Beer is solid, got some big ones too. It's a bit hokey pokey, its German themed if you like that. met a guy from Germany and brought us our beers and food. He explained everything and was pleasant. We live about 25 minutes north, so we come down to the area to try things out. I'd be back again. We had snitzel chicken with gravy. Good stuff.

This place by far exceeded my expectations!  The area where the restaurant is at also has a gift shop,  meat market, catering venue, walk up BBQ it's like it's own little town. We were greeted and seated pretty fast considering how busy they were. The waitress that helped us was so very friendly and had great recommendations not only about the menu but also about places we should visit while we were in town. The homemade biscuits and jams they bring for an appetizer were delicious, I had to stop myself from eating them so I would have room in my belly for my meal. The moonshine lemonade was mmm mmmm yummy. I had the pork chops, sweet potatoes with creamed corn oh sweet Jesus I cannot put into words how delicious it all was. This place is definitely worth the nice drive out.

We've been going to Loveless Cafe for about five years and have always ordered the breakfast. On our last trip We decided to try the other fare. I had the breaded pork chops, one of my favorite dishes, with Mac and cheese and mashed potatoes. My wife ordered the BLT sandwich with American cheese. We also ordered the fried green tomatoes as an appetizer. 

The green tomatoes were excellent. The rest of the dinner was so bad we couldn't eat it. The pork chops were so over cooked they were like shoe leather. The mash potatoes had so much white pepper they were hit. The Mac and cheese was tasteless. 

My wife's BLT was cold and the cheese was hard and dry, not even melted.  Oh well nothing ever stays the same. I could see if one item was off or bad , but two entire meals were not eatable. No need to return to this place. They do just fine without our business.

Several people recommended to us including the guide at Adventure Works just down the road.  Our waitress Megan was great and patiently answered all of our questions about the different dishes they are known for.  Everything we had there was amazing!!!  Would definitely go there again if we return to Nashville!

Pretty cozy place to eat. The staff is great and inviting. They give each table biscuits and some homemade jam to try out. I had the country fried steak with hash brown casserole and fresh fruit. The steak was made well because the meat as well as the batter were seasoned well. Didn't really like the hash brown casserole because it was too cheesy. Kenny, our server, kept checking back with us, which I appreciate. All in all, a quaint place to have a meal at.

Was told this is the place for fried chicken and biscuits while in Nashville. Biscuits are heaven!!!! So good. Mac and cheese was lacking. Fried chicken was good but mine was a little too crispy around the edges and did have a touch of the burnt oil taste to it. But ........ we did eat at about 7pm or so as well.

Very nice restaurant with friendly staff. Food was very appetizing. Live music was entertaining. Oh, beer if you want some. They tapped a keg while we were there and everyone that wanted a free beer got in line and you also got to keep the glass mug, offer good until the keg went dry. 

Located in very nice mall (Opry Mill).
Awesome place with fantastic food, servers and music. Going again tonight.  The sausage triple platter is especially good.

Service was great, since I have access to several Gern cooks, and spent 12 years living there this was good. John our waiter good.  The best part that goes with the meal was the music from the "Euro Expres" band made the meal taste even better.  I was back in Germany!

The first time I've felt that anyplace was worth the hour and half wait to get in. There wasn't a single thing on our plates that wasn't delicious. Service is top notch, and even management chips in to make sure everything is running smoothly.
Excellent! Most friendly service, authentic German traditions, delicious food and beer straight from Germany! Love it!

Fat Kat Slims is pretty average, kinda pricey for the quality of food the serve. I don't live in the area and I won't be back if I am. Nothing to write home about, service was awkward and kinda slow. Had a cool aesthetic but other than that not remarkable at all.

I've been to Loveless about 4 times now and I've never been disappointed. The ambiance, the service and the comfort/Southern food is all great. I will emphasize the great service as every waiter/waitress I've ever had is extremely friendly and nice. The only downside is that due to the popularity get ready to wait about an hour and a half if you bravely decide to come for brunch on a weekend. Having said that, the wait is long on weekends they have outdoor games like corn hole and stores on the property which you can kill time browsing  the area.

Breakfast, lunch or dinner this place is good for any meal. The main draw is a big plate of homemade, warm biscuits they bring to your table with 3 or 4 different types of jam. I could just eat these biscuits and nothing else and be happy. 

Their fried chicken is one of the most popular things and my friends have gotten it and loved it but I actually have never ordered it. The reason is because I'm a big fan of their barbecue so I keep getting it over and over! Loveless has their own smokehouse which is something you can check out while you are waiting. The barbecue pulled pork is served over 2 "hoecakes" which is pretty much a cornbread pancake, then you get to pick from 2 sides. I've tried a lot of their sides and really you can't go wrong with any of them. I've been here for dinner before and they have dinner specials so one time I had the chickin & dumplins which is awesome as well. 

This is one of those places that if you're in Nashville for only a weekend you better check out and if you're a local you have to try at some point. Great place!
Better than the reviews say, if that's possible.  World class Southern fare.  Make this a stop when in Nashville

We've been wanting to go to this place since we moved to Nashville a year ago. And, it did not disappoint. The atmosphere is awesome. All the waitresses are dressed Bavarian style. The gift shop has really neat mugs and the typical beer boots. But the food was SO GOOD. We tried two different schnitzel's and the flight tasters of German beers. it was all amazing. A tad over priced, but still worth the visit.

One of the best restaurants that Nashville has to offer! I totally recommend the pull pork, fried chicken, and catfish. The place has a special to get 3 meats and 2 sides for $16. Portions are more than enough with tons of delicious sides to choose from like the hashbrown chessy casserole and cream corn. Make sure you save enough room for the endless melt in your mouth fluffy biscuits and warm peach cobbler for dessert! 

Can't wait to go back  =D

I don't get it.
I don't get it all.
The biscuits are BLAH boys.
The cheesy hashbrowns were epic.
Its a cool looking roadside place , but otherwise its average to poor for breakfast.
No love lost the Loveless.

Overall it's good that they're here for teens and young people.  Decent facilities and plenty of parking.  I don't like however that if you drive there to purchase advance tickets they still charge you the convenience fee you pay if you order online.  That's ridiculous!  I also don't like that they've compromised and book bands that are clearly in opposition to Christ.  Like I said, overall it's good they are in Nashville.  They bring in a lot of bands faithful to the Kingdom, and provide a good hangout for teens.

This place should be avoided at all costs for Mothers Day Brunch in the future.  1pm reservation we arrived for at 12:45pm. After 47 minutes of being shifted from line to line we were finally seated.  The selection of food rivaled a Shoneys buffet and the waitstaff were inattentive at best. Family of 4 paid $240 for what would have been better served for $50'at Cracker Barrel.   Manager said "yes, we need a new system because this happens every year and at Easter!"  Trust me when I say, there are better places for special occasion brunches like Mothers Day and Easter.  On a scale of 1-10 it registers a form 1 and that's only because the location at least was accurate.  Just a horrible Mothers Day brunch.

The Loveless is very popular. We bring people in from out of town all the time, as it seems everyone that visits has to go to the Loveless. For me, it is a bit pricey (supply and demand) and pretty average.

Starting out on the negative side, there is the wait. Pretty much all the time (late afternoon opens up a few more possibilities, but expect an hour or more at breakfast). This is due to the popularity with tourists. But they do have shops ringing the restaurant, so you can entertain yourself by taking a walk around the property. The main store is the one that sells their hams, preserves and biscuit mix. 

Once you are seated, you will want to figure out if you go for the all you can eat, which means you will sign up the table, or order individually. I think the all you can eat is only an option if you meet two conditions.

1. You are really hungry
2. You want to try a bit of everything

We have done it once and I would rather order a normal sized breakfast. 

Food? The biscuits are the draw, although I thought they were better when the biscuit lady was still alive (Carole Fay Ellison passed in 2010 at too young of an age). They are still the draw at the Loveless and still good. I find the ham a bit too salty for my liking, but some really love the extra salty country ham. If that is you, they have you covered. I have a hankering for the pork chops myself, but that is because my wife and children are not big on pork chops, so this is my opportunity. I also like their omelets (if you want something a bit different, try the pulled pork omelet).

My one trip for lunch was family style with Fried Chicken and Catfish, neither of which is on my list of the best food (I make a bad southerner?), but I did find both tasty.

Overall, I just feel the place is a bit too hyped up. Still worth a visit and you might find the options even more spectacular than I do. For me, it is just average. Your mileage may vary.

Unfortunately, the valet most likely ruined my experience here.  For starters, there is NO parking available except for some abandoned buildings across the street from the rear of the winery. However, the valet claims to own ALL of these spots and was EXTREMELY rude and even aggressive towards our party for attempting to park.  The valet loudly threatened me that if I didn't try to park on the street he would call a tow truck while I was inside their restaurant. 
Seeing as how others in our party were waiting inside, (and at this point there was no way I would let the valet near my car) we had to park around the corner and leave the car in front of the Rescue Mission.  
When we got in, the bar staff was friendly and we ordered some drinks and appetizers.  We had the fries, the duck tacos, and something else I don't remember. The fries were not memorable, and the duck tacos might as well have been dry pulled pork because that was what it tasted like. 
We did not see a show there so I admit I cannot rate the music venue space.

Let's talk parking: valet cost $5. The only free parking is located to the left of the valet lines. There are about 4 spots that don't have "no parking - tow zone" signs above them along the chain link fence. The other spots clearly state you will be towed. The valet told my friend it was okay to park there despite the signs and she wasn't towed, but it's rather confusing on your first visit.

F&B: pricy. Drinks & appetizers run about $10 a price. Entrees are $15+. For ballers on a budget, this won't be a regular stop. 

I went with the cocktail described by the waiter as the strongest available: Tri-Spritz. It did not disappoint in flavor or alcohol %.

I also couldn't resist the truffle fries that were of course uber delicious.


3 stars for lame parking; food was 4 stars.
Great atmosphere, service, and food. Visiting from NM and decided to stop in. Worth the stop!! Be prepared to eat when you go in!  Biscuits prior to your meal will keep you going back for more!!!
Went to fat Kat Slim's tonight. Had a great time. Great food. Great service!  Huge chicken fingers!!!! Definitely check out the specialty cocktail list they know what they're doing!!!

They have lost their edge...no longer special, alright but nothing to write home about.

They have a system to maximize profit and that rather than charm and service trump customer happiness.

The regular employees try to tone down the eagerness of the summer student workers and seem to enjoy watching people wait...

Chicken fried steak was more grease and batter than steak...heating pie was done in a micro wave, nothing country about a micro wave.

Their beer selection is pretty weak...not having micro brews is a micro aggression.

Poor service here. Make sure you check your bill as the bartenders add drinks you didn't have. The bartender was confrontational and cussed at us when we asked about charges . Music sucks there as well. VERY Loud to cover poor voice. Wil NEVER go here on next trip to Nashville

Hands down the BEST biscuit I've ever tasted!!!  This place is wonderful!  From the gifts shops to the atmosphere of the restaurant. You will enjoy every minute you spend here and also enjoy your meal!  Staff is friendly and incredibly accommodating!!  I hope you enjoy as much as I did!!!

Classic southern comfort food. I had their fried chicken with mashed potatoes and gravy as well as macaroni and cheese. The country ham is excellent too. Almost all of their menu items are homemade and you can tell. They're famous for their biscuits and preserves! They are usually very, very busy, so definitely be sure to plan your visit. I don't recommend coming on a Sunday unless you're prepared for a long wait. The best time is around 5 PM on a weeknight right before the afternoon rush! Great service as well.

City Winery has a great atmosphere. One of the most unique one in the city of Nashville. They have a fully stocked bar that stock themselves. The venue is small so there's a close knit atmosphere. The food while slightly overpriced was good and well seasoned. The waiters were attentive as well. The music was nice. MoonChild was a good group. They had the venue staying on there feet for them. It was a great concert experience.

I visited City Winery while visiting Nashville.  I looked up the winery and was hoping to see a show as well, but they were sold out!  Upon arrival, we were greeted by the hostess and seated at a great table in the middle of the winery.  I loved the industrial space and the decor was made you feel comfortable.  

Our waitstaff-Peter was so knowledgeable and friendly.  I decided to start off with a flight of wines - that cost $20 - this was a good choice.  I had two whites and two reds.  My favorite was the Pinot Noir. 

Food - We decided to try the: Margeherita Flatbread; Calamari; Pulled Lamb Sandwich; Potato salad and seasoned fries.  Everything was good except the Calamari.  I explained my thoughts about the dish and the item was removed from the bill.  

City Winery is a great place for a group; date night or a special occasion.  If I lived in the area-this would be my go-to-spot for sure!

First off we were seated with another nice couple whom we never met before at the same table.  Wasn't what we expected but ok it Christmas no need to be that way.  Then first course arrived.  There was 6 small pieces of pickled red and orange colored beets.  All less than 1/2" in general size strong vinegar on them. Like not diluted at all. Then a chunk of cheese in the middle on top of about 10 small blades of fancy lettuce. Also the lettuce was a bit soggy. There was on chunk of cheese in the middle on top of the lettuce.  Tasty little piece of cheese. It was less than 2" in diameter.  We were supposed to divide this into 4 portions between me and 3 other persons.  First off it was extremely awkward to take and try to divide such a small portion for a Christmas meal that cost $35 each person.  Food wasn't cooked properly, potatoes raw in middle and waitress was so rude when I asked for more salad.  She said "That wasn't enough for you?"   Anyway we tried to eat the food and not be completely angry for her treatment, dry turkey, cold food and pushy rude behavior.  Food was slop not fit to eat and I showed the manager the potatoes in a napkin infront of several people going directly to her. I wasn't going to pay for that crap.  They were busy and several seen how I was disappointed.  Never again going there. Save your money.

First, I want to start by saying that before I write a review I give establishments ample visits to earn the rating. I've now been to City Winery 3 times and remain less than impressed.

SERVICE: The service at City Winery is either on overdrive and in your face or non existent and there doesn't seem to be a happy medium. During my last visit to City Winery on Friday (upstairs in the "lounge") our waiter asked for our drink orders and food orders at the same time. Our food came out first, after about 20 min (without even water on the table) and then about 10 min later, we got our drinks. Also, on a previous visit I was denied a taste of one of CW's on-tap wines because the bar was "too busy". 

PRICE: Pricing for shows is competitive. 

PARKING: Valet - I've been charged $5 sometimes then they didn't collect payment another time..not sure what the deal is, but they never seem to have enough attendants working for when a show that seats a few hundred lets out at one time.

FOOD: The food is tasty, nothing extraordinary, especially with the great food scene in this city. A little pricy.

SEATING: Unless you buy seats at an entire table you'll be sitting with strangers, which can be fun, but not when you're literally rubbing elbows with them. The tables are tiny and wayyyy to small to seat strangers together. Also, it's a bummer that you have to buy a seat - City Winery is more about selling the "experience" than a ticket to a great show. Also, you're SOL if you have more people in your group than a table can accommodate, so I would be very hesitant to say this place is group friendly. 

Overall, Nashville has such wonderful, unique and historic venues (lookin at you Ryman, Marathon Music Works, War Memorial Auditorium) that I'm not really sure how or why City Winery has a place here. I would much rather go to a show at any of these other venues or a laundry list of others not mentioned before coming to CW. 

In short, go back to New York. However, I'll likely return because they book great shows.

There was no way we were coming to Nashville and not coming to Loveless Cafe. I'm so glad we did! But I wasn't blown away by the food or the biscuits. Yes, they were good - but really just barely if I'm being completely honest. Did we get a bad batch? Not sure but we had them out before our meal (a bit too crisp at the bottom but not exactly burnt) and we ordered biscuits and gravy and neither version was very impressive. I mean it doesn't help that both my girlfriend and I are pretty awesome cooks/bakers so when dining out it sometimes takes a lot to really impress us as we can make most all of this stuff better ourselves.

I did however love the hash-brown casserole, now that was somethin'! and I will be recreating this at home, thank you very much! I also adore jam, like make homemade jam of all sorts myself but I wasn't impressed with any of the jams either.

We shared a large platter breakfast plate with french toast, eggs over med, bacon/sausage mix and hash-brown casserole that was all tasty but again nothing stand out about it in any way.

So I'll say this place is probably a bit of nostalgia mixed with yes, you should definitely get there but it's probably one of those one and done or when you're in town you go type places but by zero stretch of the imagination one of the best biscuits, breakfasts' or meals you'll ever have type place. Just down home, get the job done type place.

Do not, not order the hash-brown casserole though ;) that would be a big no, no. It's delish!
Worth the wait time! Biscuits yummy!! Homemade preserves delicious. Watermelon ribs excellent!!! Best ribs ever!!!! Must go asap.

Biscuits galore! What a cool little compound. Had a bit of a wait for breakfast, so we meandered around from shop to shop for about 45 minutes. We were seated, served and had paid the check in probably less time than we waited, but when we rated our favorite meals from our time in Nashville, Loveless and Farm House were definitely the top two (though we couldn't decide which was our fave).

Excellent night listening to Jesse Cook. Had good seats but across table and they switched them for us very easily and with a smile. Had great staff, Shanning, waiting on us. Made the night even better. 

Great place and in my list for many reasons, most especially that performers like Jesse would never come to Nashville without your venue.

For the ultimate southern food experience, this is the place! We had a 30-minute wait, but it went by quick as we walked around the grounds and peaked in to the simple shops there. And the wait was totally well worth it.

Everything we had was awesome! At our table, we got the cat fish (essentially, fish and chips), the chicken tenders (which were more like chicken filets) and the pork chops (while two pork chops would have suffice, there were three). The servings were gigantic, not to mention 2 sides each, and we definitely SHOULD HAVE split just a couple of dishes, but we wanted to try so many things that getting several items was essential! We all loved it all. No complaints. Everything tasted so good! I was completely satisfied and I feel like I got some true southern food exposure.

This place lives up to the hype. Definitely worth the effort and whatever wait is required!

Dear Loveless Cafe,

My new husband and I ventured into your establishment late Wednesday afternoon to have some lunch after horseback riding.  We are visiting Nashville on our honeymoon and were told that Loveless was a place that we must stop.  While we enjoyed the nostalgia and the staff, we were disappointed.  The food was not that great.  Matt ordered the blt with fried green tomatoes and I got the chicken hands as our waiter called them.  The best thing about our whole meal was the squash casserole.  My chicken was bland and dry and matts blt was nothing better than what I could have made for him at home. What was most disappointing was going to both gift shops and seeing every little trinket from coffee mugs to quirky ornaments was made in China. When your company is representing Americana....it is a shame and a poor trust in your country to not produce in America.  So sad that this piece of American history chose to commercialize in this way.  Then hidden back in a corner and under advertised was the shop that held the true treasures, Tennessee local artists!  You company should highlight these people...they are what make your establishment what it is.  Being that you are locally owned, you should completely understand this market.  Overall, when we come back to Tennessee, I doubt we will come back to Loveless or recommend it to our friends and family.  Once was enough for us.

I stopped in this location for a quick late night wine flight. The bartender was very friendly and the wine was good. The venue is beautiful like the others. They allowed us to check out the event space even though they had a concert going. It looked amazing. The upper balcony was a great viewing area. This visit, along with the other City Winery locations I have visited, was outstanding. You can tell there is a quality standard within the brand and it is maintained very well throughout.

We had a large goup of 12 and we were seated fairly quickly for such a large group.  Food was fantastic. Service was great. I had the chicken and waffles. They were very tasty. The biscuits were very yummy too.

3 star on food.
3 star on service.
4 star on wine.
4 star on ambiance.

I've been to city winery a few times for work events. The space is great for large crowds. But this was my first time having dinner there. 

I was a bit hesitant based on the reviews but everyone has their preference.. We made reservations for Sunday this Labor Day weekend and there were several spots. 

We sat immediate after paying 5 bucks to self park. Drink offers and apps were taken pretty quick. But when getting our check it took awhile once food was out and we were done

The cheese plate and mussels were sub par.. There are many places in town with a much better taste and display.. It was poor cheese selection that I could have gotten at the Kroger cheese isle.  

My wife had the salmon that was perfectly cooked but lacked taste.. It was very bland. I was surprisingly pleased with the burger. Well cooked and wasn't bland so  thumbs up to one dish being good. 

The wine I thought was pretty good. We ordered a flight of reds and all were .

With all that and a 95 dollar tab tip not included.. It isn't worth a 2nd try.. Maybe a stop for a glass of wine but there are many other places with free parking and not as hidden to get to.

We came for Brunch. Was disappointed the only parking options were pay to park at $10/2hrs or valet. The restaurant was pretty empty at 11a for a Saturday and the service was slow..
