BUT the waitress was so nice and the food was worth it! The gravy was amazing...  You will not be disappointed. I was sad when my food was gone.

This place was awesome! Super great venue if you're looking to get a little variety and want to hear each individual artist, rather than just the cover bands on the strip. The venue is small, but intimate. Definitely more of a young, hipster-y place. 

Go on Tuesday Nights! It's free "New Faces" night! You never know quite what you're gonna get!

I really really great food and beer!! It was however EXTREMELY loud and we asked to be seated away from the stage. I should have expected live music being a Saturday night, but it was so loud that we couldn't hear our waitress and she couldn't hear us. I couldn't talk to my friends, only lip read. After being moved to the other side of the restaurant, it was still loud but it was at least tolerable!
Our waitress was very friendly and knowledgeable! The beer was cold and refreshing! The food I just can't get enough of. I'm of German descent and this was very rich, authentic, comfort food, just like home cooking. I wanted to take pictures but I completely forgot when our mouth watering dishes were placed in front of us!
I highly recommend Bavarian Bierhaus for a fun atmosphere and DELICIOUS food and beer! Just ask to be seated away from the stage if you want to have any conversation.
Great atmosphere and instantly reminded my husband if his time in Germany. Live music is a huge plus.

So, my husband is first generation American with two *VERY* German parents, and a very German family, in general. We spent a few weeks last October traveling around Europe, including several days in Munich. We frequented many a beer hall (including the infamous Hofbräuhaus, which is essentially what Bavarian Bierhaus is going for), so we were excited (read: hopeful) to try this place!

Large open room atmosphere, great German decorations - loved the hops hanging from the chandeliers, as I remember seeing that in many restaurants in Munich - totally took me back! Bench seating, but they don't seat you with strangers, which honestly was part of the fun of the beer halls in Germany, but I get that we as Americans aren't generally used to that, lol. 

Service was nice, and menu was exciting - we saw several dishes we recognized from both my German mother in law's kitchen, and from our time in Germany. We ordered a pretzel and some bier cheese - the cheese is worth it! Really tasty. We also ordered two .5 L dunkel's, which were lovely and definitely tasted as they did in Munich.

I had intended to order the jägerschnitzel, as it's one of my favorite German dishes, but chickened out at the last minute, because I was terrified they wouldn't do it justice - especially the spätzle, haha. I was right to avoid it, but more on that later...I opted for the brats in a blanket, and my husband ordered the wurst plate, with a weisswurst and Oktoberfest brat, sauerkraut, and spätzle.

Food comes out, and my brats in a blanket are...hard. Overcooked for sure. The smoked brats had decent flavor, but just way overcooked. Fries were good, though! I dipped them in leftover bier cheese, totally recommend. My husband's reports on the wurst plate - weisswurst had basically zero flavor, very bland, but the Oktoberfest brat was good. Sauerkraut was sauerkraut, yay! 

Now, about the spätzle...it's from a package. Hands down. Like, the kind you can buy in the international section of your local Kroger. If you've ever had real spätzle, it's almost like a German dumpling and a noodle had a baby - they should be slightly dense, buttery, salty, and delicious. These tasted like...rubbery eggs. Really, really disappointing. I get that they're feeding the masses here but I make it at home from my mother in law's recipe and it's so simple to prepare, and 100x more delicious than the freeze dried stuff they're serving here. 

So...in conclusion. Come here for beers and a pretzel. Entree food was mediocre, at best. Service was great and prices were high, but eh, that's Opry Mills for ya. I might come back for that apple strudel, though...!

This is a must go. It's about 30 min outside of nashville but absolutely worth the drive. The service was spectacular from the hostesses to the servers and even the bakers making the biscuits (you can even watch them do it!). The portion sizes are perfect. Not too big and not too small. I got the country fried steak and a side of the hash brown casserole. The casserole was insanely good. You must get it if you go!

I rarely give a restaurant five stars, but Loveless Café earns it. I do my share of traveling and this is hands-down the best breakfast in the United States, especially if you like southern cooking. Once you check put the strawberry, BlackBerry, and peach jam on your biscuits you will be hooked. The hash brown casserole is wonderful as is the sausage gravy. Everything tasted so fresh Like breakfast should taste. You will want to get there early as we were told by the restaurant to arrive at 9:45 and there would be no wait. However when we got there at 9:40 it was already 40 minutes, but only took about 25 to get to our table. This is a great place out in the country and you will want to visit.
The olive oil cake tasted pretty good, but was extremely dry. The texture was  like cornbread. overall not a good experience.. On the plus side the drink pour was more generous,

My friend recommended me to this spot and I was happy that she did.  I was a little surprised at the wait time of an hour, but there was plenty to do walking around the grounds.  When we got seated, the staff was hustling and bustling.  As I looked around to the full dining room, everyone seemed so happy.  That is what good food will do.  I had the sampler with hot fried chicken, pulled pork, and catfish.  So good, every bite was top notch.  I watched them making the biscuits in the back and frying up the chickens across the way.  It is worth the hype, just try to be patient, your belly with thank you, your cardiologist, not so much.

What's not to love, it's all the delicious biscuits you can eat. The country ham with redeye gravy is delicious. Ask the waiter for honey to go with your biscuits...fabulous. I think this place is a must see, 500,000 people a year visit, that kinda proves the point.

The service is top notch, and so is the coconut cream pie!

Visited with my family while visiting Nashville for the first time and I highly recommend stopping by ! We waited for an hour and a half but it was very worth the wait plus there's a lot to do while you wait they have cute little shops you can walk through and there is plenty of outside seating area to relax and enjoy the weather. The biscuits are just heavenly and the food was just amazing. I love the history and the workers were very kind . Overall great place highly recommend !!

The most famous restaurant in Nashville and rightfully so. Best biscuits in TN. There's always a crowd and well worth the wait. Come out Sunday for lunch when they have a special brisket special that's phenomenal. All the preserves go well with the biscuits

I wanted to hate this place and assumed it would just be another kitschy tourist trap in Opry Mills, but left liking the place. They have a nice selection of German beers and they are available in 0.3L, 0.5L, 1L. the beer prices, even by Nashville tourist standards were very high ($7.50 for a half liter, which is roughly a pint). I was excited to see currywurst on the menu having eaten it on the streets of Berlin and falling in love with it. While it was nowhere as good as what I had in Germany, it was certainly better than any I've tried in America and certainly better than The Pharmacy's sad attempt. I will certainly eat it again. The wife had a wurst on a roll with potato salad and said it was very good. Overall, a decent experience and, while overpriced, a nice addition to Opry Mills.

Got delivery through orderup. Dude was nice, no problems there. 

They didn't have our order so the poor guy had to wait (got our order about 1.5 hr after order time), but we figured 'hey! Our food will be super fresh!'  

Well, here is what was $18 and $12.
Refuse to take revs for 10 people. Total arrogance! Food is not best by far in Nashville. Try other places!

This is a MUST in Nashville. It's important to go into it knowing that it's all about the experience. If you go during a busy time, you will wait.  Even if you go early, you will wait... but it won't be as long. If you have a larger group, you will definitely wait. Don't be surprised or frustrated by this. If you're impatient, then don't try to eat here.

Go when the weather is nice so you can pass the wait time checking out the store, playing corn hole and wandering around the grounds. It's a bit of a drive, so go when you are in the mood to enjoy the drive to and fro.

The food is classic southern and will not disappoint. it it a little overpriced? Sure. But you're paying for the experience just as much as anything. You'll get delicious food, and it will be a large portion.  You will leave stuffed and happy.

Again. Know what you're getting into. You don't go here for a "quick bite." You make an outing of it and enjoy taking your time driving out in the country, socializing with those in your party or strangers who are also waiting on a table, and eating a delicious southern meal in a charming old building that has been a part of Nashville for years and year.

I've been here a few times but took my girlfriend here for the first time a few days ago.  We got there around 6:30 on a Thursday night and only had a few minutes wait.  Our server was very friendly as well.  I ordered a bbq sandwich with fried okra, and my gf ordered a three side plate.  She chose fried green tomatoes, hashbrown casserole and mac and cheese.  

We always sample each other's meals and everything was cooked perfectly.  My only complaint but it's a small one is that the bbq sandwich really needs more bbq.  Other than that, we enjoyed all of it.  We split the banana pudding after, then went in the various shops and got a few things to send to family for Christmas.  It's not expensive, it's great southern food cooked right, fast and good service, and of course they have their amazing biscuits.  I'm a huge fan of the Loveless Cafe and definitely recommend it.

So good we came back twice. Once for lunch and once for breakfast. From the service to the food to the collar greens my husband couldn't stop raving about. The ones he loved so much he ordered a side with his breakfast the next day. Special place, wonderful food with true southern hospitality.

We are in from out of town for the CMA Music Fest and this place was recommended by family that lives in the area.  The wait was over an hour, but that was because they were busy.  There are a few shops on the property that you can visit while you are waiting.  

The food was excellent.  The biscuits are great when they came out warm.  The preserves they served them with were all good.  I enjoyed the peach the best, but the wife enjoyed the blackberry the best.  

I am a big fan of country ham and theirs was great.  The omelette that my wife had looked good and was packed full of vegetables.   

The server was very friendly and made good suggestions without being pushy. 

If you are in the area and are willing to wait this is a recommend for me.  

One thing we saw on the menu but we did not do since there was only 2 of us was the family style all you can eat.  Looks like a good way for 4 or more people to eat all they want while paying the same price that a regular meal would cost each person.

I'm not sure if it's the hype or a staple in many travelers to do list, but waiting 1.5 hrs for some over priced biscuits is not high on my agenda. 
They have a neat set up where you can visit their store or play corn hole, but can't say I'll be visiting this place again. One and done.

Dropped into the City Winery for brunch and could have stayed the entire day. One if the coolest new places I have visited in some time. 

Firstly, the decor and ambiance is super! Even if your not a wine lover, this place has a rich, warm, homey feel that adds to the experience. 

There is an upstairs and a downstairs area for drinks and food. Both have outdoor patios that give you some great views of Nashville on sunny summer days. 

In addition, they have a concert venue that provides not only great entertainment, but seating that allows for food and wine during your show. Very cool!!

The staff was well versed in the wine and food selections. They were helpful but not pushy with any particular selections. 

We shared the Huevos Rancheros and Vegetable Frittata, both of which were delicious. 

The Frittatta was perfectly cooked and was very rich in flavor while not skimping on the vegetables. Likewise, the Huevos Rancheros was fantastic. Perfect blend of spices, black beans and egg. 

All this topped with a great Pinot..... Life was good this day!

10:30am on Friday had a twenty minute wait, but service was efficient and friendly once we were seated. French Toast was perfect, but no turkey bacon or turkey sausage available for those of us who don't eat swine. Just wish I had room for pie!

I came to this place exactly a week ago at the end of our stroll through Nashville. There was a 1-hour wait for my party of 8, which we didn't mind because the beautiful scenery outside and that warm humid breeze... and the fact that is place is a must-go-to when in Nashville.

The atmosphere is nice, the inside looks like a house converted to a restaurant so it does feel homey. We ordered the Family Style supper. We chose endless fried chicken, fried catfish, okra, fries & mac and cheese. 

I feel I must mention that the service (at least ours) was bad. Once we were seated and our drinks were brought to us, we didn't see our waiter again for about 15 minutes. You might think: "Because of the high volume, duh!" No, NO. We saw the other guy waiting on the table next to us go to them at least 8 times to ask if the food was good, if they needed something, if they wanted more drink. When our waiter was taking our order, a glass of water got spilled and he was completely unfazed by it. He didn't offer napkins or to call anyone to clean it up so of course we had to take care of that because it was going to be another almost 10 minutes before he graced us with his presence.

Finally after sitting there half hour with lions roaring in our bellies, the biscuits and jelly came out. They were the warmest, freshest, softest, scrumptious biscuits I've tasted in a long time. Break one in half, spread a little butter on it, some honey and then you can take a bite of heaven. 

Unfortunately for my waiters timing we were all still on our first biscuit when all the food came out. Give us at least 5 minutes w/ the biscuits please!?

The food was so good, you would have thought grandma was back there making the mac & cheese herself! Everything on the table was just right, it was helping us cope with our waiter's service

(This review was written about a year ago but I didn't publish it so instead of "exactly a week ago" it should be "almost exactly a year ago")

Overall (and probably very unpopular) review: 
not worth the hype

((Lunch/Dinner review - NOT breakfast))

Good: no wait when we went (late lunch); biscuits delivered right to the table with fresh spreads. They were warm and delicious, light and fluffy. Seriously good.  Our server was helpful but not overly attentive or pushy-perfect. She was prompt with our drinks and food delivery, a great server (sorry I can't remember her name!) And you will not miss with the pimento cheese bacon burger. Holy wow. The sweet potato side was super sweet but delicious. 

Meh: Meatloaf was lacking. We expected much, much more in a country restaurant setting. Cracker Barrel's is better (and cheaper) and that's not saying much. 

Bad: Old, stale French fries. Flavorless and half crunchy, half soggy. Asked specifically for new fries, extra crispy and fresh... was delivered the same blah fries, just double fried (old fries dunked a second time in the oil). 

I'm just glad there was not a wait. We would have been much more disappointed, I'm sure.

Heavenly!

Walking into this HUGE space was like walking into my happy place. It was a little commericial in the front, but the prices on the retail were slightly better than when you order from some place like GermanDeli.com, but way more than if you have access to a base commissary. We loved the walls of steins you see, but didn't try that program. 
We were seated quickly since we purposely came before the Saturday rush. Our waiter, Fatjon, was fantastic! He was prompt, courteous, and funny. 
Between 4 of us, we have all the traditional plates: jägerschnitzel, saurbraten, rouladen, and the giant pretzel (plus beer). It's rare that I don't have some sort of feedback about food, but I have not a single thing to say besides it was fabulous. The flavors were great, thick sauces, spot on preparation, and absolutely delicious! If I didn't know I was in a very Americanized place, I'd have definitely felt at home in German. 
Con: The cost is a little steep. It was $122 for the 4 of us, so I'll stick to making it mostly at home, but nevertheless...we'll be back!

Got the mediocre Country Ham. Hash brown casserole was good, have had better. Service was fine and biscuits were good, not amazing. The slice of Chess Pie was delicious. Really wanted to love this place more.

I have not seen a show here so can only speak on the dining experience. I took my mother there for her birthday to try some of the wines and share appetizers. You wouldn't think this would be such a let down. The food was a TERRIBLE let down. we first ordered a flatbread which was supposed to have parmesan, mushroom confit, red onion, apple butter, and red pepper olive oil. When it came out it also had some kind of greens on it....guessing collard. If you are going to put ingredients on a flatbed, you need to have it on the menu. Even though it took a long time to come out, it was still overly doughy with a strange bitterness taste. We sent that back immediately. 

While looking over the menu to find anything else to eat while we drank our overly priced wine, we thought maybe we would share a bottle of wine. The sommelier came over to us to go over some of them. You would think he would go into detail about a few wines, but instead asked a question or two of what we liked, pointed to a page for us to look over, and then pointed to the most expensive bottle of wine on the page. 

Still wanting to give it a chance, hoping that the flatbread was a fluke, we ordered the risotto balls (a recommendation by our server). They were BLAND. If you live in the south or are going to have a restaurant in the south, learn how to season your food! We heard the chef came from Holland House so I was really excited to see what it was about. Total Let down. I will NEVER go back. 

Another thing to mention is the LBTD tax (%15 added on to the wine on the tap) that they slip in there. There is small print on the menu letting you know this, but it is very small. 

I wouldn't even waste my time.

Unexpected disappointment!! We came in a big group so we were placed in a separate room with 2 long dining tables away from the restaurant. The air conditioning was on very cold and there was no ambiance. No greetings when we entered. The food had been pre-ordered. Not what we thought it would be. The meat was very dry. Couldn't tell the difference between pork and turkey. Sweet potatoes looked and tasted canned. The biscuits and green beans were the best. But overall sad to have this represent Nashville or Southern cooking. You've lost the spirit of why you became famous!

Glorious southern breakfast! This café/souvenir store/motel was a charming, kitschy stop on our vacation. They don't take reservations and were crazy busy on the morning we visited. Luckily, they give you a pager and you can ramble around the General store buildings while you're waiting. 

They serve all sorts of home-style Southern foods, but we were after breakfast. when they seat you, they bring you a plate of biscuits with fresh butter and jams, and keep refilling them all through breakfast. Delicious. Our table shared biscuits and gravy, which was on point, a wonderful and enormous chicken fried steak, and the best cheesy grits I've ever tasted. The ham with red eye gravy was authentically salty. Service is swift and friendly. 

While it seemed a little touristy, so did everything else in Nashville. We'd definitely go again.

If you're a savvy traveler, you would have already seen Loveless cafe on all the top lists "What to do" and "What not to miss" in Nashville. With so much publicity and fame, you would have thought this place to be a tourist trap. CONTRARY. It is the most "homey" and welcoming atmosphere! PLUS their food is OUT OF THIS WORLD. Fried chicken for breakfast? While a norm in Nashville, Loveless' take is far from the norm. THIS IS A MUST.

Paid a visit for breakfast and I was stuffed after the biscuits! The biscuits are absolutely amazing along with their spreads. I highly recommend visiting if the opportunity presents. Staff was incredibly friendly, family friendly and fun environment. Shopping also on property.

Based on the reviews, I was expecting something good. Sadly, it was not. It felt like a touristy chain restaurant with Americanized German food.

The giant pretzel did not seem fresh (and I know a fresh handmade pretzel can be delicious), and the beer cheese dip was flavorless. (I think they just used the beer cheese soup as the dip.) The sausages were fine - nothing special. The best thing I ate was the red cabbage, which was pretty good. The whipped mashed potatoes appeared to be instant potatoes. The potato dumpling was rubbery and for some mysterious reason had a crouton hidden in the middle (which is apparently a traditional thing?).

Service was fine, no complaints there. Space was huge and seemed to be clean and orderly. Prices were moderate, but the food was not worth it.

I wanted to like it and wish I could have better things to say, but I was totally unimpressed. :(

Good food. Good service. Maybe expected more from having almost a 2 hour wait. Really anticipated to be wowed. 
Typical southern food. My gf and I split the fried pork chops w/ eggs (Sunnyside up bcuz what respectable self proclaimed food critic wouldn't) and the Southern Sampler (Fried chicken, meatloaf and BBQ). The chicken was good and so was the BBQ. The meatloaf seemed greasy and plain. Our sides were the Mac n cheese (the real deal!!!), fried ocra (avg) and the hashbrown casserole (basic and under cooked). We ordered the fried green tomatoes as an app which were tied with the Mac n cheese for amazing.
I'd say overall the food was average but maybe people go there more for the experience than the food. I will say Ms. Anne and Rock in the store were the best and would be the only reason to give a four or five

The food was tasteless and the waiter, grumpy.  I had the fish & chips - a waste of time and money.  One big piece of fish that was tough and over cooked.  I couldn't even eat the "fries," which were soggy lumps of undercooked potatoes.  We ordered the potato pancakes as an appetizer - they were cold, hard and tasteless as well.  We won't be going back again.

What a fun music venue. We saw Bobby Bare and Bobby Bare Jr a couple of weeks ago and it was a fantastic show. It's nice to have dinner options beyond the standard bar fare (ahem, 3rd and Lindsley). The wine selection is as good as you'd expect from a place called "winery". A few gripes - we bought VIP tickets and must have been the only ones, because they didn't open that section. They gave us decent seats, but didn't offer to reimburse us. The tables are community, so we got seated with some obnoxious college kids constantly snapping selfies. Service seemed to still be working out the system. But a great show will save a lot of service sins.

I worked in a fine dining German restaurant years ago, so I am going to try to not rate this place based on that. As usual, I will cover the good and bad, and try to avoid the ugly. I should note that I did not have the full experience, as I was with my daughter who was yucking German food at the time, so my in-house experience was in the bar waiting for food.

One thing that struck me was how much the employees, bar and floor, were spending with another employee who was at a table in the bar area, rather than focusing on customers. I understand it is a slow night, but had I not paid my bill right when I ordered, I would have had a difficult time getting any type of attention. I hope this was an off night.

First, the atmosphere is on point for a German bierhaus, except perhaps a bit too bright and a less communal feel in many ways. The beer comes in standard European sizes, all the way up to a liter stein. And, while I did not see anyone drinking out of one, they have steins for regulars in their own little lockers. Did not see a Stammtisch, so not sure if they have that type of designation for strong regulars.

The food? I had the King Ludwig Patter so I could try a bunch of different foods. The rouladen was good, but a bit dry (overcooked?). The Kassler Ripchen was nicely smoked and the highlight of the meal. A chop and the two krauts would have been a nice meal. The cut is a bit thinner than I have had in the past, but very nice flavor and well cooked. I did not get to try the Knackwurst that came with the plate, as it was missing when I got home (my spidey senses were tingling to check before I left, but I ignored them, so I put this on me). 

As for the sides. Pretty standard sauerkraut and the red cabbage is not the overly sweet crap I have had at some German restaurants. As for the whipped potatoes and gravy, I felt they were rather fake feeling and would have much rather had some Spätzle than the potatoes. Honestly, the downpoint of the meal.

I also grabbed an Apfelstrudel for dessert. Not the style I am used to (had a topping), but very tasty. I would much rather have a drier version, like I am used to, but different strokes?

I really would have like to try a wurst of some type, so I am a bit saddened they had a lack of quality control that night. Yes, perhaps I should have contacted management to get it fixed, but I live on the other side of Nashville, so I am not sure when I will get my next chance to travel over (but if they read this and keep a list, I would still like to try the wurst).

I will likely get back at some time and try a schnitzel next round. I would also like to Spätzle.

We went on a Friday morning and got seated right away. Service was good. The biscuits were great and the food was really good. The southern omelet was loaded. Prices were pretty decent for breakfast too. If you like strong coffee it was pretty strong. Definitely cute and lives up to the expectations.

Friends and I came here for breakfast on our first morning in Nashville and were not disappointed! 

Biscuits and homemade preserves to start off a meal?! Yes, please!
Moonshine in your Bloody Mary?! Of course!
One of the best southern breakfasts ever?! For sure!

I loved the Southern Plate (eggs, bacon, sausage, country fried ham and hasbrown casserole). It was the perfect amount of food and gave me a taste of what Loveless is known for.

Our waitress was great, the host was even better! If you're in Nashville, this is a must visit piece of Americana history.

If you're contemplating stopping here and you love southern home cooking, the answer is yes!! 

My group of 4 came at 1 on a Friday, and we were quoted a 45 minute wait. We had fun exploring "Hams and Jams" and hanging out at a picnic table in the sun while we waited. Hams and Jams also provides complimentary, delicious coffee.

Our server could not have been sweeter, and she provided great recommendations for drinks and food. She brought out a plate piled high with warm biscuits and homemade peach, strawberry, and blackberry jelly. The biscuits melted in your mouth, and the jellies were sweet deliciousness.

I ordered the hot chicken (daily special) with macaroni and cheese and hashbrown casserole. The breading on the chicken was perfection.. It was the right thickness, crunchy, and had a good spicy flavor. Both the macaroni and cheese and hashbrown casserole were cheesy deliciousness.

My bill totaled less than $20, which was amazing for the amount of food I received. I would highly recommend visiting!

From the ambiance to the service to the food, this place was exactly what we were looking for on our girls trip Tennessee vacation. The food was fresh and definitely had that homemade taste. It was cool to read up on a bit of the history and to see all of the many people who have found themselves dining at the loveless cafe throughout the years. Our server was wholesome and checked back on us frequently. The chicken salad sandwich was one of the best I've had and their smothered red potatoes were perfect to go along with it. Make sure to try all of the jams that come with their biscuits as you'll be sure to find a favorite. This place is worth making the trip outside of the hustle and bustle of down town Nashville.
Excellent service, excellent biscuits, great atmosphere.  I'm not much of a jam/jelly person, but all three I tried with my biscuits were above average...ok they were all yummy!  I'll be back!

Where can you go where it's Oktoberfest all-year-round? The Bavarian Bierhaus. It's connected to the Opry Mills Mall, but don't let that deter you. The food was great, wait-staff was fabulous and the entertainment was awesome! We came in the day after Christmas for a rather big meal... yup we were hungry. From the photos I saw of the pretzels, they looked appetizing, so I ordered one. That was way more than enough and it was quite appetizing too + the bier cheese: for dipping. Here's what else we had: smoked bratwurst, black forest schnitzel: chicken schnitzel that's topped with Ham & Swiss Sauce. Never had schnitzel before? It is a thin slice of tenderized meat that is breaded and fried. It was quit tasty. We especially loved the live entertainment that night... a lovely man and woman singing + playing the accordion. It was so cool. My daughter wanted to join in on the dancing fun, too. Our waitress was fabulous and was super attentive to our table and made sure we had all that we needed to make our dining experience a superb one. I don't get to have German food that often, so this was a real treat!

I took my staff to lunch at Loveless to celebrate a co-worker's birthday.  It was a big hit.  Many of us were new to Nashville and really enjoyed this staple.  As a true southerner, I would say that the biscuits are a little overhyped but they were still quite good.  It's just a matter of personal taste though.  I will definitely go back and take more friends in the future.

Not sure why anyone would leave a Negative review about this Restaurant its AMAZING food and service !!!! Nothing beats Great service Thank you Brittany for that but Great food and this place has both a must try in Nashville don't pass this one up !!!
Loveless Cafe has a country vibe! Their biscuits are amazing and you must order them! The waitress and staff are super sweet! If you're in Nashville, gotta check this place out!
The place was smoky and not friendly. I would not recommend spending your money. I tried the Collier & McKeel Bourbon, not impressed.

The acoustics were great and I enjoyed the show.  The drinks were overpriced.  The menu online did not match the menu, which was disappointing as the item I planned to order was not available.  The food we did order was just bad.  I ordered a steak which was over cooked and over seasoned.  My friend ordered a pasta dish which was dense and lacked flavor.  I will go back for shows, but will not order food again.

So far as atmosphere goes? Just lovely - absolutely perfect! All else needs a little more work to get there. You can tell the food is inspired, but just isn't quite... good, to be frank. Or if it is good, it is just good, and certainly not great. Poorly seasoned, odd flavors, everything we ordered was missing something or had too much of another thing. I cant remember if we had a waiter or waitress, they paid us so little mind. Won't be on the list of places we re-visit unless maybe for a glass of wine before a show... we'll see

Edit: As promised, the manager did contact us. No change in my review, but it's always good to know that concerns are being heard and not falling on deaf ears. This kind of commitment, I'm sure, will lead to improvement.

Bavarian Bierhaus in Opry Mills is an authentic German restaurant/bar exuding the spirit of Oktoberfest.  It's impossible to miss the huge building as it proudly displays the name with their emblem of a lion holding a stein in the classic royal blue and white, as the colors of Bavaria. The style inside is reminiscent of a Munich bierhall with large communal tables and benches to sit on and a stage for live music. Near the entrance past a small gift shop and colorful mural they also have a bar area with smaller bar tables and chairs and an outdoor patio area. 

Although this is a bierhaus they have a full bar. If you are unsure what type of German beer you'd like to get you could opt for a flight of 6 beers, 4 oz each. They will give you 4 of the famous beers then you can pick the other 2 for the flight. These are served on a large wooden paddle. If you want one certain type of beer they have 3 sizes to choose from--.3 liter, .5 liter, or 1 liter of beer. I got the .5 liter of the Paulaner Premium Pils which was refreshing and really good. Somehow it is also more fun to drink beer out of a huge stein than just a regular pint class. If you want to be THAT person who gets wine at a bierhaus you can order to your liking as they have 4 different reds and whites each.

The food menu has many of the German staples such as wurst (sausage) or schnitzl (breaded chicken or pork that is pan seared). We got a giant pretzel ($9) that comes with mustard and we also got a side of the warm bier cheese ($3). The cheese is worth it to get with the pretzel and our server told us as much--it was great! The pretzel was a good choice to soak up all that beer we were drinking as well! 

I was really impressed by this gem of a place in the Opry Mills. Parking is easy as there is a huge lot and they are open until midnight I believe on Fridays/Saturdays so it can be a great place to go hang out and have a few drinks with friends. Whether you come to have a few beers, a meal or to hear live music it is a good spot for large groups as they have plenty of room.

New place but pretty fun. The bar tenders were prompt and pleasant. I've had the patty melt and breakfast sandwich. No complaints food wise. I could definitely see this as a great pregame place for preds or titans games. I'm looking forward to see this place in full swing come this summer. The outdoor bar looks like a lot of fun in nice weather.

I have passed this place probably 500 times but never stopped until last night. A friend and I went in and tried their charcuterie tray with assorted meats and cheeses which was excellent.

They had a number of very nice wines to choose from and we enjoyed ourselves very much.

Their biscuits are life, but I've been Keto for three months  so I had to branch it and try new things. So my staple fried chicken, fried fish, fried pork chops, had to go. So I mixed up this visit: Sunday brisket, cucumbers and onions, and turnip greens. It's a WIN!
The only complaint would be that the pieces had a bit too much fat, but they were still good. Good color, awesome hickory flavor, tender the au jus really set it off. A really good meal with a really good price.

Ok people, listen up. If you are in or near Nashville, you NEED TO EAT HERE!! I give this place 25 stars, but Yelp only offers 5, but just know it's really 25. My husband and I came to Nashville on our honeymoon, and people told us 100 different places to eat, (most of which sucked). Then, we took a carriage ride and asked the driver where he likes to eat. He said the Loveless Cafe, and so we were like it can't be any worse than the other God awful tourist traps we went to. Oh. My. God. Y'all. The food tastes like little baby Jesus came down from heaven and cooked the food Himself. I had the 1/2 fried chicken, fried okra, and mashed potatoes. My husband had the chicken livers, fried green tomatoes, and hash brown casserole. Oh, and THE BISCUITS!! LORD JESUS, the homemade biscuits!! I took one bite and the hallelujah choir started singing. I imagine it's what the food must taste like in heaven, and I'm not a really religious person. Seriously, go. It's like 30 mins outside of Nashville, but it's worth the drive. You won't regret it!!

Loved City Winery! The wine was fantastic and the food was even better. I got the grouper and my boyfriend got the steak. Both were delicious, we didn't want them to end! You can tell everything here is made with quality ingredients. We will most certainly be back!

The wait was fairly short during breakfast. The portion sizes are good. Most of the food tasted great, especially the biscuits. The biscuits were really buttery and soft. Honestly some of the best biscuits I've ever had. They did give a very small amount of preservatives and we usually ran out quickly. Some of the food was salty but it was overall a good experience. I would definitely recommend trying as they have biscuits to die for. I even bought some of the biscuit mix at the shop next door.

The wait time can be long on a busy weekend morning, especially Sunday. But any Nashville native knows and expects this, and tourist should too. If you're looming for some good ol southern comfort food, it doesn't get any better than this!

Stopped in one day when in town building the brand for a company who will remain nameless here. Grabbed a quick lunch with a nice wheat beer and enjoyed the atmosphere and food. 

Great location where you can shop or catch a movie afterward as well. 

Would recommend for groups and families too! Live a little.

Five stars all day! 
Got to visit the store and eat at the Cafe. 
The wait wasn't too long, but any wait would be worth it. 
The portions are good size and everything tastes amazing! The hash brown casserole is the best! 
We bought a few things for the kids at the store, it's pretty cute and quaint. 
You can also sign up for their email list and order from their website.
Good service and good food. Nice touristy flavor to the place as well to do a bit of shopping (kitchen items, cafe branded clothes, souvenirs, etc.

Horrible. Food was tasteless. Portion were small. If you want to make it in Nashville you are going to have to do something. If you just want to be a bar then don't act like a diner. Never going back. We were the only ones in the restaurant part and maybe four people at the bar.
We went today for a event ! The girl at the Bar made use a great drink while we were waiting . But the food was HORRIBLE!!!!!! I would go for event and order wine with NO FOOD
Well worth the drive from Nashville. Very capable wait staff, very decent prices, very good food.
Food was amazing Kimberley and Ryan were great servers have the best time!! Large group of 11 took reservations! Killer bloody Mary's we would definitely come back again!!

I have been lucky enough to eat here twice.  Once for lunch and once for breakfast.  Some great food and atmosphere.  They have some traditional Southern eats (chicken and waffles) and some interesting new things. I add the BBQ pulled pork omelet for breakfast.  

Can't wait for the 3rd time!

Rocketown is great!!! The main bldg. & the smaller white bldg across the street, are both great venues. Concerts are why I have been to both locations this far & we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves! 
Thanks Michael W. smith for your vision & opening Rocketown!

Went here for a birthday dinner and it was great! Very reminiscent of the Beer Garden at Epcot/Disney World. We went on a Saturday night and had no trouble getting seated (we reserved on Open Table but were early and they sat us right away), there was live music that was fun and interactive with the audience, service and food were great and the desserts were delicious! The little gift shop by the registers is a lot of fun too. All the staff were very nice, the restaurant was large and busy but very clean. Really enjoyed our evening here!

We are visiting from Houston and coming here was on our list of must go places. I am so glad we went! Mark was our server and he was so funny and genuine. It was very refreshing and made our experience even better. The food was as great as we were told it would be, but Mark was really the highlight! Thank you Mark

This was our first time at Loveless though we've been in Nashville for a few years now. EXCELLENT FOOD! And even more EXCELLENT SERVICE! Barbara was the woman who served us, and she was very welcoming and helped us select the perfect meals. I chose the quarter fried chicken with the hashbrown casserole and the sweet potatoes. My friend had the chicken and dumplings with the squash casserole and slow cooked green beans. Both option were truly amazing. For anyone passing through Tennessee or looking for a new place to eat - please check this place out for some really great Southern food.

And I totally forgot about the biscuits, but yea...some of the best I've ever had!

I never like leaving bad reviews on a place. I really don't. I'm sure many people come here and enjoy it as the reviews reflect and I'm glad for them. 
However, I came here for a show as an out of state visitor. I didn't feel comfortable or welcome at all. As soon as I arrived and stepped inside it was very, very clear that I had arrived alone and would stay that way all night (had I stayed). The venue is very small so it can't be because no one knew I was there. A couple people continued to drink their beers like I was completely see through. 
No one acknowledged my existence. I tried making eye contact and all that but I still just stood there awkwardly. 
Due to my social anxiety, I stepped outside and sat down. 
During that time I received a short phone call from a friend where I repeatedly mentioned that I have both social anxiety and aspergers which makes it hard for me to approach people and say hello and that I would like very much if someone would talk to me because I'm only shy at first. 
Whoever was outside taking ID definitely looked at me when I said that but continued to talk to his friend. 
No effort at all was made to make me comfortable. Not even a hello. 
I ended up leaving despite having paid for a ticket to the show. Despite being visually distressed, no one asked what was wrong/ if I was okay or offered to fix it. 
Very stuck up attitude toward non locals from what I can see as the regulars were all greeting each other. I have never felt so out of place at a venue before. Ended up going to another bar where the people were friendly and enjoyed my night anyway. 
I won't come back here.

Meh. Mediocre. That's how I feel about this place. My boyfriend and I have been here twice now. The first time, valet parking was mandatory and $5, then obviously you tip the valet driver. We were only coming for a pre-dinner glass of wine. Starting the price of my glass of wine at $10 before I even order seems absurd.

Fast forward. I found a Groupon and thought it was definitely worth another try. Afterall, I hadn't tried the food. So we came back for brunch after church on a Sunday. The service, also mediocre. I did really love the drink I ordered here though. It was different and pretty refreshing- pecan't even. My boyfriend had the bloody Mary which he liked as well. We ordered the blueberry corn muffin, probably my favorite thing I ate for brunch. Actually, definitely my favorite thing. For entrees I ordered the frosted flakes pain perdue. For me, it was overly sweet and pretty soggy. My boyfriend ordered a croissant eggs benedict, which was pretty good. 

So honestly, the food is okay. The service is okay. Wine is alright. Drinks are pretty good. For me, nothing was bad but nothing was good enough to make me want to come back either.

This was our first visit and it was wonderful, we will definitely return and already plan on bringing family when they come to visit!

We went early Friday afternoon and there was a bit of a wait. We were given a buzzer and then had a lovely look at the little shops around the property before settling down on some porch seats. There is plenty of seating spotted around the property to make waiting pleasant.

Once called for our table we were introduced not only to some amazing biscuits and preserves, but to the amazing Susan (from Georgia), waitress extraordinaire. 

I am not sure a written review can properly express how wonderful Susan was. She was friendly, funny and went above and beyond in helping us enjoy our meal.

We chose the fried chicken platter and the pulled pork platter at Susan's recommendation. Both were perfectly cooked and deliciously seasoned. Our sides, smoked creamed spinach, creamed corn, Mac and cheese, and fried green tomatoes were perfect additions to the meal. The portion sizes were more than generous, and we took plenty of leftovers home with us. We would have happily devoured more of the meal if we had not enjoyed so many of those incredible biscuits before the food arrived. 

During our meal we happened to overhear a nearby table inform their waitress that someone at the table had celiac disease. It must be frustrating to go out with your family to eat and have to be so conscious of what your limits your choices. The staff handled this beautifully, a man who was either a supervisor or manager came to the table and explained not only what the ingredients were in the dishes, but where in the kitchen (or outdoor smoker) they were prepared. 

Susan's kindness once again shone when it was time to pack up our leftovers, not only had she brought me extra BBQ sauce (warmed up!) during the meal when she passed by and noticed I was a little low, but she brought me a small container for taking sauce home with me. She also brought us some biscuits to take home, saying "you have to have biscuits to enjoy with your leftovers".

To sum up, the property is charming, the atmosphere welcoming, and the food is mouth watering. The staff are all cheerful and we obviously cannot say enough about how much we enjoyed having Susan as our waitress.

The Basement is one of the venues in Nashville to see true singer/songwriters. The venue is small, dark and intimate. We came here to see three acts on a Friday night and luckily we got there early enough to score front row seats. It was a mere $5 for entry and to be honest these acts deserve so much more. I was impressed with the talent we saw and the energy exuded on stage. The sound is excellent and there is no bad seat in the house. 

The Mountain with Amethyst Kiah, Shannon Labrie and Jillian Jacqueline thanks for the amazing performances. 

Side note I usually hate box wine but the one they serve was actually pretty good!

Another lovely experience at loveless cafe. I typically plan on a two hour wait when going here, and they got us in with an hour and a half. 

Their biscuits are the best I've had in the south. I typically purchase the mix to make them at home and fresh jelly from their store while waiting to eat. Cornhole helps pass the time too. 

Our server was friendly and attentive. Our food came out fresh and as ordered. My only recommendation for loveless would be that they wipe menus in between guests. Mine was pretty dirty.

Bang for your buck: 5/10
Quality: 4/10
Service: 8/10
Ambiance/Location: 10/10
Overall: 5/10

I wanted so desperately to love Loveless Cafe. Everything about it seems just so much up my alley, but alas, a glowing review is not meant to be. 

Let me at least start with the pros:
-They have Dr Pepper
-Their biscuits are very very good 
-As are the preserves. Especially a fan of the strawberry.
-There are about two dozen items on the menu that at least sound like they'll be delicious 

The Cons:
-The food: I got the fried chicken. It had so clearly been sitting in a warmer all day. It wasn't moist and juicy with a crispy crunchy coating like a good fried chicken should be. Nope. This was dry and stuck to the bone. I couldn't even finish it because it was essentially inedible. It lacked so much flavor that I doubt it would have been very good anyway. Dave got the pimento cheese burger. The pimento cheese lacked any of the flavor composition you want in a pimento cheese and the burger itself tasted like it came from GFS. We got a host of sides because I just love sides. I'd struggled the whole time we waited for a table to narrow down to sides because honestly I wanted them all. I finally talked myself into only getting the 2 that came with the chicken meal, and I'm really glad I did because it simply meant less food to be disappointed by. I ordered the hash brown casserole. It was very meh. Dave and I shared the fried okra; it was too greasy. Dave got the macaroni and cheese and it was so bland. It didn't taste cheesy and wasn't even a little creamy. We both wanted dessert, but I figured it was better not to even try.
-The service: Our waitress could have been more attentive. When we asked for something she brought it pretty quickly, but she didn't check in on us and didn't seem concerned that I didn't touch my chicken.
-The Wait: we waited for over an hour for a table. It was a Sunday afternoon and Loveless is popular, so that's a little understandable. However, waiting that long for a super disappointing meal stinks. 

Overall, Loveless is touted as a powerhouse of Southern cooking, and it was just Cracker Barrel with higher prices, way worse food, and a much longer wait.

We came here on a Saturday evening for dinner and so much fun! There was a live band playing and be prepare to make new friends at your table. It's a picnic bench and you're seating with strangers so it's good to interact with your neighbors. This is my first time having German food and beer. It was delicious from the sausages to the soup. The soup and sausages is a must, thanks to the travel channel.

Driving out to the Loveless Cafe was a spur of the moment decision on our trip to Nashville and it turned out to be one of the food highlights of our trip! Just driving to this quaint cafe you feel the cozy, rural sights taking your stress away. We had an hour and a half wait for a table but with the shops and beautiful weather the time passed quickly. Once seated we had an amazing meal with the best server! Owen made us feel like we were in his home and there was no feeling of being rushed so the line of people waiting to get in could get a table. We truly felt like we could enjoy our meal and have a chat. The biscuits are truly the best I have ever tasted and the Fried Green tomato & Pimento cheese biscuit was amazing! We will definitely be going back again and again now that we know about this warm and inviting place! Thank you for such a memorable and friendly experience!

A definite must to go for breakfast. So cute and quaint. Service was friendly and you need to check out the market and smokehouse. The fried pork chops with white gravy is delicious and feeds two people. The waiter was helpful to choose something off the very long list of breakfast items. Gets busy, make sure you party is complete before you ask to be seated. They food is quick to come out and they bring biscuits immediately to your table with fresh jams, yum!!

Heavenly biscuit is no lie!

There will be a wait, but they're pretty accurate how long it takes and you can check out their cute store just outside.  Drove 30min from Nashville while we were there for a long weekend in Oct 2016.  Definitely worth it.

This restaurant is a far piece from downtown Nashville we were staying by the airport and it took us between 20 and 30 minutes to get there don't let the distance or the wait scare you it is well worth it

Honestly some of the best food I've ever tasted I have the fried chicken mashed potatoes and macaroni and cheese the husband had their daily special which was brisket over toast mashed potatoes and green beans

The chicken was perfect juicy inside crispy on the outside not over breaded and macaroni and cheese was amazing its obvious everything here is made from scratch my husbands brisket literally melted in your mouth and the green beans or seasoned perfectly.

We stopped in on Saturday around 1 o'clock the wait was 2 hours and we were just too hungry to stay we came back on Sunday around 4 and still have an hour wait the food was well worth it in the meantime we walked around to all the shops on the campus and you even are able to check out corn hole bags to keep you busy.  We walk through all the shops and even got a t-shirt that said praise the lard and pass the biscuits the lobby is full of autographed photos from celebrities who have stopped by and  the decor is like being in your grandma's kitchen. 

When they first sit you down they bring you their scrumptious biscuits and homemade strawberry peach and BlackBerry preserves.  If I would have known these were so good I probably would have bought them in the gift shop rather than the t-shirt they melt in your mouth

The service was as good as the food.  Kramer was our waiter we never had to ask for anything my tea glass was always at least half full and he stop by several times to see how we were doing.  If I have to find something I didn't like I would say the tea probably wasn't sweet enough but that's nothing that would stop me from coming back.

 can't wait to come back to Nashville to eat at loveless again next time I'm getting breakfast
Incredible service. Wonderful staff. And downright delicious food. One of my favorite places in Nashville. The food was perfect. Great place. Not too be missed.

Oh my. We are stuffed. If we die tonight it'll be from carb overdose as it was embarrassing how many biscuits we ate. This place was phenomenal. We're from Texas so we are not unfamiliar with delicious southern cooking but this was good stuff! Our waitress, Virginia, was so friendly and the epitome of a sweet southern girl. I had the bbq pork plate with cream corn and mashed potatoes. The pork was delicious. The bbq sauce was a little sweet for my taste but that's a regional preference. The cream corn was delicious and reminded me of my grandmother's! He had the fried pork chops and eggs. The chops were perfectly crispy and hot out of the grease when they arrived! We even had a side of sausage gravy to eat with our biscuits. The gravy was great and they weren't stingy with it either, which is always our biggest complaint with restaurants and gravy. Overall, it was all delicious. I wish we would have saved room to try the pie but there were just so many biscuits.

From this point forward all other country cooking is forever put to shame!
Catfish = about the best I ever had
Green beans = best ever
Turnup greens = as good as ever had
Buscuits and jams= as good as ever had
Meatloaf= excellent 
Pecan pie= best ever
And yes I ate all the above! And then some!!

Even though Loveless Cafe was a bit out of the way from where we were in downtown Nashville and even though we had biscuits and fried food the entire weekend, we knew we couldn't leave Nashville without trying the iconic Loveless Cafe. Before going, we tried to call ahead and see how long the wait would be since we didn't want to miss our flight but the guy who answered the phone didn't really give us a good estimate. So we ended up ordering online for pickup which was easy enough.

When we got there, there didn't seem to be a line but our food was ready for us anyway. We sat outside at their picnic benches which worked out since it was such a nice day. We had the BBQ pulled pork with hashbrown casserole and creamed corn, fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit, blue ribbon salad, banana pudding, and an order of regular biscuits. The pulled pork was a little dry and could have used more BBQ sauce. Hashbrown casserole was good and something I haven't seen on a menu before so it's worth a try but not something that I need. Creamed corn was standard. Fried green tomato biscuit was AMAZING. Nice acidity on the tomato to complement the cheese, and their biscuits are definitely winners. Blue ribbon salad was good with the pecans and veggie chips, and honestly, greens helped balance out the meal. Their regular biscuits are so delicious and their jams are the bomb dot com. I'm not a jam kinda gal but they converted me. The banana pudding which everyone raved about and I was pumped for was honestly a bit of a letdown. It tasted pretty normal to me. Next time I'm in Nashville, I'd get the biscuit sampler and dessert sampler - I was just too dang full this time around.

This place has the potential to be a great spot in Nashville. It's lacking in customer service and food menu, but with changes made I think I would come back.

There is a nice amount of parking out front, as well as street parking. There is a beautiful outdoor dining area, that is dog friendly, and has a mini golf setup. Inside there's plenty of seating, from booths and tables to bar seats and couches. 

We had to approach the bartender, as there were no servers walking around, and no menus visible. I was expecting more from the menu, it didn't really compliment your typical wine dining menu. 

My friend ordered a salad and I ordered the burrata. The salad did not look very good or fresh at all. The burrata was pleasant, though they were heavyyy on the balsamic. There was no music, it was kind of a dead space but could turn into a great brunch space or event space with some changes!

We live close to this legendary restaurant!  We are lucky to be able to visit often and even order to go!  For locals, this is the best option for busy families. 
We've invited friends from out of town to eat with us at Loveless. All meals are fantastic!  Be sure to arrive early during peak times as it can get very busy. It's so worth it!

Adding the fifth star after today's lunch.  Service was top notch, with a big thanks to our server Alesha, and the food was delicious across the board.  Rouladen was enjoyed by several in our party and personally I really appreciated Bob's prior response on Yelp about how they prepare that dish.  Great beer selection and definitely will be back in the future for the earlier morning Bayern games.

We came, we danced, they held my ID hostage... My cousin plays in the band here so I hesitate to leave a negative review, but I have to let y'all know what this place is about. We ordered $35 worth of drinks every round about 4 times in a row. When I was ready to slow down, I went to the bar and ordered an Angry Orchard. She delivered the bottle and then informed me she couldn't close a tab under $15. "Oh, but I've spent over $100 already." Doesn't matter. Her manager came around and gave me more sass than I've ever been given in a professional establishment (and you know I love some sass, but like... not when you're the manager of a bar). Y'all. I had to buy two more drinks as we waited for our Uber in order to get my freaking ID back which was being held hostage. When the manager could have shown maturity she showed hostility. Can't recommend this place with a good conscience.

Total dive bar! We stopped by on a Wednesday  afternoon, mainly because I had to pee. LOL. We ended up having a beer ($4/each!) They only serve beer and shots. Music was decent. Service was decent. Hated that people smoked inside.

I was in Nashville for a business trip. Something big was happening so I ended up staying out near the airport. I was with a co-worker. I was looking through the Interwebs looking for someplace interesting with Southern comfort food to eat at. Loveless Cafe kept coming up as a place we had to go. OTOH, it had every sign of being full on tourist trap. Finally, the positive reviews won out.
Driving in continued to screen tourist trap. Spending a short time in the waiting room screamed tourist trap.
Fortunately, the food didn't.
We had an excellent meal. I'm nor normally a biscuit guy, but these really are nice with some butter and jam. The dishes we tried were pretty much perfect, and the pie lived up to billing. The only thing that didn't wow me was the moonshine. It was just a bit too sweet and smooth. It tasted a lot like Dutch Genever. That's hardly much of a quibble.
Even though it's a big place, it didn't feel overly large and our server was a nice, earnest, young man.

I was so looking forward to loving this place- but sadly, no. 
And I was so looking forward to seeing one of my favorite bands- Toad the Wet Sprocket. Again, sadly no.
This was my experience:

1. Bought VIP balcony tix $60. Seemed reasonable at the time, now I feel dirty. 

2. Ordered the $15 burger. Asked for it medium rare, came out medium well. Tasted more like a $5 burger. Couldn't talk to our server about it because he was busy with other tables. Only ate it because I was starving.

3. The band comes on stage after the the opener- the opener dude was good especially if you like hearing the same sad song over and over again. He was however, funny between songs- whatever he said because the audience on the floor laughed. 

4. Toad takes the stage. Expectations high. Unfortunately, I was highly disappointed. The sound/acoustics sucked. And maybe it's because I was in the VIP balcony seats- it was very difficult to hear and understand the vocals. The band was too loud and the vocals were buried. 

5. Toad played a lot of their new stuff off their new album. Not a lot of the stuff that made them famous. I was surprised at the lack of their older and more popular music they DIDN'T play. 

6. Because of this experience, I probably will not eat or see another show at City Winery for a long while and Toad has broken my heart. I left feeling empty (crappy burger) and not just in my stomach and wallet- my heart as well. I spoke to a few others standing in the valet line and they agreed. They didn't play nearly enough of their older stuff.   

It hurts me to write this, but $60 on tickets and $50 dinner (burger, two glasses of wine + tip) and I feel dirty. I took tonight off from work for this. Not worth it what so ever. Not at all. Essentially I lost money.

Good bye and good night Toad the Wet Sprocket and City Winery. You both were a HUGE disappointment.

This place has some cheap drinks... I forgot how they structured it but they had $1/$2/$3/$4 for a variety of drinks and shots. My friends and I got some jello shots and they were pretty strong and good! A lot of the jello shots I've had before are nasty but they make them good here at Big Shotz. There was a live band and a good fun crowd the night we went, and overall we had a good time. I would definitely recommend coming here to start off a good night on Broadway... especially with their well priced drink specials!

On another note, there is a hip hop club above Big Shotz which is called Plush Ultra Lounge.. which we checked out. After a few days here, us girls from LA were hoping for a little taste of home in Nashville by going to Plush, hahaha. However, this place was super hot inside and the music was just not that great. You could also see it when there were just a bunch of people just standing around. After a drink or two, we decided to leave and enjoy the honky tonks in Nashville as we could always enjoy hip hop back at home, haha. 

Overall, I really liked Big Shotz, but Plush was a miss.
You got a problem with fried chicken, country ham and biscuits done flawlessly? Yeah, well I got a problem with YOU.

This place made my dreams of finding authentic Schnitzel in the US come true. Oh my where do I start, the ambiance is so cool and authentic. great gifts and goods shop, with very reasonable prices. they have an amazing beer selection, staff is very friendly and knowledgeable of the menu. I loved the outdoor seating area. the food authenticity and quality is the same as I had when I visited germany. I highly recommend this place for people who are looking for good german food and beer.

This place is super unexpected in Nashville, a real honest German hoedown in the middle of Tennessee. The beer is awesome, it's actual legit important Bavarian beer and I loved the Hef and Oktoberfest. I've been here for a special event and at the bar just for drinks. The food is decent, I'm not the biggest on German food but the pretzels are super good and huge. The live music is great and on a busy night it really feels like you're in European Beer Hall. This is not somewhere I'd go just for food or drinks unless I was really craving the whole experience, or happens to be at Opry Mills and craved a beer. But it is fun and the staff is great, I'd give the overall experience 4.5 stars.

Coming from Toronto this restaurant provided a lot of firsts for us. Biscuits, grits, fried green tomatoes, moonshine, barbecue, and hash brown casserole were great ( well to be honest we each only took a sip of the blueberry moonshine and that was enough!) but we loved the food and loved the experience. The drive back to Nashville was amazing along the Natchez Trail. We will return when we are lucky enough to come back to Nashville.

It's like Cracker Barrel except the food is way better. I wasnt a fan of the barbecue pork, but the fried chicken was so cruspy and juicy. Their sides are incredible! My favorite was the squash casserole which was basically a savory mush of chopped squash. Of course, their biscuits are fluffy and hot and theyll give you so many that you wont know how to act.

The service is the friendliest on earth, and the portions are huge! Come hungry.

I haven't been to Germany or an actual German Bierhaus but this seemed as authentic as I could imagine. My fiance & I watch a lot of Travel Channel & Food Network & we've watched a lot of episodes featuring German Restaurants & famous German dishes. 

It was very hard to choose what we wanted to eat - Käsespäzle, Jägerschnitzel, Schweinbraten or a Giant Pretzel?! We ended up ordering the Bierhaus Wurstteller ($21) -
Oktoberfest Brat, Smoked Brat, Weisswurst, Red cabbage, Sauerkraut & Bread dumpling. We were going to order the Jägerschnitzel but we were soo full of the brats & beer we didn't. The brats were soooooooo good - I honestly wish I could just eat this dish every single day.
Oh & their dijon mustard on their table was also sooooo amazing - I literally dipped everything in it.

If you're in the area or at the mall, this place is a MUST! Happy Eating!

I am a regular at City Winery.  Their show selection keeps me coming back time and time again.  In the past few months, I have seen a rock show, an acoustic show, a band I loved in the 80s, a funk show, and attended a wine tasting.  
I have a few reasons why this is one of my favorite venues in town.
1-valet parking right in front (7$) but free for VinoFile members, which is their annual fee membership club. Parking at many music clubs in Nashville can be a pain, to say the least.
2-seated! If you have a ticket, you have a reserved seat (unless otherwise noted for the occasional standing room only show.)
3-upscale dining.  The chef does a great job with seasonal ingredients.
4-shhhhhhh You can actually hear the artist as most patrons respectfully keep their chatter down.  That being said, of course their are exceptions depending on the type of show
5-they are actually a winery, and their locally produced offerings are on par with higher end wineries from notable winemaking areas
6-its just plain cool
If you are coming to town, check their show schedule.
If you live in town, check their show schedule.
City Winery is a dining and music jewel in a city that's got lots of gems... but this one ranks up near the top for me.

Loveless Cafe is a Nashville icon. They are so good and have branded themselves so well that tourists and locals drive to the outskirts of Davidson County to eat here! 
My family loves this place and it has become a frequent request when they come into town. The portions are very large and we always have leftovers. 
I think they are best known for their biscuits and they are extra special to me because my grandma use to make similar biscuits that she'd cut out with an old tin snuff can. I've never been able to replicate them. Loveless does a pretty excellent job of it. 
Their pork is also delicious! They give you so much, it's nuts! The menu has many options of country comfort food.
Be prepared to wait, the line is always long but it goes by quick because there are lots of things to do on the grounds of the Loveless Cafe complex. There are cute shops, corn hole, Benches to relax on. It's a lovely place.

If you want genuine southern food, definitely come here. Being from Massachusetts my family and I aren't really used to this southern food but it was very delicious. They said the wait would be 25 minutes and it was 10 at the most. While you are waiting you are free to walk around the property and explore. The food was truly southern and the staff was attentive and friendly. When we accidentally dropped out pie out of the to-go container in the bathroom, there just happened to be a worker in the bathroom and she ran to get us another pie. Great food and great staff!!

This place is amazing! The biscuits with their jams were fantastic. We ordered cooked-in pork and fried chicken. Well done! The pork was shredded and surprisingly not as oily as I thought it would be.. maybe because it didn't have a lot of fat. It was served over pancakes which were cooked very good! The fried chicken was one of the best I ever had. There was something different in their breading. :) Their mac and cheese was also creamy -- very nice! Cheese melted and coated over the pasta the way I liked it. Creamy corn is also a recommendation for the side. Apple pie for dessert was also quite heavenly. Will come back. :) What a great intro to Southern food!

The trek out to Loveless Cafe from Nashville is so worth it! We came out here to try the biscuits and were amazed by the scenic drive and the bucolic setting for the Loveless Cafe. I felt like I had stepped into a time warp where motels were the epitome of charming places to stay with your family and hang out all day. 

They had a restaurant, a small gift shop, and BBQ. We got here for a late breakfast and were charmed by the ambience. They also served their famous biscuits with three types of jam! It was a great experience for breakfast. Very filling and way better than the typical diner food. 

Service was fantastic and full of Southern hospitality. It being a hot day, the server also offered to give us water for the road. So thoughtful and it made me love the experience of eating at Loveless even more. I brought home some biscuit mix from the gift shop, too!

*Review is for the wine and light bite pairing class only*

My friend and I had both never been to City Winery and decided to check it out when we read the description of a wine and light bite paring class which sounded quite frankly, absolutely delightful. The event listing was a "Wine and Picnic Pairing" with the Beverage Director 
 of City Winery Jenelle Engleson. She pairs local wines with a menu specially created by the one of the chefs. The theme was supposed to showcase how wine and food can be paired for outdoor events/activities. 

We arrived a little bit early and there wasn't really anywhere to wait before the group was to go into the dining room for tasting class. My friend and I just stood in the lobby before it was time and looked around the venue. There was a concert that night so people were filing into the room for the show. Their restaurant is to the left when you walk in and is an open and exposed area but upscale. They have a patio outside connected to their restaurant. 

When it was time to do the class we were lead back and upon entering each handed a glass of sparkling wine to kick off the event. There was a long rectangular table in the middle of this pretty dining room that was set with burlap and candles and each place setting had five full classes of wine plus a couple of empty wine glasses, two complimentary tickets to an upcoming music show of your choice and a review paper and pen. We could sit wherever we wanted and it was a communal experience so you could introduce yourself to the people sitting next to you. 

When we got started Jenelle introduced herself and the chef who designed the menu. They had a station setup for all the treats and they did an introduction where the chef described each food we were about to eat and then the group could ask him questions. The menu consisted of a curried chicken salad in a tart (my favorite), potato salad inside the skin, a BLT skewer and a yogurt parfait. Although all the food was incredibly and although it was marketed as "small bites" this was enough for me to have for dinner and be okay. 

During the wine and picnic pairings I had an epiphany. This was the first time where I actually really realized that the right wine does bring out the flavors in the food. It was so incredible. For example, I took a bite of the chicken salad tart and the wine that she paired with it. Then she told us to take a sip of this sparkling wine that she said also went well and the flavor suddenly changed. I thought that wine pairing was kind of just this fantasy idea of a way to sell you alcohol but it actually really enhances the dining experience. I was so glad I did this class! 

I cannot say enough great things about Jenelle. She was knowledgeable and made learning about the wines approachable for someone like me who really just knows the basics. I ended up buying a bottle of the wine I liked and she brought it right over to me and was very nice and friendly. 

Overall, so worth the $30! My friend and I plan on doing more of her classes. I also cannot wait to use the complimentary ticket passes to come back and see a show here!

Cute touristy cafe about 20 minutes outside of downtown Nashville. We went there after a hike around 2pm and there was still a 45 minute wait. The wait wasn't that bad though because you can walk around the property and visit their shops while waiting. Once we were seated we got a fresh plate of biscuits and homemade jams. OMG I was in heaven with these... I'm not usually a jam person (especially where there is no peanut butter) but these jams were AMAZING! My favorite had to be the blackberry jam because it had whole blackberries in it. We knew we couldn't leave with out trying their famous chicken fried chicken, so obvious we had to get a half chicken. As the sides we got fried okra and mac n'cheese, my boyfriend's favorite. Sadly the mac n'cheese did not please- it just lacked a lot of flavor. I ordered the chicken fried steak off the breakfast menu and got it with poached eggs and cheesy grits. These were some of the best grits I had in Nashville! 

Service was great and we even got to take home some extra biscuits and jams!

I was... actually shocked by how much I enjoyed this seeming tourist trap. Came in on a weekend and this place was busy. Their dinning room is gigantic so I doubt that there's often a wait. The hosts didnt seem too happy to be there, but they also have to deal with tourist and those silly costumes. Nonetheless, I snagged a spot at the bar and had a great experience.

Food: I had the brats in a blanket and it was the best anything-in-a-blanket that I've had. Not typically a huge fan of this kind of fare but the blankets were so crisp and buttery on these things. I didn't have enough carbs so I rent ahead and order a giant pretzel which was salty, warm, and soft. 

Drinks: They serve absinthe. You're welcome.

Seriously amazing! We made the drive here as we were passing thru Nashville. This was worth he wait as the restaurant was clean, service was top-notch and the food was outstanding!

I ordered poached eggs to go along with my biscuits, and was impressed they even attempted to poach an egg and they were able to do so with precision.

This was just okay. I waited an hour and 10 minutes to be seated, which I don't have a problem with had the food been as amazing as I had heard. I ordered the chicken & waffles, which came with biscuits also.  The biscuits were delicious - light, soft and the homemade jam was a nice addition.  The chicken and waffles was pretty sad though. The chicken was extremely dry and the waffle was something I could have made at home. This was a very disappointing visit. I can get better at a local dive diner here in Pittsburgh.

The establishment is very underwhelming and dull. The service was slow. Highly advise not to get the froze. Food was good, however breakfast items don't come with a side. Definitely will not be coming back.

I started going to the Loveless Cafe in the 1950's, when dad would  take the whole family. I took my wife there around 2010 and this is my first visit since..This is not an attempt to compare & contrast today with some 60 years of history. Loveless' reputation as a "must see" tourist destination influences this writer not a bit. No, this review concerns the meal that I was served on Wednesday, April 26, 2017.

I came in a large group of people mostly from out church. Our server was Mary. She was tremendous! She took all our orders and made sure that everything went well throughout the meal. First came the biscuits and preserves. The biscuits were good, but not great. The assorted preserves were held in little plastic cups...isn't that special.

I ordered a real Southern meal: half a fried chicken with, for sides, turnip greens and grits with banana pudding for dessert. Southern fried chicken should be tender on the inside and crispy-crunchy on the outside. My chicken failed on both counts. while parts of the breast were tender, the rest was, well, not. It could have been left in the fryer a tad too long. My chicken wasn't crispy-crunchy on the outside. That might have been due to errors in the breading process. Just looking at the color of the chicken, I'd say that the grease in the fryer should have been changed before my chicken was cooked. Too bad that it wasn't. Shame on them.

My turnip greens, grits and banana pudding were pretty good- especially the grits, a real treat. Now my wife ordered the Southern Sampler with hash browns and coleslaw, plus their Whisper Creek Tennessee Sipping Cream with coffee. While  she said that she was disappointed with the chicken, she describes the Whisper Creek as "Awesome".

The meal that I had may not be typical of what Loveless normally serves. The rating reflects the meal that was served to me. I just have to return are eat another meal at the Loveless Cafe.

If you are other them white they will just prefer for you not to be there. Special if you are Latino like me and my wife, I been living in Nashville for 26 years and I never found people more racist them the girl at the door and the other guy she called to tread me and push me, and said racist stuff to us. If they have any cameras at the front door please check it out to see what they did to us!

This place was incredible! Never thought that I would eat 8 biscuits in one sitting, but here we are. First of all, this place is huge.
