There is a ton of seating, and the property has several stores to visit while you wait for your table (expect a long wait, we were told 1 hour 15 minutes and actually waited 45 on a Saturday), along with cornhole sets and picnic tables. I ordered the biscuit sampler (bacon, ham, sausage, chicken) and it was fantastic. All were delicious and cooked well. My favorite was easily the chicken, which was fried perfectly. The bacon one was good, but a little underwhelming, as it just didn't compare to the others, and expected it to be special from such a location. I also ordered home fries, which were good and I liked the seasoning on. 

Other orders at the table included another sampler (pork, bacon, sausage, tomato/pimento), grits, scrambled eggs, and the country ham. Was told that the grits were the best that my sister had ever had in her life. The other biscuits were good, and the ham was tasty. 

In addition, these breakfast plates come with MORE biscuits. These are served plain, with butter, syrup, and strawberry, peach, and blackberry preserves. I tried them with butter and all 3 preserves. All were great, but blackberry was my favorite. 

Would return, but try to get there as early as possible to avoid such a long wait.

I need 5 more starsssss!

Ya'll better find out how to get here because it's in the middle of nowhere but everyone seems to know about it! We put our name in for a 45-minute wait, by the time we were being seated the wait extended to 1 hour 20 minutes. The waiting area is covered in headshots (you know, the kind you get when you move to L.A. to be an "actor/actress," #noshadebutshady). I was wearing my Saint Mary's College sweater (go Gaels!) which prompted the manager to share that he used to live in Moraga. What a small world. I was in like Flyn! After reminiscing about California, he came around with multiple samples of his favorites:

* Banana pudding - If only I could bring back to S.F.
* Greens - ABSOLUTE PERFECTION!!!!!!!!
* Creamed Corn - new favorite fall side dish
* Apple butter - reminds me of my moms pb&js. Delicious!
* Pimento cheese - not a fan

For my entree, I went with the fried chicken with a side of mac n cheese + greens. My friend told me that people in the south usually put Velveeta in their Mac n Cheese, which is... different. I prayed there was no Velveeta in this dish because they were so creamy and hearty! These greens right here tho!!!! Oh. My. God! I at the sample Keith brought all to myself along with the side on my plate and would have happily devoured more. The best greens I have had in a very long time. They were not bitter and not vinegary. Thank the gods! Everything was washed down with their famous peach tea with moonshine. 

Oh, I almost forget about the dang gone biscuits! These bite-sized bits of heaven need no butter when adding the house-made preserves. But let's be real, who skips out on butter! 

The store on property sells much of their favorite items on the menu; the chicken batter mix, preserves, the biscuit batter even ham! I purchased a trio of preserves and my friend gifted me the chicken batter mix. 

If you are visiting during Fall, take a detour along Natchez Trace Parkway before or after dinner, to enjoy a scenic drive in the countryside of Tennessee. Bon Appetite!

AMAZING biscuits.. I could have eaten just the biscuits!!   We stopped here after a leisurely trip along the Natchez Trace Parkway.   We had just had lunch a few hours earlier but our waitress, Barbara, talked us into their chicken pot pie soup along with the biscuits.. if the meal wasn't delish enough to entice us back..it was Barbara's delightful personality that had us show up the next morning for breakfast.  Trevor was our 2nd trips waiter and he was equally attentive and awesome.. we didn't stop there.. the next day we ate breakfast there as a farewell to Nashville before we headed back to Chicago.  Cute buildings, awesome food and wait staff.. a must stop! A little pricey for the average breakfast but well worth it in memories!!

Went to the Loveless cafe this past weekend on my visit to Nashville. The biscuits were top notch! I rate this four stars because i felt like the Server was rushing us out of there. I know this place probably gets very busy on the weekends, but we were there pretty early and there was still lots of seTing. I hate being rushed...
Best breakfast I've had in a long time.  The biscuits were perfection.  The bacon was delicious.  The service and atmosphere were amazing.  Loved this place!

2nd time to Nash, and i finally made my way out to Loveless. Is it worth the 30 mins ride from the city? Absolutely! if youre a degenerate like myself and friends, grab some beer from the gas station next door and enjoy the wait. we waited over an hour at 11 AM on a saturday. 

Now onto the goods...

free biscuits and jelly for the table? dont mind if i do. especially since these biscuits are soft, moist, and go down smoothly. they come with 3 different jams to dip them in. my favorite? peach. all 3 are home made and available to buy.

i decided to switch shit up a bit and get a bunch of sides. first being the pimento cheese and green tomato biscuit sanndwhich, unfortunately, i hated this. too much cheese, cold cheese a matter of fact, i tried 2 bites and had to put it down. im sorry loveless! but the sides that made me fall in love them with them were the mac n cheese, the hashbrown casserole and the sweet corn. mac n cheese speaks volumes here, its gooey and cheesy and probably one of the bests ive had. however, the hashbrown casserole was so unique. ive never had anything like this before. it tastes like chicken, then mushrooms, then cheese and lastly hashbrowns. whatever the mix of flavor was, i suggest getting it. the sweet corn was very filling. also another unique side. heavy, and sweet, but chunky and filled with corn. 

service was great and food came out quick. i think that slows everyone down is the eating and falling into a food coma part. i almost fell asleep at the table, but ill be honest, it was worth every second of that coma.

Overpriced with an a**hole bartender!  I asked for thousand island on my reuben sandwich & got charged 50 cents extra. A very small 10 ounce beer is $6.50. One beer, a sandwich & dessert was $35. I don't mind paying more at times, BUT it's definitely not worth it when you get sh*tty attitude from the staff. I won't be back.

My husband and I lived in Germany for several years and loved the food. We have searched the United States for 30+ years for good, authentic German food and have only once found it....until today. The décor took us on a trip down memory lane, right back to a Bierhaus in Munich! The service was great and the food were delicious! Although we sampled several different dishes ordered at our table (and each was wonderful), there are others we can't wait to try! We will definitely be back! This restaurant has earned our seal of approval!
Update: I tried their hashbrown casserole and am in love. Just FYI.

We went out of our way to go here solely because of its hype and reviews. This place is off the beaten path if you're coming from Nashville. 
We had a wait (~30 mins) but entertained ourselves with corn hole and wandering through the shops. 
We LOVED the biscuits and variety jams. 
FYI- a friend I was traveling with asked "do you have a gluten free menu?" and our waitress responded "sweetie, I'm pretty sure we have gluten in our heating and air system"! 
We came to a BISCUIT spot, so we just laughed this off and my friend picked from the menu.

I came here with a few friends on a weekend for brunch. We waited about 2 hours but it was completely worth it. Besides, we were able to pass the time in their retail shop and by playing cornhole. I got the chicken and waffles with a side of biscuits and sausage and gravy. The food was AMAZING. If you're in the area this place is a must try. The service was wonderful as well!

I've wanted to try Bavarian Biehaus since it opened and was so excited to see that it was listed good for kids as we have a 4 year old.  My husband, daughter, and I took the drive to Opry Mills on Saturday evening and crossed our fingers we would have to wait less time at the restaurant than getting off the exit to Opry Mills:)  This place didn't scrimp!  The outside looks just as amazing as the inside. The restaurant was busy but we were able to sit right away.  I do advise when going to sit in communal seating, even with kids.  We sat in the section with table seating and although it was a bit quieter all the fun is definitely in communal seating. 

The restaurant really creates the Oktoberfest vibe.  My husband went to Oktoberfest in Germany and was really impressed with everything from the decor, the food, the music, and rowdy groups of people drinking steins of beer.

We had the Brozteitteller which is an array of meats and cheeses, as well as, a pretzel and rye bread... For dinner my husband had the fish and chips which he really loved and I had the chicken schnitzel w/ spaetzle. My daughter had a GIANT hot dog from the kids menu. Everything was good!

After dinner my daughter got a kick out of dancing with the band which was her favorite part! Will we be back?Well according to my daughter it's her new favorite restaurant!

Drawn to the replace by reviews. Was really excited about visting. Great news did not have to wait long. Surroundings  were super cool. Waiter was exceptional and suggested the fried chicken. No hesitation on my part I love fried chicken 

Chicken was tender but bland. No flavor. Greens were cooked well built again very bland and macaroni and cheese was very milky no structure and not like homemade.

Would not bother again better food at the Craker Barrel. 

I travel and eat out at over 50 resteraunts a year. Don't waste you time going here for the food but a maybe for the ambiance! I will admit the grounds are super cool.
A true classic. Country ham and biscuits with red eye gravy - it doesn't get any better than that!

Headline: mediocre food (for the price) that's overshadowed by really bad service.

We had a reservation for Mother's Day, but they didn't have a table ready for us so told us we could either wait or sit outside. It was a nice night, so we chose to sit outside, which was empty except for one table of loud, drunk a-holes. Even though the patio was completely empty, they sat us (a family of 4 celebrating Mother's Day) within arm's reach of the other table. I understand that waiters have sections and want tables close together, but seriously, this was ridiculous. For the first hour of our meal, we listened to them (we had no choice...THEY WERE YELLING!!!) discuss the finer experiences in life...you know, like finishing an entire bottle of vodka in one sitting. 

Our waiter was a nice guy but never told us anything about the wine, menu, or specials. Interesting, for a place with "winery" in the name, that they hand you a wine menu that's longer than "The Odyssey" and don't tell you anything about it. Our 4 entrees came out in 3 trips...2 at first, the 3rd about 5 minutes later, and then the 4th about 15 minutes after that. 

The food was good, but nothing special for comparably priced places (~$25/entrée). The pork belly dish MAYBE covered half the plate. It's a small piece of meat with some mashed potatoes and a few peas. It was good (both bites!), but I left hungry. 

Maybe they could use the $5 you have to pay for parking to put some food on the plates.

We won't be back.

We went with the family for a lunch on Sunday.  There was a very short wait for a table for 8.  

The place is huge. The beer was a mixture of German and local.  We all had different dishes and shared around the table.  Everyone loved their meals and the menu has enough variety that you could go back many times and not repeat anything on the menu.  

Highly recommended!

All the key elements of the German Oktoberfest theme are here - the fare (large steins of beer, pretzels, meats), the garb (severs dressed in traditional outfits) and the facilities (long communal tables and a performance stage).  Big fan of all the execution and would recommend drinking and dining here to anyone even if they weren't looking to feel like they are in Stuttgart or Munich.  

Dinner dishes are $15 or more (I.e. Half chicken dinner for $17) and half liters of beer in non-happy hour settings run you $7.50 each. Not bad given the quantities of food and beverage you receive.

Will sample a few more meals before throwing on the fifth star but the adults and kids all enjoyed their appetizers & drinks here. Only criticism at this point is of the rouladen which was just OK - not flavorful and moist as grandmother used to make (although maybe I'm to blame for expecting such authenticity and not appreciating the availability of such niche dishes).

A Nashville tradition that doesn't disappoint on the food.  We are regulars for breakfast, but that's all we come for, so I can't speak of the lunch and dinner. Their country ham with red eye gravy is excellent as are their cheese grits and hashbrown casserole. Love the sweet tea, not killer in the sweetness.  Be early or be patient. After 8 on the weekend, be prepared for an hour or more wait. Fortunately, the pagers they give you work on the entire property so you can go shop while you wait.

Went again after the Vanderbilt commencement ceremony. This time I was in a large group and each person ordered something different. I got the fried pork chops, which were huge portions (2 big pieces) and very tender and juicy. A friend had the fried steak, which was also very good. I would give it 4 or even 4.5 stars because the food is delicious and the biscuits are always amazing (and the preserves are heavenly). Just be prepared to wait (we waited about an hour).

You must go here!!! Robin needs to be your server!!! It was a great experience. The grounds are adorable with a lot of parking and a lot of opportunities to shop. 
I purchased peach preserves, a hat, and pumpkin pecan butter. 
The food - amazing! My sister and I ate two servings of the piping hot biscuits served with housemade preserves that would make you sing! 
My sister liked the blackberry preserves the best. I loved the ham and eggs (the ham and fried chicken are signature dishes. Oh and the hasbrown casserole is soooooo good! I also had a strawberry dipper made with Strawberry Whiskey that was phenomenal. This was a truly great experience I would recommend coming even though you'll wait a bit for a table, grab the kids, grab a drink and play some bean bags (cornhole) or sit on one of the many benches around the property and relax. It's worth it and the drive to get there even better!

While I had a good time here and saw pretty cool bands (like Faux Ferocious), I wasn't into The Basement when I went there. My Yelp rating is more like 2.5 stars. 

I'm really not trying to be a hater, but there was an attitude in that place that soured the night for me. It's a cool looking venue - dark, dingy, rough around the edges, and a little grimy (all pluses for a rock club) - but the patrons and even some of the people working the club that night were kind of snooty. Of all places to be snooty, they were snooty here! 

Perhaps it could have been a bad night, but I got the feeling that this was Nashville Indie Rock Elitism B.S. in full force... Meh... That being said, I'll take the Hi-Tone in Memphis over The Basement any day (just saying).
The ambience is great. I did not order the food but was shocked at the cost for two glasses of wine.  $32 with tip! wth?

I waited nearly an hour and I would wait an hour every single time for this food. The service is very quick once you are seated so it all balances out somehow. I ordered my food and received it in less than five minutes along with hot biscuits. The biscuits come with three homemade preserves: strawberry, blackberry and orange marmalade. Devine! The biscuits are small so you can try each preserve on a different biscuit guilt free.

I ordered the pulled pork platter with fried okra and sweet potatoes. I am positive it was a pound of pork. See the picture for proof. It was flavorful, not overly sauced and juicy. The cornbread cakes are under the bbq soaking up all the pork goodness. My fried okra was cold but I didn't care because I was starving. The sweet potatoes are creamy and not too sweet. They were piping hot! 

I got pecan pie to go. Let me tell you that this pie is the pie of pies! Wow. My tastebuds sang harmoniously in an angelic choir when that pie came to play. I'll be back Loveless. I'll be back

Such a great breakfast spot! If you're not here before 9:30am on a weekend, you're looking at 45+ min waits. However, there are a lot of little shops on the premises that are nice to walk around at. It helps pass the time. The biscuits were some of the best I've ever had. Their strawberry jam in particular is to die for. Their cheesy hash brown casserole is so good, I had to order a second side of them to go, lol. Their cheesy grits are very creamy, but if you don't care for American cheese, I wouldn't recommend them. I prefer cheddar so I wouldn't order them again, but if you like American cheese- the cheesy grits are definitely for you.

The Loveless Cafe, has good southern food sometimes, but there really are much better options in Nashville for southern country food. The food at the Loveless Cafe was a lot better and actually had a unique tasting before the Loveless Cafe, went to being owned by a corporation instead of continuing being family owned and operated! Some of the recipes have changed and if you are a regular before the big "change" hit then you can taste it! I grew up five minutes downtown the road from the Loveless Cafe and my family dined at Loveless often for dinner. The wait back then was long but now the wait is rather outrageous! The Loveless, now is sadly just a tourist trap and not a place where you run into your Bellevue neighbors. The Loveless Cafe, is the type of place for a "bucket list" and or a place to just say you have had a meal at the establishment. The staff is nice and most have smiles on their faces but they will rush you out before you completely finish your meal! I wouldn't say I've ever experienced southern hospitality since the "change" happened. 

If you happen to get the opportunity and wait out the wait list, then I suggest eating the squash casserole, fried okra, carrots and the biscuits. The fried chicken is hard and the meatloaf is just basic and dry. The green beans are nothing special and that is actually surprising! 

If you are a tourist looking for wonderful southern food then I highly suggest checking out Arnold's in downtown Nashville! The baked chicken, roast beef, greens, green beans, macaroni and cheese, and the spicy chocolate pie are awesome at Arnold's!

I dream about their darn biscuits. I almost need to unfollow them on IG because my heartaches when they show up in my feed. LOL Gosh they are good. I am a picky foodie and I am hard to please when it comes to biscuits. These are perfect. Lacking nothing. They are buttery, flaky, tender, moist, full of flavor, just yum. 

As far as the entrees I have mainly had breakfast. All of their breakfast meats (bacon, sausage, ham) are awesome. The eggs are eggs..lol. Pancakes, GREAT! I have also had their fried chicken..so good. 

Just go. You will not regret it. The service is friendly and prompt. The wait can be long but they have all kinds of things to walk around and look at and a little shop to browse. It is worth the drive and the wait. It is my go to every single time I am in town. 

LOVE IT!

It's a bit out of the way and still usually a bit of a wait once you get there but we felt we needed to experience it. The biscuits are fantastic, and they alone could be considered worth the wait. The rest of the breakfast was hearty and delicious as well.

Unfortunately I was a victim of a security breach through there website when I purchased tickets a year and a half ago. In addition, I wasn't able to attend said show due to having to be in the ER that night. Immediately following the incident, I was sent a gift card in the mail and was told I could have tickets on the house to any show I choose, due to the security breach. Which was awesome! Well for the longest time, browsing through the upcoming shows, there wasn't anyone I wanted to see. Finally I found someone I wanted to see, Ani DiFranco. It being a year and a half later I was weary of them still giving me tickets, but I asked anyhow. There was even a new box office manager since the incident had occurred. Amazingly he, William, was well aware of the incident and still granted me the tickets (which that is very rare when there is a new manager). We had an amazing time. The food was excellent, our seats were great, and it's a great atmosphere. If you are looking for a more personal concert experience, this is the place to go. And the manager on the floor, Mike, even took the time to stop by our table, acknowledging me by name, making sure I was enjoying my visit. That was my first time at City Winery and I am beyond impressed. I have worked in the service industry for 15 years and it is very hard these days to find an establishment that truly cares about their customers. Sorry for the long post, but thank you so much! I will definitely spread the word.

Upon our arrival to the Loveless Cafe I was mentally ready for the wait. The wait was about 45 minutes to an hour. However, the cafe has little stores you can check out on campus. The history behind the cafe is pretty cool it use to be a motel. If I had known the biscuits were going to be that delicious I would have saved myself and not ordered the pancakes. Needless to say I did not even touch the pancakes because I was so full on biscuits. The jams that were served with the biscuits were so good best jams I have ever had. There was a strawberry, blackberry, and peach. I also have to say the OJ was absolutely great! Next time for sure I will be ordering the waffle and chicken, and take home the biscuits and jam for a snack. I also, noticed throughout our meal, our server was not so great. We didn't get drink refills until the end of our meal. She really did not check if we needed anything else. Other than that this cafe is a definitely must if you are visiting Nashville.

Brought my mom here when she was visiting Nashville so that we could both check this off our bucket list. The wait, as expected was pretty long. I think 35-45 minutes. However they have so many little places to check out on the grounds you don't really notice how long you are actually waiting. We got a seat on the outside patio, and our waiter was quick with bringing us coffee and tea. Biscuits come out first with an array of jams and you can even request their pumpkin butter! They are yummy. Not "oh my God, best biscuit I've ever had" yummy, but still very good. The food however, was not as delicious. It was a busy morning for them, but I would not come back here. Well, actually I would come back here, but just not for breakfast. I would love to try their lunch and dinner foods.

A few friends and I went to loveless on our trip to Nashville because we had heard it was the place to go.

For an hour and a half wait? 
Meh.

Now, coming from Chicago-- Im used to the variety of breakfast/brunch options. So maybe I have just a different idea of what brunch should be. All and all, it was very plain. My favorite part was the Hash-brown casserole, and honestly I'd likely just recommend a bowl of that and some biscuits.

If you have the time, worth a stop to a "must go" breakfast place. Otherwise, i'd pass.

My wife & I were in Nashville last Fall and wanted to try out one of the restaurants I had seen on the Food Network. We were directed to Loveless Cafe and we were not disappointed. The biscuits lived up to their billing and the veggies were fresh and delicious. Unfortunately, we did not have room for dessert, but be sure you get some when you go. If you're in the neighborhood, treat yourself to a good meal - but order dessert before your meal since they run out quickly.

Excellent! I had the bbq pork omelet.  Their biscuits are great! 

Well worth the wait, there's plenty to do on their property while you're waiting.
Super great breakfast spot! Love the drop biscuits and the jam was good too! Portion size was ample and service was excellent! No complaints at all- really enjoyed this spot.

I think Loveless is the first place I've visited twice in the same week while vacationing in a new city. But once you try the biscuits you'll understand why! I tried biscuits all over nashville and these were by far the best, and the trifecta of homemade jams doesn't hurt either! For breakfast I had the country ham (which I honestly didn't love) and a side of grits (which were amazing and cheesy). I tried bites of my friends' bacon (I'm not usually a bacon person but this was maple-y and smokey and awesome), sausage gravy, and hash brown casserole and I loved it all. We went back for dinner and the highlight was definitely the pulled pork/house BBQ sauce! The sweet potatoes and Mac and cheese balanced out the meal with all of my favorite sweet, savory, cheesy comfort foods. You 100% will be stuffed when you leave!

Absolutely LOVE this place! We had a party for a travel hockey team this past Saturday, and everything was perfect.  Our waitress Tia did a fantastic job taking care of 16 adults and even more 10-11 year old kids always with a smile on her face.  Highly recommended

My best friend and I enjoyed our brunch meal at Loveless Cafe. 

We're tourists and made this our "on our way out of town" meal since we knew Loveless is known for having long waits (and especially on a Sunday!). We had a party of two and were quoted a 1 hr. and 20 min. wait time - and we waited exactly that! We had no problem, though. After all, we had nothing to do but drive back home that Sunday. It also helped us work up an appetite! 

I want to give the brunette hostess her props, she kept a smiling face on and greeted every guest that walked in with a positive attitude and smile. I know that for myself, that would've been hard considering she deals with person after person, same question after same question! 

The biscuits definitely lived up to expectations! They had a sweet taste - different than biscuits you'd get from Cracker Barrel or your typical southern restaurant. Don't fill up on them, though! The food is where it's at. 

Cons: Not a lot of waiting room in the actual restaurant building which sucked when it rained, however, there were plenty of places on property to walk around and look at while bored waiting. Unfortunately, rain doesn't make for good photo opportunities outside so that was unfortunate. 

TIP: They don't take reservations on weekends. Get there early.

1st time to this quaint and cozy cafe. Our waiter Mark had the gift of gab- very pleasant and welcoming. Once seated he brought over complimentary warm biscuits with assorted jams and butter. Yum! I decided on the local fav chicken and waffles. My husband had delicious pancakes and crisp bacon. No complaints. 

Afterward we checked out the gift shop and their smokehouse. It was very interesting learning how the meat is smoked, quite the process. Great experience

This is one of this loudest restaurants in Nashville and it was extremely annoying. On a busy Friday night, we could barely hear each other at our table for four.  The service was very slow...it was nearly 40 minutes after we were seated before we got our drinks. The food is excellent and our waiter was very nice, just overworked.  Even with the great food, we will not be coming back- too many other restaurants in Nashville. 
.
This is our second visit to the Bierhaus, we're enjoying eating through the menu. Great Food, Beer and Service.

Great food, and fabulous service! The hostess was very welcoming, and our server was on it! Just expect a wait time almost anytime of the day, especially on weekends. We ended up waiting only 20 minutes on a weekday around 2pm. On Sunday we went for brunch and it was over an hour wait. But that's to be expected at such a popular place. What's great is that as you wait, you can walk around the property to the shops and so forth!

I had looked forward to going here for months since I heard it was opening. I was so disappointed when I did. First off it took nearly five minutes before I could get a server and it wasn't even the one responsible for our table. Then the server that was supposed to be ours decides to show up with teas that we didn't even order but not our beers. The the Doner Kebab that I do loved in Germany and was on the online menu was no longer available. I was so upset I just walked out.

The food was so good. The service was pleasant and fast. Everyone was well trained and seemed to work as a team. The fast paced flow was flawless and uncompromising. When you get good service and you see good service being presented it makes your meal that more enjoyable.  I had steak and eggs. The cook or someone from the kitchen brought my meal out with a smile and seemed to have great pleasure in presenting her plate. The food was delicious.  When you have a great steak you don't need sauce.  That's blasphemous.  While the steak could have used a little more seasoning for my taste, it was still good and I did not grab the A1 bottle.  What can be said about the biscuits and jam that hasn't already been said. mmmmm...Heaven!

I went here on my first trip to Nashville and it was so good! It's way out in the burbs, so it's a bit of a drive, but worth it if you've got the time. The biscuits are a good as people say - they are so soft and perfectly buttery and they come with three equally tasting jams. My friends and I ordered the BBQ pork, fried chicken, fried catfish, and pretty much all the sides between the two of us. Everything was so good. We are all from the west coast and there's nothing like it there. The plates are giant - we could not get through it all. For dessert, we ordered the pecan pie, chess pie, and banana pudding and all were sinfully good. My personal favorite was the banana pudding. I would go there anytime! 

They serve breakfast all day and they have a different special every day. If you want hot chicken, they serve that on Monday. I was bummed I missed it. The cafe is in a cute little redone motel complex  complete with a parking lot. Super good southern eating, totally worth it.

Really wanted to like this little place, however it is overrated. The wait was 2hrs. Bathroom needed cleaning to the point I had to go outside to get some fresh air. On top of that once I received my food there was a long strand of dark hair fried into my fried green tomatoes. Biscuits were great!! If it wasn't for the waitress being attentive, I would have given this place 1 star. Beware. Find a Cracker Barrel. Not worth the wait at all.

They had me at wine on tap. I came in on a Monday night for dinner and was excited to find that parking was free. This is usually not the case although valet is $5-8. There was no wait and we were quickly seated and quickly wined. Our server was fantastic and knowledgable about wine. I ordered the lamb shank osso bucco with vegetable root hash. It was perfectly fall off the bone.  My partner in crime had the trout on a bed of raisin couscous that was good but not quite to the level of the osso bucco. Im excited to learn that City Winery allows you to buy the wine on tap in a growler type (but clearly not) fashion. I recommend trying the Obsidian Ridge Cab Sauv on tap.

So I have been back another time since the glaad concert. Again to see Meghan Linsey. Surprise surprise.

The second time was Meghan Linsey with Sawyer Fredericks.

Parking this time was not nearly as wonderful as last. I waited and waited and waited by the valet station - where they were all standing and fetching cars for others from the show prior... And no dice. I would estimate 15-20 minutes before I reversed enough to turn my car around to leave. 

Luckily there was a spot within walking distance as it was raining. Still strange no one wanted my money... And I always too well...

Again the seats were excellent. I was at a table next to the stage. Three seats in. With a group of acquaintances and some strangers. The tables are long so you're often mixed up close with people you don't know... But I didn't find it too bothersome. 

The guy next to me ordered a few cokes and some sort of appetizer. I had a glass of wine.

Why am I mentioning what this stranger next to me ordered? Because it appeared on my tab and was unable to be taken off.

I waited a long time to do this review on purpose. As the review is not about getting it fixed. But about the attitude at the time. As though I was lying about this single male next to me not being with me because I was a single female. 

The venue is still nice. Service seems to have gone down on most accounts.

Wow. Went here for brunch on a Sunday with a Groupon. Atmosphere is great, location is kind of isolated. Everyone around us complained about the service and we waited 45+ min for our check. We literally debated walking out and seeing if anything be would notice. They also had a weird service model where one person took your order but then other people waited on you throughout... So you never had a dedicated person to notice, that for instance, my coffee wasn't topped off for over an hour and our water was empty. 

Sorry, but this is a no. Service trumps all.
If you like raw asparagus, undercooked steak, and eating your dessert with your hands, this is the place for you! BTW the service stinks.

This place is alright! The location and atmosphere allow for a fun place to get together with a big group where you can chat loudly without having to worry about bothering anyone around you. On Friday nights they have live german music which is fun. I ordered the chicken schnitzel sandwich and wasn't too big of a fan. It was okay, but I probably wouldn't order it again. The fries were good though! My husband got the currywurst and loved it. The prices here are pretty high compared to similar places around. Overall, not too bad!

This is in the Opry mills mall.  Good beer drinking environment with the layout consisting of octoberfest tables and the liter beer mugs.  A German style band was playing while we were there making a fun interactive environment. The food on the other hand is mediocre at best.  I am German and was hoping for some decent German dumplings and sauerkraut.  Neither were very good at all.  So this is why they only get 3 stars from me.  Step up the food game and I would give a 4.

Southern cooking at its finest!!!
Biscuits and jams to die for! The best catfish I've ever had! 
Food came out quick and hot!

Would recommend to anyone! No wait. Food was out quickly and delicious at that! Friendly staff and homey environment. They have the best biscuits in the entire world. Great price for the amount of food we got!

First time in Nashville had to make the short drive to the Loveless. It reached and surpassed our expectations! A definite must see and do for anyone visiting. Our wait time for a table was less than ten minutes. The atmosphere is incredible and our server was so sweet. The food is good old country diner fare  and the biscuits are great. They must be because they make 7000 a day. Thanks Loveless for making our first stop in Nashville one of the most memorable.

The food that I ordered made this cafe seem very overrated. I picked up my friend from the airport and we drove 30 minutes to the restaurant. Luckily, we didn't have to wait, probably given that we were there at 8am on a Friday morning.

The biscuits were indeed delicious, and they were so buttery that there was no need to spread butter on them. The homemade jams were also yummy. However, the fried chicken that came with the waffle was neither juicy nor tender. Rather, it was dry and overcooked.

Not sure if I'd drive 30 minutes to visit again, but at least the scenery was beautiful on the way out there.

Went to The Basement on a whim with some friends while visiting Nashville! The band was pretty good, but it was extremely packed...like I don't know if it was even legal for that many people to be there. The bar area was extremely crowded, which made it hard to get a drink.

Wow! Talk about impressed!
I'm not crazy about southern food BUT Loveless cafe has converted me over to the south.

Now I know all the places I have been eating at didnt cook southern food the right way.

Next Saturday my husband and I are returning with our family.

Came early on a Friday morning, so the place was pretty empty and quiet.  The wait staff is fantastic! The ladies and gentlemen at the front of the house are very kind and friendly. My server, Lucas, really went out of his way to make it a personal experience for myself and my husband.  The parking lot is easily accessible and there is plenty of room for parking and visiting the surrounding retail shops Loveless owns.  

Lucas was prompt in greeting us and was able to answer all of our questions with honest answers, which is very refreshing! He was attentive but not in our faces while we ate... Again... So refreshing to have a server who understands balance! 

We ordered the Southern Breakfast Sampler, which comes with two eggs, their specialty ham, bacon, sausage, and your choice of hashbrown casserole, fried potatoes or fruit.  I ordered hashbrown casserole and Lucas made it possible for my husband to order more meat instead of a side.  A coffee, a hot tea, and two breakfast samplers = ~ $35.   Reasonably priced and, we did not mind spending the money because the service we received was great.  

First: let me rave about the hashbrown casserole.  Oh my god, it is so decadent! Creamy, tangy, cheesy, and with hot sauce, its perfect.  Some of the best hashbrown casserole I've had.  My next favorite item: the ham!  It was absolutely perfect, though I wish I had more of it on my plate!  It's tender, juicy, slightly sweet, salty, and perfect.  The bacon, when its fresh, is also very tasty.  Crispy, salty, and smoky.  I wasn't fond of the sausage by itself, but with the blackberry preserves, it was awesome.  

The biscuits were okay.  I was very enticed by the sound of them by all the reviews here.  But sadly, I was slightly disappointed when I tried them this morning.  They were a little chewy and dense, but again, with the preserves or gravy they were decent.  That's why instead of 5 stars I gave 4 stars.  The hype is a little high for this place, but I still enjoyed my breakfast.

After some awesome hikes along the Natchez Parkway this place hits the spot! I was tired and just wanted some good comfort food and then we realized how close we were to Loveless...so excited! At 4pm it was already busy but we got right in and our server was so friendly and helpful! We decided on just sharing the chicken fried chicken and then added some extra sides. 
First the biscuits came out...for some reason I've been on a real biscuit kick lately so I've had my fair share and these are some of the best. They have a good flake and a slightly salty, buttery taste; add the butter and jams and they are almost a dessert. Then the food came out and everything was spot on. I didn't think that the fried okra would taste fresh but it was some really fresh tasting okra!! The side of the day was garlic mashed potatoes and those things were garlic-y, which in my world you can never have too much garlic so they were perfect. The food all came out quickly and was still warm, a major bonus!
This place is every bit worth the hype it receives. It's good comfort food with really good friendly service.

Don't know where they came up with the name loveless because this place is full of love (insert your groan here). I chose to have my birthday dinner here on the way out of Nashville after hearing so much about it and didn't regret it one bit. Our waitress gave me my dessert with a candle on it and announced to everyone that it was my bday so everyone sang to me.

Long wait during dinnertime but well worth it. You can pass the time quickly by exploring the shops around it or playing cornhole out front. Great southern food and hands down the best biscuits I've ever had. I ended up buying their mix to make my own at home (plus a lot of other items I didn't need -  oh Loveless Cafe, you sure are smart with your marketing).

Stopped in based on reviews and we were amazed.  I'm from Milwaukee and we have great authentic German restaurants.  Bavarian Bierhaus kicked the crap out of them.  I'm German and know what laberkasse is, theirs was fantastic. I do not suggest that for most Americans. My wife ordered the pork schnitzel and it was authentic and perfection to say the least.  An odd restaurant to find in Nashville, but damn is this place good.  

Great and I mean great service.
Amazing beer selection.


Go here, you won't be sorry that you did.  I will be back!!

The Loveless Cafe was such a great experience that I find myself wanting to change my address just so I can dine here again soon. I learned about this place while planning our trip to Memphis.

Let's start with our sweet waitress, who quickly offered suggestions when we were struggling with what to order. (The menu options were bountiful and mouthwatering.) My husband and I both ended up ordering the Southern Sampler Platter and my son ordered pancakes. Let's just say that it was a good thing we hadn't eaten all day.

For my sampler, I ordered fried catfish, fried chicken and pulled pork BBQ, along with fried green tomatoes and creamed corn. (Yes, that's a lot of fried foods but I was on vacation.) I loved everything--especially the creamed corn. Yum! The fried chicken breast was tender and juicy, the catfish was lightly breaded and flaky, and the pulled pork was so tender I almost didn't need to chew.

Even though we were stuffed (and couldn't finish our entree), my husband and I decided to split a piece of their chocolate chess pie. It was rich and utterly sinful.

The next time you're in Nashville, TN, and you're looking for some good 'ol Southern cooking and hospitality, stop in at the Loveless Cafe. Your taste buds will thank you! Bon appetit!

So the complaint 2 months ago, you must of had a bad day. Parking is $9 for valet and the parking lot right next to it is $7 for 1 hour or $15 for 6 hours. The Winery is not in a bad spot. It's about a 10 minute walk from downtown.

This place deserves no less than a 4 star. The service is great. The wine selection vast and the food is pretty good. Our server Samantha was great. She explained everything and took care of use. 

If you don't come for the food they have a tour and you can purchase wine. The scotch and whiskey selection is pretty good. Not a lot of option but high quality liquors for a good price. 

Highly recommend you stop on by for the tour or the food. Or just grab some wine and enjoy the sunset and the skyline view.

Ate late lunch today around 1:30. Food was fresh, hot and plenty of it. Susan our waitress was friendly and gave great recommendations. The place was clean and organized and prices were reasonable. Only five miles off the interstate and easy to get to. Definitely worth a detour. Homemade biscuits and jams are to die for. Go if you're in the neighborhood and want great home cooking.

As a music venue City Winery in Nashville downtown near the Music City Center is now in the top ten here. Yesterday I loved the sound of roots music great Rodney Crowell singing the songs he has written, in the big room of this performance venue. The day before the Deslondes performed from the new stage, which features a great sound system and acoustics. I think the City Winery Nashville will be as well known for its music as for its tart Napa Valley wine and wines produced here, in Music City USA.

Amazing! Amazing! Amazing! Went here with my mother and the place lived up to it's hype! Make sure you give yourself plenty of time (our wait was estimated to be two hours but was a little over an hour). The drive was scenic and they have tons of activities, chairs, and cute gift shops to keep you busy while you wait. The food was to die for (the biscuits were out of this world) and the atmosphere was quaint! Couldn't have had a better brunch :)

Sooo yeah this review is going to say everything you have already read about. The biscuits are heaven in your mouth. The jam makes you reevaluate what you have been eating before. Store bought jams will never cut it again. 

My table had the country ham breakfast, fried catfish dinner, and the fried chicken dinner....everything southern! All I can say is more heaven. The greens and the hash brown casserole are must have sides you should try.

You can purchase their bacon at the country market, Hams & Jams, next door. Cajun bacon...Jalapeno bacon just gives you a glimpse of what's to come when you step foot into the store. 

We took a longer route to get to this restaraunt, and it was worth every 40 minutes

Wow! This is some awesome breakfast food! First of all, Loveless Cafe is a really neat place. There are little shops around the cafe & there are places to play cornhole using their boards while you wait. Every table gets biscuits & jam....the blackberry jam is to die for! I got a breakfast sandwich & it was yummy! Friends I was with got biscuits & gravy, breakfast ham, omelets and the breakfast bowl. Everyone left happy & no one left hungry!

Totally not my scene. Came here with out of town friends who wanted to go to a hip-hop dance night. The music was good, the drinks were fairly cheap (bottled beer was all I drank anyway. I didn't have any shotz). 

Security at the door was a little excessive. I don't think I needed to be groped like I was being processed into prison. Pretty sure my wife isn't hiding a gun in her bra, and I'm pretty sure I don't have one in my boxers. I don't think that I've every had that kind of scrutiny when trying to go into what is basically just a bar before.

As locals we usually stay away from the touristy spots but I'm glad we didn't with here! The atmosphere is wonderful! The service was a little slow but he had several tables. We started off with the giant pretzel and ordered the warm bier cheese along with the mustard. The pretzel was the best we've ever had. He ordered the wurst plate and I tried the regular brat and the smoked brat and both were on point. I've never liked saur kraut but liked theirs. I ordered the jager schnitzel and it was delicious. I ordered the fries with mine and they were good as well. Their beer selection was really good and didn't disappoint. We will be returning to listen to some live music.

Such good food and such good music that comes through here!!!!! When I come I usually love the pizza, the service and of course the wine!!!! Also the woman at the front ticket desk tonight saved all of humanity for me because I came in late to the Girls of Nashville show and she was just so kind and generous and helpful! She has mid length brown hair and was wearing a pink shirt, I don't know your name but you saved the night! Thanks City Winery!
First time here. Great atmosphere with authentic music and clothing. Served by a very cute girl named Allison. Always smiling and very knowledgeable of the menu. An overall great experience.

We accidentally arrived at a peak time, so we weren't able to be seated (and we were starving.)

Good news, though! The gift shop next door also sells food! We walked around the property a bit, poked our heads inside the main dining room to take in its charm, then headed over to the shop across the parking lot. It was darling, lots of Southern-inspired knick nacks and foodstuffs. 

We were able to get a dozen biscuits with butter and jam AND some BBQ. We ate in the car like animals, but we didn't even care how it looked. It was so good! The biscuits were the perfect size (small enough to justify going back for seconds, and thirds, and fourths...) I highly recommend you order some, even if you're not able to eat inside. 

Next time I'm in town, I'll plan accordingly and come back!

We went for breakfast and it was delicious! I had a bbq pork omelette and a biscuit with a fried green tomato and pimiento cheese. There is definitely a bit of wait (a little over an hour for 8 people) and they require your whole party to be there to put your name on the list. There are cute shops around the restaurant with souvenirs, coffee, snacks, art, jewelry, etc. to wander in while you wait. Plus, they make their own hot sauce!
Great place to have an authentic German meal. Live music, good food and excellent service. Charles took care of us. He was fantastic! Ask for Charles when you go there.

This place is an ABSOLUTE MUST VISIT when you're in Nashville. Wow is Loveless a revelation. It's about a 20 minute drive from downtown, and there can be a wait, but the food and atmosphere is well worth it. The Southern hospitality here is incomparable: the servers are warm, kind, and attentive. And this food is finger-lickin' good. Come hungry, because the portions are HUGE.

The feast begins with their famous biscuits, which are buttery, savory, and addictive...and have FREE REFILLS. Better still are that they come with sweet preserves, a perfect accompaniment for the biscuits. My friend and I then ordered the pulled pork BBQ and fried chicken respectively. The BBQ was some of the best I've ever had: tender, rich, and flavorful. The Mac and cheese and coleslaw on the side were also excellent. The fried chicken was superb - crispy on the outside, and juicy on the inside. And while I loved the food...I could barely finish because the portions were so big. 

Loveless is an absolute treat, and it's a must visit for Nashville first timers.

A Nashville native told me that "Loveless Cafe" was a "must visit" place to eat during a recent trip to Nashville.  I must agree!  There was a long wait, but we were able to quickly pass the time playing corn-hole, browsing the shops, and sampling the complementary peach tea!


I ordered the meatloaf, and it was excellent!   I can think of any other restauarant that has meatloaf that is any better!

every time we visit Nashville we go to Big Shots because their alcohol selection is much cheaper than the rest of the places down the road. That man said I'm going to give it a 3 out of 5 because the bar itself is kind of small which fits that died of personality type of field which I kind of like butt compared to the other bars in the area it doesn't hold a candle to them. It's just really small the clientele of the people are not the best it just came match up to the places that's around it but me and still a cool little bar always have loud music just like the other 4000 bars downtown Nashville but the drink prices are excellent so I will be back

Just ok , it's a neat little place but if you base ur review just on the food it's just ok 
Prob won't eat here again 
Wait staff was friendly and helpful and kept out drinks full didn't have to ask for anything 
For five stars for the staff 

Ok on the food 
I ordered the hot chicken plate with Mac and cheese and turnip greens 
And biscuits of coarse 

Hot chicken was good but wasn't hot had like a luisiana hot sauce over it  good but needs more heat 
Mac and cheese was average little dry 
Turnip greens was good but it was hotter than the hot chicken 
Couldn't hardly eat the greens for it burning my throat 
And the famous biscuits was just a biscuit nothing impressive I've had better biscuits at Hardee's 
In all it was a disappointment cause I've wanted to eat here for two years and when I came the food was better than what I can cook at home

My wife got the dark meat chicken plate 
And she said was not good at all

Oh my goodness I can't say enough good about this place! Some locals in Tennessee told me to check this place out because I was visiting from California and was that a great suggestion! The staff was super friendly, the biscuits were to die for with their home made sauce and the omlett I had was delicious. This place is definitely something you should check out if you are in Nashville.

Food - everything that we got was excellent.  Our family tried the schnitzel (both pork and chicken), both which were crispy on the outside and tender inside.  The salmon was tender with a crispy skin.  The mashed potatoes on the side were smooth and creamy, and homemade pickles on the side.   We also tried the spatzle instead of fries--it's an egg noodle.  My wife thought they might be homemade, but not sure.  

Ambience - This place is very family friendly.  It reminded me of being at Disney.  Even though many people were having beer, it doesn't feel like a pub/bar.  It's brightly lit, again taking away from the pub feel.  It's a giant area, and there were many couples that were seated by themselves at tables meant for around 8.  

Dessert- we had the sampler.  The black forest cake was very good: cold, tasty whipped cream, and did not taste like it was from a box.  The apple danish is sort of a warmer/moister version that I'm used to, but very good and worth getting.  Lastly, the pretzel bread pudding: too hard and not moist.  Not sure if we got a bad piece, or it's supposed to be like that.  

Beer- We didn't have any, but most people around us had beer.  Many had the samplers, which consist of 4 smaller glasses.  

Price- a little more than expected, about 20% more.  But it's in a touristy mall, so it's expected.  

Overall, a pleasant surprise.

We went to a pod cast show at the beginning of December.  My biggest complaint is that I purchased VIP seats that turned out to be at the literal back of the room--like literally we were against the back wall.  They made some noise about it being on an elevated section and what not but it was in no way better to be at the back than the front.  The balcony seats honestly would have had a better view.

I agree with the other reviewers about the wine, but it was definitely overpriced and nothing special.  We both enjoyed our food but it was a limited sampling to be sure.

Buyer beware--if you're going for a show, avoid the VIP seating (or pay better attention than I did because I honestly had no idea this would be at the back of the room) and sit closer to the front.

This location has great atmosphere and has fast become one of the best venues for the small and intimate music that Nashville is known for.  I highly recommend it for a fun show, as they have a good wine and cocktail list.  HOWEVER, I equally recommend that you eat before you arrive.  The food started out as reasonable quality when they opened, pricey but not bad for a music venue, but wow has the situation deteriorated.  I attended a show and ordered dinner this past Monday night, and what a disaster.  My $15 hamburger took a full 45 minutes to arrive and was so overcooked I could hardly eat it.  The waitress offered to have it re-cooked, but the music was starting, and I sure didn't want to wait another 45 minutes.  When I inquired about a half-hour into the wait what had become of our food, I was astounded when she answered, "I know, it's slow, I'm sorry, but the restaurant is really busy tonight."  This was a reference to the other half of the house, outside the music venue, and to be told their food took priority was just ridiculous.  I am confident it was not her fault, as I could see no one around us had food either, and we had arrived early, a full hour before the show, to avoid this exact problem.  Diners beware and skip this if you can, but the music and the bar selections are good.

I loved Loveless!
#mesocheesy #tooeasy #ilovelove

If you've got some time to kill, head 30 minutes outside of Nashville to the Loveless Cafe. It's known by many in the area as having the best gosh darn breakfast in all of Tennessee! Yeehaw! And biscuits are their jam!!! (get it...? biscuits have jam on them...? sooo....biscuits and jam...? yeaaaaa).

The menu is so expensive it's nearly impossible to pick which delicies to scarf down. My usual thing is I want to try as many things as possible at new places so I went with the Biscuit Sampler Platter for $11.99. You can then choose 4 biscuits from: Fried Green Tomato & Pimento Cheese, Barbeque, Country Ham, Fried Chicken, Bacon, Sausage or Steak. I went with the Ham, Chicken, Sausage and Bacon because meat! All were good but let's be real, bacon makes everything better. Actually the plain biscuits with some jam preserves were the best thing of all - even better than my meat between the bread.

If you have to wait for a table, they have some cute shops outside the restaurant. Even if you don't have to wait, they are worth a stop in after dining. I bought a couple of floofy headbands for myself while there.

Loveless Cafe was a fun place to go, but the hype might have slightly exceeded the experience for me. I'm glad I went, think everyone everyone should go, but it's not a place I could see myself driving distances for again. Been there, done that.
Incredible venue with the best atmosphere and service! The food is delicious.  The wine is perfection.  And, Soplia is awesome!

Heard so much about this place. Went with 11 friends and while we waited 1 1/2 hours it was worth the wait. You can visit the shops while you wait or play corn hole. 
They were very accommodating and sat us all together. The biscuit are amazing and the sorghum was delectable. 
The country ham was a little salty however the fried chicken was to die for.  
If we are ever back in this area we will definitely visit again.

4.5

Before I get too into this love letter, I have to say that the address has always been a concern of mine. For tourists interested in coming to LC or new transplants eager to see what the fuss is, y'all should all know that this isn't Nashville proper. You will drive a good ways away from the city limits to come here. Whether you want to call it Bellevue or Pasquo, it's all the same to me. You just shouldn't call it Nashville. Doing so, you're going to be surprised why you're so far away from all the other Nashville attractions you've read about and want to see.*

Logistics out of the way, The Loveless Cafe is everything that's wonderful about living in the Nashville metro area. To begin with, driving to it on Hwy 100 from the city is something that's pretty in every season, but early fall is my favorite time to do so. The winding road and turning leaves leave no doubt that you're in the southland and you're about to enjoy some fantastic eats. The drive really prepares you for the experience. Once you arrive... yep, you're here. TLC is an old motel. I think that adds to the charm. It looks like a movie set. Having the cafe and motel unchanged (where it counts) since the '50s is a testament to the power, honor and necessity of tradition. I am so pleased to know that no soulless developer (from out of town, no less) has been able to destroy what should never be touched. I wished the city of Nashville followed suit. So, charm, drive, motel... you're caught up. Park out front or along the back and get ready to do some serious eating.

This ain't the place to be if you're on a diet or (unfortunately) have dietary restrictions. This is heavy, sugary, fried Southern goodness. A steady diet of the stuff WILL kill you so only come here on special occasions. Give your name to the nice people up front and take your seat. Pro tip: don't come here on the weekend or for brunch. That's amateur hour. Come here for dinner during the week and you won't suffer through the pain of waiting behind a family from Modesto eager to take a group selfie with a gingham tablecloth background. I have to let folks know how to do things...

Okay, you're seated. Get ready to eat all the food. Remember, no diet/restrictions. Start with sweet tea and keep it coming. Next, say 'yes' to the biscuits and keep them coming. You're going to want to try all the preserves AND the butter, so save (at least) a biscuit half for each type. They're canned on site and they're delicious. I can't choose between the peach, strawberry or blackberry. They're all addictive. Okay. Strawberry. But I wouldn't turn any of them down. Next, you're here for dinner so go all in. Depending on the day of the week, you'll be able to choose from a special menu. I don't need anything special because if you're going all in on a Southern feast, you gotta go for the chicken. Get the half fried chicken. It'll come with the back, breast, wing, and drumstick. You won't be able to finish, so eat half of the half. Why won't you finish? Well, you're going to consume a gallon of sweet tea. The biscuits are coming to your table as fast as you can eat them. Oh, and you get sides with your chicken. The choices are awesome so choose wisely. As much as I wanted to go for cheese grits and greens (man, I could go for that now; I'm hungry), I chose the fried green tomatahs and mackincheese. I was very happy with both choices. The tomaters were crispy, nicely-breaded and flavorful on their own. Plus, the serving was generous. You're not going to receive one lone, sad tomato. The mac was a bit creamier than I like (I prefer the southernized, post-church baked and a wee bit crispy mac) but it was tasty nevertheless. I wanted to end with peach cobbler but I couldn't be a hero. I was stuffed to the point of discomfort and I had a long drive back to the city ahead of me. I am pretty sure I was food drunk. It's a thing. Next time, dessert. Next time.**

*Seriously. Look at a map. Does this look in town to you?
**Next time to be determined upon consultation with my physician.

Came here to grab lunch on my way through Nashville while on a road trip with my husband. We came at around 1pm on a Saturday afternoon and wait time was minimum an hour and a half. 

I ordered the Southern Sampler Platter since I read great yelp reviews about their fried chicken and country ham and wanted to try both out for myself. The Southern Sampler Platter allowed you to pick 3 of their meats so I picked the fried chicken, country ham, and pork barbecue with 2 sides (I got the mac & cheese and mashed potatoes). All I need to say is GET THE FRIED CHICKEN!!! The chicken meat is juicy and moist and the outer skin layer is crisp and not the least bit fatty. Yummmm!!! The country ham was a little tough, not tender at all, and extremely salty in my opinion. The pork barbecue was ok- not terrible- but definitely worth a bite. The macaroni & cheese was pretty good and the mashed potatoes with the brown gravy was delicious as well. However, I didn't love the red eye gravy that we also got on the side for the mashed potatoes. And last but not least (or I should say first off in the meal), the biscuits here are amazing with their homemade jams!!! I don't love bread and biscuits but the jam here is finger licking good!! Be sure to try it out!! 

On the whole, this restaurant is an awesome brunch/lunch spot and if I'm ever in Nashville again I will definitely come back here!!

I have been to many shows at the City Winery Nashville. The upstairs lounge is a great intimate venue where one can choose their own seats. Chairs upstairs are padded, much more comfortable than those in the main room downstairs. The shows have all been great. Service is attentive. Although the Food is tasty, I wish that the menu would get an update as it doesn't seem it has changed in quite awhile. I attended several shows within a few weeks time and could not bear to eat another meal there the last time around.

I've eaten at the Loveless many, many times and couldn't believe I've never left a review. Yes, this is a touristy place. Yes, there's apt to be an extra-long wait. Yes, it is all worth it! The food is wonderful and the service is great. Their veggies are all fresh and perfectly seasoned. The biscuits are fluffy and hot. Preserves are delicious on those biscuits! I've never had a bad meal here!

Great southern style food. Nice place to stop and get some breakfast or lunch. Biscuits were really good. You might have to wait before being seated, but it went really fast. I had a sampler, which consisted of fried chicken, smoked turkey, and country ham. Everything was really good as well as the service.

A place known for its biscuits? Sign me up!

I perused Yelp for restaurant ideas prior to my trip to Nashville. This was on my itinerary before I even showed up, so I was surprised to see a pamphlet advertising this restaurant in my hotel lobby! I had no idea that it was sort of a Nashville institution!

At 9:30 AM on a Monday morning we had a 15 minute wait. We were given a buzzer and informed that it worked everywhere on the property, so instead of waiting in the restaurant building, we walked around to the "Hams & Jams Country Market" and "Lil Biscuits Gift Shop" to check out the wares.

Once seated we were immediately presented with a platter of fresh biscuits, jams and butter. I had to control myself and not eat the entire plate prior to ordering non-biscuit food. I ended up ordering the Southern Sampler Platter which came with country ham, bacon, sausage, eggs, and a choice of hash browns or grits. I selected the hash browns which were, frankly, not great. I did try my sister's cheese grits and had an immediate sense of regret due to my choices. Live and learn. 

My sister ordered the barbecue, which turned out to be pulled pork. This was delicious, and it was way better than my meal. 

Food portions were huge. Service was good. The place had a diner-y feel. 

My sister picked up some ham from their store since they had some conveniently small portions vacuum sealed.
Great food, great service and fun atmosphere with authentic German music! I recommend for anyone who enjoys German food

While wandering around the chintzy Broadway/District area, walk right past Big Shotz and don't stop in.

The "shotz" that they have are all pretty disgusting and taste like a hangover waiting to happen. While cheap, I just don't think it's worth it. They come in a small cup (larger than a shot glass but much smaller than a solo cup), so it's hard to enjoy your drink while also listening to the music.

The venue is also not well-designed. The bar area is very small, making it difficult to get your order in. We were also trying to stand near the band and kept having to move over so staff could access the back rooms for more beer/liquor bottles. Just not a pleasant experience overall!

Wine tour and the ladies who did it-- AMAZING, sweet, and absolutely Amazing at their jobs.  

When we went on the tour, we left our table and left items there. Returned and they dumped out our drinks  asked politely if they could refill a few. The manager said he would comp them and then went back to the waiter who said they were all empty and then said he would take only half off. We all paid $51 for a tour. Giving them $300 in business. 

The sad part is we were planning of buying 6 bottles and after not being able to give us a few mimosas on the house, they lost all that business we would have given to them if we purchased the wines. 

They need a refresher on customer service.

My husband and I loved this place. It was s little bit of a drive from downtown Nashville but absolutely worth the trip. The manager and our waiter Owen were so welcoming and did a great job. The biscuits and jam were so good I could have just ate them. The southern sampler let us try a little bit of everything and the banana pudding at the end was awesome. Portions were large so doggie bags were needed. I would definitely eat here again!

My food was fine, but didn't leave a good OR bad impression.  

Overall, this restaurant reminded me of a Cracker Barrel.  
(Food wise, over-packed dining area. Which makes everything loud, because of too much talking at once.)
I know they are famous for their biscuits and preserves...


And the  cafe's history. I'm sure it was pretty cool, way back in the day. 

But it seemed like  The atmosphere is about Merchandise, more then it is food.  

*Cracker Barrel has a shorter wait and a really fun store.

I went to a concert there where they offered a general admission standing area for the first time. Don't do it! There wasn't a seating map online so I figured GA is always in the front, right? We were shoved in a back corner, roped off like animals. And they had put a (limited) bar for us in the GA area too, but it was in a front corner instead of behind us?? So it took up more of the standing room that people would want to be in. Made no sense. Everyone else at tables got fancy glasses and they were giving us plastic cups. We asked to upgrade to a table because we had no idea it was going to be like that and they told us they weren't allowed to do that for anyone else anymore, they had gotten in trouble with a manager or something. Probably because they didn't have enough tables for everyone from GA to move, but then we stood there the rest of the night with empty tables right in front of us. People were sitting on the floor against the wall all night, it was a joke. They stressed that it was a new thing for them so I really hope they don't keep trying it. Honestly the whole vibe of the place was weird too because there are constantly servers everywhere and I wouldn't recommend it for an artist you're really excited to see

Place is very popular so be ready to wait, but they do a pretty good job of moving things along. You get all you can eat biscuits which is pretty nice, not the best biscuits in the world but they get the job done. I guess their chicken is supposed to be something special but I found it to just be all right. Same with the country fried streak it was just ok. I will say the sides were amazing, great cheese grits, Mac and cheese and hash browns. Good food but not mind blowing, I didn't see what the big attraction was.

First, this venue has promise. I came for a multi-day corporate team event, so I haven't been for the nightlife or a la cart dinner yet. It has a large bar on both floors, ample space for patrons and/or large groups, and a nice looking interior.

A few of cons:

1) After parking my car in one of several available parking spots on the lot, a valet ran out to tell me I had to valet my car - which meant I had to give him the keys for my car to sit in the same spot all day. Huh?
2) The upstairs area is open to the entryway and multiple times in our meetings we were interrupted by loud groups of women squealing, something like "Like oh mah gawwwd!!"
3) The food was mediocre and healthy options were extremely limited. Fried chicken fingers aren't for everyone at breakfast, for example.

Some promise:

1) The main dining and concert areas are nice.
2) Wine on tap.

I've eaten here a few times but have never posted a review. It's a tourist fave--every time I have out of town friends in they want to make a stop at Loveless. As mentioned it's not really in Nashville proper, it's kind of out by itself away from everything. There's usually a wait and it's kind of pricey for what it is. All that said--it's really good food.
Down-home southern cooking is not really my favorite dining out option these days but every now and then it does really hit the spot.
Loveless does a few things really well--number one the biscuits (which are much better than a certain biscuit competitor in Nashville). Number two is fried chicken--it's really crispy and tender without being too greasy. The sides are all solid. I opted for mac'n'cheese (super creamy like I like it), fried green tomatoes (spot on) and I doubled down to add turnip greens brewed in pot liquor--which, though not a greens connoisseur ended up being the highlight of my entire meal surprisingly enough (very, very good). I went with a half chicken on my recent order and had enough for lunch the next day. Way too full for pie though!
Interestingly enough the sweet tea is good but only semi-sweet. As I rarely opt for sweet tea that was somewhat of a surprise 'cuz in a down home southern space like this you'd expect it to stick to your teeth from sugar overload. It doesn't which was kind of a nice surprise--Loveless: classic southern without descending to lowest denominator.

Great food but be prepared to wait for a table. They do have shops for you to browse (tad pricey for me) but if you buy something the have a store to ship your purchase.  The menu had a wide variety of very interesting meals my wife chose the fried chicken which she said was finger licking good. I had the breakfast with county cured ham. I was glad I asked Cindy about portion size. They are large my wife and I brought some of our meal home. It was well worth the wait. We'll stop again for a meal

Came here to see Darrell Scott last night. Went by myself so was able to score 3rd row with a great view! The room was just beautiful, with plenty of space for walking to bathroom and such. 

I had dinner at the concert, a few glasses of the City Winery Chardonnay, the crispy Brussels sprouts, and the wild mushroom risotto balls. The brussels sprouts were a stand out, with a tangy vinaigrette and feta.

The only aspect of this review that brings it down to 4 stars is slightly off service. Understandably, it was dim in there during the concert, however, our tables waitress came to our table 3 times... each of which I attempted to get to attention, each of which she completely ignored me. To the point the gentleman next to me noticed and made a comment to me about it.

All in all, it is a wonderful spot with delicious food. I will be back for a dinner in the dining area, and hopefully a few more concerts.

my FAV biscuits!! worth the drive. 

PROTIP: order biscuits to go and eat them in a park or at home! they will still be warm 20 min later (Which is what i usually do) 

the breakfast food is aites to me (but i dont like heavy breakfasts to start my day). 

tourists: watch out for the drive. this isnt technically located in "nashville" but 20 minutes west of nashville.

3.50 stars.  The opposite of love is indifference.  And that is fully clear at Loveless as you will find delight in nearly everything that they serve.  Probably the most amazing part of the Loveless experience is the sheer size of your plate.  I had pulled pork, fried chicken, fried okra, mac and cheese, and cheddar grits all on the same plate - sort of.  The portion I ordered was so large that it did not all fit on the plate.  As for the actual food?  Aside from being tremendous, it is also delicious though I would give a definitive edge to Monell's for best breakfast I have experienced in Nashville (note: I haven't been to Arnold's Country Kitchen yet).  Still, this is the place that most people will talk about in Nashville, and it's at least worth a visit.

Last night my wife and I ordered two drinks, hot chicken egg rolls (terrible idea), the chicken wings (also terrible), Brussels sprouts (pretty good if wasn't swimming in grease), and the poke bowl with tuna. The poke bowl with tuna gave my wife food poisoning and we couldn't enjoy the show. Only good part about last night's experience is the service and the music. Food is trash. My wife is still sick this morning

Fried chicken and grits at 9am on a Monday?  Why yes, I think I will.  

My husband and I saved Loveless Cafe for last on our 5-day trip to Nashville.  We decided to go on the Monday we flew out so we didn't have a wait.  Luckily, we only had a 5-minute wait and got to chat it up with the locals.  

We were seated and presented with a plateful of warm biscuits, butter and three different jams (strawberry, peach and blackberry).  

The server, who was as sweet as the jam I was enjoying, recommended the fried chicken.  I ordered eggs, fried chicken and grits.  It was the best fried chicken and grits I've ever had.  In fact, the biscuits are the best I've ever had as well.  The chicken was crisp and simply coated, juicy and moist inside.  The grits were super creamy, salted perfectly and had the right amount of cheese.  

I don't ever remember what my husband had because I was too consumed with my delicious meal to be bothered.  

What I thought was going to be an overrated and overhyped meal turned out to be one of the best meals of our trip.  I'm so glad we made the trek out to eat at Loveless.  No matter what the wait is, this is definitely worth it.

Disappointed
Lived here 35 years. 
Made reservation for 10/22 birthday dinner for wife- party of 7. You gave us a table for 6 with chair pulled up to end of table. Extremely inhospitable. We sat and ate at crowded table, while looking at an empty table for 8 the whole time. This is one day after spending $50 in gift shop a few days before on a gift collection for visiting. 
Won't be back. Too many other great restaurants.

So far so good,  I'm from Bavaria and had high hopes for this place and was not disappointed.  Food was fantastic,  we had simple things like obazta,  currywurst and leberkäse, the potato salad was great  (not my moms, but! Mmmh)  it was not warm, which that is good, not sure who came up with warm German potato salad, but that oerson should be punished! We will be back and try the haxn, roladen and schweinebraten. Can't wait!
This place was a big disappointment.  Waited over 30 mins for the fried chicken... both orders were bloody enough to spill on to the plate... poor waitress had to handle it... Sucked

AVOID THIS PLACE! The staff is absolutely horrible. They overcharged me and were incredibly rude when I tried to question the bill. They even got a bouncer involved, embarrassing me into just paying it. The following day my credit card company called and saw multiple charges that looked fraudulent. They advised me to cancel my account and get a new card (which I did). 

Too much energy was required for just a dive bar, and there are so many better spots to choose from in downtown Nashville. I truly don't know how they stay in business and I certainly will never be a returning customer.

Maybe we're idiots, or maybe we're not. Puja P had her heart set on seeing a show here but we hovered under the Basement's "USE ALLEY ENTRANCE" sign having no idea where to go. The front door was locked. The alley gate was locked. We heard merriment and saw Christmas lights underneath the balcony floorboards but could not imagine how to get in. 

We'd been an hour late to the start of the show. Was it already over? That would've been in line with our experiences of everything in Nashville closing after 10pm. It was only after admitting defeat that it occurred to us that you have to walk literally DOWN THE BLOCK to the BACK of the house to get in. Jesus. In New York City, alleys are adjacent to houses, not behind them.

While Karry L used his sexual prowess to hail a cab, Puja P and I cut across some backyards to briefly check out this newly imagined entrance. Sure enough, there was the bouncer, who told us: "I just got a text message from the bar, he said to stop charging the cover so you guys get in free." Woot! 

(Later on, Puja P tells me that he didn't get any such text message. But how do you know?! The cover was otherwise $5)

Just from hovering inside briefly, it looked like a cute, intimate space, rough around the edges in a good way. The bit of music we heard was a girl + guitar deal. There's a little outdoor deck for nicotine escapes, which explained all the noise we'd heard standing outside. Then Karry L appeared, hangin' out the passenger side of the cabbie's ride. We should've figured out the ingress situation earlier.
