Worth a visit as a tourist? Yes, I think so. It still isn't located in the most convenient location if you have other destinations afterward and don't want to drive or get a cab, but at least now we all know how to get in. Because you've gotta start somewhere.

If you're visiting Nashville and you don't go here, did you really visit Nashville? ALSO- if you're from the Nashville area and have never been here, can you even call yourself a local? I love breakfast food and you can never go wrong with Loveless. Definitely worth the long wait for those amazing biscuits

The food wasn't all that bad. I order the garden omelette, it tasted good but need to add seasoning flavor to spice it up. 

The place is nice to see a lot of famous people photos with an autograph.

The service and the food are outstanding. They managed the 45 minute wait with appropriate discussion and options for walking around their facilities. The fried chicken was outstanding (not as good as Bubbas in Dallas) and the biscuits were tasty as well. It is about 30 minutes outside of Nashville but worth the experience!

This place is hyped up more than it should be. The biscuits are great, staff is always friendly, the buildings and shops are adorable. However- we've never been impressed with our meals. The fried chicken is dry, the omelettes are bland, pulled pork is greasy, and sides are always far too salty. The biscuits are the only thing that keep me coming back but I'm at the point where I don't know if that's enough anymore

We came for Burger Week, yes, rather strange timing, but I'm so glad we did. The burger was excellent, cooked perfectly, and I loved the mozzarella, fried onions and what I think might have been thousand island dressing called aioli. When anything is served on a pretzel bun, it's like having a treat for dinner, because I savor the bun separate from the burger. I wish I had known about the fresh sauerkraut on the side because I would have skipped the hot bacon spinach salad (which should have been in a bowl). 

So that was good enough, but then the pretzel bread pudding put it over the top. Anyone who knows my reviews, knows that I love a bread pudding. This gets 4 forks (top rating) for sure on my blog: https://breadpuddinglovers.blogspot.com/. It's luscious.

I came here a couple days ago around 11am before the lunch rush and we got seated right away. The cafe looks like it has been well kept and definitely has the old school feel. When arriving you can definitely tell that this is an attraction with its set up of small gift and grocery shops located around the cafe. 
Upon sitting down you can tell it's starting to get busy around us. It took a small wait for our server to come to us initially however that is the only small "issue" if you can even consider it one, that we encountered. Once we met her she took our drink orders and proceeded to bring some of the fresh biscuits and jam out. This little things were so good, I can see why this is a popular item. The biscuit is rather more chewy and dense than dry and flaky. The butter and jam on top compliments it perfectly. 

I was torn between several things on the menu but ultimately decided on the fried pork chops and eggs with hash brown casserole. My cousin went for the chicken & waffles. Oh my word, the pork chop was a win! It's perfectly cooked, not overly done so that it's dry and has the perfect level of crisp to it. They're thin chops with the bone in but they were still juicy and flavorful. I loved dipping it in the side of gravy this give you and then breaking into my over easy egg, it was perfection. I was also very happy with my hash brown casserole. The cheddar cheese they used is amazing. I also had an bite of the chicken and my cousin said it's the best he's had so far on his visit here. The chicken breast had a great batter as the skin was super flavorful and the meat itself was not dry at all.

Throughout the meal, our server was very attentive and even brought out a side of soda for me to refill, I had yet to drink even half of my glass yet! Also the biscuits were refilled before we could even ask. 

Overall I am pleased with my experience here and glad it's only a short drive for me. I'll definitely be thinking of loveless as a go to spot for future visitors.

I came here for brunch on Sunday not knowing what to expect. My friend bought a deal on Travel Zoo and we were both pretty excited to actually be able to go out for Sunday brunch, since we are both usually working a brunch shift on Sundays. The place was fairly easy to find, and they had their own parking lot, which is a plus for a restaurant so close to the heart of downtown Nashville.

The building was enormous yet beautiful, with lots off wood panels and seating available outside. Their restaurant was fairly full, but it's also spacious enough so it did not feel crowded. They had a full bar, which included wine on tap, and I saw noticed a large party all sitting together, so yes, they are able to accommodate large parties. 

We made a 12:00 reservation, but arrived 15 minutes early. We were greeted by a friendly manager who was happy to show us to our table, despite our early arrival. We asked him to sit outside since the weather was beautiful, and he gladly showed us to a table outdoors. I felt very welcomed and comfortable.

We scanned the menu, which was smaller in size than many restaurants, but I personally find that an attractive feature because it makes decision-making easier We started off with a couple of "brunch cocktails;" mine was called the Spanish Violet (I think) which had a very soft violet color, a citrusy taste, and a lemon peel garnish. My friend ordered some peach mimosa, which wasn't bad. I wish I had stuck with a classic mimosa, or maybe the brunch cocktail that had orange juice in it because the more I drank my Spanish Violet, the less I liked it. 

For an appetizer, we ordered the pastry platter, which came with a wide assortment of delicious pastries, butter, and apple butter. This was probably my favorite part of my dining experience, and I highly recommend starting with this if you dine hear for brunch.

For entrees, I ordered the vegetable frittata and my friend had the huevos rancheros. They were OK I suppose, though I would question what they think a frittata is. Both of our entrees were drizzled with might have been sriracha, which I loved, but my friend did not since she is sensitive to spicy foods. We were full after we finished, so redeemed our coupon, received our check, and that's all she wrote.

The manager did a great job creating a great first impression, and really setting us up for a wonderful dining experience. If only our server followed suit. My biggest complaint with her was how long it took her to greet us. I had my phone with me, so I was able to check the time in semi-regular intervals since I had somewhere to be at 2:00, and I remember it took our server at least 5 minutes to even acknowledge us. Luckily, the had water carafes on the table, so we did not have to wait for her to drink some water. After sitting down, it took about 10 minutes to order our brunch cocktails and another 7 minutes or so to order our appetizer. I understand servers get busy and weeded, but we were one of three tables outside, and even though inside was busy, they had plenty of open tables, so surely, our server could not have been that weeded.  Luckily, the kitchen was working at a regular pace and there were food runners on the clock because it did not take us very long to get our food. While we were munching on our pastries, our server took our entree order, which was at least 20-25 minutes after sitting down. Afterwards, I only saw her twice; once to actually check on us while we were eating our entrees, and again to deliver the check. On one hand, maybe she thought that my friend and I were the type who needed space, so she didn't have to be around so much, but it was also the way she spoke with us and how promptly she took care of a neighboring table that implied she did not care for us (maybe because we're young? I work in a restaurant, I know how much it sucks to deal with college-aged customers).

Our entrees and brunch cocktails were taken care of because of the coupon, but the check was still almost $25 dollars because of the pastry platter (which I knew wasn't included in the coupon) and taxes. Our server ended up charging us for the pastry platter for 4, rather than for 2. I brought it to the attention of the manager, who was the same person who seated us, and he said he would change it. Instead, he took it off of our bill! 

Overall, I had an OK experience. I would have left four stars if our service was better, but maybe also two stars (perhaps a little harsh?) if the manager wasn't so accommodating. Would I come back? Maybe, but I probably wouldn't recommend this restaurant to a friend looking for a good brunch spot.

Yum. Those biscuits, That peach jam. My mouth is watering. The biscuits are the star - they are soft inside with a slightly thick exterior, they melt in your mouth with the right touch of salt. 

We waited over two hours for a table on Memorial Day. There were plenty of shops to look in and the view is nice enough. They had free beverages all over the grounds for guests who were waiting. I think it would serve them well if they'd set up a place to sell biscuits to guests who were waiting. They'd make a killing and guests would be less agitated as they waited. Our waiter was kind but a little over bearing. He went beyond the usual southern hospitality and I thought he was going to pull up a chair and eat with us. The fried chicken was delicious, hash brown casserole was tasty, cat fish was good. Nothing was bad but nothing - other than the biscuits - blew me away. It is well cooked southern food in a fun atmosphere.

Well, butter my butt and call me a Biscuit!!  Finally visited the world famous Loveless Cafe!  I drove there from Clarksville and took the scenic route...just a beautiful and peaceful drive.  Everything on the menu just looked so yummy. My awesome server Megan helped me out (I cannot say enough kind words about her). She just rocked!!
Ok I ended up ordering the Chicken Fried steak meal. As you can see in the photo how big the steak was. I could've put a saddle on it and rode off...lol!!  It was hands down cooked perfectly with the right seasoning. Had 3 sides:  Mac & cheese, mashed potatoes, cream corn which was amazing. I couldn't finished it...but guess what's on the menu tonight. 
Really enjoyed walking around to their other little shops as well as looking at the memorabilia on the walls up the cafe.

This place is everything I wanted it to be. A bit kitsch and cute and all the biscuits I can eat. They're buttery. They're good. Less flaky than I anticipated but still oh so perfect. I actually like the fact that it's a bit inconsistent in cooking some are a bit more brown or less so. The service is amazing and friendly. If you're not anticipating eating a lot, the a la carte orders (ie biscuits and gravy) are perfect size. 
It's totally worth a trip here when in Nashville. I love the fact that if you don't mind eating at off hours you can make reservations. I stopped by the shops and wanted to buy everything.

What a fun little booze stop! $4 shots and jello shots $3 drafts..have a special after 5 p.m. monday,Tuesday, Wednesday  $5 draft free refills till keg runs out..live music..visited in the day time wasn't crowded, however stopped in at night was very smokey so had to leave...
Nice location, the shop is great but was not that impressed with the famous food! Still worth the trip through!!
Got the Ruben rolls and were disappointing. However the atmosphere and beer were great. Next time I would go for the chefs special.

This place is a decent enough concert venue but the chairs are not made to sit in for any length of time.  They feel like sitting on stadium bleachers after  a while. The staff is courteous and efficient.  I agree that the 25% tax on drinks is a rude surprise, especially when the pour is on the lighter side. The only dish I tried was the smoked bone marrow. It was okay, But the bread must have been very expensive as there are only 2 small thin toasted slices. The menu stated preserved lemons in the dish. I assume the lemon was supposed to be in the gremolata, but there was no citrus or acid notes and the garlic dominated the whole dish.

I came here as a new customer tonight and was sadly disappointed. There were multiple advertisements for "lowest priced drinks downtown" and "$2 draft beers and $3 bottles until 2:00 am". 

The drinks were actually $5 for a bottle. If there are any "happy hour" specials in the future I definitely won't be taking them seriously.
The burgers were great. Big portions of fries and onion rings. Our server was very friendly. Will be back!

Went to this place for a drink and it is a MUST!!!  We ended up leaving then going back because it was such a great time! The atmosphere is awesome, the beer is awesome, the food is incredible, and the staff was VERY friendly! If you are in Nashville you MUST go here!

Great venue for a show,  Saw Arlo Guthrie's 50 year show here, and when the first scheduled show was cancelled due to snow City Winery was great to contact early, and gave if the option of a full refund or to hold onto the tickets for a new date. We held the tickets and enjoyed a terrific show. The valet parking was spot on, and the venue itself was overall charming and inviting. The teperature, lighting, acoustics and ambiance was outstanding and the seating at the dining tables was a little tight but comfy.
The staff from valet to host to servers were all quite good and the wine and food were very good and reasonably priced. Overall, I'm sure some come fond little things to be picky about, but I had a great experience and would not hesitate to dine and see another show here in the future, and that's 5 star worthy for me.

When we finally found it and you get pass the long wait   We enjoyed our trip we are breakfast eaters and they serve it all day   Ham is extra Salty but if you dip it in the gravy wasn't so bad. I had some fried green tomatoes they was yummy.

The best service I've ever had!!! Not only was the food phenomenal, the bartenders made the experience one to come back for. Jenna was a sweetheart, Kait was a delight and Jason and Josh were absolutely hilarious. Whether it was busy or not I never had to wait for a thing. You won't find better bartenders anywhere. The frisky frog definitely lucked out with them

This place is so hipster!  Even still, I enjoyed my visit here.  Our movie was showing in the upstairs theatre which is TINY!  You can't really have a bad seat in this theatre (unless you're a short person).  You'll want to arrive early if going with a group so that you can have seats together otherwise it's highly likely you'll be separated.  We went to a matinee and for two tickets it was $17.  They have the classic popcorn and sodas at the concession, but you can also get hummus and craft beer and other hipster things.  We went with a large popcorn and large coke for $13.  You can get refills on both for $1 each.  There is a very small lot right next to the theatre for parking.  Once you get your ticket they will provide you a pass to place in your windshield (this ticket is good for 2 hours before and after the show in case you want to check out some of the local shops or restaurants).  If you can't find parking there, there is a paid lot directly adjacent to the theatre.  Overall we had a very pleasant experience at this theatre.  There are also several highly reviewed, affordable restaurants and bars mere feet from the theatre should you want to grab a bite or drink before or after your show.

The Family Was had a great run on Greenwood Ave. It really was East Nashville's version of the Cheers bar where everybody knows everybody. It makes me sad to drive past this shuttered location, but I look forward to the Wash reopening in their new location later this year. It will never be the same, but perhaps it will still be great.

So far this venue has been able to book some of the top artists I've seen in a while. I went to one show that was sold out so the venue was very packed and crowded. Luckily I'm able to go back for most shoes so I watched it from side stage where I had plenty of room. Overall it's a good venue with good staff and good shows.

The Belcourt is amazing. It's so wonderful to have a theater so historic, beautiful, and unique in town. From classics to indie flicks, they have it all. Service is always wonderful and they have so many fun and exciting events as well, including after-showing interviews with directors. So grateful to have a theater like this in Nashville.

A go-to place for one evening when we are in Nashville.  Food is good, entertainment is good, staff is good, atmosphere is OK as it's just a hotel dining room but that's easy to ignore.  It's the entertainment that your there for and some are great and some are not so and that's what makes it fun.  Always on my list of places to go when asked by friends going to Nashville.
LOVED their sauces. Wish they were a big enough place to bottle and sell them, would have been worth checking my luggage to being them home! Fun atmosphere too.

Giving this place five stars based on my experience the past couple of Thursday nights.   First of all, this place is much cleaner, newer, and fresher
than any of the other bars on the street.  The stage and lighting are phenomenal, and the band, Smashing Pilots is OUTSTANDING!  Geared up in grunge, these guys rocked the roof off the place.  I couldn't believe my eyes or ears... all 90s rock!  Unlike anything else in Nashville, definitely a MUST SEE.

A friend gifted us a dual membership to the Belcourt for Christmas last year.  I have always loved this place but this year I've attending more movies/events due to the membership.  I cannot express enough how in love I am with the Belcourt!!  

It's a little like a step back in time every time we attend a movie or event here.  The concessions are reasonably priced and they have local beer on tap!!  PLUS members get a discount on tickets AND concessions!  

I encourage everyone to support this wonderful theater!

We stopped here for a late lunch after reading some of the reviews on Yelp. 
I had the Drifter sandwich and my wife had the pork BBQ sandwich. Both were excellent! They also had 2 for 1 beer specials. 
Will definitely stop here again.

I can't really speak about the food, except the tater tots which...seriously who doesn't love tater tots.  

Drifters is a dive bar in the best sense of the term.  No frills, Cold drinks, laid back place.  Great beer list, everything from High Life to a good local craft selection.

My wife and I came because we heard the music floating through the air one night.  Sat on the back patio and listened to Luella Woods and Tim Caroll swap off singing and playing with some killer local talent playing with them.  

This has become our Summer place to come and grab a drink and listen to some music.

Being a huge fan of indie films and documentaries, I absolutely love the Belcourt.  I have never had a theater experience quite like it.  The staff is wonderful; they are passionate about the movies and their fabulous venue and they have a phenomenal sense of humor to boot.  I have only been once so far to see Altered States and we won a float in a sensory deprivation tank!  Now that I have permanently relocated to Nashville, I will be popping in on the Belcourt quite a bit.

I'd like to "wash" this place right out of my hair! Though our waitress and trainee were great, sorry but it's just not as "cool" and "hip" as it seems to try so hard to be. You have your magazine reading, texting, arrogant hostess, your red, ripped bar stools held together by black tape and questionable menu. Gorgonzola chips were tasty but the chips, we know, were from a bag. The "pies", served in a to-go pie tin, had way too much cheese on them and not much else. I totally get wanting that, oh, seedy, sort of eclectic feel about a bar of this sort but can't help feeling we, as customers, deserve more. Lots of competition out there folks!
Couldn't ask for a better home bar. We always look forward to Summer nights on the porch listening to music here.

Came by with coworkers for a few drinks after work. Chris at the bar is super cool and made an excellent beer recommendation for me. 

There wasn't a live band going only the point but as someone with 10+ years as a DJ I could say the music equipment here is quite good. I would definitely come back to here some live music.

Awkwardly set up venue. The best view will be facing the stage because near the bar or anywhere else you won't be able to see anything past the beams. Overall, an okay experience. The box office is cash only.
For great music.... This place can compete with any in Nashville. It's out of the way but it's a hidden gem and a place the locals of East Nashville know of. You want to "feel" Nashville. Come here

I came visited this place due to a concert that was scheduled here for the artist Elohim. I will say that is aas very funny and a pretty good venue. They had an array of drinks available and everyone was generally nice. The restrooms were clean and the atmosphere was very inviting.

I will say that the main drawback lies in the fact that you can't exit and re-enter, even if u give them your ticket or anything like that. This was very annoying as a friend of mine had her purse and couldn't enjoy the show. The other bodyguard was very nice tho and let her stash it onstage in front of us. Overall it was a fun experience and I recommend checking this place out!

You don't go to the Commodore Grill for the food. You go for the music. The menu is okay and the servers are friendly, but there's never enough of them. But it's your standard bar food, and not a very extensive list, so just be prepared for that. But one of the top places to hear songwriters in Nashville.

Summary:  This is what local indie theaters around the nation should aspire to be.

I recently attended the RiffTrax event at the Belcourt after many years away from town.  The last time I had visited was when Rush released their Beyond The Lighted Stage documentary and the improvements to the theater are outstanding.

The theaters themselves retained the old school theater feel that made them so welcoming and enjoyable to a film buff.  The theater where I was viewing RiffTrax was outstanding for a live show with great sight lines and outstanding sound.

The remodeled lobby area provides good flow for those in attendance and the snack bar has a wide range of beverage choices (even for those of us who don't want something alcoholic!)

Bottom line:  I would see another show here in a split second.

Went on a Friday evening for happy hour and really enjoyed the atmosphere: nice, clean, and safe. They played a variety of music which was cool. I got the buffalo wings, well seasoned but not crispy. My friend had the catfish and fried shrimp. I tasted a shrimp and it was really good, well seasoned, and jumbo size. I'll be back because you can't beat a bar that offers $3wells with good food.
Awesome bbq with a ton of different choices on bbq sauce. Atmosphere is dive bar like with super friendly staff and great prices on drinks.

Basic medium size venue.  There is an upstairs in the back that you can look out from.  It is especially helpful, when realizing you are going to shows that are inhabited with mostly under 21 year olds who want to mosh at the slight hint of volume, it doesn't even matter if the music is moshable.  They offer an outside patio for smokers, especially helpful since once you come in the venue you can't come back out.  The bar is standard and has a spending minimum of 10$ when using your card.  Sound is ok, but once you are near the front that usually goes out the window.

I used Drifter's to cater my wedding and couldn't have been more pleased. Marc, the catering director was responsive and easy to work with. No weird hidden costs or surprises on the bill, and my guests loved the food.

What a fun venue! I've lived in nashville my whole life and have just been here for the first time. I wish I had gone for something else sooner. The ambience is very intimate but not too crowded and the sound was great. They have a balcony area with some stools that allows you to see from the back if your not a front row type of person. The bar is large, allowing for multiple orders at a time. I liked that everything was black and white inside as well, which made all the focus on the band and not the decor. I'll be happy when another artist I like comes to this place for me to go.

Starting off, I have a bit of a background in barbecue and the smoking of meats in general. It's a passion of mine and often partake in the pastime on the weekends. This fact may have affected this review slightly.

Drifter's seemed like the perfect place to go, having a night to go out to eat with a friend who had dropped into town. It was barbecue, in one of my favorite spots in Nashville, and it was......well, barbecue! We arrived to see a very southern-looking, slightly roadhouse-looking visage behind a porch that was overlooking the 5 Points area. It was gorgeous. Going inside, we were told to sit anywhere and we took a seat at the end of the bar.

Everything was great, with signage checkering the walls and not a whiff of pretension to be had in the entire place. Our server was pleasant and directed us to the many local craft beers while we browsed the menu. Not being a beer drinker, I left it to my friend to try a few. But we were mostly ready for what we came for: barbecue! The many different sauces was an exciting prospect, and I was ready to dive into every one of them. 

Ordering a pick-two combo of brisket and pork, while my friend ordered the sliders, our food arrived around 15 minutes after we ordered. My first impressions were that of excitement, and I went right for the baked beans. They were decent, however, the sauce was a bit too thin for what I imagine to be "southern" baked beans; while the beans themselves retained a bit of stoutness that told me this was not the slow-cooked baked beans I was used to.

Next came the sauces! My friend calls us sauce whores because of how much we eat and make sauce. They had 5 different ones ready for us and I wanted to get to them before I tried my pork and brisket. 2 of the sauces were highly vinegar based, which I'm not the biggest fan of, and the atomic was simply untouchable as it was just insanely hot. Settling on the sweeter, tomato-based sauce, I moved on to my main course.

The meat wasn't bad, but I really can't say that it gave me anything worth coming back for. The smoke was there, however, it was somehow just still completely devoid of flavor. The sauces also did not impress me in the least... Were they bad? No, they weren't. Was I blown away? Sadly, there are better store-bought sauces... And I hate to say any of this because I wanted to like it so badly. The place looked like a winner, had great prices and a great view, friendly staff, and good beer; the food was just lacking though. It wasn't bad, just wasn't good either.

Try this place out! Just keep things in perspective. Don't go in thinking you're going to be getting the best and you'll be happy. The fries and tots were probably the greatest part, perfectly cooked and not greasy! I just wish that their beans and meat were as on-point as the fries. I just need a bit more flavor to make the barbecue the way it should be... unforgettable!

The Drifter sandwich is pretty tasty. It's a great concept. The pork is cubed (not pulled) and the brisket is outstanding.

This is more of a dive bar than a restaurant. I had a very long wait to get my sandwich to go (at a pretty quiet time of night) and was glad I wasn't eating in. The service was not very friendly and the place wasn't very welcoming.

Coming from Australia, we weren't sure what we were getting ourselves into for a late dinner on a rainy Sunday night from the look of the outside of this place
Once inside it's a simple place with bar, table and chairs as well as TV screens around the tops of the walls with different sports shows.
The food and service was great! I had the Pick Two Dinner Combo (brisket & chicken) and my husband had the BBQ Sampler Platter. Tasted sooo good!
We would definitely recommend this place!!

This place is awesome. We drove into town for a show that was a whopping $5 cover. Cheap beers, good vibe, fun atmosphere; no complaints! Cash-only. No liquor, if it matters to ya. I love how old school it was with the vending machines everywhere. Jukebox had killer tunes. The sound system for the stage setup was perfect. Loved the back room area where the bands load-in and it had the bench seats; so great. Played pool all night/morning. We had a blast. I will def be back! \m/

Awesome staff and great venue!  Front door was super outgoing and it set a positive tone for the rest of the night.  I would suggest you get food before you show up though.  None was available other than slices of pizza

This place has had the worst customer service I have ever received. After having to leave the venue 4 hours early because of random threats from a man at the venue (who was showing his gun to fellow party-goers on NYE promoting others to request he got kicked out), we tried to discuss options with the managers to refund us at least a portion of the $200 on entrance fees my group paid just to leave within an hour of arrival. We were not able to get ahold of them via email or phone after many attempts. Biggest waste of money we have spent on what was supposed to be a celebration of my new engagement. Very disappointing.

The Exit/In is probably my new favorite small venue in town. One, they traditionally start on time. That is huge. HUGE! Especially if you are watching a band on a Tuesday night. It's also smoke-free and the bathrooms are clean. I haven't been in when it's been packed but so far I have had plenty of space to enjoy the show. The stage is high enough that anyone can see, even shorties like me. Also the decor is pretty rad. I love the sign above the bar with all the artists who have graced their stage.

So far I have seen Classixx and Run the Jewels (El-P and Killer Mike) at Exit/In. Two different crowds, both an equally pleasing experience. I should also mention that the artists head to the back after their show to sell merch. Both artists were incredibly friendly and posed for photos with their fans. This definitely adds to the charm of Exit/In.  Overall it's a solid venue!

What a nice venue this is.....
Plenty of parking (pay), lots of room to walk around, plenty of bathrooms..
plenty of good air circulation.

I went here for an event.
It wasn't a music event, it was a food event.
The place was lovely..  spacious.
I got there early enough that I got a free parking place, and didn't have to pay for the lot adjacent to the bldg.

I wouldn't mind going here to see a musical venue, one of these days..
It was very nice for a food event.

Me and my partners played a "rock gig" at this place and let me tell you, the place was B E A utiful. This joint really knows how to throw a rock show. A little smelly in some areas of the venue but nothing a little Lysol and complimentary breath mints can't fix. Only complaint is there weren't enough chairs, I feel like I threw my back out LOL haha gotta go!

I was pretty surprised by this place. It's the bar/grill for the Holiday Inn where we are staying and they have a ton of live music at night starting at like 7pm to about 10/11. The musicians are pretty impressive because, well, NASHVILLE!! Everyone here is super nice and friendly. The drinks are okay... as expected at a hotel like this. The food is pretty good. I like their buffet for breakfast.

Went out to drifters last night for the second time for some drinks and to listen to the band.  Very fun atmosphere, sat outside under near lights and the band was fantastic.  Their food is really great as well.  In the past I've had their sliders, yummy pulled chicken and pork and brisket, great fries.  Last night I only had a cup of chili, big chunks of meat in it, very filling and it was a big serving.  This is a great bar and hang out spot, I know we will be back soon enough!

What a great place!

My BFF that lives in Nashville lives within walking distance of this place and has recently discovered its greatness.  I am so thankful that she took me here.

One of the first bonding moments I had here was with the dude working the front ticket counter who was wearing a band t-shirt for the band Anvil.  We swapped stories of meeting the band (I when they came to Austin and he when they came to Nash at The Belcourt) during their promotion of the documentary Anvil, the Story of Anvil where he told me tales of the staff taking the guys honky tonking down on Broadway street.  Because this is the type of stuff The Belcourt has:  independent doc film screenings and indie movie showings that host Q&A's with film makers, actors and in this case musicians.  And who knows maybe the actual staff will take you dancing downtown.  :-)

Build in 1925 as a silent movie house The Belcourt has been lovingly preserved for all to enjoy--thank you for that!  It was even home to The Grand Ole Opry for 2 years back during the Great Depression.  I love it when communities take the time to preserve their movie art houses.  You should definitely take a glance at the architectural touches inside the theater.  

You can get alcohol here in addition to traditional movie theater fare like popcorn and soda AND you get free parking for the adjoining parking lot after you buy your movie ticket so be sure to go back and take of that before watching your film.

You can join as a member to get cool perks.  I am on their mailing list even though I don't live in Nashville just to keep up with what they are programming and showing.
Not bad for a Thursday night,but inconsistent with the mixed drinks and pricing. Good mix of music, friendly crowd.

Came here on a late Sunday night looking for food. Hog Heaven next door was closed so we stumbled through the bar into an experience unlike any other. In a corner in the back behind a counter was Buford ready to make us pretty much whatever we wanted given he had the ingredients. Springwater is a classic dive bar that often has live music but this night Buford's Little Sandwich Shop stole the show. We chatted amicably and the food, a chicken quesadilla and a cheesesteak, were very good. But despite the food it was worth it to meet Buford and have a true Nashville experience.
A super cool little independent theater that I do not frequent enough. They play classics sometimes on the weekends as well. Oh and THEY HAVE A BAR.
Black bean burger is great! very vegetarian friendly and fun environment.

Goodness gracious, I love Drifters.

We now have Edley's down the road from 5 Points, but where else can you get barbecue and Tex Mex together? This is a beautiful combination, my friends. I highly, highly recommend their pulled pork chimichanga. That sucker always has me coming back for more. If you're not of the meat eating persuasion, however, they have plenty of vegetarian options. I've never been disappointed by anything I order there.

Their patio is perfect for warm nights outside and there's also a ping pong table in the back. You're also likely to be there during a drink special! Be sure to take a look at their calendar as they have rotating weekly drink specials.

I've been to this place a few times and it is one of the few places in town that gets the right amount of smoke in the meat to not hurt the flavor. I've had the wings, pulled pork, and tonight I had the ribs. Each of these did not disappoint. The only thing preventing a 5th star is the service. Each time I've been there's been some kind of problem .Technically this should be a three star review, but the food was good enough to overcome the poor service. Tonight our server was a very attractive woman who really knew the store. But when she brought our first round of drinks where we were sitting outside, she dropped the lemon  of one of them on the not so clean picnic table where we were sitting. She actually attempted to put that dirty lemon back on the glass it fell off of. That is horrid and appalling. Our faces made her see that she was grossing us out so she removed the lemon but did not replace the drink as she should have. This kind of service is unacceptable. The outside tables are like the outside tables that many have in his or her backyard. Would you want anything in your drink that just bounced of a table that has been exposed to the elements? Hell no! Drifters is great other than the weird service you get from time to time. East Nashville is the kind of area where the Carla from Cheers mentality rules the day. But it's fun and well worth the occasional headache.

This is without apology a very basic music venue.  The size is perfect - big enough for a crowd to generate a lot of energy, small enough for everyone to feel up close and personal.  Big enough bar to keep the drinks flowing.  Perfect spot to resurrect the college experience with the White Animals.

Pro tip: I'm reliably informed that they not only offer the finest selection of Hot Pockets in Tennessee, but selections also include White Castle sliders.  I did not validate this myself, your mileage may vary, offer good while supplies last.

From the band list overt the bar - would to have seen the Hoodoo Gurus here.  Doh!

Beers were all canned and the few that we chose were overpriced. Seems that they charge more than they should so that when they do their extended happy hour specials they are not blowing profit. Service was extremely slow on a Thursday night. The brisket was great, the sauces were so-so, and the sides bland. Wish I could have had a larger portion of meat and none of the sides that came along with it. Parking lot was full, but I did get a spot about two blocks down in a more residential area.
People that use the term "dive bar" should not be aloud in here! Its simply just a "real" bar! for "real" people! I love it!

I loved this aptly named, distinctly Nashville bar and live music venue in Midtown. We visited friends for Vanderbilt homecoming and I'm glad we opted out of the downtown melee to be here. Despite the homecoming crowd, there was good service and plenty of room thanks to a spacious, warmly lit patio. I wish I caught the name of the band playing - they were really good. I didn't have a chance to try anything on the menu but there is a great selection of local brews. 

I especially loved the brooding, industrial chic decor with all its details and custom touches - machinist stools line a long steel-edged granite bar, reclaimed Jack Daniel's barrels serve as the sink base in the bathroom, and wall art features original U.S. patents for different musical instruments. I would love to have a venue like this in DC, but The Country rightly belongs to Nashville as a great homage to Music City.

Exit/In is a small/mid-size (500 people) capacity music venue in Midtown Nashville. Their calendar often features smaller artists but a variety of genres. I came here on a night where there were 3 rock bands. As the bands were smaller/local the place was not at all packed so it was nice to be close to the stage and not have my personal space invaded. 

Venue: 3.5/5
The venue is mostly standing-room only with a small upper balcony with a few select tables and also a few seats in the back of the first floor. The stage is easy to see from most anywhere you would be standing. 

Although I am a fairly tall person I noticed that the bar is super high up. If you are short you would definitely have to work to catch someone's attention as the bartenders might not see you! Behind the bar are plaques of different bands that have performed at this venue. I was surprised to see that Billy Joel, Johnny Cash and B.B. King have all graced the stage of the Exit/In. The historical aspect of imagining these artists on stage is definitely cool.  

I saw a sign that said "Tiki bar" that led to the outside door but when I went outside it was just a smoking patio with a wheelchair accessible ramp. It was disappointing. Was there ever a tiki bar or is that just trickery? 

Staff: 3/5
My first encounter for staff was at the door. I told the guy that I had bought tickets online so that my name should be on the list. He gave me a stare then said "ID" and then looked up my name on the list and wordlessly handed me my card back as he held up the stamp and waited for me to read his mind and stick out my hand for the stamp. Miserable guy. He gets a 1/5. 

My second encounter with staff was one of the bartenders who was absolutely delightful. Smiled at me, ran my card right away and thanked me for who knows what but it was still nice. He gets a 5/5. 

Overall, I'd come back here if a band I really wanted to see was performing. Otherwise I would not go out of my way as the venue and my experience with the staff were both a mixed bag.

Drifters is a "dive bar" style BBQ restaurant / bar that occasionally has live music. You can sit inside or they have a good size outdoor section that is dog friendly. The staff is incredibly nice, always have a great experience. Their ribs are fantastic however they run out so availability is hit and miss. That said, in my opinion, the Drifter's burger is probably the best burger in Nashville. I highly recommend Drifters and would give them a 6th star if I could.
Food was amazing for being BBQ nachos, but the service was a little slow as sat there for awhile before anyone acknowledged we were there.   Overall a good experience though.
One of my favorite bars in East Nashville. The brisket nachos are the perfect bar food. They used to have the BOGO little green beer cards- I liked that, kind of like having neighbor monopoly money.

The biggest pro is that the Belcourt shows great movies, films you can't find playing anywhere else in a 3 hour radius. This includes even bigger name Oscar runner films as well as indie, foreign and artsy films. It's a neat looking building, good preservation, good location. Concession choices are better than most. On the down side--parking pass comes with a ticket purchase but there aren't really enough parking spaces available for every ticket purchaser. We got there on our recent visit to see a 2:30 pm matinee film and though we were 40 minutes early we were out of luck on parking and had to use the pay lot across the street. Also, though the inside is nice and new looking it doesn't look like the historic building it is (much more modern) and the seats are pretty uncomfortable. Also, I am curious on the NP status of the building--will it remain an NP now that the restorations are done? I assume ticket sales cover the costs of doing business now. Great films are a cultural contribution but I'm not sure it's on the scale of feeding the homeless or educating youth in the sense that donations are due to them once restoration is complete. Anyway, nice new building, excellent film selections, good concessions, clean restrooms, decent location, and nice film series/midnight movies, etc.

Went in for brunch. Service was great but ordered the eggs Benedict and the poached eggs were hard boiled. The manager came out and assured us they would fix it. Their solution was undercooked eggs with watery egg whites. When we told the manager, he tried to convince us that eating raw eggs was safe!!??? After we expressed that we would not eat raw eggs, he told us to order something else because "they weren't going to get the eggs right." The bottomless mimosas were great but I would never go back. The food portions were small and the food was very below average. Would not recommend.
devastated that they moved, but I still love you. You definitely livened up my side of town. baked brie is exceptional, musicians are always incredible.
Very Cool place with great food, music, and people. If your looking for a place that is away from the craziness of downtown Nashville, this is it.

What could I say about the Sheppard's Pie that hasn't already been said? The consistency of the quality has changed over the years I have noticed. Occasionally I get a dill seed, or whatever it is, stuck in my teeth! 

I really dig the windowed off from the music room so that you can watch a band and still have a conversation. I wish more clubs would do this! 

I had a bad experience coming here once where they made me and a dear friend wait outside for 15 minutes outside in the cold before they opened the doors. It was pretty off-putting and my friend, who was from out of town, requested specifically to eat at this restaurant as we had had a good meal there the last time he was in town. He didn't wanna go back there the next time he was in town. 

Over all though a good place to occasionally eat when I get a hankering for the Sheppard's Pie!!
I've seen a handful of good shows here but nothing about the venue ever struck me as special.

A wonderful old theatre and no doubt as to the reasons why it was chosen as the premiere location for the Hank Williams film "I Saw the Light." We were treated well and the premiere was wonderful. Before the show you can take in the experience of being in a place with a lot of history and when the film starts all of that fades away and you are immersed into what you ultimately came there for.

Drifter's is a cool little spot in the 5 points area just outside of Nashville. The hood has a bunch of food and live music options and is definitely worth a visit. 
We sat out on the patio to watch the live music and WTF, no country music. Darn! 

Our food was tasty but nothing special. We were looking for a real down south vibe and Drifter's was more of hipster joint with more mustaches than cowboy boots. I can get that at home.

I should have known when I saw the vegan menu.

The Mercy Lounge was an awesome venue! We went last night to watch The Boxer Rebellion and were blown away. It was comfortable and had a great drink selection with solid prices. Our only negative was the lack of food served either at the lounge or nearby otherwise we loved it and can't recommend It highly enough!

What an amazing venue.  Intimate feel, great acoustics, full bar.  Great place to see a concert.  It doesn't hurt I was seeing Stephen Kellogg for the eighth time.  By far the best venue yet.  Just a perfect evening.  I will be looking for more of my favorites to play here.

I've got to be honest- I'm not a fan.

The food seems very plain and bland to me. Maybe it's all the years of surviving on hot chicken, chicago dogs, and everything doused in jalepenos and hot sauce. I know I'm at least a little biased because growing up, everything my 'rents cooked tasted like cardboard and they had never heard of spice. I could probably live off of condiments.

When I last went, the service in an empty house was sub-par. I was told someone was going to get my refill and then waited a very long time (10-15 minutes) before that ever happened. With a mild esophogeal condition, I can't guarantee dry food will make it down the throat completely without some liquid to wash it down, so I literally have to pause eating if I wait on a refill. I'm normally quite understanding, but felt that a 10 minute wait in an empty house was a little excessive.

Call me a typical American, but I like my food to have flavor.

I highly recommend the BBQ nachos! This is one of my favorite places to grab a beer. The staff is so friendly, and they have great deals on beer! During the day the place is slower. Make sure to sit at the bar and make a friend. 

Signed,
A Regular

Went on Sunday to listening to a band. It was a beautiful day to sit outside under one of their umbrellas or canopies. 
They are dog friendly and unfortunately smoker friendly outside. Fortunately, the breeze kept the smoke down. 
A big storm blew in and our waitress informed us in time for our large group to get a table inside.
We got served inside. We didn't care for the smoked wings. The dry rub ribs were tasty.  The fries were nice and crispy and good. The hush puppies were very good. One person on our group got a salad. It was huge and a great variety of veggies, not just head lettuce.  The two for one beer specials were an unexpected treat. Good variety to chose from. 
Super area of Nashville. Easy pay as you go parking lot. $5 for 2 hours. Lots of little shops to explore in the area. 
A bit of a dive bar but great vibe and fun atmosphere. Service was good and pleasant.

Good spot! The bartenders and doorman were friendly and helpful. The cleanliness was better than most concert venues in town. The sound was great!

There's an outdoor smoking deck with a nice view of Downtown. There are two flights of stairs up to the venue and a step up to the bar area. There are a couple tables along the wall but its mostly SRO. 

Mixed crowd of young to old and all seemed welcome.

I recommend!

This place is hit & miss! Breakfast can be a challenge, staff is nice the food is good when the want it to be. Had the meat lovers omelette had no bacon even though its was advertised with it. Very little meat, when I showed them the comment was I should've ask for extra meat, thought the name said it all, guess not.
Also it wasn't a true omelette it was folded over unscrambled eggs. Had the country skillet the next morning ask for no peppers of course it came loaded with them. Morons!!
Pint and a pie any one???? This is a prime example of an East Nashville neighborhood favorite. Low light, funky feel, friendly crew and good music. Order your self a pie you will not be disappointed.

Saw first film in the newly remodeled building today.  The movie wasn't my total cup of tea, but that happens.  What a great new space they have created; will definitely be back for many films!  The inside ticket sales area, however, seemed a bit cramped.  It's located just inside the building from the new main entrance.  On the other hand, the concession area, which I didn't partake of, was large and a vast improvement over the old one.  All in all, a big win for Nashville!
Our first taste of Nashville was a score! Cool grungy atmosphere with unexpected awesome BBQ.
Very cool atmosphere, had a writers night when I was there and all were very good. Nice big patio! Try the grilled cheese!!

Don't ever go here.  Their bouncers have a Napoleon complex and will kick you out for going to the bathroom.  You can be a VIP and get kicked out for no reason.   Take it from a local.  Never go here.

Great venue and great service. Bartender was beautiful and nice and the sound system is great. Came for a songwriters round. Definitely a great place to check out if you are a local or not. Not super crowded (like Broadway is) during the mid evening, which I think is great. Better for hearing some of the original songs and songwriters coming out of Nashville. Pretzel bites were bomb btw.

A couple of weeks ago I decided to check out an East Nashville favorite for the first time:  The Family Wash.  I had driven by it several times, heard several great things about it, but for some reason had never made my way in.  Ridiculous, I know.  After a last minute decision to grab a bite, coupled with the fact that there was no wait for seating (I was starving), proved to be a great decision.  First of all, we had an awesome server (Stephanie--if she's there, ask for her, she was fab); Second, an impressive beer selection immediately caught my attention.  I asked our server for her food recommendation since I was a first timer, and she suggested the Shepherds Pie: A GREAT choice, it was delicious.  We also opted the spinach and artichoke dip as an app, which was quite tasty as well.  Rumor on the street is that their mac and cheese is pretty much to die for, but we didn't opt to add more calories this time around. Next time.

So, as I mentioned, the beer selection was impressive.  Several local brews on tap, along with seasonal selections from around the US.  I opted for the Jackelope Red Ale, and it did not disappoint.  In fact, it was really, really good.  If you've not tried Jackelope yet, do yourself a favor and make a visit to their taproom... I have yet to have any of their beers fail me.

After the first beer was served and food was on the table, the night continued to get even better with the addition of live music.  We are so lucky to have such talent in Nashville playing at joints like the Family Wash, and, they have live music every single night they are open.  Pretty awesome.

Don't wait as long as I did to check this place out--you'll be glad you paid them a visit!

A couple of items to note:

Tuesday is Pint & Pie night: A draft beer and Shepherd's Pie for $10 (Normally the pie itself is $11)

Thursday is $3.75 Draft Night 

They are closed Sunday and Monday

I dropped by here last week to see my first concert since moving to Nashville. As I had come to see the band, and hadn't heard anything about the venue, I came in fresh with no preconceptions. What I found was one of the best small concert venues I've had the pleasure to experience in my three decades on this planet.

The stage is perfectly set -- accessible to a GA crowd with excellent site lines. The sound system was great, though the drums/bass can easily overpower the higher register instruments and vocals in space like this if not balanced correctly. Decor was appropriate for the crowd, drinks were reasonably priced.
A nice deck and a good place to sit and listen to live music and drink a beer on a pretty day.

Claiming to be the oldest bar in Tennessee, Springwater is a place you have likely driven by many times, but unless you turn on the road between McDonald's and Centennial Park, you'd never know it was there. The place definitely has an unpleasant odor upon entering and teeny tiny bathrooms, but overall it was a good place to listen to some great live music. Everyone I encountered who works there were very friendly, and there are plenty of seating options amongst a covered patio, a room with the stage for bands and a third room with pool tables. It is the true definition of a dive bar, so if that's what you want, you'll love it. I will most definitely return in the future.

Went here for on Saturday night with a group of 8. The waitress was attentive when we first arrived, and then ignored us for the next 30 minutes. We then resorted to ordering from the bar, which I imagine she did not like, because she then ignored us completely until it was time to pay the bill. We also got pizza and it sucked.

Poor service. Food was basic bar food. No problem with that. Waitress was slow and got our order wrong. Paid with card and left cash tip. Total was 8.70 but when looking at my bank statement I was charged 10.70. Not a big deal financially but I won't be back.

I had my 3rd horrible experience at Exit in last night and I'm never going back. My boyfriend and I both brought 20 bucks cash to see his best friends band play. We brought 5 dollars for the cover and enough to get 2 beers each. We basically wanted to have low key night and not spend much. We were having a great time and walked up to the bar to get our second round of beers. He ordered a miller light and the bartender opened the beer and put it in front him so he started to pull out the money to pay. At that point the bartender said, "it's a 10 dollar minimum". My boyfriend politely said, "no thanks then, I'm good." Then it got ugly quick. The bartender proceeded to tell him that he had to buy the beer and reach the 10 dollar minimum or he would be kicked out immediately. He refused to buy the beer and then we were surrounded by three bouncers to "enforce" kicking us out of the bar. I asked the bartender why he couldn't just ice the beer for a few minutes and sell it to someone else and he said, "No one drinks Miller Light"?!? The whole thing was ridiculous and poorly managed. If I was the owner I would fire everyone on staff and start over. There are too many other great venues in town to put up with this type of treatment as a paying customer. The entitlement and rudeness of the staff seems to be encouraged. I remember going to Exit In back in the day and liking the staff, maybe there is new management? Either way, I will not be back.

The Belcourt is one of my favorite things about Nashville, and I'm not just saying that because I'm a former employee (I only left because I moved to California). The Belcourt has introduced me to movies I'd probably never have seen otherwise. Most very thought-provoking and so good but without a mainstream following or release. You're more than likely not going to see crap, though you may see something strange. I also love that they do midnight movies. Going to see The Room at midnight, throwing plastic spoons around, and screaming at the screen once a year really gets your stress out. I love the remodeling. At first I was very wary of the remodel, mostly because of the nostalgia from when I was an employee and fear the theatre losing its character. Since a visit to check it out and a midnight screening of the aforementioned The Room, my mind has been put at ease. The '22 Hall looks almost untouched, though I believe it got new seats and other necessities. I think the '66 Hall has a few less seats, but not by many. Looks pretty much the same as well. The Belcourt will always have a special place in my heart.

My boy How to Dress Well played at the Exit/In on Tuesday for only $12! Can't believe more people didn't take advantage of this amazing deal. Speaking of amazing deals, the Exit/In does not have any that apply to either Shiner Bock or PBR beers, since I spent over $11 on just two beers (that includes a generous tip for the bar man).

First How to Dress Well played "A Power", and then he played "Face Again". Following this tune, How to Dress Well played "Repeat Pleasure" and then he dropped "Cold Nites". The next tune was called "Very Best Friend", and after this one was done How to Dress Well played "Childhood Faith in Love (Everything Must Change, Everything Must Stay the Same)". "Suicide Dream 1" was the song that came next, and "Precious Love" of course followed that one up. We're not done yet, so hold on there are still a couple more! The next tune to be played was called "Set It Right", and the next one after that was "Words I Don't Remember".

Now, clearly How to Dress Well chose some good songs to play during Tuesday's Exit/In show, however I can't help but feel that there were a few songs missing that could have given this venue more of a wow factor. For example, I thought "2 Years On (Shame Dream)" would have made a good addition to the song list. I also wanted to hear "& It Was You", which would have sounded good inserted between "Cold Nites" and "Very Best Friend". Most importantly though, I thought How to Dress Well should have played their song "What You Wanted". Even more importantly I would have enjoyed hearing "World I Need You, Won't Be Without You (Proem)", which would have been a good opening track that would come in before  the other track that ended up being used.

Despite these minor complaints, the Exit/In still gets my certified approval. Next time How to Dress Well or another good band is in town be sure to head on over to this cool venue, where the music is good and the beer is better!
Nothing special. I'd say below average BBQ/Tex-mex. I had the brisket nachos and fried pickes. Probably won't go back there cause there's some many better BBQ places in Nashville.
Came here to watch a game and ordered food--it's over 50 mins and still waiting. At this rate the game will be over

Went here for the Yelp reviews, came away very, very full and pleased! The brisket and pulled pork were fantastic (the husband got this!) and I got a delicious (HUGE!) chimichanga. Loved it! I ate half that night and had the second half for lunch the next day. The hush puppies were also great, though I preferred dipping them in the bbq sauce as opposed to the sauce they sent them out with. It was also rather inexpensive!

We JUST missed happy hour, so our waitress brought us two 2-for-1 coupons to make up for it, which was great! Great vegetarian selection too, the others aren't lying (!), which is definitely unusual for Nashville. 

We'll definitely be going back, and not just because we got coupons.

Came down for a quick bite and a few drinks around dinner time. Food was OK, drinks surprisingly expensive. $10 for a not very generous Malibu and pineapple juice. Manager, Todd, wasn't friendly at all. Do yourself a favor and walk a block for food/drinks.

We ordered the hush puppies as an appetizer which were basically flavorless. I ordered the chicken wings which are pretty big, so I'll give them that but the meat was over cooked as it was super chewy, fatty, and pretty flavorless as well. The skin was rubbery and over charred. My boyfriend had the ribs, which were also dry and flavorless. Definitely not that "fall off the bone" kind of experience you look for in BBQ. I guess their sauce selection was pretty good. They only "allow" 2 students in the bar at a time which is what you make of it. Just a very disappointing experience especially for the price. Would not return or recommend to friends. Maybe enemies.

The food was just okay, the food is way overpriced. Music was pretty cool, but the experience was not worth the money. I've been to several other restaurants/bars in Nashville that are half the price and have a DOOR NOT MADE OUT OF PARTICLE BOARD. The building is a complete dump, food is not anything special, so why is it $15 for mac and cheese?
I didn't take a picture of the food because I just dove in!  Everything was delicious.  There was also great live music performances.

The Belcourt sets the standard for cinema. No 3D blockbusters, but the collection of films that they rotate can not be found any where else.

The theater itself is comfortable with good sound. 

You can buy a beer with the movie, which is awesome. They even have local drafts.

Just go.... Go..... Go...... Go..... And watch movies you never heard of tell a story you never heard. It's good the soul and good for the community.
This place was freaking amaze balls!!!! Food was delish...drinks were like sweet baby's milk. I will come back every chance possible, and I will succumb to their delicious offerings.

Tell me why you would cage in the 21+ crowd & limit them & their beverages to a small area around the bar??? Is this Disney on Ice?? Ridiculous. Money is in your drinks. Limit the under 21 area. I will not come back.

Went to see Hexagon Presents (which I highly recommend) and surprisingly the food was great!  I had the brussel sprouts and warm kale salad (which did not get shared) and my s.o. had the chicken and biscuits.  We'll definitely be back especially for Hexagon Presents.

The Belcourt is great. They show the smaller films, the indie films, and the foreign films that the big theaters don't. Prices are reasonable. Seats are comfortable. Unlike some smaller theaters, Belcourt has high quality movie projectors so the picture quality is fantastic!

My friend was visiting and of course wanted to hear some live music. She had already experienced Broadway on previous trips, so we managed to compromise on trying The Country. It was a Tuesday night so I was happy to find live music somewhere other than downtown. The location is in the Vanderbilt/Parthenon area which is always a relief for me because parking is manageable. The bar itself is pretty nice. Had a big patio area with lights that was cute. The inside is very open and dark, but not too dark. What I would expect from a bar. The decor is actually really nice. I mean, not a ton to it but you can tell it's fairly new. Good beer selection. The only kink was they weren't serving food that night...don't know why because the bartender was very short with us. Not exactly service with a smile, but I guess they don't put their "A" team on a slow Tuesday night. It was fine. We got our beer, listened to some music, but then had to go somewhere else to find some food. I would definitely be down for trying this bar again on a weekend, especially if visitors are in town.

It's a dive bar. Correction, it is a dive, CASH only bar (with an ATM onsite). Beer was reasonable, clientele was... well, "divey". Pool tables, a few drunks, attentive bar tender and the possibility of live music. Not bad! I am a fan!

A few of the less than sober occupants did tell me this was the oldest bar in Nashville?

We chose this place based on the reviews and it did not disappoint. Quaint bar with a neighborhood feel, service was friendly and fast. Answered all questions we had and was a good conversationalist without being annoying when you wanted to have a private conversation.  BBQ was great. Highly recommend the sampler platter! Great option to try multiple items. Great selection of BBQ sauces.

I enjoy this venue quite a lot. They get a good amount of acts I really want to see, so that's always good. 

Spacious and never too crowded.
Great patio with live music most days. If you want more of a quiet scene and not the crazy honky tonk on Broadway, this is your place.

Came in for the Funday at the Frog event last week and saw a DJ there- he was awesome! Paulo with the hat. After that, the party died down, but it was still fun. Bartender was super nice and made delicious drinks. I didn't try the food yet but I'll go back if I see that DJ on the event flyer again.

Amazing BBQ. Decent music and great patio atmosphere. Didn't expect to get food this good in this area, given the options in nashville. We went twice on the same weekend. Sausages might be the best I've ever had.

Kind of went here by accident, but I'm so glad we did! First of all, we were in Nashville for a weekend from Chicago and my husband wanted to have some BBQ  although I'm not a big fan. I was so surprised by the variety on their menu. My husband was able to order a variety of BBQ sliders (which he said were fantastic) and I had the vegetarian black bean nachos. I'm not even a vegetarian, but these were like the best nachos I've ever had. We were planning to go out to dinner later that night, but canceled because we outdid ourselves here. The service was great and we had fun playing ping pong outback - great spot! oh - and I should mention we almost went to the larger bar/restaurant next door (don't remember the name) and we walked in and it was a big cloud of smoke - yuck. Where can you still smoke in restaurants? or even bars? I don't get it. Anyway, drifters had no smoking inside which is how we ended up there!
We went on a Monday during the 8 on 8th band promotion time period. It was a great place to get a local music feel. Drinks were affordable.

Now that I no longer live in Nashville, I can say without hesitation that the Belcourt is one of the things I'll miss most. From the super friendly staff to the great concessions to the rotating art in the library, this would be an exceptional theater under any circumstances, but there are two things that make it truly wonderful: 

1. The brilliant curation of films, which entails everything from high art to popcorn flicks to 80s cult B-movies (on VHS, no less!) to the pillars of cinema (often paired with a live orchestra for silent films) is unlike any I've seen in a similar-sized theater. Often films will be shown with a guest speaker or commentary (in-person or via Skype) from the directors themselves, which is great. 

2. The community--as a nonprofit, the Belcourt is one of the most enduring and beloved arts organizations in Nashville, and you can tell that the the people who go there love the place. The audiences are always respectful (unless the film calls for them to be otherwise), and there's a sense of solidarity and love for the movies here that it's hard to find elsewhere.

Had our wedding reception at the ONE venue upstairs. Allison and team were incredibly helpful throughout the process, always responsive. The room is stunning, and the layout was perfect for the occasion. We had a live band in the main room, with guests being able to step into the connected bar room area for drinks and conversation. Beautiful view of downtown, and within strolling distance to Broadway for the post party. So glad we did our event here!
Fried pickles were awesome! Beef and pork were deliciously smokey. Casual atmosphere, large outdoor seating area.

Exit/in is the closest and coolest venue in Nashville. It's quaint and small so seeing an artist that close with the sound quality is an amazing experience. If you have a chance to see an artist here, it is a must see venue!!
We went to the Postmodern Jukebox show last week. I liked that we were able to get right next to the stage and almost touch the musicians. If a group we likes plays there we will be going back

Recently went on a Tuesday with friends for their Pie & Pint night.  We were there for about 2 hours and saw 2 different acts.  A solo acoustic act was playing, who was awesome, and seemed like a good fit for the venue.  We got our beer and pies in the meantime - everyone got the traditional pie, I ordered the veggie pie with no cheese and extra garlic.  It was delicious!  Waitress was, for the most part, attentive to our table, although it looked like she was the only one serving (and according to her, plating the food).  

Once the second act (full band) got on stage, forget having a conversation.  I am always down to listen to a great jam session, but not in a small room like we were in...the only time we could hear each other was in between songs.

All in all, awesome vegetarian shepherd's pie (inspired me to cook up my own version a few days later!) and wonderful atmosphere.  I'd definitely say this is a place with it's own flair, and I'd return again!
Great bar. Hannah was an amazing bartender. She took great care of us. We were here on two different nights and both bands were great. Highly recommended.

Nashville needs more places like this. The amount of culture and genuine entertainment that a place like the Belcourt creates is incredible. They are constantly throwing events (like outdoor movies and midnight classic showings) and the staff is always friendly and seem eager to serve and assist you. Not to mention the movie selection... I have yet to see a film I didn't like at the Belcourt. Each film seems to be hand picked for greatness.

The sound system and general aesthetics of the theatre are excellent. Everything feels classy, but cozy. I could come here every day.

Great east Nashville watering hole with an eclectic offering of live music every weekend including Pal Sheldon and His Awesome Friends - they play here in warmer months every month. Super friendly and casual vibe. Every time we go there we always see someone we know. Yummy wings, beans, brisket, burgers, salads and some fine vegetarian food and it's not overpriced! Good for the pocket! It's our fave local semi dive bar.

I was immediately addressed by everyone on shift. Great beer selection and I went with their signature pulled pork sandwich "The Drifter" and was blown away. Great meat, great bread, and I'm from Texas. Would recommend even if they were cheering for Alabama.
Great place to see a show  we sage plain white tees and beta play and it was awesome.  Jessica the bartender made everything easy and fun.  Good prices too!

So so yummy that I came here twice in one night! They have 2 for 1 drinks on happy hour and the bbq is delicious! Like any good place, they make all of their own sauces and offer a variety of them. It's a nice local joint to get some good food and drinks with many other places to hang out nearby.

Hard to believe that this is the Resturant for the Holiday Inn Vanderbilt.  Great service- our server recommended the spicy chicken strips with mini waffles. It was awesome. Apparently he thought it took too long and included a yummy brownie dessert on the house. Food and drinks were excellent and if you can head over on a Wednesday night- open mic for songwriters. Some better than others, but the spirit of Nashville was alive!

This place is one of the best to catch live music in the West End area. I take friends and family here all the time. The beer selection is better than its sister bar, Jed's, but you'll pay for it. Bring a few dollars to tip the bands playing. Unlike Soulshine Pizza, they don't have a way to pass credit card tips to the band.
Hidden gem in west end. Came in on a Saturday and had a great time. Bartender super friendly, the band playing that night was good.

Yesss!!! Bring Nashville to the table!!  First off the happy hour specials are great.  Either a double well drink or 2 beers for 1.  The service was so awesome.  The gentleman that waited on us was on point and full of great suggestions.  The food was tasty specifically the pulled brisket and pork.  The coleslaw was done perfectly.  The beans were delicious.  I will be back.  The place was the perfect price!!

Yes! Finally something that gives Nashville a true cosmopolitan vibe! Somewhere to find great independent movies, documentaries and foreign films that encourages diversity and ignites the mind. Also, It is a bargain for sure with decent parking and is walking distance to great bars and restaurants. It is an absolute perfect place for a stimulating evening out. Long live the Belcourt Theatre!

The Belcourt has a special place in my heart. From the unique films to the drinks and friendly staff... this place always makes me happy. It's historical significance tops everything and I hope it stays around for a long time. Do yourself a favor and see a movie at the Belcourt.

Came here alone on a Thursday night for dinner and free music.  Very satisfied with the experience.

Staff: Bartender was very nice.  I'm told it's a Southern thing, but very patient while I pondered my beer options. 

Food: Had their grilled cheese and chips. Nothing special, but satisfying and reasonably priced.

Booze:  Beers on tap.  Recommend the Kentucky Bourbon Barrel if you get the chance (Serving size is smaller, but it's higher percentage and tasty.  Price and size were similar to what I got when I ordered the same at The Listening Lounge).  Kudos to The Country for having a reasonable selection.  

Ambiance: Very relaxed. Clean and updated decor. Place was not full.  Thankful that it felt comfortable enough to sit alone, intermittently reading a paper and listening to the music. As for the music, I liked one person more than the other.  The crowd was very subdued, but at least the first artist rocked out and had a good time. 

Price: Pretty reasonable.  I think it was $23 for dinner and 2 of their most expensive beer on tap.  And the 1.5 hr of free entertainment.  

Overall: I wanted to go back, but we ran out of time in Nashville.  Would've liked to try a few of their appetizers.  If you're in the area and looking for something easy without a big crowd, consider this place.
We loved this place. Casual, friendly, attentive service and good food- not too pricey! Good food. And live music! Shepherd's Pie was excellent. Did I mention that all the food is good?
Took over 50 minutes to get our food, DONT COME HUNGRY! you'll never get your food! Totally disappointed!
Unfriendly staff and cannot make a drink. Might be ok for a beer. Was not there to see the live music. In from out of town- did not display the Nashville hospitality expected. Pass on this one.

House drink Mr Frisky was horrible. The gumbo was nothing more than gravy over rice with some shrimp pieces tossed in. I gave it two stars because the fried shrimp and alligator was good. The Cesar salad was boring. We went here on a recommendation of a couple we met on one of our outings well they don't know good gumbo at all. Service was slow definitely won't recommend this place

Good booking

Good sound

Smoke free

They book the Melvins frequently

Upstairs balcony helps short people see

Bathrooms aren't horrible - bonus!
HIGHLY recommended. Small place and a small menu but they do what they do well. Appreciated the many vegetarian options too. Plus, service was top notch, super-friendly.

I randomly walked in one night and was told Matt Wertz was playing. Ah! Had to see him, as I've been following him for years now. Love that this is such a well-known music venue, but they mostly feature rising stars. It's small, dark, musky, and is on the Vanderbilt campus, so prepare to wade through a sea of students. Tickets were $25, and there's a $10 minimum at the bar FYI. So it's a slightly pricey place. They need AC! 

As for the talented Matt Wertz, he killed it. Check him out immediately!

1. Get a membership. 2. Get on their mailing list so that you know what is going on. 3. Keep Belcourt in your rotation when you are looking for entertainment. My biggest problem with the Belcourt always used to be that I would forget about it and then get mad at myself for missing the amazing movies and other shows. After following advice 1-3 above, I can now say I'm a regular visitor and have seen so many memorable movies. 

They also have some great festivals - Japanese movies, Hitchcock, etc. You know. Some you've seen before but never on the big screen. Others you cannot even get on your own. One of my favorite things to do is to go see all of the Oscar nominated shorts in the weekends prior to the Academy Awards. Always some amazing films.

I just attended a Passenger concert at Mercy Lounge and absolutely loved the venue. It is the perfect size to have a good crowd yet still have that intimate climate that many long for, especially with an artist like Passenger.  Also Mercy Lounge has one of the key components to a good venue, levels.  I am short which makes it hard to see in many crowds unless I maneuver myself up to the front of the stage. Since Mercy Lounge has levels I can stand on the edge of a higher platform and see right over all the heads around me. Typically artists prefer levels too because then they can see their audience and connect better. All together, Mercy Lounge is a great venue and I highly recommend booking there or attending their shows.
Outstanding BBQ!  The pulled chicken, brats, brisket, and pulled pork were great.  The sides were great.  The fries, coleslaw, and beans were delicious.  Great variety of BBQ sauces.

2013/014

We came in to see "Chasing Ice" a few weeks back, and enjoyed the movie as well as the comfy seating. 

I like small theaters, as I'm not into going to see a movie for the ambience of hundreds of people around me for a first run movie. I honestly didn't notice any of the architectural details of an historic place; you see one indie theater that used to be historically- and cutlurally-significant, you've seen them all. 

They do offer the kind of foreign and independent films that generally attract a more subdued crowd. However, at the time I saw the movie, the women behind us kept slurping/whispering throughout the entire movie. I kept glaring at them, only to find out that my husband knew one of them. Oops.

Given the blue laws of this state, I was surprised to see them offering alcohol.

Great place for food and music. My husband is a musician so we went to play at the open mic. The songwriters featured are always great. We will be back for him to be featured in Dec! The drinks are great and the spinach and artichoke dip is amazing. 
Debbie, the MC, is fantastic!
