One of the friendliest staff I've ever encountered.  Special shoutout to the head of security Eron, who is a pro and is extremely cool.

This is one of those fabulous places that sets Nashville apart from other mid-major cities. This is a truly viable, supported indie theater. 
I am not sophisticated or edgy enough to truly get wrapped up in the indie film world, but I do know this: every film I have seen here I have enjoyed on some level. And the films always leave me thinking...
I even joined their membership. I love their monthly mailing. 
They do host major motion pictures too... I saw The Shape of Water here, as well as Manchester By the Sea and Captain Fantastic (which you MUST SEE). This is my kind of theater!!
Good hummus from a local caterer and good enough wine. And as an added bonus, BOURBON. 
There is a parking structure down the alley by Hopdoddy where there is plenty of parking. 1 plus hours free depending on the time of day. There is a pay lot directly across the street. There is free parking, but only if you are like one of the first 30 to arrive.... (You must get a parking pass inside)
It is recently renovated. Comfortable. 
Plenty of eats nearby if you want to make a full date night. 
Even if I go alone, I always try to find an excuse to go.  You should too.

Friendly atmosphere the Friday night song writers night was great, (i think it is held the third friday) they hosted a variety of local talent. For more info on the talent night  check out Hippie Chick Twang on Facebook her and her son were the hosts and she was a very talented songwriter and guitarist.

Ticketfly's online ticketing was completely down for an extended period, and whoever manages this venue seems to very rarely answer the phone, so I went to Exit-In when another show was going on in hopes that the venue would be able to sell a ticket to a show held the next day (thus also avoiding the huge percentage-wise fee for purchasing online, so I was ok with the inconvenience of making a trip over there). But the box office couldn't even sell a ticket to their own venue for a show held the next night. I was referred to two other locations which apparently can't even sell tickets while the Ticketfly website remains down.

Have been to one of more concerts at this venue previously and found it sort of so-so in terms of layout and sound quality, but had never heard of a concert venue unable to sell tickets to its own shows held the next evening, was kind of annoying as a customer as this information is not made clear from the website and this is a very unusual policy for a music venue - if someone from Exit-In reads this, please note in your FAQ or elsewhere on your website that tickets for future shows are not sold at the ticket window, as I think the common understanding is that the selling of tickets to current and future events is a core feature of most venues' ticket window or box office if they have one.

***
Update: Thank you to Jeremy for the fast response to this (below). I still think it's sort of lame that there isn't a way to buy tickets in advance of showdate at venue without relying on a web interface which as I recall regularly charges over 20% in fees not even displayed to customer until checkout, and that same interface now appears to have suffered a pretty massive hack and presumably/possibly may have exposed customer payment data in the process (not sure of this but it seems to very often end up being the case in these situations). But you and other staff I have interacted with there have always been professional and courteous on the venue's behalf. Thanks for taking the time to respond and for doing it in a professional manner.
 
****
Annnnnd update yet again. Can we talk about how stupid I was with this previous review? Venue I had gone to to try to buy tickets was Mercy Lounge/The Cannery, not Exit-In; related venues, I think, but not the same. Sounds like I might have run into the same problem regardless, but Exit In is a way better venue than this previous review allowed for. I think 5 stars in terms of actual venue quality is fair, and again I appreciate that someone from the venue replied with such class. Still  of a fan of the online ticketing interface used, but 5 stars for the venue itself (and for its staff!).

Best venue for weird chicks pushing their way to the front and saying "excuse me" followed by 7 d-bags with sunglasses at 10pm in a dark room. Also, the sound is average if average is the sound of your record player playing on the first floor when you're on the second. Bartenders are good...not counting the bad one. Want to go to a concert at the ass end of a horse stable? Come here.

I'm an indie film maker and as such I have a taste for independent and foreign film.  Finding a place which supports such art was essential for me when moving to Nashville.  This place is outstanding.  My wife and I watched two films in one day for our first experience and will likely become members in the new year.

Came here because this was the only theatre in town playing Patti Cake$. Left here learning that this is the best theatre in town altogether!

Ample parking. Super clean everything. Plenty of great choices for beer and wine. Fun staff and well mannered audience.

If you enjoy movies, appreciate good beer and wine, and want an uninterrupted movie experience at an logistically painless theatre with facilities that are not unpleasant to use... then this is your spot!
Beautiful theater, great movie selections, and a kick-ass concession stand that supports a good cause. I'm always a fan of the Belcourt.
Pint & Pie night was well worth the extra day in Nashville.  Great atmosphere!

Listen Yelp.  I destroyed their food (in a good way).  I was so hungry coming from downtown.  Coming to Nashville, it is a must to have a plate of BBQ.  Glad i was able to look up this place.  Located in five points, easy to get to.  Inside is cozy, not to grand nor small.  But the BBQ ribs was cooked perfectly.  The collard that i had were absolutely delicious.  Beer selection and service was oin point.  Loved it, accommodating as heck and will be back.

Grade: A

Drifter's was open where most airlines almost weren't. This was the first stop that I brought my friends to when we finally arrived in Nashville. It had been a while so I had to get the Drifter, which has changed a little, no more middle bun in between, because who needs more of that anyway?

Other than that, the special was dollar Hi life bottles. Despite the shitty weather the staff was really friendly and my friends were happy with their first Nashville experience after having waited almost 14 hours to arrive.

Somehow I've never reviewed Mercy Lounge. I notice I've covered most of the other music venues in Nashville but slipped up with this one--and some of my earliest Nashville shows took place here. Before I even lived in the area I took a few roadtrips to Nashville to see shows here when bands I really liked were playing. It's mostly a solid place to see a band with a few notable issues.
First---it's a great size and decent layout for a mid-sized (popularity wise) band. It's an intimate, up close kind of place. Bigger than the End, smaller than Marathon. They have on-site parking (huge plus) for only $5 (not bad at all). Drinks are cheap. Easy in and out and I've seen some pretty great shows here.
So what's not to love? Well...even if you're not an ear-plug fan (and I've made myself become one anyway over the past few years to save my hearing and still keep going to shows) you better become one at least for the night if you're headed to Mercy. That's because the acoustics in this place are outright deafening. One of my favorite bands played here a few years ago and though they are a fairly loud band this was the loudest I've ever heard them and I've seen them 10 times in 10 different venues over the years. Here I could barely make out a word of the vocals (and they have clear vocals typically, a very narrative song-writing is important kind of band). I left with the worst headache of my life. Plus there are some posts and polls in odd places so if it's an active show watch out. And getting to and from the bar with a drink at any point can be cumbersome.
That all said, I saw one of the most active shows by one of the loudest bands around here not that long ago and it worked really well with little to no issues for me. Sound was clearer than in previous visits. I've noticed some great shows coming to Mercy in the next few months so I may have to revisit, particularly for the more singer-songwriter style events.

Had a great first experience and returned a week later only to leave hungry and frustrated. On top of that, I wrote one good review & one bad review to find them both deleted by Yelp. Am I only allowed to write good reviews?  The first night we had just flown  into Nashville for the first time. Bartender was warm & welcoming. Drinks & burgers were great. We were the only people there. We were so happy. Wrote a 5 star review! 
Came back a few nights later & there was live music,  but the place was packed with a young drinking crowd so we left. Then, we tried it again our last night in town. Different female bartender than the first time. This one "carded" my 70 year old husband who ordered a drink. (We walked over from our hotel & he didn't bring his ID -  why would he need it?) Right? 
So I gave her my ID; which she made me take out of the plastic window of my wallet  & hand to her. She still didn't make the drink. When questioned she indicated it was the law to card everyone regardless of age.  We spent 7 days eating and all over the city. We patronized many bars, honky tonks, restaurants all over the City & not once did we get "carded".  I later found out that it is not the law to card someone regardless of apparent age. 
So, feeling pretty annoyed, we order food for dinner. After she takes the order, she asks for a credit card to "run a tab". A tab for what?? The drinks we can't have? So I ask her ... she says she can't order our food without a credit card. Seriously, we didn't have orange jumpsuits on! Did we look like criminals? No wonder there were only 2 people in the whole place. I tell her we are paying cash - did I need to pre-pay for the food like McDonalds?  By then my husband was so angry at being treated like criminals he insisted we leave. Will never go there again and will tell everyone I know about how we were treated.

Our teenage daughter was in the mood for BBQ, and that is what led us to try Drifters. We were not disappointed! From the outside, it looks like a seedy little hole-in-the-wall (there is a sign pointing you to the alley!). When you walk in, it is dark, loud, & looks just like a bar. Get past that and it is very inviting. The food was AMAZING! The brisket was awesome, the ribs were smoky, and the sauce bar was great! We would definitely go here again.
Awesome music venue. Great food and music. Great drinks as well. Always good fun here and you never know who you'll meet!

I've only had their BBQ sampler platter. It's big-- can easily be shared between 2 or 3 people. It comes with 1/3 of a rack of ribs, 3 oz of pulled chicken, 3 oz of brisket and 3 oz of smoked sausage. The BBQ itself was pretty good. The brisket was really good as was the  sausage. Their hush puppies are super delicious though! And often times you'll go there and there will be some kind of live music going on.

If my typing fingers had to stand as long as I did on Saturday night I may not be able to type this. Stage is situated perfectly, bathrooms fairly clean, and not too hot but very few tables and chairs. I don't mind standing at a show but it gets old after so many hours. Band was great but that was why were there. Seats in pool table room have seen better days. And drinks were a bit too watered down. If they gets some chairs and some tables where I can sit and have someplace to put my drink it could be bumped to 4 stars...

We stopped there for Saturday brunch, as the sign outside was welcoming people to try their brunch menu.  Looked like a nice, clean place.  Waitress was nice.  Took over 1 hr. for 6 of us to get omelets and hot chicken.  Wasn't anything extravagant and the manager compensated by taking $1 off of our bill.

Love the theater but just had a horrible experience.   Confusion with one line, two cashiers,  one only doing will call.    Missed the beginning of movie so I left.    Figure it out.    That was a mess.

Love seeing movies here. Very decent prices, a good selection of unique and classic films. You can drink beer during a movie! They have cool midnight shows, and small independent films not showing anywhere else in the city.I haven't been to a Regal or Carmike cinema in years, but I make it to the Belcourt at least once a month.

This is going to be the shortest review ever.

Mean Girls, Harry Potter and The Sound of Music on the big screen all for $9? I'm in LOVE
Great outdoor patio! Love drifters...almost always live music and drink specials! best place in 5 points to sit outside with friends and enjoy the nice weather!

This is one of the best venues I have ever been to. It would get five stars if not for the pudgy, power tripping doorman with zero people skills. This venue is an intimate setting where the band and the audience can feel each other's energy effortlessly. 

     My wife and I flew in from out of town to see a band that wasn't coming to our town. What an amazing show! So glad we made the trip. Definitely a wonderful time. Nashville treated us well.

Cannery Ballroom is too cool! I cannot believe I haven't been here before. The venue lends itself to intimate concerts. We went there for Maren Morris' last concert of her Hero tour. It was awesome! I felt like I was right on stage with her. The acoustics in the room were great. I'd recommend making your way to the front if you are short because standing behind tall people stinks. Luckily I wore heels and It wasn't a problem. You will be standing the entire time, so wear comfortable heels/shoes. 
If you get hungry, there is a guy outside cooking delicious mini burgers and fries. The security will let you in/out once you have your hand stamped. There is also a full bar. The bartender was kind enough to make me a mocktail! It was delicious. 
The best part is the parking. I thought it would be horrid and we almost took an uber, but didn't. I immediately found a parking spot right out front and if that fills up there is $5 parking next to it...great deal for Nashville!!
I can't wait to attend a future concert at Cannery Ballroom.
Everything about this place is fantastic! The service is stellar. The atmosphere just perfect. And the live music? Perfect. If we weren't from Michigan on vacation, we'd be back next week.

For my first time in TN, this location was cool and vibey!! Just be prepared to pay at least $5 for parking.  I came here to attend a Thirdstory concert (which was totally awesome by the way). The only reason why one star is lacking is BC of VIP meet and greet and not a lot of premium liquor.  I was able to meet the artist and wanted to video chat and was told no by the venue staff.  When I told the members of Thirdstory they were more disappointed with the fact that I wasn't allowed to video the meet and greet.  The concert was great the facility is great for live music and if in TN again, I will definitely see another show.

I was staying at The nearby Marriott and wanted to get something to eat hear some music. It's Nashville! I had dinner, drinks, and some live music.

Pros - new bar with an old feel. Edison bulbs. Classic musical patents for decorations.  Matte black. Good sound system. Good food. 

Cons - it was bar service but there was no way to know that. Say at a a table for quite awhile waiting for what I thought  was a waitress to stop by the table. 

While this might not be an old, classic Nashville bar, it is also not a tourist trap. It's a nice clean new bar with good music and good food. I had the Korean barbecue tacos. Fit right in with the mostly hipster crowd. The tacos were good, the coleslaw on them was very fresh, the sauce was a little sweet and a tiny bit smoky. The music was great. I would definitely recommend coming here if you want a place to eat and listen to live music

The service was awful. The waitresses ignored us for other tables with larger parties. When we reached out pointing out that we had been waiting longer than the people they were serving three separate members of the waitstaff obviously didn't care.

We ended up walking out after the pattern became impossible to ignore.

Really great, personable service. Good atmosphere. Eh food. 

I read reviews about their shepherd's pie so I was really excited to try it. I got the veggie one and added roasted garlic to it. First off, just so everyone's aware, it had about a 2 inch thick layer of cheese on it. Not that I don't love cheese, but it was a. ton. of. cheese. Next time I would definitely ask that they go light on that part.  It was good, but not great. I wouldn't go back because I was blown away by it.

It was a bit of a disappointment, just because I was really hyped up about it, but nothing was bad by any means. They also had good happy hour prices even on a Saturday when I went. I think it went til 6:30 and we were able to get a cheap appetizer and discounted Yazoo beer.

Well, It's been three months, and I've been back enough times to justify a review update. The Country has impressed me over the last few visits. First off, my hope of seeing taps rotated? It's happening! They have a great selection, including some Michigan beers (but hey, I'm partial) and high-grav options. In truth, my friends and I never come here to drink cocktails, but their menu looks promising, and I am sure I'll try some eventually. I also don't usually come here to eat, but that may be changing soon as I recently has an amazing burger, with an aioli to die for.

While I did not attend their New Years Eve party, I stopped by the night after and got a glance at the photo back drop, ice luge sculpture and NYE menu, which certainly made it look like it would've been a great time. I'm excited to see what other events and musicians they have in the future. It is nice to have some live music on our side of town.

I have to give props to Lee, the bartender who is there pretty much all the time. Seriously great service. Also, my friend lost his [beloved cowboy] hat the last time we were there and Lee helped us track it down.

My friends and I will certainly continue to come to The County. Can't wait for some warm weather patio drinks here next summer!

Loved the BBQ.  Great music.  Bar-like and a tad rowdy, which fit the place well.  Service was really quick and attentive.  Place is behind the fish joint, just up the alley.  Parking was scarce, so we went across the street and paid ($3/hr).  East Nashville section know as the five points.  Nice scene with a lot of bars around it.  Highly recommend.

Nice little dive joint hidden in Nashville. The area around is pretty cool. The food is great! Don't let the biker vibe stop you from going. 

I recommend the wings! They are the size of a pterodactyl.

So much fun to see a show here!  Saw Guilty Pleasures perform, an 80's cover band, who were AMAZING!! Room to dance, a bar, not a lot of seating, but again, there to dance!!  I recommend bring some cash money with you.. they do have an ATM, but $3 fee with your withdrawal. Wahhwahh.  Had a great time!

Ugh....sat, game day, tv's, big bar...and it's all down hill from here . No support for wait staff, no manager, no organization and we were told after waiting an hour for glorified bar food that the kitchen was small and it's an "each man for himself" approach. No thanks. Too late to abandon the order but I would never come back for this kind of torture.

This is one of Nashville's most special places and my absolute favorite spot in town. Great mix of repertory offerings, midnight movies, special events, and new foreign and independent films. Clean theatre; courteous, friendly, unpretentious staff; and great concessions including some local beers on tap.
Foods good service sucks waited 15-20 min I finally moved to the bar flag someone down. Lazy!!!

Friends and I came here to watch Langhorne Slim & The Law with Margo and the Pricetags opening for them. 

Man what a venue. Located in the Sobro (south of Broadway) section of Nashville, Mercy Lounge is quite a famous music venue in this city and the atmosphere was incredible. 

I love country, and though this was my first time hearing of Margo and the Pricetags, I fell in love instantly.

But Langhorne Slim & The Law. Man. What a set. 

There's a smoking patio out back in addition to a smaller area with a photo booth and some things to look at. 

I liked it a lot. Cramped as it was a packed house for Langhorne Slim, but it was a show I had absolutely no regrets going to.

I went here for a reservation and the manager was very rude. We waited for our food for 2.5 hours and the manager said he would take 10% off of our food and then he cancelled the food. The restaurant was empty. The servers were great and obviously not their fault. There is a management issue and needs to be fixed ASAP. Would not recommend

Relaxed atmosphere. Popular spot, as I'm sitting here there's a production crew that wrapped up filming for the day just chilling and eating good food. I think their server is the same one as mine so she's killing it, I hope you get her when you stop by cuz I can't remember her name. Paid parking but like $5/2hrs so not too bad, paid much more for less time and poor service here in east nashville. Veggie options. I'd ask for what's truly vegan tho. After you're done rocking out to live music here you should stop by one of the other bars on the block, 3  Crow is excellent, Tenn Sixteen has some of the best gumbo around...just come to the 5 points area man. You won't regret it
Good fried pickles, DRY, DRY, BBQ, got the sliders, dry as roofing shingles. Good beer though.
We didn't get greeted for awhile, our bartender was extremely slow too, we pretty much got ignored the whole time!

Great place for outdoor eating with a simple vibe and yummy bbq. We had the pulled pork bbq sandwich and fried catfish. Great band was playing and was a fun place to chill before heading to Family Wash for a show.

Hozier at Exit In. Another great show at an awesome venue. The venue is definitely old school but very good acoustics, decent selection of beer and a tiki bar for the smokers. Nashville's musical heritage.

Drifters is always on the top of my to do list when visiting Nashville! My dog is my road trip buddy for the 20 hour drive to visit my brother, and she looks forward to eating here too.  The food is delicious (I always bring bottles of sauce back), the service is quick and friendly, and they always bring a bowl of water right out for the dog.

Well, I know this isn't necessary a completely fair judgment, but I can only judge it based on when I was there. Apparently I was there on an unusual quiet day, because it was a Saturday night and there was hardly anyone. It was the Saturday right after gay marriage became legal and all these Pride festivities were going on.

Pros: The venue is huge and can accommodate at least 2 groups playing at the same time that wouldn't bother each other since they're on the opposite end of the floor. They have free pool and darts, and I love the balcony (smoker's area) because it has a good view of the city. I didn't smoke, but that didn't mean I didn't enjoy the scenary.

Cons: Because there were hardly anyone there, the music was painfully loud, and the only way I could escape it was to go into the pool room. Considering how little people there were, the cover charge seems unnecessary and overly expensive for what we got as an experience.

So, all in all, I would have to be really in the mood for music by random bands or my favorite bands play there to go back. There are bajillions of places on Broadway with live music.
Such a great live music venue in Nashville. I've been three times and have yet to be disappointed! Very fairly priced drinks, great atmosphere, and free nearby street parking.

Juicy 6 ounce burgers, infused with ground bacon, served on a toasted bun with a side of french fries. $7.50.
Bacon and cheese are $1.00 extra.

Juicy, tender, tasty, (did I say juicy?) on a toasted bun.  How many places do you know that toast the bun??

French fries, crispy, matchstick thin, salted..  Oooooh, so good.

Cold beer, full liquor bar, decent prices, non-smoking interior, familiar music coming from the speakers, TV's on silent...  every chair in the place is taken.

Where else would you go for a juicy bacon burger on a toasted bun for $7.50?
NO WHERE!

There's a ton more stuff on the menu, but I prefer the burger with bacon!
Even the fried pickles hit the spot.

Burger you, burger me, no lines out the door, no $11.00 burger, no extra price on the french fries.  

This is heaven.
*Even the waitstaff is pretty efficient.

I was in here about 6 months ago and the service was practically insulting. However, my friends invited me back and I decided to go after swearing I wouldn't be back. The beer specials are great, and the food was delicious. However, what really made me happy was the service I received from Leah. She knew exactly what she was doing and had a vast amount of knowledge about the menu as well as recovered any thoughts about this place I had. Because of her, I WILL be back.
Went to Tin Roof. It was relatively empty. After waiting nearly 30 minutes left and went here. Fish tacos were really fresh and good
Awesome music venue. Outdoor patio is very nice. Very nice sound and night club feel. They have good tap selection and serve food. We did not try the food.

Yes! My favorite venue! They constantly bring in great acts ranging from just about every genre and popularity. I've seen some wonderful shows here, some of the best being Mac DeMarco, Avey Tare's Slasher Flicks, and Slow Magic.

It is an intimate venue with a lot of history and chill atmosphere.They have a small balcony and even a smoking area just outside by the stage that you can use to escape a hot and heavy crowd. 

If you're in Nashville, your Music City experience is not complete until a visit to the Exit/In.

This is for January 22, a Monday, early afternoon so it was slow. But with the interior, list of activities & drink list I can see that it probably gets super busy at night. 
The chips and salsa were really good. Best tortilla chips I've ever had, nice job. I got Philly  sandwich and fries. It was ok. The chicken strips the kids ordered looked really tender and breaded good. What I wish I'd ordered after seeing them lol. 
My son had turkey club he seemed to like it but still hungry after eating it. 
Service was ok. There seemed to be workers everywhere then gone to who knows where when wanted to ask for something. But maybe it. As prep time for evening or something. They were nice and we had a good lunch. 
Place is very clean. They do great on that. 
As we were leaving I saw they had a corn hole game, that's always a fun one.

My boyfriend and I saw Meg Myers with Jarryd James opening last night. This was my first time coming to Mercy Lounge and it's a really nice little venue with exposed brick and red velvet, a bunch of modestly priced drinks and a really nice lighting and sound system. It is a standing venue, and pretty small. I'd say full capacity (standing) is maybe 500 packed tight? Crowd was 18+. Meg rocked, but that doesn't have to be said. *wink*

The major downside of this place (and Cannery Ballroom, for that matter) is that there are no seats, and not enough air flow. If you have a delicate constitution, get lightheaded standing in one spot for a long time or are claustrophobic, I can't say I recommend. I don't even have those problems and the lack of air flow, crowding and standing was getting to me. Just a head's up.

Visited here a couple times recently for their ribs.  They always fall off the bone and some of the best I have tried in Nashville.  I have only visited during lunch and the waitress/bartender is awesome and has a great personality.  Looking forward to my next return!

Wow little hole in the wall looking with great staff very informative our waiter said they use a dry rob on their brisket & a little bit of wet rob just before they take it out.... we got the brisket plate it came with black beans, slaw & fries.... it was great thanks
Phenomenal environment! The shrimp po boy was amazing! Sampler platter had a great variety! Food was excellent!!!

We sure do love to keep things local here in Nashville! If you ever become a member of anything in this town, be sure to join at the Belcourt! You get reduced admission prices and a discount in concessions. PLUS, you get to watch any and all of the great movies that come through here; movies we wouldn't normally get to see in any other theater around here and I'm so grateful for that!

Quite a divey place for some beers and BBQ.

2 for 1 happy hour drinks was definitely a plus, but after eating all that fried hush puppies, fried green tomatoes and big platters of BBQ meat, I had no room for the 2nd beer. The above mentioned food was decent but nothing mind blowing as many other writers have said.

Was visiting Nashville and happened upon Drifter's by accident in my search for BBQ after a much closer restaurant was out of chicken, ribs and practically everything else but the BBQ sauce. However, Drifters was the most pleasant surprise in a visit filled with great meals!  Drifters looks like both a dive bar and a down home restaurant at the same time, and as out of towners we appreciated the comfortable, informal environment. The staff were welcoming and friendly and very attentive. Leah our server was great and by the time we left we were hugging the Manager goodbye - it wAs that kind of place! In terms of the food, it was nothing short of spectacular. We had the half baby back ribs dinner and a pulled chicken salad and both were great. The ribs were perfectly cooked and the meat fell off the bone. Drifters has a BBQ sauce bar so you can choose your preference for your ribs - I liked the Smoke Fire best, which was a Texas style sauce with some chipotle kick to it! Also had the tots, the baked beans and the cole slaw, all of which were superb. I did leave there a little disappointed, but only because I don't live nearby and can't come back any time soon. However, I am definitely going to tell all my Nashville friends about it, and look forward to visiting on my next trip!!!

Bands/performers: 
Security and staff was kind of weird and a bit rude. I was doing merch for a well known band and they made it complicated for the band members to get back stage. Make sure to bring your contract, they misplaced out & it was a bit complicated to get our buyouts before they found the contract. Also make sure to do sound check because things got complicated when request where made to have the musicians sound like the band wanted to.

I can't even begin to explain how disappointing was.  I got the bbq sampler platter, so I tasted all the main stays.  All of it was flavorless and dry.  The chicken was the worst.  Then the pork. The ribs were sad.  The sausage was fine - I think they source it elsewhere, which makes sense. The service was good - not their fault.

We stopped in here for a drinks. The location was convenient as it was just a short walking distance from our restaurant. We did not eat any of the food because we were waiting on our restaurant to call us with an open table. The service was prompt and pleasant. Their beer menu was decent. Their are no cocktails on the menu and for good reason...the one I asked them to make tasted like cough syrup.

I'll start by saying I'm a bit biased. I'm a new board member. The Belcourt is one of our local treasures. The beautiful theatre and the incredibly talented and dedicated staff honor its tradition. Between the wonderful film selection (new films are added weekly!), special events, great popcorn and bar-yes, I said-bar, becoming a member of the Belcourt gives back-tenfold. Bring a group of friends, see the midnight movie series. It's money well spent.
Cool little spot with live music. Their food was really good, everything from the pulled pork, to pulled chicken, beans, and so on. But their sausage, wow, really really good.
Dry nice spot and they had a great show of song writers. The service was very poor and the woman behind the bar was either having an incredibly bad day or is just a rude person.

Went to Springwater to see a friend's band play and before going, I read all the reviews about how it's definitely a dive. Well to that, it did not disappoint. I've been in a few dive bars in my short time on earth, and this is definitely the most divey of them all. It's literally right across the street from Centennial Park, tucked behind a McDonald's. It's a pretty tiny place with two separate rooms, one with the stage where bands play, and the other has pool tables and a few tables with chairs. Considering the look of this place from the outside (and kinda on the inside), it was fairly clean and didn't smell (which I think a few other people have mentioned).

The bathroom left a lot to be desired, so you might have to meander on over to the McDonald's if you're picky about that kind of stuff. I wasn't drinking but I did overhear the bartender tell another patron that they do accept credit cards, but there's a $2 service charge of some sort. So, I would say they're definitely cash preferred so you might as well just take out a $20 and let it be. Overall, a nice little place if you want somewhere casual to hang out and get drunk for a really low price.

We stayed at this Holiday Inn for 5 nights. We spent part of every night listening to the singer song writers and had dinner a couple of those nights. The music was mostly good, sometimes not so much but very little was bad. The food was good the people and service were great and we are already planning a trip back. Definitely worth a trip!

I ducked in here last year and was too early for the show but hung out in a very funky room with a very cool group of performers until we had to head out for another commitment.  Everyone was so cool AND welcoming, it was on my return trip list fo sho.

So, this year, we found ourselves roaming the neighborhood, looking for a white bbq sauce fix, and we decided, why not put the two together!?!  

We stuck a head in and asked it they were cool with carry out carry ins, and they totally were.  We ran next door, grabbed the addictively enslaving turkey sammie from Hog Heaven, and came right back to sit at the bar and enjoy a few adult bevs with said sammie.  It was a match made in Nashville heaven.  The barkeep was attentive and welcoming, which should maybe be this city's new motto.  

I didn't notice any smoke until my post-bbq, cigarette-sucking dining companion lit up, happy as a clam, and announced he was home.  He was blowing smoke at me, though, for affect, so that was key re: my noticing smoke.  Smoking never quite "took" for me personally, but I thoroughly appreciate a little touch of smoker's haven while imbibing. 

Next year, third time has to be a charm, and I need to catch a band PERFORMING here.

Thanks for the great time!

P.S. I used the bathroom and was not scarred for life.  Don't get me wrong, I'm a huge fan of creature comforts, but I was also secretly raised a townie, so I've used the bathroom next to a tractor pulling a hayride wagon.  But, compared to that, this was a dream.  Its all about perspective, kids.

Cool place to go. They have live music which was okay. The food was good and I like there beer selection. Pretty busy and staff did a good job. I will go back and visit soon. I think with a little better music option I would give it a 5 star so we will see what happens next time.

Inside the Holiday Inn, not a bad little spot. Dinner and / or drinks while listening to some singer / songwriters. The menu is actually pretty nice. I went with the spicy chicken Alfredo and it was good! It does have a little kick to it. The chicken was grilled to perfection. My friend had the Mediterranean chicken and she said it was really good. The service is kinda slow. Overall, a pretty good experience!

This venue was the perfect size for a small concert! The atmosphere was cool with the a lot of industrial details around the room. Super easy to get in and out, the line moved fast, and there's a parking lot right in front that only costs $5 to use.  This place could've been 5 stars, but it was VERY hot! It felt like there was no air running and with everyone packed up by the stage it was hot and the air was stale. I've been to other venues of this size and have never had it be so hot. Towards the end of the concert my friend and I walked to the back of the room where there was more space and it was much cooler and more enjoyable from there. Overall a good place for a cheap concert!! Just try to wear lightweight clothes!
Awesome atmosphere! Lots of great beers on tap. Outdoor space with garage door that opens into indoor space. Very country chic!

Awesome place! Visited from New Orleans and came here to check out the LSU Tigers for the College World Series.
Great atmosphere, excellent beer selection, and delicious  food.
Special shout out to Jenna and Jot for top-notch customer service even though the power went out for a minute or two we had a blast and they made me feel like home. 
I will surely  be back and recommend it to everyone.
If you're short like me, get there early to get a spot on the small raised platform. It helps!

Our first meal in Nashville. It was great!!  Perfect atmosphere. Perfect service. Perfect hush puppies. 
Two for one happy hour beers was a nice Friday night surprise. 
Ribs are nice. Smoked nicely. Pulled pork and brisket done nice. Sweet bean side nice. Nachos very good. Fried pickles very good. 
Cole slaw a little to "creamy". Sausage good. 
Overall, great pub feel with great food and service.
Add: big whisky selection. Nice effort.

Super mediocre. Mac and cheese was good, Korean pork tacos had a huge bone shard in them, drink was unnecessarily sweet- almost undrinkable, music was ok, but sound was bad. Service was lovely. Product unfortunately not so much.
Nice low key atmosphere.  Outdoor dining.  Live music.

We waited 1 hour for our food, it was room temp french fries and sandwich (not even warm). The wait staff was very uninterested in us. Then we talked to the manager and she gave us $1.47 per person off our bill. Extremely disappointing -- last time coming here

Drifters has great BBQ! And this is a great feat considering this type of food is hit or miss in Nashville.

A large birthday party I was attending decided to eat here after realizing we had no reservations on a Friday night. Woops! But Drifters had some open tables and were able to accommodate our big group quickly. 

We had to try the BBQ brisket nachos, and they were exceptional! They have a variety of BBQ sauces in bottles on your table, and the sweet and spicy was my favorite. I also had the pulled chicken burrito, and I loved it! Decent salsa and good fillings. I sampled the wings, and they were great too, I like that they use a dry rub on them. Their menu is great, and I had a specialty vodka cocktail that was tasty too! 

All around a great meal, Drifters will be my stop when I need good BBQ!

I heart this place.  An IPA while watching a non blockbuster movie, you know, one that's well acted and has a plot.  Stoker was very cool here.  Filmed in Nashville, and it started with a forward by Nicole Kidman saying, "Welcome to the Belcourt...Thank you Nashville... If they are still playing this movie when I get done filming my next project in Europe I'll come back and do a Q & A after one of the showings..."  Just lovely.
Fun venue. The bands were great, the bartenders are fast. People are very laid back here and you do not get crushed. It was super warm with all the people so dress in layers.

Took some time to get service when we first sat down, but the food was good and our waitress was really nice. I had a brisket sandwich with hush puppies; my husband had the ribs. They kept running out of beer, so some friends had to keep going through the list. Music outside needed work (at first we thought it was the equipment making that loud scratchy speaker noise, but when someone different got up to sing we figured out that the girl was just screamin into the mic). We would have stayed on the patio to listen to the guy (Ben) sing if he was performing alone.
BBQ was great and prices were better!  Friendly and efficient service.  Fun atmosphere!

The Belcourt is a Nashville mainstay and a cultural treasure. As a local student, my Nashville routine wouldn't be nearly as enlightening without it. Come for the limited releases and programming, and stay for the profound sense of community and ability to drink while watching a midnight screening of Tommy Wiseau's magnum opus. 
The new renovations did not bring the sterility and identity crisis I was expecting either. The theaters were immaculately renovated and screenings are beautiful graphically and sonically.

Entirely too hot summer day to do anything outside so we opted for a movie. Belcourt was the perfect spot. We appreciated the free parking and the helpful cashier inside. The building itself was beautiful; very modern upon entry but the integrity of the older building was maintained within the theater itself. There isn't a bad seat in the joint and the popcorn was delicious! Plus, you can get a refill for $1! Their selection of films was a welcomed change from the other theaters around town. This place is a gem!

I have mixed reviews about this place. Great area.  Great remodel.  It can be a bit empty at times which makes it kind of boring.  Although, when there are people there then its rather fun.  I'm sure its tough to have two bartenders as it appears slow a lot, however, it'd be nice to have more people tending bar when its busy.  It takes a while to get a beer.  Also, they need to change the name.  The name really takes away from the chances of this place becoming popular.  All in all though, not bad.

If you've ever eaten a drifter that has been barbecued, this place makes better tasting things than that. Yuck. I would recommend a name change. Or some sort of insurance against someone stealing the "S" on the sign. It could end up being very misleading. It will be worse when someone is disappointed that there isn't a cooked drifter available to eat. You don't want to look that guy in the eyes.

I came here with my two brothers and my dad. We were flying out of BNA a few hours later and decided to get something to eat. Happy hour all day? Sure. I mean, I don't know if it's all day, but it seemed like it was. Buy one beer, get one free. They even give you a little card for it. That's cute. I got a couple of Sweetwater tallboys and it paired wonderfully with my giant stack of meat that I ordered. Brisket, for the record. Just regular beef, if we're off the record.

Came here last night for the first time for a concert. Love the wide open concept of the venue but unfortunately, the parking situation is a MESS! Not only is it super cramped, but they only accept cash. It's 2015, they should have a card reader for their lot attendants. Instead, we had to search around for 45 minutes for a parking spot/lot that took cards. Will be steering clear of this place for concerts until they get their parking situation fixed!

Brunch was good BUT server never communicated that mimosas are $20 PER PERSON for one pitcher of mimosas for the two of us we were forced to pay $20 PER PERSON FOR ONE PITCHER OF BOTTOMLESS MIMOSAS. That was never communicated to us what was communicated was that the pitcher would be $20 and it would be bottomless after that we were not accommodated for the misleading information we were provided. Horrible service and management brunch totaled $66 for two people not worth it all.

Finally saw a show here, Machines Are People Too.  I frequent the area a lot and it's always a similar type outside.  Great Nashville scene.  Super artsy, young, hip crowd and incredible atmosphere.  It's humble but classy and offers upstairs seating.  Though the bar isn't that high end it's well located so it never feels too crowded and the stage is easy to see from everywhere.  And because of the great area (Elliston), there are other places right next door to grab a drink or two (or three or four) before the show.  Sound is legit too!  And the bouncers/bartenders are super nice and accommodating.

Arrived here late after our flight landed and we checked into our rental down the street. The wait staff was nice and brought our drinks promptly. It was a bit tough to get water refills, though.

I had the catfish and the brisket. The catfish was done correctly, but the piece was really small. The brisket was tender but a bit too "mushy" for my taste - as though it had been sitting in water. I loved the "sauce bar" - lots of options, and all very flavorful. The hush puppies were the surprise-and-delight piece of my meal - the sweet onions and pickled jalapeno made for a super unique flavor, and the dipping sauce they came with was great.

One side note: we were there for over 2 hours on a Friday night and there was no live music. A band was setting up as we were leaving, after 11pm. We had hoped based on the reviews that we would at least hear live music coming in from outside, but either there was some confusion or a scheduling error.

Chose this via Google Maps, figuring what's not to love about bbq... and it's Nashville, chances are it's gonna be awesome.
A)This is situated in a hip little neighborhood and is on one rad corner. If you want to keep eating or drinking when you're done here, there's plenty.
B) It was a Tuesday early evening. Weather was splendid on the patio (inside seating and bar as well). Live music was just starting and did not disappoint. 
C) The BBQ was drop dead amazing. I ate every last bite on my plate and would've taken a bath in their made-from-scratch sauce (of which there's 5 varieties). Some of the best, smokiest, most scrumptious brisket I've had. Even the beans, which I don't normally touch, were devoured. AND the coleslaw!
D) Add to that 2-for-1 happy hour drinks and what more could you possibly want?! Except of course maybe a server who gives a damn, which in deed Drifter's delivered on. 
Happy beyond what I even expected. Returned two days later for a Round 2.
A true gem and one of my favorite places in Nashville. The only downside is that the parking lot is always full, but it's usually not that hard to find parking further down the street.

Right at the hub of the Five Points area, this place had the feel of an old garage with a covered patio. Not much on decor, but the service was prompt & friendly. I was in the mood for a sandwich, so had the Drifter, a nice pile of brisket and pulled pork. Pretty tasty, a tad on the dry side, but fixed that with plenty of sauce. Cole slaw was really good, and the spicy pickles were a nice surprise. Dinner companions dove into a plate of brisket nachos, which they really enjoyed. Saw others playing corn hole on the covered patio, even though it was raining outside.

I have been visiting Nashville quite a bit for the last two years and found this place based on recommendations. When I first started going here the food, service and music were great; however, lately seems service and food have been on the decline. It takes days for them to call you back about a reservation but that's after having to call several times and leave more messages. Also the last two times I visited they ran out of my favorite, meatloaf. This time around same deal with service but they did finally have the meatloaf. Clearly the quality has gone down. Don't know if they changed cooks recently but def a change in quality. I feel that based on my experiences that management and owners really don't care about the feedback cause business will not be an issue as they can still pack em in, although when I went this past Saturday night there were several empty tables. Good food and good customer service go a long way nowadays. Best of luck.

The Belcourt... We looooove the Belcourt! It's a great theatre and I feel so lucky to live blocks away from it. 

We're members and try to catch as many shows here as we can. The staff is always friendly and I love their concession stand. The prices are reasonable and everything is good. The seats in the theater are comfortable and the screens are nice. 

There are always great movies playing. We love catching the old classics, the films we've never heard of, favorite movies we know and love, sneak previews of movies not yet out and current movies that we'd rather not drag ourselves out to the mall to see. 

The Belcourt is awesome. That's just all there is to it!
Hoping the band is better than the service. Security turned me away to use the restroom. Okay, fine. But then I saw the same guy turn away a 4ish year old little girl. Not impressed...

It's OK; I guess it depends on what you're after and what you're comparing it to. Beer selection is just good enough to include an IPA. Wings, I'd be sure to order extra crispy on a hypothetical future visit, although they have some interesting sauce choices. I specifically asked if the ranch and blue cheese are made in house, because that's important to me, and she said yes. If that's true, they do an admirable job of imitating factory-made dressing. If you have other criteria than an expansive beer collection and the best wings ever, maybe this is your place.

They were great before the revitalization, and they are still great. This place has it all: art, popcorn, soda, beer, snacks, screenings of old, foreign, and new movies! I am right at home. The seats may not be high-backed or reclining, but they are comfortable and I am happy here.

I've seen several shows here now and I really like the venue. It's located near some of the best bars in Nashville--places that serve great bar food, cheap but quality drinks and even allow cigar smoking. The venue itself is a good size with mostly standing room well suited for getting up close to enjoy the show. The drinks are fairly priced here as well. The only downside is that parking is pretty non-existent for the venue itself though there is an overpriced lot behind it, but if you get here early there is plenty of free weekend and evening parking on the street further down.
There's nothing not to love about a historical building loved by its community and turned into a classy and amazing movie theater slash art gallery.

The Belcourt is a beautifully renovated piece of Nashville history: the Grand Ol Opry was held there in the 30s. With a well-rounded roster of movies that encompasses everything from "arty" and mini-mainstream films (Inside Llewyn Davis), to seasonal, topical and director's series, the Belcourt satisfies every moviegoer's desires in its twin theaters. There are also concerts and occasional children's plays staged by Olde Worlde Theatre Company.

In the summer they show movies outside on the side of the building, with the audience in the parking lot. If you are an insomniac, the Midnight Movie series will be just your cup of tea. It is one of a very few Sundance Film Festival affiliated theaters, which means that it screens those films long before they show up anywhere else. Their largest fundraiser (the Belcourt is a non-profit) is a red-carpet event with cocktails, appetizers and other fun things that accompany the screening of the Academy Awards in the theaters.

As the Belcourt is a true community project, their concessions reflect that spirit, selling Olive and Sinclair chocolates, Yazoo beer, and other local goodies.

If you live anywhere near Hillsboro Village and enjoy movies, it is worth it to get a Belcourt membership for $45. Not only do you get first notice of movies and events that quickly sell out, you also get frequent discounts AND free parking. 

The only possible con to the Belcourt is that the lobby is fairly small and can get congested before/after movies and events. But hey - grab some popcorn or wine (yep. You heard that right.) find a seat and enjoy the ride.
Great, historical theater! Lots of unique events and arthouse films. Love it!

I've been here many times over the years for random shows and I've always had a good time! It isn't my favorite sound-wise but depending on who's playing, it gets the job done. You can always count on good people watching here, that's for sure. 

If you're seeing a well-known band, plan on getting cozy with everyone around you. It can get a little packed. There is some seating, but it's very limited. There's a balcony that's great for getting some fresh air, having a beer and taking in a pretty good view of the Nashville skyline. 

You can pretty much always count on drink specials happening here and the bartenders are great. While we're on the subject of drinks though, I have to point out the floor situation in this venue. There are different levels that go up to seating and then back down to the main standing area. BE CAREFUL, hahaha. There have been so many times that I've seen someone completely wipe out because they didn't realize that there was a step there. If that happens to you, luckily there will be enough people standing there to help break your fall and save your tailbone/face.

Totally love this place. Amazing BBQ, hefty portions, cold beer, brisket nachos are a MUST! And good prices. 

Went there on July 4 after trying a competitor on Main St-you know who you are! They were out of pork and chicken at 6:00 pm. Come on, what BBQ place runs out of BBQ on July 4!

BBQ was very disappointing. Got the sampler platter, and most of it was dry. Left off the sausage, but waitress was nice enough to give me a discount off the bill. The rub was good on the ribs, but none of it was smoked that much. Staff is nice, dive bar feel is nice. But the food was definitely not good.

Adam was our server and he was so informative about the menu and also other places we should visit while we were there. The BBQ was really good but the sides we just average. It's a cool hole in the wall bar if that's what you are looking for... Adam made our experience exceptional!!
We had nice dinner while watching up and coming singers and song writers, great entertainment. I would recommend.

I really like the atmosphere at Mercy Lounge. Its a cool room and it sounds good up there. I also like that there is a deck so its easy to escape outside. It can get a little crowded in there for big shows and its kinda hard to get a drink, but that's to be expected when you have popular bands play a small room. 

The only complaint I have is that the online ticketing kinda sucks. There has been several times that will call has had trouble finding our tickets and one time ticketweb sent tickets to the wrong show, names of artists weren't similar and the date was different. Not really sure how that happened.

Oh jeez. I wanted BBQ but I had no idea this was hipster central. I am surrounded by losers with crappy beards and no jobs. I will admit, I get what they were going for with the way this place is. The atmosphere is different and I liked it. Sadly, after that, everything else sucked. The service was garbage. Our waitress interacted with us maybe twice. She directed us to the bbq sauces, which is another positive for this place. There is a multitude of bbq sauces and I appreciate the variety. The food is mehhhhh. The french fries are so salted that after I ate 2 or 3, I needed a coke to re-hydrate my mouth and wipes to get all the salt off my fingers as well as the grease. The pork was dry and not salted at all. Maybe if they took some of the salt off the fries and put it on the pork it would have tasted better.This place wasnt all that, especially for the price. I would skip out on this place and invest that cash somewhere better

The building is beautiful and has a wonderful ambience which places you in the movie watching mood. There are all your standard movie theatre fare served and a bar.

No matter what your favorite style of film (cult classics, documentaries, foreign films, and movies you will see nowhere else) they will be playing here.

I absolutely love The Belcourt Theatre!  

Go once, I am positive that you will be hooked!

If I wrote this after my first visit, I think it would have been a five star review.  I think Drifters has potential to be a four star joint but it's uneven in presentation and the food.

Pros:
Service - fast, friendly, and funny
Fried pickles!
Amazing Happy hour prices and duration
Outdoor seating
Ping pong tables and a friendly ping pong league
Local beer on draft
Wonderful Vegan and Vegetarian options

Cons:
BBQ - I've had the sampler plate several times and like the sausage and ribs but the pulled pork and brisket are just ok.
BBQ Sauces - Not really a huge fan of any of them.  Not terrible but not great
Hush puppies - just ok.  Perhaps since we're so far from an ocean but they're not worth ordering

We've been a bunch and I might return but it's more for the location, service, and prices rather than the BBQ.

I really expected more from Drifters just by the reviews I read so I was a little disappointed. The fries are delicious, the nachos are good the tortilla chips are just a little over cooked for my liking. That's preference though. Overall it's a decent place and being a bar it's open until 3am so if I ever need fries late, this place has my back.
If you're into bbq definitely come and try theirs. That's obviously the biggest thing here, being a vegetarian I didn't try much, I'm also the worst pickiest person alive. My sisters boyfriend loved it and all the different bbq sauce options they have. The queso is really good I definitely recommend. Parking all around that's free or cheap. Would recommend eating outside because once it gets busy it's super cramped.

Service wasnt the best but hell. Who really cares when your at a fun place. My wife and I were passing through and felt in the mood for bbq. I yelped this place and decided to try it out. The only other place that I really loved was phill's in sd (5/5). If you know of that place we got a base to gague. If not then, my bad. The pulled pork was good. They have these ketchup bottles filled with bbq sauce on the table. Like 4 or 5. I went to get some drinks for me and the chick and the bartender said, "hold on ill get your drink tickets". Drink tickets? (I went on sunday) he came back with two drink tickets. Buy one get on free on any drink. The price at the bar were same as any other place but 2 for 1. That was cool. I want to do 5 but the server was so so. Plus, I would like to believe I am still giving a good reference as I think 4 or 5 stars are pretty much the green light. I say go for it. Its a little divey, but that adds to the fun, Esp. For a gen y crowd

Enjoyed a few beers at this eclectic place while listening to great live music. Food looked awesome, although we didn't have anything to eat, and bartender was super friendly. Would love to go back and try something the veg pie !

This is my favorite place in Nashville. I like the popcorn and membership is a great deal. I have been sold out more times in the last six months than the previous six years. New Nashville means lots of independent film lovers, I guess.  Still, go to The Belcourt! As a bonus, i once saw the Mayor seeing a matinee in pajamas here.

Ahh, Drifters. I will start off by saying that the BBQ is only mediocre and overpriced. However, it is good enough to serve as good drunk food when the opportunity creates itself. This place is not about the food, it is about the people and moderately priced booze. Plus, they feature great music in their outdoor space on weekend nights. While Drifters has a fairly large group of employees who tend bar throughout the week, they are all the kindest and most attentive that you will find anywhere in East Nashville. The same goes for the clientele-everyone I've come across at this place is very nice, interesting, and not stuffy (which can be an issue at times at other East Nashville joints). Bottom line-when you're at Drifters, you feel at home. Great drinks, great people, and your tab won't break the bank.

I was excited to try the Family Wash as I love me some chicken pot pie and live music. The scent of thyme had my mouth watering as we sipped beers and waited. I loved the vibe of the place-very intimate and eclectic-but alas, I was not wowed by the pot pie. The crust was simply a round of puff pastry, and the filling bland -not even close to the yumminess of a homemade pot pie. My hubs had the bangers and mash, which he thought was tasty, but overpriced for the amount of meat he received. Overall, if going for the live music, it may be worth it, but next time, I'll stick to drinks. Service was good.

friendly, upbeat, attractive staff with healthy skin and smiles.   good service and great tunes on the speakers.  not too loud and not too quiet.  some football too on the screens.  haven't tried the food but id be willing to bet it's out of this world.  exposed rafters are a classy touch, with a fully exposed HVAC system sitting pretty up there too, with nothing to hide.  I think this is my new favorite bar.  can't wait to try the food.  I hope it's served in disposable containers, even if I order it for here.  namaste!

Methinks NOT NOT NOT!!!
Tony and I stepped into the place looking for HOG HEAVEN...and we were in the wrong place...definitely the wrong place.  It is definitely a dive...and I know Dives..I am from West Virginia and we have a ton of dive bars...so this reminded of all the dives I have be in back home..
I would not go here again!
Too Dirty!!
The people a little scary!!
Too dark !!!
and I don't drink anymore..so this would not be for me!!
Sorry.....

I was only in Nashville for a night, and I'm so glad we chose to eat at Drifters.  I'm a vegetarian so I was super excited to see I could get a tofu bbq sandwich!  My boyfriend ordered the brisket and was also very satisfied. We were there on a Monday, so although there wasn't any live music (we went to Broadway for that anyway) it was trivia night.  We had never done trivia before, and the host was so nice and we had a lot of fun.  I would definitely recommend it!
Come for the tater tots, stay for the smoked chicken wings. smoky and perfect. Coleslaw and beans win too.
Established in 1896, this is a bar worthy of patronizing. Historical in its right, we grabbed a few beers, ate some of Buford's grub, and snapped some pics.

I attended an event at One event space at Cannery and had an amazing time. It is the third floor of the Cannery Ballroom. 

Pros: wide open space. Definitely room to play and host any type of event. There is a smaller room off to the side that can host a bar and some high top tables. There is an elevator and stairs to the venue. I don't know what the venue provides, but it appeared to have limited restrictions on decorations. 

Cons: there is no patio. Only a small stairwell for those who need some fresh air. There were several events also occurring that night throughout the building and the signage was terrible. The lines were a mess and we had no idea where to go. 

Overall, it was a great place to attend an event. I don't have knowledge of prices. I would suggest looking into it for an event. The capacity is 400!
Had to feed the nieces and nephew. Pulled into 5 points and told them to pick. I'm glad they picked Drifters. Divey little bar. Good BarBQ. Fun servers. Brisket Nachos for appetizer is a good start.

Excellent beer selection. The half chicken and ribs looked amazing. Was not in the mood to eat, but if I did THAT is what I would have ordered. They have ping-pong and cornhole. Great outdoor seating.

If anyone is thinking about going to the exit/in in Nashville for concert don't do it. Me and a friend were there for 15 minutes when my friend was dragged out by his arm for allegedly giving alcohol to a minor. We never talked to anyone but each other the entire time. He was not allowed to explain so I went and talked to security and they said that regardless they have to go with security's word. I asked about cameras and they said they wouldn't take the time to check. They also did not attempt to talk to the minor to get the story straight before jumping to conclusions. I politely asked for my money back since I did nothing wrong and I was a paying customer. They said it didn't matter cause they were a private establishment and their are no refunds. When I attempted to leave the guy at the front made another snark comment about "we saw what we saw". I replied ok but you didn't cause it never happened and I left. A whole day wasted. Don't go to the exit/in they were rude from the get go and probably made some excuse to kick us out.

How could I have not written about ANY of my visits to this place!

I fully agree... this is the BEST Dive Bar in Nashville.  
That said, Nashville's not my favorite city.  
The whole town's a little too clean and flashy AND worst of all,
way too 'Country'-fied for my 'Big Easy' Gimmie- the-P-funk desires. 

When we first went (2008), the Springwater only opened at 4 pm. 
SO, in my vast knowledge of 'Dive Bar',  I truly felt they where cheating. 

As y'all know I take this genre very seriously!  I am very happy to report #1, because I just noticed they now have a website and #2, my Annual, Nashville, Birthday Bar-Hopping Bash is next month... they now open at Noon!

This place is cool and dirty. 
I have never failed to have . . . 
a great time, good conversation or low bar-tab when visiting.
(*I do believe they are cash only, pay as you go) 

GO!

Three stars. BECAUSE of the service. Beer was good, ambiance was good, food was good, service was horrible. We have been driving all day from Texas, we wanted somewhere to hang out an relax. Our waitress was rude, it took us a while before we got any service, though the joint was almost empty besides the bar area which the bartender was taking care of. I would have given more stars if my waitress wasn't so rude.

2.5/5

I was passing through on a road trip, thought to check it out for dinner.
The atmosphere is charming but the brisket was drrrrryyyyy and I had to smother that sucker in so much sauce to get a sense of flavor. Waitress was lovely and the blues band was great.

1) no chairs.
2) speakers aren't hung so sound will travel to the back of the room. speakers seem to be closer to the stage and sound does not travel to the entrance of the room.
3) no chairs.
4) A line that first begins outside the chain link fence, outside the property?  Really?


I was the second person that walked into the ballroom and I went directly to the stage.  Had read reviews and determined that the front stage area would be the best observation deck.
Wrong.
People began squishing me in and crowding me so tightly, I got nauseous.  No air ventilation. I began sweating. Rocking..  
I had to find some air.
I left the front of the stage and wandered over by the bar, by the bathroom hallway.
The lights went down, people were swaying, sitting on the floor, against the wall, some were crammed in the window sills, trying to take a load off their swollen feet...

I found air and a seat in a window sill. Two other people came along and begged to share the window sill with me.

The music began, but none of us wanted to leave the window sill.  So we sat together and listened to the band, in the other room.

Face it, this venue is highly restrictive.  If you need to sit, if you can't stand people crowding you, and you have to sit in a window sill, just to sit down....  
I don't think you're going to be very happy.

Music?  Honestly, I can't remember.  Sound?  Muffled from the other room.
Temperature?  As long as you're not in the crowd, it's nice.. I felt the A/C working.
Bathrooms?  Never got a chance to see them.
Staff?  Never conversed with any of them.

No matter how much I love music, and no matter how much I would travel to the ends of the earth to see my favorite band perform... I would not return here.
Not unless they got some chairs for us to sit and enjoy the bands performing.

DO NOT WEAR HEELS.
Ordered eggs at 12:30 they didn't come out until 2:00pm and smelled like crab. Worst place ever

Loved this place!! Came by on a Friday night after dinner to check out some music. Once we were convinced by the music we stayed for a while and got great drinks and even some delicious peanut butter pie. We stayed for 2 sets and both were amazing! The place itself is also super cool. The only downsides were service wasn't too great and it seemed a bit quiet for a Friday night, but we enjoyed ourselves anyway!

Prestiegelöst lokal honky tonk bar med avslappnad stämning, kall öl och god mat. Hipster vibbar existerar inte här. Kom som du är, blandad publik. Vänlig personal som hjälper dig gärna, eller bara pratar bort en liten stund om de har tid. Jag blev t.ex. till min BBQ-rätt erbjuden ett par kryddstarka BBQ såser som inte fanns framme i den vanliga sortimentet på borden (där fanns det 3 stycken att välja emellan). Han som serverade mig frågade om jag skulle vilja pröva några starkare varianter och skyndade in i köket och kom ut med 2 behållare med söt/stark resp. stark/stark BBQ-såser.

The worst restaurant experience of my life. We waited over 2 hours for brunch that came out ice cold. Tables who came in and ordered after us were served before. The server was fine but manager could care less that we had a poor experience and would not offer to make our experience better in any way. Would not recommend ever and if you're on any type of time crunch absolutely do not stop in.

The Cannery Ballroom gets great shows.  That's hard to deny.  And the prices are good--both in terms of tickets and not unreasonable at the bar.  People complain that the stage is in the corner, but I personally don't think it matters (There are bad seats (aka those to the side) when the stage is in the middle of a rectangular room too).  The warehouse-like feel is also really cool--modern as opposed to honkey tonk.

I've been to Cannery a few times and each time has been a good experience. One huge plus is the parking lot that is adjacent to the building. Parking is $5 and I don't have to walk a mile in the dark to the venue. The room is huge and I don't feel claustrophobic in there. The bar is pretty big and has always been well staffed when I've been there, so getting a drink isn't that hard. The stage and the lights are great and they book some great shows there.

Love this venue, my favorite band Paper Route only plays this venue when they are in town, which makes it great. Very nice small place which makes shows much more intimate. Really enjoy this place and wouldn't miss a show here for the world.

This independent theater has been setting the gold standard for years, and the recent(-ish) renovation has only made it more impressive. Buying tix online is easy, and then you can just check in at the ticket counter. You can, of course, take a chance and just purchase tickets day-of, but often it's a packed house. So do yourself a favor and buy in advance. 

The theater is pristine and has all the trappings of a traditional "art house" cinema in a modern setting. Restrooms are immaculate, and the lobby is fresh and bright with loads of windows for a healthy dose of natural light. Concessions are top-notch. I'm talking a wide range of craft beer and wines, yummy snacks and ice water offered without being pushed to buy a spendy bottle.b

Though not worth a ding in stars, I don't find the chairs particularly comfortable. So if you are coming for a long flick, bring a sweater or jacket to cushion your behind; you can thank me later. 

Otherwise, go! Enjoy! See something weird or different to scratch your intellectual and artistic itch - you know you wanna head over right now.

This is our second visit. Both times we've had a different experience. Each time my husband got the bottomless bloody Mary's and I the bottomless mimosas. 

Our first visit our server was AWFUL ... this was just a couple weeks ago. The server MAYBE brought refills every 45 minutes. 

Today our server was AMAZING!!!  Refills came around every 5 minutes to all the tables. So great. I never had a half empty drink. The only downfall is as my husbands food. He got the gator tail and it was way overcooked- like he was chewing alligator bubble gum. Yucky!  Anyways....I wish we got our servers name. She was super nice and did a fantastic job!!!
Amazing corndogs and fries. One of the best corndogs I've had actually. Really good smoked wings and bbq sauces. The bartenders are some of my favorites in Nashville.

The Belcourt is amazing! Everyone there is so nice and friendly, the concession stand isn't too expensive and every film I've seen there I've loved. The history is so rich too, and I feel special being there even though they recently remodeled, it still has the charm it did when I use to go there back in the mid 90s with my grandmother. Definitely one of the best places to see a film in Nashville.

Very happy about the amount of vegetarian options! Got the BBQ black bean nachos and they were awesome. Ate hush puppies for the first time! Server was awesome and patient since we hung out for almost 3 hours.
Nice casual atmosphere. Young vibe. Went on Sunday evening , no brisket, no ribs, they were all sold out, very disappointing. Wait staff was slow.

Great BBQ in a relaxed environment! They have a good selection of sauces, reasonable prices and friendly staff.  We tried a little of everything. We had the sampler dinner, hand dipped corn dog, smoked wings, and a BBQ sandwich.  Everything was hot and delicious!

It was pretty dull inside, however it was a Tuesday. $2 off chicken and catfish tacos on Tuesdays for happy hour I believe 2p-7p. Also half price select appetizers like my cheese squares! Everything was really tasty & fresh! 

Whenever I'm near Music Row again, they can have my coins.

Passing thru Nashville on my way to Memphis and decided to stop for bbq.   I ordered the Drifter and my wife ordered a pulled pork bbq sandwich with Cole slaw on top. The service was awesome.  The food was average. Was not hot but warm.  I was expecting slices of brisket with pulled pork.  However it was all shredded.  The restrooms were disgusting.
Happy new year!  What a cool spot to party.  They have a awesome amount of talent coming through here on stage.  Besides the drinks being a little higher in price, I have nothing bad to say.

Each time I come here I always wonder why I come back. The service is terrible. There were only 4 other people in the bar at dinner time on a Sunday and it took at least 50 minutes for us to get two sandwiches and the last sandwich came another 10 minutes after that. The sandwiches were supposed to be panini's but the meat (turkey and bacon) was not warm and the bread was lukewarm. It was supposed to come with ranch, which none of them did and the waitress seemed annoyed when we asked for a side of ranch. I've been here multiple times because I live down the road and the experience is usually the same.

I spent several days in Nashville and a writers round happened to be taking place on my birthday, and one of the artists performing that I wanted to meet was there, so I ended up coming here for a birthday drink and dessert (had dinner elsewhere on this night).  The dessert was really good, and I like the over all layout of the establishment.  I saw other groups get meals and it appeared everything was coming out in good order.  Parking, there is a way to get validation but there are meters within a block of the hotel where this restaurant is and they are free after 6 PM.
Drifters is my go to spot for BBQ nachos and live music. My first experience here was a bad one, but since have been back many times and will continue to go!

I really don't know how the reviews are so positive for this place.  Maybe I just came on an off day?   I checked Yelp expecting to be led to some awesome bbq but that was not the case.  I came for lunch and I ordered the sampler platter that had a few ribs, pulled chicken, chopped brisket and a sausage link.  First off, the sausage link was the same as you'd get from the grocery store made by Eckrich.  It was just warmed up and there was nothing barbecue about it.  Next, the pulled chicken tasted like leftovers from the day before.  It was extremely dry and I actually had trouble swallowing it.  To top it off it had ZERO flavor to it.  I really enjoyed the brisket.  It had good flavor and might be worth coming back for.  The ribs were nothing special.  The atmosphere is actually nice and the people are nice. As I said before, maybe they had an off day but I don't come to Nashville often enough to make my way into this place again.  I'll be trying other barbecue joints next time.

The Belcourt is flat out fantastic. It really is.

I love that they show everything from edgy documentaries to cult classics at midnight. They also have some incredible events like Oscar viewings, concerts, comedy, and the latest Wes Anderson film. It's a historic site, so the interior is very classic with the red curtain and updated but still unique. They also serve alcohol and food! Score! 

I love the Belcourt and need to frequent them more often!

I've been here MANY times since 2000 and the venue is pretty good. Always has great bands come through. From legends to nobodies just starting to make a name. 

Cons: the staff has become increasingly rude over the years. Shitty beer selection.

Hands-down the best barbecue I've ever had. The ribs came right off the bone, the pork was flavorful and the sausage was just sweet enough. For my first dining experience in Nashville (and all of Tennessee), I couldn't have asked for a richer experience. They were even dog friendly, allowing our little pup to eat and drink with us on the outside patio. Live music was performed outside, which added the final touch to an incredible evening.

Great little place! 

We are on the road for a few days and looked for a dog friendly place. Found this through Yelp and headed in.

Great food, beer and service. Very friendly and accommodating for our two large dogs.

Highly recommend. Thanks!

I went to the Belcourt this week to see 12 Years and Slave. I have never been attracted to this theater because they typically play independent films that I have no interest in. However, the experience of being in the theater is worth seeing any movie. The theaters remind me of stepping back in time to the old days of stage play. But instead of a stage they have a movie screen. The screen in smaller than a larger movie theater but get the job done and I didn't notice any discomfort in watching. They have a concession stand offering popcorn, sodas, candy, beer, etc... Tickets were $9 and the concession stand was cheaper than a bigger theater would be. I would recommend this theater to anyone in the Nashville area.
Hog Heaven next door was not impressive at all and neither was this place. Its a super divey bar. Its also cash only....it's 2018....I don't want to spend $4.00 at the ATM to get a drink.
Great beer bar dive with a shockingly good sandwich shop out back. Get a beer and let Bruno hook you up with the best Reuben in Nashville.
