I'm giving this one star because of the s***** attitude from the bartender. It was our first time there last night (Thursday.) Myself and 4 girlfriends met for drinks and sat on the patio. There may have been a total of 15 people there max--so they were not busy. He didn't say hello, didn't smile, and seemed put off when I asked if they had champagne (which was $10 a glass--too much) and he acted like it was a lot of trouble to tell me the seasonal beers on tap. No thank you after I paid and left him a tip that he didn't deserve either. He was also rude to my other 2 friends who ordered a drink. 

The place is gorgeous and it's a great patio so it was disappointing that the service was poor. 

Also, it stunk inside as if they mopped the floor with old, dirty water.

I was so excited for the show last night, but the venue is so disappointing. Everyone was just crammed up to the stage, which is in the back corner. We made it close to the front, but there was no hope of making it back to our spot after a bar or bathroom run. So, we hung out near the back and we couldn't hear anything. The speakers do not fill the room. They are half way up the room, pointing towards the stage. I saw a handful of bar stools around the giant bar. Speaking of which, we never had to wait for longer than a few seconds to get a drink. So that was a plus. Also, there were plenty of restrooms. Another thing this place has going for it is close parking. We were lucky enough to find a free spot in the actual Mercy Lounge lot, but they have a pay lot that is in the same area. I don't usually mind to pay to park downtown to have to keep from walking in weird areas. Overall, I was so excited to see the band last night. I am a huge fan, but I just wasn't able to enjoy myself as the venue is such a bummer. I don't know that I will back to a show there, unless there is some kind of seating.

The Belcourt is the best theater I've had the chance to participate in. Their Midnight Madness movies are exceptional in addition to the quirky new/obscure films they continually show. 
You better come to the Belcourt at least once if you want to experience Nashvegas.

I was introduced to Drifter's by coworkers for a go-to happy hour spot after a long day at work. Happy Hour is great but their BBQ nachos are amazing. Get loaded BBQ nachos with EVERYTHING. Probably some of the best nachos I've had but it must be LOADED with EVERYTHING. 

Parking is probably the biggest pain but great place to wind down!

Wow we got a mile outside downtown Nashville and found this gem of a place.  Forget the crazy crowded overpriced tourist traps, this place was where it's at.  Really great local music ("Free Cookies" was playing when we were there) and a really friendly chill atmosphere.  And great parking and excellent food and drink (and a lovely happy hour special on top of all that).  I would hang out here all the time if I lived in Nashville.
A fun, funky joint in East Nashville. Marcia couldn't have been more accommodating and terrific, and the food couldn't be tastier. If you want a casual genuine local Nashville experience, head there!

Where I come from we have amazing shows and awesome venues. We drove 4 hrs to see a show here.  It seems there is 3 clubs in one place so confusing fir concert goers.  There was so much security you would think we were in a bigger city must be alot of problems to have so many on staff. Weird thing is I never saw them inside, felt safe though. The place has 2 major problems horriable sound due to the shape and nightmare bathrooms. The sound was aweful unless you were right next to  the stage. The bathrooms were designed for tiny people with no legs and were pretty gross. The bartenders were on it and amazing. So as far as seeing another show here? Nope not wasting my money I wish the band we saw would come play our town again.

Incredible theater! They play all the best movies whether it be classics, the never-before-seen, and new indie flicks. 

Never before have I seen an entertainment venue such as this do such a spectacular job at preserving their history and going out of their way to educate and accommodate their guests. I've attended a few showings here (Boyhood, Rocky Horror, and Citizen Kane) and each had a speaker or some sort of film expert preface the showing so that we could really indulge ourselves in the experience. 

They strive for excellence and deliver nothing less. I hope to see the Belcourt thrive for many years to come.

I'm in love with the velvet curtains and open space with a high ceiling.  It feels like I'm time traveling.  I've also found that the doormen and bartenders are very friendly.  I like exploring the city but have to admit I can't stop coming back here!

The sangria was watery and tasteless, but at least it was only $10 a glass.

The waitress first informed me that "we don't have sangria here". When I informed her that it was red wine like merlot, fruit, and usually triple sec and/or brandy, she eventually brought me a water glass full of ice and a thin dark liquid that tasted faintly of fruit. The bill at the end of the night had an "open liquor" charge of $4 and a $6 "upcharge" for the sangria that the Grill refused to alter. The nachos had barbecue sauce! and service was poorer than average. What a joint.

Absolutely awful for brunch. Maybe better for night life, but they should stop trying at brunch. Which should be one of the easiest meals of the day?? We had 22 of us for a bachelorette party so called weeks in advance for a reservation at 10 when they open. Showed up at 10 after, and doors were still locked. Got a dirty look and an eye roll when we knocked. Had to call to have them open the door. Said we have a reservation, was told they dont taje reservations and we could "push these tables together" ourselves... 

ordered bottomless mimosas for almost the whole party, 2 of the pregnant ladies of the group ordered virgin bloody marys, the server first brought over single mimosas, after telling her that's not what we ordered, she then went to go make the virgin bloody Marys as we watch her pour vodka in a glass...  we tell her we need 2 virgin ones. She had her mind set that someone ordered a regular one as well? No one did.. food comes out, eggs Benedict was a hard boiled egg, 2 orders did not come out. Waitress takes her order again for an omelet with green peppers and sausage, everyone is done eating by the time that one comes out as an omelet with bacon and jalepenos and a runny egg center. This guest did not eat at all, but did enjoy the bottomless mimosas. 

We asked to talk to the manager who was the girl that was slamming food on the table and rolling her eyes as we were knocking to get in. Not friendly and blaming everyone else for the issues. Always saying "I'm sorry, but they didnt tell me about the reservation." "I'm sorry, but they dont tell me anything" "I'm sorry but I didnt have time to push the tables together." "I'm sorry but it's just me and the server today and it's her 3rd day"... take some responsibility. Look at your reservations for the next day you work before you leave for your shift.. put the tables together the night before or come in earlier.. have better training for NEW people. No, it's not the servers fault it was her 3rd day. Luckily she was super sweet despite getting a few orders wrong. 

Also asked to speak with the owner I think before we got our food to find out after we got our food that he left. He knew we wanted to speak with him, and left..  The most helpful person there was the chef's husband who came in to help(but doesnt work there) and actually listened to our concerns and who we had to get the rolled silverware from while we already had our food. 

Just absolutely awful, thank goodness for the bottomless mimosas and we still had a good time because of the ladies we were with. Definitely a memorable experience (not a good one, though) to many of our first trips to Nashville. Please do yourself a favor and go somewhere else for brunch. Pinewood Social was absolutely worth it and super cute place. Way better of a place to hang out.
Super moist pulled chicken and several great sauces make for a very tasty meal ! Food 5 star, Service makes it 4 star.

Mercy lounge is a great venue, but it is VERY intimate. If you are seeing a well-known band, be prepared to get very comfortable with the people in the room. 

There is a back room with pool and a second bar that many people don't know about. Definitely check it out if you are sweating to death in the other room. 

In the main concert room, there aren't many seats, so I suggest getting there early if you want a place to sit for the concert! 

Parking is limited, but there is street parking nearby. 

If you are bored on a Friday night, and see tickets to a show at Mercy Lounge, buy them! I have not been disappointed by the local acts they bring in.

Traveling south we picked Drifters based on Yelp review, as we were looking for some good BBQ.  We started with the fried pickles which were advertised as being spicy, they were not but overall were fine.  

I ordered the rib basket with a side of Brunswick stew.  I have had a lot of Brunswick stew and living in GA believe I know a good one when I taste it. This was more of a chili taste with brisket piled on top.  The brisket was good, but a good Brunswick stew is made with pork and chicken, more vegetables (okra, corn and Lima beans) and has a nice tang to it.  This was not close to what I was hoping for.  The ribs have a dry rub, and were dry and needed one of the house sauces to eat them.  

My wife had the brisket and pork combo.  It was good,  cooked well, tender and portion was generous.  She had the baked beans which were nothing special, having a little extra spices added.  
Overall, Drifters is an above average BBQ restaurant (3.5) but really nothing special.  Service was very good and friendly.
Love this place.  Dive bar but friendly and fun. BBQ is fantastic.  Out of brisket tonight though.

Awesome show, but have never been so hot at an indoor concert, everryone complaining, people left early.  Wasnt because of a sold out show, because it was unbearable when it was only half full. To me, the sign that the venue cares about the patrons is if the restrooms are taken care of.  This was not the case. A mess.

Went in on a whim on a slow cold day and ended up staying for over 2 hours chatting with the staff and a couple of regulars. Could not have had a better time. Everyone was incredibly friendly, funny, helpful and laid back and the drinks were refreshingly well priced. The only food we got were the hush puppies but they were fantastic. Can't wait to get back. Kudos to Marie, Patty, Adam and Ben for such a great afternoon.

I absolutely LOVE going to see movies at the Belcourt. Movie watching is definitely one of my main hobbies, and there's no better place in Nashville to indulge in it than the Belcourt. Between their midnight movie series, the Saturday morning series, the outdoor film series, and the endless array of independent cinema they have on their reels, there are so many options for people to enjoy here. 

I'm beginning my membership tomorrow. I know I won't be able to use the student discount forever, so I may as well take that one step into adulthood before I graduate. As long as I'm living in Nashville, I will be a member of the Belcourt. The movies and the staff are what keep me coming back, though I have to admit that the specialty cocktails they create for the midnight movies are a definite bonus! I could go on for much longer about how great this place is, but I think you get the picture by now!
Great music, never too crowded, free parking, and it's non smoking!  This is an excellent choice for experiencing live music in Nashville.

Some of the best BBQ in Nashville. Friendly staff, never have to wait long to be served even on trivia night. The absolute best Brunswick stew in the state, honestly. The prices are fantastic, and there isn't a bad thing on the menu.
Best live music off Broadway without all the tourists! Great neighborhood feel with fantastic live music daily! Check them out. It's a must to see in Nashville.
Good atmosphere to watch the game but very slow service. Our order came out wrong and the alligator bites were raw. Really only positive was drinks were good.
Well they changed the menu again, no more kale salad  such a bummer!  Definitely recommend coming for Hexagon presents still though!!

One has to remember that when you go to a venue blocks away from a college campus you're admittedly going to be seeing shows with bunch of drunky drunks. We saw Toro Y Moi at this establishment and we may have been the oldest people in the crowd. There were plenty of frat boys and dude-brahs attempting to dance while spilling beer all over themselves. There were a few girls most likely on some 'other' intoxicant because one was waving a stuffed squirrel up front while her blue haired friend humped her and her boyfriend made out on both their necks. And although Toro Y Moi is a little more electronic on his albums, he pretty much killed it with a live band backing him up. As soon as the place filed up the sound seemed better, I certainly left with ears ringing. My boyfriend got a gin and tonic that was $8 and served in a small plastic cup ... um what? At least it was 3/4 gin. Anyway, it's okay for what it is, not the finest place in town and not the worst.

The bands I've seen play at Mercy Lounge were amazing and sounded great in this venue. The one thing keeping me from giving it a 5-star rating is that people at the bar are sometimes loud and obnoxious and really distract from the concert experience. This, of course, is a potential problem anywhere there's a bar in the same room as the show, but it'd be nice if Mercy Lounge tried to separate the two a little more.

Looks a little shady but is actually a fun little place. Lots of good beer. Lots of good food. I had the pulled pork chimi and it was awesome! Corn hole in the back. Live music in the front. Within walking distance of a lot of places if you want to do a pub crawl. Nice place to hang outside in the summers. I keep hearing about the corndogs so I'll try that next time.

This venue is alright. Far from my favorite place to see a show in Nashville. 

There's a huge line to get in, which seemed a little dramatic, but fine. That's cool. While in line, some red bull girls brought us free drinks which I liked, but when we got to the door, we were informed we would have to finish them or toss them before we came in. Again, I get it, but geez. I had literally just been handed the drink a few minutes before. 

Once inside, good luck. It just kind of is what it is. No place to sit. Just a big open room. Maybe I'm getting old. I probably would have preferred that in my 20s, but I felt like we didn't even know what to do with ourselves. We just sort of stood in the back the entire time, near the end of the bar. 

The sound wasn't great. It always seems weird to me when I'm at a venue in Nashville, TN and I feel like the sound could be a lot better. The speakers weren't well positioned and there was quite a bit of feed back in the beginning. 

I did enjoy myself, but when the show ended, I was more than ready to leave.

Passing through Nashville on a recent x-country drive and I NEEDED ME SOME Q.  Drifters provided !

Fellow yelpers steered me to this dive and IT WAS GREAT. We had the combo platter.  Ribs slid off the bones, brisket & sausage were also perfectly smoked & prepared.  Sides were tasty classic preparations.  Service was Friendly and Quick.  Food & Service were  5 star.  4 stars cause, although they had a full bar, they did not have any NA Beer.  Doesn't matter, next time in town, I'll be back

We were looking for an alternative to the downtown Broadway scene. We found Drifters on Yelp and decided to try it. We came for drinks and live music on the patio.  The drinks were great and the music was awesome.  The only downside was we arrived toward the end of the bands set.  It would have been nice to have another band come on after.

Called over two months ago to make a dinner reservation for my wife's 40th birthday party.  Party of 11.  I even repeated the date back to the guy on the phone to make sure we were all set. I even let him know it was for my wife's 40th.   

Showed up this past Friday night (11/7/14) with my wife and our friends, all of whom had traveled great distances to join us for the weekend to find out they had no record of our reservation.  Wow.  

They tried to seat...ahem.... cram us at two separate high top tables right by the entrance and when they gave a bar stool to one of our friends, she was told not to put her feet on it because it was broken.  

I'll admit they did try to offer us a free round of drinks but I was not having it.  This was going to be our first meal out together to kick off the weekend and to be seated separately (on broken barstools) was completely unacceptable.  

We walked out and went across the street to the Porter House Bistro.  I'm writing a review of this place next.  We were seated immediately by a wonderful staff and were treated to one some of the best food and cocktails of our entire weekend.  The chef even came out to greet us and took a bunch of photos for us as well.  

The Family Wash might be good for beers, live music, etc., but I will never know.  You blew it, guys.  I will return to East Nashville (hopefully soon and often) and will spend my money elsewhere.

I love this place, however, please fix the food.  The food is REALLY not good.  Everything else is awesome. Its easy to have even ok food at a venue but this food is rough.  The music rocks and the staff is great.  But please just fix the food.  I gave it 5 stars because this place is great.  They just need to get something corrected on the food.  The pretzels are stale, the mac n cheese is oily, the grilled cheese is cold and undercooked, everything on the food needs work. But as I said this place is great for music.  If they get the food going then Id say their business would double in a short amount of time.

I think this place can be great. I am a huge fan of Jed's, so when I hard they were opening a music venue next door, I was pumped. My friends and I had been speculating what was going to open for a while and we are glad to welcome another bar to our neighborhood.

We were there for their grand opening party and I was impressed by the band and the beers. The band was playing covers and sounded great. The draft beer selection was way better than next door. I hope to see them change them up with local and seasonal brews, but we'll see. The owner was also there, socializing and making sure everyone was having a good time.

Another reason I see my friends and I coming back was the patio. We're all about some good patio drinking, and while we will still enjoy some patio beers at Jed's, this will be the "classier" option to start the night out. I also see some dancing in my future here.

All in all, I need to go again to give it a more detailed review, but I am excited to see where The Country goes and what kinds of acts they can get in their doors. Perhaps it can earn the coveted five-star review in the future?

What a little gem on Church street. Plenty of nearby options for pre game (or after party). The venue has great sound quality, friendly bar tenders, and most importantly, some fabulous acts in a the best music venue-dive in town. I saw Cee Lo here - he had two great openers and the crowd was super friendly to a gal flying solo. I would definitely come back to catch one of the many recognizable bands who come through here, and I can't wait to catch a discovery act they find.

I've been here on Friday nights with live bands, Monday nights for trivia (which I am so not good at) and eaten and drank all the times in between and I really love this little biker-bar-style place in East Nashville.  

The service has always been great no matter how busy it is (and its usually very busy), the food is good BBQ-style smoky goodness and the beer is always cold.  You can sit inside, admittedly a smaller space, or they have a very spacious patio, and the stage for previously mentioned live music is outside.  

I highly recommend their nachos (can be had with or without meat for my veggie-loving brethren) and their spicy black bean burger is a thing of beauty.  The patio can get smoky, and parking is limited in their small back lot, so keep that in mind.  

But there's always something fun going on here, and its become a go-to place with friends, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a good time that its too fancy or pricey.  Drifters is one of those places you cross the river to enjoy willingly.

We wanted a dive. 

We got a dive.

Beer was cheap.  Cash only.  $5 cover for the bands that were there.  

We came as one band finished their set.  Next band sucked, but we played darts and laughed at ourselves instead.  

Iconic music venue in Nashville.  Although we didn't hit it on the best night for music, if you are lucky, you might be there when it does. Attracts some pretty awesome musicians.  See? http://www.rollingstone.com/music/videos/premiere-the-black-keys-invade-iconic-dive-bar-on-little-black-submarine-20120904

Cool spot.  I'd totally come back here again.  Gritty, smoky, and dodgy.  Dig it.

I photographed the AMA's this year and this is the venue that I was assigned to on Saturday night. It is a cool little spot, the stage is on the small size and I was front and center with my camera. I was pushed and almost knocked over SO many times. The lighting was great though and the service was good for how packed it was. The drinks are expensive...$7 well shots, so I wasn't too excited about that. But I will probably go back if they get a show worth watching.

this was my first time going last night to their annual 12 hours of terror.. I can honestly say it was the most fun ive had in years. it was truly magical eventhough i went by myself people around me were so nice and i never felt alone...first time and definately wont be my last. the staff there was so wonderful...i cant say enough nice things about you guys...thanks for a magic experience i will remember forever.

Was there recently for the I Saw the Light movie premiere and I have to say, staff were amazingly wonderful. I had a great experience. I'm from out of town, but would definitely see a movie there the next time I'm in the area. I have nothing but wonderful things to say about this place and the people associated with it.

This local art house theater is a Nashville institution that celebrates independent filmmakers and classic cinema. After decades of being well-loved, the aging theater recently reopened after a major renovation. The result is a beautiful new lobby, updated bathrooms, a well-stocked concession area that serves standard movie fare as well as alcohol, and gorgeous theaters evocative of classic Hollywood glamor. The only knock is that the seats can be a tight squeeze if you're packing extra pounds. Rule of thumb -- if you need a seat belt extender when you fly, you might not fit.
VERY good BBQ. Bevare that the portions are enorm so do not ordet too much. I was done after my nachos (which was very tasty!)

We went to Drifters because my friend was craving their BBQ chicken burrito.  We went for the food, but this review is really about Marie the bartender and guest manager who went far out of her way to help me.
   
I was visiting from out of town, and it was my last stop before heading to the airport.  We ate outside on the patio.  Super relaxing.  I was wishing I could hang out longer to hear the band that was setting up.

When I got to the airport, I realized I didn't have my hoodie.  Ugh.  It's my favorite one, very unique, a gift from my sister...I must have left it at Drifters.  So I called and got connected to Marie.  She didn't see it, but took my number just in case.  The good news - when I landed there was a message waiting for me that she found it.  The bad news - I didn't have a way to get it!  Hearing the disappointment in my voice, she offered to mail it to me personally.

A huge thank you to Marie!  That was very kind and I really appreciate it!

Aweosme place!  Music every night!  And the music starts around 6pm which is EXACTLY what Nashville needs.  Good music that starts at a reasonable hour and and the music still plays into the night!  Great food and good deals on drinks!  And music every night...and music every night... and...you get it!  Just go. Its fun.

Ah, Drifters... No frills at it's finest!
It's tucked right in the heart of five points, but doesn't feel "too" hip. You'll see all kinds here... Old, young, couples, families, dogs too!

The food is consistently good. I always go for their BBQ pork sandwich, my man goes for the pulled chicken sandwich. It's one of my favorite places for BBQ in Nashville - and I'm the kind of person who has to sample BBQ everywhere I go. LOVE IT. 

So the food, it's good. The atmosphere is what keeps me coming back though. The staff is so friendly, the crowd is usually really chill, and the outdoor seating is the best! Especially when a local band is playing, which is often.

For me, summer is Drifters season..... I'll be there quite a lot over the next few months. See you there!

Great dive-bar scene with plenty of outdoor seating. The food is surprisingly good, but I'm not a bbq fan...so I usually order the veggie burger and it's delicious! Beer is reasonably priced. 
This is a traditional spot for me to hit, as I usually alternate between Drifter's and Beyond the Edge.

A beautiful theater that charges reasonable prices.  And I love that I can enjoy wine or beer during the movie!  They also offer coffee and tea!  

There's something about going to the belcourt that is so much more special than going to a big megaplex.  I wanted to post my 5 stars, because this place deserves nothing less!

I was teetering between 3 and 4 stars, because the service was good, and overall the food wasn't bad. The problem is that I felt the queso dip could use a little more punch to it, and the ribs were very so-so. They do have very crisp french fries, which is one of my favorite things. Also they have a selection of bbq sauces which is nice. I felt several of the sauces could have been left off, including the Texas sauce. This sauce was more of a letdown to me since I moved here from Texas, and was simply not blown away. I have been here once before when visiting Nashville, and I was more impressed on that visit. I will be more scrutinizing of places now that I am going to be using yelp more frequently. Overall this place is worth a visit, and I will return. The great service, live music, and overall quality of the food is good.
Dim lights, dramatic ambiance, authentic country music and stiff drinks, my kind of place. I forget the name of my bartender but she was amazing.
The hush puppies were AMAZING! Best I've ever had. I wish the chicken strips were bigger, but the sauce was great. I'll definitely be back.

Beer wasn't great (had the kazoo spring) yuck took all I had to actually choke it down. Staff was friendlier to the men  guess what women drink beer too and we tip as well.  Met some cool people in the short time we were there that's about as memorable as it gets

I am a guy who enjoys a good whiskey in a good place and this is definitely one of the best.

I've been in Nashville for a couple of months and been to enough number of bars including the famous Honky Tonks and loved them, The Country was the best.

It helps that I live pretty much next door to the place but that's not the only reason. Their selection of alcohol is amazing and the beer rocks!

The bartenders are amazing and super friendly too! Always a plus point!

The classic looking patio goes amazingly well with the setting. I really liked it the other time when there was a slight drizzle and I was starting to get a light buzz.

All in all, definitely a great place to be!

I'm surprised I'm the first lower rating for this place.  The food was fine but nothing special.  The pulled pork was a little bit dry.  This place has a really good selection of beer and is upscale rather than relaxed.  They must have really put their energy in the bathroom design; they were really nice.  The bands were okay but they were free and seemed like a regular thing.  We were there on a Tuesday.  I would go here if you are a beer connoisseur looking to have a drink with friends.  If you are looking for music and food too, I would skip it.
No wait staff for the patio. The bartenders are extremely rude and the drinks are average. The patio has potential but the service makes you never want to return.

When you think about BBQ you should need to remember it's not just a type of food it's a culture. Drifters captures it perfectly. Great food with a BBQ sauce station and some great beers to choose from. They always have live music and the bands are excellent. Now throw in the fact you can bring your four legged kid with you... and you have a wonderful hang out spot.

Mercy is a staple in Nashville and a really great venue. But that is kinda where it ends. No bells and whistles, very basic, certainly needs some upgrading, bathrooms are horrid. It kinda just is what it is. But that is okay. I'm not here for the venue, I am here for the shows. 
It's not a place to go "party" - it's a place to see a good show. 
It beats out places like 12th and porter ANY day. 
But they book great shows, always have a friendly staff, management is great.

Wish I could give this place zero stars. They ignored us when we sat at the bar to place an order and finally someone spoke to us... 40 minutes later we still haven't received our food and the staff is horrendously rude. Not worth it y'all! PASS!l oh and then when we got the food FINALLY (what was supposed to be jambalaya and a quesadilla) we had two TINY cups of gumbo.. $40. Not even what we ordered. No refund offered or anything. Management needs to get a grip on this horrendous restaurant.
Hard to evaluate bartenders are unresponsive and sully band seems good and the crowd responsive, but come have a pulse of

I went here to see Sam Hunt. The show was great. The event venue is fine, it's a large room with a stage. The stage is where it is to allow for the max amount of people. If you want to be close to the stage, get there early. I arrived about an hour and a half before the show and got right up in front of the stage. And there was free parking! I didn't get anything from the bar or go into Mercy Lounge so I am not sure how that is. 
I do think the staff at the Cannery Ballroom need some training. I emailed them about tickets (I wanted VIP tickets), facebook messaged them, and called them. No one ever had the decency to email me, call, or message me back. There was plenty of time before the show for them to get in contact with me. Even if they were sold out, I still would have appreciated being told that.   Working on customer service would be a good way to improve this business. 
Otherwise, I had a great time and the show was great.

This is one of the finest shitholes I`ve ever peed in.  Seriously, its THAT good. They only serve beer, its steeped in the cheapest tobacco smoke possible, and on any given night the patrons look like the extras from some action movie scene. Its cheap too. They even have a playboy award for 13th best dive back...like from the 1990s. I like to think of myself as a dive bar expert, and this one passes all tests with flying colors.

Exit/In is a great venue! I have attended a variety of shows from a packed out house to a half full performance. It's dark, musty, and a great experience. If hanging on the stage isn't your preference, hit up the balcony upstairs. I can also usually hang toward the back and still maintain my personal space without issue. 

They have a good selection of beers and spirits and there is a $10.00 minimum to use a card. Well drinks are $5.00 so grab yourself two for the show and you are set. 

Shows vary in prices but are always affordable. Yeah, parking can be slightly tricky at times, but it has never been impossible for me. A good amount of side street parking and even if you have to walk, it really isn't bad at all. 

If you are looking for that in between venue for rising and mostly-known bands before they get really big, this is your spot!

Really upset/disappointed with this place.  Came all the way from Chicago to Nashville for our 5 year wedding anniversary to see our favorite band (a band who's show we actually met at) Delta Rae at the Exit/In.  

Upon entering I was told my 42 year old wife was not allowed to drink because her ILLINOIS Temporary License which was not expired (while she awaits her formal license to be sent in the mail) was over 20 days old.  We had drinks prior at a restaurant down the street and also a bar next door with no problem. 

It was very upsetting to both of us and completely ruined what was suppose to be a memorable anniversary night in Nashville. I tried to see if they would work with us somehow but they refused stating it's the law (as if she's underage). 

They wouldn't even refund us our tickets.  Thanks Exit/In
Great small venue! It has everything you need to put on a great show. And they have a wide range of artists that come through. A few I've seen are Cursive, Save Ferris and Ingrid Michaelson.

Drifters has the potential to be a powerhouse BBQ provider here on the east side, but the past several visits have been somewhat disappointing. I'll be the first to admit that they have some great items on their menu, and the pricing is wonderful for what they offer, but the quality of the BBQ leaves a bit to be desired.

During the most recent visit, I ordered the combo with three sliders (chicken, brisket and pork) and fries. Starting with the pulled chicken, I found the flavor to be slightly questionable. I could immediately see that it was dry and not juicy at all, and there was something unusual about aftertaste that I just couldn't put my finger on. Next, I moved on to the brisket and found the same issues - dry and not very flavorful (especially compared to some amazing brisket I've had at some other local places). The final slider - the pork - was pretty good, but nothing too spectacular. What helped was their selection of sauces. We had a sampler of the Georgia, Sweet & Smoky and Sweetfire (which are just 3 of the 9 they offer), and they helped provide some of the flavor that was absent in the meat. The fries were great, though, and I easily could have polished off another order.

In past visits, I had the chance to try the hush puppies, which are really something special. Sweet onions and jalapenos encased in a battered shell and coupled with their Alabama sauce - how can you beat that? I've also had the pork plate during past visits and it's been OK. Maybe we caught them on a bad night for this recent trip, but as much as we love having a BBQ joint here in the neighborhood, we'll probably continue to fulfill our BBQ needs outside of the 5 Points area.

The food was wonderful.  Great portions. The smoke on the ribs was great. The coleslaw a little dry but do NoT let that stop you from coming here. Is dog friendly and Max, our server was great. Just as we were leaving, a band was setting up to play. Please, if you're wanting ribs, please, stop by and eat here.

My review for Cannery needs to really just be a copy and paste of my review for Mercy. 

They always book great shows, great staff, great manager. It's a GREAT room for wedding receptions, events, etc because it is literally raw. Just an old building with lots of floor space and brick. 

No bells and whistles, nothing special, but it's a great place to see a show!
I'm a huge fan of Black Bean Burgers...not a vegetarian just love them. This is by far the best one I have ever had!!! Absolutely delicious...so flavorful. A must try even for a meat lover.

My bad experience has nothing to do with the quality of the food or drink. Me and wife went here while on vacation from outta town. We sit at the bar and while checking out the drink menu the bartender strolls over and says all well cocktails are two for one along with most beers etc...so we order 2 whiskey and cokes. Plain and simple. Drinks get made, we drink em, and I ask for the check.(we just had the one round because we wanted to bounce around to many different places to see more of Nashville on our somewhat short stay) What do you know, when the check comes out the drinks are not two for one. Now they're only five bucks each so it's not the end of the world but I decide to say something anyway..."I thought you said these were two for one?" To which the bartender replies "Oh, well those are doubles, so..." and then just walks outside to deal with another customer. I know for sure I didn't order doubles so why the hell did I get charged for them? More then likely by checking our ID's when we ordered she noticed we were from outta state and just figured she'd take full advantage of us. While she was outside I just paid the tab, with a tip,(don't ask me why) and we left. Wasn't gonna wait for her to come back to argue over five dollars.

Very intimate music venue...as in very tight space. The acoustics were great but there is literally no space. Overpriced and water-downed drinks. If it weren't for the great entertainment would never come back.

Food was amazing. Could not have been happier. We came here around 8pm on a Thursday after spending the day brewery hopping and the patio was a great place to sit and relax. The live music was enjoyable and not too loud where you can't hear the person you're with. 

We ordered the hush puppies which were very good, but very filling so I definitely recommend if you have two or more people. 

I got the bbq plate with pork and it was AMAZING. The meat was juicy and the sauce was to die for. The fries -- don't even get me started. So crispy and crunchy and amazing. I cleaned my plate. 

I highly recommend Drifters if you want good bbq and a great atmosphere.
Good spot for a burger and happy hour is all day on Tuesdays so that is always a good thing. I love this place for staying non smoking so that is plus!

Yep, I see a few 1 star reviews for unfriendly staff...I concur. However, this 1 star review is to warn you to not order the chicken under any circumstance. For $8, they bring you one sad chicken wing that was cooked God knows when, that they have warmed up in a microwave alongside a miniature biscuit. If anything, it would be good for a laugh 6 beers in.

Okay, okay, don't order food at a bar and expect a lot. So let's talk about their beers on tap. Hmmm, slightly cooler than room temp, served in a warm glass. Umm, I'll go elsewhere thank you.

After walking out of Beyond the Edge because of the smoking we went here. Waited what seemed like forever to get our food while everybody around us had there's in a matter of minutes. Our waitress forgot our appetizer order. We both had the burritos, nothing remarkable.

Today, I had the nicest surprise on my lunch burger...
I ask that my bun be toasted and when it arrived, I saw a little garlic butter with garlic on my bun.
What a treat!

I like this place.

Went here twice. First time had a pretty darn good experience. Great food. We got stew, nachos, and a taco salad. Service was fast, portion sizes were enormous. Live music, pretty nice outside venue. Our server seemed like she was worked like a dog.

Second night I really wanted to try their ribs. Had to go physically find a waiter to take our order after waiting at least twenty minutes. He then came back to tell me they were out of ribs. Took a good 10-15 minutes after that to get our drinks, no service recovery. We left disappointed. Might try going on a weekday or for lunch

A really fun place. Truly a dive bar but with character. The bartenders were really attentive and friendly. We were visiting from San Diego and they really took care of us. They had live entertainment that night and the band that was playing, The Stoves, were really good. We had the Nachos and pulled pork and pulled chicken sandwiches. They were all good. The best part were the sauces. Keller brought over a sample of all of their sauces and I couldn't make up my mind which was the best. We will have to come back and test them again.
Awesome experience. Special thanks to security (Eron) for helping  with my special needs.
Great beer options and a very cool atmosphere. Ordered the smoked chicken tacos, which were delicious. They also have live music regularly.

Maybe it's because the Belcourt is where I first saw The Rocky Horror Picture Show (as a 22-year old; far too late, I know), but I have a lot of love for this small indie theater.

In a great location, the Belcourt is all you need in a small theater:  cheap tickets, plenty of seating, a historic home-town vibe, and the ability to buy alcohol at the bar.  It's not rocket science.

I also saw the recent Amy Winehouse documentary here.  Can't wait for the theater to open again this summer!

So for my 1800th review the Exit/In is a worthy venue.  I saw my Oxford, MS pals the Kudzu Kings here and crazy Kudzu Dave, the bass player, virtually lives at my house in New Orleans about half the year and I've known the folks in the band from since and before the band started.  I was also glad to see quite a few folks from long ago that I hadn't seen in many years show up for the show so that made the whole experience even better.  The venue is spacious while not being too big to lose the ability to have a good view of the performance from pretty much all over the space so it was intimate without being cramped.  They also have an upstairs balcony level area that also adds some more good space to view the show.  The sound quality in the space was also of good quality which isn't always the case in some venues.  I was also happy to see that this space has hosted a LOT of famous and less famous quality bands and they have a pretty extensive list of them on the wall behind the bar.  The bar service was quick and easy but it did take the bartender's longer than average to remember my tab. The Tiki Bar exit that leads to their patio did not have a Tiki Bar but it does lead off pretty near to Cafe CoCo which is an awesome place to grab a snack and more beer after a show!  

Overall this is definitely an awesome venue to watch a show in and it is just a perfect size place to have a great music experience.

Cannot give this place a higher rating. I've rarely had a better movie-going experience, with knowledgeable and hospitable staff, high quality refreshments, gorgeous theaters, and excellent movie selections. You also get a parking pass that is good for 2 hours before the movie time and 2 hours after, giving you time to explore Hillsboro Village without the hassle of street parking. I will be back soon; I would see any movie shown here at any time.

The BBQ tofu nachos are my favorite thing to eat in Nashville when I go out, hands down. I get a craving for them sometimes and will drive all the way across town just to eat there! They have a great selection of things that are not BBQ and lots of vegetarian options. I give 5 stars for the food but a 4 overall because the ambience and service are just ok. It's nice and clean though and everyone is friendly so I highly recommend it.

This place is amazing! A little off the beaten path, but so worth it. Huge dog friendly patio with bags and ping pong, and the inside is divey and wonderful. The food is very very good, and the prices are really reasonable (and the happy hour specials even better!). I'm a vegetarian, but my husband is not, and we were both so happy here. I had the fried tofu sandwich with cole slaw and he had the pork sliders with tots. Both left us so happy and full (but not too full to try the banana pudding!). The portion of tots was enormous, but they were the perfect conduit to the delicious BBQ sauces they have. The sauces are all available via BBQ sauce bar--our favorites were Texas and sweet & smoky. The banana pudding was pretty big; my only complaint was that it could have been more banana-y (and even then it was still really good). Highly recommend this place! If only they would pick up and move to Phoenix, AZ!

You've just gotta love a place like this.  And that people "get" it.  It's authentic as hell, just a good bar with great sound.  We saw GPN here on Halloween night a few years back and, as others have mentioned, the crowd is a blast at this place.  GPN dressed up as some old country stars and did a few tributes which were well received.  EXIT/IN isn't fancy, isn't expensive, and isn't really touristy although if you dig live music and happened into this place on a trip I doubt you would be disappointed.  It's a little out of the way and not smashed in between other bars, parking isn't great, but despite the dark and somewhat sinister vibe, you just know it's safe.  There's only one reason to come here and it's for the music.  They take it seriously and get it right.  So for that, and the love the locals have for the place, 4 stars.
Friendly service and cheap digs. Dive bar feeling without all the diveyness. We got the tots, fried pickles, beer and vodka drink. Good stuff

Went on a Sunday night around 8:30pm.  There was an $8 cover per person.  The the kitchen was closed.  Half the draft beer was sold-out, making the otherwise decent beer selection below average.  The band playing was good, but the acoustics in the place were bad.

Bottom Line:   Go somewhere else.  The acoustics are not good, there is a cover charge, the kitchen was closed and the beer selection was sub-par.

Stopped in Thursday night after having dinner in the Gulch. None of our group had ever been. We had originally thought we were going to stop into the Tin Roof, but all they had was hockey on the TV. Walked down to Frisky Frog and the music we heard sounded good and we decided to stop in. Place was not super busy, but lets be honest, it was a Thursday. We grabbed some drinks and sat close to the band. The  band was great! Such a variety of music, including rap. Great music to sing and dance along to. Drinks were good and strong. 
We enjoyed ourselves so much that we ended up going back again Friday night after making some rounds.

Cannery Ballroom-sardine sweat shop. So hot it must have been in the eighties last night for Rival Sons. Unenjoyable to the point of no return. It's not me Cannery Ballroom it's you and we won't be seeing each other anymore.

In town and staying at the Holiday Inn, I wanted to get a quick bite to eat before heading out for the famous Nashville music scene so stopped at the hotel restaurant to eat.  It was the Commodore Grill on a Wednesday night.  The food was good, service was good, but the music was great!  Groups of three singer/songwriters took the stage for three songs each then left for another group of three.  Found out it was "Songwriters Night".  When I asked what was the gig, (really, Holiday Inn?), was told, "welcome to Nashville" in a smooth Tennessee drawl.  

Awesome experience ended up parking at the Commodore for the rest of the night and am looking forward to a return visit.   I'm not a country music fan but these live performances were great.  For anyone looking for a real Nashville experience by performers who really put it out there, check out the Commodore Grill.
Waited for 1.5 hours for chips and queso. Queso was cold when we got it. Bartenders are good at their job and very nice. Kitchen is very slow however. Management seems to be non existent.

I'm from Saint Louis and have traveled to Nashville twice now to see shows at this venue. Both times were fantastic! Great space, great bar, great staff and great sound quality. It's a 5 hour drive that really feels worth it after seeing shows here.

Had the woodchuck cider and a tofu sandwich. Big heavy sandwich, in a good way. Tofu fried, a little bland in terms of the breading, but great texture/moisture level, and bland tofu breading works as a good base for their variety of sauces, many of them spicy in unique ways. Good outdoor seating with good lighting. Parking's a pain but its a pain for any business in this area.

Film, food and wine, and special events.  Car parking free when you get your ticket and number for the parking machine.  Wish they would do the Lord of the Rings uncut Trilogy lock-down again. What fun that was.  Perhaps a Harry Potter lock-down soon...or even something a bit more serious all day/nighter.
Belcourt East any time soon please to save us the trundle across the river.

Love the Belcourt! I, unfortunately, don't go as frequently as I'd like (but, that's only because my wallet is tight). That said, though, their movie tickets are SO well priced...and a bar inside?...most excellent. Just a short 7minute walk from house, I couldn't ask for a better landmark in my neighborhood.

The sampler was one of the best bbq i ever had, it is a bit costly, but there was plenty of food left over on my wifes plate. None on mine. I like to eat. The service was great. If i go back to nashville, i will be eating at this place again.
Awesome place to have a casual drink and listen to amazing live music from the best in town. Highly recommend, and will be stopping by next time we're in town!
Drifters, oh Drifters. I love you so. From your amazing two for one drink specials to your BBQ tofu you make me infinitely happy.

Without a doubt, my favorite pub/restaurant/hangout place in Nashville.  We've been coming here for about 5 years and always enjoy ourselves on our rare date nights.  Great atmosphere, good music, fantastic beer selections, and the menu (while small) always delivers.  Hard to pass up the shepherd's pie, but if you can...try the meatloaf and mac & cheese.  

We also see families in here quite often so it is pretty kid friendly.  In fact, they have kids nights at least once or twice a month.

Passionate owners who care about service and their restaurant.

Cool atmosphere....good beer selection!
Chicken pot pie = fantastic
Meatloaf = stupid good

Horrible. The worst BBQ I've had in years. The meat is burnt and dry. The sauces are below average. Cole slaw is heavy helping of mayonnaise. The other menu items might be better, but this place should not call itself a BBQ joint.

I had no clue what to expect upon my arrival at Exit/In, but I was MORE than thrilled when I walked in.  Intimate, but not too small or cramped.  Larger than High Watt, but smaller than Mercy Lounge, this venue is perfect for rising stars in the Nashville (and beyond) scene.  I can't wait to check out another show here!

This is an old style neighborhood type bar. The music on a Saturday night was very old school. We ordered two drinks the Creamsicle (which used to be on their menu but the bar tender will still make it) and the Caucasian. Both drinks were really good. The Creamsicle had a slight medicinal taste but overall a pretty good rendition of a Creamsicle. The Caucasian was very yummy. Chocolatie and creamy. Kind of like a really good chocolate martini. My only complaint was that the band came around very quickly to ask for tips. I think they only played about three songs. Overall though a really fun and comfortable place to hang out at.

I used to LOVE this place, but this one experience will forever ruin Frisky Frogs. I'd gone before, for preds game and such, but I went for brunch with my girlfriends and some friends from out of town. I made a reservation beforehand for 11:30am.  We get there and the guy at the front (later found out he was one of the managers) tells me I am early and "I guess I can sit you"...as there was a table already reserved for us with my name on it. Then he tells us we are not allowed to order before 12:30p so the kitchen can get set up. Weird, but we ordered unlimited mimosas anyway. Finally ordered food...waited....waited....waited...food never came.  WE WAITED FOR 3 HOURS. No joke. Turns out they cancelled our order because the group at the other half of the table (who arrived after us) got their food so they thought that was the whole table. Got the manager over, told him we get it, half of us work in food service, but still that was unacceptable. This one manager (they are twins, one brother is SUPER NICE, but the other one, the one we dealt with, was a super ASS) tells us he is sorry but this is just something that happens and we can wait for our food or he would be happy to cancel our orders. We asked about our drinks and he said he could give us 10% off, but that is the best he could do. 10%...are you serious! I told him straight up we were getting up and walking out, not paying for anything, and made sure our waitress (who was super overworked and was basically doing the whole place by herself) was not on the hook for any of this. We gave our waitress a big tip and left.  Will never walk back in that place again. I apologize to the other brother I did not have the pleasure of meeting, please know all these bad reviews are because of your brother.

Best happy hour, best staff, best live music, and best food all in one place!  Drifters does an amazing happy all beer and single liquor pours are 2 4 1 Monday-Friday from 11-7, and all day Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday!  The inside is non smoking but they have a huge patio which allows smoking and is dog friendly.  Some of my favorite menu options are the BBQ nachos, hush puppies, corn dogs, ribs, and actually I love their fries! They have a great assortment of BBQ sauces that range from sweet and smokey to fiery hot. It is a little dive barish but I think that leads to the charm and appeal! A must try!

I had the gumbo nachos and added shrimp. They were great!! So were the 2 for 1 drinks. The best part was the music, they played all the hits!! Casey, the bartender was very friendly and nice to talk to!!! I will be back!!

Went there last night for the first time to see Smith and Myers and I thought the place was the worst small venue I've been to downtown Nashville. No circulation of air throughout the place made for everyone around my wife and I sweating our asses off. Level of the floor to the stage left viewing at a minimum. People at the bar ignore you. Just overall a horrible experience. I will not be back there for anything again.

Stopped in Thursday night after having dinner in the Gulch. None of our group had ever been. We had originally thought we were going to stop into the Tin Roof, but all they had was hockey on the TV. Walked down to Frisky Frog and the music we heard sounded good and we decided to stop in. Place was not super busy, but lets be honest, it was a Thursday. We grabbed some drinks and sat close to the band. The  band was great! Such a variety of music, including rap. Great music to sing and dance along to. Drinks were good and strong. 
We enjoyed ourselves so much that we ended up going back again Friday night after making some rounds.

This movie theater might not have reclining seats but it has amazing movies and a whole downtown area right down the street. I love going to lunch and then the movies right after. They play old and new movies. The area couldn't be more perfect. The prices are very reasonable and everybody is very friendly.
Hard to find but well worth the effort. Had the half pulled pork and brisket sandwich. 4 oz. each and super flavorful, Try the super hot sauce. Fries were hot and seasoned to a T.

I would give this place 0 stars if I could. We came here shortly after they opened on Saturday morning (9/16/17) for breakfast. First off, their coffee machine was broken and I had to run next door to get some coffee. We immediately ordered food (eggs, with bacon, and toast), nothing fancy, and over 1 hour later still had not gotten our food and people who were seated ahead of us were still waiting. It's not even like this place was busy. Our server was TERRIBLE and seemed to be avoiding our table. She came over after 30 minutes of waiting to say our food was almost ready....30 minutes later, still waiting. Not sure what her definition of almost is...hmmm. After over an hour of waiting and no refill on my husbands tea, I walked over to tell her we would like to cancel our order if the food is not ready. She said she'd check and let us know. We watched her go to the kitchen, and waited another 5 minutes of hearing nothing and her ignoring us. At this point I told another waitress we want to leave now and have no interest in dinning here. This waitress, told us she was sorry that they just started serving breakfast within the last couple of weeks and are still adjusting. After hearing this, I'm thinking they should maybe go back to NOT serving breakfast. She then told us don't worry about the tea. OK, yeah, thanks for the favor?! So after an hour and 15 minutes of completely wasting our time and starving, we ended up at the same coffee shop I had run over to for coffee this restaurant did not have. Moral of the story-avoid this place like the Plague! So many GREAT food options in Nashville and this is NOT one of them...not even close.

Had the pleasure of coming here this summer during 48 hours in Nashville that was apparently right after the theatre re-opened from renovations. The sheen on the walls and the seats was immediately apparent, as was the programmers and staff's love of film! If I lived in the area, I'm sure I'd come here all the time. Intriguing neighborhood around the cinema as well that offered more depth to Nashville than the country centric downtown I experienced before coming over to this place.

My favorite place to watch movies.
It's so great, I became a member.
Good variety in movies, comfortable seats, people don't bring their children, and it's never over crowded...

This place rocks and I am SOOOO glad it's nearby.
I also love the neighborhood and usually go wander, after a movie.
Lots of parking (free), conveniently located to restaurants and cute shops and it's clean......

My favorite theater.

A classic venue, dark, dingy and always packed for the shows I go to.  We strolled in at 9.45 pm on Saturday for Mogwai and they came on at just after 10.00pm, perfect.  We managed to stand on the steps stage right which is great for 5.'0 peeps.  The wall of sound from the Mogs was great and very very loud, A good time was had from everyone.  Bartenders busy and efficient, bouncers, busy and polite.

The food wasn't bad for a hotel restaurant, but the truly amazing thing was the music! I know it shouldn't be a surprise being in Nashville, but the music was great from a group of writers and great singers! Great ambiance, and getting to see one of the great country music writers Will Rambeaux and Co play was a treat and a pretty spectacular welcome to Nashville for a first time visitor!

I just wish I could have stayed for the Japanese Country band that was about to go on stage. 

I enjoy the venue much more than the food. That's not to say the food is awful, by any means. But my expectations have been being raised for so long about the amazing and out of this world Shepherd's Pie. It was good...don't get me wrong...but it didn't live up to all the hype I've read and heard. (Although it's great hangover food to have in your fridge.) Maybe I'll try another dish next time I go.

Convenient, casual and clean. Plenty of parking. Our team had a  casual corporate after hours dinner. Service was slow and not overly attentive. Food was typical Bar n Grill offerings. Live music was a nice touch.

It's not often you walk in a door and feel like you just came home, but that's what happened here.  This place is the very definition of funky. No contrived "upcycling" here. No contrived music or food. All real and gutsy. If you need for your plates to match, your music to be quiet, and your kids to be perfect, don't come here. It can be loud, and the meatloaf is better than mine. And mine is GOOD. We also had the gorgonzola chips.  I'm not a great fan of blue cheese, but these are addictive. The service was great and the music outstanding.
Took an hour and a half to get a salad. No music, very dull atmosphere. Do not recommend.

Amazing food and great ambience. Was wanting good barbecue after a long flight from Los Angeles. 

My girl read some good reviews about Drifters and we set out GPS as soon as we landed. It was on the way to our hotel.

We ordered the fried pickles, hush puppies, corn dog and the Hickory Smoked Sampler Platter (pork ribs, beef brisket, pulled chicken and French fries).

The ribs are amazing. The meat pretty much falls off the bone. Some of the best barbecue I have ever had in my life! If this place was in LA, I would eat here every day.
Cool joint.  Nice place to see live music.  Nashville can be a tough spot to compete for attention.  Mercy Lounge certainly holds it's own.

I am in love with this  THEATER !!!
Noel and I went here to enjoy "The Interview" with Seth Rogen and James Franco. The theater is very nice. 
I love buildings from the past !!!

I purchases my tickets online, and had them set to pick up at WiLL CALL
the parking lot to the side is machine pay but if you go to the ticket window they will give you a code to put into the machine so you can park for FREE..I didn't know this, so I paid $5..now I know ..and I will remember !!!

The concession stand had many choices !!! Full bar stocked with alcohol and beer, including draft. The food choices are not your normal movie theater. We bought two large sodas and buttered popcorn and it cost $18.50.  The movie tickets also cost me $18.50 for both tickets. $37 for a great afternoon out with my lovely daughter...plus the $5 for the parking but the end result PRICELESS MEMORIES with my daughter..

There is theater rooms to show four movies at one time here. They show a lot of independent films. You can become a member and support the theater. Check out their website at belcourttheater.com  

I hope you go and enjoy the show!!!

Came here after a rehearsal dinner. We enjoyed the change from country music that we had been listening to all day. Best part was the fact that they had a patio so we were able to head outside as a group and have a conversation while still listening to the band without having to shout over the music!

Off the beaten path but a great find. Food was good and all day happy hour on Sunday is tough to beat. Their menu changes based on what they have left so be prepared to have alternate choices in mind. By far my favorite was the lady who played the accordion (she also played the keyboard) which is so rare but awesome.
0 Stars. Not allowing "chains"as in a necklace,is pretty ridiculous as as a dress code.
Awesome food!! Brisket was sooo juicy and we loved all the different BBQ sauces to try! Pretty good beer selection too! Very friendly staff!! Nice outdoor seating as well!

I really don't understand how this bar has gotten this many good reviews.  The mixed drinks are WEAK so weak I'm concerned they water down their booze.  It's always uncomfortable temp wise.  I don't know where the friendly staff everyone keeps talking about is they must not work on the nights I'm there, but the thing that pushed me over the edge was I was trying to buy tickets to a show and they were supposed to be $20 if you bought them in advance well the website kept trying to charge me $25.  I contacted the bar and the person who got back to me was friendly but not able to resolve the problem so I just don't get the tickets for the price they advertised.  Instead of coming up with a solution so I could get the tickets for the price they were advertised for I was told I would have to pay $25 cash at the door which would have been fine with service charges that's how much I would of had to pay if I bought them in advance my problem is not the money it was them not honoring the advertised priceand not caring that I was getting overcharged $15.  So I'm keeping my $60-$75 for the 3 tickets I was going to buy and the $60 that I would have spent on booze and giving it to a business that  does right by it's customers.

This theater reminds me of the theater I worked at while in high school. It was one of the best jobs I ever had. I can really feel a close knit, caring atmosphere along with workers who care about the customers and the movie experiences. There are so many events and promotions, as well as a great rotation of independent films. I love going there so much!

Who would have thought that printing your own ticket to a show at the cannery would mean a wait outside in the rain for hours. But people and some of my friends who had will call didn't have to wait at all. Something is wrong with this picture. Lesson learned if you go to a show at the cannery go through will call. I guess the employees scanning a printed ticket need some help learning how to use the scanners. What a joke!! BTW the show was great even with the completely asinine employees running the doors.

I love this theater. They are a non profit movie theater offering popular films , as well as low budget and sun dance selections as well. For show times I would suggest getting on their website and map out what movie and when you want to see them. They offer concessions that are less expensive then surrounding movie theaters. This theater has a lot of history and takes you back to the early days of black and white films, minus the black and white part haha. A couple drinks in Hillsboro Village and movie will complete any date night in Nashville.

Nashville is bursting with great BBQ restaurants, such as Martin's and Edley's, but Drifter's shouldn't be mentioned in the same breath. My meal, a plate of dry, under-seasoned pulled chicken, oily hush puppies, goopy cole slaw, and sweet sugary baked beans left me disappointed and feeling ill the rest of the night.

We loved this place.  Good BBQ, good music, great beer selection, cool patio.  We were just passing through Nashville for one night, but if I lived here or nearby this might become my new favorite hangout spot.

What can I say..the Commodore is the first place I came to when I first visited Nashville. The friendly, warm people I met convinced me to drop what I was doing and move here. Literally graduated high school and moved here at 18 after a songwriting camp held at Commodore/Holiday Inn. The food is a little pricey, but it is always DELICIOUS. Last time we all went as a big group and I was playing a show that night. Anyone who ordered a cocktail felt it was very weak, so we all decided to just drink wine or straight liquor. Best place to bring someone to experience good local and acoustic musicians/songwriters. Parking can be validated now which is a pain but there's ample space which I love. Always recommend:)
The place is cold and austere...and the seats are uncomfortable as well as small screens. My 55 inch seems bigger than some of these screens. It pretty much sucks.

this is a great place!!!! we love it!!

http://www.watchonlinevideos.org/dailymotion.php

It is a cute older bar so don't expect fancy modern architecture. Other than that I love the friendly service and the friendly customers. Beer prices are great $4 for craft beers and $2 for Pabs during happy hour from 2 to 5pm. It is cash only. So if you are at the park and need a nice cold beer stop by.
The ribs!!! Got some just out of the smoker..they were amazing. The smoked pork is perfection. Try the Georgia sauce!

This was the worst concert experience I have ever had.  I bought tickets for my brother for his birthday as we are big Chris Stapleton fans.  My brother's girlfriend forgot her ID and the person checking at the door could not have been more rude or disrespectful.  We has various other forms of ID, offered to be X'd and no one in the group drink, we made it clear we had driven several hours to get here for the show.  We could show a photo ID picture through the phone and then had at least 4 other forms of ID to compare it to including a social security card and health insurance card.  I understand rules are rules, but the man working at the door was rude, disrespectful and flat our inappropriate to be a "professional" your organization has employed. I love music and attend several concerts every year and have never had such a horrible experience. If we had to have been denied entry there was a way to go about it with more class and appreciation for your customers. I have attended several events at your venue and will not do so again.  I was stunned that the elderly women in front of me, who clearly had a disability, and did not have an ID as she is unable to drive, was also denied entry.  You should be ashamed of yourself as a business and as a venue.

This place was cool. We were visiting Nashville and heard a band playing on a warm afternoon so we stopped by to see what was going on. We had already eaten, and weren't driven by an alcohol frenzy, so we stopped in for lemonade and an iced tea to watch the band. The waiter was totally cool about it, we didn't feel pressured to order more and it was a nice time. I wish we had been hungry enough to try the food. Seems to be a biker hangout, but at the same time not really. who knows, I enjoyed it....

I came here for lunch on a Wednesday with my boyfriend and ordered eggs Benedict with steak, and wow! The steak was phenomenal, cooked perfectly! I loved every bite, and I am super picky about my steak. So kudos to the chef!! I also had the gator bites and they were so delicious! My boyfriend ordered the shrimp platter and he enjoyed it. Another time that we came, he had a burger and loved it too. Overall, the food here is very good, highly recommend having food here if you come for a game, enjoy their food with your drinks, you won't be disappointed.


Update: 12/31/17

I've come here a couple times, but the most recent time I came was in New Year's Eve. I've got to say, I am so glad I did! They had a huge party here, and my boyfriend and I were able to stay somewhere warm and ring in the new year at a fun atmosphere. (We we're planning to walk around downtown before learning about their NYE party)

We even invited a few people to come join us and we had a blast here.

We had great service for bar drinks. No issues there. But we ordered three different appetizers- food that should take no more than 10 minutes. We gave them about 30 because it was slightly busy. 45 minutes go by, and we start asking questions. No one can tell us anything, people are "going to check on it", still resulting in no food. No one would come and talk to us to tell us what was going on. Nothing. We went up to the bar three different times because it had been over an hour at this point (we were starving). It was shift change, we had already been forced to tab out and pay for our food. The bar back very rudely and loudly said to another bartender "you handle this, I've already talked to this guy." NO ONE WOULD TELL US ANYTHING. We finally just cancelled our food. It was then an act of Congress to get our money refunded. You're a bar serving bar food only at the time we ordered. There's no excuse for food not showing up at the table and for no one having the decency or leadership to step up and let customers know what's going on or make it right. We will never be back.

Went there for lunch - it wasn't busy but the food was good - they even make their own BBQ sauces - the fries were good and hot.  Adam was our server and really went above and beyond on service.  Additionally, met the owner - who was a really nice guy and shared a lot about the city.  I would definately go back to check out some of the live music.

Oh man, this vegan has a big heart-on for Drifters. You may not expect a barbecue joint to be frequented by the vegan crowd, but that tofu sandwich is to die for. Not only that, but there is a full vegetarian section on the menu!

I have mainly had the tofu sandwich but one time got experimental with the vegetarian burrito (that can be vegan). The tofu sandwich is 4 pieces of plain fried tofu on a bun toasted with olive oil and lettuce, tomato, and onion. This may sound plain, but then you slather on the BBQ sauce and stuff your face. They have three BBQ sauces on the tables and then three hot BBQ sauces that you can ask for. I like to put a good layer of the Atomic and then supplement with the Drifter and Texas style. I was told that a couple of the sweeter sauces have honey in them, I make an exception here. 

I also make vegan exceptions for Bloody Mary's on Sundays. They put BBQ sauce in them and put a rim of BBQ rub. OMG , best thing ever. Sundays are 2-4-1 so it is a good day to go get day drunk with double pours.

The beer selection is also pretty good and when it warms up the patio is great with live music in the evenings. 

This is my go-to on the east side. I take people here a lot. I've had first dates here. I've invited out of town guests. I just take anyone who is willing to go with me. It is well worth it.

I am a member of the Belcourt Theatre.  I am so glad to be part of this non-profit organization.  The films shown here are wonderful.  I recently saw I,Tonya and was blown away.  Keep up the good work!

If you're into strange artsy movies, this is the place for you! I'm not and I didn't like the movie or the price. 

This is the place for the non-mainstream movie goers--keep that in mind.

This was my first time at this venue this evening to see a friend play. I was told I could pay my cover charge at the bar. What they failed to tell me was there was an added service fee. Why not just put an atm in the place?

Then to top the entire experience off the female bartender was beyond rude, she was downright insulting. I asked if I could pay my beer and cover charge together and she said no because she needed to validate I was over 21. The bouncer couldn't have shook his head? Or given me back my ID before taking back the receipt? A completely idiotic process. 

The bartender then proceeded to tell the bouncer was happened, hands gestures and all, right in front of me. And then again to another manager/person at the sidebar! 

Don't bother to waste your time here. If your friends are playing a show, tell them to move it to another venue. This is Music City. You don't treat customers that way. There are plenty of better options. As for the bartender, the local may want to reconsider their customer service in the hospitality business.

Behold, the BBQ Brisket Nachos.  So amazingly delicious, you won't be able to stop picking when the plate is almost empty.  Layers and layers of perfectly layered corn tortilla chips with melted cheddar, BBQ sauce and BRISKET.  Must have.

Also had some spicy fried pickles, ribs, and wings that were tasty.. but I'd come just for the nachos.  Service was great and they have awesome happy hour specials!

They also have self service for their sauces.  Of course, I had to try them all.

I was quite happy when we stumbled upon Drifters. Coming from Houston, TX, our bbq standards are set very high, but we happened to stop in Nashville on the way to Lexington. Coming in around 10:30pm at night, the quality food selections were limited for a late night dinner, but Drifters definitely did the trick.

Drifters wasn't crowded at the time because we came in so late, but it definitely had that local, cool vibe of getting crowded whenever they have live music or an event going on. It's a no frills, nothing fancy kind of place, but that's what makes the place feel so homey. There is plenty of indoor and outdoor seating available, and they even have a stage where live music would play, plus a full bar.


As far as food goes, we tried 2 of their 2 meat plates, and their famous bbq nachos. The bbq nachos are huge and plenty to share! They are piled high with bbq brisket, cheese, pico de gallo, avocado, jalapenos, and a dollop of sour cream in the middle. For the 2 meat plates we tried their pulled pork and sausage on 1 plate, and brisket and pork ribs on the other plate. For sides it came with coleslaw, bbq baked beans, and French fries. Out of the 4 different meats, the pork ribs were by far the best! They came out super tender, well seasoned, and smokey. The sausage and brisket, compared to Houston bbq, was just ok, but we were starving. And the pulled pork was really good as well, it came out juicier than I was expecting. Don't sleep on the sides either! The bbq beans were some of my favorite that I've had in awhile, and I don't normally like beans. If you're in Nashville, come check out Drifters! Solid bbq, cool atmosphere, and live music on Wednesdays.

Oh and I almost forgot, try ALL 5 of their homemade bbq sauces. They are each unique, and go perfectly with their bbq. Half of the fun of eating here was trying the different foods with each of the sauces. My personal favorite was the "New Mexico" sauce.

I wish I could give 0 stars. I came with a bachelorette party 14 of us.. a few of us came earlier because we knew we would probably have to wait. We were the first ones in the restaurant. The servers were super friendly and they were quick to serve our mimosas. They took our orders at 11 AM. We were not served food until 1:30PM... well, half of our table got food.. one girl found a hair in her burger, and for two girls they "forgot to put their orders in" and a few we were still waiting on. We called the owner over multiple times, not once did he apologize for the wait or other issues. Once we noticed another table complaining to the owner, we called him over. One girl from our party said this was horrible service, and the owner simply responds, "YOU'RE A HORRIBLE PERSON" and walked away. 

...the servers deserve better than to work for an establishment like Frisky Frogs.

Food was good, wait staff friendly, but............NO MUSIC!  Checked the website first which showed music from 7 to 9pm, then called ahead to confirm the website info.  But even with this, no music the entire time we were there.  Arrived at 7, ordered food, finished, still NO MUSIC.  At 8:30 musicians arrived, set up, then went to the bar to drink.  WHAT?? They were one and a half hours late but STILL NO MUSIC.  We left.  If you're going there to eat, fine, but if you're going to also hear music, beware.  You might be disappointed.

I am only giving it one star based on it being the Nashville Patriots Fan Club Bar. It's a great spot to go and watch the Patriots game, but definitely get there early to grab a seat. 
Now I understand the wait for food as I'm sure everyone showed up and ordered food at the same time, really bogged down the kitchen. I wouldn't have minded waiting the hour and half for food, as the server told us it would be, except when it finally did arrive it was less than mediocre. 
Wings were small, cold and absolutely no flavor. We ordered Nashville Hot, but it should have been more like mild.  Burgers were small, over cooked, served on a large stale bun, cold and slapped together with "toppings", paired with undercooked cold fries. And it wasn't "cheap bar food" as our bill came to $55!! - A dozen wings, 2 Burgers and 2 Bottled Bud Lights! Now I don't mind paying for food, when it's good, but this wasn't and I don't think it matters that it was busy, I was happy to wait, but wait for hot, flavorful and even mediocre food. 
My feedback would be to pair down the menu during the Patriots Games, serve something that is quick, flavorful and filling. You can't offer a large menu (although it was paired down, obviously not enough). I know I should give it the benefit of the doubt and try it again during a slower time, but even then, nothing on the menu looks worth trying.
