We love this theater so much.  It's such a treat to be able to come and view all sorts of cool independent movies in such a lovely little theater.  They have all sorts of mini-film festivals and great midnight movies over the weekend, yet hubby and I have yet to attend a special screening event.  We're not Belcourt members but we're thinking of becoming ones.  Since we now have Movie Pass, we have been spending more time here  and I would really love to make it out to one of the special features.

They'll validate your parking if you're fortunate enough to snag a spot in the very small parking lot, but I'd warn to expect to have to park in one of the nearby lots.  The Belcourt seems to get crazy busy during the evening weekend shows so try to head in a little early. Come and enjoy some of the beer and wine that they have on tap!

Went on a whim with my boyfriend while we were vacationing. We wanted a little break from going out, and came across this while looking for things to do. We were staying at the hostel downtown, and it was only about a 15 minute drive. Very neat theater and left so envious that Milwaukee doesn't have one like it. Glad we chose it over the other standard movie theaters. We saw The Source Family and returned home telling our friends all about it. I would, without question, get a membership if I lived in town. 

The only downside- a girl working at the concession stand. She was visibly impatient as we took a FEW SECONDS to decide what we wanted. We really enjoyed the movie and forgot about her as soon as it started, but we did think back to it later a little annoyed. One of those -I wish I would have said something- moments. The man at the ticket booth was very nice though (: So to the concession women- sorry to inconvenience you at your job.

The sound is one of the worst I have heard. The stage is in the corner of room and the view is of poles!  

I'll never go there again. Even if it is one of my favorite bands.

I would give zero stars if I could. All around horrible in everything. The waitress we had was slammed so not blaming her but management needs to really get a grasp on how to run a restaurant particularly on a Sunday game day. Was absolute chaos at this place and poorly ran operations. Food was cold and drinks were terrible. We had to find our own table and carry it to a spot with chairs. We got there to watch the Titans/Pats game and left after first quarter.  Also the men's bathroom was complete disaster. This place needs a complete overhaul or shut down.  Amazes me how a place like this stays in business. Avoid this place altogether!  This bar needs Jon Taffer (show on tv-Bar Rescue) for some serious help!

Saw a great band here.  The drink selections were really good they have the usual hipster PBR tallboys but when I went they had Sierra Nevada IPAs and Barleywines and the like as well.  Really nice venue I would be happy to come back here again to see another band.  Good stuff!

What an absolutely lovely place! Just make sure you purchase your tickets as soon as possible, get a parking pass and bring it quickly to your car outside, and I mean QUICKLY, because within minutes, cops (lurking somewhere in the dark) will come out and write you a ticket. It happened to us. Belcourt was so nice that they took the ticket and told us "not to worry about it".

Had the sliders the other night.  Pretty good.  I've been in before but didn't eat, however the smell was so captivating I had to go back and try some.  Great place that not everyone knows about, so you can typically find space.

One of the two primary 500-capacity standing room rock clubs in Nashville (the other being Exit/In), Mercy Lounge is a solid music venue.

Situated at 1 Cannery Row, Mercy Lounge is part of a complex of music venues, including the larger Cannery Ballroom and smaller High Watt - together, quite the music hub! In an old cannery factory/warehouse, each room has an industrial feel, with hardwood floors, exposed brick and ventilation, and high ceilings.

At Mercy Lounge, you'll find both local and nationally touring acts. The sound here is generally good, though a number of factors go into that (PA system, band, sound engineer, number of bodies in the room, etc.). The floor plan here is nice, with the stage in the front of the room, bathrooms in the back of the room, the bar and merch table on separate sides of the back half of the room, and a slightly elevated area with bistro tables/stools between the bar and stage. Also available is an uncovered, outdoor deck, where smoking is permitted.

The bar offers a decent selection of fairly priced beer, liquor, and wine, and the bartenders do a good job.

Parking can be tricky, especially on nights with multiple rooms hosting shows. There is a $5 paid parking lot at the venue, but I generally look for free parking on adjacent streets first.

My biggest gripe with Mercy Lounge is the structural columns that, depending on where you stand, can partially obstruct your view of the stage. So keep that in mind when hunkering down for your spot.

If I could give negative stars I would. Arrived for brunch, was told to "seat ourselves" but then was never approached by anyone, and didn't even see any waitresses. Went up to the bar three times to politely ask if anyone was going to come over to us and the bar tender was very rude and agitated. Finally approached by a waitress, she took 10 min to get out first round of "bottomless mimosas" which were mostly orange juice and very small. Finished them quickly and then had to wait a half hour for another round. The rest of our mimosa experience continued on like this. 

Not only were we neglected but every other table as well. Multiple tables got up and left. 

Eventually two people in our party got their food (ice cold), we had no silverware and our waitress did not care. We went up to the bar two different times to get silverware and received to-go plastic forks. 30 min later the rest of our food came out, ice cold and wrong. Sent it back and waited another 45 min, the other two people in our party obviously had finished by then. THIS IS THE WORST RESTAURANT EXPERIENCE EXPERIENCE OF MY LIFE. We did not receive an apology once.

I went to hear a Facebook friend (and others) sing. Everyone was very talented and/or funny. I ordered the Commodore Grille Steak that came with mashed potatoes. Both were delicious. When the waitress came to take my plate, I slapped her hand (or at least pretended to)... as I was hoping for some bread to sop up the gravy -- ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!

I am going back in a couple of days and will order the same. Just hope I get the same waitress!

The very chocolaty dessert was mighty fine, too!

I got a glimpse of a potential buffet around a corner - wonder how that thing is....


Update: I have been back twice to see the same and MORE friends perform -- and order the Commodore Grille Steak every time! Always mighty, might fine! And servers are always sweet and friendly and helpful.

Updated 01/10/14: Had just headed some soup at home as I planned to stay in and get some work done. Around 5:00, my sister called from Nashville and told me my singer/songwriter friends (and another new friend) were performing at the Commodore again... so I ate my soup and jumped in the car. About two hours later, I only ordered a drink and warned the waitress I'd be ordering a "CGS" to go eventually. A few minutes later, she brought out a chicken quesadilla for someone else at our table - I was suddenly hungry and just had to order one; not the frontrunner on my search for "the world's best chicken quesadilla" but sitll, mighty good. Of course, I now have CGS waiting for me in the fridge for lunch tomorrow! 

Good food + good friends + good service = a mighty great time (well worth the four-hour drive!)

Visited here on Friday night around 7pm.  We did not eat so I can not give it 5 Stars.  

Adam was our bartender and he was very friendly and knowledgeable and attentive.   The beer was cold and live band played a good mix of new and old country as well as good Southern rock songs.  

If you want a good place to go to get off of Broadway, this is definitely a good place to go!
We came for brunch on a Saturday and ordered bottomless mimosas and they kept them coming. Chicken and French toast was amazing.

I love Drifters. When we were looking at houses in the area it was the only place around that was non-smoking and we were happy we checked it out.. On our first visit, the waitress suggested the Chimichanga and I am so happy she did. On the menu it lists as pork, but you can have chicken, tofu or Morningstar. My husband loves the ribs and we both love the atmosphere. It is one of my favorite patios since it is so dog friendly. Check it out!
Good sports bar for Patriots fans. Wish they served food though, I walked out really hungry. The customers had food delivered to them during the game. Just really strange to see that

Definitely a dive bar. I liked it. It's kind of in an interesting spot because of its proximity to the Vanderbilt campus, so there is all this new looking, flashy, brightness all around, and then tucked back behind all that you'll find Springwater. 

Live music of all kinds. Front bar, back bar, pool tables and darts. Darts are free to play, but pool is going to cost you (something like $1, or less). When I was there on a Sunday night, the place was pretty empty, but there was some music in the back room. Seemed like a decent place. I didn't try the food. I'm sure I'll be back at some point.

Oh boy, we tried really we did...scared of the reviews and as well we should be...absolutely an unorganized cluster. Maybe 30 customers and 10 staff and the staff could care less...avoid this place, seriously,  spend your money elsewhere. We are collectively in agreement that this establishment should be closed.

Great experience all around. Came here for Sunday Funday with Josh as our bartender. We found out it was his last day training- he was super friendly and on top of our drinks. Mr Frisky drink- so great. Really fun atmosphere and can't wait to come back at night.
Cool little place in a fun area. It's a basic bar but the BBQ is great and staff very friendly. Looks like it would be a lot of fun on the weekends. We very much enjoyed it.

I was just assaulted by some 7 ft tall jerk who works there and am filing a police report right now. 

EDIT: My girlfriend just spoke to the owner who was very apologetic and informed us that security is outsourced through a company called Axis Security. He also ensured us that the individual involved will no longer be welcome at his venues.
Great place to watch a game plenty of tvs and the staff is great. Will come back again.

This is a "no frills" kind o' place...cash only, smoke inside, dog-friendly, open during snow...yep, you read that right: OPEN DURING SNOW. We drove up a day early before Erin's course viewing so we could explore a little bit. We had this planned for at least a month...then Winter Storm Jonas shows up and dumps cold misery all over Nashville. We called around to places within a few miles, hoping we could catch an Uber ride somewhere once we found a spot to take the pups. We were losing hope when Erin called her cousin Jennifer for advice, who then asked her good friend (also an Uber driver) to tell us what only a local would know. Springwater was 1 of 2 sppts he named, but we never even called the other place. I think we stayed for 3-4hrs, just biding our time until nighttime spots would open. Don't think I'll ever forget this day of darts, billiards, drinking and freezing our asses off!

I've always loved this place for Saturday or Sunday brunch. The food is cheap and I have never had bad services. I am sad they are rebranding and changing their menu. I was not too impressed with the new menu

Listen. You buy a movie ticket, likely from the same person you bought a movie ticket from last time, and this person also gives you a parking pass, so you can keep your car in that lot right next to the theatre where you already parked anyway but didn't know if you were gonna pay for it. You can then walk straight into one of its cozy-ass theatres as planned to see that artsy foreign- or independent-movie you can't see at AMCs everywhere--or, GOD, just like, The Favourite, even though all your hippest friends are all, "it's so overrated"--OR you can make one of several pit stops: 1) at the fully accessible restroom, 2) at the fully accessible elevator to the 2nd floor, 3) back at the desk for assistive devices for no extra charge (for anyone hard-of-hearing or visually impaired), or 4) at the bougie concessions stand, where you will find, as promised, more than popcorn. You can stick to your New-Year-New-You Mediterranean Diet as planned and get a hummus or charcuterie plate with the red wine du jour. Or you can spring for a specialty cocktail or craft beer on tap to wash down those Milk Duds. You decide.
Another great film at the Belcourt, plus delicious snacks. Not your typical choices from chain theaters.
Best bar in Nashville!! They have the best nachos i've ever had. i definitely recommend coming here and eating their BBQ, too. They have an amazing staff as well!

I went Sunday night to see a movie and had a phenomenal experience. I love being able to order the cocktail of my choice before finding my seat for the movie (or even getting up mid-way through the movie to snag a some popcorn and an old fashioned). The staff is always friendly and I had a particularly good 1st impression/encounter with two of your staff this past Sunday. I asked them their names at the end of our brief interaction, "Anthony" and "Dillon". Both were friendly, engaging from the moment I first walked in the door, to the moment I left! They treated me like I was one of their friends, and not just a first-time patron. Thank you Anthony and Dillon for all you did to make my experience this last week a special one. I salute you!

We came here because we needed a dog friendly restaurant, and this olace exceeded expectations. Food was delicious and the staff was super friendly. They have a really nice outdoor patio that's perfect for pets. It's overall a very nice atmosphere

That food is pretty amazing. The music is fun and it's hard to stay still. Marie( The bartender) is AAAMMMAZZZIINGG. She surely kept us entertained. There's so many different sauces and they are all really good.

Brisket was good but the fries were not hot and a little overcooked. Service was excellent. Had the pulled pork chili as a started and it was good but the Brunswick stew was not good. 
Had the brisket dinner with 8oz of chopped beef brisket. It was tender, not stringy and had a good flavor even without any sauce. However the side were just so so. I would come back if for nothing else but to have the brisket.

Frisky frogs is straight trash. We got there on a Saturday at 11:45. We ended up leaving at 2pm because our food wasn't even cooked yet. The bartenders had food sitting on the bar and were just sitting there talking when customers had already been there for 2 hours. There were three other tables that had been there for 3 hours and still hadn't gotten served. Frisky Frogs is the biggest waste of time in Nashville. We are visiting for our friends birthday and all we wanted was some breakfast food until we went down to Broadway street for the day. This is my first post on yelp because Sometimes people can overreact but that was the most ridiculous restaurant I've ever been too. Do not waste your time on this place. If I could give this rating negative stars I would. Please don't waste your time. 
Bubs approved.
Sucky service. Asked for a server twice to two different people and they never came. Wouldn't come here ever again.
What a great find in East Nashville local atmosphere ! terrific barbecue and great service  a real gem!

This place does not deserve one star. We waited 3+ hours for food and it never came. The manager cursed us out for patiently waiting for food. Do not eat here. This place does not deserve anyone's business. I have never been more disappointed in an establishment in my life. The owner here should be not operate a restaurant for disrespecting customers like this. 

Attached picture is the owner and he should not operate a restaurant. He cursed everyone out for them to not serve their customers. 

I have never posted on yelp before, and that is how pissed off I am at this situation. Do not come to this restaurant/bar.

My wife and I had dinner recently at Drifters.  It was nothing special.  We were with another couple from Minnesota and were visiting Nashville    Drifters was near our Vrbo and we did not want to drive far for dinner as it was a rainy evening. We were there on a Friday and on street parking was tight but there is a pay to park lot which serves the Five Point neighborhood.  We started by sharing the hush puppies as an appetizer. They were very good but afterwards things went downhill. My wife had the half order of ribs which she shared with me (there was a lot of food there I cannot imagine someone eating a full order !). They were a bit over done but not bad.  I had pulled pork and sausage.  I thought the sausage was fine but the pulled pork was very dry and required lots of bbq sauce.  For sides we had the baked beans, coleslaw, and sauerkraut.  Neither of us finished the sides. Our friends seemed ok with their meals.  One ordered the sliders which were huge.  We all four shared the banana pudding which was really very good.  Service was friendly.  I would not make a special effort to return.

Fun but horrible service- not the staff's fault- poorly managed obviously!  Not enough help- you would think that at a Patriot's bar - on a weekend when the Pats are playing the Titans AND hosting a huge tailgating party for Patriots fans they would have the smarts to have more than 2 bartenders on and a scant amount of servers on‍! ‍

Great local spot. 
Friendly bartenders!  Live music was good and could be heard outside. 

Love the decor and the outside is fantastic! 
They came and lit the fire pit. 

Drinks were evenly poured and they came to check on us as well. 

Two complaints needs to be a smoking area. 
And parking is in a pretty sketchy area.

I've been to The Local a few times in the last few weeks including Tin Pan South.   Nice Friendly Bar with Live Music and a Fantastic patio!   My friends and I enjoyed the patio this past Saturday and we just love the upgrade to outdoor seating area!

We ate here Sunday night. The food was SO GOOD! My husband is a vegetarian who loves BBQ and finding a place that has tofu that is actually decent is difficult, but drifters did it right! Love the dive bar feel to it, even though it wasn't what I was expecting a bbq joint in the south to be like.

Great place to stop in and get a drink with food. I was able to be seated quickly at the bar. Great selection of drinks and beers on draft. The food was amazing, highly recommend the nachos with brisket.

Getting to this venue early to see one of your favorite artists is not a good idea. You'll want to have as little interaction with the power hungry security guards who start yelling orders as soon as you step into the line. I understand their job is to establish and maintain order but the rude vibe they give is totally unnecessary. I was told by other people in line this is normal, so maybe it's just that I don't get out enough. 

The bartenders were polite and made amazing looking and tasting drinks. The sound and lights were great as well and the A/C was pumping so it didn't feel hot despite the large amount of people that were packed inside. I was able to grab a seat upstairs that had a great view.
Great setting for live music. Long long list of stars that have been through on the wall! Better than expected beer selection.

Went with some friends to Frisky Frog's. It's a neat spot. It's a good place to go watch a game with all the tv's that they have.

The service here is pretty bad. It takes a really long time for you to get food and the waitresses don't really check on you. My frog legs were good, but the fries were cold.
The ribs are amazing ( literally fall off the bone) but the brisket tastes like roast beef. They have live music that is really good, and a good ambiance.

I honestly don't understand how they have 4 stars... we were cool with the atmosphere of the restaurant, but when I went to the bathroom I saw the kitchen. FILTHY!! Prep table was open and gross AF! Things that should have been refrigerated weren't.. and the cooks were not wearing gloves to say the LEAST! We just canceled our order and left before getting the food.

Went here on a recommendation of a local as we are from out of state and we where looking for where locals go. Waitress took our and it arrived fast, but the pork ribs where really dry and over cooked. We talked to the waitress and they drought us some fresh one and they where awesome. We don't care for spicy food or sauce and they had 5 sauces to choose from from sweet to spicy. The staff was great and the atmosphere is the type we really enjoy.

Since moving to Middle Tennessee in late 2014, I have probably been to the Belcourt close to 30 times and I've never once had a bad experience.  The staff is friendly, the popcorn is delicious, and most of the time I will leave intellectually stimulated by whatever film I just saw. It's a stark contrast to your typical multiplex experience to say the least. 

But most importantly, as a basically lifelong film fanatic, I can assure that you are going to be surrounded by other audience members who have a true mutual respect for the viewing environment.  Before every film begins, a message comes on the screen that strictly forbids talking or cell phone use of any kind, and that if this rule is violated, a staff member will take care of it if it's brought to their attention.  In my two dozen plus times at The Belcourt, I have never once seen this ruled violated by an audience member.  This is hands down the best theater not only in Nashville, but Middle Tennessee in general, and a true haven for dedicated movie lovers.  I'm extraordinarily anxious to leave Murfreesboro and live in Nashville, so I will have the opportunity to come far more often and join their membership program.  

A couple things of note:  The parking lot is usually full, but you'll probably find street parking on Belcourt Ave, or the next street over on Acklen. 

It's a tired joke of how outrageous concession prices are at any cineplex you go to, but I always make a point of getting a popcorn and soda at the Belcourt, and I encourage you to also make a concession purchase when you visit.  As mentioned before, the popcorn is delicious, but more importantly The Belcourt is offering the Nashville community a truly invaluable product that would be almost non-existent in the area without the theater's presence, which are interesting and diverse films throughout the entire year.  I'm the type that makes Top 10 lists at the end of every year, and almost every entry in my personal list of 2018 was something I saw at The Belcourt.  So remember when you're passing by the stand, you would be supporting a non-profit that continues to make The Belcourt an irreplaceable cultural mecca of the city, as opposed to just filling the wallets of some rich executive with no connection to Nashville.

I absolutely love this theatre, and it would be so hard to fill the void of finding a comparable place if I ever left Middle TN.

Now this is what I call a home away from home! I could eat twenty plates of the bbq brisket nachos and rock out to the kid rock cover bands! They have great two for one draft beer specials that will make any beer girl get out of her snuggie! They also have great vegetarian options for all you hippies.
Awesome spot to check out some local talent. Plenty of seating and nice service. I liked how 4 different musicians shared an hour time slot. On a good night you could see 16 different musicians.

My mom, fiancée, and I saw the Ultimate Garth Brooks Tribute this Saturday. We had a wonderful time. The band was fantastic and the staff was amazing! My mom needs to use a wheelchair because of arthritis in her knee. Eron was very kind and made sure that we were comfortable. They personally escorted us from the elevator to the stage area and made sure my mom had a great view of the performance. Additionally, the staff is extremely responsive via email. My fiancée emailed the venue in advance to make sure that the space was wheelchair accessible. The staff responded immediately. Thank you, Eron, for making our first country music concert and visit to Nashville so memorable.

This place was super laid back. The live music was good and great as background or just to listen too. The musician played for several hours without a break and only stopped to pack up. The BBQ fell off the bone and the side portions were big enough to not feel cheated and small enough to not take away from the best ribs I've had in a while. Lots of locals and the staff was awesome, checking in just enough to meet your needs and not make you feel ignored.

the worst establishment. employees with serious attitude problem. long wait for food and not apologetic about lack of service and no food afterall. avoid unless you want to be treated poorly by douche guys

Beer
Food
Music

Built on top of a spring, what else do you want?

1896 built at the same time as the Parthenon! 
Password no longer required ;)

This bar restaurant had a great atmosphere.   A variety of Tex mex and BBQ along with Vegan options.   The portions were huge and more than generous.    The BBQ was mediocre and did not have very much flavor.   They had a vast selection of BBQ sauce which was helpful for helping out the meat.   Our server was awesome and attentive.    Just wish the BBQ has been better.

I think one star is being generous for this establishment. At first glance this place seems like a good time. They have a nice patio with live music, but that's where the good times stop. It's self seating so my boyfriend and I find a quaint two top that hasn't been cleaned yet so we sit at a 6 top waiting for someone to come clean it. 20 minutes later: no service and still waiting for this table to be bussed. Since we had plenty of time to people watch and to try and figure out who our server was supposed to be,we noticed a lot of chaos and disfunction going on. We see one female waitress who seems to be the only one doing her job, and another male server who took 20 minutes to split this other table's check and had to apologize to them for how long it took. This other two top had to ask for their check 3 times before they got it! After 30 minutes, my boyfriend goes up to the bar and orders some cocktails and asks if we could get service. The bartender promptly made our drinks and said she'd send someone down. FIFTEEN more minutes later we finally have someone come down to take our order. It took another 30 for it to come out. While the jalapeño infused fried pickles were okay, they had less breading then some places so they were on the soggier side. I got the bbq sliders and they were so dry I had to coat them in bbq sauce. We ordered one more round of drinks from our server and then closed out; only to realize that our server just assumed we hadn't already paid for the drinks we got at the bar so he double charged us. My boyfriend got the yuengling 2 beers for the price of one deal as well. So when we asked for the bill to be adjusted we realize he STILL charged us for the beer even though we paid at the bar so we had to go back and ask him to re-adjust it. AGAIN. With all the choices of food, live music and great atmosphere; this place needs to step up their service and food. We don't tend to spend more than an hour and fifteen minutes at restaurants and we were there for over 2 hours. Oh and that two top we wanted to sit at? Sat dirty the entire time.

Oh they have really changed the look of this wonderful Theater 
Looks completely renovated and their prices are lower than most others and I really enjoyed the movie with natilie portman 
Playing John Kennedy wife ..a great place to check out

Thanks for fixing the issue! Appreciate it.


The music and beer selection here are good. We went in on a Friday night. It was pretty quiet, not a huge crowd. The reason for our original 2 star review is upon checking our credit card statement we found the bartender gave himself a higher tip than the one we gave him for two beers. It's pretty shady to change the tip amount on the receipt. I don't know that we will be back. But if you go, pay in cash.

The place keeps getting better.. I don't think you could draw up a more perfect venue for quality original music, cheap drinks, good food and great atmosphere... the Owner and staff are friendly and approachable.

Marie is the best. Truly the best. Worth the 30 hour drive to hangout with her and have a drink at drifters! Make sure to get a cold yuengling and a good order of hush puppies. No better a place to escape from the Tennessee sun! This is the spot.

Saw the Airborne Toxic Event here and the venue was awesome. I showed up an hour early and stood 2 feet from the center stage, so its kind of hard not to love a place for that. This venue is really small compared to other places I have been, so you'll have a great view no matter where you are I feel.

Definitely coming back here next time a great band like TATE shows up.

I hate to give this place a bad review because I love the artists that it books but everyone that works here seems to be in a bad mood and self-righteous. It's a shame to see a music venue with employees like that-

What a fun place... great vibe... friendly staff... tender ribs and brisket... no sauce needed! sides were outstanding, especially the hush puppies, slaw and beans... good drink specials. Leinenkugel Summer Shandy on tap was a bonus! definitely recommend!

Traveling through Nashville with only 2 days to visit, we wanted to go to the best BBQ joint in town. Drifters had 4.4 star average, with a few other places being 4.5-4.7 stars but it was on our way back to the campground after a late trip to Jack Daniels Distillery and was open till 1am so we decided to try it. I am very glad we did! The atmosphere was as laid back as you'd want to see, we ate outside, where there was a band playing at a decent level so we could still have a conversation. It truly felt like we were at a neighbors back yard bbq. We ordered a couple of beers, bbq nachos and a sampler plate. I am not a big fan of sausage but the smoked sausage on this plate was amazing! The bbq nachos with the brisket were by far the show stopper though! Please do not waste tummy space on the fries and sides! We did end up trying a few of those other higher star places but was disappointed by them after eating at Drifters. If you're passing through or in the vicinity and have not been there, go and order the nachos with the brisket, I promise you will not be disappointed!
This is one of my favorite restaurants to go to in Nashville. Especially if you like a nice day out with some BBQ, this is the place to go!
Great food. Good deals, two for ones most days. Also have a great outdoor space with ping pong and corn hole. A lot of fun!
This place took so long to deliver any service what so ever AND when we finally did get our food it was cold. Never again.

Bartender was too busy to be bothered on his computer. Seemed super annoyed. I get it -- we aren't locals at the dive bar, but it's your job. Gave him $20 for $13 tab and never brought us change. Super rude and acted like he had better things to do. Place is a dive bar, which I love, but the smell of natural gas is overwhelming. Save your time and your money and go to Villager Tavern or Santa's.
Love the atmosphere here! Small dive bar vibes and their patio was perfect! We brought our dogs and they were just as welcomed as we were! Great spot.

This is a very nice intimate venue for concerts. The  sound system is great and the old building has a lot of charm. The wine was not very good and cost $7.00 but I think that is to be expected. There are 5 or 6 cafe tables with stools but otherwise a stand up venue. All and all, it was a great experience. The band I have seen several times in other venues , but they sounded the best I have heard here. I think it is due to the acoustics.

We were here for a recent wedding and the staff and wedding was absolutely wonderful. The staff was kind, courteous, attentive, and all around wonderful. They had the bride and groom in mind while also keeping track of every other guest in the whole building. I would wholeheartedly recommend this venue for any wedding or similar gathering as the staff will exceed your expectations.


Thank them and good night!

This is a dive bar, first and foremost. Having said that, the barbecue is great!  Tried the BBQ sampler, but switched out the fries for the hush puppies and the black beans for the standard baked beans. The ribs are dry-rubbed and were very good. The service was fast and friendly. Highly recommended!

The music and beer selection here are good. We went in on a Friday night. It was pretty quiet, not a huge crowd. The reason for our low review is upon checking our credit card statement we found the bartender gave himself a higher tip than the one we gave him for two beers. It's pretty shady to change the tip amount on the receipt. I don't know that we will be back. But if you go, pay in cash!

Learned about this restaurant in 5 points (Woodland St) on Yelp.  They appear to serve later than several other restaurants in the area.  The 1st thing that I noticed was the large outdoor patio - we sat outside as it was a nice evening.  We mainly went to have a couple cocktails, but we also sampled the side salad, fries, and brunswick soup.  All of the food was appetizing!  Our cocktails were also well done.  Our server was pleasant and it didn't take too long to get our orders.  Nice spot to grab a drink in 5 points.  Gotta sample the BBQ on my next visit.
What a treat.   Gritty, pool, darts, loud music, $2 PBR.   Stop in, mingle, have a cold one.

I've been coming here since it opened.  It is a perfect neighborhood bar/bbq place...although tourists do pop in frequently.  It's nothing fancy, but the beer and banter is always good.  The bbq nachos and ribs are the best things on the menu--play around with the different bbq sauces.

1. Best French fries in not only
Nashville, but the world. 2. Gina is the best bartender I've ever had. She gave us some secret ingredients we asked for and even squirted my mustard for me. 5 star service for sure. Come see Gina on Monday's and Tuesday's!
Bad service, the bartender was rude, ordered food came to us cold.  Not friendly won't be going back.
Nashville's best theatre with an array of indie options. At times, Vanderbilt professors lead film discussions. Plus, this theatre is non-profit.
Going to see Declan McKenna tonight. I have two spare tickets for attendee. Not for sale. LGBT friendly. General admission. I'll finish review after I see the show.

I went for a late dinner at 9:30 pm on a Tuesday night after checking into the Holiday Inn. I was alone, for a business trip and did not want to wander out for food. 

The grill was a pleasant surprise with a great vegetarian pesto penne. The grilled ciabatta was really good. 

There was a group of college students jamming at the mike. Though good, they were really loud and I was tired so asked the waitress to get my food to go. She was very obliging. As she got the food, the jam session ended. There was a very good and very unexpected solo piano encore by a visually impaired college student. He was so good that I sat down till he was done. The MC was very encouraging as he should be with such talent in house. 

So four stars for good food, reasonable price for quality and quantity of food, good service and for encouragement of young local talent.

My waiter was Blake.
Wait to order time 3.35 min
15.06 for food to be delivered
Blake got a little lost in where I was.
Food was cooked and taste was just the usual.  The house bbq sauce was okay.  It tasted like a bottle bbq sauce.  The baked beans tasted like they came from a can.  The coleslaw was okay, a little bland for me.  The portion size not much for the bang.  Got the pick two combo.  Prices as advertised on web site.  Live music not happening.  On web site said that live music does not play during Fall and Winter.  Even though the web site said that there was live music.  However no music was playing at the time I was there.  I even stayed when there was suppose to be a new group but even though they were set up already no music.  There was NFL on the tv.  This is definitely a casual tee-shirt and jeans spot.  I had okay music on the inside but not too much to talk about.  All in all it's just okay.
Side note: Be careful with your cell phone the waitresses will look at what you are doing.

Here tonight for a gig recommend by my daughter. Hanging by the bar. Just had to mention how awesome Casper was tonight. He saw me leaning against the bar and made a point to introduce himself, shake my hand and said he'd take care of me. And boy did he. My next drink arrived before I knew I wanted one. Anyway, thanks Casper for making my night out with my daughter so much easier.

We attended a show there last night for the first time. My husband is a disabled veteran who walks with a cane and has a service dog so events like this are hard one him.
The security staff were amazing. We were treated like they were watching out for a family member. We entered first, didn't wait in line, they brought him a chair until the doors opened. They provided us stools, told me where each guy was going to be in case we needed anything. Security checked on him throughout the night. We even were walked out of venue safely, behind the crowd. 
I can not say enough about how caring security was. We will be back!

Too bad I can't give Drifter's zero stars. It was THAT bad. My husband got the kielbasa hot dog bun sandwiches w sauerkraut. He wigged out when he tried the sauerkraut. Who makes 'bad' sauerkraut? It's already fermented, but we all know what regular kraut tastes like. This didn't. It was just plain weird and icky tasting.
     I follow a keto way of eating and find there's usually something on any menu I can order. So, I went w the large dinner salad with added brisket for $12.79. The salad was a big bowl full of bland iceberg lettuce, about eight super tiny squares of chopped tomato, and maybe 10 thread-bare pieces of shredded cheddar cheese. The brisket was beyond horrible. It was cold, greasy, and mostly in hard chunks. I was fairly hungry, so I tried to make the best of it. I tossed everything w my balsamic vinaigrette and ate it all. Within two hours after returning home I became violently ill. I vomited all night and the next morning until 10:00. I thought my organs were going to come out. I was also sick on the other end.
     I didn't notify the restaurant because first, I figured they simply didn't care about the quality and taste of their food, and second, I thought if they didn't care, why would they care if one of their unimportant customers got as sick as a dog from eating their slop.
     Seriously, don't eat at Drifter's BBQ in Nashville on Woodland.

Mercey lounge is a venue in the Cannery with several event areas. We saw a 90s grunge cover band there. The spot is easy to get to though the parking is a bit tricky. It is a fairly clean establishment and the customer service is pretty good.

The best wings in Nashville without a doubt - a great selection of bbq/hot sauces - amazing burgers, too!  The staff is fantastic (especially Sarah!); also, a dog friendly patio!  Usually the live music is decent, as well.....highly recommended!

Very cool spot with a heavy focus on music. Pros: clean, great stage and sound system, neat decor. 
Cons: not incredibly inviting staff, hard to get a drink, very expensive beer.

This bar is one of the oldest bars in Nashville and has been open since 1897.  It has such a feel of quaintness and old time goodness.  The band hadn't started playing but the venue is small and I think would have given you the feel of a personal concert since the tables were less than 2 ft from the stage. They only serve beer and soft drinks, but it is a local hangout if you are looking for something other than the nightmare of Broadway.

I've been to several shows at the Cannery, and I've always thought the house sound was unnecessarily loud. I bring earplugs to rock shows, but last night I saw The Wind and the Wave - basically mildly amped acoustic. The volume level was insane! My ears are still ringing. Butch Walker played a great set after, but I went around the corner and listened through layers of brick to enjoy it.

This isn't Spinal Tap. No need to put everything on 11. I've been watching live shows since 1970, and there's absolutely nothing gained by setting the sound board on stun!

Amazing venue!
I've only visited for the Rifftrax Live events, and they have always been impressive.  Great service and presentation.  The staff seems genuinely happy to host the event.

Great place for unique events.

(Frequent traveller from out of town)

This was my first concert experience in music city and I'm hoping this place isn't representative of what Nashville has to offer. The most important things to know are that parking is actually $10 cash and you should dress light because there is essentially no air flow in what in all honesty is just an old warehouse. Security was efficient, but not too friendly. I was treated like my out of state ID was fake which felt silly and unnecessary. Bartenders were similar. Canned tallboys are $5-7. Yuengling was cheaper than Budweiser, which was uncanny but convenient. Doors said they'd open at 8, actually opened around 8:45. Show started right on time. Sound was good, but not great. Floor isn't inclined so it's not easy to see the band because the place holds like 1,000 people. Leaving the parking lot wasn't too terrible for a sold out show. I wouldn't go back unless I really, really liked the band. It was just too humid and claustrophobic and felt like way too many people for what I'm pretty sure was the second floor of a very old building.

There is always something worth going to watch at the Belcourt. I've been coming here since I was an annoying teenager, before I could appreciate its awesomeness or partake in their adult beverages. The old theatre atmosphere is so warm and fun that it's even worth going to see a bad movie here. You'll still leave happy with the whole experience. And they do in fact play some terrible movies on occasion, because some cult classics are so awful that they just have to been seen (The Room, for one). 

As I mentioned, they serve beer and wine, which is a treat. And I always get the impression that the folks who work here truly enjoy their jobs. Everybody wins.

Stopped in for an early dinner on my way through Nashville. I sat on the patio with my dog and ordered the sampler plate. It included 3 oz of brisket, 3 oz pulled chicken, smoked sausage, 1/3 rack of ribs and 2 sides. The ribs fell off the bone and the sausage was fantastic. I wasn't too impressed with the chicken, but the smoky brisket, perfectly crispy tater tots and tasty slaw made up for it. And they offered 5 varieties of sauces with varying heat and sweetness. Waitstaff was excellent, took great care of my pup and included wet wipes and plasticware with my to-go box. Don't let the dive-bar feel throw you. This place is legit and definitely worth checking out.

Fun bar with trivia on Monday nights and friendly bartenders. The bartender helped me save a drunk fly by putting it outside - how nice is that? 

Wasn't particularly impressed with the BBQ though, a bit dry. I liked that their menu had options for vegetarians as well.

I have a love-hate affair with Cannery.  The bands they book here are incredible.  I've seen Mat Kearney, Grace Potter and the Nocturnals, Alt-J, Punch Brothers...you name it...I've honestly lost track of how many times I have been here.  So why don't I LOOOOVE it you ask?  Its the layout.  It's that simple.  There are currently three different venues within the Cannery Row complex, with the Ballroom being the biggest.  The stage is far back within the open space.  The bar runs along the far wall.  But the problem is that unless you are right in front of the stage you are pretty much guaranteed to be off to the right, in some cases they very far right, and good luck seeing anything whatsoever from that angle.  The sound as a result of the odd positioning isn't always on point either.  Even with the massive bar it can take a long time to get a beverage.  But yet the acts are so fantastic.  They really are.  I grumble every time I see someone I love playing here, but I go anyways and hope I can get close enough to actually see them.  The space can also be rented for private parties and weddings, and for those sorts of things it works really really well.  I enjoy special non-concert events here very much.  But just be aware that you might be visually impaired at any show unless you get the coveted spots directly before the stage.

We love this place, great place to stop for a cold draft beer and great bbq. 

Menu is not your typical southern bbq joint but everything we have tried has impressed us. The bbq nachos are amazing and the smoked bratwurst will leave you craving them over and over. The hot German style mustard served with the brats is awesome. 

Very friendly people and sitting in the deck listening to live music can't be beat. We have become regulars on weekends. Sunday's offer happy hour all day. 

Prices are very reasonable and the quantity of food on the menu is very plentiful.

They have redone the lobby and now it feels like a shot fun style entrance. They repositioned the doors so that they face the parking lot and that is nice. The new bathrooms are a huge improvement as well.
However, they have not replaced to original seats. The first three I sat in were broken. They do not compare to a new theater in terms of comfort. The result is that you get some of the old and some of the new. We will see more movies here in the future.

As far as East Nashville BBQ joints go, this  one is the best. Their smoked chicken quesadillas are phenomenal. (I've eaten them twice this week... Don't judge me.) When you add great drink specials and a low key outdoor patio (that's pup friendly) to the fantastic BBQ, it is easily one of my favorite places to eat out in East Nashville.

Great spot here in Nashville!  Great band, Nirvana! Yes!  However, the bartenders are a bit lost.  My greygoose burns when I drink it.  I drink greygoose regularly, so I know it well.  I asked the bartender who said it was greygoose.  I doubt it.  Last drink here.  Again, the bartenders are a bit spacey! The one female bartender is too busy biting her nails in the corner to come help us.  There's 4 bartenders on duty but none are interested in checking on customers.  I bet they'll be interested when the check comes and their tip.

The band, the fried catfish and jambalaya are great.
The bar was really nasty and the wait staff was pretty salty. The venue is great for a small band

Mercy Lounge, it has been twice now that you have provided an awesome drinking experience. Whiskey fueled dancing, furious drinking, laughing and tom foolery. 

This place is a host to an excellent music venue. The crowd both times was, fun, enthusiastic, non-violent, and raging or maybe that was just us.. bonus.

The new years eve event was fucking awesome. Sweet ass 90's cover band destroyed the venue. And as I am attempting to recall the night through a whiskey tinted memories. One thing is for sure.. We had a blast.. and will return.

Jamie is the best!! She is so friendly and welcoming and pours a great drink. Pretzel bites were so good we ordered a second basket. Our welcome to Nashville has been the best, we will be back! Thank you Jamie for getting our trip off to an awesome start!

Super cozy spot with awesome food. Had the homemade massive corn dogs that are spot on. Thick layer of hush puppy batter. Best tater tots I've ever had on the side. Chips and queso on point to start. Homemade sauce bar all with a different tastes and temperatures. Tried some of my friends brisket and the Mac and cheese as well without disappointed. 2 massive corn dogs with a Mountain of tater tots for I believe under $8! Definitely would go back and definitely recommend!
Met a friend here for pint and pie night. Ordered the meatloaf - yum! The music was great. I really liked how cozy this spot was and will probably return.

One of my favorite venues in nashville. I've seen some of my favorite bands here and have never been disappointed. The venue is big enough to fit a large number of people but still small enough to be an intimate show. The only problem we had was that we had gotten one pbr from the bar and our tab was $14. Which is a little sketchy. But oh well.
What a fun bar! Plenty of seating, nice and spacious, lots of TV's, and it was nice to see that they attract so many people of differing ethnicities! I'll definitely go back :)
Great late night food. BBQ nachos are my favorite. It is open until 2 am I think. They do stop serving food at some point.

I will first say that I was brunching with a large group, however, we waited over TWO AND A HALF HOURS for our food. Four people in our group never never ended up getting their food (two order were not even put in), and one plate had a hair in the food. ON TOP OF THAT, one person of my group told the owner about our horrible service. The owner responded by calling the member of my group a horrible person. What type of OWNER does that?! This is such a poorly run establishment. I will never return, and I would never recommend this place.

So after moving to Nashville I was introduced to The Family Wash.  It was one of my favorite places as I enjoyed the food, beer, and live music.  Unfortunately after returning from a long business trip I returned to a changed establishment.  One of my favorite items on the menu was the Meatloaf Sandwich.  My friend and I ordered the same thing and it looked as if they took one portion and put it into a blender, then making the sandwiches with this monstrosity.  It just isn't worth the wait any longer.  Go to Mitchell's Deli for good beer and robust meatloaf sandwiches.
You so cute and cultured Belcourt.  So Indy and hip.  I love your full bar, thank you.  Oh and your parking lot. Thank you for that too.

There BBQ is amazing and I LOVE GOING HERE. but... Recently had one of the waitresses steel a  pair of my sunglasses then lie to my face after  the next time... Only a week in-between I called the day after I forgot them there. Yes my fault. But when I called "'they didn't have them " but she stole them. After me calling and saying they didn't them.  I show up today. Full on front lie to my face about they were a roommates, when I could give a reason and " show " that they were mine. Just not cool.

My wife thinks that the two stars are generous. Bad experience for us. Went to see The Devil Makes Three last night.  Waited in line for half an hour or more and opening band was playing when we got in.  The room was crammed full, hot and there are no seats.  Maybe I'm too old for a venue like this but I wanted to NOT stand up in a tightly packed crowd that makes you feel like  you are the one being canned, while strangers push past spilling their drinks while trying to dance.  We stayed for about 20 minutes before we left.   Didn't even see the Band I came for and it was just a big disappointment.
Great venue and music, but can someone address the announcer tonight. She was wasted and couldn't say the name of the bands right. Not cool...

Very simple yet awesome venue. There's been a ton of shows I've wanted to see here and not been able to make. I saw William Elliot Whitmore on 4/8 and had an amazing time. Staff was friendly and attentive, even when we were unaware it is cash only (should have thought ahead!). The show itself was wonderful and the crowd wasn't horrible. I will definitely be back to see a show here!

I rarely review restaurants or bars I've only been to once.  If the food and service is bad, I just chalk it up to experience.  Taste is such a subjective affair...but for this restaurant, I am going to make an exception.
The Family Wash is a hipster venue that lacks in both substance and style.  It was on our list of top things to do and see in Nashville...and it blew!  Big time.  We arrived at 7:00 p.m. hoping to grab a meal and see some live music.  But as soon as we arrived, the hostess said we could eat there, but we had to leave by 8:00 pm (when the music was scheduled to begin) because they were booked.  What restaurant on earth tells a paying customer that they are on the clock?  Extremely rude.  But it gets worse.  As the "witching hour" approached, the hostess and our waitress made a point of striking up a conversation next to our table talking about how "they were warned.  I hope they finish up and leave soon."  I was tempted to drag things out to see if they would really toss us, but by this time, I really WANTED to leave.  Never to return.
The food was mediocre at best, the service (when not plotting to bounce us) was good.  All in all, a cramped, uncomfortable evening.  Maybe you will have better luck, but I won't ever be back!

This place does not deserve one star.  As someone who works in the restaurant Business I understand how busy and crazy things can get but this was unacceptable treatment of PAYING customers.  We ordered our food before most other tables in the resultant, and after saying something the manager came over and apologized saying they were short staffed so we brushed it off.  But then ONE HOUR later we were still not served.  Finally, after two and a half hours of waiting half of our party received their food which most of it was cold.  Then after they were all done eating the other half was served their food except four people at our table, whose orders were not put in at all.  After insisting we speak to the manager he ignored us, and then called us horrible customers.  We were just asking to be treated as paying customers.  If this place truly wants to reinvent their terrible reputation then they need to replace their manager and hire more staff.  I will NEVER recommend this place.

There are very few things that frustrate me in life. Vegetarians are up there on that list. 

I was headed down to Nashville for a girls weekend early this fall & had a vegetarian in the group. As a self-proclaimed food aficionado I am pretty big on keeping people happy when it comes to dining options - and I spent hours looking for vegetarian friendly spots in Nashville leading up to our trip. God, what a difficult task in Nashville! Most places that I came across had one or two items that catered to vegetarians, but for the most parts the menus were sparse. ...and a person can only eat so many veggie burgers in the course of a long weekend.

Luckily for me (and the vegetarian in the group) I stumbled upon Drifters. The menu had plenty to offer in terms of Tennessee-style BBQ & it had an extensive vegetarian section. 

We got there right when they opened, so we had no problem finding prime real estate outside on the back deck. Our waitress was friendly & knowledgable, especially when it came to the beer selection. I was happy that they had so many local beers on tap.

We started with an order of the hot fried pickles to share and they were certainly delicious. I did a BBQ combo that I wasn't in love with, but it did keep me full for the rest of the day. A couple of others in the group opted for the chicken tenders which they gobbled up. 

For whatever reason though my vegetarian friend opted for veggie burger -  A VEGGIE BURGER. 

Vegetarians... they kill me.

This place is tucked into a side street unknown to google maps. We only came here once but they have a really chill atmosphere, friendly waitstaff and bartenders.  We were there on a Tuesday and there was a really good band there.  I had BBQ brisquet nachos and they were great.  My husband highly recommends the ribs.  I expect this place is a good place for an after work drink as well as dinner with the family.  We saw all kinds while we were there.  The food was good but the atmosphere made for a good bar/ dinner hangout as well.

I came to The Commodore to play a round (May 7,2015). I was not expecting what happened! This well-trained wait staff was awesome! Our food was not only delicious (everyone agreed, and there must have been 20 of us!) but even plated like a high end restaurant! The prices were reasonable. Staff is excellent and friendly. And the entertainment is great, too! (Nod to Debi Champion!)
I will be back! Thank you!

Best bar in Nashville.
Some would call it a dive.
It's smokey.
You don't want to use the bathrooms if you don't have to.
The staff is awesome.
This is where the real bands of Nashville play.
You might get knifed in the parking lot.
They have an outdoor patio.

I'm really surprised that it has taken me this long to review one of my neighborhood favorites, The Family Wash. The Wash has been one of my favorites since I moved to the east side 3 or so years ago. This little place has great food, great beer and a nice rotating selection of local musical talent. Plus, every December they have a jazz group perform A Charlie Brown Christmas, which might be one of my favorite things ever. They get double points for that. 

The Wash is fairly small with limited table and bar seating. I recently found out that they take reservations, which I highly encourage. The inside is a mish-mosh of thrift store finds, vinyl, Formica and twinkle lights. It feels more like you are hanging out in your friend's basement than at a dining establishment, which is a good thing.

The Family Wash has one of the absolute best deals in town: the $10 Pint and Pie night. Every Tuesday you can get one of their signature Shepherd's Pies along with a pint of beer. Since I'm rather frugal, I usually go to the Wash on Tuesdays. And the majority of the time they have a wonderful beer selection consisting of local favorites and solid craft breweries. 

My favorite way to order a pie is the traditional meat pie with added garlic. They take roasted garlic, mash it up and put it in between the potatoes and the cheese. It's PURE heaven. The portion is really big and I always tell myself I'm only going to eat half and save the rest for later. But I'm delusional and most of the time I eat the entire thing. It's hard to have will power when something is just that good.
Dive is an understatement. Walked in with friends, walked right out. Still stink of cigarettes.

Oh, Nashville, what we would without the Belcourt? Well, now we know, because it seemed like they were closed FOREVER for renovations. But it's open now - and I'm so glad. 

The Belcourt is, quite simply, THE place for indie, foreign, and classic films. And now it's ever snazzier than before. Wine, beer, and concession goods. Snazzy theaters. The best films. You might even run into a celebrity or two! 

The cons? The upstairs theater is TINY - and the seats are totally flat. Good luck seeing anything in that theater. And the parking lot is SMALL (they give you parking pass to put on the dash of the car when you buy your ticket), and street parking in Hillsboro Village SUCKS.

I love you, Belcourt. I'll be seeing you a couple times a month for all time.

The food is good and it's a great place to see live music. The stars would be more if I didn't feel like the staff wasn't so pretentious. Typical hipsters who tend to look at you from down their noses. Still, I love the neighborhood vibe and like taking out of towners there for a surpise gem of a joint right in the middle of a residential street

Drifters is a cool little dive bar. We ended up here after wandering around Nashville and realizing that all the bbq places we wanted to go to were already closed. The staff was friendly although the service wasn't particularly fast. I had the brisket dinner and my overall impression was that everything was ok. The brisket was tender,though not particularly memorable flavor wise. The cole slaw was take it or leave it for me. I'd make a return trip probably just to enjoy the atmosphere of the bar or watch a game rather than go for the food.

DO NOT GO HERE. This place is terrible. I am a waitress and never complain about anything. Food came out and we had no silverware. How can you eat French toast with hands? Went to the bar to ask for some and they couldn't find any. Waited 15 mins for a fork and food was cold when I finally got one. Poor waitress was new and had 10 tables. Didn't get my money's worth for bottomless mimosas. THIS PLACE IS A JOKE.

Great, local, inexpensive, good beer selection great BBQ, and veggie/vegan options. 

Friendly staff

Lot of extra spicy sauces

Good music 

Quick service 

Nice and air conditioned ! 

Would definitely recommend

I miss the old theater! I mean, the new renovation is nice, but it lacks the character and charm of its previous incarnation.

They're still doing a great job, though. 

I first came here in the early 2000s and saw Life of Brian. And now I'm looking forward to seeing Tom Waits' BIG TIME on the big screen.

Great place for artsy movies. You won't find any mainstream movies here! I'd recommend seeing a movie during the week or daytime if possible. It's close to Vanderbilt and in a busy area. Parking is extremely limited. Staff were friendly and helpful. It's somewhere that I would go back to, but only for a matinee during the week.

This bar is one of my favorite bars, ever! Great service, awesome prices, delicious food. The bartenders were eager to help you with your order. Security even held the door for anyone walking in or out. I will definitely be going back!
Saw an artist named matt Sperrazza past Thursday.   He was one of the best acts I've ever seen.  Def coming back.

Waited over 45 minutes for lunch.  We had one member of our party order their 9 wing meal and 40 minutes into our weight they came out to tell us they actually had 6 wings.  This was at 1 pm on a Saturday.  Will never return and suggest you think twice before coming here.  Below is a picture of the grilled chicken tenders.  Never seen such a sad pathetic plate.

Would've given 1 star, but 2 stars because they have bottomless mimosas, bloody Mary's, and service was good. Honestly, the hash browns were just a sorry excuse for French fries. They were totally tasteless and unseasoned. The "cream cheese grits" were actually grits mixed with cheddar cheese, bacon, and peppers from what we could taste. Overall, not a fan. Not coming back
Great neighborhood pub. Bartender Tyler took great care of use. Cocktails had a great mix. Appetizers were good. New place with nice decor. Definitely will be back.
Awesome outdoor area, fun to meet up with friends, bring your dog on a nice day

We picked this place on a whim because we wanted to replace the bad taste of our last rib experience elsewhere. Our bar tenders Kellen and Matthew were attentive, friendly and made great suggestions for both food and drinks. The ribs, fried pickles, hush puppies and pulled pork chimichanga were outstanding. We had a great time and we'll definitely be back.

Trying to find a meal to appease both a vegan and a person that will eat any animal walking is always a tough challenge.  Look for further, Drifters is the place to be!  I didn't expect any greatness considering it's a BBQ joint and they had a tofu sandwich as an option.  Boy, was I wrong!  First off, being able to eat fried pickles that do not have milk or eggs is a real treat for me and I am glad these were the ones I was able to eat.  They were so damn good!!!!  The tofu sandwich had that same nice, thick and flavorful breading on it making it a super amazing sandwich.   I was super impressed with them and hope to return there again if my travels ever take me back to Nashville.
Great food.....great service.  Very friendly atmosphere.  Marie behind the bar is the best!!!!

This place has been the go-to songwriter hangout for over a decade, stop in and you'll know why. Easily dismissed as a Holiday Inn restaurant, the Commodore Grille is so much more. Great food reasonably priced, wonderful staff with little turnover so you know they are treated well. Great to get to know them whether you are an out of town guest or a regular like me. Tom is hands down my favorite bartender in Nashville, always remembers my drink. And the music...I play here often and it is one of my favorite rooms. Great sound system masterfully handled by the legendary writers night host, Debi Champion. Whether I am going there to play, to listen, or just to hang and have a couple of drinks, this is the place.

Love this bar. Great draft beer selection with fairly consistent rotation of certain handles. Attentive bartenders. Only tried one sandwich (All Nighter I think it was called), but it was great.

Live music most nights which can be a little overbearing. Outdoor patio seems like it will be great in warm weather.

I would actually give this place 5 stars for the shepherd pies because they are awesome.  I'm giving this poor review solely based on the service, which always sucks.  Every time I've been here (I'm done BTW) everyone from the hostess, the wait staff and even the manager have been snotty and rude.  I keep going back for the food and hoping things have changed or gotten better, and this last trip will be my last.
Great food. Awful service. Sat for over two hours waiting on our food order. Waitress checked in with us three times during our lunch. Food came out cold. First bad experience here out of 10.

went there on a sunday after a flag football game with our team. we normally go to beyond the edge but decided to try drifters. it was great. the waitress was awesome and patient since there was many of us and we were still pumped up after the exercise so it was hard to get us to pay attention. 

we ordered food which was came quickly and was good. the beer was all on happy hour. good service and plenty of seats. also way less smoky than the neighboring bte. only thing that i didn't like was the band. it was kind of loud once they started playing but that was really our problem not theirs. on any other night it would have been welcomed. 

if you are in east nashville, try this place out!

I consider myself a serious foodie, so I was surprised to find that this place was just awesome. Cool vibe, easygoing, service was super friendly and attentive yet not clingy. Ribs and smoked wings were excellent! Maybe a little too smoked, but still juicy with an awesome caramelly thick crust. Ooh, the hickory flavor! So good! Sauce choices were varied and spectacular- perfect since I'm not a big fan of sweet sauces. Sauerkraut and cold slaw were excellent. The music was great, too.

An excellent venue for music and other cool events for all the hip artists of Nashville! Good looking people and great sound systems they have in place. Makes the band experience exactly what it should be.

The small Parkin lot gets full fast. Don't pay for the other lot, parallel park on the well lit Palmer PL which is one street over & save a few $

Parking was very close to the building and only 5$. Security was fine. They did their job. They offer canned beer inside. Bathrooms are clean. I like not having seats, yet I think I'm getting to old not to have seats, if that makes sense. My feet started hurting towards the end. It also became very apparent to me that all those times I pretended to be looking for someone at the front....no one fell for it. Being 5'1", that got old real quick last night. I recommend locking arms with your party and ignore them and their excuses about why they need to cut in front of you. But the group that did it to us got kicked out for lighting up. Just because someone sings about weed, doesn't mean you can light it up right in front of security, dumb@$$es. So, seeing karma served on a plate right in front of you is always fun.
All in all, great experience. Pretty venue inside!

Live music was good service was trash drinks were just as bad. Don't know if it has to do with being the only Spanish and black person in the restaurant but our service looked at us for a good 20min before come over asking us if we were good and walked away before we could answer. Then when she comes back to take our order finally she starts taking the order of the table next to us at the same time pretty much ignoring us. Folks who sat down 20mins after us get their drink while we wait. When drink finally come they taste horrible and she brings the wrong beer. That one star is for the singers they were great. The server was Cindi and we was also extremely rude

Went to this place based on reviews. Some what of a slow night, with practically everyone on the porch for the live music. Still not very busy. Service was the worst. Server even said at one point, "is there anything else I can get you at one time because I'm running back and forth a lot". Ummmmm it's your job. Food was mediocre at best. Would not recommend. 2 stars only because the baked beans were awesome.
A delightful dive bar. Complete with mildly aggressive bouncer, poorly felted pool table and awkward punk band playing in the back. I'd return at some point.

This bar.. oh this bar. It has so much potential; the patio is BEAUTIFUL. The inside is fine.. it's nice. No hard feelings toward it. They serve an assortment of beer, which is beautiful. The food is also good. I have no qualms with it

BUT. It's too damn loud... EVERYWHERE. I have a hard time talking to my friends outside from the farthest point away from the music

Sometimes there are random nights that they are hosting events and it's 10-20 dollars to get in and it doesn't feel like a "local joint." 

This bar could be good but feels mismanaged and trying to be something they are not.. they could just be a great local bar with live music to get a beer out that doesn't make you deaf.

The bartenders are extremely rude. Treat you like second-class citizens. Drink selection is very limited, and everything seems a bit dirty/out of order. Music was bad the night I went but perhaps that was just that night. Overall I would not go back.

This is the only "dive bar" where one can drink a Pabst for $2, while sitting outside on a new smoke-free porch and view the Parthenon. 

Assuming the latter the greatest architectural achievement of the ancient world, there is a certain 'frisson' as the French would say that the lowest of low places, to quote Garth Brooks, in the city where 'low places' bring millions to folks who compete for trashy women, drunks in pick up trucks, etc,  and all are commandeered by a funny looking old man who endowed a University, Vanderbilt,  which is finally winning football games, by hiring a black coach.

 At a buck a toss on the JUKE BOX, one can get the greatest range of music selections one desires, from Brooks, to Bob Dylan, to Miranda Lambert, to Rolling Stones, and even the latest from Loretta Lynn, if you really want to go that far back

. Younger writers have mentioned bands, and I've heard there's JAZZ on Sunday, sometime,and junky bathrooms, and friendly wait staff,  but the biggest attraction of the place is its HUGE parking lot, covered with gravel, which reminds me of the days when I first started my research on DIVE BARS, in the state where they were INVENTED. LOUISIANA.

If there was a bar that screamed old nashville this would be it, because it is it. No frills, just the people that surround you, cheap beer and good local beer on tap,  music, billiards and more. Everything is cheap like a throwback and if you are local you cry because it just tastes like the Nashville you knew from the beginning. The taste never changes. There is no sex appeal. She is a legend and you will remember her for the imprint she makes

I've been to some dives and Nashville and this place has beyond the absolute worst staff I've ever met in my entire life. 

When I addressed the issue of a transaction with the owner he accused me of making up the issue I was having along with trying to tell me it wasn't possible his rude bartender who was half asleep could have made a mistake. Not sure what happened but these guys tend to wake up on the wrong side of the bed. 

The issue the customer is always right, these guys don't seem to comprehend that. Good luck with that in this town.

Shows great movies. Prices a little high, 10$ for a medium drink and small popcorn. Seats also pretty small and close together. If you don't mind price and seats then it's great time to see great classic movies in a theatre setting with others.

Nashville's version of Cheers! Everyone knew everyone and welcomed those that weren't regulars. Our bartender Marie was fantastic! She was right on top of what we wanted and suggested when we didn't know. Oh the tater tots are soooo good with all the dipping sauces ....yummm

This was an awful experience for eating. We are from out of town and have been waiting for an HOUR for our food. There are only a couple other people in the restaurant and no one seems to be working. People are walking out of the kitchen with nothing and talking and walking around and not cooking. It was not worth it. There was nothing and the food was awful. Their chicken tenders were the size of our pinky's. McDonald's chicken nuggets are bigger than what we got. The food is completely over priced and did not match up to anything. It is a waste of time and not worth the money. Management did talk to us but no one was straight up about what was happening in the kitchen. After all of us were done our other party member just got his food. It took way too long. They did take off our meal price at the end but it was miserable waiting for everything.

Came in for lunch at around 2:30pm. Cute industrial/rustic interior. There is a stage for a live band, but we visited during the week at lunch and the jukebox played good country. Our service at first was great, however we encountered shift change and our food was brought by a new girl. And she never came back lol. I abandoned the idea of ordering a second drink, as it was empty before I even finished my meal. The food was good, quality was met with cheaper prices than in the downtown area. I had the cheeseburger and my boyfriend had the pork sandwich with sweet fries. This place is definitely more of a bar than a restaurant and I would recommend coming in for drinks rather than making it a dinner stop. I think that if we sat at the bar we would have had more attention.

I love this venue.  There are a lot of fancier and bigger places to see shows in the area, but this is just the right size for me.  It's no frills but nothing missing either.  The bar has a good selection and you can get to it quickly easily without missing any of the show.  There isn't a long wait for the bathrooms.  You can see the show really well from just about everywhere.  On top of all that the staff is really friendly.   I'm looking forward to seeing a lot more shows here in the future.

My family of 5 went to Drifters when we traveled through town. We visited on a Friday night. We expected it to be busy but the wait inside was a bit over the top, so we sat outside. I do wish they had heat lamps outside. The food was quite delicious - especially their baked beans. My children loved all their food. The only negative is their parking and the fact the building is kind of hidden. I do know that it out of their control. 

This is quite a gem. If we are passing through again, we would definitely stop again.
Great music venue, albeit on the smaller side. It gets crowded, which sucks for short people like me, but the acoustics make up for it.

Top notch rubs for ribs n chicken. Good service. No tough eating bbq meat...this is the kind you want- the soft yummy kind.  A zillion sauces to choose from and they explain
the sauces well too.

If I can say anything helpful, 
1. try to keep smokers away from the doors and windows so us sponsoring fans eating your delicious food dont have the smoke taste mingle with your AWESOME bbq taste. When i eat this stuff you make, its so good I want nothing to interfere with my enjoyment of it. This has become a religous experience for me.
2. Try to anticipate demand for weekends and holidays because I came a few times when you ran out. Since your food is too damn good, I cried when I had to eat ??horsemeat?? somewhere else. I cant handle withdrawal from your food its so good I want a IV of it please? That includes your quesadilla.
3. Your service is fast and excellent. Keep up the soft meat and excellent taste...its paying off... your chicken isnt dry.... I know what good BBQ should taste like.  - the BBQ meister..... Ive been here 5 or 6 times allready...

Take it from a local, who was raised in Nashville.  This bar has been absolutely cursed from the get go.  Frisky Frog's owners were crooks, and the new owner of "Live Oak" (Gavin/Brennan?) is absolutely clueless on how to operate a bar. He drives around on scooters all day, and is constantly drunk. Do yourself a favor, and stick to the staples, Tin Roof or Dawghouse!

I've been to local movie houses in Atlanta and L.A.  and despite the reputation those towns hold as movie towns, the Belcourt outdoes the competition. It's due to the fact that their movie selection is bar none along with the pricing as well. Parking is amazing and so is their selection of concessions. I can't say enough about this theater and how it feels like home. I'll always go here instead of a corporate theater like AMC or Regal.

Beer selection: 4/5
Sauce: 5/5
Food: 4.5/5
Atmosphere: 5/5
Service: 5/5

Stopped here for lunch before shopping at Fatherland. We wound up finding parking on the street (for free) but the majority of the parking (lots) around here are pay lots. It's situated back from the main road a bit, behind another building, but there's a sign pointing you in the right direction and it looks like there's a few bars and restaurants right across the parking lot.

On Sundays all day they do bogo happy hour on beers... count me in. We both ordered BBQ platters and the bbq itself was so tasty, food came out fast, and I loved that it came with 3 sides (small sides, but I like variety). They have a sauce station to select your own, so we tried the Georgia, sweet & spicy, and New Mexico. All were super tasty with a nice kick, but I liked the sweet and spicy most, like I figured I would. 

The daily side of Mac and cheese was disappointing -- dry and not too flavorful, but slaw was nice and creamy and beans were tasty. 

Atmosphere is a cool dive bar vibe, and it looks like they have a little dog friendly patio situation, it just wasn't the right weather for it this weekend.

We'll be back!
Best place in Nashville to see a local band or up and coming act. The venue has a great setup and the shows always sound great!

This place was recommended to us by a local at the Hockey game last night.  He was right. We went for lunch.

There are 2 buildings at this location.  The lower building had a line out the door 2 @ 11 AM and the upper building was empty when we got there.  We paid ($6/2 hrs) to park in the adjacent lot, they only have a few spots available at the restaurant.
