My wife & I ordered a full rack of ribs that comes with fries, baked beans & cole slaw (sides can be substituted) and a bowl of chili.  I am glad we split the meal.

The ribs were cooked to perfection with a rub.  At the table was a sweet & smoky BBQ sauce that was excellent.  They also have a sauce bar that includes a Texas style sauce, a hot BBQ sauce (2nd favorite), a mustard sauce and a 4th that I didn't try.

The baked beans are the best I have had.  The cole slaw and fries were standard.  The chili was interesting because it had corn in it.  It had a very nice flavor.  My wife thought it was a little spicy.

Don't forget Happy Hour 11 AM till 7 PM. :)

Definitely a place to return to the next time we are in town.

The Belcourt Theatre is a true gem in Nashville. Showing great quality films that you won't see in every theatre around. The venue is clean, updated, generally great. Seating is traditional seating, no loungers, no recliners but seriously you are there to watch a movie, you can nap on your own sofa! 
Ticket process works so smoothly and they do give free parking vouchers of the Belcourt spaces with the ticket purchase. This is a popular area so parking spaces go quickly.   All the staff was very hospitable and professional.
Will be keeping an eye out for future films to view here!

Walked in with a friend who hadn't been here for twenty-five years. He said it's changed!  The theater is very nice. It's very updated, yet keeps its historic appeal. And the surprise is that the individual movie rooms have the decor of the era e.g., the 1925 room and the 1966 room. Several movies run on the same evenings. A concession counter provides the usual movie foods and adult beverages. The counter people are pleasant and informative about the venue. An elevator is available to see the art display upstairs and to enter the offices. This theater is a gem in the community.

One of Nashville's gems.  Every time I see a movie at the Belcourt, I'm reminded of how lucky we are to have this special place as both a part of our history and a part of our daily lives.

I love the variety of films here, as well as the low prices and friendly, laid back staff (who know their stuff about the movies shown at the Belcourt, a huge perk).  I am also a patron of the Nashville Jewish Film Festival and get to experience how the theatre opens its arms to the films and events year after year.  The Belcourt is a one of a kind theater and a place where everyone - employees, customers and Nashvillians - feels happy and excited to be a part.

The only drawbacks to the theater are the parking (though the lot is quite large, it often fills up quickly during popular films), the tiny ladies room, and the expensive concession stand.  I can understand paying competitive prices for concessions, but $4 for a cup of drip coffee is a bit much.  Nevertheless, I will continue to frequent The Belcourt whenever I'm in the mood for an indie or art flick.  This place truly is a local gem.

Buford is gone.  Smoking inside is gone.
Cold cheap beer and good AC.

Sadly, a disappointment. Went to a bar across street which was packed with opposing football team's fans so headed over to commodore grille for some Vandy camaraderie, 1-hr pregame. Plenty clean, nice/fast servers, and convenient ladies room...but overpriced cocktails in sad little plastic cups. And the place had two groups of mizzou fans and one group of Vandy fans -- empty! Maybe coming during a radio sports broadcast would be good but don't expect to get your pregame hype on here!

A perfect spot for an after-work drink. Now that the weather is getting nicer, the outdoor patio is perfect. The Local is farely large, with a roomy interior and lots of outdoor seating as well. There are tons of beers on draft, and almost always a band playing.

Most recently, the space was being used for a benefit for Miss Amazing, a really great organization showcasing the beauty of girls with disabilities. Love that the Local supports such a great cause!

Still a great place for burgers & they toast the bun..
Infused with bacon.. good stuff BUT they NOW charge you $1.50 for fries.

First off, the door staff is horrible and mean.. except for ONE security guy checking bags- he was a very polite, handsome black man. But hands down the most memorable person at the venue was an especially discourteous, scruffy looking white guy checking IDs like a junior high hall monitor who'd rather pull a girl's hair or make her cry rather than smile at her and was working the night of 10/7/18.  The guy clearly has an unchecked, undeserved power complex and seems to hate his job as much as he hates the patrons happily showing up to spend money at his place of work. Perhaps if he's so unhappy with his current position he should find gainful employment elsewhere, something in the lucrative Port-O-John industry or a sewage treatment facility would be more appropriate, that way excited concert goers aren't subjected to the wrath of his hyper-inflated, false sense of importance covering a crippling inferiority complex that's obviously made him physiologically incapable of human interaction that doesn't involve rudeness or blatant misogyny on display toward women in line that was consistently derogatory or belittling. His over the top rudeness has no place on Cannery Row or in Nashville. We have a courteous city and his poor attitude doesn't reflect that fact but diminishes it, and it probably makes other women extremely uncomfortable, and personally it ruined my entire evening with friends. No thanks to whoever hired this self loathing, woman hating, half premature ejaculate in human form, half bottom dwelling troglodyte getting his kicks by scowling at happy patrons from his post at the door and savoring the only power he'll ever have over what HAS TO BE his only opportunity to be near actual human females throughout the course of his pathetic daily life and the only women he will ever have the pleasure of disappointing in his small, anger-filled, micro-existence on this planet. 

The artist was fantastic, it's a shame I'll be seeing them elsewhere to avoid the a power hungry little impotent gatekeeper and ruiner of good times checking IDs. Unfortunately I missed his name, but who would ever want it anyways? No more shows for me at cannery for awhile.

Stumbled across this gem with my Dad - we literally were just walking around Centennial, saw the "cold beer" sign and decided to go inside - so glad we did! Springwater is an interesting place. The bartender told us it was the oldest bar in Tennessee so i was stoked to be inside it! It is grungy looking - lots of old photos, signs, and the booths are worn (which adds to the ambiance). It's small so I can imagine how packed it must get at night. The bartender was so nice, she kept asking us if we needed anything. My only complaint is the cigarette smoke. Since the place is so small, it's somewhat suffocating to be engulfed by cigarette smoke. Oh well, I still had a blast!

I've seen a handful of shows here. The staff is always wonderful, from the box office to the security. Depending on when you get there, parking can be pretty easy. If you're there just before the show starts, don't bother with the parking lot. Drinks are reasonably priced and they have a great pop up burger joint out front called Boutique Burgers. 

If you're in town visiting try and catch a show at any of the venues attached to it. You won't be disappointed.

While Drifters claims to be The BEST PATIO in Nashville it does not claim to be the BBQ in Nashville. 

The Patio is nice, the staff is friendly, the music is good.

The BBQ Is terrible. 

Maybe it was just a bad night, but I was all ready to enjoy "The Drifter", but instead I found a soggy bun covered by tasteless brisket and pulled pork. 
 
The nearby "Sweet and Sour" BBQ Sauce helped this somewhat, but I still felt like I was putting Ketchup on a bad Steak. 

All I can recommend here is the live music on the patio. I'd come back for that, but that's all.
Love the local vibe. Local musicians and song writers  this is probably one of my favorite spots in Nashville so far!

Wife and I had a foodie weekend and we ended up here for lunch one of those days. Service was ok, we had a new server that struggled only because it was her first day, but did a good job of managing through a tough lunch. Got the fried catfish and it was very good. Tarter sauce was spot on and the fries were great. Wife got the small nacho plate and some BBQ and it was good. The vibe here does remind me of a dive bar, but don't get turned off by that because the food is still top notch!

I would give 0 stars if I could! The absolute worst venue ever. Is a over 21 venue only but booked a band that was underage. Band and crew were not made aware of the age requirement. They didn't not let camera guy. Band had to leave after set and couldn't support other bands!! Worst venue ever!

I love the belcourt. I'm so glad Nashville has held on to a little piece of its history in this building. The remodel made it really nice inside but I'm glad they kept the old movie screen because it creates an ambiance that other theaters don't have. I also love the cookie/pastry selection they have at the counter from local businesses as I am not a theater popcorn person but like to have something other than candy. 

Tip: if you haven't been to their showing of Rocky Horror Picture Show, go! It's so much fun.

I'll start by saying that Cannery Ballroom might not be the most ideal concert venue for everyone. There is no seating so be prepared to stand for 2+ hours. I think that's the most important thing to know. 

The Cannery Ballroom is in the same building as The Mercy Lounge and the High Watt. Since there are multiple venues, they will ask you out front which concert you are there to see and point you in the right direction. Parking isn't bad if you get there early enough. There is a smaller lot with free parking and then a bigger lot for $5. I believe it's cash only but we were lucky enough to get a free spot. We were there Halloween night to see Ghostland Observatory so I figured it would be pretty busy. We arrived at about 8:45 for a 9:00 show. Check-in was super easy. A security guard did a metal detector test and looked inside my purse. Inside, a person scanned my mobile tickets on my phone and we were in. The Cannery Ballroom is one big room. Right when you walk in, the bathrooms are to the right in a separate area. The bar is also to the right and is pretty big. They had about 8 different options for beer and then also mixed drinks. Beers were $5-7 and I believe they were all tall boys. Not bad for a concert venue. The stage was in the front right corner but can be seen from anywhere in the room...I think. It might be hard to see when the room gets really packed. The room wasn't too busy yet so we were able to get right up front. I'm not sure if this was the best choice. The sound was really loud. I know concerts are loud, but this just seemed unnecessarily loud. The building is brick so I'm guessing it has something to do with the acoustics. The crowd was of course pushy and packed but that's what you can expect with GA standing rooms. Like some of the other reviews have mentioned, it gets really warm in this place. I mean this was October and once the show really got started, it was pretty hot. I had a t-shirt and jeans on and was uncomfortable. I could see the singer was just dripping in sweat. I don't think I would come to a concert here in summer. But I'm also a person that doesn't like the heat. 

The tickets were a good price compared to other venues in Nashville. It's nice that you can get right up to the stage if you don't mind how loud the sound is. Standing in the middle of the room might get you better sound but then you don't get as good of view of the stage. Overall, it was a fun night and a nice venue. I would come back for another concert!

My only complaint is that there aren't more Belcourt Theatres in town! I have been seeing films here since I moved to the area 12 years ago. It's a true art house with a variety of genres and access to limited opening release films. 

If you are into old films, they have lots of classics playing throughout the year and even do holiday specials. It is very family friendly. 

I do miss the old feel to the building (and the funky bathrooms) but it is nice to have more space for events. 

The concessions are on point- local beers, wine on tap, and unique snacks. Some membership levels even have free refills on popcorn and soda!

This is a wonderful place to connect with likeminded individuals who enjoy experiencing films in a smaller and more intimate space. 

Go see a film! You won't be disappointed. 

Parking in the lot is free too!

Staff see the place as more of a hangout/clique. No sense of urgency to move customers through queue. In fact, the person at the ticket counter chatted it up for 2 minutes with a lady in front of us while she hustled him for a teacher discount without showing any proof of ID. 

When we asked what time the movie would start after previews, they looked offended that we would interrupt their social gathering while they held up the line. He proceeds to stare us down as we are walking outside after the movie while mocking us with the short stocky red headed girl laughing behind the concession stand. Case in point: the picture I took of the ticket counter guy mean mugging us while the red headed girl egged him on (it's attached here with the girl circled) . It's a big hangout for staff, no sense of urgency for the customers trying to get in to the theater. If you got time to lean, you got time to clean. 

Movie selection is good, but theater upstairs is cramped. And the projector is right above the audience, exposed, making noise the entire time.

Mercy Lounge brings in some really incredible acts either before they hit it big or right after.  The tickets are so cheap and the space very small with great sound.  It can get really hot in here when its sold out, but they have a lovely little deck outside that's great for cooling purposes.  The bar is small but the bartenders here are always on their game.  Sometimes for smaller shows or showcases you can sit at a table and relax while you enjoy the music.  When its sold out its a free for all and really packed but compared to other venues its really not that horrible.  Sure its a battle to get back to the bar from your great viewing spot (there really isn't a bad place to stand here) but even if you can't get back to that first spot you can see quite well from anywhere inside.  Seeing a show here is an overall great and inexpensive experience, and usually you want to see the bands playing here while you can before they are playing bigger venues to more fans.  Yeah you feel like a music snob ("I saw them at Mercy last year and now they're at the Ryman") but the acts here are worth the stuffy dark room and rampant PBR.

Obsessed! 

We landed in Nashville at about 10 pm and the first thing I did was open up my yelp app to find some Bbq! 

So glad we came here. We got a sort of sampler platter with ribs, brisket, hot links, fries and fried pickles. It was SO good! 

Definitely recommend! Chill spot, good drinks, friendly service and lots and lots of yummy sauces!

I don't really like independent movies which is why I don not enjoy belcourt. It is full of conceited hipsters and college/grad students that don't know anything about the politics and socioeconomic status of this world. The films are ok but the audience just ruins it fo rme man

After reading reviews, I wanted to voice my own opinion as the previous ones mention a lot of the rude service or angry staff. We came early (it stays pretty empty until about 10 mins before the show starts btw!) and got in with no issue. No hassle with the doormen, will call was quick, they just asked for my ID and name. Bartenders were quick to serve us and we had no issues getting more drinks throughout the concert. It wasn't particularly crowded for our show and we had a great time. There's a "tiki bar" sign for the patio but there was no bar for our event, just an outdoor space where everyone took smoke breaks during the show. There's a small upstairs area with a few bar stools near the front, which would've been great for those who don't like to stand the whole time. Merch booth was tucked in a corner in the back so it didn't interrupt the show. Bathrooms are small but accessible.

Oversold tickets so there weren't enough seats for my party of 3. And no, we didn't care if we sat together, there were literally no seats left. Didn't apologize and were clearly annoyed. Takes days for refund to go through. Wish I hadn't spent $20 on the uber ride over! Love small independent theaters and support the ones where I live, but this one really needs to get it's sh!t together!

Absolutely no reason to go here. Waited for 1 and a half hours for our food and never came. Finally cancelled the order after them telling us "how busy they were." Does not deserve to be in business and the only reason they are is by serving underage Vanderbilt students late at night. The bar tenders work hard but the owner and management are incompetent and unable to service the basic functions of a bar/restaurant. When we left the restaurant, the two kitchen workers were smoking pot in the alley, with no workers in the actual kitchen period. DO NOT COME HERE!

The evenings are getting cooler.
Cool breezes flow around the patio that has little white lights strung about.
A band is playing on the bandstand and the tables are filled with music lovers..
and beer lovers.

Friend and I got a hightop outside on the patio.
Shared a meal, a drink and sung along with the musician.

Burger was cooked MR, as requested. Infused with bacon.
It came with fries, even though I didn't order them.
Friend had the corn dog and it came with fries he didn't order, either.
Ample portions, cooked as requested, served hot.

Nice place for a pleasant evening.

After a day bouncing about Nashville and stopping by  the Parthenon, we wanted - no, NEEDED - a drink.  This place was the closest walk, and it turned out to be a blast!  Very kind bartenders, large beer menu.  It's beer only, but I loved that.  

It states it is the oldest bar in TN, and I believe it.  I know these places like to keep their "cash only" status, but in 2016, it may be time to kiss that vestige goodbye.  I'd still go back, though!

Checked out the mercy lounge for the first time last night to see Porches & Girlpool play and I was not disappointed with the music or the venue. It was relatively spacious for a small-medium concert and wasn't overpacked despite there being a decent amount of people there. They also have a fairly affordable drink menu, which is always appreciated. Service was fast and the overall vibe of the venue was cool.

My only critique is that their photobooth didn't work and tends to steal people's money --  that being said, they have a sign explicitly stating this, so using the photobooth is really at your own risk. The staff also was very transparent about this. Overall a fun venue, would recommend checking it out!

Not bad, not bad at all! Drifters gets a major nod for being a BBQ joint with a dedicated vegetarian menu. Keep your expectations in check, though, after all it *is* a BBQ joint. No culinary wonders for those of us avoiding the offerings from the smoker (however, my guy is a BBQ fanatic and ordered the most monstrous plate of nachos with some kind of BBQ meat splayed across 'em. This looked like a delicious mess, which was confirmed), but utterly basic basics: tofu, which I'm a fan of + Morningstar Farm protein, which I'm not a fan of (and if you're vegan, know that Morningstar Farm is not). 

I ordered the Tofu Dinner w/o slaw, which also comes with fries and beans (not sure if that was meat swimming around with those beans so I didn't taste them. It sure looked like meat shreds). It's a generous portion and although I wasn't blown away by anything on the plate, I can see it being the perfect late night food (yes! they have late night hours!) and it sure did treat my lingering annual hangover right. As did the Bloody Mary.

The staff is nice. The patio is sweet and the interior is the perfect dark, divey BBQ joint kind of atmosphere. I like this place a lot. And I'm just so appreciative of a BBQ place doing something cool for vegetarians that is truly unexpected. What's not to love about that?

Ok I'm from KC so BBQ is kind of a big deal in our neck of the woods. Had the brisket sandwich and tots. Good fresh bun and generous amount of brisket. Good hickory penetration, not too dry. House sauce is sweeter than KC likes but good smokiness. Tots were spot on. Nobody likes a soggy tot. Great hole in the wall vibe, good service, and the soundtrack reminds of all the songs I need to add to my Apple playlist. Nice BBQ break for a KC chick.

My thoughts on the Cannery Ballroom echo my thoughts on Mercy Lounge pretty much verbatim (they are in the same building after all). I feel like the room near the stage is a bit freer in the Cannery than in Mercy but it's been awhile since I've seen a show at Mercy to know if that's actually true or not. Anyway, for the Cannery as a music venue:
I see a lot of reviews complaining about the drinking area being roped off to a tiny space? I've been to several shows, most recently in November 2017, and this has never been the case. Of course they've been 18+ shows but they stamp you if you're 21 and up and you can go wherever you like with your drink. Maybe at shows where there are very young attendees it's different? I thought this was a bar and all shows were 18+ but I could be wrong.

PROS:
*Good size for working bands and artists to headline (not the kind who play the stadiums--we're talking about up and coming, used to be, niche, cult, local, underground, etc.). You can see the show from pretty much anywhere in the room and navigate your way to the front if you wish fairly easily.
*Easy parking--get there early and park for free on site, get there a bit later and park in a pay lot connected to the main lot for only $5 which is not bad at all by Nashville standards
*Easy bar navigation--they will greet you, serve you, etc. pretty quickly
*If you're a smoker there's an easily accessible deck and they let you in and out with no hassle. If you're not a smoker that deck is far enough away from everything that nothing drifts back in
CONS:
*Acoustics at Cannery (and Mercy) leave a bit to be desired as everything gets 2x louder than it needs to be as it echoes off of every stone and brick surface area. WEAR EAR PLUGS! If it's a particularly loud act try and stand midway back from the stage. On my most recent visit the opening acts sounded great but I moved to the front for the headliner and it was deafening. That in some ways was simply due to the nature of the band and the music they played but better acoustics would've softened it enough to hear the range of the performance a bit better. I overheard someone on my way out telling their friend "you never stand too close to the front, always half back and the sound's better". Maybe for this place but I've been in several venues where you can stand right by the stage or at the very back and whether the loudest of metal or the softest of folk music if the acoustics are right it'll sound great wherever you are. 
*Drink prices and selection: while not as bad as Bridgestone or the Ryman, the FAQ on their website is a bit misleading when it claims "drinks start at $3 and go up". I ordered my share of different beers and drinks and nothing was $3--not even PBR or Miller Hi-LIfe. There were no (or few b/c I didn't see them) craft or import beer options so if you're a beer drinker it's standard mass produced American beers for 5 bucks a pop.
*Entrance procedure: it's odd. You get here and park but if you walk to the door to line up they direct you outside of the gates and down the sidewalk then march you in field trip style once gates are open.

That's about it. I'd see another show here if it's the right act but this iisn't my favorite place to see a band in Nashville by any means.

Cold beer - check
Live music - check
Divey atmosphere - check
Shots - no check... 4 stars

The Belcourt is my favorite thing in Nashville. I would like Nashville about 35% to 45% less if the Belcourt wasn't here. 

The new building isn't my favorite. How did it take millions of dollars to make everything look somehow at once cheaper and newer? They've traded the rundown, ramshackle charm of a 1920s movie palace in decay in for something that looks a lot like cinemas in Williamsburg or downtown Manhattan, and they've compromised the original facade's tripartite arches--still used as the theatre logo--in order to build up. Basically, the Belcourt is now a white gallery cube, fitting perhaps because some shoddy local artists now seem to be on lowkey display and because the theatre shows self-described art house films. Perhaps it's just the tone of white and the absolutely pristine nature of the affair, or perhaps it's just the kind of nostalgia typical of millennials to yearn for the original. On the other hand, the new theatre upstairs, the conference room/educational spaces, and the new entryway for the smaller theatre downstairs are really welcome additions. 

The new upstairs theatre allows them to show more obscure, less popular films to smaller audiences--but I'd suggest sitting in the first two rows because the screen is quite small and the height differential between rows is not enough to allow one to see subtitles. The original "1925 Hall" (where the Opry was briefly located) isn't a truly remarkable old movie palace space, however, the continued presence of a decorated proscenium and the old, red, velvet-y seats ensure that even postmodern biopics about David Foster Wallace feel like you're watching them in a 1960s time machine rather than a Regal Cinemas. The second theatre downstairs is newer, likely from the 1980s, but has excellent sound and picture quality. 

The concessions aren't really a step above what you'd get at a normal multiplex beyond a wider selection of beers (the Regals at Opry MIlls and Green Hills Malls have mainstream Trump beers; the Belcourt slyly eschews GOP beers for the impartial PBR and local/Southern brands) and hard alcohol. You DO get $1 refills on any size popcorn, which is great if you have only had breakfast and felt as though that Truffaut movie was going to feed you more than Fido. In fantasies, they serve like kale chips, green smoothies, and burgers. 

Parking at this point is competitive during peak hours. I'd recommend getting to the theatre an hour to an hour and a half before your movie when there isn't such high demand, parking, and then grabbing a beer at the dive bar the Villager Tavern. Your parking pass lasts two hours before and after the film so make use of it. Just don't patronize the nearby chains like Jeni's which have turn Nashville into a monstrosity.

Overall the film selections are outstanding, diverse, original, and often adventurous. Sure, the Belcourt tend to keep some real stinkers masquerading as independent film ("Nocturnal Animals," anyone) for too many weeks, however, between the mainstream first run independent fare (which is often v good) they run anywhere between what I have counted to be two and eleven repetory films a week: on Friday at midnight, you can see a cult classic horror film about a serial killer Santa; on Sunday at noon, you can watch a film celebrating indigenous black culture on South Carolina's coast; on Tuesday night, you can see a biopic with sterling performances if lackluster script; on Monday afternoon, you can see a newly digitally restored "Battle of Algiers" with a seminar led by a Vanderbilt professor afterwards; and, on Saturday morning, you can go to a roundtable discussion of black gay male sexual identity to accompany your viewing of the aforementioned "Moonlight." Really, the offerings are exceptionally diverse and adventurous for a theatre with only screens serving a relatively conservative, otherwise artistically unadventurous blue dot in a red sea. 

While I go to the Belcourt at least twice a week, I don't really see the great advantage to becoming a member. You get 20% off only the non-alcoholic concessions (boo!) and, especially if you're a student, the ticket discount isn't large enough (student and all matinee ticket prices are $8.50, while member tickets are $7; normal evening tickets are $10) to make the membership fees worthwhile. 

I mock the employees a lot but perhaps shouldn't. Some of them are totally the performative media/theatre studies types who turn purchasing a ticket into a one act play about being a FRIENDLY hipster in a dead end job making sacrifices so you can get your parking pass but a lot of them are just chill af. I've gotten free concessions before late at night, and I've also had a ticket refunded for a film I found unwatchable--twice. Like I said, I come here a lot, but, generally, the employees are gracious without acknowledging the fact that I probably go to too many movies.

THE BELCOURT IS THE BEST CULTURAL INSTITUTION IN NASHVILLE.

This theatre is a non profit venue to watch independent films.  The theatre first started in 1925.  



The theatre also has food.  Most of it is typical movie theatre, but they have bratwurst.  



However, this is my favorite part of the theatre, a full bar!  Yes, please!



I had a mimosa while watching the movie.  



I like this theatre.  It's a good place to watch independent movies and to enjoy a cocktail while doing it.

I have a special place in my heart for the Belcourt Theatre. This is a jewel in Nashville. Prior to its renovation, this was a hip, older move theatre which prominently had viewing for independent and hipster films. This place had a certain charm of the older days in the former building. I had been to Belcourt once before the renovation and honestly I kinda liked the older feel that the Belcourt exuded during my visit. I felt like I was temporarily transported to a different time during the movie experience.

But alas, things change. The renovations are certainly modern and sleek. While then charm might not still be there, this is certainly somewhere that independent films continue to live on! This truly is the best part of this theatre. The genres and selections of movies makes for an endless options of movies. I seem to always want to come back to the Belcourt again and again.

The snack bar/concession area was updated to provide an assortment of local beers along with popcorn (and $1 refills!) 

The parking is somewhat of a headache during popular times so be aware. I recommend parking on Belcourt Ave and arriving a little early to enjoy the area. 

If you have time for a movie and want something that might not be heavily promoted, but will fill your love for movies - please do yourself a flavor and come to the Belcourt!

3.5

As an event venue, Mercy is a bit tight. As a music venue, it's intimate. Does that make sense? Enjoyment of the space will entirely depend on what brings you out. 

To try & enjoy ML as an event venue with many people moving about, the space tends to get very cramped, very quickly. It's hard to pay attention to a variety of things at once because it's rather difficult to move around. It's the sort of space that if you are planning on having an event, you should plan for either something small or something progressive that allows guests to get in and get out to another space. Spending a few hours in the confines can be a touch claustrophobic.

As a music venue (its intended and best use), Mercy Lounge makes much more sense. The space that's cramped as an event venue becomes intimate for a musical performance. That has much to with the fact that, typically, for a performance people aren't milling about. They're staying still and being respectful to the performers, other guests and to the venue. For shows, the bartenders are quick and friendly. The beers are $5 a draft pull and the acoustics lend themselves well for concentrating on one thing (with lots of voices and feet bouncing around everywhere, with a lot going on, it can be a bit overwhelming in another setting).

Come for the music. Think carefully about an event. Enjoy your time.

Drifter's is a classic dive joint.  From the minute you walk in you get an instant low key laid back local vibe.  People at the bar knew each other, knew the bartenders and didn't seem to have a care in the world.  Had it not been a dreary rainy day, I would have brought my pup and sat outside to enjoy some brews since they had a nice patio as well.  

I can't speak much for the BBQ as I'm a vegetarian, but the hush puppies were on point.  I enjoyed mine with some BBQ sauce, as I didn't care much for the dipping sauce that was served with them.  I also got some chips and salsa.  Now being a TX girl, I knew this was risky, but I was told the salsa was made in house, so I gave it a go.  Not sure if I'd call it salsa, as it was more like pico.  You know big chunks of tomato and diced onion.  But it was still good.  My man got the ribs and I did try the tiniest of bites, just so I could say I tasted it.  Wow - SMOKEY!  These meaty bones were defiantly slow cooked over a smoke pit for sho!  My man enjoyed them.  The baked bean were just that - nothing wowed me about them.  And I'd say the same for the coleslaw.  Overall food wasn't bad, but not sure I'd call it the best!  They did have some veggie options, but they seemed rather predictable and not worth the try for me.  I would have loved to see some BBQ setan on the menu or something at least trying to run with the BBQ theme.  My man said to give it 4 stars, but being a southern girl, I just wasn't that impressed.

They had some nice brews on tap, which made me content.  And the staff was fantastic.  I could see this as a great place to hang out and drink some cold ones.  But I'd be up for looking for some other BBQ places to try out.
Oldest bar in Nashville. Loved it! A group of us in town for LSU had a blast!! Stopping in next time in Nashville.

This theatre deserves nothing less than 5 stars. It's a lovely old movie house, lush velvet seats and all, originally opened as a silent film house in the '20s. (Renovated since then, of course - nothing looks particularly shabby.)

I visited on a late Monday afternoon and it was calm, quiet, and awesomely air-conditioned. I assume they have more moviegoers at a more normal time - the location is excellent, right off the Vanderbilt campus. Programming includes repertory, cult classics, indie/foreign, kids films, second run, etc. Plus lots of special programming: outdoor films in their parking lot, midnight screenings... Sometimes they do some first-run stuff as well. It's basically everything anyone wants if they're choosing not to go to a multiplex! 

Later this month they'll be screening the hilariously brilliant Japanese horror cult classic "House." Watching this on the big screen is a necessary life experience. 

All tickets before 6pm every day are matinee priced: $7.75! Ahhh glorious. They automatically gave me with the receipt a free parking pass for their lot.

Two women in the row in front of me actually took care to sit slightly toward the left so they wouldn't block my view - so thoughtful!

Worth a visit as a tourist? Yessir, especially if you need some peace and a temporary change of scenery via silver screen. If you're a local? Get yourself a membership!

We came on a Sunday afternoon looking for a patio to enjoy the sunshine. This place is huge and someone put a lot of money into it- it's pretty! They have lots of beer and some good looking cocktails. They have live music Mon-Thurs. Very laid back vibe and good for groups.

We have the pretzel and Brussels sprouts to snack on. The pretzel and cheese sauce was particularly good.

Awesomeness place came thru last night 
A free concert was playing they have multi
Stages and the crowd was very hip the 
Gentleman at the front desk was very 
Polite and professional great place to visit

The EXIT/IN was a great place to catch a show! I went here on a Wednesday night to see the awesome band Superorganism. Tickets were cheap which I always appreciate. It kills me to go to a big venue like Bridgestone, spend $150+ on tickets, and be up so far you can barely even see the performer. The EXIT/IN allows you to get up close and personal with the band performing. Parking can be a little tricky but we were able to find free parking on a side street close by. The check-in process was quick and easy. Have your IDs with you, even if you bought tickets online. I did see security around but they didn't say anything or bother me the whole night. Maybe they have listened to the feedback or maybe this was a smaller show so they didn't have to be on such high alert? The feel of the place is a classic dive music venue. I loved it. Behind the bar, they have a list of names of people who have performed at the venue before. Cool touch. I didn't check out their drink menu too much because I had a sore throat, but they had a good selection of beers and mixed drinks. The stage is raised so you can have a good view from anywhere in the room. There is also a balcony if you really want the bird's eye view. We were pretty close to the stage because it wasn't a super packed show and we arrived on time. The opener ended up cancelling so the band performed a little earlier than expected. I felt bad for people who came later because they probably missed half the show. That's why I'm always on time! The sound was awesome. The band was of course great. One thing that kind of put a damper on the concert was the video stopped working. The band had really cool video work for their background and for about 4 songs it didn't work. The venue had to shut off all of the lights and reboot everything it looked like. At one point the band was almost playing in the dark. I get it, these things happen. The band was cool with it and cracked jokes with the audience. Overall, it was a fun venue that lets you really experience the band for an unbeatable price. I would 100% go back to check out another show!

This place is as divey as it gets. Driving by, most people wouldn't even realize it's there, or that it's open. After reading that it was the oldest bar in the entire state of TN, and realizing it was walking distance from where I live, I had to check it out. It was relatively empty around 7:30 on a Friday night - one booth of people, and a few people at the bar. The bartender was friendly, and quickly served us up some draft beers. The place is dark and grungy, in a comfortable kind of way, with torn booths and a stage for performances. There's also darts, music playing, and some outdoor seating. It was a fun spot to grab a beer before dinner.
Super friendly bartenders and patrons. Bbq joint, in and outdoor seating.  Music some early evenings. Some art works dot the area. Fun.

Y'all really pissed me off tn...... I came from out of town to attend a wedding and was genuinely disgusted by the way the staff treated some of the guests. I won't go into details but I suffice it to say that it was completely inappropriate. Would not recommend for anyone trying to celebrate an otherwise

Just visited this place last night and I have to say it's a new favorite. They make a tasty burger and have lots of great beer options. The vibe is laid back and the outdoor dog-friendly patio is perfect in nice weather. We really enjoyed the music too. It wasn't overrun with people but we didn't stay very late. I hope it hangs on, bc I'll definitely be back!

Absolutely awful establishment!! Waitresses didn't come once to our table. They served tables around us, and completely ignored our table! The staff was a complete embarrassment. The food was awful. I ordered a panini and got one slice of turkey. A disgrace of a business. I will NEVER go back and I Recommend No One ever go back!! Am embarrassment of a restaurant. Hope the GM and the staff all go out of business and jobs!

I have not eaten at The Country, so I cannot review based upon their menu but it does look a step above typical bar food offerings. I am basing my review on the facility, staff and parking. My husband's band played here, and it was nice while loading in all his equipment there's an alley right next to a side door. Inside was big, clean and offered plenty of seating. There's also a very nice patio outside with great tables and benches to enjoy the music. The staff were all very friendly and I really loved the orange cream martini, which tasted just like an orange cream ice cream bar. What really earns a 5-star rating, though, is the parking. The Country is right next to Centennial Park, an area that is often parking-challenged. However, they have a dedicated lot and it's free! I'll give you a moment to let that comment sink in. Yes, free, convenient parking does still exist in Nashville!

Came here to support a friend, who was hosted a Patriots party here. Word to the wise: If you come here on a football Sunday you are going to be surrounded by Boston accents and Tom Brady jerseys. If you are looking for the Nashville Patriots Headquarters you have found your spot. 

If you want to avoid the Massachusetts crowd, they have great happy hour specials Tuesday-Thursday featuring $4 Crafts beers,
1/2 Price Select Appetizers, and $3 well drinks. I have had great service during Happy Hour. The bartenders have always been friendly. If you are looking for food options their menu includes frog legs, gator tail, and hushpuppies. Not something I would eat every day- but hey, when in rome.

Marie is the best bartender to grace this planet. She takes care of everyone in a timely manner and makes the best drinks. Her music taste is impeccable and she looks out for everyone in her bar. 
Drifters has great food and a great happy hour! Cheers in East Nashville.

I couldn't be more grateful for Belcourt Theater. This place gives me option other than big boxes cinema like AMC or Regal. Belcourt also have the personality of its own, looking at the movies that they are showing. Every time I watch a movie at Belcourt, it reminds me of what movie-making is all about. Sure, big box office money is great - but, for an artist, money is not everything. There is character building, story telling, pacing, dialog, etc. From my perspective, I believe Belcourt has found a happy medium. Parking can be horrendous, but that's expected. As for constructive criticism, it will be best if Belcourt can announce showing time at least 2 weeks in advance, so people can have ample time to make plan. Currently, I can consider my self lucky if they announce their showing schedule at the same week. Oh well!

I appreciate everything about this lovely art-house theater in downtown Nashville. It's got a great selection of films, helpful staff, and posh seats. The bathrooms are pretty darn nice, too! In those, the shelf above the sink is perfect for putting down your purse or bag while you get your hands clean. I wish every bathroom included this feature!

My family and I came out to see the Korean film
Parasite at the end of Thanksgiving weekend, and it was an excellent way to wrap up our visit. We had no trouble with parking in the Belcourt lot, and we arrived early enough to walk around the theater and see some of the artwork on sale, benefiting homeless artists and a non-profit organization Poverty and the Arts. Thanks, Belcourt Theatre!

Please have mercy :P  

One of the nicest music concert places in town, way better then Cannery next door and room is quite spacious and sound system pretty well set up. I have been here for a few concerts already and best part is , its never that expensive and the crowd that comes in is 21+ and well  maintained.   

The stage is amazing and everyone is catered as GA so nothing to worry about, music speakers are well placed and on top of that they have a open patio outside as well to breathe. 

So do go enjoy this spot and no matter who is playing you can go to the rooms next door or go downtown for boradway fun.

My husband and I drove 10hrs from Oklahoma City to see Passenger perform on 10/13/18. I have a rare lung disease that doesn't require me to wear oxygen all the time, but it does cause me to get really tired if I walk for long distances or am on my feet for a long time. When I heard the Cannery Ballroom doesn't have seating I emailed and called the venue to see if they could accommodate me by allowing me to have a chair in the back of the room. I was told it shouldn't be a problem and the day of the show when I let Eron from security know he was more than happy to accommodate me and a few other people who saw what I had done and requested a chair also. He made it a point to say they really want guests to enjoy the performance, and they try to make good music accessible for everyone. They wanted me to spread the word here on yelp so other guests who are disabled will be encouraged to get out and see more live music! I agree with him 100% and I'm so grateful they have this attitude! I'm more than happy to give them a 5 star review. Aside from the helpful staff it was a great place to see live music in an intimate setting, plus fast bar service and close parking. Thanks for a great night of music, Cannery Ballroom.
Excellent venue.   Love this place.  Best venue I've been to. Drinks were good and best of all seeing my Nashville favorites, The Dead Deads

I can't believe it took me [redacted] years to get here. Sadly, I only experienced the pre-renovation Belcourt from the outside. With Nashville's growth in the past few years, it's surprising to me that the Belcourt stands alone when it comes to the caliber and type of films it shows. Surely there's more of a demand for this sort of cinema than one theater can manage for an entire region. Surely. But, if it's not the case, the Belcourt more than suffices for the needs of art/indie/foreign film lovers.

I won't insult your intelligence and describe the what of the Belcourt. You come here because you love film. Period. That's why you're here. For the other bells and whistles, I'll spend some time bending your ear. Parking is... yeah. The theatre has a dedicated parking lot but other Hillsboro Village patrons can park in it. It's free for Belcourt patrons but just getting a spot can be an issue. It's frustrating. You would think someone coming to the theatre would have priority over someone parking his car and going about his merry way but things are what they are. Parking is a bit of an issue in this neighborhood. Allocate for some difficulty and arrive earlier than you would think you need to.

The theatre design is interesting. This is not a megaplex. There are (only?) six or so movies playing at a time. But all of the films playing are quality. And the individual theaters are pretty relaxing, complete with big screens, cup holders and space to man spread. Add some velvet curtains to the doorway and you have the recipe for an old-school cinematic experience. Adding to that experience: wine. I felt oh-so-classy watching my documentary whilst sipping a glass (well, cup) of white wine. If you want to be a film snob, you need to go all in. You can do that here. There's also craft beer and other better-than-expected snacks at the ready. And, least you think the air too rarified, there's plenty of popcorn... buttered with real butter. Lots of it.

Oh my goodness. Best little hole in the wall place I've ever been! Pickles jalapeños, hush puppies, the brisket and the pulled pork. Couldn't have had a better meal! The sweet heat and jalapeño ranch sauces you MUST try! Great little place and I highly recommend
Great variety of sushi that's always fresh and reasonably priced. It's a small place so get there a bit early and expect a bit of a wait. Cozy atmosphere and friendly staff. Loved the ninza roll.

One of my favorite dives in Nashville. Don't expect anything fancy, but it's a great place to grab a Shiner and people watch or interact with some local flavor. If you get hungry, head through the back door and find Buford, he'll hook you up with a solid burger and tots on a paper plate. It'll hit the spot.
Springwater isn't for everyone, but if you want a slightly gritty, authentic Nashville experience, you will love it. You won't find many bachelorette parties or groups of tourists here.
As the oldest bar in Tennessee, this place is iconic. Taylor Swift did a Coke commercial on their stage and the Black Keys filmed a music video here. 
I would say this is one of the top 10 dive bars in America.

So I ordered buffalo wings and I got 6 wings, I'm from buffalo and if you got 6 wings in buffalo we would say forget it.   They were good but 6 wings for the price of 10, forget about it don't buy wings from here it's a RIP off.

When visiting Nashville, it is imperative to make sure you eat at a BBQ place. Coming from Texas, I have had some pretty damn good BBQ. I found Drifters on Yelp and was excited because they also had vegetarian options for my boyfriend who is vegetarian.

We ubered to this place which was one of the best decisions. They have a parking lot but it is shared amongst many establishments. On a Saturday night, you can imagine it wasn't fun. None the less, we didn't have to worry about it (on a side note, Sunday afternoon is fine). 

As soon as we walked in, we were greeted by the hostess. She sat us down quite quickly for how busy the place was. There were a lot of options on the menu. It was a good mix between Mexican and BBQ (interesting combo but no fusion). As per all the Yelp reviews, it sounded like the Hush Puppies were a must. They were pretty tasty but I didn't see the whole hoopla about them (I would give them a 4/5).

I was super excited for my BBQ. For $9, I got brisket, pulled chicken, baked beans and fries. Unfortunately, as I started eating my food, that excitement went down. The brisket was very dry. I am used to brisket that melts in your mouth and is juicy. The pulled chicken was the same. Except for the color, you would not be able to tell apart the difference. The baked beans were quite yummy and so were the fries but it didn't cover the disappointment I had over my BBQ. 

Overall, it's a fun place to relax but if you want to go enjoy BBQ, might not be the best option.

A little history lesson: Springwater is the oldest dive bar in the state of Tennessee. It is a dive bar. If you are not looking for a dive bar experience then move on. If you are, you won't be disappointed. It doesn't get much divier than this. Springwater is located down the street from the Parthenon and can be easy to miss if you aren't looking for it. Parking can get a bit busy in this area but we always find a spot somewhere. There is a parking lot at the bar and then street parking in the area. The bar has two outside patios out front and in the back. We didn't check these out ourselves but they were decently busy on a Saturday night. There is no mistaking that this is a dive bar right when you walk in. There is a pool table in the middle of the first room and then a dart room off to the right. The bar is to the left with some bar stools. Then there is an additional small room where the stage is for live music. The stage was small and kind of tacky in such a great way. There were metallic streamers and lights for decorations. There was a $5 cover for the music but we planned on leaving before the music started so we went to the bar to order a drink. WARNING: Cash only! They have an ATM if you need it, but just come prepared. The bartender was nice and they have a decent selection of beer on tap. I was surprised I was able to get an IPA on tap. Sometimes dive bars just have the usual light beers. Prices are cheap and the beer is cold. A score in my book! They have food available if you are hungry. We didn't spend too much time here because we had somewhere to be, but I'm glad we checked it out. How cool to say you've been to the oldest bar in Tennessee?!

They didn't have sweet potato fries unfortunately but their side house salad was really good! Their regular fries were average, a little lackluster. I enjoyed the atmosphere. They have live music and if you go on Sundays at 8 you get to see Marc Allan Barnette and he is amazing! Highly recommend going to watch him. 
My husband got the brisket on biscuits which were cute and the biscuits were nice and flaky. He said it tasted good too. 
It's very dimly lit in there and the servers seems to be really busy. The other food on the menu looked really good too!

I really, really, really, really, really like this place and for so many reasons, but after eating there this afternoon, I have come to realize this place is like any other place IN THAT dependant on cook and waitstaff...   it can be a great experience or a shitty experience.  Today was a shitty experience.

But I will not hold that against Drifters. I will hold that to the staff waiting on me and cooking my burger.  they failed miserably today.

Bummer too, because today is National Hamburger Day and I had chosen Drifters to spend my hard earned money.

The music made me curious. I am not much (well, not at all) of a dive bar kind of guy. Eating at said dive bar? Forget it. But, the strains of melodic chords will pique my interest almost every time. Add to that musical curiosity, the siren's smell of smoke? Forget it. There were only so many times I could pass by Drifters without walking in.

So it came to pass on a late summer Thursday where I couldn't take any more and had to have some of what I was smelling/hearing. The dining room wasn't too crowded and football played silently on the tv for the few who were watching. I sat down and discovered that Drifters was in the middle of a drink special. Yes, please. Tonight's special was a 2 for 1 sweet tea vodka concoction. 2 boozy drinks for $5? I can do that. I came in thinking about an American Blonde and soon was fist-deep in plastic cups and cheap booze. This was starting well. 

Because I decided to go all in, I started off with a basket of fried pickles. They came to the table screaming hot and with copious amounts of ranch dressing. No, this was not a meal I could sustain on a weekly basis but as a treat... pass the grease. For my meal, I decided on the BBQ pulled chicken sandwich with a side of fries... and another side o' sauces. On every table are a basket of sauces -- 7 in all -- that will make the trip to Drifters worth your while. SEVEN! I love sauce almost as much as I love juice and strange-colored soda. This was gonna be fun. I tasted the meat on its own first to make sure there was good flavor going on. There was. If I'd had two sandwiches, I would have eaten one plain. That's how good the smoke was. Now, it was time for the sauces. I would try each I was sure of with a bite of meat and dip my fries in the ones I wasn't so sure about. My favorite (to the shock of none) was the sweet & smokey. With a molasses base, it was a forgone conclusion. The Texas & Drifters had the tangy vinegar kick that I look for, but I prefer that flavor profile with more of a texture basis (ie slaw) than meat & bun provide. Georgia had a nice, subtle heat by way of the mustard/pepper base and New Mexico kicked it up with the unabashed pepper profile. I only dabbed Sweet Fire and stayed the h#ll away from Atomic Buffalo. My colon thanked me for the wise move. And guess what happened to make this mess o' BBQ eatin' even the mo' betta: an entire set of '90s hip-hop started to play over the speaker system AND my waitress came up to my table, rapping.

Why don't I come here more often?

In the cluster of bars and restaurant in Five Points of East Nashville is a Texas style BBQ joint that doesn't disappoint. From having BBQ nachos to actually doing pretty well on their brisket game. What's also fun is the selection of BBQ sauces to please the palate of different regions so all can enjoy. 

They have 2-4-1 happy hour and a small selection of draft beers and the staff is friendly. If you want to get away from the smoky atmosphere bars, this one is a good escape and there's plenty of ample seating on the patio where they also do live music. 

I'm a fan of their drifter sandwich if you want to try a catch all. They put pulled pork and brisket topped with cole slaw for your sandwich with fries. Can't beat that if you're hungry. Also their salad serving is huge. Also a great option if you're hungry. 

It's tucked behind Beyond the Edge but it doesn't disappoint. Makes a fellow Texan happy going here.

I have stopped by three times for lunch and the food has always been awesome. Buster always comes up with a great special at a good price. The staff is always friendly and engaging. I will definitely be back!

Bummer. Would only go back here if I was 12 beers deep and in need of some not good food. I went today with customers and coworkers. I ordered wings and they came out black. And when I say black, I mean burnt. And when I say burnt I meant BURNT. Super dry. I was so pissed but just sauced then up and ate them because I was in a time crunch and didn't want to cause a scene in front of the people I was with. Super unhappy with this place. Will be a while before I ever give it another shot. May never go back. Fried pickles were alright. Other people I was with were upset with the amount of grease on their pork and brisket.

One of the best places to sit, contemplate life, watch the sun set and kick back and hang out on the internet, listen to the local gossip and just be.....
Non smoking so you smell good, when you leave.
You are greeted by name when you arrive - whether you were there the previous day, or six months ago.. you are remembered, because this bar is similar to "Cheers," where everyone knows your name!

The only thing missing is Wild Turkey Honey..
and a good menu.
I don't go to Drifter's to eat, I go there to "just be."
My neighborhood, my Cheers, my world...
And like all the other drinking establishments around the neighborhood, there is plenty of live entertainment, outside on the patio.

I'm into all kinds of music but I really like traditional country music. I moved to Nashville from NYC a little over a year ago and made the rounds looking for a bar that had decent food, a good booze selection and good music (without being a dump full of townies, bros, and drunk bachelorettes)... So that pretty much rules out any place on Lower Broadway... I find the staff at The Local to be attentive and polite, (I don't know, maybe because I'm polite to them?)... Maybe there's a difference in the patrons on different nights, so I can only vouch for the vibe on nights where they feature classic honky tonk music, usually Friday, Saturday and Sunday. On those nights The Local attracts a nice mix of regulars and some out of towners of all ages. The sound guy is great and you will be hearing world class musicians do their thing (it is Nashville, after all)... I'm not young anymore, but I quickly discovered a local scene of mostly young people who are devoted to keeping the look, sound and spirit of traditional country music alive. The crowd on these nights is really great... some older Nashville folks, some tourists, and young people all tatted up and pierced, in vintage western wear all dancing and having fun together. Good country music and good country folks! ... it's quite endearing actually... I only drink bourbon and beer and the selection is good on those... I haven't tried everything on the menu but so far what I have ordered has far been superior to run of the mill bar food... 2 thumbs waaaaay up!

Great little spot.  Great burger and nachos.  The only reason I took off a star is that their wine selection was not great but it was a good local spot to get a bite and a drink.  There was a stage but no one was playing when we went.  Good place overall .

I heart this place so much.

The movies are inexpensive and original (lots of indie flicks.) You can buy beer and popcorn. I think that's it. That's really all you need to know. You can also catch live shows and talks from time to time. Midnight Movies is cool. But I really think cheap tickets, old theater, beer, and popcorn - 'nuff said.

Just became my favorite venue to listen to live music in Nashville.  Thanks to Eron and the entire security staff for making my daughters night so special before having a major surgery next week.  It's good to know there are people like Eron and his staff and business' that still have a heart and compassion for people!!

Love the local vibe. Local musicians and song writers  this is probably one of my favorite spots in Nashville so far. Typically they have two bartenders on so you do have to order from the bar as they get quite busy but I typically sit at the bar anyway haha the food is good too!

Decent burger.. made by hand.
french fries....
cold beer.
good music.

nice little neighborhood non smoking bar......

I was here tonight to see Theory of a Deadman. I had VIP tickets and my husband and I settled in our spot right in front of the stage. I started feeling light headed and the room was spinning. Thinking it was low blood sugar I sent my husband for a sugary drink. I want to add that I had ZERO alcohol in my system so I was not drunk . As he stepped back up beside me I was passing out and fell into him. He got security and their concern for me was overwhelming and so sweet. The security guy left and brought back some juice and water and expressed to me that I should step away and sit down or get some air, but I was determined to not give up my awesome spot in the front...... I'm stubborn ‍ and I was optomistic that I would be better once the juice kicked in. He let me know that if I needed ANYTHING to let him (or one of the other security personnel that he pointed out) know. I started to feel better, but then I started getting weak, nauseated, and dizzy again after a short while so my husband led me to a sitting area where he left me to find security again. Eron came. He was so nice, very professional, very concerned, and went so far beyond what I ever expected. He called an ambulance and had two of his female security officers stay with us and help me outside when I felt able to walk out to meet the ambulance. Those ladies were also very sweet and helpful--complimenting my makeup to make me feel better and fanning me with a clipboard to cool me off. Eron checked back in with us while we waited and then I left in the ambulance. I was able to get back to the concert and see the last 4 songs AND Eron was at the entrance when I got there and had us escorted backstage! I may have missed 3/4 of the concert, but I was over the moon because of his gesture. I was greeted with a hug from one of the ladies that helped me, too. I wish I knew everyone else's names, but there are parts of the night that are fuzzy. Thank you so much to everyone for all of your help and concern. The staff here went above and beyond and are simply amazing.

I spend so much time here that I've nicknamed it my home away from home. They are doing a serious service to our community. Everything they put out is high quality. The staff is very nice. The prices are great. This place keeps me going.

If you want to be treated like absolute trash, definitely check this place out. We had an awesome, amazing time in Nashville for my husband's 40th (reviews to follow), but this place was the one and only loser of our trip.  I pre-purchaed tickets for the Sept 1 Sam Holz concert.  The bouncers/doormen/henchmen let some of us in (the females) without ID's (in San Francisco we don't go out with ID's at 40 but apparently in Nashville they're super strict so beware and bring your ID's) and denied the husbands, only to take their and our money first. They then came inside, lifted the females bodily and threw us all out when one of the husbands called them out for only requiring ID's of the men. These bouncers are the kind of guys who have no power in life so they wield whatever ounce of self-importance they can muster.  The ambiance was OK, the drinks were OK, venue would have been fine if the bouncers hadn't been so nasty and stolen our money. Love Nashville and we will be back, but I've never had a worse experience at a bar. Too bad they didn't know who we know in Nashville. If we'd had a good night they would have had a country music legend in their midst.  Be careful who you treat like waste matter, you never know! We were sure to pass along to our Nashville friends where NOT to go.

After reading raving reviews and one missed opportunity by walking into the wrong establishment (see my Batter'd Fish House review lol) I believe my expectations were just set way too high. I arrived on a mid week afternoon during happy hour and sat at the bar on a gorgeous afternoon. Drinks were 2 for 1 aka the express lane to your final destination of getting drunk af. So by the time my brisket sandwich arrived I was feeling fantastic off some local craft beers. To my surpise, the meat was unusually dry, and lacked that delicious bark brisket should have. I'm just going to mark it as I showed up too late I missed the good batch of lunch BBQ, and too early to enjoy the meat set aside for the evening rush. Their sauce selection was fantastic, housing an all time favorite of mine, a good mustard/vinegar sauce. The tangy/hot combination is the key to my heart, I swear.
There's a really cool group of locals here that give it a unique vibe and a cool sense of community that I've learned to appreciate in the Five Points neighborhood.
I look forward to giving this place another shot, I really believe it can "wow" me, but my first impression wasn't up to my standards and expectations.

One of my favorite Nashville venues! 
My main concern with this locale is parking. 

To be such an intimate place, the Staff could brush up on politeness. 

I've seen indie to rock at this legendary spot! It suits most all genres and the sound quality it great! 

Def like their FB page- they have ticket giveaways!

Mercy Lounge hosts a variety of local bands, events, and artists that are gaining popularity.  

I like Mercy Lounge but it's not my favorite place to see a show. It gets very stuffy up there, and the last time I saw a show I could smell the hipsters as soon as I walked in. It smelled musty. 

I appreciate the drink specials and smoke free atmosphere, and it's cool to be up on the second floor and have a great view of the city. I will say that you get served drinks rather quickly and they are reasonably priced. 

But there's just something about it that doesn't get me excited when I hear there is going to be a show here. The parking can be nutso, I remember when the lot outside was free and miss it. Now I have to park down the street (and once I somehow stumbled upon Third Man Records!) and it's a bit of a trek to get there. Good think I typically wear comfortable shoes to a show!

I like Mercy Lounge but it's not a venue that gets my engine running.

I like the Mercy lounge for a small venue.  The sound and lighting was respectable - which is a must to see live music.  I enjoyed that they had an outdoor patio so you could sit outside and view the Nashville sky line for a bit if you wanted.  The bathrooms were a tight squeeze, but manageable.  It did take a bit of time to get a drink, but when you're trying to serve that many people with only a few b-tenders, what else do you expect.  I was saddened in the beer selection and the fact there were no drafts on tap!  Really you're a bar for brew's sake!  So we opted for the $3.00 PBR's which I guess is a good deal if you're 21 and broke LOL.

This place blows. Took 2 hours to get our meal and that's not even an exaggeration. Did the bottomless mimosas and got served straight OJ. Would never recommend under any circumstances. Fuck this place

The final stop on our dive bar hop was Springwater. Why the hell it has taken me so long to come here I will never know. 

It's so dirty and divey that it made my heart skip a beat when I walked in - in a good way. That was love I was feeling. The first room has pool tables, characters ranging from maybe homeless to that dude might be lost, a random dog chilling in a booth, and 70s bucket bar seats lined up in front of the fairly short bar. We grabbed a seat and got us some cheap cold Miller Lites and started immediately talking to the bartender and the people around us. 

In the back room a band was playing and it is dark and loud back there. I greatly preferred listening to the band from the other room but your interest in the band may vary. There are some tvs above the bar to watch that sporting event you want to keep up with also. Bathrooms are small but definitely not the nastiest I've ever seen. Small patio too but you can smoke inside so not sure why the patio is there - perhaps for some fresh air or to watch the characters driving around centennial park at night. 

People watching is the best. The night we were there an entire wedding party came in including the bride in her white dress. A guy wearing a shirt saying "in dog beers I've only had one". A dude bruh trying to drunkenly hit on my friend but repeating himself mercilessly. It's got everything you would want. So you gotta go!

Mercy Lounge is obviously a major player in the Nashville music scene. The focus is definitely on the show - the sound quality was awesome, and the local bands were surprisingly great. Admission was a super reasonable $10. Even though the venue is serious about their music, the space and the crowd give the impression that this is just a regular hangout with no pretenses. Bartenders were responsive, always looked your way despite how busy the place was, and somehow understood what you said despite the fact that they probably couldn't hear you at all.

We did have a funny time counting the number of minorities... it totaled 5 or 6 that night, across several hours, for a packed room across a huge space. Not so great, but I do realize it's Nashville..

Worth a visit as a tourist? Yes! It's not a visit to Nashville without live music. Mercy puts on great shows that feel representative of the talent that Nashville has to offer.

Really enjoyed attending a concert at this low key venue. It was cool to see all the artist names written on the wall. The bartender told us that the place opened in the 70's so many now-famous artists have played here.

Basic place. Convenient being in our hotel. 
Service was mediocre and the food was fair. I did like the live music, especially the songwriter nights. 
Good place to grab some drinks and listen to some music if you want a relaxing night at your hotel.
Great Venue. I did get a refund for the past show that was cancelled. Thanks!!! Will see another show here.
One of my favorite hangs.  Always somewhere to sit, great live music on the weekends and I dig that they have a pong table out for people to play.

I'm a member and It's nice to have a theater in this town that shows independent movies but the headache of actually trying to get a parking spot in that tiny convoluted parking lot and end up having to pay metered parking at the lot below that does not always work and then finally getting through the 15 min concession line only to find out that they oversold the movie and there's not a single available seat left is not worth it any more. One or twice, OK but it's like this Every. Single. Weekend. My husband already cancelled his membership. I might have to, too. Not worth the stress.

I didn't really give these guys proper attention since I just stopped in on my way to the airport and got a pulled pork sandwich to go. The gal working at the bar was super nice and the roadhouse feel of the place was just fine. Ate the sandwich 2 days later but even then, I think it was the best pulled pork I ate on my zip thru Louisville, Memphis and Nashville. It wasn't all super shredded, some good chunks on a nicely grilled roll. It would have been even better in real time with some great sauce and sides. Next time.

The rudest door staff/ security I've ever encountered. Spent more time talking with each other than anything, and then ignorantly kicked out a whole group of people who had been in line to pay for merchandise since the show had ended, claiming that he'd already said something when that wasn't the case. Another staff member chimed in to accuse our group of also being racist as a joke with each other, while talking over our attempt to tell them we'd been waiting patiently with money in hand.  Bar staff also didn't seem to know what they were doing. Had to explain the description of a well known drink, and both times I received it, there was a huge difference in the amount of alcohol served... 
I can get over the long wait time to get in and the inconsistent cocktails, but the staff there has no right to talk down to it's paying customers solely out of arrogance and I will not be returning unless there is a staff change.
Security guards were so helpful and went above and beyond my handicapped sister and I!! So grateful for how wonderful our experience was !

Umm, can I get an Amen for The Local!? It is a perfect spot for a casual date, meetup with pals or solo hangout. There is absolutely no reason there should ever be an empty seat here. The happy hour specials are terrific, the peer selection is awesome and the food is top-notch (in a dive bar kind of way). Those fries are the stuff that fluffy, potato-loving dreams are made of!! 

But, in the fair Music City, I must also draw attention to the fact that this is one of my favorite places to listen to local, up-and-coming acts perform. The space is intimate, and yet with the gorgeous patio you don't feel penned in. I love that I can listen to the live tunes even if I decide to grab some fresh air outside. 

Are you coming to a Vandy game? Tailgate here! Are you seeking shelter after a sunny day at Centennial? Chill here! Are you bored with the blah food options on West End? Seek refuge in a burger here! Are you missing your college days but can't stand to go to a college bar? Grab a brew here!

Honestly, The Local checks every box!

I've seen a prior review mentioned it being in a "bad area" and I have no no no clue what they're talking about.  It's perfectly fine.  And it's within close proximity to the convention center and a less than 10 minute walk to the broadway party district.  

Very cute place.  Great servers.  But it got HOTTER THAN BLAZES by the time the show started, the A/C system is apparently not designed to keep up with the heat generated by the crowds.  

And also, I don't know how they haven't been sued b/c they have loose rugs (with no sticky backing) laying around the place and I tripped TWICE on these things that were all bunched up and almost killed myself (didn't see them with a crowd of people around me).  I don't know how someone hasn't got injured on them yet!

Most people seem to be reviewing this place for dinner and live music, but I came here for the breakfast buffet. At $11.99 for a slightly upscale continental breakfast, I wasn't impressed.

Compared to the East Coast, food in Nashville is so cheap. I can get a massive dinner for $10 in Nashville so the price for a mediocre buffet was too high. I had a bagel, bacon, eggs, pancakes, and an apple pastry. The bagel and eggs were on par with what a Quality Inn would serve on a continental breakfast. The bacon was actually quite good as were the pancakes. The apple pastry was pretty good too. But if you stay somewhere like a Hyatt Place, you will get a better breakfast, and it will be included in the room cost. 

The saving grace of this place was the wait staff. I ate at the bar, and the guy taking care of me was really friendly. The whole staff was dressed up for Halloween, which was cute. 

I wouldn't come back here for anything other than the live music, personally.

2 stars off for counter service: $8 for 2 lilliputian tamales that were about 1.5 inches short and dry as chalk in your mouth on a summer day in the Chiapas. I was told "they were good" and I'd get a decent amount. In other words.... screwed over by otherwise usually accommodating and very genuine staff.

The experiemce wasn't in line with the general brand and experience which, if consistently applied in ALL their affairs, would get the 5 stars. 

It's the little things, (apparently like their artisinal community yoga goat-crafted, gold-flake, small-batch powdery ol' tamales,) which count. And whoever's counting how much $ they make off of delivering cusomers a thing, which is ... absolutely nothing worth putting down your throat-hole.

If the profits were all going to a just cause other than the overhead of the theatre, yah, I'd be prepared. But this just felt dirty. Gritty, and dirty. In the mouthal area, sure, but also like I'd been touched funny back THERE when I wasn't looking.

Went here on a Tuesday night to see Joe Jonas and DNCE, first visit ever. We did have to wait in line as others mention but it didn't take that long at all. Inside is just an open space. It's essentially a contest of who is the rudest person in the room. People shoving and stepping on you trying to get closer to the stage. If someone tall is in front of you, too bad, you can't see at all. And yes, it was hot. But my biggest grievance is that there was a tiny section carved out by the bar for 21+. Corralled into about 1/8th of the venue, we had to stay over there to drink. Luckily for us, this is where the giant poles are located. Was this just a thing for DNCE? The 21+ area was PACKED. So I am not the only "old lady" there!
Worst LIT I've ever had. I didn't want lemonade. The music was amazing but a little light on the alcohol.smh

The diviest dive that ever dove? I think so.  Only didnt give it 5 stars, b/c you're still allowed to smoke inside -- weak.
But grab soem ribs from next doors, saddle up at the bar with a wad of cash and get you some drinking done!
This is Now called Live Oak. It's under totally new management and is Amazing. Super friendly with great food and place to watch any game. Also the patio has a putting green.

Pretty good BBQ. Drifters is half dive bar, half barbecue restaurant with a cool outside area where they feature really good musicians. I ordered brisket and it looked more like pulled pork, but I shut up and ate it and it was good lol. I enjoyed the sauce, as well, and the service was on point.
Don't go!!!! They collect a cover and the band played 1 minute of a last set. Not worth making the trip to the Gulch!!!

Great little spot with music of course. We got lucky and had multiple players doing some bluegrass. They have a nice outside patio for the warm days. Staff seemed be really engaged with the customers. Looked like they actually cared.

So, I'm old. And that makes me not love standing-only venues. But I shall write this review for the spry young folk who don't mind standing. The get great bands and have very reasonable ticket prices. Good acoustics and very good bar service. The restrooms are gnarly, but that's not what most people look for in a concert venue. Awesome cover bands on rotation - Yacht Rock Revue, The Guilty Pleasures, and My So Called Band. All rad.

I had some time to kill before checking into the room I rented, and I was in the neighborhood shopping, so I decided to stop in and see a movie at the Belcourt. If I lived in Nashville I'd probably have a membership. The staff were friendly and there's plenty of parking for patrons.
