I saw a show in the late afternoon, so there were only a dozen or two people in the theater. Prices are very reasonable, and they show a great collection of art and indie films that can be hard to find at mainstream theaters--I saw Obvious Child when I visited, and I can't even find that being shown in Chicago outside one theater. It's not a run-down place; it may not have the fancy seating that brand new theaters have, but it's perfectly comfortable. If you're visiting, have a couple hours to spare, and are in the area, check out the schedule. And if you're local, you have no excuse!

Fav place to see alt national touring bands (think Melvins, Quicksand, etc.) Love that they do not allow smoking indoors and have an outdoor patio for that - no need to shower when I get home! Bar and door staff always really friendly. Have several options in the tall-boy cheap beer category (not just PBR - yo!)
quaint theater! always have interesting/new/foreign/obscure movies! would love to be a member here!

It's 11pm. I'm fresh off 30 hours of travel, including an interminable 6hr layover in LA, and the only thing that can save my life is meat. 

And not just any meat. BBQ meat, yo! King of all the meats, emperor of char-grilled protein. Enter the Yelp app. Hulloooooo Drifters, just 1 km away. Drive, Joshy. Drive like you've never driven before old sport. 

We're almost the only ones there. We get the chilli, the hush puppies, the 1/3 rack ribs, the brisket sliders, some more brisket, the house salad with brisket dressing. The chilli ain't the best I've had, but urrthang else is freaking sensational. Gobble gobble. Brisket on the chin. Forget it, keep eating, save it for later. 

Oh, and the best part? I haven't told you this yet - the house-made sauces. Good lord, the sauces! Atomic Fire, New Mexico, Drifter, Sweet Fire . . . there's about 8 of them, and they range from sweet and smoky to vinegar and garlic-laden fire. They need to bottle these and sell them. I'd buy them all. And then resell them in my own country under my own name and make billions, muhaha!

Cat was very friendly and super helpful! A bit disappointed in the food though just for the BBQ. The fries were fucking great! I heard that Nashville is famous for there BBQ and I was highly disappointed on what we got. My friend and I both went, got BBQ sheared chicken but no sauce. So we had to choose our own and putting it on the sandwich and it ended up being super dry.

Would go again - but for the beer!

The acoustics here are terrible!!

That said, it is a nice big space and I appreciate that there is an outside sitting area with pool table.

Here from out of town and decided to try this neighborhood bar.  As someone else stated, it's perfect for a beer and some banter.  I ran into some locals as well as some other people that were visiting from out of town.  We laughed, we drank, and we played music on the TouchTunes jukebox.  The bartender was really nice and the vibe was perfect.  I cannot speak for their food but I wouldn't be afraid to dabble.  I'm sure it's like any other bar with food.  It's bar food.  Nachos, wings, and some bbq.  Anyway, the beer was good and it was a perfect pit stop after my slice at five corners.
This is a great place for live drinks and music! The draft beer was good. I wouldn't go for the food though.

Went here on a Friday night and got right in.  The happy hour drink specials were worth the trip alone!  My husband and I split the sampler and all of the meat was tasty!  We tried all of the bbq sauces and did have a favorite but can't remember its name.  I also had the banana pudding, but I wasn't a fan.  The staff was very friendly too!  I'd come back if in the area.

I love this place!!! You have to come here and meet the bartender Crystal! Best ever :)

They have good live music, lots of debauchery, and strong drinks.

You can request songs from the bands that play live, just make sure you tip!

Had a horrible experience coming into this establishment with Brooke. Took 15 min to even get acknowledged on a Sunday night. Moved into an open spot at the bar and Stephanie was amazing! Cared about our experience and checked in on multiple occasions. Made us feel welcome even when she was very busy! Thanks Stephanie!

I came here on a Sunday with some girl friends. The band was fun. However, the food and the service was less than great. We ordered chips and queso, as well as entrees. After we finished our meal we asked for our checks. Our server incorrectly split up our checks. When we pointed out the issue, she responded with "Well, what do you want me to do about it?" We helped her split everything up to the appropriate ticket. When she came back, a 20% gratuity had been added to our check. There was no mention of an auto grat on the menu. Had I been able to write in my own tip, I would have tipped her. But, not 20%.

This place is an eye catcher! 3 floors with live music and bars! I would've given this place 5 stars if it wasn't for the service that we got on the 3rd floor bar. I was with my boyfriend and his best friend, who is black. Which doesn't matter right? Then how come the two blonde bartenders served EVERYONE else around us and didn't bother to acknowledge our presence. One blonde bartender was older and wearing glasses. She was having a great time talking to two men from North Carolina who were RIGHT NEXT TO US. The other blonde bartender made drinks for people who came to the bar after us and then got on her phone and talked to the servers while we were STILL waiting patiently. When we FINALLY waved her down she gave him a smaller size drink than my boyfriends (they got the same thing) and then didn't even hand him the drink but she put it on the edge of the bar on HER side for him to reach over and grab. This is disgusting. I hate to think this happened but it did. Y'all should be ASHAMED.
Gina is the greatest bar tender I've ever had!! She served me the best Miller Lite's all night long!! Oh and she's beautiful!!!

Please read what happened to my friend at Honkey Tonk Central....absolutely awful: 
https://www.facebook.com/marshall.gregory/posts/10205989182234258?fref=nf

Well ya see now I went down to the Honky Tonk Central in good ole Nashville.  Let me tell you this place was wild as young buck lookin for a philly.  From what I can remember there was tig ole bitties bouncing around everywhere and the music was just about damn near perfect.  My one and only one complaint was there was a huge empty bottle of tequila on the bar which made me more frustrated than a dinkleberry stuck to my sole butt hair... turns out it was the damn tip jar! God bless merica

Got a pitcher of Yazoo for $15, grabbed a seat, and listened in awe to the bluegrass band of the night. A definite must stop whether you are visiting (we are from california) or a local. Great talent on stage, relaxing environment (great for a chill date or to catch up with old buddies). The sound system is really great. There was a $12 cover charge when we went on a Friday night... 100% worth it. The decor was fun too with posters of various bluegrass concerts and festivals, dim lighting, and laid back seating/tables.

This is a mandatory visit on a trip to Nashville. The first time I came was on a Saturday night and the place was completely packed. The bathroom situation was sketchy at best but it's a fun environment. I returned a couple weeks ago on a Sunday night and it was much less crowded. Go to the top floor for an awesome band and dancing experience. I will always come back to honkey tonk whenever in town.

I would venture to say that the Station Inn is the most authentic music venue in Nashville, and I just love it. This was my second time here and my second time in Nashville. 

Both times that I've been we've seen a great bluegrass band - the first time it was Fireball Mail, and this time it was Blue Mafia. Get there early for shows like this, the place fills up so quickly! Cover for both shows was around $15, cash at the door. On Sundays they have a bluegrass jam. Unfortunately they didn't have it happening when we were there last weekend, but I would have loved to go to that too. Occasionally, you'll get some famous talent stopping in as well. The Steeldrivers still play here!

They have a few local beers on tap and sell beer in pitchers, and they also have cheap delicious popcorn too!

Went today (a Saturday) between 2 and 4. Great band. Great crowd. Ordered beers from the bar on first floor. Bartender had my card for 3 min tops. I grabbed it as soon as she brought it back, even left a respectable tip. Just a few hours later I'm getting fraud alerts from my bank. Very disappointing. I won't be back. Management needs to get control of its staff.

Was there for a bachelorette party. They really made us feel special. They let us reserve a table for 16 ladies in the back room with an amazing view of the river. They held a VIP booth area for us right next to the band. The manager really helped to make this all happen as easy as possible. The only thing that I would warn you is not to get the spicy chicken unless you like your food really really hot. Over all the experience was amazing and I would defiantly come back again.

Came here for some live music yet they're not using the main stage so we can't really hear anything.  Beer is a flat 4 or 5 bucks and pitchers seemed reasonably priced.  I only had popcorn so I can't judge the food. I wasn't real happy about paying $2 for stale stuff as well.
Good buffalo wrap, nice music, it was cool to be on the 2nd floor with balconies and open windows during lunch time.
The door man was so southern and nice. We got our drinks fast and although packed you didn't have to run into people every time you chose to move. The music was good as well.

We went here for a day drink - no judgment from y'all - and it was certainly okay.  Really, just fine. For those of you from the East Coast, you know "fine" is not how you want to be described.

Now, I can't comment on food, but what I saw looked decent...the service was a little rough around the edges.  That's why this place gets two stars.  No, it wasn't crowded, and the beers on tap were plentiful, but the bartender was not paying all that much attention.  It might have been too early in the day, but there was also not any live music, nor was there any semblance of a server at the patio tables. 

The rooftop deck offered amazing views of Broadway, but from my particular visit, this was the only plus to the place.

We saw the Debbie and Doyle show at the Station Inn.  It was wonderfully politically incorrect and over-the-top. Doyle is the reincarnation of Jonathan Winters.  Debbie has captured the image of a county star which makes her blue remarks all the funnier.   I wouldn't recommend eating here but the beer and popcorn are fine.  

The show starts at 700pm but the doors must open before 6:30.  We got there at 6:30 and the place was more than half full. 

If you pull in next to The Station Inn you have access to a large parking lot on the next Avenue.

I had so much fun that I we went twice in one day. We ran the Country Music 1/2 Marathon and this seemed to be the unofficial-official after race spot! Wr had lunch there and it was the typical bar food...nothing to write home about but after a long race, who cares. The drinks were great and the atmosphere made up for the food.
We returned later that night as we were bar hopping. Had a great time!
I would definitely return next time I'm in Nashville!!

Loved this place, only been once, but it was almost a Holy experience. Coming in from Knoxville, treating my sister to a birthday concert in the form of seeing Chris Whitley live.  I'm a huge Chris Whitley fan and saw him years back kill it at a show in St. Louis. On the way into town, my sister's car broke down, but we still made it to the show. What could have been an awful experience turned into a great one because everybody we encountered took good care of us and displayed true hospitality, patrons and staff alike. This is a small, intimate venue for serious music lovers. I didn't know this at the time, but Chris Whitley was dying from lung cancer and would pass away only a few months later. This place has, or at least had soul the last time I was there. Gotta hit it up again soon!

While on a visit from Colorado, we weren't sure what to do during the holiday weekend so thank you Tennesse Tourism for advertising the event!

Normally a free show but we sprung the extra clams for the VIP experience.  It was worth it to have on the rail access to the entertainment, catered dining under tents and the air conditioned port-a-potties was a special touch!  Lol. Honestly a good time despite not knowing many of the bands or their hits (no spandex here tonite!) 

Only thing missing are booths offering local artisan wares for sale.  That would be awesome!

Definitely Lyft or Uber as the traffic is insane when the music is done.  Safer and oh so convenient!
Saw Seether here, and the venue was amazing!  The atmosphere was breathtaking and the sound was wonderful!  A totally great venue! Way worth it.

If you want to be in the heart of Broadway and hear some awesome live music at any time of day on any day of the week, go here. At night, they will have 3 live bands going on 3 floors. You can walk to the river from here and be in the heart of the action.

This place is massive. Bartenders are fast, lots of hot people dancing and going on stage with the band and the music is always good. They leave the doors open so you can hear it from the street.

The best part is the balcony overlooking Broadway where you can drink and people watch. Huge windows overlooking every corner of the street. Some of the balconies have a background of brick walls from the building across the way and with the wind blowing and the music going, that feels pretty nice. Not many places, if any, on Broadway that have that.
Wanna get drunk? Wanna see bachelorette parties and listen to good music? Wanna do that on three different floors over looking broadway? You've got your spot.
Live original music. No  smoking. Cold beer. No cover. Be sure to thank  rocky the owner for having a venue for upcoming writers and singers

Walked in w a group of 5. Got carded. Walked up to the bar. Got carded again.  Went to a different bar in the same restaurant.  Got our drinks.  As we were sitting at our table, we got randomly carded for no reason AGAIN! At that point, I'm out. I'm not going to profiled(and I don't need explain WHY)) anymore today.  Never going here again

Great time!!  First floor was just too packed.  We partied on the second floor.  The band was great!
Would definitely go again.

I'm an out-of-towner who dropped in for the Sunday Night Bluegrass Jam. Based on the crowd there, I don't think they really need one more 5-star review to draw more audience, but I'll give them one anyway.

The place was actually surprisingly comfortable - lots of chairs, cool, no unpleasant smells like some of the classic old-time venues have.

The music was excellent, and seemed to get even better as the evening went on and various musicians came and went. They were already jamming before 8:00 when I got there and didn't stop til after 11:00.

If you are really there to hear the music, I would recommend getting there early and finding a spot close to the musicians. There are no microphones for the bluegrass jam and with a lot of chatter in the audience, it is hard to hear the music if you are sitting halfway back or all the way in the back.

Great atmosphere, great drinks and snacks. My favorite is the "thing of popcorn." We went in a Sunday night for the Bluegrass Jam. It was relaxing and fun. Everybody just piles in and enjoys the music and company.

Dammm !!! So much Fun. 

Country on Steroids X 10. 

Honk Tonk is way cool and a Bad Ass Hang Out. 

I loved it 1st time here and super fun nothing like Los Angeles, it all Country. 

Can't wait to come back. 

A lot of fun and a lot of people.

Very cool set up. It is 3 floors with a different band playing on each floor. We sat on the top floor because it was the least crowded, our waiter was on top of everything, always asking if we wanted refills before we ran dry.

What a gorgeous bar. The live music talent on Thursday night was seriously incredible. 

Reason for the rating: Since when do you serve 12 year old scotch in a plastic Dixie cup? For such an aesthetically appealing place, how in the world could that be how the owner would want customers to experience a "nicer" establishment? The orange slices on our $10 old fashioned's were so old that they were covered with a white "old bar fruit" slime. We found it completely bizarre but it is indicative of why the bars surrounding this one are packed to the brim with people while Famous had us and only us there. It was so awkward that we weren't quite sure how to leave without openly offending the workers. 

There's a reason you're not doing the business you feel your upscale bar should be doing... it's all in the details that aren't being executed by the bar staff.

Decent music and bar service.  Almost empty bar and stage which is odd for a bar this close to broadway, might have something to do with the horrible bouncers.  If you are sitting on the couches, please keep your feet on the floor vs tucked under your legs with boots on the seat, its HIGHLY frowned upon!!!

Great venue. Acoustics are incredible here. For everyone complaining about the drink prices -- use your brain. The domestic beers are $11.00 for a 25 oz. beer and $13 for Import/Premium. Which means you're getting two beers at $5.50/6.50 a piece. Which is pretty average for any bar or venue on Broadway, especially a nice, new venue located directly on the water at the end of Broadway like Ascend. Were you expecting $5.00 tall boys? Let's be realistic with our expectations here, folks. 

I do agree with the coordination and logistics of some of the tents/food trucks though. I would imagine those are some of the kinks that will be worked out over time. 

The grounds are incredibly nice. I appreciate the security presence coming in. I do think the removing of your water bottle cap if purchased is a tad overboard. 

All in all, a wonderful venue.

Loved this place! Even on a Sunday night this place was busy. They closed off the second level but the band playing with the brunette hottie lead singer was so much fun. My cousin, his girlfriend and I were tired but wanted to experience Nashville's downtown and honky tonks. "Oh, we'll go for an hour for a drink and head home." We didn't get home until past 3 am, with a stop at a Waffle House.

The bar was long in the center of the room and drinks were cheap. The bartendress gave us nice shots of Fireball and worked that bottle opener almost as well I do. ;) It was funny to be one of two Asian girls in the whole joint. Well this one genuinely loves country so I prefer this over any hip hop club in the Bay Area.

The game plan after this spot was to get a drink at every spot that had a band. I did not know that EVERY spot would have a band. OMG, it was an awesome night and Honky Tonk Central kicked it off for us. SO much fun.

If you are looking for a great dive bar with a local Nashville flair, this one is work checking out. The servers are friendly and the beer is cold. Check out their events as they always seem to have something going on.
The lunch was excellent, drinks, chicken tenders and salad.! The music was two guitar players that were fantastic

Three levels of bar and live music? I had a great time! When we went the second floor was closed for a private party, but we perused the packed first floor and the moderately packed third floor. The band was good, the drinks were reasonable- I'd go back, and I've already recommended to a friend who was in town visiting!

One of the better and more lively bars on Broadway. It is at least 3 stories with some outdoor areas and balconies on the 2nd and 3rd floors. 

It's not the cleanest place, but it's downtown bar central so it's to be expected. 

Live music, gets rowdy on the weekends. Much calmer during the week. 

I think this places draws a younger crowd than some of the other bars in the area.

On our first visit to Nashville we stopped at the Honky Tonk for a drink and we decided to stay a little longer because the vibe was great!! Tom Bridges and his band was playing and they incorporate the crowd like no other band I seen. It's great for all ages!! The bartenders are great. We spent a week in Nashville and we kept on going to this place because it was a great time no matter what day of the week.
Good music and a fun place. First time in. Big place. Lots of people. I for sure will be back.

Bushwackers!
So, I was introduced to these at a BBQ place in Auburn, AL after a football game one Saturday. Alcoholic milkshake, basically. And on a hot Nashville day, who doesn't want that. Every time we saw a place that sold them, we stopped & got a couple to cool down. 

Also, I got mistaken for someone that worked there. A lady came in, on my way back from the rest room, and she stopped to ask if I mind if their party (at least 15 people) could push some tables together. I said sure & walked-off, didn't bother me any. Hope it didn't create any trouble:p

Great dive bar feel with live music.  Going to The Stillery next door for dinner but the music pulled us in here first. Bartender was wonderful and the drinks were good.  If I lived in Nashville I would hang out here.

Great bar!  Kinda speak-easy like!  Down an alley off the main street!  Great atmosphere and excellent service!  So happy we accidentally found this place!  Didn't try the food, but the bar service was beyond reproach!  Will definitely be back when we come to Nashville!

The corner location and volume here draw the crowds, but the restroom attendants and urinals where your shoulders touch your neighbors' sent us on our way almost as soon as we entered. Much more of a 20-something college-town bar, hence the gimmicky, misleading name I suppose..

This festival is always a great end to the summer. There is usually always a good headliner. I like the addition of beers and bars. It ups the ante a little bit. This time of year isn't the hottest at night so it makes for a pleasurable experience. I'll never forgive myself for missing the Alabama Shakes but I most certainly will be returning each year to enjoy this part of Nashville.

Good god this is a HUGE multilevel bar with fantastic people watching.  Bar service is very good even when it gets crowded.  Fun live music.  The beverage list isn't very big and beer is only served in bottles.  Even during daytime hours you will find a good age distribution in this bar and a bunch of people drinking and having a good time, listening and dancing to live music.

We went in here to get some relief from the scorching temperatures outside and get some water. We sat near the back and ordered water. There was a man in the restroom handing out soap and paper towels for tips, which I find extremely annoying but paid him anyway because he's probably struggling. Our waitress came up and asked us if we wanted to order anything, but we told her we were fine. She then came up again and showed us the menu as if we had to purchase something even though the place wasn't nearly full at 11:00am on a Thursday. Finally, so she'd leave us alone, we ordered a Jack & Coke on her third attempt. It was in a 6 oz plastic cup and it cost us $10. This place is kind of a joke if you just want to get water and listen to music. Be ready to spend your money.
Really good place, but the property is going to be redeveloped soon. Go there quickly if you want to give it a try.

This was one of the recommended places to go to in Nashville.  It is a great time: 3 floors of bands, bars, dancing, fun. With that said, it definitely gets crowded.  We went here on a Sat night, and it was packed on all floors. 

The girl's bathrooms were filthy esp by the end of the night (you know what kind of filth).  The bands they had were great and got people to dance.  I was a little scared for my life bc when we were on the 2nd and 3rd floors' dance area, the floor shook when someone jumped much more when everyone was jumping.  It's probably the norm here.  Also be careful of the balcony.

It took awhile to get drinks.  I was just glad they had my sweet tea vodka and unlike any other bars in other states, I didn't get a strange look for it.  I would recommend to go if it's your first time, but be warned if you care about sticky floors and tables and bathrooms.
Super fun place with GREAT music!  Server Chris was so awesome!  Nice and super attentive!  Love this place!

I took off one star because I had to walk down a cave to find the restroom. Other than that, this place is nice for big events. The closest parking we found ($8 before 8 AM) was at Printers Valley, which I don't recommend because it reeked of urine smell and dark. There might be closer and cleaner parking around, but we were too lazy to drive around at 7 in the morning.

2013/#1
Hands down, the best stop in Nashville! Band is high energy, bar has a good layout & is centrally located! The life of the partay!!!
They had the Warriors game on!! Winning in Nashville. :) drinks were reasonable and you can't beat 3 stories.
Great place to go listen to music. Three levels of bars with each level having a different love band. Prices on beer is pricey at 4.00 a bottle for bud light. I would go back again.
Stop here every time in Nashville. Whoever is playing here is better than the last. Little dive bar away from the chaos of Broadway

The live music is what really makes this place. It's a great dive bar that serves bar food. We were looking for somewhere low key to enjoy some music while we ate dinner, this place hit the spot.

When we went, they were out of pretzels for the appetizers so we ended up with the egg rolls. Best happy accident ever, order them - you won't regret it!

My husband tied to order the rib sandwich but they were out of ribs, so we both ended up with the pulled pork sandwiches. They were good, but I wish it didn't come with the sauce already on it. I prefer to have control over how much BBQ goes on my sandwiches. I think the sauce was a bit overpowering. However, it was decent and I left full and happy.

The atmosphere is what makes this place fun, the server was also great. Great low key place for a quick no-frills bite.

I am rating as a 3 star only for the fact that our service was horrible (see below for reason). As for the atmosphere and the food they were great. We sat on the roof top (up the stairs after elevator ride) and had the chicken sliders with Nashville fries and they were so good. I would definitely go back again and hopefully will get better service. 

As for the service we went to have brunch with friends (roughly 13) and it took a little bit to get our orders in which is understandable, but after we ordered my girlfriend never got her first drink and we were completely done eating before the waitress came back to ask if we wanted another round. We let her know she never brought the first out more than once and we ended up getting one beer after 2hrs. When we went to get our check she had rung up 3 beers on our check (which she took off after we reminded her she only brought one). Hopefully our next time will be a better experience.

Two words: Pokémon and Symphony. My childhood loves came together tonight at Ascend Amphitheater in beautiful harmony. The venue was clean, organized and the staff were helpful and friendly. The sound and lights were top notch and so was the reserved seating. Concessions were a little pricey but I had Ben and Jerry's for $8 which really wasn't too bad. This was my first time at the venue and I'll be returning.

Disgraceful place. 
Ordered a vodka by 215 am, was obliged to throw it by 2:30 am.. the place closes by 2:30 instead of 3 am.. be aware. Bouncers and servers have the worst attitude. Our party got several drinks vodka, whiskey and rum, bad quality all of them..

No drink specials,  but a wonderful atmosphere and an extremely talented live band.  I wouldn't mind paying so much for drinks if the band got a cut,  but you are supposed to tip them on top of drinks. Pricy,  but a good time and seemingly a staple of Nashville. I loved loved loved the songs the bands played. Very hot country songs.
This place is shit, waited for 20 minutes to get a drink, and was completely ignored. Never come here

I love this place, its huge 3 floors  that open up to the outside.  Each floor has a band playing and of course a bar for those drinks.  When I went we sat down on each floor for awhile had a drink and enjoyed the music!  Its especially nice if you can get a seat along the outside wall thats opened up to outside, great view of the street and all the happenings outside,  which is a show in itself!
Three floors of bands and bars.  It is a destination.  If you don't like the bar or band where you are, go up or down a floor.

Quite possibly the best bar in all of Nashville. The staff and the regulars are welcoming and helpful. It's on music row so there are always songwriters in house and they frequently break out in original songs. The beer is cold and affordable. What's not to love!?!?
Close to our hotel, so fun and packed with great people and wonderful music. My friend attempted to sing on stage every night we went :)

If you visit only one place on Broadway, make it this one! The service is amazing in spite (despite?) the crowds. Everyone was super friendly; sharing tables due the size of the crowd was fun. The music was outstanding and really made you feel like you were in the middle of the C&W experience. This is a gem and not to be missed.

Came to Nashville on our honeymoon and after walking around all day we were in desperate need of some lunch! We walked past several bars but we liked the look of this one with the balconies and we liked the song the band was playing so we went in. Very happy we did!!! Made our way up to the third floor which was a little less busy and it was a nice day out so all the windows were open...definitely a plus for us, who had just fled a snowstorm up here in Boston!! Bartenders were nice and quick with drinks. Looked at a menu and decided on a couple of sandwiches. Bartender was completely honest (which I appreciate) saying that the kitchen was very busy and it may take a little longer than usual. We had cocktails, live music and sun...waiting a little longer wasn't an issue for us! At about the 25 minute the bartender came over and repeatedly apologized as the meal I had ordered had been 86'd... Still no issue for me, I was torn between 2 sandwiches anyways so I ordered my backup. 5 minutes later, the food was out- it was hot and delicious! We had such a nice stop here! I definitely recommend making this a stop if you're ever in the area!!

One of the most authentic-feeling places I've ever spent time in. The vibe is true Bluegrass. I used to go to the jams on Sunday's all the time. Amazing. Space is limited so get there early, and the only food they have is popcorn and pizza.

Hmm..not much to like about this place. The seating is so uncomfortable especially for how long the show is. Another point on the seating...we only had the small high top tables to choose from, and we had a party of 6. We were pushing the two tiny tables together, and this punk waiter said we couldn't do that... unbelievable!!! We moved to another section and moved tables together. The food... mediocre..don't get the turkey sandwich. My friends had patty melts and said they were ok. Fried pickles were pretty good but so expensive. Just robbery, about $9 for 5 fried pickles..why should pickles be more than onion rings and the same price as sandwiches? As for the service...everything took a half hour to an hour. The waiter was such an ass. He was flirting with all the girls at the two end tables (Hurley shirt, brown hair, has a kid named Maverick--I know this because he pulled out his phone and was showing the girls his kids and they were flirting even more after that). So, he was ignoring us the whole time...couldn't even get a water or a box for an hour!!! Would never return.

I was really enjoying the place until this cock diesel looking trash guy shoved his trash can into me thinking that I was drunk.  I did not argue with him & kept on walking.  As a business owner, who is in the service industry,  I would say that it's the illiterates like him that can shove your business down the drain, not knowing what it's like to serve people.

I love live music, I absolutely love Nashville. This place is awesome they have live music all the time (THE MUSIC IS GREAT) and they also have raspberry WOODCHUCK CIDER on tap, that's like finding a tugboat at the airport. The staff is great and friendly

Surprising! 

We waited too long and couldn't find any local restaurants without a 40 min wait. Stumbled upon Nashville Underground and couldn't have been more pleased. The fried green tomatoes and the honey roasted brussels sprouts with pecans were addictive. 

I've had Nashville's hot chicken many times before and wanted to do something less likely to give me heartburn.  The Broadway BBQ chicken was suggested.  I paired it with the Truffle Mac and Cheese and again, I was pleasantly surprised. The juicy bbq flavoring left me wishing I had ordered my  very own versus sharing it! 

Will definitely try more on the menu next time I come to town!
Not bad for bar fare.  You really go for the atmosphere anyway.  Will say though, the wait staff leaves a lot to be desired.
Ohhhhh the bands today were awesome! Food was good. Bartenders were super on it without being pesky (we are not much of a drinker). What a FUN HAPPY place! You must go.
3 floors of live music...shoulder to shoulder..if you can handle the crowd, this is a great place. Very cool to look out over the patios here down over broadway.

This place is awesome!!!!! I had so much fun!! The band that was performing was so good, and fun! They kept the crowd dancing! It's such a cool and fun bar to go to if you are in Nashville! I will be going back, because I had a fun time. I had to buy a hat!! Thanks Honky Tonk Central for a fun time!! You guys are awesome!

This was one of our favorite places on a recent girls trip to Nashville. Great venue for live music. We went on a Sunday night when they air the show live for radio. A local recommended it to us when we said we wanted to hear good bands playing their own music. Sean McConnel was main act the night we were there and did not disappoint.

We dropped in here during a recent trip to Nashville.  What an awesome place to drink a few Beers and listen to music.  I know there's 100's of these joints around town, but this was around the corner from our hotel and was a ton of fun.  There were multiple levels, I think at least 3 maybe 4, I can't remember exactly.  The band on the main floor was a ton of fun.

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ZhA88ILcgEP9DNwZDx7f0A?select=So23CpKLJ7aYIlj3Bwxrfg#So23CpKLJ7aYIlj3Bwxrfg
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ZhA88ILcgEP9DNwZDx7f0A?select=OYjeqpbup17ahf9Z1DullQ#OYjeqpbup17ahf9Z1DullQ

The girl playing the Violin was awesome.  She jammed and had the place on their feet all night long.  It's too bad I can't remember the name of the band....funny thing is that one of the guys in the band playing the night we were here was playing at one of the bars in the airport when we left the next day...awesome, that's why I love Nashville.

Return Factor - 80%
First time to visit this place. Very impressive atmosphere with great service, music, and food! Definitely would recommend this venue to anyone who visits or lives here!

Bartender heather was horrible!!  No smile slow service!  You can look good behind the bar but service should match!!!! 
Live music was nice but didn't say because of service!! Two thumbs down!!!!
Hit this place up before the NCAA tournament games. Live music was great and the bartenders were on top of it despite the large crowd.

Very nice, new venue.  Staff was super polite, as was security.  Plenty of (expensive) food and beverage options.  We were seated promptly for our show (Flight of the Conchords).

The seating seems to be severely flawed however.  The stage is so high up, that sitting close isn't really worth it.  The act generally sits 6-8 feet back on the stage, and the seats begin about 6-8 feet FROM the stage.  We sat in the third row, and it felt like sitting in the 13th row.  We could only see the top half of the act.  Felt like the stage should be lower, and the seating more on an incline.

With the venue being outdoors, if you aren't in the first 4 or so rows and it rains, you're gonna get soaked.  It started getting really windy during our show, and all the cloth covers on stage were blowing wildly (revealing all the techs and computers working the magic), as were the speakers hung with cables above our heads.  I trust the engineering to a point, but I must say I was pretty nervous as the GIGANTIC speakers were swaying about 20 feet above my head.

It's a decent venue - nice because it's new, but lame because it's an outdoor  stage with a lawn and folding chairs.  Would much rather see a show at the Ryman, TPAC, or even the Bridgestone Arena.

A night at the symphony at the lovely Ascend. As always facilities are well maintained, the drinks are cold, and the entertainment never disappoints. It is truly a pleasure watching our local Nashville symphony outside on a beautiful Middle Tennessee evening.

I was in this bar Sunday December 28 th early evening. It took awhile to post this because I just signed up for yelp! Ok, the bar was great and I was enjoying the country music until the band started playing rock from the 90's. I like some of that but not in a Honkey tonk. The singer said he would play any request for 20$ so I grabbed a 20$ and asked for Hank Williams jr. I was told by this "country band" that they didn't know any Bocephus WOW!! I then went back with my 20$ and asked for Johnny Cash, he rolled his eyes at me and played it! Next I went with another 20$ and asked to hear east bound and down ( just sang it the whole way to Nashville being silly) and the singer wouldn't sing it so he walked off and the band played it without the singer!! Lesson learned, not all "country" musicians care to play the songs by artists that paved the way for them, even if you pay them!

One of the main bars on Broadway where they have 3 floors and 3 different bands playing. The bar gets VERY overcrowded and mainly had a very young crowd. The beer selection had regular beers, nothing crafty. The bathroom lines are also a nightmare. It was fun to pass by just to say you went to Honkey Tonk Central, but definitely keep it moving to the next bar if you want to avoid amateur hour with all of the 21 year olds.

I want to give you 5 stars but tonight was so much different than before.  We always get really prompt service and tonight we saw so many tables with food and we didn't get our food till show started and we were the 5th group in the door!!! The music was awesome.  When I return I will probably eat at home and sit in balcony.  This was my first time sitting in lower area and I did not find it enjoyable.  Our waitress was either under trained or over booked with tables. It took forever to get in our food order and the almost an hour to get our food.  That is not our previous experience!  If I had dinner I might not be upset but since I waited a. hour to be there when doors opened at 6pm I assumed I would be served promptly. All our other times this has been the experience so I don't know if it is where I sat or who served us. I enjoyed the music so much.  I would have enjoyed it much more with some food.

This is an ok place to hear music, but it's so incredibly hot and uncomfortable. I find it pretty insulating to your guests when you know you have a problem- which our waitress acknowledged at the beginning of our evening- and choose to do nothing about it.  Seating is extremely limited at this place anyway, but if you want to stay under 90 degrees, do NOT sit upstairs. The whole place is under air conditioned, but upstairs is a sauna. Also if you don't get there as the doors open, they won't even have a bar stool available for you.  They move them all away so you have to stand through the show.
This place is really depraved. This is the worst broadway bar. It is jammed pack and sometimes it is dangerous on the third floor. I watched some american idol person here and it wasn't that good.
This place simply blew my mind. 3 stories tall and live music on every level. Had a great time, next time in Nashville, I'll be back!!!

5 star venue !  This is one of the nicest and most fun bars I have ever visited.  The hospitality was off the charts fantastic as well.  If you are looking for a private event space in Nashville , look at this venue!! It's fantastic.  Best rooftop in the city, overlooking the stadium and the river.  Mae will treat you right !!
Lindsey M was just the BIGGEST bitch to us! Just trying to buy a t shirt Lindsey... Calm down and get a new attitude.

I was glad that we wondered into this restaurant. I had the Strawberry salad, perfectly fresh and a beautiful blend of ingredients. Also tried a Music City Mimosa, which I loved, but thought was a bit pricy at $12. My husband had a burger, and he enjoyed it as well. The entertainment was great, both artists we saw had wonderful voices, and I loved that you could listen but they weren't so loud that you couldn't still have a conversation.

This review is coming with the caveat that we're extremely spoiled in Nashville when it comes to concerts and venues, and I completely admit that. With that being said, I do appreciate Ascend for the outdoor venue space that has been sorely missing since Starwood. 
I've purchased tickets in both the lower level and sat in the lawn, and the sound is infinitely better in the lower level. Like most of new Nashville, drinks are expensive and traffic is a beast so just go expecting that as the norm when venturing out. However, what caused the 3 stars instead of 4 is the ridiculously strict rules around the middle walkway. I completely understand not wanting people standing in this area when the main act is on the stage, but I was scolded and told I was not allowed to stand (very off to the side and out of traffic) in the walkway for an opening band that I was watching. It was very obnoxious and frustrating. 
If you have lawn seats, you have the option to bring chairs and I recommend doing that unless you are willing to pay the rental fee. I sat on the hard ground at the last show I attended and it was very uncomfortable. 
I also give them props for bringing a wide variety of concerts here; from the symphony to hard rock, they have an eclectic lineup!

Went here on the Fourth of July to listen to the symphony and watch the fireworks. The venue is really nice, and we had a good view of the fireworks. We could hear the symphony well from the lawn area. So why didn't it get 5 stars? One word: $5 water. OK, maybe that's two words. Or one word, a number, and a symbol, but I'm thoroughly ticked off. Out on the street, vendors were selling water for $1 to $3. Here it was $5 at the concession stand and $7.50 at a cart. For $7.50 I'd expect it to include a haircut or a hamburger or something, but no. There was a taco truck at the back, but they were forbidden to sell water. And no, you can't bring in your own water from the outside. Nice venue, but I'll only go in the dead of winter so I won't die of thirst.

Great Nashville bar with good music! It's 3 stories which makes it easy to jump back and forth to listen to the different bands. There are also nice balconies to look out of Broadway and take a break from dancing. Would definitely come back.

We had a great time here. Location is just around the corner from Broadway and is a mix of locals and tourists. The manager there this Saturday was in a great mood, keeping the patrons happy, and checking in often with the new bouncer(doing his job well too). Drinks and bar food was right on, and the band playing til 10pm was entertaining. The tables on the sidewalk are a great place to hang out, and are rare in that part of town..look forward to coming back.

The only thing I didn't like about the Station Inn was that we didn't get here until our last night.

We loved everything about this little room, the band was spectacular, the $12 cover was dirt cheap considering the quality of the band... it was really special to see 6 pro players just ripping through some standards late into the Tuesday night.

We didn't have any of the food, I don't think that is why people come here. The beer was affordable and cold... all-in-all, 10 stars.

Great place!  We stayed on the first level, LOVED the band that was playing.  Pretty crowded but a fun place to have a drink.  I didn't order food but it looked like they had typical bar type food (burgers, wings, fries, etc).  Drinks were a little pricey but hey, it's downtown Nashville.  Except for one bartender, the rest needed to get the sticks out of their asses.  Not friendly at all, no smile, no "hi, how are you"....nothing.  Just a "what can I get you" with a crappy look on their faces.  I would definitely come back to check out the second and third floors.

Worst place I've been to in quite a while. Perhaps my expectations were skewed given the excellent alternatives. I went with my girlfriend to enjoy some music after a long week of work. 

Overpriced drinks, including one awful rum and coke.....unable to describe what it tasted like as I've never tasted a drink so bad. Not sure what brand of rum they use but it sure ain't rum. Music was average at best.

Also beware although it advertises that it closes at 3am, it closes well before that. I got served a drink at 235am, by 240am I had the most obnoxious, overzealous bouncers pushing me out the door telling me that i had to leave the drink. To make matters worse, I was completely sober and was only starting my 3rd drink. A member of the Nashville police department grabbed my beer and threw it in the rubbish bin, followed by one of the obnoxious bouncers throwing me aggressively out the door. I have not experienced anything like that before. Suppose it's an indictment of the trajectory our police department at Nashville is going in. I'm sure he enjoyed plenty of drinks after hours for his sterling service.

In summary, woeful drinks, terrible staff, brutish door staff and average music.....I would advise to stay well away from this sorry establishment. There are far more attractive propositions in the offing in the great city of Nashville.

Alley Taps is nestled on the lesser (by A large margin as there is nothing else there) traveled side of Printers Alley.  You wouldn't even know its there if there wasn't a sign standing outside the place.  Inside it's actually about 3x larger and a lot nicer than expected.  I did it eat there, but it looks like it's more of a drinking spot than eating spot.  I'm definitely not demeaning their food as I didn't see it.  There are several seating areas, tv's, and lots of bar seating.  At 3pm they have 2-4's.  They actually pour an excellent Guinness.  They have have live bands everyday after 5pm.  This place hasn't blown up yet, but it definitely could with their offering coupled with the new hotels that are popping up.  At its present state this is a great place to come without the tourist clutter downtown.  If they get the tourist good for them.

Not bad.  Only the first floor had live music, but as it was too crowded and hot we went to the third floor.  It had a nice view of Broadway, but piped in music rather than letting us hear the love music on the first floor. Nothing was on tap, no happy hour, and the drinks were overpriced. The bartender was very helpful.

Great atmosphere, beers, and a great lineup of musicians. Good for interacting with the entertainment, intimate, and you can still talk to the people you're there with. 
They'd do even better with more food selections.

Pulled pork and Nashville hot chicken were both very good. Normally things like slaw are just a throw-in, but the pickles and slaw here were very good. Service is good especially given they just recently opened.
The best addition to Nashville in the last 20 years. Perfect blend of the beautiful weather and music with intimate lighting and sound. A perfect 10.  Thank you

Followed the Yelp reviews to this gem just a block from our hotel. Got here on our first day for happy hour (2-7pm) where they have 2 for 1's. It was an awesome start to our evening. Great mix of friendly locals and travelers looking to avoid Broadway. Came back tonight- great live music. Easy vibe. Perfect way to start and finish our time in Nashville. Will tell everyone I know to stop by here. We'll be back.
Lots of fun. Even if you don't like country music!

Been here a few times to see the Time Jumpers (q.v.). and Tim Akers' Smoking Section (q.v.) There was food and booze. The music was so good I can't remember what I ate or drank, but I remember it didn't suck, in fact I think I thought it was pretty good. Seating is way tight, but again, no tighter than seats at any concert hall. What I remember distinctly is that I had a rollicking good time each time I was here, and I can't wait to get back. When in Nashville, put this place on your list. It's as good as it gets.

This bar has three levels- all with outside decks which is pretty nice. Live music on each floor as well. I will say that I have watched them turn a lot of people away so avoid this place if you have a fake id . It's not my favorite on Broadway but definitely worth stopping in for a drink.

If you go this bar you probably a tourist b/c that is the only reason I can think that you would pay $5 a beer and wait 10 mins for a drink when there are bars with $6 pitchers and 2 dollar drinks less than a block away.

We arrived in Nashville late Sunday night and headed straight for the Station Inn and the weekly bluegrass jam. It was a lovely, intimate experience with a great sense of community. A very chill, comfortable spot that will give you a bit more of the locals experience.
My coworkers and I ventured here for a drink on a Thursday night. We went to the top level, which had a nice view of Broadway, and the musicians upstairs were good!
, An awesome upscale nightclub with amazing R and B mix by some really talented D j's.

This was my second time visiting Honky Tonk. We stopped in for "a drink" and ended up staying for hours. The bartenders were very friendly and we never had any trouble getting a drink, even when it became super packed later in the day. Best grilled chicken sandwich I've ever had in my life! Atmosphere was wonderful, too. It was hard to leave. We will definitely be back!

This place isn't fancy at all but the people were very nice. The music was unbelievable which is why we were here. We were only in town for 3 days but ended up going here twice. The music was much better than anywhere on Broadway. Don't let the unassuming looks of the place turn you off. If you like bluegrass then this is the place to be!

Pretty fun bar that on many nights has three floors of entertainment with open balconies that let you watch the drunks make their way down Broadway, just be sure to bring small change.

The reason for the two star rating is that during my last two visits, two different bartenders tried to scam me. The first was a classic over-charge on my credit card which the bartender said her manager would have to correct and she had no idea where he was so I could "either sign it or wait like twenty minutes." The second instance I paid cash and the bartender never brought back my change ($20 for a single beer.) Ten minutes later I was able to get her attention and she said she had assumed it was tip, then tried to bring the wrong change. Another patron caught this happening to his very drunk friend while we were standing at the bar. 

The moral of this story is of course if you are a bartender here who is going to scam people, make sure those persons are so drunk they can't feel feelings... Let alone count change.

Great venue! I've seen several bands play and they always sound great! I love the chicken wings! My only wish is that they'd have assigned seats! It's a real drag having to get there an hour or more before the doors even open to stand in line outside to get a seat. I'd pay a little extra to have an assigned seat!

Honky Tonk Central is my favorite bar to visit on Broadway. We always make it a point to go whenever we are in Nashville. I love that it features different bands on all three floors, so you can find whatever fits your mood. If you don't like what is going on on one floor--move along to the next! Each floor also has a bar, tables, and dancing area. I like to get my drink and stand on the patio on the 2nd or 3rd floor to people-watch the characters walking up and down Broadway!
Incredible musical experience. Intimate atmosphere that feels like sitting with friends. The focus is certainly the music and the music is worth every penny. I could have stayed all night.

I love this place. My favorite place in Nashville. But watch your tab closely. I have on multiple occasions been charged for things I never had or ordered. They have charged me for my whole friends tab after he paid cash for it and then they pretended not to be able to find the receipt. Whether it's confusion by the staff or an intentional way to attempt to take advantage of customers doesn't matter. It needs to be fixed and addressed! I'll be watching like a hawk from now on.

What an awesome venue!! We saw Sam Hunt and had assigned seats. They were great! There is enough leg room that people are able to walk by without you having to stand up every time. Drinks and food were pricey, but that's to be expected. It's a much smaller venue than what we are used too, we loved it!

This was a pretty cool place to go to in Seattle. A guy at another bar called it "Roofy central" lol, but it was still fun and packed. There seemed to be a few bachelorette parties going on, which is always fun. People are able to ride the bull in the bar and it was pretty entertaining watching people fall off. The drink prices were reasonable and the service was just good enough to not get made. I would recommend stopping in if you are looking for a little bit of a younger crowd, dancing, and good music.
Stayed in Nashville for 5 days and thought that the Honky Tonk had the best atmosphere and talent!

What I remember about Benchmark is not the band or the beer selection or seating, but the bathrooms. This place had by far the oddest bathroom stalls I've ever encountered. That being said, they were clean and had more than one in the bathroom. Helpful things. 

Also helpful was the giant container of water available for hydration. As a local told my friends and I, "Everyone comes to Nashville thinking they can out drink it. They're wrong, all wrong."

Stay thirsty, friends. This place is A-OK to quench your thirst, alcoholic and non.
Very good food and drinks. We enjoyed the music. Very fast and friendly service. We would definitely come back.

The plates were a little on the small side! But the band was so amazing! Not sure how I felt about the Mac and cheese or corn bread but the fried tomatoes were to die for! Our server was very sweet and took good care of us. The venue itself was really nice and had a great feel to it!

Coolest/most fun bar I have ever been to. Every level of this bar was great and offered something f different from the other levels. I had an amazing time and stayed until closing because the music was great and the drinks were good!

Do not miss the Time Jumpers if you are in Nashville on a Monday night, when they play at 3rd and Lindsley. They are the best live band you have ever seen. Every single musician has won multiple Grammys. They play Western swing and classic country, and it's a joy to hear. Throw everything aside and go here.

Call ahead or use their website to make sure you get tickets, and show up early (7:00 for a 9:00 show, at the latest) if you want a seat. You can't beat the price, it's €15 to get in.

The beer's not cheap and the food's not that great: stick with the burgers and fries. But you are here for the music, and it is well worth your entire visit to Nashville.

There is free parking but it is a bit tricky and you might want to take a cab, you can afford it.

On other nights they have a wide variety of music, usually not country. Call ahead or check their website to see who's playing.
Food was lame. Drinks were expensive and small. Music was so loud you couldn't hold a conversation. Never again.

We just returned from Nashville to hear The Time Jumpers on Monday I play steel guitar and enjoy watching and listening to Paul Franklin .The whole band is spectacular if you love quality Western Swing and the food is very good and reasonable if you want to eat not to mention VINCE GILL doing his best playing and singing. The first time we saw them at Station Inn but like this location better. Need to get there early if you want a seat.
Good music, pretty good Hot Chicken. Not as crowded as many of the other places on Broadway, but then again, this place has only been open for a few weeks. Overall, not disappointed.
Great environment and great time when visiting Nashville.  It is a great place with several floors to explore and great beer selection. I went there every night during my visit.

This place is massive, and it's in the heart of the touristy Broadway section so if you dislike crowds this may not be your place.  For the most part though, the bands are excellent and there are 3 floors to choose from so you can get whatever you want.  Drink prices are about average, and table service can be very good despite the crazy crowds (it presumably helps if you pay cash and tip well upfront).

It naturally seems to be mostly tourists that populate this massive establishment, but I'd definitely go back.  I'm a fan.
Great place. Great music. Cold drinks. The band playing was very good. Interactive with the patrons. It made for a great evening.

This place has a great rooftop and a killer location. I had to give it a couple stars for that. We came for brunch on a Saturday. It was busy like every other place on Broadway and had a fun vibe on the roof. The drinks were fine. Overpriced but that's typical in the area. The reasons my stars are so low is the food. We ordered avocado toast and hot chicken and waffles to share. The toast was plain, un-toasted white bread. The avocado wasn't fresh, it was a paste from a package full of citric acid and flavorless. The eggs weren't to temperature and couldn't be finished. The hot chicken and waffles were ok but very unimpressed. Hopefully they change up the kitchen and make great use of the space.

Definitely go here if you are in Nashville. Amazing music (based on the two times I've been), cheap beer. Can't speak to the food as I haven't had it. If there is a cover charge, I guarantee it will be worth every single penny! The only *odd* thing is that the ladies bathrooms have curtains instead of doors outside the stalls. I sort of had to hold mine closed with one hand to prevent a different type of show to other unsuspecting guests ;)  Get here early if you want a seat!
Visit the Nashville Underground for the atmosphere, not the food. Really enjoyed the band. The service was great! Food not so great...sorry for the let down.

This is a great little venue for live music. With the table setup they have there isn't a bad seat in the house, and they're open a couple hours before showtime for food and drinks if you want to "pregame" it. The food is average for bar/pub type grub with decent portions. Drinks are reasonably priced. They seem a little short staffed server-wise, but if you're impatient for a drink there's a full bar on the main floor. And who doesn't love free parking? The venue even gives specifics on how to avoid paying for parking on their website. You gotta love them for that.

Surprisingly they have really good food here. And, the service was really good! Came in for lunch in a Friday. Live music and good tots, chicken fingers and salad. Not a bad option for downtown Nashville.

I almost don't want to give it a good review because I want to keep this place all to myself.
This place is just great! Friendly staff, clean as it could be. My wife and I had a really good time dancing to the DJ upstairs and the band downstairs

Wanted to go Honky Tonk hopping but we enjoyed the music here so much that we never left.  We took a shuttle from the campground to the Broadway Honky Tonks so that we could enjoy the day and not worry about driving back.  We ordered the chips, Queso and salsa which was really good especially the Queso and then later ordered onion rings and tater tops which were both really good.  The only thing I marked them down for was the price of the beer.  Coronas and other beers all seemed to be six dollars each which is pretty high.  Service was A+.  We would go here again and may tomorrow.
The first musicians were good but almost everything was a ballad.  We were about to leave when we found out that there would be a band change in about 45 minutes.  So glad we stayed.  The next band was great.  The front man had a great personallity, getting the audience involved, a great voice and a super band.  They had the place packed and some people dancing.  Lots of middle aged people dancing and acting silly.  So fun people watching.  Everyone was having fun.
Great venue for live music. The food is okay but I'm really here for the show. Get here early. It's first come, first serve for seating.

Awesome time ! Highly recommended- great bands and awesome service !!! Bands were very good ! 
I was a little taken back by the gentleman working in the bathroom - but all good. We will go back later today as it's on the main stretch to our ho

While visiting Nashville with a group of friends, Honkey Tonk Central was definitely our home away from home! The service was great (excluding one night with a waitress we dealt with around dinner time). The live bands were awesome, and very personable with the crowd. We always had a great time when we stopped by Honky Tonk Central (which was every day we were there for a few hours at a time!) I would highly recommend Honky Tonk Central to anyone who is visiting Nashville and wants to get a taste of a real Honky Tonk!

Stopped in for an appetizer after a visit to the Hall of Fame. This was our first Nashville Country bar experience! Food is good, nothing special but decent bar food. Annoying they don't allow substitutes on the app platter which sucks! 

Despite the average food, I gave it 4Stars because the band was really great! They knew just about every cover song and played on request! Cute little female singer who could really sing, token fat guy with a great voice and a second guitar player who could sing as well! Shot out to "Hoss Skelton and his band"

Went for stand up and REAAALLLY liked it. For a dive bar, it's actually fairly well lit and a couple of decent brews (in bottles mind you).

Baller as all heck! Go here!
Food was good. A little pricey but it id Nashville.  Staff was kind and courteous especially at the bar!  Music on Thursday was outstanding!

In from NH.hittting all the downtown spots. We were looking for a place for dinner and music without all the crowds and better food than what we had at a few of the places we hit. 

Great service friendly and great sandwiches and apps.Band was top notch, Good drinks, beer selection a little thin.

The bar is cozy with plenty of room to sit and enjoy the music.  The drinks are basic,  but come for the music.  The Willies on tap tonight playing 20's inspired swing, blues and jazz.  The 7 member band is fronted by Jen Jones an energetic lead vocalist who keeps the band in order. Worth hearing for a good time trading off between country and blues.
Best place on broadway!! Always great music and a very fun atmosphere. Bartenders are always quick, responsive and pleasant. Food is great too.

So, great venue. Love having yet another place to hear live music in Nashville, and with AmSouth/Starwood Amphitheater gone, this place was sorely needed. Obviously it is nowhere near as large as the old amphitheater venue was in Antioch, but it is downtown Nashville with a killer view of our humble skyline and within walking distance to all the best that downtown has to offer.

Pros: Our group went for the recent Needtobreathe show and had a blast. The acoustics are great, and the venue sounds like a true amphitheater. Everything was neat, clean, and relatively well designed.

For the cons: You will NEVER get me to pay $16 for a single beer. What in the crow?! Also, the seats in the reserved section need to be rethought. It was incredibly hard to find your section and row, but when you finally reached your destination, not all the chairs are marked with the numbers, and you don't realize upon your initial visit that the numbers that are there are tiny and stuck on little removable magnets on a minuscule sticker on the back of the chairs in front of you. The crowd departure needs to also be rethought. The gates are tiny, and when you have 6-7,000 people departing at the same time, it becomes a complete cluster trying to simply get out of the venue.

Overall, we will most definitely be back, as we have tickets to another upcoming show in just a couple weeks, but we will be more prepared and most certainly will have had a drink or two before the show. $16, hah! I can't help but laugh every time I think about it. (Oh, it's also $4.50 for a small bottle of water, so be prepared for that too.)

This is a beautiful venue! My friend won free tickets but I'm not sure I would've spent money to sit way back in the lawn. Also check the weather before you go- it started raining during the show and there is not many places to run for cover.

This is a real country bar nestled right in between the music studios. Very cold beer, nice people locals not the bachelorette parties lol. I wouldn't call this a dive it's pure country more like "authentic".

Came here day drinking!  Each floor offered a different vibe and a different band/bar.  Even though the bar was packed we found a small spot for the four of us at the main bar.  We were served immediately and I've never seen a hot bartender POP bottles that fast!! It was like in the wild Wild West and someone just shot the lids off of our Mich Ultras.  She kept the beers flowing ($5 each yikes!!) and then took our food order.. 

We got the fried pickles, chicken nachos, and tator tots.  Food came with paper plates and plastic ware, totally appropriate.  The Tators took me back to my 1st grade cafeteria and I LOVED IT!! Perfectly fried and sans the grease! The fried pickles are piping HOT so wait for a minute before you burn your taste buds.. But equally yum!  The nachos were just OK but after 5 hours of day drinking, we were pumped.

The best part of this place was having an epic dance off with a cowgirl on the second floor.  I hope she's there next time we go!!  Outdoor balconies are clutch too ;-)

What a great place. Tons of seating. Great band. Lots of windows to see all the action going by as well. Great food too
Nice crowd

Located in the heart of downtown Nashville, Ascend Amphitheatre provides top touring live acts. 

There is not a bad seat on the house. The view of the Nashville skyline and downtown is beautiful. 

This venue is walking distance to Acme, Tootsies, Pinewood Social and many Nashville honky tonks. 

There is also not a bad seat in the house. They rent lawn chairs to sit in, as well!

On a trip to Nashville my boyfriend and I found ourselves stopping into this bar a few times. The bands were great every time. They played a mix of country and pop songs.  We thoroughly enjoyed the music. The draft beer was $3 all day every day. Decent selection of beer on draft. The bartenders were friendly. It has a "dive" feel to it but a place worth visiting more than once!

Went on a Thursday to the 3rd floor & the service was not great. My friend & I walked up to the bar, very close to the bartender, had our money out & ready yet we were forced to watch her put on her lip gloss & walk to the other side of the bar. Just had to laugh. Had a pretty good time dancing to the band other than that.

Went on Saturday & the first floor was so crowded we could not even move so we went to the 2nd floor & there it seemed the bartenders were moving as fast as possible (although it took me 10 minutes to get a bud light, at least she was working as hard as she could & was very pleasant). 

Because it is right on the corner & the bands both nights were good, I would recommend stopping by for the first bar of the night just to experience it and then moving on.

I came here for a private party so I'm not sure if my experience would be as common as the next, but I can say the place was alright. Bands on every single floor were good and the bartenders were actually real nice. The people working the door however were giving me such a hard time it's unreal. I understand it's their job but the power trip they were on almost made me not want to even go inside in the first place.
Stopped here on the trolley tour and was surprised it was so good. Great decor, music and vibe. I will definitely come back again.

Nice amphitheater with ample lawn seating, came here for a Beck concert. Annoyed that we brought in umbrella and lawn chairs that were too high so had to rent their chairs. Plus we had to leave our umbrella and chairs (all 4) that we picked up today from Walgreens. Rent four for $7.50 each. Hope no one steals our stuff!

Great bar. Beautiful decor and such a great atmosphere. 

Has a great wine collection and out of most of the bars is easy going and relaxed.
If I had to describe it I would say the affordable sophistication on broadway. 
A nice break from the crazy honky tonk outside.
Which is still amazing but some times you need to escape from.

I highly recommend visiting. Xx

Honky Tonk is a great venue to drink and watch the game and of course to hangout at night. The only thing is at night is gets extremely packed so it's best you come early or be prepared to wait on a long line or be denied entry. Live music is great!
Unbelievable brunch - best we've had!  Beautiful trendy bar.  Awesome chicken and waffles and breakfast quesadillas.  #monkeybreadgamestrong
Great location and rooftop. Big TV. Terrible service.           Drinks decent. Standard price

We went for the Sunday night Bluegrass jam and it was one of the highlights of the weekend. The performers were fantastic and the talent performing was a joy to watch.  If in Nashville, do yourself a favor and stop in on a Sunday night.  I promise you won't regret it.

Honestly I never leave reviews but I don't want people getting extremely ripped off like i was. Visiting from Florida and went downtown to show the bf Nashville. Stopped in here cause the balconies looked cool. Bartenders were rude as hell. Double vodka and cranberry for $19. Someone actually warned us as we approached the bar to be careful that they don't scam you. I've been charged twice for that drink, so $40 for a double vodka and cranberry. Many reviews are mentioning the same situation and apparently reaching out is impossible so I don't have hopes in getting that money back. Also my bf had his wallet picked up and then someone said "oh I thought it was mine" which was bullshit. Personally I don't think this business gives a shit about what their customers think, so this review is simply a warning

I went on the Saturday of Memorial Day weekend. It was packed but I loved it. 3 floors with 3 different bands. I drank a ton and didn't spend much. One of the girls I was with got kicked out for being too drunk, but the guy kicking her out couldn't have been any nicer about it. She had lost a shoe and he searched the bar for it and found it. And nicely led us to an elevator so she didn't have to walk down the stairs. If you get kicked out of a bar in Chicago, they aren't gentle or friendly about it. Can't wait to go back here!

So, for those who don't know, this spot on Broadway St is owned by the infamous Gavin DeGraw. We were seated right away and had a very friendly waiter. There's an upstairs to this restaurant where I suspect the younger crowd goes to dance. There is a great rooftop lookout that overlooks Broadway (great for pictures).

The food was delicious! Not only was there great music played by very good looking country artists, but there was also plenty of drinks to go around. I ordered a mild hot chicken which was spicy enough for this Wisconsiner. I recommend going lighter when ordering the spicy chicken, since the mild was pretty dang hot. 

I will definitely be coming back to try this place out again...even though I can't decide if it'll be for the food or the cute singers!
Coolest dive bar ever.  Love the live music there--unlike any other place in Nashville or the world!
Such s great spot on broadway. They invite everyone in they have great bands and they really appreciate their customers. Refreshing

I'm a local who has always enjoyed Honky Tonk...until....

My friend and I decided to go here on a casual Wednesday night. We got in line for the bouncer to check our IDs. The bouncer granted me entry then proceeded to check my friend's ID while I waited patiently inside. She started laughing and yelled out to me "He thinks your ID is fake!" Apparently, he told her to tell me to "get a better fake ID" when in fact, I have been legal for years and my ID is 100% valid and verified by Metro police. We immediately left after I told the bouncer my ID was real and he called his security on me for no reason. 

Go here if you want to feel unappreciated as a customer.

Wasn't happy with the staff. We were given a hard time getting to our seats when using the Passbook app for entry. Security demanded a paper ticket to get to our seats. Luckily, I had planned for such an issue and had print outs in my pocket. Compared to previous set lists, Manson dropped 1 song, and the Pumpkins weren't allowed to do an encore due to the city's 11pm noise curfew. So much for "Music City". 

Keep in mind that this only pertains to the venue. Smashing Pumpkins delivered 5 stars for sure.
FOOD IS EFFIN AWESOME! !! Do not let the location or size be a factor not goin here. Great atmosphere! !!
A must if you are in Nashville!  Small venue with great entertainment, food and drinks!

Came to see the Time Jumpers and we enjoyed the event. A nice intimate setting for a concert for such big names in the band, but we still had plenty of space to be comfortable. Our waitress was lovely and gave us great reccomendations about other nearby attractions when she heard we were from out of town. Honestly, the food is sub par, but I wasn't expecting much more, being that most people come for just the music anyway. Would gladly return to see another show.
Its a bar, in Nashville, with lots of beer and dancing and country music.  Probably indistinguishable from about 15 other places within a 2 block radius.

This is a wonderful place to grab a small bite to eat and have a drink!  The food was pretty simple things: we ordered the ham and cheese sliders and the bbq sliders and both were really good for bar food.  The drinks were good.  The atmosphere is probably the best thing.  It wasn't crazy packed but there was still enough people to make it fun.  The music was good. Defiantly a place to check out!

Buyer drinker consumer beware. Went in here last night to the first floor bar and ordered two coors lights. So the first bartender says sure that will be $18.00. Wow ok that seems a bit high for two beers but oh well it was good music and busy. Then we order a second round with a different bartender and it was magically only $12.00 for the same two coors lights. Someone is making a lot of extra tips last night from over charging customers!!! Be careful is that really worth losing your job over thief bartender!!!

Great spot to see a concert.  The bar wraps around the entire back wall so you rarely have to wait for a drink, and the prices are pretty fair. The acoustics were surprisingly good, and the balcony tables provide a great view if the stage all around.  Definitely worth getting there early for one of the balcony tables-- but if not, the gently sloping standing room is great too.  I'd definitely come back and see another concert here.

Hot, hot, high energy bluegrass music the night we were there. Super-talented musicians. If you have any pretense about you, you'll hate it but if you don't have a problem sitting on mismatched chairs at vinyl tablecloth covered tables listening to musicians wow you, get there in time to grab a table and some cheap beer ($15 Yahoo pitchers) and $2 popcorn. Prepare to enter bluegrass heaven!
Way fun place with awesome bands and several levels.  Better than most on Broadway!

After dinner we wanted some live music that was more chill than Broadway. The Station Inn was just the right dose of chill, dive, and amazing bluegrass. 

A $12 cover got us a back row booth (only 50 ft from the stage) that was pleasantly worn and cushy. The bar was small with the basics and frozen pizza, and the wait staff did an overly OCD job of keeping aisle ways clear. 

However, as to be expected, the music is why you come, stay and leave satisfied. Monday nights are a combo of song writers and studio artists. They banter back and forth, tell stories and offer depth and soul.

A group of us came in on a Wednesday night. We went to the 4th floor. To be in you have to be over 21. But the bartender carded us again. Customer service was terrible.  The dance floor is amazing but the music is not good and when we asked to change to turn up, the bartender gave us much attitude and refused to do so.

How can you say no to free music? No matter what kind of music it is, people love free. But, what if the free music was totally awesome? Like Matt & Kim, ZZ Ward, Michael Franti, Local Natives, Moon Taxi and many many more. 

Sitting on the grass, drinking a cold beer, hanging with friends and listening to this awesome music is exactly why I love Nashville so much. Shhhhh.....don't tell the rest of the country we are so awesome! 

Thanks Lightning 100 for hosting such a great event!
Went to Big Stage Mondays and it was fantastic!  For $10 you see a 2 great singer/songwriters and each introduces a "new face" who also performs.  One and half hours of great music.  What a treat.

Food wise, I ordered the nachos and let me tell you... was NOT worth it.  $20 for bland nachos that were mostly chips. Go to peg leg porker for bomb ass nachos that are worth every penny. Spent a few nights in nashville and I've come to the following conclusion.... come here for booze only.

Awful if judged by the bathroom attendants. Which is reason enough not to go. They are militant and absolutely offensive and terrible. Will not attend again or recommend to anyone ever. The music is okay/good and the bartenders are great, but the bathrooms make it bad enough an environment to skip for all the other better bars on the strip without bathroom attendants or at least ones like this. Note to management: Fire/get rid of the bathroom attendant who threatens to call security on you for bringing your drink into the stall with you in order to protect yourself from being roofied.
