As someone who had had a close friend roofied and raped thanks to a date rape drug in a drink at a bar, I do not take well to a bathroom attendant calling security on me (first floor 3:30PM on Saturday, May 21, 2016) because I chose to be safe and responsible by taking my CLEAR liquid drink into the restroom with me to avoid a similar fate. This is absolutely unprecedented and insane. Anti-woman and terrible. Fix this poison at your establishment or you will surely face legal ramifications in  the future. Everything women should stand against. Unbelievably appalled.

Might as well had a full body cavity search at the door and given a hard time and my wife's e-cig was confiscated.  Every pouch and every pocket will be searched while drunk assholes are allowed to be insanely over served and spill drinks all over the place.  Venue is otherwise nice and the sound is incredible.  Hire better people.

When there are so many places on broadway to see, this place defiantly caught our eye just walking around on a Friday night. 3 stories, different bars and bands sounded really cool. We stayed downstairs and got a seat which was great to have since we were there for live music. Seats are a little old, but they get used a lot. Beers were a little high, but had a good selection. The bartenders were on it, normally takes about 5 minutes to get a drink other places, and I didn't wait more then a minute for a beer. The 2 bands we saw were great! We stayed for about 3 hours and had a blast.
This has a great decor and atmosphere. And the live jazz is a fantastic usp. Get down there this place is really that bit different.

I lived in Nashville for 20 years and the Station Inn was the one single thing I missed when I moved away 5 years ago. With great excitement I made my way there tonight to see what the last living venue in Nashville for live bluegrass had in store. I was horrified to see a full bluegrass group on stage playing through plugged in and wireless instruments and using in-ear monitors. . .  and it sounded that way. No communication and zero subtlety to anyone's playing on stage. In other words, the exact opposite of everything that makes this revered music so great. I suppose if bluegrass is going to die, the Station Inn is as good a place as any to host the memorial.

Walked in on a random Monday night. Visiting Nashville for work, and I love this place. Unpretentious bar with a good selection of beer and a great lineup of young artists. Came back a second night just to unwind. I didn't eat anything so I can't speak to the menu.

Went to the Ray LaMontagne show and his vocals were off for half of one of my favorite songs. If we're paying money for a ticket, the audio team needs to be prepared. It took a good 3 minutes for them to turn on Ray's vocals. And $15 for a Bud Light? Give me a break.
Neat place and great music right in the heart of Nashville's Gulch.  Limited drink and food selection detract little from the music on stage.

My first dive bar experience in Nashville, and it does not disappoint.  Walking through the door, I was greeted by a haze of cigarette smoke.  I forgot that smell when Minnesota banned smoking in bars, can't say I really miss it...but I'll accept it for part of the "allure" of this bar that feels lost in a bygone era.
Dimly lit, sad country music playing from the soundsystem, and locals in small groups throughout the room...this is a place to learn something about this city.
No live music playing at the moment, maybe some will happen while I'm here.

Note, $5 minimum on cards, no local beer...standard American fare only...go for the Shiner Bock for 3 bucks. I dig this place, a lot.

My husband and I traveled to Nashville for an anniversary trip as well as never having been to this infamous music city and had a blast!! The Station Inn was recommended to us and we walked by the place and thought this place was certainly dated and likely historical in the Gulch. We went and had an outstanding time hearing great artists such as Jim Rooney and Sam Bush. The people were nice the music was great and it was a great experience I would recommend when visiting Nashville.
This place was charming and had great music. Decent moonshine prices :)

I liked the music in the place on Friday nights, although there seemed to be issues I thought but did not know what. First time I used my credit card as a tab, I had two Budlights. I went to pay her, gave a check card, she (Carmen R) charged 33 bucks, I am guessing that is 6 bud lights and some change. I said I only had two, she usually said "I can't hear you what do you want", so I said I ONLY HAD TWO BUD LIGHTS, loud music on the back ground. I thought she still looked at me like I can't hear you, I thought,  "how is that my voice now", "can you hear me"? She said she was polite with me, I had way too many. I asked to show me my order list, she said give me your credit card, pulling the credit cards from my hands. I said what do you want to do? "it seemed like she wanted to hold on to my credit cards". I think she may have not known what even my name was. I said I think this may not even be my order or this is not my order after she said maybe "what" again. She look at the receipt which only had check :33:00 said, is not that your name? Ryan Davis. I said that is VISA you charged from not from the order or tab ticket #. I am not sure when, I asked for her boss, she said I am the boss. I may have said after that I want to talk to some one else, she may have said "I am the boss." I said I am not going to pay for it then. She said F* you and walked off. I do not know, but that is not what I was expecting or wanted.
This place is terrible. Been twice and will never return. Bartender is terrible. He walked by my empty beer probably 20 times and never asked if I needed another one. Terrible service

Awesome venue. There was a huge line but it moved very quickly. They did a fast check of bags and a pass through a metal detector. They had many drink options, though some could be pricey. The place was packed but emptied relatively quickly as well. The sound was awesome and the stage was well placed and designed
Off the chain!! Country music!! Friendly  people!! Had a blast!! Gotta come back!! First time in Nashville! Not my last time!!!

In town for the night, looking for a nice cozy place to watch the game, eat some good food, and enjoy a cold beer. So glad I came here!

My bartenders were personable, knowledgeable, and on top of every aspect of service. My food was delivered hot and fresh, in about 14 mins! I had the buffalo wrap- nice portion and the fries were super delish!

They didn't have my go-to bourbon, but they made an excellent recommendation. Overall, everything was much better than I expected. If you're in Nashville and want something laid back, downtown, and engaging, go here!

Great venue to catch a show. Both big names and local bands alike. Not a bad view in the house and I love the fact that there is plenty of seating!? Whether you want up close and personal or if you prefer to chill in the back, relax and watch a show, they've got a table for you.  It's got a good food menu, full bar and we've never had bad service! Highly recommend!

Although some might deem this a tourist trap, my friends and I could not have had a better time in Nashville!  We started the night at Honky Tonk, made our way down Broadway and down 2nd street then found ourselves back at Honky Tonk because it was THAT much fun.

It has 3 floors with 3 separate bars and 3 separate bathrooms which is great because you don't have to leave the floor unless you want to hear a different band.  Oh yah, there are different live acts on each floor, each with a different vibe.  I really enjoyed their Honky Tonk Tea, especially a decently large cup for $7.

BEST TIP EVER FOR 90 DEGREE NIGHTS: The 3rd floor has the best air conditioning, specifically this area towards the left near the stage/bar area.

This place is HORRIBLE! My first time here and I accidentally was in line for the men's bathroom so the MANAGER screamed at me and kicked me out! These people are horrible an insane! DO NOT EVER GO HERE! I apologized for accidentally being in the wrong line bc I've never been to Nashville before and they still screamed at me! Wow! Horrible people!

All the ambiance of a local VFW hall ... and that's why it's AWESOME!  Amidst the contrived fakery of most of Broadway, the Station Inn stands alone down in the Gulch as a beacon of authenticity.  Excellent and authentic bluegrass daily.  A must see.

Every time I come here, I think never again. Once again, the same thing. Why do people pay to see a band play and then talk through the entire performance. They ruin it for all the people around them. I have probably Been here six times and every time it's the same. The food is mediocre at best. And the sound system sucks. They have great performers play there but it's not worth it when you can't hear what you pay for. Never again!!!

We hosted a corporate event at Honky Tonk Central in July 2014 and couldn't have been more pleased with the venue and service we received. The vibe walking into the bar was fantastic - the place was crowded and the band sounded great. Our party had the entire 2nd floor reserved, with a private band for entertainment. The space was clean, large enough for our group of ~80, and had great views of Broadway from the open balcony and all-around windows.

The appetizer buffet was a hit and the service was impeccable. Thanks to Frank, Amanda P., Kori M., Leah C., Paige R., and Roger G. for being a great crew!

This three-tiered country club always seemed to be busy and bumping at every time of day. My wife and I came to check it out late at night while we were bar hopping.

The place is clean for as busy as it is. There is a lot of security and wait staff maintaining cleanliness and keeping a good eye on the patrons. The bathrooms are staffed also, and that's cool too if you're into that kind of thing. 

My biggest issue with this place is that it took me at least ten minutes to get a bottle of beer at the bar. I understand they were busy, but I got passed up for people who walked up after me. That can be really irritating. Although I know they were very busy, I felt perhaps they were understaffed. Overall, I had a good experience here. I just feel that there are bars on Broadway that suit my taste better.
From NY.. ive bartended for 24 yrs.. these 2 bartenders are 2 of the best I've ever seen.. and the wings are amazing..

I've seen a number of shows here and I've enjoyed them all. The sound is incredible and that's the part that really matters in a town with so much competition with live music. The space is massive and the bar area is well laid out servicing all areas of the venue. 

Sunday shows by Lightning 100 offer $2 Yuengling bottles- Lager and Black & Tans. Not too shabby!

Keep an eye on their concert calendar and definitely check out a new or favorite artist.

Nice place to stop and have a beer. We were passing by early in the day, so we sat outside and people watched. There was live music playing next door that we were able to enjoy. The beer was reasonable. The nachos were just ok. The staff was friendly. I bet this is a fun spot at night.

This was my first Nashville bar experience and it didn't disappoint! I loved the atmosphere of the first floor bar with the live band playing in the corner. The bartenders were all very friendly and for as busy as it was, always stopped by to make sure we were doing ok. I gave it a 4 star because the mixed drinks were just ok and pretty pricey but that was expected for this tourist attraction.

We had a blast here on St. Pattys day which happen to fall during our vacation. It had 3 levels and each level had a different bands, also had green beer. Good vibes, and decent dance floors! What more could ya ask for?

A really great space to see a show, beautiful venue, however the Live Nation security folks take their jobs a little bit too seriously and are very invasive. Shining flashlights and basically acting like military commanders. Calm down guys, I'm just here to enjoy some music.

Just dropped in there during day and I loved the atmosphere! Someone came to attend to us right away and it was pretty good service. They had a live band playing and they were pretty good. I was disappointed that they didn't have any beers on draft, but they had Shiner Bock in a bottle so that kept me happy.

My wife wanted to see Florence and the Machine for her birthday.... So I figure what the heck. Sounds fun! She booked the tickets in section 103 row R. I have to say this is one of the best venues we have seen a show in. Our seats were great but I honestly don't believe there is a bad seat here.  The lawn area is close enough for great visibility, just bring a blanket or small stadium chairs and you are set. I did see some people had to leave their larger umbrellas and chairs at the gate some I'm not sure about the specifics of what you are allowed to bring in. The only negative I  have is the concession prices.  Expect to pay about $10-$15for a beer or almost $5 for a bottle of water.

Stopped by a few other places in printers alley that were way too loud and chaotic. found this place by accident, and were so happy we did. Super cute place, good atmosphere, great music, friendly staff.

Cool country bar. I mean theres over 20+ to choose from. All country and all sell liquor so you cant be too picky. Had a live band. Only thing I didn't like was how they didn't have a bouncer or security at the door because a panhandler came in asking for money. Im not oblivious to times being hard but thats not really cool in a packed bar so they need to keep someone at the door.

Great bar to stop in for some music. Didn't leave the first floor, but understand there are another floor or two upstairs with different acts. Decent selection of beers and prices weren't terrible for Broadway. Bar staff was very friendly, and the two bands we saw were both very lively and talented - great for a cold January weekday afternoon.

When my friends told me to meet them at Honky Tonk Central after I landed, I didn't realize that was the name of an actual place. I just assumed that was just what they called the downtown area of Nashville.

It turns out Honky Tonk Central is a huge, three-story tonk bar with live music on every floor, and fantastic people watching. I wouldn't say it was mind-blowing in any other sense, but it's a good first stop to set the tone and kick off a trip right.

The bartender lost my card, found it on the floor and charged me twice. I've been calling all week and left a post on their Facebook page to try and get this resolved. No one picks up the phone and no one has responded to my post. I don't live in Nashville, and they've made it impossible to solve a problem like this.

From a local $9 for a mimosa that i have to walk 20 feet to a juice bar is kind of ridiculous especially when your bartender has the pouring measurement right beside her(another glass looking like sand inside) for exact pour. Will not be back!!
Far too crowded, but as a non-drinker hanging out with two who were drinking, I still say I had a good time.

Stopped by Honky Tonk for a few drinks before lunch. Went up to the second floor to sit by the open balcony.  Really pretty view of Broadway. 
We had a cool bartender Lindsey from Detroit. She was cool as hell and kept us laughing while we had our cocktails. I had 2 graham cracker shots which were very good. I also had a honey b drink wine high was pretty good. 
There was live music as well and they took requests. We had a good time.

Dive bar of dive bars.  Pricey beers, but live music all the time.  We split a burger and onion rings, not bad.  Wouldn't dream of ordering a salad there tho, can't believe they are on the menu.  Great atmosphere for listening to music, and people watching.

Tiny place, with a lot of attitude!  This has quickly become one of my favorite places to go in Nashville. If you are looking for a quiet, chill and small place to grab some drinks, listen to great live music that isn't loud and just relax this is the place. Great place to go with your friends or significant other for sure!

OMG OMG OMG OMG OMG OMG - I believe The Station Inn was literally one of the top things that we checked out when we were in town.  This dive bar was opened back in '74 by a group of six bluegrass pickers and singers (Red Smith, Bird Lee Smith, Jim Bornstein, Bob Fowler, Charmaine Lanham, and Marty Lanham).  It was originally located near Centennial Park, but moved to it's current location off of 12th Avenue.  They are internationally known to be the place to go to hear Bluegrass and Roots music (I wholeheartedly agree!!!).  The venue is first come, first serve; basically, if you see an artist/group you want to check out, you go stand in line, pay cash, and find a spot at either a table or pull of a folding chair.  We were so lucky to find two available seats by the stage - best seats in the house! :D  We saw Willie Watson (Americana folk singer, who sang and played the rhythm guitar with Old Crow Medicine Show) which opened up with Mandolin Orange (a traditional acoustic/electric duo from Chapel Hill, NC).  I was SO AMAZED - Mandolin Orange was very cute, laid-back, and easy listening, with their violin, mandolin, and guitar.  Willie Watson was ridiculous with his 1930s folk/traditional songs, with him rockin' out on his bango, guitar, and harmonica.  The venue itself is dark and people seemed to be having a great time with bar food (pizza, nachos) and beer.  There was one fellow who was quite intoxicated, and Watson actually sent him a message (in a nice way) to have a seat and not to block the audience views (the dude actually got sour and left).  I highly recommend checking this place out when you're in town/area - it was filled with mostly locals, so you know it's legit!  There's a free lot in the back, but just be aware that people tend to double-park (but, it shouldn't be a problem, since all stay until the end of the show). :D

+Bluegrass/Roots music :D
+first-come, first-serve basis in terms of seating
+tight parking (high possibility of double-parking)

Came here on a Sunday night with my Husband on our first trip to Nashville.  We enjoy a good time but also appreciate being able to find a seat. We spent most of our time on the rooftop. The live band was on the first floor, but we were into the music they were playing on the roof. It was also not so loud that we couldn't hold a conversation. After we couldn't get into a couple of places for dinner we opted to eat here. We both enjoyed our dishes and it was not your typical "bar food".  The view was great and the space heaters were a nice bonus on a chilly night.  We would definitely come back here.
Great atmosphere, friendly wait staff, good food and fair prices. A solid choice down on Broadway. Definitely a relaxed bohemian type vibe with lots of couch seating areas

Cool bar, always playing music. I believe they start around 10 or 11 AM. The place is also on 2nd Ave. so its a little calmer than broadway, yet still really close if you want to hit up those places. Bar tenders were really nice and observant.  Next time I'm back in Nashville, I will definitely stop in a few times.  I heard the egg rolls were really good, the locals (musicians) were eating them...

Great music, horrible bartender service, we have been waiting for 1-1/2 hours for our food and it's still not here. Waiter says it's because it's such a big party.  Not one visit to check on us or ask for drinks.  Food came, cold, no silverware napkins or condiments. 3 meals came out after everyone else was finished  eating.  Check out took forever. Horrible.  Never again.  This is my first Yelp review.  Probably the worst restaurant experience I remember.  

We were 45 minutes late getting seated for our reservation. I'll bet the table before us had the same issue.

Yep, after living here 5 years we finally got to 3rd & Lindsley,  Kicked ourselves all the way home for waiting for long..but hey, we travel for work a lot, we're old, Mad Men was on, I had to wash my hair...w/e.  

Crikey, did we enjoy the show!  We got there at 7 for the 9:00 Time Jumpers show.  We ended up sitting with a couple visiting from out of town as the seats were very slim pickings...but that was fine.  

The food was bar food...the service was fine considering those servers were working their tuckuses (tuckesi ?) off.  You don't go there for the food anyway, silly.  We didn't starve.  And, dinner for two, 6 beers = $48?  Can't complain.

The show...The Time Jumpers were amazing.  Such tight sound and just plain old FUN.  Dawn Sears' voice leaves you with a lump in your throat, seeing Vince Gill in that setting was a real treat, Paul Franklin's steel guitar is like watching magic happen.  It was pure delight.  

The venue was better than I expected it to be.  They had us crammed in there pretty good, but that's how it's done.  The restrooms were clean and available (a plus).

We had a blast and can't wait to go back.

I have never seen a group of well mannered adults treated as badly as we were.  A waitress (not even our server) handed us the bill for the group at our table before us, then had us kicked out when we refused to pay it.  Fun place, just be careful what is on your tab...

This place was so much fun! I had never been to a place like it before. Although it was crazy crowded on a Saturday night, it had an awesome vibe with different live bands on every floor. Definitely a place I would love to go to again next time I'm in Nashville.

For our first time in Nashville,  this ended up being our go-to place for great live bands all throughout the day and night.  After visiting other bars on Broadway,  this is where we ended up time and time again.  Nothing fancy,  but a lot of fun.  Go here!

Walked in, looked around, walked out.

Too many old people dancing. What was it, a Wednesday?

EDIT: It was a Wednesday. My bad.
Had a great time!! Cool place mixed crowd and great music. We went on a Friday afternoon. All tables were filled but it was not crowed. Next time I am in town I will definitely visit again.

This place was perfect on a Saturday night when everywhere else was getting crazy packed!

There were three floors - each one with a live band and plenty of seating.  We ended up spending most of our time on the second floor listening to a great band, and eating some really good chicken tenders with the most amazing bar-b-que sauce!  I would recommend that sauce to anyone, it was great!

A little more updated, this place didn't feel like the floor was going to cave in at any moment like some of the other older bars on the strip which was reassuring.  They also have a great view of the strip on the upper floors, which makes for great picture opportunities.  The doors also open in the summer (we were there in the winter) which I can imagine would make this place even better - you wouldn't feel so caved in like so many of the other bars!  A must see!

loud, the only drinks options were things you could pretty much get at any bar. This place is full of noisy tourists. Usually isn't a place to sit. Not my scene I guess. The environment was kinda stressful.

Beautiful place with 5-star potential but LOTS of kinks to work out. Poor crowd control with cheaters standing on stairways during shows and some serious mud issues when it rains. Brewing issues with promoters' heads exploding over the couple dozen people getting a watered down show for free outside the gates. Clumsy park and greenway closure planning. Underutilization if all the gates available to let folks in. Complaints abound about smokers but that can be solved with more general metro laws about parks and smoking.

Great sound, lovely outdoor space. The backdrop is amazing, too. Concessions are stereotypically close to laughably overpriced, but the forgiving policy on bringing snacks and water is a nice balance. Some info is harder to find, like gate open times, but mostly well communicated

Highly likely that season two will be far better planned and executed once all the disparate parties involved start to have better right and left hand coordination.

Definitely a gem for Nashville that just needs a little more polish.

Literally the worst bar experience in Nashville. Impossible to get a drink, and horrible service. They don't know how to run a bar, especially not a 4 story bar. Paid good money to get into their NYE event and we got nothing that was "included". Ended up having to wait outside the bar for an hour in freezing cold weather, and they wouldn't let us past the 2nd floor even though our tickets included all 4 stories. Will never go back and would never recommend.
A lot of restaurants on the strip, Nashville underground a great spot. The chicken sliders are to die for, great spot!

Stumbled upon Alley Taps while visiting for a birthday. The atmosphere is very relaxing and inviting. When we walked in we were the only two people in the bar. Dave and Kyle were our bartenders and they were amazing! Both were genuinely interested in talking to us and had great recommendations on places to check out around town. Kyle made us an incredible raspberry margarita, without a pre-made mixer. Because of Kyle and Dave's kindness and hospitality, we'll be stopping in one more time before we leave.

Went here for New Years Eve last night and I'm pretty disappointed. Waiting in less than 20 degree temperatures for half an hour and being let in one by one. Why sell that many tickets and not have everyone allowed in? I will avoid this bar from now on.

Came here after the stage on Broadway. It was a Thursday night on the day after Christmas but the place got pretty packed as the night went on. The band was great and played a lot of my fav country music. The crowd was mostly mid 20s-early 30s Everybody seemed to be having a good time and dancing.

My friends and I LOVED their roof top bar. It was so fun . We drank , ate and danced the night away. I will definitely come back to this place next time I visit Nashville. Also they have the best fries I have ever had !!

This place is awesome! Went to see Natalie Stovall and the Drive, the sound was amazing! Only issue was we never got a menu or even asked if we wanted a drink...everyone around us got service but no one even looked at us....I would come back though! :)

The one star is for food service. The music, Mandy Barnet, was great but we got our food, overpriced bar food, at 8:40 and the show was over at 9. Go for the music and make reservations somewhere else for the food. 
And get in line and be early as we arrived at 6:15 and there were only 4 seats way back behind the bar. If you want to enjoy this venue go early and eat somewhere else.

Don't pay the band on the 3rd floor! More specifically, don't pay the girl with the ash blonde short hair on the 3rd floor. She came around to our table asking for tips for the band, which isn't uncommon in Nashville, but minutes after she took a $20 for a request, we found out her band was done playing and she was long gone. This was the second time in one weekend where she did this. According to the staff here, this happens all the time. DONT GIVE MONEY FOR SONG REQUESTS. Total scam.

Great place to catch some music. The beverage options weren't that great, but a place like this isn't about that (or the discomfort of metal seats for extended sitting). But the band and divey atmosphere in a pretty modern neighborhood was worth the $15 cover and made for an enjoyable Friday evening

Had some friends visit Nashville for the weekend from Wisconsin. The bartender thought my friend's driver's license was fake and tore the holographic film off her ID, thanks to the bartender she now has to get a new driver's license. 

Not to mention, the bartender had a horrible attitude! There are plenty of other bars to go to in Nashville!
Hands down one of the best places to go to in Downtown Nashville!!! This bar has 3 different floors, and had a band playing on each floor. Open patio windows to Broadway Street. It was the coolest!!!

Coming here really made the trip for us. My daughter wanted to come live through a real Honky Tonk and hear all the talent that is out there. So as our Lyft driver takes us to the  end of the street at Acme's and suggests we walk down to the other end, we are a little concerned because there is no music at several venues. Then we see one across the street but as we make it to the corner we see that Honky Tonk Central has a live band playing. And not just any band, they are playing new and old country along with the some old and new rock favorites. 

Chris, the lead singer, had a true country tone and the female lead vocal Karla was absolutely awesome. When she sang Gretchen Wilson's Redneck Girl I could see the big smile on my daughters face I had been waiting for. The crowd was ready to party, we had a lot of military and the band had a lot of shout outs for our service guys. The crowd was loud but friendly, had no problems and we were there for 4 to 5 hours. Which brings up another point, the band doesn't take a break. They have solos or duets so that some of the band members can take quick breaks. They also had a couple of guys through out the night come in and play with them. One guy had just gotten engaged and another guy was leaving for Texas. They played very well with the band.

The bar is large and we never even made it to the other floors. The bar service was pretty good considering how many people were there. Our waitress was on top of our drinks and when she left BEFORE WE DID, she just informed us to go to the bar.

Thank you HT Central, made our first trip to Nashville a complete sucess and can't wait to get back.

This place was really good and the band was awesome. The one thing that was kind of a bummer was the bartender a blond named Amy. I don't know if she was drunk or on something. When we sat down she was yelling at the guy Shawn that played in the band, who was sitting next to us.Yelling at him to lose her number, stop texting her and leave her alone and how much she hates him. He was saying to her, your always drunk.That was kind of awkward! It went on about 10 minutes. Then she was all over the place. Stuffing her face with fries while taking orders at the bar, 3 guys walked up to the bar to order drinks from her and she starts telling them how much she hates guys,up on stage with the band(the band even said, this is Amy she's "supposed" to be bar tending) We also saw her give away a lot of free alcohol drinks, it looked like the girls were her friends. The other bartenders picked up the slack for her or we would have never been served. Other than her, the place was good.

For $12 per person we experienced world class bluegrass.  If you are truly a music lover and want to experience polished, professional musicians in a intimate setting go here.  Make sure you eat before you go. Just popcorn and pizza available for food.

The best place we visited the evening after a noon Titans/SD game.  Friendly bartenders, reasonable prices, good apps.  Outstanding female vocalist as well.  WIll most certainly be my go-to spot in BNA
This bar does not have happy hour I'm not sure why it is listed as having it, otherwise good band we were just here for drinks

This is a great  venue for an intimate live show. 

There was ample free parking, great service, and a terrific, clean house sound system. Not too loud and mixed just right. There is also ample table seating both upstairs and down with a variety of solid sight lines.

I highly recommend this spot for a mature, enjoyable concert experience. We saw The Waterboys tonight and it goes down as as unforgettable gig.

This is such an awesome addition the riverfront!  The sight lines are great from wherever you sit, including the lawn. My only concern would be if it rains, there aren't a whole lot of spots to take cover from!
Great place to relax and listen to music.  Super talented musicians and cold beer!  Didn't seem to be super touristy when we were there on a Monday.
Walking by heard Isaac Matthews voice, had to go in. Drank Woodchuck cider and fried pickle chips, enjoyed both. Best part was Isaac's voice.

The Back Corner is what Nashville has been waiting for...New York City meets Nashville. It's located next to 5th and Taylor and is less
Broadway more Flatiron. DJ, mixology, and swanky lighting. Lounge feel with great small plates from 5th and Taylor. Perfect spot to host a party or kick it on the weekends.

I'm not sure if this place normally has bad service and mediocre food but they did today. My burger tasted like it was sitting around in grease before it was tossed back on the grill for a quick warm up. Our server never came back for refills and when we needed to leave, we had to ask the bartender to get our server. Based on thus experience today, I wouldn't recommend this place as a good place to eat. If you give poor service, you should apologize and you should have your manager come out to offer a reduction on our bill.
The food is great! Literally one of the best burgers and fries I've had in Nashville. Service is hit or miss, hence the 3 stars.

During the day there's a crowd. At night it is packed! The place has three floors and has a lot of fun things to offer. You can look down on Broadway from the third floor, watch sports on TV, get food/drinks at the bar, or just clap along/cheer to live music. I came here expecting a good time, and I got it. Only got a drink, but the experience was great, and there were a lot of tourists (as expected).
Out of many drinks both times I was here. Most recently on a Friday, they were out of pretty much all house wines. They ended up giving me what they had left of a house wine- was awful.

We just saw Styx w/the Nashville Symphony Orchestra and really enjoyed the venue, sound and vibe.  This was our first visit to Ascend and we were really delighted with the entire scene. 

The lawn area has many great vantage points ... If you are near the front of line and you sit in very front on lawn you will get a great view of the artist and stage ... If you get there a bit later go to the river side of the lawn where it seems that area is last to fill up but still great views.  

There are about 10 picnic tables that are available but I would recommend bringing a blanket and beach type chairs to sit on.   Our venue had food trucks and we loved the wood fired pizza that was about $12 for a 4 piece pie.  The beer is the usual fair of bud with some craft ones as well.  25oz bud light was $11 and I was told the craft beer was more pricey-  $14, so you may want to pre party or bring a wad of cash.  They had plenty of alcohol drinks as well.   

One note, the line to get in forms down 2nd towards Broadway and gets long ... we noticed many folks coming in from the opposite way up 2nd in a much shorter line merging at the entrance with our line so that could be a short cut for future concerts.

This place is a bit rustic, but if you like bluegrass...it's a great place. The food isn't much, however..... The hotdog with pimento cheese is surprising pretty good.
Not really a dinning establishment... Rather it is know for some great music.   Seating is somewhat of a challenge. (Folding tables and chairs)
So come early to get a good spot of prepare to stand.
The draw here is the music. Small venue makes the sound incredible.

Came here with some friends in the middle of the day to enjoy some food and live music. We sat up on the third floor which was nice because it wasn't as packed as the others.

The live music was pretty good and enjoyable with some drinks and food. The mixed drinks are tiny for how expensive they are. I would skip them and just get a beer instead if you want a drink. The fried pickles were really good and came with a lot so it was perfect to share between 7 other girls. For lunch I split a buffalo chicken wrap with my friend. It was the perfect amount of food to split as they gave fries with the wrap as well.

Overall the place was okay. Okay drinks, decent food and some good music. Also we got our pictures taken with the honky tonk sign which was a nice feature! I would tell anyone to stop by and  see it at least once while in Nashville.
Awesome live music! Cash was flying for those Southern strings. Come here if you are looking for somewhere fun to spend your Friday night in Nashville

You can't miss with anything on Broadway! Live music everywhere, no cover and cheap drinks! This should be the new marketing slogan for Nashville. My favorite place that I can remember is Honky Tonk Central! This was a 3 level bar with live music on every level. The biggest thing about Nashville is that free live music at a bar is amazing! The talent is beyond good and I don't even like country music. This bar didn't disappoint with several bachelorette parties on each level, beers under $5 and no cover!

I went to this venue twice for Nashville the Beautiful events. I love any events that NTB throws. However, this venue was not great. First the bar was poorly managed. Not only were there only two bartenders to accommodate the crowd, which cause long bar lines, the drinks were very subpar and expensive. The drinks they make would not be acceptable in 5th & Taylor, not sure why they dropped the quality at their event space. Also, the bathrooms are poorly managed. Toilet paper and soap run out immediately, which makes you question the staff's sanitation, since you can order food at the venue. Now that Nashville the Beautiful is no longer using this space, I doubt I'll go back. I would recommend that people look elsewhere for their events.
Favorite bar I discovered in town. Nice prices and friendly people. Drinks were strong and music was great. They have one guy there almost every day and he is fantastic
Band was on point. Lots of great cover songs and interaction with the crowd. Drinks were ridiculously expensive.  Would go back but not to drink there.
Love the station inn! Really the only place in the Gulch I'd make a special trip to go to. Doesn't matter who is playing, it's always am amazing show... I'm always wowed by the talent here.

The good:
Great bands play here!
3 floors of music
Great place to people watch
Food is good

The bad:
Gets crowded quick
Too many drunk (former frat boys) 29 yr old men who think they could fight in the UFC.
Expensive beer
Overworked waitresses
One of the most fun bars in downtown Nashville. Live music, pretty good food, and a good crowd.

When ascend you to a food place, you should go there. You'll be glad that you did.

I have such great memories of this place. When I was young and reckless, I went to a Dixie Chicks concert here. I got lost in the building and ended up exploring the innards of it. I climbed up into the rafters and then I managed to ascend to the top of the building, and down into the balcony, and eventually made my way to the expensive seats plenty of which were still available and then watched the Chicks getting it on. This was actually before the days of the whole backlash against them, but I don't want to say that out loud because I don't want you guys thinking I am old.

Anyway the bottom line is that this is a beautiful venue and has wonderful memories for me.
One of the best local music spots in Nashville. Food is just ok and the cover charge isn't always what's stated on the website. Beware.

It was late on a Friday night. Stopped in after visiting a hipster joint down the street. Just one other person in the establishment. Matt unequivocally let us know that it was a "take it or leave it" kind of joint.  We bellied up for some basic brews and local conversation. Add in a perfectly cooked frozen corn dog and you have a perfect way to end the evening. Although near Vanderbilt, it apparently isn't a big college hangout because Matt won't put up with any BS. Just made it better in my eyes.

We went here both nights that we visited Nashville. It has a younger crowd and amazing bands. The first night the band played a 90s mash up that was pretty fun. They also played a lot of newer country. The second night they played rock n roll and country (new and old). There is no cover and the bands request $20 to request a song. Not bad considering there is no cover and there is nothing better than listening to your favorite song live! Also the view from the 2nd level perfectly shows downtown. Definitely would recommend this place if you want a fun night out on the town.
Great live bands! Seems like a local hang out. Food looked good but typical bar food.

The service was terrible. We made a reservation weeks in advance. The restaurant lost our reservation. After finally ordering food our waitress "forgot" to put all the orders in and people were left sitting while others ate. The waitress messed up the checks and and spent 20 minutes looking for the manager to fix. When she returned she asked me to just pay for extra food on my bill. We ordered one appetizer for the table to share yet several people were charged the full price on their bill. During the 40 minutes we tried to get our waitress to fix her mess the manager never came to speak to us. Our waitress was unable to fix her many mistakes and we ended up paying for things we didn't order just to get out of that place. I would not recommend it to anyone and will not be returning.

I really enjoy this bar on non Peak days rather than the weekend. This bar is unparalleled when they play good acoustic music without all the electric and full band overlay. The bar is comfortable the seating is private and it's a good mix of Ages people who are locals and visitors from out of town

I suggest the beef or chicken skewers they are cooked well healthy and flavorful.
Gave it 5 stars because Tim Bridges is sizzling hot! Going back next weekend!

This place is a joke!  The servers and bartenders are miserable and rude.  We stopped in because of the live music. If you are here-keep walking. Give another place your money.  It is OBVIOUS they take it for granted here and they have NO interest in making this place a good experience.  $31 for 2 domestic beers and vodka/sodas.
This place rocks in town for my 40th and by fat best place 3 floors 3 different bands outside atmosphere great service a must when in town!

Loved, loved, loved, my experience here. The band was amazing. (Frank Solivan and Dirty Kitchen) True musical excellence. Worth every penny at a modest $12 cover. Bartenders as well as door staff were very nice. As the other reviewers mention your alcohol choice is only beer. But they have goo goo clusters! 

Skip the cover bands and mediocre bars on the strip and treat yourself to something real.

I went here with a friend who is a Nashville local. He recommended the Doyle and Debbie show as "like seeing George Jones and Tammy Wynette, but on mescaline". they did not disappoint. the music was great, and the act was hysterically funny. it's a sort of Stephen Colbert style social satire. the venue is superbly decrepit. they only serve beer and "coolers" (Smirnoff Ice) so you may want to pre-game, but be sure to support the place and buy some drinks while you're here.
Great place to go if you don't want to be surrounded by a mob of drunk 20 yr olds. Music was great. Beers were good. Didn't try the food.

We've wanted to go to 3rd & Lindsley for years! Finally made it out the Tuesday before Thanksgiving for an MV2 night with some of their young artists. Nora Collins is going to be a good one! We had a blast! Highly recommend this place!!

Love Bobbys.  It's a great dive bar off the beaten path.  I love how they have song writers night and also have other nightly activities (comedian night etc) 

Highly recommend for a good local time!!

The food here is so bad. I've eaten the strawberry pecan salad (thumbs down), the spinach-artichoke dip (ew! How do you mess up spinach-artichoke dip??), the potato skins (meh), the philly cheese steak (two thumbs down), and the chicken wings (very mediocre and the ranch was lumpy). The mozzarella sticks were alright. Do yourself a favor and eat before you go. This place must only stay in business because you're trapped at a table for the concert, so you may as well eat there. Don't fall for it.

The War Memorial Auditorium is a majestic and beautiful historic building. 

After climbing many levels of long marble steps, you're greeted with enormous white columns and a huge courtyard. This is truly one of the most beautiful buildings in Nashville. 

The auditorium was built as an incredible memorial for the fallen soldiers who gave their lives for our country in World War I. For more information on this incredible building, you may find this link helpful :

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Memorial_Auditorium

( The State Capital stands behind the Auditorium making it even more impressive. The lighting and the beauty of these two landmarks is absolutely breathtaking. )

Now for my review on the auditorium itself:

We purchased VIP tickets for the Cowboy Jack Clement tribute benefiting musicians without health insurance. ( I've known Cowboy all my life, so this was one tribute I wouldn't have missed for anything. ) 

I could go on and on about the line up of incredible artists, how great the show was, and how much I enjoyed it,  but this review is about the auditorium.

Our seats were in the balcony ( 3rd floor) which gave us a great view of the stage
but the elevator only goes to the main floor. If you have trouble walking up stairs, buy your tickets for the main floor.  

The interior of the auditorium is beautiful, even the ceiling is something to admire.
The stage is more than ample  for a very large band, choir or even orchestra. Unfortunately the sound wasn't great which is a shame because the atmosphere is amazing. 

The auditorium sells drinks which include sodas, beer, mixed drinks and water. 
( no wine) On the third floor, the "bar" is basically a closet with a counter and one girl operating it as a "cash only" bar. ( a small beer - $8.00, large - $15.00 )

Now for the worst part....the ONLY restrooms in the building are in the BASEMENT. 
This may not be an issue for some people, but for me it was a real inconvenience. 

Every time I needed to make a trip to the ladies room, it involved going down 3 floors to the basement and 3 floors back to our seats.
( approximately 100 stairs each way.) Recent knee surgery made this a painful inconvenience. 

Another problem is the seating. I'm 5ft. 3in. and I had absolutely no leg room. My son and husband are over 6 ft. 3 in. and were so uncomfortable it caused us to  stand in the stairway a few times. ( my purse was in my lap the entire time -no room on the floor by my seat.) I felt like I was sitting on an airplane. 

It was very cold and windy that night so we used valet parking. ( Parking is also an issue here.)  
If there's another event at the auditorium that I absolutely don't want to miss, I'd definitely get tickets on the main floor.

HTC is another country music bar on Nashville's main drag.  This is another multi-tiered bar that is perhaps built a little better than the other re-purposed buildings nearby.  Crowd was a good mix of ages with college kids, bachelor/ette parties, and also old folks just listening to music.  The bands vary by floor but we just stayed on the ground level.  Both bands we saw were alright with the second one being a bit obnoxious with people on cell phones; I agree that you shouldn't be on a phone if you're right next to the band, but if you're in the back of the room and the singer calls you out then he's just a jackass (he did this multiple times to different people).

Bar prices seemed a bit higher here than in some of the other bars.  Beer selection was decent with the list having ~half domestic options with a number of local microbrews thrown in.  Bartenders are decent given the volume of people they have to deal with.  The male bathroom attendant was hilarious but also a bit pushy; didn't bother me but I can see some people getting uncomfortable.  Overall this is a worthwhile place to stop by but not worth a specific visit when in town.
Really cool place!! Have been here a couple of times and had great experiences. Didnt catch the bartenders name the last time I was here but she was an absolute doll. Will definitely be back!

Fun live music and friendly staff. It's near Printers Alley and a good alternative to Broadway. Not as touristy! The live music was great, but then again you get that almost anywhere in Nashville! Would return in future.

Ow!!!  Honky Tonk Central on a Saturday night celebrating my niece's outstanding accomplishments.  I can say Honky Tonk and Honky all I want and no one will be upset because that's what it's called. Three levels of locals and tourists packed and overflowing off the balconies. Yeah buddy! This place has that Nashville energy and live music right in the heart of it all.  This is where the action is and what you hear every visitor rave about.  Come here and you know you are in Nashville.  Woo!

Stopped in for an appetizer after a visit to the Hall of Fame. This was our first Nashville Country bar experience! Food is Really good for bar food standards! Annoying they don't allow substitutes on the app platter which sucks! 

I have this place 4 Stars because the band was really Awesome, and for what it is, a country bar, its definitely doing everything right. 

The band knew just about every cover song and played on request! Cute little female singer who could really sing, token fat guy with a great voice and a second guitar player who could sing as well! Shot out to "Hoss Skelton and his band"

I came here for the TFIOS event this past Thursday. I was media so I was able to snag a reserved seat in the balcony ... felt bad for the poor teens standing near the stage!

I can't speak for the venue as a concert place, but for TFIOS it was fine. Easy to see the actors + writer (John Green! *fangirls out*) from where we were in the balcony. Good acoustics although I don't think it was meant to play movies/clips from movies.

I'd like to explore this place more if ever back in Nashville.

Do not come here! !!! I am on a Bachelorette party from Chicago,  2 of of the 10 girlss had their phones and wallet stolen from their purse, along with other women from the bar.  Security did nothing to help us, would not even call the police for us and told us to do it ourselves.  This place is criminal infested with terrible security that is worthless!!!!!

First time here, wasn't sure what to expect.
Got there and all the tables were taken and saved.
People were eating and looking around at one another.

I got there and leaned against the bar, looking around, looking for an available seat.
Bartenders were pleasant and asked me if I needed anything.  So no problem getting a drink, if I wanted one.

The lights went down and I saw an available seat at a table with a couple of men.
Went and asked them if I could share the table with them.
All night long, during the concert, the waitress was there asking if anyone needed anything.  She was prompt and constantly within view.
So no problem with table service.

It's a great venue. Plenty of tables and chairs, everyone got a good view of the large stage, acoustics were perfect...  volume wasn't screeching loud.
It was perfect.

Price of the ticket was $20. No drink minimum.
I loved my seat, I loved the venue, it wasn't too big, wasn't too small... 
I will be back!
And just so everyone knows... no problem coming to the club, solo..
It's safe.  I had no problems..

And after the concert, there must have been a dozen taxis outside waiting..
Safe neighborhood, as well!

I will return!

Went in for the comedy show...seemed sorta dark an didn't seem like our vibe. 

So my gf an I went on to downtown and drooled over $400.00 boots....yeah we didn't get any. 

And they only take cash here at this place.

Great music, food, customer service and atmosphere! Note that the music is loud and the place isn't for people who want to be calm or quiet, but if you want live country music, the occasional two step dance and a low key but fun atmosphere, this place is perfect.

I was visiting Nashville two weeks ago with two girlfriends of mine. One of the girls I was with was leaning against the wall texting, and the bouncer accused her of being drunk and threw her outside. When I asked him what his problem was he proceeded to yell in my face that I could chug my 11$ drink and "get the f#*% out". He then grabbed my hand that was holding the full drink and threw the drink down my shirt, and without letting go of my hand he literally threw me outside of the building, where him and his friend flipped me off while they were closing the door. I spent the rest of my night soaking wet and smelling like booze. I would not suggest wasting any time at this over priced shit hole.

What and interesting spot. Like most places in Nashville the non-descript exterior hides a warm, fun filled environment on the inside. Since the name of the place is also it's cross streets, if you can't find this place, you have had too much to drink and need to go home. With that said, the musical performance by The Time Jumpers is sure to bring smiles to those familiar with archetypal southern favorites and newbies alike. The crowd is a mix of Nashville locals , travelers and a few younger people like me.  Everyone was friendly. 

The food is basically upgraded bar food with some good entrees as well. I felt like a patty melt tonight and damn was it good. The menu indicated "Angus beef" and it was and epic combination of sautéed onions, Swiss and rye. Fries have some sort of seasoned salt but there is something really good about them that I can't identify.  My partner in crime had the prime rib dinner which was also very good. 

Parking is slightly better than most places in Nashville with a few nearby businesses not needing their parking lots at night. Bring a Mini Cooper to fit in small places. Also get here early if you want a decent table, or a table at all for that fact. Some friendly stranger indicated she paid someone to be here at 5 to secure her a front row table by the stage. That's dedication people.

A humongous tourist trap full of music, booze, and women. So naturally, I walked in.

For the most part, our group of friends which included a happy couple and two (soon-to-be) bachelors had a great time. 

The cover band was mediocre, but the song selection was awesome covering various pop hits from Guns N' Roses, Lil' Wayne, Toby Keith, and many others. The crowd was diverse, but for the most part got along. And some nice southern girls even bought me a shot. That rarely happens in Man Jose (and other areas of the Sillyc*ck Valley).

My only knock on the place is that my group of dipsomaniacs went on a weeknight, so they shut down the top two floors. No problem (since the first floor had a nice crowd). 
But we were all on the bottom level surrounding a large circle bar with only one bartender. And she just happened to be the most inefficient bartender of all time. It was painful to watch her pour drinks and struggle to take bottle caps off of beers and mess up orders. They probably could have brought in Walter White's son Junior (aka Flynn) from Breaking Bad and we probably would have received faster service. 

Luckily, they brought in a professional that made drinks fast and took four bottle caps off in approximately 1.7 seconds. Seriously, she was poppin' bottles like a mainstream hip hop artist. And eventually, we were poppin' bottles to a cover band covering Lil' Wayne in the middle of Music City.

Good times.

Overall a pretty good music venue. I'm here now for a concert. It is a smoke free, not! People smoking all around me. You would think they would take the necessary steps to enforce the no smoking rule but no. The stench of cigarettes is why I'm only giving it 2 stars. 
On a positive note, prices for food and drinks aren't that bad.  In line with other venues.
Fantastic little place to listen to music in Nashville. The folks there are out of their way friendly and work to make you feel welcome. It's definitely a gem.
Exactly what I expected from a Nashville country bar... Great music, good people watching, beer and fun.

Don't go downtown much unless we have people in town, but if we do I avoid this place. Typical tourist trap. Always crowded and $5 miller lites to boot. Plenty of other places on Broadway that are far better.

Brought in by the live music 10/16/14. Tried a slushie. I couldn't finish it. A lot of booze. Went back to $4 16oz. PBR. We got there when one act finished and another one started. It was a husband and wife duet. Really liked them. A lot of rock covers gone country. Not a big country fan but I enjoyed it. I requested a song for my wife. She was surprised that we were from Wisconsin. She has had a lot of folks from Wisconsin the last few days. Wisconsin represent. I'd go back for sure.

I guess I'll be that person that breaks the 5 star trend. I remember going to Live on the Green when it first started and it was amazing. Being able to just sit and relax while listening to music was awesome. Now, not so much. I fear, dear Nashville, this event has outgrown its tiny space. I went mainly to see City & Colour and while I'm glad I toughed it out to the end, it was not pleasurable for the most part.

At first, yes many people were lounging on blankets and enjoying the opening band but as the night progressed it got considerably more crowded. Those with blankets and lawn chairs seemed to just give up after awhile and retreat to other places or leave all together. We were CONSTANTLY being pushed or bombarded with "excuse me I need to get by" as people walked over others to stand towards the front. Soon it was no longer a fun, live show but instead of was the dodging of the beer and cigarette smoke as people moved around you, most with no sympathy to your presence whatsoever. 

Lots of great local food trucks, companies and beer vendors but getting to these stands were a gamble of either losing your spot on the lawn (if lucky enough to have one) or braving sending one or two of your party to navigate through the crowd. The lines were outrageous, mainly just groups of people standing in whatever fashion they deemed fit. While, from what I saw, prices were quite reasonable for a "concert" event, the lines just weren't worth it.

Most of the artists that play this event are not the "lets all dance and move to the beat" kind of artists, at least on this night. City & Colour is a perfect example of the type of music this event was made for! It would have been awesome to just sit and be able to listen to the heavenly vocals of Dallas Green while enjoying a beer but instead you have to settle for listening to the music while filtering out every single social hour conversation going on around you. If you just want to hear the music and don't care about actually being able to see the artist, then find a spot a good distance away and you'll be fine. 

I feel like this event could be amazing, if run more efficiently. Possibly moving the beer tents and such away from the stage vicinity would help thin out the crowd of those patrons that make you think "are they waiting in line or just watching the show?" Before you go, ask yourself this: Do I want to be constantly stepped around, over or pushed aside by what seems to be every single person who has crawled out of East Nashville's hipster woodworks? Do I enjoy having my feet stepped on, beer spilled on my shoe and cigarette smoke being blown in my direction by countless people with no decency for those around me? Do I want to see great artists for free but sacrifice my comfort as I stand for 5+ hours? If so, then this is the event for you! I appreciate the fact it's a free show and I guess this is what you should expect with a show like this but guys, this isn't Bonnaroo. You do not have days to spend socializing and getting messed up as you listen to the music. It's a concert full of regular people who may or may not enjoy the fact you are plastered on a local pale ale as you smoke your billionth cigarette of the night. Most of us just wanted to be able to enjoy a great night of music but, at least in my opinion, this time it fell very short.
Awesome new venue.  Design and sound are great.  Sat on the lawn with a beach chair.  Great evening.

This is seriously one of the coolest events in Nashville! 

I saw Gin Wigmore, ZZ Ward and Matt & Kim a few weeks ago, and my mind was blown! Who knew that space could hold so many happy music fans?? What an awesome set-up! I got to grab a blanket and relax with some friends while listening to some kickass music. Life in Nashville is dang good!

It is so dang good in fact, that I chose all of my MBA classes based on the LOTG schedule; so no Thursday classes for me in the Fall!

If you haven't hit up LOTG, you need to free up your Thursdays and head on over! It is not to be missed!

One of the things about the various listening rooms in Nashville is when you get to see so many mind-blowing bands, musicians and singers. The space becomes associated in my brain with the musical magic that happens so consistently inside it.  I'm a huge Time Jumpers fan (I've been 8 or 9 times now since moving to Nashville in 09).  I recommend to everyone - come to Nashville. Stay over Monday Night. See the Time Jumpers.  Guaranteed. 

Another thing about amazing venues like 3&L is how popular they become. Of course - amazing talent will draw crowds.  So getting in line early (like hours before doors) and waiting another couple hours (time to sample the extensive but for the most part ordinary bar/fried food menu.  It's certainly a magnitude of order better than the menu at the Station Inn (Time Jumper's former venue) but not amazing enough to warrant 5 stars. I'll keep trying it, though, and guaranteed you won't go hungry (unless you're vegan). It's just not very foodie-ish. Nashville has a lot of amazing culinary talent doing interesting things.  You don't come to this venue for dinner, though, you come for the music and have decent barfood dinner/snacks. 

Take note of the seating; You'll be in seats for several hours. On the main floor the chairs are wooden with no arm rests and have short square backs. The chairs on the balcony are wooden with no arm rests but have padding on the seats. There are also padded stools on the balcony.

Sound is great throughout the room, too.  Be assured, you will have an amazing musical experience at 3rd and Lindsey. You just won't remember the food.
This was our favorite bar in Nashville. The bartender was great and the music was fantastic!

Great show and venue. Food was great and we had a really nice server. Only problem was that the prime rib sandwich was sooooo salty that it was inedible. After one bite, my mouth felt like I had just gargled with salt water. Seriously, no exaggeration. Sampler platter was amazing though.

Wasn't too impressed here. I'm giving them 2 starts for the following reasons: 

1. Our server Katie had a ton of tables and worked her butt off running around doing everything. There were 2 servers for the whole third floor. (The bartenders don't count, but we will get to that later) 

2. The music was amazing. We got to listen to two bands and they killed it! It's so cool to listen to bands live. Also, the third floor has an amazing view! 

For whatever reason the food was taking forever, which was fine but we were starving so if they would have told us that the kitchen was understaffed or backed up we would have just gone somewhere else. 

The thing that upset me the most was the two blonde bartenders. They were so rude. I think I saw them each smile 4 times total. The poor waitresses were running around frantically and the two girls just sat there at the bar on their phones. No since of urgency at all. They seriously didn't do a thing the whole hour or so we were there. Why they staff two bartenders?? Idk. I'll attach a pic of the girls texting with their backs to everyone. They didn't give me bad service but watching that happen and those poor girls running around made me feel really bad for them. If I were the manager I would have cut that off a log time ago. Speaking of the manager, she made eye contact with us twice while we were looking around for our server and just kept talking to the bartenders. They are probably always on their phones because the manager allows it. Pathetic. 

Good job Katie and band.

Honky Tonk Central has always been one of my favorite places in Nashville. It doesn't have the old school legendary character of a lot of the places on Broadway, but what it lacks in heritage, it makes up for in good times. 

The open air 3 story bar has live music on every level. So you can freely roam floor to floor listening to a different live band. We enjoy visiting the other venues on Broadway, but it always seems like we find ourselves back relaxing at Honky Tonk Central overlooking the city & listening to some awesome bands.

We went there last night and it was such a cool experience!
The Time Jumpers are a band of 9 older men (including Vince Gill) that usually play Mondays for $20. The venue is smaller so in order to get a table, get there at 6:00 and have dinner and drinks before the show starts at 9:00. 
The band is bluegrass and they pulled groups on stage (pre planned) to perform. Last night, Kacey Musgraves came and played with them.
One of the best experiences during my time in Nashville!
The owner hit my female friend in the face. He was drunk and violent. Never go there if you have respect for yourself. There is video footage.

Bluegrass DREAM!  Sunday night keeps it rocking.  Love this bar and the atmosphere.  Nothing beats a dive bar where you can walk right up to people jamming.  The pictures on the wall display the history of this establishment.  What a gem!  The popcorn and cheap pitcher beers will keep you going all night

Went to a wedding in Nashville and ended up here after the reception.  Great American people and fantastic live music venue.  I'm sure for the Nashville scene it's considered 'touristy', but what the heck, I was a tourist!  It's slightly divey very loud and serves cold beer.  Stop in if you have the time!

This place is popular in Nashville the food is bar food so don't expect to much place it's old but nice parking was full but across the street is a public parking for $10 all night we went Wednesday night they have 2 great performers the sound was excellent the show was great if you want to see new artists give a chance to 3rd&lindsley for sure you aren't gonna be dissatisfied

It was a decent place. The live music this afternoon was very good! Both of the singers were excellent, our waitress was very attentive and nice but the food was subpar. Got a burger and it was a frozen patty, disappointing. But seemed like a decent place to hang out otherwise- just don't eat!

This place was great! They had an awesome band playing while we were there, the waitress was attentive and available, but not overbearing. This was nice since we wanted to listen to the band. The food wasn't gourmet or spectacular by any means, but that's not why we went -- we got some wings and a buffalo wrap. Like I said, both were good and I felt like the prices were pretty reasonable. It's a big place, too.

We clearly went to this establishment for the music and we were not disappointed whatsoever.  The show was fantastic.  We saw a tribute to David Bowie and while we were not that familiar with the music the band and singers were amazing.  The atmosphere was that of a club and perfect to listen to music.  In terms of food, typical pub food and pretty average quality.  I wouldn't go here for the food but for the music, absolutely.
Great atmosphere here! From Boston and even though we did not fit in with eagle fans it was great! Jazmine is awesome!!!

The finest bluegrass in Nashville! No pretense, just world-class music. Always worth the cover charge. 

The Station Inn as as casual as it gets in Nashville. That being said, it's primarily a listening room; that is, people come to hear the music and respect the musicians by not chatting while they are playing. 

About food and drink: if you don't like ballpark food, then you should probably eat before arriving (shows usually begin at 9pm anyway). It's a hot dog, pizza, beer, and soda kind of place. If you drink beer, go for whatever local Yazoo is on tap. Bottled water available. 
People come here for the music, not the libations.

We got to the venue at 10:30. Being out-of-towners, we didn't know what time the band would start and finish. So, we walked in the front door and the doorman asked if we had tickets, which we didn't. He said that'll be$20. 

We really wanted to see The Steeldrivers, but were hesitant to spend $20 each if the show was half way over. The doorman (Nelly) insisted that they had just started their first set, so we decided to go on in. 

By the time we got a drink and found a table, the band finished and the place was cleared out! 10:50. The waitress agreed that it was ridiculous that we had just been coaxed into paying $20 for the tail end of the show and that we should go see Nelly to express our concern. 

When I mentioned it to him, he just laughed and said, "well, they didn't take a break." I said, "you told us they had just started." He shrugged. We left unhappy.

Nelly is a liar.
I LOVE this place! Great atmosphere! Great Western Swing band!

Came back for another Monday night show with The Time Jumpers. Great sound. Again. That's a huge plus. 
The food was good and priced well. Apps came fast and were pretty tasty. Entrees were well presented and good. No looming pressure from our server which was appreciated. 
Overall, another perfectly enjoyable evening. Someone else said it was bar food. True. But they crank it out and it is fairly priced and we have all paid a lot more for much less

I LOVED the new amphitheater! We went to see Needtobreathe with Colony House, Drew Holcomb and the Neighbors, and Switchfoot. We had tickets in the pit (which was standing only), and the view behind the stage was just an incredible backdrop for these awesome bands. 

The Hattie B's hot chicken truck is really cool to have onsite, and I appreciated the availability of beer and drinks all over the facility without having to stand in line. Also, there were several bins for recycling which makes me very happy to see!

The seats in the middle of the theater were padded and awesome! After 4 hours of standing, I was really wishing for a place to sit down. The lawn was awesome too, though! Spacious and nicely elevated for a great view of the stage. 

My "feedback" is this: On the website, the General Admission Pit, listed as PITGA on the tickets, is listed as "orchestra". That was confusing, leading us to be unsure if we were on the lawn, or where exactly we'd be. There is also no information as to if the pit will have seats or no seats for the concerts. Several photos I found on Instagram led me to believe we'd have seats (if that was where our tickets would be) but for this concert, there was no seats. I ended up with a bulky bag holding a blanket that I had to carry around all evening because of the lack of information on the site.I'd appreciate a few more details to help people be better prepared!

I cant' wait to go back to more concerts here; yay Nashville for finally having an amazing outdoor venue that can accomodate large shows.

Nothing special here unfortunately.  was staying in downtown Nashville and couldn't decide what to eat.  place had OK / decent reviews so I decided to give it a whirl.  good location, live music.  it goes downhill from there.  beer in plastic cups and it tasted stale (Yuengling).  the Spicy Chicken Mac & Cheese was sub par.  I'd say one step above Kraft Mac & Cheese from a box.  sorry. just didn't do it for me.

Walking into Honky Tonk Central, all I could think was, "This is my worst nightmare." If you're not a major fan of crowds & country music, this might not be the bar for you. As my friends & I (a bachelorette party) wove our way through the first-floor throngs of people, we passed deeply accented folks wearing cowboy hats & flannel shirts, all fist-pumping to a live rendition of a VERY country song I'd never heard before. It was like a slow-motion scene from a movie, looking into all these people's eyes & seeing how much joy they felt at being there while I felt *completely the opposite.* Oh my God, it was gonna be a bad night.

But this is a four-star review, see? Which means things changed. This bar has multiple floors, & when we got to the second floor, we found things to be a lot more chill, much more our style. Did I mention that we're all Northerners? Country isn't quite our jam (why did we come to Nashville? Beats me), so we were thrilled to find that the live music on the second floor was more rock with a country twist - Tom Petty, Rolling Stones, Johnny Cash, The Eagles. The kind of music you know in your soul. We claimed a corner of the room - which wasn't nearly as busy as downstairs - where we piled our coats & got to dancing. We had a great time, & we got fairly hammered because this bar is surprisingly inexpensive.

The people-watching is great, too. The second floor was filled with all kinds of characters, & the atmosphere in the bar was friendly & low-key enough that we struck up conversations & danced with some of them. Lots of interesting folks & good tunes. But beyond all that, it was a great space for dancing & not giving a damn who else was around, the way a bachelorette party & a good vacation ought to be.

The only negative is that the top floors close earlier than the first floor, so we were all sent back downstairs at some point. My friends & I still had a bucket of beers, so we settled into that terrible downstairs crowd to finish off our drinks before heading home. While we were watching the live band, one of my friends was robbed - like, someone just pickpocketed her wallet right out of her purse. She felt it, but thought it was because the place was so busy. By the time she realized what had happened, the perpetrator was long gone. As she sobbed & I made my way to a bouncer to tell them what had happened, some guy overheard me saying what had just happened, & he passed her wallet over to me. He'd found it on the floor, minus $150 cash but with all cards & her IDs still inside. It was the best-case scenario after being robbed, to be sure, but it was a low point of our visit. 

In other words: When you find yourself at Honky Tonk Central, grab a bucket of beer, head up to the second floor, prepare to dance, & don't forget to bring a very, very secure purse.

This venue is awesome and a great addition to downtown Nashville!!!  So happy to have attended the inaugural show with Eric Church.

Great layout, spacious, plenty of restrooms and food/drink options, and just a nice chill place.

Yes drinks are outrageously priced but otherwise it's fantastic.

I had the opportunity to see Bryan Adams in concert here and i loved it. Not only have i loved him my whole life , had a lot of fun, singing and dancing to most of his songs, the place was also very cozy, and the seat comfortable, although did not stay seated too long as i went to the front to see him close :) had a lot of fun here. 5 stars :)

A lot of people moving to Nashville are moving here because of country music and what it brings to the city. I am not one of those people. I don't listen to live music often. When I do, it's more often than not at the symphony hall or the opera (no I'm not 90, some 20/30-somethings like classical music, too!). So it means a lot when I say that listening to the Sunday Night Bluegrass Jam was one of the most wonderful and memorable experiences I've had in Nashville since moving here a year and a half ago. The music was great. Classic and interesting and moving. And the venue was amazing. It seems like it's the last original building in all of the Gulch! Skyscraper, skyscraper, skyscraper, The Station Inn. It's a Nashville legend. And it's still a great time. I highly recommend attending one of their Sunday Night Bluegrass Jams. It's a unique experience in this city. (Go early! We had to wait until people left before we could sit!)

Usually I tend to avoid bars that are described as touristy, however, I had a great time.

My favorite part was an awesome band they had playing. Their lead singer was a woman named Autumn Reynolds. She had such an amazing voice!! She could sing any country song well, if not better than the original singer. By the end of the night, major girl crush was developed. 

The only reason why this receives 4 stars instead of 5 was that it was slow to get drinks, but that's somewhat expected for a touristy bar in Nashville. The bartenders were very hardworking and made great drinks, but it would be worth it to add another bartender during busy times.

I love the decor and atmosphere here!  It's right on the river and there are a number of good spots to get comfortable and enjoy the live music or the beautiful view or the amazing local artwork.

I definitely didn't give it 4 stars for the service or food.  We sat at a table upstairs on the rooftop and we were ignored by 3 servers.  It wasn't even very busy.  So after a while (it seemed like 20 minutes) I went to the bar to try to get some service.  There were two other guys at the bar that got served before me and then I just sat there while the three girls just huddled up and seemed to be gossiping.  Eventually one  asked me what I wanted and I ordered two drinks and I tried to order the pretzels with beer cheese. She said they're not serving them now. We ended up skipping food and going somewhere else.

Having said that, it's still worth checking out.  You can relax at the awesome bar downstairs and enjoy live music or can relax in the swivel chairs in the next room and watch the band on tv or can enjoy the amazing view of Broadway, the stadium and the river.  It's a fantastic location that's right next to the Hard Rock Cafe.  The local artwork is also incredible.

Summary:

Design & Decor:          5
Location:                      5
Artwork & Ambiance:  5
Live Music:                   5
Service:                         1
Food:                             ?

If it's a weeknight and you are looking for a bit of a crazy crowd,  you might want to go elsewhere. 

It's huge. Which makes it look that much more empty. Of the 3 stories, only the bottom floor was open. It took the band *quite* awhile to go on. I don't know if they were waiting for someone or what, but the groupie with the crazy short shorts on kept us entertained. Beer selection here was slightly better than The Stage, and the waitress was attentive. 

Not my favorite, but the band was pretty good when they got going, and it was pretty nice to sit so close the stage without too many people crowding around.

The rooftop bar was empty and I had to wait for one of the 5 people working to give me a menu. Thought I would try the nachos and I guess they don't melt cheese on the nachos around here so I have to give a bad rating. Who serves nachos with cold cheese ??? Cool view but service and nachos are a no go.
Food is perfect every time we come! The staff is phenomenal. This is a weekly lunch stop for us and my wife and I make this place a stop when we get out on the weekends. Great food and cold beer!
