Great downtown Bar and restaurant. Jessica and Lila were fabulous waitresses and the food was phenomenal. I really enjoyed the Nashville hot chicken and waffles, this is the real thing guys!  Great entertainment, food, music, venue. Truly enjoyed it!

This place is okay- a 3.5. We were there for 2.5hr, though, and felt like we were listening to the same song the entire time, despite pleas to the DJ to mix it up a little bit. I certainly wouldn't go there if you're looking to dance; to sit around and chat it might work. (You might as well just go to 5th & Taylor next door and grab a drink at their bar and enjoy it there or in their beautiful outdoor space if you are just looking to chat.)
Good crowd though- everyone seemed friendly, a nice mix of different types of people, etc. I appreciated that.
Also, there had been a vase of flowers at the front door which I guess we're knocked over- no one working there bothered to clean it up so entry/exit were very slippery on the wet tiles.
The drinks seemed fine, the service "ok", and the ambience pretty good. I say ok for the service because they showed up quickly upon arrival and stopped by regularly, but someone in my group asked them to talk to a manager and their response was "I don't have time for that."
Very cool joint.  Paid a cover charge to see two great acts perform.  Scott Mulvahill and MountainHeart.  Good drinks, good service.  Safe. Would be glad to go back.

This was simply a great bar. Loved everything about it. Great drinks, extremely attentive bartenders , great music and a fun atmosphere. My wife and I highly enjoyed our night at at this bar. They even have a photo booth! Don't even get me started on the nachos!! Omg!!! Must get the nachos!! The band that was playing while I was there had a female singer whose voice was amazing! Deffinently recommend thus as a MUST STOP for anybody visiting Nashville!
If you want to experience old Nashville, not what Lower Broadway has become, come to the Station Inn. You will have a great time and be treated to world class musical talent.

Grabbed appetizers and few drinks with my party of 3. Waitress came back with our drinks and didn't know which drink was which. She smelled them in front of us to figure it out. A little odd but we laughed and made fun of her. So it was fun all around.

Pretty cool experience. I came to listen to the Music City Doughboys, Nashville's only Western Swing band other than the Time Jumpers.  It was a really good experience.  It cost $12 for the 2 hour performance.  Great deal.  Also, parking in the back is free.  And the Station Inn is located in the Gulch so lots of great hangouts for before and after.  I'm definitely coming back to listen to other country music or bluegrass performances... For a music venue that is so revered, the Station Inn is surprisingly unassuming, laid back, and very casual. It really seems like someone's cellar or something and they sell soda and pizza. Its basically a listening room, but it was actually really cool.

WOW!

Watching the Time Jumpers jam after a $13 prime rib meal is hard to beat.

This is an absolute must see on a Monday night in Nashville.

The guy at the front door tonight is a complete jerk called my 50 year old partner "old as dirt" but he needed to see his id.  We brought a guy from. Australia clearly in his late 50's didn't bring his passport refused to let him in.  Then caused a ruckus almost escalating into a fight.  I don't understand what their goal is there but they lost 9 patrons tonight because the guy at the front door was an Uber aggressive jerk with a napoleon complex.  We were there at 1020pm.  Don't go hear if your older than 14 and not wearing a tight skirt.  Borderline age discrimination.

We are locals and we LOVE this place for the most amazing breakfasts!!  Why wait in long lines at the other breakfast places when you can walk right into here and be served immediately!!  Bartenders are awesome.  The "Bloody Mary" is amazing and you get to make it yourself with all the goodies they have set out for you.  It will not disappoint!!  Highly recommend for a great downtown Nashville weekend break!

Still an awesome place and they do have "live music" each weekend morning too!!

Its Cheap Friendly and filled talented people. There no longer smoking in the bar. You will see some of the best songwriters in Nashville at Sam's Jams on Weds noon to and Lizards Writers Night on Thursday. Its right on Music Row, who know pop in for a cold one.

A very nice venue, unlike the venues I grew up going to in Florida. First of all, the food was FANCY! I got a portobello mushroom burger with arugula and a jack and Coke! (Well, Pepsi.) the bathrooms were clean and there were a sufficient number of stalls. Staff was helpful and smiling. The seating was very well thought out, it didn't look like anywhere was a bad place to view the state from. The grass you sit on is soft, but they allow you to bring low-back chairs or a blanket. I want to come back soon to enjoy another show here.

I was there last week and loved it. I'm from California, and didn't want the experience of flashy Broadway. I ordered pizza and beer and caught a blue grass jam session. The place filled up real fast. The staff is friendly! I will be back when I return to Nashville. Thanks, Marty!

This place was crazy!! Awesome band was playing all weekend beautiful women what more could you ask for?! The only reason I'm giving it a 4 star instead of a 5 star review is bc I'm pretty sure one of the bartender's stole $20 in change she was suppose to give to me but just threw it in the register instead but the manager made things straight and gave us a free round of drinks so that was ok.

Courtney & Daniella are the best bartenders in Nashville! As a local you want to be treated well & you want your bar staff to understand you aren't a tourist! We have been treated so well all day! Both these bartenders are friendly, engaging & fun! 
I recommend this place to locals & tourists alike!
Had a great time with my friends. We tried local Tennessee beers and all of them were great. Live music was awesome. Great place to visit if you are in Nashville..
Went on a monday night, incredible music and vibe!  Treat yourself and go back in time and visit the Station Inn for a true ole time Nashville experience. You won't regret it!

Went on Sunday brought some friends visiting from Michigan, was disappointed in not getting a table. There was six of us and we noticed two tables with one person obviously saving the table but drinking water? We left and took our money else where and had a great time. 

Here's hoping that someday Honky Tonk Central gets a policy on table saving.

Busy place on the weekends and at nights. Each floor had a different band playing which was nice. It's a fairly typical Broadway bar with multiple stories. A stop for lots and lots of bachelorette parties.

Who doesn't love live music and people watching?!?  The res of the experience?  Meh!  The bartenders were difficult to flag down (They tended to stand on one end of the bar chit-chatting quite often.) and the cocktails were not too tasty.  

As for the other bar patrons?  A few too many individuals who could not hold their liquor.  I do not appreciate have cocktails dropped on me because other people could not hold their beverages straight?  l

As for the bathroom?  Nasty!  I could not have gotten out of there soon enough.  

Would I go back here during my next Nashville visit?  I hope not.

the band playing there today was so talented, and incredibly entertaining.  Brought many customers on their feet, and was able to keep the customers smiling and laughing with their wit.  Buffalo wings and beers- great.

Great music. Great People. Great Bartenders. 
Met Will tonight and he exceeded my expectations as a superior bartender.  I feel a sense of home here.  This will be a regular spot in Nash.
Brand new music venue for downtown Nashville and a truly great addition!!!   Highly recommend!!!!
I've been in Nashville for 3 days. Checked this place out each day and the bands on each floor were great. Lots of talent. Come here for a good time day or night.
Fun venue to check out "The Time Jumpers" and have dinner. Food was average but the drinks are great.

Don't go.  Very rude establishment.  Refused our valid government ID since we are not from the USA!!!  Demanded passports!  Who the heck carries around a passport?

If you aren't USA born and bread, go elsewhere.  In fact, go  to the Swinging Door Saloon just around the corner.  They were happy to take our money, sang great music and provided us with decent food.  And the best was, they were happy to accept our NON-USA government issued ID and our NON-USA Visa card!!!!!

Benchmark, you are the only place in Nashville that has NOT been pleasant to us!

Was on the green for Live on the Green, and wasn't green with envy at all while I chilled in the VIP. 

One of Nashville's premier mini festivals, Live on the Green is a fun free concert experience. They have some alright lineups, usually headlined by one band everyone comes to see. The nearby streets get packed so you may want to come early. 

Got VIP tickets and stood from the side of the stage. Got to see Cold War Kids when I went and they put on a great show. The VIP included some food, nothing special. Just some pizza and donuts. What made it worth it was the view and the free beer, despite the beer being of basic quality. 

Come to Live on the Green for a fun concert experience.

BY FAR the worst experience i've Had in Nashville. We went her for the 2018 new year celebration. We paid 50 dollars per person online for tickets just to get into the bar, which was pretty standard on NYE but when we arrived there was a HUGE line. They had oversold tickets and were not letting anyone in. To make matters worse it was 3 degrees with windchill. Once we got into the bar, they weren't even letting people up to the top floor. The fire alarm went off and none of the staff addressed the problem. After waiting 30 minutes (not an exaggeration) to get our drinks, the bartender didn't even give us limes. 

This was such a terrible experience, and the worst part is they aren't even addressing how terrible they messed up last night. I'm sure other people will be writing similar reviews.

Live music, fabulous location, beer and food trucks. Doesn't get much better. 

The FREE Live on the Green music festival series has been going on in Public Square Park for 6 years - and my husband and I have been lucky enough to go to almost every single one. Held on Thursday nights (for typically 5 weeks in a row) the festival boasts some of the best music in town and it's not to be missed.  Last year, they added on a weekend festival to cap off the series. HUGE success as many more folks attended on the weekend. (my only reason for not giving it 5 starts is the fact that they've definitely outgrown their venue. I also wish they would make this event 21 and up, but the logistics of that would be difficult.)

The 2015 lineup is incredible! Passion Pit, Ben Folds, Rodrigo y Gabriela, Moon Taxi. I'm drooling already. 

Over the years, more and more amazing food trucks and beer vendors come out to participate, providing guests with anything they could possibly want to nosh on and drink. 

But with that comes the crowds. We attended the first show of the year last night and were amazed at how crowded it was - so be prepared for that. The event is always a blast - it's always so fun to be surrounded by like-minded music fans, enjoying the summer weather and having a great time. What a great city we live in, huh? 

Enjoy! 

Tips: 
Get there as early as you can (the place starts filling up around 5). 
Many people bring chairs to sit in, but as soon as the shows start everyone stands - making the chairs just a pain to lug around. Bring a blanket instead. 
The food truck lines are unavoidable, so if you have a hankering for a specific one, be ready to wait. 
Porta-pottys abound - no getting around it. :) 
I wish I had a tip for parking, but my husband and I walk to the event, so I have no words of wisdom there. 
Children are welcome, but strollers at this event would be an absolute nightmare due to the sardine-like crowds. 
We always bring our dog - and see many others, so crowd-friendly dogs are also welcome. Your bags will most likely be checked on the way in, so don't attempt to bring in beer - you'll be turned away. 
There is a couple water fountains at the location that are meant to be played in - enjoy them on those hot summer nights!

Extremely cool bar. Didn't have to wait to get it, but it was around 2 am when we got here and it was dying down. Service was crap but it's understandable with how many people where there.The band that was playing was fantastic! Love this place

War Memorial is where TPAC sends its less mainstream acts. The up and comers or those that maybe had their heyday last decade. What this means is you can see great bands and shows on the cheap in what amounts to a pretty good venue. Breaking Benjamin, Brand New, and the Flaming Lips are a few groups I've caught here. The venue reminds me of a very nice high school or community college auditorium. There is a large general admission standing room only floor surrounded by a wrap around balcony. The best seats in my opinion are the front balcony but really the size of the place means their are no bad seats. Acoustically it's small enough that a good rock band can really blow out your eardrums but a quieter performer can still put on a good show. It's not however perfect, The speakers are all to the front and on stage so you don't get the immersion of surround sound that larger venues with overheads and back of venue speakers have. And there can certainly be a rough concert in a gym sound to the place. Honestly if your band or theater act is playing here just go. It will be a good time. I'd recommend lyft to get here but there is parking downtown if you must drive. There is usually beer and alcohol served. A budlight will typically run you 8 dollars. The restroom situation is a bit of a hassle  they are in the basement and a bit hard to access if your in the balcony, at least you will burn off a few calories from the beer getting to them. Overall though this place rocks.

Awesome place!! Musicians fantastic! Went there for the Sunday Jam. Probably the best experience of our Nashville trip. Talented musicians (aged from 8 to 80) doing what they love. 
Will recommend it to all! 
I'll be back there every time I visit Nashville.
LOVE IT!!

Drinks were served in plenty! Deep fried pickles were ok, but chicken nachos were SO good!
Guy singer for Oct 17, was good.
Waitresses were very nice!

Great place for live music, drinking, people watching, and just fun. Not sure about the food but I hear the wings are "the best". Never saw so many "Brides To Be" and their entourages. Looks like cover starts at 10pm so start before then and stay. Boots and black are obviously in. Wear anything, might include ear plugs. Yeh, I'm over 50.

We were here on a Monday night and we love this place! The live music was awesome and it wasn't packed at all - the type of vibe we love.    

Between my friends and I, we shared the supreme nachos and catfish basket which was surprising more than enough for us. The portion was very generous and it was delicious. I love being able to try local beer and tasted my first moonshine. It was a great experience overall. 

The staff took care of us very well so it is an added plus.
The beer was cold and there was a band. Not a bad band but not that great. This is a good 21-25 year old spot.

Good music
Great Band
Service is slow because it was packed!!!!

If you are in Nashville and want to listen to great live music and have a great time this is the place. If you are lucky enough to have Sebastian be your sever it makes it that much better. That kid works his behind off. Had a great time.
My favorite place ever! 3 story bar with awesome music and delicious burgers! Saturday morning is packed!
Dark, dingy, but good for live music.  The bathrooms had this overwhelming sewer gas smell - egads.  Cheap draft beers kept us there for 2 drinks, instead of our standard 1 and done.
What a great place with below freezing beer on tap! 3 floors of casual class, and a rooftop view that's not packed with college kids! Good burger and service!

Ohhhh Nashville Underground. 
Don't get me wrong, this place wasn't the worst. But it wasn't stellar either. We started off on a bad note when we arrived early for our reservation, only to be seated over an HOUR later. The very nice hostesses were both apologetic, but when several larger parties are waiting for tables, I would at least try to make things happen. (I worked in food & bev for long enough to have a solution for tables that overstay their welcome..but I wasn't going to tell them how to do their jobs!) 
Regardless, we decided to pass the time valiantly and drink. The bar was rather scarce at the far end, so a few of us went to get a drink. The bartender (with the black messy bun) could not have been more rude...which explains why no one wanted to be in her company. She straight up told us she didn't want to be there. At least act like you like your job to get a few extra tips, amirite? I was kind of in shock about the whole experience leading up to this point but had to remind myself that it was the busiest part of Nashville on St. Pats. This is why I could cut some slack. The waitress at our table was very nice and handled he workload rather well. Unfortunately, the food wasn't anything special. I did enjoy the hot chicken on top of my Mac and cheese, as well as the asparagus off of a friend's plate. 

I would recommend this place IF you and a few friends wanted to grab a beer and enjoy some live music. But then again that is almost everywhere in Nashville, so take your pick!

Don't eat the brunch here. It's all sad sad food. Fishy gumbo, soggy fries, nasty salad, "avocado toast" on untoasted white bread smeared with guac (not FRESH avocado...blasphemy!) and "meh" biscuits and gravy overloaded with pepper. No one in our group was happy with their items.

Come for the drinks and atmosphere. Eat somewhere else, just sayin.

I love the look of this place. The female bartender on Saturday night was awesome. The male bartender on Sunday night was not so great. 

They had a great local gin along with a good variety of other gins which I appreciated. I loved the atmosphere, with very old architecture and hodge podge appearance. There was a couch (living room style) in one of the areas with a tv to watch games which was nice. I like the entrance in the alley way as well. I didn't try any food. This rating is for Saturday night. 

Sunday night, the bartender didn't communicate well when taking orders. For example, they apparently had a 2 for 1 deal on beers. He didn't say anything when my friend ordered a beer. He just tossed a chip onto the bar and walked away. We had to get his attention to ask what the chip was otherwise we would have just ignored its presence as it wasn't necessarily given to anyone. The first set of drinks were very weak. I watched him measure with a shot glass and he didn't even fill it all the way up. The second drinks he didn't even measure, just poured the alcohol in and they were much better. I guess he liked us by then?

Then the live music that was playing was all sad. We requested a happy song and put money in the tip jar. He continued to play sad music and stated that 95% of people are sad (so that is why he is singing sad songs). 

Then , things got weird. Our friend walked into the men's restroom and the bartender and the musician were canoodling or something more sinister. When my friend walked back to the bar, he looked stunned and said we needed to leave.  

So, needless to say, we had an interesting experience.

We came here on a Friday night and had a lot of fun.  Once the live band starts playing the place gets pretty crowded up front but there was always room to get a drink.  David Ray and his band were playing when we were there and they were great.  All of the band was very good, David Ray knows how to get the crowd going, the guitar player was excellent, and the fiddler player was so good.  I recommend coming here if you are in town, especially if they are playing.

Anyone who has ever seen them, they had a blonde woman come in while David Ray was taking a break. I cant remember her name but she kept the crowd going and was a lot of fun as well!
Awesome music.  The bar is a bit expensive and they started charging us for bottled water all of a sudden.  Water at a bar should be free always. I'm trying not to get crazy drunk and sick.

War Memorial is the worst venue in the city. I've attended several concerts here, and every time its the same situation. If you want to get a drink, including water, be prepared to wait in a 45+ plus line while you miss the concert you paid to see. The bartenders are nice, however they aren't use to dealing with large crowds. You also can't start a tab, which slows down the process further. While at JRAD last night, we waited in line for over 30 minutes at the start of the second set, to be told when we got up to order our drinks, that they were out of all beer and mixers. If you're in the back of reserved seating you won't be able to see the stage. The only thing that would get me to go back to War Memorial would be Jerry Garcia himself coming back to life and playing a one night only show there.

I loved this place. I came here as a tourist and I didn't try any of the food because we had just eaten at Jack's BBQ. Therefore, the only aspect I can judge about the Honkey Tonk is through drinks and music and both were some of the best I experienced in Nashville. The drinks weren't watered down as they are at most bars, yet they weren't too strong so they tasted great. However, the music was the true gem of this place. There are three floors and each floor had great music. However, the third floor was my favorite. I am a country fan, but my boyfriend is more of a classic rock fan. The band that was playing covered country (of course) and classic rock which he loved. It was impossible not to get up and dance even for my boyfriend who never wants to dance. It was very crowded but perhaps because I am 24 I didn't mind it and found it was more crowded at the other bars. Don't get intimidated by the line because there are three floors so it doesn't get as packed as you'd think. Plus, if they have bands like they had Sat night the music is completely worth it.

Worst service. Took 1 1/2 hours for a medium burger, after asking 6 times where it was. Waitress argued with us about order, then realized she did take it & blamed the kitchen. Rolled her eyes & complained numerously that her job was difficult. Each time we asked for a manager, a different security guard came to talk to us. There are too many other good places to choose from , don't waste your time
Does this place still exist?  Tried to go on a Friday night at midnight and found it unopened.  Maybe some better signage and posted open times would be helpful...

This place is a nice swanky joint downtown of Nashville. I can't believe there hasn't been a review for this place.

First off, myself and group of friends were attracted to the beautiful country live music coming from this place. Nice building and nice set up. So it wasn't hard to decide to eat here.

The menu was amazing! Lots of delicious meals and appetizers. Which I wish I had the chance to try all I them. The deep fried catfish was my choice. It was so succulent and perfectly seasoned that I left no crumbs else on the plate.

The service was good! Our waitress was quick, the food was quick and the music was good. Can't complain! One thing that would be nice if they had free appetizer like chips to hold us over while waiting.

Overall, if you are new to Nashville this is a must try place. Love this restaurant and bet it rocks on with its live music!!

What to say? Well, the overall vibe from this place is right up my alley. I don't care for locations where I am forced to stand, pressed against sweaty masses of kids pretending to be adults. I like a place where I can sit and eat and have a drink and enjoy good music. This place absolutely fits the bill. The food? The food is bar food. But it's plenty good bar food. I would rather they have a nice selection of taps, but given the quality of the sound mix, the comfort of being able to sit at a table and enjoy a show, and the overall feel, I am more than happy to come back again and again.

Music and drinks were great.  However, clean up a little. The main floor in this place smells like a morgue that lost power and refrigeration for 6 days.  Go to 2nd and 3rd floors for breathability, where it is less musty.

Saw Haim and Lizzo here. This venue was wicked. Drink prices were outrageous. The bathrooms are on the bottom level so if you need to go while the concert is going on it may take a while. They served food but didn't purchase - just a nice perk. The concert was hands down top 5 best concerts I have ever been too and that's saying a lot. I sat front row at Fleetwood Mac and I was in the very back row in balcony for this one. Still top 5 of all time.
Rooftop DJ and service was great. Bottom floor... the most disrespectful and rudest bartenders I've encountered in all of Nashville.

Okay...I give out 5 stars as often as Paris Hilton speaks a four syllable word...so I really enjoyed this place. Veruca and I saw the Time Jumpers....Vince Gill....what happened bro? Doesn't matter...these guys as a band were awesome. Drinks were reasonable....seating is tough....real tough..get there early kids. This place is totally my friend though...minus the cowboy boots. Loved you guys....will be back again in my lifetime. Try the red beans and rice...it is good!
Bad. Just bad service is terrible, food so sub par I think they got it out of the trash
I have been stopping here for 15 years. This is the kind of place that all big stuffy bars try to be. Just a cool place to hang out and chill.
Didn't eat just drinks food look good. 46 bucks for 4 bloody Mary's and build your own. Another tourist trap.

This place is an absolute disgrace! We thought we would grab some dinner at the Honky Tonk Central! My sister and 3 cousins entered, i showed my ID  and as I went to enter and the bouncer told me I could not enter with my very small backpack. I chose to bring my backpack due to the fact that it  had been down pouring ALL DAY and my party of five needed jackets and umbrellas - the bouncer insisted I could not come in with my backpack even though I promised him he could look through it. He told me I would not be welcome at any of the other bars in the area with a backpack, which was Of course not true at all! The real kicker was while my sister and cousins  went to use the restroom at this extremely poorly run place - I watched a young girl walk right up to the bouncer with a backpack purse on and scoot right in! This place obviously discriminates against 50 year old women! Fortunately we were able to get excellent service from JasonAldean's  bar, Luke Bryan's bar,  and Blake Shelton's bar and I was more than happy to leave exceptional tips for the excellent service I received from these great bars that obviously respect all women - not just cute blondes! The owner of the Honky Tonk needs to revisit their "backpack" policy and train their $10 an hour, super rude "bouncers" to learn how to deal with the public! This guy was a real "jerk"! As a visitor from California, I am surprised and disgusted by this kind of treatment! What a disappointment!!!
Cozy, laidback, open bar with friendly staff. It just opened up, so they're still working out the ambiance and the construction, but you can tell it'll be great. Check them out.

What a wonderful experience. I loved every second of Counting Crows this past Friday night. What a wonderful addition to Nashville. The backdrop of the amphitheater is the beautiful Nashville skyline, took my breath away! The size is perfect and no matter were you are you are always close to a bar, food, and restrooms!
Great place to see top bluegrass bands. Make sure you come early, since you need to line up and make sure you get inside and get a good seat.

Very disappointed!!  Stopped in to have drinks at our second stop in Nashville, blonde Monday night bartender carded me and saw I was from out of state and decided to charge me $16 for two small shots of Jack in a paper cup. Very unprofessional.  When asked about the price, she mumbled something about having other shots for $5.  She lost this place some decent business as we were planning to meet people here for dinner.

Came here on the recommendation of a local musician. Fun place for live music styled like a music hall. Saw the band the Time Jumpers. They've performed with Willie Nelson, Miranda Lambert, Amy Grant and Vince Gill. Very fun and lively blues country and western music. Enjoyed it immensely.

They performed for a couple hours, favorites were "Don't roll your bloodshot eyes st me" and "All that's left".

What a great place to have some drinks, even though they are expensive, and listen to some great Music.  We were lucky enough to be there the day a former contestant from "The Voice" showed up and was asked to sing.  I don't watch the show, so I don't know her name, but she was really good.  Sing along, dance, or just sway around in your chair.  Don't expect to be able to carry on a conversation with anyone as it is very loud.  Do take yourself upstairs and see the view!

Attended a private party here the day before the 2015 CMT Music Awards.

Live band, good food, cold drinks.

And a great view of the action on Broadway from the 2nd floor balcony.

No complaints.
A bunch of country music artists incapable of writing a song. Menu items featuring out of season produce. Pretentious as it gets. This is essentially a dressed up dive bar.

While my concert was amazing and the location was awesome, I am HIGHLY unsatisfied with their policy on confiscated items. This is an email I sent directly to their livenation account: I just left a concert and my items were STOLEN. Your policy on throwing confiscated items in grass is ridiculous at best. All I was told when I asked about it was that "you had the option to take it to your car" and NO ONE gave me that option. In fact, I was told that they would keep it in a secure area and that they NEVER have problem with theft. Which is strange because almost EVERYONE who came there couldn't find their belongings. I had an item that was fairly unrecognizable so I attached a keychain that had sentimental value to me so I could recognize it. Thanks to your lying employees and incompetent policy, my items are gone for good. This email is to thank you for your careless actions. Oh, and one of your security SNATCHED a set list from a PAYING fan's hand. Keep in mind who keeps you in business.

The music 5 stars! Amazing venue! Time Jumpers on Mondays are such a treat to see and you cannot beat the price!  Food is bar grub and service is on the slow side just because there are so many peple packed in and it seemes a little hard for the server to get through. I was cold and wished I brought a sweat shirt. If you have a large party you might need to go early to sit together, but small parties of two can probably sqeeze upfront right before the show without a problem.

I thoroughly enjoyed NYE at nashville underground! The line may have been a little lengthy, but it was New Years so I understand. What really made the night was that our bartender Eden introduced herself and remembered what my husband and I were drinking all night. She served us with a smile even though they were slammed. I really appreciate her service and hope to see her there again soon!
Here for the 2nd time this week to see North Mississippi Allstars.  Ate here last night.  Good bar food. Great concert!

War Memorial has an interesting mix of acts....I've seen popular 90's rock bands, one of Jack White's newest projects, and a variety of other bands. It's definitely unique! 

I really like GA because even if it is sold out, it's never too crowded. You can hang in the back and dance or mosh in the front (if it's happening). If you prefer to sit down, they have an entire balcony with seats. Sweet! 

My only complaint is that the drink line out front is always long and you are jostled around while waiting because it's pretty packed right there at the entrance. They typically have some beer stations in the venue that makes it a bit easier though. 

Overall, the shows I've seen here are always a good time!

Great music. The appetizers were delicious but the Prime Rib Sandwich was AWFUL!!!! Very fatty and tough. I would have given it more stars if the sandwich was good and the wait staff more attentive. Couldn't find the waitress for over 30 minutes to get our check. Seems like they may have been short staffed though. I will still go back.

I was really disappointed with this place. I had reserved a big table for a bachelorette lunch and had high hopes but this place failed to deliver. I don't know if we just came on a bad day, maybe this place is good otherwise and we just had bad luck. First of all, we waited about 15 min to just get our table cleaned and get menus. Once we got menus the manager came to our table and said they were closing the rooftop in an hour which was fine because we were planning on leaving by then anyways. It took another 15 minutes for someone to just take our order. A couple of us ordered bloody mary's and they were awful.... none of us were able to drink them. Then once we placed our orders, a couple of us got our plates and were waiting for everyone else to get their food too. Well we ended up waiting about 30 minutes for everyone to get their food. The food trickled in one plate at a time and by the time we all got our food we had to inhale it since the floor we were sitting in was closing. If the rooftop was closing due to personnel issues, I just wish the manager would have told us beforehand so we could have gone somewhere else. I felt bad for the waitress because it looked like she was doing the job of 3 different people. The food was mediocre as well. Nothing I'd go back for.

We sadly only were able to go on Saturday night, but it was an amazing atmosphere! Who doesn't love amazing atmospheres, local brews, and free music from great headliners?! It was our first night in the city, and it was a great introduction to Nashville. 

The beers were only $6 which was great for a festival of its kinds, especially being free. 

I would 100% go back to this event, hopefully next year!

We went here for my birthday on a Bluegrass Jam Session night and it was amazing! We had such a great time and they sang happy birthday to me! It was wonderful. Nothing fancy - just beer and good music.

Awesome!  The service was fantastic and the music was better.  This establishment is not jammed with drunk kids which is a big plus.  If you are in Nashville, take a very short walk from 4th and Broadway area to 2nd and you will be happy you did.
Acoustics are a little loud but they have a great calendar of shows.

Fun place for a beer on the open third floor.  Good views and good music. The staff was efficient and the band interacted with crowded bringing everyone together.  A fun place to take break.  We did not eat here so can't vouch for the food but people around us seemed pleased.

Killer nachos. The live music was great. We went in the middle of the afternoon but it seemed as though it would be a great place to party at night with 3 floors packed full of people. The prices were the same as anywhere else downtown.

Great food and drinks, but a little disappointed that we were here for all of a few hours, requested Wagon Wheel, paid good tip and they didn't play it. It's a country bar and no Wagon Wheel!???!! Maybe they didn't know it....

Its a cool place to catch a concert because its kind of small and you can usually get good tickets if you are an early shopper. But it has a few drawbacks......You will most likely have to walk a good piece if you are there at concert time....come a few hours early and you may get lucky...with cheap/free street parking. TPACs web site has some good info on parking.

If TPAC has something going on you can use their valet (right across the street) for a large fee.....(18 bucks!) and they tell you to come get your car just as soon as your show ends or you may be stranded.

Some cheaper limited view seats are worth it....some are not. If you buy far left/right floor tickets your view will be blocked 80% due to poor placement of amp stacks on stage, but tickets will be 20-30 dollars cheaper. (this is not true for all shows but just ask to make sure)

No food of any kind is sold or allowed to be brought in..... 

You cannot (if seen) bring in outside food or drink.(they will make you throw away your drink/food before entering if seen)

Drinks are sold, but are expensive for the venue I think. Plain Water is 4 dollars a bottle......Drinks are even more.

Be prepared ....they check bags and purses.

Can be super cold in the winter and the seats on the floor are as uncomfortable as the Rymans (you WILL get numb ass after an hour) so be prepared.

Long lines at all bathrooms is normal, so go during a song.

The security/house staff is quite overbearing when it comes to phones/pics/videos. If they see your lit screen they will give you 8-10 seconds to focus and take a picture if you linger they will be on you like white on rice! They also bust balls over approaching the stage even if an artist is handing out picks/items to fans, and they will not tolerate dancing in the aisles.....imagine that!.....you must dance at your seat.

It could be more fan friendly........but tickets are somewhat cheaper and its small....sooooo.

Typical bar food fun atmosphere with a variety of bands playing on each floor they have some neat local beers . Our waitress was very nEach band that plays walks around every few minutes asking for tips . We did tip every time . It was little off putting when my friend gave 5 dollars and requested a song and the response was that will be 20. All ages allowed I I saw kids ranging from infants to 13

Nashville Underground is the biggest extortionist scam in Nashville. At the end of our night, they gave us a receipt with nothing broke down upwards of $200 and refused to specify what cost what. Poorly ran, no help from management, and refused to speak with us about specifics. I'm very skeptical of their honesty, and warn anyone who considers spending time here to be very frugal and knowledgeable of what they are purchasing.
Come by and have a few drinks listen to the bands on one of the three floors have a bite to eat and enjoy yourself. You never know who you will see here.

It is no surprise that the Ascend Ampitheatre exists in a town known as The Music City.  Just a few blocks from the honkey-tonks of Broadway, the indoor Bridgestone Arena, and the legendary Ryman Auditorium, this venue is a beautiful addition to the music scene.

Dropped into a riverfront park, Ascend is a smaller joint that is easily accessible from the street grid.  I don't know what the parking situation looks like since I was staying at the Hilton a couple blocks away.  However, I found this easy to get into, seemed more intimate, and the staff were friendly and accommodating.

Granted, I was seeing the legendary Neil Young - so the audience may have been on the nature side - and the weather was absolutely delightful, but I had an amazing time.  We had reserved seats in row T of Section 103 and found the sound to be great, perfect sight lines to the stage, and a great audience.

If you have the opportunity to catch a show at Ascend, do it.  Oh ... and Neil Young is still rockin the free world at 70 years old.  An amazing show - even though I would have liked to have heard a few more of his monster hits like Cinnamon Girl, Old Man, or My My Hey Hey.

The band Jordan McCant and Autumn Reynolds was awesome!  The bartender Danielle was amazing, super friendly.  The bartender who sang with the band absolutely incredible definitely already a star!   Five starsto this place you guys are awesome!
I was here for a private party and during the party and food was great and so was the service.  After the party the service downstairs wasn't good and very slow.

This place is awful and racist. I asked the bartender (a blonde chick with a terrible sport's headband and sparkles in her hair) for a water and because I intended to bring it to the bathroom attendant she insisted I pay $2.25. I fully intended to tip her and the sweating attendant never asked me for the water. This chick clearly thought that serving beer makes her better than those that clean bathrooms which is totally wrong. It was offensive. I find a place that employs people like this to be downright offensive. Bottom end this dumb bitch lost out on a tip because she's an idiot and will probably work in a bar for the rest of her life.
Local flair, loved the Bluegrass, highly recommend.  A place you definitely want to see succeed.  My wife and I will be back, very casual, and everyone was into the music!
Good selection of beers.  Excellent happy hour.  Live music is better here than on Broadway downtown.

We checked into our hotel and headed straight to Broadway. Honky Tonk Central's open-plan three story bar appealed to us, as we wanted to see the city and get a bite to eat. We sat on the 3rd story balcony and enjoyed a couple drinks with our lunch. The portion sizes on the food were pretty impressive. However, the drink prices were as high as the third story balcony we were sitting on.
Me likey!  Kudos to an awesome staff who made this first time visitor welcome!  Ok, so I'll make this longer.  The band was also funny, and sang a little Justin Bieber.

What could be nicer than seeing an old 80's band from your home country (OMD) sitting on the grass with a tarp pulled around you to protect from a light drizzle supping a pricey glass of wine with the one you love.  Sing a long we did with the Nashville skyline behind the stage.  No brolly's aloud, chairs avail to rent and a good view no matter where you are. A great addition to the city

We've visited Nashville many times and always end up in the 2nd level. The first level is usually crazy packed and loud! I highly recommend venturing up to the 2nd level for a great time! Every singer/band on the 2nd level has been amazing in our experience. And i can't forget to mention how quick the service is on the 2nd level!! Quick food and quick drinks!! Don't stand in line on the first level head upstairs!!

Sexually profiled by an African American bouncer here. Luckily someone let us in. Do not hate on gay people or "pretend to be gay" not to let a beautiful 21 year old in. It will bite you in the ass. 2015, you ignorant POS.

went to a Wild Feathers show in this space. Arrive early for a decent experience. They put down a TON of tables, which can be a fight to arrange, especially if there are more than 4 people in your crew. If you are around one of the trafficked areas of the bar, you are going to HATE your show. People are moving around like crazy. The bartenders are slightly slow in my opinion, making pretty typical drinks in a mediocre timeframe.  Can't speak for the food though.
Awesome place for live music and great drinks.  We came here multiple times over the span of a week.  The red bull slushie is amazing.  They truly have the best live music on 2nd.

This place is a guaranteed good time if you're in the downtown Nashville area. Lucky for us, this bar was right around the corner from our hotel (also not so lucky for us, because the noise level is redonk when you're trying to sleep after a long day of day drinking) but whatever, we were there for a bachelorette party and probably shouldn't have been sleeping anyway.

3 floors of huge bars, live music, and good looking people: what more could you ask for? We found ourselves here every chance we got and I think it's where most of our memories from our trip came from.

I highly recommend this place if you're looking to dance and party. I just wish it wasn't always SO crowded and was slightly easier to get drinks. But besides that, it's like a bar on steroids that is a ton of fun.

Terrible place to go with an extremely rude staff.never got the drinks we had ordered and they made us wait outside in 11 degree weather with the doors locked due to "overcrowding" when there was hardly anyone inside! Save your money and go elsewhere!

Our  Annual girls trip was to Nashville this year. We had a blast at Honkey Tonk. We enjoyed the best bands, best service. Everyone was so friendly! We visited other bars, but always ended up back at the Honkey Tonk. Hands down our favorite of Nashville. The bands were great, engaging with the crowd, so much fun! Already planning a return trip with my husband!

I saw Florence and the Machine at this amphitheater last weekend. Entrance was easy, the bathrooms were nice, plenty of beer carts, seating was general admission on the lawn & although it had rained it wasn't too bad. The view from the amphitheater is exceptional and it was a great way to start a weekend in Nashville.

First off...the food is awful. Straight from the freezer, to a fryer, to your table hopefully warm. The service was great though. If you are going on a Monday for the Time Jumpers get there early like 6:00. The tables start getting full about then. Eat before you go though.

FREE LIVE MUSIC! Lots and lot of people attend (about 15,000-20,000) a night. 

The only downfall is being crowded and blazing hot in the Tennessee sun.

There was knee slapping. There was jigging. There was everything is expect when I saw Old Crow Medicine Show. 

I attended the new Amphitheater with my friend who had an extra free GA ticket. There were sights, sounds, old men dancing, and an overall good time. The place definitely makes for a good concert venue. 

Upon arrival we ordered up two tall boys of bud light. The beer selection here is lacking. C'mon there are so many great breweries in Nashville. Why on earth are you forcing people to drink this?

The lawn is nice. Perfect for a big group to lay out and enjoy themselves. We saw people who attempted to sit or stand in front of the lawn were quickly ushered along. Unless of course you sat in the end of the lawn, all the way to the side. No one was shooing anyone away, you would have to do it yourself. After awhile though, how many times can you say something to different people. 

The highlights though were the environment and the culture. You ain't in Tennessee unless there is a sign that says, "Please No Guns", no metal detector, and just an old lady politely asking if we did indeed have any guns. As I mentioned the hooting, hollering, knee slapping, and dancing were out in full force. I'm glad I got to experience first hand. 

This is an awesome concert venue. Just needs to step up the beer game.

Not a fan of the tip "shake down" as the singer stuck his collection drum in our face as he paraded the room begging for cash because "Honky Tonk don't pay us". Well, we all know by now that no bar pays their bands but every other music club we visited had a jar discretely placed on the stage....and we know what it is for if we like your music.
Excellent new bar in Printers Alley...great atmosphere in a very unique location. Small food bites and very friendly patrons!

Absolutely awful food & service. Took us 90min to get our food after ordering and the waitress never came back to check in on us. After the long wait, the food was meh. So many great restaurants in Nashville, skip this one. Having a great band is the only thing this place has going for them.

This place is a great music venue, and a good place for drinks, although a bit on the pricey side. However, I do not recommend eating here. I ordered the cheeseburger and fries, and my 2 friends ordered the patty melt. After 30 mins of waiting, the food finally can out.  The meat tasted like dog food. There was a funny flavor, and I think it gave me food poisoning! The only redeeming part was the fries, and you know those are frozen. The same went for the patty melts. All in all, stick to beer and wine, or fries. The mixed drinks are weak and you'll have to order a lot to taste anything.

A truly great place to stop for a beer. i had a seasonal draft of a peanut butter stout that was recommended. the staff is friendly and the environment is classic, comfortable and laid back. You should go.

I LOVED this bar. It is a dive bar and I mean that in a good way, they had exceptionally great bluegrass music. I will note that they only serve beer and hard cider which can be an issue for some.  If ever back in Nashville I will plant myself there for a few days!! Wish it was near to Chicago so I could go all the time.
Ordered two drinks. They were over priced and did not taste good. Had to drink it tho cause it cost so much.

Perfect place to hear some authentic bluegrass picken away from the noisy mega-honky tonks downtown. Intimate venue with no smoke smell that is much more family friendly (at least for teens) than anywhere else we went - the focus is on the music and not the drinking. It was absolutely perfect for what we wanted to do, give our music crazy 16 yo a night on the town.

The owner plays a stand up bass and emcees when he and his buddies play and it's obvious they are having a blast. They book other acts and the cover varies depending on who's playing but we thought the "house band", who also play Sunday's for bluegrass night, were amazing.

Prices were reasonable and the food is decent comfort food - the pimento cheese is especially good though. Overall the perfect place for anyone looking for great music and friendly atmosphere.

How could I not like this place? 

-There was a big, burly security guard walking around the first floor like he was auditioning for America's Next Top Model. It was fantastically hilarious.
-The live band was really good. They mostly sang country songs but then added a few other random songs into the mix. The lead singer sang a country version of "Hit Me Baby One More Time". It was great!
-The beer was pretty cheap.
-I really liked my food. I got fries and chicken fingers with buttermilk ranch dressing. The chicken was soooo good and the dressing was delish!

It was definitely a great place to start the night off.

The grounds are beautifully kept and is enjoyable for a leisurely stroll. Being married to a war veteran makes this place much more meaningful to me. 

The war museum annex of the TN State Museum, covering the many TN residents who made the ultimate sacrifice in defense of our country, is located here in the basement. The entrance can be a little difficult to locate but so worth it. It is also free and covers all of the wars. History buffs will enjoy the photographs and the memorabilia on full display. 

I cannot wait to come back to enjoy a concert in the auditorium.
This place is amazing! Everything from the wings, Mac and cheese, ribs, and YES the banana pudding!

Picture some of the best music you have ever heard in a VFW hall. With folding chairs and all. We went for the 9:00 show and saw Heather and Shannon Slaughter. Their music was amazing. In any other city you would have had to get tickets in advance and paid twice as much. If you are visiting Nashville stop by and for sure you will hear a great night of music.

This is a really good venue.  It has easy access to the interstate just off the Shelby Ave exit ramp and over the bridge.  There's parking nearby and if you use www.parkwhiz.com you can get great parking a block away for $5 or $6.  The facility is nice as is the layout of things.  The box seats they offer are awesome.  You pay a high price but you get free parking a block away; access to a private lounge and private outside courtyard.  The lounge has a free buffet provided by Margaritaville and a live band performs while you dine.  The lounge also has bathrooms.  You can go in and out of the lounge as often as you want.  The box seats are located between the chair seating in the front and the lawn in the back.  What's great is you have four chairs and a table with plenty of room.  Plus the box seats are a couple of feet higher than the people in the chairs so you can stay seated the whole time and still easily see the stage.  Or you can stand the whole time and not have to worry about people behind you complaining.  This is because there is a walkway between the box seats and the lawn and the lawn is a little higher up the slope.  My only complaint is how much concerts cost these days.  I don't think this has anything to do with the amphitheater, it's just artists are charging ridiculous prices for their shows.  Then on top of that you get ticket brokers buying up tickets with even higher ticket prices.  But if you do get to see a show there, you'll enjoy it.

Rather a disappointment.  The sound system was lousy. I think the band was ok but the sound system muffled them terribly.
Service was friendly but slow. I had the pork chops which were over cooked and chewy. The garlic mashed potatoes were tasty but a bit over the top on garlic. My husband had the Nashville hot chicken with medium sauce. Not impressed. The fries were tasty. The cole slaw was good. Our friends had burgers and thought they were good. But not great. 
The roof top bar was nice. 
They really need to step up their game on the quality of the food.

To be completely honest, we ended up here every single night after we made our rounds at the other bars in Broadway. It has 3 levels, all with different vibes, so the wait is never long and it is never too crowded inside. There is always lots of energy and plenty of seating and room to dance. I liked the fact that there are all different age people here, I spoke with plenty of people my grandparents' age. There are also lots of bachelor/bachelorette parties which always make for a good time. Overall, if you aren't sure where to go on Broadway, Honky Tonk Central is a safe bet!

Have cash, come early if you want a good seat, drink, be polite or leave, & enjoy the best music in Nashville!  This place may not impress some folks by its looks or folks that expect a fine meal, (although, the pimento cheese is great when you're hungry enough) but nothing beats a beer & hearing the musicians I've heard / seen play here.

This place was nice and super country "typical Tennessee"  upon entry we were carded then we headed to the bar,  we got drinks very fast even though this place was jammed packed on a Saturday night.  

This is a 3 level country club,  live music playing,  very enjoyable atmosphere.  Everyone is super nice. 

Drinks are great. Place is clean. Great spot to visit when walking thru Broadway.

Don't fall for their advertised "deals". Was told there were 2 for 1 deals but only to find upon closing out that I was charged full price for not specifically wearing Preds gear. I live in Nashville and was, indeed, out supporting the Preds. I really wanted to love this place (nice bathrooms, not super packed), but unfortunately will not be supporting this bar. Locals beware.

We saw Eric Church's acoustic performance at the inaugural performance.  Incredible show!!

Beautiful venue with a nicely sloped open lawn area for GA.  Bring a blanket and arrive early so you can save your spot -- also, if it had rained recently you're going to want a blanket to sit on before the show and stand on after.  There are no bad seats in the lawn EXCEPT for the two giant light stands that are about 50/60 feet tall -- if you sit directly behind one you're going to have a bad time.

I see a lot of other reviewers complaining about how expensive drinks were.  Ummm... really?  What did you except?  $4 2-4-1s?  Of course it's expensive!  It's Nashville!  At a brand new venue!  Personally, I felt $12 for a 25oz domestic beer was a very reasonable price for a stadium/venue.  Also, sneak in a flask, drink beforehand, don't be a rookie.

Had a blast and can't wait to come back.

Great music but the bar tender on the second floor lost our friends credit card while on vacation.  She was not helpful in finding it either. We didn't have a tab and just paid for a drink. The rest of the staff was descent but clearly this girl wasn't the brightest bulb in the bunch. Just make sure you keep an eye on your bar tender as it could of ruined someone's vacation.

Nice bar, good music. We stopped in for lunch. We had nachos, which were good. I had the chicken salad sandwich...very good! My husband had the pulled pork sandwich...could have been more tender. We were there for the music and drinks not so much a 5 star meal so it was worth the time and money.

What everyone else said, AND you can even talk politics here without fearing for your life. Mostly intelligent, and definitely diverse, points of view can be had for no charge. You get (at least) what what you pay for here, where "Cheers" meets "Deliverance," and Music Row Democrats mix with Skid Row Republicans.

The food was the worst in Nashville.  I enjoyed the entertainment.   Frankly, the only reason we went was to see The Time Jumpers.  The music was exceptional.  I mean, the very best musicians in Nashville.   We missed dear Dawn.  We went to the afternoon songwriter show & enjoyed it.  Very limited menu.   The meat in the patty melt had an odd texture & was under seasoned.  The brisket was inedible.  We tried to order something easy at the evening show because we had to arrive so early to get a seat.  Epic fail.  Go to the shows.  Eat before you go.

So, I've been here exactly once. One time. Tonight. I watched the Melvins, a life long dream, and it only cost me $18 to get in the door. I had seats that gave me an amazing view of the stage (I have grown too old for mosh pits, but I love to watch) the band was amazing. The food was exceptional, and the staff was outstanding. The venue was clean, and small, the best I've seen in a very long time, and I go to stuff like this a lot. 3rd and Lindsley will have my business at any point and time that someone is there that I even kinda wanna see. They are top notch!!

This is incredible. You never know who you are going to see here, performing or watching!

This is a legendary venue so you have to make a stop by. Sunday is a bluegrasss jam and you just get in as long as they have room. Beer is inexpensive.

They know they are a legend so you can buy old concert posters, t shirts, postcards, etc.

Gigantic three level party bar. Lots of live music. Lower level is often loud, fun and packed. Level two was a lesser band, but room to sit and hang out. Third floor was also fun. This is one of the larger, more touristy spots, but it does a lot of things very well and it worth a visit. 

Food was so-so, but it this is a bar about music and drinking, so go for that.
Great bar for the locals and tourists. Beautiful decor. Great service and food. Best thing is the roof top patio. Best in town!!

What an AWESOME TIME!!! 
Best entertainment on Broadway!
Food was Good for what I would consider bar food.
Staff was great through out our multiple visits.
Honky Tonk Central is a must!
Be sure you ask for Crystal, BEST bartender there!!!! If she's not there look for Kelsey she's a close second!

Walked in and get stuck every night. Stay put to the first floor. There was a great live cover band that knows their country songs . Beside the music the Honkey Tonk Tea was awsome. Drink it away like its lemonade and get drunk as.......... ;-)

The place to go!  We had drinks, food and listened to the band.  Everything was great!  It was super busy on a Saturday evening of course but Monday evening was great.  The bands were great!  They were a lot of fun and played lots of different types of music to get the crowd into it.

Great party atmosphere! But bar service sucks!!!!!! The bartenders sure know how to ignore you even if you're waving $100 bill. That's exactly to happen to my friend and I; we waited about 30 minutes to get served. HORRIBLE bartender service!!!! About 2-3 bartenders present with a full house. That ratio is incorrect!

The service here was SO SLOW. 

We were seated at the bar and initially, our first two drinks came quickly. However, once we tried for a second round the bartender was nowhere to be found. She kept walking past us not looking our way. We finally asked her to get some more drinks and she told us she would be over in a minute but never came back. Spent the entire time at one end of the bar talking to the same people, walking past us to type on the computers, and then would return to the same area. We ended up ordering from a different bartender about 10-15 minutes later. 

There was a growing number of impatient customers standing at the bar to my right who were holding out their credit cards trying to get service. I overheard one guy saying he had been waiting 20 minutes. Another woman gave up and left. The guy directly to my right ordered 3 rounds of beers for he and is friends when a bartender finally came around  because he said he knew it would take too long when they wanted more. 

The music here was actually really good but it was a bit too loud to have any type of conversation. 

Also the bathrooms are INCREDIBLE. So pretty and clean with tons of mirrors. That's the only thing I liked about this place.

If you love country music, patriotism, and good beer for a decent price, this is your place. The place was packed, so it took like 10 minutes to get a beer, which I wasn't a fan of. They need a few more bartenders here, as they seem overworked. However, the bartenders made up for it with their awesome personalities and attentiveness. This place is ridiculously huge, with three floors. I stayed on the first floor most of the time. The band was absolutely amazing, playing a mixture of old and new country. They even did a few songs for the Vets that were in the bar, and it was really heartfelt. This was one of my favorite visited bars while in Nashville.
Good vibe, lot of energy for a Sunday ! Live music and cold beer what more could you ask for in Nashville

My friend and I were visiting Nashville and part of the reason is we had tickets to a concert at this venue.  We parked in a small lot a few blocks down the street, which we expected since we were in the city.  We had lawn seats so we weren't expecting to see the stage very well, but the venue is not that large so we were much closer than expected.  We were glad we didn't pay more for the reserved seats since those looked like they were just folding chairs.  The weather was perfect for our concert so it was wonderful sitting out next to the river and being able to hear the sounds of the city in the background.  One of the major perks of this venue was the bathrooms.  I've been to multiple venues like this where the bathrooms are downright disgusting.  These were very clean and seemed brand new.  Also, there was no wait, which can be a huge issue for the women's restroom.  There was plenty of food and beverage options and they had a nice setup for merchandise.  Overall, I'd definitely be willing to go back.

Day or night or even the afternoon you can always find good entertainment hold beer and some nice grub. Gina the bartender is super friendly on the first floor. Not much different than many of the Broadway places but this place is also a lot of fun.

Update: once we became familiar with the drill this has become one of our favorite places in Nashville with top-notch entertainment and reasonably-priced menu offerings. That said for a 9:00 PM Monday night Time Jumpers show we arrive at 5:00
PM to get in line for the doors open at 5:30 and we want to be assured of a decent seat. We have found the same people attend the show week after week and it been very pleasant to visit with them. Most times we've shared our table with others and have met some very interesting and friendly folks.

A must-visit for locals and tourists alike. I've seen several shows here--it's ALWAYS packed. Decent beer selection and okay food assortment, but you're not coming here for a meal. The acoustics were great for the shows I've seen here. Parking can be annoying (random people standing out in what appears to be a business lot, charging $6-$10), but what can you do? Welcome to Nashville. 

I love coming here. I'd definitely recommend you make it out too. Dive-y, but a classic Nashville haunt.

really good concert venue, it helps when the weather cooperates.  beautiful sky,  lights of downtown and your favorite band  playing their great songs.  open lawn seating is okay if you bring a chair or blanket.   lots of standing areas.  restrooms & concessions accessible.  overall a good concert experience.................
Not a dive bar. Total opposite of it in fact. If looking for an up tight sort of experience this is the place for you. Make sure you drink with your pinky out to be able to fit in with the clientele.
Great place and awesome staff but the owner doesn't play for employee parking which is pretty ridiculous

Oh WOW. Where to begin with Honky Tonk Central. I was here a few weeks ago for my brothers bachelor party with a group of 18 guys. Let me start out by saying if you don't immediately B line it up to the third floor you're doing it wrong. The music is awesome, the bartenders are cool and it seemed to be where all the bachelorette parties were which is never a bad thing. Honky Tonk in general is an absolute gold mine and I would love to shake the hands of the owner. Obviously, it is very touristy but the fact of the matter is you will get drunk and have a blast.
Stop by here every time I'm in Nashville. Great live music with hot singers. Love it!!

Went to this place for drinks at the end of our bar hopping extravaganza. The place is pretty cool and they have live music. The Kentucky Bourbon Ale came in a smaller glass than expected. Other than that, good to go.

The music and touristy vibe are great. The dirtiness is a total deal breaker. We were at Honky Tonk 3 years ago and while it was dirty, it wasn't disgusting. This time full on gross! Someone vomited on the floor (before 5pm on a Tuesday) and it was NEVER cleaned up for the hour or so we spent there (I know, I know...why the hell did I sit there looking at that for an hour?!?) Our waitress was spacey and took forever to bring the drinks, which was fine, because again...the grossness and the accompanying smell forced us outta there! Went down the street to Tequila Cowboy, better music, way cleaner and a super friendly waitress running drinks to us constantly.  So, I guess pop in cuz it sure does look cool from the outside, but move on.

Who doesn't love live free music?! No one, that's who. LotG always brings in awesome bands to play. Therein lies the only problem. It's such a hit that everyone and anyone shows up so it's always crowded. I remember when it first started, there was maybe only a handful of people so no matter when you came you could still stand right up in front of the stage. Now you have to practically camp out if you want to be close, otherwise you're way in the back. I always have a good time. Cold beer, food trucks galore, great music. Summers in Nash don't get any better!

Bobby's is a local bar that reminds me of that show "Cheers"  by the time you leave, everybody knows your name.  It's the only bar I have ever felt comfortable going into, sitting at the bar and drinking a Beer by myself.  The locals that hang out there are super friendly and make you feel right at home.  It's mostly a older group during the day and during the evening, but the weekends when they have open mic,live bands etc etc it's a totally mixed group.
If your just a down to esrth, nothing fancy kind of person..you will love Bobbys.   Don't forget to bring your guitar, you will always be welcome to play, sing, dance....whatever is entertaining,  is welcome at Bobbys!     Rebecca Marks from Cali....

Honky Tonk Central is a standard touristy bar. Hey, it's Broadway what do you expect? However, they get a full five star rating from me because, well, I am a tourist, and they had a great live (and incredibly cute!) country band from San Antonio playing a phenomenal playlist ranging from classic country hits to modern favorites. The bartender was also kind enough to let me use to the plug behind the car to charge my IPhone.

While in town for a conference I stopped in here and was pleasantly surprised. I love that the bar was old time with wooden floors, made me think of my time living in New Orleans. There was a live band called Smoke N Gun and they were amazing. Alexia's voice was great, it made it hard to leave the bar. I thought the service was decent and I enjoyed my honey lager.

Their balcony has the best view of all of Broadway. It can't be beat. They also had what I came to Nashville for, genuine country music playing all night. It's such a feel-good place, and if you're doing your bachelorette party in Nashville, Honky Tonk Central should be a stop for your group. It's a great crowd on Saturday nights, and I would definitely go again.

Famous Saloon came in and saved the day for us after our original rehearsal dinner venue cancelled on us 2 weeks prior to our event. Amanda was so sweet and was a joy to work with. We used the Green Room and our guest couldn't stop raving about how much they loved the space. The decor is very unique yet very Nashville. The food was amazing as well! And of course everyone had a blast on the rooftop patio after our dinner was over! Thanks for helping us have an amazing night before our wedding Famous!

A friend's family came into town and wanted to go to Lower Broad so we started at Honky Tonk Central.  It's great to have a different band on each of the 3 floors!  We ordered food and the burgers were really good and huge!  Two people could easily split one plate.  The bartenders were friendly and prompt.  Overall a good experience.

This place has the worst service! We ordered our drinks and never could get the waitress with an attitude to come back to take our order so we moved to another section. That was a bad idea also. This waitress also was very unfriendly, unpleasant and couldn't get our drink order right. We asked for the $2 beer and got something else and was charged for it. I never did get my water refill so my husband went to the bar to get me one. The waitress disappeared and when we did finally see her we tried to get her attention a few times and she would completely ignore us as if she didnt see us. We had to ask security walking by to please call our waitress. We saw other customers frustrated, looking around for their waitress as well and it wasnt even busy. It looked as if everyone hated their job....no smile, no thank you, nothing. Of course I wasnt going to leave a tip because I didnt receive any service and got 2 rude servers. To top everything off, I saw my bank transaction history a few days later and the waitress decided to give herself a $3 tip on my bank card. I guess she doesn't realize that is stealing and against the law. If you want horrible service by rude waitresses and to be stolen from then this is the place for you. Never going back here or referring anybody.

Went here today and explored all 3 levels and settled up top. Got an awesome server named Colt. Quick with the drinks, very personable and great dude. Band was really solid and made for a nice afternoon of boozin. Took care of Colt and before we left he hooked us up with a shot as thanks. Will be back.

I would give this place a zero if I could. The female bartender on the 1st floor is a scam artist. Served us 2 rounds of drinks when we only ordered one on 2 occasions. She was extremely unprofessional when mentioned it. Because we were dissatisfied with her service we got kicked out the bar. Note to management, your bartenders need a facelift. They are awful.
This bar was fun.  We came to listen to the live music on the 2nd floor and watch drunk people dance and look like idiots.  Good crowd - bad food but a nice place to hang out.

Over aggressive bouncers.  Band requests $ 20-100 for song request.  Bartenders try to cheat you with change.  Tourists beware!  Had a great experience at every other place on Broadway. It's not a case of one bad employee. Obviously it's there standard business practice to try and take the tourists $.

This place has poor management, called three days before. They told us we had the upstairs bar! Get here and there says no! Some douche with long wanna be red hair facial hair was rude to us. Told us they they did not staff up! Walked out this place sucks!!
Very nice bar. Upscale looking, we enjoyed some cocktails and a really talented guitarist by the name of Andrew Vanetten. I highly recommend you check him out!

I was told this was the place to go in Nashville. It certainly is the biggest bar. Three floors, all 3 with a different live band. Music is good.  Food is average. Prices are average. It's definitely worth checking out. 

From a fun standpoint, it doesn't blow away the competition. In fact I think I enjoyed some of the other bars more.  I say I think because I was quite intoxicated and running amuck.  

All in all, this is one of the best watering holes I visited while on my drunken travels. But I do recommend visiting all of the competition as well.

DO NOT EVER COME HERE!! My boyfriend is about to deploy, so I came from San Diego to visit him in Huntsville and he wanted to show me the night life in Nashville that he's always loved. We went out to dinner with his best friend and girlfriend and then went to honky tonk central. None of us had been, but from the outside it looked like it would be a good time. WRONG! After about half an hour there my friend told me the bouncer was kicking her boyfriend out for spilling some of his drink, when he only spilled it because some drunk asshole stumbled into him. He then went to pay his tab and the bartender charged him $75 for 3 drinks! What a ripoff! Turns out they charged him for 8 drinks but we couldn't prove it wasn't our ticket and they had his card anyway so they charged him the full amount and kicked us out. Additionally, all the bartenders are girls, so they will not serve other women. I waited 20 minutes (more than half the time we were there) to get a rum and coke and couldn't even taste the rum. The whole time I was watching guys come up and leave with drinks, while also taking shots with the bartenders. What a terribly unpleasant experience.

There isn't really a whole lot to say about this little spot, but you can expect some serious Nashville charm, live music and a cold beer.  You get to make your mark by placing your "stamp" on a dollar bill and adding it to their collection.  Thirsty?  Like beer?  Stop on by!

5 stars for the music; 1 for the food.  You don't go here to eat. My husband ordered a Caesar salad and was brought a plate of Romaine lettuce (from those bags?) and a small cup of dressing (from a bottle?)    I hope some of the other foods are better than that. I'm glad I ordered only drinks.  We went Monday night to see a performance by the band "The Time Jumpers," which plays a genre of music called Country Swing that sounded to me like songs from the 1940s.  You will appreciate the performance very much if you are a musician, since the performers are extremely talented, but not everyone will appreciate this style of music.
Rip off due to unethical behavior of just one band supposedly playing requests for $20 per song. They take your cash and walk without playing the request

Briefly stopped in here to grab a beer and listen to music - loved this place! There was a great band playing and it wasn't too packed so we could really enjoy ourselves. Will definitely be coming back!

Pretty cool place for tourists like myself. My niece and I had a good time. The drinks are SO expensive at this place that it's worth it to go to a place like Roberts just up the street for cheaper and better everything. This place is cool but make sure you bring your wallet.

Beautiful venue in a beautiful setting! I went to see Chris Young, Jerrod Niemann and Cam on a cold and dreary Wednesday night. Be warned, in times of inclement weather there is little relief at this venue, as pretty much every part of it is outside. The "loft" in the back offered a little bit of shelter, but the roof is not a complete roof overhead so the rain will still get you. There was an ample selection of snacks, beverages and alcohol stations throughout the venue. Food/drink pricing was average for a venue, expect to pay $11.50 for a tall beer and more for premium liquor. You can tell a lot of money and effort went into the venue and it definitely paid off. Restrooms are a little cramped when there are a lot of people, as with most venues. Customer service was awesome throughout, friendly workers with Ascend bank handing out free ponchos and the concessions utilizing touch screen signing for their transactions. There is assigned ticket seating in front but the lawn gave a great view as well, even from the back pavilion "loft" area. Plenty of space to spread out and picnic tables were set up throughout as well. I'm hoping a venue like this will attract some bigger acts to Music City that would rather play in this space than something like the Coliseum. I will definitely be back for shows!

This is for the music, we have been here for 2 days and stepped in and out of a few bars and the music here is top notch! 

Cozy little bar with great music!

Had my first visit to Nashville a few days ago, and my nephew told me to be sure that I stopped by this bar. Best recommendation ever! Walked in to amazing music (Kassie and Wilson performing on a Friday afternoon), Laura behind the bar made us feel like regulars returning after being gone too long. It was a struggle to leave, but we were in town for a wedding and had to keep on schedule. Managed to sneak back to Broadway after the wedding the next night, and we did the stroll looking for a place to stop and listen to the music. I wasn't surprised when we ended up back at Benchmark, perched on barstools as the charming Vanessa and more fantastic music made the evening fly by. Can't wait to go back to Nashville, and I guarantee that a couple of visits to Benchmark will be on our schedule!
Amanda P. Was the best bartender I have had.  She served our company party fantastic and entertained with her wit.

If you are a bachelor/bachelorette party, this is a required stop for a Nashville night out.  If that sort of scene bothers you, I'd probably visit Honky Tonk Central either during the day or just not come at all.

My husband and I visited three times during our 5 day stay in Nashville.  The first time was for lunch (nothing to write home about- pretty much the same bar food they sell everywhere else), the second was for a few quick drinks, and the last time was on our last Saturday night in town.

Daytime entertainment is, like most places on Broadway, mostly acoustic.  Some acts were better than others.  On the Saturday night we visited, we were able to snag two seats at the bar, so we sat tight for hours (especially since there was a big screen TV in front of us, playing the Final Four games).  All the times we were there, there were no cover charges.

I liked this place because you have three floors of music and it was pretty wide open (unlike Tootsies) so even though it was packed, you never felt claustrophobic.
