I saw Isaac play here a couple of years ago.  We loved his music and have even enjoyed following him on Facebook.  I recently caught a video of Isaac playing at the Benchmark ... got me revved up for a long overdue return to Nashville.

Was there recently and said what has happened to the lower Broad I once knew. I saw three people vomiting and many stumbling drunk. The police stood by and seemed not to care. Nashville has tons of musicians but only a few will make it to the next level. Most who play here will not. The food was just alright and the toilet gets a D at best. Go to the Blue Bird. Better neighborhood.

We are locals and we LOVE this place for the most amazing breakfasts!!  Why wait in long lines at the other breakfast places when you can walk right into here and be served immediately!!  Bartenders are awesome.  The "Bloody Mary" is amazing and you get to make it yourself with all the goodies they have set out for you.  It will not disappoint!!  Highly recommend for a great downtown Nashville weekend breakfast!

First experience at 3rd and Lindsley was a good one. 

Since I had a group in town who wanted something fun to do, other than Broadway, I found 3rd and Lindsley. We had a great time. Saw the first show, which was Justin Forrest who was a grand surprise as well. I didn't expect great blues. We didn't eat so I can't comment on the food but our drinks were delivered quickly each time. The place is clean and staff is helpful, friendly and efficient. Not only will I go again, I can't wait to go again. Its a great deal, a great place and the entertainment is over the moon.
Great atmosphere. Great food. Fast service for being so packed. Love this place so much! Best place in Nashville!

Our company hosted a private party on Friday night. Our expectations were definitely exceeded! Frank (catering contact) was awesome! Our customers were very well taken care of. The venue was awesome! Couldn't have asked for anything better.

We were so happy to stumble across this place as we were walking around the downtown area. It's adorably located in the middle of a large brick alley- we would have missed it if it wasn't for the pop-up sign on the street. The atmosphere is really fun! The entire place has a prohibition-era theme with a long bar, a stage for live music, and lots of decoration. 

They have 2 for 1 drinks for Happy Hour during the week, and we were pleasantly surprised the strength of the drinks. The female bartender was generous and polite. If you are looking for a hip place to grab a good drink or craft beer, you should definitely look for this hidden gem! When we return to Nashville, we will be back! Thanks Alley Taps!

This bar/restaurant is massive and located right on Broadway. There are 3 floors with live music with people of all ages. The drinks were average priced.

I didn't eat here personally because of the night scene- didn't seem too clean of a place to eat at. There are bathroom attendants and great bartenders.

ATM charges $6 to take out money, so if you want cash on you- I suggest taking it out elsewhere! The bar accepts cash and card however.

I attended my first concert this week at Ascend and was thoroughly impressed. The view is outstanding from any seat or the lawn. The sound system is crisp, clear and easy to hear anything from all spots. The location on the riverside and the base of the pedestrian bridge is unique and enhances the experience. 

If you have the opportunity to see a show here; do it!

One of my favorite bars in Nashville. What makes it my favorite you ask, Isaac Mathews.  Awesome singer.  If you haven't seen him play you are missing out.  One of the main reasons I go there is to see Isaac.

I made reservations for 4 with opentable.com. Life got in that way, and I used the site to delay our reservation 30 minutes. When we arrive, I learned the site and the restaurant weren't communicating, and our reservation was cancelled. It was a slow, rainy night so we were sat right away. No big deal. 

The live music on the first floor was so loud conversation was impossible except for what we could fit in, in between songs. It's okay though. We spent most of the time with our mouths full. The fried green tomatoes are delicious. We actually ended up ordering a second serving after our party devoured the first in a matter of minutes. Crispy meatballs were exactly what you'd expect. Calamari was a bit too chewy for my liking. But, the bacon on the charcuterie tray, oh my gosh, that bacon. Goodness gracious. Everyone should try it! It's the perfect blend of crispy and chewy, salty and sweet. You just need to try it for yourself. I'd recommend washing it down with a Tennessee Mule - they don't skimp on the Old Camp. Forgo the banana pudding unless you like crispy wafers. They're not my preference, but they might be yours. 


So they advertise as the tallest bar, whatever. The second floor was closed. The third and fourth floors are office space you can't actually get to. The roof top has corn hole, and I'm told they'll be getting more games soon. They play pop music up there too which someone might appreciate. I prefer country; it is downtown Nashville after all. 

A little forewarning, don't take the stairs, only use the elevator. I thought I'd go down the stairs instead of waiting on the elevator, and ended up locked in the stairwell because the doors lock automatically. I knocked the the rooftop door for almost five minutes before finally getting someone on the phone who could come let me back in the bar. Talk about a scary movie moment! 

Overall greatness: food = yes, bar = no.

Don't go for the food! 
  Frozen filler hamburger  patty , dry chicken and cheap prime rib.

I went here for the music and the view but the fried catfish was surprisingly good. It's a great cheap lunch option in the area. 

Later in the night, the bar atmosphere is a lot of fun.

I was looking for the quintessential Nashville music experience and this was it.  I went to see the Roland white band and had a blast.   The place itself is really low key with some folding chairs and picnic bench seating.   The food is so-so serving pizzas and things of popcorn.  But that's not why you came here.   The atmosphere is great. Doors opened at 7 and we had time to get settled and chat it up with our neighbors for the evening.   Turns out we got some great tips on places to go things to see in town thanks to a bluegrass talent scout we met.  

The band was great.  tons of interaction with the crowd, kept things lively.  I enjoyed every track they played.   

If you're looking for a place to listen to music away from the chaos on Broadway come here its worth it.

$? no way..
we paid $9 for a small pitcher of coke. that is absurd..
other than that it was 'jam session night' so there was no cover.

the music was amazing.
What a disaster. Despite having tickets and being here two hours before show time, there are no seats. People are squeezed in like sardines. The fire department should be called.

I had an amazing day at this honky tonk. People underage are welcome here during the day and we sat and listened to the band for about 2 hours and I could have easily kept listening to them enjoying my soda. The band was super friendly and played a range of classic and modern country songs. If you don't like the band on one floor, there are 2 others you can try. We never switched floors because we loved the band on our floor but it would've been easy if we wanted to hear other bands as well. High recommend this place and we will probably go back tomorrow!

Good music and fun atmosphere. Food just average, nothing special. I don't think people go there for the food, they go for the entertainment and the drinks. Three floors with live music on each so you can't ever say that you're bored.

Honky Tonk! This place was very fun. Three floors of awesome music. A great view of the strip on the top floor. With three bands playing its easy to find one that suites you best. Also the crowd seemed friendly I was able to make some cool friends at this bar.

Cool bar to hang out in but it can get super grimey. Can get really douchey at times but the three levels are cool to check out. If you can hang out near the balconies and oversee Broadway it's a good time. Really it's 3.5 stars from me.

This is the largest bar in the area - three stories with different bands on every floor.  As you go up the floors, the food selection, bar selection, quality of the bands and spirit of the crowd diminish significantly (no food on the third floor and no cocktails).  On the plus side, the bands are good and fun, take requests for songs, and try to excite the crowd (especially on the first floor), on the minus side - they walk around the tables with their tip jar.  I understand the importance of tipping, but the jar is already big (more like a bucket), sitting at their feet, and anyone who wants to make a request for a song or go outside has to pass by it anyway.  So they look like street performers when they ask for tips.  The honky tonk tea (a version of a long island iced tea) is good, the lemon drop is lacking.  The atmosphere, however, is great - it's loud and fun, with people tapping their feet and singing along.

If you like dive bars and quality live music then Bobby's is the place. Day drinking can't be beaten, and if you do it at Bobby's on a Wednesday then you'll get to experience Sam's Jams....... and afternoon of all original music. A side note, if you're in town doing the "Vacation Thing" Bobby's is the only bar on Music Row...... so get off the tour bus and have a drink.

We came on a Wednesday around 6pm. We got the best table ever on the 3rd floor eight by a window. We had some good, but sugary drinks and enjoyed the BEST nachos. Get the chicken. It is so yummy!!!! Our waitress was just okay and so was the music. But the view we had at our table and the nachos made this place worth being at!

I have never in my life been treated with as much disrespect as I was treated this evening. My friends and I entered Honky Tonk lured by the music, and proceeded to the bar. I ordered a round of drinks and left my card with the lovely, friendly bartender. As it began to fill up, my party decided that it was time to go. At no fault of the bartender, it was difficult to close my tab. I couldn't get her attention, so I tried to wedge in so that I could signal for someone to close our tab. Numerous witnesses attested to the fact that a young female patron was staring me down as I did so, even going as far as to call over a "friend" or boyfriend of hers to push me and actually pull my hair. Once he pulled on my hair, I did in fact turn to him and confront him. His female friend attacked me and I do, in fact, have scratches to prove it. He called me a slew on horrific names and spoke to me in such a way that I wished his own mother could have heard, as she would have been disappointed and appalled. I know, as I am a mother myself. I turned to the bartender who noticed the commotion and asked for my tab. Once I did, I felt a complete drink being dumped on my head. Witnesses will say it was the original young girl patron, I however thought it was the man because as I turned to him he gave me a smug grin and a wave. I reacted as only a woman assaulted would react. I screamed and was held back by my friends. The bartender motioned for the other female to be removed, however, the insanely disrespectful and horrific "man" commiserated with a large bouncer and this is where my main issue takes place. A MAN, a large man, employed by Honky Tonk turned to me, a drenched (from the drink,) hysterical crying (from shock,) mother and started physically pushing me out of the establishment. He even went as far as threatening to put me into a cob car himself if I didn't comply. He didn't know that my own husband was law enforcement himself and was inside trying to defuse the situation. As I cried that my card was still inside, he used his large body to physically push me out. My husband attempted for 20 minutes to get my cc back, and was told it was "lost." My friend went in later and a full 30 minutes later was given the card but with charges on it that I did not authorize. My family has been in the restaurant/bar business for 40 years and I have never, nor has my family ever seen such Unprofessionalism. We plan on contacting the better business bureau, as well as a lawyer for the the physical harm that has come to me. I encourage everyone to stay away. Any establishment that would allow this to happen, is not one that should stay in business.

This is one of my favorite Nashville venues. Even on the grass you feel up close to the personal. The acoustics are amazing. You can rent lawn chairs for $15 for 2 (limited supply) just please don't be the jerk up front who insists on standing and blocking the view of a couple of thousand people. The view of Nashville waterfront and skyline makes anything you see a bit magical. Of course Van Morrison is the Man!

This may be the busiest bar/restaurant on Monday nights in Nashville. The reason? Simple: The Time Jumpers, Nashville's country big band that should be on every music lover's list. Attending one of their performances has been on my bucket list for several years. So glad I made it. Seeing this band in person you understand why pretty much every performance of theirs is sold out.

Not a bad seat in the house, good sound on the night of our visit and the crowd is respectful of the performers. It's very likely I'll be back to see this band again even though it requires a 600 mile flight.

Average bar food. Nothing spectacular going on here. With the kind of crowd they command on Mondays alone, not to speak of other nights, a little surprised they aren't kicking the food quality up a notch. It wasn't bad, it was just OK bar grub like burgers, your requisite appetizers. How not make a *great* burger instead of an average one? Mostly a beer crowd from what I observed. When I ordered a Zinfandel they brought me some God awful kind of blush wine that I requested sent back. I had asked to pay the tab for a party of five and they complied without complaint. Service was above average to my eye for this kind of venue.

If you come, come early, particularly if you're seeing the Time Jumpers. Parking is pretty limited. We found a spot up the street 50 yards or so. Not particularly inconvenient, just very limited. Overall a great smaller live music venue well worth your visit.

As a new Nashville resident, I was lucky enough to attend my first event at War Memorial Auditorium just last week! I attended a living taping of NPR's Ask Me Another. It was hilarious, intelligent, and absolutely a joy to view live (I listen to it most weekends on the radio)! Several Nashville celebrity guests, including Martina McBride and Connie Britton, participated in the taping, which was really cool!

War Memorial is a great venue for events and concerts - such a gorgeous building. The interior isn't quite as fancy as you might expect from the outside, but it's a big venue that is flexible for different types of events. (When I attend Ask Me Another, they utilized chairs on the floor of the auditorium, but for concerts, they can remove the chair and make it standing room only). It could use a little renovation/updating, though. 

They sell water, wine, and beer, which you can take to your seat. The only bathrooms are upstairs - we went upstairs to our seats and then had to walk all the way down (oops). 

Only con? The seats upstairs are pretty close together and the elevation could be better. I'm a short girl, and I had to swap seats with people to try to see over taller people in the row in front of me. And I hit my knee on the chair in front of me dozens of times (and I'm only 5 feet tall)! But such is the situation at almost every auditorium I've ever been in!

Some great events and concerts are held at War Memorial Auditorium, so I'm sure I'll be back.
Had an amazing time and the music was great! Security was friendly. Ordered from several bartenders, all but one were friendly. Definite stop!!! Had such a great time we went back the next night.
Great prices for good food in downtown...try the nachos plenty to share

3rd and Lindsley is an interesting spot to catch a show. I particularly like heavier rock shows at this location as the acoustics and set up here are intimate but clean, comfortable and a little more upscale than some such shows typically get. To top it all off, this place actually has food with waiter service---and it is pretty good! It's nice to stop in for a band you really like but that isn't the normal crowd-drawing Nashville act, get in when the doors open, sit and order a meal and a brew, and still have time to get in the pit near the stage after a good meal. Parking is odd here as you're likely to end up in one of the many neighboring businesses which close before this place usually opens but luckily they're all mostly cool with that.

How can people not give this event 5 stars?!?
This is a FREE outdoor concert. 
My only complaint is that I only enjoyed the last night of shows. 
No hassle getting in with the guards especially since I was just carrying my cell phone. 
There were so many tents with free stuff from vendors and sponsors and merchandise tents.
Loved the variety of food trucks. Only in the south do you see a Catfish food truck! There was such a variety that no one would have walked away being disappointed. 
I thought the lines to the food trucks and beverage tent were great. 
The prices are INSANE!!! Water for $2 and beer for $6. Thank you Nashville. 
The lines up are great and even though I was not aware of any of the bands except one, Jimmy Eats World, it did not matter. This is the way to discover new bands and just hear some good (free) music.
The crowd was also entertaining. ALL ages were represented Saturday from ALL areas of town and ALL walks of life. 
I easily was able to stand on the far left side of the stage and was really close, was not crowded by anyone abs saw great. 
People came and left all throughout the shows. Seemed more people were there to socialize and drink than for the concert. 
TIP if you come after 6pm you can park for free 3 blocks west by the Capital on Charlotte.

I saw a small little show here. Never have been here before, I was hesitant hearing some negative reviews.

Personally I had a great time. They can get some really decent acts for being so small. It was packed when I went so the bar service was really slow and hard to get to, but the beers were pretty cheap so I can't argue about that. 

I'd come back again.

Went there to go see the talented and incredible Brit Stokes. Anytime I come to Nashville I always look up two of the best,Brit Stokes and Isaac Matthews. Not only was Brit and the band so good but the food (nachos preferably) was incredible. The waitress was top notch and she worked her tail off the whole time. It's only fair and suiting that you tip the band well, tip the waitress well and go see Brit Stokes at this really cool and classy joint. I felt like I had quality seats at a top notch concert. Do yourself a favor and go to Famous Saloon and order the Nachos and enjoy the shows. Great food, Great Music, Great times. I'll be back next time I'm in town.

This place is absolutely gorgeous and stands out among all the other restaurants/venues in Downtown Nashville.. the staff, food , drinks EVERYTHING is top notch!! You feel like you are stepping into another city when you walk in. Nashville needed Nashville Underground

Another awesome Broadway Street Honkey tonk!   Huge bar, food service and great music.  
Huge TV for the sports fans!!  
Didn't have the food here but the wings smelled amazing!!!

yes, we were too old for this place...

but not being a country music fan (why the hell were we in nashville then, right?) the music lured us in: this is a good place to hear country bands break out into crossover music and black eyed peas. drinks are strong and there's an awesome photo booth. yeah, it's worth going here if you're touring broadway ;)

Rex (the manager) went above and beyond to make our experience. The live music and food were awesome as well. The experience was made by Rex and Chelsea and would love to come back on my next visit to Nashville.

Stopped here the other day to grab some food and listen to some music. The band was great as well as the food. It was not pricey and you got plenty of food for what you paid . It was nothing extravagant and the menu was simple, but it was still delicious. If you are skeptical about the food at least go for the atmosphere.

Typical bar on Broadway..etc it is 3 stories tall on a prime location...corner lot of 4th and Broadway..It looks sort of New Orleans style with all the windows and doorways with little balcony areas...

But again,...its just a bar...
There was a major accident a few months back..someone fell to their death...I was afraid that would happen...
But if you like loud, rowdy and drunken excitement..then have at it !!!
Nice place.  Good service and food. Nothing fancy. Hot chicken nice and spicy, and that was only medium! What would 'ring of fire' be like?

This is what Nashville needs. It's a stylish, classy bar atmosphere with top-notch service and really great food (bar food + some more creative options like Avocado pasta!). I love that it is located off Broadway, because it IS different than the sticky sweaty honky tonks we are all used to - and I do love those too. Famous Saloon picked our group up from the Gulch in a private, pimped out shuttle bus (more like a party bus) and drove us to them. We had a fantastic dinner and the best bartender/server, then we danced the night away: first downstairs to country music and then upstairs on the rooftop with a DJ. This is a very cool addition to our bar scene!

Had a really good time here with my wife and nephew. It's new so it's super clean. The wings were killer. The ring of fire sauce is actually really hot. They put the Titans game on for us and the staff was really pleasant and chatted with us. In the men's room, you can see the bar and televisions from the urinals through the windows so that was really cool. We're local and this is the nicest place on Broadway. We'll be back!

It's A  " Honky-tonk "  so unlike other people I'm going to rate it in the classification it falls into and what you expect to find in one! One large stages with singer-songwriters, musicians & wannabes playing country music! The usual beer selection with a few local hand crafts! Very noisy loud! Pretty much filled with the usual fast-food you expect to find in one!

If I could give less that a star, I would. Love the music, but the service was God-awful. I have never been treated so poorly by a bartender (and I'm from New York)... I very politely asked for water (on a day when it had been 90+ degrees and dehydration was a real possibility), was consistently ignored, until she finally slammed down a bottle of water and told me they don't serve tap water. Maybe it's because I'm from out of town, but I had never heard of such a thing, so when I questioned it, she had security escort us out. Seriously? We will not be returning.
Came from Philly to Nashville to check out this spot. Very well lit. Good food.. Try the fish tacos they are my favorite. The drinks are well made and very reasonable.

This place was the best dive bar- met so many people from all over the world. Music was great classic Nashville-- what Broadway is missing and strayed away from. Beers were most $5 and they had a few local selections. I enjoyed myself and posted a commemorative $1 bill to the wall- def check this place out if you want to "old" Nashville true country live music.
This place was miserably hot but luckily we got a table next to a large fan. On the flip side they had great band.

This three floor honky tonk had three different bands and a huge variety of music. 

It was crowed, but easy to navigate.  Found it a difficult to get drinks on the 1st, but no issues on the other two. 

We were invited to grab some open seats at table and enjoyed watching the bands and their interactions with the audience. 

This is a place you must stop at while walking down Broadway.
This is a nice bar to hang out . It's more for single people. But it has nice balconies and is huge!!!. Not the best price in drinks but have diferent groups playing in each floor.
Great place with great bands. Solid lineup compared to most places on Broadway. Always a good time.

I don't know shit about bluegrass music, but we came for Sunday night bluegrass jam to experience it live. The space is divey and homey with low ceilings and a casual, warm atmosphere. Cheap drinks and free live music? Good enough Sunday night plan for me.

We happened upon this gem - we heard two guys on acoustic guitars and that's what grabbed our attention. Great little dive bar with awesome music, laid back, authentic atmosphere. There's country to rock, and though we only came in for one drink, we stayed for a few hours. And hope to be back!

Not sure what the craze is with this place. Seemed very similar to all the other bars except for the fact the beers were way more expensive than anywhere else we went. Not my favorite of the night but a cool place nonetheless!

A little too "gritty" for my taste, with only a token, rotgut wine on the menu. But I appreciate that they aren't trying for an upscale vibe and I am clearly not their target audience! The band we saw was lively and talented, but it was hot and sweaty and condensation from the ceiling was dripping on my head so I had to move on to the next stop. Let's just call it... "Authentic."

This place is very cool! It was my first time in Nashville and I wasn't really sure what to expect. We ended up visiting this bar 3 times during the weekend. The live music is of course awesome and a band on each floor is pretty cool. I thought that the bands would drown each other out, but the floors are very distinct. We stayed on the second floor for most of our first visit by the balcony which was nice. 

Our 2nd and 3rd visit was before and after the Browns/Titans football game and it was awesome how many Browns fans were there. It was also pretty awesome that Honky Tonk Central was one of only 2 bars that were open around 10am. I'm not sure why they other bars are not open but Honky Tonk definitely caters to the "early drinker". 

It does get crowded there, I mean SUPER crowded, so that can wear on you a little but it's definitely worth a stop if you're in Nashville. You can't pass up a good Honky Tonk bar!

A decent, but small venue.

The small size likely makes some events nice because of the relative intimacy of the venue, but it also has a serious downside.  That is that the floor seating consists of uncomfortable folding chairs, that over the course of a show of any length, will consistently remind you that you've been sitting in a folding chair for a while.

I would absolutely see another show here, but I would certainly be more interested in seating on the second floor which is entirely built for this purpose.

Was extremely excited to attend their NYE event. Unfortunately the top floor flooded and we were not allowed in. We were promised a refund by the management and now they are not refunding any of the customers who didn't make it in due to the flooding. Extremely poor management in my opinion.

It looks like fun from the outside, but it sucks inside. I would have given it 2 stars, except that they had a bouncer at the bottom of the stairs with a serious authority complex. He tried to point me outside when I came down and after I told him I was looking for my friend he told me I needed to leave because I had enough to drink. I had only had 3 drinks, and was wobbly from my high heels. As I'm trying to kindly explain this to him he again refuses to let me into the bar I was already in. I pointed out that I was drinking water and he promptly snatched it out of my hands. I am a very calm, nice, and reasonable person who has worked in bars and restaurants. This was the most appalling treatment I have ever received at a bar. I went to the front and asked for a manager and he was not as rude but equally useless. He didn't seem at all concerned about his employee being in the wrong, but instead wanted to know which one let me back in to talk to him, though there was no reason for me to have been kicked out in the first place. This was my birthday celebration and this was the worst mistake of the night. I would never go to this disgusting tourist trap and give a dime to pay employees to disrespect women just because they can get away with it.

We enjoyed this location, a band on every floor is always great because if you don't like one you can just make your way to the next. The balconies on every floor is definitely one of the best parts about this bar. It's great to see the chaos on the street down below while you're comfortably standing in a bar listening to great music. It's also smack dab in the middle of Broadway so you get a great taste of the vibe of the city. 

Only thing I didn't necessarily like was that this bar has bathroom attendants. I don't need someone to put soap in my hand or rip my paper towel, and I don't need small talk while taking care of business. 

Other than that, great bar.

I had high hopes for this place. However, we walked in and were immediately greeted with stares from everyone there. Then we find out there is a $12 cover charge- on a Monday night. Considering every other place we went to didn't have a cover charge, this is a little steep. The music seemed great and I wish I could've enjoyed it, but we decided to leave after being awkwardly confronted after making it halfway to the bar to be told there was a cover charge. Not only that but they made it uncomfortable and were rude. Maybe this place is better for locals than visitors but i felt like they could've shown a little more courtesy in the way they spoke to us regardless of who we were. Otherwise, the actual place seemed like a cool little spot and what little we heard of the music was nice.
Love, love this place. Rocking music all day long, good food and fantastic staff! Go Tara!

Honky Tonk central is on of the better venues on Broadway. The bands are usually very good. Most nights they have a very large crowd if you're lucky you'll get a table. The next time I'm in Nashville I will definitely come back to Honky Tonk Central. Great place to listen to good music and watch interesting people.

This place rocked. Great bluegrass and mountain music on a thursday night in January.  The aesthetic is perfect- divey, southern and authentic. Much better alternative to the insanity of Broadway downtown. I felt it was worth the $12 cover.

Crowd is always on fire, never a dull moment.  The music acts are either super stars or super duds, not nearly as consistent as Rippys music down the street.

This is a must do tourist spot

Better acoustic music down the street at Rippys

This bar was so much fun! We went here two nights in a row! The fried pickles and fried chicken were very good as well as the drinks and live music. The Yee Haw drink was my favorite and the country bands were so good! I was dancing the whole night. There are three floors and on every floor there is a country band.

Total Downtown Nashville experience. Got pulled on stage by the lead singer of the band for a dance contest for single girls - completely mortified, but had an amazing night. Never seen so many combos of fireball recipes ((dangerous)) lol

We found a great little bar along printers row and were pleasantly surprised! Beautiful inside. Prices are good and the atmosphere is fantastic. You almost feel like a local the minute you walk in the door. Natalie the bartender was fantastic and we met some really cool people while we were there. We will definitely be back!

This place was awesome!  Though the decor of the building has the feel of the 60's, you shouldn't be alarmed.  For just $15 we saw a great group (18 South).  The beer prices are reasonable for Nashville ($4) and the staff is friendly.
We'll go back without a doubt!

Wonderful little historical venue. Good drinks. Reasonable prices.  Tiny music stage makes for intimate live music. Great hangout for some amazing music talent. Makes me sad that it's being shoved out by growth. I'm told next year this time, it won't be there and will be replaced by a parking lot.

Awesome music venu and a must do if you're in Nashville. Parking can be a bit tough, but what's new if you're from Nashville. 

Make sure to see the Mummies as they're amazing!

Crowded bar with multiple floors. Live music setup on each floor playing covers. The bar can get crowded at times so the wait for a drink might be a little but there are other bars to move between. The views of Broadway from the balconies is nice. The bathroom lines can get crowded and messy

Took a chance in Printer's Alley to get off of Broadway for a little while.  

This place is quaint and had a decent crowd and pretty good band for Wednesday night.  

We didn't eat there so I can not give 5 Stars. Good draft beer selection and good service. 

Take a chance and get off the strip and check this place out on Printer's Alley.

Honky tonk was a bar we went for New Year's Day to watch football. Had a big group of friends and were having a great time. One of my friends got cut off and as I went over to get him out of the bar, a security guard sucker punched me and put me in a choke hold. I have a busted lip and couple marks on my face. Even the bartenders had my back and said I didn't do anything wrong. I called the police and filed a complaint. But never once did a manager come out and talk to me. I will never recommend this place to go if they have this aggressive security guard working there. He assaulted me and got sent home. It is all on camera and I will proceed with legal actions. Ruined my trip to Nashville.

While touring around with family from out of town we stopped in to give them a taste of the touristy part of Nashville. We had the fried bologna sandwich which was tasty but definitely a gut buster. Waitress was nice and efficient. The bathroom attendant has a hoot! The band was Ok but nothing special. I would include it as a stop on a downtown crawl but not as a destination.

This was my first trip to Nashville and first time at benchmark. The bar was pretty nice. It's small and there is limited seating. There was no cover charge and of course there was live music. The music was awesome. There were no waiting staff so we had to go to the bar. This is where the issues I had came into play. The bar opens tabs but keeps your card. I opened the tab and they kept my card. I went about my evening and when I went to close my account prior to leaving I found they had given my card to another patron. 

I couldn't fathom how the staff would not check the name on the card before giving it to someone. That's a first for me. The bartender initially said she gave it back to me and I explained my tab was still open and she confirmed that it was. They looked all over the bar before realizing they swapped two cards mine and the other patron. 

Needless to say I was a little upset. I had to call and cancel my card and lock my account. The staff somehow reached out to the patron who had my card and he came back at bar closing and gave the card to the staff. I spoke with him and thanked him for returning it but at that point everything was closed and locked anyway.
FUCK THIS PLACE.. The security guard told me to fuck off. Was looking for a first drink... I guess not here. The guard was wearing mask. I hope the owners can his disrespect self.
Donny Lee rocked the house. Stopped in for one beer, but spent 4 hours. Great time. Will definitely add Honky Tonk Central to most fun bars in Nashville.

We wanted live music, and BOY did we get it. We happened in on a night when there was incredibly gorgeous Bluegrass music being joyfully played and sang by a mix of a regular band plus their friends from the audience. I think it was perfect: we got a little something different than what happens most nights, but it was exactly what we hoped for.

Someone must have read my review because they took that dreadful black tarp off the fence..
That was a ridiculous move, to begin with.
If you're going to build an outdoor concert venue in downtown, expect local residents to watch from the other side of the fence..

It could be an awesome place , but is WAY too loud! It is painful in the bar. Either turn it down or install sound dampening in the ceiling. As it is, I can't stand to be in the bar more than 30 minutes at a time. It's a shame cause it's an awesome bar....

Initially walked past this place but the music made me step back and walk in. Adam Rauscher was playing with Dominique Hutchinson. My husband d and I ended up staying for 4 hours enjoying the great service and great entertainment!

Deff one of the bigger honky tonks on the broadway strip. I mean theres actually some space to move in this place. When we got here there was no music on any of the floors. Maybe we can during the bands break but even still there was no music playing at all. It was easy getting drinks here, and a good spot for bigger groups, but might have less of the Nashville charm as other places.
The ironically named Underground has two good rooftop bar areas.  The have a good selection of beers.  The food is also pretty good, but our waitress was kind of rude.

Great live music in a cinder block building amidst upscale area. Intimate size makes it easy to see everyone on stage. Eat before you go unless you like frozen pizza and popcorn. 

Our 16-year-old son was thrilled to be able to see a live show at night.

Service is badass, music is badass. The vibe here is super rad and very fun!  Drinks aren't terribly strong and the food is just typical bar food, but this place is so cool. Also there are three levels!

For live music- 5 stars! Has a huge stage for performers and it's a large bar for group gatherings but as much as I appreciated the entertainment, I would be happy going to a smaller more intimate bar where it's easy to get a drink and you can enjoy the music with out being surrounded by a loud environment. 

For food, it's bar food. The service is nothing special. The margarita special for 5 dollars was watered down. I would definitely go hit up a BBQ joint then eat here if you are looking for dinner. 

For night life it's like a college party. Crazy, crazy lines with a younger crowd so I would just walk down until you don't have to wait in line and can actually breathe in whatever bar you get into. Maybe it's because I'm getting older but if you're a tourist, it's worth being able to get a sense of live music in those smaller bars.

First trip to Nashville and first place we stopped at. The music was very good but the service was awful. We sat at the bar got 2 beers, bartender took credit card and never acknowledged us again. We tried waving her down multiple times but nothing. We finally decided to eat somewhere else and had to find another worker to get our card so we could cash out.  Pretty sad for this place because I only heard good things.

A favorite music venue on my first Nashville experience 9/7-9/11. Great area and location. Stayed on the first floor and enjoyed the comfort of the couches and foot stools. Had eaten earlier across the street at The Stillery - great food - so didn't eat at The Famous Saloon. Maybe next trip.  The bar menu was perfect for a snack.  The only drawback was the ladies room first floor - although handicapped accessible -  lacked ADA grab bars on the walls as required. Once home I contacted management.  Today I  received a callback from Michael Shaw. He listened and was very receptive to my restroom safety concerns. He explained The Famous Saloon was a new venue that recently  opened and that the lack of ADA bars was most likely an oversight. He assured me that he would have maintenance bring the restroom up to ADA standards.  I thanked him and told him that I would be coming back for another visit. I'm hopeful as a disabled crutch user that Michael Shaw is a man of his word and that he will be sure that the simple fix of ADA wall bars are  implemented for all that visit The Famous in the future. It's good business!!!!

First time in Nashville on a girls trip. Super friendly staff and awesome food. Saw Isaac Mathews.  Honestly never a country fan. Man he changed my mind. Truly AMAZING voice!!! Lucky enough to meet him, sweet person. Highly recommend.

This place is unique to the area, and an establishment for future lounge/clubs in the city that is Nashville. How convenient to have a place  right across the street from where you live, can grab a drink when you get off from work, before the stressed come out to get loose. 

I was on soon enough to read the review of the patron who complained of the manager. I was in the vicinity of the encounter. With the place being as crowded and busy as it was, the manager could not have handled the situation anymore professionally than she had, given the circumstances. To add, the place was congested with people, and the fire alarm was going off. Given those circumstances, you can imagine the hand dealt.

As is with a patient, they sometimes think they are the only one the doctor has to tend to. That was the case with these patrons who were being irrational, and also drunk. I was there, near the entire incident, and the manager did not just instantly call them a bitch. In fact, she asked a question, after accidentally bumping into them. The women said, "did you just push me,bitch?" And the manager replied, "Did you just call me a bitch?" Any reasonable person can see how that can get misconstrued. 

With the place as busy as it had been, and that particular group as incorrigible as they were, the manager could not have handled the situation any better. They were a small part of a large whole-which was the entire place packed with people. She excused herself from bumping into them, as it was crowded. They chose to escalate the situation when she tried to resolve it. Given the circumstances, which was the place being packed, she had no choice but to have them removed. They were not within reason.

We stumbled across this place while walking on Broadway. 

The music was loud and everyone inside looked like they were having a great time. 

We walked in and there were a ton of people dancing on the first floor and the tables were full. We went upstairs and another band was playing! 

There were a few empty tables, so we grabbed a seat. The music was great, the atmosphere was fun and the waitress was friendly. 

The food was ok and the price was very reasonable. I would go back for sure!

Upstairs and downstairs with two different bands and styles of music. Balcony's to get fresh air that look directly out on Broadway. Great place to dance with plenty of room. Cocktails expensive with watered down alcohol. Atmosphere nice

This review is for music only (we didn't eat here).

We came here because we heard a great band playing. At 5pm on a Saturday night, this place is exactly where you want to be. The music is great and so is the energy. If you need to get away from the noise, you get step upstairs, but we all had so much fun we only went upstairs for a drink before we realized the band was too good to miss out on. We stayed for the changeover (although the first band was better than the second), and then headed to dinner. 

I would come back for more. It's a less "trendy" place than Tootsie's, but I actually had more fun here than there because it was less crowded and the bands were better!
Dive bar without the grime. Great warm place with music to be heard. Good place to hang for a beer.

Being Germantown residents, my husband and I were excited to see the new bar/club at The Back Corner at 5th and Taylor. The second I walked in, I knew I had to book it for our 15th wedding anniversary/vow renewal! So thankful we did. Belle and Michelle were great to work with. Belle went above and beyond to make sure all details were tended to. The venue was perfect - so vibey and ideally decorated. The sound system was great. The staff was a delight to work with! The food was delicious and the drinks were wonderful! All of our friends and family continue to talk about the evening and experience. My husband and I look forward to going back to reminisce as well as enjoy more drinks and food .  Welcome to the neighborhood, TBC. Thanks for being so great.
Awesome place when in Nashville bartender was great And service was quick .. can't remember her name though she worked on wed

After hopping around to a few different bars, we finally settled in at Benchmark Bar & Grill. They had just the laid back chill vibe that we were looking for. And the music was KILLER! Dominique Hutchinson has an amazing, soulful voice. The drinks were inexpensive and decent, and the bar tender was just the right amount of surly. Will definitely come back if we're ever in Nashville again.

My past few visits to Nashville I've found it to be consistently the best bar on Broadway. 
3 levels and 3 stages with live bands. Fun crowd. People watching. 
The bands on the main stage are great!

Really neat place to listen to some good music, have a few drinks, and maybe watch a ballgame. The drink prices are reasonable and the servers are friendly. This place is huge - three floors with three different bands playing all night.

Lots of fun! Be sure to check it out when you are in town.

I only got to Live on the Green once this summer but looking forward to returning next year. We had VIP tickets, so we were treated to lots of delicious food and enjoyed the show from the towers at the side of the square, which offered great views of the stadium, river, other parts of Nashville and yes, the stage. The music might have gotten a bit lost as I happily devoured appetizers such as candied bacon and bacon-wrapped peppers. But, this free festival is just one of the many things that makes Nashville so great. The audience range in age from young to old, babies, dogs, hippies and businessmen. Just a lot of different people coming together for some great music outside. I love this town.

We had a group of 30 people, we didn't have a location to eat a last minute dinner. The manager Rex made it happen. He and Courtney, got our tables ready sat us all together, let us split checks. Four hours of Great Food, Great Drinks and the best music talent we saw in Nashville. Prices on food and drink were below Broadway market price. A must go for food and fun!!! Thank you Rex and Courtney (and all of the staff at Nashville Underground). Oh and their Bushwhackers rival any whacked from the South!!!!

While in Nashville for vacation, we were looking for somewhere with a bluegrass set and did we find it! Sunday night is their bluegrass jam session- this place was packed with people from all over the world. Super cool place to have a beer and listen to some raw talent (old and young) just enjoy playing music together. I highly recommend making a stop here if you love live music and would like to get away from all the lights of the broadway strip!
Awesome venue, seating was perfect. Huge disappointment to pay 15 bucks for 2 bottles of water. I get that you gotta make money but almost 5 dollar profit a bottle is ridiculous.
If you are in Nashville, it's a must to come to the Station Inn. Plain and simply, it is the greatest music venue on the planet!

Went there with 50 of my coworkers so we had a price fixed meal. We had pulled pork, chicken, coleslaw and blueberry cobbler.  I wish I tried their wings, I don't know how the food is. I don't know what kind of drink I got but it was good.  We were on the fourth floor, so we had a great view. There was a band playing and they were very, very loud. I'll go back just to try their Bar food and get their specialty drinks.

We went to a concert here last night. It is a great venue for concerts. Good acoustics and plenty of room. Bathrooms are pretty far away and on a different floor but were extremely clean. The exterior is really amazing and beautiful. You would never know there was an auditorium inside.

Finally got to catch a show here on Sun! Boyz II Men with the Nashville Symphony was amazing! I bought pre sale tickets so we had amazing seats! Sec 102, row B, center stage! We paid for parking on Peabody which was pretty convenient, no traffic getting out. Got there a few minutes before the gates opened so there was quite a line, but went by pretty fast. We wanted to grab something to eat, and I was pretty disappointed in the food choices inside the venue. But we went with Martin's, which was ok. Restrooms were nearby and clean. Overall, he venue was very clean. Love the views of Nashville from just about anywhere in the venue. We were fortunate to have very beautiful weather that night. Lawn seats wouldn't be bad either, they even provide law chair rentals. We had a great time!
Great atmosphere, great singers and great waitresses! Tons of energy there! We will definitely come back!

Honky Tonk Central was just what we were looking for. Great music and good food. The band was amazing and played a good set. As for the food, you can't go wrong with the cheese burger and tater tots. Overall a good time.
Great low key "hole in the wall" place. Definitely more locals than tourists and such a relaxed feel to the place. Not a place for food, but fun and unique atmosphere.
Service was great. Food was cold and soggy.  I would recommend it but keep on top of your food order!!

Everyone stops at the first floor where it's usually packed. 2nd floor is the spot where it's not horribly loud music and great musicians. Nachos are legit as well. Been there the last three trips to Nashville and seems to get better every time. We'll be back again!

This place has a great roof top bar area with live music, there is also a downstairs. It gets crazy packed inside but service was fast and friendly upstairs, downstairs seemed a lot busier and hard to get the bartenders attention. We had a great time listening to live music after the Titans game on a 75 degree Sunday in December on the roof!

Honky Tonk Central is an overpriced and overcrowded tourist attraction bar, but so is every bar in downtown Nashville on Broadway.  The musicians on the 1st floor weren't bad, but they push for "tips" too much.  It is a great place for people watching, but there will be at least 25 bachelorette parties in attendance "wooing" all night.

One of my worst experiences in Downtown Nashville. Over crowded. Slow bar service. Very very dirty. On the top floor there were only single restrooms and I stood in line for 20 minutes to use it. Once I got in there it was covered in urine and feces. I couldn't even wash my hands because of all the trash and beer bottles in the sink. To top it all off they were out of my favorite beer, Blue Moon. The only good thing is you can step out on the balcony to breathe fresh air instead of the horrible odors through out the building.

New Years Eve at the Nashville Underground was nothing short of a disaster and total disappointment! 

Upon arrival we were greeted with a closed door! Security guard on inside secured the door so we could not open it to get in and sit at our $1055.00 table we paid for! It was 11 degrees outside and a huge line of customers that paid to get in were made to sit and freeze. All the while Joey DeGraw (one of the partners) sat just inside the door, laughing at the irrate patrons. I guess no one told him how business works...treat the the customer with respect because they pay your bills! 

We were told prior to our arrival that there would be two lines...one for VIP and one for General tickets...that didn't happen. Though they said we could not enter because of capacity issues (which all seats were presold and accounted for before NYE so I am not sure how they over shot capacity) once inside it was surprisingly light on people! We arrived to our seat just moments before midnight and were given a single drink even though we prepaid for two plus a champagne toast (which we never received) and a charcuterie board we prepaid for but never got! To top it all off the fire alarm went off the entire night. We had our fill of being mistreated and made our way to FGL House where we we treated amazingly! Nashville Underground is not destin for longevity at this rate...we won't be back unless we get a refund and apology!
Good music! Service is good and waiter was funny.... food was pretty good 4stars but overall a 5

This was our favorite bar on our trip to Nashville! I wish I could remember the name of the guy who was performing on the first floor last night because he was amazing! This place had the best atmosphere and fast service for being crowded. We absolutely loved it.
I love my military history. Huge selection of war memorabilia. I really liked the "Band of Brothers" stuff.

Tried to give homeless teenager money from inside and was asked to leave. Business stated they did not care about homeless teenager begging for money in the street. I was escorted out like a criminal by their wannabe security personnel.... very unfortunate because this young man made several dollars and was very happy with my donation! Shame in you honkey tonk!

Go when Isaac Matthews is playing!

The service here is great and the people are really nice. They have some pretty quirky signs up which made the experience even more fun. We didn't order anything crazy but there was always someone ready to take our order and answer our annoyingly stupid questions like do you have bottled beer. (They do. There's a row of them above the bar so you can easily make your selection.)

I would highly recommend this place for locals or tourists.

Being the musical snob that I am, if I lived in Nashville and anyone remotely interesting played this venue, I'd be there in a heartbeat. Seats maybe 350, room for more to stand, balconies, great staff, decent eats.....love it!

I've got no good reason  to not add the 5th star.  We attended the Sturgill Simpson concert last night.  The place was JAMMED with people.  Sturgill sold out two nights and if you haven't heard him...get on that right away.  The servers stayed on top of everything and we didn't have to wait very long for dinner or refills.  Dinner by the way was really good! I'm always surprised at how tasty the food is at 3rd & Lindsley because I'm never expecting anything other than bar food.  I had prime rib, which I never order but wanted for some reason.  It was good.  It was the sides though that impressed me the most.  I was totally expecting frozen broccoli but you could tell it was fresh and NOT mushy!  Same with the small salad...very tasty and fresh.  Also worth mentioning is the clean restrooms.  Seriously, with crowds that size you could expect a disaster waiting but they are always clean.  Free parking and plenty of warnings to not fall for the guys trying to con you to pay for parking.  It's a great, small venue and we will be back many times.

My family and I were in town for vacation and we ended up here on the rooftop. It was a blast. They had a DJ cranking out the tunes and people drinking and having a great time. It's nice to go somewhere and actually have a DJ and not live music.

Very lively and chill. It has two floors. The first floor is always full of people but if you need some space there is always the second floor. There is live band music on both floors but if you need some quality time with your family, friends or significant other go to the second floor.
The food here is good, but nothing special. The live music and atmosphere is great though!

Great music venue. Food isn't bad either for bar food. We listened to a great band. It's a little off the beaten path. Waitstaff was very nice but their definitely weren't enough of them.   They don't have a set closing time, just whenever the band finishes so plan accordingly.

Great party bar right in the heart of music row. I stopped in while I was in town this past weekend on a Sunday afternoon. My husband and I were looking to watch some football but also not be too far from some live music. Honkey Tonk Central was a great mix of both worlds. The first level of the bar has a ton of TVs playing every NFL game you could want. In addition, they did have quite a large band playing contemporary and classic country throughout the afternoon. The band was super talented and had high energy. It was a great place to get our sports fix and have great live music. 

Drinks were good and bartenders were quick, efficient, and friendly I sadly didn't partake in any of their food, but the chicken wings smelled heavenly.
Ok have to rate on the food. It's not bad for a bar. I had chicken sandwich with tater tots. Course the band and love music is the best.

We attended CMA Fest last weekend and before going, we heard all about Nashville Underground - how it was such great food, music and a friendly atmosphere. We decided to check it out ASAP and are SO glad we did; we LOVED it! The food was amazing, the music enjoyable and the service awesome! We even sat on the patio and with how hot it was, the waitress was on top of our water, other needs and continued fun conversation too. Nashville Underground was definitely a highlight of our trip and we'll for sure be back!

Tarps are back up on the fences.
They don't want the locals watching from the street.
Will find a roof to enjoy the concerts from because I'm not paying their exorbitant prices for outdoor seating.

Great evening last night with Long Players and special guests to re-enact Fleetwood Mac.

One of the best shows ever!

Food was also very good as was the service.

Love it.

With so many great bars on Broadway, there's no reason to go here. The "cocktails" were way overpriced for what you get, which is a subpar mixed drink (vodka and lemonade for $9) in a dinky little plastic cup (think what you would find to use for water in a waiting room). Food is even worse. I got the pulled pork sandwich, the pork was dry and lacking flavor, and the chipotle BBQ sauce looked like something one would find in a baby's diaper. My friend got the chicken tenders and they were cold inside. To seal the deal on this place being a terrible experience, the waitress shorted me on change. Save yourself the poor experience here and go down the block to Tequila Cowboy, they have significantly better food and drinks and better prices (my drink there was twice the size, much better quality, and cost me less.

Fun times, as long as you're drinking and not uptight. It's very crowded on the wknds and you have to be ok with drinks, crowds, and loud, obnoxious people! Always good music, but take your own flask, as alcohol in downtown Nashville is incredibly expensive!
Great spot for drinks and live music. Great band called Lower Broadway band performing.

I went here while I was on vacation in Nashville. I loved this place! The band that was playing was awesome. Great view of Downtown Nashville. I can't say much for the drinks since I don't drink... BUT if you don't drink, I highly recommend the Sweet Tea. It was honestly some of the best I ever had. Definitely a fun time here!

Was not a huge fan of this place. The food was not good, my fish tacos were bland and fishy. The waiters picked up my food and my drink before I was finished which I thought was rude. The band upstairs was overbearing they came by our table twice and specifically asked for a tip, so rude. I would have left one if they would have just left a bowl for me to drop one by but asking twice within a hour is not cool. The prices were ridiculously high. For a Coors Light is was almost five dollars. I definitely recommend trying somewhere with better food, service and prices.

!!!An amazing set of cosmic variables aligned to create a magicle backwoods night at the station inn. Randomly stumbled upon it through an ad hoc waiter recommendation. The "Pizza and Yuengling" sign signaled good vibes instantly.  For 2.5 hours, we experienced the best banjo-tastic bluegrass music I've ever witnessed. Next visit to nashville, "Station Inn" WILL happen.

Just visited Nashville for the first time and this was my favorite spot! We ate there for lunch and then continued our drinking there at nighttime. Such a lively atmosphere and great musicians performing. Relatively Pricey cocktails but well worth it.

A sublime venue for music and ambiance. I feel that no summer in Nashville is complete without visiting Ascend for a show. One of the highlights is the acoustics. You can listen while still talking. You can hear the lyrics without sacrificing a sense of socializing. you get to see the Nashville skyline and delight in a top notch band at once. great food and drink selection too!!

How is it that I'm a live music junkie, have lived in Nashville for almost a decade, and only been here once?  Serious life fail on this one.  My first concert here assured me that I will be back pretty regularly.  Beautiful space, great staff, great sound...again how has this not happened before?!  

Be prepared for lines to get in and get beverages (oh wait, like all other concert venues) but the staff are really great and things move along quickly.  It sort of reminds me of the Ryman but larger, and with a standing-room-general-admission area that can be a real blast given the right band (in my one experience it was awesome).  

Its right downtown so come early for the whole park-and-walk of downtown Nashville.  Tickets are usually reasonably priced for this venue.  I cannot wait to go again.
Great music. The corner spot is very nice for people watching. I don't like the bathroom attendants looking for a handout - very big turnoff. The beer is expensive too.

We had a great time at Famous! Beautiful decor! The guitar pick art is a must see... The truffle fries were amazing, but the last time we were in they didn't have them  The lower level is live music and the roof top bar has a DJ.

Favorite place to go to during my weekend in Nashville! My group always ended up starting and ending our night here.  We visited this place 4 times in one day.  There's lots of space, and the crowd gives off a really nice vibe!

I was looking for a fun dive bar, and thought I found one. This place has only bottled/canned beverages and no liquor, which I was not expecting. I would have liked it better if I could have a draft beer or cocktail.

We came here towards the end of our night and just stuck to the bottom level, it was good. The band was great, it wasn't super packed so you had space to move around and dance and it was a pretty chill relaxed spot. I would try it again, if we had more time to check the other levels it would be worth a shot, seemed like a good place for entertainment
I had a great time here. The band had some questionable song choices but all in all I had a great time.  Good party atmosphere and large bar to belly up to.

Had a horrible experience. The bartender with the blond dreads in a man bun was a complete jerk. He yelled and argued with us about having an attitude when we confronted him about how rude he was when we asked him what the specials were. We went to leave a tip which he didn't deserve, and he said, " I don't want that."  He should be fired.

The family and I was there for the first time to see Ward Davis and it was awesome!! Great intimate venue to watch live music!! Not a bad seat in the house. I was looking at the up coming shows, and they have a fantastic lineup. Any and all kinds of music is represented, so you will definitely find something to get down to. I can't wait to attend another show!!

Foods ok but the beer is cold!!

My husband and I came here during CMA fest for a quick beer before heading to LP Field. Although the bouncer was super nice and let my husband take his Pita Pit purchase from next door inside, which was a perk, the music was pretty crappy, which was most definitely not a perk.

The place has a decent selection of beer, and seemed to have a lot of space/seating, but there was definitely a better vibe at a lot of the other venues on Broadway. Maybe it's just that 2nd Ave thing.. I mean, after all, it is on the same street as Hooters and Coyote Ugly.
Please GO TO THE BLUEGRASS JAMS on Sundays. It is almost a religious experience, it's transcendental. It was one of the most amazing and soulful experiences I ever had in my life.

Won't play Beyoncé. Made everyone boo at me for requesting with $20. If you want to hear the same freakin songs you hear at every other bar on the strip great. Don't ask for anything original or they'll shoot you down.

Super coole Live Musik Location, wie ich sie in dieser Art in Deutschland sehr vermisse! Jeden Abend spielen hier top Bands aus unterschiedlichen Genres. Von R&B bis Country bekommt hier jeder Musikliebhaber erstklassigen Sound zu hören. Der Service ist allerdings sehr langsam und die Auswahl an Speisen sehr mager. Also zum Essen würde ich hier nicht extra her kommen. Aber ein Bier zum Konzert und eine Handvoll Chips gehen immer! Für alle "Starhunter" auch ein Geheimtipp! Hier tummelt sich alles was Rang und Namen hat und der Club ist fern ab des touristischen Broadways von Nashville.

Loved it!!!! We took a tour of music row that started and ended here. Before the tour we stopped in for sodas for the kids. The bartender was so friendly and even lent us a ukulele for a picture on their stage. We enjoyed the few minutes we were there so much that after the tour we went back and had some drinks and lunch. Definitely recommend!

I am giving 2 stars bc I came here and had a great experience the first time - nice workers great servers and friendly patrons ... 

I went back a year later and apparently they hired some horrible rude people.  I was here for a friend's bachelorette last night and when I got out of the bathroom I asked a worker how to get back upstairs twice because I couldn't hear him over the band.  He grabbed my arm and said to walk outside with him.  I said I was walking upstairs where my friends were and he yelled in my face not to talk back to him and to walk outside.  

He walked me outside.  I explained what happened to the bouncer and walked back into the front door.  What a rude inconvenience.  Loser with a Napoleon complex - cut your man bun and don't be rude to paying customers.   I went back inside only to get my friends and leave.  You know how to lose business.
My favorite new/old beer stop in Nashville! They make the newbies feel right at home.
This is a tourist trap. Price gouging and overcharging. Buckets of beer are priced from $36-$49 depending on the waiter/waitress. I don't recommend opening a tab! Buyer beware!!

My husband and I were visiting Nashville meeting up with our daughter and her friends to celebrate her 30th birthday. What better way to celebrate than to pub crawl among the vast options along Broadway and all it's side streets listening to some kick ass music? We found Benchmark by chance, but ended up staying and finishing our night there. We had a blast. The crowd was lively and energetic, yet it wasn't crazy crowded where you are elbow to elbow. The band was great. The bartenders were friendly and provided fast service, and that's a big deal coming from a former bartender. I did have one mishap between the beers and the fireball (yikes - getting too old for that though), I somehow "misplaced" my coat on what was probably one of the coldest nights of the year. Checked with the bartenders but no luck, so was disappointed that I had to walk back to the hotel freezing my butt off. Unfortunately we had to fly home the next day, so there went my coat. I called the bar and left a message asking if they would call me if they came across it. To be honest, I was pretty sure I would not hear from them at all. It took a couple of days, but the owner, Jamie, personally reached out to let me know they had found it. I gave him my address and asked if he would ship it COD. He got it out that day or the next and he graciously paid for the shipping himself. That is southern hospitality for you. Thank you, Jamie. I appreciate it. That was my favorite warm coat! We love Nashville and are already contemplating when we can return. When we do, we will definitely check out the music at Benchmark again.
Nice dive bar...music is on all day all the time...haven't tried the food but people seemed to be happy. It's a great happy hour spot. Grab some friends, request music and enjoy listening.!
Atmospheric, good service and cheap beer. Best thing about it was My One and Only, an extremely talented husband and wife duo.

As promised, I went back last Saturday AND Sunday nights.. Caught Tim Bridges and The Honky Tonk HitMen on the 3rd floor, Sat night and then on the 1st floor Sun night. AMAZING performers.. If you want a little preview you can watch some videos on YouTube.. Search Tim Bridges 2224... Or AMKing925.. I recorded the band..

It's a bar, 3 floors, 3 bands, lots of folks....lots of folks. The balconies are pretty cool. Dirnks were on par with the rest of the bars in the area, overpriced and weak. Can anybody make a good gin and tonic in Nashville? Anyhow, yeah, it's a bar, and it has bands. Bouncers may have roid rage is the only thing I'll say. Some little twerpy kid wasn't happy about something and got in the bouncers face and the bouncer, all 300lbs 6'5'' of him felt it necessary to headlock, take him to the ground and handcuff him. Looks like that bouncer wasn't allowed to be a cop, thank goodness.

Legendary bluegrass venue in the Gulch neighborhood of Nashville! It's a dive with $11 pitchers of bud light and $2 baskets of movie theater style popcorn. The music however is at a very high level. Friday and Saturday nights at this place are a real party! I just saw Scott Simontacchi and Ryan Cavanaugh kill it there this past Friday night! Lots of players from the ABC Show, "Nashville" play here. Go check it out FO SHO.
Drinks are expensive, but the music is really great. I love how there are three floors with three different bands playing. I definitely plan on dropping back in the next time I'm in town!

We were looking for a good place  to hear some live music outside broadway and this definitely is a place to visit

The music is great and service is great and not hard to get a drink

This is a must visit

My friends and I were enjoying ourselves at Honky Tonk this past Saturday night along w every bachelor and bachelorette party in USA. A guy from one of these parties pushed me off a stool, which resulted in me falling into another customer. A waitress whom I had noticed was incredibly annoyed all night by observing her scream at customers to get out of her way - proceeded to call me a rude bitch. Two things I have to say about this...1. I have been in the service industry for over ten Years and therefore have an incredible amount of respect for people in this business. 2. I have dealt with some major jerks myself - but rule #1 - you never curse at a customer. The door guy extinguished the situation and he could not have been nicer. He also mentioned to me that waitress had been in a bad mood all night. Get a new job if you do not have patience for a packed bar. You're working on the hottest street in the state for gosh sake. Star for nice doorman and star for great music.

An above average spot. A really nice bar. The band was good. One thing about this place that bothered me was that they didn't serve Gerorge Dickel. Tennessee only has two whiskeys, Jack Daniels and George Dickel. One can get JD anywhere, so since we are in Nashville, only about 80 miles from Tellahoma (where Dickel's made) it should be an option.

 The first day I drank Dickel was the last day I drank Daniels..

We came in earlier in the day as we had a few kiddos with us and this place did not disappoint!  I love that every floor has a different band playing, even on a random afternoon.  The kids were happy to sit at a table and jam to the band and I felt like our server paid enough attention to them that they felt like "adults."  Not many places are willing to do that even during a less than busy time of day.  The food is standard bar fare, but it was all done really well and our drinks were on point.  The place was not packed, but there was a decent amount of people on every floor.  Good atmosphere and a a good time.  I would definitely come back without the little ones!

A triple decker bar. An impressive live band. Large dance floor. Fun night! A must stop for all those looking for a good time.

This was my first taste of the late night Nashville strip scene and it was a great way to start off the weekend. Live covers all night and a rowdy crowd made for some great laughs.

Holler 'N Swaller!!

Great concert venue. We saw Casey Donahue Band! They were great. The best part of our experience was having Candice from CA as our bartender. She provided drinks the entire night and was attentive. AMAZING BARTENDER. Will come back again because of her.

Saw Pretty Lights here and it was amazing! Having the skyline in the background was wicked. Recommend comfy shoes, big mistake on my end after a night standing on a hill but I can't wait to make this trip for another show!

I want to give them a better grade because the are a bonafide Green Bay Packer bar- but I can't. I'm here for the Sunday Night Football game on Nov 4...
The bar service (from the kitchen) has been slow,and because 'the kitchen (upstairs) is overheating' the back door is standing open & the 53 F degree, rainy breeze is blowing through the joint. 
If I had wanted to attend an outdoor game and freeze my a$$, I'd have paid for the privilege. 
Despite complaints - beyond me- the door remains wide open. 
Get it figured out.

Definitely not 4.5 stars. Pizza reminds me of the pizza I had in school. Not wood fired.

Originally gave this place 2 stars. I have since realized I was way too generous. This place has good live entertainment but that is it. Bartenders don't know their menu. Food isn't good. 

Very disappointing.

I have only been one time but this venue exceeded my expectations! I went for the Halloween show of Pretty Lights and was very impressed with the venue and the staff! Easy security that got us inside fast even with a long line! Lots of options of drinks. (yes you will pay around $10 for a beer but thats the same at like every venue) It is bleacher style seating that has an incline towards the stage so no matter where you sit you have a great view! It was raining most of the time during the show but the crowd was amazing and the staff did a great job watching out for everyone! Would return again soon!

This venue was neat, with its historical monument feels outside and clean and classic look inside. It's located in Nashville and there is free parking from 6pm-1am by the library which is right across the street from War Memorial Auditorium a quick minute or 2 walk. Check in was easy and quick, the security attendants were helpful and friendly from doing their security search to helping us find our seats. There were several pop up bars available downstairs, upstairs and one in the bathroom hallway. They have a concession both with snack and beverages available too. Our seats were clean and comfortable with a great view of the stage, with the U shaped seating and standing option by the stage there really wasn't a bad seat in this venue. The best part was their music selection during the line up change, man Nashville knows their music! We almost forget we were at The Used concert, those songs had people dancing and singing. The restrooms were located down in the basement area which was a walk from our balcony seats and 2 flights of stairs. But they were clean and well attended for a busy concert event. My only issue was walking into the building, it could have a bit more lighting and I was wet from the rain and was like a ice rink. I slid my way into the entrance.

Probably one of my fave venues due to the layout. No matter where you stand/sit you have a really good view. Nothing to block the stage like at other places. Also, well ventilated. You may not think that's a big thing, but who wants to stand around sweating your butt off? I can stand right in the middle of the crowd and still be comfortable. You can easily get drinks right inside the room or at the stand just out in the hallway. Only problem is the bathroom is in the dungeon. No problems finding parking nearby. WIll definitely be back if they bring in more good shows.
We did some day drinking and stopped by honky tonk for some appetizers and got to listen to the band on the second floor.  Prices were reasonable . Nachos and wings were good

Awesome experience! We had a party of 8 and made reservations. We were seated right away near the live entertainment. Our waitress was extremely helpful with drink choices as well as entrees. The food was fantastic especially the hot chicken and fried green tomatoes! The banana pudding was enough for us to share and was delicious!!! The operations manager,Teddy, was super nice and showed us around upstairs. The outdoor spaces were very unique with outstanding views. We thought the decor was top of the line and created a hip Nashville vibe. We're looking forward to returning to Nashville and Nashville Underground.
The entertainment and ambiance was good.  The food was okay.  The staff was unfriendly.  Be sure to check out all three levels and have fun!
This is a happening place for sure BUT not enough workers equals bad service. Not enough room and too many tables taking up space.

I'm giving this place 5 stars because as a music venue its quite possibly one of my top 3 places for seeing a show, especially since the place underwent a drastic makeover since my first time checking it out.  It has amazing acoustics, lots of seating, and an overall ambience of just plain awesome.  

My one caveat here is that the food, while good, won't really blow your mind.  It's bar food people, and that's ok.  It's good for bar food as well.  Sandwiches and appetizers, which is really all you need when your focus is on a concert.  And it may take you a while to get your food, and your drinks, if you are fortunate enough to snag a table for a Sunday night show (Lightning 100 puts on Nashville Sunday Nights Live at 3rd and Lindsley every Sunday, with some great up and comers and local favorites...doors open at 6pm, shows at 8pm, so if you want a seat, COME EARLY).  At my last visit I noticed each server had a very large section to take care of, so keep this in mind when ordering.  They bust their butts, so give them some patience.

But onto why you come to this essential Nashville establishment...THE MUSIC.  Oh my GOD the amazing music, and it's so intimate in here.  It's like being totally immersed in the whole musical experience.  It's so much fun.

Your best option is to come early, get dinner, have drinks, and wait for the show.  Bring friends.  Check out an artist you may never have heard of because someday when they play Bridgestone Arena you're going to be happy you did.  Again, it fills up in here quickly, and parking is pretty limited at the place itself, so be ready to walk from the surrounding streets.  It's not expensive at all for a night out here (tickets are usually around $10, and the entrees on the menu are about the same).
