I have only ever been here for shows so I'm not sure what it's like on a regular music-free night, but for all the shows I've been to here I've had a great time, and I will continue to come here and check out whatever performers they have.

We happened upon this bar by accident. Great little dive bar. They had great live bands and the drinks were good and inexpensive. Bartenders were nice and you never had to wait long for a drink. They also have TVs and you are able to watch your favorite sports team. We will
Definitely return on our next Nashville trip.

Enjoyed honky tonk the location was great the music was both both in the day and later in that night. The bad at night was phenomenal the definitely were crowd pleaders. The food was a bit to over fried and bland for my liking. Next time I'll stick to beer and liquor and enjoy the show.
Sweet spot, beautiful interior, and excellent vibe.  Live music was kickin' and the bar tenders were super friendly.  One is now, actually, the mother of my child.
Loved the third floor bar and view of the water area.   Our server was friendly and prompt.   We enjoyed a shrimp po boy while enjoying the sunshine.  It was flavorful.   Definitely will b

Restrooms suck. Has nothing to do with the lady in the restroom. HTC has not been keeping up with their stalls, they do not lock and I did not have a place to put my bag. Also the crowd is not so clean in the restroom they think it someone else's prob.  If a place is not keeping up with their restrooms, what else are they missing.

This place was recommended for their burgers and I was excited to get one!  Salty, I mean saltier than the ocean!!!  I ate 2 bites thinking maybe I got a pocket of seasoning but that wasn't the case.  They took it off the bill, which was appreciated, but certainly wouldn't recommend getting burgers here

We had time for just a few songs (and drinks) on Broadway before heading over to Monnel's to stuff ourselves silly and ended up at Honky Tonk Central due to there being enough room without having to wait in a line. 

We could easily tell upon entering that this bar catered to the out-of-town crowd. Hints: the layout, a half dozen bachelorette parties sprawling throughout the three floors of the bar and the general "lets get shitfaced" vibe.  We found a perch at the bar and ordered our drinks - ginger and Jameson and a Bloody Mary. Yes, it was 5 p.m. and yes, I wanted a Bloody Mary. Yes, the bartender could have looked at me a little less like I had two heads. The drinks were standard - nothing to write home about yet no complaints. Unfortunately, we must have arrived at a bad time on the schedule because live music was only playing for about 50% of the time we were there - est. 1.5 hours. 

Lucky for us, the remaining 50% of the time was filled with a drunken shitshow of a fella from Columbus, Ohio who seemed to take a great interest in my boyfriend and me. Visual: fairly sober us trapped by spitting, red-cheeked, and offensive him. The bar probably should have cut him off. Don't get me wrong. I am down to get down, it's just that in between making offensive statements he probably could have wet himself without thinking twice about it.

In conclusion, great bar for your standard tourist-style Nashville visit. Sometimes all you want is a vodka cranberry, glittery cowboy boots and drunk cohorts.

Great place to see a show!  I have been several times, and always had an amazing listening experience.  Will be going back for more!

The salad I had was very average, so I won't be ordering food here again, unless maybe to try a sandwich or something.

Awful got kicked out for no reason had multiple witnesses that said I did nothing and the security still kicked me out will not go to that place again  way to go guys  have fun with the person that actually threw something off the balcony that will  probably cause  an issue in the future you just lost a customer

This was the first bar we stopped at after landing in Nashville on Friday afternoon. We were greeted with a friendly bartender and 2 amazing live singers. Food was bar food, but was good! Drinks were super cheap!
Talk about the complete opposite of "Southern hospitality"... Rude waitresses and gross food ruined the entire experience.
Great atmosphere and view from third floor. Menu was kind of limited and drinks were pricey. Music was good with different live bands on each floor.
This place is cool, they had a band there that was country music entertainers that brought tears to my eyes.  We order the catfish and it was good, very seasoned and delicious .
Great service and the guys performing live music were great. Ranch dressing was also good. Very pleased

Fun place to be during CMA Fest. Went for drinks and to hang out on the rooftop bar. It was very nice. Loved that they have self serve water. I heard there was a bathroom attendant which is cool. We played cornhole up on the roof. Wish we tried some food.
Bands were good! Has 3 floors with different band on each floor. Drinks are good. Pieces are normal. Good spot

Incorrect information.  This place closes at midnight.  We were very excited to visit but unfortunately came to a closed establishment.  For all of the fun that Broadway offers until 2-3 AM, it is not worth it to head here.

My co-workers and I went for lunch and this was the worst dining experience I think I have ever experienced. We arrived about 11:50am and did not get our food until almost 1:00pm. There were several people who arrived after we did but received their food, paid their tab, and left before we even received our food. Customer service was very poor. We were basically ignored and had to wave down one of the waiters who still did not come over when asked. She told us to hold on but started clearing tables around us rather than assist customers. The floor manager came over and basically told us some BS about them being busy and all the orders went in at once even though we were there before several people and our order was already taken and in the kitchen however, those that arrived after us received their food before we did. Then the kitchen manager came over and said "can I help you" ugh sir who are you!?!? He just walks up to our table and don't even introduce himself or nothing. Then he explains that I don't know if they told you but they brung the wrong order out. Really? So I guess they continued bringing the wrong order to everybody else. We didn't order steaks or anything. We had wrap, sandwich. And quesadilla. It does not take long to prepare those things. And on top of all that, the waiter never came back to give us refills or anything. Just poor terrible service. I'll never go back!

My favorite bar on Broadway! Three stories with a different band on each gives you plenty of room to spread out and still enjoy live music. I also liked how much open air space you get to keep the place from getting too overheated. Great drink specials and an overall good Broadway honky tonk experience
Just Go! Great place to enjoy " honky tonk"! On Broadway, such a great experience! So much fun and great place to enjoy drinks and live music! Just Go! And enjoy!
Okay service. Day band okay but entertaining. The people watching was the best. I get it they all work for tips.

It was mid July and pretty hot. It also just rained so it was also pretty humid. The sign read cold beer and I could feel the a/c as the door opened and I stood outside. I was sold and went in.

A pint of craft beer was $6 (expected). Service was okay but awkwardly slow for not being busy. A guy behind the bar walked by me no joke 6 times while I stood there with my card without acknowledging me. There was a pitcher of water on the bar with cups so I can't complain that much, I pounded about 3 of those as I attemped to regulate my body temp and stop the intense sweating the TN weather brought on.

The live music was decent. Plenty of seating. The food that came out didn't look great, I wouldn't eat here. Grab a beer and cool off if you feel like you have to be on Broadway Street. I personally would rather get kicked in the face over spending much time in this area.
This place has always been one of my favorite broadway bars. Amy Wood makes the best lemon drops in town! The music is great and the service is top notch!

2 bottles of Miller lite 15 dollars (hope that includes her tip) plus having to wait while the bartender waited on every one around us and still having to get her attention they need a negative star rating won't ever come here again

If your a true music fan and go to Nashville, 3rd and Lindsely is paradise. We saw Vince Gill perform here with his Western Swing band for fifteen bucks! He came thru Chicago where we live a few months later and tix were $60! 
Top Nashville talent plays here, you never know who is going to drop by.
Cheers
Danno

Great bar for mid day music and drinks! Staff is quick and friendly! Only issue is the restrooms, could be a like for a mile! But I would highly recommend  this place anytime of the day to be honest! The blackberry moonshine gets you! :)
Pretty awesome bar! Great music and service. My sister got called up on stage which was hilarious!! Definitely recommend stopping here if you go come to Nashville!
Music played by experts. Thought we'd stay for a while and then book. We ended up staying the night and wanting more. Now we have a place to hang out on Monday. Well worth the $20 to get in.

Still the best music value anywhere! If you go on any Monday to see the Time Jumpers - all superb musicians - be sure to get there early to get a seat. And only $20! We were fortunate this visit to have the guy at the door ask "you wanna sit down front?" (Wait, it that a trick question???) He led us to a table right against the stage to share a table with a lovely couple from Indiana who'd been in line since 3:30...we felt a little guilty but that quickly passed. Vince Gill is the most recognizable performer, but he's just one of the boys in this group of studio musicians. If you aren't really a fan of excellent western swing/country music when you arrive, you will be a convert before you leave...good drink prices and variety might help lubricate your attitude. Selfishly, I'd like to keep this little gem a secret, but how can one not openly proclaim wonderfullness!

Great food and service! This place is really big and you can get food on any floor plus it wasn't very crowded for a game day! The food was delicious and it was reasonably priced! We will definitely be back!!

Thought this was a good place once upon a time but this time around the entertainer was talking and cussing at customers more than singing. Shut up and sing Isaac!! And you know what?? He wasn't even that good and the mic was wayyyyy too loud. Distortion loud. It was very off putting. And apparently anyone with an unfavorable opinion will get harassed from the business. Pathetic. Not recommended
This place is ROCKIN!  Great entertainment especially on Sunday afternoons.   Great service and great bartenders too.  A must see in Nashville.

Went to this place with friends during a weekend in Nashville. It has three floors with live music on each, and patios surrounding the area (which is great if you want to get away from the smoke that pervades most bars in the area). There were about a million bachelor and bachelorette parties, and not much selection for beers. That said, we had a great time - lots of fun music and happy crowd.

Last night we had tickets to see The Mavericks AFTER 2 reschedules.  I don't know if this venue oversold this event or what, but there were only 20 tables (if that many). We got there before the doors opened and there were a 100 or more people standing not able to get a drink or something to eat.  There was a smaller balcony in the corner but we were told that was for the band.  There were so many angry people leaving and getting their refund, but the management didn't seem to care that there were unhappy people.  I won't return, I don't care who is playing.

Went here twice over the weekend, one Friday and one Sunday night. Fri heard the Tennessee Mafia Jug band, Sun was a big bluegrass jam that a friend played in. This is not a hoity-toity place. You get pizza, popcorn, or beer and that's pretty much it (well, there are some assorted packaged snacks and soda). The lack of options is somewhat refreshing. Place is something of a holdout in a built-up modern neighborhood. Relax and enjoy the music, that's what this place is all about!

We went Sunday10/21 for the Bluegrass Jam session. The workers were fantastic. The snack bar had great options and was delicious. The ONLY reason I give 3 stars is the people were very loud and noisy. It was like they were there to socialize and not listen to the great music. If the crowd would have cut the sound level in half would've been much better.  Maybe if they announced music is starting and lower the lights might help. We actually left after 45 minutes because we couldn't hear. And that was after waiting in line 30 minutes to get in.

Over the years Nashville has changed a lot, but walking into Station Inn is like stepping into a time machine and hitting the 'good times' button. The management has the recipe for success, and there is no need to keep up with the trends. The venue accentuates quintessential country and western music; as the bass rattles the popcorn pops, the beer flows as the slide guitar moans, adds in some pizza and a banjo and your in the Inn!
Excellent spot to listen to some live country music!  Tater tots with chill and cheese were really good.  Only downfall is that it can get a little crowded
Enjoyed it. Did not eat just had a few beers. But atmosphere was nice and band on the first floor was the best of the 5 we listened to cruising through bars.

awesome place and we love it!!!

http://watchonlinevideos.org/dailymotion.php

One of the best places to listen to music in Music City! 
The revamped room has tables and standing room, with not a bad seat in the place. 
I highly recommend the Sunday night shows, sponsored by Lightning 100, but you'll want to get there early and have dinner to get a good spot. 
Edibles include sandwiches, burgers, wings- your typical bar food. Nothing terribly fancy, but you can also find a salad or fish dish if you're eating healthy.

Love this venue. We came here tonight for the first time and we were so happy. The service was great, there is seating upstairs and downstairs (upstairs has a better view of the stage) - there is also a section for those who want to stand in front of the stage. 

While waiting for our show to start, we decided to order dinner. I ordered a burger and salad and my boyfriend had fish and chips. Unfortunately, the food wasn't that great. Salad was pretty much lettuce and a ton of bacon bits. Although we weren't fans of the food, our waitress was awesome and always checking on us to make sure we were taken care of. 

We plan on coming here again. The staff was great and the venue wasn't huge so you could really enjoy the music you were listening to. Highly recommend checking out a show here!

Great find for live music in Nashville. The only difficulty was finding the place, since it was dark and in a fairly industrial part of town. Bobby Long was playing live that night and couldn't have enjoyed it more. What a great live music spot with ample seating!

Saw the good Yelp review and that it was "Off Broadway" so tried it. Glad I did. Was Thursday afternoon so not crowded. Just wanted good burger and good music and got both. Oh, and great friendly service from Shannon (think that was her name). Ordered blue cheese burger. You know there burger is good when they ask how you want it cooked!  It was hot juicy and delicious!! And the fries were those thin kind I like and were served hot. 

Solo singer was Nashville good but only got to hear a couple of songs before he was done. Duo act that followed was just ok I thought (wished I'd gotten there earlier). 

Shannon checked on me often (maybe too much but rather more than ignored)

3-stars for this place but this venue has the potential to be perfect. I decided to make the trip down from Louisville to see Florence + The Machine. Great show! The sound was better than expected to be an outside venue.

On to the good and the bad of this venue. I've been to many cities for many different concerts. Big. Small. Outdoor. Indoor. You name it. 

This venue is completely outside in downtown Nashville. There are seated sections in the front with a sidewalk separating the general admission lawn section in the back. I'm not exactly sure of the exact capacity but it has to be well over 5 or 6K. The seating as well as the lawn is gradually elevated. As far as seeing the show, there are no complaints no matter where you stand or sit.

The show area is fantastic! The rest of the grounds is another story. It holds a lot of people. Fine. The problem occurs with the drinks, concessions, food truck(s), other food, drink stands, merch tables, radio station booths, atm, restrooms, and other stands around. They're concentrated in practically 2 locations on opposite ends. The lines are one thing, but lines intersecting lines, chaotic, and rude people... not a user friendly experience to say the least.

Peeve number 2! If you're going to have a food truck then have more than one truck on the grounds! It was next to impossible to get food from the one truck that was there. There was one line with literally 50 people in it when I walked over! 

Peeve number 3! I went to the regular concessions to order a bottle of water. 4.75... ok... typical price for a venue bottle of water. Fine. They took my lid! They literally opened the bottle up and took my lid! I asked for it back and they ignored me! The cashier and the girl that gave me the bottle of water wouldn't even acknowledge me as I was asking for my lid. What... you can't give me a legitimate answer? Later on I saw a girl with a bottle of water and one of the event workers took her lid too! What's with that?!

Peeve number 4! The prices! Out of all the cities and venues I've been to I have NEVER SEEN prices that expensive. Craft beer... 16 dollars! Domestic cans... around 12 dollars! Domestic premium(whatever that means) cans... around 13 dollars! I shudder to think what the vodka stand was charging over in the corner. Drink before you get there!

The lawn did get muddy last night as it misted rain throughout the evening so don't try to wear fancy shoes if you have lawn seats.

I've been to countless shows at the Ryman and a few at Exit/In(is it even there anymore?). This was my first show at this Amphitheater. Tell me that Nashville has more venues that are better than this one.


Take-aways:
1: Great venue with numerous planning issues.
2: I doubt I'll make the trip again unless I buy seats that aren't on the lawn.
3: Drink at one of the many bars downtown before you get there. (Prices are outrageous)
4: Eat somewhere downtown before arriving at the venue.

We came for some drinks and to hang out while waiting to head to a Karaoke bar, and it was a fun place to be! Great tunes from the band playing, and just fun to hang out by the bar. We mostly had beer, but did have some fireballs, which were tasty.

It is a pretty loud place, so it's not all that easy to have conversations, but it was a fun place to hang out. One thing I wish was different was that I didn't love that there was a bathroom attendant, who expects tips. Other than that, though, a fun spot.

My party stopped here during our Sprocket Rocket Party Bike tour.  We got the sprocket spot as recommended by our driver.  Please save yourself some money and do NOT buy this shot.  It was disgusting and thick like cough syrup.  It tasted like melted red jolly ranchers.
NOPE.

Gorgeous interior, amazing food, killer tunes and when the dj is rocking the rooftop it feels like a killer Caribbean bar up top!!!  Chicken and waffles is insane and I couldn't find a whiskey cocktail I didn't enjoy.

I had a nice time at Honky Tonk Central. I only went in because I needed a beer to cool off and this just happened to be right near me at the time. I was around 2 pm on a Friday and the place was crowded!!! All 3 floors were packed to the brim so I knew it had to be a fun place. My fiance and I were able to find 2 seats at the bar and the bartender actually saw us right away so major kudos for that! Since we were visiting we decided to try a local beer. We each ordered a Yazoo and paid in cash since starting a tab may have been a mistake. While drinking our beer we enjoyed listening to the band...they were playing some old school country which I loved. 

We stayed for a total of 2 beers each and then continued our journey down Broadway. The bartenders were all really great, but the price of a beer was insane! I guess paying $7 for a beer is okay when you are visiting a bar like Honky Tonk Central.

This is such a fun place to hang out any time of the day! I stopped in around 5 PM, then again around 9. Different vibes on each floor of the building, which is super fun. First floor is loud and rambunctious, second floor has more tables for talking and eat. Also love their little porches you can stand on and watch people. It is pricey, but it's a touristy bar in Downtown Nashville, so it's to be expected. Only dinging this place for the cleanliness, which was less than stellar. Use the bathroom somewhere else.

my husband and i had a fantastic time here on a recent monday (yes- monday) night.  service was friendly and efficient.  the drink prices are steep, and the servings are small, but when there's a good band playing, it's worth it.  i do think the band makes a big difference in your experience because, while we loved the first band that was playing, the second one was kind of a dud, so we ended up leaving.  that being said, it's definitely worth it to try this place out.  we hadn't anticipated ordering food, but we were enjoying ourselves and starting to get hungry, so we got buffalo wings, fried pickle chips, and a side of fries. the food was actually really good, nothing gourmet, but good.

overall, this is a solid spot on Broadway.

This spot is a Nashville institution and you are bound to see amazing music here any night of the week.  Bar is beer only and food is cheap pizza and hot dogs.  So if you want something else then eat beforehand.  

I showed up about 8:30 for an 8pm show and the place was full, and there is quite a lot of seating.  This is a singer/songwriter kind of joint.  Come here if you want to be captivated by good music!  It's not a very social joint. 

The staff (I think it was the owners), were all very friendly and welcoming!  This is refreshing in a tourism town where hospitality can at times be a little jaded.

Favorite spot in Nashville! No cheesy gimmicks. Beer, great music, food. Everyone that goes there is there to listen to good music not get annoyingly drunk. I would come here again and again and again!
Fantastic place to catch excellent music.  The night we were there the low key but energetic vibe was perfect.  Full house but not insane, fun crowd, no frills service was friendly and efficient.

I only go here during daylight as it gets way too crowded with bachelor/bachelorette parties after dark. Great music and the higher up in floors you go, the better the experience, in my opinion. Our service was great as it was not too crowded on a Friday late afternoon. We did plenty of people watching and still sat close enough to see and enjoy the local band. There was a group of college (Clemson) boys who gave us plenty to laugh at. 
After drinking and dancing, we got hungry and decided to give the Frito Pie a try. It was really good and I would order it 100 times more. Perfect food to offset the amount of beer we drank. After that, it was very nice to see that the line for the ladies room on the 3rd floor was not long and the single stalls were quite clean for a honkytonk bar. This place is a very well known and they have a reputation for great local music and wild times. Enjoy!!!

Food is amazing! Kid friendly, dined with 6 kids and got the chicken tenders basket and a couple sides. The service is great! Keeley tawtar was our server and she was amazing! Knows the menu very well and was so great with the group of kids. Definitely will be coming back!
Great atmosphere and live bands. I was refused a cup of water and told I'd have to pay $2.50 for a bottle. I've never been to a place that refuses someone a cup of water/not sure how ethical that is.
Great place to party with friends or chill/listen to good music. Had a blast! Would definitely recommend!

Great time and awesome location!!!
Where else can you have roughly ten thousand people outside of the court houses? Only in Nashville!
Great time and everyone was respectful and the place was very clean!!!

The music was great and I needed a break from the honky Tonk country atmosphere and this was it!!!

It didn't hurt that I scored backstage tickets this past Thursday and Friday.

Great tunes and the 3rd floor was rocking!  Broadway and 4th Ave the sounds are booming. Drinks flowing and this band is jamin!  Welcome To Nashville, TN
Honk Tonk Central is exactly that...Central to the fun!
#KatrinaAustinBand was on fire9
Day # 2  #2019RoadTripUSA
Our server was Amazing. She was annoyed when we tried to have fun. And showed her butt

I don't know if Yelp will allow this, but for 8 years, before I started hosting Sam's Jams on Wednesday afternoons in 2014, I was just a patron who loved to play at this place.  My favorite songwriter on the planet was tending bar there and it just felt like everyone was one big happy, but dysfunctional songwriting family!  As it evolved under new ownership, it became non-smoking and then the flood gates really opened from live music just one night a week to seven nights a week and at least four afternoons a week, too.  It STILL feels like family!  The comparisons to Cheers, where everybody knows your name, pretty much ring true for locals and not-so-locals!  It's a people place, if there ever was one.
Came from California and had a blast here! Lisa the bartender was then best put here!

Great place for live music. Acoustics & sight lines are good, ticket prices are good for exceptional entertainment! Food is typical bar food, good for what it is. Good beer selection, reasonably priced. Attentive,friendly service. Been 3 times, will certainly go again.

After reading some of these reviews, I have to say - some of these tourist have no idea what they're talking about. If you want to see some live music in the evening without fighting the crowds on music row, this is THE SPOT to go! The owner is a really nice guy who loves to jam with his fellow musicians. They're cool people! The drinks are reasonably priced, either $5-$6 depending. Get there early, get a good seat, and don't order the pizza... it smells up the place. Enjoy the show! You won't see anything better :)

Packer Bar downtown!  We had a great time watching the playoff game. Upstairs is the sports at with good TVs. Music playing downstairs. $4 beers (not bad for downtown).  We loved that we ran into lots of people from Wisconsin.

Honky Tonk has really good music. We usually do a beer or a shot in each level. Great views too!  We've never tried the food but it looks delicious with large portions. 

I rarely give reviews below 4 stars however we were treated pretty poorly last night after spending quite a bit of money. Let me preface this by saying we were sipping water and not even drinking anymore. I have zero clue why the 3 of us where approached and told to leave.  I don't know if we were mistakenly identified. They told us to leave right away.  They escorted us out.  We weren't given a reason. It was horrible & weird.  I have no clue what happened but I felt terrible over it. Not a single one of the three of us were acting foolish and we tipped well. 

We'll give them another chance next time for sure but pretty turned off at this point.
Wonderful little place with live music! Right on the middle of all the action, along Broadway! There are many places to stop, this can be one of them! Enjoy!

The BEST place to see live music in Nashville!  Small, cozy venue with really good sound!  You never know for sure who will show up, but it is always a great show!  I can't say anything but I wish I lived closer, so that I could go back on a regular basis.

This is the first bar we ended up going to in Nashville, mostly because they were one of the few still serving dinner by the time we entered Broadway at about 8pm. 

The live music was great, food was typical bar fare (and therefore delicious) and the drinks were great as well. My girlfriend enjoyed the Blushing Bride shot and Vodka Energy drink slushee so much that we gave Benchmark another visit our second night in the city just to order a round of those again.

Great little dive away from the chaos of Broadway, definitely recommend as a place to start or end the night.

We had a big private party for over a hundred people and they charged us 93 per head    Food ran out and they used same lame excuse that some people went back more than once through the food line.  For tacos sliders and bar food. Cool place but we prob should have just run individual tabs because the amount we paid wasn't a value for what we received.  Nobody bothered to respond to emails etc. we spent over 14k with them.

I wouldn't go here for the food. Ever. Ordered a cheeseburger. They give you a choice of American or swiss, but if you say swiss you will still get American.  The burger came was severely dried out and tasted like it had been in the freezer too long. The sweet potato fries were also over cooked but there no point in telling anyone your concerns because no one cares. The bartenders are super bitchy and the drinks are over priced for what they are. The sodas taste weird too. Cool music but I'd stick to beer and eat before or after

We came to Ascend Amphitheater for Dave Matthews & Tim Reynolds. I have to say we were really impressed with this venue.  

We were in the lawn and even those seats were really nice.  We had the option to rent chairs, but we didn't bother since we knew we would be standing once the concert started.  Sound was great even from where we were sitting.

There were plenty of restrooms and they were all nice and clean!  

Plenty of food and beverage options as well!

We used Uber, so I cannot comment on the parking. You can walk to Broadway or basically anywhere else you want after the show to enjoy the nightlife Nashville offers. If you want to Uber back right after the show, your best bet is to walk to one of the nearby hotels and get an Uber from there, you will miss the surcharge by walking a short distance and it will be easier to find your ride.

Great little venue and we would definitely come back here again!

Kitchen closed and would not serve us food we tried to bring some food in so we could eat and drink and they wouldn't let us do that either. Place sucks. Needs to be replaced by a bar with a manager. (There was no manger on duty there)

Well, first let me say that I did not have any food while I was at Honkey Tonk! But my boyfriend and I had our first experience to Nashville, TN, and we spent 3 nights at Honkey Tonk. The first night was my birthday night!! The band on the second floor invited me on stage and sang Happy Birthday to me, and allowed me to pick a couple songs for them to play. They were AWESOME! But also we went there during the day, and the bartenders were absolutely lovely, except 1. They were accommodating and even took pictures for us. I would definitely come back to this place! Their music selection is 99% country, and 1% everything else. But I LOVED it, because I love country music, and having s good time and singing along to bands!

We found this place on yelp and went to see Battle of the (College) Band the night before we were flying home to Phoenix. Great venue, as others described in other reviews. However the food was very average. I had the tilapia sandwich and it was fine, but would have been better if the broccoli was actually cooked and not crunchy and had some seasoning. The sandwich bun was also ok; not great. If they put a little more effort in the food this place would really rock. All in all it was very entertaining and we had a great view from the balcony. Enjoyed the evening. Just wish Bobby Flay would give them a little advice on how they could improve their food.

I went to see the Time Jumpers(with Vince Gill), it was probably the best 20 bucks I ever spent!  I believe they play most  Monday nights there.  What a place to watch live music, nothing beats a small intimate venue!  Our waitress gave excellent service, even with the show being sold out!  Food was good and affordable. They have a bunch of awesome painted portraits of music legends.  This place is a most do!  It is about a mile off Broadway, but you can get a golf cart ride for tips only, it is called "Joyride provided by the city of Nashville. Oh yeah, their alcohol there is pretty good too!

This is one of the best rooftops in Nashville, which is saying a lot. 

My wife and I also ordered dinner on their rooftop late at night. We got the fried green tomatoes appetizer to share which was absolutely delightful. 

For our entrees the wife got a smoked avocado wrap with a side of braised brussel sprouts. The wrap was absolutely delicious and the brussel sprout as a side added a decent punch to her great meal. 

Myself, I ordered the shrimp n grits entree. Wow. My goodness. I cannot entail how satisfied I was with this creation. I have had a lot of shrimp n grits in my life and this takes the top of the cake. Absolutely incomparable in its taste, context and delight. 

Best place in Nashville hands down.

Unfortunately, I need to give this establishment 1 star due to the inability to reach anyone about an item that I left. I was in for business and out the next day so unable to just go back to pick up the item.

A friend and I have called their listed number continuously for 3 days/nights - no answer. I posted 2 requests on their Facebook page - no comment or reply. Today,  I submitted a quote request for a private party hoping that someone would respond or call me. The auto response to the form listed a different # of which I left a voicemail - NOTHING.

Unbelievable!

We really enjoyed our Sunday afternoon here listening to bands and dancing too.   Fish tacos are great too.  Blake, who worked the second level was by far the most attentive professional server we experienced in our 3 day Nashville tour and over 20 establishments we visited.   Thanks Blake, we appreciated it!

Hell I don't listen to country on a regular, But this place was great. Other than the meatball bouncer copping a attitude at the door while I was trying to get a hot dog....I understand no drinks outside, just tell me where to put it. Attitude was rectified when I hit him with kindness in verbal judo.

Great group,fabulous bartenders and the music was worth hanging around for.
Dance floor small and the request  for tips for the musician is  sad. Pay them a living wage.

Seriously, it's just fun. Ended up here late on a Sunday night. Good drinks, good atmosphere, even better cover band. Loved the country style version of "I Like It" by Cardi B. Hilarious! Our group had a great time.

We were in town for a Bachelorette party and hadn't eaten dinner yet. It was getting late so everything downtown was getting to bar instead of restaurant hours, including Nashville Underground. We ordered food expecting nothing outside of typically greasy bar food, but our whole party was pleasantly surprised. I had chicken and biscuits & gravy and it was phenomenal. Everyone mentioned the food we had here all weekend.

The only reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is because it smelled like smoke, the noise level was at a point where we had to yell and point repeatedly at the menu for our waitress to understand what we were trying to order, and a basic well drink was at least $12.

I get it.... Tourist Central, but still a lot of fun.  Three floors, multiple bands, great location.  It is a place to at least stop by when in town.  Set your expectation to what it is, you will have a great time.
If anything, some great photos from the 3rd floor of Broadway to post on Facebook to make your friends jealous.

I'm in Nashville on Spring Break with my two roommates, and we had the worst experience here. We just moved to Arkansas, and apparently the bouncer isn't trained well enough to identify a legitimate AR driver's license- he wouldn't let us in, folded my friend's ID, and refused to look at alternate forms of ID. In short, he was a complete asshole. Don't go here if you don't want your night to be ruined.

I drove 450 miles to see my favorite band last week and to say it was the best concert I've ever attended would be a huge understatement. I was a little worried that traveling that far to see any musical act would lead to extreme disappointment and regret but it was anything but a letdown. It was magical.

War Memorial is in the heart of downtown and very easy to get to for anyone lodging in the downtown area. It was less than a mile walk for us. Upon walking up to it, we instantly noticed how beautiful the outside was and how huge it looked from the outside. There were signs pointing us to the will call area and I showed my ID and we were on our way. 

We skipped the opening bands because we had a lot of other Nashville spots we wanted to hit up first, but we arrived at 9 PM a few minutes before Brand New hit the stage. The auditorium was packed, but we snagged a few spots in front of the sound booth where there was a bit of a platform so it was raised a little bit off the ground. It was the perfect spot to be able to see everything, but the acoustics didn't sound the best in the beginning. People were singing louder than Jesse himself, so that was a little sad. It was fixed pretty quickly though and I was blown away at how incredible they sounded. They played for two full hours. My feet hurt by the end and I walked out without a voice, but it was worth it.

The only cons (besides the sound in the beginning) I could comment on are the drink prices. I've gone to hundreds of shows before and I'd say the prices here were even worse than what I'm used to. The drink was made really stiff though and so we only got one, so I guess it was an even trade off. 

The bathrooms were downstairs and there were a lot of stalls, so surprisingly no wait for the ladies room! I don't know that I'd travel to Nashville for another show, unless it was one of my other favorite bands, but I'd highly recommend checking out a show here for anyone in the Nashville area.

Our kind of place!
A hole in the wall joint with friendly locals, a nice bartender and local singer/song writers. Off the beaten  path (not walkable), in a neighborhood, but well worth the Uber ride.

One word: BUSHWACKER 

Order it. Unique to Benchmark. Think Wendy's vanilla frosty meets the muscle of moonshine. It is SO tasty. I literally think it has 8 different drinks in it... It's divinely dangerous!!! :-) Anytime we have friends in town, we visit and everyone enjoys!! In fact, several are obsessed with it and contemplate visiting just to get a Bushwacker!!

They have good quality bar food you'd expect (like burgers) and some you wouldn't (adult Mac n Cheese bites!!!) remember, it's a bar, so don't expect fancy fine dining. 

They also have an amazing Vegetarian Blackbean burger!!!

The beer selection is above average- they aren't a microbrewery, yet they feature a decent amount of local favors!!! 

Music has been awesome every time we go. It can get crowded but typically not annoying. And they have a spot in the way back that can be quieter or the upstairs when that's open/ not hosting a private party. 
And the staff/owners have always been SUPER friendly!!! 

Definitely worth the trip for a 'classic bar' feel with good food, beer and drinks without the cattle call feel often found around the corner on Broadway!! 

Ps- found out they are on the Nashville Haunted tours too...

We come up every month from Alabama to hear Sixwire play at this venue. It is easily the best venue for live shows, acoustics are amazing. We get a good meal, most everything is good (we just don't recommend the red beans & rice), and an awesome show. Love it.

Just left.  They will entice you to put in money for a song request, then when they do not play it, they tell you that you made the wrong song choice. The people there are so rude.  Do not go!!   So many awesome music venues in Nashville this is not one of them.

Another bar on our bar crawl...the band here was great! The place was kind of busy when we got there however there were seats at the bar. You couldn't really see the band as well from where we were sitting, but really enjoyed the music. In total we stayed for 2 drinks each and a shot...I think this place was a bit on the pricier side for drinks but we had fun.

Horrible bar.  $18 for a drink, no atmosphere, bathrooms were disgusting, waitresses extremely rude. Tried charging us for drinks we did not order. Do not go here, so many other better spots on Broadway that actually had a pulse. Customer service better step it up if they want to stick around, bad reviews travel fast and travel far. Would have given this place a negative star rating if it were possible.

Like everyone's mentioned there's different floors for different music. My friend and I got some drinks and sat in on the live music on the ground floor before heading up to the rooftop. I don't know if this is always the case but since it had just rained all day, it was very beautiful and breezy up on the roof. With mostly music from the 90's onwards blazing, it was a good dance atmosphere. I'd recommend people to come check out Nashville Underground, but of course as the night wears on, it gets more and more crowded so be prepared to stand in line.
Great little pub with great beer and live music. We stopped in 2 nights in a row while in Nashville.

Here on a special Girls week vacation; causin' trouble and makin' new friends with our awesome bartender Shelley who kicked ass!  Our new home away from home.  We will be back for Shelley.  We love Shelley!

I would give this place a zero. The fact that they won't let people in without passports is ridiculous especially when your at a bar. The bouncer sent everyone home without a passport. Valid drivers license for folks that are clearly over drinking age was not sufficient. My husband and I were turned away and bouncer said come back with a passport.  Good luck to you & Gavin. Plenty of other roof tops will let you in with a license.  I only use my passport for traveling internationally.  Was not aware that Nashville Tennessee was outside the USA.

Had a business meal here the other day.  There were about 35 of us. I was a little nervous as we only had one server for our group.  However, I must say that Kaitlyn the server was absolutely amazing.  She handled our group with perfection making no mistakes along the way. 

The drinks were flowing and the food was great.  I have eaten at countless restaurants over the years and without  a doubt the service from kaitlyn was the best I have had in any large group setting.
Do not order a mixed drink.  Neither one we ordered tasted like it had more than a drop of liquor on the straw.  And the coke was flat.
So walked in, place is packed, live band playing  band shuts down, DJ takes over. Place empties out. Take a hint. People come to Nashville for live music not stuff you can hear on your truck's FM.

This place is fun. It has multiple floors with a different vibe on each level. I loved the floor that had a projector playing the predators game on the floor and then transitioned to a dance floor with cool lights after the game. Rooftop is pretty and great view of the city. Food is average bar food. Service was very slow and it wasn't even busy the night I went. Drinks are expensive (just like most places on broadway). Would come back to watch a predators game

Three floors of fun! It's less crowded than other bars nearby and decreases as you go up a level. The 3rd level music lacked the most. It's large and spacious and the 3rd floor has the best view of the streets but I would suggest hitting up another bar after checking out the view.

Service was terribly slow!  Waited 1.5 hours for food to come out after placing our order.  Nobody offered to comp some of our bill to make up for slowness.  Then, on top of it, the bouncer shows up to tell us we need to leave the upper level.  When I turned around and asked the bartender if that was true, he said no.  But the bouncer continued to harass our party and randomly asked one person to leave.  For no reason at all.  We all stood there in shock.  After making us wait for our food for way to long, then randomly having the bouncer show up for some unexplained reason, the bartender did not seem apologetic at all. He seemed confused.  Worst experience ever!!!!!!

Benchmark still has the old Honky Tonk feel.  Best bar on strip.

Isaac and Bobby are the most authentic artists down here.   Worth the trip.
If you are over 25, avoid this bar. Lousy bar service (check your bill carefully) and the clientele is pretty low end.

This place is awesome!!   We descended on them as a traveling hockey team with a group of more than 40 and these guys took the best care of us!  The food was amazing, the server Dakota was fantastic and couldn't have done a better job taking care of such a big group and the manager Teddy shuffled things around to make it work for us!  Bull rides were so much fun - I can't stop thinking about the Poutine - wish I had time to go back for more!  Will definitely be my first stop if we come back next year!!

Came to Nashville for the week and every day we ended up back here. We had a hard time finding a bar with a good selection of beer on tap and this place had an amazing selection served ice cold. This was by far our favorite bar on Broadway. If you are looking for a more laid back place than some of the crazy bars, but with the best beer selection (not Jell-O shots), this is your place.

Hey folks whining about limited menu and no mixed drinks. This is classic music row bar that harkens back to the way it used to be when Kris, Johnny, Waylon and Willie were hanging out. 
They had to move a few doors down from original location a few years ago for "progress". 
Still this is the real deal. You like beer, you like song writers, you like real country? Okay then. 
You want glitzy crap go down to Wild Horse or one of those new bars on Broadway and donate your cash to Luke Bryan, Florida Georgia Line or the latest flavor.

This event was well organized, entertaining, and delicious! Fun for the whole family during the day and at night turns into quite the concert. I enjoyed the small stage more than the main stage. It's Nashville, so the small stage artists were still amazing, and I could move around much better over there. Food trucks were diverse and delicious. Parking was easy to find on the street close by if you come early enough.

I wish they would mow the grass. We had seats in section 101, row E. The grass grows between the narrow strips of concrete which are in front of each chair. So, there is grass under each chair. It was so long that it went up my dress and tickled my calves all night. 

Also, regarding those narrow strips of concrete, be very careful walking to your seat. The step-off is 3-4 inches, more than enough to sprain an ankle. 

Other than the grass, it was a decent amphitheater experience. The bathrooms are very nice.
Loved the band - Donnie and Sam. Good service and enjoyed the Fritos Pie. Much better experience this go around!
Dylan was awesome ! Would come back again. Great food and atmosphere. Bartenders and service are excellent as well!

Green fried tomatoes were awesome as was the Hot chicken and shrimp and grits. Teddy the manager was very accomodating and brought us out some collard greens that were the best we ever tasted. Will definitely come back next time we are in Nashville!
This place was awesome. My friend and I were the first ones in here. Had some chicken and waffles and they were the best damn chicken and waffles and eggs and coleslaw) I've ever had.
Stephanie, Jorden and Teal serve the best drinks!! Such a fun bar!! The service here is great, they make quality drinks with a great attitude!
Not a single person in here and our service was still slow as molasses.  This place was dead.  We ordered the hot pretzel app and left.  The pretzel was awful too!  Avoid.
$12 for a Jack and Coke. 'Nuff said. More since Yelp requires it. Average band if it wasn't Nashville. 15% full.

Yummy Food, Friendly Service and Music are Top Notch! 
Catch The Timejumpers on Monday at 8p!

Great acoustics! The bar has a great set up with balcony seating, lower seating, and standing room for dancing. The food was good for bar type food. Overall great experience, we will definitely be back!

I have been going to Live on the Green since the start in 2009, when I was brand new to the Nashville scene. 

Every year it gets bigger and better - this is a must for locals and tourists!

So many great bands - whether they are popular, local bands, bands that have almost made it, or well-known bands that you are dying to see. It's always a great mix of music and well, I believe that is because it is put on by Lightening 100 - who is always on the lookout for the best music - new and old! (I swear that I secretly don't work for them - I just love them!)

Anyways, the best part - it's free!!

You can bring your lawn chairs, blankets, pets (although yes - bringing your cat is awkward...please just get a dog instead of acting like a cat can be a dog), friends, cash (for beer of course), and be ready to party!

I would recommend finding parking a little bit further out and then walking - parking is tricky downtown in the first place, but with an event - it's 1,000 times worse. Or, this year - they started parking at Marathon Music Works and a shuttle will take you there and back and there is an after party there too! I haven't tried it out - but I'm sure it's awesome as well.
Great place off of Broadway. Shelly and Daniel are fantastic behind the bar!!!!!!!!!  Live music is great great view from the rooftop

We came to Nashville From New Jersey for a girls weekend, there is 10 of us and we all work in the industry so we appreciate a good bartender/server. Amanda was our bartender, I've never seen a girl hustle  that much. We go to bars and analyze these situations. That girl takes 5 drink orders from different parties and has it down to a science, she doesn't miss a beat and we went back to the bar just to see her. People like her make your trip pleasant so go see her and enjoy the amazing live music!

We only got to pass through Nashville for a few hours, and after we walked around we decided to get food before we hit the road. This was the closest restaurant so we stopped inside. The server was really nice, though a little slow compared to our normal tristate experience. I had the sweet tea which was amazing, and definitely complimented the BBQ pulled pork. What really blew me away was that at 11 am on a Monday, there was a live act covering country songs. I was so excited to see this, I never wanted to leave!

Love the venue for bands. We come to see Rubik's Groove and Vinyl Radio.  The venue is small enough that you can see well pretty much anywhere you sit. I gave it 4 stars because the food, while good, isn't great.

Honky Tonk Central is always crowded and busy during the weekends and the staff isn't very friendly. It's pretty much standing room only and you have to fight your way to the bar to order drinks. They have good music and a "dance floor" area if you can get to it!! Stop in, have a drink, then go to the next bar.
Great little bar in Nashville! Listened to WCB- Wes Cook Band and drinks were reasonable! ($5.00 beers) They serve food but we didn't order any this time. Would come back!

When the food finally came out it was pretty good! Our bartender upstairs was awesome! She dealt with like 3 large parties with no help! The place actually ran out of wings during the national championship game.....guessing the manager dropped the ball on a lot of things last night!

This was wonderful!  I was walking through downtown Nashville and heard a fiddle playing (fiddles/violins are my favorite music).  I ordered a sandwich (I don't drink alcoholic drinks or carbonated drinks, so it is difficult to order in bars!)  

The waitress was really nice and even offered me some caramel popcorn for dessert!

The music (I believe Katie and Mark) was wonderful, I sat and listened for an hour and would have stayed longer, but I couldn't.

A great evening!  Really as good as it gets!  They even played my favorite fiddle song "Orange Blossom Special" for me.  I was in seventh heaven!

Food was excellent, no coffee.
We had some of the BEST service ever from Heather! She was always always checking on us! She was so sweet and kind! The music was amazing! We enjoyed our afternoon so much! Can't wait to come back!

A group of coworkers and I stopped in for lunch on a Tuesday.  We arrived after 12:30 and the place was empty.  Not the best sign.  It was so empty that it was "seat yourself" on the first floor.  

Orders around the table varied -- some hot chicken salads, a burger, the hot chicken ramen, chicken salad plate, some appetizers.  Our food came out relatively quickly, although the restaurant was empty, so I would have been mad if we had waited a long time. 

I had the hot chicken salad at a "hot" spiciness level.  First few bites--not hot.  Then out of nowhere the heat kicked in.  Not so hot that you could not eat the food but definitely hot.  The chicken on the salad is chicken tenders.  I must have touched one with my finger and then touched my face because the skin on my face started to burn.  Won't do that again.

Feedback from others at the table--the hot chicken ramen was more like a bowl of noodles.  Not much broth.  The coworker who had the burger said it was "disgusting" and did not finish her food.  The side of macaroni and cheese was "really good" I am told.  The sides are really small I will note.  The person who ordered the boiled peanuts said the peanuts were cold.  That's just gross.  

My salad was fine.  It was a salad.  I thought the chicken was good.  I would order it again--just maybe the medium heat level.  The service was fine.  All-in-all, a solid three-star Yelp experience.

*This review pertains to their lunch only!

My search for good gumbo in Nashville surprisingly led me here. I work downtown so I wanted something quick and easy, but inexpensive as well. I entered around 1:45pm and sat at the bar, unaware that their lunch ended at 2pm. I was happy to know that I just made the cut! I was greeted quickly by the bartender, who suggested some of her favorite items. I knew I wanted gumbo, but she gave me a sample size of the chicken and dumplings soup. It was sooo good, the best I've had only second to my mother's. The gumbo was delicious but a little heavy with okra. The entire menu is $10 & under, there is plenty of parking, and you have the option to call in your order ahead of time. 3rd & Lindsley will become my go-to this winter for hot food during lunch hours.

The service was absolutely incredible! Our appetizers were all amazing! We got fried green tomatoes, calamari, chicken tenders, and the roasted Brussel sprouts and honey and all of them were delicious! Our entrees were fantastic, everyone was passing around their plates making sure to get a taste of it all because we couldn't get enough. The steak salad was phenomenal, the hot chicken was perfectly juicy and crispy, the pulled pork sandwich was great and the ribs were falling off the bone amazing. We walked in hoping to go to the roof top, but grabbed a bite downstairs first, and we couldn't have been more pleased. Excellent!! Our waitress Alison was a sweetheart and the live musician was incredibly talented!
You can't beat this place for BBQ when you are near Pilsen, or even when you're not. Fun, festive atmosphere, and delicious food.

What a great afternoon we had at 3rd and Lindsley!  We attended the Singer/Songwriter show they had last week. The 2 Grammy winning songwriters told stories of how the songs came to be and drew in the audience when the beautiful songs were performed. The up and coming singers were as engaging and entertaining. 
The food was subpar. I ordered chicken and sausage gumbo. There was no chicken to be found. I question the server about the whereabouts of the chicken and she said it was sausage only. I showed her the menu, where it clearly stated chicken and sausage. She replied with, "oh...". I only ate about 1/3 of it, as the flavors just weren't there. My fiancé had chili and said it was just okay. I'd recommend eating before attending a show here. Definitely look into seeing a Singer/Songwriter event. This beats hanging out on Broadway any day.   Thanks for a lovely afternoon!
Had really good food.  We got the poutine and fried chicken and it was really good!  The live music always killer and the bar had some good local drafts
Hole in the wall on Broadway with- hands down- the BEST bands on entire strip. You could go there when they open and never leave until they close and not be disappointed!

Gahhhh I felt like we hit the jackpot that Vince Gill was there with the Time Jumpers tonight! My sweet step mom cried tears of joy when she saw he was there and tears of joy during each song he sang and then tears of sadness that he wasn't able to take a pic or sign her new Time Jumpers cd - She was just 3 people left waiting as he loaded out the last piece of gear. She grew up listening to him and Amy and through the tears she said, "That's okay it was a fantastic night, I had a good time"... and it was on her bucket list so glad we were able to get tickets and get a good seat. Our waitress was o! The music is like none other. The drinks were meh (wine, seemed watered down), the food was decent. The sampler platter tasted like it was just warmed up (whereas in the past it's always been really good!), however the turkey swiss croissant was really good and so were the fries! It seems like it's always hit or miss. I'd say don't choose a seat that is in the far back bc you'll be forgotten in the mass of people when it comes to refills and bringing food out timely.

We almost didn't make it to the Station Inn but I'm so glad we did because it turned out to be the highlight of our trip. If you've had your fill of 'Nash Vegas' and want to experience amazing talent in a low key setting, this place is for you. We visited on a Monday and got to see Val Storey, Carl Jackson and Larry Cordle do their regular gospel/bluegrass show. The welcome was warm, the beer was cold, everyone on the stage was a professional and Val has the voice of an angel. We arrived at about 10, right at the end of the first set and got in with no problem. What an amazing night!

Small place with friendly staff. More of a local hangout then commercial bar. Had a couple of acoustic singers that were very good. Typical bar food that was all very good. Buffalo chicken wrap
Quesadilla both excellent.

I was determined to go to a honky-tonk bar while in Nashville.
I had a list of places to do Saturday night with my friend but my foot had other plans...  decided to step in a hole, sprain itself and have me unable to walk for the rest of the trip.
Thankfully the hotel I was staying at let me borrow a wheelchair so, Sunday, after brunch, I was able to go to Honky Tonk.

Right on Broadway, which is the main tourist street filled with bars, restaurants and lots to see and do, we went in.
People immediately made way for us and my wheelchair, made space for us at the bar, and were so nice.  The place is super casual, almost dive bar like.  Bartenders are flirty with the patrons, doing shots with them, making conversation, and singing on stage with the band.
Drinks are cheap, strong, and served fast.

Live music was great, even for a non-country fan.  I was dancing on my chair, enjoying the crowd dancing and singing, and having a great time.
The people visiting the bar are there to have fun. They make conversation with everyone at the bar, which gave us the opportunity to meet another guy visiting from Florida, and talk to locals that were just there to hang out and even invited us to some beers while we listened to the band.

This is exactly the type of bar I wanted to experience before leaving Nashville and so happy I was able to.  Even more appreciative that they accommodate me, and made me forget about the pain on my foot and wheelchair while I was there.  

Real fun place to go and chill with friends, people watch, and enjoy some live music.

My husband and I decided to go here for a few drinks and some music. The bar only serves beer, but they have a decent selection for being such a small place (4*)The woman working was really rude(1*), but the man was really nice(5*). We were talking to one of the guys in the band before he started and we got shushed by the sound guy(1*). We weren't even talking loud or being crazy! Later on in the night the woman sitting next to us was telling us something and a random woman walking by shushed her. I think she worked there because I saw her yelling at someone else earlier(1*)! I've never been to a bar where they expect you to be completely quiet. It was actually really annoying. We were sitting having a conversation. Not screaming, jumping, or being obnoxious. I'm 35. The woman talking to me was probably mid50s. We aren't children in a library, we are adults at a bar. We are having drinks and listening to music, we aren't in church or school. We did have pizza, which was good,  but the crust seemed like it could have used a little more time in the oven(3*).  When i went to pay our tab we had been charged for an extra beer but it's so loud in there I didn't even feel like trying to argue about it.(1*) So after a $15/person cover, $50 tab for a small pizza and a few beers, plus tip we spent almost  $100. It's not somewhere I'd choose to go again.  We could have gone somewhere more fun, with better drinks and not been treated like children for the same amount of money or less.

I wish I could give 0 stars! This place should be ashamed of the two bartenders they had working the first level bar (to the right when you walk in) on Saturday, Sept 29th. The place was not busy at all. My group of 4 walked in looking for a game to watch, stopped at the service station (there were no servers waiting for drinks) to ask if it was possible to request a game on one of the tvs. The male bartender responds rudely with "you need to get out of here you can't order a drink here". Finally asked the female server the same question on the patron side of the bar who then responded rudely with "excuse me? We don't control the TVs". Even if the bar was busy, that is no way to respond to a simple inquiry about a game on tv in a sport bar. 

If these two were that overwhelmed that one question was too much for them, it sounds to me like Nashville Underground should look to hire waitstaff who can handle more than 10 people at a bar! For Christ sake you work in a Nashville bar on Broadway on college game day. And this place is supposedly popular for college football viewing! HA what a joke. 

We will never return to this place again and will continue to warn everyone we know. Every other bar/restaurant had the friendliest staff who truly made us feel welcome and we will be sure to rave about every other bar we visited. Nashville Underground is a disgrace!
Great bands and fun atmosphere. Three levels of entertainment and plenty of room at the bars.

People think I'm white (not completely true) and I wear a lot of muscle tank tops, so that's how I ended up with the nickname "Honky Tank Central."

I think it's a bit offensive, whereas I am a lot offensive, so it doesn't fit.

But you know what does fit? Oh wait I can't link to my X-Rated films with Barbie on here.

This is my favourite place on Broadway because all of the spectacular goddesses seem to be going in here with their short stocky cowboy-hat Rich boyfriends.

There's often a line outside to get in which is not the case for most of the places along Broadway, and I saw some of the most stunning women coming in here on the night of the Bruno Mars concert.

Honestly I'd probably rather have been in here than watching Bruno Mars, just based on the girls that were coming in here.
Worst service ever. They treat everyone like tourists ... as if they won't ever see them again. It's embarrassing to be a Nashville resident with people like this.

Food would only be good if you were drunk. To call it mediocre would be generous. Got the lemon pepper wings... bad. Chicken tenders not very good either. Only good thing was fries, but it's pretty hard to screw those up... although I thought the same thing about chicken tenders, but I was wrong.

May want to check your Saturday night bouncer who thinks it's acceptable to grab women by the wrist to stop them and then get upset when women call him out for it. He also asked my friend "to do a cart wheel" in order
To get in. Completely unacceptable.

It was ok. From a first time Nashville visitor, I didn't like the atmosphere on saturday night compared to other places.  During the day it was better, got some appetizers(It was decent).  My wife really enjoyed the mixed drinks they specialized in.

Ok, famous hot chicken, local brews served below freezing? (Not sure about the science on that one, but it's really cold!) here's the kicker: acoustic guitarist in the middle of the afternoon playing whatever classic rock and folk music I request. Oh yeah, and they have adequate screens showing hockey and baseball. It's like they knew i was coming. Not too shabby!

Our friend lived in Nashville and suggested The Station Inn to see some great local bluegrass. We stopped in on a Wednesday night and had an amazing time. The staff was great, the doorman and the bartender were both very friendly. 

The place is huge, so if you get there early, you can get a great spot up front or be seated with a large group of friends. It is nothing fancy, a bit of a dive bar, but that is definitely more of our scene than some of the other clubs we passed. The walls are covered with posters from years of great up-and-coming acts and I'm sure any act that plays there will be impressive and entertaining. The particular show that we saw was Mike Bub and Friends, a mishmash group of musicians who played wonderfully off of each other and put on a great show. One of the musicians invited to play with Mike that night was Scott Vestal, an amazing banjo player who we had seen years before with the Sam Bush Band. This place gives off the vibe that you never know who might show up to play here!

My only complaint is their very small beer selection. They had only a few beers on draft and mostly cheap domestics. They had $15 pitchers of a local brew which was pretty good and that's what we drank most of the night. 

If you like bluegrass and you're in Nashville, The Station Inn is definitely worth checking out!

This three story monstrosity sits on the corner of Broadway giving patrons a view into the looking glass of tourist town. A couple buddies and I showed up here after lunch and went straight to the top. It seemed to be the least busy as people weren't willing to walk up any further. We hung at the bar waiting for the rest of our group and watched the Masters. I'm not really a golf fan so I was a little bored but as time went on the bar got more lively. Bachelorette after bachelorette showed up with their woo-crew with one goal in mind... get turnt. As annoying as they can be, the bachelorettes got the place once after the band started and the woo-ing was held to a minimum being that it was still only 3pm. Even better than the show inside was the people watching outside. The balcony allows you to look down on a sea of party busses and whatever else rolls down the road. I saw musical acts, tractors pulling wagons of drunkards, and pedal bars regretting not being pulled around by a wagon or monster truck. We had to head out for an early dinner but I can only imagine what this place looked like only a few hours later.

Terrible music. Really wanted to like the place and music but both bands were so out of tune it was painful. The singer on the 1st floor even had to use her phone for the song lyrics. Definitely ruined the performance  esp. since it was a classic Aerosmith song. 

Smoke free on the 1st floor but smoking allowed on the 3rd floor. Bartenders were swamped so be patient, they're just trying to stay afloat.

Terrible service and cold food. When we arrived the second floor wasn't very crowded at all, yet the service was still horrible. Seemed very understaffed. Waited 45 minutes for the food and it was cold. Took 30 minutes to tab out. Avoid at all costs!!

The rooftop bar was cool. 

We had drinks and nachos. Never in my life have I had nachos with no flavor. Between the cheese, beans, corn, tomatoes, etc...none of it had any flavor. It was the strangest thing. Neither of us could really taste anything. Worst $16 of nachos and that's saying a lot as I'm a frequent nacho order-er at football games.

Stick to the drinks.

Food menu is not very big. Dry wings were good and so was Nashville chicken sandwich! Yummy! Roof top is nice with view of river. Second floor was a nice place to get away from crowds when it's open to the public! Clean bathrooms!

We're talking about a legit old school bluegrass jam here. Sunday nights. It's free admission and it's so worth getting downtown for.

Every Sunday night his place turns into a dream, with amazing bluegrass artists all coming together. It's pretty magical to watch. It does get rather packed so be sure to get there earlyish. Cheap beer. 

The vibe isn't anything fancy, not that you'd expect that walking in. The Station Inn is everything it's meant to be. True. Real people. Great music. Rustic.  If you're a person who enjoys live music, this is something you need to do at least once in Nashville.

Also... Emmy Squared next door makes a mean pizza for before the show. See you there.

Great bar service, even when packed.  They always seem to have a great band or singer playing as well.   Have only tried a limited amount of food but it was good each time.    This is a one of the places I look forward to when I visit Nashville.    My only advice to the management is to try and keep the bathrooms cleaner.

Today we had this AMAZING waiter Kirk! This guy had so much pep in his step, managed the entire floor efficiently and was a TON of fun! He literally made everyone feel special and made the atmosphere so much fun on this Saturday afternoon.  Thanks so much for making our day such a great time. We had no intentions of staying this long, but he made it worth it! Rock that bandana! You made our time there one of our most awesome memories of the trip!

I was really looking forward to going to this bar as it has a cool location and layout. My boyfriend and I were visiting from Wisconsin for our spring break. We arrived at the bar and sat down and the bartender asked us what we would like. She then asked for our ID's and after looking at them for about 5 minutes she very condescendingly told us that she wouldn't serve us and gave us our drivers licenses back. We were very confused because we are 23 and 22 and we asked why she wouldn't serve us and she said that the ID's were "opposite". We asked to speak to a manager and she replied that she was the manager and asked if we'd like to speak to the owner and we said yes. She then had a police officer come over (most likely to kick us out) and he looked at our IDs and said that they were legitimate and told her this as well. She continued to be rude but asked what we would like after making a scene and embarrassing us in front of everyone sitting around us at the bar. We left and will not be going back. Very disappointing and horrible service.
This is a lifetime memory of great music. The Time Jumpers are so amazing I'll never forget them.

Johnny T. got it right. What could potentially be wrong with Broadway can be found at this place. 

I was bored out of my mind. The music on a three levels was uninspired. I had it in my mind that I wanted to leave right when I entered and I should have followed my instinct. 

Instead, we stayed for about an hour. Paid $13 for two beers ... Twice over. The music was not up to the standard of other places on the strip. I'm sure I'll be back, but it's because of the location.

Went there with a business group. We had reservations and were promptly seated, with great seats next to the stage. We got lucky and visited this establishment on a night they hosted a live production of Nashville Rising Song. We heard some really great music. The service however was not real impressive. The waitress, although pleasant, wasn't overly attentive. Two of us got our food first, the other 8 people didn't get theirs until about 10 minutes later. Being polite, we waited to eat until everyone at our table had their food. By the time everyone had their food, ours was cold. The food itself was pretty good. I'm willing to try this place one more time to see if the service could be improved, but they'll only get one more chance to get it right for me.

This place is great and has multiple levels and all different kinds of music. We spent the majority of our night here and had a lot of fun. People from all ages were here and drinks were reasonably priced.

Love this place!! We sat on the upper level for a show on Sunday and even with a packed house our server Brittney did an amazing job keeping our drinks coming and checking on us to see if we needed anything. The view of the stage was perfect and the music sounded great! We ordered a sampler platter of appetizers as well and they were all delicious. I highly recommend the fried pickles and chicken tenders! TIP: Get there early to get in line before the doors open to get a good seat and get a Lyft or Uber to avoid the parking headache.

This has always been one of my favorite venues on Broadway to see a few local Nashville bands. Probably a little pricey, but it is on Broadway, so that's to be expected.
Mostly good bands playing all day, and the sound guys do a decent job on the mix.
Another good stop on a Nashville trip down Broadway.

Great place if you want to be completely ignored by the bartender in a nearly empty restaurant. Walked out with my time wasted and not so much as an acknowledgement of my existence by the staff. Pathetic.

Sooo I've had the most wonderful experience at Nashville underground! The service from Courtney and Daniella was so friendly and personable! 
These two really made my friend and I who are locals have such a fun day!!! 
They are great and I recommend you all come to see them!!!

A hidden gem in the heart of downtown Nashville's historic Printers Alley. They have Guinness on tap and it's a Steelers bar!! (Original owner is from Pittsburgh)
The wings are mouth watering and the hot dog on toasted Hawaiian bread will knock your socks off.
Great ambiance, friendly bartenders and dozens of craft beers.

Great environment with three levels of seating open doors to the outside with smoking on the overhang balconies looking into the street--lots to  drink selections and a great appetizer platter!  Friendly waitresses and others not assigned to us came several times to check in.

Very cool nostalgic venue, But felt so sorry for the servers.  When you let everyone in venue at one time, they just cannot keep up.  She worked so hard to keep us happy!  Thinking maybe more staff would be helpful.
I didn't eat, Because I felt like reviews on the food served were not good.  My husband had a burger, He said it was ok.  He has had much better, Just using good locally sourced meat can make a world of difference.

I LOVED the atmosphere here! The have love music on all 3 floors and when u enter u can just go to whichever floor u want. We went to the 3rd floor to get the best views of Nashville from their balcony. I also love that they have a kids menu and that my kids were welcome there. Their food was amazing! Their fries are especially awesome! Definitely would go back again!

If you love bluegrass, this is the place to go!  We've been here twice & both times the music was unbelievable.  You have to like being in close quarters with other people to enjoy this place.  It is usually packed!
Don't miss it!

You MUST go here. I strongly suggest you look at their website in advance so you don't end up catching the last five minutes of what seemed to be an incredible acoustic/folk show like we did. It's only beer & wine and seating consists of standard chairs or some old bus seats against the wall!

This is a reality check for ALL of downtown Nashville. I get it. It's hip and cool to be down here. But magic has not found its way into your well spirits. $10 for a well and diet...... shut up. 

That's crap. It's extortion and anyone trying to claim otherwise is on the take or wasted. Great bar. Great music. But your prices are way off.
Very poor service. Waited 30 minutes for a server after being seated. Two waitresses continually walked past us and just ignored us.

This is a great fun place to take your friends and family if you want to have a chill night but also have great drinks and great entertainment. Best chicken tenders ever!! The waitress, Brigham, gave great recommendations and was so attentive even on a busy night.
Pulled pork sandwich was good. Bloody Mary was under dressed, and without a chaser. Live music and quaint setting to listen to the performing artist. Kaley Hill was awesome.

Ascend is a great amphitheater I always have a good time here. My son got me a box seats for my birthday and I was super excited because normally I would be on the lawn which is not bad either. When you have box seats you have a table of four and you actually have service, unfortunately there was only one waitress because they were short staffed so we ended up having to go get our own drinks and food I would just say for the premium seats it's not acceptable to be understaffed at the price you pay for those seats.  Hence the four stars.

This is exactly the place you want to be if you are looking for a standard, "honky tonk highway" experience in Nashville. The band on the first floor is jamming out every night. It's gonna be the same set of like 10 songs that everyone wants to hear and requests. One of the nights we tried to get them to sing Taylor swift and it took multiple Venmo attempts to get it done. And I spent every day of the weekend in Nash ending up here. 

The bad. They card every single person that walks through this door even if you look like someone's grandpa. The alcohol selection may not be refined enough for the classier person. There are a LOT of bachelorettes.

The pro. There are a lot of bachelorettes? Depends on your opinion of them. It definitely gets a little rowdy here (first floor comments only) but not in an out of control way as far as I can tell. I didn't stay out late any of the nights I was here so the before midnight crowd is respectable but I can't say anything about the after midnight crowd.
