Stopped in with what felt like the whole city of Lexington, KY to watch the SEC semifinals. Wildcat blue as far as the eye could see:) 3 levels of standing room only (if you consider sardines in a can "standing room") Anyway, buckets of domestic light beer were going for $30 which I guess is part tourist attraction and part supply and demand. I think on a less busy day it would be a great place to get gouged for beer and watch a game or see a band on the first level. It was just a little too much so we only stayed for about half the game before we bailed for a less busy spot. But the energy was great and it was def Wildcat friendly:) I would go again. Like I said, it was a little overwhelming but that was just because of the SEC Tourney... I think.

Showed up at 5pm during the week. Completely dead, which is fine... supposedly happy hours. Ordered a drink and after it was made the bartender informs me it's $10 minimum for credit cards...."but it's 2 for 10$$ so you have another one coming...". Gee.. thanks. No band. Happy hour. Yet a two drink minimum. Awesome, not

Actually had a nice time at Honky Tonk Central on Thursday night, August 9th, with one major exception. I ordered a beer and a cocktail from the bartender, I paid with a one hundred dollar bill and she gave me a twenty dollar bill as my change. When I tried to tell her she was wrong, and after entirely too long of trying to convince her of her mistake, which included me asking for a manager or supervisor and her saying that there was not one,  her only excuse was, "oh, you're from California, you should be use to being overcharged." Being an industry professional, I know that bartenders should never try to grossly overcharge a costumer. This alone really hurt my Honky Tonk Experience.

Here in Nashville on vacation, and I had seen good reviews for another restaurant next door. We accidentally wandered into this one thinking it was the one I'd read about but THANK GOD FOR THAT! It was amazing. My husband had the hot chicken salad. And I ordered the Ramen.... Holy hell it was soooooo good. You also get to pick your level of spice for everything. We went with hot because we are lovers of all things spicy. The server said that it runs hot but we went ahead with it. THE HOT IS HOT PEOPLE! I can handle high heat but damn. Still worth it, you could still taste the amazing broth and the noodles were perfectly cooked. One of the best meals we have had here in Nashville.

What a great stop! So many options but this one was a great pick. I was traveling on business so I was by myself and found a seat at a table that was large. It was crowded and it was the only one could find. There was a band playing and they were great. I loved that the music was loud but it was easy to talk to people. The waitress showed up quickly and I ordered a chicken salad with ranch. It was delicious. My only complaint is they put a paper down before your food on the plate and that got soaked by the dressing which made it hard to tell if I was eating some of it!

Since I had a big table, a nice couple asked if they could join, I liked the friendly atmosphere. 

The waitress checked on me and got my check quickly and I got out for $13!! Granted I didn't get a drink (driving) so it's a great value.

The only area that was "busy" was upstairs, and they had one bartender running bar and floor and it took 15min to get my tea because she had to run downstairs to get it, by time we got our appetizer, we got our food also  and it was ALL wrong and the food was so cold, the fried green tomatoes were soggy, they ignored all our bruger requests. Very disappointed! First time In Nashville and we picked this place to eat! Next time I'll be looking at reviews! Would have done 1 star but the bartender was sweet!

The drink price reflects the location and the name. $9 for a small vodka cranberry is steep BUT the entertainment and overall vibe here is worth it. There were some really great performers on stage here and even though we went on a Sunday night, the whole place was still lit. This is a classic Broadway experience and I would definitely recommend making a stop here while visiting.
Avoid! Blatantly rude, unfriendly staff. Too many other bars and live music options in Nashville to waste your time and money here.
If you were drawn here by the mouthwatering picture of poutine, don't. The drinks were fine and the food okay, but it's just not the foodie place some makes it out to be.

This was probably my favorite music of all the places we went to in Nashville. It has an unassuming back alley entrance, and it's located in the basement, so small cozy venue. We wandered in randomly on a Thursday night just in time for a singer/song-writer fest and were blown away by the talent of the performers!

However, as far as I know the musicians performing are not affiliated at all with the venue, and my review has to be for the venue. The bartender here was extremely rude to my friend and I. When my friend ordered a gin a tonic she refused to tell us what kinds of gin they had and just repeatedly shook her head when my friend named 3-4 gins, until my friend finally just ordered a drink she didn't want. When we asked for water, the bartender told us to serve ourselves with plastic cups in the back, even as we watched her serve water glasses to other customers who asked. With plenty of other venues in the area, I'll choose a place with better service. Everywhere we went in Nashville people were friendly, welcoming, and helpful, except here.
They were out of vodka, all they had left was their well spirit. I understand they had a busy weekend, but Monday night guests shouldn't suffer for this. Our bartender was "embarrassed".
Beautiful venue with a view of downtown Nashville and the river and bridge. The general seating in the grassy area was perfect for dancing and enjoying the night.

We stopped by on a Sunday night to see the open bluegrass jam. There were so many talented musicians playing together. It was packed but people came and left regularly so we didn't have to wait long to get a seat.

One of my favorite venues I've ever been to in TN.  It's an outdoor venue so it went perfect with the concert that I went to.  The views of downtown were beautiful from this venue.  The front area close to the stage is called the Pit... from what I saw, there weren't any seats there.  Everyone there was standing, but not like it really mattered if there were seats anyway.  Everyone, everywhere was standing and dancing cause it was such an awesome concert.  We got our tickets in section 103 row S.  It wasn't far at all from the stage.  Got a great view of her, and they also had big screens on each side of the stage for you to be able to see her.  Our section had seats to sit down in if you'd like.  The lawn area also didn't seem bad at all.  It's in the very back and you have an option to bring a lawn chair or towel to sit on.

Loved this bar before today... had a disrespectful bartender that said we were in high school. If we're in high school why are you letting us sit at your bar? Just rude and didn't pay any attention to us. The guy before her was amazing though so props to him. P.s NOT IN HIGHSCHOOL just on vacation let us live our lives

The food wasn`t very good, too crowded and people started to get drunk & stupid early. We were there when the doors opened @ 6pm for a concert at 8 @ TBshakedown and by 6:30 the stupid started. Strong smell of smoke that was not cigarettes. It reads that 3rd and Lindsley is for all ages, I don`t agree with that at all. I guess if you buy tickets to go there, get drunk and act stupid then this is the place for you. Don`t get me wrong, we like to have a drink or two & have fun, this wasn`t that kind of venue. We want be back.

This was our favorite spot in Nashville. The staff was wonderful. Manager Teddy is just a great guy who went above and beyond to make sure we had a great time. The waitresses were all wonderful. The chicken wings were by far the best chicken wings I have ever had! Amazing. The fries also amazing! The highlight was the performer. Rexton and Chad were absolutely phenomenal. How does this kid not have an album out? They were super nice guys as well and made our trip memorable by playing our wedding song as we were celebrating our 18th wedding anniversary! We were here 2 nights in a row after realizing we couldn't find a better voice in all the bars we went to while we were there! Keep up the good work. Can't wait to come back next year and see the changes coming to the Nashville Underground!!!

I was there with some friends last night and we were intimidated by the bouncers to leave, without any cause. There was a woman manager that was responsible for making us go, and when I asked for her name the bouncer would not provide me with her name and just kept repeating "you need to go". I felt highly disrespected and it was completely unprofessional. There are plenty of bars on broadway to have a good time, so don't go here if you want to feel at all respected.

Great place to kick back! I caught the Bad Movie Night event. Cocktails were delicious and the small bites selection was amazing! Get The duck wings. The fellas at the bar and setting up the movie were so welcoming and great to have around. I'm from Chicago but I WILL be back!

The food was great but our service was terrible. Our server wasn't aware of the drink specials so my friend who got hot chicken was suppose to get free beer but wasn't aware and also was charged more for her drink when she asked the server prior to ordering it. I ordered a pulled pork sandwich but needed a plate since it was served in a basket so I had to wait 15 minutes for a server to come and then I finally asked another sever who brought me one 10 minutes. My food got cold but I was so hungry, I just had to eat it. The band that was playing was amazing and overall a decent experience my best suggestion is to have more than 3 servers on the floor on a Saturday night. Pictures are our tenders with Mac and cheese, hot chicken and a pulled pork sandwich. I would say 3.5 stars but the food was really good.

Stopped here for dinner one evening. My fiancé has been here before with a large group, and recalled it being quick service without a huge crowd. When we arrived, there was a bit of a wait, but maybe 10-15 minutes. Once seated it took maybe another 10-15 for anyone to come over and acknowledge us. We both ordered different beers, and again, another 15+ until Jeff recurved his beer. The one I ordered was out. Our food came out at a decent time, I ordered the hot chicken Mac and cheese, which was actually really good, although on the cold side. There was a band playing, but I wasn't impressed. It was an okay experience. I likely won't be headed back, but I can see the benefit if you're with a large group as it very much accommodates that.

Some of the best music you'll hear in Nashville!  Small, old place with simple tables and reasonably priced drinks ... and a fantastic studio quality sound system.  This will be a must see on every future trip.

The Station Inn is a classic, hole-in-the-wall venue featuring top-notch live bluegrass. It sits on the edge of downtown Nashville in a neighborhood known as the Gulch. The Ridgetop Ramblers were playing on the night we visited and the five members are all excellent singers and musicians. Fully enjoyed their set. We arrived about an hour before the music was set to start and the place was already very nearly packed. They serve beer only, no wine or cocktails. You can get a little thingie of popcorn for $2, though. By the time we left (around 10pm) there was a solid line of people out of the door hoping to enter the sold out venue.

Really disgusted by this bar.
They tolerate gross drunk men practically molesting the young bachelorette parties and the place is sticky and dirty. One of the least decent bars I visited.

Don't get me wrong: Honky Tonk Central has a great location, a great balcony to people watch, and great artists singing at every level. It's just the rest of it was a drunk, sticky, smoky, disgusting mess the night my friends and I came. I was not impressed.

This places service is horrible!   I asked for more gingerale after my friends drink almost made me vomit!  Bartender then made a double Jamison and ginger and told me it would be horrible.   That wasn't what I asked for at all so I just left it.  On the way back to my group security told me I had to leave.  So basically the bartender had me kicked out for complaining about her horrible drink.  What a joke,  do yourselves a favor and go somewhere else!

Stopped here with my wife on 10/07/17 earlier on that Saturday evening and visited each floor, band and bar.  I found the bar staff to be very inattentive and was shocked at how dirty the third floor bar was.  At the time we were there it wasn't crowded and there were several staff members standing around.  The floor was disgusting behind the bar, covered in debris and the bar top was sticky.  No one was taking time to clean and we watched several customers get frustrated with how long it took to get a drink.  The band on that floor spent an exorbitant amount of time explaining how tips for the band were necessary and how long they had played with the owner of the bar.  If only they knew that more people tip when they hear music, not during long dissertations.  Play music, drink beer, have fun!  This will not be on my list of Honky Tonks to visit on my next trip.

We had 1 free night during our conference, and wanted to go somewhere casual downtown with good food & live music, that wouldn't break the bank. These guys delivered! It was a Tuesday, so not at all crowded. The music was great, & not so loud you couldn't carry on a conversation. We tried several different things on the menu, but we all tried the hot chicken, & it was amazing! We went for hot (there was 1 level higher, & we didn't go there), which I found to be hot but not painful (varying opinions on that in our group), & not so hot it masked the delicious flavor. I rarely order fried chicken in a restaurant, because I'm worried it will be too floury, too greasy, or bland. This was perfectly crispy, not greasy, & certainly not bland - wowza! Fried green tomatoes were also perfect - thick slices of heirloom tomatoes, light breaded & perfectly friend, with a tasty sauce lightly applied. They had a good selection of draft beers, including some local favorites. Our server, Ben, was delightful. Super helpful without being pushy or intrusive, made great recommendations. I'd definitely return next time I'm in Nashville! Compared to the other places we stopped in on Broadway, it felt more personal, less "commercial country."
The most authentic country music listening experience in Nashville. Such an amazing crowd...felt like home.

The Good: Went here before the Titans game and it was a great choice. They have several floors with lots of TVs playing all the Sunday NFL games. Good selection of bar food and adult beverages. Short walk to Nissan Stadium Bridgestone Arena.

The Bad: Restroom attendants. I don't need someone hanging out in a red try handing me a towel for a dollar, why do they do this?

Party of 25 girls here for a bachelorette party. Came in for the bull riding attraction at 4:30 pm on a Saturday. Nearly 100 degrees outside, so we really needed some water first in order to begin to enjoy ourselves. 40 minutes at the second floor bar and still couldn't get anyone's attention. 2 bartenders staffed at a bar this size on a Saturday night...not their fault, but certainly management's. Went downstairs to a bar equally understaffed. Found a waitress and asked for a manager, who said she couldn't find them. Very subpar service and a disappointing experience. With 50 bars on Broadway, I would choose another.

The dreaded task of bringing out of town visitors to Broadway was upon us. A Saturday evening stroll down the main strip was luckily enough for our group and we managed to escape fairly quickly. After that experience, we were in need of some refreshments. While I must admit that Broadway is not my favorite, I do enjoy a visit to Printer's Alley. We popped into the first place we saw, Alley Taps. It doesn't look like anything special from the outside so I was a little hesitant. But wow! Once we got inside it was pretty awesome. Plenty of space and seating, nice decor, friendly staff. We chose to sit at the bar but the other room had huge leather couches that were awfully tempting. They have a nice beer menu and prices are normal for craft beer. We were too early for the live music, but they have a small stage with bands performing. 

My advice: step away from the honky-tonks, stroll (or stumble) up to Printer's Alley, and stop into Alley Taps. It's a more laid-back atmosphere which one can really appreciate in all of the chaos.
Rude is the word of the day. Don't mid it being busy but the bar tender could have been ten times nicer!!!!
Loved the Sunday bluegrass jam. Nashville institution!

Came here on a Sunday night and loved the vibe and the music.

@Merlin C, I think the elite status got to your head. It's asinine to "round down" the  rating because of the pizza. The place dubs itself as a music venue (as it should based on the amazing music) and clearly offers the pizza as a snack to the beer and music. It's like rating the Metropolitan Museum of Art in NYC 3 stars because their cappuccino at their cafe came out a little too frothy.

Why haven't I left a review for this place. I've been a handful of times. Face palm. 

Great outdoor venue. Cheaper than most and just as comfortable. Maybe minus the scorching heat at times.  Same decent food and drinks as all the other venues. 

I haven't paid for seats yet. I've always sat in the lawn and brought blankets to sit on. It's worked just fine and you get to enjoy the music and your company

Super packed tourist destination
Atmosphere / decor - 3
Service - 3
Food - NA
Location - 4
Value - 3

Overall 3

This place was packed every time we drove past it so we decided to check it out. This is very clearly a tourist destination so if that's what you're looking for this is a great place to go. The drinks are really expensive ($9 for a well tequila shot). There was some live music and a few floors which is cool. If you can snag a seat by one of the windows you get a nice view of the strip.

This venue was great!  Small enough to feel close, seating for almost all.  Fantastic bands like the time jumpers(which Vince gill is a part of!). Little did we know the counting crows would be there watching and two girls from the voice would be there and would sing too!

Food a mediocre but who goes there for the food?  

Get there 2 hrs early for time jumpers.... Place fills up!

With 3 levels of live musicians, rotating throughout the day, you can pick your music mood as you go. The atmosphere changes with the bands. Mixed drinks had good reviews from our group, like the "Graham Cracker" rumchata drink. Drinks were about $10 each. We stopped by for the music midday on a Friday and the bands were all great. Old country favorites, a few new popular sonhs, and some classic rock - we sang along in our seats. Food smelled great but we didn't eat here.

A few bachelorette parties came through and danced. The space is large enough that you could sit to enjoy the music and eat with your family, or gather around the band and dance like wild, without bothering each other.

Musicians here, and in many other local places, will play to the crowd. A $20 tip gets any song you like.

ATMs on every floor. Easily-accesible sibgle stall bathrooms on each floor. Balconies to view Broadway. Stores to buy cowboy boots, souvenirs, etc. right across the street.
First time in Nashville...great little bar off of Broadway....artists playing original songs. Refreshing from the loud bars on Broadway playing covers. Laurie was a great single handed bartender!

Stopped in with the intention of having just a beer or two. Went to the roof top level and met Bobby Two Times the bartender and ended up staying for several beers while the wife had a few tequila drinks. He was one of the best bartenders I've met in quite some time. I'm a native of middle Tn and have seen Nashville change dramatically over the past decade. It was refreshing to meet a bartender who could still carry a conversation, mix great cocktails, and even give pointers on where to find some great international food selections. Most want to just take your drink order and move on to the next customer. He was able to do that but also continue the conversation with myself as well as other patrons. I will definitely be returning!!

I love this bar to the moon and back! It's my favorite place in Nashville. The music is amazing and the bar staff is phenomenal. If Jen and amber aren't there I tend to just go home and then come back on another day when they are there.
This is a really cool venue. They bring in such talented musicians. Definitely check it out.

Walking down Broadway at night, I saw lots of live bands and bunches of girls having their bachelorette parties in the various bars and establishments in this area.  It was interesting to watch for a bit, but not the vibe my bf and I wanted as the last stop of our road trip over Memorial Day week.  

As we reached the end of the street, I decided to pop in here because I thought it was Acme Feed, and I had read online that it's a really good place.  Didn't realize until after we walked out that it was actually Nashville Underground, oops.  But I'm glad that we came in by accident.

Multiple floors, each with a slightly different vibe.  Ground level was a country band that was pretty good.  The second floor was closed for a private event.  We went up to the rooftop bar and saw a cool dance floor with a DJ who spun nice tunes, although it was kind of empty.  

Lots of different kinds of beer on tap, and I was happy to finally try some local Yazoo Gershwin beer at the rooftop bar.  It was so refreshing and delicious.  Probably the best tasting beer I've ever had.  I really liked the flavor.  Very nice and drinkable on a hot night.  

Outside was a nice view overlooking Broadway.  Then we realized that there was another floor above us, so we went up to the top-most rooftop bar.

That part was split into two sections, both outdoors, with another bar in between.  We were able to sit down on some lawn chairs and chill with our beers to enjoy the music and see the pretty night lights from the skyscraper nearby.  What a fun way to end the evening without all the craziness of the party animals going nuts in the other bars.

The freaking fried pickles. THAT RANCH. literally I am such a ranch fanatic, and this was probably the best homemade ranch I've ever had. So good. Pickles were spicy, which is a change from the normal for me--(from Pittsburgh and they DEF aren't spicy up there). We went upstairs to the rooftop, and hung out on the cute couches they had. Wasn't super busy because it was a Wednesday night. I know that there are a lot of these rooftop type bars in Nashville to check out, but I would absolutely come back here again. Great atmosphere.

A friend recommended this hidden gem on our first trip to Nashville. It's hidden in a back alley and felt kinda speak easyish. Friendly bartenders, great drinks (loved the Oatmeal Cookie Moonshine), and the entertainment was on point (of course it was). They had a blues band playing a wide variety of tunes with a Little Rock and roll thrown in. Super down to earth crowd. We even felt comfortable enough to get up and dance a bit, even though were the only ones tearing it up. Overall a great time and we will definitely be back!

I was lucky enough to enjoy some awesome bluegrass music on christmas night at The Station Inn. What a treat! The Station Inn provided a wonderful, authentic atmosphere and an amazing live music experience. The crowd was full of music enthusiasts as well as tourists. We enjoyed a few pitchers of beer and snacks. The room is laid out so you will get a great view no matter where you end up sitting. There is an open and airy feel in the restrooms (haha! think curtains on the stalls - if you are a person into a super private restroom experience, bring a friend to the bathroom with you to hold the curtain shut more). Aside from the amazing live music, I love love love all of the show posters on the walls!! The mix of older and newer flyers hanging serves as a sort of poster museum. I can not wait to return here on my next trip to Nashville!

We went to see the Long Players do the Van Morrison "Moondance" album. Got there when the doors opened, thank God, since the place was already partly full before that and the tables filled up real quick. Decided to sit upstairs in the balcony. Good idea given the fact that the dance floor was full of people and the sight lines from the tables on the first floor couldn't be that good. Decent sound upstairs so we were happy with the show. And I can recommend highly seeing these guys do anything. The musicians were spot-on in reproducing the instrumental part of the album. And the rotation of singers made the night even more interesting and enjoyable. The second set was a variety of Van Morrison tunes,some hits and some just wonderful tunes from his catalog.

Two stars? Yeah, because the service sucked! We waited about 15 minutes from the time we sat down for someone to take our drink order, then another ten or more for it to be delivered. Then another 30 minutes before we could order our food. THEN we waited over an hour for it to be brought to the table. Neighboring tables had their food and finished while we waited and waited and waited. reminded our waitress, Stephanie, twice about the food. It finally arrived during the show despite the fact we arrived two hours before the show started. TWO HOURS! That was absolutely inexcusable. And of course, when you wait that long, the food was lukewarm - gumbo that isn't hot just doesn't taste good. And the rest of the food was just mediocre. Not very tasty and none of it was straight out of the kitchen. 

So, advice to the wise - go to 3rd and Lindsley for the music and some drinks. FORGET about the food - they don't know how to make it tasty and they don't know how to manage orders and timely delivery.

I love the Honky Tonk. It has really good BBQ, several areas for music from small stage to larger. It usually has good ol fashioned country music and honky tonk playing which is a plus. The atmosphere is great and the cost of food and drinks isn't too bad. Probably the best place to find BBQ on Broadway. I highly recommend.

If you are going for drinks and music cool but if you are going for food look elsewhere. The avocado toast is LITERALLY a small piece of toast with sliced avocado on it. Everything else was small portions and mediocre at best. Definitely not worth the cost when you are in a city with great food I would never recommend this place.

Honky Tonk Central is another one of the anchors on Broadway, and one of the reasons why Nashville is known as Nashvegas. Honky Tonk Central calls for a wild night full of dancing, singing at the tip of your lungs, tequila shots, and coronas. With three different floors, you are able to get a great view of Broadway, and Will have room to dance with friends. There is always live music on each floor, and Honky Tonk Central always is featuring some
Of Nashvilles best hidden talent. Definitely stop by if you are on Broadway looking for a wild night out!!

I would compare the Honky Tonk Central to a bar in the middle of Times Square in NYC. Very touristy. There are 3 floors with outdoor balconies which is very cool but on a Saturday night the place was packed. The live music on the first floor was subpar. Definitely better places on the strip for live music. I went up to the third floor to check out the live music up there and it was just as bad. 

Drinks are totally over priced. $9 for a tiny cup with hardly any vodka and seltzer. Come on I get better prices in NYC!

Overall, this place is good to maybe spot in and see but I wouldn't spend too much time here especially when there are much better options on Broadway.

We tried this place twice during our stay.  We got there too early the first time.  We went for drinks....... $6 beers and hit all three floors for music and it was awful!  We went on a Friday and expected more.  The second time we showed up and it was very crowded, service was slow and still $6 beers We had to go to the bar because the waitress could not keep up.  Of three floors only the 3rd floor had ok music.  If you want music go to Tootsies or Robert's Western. I am not a college kid but That is the crowd they cater to.

Seriously so poorly run that I am 35 th in line to go to the bathroom!!!
Food sucks.  Drinks are expensive but the music is awesome!

Great for a night of dancing! Fun vibe and great drink choices. The frozen Red Bull vodka is delicious! Can get really hot and crowded at peak hours, but always a good time. Do NOT take elevator, extremely sketchy and always overloaded.

Here's how our first trip to Nashville went. We would try a new bar out and then agreed, "If this place sucks we'll go back to our place Honky Tonk." By day two of our trip Honky Tonk was considered "our place" because we visited there so frequently throughout and day and night because it was an awesome awesome time. We first stopped in the day we arrived to the city on a Wednesday afternoon and there was live music going on on each of the three floors. All of the artists were great and the place wasn't packed so we were able to get a table on the third floor right near the corner balcony spot, ideal for people watching. The band playing was fantastic and the guy came around asking us for requests. We stayed for a while and then went down to the second floor to listen to a different band. It is pretty awesome that while you're on the third floor you cannot hear the music going on on the other floors unless you're standing out on the balcony. We went back to Honky Tonk that Wednesday night and the place was rockin'. We had a blast listening to the band on the first floor, people were really into it, dancing up a storm and there was definitely standing room only. We came back Thursday night and hung out on the third floor again, amazing music and we just hung out on the balcony watching the comings and goings on Broadway, super relaxing and people coming around regularly to ask if we wanted more to drink. We came back that night and the afternoon and night following, like I said earlier, we considered this our go to place because it was always consistent. 

Honky Tonk Central is not where the locals go, according to people we spoke with, but we didn't care. We met tons of people from all over who were doing the same thing we were, listening to awesome music and had a great time. Bartenders weren't the friendliest but we didn't care. If you don't check out Honky Tonk, you're missing out.

The beauty of Nashville is that you can wander into just about anywhere (coffee shop, hotel bar, or bar/restaurant) and find talented entertainment. We loved the 2 guys who were singing there on Sunday night and stayed for 2 drinks (we just had one if the entertainment was ordinary).
The Famous is a cut above most of the places on Broadway. The decor is modern, clean, and musical. They have heard of wine and have some decent ones by the glass. The service was warm and efficient. 
We'll go back the next time we're in town.

Went around 4:00 on a Saturday. Horribly understaffed. After 40 minutes of waiting on our order, our food was COLD. A chicken breast and fries cold enough that I didn't want to eat it anymore. Asked the server for silverware and he didn't even respond. Had to go across the room to find silverware. The food is overrated. The burgers are mediocre at best. Then, it took another 20 minutes of standing at the counter just to close the tab. I do NOT recommend.

To the friends and strangers planning a visit to Nashville, here are some reasons to swing over to Nashville Underground:

* They have a mechanical bull on the second floor (I didn't dare risk humiliation on this but it did look fun)
* They have an LED dance floor with video projection capabilities (You could watch Monday night football and jam out at the same time if you wanted. I mean, I didn't actually test this out personally, just got to see everything turned on without a DJ)
* They have a fireplace by the stage so you can get all toasty whilst you enjoy some tunes (So cozy)
* Rooftop views (Need I say more?)
* Rooftop views (Ok they have two rooftops so I felt the need to say more)
* The Flying Pig (BBQ goodness hello)
* Nashville Hot Chicken (Haha we couldn't even handle mild but it was still good)

To the top-notch manager that is Teddy- thank you, good sir, for the fabulous tour of your establishment. And to the fine staff that put up with us for four and a half hours- thank you, good people, for the prime service.

PHYSICALLY ABUSIVE DOORMEN!! ASSAULTED MY BOYFRIEND AND BROKE HIS WRIST. PRESSED CHARGES!! This was the most terrifying night of my entire life. I was celebrating my birthday in Nashville. I asked my boyfriend to take a photo of me so he placed his beer down on the ground. A waitress opened a door which caused the beer to knock over and break. She started cursing under her breath and then screaming for us to be removed from the establishment. I asked her name and she then provided me with a FAKE NAME. We were escorted into a stairwell at which point we requested to speak with a manager. My boyfriend was of course incredibly upset that this disgruntled employee was ruining my boyfriend and admittedly was being a little aggressive in his tone when speaking with the manager. He never once raised a hand, displayed any physical movements, raised his voice, or use derogatory language. The manager then said he did not want to allow us back in due to my boyfriend's anger. My boyfriend then asked the doorman for the managers name. The manager refused to give it to him and my boyfriend continued to press him for it. At this point my boyfriend's back was facing the bouncer. THE BOUNCER THEN GRABBED MY BOYFRIEND'S FACE FROM BEHIND AND SLAMMED IT INTO THE GROUND. AT NO POINT IN TIME DID MY BOYFRIEND RAISE A HAND. HE KEPT HIS HANDS BY HIS SIDE THE ENTIRE TIME AND THE BOUNCER CONTINUED TO PRESS HIS FACE AND ARM INTO THE PAVEMENT BREAKING HIS WRIST AND CAUSING BLEEDING AND LACERATIONS TO HIS FACE!!! At this point, I tried to grab my boyfriend and pull him away (I am a little girl and not very strong). I was truly terrified this large bouncer was going to kill him. People started videotaping the assault as no one could believe that an innocent man was being tackled and assaulted when he never raised a hand. After I tried to pull my boyfriend away, a second employee started screaming "SHES SWINGING AT ME!!". Crazy! I wouldn't know how to throw a punch if I TRIED. AT THIS POINT- THE SECURITY GUARDS HANDCUFFED ME!!!!! I did nothing but attempt to save my boyfriend from being beaten to death by these crazed security guards. Neither of us every swang or raised a hand to anybody. They kept us handcuffed on the side of street for a hour. MANY people kept coming over trying to help us as EVERYONE saw the security guard completely randomly physically attacked my boyfriend. This was the most terrifying and humiliating night of my life. When the police finally showed up they of course let us go immediately as we had done nothing wrong. We were detained for no reason and my boyfriend was brutally beaten by a Honky Tonk Central bouncer. We are pressing assault charges and hopefully justice will be served and this maniac will be taken off the streets and no longer be able to break anymore bones or injure innocent patrons.

We stopped in here on a Sunday for lunch and had a wonderful time. We ordered the nachos and a side of fries. They were both delicious. The live music was awesome. We only hung out on the first floor, but it was such a great time. We will be back!

I've only had the privilege of seeing one show here so far (Smashing Pumpkins w/ Marilyn Manson) but I loved every part of the experience! We used Lyft and got dropped off right at the entrance. We breezed through  friendly security and had our tickets scanned on my phone with no problems at all. We found a great spot on the grass and set up camp. It didn't seem like there was a bad seat in the house. Sound quality was great, bathrooms were clean and easily assessable, and drink/food lines were short and moved quickly. You're allowed to bring in bottled water and small snacks, but nothing that requires utensils or has bones. Despite the heat of a mid-August night we really had an amazing time. Nothing like cuddling on a blanket w/ your lovie looking at the bright lights of the city while listening to the romantic sounds of Marilyn Manson. ;)

One of the best music venues in the USA. Not just Nashville, but America. I say this as someone who lives on the Sunset Strip in LA and frequently travels to NYC, Chicago, and has spent plenty of time in New Orleans and Austin, too. 

Whether you are a local or a tourist, this is a must-stop. I repeat: MUST. If you have chance to go here and don't...you suck. Hang your head in shame. You really need to trust me on this.

They host bands that are 100% pure Bluegrass / Americana, not country music. You will find the very best musicians in the entire genre play here. Pretty much every soon-to-be great band plays here on their way up.

We caught a young (early 20's) foursome called The Barefoot Movement. Un-freaking-believable. Go listen to them on Spotify or Pandora. Some of the best bluegrass I've ever heard. They will be famous one day. I guarantee you. And that's the point: this wasn't a unique experience. Great bands come through all the time. All. The.Time. Whomever is playing tonight, or tomorrow, or next week, will probably blow you away.

All in an absolutely priceless mega dive-bar atmosphere. The kind of vibe that enhances the experience. Who the hell wants to listen to the music of the Appalachia's in the Ritz-Carlton?

Make sure to arrive AT LEAST 30 minutes prior to showtime if you want a seat, maybe more.

You haven't been to Nashville if you haven't been to The Station Inn. Even if you lived there all your life. It's that simple. Now get.

Surprisingly fun experience here with some incredible blue grass players and three fiddlers.  Not fancy with frozen pizza served by the bass player and hot dogs or a popcorn thing on the side but at least half the crowd was local.  This is a rare gem!

A fun time for a while, but security is the most shady group I have ever seen.  After throwing a guy out of the bar, they proceeded to throw all of his friends out for nothing to cover up their bad decisions.   Arrogant, should be shut down

Went there last night to listen to music and drinks. My friend and I bought 2 WELL vodka and soda waters and were charged about $3 extra for a "mixer"??? The soda was flat too. If you want to bring people back to your bar, don't charge outrageous up-charges for mediocre drinks. I have never had this happen at a bar before, usually there is a set price for your well liquor and if you get a splash of water they don't charge $3. I'll never go back

Wouldn't go back or waste my time. Service was terrible. If you do decide to go here, I would suggest you pay in CASH since our server (Server #216, Courtney) decided to change the tip and charge the bottom line total of our overall bill. Several phone calls have been placed to the establishment and an in person visit was made to get this issue resolved. To date (2 weeks later) no contact from management or accounting. Good luck!

Like many others, I'll go into just about any place on Broadway, and the Underground might be a pretty good secret? If you need a break from the wall to wall country, the upper floors were actually playing 2000s hip-hop with a light up dance floor. The rooftop patio was very spacious, and the view of Broadway from up there was the best I saw all weekend.
Food and service were below average. I suspect that doesn't matter much as one would go there for the drinks and entertainment.

Service was good but the food terrible. Got the cheesy BLT and it was so greasy from the butter they used to grill the bread. Then it was two American slices not even melted with lettuce, tomato and bacon. Over priced. The bacon was delicious. Then after we finish eating a cockroach crawls up the wall by our table. We left shortly after

Try to stop in today to listen to a great singer we previously heard the day before. 3pm was listed as the opening time. Tried to enter at 3 pm but doors were locked. An employe walked out with tri-board listing specials at 3:10 but she locked the door on her return as we tried to enter. We left to go to another venue. Poor showing for a place that received good reviews.
This is one of my favorite places in Nashville for music!  Love their music offerings, love the intimate setting so that every seat is a good one!  Acoustics are really good. Service is great!

I really do love it here, and unfortunately it's getting SO BUSY.
If you come during the week, you really need to make plans to be arriving around 5pm even if the show isn't until 8pm. Plan to bring your big pocketbook and just eat and drink until it's time. But it's a must if you want a good seat.  A couple years ago, you could arrive around 6pm without a ticket and get a decent seat. Long ago are those days.  I even recommend if you want to see a specific show you buy tickets ahead of time. Don't assume you can just get tickets at the door. Sometimes shows are sold out weeks in advance. We came around 6pm and ended up sitting in the back by the door.  1. It's cold back there with the wintry door swinging open letting people in and out. 2. You can hear things really well in this venue ie there's not a bad seat in the house in that way, however... 3. Sitting in the back is horrible if you want to SEE anything. People are standing in front of you (including servers) to get the drinks from the bar, and it's just not fun.  For food, it's bar food. We ended up getting the party platter which was great variety. As our meals, the husband got a burger which was "fine" and I think I got tater skins. I mean how can you butcher those up? I'm still waiting to find my go-to dinner option sometime and when I do, I'll definitely let you know!!

The man friend and I came to Nashville for a long weekend. We both don't like country music but enjoy Bluegrass. We found out about this place from a local when we complained about wanting to escape from the drunken bachelorette line dancing honky tonks. Stations Inn is a hole in the wall dive bar so I felt very much at home. Walking in there were mixed matched worn out folding chairs and tables all full same with the standing room at the back, we knew then we had come to the right place. We stood as close to a wall as possible and still created a fire hazard until seats opened up. The band was circled up among the tables not on the stage. The music was amazing! The experience was made even more incredible because it seemed like it was an impromptu gathering of musicians. A man walked into the bar with a guitar and just sat down and started playing along. I felt like I was listening into a friends private jam session. On this night the band was made up of men and women and all ages. One 9 year old boy was very impressive on a fiddle. We only had a few bottles of beer so I can't speak on the food, however the entertainment alone is worth the stop!
This was a fun place to hang out and listen to music. Bartender was friendly and helped us find another BBQ restaurant that stays open later than our original choice.

I came to this bar for my 21st birthday and I will NEVER go back! Not long after we got there and order many drinks (there was 10 of us) and sat down to enjoy the night, one of my friends who was there for my birthday asked for a water and got a shocking response. The bartender told her it was $2.50!! According to the LAW, if an establishment serves alcohol they are required to provide FREE drinking water. When my friend kindly questioned the bartender about this absurd topic, she was given absolute bs. She was persistent in finding out why their policy was above the law and kicked out for this reason. So after spending atleast $100 and only being there for 5 minutes, we had to leave. Also to make matters worse, my friend has a medical condition where she needs to have water accessible at all times and when she told the bouncers and police officers that, they said "I don't care, go find water down the street". The staff we dealt with were rude and beyond disrespectful. I would take my money elsewhere if I were you.

Came here during the CMA festival because we thought we could get good views from the top floors. There were 3 stories and had a different band playing on each. It was a younger, more mainstream crowd than some of the other places we went on Broadway. The service was okay, and the food was mediocre bar food. The views were the coolest part.

Was in the bar on a Tuesday night, it was not busy at all the bartender was talking to a friend I had to walk down to where she was to get her attention, walked back to where I was standing and there had been a gentleman next to me I ordered my drinks she gave me attitude as she did when we first bought our drinks. Walked away and I calledher back for the guy next to me she got cocky and said she had it and I didn't need to tell her how to do her job. She then threatened to kick me out. We were here the night before and had no issues and the staff was courteous friendly and served us with no problems. The staff needs to learn how to treat men and women alike since men and not just cater to men since women will tip better if you give them respect.

Best bluegrass venue in the country. Was here for Open Jam and what a fun experience! Basic selection of food (pizza, chips, and popcorn). The music and crowd was amazing, and a must do in Nashville. Only serves beer, alcohol wise, having Bud Light and several Yazoo beers on tap.

Came here to see Anderson East. The venue is very nice with a lot of variety between seating areas. The sound & acoustics were great for an outdoor venue. The only potential drawback for some may be the seating. We upgraded when renting lawn chairs so figured why not. I'm a larger athletic build & the seats were a little cramped for me, but luckily no one sat beside me.
Just not good. Band on the top was lame, no elevator which discourages some and the food was not worth it. And the drinks were tiny tiny. Sorry not a representative of Nashville

Came here for the Louis York & The Shindellas concert and it was fabulous! The speakers are loud and clear. I don't believe there were any "bad" seats. The staff was very accommodating. Nathan and Jeremy helped me exchange my tickets and ensure I still had a great view. It wasn't until I visited the balcony that I realized they're all good. There isn't much leg room unfortunately, but that's due to the age of the building.

I saw Old Dominion here and they said it was a sold out show but I was pleasantly surprised at how easy it was to find parking. I had lawn seats which you can rent, 2 for $15, and had a good view of the stage despite being all the way in the back. There were tons of food vendors and it looked like all seats had good visibility, no obstructed views

What a cool place for a concert! It has that perfect "Nashville" feel too! There is upper/balcony seating, room by the bar, and a lower pit area that puts you very close to the band performing. 

My friend and I went for an Echosmith concert and we had a great time! I really enjoyed the venue itself and parking nearby was only $5 (on a Thursday). I will definitely be looking for more shows at this location.
The food here was good but for a large party of 16 there was poor service. It wasn't busy and we waited for over 2 hours for our food. They did make up for it with fries for everyone!

This is definitely a stop worth making while in Nashville, but it requires planning accordingly if you expect to enjoy yourself. After reading multiple reviews, we decided to arrive at 6:30 pm on a Sunday and the doors open at 7 pm. It was a great decision because we were the first in line and by the time the doors opened, the line was easily 60 people deep. Once inside, it's a free for all with seating. Grab a seat before going to the bar! The seating is gone within minutes and there is little to no standing room. The music is great and the bluegrass seems really authentic. My only criticism is that they allow too many people in. They continue to usher people in so everyone is packed together and trying not to block others' view, so it becomes really awkward sometimes as you're trying to watch the show, but someone is standing in your way "unintentionally". When we left at 8:45 pm, there were probably 80 people in line. It's a shame that they probably didn't know that they wouldn't get a seat and would be sandwiched against a partial wall somewhere with a handful of other people.

Ended up here the other night for dinner, drinks, and a little of the Titan game. It was a last resort kind of thing because everywhere else was filled up, but it ended up working out. 
I had the hot chicken sandwich which was delicious! My boyfriend had the same thing and loved it. The fries were also super tasty. My favorite part about this spot was all of the rooftops. One of the managers took a liking to us and showed us around, very cool (didn't catch his name but he was so nice and made us feel welcome as out-of-towners). Our waitress was also really sweet and attentive- which I know can be difficult when you're also tending to the bar crowd, so I appreciate it even more! I would definitely check this place out again, even just for drinks and hanging on the rooftop.

Neat space with a upstairs and downstairs bar. It is annoying how the bathroom is only upstairs. The bartenders have poor customer service. They don't serve the bar I had to walk over to them. Even then when I came back and made eye contact with a quick bar the bartender walked away from me. Love music is great here!

WMA is my least favorite place in Nashville to see a concert.

I've attended two concerts standing in the general admission section on the main level, and one concert (this week) seated in the balcony level. 
I had high hopes that my experience in the balcony would be better than standing below, but no such luck.

To break it down...

Standing on the main level gives you a really disappointing view of the stage. It's rather high up, and due to some venue technological issue, the artists cannot perform right up to the edge of the stage - they're a good 5-7 feet back.

The balcony is pleasantly small, and each seat does feel pretty close to the performers. However, the volume and sound quality no matter where you are is terrible. At this week's concert, the volume was so loud it was almost unbearable. I'm 26 - I don't typically complain about the volume at a rock concert, but this was ridiculous, and I wasn't the only one complaining. Lots of audio feedback and popping too. Unacceptable in music city. 

Overall, I've given it three chances, and in the future I will be very, very selective about who I pay to see at WMA. After this week's event, I was definitely regretting the $100 I spent on two tickets.

I came here for lunch with my mom, aunts, and family friends while in Nashville for the weekend. Shelley was AWESOME! Very attentive and patient with us (we were a decent-sized, somewhat indecisive group). Super friendly and very sweet. Would definitely recommend this place just for her!

The live music was amazing. Definitely one of the highlights of our trip so far!

Walked 35 mins from downtown to here and the beer was oh so worth it! Ice cold beers, friendly service with real southern hospitality. This is a no frills place. Got to try a few local TN beers and some of my usual favorites too. Will def come back next time im in town.
Nice place to catch a live performance from some local and not-so-local singer/songwriters. If you can't get to The Bluebird or The Listening Room, go to Bobby's.

This place is terrible. The drinks are over priced and gross. 
The music awful. 
Bar service subpar. Didn't drink because it was gross bartender didn't even ask why.
Too many other good choices around.

Live On The Green! Music Festival is a great addition to the musical tradition in Nashville hosted by Nashville's Lightning 100 independent radio station. The bands are generally folks that you might find on Alt Nation -- but before they're on Alt Nation on Sirius/XM because Nashville is just that awesome of a music town -- or bands that you would find on Lightning 100 itself. It's a great mixture usually of up-and-coming local (or at least recorded in Nashville local) bands and bands that have just popped onto the indie/Americana/Alternative charts.

It is a free show.

But, I'm an old man these days and enjoying the concert pressed up against 20000 of my not-so-closest friends whilst sweating my body away is no longer my idea of a good time. I always opt for the VIP tickets which do have a cost and are limited in supply. The VIP tickets include free food, two free drink tickets, air-conditioned restrooms (real restrooms, not port-a-potty), and seats with huge fans blowing onto them. And, bonus, you can get closer to the stage as a VIP than the crowded, sweaty masses.

So, be an old man that enjoys music like this guy... buy a VIP ticket (But leave me one) and go to every Live On The Green! Music Festival in 2015 (as the 2014 shows just concluded in early September on the 6th).

Multi level bar with entertainment on every level. No Johnnie black & no bulliet bourbon. This seemed to be the only bars on broadway without these liquors. We were also charged two different amounts for two different rounds with the same items.
Great music.  Thank you Becki McLeod.   Bar service terrible.  Minimal table service.  Young lady acted like we were inconveniencing her.   Won't b back.   Better food And service in Nashville

This place is awesome!! The live music is awesome!! The food, drinks and atmosphere is great! All the bartenders are very attentive! Expect to spend a lot of money because the drinks are HIGH!! But had a great time!

My husband, sister, cousin and I stopped in for a bit on 9/20/2015 to listen to some music and have a few drinks. 
The service was ok, nothing exceptional. Two bartenders during peak, although one disappeared for some time and it took us awhile to get our next drink. Understandable given the location and amount of business. 

The reason for the low rating is the drinks. My husband and I drank Bourbon on the rocks (our usual brand) and my cousin drank a mixer. Independently, all three of us made a statement about the booze tasting watered down. My cousin said she could barely taste the booze in the drink. Both my husband and I remarked that the bourbon didn't have it's usual bite, and despite just being set in front of us on the rocks, tasted as if it had been sitting for awhile and the ice melted (ie, watered down). All 4 of us have grown up in the bar/restaurant industry and know what a drink is supposed to taste like. I can understand watering down a mixer, but a bourbon on the rocks? That's ridiculous! 

My advice? If you go to check it out, skip the liquor and stick with bottled/canned beer.

I can't believe this music festival is free! get here early and you can get five dollar parking. Amazing selection of food trucks that have won best of Nashville awards for many years. Such a great atmosphere and even Festival T-shirts are only 15 or $20. Everyone should come here at least once though I guarantee you if you come here you're going to want to come back every Thursday!

It's a shame this place looks so good when they are either short staffed ( all the time ) or workers who don't care.    Music is good, food is good, drinks are good when you can get them.   There are too many other places with the same thing including good service.   Don't waste your time here
Great bar, I was there twice on my visit to Nashville and the music was really good both times, it's a tourist spot, but an enjoyable one! I'd recommend it.

Not a bad meal for $10 on Broadway. This place is very reasonably priced & the food wasn't bad. I really liked the baked beans. They were sweet & had bacon in them. Only giving 3 stars because it wasn't good enough to wow me, and I probably wouldn't go back because there are so many better options close by, but you can't beat the price. If you are looking for something cheap on broadway look no further!

I've visited Honkey Tonk Central a few times and it's always a total blast. It's definitely more of a chill atmosphere earlier in the evening, but as soon as the sun goes down the real party starts. I absolutely love grabbing a beer and hanging out on one of the third floor balconies. It's great for people watching over Broadway! 

The music varies, but they generally have some very talented acts who play all of the country classics. 

It tends to get very crowded in the evening - it's definitely a bachelor/bachelorette haven, but as long as you go in with that mindset it's not that bad. 

The bathrooms have always been clean when I used them and the drinks are (in my opinion - coming from Orlando, FL) fairly priced.
Dylan was great! He was extremely nice and great confidence builder for us oldadies. The "Dots" had a blast!!! Will be back to take on the bull again.

Visited this location when me and my roommate were new to Nashville and looking for a new hangout spot. Giving it a one star is very generous of me! Service was terrible, management was even worse!! 
It took over 17 minutes to get mine and my roommates beer. I order their Mac and cheese and it came out cold, and tasted like it had been sitting for quite a while. My roommate order their burger, after being told they were out of TWO of her first choices. Burger was terrible, ordered medium and came out well. 
After mentioning to my server about how disappointed I was with the whole evening, all she did was offer me a free dessert and did not try to fix the situation at all. 

The music was so loud our server was having to yell at us and I left with a massive headache. 
The service was horrendous and the young blonde manager who gave me a dirty look after I complained, was so rude. 

The restaurant was dirty, the food was terrible, and the staff was worse!

Please save your time and money by not even entering this establishment!!!

This place is AMAZING! We are from the LA area and we would never be able to experience something like this back home.  We went on a Sunday, open jam session. What a surprise! Amazing musicians playing Bluegrass and an equally great crowd!! NASHVILLE has such a unique music scene and the people make the experience even better. Will definitely be back!

Very modern and comfortable venue.  We were there the second day after their opening.  On the 1st floor they have a few couches up front by the stage along with comfortable booth and table seating.  Nice bar area too.  They have a large variety of cold beer on tap (28.6 degrees) and a nice variety of food selections.  Had the Chicken Caesar Salad and the  Goo Goo Cluster Brownie Sundae - both were good.  See their menu online at their site.  Server was friendly and efficient and gave good  food suggestions.  The acoustics were good also.  Planning on going back this weekend!

Mediocre food and an hour wait for a table. The night we went here there was a big football game on and the crowd could have cared less about the live music. This lack of engagement made the band bored. So it wasn't the best situation. Hopefully it's more fun on a regular night!

As of today I have attended 4 concerts at Ascend Ampitheater and each and everyone has been fantastic and AFFORDABLE! 

Getting to the heart of downtown nashville and parking is usually the most expensive and annoying part of any of our great downtown venues but Ascend is right on the river and you can park for all concert across the bridge for $5, thats hard to beat!

After concerts you are walking distance to broadway and SoBro, so you can always find something to do downtown.

As for the food inside it was all actually good too, the frozen lemonades were the best i've had at any entertainment event, and the food was quick and not too overpriced.

If you are going here for a concert I would recommend getting seats closer to the stage as the Lawn fills up quick, but there really isnt a bad view in the house.

Disappointing. The hot chicken sandwich was a huge disappointment. I'm not sure there was chicken on the sandwich, it was a flat piece of breaded, fried something covered in hot sauce. Fries were good but you can get them at half the cost at any fast food place. The pickles? Delish! When I commented how good the pickles were, the bartender brought me extra. 

And the bartending staff was also disappointing. There were two young guys who had zero skills in the noticing there were people needing drinks department. If it weren't for for bartender Lauren, I would have sent back the food and left. She was professional tho I suspect she knew the food was sub-par but her attentive and friendly personality made me still want to pay the bill. 

The location is good...towards the end of the rowdy Broadway crowd. The 7-9 pm band was great (earlier band not so much). I'm confused by the entire experience.

This place was amazing!  It has multi story servicing at multiple bars! I was drinking (heavily) at the bottom floor (entry point) and Mallory was the best bartender I had in Nashville! She was quick to help, provide, and pour! I will definitely be back to Honky Tonk! She made my weekend in Nashville worth it!
Also, big shout out to Kelsey, Lisa and Stephanie!  Quickest drinks served on St. Patrick's day.
I was asking to put on the Indians game...(a postseason game 2 games) and was a told no chance. Even when there were multiple TVs with duplicate games on.  This place was so awful and I forgiven

This seems like a special spot with a unique history, but we had a terrible experience. My friend and I (literally seated in the very back corner) were talking waiting for the music to start. When the music started we were still chatting, which I did not think much about until an older man (owner?) came over and told us to stop. We of course instantly stopped, horrified that we had been scolded, but every time I looked over this man was glaring at me from behind the counter. After five or ten minutes of enduring the glaring we left. I am the kind of person that never ever gets in trouble and it was all kind of awful.

Well thank heavens.  I've been "saving" my 200th review for something Bicentennial-Worthy and this is definitely it!  
Hubby and I are rarely home together during the week as we both business travel a lot.  This week we decided to finally check out one of the classic Nashville attractions, The Doyle & Debbie show at The Station Inn.  OK, the bar itself would get a 4 from me and I'm sure there are those who would trash it to pieces.  However, it is what it is and it's not pretending to be anything else ( much the same way as John A's over in Music Valley).  Bring cash, don't expect fancy drinks or an extensive menu of apps, get over yourself and have a good time.  The prints on the walls reflect some of the great talents that play or have played here.  I hope it never changes.

Now, for the show.  I was excited to see it although I was kind of dreading a night of jokes that might take digs at some of my opinions that don't necessarily line up on the same side of the aisle as some folks around these parts.  I mean, I can hang...but it gets tiresome.  I had nothing to fear as it turns out.  This show is just flat out funny.  Oh my...the in your face humor/satire is great but it's the subtleties that really get you.  The uneasy smiles, fidgeting and general awkwardness are hysterical!  And the show...oh my...I don't want to give anything away but it's some of the best satire ever.  The kind that has you wondering if it really IS satire at all.  It's that good.  I'm going to drag every guest we have from out of town to The Station Inn for this show.  Go and have fun.

Bu far my favorite bar in Nashville. Cheap drinks with an amaxing atmosphere and people. The bands and levels on each floor keep it interesting while the writing on the walls allows you sketch your name into history. Beautiful views, beautiful people, and only great times!
Kevin the bartender is the best!! I recommend this place for before dinner drinks or late night!
Good music, cod was good, my son said the bbq sandwich, he loved it.  Two craft drafts and only $32 but I tipped very well
Great little place. Good bands and drinks. If you are looking for a chill place this is it.
This is the best place in town.  Great bands and outstanding service. Everybody is very kind. Sound system has good quality.   Definitely a must see spot in Nashville.

Nashville in general you can't go wrong anywhere.. we came here for a bachelor party (late breakfast) the place was not very busy but had live music, roof top bar/seating. 

Good vibe, nice view, nice servers.. 

BUT our food took more than 45 min to get to us, and most of it was breakfast food, quick and easy to make and prepare. 

My side of fries were cool, and sand which was less than warm.. 

The reason for 2 stars is because food is good and place is fun. Other than that I'm very upset we passed up other places because of long wait times, that I know are better, to experience a long wait time on a place that really wasn't too busy.

Hands down my favorite outdoor venue in Nashville.  If you can, get a VIP or box ticket, as the experience is first rate.  With VIP, you can enter through a reserved line, and just after you enter, you are steps from the food and drink lounge, which often features live music of its own.  The space has 2 bathrooms, a bar, a moderate buffet, popcorn, air conditioning and beautiful leather seating.
Once in the venue, there is not a bad seat in the house. With box seating, you get a designated server, food menu and bar service.  You will question if you are really at an outdoor concert!  Too cool.
Lawn seating is just behind the box seating, and you will have access to many higher end liquor selections in a food court type setting.
Even in the heat of summer, the evenings are quite pleasant here.
I have been to many outdoor amphitheaters in several different states.  Nashville got it right!
As an added bonus, its fun to watch the city lights come up as you watch some great live music!

This venue is beautiful! Nashville did a great job making a comfortable, well lit, nicely staffed and right on the water home for their newest venue. We saw the 3rd show at The Ascend and this was the 4th concert we had traveled to in a week and of all the venues and shows we saw this week this amphitheater tops the cake for enjoyable and comfortable viewing.  The city served as a beautiful backdrop to the perfectly lit stage. Staff was nice and we witnessed a few partiers be comforted on their trips in a way we viewed as positive for anyone in their situation. Happy show goers are a great thing to have at a venue as the positivity spreads far in these things. The bathrooms were kept clean and checked upon by staff frequently through the evening. I only witnessed the women's bathroom and was very pleased to have such a clean restroom (and while on the road I must say is still the cleanest I have seen), but I was told the men's room experienced longer wait times and supposedly have less stalls then the women's, but overall were still nice. We very much enjoyed this experience and although we live far away we will definitely be back! Thank you also to Live Nation!™ for your helpful and friendly staff, this experience was furthered by all your employees on 8/4/2015.

This really was one of the coolest experiences that we had in Nashville. Reading about the cool things to do here, we kept hearing that the Station Inn would provide a unique Bluegrass Experience. We stumbled in for a Bluegrass open mic night so to speak, and were blown away. There in the middle of this small place was a circle of artists that ranged in age from children to grandpas playing their respective instruments harmoniously. We grabbed a couple of seats - which aren't fancy by any means and enjoyed the show. The bar is really divey - most of the seating is standard metal folding chairs. There are a couple of double seats along the back wall if you are looking for something more comfortable and you have a date. There is a snack stand that sells beer by the bottle and other drinks. For snacks they have pizza, nachos, popcorn and some other random pre-packed items. Nothing fancy about this place - but it will be an awesome experience. As we sat there, we saw person after person walk in and join this ever-growing jam session. Station Inn is right in the middle of the Gulch, and music starts at 8. So a prefect after-dinner spot.

Amazing view on the roof top!  Bartenders are great and love the decor.  I have been here many times at night and was happy to hear my niece was allowed in during the day; she loved the live music and keeps asking for me to bring her back!

NYE at Underground in Nashville was one of the worst experiences getting in to the place for the 20 guest we had so called VIP table which was horrible to get that cost 4000 to rent. I complained about a horrible door guy to Tom D. who was my contact supposely only heard from him once and said a Kelley was going to call to give me details never contacted me. Get to Underground and Tom is the door guy rude as anything just asked I have a 4000 table and my guest frozen outside. He ignores me and complain straight to Tom D today just to keep it to themselves and I and he is rude again in his email trying to blame my group for not coming all together. I would not get any VIP table at this place no matter if Nashville is sold out

Their Nashville fries taste like arbys fries, but they are straight. Fricken bomb.com y'all. Salads are humongous and super yummy. I got the chicken caesar, muy bueno. Chicken tenders were okay. They were saltier than expected. Roof top is the bee's knees. Good view of all of Broadway since it's at the end of the street.

Stopped here on a Sunday night and Monday afternoon. I'd say this place was almost as equally packed both times. We were able to get seats both times, once at a large table, after about 15 minutes of looking for one and the second time at the back end of the bar. We didn't eat here, just came to enjoy drinks and music. The music here was great! They played a lot of crowd favorites and were very entertaining.

My complaint about this place would be the slow service, when we were at a table it took sooooo long for our waitress to come back...on Monday when we sat by the bar it was easy to see why...the waitresses spent 1/3 of their time working and 2/3 of their time standing around, complaining about customers and watching the basketball game! I mean, it was really uncomfortable hearing them make fun of a patron because they didn't want a lot of cranberry juice in their drink, or asking for something else specific. The waitresses would throw glass and empty cups into the trashcan behind us and send ice and other bits of trash flying into the air and onto the floor. When we sat down the one bartender completely ignored us, I assumed her job was to only take orders from the waiters because it was blatant, but then I saw her serving the customers right next to us so it was clear she just doesn't like money. We stayed for one drink and left, it wasn't worth the hassle of listening to the rude waiters and dealing with the staff. Being on Broadway you can find a great caliber musician at one of the many bars there, you would think they would fight a little harder to keep customers happy!

Personally we liked the music at other places better, so if this place is full you are better off somewhere else!

It was a worst experience they kick us out thinking we were the condensation coming from the air
But if your ever visiting Tennessee this is the worst spot ever

They shutdown the kitchen because they had too many orders while we watched the manager rage-quit.  Great place to drink and massive TVs at every angle, but this place must be run by a bunch of downsies smashing their cocks in toilet seats trying to churn butter

First time at 3rd and Lindsley, specifically to catch Vince Gill with the Time Jumpers. Unfortunately, Vince didn't make the show, but am awesome show nonetheless. I actually don't think Vince would have added anything to the experience since the band was amazing. Our server Garret was very attentive and polite. This venue fills up quick on a Monday night so get there early. We arrived a little after 6:00 for an 8:00 show and seating was filling up quick.

This has got to be the coolest place I've ever seen a show, and I've seen hundreds. Went to see Slayer here, because I wanted to see Slayer, but when we arrived, I got so much more. Suck a great old building, beautiful interior, I can't say enough good things about the look and feel of this place. The show was amazing (of course) and there wasn't a bad seat in the house. We had seats, just off the side of the stage, and thy were SO comfortable, considering most places with seats have hard, small seats, these were roomy and soft. I will be looking for any opportunity to go back to War Memorial Auditorium. another great thing is there's lots of free parking after 6, so that saves over most other venus in Nashville. I cannot wait to go back

The bartender upstairs was very personable and changed one of the screens to the desired football game that was on. Their bloody Mary's are hands down one of THE best bloody Mary's I have ever had, as they are homemade and not some Mr. T's mix. 

They have a pretty decent selection on their menu, but I ordered their seasoned fries and beer cheese dip. My friend got the mac & cheese bites, but I guess they weren't too good since she only ate a couple and ate my fries.

I really hate to complaint. But I'm here for a friends concert today. I was the first person in line to get into the door. The first person to sit down and order. After ordering it took 15 mins for me to get my drinks and water. I order chips and salsa and the prime rib dinner. Everyone's food came out before mines. After waiting for a total of almost 30 mins both my appetizer and dinner came out at the same time. My dinner was suppose to come with a salad which I never got. So I asked for it. And the waitress didn't know if the came with a salad or not. That's why she didn't bring it. Well hello it clearly says it on the menu. I though waitress are supposed to learn the menu before hopping on the floor to serve. But anyways I asked for another side of fries instead since it's too late to eat a salad. And asked for more salsa for my chips since it was not enough to dip with for the chips. She told me she would have to charge me for the salsa. I'm not asking for anything free or want anything for free. But since you brought my food out all LATE. You brought everyone's else food before mines and I ordered first. You should have at least accommodate me for the sauce. But good day. I won't be coming back here again. I was here for the first time last 2 months ago everything was PERFECT. But this time is just sad service. Oh and she didn't even apologized or anything. We ordered everything at one time and got everything one by one.

We went in there on Wednesday, May 11th and I liked it right away.  This place has 3 floors and each floor has a huge bar and a stage for live music.  I was surprised that they had bands playing in the middle of a weekday there.  That was great.  We are from San Jose, Ca.  and I wish we had a place like that here. 
     We didn't order any food there so not sure what they serve but since it's a bar and grill you can pretty much guess what they have.  The second floor was closed for some reason I don't know.  But both bands on the first and third floor were playing country music and they were really good.  
     The bartender on the third floor was very attentive.  She didn't make us wait to order our drinks which I really liked.  So many bar and grills I've been to where the bartender kind of ignores you for 10 minutes while they bullshit with people at the other end but the barkeeps here don't do that.  They help you immediately.  If you get there and the first floor has no place to sit down simply go upstairs and you can find a spot at the bar.  
     I will definitely go back there when in Nashville.   Great place.

Was here with a group of 9 on Friday night. We decided not to go back on Saturday or Sunday. There are better places to grab a drink and hear great live music. Our table order some food and the waitress added an 18% gratuity to our tab. I get it at a restaurant but not when you are ordering bar food and buying drinks ( and a lot of them too!) She pulled the same stunt when she brought us a round a shots. YOU WANT $18 TO BRING US SHOTS FROM THE BAR TO OUR SEATS WHICH TAKES ABOUT 30 SECONDS OF YOUR TIME???!!!! GET REAL! Never had that happen anywhere before and won't happen to me again because I will not be back. Try Tin Roof or The Stage. Those places don't try to hose their patrons.

So they have a extensive beer selection as well as over 20 on draft. The food was just ok. I had s brisket melt that was good but with a little more work would have been fantastic. My mans burger was also good but the party was more like a frozen patty. Now his coleslaw was super fresh and obviously home made and he lived it. I had there o ion rings and they melted in my mouth. A solid bar good place

While this is obviously a tourist centric bar (being in the heart of Broadway) I still loved this place and was by far my favorite stop on my trip to Nashville. Obviously not the best choice in alcohol (basic mixed drinks and beer) but the atmosphere was great. Three levels of live music with friendly bar tenders at each stop. There were plenty of seats, food, and good music to go around. I recommend the top floor as its a little less crowded than one and two. The place is loud but not ear drum shattering. I could clearly understand the band and had a blast singing and dancing to all the songs. Great stop if you're on Broadway and want a cheap drink and great entertainment.

Wow. This place is huge with 3 different stages and 3 different bands playing on a given night. I was only able to make it to the first floor because we were lucky enough to get a table there. The drinks were reasonably priced compared to the other bars on Broadway. The band was great and they were singing a lot of modern country which I really enjoyed.

One of my favorite bars in Downtown, and never has busy or shoulder to shoulder as Tootsies; nor is it as touristy.  I love the open balconies.  Flagging down the bar tenders is meh, neither harder nor easier than any other bar.  What do you expect?  Smoking allowed on the balconies is a plus (for me, maybe a minus for you).  ...and good people watching from them!
