And of course, if you don't like the music, just walk upstairs (or downstairs)!!

Not your typical Nashville tourist bar. Downstairs has the live music we all expect in Nashville with lots of open space and huge couches lining one wall.  Huge bar nice back room with a bar and do check out the roof top bar.  It's a great place to eat. The Nachos, and wings are great as is their bar.
Typical overpriced Nashville bar, drinks were good but holy cost Batman. We were on the rooftop which has an excellent view of the river, but it's really only good for one drink.

First time to Nashville, just had to come downtown to Broadway. We stumbled across Nashville Underground and it was beyond the best taste of Nashville that we could have ever asked for. We went up to the rooftop and met our bartender, Bobby Two Times, he has the heart and soul that we were looking for in the Music City!! The Hot Chicken was to die for and wish that I could enjoy it on a regular basis but our service superseded all! Thank you Bobby Two Times for putting such a wonderful impression of this lively city!

We hit Broadway on our Nashville trip and were blown away by how busy it was! We walked all of the way down to the what looked like the end and found this place. Turns out that was best because this place is so much fun! Great food and a super friendly staff! We had a great time there and wanted to share!

We went on Sunday they have great bands it was a great time.  One of the stalls in the women's bathroom was not working.  It was during the day so it was not that busy but the women's bathroom had a long line.  One of the guys said you should go in the men's bathroom no one is in there.  Should we have went.......probably not but we did.  When we came out there was a guy there that yelled at us we were out.  I walked back to where my friends were.........we were in a group of 8.  Our food had just come out.  When I got back to my seat the manger was behind me yelling at me.  I said I was sorry, we just got our food can we eat.  He said no ....grabbed my food and through it in the trash.  Told me we were out......I said I needed my credit card back.  He was so rude, I paid for the food he through out and we left.   I could see if I was drunk and rude and yelling at him.  We were very nice about it.  The police officer he had brought over could not have been nicer.....I think he felt bad for us.   He was just very rude and had no right throwing out the food.  I had other friends there that could have eaten it.   I am not one to sit and argue with someone especially someone that acted the way he did.   When I asked for the manager he said he was the manager.  I can't imagine working for someone like that.  I can say I have never in my life been kicked out of a bar.   The funny thing is you commented on our FB page how happy you were we had checked in.   Great time..........look out if you go in the men's bathroom.  ;)

This place was great!! The music was excellent. It's definitely a neighborhood divey-kind of bar (clean, but not fancy at all) but very enjoyable.
I'd definitely recommend getting there early -- less than 45mins in advance and you'll have trouble finding a place to sit.
The bartender Bobby 2 Times made our evening an experience to remember. Don't know what you want to drink? He will create you a one of a kind beverage. Great time! Will be back.

Honky Tonk Central was the first bar we walked into after arriving in Nashville and I think maybe the best of all the bars we went to. We had so much fun (we tried to get back here over and over during our stay, but it was just too busy each time we tried). 

We arrived while the Titans were playing on TV, and live music on stage. We immediately got a seat at the bar and ordered our beer. I ordered a local brew (well a few), Yazoo Pale Ale. We sat at the bar for a few hours and listened to the music. I really enjoy country music, my boyfriend however is not a fan, but even he enjoyed the whole honky tonk experience. Corey Johnson was on the stage, he was a great singer, kept the crowd engaged. At one point a couple left to go watch their team play (Saints-paying against the Browns) as they walked out, Corey asked where they were going and told them if they left, their team would lose, it was all in good fun but it turned out great for Cleveland fans, because they left and their team lost.  The Browns won that day! Wow does that mean that now we're going to have to go to Nashville and listen to live country music every time the Brown's play? Haha!

The bar has several floors, although we only visited the first. The ground floor has giant windows all around, so you get the bright lights from outside, and don't feel like you're missing out on a nice warm day. 

We only ordered drinks, not sure if they had food. We had a great time here, tried to go back several times over the next few days but the crowd was so thick we opted for other bars.

If in Nashville again, will definitely try to get back here again.

Our daughter lives in Nashville. We visit Honky Tonk every visit. We always love the music and love that this place is huge and can handle the crowd volume without seeming crowded. It is on the corner and is three floors with balconies that over look Broadway. The last two times we have been lucky to have the same bartender by the name of Jordan. She is great. She makes great mixed drinks which is hard to sometimes find on Broadway. We also heard a great up and coming singer by the name of Jackson Capps. We stayed for his entire set. Look him up and visit him on stage at HTCentral. Also, look for Jordan!

Delicious Manhattan made by our favorite bartender, Emellee.  The Famous Saloon has a nice, clean atmosphere.  Guitar pick murals are unique enough to stop by and grab a drink.  Heard a great new artist, Chris Cole.  He was great and had plenty of talent to rock out requests on a whim. I will definitely stop back to this place when I am in town again.

One of the best things about hosting first-time Nashville visitors is we're compelled to do touristy things we might not otherwise do. As a 7 year resident of this area, a visit to the Station Inn was long overdue. I'm not really even a bluegrass fan, but the two bands we saw (both from Indiana, ironically) were great. Almost all seats were taken by the time we arrived, but we found a place to stand that wasn't in the way and offered a great view of the stage. This is definitely a must-visit for anyone visiting Nashville, or those of us who have lived here a long time and never been.

Yet another fun stop on the Honkey Tonk Strip! This place has no cover, just like all the other bars on the strip. I think that this place was only one floor, but I'm not 100% sure. This place is on the corner with the entrance toward the front of the room alongside the stage. So it was easy to com in and start dancing without having to muscle through a crowd of people. The night I was there the band was amazing, hopefully they were a regular band, and they were a request band. There was plenty of dancing going on here. The bar was in the center of the room, so there wasn't much overcrowding while waiting to order a drink.
Definitely would recommend the Key Lime Pie drink. Ask for bartender Stephanie, she's amazing!
The rooftop had the best view of the city and Cumberland River. Moscow Mules were delicious!

4.5

When living in Music City, you expect great music and great concerts. All genres of music come here and I'm always on the look out for some great shows. This summer the Ascend Amphitheater has a pretty amazing line up and when my boyfriend told me he bought tickets for Portugal. The Man, I was pretty excited. However, I was a little nervous about two things. One, he got the lawn seats so I didn't think the view would be great. Two, it's an outdoor venue so the experience all depends on the weather that day. I just crossed my fingers and hoped for the best!

We went to the concert on a Saturday night. The venue is in a really nice location. There is $5 parking across the pedestrian bridge so it's just a short walk over. We were pretty early so we were able to grab a drink downtown and then walk to Ascend when we were ready. We got to Ascend around 6:30 so make sure we got a good enough seat for the show at 7:30. Check-in was quick and easy. They check your bags so don't try to sneak anything in. There is food and drink for sale but of course everything is pretty expensive. At first I was shocked to see the price of beer at around $15, but then I realized the cans were pretty big. I think they were 24 ounces so really you're paying $7.50/beer. That's not much worse than a beer downtown. I didn't look at the food options but I did see a food truck or two. I was pleasantly surprised by the lawn seats. The lawn is on a slope so seeing the stage is no problem. We got a seat right at the front of the lawn and had a perfect view. We just brought towels to sit on but you can bring low chairs or rent chairs. I was worried about the people constantly walking back and forth between the lawn and the seats, but security does a nice job of keeping people moving along. They don't allow people to sit on the ledge of the lawn. They don't allow people to linger or watch the show in the walkway. People might complain about this but the people in the lawn paid money to see the show too so not blocking our view is just common courtesy. The sound of the show was very loud and I had no problem seeing the stage. The lawn seats are a pretty good deal! They are about half the price of the normal seats. I had a blast at this show and would definitely come to another show here! 

Now here is the warning. It's an outside venue. Sometimes it rains. That's the risk you take with going to a show here. They don't reschedule shows so if it's raining, the show goes on. If it's lightning, the show might get delayed. We had some lightning in the distance so I thought it was going to pour on us. Luckily, the weather stayed clear and we had a perfect night. I think if it was raining the lawn would be a mess and it would be hard to enjoy the show. My advice, bring a poncho just in case and bring plastic bags for electronics. Do a stay-away rain dance and hope for the best! If you get a clear day/night, you will really enjoy this venue!

Super chill venue with a great atmosphere to it. I came to The Back Corner for a private show, and wasn't expecting it to be too amazing, but I was blown away! I loved the set up of the venue as well as the sound. I look forward to attending more events here in the future!

The service sucks. One in our party never received his meal even after we asked multiple times. Another in our party, the meal was so over done it was like leather. The manager sucks. Need to fire the management team.  They eventually provided the missing meal. The manager adjusted our bill. Even with the credit does not excuse the extremely poor service. I do not recommend. There are too many other locations to patronize.
My home away from home when I am in Nashville. Best place to watch a Packer's game is upstairs.

What a great experience! The food was delicious. Fried pickles and Hot Chicken Sandwich and fries were so good. And the kids said they were the best chicken tenders they've ever had! The mechanical bull was a blast. Plus everyone who worked there was so helpful and patient with our large group. Dakota was the epitome of southern hospitality. Thank you so much for a great time.

Where to begin? For starters: They don't allow smoking! Thank the Good Lord & Baby Jesus.

For the con's: Let me put this early in the review - do NOT go for the food. It is all microwaved/deep fried FREEZER food from Sam's Club. It. Is. Terrible. Sure the prices aren't horrendous, but the food IS. The cheese sticks are straight up the "Farm Rich" ones from the green and white freezer bag. Yeah, you know the ones I'm talking about. Pre-packaged, not fresh burgers. Even the waitress said nothing was made in-house. Everything is from cans, bags, and came out of the freezer. All the other review are correct also, the service is SLOWWWW. They also got our order wrong twice.

For the pro's however: The venue is very neat. Used to be a TON smaller, and it appears in the last few years they've bought the place next door and knocked out a whole wall, doubling their size and moving the stage out another 30-40 foot. This is a cool place to come watch talented acts on a super small stage. Decent seating from the floor, ok seating in the balcony sections, however if you get the wrong table on either side, you'll be looking at the speaker boxes all night.

All-in-all, very neat, small, and intimate venue to see true Nashville talent and artists for a pittance of a price. Go! (Just eat before or after the show...)
Pretty standard Broadway bar.  Food is pretty generic.   Service is unattentive.   Nice tap list.  Live music.  Given the number of options available, I would pass on this joint.

This was a decent restaurant we didn't go for drinks just food! We sampled the shrimp po' boy the pulled pork sandwich and the hot chicken sandwich. It was good but nothing special. The atmosphere in the restaurant was great though, really enjoyed the live music!

Our uber driver warned us of this. This bar will try and double charge you. Happened to our group with 3 different servers and bartenders even when we paid cash they gave back incorrect change. We had to correct every purchase we made as they double charged us. FAKE NEWS! Sad! Folks, please double check your receipts.
This is a unique space for Nashville. It has a lounge vibe with a good DJ and great drinks. It's a good place to go for some dancing and drinks after a night out to dinner

The only place hopping on a Sunday night.  With 3 floors to choose from, you can expect to find your desires flavor of... country music.  Actually, the band on our floor did play some other soft rock hits (journey, etc).  Since I'm not really a country buff (shhh), this was a pleasant surprise.

Bartenderess was friendly, and we found a TV with a soccer game on.  The bottom floor was the liveliest, with folks dancing and a very busy bar.  The top floor was a little more mellow.  Drinks are served in clear plastic cups, which might give you an idea how cheap this place is.

In the bar scene of Nashville, Honky Tonk Central remains King as the biggest and the best, catering to the widest audience.  No wonder it's the only place on Sunday to have more than a few people in it :)

DON'T GO HERE!! And definitely DON'T give them your credit card!! Had the worst restaurant/bar experience of my life. Ordered fries with gravy that were never delivered even after asking 4 times over an hour period. Mac and cheese came out after 50 minutes and sat on the bar counter in front of us for 10 minutes getting cold before we could get the barback's attention & ask them to give it to us. The bartender lied to us and said there was no way to contact the manager & lied about what his manager even looked like & then the barback was able to call the manager on a walkie-talkie. Manager was the opposite of helpful & basically said there was nothing that could be done. Left after 1.5+ hours, never got the fries at all, was told they were taken off check, paid for what we actually had and then was DOUBLE CHARGED for that order anyway (way more than what the fries were)!!! They also continue to have 2 $5 holds on my credit card that I can't get taken off the until they process....apparently just so they can literally steal more money. No apology nothing from anyone there except the Barback who was very nice. This establishment cares nothing about customers and is dishonest. It's in a great location but there are TONS of other great places around. I've never had service nearly this bad in Charleston, Boston, NYC, or any other large city I've been to. Please don't give this place your credit card so they can steal your money and put fraudulent charges on it too!

Great atmosphere! We went on a Monday night. I am pregnant and was very happy not to be bombarded by sloppy drunk people. We also sat at the bar and ate chicken fingers which were delicious! Neither of is felt like having a drink and we still got excellent service!
The bartenders are great! The drinks are cheaper here than most bars in Nashville. The band ended at 10:00pm ... the bar stays open til 3:00am. I would have stayed longer, but there was no music.

What more can i say then this is a great bar, with decent food. No matter what time of day it is you will hear live music. Music was great, bartenders were great, just a laid back chill spot that i could stay for hours!
This place is freakin' awesome! The bands are always great! The food is awesome! I have to say, this is my favorite bar in Nashville!

It could be an awesome place , but is WAY too loud! It is painful in the bar. Either turn it down or install sound dampening in the ceiling. As it is, I can't stand to be in the bar more than 30 minutes at a time. It's a shame cause it's an awesome bar....

3/24/17 update: 
They are ironing out the issues and I've personally bumped them up a star. The music on the ground floor is loud, but not painful; the rooftop bar has an awesome view of the city, multiple TV's for watching the "big game"; the food is one of the best for "bar food" (really it's better than "bar food" and should really be considered a restaurant that's also a music venue); they have a great bar tending a wait staff. As I hoped and suspected, this is fast becoming one of the best honkytonks downtown and is re-making 2nd Avenue a destination (along with George Jones's new renovations and the Wild Horse which always packs a crowd).

I am so upset!!!  I walked in to this place with six other women, all of us in our 40's, and very respectable. We walked in and we were immediately approached by a man and told "If you're here to party and talk and be loud, you need to leave". We seriously just walked in and we had not said one word!!!  My friends who had not been here before were very insulted. We had to walk out because it was so uncomfortable. I will never go again. And will tell all that I know to never go. 
I love listening to bluegrass, but not being insulted. I've never felt so uncomfortable, even as a crazy teenager, have I ever been approached like that.

Went here for a work event. Multiple stories to provide a lot of space. Food was typical bar food but still delicious. Drinks were strong but delicious. There is a outside deck in the top floor with games. Perfect place for a work event and I would go here again if I was looking to have a drink off of broadway in Nashville. Thanks for the hospitality!

Beer only, but cheap beer! We shared 2 pitchers for $14 each. Very cool live music. Just beware that there are some patrons there that think they're at their own private concert at the Grand Old Opry. My fiancé and I were having a conversation and were publicly shamed for talking. The music is good but not like stop all conversations good.

Went there on Saturday with 3 friends.  Made a reservation online and when we arrived we were told we couldn't be seated and our reservation meant nothing.  Exact words of the manager.  He left and a very nice security guard came over and told us to go upstairs there were plenty of tables we could help ourselves to.  We did, and were told someone would come over and serve us.  30 minutes later I go up to the bar and was completely ignored.  So after 5 minutes I went back to our table and finally someone came over.  We were told we couldn't put in an order for 45 minutes and it'd be much longer after that before our food would come.  We left.

Passing through Nashville and decided to check out Broadway.  After checking it out for a bit, I decided to get something to eat and stumbled upon Nashville Underground. I have to say that the food was fantastic and the service was even better. My group sat at the rooftop bar and was served by the one and only Bobby Two Times. I have one word for this guy... phenomenal!  Next time I'm in Nashville, this will defiantly be the place that I will stop at.

Horrible service. Went there during the late day and decided to try it again two days later at night and the staff cared more about talking to young women than letting tourists in to listen to the band. DON'T GO HERE.

I'd never heard of The Back Corner so any preconceived notions flew out the door upon entering.  One word- Gorgeous.  The space is long and narrow, rustic with exposed brick and iron rafters.  Lots of wood trim give a feeling of warmth.  The focal point is a gorgeous sculpture hanging from the ceiling, a reclining bass (the instrument, not the fish) with a headless figure on top....just go see for yourself since it's artistry is indescribable.  The bar is a diamond shape right upon entering.  Great pours at an affordable price. There's a dance floor beyond the bar and the stage is at the back of the room.  There are two lofts on either side running the full length of the room with staircases right past the entry; I suggest heading up to the comfy sofas and watching a show away from the teeming masses.  The lighting is soft and the sound system rocked.  We didn't try any food so I can't comment on the menu.  I didn't notice any cocktail servers which would help, the bar is busy since everyone crowds around it upon entering to get a  drink before finding their spot.  All around a great addition to the neighborhood and a classy intimate place to watch a live performance.

Came in around 4pm when it was slow, Elizabeth the local bar tender was awesome and insightful giving us tips of local things to do! The food was amazing and the drinks delicious! Major thanks to Elizabeth. The men's bathroom faucet does need to be fixed...pointing in the wrong direction .

While walking to another spot we saw a sign on an exterior wall advertising beer below freezing. Had to go check this out and YES, their beer is very, very cold and the live music was great! Many different bars and areas to socialize. More than one rooftop bar and a corn hole area. This place is huge!  Happy hour pricing too!  Manager Joshua swung by to make sure we were happy which we were. My favorite find of my Nashville weekend.
Awesome atmosphere and fantastic music! Drinks are great. Burger and pulled pork were delicious! Will definitely be back. Staff are excellent and very attentive

Was only here for about 30-45 minutes, but I knew I had to write a review because the atmosphere of this place was really very cool and unlike any other bar I had been to.  There are three floors to this bar, and on each floor there is a different band.  What is nice about this is you can still hear some great live music, but because there is so much square footage you are not be sardine smashed with the rest of the people in the joint.  One bouncer here was a bit of an angry man, but other than that had a great time.  I would recommend my friends stop here for at least a drink in Nashville to check out the three floors of music.
The Auditorium is a great venue. It can be difficult to find parking.  Also, the food that is sold inside is very unhealthy

I recently came and saw the Time Jumpers with some folks,  and really had a great time. 

We sat at the bar for a bit while waiting for the rest of our party to arrive. Our service was swift and our beer cold! Our table had an excellent view of the stage, and the sound of the show was just great in that space! 

Music aside, the food was pretty tasty too -  I shared the prime rib with someone and was very happy with it. 

I definitely can't wait to see more shows here!

In town for the weekend and stumbled on Bobbys for a PBR tall boy.  The dive bar theme with live music was great and not overstated.  Much cleaner than a dive bar in Philly. Bartender was friendly and served up limes with Coronas.  Great dart board.  Plenty of local characters at the bar providing advice to the band.  Worth a look in.

1st time going to Ascend Amphitheater. I went to see Charlie Puth yesterday (8/28/2018) and the staff did amazing job for helping people to find their seats and being patient w/ customers asking about the merch (like looking at sizes). My ticket was close to the front. And it was a very awesome experience. The staff did the chairs amazingly spaces so we (as fans/audience) can stand or get through. For advice, just be careful of being overheat/sweaty. It was like 92 degrees on a hot summer day.

I wish that I could be in the town longer to be able to know how consistent this place is...but having been there three different times, I'd say it is middle of the range. This past Saturday night the David Ray band was playing and although there was a group of drunk women that kept running into my mom and I...overall it was a good experience. The music was good, the singer had a good personality, and he could actually sing. It was super crowded, but you would have to expect that on a weekend night. We just went again tonight and I was really looking forward to it, but ended up leaving after a couple minutes. I love music and like live music loud, but this was just way too loud and even I couldn't handle it. There weren't many people in there anyway, and no one was dancing at all. I can't say I don't like this place, because I'd probably try it again if I was staying, but only on a Friday or Saturday night and if the music was good. I think that would like to try the other floors as well to have that experience next time. Hopefully next time I could update the review with a better score :)

I have been to this venue many times and it never disappoints. Whether you're a local or a tourist I'd highly recommend a visit to 3rd and Lindsley.

 I have seen many different musical acts from all different genres. It doesn't  matter if you're sitting in the balcony or standing right in front the stage the sound is always good great.
  
 If you're up to dinner before the show, it's also not a bad place to eat and everything on the menu is very reasonably priced.
 
 A couple more things that set  3rd and Lindsley apart from other venues around Nashville are parking is usually always free and almost all of their shows are all ages which makes it more family-friendly.
Fun place!  Stopped by mid-day on a work day.  Great band.  Fast service (drinks only - didn't eat).  Nice crowd.  Nice accommodations.  We may be back tonight!

Whoever the bouncer working the door was tonight is going to end up with a boot down his throat. I hope you people know it is illegal to take someone's ID especially from someone out of state? Your meathead moron bouncer took my girlfriends ID because the idiot thought it was fake. Not everyone is from hillbilly central. The police will be contacted and charges will be made.
Such a great place tucked away in Printers Alley.  Great whiskey selection, fab jukebox and loved our bartender Amber!  Nice hideaway!

Certainly in my top 3 bars of all time. Great live music. Fun/authentic/local feel. Dirt cheap beer with dollar bills on the wall and a friendly bartender who is cracking me up. So glad I happened on this place!

Great live music on 3 floors. Right in the heart of Broadway. A line to get in but it moved quickly. Beers were expensive but seemed like comparable to the bars around it. Awesome 2nd & 3rd floor balconies with great views of Broadway.

This was my favorite meal in the four days we were in Nashville. We stopped in on Friday night because everything else was packed. The band was excellent and the food and drinks were even better!! Check out their bbq chicken and collard greens

Went here with my bros and it was an interesting place. Great atmosphere and the food was decent. The only issue is that they totally messed up our order. We received several items that we didn't order and were missing a lot of items. Service was a little slow but it's a busy place in Nashville so understandable

Welcome to Honky Tonk Central! If being in the middle of lower Broadway with a dozen honky tonks surrounding didn't feel like you were in the middle of it, this three-story mega bar is actually named Honky Tonk Central. 

Different bands and performers are playing live music on every level. Although they don't have a rooftop per se the 2nd and 3rd floors have mini European style balconies that overlook the street below. 

Tough to differentiate this bar from the dozen other honky tonks lining lower Broadway but it certainly has a fun scene!
Great live music venue, we heard a bluegrass band for a $10 cover. They only have beer (no wine or liquor) fair warning

We stopped in here for a beer and a bite and were surprised at the quality of food. We had the hot chicken sandwich and a house salad. I usually don't order a salad at a bar, but the vegetables were crisp and nicely presented. The chicken sandwich was fresh and HOT! It should have come with a warning! So good!

TBC is a great addition to Nashville's nightlife! A mix of dance club and lounge bar, it seems to have everything you might want for a good night out, including an outdoor patio with fire pit. There's no cover, which is a huge plus, and the staff/bouncers have always been polite. 

I've never been here for an actual show, although I've seen the DJ play some tunes and play videos on the large screen. There's also random couches on stage and apparently it's perfectly fine to sit on them while everyone is staring from on the floor. Music can be a hit or miss at times, but when it's good, you know everyone will be dancing!

Really fresh chicken! We had no trouble getting a table on a Thursday night, our server was Morgan and she was really nice. 
Kitchen forgot tomato on one burger but she took care of that right away.
They have some pre made slushy drinks and I tried one wich was ok but not awesome. I think my problem with it was that they used some vodka I didn't like but if you are not super picky (like me) you might really like it.

The thing with "build your own hamburger" worked out really good for all of our burger eaters. They where super happy. I would go back any day for my buffalo chicken fingers. Also appreciate that you get a bunch of sauce!

A fun place to eat, drink, and listen to music. Different live bands on every floor. Tables are far enough apart you're not sitting other people's laps. Food is typical bar food, but a bit better than most. Drink prices reasonable. Servers super friendly. Music a little too loud, but that's probably just me.

I had a hot chicken salad for $5 98 soecial and it was absolutely awesome! Arugula, blueberries, strawberries, more -  complemented the hot chicken perfectly. Sat on the rooftop bar w a cold beer overlooking downtown Nashville. We could hear the music from all the honky tonks carrying on the wind. Cheap and fabulous!
This place was fun!  We were here celebrating a friends 40th bday!  The band was super fun and they sounded great :)). We were drinking heavily and interacted with them quite a bit haha ;)--

I spent more time in this bar than I'd like to admit.  The bands were all pretty good on the first and second floors.  Beer was reasonably priced. It was constantly very loud and very full of very drunk people.   Definitely a dive bar scene.

3.5

I was torn between a 3 or 4 star for this venue. I went to my first show at the War Memorial Auditorium on a Sunday for the Conan & Friends tour. I LOVE Conan so I was on the website buying the tickets the minute the pre-sale started. We carefully picked our seats and thought we had the perfect spot. After paying for the tickets online, they were emailed to us and we just had to print them off. 

Finally the night came to go see my beloved Conan. We followed the directions on the WMA website and found the free parking they suggested. It's Capital Hill Center parking and is free after 6 pm. There were plenty of spots and it's only about a block down from the venue. The show started at 8 pm and we arrived around 7:30. The line was out the door and wrapped around a bit. However, the line went quickly and they had Conan Brand Reps walking around and handing out pins. Gotta love free stuff! When we got to the front, a security guard checked my purse and did the wand scan thingy. A lady then scanned our tickets and directed us to our seats. We wanted to use the restroom before the show started so we followed the signs to the basement. This was the first negative. There are only one set of bathrooms and they are in the basement. If you are seated in the balcony, it's kind of a long trip. There was a small bar down by the restrooms so we decided to grab our drinks here. They had a decent selection of beer and mixed drinks. I was able to get a tall boy IPA for $8. Not bad. We headed back upstairs to find our seats. Another negative I noticed. When you first walk in, the main bar is right to the left. There isn't a lot of room and when the line gets backed up, it's hard to move around. The front area gets crowded fast so you find yourself pushing your way through the crowd and lines. I wanted to check out some of the merchandise but didn't want to go through the sea of people again. Our seats were in the balcony and were easy to find. Up some stairs and to the left. We were on the left side of the stage in the middle row right in front of the stage (if that makes sense). We had the perfect angle to see the performers, or so we thought. The auditorium is older so the seats are old theater seats. They were comfortable enough and I think the stage is visible from all seats in the balcony. I did notice the floor seats were just padded chairs they put out for events. I understand why they need to do this but I know those seats were not cheap. I could see people being disappointed by this. We were lucky enough to have the row in front us stay empty. This gave us a very clear view of the front of the stage. The show started and everything was good. We could see Conan, the sound was good, and of course the show was hilarious. The big problem came when one of the comedians performed and his show was based off of a powerpoint. On the back wall of the stage, there was a big screen. At our angle, the big screen was completely blocked by the huge speakers they have hanging from the ceiling. Everyone around us craned their necks trying to see what was on the screen. Without any visuals, we couldn't understand his jokes and missed out on an entire set. I also felt bad for the comedian because no one in our section or the section across could laugh at his jokes. While our tickets were not the most expensive, they also weren't cheap. Next time I will choose a center seat in the balcony, even though that would put me farther away from the stage. If I didn't need to see the screen, the seats would have been perfect.

While I listed some negatives, I rounded up to 4 stars because I know it's an old building (built in 1925) and I'm against tearing places like this down to build new shiny ones. The architecture is beautiful and you can feel the history of the auditorium. I liked the fact that this venue has seating because I get so annoyed with standing in GA crowds. While it's not my favorite venue in Nashville, I would go back for a performer I really liked.

I went to the Underground for an office holiday party. As a vegetarian, the only thing I ate here (or all day) was their truffle Mac and Cheese. I got a horrible case of food poisoning and ended up in the ER.  Even worse, when I tried to contact the restaurant (three different people), not one returned my call or emails. I won't go there again and I let the party organizer know also so they don't plan any more parties there. I would avoid it at all costs. Or if you do go, avoid the Mac and Cheese.

We made a reservation for 7pm on a Friday. When we checked in, the hostess said to go to the 2nd floor because it was "less crowded" with no direction on seating. The 2nd floor didn't have tables, so we went back downstairs. There was no one at the hostess stand, so at this point, it was a free for all. Don't bother making a reservation, because it doesn't mean anything at this place. It took 20 minutes to get a waitress, and the food was just okay. 

The only reason I'm giving 3 stars is because the band was good.

$12 for a cover in Nashville may seem like a lot considering every bar seems to have live music but this place was so worth it. I've seen big name musicians live who couldn't hold a dime to the band that played last night. They were so insanely talented. I was absolutely blown away. This place is the reason Nashville is music city. Only bummer is that it's cash only and they don't serve liquor. Otherwise if you're coming to town you need to go here!
Me and the fam came here for a weekend trip, had a blast.  The blue grass music was great.  Drank some good beer what else can you ask for.

The food is okay, but you're in here for over an hour and won't get food despite the fact that the entire place is empty. Just get street food. Quicker and probably better. We wish we got McDonald's. Wouldn't have killed the vibe.

A quick in and out drink. Tried to hit up all the bars on the block for a drink at least. If it was good we stayed. Had one drink and listened a bit and moved on. Nothing horrible but nothing special either. Was nice that they had the windows open. VERY small bathrooms.

The first 10minutes sucked. We sat at the bar. Waited. Waited some more. Watched what seemed to be the lone bartender struggle to service her customers at one end of the massive bar. (If she was our bartender we likely would have left.) Then came along Austin; a great guy, who provided great service to our group for the next 3 hours. He kept the drinks flowing and was genuinely personable. Even the other bartender/server (didn't catch his name) was helpful - he provided us with recommendations on where to get tattoos without getting ripped off by local parlors taking advantage of tourists. 
Other than the service; I like the "lounge" decor of this place. Over 7 years, we haven't been to a bar in Nashville quite like this one. 
As far as the entertainment; in all fairness, we were here during the day on a Thursday so I wasn't really expecting a 5 piece band. However the duet that performed provided good background music. Nothing particularly unique about the guys who performed.
The one thing I thought was very odd: the bathroom on the main floor. Single occupancy. Uh. This wasn't a big deal on a Thursday afternoon but I can only imagine the problems this would cause during peak hours on a Friday or Saturday night.
Overall, I say give this place a try. We'll be coming back, and we hope to have as great a time as was had during our first visit.

Totally agree with Johnny T - this place is a mashup of South Beach meets NYC in Nashville. Modern art in a repurposed warehouse done surprisingly well. It's a little hidden - right behind 5th and taylor

Went on a Saturday night
Pros:
Late 20s were the majority
Great Live DJ 
Swanky atmosphere
No cover
Good looking crowd before it emptied out
Mixed ethnicities - globalism in full effect

Cons:
30 minute wait to get in since it was "near capacity" - PTSD of NYC's meatpacking district began to kick in
Ran out of beer - no tap, just a small mini fridge
One to two bartenders at peak hours
Bar is oddly designed - inefficient and awkwardly located
No dress code
Music system could use some work
Friendly wait staff and bartenders. Great off the beaten path location if you're looking to get away from Broadway. Drinks were reasonable and friendly environment
I was there last December and had a great time. Good live music, good crowd. I'll be back next time I'm in town!

Loved the fact that this was a three story bar.
The third floor has little balcony that you can look up and down broadway.

All three stars are for The Time Hoppers: they're awesome! It's a great way to spend Monday night in Nashville. Better to attend the show thirsty instead of hungry... the beer is cold and the food is terrible. Also probably safest to stick to beer; the table next to me sent back two mixed drinks!

A "MUST" when visiting The Music City. Sunday night bluegrass jam session was a load of fun. Microwave nachos and cheap beer topped off a night off free-ballin' finger-pickin'. Jam 'starts' at 9; get here early to get good seats (730).

My daughter and I went to the Niall Horan concert last night. It was a great night! Weather was perfect for an outdoor concert. The show was sold out. A worker said she had never seen it so crowded. The staff handled the crowd perfect. We did not have to wait long to get in and the line was crazy long. We also were given the option to pay $10/ticket to enter through the fast lane. We did take advantage of this option. The staff helped us find our seat and was super friendly. Great experience!
The bartenders are wonderful but the band stopped at 10:00pm the bar stays open longer. I would have stayed later if the band had played longer.

The worst service ever.  Walked at 5pm and only two others in the bar. Bar tender did greet us a warm welcome. The waitress was dressed terrible ripped  holes in her stockings. She got us our water right away. Then sat down at the bar with her phone.  We tried to get her attention several times with no luck. Walked out.

I like the music and the option to move around and the bands I heard were all good. The food was alright, bar food, nothing special. I ordered a Michelob and a Jack and Coke and it was $17. I imagine they must split profits with the bands to be charging that much but still seems high to me. I'm not sure I would come back.
Food was decent but took way too long for food to arrive at lunch with a small crowd. We then made the mistake of ordering dessert which took a half hour to come out.

Oh Nashville, you country music loving bunch of people.  This bar is loud, rowdy with goofball college kids, and there are three floors of it.  They have a balcony for drunk party goers to hang off and shout obscenities down at the people passing by on the street.

This mixture is everything I dislike in a bar.

However it's a place you have to go when your in Nashville.

After 5 or 6 shows here Ascend has solidified its place in my mind as a top venue in Nashville. Nestled up against the Cumberland you will be treated to beautiful views of the river and the sun setting behind the stage. Excellent premier acts regularly book the venue, taking the opportunity to play a festival like atmosphere and making the general admission lawn seats one of the best entertainment deals in Nashville. The sound is clear and not spoiled by the surrounding traffic like you would fear and the sight lines are excellent if a little long from the very back. Restrooms are large and easy to get to. Pro-tip: the ones in the very back at the top of the the hill tend to be less crowded in my experience. 
Beer and food are comparable with other places which is to say expensive. Expect 12 to 16 bucks for a 16 to 24 ounce can of beer. Entrance and security are not too terrible but avoid bringing large bags. If your on the the lawn I'd recommend a blanket for sitting between sets, but you should expect to be standing while the band is on stage if you want to see. You can also bring a small beach chair or rent them at the venue for a pretty reasonable fee. Parking at Nissan stadium is the way to go if no other major events are happening as you can pretty easily hoof it across the veterans bridge and drop right in to the venue avoiding the downtown traffic doomcluster. Overall I'm always inclined to grab tickets to an Ascend event. Metro really did a nice job creating this venue and giving us another great location for shows.
Absolutely loved the girl on stage and the bartenders. We wandered to here new to Nashville and after a drink at Benchmark we left but ended up back there. Just the comfy home feel was awesome.

Staff was good, band was good, chicken nachos and chicken nacho sandwich was not. Also tipped 10 dollars to band asking for requests and never had the song performed. Go for the drinks and atmosphere but I'd definitely skip those food items.

Spent the majority of our downtown time here on a bachelor party the other weekend. Good barfood (especially the tots) and friendly service. Good bands and a wild good time in a great location with terrific views of Broadway.  Don't worry about the line it moves fast but plan on a few minutes in the bathroom line if you are there on a weekend night! Hope to make a return to this great place.

I love concerts at Ascend. After the Ryman, it's my favorite music venue. I love that it's outdoors and that the set up is very accommodating. The way it's designed allows for good views from pretty much anywhere you are on the lawn and in the chairs. It's also pretty affordable and they have a good selection of food and drinks. Of note, there is usually a taco truck or some food truck on the far side of the venue so if you don't want stadium food there are other options, you just have to look for them.

Im sad to know I'm giving 2 stars, but honestly I've had & is Way more places with better food. We ordered calamari, marinated grill chicken and shrimp and grits and boy o boy when the food came  she originally said to us " ooo don't touch the calamari because it's hot" since my baby was already digging in, I had expected it o be hot. As she left I reached in for a calamari and honestly if You want a Soggy, Cold, Bad batter Calamari then go right ahead. My husband and I didn't enjoy it at all and we never finished it. 
Secondly I'm someone who don't eat Pork at all, & while reading the menu I didn't see that the Shrimp and grips had 'pork' and as I started eating the grits was too SOUR , I don't know why and then finally I bite into something weird and just not a taste that I'm use to. So I go look at the menu online to read that's in it again the. Asked her " hey is this sausage Pork? " & her reply to me was " I don't know, but for you I can say Beef ".  I was really bothered by that response because I especially am bother I ate pork when I Don't eat that in my life! and she didn't even offer to go FIND OUT or take it off the tab since I BEARLY ATE ANYTHING! but I will Never go there again. 
And Lastly, the ONLY Thing I could say was good was the Fries.
Great bar and really cool atmosphere. One of my favorite local scenes. The service was outstanding. Good drinks and good eats. Highly recommended for late nights!!!!

I and three others, out of a group of 6 friends who ate at Benchmark last week, fell ill after eating at Benchmark B&G. The only thing in common to the four who suffered abdominal distress was the bar food we ate there. This included the chicken wings and the cheesy nachos as well as the fried pickles. We were all laid up within a few hours and for most of the next day as the bad food worked its way through our systems. The wings were delivered hot on the outside and cold on the inside and were not finished because we weren't sure they were cooked but before we returned them, a cockroach crawled across the wing basket as we sat at the bar. The bartender quickly removed the food and comped the food tab. The nacho cheese was a strange milky consistency that had little to do with cheese. Not sure which of these three were the culprit but stick to the beer and wine if you don't want to lose some weight. Music and staff were good.
Close to down town. Parking can be rough if you don't know that 100 feet away they have a free lot. Great bands. Above average bar food. Friendly staff. No bad seat.

I've always wanted to visit, and it was 100% worth it! Get there a half hour before the show starts to get a good seat and a drink without waiting in line. We saw Larry Cordle and it was an awesome show- an intimate venue with great sound, a casual and laid back atmosphere, and good bar service. A must-see for bluegrass and country fans.

I feel honored to have stepped foot in here. We tried the last time we were in town but were unaware of the fill up policy and came too little, too late. We got there nice and early this time and enjoyed some great blue grass with some fun surprise appearances. Get your pitchers of light beer and your frozen pizzas early and sit back for a great show.
Visited Nashville and went here, don't be turned off by the name - had non-Honky Tonk music and good variety. Drinks are a bit steep ($18 for cheap wine and cider.)

If there's one word to describe Honky Tonk Central, it's probably "consistent".

During the "winter storm" of 2015, it was the only place consistently open every day. There was always great live music (mostly acoustic when the sun was out). The bartenders are nice.

I had to eat lunch here out of necessity, and it was surprisingly decent for bar food. The fried catfish basket was a lot of food, and was nice and flakey. I also substituted the fries for onion rings.

They had a problem with beer delivery due to the weather - they only had Yazoo Dos Perros, but that's not a problem because Dos Perros is delicious.

Sadly, I was unable to attend one of the crazy nights here because they never opened up the second and third floors again after the storm while I was there.

So basically, to me, it was a low-key, family-friendly music bar with acceptable food. Which I guess is not everyone's experience with the place.

Good music, but sub par food. Tater tots and onion rings tasted good, but the burgers were very ordinary, and none of the food items were hot or even warmed up. I'm rating this place 3 stars only because it has live music on all the 3 floors of the bar, with a nice view of the intersection from the balcony, which is great for people watching. Good for music and drinks, but not food. Not too bad on the price.

We happened upon this restaurant on a sunny 60 degree day in January and everyone was so welcoming! Suggested we look at rooftop dining so we did and enjoyed the beautiful river view and delicious diverse menu. Will go back for sure!
Probably my favorite new dance spot in Nashville. I have been searching for a venue with an amazing DJ and cocktails. You will find both here

The Good:
1) Great Dive bar for music.
The Bad
1) A/C I found inadequate when I visited. 
2l There is only beer available nothing else, no wine no liquor.

I would go for the music, otherwise I would head elsewhere.

I had never been "honkey tonkin" until last night and this was our first stop. And, of course, we made our way to the bathroom first( once you get a seat you don't want to loose it--or, so I've been told).

One we were finished with that unique experience (there were empty and half filled bottles in the stalls--bad decisions evident) we made our way out to find a stool or table so we could or elder and listen to the music. 

We found a few stools by the bar and grabbed them quickly and ordered a few drinks. My friend asked for something with Vodka or Tequila and something else that was sweet and fruity--what she got tasted like fruit punch and sadness (the sadness is because I don't appreciate vodka).

We moved from the bar to a table shortly after finishing our drinks (which we now know was a bad decision-the beginning of the end). Leaving our proof of purchase (and sitting rights) behind we were shortly informed by one of the table staff that we had to leave if we were going to order anything (in a not so friendly manner). So we did.

The music was good but a little forced (they had to ask for a few minutes to make the money to play "the Devil Went Down to Georgia" after they said it was their most requested song) 

In all, I'm glad that I experienced it once.

If you are looking for non-touristy, Nashville music, this is the place! The Sunday night Bluegrass Jam was recommend to me by the staff at the hostel I was staying in and I am so happy I decided to check it out. 

Coming off Broadway, this was a totally different and more authentic Nashville experience. The atmosphere was very cool in that everyone sits together at long tables to listen to the music. I liked how people came on and off of the stage as they pleased to play their instruments. 

I will say, I had not eaten dinner before coming to this venue and the food is not good. Do not come here to eat, but if you're looking for great music, this is the place.
This establishment is fails to accommodate  for its crowd. I regret wasting my money here. They have no accommodations for men

After being in Nashville a few days we stopped by Nashville Underground for dinner. It was the best we had had! A few of the other places only had sandwiches so it was a great to have a full menu of choices and it was delicious. Great live music too!

It was one of the more packed bars in the area but my review is mainly for their huge order of nachos which is good and filling. Can definitely feed at least two people. We were able to find a spot at one of the tables and were worried we wouldn't catch a waiter but we actually got one pretty quickly. Make sure to make eye contact with the waiter otherwise they will probably not come by.
The lively music and cheap beer made this the perfect end to our trip. A must do when you come to Nashville!

Great music, but my take away at the end of the night was just how BAD the service was. We got a couple drinks during the opener, but she disappeared during the main act. Everyone in the section was looking around wondering where she went. She forgot our beers twice, and lost my card! Do not give them your card! The few times she did come by, she purposely tried to rush passed our table. I literally had to yell "excuse me!" loud enough to be heard over the band. It really wrecked the night and distracted from the band that I paid to see.
This place is awesome! Stephanie makes the BEST drinks and had the personality to match. 12/10 recommend!!

Amazing Xmas night eve with excellent live music. The other 2 floors were closed for the night but fortunately the ground floor left us satisfied.
They have a good choice of beers too(locally brewed) and other lagers -Coronas and Buss etc..
Will return for sure to enjoy the live music.
Alex is the best waiter.  Super busy on Labor Day weekend but he took care of us!!!!  Go and see him for best service in town.

Another ginormous venue on the lower end of Broadway with 5 floors and a rooftop. It even has a lighted dance floor on the 5th floor. The only thing is the restrooms are on the 2nd floor, so if you're on the main floor (1st) gotta go up a flight of stairs or take a slow moving elevator. They serve food too. We were there for a company event with a pre-fixed menu. I opted for the hot chicken - how can I resist? Food was delicious, or actually the hot chicken was delicious but the cole slaw tasted like a came out of a bucket sitting in a refrigerator all day. Needless to say their version of the hot chicken made up for it. The menu also had baby back ribs, and I had a taste of one and there were really good and tender. NU also serves local beer and had a chance to sample quite a few variations. We went on a Tuesday night, and it wasn't full but had a decent crowd, but I can only imagine how packed it gets on the weekends.
Not the friendliest place. As a local, this is one of the worst bars to visit. The staff isn't very friendly and they could care less for quality or hospitality. Good luck getting a drink.

Horrible horrible customer service, waitstaff and music. Brittany is the worst waitress have ever encountered, along with bar management and security. If you are looking to be charged for drinks you did not order, and then be forced to pay for them or leave, you have found the spot. Do not come here, there are so many other great places to go do not waste your time. Brittany- you are better fit for McDonalds.
much more beautiful in person!!! The employees are all so friendly and helpful and certainly know how to make a first concert smooth and memorable!

Went here on a Friday night.  It's three levels with three different bands and bars so plenty of space for you to find somewhere you like.  The bands were all good, though some of the crowd was definitely on the very young side.  A solid stop if you're just looking for some live music and drinks in a larger bar setting.

Terrible food and bad service, we had a group reservation and ordered at the same time. Entrees all came out at different times, one super late, and were really terrible. I wouldn't recommend this place.
Went here a couple times during our stay in Nashville, and it's a good little dive bar. Good music, quick service, and decent prices.

I'd skip this spot because of the food and entertainment. We couldn't get a reservation for 13 people last minute and the Nashville Underground was able to accommodate us at a table front and center of the stage. Should have been sign #1 that maybe this place wasn't going to be the greatest. It was a Sunday night around 7 and we were starving after doing the pedal tour all day. The menu itself is just straight up unhealthy, very difficult to order anything health conscious. We ordered the meatballs, calamari, house made chicken tenders and wings for the table. The appetizers weren't terrible in flavor, just bad for you and salty. 

Not sure what I was thinking but I  ordered the pork chops for my entree and the meal was the saltiest meal I've ever had in my entire life. The mashed potatoes were inedible because of how much salt was in them so I was unable to eat the rest of the meal. Others felt similarly about the food in that it just wasn't good. Word on the street was that the mac and cheese was good. Our server was nice but the entertainment was lacking. Most of the time they weren't playing and it was just an empty stage. Maybe we came here at the wrong time of day but it wasn't an upbeat vibe like you'd expect from a bar on Broadway in Nashville.

Good ol' Honky Tonk. You really know how to get the party started.

This place pulls in $20 tip song requests and gets the crowd doing a sing along like no other bar on this strip. And I'm talking all the hits you probably want to hear on your trip to Nash like Wagon Wheel, Shania Twain, etc.

The space can get really crowded and and the drinks aren't as generous as elsewhere, but you're coming for the vibe of the place which is just FUN. Enjoy it!! :)

The pretzel and wings were freaking amazing. Never sure what you are gonna get for bar food but this was a sweet surprise. The name is on point, the place is quite literally down a dark back alley. We were very happy with this little hole in the wall type bar. They have live music and a full bar. Definitely a stop to make in this town!

Music was good. Food was ok. Price was too much and the entire ordeal took forever. Literally took 15 minutes to get us the check after we asked for it, and the place was not even that busy. Super lame, the rest of the strip has more to offer.

If I could give this place 0stars I would DO NOT GO HERE staff is aggressively rude and will arrest you if you attempt to have fun in their bar... rly weird and embarrassing TRUST ME DO NOT GO manager has a tiny tiny pr*ck and takes it out on everyone around him

It is the unpretentious (I was here first) underbelly of The Gulch, and the gulch is better  for it.  Hope you like beer (thats all they serve) and food only for those that are really hungry, this place is music city.  Forget the glam and pomp of the Ryman or Bluebird, a piece of Nashvilles musical soul resides within these walls.  Need I say more?
Samantha and Tyler killed it!  Ambiance is great and drinks are strong! Who doesn't like a good strong drink! Definitely a must in Nashville

Our experience in a nutshell: good food, fun atmosphere, lousy service.
Comfortable fun seating. Very few people in the bar area and lots of staff. Not even remotely busy. Still took a while for any server to come to us. We ordered drinks, they asked if we wanted food. We said yes, we were nearly ready, just one minute to think. Fifteen minutes later she still had never returned, despite having walked up and down the main area multiple times and never even glancing over as I was trying to get her attention. Finally I had to walk up to the bar and ask her to take our order. After the food came (the nachos with pulled pork which were quite delicious and flavorful) we asked for some silverware. There were two us, just my wife and me. The server brought one set of silverware. Huh?? What kind of idiot brings one set of silverware with a napkin to a table with two people??  My wife and I just kind of stared dumbfounded at each other.  We wondered if she was just high or something. Yeeesshh. We'd still recommend this place for food, music and atmosphere. But, they need serious attention to service.

I ordered the BBQ chicken which was described as bone in on the menu. They brought me out the pulled pork, I told the food runner I ordered the BBQ chicken and he tried to tell me that the pulled pork was bbq chicken???? I sent it back. They finally bring me out the Bbq chicken and it's ICE COLD. We were probably one of 5 tables in the restaurant. Server was extremely un-attentive. Only recommend if you're going for drinks.

Awesome venue with great music on a Monday night. Arrive early (doors open at 530) for a most pleasurable musical evening with the time jumpers (with Vince Gill) for a mere $20 they played gem after gem for 2 hours. Had a blast and the servers were amazing as well. Definitely want to come back next time I'm in the area.

When in "Music City USA" what better thing to do than hear some good music! 
This concert by Vinyl Radio was SO MUCH FUN!! 
Got there early to get seats...this place has a bar and a pretty good selection of bar food.  It's a small space so seating is at a premium! 
We ordered some beer and nachos that turned out to be acceptable, not up to what I'm used to in South Texas, but this IS Nashville after all! 
Once the band started, things got serious....seriously fun! Great cover band doing music from the 70's and 80's. 
What a crazy night....remembering those good ole days!!

Awesome new venue for music! I was here last weekend to see Lake Street Dive and Grace Potter perform, and the experience was great. There's standing room in the front, ticketed lawn seating in the middle, and standing room and tables at the very back. Acoustics are great. Apparently there's been some complaints about the noise from nearby residents--I guess that's the price you pay for living in the middle of Music City.
We had a great time on the second floor with Ashley and Angie. They rocked and the vibe was perfect!

Horrible.  It's not even worth my time to explain.   Nice rooftop views, but there's idiotic and incompetent management/bartenders running the place.  You have to try really hard to screw up a venue like this in one of the most prime pieces of real estate in downtown Nashville.

So if you want country music I would suggest not to go here. There music is astronomically loud and food was a disaster. My husband ordered the pulled pork and it came out cold and with hunks of fat in it. 1 thing that was a plus our server was very sweet. Doesn't help though after they tell you that they don't take reservations that you had made online and there is open seating....

Great rooftop bar for a drink! They have a flight of stairs to hike up or an elevator to the top. Great views at the top. Ordered the saloon blt, gumbo soup, and chicken nachos. Awesome food. The top overlooks the stadium with a great atmosphere.

Came here for Sound Tribe concert and did it rock. The house was full but the line kept moving fast outside to get in, the only bad thing here was the bar which had such long lines that the wait was forever and they ran out of water bottles.

Sound - was pretty good and balanced not as great as tpac or rymon but on part to them.
Staff - was great and courteous but that all depends on the kind of concert and crowd you are expecting.

Overall good place and parking will always be expensive around so might as well uber.
Drinks were a little overpriced for what you received but other than that, GREAT music and vibes.

This reminds me of a rustic version of a great blues / bluegrass club of yesteryear. The music was lively and original ... the crowd was older and much more mellow then Broadway. Beer was cold and popcorn was stale. Worth visiting but not worth the $15 cover imho.
Food is trash but the rooftop is nice. Bartenders can be bitchy, but they are bartenders after all.

Tourist tap in Nashville. Bartenders don't care and they know people won't stop coming.  How about a smile and acknowledgement people? Didn't eat the food was on a liquid diet. Music was good and changed thru the night.

Well this place is a Honky Tonkin' good time!

The venue itself is HUGE with something different on every floor. This place was definitely busy and a bit crowded but still had plenty of space to move around and get drinks. I found the top bar to be the most accessible. 

The vibe here is awesome. Everyone, staff included were very friendly. 
Gotta love Nashville for their love of live music. 

Drinks were great and just strong enough. 

This is one of the places I stayed at the longest and latest. 
One of ( if not my most) favorite spot on the strip. 

4.8/5

I can't believe the stupidity we  encountered, at 27 yrs old I've never Been turned away but the idiot in front " big e" pushed us away forcefully.  If you want to be assaulted and mishandled then  this is the place to be.  "Big e" assured that 12 of us would not be visiting honkey tonk central again,  tootsies is the place to be.

I can't stress enough the improper treatment of large groups by the honkey tonk central
Employees especially "big e":  it is exceptionally inappropriate the treatment myself and my family endured at the hands of the honky took central team.

There is a light up dance floor on the 4th floor which is cool. However, there are tons of security that are watching you like hawks and will not let you Juul/vape. The music was not that great.. very overrated

If I could give this place a zero I would.  We made a reservation and were there to watch the SEC tournament games.  50 people in our party.  Had no waitress period.  Had to go to bar individually to order.  Stood in line every time for 20-30 minutes trying to order.  Was told they closed kitchen for orders and couldn't place an order for 30 minutes.  An hour later still not able to even place an order.  Once we were told we could place orders again, we had to stand in line to do so at the bar.  Stood in line another 30 minutes.  Waited an hour longer before food came out.  Were told they ran out of beer.  Totally not prepared for us.  We would have left if we were able to.  HORRIBLE!!!

I have been to amphitheaters all over the US and while Ascend Amphitheater is not in beautiful scenery, it is very well done and I am thrilled to have it so close! It is right there in downtown Nashville and small enough to make every seat a treat! It also made it quick and easy to get an uber ride to and from the venue which no doubt was the cost or less than parking.
We went to see Kings of Leon and had seats towards the back which made for quick access to the bathrooms and beer carts but one look at the lawn and I wouldn't have minded it either. Very nice looking lawn that was sloped only enough to make viewing good for all and not a dangerous slope as we have experienced at other amphitheaters. Seats were padded & comfortable with enough leg room that exiting the row was not a bother to those you had to pass. Right behind us they had tables and chairs which we will look into our next show there, very nice to sit at a table and have a plce to set your drink. (only complaint about our seating was no place for a drink other than the ground)
We will return as often as possible! Ascend is a wonderful venue that makes a concert feel almost intimate.

Good music. Had fun until.... Security staff are assholes!!!! We got kicked out after being got told once to get once off the bar stool once. Which I understood and got off. We spent over a couple hundred bucks in there. Fuck those stupid big headed security dike bitches! Assholes!!!!!!!!!!! We weren't out of line. Respect they need to learn the word. BT you need to check your staff!!!!!

We popped in here to grab a Pineapple Mimosa advertised on the board on the sidewalk. It's off Broadway so a little calmer area but a lovely street indeed. It's super nice with an epic bar that stretches back to the stage and another bar in the back closer to the river. It's not like some of those rather *rustic* bars on Broadway, this area just seems a bit *ahem* "cleaner". It's really nice in here and the staff was extremely gracious and friendly. Great selection of Craft Beers, Domestics, Imported, Mixed Drinks and the Pineapple Mimosa was fantastic. We both wanted another but we had only and few minutes to reach our Trolley stop. This place really has the charm and touch of class of Country past. Certainly worth a look and if you have time, plan on staying a while.
Horrible service and attitude from staff.  This is a bar, not a restaurant. I'm absolutely shocked that anyone gave over 2 stars.

Awesome venue! There truly is not a bad seat in the house. I love going to see shows there. Their Nashville Sunday night is super fun to go to! The food is pretty good and the waiting staff is real quick and attentive considering how large and crowded it can get in there! If you get a chance to see a show here do it!!!

Just a response note to P.R. To say that servers are not supposed to serve someone without their us government issued id. It will provide you with all that information as well. Here' a a link you can check for yourself . I adore these kinds of small, unpretentious music spots. As others have said, the emphasis here is on the music. The show starts at 9pm, which is a little late for me. I arrived about 8:40, the place was empty, but it became pretty respectably filled by 9:30 or so. The bar serves beer and cider only, with a few basic snack foods. The walls are covered with music posters, the atmosphere is laid-back. Cover on a Wed night was $12, beers $4 or $5.

I saw a great show with Jordan Tice, sat right up front. What more can you ask for?
Great place to go if you're from out of town.  You can feel the Nashville vibes!

I have been here multiple times for drinks and music only.   Never tried any of the food.    They always have great bands playing and service at the bar has been fast and friendly.   Great balcony areas to people watch.

Really wanted to like this bar.  Came in during a weekend when the NCAA basketball conference tournaments were going on and we spent hours there wanting to watch a particular conference tournament while also watching other games that were on.  For some reason, even though there were like 30 TVs in the restaurant, they weren't willing to turn one to to another channel so we could watch a couple of the other games.  The food was mediocre at best and I was willing to overlook that if we could stay and drink and watch the games we wanted, but overall a terrible experience.  We love Nashville but there are about a hundred other restaurants we'd go to over this one.  Not worth the time or the money.

Wise! 

Zeota Road! If lucky to hear them here: consider yourself blessed ~~

SetUp: 2 beauty gals with madTalent + fiddle from SouthDakota (!?!) now, killing it. 

brother crushing it too on all the guitars (Parachute and GBrooks - calling Baton Rouge) -- they pulled in one of bestBESTbackup guitarist: Jay! Really killing it for all ages and such.... Feel lucky to have heard 'em here first...
Always a long wait and I had a rude bartender on the first floor. Music is good on every floor but service is better upstairs.
Good venue for a fun concert. The refreshment prices are way over the top expensive!  $7.50 for a bottle of water? Are you kidding me!?!
The Chicken N Waffles are so good here. Music is good, beer is cold, friendly wait staff.
Atmosphere is great. Service was okay. Drinks are way over priced. The hot chicken is ignorant hot. The chicken and biscuits was bland and rubbery.
Friendly service. Food was good. Music was great. Only request would be to turn it down. Would be even better if not so loud.
Food was good, better than most for bar food. They were short servers but told us right away so we ordered from the bar. Fun place, good food for a casual night in Nashville

With mixed emotions, we have to give this place five stars, and would have given six if that was an option. Our dilemma is that we really do not want everyone else to know about this place. We selfishly want to keep it to ourselves. You see, what makes this place so perfect is that it already has the best clientele, best staff, and best vibe. 

If you are looking for a touristy "honky-tonk" experience, there are plenty of downtown options for you. If your idea of bar food includes things like a $25 bowl of squid ink infused gluten free ramen, there are plenty of options for you in the Gulch. If you want to swill $6 drafts while your senses are assaulted by a shockingly loud and untalented house band, Soulshine Pizza is just the spot for you.  

All kidding aside (mostly),if you want to grab a few beers in a low-key, safe, friendly little bar where a guitar is routinely passed around so that the patrons can sing a tune, this is your spot. The crowd here is eclectic and warm. Just don't tell anyone else, OK?
Merry thank goodness you guys have been fun Erin tthank morning I hope was love u I you have to do get be w

Extremely disappointed that I called for a reservation at 1:00 and was told no problem.  Arrived at 6:15 for our 6:30 table and was told by waitress that someone took the reserved sign off the table.  Manager Teddy offered to give us a table downstairs with the live music, but our reservation was for the 2nd floor college football section.  Game was on one TV downstairs and super loud music playing!!!  Others came in and got a table but they would not honor our reservation! Worst of all, this went on for an hour!  Not a business I will return to!!!

My favorite bar on the Broadway strip.  There was country music live downstairs with a great rooftop. The rooftop overlooks the river and they played current hits and hip hop. So if want a little different feel from the honky tonk hit the roof at Famous Saloon.

For fans of outdoor venues this is a beautiful backdrop along the river. Definitely one to plan to arrive early and soak up the sunset before the show. Take advantage of the food trucks because the food in venue is pricey and tends to be at front of venue. One weird thing is you can't lean against the wall along the walkway. There is a phone charging station and we were leaning against the wall waiting for phone and had to stand up. Trust me, it is like an alarm goes off as soon as you touch it. Funny but didn't ruin an evening just different. The sound was great and the walk over bridge from the parking at stadium saved us time missing a lot of traffic after the show. We were driving back to hotel and heading north. One thing to note is food is scarce after 9 on weekdays and construction makes the evening drive a pain heading north.

The entertainment was fantastic. I really  enjoyed the show but the door man was quite rude. I was told to stop talking to my wife as if I were distracting others. Though I  asked those around us after the show if I were being disruptive or disrespectful and nobody said  i was. Being told to stop talking quietly to my wife was definitely a  mood killer. I was having a  great time  until then. Will not be back.
I love this Packers bar. No better place to watch a Green Bay game in TN! Try the chicken bacon quesadilla for a good hearty southern meal

Off-Broadway!

We liked what we heard as we were walking by, so we went in. Luke Lander was singing, and we stayed for a couple of hours. We really enjoyed his music. 

Beer was colder and more reasonably priced than at honky tonks on Broadway. We had eaten at Pucketts, so food was not an option; however, several others were eating and their food looked good.
Yummy fries and chicken! Great atmosphere! Roof top is a nice spot to look down on Broadway! We tried it night before NFL draft so service was spotty but overall it was great!

I've been to outdoor venues like this in a few different cities around the country, and I enjoyed my time here. 

As per usual with venues like Ascend, I had lawn seats, and I was happy to find that there seemed to be a pretty good view of the stage from basically anywhere on the lawn. We chose to sit up toward the front of the lawn anyway, to avoid being blocked by the inevitable tall person who would find their way in front of us. 

More importantly though, the sound. The sound here was surprisingly great. I think because it's a relatively small outdoor venue, as far as they go (6,800 capacity) the sound was really, really good. The bass was punchy, and everything else was really well balanced. 

Food and drink prices, however, are astoundingly, out-of-this-world ridiculous. $12.50 for a Bud tallboy? You have got to be kidding me. $10 for a lemonade and a pretzel? Come on now. Why do places like this do that? I already paid $100 (2 tickets at $50 each) to sit on the lawn. What is this, a Yankees game? Thankfully, you can bring in your own snacks and beverages.

One last thing, I wish that the "No Smoking" section was not just for the seated section. Extend that to the lawn as well. I don't understand the thinking behind that.  

Not a venue one would find themselves at all the time, but it is a very nice place for a concert.

Today we had this AMAZING waiter Kirk! This guy had so much pep in his step, managed the entire floor efficiently and was a TON of fun! He literally made everyone feel special and made the atmosphere so much fun in this Saturday afternoon.  Thanks so much for making our day so much fun. We had no intentions of staying this long, but he made it worth it! Rock that bandana! You made this day!

Don't trust the short Blonde singer.  She ripped $40 off us.  We paid to have someone in our group sing, then denied that we ever paid.  We complained to the manager, who arranged to let us sing, by that time I was  pissed off and just wanted my money back. Was told they wouldn't do it.  The place can be a lot of fun, just sucks you can't trust anyone anymore.

Was there and saw an AMAZING band. RodeoGypsy. They mentioned they were playing the next day there too so we went back...... that being said the music was where the positives stopped. Service was straight terrible. Over 30 minutes every time you ordered a drink at the table. If you went to the bar the bar tender would take your empty and then not say anything... you had to ask every time for another drink.... was just really weird.  It was like no one that worked there actually wanted to be there

A great little bar of of the overly load and crowed Broadway honk tonks. This a great little place with good service, good drinks at a fair price and you don't have to yell in the waitresses' ear to order. The entertainment was awesome, even asking for requests. This was the 1st time the two of them performed together. They did the requested songs great, unrehearsed and using their iPhones for the music and lyrics. Just waiting for her big break, the female singer will go on to become a country star someday. I think her name was Jessie and I am sure I will recognized her when she hits it big.
