We really enjoyed Honky Tonk Central. We stopped in for music and drinks. We watched a few bands on a few floors and they were all great. 

The drinks are strong and the bartenders did a great job with the big crowd on a Saturday night. 

My cousins went earlier on the day and got the hot chicken. They said it tastes really good but will light you ON FIRE it's so hot! lol. Be ware! They didn't offer different levels of hot like Haddie Bs

I went with a group of people to watch Bluegrass at the The Station Inn.  What a great experience.  Normally there is a cover charge but on this night there was not.  

As noted in other reviews, this place is a dive with an assortment of chairs in tables.  You have to find your own seats, which can be difficult.

The bar is towards the far end of the room across from where they band plays.  The service is fast and friendly--easiest to open a tab.  They do serve food like pizza--we had eaten so just had some popcorn (which fit the atmosphere well.

This night they had a Bluegrass jam that was excellent and no surprise you can hear the music really well.

The Station Inn is definitely worth a visit.

If people are showing up here for great food and fancy drinks... they're not using their Yelps correctly.

The beer was flowing, the pizza was cooking (there's something about the smell of a frozen pizza cooking...), and the tunes were carrying.  My only complaint would be that several tables around us apparently showed up for Chatty Cathy Hour.  Talk to your buds, sure, but if we had to hear about "Steve's ex-wife" from turtleneck who never once turned in the direction of the music... whew.

Once we moved closer to the jam circle (Sunday.  What a lovely thing.) we had a lovely, lovely time.  I'm looking forward to proudly hanging a framed version of the Station Inn poster I took home on my wall.
This bar has a great classy but fun vibe. Generally when I have been there is a DJ. It can get very crowded on the weekends.
I saw a lot of reviews complaining about poor service. I had nothing to complain about. I experienced great service and entertainment. The appetizers and drinks were pretty good too.

Wow so fun!! Impressed with the artists and venue all of it!! A mist do when in Nashville. Cozy venue great drinks atmosphere is wonderful! Thanks to a local couple I met at Lukes on Broadway that led us here!! Awesome!!!!

$13 for a red bull and vodka. What happened to Nashville. That's insane. This is a cool spot a little bit off of broadway but come on, Manhattan level expensive. 2lb wings were okay. Nachos okay as well.

This is the worst service I have experienced so far in Nashville, Would recommend anywherer else but here ,bartender downstairs bar obviously needs to find a new profession, visited 8-31-2019 10:50 AM

I am one to praise restaurants but I am severely disappointed. I had to ask for a side of honey mustard several times and when I went up to the bar to ask again and the bartender was beyond rude. Its a side of honey mustard, no bid deal but when treated with such disrespect, I asked for the manager. He blew it off which only made me more upset. My party of 11 dealt with similar issues.
Thank you for being the exact opposite of the establishment diagonal to you. You guys welcomed me with open arms after my racist experience at Whiskey Row. I love you guys for that

We experienced the worst service while trying to visit. The waitress was extremely rude from the moment we sat down. My friend had asked about the seasonal brews, since on the menu it states, "ask about our seasonal brews," and she got real snarky and rude saying, "she doesn't know why that's on there, it shouldn't be." My other friend tried to order an iced tea with her meal and she had to make a comment about her Long Island ice tea not being a real ice tea, it would make it taste differently, when all she wanted was a tea with her meal as well. While ordering one of my friends asked how a drink was and she stared at him and just wrote that drink down and walked off. She never checked on us to make sure we were ok, only stopped by to make rude comments. My boyfriend had a medical emergency and we were trying to leave and not disturb anyone. I hurried over to get our waitress and waited beside her while she helped another customer. She ran up to me screaming in my face that we had tried to dine and dash on her without paying. I had never even left her sight. When I got my receipt I was looking it over and the waitress again thought she had the right to get into my face and ask me what I was looking for. She tipped herself $18 on my card and $10 on my friends. This by far, was the worst service I have ever experienced. My family and I have been long time customers of the Honky Tonk Central and I don't believe we will ever return now.

My family and I stopped in for a couple beers. Upon leaving, we stopped at the restroom at which time our waitress RUDELY approached and accused us of only leaving her $9 to which we actually left her $24 on the table. After swapping a $5 from her for a $20, I returned to our table because I did not believe her. There laid our original $20. Not only was she rude our entire visit but then she tried scamming us, guess she took us Nashville first timers for idiots. Very disappointing! Will not return.

Great onion rings (bun not heated on hamburgers). Yummy drink - Purple Heart but $11. Band was good. Not a lot of people in the place at noon. When she came around with the tip jar - we put a $5 in and asked for Wagon Wheel. She promptly told us that was a $20 song?!?!?!?!

Music 
     Loud not great loud 
     If it's louder is sounds better right - nope
Cleanliness
     Not very 
     Dirty floors and tables 
Food 
     Average bar food nothing special

This was my favorite experience in Nashville!  On a Saturday afternoon, over a 2 ish hour period we listened to 4-5 songwriters sing their songs, play their instruments and tell stories.  It's dark and intimate, they do have waiters that come by taking food/drink orders.  I didn't eat or drink so I can say anything about that.  They artists are happy to sell you their albums, ask where you're from and more!  Truly a wonderful and once in a lifetime experience!
Saw a great local artist here! A little off the beaten path of Broadway but had great talent and cold drinks, what else do you need?? Tip: got a shot! They have hilarious shot glasses!!
One of our two favorite spots while visiting Nashville. We went every day at least once. Saw some good bands. Most of the servers were friendly. Food was good. It gets crowded so plan accordingly.

How do u have one bartender on for a Saturday night... Sat at the bar and waited for him to even acknowledge us. People came in after us, got served before us. Coming from the service industry, this is poor planning. Said something to the guy at the door on the way out about not even being acknowledged at the bar and he just kind of looked at us and shrugged.

Our 3rd favorite bar we visited in Nashville! This bar has your popular country tunes being played live by a kick ass band who keeps the crowd going. The bar is large and smack dab in the center. The bathrooms are a bit run down but oh well. Nachos looked tasty but we came here pretty full. The beer prices weren't the cheapest on the strip but this place has great vibes during the day, even on a Sunday!

Disappointing. Had pulled pork. The meat was cold, the coleslaw was warm. Took a loooooonnnngggg time to get order. Probably sitting around somewhere waiting to come out. Not so impressed, fatty meat with poor flavor. I went there as I was in a rush and did not have time to wait in line which is a bad sign. I would not eat there again. Maybe for a drink, maybe not. Just my impression from one visit. You may have a different experience.

This was our first stop off the plane. We got in around 10:30 and couldn't check into our hotel until 3. This place really helped us get the party started. 

Live music, fun atmosphere. Next time we're back in Nashville, we'll be back! 

For sure a new tradition!
Sweet prohibition style bar underground Nashville, 100+ yr old building and really cool. Great bar & live music venue!

BEST BAR IN NASHVILLE! This was our favorite bar while we were in town. Great music all the time, especially the lady that sings on Friday and Saturday nights. Drinks were amazing and reasonably priced. Highly recommend trying their slushies, both were very good!

We came in around 5:30 on a Friday night. We were heading somewhere else, but accidentally walked through this door and decided to stay. 
The atmosphere is pretty typical of the Nashville Broadway scene. It was pretty cool and there was a live duo playing. 
Once seated, we were each given a water and menus. After about ten minutes, a server came over and asked if we were ready to order. I requested a beer list which she produced and then left again. A while later she came back and we ordered food and drinks at the same time. 
After 13 minutes (yes, I timed it) I went to the bar to retrieve my own beer. The server was standing at the bar and I asked if the beer sitting at the bar was mine. She said yes and handed it to me. 
I ordered the shrimp and grits and it was great. My wife had chicken and waffles and she said the chicken was among the best she'd ever had. 
No one ever came by for drink refills or to ask if I wanted another beer. Also, I had to take a silverware roll from another table since there were three of us at our table and only two sets of utensils. 
As we went through our meal, I noticed something in my beer. I fished the bug out and showed it to our server. They took the beer and one entree off of our bill and apologized profusely. What sucks is that I had already drank most of the beer before I noticed. 
I don't expect much on Broadway since fine dining isn't really the reason people are there, however, everything except the food was sub-par at Nashville Underground. Maybe it is better for night life than it is for dining.

Horrible service. Went there during the late day and decided to try it again two days later at night and the staff cared more about talking to young women than letting tourists in to listen to the band. DON'T GO HERE.

The band was great!

Great BBQ burnt end's and friendly staff.   The Mgr (Teddy), goes above and beyond to service guests.

A++

I live in the flats across the street. Nothing that TBC has done is wrong. The catwalks and open floor bar are pretty cool. But after stopping by for 6-7 times in the past 6 months, I can honestly say the people who choose to come here don't know how to be chill and meet new people. 

This realization came to a head tonight when I finished up at a work party (researchers, medical people, etc.) Uber nerds who don't know how to talk to people..... yet they were way more relaxed and chill than the people at TBC every time I've been there.  It's a clique posse circle while people watching place with zero interactions outside the people you bring with you. 

If you have a small group and want to dance to club music and look at people while ignoring them, this is totally your bar.
This place is cool. Live band, affordable drinks and friendly tourists to buy me drinks, haha! :D

I have been here multiple times, day and night, in the winter and in summer. This place is a staple if you're going to visit Nashville.  They have multiple stories of bars and live bands, and it's always a fun time! The only complaints I have about this place is that it gets super crowded and the prices are a little more expensive than the average bar down there.  Overall, this is a fun place to go and hangout with your group of friends!

great rooftop bar off broadway! I was looking for a place to eat lunch that wasn't super crowded like the bars on broadway. It has great views of the river from the rooftop and played live music downstairs.  I ordered the shrimp quesadilla which was really good and had a few beers. Awesome service! I came back the next day to have a drink in the main floor bar to listen to some live music.

The bouncer with the giant beer belly (extremely over weight) has a beard and mustache (sorta heavy on the facial hair) was confiscating fake identification cards and then selling them back to the kids or to other underage people and making a lot of money. The establishment is a scheme and the drinks are way over priced. Do not waste you time there!!!

My wife and I happened to be in Nashville, for a couple of days , seeing some friends, when we decided to go The Station Inn.
We'd never been there and had no idea what to expect, and OMG, ARE WE GLAD WE WENT!!
We were blown away, by the band, STEEL WHEELS, from Virginia!!!
We are now, BIG FANS of the STATION INN AND OF THE STEEL WHEELS!!
A GREAT EXPERIENCE!!! 5***** NIGHT!!

Great selection of beer, great happy hour (11-5 on a Sunday?!), and an awesome vibe. Low lights, and the best smelling bar I've ever been to. No joke, it's not just that it doesn't smell BAD, it actually smells GOOD. It feels like a modern speakeasy! Hailing from Seattle, we'll definitely be back!
The BEST small bar off of Broadway. Live music every night. We really enjoyed TheNashMash615 on Sunday night. Multiple artists and great music. It is a full bar with a great bourbon selection.

You will likely have joiners at your table. I went with my dad and the couple at our table kept referring to me us as husband and wife no matter how many times they were corrected ( YUCK and so awkward) they turned out to be swingers and followed us after we moved seats. The show was cool. Worst nachos and tater skins I've ever had.
Delicious catfish!!!  Took a chance and ordered the basket- was not disappointed!!  Catfish was mouth watering- music very loud, but excellent service!!

Not a bad bar to hang out in. The staff on the other hand are not nice at all. The impression is they are not happy workers. Ordered a few drinks without a smile and attitude. Well to say the least there. Are many more places that will actually appreciate our being here and business. Advice move on there are other places to have a good time. This place seriously needs a bar rescue episode.

Every floor has something amazing. And then you get the the roof and the views are amazing. Great friendly staff, clean bathrooms, mechanical bull, dance floor, fireplace. Anything you want, they have it.

Never got the drink I ordered. After waiting 40 minutes for our tabs manager comes out, doesn't apologize, and states she will call the police if we walk out...no one had said anything about walking out. They already had our cards...worst customer service but the band was good.

This was a quick lunch spot for us while we were out and about in Nashville on a short weekend trip. There wasn't many options for parking as there were only about 10 spots infront. There was a lot next door that charged a $10 fee. I do think parking can probably be tricky at most places in downtown Nashville so this wasn't surprising.

There was a huge stage inside for live music. We got to see a few really good acts. It is loud so I wouldn't suggest this place if you are wanting to go out somewhere and chat with people. It's more for watching/listening the musical acts.

We came with my husband, parents and 3 kids. They didn't have a highchair which kind of stunk so our little one at to eat on our lap. They also didn't have a kids menu. Kids are allowed but I wouldn't consider this a kid friendly place.

The server was friendly and helped us find something on the menu that the kids would like. The food was pretty typical American food. Not bad but not outstanding or anything. Typical bar food. I think I would have enjoyed this place more if I had a few hours to kill (without my kids) and drink a few beers while enjoying some good local Nashville music.

I requested the melodic excellence of Oasis from the band on the third floor.  They said they would play the song, TOOK MY HARD EARNED MONEY to play the song then told everyone at the bar I was lame for requesting Oasis because it was clear I was out of town.  That's correct, I am from out of town and the four scum stole my money and faith in music.

Everyone know Oasis is great except for the bigots on stage who decided to play racially fueled hate music.

If you are from out of town, don't go here because it is clear they just want to steal your money and screw you over.

De used to eat dinner here ...regrettably...the chicken tasted like it had been fried in a vat of old oil with fish.  Service was horrible.  The fact nonone was eating in there should have been the sign

This place was packed when I visited on a Monday evening.  And I can see why.  The music here on all levels (literally, on all levels) was fantastic.  The food here (I tried the wings) was really delicious.  The drinks were good, and the service was wonderful. 

Back to the music, which may be why you visit -- the band that was performing here did rock, pop, and country hits, and they were fantastic.  They did versions and covers of Fleetwood Mac, Billy Joel, and Pat Benatar, among others, and really hit it out of the park.  There is plenty of room here, so the capacity here is huge.  A great find during a visit to Nashville.

This was our first stop on Broadway... and dang it was fun! Three stories of live music, food, and drinks. We enjoyed listening to a band out of KY who performed a little country and southern rock n roll! Definitely up our alley! For apps my husband and I shared SW chicken egg rolls and wings. The rolls were superb and the wings were Nashville hot! Definitely loved this joint!

A hidden gem in the heart of downtown Nashville's historic Printers Alley. A Steelers' bar (original owner is from Pittsburgh) and they have Guinness on tap!
The wings are mouth watering and the hot dogs on toasted Hawaiian bread will knock your socks off.
Great ambiance, friendly bartenders and dozens of craft beers!

Everything you'd expect and more! Attended the time jumpers show on Monday. The show started at 8, but crowd shows up hours early to hold down tables for the evening. If you want a table with service, you probably have to arrive like 90+ minutes before the show. We sat at the bar and had a great time and great service. Music was fun and like an educational lesson. Onion rings were good. Didn't try other food. Prices for drinks are right. Enjoyed this Nashville treasure!

As absolutely ridiculous as it is to admit, I didn't know where 3rd & Lindsley was.* Yes. I know. But I knew that it was a staple in the Nashville live music scene and that I needed to check it out. What better timing, then, was it to have a friend come in from out of town who wanted to see a live show? Perfect. Done.

The first thing that you'll notice about 3rd & Lindsley is that there's breathing room. I get the 'intimate' nature of a lot of live music venues is what draws crowds. I don't like smelling strangers. Having some room to manspread is a-okay with me. You can choose from tables downstairs to stools upstairs (and at the bar). That said, 3rd & Lindsley isn't so cavernous that you'll feel lost or have a hard time hearing/seeing what's going on onstage. After paying a $10 cover, we walked in, grabbed a table and sat down to enjoy some good tunes. The atmosphere was extremely laid back. I don't know that the band had a huge following, but it seemed that everyone in the venue was having a good time (and a few ladies were having a *very* good time). Besides that, their talent was undeniable. There are *so* many good musicians in this town. It's unbelievable.

Since the place wasn't overrun with people, we decided to hit the bar rather than wait for table service. On the Thursday night we were here, there was only one waitress and she looked to be in the weeds. Since I paid cover, my friend got the drinks. I don't know whether there's a cocktail menu from which to choose but this doesn't seem to be a cocktail kinda place. He got a beer and I got a Jack and Coke. The pour wasn't exceptionally strong or large but I don't know how much he paid for it. We had just come from dinner so we didn't look at the food options although I don't know that I'd ever, willingly, eat at a music venue.

I'd come back. The website calendar is very easy to navigate, the cover price was fair, the staff were nice, and the vibe was very laid back. Oh, and the sound quality was fantastic. Professionals play and work here, without a doubt. Given its location, I don't know how much random foot/tourist traffic it gets but given the quality of performer the venue is able to book and the ease with which a patron can see/hear what's happening onstage, I'm not at all surprised with the popularity of the venue from music lovers in the know. 

*To my credit, my grizzled rideshare driver blanked as well and we both felt very dumb when we realized where it was.

I will never return as the prices for concessions were robbery .  9,00 for a bottle of water !  Cop - homeless - searching belongings - metal detectors .  And the performer asked for the audience to come closer and the gestapo would not allow.  How embarrassing for Lucinda Williams !  Nope never again !
Brynn and Kennedy helped us through a snag with our tickets at the gate. They were very nice and a huge help.

Honky Tonk Central is one of the best bars in Nashville. This is a MUST visit for Nashville nightlife. The live music, DJ's, and drink specials are great. You can't go here and not have a great time. I came here on a conference for work and went to this venue as part of the bar crawl. It was definitely a great time and totally worth visiting. The name speaks for itself when you think of Nashville and Country music. Go and have a great time!
The owner was very rude to our group and some others regarding noise.   We were just TALKING. The show had not even started yet. We will never go back!

We were there Saturday night around 9. We were met with by a sweet hostess who told us it would be a little wait for food but we were welcome to sit down. We decided to give it a try. There were a lot of sports fans there and it seemed fun.  We were greeted by a manager named Sher and she gave us our water and told us our server would be right with us. We waited a few minutes and Sher came back over and apologized for the wait and took our drink order and even though the place was packed, she kept coming back to check on us. It was a great experience. The other manager Rex checked on us too. They were bussing tables and helping the servers. The food was AMAZING and the music was fun. This manager made sure everyone eating was taken care of and had what they needed. She has us laughing and suggested the Bushwackers which were so good.  One is all we needed.   We had a great night. Thank you so much Sher, if you ever read this. You made our dinner and night out so fun.  We will return for the food and drinks and we hope to see you too!  The rooftop view is phenomenal and as busy as it was there everyone seemed to love their job and wanted to make sure everyone had a great time!  Bravo to Nashville Underground for hiring such a great staff! We are local and it was our first time but definitely not our last! Oh and that hot chicken is the best in Nashville.  I've had the others and this one IS the best!
What an epic venue tucked away and exclusive to budding artists in Nashville! Loved seeing Charlotte Sands perform live and can't wait to visit this again!

I went to Hattie Bs and the wait was 2 hrs, so my group decided to walk around broadway we found this place! Not only was the live music amazing but the hot chicken was fantastic!! The waitress was so good I enjoyed myself!!

On the corner of forth avenue and Broadway, can't miss it! They have a live band every night which is great entertainment and there is no cover at any of the bars (something I'm not used to as a Chicagoan). I LOVED the yee haw drink (very sweet, has a hint of coconut and pineapple). If you're 21+, I'd recommend going here! Pretty pricey but definitely worth the experience.

BRING CASH HERE!!!!   So, I am really confused.   I came there, and the staff was amazing.  So nice.  But when I went to pay my tab, they asked me whether I wanted to use a card or cash.  Apparently there is a huge difference.  Why?   I know there are credit card fees.  But why is my tab 20 percent higher if I use a card?!?   Is this place actually paying their taxes???? Or, is this just a way to make more money?   As a local, I want everyone to pay their share of taxes.  Because I do......

Indeed one of the hottest place on the planet for going to see bluegrass and acoustic/folk music. Sure the sign says "World Famous Station Inn" and guess what? It really *is* world famous to musicians and acoustic music lovers. Bluegrass fans travel from all over the world to catch a show here.

Caveat: the neighborhood that has sprung up around The Station Inn is nothing like the bar itself. The Station Inn is old, dilapidated, run-down, usually over-crowded. It's endearing. What's sprung up around it is hipsterville, young, urban, trendy, outrageously expensive. High rises being built within a stone's throw. The two are at odds. 

If you like a great dive bar with world class music, you'll find it here. If not, the rest of the neighborhood will suit you just fine. Beer is the main order here. Rest of the neighborhood? No trouble finding a menu with dozens of martini options. 

Privately I have to wonder how much longer the owners can hold out. 20-30 years ago you were risking it parking here. Now? Main danger now is no parking due the crowd of Lexas, Hondas, Mercedes and Beamers. What used to be a colorful and eerie part of town is now more. The land the bar sits on is worth a gold mine.

But what the hell. Come here for the music and be glad you visited. I did for the first time in about 20 years and really enjoyed my stay. I hope to return once again in the future. If you're in it for the music, it's happening here on a regular basis. If you're looking for just a place to have a cocktail, might be best to move on. This is my kind of old-time music joint and it's just fine.
A great place for live music drinks were tastey and priced reasonable for a live music venue

Ascend amphitheater has an amazing view of the city and is particularly great during the sunset. However, the staff there over reactive to everything. I think I've seen people kicked out for just about every reason possible. Don't smoke unless you're in the smoking section. They will confiscate your e cig vapes or you can leave the premises. Their beers cost $16 and the cheapest one was $13. The food is outrageously expensive. I haven't even begun to talk about the sound issues. This is a town of audio engineers. The sound should be amazing! Unfortunately, the music is played way too loud and there is lots of audio distortion, with clicks and pops happening frequently throughout Dwight Yokum's set. The vocal wasn't loud enough during Lucinda Williams set either. Overall, I wasn't very impressed with this last concert. I've never liked their customer service. It's a pretty setup though if they fix some things.

I mean if I could give this place zero stars, I would. I get it you're a new bar but why in the FUCK would you sell that many tickets for $50  ON NEW YEARS EVE when you can't allow that many people in your bar? Use your head... you let over 100 people wait outside in 13 degree weather AND not to mention me and my friends didn't even get in so I will be getting my money back because YOU don't know how to plan New Year's Eve in downtown Nashville... that's very embarrassing.  I hope in the meantime (before your bar gets shut down) that you all as a staff will be able to use a little more common sense and treat your guests like guests. Don't tell me I'm gunna get food and a champagne toast when I didn't even get in

Lost a star in my book tonight. It won't hurt you and it won't matter. And even though we love you (and the great music made on stage here hundreds of nights a year), when you sell hundreds of tickets and people stand in line starting at 4:30, they're going to be hungry. So when (in your words) "400 people ordered at once" it's gonna get crazy.   Don't get me wrong. I wouldn't want to cook food for that many people...hungry people...but maybe think through some options that don't leave you saying "the kitchen is messed up." Making more burgers takes time, right, but some of our party waited well over an hour for their food (and finally got their food well after people who ordered after them). 
Maybe plan ahead? Maybe give ordering pads to people in line and process orders as they enter...I don't know. That's your business. I just think you could do better at that.
Still love ya...always will. But next time we'll likely eat before we get in line. 
And by the way...I'm still waiting for my fries.

Out of all the bars on Broadway, this was my favorite one. It was pretty packed on the first level, but the second and third floors were easy to go through. All floors each had their own live band playing music, which was fun! I also liked the fact that there were multiple drink stations all around the place where you can buy beer, if you don't feel like going to the main bar where it could get busy. There were also balconies where you can check out Broadway from above, which was really nice. Overall, it is a huge place with a fun and beautiful crowd and good live music!

We came here for a bachelorette party and had a great time up on the third floor. One of the girls in our group has multiple sclerosis and has a really difficult time walking downstairs because she feels unsteady. When we were ready to leave, she walked to the elevator and asked if she could ride down because she didn't feel safe walking down the stairs. The employee at the elevator was rude enough  to look her up and down and say "You don't look disabled to me". When she tried to explain her situation, his unwillingness to help and aggression in response were appalling. We were absolutely outraged at his behavior! We're not sure what she would have needed to do to "appear more disabled", but perhaps the employees at this establishment could benefit from some training on the American Disability Act.

I am sorry Nashville Underground I really am but it was bad. 
My friend and I booked a table for 7pm, we arrived on time and were greeted by a female hostess with long blond hair.  She said "Where would you like to sit?" We said, "On the roof."  She directed us on how to get there but did not show us. There were a handful of people on the roof and 1 bartender but no servers. We sat at the bar and chatted with a nice, young, slender male bartender with brown hair, and a gotee.  I ordered a cider and my friend had a beer.  The cider tap ran out so he gave me what he had for free. He did not offer me another brand or if I wanted to try something else. 

I ordered a hamburger with no bun, and fries. My friend ordered hot shrimp with macaroni and cheese. The shrimp arrived without macaroni and cheese. My friend asked didn't I order macaroni and cheese? The bartender didn't respond nor did he ask if she wanted anything else. I took one bite of the hamburger and sent it away. It was disgusting and tasted like old meat. There was no way I was taking my chance on eating it. The bartender did offer to get me something else and not charge me for the burger. I ended up getting the pulled pork and it was edible. Both my friend and I said we would never be back and it's such a shame because they have an amazing location. Good luck Nashville Underground with all the amazing restaurants in downtown you really need to step up your game.

Our first time here and we could not believe how rude this bartender was to me. We order 4 drinks, my husband did not hold his drink when handed to him bc he was too busy getting money from his wallet, so I reached out to get the beer that was set on the table. Next thing you know this CRAZY, RUDE, UNPROFESSIONAL bartender snapped at me "You can't do that!!!! You can't get the beer until he paid first?" Dumb girl, then why where you trying to handed to him? Such rudeness, she shouldn't be in this industry if you don't have a customer service mentality!!
Not the friendliest place. As a local, this is one of the worst bars to visit or play at. The staff isn't very friendly and they could care less. Good luck getting a drink.
This is one of those gems of a place that we just decided stop in on our way between two destinations.. loved the view from the rooftop bar! Great place to stop for a drink.... or 6
My favorite place for live music in Nashville.  Great atmosphere - nice stage area and intimate setting without being crowded.  Good acoustics.  I've loved every show I've gone to here.

This place is awful, there is a guy that goes by "John"? Middle name or whatever  on the second floor, huge red beard -tonight-is an absolute dick/I just closed half a million dollar deal and offered $4k to get us in VIP and he practically spit in my face-I will never be back here, so disappointed, tried making my best friend's bachelorette party amazing and he single handheldy ruined our experience at this bar...moving on!

First time in Nashville and this was the second bar we stopped at.. And the last! It was awesome. Atmosphere was great, the band was great.. The drinks were strong and the bartenders were friendly. The women's bathroom was absolutely amazing!!! If you need something, it was there. we've been to expensive bars/restaurants/hotels but this was very impressive. The only complain I would have is that the stage is as soon as you walk in.. It gets really tough walking in and out if you're a smoker.

I hate to give a little bar a mediocre review, but I wasn't a fan of Alley Taps. A group of us came here after a convention to listen to some live music and enjoy some drinks, and it was just an okay experience. 

The live bands were great, but pretty much every band playing at any bar in Nashville are talented and fun to listen to. The atmosphere here was relaxed and chill, and there was plenty of seating. The lighting was dark which made the whole place feel intimate and cozy. 

The problem is that for a place that supposedly specializes in beer, they didn't serve their beer at a proper chilled temperature. Even worse, every beer we ordered was almost completely flat! I even had a glass of sparkling wine to mix things up and it, too, was flat (had about 3 bubbles in it). 

I can forgive a lot of things but I cannot forgive overpriced, warm, and flat drinks.

I used to love this place. The last several months, it has really changed. The service is very slow, if and when they remember you placed an order. Just 2 weeks ago, my drink had a beer cap in the bottom of the cup.
They definitely need to make a few changes.

This venue is amazing.  That being said, I went to 3rd and Lindsley with a purpose, to hear Christone "Kingfish" Ingram play some blues in Nashville, TN and Kingfish put on one phenomenal show!  If you've never seen him, you should.  You WILL be a fan!   I was fortunate enough to meet and hear this young man when he was just 15 at a blues club in Clarksdale, Mississippi, and had the pleasure of sitting next to his sweet momma.

As an additional bonus, at 3rd and Lindsley, we sat with Ms Thornetta Davis, and her handsome husband James.  She's the blues Queen of Detroit!  We were blessed beyond measure that night!

Thornetta even sent me one of her CD's (because it was my birthday night) and it's so great that we listen to her and Kingfish all the time when we're riding on the bike.
I hope someday they get together and sing, I can travel!

Our bad experience was our server.  She charged for premium, without asking, and took so long to bring the drinks they were watered down when we received them.  My husband asked for a Guinness, and after 30 minutes went to the bar to just cancel it.  Our server saw him there and grabbed the Guinness and popped the top.  My husband said he'd just canceled it, and she said she couldn't put it back.  When our bill came, and we saw all the charges weren't correct, we asked for a manager.  He gave my husband $2.50 cash for the beer, but nothing about all the watery upcharges.  

If you go,  watch your credit card VERY closely... or be very wise, pay cash.
Charges for Titos's and serves well. Unless you want to be taken advantage of, keep walking down Broadway for a better bar!

Bluegrass jam venue.  Musicians form a tight cluster and mostly jam and play for each other.  Most customers don't seem to go to listen to music, but treat it as a backdrop for conversation.  I had to move with my folding chair to behind the musicisions to hear anything.  Outside of being bumped by a guitar case, nobody seemed to mind me being there.  Food is has good  pizza with a good selection of beer.  An
Enjoyable evening once I got dialed in to how it works.  I don't hear much live bluegrass where I live, so I was happy to hear
The real thing again.

I've been coming to Nashville on a regular basis (at least four times/month) for three years.  Benchmark is consistently a fun, friendly atmosphere where you can find amazing talent.  So much better than the vibe on Broadway, around the corner on Second Ave. you'll find great, friendly bartenders (Whitney Love and Co.), good bar food, music that will keep you in there for hours.  At the top of that headline is Isaac Mathews.  Isaac is friendly and interacts with the crowd and will amaze you with his pure tone and talent.  Bobby Tomlinson joins him from time to time and adds to the fun and talent as well.  You won't be disappointed if you come here for a drink, an hour or a night.  Ask Isaac to play "Like a Cowboy".  You won't want to leave.

Great venue. Not a bad seat in the house. Great sound. Super location. No line for the ladies room, men's was a different story. Drinks are ridiculously expensive. You an bring in one unopened bottle of water. Do it.

We visited Saturday night and it was a fun bar.

Positives.

Guys, you need to check this place out. I'm married but noticed there were plenty of attractive women and they outnumbered the guys probably 2 to 1. It's one of the few bars I've ever been to that wasn't a sausage factory!

Even though the place was packed and appeared understaffed the Bar Tender on the 3rd floor was prompt and polite.

We ordered chicken tenders and fries (a little overpriced but that was expected) and they were on the table in record time and they were fresh so the kitchen staff was on top of their game!

Drinks were good and reasonable for the area.

Awesome views of Lower Broad from the balconies on the third level. You can see all the action in the area and get some fresh air too.

There was a decent house band that played a great variety of music from old time country, new country, pop and rock.

Large TV's throughout the bar to watch sports or whatever. They had the Game 5 of the Predators Ducks on to watch while we were there.

I wish I could give 5 stars but there were a couple negatives.

The lower level was so over crowded you couldn't move, that's why we immediately made our way to the 3rd floor.

The restrooms were absolutely nasty, urine on the floor and the sinks filled with empty cups and beer bottles.

The staff for the most part was polite and attentive. Unfortunately there was one or two security staff who had "tough guy attitude". Let me be clear, most of the staff including the security was very nice and were even helping try to keep the place clean but the one that stood out was about a 400 pounder who had a terrible attitude, he was vaping in the bar and it was blowing right in peoples faces. At one point in the night he was throwing things away that a bachelorette party had left on the table next to us to save their spot while they all visited the restroom. I tried to tell him they would be back in a moment and he just gave me a dirty look, yelled something at me and continued to toss their stuff out.

All in all it was still a great place and of course very touristy but I could recommend it to locals too.

The Station Inn averages out to a "high 3," but I ultimately had to round down because of the insulting food quality. The "pizza" is minor step up from the stuff my sister and I used to make when we were kids and ran our own "pizzeria" and made "deliveries" to "mom's room." The "pizzas" were basically Wonder Bread and ketchup, topped with melted string cheese. Gross. It's not much better at Station Inn, where you're basically eating oven-baked cardboard, canned tomato "sauce," mystery meat ("sausage"), and Kraft something cheese. Enough irony for you? OK, I'll stop.

The music, on the other hand, is terrific, and I recommend staying for a couple hours and getting a full and wide gamut of bluegrass sets. Other reviewers here are lauding the "authenticity" of the music, but I'm not sure I can actually speak to that. For one, "authenticity" is very much a "cultural construct." Is there really an obvious delimiter for breaking off the inauthentic form the authentic, the inorganic from the inorganic? And what of musical genres themselves, given what we know about hybridity and cultural mixing? Last, I've been sour on "authenticity" as a concept in recent years. Like "neighborhood," it's often seeped in artifice propelled by urban real estate development, and live music venues are frequent nodes for cultivating this mystification. Don't believe me? Read David Grazian's Blue Chicago ethnography about "authentic" jazz clubs in Chicago, where proprieters (sp) purposely rip seats and make internal decor look cheap so the place feels more "authentic." I was so outraged reading the book that I had a hard time getting into live jazz/blues music for about a year afterwards, so distracted was I over whether venues were trying to pull an 'authenticity ruse' on me.

Bottom line: the music here is great, authentic or inauthentic, and the food is downright horrible. If you come here after a good meal, well, that's the way to do it.

Very poor service. Waited 30 minutes for a server after being seated. Two waitresses continually walked past us and just ignored us. My wife asked one of them if someone was covering the area and rudely replied Yes! I will get to you. Ten minutes later I asked another server and he got us somebody from another section. Was not super busy in there not sure what the issue was.

So surprised by how much I liked Honky Tonk Central. To be honest, I had never been to Nashville and wasn't all that excited about Broadway. But, I LOVED this place! We sat on the second floor. There were a ton of tables, servers to keep the drinks flowing, and an amazingly talented band. I don't love new country music, but this band was so talented and engaging that I let my "Steve" drink settle in and I embraced the atmosphere that is Nashville. I was sad to leave. This place is so much better than Tootsie's or any other of the "must do" bars on Broadway.

I just got through listening to Jesse Kinch's performance of "After All These Lovers," one of Jesse's originals, at The Back Corner.  Unbelievable acoustics surrounding great talent!  For music events, it's clear that The Back Corner is the place to go in Nashville.

Attempted to come to Honkey Tonk to ring in the new year after paying $80 for their "NYE Fast Pass" which supposedly would allow you to skip the line into Rippeys and Tootsies as well as here. This was our first stop at 9:30pm (much before the rush to get into places before midnight) and we were still told we needed to wait in line. 

Essentially myself, as well as 7 of my friends, were collectively scammed out of $560 for absolutely NOTHING. Additionally, the passes could only be paid for in cash, so I highly doubt that the large profit this bar is making on scamming its patrons will ever be reported on their tax return. 

Please reconsider before paying to attend any special events at the Honkey Tonk.

My boyfriend and I came by last night and the music was great. The female guitarist who just turned 21 is a damn rockstar. Purple rain!! Only downside was the creepy pinky ring dude who kept trying to high five me and my boyfriend between naps who needed to be to be cut off. He is probably nice sober though. 5 stars.

I dont write negative reviews yet we wont be going back. To many great restaurant options available.  Waited 50 minutes for a chicken salad and a small hot chicken dinner.  Chicken dinner may of been the worst I've had. Thank goodness the fries were good.

We decided to eat here because it wasn't as busy as the other bars in the area (it was packed about 15 minutes after we sat down).  I will absolutely be back next time we are in town for food and drinks.  I had the pulled pork wrap and it was one of the best dinners I have ever had.  It was seriously delicious.  He had the Nashville Hot Chicken Sandwich and really like it as well.  We drank long islands and they were well made.  The bartender was nice and even tho he was overwhelmed, he did a good job.

Popular country music songs played by a local band, great bar with ample seating, ID check at the front door, not too crowded for a Monday night, and a good ambiance.

Bigger than Tootsies and not as crowded, not as big as Jason Aldean's but more crowded. I'd come back (no cover charge!). It's so nice to hop from one bar to the next without the commitment to stay after having to pay a cover charge.

Come here for the club and music, but avoid the food.

Nashville Underground is located at the end of Broadway street in Nashville. It's a solid location that's a bit away from the usual raucous you'll see on Broadway. 

One thing that I like about this place is that it contains a bit of something for everyone. There's a live music section/pub style restaurant on the first floor. The second contains a mechanical bull (which I rode and fell off).  The third contains an LED dance floor. A rooftop bar and private spaces for parties. If you come here to drink, club, and have a good time, you'll love this place.

But I'll have to remove a star due to the terrible food experience here. My friends and I ordered a variety of things so I know it wasn't just a single dish. Food ordered below:

-G's Southern Steak Salad: The steak wasn't precut and it was placed on top of the salad. The steak was so rough that we couldn't cut it with the knife provided. I asked the waitress for a steak knife and we still had trouble. Gave up on trying to eat this.
-Jumbo Wings: Forgot the sauce we got it with this, but the sauce came out too...sweet with a peculiar flavor. My friend that ordered this shared it with the rest of our group hoping that she didn't have to touch it anymore.
-Build Your Own Burger: A simple burger that's super hard to mess up. Fries were a bit unseasoned.

4/5. Honestly, the clubbing experience was so solid here that it saved this place from a lower rating.

It'll cure you winter Full Moon Pickin Party blues! 

Attended a free Sunday show and really enjoyed it. However, I'd rather pay the $15 for a pickin party if it's warm. Great atmosphere and you can enjoy the music WHILE socializing.

Visited on Sunday night. The bar was slow but the female bartender serviced every client who walked up before taking the time to take our order. I ordered two drinks, the total was $20.  I did not tip her because she was extremely rude and acted as if we were inconveniencing her by ordering a drink.  I noticed that she added a $5 tip to my bill. This is extremely frustrating not to mention fraudulent.  I would suggest Paradise Park, where the same two drinks are $14 dollars and they use real red bull.

We came here early on a Saturday night and it was a welcome respite from the shoulder-to-shoulder busy bars of Broadway and other Printer's Alley bars. 

The theme is a Prohibition-era Speakeasy. They have a really neat little house band that plays good music and dresses in period. The walls of the bar are combination exposed brick and rock, giving you the feel that you're underground. The lighting is low, romantic and charming. I would have loved to see the bartenders dress in period as well!

We stayed long enough to have a few beers and listen to the band finish. Definitely a fun spot that we will return to occasionally!

We came in on Sunday night at 8pm. The place was packed, standing room only. The only reason we stayed is because of the awesome band. A female was upfront with a 10 year old killer drum player and 17 year old crazy guitar player. They played everything from AC/DC, Tom Petty, Led Zeppelin, Neil Diamond, etc.

There is a long wait to get a drink at the bar but for $10 you will get a double pour in your drink.  About 40 minutes a partial table cleared and we got a seat but there was no table service.  It took about an hour for someone to come to clear up the table but did not take drink orders.

What an awesome spot! And it's the only Pittsburgh Steelers' bar in the city! Great spot for weekends, rad ambiance and super friendly bartenders! Game day they have 2-4-1 beers! The live music is a nice change from the Broadway honky tonks. The hot dog is STELLAR! 
Truly a hidden gem!

All you have to know about Honky Tonk Central is....$6 for a freaking PBR.
Mediocre bands playing the same old songs you hear back home on a Monday night (unless you've come to Nashville to hear Bon Jovi covers).
The bar caters to the Frat and Bachelor/Bachelorette Party crowd.
Do yourself a favor and go across the street to Robert's and hear real country music played by amazing musicians (and only pay $2.50 for a PBR)
Stopped in here on Saturday 8/8/2015 and listened to an amazing band!! If anyone knows the name of them please let me know. They played great together and amazing acoustic by the lead singer!!
Hard to argue with the free music bluegrass jam on Sunday's and no-frills atmosphere. Just get there at 7 so you can get a table and then get your beer straight away
HAD A PHENOM TIME!!!! Vampire Weekend had my total respect. Everything at this venue is top notch. My favorite venue in Nashville to see a concert (and I've seen over 50). Go!!!!!!!!! I impore you.

Came to the underground for the first time with my Family and we were not disappointed. The manager Teddy was amazing and showed us the whole restaurant. On the roof, our bartender was Bobby and he was awesome, super personable, quick service and BOMB drinks. SHOUT OUT TO BOBBY 2TIMES! Thanks for an awesome experience!
Stopped in on a rainy Friday at lunch time. Had a soloist playing. He was enjoyable. Bloody Mary was very tasty. Ordered burger with habanero cheese and was pleasantly surprised. Delicious.

One of my favorite clubs in Nashville. The only place that doesn't play country music which I love. I love when they play hip hop & top 40's. You can check out the calendar to see what they're playing for the night, the ambiance in there is great-definitely a mix of LA & New York. It's a mix crowd which I love. The manager & all the staff there are very welcoming, I normally reserve a table there when I go & the prices are very reasonable.

I love the speakeasy vibes, it's in the heart of downtown Nashville but just off the beaten path. It's much more lowkey with dimmed lighting, real local talent, and inexpensive drinks.

It's a great place to come to just hang out with friends or family, as there is open seating, couches and TV's in the back, and quick service.

Great happy hour--definitely check it out sometime soon!
This place is a gem. The staff is the very best and you're going to learn something new when you start talking to the person sitting next to you.

I would have to say this place has some of the best food for a bar with live music just off Broadway. But I have to say I am skeptical of their happy hour practices. I ordered a house wine which I was told was on the happy hour menu but they were out so I could order the full priced option? My friend ordered a beer two for one. When he went to order the second one was told it was to late. When I did get the bill the wine was not on happy hour at all. I had to question the bill and was able to reach a reasonable expectation but it was more work than dinner and a drink should be.
Dylan made my bachelorette party amazing!! We had a great time! We will definitely come back as long as Dylan is working, plus he's hot and sexy!

Great towny cute spot. Wildly talented bluegrass artists perform here. They offer vigorously buttered and salted popcorn and beers. 

They are weird about running cards, but hey at least they take cards at all. I didn't mind too much.

Honkey Tonk Central was a very fun atmosphere, the band was singing current country hits and they took song requests for tips. I must say, my group was disappointed with the service, they were not attentive at all. The drinks were also very overpriced. You can find the same menu items for cheaper all along Broadway. Rock on, Nashville, TN

This place was such a gem to find!!! Broadway was way too crazy for my taste, and a Lyft driver had mentioned that his friend's band was playing here that night. I'm so happy to have stumbled in. The music was fantastic (Just Whiskey), the drinks were flowing and the ambiance is cozy. What I really love about this bar is that the front part of the bar has no TVs, while the large back room does. So it seems like a great place to hang out and watch sports with a crew, or have a more intimate drink with a friend or date.

The bartenders were spectacular, they have specialty coffee drinks, and an excellent beer list. Just the perfect bar!

Ascend is a nice facility in a nice location, with good bands, BUT "SECURITY" IS INVASIVE & possibly illegal.  They opened my wallet & fondled the contents... two different employees at the same show. 

1.  At the entry gate, gate screener didn't just search my bag.  She took everything out and opened every container inside, including my WALLET!  Yes!  She put her grubby unbonded hands inside & moved my money, credit cards, etc. around.  I had done nothing wrong, unless you count buying a ticket to the event.  It was an unnecessary invasion of privacy!  Even police are not allowed to open a person's wallet without consent, and these gate workers are NOT cops!  STAY OUT OF MY WALLET!  

2.  During the show, a man sitting next to me was smoking.  Rather than directing him to the smoking area, which is what should have happened, they made him stand up & empty his pockets, then patted him down.  When they didn't find anything on him, they ordered me to hand my bag over to be searched AGAIN because the stupid kid rent-a cop thought we were together when we were not!  Kid stood right in front of me so that I couldn't see the show & shined a bright flashlight in my face as he opened everything in my bag AGAIN, my wallet AGAIN, and when he didn't find whatever it was he was looking for, he told me I was under surveillance & threw my bag back at me & my stuff fell all over the ground.  I had no flashlight to find everything, but luckily my neighbors helped me gather my things & put them back in my bag. 

This place has always has eerily strict security, but is now a full-blown police state manned by wanna-be cops who have obviously been empowered by management to perform illegal searches while treating people like crap.  Innocent people, btw.  I did NOTHING but buy a ticket.  I followed all their rules & still had my wallet taken out of my bag & ransacked twice at one show.  I will NEVER NEVER N.E.V.E.R. be back & am going to let everyone in my many music-related forums know that Ascend is NOT the place to see jam & rock bands!

Venue  - Huge place definitely one on the top biggest ones with multiple levels.

Crowd - Good fun crowds out for a good time.

Staff - Staff here is always cool and does the best they can and keep cool during rush hours.

Location  - In the heart of Nashville and its popular Broadway district. 

Prices - Decent prices just like any other bars on the strip.

Place is popping, always busy, worth checking out for sure. One of the Originals that has been around for a while.

Fun rooftop bar now that spring has finally sprung in Nashville! The second floor has a unique feature: the sports games playing on a large TV projected onto the floor. The third (top) floor was my personal fav: two separate outdoor patios with great views of downtown and the Nashville skyline. Corn hole, too! Can't speak to the food though.

So we brought a large group in spending a lot of money. We moved up the third floor. We found there was only one bathroom on that floor, in order to be efficient we had two guys in the bathroom simultaneously, the want to be security guards kicked us out, hurting revenue and reputation. We'll take our business to a bar that understands that the faster you relieve yourself, the faster you can reorder, increasing revenue, profits and customer satisfaction.
Loved the Sunday night free Bluegrass concert.  We followed the concert with dessert at Bar Louie, around the corner, which is open very late.
Love this place! Sat up stairs on the second floor..great food, music and drinks. Service was perfect. A++

I've never been kicked out of a bar!! I only had 2 drinks and was not drunk. Went into the stall with my beer bottle because I didn't want to leave my beer at the bar unattended and get roofied! While I was peeing the bathroom attendant started screaming that I was going to be kicked out due to bringing a beer bottle into my stall. When I came out of my stall she wouldn't even give me soap, just insisted that I be escorted out. Seriously?! After a beer bottle into the bathroom stall?? (No I didn't
shatter it or anything) A gentle reminder of your policy would've been sufficient. Completely unprofessional bathroom attendant and then security.

This venue is very nice with not any bad seats and a beautiful view of the Nashville skyline.  The women's bathroom was plentiful of stalls and therefore the wait very short.  The big negative I and the group I was with saw was that it needs to be no smoking, or at LEAST have a designated smoking area.  Come on, this IS 2015.  It really was a downer to sit next to a family of smokers (nicotine AND marijuana) while trying to enjoy Earth Wind & Fire/ Chicago.  Not only did it stink but we did not feel good about breathing in all those carcinogens.  I would give it four or maybe 5 stars if something is done about the smoking issue.

This bar is a joke. They treat their guests with their thuggy security thugs like criminals. The security staff is rude abusive and just downright rotten to the core customer service wise. I was with a group small one of 4 people two of them went on the dance floor and the other person went to go get them and we were about to leave when all of sudden by accident I close my eyes but not because I was drunk I was 110% sober. In fact I was so sober then there was more people in the bar that they should have focused on throwing their ass out instead of mine. When asked or told this is wrong going down the elevator the supervisor or what not in a blue shirt with a stupid buzz cut and about five seven and height told me to shut up. What a jerk. You don't tell guests to shut up when asking a simple question as to why you're being kicked out when you've done nothing wrong. They also did not care that I was the only source of a ride home for a young girl legal age of course to get home an hour and a half away which is why I close my eyes because I did not want to go to the stupid bar to begin with but after the way I was treated I will not be going to this stupid Honky Tonk at all. I spent my hard-earned money to come from California to Tennessee to give them my tourist dollars and they totally treat me like crap this so-called Southern establishment. You guys stink. I will write the Better Business Bureau as well as Jon Taffer of Bar Rescue as I no the head creator and tell them to publicly bad-mouth this dump. You guys always treat your guests like this? If you do you deserve to go under. I will never step foot in this stupid bar any of its Affiliates ever again. You guys might want to fire your head of security or your security company for allowing their engines and themselves to treat your guests like common criminals in their Thug Like manner. I wish I could give this place zero stars because that's really what you guys deserve. I hope you go out of business. Have a nice day

Love it. Stayed here for pretty much 30 hours this past weekend when my best friend and I spent a weekend in Nashville. It is super touristy, but as a tourist it was just what I wanted to do when I went to Nashville. 

Live music on every level, windows open letting in warm air, and a friendly crowd looking to have a good time and enjoy themselves. We found that our favorite level was the third because it seemed to be less crowded than the other two. I love it and will definitely spend just as much time here on my next trip back to Nashville!

A few years ago this place was great, but since the boom in Nashville the staff is absolutely terrible. Incredibly rude and treats you horribly. If you can avoid this place, do. They act pretentious and you don't have the true Nashville experience here.

5 STARS! When ended up doing the backstage show that they offered during the middle of a Saturday. The song writers were great and even featured one who wrote a few George strait tunes. We loved the seating and the feel on the inside as it really made you feel backstage and really close to the artists. The stories that they told about the song writing was really cool and they all perform their songs. 

When we first walked in we were greeted with a shot of Fireball, free on the house, which was pretty cool and really got the vibe going. I would have to say that if we ever come back or have friends visiting Nashville we will we will highly recommend them booking this backstage show opportunity. They have food available as well but we did not order.

AlleyTaps is an amazing, little hidden gem in Printers Alley! Amber is the bartender. Plus Alley Taps is the home for all the STEELERS GAMES! Make sure that you make your way down to Alley Taps. Tell Amber I said hi!

If there's any truth to the rumors --- an iconic live music is on the verge of shutdown by corporate monsters. 
If so, I am glad I had the chance to experience Bobby's!
Live music, beers, friendly regulars, and best yet, no problem finding free parking ! 
A must see for Nashville visitors and residents alike !

3rd and Lindsley is the perfect example of don't judge a book by its cover. I was so excited to see that DeVotchKa was coming to Nashville for a show. When I saw that it was at 3rd and Lindsley, I had mixed feelings but wow, was I wrong to do so. 

3rd and Lindsley is located on a corner in a strip of a few other businesses. While there is parking out front, don't count on it. I got there about 45 minutes before the opening act and it was already full. Luckily, there is a parking lot across the street. This one is paid but for $10, it's not bad. The concert tickets were only $20 so I was fine with dishing out a little extra dough. Upon entering, the bouncer asked for my name. They have a list so I guess that's how they keep track of ticket sales. It works. 3rd and Lindsley is kind of set up like a dive bar with a stage. The bar is to the right when you walk in. It wasn't too busy yet so I decided to grab a beer there. Friendly and fast service. Beer prices are good. I then went to look for a seat. On the main level there are normal tables with plenty of chairs. The lower level stage area is open if you wish to stand. The nice thing is the main area with all of the tables is slightly raised so if people are standing, you can still see. There is also a second level with seating but the band insisted that everyone sit on the main level. No problem. I was able to snag a seat right up front. I had the perfect view. I was really close to the stage but still had the comfort of sitting down. There was a server assigned to the area and he was really attentive. Not in a pushy or annoying way, just a quick check-in to see if I needed another beer. While I didn't order food, the menu looked decent. When the show started, I was really impressed by the sound. Really clear and the perfect volume. I was so happy I got there early because I had the perfect view. I love DeVotchKa so getting to see them so close up and with such great sound was amazing. I could see how this place could get cramped if it was a sold out show, but this night was busy without being too busy. While it's not the fanciest place, it delivers great sound at unbeatable prices. I will definitely be returning when another band catches my eye.

Tri level bar with three stages and three bars on three levels. Live music every weekend. Lots of variety with their music groups they have rotating throughout the day. Drink prices are a little steep, but strong. Don't ask for a 'long pour of anything, because they make it a double, which is double the price! $18 for a 'double' cranberry vodka! 

The drinks are a little more stiff than most places though, but expensive. Also, be prepared to wait for the bathroom line for a long time here. Single room. No stall, just a room.

Still one of my favorite places to be when I'm in Nashville.

Came here on vacation and it was a really good time! I don't listen to much Country music but boy do they know their Country music! The cover band was great and knew every song that was requested. They even played some Metallica and other rock songs too. Our server was very nice and greeted us dispite the loud music. We ended up just ordering Cokes and Sprites since we weren't in the drinking mood and the server was kind enough to comp our drinks which was very nice. Next time, I'll be back for the food and drinks and more Country music!

Honky Tonk is located right on the corner of the main tourist strip Broadway.  We walked passed it a few times and after hearing the band we decided to go in and check it out.  It was early afternoon on a Monday and they were packed.  It's a huge bar with plenty seating and tables as well.  It could use a remodel as it was dingy.  Our bartenders were awesome and quick.  I was drinking Patron Margarita's and they were made so well that I kept drinking I enjoyed them so much. 

The patrons hanging out in the bar are mainly tourist and they were all fun and having a good time.  From plenty of Bachelorette's  and every single age group.  This is just another thing I love about country music, no age limits.  You can find every age group who are country music fans.  I guess Nashvilel is the number one destination for Bachelorette's to come and party.  They are everywhere.  I can totally see why.  So many fun roof top bar's and plenty of fun thing's to do along with such great restaurants. 

We had eaten a big breakfast so we did not try any food here and not quite sure I would. It may be a tourist bar but the drinks were very reasonably priced, great service, and the band was awesome and very engaging.  Most folks don't realize these bands work for tips only, so take care of them if you are enjoying their music.  We tipped well, requested a song that they played very well and I even purchased their CD.  They were really good and so engaged with all of the patrons throughout the bar.

We had a fun few hours hanging out drinking and enjoying the fabulous band. Hit this place up as it is really fun.

I could have done without the restroom attendant. I appreciate trying to help folks out but I never go into restroom with my purse so I had to go back to give money for handing me a smidge of soap. Really didn't fit the place.

Great bar on Broadway in Nashville with fantastic music on every floor with the third being my favorite floor. It's awesome to look out onto the street from above and enjoy the sights and sounds of what is now to be considered the new NashVegas. The band was absolutely fabulous and the vibe is really chill. After a few hours of being there, had to order some food, nothing major, just chicken fingers and fries. The menu has typical bar food and they were good, not great, but good enough to feed some of the liquor in my belly. It's convenient that they have a bathroom upstairs because heading down the stairs would definitely not be appealing. I would definitely say that if you're ever in Nashville, this is one stop that you definitely have to make because it's one of the iconic bars in town, and you will have a hell of a good time!

Ambience is divey but man, this is a can't-miss stop when you're in Nashville. So glad I made it this time since I wasn't able to my first time in town (I actually went twice during my stay). The Bluegrass Jam is one of the best nights in town, and you'd call me a liar if I told you it's free--but, remarkably, it is.

I got there a few minutes after the jam started and still was early enough that there was plenty of seating still available. They don't have much of a menu, but guess what: You're not coming here for the food; you're coming here for the amazing music. The bluegrass jam welcomes anyone who brings an instrument and wants to jam, and there's never too many. If I'd kept up my lessons and could play the fiddle, I'd be up there with the rest of the players!

Real talk, this place can't be beat. The rest of the Gulch has been built up but the Station Inn is like taking a trip back in time; it's stayed true to itself all these years and I love it. Luckily there's still parking available, either on the street or at the lot across the street, even though the Gulch is all fancy now. Parking in the lot isn't bad; on a Sunday in July 2018 it was free for the first hour, and $5 for two hours. Well worth it!

Nicest bathrooms in Nashville!  Bartenders Ed & Charity were fantastic! We have a group of 6 visiting from Wisconsin and they both were so pleasant and entertaining. We felt very welcomed! The only thing we would suggest is using plastic cups instead of glass. The drinks served in glassware was nice but seemed risky. We all agree 5 stars for bartenders but gave 4 stars because of glass, table set up in dance area and music should have been louder.

This small dive was an interesting spot for an hour.  For true musicians, I can see the draw.  Individual artists came in and joined others as time went on.  There is nothing great about the food or drinks but the character of the place is interesting.

After the trek from Tuscaloosa to Nash, I was super excited to make it down to Broadway. Once we walked around a little bit, we decided to stop at this honky tonk! It looked like the perfect mixture of chill and fun from the outside, and that it was! We were there from 6pm to midnight, as the amount of fun we had made us lose track of time. Tried some local brews, ate some tater tots, and danced a TON! If you are young, but don't mind out hanging with an older crowd, and looking for a fun experience, this is it! Bands were great, large bar, not much selection, but overall a great experience!

Great venue for an intimate concert experience. We went to the Station Inn to hear one of my favorite bands (The Steel Wheels). I was a little apprehensive when we first walked it. I thought it sort of looked like a dump. But, it was clean and just really casual. There were quite a few tables and chairs so everyone could sit and enjoy the concert. 

They don't usually pre-sell tickets but I contacted them and said we were coming from out of town. They promised they would get us in and gave suggestions on when to arrive. They were extremely friendly and helpful. We ended up with great seats up front and I got to meet the band afterwards. We are definitely planning on going back!

Seriously some of the best Hot Chicken I've had with great ranch and bleu cheese dipping sauce. Great atmosphere, cool lit up floor with roof top patio, and best of all that beats any place is a chill attentive bar tender- go see BOBBY 2x's!!! He recommended some great Nashville staples too.
Music was exceptional.  The cockroach doing the back stroke on our table at midnight was not.

Love the music. Had a chicken sandwich that had grill marks on it. Very processed chicken sandwich tastes like rubber. Nice vibe but waitress not very kind at all.  She didn't seem like she liked her job at all.  If I had her again I would ask to be moved. A young gal that was bitchy from the get go

Awesome addition to Broaaaaadwayyyyyy. We saw Hall & Oates and although I have some reservations about their show in particular, the sound was great and the weather couldn't have been better. (Even the seated section is open air, so be prepared if the weather isn't good.) The lawn is very nice and if you get there early you can put your lawn chairs right behind a low wall that you can put your feet up on. Looked very comfy. Lawn chairs have to be the low kind though. Drinks were of course pretty high, but there was a large selection of draft and canned beers and liquor. Not all bars accepted credit cards though so be forewarned.
Nice, not overwhelming.  Friendly cool and chill.  Will is the man.  Packer fans couldn't get a better place to watch the game

We came here since all the places a couple of smaller venues didn't have a table. We didn't care for the food. We had much better food at Hattie B. the chicken felt like it was spoiled before they cooked it. Had to eat when we got back to the hotel. The place wasn't too crowded, that's why we decided to go in. It;s more of a sports bar (upper level completely) and downstairs there's a stage. The bathroom has a pink slanted counter and a lady handing out paper towels and a portable dispensing soap bottle for a tip. The counter reminded me of a strip joint vanity area. lol

 We stayed for a little bit. It was okay. The entire district seems chaotic spring break, vegas new orleans style. We may venture out a bit and try some other places that are less of a touristy trap and where the locals like to go.

Staci (yea with an "i") and Whitney were great! They made sure our drinks were never empty and made the best mixed shots. Even thought they paid me for this review I would recommend the Benchmark!  I'm totally kidding on the paid part. There was great live music and tv's were we could watch the NBA playoff game. They are worth the visit for good service, great drinks and music!

We really only decided to come here based on the live music we could hear from the speakers as we passed by and we were very pleased with our decision! Great beer selection and WONDERFUL pizza!!! I was not expecting bar food to be so delicious. The friendly staff and live music were an added bonus. Highly recommend!
Nice venue, but the price gouging is beyond unreasonable.  Plan ahead with a big budget if you plan to partake of anything ... $13.50 for a 16 oz craft beer

I like this bar, but I think it is absolutely bs that they make someone stand in the bathroom and put soap and paper towels in people's' hands and don't even pay them. They spent the time to make, print, and laminate signs informing their customers that they DO NOT pay their bathroom attendants to "encourage" tips. I tipped because it is not the bathroom attendant's fault, but I feel that this is not the correct way to run a business. If you want a bathroom attendant in your establishment, pay them. If you don't, I know damn well how to put soap on my own hands. Pick one. Happy to tip, but I don't like the approach taken of hiring bathroom attendants and then guilting people into helping them make approximately no money for doing a demeaning job.

The prices on concessions are out of this world. Water is $4.75. Beer is $16. A $9 bottle of wine is $50 or a glass is nearly $20. And you'll wait in line for a half hour. Oh my Jesus. I'll just dehydrate, thanks. The sound quality is horrible, you can't hear a thing, people stand in packs talking and yelling and acting like they're at a baseball game or something. So disrespectful to the artists, I am embarrassed on our city's behalf. I would suggest an area to the side for this foolishness? Get out of the way of the people who came here for something other than a mating ritual, please. We spent the whole 2.5 hours walking around trying to hear and see something. This venue had the potential to be really fabulous and a great outdoor attraction but I wouldn't go back if you paid me. It was honestly the worst concert experience I've ever had.
Ohh yeah, Best time ever. Looking forward to return visit!

I went for lunch here with 3 friends. My burger and salad were great but the two friends I was with only had sides - cornbread and mashed potatoes. The side of mashed potatoes was probably the smallest amount I have ever seen given. It was in a little container that ketchup would be in! I was in awe of how small this amount was especially with the price. They also told me that the cornbread was the most unique one they had ever tried and they didn't really enjoy it as it was so different. The atmosphere of the whole restaurant was very nice though.

My all time favorite honky tonk. $8 cocktails with two shots of yumminess in each drink. It cannot be beat. The location is epic, the music is unbelievable, the waitresses are super nice. The cocktails are the best. I cannot stop thinking about how awesome my experience was.

We have stopped here a few times for drinks before dinner. The music has always been great and service too. It's a total dive bar that we love visiting. They have lots of fun drink specials. They do serve food but I've never eaten there. Always a good place to stop!

I was there two nights ago and was on the top floor during last call. My friend and I purchased our final beverages and were rushed out of the top floor. No worries, we thought, let's just go down to the main floor. We come down the stairs to the security guards smoking weed in the staircase. I'm no cop so I didn't care, but they told us that we couldn't go into the main floor and that we would have to finish our drinks in the staircase and then we could get in line AGAIN outside to come back into the bar which was already closing.  I have a feeling they either wanted us to grease their pockets to get back in, or they were pissed we interrupted their smoking sesh.  I even mentioned hey man I don't care about the smoke or anything and he was like "it's CBD" lol ok buddy, I use cbd oil every day and as a California native with a valid medicinal marijuana card, I can tell the difference but nice try.   ended up having to pound my drink in a staircase reeking of piss to end my night because of these two douche bags, wouldn't go again. There are plenty of other venues nearby with better entertainment and less shady staff.
This is the best chicken and waffles I've ever had! Great Bloody Mary too! Wish I didn't have to go to Nashville for it!
Unfriendly service and very unpleasant... sorry pick another place and you will enjoy more!

Nashville's lounge revolution continues. We've gotten Nashville's take on Brooklyn, LA and Vegas. the back corner is very Miami Beach. When I walked in I, immediately, thought of Haven (RIP https://www.yelp.com/biz/haven-miami-beach-2). From the LED wall to the music to the drinks to the vibe... I didn't feel like I was in Nashville anymore. the back corner stands out and gives Middle Tennesseans something that's not readily available in this area. If you're in the mood for a little coastal cosmopolitanness (is that word? It's not a word), the back corner is about to be your new favorite place.
