The neighborhood gets things moving in the right direction. For as much as Germantown has (scenic streets, fancy high rises, coffee, good eats) it didn't have a nightlife destination. Putting one here makes a lot of sense. Building off the 5th & Taylor imprint, the back corner starts off fancy (but not pretentious) and builds to memorable. Upon entry, the first thing you notice is the LED wall and stage. With a changing display of electronic intoxication, you're drawn into a world far away from Lower Broad. If you can break your gaze away from the stage, you'll notice the upper and lower lounge seating. Intimate, cozy and a bit mysterious, the seating at the back corner lets you decide whether you want to be front & center or if you're rather sit back and take it all in. You can be as public or private as you'd like. If indoor seating isn't your thing, make your way outside to enjoy the fire pit and Germantown night sky. Just do us all a favor and refrain from smoking. Seeing cigarette butts along the patio or by (in??) the fire pit is not sexy and very off-brand.

All the above said and noted, the back corner is not a huge space -- which is a plus and minus. It's a plus because it never becomes the cavernous mess of bass and desperation. The minus is crowds gonna crowd and with a lot of people, the space will be tight. I don't know how to fix that. I suppose a velvet rope and waitlist will keep crowds at bay but neither feels very Nashville. Hmm... Another minus (relating to the size) is that there's only one bar. One bar in a space this cool is a bit tight. I know the space behind the bar isn't huge but I would staff it with 3 bartenders at a time so as to keep up with the crowd. Because you're going to want to drink. A lot. The cocktail program at the back corner is a bit unusual for Nashville -- and very Miami. Expect rum, colors and a boozy punch. Actually, the menu could use a punch. Get on that, tbc. Re drink progression... start with the gimlet. It's pretty to look at and refreshing to drink. All the mixers, juices, etc. are made in house so you're getting quality fare. From there, hit the No. 4 and, then, the No. 2. If you're still upright, drink some water. Water? Who am I kidding? Cocktails! You're in Miami, [redacted]! Well, sorta.

If you need some noshes, 5th & Taylor is serving up bites. Don't come here for dinner. Who eats food? Let the music and booze nourish your body. As perfect as the back corner is for DJ sets, live music (this *is* Nashville, after all) works as well. the back corner isn't the Downtown dance club people have wanted for a (looooong) while. But it is a welcome addition to the city's nightlife scene and, very possibly, you're new favorite place to go. Bienvenidos a Nashville.

Paid to attend their NYE event. Unfortunately the top floor flooded and we were not allowed in. We waited in line for over an hour and were told repeatedly they would get us in as soon as possible before they finally announced they were over capacity and no one else would be let in. I've called multiple times, written emails, and left Facebook reviews and messages and still have heard nothing back. I was promised a refund and they have completely avoided taking responsibly. Awful management/customer service.

Beautiful venue! Tons of concessions (despite hilarious $7 prices for water bottles, $15 "glasses" of wine, etc.) and clean, huge bathrooms. 
Tip - you can bring unsealed plastic bottles of water in. Lots of vendors outside charging $2. Do yourself a favor and grab a couple of those. Giant draft IPAs cheaper than Mich Ultra? IPA it is 

Parking - if you're lucky, there are free parallel spots downtown after 6pm, but of course not tons. $5 parking in the R lot across the pedestrian bridge, just need to walk over the bridge. Smaller lots near the venue $10-$50. 

No umbrellas allowed. Just read the rules first. Definitely did a pretty intense pat down and bag check so don't think you'll get away with sneaking something in. Saw them check someone's hair...  

Lawn area is spacious. Amazing views of Nashville. 
However, the lawn crowd every time I've been to Ascend has been awful. I've been to tons of outdoor venues like this and people are clapping along, paying attention, even dancing during the headliners! Went to two shows in the last week - had a visitor come just to see them. Lawn was just lots of bored people playing games on their phones in the lawn, not clapping, screaming at people who were up and dancing, carrying on loud conversations as if they were out at the park. It was so quiet for such a large venue, even the bands noticed... awkward. Jason Mraz, Cake and Ben Folds - not really your sit back in silence kind of bands. 

Basically, if you want the vibe of a symphony and are fine staying still and seated on your blanket, the lawn is your spot. If you're trying to dance, sing, enjoy a favorite band, you need to absolutely get pit standing tickets or seated tickets or you will be very disappointed. We ended up moving just so I could go stand on the sides of the venue with others who had my same thoughts to dance and sing along, so the crowd of loud talkers on their cell phones stopped flipping out about people dancing and having fun. Felt like a bad picnic of people watching people watch a concert. 

Also - very inconsistent sound. I thought the opener was set at a great volume, but was struggling to hear the headliners. I know there are sound rules for the city but please turn it up enough so people on the lawn can hear.

Will be back, but 100% in a seat or pit.

Nashville has a jewel with the Station Inn.  I have been there 3 times and each visit has been a treat.  I was there Saturday, Feb 21 and enjoyed Larry Cordle.  I took a friend and his daughter and we all had a GREAT time.  My friend bought 3 CDs for the night.

If the show starts at 9pm, I would get there around that time so you don't miss any great bluegrass music.  It's first come first serve as to seating and they have ATM outside to pay for the door.  They have a decent selection of beers and sodas.  Some nice snacks but we did not try their pizza or anything.  You can run a tab for your table and pay with credit card at the end.

My buddy summarized it as a great night to just listen to quality music and forget your worries.

Went there with a few peers from work. Downstairs was vibrant/loud but looked fun. We went upstairs so we could talk shop; have a sip and some
appetizers and enjoy some music. 
***I just reviewed my transactions on my card and realized I was charged twice for my order. Just be sure save review your receipt as they seem to have the going @honkytonk

Let me tell you something-There are many choices on Broadway, but I feel that Honky Tonk Central was one of the best--I simply had a fun time!

It was a Thursday Night-standing room only-it is a large bar/club with enough room to dance!  There were two different bands playing and they were both very talented!  They had great crowd control and rocked the house!  

There was a nice age mixture in the bar and I made friends and we crawled to a few more bars together for the rest of the night!  

The drinks were a lil off--so I moved to bottled beer to keep myself happy!  

Note:  They do ask for ID - bonus-No cover!  The bands play for tips--so be generous!

The Nightmare Before Dinner:

Came here for a weekday lunch, and was looking forward to the Poutine, and instead had to look past it.

The whole dish was cool, so that the cheese curds were not melted, they were congealed and hard.  The egg on top was underdone, and resting on fries that were not crispy.  The entire dish was so over salted, that there was no discernible flavors, other than salt.

Odds of returning?  Zero.

My wife and I caught Beth Hart on a Saturday night.  First...get there early.  We came in 2 hours before the show and still were about 150th in line.  Suppose it depends on the show.  Most main floor tables and balcony tables we full.  There was plenty of  space on the main floor to stand, but we were looking to sit for the night.  We grabbed two high top seats along  the bar on the right as you walk into the venue. Even with being 75-100 feet away the seats and sound was fine.

We split a  veggie quesadilla, chips and salsa, and fries.  The quesadilla was fresh and filling.  Beer was cold and readily available.

The staff at the bar was very busy, but still found the time to quickly check in wiht us often.   

Will definitely go to another show at 3rd and Lindsey when the opportunity arises.

If I could give this place zero stars I would! My friend's and I were there and the bouncer started picking on this guy that was intoxicated. All he was doing was singing. Meanwhile all these drunk women were doing the SAME THING and he didn't throw them out. We followed them out and my friend asked "why are you throwing him out? He wasn't doing anything" and he said "why don't you stop being a B*TCH and go to another bar". Now call me crazy, but I don't think that was warranted. If this is how the bouncers treat the patrons, you're going to lose A LOT of business! PS- he was a younger guy with short brown hair and too afraid to give his name when asked, COWARD!

Great Honky Tonk, we went on Thursday the 7th of nov 
The band was a really great band, I don't know their name but they were a family band from Nebraska???
They were a great band, The type of band that can play anything. Great bar -a lot of fun. Restroom was OK, There is an attendant which keeps it up a bit.

Interesting night. I was enjoying the night with my husband.  We started on the ground floor. I ordered a blue drink and they served it in a small fishbowl type glass. Now get this.... I go to the second floor and they ask me to pour it out. Why? Because they don't allow outside drinks ! What ?!?
I explained that I had purchased downstairs and accused me of lying. I go downstairs and ask for a manager. I explain the situation to him. He says "my bad, I never told the employees that we started this new drink." I ask him to go with me and explain to the bouncer because I was humiliated and I wanted an apology. He refused. Hmmm, just wondering if they treated me this way because I am Hispanic. Very rude stuff. 

I gave it 2 stars because the nachos were good.

Hanging out on Saturday Night with friends and decided to come here for dinner since it was the "hot place" to go.  Each floor has stage with performing band dependent on what genre of music you prefer.  Music was good.  Food was so  so...waited a loooong time to eat....when food finally arrived, fries were cold and chicken tenders salty.  Server gave us food/drink bill and we paid even before our food came! Not impressed.

This place is a lot of fun on a Sunday night.  We arrived around 8pm for their bluegrass jam.  There is no cover charge, and it lasts until 10-10:30pm or whenever the crowd dies down.  There is a circle of musicians playing bluegrass music in one corner, and a bunch of seating facing them.  It's nothing fancy - just a dive bar with your standard beer and limited bar food - no liquor.  People come and go, and the musicians are just jamming rather than performing for an audience.  It's a bit tough to hear them from afar as the microphones are not on (or at least it seems that way), and it gets loud with people chatting and trying to compete with the music.  I wish an announcement was made for everyone else to quiet down.  We sat about 10 feet from the musicians and had a hard time hearing them sing.  All in all, it's a great place to hang out on a Sunday evening.  Metered parking is free on Sunday evenings.

So I have a mixed reviews. We went here during the week because I LOVE rooftop bars but when they got there they said the rooftops weren't open. Although they said we could go up there, but there isn't anyone up there staff wise, which was kind of cool because we just got drinks and went upstairs and had the whole place to ourselves so that was awesome. But the bad part of the review was the food wasn't great at all. Just pub style food that felt like it was frozen and just fried to order but the worst part was I went up the bathroom and right when I walked in there was a cockroach just sitting at the sink which believe me I live in Florida I understand bugs are everywhere but definitely NOT something you want to see when you go to wash your hands and when you had just placed your food order.

Hands down, best time I had in Nashville!

I'm not into bluegrass music, per se, but when in Nashville you do as the natives. Though banjos twanging may not be my thing I do love live music. Especially live acoustic music.

We went on a Sunday night which means Bluegrass Jam Session night! There is no cover but it's actually quite priceless. Artists sit around in a circle-ish form playing various songs. Performers will come and go at their leisure, joining mid-song sometimes, playing different instruments and singing their hearts out. I was amazed how well the sounds meshed together when I'm sure some of the players had never been there before. They did a great job of passing the baton and letting everyone have a little solo jam session to highlight their skills.

On the night I went, there was a young lady of probably just 14 or so. The group of adults were so welcoming to her and they were very encouraging, as well. I loved the open & accepting nature of the more seasoned jammers.

The jam session starts at 7pm with audience members coming & going but I suggest getting there prior to 7 to ensure getting yourself a seat.  There isn't much fancy beer but they do have the usual PBR, Bud, etc plus a couple of local brews. A pitcher of Yazoo Pale Ale is $15 which is a great deal and better than Bud...though a pitcher of that will run you just $11. In addition to drinks, they serve food but it looked a bit sketchy. I would just get food prior to hanging at Station Inn.

I saw people of all sorts, all ages, some on dates, big groups of friends, some families including father & son, partners or performers sitting solo - it's a real come one, come all type of place where no one can really feel out of place.

It's dark and a dive but dang is it a delightful deal!

At first I was in lust with this venue, but it wore off pretty quickly.
A number of concerts I have attended and the sound system and view has always been good,
but then they put some kind of black netting on the fence and now it's more of a sore thumb.

The city should be embarrassed that this place is now tacky looking.
The prices were a little high BUT my Bloody Mary was amazing, worth it for sure. The DJ they had on the roof top was so so good. We had a blast here!

Having three floors was definitely a great set up, and there were plenty of different music types. It provides a great view of broadway and you could spend a majority of your night here because there are so many options for great music. Although the service at the bar was pretty good, a gin and tonic was $9 and they tried charging for cups of water, so that was a little disappointing. I would definitely recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville because of the wide variety of options.

Tourist review ahead!

We visited Nashville for a couple days, originally planning to attend a big-name concert that was canceled after we'd booked our flights. We decided to go on the trip anyway and found out about the Big Stage Mondays (songwriter showcase) show at 3rd and Lindsley. We grabbed a couple tickets ($10 each) and showed up early in the afternoon for the show (doors at 2pm, though it was sweltering out and they let us in a little earlier than that.) 

They have some typical bar food, and a full bar for drinkin'. I didn't see much on the menu I could eat (gluten-free options) so I didn't eat anything. I did have a couple local ciders, so that was cool. We grabbed a table with a good view and settled in for a show that featured a couple local solo songwriters and a duo that seemed to have big league potential. The songwriters we saw had some serious country music credentials and even though country is not my usual first choice, it was a really cool experience. The show was a couple hours long. 

Note that this place is a decent walk from the main strip of bars downtown; walkable, but in 90+ heat it was pretty unpleasant.

This venue gets it right when it comes to live music. Period. The variety is fab. The sound system is great. The stage and lighting are great. Tonight we are watching a U2 cover band. Dang! They are incredible. I feel like it is 1987!!
We also enjoy the local artists playing original music. There is live music every single night! Weekend acts will be bigger draws typically. 
Not to be missed is the Journey tribute that plays here quarterly, Resurrection. You won't believe how spot on they are!!  The Time Jumpers are here regularly, Vince Gill often sits in, and they are awesome too. Very traditional country. Many of the acts aren't country at all. Just wanted to clarify! 
Arrive at least an hour early for the more popular shows. if you want a seat. The venue is spacious but only holds about 300. The perfect size if you ask me!
This is mainly a seated venue. But there is a dance floor. The food menu is pretty good. Their wine selection is solid too. Far better than many typical live music Clubs. 
Put this place on your list to check the entertainment calendar, whether you are a local or paying an upcoming visit to Nashville. 
Parking is free immediately in front of the venue. There is a parking lot next door that sometimes charges $5, but usually not. Uber is easy as this venue is right near downtown.

I have been to 3rd and Lindsley a few times now to see the cover band Guilty Pleasures.  This place is a pretty good place to see a band.

So you come in and there is a bar to your right.  Also note if you walk directly to your right there is a bathroom there.  Typically less busy than the other one.  There are tables throughout including upstairs in a couple of balcony areas.  

The stage is at the back and you have to go down a couple of steps to the floor which I suppose is a dance floor or mosh pit depending on what type of band you are seeing.  Bathrooms are off to the side of the dance floor, multi-seaters, but still can get a line going.  Depending on how packed it is, you need to plan ahead.

Drinks are stout depending on the bartender.  I like stout.  I noted they do have Tito's vodka and they have a section of top shelf liquors for those that don't want the rot gut well drinks.  I don't want those. 

Overall, I have had some fun times at 3rd and Lindsley.  Go check out a live band and get your dance on and drink on here!

We went to the Monday songwriters show.  It was amazing!  I had bought my tickets a few weeks in advance and having never been to Nashville I wasn't sure what to expect.  There were 4 songwriters who had written for huge stars and told really interesting stories.  We walked from Broadway.  We did eat there and it is typical bar food.  I was happy to see they had a number of vegetarian options. I had the veggie quesadilla which was huge.  It came with a number of fresh vegetables inside and was better than a lot of vegetarian bar food we ate on Broadway.  The last day we were in Nashville our uber driver who is a musician at night told us we had to go to songwriters at 3rd and Lindsley and was happy to hear that we already did.  It's a great way to spend a Monday afternoon.

Came for drinks only.   Bartender was amazingly friendly.  We came early so there was no live music.  We had just arrived in town.
Wish we had come back later.  Regrettably we went to kid rocks to have a terrible food/bartending experience with music... 
When in Nashville and you want to experience southern hospitality...  Come HERE!!!!!!

Great Venue! Great Event! Great Staff!

That's the short version of the review. But, in all seriousness, this place provided the perfect setting for an evening spent with Judah & The Lion. 

Great Hometown crowd came out and appeared to put this place to capacity. Layout is really nice, and the grass area provides for a nice casual way to enjoy events. They offer rental chairs or you can bring your own....or you can bring a blanket or just sit in the grass. 

Staff was friendly and helpful and had no issues anywhere. Security did a great job processing large volume of people quickly so we could get in to the event.

Plenty of vending stations to get a drink or some food to enjoy with the show. Prices are on par with any other venue you've been to previously. 

If you haven't been, this place is really awesome, especially on a day where the temps didn't get to high. Put this one on your bookmarks to try and catch a concert, we will definitely be returning here!

Our waitress was awesome. The venue was packed, all seats full. Service was timely, cheerful and downright delightful. The drinks and foods were very reasonably priced and tasty. 

We saw Tim Akers & The Smoking Section last night at this venue; to say the band was amazing is a gross understatement! I have not yet had enough coffee to think of the appropriate words to describe this band of 16 or so musicians. 


Tim and his band @ 3rd and Lindsley combined to make a wonderful 33rd wedding anniversary celebration for us.

Open seating, food was ok. Mostly people or there to drink and have a good time.
We were there from 12 noon till around 145, struggling singers!
Free rockin' music and all the food trucks and beer trucks you could ask for.  Don't get no better than that!
Nice place. Cold beers. What else can you ask for. Will stop by again on next trip to Nashville.

I didn't go here to eat but I definitely went here to dance. This is one of Nashville's favorite dance bars and it gets poppin! If you're looking for a good night out this is definitely one of the places to be at!

Worst. First and last time there. Ordered food, came it to pick it up, and they all had no idea what I was talking about. Super lazy employees. The guy just came over and told me 8 min. I asked why. He said it just came though. After 40mins of waiting. Total garbage. The building should be shut down. Ain't got a GED between the 4 of the idiots there. I said I wanted it cancelled and the guy just walked away. It's a joke there and way overpriced.

Came here during a bachelorette party for some lunch. We went to the second floor and sat down and listened to the awesome live music that was happening at the time! 

We ordered some beers and fried pickles to start. There were 8 of us and more than enough for all of us to have plenty of fried pickles so that was great!
Not all of us ordered lunch but those who did got some wraps and I got a salad.

The food was pretty average nothing over the top stuck out but it was very good and the overall experience was definitely worth stopping by! 

Definitely somewhere you should come if you're visiting Nashville even if you're not coming for food, it's awesome how there's live music on the different levels and a great place to just take it all in! Plus the windows give you a nice view of broadway so you can take it all in!

You know those Native Nashvillians who are super anti-broadway because they feel like it depicts natives inaccurately? Thus they never explore what Honky Tonk highway has to offer? Well, I am not one of those natives. I have lived here since I was three years old and love embracing some of Nashville's most well known culture, it's country roots! That being said, even if you don't like country music you will have a blast here.

Top 5 Reasons Why I LOVE Honky Tonk Central

1) You never know who you are going to meet here. Seriously, I have met people from all over the world here! One time I had a conversation with an astronaut from Australia. I know locals get sick of the tourists, but honestly I love them!

2) The crowd is always rowdy. If you are looking for chill vibes then don't come here. The crowd is always so much fun! Everyone is mingling, dancing, drinking and it makes for an awesome environment.

3) Celebrations get special treatment. We came here for my friends 21st and ended up on stage/getting a ton of free drinks. I always see bachelorette parties here and it is a great place to celebrate anything.

4) They don't solely play country music. There is some rock, top 40 and throwbacks into the mix. I always love it when they play the old 90's song! And everyone goes to the stage and dances! Seriously love this place.

5) Three stories, three different vibes, and three balconies. Enough said!

PS: 1st floor is where a lot of the older people stay and they play a lot of 80's rock/famous older songs. 2nd floor is a lot more chill. 3rd floor is my favorite, a lot of young people, locals and newer country/music. Check it out!

Great rooftop bar! 

My friend and I came here to grab a couple drinks before the Stanley Cup Final game 3. There was a country band playing on the first floor. We took the elevator up to the roof and found two seats at the bar. They were running a pretty cool special: anyone in Preds gear could get two for one local beers. Love the support of the hometown team. 

I liked the atmosphere. It wasn't as insanely packed as the other rooftops. The bartenders were all nice. We headed back downstairs after a couple drinks to check out the band. Great vibe. Nice TV setup at the bar. I would definitely hit this place up again.

I'm giving this concert venue NO stars.......
Storming and lightening last night, they didn't cancel concert.. instead they opened the gates at 9pm.
Storming and they do not allow umbrellas.
I absolutely hate this venue. My GA tickets were $40 PLUs $50 in additional charges from Live Nation.

I will not support this venue.
It sucks. I do not recommend it.
Worst concert venue in Nashville..  sopping wet, muddy, no umbrellas, no cover or shelter from a storm and they open gates and have concert after everyone left because of safety measures..

YOU SUCK!

Hidden gem in the side roads of Nashvegas. It all depends on the music at the end, and we were lucky. JazzCountry - awesome. The location itself is classic. It is cosy but not classy. Not posh but livrly with some old items everywhere. An old piano, signed guitars which you can buy fir 300-1000 bucks. This could be a nice gift. Better than in a gift shop - buying China products. So a great place. But on the rough side, but this was fir me even better.

My fiance and I stopped here for a quick lunch on a break from our guided tour. Originally we were going to go to a place down the street but there wasn't any seating available so we settled for here instead...

Atmosphere: Very open floor with bar in the middle of everything, a stage up front, kitchen in the back, and high top tables lining the walls and windows. The windows in the front behind the stage and on one side of the restaurant are huge and let lots of light in. Not surprisingly, IT IS VERY LOUD. If you are looking to have a conversation with someone, do not plan on going here for your meal. My fiance and I were shouting at each other, even after sitting at the very back tables. They keep several of the windows open so if you don't want to be cold, try and score a seat at the tables against the wall. There are minimal decorations, a few posters and nostalgic ads but it looks like you'd expect a restaurant in the honky tonks to look. When we went it wasn't overly crowded but I know at peak hours it can get pretty cramped.

Service: Our waiter was fine. He came over pretty quickly and took our order. When we asked to move tables (it was too cold by the windows) he was very accommodating. Our drinks came out quickly as well as our food. We probably waited about 10 minutes or so. The waiter didn't check in with us, but maybe that's not the norm in a place like this? When we were done he brought our check and thanked us.

Food: The menu is pretty much all sandwiches, wraps, and burgers. There were some appetizers and salads. I think there may have been some pizza of sorts too. I did get a salad, the "Sienna", which had grilled chicken, strawberries, mandarin oranges, red onions, almonds, and blue cheese in it with a balsamic dressing. It was okay. Nothing to rave about but as I was looking for something semi-healthy, it was a decent choice. There was a huge amount of lettuce and plenty of strawberries. If I were making the salad at home I would've used a blend of greens vs. iceberg (which I could tell was bagged because it came with the little shredded carrots in it and had that bagged flavored taste), more blue cheese, and slightly more mandarin oranges. Also more chicken. The chicken was okay but a little dry for my liking. I think some cucumbers would be a nice touch too. The dressing was fine but I would've offered a flavored vinaigrette like raspberry or orange. This is me being a salad snob though. Like I said, a fine salad. My fiance got the "Southern Style BBQ Sandwich" (pulled pork  with chipotle BBQ sauce and pickles). He said it was good. The pulled pork was flavorful on it's own but the BBQ sauce elevated it with a tang and sweetness. The amount of pork was decent, the bun was standard, and the fries were average. It came with a side of coleslaw that also decent. It wasn't drenched in mayo or vinegar and tasted fresh. Being a bar, they had a good selection of drinks. They also have a kids menu available.

Cost: Reasonable. My salad was $11.25 and my fiance's handheld was $10.25. I can't remember seeing anything over $15.00 actually. Our meal with a soft drink and beer was under $40.00, so not bad at all.

Would I go back? Eh, maybe. I feel like it's kinda a been there, done that situation. I don't think there is anything on the menu I am dying to try but I wouldn't NOT go back, especially if there was a good band there or something. It's not the best place I've ever been to but not the worst. If you picked this place you would probably have a fine experience, but if you went somewhere else I don't think you'd be missing out on anything either.

My husband & I are in our 60's and were entering this establishment, which we have been going to for YEARS & this PUNK ASS RENTA COP, RUDELY told me I had to enter on the other side!! I obeyed his COMAND!! As I was trying to enter, another elderly couple were exiting the entrance!! I asked the RENTA COP, aren't you gonna YELL at them!! He grabbed me and told me "Have a nice evening and told me to LEAVE!!! That's OK!! We will spend our MONEY somewhere else!! There are LOTS of BETTER PLACES on BROADWAY!! Honky Tonk Central lost our business!!! I could of had him arrested for assault!!!!! I guess they only want DRUNK YOUNG PEOPLE in that PLACE!!

Waitress brought the wrong drink TWICE, I'd forgive it cuz it's loud but she had attitude the whole time. The band playing (which was quite good by the way) came around with a tip bucket pestering for tips, yes, pestering, then COMPLAINED the tip we gave was too small! Then called us out on stage about it, who does that? Would have gladly tipped at the end of our meal rather than her hassling our table while eating after only 1 song! There are many great places in Nashville, this isn't one of them. Other than that the food is good but its not worth the price.

I hate to leave this review because I don't want it to turn into a cluster like the bars on Broadway!  BUT....this was our favorite night in Nashville. Such a fun vibe with the greatest band. If you get the chance to see Caldwell Jack & the Six Pack....run don't walk!!!
I actually thought this was one of the worst bars I visited while on my trip to Nashville. It was dirty, smelled, and the drinks weren't that great.
Fantastic open-air venue on the river just south of downtown Nashville. Super easy entry/exit setup and great visibility from all seats.

Touch and go to say the least, but the music is SO worth the stop. My husband and I stumbled upon this place after hopping around downtown and we are so glad we did. A guys named Isaac Mathews was playing and he's absolutely incredible. We made it a point to find out his schedule and come back for round 2 the next day. Service is touch and go- our first day we had incredible service and the 2nd not so much. Again, didn't make us want to leave because this guy kicks ass. Suck it up and get a frozen bushwaker for $5 and listen to some good jams.

I had a very bad brunch experience here. The food was not good, and overpriced. The waitress was being overworked/stressed and ran my card for mine as well as someone else's order :( 

2 stars because it's a cool bar and i have hopes that they can serve a beer better than they can make eggs and function on brunch days!

0l
Great music. Poor Service. 
Stopped in wednesday night on the reccomendation of a friend. The music was great so we decided to hangout on the second floor. I ordered a beer and the fritos pie from our bartender, Samantha. The beer was good but my food seemed to take forever. 
After I'd long since finished my beer I finally got the attention of the other bartender who grabbed her for me and said I wanted to cancel my food because we were leaving. She said I couldn't cancel because my food was likely already done and waiting but that she hadn't gone to get it yet.

I could understand if the bar was slammed but it had actually been pretty empty for the last 15min and she was joking around at the register with the other bartender, so to know my food was done and just getting cold was ridiculous. 
She of course went to the back and came out with a fresh attitude and luke warm food.
I choked it down and we left. Overall horrible experience. With so many venues to choose from in the area I would never recommend this place based solely on service.

Went to a private all white party Labor Day weekend and I was impressed with this spot. Since being in Nashville I've not found a grown and sexy spot yet. However, this event was everything. I hope there will be more to come.

Such a great stop! We went in on a Sunday night (Labor Day trip), and this place was so worth at least stopping into for a half hour for authentic blue grass music. Sundays are a pick-up night where anyone can bring an instrument and join in. It was pretty neat. I bet the bands are even better.

If you want the Nashville experience stop here for a beer before carrying on in the Gulch or Midtown. It's a must-see-spot.

They only serve beer, but even if you don't drink beer I strongly suggest stopping by for the music.

If you like music you'll love this place. The grass in here is blue and the atmosphere friendly. We even witnessed a proposal from one of the musicians from on stage one of the nights we went. Get off Broadway and see the real Nashville.

I dislike having to give only 2 stars, I really do because the venue is great! The Staff is AWESOME, funny and had a great sense of humor. The service was really top notch and the bar tab at the end of the night was mind-blowing to me in a very good way!... So why the 2 star review... Welp. Simple. BLOWN SPEAKER Stage right (left if facing the stage) hanging stack middle speaker in my ear all night kind of ruined my boogie time for my favorite band that I traveled 2000 miles to see. Even the band was pissed for the first few songs because the sound tech didn't get it dialed in. Bad form. It is what it is, i'll for sure go back and when I do, if the issue is corrected (I highly suspect it will be) I'll rewrite my review. See ya next year.

I still can't believe this is a free show! This event is three days of incredible bands. My sister and I went and saw CZ Ward and Matt & Kim. 
The crowd was huge but very polite. 
There were food trucks and merchandise tables surrounding the event. 
The stage was huge - very few places you couldn't see the stage from. 
The line up was excellent a full day of music on each day. Jimmy Eat World, Cold War Kids, and Larkin Poe were other bands playing. A lot of people brought their children, dogs, and picnics. Lots of dancing happening. It's a quick walk to the Johnny Cash museum and Ryman from where they host this concert. The river walk is also near by. For a free show - it is run very well. A lot of fun - I'm hoping to come back next year.

Really fun experience on a Sunday night and actually FREE! You can read all about it from other reviews but a tip that there is ONLY beer, no wine or hard liquor. And they only serve pizza and popcorn so eat beforehand if that's not what you're looking for. 

Also, def come before 7:30. That's when we arrived and there was already a line. We were the very last to get in while others had to wait til someone left to take their seat. It's seating room only, no standing so they can't just pack them in. At 8pm, I overheard the hostess say there were about 90 ppl outside waiting in line!

What an excellent venue! The sound system was terrific.  The music was great. Our waitress did a tremendous job with a full house. The food was typical bar food. Prices were just fine. No complaints about the food or prices. The bathroom was uniquely situated.  There are two locations for the bathrooms. Parking is a bit tight for free parking. Open seating everywhere.  I'd try the upper level next time.

I had a great opportunity to volunteer for a non profit here during several concerts in 2016 including Twenty one Pilots, Weezer with Panic at The Disco, BORNS, John Williams with the Nashville Symphony Star Wars and E.T, Jimmy Buffett and so many more. It was a great experience for a good cause.

 I wanted to chime in here on the fact that the volunteers work the concessions a lot of the time and we did nor do get paid for it. It went to whatever organization we chose. So appreciate the workers behind the counters volunteers or not the line gets long and they work as fast as they can. The staff treated us great only complaint was parking. We could park and walk across the bridge however we would get there at 2pm and leave at 3am and tired so sometimes we would pay to park closer. I think Ascend is a great asset to Nashville and that was 2016 much has changed they have improved a lot on the venue as I am a patron now not a volunteer. 

Unfortunately concessions are overpriced like all events are. One artist (I will not say who) requested us not to serve anything with a bottle (that could be thrown) water for example so we had to open water bottles and other drinks pour them into plastic cups. It was strange pouring 5.00 water but could not let the customers take the bottles.  For the most part people where great about it as we explained that it was at the artists request not Ascend and its for everyone's safety. 

As a volunteer and a paying customer I enjoy the venue, lots of space for seating. But parking super close ehhh but that is Nashville so you get used to the little lots that charge a fortune with the kind stranger who will watch your car all night for an extra 10.00 :) Thank you Ascend for the memories and your employees being extremely kind when volunteering and when being a customer to the shows.I love to see familiar faces when we attend events there. 

A MUST there is something for everyone !

Worth coming down to watch some real local bluegrass. we popped in on a sunday evening show. we stayed for an hour. although i enjoyed it, it was pretty repetative. we enjoyed a pitcher for about $15 and grabbed some gear being sold off to the side. we enjoyed an hours worth of the bluegrass jam, which was pretty interesting to see. everyone flowed nicely and seemed to know a thing or two about playing some bluegrass. i feel this was fun, and an interesting thing to see, but i wouldnt spend my whole night here. the place fills up quick with long lunch tables, and chairs on each side.

Terrible service. Ordered food, it sat at the bar for over 10 minutes. When asked about wait time on the food, they told us our food had been sitting at the bar for a while because they didn't know who had ordered it. Everything was cold. They never came back to check on us. BY FAR THE WORST EXPERIENCE.
Was in town for 3 days and every night we ended up at this bar! Music and Service were top notch. Doyle was the best bartender in town. We will be back again!

We have NEVER had a more enjoyable music experience. New Monday is an evening spent with remarkable, I repeat, remarkable musicians.  Each one, as they did their "thing", blew us away. The love they have for each other is palpable and there was humor and a spontaneity that made this small, low-key, pizza/beer place come alive. We did not want this gig to end-ever. Val Storey and Carl Jackson are not to be missed if you can help it.

Honky Tonk Central is proof that Nashville has a *lot* of tourists. Don't get me wrong: I appreciate the fact that HTC helped to revitalize lower Broad (I remember when there wasn't much Downtown that wasn't on 2nd Ave) but this sort of Nashville experience is definitely one you're going to want to wait and bring your out of town friends or hit up as part of a lower Broad crawl. I can see the appeal HTC has for tourists but it's the local landscape that has me a bit confused.*

By now, you know the score: no cover (much appreciated), multiple levels, big crowds of folks committed to woo-hooing their way to a good time, live music that may or may not be pleasing to the ear, tvs, drinks of fluctuating strength, etc. You know what to expect. If, for some reason, you find yourself drawn to HTC, make your way to the balcony. The breeze and view are the star attractions at this Downtown Nashville mainstay. To be able to look out and see the sea of humanity bathed in neon and walking the street in droves is a pretty powerful scene for anyone who can remember a time when such a scene wasn't common. HTC may not be my cup of tea (or, jug of moonshine) but I recognize its importance in the Downtown Nashville landscape and appreciate its role in changing a dead scene into a thriving one. It may not be a place I'd go every weekend but when I have friends in town, I wouldn't doubt that I'll be sucked into its orbit... along with the rest of you. You can't fight the moonlight.

*Which brings me back to my opening sentence: there are so many tourists coming to Nashville, HTC doesn't have to worry about a locals contingent.

We went up to the rooftop for a change of scenery from the bars on Broadway. The views are nice, and there was a DJ spinning top-40 style music, so it was definitely different from the live country music everywhere else. The bartenders were awesome and the chicken fingers were actually very good...I'm not really a "chicken fingers" person, but these were great. I would definitely come back.

First time here visiting from California. Came here on a Tuesday night and had a great time! Our server was nice and quick, the restaurant itself could be a little cleaner but nothing too dirty. We ordered a few drinks and some appetizers. The nachos were huge and delicious! The nacho cheese had a small kick to it which made it taste better than regular nacho sauce. The fried pickles were great and the ranch even better. The drinks were alright, small and expensive. However if you're in the area give this place a try. It has two different levels and a stage on each, which is fun to experience the live music.

I'm not a country music fan, and after walking down all of the honky tonk, it was refreshing to hear top 40 music blasting through the street. When we walked to the door bouncer checked our ID's (like any club or bar would) and began to hold up my ID to the light, he  bent and twisted it, he even asked the bouncer if it looked real. I'm not sure how things are around here, but in the Tri-State area I'm accustomed to bouncers scan your ID. Perhaps it's a thing Nashville to invest in doing as well.

It's a shame that my first impression wasn't very good, because this place was an otherwise really good bar. We were there early so it wasn't crowded but people were slowly making their way down the honk-tonk. 

This place has an elevator so after a whole day of walking it was nice to use that instead of stairs. Their outdoor patio was really nice and you get a view of the Nissan Stadium from it. Again, the music was far better, imo, then most of the country music playing at some of the other places.

Alley Taps is located in Printers Alley but on the East side of Church around the corner from the Courtyard Marriott.  

Just opened a few months back and the inside is very nicely refurbished - a stage to the left, long L shaped bar along the wall and a front room that has cozy leather furniture. 

Entertainment is no cover, 7 days a week and a bit different vibe than Broadway - more of a jazz blues vibe that is nice.   Note the bands work for tips only so keep that in mind and feed their jar accordingly.  

Full bar, limited local beer ... but our favorite West Coast IPA was on draft which was a plus.  Full bar, 2 for 1 happy hour 3-7pm was a perk.  

Plenty of servers behind the bar kept drinks flowing so that was appreciated. 

The total area is engulfed by the music so that could be good or bad - for us we couldn't chat or talk to bartender as we sat at the bar.  The Mgt may want to consider a bit of volume control.  

The menu is limited and very much bar food. We ordered a pretzel that was over micro waved and not very good.  I would not recommend coming in hungry unless things change (or your drunk and have to  eat).  

Overall nice place, good music, decent happy hour.

Awesome rooftop bar pulling great beers. Great view and games. But the highlight was our bartender Bobby Two Times. He was personable and funny. When we told him we were from out of town he wrote out a personalized list of places we should visit in Nashville, many of which were the highlights of the trip. Can't recommend this place enough!

Great music...

...but as a restaurant: below average food, below average cleanliness, amateurish, average service. 

Go for the music but eat somewhere else. Unimaginative bar food.

The Back Corner is exactly what Nashville needed! It's the perfect place for the locals to go to for a night out. It's literal the back corner of 5th and Taylor. Not a small place, but it's just the perfect size. It's smoke free, but there's a good size patio with a fire pit! There's no cover at door and no line! Score! We had table service right next to the dance floor and it was completely worth it with a minimum of only $350 and bottles starting at $150. But it choose not to bottle service, it's not hard getting a drink at the bar either. The DJ last night was pretty good, played lots of different genres! Great atmosphere and the crowd was a good mix! Will definitely be back for another event!

Had tickets for Doobie Brothers/Steely Dan show for May 20, 2018. Show was to start at 7:30. At around 6:00 there was a Severe Thunderstorm  in the area. By 7:30 there was still rain and lightning in the area. At 8:00 with rain still falling Ascend chose to open the gates at 8:15 with yet more rain on the way. 

This was a poor decision by management. There are many music venues here in Nashville. Avoid Ascend.

3 girlfriends and I came to town for a long girls weekend. It was recommended that we go to Nashville Underground. We made reservations for 8:30pm. Once we got inside we waited about 5 minutes for someone to come to the hostess stand. We were met by a very rude and abrasive guy who told us he had no tables available for us and that it would be at least 20 minutes before something opened up. He said he would go check to see if he could fine one. While he was gone a very friendly security guard came to us to make sure we had been helped. He told us there were plenty of tables opened on the second floor and that we should just go up there and grab one which is what we did. After 30 minutes of sitting at a table with no staff we were finally told it would at least 45 minutes before we could even place an order and much longer before we could get our food.

While the venue manages to attact some of the better acts in town, tickets are incredibly overpriced. $100+ for some shows to sit in the grass and have your view blocked by people constantly moving & stealing spots? No thanks.

On top of that it just seems pointless to have an outdoor only venue in Nashville. This really should have been built as an indoor-outdoor venue, like stadiums with rectractable roofs. There's a high chance of rain basically constantly in Nashville...and if you're lucky enough for it to not rain you're going to have at least 95 degree heat and full humidity most of the summer. Then you have the entire winter season when they can't do shows. Plus with it being totally outdoors they've become a major headache for people who live in that area of downtown and even toward Donelson (not me, I'm not dumb enough to move by a stadium, but just saying). They're also terrible at communication when it comes to weather delays...they don't seem to ever cancel and instead think it's acceptable to push an opening act back to 10:30pm! 

Parking has been another issue...it's a major headache to get in and out and parking anywhere near there is at least $30 most shows.

Not to mention it has recently come out that supposedly the venue was built with money that was meant to go to flood victims...wouldn't surprise me in the slightest.
Shelley is the best bartender!  Great time. Great drinks. Great music. In the heart if the Broadway district.  Good music. Sarah,Beckie and Andrew are awesome!

This bar is a fun place to visit. We were on a bar hop tour. The music was good and everyone was having fun and dancing. They had the game on so it was nice to watch the game, enjoy the music and have a couple of drinks. 

There were a couple of reviews that mention the venue. I will say that the venue is huge and lots of space for a lot of people. I posted a picture of the crowd!

Overall: I will give this place 4 stars. Fun atmosphere and good music.

Lots of great reviews for this place. But I must have gone at a bad time. We went for happy hour and it was buy one get one free, we ordered a double (recommended by our bartender) and it was weak. But still we were looking forward to the food that had mixed reviews.

We ordered the nachos, the breadsticks witch cheese, and the buffalo wings. The prices were about right for Nashville, it was $40 for three appetizers and 2 drinks. But we wouldn't spend our money here again.

The food was pretty rough, the breadsticks were yummy, but the nachos were from a bag and the sour cream came pre-packaged.
The wings were not bad, but definitely nothing to brag about.

Basically think of this place as cheap bar food and cheap drinks.

The service was interesting. We weren't sure whether to seat ourselves or order at the bar, we found out later that you ordered at the bar. That was all fine until we went to a table and we weren't sure whether they run it over it or not, my husband noticed it had come out and was sitting on the bar for about 5 minutes, so he went up to get it. He was told that they usually run it but we're busy.

Overall, I would only come back here to listen to the music or escape broadway for a cheap drink. We weren't able to listen to the music, but the line up looked pretty solid. You can see the line up in the photo I posted.

Well, the server has ignored us twice. So... all I can say so far is they are good for music, but if you aren't drinking, they aren't going to wait on you. 

To be continued...

We were ignored again. My husband had to track down the server to take our order. 

Don't wait until the last minute and get mediocre bar food from here. Come early and sample one of the better food opportunities Nashville has to offer, then come here for the music. 

Oh and don't order a margarita, not even a top shelf, they suck here.

I was a tourist which maybe made me love this place even more than the average joe, but how could I pass up the chance to go to a place called "Honky Tonk Central"?! We were not disappointed and had a blast! It seems to be a big place for bachelor/bachelorette parties too because we saw several from out of town.

I had the key lime pie drink which was excellent and truly/dangerously tasted exactly like key lime pie. The bands cover popular country music songs and it is just a lot of fun over three levels with windows open and a casual, welcoming ambiance. The fried pickles are so yummy! I had my share visiting Nashville and I liked these best. 

The staff is super friendly as well. One server we had, Josh (I think his name was), was awesome and made a friend with everyone that came in. I loved the vibe and the bar tradition of "hollerin' and swallerin" -- fun, fun time.

This place is the perfect venue for an aging concert goer like myself. If you come early, you can sit at a table with service and everything. They get a wonderful and wide range of acts, from up and coming local bands, to 90s artists, and festive cover bands. The shows start on time, the space is very well designed, and there's just an amazingly intimate feel. Whether at a Moon Taxi, Yacht Rock Revue, Jewel, Wild Feathers, or the Long Players, it's a an evening well spent. The Sunday night Lightning 100 broadcasts are a particular favorite. Those things run like a Swiss clock, and on a school night, I sure appreciate that.

I've been to most of the popular music venues in Nashville now so it's hard not to compare one to another and see how they stand up to each other. The War Memorial Auditorium is a perfectly fine place to come and see a show, but just not my favorite due to some reasons I'll list below. Although it is an indoor concert venue you enter through a security check outside and then into the courtyard with the 'Victory' statue. The location and the exterior is the most unique thing about the auditorium. The inside, however, does not wow. My friend and I saw the Haim concert here, and that was awesome to see them! 

Pros:
-They have multiple concession stands and bar areas for snacks/drinks
-We had a good experience with the staff, from the security people to the bartenders
-Because the auditorium isn't very big and the seating is in the shape of a 'U' it is easy to see the acts no matter where you sit

Cons: 
-The bathrooms are in a basement so if you have seats on the upper level you have to go back down two sets of stairs
-Although historic, it really needs some updates like little lights on the stairs so that you don't trip and fall! 
-As with any concert venues there are lines, lines and more lines for everything

Overall, if good acts come here I'll go back. It's a decent venue with good seating and acoustics.

Do you enjoy the outdoors? Do you enjoy music? Do you enjoy venues that are easily accessible to downtown and there are multiple parking/transportation options? If yes then I'll see you down at Ascend since that's where I'll be listening to every music act/concert I can here!

I've been to two shows here (The Lumineers and Ray LaMontagne) and I enjoyed my experience at the venue both times (although the Ray concert was super weird but that's another story about him as an artist)

Other pluses to Ascend are that security lines are efficient, they allow you to bring in sealed plastic water bottle per person, they have concession stands and multiple bathrooms. If you are coming from out of town to see a show here then you can walk to Broadway after and continue the fun after the show since all the bars are close by here. 

The only negative thing I can think to say is that with this Tennessee weather there is always the chance that your show will get cancelled due to a thunderstorm or severe weather (of course this has nothing to do with the venue). However, on a warm summer evening Ascend is the place to be!
Loved the third floor bar and view of the water area.   Our server was friendly and prompt.   We enjoyed a shrimp po boy while enjoying the sunshine.  It was flavorful.   Definitely will be back

This....this is what I've been waiting for in Nashville! I'm not a honky tonk kind of girl and I don't enjoy overcrowded bars with bad live music so this felt like a breath of fresh air! For one, having a DJ that is spinning house music is almost unheard of around town so definitely keep that up...please! The other really redeeming point to this lounge is that the drinks are good and they are inexpensive. I'm so used to going to new bars and paying $15 for a bad drink making it very difficult to order more than 1 without taking out a second mortgage. The Back Corner actually has drinks under $10 and they are delicious! 
The vibe in there is relaxing and cool. It's easy to go in there, make yourself comfortable, drink a couple cocktails and just chill for hours. Next time I'm going hungry because the snacks looked pretty great!

What a great place to see a show! No frills, just a nice bar with fair prices and good music. If you go on a night where there's a cover charge, remember that it's cash only on the way in (you can use a card at the bar), but there's an ATM outside. I also loved that there was a bit of free parking out back.

Monday nites with the TIME JUMPERS still the best music deal in the country! And they start playing at 8PM now so the show's over about 10:30. We arrived just after 6 and found the last table on the floor...full house. But, there's not a bad seat in the house because of the intimate size. Way too much good to say about the band...these guys - including Vince Gill but not fronted by him- play some of the best western swing/blues/rockabilly/ country to be found anywhere..and for $20!  The food is pretty good, drinks too, and reasonably priced. Excellent waitress. Eclectic crowd all ages. Wish we lived in Nashville so we could go every Monday nite.

Sunday bluegrass night was fantastic. It's free, which you can't beat, but really what makes it so special is the amazing level of talent. On my last visit, I was pleased to see the performers were a mix of all ages and genders, including a young girl, who was fantastic.

Just came here to drink and listen to music, but it was great for both. We rented a floor for a business party a few months ago and had a terrific time. 

This is the first time we have been back. We stopped in for a beer and had several. The service was quick. The music was awesome. It was crowded, but we found a couple of stools. One of our favorite places in Nashville for just good ole party music and drinking.
Great music, cold beerGreat crowd. Who could ask for more! You n the strip 3 flora of music. Shame I cannot post the video!  A must stop.

This is a tri-level music haven, filled with all the local talent! The balconies scattered along each level give a great view of all of Broadway! The music is fantastic and gives plenty of opportunities for dancing and indulging! Highly recommend this for daytime or nighttime! You can't go wrong!

"I LOVE THIS BAR! It's my kinda place...." - Tobey Keith

A total hidden gem, the service was awesome! I wish I remember the bartenders name, but he was a total star. The whole vibe of this bar is laid back, relaxed, and fun. 

We were waiting for a reservation at Puckett's on a Sunday when we decided to check this place out. It was well priced, and great drinks. Best of all after we settled in a band started playing, and they were terrific. 

I offhandedly asked the bartender if he had any decks of cards we could steal, and lo-and-behold he came up with a deck for us! 

All around great experience. Will visit again.

A hidden gem, very "locals only" bar - since it's all by itself on the even though it is considered on Printer's Alley. 

Walk-in with no hastle right into writers night. Local music with beer in hand. This bar has great service and cheap drinks compared to Broadway.

As we walked away from the honky tonk towards the Nissan Stadium, we overheard some top 40 tunes. Naturally, we quickly turned back around, and ran towards the music. 

The name is misleading, but the place is great! Multiple above-ground floors with lots of room to hang and dance. Spacious two-tiered rooftop bar is perfect on those warmer nights. There are couches and high-top tables with umbrellas, perfect for groups looking to lounge. 

Located at the end of the honky tonk, the rooftop here is the perfect place to get a picture with the entire strip in the background while you enjoy Top 40 hits.
In a world of staged experiences and photo opps it is so refreshing to enjoy a concert and fellowship at "the real thing"...

Free live music, excellent craft beer selection, pup friendly and a splash pad to cool you down... what is not to love!?

Our first night in Nashville we heard that Cage the Elephant and Delta Spirit were playing a free concert. A huge plus it was walking distance from our hotel and the walk there guided us through our first look at "honky tonk row". 

While it is good to get there early if you want prime seating or standing there was ample room for everyone. Jesse checked out the beer tent and was happy with the great craft beer selection and the prices ($6 a beer isn't too bad for a festival). They also had wine, liquor drinks and water available for purchase. Did you come here hungry? No problem. There are several delicious smelling food trucks lining the festival perimeter. There is also a complimentary photo booth complete with props. Most impressively the lines were short for food, drinks and entry into the festival.

We dipped our feet into the water and took in the live music on this perfect Nashville night.

I am visiting from FL, and it is my first time in Nashville. My boyfriend and I actually had other plans as far as where we initially planned on going to eat and just so happen to come across this chill laid back hot spot with live music entertainment. We genuinely enjoyed our experience here at Nashville Underground. Our server Mariah was very nice, sweet and attentive. We received our food in a timely manner. The alcoholic drinks were pretty solid!! I highly recommend trying out the drink "Smashville" especially if you're a tequila drinker like myself. SO GOOD! The food is your usual bar food. But I must say everything we had tonight was good, we had no complaints. Our server recommended the Mac and Cheese (which is a popular side dish) we loved it!!! They also have a rooftop bar, so go check it out! The restaurant/bar overall is such a cool, chill spot to be at to just kick it with good company. Keep it up Nashville Underground, and thank you for welcoming us!

If you like overpaying for mediocre food, weak drinks and receiving rude, sub par service, you'll love this place.  On a more positive note, the location is good, right in downtown by river with nice view and the live music was quite enjoyable, but other than that, it was just OK.

My review is based on visiting on a few Friday nights and as you can see, I give it all the stars! Nashville the Beautiful hosts To the Maxx with DJ Chill on Friday nights and the music is so on point. I love that there is a place to dance where you're not touching cheek to cheek unless you want to. 

When you first walk up, the doors provide you a last minute mirror check before you open the door to an evening of possibilities! You'll walk straight into the bar that is often packed and you can either wiggle to the left or right and head to the dance area or head upstairs and check out the scene down below. I love that you have options here. You can bring a group and have drinks and keep to yourselves or you can head to the dance floor and be greeted with smiles from other dance lovers.

They also have some food options but I haven't been able to try those because I was too busy dancing. They have a full menu so whether you're a tequila sunrise drinker to a wine-o, they have something for you. 

Thanks TBC for providing a great space to dance to quality music and bringing a night venue to Germantown!

Our first trip to Nashville but fourth day we discovered the Famous Saloon. What a find!  The singers performing were the best we had heard from about 25 different performances we had listened to. Our server Shelly, was fantastic!  She was super sweet and provided excellent service. We never ran out of drinks at any point. We have had some terrible service in Nashville but this was by far the best in town! Thanks Shelly for being our best server!We had appetizers as well and they were very good too. 
The floors, tables and restrooms were all very clean as well.

I was quite surprised by this place as it is just off broadway in downtown. Went there to watch the UK game(which they couldn't get for some reason) and stayed for the music. We saw two groups while we were there and they both were great. Guess that should be expected in Nashville. The bartenders were nice and actually took time to talk to you. We compared notes on margarita recipes and how to make the best. Got one of the girls a raspberry margarita and after ideas of what to put in it, it turned out great. The food just above average for bar food. The blue cheese burger was really good. Had a mound of blue cheese. The bbq sandwhich was also good. It has slaw on top which my friend likes. The chicken tenders appeared to be premade. Not horrible, just average. Overall, I would say a pretty good sports bar to catch a game and listen to some music.
Great drinks, super cool venue. Music was great on all floors. The rooftop was the best part!

The Station Inn was a recommended music venue in Nashville. 
My sister and I came for the gospel music event. 
It is a smaller dark venue. 
They offer bottled beer and snacks. 
The souvenirs were fun and they had CDs of the performers. 
The musicians were great. Nice to sit back and listen to one of the many genres of music you can find live in the Nashville area. 
The reason for the three stars is that it was what I expected, it didn't feel unique or like a destination spot to me. 
It wasn't bad but not great either. 
Everyone seemed perfectly nice and it seemed like there were a lot of regulars in attendance. 
The musicians roamed around the crowd in between sets and invited people to sing on stage with them - people they knew were musicians. One of the performers invited worked sound at the club. She was really pretty good. 
All in all an average experience.

They literally take your valuables and promise you there is no theft at entrance then throw it in the grass at the entrance. Anybody walking by can steal it. And the excuse? You could've taken it to your car. WELL MAYBE WE WOULD HAVE HAD WE KNOWN YOU THREW IT OUT TO THE PUBLIC. this venue is literally screwing people and telling you to f *** off.

Great Nashville spot if your in town for some good tourist hopping of a local favorite.

Always great atmosphere for a drink or some yummy grub.

Super Talented guest musicians sure to please.

No, it's just not country in Nashville most of the musicians will be happy to play a request for your favorite song.

Don't forget to tip these local musicians who are very underrated and working hard to please you.

Very friendly staff!!

This is the BEST spot for live music on broadway. Service is generally pretty good during the day. At night they have a hard time keeping up with pouring, as it's generally pretty crowded on all three levels. 

There are three levels of music. The bands interact with the crowd. The drinks are small and overpriced, but that's the case in all but about two bars downtown. 

If you're traveling with children, definitely go during daylight hours. 11-3 is good. People are still relatively sober. After dark.... things get wild. 

During the spring and summer (after dark).... it's what we refer to around here as Nash Trash Season. It's definitely a great place to people watch.
Great atmosphere! We went for some entertainment and a few drinks! Nothing special on the drink side but the band was amazing! Don't forget they play for tips!

Poor management and customer service!! 

Will not be going back again!! By far the worst experience I have ever had on Broadway and worst NYE. The bar oversold tickets, which created a line that was over 45 mins long. The main doors were closed and even though we had already purchased $50 tickets, we were forced to wait outside in the 14 degree weather. Once we finally got in, the fire alarm was going off, very loudly over the music. None of the staff was acknowledging the alarm, letting the crowd know whether or not there was any kind of emergency. 

It took over 30 minutes to order drinks and there was no countdown or anything for the clock hitting midnight. Even though we purchased the more expensive ticket to go up to the roof we were never allowed up there and couldn't meet with our friends who were already there, missing NYE with the people we wanted to spend with. 

I've emailed the bar twice with no response and they have shown no remorse or given any kind of apology for how poorly things were handled. If my friends and I continue to be ignored, we will definitely never return and make sure our friends know to do the same.

An auditory orgasm!! The three  part fiddle harmony is indescribable the best there ever was!!!
Dr dave. Left in photo

F you like good acoustic swing and country you will find it with Time Jumpers-- They own it
captain Ron

My sister and I found this place while walking through downtown Nashville. 
We heard live music which was a draw for us. 
The bar is decent - out drinks were average my sister got a vodka and lemonade, I had a mimosa. 
There was a good amount of seating. 
It is located in an area with lots of shops and restaurants and it's very close to the Ryman. 
Parking seems pretty good in the area too. 
It was not overly unique - it was exactly what you would expect from a bar/live music venue. 
The drinks were a decent price. I'm not a fan of drinks being served in plastic cups. I understand why some bars do it - just not a fan. 
It's also located right near the river walk area. 
We didn't have any food but they did serve food. 
All in all it was ok. I would go back again.

Last night we attended our first concert at the Ascend Amphitheater, The Lumineers put on a great show, perfect to showcase this venue.  

The BØRNS was the opening act a great accompaniment for the headliner and actually had the crowd in the palm of their hand. The stage reset was timely and the Lumineers came on exactly on time. (9:15)

I must say that the Lumineers instrumentation, musicianship and stage show was as entertaining as their music. 
About half way through their show, the band walked from the stage, right through the fans to a makeshift stage that was set in the middle of the amphitheater, which caused a "In The Round" type show for a few songs, then while still singing, Wesley Schultz the frontman, guitarist and one of the founding members waltzed directly through the audience of enthusiastic fans to reclaim the stage and take the show home. 

All said, I must give kudos to Ascend for accommodating the bands show, having the secondary stage, instrumentation, sound & lighting a follow cameras to project onto the Big Screens on ether side of the stage. (I believe they could use bigger screens, for those in the rear, General Admission area of the amphitheater)

I will add that we were asked to empty our pockets and were wanded with a metal detector upon entering the venue.  They offer food & beverages for purchase, we saw extremely large beers, flashy lighted cups of adult beverages, smelled popcorn and other party favors that you'd expect at a concert. 

All in all, we had a fantastic evening and enjoyed the show. 

Thank You Ascend for your well prepared venue and showcasing great talent.

3rd & Lindsley as a live music venue is both intimate yet also there is enough space to never be packed to the brim. This is something I appreciate from a venue that I don't feel like a sardine or don't get elbowed in the face trying to see my favorite artists. There is a parking lot outside and there is not much else around this neighborhood, however it is a few minutes in a Uber to get back to Broadway if you want to go out after a show. 3rd & Lindsley is two stories with a large bar on the first story then additional seating on a rounded balcony on the second story. The standing room by the stage is down a few steps so that the bar area is slightly elevated above the crowd which makes it great to see from no matter where you are. 

I've been here on two different occasions. The first was to see a 90's rock group, G. Love (think of Sublime meets Beastie Boys) on a Sunday night for one of the Lightning 100 radio broadcasts. If you get the chance to go to one of these events it is a lot of fun. The second time I've come was to see coffeehouse acoustic performer Joshua Radin (voice as smooth as butter). Both tickets were very reasonable and affordable. Most shows you find at this venue will be $20 or less. The bands they book are mostly rock or alt rock but I have seen some country artists play here too. 

If you want to be seated the whole time you really have to arrive pretty early and likely plan on just eating dinner here before the show. We've shown up like 20-30 minutes before the time and every single table has been taken. It's not bad to stand and watch the show but if there are openers it can make for a long night if you have old knees like mine. Any standing room by the stage is a good view and even if you stand back by the bar you can still see everything. Upstairs most tables have a good view but one time we went up and the only table that was left was an obstructed view. 

My only gripe about this place is that there are only a couple of women's bathroom stalls so a line can form if you don't time it right. Also, it can be hard to grab a beer at the bar once the music starts as people just stand in front of the bar and don't move. Otherwise a great venue!

Sad that the horrible customer service ruined what could have been a great bar with a great location. First time to Nashville this weekend and was given a horrible first impression by this place. The women's restroom attendant on the first floor was beyond rude and disrespectful. Used the restroom and upon saying to myself under my breath that I couldn't locate the soap, she sharply snapped "Well if you would stop moving, I'm trying to put it in your hands!" Oh, hello to you too! Later in the evening I realized that a ring that is very special to me was missing. Believing I must have removed it in the lower restroom to wash my hands, I entered to check and was immediatly snapped at by the same rude restroom attendant, who aggressivly barked that "The ring isn't here, there's no point in looking! Why are you looking by my stuff? [Her lineup of toiletries on the counter] I didnt take your ring you don't need to be checking in here!" Excuse me? I will check wherever I feel neccesary! She then later rudely attacked my friend who was helping me the same way, barking that "I shouldn't have taken off my ring then if I didnt want to lose it". Absolutely despicable customer service. I wish that the amount of money that my group of 17 spent that night was spent elsewhere. The irony that these restroom attendants are meant to be hospitable and welcoming is not lost on me!

Got in right before lunch and had a great time listening to the live music. Good drinks and HUGE portions! We saw so many wasted nacho baskets but 'Murica right?

it is tourist central, but for an energetic lively time, this is the place to be!

Honky Tonk Central is a great time. There are three big floors of live, local bands. I was truly blown away by the talent. Each band played four hour sets non-stop, and then when they were finished, the next band would set up. It was incredible! My favorite of the weekend was the Harold Allen Band, but there were so many other great ones. I felt spoiled. 

The layout of the venue is awesome, with big, open floor to ceiling windows that have balcony railings which provide for a really cool indoor but yet somewhat-outdoor vibe. 

Service was hit or miss. We scored with John, who took care of us on Saturday. He appeared out of nowhere every time we needed something, and he was as sweet as could be. On Sunday, our service was really spotty. We would have been better off just going to the bar and ordering there. But in all fairness, we only saw one girl working the entire second floor. 

The beer selection is limited but when I session drink I tend to go for the easy stuff anyway (pro tip!). That said, the beers got progressively warmer as our Saturday tenure wore on. I don't know if they couldn't get those domestics on ice fast enough for the busy crowd or what, but by the end of the evening I was icing down my drinks in a cup of ice water. We did order dinner during one of our visits; the buffalo chicken wrap with tots was legit!

Definitely looking forward to return visits on future trips to Nashville!

I have been coming to LOTG since its inception! I am an OG LOTG attendee. I have loved seeing the festival grow with the city. The musicians are stellar year after year and I love seeing all the vendors, food trucks, and Nashvillians coming outside to enjoy beautiful music.

Last week, I went to go and see Passenger and when he asked everyone to be quieter, the audience responded with silence. When he asked everyone to sing, the audience sang along. How awesome! 

Band of Horses played back in 2010 and it's awesome to see them part of the 2016 lineup. I love seeing all sorts of people at LOTG. What a testament to a quality festival when you see kids, families, young adults, couples, etc. everywhere. 

Thank you for showcasing quality music, quality food/vendors, and quality people that Nashville has to offer every Thursday (and then Labor Day Weekend) in August.

I haven't experienced VIP since the first year and hoping that I will get a chance this year. Thanks LOTG for all that you do. I know it is tons of work and please know that we appreciate you all so very much!

First time in Nashville and came here on the recommendation of some strangers on the Internet. The Station Inn turned out to be the highlight of the whole trip.

My wife and I arrived at 7 and, not knowing what to expect, felt uneasy based on the look of this place from the outside. Old and run down. Definitely didn't look like a friendly place from the outside. A few other out-of-towners were also standing around on the sidewalk and said they felt the same way. I went in anyway with my wife right behind me. It was black inside - no lights on except for the lights behind the bar on the other side of the room. The only person I saw was John Carter Cash setting up some things on the tiny stage. I said "hi", he looked up at me, and I walked back out. Clearly we were there way too early.

We went to a bar/restaurant nearby for an hour and then walked back over to The Station Inn.  By this time people had arrived. We paid the cover at the door and we found a place to sit. Don't expect anything fancy. It's mostly long rows of folding tables with mismatched folding chairs crammed into a relatively small building. 

After we got a few PBRs from the bar, the music started and any concerns we had were forgotten.  We heard several performers that night. One person we'd seen at The Grand Ole Opry the night before showed up to jam with one of the bands. It was borderline magical. Happy people watching happy people make amazing music.
