I experienced a lot of Nashville while I was there. Nice restaurants, bars, shops, museums, and tours.  I can honestly say that The Station Inn was the best part of the entire vacation. Next time I'm in town, I plan to go more than once.

You have to be in a mood for the crowded, loud, cheap/expensive drinks. Despite these elements we enjoyed ourselves and were able to get a table to have a couple drinks on a Saturday night.

We left and went elsewhere after making our way up to the third deck.

The service was okay but with those crowds its hard to expect excellent.

I would take tourists here, but locals can find other good spots.

What a surprise this bar was! We happened to walk by and visited just to kill some time before a Titans game and we loved it. We went on a Sunday and they had a Bloody Mary and mimosa bar (so cool). I went with the mimosa bar - they had every juice you could imagine along with fresh fruit and syrups. The grapefruit juice was tasty and refreshing. I also noticed that the Bloody Mary bar had three different kinds of salt to use for the rim which is really unique. 

It was huge inside and had ample seating on their two floors. There was also one section with some couches and a screen to watch tv. Before you leave check out the bathrooms for THE coolest sinks ever.

Super chill and a comfortable pub. Great beer selection friendly staff. I sat at the bar where the woman next to me happened to be one of their bartenders just hanging out. We had a great conversation. 

It was happy hour and $5 pints were on order. The bartender noticed I was busy chatting away, so she took charge and added another pint on my tab before happy hour ended. Pro move and much appreciated.  As you'd expect in Nashville, the guy playing guitar and singing was awesome. 

I guess it says a lot about a place when your people want to be there off the clock. Next time I'm in town  I will definitely make another pit stop at Alley Taps.

Went to see Time Jumpers show Monday nite; excellent experience! The staff advised we get there near 5:30 (for 9PM show) since it fills up quick for popular shows; so, the 3-hr wait inside was a bit long. But we got great table; even that early the stage-front tables were taken. Probably will wait a bit later next time, maybe 6-6:30. Table service was terrific all nite; waitress was very attentive and got every order right despite a full house. Drink and food prices reasonable, although I couldn't recommend going here to expect a culinary delight ... just basic bar food. Parking available on street and at nearby business (except for the clowns across from the entrance that have a "we'll tow you any time" sign posted, like they'll need the spaces after they close). The venue has great acoustics and it's intimate enough that there's not a bad seat in the house. even the bathrooms are clean. Just pay attention to your GPS to get to the place. Best show ever!!

What a FANTASTIC night we had at this establishment.  Staff was so friendly and very fun.  They took all our ribbing and jokes with a grain of salt and actually joined in with us.  Place was very busy but our party of 15 didn't seem to have any problem getting seated after a semi-short wait outside.  I was happy to get into the building though because it was cold outside.  Being a chef myself, I am very picky on how my food is prepared.  No worries here.  Expertly prepared and served at appropriate temperatures.

Staff was attentive even though very stretched with all the patrons that were there.  Entertainment was second to none.  Absolutely GREAT musicians.  Upbeat, warm and accommodating.

The only problem we have is that we actually don't live in Tennessee because I would make sure I hit this place at least a couple of times a month.  If they were able to handle all this volume on New Year's Eve then they definitely deserve my vote every other time of the year.  Can't wait to get back to Nashville so I can visit this diamond in the rough again.

Was able to go to grand opening concert. A wonderful and needed addition to Nashvegas. Ticket fees are high but expected. Drinks are about the same as the Titans games, HIGH. Food prices HIGH. Won't comment on the food as it has to get better. Right now FAIR, but then again, eat before you go, not while there. You could spend a lot when a dinner at nice place could be the same. Seriously 5 dollars for a coke?!?! Or 6 dollars for hot dog. A HOT DOG!
The Nashville skyline as the backdrop is lovely which is a plus.
Seating was fair with padded folding chair, but no numbers?!?! Hope they change that. 
Chairs on the lawn have to be a certain height I heard. Not sure what that means, may want to check this. 
Parking in Nissan Stadium lot, just over Shelby Street Bridge is 5 dollars. Excited to have this as a new place for entertainment.

We landed here to watch basketball during a downpour of rain. Ended up on the floor that has the mechanical bull. It was not quite as loud as there wasn't live music on this floor. We ordered some fried jalapeños and pickles which were good. Also got the hot chicken sandwich - medium heat. It was excellent! Unfortunately did not get a photo as we were hungry! Ladies bathroom needed some attention. Multiple stalls without toilet paper or even a tp dispenser!

You want a bar that truly gives you the Music City warm fuzzies? This is it! Beer? They have it. Live music? All day long! The energy is contagious and it's an all around fun place to have a great time with friends. The bathrooms? Well ... just imagine what your college go-to bar bathroom looked like - this was similar. But you honestly can't expect to have pristine toilet seats along Broadway. Just suck it up and enjoy yourself! Grab those boots and make your way here - you'll definitely want to include this place in your bar hopping plans.

We were extremely disappointed when we came in - we heard very good things and the bar itself was very fun. Unfortunately our food was a different story - we waiting around 45 minutes for burgers, half of which were cold. Our waitress forgot to put in one of our orders, and we received nothing but curt service in return. We enjoyed the multiple other restaurants we went to in Nashville, but we would never return here.

Bartender we rude.... I'm from out of town and been to at least 10 bars this weekend including restaurants.  He literally ignored me at the bar when I asked for a drink and when my food came, it seemed I was an inconvenience to ask for anything.  When I asked for a togo box, he literally threw it at me. It was the absolute service I've had in Nashville.  Now I know why they are off the beaten path and not busy...... needs a lot of customer service improvements. 

- disappointed customer

Found this little bar just off Broadway. It has a great locals feel to it, the music was great... great performer but not so loud you can't still carry on conversation. Dennis the bartender/manager was phenomenal, and had a great personality. The menu is a "bar food" menu but the wings we amazing, the best tater tots I've ever eaten, and really great burgers and pork (we had a big group). The food came out really quickly as well. I would definitely return!!
It was okay but the service was rude. You're better off at someplace else on Broadway where the band and servers actually try to take care of people

The Listening Room Cafe was one of the best parts of my trip to Nashville. I have been following their Instagram for a few years wanting to see a show in person. My party of four secured "tickets" to the Monday night Song Suffragettes show and we were not disappointed. The ladies had an amazing amount of talent and I cannot wait to see how they shape the music industry in the years to come. The venue was spacious, clean and relaxed. Our party tried the fried picked and green tomatoes. We also had three meals we shared. While the food had good flavor, it was a bit cold. The waitresses were busy seating and serving so we didn't want to disturb them. That was our only complaint. The experience definitely made this a memorable night. I will visit again in the future as I know this is a newer location and they are working out the kinks still.

Hit the 8:30 show last night a little more music and a little less talking by the headliners would have been better. Alissa Griffith was the highlight of the night. Absolutely terrific.   Food and service was fine the venue was great. Well worth checking out on your next trip to music city.

The Basement East has ping pong tables and tournaments. The stage has a great sound system. The bands seem to always be pretty good, with a variety of musical choices. There's also a nice outdoor patio on the back of the building that serves food as well. All in all it's a pretty sweet place.

I would love to give 5 stars for the amazing show and extraordinary talent, but my server  was less than amazing. I practically had to be him to bring me and my husband another round. The musicians where absolutely wonderful!!! I had a awesome night and a lot of laughs.

We ordered our food and 50 minutes later the manager asked us if we ever ordered! About 20 minutes later, the manager asked us who took our order. He came back and said he would discount our order because of the long wait. Ten minutes later we had our food. My turkey burger was slightly above room temperature, but my fries were ice cold and limp! The other people in my party said their beef burgers and onion rings were on par with the other premium burger places. We walked in at 2pm on a Monday with very few people seated and expected a better overall experience. I am not sure if I will ever return, but the rest of my party was not receptive to the idea. On the positive side, their prices are lower than the other premium burger places in Nashville.

I used to like this place somewhat solely because of the staff.  Cool bartenders that you can talk to make a place fun, but the 30-somethings in suits dancing awkwardly to modern rap seemed a bit odd next to a smoky pool hall.

Last time I went, however, the odd clientele and atmosphere took a turn for the worst.  Some dude, claiming to be an MMA fighter, tried to pick a fight with my friend.  We got my friend, who'd done nothing, out of the bar, and I went to close out my tab when the guy approaches me.

Now, I've got a secret security clearance with the army, and may need a top secret one some day.  As such, I don't fight with dudes at bars.  Its bad for my future.  This douche thought he'd let me know that he could "totally slam my head through the cigarette machine" positioned nearby.  I told him that I'm sure he could, and he reached out to shake my hand.  I was ready to leave, so, I went to shake it, at which point he gripped as tightly as he possibly could, and starting to buck up to me.

I asked him to let go of my hand, to which point he did, holding his hands above his head, palms towards me, with duck-ish lips and bug-eyed.  I think I pissed him off by snickering at this point, but watching a Jersey Shore wannabe attempt to intimidate me just got funny after a while.

So, I walk outside and by the bouncer whom I thought was a friend of mine at the bar, and with whom much of this took place in front of.  Thats when Anderson Silva wannabe comes out and attempts to put me in a head lock in front of the bouncer, who informs me that "I probably deserved it."

At this point, I shoved the douche off me, and listened to the bouncer give me some bullshit about how I can't "go around picking fights with people", before just telling them I had to get going.  It wasn't worth getting arrested over, and this bar certainly isn't worth your time or money.
Really good venue for listening to music. Only had drinks, so I can't give a food review, but the staff and bartenders were very attentive & friendly.

Requested a song or just anything by a popular band along with acknowledgment of 2 friends' birthdays with a tip while virtually no other requests were placed, 2 hours later and nothing, unacceptable and disappointing after having good experiences here in the past.

Was excited for this place. Disappointed. There werent many people when we got here. A table that came in way after us got their food before we did. Asked for coffee when we ordered, had to ask again for it. Sent it back, wasnt good.  Dont recommend the chicken and waffles. Breakfast sandwich was pretty good. 50min wait for food when not busy is too long.

Was here over the weekend and had the time of my life! So much fun we actually spent most of the weekend there! The bartender Kasi was such a delight, even shared her personal stash of candy with me! Amazing service, yummy food and the music was on point!! Def going back there a lot!!!

This was a first time visit and it was very good. The service was top notch. Felicia was very attentive and on top of it. I had a cheeseburger on a pretzel roll and sweet potato fries. The fries come with this sauce that's out of this world. I put it on my burger as well as the fries. I asked for my burger to be medium. It was done, but juicy and flavored nicely so I ignored the doneness. If you want well done, you may get a hockey puck. Just saying. Will be back!
Best live music performance I've ever seen, period!!! We did both the 6:00 and 8:30 shows!!!
The food is great! Especially the Macaroni balls! The environment is perfect for any gathering and Ashli, the general manager will take care of anything that you need. The music was TOP Notch. Go!!

For me, this place is as good as it gets. The price of the food was very reasonable for what you get- a live stage show. We had the turkey-apple sandwich thing which was amazing, along with their home-made fries. Service was also outstanding.

The listening room is a great place to catch premier songwriters (e.g. Jason Duke)... Saturday brunch buffet was awesome! If you want a real taste of the Nashville music industry, check this place out!

Great burger, and atmosphere! The mural on the wall adds great character to the place and comes with a great story!
The sweet potato fries are tops!

i saw with some of the other reviews that their orders were messed up too... looks like they still haven't straightened that out because both mine and the bf's order got messed up.   Regardless of the mix-up, the burgers are pretty damn good.  The meat is really tasty and I like the seasonings they used in it.   I had the burger with cilantro and avocado but they put down 4 slider patties instead of the 1 larger patty(?).  Kinda awkward to eat and it got super messy because the meat kept wanting to slide out.  

I will say it is nice to see a non-chain out in the Hickory Hollow area
Best beer & burger spot in Antioch

Had a good time.Took the Easter brunch ride. It would've been nice had it not been so cold and rainy. Food was alright. Plain, but edible. Drinks were good, a little pricey, but they were good. Loved going to the upper decks and sitting at the tables and just enjoying the ride. Wish we could've just done that rather than paying for the show and food. It is a nice boat and a neat experience though.

Food is delicious, but the service was a bit lacking. Waited for 20 minutes for a drink refill while our server was standing at the corner of the bar talking with other staff. I had to actually ask him to come and refill our drinks. Hoping it was just an off day, because I plan to come back.

Okay, as a very huge Johnny cash fan, I FREAKED when I saw this on a trip over the summer. I immediately dropped by. I walked in to a rather small giftshop and looked around a bit. They have everything. Huge collection of shirts, CDS, books and even signed memorabilia and baby onesies you can buy. 

I walked up and purchased my ticket which was fairly priced and went inside. This collection of his memorabilia is UNBELIEVABLE! Not only do they have all his gold and platinum records, stage outfits, wedding outfit, personal fan club items, etc. but they also have a lot of June Carter's stuff as well. They even had a little heart shaped box of chocolate John wrote a love note on in sharpie on display. 

The coolest little place I've been to in Nashville. I recommended for anyone who likes Johnny.

Great show! We had a fantastic time at the Listening Room Cafe.  The online reservation process was easy. The website is very well done and all the information you would need or want is there. There is complimentary valet parking which is a plus!
We took our 10, 14, and 17 year old with us and they all said it was a fun experience. There's no smoking and for the most part it is family friendly. The show is very good and worth going alone! 
The food is just okay and nothing to write home about but we didn't eat anything we absolutely did not like. 
Our waiter was just okay and wasn't super attentive to us. I could tell he was very attentive to the tables around us that ordered alcohol (we only ordered water and some sodas). Even so, we loved the show and would go again when in Nashville!

I want to like this place and it has potential. We went on a Sunday afternoon as they were finishing brunch. lt wasn't very busy but it still took about 15 mins for someone to come take our order. They didn't have a kids menu which is fine but we ordered the chicken fingers appetizer and asked for fries instead of onion rings. My husband ordered sliders and I had the chicken sandwich. Drinks were wayyy overpriced but I ordered one anyway. It came out wrong. They corrected it. No big deal. The food came out about 30 mins later and we just got fries for the kids no chicken fingers. Had to wait another 5 minutes for our waitress to show up and tell her as someone else dropped of the food. She apologizes and says it will be another 15 minutes for fingers. We cancelled that. 2/3 sliders were incorrect and had to send those back as well when she came back 10-15 minutes after. The food we did get was good and we get that a new place had to work out the kinks but it wasn't even busy. Didn't get any credit or adjustments for the inconvenience. Also hates the 1 bathroom downstairs.

This is a great venue to hear great live music from the songwriters themselves. It's a quiet place so you can hear the acoustics perfectly that is different from the live bands you hear on Broadway. It is about a mile walk from Broadway or you can take a quick drive or uber/Lyft ride there. The food isn't bad either. I had the Alfredo pasta and it was great. Also has good ribeyes. A must stop to hear premium good music.

Good environment with a great band playing the day we went. Less crowded than some of the other restaurants on Broadway. As far as gluten free, not a huge selection but managed to get a burger with no bun.

Good food and great music, but crappy service. We were told table service was only happening upstairs so we headed up there to eat. The brunette upstairs was the most unfriendly server I've ever encountered. Her first impression was not 'hi' or 'welcome' but 'what do you want?'. She then proceeded to tell us she was way too busy and we had to order the rest of our drinks at the bar. Let me clarify it was Nashville on a Saturday and dead upstairs. She clearly doesn't understand what it means to be busy. She told us everything we would need is in the bucket on the table and when I asked for a refill she acted annoyed. She clearly doesn't like her job and doesn't understand customer service. The awesome musician saved the day!

Great lineup of songwriters and singers when we went. The food is okay, perhaps some of the dishes overpriced, but the drinks are solid. It's worth it because they don't charge a cover for the music. I was surprised to hear some recent hits as sung by the people who wrote them for artists like Tim McGraw, Blake Shelton, Chris Young.
They don't monitor how many people they let in. The first section you couldn't move, it was hard to maneuver through out the museum.

This museum was fantastic! I don't know why Lonely Planet makes it sound so poor. Prices were relatively high (15$) but it was worth it. 
It is a very modern, interactive museum with an amazing array of personal items, e.g. letters, clothes, furniture and instruments. 
It's a good mix of his personal life and his career as a musician and also as an actor. 
Johnny Cash fans will probably need at least two hours.

"It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places."

The place is cool. The music was great. The food was bad.
The service was horrendous, and then a few days later I saw where I had been overcharged for more than $20.

And, when I say horrendous, I mean nearly 30 minutes before we saw a server (the place was not busy). We saw her when the food came, but never saw her again. We had to flag down someone else to ask for another beer and water, though the water never came. Then, we waited a good bit at the end of the evening trying to catch a glimpse of her to get a check, eventually just going to the front of the place and asking for it. 

Then, of course, charged $50 on a $24 bill.

I talked to a manager by phone who sounded pretty aggravated to field the call. Their calls roll to their personal phones. Service industry don't live in the office...
It wasn't the attitude you would expect on calling to report an overcharge, and there was even a tone at one point like I might be making this shit up or something.

I didn't hear back from him for 5 days, at which point I contacted the owner. 
He was sympathetic and accommodating at first, 
and agreed to refund the entirety of my bill. 

I waited for 2 weeks, but the check never came. 
I contacted him again and he was less than caring.
A reply email that he meant to mail it 2 weeks ago; but had an emergency; but actually did just run across it yesterday and it was on its way.

The check did arrive after another request, but not only was it not for the entire bill, it was not even for the entire amount of the overcharge. 

He did include 2 tickets to get in the door; like I would want to experience this again.

Both of these guys double-talked so much they couldn't keep it all straight, not for some schmuck like me. It was palpable when you talked to them and evident in their actions.

It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places.

Spend your money somewhere else.
This place does not care about its patrons; plenty of tourists in Nashville.

LOVED this museum! I thought it was a little pricey for being so small but still worth it! Loved all the artifacts and readings on them. Really loved the station where I could hear one of Cash's songs in different types of taping- amazing how the sound is so different. Loved the staff there! They would chime in and add to things to what you were reading or saying. One even started dancing with me haha!

This place is quickly becoming my new hang. Small but very solid menus. Try anything with the habanero sauce. The portobello press is awesome!  Good rotating beer selection as well. Parking across the street in the fire house lot or down the street near the atm if the lot is full for a show. 
Also the venue, if you are considering going sounds good and is quite large.   Check out a show sometime!

I love the burgers and fries! I went here on a date and was thrilled by the quality of the food and the prices. I've went to several gourmet burger places that charged way more for mediocre service and food. So, I was pleasantly surprised by this place. There was a very laid back atmosphere, music, and great food. I hope to go there again, soon.

This was an awesome experience. I would recommend getting there a little early to get a good place in line if you have tickets already. We got seated at a high table along the side of the room. I'm on the shorter side so I was excited that I would be able to see the stage well.

I did not eat so I can't speak for the food. The menu looked like your typical Nashville items, fried everything. I read other reviews that said to eat beforehand so that's what we did. As for the drinks, I had a thyme warp. Similar to a Moscow Mule but with a thyme flavor added in. It was good and large!

The entertainment was AMAZING. Songwriters playing some of their best. I recognized every song and it was so cool to hear them sung by the people who actually wrote them as opposed to the ones who recorded them. They gave back stories and a little information about where they're from. 

This place is a MUST SEE in Nashville. Order tickets beforehand.

I'm not sure why, but I thought this place was going to be bigger than it was. Maybe because I've seen the 360 Burger sign for a long time, but never the actual restaurant. The restaurant is located at the end of a strip mall. They've got a small patio in front, with 4 tables on it. 

We walked in & waited to be seated. They didn't have a host & we thought maybe we just seat ourselves, but then our server came over & sat us. It seems that they only had one server and one food runner, but we never waited for anything. Our server was very fast. 

Inside, they've got a small bar area which probably seats about ten people. They've also got a small stage area for a band. They've got about 8 televisions on the walls. We ate during a March Madness game & the tvs were loud, but understandable. 

I skimmed the menu and saw they had a mushroom & Swiss burger. It was over. I had to order that. I ordered it with a brioche bun & with waffle fries. It didn't take but about 10 minutes for us to get our food. I ordered mine as medium instead of the usual medium well they cook the burgers & it was cooked to order. 

The waffle fries were hot & delicious, just needed a little more salt. I was able to try the regular fries and they didn't taste too fresh, maybe they had to cook the waffle fries and therefore they were better. My burger was very juicy. I had to be mindful of that when placing my bun on the plate so I wouldn't get the bun soggy. I was very happy the burger was cooked to order. The meat has a nice flavor, the thing was LOADED with Swiss cheese & mushrooms which made me very happy. 

The prices are very reasonable. I think both of our burgers were 10 bucks each & came with a lot of fries. I'll be back when I'm in the area & craving a juicy burger.

I have been here a few times - mostly during Songwriter's Festival.
I have always had a good seat, whether it was on the couch, a big overstuffed chair, or a barstool.
Music always sounds great.
I have never felt like the place was so crowded I couldn't enjoy the performers.
In fact, every time I have been here, I have always gotten a great seat and no one standing in front of me, to block any views.

I really like this place.
Food isn't bad, either.
Good beer.

Two stars because the boat didn't sink. Service was poor to spotty. Dinner was acceptable. Trying to get a cup of coffee was sort of an ordeal. The dessert was served only to the people seated who did not go outside to see the bottom of broadway. They never came back to serve the dessert. We asked 3 times before we got one for my wife. 
I suppose I would recommend not doing the dinner for $90.

I am in the area often and the burgers are good. However, management changed the fries from the skin-on, golden brown ones you see in initial photos. Those were tasty. Distinguished 360 and made it a place to recommend. Now they serve  the frozen, food supplier fries with no taste. Hope Management rethinks this poor decision. I'd have given four stars if old fries were still served.

I got a Groupon for this but that was a while ago so I can't say if it's there or not anymore. That made for a great outing for me and my husband already! We really enjoyed the exhibits. I feel like the first part of the exhibit from the early part of Johnny Cash's career was a bit narrow (meaning it was hard to move around...the exhibit itself was great) considering a lot of patrons wanted to stand there and read absolutely everything displayed there. After that initial part all else was good. My husband is a musician and enjoyed seeing the many guitars on display. To get trough the entire museum takes at least a couple hours of you take the time and enjoy it, so it's definitely worth it even if you don't have the Groupon. 
The gift shop was nice enough. High prices as one would expect but if you're a fan it's worth a look around.
Great bartender Dennis! Delicious fried pickles and chicken tenders. Great chill vibe.

Kenny the bartender was great.  The piano players were also amazing!! However your waiter was not so great. It's wasn't even busy when we went in. It was a Thursday night. Not friendly at all. Not on top of getting your drinks. I walked up many times to the bartender just to get another drink. When the waiter did come over he expected a tip. You had maybe 20 people in the bar dude. Wouldn't want to see you on a busy night.

We stopped in Nashville overnight and, after driving all day, were looking for something good for dinner. 360 Burger came up first on Yelp and a burger and a beer are always a good idea so we went there. It was a great choice! I had the Sliders and a beer and my husband had the Pretzel Bun Barbeque Bacon Burger. They were both delish! The server was friendly and attentive. He told us that the meat for the burgers is locally grown, very fresh. Awesome! As we were getting ready to leave, a live band was setting up to play. If we come through Nashville again, we will definitely stop here again. The only bad thing I can mention is that someone was smoking right outside the door and when people came into the restaurant, big clouds of smoke would come with them. But the food was terrific, the service was great and , except for the smoke, we really enjoyed our visit.
Excellent layout!! Great museum and was easy to get lost in a world of music. Cool gift shop, didn't have the coffee but it smelled amazing.

Blue Bar has the makings of a very bad choose-your-own-adventure experience. For a $10 cover charge on New Year's Eve, you had two options: turn left (I suppose this is the Rack Room side) and you can sit in a brightly lit white room that has the feel of an old basement and pay $1 per song if you want to hear any music. Had I had the opportunity and the jukebox had the song, I would have torturned the crowd with back-to-back playings of "What's New, Pussycat" or some Spice Girls song.

Turn right, and you go down a long hallway to what appears to be the Blue Bar side of the house. No offense to schizophrenics, but I'm afraid the DJ that night was suffering from a bad case of music-schizophrenia. Just as people were getting into the groove, he'd change the tune and tempo and it just killed any mood. Perhaps it's just me, but guys dancing in suits is just weird. There was plenty of that. 

As if those issues weren't enough, asking $7.50 for a Jack and coke is ridiculous...and a poorly made Jack and coke at that. I mean, it's ONLY two ingredients. I'd rather pay the extra $4.50 at Patterson House down the street for an infintiely better cocktail, but that would be comparing apples to crap. 

During past visits to this place, the music was just OK and the staff was just OK, but after a hiatus from this place for a few years, I'm reminded why I should never return.

This is a great local restaurant. They have a wide variety of hamburgers and other food. Everything is very fresh, hot, and the service is great. The quality of the food can't be beat. They make a mean burger.

Another thing I like is that we have 3 small children and they do not complain about splitting plates.

My biggest complaint is they stopped serving their baked beans. 

Keep in mind that everything is prepared to order, so you have to wait a bit, but it is a wait that is well worth the freshly prepared food you get in return.

Finally let me say if you want Antioch to rebuild, it will take businesses like this. That depends on you supporting them, and this is one worthy of support.

This used to be a favorite spot to take people who come to visit.  Highly disappointed that they chose to only sell bottled water during CMA Fest.  Every other bar gave out free water or had stations set up.  The music was also not as good as normal for this place, we didn't stay long.

Incredibly tasty!!! I dined here for the first time tonight. I had the opportunity to enjoy the turkey burger with habanero cheese and fries. I found it flavorful and juicy. To top it off the bar had Angry Orchard apple cider, which made my meal even better. The bartender was attentive and pleasant and overall I would count this as a positive dining adventure.

Talk about a shitty place. I only say shitty, because there's literally one bathroom on the ground floor during peak times and there's nowhere to go, and trying to get a drink at a bar is impossible.

 We hear there are more bathrooms upstairs, but then we have to wait in line and when we didn't realize this, the bouncers were complete assholes. I actually heard them call a bachelorette party a "bunch of cunts". 

This place is worse than the music that Dierks Bentley makes. In some respects, it's the same exact bar as every other downtown Nashville bar (crazytown, honkytonk central, etc), but the staff at other places seems much more professional. For contrast, Nashville Underground also recently opened, and the staff there is extremely pleasant. Of the country named bars downtown, like FGL house, AJ's Good Time Bar, and the George Jones Museum, Dierks' bar is the worst. Hopefully it loses money and shuts down soon.

Quality night provided by talented musicians with great banter to boot. They had us singing, dancing and dying of laughter! Why not five stars? The public announcing of "oh we got 20$ for this song" to "whoa $50 we'll definitely play that!" became quite obnoxious. I've never heard of such steep "suggested" tips at a dueling piano bar. Two five dollar requests were physically crumpled and thrown out. If $20 is your rate, then post it. Otherwise a good time but it did feel increasingly like they were begging for more money as the night went on. Not cool.

I loved the Johnny Cash Museum! I know the tickets are a little steep at $19pp, but I wanted to pass along that I found a Groupon for $20 for 2 people or $38 for 4 people - and I had an extra ticket after our party of three, so I was able to give it to someone else in line.  The museum took about 1-1.5h to get through, and I'd recommend it for adults, but may not be interactive enough for kids depending on the age.

Really cool place for lunch or night on the town the food is really good and well done. 

Had some sweet and spicy fried pickles and Pulled
Pork sandwich that were excellent.

Wait staff was very attentive. 

Oh and by the way the music was really cool as well.
Excellent time Well worth the trip to 4th and Broadway

I paid the piano player $20 to sing Happy Birthday to my 75 year old Mother.  He brought her on stage and proceeded to sing Happy Birthday I want to *#$% you.  Continued to sing explicit words to her.  She was completely humiliated.  I left a message for someone the next day to contact me, but none ever returned my call.  Trashy place.

So, I found myself at this bar on a Sunday night.  I can't comment on the food, I didn't eat anything.  I CAN comment on the experience.

First, they had a live band that took requests from the audience periodically, and played a good mix of new and classic country.  The band also had a few people from the audience play, with the highlight being Keith Whitley's son playing some of his dad's tracks.

The drinks were fair priced for Opryland, and the bar was 100% the local spot for drinking.  As an FYI - you can smoke in here, so, yeah, it's not for bringing your children.  

We had Hope and John Boy as our tenders for the night.  Both were attentive and regularly checking on everyone there.  This is exactly what I was looking for: local bar close to the hotel that was a no-frills watering hole.  

Last thing: If you are staying at the Gaylord and are looking for upscale/fancy dining, don't come here and bitch.  This bar is for people who aren't paying 27 bucks a day to valet their Escalade.

Hope you enjoy it as much as we did!
Who are we kidding here,.....? I'd visit the place Johnny Cash washed his clothes at! It's music history son,..... enjoy!

I really wanted to enjoy my lunch at 360 Burger. I was thrilled that there was some life being pumped back into Hickory Hollow, and after recently learning that some of the chefs studied at Johnson & Wales (my alma mater), I was pumped. The sad truth is that my lunch was a letdown.

I ordered the 360 burger with gouda on the pretzel roll, medium rare. I received a well-done burger on a giant, tough pretzel roll, which muted the flavors of the burger and toppings within. After I removed the top bun and was able to taste the meat, it was noticeably "off" - tasting gamey and I daresay, perhaps old? Apart from that, the meat was unseasoned and boring. 

I will say, they got the sweet potato fries right - they were cut like shoestring fries, well cooked and well seasoned, and served with a great spicy aioli. 

Will I come back? Maybe for fries and a beer, but I'm not at all impressed with the burger.

This was a fun place to have brunch. The food was OK, and pretty overpriced for the portion sizes. The service was ok but our server was pretty out of it and didn't offer us anything to drink at all. A band of young children came on the stage and we actually thoroughly enjoyed how good they were! But we waited forever to get our food and the band started much later than they were supposed to. Ultimately this is a really cool place and I would definitely go back but maybe for drinks instead of eating.

Found them on Yelp. New to the area. First time walking in. The place looks great, very clean looking. Menu was nice and variety. Easy to read and not overwhelming. Was greeted first as we walked in. Drinks ordered first thing when we sat. 
Food was very presentable and a lot to eat. I ordered Cilantro Guacamole burger. Amazing. The cilantro was in the burger meat blended and had flavored. Cooked right and fries were great.
Our server was cute and she kept watch and filled drinks just as any server should do. I could have the worse meal and if she tops off my drink and stops to checkup a few times, I'm happy. She did just that, think her name was Katie.
Overall great experience for first time. Will be back.

Only thing I noticed when I first stepped into the place, was the smell. Honestly don't know why but it was a stinky urine smell. Or a dirty mop used to clean the floors. I've smelled this kind of place being downtown in the dive bars and don't know why it smelled like that. But you get immune to it within a few min and don't notice. But first time in, I could def. smell it.

Still great experience.
Will be back.
Nice place, we came at 8pm. Very quiet. Don't  be fooled tho, they only have one pool table- so it's by no means a rack room. Which was sad.

This is a must stop for any Johnny Cash fan.  They have a large collection of Johnny's memories and artifacts.  Showing the story of his life as you walk through.  You can even have your picture taken with him via green screen.
The cruise was nice, show lasted bit too long and the food was HORRENDOUS!! EAt before you go!

Do not go here for food. Not only did it take over an hour for my four friends and I to receive our burgers and fries, but the food arrived cold! How could the food be cold AND take an hour+ to prepare? Someone seriously dropped the ball here.

I do not recommend this place for anything except its Bud Lights and maybe live music.

We went there last night. While they were very very busy that is no reason to be rude. First off we were at bar 20min  and kept getting ignored. We had looked at beer menu that apparently not up to date. When we ordered two beers from menu she rudely said we don't have. Then she walked away not giving us the opportunity to even order something else. We are here 4 more days and will not return there. All the other places were more or equally as busy and some with less staff and we encountered no rudeness and were impressed with other establishments bartenders ability to keep up.

Great venue and great music. We paid a $7 cover and our child was free. It was nice to find a family friendly music venue. Would have given it 4 stars were it not for the incredibly slow food service.  Not our waitress' fault, but rather the kitchen's. It took about 40 minutes to get entrees out. The food was tasty, though.  We had hummus plate, BBQ chicken salad (kitchen forgot the chicken!), and the rosemary chicken with Brussels sprouts and mashed potato. The chicken thighs were slightly undercooked. Besides this, it's a good venue and a nice night out.

One of my favorite places in Nashville. Great entertainment no matter which decade you born in (I think you have to be 18, though, to get in). Get there early for a table or go after 11:00 if you want a packed party atmosphere.

Smaller museum, but really well done. Shows a timeline of his life, all his albums, interactive audio and video. When they play Hurt as you leave the tour, it's hard not to get choked up.
Great showcase of one of the all-timers!

Fried pickles are my fav! But these have been salty each time I've had them
I ordered the bbq burger. Super greasy, even made my bun soggy --YIKES. My sister had the wings she said they were pretty good. Kinda ass backwards if you're gonna be a burger spot  but hey, the server was BOMB ask for Luke! He made it all worth it

We were told by several Nashville locals to check this place out. The hospitality was just as amazing as the music and definitely made our experience. We stopped in during the day due to issues making a reservation online, and the host, Emily, was unbelievably helpful in getting us in that night and giving some Timing tips to make sure we got a good seat. When we arrived verrrry early for the 8pm show, we were given helpful options to buy time. We ended up standing in the back for the 6pm show that had just started (the manager even found bar stools for us!) the night host (we didn't get her name) then helped us getting a great, close table for the later show! 

I don't think we were overly nice to get such great service, they were just that awesome! I also saw some comments about the food, but we had no complaints: an interesting take on fried pickles & salads with blackened shrimp were delicious. 

The music was on point for both shows! Really cool to hear the guys who wrote popular songs we'd heard at the later show; I've added some up & comers to my Spotify list from the early show. 

I will absolutely be back on any & every trip to Nashville!

By far, the best thing my mom and I did in Nashville. Good food, service, and extremely talented performers! Whenever anyone asks what to do in Nashville, this is my first recommendation. If you watch the show "Nashville", this place is very similar to the Bluebird Cafe, the difference is that the Listening Room Cafe is located right downtown Nashville, walking distance from Honky Tonk Row. Perfect place to grab a bite and a drink (or two), and listen to some authentic country music.

You don't go here for the food or drinks obviously. The entertainment was excellent. However, the drinks took a very long time for a half packed crowd. Also, they forgot our food order and we got it 5 minutes before the show ended.

So I returned to 360 to check out the cheeseburger instead of turkey burger. While my burger was a but more well done than expected, it was still fantastic. I also had the opportunity to try the hot apple crisp and it was amazing!

I should be giving this place a 2 star for my true feelings, but its new and I really hope that they can make it, as Hickory Hollow definitely needs someone to breath new life into the area.
The service was great, she was friendly and gave us the speech, which I enjoy, love learning about "what their deal is" she told it it was all local beef, grass feed vs grain feed... cool!
I ordered the 360 burger, on sourdough (she said it was, didn't taste like the sourdough i know of) with an egg and bacon. I got grilled asparagus as a side, i know odd, but it was the best part of the meal and much healthier than fries!

I couldn't get pass the meat...something smelled off...gamey, old, mixed with some other sort of meat, i don't know, i ate 2 bites and I was done. 
Not sure what happened there, I've definitely had grass fed, local meat before and it's usually top notch! 
This place could be a hit, but you have to fix the burger...I'll be back, as its close by and i believe in second chances. fingers crossed!

A fantastic stop when you're in Nashville to go see the legend himself. Great opportunity to listen to his music see his albums and attire from the various stages in his life. There is also a café in the ticketing area. Don't forget to spend some time upstairs to see Patsy Cline and all the things she's done. $18 is worth a visit. Highly recommended.
My friends and I came by for brunch on a Saturday. Thankfully it wasn't crowded. The food was great and I enjoyed the live music. I will definitely be back!

Hello, I'm Johnny Cash...

I hear the train a comin'
It's rollin' 'round the bend,
And I ain't seen the sunshine
Since, I don't know when
I'm stuck in Folsom Prison
And time keeps draggin' on

On down to San Antone...

There were plenty of things for me and Jamie W. to do during our brief visit to Nashville earlier this month, so whittling the list down to the must-see's wasn't easy. If, however, you had to choose one thing to do in this city, I say go to the Grand Ole Opry for a show, but a close second would be a visit to this tribute to the Man in Black. I'm a late bloomer when it came to appreciating his music and legacy. I remember his ABC-TV variety show when I was a kid, but it really just started with me with the superb biopic "Walk the Line " preceded by his late-period renaissance with producer Rick Rubin. For just $16 admission, what this tight-fitting but extremely well-organized museum does is make you appreciate the entirety of his life and career with very little filler (photo: http://bit.ly/1drkU6b).

It's only two years old since there was a museum at his home in nearby Hendersonville, but in true Cash fashion, it burnt to the ground. This one is in the heart of the Downtown area on 3rd Avenue near the honky tonks on Broadway and across the street from the Goo Goo Shop. Sponsored by the Cash family, a key differentiator from other celebrity museums, the exhibits span all the different periods of his life from his childhood through his Air Force years and then onto his salad days as a musician where he got his break at Sam Phillips' Sun Records recording with the Tennessee Three. Of course, his long-standing marriage to June Carter is well covered here down to her performance gowns (photo: http://bit.ly/1zmSpRb). There are several interactive exhibits which present Cash's music through all his periods.

Two separate areas are devoted to viewing vintage footage of him throughout his career, one focused on his music performances, the other on his many appearances in films and on television. For instance, I had no idea he played a homicidal maniac who terrorized a very young Ron Howard in a sleeper called "Five Minutes to Live". What I did learn more about were his mid-80's recordings as one of the Highwaymen (photo: http://bit.ly/1bcYSlT) and his last years when he made the American Recordings with Rubin, a quartet of albums that served as a fitting epitaph. An unassuming door leads you to the well-stocked gift store  (photo: http://bit.ly/1DVfR3v) and the small adjacent cafe. It's amazing how comprehensive the collection of artifacts is here and all of it done in a respectful tone.

I keep a close watch on this heart of mine
I keep my eyes wide open all the time
I keep the ends out for the tie that binds
Because you're mine, I walk the line.

Definitely could've lived without. Went here based on reviews to get my husband a burger for his birthday. Menu is short with very little options. Choice of type of burger is.... Beef. Sure it's supposed to be "fancy" but, still it's beef or chicken on the menu. We had to ask about a kids menu though clearly we had a 7 yr old at the table. The sweet and courteous waitress had to tell me what kids meals they served because they weren't on the menu.. There were 5 other kids though in the tiny restaurant so clearly it wasn't for a lack of use. Kiddo and I ordered tea, musn't be popular bc it was sour. Burgers got to table and meat/cheese was with opposite toppings/condiments, so we flipped patties. It looked nice...but then we ate. Tasted like a grease infused patty burnt on a skillet. Ew. Bad smell, bad flavor, bun was BLACK around edges, not brown, black! Sweet potato fries were good. Milkshake was good. The worst part was who I believe to be the owner doing "live music" which sounded like something you'd hear in an elevator on a cruise ship...awful. I never want to hear a synthesized version of Hotel California again....ever.

While there is certainly room for improvement when judging the quality of the drinks or the cleanliness of the tables and bathrooms, the scenery is unmatched.  If you enjoy seeing an exposed areola entering the mouth of a fellow patron as they bond over music that was close to decent 25 years ago and the lowest quality liquor that is allowed by the FDA then look no farther.  If you crave frozen cheese sticks, you are in luck, but if not it's proximity to Waffle House leaves you with quality options.
Fantastic venue for live music...excellent food and atmosphere! Recommend highly the smoked chicken wings with a Kentucky Bourbon Barrel Ale. Music talent is first class!

The Big Bang Bar is a Dueling Piano Bar, that never dissapoints!
From the comedic, original perfomances... to the best bar tenders, this is the place to go any night of the week
THIS PLACE FILLS UP FAST THOUGH
If you want a table, you HAVE to get there EARLY!!
It's standing room ONLY by 8:00 pm

When we go, we get there around 6-6:30pm on weekends (Which sounds very early to be starting out for the night, but you can spend COUNTLESS hours in this place and not even know it)
We go early, get us a table for the night, get some food and drinks, and wait for the fun!
*TIP-- HOLD ON TO YOUR TABLE! Make sure at least one person remains at the table at all times, or someone WILL take it.
(It gets that crowded)

Also- new one in the Boro. Will have to check it out since its a lot closer to home

Awesome place with great vibes! The entire staff was great and the stage setup was perfect! Parking wasn't the best but wasn't bad either! The setup and stage really made everyone kind of feel like family. The sound and lighting was perfect, unlike a lot of smaller venues that tend to over do it. Overall one of the best small venues I've been to & I'll definitely be back! 

If you enjoy good people, great drinks, and awesome live music this is the place for you!!

The owner of this establishment is wildly inappropriate. 

Let me elaborate. Last night we left Rebar to go to this bar and it was sometime before midnight. There was a person who was talking to us, who had obviously become really drunk, and started to act a little mouthy. The owner engaged him in a verbal argument through the open patio window and was not backing down. I think it's really unprofessional to not simply recognize someone is intoxicated and ask them to leave your establishment. Done. Altercation over.

However, the owner would not stop. I leaned over and politely tapped him on the shoulder and said "He might be very drunk, you should just ask him to leave."

(He was yelling at the guy: "You, motherfu**er are a liability in my establishment!" Which is probably true, but what happened next speaks to a deeper issue.)

And he whipped to the side, and screamed at me.

"Don't you fu**ing touch me you stupid bit**!!"

Woah there, homie. First of all, you don't talk to a lady like that. Secondly, I did not do anything more than put two fingers on your shoulder in a polite manner to tell you that I agreed with you, he needed to go, and you both needed to end it- you were drawing a crowd on the sidewalk adjacent to the patio and my friends were sitting close to this. You were not dealing with myself or my friends- and we were not obnoxious in any way. I was trying to help diffuse the situation and, attempt to, also get you to get rid of this guy who had been following myself and my friends around most of the evening without drawing too much attention to myself for being the whistleblower potentially and/or my girl friends.

Clearly, the owner is more concerned with being a hot headed loose cannon than he is the safety of his female patrons. He also seems to like to degrade and berate female patrons, too, as you can see.

We seem to visit Nashville enough- and we will not ever be returning to this establishment.

I advise others not to either.

You, sir, pissed off the wrong patron.

Very cool place.   4 singer song writers play their best.   Local brews.  Food was okay but who cares.  A great night of fun.   Not so loud that you can't hear your table mates.  A little bit of an older crowd.   30-40 scene. Lots of couples on dates.

This place is amazing. The tickets are $20, but it is well worth it. 
The museum takes you through the life and works beginning to end for Johnny Cash. 

It is a pretty extensive collection of materials and works from the Man in Black. The tour took us about 1 hour to get all the way through, which to me is well worth the money spend. 

And we learned quite a bit !

My mom, sister and I visited Nashville for the first time from California.  The General Jackson Showboat was such a pleasant experience.  The boat was in very good condition.  The staff was nicely dressed and polite.  The decks were well lit toward the evening time.  The restrooms were clean and stocked with all the necessities. The dinner area at floor level (where we sat) had round tables setup that sat about 9 people to a table.  The table settings were finely arranged. The two servers at our table provided excellent service!  I don't think anyone at our table had to ask for anything. The dinner was a chicken breast stuffed with spinach and cheese and had two sides to go along with it.  Dessert was a chocolate cheesecake.  The food was very good and so was the tea and coffee.  
The show was wonderful!  The performers were talented and gifted.   The performers outfits were flashy and glitzy.  The band did a great job too!  The show had a variety of country music that gave tribute to both the older and newer musicians. The weather was perfect with clear skies and the river was like glass.  It was about a 3-hour ride.  We would book this show again!

I'm a huge old school country fan, so when I was we where in town and blocks from the museum I told my husband we have to go. 
One thing you need to know is that it will be packed with young and old. 
Fun and full of interesting things!
I love that it is set up that when you enter its his early years and you end with his last recording "Hurt" his cover on the Nine Inch Nails song months before he died. With the showings of the movies he was in and live showing of old concerts. 
I think his son opened this museum in 2012.
If I come back to Nashville, I will return.
Heather was our bartender for my bachelorette party, she handled our group of ten like a pro! She was SO NICE. I really appreciate her making our group feel welcome. And also, your bar is AWESOME!

Took a Sprocket Rocket tour at 1pm (if you don't know what that is you should look it up, we had a blast) & they gave us wristbands to go into this bar during our break. The wrist band got us 8 beers & 8 mixed shots for $40. Not too shabby at all!

We only went in the afternoon but the band there was great & we had a blast. We ordered fried pickles & the queso dip & we loved both for a drunk snack.  While the service wasn't the most friendly we had all weekend, they still were doing a good job working hard to get our drinks and food out quickly.

It seems like more of a dive bar so if you are looking for a typical Broadway experience I'm not sure how it would compare to the rest of the bars considering we only went during the day. But if you would like to get some day drinking it I think this would be a fun little place to experience.

Cool bar and fun environment but very sexist. A group of friends and I were in Nashville from out of town and one of the guys was told he couldn't dance with his female friends near the pianos because it was "females only". Extremely sexist.

My mom, stepdad, and boyfriend Started our journey on the main level and moved up to the rooftop (my mom is handicapped so they let her use the elevator while we took the stairs). Went to the bar on the roof to order a round of drinks & was greeted by the bartender with one of the worst attitudes you could have in the service industry (I myself am a bartender). Decided to leave after a guy was persistently trying to sell drugs to my parents and the couple in front of us was half naked dry humping and security did nothing about it. Proceeded down the stairs while we were greeted by another security guard who told us my boyfriend was being kicked out for "stumbling down the stairs"... FYI he was walking slow with me down multiple flights of stairs since I was in heels! After bantering back and fourth, we decided to leave and although I will be back to Broadway St, never again to DBWR. Couple be a cool place if you had better employees!!
The music was great!! Abby Cone is a new favorite.  I highly recommend the handheld smoked turkey with avocado.  Great place for a night out in Nashville.

As a new restaurant I will admit that I think this place will be able to gain more stars from me in the future.  The server was extremely friendly, and slow.  It was a Friday lunch, but we were one of the first tables in there and seemed to be waiting awhile.  I originally ordered the cilantro burger, but after being told it took longer to cook the stuffed burgers I changed my order since no one else in the party was having a stuffed burger.  I might as well have stuck with the stuffed burger because the food still took forever to come out.  

I had the Pimento and Pig Burger (and added a fried egg because...I can), two at the table had the Farm Boy, and one had the Salmon Burger.  The two with the Farm Boy (country ham and egg) didn't seem wowed, the Salmon burger liked the flavors.  The prices were high ($12 for beef and $11 for the salmon).   All agreed that the fries were lacking, maybe a little underdone.  I thought the roll was pretty fantastic.

I was intrigued to learn of the connection with Swett's and that the sons were graduates of Johnson and Wales.  Not typical of what you'd expect at a burger joint.  I do think the flavors are spot on at this place based on the burger that I ate.
I think it's ballsy to open a gourmet burger joint in a shopping center where you are the only tennant (let's face it there are not one but two empty Best Buys in Hickory Hollow) and charge more than what you'll find in spots like Burger Up, Pharmacy, Gabby's, etc.  They use quality ingredients, but maybe they need to work on the food cost to come down a bit on price.

I remember the early days of the Pharmacy, and let me tell you they sucked.  It took over an hour to get a burger and it came from a waitstaff with a surly attitude that acted like they were doing you a favor to let you eat there.  260 Burger is already several steps ahead of where Pharmacy started from in my book...except the price.  I'm looking forward to having another meal there soon.

First time here. Was promptly greeted and told we could sit wherever we liked. I pulled up a seat at the bar and Matt (awesome bartender) took our drink orders quickly. Service was outstanding,  the burgers were truly amazing. 5 star all the way. Fries were fresh cut and crisp on the outside, perfectly tender inside. The bun with the burger was obviously sourced locally or made in house because it was by far the most fresh and tasty I've ever had. Clean place, friendly and knowledgeable staff, cold beer. Will be back weekly. This place rocks! A much needed change for the Hickory Hollow area.. Swing in and check 360 out.

I stopped in several times over the course of a couple days in Nashville. Bands were good. Drink selection and prices were average for Broadway. Servers were really good even though they were busy. Men's bathroom is really small but oh well. All in all an average downtown bar in Nashville

The music was absolutely great! We were only looking for a place for dinner with some music but ended up staying 2.5 hours just to listen to more! The food was good too. I had the mushroom "burger" which was probably the best selection at our table (out of the chicken strips, wings, and turkey sandwich). Service was awesome as well as beer selection.  Four stars instead of five for the small menu and the food could be a bit better.

A quick little walk through and glimpse into the life of the man in black. Beautiful imagery going back from his boyhood until his death in 2003. If you're a true Cash fan, watching the video for Hurt will give you goosebumps. They have several monitors set up to watch video and music clips along with hand-written notes, poems and lyrics. It's not a big museum, but if you take your time be prepared to spend about an hour inside. The gift shop in the front has a lot of memorabilia including coffee cups, cds, t-shirts and even onesies for your little one. After leaving here, I actually had the feeling of knowing him. As the saying goes, Johnny Cash is a friend of mine. Definitely worth a stop in to see.

The wife were walking in the hood with the pups when we saw the chalkboard sign stating that brunch was being served and pups are welcome so it only made good logic to go in and try. We sat on the deck on a overcast day and enjoyed a couple of nice mid mid morning libations. The service was East Nashville good and the drinks were
Ok. We did not get any food only because we had just eaten at Edley's before happening on to this spot. It was a great atmosphere and we enjoyed our time sitting on the deck and enjoying the people watching. The food from afar looked good and we would certainly return.
I am not a huge Johnny Cash fan, but I really enjoyed my visit.  Definitely a must see.
You can't ignore this legend and not visit the museum. It cost about $19, enjoyed dit but left not knowing how he died, which I heard he died.

Long time fan of Johnny Cash. The museum located downtown and is small and very pricey. You can spend a lot of $$ visiting attractions in Nashville. Look for the groupon ticket and go for half price. The museum has a good account of the life of Johnny Cash and the progression of his career as a musician. I learned a lot I did not know about him.  The collection memorabilia is  outstanding.  We stayed 2 hours and I could have stayed a bit longer.  The parking lot next door is about $9/hour costing as must as a visit to the museum. Take a roll of quarters and park on the street, meters only allow you to pay for 2 hours/ for $3.00

I never ever write these things, but as I sit in the drive thru of Burger King after dropping 33 bucks on unedible food, I thought I would tell my thoughts.

I chose this restaurant because I read really good reviews on here. We were the only people in there at the time so there was no excuse for the service and dinner we had. We ordered fried pickles while we looked over the menu. Well we never even got them and the waitress was dumbfounded when I brought it up. My medium well burger was so well done that it was like a dried hockey puck and so was my husbands. The french fries had obviously sat around for quite some time after being burnt. I mean it was horrible! 

Our waitress never came to see if we liked anything and when we got our bill, the fried pickles were on there. So i dont know who wrote the previous stellar reviews, but they were either delusional or employees. The sad part is my husbands company just built a new facility down the road and I guarantee they wont be eating there. What a shame or sham?

Me and a cousin ate at this restuarant last Monday May 19th. I ordered the Bleu Cheese burger in the pretzel bun(waitress suggestion) with sweet potato fried. She had the All American with Onion rings. My burger was tasty, the sweet potato fries had a bit of an old taste to them but tolerable. My cousin did not like the Onion rings. I tried one and it seems like I was eating more breading than the actual onion. Nonetheless the food was good. Our waitress, petite blonde with tattoos, was exceptionally attentive and very sweet. I will return :-)

I really enjoyed myself and glad we went to the Museum. I'm a 25 year old and really enjoyed it. The Museum was set up perfect to where you're able to enjoy everything without it getting too crowded. There is lots of memorabilia. His Grammys, letters, outfits, personal writings, home furniture. This experience was great! There is an awesome green screen that allows you to take pictures with Johnny Cash. I've posted them.
Fantastic night filled with laughs, singing great drink service and dancing. Only negative is the consistent asking for 20.00 song requests. Forget hearing your song if you give any less then 20.00.

The food was  pretty good but the service was terrible.  We ate on the roof top and we had to go find our own condiments and the bar tender eventually brought us our drinks because our waitress was MIA.  I have never seen so many waitresses and bar tenders not working and taking selfies. Then before we left they turned off the country music at this country bar and started playing Justin Bieber.  No thanks!

A cute place but they have problems with the help. We went today for brunch and to watch the game. No brunch today, but we called?? We had a group of 12! Hope they get their act together!! Today they didn't have it!!
Best music venue on broadway. Never too crowded and the bartenders are amazing! You'll have to hear Robert Meza play to believe it !

We went here and the place was dead. Yet it still took us 10 minutes to get a drink because the bartender was standing there talking to his friend then he went to the back and didn't come back for a while. The bathrooms were disgusting as disgusting could be. Needless to say, we didn't stay long. Had one beer and left. Not impressed with the service whatsoever.

A wonderful escape from noisy Broadway and cool ambiance too. There was a great band playing the night we were there, and the bass player even smiled at me the whole time. Maybe that's why I liked it there so much. Drinks were the same price as everywhere else downtown. We got a table right in front of the stage and stayed for quite a while. I would hangout there again, for sure.

Our Uber driver recommended Listening Room Café as the place to go if looking for good local musicians and it did not disappoint. We arrived about 45 minutes before the doors opened (i.e. time of show start) and it was well worth it as we were able to get a great table assignment and we simply sat at the bar until the stage room opened. The artists were awesome (Briana Tyson, Cameron Bedell and Garrett Moshier) and our server was great. I'd highly recommend this spot!

I LOVE this place! Such great entertainment and energy! I've gone before with my husband, my parents, friends and co-workers. Each time everyone has had an absolute blast. The musicians are very talented and even their awesome bartender, Kenny rocks it out when he jumps on stage to sing and play the drums. 
....If you are looking for a fun, unique experience on Broadway this is the place to go!
Amazing musical artists, great service. I would recommend this to anyone visiting Nashville.

The vibe here was pretty cool. We went out on a Saturday night as we had family visiting from out of town. I have never been to this bar so wanted to try it out. We went up to the third level since the first level was packed. Tons of space upstairs, good dj. I am giving it three stars because our drinks were overpriced for a bar on Broadway. The bartender was charging us differently. It was like he didn't know the prices so he made it up as he went along. He charged my husband one price but my cousin a different price, for the same drinks (she bought the next round and her total was different).

The weirdest thing was I ordered a vodka on the rocks and was charged $3 for ice? Never in my life have I seen an upcharge for ordering ice in a drink. I mean, it's ice. My cousin ordered a gin and tonic and was not charged for ice. It was annoying that I was charged for ice. There are plenty of bars up and down Broadway that have cheaper drinks so we left after that.

It is a lot of stairs to get up to the top but we wanted to be on the roof top anyways, so that part was fine.

Mediocre food at best. I ordered a pizza which tasted mostly like a frozen pizza from the grocery store. Limited drink menu. Sat upstairs and got poor service. Ex. I had to go to the bar to get my own water refill and at least once there was no one behind the bar so just had to wait for someone to show up. Pretty sure it only stays open based on the need for more restaurants to cater to the large tourist crowd.

I came because I had a living social offer. I'll come back because the food as service were great. A Thursday night at 7 isn't the best time to get the usual feel for a Nashville Bar, but it was the perfect time to really experience the food. I travel a lot and eat in restaurants ranging from dives to coat and tie only.... Here, the menu is limited as you would expect from a bar. I ordered the Sweet and Spicy  burger and my wife ordered the Sweet and spicy chicken sandwich. Both we're cooked well and tasted great. I'd put them up against ANY burger I've had in Nashville including at the Pharmacy. The fries were actually potato wedges which I prefer anyway. The musician was Adam (didn't catch the last name) but he was really talented. The only reason I wouldn't give it 5 stars is that they were out of Guinness.... The Stone IPA was a great backup option. They have an impressive (10 tap?) collection of craft draft. To sum up, this place was awesome and I'll be back!

I hadn't been to Burger 360 in a while, but I recent made a visit. They've made several changes, such as menu and style of food. In my opinion, these changes aren't the best, and I'll probably never go back.

This place is great. You can laugh for hours while the musicians entertain you with witty jokes and songs. Very talented staff that helps out with some songs the way. Never been disappointed with the show but the drink prices are a little steep.

Song Suffragettes were awesome.  Would love to review the food, but we still don't have it over an hour after ordering.....

Food finally came out, definitely was not worth the wait.  E-mailed management the day after expressing disappointment.  Never heard back.  With how long it took to get the food, I expect a reply in about 6 months or so....

Probably some of the better singers I saw were here. The bar is about average, drink selection is good and prices are average for the downtown area. Food selection was again about average for downtown. We had the fried pickles and they were good. Worst part about this bar is the bathrooms. They are prison style stainless with no seat, no urinals, and only one person at a time which in a busy bar is no good. For some reason they never really had a crowd when I was in several different times over a couple days but I didn't mind as I was looking to escape the Broadway crowd

This is one of the worst customer service experiences I ever had. The food and drinks are good, but the staff is awful and they just communicate terribly. They have about twenty managers which means nothing ever gets done and the staff has a horrible attitude and they clearly don't care about their jobs.

The museum is amazing! The interactive stands to play hits at your leisure is great. There is a vast collection of hand written and other memorabilia from his life that really help tell the story. 

I did not, however, appreciate the cashier Courtney blatantly making fun of my mother to her coworker for asking questions about a shirt purchase. It was extremely rude.

Great museum if you are a Cash fan! 

Took us about 30 min to buy tickets and get in and another hour or so inside the museum.

There is a TON of things to see and ALOT to read so you cN stay longer if dedicated. 

I am definitely a fan of his music and really enjoyed my time here. Would recommend anyone coming to Nashville stop by.

My knowledge of Johnny Cash before this museum tour was embarrassingly minimal. My husband apparently has been a huge closet fan for our entire marriage. Oh the things you learn! Well anyway, we decided to take a weekend and play tourist.... which of course meant visiting the Johnny Cash museum. In true closet fan fashion, my husband slowly strolled in the museum reading every little detail posted on the wall. The museum was a lot smaller than I expected, but it did have a lot of information. Even the worlds biggest closet fan could probably only end up spending an hour and a half here. The information was good, and we enjoyed ourselves.

The museum inspired us to learn more about Johnny, and we ended up renting the Ring of Fire movie. Which was great! I wish we would have watched it before going to the museum, I would have appreciated it more.

I'm not sure where the "360" comes from, but the burger part is very clear. 360 Burger is about burgers. Beef, chicken (grilled or fried), turkey, salmon, you call it. Pick your bread and then either choose one of the predetermined "local favorites" or go with the extras you want.

Beer and "happier hour" specials are priced at a nice round $3.60 and I got here in time to get two beers (small ones, but still two of them) in frosty mugs for that nice price. Spirits, wine, mixed drinks are also on the menu.

I went right to it with the "certified grass-fed beef" and the local favorite that they call "Pimento and Pig" which is a good scoop of pimento cheese and two big slices of bacon. With my side of waffle fries, this was a big sized meal and was quite tasty!

It's Nashville, so of course there is a stage with local music. And the ladies waiting tables are all very attractive. Because. Fortunately, I got here on a night that the music hadn't started yet which meant that I could enjoy my meal in a bit of peace.
so much fun! you need to check this place out. the muscians are great and the crowd is fun.

I really wanted to like this place but I'm afraid it was not meant to be. I took my family who had come in from out of town.  The venue is great and our waitress was lovely, but the food was unbelievably bad.  My daughter ordered plain pasta with butter, which is pretty hard to ruin, but it was completely inedible. My mother ordered the recommended signature sandwich and it came with cold bacon, cold toast, hard chicken and cold fries.  I had the portabello sandwich without the bread and got a measly slab of mushroom on lettuce (without the promised cheese).  The pulled pork plate was eaten - but at great cost later that evening.  Sorry, guys.  We WANT you to succeed but you've got to do better than this.  As to the music, I know these evenings are hit and miss and unfortunately this one was a big miss.  Artists -- even young ones -- need to know this is a PERFORMANCE.  A little energy.  A little preparation.  And, dare I say, a little talent, would be welcome.  People were snoozing in their seats.  Raise the bar, folks.  Raise the bar.

I love the downstairs layout and the few times I've been, the music has been great. My last visit was a bit of a bummer. Let's just say I'm no spring chicken and having to walk up MANY flights of stairs to enjoy the rooftop bar was a bit of a bummer. There's an elevator, but apparently only for staff. I'm sure I could have used it if I'd asked a manager, but who wants to admit they're old and feeble? Rooftop service was great, and food came quickly. A few more fries would have been nice with my $14 fish and chips, but the catfish was good. I'll be back, just probably not to the rooftop.

I've been to several shows here. The venue could be really cool but yall should really tell your sound guys to take it easy on the general volume of everything (could easily be 10db less), and the level of the kick drum and the bass are constantly too high. Also a little less reverb on the vocals would go a long way. And I'm not a crotchety old person, and all my musician friends agree. I know the current fad in live sound is to make everything loud and rely on the subs to make the vibe happen, but most music doesn't need that.
Food is mediocre and the night we were there the music was mediocre too. It was a special evening for my husband and I and we were excited to be there. But sorry it didn't deliver.
Great place to spend a few hours. Come early if you want to sit. Fantastic music, interactive crowd, and very tasty house drinks what more could you ask for.

Love this place!!! I had the opportunity to check this place while on a cross country road trip. The day prior I went through the Elvis Presley museum/house and while this one isn't quite as big and elaborate, this still do a great job at telling his story line while also providing items of his for display. My only complaint is that I wish they would have regulated the amount of people who were allowed in. It becomes a little too crowded.
Great food and atmosphere, been twice csnt wait to go back!

Terrible service!! It was noon  and 3 people were in the bar and we couldn't hear each other! No live music which was fine, but when we asked the bartender to turn it down she was extremely rude and condescending.  Never going back!

Loved it here! Small space but so much to see and listen to. We only have ourselves an hour to tour but you could easily spend 3-4. The Hurt music video at the end was just so moving. He was truly the man!!!

A little pricey for burgers, but hands down the best burger I've had in a LONG time! The sweet potato fries are to die for and there are many burgers to choose from and all I've tried have been delicious. The restaurant itself also has a cool, laid-back vibe. They have trivia nights and live music nights as well as a full bar and drink specials. If you're craving a burger it's a must.

The captain and the staff of the General Jackson were extremely accommodating to our party.  The food was very good, but more importantly, the entertainment was fabulous.  We never expected the show to be so good.  We spent $135. for each Captain's Table ticket, but it was well worth it.
