You get VIP treatment during the entire cruise, which includes first to board and meeting the captain for a little history of the ship, front row seating on the top deck in front of the band, a free cocktail, escorted to your table for dinner by your own waiter, another private tour by the captain, which includes the bridge, and a free General Jackson tee-shirt.  A must see while in Nashville.

I can't speak highly enough about the service and the atmosphere. I loved the old structure mixed with the new sounds.  Food wise, my group split a lot of shareable items.  The fried pickles had the perfect about of "fry" and sauce.  The artichoke dip with the garlic pita had the perfect amount of seasoning. The meatball slider could have used a bit more spice and the fritters could have used a bit more shrimp, but we had just eaten a most amazing Tennessee Hot slider. I must say though, my favorite item was the side of grits. Maybe it's more nostalgic than anything, but I've never tried grits as good!

Please do not waste your money if you are looking for a fun time. This is a very touristy trip with marginal food and the show is over the top cheesy. The servers had terrible body Odor and the boat was dirty. Too many other great options out there in Nashville for authentic country music and the river is not scenic at all with dirty water and manufacturing industry lined shores.

The singers were talented but again, one of the cheesiest shows ever....felt bad for the performers.

Your experience at the Listening Room definitely depends on the performers that evening. All the seats are good, but your service will really depend on where you are sitting. The food is really overpriced for the quality, but that is to be expected at a cafe like this. There are better venues for live music in the city, but this is a historic option. Be sure to check out the line-up before you buy tickets!

I've been to the  Listening Room twice when visiting Nashville. I really enjoy this venue. The room is large with comfortable seating. My daughter usually buys tickets beforehand, but both times we went, it was not sold out. The singer/songwriters are always super talented and it's nice to hear the background about why they wrote their songs. They have a decent draft beer list. Haven't tried the food, but I honestly come for the music. I would highly recommend coming here for some wonderful entertainment.

I wish I could review LRC separately for food & venue-this place is a solid 2.5 stars for food, and if I could give it 10 stars for venue/music/event I would.  For starters, the place is a little chaotic between shows, so check in & go grab a drink from the bar and sit in a booth while waiting for people to filter out. (Bonus points for free valet). We started with fried pickles before the show, not impressed. They weren't hot, so it made me think  they were sitting out for a while and the batter tasted over cooked. They had a sweeter flavor than most fried pickles I've had, so I'm sure they are good when they're hot. For dinner food my walnut cranberry salad was okay, my friend said their turkey on their sandwich tasted like soap, and the PBLT & brisket sandwich were just okay. 

Now, onto the good stuff. It's a singer/songwriter venue, and man, this is how music was meant to be listened to. It was incredible. It was an intimate setting, the acoustics were great, the songwriters were extremely personable. I would go back in a heartbeat to listen to the songwriters they bring in.

UPDATE: I spoke to Kevin via email regarding the extremely poor service my table received. Kevin spoke with the GM, Chase and stated that they would "be happy to refund the balance of my tab." I emailed back thanking them and gave them the necessary information in order to get a refund. It was now been 10 days since that email. I have called as well as sent another email. Surprisingly enough, I still do not have a refund. They have yet to give me a call back or answer my emails. 

WARNING. DO NOT COME TO THIS ESTABLISHMENT. They do not care about customer service and just want your money. I will be warning all friends and family about this.

It was terrible. I was with a group that had made reservations for brunch well in advance. There was practically NO food on the buffet. I got a tiny pancake. I had also ordered coffee... it never came.

I was one of the lucky ones though... some paid for the buffet and got a piece of fruit only... some got nothing, but insisted on not paying.

There was only one other table besides our group, so the restaurant wasn't even 1/2 full. I have no idea what they would do if any locals actually came to their Sunday brunch... I imagine not much different though.

My bill was $25.00 with a 20% gratuity. $30 for a pancake and water... I should have refused to pay. The owner of this restaurant owes some serious refunds to the people in my group, and I can assure you that none of us will ever return!!!

Food is deceptively good.  Does not look like anything special from the website and other reviews but sweet and spicy fried pickles and fried green tomato sandwich with pimento cheese?  Yes please!  Bloody Mary's are fire and the music is incredible.  Oh and they take reservations for large groups.  Love

I came for brunch with a large party expecting the buffet.  The buffet was small and resembled a hotel breakfast. So I decided to stick to the menu. Had a fantastic turkey and apple sandwich with the best sweet potato fries I ever had. I also tried the gravy from a buddy of mine, pretty good as well. The sweet tea didn't taste much like tea. The service was ok, the waitress seemed like she was working, but the infrastructure isn't ideal. Ok experience, better if you like live music.

If you don't like this place you're an a-hole. 

This is a must for anyone into Johnny Cash / music / rock n roll. I've never seen so much stuff / info in such a small space. This is literally one of the most well designed museums I've ever seen. Everything from Johnny's personal letters to his awards to his clothing to yearbook photos to parts of his house were there. Detailed descriptions explained everything. Honestly was amazing!!! Plus it's across he street from the goo goo store.

This was a great place to stop...the artifacts and stories were outstanding and the venue itself is really kept up.  Very well lit and clean.  The gold records, grammys, and record covers were really neat to see.

The last stop on the self guided tour is the "hurt" video and the awards that went with it.  That video is a work of art.  If it doesn't give you goosebumps then you are dead inside.  The gift shop was mostly standard fare..but there were some hidden gems (autographs/one of a kinds) if your willing to step up and spend it.  A must see for tourists for sure

So,  first time here.  We asked at the door who would be playing tonight, the answer we got from the lady selling the tickets "Oh, country music, the usual stuff".  Turns out we bought tickets for a benefit for some Christian ministry.  Not cool!  Also,  the board on the sidewalk advertises a $10 cover.  Cover is actually $12.  Also,  there is a $10 food and beverage minimum on top of the cover which we found out about once we were seated.  While this may very well be a lovely place,  clear and open communication would greatly improve visitor experiences.

Very disappointing.  We arrive at 1:15 on a Monday between hockey games.   There are 3 people in the restaurant when we arrive.   We had 30 people in our group and the gentleman said we needed to call ahead even though no one was in the restaurant.   He sat us anyway because we were just going to come in individually if he didn't.  They took our order in a reasonable amount of time (we were all sat at different tables rather than one big one which was fine with us).  We were told we couldn't order off the lunch menu even though we were there at lunch.  There were 3 at our table and 2 drink orders were wrong.  The food came and it was correct except the dressing on a salad that was supposed to be vinaigrette and they brought blue cheese.  She asked for vinegrette and they just brought vinegar.   The burgers are good but nothing special.  The molten chocolate cake was very good.  With our big group we didn't even fill up half the tables.  We will not visit here again when we are back up here for our next hockey tournament.

We had a great time tonight! Makers series with four very different artists. We all enjoyed it. The beauty of this sort of gig is that they aren't specifically country music influences which appeals to the non-country fans. Artists ranged from experienced to new performers but they all did a great job in letting their personalities shine. The place was only half full on a Thurs night. Venue is very nice, has great acoustics with a warm ambience. 

We all ordered dinner. Food was good. Mac cheese balls were overpowered by Parmesan in my opinion. The smoked chicken was good but mine was a little dry in places. My friends was perfectly moist. I grabbed some BBQ sauce and it was great. The black eyed peas, green beans, corn on cob and sweet tator tots were all good. 

I had two cocktails- the pear, which was very enjoyable, and the seedling which was good but I wish I'd skipped the black pepper  garnish. 

We all agreed it was a very pleasant night and would absolutely go back. The free valet parking (if you spend over $20) was also hassle free.
I expected a better band at this place.  Seriously.  Doesn't have to be country... but these people were awful.

We went here on Sunday night during Labor Day weekend and we went straight to the rooftop. The bartender was not that great. We waited for about 20 minutes and never got served a drink. He served everyone around us and we finally got fed up and went back down the second floor bar. It was such a bummer because we heard that the rooftop bar was really fun.

Oh my. I hate to do it but I'm going to have to drop a couple stars on this place. My group and I decided to stop in on New Years Eve and see what was gong on. I had fond memories of dancing and fun there a few years ago so I thought it would be a decent choice for us. WRONG. The rack room side was waaay too smokey and the music wasn't continuous. The dance side was honestly just kind of lame and tacky. Too many girls in sequined-out dresses and stilettos wobbling around and the DJ, although energetic, was playing pure crap. It appears that the average age of Blue Bar patrons are in their mid-late twenties and thirties. So why was he playing "music" that would appeal to 18 year olds? Some kind of booty-bass, thisismyfirsttimeataclub kind of music. Maybe I'm just old now, but I would much rather hear stuff that has actual lyrics and a good beat to DANCE to, not just drop it like it's hot. Also, there were NO TABLES ANYWHERE. There used to be high tables that you could at least stand next to and sit your drink on. The only way to have a table that night was to be part of  "Jason's" entourage and then you would be allowed access to the lounge part of the dance room. LAME. Wonder how much he paid for that crap? 

I realize that this was NYE and maaaaybe not what's typical for a Saturday, but I probably won't be back to find out. Boooo.

My friend and I were in Nashville for the weekend and we recommend to this place by our tour guide we had that morning.  This was exactly what we came to Nashville for and it was right downtown.  There were 4 singer/song writer performers that night (we went on a Saturday) and they were all great!  A nice change from the bars on Broadway where you are all cramped and sweaty.  We got a table in the front row and reservations were only $5 for the Saturday show.  Well worth it in my opinion.  I only give it 4 stars as the food was nothing exceptional - stay away from the apple slaw as it was terrible!  Also, if there happens to be a bachelorette party in the room, they tended to be a bit noisy and not really interested in the performance and were sometimes a distraction.  Other than that, if you are looking for some live music from actual songwriters this is a great place!  We had a great time and would recommend it!

This place is awesome! One of the best locally owned restaurants in Southeast Nashville. All of their food is locally sourced which makes for fresher and healthier product. Their burgers definitely rate an A in my book. I've had a few better, but not many. Their BLT sandwich is also something to enjoy. They've got good sweet potato fries and fried pickles. Live music and a full bar, but still very family oriented. Smoke free.

I've been to other wax museums but they don't hold a candle to the madame. Technically, no one should hold a candle near wax statues, but I digress. Lots of fun to be had here! Celebrities from days past as well as contemporary ones make this a well rounded experience. I wasn't a huge fan of the staff members making us take a bazillion pics in a couple of places so that they could try to sell us memorabilia at the end, but it's a business, so...*shrugs*. Still totally worth it!

Visited Nashville for a convention and passed by this bar after dinner. Didn't know what to expect but it was a pleasant surprise. We got there before the big crowd and really enjoyed ourselves. Andrew, Todd and one other fellow played the piano and drums. Great performers and had an awesome time. 

There was a waiter attending drink orders, but he never stopped by our table which was disappointing but the bar wasn't far from the stage.

A really fun & affordable place to hear live music in Nashville! This was the first stop for my friends and I right after landing at the airport, and it was definitely one of the highlights of our trip.

You can purchase tickets online in advance or at the door, and they'll seat you based on when you check-in in person. Get there earlier = get a table closer to the stage. The food/drink service was pretty fast considering so many people arrive all at the same time, and the draft beers were a great deal at $5 each for a lot of local beers.

The food was just alright - I'd recommend eating somewhere before if you have time (we didn't). But the atmosphere is really intimate and it's awesome to hear up-and-coming singer/songwriters. It's way better than going to any loud honky tonk on Broadway!
This place is really good, was the one burger place I could go to and actually get full and not feel bloated.. definitely awesome food.. I'll be going back again soon.

NO SEATING AVAILABLE!  They 'pulled' the seats supposedly at the artists request. I would not have bought tickets if I knew I would have to stand for hours. Their website and the confirming email I received said nothing about this being a standing room only show. There are about a dozen seats with small tables reserved for VIP's. And that is it.
Nice but crowded. You can move at your own pace but plan for an hour to see everything. Bit $$$ but its a tourist attraction.

Wasn't a big fan of the brunch we had this morning. Great music but super loud.The breakfast burrito was bland and basically filled with undercooked sliced potato. 

The Pub Mary was way too salty. I liked that they took a risk with it and used fresh tomatillo, but for every sip of drink I had to take a hit of water.

Very overpriced for what it was.
Food is terrible but great venue for live music. Be aware, if you don't specify the vodka you want, they will charge you for the most expensive one they have.  What a rip off.

I want to start out by applauding the guys on stage who played that night, they were awesome. Not only are they great at playing but they were pretty hilarious too. The crowd was really fun and bartenders were great. Overall we had an amazing experience here and it's a must-go if you're in downtown Nashville.

Tried another popular open mic and fell short so decided to research all others. Found we weren't near those either so went with The Listening Room. Everything happens for a reason! What a great night! Let's start with the food: great! The turkey apple crisp sandwich: amazing! Drinks are good and Von is a great server! The singer-songwriters are gracious and humble.  This is a great venue! You can't go wrong here. Close to downtown, great food, great servers and amazing singer-songwriters!
Great place all around! Enjoyed the food and the drinks did the job! One of our favorite spots so far this weekend! Caroline on the 2nd floor was awesome as well...great service!

I really enjoyed my visit here. It's set up really well, with plenty of exhibits to keep you occupied for hours, but in a way that you can do a quicker tour as well. There's a short film you can watch, a number of interactive exhibits, and lots of information, broken down in digestible and easy to follow ways. I would definitely recommend this as a stop for anyone visiting the area.

Great relaxed atmosphere with good music and good food. Can't ask for more really. Just off Broadway so seems a lot of people seem to miss it as it was pretty empty when there were a ton people a block away. Do yourself a favor and give it a try.

I enjoyed the museum! as a big Johnny Cash fan, I'm the type who would have liked to have read the descriptions of all the items in the exhibit and go through it at my own pace. it was too crowded (not much space to begin with!) to do that when I went but I was still able to spend time looking at my favorite items such as his yearbook, military items, lyrics, etc. the store is great too, the merchandise is quality!

We went on the lunch ride despite the poor reviews, because this is the only paddle boat ride available,  and had a fantastic time. The price was affordable, the staff was very friendly and courteous, the boat and bathrooms are very clean, the food was delicious, the show was entertaining and the scenery was beautiful. Very relaxing thoroughly enjoyed it. Highly recommended.

We went to this restaurant for a goodbye brunch for 50+ people. The manager was so confused and the wait staff had no clue how many of us were coming in. They do not have any decanters for coffee. One of our organizers even asked if she could help get the coffee to the group she was told they do not have decanters and can only do one cup at a time. Half the group did not get their drinks. When we first walked in I asked the waitress if they have a gluten free option on the buffet the waitress couldn't even tell me what was on it. Once the buffet was empty they did a terrible job refilling it. They provided menus to our group but then told us that we could not order from the menu. So we paid $18 for an empty buffet. On top of that we had to pay a gratuity of 20%.  Also I saw into the kitchen there was only 1 cook working. I asked the manager if she could run my card and she told me she could not that only a server could.  I find this terrible. I hope that the management reaches out to our group to make it right. Also we had people from all over the world and country there this was their last meal in Nashville and all it did was leave a bad taste in our mouths!

We came into this place on this past Saturday night. It was a hot one in Nashville, upwards of 90 degrees & humid as all get-out. One step into this place & a HEAT WAVE hit you. It was easily over 100 degrees in there. Which I guess makes the attitude of the bartender appropriate? She was cold & ignoring patrons. I even saw her throw cards back into peoples faces. No thanks Dierks.. nothing compared to the Jason Aldean bar.

Haven't been in a year and won't go back again. Burger size is much smaller than before. The bun swallored it. The burger patties appear totally different and the burger was very dry and nothing special whatsoever. The raw vegetables and other tasty sides are no longer avaialbe. Changing bun types now cost $1 more, choosing sides other than fries now cost $1 more. Two burgers and one drink cost $31 plus $5 tip. We both thought Five Guys would have been far superior and less than half the price. Very disappointed. This place started off great and we loved it. The menu, food quality and prices changed. We would rather see prices go up than food quality and menu item availability go down. KInd of insulting to be hit with a dollar to make changes that used to be included.

What a cool place! I was staying at a near by hotel and wanted a quick bite. The staff is so friendly and the burgers are amazing. The meat has the best flavor and the brioche bun was an added bonus. This would definitely be my spot if I were a local. Check it out. Just a really cool fun vibe and great food.

WAY COOL and I loved the mini theater where you could watch Johnny cash as an actor. In one scene he grabs a young Ron Howard as a shield and he (Ron) gets shot an dies......bad dad.
Lots of goodies, videos, music stations, records and displays with his guitars, song sheets and outfits he once wore. Make sure you visit the "Hurt" video display before you leave and watch a master of his craft at the end of his days.
My only gripe is that we didn't have enough time to tour the Patsy Cline exhibit there too.

It was a busy evening and we were directed to the top floor, rooftop and were told there was plenty of room for our table of 6...we headed up three flights of stairs and ended up not being able to sit at a table until another group left. Once we were actually seated, we ended up ordering beer and appetizers initially. The waitress actually surprised us...she didn't write anything down, the drinks came out right but the appetizers came out at all different times. We waited over an hour for our burgers and they never came. The waitress finally went to ask the manager and they had no explanation as to why we didn't have our food. For the appetizers, we ordered a pretzel, hummus and fried pretzel. They were decent. The waitress was sweet and accommodating. The view was awesome!

I am a huge fan of this venue. It's in that sweet spot of being the perfect size; not too big and not too small. I came here for the first time on Friday night for a sold out show, but never felt annoyed with the audience. It was very crowded but not so bad that I couldn't go to the bathroom or wait a long time for a drink. I appreciate that! You can always find a good spot along the sides, and we were even able to get close to the front later on in the show without issue. I love that! Drink prices are reasonable and the bathrooms are very clean and new, which is a nice change from some other venues in Nashville. 
I really enjoy the Basement East and can't wait to check out another show here!

The atmosphere of this place makes up for the lack of good food.  It's not even good bar food.  To their credit, there was one waitress and one cook there the night we went.  The entertainment was what made us stay.  The guys playing were super.

We were pretty disappointed by this venue.  The service was terrible, but it was apparent that they were severely short-staffed.  It took 45 minutes to order a drink at our table.  Another 45 for a plate of hummus.

The performance was also a letdown.  A stage with 4 different musicians playing together and taking a turn with their own original songs.  We actually did not enjoy any of them.  We saw far more talent and excitement on Broadway (and for free!).

Stopped in last night for a couple of drinks. I went in first & was served pretty quickly. My wife came in about 3 mins after me. We sat at the bar for almost 5 more mins waiting for the bartender to ask what she would like to drink, but she was too busy talking to another co worker about what she did the night before. So, I told my wife that I was going to the restroom & that I would be right back.

I walked into the men's room & they only had lights working near the urinals....I turned my flashlight to be able to see the toilet & there was mold all over it! NASTY!!!!! 

After I left the restroom I thought it couldn't get any worse, but I was wrong. My wife was still sitting at the bar without a drink! I paid for my beer & we left. Save yourself time & go where the service is great, like Robert's Western Bar down the road. They took great care of us!
This place is amazing! Decent prices for some amazing food! Only been here twice but walked out satisfied. Great atmosphere. Awesome staff. Never had any problems with service ever!

Absolutely delicious! I had the Spicy Rooster with aioli & a side of sweet potato fries. It wasn't as spicy as I was expecting which was fine but the flavor from the jalapeño infused oil that the chicken was cooked in have it that extra pop of flavor. Will defiantly be back!
Good venue with plenty of space. We went to the Dixie chicks tribute concert and it was a good time.

We had a large group event - 50+ people a few weeks ago that went horribly!  Reservations were made, but the manager never informed his staff of the large group coming in so they were completely unprepared.  They ran our of food on the buffet before even half of our group went through the line and only refilled it ONCE maybe twice and we were there for at least an hour and a half. The brunch buffet was more expensive that was advertised on their website and I wouldn't really classify it as brunch at all.  Bland sausage gravy and biscuits, eggs (if you could get them since they never refilled them), bacon, chicken wings, fruit cup and yogurt. And french toast that was only meh. Unbelievably this southern establishment didn't even have grits anywhere on the buffet - or even on the menu.  It was almost 30 minutes before I received my drink order as well - a half decent sweet tea.  The wait staff was wonderful - doing the best that they could.  But they were understaffed because the manager never told anyone that a large group was coming in.  I left there still hungry and almost $30 lighter in my wallet.  Nashville was a wonderful city, but this restaurant was just the pits.  Save yourself the grief and go to Pucketts's Grocery.  The food was much better and the live music fantastic.

I love this place, such a fun environment for a bite or a few drinks and some live music! Also, I enjoy the variety of options available from honky tonk, to club, to rooftop bar which are all done well! It's pretty busy on weekend nights (like much of Broadway) but seems to deal with the crowds better than most of the big bars downtown. It's like it was better designed to handle the large crowds without feeling too cramped or claustrophobic. I've gone after weekday Preds games as well and had good times then as well. Our crew has had Jasmine as our bartender a few times and she's a rock star who kind of typifies the vibe here. Fun, friendly, no pretense and just happy to suggest drinks and joke around with the guests. She's awesome, and service from other staff has been great as well! Whiskey Row is the real deal!

This was BY FAR, the HIGHLIGHT of our trip! 

We saw Bonner Black and friends: 
Katie Mae Smith
Taylor Matthews
AJ Kross

I was told about this place by a local so I had purchased tickets online prior to our trip. Approx $7 per person. + $10 food/drink minimum. Totally worth it!! 

Everyone was sooooooo talented! We didnt want the show to be over. 

This is their new location and we were told it was more intimate and better than their previous one. It was a small audience. Maybe about 40 or so people. 

Didnt order any food. Just got a drink. Service is good. 

You MUST come when in Nashville. Awesome intimate venue and exceptional talent!

We just missed happy hour (still had a drink or two, though), but the food was great and service - courtesy of Nick, our server - was top notch! Kids loved their Krabby Patties and the Tropic Thunder Burger m-m-m-m-makes me happy!

As a Johnny Cash fan, I greatly enjoyed my trip to the Johnny Cash Museum. I was on a a tight schedule so I was there for about an hour and a half. That being said, I wouldn't have spent that much more time there because it was about the size of an extensive exhibit at a bigger museum. 

Between the cool artifacts and movie compilations, I thought that this museum was well worth my time and money. There were iPads that made the information a bit more interactive. There were also handwritten letters and many artifacts that gave a lot of insight into the personal life of Johnny Cash which you really won't find elsewhere. 

I thought I was semi-knowledgeable about Johnny Cash, but I definitely learned a lot. This place is perfect for people who are interested in music history or are at least moderate fans of Johnny Cash. However, it's scope is limited so I wouldn't recommend it for others due to the price of entrance.

Good music scene.  Stay away for brunch, nothing special at all.  Food was mediocre, the scramble came out moderately hot, the buffet look like something out of a cheap hotel.  Orange juice was concentrated out of a bag.  Coffee was burnt.  Come for the music and a cocktail, that's about it.

Fantastic burger. I have no clue how this restaurant isn't rated 5 stars. Other than super busy days/nights service is flawless, and the burgers have never not been amazing. Also, where else can you get freaking awesome waffle fries!?

Pretty much is what it's name says it is. Nothing fancy, just a big room with a bar and small stage.  It's a perfect size venue for showcases of artist and songwriters.  The room is just big enough to accommodate a small crowd and keep an intimate vibe musically.  I didn't eat there but they have foods.  I think it's a nice stop if you visiting and staying downtown Nashville.

I'm a huge Johnny Cash fan, and the Johnny Cash Museum was my first stop on my first trip to Nashville. It didn't disappoint. From Yelp to Trip Advisor, the reviews of this place rock. It ranks #1 on the Forbes and National Geographic Travel Lists and is one of only six Nashville attractions that has received the 'AAA Gem Rating',  and is authorized by the estate of Johnny Cash. What does all this mean to a visitor? It simply means, whether or not you are a Johnny Cash fan, you will be WOWED. This is a must see Nashville attraction.

For a complete review and TONS of photos--please visit my site at: www.TNBTA.com

I must say I was disappointed . We have been waiting for this bar to open. Well, we are back in Nashville and went here first... we didn't eat so we can't comment on the food. The bar service was mediocre at best. The worst part is...  THIS BAR HAD ONE RESTROOM, LIKE ONE STALL, FOR THE ENTIRE BAR... And it's a shared bathroom for male and female. I stood in line for 10 mins at 4 in the afternoon. We paid our bill and left because I wasn't going to do this all night. Highly disappointed they only thought it was important to have a 1 staller ... Band was good but wasn't staying!!!!

From previous posts, their answer is there are other restrooms upstairs. But the upstairs was closed today so, no other option but to leave. Besides, who only has ONE STALL on the main floor??? Poor planning!!!

I'm a Johnny Cash fan and this was more than I expected to find after hearing it was in a relatively small footprint.  Great storytelling following his timeline, listening centers, hand written letters and music, clothes, items received from Folsom Prison, etc etc etc.  If you are a Cash fan, you'll love this and it will give you a spine tingling sensation. It was the biggest reason I came to Nashville, and I left happy.

Good place for music but the food was just plain mediocre to not good. In a town with an abundance of excellent choices I wouldn't waste calories here.  We had the Saturday brunch, I ordered an omelette with smoked chicken, spinach and smoked Gouda with country potatoes.  They over cooked the eggs to the point that they were browned, the country potatoes were just cubed deep fried potatoes a little on the greasy side.  My girlfriend ordered the "potato hash" which came with 2 choices from the omelette ingredient list.  She got smoked chicken and smoked cheddar.  The potato hash was just the deep fried country potatoes with the ingredients tossed in.  Stick with music and drinks, it seems that's more in their wheel house.

This is a great museum for anyone who is a Johnny Cash fan.  It was larger and encompassed a lot more memorabilia that I was expecting.  It was fascinating to see many personal items of Johnny Cash's and read quite a bit of history.  I would highly recommend.  Also, the gift shop has a nice selection of items with a coffee shop attached.

First visit, last visit!   Came for the 9 pm show.  30 minutes and still waiting on a beer.  No take service.  Bartenders are so slow.  Apparently the owners don't care about customers or making money!  Lame, lame, lame service!  Bring a six pack!

Beautiful alternative to Bluebird Cafe. Great song writers in a Round format where each writer takes turns singing a song they have written. Roomy, beautiful venue. Younger scene than Bluebird if you  cant get tickets there. Loved it. Two shows a night. Inexpensive and you can use the valets to park. We walked from the footbridge. Pretty at night.

The music was amazing at this spot. We are from out of town and came to catch a songwriters round. Everyone was listening attentively, and the food was very good. I would say the prices are a bit high, but I am glad they are supporting the musicians. The wait staff were a bit slow, but given the atmosphere I don't blame them.

Great music, horrible service. It took 45 minutes to get someone to take our order and another 45+ for him to bring out our waters. I would have gone to the bar but I didn't want to miss the performances. 
I still haven't received them, I'm just hoping our appetizers and waters show up at some point. 
Musicians are amazing and the food sounds great, I just haven't received it to let anyone know how it tastes.  
Edit - I just walked to the bar to get my own water. No idea where the food is and no sight of the guy who took our order. 
I created a yelp account just to leave a negative review for this place. I feel bad doing so, but I've never had worse service at a restaurant or bar. I wish I'd known how non-existent the service was because i'd have eaten at one of the many amazing (reviewed) restaurants nearby instead of wasting my time here.

Far from impressed.  My husband and I ate here this past Tuesday around 5:30.  The waitress who sat us had her booty hanging out of the bottom of her shorts.  NOT a fan of using sex to sell stuff :/  I'm not sure which was more fake, her tan or her attitude.  There was only one other table of guests when we got there.  Obviously, I don't know how long they waited for their food.  But it came to them about 10 minutes after we were seated.  Then our food took another 10 minutes to get to our table.  I was really disappointed that it was just warm.  The cheese on our burgers had already started to solidify and our fries/onion rings were cold...no to mention, frozen items, not fresh.  We were on our way to a concert and were already behind schedule because of the wait on our food.  So I didn't complain and I wasn't about to send it back.  If you've seen the movie, Waiting, you know exactly why.  Needless to say, we won't be back.
Lots of memorabilia, info, clips and such. Excellent complement tour to the Country Music Hall of Fame Museum - both are included on the Nashville city pass.

Was there on June 13, music was absolutely fabulous! HOWEVER, we waited a very long time for a very disappointing COLD meal! And 4 of the 6 of us had some intestinal issues afterward. This has so much potential..... Fix this food problem!!!!
Best food I had in Nashville . I love the chicken sandwich. Everything we have tried is soo good. And of course Dana Marie is the best. Always great music.
The burger was good the fries were cold and the waitress got mad at us for tellin her to wash her hands after sweeping the floor. Gross!!! My first and last time here!

Big Bang is a must-go while on Broadway!  Although I haven't been in a dueling piano bar before, I'd have to say that it was definitely an entertaining way to spend a Saturday night.  The talent here, like that of every other bar on the row, is amazing, but add a bit of comedy, crowd interaction and music from all different genres is what makes this place stand out!  One of the musicians, Justin, played the piano, guitar, drums and was a crazy good singer.  Where else can you find that kind of talent?  I've been to a few bars on Broadway and although they all were fun, the Big Bang stands out among the rest and let's just say I'll be back!

Came in on a Saturday during lunch to find out they were out of burgers. My appetite went out of the window immediately! I ended up having just the lobster bisque. It was too rich for my taste but wasn't terrible either. My friends had the steak and eggs, fried egg bagel and scrambled eggs. They said theirs was good. There was a girl performing an acoustic song when we got there but she only sang two songs. I forgot her name but she was extremely talented. 

The service was terrible. Our server was extremely slow.
Terrible service. So bad that we left before being served. They were disrespectful and left us sitting there for 30 minutes. I'll never know if the food is good as we'll never go back

The experience started off well; nice solo act performing with her guitar, friendly host, beautiful atmosphere. But our visit ended terribly. Service was horrible, waitress was slow and not very friendly, management was awkward, entire visit was too long and our food came out cold. We stopped in for brunch bc of recommendations from visit nashville sites, and a banner on the building. We would have had a better time stopping somewhere else...
Nice venue. Good music and good food. Plenty of room. Visit this place!

This place gets the 5 star review based on ambiance and original live artists' performances alone! Shocked that the yelp reviews are not better.  We saw "Jordan Minton and Friends "... This is the sort of music that You want to come to nashville to hear. Loved every second of it. Didn't order entrees but got some ridiculously good mixed drinks! Loved it!

My family met friends at 360 Burger last night and receive 4 stars from all. Food was great and they even serve a black bean burger for the vegans in our group. The only negative comment was from my 13 year old who is into all things ice cream. Apparently they no longer serve shakes. Not a deal breaker for the rest of us. We were seated immediately (party of 8) and the server was very attentive with beverage refills and check-ins during the meal. Southeast Nashville has experienced some positive growth recently and this is a terrific addition. I love to find good places to eat in our community and we will absolutely be back!

I would give it a zero if I could. On Oct 31, 2014, I was refused entry even though I paid $25 for the block party entrance fee. The front door bouncer declined to let myself and every African American male who paid for block party entrance into the establishment.  When I asked him what his reasoning was for letting the white friend I was with in and not me, he replied, "because I said so." I will be reporting this experience and these observations to the regional human rights office.

Could't get into the Bluebird Cafe so my Girlfriend and I thought we would give this place a try. We were not disappointed, the food, drinks, and music were amazing! Would definitely recommend to anyone looking for the Nashville music scene!

Blake did an awesome job organizing a private party for 90 women educators.
The food was good and the drinks were reasonable!
We all had a great time!

As a Nashville Native and a lover of Broadway, this place is the worst establishment on the strip. I have came here a few times and i always have a bad experience. I'm a very observant person when i go into places, and from what i have seen, this place is terrible. First, of all this place is infested with bugs, especially gnats and roaches. Gnats especially on the third floor where the bathrooms are located. Before, I was able to form my own opinion and visit initially i was warned about the racist and aggressive security and was also warned about the immense drug flow that goes on. Management seems to be very unprofessional to customers. I noticed when I was on the second floor, a guy kept throwing fruit at customers and employees like a joke. I later found out that was the General Manager. SERIOUSLY? I travel a lot and have been to MANY nightclubs, I've never seen anything dysfunctional like this. If you're going to be racist, at least try to cover it up or something. If you're going to enforce a dress code, make sure you enforce it towards EVERYONE! Not just those on the darker side on the spectrum. This bar has a AWFUL reputation in Nashville and I truly can see why. Don't spend your money here!

Visited the Best Burger place in town again last nite and wasn't disappointed in the burger nor the service but they changed their onion rings. They are not worth ordering.  Talked with several people that ordered them as well and everyone was disappointed in the change. Burger is still tops but onions I would rate is an zero.

Great music. Rocking country band was downstairs, one of the best we heard all weekend.  Upstairs more mellow/ acoustic absolutely fantastic quality.  Enjoyed our time there and wished we would have found this gem sooner.
Music was cool (live band). The steak and cheese was delicious! Fries were gigantic and the onion rings were on point!

This museum was well worth our time and money! While it was not very big in size, there were lots of artifacts that allowed us to spend a lot of time there. It was amazing to see  all of the pieces Johnny Cash owned and to see his handwritten lyrics and notes. The layout of the museum was very organized, starting with a brief overview of Cash's life by each decade and then showing artifacts from the beginning to the end of his life. I did not purchase anything from the gift shop for fear it was overpriced.  However, after walking into more places downtown I quickly realized the merchandise was the same price as other places and better quality. I would highly recommend stopping in this museum for a visit.
Stopped by the Swingin Doors Saloon while on the pedal tavern. They had a great 2-for-1 domestic drink special for pedal tavern participants, can't beat it!

I'm about two weeks late writing this. I hope I remember their names correctly, Kenny and Angel. They were super cool and friendly all night. Thank you both!

We spent the night going from the patio to inside and back out. Never really had to wait for a drink. Can't wait to come back and live it up on a Tuesday. 

The band was also great!

Small but worth it! 
I have no idea why it's $20 to get in but it's a small place about 10 rooms cataloging JC's life. I liked it! I don't know that I would need to go back but it's a bucket list item checked off! So that's the shirt of it!

My friends and I took a trip on the General Jackson and it was a lot of fun. The show and food were great, as was the ride itself. The musicians are all extremely talented.

The best part was the two man show upstairs after the main show.

The staff, especially Lolita, was extremely helpful. I was running late and I should have missed the boat. However, the staff held the boat at the dock so I could make it.

I would recommend the General Jackson to anyone in Nashville.

Lo Cater was having a 80's night so after reading some reviews from fellow yelpers we decided to check out this spot...

Overall I liked it! Great stage area to accommodate live band and singers. Plenty of seating, 2 full bars, outside patio area with a decent view of the bridge, valet parking and other parking sites that are free within walking distance. Minus one star to the dude at the front door attempting to charge us 10$ even though we had reservations already and there was no for mentioned of a cover charge in thee advertisement SOOO no that wasn't happening on my watch! Food was decent and drinks a fair price, I had the barbecue nachos and my better half had wings along with two beers and one wine concoction I'm not sure what the name was but she hated it and I loved it! Total price $52...not bad in my opinion

So yes I will check out this spot again to hear local talent and partake in the ambiance a lil longer...fan!

I gave eaten here 3 times.in the last 2 weeks, I just love the wings (gotta get by from 3 to 6p.for 50 cent wings)I love the Burgers as well.the staff are always nice and The Owner always stops by to make sure everything is ok. Will definitely Return.
Hot server is on point.  Blood Orange mimosas are on point.  Food is on point.  Freaking awesome!  I will be coming back here.

Everything you ever wanted to know about the Man in Black. Extensive collection of his letters, photographs, guitars, costumes, memorabilia. Great video archive. Really fleshed out his biography along with his music. Enjoyable way to spend an afternoon in Nashville.

I have eaten at 360 Burgers many times since it opened.  I have tried many things on the menu too.  The Sliders (wonderful), NOLA Shrimp (not on the Menu anymore but fantastic), Fried Shrimp (yummy) and last week order the Fried Mushrooms (best I've ever had).  While I think everything I have eaten is great - I generally slide (sorry for the pun) to the Sliders with Onion Rings.  I haven't had one of their big burgers yet, but that's only because I'm a small person and the Sliders fit my appetite much better.  All my friends get excited if I ask them to come with me to 360 Burgers.  The food is great, the service is great and I love the atmosphere they have.

The drinks was fabulous. As for the food, I just got the hummus plate- but it was good. Entertainment- great. I much prefer lesser known artist singing originals, than crowded downtown average singers.

Visitors and guests be warned , I just spent the last 45 minutes standing outside for no reason waiting to get into be show tonight. I have been to the listening room three times now and never had to deal with this. Their ticket policy is such that if you do not buy tickets ahead of the show you want, then they make you stand outside for the first 15 minutes, while the show is going on , before slowly letting people trickle in. Also known as wasting my time. There are literally hundreds of other live music venues within ..5 miles and I would tell people to go anywhere else before trying to get into this place without pre-purchase. Thanks for nothing Listening room.

Super cool! 

I'm not particularly into Johnny Cash, but this definitely won me over. It's a nice size, though small, well-laid out considering the space constraints. 

After purchasing your tickets, your first stop is a nice person who explains the layout and a few top things to see. That was helpful because though it is well laid out, there is one weird thing where you need to walk a direction and then backtrack. 

I really liked the curation of materials. We skipped the listening stations and focused on the history, costumes, records, and other archives. The last bit of space is the best, the introduction to his cover of Nine Inch Nails "Hurt." I've seen the video many times, it's my favourite JC song, and I saw it in a whole new light after going through the museum. 

I'd recommend visiting this museum if you are in town.

The food is okay but nothing special. I had a horrible experience. I ordered 3 beers all together. The waiter forgot to bring the third beer so I asked another waiter who made sure I had one. No big deal. When the ticket came, I had been charged for 4 beers. When I told the server, he stated I had four beers and I was wrong and basically insinuated I was drunk and didn't know what I was talking about. I ate a lot and was inebriated in no way, just pissed of the accusations. I've never had this sort of treatment. I spoke with the manager after asking for him. He took the one beer off and gratuity. The server did not apologize. Needless to say I won't ever go back or support such rudeness. Never in my life had I been treated this way.
Best live music I heard in the Broadway area (which is saying a lot). Drinks are priced just below everything on the main strip and the bar had a cool atmosphere. Bartenders were very nice as well.

This is a great option downtown. We got there right before they started charging cover which we were happy about. This isn't a huge space and all the seats full up quickly. Even though we didn't get a seat, there was plenty of room in the bar area. The bartenders do a great job getting the drinks out fast. Did I mention they are soooo reasonably priced? 2 glasses of wine and 2 beers for only 20 bucks.

The dueling piano players are extremely talented. They knew tons of songs and do a great job keeping the energy up with the crowd. They play a mix of old and new and everyone is singing a long. 

If you're looking for something different to do downtown, then definitely check this place out!

Finally made it up to this place. Moved to Antioch and was looking for a much needed neighborhood bar, thirsty turtle sucks, so I walk in and instantly seated and recommended drinks food. Ordered a drink and app. And before I could have 4 chips my entree was out hot and fresh! Good music and a lot of bright natural light which is rare for a bar. I'll definitely be coming back again . Excellent!

Decent sandwiches, salads...nice set of musical talent, not too loud...can still talk over the music.  Industrial decor...very open...the apple fritters are unique, and the turkey, bacon, apple crisp sandwich is one-of-a-kind.

Off Broadway, but what a heck of a great bar to fall into and listen to some great music while being served by some of the sharpest and most attentive bartenders in Music City.  Nothing special...except for the authentic flavor of a great southern bar.  Just killer!

Right off of Broadway is a small bar that is always just busy enough to be a good time but never full enough to warrant a line. 

We seem to come in here when we are not quite ready to stand on line at the Stage or Honky Tonk Central, but with the usual Nashville crowd and performers plus the added benefit of no lines, fast service, and cheap drinks, the Swingin Door is a winner.
Must visit location in Nashville. This man was a saint, a sinner, and spoke his truth.

The meal was great, but a little late. Service with a smile? More like service without a smile. The food was satisfactory, but not made in a factory. Overall the time was a ball. Thank you riverboat for dinner with a float. The drinks were expensive

This place was nuts! 

By this point in the night one of my buddies had gone to the hotel, and another was visiting some friends in town. That left me with one guy, and we had a blast at this place. We pretty much stayed in the pool hall side, and met some interesting characters. 

One guy looked like Johnny Depp from Pirates of the Caribbean, the bartender was from Iowa which lead to some pretty interesting conversations, and we ended up partying with this guy who runs some underground gambling activities. Crazy night! Left this place to head downtown, but we certainly enjoyed our time here!

*****

Get to the Listening Room Cafe!
We attended the day of the grand opening of the new location and had a great time.  The artists who performed, including Chris, the owner, blew us away. The talent on the Listening Room stage was second to none.

The location is away from the hustle and bustle of Broadway, which provides a more laid back experience. It is an easy walk up 4th Street that is well worth the effort.

It is obvious that Chris has put his heart and soul into this project and to hear the setbacks he has overcome in opening this location, you can't help but appreciate his fortitude.

Thanks to Chris and the other talented artists for providing us with a great afternoon of music. Good luck in the new location!

Stopped in for a drink and discovered a quaint atmosphere on a Sunday afternoon. Carlton Anderson was playing the guitar and singing some great tunes. We requested a little Dierks and Carlton made it his own. Talented guy and will keep an eye out him on our return trip to the awesome city

Yes, I'm a local and no, I don't "hate Broadway".  We end up in the honky tonk district if we have out of town guests or if we attend a game or a show we'll take a lap too.  Last night I had a cousin visiting (bachelorette party, go figure) and she texted me that they were at Swinging Doors.  We'd walked past this bar a few times and always said, "We've never been in there" whilst walking right by.  Turns out, it's one of your better honky tonks.  The bartenders had a lot of personality, the music was really good and the whole place just felt newer, cleaner and smelled better.  Several HD TVs placed well so we could keep an eye on the Preds waxing the Blackhawks was good too.  This place and Robert's are going to be where we steer our guests.

I love me some Johnny Cash.  Seriously, I find it hard to believe anyone doesn't love the iconic Man in Black.  This well-done museum is a great homage to his life and legacy.  Located in downtown Nashville, the museum is definitely a little small for the amount of traffic it gets due to its location and attraction for tourists, but its worth a jaunt through.  There's so many interesting items to view as well as a listening tour of Cash' music over the years.  An interesting man with an interesting life, this museum does a great job of showcasing Cash with respect, making it at least feel more like a genuine spot of reverence than just a blatant cash grab.  This is something I recommend for locals and tourists alike, though off days are better to avoid the crowds and the crush within the confined space.  There are usually living social or groupon deals for admission as well, and parking near the building entrance, which is close to the pedestrian bridge.  Definitely worth a visit.
Tammie, the curly haired bartender, really just made our day.... We needed a place to go in this big city and she made is feel so much at home. Thank you, Nashville.

Oh my! OHMY! Bring the machete to cut the smoke and your own disinfectant to clean the table. Ran in outta the rain cuz it was a late kitchen and ran out just as fast as we could! Oops! Don't just don't unless you're up to date and then some on your tetanus shots and other vaccinations. I'm serious.

This is the place to go if you're not in the mood for country music. They were playing indie music when I went here, the guys did a great job performing. I heard from the waitress that the first show is free, and second show charge a cover on weekdays, the cover is cheap anyways. The food is decent, it was a good experience overall.

What a fun interactive tour!  This was our first time at a wax museum. The figures were so life-like. It was really amazing!  We have teenage and college aged kids with us and they really enjoyed it. So many photo opportunities throughout. It took us about 40 minutes to go through. If you have AAA you get $6 off per ticket so we saved $30 for our group of five.

I've eaten here many times since the place has opened and the food has gotten worse and worse. It seems that the food costs are eating at the place because the burgers gets smaller, the condiments get smaller and smaller. Hell, the last few burgers I've eaten had lettuce that was store bought from a bag rather than the way it used to be (fresh peeled, you can tell the difference.) and the tomato pieces are the ends of the tomatos, like silver dollar sized. The meat is always either dried well done or red on the inside. The fries get smaller and come in lesser quantities. Almost every time I've ever eaten there the food makes me sick and I regret it shortly afterward but it's close to me and convenience sometimes talks my body into doing dumb things.

Not to mention, the service here is garbage. There are new faces there each time I go in, except for a few regulars that have been there awhile. The only awesome server there is a shorter man named "Oli" I believe (oh god, hopefully I didn't spell it wrong) and he ALWAYS takes care of me and my friends. I tip him 35%-40% each trip just because he works his butt off to take care of me.

The worst trip I had was when I went to the bar and the bartender flat out ignored me. She was too busy chatting with a fellow male employee and texting on her phone to notice I was waving my hand and saying MISS after I had spent about 2 minutes trying to get her attention to tell her I wanted another drink. Why would you do this to your customers, just be helpful and take my money, I have lots and I want to spend it there.

I really wanted to give this place a chance. I really did, I don't think I'll be going back. For the $10 they want for a overdone burger and cold tasteless fries you could go buy 10 double cheeseburgers and have the exact same experience.

I HIGHLY discourage anybody from visiting this place, and hope that eventually they will read some of these reviews and go "huh, I guess we have room for improvement" (probably not).

I can't believe I am going to have to resort to fast food again.
Best Saloon in Nashville. Great service, friendly, personal and outstanding live music. Food looked great.

My wife and I stumbled upon this place in Nashville after dinner at Husk. The music is top notch and it is a way different vibe than the typical Broadway scene in Nashville. Apparently you need to make reservations. Luckily, the nice lady at the door let us stand in the back and we were able to nab some chairs. We didn't have the food, but what was coming out of the kitchen looked pretty good.

I really liked the Johnny Cash Museum. Was in and out in about 30-45 minutes. The museum was kindof small but good for what it was. 

TIP:  Watch for Groupons for 1/2 off!!

They had a lot of cool old things of Johnnys.  There were also iPads that made the information a bit more interactive. There was handwritten letters, clothes and many other items to view. 

There is also a museum store for you to grab your Johnny merch.

Music and mimosas were good. I guess we were here while they were in between seasonal menus so we had four(ish) items to choose from, and none of the delicious items listed on their website. The food was baaaad and it took a long time to get if. Maybe it'll be better when they set their new menu but for now just stick with the booze and music to be safe.

The venue is cool to hear music but we were surrounded by folks who wanted to do more talking than "listening". I loved my turkey, bacon, apple sandwich but the other people in group did not care for the blah chicken sandwich, burger and salad that was served with no dressing. The biggest issue was the super slow service. Either the kitchen is not equipped or they are understaffed.

My SO and I decided to break up a road trip with a stop in Nashville specifically to visit this museum. I purchased a Groupon that guaranteed admission for two for the low price of $19 and was blown away by the high quality experience we received for our money. This museum is an obvious must see for all Johnny Cash fans, but the exhibits also provide an education into the evolution of rock n' roll for all music enthusiasts. The facility is clean and well-lit, displays are thought out and plaques/signage are easy to read. The staff members are professional, attentive and knowledgeable about the exhibits. With ample parking nearby, there is no excuse to skip this delightful Nashville gem of a museum while you're in town and pay some respect to the Man in Black!

The environment is comfortable and the décor is nice.  My problem with 360 is the food and service.  For a place that is trying to be known for hamburgers they need to do an overhaul.  My hamburger tasted like they dumped a whole bottle of garlic in the beef.  The beef did not taste good at all it was of poor quality.  The server asked me how I wanted my hamburger I said medium-well but it came out well-done plus and charred.  The pretzel buns are overwhelming and it takes away from the burger.  You would be better off with a potato bun instead a personal favorite.  I also ordered bbq wings but they had so much bbq sauce on them you couldn't even eat them.  It was completely drenched and thick and gooey type of bbq sauce.  The night we went the owner did not come to our table and ask how the food was but sat around in the middle of the restaurant looking clueless. 

I almost forgot we order the wings as an appetizer but of course the entrée comes out first and then the wings.  

Unfortunately this place will not last.  If you don't care about service and food quality how do you expect customers to return.

Pass on Brunch...
It's not in my nature to be cruel but in adherence to the traveler mantra I have a duty to warn others in regards to this brunch.  Don't go!  We heard good things about the music that happens at night but if that's true, fine, but the brunch service has a ways to go.  

The rest of this review will be for management, hopefully they'll take steps to improve.  
Service: our apathetic waiter was at best, vacant. He took 20 mins to greet us at our table because he was "making coffee"...  So either the hostess should not have sat us at his station or maybe coffee should already be made (we arrived at 10:15, opening time is 10). The best was when we asked if we could get a to-go cup, he said he'd check. Came back ten mins. Later and when I asked again about the To Go, he said "probably, I'll check!"

Food:  I've seen better buffets at Country Buffet.  Cold, soggy, tiny waffles; hockey puck sausages, sausage gravy eew, rubbery eggs.  The seafood? Dip was good as was the fruit plate. The rubbery, hard eggs, waffles and sausages aren't surprising when they sit in a chafing dish for forty minutes.  Kudos to the kitchen for having food ready at ten a.m. But the service staff isn't helping you when it takes a party of four almost forty minutes to get plates to eat...btw, there were only eight customers (including us four) in the place!

Cost:  for three buffets, three drinks and one bottomless mimosa (eew) and a bagel sandwich the tab was almost $150.  We're from Chicago, we KNOW high prices but that was absolutely ridiculous considering the venue, service and quality of food.  If the restaurant wasn't so far away from everything we would have left but decided to stick it out and give it a shot. Lesson learned, listen to your gut and run!

I suppose we're just tourists and there's no chance we'll greatly affect this place but they should seriously re-consider the brunch trade because at this point they are just hurting themselves.

Again, I feel bad to leave a negative review but when the only good thing you can say about a restaurant is that no one got food poisoning, things need to change!

Hands down an Great music venue

Food quality was less than ideal and a bit pricy for what you get.  Did not finish salad entrée, just did not taste fresh.

We came here on a Saturday night to the early seating and did not have to wait very long to get in since we got there about 15 minutes early. We were seated at a great table with a great view. Our server was good, but they were out of many of the items on the menu (and we were the first seating of the night). Also, once the show started, she barely came around.

The show itself was awesome and the atmosphere was great! There were 4 artists who all had written songs for famous people. Their own music and voices were also great. We took our kids and they had high chairs and one artist even snag a children's song (coincidence). this would have been a 5 star review had the menu been fully available as the food was decent.

I love live music, which works out well since I live in Austin, TX. However, this also means I have high standards and happily the Listening Room did not disappoint. 

First, be sure to get reservations. They are free (at least they were every night that we were visiting Nashville) but it guarantees you have a spot to sit. Without a reservation, you are guaranteed to either stand in the back of the room or not be allowed in at all. Even with a reservation, get there early! We arrived 30 minutes before the music started and were one of the last tables seated.

Second, eat before you come. The food is definitely not the best, but you aren't coming for the food anyway. To note, we ordered the fried pickles and they were overly sweet, almost like they were cooked/rolled in a syrup before being fried. Not really what I want in a pickle. My husband also ordered the Mac and cheese, which was tasty, but a very small portion. 

The drinks were tasty, a little on the small side, but good. I had the watermelon crawl and it was delicious - they were out of watermelon, so they made it was pear juice. I guess I technically had a pear crawl, but still tasty! 

The music is AMZING. We stopped in on a Monday, where they were featuring the Song Suffragettes, as they do every Monday. The set consisted of 5 female singer/songwriters and each was beautiful and incredibly talented. 

As soon as our vacation ended and we got home  I started looking at past artists from the Listening Room and can now say that I have a full playlist on my Spotify account made solely of the artists they host.

The General Jackson Showboat was pretty nice. The boat goes from Opryland to Downtown Nashville. It provides plenty of great spots for pictures. They did a performance that was basically the history of country. It was a great experience to see as I was not a big country fan. The food was okay. It seemed satisfactory. The desert was great. It was an interesting twist in strawberry shortcake.

This place is pretty decent. I've been here a few times with co workers; the burgers are pretty good, the appetizers are pretty good, and the staff is always friendly. They do some pretty darn good fried pickles. It isn't mind blowing, but it's far from disappointing. I'd probably give them three stars instead of four but it's hard to find a really good burger in Nashville. 

The only discouraging thing about this place is the price of their chicken caesar salad. How a plate of lettuce with a cut up bit of chicken on it can cost more than their selection of burgers is something I'm rather curious about. $15 for a salad and an iced tea seems steep to me. However if you stick to the burgers, I suppose that isn't an issue. 

All in all it's worth a stop if you happen to be in the area.

Wow! What a remarkable journey down the Cumberland river in nashville. One thing I loved about it was being able to see on the outskirts of the city. It was a treat to see the river and the side of Nashville off road. The nighttime view of city was remarkable, very beautiful sailing underneath the pedestrian bridge. 

There's a show at the end of the night on your way back to the dock which I was very impressed with. The entertainment was amazing, it takes you all the way back to when country first began and had a great timeline that shows you best of country hits of each decade. The flow of the show was just perfect they did great, but the last 10minutes did seem to drag a little because your getting a little tired around ten.

The downside was the drinks were crazy EXPENSIVE for a single beer of a local brewery. 14.50$ Whaaaat???? There insane to ask that much for a 16oz beer. The food was average not like mamas home cooking food and service a bit slow but very pleasant. 

Ultimately if your looking for a good southern country entertainment and love country music this would be something great for you and your family to check out. Very family oriented!

I stumbled across this place after spending a few hours at Game Galaxy Arcade a few doors down with my little brother. The burgers are delicious and offer a lot of bun and topping options I haven't seen at other places. 

The cheesy goodness burger is a classic cheeseburger with three cheeses and perfectly satisfied my classic burger cravings. My fiancée got a cilantro avocado burger that was spicy and different and delicious. My brother had sliders that totally filled him up. There's also a good variety of fries and onion rings and two for one draft beer every day! On top of that, the two times I've been, I've had excellent service. This isn't the spot you'd expect to find such a good burger joint, but it's well worth the trip.

We had walked by on a Friday night and loved the music coming through the open window but we had other plans.

Saturday, after the Country Music Hall of Fame, we were looking for lunch and music.  Again, the sounds coming out of the open window drew us in.  Carlton Anderson was playing that afternoon and did a great job working the crowd and singing standards with his guitar!  Good luck in the music business.

We ordered 2 orders of Southwest eggrolls and 2 burgers with tots.  The bar mistress was attentive to our drink and food orders.  The Southwest egg rolls portions were generous and yummy.  The burgers were great and the tots were crispy & yummy.  Plus, a great food value in downtown Nashville.

Let me start by saying that I want to give 4 stars, but the inconsistency makes me give 3 stars. The last time I went, my fiance and I couldn't get well done burgers for the life of us. Granted, the owner bought a round of drinks for us for the inconvenience, but it sucks that we couldn't get a well done burger to save our lives, and they kept giving us cool, pre-cooked fries from a bowl of fries sitting on the counter. The owner had to go back back and tell them to drop fresh fries.

However this time I got a chicken sandwich and vegetables instead beef and french fries, so there was no issue with cold fries or medium well done burgers instead of well done burgers, as ordered. And I wish I could remember my servers name, but he was fantastic. I asked him to watch my plate and drink while I went to the restroom, and he and other servers literally set up a perimeter around my table. How hilariously good is that?!  I drink a lot of water, and my water glass was never empty for long. Also, if you go tried the bomb pop drink. It is fantastic and really reminds you of a bomb pop from the ice cream truck. The service today was great, but because I've had a couple of times where the service was mediocre and the food was average, I am reluctant to give it 4 or 5 stars.

If I go again and get the same service (I really wish I could remember his name) as I got today, I would not hesitate to upgrade the star rating.

If you're trying to decide between this and the country music hall of fame... This all day long. They have a great selection of memorabilia really depicting the life of Johnny and June. Additionally they have some great souvenirs if you're in the market for some Johnny Cash swag.

Everything you want to know and see about Johnny Cash is right there. Even though the place is small, it still manages to fill up so much details, photos and memorablia about the Man In Black. What I really liked were the listening booths that cover ALL eras of Cash, as well as a collage of most of his record albums and 45s! If you love Johnny Cash and are ever in Nashville, Tennessee, you don't want to miss this!

I'm a huge Johnny Cash fan so for me this was awesome! But even if you're not a huge please visit this museum. It's very informative and has lots of Johnny's personal items. There are hand written notes, some of Johnny's drawings, and clothes worn by Johnny and June Carter Cash. The video presentation is informative. I had forgotten some of his TV appearances. Be sure to visit the gift shop!!

Tip: Pasty Cline museum on the second level.

This place has some great attributes - cool decor, friendly staff, craft brew, and garage doors.  Now on to the food - started with the onion rings which were tasty but not very hot.  With the speed in which they served our skeptical nature thought food lamps were in the mix - boo on that.

Burgers were very good - opted for the pretzel bun and sweet potato fries.  Fries were a bit soggy but tasty.  The aioli dipping sauce was great!

Overall it's a good addition to the neighborhood!!

So this is definitely a great burger place to go, and one that should not be passed up. Starting from the outside, the building looks nice. Large windows, a small patio, good lighting. Once we went inside, our waiter was prompt and very friendly. The inside has a rustic, sports bar feel. A bar, a row of tall tables, no booths, only tables. 2 tvs per wall, all but one showing the hockey game. My partner and I got the sriracha hummus for starters and a drink. The drink was good potency and the appetizer was rather large. It could easily have been a meal for one, but the pita bread was very fresh and the hummus has a good mix of spicy and flavor. The burger was huge. I got the bayou bleu and my partner got the gooey cow. Reading the menu, they should like crazy burgers, but they were delicious! Perfectly cooked, excellently seasoned, the sauce was superb and matched the flavor. The meat was fresh and the sweet potato fries were freshly cooked to the point where a few were too hot from the kitchen! All in all, a great experience that everyone should go to.
Went for lunch based on yelp, it was terrible. Service took forever!! Food was blah. The only high point was the outdoor patio. Don't bother!!

We love you Dierks and your new place is really cool.  Music groups are awesome.  Unfortunately your bar tenders are horrible.  They are not well trained, service is extremely slow and it was not even that busy.  We all know money is made with serving booze.  You need more help and your folks need to be trained on how to make drinks more efficiently.

Came here for a 2nd time last night. This place is so much fun. There are people of all ages. Many people come in groups to celebrate various things, mainly bachelorettes, bachelor parties, birthdays...you get the idea. The bar is big with many tables. there is a bar with bottled beer and cocktails. There is also table service. The musicians are very talented and switch from one instrument to the other. They take requests and will definitely play your song for $20. If you are looking to get away from country music and the honky-tonks (I don't know why!), this is your venue! Go to the Big Bang for a lively experience...highly recommended.

We held a private event at the Listening Room Cafe and I feel compelled to write a superb review for their excellent and attentive service. 

When trying to find the right space in Nashville for our party, I stumbled across the Listening Room Cafe by pure chance but it was exactly the place I was looking for to host our event. The decoration is rustic interiors with brick background, wood beams and elevated ceilings. The sound system is amazing and they have a projector as well to use for tv or your own a-v hookups. There is also plenty of parking for your guests which is a HUGE plus in the downtown area considering there are parking lots at every turn and corner. The outdoor patio has a nice view of the Nashville skyline and is a great place to catch a drink on a cool evening. 

The Owner was a pleasure to work with and helped work through every little request I had. He even helped the kitchen prepare a custom menu with a authentic home recipe for our guests which came out incredible. We created a customized menu and bar menu for our guests and they were willing to accomodate all of my requests.  I especially enjoyed the local Yazoo beers on tap. I got to try a lot of the offerings on the menu and highly recommend the fried pickles, southern fried chicken, whiskey salmon, and broccoli casserole.  Our guests left the evening with an awesome and authentic Nashville experience and I even got on stage and played a song to close out the evening. 

If you are searching for a place with character, a place where you can support a local business owner with a vision and dream of the perfect singer-songwriter venue, and a place that just gushes with that local Nashville flavor then I highly recommend the listening room cafe. The sound system is awesome in here and really gives the musicians a platform to perform their trade. I look forward to coming back soon and enjoying the listening room cafe another time. Support Local!!!

Overpriced. 

It was a nice museum with a nice layout but the space was too small for the amount of people walking through. I wouldn't pay to do it again.

Great museum dedicated to the Man in Black. TONS of memorabilia, neat interactive videos, recordings, and instruments. We used our Nashville city pass to get us in, and I definitely found it interesting & insightful. Only downfall was that it was incredibly crowded, but I guess that comes with the territory of going to a touristy spot on a weekend.

Quite impressed!  From the warm greeting at the door by Justin to the suggestions and menu explanations. Food was great -the sweet potato fries, awesome! 

Don't discount this Antioch diamond in the rough...can't wait for my next visit.

We went on March 18th, there were 4 of us.  The service was absolutely horrible, we sat for 15 minutes, no one even came to our table. We flagged a waiter and he said 'we are very busy' very rudely. We proceeded to go to bar and get our own drinks. Music was starting, still no one had come by. My friend went to ask at front and she sent a nice young lady. Our food took over 45 minutes to come and it was cold. My friend and I had split a sandwich and they didn't even bring an extra plate or divide it for us. 

We missed lots of the music trying to figure out food situation...PLUS it is not like Bluebird, everyone was talking so not easy to concentrate on music.  Music was very good, but ambiance doesn't support it.  It is too large a room with too many people, I would not return.
We got there and bought a drink then the band stopped playing.  45 minutes later we finally gave up on music and left.

I love this place. I find myself continually coming back week after week just to see what's going on. The atmosphere fits the Midtown vibe and the staff is always friendly and attentive. During the week it's a great place to grab a happy hour beer and watch espn. On the weekends it's an all out dance party. The jock there, Darren B, plays some of the best tunes of every flavor in town. If you're looking for live music I hear Sundays are the best time to go. Reasonably priced drinks and fast, friendly service will have me visiting Blue Bar whenever I'm in midtown.

If your a Johnny Cash fan this is the place to go! About two months ago I came to Nashville for the first time from New Jersey and HAD to come here and I ma so happy I did! It reached my expectations completely! From the memorabilia, the records, the music the whole experience was amazing! 

In general, it's a small museum but there is so much in there! I thought I knew a lot about Johnny Cash before going in there, but when I came out I learned so much more! So many great things to look at!  More than enough to keep you busy for an hour or two. And the best part is, your allowed to take all the pictures you want!  The price was also a great bargain and was easy to find!  

My boyfriend who is not even a Johnny Cash fan had a great time and actually wound up coming out of there a fan! This is not a place to miss when visiting Nashville!

New Appreciation for Johnny Cash
