All my life I have seen Johnny Cash from time to time on television and enjoyed his performance. I cannot say I went as a country music fan because I am more rock but this museum made me appreciate Johnny Cash more than I already did.
There is so much about him and I like the way it's organized. No one rushes you. You can spend as much time as you need. There are many things about him I really just didn't know. I came out of this museum as a real fan. Johnny was an awesome person. Wish I had gone sooner

We didn't eat but we did get an amazing deal on beer right before we went to Beyonce! It is less than two miles away from Nissan Stadium so its super convenient to pre game any football game!!!! $10.50 beer buckets with six beers ALL DAY ON SUNDAY. And two-for-1 drinks (mixed, draft, bottles, and cans) all day on Sunday. You just can not beat that!!

Great cruise, show was good.  We didn't do the dinner cruise, so we relaxed on the deck and took in the views.  One thing I would say is that the Opryland Hotel didn't have good signage for getting to the boarding area.  Massive hotel with bad signage.

SO much fun!  I really enjoyed how the pianists alternated every so often - so you got a different style and personality mixed in.  They ALL were great. Interacted with the crowd, darn near played every song thrown their way. FUN bumper stickers.  Not as crowded as other places on Broadway - which was nice to be able to dance about a bit.
Great place!! Wonderful service!! Our very large group was well accommodated and we had a great experience! Thank you! We had a good time!

I have to update my review as the menus here has changed. As it says below (I left my original review which was a 5 star review from me) this place had a small but fantastic late night menus of quality wraps and sandwiches!  It was a gem in a sea of Nashville southern blah of mediocre BBQ and greasy bar food. Unfortunately, this has changed and they have succumbed to the typical Nashville late night menus... Bratwurst or Italian sausage sandwiches, grilled cheese and quesadillas. I hope that they improve this unfortunate change, although I don't have high hopes.  The beer still rotates out but I've been noticing less and less interesting brews and more typical run of the mill stuff.  


Original post:
This place is quickly becoming my new hang. Small but very solid menus. Try anything with the habanero sauce. The portobello press is awesome!  Good rotating beer selection as well. Parking across the street in the fire house lot or down the street near the atm if the lot is full for a show. 
Also the venue, if you are considering going sounds good and is quite large.   Check out a show sometime!

A perfect Broadway gem!  We ducked into this place several times because we seemed to find the only empty seats each time we peeked in. 

The food was fast, fresh, and piping hot.  We didn't order anything elaborate, but it was yummy every time.

The entertainment was spot on and the guys playing were a good time as well as accomplished, polished performers.  Each staff member we encountered each day was friendly, welcoming and accommodating.  One day while we were sitting the bartender passed out bottle cozies, which I thought was a nice, hospitable touch.

Thanks for the many good times--we loved it!

A must-do for any fan of the Man in Black. Seeing the relics of his life and work, both musical and religious, was awe-inspiring. Don't miss this if you're in Nashville! (One star off only because it's rather small.)

Great music and awesome atmosphere. Your bathroom arrangements are the absolute worst I've ever seen. When your customers have to wait in a line for over thirty minutes to use the restroom it's a huge issue. People left your bar and didn't come back because of your lack of restrooms. Ultimately, it's asinine to lose money over some renovations that must be done.

I thought this was a great venue.  All the musicians were talented, very impressed with them moving from piano to guitar to drums.  I thought the drinks were good, and reasonably priced.  Thoroughly enjoyed this visit.

Was so excited to come and try this restaurant, as the grass fed beef is such a great seller. As I walked in it seemed there were only two servers for the full restaurant, so as you can imagine, the service lacked in parts. Im sure if they had one more server to help, I wouldn't have to say that, though.  I ordered the Cilantro avocado burger and was less than impressed. For the pricing they have, as well as the crowd, I was disappointed. Food took almost 40 minutes to come out and I was on my lunch break, so had to eat it out of a to go box. Might try it a 2nd time, who knows. Hopefully the next experience will be better.
Great intimate setting to hear REAL music in Nashville. It was amazing! Minus one star because the food was just OK

Had high expectations for this place since it is so well known! Came in on a Saturday morning around 11:15. It was pretty quiet, though the space is pretty large. Ordered brunch and some drinks. Drinks were good, brunch was a let down. French toast was mediocre. I got scrambled eggs, potatoes, and bacon, and was really disappointed. They first forgot my meal, then when it came the eggs were cold and just tasted flat out bad. The potatoes were a bit hard and under-cooked. Friends of mine ordered the 2 for 1 mimosa deal they had - each getting one. When the bill came they charged them both full price mimosas and then said they couldn't split the deal between seats - something they should've explained before. Luckily they fixed it, but it was a bit off-putting. The only plus was that there was live music. I would say maybe come in for drinks or a snack to check out the place and hear some music, but pass on the Brunch.

We both had a lot of fun here.  The food was fine, and the drinks were well priced.  We were there on a Sunday night and it wasn't busy, but the live music was incredible (Carlton Anderson (sp?)). Jalapeno burger was fine, and the philly cheesesteak was actually pretty good.  We both enjoyed our time here and LOVED the live music-- it really gives you the Nashville feel.

Like the other reviewer mentioned, this place used to be a neighborhood favorite for us. Great sandwiches, casual bar, nice outdoor deck, great beer selection. But to wait a month of brats/dogs for the "new menu", which is basically eggs all day (Brunch menu) and less-than-inspired bar food for the "late night menu" is a sad state of affairs indeed. I was ready to make this our Sunday NFL headquarters until this turn of events. I get there are some people who don't get out of bed to eat until after Noon, but seriously - egg burritos until 3pm Sat & Sun?! I had eggs at 7AM, thanks. I'm good. Fix me up that delightful Cuban pork sandwich and we're friends for life. Until then.......farewell my friend.

Pretty decent place! You can make a lot of requests for songs, so it's a good place to hear a variety of music played on piano. The musicians were pretty awesome! I didn't like that there was a cover (even though it wa only 6 dollars), and there wasn't very much seating. The upper seating area was entirely reserved. But it was a pretty fun place and we enjoyed our time here

I had a GREAT time here!  I am not a giant fan of country music but it was so fun to sit and listen to amazing talent perform their songs.  i was thoroughly entertained the entire show.

i did eat before I came because i heard the food wasnt the best.  I did order the fancy lemonade which was awesome and the fried pickles but I didnt love those as much mainly because they had a little too much kick for my palette.

Im not sure I would recommend coming for food but I 100% recommend coming for live music, definitely worth the price of admission :)

We loved this place!
I'll admit I was a bit hesitant because of comments about it only being 2 rooms of stuff. Yes, it is a smaller location than it obviously used to be, but it is a LOT of stuff crammed into the small space.
I dare say it's not enough space. But, it's obvious watching The Hurt video that it used to be in a larger space.

If you're into music at all it's a great museum. If you're into Johnny Cash, it's a must-see!!

Been going to the Bang since they opened the first one in St. Louis. After only a half hour or so, the impression one gets is that these musicians know most every song composed from the past two centuries.  Their competence while doing the standard piano bar setup and moving to the small band format is entertaining to watch. They are all wonderful singers to boot. They work very hard to try and get to every request made each night and their patter between tunes is quite funny. 
The food is quite good. The Rock 'n Roll Salad is a favorite of mine along with the pulled pork sandwich.  Being a non-drinker, I'm not one to pass judgment on the beers and what seems to be a well stocked selection of mixed drinks. I know Coca Cola owns Middle Tennessee, but a cold Pepsi would better suit my taste. 
The concept of the piano bar is not new and, nationally, there are other brands out there. However, I find The Big Bang Bar to be one of the good ones whose staff really does take care that a good time is had by all.

I wasn't a massive country music fan, but I always did like Johnny Cash when I heard his music.  Given that I was in Nashville, walked by the museum several times, and saw ads for it everywhere, I decided to be a tourist and check it out.  The museum has a cafe and gift shop in front.  The gift shop is overpriced however the gear is unique and cool, which makes it somewhat worth it (I grabbed a tank top).  Museum admission is similiarly pricey at $16--especially given the total size of all exhibits--however as even a casual fan I found it worth it.

While the space is limited, it's packed with worthwhile exhibits and content.  From the recordings strewn through the space, the chair from the "Hurt" music video, dozens of costumes and a butt-load of history, there is plenty to engage with.  And what's there is worth engaging with.  Johnny Cash had a fascinating life which, while not always rosy, was very well lived.  The care put into this tiny museum shows and can easily be appreciated.  You can zip through the place in 15 minutes if you wish, but instead you'll probably find yourself spending closer to an hour.

I find myself listening to Johnny Cash a lot more nowadays.  Unless you're diehard against country (and if you are, why are you in Nashville), given this a visit if you're in town.

I needed to go to the potty. No line in the men's so I went with it. Literally got chased out by an employee (a tiny little "man")  for using a restroom with no line. He pounded on the door. Not because there was a line, but because he could. I'd avoid this place when there are several other places to go where you will be treated more kindly.

This place gets no stars.Here's what to expect from Swingin Doors Saloon In the ladies room,  a prison toilet that was backed up and overflowing onto the floor by 10pm. Drinks in plastic cups- that's just lazy ownership, why not spring for real glassware and a dishwasher. I felt like I was at frat house- with a prison toilet. In fact I've been in cleaner frat houses.
Not to mention the crap bartenders;  the "Manager" was a little doogie houser. Ordered a shot asked him to make something in Preds colors and he tried but I had to tell him what to put in it and tell him what curaçao was nasty! tasted like bad watery kool-aid. Seriously and this was the manager-Dalton. Kelly was our 1st bartender, she was just pissy, no smile, no nothing. Then there was Kara (or Cara), again pissy. I left a note on my cc slip attempting a cordial suggestion and she immediately turned around and asked what was wrong with the service received. Should not even have to ask, really. I have no problem with confrontation and would gladly have spoken with her about her attitude, but she would never actually hear me, nor would the boss (HA!) doogie. I came in from the porch and she took a bottle I had on the bar saving my seat, held it up and looked at my friend and said in a really witchy tone, "Is it okay to take this bottle now", tipped it over and poured the swallow of beer on the floor. On the floor! I guess I should thank my lucky stars she didn't throw it at me! I have held almost every position in the restaurant business, so I probably have high standards, but I would not send my worst enemy to this place. There are so many choices downtown that do not give Nashville a black eye as does this hell hole, it really is not fit for humans- or animals. Dear everyone who lives in or visits our lovely city, DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE. NEXT!

I came here for brunch last week.  The entertainment was amazing and was the best part of the restaurant.  The artists were very talented, we loved listening to them sing.

The food is pretty basic and pricey.  I had their award winning turkey sandwich which I did not think was super special.  And my friend had the crabcake hash which she seemed to enjoy, but didn't eat much of it.  They did have 2 for the price of 1 mimosas which was a definite plus!!  All in all, I'd go back for the music but not the food!

360 burger has great burger selections. Had the LeBron burger it was delicious! Nick was a great server. He was prompt and ready for questions. Plus it was game night so I had a chance to use my Taboo skills.

I'm a huge Johnny Cash fan and this stop was definitely one of the highlights of my Southeast road trip this fall! Despite its relative small size and somewhat hard to find location "off the beaten path" my friend and I had an excellent time! Regardless if you're a diehard Cash fan like me or just a casual fan, you'll enjoy yourself here - that I can promise you!

The small size of the museum is actually a positive I think. Sure it's no Graceland but going here will not take up your whole day! The artifacts on display are carefully chosen and represent some of the best of the collection! The video room has some of Johnny's classic TV clips running every 10 minutes or so - very nice to see! The American flag tribute/display was also a highlight!

If I'm not mistaken this museum is relatively new so I'm sure it'll only get better with age! The gift shop was amazing as well - so many cool and interesting souvenirs! Good thing I visited near closing time - I could of spent all day and emptied my wallet at that wonderful "little" gift shop! :-)

All in all if you're looking for something new and different to do in Nashville and are at least vaguely familiar with Johnny Cash's music - you'll have a great time here! Well worth the price of admission! Happy rockin' y'all! :-)

This place was amazing. If you love Johnny Cash you will enjoy this place. We had so much fun and enjoyed glimpsing into his life and things and learning new facts about him. The pictures at the end where so fun and cute enough to put up in the house. I would go back again.

Well we have lived in the nashville area for a lot of years, finally got to try the General Jackson show bout for the first time. We really enjoyed the bout. And getting to walk around the bout and the captains station. The ride down the river was very pretty but a little cold. The staff was great and very friendly and accommodating. The food was not that good but would try it again to see how it will turn out. The entertainment was very good we really enjoyed it. They performed very well!  It was a very good evening.
Very neat to see the history of his life through time:  well put together museum.  I would make this a must see while visiting Nashville.
We ate at the 360 Burger in Antioch. This place was awesome. I liked the friendly staff and the cool burger on a pretzel bun.

The band is the only thing I enjoyed at this place. The place smelled of smoke. The bathroom was gross and we stopped a drunk leaving the bar that was wanting to drive home. Went to get assistance from bartender for cab for him and was surprised by their lack of help in detaining this guy or getting him a ride. Can't they be held liable if something were to happen?

This place is a must for any Johnny Cash fan. I picked up a magnet sun records for our fridge. Lots of great history and things owned my the man in black and June. Well worth the price of admission. Gift shop was nice but a little spendy.

We started off having a great night until the bouncer kicked us out without a reason.  We were there with all of my aunts and uncles and just settled a $400+ tab.  I asked for the manager and he was this dopey geeky little guy that didn't care.  We let them know we also had civil servants with us and he was completely ignorant.  There are so many bars on the strip that do not have this $6/person cover.  Save your time/$6 and dignity and find yourself a real Nashville country bar.

I like the Listening Room; however, WATCH THE WAIT STAFF!  I went there yesterday for lunch.  My bill was $40.42, I gave the waitress a $6.00 Tip (which was fair).  I get home and logged in to see my charges for the day and was horrified .... The waitress gave herself $2.00 more.  My card was charged $48.62!  CRIMINAL!  For this reason, I will NEVER eat here again!
Awesome place to hear new music, and the food is great. Song Suffragette shows on Mondays are really cool.

Great place to see higher quality music in nashville. Music started at 7pm on Friday with three singer songwriters. One had a big hit song for rascal flatts so this was real talent. Good sound quality. It is a full restaurant with small tables surrounding the stage.  The food is decent.  I suggest the fried pickles.  They have a nice selection of sandwhiches and a few entrees. The greenbeans that i had on the side were exceptional. Sangria was awesome but the music was awesome!  Second band had so much energy and had a maroon 5 vibe. This is a great place if you want great music, solid food, and an actual table while you listen.

Loved the atmosphere and the musicians. So nice to see how people migrate to this town for their love of singing and songwriting. Fun place for an evening in Nashville and less touristic than many other places in town

First, I'm sorry to be so negative, I am not inclined to be nasty but we are here now with a group of nine and this place is an absolute joke. The music is fine but the service is worse than a third world country, honestly. We waited an hour and a half for French fries and they refused to make cocktails that we ordered and offered bus light instead with no apology. We made a reservation for dinner weeks ago and have been treated so poorly. They eventually explained that they were short staffed but no one attempted to make the situation right. This is my first time in Nashville and I am appalled. I would give negative stars if I could.

This place is not my scene but the bar itself is a pretty innovative and cool idea. I will give them 4 stars for coming up with a new fresh cool idea. I would recommend trying the place out to see if its your scene, this place is a lot different than a lot of other bars in Nashville and across the US.

Been once on a Friday for lunch.  I had the PB&J burger and it was outstanding.   My bf had the pimento cheese burger, and he loved it.  So glad to have a place like this in HH.  We can only hope to get more places like this in the area.  HH definitely needs it to continue the revitalization of the neighborhood.  We'll definitely be back soon!

This was a great place to hear some up and coming artists, grab an inexpensive drink, and hang out! The food options looked tempting but we had already eaten, so I can't speak to that. Our experience was positive, though!

Interesting menu.  Not at all what i expected.

Visited mid afternoon on a Saturday. Good crowd, but not packed out.  Even so, it took a good 15 minutes for server to take our order and then another 20 minutes or so to get it to the table.

Our server was pleasant, but obviously overextended.  Looking around, i think she was the only one working.

I might try one more time, but if experuence is not better, this one goes off my list.

I love Johnny Cash. But this museum was only so-so. Maybe it was the hangover I was feeling but I wasn't overly impressed. The place is small, they could definitely branch out or up if they were able to. That made it very crowded and hard to see things. Our ticket was $20. A lot, I felt like, for such a small place. The gift shop was also expensive. I understand that the area and rent or mortgage is probably expensive but you'd think the Cash family could afford to make it bigger and lower the prices a bit. The cafe that's inside also doesn't really go with the whole vibe of the place. Make it a restaurant or a bar, and it'd be much better! We'd go again, but it wouldn't be on the top of my to-do list while I'm in Nashville.

We went last weekend during Mardi Gras Y'all. It wasn't very busy at all because we went late in the afternoon. The service was good, the music was great, and the food was amazing! -As to my knowledge there is no children's menu, but you can get a side of mac and cheese for $3.

Awesome venue for live music. Big enough to fit a good size crowd but small enough that it still feels intimate.  Also I was very pleased that there was a vegan option on their food menu on the pub side.

It was very interesting to see different parts of Johnny Cash's life in the museum. There is a lot to see, hear, and experience. The only downside is that the museum itself was jam packed with people so I couldn't take my time reading everything, and it was pretty pricey to go in to the museum itself.

Was enjoying a long weekend in Nashville.... until we came here! Rude staff, especially the bouncer(gave me a real hassle). My drink was decent at best, the only thing they've got going for them is the name and the music. Otherwise I would not waste your money here. Don't even get me started on the rats!

Dierks did a great job with this new bar on Broadway. The menu is a little different than most of the places in the District. We had the wings, which were nice and crispy and the sauce was on the side. The sauce was hot but had a little sweet taste. Very good. We also had meatball and hot chicken sliders. Both were very good. I liked the idea that you could order the sliders as single sandwiches. 
We visited Whiskey Row 2 days, Wednesday and Thursday and both days were very busy. But we were fortunate enough to get the same server both days. Michelle was great. Very pleasant and attentive. 
We are in Nashville all the time and plan to frequent Whiskey Row quite a bit.

A must visit when coming to Nashville and for anyone who appreciates American music and its history. They have an amazing collection of memorabilia. The stories associated with Cash's personal items were very interesting. A++

Food was horrible, entertainment was like a bad cruise ship performance. This was a Thanksgiving dinner cruise and the meal was not what I consider traditional Thanksgiving. The servers did do a pretty good job.

The Johnny Cash museum is everything a Cash fan could ask for. The exhibits covers 100 percent of his life and give an in depth look into the Man in Black. The items on display give such an intimate look that you couldn't find anywhere else. I am in debt to the Miller's for bringing this museum to fruition giving me something that I could appreciate this much.

If you are a Johnny Cash fan this is a must do on your bucket list!

Terrible management. 2 times trying to come in we have been treated very poorly. One time we tried coming in at 11pm because the door was still open and the nba finals were on and they very rudely told us they were closed from the table they were all sitting at chatting. From my experience working you are not closed until you lock the door and if you are you apologize not rudely reject people. Then the next time the manager and girl at the front door were not friendly at all! We didn't realize we needed tickets because the sign was posted on the front door who I was covered by people waiting in line so we waited in line for a long time in the wrong line. And they made it seem like it was our fault. After that I suggested they post the notice about the lines elsewhere where it could be seen and the girl completely ignored me and did not apologize. Also someone in our party asked if they could use the bathroom because we were at the front of the line (the wrong one before they sent us to stand in the correct line) and they refused even when she offered to leave her cell phone at the front desk. This was just terrible service. There are so many places to go in Nashville stay away from this one! You will be much happier! Take it from us! The only good thing is the singer's are very talented
Great atmosphere! Good people! Friendly staff! Amazing talent on piano, drums, and vocals!

Yup. They got BEEF, and some good one at that! Now it is located in a dead-beat strip mall but that means PLENTY of parking for us burger freaks! When u walk in its got this whole Western motif goin on with the rustic wooden walls n furniture and bar and all. I have NO idea why its called 360. Our server was very efficient and helped me decide on the mushroom Swiss and my cousin on the avocado one. The fries were very unimpressive but thier bun was ON POINT and once u get all up in that beef patty, u know that cow was alive a few hours ago. It's fresh all right! I liked my burger though my cuzzo was a tad bit unmoved by the entire dining experience. He says M.L Rose is better, but I think 360 got it going on, even more so than M.L Rose AND Burger up. No fancy gimmicks like stupid truffle fries. Just got ole fashioned American Cheeseburgers!

You don't have to be a Johnny Cash fan to truly enjoy this museum. There is a lot of history here and it was actually more informative than I expected. We came early in the afternoon and while we were finishing our visit, we noticed that it got very crowded, so I would definitely recommend coming as early as possible. Overall this was time and money well spent.

Had a blast here when I visited in march!  Honestly we just chose this bar cuz it was freezing rain outside and since we were a bachelorette party we cut the line and got in asap.  But this bar was such a blast!  My friends crushed a couple rounds of pickle back shots and loved them.  I had a couple peach moonshine shots and I wish I had a bottle of that stuff.  Staff was attentive and forgiving of the intoxicated crowd.  Bathroom was disgusting (wet, sticky, and no TP, and only one stall.)  But that was all forgotten by the amazing live  band that rocked the house and got everybody dancing.  The main singer had an amazing voice & vocal range, and did a great variety of music (loved hearing some alt rock in nash!  Sorry not sorry I'm not a country music fan.)  Honestly she even made a country music song feel good.  The crowd ranged from a young lad out for his 21st bday to grandparents and everything in between.  A very comfortable environment.  The sort of place you'd be comfortable checking out solo or with a group.  Yes it was crowded but when I pictured partying in Nash this was the the scene I imagined.  There isnt much great live music in my home town and I really enjoyed my night at swinging doors.

Great live music addition to the east side. I went in back to back evenings this spring and saw a fantastic Prince tribute on a Friday and an amazing Allman Brothers cover band on a Saturday. The crowds were light, presumably because it was Bonnaroo weekend, but the space has nice high ceilings and seems like it could handle crowds nicely. Awesome selection of beers on tap and the bartenders were knowledgable and friendly.

Person answering the phone taking orders was rude. French fries was over cooked and the burger was not all that. I had to wait for my food and it wasn't fresh. I don't know if the place has changed owners but there food used to be really good. I don't know what happen.

This place was awesome! I love Johnny Cash but I love him now even more after having learned somethings about him I didnt know before.  Like how much of a humanitarian, activist and renaissance man he was all in all.  I enjoyed alot of the personal mementos of his, notes, the ad he took out on billboard asking why the radio programmers were not playing the ballad of Ira Hayes, the family crest he drew himself, I mean really this place is super cool.    The museum shop was ok but you know they even have original pressing vinyl of the man black himself, so if you are a collector well you can yours there!....for about $250...

I love museums.  Im a fan of country music so of course when I heard there was a Johnny Cash museum I had to check it out.  The museum is small but it was well worth it.  You can listen to some of his music and check out the memorabilia they have on display.  There is a lot to know about Johnny Cash and this is the place to check it out.

Great place for brunch on Sunday's! Super relaxed, great music, great service. We will definitely be back. Food was delicious, the portobello mushrooms were amazing, along with the mimosas. Mallory and Alex were great, very attentive and personable.
The wax figures will definitely amaze you. They are so detailed, you would think they were actually real human beings. Trust me, it's fascinating. A must see.

Decent place, crowded on the weekend. Go there on an off night though and the locals can be super rude. As a traveler, I always try to fit into the local culture and get to know the regulars, but my sister and I were insulted from the minute we walked in. Bartender thought it was funny. Not a way to welcome tourists spending our money in their bar.

I can't say if it's always as good of an experience as we had, but we had the best time! I wasn't sure what cocktail to order so they helped me come up with something special to order for me. I had the cheeseburger & fries which were very tasty. But nothing compares to the experience. Baylor Wilson & friends were performing when we went and they were AMAZING. Loved our time here. So amazing. The talent was unbelievable
Fantastic catfish and chicken tenders.   The only place to eat in Nashville.  Hush puppies are amazing

I'm really really bummed. I went to call and place an order for my favorite salmon burger on a pretzel buns with waffle fries and was going to get some honey wings too, after a killer workout. The guy on the phone informed me that they've changed their entire menu and I'd have to go look online to find it. My fiancé was leaving from a meeting and was going to just stop in and pick it up for me as a treat...but I couldn't find one single thing either familiar or delicious sounding. Not one appealing thing. It all sounds like really greasy and gross. I didn't see much of an appetizer choice, and they got rid of the wings..in lieu of their wings you can get breaded boneless ones but I'm not about that. I am soo sad and disappointed. Adding new items is great but why do a complete menu overhaul? Everything was so good.

My friend discovered this place when I came to town for a visit so we could get some traditional Nashville music/performances in, woo-hoo!

To start, it really sucks. You are outside, in-line and it was cooooold that day. Not fun and the reason I am giving 4 stars instead of 5. You then have to stare inside where people are eating and drinking and are warm and will them to leave. 

Once inside the venue was great! We didn't eat here but the drinks were boozy and creative. I really liked the options. Service was fair, but I did just go up and get my own drinks a few times. 

The band, Amber's Drive, was excellent! Great group of 3 guys but one of them had the most impressive voice and I think he should do 90% of the singing! We had great seats and bought the band's CD afterwards. 

If you are looking for something fun to do in a nice place with decent drinks check it out!
My friend purchased the tickets, but they were not costly, I think around ten bucks or so, a great deal, too!

Just be careful if it's cold outside cause you'll be waiting.

If I could give no stars for this place, I would. I was part of a group who made reservations to come in on a Sunday morning for brunch, and the service, food, attitude were all below acceptable standards. I was one of the first people there and placed my order for the brunch buffet and bottomless mimosas. Thanks to APPALLING service, I got two tiny drinks. When I tried to flag our waitress down, I got a surprisingly snarky response. I'm not used to being talked to like I'm an 8 year old, especially when I'm paying for the pleasure. 

The restaurant ran out of food for the breakfast buffet, so many members of our group were waiting on their food or unable to get basic menu items. My mind was blown by how poor an experience it was. The person who made our reservation complained about the shortcomings, and apparently got blown off. No love for this place. I've seen better service at IHOP.

I was really looking forward to this museum. It was crowded and much smaller than I thought it would be. It's well done, but really small. Does a good job of telling his story and giving examples and historical items. I was just let down because I wanted more.

GO HERE. If I came back to Nashville and could only do one thing, I would come back here. 

Ticket: Getting tickets was a breeze, ordered online, showed up early as recommended and was seated at a table for 2 front and center of the stage.

The Entertainment: The three girls who sang the night where there were incredible. I couldn't even speak I was in such awe of their talent. They were Carole King Jrs. in the making - amazing voices and song writers. 

Dining: I was very pleasantly surprised! Sick of BBQ and Fried Chicken, I took a chance on the mushroom sandwich and it was FANTASTIC. On top of that - the had Harpoon Ciders. We were very excited to get our hands on some Boston brews while on vacation!

Worth a visit if you've ever been a fan of the namesake or if you enjoy a museum that mixes history lessons, music, and memorabilia.

Self-guided and it doesn't take one very long to move through the place.  Be patient, due to its size and the amount of other patrons, you may feel a bit tight from time to time.  

There were some really interesting facts and a ton of costumes/outfits on display.   The area regarding his lake house was a "ha, I didn't know that" moment, while the final area which centered around his recording of "Hurt" and the video was very touching and lasting.

Good gift shop upon exiting, if only I could wear retail souvenir shop sized shirts, I would have purchased more than one!

This food experience was very disappointing. I was looking forward to eating here, but my expectations were shot.  We ordered wings for an appetizer with bbq sauce and half honey hot. I specifically told the waitress that I wanted my wings to come out before my entree.  I didn't get my wings until after I was done with my meal!  It looked as if they poured a whole jar of bbq sauce on wings.  You only saw sauce, no wings.  I ordered a cheeseburger and onion rings.  The burger was bland.  I was expecting a well seasoned, well cooked, juicy burger, but I received a dry and flavorless burger.  I was disappointed with my food.  The onion rings were ok.  For the price, I expected more.   I would not recommend this place.

We went for a brunch cruise and the food was terrible.  Very disappointing.  The eggs were weird, waffles hard as rocks, the chicken was cold and tasteless, we paid good money and when the cruise was over we had to go out to eat because we could did not enjoy the food on the boat.  The performers were very energetic and had great voices but sorry very cheesy.  The big fake smiles were hilarious but I noticed many of the older people really enjoyed it.  One lady was so emotional she cried.  

The boat seemed older but it was nice, we were able to walk around and it was nice being on the water.  I would not suggest the brunch honestly, not sure if the dinner option has better food and maybe a younger crowd.

My boyfriend and I spent a few nights in Nashville and booked a dinner cruise on the General Jackson Showboat at the suggestion of our concierge.  This was a waste of a perfectly good vacation evening.  I cannot speak to the views as we took the boat in the late fall and it was dark the entire time (and there was not much of a view until we pulled into Nashville), but what I can say, is that this is best avoided unless you seriously don't have anything else to do with your time.  First, our waiter was inattentive, hard to track down and generally seemed like he resented having to wait on us at all.  Perhaps our much much older table-mates had a better experience with him, but ours was dismal.  It was impossible to even get a re-fill on our drinks over the course of hours.  Second, the food was abysmal.  Dinner was Prime Rib, period.  There were no options.  And this was not good prime rib, it was the cheap, salty, grey, gristly nastiness that you might expect to find on the buffet line of a rundown strip club in old Las Vegas.  No thanks.  Even the dessert was inedible.  Believe me, I have a sweet tooth, so would generally be inclined to eat my dessert.   If you cannot make something that I can stomach more than one bite of, you are definitely doing it wrong.  I think it was supposed to be strawberry shortcake, but no other strawberry shortcake I have ever had featured overly sweet strawberry jam-type goo over a tasteless hard puck of a biscuit.  Disgusting.  Finally, the show was energetic and had a decent premise - an overview of the music of Tennessee (Appalachia, Nashville and Memphis).  The performers were good and it is due to their efforts that this receives more than one star from me.  The execution of the show however was cheesy and there was a definite undercurrent of Southern Republican ethos to it that I could see making some people uncomfortable.  

I would not do this again.  If you do book this through a hotel, be advised that your shuttle driver will have your tickets (they will not be held at will call like you might suspect).  This is relevant if you miss your shuttle (like some other people we ran into did) or opt to drive your rental car to the boarding location (like we did), which will require you to find out which shuttle was meant to be yours and hope you can catch it when it arrives so that you can get your tickets.

Ended up here on a recommendation from our lyft driver. I really liked it. The crowd is definitely hipster and younger than I am. And at first that bothered me, but as it started filling up, more people like me arrived. We saw four bands for an incredibly low price. I cannot believe how inexpensive live entertainment is here. The only drawback to me was that there weren't many places to sit. None of the acts we saw were country. Which was a good thing for me. I like country, but after all of the honky tonks,I'm good for a while.

Management needs to take a step back and evaluate their staffing for heavy traffic weekends.  One bartender to tend to not only the bar, but an entire floor of customers is unacceptable!  People from all over the country come to Nashville to experience country music and the down home country food.  If you're looking for either, skip this bar.  Spend two hours waiting for that table at the hot spot restaurant on your 'Must See List.'  It's worth more of your time waiting at a bar that's well staffed with better food.  This is my first ever yelp, and I hope that this helps better your Nashville experience!

Mark the bartender is awesome!!! Having a girls night and got hit on by a creepy stalker type and he looked out for us all night!!!!! Once at our table all the gals kept checking in. Totally recommend for great music, great food and drinks and an amazing staff!!!!

This was a huge disappointment. It took almost 2 hours to get breakfast. The server never came to fill coffees. The food was cold and bad. The server complained of being hungover after a rough night on the town. He tried overcharging us and then didn't want to do anything about it. "I guess i can ask the manager if you want". Of course since we were in a party of 6, gratuity was put on the bill so I guess the server didn't really feel it was necessary to offer any service. He never asked how our meal was. It took 30 minutes just to get our checks and pay. Terrible way to start a day. Do not go to this establishment. And if you do, pray your server is not Charles because he is rude and unhelpful.

Dinned here for Brunch this past Sunday and have mixed feelings. The atmosphere is great if you are in the mood to listen to live music. The food is PHENOMENAL - truly, everyone enjoyed their meal. The service, however, was less than to par. Our mimosas were forgotten and you could tell they had our server running all over the place (not sure if they were understaffed or under trained). I will definitely give this place another try in hopes of better service!

Amazing! This museum was in our plans for our 12 day vacation, it was over the top. My favorite part of our vacation and I would definitely return. It's a MUST SEE!!! Good for children (mine were 9/12), younger might not understand it or be able to slowly take in all of the information. My parents loved it as well, mom was crying when we left.
Puts you there w Johnny, in his life. Not only has tons of artifacts, but pictures, movie scripts and letters and songs....pay stubs and interactive devises. 
The gift shop has so many options and items that I struggled to just buy a few items. I love Johnny Cash, love his music and his story.

Music was great. Drinks were delicious. (Which should be rated a 5!!)

I would highly recommend eating before hand. Our food took over and hour and all five meals were cold when they were finally served. Also, one meal came out five minutes after the rest (and it was STILL cold!!). The food was a major let down.

If I could give this place a "0" I would. We were celebrating a 21st birthday here, paid $12 for a shot, and got screamed at by the bartender. To be fair, a shot was bought for the birthday girl and she had not seen her ID yet--that was our fault..but we did inform the bartender she turned 21 yesterday while we were waiting for her to find her ID. The bartender did proceed while this was happening, however, to say "I don't give a shit" and proceeded to tell us how she had "3 college degrees." Then told us she was the manager (blonde, short hair). When I tried to calmly talk to her, she told me not to speak to her like a child. This did not have a to be as big of an issue as it was. It was blown way out of proportion. She yelled at us because some of us were drinking water and sitting at the bar (there was NO ONE in the bar). I have worked in food service before and this customer service is awful--if you serve alcohol you should not be someone that INSTIGATES bar fights. On a positive note, the live music was wonderful! I believe he said his name was Isaac Matthews. By the way, I have 3 college degrees...and don't work at a bar. Do not waste your money here and don't you dare try to get hydrated here!!!!

I visited the museum with my younger sister and we had a blast! We took tons of pictures, and enjoyed an hour of learning about great artist from different genres and eras.   $25 can be pricey so I would recommend looking for different coupons, and maybe asking for a buy one get one free price! Definitely a good pit stop if your in Nashville doing tourist things!

As someone who does NOT listen to country music this was quite the experience for me. My friends dragged me here (against my will) for dinner and a show. The food was pretty good and the music was great! 

I don't remember the name of the guy who was performing but he played a bunch of different songs. They were all different and there were even 1 or 2 songs that I would have happily listened to on my own!

I highly recommend this place if you're visiting Nashville!

I've been here twice on separate occasions. I love the music, dueling pianos but I don't like that after I checked my bank account they have charged me for 3 separate checks only 1 which is mine. Jason/Jamie contacted me within a few hours after I posted about my situation and took care of everything which is nice to know they care about their customers. Angry orchard draft is &6. Delicious. 
Get here early if you want a good seat though we got lucky and got seats after people left. Just became a matron of honor and hope to bring my bachelorette here next summer before her fall wedding. Which I saw this place is great for bachelorette parties. 
6 dollar cover on Saturday and free Friday.

From the moment I walked in, I felt at home. There is much more I could write, but come on in and ask for the Chef..you'll be able to see by the smile on my face. Makes work a bit easier when it's always a killer show, amazing staff, and pitch-perfect sound.

Had to wait in line for about 20 mins...brrr!Standing only...no tables!!  Drinks were reasonably priced. But enjoyed all the bands that perform. Larkin & Poe rocked it out!!  Wishful thinking...but it would be great if they had some kind of heat for the deck.

We got two burgers and some queso con carne with pita chips. The burgers tasted completely off, like something was wrong with it. The meat seemed old and we could not even risk eating it. The queso had literally two pieces of ground beef and came with tortilla chips (far from the description of the item on the menu). It was a waste of $30 and we got it to go so we were out a whole nights meal. NEVER. AGAIN.
This was a great place to visit while in Nashville. Everything you want to know about the man in black is right here in this small little museum. Definitely a must see!

Dinner = unacceptable (bland chicken, basic roasted potatoes, sludge -- I mean creamed spinach -- from the bottom of the Cumberland River)
Dessert = caramel cheesecake that was decent but NWTC (not worth the calories) 
Drinks = strong 
Service = weak
Show = cheesy
Decor = what century are we in? 

My biggest complaint is that they didn't have dinner options or even a menu to pick from.

Save your $90 a plate and go to a nice restaurant where you can CHOOSE your food. There are plenty in Nashville.

Are you sure you want to risk having beer spilled on you? How is it possible that a place like this would hire people that can't hold on to their drink trays? As the show ended this klutz dumped at least two beers and a couple of glasses of water all over me and table and floor. This guy was so clumsy that after the first dump he proceeded to knock over a bottle of root beer on the table!  I wondered if somehow I had pissed him off somehow and this was his  revenge! But we don't even live here. So management, I hope you will reevaluate who you hire, because you were lucky it was me and not someone that is lawsuit happy. And if you like to hear the lyrics, forget it. It was so loud and acoustically deficient, making the performances less appealing.

I honestly do not know what to tell you. After months of waiting for the right time to try this place out and the expectancy of a great grass fed burger I'm left speechless. From the moment  me and my two children stepped foot in the restaurant I could sense this place was starting to disappoint. There were no host or hostess at the podium, there was a awful band playing extremely loud music in the far left hand corner and to top it off the dining area was poorly illuminated. This place reeked of disaster. I approached the bar and asked, "can we be seated" and we were guided to a table that had the light flickering on and off intermittently. So as we sat there for nearly 12 minutes I prepped the kids and stated that in three more minutes we are leaving if we do not get our drinks. At long last, on the fourteenth minute we had a waiter. They must have had two waiters for about 30 people. I couldn't believe it. Our burger experience just kept growing worse. We received our appetizer promptly after all it was just queso and chips. Our main grub now that's another story. The only upside is this, they did make good on the 50% off appetizer that is offered through Yelp and because of the extra long wait for our burgers they did give us a free appetizer. But that's where it ends because I have never in my life tasted a burger without texture and mushy before in my life. Ugh just thinking about it now just... I don't know if they can be called burgers or not it reminds me more of a patty made from soggy bread totally disgusting. Oh, and by the way if you show your Yelp coupon be prepared to be  stalked, followed and repeatedly asked ,"how is everything?" All in a vain attempt to win you over. All I wanted was a good, no great burger!

Only wish we had found this place earlier!! Our goal was to just stop in for one drink at the different bars on Broadway but when we found this place we spent our whole evening there. Great music, great staff. Everyone from the door guy to the bartenders are musically inclined. Get there early for a good seat!!

Always a good time. Live dueling pianos - Music is 80's to present. Standing room only on weekends so arrive early if you want a table. Avoid getting into the piano playing tip wars (e.g. Rocky Top vs Sweet Home Alabama).

The service was really slow. Food was fairly decent but nothing to rave about. I had higher expectations considering the Swetts pedigree. Pharmacy Burger & M.L. Rose are better options for affordable gourmet burgers.

Dueling pianos excellent, all 8 or 10 of them. Worth every tip they get.  Its Nashville for Gods sake what's not to love about the place, its talent, restaurants, hospitality.  I truly hate to give a 'negative' but here goes. The wait staff......ok that's about it. Not too friendly, I'll leave it at that.  I visit at least 3 times a year and hope to continue doing so. Well worth a try when on Broadway St.

This place was the highlight of my Nashville trip. This place totally encompasses everything Nashville is about. The music was amazing, beautiful, and so entertaining. I thoroughly enjoyed my time here and if I lived in Nashville I would come here every weekend. I will say the food is nothing special. I wouldn't come here to eat. I would get a few drinks and maybe an appetizer because the food wasn't all that good. I got the Hot Chicken and it didn't taste anything like Tennessee Hot Chicken. It wasn't spicy at all. My boyfriend had the Pork Steak and he thought it was good but not worth the money. Also, all of our food came out cold except our Fried Pickles appetizer. (Which was good) BUT I would still come here in a heart beat because the music made my heart happy.  there's a $10 minimum per person so getting drinks here would be perfect for me.

Don't go for the service or the food. The music is good but that's it. It took an hour to getting a drink, the food came out cold. The ribs were tough, the vegetables cold and mushy and the Mac and cheese tasteless. Project 48 were playing and they were energetic and worth the listen.  Our server was uninterested and seemed to be going through the motions.
Absolutely the best meal in 3 days in Nashville. The meatloaf was - to die for !  Don't pass this location up - stop in and enjoy !

This place needs a visit from Bar Rescue. Food was sub par, bartender was unfriendly, establishment was in shambles. There was a nice group playing music, but a drunk was being allowed to keep interrupting their act. Come on Jon Taffer, come to the rescue!

If you are under 75 and can walk on your own (without the need of a walker)...think again. The lunch cruise we went on was seriously an older crowd. The singers on the show were basically anyone who didn't make it in Nashville all dressing up like their favorite singers and hoping the crowd doesn't notice they aren't them. Good iced tea and pulled pork but I wouldn't be excited for the rest of this buffet lunch. Incredibly boring ride overall. I think the cruise on Gilligan's Island was more fun. Save your money and go to the Opry where they can really sing and don't have bedazzled microphones.

Food was not good at all, burnt short ribs, and dry chicken. They did not have sweet tea, which was shocking for a southern dining experience. We attended the Nashville nights event and some of the performers were talented but all they did was sing covers of country songs. There was nothing organic and it didn't really feel like Nashville. The boat is beautiful and the ride into downtown was great. I would never waste money on the food again.

The museum sits in a very touristy part of Nashville that made us a little leery of going into it.  We were afraid it would be something cheesy and overly commercial. We were completely wrong.

Any fan of Johnny Cash will truly love this museum.  It's a little small, but beautifully put together with so much to see.  What really made it different for me were all the the things he and others saved and held onto for so many years.  Things like hand written letters to fans, army discharge papers, responses to job inquiries, just really neat things to see and read.

Then of course there was the incredible library of live performances and TV appearances that you could spend hours watching.
Good food, slow service. Took forever to get a drink. Took 1.5 hours to order drinks, food, eat and get a check. Far too long for a burger joint.

So glad I finally made it over to Antioch to try 360 burger. I spent the morning at Percy Priest Lake Beach. Since I was in the area, I stopped by 360 burger after I heard good things. Wow one of the few times that a restaurant exceeded the hype.

 Two words: Pretzels Rolls. Amazing. As a Philly native there are few things I enjoy more than a  soft pretzel. Its one of my must haves as soon as I land in Philly. So I'm skeptical when people try to duplicate it. But 360 burger's pretzel rolls rock. The mix of salty and chewy was the perfect compliment to the juicy delicious burger. I got the basic cheeseburger with grilled onions.

 IT wasn't basic it was very well seasoned. And it was huge, I took half of it home. The sweet potato fries and aioli mayo were delicious. They were thin cut and crispy but not overdone. So many times when people try to do thin cut fries they overcook them. I was very impressed that these sweet potato fries were perfect. Also got a ton of the fries. Ended up taking about half of them home with my half of a burger. 


My waiter was friendly and attentive (disclaimer, I came in for a late lunch on a Friday afternoon and the restaurant was not very crowded.). Anyway, he offered my a water to go, which I always appreciate and he got e a lid so I could take the aioli home. 

There was a decent draught selection and I enjoyed my Sweetwater with my burger.

On vacation fom St. Louis... this is hands down my favorite venue in Nashville!!! Myself, my husband and several of our friends came here back to back night and had an amazing time. The entertainment, atmosphere, service, and management was SUPERB! I will most certainly come back anytime we are in the area!

We stumbled across this gem while cruising Broadway. Its set a little bit off the main drag and we were pleasantly surprised when we walked in.  They had two amazing guitarists and not to mention a great bar/waitstaff who were always super friendly.  We ended up ordering some ribs and they were fall off the bone AMAZING. Seriously, we thought they were better than Jacks BBQ on Broadway.  We loved this bar so much we went back a few times during the course of our stay.  Definitely a place to check out!

Visited the Johnny Cash Museum on August 6th 2017 and loved, loved, loved it. It's a self guided tour with displays from childhood. Very well done time line that provides a lot of relevant information about Cash, the times and the music. I spent about two to three hours and left feeling very differently about Cash, in a good  way.  It's a must see when visiting Nashville. The gift shop was over priced, as expected.

We experienced a Monday night here with the Song Suffragettes.  The whole family
enjoyed the night.  We ordered dinner, drinks, and sat back, relaxed and listened to
some really talented female songwriters   Very enjoyable evening!  Hope to return some day.

Stopped in today between 1 and 3:30 pm on our trip to Nashville because the music sounded good from the street. While my husband ordered I went to the ladies room. It was disgusting. There is a cabinet in the ladies room that holds extra paper towels and toilet paper. Apparently maintenance is self-serve because both the towel and toilet paper dispenser were empty and a stack of towels and the roll of toilet paper were placed on top of the cabinet along side a pile of trash because there was no waste basket in the rest room at all! When I returned to our table our waitress was serving our drinks and I told her of the situation. Her reply was that she knew, had told someone and shrugged her shoulders. Awhile later she told us she reported it again, this time to someone in security and he was looking for a trash can. Later I went back and there was a trash can but the floor had not been cleaned and the towels and toilet paper were still just on top of the cabinet. Upon further look if the cabinet, alongside the paper towels was a package of coffee!! Don't order coffee here!!! Or food. It wasn't that great. And the acoustics were terrible. So disappointed! Figured if a star owned the place the music would be great. And c'mon Dierks, aren't you making enough bucks to put a trash can in your bathrooms? I will NEVER come back here again. And by the way, it's not even worth ONE star in my review.

What a shame.  The burgers are awesome and super cheap.And the staff is friendly and fun but the beer prices off happy hour are ridiculous.  If you drink water coke or sweet tea this is your spot.
 $4.25 for a can of PBR!!!!  Come on man!!...And no domestics on draft?? That's just snobby. It's Antioch...lol  And only 16oz beers???? Right down the street Casa Fiesta has 32 oz beers for cheaper than your 12oz bottles.  I'm a bartender and a heavy drinker but I'm not gonna spend $24 on beer plus a $8.99 burger.  That's $32.99 for what?
It's just a shame.  I'm gonna do a 360° and take my butt back to Casa Fiesta...
Awesome place for music and orange moonshine drinks.  Great Sunday funday!  We highly recommend, must do in Nashville

Went here last night. Saturday march 1. Was celebrating my b-day. The place was kinda empty it was late. They weren't serving food anymore. And the one drink I had was completely nasty. It was the Aztac drink 11.00 dollars of nasty. The servers were either lazy an rude or tired. We was seated at a table but after 5 mins had to go get my own drink from the bar. First and last time there. Yuck.
Great food, friendly staff.. one of my favorite places to grab a burger in Antioch!  Check it out some time, you won't be disappointed

The service was terrible we waited 30 minutes for our beer and ended up cashing out since the food was going to be another 20 minutes. I have been here before and the food was fantastic but they need to fix their operations.
First let me say I am a fan.  We very much enjoyed our tour of the Johnny Cash Museum.  It is a one flour museum with a lot packed into it.   A nice selection in the gift shop.  Don't miss it.

As Nashville natives, my friends and I used to love this bar. Saturday night we all decided to go. Upon entering there was no one at the door. After walking in and heading to the bar, two of us were very forcefully grabbed by a bouncer we have never seen before. He is an overweight African American and has a horrible attitude. We immediately turned right around to give him our identification. Upon taking our identification back out of his hands, he immediately got in our faces and accused us of having an "attitude" and that we forcefully grabbed our IDs back out of his hands. In fact, there were other girls with us whom we were trying to get their attention so that they could show him their IDs but he ironically wasn't interested in their IDs and just wanted to know if we "forcefully grabbed our ID's out of his hands". Needless to say this has never happened before and we will never be back. What has Nashville become?!

Don't waste your time, there are many better places on Broadway. The service was painfully slow, food served cold, it took forever to even find the server so you could order a drink. This place needs to find a way to separate dining patrons between drinking/clubbing patrons. We were here for lunch and were surrounded by people standing all around our table, pouring over from the bar who were there to party. Our experience was unenjoyable on many levels.  Overpriced and overrated to say the least.

Drinks were decent and the band was good! Service was slow. The wings say "grilled" but really come out fried dry and with very little meat. Sweet potato fries OK but how do you really mess those up! Go for a drink and check out the America flag bar, skip the food.

Im giving them 3 stars for sone reasons:
The place is nice but a little bit loud for lunch, a little bit pricey. 
The hamburgers are really good, good flavor although the selection is poor.
We tried the fried Oreos with Ice Cream and they were really good.
I ordered mine medium well but came well done, but the server offered me to re do it the right way. Beside that, the server Tony did a great job. I will definitely come back for another try.
Made a reservation on their website.  Arrived with an email confirmation of reservation and was told they were closed for a private party.  Highly NOT recommended.

One of the best burgers in Nashville. I work nearby and this area has very limited places for lunch. This place is a gem though. There are a lot of different burgers to choose from and the service is great. Still have not stop after work for a beer, but the selection looks good.

Came here tonight. The tap option was low but the drinks were good. Mainly beer not many "mixed drinks" options. The food menu was slim, but pretty yummy. If you don't go to eat a meal at least try the gauc. It was so fresh and delicious. It was reasonably and normal priced menu. The patio was nice and lots of seating.parking seemed limited but free.

I just read that there will be an expansion to the museum. That's good cause it needs it. It felt cramped and with so many people moving slower than snails it was hard to enjoy the glass enclosed items of Johnny's. My boyfriend and I enjoyed the Movie and TV sit-down that was cleverly done. We LOVED...LOVED...LOVED.... the Sun portion of the Museum and as a historian it was done with such marvelous tasted. Really enjoyed the items that were shown but you guys really ought to add that piece of history in his Air Force that he was the first to hear that Stalin had died while stationed overseas. Keep up the good work we'll see ya again soon.

Worst food ever! Ordered shrimp fritters and couldn't identify a single bit of shrimp me or even the flavor of such as n their shrimp and corn fritters. Waitress just shrugged her shoulders and said, "It is what it it is'.  The band was no better than a small town dive bar band....actually, probably not even as good.

Recently, I visited Nashville for the first time, which was surprising to everyone since I have spent my whole life in the southeast. I knew that "Music City" is the hub for country music and thought I should enjoy it (at least the "classic country" portion). Being a big Johnny Cash fan, I naturally found my way to the museum and spent the good part of an afternoon exploring and learning even more about one of my favorite artists. 

I got there a little after midday and there was a decent crowd lining up to enter the museum. The price was almost the same amount as the Country Music Hall of Fame but was well worth it for Cash fans and country music fans (it could win you over to becoming a fan if you let it). I had read a biography of the man in black, but there were many cool artifacts and tidbits about his life that I never knew till visiting. From the interactive music mixing display to the theaters showcasing his musical and acting talents and the various awards he won, Cash is on full display. The museum ends with props from his last music video, for "Hurt," and like all good museums leads to the gift shop. This was the highlight of my trip and I would love to revisit with others!

Glad I got a chance to try this place out. Loved all of selections they had but I made my own which I was very happy with. 

Beef, sharp cheddar, carmalized onions, fried jalapeños, and raspberry jalapeño jam. I was surprised by the raspberry jam but I fell in love with it. You get the kick at the end. Waffle fries are also really good! 

Service is super friendly and very attentive. Place is nicely decorative. Even have a place where the live band is.
The 2 dollars off is not able to be used. The bar needs a print out of it, which doesn't make sense if you're on Yelp.

Really wanted to like this place. Made my husband go in despite the awful reviews... my thought is how bad can a bar be? Then one drink ordered and immediately annoyed by a $3 rocks charge. Sure maybe it's a bit more of a pour, but a $13 whiskey on Broadway is the most expensive I have seen

I really like Whiskey Row when I do hit the Broadway bars! The multi-level space provides for a variety of "vibes" on your night out. From live music space, to a club-like room, even to the awesome rooftop, there's a space for everyone on your next honky-tonk bar crawl!
The "hidden gem" of downtown Nashville! Great food, great music, and awesome upstairs patio!
LOVED the drinks here and the music! It was a friendly spot to walk in with a decent cover, and my under-21 sister was able to come in as well, which was rare in Nashville at night.

This was an ok experience. The boat is supposed to pull out at 7 pm. It left the dock at 720. Upon being called into the dining room the salad was on the table. The waiter was rude. He did not take a drink order at all. He got mad at me when I didn't want him to clear my salad plate as I was not done. We were the last table in the place to get our main course. Nothing was hot. The carrots were completely unappealing. The food was ok at best. Dessert was terrible and it was evident as almost every table did not eat their cake. The show may have been good if I had been able to see it. If you are up on the balcony don't count on seeing the show. I could see nothing. The music was good and upbeat. All in all yes it is a novelty trip but it is not worth the ticket price.

This place was fairly busy for a Monday night however with keeping that in mind, the time it took to get our drinks was incredibly long.  Additionally the service was quite poor, rarely checked in on us and never brought requested hot sauce or other condiments out.  The music was good but the most disappointing thing was the food, an incredibly bland whiskey burger with dry jerky-like bacon topped on it and the fries that could've been microwaved for all I know.  My peers seemed to like the wings they got but based on my experience I would not go back.
Love this place. Great music, decent beer selection from local breweries, fantastic atmosphere
Not from Nashville but this is what I thought Nashville was supposed to be.  Broadway is loud music and college bars.  This is real music.  Food is great and service is fantastic.

Good little museum but we do feel it is over-priced. They had some great memorabilia, clothing, hand-written letters from Cash and history about his acting career and timeline of his music career. Bathrooms were clean and it was nice and cool inside on a very hot summer day! Gift shop is very over-priced.

Had such a great time and the band was awesome   But after tipping the band to play the next song and paying our check, the bouncer decides to tell us to leave. Smirk and all.. Sorry this review would have been 5 stars but the bouncer deserves nothing. No respect and will not be back.

AWESOME. If you are visiting Nashville you have to check this museum out. It's well worth the money, and in my opinion is much more interesting than the Country Music Hall of Fame. My only regret is not buying something in the gift shop, but there was so much to choose from I couldn't decide!

Every time I've visited, my experience has been different (good, for the most part). I like that their mixed drinks are reasonably priced; if you want your money's worth, get their namesake. The menu changed a bit recently when the owners changed. I don't really notice any other differences, but the waiter I had mentioned how much better things were. The service seems better and more attentive. 

Burgers have been good if not terribly unique. Sweet potato fries need batter or seasoning. I'm still not decided on the pretzel bun being used for everything. This being Nashville, one of their draws is live music. I haven't heard anything bad yet, but it can get a bit loud. 

Overall, this is a place that you don't really expect to be in Antioch.

I love the Nashville Big Bang--music is always great (play by requests), and they will play anything so there is usually a good variety. There were a combination of 5-6 musicians that filtered on and off the stage in different combinations.

Big Bang is always interactive and this location is no exception. Great place to swing by for some shots (must get the obnoxious light-up shot glass). 

I will say it is harder to find than most bars on Broadway because it is upstairs.

Walking down Broadway in Nashville this is a place you could easily walk by and never know it was there. Just a doorway leading up to the second floor venue.
Big Bang is a great name because you get a lot of bang for your buck. 
If you don't know how Dueling Piano bars work, You write down a song on a piece of paper and give it (with a few bucks) to one of the pianists and they play your song.
These guys are talented! They also from time to time have accompaniment from a drummer or guitar player. 
This is now by far my favorite place on the Nashville strip.
Waiters and waitresses also sing and dance in between taking drink orders (they do a great job at both) 
Sadly they weren't open on Sunday (even they have to rest) but if you are in Nashville you need to check it out.

Cover is just $6 after 8:30pm, drinks are well poured and fairly priced.

Get there early for a good seat!!

I frequent swinging door monthly...but I believe last night was the last.  Spent $40+ on alcohol and food. I then went back to the bar to grab a couple waters...they refused to pour me a water that wasn't a $3 bottle.  I realize SD has the right to not serve a drink but that is so ridiculous!  We left and went to Barlines in the Omni.  They gladly gave me waters and laughed that swinging door acting like that!
Great burgers and wonderful selection of beer! Also on Friday and Saturday nights they have live music and the bands that I have seen there are top notch!

Wow, lived here all these years,  family came in to town and invited us here. What an awesome place. Great music at a great price, extremely genuine Nashville treasure. Food was better then our Broadway adventures. Free valet parking was super convenient. For $12 bucks a person, $5-6 beers, great deal.

Had my hubby bring home chicken sliders...should have probably went with the hamburger sliders. More bread than anything. Definitely wouldn't order this again. Sweet potato fries were just okay; I've had better.
Went here on a Saturday late night after a show at TPAC.  The bartender, Dana Marie, was fantastic!!!

I've been wanting to check this place out for a long time.  When our songwriter friend Simon was scheduled to perform I wasn't going to miss it for anything.  You can purchase tickets at the door but I wasn't taking any chances so I ordered them ahead of time.  It was a good thing I did because they sold out.  There was a long line of people waiting to get in and others on a wait list in case people with tickets didn't show.  Performing songwriters included Simon Reid, Sister C, and Michael Ray.  The songs told a story.  It was a fabulous show.

Seating seems to be first come first serve.  After standing in line, you make your way up to the counter where you give them your name and a hostess seats you.  If you want to sit with your friends then you should purchase your tickets together and make sure you get there at the same time.  The service was great!

I started with "The Show Cabernet" as I looked over the menu.  The couple sitting at the table with us had been there before and recommended the Country Fried Chicken so that's what I ordered.  It came with red skinned mashed potatoes and green beans.  The food portions were huge so I ate half and took the other half for lunch the next day.  The food was good and the wine was great.  We will have to make a return visit before long.
Just awesome! Very entertaining and the staff was very attentive and helpful. They really looked out for me as I was by myself. Get there early for a good seat.

An excellent place to visit. However I think there needs to be more " listening stations" 1  headset and up to 4 songs/videos per decade was very frustrating. We were there on a quiet day,one could only imagine what would happen if a bus tour arrived. Parking close by is  expensive, we found a parking metered space that had no time limit and cost $1.50 per hour, far cheaper than the private parking charges.
This place is terrible could not be worse. Giant lines. Terrible service. Have to wait in line forever to do anything. DO NOT COME HERE
Great place for food and seeing the best local talent. The nice twist here is you can actually hear the performers.

We came for brunch for a bachelorette party. It is cute, the food was pretty good, the music was great... But the service was INSANELY BAD. It started with our waiter bringing us coffee, 10 minutes later the cream, another 10 min later sugar. So, coffee was cold. Then when we ordered food the Bride asked for a side of toast and was told they couldn't do that. When we pointed out that they serve toast/sandwiches with bread elsewhere on the menu he said he would have to check if they could... 

In general he was extremely rude and condescending anytime we asked for anything-- water refills, salt, ketchup. We were made out to feel like a burden. THEN we get our checks. Our BOGO mimosas were charged double, and the waiter refused to listen to us explain and told us we were wrong. He brought the manager over, and though it took him awhile to understand what happened he was apologetic once he realized the waiter's mistake. Waiter brought us wrong checks again. An hour after we finished eating we finally could leave. This whole time our dirty plates sat uncleared.

A lot of us worked in the restaurant industry as servers, and we were sympathetic about having to serve 10 people... But he was so rude to us, and took no ownership of his mistake. He tried to blame the overcharge for the size of our group. Our quick brunch was a two hour ordeal, and ruined our bride's morning. This place needs to get Eli outta there.

One of the most amzing collections of anyone's personal life let alone the life of an icon like Johnny Cash.  I think some of the more negative reviewers missed the mark on this place.  Going through and reading about his life and career with all the included memorabilia and personal memories of his life was, to me, like being able to go theough his personal effects.  They allow as many pictures as you want but I felt uncomfortable taking pictures of his personal things there.  It is an amazing collection cataloging the life of a great man and musician and must see if you're near enough to it.

I absolutely love this place!! We started coming here after craving good burgers in June 2013. Ever since then, this place has been a weekly stop for our family and friends. I love every burger on the menu! And I have never been to a burger place that hits how you want your meat cooked right on the nose!
Enjoy live music, this place has it! The service is always great and pleasant. I usually come in with big groups and the servers are more than happy to serve an accommodate! Two of my favorite servers are Tod and  Matt.
Food options are great! I love the pretzel bun, but you can get a regular bun too! Sweet potato fries are da bomb!!! And if you are still hungry after you mama Jana burger, their brownie with ice cream is divine! 
Check out 360 burger!

Dana Marie, How I love your shakes and I'm not talking about your ice cream swirled in a blender. 

She danced, she moved, she shook her booty, she listened but acted like she didn't and she got everything right. She delivered a burger just like I wanted and did the bottled beer with sass and pizzaz. 

When you go to a fine steak place you expect fine dining and great steak. When you go to a honky tonk with great live tunes and a burger menu that you want to try, it should deliver it just right. 

Swinging Doors Saloon swings the right way for me.

I'll be honest, I didn't know a thing about Johnny Cash except that I could recognize a song or two and that there was a movie chronicling his life played by Reese Witherspoon and Joaquin Phoenix. However, this is a must see experience. They told his life story beautifully, and I felt like I knew him by the time I left the museum. I wish I had more time and it was less crowded because there is so much to read, music to listen to and movie clips to watch. You could easily spend 1.5-2 hrs in the museum, just because there's so much stuff. It's also nice how they dedicated a small section of the museum to other musicians that Johnny Cash worked closely with like Elvis. Yes, the museum is small and it gets really crowded. To truly enjoy, try to go during off peak hours. Fan or not, there is no denying that if you visit the country capital of the world you must visit this place. There is something magical about seeing and being so close to the memorabilia that was once a huge part of the life of one of the one of the best selling musicians of all time. After leaving the museum, I can say I'm a fan. 

The Patsy Cline museum recently opened above on the second floor, but to be honest I didn't think it was worth spending almost another $40 on two additional tickets. I will save that for another day and time.

As owner of Music City Pub Crawl, we bring about 150-200 guests to Swingin' Doors each week. Many enjoy the burgers, pizza and drinks, as well as the incredible entertainment. But I recently discovered another facet of Swingin' Doors which was their catering skills. We hosted a corporate group last week that stopped here for a buffet-style dinner. For $10 less a person than a competitor, they customized and prepared a menu that surpassed my request. It was easily one of the finest meals I have seen buffet-style. The menu was a garden salad, catfish, ribs and smoked chicken.  Everything was spectacular, bountiful and fresh. I was truly impressed and my guests were very pleased. We have already booked another catering job for 125 guests. I would highly suggest them to cater your next event. Well done Swingin' Doors Saloon.
Best live music in Nashville!!! No, seriously, original artists; heartfelt and soulful, talented artists. I wish our stay could have been longer. Loved loved loved...
