We had a great time at TLR. Great acts and service. The fried pickles were awesome.  The dinner food was OK. But the reason to go is the music and with very friendly service and staff that outweighs the OK dinner food. We will definitely go back and tell our friends to check it out!

I'm super cheap and was not thrilled when my guests wanted to go to this museum. $20 was certainly more than I wanted to spend for Johnny Cash, and I was annoyed to hear that the Patsy Cline exhibit was a separate charge. (Spoiler alert: I probably would have given this 5 stars if admission was $5-10 cheaper)

I was pleasantly surprised by the exhibit. There are a lot of videos, artifacts, and interesting things to read. And there were several interactive activities that I was impressed by, including one in which you could re-mix one of his songs. The museum held my attention, though I'm not a Johnny Cash fan.

Again, my main complaint was the cost (though that complaint applies to most of the tourist traps). They advertised a "green screen" where you could "get you picture taken with Johnny." I was not pleased to hear you had to pay for this - $20 for one picture! I will say, however, that they edited the photos nicely so it really does look like he's in the picture. My cousin was very pleased to buy it.

Wanting to do a "tourist day" in our own town, my wife and I decided to visit the Johnny Cash Museum on a Saturday. We loved it! It has a ton of Cash artifacts and displays that detail his music, the eras he lived and sang through, and the people he touched. There are some interactive stations where you can experiment with sound mixing, plenty of music stations where you can listen to different recordings of Cash and his close contemporaries, and clothing and musical instruments that the man wore and played on tour. Our personal favorites were the things from Cash's personal home (including his grandfather's piano that was his most prized personal possession) and all the June-Johnny love artifacts (there's even a poem he wrote the day of June's funeral). 

Negatives: The only beef that we had with the tour was that the entrance to the tour was extremely crowded. It loosened up after the first hall but it was initially kind of overwhelming. Hopefully at some point they can extend or build onto the building, which would help with overcrowding. 

Rebuttals to some other criticisms I noticed in other reviews:

1. The Cash Museum has nothing to do with parking prices in downtown Nashville. Credit high crime rates, white flight, and the expansion of the suburbs in the 1950s-70s which made it possible to have a ton of cheap parking in downtown Nashville in years past, but those days are long gone. Its not the museum's fault if parking lots of being turned into high-rise office and condo space. Like any other city, its expensive to park. Either learn to parallel park (free on weekends), or ride the bus. Its $1.70 for a bus ride and they all lead to the downtown terminal.

2. The price of admission is honestly not that bad. $16-18 is pretty typical for museums. If you're a Johnny Cash fan, its worth it. 

3. I saw a lot of complaints about prices in the gift shop. Are y'all new to museums or something? When has a museum gift shop ever had bargain-bin prices?

I would give this experience 2.5 stars if I could, because of the two hour trip, I hated the first hour and loved the second. The first hour you're herded into the main boat ball room, which is kept at a breezy -10 degrees, and proceed to put on the most cheesy and staged show I've ever seen outside of Gatlinburg. It's a shame, because it's definitely a talented cast. The highlight of this hour was when the two very pretty singers pulled up a grandfather, sang a creepy Grandpa song to him, and asked if they could be his granddaughters too. He very clearly stated, "No, but you can be my girlfriends. Well, kind of clearly. There was a drunken slur happening there (bottomless mimosas for $14!) They were completely thrown and off script for like 30 whole seconds. His wife was less amused. The food is unremarkable. For the second hour, they let you actually go outside and have normal, real human musicians playing and an out door bar set up. I give the first hour 1 star and 5 to the second.

I will be going to this bar for the second time in a row on my trip to Nashville. Excellent service by the bartenders and delicious affordable drinks in fun serving cups that they allow you to take home as souvenirs. Hilarious entertainment and fun. The artists are incredibly talented that I almost wanted to sign them to a record label. The Big Bang honors old time rock n roll and makes you remember the good times, while getting a nice buzz with friends!

I'm a longtime fan of The Listening Room. It has gone through many iterations. My only comment intended to be helpful to the ownership, is that you really need to work on your menu and finesse. I've had mostly not-so-good experiences with food there. I will keep going back and back because I love the place so much, and the great support it offers the writing community. So I would highly encourage everyone to attend shows as they are the best in town, but don't have high expectations for the food yet. Cut them slack as they figure it out and let the food catch up with the outstanding venue. Be supportive of them as they are really trying, I'm sure. Best part of the place is the valet parking! Two thumbs up!

Part Two follow up...I only made those comments to be constructive. There are some very good things on your menu, but I think you can top others. You have one of the best music venues in town both for seasoned pros to the tourists. Keep up the good work!

The restaurant has a great open space with a clean look.  The breakfast buffet was sub par, food was barely warm, chicken was dry.  Had to ask to have utensils put out on the buffet in order to serve some of the items. The bottomless bloody Marys helped offset the cost of the food. Bloody Mary's and Mimosas were good.  

The music was good unfortunately it ended 15 minutes after we arrived and was switched to football. No real listening happened not sure If this was due to the time we arrived.

This is a no-cover dueling pianos bar on the main strip in downtown Nashville. It has a fairly large seating area and a separate bar, with a small spot open for people to dance. The acts were very energetic and some were quite talented with playing piano and drums, and also being able to improvise. There was a college age heavy crowd though I saw a few other groups with people in the late 40s range. Drinks were meh and about $6 each, service was friendly but they did not have enough staff to keep each group properly served. The poor girl was running around as fast as she could but she had too many tables to keep up with. The music selection was mainly pop, with a little bit of country mixed in. You could request songs (along with a tip) and the higher the tip the more likely your song would be played (if they knew it). We had a decent time and would consider returning, but with so many music places available it would probably be a long time before we find ourselves back there.
The service and people here were awesome! Our bartender was the best! We returned for another afternoon of fun.

Hands down one of the best burgers in Nash. The cilantro avocado burger is to die for. All grass fed beef and lots of varieties of fries to choose from. The service is always extremely friendly, as well!  Love this place!

This place is awesome. If you're looking for a chill place off Broadway and interested in great talent and original live music this is the place.  We just saw Gina Vernier, Jeffrey East and Summer Overstreet. Phenomenal singer songwriters with distinctive styles. You'll be inspired to support up and coming artists.

Drinks were great, food was okay. I ordered the pulled pork, which was very dry without a lot of flavor, but that didn't prevent me from giving the highest rating to this place. 

A must for first-time travellers to Nashville.

So I was in a different area and wanted to try something new. Thanks for Yelp I found this place and it had a ton of great reviews. I will be adding another one. Place is small but very clean and seemed like they just opened that day. Service was on point and the burger, it was worth the $10 charge. I would not say the best burger I have had but definitely suprising. I ordered the cilantro avocado burger with fries. If you are a burger fan you have to try this place out.
Wow this place is a hidden gem! Didn't get any food, but great entertainment and wait staff. Man these musicians are talented.

I have not felt more unwelcome in my whole stay in Nashville until tonight when i went to Blue Bar.  They were rude and inconsiderate to out of towners. I would recommend to anyone visiting here to not go to this place!!
Great self guided tour, full of so many interesting stories and facts. I wasn't sure if I would like it but I would definitely go again!

I have learned a lot about The Man in Black. I think they did a great job showcasing Johnny Cash life. It was worth the price I paid, but way not get it cheaper. Check Groupon before you go.  If nothing is there they have AAA discount for dollar off.

We were in Nashville for a whirlwind 48 hours to see a show at the Ryman, so the next morning, we had a bit of time to kill before we headed back to the airport, and I came across the Johnny Cash Museum on Yelp... and well, we just had to go. 

We were staying downtown, so after lunch at Puckett's, we walked on down. You enter into a little gift shop, then at the register you see the admission for the museum. I think it was $14 bucks per person.... then you walk on back. 

I was amazed to see the variety of things in here... from Cash's school report cards, to Morse code manuals he used in the army, to stage outfits, of course all of the records, but some really nice and awesome hand written set list, lyrics and notes to be viewed as well. It is small back there, but there is a TON of great stuffed packed in. 

They have ipad audio stands that you can put on some headphones and listen to Johnny's songs in each decade. His cover of NIN Hurt plays in the background and it never fails to make me shed a few tears. Also very cool, a station where you can listen to Get Rhythm on 33, 78, cassette, CD and MP3 formats, to hear the difference between each one. (Now to go and finally get that replacement needle for our record player!) 

Super intimate feel, so much so that I also shed a few tears after reading a few love letters penned to June... 

A MUST for any Johnny Cash fan.

I went to this place because I was told they have live music for late night options. The music was great! I ordered wings and after about 20 minutes I asked where they were and asked if I could just get my money back. At this point I was "reprimanded" by the bar tender and the manager. I was asked to leave as the manager literally threw the wings in a to-go box. The man anger made a scene and told me "I should leave"... It was literally the worst experience I have had in a bar. I felt like a complete idiot.
Wonderful museum filled with lots of memorabilia. Great place for any Johnny Cash fan to visit!

Stopped here on a Tuesday afternoon during 4th of July week. It was a pretty full crowd and the band that was playing was amazing, probably our favorite of the week. Our waitress was very nice and frequented our table and made sure we were taken care of. The place was very clean and nice. Unfortunately it gets really busy later at night and we never got a chance to return. We would recommend it, we had a great time. If anyone knows the band in my photo please let me know we would like to follow them on YouTube or any other social media. Thanks in advance!
Great burger place with live music during the evenings.  Had the PB&J burger which was terrific and a craft beer.  Highly recommend.
Surprisingly delicious. If you don't mind country music - I'm serious - they serve great burgers and generously-portioned sides. Try the Smoked burger minus BBQ sauce. I'll be back for more

The entertainment was great but it was hard to enjoy the music because our service, the food and overall experience was very disappointing. I highly recommend eating before you arrive and just ordering drinks, don't order any food.

My rating is for the Saturday brunch.  The items included: fried potato, scrambled eggs, French toast, bacon, sausage patties, and biscuits.  There were also some fresh vegetables and fruits and yogurt.  Food tasted fair, seating is plentiful and atmosphere is excellent, with great music.  Service is slow and friendly.  Really just wasn't worth $18.  If price was $10, may be a three star.

Meh, I'd skip this place for brunch.  Live music doesn't start until 12 (which is really why we came here).  Food was just ok.  Nothing special.  Ordered shrimp and grits.  Shrimp lukewarm and shredded cheese on grits not even melted.  Lobster bisque was terrible.  For the price, I'd head to Southern Steak and Oyster for brunch.

We just went there on August 12 and we were surprised there were a lot of people there (to the point that no one was motioning the number of people in or out - could be a fire hazard) .  But on the other hand when you walk in there are many different kinds of t-shirts and gifts in their store.  General admission is $18.00 per person.  
    So much memorabilia it's unbelievable.  The exhibits start out with Johnny Cashs' childhood and his military service in the Air Force.  As you walk through the museum you can hear his music and see different documentaries on his prison performances and clips from his TV shows.  There are walls with all of his gold and platinum records, a history of his musical career, all of his 45 singles that he sold, all of his album covers, his 8 track tapes, and cassettes.
Not much to say! We have been to a few dueling piano bars and this one did not make the cut.

The Listening Room was a pleasant surprise! We had no problem parking and the food was delicious..great drinks too. There was no line at all and the concert was fantastic. Bucky Covington, Craig Campbell..to just mention a few of the talented songwriters that were there.

Not a big fan but fell in love with the musuem.  The displays were very interesting and i found myself reading every single page of the man's life history. we were rushing to the airport to pick up someone so had to hurry through and got to see only half the museum. Despite that, i'm still glad we visited!
Wasn't what I was expecting and the cost is more then it should be honestly, but the pictures to walk around and see were a good memory to see. My favorite part was the end with Cash's Chair.

This place is everything that tourists love and locals make fun of.  Amazing musicians, all of whom are multi instrumentalists, singers, and killer entertainers.  Is it filled with bachelorette parties, packed on weekends, loud, obnoxious, and filled with out of towners?  Yup.  That's what makes it a really amazing time.  Try it out, bring all your friend stuff and get sloppy.
My wife an I had lunch here. The burgers were awesome! Very well seasoned and cooked at the right temp. Even the fries were crispy and hot! Very well portion. Only down side was the price.

If you're trying to decide between this museum and the Country Music Hall of Fame, do this one. I spent more time here than I did at the Country Music HOF and this museum is less than half its size.

Cash fan or not, the fact that this legend gets his own museum in Nashville ought to be enough of a reason to go. Conveniently located in downtown, there's almost no reason not to. Well worth the $17 admission (not Cash only).

Plan on being here for at least 2 hours.

What a great first night in Nashville. We were able to witness and meet great talented people.  I had the Carly's "hide the wine" sangria, Uncle Zobb's margarita  and the famous turkey apple crisp sandwich. The drinks we're phenomenal. I was a little underwhelm with the turkey apple crisp sandwich.  It was good but I wasnt quite blown away given the reputation. I would say Josh Matheny, Elise Hayes, Josh Dorr and Emma White were amazing. The sound quality was good. The tickets were easy to get, unlike the blue bird cafe.  Both Josh Matheny and Elise Hayes are going to perform there in a week but we felt like we didn't miss anything.
Great pace to visit when in Nashville! It's a must to have on your list! Great entertainment and they even include the audience! It and experiments you won't get anywhere else!
Stoked to have a great smoke free pub to hit whenever! Just behind the venue. It's open all the time, not just when they're shows. Great food too!

We were excited to stop by here, my sons first pick to do on our trip. Tons of cool memorabilia through the years and sample music to listen to in different recording types through the years. Lotsa history in here on Johnny Cash and the gift shop had a great variety of cool stuff to purchase! Staff friendly and helpful. A must see in Nashville!

This place is fantastic. Great burgers. Local music that's gets to the soul of Nashville rather than the stereotype.service is up to par. If your near a ouch it's the best one here. If your driving through Nashville on the 24 its worth the stop.

The atmospere was great. You could really tell the meat was organic and grass fed. We were here on singer/songwriter night, good music. The service and envirorment were comfortable and inviting. I really hope that this local resteraunt expands and goes places. P.s. Prices are very reasonable.

Dueling pianists, often accompanied by bass and drums, play cover requests, spiced with friendly or biting commentary. While there's plenty of fun watching the waitstaff do the time warp, the real attraction is the musicianship of hearing on-the-fly versions of everything from 60s classics to the latest Bruno Mars. Not the extra loud atmosphere of other Broadway bars.

I had a great time. My first time at a place like this I didn't know what to expect....classical or just a guy playing a piano. Well let me tell you I was wrong it started off with 2 guys on different piano playing one song then going right in to another. They interact with the crowd about songs and requested songs. If you want your song played TIP them. they also break into a full band and the drinks were priced right. Overall a great time cant wait to got back

Attended this bar on a Saturday night, and the place was definitely full of entertainment. These guys are seriously SO talented-- as most play all the instruments as well as sing, NOT to mention pretty much know every single song the crowd asks for. For me (as I am not into huge crowds or the typical dirty bar scene) this was an excellent stop while in Nashville. Actually went here with my boyfriend and it served as fun, but chill bar date night. The staff was really friendly and helpful, and were constantly asking if we needed anything. Also I liked how this bar was cleaner than a lot of the others and the staff was constantly cleaning up used cups, etc, so things would not get too messy. If you come to the Big Bang-- definitely expect a good time and lots of laughs!

AMAZING !!!! It was our first time to Nashville, and nothing compares to this place!!! My husband and I came twice during our stay because we had SO much fun !!! Huge shoutout to TYSON who just killed it !!! He was able to play all the songs we were requesting and it was amazing. Also, as a tip, request Kenny's Prince mashup because your life won't be the same afterwards. It was incredibly amazing !!! What a talented group of performers !!!!

Pretty good, I got the salmon burger and my boyfriend had the cilantro and avocado burger I believe is what is was called. We checked in on yelp and got a coupon for free appetizers! Lol that was pretty cool. But we will be back!

This was my favorite bar in Nashville - which says a lot about me, I think, namely that country music is not my thing!  If it isn't yours either, then make this place your home.  We had a DAMN good time here on a Sunday night, no cover, place was crowded but you could still get a table and drinks fairly easily.  They had three pianists, who rotated so that they could take breaks and/or play the drums.  Most of the piano players were young and cute and funny, but all were extremely talented musicians.  They were making everyone laugh all night, and they could turn ANYTHING into a great piano song.  I was singing along all night!  Yeah it's mainly pop music, some current, some 80s/90s, but let's be real - I love that stuff.  And these guys could turn Baby Got Back into a piano song!  That is impressive!  $20 for a request is pretty steep, but I imagine drunk people are willing to do it.  I didn't feel the need to request anything since their whole song list was like putting my iPod on shuffle. 

There's plenty of honky tonk and country on Broadway.  If you need a break from it, go here. You won't regret it!

Attended the grand re-opening last night and thought the venue was amazing!  The line-up stellar - the place was packed!  We had fried pickles, fish tacos and the nashvegas burger - everything was great! My husband tends to be a 'burger snob' and wanted to go back the next day for another one!  The home-made chips are perfect too!!  

The owner is wonderful - he stopped and talked with guests all evening!  He is very friendly and approachable.

The venue is perfect!
Great music, low quality food. My waiter lost my credit card and showed great indifference to that fact. Not good...
4 great songwriters and great drinks. Food is good. Come for the music. Wait staff was very good. More enjoyable than cramming into a bar on Broadway.

First I am not an employee. I might be delusional. LOL. This is my second visit to burger 360 and just like the first time the service was great and the food was served hot and fresh. Our waiter, Taylor, was above par refilling our drinks before they were even half empty. 
The serving size was that same as my last visit 6 months ago. The only thing wrong  was really my fault. I ordered my burger with the habanero cheese and it packed a bite. The burger took some time to cook but they cook them fresh so you not getting a burger that has been setting for awhile. 
Don't come here in a hurry cause this is not a FAST food joint. They take their time and get it right and as long as I continue to get good food and service from them I will continue to visit one of the best burger joints in Nashville, much less Antioch. 
Good eating!!

I really enjoyed the museum with factual information on Cash. Lots of information...photographs, handwritten letters, video clips, and simply a must see on any trip to Nashville. My favorite he played in was when he played the villan in a Columbo episode.

I will have to say this place is pretty cool but I have to give 2 stars because last night my girlfriend and I went and there were maybe 10 other people in there and I tipped them and make a request for a Boston song 

They instead wanted to keep playing rap music because some drunk people kept giving them $20 

It sort of pissed me off. I wasted 2 1/2 hours waiting for my request to be played and it never was..

Very disappointing 

I will not tip these guys EVER again

Great spot! We were immediately welcomed by a friendly and fun staff. Jake is an amazing bartender! I love his upbeat personality and he makes outstanding drinks! We enjoyed the bands both days we were there and food is delicious! Each floor has a different, but cool vibe and I really like the decor. We will definitely go back next time we are in Nashville!

A trip to Nashville is not complete with out stopping at Big Bang !!! A really great time nice new location, a great alternative to country music. They take requests for any type of music and was blown away by the drumming of Tyson I believe that the long haired guy, only to be amazed by his singing and showmanship the waitstaff is very entertaining but in a fun and different way!!! Good time!

Being our first time in Nashville, we stayed downtown and did the touristy bars along Broadway.  After 3 days of the crowds, annoying bachelor/bachelorette parties, and drunk college kids we wanted to venture out and just listen to some good music in a different atmosphere.  We heard about the Listening Room located just a few blocks from downtown and made reservations which surprisingly was only $5 per person.  They have 2 shows Monday through Saturday nights at 6 and 8:30 pm.  I called the venue to find out what time I should arrive for the 8:30 show.  I was told that the 6 pm show ends at 7:30 and since the seating is first come, first serve, I should arrive at 7:30.  Glad I did because we beat the crowd in and were able to get a great seat.  However, this location has plenty of seating....but if you want to sit near the stage, plan on coming early.  They have a $15 per person minimum once you have been seated....ordering drinks at the bar in the wait area do not count.  The prices were fairly reasonable....My Yuengling was $4 a bottle....cheaper than I had on the strip.  The menu was typical bar food.  We ordered the cheese plate that came with pita chips, gouda cheese, cheddar cheese, and a generous serving of pimento cheese.  Other items on the appetizer menu were hummus, chicken sticks, and hot wings. They also have dinner items as well.  The music was excellent.  There were 4 artists sitting side by side on stage...each one taking turns playing songs they wrote themselves and usually giving a short intro on how they came up with the song.  All in all, we had a great time and would highly recommend to anyone looking to hear good new music.  One final thing....if you are staying in the downtown area....even though it is about 10 blocks from Broadway, I would recommend taking an Uber especially on the way back since this area could be a little shady at night.

Our waiter was very pleasant, and took the time to tell us about the menu. The food and drinks were delicious,  and even my toddler enjoyed his kids meal. Service was quick, we are definitely coming back again.

We had 7 of us from ages 9 to 79 went on a beautiful afternoon.  I choose not to add the food option based upon the reviews here, Opry Mills is where you park so there are plenty of restaurants nearby. 
Things I did not see mentioned.
The keyboard entertainer up top made this trip very enjoyable.  He got the crowd going, I think he name was Casey.  
Had it rained as was in our forecast - the ride would have been a lot less enjoyable and we probably would have been squished.  
There is a short list of food for purchase that we didn't find out about until the ride's end if you want something to hold you over. 
Drinks are pricey but it's a cruise after all.  
"Sunday in the South" theme was not for us, we hardly watched the show.
Buffet - I did a walkby and was happy that wasn't our lunch.
Overall enjoyable smooth sailing to downtown and back.

On a road trip I stopped at several museums but this was the best.  Price is $17.95 for seniors and we forgot our $1 off coupon you can get at any hotel.  
The place is clean and when I accidently touched the glass by the Remington piece, someone was there to wipe my prints off as soon as I walked away.  I apologized when I saw him at the end of the tour.  Very interesting.  Give yourself some time to really look at all the stuff.  Sooooo much to see.  More than I thought there would be. 
One problem.  I had my photo taken but they were not very good at directing me on how to stand so the picture would look like I was playing with the guitar with Johnny.  Make sure you check out the other photos and ask them to set up the photo exactly like the example.  I personally think $12.95 is all they should have charged me for a printed copy.  I did not need the $5 to down load it.  I wish they would correct that part.  But it is a cool picture.
Good food, good live music, the bar staff (Dana) was so nice.  Just got into town, and glad we stopped in here for lunch.  Had a great time.

I was a bit confused by this place.  First, if its a sporty bar place please put on more variety games/sports on their 20 tv sets.  All of them had basketball (same useless channel) and it was not a game. I do not care for basketball but I will watch hockey, NASCAR, golf, even curling but something else, please.  Secondly, Is it a fast food burger place?  Is it a casual dining place?  Now, the burger.  it was ok.   Fries, skip them.  Thirdly, Service was very good.  

I am not sure about this place, odd.

I hit this place up for a friends birthday party.  The food was good and priced nice (hey! Free shake with a Yelp check in!) The HUGE problem was the house band.  We had a larger party and it was impossible to talk to anyone that wasn't directly next to you.  The music was very loud.  At one point the saxophone player made his rounds to the tables and played to people...it was super uncomfortable.
I want to go back to hit up there extensive happy hour menu but I'll be sure to check out the entertainment situation first.

Oh. My. Gosh. If this place was closer to home I would be broke. My girls and I were in Nashville for a bridsmaid's weekend and we just stumbled upon this gem. 
Routy fun, with a great atmosphere. The musicians are ridiculously talented and also entertaining because of their senses of humor. Be prepared to sing along, if that's your thing!

We had a lovely time on the cruise. the entertainment and food were excellent. My one very big complaint is they didn't recycle, the beer bottles and cans went right into the garbage can, I watched. Very disappointed in that.

THIS PLACE HAS DELICIOUS FOOD! It was our first time there, so we asked our server for some suggestions. His suggestions did not disappoint. I had the PBJ & O burger (sounds weird, but try it. You will LOVE that burger) and my husband had the slippery pig. Our server was attentive, the vibe was great, their menu selection has enough variety to satisfy even the pickiest of pallets, and they are reasonably priced. Their sweet potato fries were fantastic! They use fresh, local ingredients which is why you can taste the difference in their burgers as opposed to other places in and around Nashville. They also have different "meat" choices such a chicken, fish, ect instead of beef on your burger. 
We are looking forward to being able to try their happy hour, which we have been told is fantastic. 
I highly recommend this place to burger lovers anywhere!

OVER THE TOP FUN!

If you don't know the name of a song or the artist, at least know a lyric or two...

Throw it out on a slip of paper, a TIP would be nice, since you are requesting it...and the fun begins!

These guys will belt out ANY song ever written. The oldies, the funk, the rock, the blues, the R&B, the hip hop, the pop...there was not a song they could not play by heart on the pianos. A drummer was added and these guys, rather HOT, by the way...they mixed it up and changed positions playing the grand pianos and master drums!

It was a blast! 
Ever in Nashville, this is a MUST SEE!
Amazing memorabilia, well-done storytelling, and a tantalizing amount of musical and video treats. Best museum I've been too in a while, well worth the stop!

Used to love this place, great bar with coolest bartenders and only place we could stop for a friend who smokes. 

Despite the shitty toilets and the music sometimes a touch too loud to continue conversation we kept going back for the great service and killer cheese sticks.

But now no more smoking so our regular spot will likely change...real shame. Most of the regulars here smoke, guess they don't like the steady business...???

Just visited Nashville for my second time over and was determined to get a 'songwriters experience. A friend of mine who's been living there for several years directed me to The Listening Room. She said it's a lot less crowded and strict than the bluebird which has to get some sell out months in advance now.

I have to say I absolutely loved this venue, however they do sell tickets in advance online. They're super cheap about $5 or $10 but you're going to want to make sure that you got those tickets so that you don't have to wait out in line like I did hoping to get a waiting list seat. I got the seats the show was great but I could definitely have done without the 1 hour and 15 minute wait because I didn't plan properly, so don't make my mistake!

Now on to the show. Once you get inside they do have a $10 per person minimum during the show which last anywhere from 90 minutes to 2 hours. Serve food in a full-service bar so it's not hard to hit. Food get 3 stars. Nothing special so is recommend having done drinks and eating elsewhere. 

Music was fantastic! When I was there there were three singer-songwriters on the stage taking turns playing songs they've written. Several of them have even written number 1 top hits from people on country music radio right now! They were so talented! The venue is small and fairy intimate but didn't feel cramped. They do allow whispering - my understanding is many others like Bluebird do not. 

Loved it! Will go again!

We set sail on the dinner cruise tonight and were treated like royalty. The whole experience was so well done. The food, the wait staff and the entertainment couldn't have been better. Food is served family style with a lazy Susan in the middle of the table. Roast beef, pork loin, mashed potatoes, mac&cheese, carrots, green beans, , salad and rolls was our feast tonight. Then a chocolate mousse pie with coffee to finish the meal. The show was so good! The ride to downtown Nashville was smooth and made for some pretty pictures.

Went to the Listening Room Cafe on a Monday night for the Song Suffragettes, and they were amazing! The idea behind the restaurant is incredible, so it was hard not to love attending a show at The Listening Room. 

However, no amount of awe-inducing singer/songwriters could distract from the fact that it took over an hour to receive two salads. It was a bit frustrating to feel like we were being completely ignored by our waiter. Other sections seemed to receive their orders much more promptly, but we were definitely not the only ones to receive our meals at the end of the show.

If you do end up going, I suggest arriving as early as possible to get your order in before the show begins. Although I'm skeptical that was the reason for our lack of efficient service, it doesn't hurt to arrive early!

Easily the best "upscale" burger place in town. I had the mushroom swiss, very good, nice and juicy. We also had the sliders, fried mushrooms, and salmon burger. The piece of salmon was huge for the price but I think putting it on a burger didn't do it any favors. It would be better as an entree. The onion rings were not my cup of tea, but if you like the beer batted thick cut kind they are perfect for you. Overall, excellent food good atmosphere and fair price. Definitely give it a try!

Very rude bartender, had to wait ten min for a beer after paying and never got the garnish for the mixed drink.. 
Then a generator was brought out and it stunk up the whole patio. It wasn't even on, it just generated a haze of fumes!

I usually love a dueling piano bar, and I figured being in Nashville there should be some great artists here.  That said, this is more set up like a concert with rows of folding chairs facing the two pianists.  It was a bit uncomfortable, and just plain awkward.  I would have expected more of a lounge/bar feel where the pianos were part of the entertainment, not the sole purpose of the establishment, to the point they did not even invest in cocktail tables.

And, they did not play our request despite the $5 tip.  I will stick to the country music bars next time.
Great great room and vibe.  Food is a little full but not bad.  A much more convenient option than Bluebird but it feels similar.  Very nice staff.  Great music!!'

Pretty cool place, a lot of good memorabilia and cool personal pieces. Learned some cool facts about a legend. $20 for a ticket not bad, but is what it is, not a amusement park. Worth the trip to say you did it, spend time to watch the Ragged Old Flag, pretty cool. Walking distance to everything.

So wife and I went on this boat trip and really enjoyed it. It wasn't 5 star food, but it was a fun night out. The weather was great. It was a chance to get out on the water. The show and food was good for what you are paying for. It's just about the experience. And we enjoyed it. 

The only thing I would add as a recommendation. Clean the outside of the boat a bit. A lot of insects and spider webs everywhere. The waiting landing needed a bit of pressure washing too. 

But again, I did enjoy our time and would bring family back when they come visit.
Get the big hit burger - you need to eat this one with your fork! Dig in don' t be shy there is always great music here!

The Johnny Cash Museum was so wonderful.  Learned such many things about JC that I didn't  know. The time seemed to stop when you're there. Be prepared to spend a few hours poring over the vast articles and music. If you want a nice afternoon getting to know the man in black this is the place to go.

I've had to move my review from 5-stars to 3-stars. I still love the food, but the last two times I've been I've waited over 60 minutes for my food, and both times the restaurant was nearly empty. On one of the occasions, some in my group waited over 80 minutes for their burgers. Until I hear that the speed of the service has picked up, I probably won't go back.

I went to The Listening Room Cafe tonight, and the food was awful--greasy nachos with fake cheese and no salsa, unimpressive mac and cheese, and the so-called "house-smoked seasonal vegetables" consisted of microwaved broccoli and carrots with a sickeningly sweet teriyaki sauce drizzled over them. It is 4 hours later and I am still feeling ill.
In a nutshell, best burgers, great atmosphere and wonderful management.  Will definitely be back often!

We want at 7pm on Saturday and everything was awesome. Very nice waiter, gave us some suggestions. He also turned cartoons on one of the tv's, just because we came with a toddler.

They took some time to cook the burgers which is ok. Especially because burgers came out just delicious. They tasted like real meat, properly cooked. Toppings were good too.
We will definitely come again.

Cool concept. Food and drink take a long time but it's tough taking 400 peoples orders and getting it all out at the same time.  Food was ok. The PBLT BLT with fried green tomatoes. Pimento am cheese on it was terrible. Way too much and it didn't make sense. The rest of the food just OK. prices were good though.

Want some good food and great music without all the hassle of getting into the Bluebird Cafe (not to knock it)? 

The listening room cafe has a large dining room and was really easy to get tickets to. 

There is free parking in their lot for customers ($10 for non-customers) and they let us park there about an hour before the show so we could hit Broadway.

They have a nice menu with lots of options. The pricing is a little high but portion sizes are good. The hot chicken is delicious, but even the mild will take your head off. 

The music is the real kicker. The talent was excellent and the show was all acoustic. 

Definitely a place to check out for a good, hassle-free evening.

You cannot visit Nashville, aka Music City, and NOT visit the Johnny Cash Museum. This was one of the highlights of my weeklong vacation to Tennessee with the wife, and although I had high expectations of this place, it absolutely surpassed them. An amazing museum dedicated to the Man in Black.
I love that you can peruse everything at your pace. There's so much to see and take in- handwritten letters and lyrics, pictures, outfits, instruments, gold records, personal items from his home, I really can't explain the amount of cool things there are to take in at this museum.
You could walk through in under 30  minutes if you're in a hurry, but to really take it all in, we took about an hour. It's absolutely worth the price of admission, and ANY music fan would appreciate the museum, but if you're a fan of Johnny Cash it's a MUST-DO. I think kids would enjoy it, although most older folks probably have more of an appreciation for what's there, but the kids could still have fun. The store is also very cool, lots of awesome t-shirts, mugs, etc for sale, I could've spent a few hundred bucks there for sure.
This museum is a short walk from Broadway- if you're doing a day in Nashville, I think this is one of the must-do's. Totally worth the price of admission, it's an amazing look at history and life of one of the greatest musicians to ever live. No cheese, no tourist trap, just a great collection of items from Johnny Cash's life. So glad I went and I recommend you go to!

Must see. Pay the money. It's worth it. 45 to 60 minutes. Great stuff. A lot of reading but it's worth it. We were a little hesitant at first because when we first came in the museum there were a lot of people and they were all bunched together but it thinned out pretty quickly. Definitely worth making the time for to learn about one of country's most influential singers.

It actually wasn't what I expected. Nice to be in the music district of Nashville & all, but the place itself and the food left a lot to be desired. The staff was friendly at least and there was cool signage to take pics.

We were so excited to have brunch here!  And then we went in.  Can you say blah?  There is nothing nothing nothing appealing about this place.  The hostess and people working there seem so  miserable. Are they overworked? Short staffed? I dont know but honestly customers should never feel like they're intruding.  Waited 15 minutes for a table and 3/4 of the place was empty.  Stood at the bar for nearly 10 minutes before the bartender asked if we would like something.  And there were empty seats at the bar IT WAS NOT BUSY! It's a big empty room with tables, no deco except for the giant sign telling everyone to be quiet and respectful of the entertainment?!?  Cmon now, are you paying me to eat here or vice versa?  And the singers?  I'd rather go to anyplace on Broadway for better service, food, drink and entertainment and NOT told to be quiet! friendly employees! Food was marginal.  Patio is 'dog friendly?'  What?  Last thing I want to to be eating and have a dog at the next table!  Left all 3 of my dogs at home, cause they don't belong at a restaurant, maybe I'll bring all of them next time..  Do yourself a favor don't waste your time, the only good thing they have here is valet parking.  Sorry listening room, you gotta try harder you're fading fast.

The music was great, food mediocre. On top of the $7 entrance fee per person they overcharged us for 1 drink I did not receive and they charged a 21% gratuity for a party of 6.....I found it absurd that the 21% was after an additional $20 + in taxes. When I return to Nashville I will come back but only come for drinks. I have never heard of gratuity after tax, especially for poor service and cold food.
It's was fun, but a little cheesy. Good place to go if you want to beat the crowd for a bit.
Ended up walking out. Had high hopes but sat there for over 15 minutes and no service. Upstairs and patio closed. Bummer
Went before a New Years Eve concert and thoroughly enjoyed it. Had to leave before I started spending too much in the gift shop.

Consider yourself warned!!  Don't waste your time!!  I don't usually leave bad reviews only positive ones, but our experience here was just that bad and I had to say something. We were one of two tables that were occupied in the place at 11:30AM.  Now I know why.  The service was the absolute worst and the food was just ok.  After finally waiting an eternity for someone to take our food order and for it to be prepared, we heard the cool yell order up.  We waited. The waiter went over and stood by our food and texted. We waited. He texted. We waited. He texted. He saw us just sitting there staring at him.  And he went back to texting.  I'm a polite guy but I was angry at this point.  I know how tough running a business is and I try to eat local.  I hope the owner reads this post, and gets his employees up to par. I'll never know because I won't be back.  $15 for a burger, fries, and drink before tip.  It was ok, but a burger for that price should be all that and more in my opinion.
Great Saturday brunch! We went to celebrate a bday and had mimosas and brunch. The food was good but the artists are the best! They get true raw talent. Cool atmosphere too.

As a first time visitor to Nashville, this place came recommended, so we made a reservation. The songwriters who performed were pretty darn good. I wish that I could say the same for the food. I ordered the turkey sandwich, which wasn't terrible, but it was cold & the bread was mushy. My husband ordered the pot roast, which consisted of a tablespoon of beef au jus, no vegetables,  & dry baked Mac & Cheese. None of which was very warm. Of course we came to listen to music, but the deal is you pay to enter, & you must spend at lease $15 per person on whatever, or simply pay the additional money at the end w/o eating or drinking. Since we don't drink, we chose from their menu.

For overall Nashville atmosphere and live music this place is awesome. The singers were outstanding, the food was really good, and the drinks pretty good as well. Overall definitely a cool place to visit. If you are coming with a big party lookout because this place gets packed! Apparently you can try braving the crowd or buy tickets for $5 a day or so early in order to confirm your seat. Overall a really cool place to come and try out. So turns out after eating and drinking here it is even more grand than I thought. It is basically the musical straight version of Nashville's / NYC's version of 58 below. Absolutely beautiful music.

Great museum to check out if you are visiting Nashville and a Johnny Cash fan. They have lots of his memorabilia and the overall museum is a great glimpse of his life. The only downside was parking, just know that your going to have to pay and probably walk.

I'm always excited to try new local businesses and 360 Burger caught my eye a few weeks ago when I drove by and they were setting up their restaurant. I really didn't know what to expect but I was pleasantly surprised. The inside of the restaurant has a classy but relaxed feel. I tried the 360 burger and it was wonderful! The sweet potato fries were some of the best I've had. My girlfriend got a turkey burger and said it was one of the best she's ever tasted. Our waiter, Justin, did a tremendous job! I will definitely be going back, and going back soon. This is a wonderful addition to Antioch!
Great place for lunch, dinner or a drink after work.  Burgers are great and make sure to try the turkey burger!  I eat at 360 at least 3 times a week.

My parents came to town for Xmas so I bought us all tickets on Christmas Eve day so we would have something fun to do. The weather was terrible so that meant walking around the boat in freezing rain wasn't the best, I have to imagine this would be really nice on a sunny, warm day. The food was typical banquet style. The best part was the apple cake that probably wasn't even made on the property. I requested the chicken and it came with potatoes and a few green beans. Nothing I'd call delicious cuisine. The show itself was decent, with some talented performers. It was entertaining although it was hard to see from my vantage point behind a giant pole. This is a decent time, but I'm not sure it was worth the money.

Finally got to try 360 Burger tonight, it was great. The experience was started with Justin and his welcoming personality, he even helped carry out (we got to go) my burgers and drinks because I was carrying my one year old. The burgers were amazing. They tasted like the best homemade burgers I've ever had. Patties were seasoned very well and it had a great smokey flavor. I got the slippery pig and my wife got the Ol' Smokey (she loved hers as well). We will be back for sure and next time we'll eat in, the inside was very welcoming and had a small stage for live music...sounds like fun! Again though Justin did a great job, I always appreciate excellent customer service and he was great.
Food was excellent and of course the music was top notch. Amazing to hear the songwriters sing their own songs!

This place was the pits.  After waiting for 15 minutes for them to give me the drink I already paid for, some guy vomited next to me.  

The bar tender seemed more concerned with validating my id (I'm 31) then actually serving us.  We were in and out in 1 drink.

I would give this place zero stars if possible.  They were out of miller lite, Coors light, pretzel,  and shrimp fritters.  My 6 year old says well what do you have and it is now known as the place that is out of everything.  We settled on a yuengling and it was warm.  Do not waste your time or money here.

We've been to DBWR twice to eat, once for brunch and the other for dinner. I'm glad we tried the brunch first because if we would've had dinner first we probably wouldn't have gone back. 

The brunch menu isn't large but the options were tasty. There were 4 of us. We ordered 2 Bloody Marys and 2 Mimosas. They had run out of OJ for the mimosas and asked if pineapple juice would be ok to sub or if we wanted a different drink. We opted for the pineapple juice sub and it wasn't bad. For food we ordered 2 breakfast sandwiches, the chicken and waffles and breakfast burrito. ALL of the food was delicious. We couldn't get enough. Will definitely go back for brunch. 

Fast forward to the weekend after the 4th of July we decided to try dinner. We had to find our own seat which was challenging. We ended up on the 2nd floor. The booth had a drip above it probably from the AC being on overload from the hot temps. I'm not sure how our waitress was able to get our order right as it was so loud but she did and was awesome. There was 4 of us again. We ordered the pretzel and beer cheese dip for an appetizer and the fish and chips, mac and cheese, turkey melt and mushroom burger for our main courses. None of us were super thrilled with the food. I only had half of my sandwich. My fiance said Jason Aldean's fish and chips were way better. The mac and cheese was ok, nothing special as well as the burger. I will say that the garlic fries were delicious and I ordered a J.I.M.B.O. to drink which was sweet but good. The pretzel had a little too much seasoning but was overall good. The beer cheese it came with was amazing. Beers at DBWR are cheaper by $1-$2 compared to some other bars on Broadway. 

Overall a fun bar with a good vibe.
Very cool! Some of the figures legit looked like real people. We did think that it would be a bit bigger but the rooms were very cool. Convenient location inside the mall next to the Grand Ole Opry.

Bought a living social deal to use while we were on vacation in Nashville.  First off.. figured the reason they were on living social... construction blocked the parking lot and the front entrance making it really hard to get to. They have a giant banner on the side of there building, printed on their door, and printed on their menus that Brunch was served Saturday and Sunday from 10 am to 3 pm. We arrived Saturday at 10 am. Was seated and ordered drinks. Then we were told that the kitchen didnt opened until 11 am. ... seriously then why does the giant banner on the side of your building say 10am?????
We are Johnny Cash fans and we still learned a lot. There was lots of music to listen to, videos to watch and some fascinating objects from his life.
This was a fun museum. It isn't organized particularly well but the memorabilia and extensive collection is great. Would recommend to anyone going to visit Nashville
Family and I had a great time. The guys that played were funny and talented. The only draw back was trying to find the place.

This is Johnny Cash Heaven!  On our way home from Florida to Buffalo NY we took a detour to Nashville just to visit this museum.  It was even better than expected and was well worth the trip!  There's a lot I could say about it but wouldn't do the experience justice.  Trust me when I say if you are a Johnny Cash fan or just like music in general, don't miss this!
Great live entertainment! Wish there was more room for dancing, though. The pianists get better as the night goes on. They also can play multiple instruments. What talent!

Entirely new location (make sure you Uber to the right address), loved everything about it. I mean it as a compliment when I say the worst thing was a wobbly table.  The musicians were real and talented with captivating back stories.  The night we went featured songwriters telling the stories of, and singing, major hits they've silently built.  It was broadening to hear the original guitar+voice, original version of so many amazing songs both famous and soon to be.  I 100% recommend getting ticket and showing up early.

Great place to listen to amazing music.  Unpretentious!  It is a treat to see and hear the musicians and then you never know who might be in the audience that will just go up and jam on stage with the performers.  My daughter and I love all kinds of music and this was a wonderful venue to visit in Nashville!
go for drinks and music!

If singer/song writers are your thing, this is a must place to go.  And it's downtown.
The food is good and the performers are excellent.

The General is a good attraction for bringing guests from out of town to.  I personally don't care for country music, so Nashville is not my favorite destination.  I can get by with the music because they put on a fairly entertaining show.  The food however, is pretty ruff.  For the price of the tickets a higher quality meal should be provided.

This place is a really neat concept. It wasn't as busy as some of the other spots nearby, but we did go in the early evening and it was still about a third full. I think it'd be best to come here late in the evening when it's busier. Still, we saved on cover which they start charging later in the evening.  The pianists are pretty talented and they sang everything anyone threw at them. We didn't try the food here, but the drinks were reasonably priced.

Such an awesome place to hear raw talent. Some long lines but worth the wait. We visited from NYC, you can't see musicianship like this up there. Nice beer selection and good drinks. Buy your tickets in advance to make sure you get a seat! Highly recommend to country fans.
I'm not sure about the actual museum because I only stop in for the coffee. The coffee is worth a review. Amazing, but I've always been a Bongo Java fan. Staff is a bit rude, but it's worth it.

I had some friends up on stage this weekend, so I took my first trip to lower broadway to check out the scene. Swinging Doors is a fun place - not as rowdy as a lot of the other places in the area seemed - likely due to the fact that it is (slightly) off of the strip.

Cool, laid-back vibe, good specials on drinks, and decent drunk food.

I like a place with such a diverse age grouping as you find here. It is clear that a lot of locals hang out at this bar, though heavy waves of tourists did come and go.

I am sure that a lot of the fun of this place depends on the band, but from what I hear the music here is some of the better stuff in town because while it isn't only acoustic, it isn't just about getting the "loud crowd" in the doors. These people have to actually be able to sing.

Good place to grab dinner & drinks while enjoying local live music. The night we went featured all women singer/songwriters who looked to be ages 17-25. Talented group of lovely ladies. Dinner was good. Hot chicken, chicken dishes, etc.Pretty standard menu. I will add, I ordered one of their house fave sides and didn't love it. The manager replaced it with no fuss, making it clear, they care about your business. Go show em some love and enjoy a good show. And for the love, stop talking while the folks perform! It's called the listening room, not the talking place for a reason. We sat next to a large party who came right before the show started, so they had to order, etc all while it was going on. Come early, get your order in, chat it up, then sit back and enjoy the music. Easily would have given 5 stars if the venue had reminded folks to listen more, talk less while performers were on stage.

We absolutely loved hearing the music writer/performers and the intimate setting. If the food were better it would knock this place out of the park. We thought the chicken was dry and the food overall lacked pazzaz. Invest in a great chef and a creative menu !!

Very good experiance. I am glad I made this one of my stops while in Nashville. Although it's a smaller museum it's very well layed out. I am not a Cash fan and don't know much about his music but I enjoyed looking at all the artifacts and reading about his life. It is a pretty small space but well worth it.

I'll preface this review with the fact that I've been to the restaurant both before and after the new management. 

Both times I visited, I had an excellent burger. More recently I ordered chicken, but was served a burger and I didn't say anything to the waitress (because, honestly... who gets chicken instead of a burger. It was a bad judgement call to begin with). 

Shortly after the new management took over, service was a little choppy, you could tell they were still working out the kinks, but to compensate gave us gift cards to return and offered really cheap craft beers. Management truly cares about the diners' experience.

I absolutely love the atmosphere of this restaurant. It's a fun place for some chill live music on this side of town.

Excellent tribute to the great musician Johnny Cash. Lots of items from his life.  Make sure you watch the video at the exit. My wife and I really enjoyed visiting this museum as we are both Johnny and June fans. We even met Johnny Cash's younger sister Joanne who happened to be visiting while we were there! Visit this museum while in downtown Nashville. Not a huge museum but you can spend hours there checking out all the exhibits.

I was very unsure about eating hear after reading the reviews, but I was too tired to drive far. This place was about 2 minutes from the hotel so I decided to give it a shot. Got the slippery pig with waffle fries. The food was good, the service was good, and the food came out in about 10 minutes for my to go order. Great place to pick up a quick bite for a guy here on business.

Happy Hour: Monday - Friday: 4PM to 7PM
2-for-1 draft beers, $1 off all liquor and half price sandwiches!

So, I just moved to Antioch not a fan of none of the corporately owned restaurants who would have thought a locally owned restaurant that serves grass-fed beef...EXCEPTIONAL!!!..I normally have to travel to Five Points, Belmont, or Germantown to get some good food..The service was great along with the food...sweet potato fries my fave and were great..I ordered the peach cobbler as well so good don't have anything bad to say this is definitely a hidden treasure in Antioch..I'm hoping more locally owned restaurants will venture out in this area..

Check your tickets here people: 10 + 10 does not equal 22...I don't remember the exact total on our bill but at the end, it was 2 bucks more than what the food and tax added up to be. I'm just saying, if they do this to every check, they're making more money every night because people don't look at their bills...

The service here is excellent though and they were super understanding and fixed our bill (even though there was never a real explanation). In fact, the whole night our waiter was delightful. The food was typical bar food. The chicken on my salad was burned, I just tasted charcoal the whole time, and my husbands fish tacos were somehow bland and super peppery at the same time...But, the fried ravioli was delicious. 

It was a great atmosphere for dinner and entertainment, we'll be back again!

My husband and I stopped in on Sunday for some drinks and to listen to Autumn Rose (group) sing on stage. This place is nice and small so  listening to music from anywhere in this bar is not a problem. We definitely enjoyed ourselves here...very laid back atmosphere. 

Food was what you would expect from a bar...fried. Drinks were VERY good! I ordered a Strawberry Moonshine cocktail and it was tasty. The bartender was very friendly which is always appreciated.
This bar is so much fun. Live music and reasonably priced beer. We had a blast. Can't wait to come back. This place is worth the trip. Stop by, you won't be disappointed.

Nice saloon with killer music.   
Nice selection of moonshine and beer. 
Nice little place to hang with friends

Bring a date or a whole crew

Best sound system in town. Band sounds crisp and the bass is deep.  Perfect drum mic set up

My first time to 360 Burger will unfortunately be my last time. I had been given a free meal promo card to try them out and so I finally did.  The Turkey Bacon Club that I got (which, ironically, is the most expensive sandwich at a little over $9.00) was not $9.00 quality.  After eating about 3 bites, I realized that the bacon was not cooked properly and not crispy at all.  The "fresh turkey" was fresh out of the Oscar Meyer luncheon meat package alright--Publix and Kroger Delis have tastier turkey. It certainly wasn't quality and worthy of shelling out almost $10.00.   And the bread wasn't thick texas toast, but seemed more like sandwich bread and was very small.  I was very disappointed,  to say the least.  Had I paid for this meal, I would have probably asked for my money back.  I'm totally grossed-out and nauseated from the sheer thought that I consumed semi-cooked pork.  The burgers may be good as some of you say, but I will never find out due to this experience here--it has not left the best impression on me.
Best place in Nashville to watch songwriters sing their hits. Amazing food. Great sound and people, from the chefs to the wait staff to the bartenders to the owner.

This was the best part of my trip to Nashville. We wanted something that was authentic and different from all the cover bands and bars on Broadway. LRC was a comfortable environment, had the most incredible performers we saw our whole trip, and had a great selection of drinks at the bar. It was so great we came back the very next night and stayed for both sets. While I agree that the food needs some work with their serving times, if you are coming here for the food you are doing it wrong. 

Come here for the music, ambiance, and drinks and just be thankful that there is also food.
Pretty cool place to see while in Nashville. My kids 5-8 enjoyed going threw checking out what they wore & listening to music.
Great museum for any Cash fan. I think it's a little pricey, but you are in downtown Nashville. I would definitely recommend it to any Cash fan.

So cool and an awesome tribute to a great artist.

I've always liked Johnny Cash but don't know his music that well, besides the more famous songs like Ring of Fire, Folsom Prison, Walk the Line etc. I've seen the Joaquin Phoenix/Reese Witherspoon Carter/Cash interpretations in the Walk the Line film and they're excellent.

I don't really like museums much, just as I don't really like reading books much although I enjoy biographies. This museum is like a Cash biography.  

This museum allows you to become familiar with Cash's music decade by decade with listening stations dedicated to the 50s, 60s, 70s, 80s, 90s and 00s. What an interesting performer! He was exceptionally talented and profound with his messages. What's also great about this is that it makes me wish I'd had the chance to know him. And June.

I enjoyed the film too - and for once I didn't fall asleep watching it. It's become a habit of mine.

Cash fan or not, it's worth a look.
What a great place! The staff is all friendly and the music is AMAZING! If you enjoy live original music this is the place for you!

Awesome time going through the Johnny Cash museum. Went in not knowing too much about him and came out as an expert. Loved learning his history and seeing all the success he had in his life. They even had a small display for the movie with Joaquin Phoenix and Reese Witherspoon. (Which is a great movie) we finished the day taking a greenscreen shot with Johnny Cash!

The best museum I have ever been to.  However I am a huge Johnny Cash fan and I may be a bit biased. I took my Dad when he was in town and he really enjoyed the museum as well.   Personally I enjoyed the last section of the museum where they show some of Cash's interests such as photography and art.  They also had an incredible collection of handwritten lyrics and notes to June.  It was a beautiful homage to the Man in Black.  Would recommend to anyone who has even the slightest interest in Mr. Cash.

My sister is living in Nashville. We were looking for something relaxing but fun to do on a Monday night. I learned about some live music at the listening room cafe. Soo glad we swung by there. Delicious food, great location and excellent talent!
Boat is cool...scenery cooler....wait staff horrible. Food mediocre. Couldn't understand our waiter and impossible to get a drink.
Spent a weekend in Nashville (first time) from NYC and had to stop by the Johnny Cash Museum.  I really enjoyed seeing all of the legends artifacts and personal items chronicled

I imagine that a true of Johnny Cash fan would love it and be in heaven.  I kinda knew him and his music and wanted to use this place to learn more.  
Someone putting the place together really loved Johnny Cash.  There is lots and lots of memorabilia.  The short film that highlighted his film and TV work was really well done. 
I found it to be a little disorganized.  I was hoping for a detailed time-line where I could see the storylines of his life spelled out.  It seemed there were several different time lines and I found myself having to run back-and-forth to get the picture.

One of my favorite spots in Nashville! 
The music is so good, all the pianist , singers are so good, this is my Nashville happy place ! 
Drinks are good too!

Lost my ID came with legitimate document a from homeland of security and my veterans affairs ID card to verify my name. The owner refused to let me in and the. Got mad when I asked him not to touch me.. To veterans everywhere please do not go to blue bar the owner does not appreciate your service. The owner does not honor documents from homeland security.. And was mad because I asked him to respect my boundaries.. What I should be doing is filing a sexual harassment suit against him.. Definitely will not be returning used to be my favorite bar that I recommend to everyone .. No more would rather go to rebar....

Typical broadway bar with multiple levels. A band is playing on the first floor and was pretty packed. Found it a bit disappointing that the name has "whiskey" in it but they don't carry any local TN whiskeys besides Jack Daniels. The highlight was the rooftop. It is a nice place to hang out and get a view. Drinks are about the same price as the rest of the broadway strip.
Had a lot of fun here, at lest the music is not so extremely loud compare to some of the others. Small but we liked it much

This place is fun! It's one block off strip. It's my new favorite place in Nashville. We went back a few times this weekend. One of our times we ordered food. We both had burgers  - one with tots and one with fries. EXCELLENT food! I will definitely be back. Great atmosphere and great food.

Looks like the place would be fun for music. Sound system is nice, and ambiance was great. Food was such a disappointment, I ordered the veggie frittata. It said chefs seasonal choice, diced tomatoes, hidden jalapeños and two chives.

Very unorganized. 1st off, we set it up with a tour co. $240 for 2 people. They told us to go to Grey Line Tours at 6:00pm. We sat there until 6:30 then the shuttle shows up. I ask the driver for my tickets & I'll follow you there. Finally got the the boat at 6:45 pm. Nobody told us it started at 6:00. Food was cold. Chicken was dry. Total rip off. The only good part was the last hour when the band played. We will never do that again. Not even when I turn 80 like everyone else on there. 
Oh did I say TOTAL RIP OFF...

Alright...I've been here twice now. 
Here was my first impression. 
For the part of town it's in, it stands out as a nicer burger spot, with live music and good beer. But if it were to be in east Nashville, 12 south, or any of the "foodier" parts of town, I don't think it would've done well. It was empty at dinner time when we went as well.. they have some unique burgers and sandwiches, and my burger was okay, but overly salty..... 

But I came back. And I am glad I did. Our server's name was Justin and he was maybe the best server I've ever had. Incredibly personable, friendly, helpful, and not too pushy. He was happy to help us look through the menu and give us his suggestions. He suggested the ol smoky, and add a fried egg. So I did. And it was amazing! Messy, but great!
The fries were nice and thick cut, and beer selection was good. 
I'm really glad I came back. I live nearby and can see myself coming here more frequently now. Thanks for turning this place 180 Justin! Er...360...idk. Thanks for making my 2nd time here memorable! You're the man!

Just go, it's totally worth it. 
My highlight was when I leaned that Johnny Cash was the voice of the coyote spirit guide when Homer Simpson got high in the desert.....

Visiting the Johnny Cash Museum was a highlight of our Nashville trip. The entire experience was personal and meaningful. It was evident from the moment we walked in the door that the entire staff cared deeply about the museum and the portrayal it had of Johnny's life. We got our tickets on Groupon for a great price which was an added bonus as well. I would not skip this while in town! It will open your eyes to an entirely new side of Johnny Cash and you likely will be listening to his music for weeks to come because of it.

It gets four stars because of the music, definitely not the food (two stars).
We went for brunch because of the music so it was worth it and we are going back.


Ok so we came back on a Monday to hear the Song Suffragettes play. Female singer songwriters coming together playing their own songs. amazing! Do not miss it. 6pm on Mondays.

Just ate at 360 burger for the first time. We went there because a friend said the food was pretty good and they had a great beer selection. They do have a great beer selection. We usually have to go to east Nashville to get good beer. We got the mushroom and Swiss burger and the BBQ bacon burger medium. They both came out well and they fries we barely warm. They were great about taking them back and re cooking new burgers for us. They did leave us with the cold fries. The second time around the burgers were a little less cooked. Too bad the beef is over seasoned. So, would we go back? We would for a beer. We'll eat before we get there.

Walked past this museum a few times in past visits and decided to give a look this time. Was pleasantly surprised with all the exhibits. Not an avid fan of Johnny Cash, visiting his museum gave me a newfound respect for him and all his accomplishments. Would recommend if you are in town. Don't forget to use your AAA discount.
Dierks, dude, your food is horrible. Your service is horrible. The location is the only thing you have going for you.

We came into this bar during the afternoon on Friday, June 22nd, to listen to music and have a drink.  It wasn't extremely busy.  I had to use the restroom downstairs and there was only one restroom each for the women and men.  While I was in the restroom, some mean and/or drunk person was yelling at the restroom to get out because they had to use it.  So I hurried out and accidentally left my expensive Maui Jim sunglasses sitting on a stand/cabinet.  Immediately after, I realized I forgot them and turned around to go back to get them and they were gone.  I went to each bar downstairs and asked the bartenders if anyone turned them in and of course, they didn't.  The bartenders weren't very friendly and didn't seem to care.  So someone decided not to be honest and steal them and keep the sunglasses for themselves.  Very disappointed with some people these days. Very dishonest.   The point is--why does such a large bar/restaurant only have one restroom each with this many people that come through.  This is unacceptable and very poor planning on the part of the builder/management.  If we ever come back to Nashville, I'm not sure I would go to this bar again.  There are much better choices down there to go to.  I did send an e-mail through your website that same day to see if anyone turned them in but I didn't hear back from them until June 25th.  I like Dierks Bentley's music but not a fan of his bar/restaurant.

Damn it is hard for me to write a less than stellar review of this venue. I have been a patron since 3 locations ago in Cummins Station, I have performed on their stages and listened to others perform my songs, it's always been a good time. Their previous location on 2nd Ave was one of my favorite places to hear live music, eat great food and drink delicious cocktails. I am not sure why they had to move, I expect either the rent went up or the building is being replaced with another high rise. The new Nashville. The previous room was big and square; even at the back tables you had centralized sound and view. The new room is shallow and wide. 

Today was the first time I visited the new location on 4th. Looked promising from the outside, but the interior is cold and sterile, and while it was mostly empty, I expect people sitting at the far side tables would not have an optimal listening/viewing experience. Friends of mine were playing, and it was my first time having brunch at TLR but their regular offerings are so delish I didn't expect a problem.

Well...muchos problemos. Starting with service, which was virtually non-existent. Took forever to flag down a server and even get a menu, and the place was nearly empty. The offerings were limited. What my friend and I received was barely edible and personally my own breakfast at home would have been preferable. Coffee served in a paper cup at a sit down restaurant that actually owns real dishes. Creamer served in a plastic cup to be dumped into the other cup. The appetizingly described potato hash on the menu, promising a fresh hash of potatoes, peppers and onions underneath two sunny side eggs, was ore-ida frozen home fries that tasted like they were baked hours ago - overcooked, cold, hard. The eggs on top were virtually snotty, whites barely hardened, and served ice cold. Requested tabasco served in yet another plastic cup that I waited 10 minutes for as my breakfast got colder. I had to get up and ask for it at the bar when it didn't come. My friend's fried green tomato BLT was gummy, bacon flabby, toast cold and hard, french fries also cold and crispy as cheetos. Not a good kind of crispy. We would have sent it all back but it took forever to get any service at all and we were starving at that point.

Brunch just felt like an afterthought, and after speaking to some of my friends at other tables who had also just eaten, it seems everyone agreed.

Didn't drink today but looking around, the drinks did look good and they have two for one bloodys and mimosas. Next time I will just sit at the bar and drink my brunch. TLR does feature some of the best performing songwriters in Nashville and the sound system is just as awesome as ever. I love you guys, and I hope dinner service at the new location will be just as amazing as it has always been on 2nd Ave, but brunch needs serious work. Too many other options in this foodie town.
Great and friendly service.  Dana is the best bartender.  Excellent food, reasonable drink prices, and great music!

Get place for a night of music. Even a standing room only event was fun. The bar-b-que was great, yes a little pricy. People should expect to pay for great food, especially when it comes with music on the side. I will be back.

The worst experience I've had at a restaurant! Sat at the table for 20 minutes before anyone bothered to come over. Then waited another 30 minutes just to get coffee that tasted worse than airplane coffee. Food took another 45 minutes to get to us as the sever we were supposed to have already brought food and drinks to a table that sat down 30 minutes after we got here. I would never come here again and would never suggest it to anyone else. Not to mention how awful the food was. DO NOT COME HERE!!!

We loved this museum!  It's very well done with videos, audio and very interesting facts about all things Johnny Cash. The staff was more than helpful with our group of 16 with a group rate and an appointment for entry with no wait! Thanks for a great experience!
Great venue to listen to music, I don't have much to say except I really had a great time and I wish I could go one more time.

A must see! Even if you aren't a fan of Johnny Cash I recommend visiting the museum. It is on the smaller side and does get busy. You enter from one room and exit right into the gift shop. There is a small cafe area near the front entrance.

Amazing, high energy music and entertainment.  Tons of tables and easy access to two bars as well as frequent table service.  Drinks reasonably priced and served quickly.  Music taken by request - how is it possible they know so many songs?? Our requests were never played but we heard many other great renditions of country, R&B, pop, and so much more.  Most impressive when bar staff participated in dances or even singing/performing.  Awesome experience!

Smaller then you'd expect, but great atmosphere. We say Baylor and friends (who turned out to include hall of fame songwriter!) and had a grand old time. The food was ok... the drinks were great!! I'd go back in a heartbeat.

If you're in Nashville looking to have a great time this place is a must! Was visiting and came here on a Friday night. It was a blast. There was a great vibe & the artists were amazing! I'm not sure if we just got lucky with the artists/songwriters but they were very entertaining. The food & drinks were nothing special, but the ambiance and live music are what made it such a unique experience.

I only visited the storefront of the Johnny Cash Museum, but the items that they were offering is a must-see for any diehard fan of the man in black. Lots of music offerings, shirts, and wall decor that would be amazing for any fan.

GREAT pulled pork, friendly staff, excellent greeter, and good prices too! The band was friendly and played one of my requests. This place is usually not too crowded. Great place to go before you do the big time bars on Broadway or go souvenir shopping.

Great music venue with pretty good food.  I think this is one of the best sounding rooms in town.  I usually come with a specific person to see in mind.  For me, eating at a music venue is a mixed benefit - I'd rather just drink and listen.  But if it's dinner time, the food is good.  It is much better than other so-called "cafe's: that offer bad frozen pizza for their $10 food minimum.
