You may have to pay a cover for some acts, but I don't mind that.  They also offer valet parking.

Burgers were good, the fried pickles were ok, but the live music was waaay too loud for such a small space. The seating and the ordering situation were kind of confusing as they did not have a hostess.

DO NoT!!!!! Come here!!! We just gave a $20 tip to the band for the next song on a slow Sunday and the bored bouncer kicked us out.  I've never seen this out, and I can not can not wait till he is fired

And if he remains i am going to be so heated because I come back often. What a dick with a power trip
Go for the music, but I would have dinner elsewhere. The food just wasn't that good. However, we enjoyed the songwriters/musicians! Great experience. Glad we went!

Would be great if they had a/c and you could
Actually hear the band.  We came for the band because we have heard them play many times and love them. But the sound was terrible. Also, no table service after 11?   Hopefully they try harder next time.
Got kicked out because one of the regulars decided to get in my face. All the men's bathrooms were backed up and over flowing as well. Don't waste your time.
The queso fries are delicious. They messed up my order but the burger I had was so good I didn't want to complain about it ima just go back and order what I wanted lol.

Well executed. Spacious. So much to read and look at. Overwhelms the Cash senses!
Friend and I got here as soon as they opened.  Best way to see it without having to push people out of the way.

If you're a Cash fan, this is the ultimate experience.. Listening to the music, watching the videos, seeing his concert attire..  thoroughly warmed my heart.

Get there early, before the masses.  Enjoy a moment alone with Johnny Cash.  Best way to enjoy this exhibit.

Incredible tribute to Johnny Cash. Don't miss the listening station where you can him hear the same recording in all formats...from the 45 to the cassette to digital. So many personal effects, I really feel like I knew the man. Don't miss this museum, it's a must for any trip to Nashville!

Loved this place! Hung out on Friday afternoon for drinks and live music and returned on Saturday morning for brunch. Rhonda took care of us both times and was fantastic! Great food, great bands and great atmosphere!

I really enjoyed the music. As far as the food. The humus was amazing. The salad with goat cheese, strawberries and pecans was weak. Pretty much all lettuce. Found a few pecans and cheese sitting at the bottom.
Good selection of craft beer, helpful bartender. Gotta try the TLR Stack, house made chips with smoked pork and bbq sauce.

A great place to come when in Nashville to get the  true country music experience  at a reasonable price - probably one of the only places you might be able to get away hearing live with kids (I paced my 9-month old in back while sipping a Cornoa).  The music / arteeests were phenominal - many of them are up and coming.  It's $7 to get through the door + another $10 minimum you are required to place in food orders.  Be READY when your server arrives to take your order early on.  Being that there's that $10 minimum regardless whether you order or not, there didn't seem like a ton of motivation to come back when we weren't ready (or patience).  If they had explained that minimum to us at the time of ticket purchase,  I think we would have been ready. Aside from that detail/misunderstanding - this was a lot of fun and we were glad we went!  

P.S. 
- When we were there, they had showings on a Saturday night both at 4 and 6 P.M.
- There's a complimentary valet parking with ticket
- They ask that you keep conversation quiet / to a respectful level for the artists

We went in last night and had the best time! It was such an amazing night with talented musicians and an amazing bartender. I haven't been to a bar with such great service in a very long time. Try the deep fried cheese curds! I'll be dreaming of those when I get back to Canada!

Bucket list stuff. What a great tribute to the man in black. The back corner looping the Hurt video may bring you to tears. The gift shop is way overpriced but you don't have to buy. Great place if your a fan.

If there is any problem with Madame Tussauds in Nashville it is this - nothing but Southern stuff. 

Yes, I DO understand that I was in Tennessee, so I did expect much of the exhibit to have southern something or another, but beyond some very few things the museum did not seem to have anything beyond southern artists.  

That being said it was fine for what it is.  It probably would have been more fun/entertaining had I taken the tour with another person (I went solo), but for the cheap cost I got off of the website I certainly can't be overly critical.
They have champagne, wine (for wine girls in a beer town) and tv's for girls who love their sports.
360 burger is fantastically awesome.  Great specials and happy hour. You've got to try it once...you'll love it.
3rd time here and the pianists sure know how to work a crowd. Freaking awesome with a dat, but tough to pick up chicks. Just sayin.

Their happy includes 2 4 1 all drafts which includes Lagunitas IPA! The service however was another story, it took 30 mins to get my beer and they were not busy but on the flip side the burger was one of the best I've had

Being from out of town I was so happy to find this gem of a bar in Nashville. It's not on the main street of Broadway, but the performers that they have are amazing! Both nights that I went there I saw Nick Smith, and I highly recommend people go check him out. He will definitely be the next big thing! He played current and old country hits and had the whole bar singing along with him. Such a great entertainer! I will definitely be back on my next trip to Nashville :)

Amazing Johnny Cash museum! I had been to Graceland a few days earlier and can say this museum is much more interesting to me because the displays were on point about Mr. Cash's music and life. We took our time and spent a couple of hours. I really should have spent more time watching the iPad videos. Overall a great place, we also went upstairs and checked out the Patsy Cline museum, a much smaller place but fun.

This is my FAVORITE music venue in town. I managed to make it to two shows during my weeklong visit. On our first visit, we had Priscilla as our waitress. She is AMAZING. She personalized our visit. Giving us recommendations as to what to order, and made us feel incredibly welcome. She gave us incredible recommendations for places we need to see in town too. When we came back for our second show a few nights later, we knew we had to request to sit in her section, and it was worth it! As someone looking into making the move to TN, she made me see how sweet and welcoming the city is, and I'm thrilled to be able to come back to The Listening Room as often as possible!
Nice collection of memorabilia from Johnnys early days forward.  I especially loved the theatre with old concert footage.  Don't miss this when in Nashville.

This is a cool little museum.  They have a TON of Johnny Cash memorabilia.  It's amazing actually just how much is here.  It is a great reminder of just how prolific, popular and loved Johnny Cash really was during his remarkably long music and acting career.  If you are even kind of a fan, it's worth a visit.  $18.95 to get in and walk around.
It was fun.   We had a couple of drinks and listened to music.   Wish the song writers had more "hits".  Only heard of one song.  Didn't eat so can't comment on that.

It was a pretty good value. $95 or whatever it was was a good deal for a dinner, boat ride and show.  Coming into Nashville at night with all the lights was the highlight. The show itself was a bit cheesy. The acoustics were not food and I couldn't hear about half the time when someone was talking on the microphone. There were some talented people in the show, but still cheesy. I'd rather spend $100 on a moderately priced dinner and a ticket to the Opry next time.
We had such a fun time here! We were in Nashville and decided we had to do a museum, it felt like a no brainer. Really cool array of personal items, videos, and detailed history of his life.

The three musicians were fantastic. However, the food and service were not.
Thet were out of their signature dish at 12:30 pm on a sat. thanksgiving weekend. My burger was overcooked and dry. 
 The fries were cold. My friend ordered the shrimp and grits, the grits tasted undercooked and service was slow. 
I will find another venue next time i am in town.
Across the street from our hotel. My friend knew someone playing here. Have been here for over 15 minutes and no one has taken our drink order yet. People who came in after us had drink orders taken.

Loved the food! The pretzel buns are delicious and they have awesome fries. Been here a couple of times and the second time the service was not that great. I think they need to select better people or really train them hard to give a better experience. 
The only thing that was really hard to swallow was the restaurant's smell. Both times we've been there it seems that there's something funky with the restrooms plumbing. It's a total turn off. But if you can tolerate it for a few minutes, you'll get use to it. Ha!

We could not get into the Bluebird Cafe...Happily we enjoyed this place. We went to a songwriter night mid-week. So did not expect to see STARS.  Getting in was smooth with prior paid. Show started on time. We saw American Idol performer Craig Lloyd Boyd...great voice and top entertainer. About four other songwriter/artists. Can't remember the food... but that it was better then we expected! We were there for the music.  We were staying downtown so this was a walk away.

Unless there's a performer you really want to watch there, I'd skip The Listening Room. It's a more intimate and spacious venue than your typical Nashville bar, but I don't think it's the only one that provides that kind of atmosphere. There's a cover charge to see each show, which is fine and understandable, and then you have to get at least $10-$15 worth of something, and it all comes out to being enough for four other venues in better locations of Nashville with better food. I got the beef brisket sliders, and they were just meh and came out lukewarm. I'm glad I got to enjoy the brilliance of Briar Cliff here, but I didn't really care for the actual venue.

This was easily the highlight of my visit to Nashville. General admission is $17, and it's worth every penny. 

it's not a very big museum, but it's full of stuff. There's stations to listen to his music, and there's a back room that shows a film about Cash and features his work. 

There's so many things on display. There's a ton of outfits, hats, and boots that he wore on TV or in concert. His gear from his time in the military is there, furniture from their home is there. There's hand written lyrics sheets and love letters and the awards he received. There's even a door from prison on display there. I love Johnny Cash, and it was awesome to get to see some of this stuff first hand.

I also really liked that there's no guide, so you can stroll and read at your leisure. I like the no-pressure situation. 

On the way out, there's also a gift shop. There's shirts, books, albums, jewelry, and all kinds of things boasting his picture or his lyrics. I ended up buying my girlfriend a bar of soap that smelled like mint called Aloe, I'm Johnny Splash, because two puns are better than one. 

There's also a cafe here. We didn't get a chance to pay it a visit, but I think it's pretty cool. If I was from the area, no doubt I'd hang out there more often. 

If you're a fan of Cash or of country and rock music, be sure to stop here next time you're in Nashville.

I was worried that this was a tourist trap, but it was pretty enjoyable. It's interesting in how it could be a story about just about anyone, and then it takes off into stardom. Also appreciate that they have a mini museum for Sun Records, so you can say you did that too. I think $15 would be a fairer price since it can all be seen in an hour. Also the Snoop Dogg cover of "Walk The Line" is horrid.

Went on this dinner cruise during a trip to Nashville and had a wonderful time! 

My boyfriend and I went on a Monday night and at first were a little worried because when we look around all we saw was really OLD people, we were the youngest ones there and we were over dressed compared to everyone else. 

Before entering the boat, there is a person there taking pictures and we were able to take one infront of the General Jackson which I thought was pretty cool. 

When we actually entered onto the ship everyone spread out and it became more intimate for us. We took tons of pictures, the sun was starting to set it was just wonderful. The river was absolutly beautiful and the staff was very welcoming when entering the ship. 

 I found a waiter and ordered a bottle of white wine for my table to be there when we were ready to be seated. About an hour we were outside and on the upper deck having cocktails and watching the band that was playing. On a loud speaker they told everyone to enter the main dining room for dinner.

The dining area was huge and looked very elegant! There was a large stage in the front with the curtain still up.  We shared the table with about 8 other people. This was nice because everyone was interacting with one another and we got to meet people from different places. 

When we got to our table our bottle of wine was warm, however, one of the servers realized that it was sitting there awhile and took it back and brought us a new one nice and cold. They poured us both glasses of wine and ice tea. They immediately brought us our salads and bread. I also noticed that there was a small menu on the table just in case you wanted to order more appetizers. The salad was very fresh and the dressing was very good. After salad was done they brought us dinner which was also very good but I think it could have been a little more hot. But this was understandable due to the fact there were tons of people to feed at one time. 

After dinner, we had about 30 mins to break away from the dinning area and they brought us to downtown Nashville where we were able to take even more pictures. The whole city lit up at night was just gorgeous and we went right under the bridge which was also lit up. When we went back into the dining area our dessert was already on the table. They forgot to bring my boyfriend and myself coffee and it was a pain to get them over to serve me. I also wanted to order Ammerato but before I had the chance to they have already walked away. 

During dessert the show started and it was excellent! They actually pulled my boyfriend on stage and made him do the funky chicken infront of everyone with the rest of the entertainment staff which was both hilarious and fun. We wound up having a great all together and is something you should do of you are visiting Nashville. 

The only complain I have is that the wait staff is very slow and rarely check up on you to see of you need anything and when they do come by the give you your food and leave quickly, if this is fix it definitely has the potential to reach 5 stars.
Awesome! Great folks! Great food! Stumbled on this joint and had a fantabulous time! Blake is a great bartender!
Groovy place. Good beer. Better food. Great service. Kinda busy, ya know, with this bomb ass burger and all.

GREAT BAR! Went there this past weekend and loved it! The moonshine, band, and bartenders were great. Even though the bar was packed, the bartenders were hustling trying to get everyone orders. 

The security guard was probably the nicest man I have ever met at the front door of the bar. He made great small talk and we complimented him on how nice and happy he was.Basically he said that since he is the first thing you see for Swinging Doors he wants to make sure you start off on a good note and start enjoying your time there before you even step in the door. 

All together it is a great bar to go too! Its a must see in Nashville!
Museum has a great amount of memorabilia to see and the videos were awesome. However, it was crowded when we went, certain sections were really warm and we found it hard to move around.

Antioch's little secret!!! One of my favorite craft burger places in the Nashville area. I'm so in love with the PB&J burger, and I ask them to add some jalapenos (watch it, they're HOT) to kick it up. SO. GOOD. Beer is cold, wings are hot and they're always trying new things to keep customers interested in coming back. They have live music from time to time, but it's not necessary for such a small space. They also have the games on, so it's a favorite spot during football season!

Went last night and we had an awesome time! Entertainment highlight of our trip. The 3 guys were great....funny and so talented. Our request for Stairway to Heaven was done so fabulously!!! The guest vocalists were a hoot! Was a real party!!

Had a great time. Some people on here are complaining that their should be more seating, but the owners know what theyre doing. If anything it should maybe be more high top tables, but take away chairs. The only complaint I have is that the audience on this particular night was lame. The performers are amazingly talented and they do a good job entertaining, but its hard to entertain people who come there to sit on their phones.

We had so much fun going thru this. Was well worth the money and time.

You can buy tickets online before you go too.

The only thing about this that was good, was the show.  The food is so not worth it and the service was horrible.  The only view you get that is not a river bank, is the one down town.  An its only momentarily.

So life like. Was nice to see a variety of singers and listen to their music. Went by myself so it was fun trying to take selfies with everyone!  Make sure to read each plaque for each musician great information. Most were very recognizable. A couple I wasn't sure of but was great fun trying to figure out!

Good food, good service!  Glad we stopped by!  I knew it was going to be a good burger when it showed up.  Definitely a "roll your sleeves up" burger!!  And you just can't go wrong with live music while you eat!

It's a cool spot, great beer selection, live music. I ordered my burger on Texas toast, it might as well been plain white bread it was soggy after the first bite. Fries were pretty bomb tho sum it up- just a burger joint.

We were in Nashville last weekend and decided to take in The General Jackson Showboat tour.  It was quite expensive.  The tour begins with hotel pickup which was quite handy.  That's a "plus".  When you arrive they tell you about an additional tour (for an additional price of $8 per person) that you can take of the boat's pilot house.  This tour was conducted by the boat Captain who was very gracious and knowledgeable.  This was a "plus".  Then you are taken to your assigned dining table where you are seated with 3 other couples.  As luck would have it we sat with 3 very interesting and tremendously conversant couples from Denmark, Texas and New Orleans.  Our dinner conversation was a "plus".  But the dinner was truly horrible (a fillet that was as tough as I imagine shoe leather would be to eat, a creamed spinach that was weirdly seasoned, and overdone potatoes that were supposed to be scalloped I think but were not even close.  The dinner was a big "negative".  Then there was the music show.  Well....the cast "meant well" but as judged by the apathetic applause, after each song and at the end, they greatly missed the mark.  The costumes were great (and there were many costumes changes!) and the musicians were pretty good.  Some of the singers (there were 3 men and 3 women plus the narrator) were ok.  The dancing was lively and energetic but, at best, the show could be compared to a lounge act at a Vegas casino.  I really thought that since we were in Nashville, often referred to as "Music City", that the show would have been replete with super talented  singers and musicians, but alas that was not the case at all.  While I would not call the show a true "negative" (like the horrible dinner), I would give it a grade of "C".  We are long time season ticket subscribers to the music theater in our town which is a third tier market for traveling broadway shows.  Sadly, this ensemble did not even come close to what we are used to seeing perform.  When asked by the driver on the way back to the hotel after the show what we liked the most about the evening, I responded "our table mates"!!!  And they didn't cost us anything!

360 burger has great burger selections. Had the LeBron burger it was delicious! Nick was a great server. He was prompt and ready for questions. Plus it was game night so I had a chance to use my Taboo skills.

The boat is spacious and the cruise is pretty especially when coming up on the Nashville skyline. But the food was horrible. Horrible. The worst part was that for a 7pm cruise the food was served at 7:20 and then the entertainment did not even start until 9pm. The show was pretty good and not bad singing an pretty fun. The crowd was dead and no audience participation but had the show started earlier it would have new a bearable experiment. Crew was not accommodating and Add the $595 this cost for our family to go and this was an epic fail.
Good music and good beers. Didn't see anyone eating. Smelled a little funny but it was fun

I was here on a Monday night and it was pretty lit. The musicians were really upbeat and cool (my favorite part was when the fiddler did a really fun feature piece) and I got some fried pickles and a slider that I enjoyed. There was a wide variety in the crowd from middle-aged people there to enjoy the music to twenty-somethings out to party. The place was packed the whole time I was there and I had a lot of fun.

Excellent music and live music experience!  We made reservations and went to the 6 pm show. The three musicians were all talented and great singers. One guy had written many hits and we recognized the songs!!
We shared an app--bbq sliders that was very delicious. Had some beers--we like the local selection of Little Harpeth beers! I have yet to get tickets to the blue bird cafe but I will definitely return to listening room for the awesome music!!
The parking lot looked small but we used uber so it was easy.
The cooks could pay more attention to the order before their plate it up. The wait staff rocks!

Pretty darn good burger!  Onion rings were pretty good.   Great little restaurant.  Full bar.  Not a huge variety of food choices but it IS a burger joint!  Service was good.  Friendly.  Place is clean.  Definitely warrants a return visit!  #GoPredators!!!

So, wait.  I can have a mash up of Bohemian Rhapsody and Tenacious D? I'm a fan for life.  

I have no idea how this is one place on Broadway that we can always find a table.  No matter how crowded it is, a table magically appears.  It's also not that hard to get a drink, even during peak hours, so that solidifies it at four stars.  

Sometimes there's a cover charge, but usually not.  I haven't yet worked out the bar's algorithm for cover charge vs. date and time but will let you know when I do.

The piano players are always funny and really do play requests, especially if you tip along with said request.  You're certainly not going to get craft cocktails, but you're not there for the drinks, you're there to here a hilarious rendition of dueling college fight songs followed up by Elton John and Usher.  

These guys are musical geniuses!

It was my birthday weekend! I had a great time. Small, quaint but great music and a popular country singer was there with his wife!!! That was a big surprise. He danced with his wife and worked the crowd!! He sang a few oldies of Merle Haggard! It was a great birthday weekend for me! This was after I got to experience Broadway street!! WoW.

Came here whilst visiting Nashville with a buddy. Loved the music. The service was very friendly, if a little sluggish. The waiters were moving as quickly as they could! I think they just need a few more people. It was slightly irritating that a lot of people there just chattered away even tho there was a sign saying to keep conversations down. It probably wouldn't hurt for them to enforce it.
Enjoyed the Cash Museum. Nothing is as impressive as just hearing him sing but the memorabilia is extensive. Worth the visit
Small portions, bad customer service. I ordered 2 burgers and 2 cokes my bill was $30. Won't be back

Worst service I've ever had.  Waiter lied about prices and didn't correct his mistakes.  Also wasn't visiting table and id have to go to the back kitche ln to get help twice.  (After waiting about 30 min to take our order and an hour for the check) 

The burger was good... Too bad the service was so bad

I wish this place met our expectations. A group of 21 of us headed down to Nashville from New York to celebrate a bachlorette party. Our first two nights in Nashville were amazing so we were super pumped for a piano bar.  The place is very awkwardly set up. It's just a bunch of tiny tables, crappy chairs and the pianos are not even on a nice big stage. Oh well. The guys playing sounded great so we didn't mind.  Our waiter was MISERABLE. He was not even remotely nice or friendly. Not sure if he works for tips, but he was rude. They poured me the wrong drink. When I told him, he just looked at me and walked away. No apology, nothing. Don't expect much from their menu. The queso dip is cheese whiz and bagged tortilla chips. Gross!  Also, we got ripped off.  We put up $35 to get our bachlorette on stage.  After seeing numerous birthday people get called up for $10, I finally asked the "security guy" to ask the piano player.  He was no help. I put up another $10 and another slip to remind them of our bachlorette.  At this point, the piano men had switched shifts so I asked the bartender for a manager. The manager said "they must have lost your slip". Well, they didn't lose our MONEY !!!! $45 and not one shout out to the bride. Such crap. The manager did not want to help at all other than telling us we can come back later for no cover. They let a huge group leave unhappy. There are TONS of places in Nashville that were a blast. I'm mad we even wasted a couple of hours in this place.

My brother, boyfriend, and I decided to check out 360 on Saturday in our continuing quest to find the best burger in Nashville. We got there around 1:30 and it was pretty empty, maybe about 3 or 4 other parties there besides us. It has a pretty relaxed vibe, and the AC was cranked in there, I was freezing my buns off. Parking is good because it's in a strip mall, so no worries there.

For checking in on Yelp, I got a free appetizer. Yay! So we opted for the fried pickles, which were pretty dang tasty. I had the Cilantro Avocado Burger with sweet potato fries. The men had some other stuff that I can't remember off the top of my head. But we all were in universal agreement that the fries (regular and sweet) were not that good. It's not that they didn't have flavor, but it's almost like they weren't cooked enough, or had been sitting around for a while before we got them. They were just kinda soggy and greasy, which was disappointing.

The burger was actually pretty legit. I thought it had some good flavor and a reasonable amount of heat. I'm not tolerant of hardly any spice, and I thought it was just the right amount. I got the burger on the pretzel bun, which I would definitely advise of anyone doing because it was delicious. We didn't have a problem with the order taking that other people seemed to have, so I was happy about that.

The service was good. Our waiter (I can never remember their names) was really friendly and even gave me some suggestions when I was trying to pick out a beer, of which they have an extensive variety. But he did check back in like 10 times throughout the meal, so we concluded that he must have been pretty bored. There weren't a lot of tables, though, so it's understandable. Overall, this place definitely could be better but it's still pretty good. I don't know if maybe they were having an off day with the sides, but I would be willing to give them another shot!

First place we ate when we got to Nashville. We were hungry and it happened to be close to our hotel. Really glad we stopped. The service was good as was the food. Staff was very friendly and prompt. We sat close to the stage, so it made it difficult to talk but the music was great. Food was very good for the price and atmosphere was fun!

This is the worst place in town. Had gift card for $50. Used $30 worth for food, drinks were not included  on gift card. Manager/Owner wouldn't even come over to talk to us about it. Food was just mediocre at best and over priced. Sangria was horrible, my advice stay home or go to lower Broadway for some good food and customer
 service.

The buffet starts right when you board the boat, so if you come in a little later than 6:30 your food will be cold. Also the show starts at the last 30 minutes, so you are sitting on a boat for two hours with no entertainment except looking out at the river. I came in with the expectation that I would be eating while a show was taking place. The only great thing about this place is that the waiter was extremely kind and helpful. Since most of our table was freezing, our waiter brought us all table cloths to warm up with. He was excellent!

Solid bloody mary, $11 but whatever we are on Broadway. Good live singers, nice menu. They have air conditioning, that's a plus. Check out my bloody mary pic...it will let you know why you should come here. Ya the mushroom was a tad mushy and the Bacon and slim jim was questionable, but it was an all around good time
I went their to get brunch for my husband and myself. Everyone there was so nice and accommodating. The food was fantastic! Service was stellar!

This place was amazing.  I heard they are closing down or something, so I highly recommended hitting this up before they do!  I was a little turned off by the $20 cover, but I think it was worth it during our Nashville trip bc it was one of our favorite spots.  Of course, with this sort of this, its always kind of the luck of the draw on what bands/songwriters you will get and if it's your style of music, but we really enjoyed who we had.  

We went on a Saturday night and were able to get a great spot right in the center (but there were only 2 of us).  Bluebird Cafe is fun for the experience, but the cover is worth skipping the hassle, and we liked the bands here better!  Food was good and decent beer selection.

Really cool environment. Very prompt service but also a little chaotic. Honestly we could have walked in without tickets because they didnt even check. Service was enthusiastic but scattered. We ordered the cheeseplate and potroast to split but they came out at the same time. An appetizer should come first. Now we had to choose, to eat in reverse or let our potroast get cold.
In summary the music environment was very cool and intimate but the food service is secondary at best. Everything will get slipped in front of you at once so just order what you want to have immediately dont expect a dining experience.

Great food and even better service. The prices are very reasonable and they have live music most nights. Plenty of drink specials for those looking for a quiet place to get a drink after work, but also great for families with kids. As an added bonus, they use grass fed beef and locally sourced ingredients and they are locally owned.
If you're looking for a great show look no further. The bar staff are AH-Fucking-AMAZING. Great service. Super friendly. The band can vary from Wrecking Ball to Queen with ease. Great time!

Always packed but for good reason. If you've been in Nashville for a while, you are probably sick of Broadway but this place stands the test of time. Average drinks and service but the musical talent here is always extremely high quality, these guys can play. Go here and hit up the second floor cocktail and cigar bar right next door for a top notch night out on Broadway.

Decided to check out the JC museum yesterday

It is kind of small but full of lots of interesting things 
Very informative 
Cool things to see 
They even have a green screen and you can get your pic taken with Johnny ( extra charge but very reasonable ) 
Allow yourself about an hour to hour and half to go thru it 
Reason for a 4 Star review is because their gift shop items seem really cheap 
The tee shirts were cheaply made and just not very tasteful 
We skipped buying anything ( we love to collect shirts from all places we visit , however we were disappointed here ) 

All in all we are glad we went. It's totally worth the money

Came here with another couple. They wouldn't let a 50 yr old woman in because her ID was expired! Come on seriously! She bought a ticket, which she won't get her money back for plus drove over 2 hours to get here. The "manager" Charles is a complete jerk. Don't waste your time with this dump.

If you weren't a big fan of Johnny Cash before this museum, you'll quickly become one. This is a terrific small museum that is full of surprises. It's far from a fawning fan museum -- really honest and straightforward like the Man in Black himself. Photos, recordings, work and music if his contemporaries, instruments, clothing and tons of stories. A great find. 

I learned so much about Cash that was worthwhile, including his work for the disadvantaged, his speech in Congress advocating real solutions to fixing the prison system (too bad they didn't listen), his personal life and wonderful candid photos. And together videos! Awesome. Do not miss this if you have any interest in music from the 50s and later.
Rude service and poor selection of beer which was served Luke warm. The rooftop was not worth the four story climb.

We stopped in Monday night and got to listen to the Song Suffragettes - what a great show! I love that The Listening Room makes it a priority for women to have their music and voices heard, especially given how talented they are! We also got dinner here and we all agreed the food was awesome. We had a very sweet server as well and really enjoyed our night!
Yes, they sure cram a killer experience in a smallish space. I'm so happy I went. Wish there was more variety in the museum shop, and some additional range in price points.

I believe the hype and the burgers are really good despite discovering that my order was totally wrong. I ordered a barbecue something burger and then changed to another, and got a relatively plain burger without any accents. However, it allowed me to really taste the beef and be convinced of the excellent quality. The service was fine (besides that whole order-taking thing).  The fries are limp, and will not taste good if you order to-go and wait to eat them when you get home. 

It's loud when the musicians are performing.

I visited The LIstening Room Cafe last week and it was really nice.  I got there pretty early in the evening and enjoyed chatting with the bartender.  It was also two for one drafts so that was nice.  They only offered valet parking which is kind of a bummer, but the guys were nice and when I tipped them seemed surprised.  

The writer's circle was good and they had some very talented people playing.  I have been to the BlueBird Cafe and have to say I enjoyed Listening Room more.  They just have a lot more space and that made the night more enjoyable.  

I will be back.

I loved the pub area, good music, decent beer and a killer quesadilla.
Two for one drinks is always good.
Friendly staff.

Payed PLENTY for a song and they didn't even play it. The song was for a bachelorette party and they called the bachelorettes in the entire place on stage to do the hokey pokey!!! I paid for everyone to go on stage instead of my party. Not only that, it was extremely impersonal. I asked for my money back they said I could not have it. For these reasons they absolutely  deserve one star.

This is a must for any Johnny Cash fan, or even if you're not a big fan, you should go anyway.  The museum tells the great story of Cash's life, but it also focuses on the lives of the musicians that he touched as well as the immense impact he had on American culture.  The museum is small enough to do in less than an hour, but you won't want to go through it that fast.  There's just so much to see; lots of memorabilia, interactive videos and displays.  We spent about an hour and a half in the museum.  They also have quite an extensive gift shop...you'll be hard-pressed to leave with just one thing.  Oh, also check out the cafe.  They have a couple of coffee brews in there with some clever names.

Great evening until Brennin done a cover. Might as well been at a no cover no $10 dollar food, drink minimum Honky Tonk. 
Mark Irwin is def the man. Played all his hits plus a few new ones.

A hidden gem in Nashville!! This is one of my favorite places in Nashville. The music is always so good! I would recommend the Listening Room for a casual low-key night to sit down, enjoy a drink or two, and listen to some songwriters play their music.

Stole a bite from my son's plate of the fried catfish...and I'll be back for my own order soon! 

We came for the music and honestly I just expected "pub grub". We ordered a plate of fried green tomatoes to share and they were perfectly cooked as well. 

In a sea of over priced over rated and sometimes under performing restaurants in downtown Nashville, this place surprises and over performs in my opinion. 

The catfish entree priced at $20, is actually reasonable by Nashville standards. My son's dish was served on an oval platter filled with two large perfectly cooked catfish filets, a mound of steamed green beans and a heaping amount of Mac and cheese then topped off with a side dish of Cole slaw. Easily, it was enough food for two to share, which puts the value per person high up on the competition. A nice lagniappe was the validation for free valet parking in their lot.  Oh yea, there was awesome music too!
I'll admit I love Johnny Cash but I really enjoyed this place. I was only there an hour because of other things we had to do but I could have stayed 2-3 hours easily. Gift shop was nice too.
Music and ambiance was incredible, but disappointed in the food. Shrimp and grits: grits were lumpy. Very spicy so be prepared! Chicken and dumplings: came out lukewarm, but otherwise good.

The food is so so, but that's not the reason to come to this place. They have great musicians who play here and it is a quiet place to listen and enjoy. The staff is friendly and works hard to please.

My husband and I came her last year as our first trip to Nashville from Nebraska. We are huge John cash fans. This museum is amazing it has so many different memorabilia from his life. One thing I remembered for some odd reason was the briefcase and johnnys credit card and thought how cool that must have been back then to be able to have something like that. This place is truly a work of art and shows of much of an artist Johnny was. However I am not sure if it was the museums intentions or not but they do play Johnny cover of Hurt right at the end!! All most had me in tears!! Rest in peace Johnny and June!

This was pretty bad. Everything was burnt. Chicken fingers should not be black. The menu even said "fried to perfection".... what? Service was pretty bad for being the only ones in there. Music was great.

Authentic Nashville singer-songwriter vibe with great hospitality and very good food. The venue is roomy & comfortable w/ a huge stage, but still seems intimate for quaint songwriter-in-the-round sessions. The menu is small, but everything our party of four had was very good, especially the Yazoo Chili. Food quality was better and fresher then expected. Nice beer list. Excellent fresh coffee and we shared a desert of mini-cupcakes that were perfect. The crowd was a bit too into their own table talk, not as respectful of the artists as I would like. Nice that you can talk a bit. We arrived at 5:30 on Saturday and were disappointed that the music did not start until 7 on weekends, so we had time to kill. Overall, A new favorite venue for us.

On our first night in Nashville last week, my friends and I had enjoyed a great dinner and as we were walking around enjoying the sights and sounds of the city, we decided to stop in to the Rack Room/Blue Bar. Friendly people, really nice guy working the door, great music, "let's go here."  We had a few beers, laughed and enjoyed ourselves. 

It was time to move on and so I asked for the check.

The first item on the check was "name, old." Now I could very well be misinterpreting something here but none of us had bourbon and it certainly wasn't free if we did. 

Apparently singing along with the Beastie Boys gives me gray hair because drinking fireball just makes us girls. 

Now, I'm thinking something such as "girls with curls", "two reds and brunette",  "girls in black" etc.. could have been used if needed or Mr. Cole W could have gotten really crazy and..... asked for a name or a card but no, instead he named us as "old."

Wow. Nice buzzkill son. Didn't you get the memo that "old" ladies tip? Or that "old" ladies can read?  

So much for everyone in Nashville being super friendly.  Don't worry, we won't be back, it's probably past our bedtime when the bar opens anyway.

Nothing to write home about. There are no swinging doors (at least in the winter). Decent priced food and it seems as though locals come here. The tunes were pretty good. Fresh chicken fingers and non-frozen burgers. It doesn't stand out too much, but in comparison to everything else around, it's better than most others.

Love the bar and Dierks but what the hell are the bouncers upstairs doing? Running a strip club? Bouncers were running outside the safety fence of the roof. Bouncers groping the patrons hoping to get them to come home at the end of the night made for an extremely uncomfortable and short stay.  Terrible music on the roof top bar only adding to the atmosphere that was less than enjoyable.

A burger and beer joint should be just that. This place seemed like it didn't know if it wanted to be casual or upscale. Having had many burgers in this city from many places, I would say this place makes the bottom of the list. The burger was just alright, and not in anyway comparable to some of the best Nashville has to offer. I was honestly disappointed in that because it was the reason I came. My wife was also disappointed with her burger. Our burger orders were put in wrong so we got the wrong patties. The burger itself was just so average. The onion rings were fantastic. Seriously. They were great! The dipping sauce for them though was terrible (spicy mayonnaise). My wife's regular fries on the other hand tasted burnt. When it was all said and done we had 2 burgers and the extra dollar for onion rings and 2 drinks and racked up a 27.00 tab after tip. Which I felt like was a bit steep for our mediocre experience. They have so much potential to be so much better.

We had Captain's Table seats this past weekend. Took my sister, who was in town for the first time ever. Let me start by saying that the entire experience was exceptional! We had an absolutely beautiful night, and was impressed with the level of service extended to those that pay for the Captain's Table (totally worth the extra money.) The food was good (not wonderful, but good, and there was plenty of it.) 10 people sit to a table, so we were with some people we didn't know. The cruise through downtown after dark was beautifully romantic, and nice with just a few people. Seeing where the boat is controlled from, and meeting the captain was a nice experience, and something I won't soon forget. The performance was phenomenal (from someone that doesn't like country music.) It didn't stop, and the performers were great singers, dancers, and full of personality. I'd definitely recommend the Captain's Table experience to anyone! 
My only complaints, the servers were all VERY hard to understand, and didn't understand us very well, someone who had better English would have made ordering easier. He was good at his job, but it took a LOT to get something ordered, or understood, and all the servers were terrible with English. My other complaint was the drinks. Very expensive, which was expected, but they were very weak and way too much nicer for the amount of money. 
Overall, I'd do the Captain's Table at the General Jackson again, probably even a few times. It was fun, elegant, romantic, entertaining, and an all around good time.

Hearing from my friends this was a good place to hang out I checked it out.  Showing up around 12:30 p.m. there was plenty of room to sit.  Seat yourself was my experience,  taking about 5 minutes to be recognized and a drink order.  I ordered the blue cheese burger on a plain bun with fries that appeared to be skin on shoestring style.   The burger did have a good flavor but the bun was hard to cut and chew.  The bun was fresh just a little gummy.  The fries were cold upon arrival,  but shoestrings are hard to keep warm.  As for location nice with other business around and parking for your friends.  This is a good hangout place with food, a place where YOU make the fun.  But as for coming in for just food, the food is just a good addition.   Now to be fair I have only tried one item...

The rooftop bar was a great time. Huge mix of people there. The service was great by the bartenders Jake and Nicole. Definitely recommend going if your in the area. Good DJ also he played all kinds of music from old school hip hop to some EDM and country.

Isaac Mathews made my evening ! He played my song :-) no one else on Broadway knew this song but Isaac winged it and totally made my day. We also had this delicious chocolate rum smoothie thing... It was delicious!! This place is so intimate and cozy. Definitely coming back here next time I'm in Nashville

It was a fast trip to Nashville, on business, but I genuinely enjoyed my trip to the JCM. A bit pricey on the admission, at $17, but, I felt like it was worth it after the tour.  Nice bonus to see the Sun Record's display, with a great photo of Elvis and Johnny.

I was aboard the General Jackson Show Boat this weekend with mom & dad;   We went on a Sunday lunch cruise.   The show and talent here was A-1 excellent.   The food buffet was simple and tasty.  For the price I would say this is a great value and we would have loved doing a night time cruise if we could have, even though the rate is about double.   The service staff was excellent as well.   If you (enjoy country music), and are looking to have a good time away from the downtown crowds, I'd say you should not miss the General Jackson Show Boat cruise. The guests were mostly 40's - 70's age range and all seemed to be down home fun loving people and the show was extremely entertaining.  If you are into big crowds and lots of bars, then downtown Broadway street is indeed an endless honkey tonk party not to be missed, the town is full of many talented bands.  Today, good fun with good music & elbow room was on our menu.  Thank you for an excellent afternoon in Nashville.

I went there with a group on the grand opening night and was very impressed with the amount of space. Very comfortable as opposed to the downtown scene. However, they were understaffed for opening night! I don't know how this was possible. There was also a very small selection of beers and didn't have the typical brews. The check in offer says one free bud light, something they didn't even have. Even though we didn't order food it was funny to see the reactions of people around us when their food came out as they busted into cheers. One couple just got up and left before their food came out. If they get the staff thing under control and have a elaborate selection of drinks this place would of got my 5 star review but i just don't understand how you can be so ill prepared for a Saturday. The best part of the whole experience was obviously the music. This is by far (with only one visit) my favorite music spot in Nashville. Here you will find the songwriters for some of the best songs in country music. The night that we were there we heard the song writers for rascal flats. This is a place I would love to try again and give a better review.

Very disappointed!!! I was on a pedal car tour and supposed to get a deal on shots, I mentioned we were with the pedal tour they charged me 36$ for 4 shots which should have been 20$ and when I said something all the bar tender said was sorry instead of making it right.
Had a ton of fun here- went and shopped at the mall then we grabbed drinks and wings here- music was great and service was too.

Awesome night, the singer songwriters were excellent and it was an eye opening peek into their world of songwriters for the stars!

The food was also very good.  We had the brisket and the specialty apple turkey club.  Both made with in-house smoked meats.  Sides were also good.

This is no way any reflection on Dierks himself.  Good service, good venue, great music!  I'm still a huge fan but I will not be going back to this place.  

I ordered two drinks last week.  Jack on the rocks and four roses on the rocks.  $26!!  Let me break it down for you.  $10 each for the drink, which is somewhat standard in Nashville nowadays but on the higher end. But they charged $3 each for ice....yes ICE!  $13 for a JD.  Are you kidding me?  Go back to Scottsdale with that bullshit!
This  is a relaxed bar with a lot of locals enjoying a friend on the the stage. He is great and the service is very good, even with the amount of  people. Had the special for dinner, very good.
A must do if your in Nashville, a lot of memorabilia if you like Cash! There is a nice gift shop inside!
The live music, ambience, service and drinks were great! I'd have dinner before coming here though it was the only thing not worth the money at all.

I love love LOVE this place! So entertaining, each of the guys are super talented and I love the entire staff there! Special shout out to my server Angel!! :)

You all are the best! Thanks for so many fun nights!

I so wanted to love this place!  It is close to where we live and I was hoping to not have to drive far for a decent burger.  We try burgers at most places we go, kind of like trying Pad Thai at a Thai restaurant, it is a litmus test.  The best part of the burger was the bun.  Nothing special about the burger, it was a litte dry.

They bragged about all the food being local, within 5 miles according to the website.  Yet, we were told the beef comes from somewhere in Murfreesboro.  I'm pretty sure that is more than 5 miles away.  Other places that claim to use local list where their food comes from (farm, city).  I guess if you don't care about where the food is coming from this isn't an issue.

I also feel the prices are high, especially for this area. The farmer burger is $12 and I can get a bigger burger, similar toppings and locally sourced meat/cheese/produce, at other places for $8 - $10.

A plus, the atmosphere is warm and welcoming.  I'm not sure I will go back considering I can go other places and 4 of us can eat for what it would cost 3 of us to eat here.
This place is so much fun!! Great music and awesome musicians. They play a good variety of music and $20 gets you whatever song you want to hear. No cover on Friday, but a $6 charge on Saturday.

Really loved this place. We were visiting from NY and couldn't get into the bluebird so we tried the listening room. We loved this place so much we came back on our last night in town. The talent showcased here is unreal. I wish I could remember some of the performers names because I would love to follow their careers. The food was pretty good too. Definitely worth a visit.

Big Bang brings the energy! Our bachelorette had never experienced a dueling piano bar, so we couldn't miss catching this place while in Nashville. Their song choices are on point! They bring such an eclectic collection from OutKast and MJ to Elton John, Bruno Mars, and classic rockers. Service was fast and spiffy, and there was a $6 or $7 cover, which is well worth the live entertainment. Floors were littered with napkins that they throw on big songs but bathrooms were well maintained, which is always appreciated. The beers are HUGE, though they do offer smaller sizes (which wasn't clarified at purchasing), so keep that in mind if you fill up quickly on beer.

Hands down one of the best values in terms of cost and size of a museum.  There are many personal letters, hand written lyrics, awards, clothing and photos.  The artifacts stretch across Cash's entire career and include impressive items such as the mantle from his burned home, a Cash and Sam Phillips signed large 45 of I Walk The Line and the Hurt Grammy Award.  The back room had a wonderful rotating piece on the Million Dollar Quartet so there was Elvis, Jerry Lee, and Carl Perkins items including the drumset used on the Blue Suede Shoes recording.  Just amazing stuff that has somehow survived so many years.
We spent as much time here as in the Country Western Hall of Fame.  It's that good.
After you're done - look up Peg Leg Porkers for some fantastic dry rub BBQ.  Ribs and beer that Johnny would appreciate.  These two made it a perfect day.

I had such a wonderful time here. Bluebird, being as difficult as it is to get tickets, was not an option. But man I am glad we came here. The songwriters were incredibly talented and the show was inexpensive. As a plus, the Mac and cheese is also delicious.

As an artist, I have to weigh in here! I've played 360 Burger a few times, including hosting a writer's night and also with my band. The staff is super-friendly and accommodating. The boys in the band love the burgers and I've opted for the salads and salmon - all were excellent and the french fries are a must! All beers come in a frothy frozen mug...such a nice detail! I would definitely recommend this place - great burgers, great music, and such a fantastic staff!

I have been to the Listening Room twice, both on Sunday afternoons, and had a very enjoyable time.  The music and ambiance is amazing, and the unlimited mimosas are top notch!  The service can be a little slow at times, and the food does take a while to reach your table.  However, the food is always delicious. Overall, it's a place I like to take my out-of-town guests to really experience the essence of Nashville.

This was my first bar in the city and I loved it! Actually, I wish I stayed longer...the burger was ok, drinks were good but the band was awesome! I liked how cozy it was...of course it was only like 3pm lol

Tried this place for the first time tonight And it was awesome! My bf got the ultimate Bacon cheeseburger with an egg and fresh jalapenos and I got the avocado and cilantro Burger with waffle fries and both were amazing! There was also a nice easy listening guitarist,  evan gibb,  playing. Awesome atmosphere and cool wait staff. Will definitely be returning!
Good wax figures and sets. Cool photo opportunities but the price was a little steep for the experience. It's a lot smaller than the other wax museums I've been to in vegas, LA, etc.

Took a small group for brunch. Bottomless mimosas were rarely refilled. They had two brunch menus that didn't agree. People were charged for sides that should've been included. B&G were lukewarm.

They fixed the bills, but it took them a while.

Seems like the locals know to avoid this place for brunch...

So I came in the day before Thanksgiving, right after I walked out of Kanye West's concert early (seriously, why the diatribe?) Cute place, not raucous party central but I prefer my bars quiet and cozy. Tiffany and Jimmy were hanging out there and were very good company. Take off a star because $7.50 for a cocktail? Come on.
I'm a local and was looking for something different.  Friendly staff. Great entertainment. Beer was $5 a bottle.

Terrible service, slow, wrong orders, and burgers were far overcooked....never again!

I recommend to choose another option, it was comical how bad it was.

I ordered a beer and 15 mins later I had to go to the bar and grab it myself!

Unfortunately, we came in on a rainy Saturday so the museum was super crowded BUT we still loved it! The museum is a GREAT representation of his life (according to my fiancé who is a Johnny Cash fan, not saying that I'm not... I just didn't know anything about him prior to the museum!). I think I'll be able to review it better when we go back to Nashville and do the tour when it's not so busy (yes, we plan on doing it again...as we don't like big crowds so it wasn't that enjoyable for us). I do wish it was a little bit bigger so there was more space because when it is busy, it's nearly impossible to move around.

Loved the museum! I learned so much more about the man in black. Great memorabilia - old photos - videos - personal letters etc. Plan to spend a couple of hours there. Staff was great - friendly. I'll be proudly wearing my new black CASH t-shirt.

This is a honky think and a place to go for drinks and hooping and halloring. We did order the hummus appetizer to go with our drinks and it was mediocre with the celery being dried on the ends and the hummus being very warm. The wine options are also mediocre but the band was great. Know why you're there. Get a beer and enjoy the music.

Visiting from Ohio and today was the day we had the BEST meal our entire trip.  If you are in Nashville and enjoy friendly people and flavors this place is a must!!!  It is extremely hard for my husband to be happy with the food choices myself and the kids like and he was extremely happy with his burger as well.  Nick, our server was very helpful with suggestions. I cannot say enough good about their food.  Gluten is my issue and they understood my needs as well.

Loved the musicians and songs and the format of each musician sharing a story and singing one of their songs. Loved everything about the show. Our waitress was terrific tho the service can be slow at the start since a hundred drink orders go in at once. Understandable. Not a big deal.  The crowd was extremely respectful of the performers and everyone quietly enjoyed the show or sang along.  

The only exception is the waiter working the far left of the room the night we went, Friday, May 25. He'd sit down at his tables and he would talk very loudly for minutes at a time (his customers spoke so quietly I couldn't hear them) during the performances.  Distracting and unnecessary, the neighboring tables would turn to glare; he kept going. After the third or fourth time this happened I tapped him on the shoulder and asked if he could keep it down. He was incredibly inappropriate in his response. Even came by a few times afterward to taunt me. The manager needs to go monitor this behavior. Horrible. This guy needs better training or to find a job at a different kind of bar.


I updated the rating after hearing from the owner. Thank you for the response.

Every time I have friends or family in Nashville i take them here first, The bartender Horse is the person who helps entertain the evening for my guests and me lately. I dont feel like im in a tourist trap here like the rest of Broadway. We always say we are gonna be here for one drink as a group. Yet, somehow end up closing the bar down every time regardless of wich group of people are visiting lately. The bands on the first floor always rock it which is great for my family. Then for my friends who come up from Atlanta love the second floor and the roof top vibes. All in all its the perfect place for tourist and locals. I just wish Horse was workin last night to get to hang with my family. Luckily they are in town till Tuesday.

i really wanted to give an extensive review about how good this place is, but sadly it was only mediocre to me :( we had an awesome server & the environment was cool & casual. the beef they use comes from grass-feed cows which I think is awesome, but i don't know I've just had better burgers.

I was in there with a couple friends on a Tuesday night drinking with some friends. I'd been a couple times before, but my bartender Jasmine made this night exceptional! She not only made sure I was taken care of but was very attentive to my friends and surrounding customers. Every time I returned to the bar she made sure I got what I needed and it was fairly busy. Will be returning, thanks Jasmine!

This is another great live music venue in Nashville, but it is a lot cleaner and hipper than the honky-tonks on Broadway. Although the food menu is a little limited, most everything we tried was good, including the local beers on tap. I had the fried ravioli and waldorf salad while my friend had the calamari and black-and-blue salad. The salads were awesome and the ravioli was tasty but the calamari was nothing special, if not a little plain. We went around dinner time and got to see some GREAT performances by some young singer/songwriters all the way from the UK! I would highly recommend this place if you actually want to enjoy some good food and music but want to get away from the noise of the main strip.

4 1/2 stars. Tons of great info about Cash's life (birth to death), along with terrific artifacts and memorabilia, with lots of film/video footage, & interactive parts. Wish there were dual headphones at each iPad station though, would cutdown on wait time and allow couples to proceed along the path together.

Putting the Listening Room on our weekend itinerary was easily the best decision we made on our trip to Nashville. It's a great change of pace from the Honky Tonks on Broadway. These musicians are amazing. My wife and I were truly blown away. The drinks and food prices are more than reasonable and tasty too.

OK so this is a must see for any fan but only have shirts up to a 2x. Also I believe everything should have museum on it not just Johnny Cash most other shops had same stuff. Staff was friendly place was clean but a coffee place inside???? Still being a fan loved it.

One of the best times to have in Nashville. This is what music city is about. Watching brilliant, versatile artists hop from one genre to the next, from slaying one instrument to another, and even the bartender hopping on stage to murder an original rendition of CeeLo Green. The performers tell you to request anything. Really. They mean anything. :) come here to boogie with your friends and listen to a wider selection than most of the bars on the strip / anything your heart may desire. Whenever I have friends come in town, I take them here absolutely.

this. place. We drive from downtown whenever we are craving a good burger. we've tried tons in Nashville and nothing compares. They use grass Fed beef and organic veggies, portions are great and it is just outstanding. not much else to say!

I just got done eating at 360 burger and it was so fantastic that I had to get right on yelp and write a review. I consider myself a food connoisseur and am very critical when it comes to my judgement of food and restaurants. 360 burger is in an odd location tucked away in hickory hollow. It is a small joint with a bar that only seats a few but the interior is done very well and it has a nice ambiance. There was a live band when I went, very very loud, band was great I must add but don't plan on having much of a conversation. Good thing was once my burger came to the table I didn't need to speak. It was cooked perfectly, the pretzel bun was great, and the burger was very filling. For $7.95 it was a bargain, sweet potato fries included. I got the cilantro avocado burger, it had habanero cheese and all of the flavors came together to create a memorable experience with every bite. I usually eat very fast but I took more than 20 minutes to enjoy each and every bite of that burger. Well done! I will be back.

Wonderful music combined with good food. Relaxed atmosphere with prompt service. I enjoyed the blpt (?)sandwich. Service was good and the entertainment is wonderful. We went to see our friends Jaime O'Neal and Rod Good do a song writers showcase. There is a $15 min per person. Oh yeah, try the cheesecake. We really enjoyed it.

We found a pretty good deal on Groupon that we took advantage of and after going, it was an even better deal than I initially thought.  If you are a Johnny Cash fan, even a casual one, I would say that visiting this museum is a must!!! Heck, I think that even if you've never really listened to Johnny Cash that this museum would be a great experience, as long as you have an appreciation for music.
If you love Johnny Cash, you'll love this place!  It was so cool to see pictures, letters and even school yearbooks from when he was a kid....even letters from later in his life. What a treasure!

When in Nashville there are so many places "you just have to go to". Well, this should definitely be on you're list. Our experience there was our highlight. Good food, service, style and of course music. If you appreciate good food and good music without a loud obnoxious crowd(which distorts the good music) then this is your place.

Get online, reserve tickets and go. Two thumbs up from a Florida boy who has no musical talent ha.

OK, so we expected Chow-Line food, and pretty much was as expected.  Plentiful, but fairly low quality, rush through the line and finish eating before the boat moves.  We were not expecting a great meal, but did expect the music to be "Nashville" quality and maybe even hear something you had heard in the past.   The dance and choreography was unique, but after 5 minutes, nothing special.   Kate Smith would be rolling in her grave to hear the way they sang "God Bless America".  We were at a table of 10, all strangers, and we were the only 2 that remained at the table until entertainment was finished.   Walk down Broadway in Nashville and lively music pours onto the street from 30-40 bars that rate above this presentation.  They were all talented, clean, and crisp, just never had the attention of the audience.  Sorry, Nashville, you need to fix this venue.  The multi caravan of Ski-doo's playing in the wake of the paddle wheel was more memorable than the food or music.

The food is incredible, fast service, inexpensive. So much goodness. I've had the Cubano, the prosciutto Maki, and the Bahn Mi, they were all good. The drinks are great, friendly service, and apparently they do brunch now on Saturday/Sunday, so I have an excuse to go back for the 3rd time in 3 days!
Such a fun spot to hit in Nashville! Live acoustic county music and great food. Make a reservation and enjoy the whiskey and good vibes!
Never thought id ever end up in nashville w my familly shelly cory and me the franco's.we visited the meuseum of johny cash, now on our way to memphis to see elvis house..

Be aware there are two seating and lots of downtown with nothing to do hard chairs and spiders everywhere. 
It's long hot and mediocre. Do not bring your kids.

This museum did not disappoint.  I came with my mom who grew up watching Johnny Cash and we both learned a lot.  There was a lot of neat memorabilia.  It is on the small side but it was nice to get through it in 45 minutes.

Man this was awesome, really fun reading about the history of the man in black. The grim reaper. Big daddy charcoal. The ooold crow catcher.
I do think this is worth the trip / price of admission. I also really enjoyed the guy who tears your ticket stub bears a striking resemblance to Old Charcoal Stick Johnny as I learned nobody ever called him. 

You learn a lot of cool facts about him here, like how sweet his house is and then that numnuts from the BeeGees burned it down the second he moved in. What a sad joke, this guy is the antithesis to Barry Gibb. But I digress, again, come through and bring your grandma with to make sure her tank top fits snug fresh out the gift shop. Get a ride here from one of the horse and buggy dudes just to hear him tell you that lil Richard lives on the top floor of the Motel 6 downtown.

Amazing place, the atmosphere was second to none. I've never been at a bar like it. The musicians are extremely talented, it blows my mind how they can play and sing so many songs as requested on the spot. They integrated the crowd regularly and get everyone to stand up and dance with the bar crew at intervals through the night. Would definitely go back again and again.

Can't comment on the food. Frozé was a little disappointing. I came just for the view and WOW! The rooftop bar was spectacular! Great views, awesome atmosphere. Live music on first floor was fun and traditional Nashville. I much preferred the style of the room on the 2nd floor with the DJ. Such a fun space that works great in the day and I'm sure is even better at night. Would definitely recommend!

Not a handicapped friendly facility.  Yes. They have a slanted ramp, but they make you stand without a place to sit for hours waiting to get in for a concert...even in the cold rain. Don't think they know the definition of ADA except for building materials. Certainly not in understanding pain issues.

Don't bother. Terrible service and very average food. Nothing special for sure. The staff seam nice but completely unorganized. 45min wait for food. Too many great burger placed to waste money on this one. Better luck next time guys
Great atmosphere, good selection of drinks, and great service from Danielle! The live music was fun and energetic!

WHAT A MESS. Took 20 minutes to get noticed. Took 20 more minutes for coffee. But wait, had to wait 15 more minutes for cream. Then food came (30 min later) and was cold and forgot the side of bacon. When it's the SEC weekend and a Saturday brunch you need more than 2 waitresses. Only thing good was the music. 

Save yourself. And don't go.

Awesome! There were so many awesome things! We got to see a short video on all the film work that Mr. Cash worked on--I never knew he was in so many movies! The chair he sat in on the "Hurt" video was there and the actual video was playing as well. It is a must for any fan! We also got to take pics with the man himself--with a green screen, of course.

Ordered a to go order yesterday about 15-20 minutes away. There was only one table there and when I arrived my order was still not ready. Weird. It was amazing though. I wish it had more fries, but I hadn't eaten all day so it was devoured. I highly recommend the pretzel bun burger with salmon and raspberry jalapeno jam. You can thank me later. I wish they did events like a sports night or music night like they used to...it has a cute vibe and staff is always kind. I would personally set up a music night if they'd let me, because I think it's a great place for it and could bring in lots of business. A sports night, like maybe half priced burgers on sundays or Mondays would be great...2-4-1 drinks or something to draw in business..this place has potential and if they are doing those things, I wouldn't know because  there's no marketing. I've never had a bad meal here. Biggest problem here is deciding...do I get waffle fries or sweet potato fries?? Oh the struggle.

Great beer selection and price.  Staff are always friendly.  Burgers are quality.  Fried pickles were a scosh too salty but the fact that there is a retro arcade next  door kind of offsets that.  Hickory Hillow needs more places like it, thankfull they are leading the way.

We noticed there was a cover charge as we were walking up, we quickly turned around and started walking away. They said forget about the cover and just come on in and check it out.

Man this place was dead. Must've been an off night. We ended up grabbing a round of drinks and grabbed a few tables for the group. The band was pretty good, played a mix of genres and songs. 

We decided to leave after a few songs ... too many other places we wanted to check out on Broadway.

The musicians are wonderful, but this is the most odd format ever.  For starters, it says on your reservation to keep your conversation to a minimum, inside voices, be respectful to others.  Well, we were in the back and the staff was chit-chatting away to the point where we couldn't even hear the musicians.  I had to go over and let one of the waitresses know that her voice really carries and she was making it hard to hear the music.  I guess we had the wrong impression given the instructions on the ticket and the name "Listening Room" for the venue.  There were 4 musicians on stools on stage, all really really great and super talented, but it was awkward to watch them while the others were singing.  It seems like they were competitive with one another rather than putting on a united show.  They were all distracted and fidgety while their colleagues were singing.  Maybe if there was some sort of muted spotlight type thing on the person that is performing and the others were in the dark it wouldn't be as noticeable.  The whole thing was just really uncomfortable.  We had saved this venue for our last night thinking it was going to be the highlight, but we left very disappointed.  I do not recommend it.

Good vibe, and the atmosphere is good. Nice lighting in the main table/audience area. Bartenders are usually friendly. If you go for music, know that the room gets loud as it fills up. There's no separation between the stage/audience area and the long bar, so if people get talking at the bar, the sound carries. Also there are louder bars across the street, so singer-Songwriters get drowned out if the doors and windows are open.
Less than a block off the main drag of Broadway, mostly the same as the other hole in the wall bars, but my group had a good time, good band, good bar service, clean individual restrooms.

Went here on a Friday night after 10 so we were only charged $6.00 to get in. It was ok, but like another reviewer wrote, they cater to the ones that keep throwing up the $20's and up. I didn't tip at all, once I could see what was going on.The later it got , the crowd started to get kinda wild, so we called it a night. The one and only time I've ever been, I may go again and then again I may not. It wasn't bad, so I'd recommend if asked for something a little different to do in Downtown.
Cilantro Avocado Burger on pretzel bun  (and organic sautéed spinach) - hella good - the hubs had the PBJO (burger with peanut butter & jelly with grilled onions!)
The food is amazing, but service usually fails. This place was way better with live music. I highly recommend the salmon burger on a pretzel bun. Their fries are killer too.

This is my favorite venue in town! It's a great size, the sound is great, the sound guy really knows how to get the best sound out of each band, regardless of the style. The drinks are affordable and are pretty stout! This is the best place to see live music in Nashville!
This place is awesome. The servers are awesome and super friendly. It was random find in Nashville and I'm happy I went!

We have been on the General Jackson 3 times now. It has really gone down hill!

The best part of the cruise for us was being able to go out and watch the lights of the city come into view after dinner, now with the later dinner time, we actually missed it because we were eating. 

Food was decent. It is a shame that they took the buffet away, some things I just don't care for.

The show hasn't changed much in the last 3 years. It is passable. 

This is a company retreat every year. I am so glad I had the chance to experience it before the dinner format change!

If you're in Nashville, this place is a must visit.  There is a lot of memorabilia.  It was one of my favorite places that we visited.  It's a beautiful tribute to Johnny Cash, and a great place for fans to visit.

It's also close to other bars/restaurants on Broadway.
So far not good. Waiting for 15 min for drinks. Had a hair in my water. Waiting on food. We will se

I was really really excited to visit this Museum! It is definitely a smaller museum, but there are a TON of artifacts from Johnny Cash's life and his time with Sun records. I enjoyed walking around and reading about his life and seeing such great items on display. I really enjoyed reading about his relationship with other notable singers like Jerry Lee Lewis, Elvis, Roy Orbison, etc. Music is life and brings people such enjoyment. Just walking around I was able to see so many people smiling and enjoying their time at the museum. The reason I am knocking off a star is because I think they have too many people in the museum at a time. I would have been fine waiting to get inside if that means I could have more room to browse. It just seems to be very congested in the museum which made it difficult for me to read everything I wanted to read. I think I was there for 1.5 hours, but I know I could have stayed much longer if there weren't as many people. 

I am glad I visited this museum and I do think you should go check it out if you have time. It's within walking distance to tons of bars and restaurants too so you can go here and then grab a drink or walk around some other shops downtown.

After a much anticipated visit, we unfortunately had a very disappointing experience. After ordering drinks and food, the bouncer came over to us and told us to quiet down despite a live band playing in the background. The manager of the bar then came over and made negative comments as well about our noise level.  Coincidently, our group included the only black person in the bar. I don't want to assume this was a racial issue; however, both the bouncer and manager made it pretty obvious that it was as our group did not raise our voices beyond the average bar noise level. I will not be returning to this bar.

For entertainment found this little place had great music and good bar in intimate and clean setting.  

Went back a few times.    Great little stop in.

I did both the cafe for coffee and the museum.  The cafe au lait was good.  The gift shop had some nice things, but hot damn is it expensive.  Who would pay $32.00 for a tank top?  The interior is nice.  The museum is cool, $18.00 is a bit pricey, but you can probably find discounts if you plan ahead.  The tour is self-guided.  There are quite a few neato things in the museum.  Guitars, gold records, outfits, letters, vidoes, photos.  Lots to look at.  It's mostly done chronologically, and separated by medium.  There are videos of his acting projects.  There is a small section devoted to Sun Records and other artists who started around the time of Johnny Cash.  The last thing is the video of "Hurt" played on loop.  I blubbered like a baby, it really is one of the best songs and videos.

Sat on top floor. Live music was good, prices affordable. Had pulled pork platter which fed both myself and my wife. Had 3 local beers which I enjoyed very much.

Only think I didn't like was that I could hear the live music downstairs at the same time.

I had a similar experience to the one Deanna had....my burger was raw and the managers apology was "I'm sorry you didn't like how your burger was cooked".  Me thinks he needs a little corporate training.
Bartender didn't know any liquors and the hinge on the kitchen door was broken so every time he went back there it was very loud.  Speaking of the door being broken, when he went back to tell the cook about my burger I could see the entire interaction (not favorable).
