Either way, Burger Republic is way closer to our house and extremely consistent so we won't go back to 360.
On a totally different note?  The restaurant was pretty clean!

Great small but mighty museum!! Love the amount of historical items and information, easy to wonder, read and enjoy. Makes us appreciate Johnny Cash even more as a singer, human being and a positive influence on others. Take the time for this when you visit.

Both burgers were delicious, and the onion rings were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside- just like they should be. 

Our only complaint was that the entire restaurant reeked of spray paint.  Apparently one of the neighboring businesses is doing some renovation and it was polluting the air.

This place is now closed.
the music is pretty much all hip hop and rap, theres a lot of smoke around and not that many people go on the dancefloor. pretty depraved

We recently visited the Johnny Cash Museum for a second time. We loved that new items from Johnny were in the exhibit. We also loves the new addition of the Sun Records stars. This museum is fairly small in space, but is still a must see for any Johnny Cash fan.
Good food, great live music, fast service during the show!!! We saw three amazing singer-songwriters perform!

The reason they receive a 1 star is because 0 is not an option. Went tonight with a group of 12 and food was TERRIBLE! Spent over $1000 and they had the nerve to charge us $28 for a credit card fee! Cost of doing business idiots! Food was absolutely horrible for ALL of us! I would NEVER go back.

The only reason I'm giving it two stars is because the venue itself is cool and has such potential to be amazing. The staff is super friendly and were really accommodating but the food was not good :( I'm sure that this place is fabulous for drinks and live music at night time but for that only. They should hire a creative chef and this place could be a 5 star worthy establishment!
The buffet was $18 of nothing. Everything was empty. I just had old eggs and a nasty Bloody Mary. How do you fail on a buffet?

This is probably one of my favorite hidden gems in Nashville. It was my husband and I's first time visiting and we have friends that are locals and brought us here. The food is okay- but the music is incredible. Being able to listen to such talented groups, hearing their stories is just magical. I'd highly recommend this spot to anyone who wants a true music experience on their trip. I would have never known about this place as it's off the beaten path. Be sure to reserve a spot ahead of time and arrive early if you want to be seated closer to the front of the stage.

So let me say this first, I normally don't do reviews RIGHT after eating. Also I had a few other lunch plans fall through and was in the area alone and not wanting a chain burger. I had heard about this place on another site (newschannel 5's story about the new hockey rink expansion). I do take this review with a grain of salt, literally, because a burger is a burger is a burger. That aside, I know that there are a TON of things going on in this area as far as expansion and revitalization, and this is a good step in the right direction. 

To the foooooooood! I kept it simple and ordered the 360 with everything on it. It arrived promptly with regular shoestring fries perfectly cooked and NOT over salted. My first bite into this burger was an explosion of salty, savory, and meaty goodness and I didn't get a lot of the pretzel roll. However the second bite gave me the home-run rating that I crave as a foodie. There was a nice 'snap' of the pretzel crust with a fluffy yet chewy roll. They definitely knocked it out of the park with the bun! The ingredients were good, blended well, and none really overpowered the other. I am not sure what kind of onions they use, but they tasted perfect for burgers! 

Anyway I digress, this was a bit expensive for lunch, my tab being around $10. Then again I'm one who doesn't care about spending a great amount for great food.

Thanks again for reading, and if you're in the area... check it out.

For me, I give it 3 stars just because its waaaayyyy too packed. Barely can walk of even stand in there. Had great music and good drinks. Had fun listening to the band play but literally had nowhere to move. Great decor and awesome bartenders but, again I emphasize the lack of space.

Absolutely the best bar on lower broadway! Plan on spending a few hours here. The entertainment is truly outstanding  . Will be back as a soon as possible. Thankyou for making my families last nite in Nashville the best!
Fun place to learn about Johnny Cash.  Not so good for kids as they would be bored
This is a must see for any Cash fan.  Great memorabilia; plenty of concert footage, videos, history and plenty of things I bet even you didn't know.

We didn't eat,  but we sat at the bar and Theresa was our bartender.  She was working her butt off trying to accommodate the large crowd for the 1pm show with Colby Dee, but we were still served in a timely manner. Thanks Theresa for making our stop here a pleasant one!

I'm not a huge Johnny Cash fan, but this museum was right off Broadway and we heard good things about it so decided to check it out. It was pretty cool to see all his stuff and learn more about him, though I expected it to be a little bigger than it was. There was also a room where they were playing video/music on a large projection screen but it got a little drowned out by the bass of the band playing next door. We got $1 off each person for being AAA members. It was still a little overpriced for being sort of small. A fun stop nonetheless.

There's 50/50 chance they will get your order wrong, but the food is good enough that it doesn't really matter. Except for the french fries, the french fries are always pretty terrible. 
The live music could be a nice touch, but I'll just say you can definitely tell that they aren't paying the musicians, and end up with the kind of quality you get for free. 

Best advice is just call in a few burgers to-go and maybe some fried pickles when you're feeling too lazy to cook dinner.
Surprisingly good hot chicken sandwich. It's a weird little place, but I enjoy seeing tinpan south shows there!

This museum is one of the best I've ever been to.  We just went there on Wednesday, May 11 and I was surprised there were a lot of people there in the middle of a weekday.  When you walk in there are many different kinds of t-shirts and gifts in their store.  General admission is $18.00 per person.  
     So much memorabilia it's unbelievable.  The exhibits start out with Johnny Cashs' childhood and his military service in the Air Force.  As you walk through the museum you can hear his music and see different documentaries on his prison performances and clips from his TV shows.  There are walls with all of his gold and platinum records, a history of his musical career, all of his 45 singles that he sold, all of his album covers, his 8 track tapes, and cassettes.  
     There is a small theater in the back of the museum where you can see a history of his acting performances ranging from Little House On The Prairie, Columbo, and film he did with Kirk Douglas called Gunfight.  They even showed a clip from his Saturday Night Live appearance.  Pretty funny stuff. 
     There is plenty of room to walk around in the museum.  It is very spacious.  They do allow pictures in there but no videos or flash photography allowed.  If you go to Nashville you have to see this museum.  It is great.
A very special venue where the music, not the crowd, gets top billing. I really enjoyed the moving performances last night from Rivers Rutherford, Bobby Ham Rick, et. al.

What a great place! This museum is not over-the-top or extravagant but a perfect representation of Johnny Cash's life. It is very well done and flows perfectly through his lifetime. Will return for sure!

the food here is pretty great as well as the music and the rooftop portion of it. the only downside is the bouncers are very rude which is never a good thing. hoping they chill out a little bit over time

Had a great time here, and I'll admit it helps that I really love Johnny Cash! From the love letters to June Carter Cash, big boots, guitars and his report car showing he did well in typing this museum is everything Johnny Cash.

Don't miss the room in the far back to the left. They play Johnny on the big screen and it's almost like you're watching him live.

I liked this more than the country music hall of fame, believe it or not. A definite must do in Nashville!
They need to hire more bartenders or open the other bar. I know you want to make tips but if you can't handle it, get more bartenders! Waited more than 15 minutes and just walked out.

Went here last Thursday for a private event. The entertainment was top-notch, and fantastic! I love dueling piano bars and this entertainment was by far some of the best. Unfortunately, the service was terrible. They only had two servers on staff to accommodate all of us. My server was Angel, she was rude and short with us. It took 30 minutes for our drinks to arrive (just 2 of us), and almost an hour for our food. The bar ran out of food. The price for my drink was $7 but on my bill it said $10, and she tried to tell me it was tax??? I looked up TN liquor laws and it says there is a by-the-drink tax of 15%, but 15% of $7 is not $3. It was so loud and she was so busy she just left, even though we wanted to order more drinks. I've waited tables before so I tried to give her the benefit of the doubt, but she was just terrible. We got up and went to the other side of the bar to order drinks directly from the bartender, who was fun and courteous. Overall, I would go again, but I would order directly from the bar.
Wow, listening room amaze me for their talents! Honestly, I am done for those noisy music at broadway, living room shine my eyes, highly recommended to try

Went there for brunch during a bachelorette party. The service was horrible to say the least. Upon arriving our server took our drink order, 25 minutes later we still had not gotten our mimosas or bloody marys. Mind, they poured the mimosas out of a pitcher so they didn't have to do much to "make" those. After getting our drinks, our orders were taken. The food was so-so but almost everyone of us had a something missing or wrong with our order. Additionally our orders didn't come out at the same time. We were a large group but their excuse was they only had 3 egg pans which just seems ridiculous for as large of a place as it was. 
After we were done eating and waiting to pay they kitchen sent us some hashbrown casserole which was good but at that point it was too little too late. On top of that gratuity was already added because of our party size. Overall I would not attend this place again for drinks/food. The band playing was good so that is a bonus. They were not understaffed when we went and we expected more from a place that wasn't busy.

You need better door management! It's mid day, you're not busy, but he wants to be rude!? Wow! No..we weren't drunk. Hadn't even had a drink?! Just wanted to listen to music and try your bar?! Wow! I'll make sure everyone knows how I feel. Love Dierks, but won't ever go back to this bar?!

We stopped in here on a Friday night, as we were passing through town and looking for a non-chain restaurant for dinner.  They were not too busy.  There were 4 or 5 open tables and we were told the wait was 20 minutes, but we only waited for 10 minutes.  Staff seemed nice and friendly. We ordered The Tropical Thunder and The Basic Pig.  Burgers were dry and fries were underwhelming (not crispy).   Definitely have had better burgers.  Priced ok for food.  Local beers on tap were tasty.  Would actually give this 2.5 stars out of 5.  Only reason for the 3 stars is the local beers!
Great place to watch great music. I will definitely come again next time I visit Nashville. The singers were all awesome. Service was also good. Can't beat the price to attend.

Amazing. My favorite stop in Nashville. The wings were out of this world. There were 6 of us and we all loved the artists, our food, & the drinks! Buy your tickets in advance because the shows do sell out on weekends.

We came here with several friends and had a great night! The band was hilarious and talented, the food was yummy (the wings were a bit too saucy), and the drinks were priced very fair! I suggest it for anyone looking for a good time!

If you love Country music, Pop, Blues or Rock n roll this is the wax museum for you! Definitely worth the $19 (If you order online) entry fee. It's 24 if you walk up. They also have a $39 VIP package that includes a tee shirt and a VIP lanyard. 
Definitely worth the trip! Friendly staff and nice atmosphere.

I was pre-disposed to love Big Bang because it's just like one of my favorite spots: Pat O'Brien's Piano Bar in New Orleans. Except that there's a cover (only $6, well worth it), the booze is cheaper, every woman in the entire crowd is married (unless they are the bachelorette), and the guys on the piano are younger, and funnier, and will basically play anything.  

We heard a lot of country classics, some Billy Joel, Janis Joplin, and some 80s hits...all songs you'd probably expect from a piano bar. But they also rocked out with very decent versions of songs by Eminem, Kanye, Lady Gaga and even threw in a Conan reference or two. The bartenders were fast and friendly and get up to dance on stage every once in a while, all in good fun.

The piano players are the stars of the show though; these guys are definitely talented, and they know how to work the crowd. Bohemian Rhapsody brought the house down, and Proud to Be An American degenerated into a chant of USA! USA! USA! All I know is that you haven't lived until you've seen 18 drunken louts* dancing together to fun. until one of them faceplants. 

And a good time was had by all.
___________

*Yes, they're with me.

You go in then down and up.  Left right down and up.  It's a maze.  Because of the building size they had to squeeze all the memorabilia into one building.  It's good venue but perhaps one day move it to a much more roomier place.
5 stars for what it has to offer.

$15 for two hours of parking, $18.65 for admission, and $25 for the t-shirt! As a record collector, I liked the audio, the 'mixing studio' and vinyl record exhibits. There were some real Sun records to drool over. Many exhibits had placards in Johnny's own writing and there were lots of costumes and guitars. The main drawback was the crowds. They don't restrict how many people are in there at a time so I couldn't even get to alot of things. There is no flow, so people will just stand and block an exhibit for ages.

It was my first time in Nashville, and I had a blast at this place. We sat at the bar and Bill was really awesome. He made my friend a drink that she absolutely loved. I enjoyed the cover band who was playing at the time. They are from Australia and I loved their song choices. There was also an amazing drummer playing with the band. Wish I would've caught his name so I could check out some more of his work. Kevin, can I email you?

This concept is so great, but the execution was disappointing.

We ordered tickets online for $12 each, a very reasonable price.  We arrived about 20 minutes before the show was set to begin.  There was a line wrapping around the interior of the building. We were told to wait in line to get "checked in". So we waited, then later they stopped checking people in and started calling party names. This tactic worked better, and they asked everyone to remain in line for courtesy purposes, which we appreciated, since by that time we were at the front of the line.  We ended up being seated at a table right up front, but far right of the stage.  We had waters waiting on the table for us, but a server never came.  We had to go to the lobby to get drinks since the bar inside was booked with table orders. At the lobby bar, I asked for a cocktail menu (since I had seen some interesting drinks recommended on Yelp), and the bartender told me that he didn't have the ingredients to make the cocktails from the menu but he could make me something and he asked what liquor I prefer. So, he made me a drink with vodka and club soda (which I don't like) but I drank it anyway. I appreciated the effort, but really would have preferred a cocktail from the menu. 

We eventually waved down a server to order food. He was very friendly, but not very attentive. The show was set to start at 8:30, and we got our food (including the appetizer) at 9:40.. and our silverware ten minutes after our food. We had to wave down other people to bring the things that our server forgot. Everything was bland, the food really didn't have any flavor, and I bet you can guess what the temperature of the food was like. We had pot roast, with macaroni and green beans (they were out of multiple side choices). The green beans were terrible. Our appetizer was fried green tomatoes, cold and bland, served with a tiny bit of some sort of mayo. Our friend at the table with us said the burger was terrible.

The show was really good. The musical talent was fantastic, and each of them had interesting stories and quips to go along with their songs. The ambiance and environment was excellent. 

If you decide to try out The Listening Room, I would suggest skipping the food and have low expectations for service. You will definitely enjoy the show!

We have been several times to this venue and have always enjoyed the artists presented. The atmosphere is casual and warm and the food and drinks are good. We keep returning so theyre definitely doing things right!
Bartender was rude & said we "wasted alcohol" & gave us snotty looks all night. Terrible wait staff..
Good beer selection, excellent burgers and killer sweet potato fries! Hard to beat 2 burgers, 2 beers and a free appetizer for less than $30. The joint is highly recommended and we'll be back!

We wanted to get a drink but we waited and waited and waited.  The bar was not packed and the poor bartenders were forced in to wearing skimpy clothing.  I would pass.  There was also only one bathroom.  Not good when you are out drinking.

We had been wanting to find a live music venue that isn't crammed full and in your face since moving here in 2016 and we have found it here! Our trip last night was a birthday present for my husband. Everyone was friendly. Service was prompt. Priscilla was our server and she was great! She even took a photo of us in front of the stage. Drinks are priced really well. Food was pretty good. Music was great. We look forward to our next visit!
GREAT customer service. Very delicious burgers and a good variety at the bar! Would recommend anybody to check this place out

It's a small venue, which can be good and bad. The good is that as far as being able to see the stage, you can from pretty much any part of the venue. The bad is that when it's crowded, you'll be pushed around, have drinks spilled on you, and standing so close that you can smell everyone's Body odor.

The food was very good, beef was nicely done. Drinks reasonable. Nice ride down the river. The show was EXCELLENT!! Loved it. 
Highly recommend, it was fun.
Little pricey, but hey, touristy thing, well worth it.

Decided to stop by this place for brunch on Sunday and so glad we did. We had reservations at a smaller spot around the corner, but the wait was over an hour.

My boyfriend and I were hungry, so I trusted Yelp and found this place. It's a cool rock and roll bar.

Their brunch mimosas are not your typical mimosa,s as in, there is not any orange juice in them. We're talking champagne and flavored vodka. 3 deep and I blew over the legit limit for blood alcohol level. How, you ask?! Well, I know because they have a machine that you can check your BAC level at the bar. 

I ordered their vegetable quiche of the day which had pimento cheese and sriracha in it. It was pretty yummy. Had a few sticks of jalapeno bacon on the side as well.

The best of the experience was our server. Super down to Earth and so awesome.

Favorite bar on Broadway! For sure need to stop in, loved the Dueling Piano. Request whatever song you would like and sing along to this comical version! NO Slayer request, though! lol Good drinks and great atmosphere!

We were very excited to learn of the new restaurant in the area and were eager to try it. The first time we stopped in for lunch and enjoyed the local farm raised cattle burgers. We enjoyed it so much, we returned with some friends a few days later for dinner. Their hot chicken is very delicious and I appreciate the local breweries they have on tap. Looking forward to this place growing and we will definitely be returning multiple times!
The prezel buns are great but the burger is meh, the services is meh.

The band was good but the bartender was horrible.  I think she is borderline schizo. We asked for a receipt and she went ballistic on us, using some pretty graphic language.  Of course, it was reciprocated and we were asked to leave. So nine of us left, along with a bunch of NY firefighters who witnessed her tirade.  The bouncer was a nice guy though.  Even out in the street, people told us that's the way she is.  I would skip this place.  There's plenty of others to choose from.

This place is so brilliant- the artists are so
Incredible, talented, and although I can't say that you will be hard-pressed to find a plethora of talent in Nashville, this is definitely a place that you should seriously consider going. Perhaps not for the food, but the drinks are wonderful and the experience is one of a kind.

Över förväntan! När jag först såg det här museet så var min första tanke: jösses, ytterligare ett sätt att profitera på och exploritera en bortgången ikon. 
Men...  Så vid en händelselös påskdag 2016 så betalade jag de $17 inträdet kostade och vart glatt överraskad och imponerad över hur detaljerat och respektfullt de här lyckas berätta Johnny Cash livshistoria. 

Här finns utställt massor med personliga saker som hans (och hans fru June's) instrument, kläder, brev mm. som presenteras på ett bra sätt tillsammans med fakta, filmer och förstås hans musik. Genom hela museet finns många stationer med tryckkänsliga surfplattor monterade där man kan ta på sig anslutande hörlurar och oftast välja mellan flera olika filmklipp och låtar att se och lyssna på. 

Man har tänkt in hela mannens liv, från vaggan till graven och allt däremellan. Man lyfter fram och har utställningar om hans samarbeten med Sun records och Million Dollar Quartet samt The Highway Men. Man har två stycken filmrum här där man kan sätta sig ned en stund och se hans framträdande respektive filmroller (han "fuskade" lite som skådespelare). Här Finns också en station där man kan lyssna på cover versioner som andra artister har gjort på hans låtar. 

Så här är ett toppenställe att uppleva och ta in "The Man In Black" Mr. Johnny Cash!

My teen sons and I enjoyed this museum. It is very professionally done, and my kids learned a lot. In addition to a LOT of personal and professional Cash memorabilia, it also has sections on the Carter Family and the other members of the Sun Studio Million Dollar Quartet
The layout is VERY confusing. The exhibits are narrow, and as you wait your turn to read the letters Johnny wrote to June, you will be forced to listen to tourists speculate out loud on how long Johnny spent in prison (he never went to prison).
We arrived midday on a Saturday, and it was jam-packed, with about 50 people waiting in the lobby. The entrance is VERY poorly designed, with three cash registers serving people trying to buy tickets to get in AND those buying gift shop merch. I have never seen this done in any museum. Gift shop should have its own separate register. There was a lot of confusion about this for folks pouring in off the street.
Other than that rocky start, it's a great stop in the middle of downtown Nashville and a well-deserved tribute for someone who would be on the Mt. Rushmore of country music.

Paid in advance for a Luncheon and River Cruise.  The boat was down for a repair but the staff promised a refund on the cruise portion.  The food was buffet style and nothing to rant about.  I have contact them twice and no reply.  The entertainers were very good! Huge waste of money for the food and cruise portion and too bad their management can't follow up on the promise to refund.

We came here on a whim after seeing a show at the Grand Ole Opry.  We were planning on just grabbing a drink and heading out.  We ended up staying for four hours!  The guys on the piano were unreal, for lack of a better word.  We were rolling laughing and singing.  There wasn't a beat missed in 4 hours, they just kept alternating pianists.  
 
We went on the night of the Alabama versus Auburn game, and the dueling pianists were taking cash for dueling the school songs.  It was fantastic.  It's a very crowd interactive scene.  

The bar service was very quick.  And drinks were cheap and strong...

This was a great Cash Museum. Self- guided tour. Lots to read about his history, lot of things to see from guitars to clothing and even some furniture. 
The little coffee shop was great with the 2 classic bean brew! And, of course, the gift shop. 
Thanks for the great reminders and trip down memory lane.

"Eat, Drink, and Be Local", it says on the back of the 360 Burger t-shirts.

I am not a drinker, so the offering of a selection of craft beers does not resonate with me and my dinner experience. But the time, money, and space that would have been taken up by such things were better spent on the incredible burgers and other sandwiches coming out of the kitchen at such an unassuming spot outside of Nashville.

With a name like 360 Burger, the specialty is not a mystery but the secret that sets this particular place apart is one that is becoming a trend throughout the country: a commitment to fresh, local ingredients. Fresh ingredients, prepared correctly, simply taste different, and in the best way possible. Those who know and love food, especially burgers, cannot be disappointed.  The beef for the burgers at 360 is touted as "certified grass-fed, DNA-trackable beef". Once again, taste the difference. The beef is expertly prepared, no matter which burger is being delivered to the table, and the flavor that comes through is one that cannot be duplicated at a national chain, much less a fast food restaurant that is accessible on every city block. The added touch is the selection of breads available for each burger, ranging from a classic brioche bun to a delicious pretzel bun to Texas Toast or a fresh croissant. Burger King may tell people they can have it their way, but 360 Burger delivers on that statement in a far bigger and better fashion.

The Bacon Basil Pesto burger is one of the more unique flavor combinations on the menu, no matter which protein it is paired with (burger, salmon, turkey, or chicken). As a traditional burger, the unmistakable basil pesto is accented by the smoky Applewood bacon and the woody flavor of the Swiss cheese. 

The Farm Boy is touted as "breakfast on a bun", and that statement is not a joke.  A breakfast burger with ham and a fried egg, pulled together with maple cream cheese on a croissant, the concept is easy and the flavors are bold but the execution is a problem. The croissant is massive, making an already large burger almost unworkable.  Don't get me wrong, I like a big, messy burger experience. Very quickly, though, the Farm Boy goes from a sloppy burger to a knife-and-fork diner garbage plate, trying to assemble all the pieces together bite by bite, rather than retaining the ability to eat the sandwich by hand. The burger is served on the croissant by default, but Texas Toast is a better option in this instance. But it is delicious no matter what!

Carnivores don't just feast on red meat, and the Blackened Salmon is the best option for those who want something a little different.  Let's face it, salmon is easy to screw up, as is nearly any fish. The salmon at 360 is seasoned and prepared perfectly, and that is what counts. With a brioche bun, lettuce, and tomato, what is already far more than just a fish sandwich is taken to another level with a fresh, rich garlic aioli and is paired beautifully with the buttery salmon and its Cajun seasoning. The Blackened Salmon burger is the best overall option for those seeking a healthy meal packed with a variety of flavors.

If eating healthy is not a priority when you walk through the door, forget the menu and order the Slippery Pig. The foundation is what is generally known as a "Juicy Lucy" burger, in this instance stuffed with Monterey Jack and Cheddar cheeses along with bacon bits, then topped with American cheese, more bacon, and garnished with leaf lettuce and tomato. Everything a burger seeks in a burger is present on the Slippery Pig. The pretzel bun and the brioche bun are both excellent choices for the Slippery Pig.

Side items may not be a featured dish at a restaurant of any kind, but are worthy of attention when they are so good that they stand out when placed next to an equally impressive entree.  The sweet potato fries are some of the best I have ever had. Obviously made fresh and not frozen, the fries were crispy and go well with a side of ranch. If your conscience will not allow you to pair a giant burger with a deep fried side, the fresh steamed broccoli was quite good as well.

The service was fast, friendly, and attentive. The atmosphere was modern, bright, and features a permanent setup for live music performances that are a weekly fixture. Parking is plentiful and convenient, and the establishment is located next to the Game Galaxy Arcade, sure to be a hit with any video game loving Millennial like myself.

Overall, 360 Burger is a gem, and sure to be a hit with every foodie that is in the greater Nashville area. Sadly, it is six hours from my home in southern West Virginia, but with more and more travel in the works in the coming months, every trip to and through Nashville will include a stop at 360 Burger. This place is not just a restaurant, it's a destination for those who consider food to be a personal passion, because those at 360 certainly do, and the evidence shines through on every plate.
A little pricey but very cool and interesting.  Learned a lot of stuff you would have never known about Johnny Cash.

This place is an inspiring place to go specially if you're an Artist/Musician...It easy to get in. Inside there's a lot of his memorabilia from his childhood and how he enters the music business, there's lots of things to read about so if you're going here make sure you spend at least two or three hours...They had a little gift shop...It would had been great if they had a coffee shop and if the place is bigger...Everything is cool and a recommendable place to go for museum visit...

Went here on a Sunday. Got the cheeseburger with everything and bacon.  The burger came on a pretzel bun.  OUTSTANDING!!!  The fries reminded me of the ones my mom used to slice herself and fry.  The beer chili is definitely something everyone needs to try bc it's that good.  I would definitely to back to this place....especially if I'm in Antioch. I recommend this restaurant for burger lovers.

In reality, I would rate this place closer to a 3.5.

I came here a couple of weeks ago with some friends and my husband. The place is much bigger than I had pictured. When the musicians started, the place was full, but there was still space to move around. I liked the place already. Not being big (or adventurous) drinkers, I just ordered a glass of white wine while my husband ordered a Corona. There was but one option for vegetarians so he ordered that portobello mushroom sandwich while I ordered the shrimp po'boy. I'm usually a sucker for po'boys. 

I actually really like the look and feel of the place. I love the concept of respecting the music and the musicians; that talking (out loud) is not "proper etiquette" in the middle of a performance. The food had arrived in a timely manner, as well as the drinks. To be honest, I wasn't the craziest fan of the food. In fact, before writing this review, I had to go to their website and review their menu, just to jog my memory of what exactly was it that I ate. So, one word to describe the food, unmemorable. What I DO remember are their homemade chips. I'm one of those people who eats all of her main food but barely touches the sides. But this time, there were some main entree leftovers and the chips were completely polished off. The only downside was that the chips seemed unevenly seasoned - some had just a dusting of the seasoning, the others tasted like there was an accidental dumping of the seasoning on them.

I would've rated the place a bit higher based on the ambiance, music, the concept, the great service, and the delicious homemade chips. However, before coming to the cafe, one has to purchase the tickets for a specific musician one came to see. We had bought the tickets to see someone else and ended up with four musicians on the stage, none this specific musician. While I mostly enjoyed their music, I still didn't get what I came to see. I really didn't like that - there was no offer for a refund either. No apologies for this little mishap. The tickets were cheap ($5 a person) but great service would've gone a long way in this case.

Great show and very clean, airy, open space with lots of seating -- totally different atmosphere than most of the music venues downtown. Free valet parking, which is a big plus in this location. The website has a show schedule and they accept reservations. Free admission, but remember food and drink sales are what pay the bills. Still - come for the music, not the food.

Just back from CMAFest. We returned to Swingin' Doors for the legendary Bloody Marys. Wow-wish we hadn't. The drinks were still great (though overpriced), but the service (especially the manager) was very disappointing. It's a tough (but profitable) week in Nashville, I get that, but the rest of town was shining with great service - Swingin' Doors not so much.

Good venue. Drinks were cheap and there is plenty of room to hang out and not be crammed against people. The cover on Friday was $10. I thought that was a little high, $5 seems more reasonable. The band was ok, but I probably wouldn't go back here and pay a cover when there's plenty of free live music at other bars.

I have been coming here for over a year and have found the service and quality of food to be of the highest quality.  Justin, Brandon and the rest of the staff always give me a warm welcoming hello.  It kinda reminds me of Cheers..."sometimes you wanna go where everybody knows your name'!  I've only been there a couple of times when there was music, but the artists were always on point!  I highly recommend this place to friends and family!

Really fun vibe! $6 cover but checked in on yelp for $2 off. Lots of oldies and the whole crowd gets involved. There was one pianist that we really loved and had the voice of an angel. Would come back again for fun pregame with a small group

This place was amazing! There were 6 of us and we all loved it! The musician/ song writer were fantastic! Loved listen to their stories and music. We loved our food. My sister got the turkey sandwich- she loved it. I had the fried green tomatoes- yum. Our waitress was attentive and did a great job. I would highly recommend this place- it was one of our favorite things we did in Nashville

I was once a frequent visitor of the big bang, until the last experience I had there. I ordered two rum and cokes for me and my girlfriend. However, mine was missing the rum part. I noticed this upon first sip, it was only coke. I'm very understanding and get that during busy times people can often be forgetful. So, I politely informed the bartender that my rum and coke was missing rum. The bartender had the courage to question my judgement on this, then took my glass, took a sip of it. I wouldn't be giving this review right now had he simply just made me another one without questioning the customer. I wouldn't go to this bar unless you want to put up with bartenders that treat customers like 3rd class citizens.

Loved the concept and the artists playing then we went. This was our first visit to Nashville and a friend told us to check this place out. The food was nothing special and service was average. there are much better places to eat, but if you're into country music, the round table act is a must see.

Been here for 1 1/2 hours and having a blast!!!!  Should be 20 stars!!!!!     Music is awesome. Can not describe how great. Funny. Perfect sound. Great entertainment.  I need more stars. A must go to in Nashville

Did not even get in the door. Made my friend dump her water that she's carrying around because it's 100 degrees out. Told me I could not come in because I had a backpack. It's a small backpack that's a purse. Needless to say, won't ever go to this damn place. No loss, plenty of other better places to go in this fine town that are okay with water bottles and backpacks.

My boyfriend and I booked this at the recommendation of someone who had been to Nashville as well as tourism guides.  The food was ok - the first vegetables we had gotten since arriving in Tennessee! Alcoholic drinks were a bit pricey and you didn't have any choice but to purchase the souvenir cup.  The performance was exactly what you would expect for a showboat but it was a ton of fun.  They played a wide range of country songs, the performers were all very talented.  Best part was after the choreographed show some of the guitarists went up to the top deck and play some more and interacted with the crowd.  A bit corny, a bit honky tonk, but why else would you come to a city like Nashville??
Great Museum if like you Johnny Cash, this is a must see when you in Nashville...  Lots of memorabilia and you have countless opportunities to listen to The Man in Black....

After spending the weekend in Nashville, The Listening Room gets an A+++++ in music and service. We attended the Song Suffragettes writer's showcase and were pleased with the quality of music these young ladies presented. Far and away from the drunken noise of Broadway! I ordered the fried green tomatoes...they were ok. Can't say they overwhelmed me, but I came here for music. Service was outstanding compared to any other venue we've been yet. The staff is constantly moving and very attentive without being in your face. Since the Bluebird seems so hard to get into, check out the Listening Room Cafe. Did I mention there was no cover, either on this Monday night???

Food was fine, service was fine.

I literally signed up just to put this comment on here.

Every time I've been here it's been relatively slow. Regardless if the house is packed or if we're the only ones there.
I don't typically mind because the food is good - especially for the area (Antioch). As far as the best burgers in Nashville? - No, definitely not.

For the time crunched lunch goers - I recommend ordering it to go. A group of 4 of us went around 11:30 and didn't get our food until 12:30 - needless to say we had to get it to go. Worst part about it was all of our orders had something wrong with it and we didn't notice until we got back to the office.

If you're looking to try it out -- definitely go when you have some time to sit and wait.
The street of this museum and the front of entrancy museum smell so bad .... plenty of hangover not super cleaning after the wild night.
I  visited 360 Burger today for the first time. It was wonderful, I had a burger on Texas Toast. My friend had the wings. The quality was worth the price.
I enjoyed the areas where you got to listen to music.  All the outfits and video were well displayed.  Worth the time.

Stopped in for food, building clearly says "Late Night Menu" on the side. Walked in and sat down, the man came over and acted like we were the biggest inconvenience, told us we would have to go to the bar if we wanted to order food. We asked for our table to be wiped off because it was filthy so he threw a towel at the table. We left and went next door. Horrible place with horrible service, we had a large group so they missed out on a nice bit of money :) Please don't waste your time.

Awesome is all i can say. If you are a Cash fan this is the place to go. I learned some stuff i did not know. I love the memorabilia, they had great pics, and a little theater to watch some old clips. It was cheaper then i thought it would be. They also have a store where you can buy some great stuff.

Eeehh. This was not a great experience for me. 

With out of town guests, a group of us decided to do a touristy brunch at the Listening Room Cafe. We came in around 10:30am with live music starting at 11:30am. Our table had about 7 people and the place was pretty empty with the exception of maybe 5 other tables (the place is pretty large). 

They offer a buffet for $18.00 that looked very similar to a continental breakfast at a Holiday Inn. No thanks. So we sat down and looked over the menu. I decided on the veggie flatbread with bacon instead of french fries that come with it normally. They offer bottomless mimosas/bloody mary's for the reasonable price of $15.00 if I remember correctly. I did not partake but had a sip and they were pretty solid. Not all orange juice and mixed properly. That's where the good ends. 

We waited an hour for our food. Then they broke restaurant rule #1. They brought out 3 entrees and then we waited at least another 10-15 minutes before the rest of our table got their food. Seriously? No one had silverware either, so we had to wait be able to eat our brunch. I was very cranky at this point and starving. Much to my chagrin, I discovered that my veggie flatbread was not a pizza, but rather a clump of veggies and a tiny bit of hummus in a thick bland pita, and made like a sandwich. Huh? Since when does flatbread = sandwich?  On top of that it was bland and boring once I started eating. The bacon was OK and they brought out french fries anyway. Unfortunately, the poor food didn't stop there. The burger was just OK, the chicken and waffles had completely unseasoned and dry fried chicken that needed salt. It was a huge portion, so I ate some of that since my flatbread was not good and left me hungry. I was not a happy diner. NOTE: One person ordered the pancakes and said they were very good, so all the food wasn't a let down, but I can't speak from experience.

I must shed light on the performers who were very good and entertaining. They were the only saving grace of this meal and sounded awesome. It was definitely neat to be able to enjoy their music at this venue. Should I ever return, I would not eat here but would get drinks and listen to the music. The place has a cool vibe and would be fun to do without the pressure of a meal.

Bartenders were kinda rude. There were wrappers and napkins all over the sticky floor around the crowded high tops. We visited on a busy Saturday night, but I've worked in plenty of bars and restaurants that we took pride in keeping spotless regardless of volume. The endless scrolling photos of bartenders in skimpy clothes twerking on the TVs was exhausting. This isn't a club in NYC or Vegas. People are visiting Nashville for a reason, so a bit more authenticity to the city's roots would be nice instead of promoting the chicks that are slinging your bottled domestic beers (cause they don't serve a single draft). The band sound-checked for like 30 mins and then hopped off the stage and didn't play any music. Overall, pretty disappointing experience. 2 stars cause the decor was nice and I like Dierks lol

Go here for the music which was excellent but do not go here for the food. I had their signature smoked pork steak which was way over cooked and very tough and overpriced. The pecan fried okra had no taste of pecans what so ever. But the music was outstanding which is why I gave them 3 stars. The music and music venue was worth 5 stars but the food was barely worth 1.

I ate so much today
All I could do is come home and lay down
The best burger
In town...
And the waffle fries
Makes the burger
I'm steak full...

Just got home from my first experience at 360 Burger. Here are the pros: good burgers, worth visiting again just for that. Sides are decent. Beer selection also decent - lots of local brews, so good on them. Go Nashville! Cons: woefully understaffed, friendly servers, just not enough of them. And the worst part was: the food took 30 minutes to come out. Two burgers. Thirty minutes. That's way too long. I *might* go back, but a word to the wise: don't go hungry.

Not a bunch I can add here to the existing reviews except that SOME of the servers there appear or act to be a little "snobby."  As if they are doing us a favor by visiting and keeping their establishment alive...?  Again, not a major deal, but on a couple of occasions I got that feeling.  Other than that, cool venue, nifty little menu for food and beverages, nicely priced, great outdoor patio, and they bring in some great musicians!  Definitely worth checking out!  The valet option is nice too.

The service was awesome! Very fast and wonderful food. We are from the St. Louis area and just
Made it from a long drive and wanted a nice hamburger. This place was great! I read reviews about an old menu vs new menu....didn't matter. If you are an out of town person and like burgers....make this part of your trip!!!

Came here for a bachelorette party and had a blast! There is a lot of space, which was definitely welcomed after being packed into some of the other Nashville bars. We were able to get drinks at the back bar without having to wait. The bartender was friendly. 
I really liked the fact that they really take dueling piano up a notch with a drum set and occasionally 3 musicians up on stage: 2 pianists + a drummer. Two complains though. First, they said that it was $20 to make a song request. However, I definitely saw one of the pianists taking requests ahead of my $20 request from others who paid $5 - $10... Second, the set up is a bit weird. There are tables everywhere, but the music was good and we wanted to dance. I wish they had a dance floor! Even a small one on the side! Other people wanted to dance too, because once we started dancing, others joined in. 
I think that this bar would be a solid 4 star place, if they only added a dance floor and didn't require $20 to get my request in (or maybe I just got duped)

Phenomenal collection of Johnny Cash memorabilia & portraits of the man from his music! I loved the way the museum created interactive exhibits by allowing you to view old tv clips, a short film about JC tv & movie career & a patriotic tribute of JC. These experiences plus the poetry and handwritten memorabilia make this museum a must see for country music fans! 
I love the way you can see JC's music emerging and the different decades he spans as an artist. One of my favorite items were the extra photos from the photo shoot of JC & June Carter on their first album together. Their expressions tell the story and make you feel like you're going back in time. The other interesting facet is the stations where you can hear JC's famous "Walk the Line" in all forms from old records to 8 tracks, cassettes, cds and mp3s. Very informative!

Really great atmosphere and food.

I had the privilege of trying the Avocado Burger and thoroughly enjoyed it. The fries were cooked and seasoned very well. And the servers and hosts were so pleasant to talk with.

Highly recommend this place, and plan on returning for lunch today.

Enjoyed the music and it has a nice location. However, the tator tots were so salty I couldn't eat them and the nachos were cold when they came out. The chips were very salty as well. I'm not sure if our server was having an off night, but she was not friendly... I would come for the music again but definitely not for the food or service in the upstairs area.

We rushed into Whiskey Row to beat the heat on 4th of July. We loved how they had the stage set up so everyone in the bar had a good view. I got "Dierks' Lemonade" which was delicious. For $13 it was pretty on-par with the price of cocktails in Nashville. While we only stayed on the first floor, the ambiance was nice and the crowd wasn't wild. It was nice to see that the age of visitors ranged from kids with their parents to folks in their 60s-70s.
All around great place.  Great live music, great bar food and great drinks.  Mark is a super friendly bartender!

360 burger was so good! Our server was very friendly and attentive! I ordered "the king" and it was amazing! My boyfriend ordered the bayou bleu. Never in my life would I think to put shrimp on a burger. So delicious!!

Had a few people tell me about 360
Burger and after reading reviews, I had to try. There is nothing like a big, juicy burger! I couldn't decide between the Santa Fe, margherita or cilantro avocado burger. I chose the cilantro avocado since it is the one I kept hearing about and for good reason! I ate every. single. bite. Sweet potato fries and all. And I'm a short, petite lil thing...it was THAT good! I will be trying those other two, too!
Could not have been a better burger and sweet potato fries.  And, great place to watch sports on big screen.

I really enjoyed the music. As far as the food. The humus was amazing. The salad with goat cheese, strawberries and pecans was weak. Pretty much all lettuce. Found a few pecans and cheese sitting at the bottom.
Song Suffragettes were awesome.  Would love to review the food, but we still don't have it over an hour after ordering.....
I'll miss this place more than words. Cheers to you blue bar. You will always hold a piece of our heart
Brought my mom to the museum. Love it!!! Very informative and loved all the items from his life. I recommend to make it a part of your trip to Nashville.

I'm giving this place four stars because I do like it, but not giving 5 STARS because of the bartender working at 3pm Monday at main bar.  The short haired blonde bartender is super unfriendly and too busy texting and being rude to help people! Other than that the music is fantastic and place is beautiful! Everyone else working there is amazing!

Very disappointed with the service of this place. We came for a bachelorette party and got a table on the second floor on August 11 in the afternoon. There were eight of us at a table. We ordered some drinks and appetizers to tide us over before dinner. We received our drinks at a timely manner. We ordered three appetizers (artichoke dip, southern fries, and the pretzel platter) and waited over an hour. From what we observed, we were one of a few tables to order food. We constantly had to go out of our way to ask our waitress, a blonde woman in black, where our food was and how long it would take. She did not give us specific answers and just stated that she doesn't know and she'll check. She never got back to us. We were getting more and more upset as other tables got their orders before us even though we ordered our appetizers before them. We finally were fed up after about an hour and a half of waiting and asked her to cancel our orders. Another woman came over and stated that there was a mix up, and that our order was accidentally cancelled. We are very disappointed in this as we checked up and asked about our food throughout the one and a half hour of waiting for three appetizers. 

We got the check and while the appetizers were taken off and the drinks were discounted, they should've comped the entire check as they did not communicate and made us wait far too long before telling us our order was 'accidentally' cancelled. 

This was a huge downer on the bachelorette and would not recommend anyone to come here.

I was very impressed with the singers/songwriters, but the food was terrible.  I ordered the hot chicken, which is supposed to be a Nashville signature dish, and it completely lacked spice. The only thing the chicken did taste like was formaldehyde with a touch of dry rub.  The only redeeming part of the dinner was the good beer selection.

First time I went it was great. Burger was DELICIOUS! Atmosphere was great. 

Next time I went and the burgers were not as great. Maybe 2/3 months since my first visit. My burger was greasy and my bun was falling apart as I ate the burger. 

Definitely recommend if you're looking for some quick food and kicking back with friends.

Had PBJ&O burger made from grass fed beef. Absolutely delicious!
Staff were extra attentive!

We went to Dierks Bentley's after leaving a bar for poor service. Went to second floor bar with some friends.   Bartender was friendly and personable and suggested some appetizers.  Food was awesome. Atmosphere was great.  Really nice place.
What a great lineup of songwriters.  I can't believe the quality of music for the price.  Nashville is so lucky!

Ugh, this place was so disappointing. The only reason it gets a single star is that I think it was our servers first time ever serving a party over three. 

The atmosphere is pretty great which makes it even more disappointing on how bad everything was. They have live music and it's a cute venue. 

We went as a large group for brunch and to share one menu between five people. The food took entirely too long to get to our table. When I asked if i could use the 50% off coupon offered when checking in on Yelp, she said she would ask the manager. I never received a small plate or an answer. Not cool for a Hangry girl. 

I personally ordered the French toast. This was a good size portion (probably the only meal on my end of the table that could actually be considered a meal). The French toast tasted great, but the menu informed me that it would be topped with candied cashews, but no, I didn't receive candied cashews. When I asked if I was supposed to have some on the order, they returned with a bowl of dry cashews...... Seriously? 

My boyfriend ordered the TLR breakfast which was a meal made for ants. We had to stop on the way home to get him more food. 

When we asked for our checks, our server went individually to everyone to get their orders again and it took extremely long to get our checks THE FIRST TIME. They were all wrong, so she took them back and went around again asking our orders. We got our checks a second time, and one group was completely omitted. Yes, I understand splitting checks is difficult, but I guess third time is the charm. When the last group finally got their check, it was wrong again, but they were already late for work (not anticipating the hour and a half it took to get the checks) so they just paid it and left. 

Sad day, listening room.

One of the funnest dance bars in East Nashville. If you are looking to go out dancing in Nashville, and not head to Broadway, then Basement East is a great option for you. The drinks are pretty cheap, the dance floor is huge, and you always get s fun and young crowd. Basement East is also located close to a lot of other bars in East Nashville, within close walking proximity.
We loved it. The service was great and so were the drinks. Definitely worth a try. Thanks Kayleigh.
This place is like a cafeteria, the hosted needs a huge tip or you are off to the side. Not the place in Nashville go! Unimpressed!!!!!!

The entertainment was great. We were there on Tuesday and they had a group of singer song writers. We stayed for two shows, drinks are reasonable. The food was a total disappointment. I had a burger which was passable. All of our food was not hot. Caesar salad with chicken, the chicken was barley there.  Chicken and dumplings eich ! Tasted like Campbell's soup. Void of chicken and served on mashed potatoes. Really two starches. What were they thinking. My food rating would be a one or two. The entertainment and atmosphere was a 4. Would only return for drinks and music

If I were just basing this on the entertainment and format, I would give this a 5-star rating, but when considering the service and food, it drops to a 3-star.

We arrived around 7:30 p.m. not knowing how the showings at this place work. From what I gathered, there are a few "shows" each night. They seat for each showing, begin serving, and various musicians play for the next hour and a half to two hours. Our show was set to seat at 8:00 p.m., so the host told us we could either wait 15 minutes or so until the band wrapped up at the bar or outside on their large patio. We opted for outside, since the weather was beautiful. About 15 minutes later I walked over to the door where the host was standing. He commented that the band decided to play a little longer than scheduled. I jokingly said, "Yeah - likely story," to which he responded with attitude that they were "all just a bunch of music loving hippies around here who don't care much for time anyway." SCOFF! Just because I got dressed up that night doesn't mean he should assume that I'm not also a music-loving hippie without much care for time! I normally wouldn't be offended at that kind of remark, but it was his tone of voice when he said it that was offensive.

Anyway.

We went inside soon after this little incident and proceeded to ask him where we should sit, since it seemed there were reservations to consider. He said we could sit at any table where there were no people, so we headed for one near the stage and sat down. He didn't bring us menus, take our drink order or clear our table.

About 15 minutes later, our waiter came. He was seemingly confused as to whether we had hung around from the previous show or if we had just been seated. We told him we just sat and he quickly cleared our table. He asked if we were seated there or if we chose it ourselves. We told him the host said to sit where ever we wanted (he said the host was supposed to seat us). He asked if we got menus or a drink order taken yet. We said neither (apparently the host was supposed to do both these things, too). Luckily, he quickly made up for the service the host was lacking. He brought us our two pints and appetizers relatively quickly, was hot on the water refills, and our entrees came not long after our appies.

The show was great, too. I loved the format, having so many acts come on along with a host to tie everything together. All the performers did a great job and it was nice to see so much camaraderie among them - they all seemed to know each other and helped one another out during technical difficulties or if someone needed a fill-in percussionist, etc. It was more like a mini festival inside a super awesome music venue.

For your NYers: the venue itself reminded me a lot of The City Winery. There are lots of tables and chairs, standing room near the back, and a decent-sized bar area.

Despite the holier-than-thou host, I would still come back here for more great up-and-coming musicians and tasty food, too. Get the fried pickles, but don't get the full size - it's pretty much a pound of pickles.
Neat and fun place to visit worth the money to check out. Very informative on his life.

Do I really need to review the BEast?! In short, check calendar, if something interests you, go. The BEast is local, the owner is a legend, and they bring in some really amazing acts. Even if you're on the fence or just want to hear live music, go! It's intimate enough, the bathrooms are decent, and the pub is a nice refuge from the main area. BEast for life!

Came in because we got a groupon and the reviews seemed good. The place had about a dozen customers on a Saturday at 7pm. The server was nice, the musical talent was good, the margaritas were yummy. But this place is so old, rundown and smelly, just not taken care of - booths falling apart, paint peeling... Our wings were dry and we had to eat outside with the parking lot for a view and the really good music from the live band at the adjacent restaurant muffling ours because they allow smoking inside this place :( The waitress didn't know how to use our groupon because after my husband paid the bill I realized she took only half the voucher price off  the bill. Oh well, lesson learned.

This was a fun night! We took our seven-year-old on this little cruise, and I'm sure he was the only child :-) thank you to all the adults who put up with the movement and questions :-) do you help keeping entertained and happy! Met a great lady from California on the deck, and look forward to your following roller derby!!  Seeing downtown Nashville at night, and the bridges was pretty cool, and worth the trip down the river.  The food was good, and the drinks are great! The entertainment was pretty cool...or we can shoot the highlight of the evening was when the girls stood for a picture with Johnny.  They were amazing and so kind! I'm sure he will remember this forever!

Great show, a bit on the pricey side if you take the evening trip.   Not really worth the $$.  Dinner is not good, not well prepared and the quality is very poor.  The steak, which is supposed to be NY strip is anything but!    A nice way to spend an evening on a paddle wheel boat with nice entertainment, but eat somewhere else.

The staff was very pleasant. I had the eggplant Parmesan. I found it to be too thickly sliced, which meant that the eggplant was not cooked evenly through. I'm a vegetarian and it's clear from the sparse number of options that the place probably specializes in meat, so take my food critique with a grain of salt. The live music was not so good. The music was loud to the point of preventing comfortable conversation where my fiance and I were sitting. So, if it's so loud that it demands attention, it should be a bit more compelling. Overall, I came in with high hopes based on previous reviews and was underwhelmed.

Had a private party at the Listening Room Saturday night. Had a great time, the manager is awesome. Would highly recommend for a private dining buy out.  Casual, local feel. A great time was had by all!

Went here on a weekday evening. Had decent service (the place was dead) and a good burger. Then went here on a Saturday for brunch. Terrible service. Not only was I ignored half the time, but multiple people came in complaining that hey had been waiting at the front for someone to seat them or something but were never acknowledged.  They advertise bottomless bloody Mary's which were mediocre at best (I wasn't expecting amazing out if bottomless). Biscuits and gravy... Well lets just say I've had better at Denny's. Biscuits were dry and chewy and there wasn't enough gravy even if they were moist and fresh.

Music: The weekday night was good. They had a songwriters round that wasn't too bad. Saturday they had a pretty good playlist going but then let some guy walk in off the street and start playing. Not sure what that says about their music standards. The guy was decent though.

It gets four stars because of the music, definitely not the food (two stars).
We went for brunch because of the music so it was worth it and we are going back.

I am a big Johnny Cash fan so for me this Museum was worth it for me. It is 18.00 dollars to get into the museum and the museum itself is not that big it takes about 5 mins to walk through all the exhibits but I was there an hour taking pictures of the records and guitars and all the memorabilia.I love the House of Cash wall, that was a nice touch. They also have a gift shop with a lot of Johnny Cash shirts and everything and anything Johnny Cash that you could buy. The Museum has a great location its right off the Broadway the main drag in Nashville for the Honky Tonk bars. The have a really good pizza place next door as well. This museum is def worth for me because I got a lot of good pictures on my phone of all the memorabilia. If you are not a Cash fan thou I would not pay 18 dollars to get in but if you are a Cash fan I would recommend it. I love Nashville, great city with every friendly people who make you feel at home

I exited after 2 minutes because it was so overcrowded. They would not give me a refund! I overheard women saying they were not impressed with it.

You can listen to his music in the adjacent cafe and of course spend money on all the schwag.

Johnny Cash deserves his own Museum.  Small, but packed with lots of information and memorabilia, there is lots to learn about the Man in Black and lots to see.  We visited early in the day.  Seems like everyone else had the same plan.

It's amazing to learn more about his career.  As a boy, he grow up during the depression and started working in the cotton fields at age 5.  As a young man, he learned to play the guitar and write gospel songs.  He also  served in the Air Force.  Every thing in his life was earned and a struggle.  Nothing was handed to him and his life was a constant struggle.  He experienced loss at a young age with the tragic death of his brother Jack.  

He during his music career, he often felt confined due to his record label.  There was a time, when he had a drinking problem and serious issues with drugs.  Even when his life was out of control, his creativity was still intact and he was writing hit songs.  There were brushes with the law where he ended up in jail.  And a suicide attempt.  At some point, this came to an end and he developed and interest in prisoners and had concerts for them.  He was also activist for Native Americans.

I didn't realize it, but Johnny had his own TV show that started in 1969.  He also collaborated with a host of other music artist during his career and was also on of the "Highwaymen".  He was an important part of the country music for nearly 50 years.  It's interesting to see the many changes in his appearance over the years.

The museum also reflects the special love of his life June Carter Cash and the many years they spent together.  Be sure to take a Kleenex with you.

I really wanted to like this place. Came here on a Sunday night around 7pm. Music was turned down kinda low so it made the atmosphere kinda humdrum. If the music was a little louder, it would've given the perception of a fun place (and would've helped drown out the conversation from the next table over). I came in and seated myself. 

I placed my order moments later. I ordered a cheeseburger, sweet potato fries and water. Took around 15 min for my food to arrive. My cheeseburger with pretzel bun was juicy and flavorful but overly salty. My sweet potato fries were clearly not made fresh. They were dry and barely warm - had to bite into one to be certain they were sweet potato fries since they weren't orange toned at all...completely brown from being dry. Water refills came - but only when there was zero in my glass. I had a moment when I had to stop eating while waiting for someone to notice I needed more water. 

Staff wasn't enthusiastic about being there - just barely friendly. 

I've satisfied my curiosity about trying this place out. Maybe this was an "off night" for them - but I'd rather drive a little farther for a better overall experience.

Stopped in for a few drinks... Friendly service. Unsweetened tea was not good at all - very strange taste, sent it back. I instead enjoyed a few Blue Moon beers on draught. They were good. Great live music and ambiance.

The restrooms (men) - Wow, this area needs some work. Filthy... Also, what's with a toilet next to a urinal (really close) and no stall? Totally weird... Why would you need both? Should I have brought a friend? A single toilet would suffice for most humans. Fix this!

First off let me say the burgers here are phenomenal. Great taste full of flavors. The atmosphere was chilled and laid back. There was a band playing when we arrived then they left around 9ish. Reasonable prices came with a side of fries or upgrade to onion rings for $1 more. Big problem customer service.  We stood at the door for about 5 min until someone greeted us then sat us down and said our server would be right with us. Not the case took another 5 min before she came to the table. Got our drinks order and disappeared.  A little over cooked i ordered medium. Finally ordered my burger which took forever to come out. There Was Only 3 Other Tables In the place. If the burger wasn't so great this place would have gotten 1 star.

Always look for piano bars when traveling. This one was fabulous! No cover, inexpensive drinks and the entertainment was fantastic. A few drunk people made it a bit annoying for awhile, but after we spoke to the waitress, a bouncer got it under control. We sang aloud for 2 hours. Incredible piano players, great mix of music (not too much country)..,eclectic crowd. Will definitely come back next time we are in Nashville!

Was in town for Zac Brown music fest and saw JC museum as we exited the walking bridge across the river

We entered the gift shop and it felt a bit small ... but ....  very much worth the entry fee.  Lots of history and videos on the self guided tour (nice use of iPad mpg throughout).  We spent 2 hours learning about the man and his life and works.  I highly reco this for anyone that appreciates Cash.  Also, make sure u spend time listening to each of the videos by era when u first enter.  The last, from 2010 after his death where his fans made the video, frame by frame, is amazing!

I'm a recent Cleveland transplant to Nashville, so I tend to be a pretty tough critic when it comes to burgers. I've had Burger Up, Gabbys, Rotiers and a few of the places down here in Murfreesboro like Busters Place... after two trips to 360 Burger, my wife and I agree that this is the most memorable burger we have had down here.

I tried the Margherita Burger the first time, and the Cilantro Avocado as well. Both are unique to 360 Burger and make the drive over to The Crossings area well worth it. My wife had a Salmon Burger and a Grilled Swiss and Portabello the second time. We tried the fried pickles (have a nice spice to them) and the wings for appetizers.

The owners came up to us and greeted us the first time, and recognized us the next time we came in.

Love the comforting feel of the restaurant. Beautiful mural covers the wall with the city skyline integrated.

I love seeing the area bounce back, and now The Crossings has a great burger place like a few of these other neighborhoods that we shop/frequent.

Wonderful night of music!!! Our server was fantastic!!! I attended the dinner and a show on 7/11/2015 with my mom and two kids (4 and 9). The kids shared an order of chicken fingers and fries, washing it down with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. They were enthralled with the music and even danced! The food was good. Their menu is in a state of flux with a new chef, so some items like pork chops are no longer available. I ordered a plate of pulled pork and side of mashed potatoes. Again the menu wasn't updated, so it didn't list pepper as the main spice in the mash. My mom is allergic and this made her very unhappy. The server apologized and brought out a huge slice of cheesecake with chocolate and raspberry drizzle. The venue was very spacious and had tables that sat four people, but a few were pushed together to accommodate a larger group. Lots of couples on dates or small groups kicking off their Saturday night. Originally I was quoted a bucket of beer was ten dollars, but when the bill came it was $20! The server did correct the price without hesitation. I think it must be very confusing to not only customers but servers too if the menu is not updated. This would only be my only suggestion to Mr. Blair, if you have a new chef please print out an updated menu to showcase a short bio and a list of the new  offerings. Please discard the nasty old stained file folders and just print it on heavy card stock. It wasn't a great first impression to sit down and see old file folders on the tables; it made me think about work and I wanted to relax;) The musicians were very talented: Bill Griese and Julie Gribble. I bought both of their CDs to listen to in the car back to Georgia. Very wonderful, authentic Nashville experience!!! We will definitely go back again.
PS Valet your car and get it validated by your server. Much easier than driving in circles to find a spot.

This place is awful. The food is disgusting. Nothing was fresh all frozen. I had the chicken bites and could hardly get through half my meal. Most of my friends felt the same about their choices. Would NEVER come back. Way better choices in Nashville. 

Our waitress was awful. She lost my friends debit card. Awful!!
Amazing self guide tour with a lot of artifacts and    memorabilia. The warmth and welcoming environment made you think you actually knew Johnny and June. A must see when in Nashville

I came here with a few friends to watch game three of the Stanley Cup playoffs after Swingin' Doors promoted themselves as a place to watch the game on their Facebook page. After getting a table upstairs a few hours prior to the game and waiting 30+ minutes before a waitress came to the table we thought we were settled in for the game... that is until a band started playing downstairs right before the game began. Even after all of the volume on the TVs was turned up, any sound was completely drowned out by the band. Shouldn't have been promoted as a place to watch the game and then not delivered on a good game-watching experience. We ended up leaving to watch it somewhere where a band played only on commercial breaks. Beyond that, food was just okay.

This is our favorite place to grab a burger in the Antioch area. My go-to is the PB&J burger, the homemade jalapeño raspberry jelly is sooooo good. They also have great sweet potato fries, which is an item that can be very hit or miss at burger joints. Good beer list, very reasonable prices, friendly staff, and lots of options. Definitely a hidden gem in Antioch!

Pretty much anything and everything you'd ever want to see or know about Johnny Cash. No chance that any fan of The Man In Black is going to be disappointed in their visit. Chronicles his life from childhood through his last days and features an overwhelmingly impressive amount of memorabilia. Everything is displayed nicely with detailed information about every item. The only cons were that the place is rather small and there is no room for expansion that I could see. I don't know how they would fit anything else into here without cluttering it up. Plus I would like to see more theme rooms, like the area dedicated to his movie and TV career. And there is no specific parking for the museum. I parked in the nearby lot, which cost $10 alone. The gift shop prices were also rather steep, but that is to be expected. But these are all petty complaints. Certainly a must-see for fans!
Visited October 2013

The $16 admission is worth the price if you're a Cash fan, as there are lots of videos, artifacts, and fun biographical tidbits from the life of Johnny Cash. You'll see personal notes, stage costumes, instruments, gold and platinum records, and loads else. There's a row of iPads pre-loaded with clips from his concerts and music videos, although I did find myself wondering if I couldn't just find all of that on YouTube. There's a great film projected in a backroom with excerpts from Cash's acting career, and some of his doodles, sketches, and personal notes. I learned a lot, and I definitely would recommend it to someone exploring the history of country music.

Decided to try 360 Burger tonight to see what it was like for myself.  I am glad I did.  The service was great, our server was attentive and affable. I had the 360 burger with a side of asparagus, and my son had the cilantro avocado burger and they both were great.  One thing I wish was, they forgot to ask how I wanted my burger prepared and it came out well done, I am partial to a medium burger, but my burger was still good.  Nice atmosphere.  I inquired about happy hour and I was told they have one on all the drinks except wine, hence my giving them 4 stars and not 5.  Don't exclude the people who drink wine we like happy hour too! Happy for the Antioch area this is a nice start to rebuilding the community.

This is our FAVORITE Nashville spot.

I definitely recommend visiting and sitting for a while. We visited on a Friday night & they had a live band. I think it was the best sounding band in downtown that night. I wish I could remember their name.. but, they kept everything going and were very upbeat with tons of variety. Because of them, we stayed longer than we wanted but in a good way - we didn't want to leave.

The stage set up is awesome. I loved how it's built into one of the walls and it's at the beginning of the building when you walk in. The entertainers can use stairs on both sides to go from the upstairs to downstairs while performing. This set up keeps everyone's eyes on them. The entire place is designed so that you can see the stage NO matter where you sit or stand.

We didn't have any food on our visit. But we hung out on the second floor. Bottles of bud light were $6 each - the only downfall.. but not a deal breaker. We weren't ID'd at the door or bar.. but about 30mins & two beers later.. security came up to us and asked for our ID's. It was bothersome but we understood and showed him, he apologized and went on his merry way.
Great place to hear some of Nashville's best singer/songwriters. I suggest this venue to everyone! The chicken tenders are to die for too.

Meh.  The drinks were okay.  It was nearly empty when we got there and started to fill up later on.  So go early if you have a big group or want to get a good table.

One musician was pretty good, one was slightly annoying.  

We made two song requests and paid $5 for each but neither one was played.  We had a lukewarm experience so ended up leaving and finding somewhere else to go.   It definitely felt like an older crowd and some of the music selections reflected that as well.

My husband and I had the most amazing time here. We did not have reservations, but got here early and where able to get a table right in the front. The musicians where so talented and a wide range of styles. After the show I shared a shot with one of the artists. They were so humble. Lexi Adams sang a few songs she had written and I was so touched. Jimmy Pritchett shared a song about his father that made me cry. Awesome experience. Oh and the food!  Fried Mac and cheese was awesome.

Food was OK.  Live Music not bad.  Friday lunch time horrible service.  Waitress forgot what we ordered couldn't remember to bring us water refills a it once but twice.  Never did get the beer I ordered.
It's really hard not to have a great time here. This is one of the best Piano bars we've visited!  Highly recommended!

During a long weekend trip to Nashville my wife and I and another couple sought refreshment in the Swingin' Door on a couple occasions. It is less than a block off of Broadway which reduced the bachelorette party traffic and the drunk males following them. The downstairs is fairly small with maybe 6 tables and a few barstools. During our visits, the bar tenders were always attentive with slight waits if a group came in to grab drinks. Two of the three performers that played during our times here were very good. We never ate here so can't comment on the food. The bathrooms were kind of gross. Overall, a decent place to grab a few beverages and listen to music.
The band and atmosphere are awesome!!!! Such a great place to hang in Nashville. Food and drinks are top notch. The waitress Shana was so friendly and helpful!!!! Definitely coming back!!!!
