Great fun. Perfect venue. And food was good. I went for the music so good food was a bonus. I had the fish tacos. Very yummy.  Get the coleslaw !!

I ordered the F Bomb sandwich (see attached) with a side of chips and guac and it was delicious. Unique and flavorful, also the guacamole was terrific. It's hard to find a good guacamole and I could've eaten theirs all night.  I didn't expect bar food to be so tasty but I recommend it and intend to try their Sunday brunch.

So excited that this finally opened up! Great location on the corner, the entertainment was excellent. The second floor was closed for a private event and there was only one bathroom on the first floor which I was in line for 20 minutes...the table I was with was halfway done with their food while I was gone waiting in line which was ridiculous. I waited 15 minutes for my waitress to bring my beer.  On the bright side, the artichoke dip and fried pickles were great! I also had the chicken and waffles which were some of the best chicken and waffles I've ever had-they were breaded with cornmeal and had a thick sauce...to die for! Def have to stop by when I come back to Nashville

This place was great! Our friends who went here Sat night said there was a ($6?) cover. When some of us went on Sun night, there wasn't a cover since they had opened especially for the eclipse crowd.

There's 4 guys in total who rotate in and out during different times. They are mostly on two pianos facing each other on stage, but some will periodically get on other instruments while the other fulfills a song request. You can request almost any song within any genre, and they will try to play and sing it as best they can. 

The guys on stage were terrific and funny. I'm no concert going girl, but I can def enjoy and appreciate the live music. Although it's a bar, the live music and witty banter is the main attraction. And come to find out, there's a bar just like this one in Buckhead.

Absolutely fantastic. I went here with a group of six for brunch on Sunday. Reservations weren't needed as there was plenty of room. There were four guys playing acoustically from 11-1, and they took turns singing / playing their songs, and played for two hours. Such great music, very mellow and chill vibe. The only thing people might not like is you can't really talk or have conversations with your friends, since it's rude to the performers, but we were hungover and didn't want to talk so it was perfect. Most bars have the bands come around with tip jars and we were prepared to give them all our money because we loved them, but they didn't even do that.

Food / drink: Some of the best brunch food I've had. My friend and I split the fried green tomato BLT and the monte cristo and both were delicious. BLT was my favorite, monte cristo was very heavy, but that was expected, and still great. Two for one mimosas/bloody mary's. Service was wonderful, and I wish I lived in Nashville if only to be able to come here more often.

Fun night out to hear good music in an awesome little venue. The set up is basic but perfect for the environment.  We went on a Saturday night.  I bought the tickets ahead of time online. The tickets say to print but it isn't necessary. When you arrive they check you in with your name.Tickets were $5 with a minimum $7 food/drink per person.  We each had a drink and shared the buffalo chicken dip. I could have done without the dip but for the price it wasn't too bad.  All of the performers were extremely talented and put on a great show. It was a perfect low key night for us after a night of partying the night before.

Great place to hear music and plenty of room to accommodate guests. I would go back here on my next trip to Nashville. Try the vegetable and chicken soup. May have been the best meal I had in Nashville. It was that good!
Color me unimpressed. Wings were pretty close to lousy. Drinks?  No bitters or simple syrup for old fashions. I suggest you try one of a million other over priced locations on broadway.

I am not a country music fan, but I always enjoyed Johnny Cash, so this was the one music museum I wanted to visit while in Nashville. When I saw the price online, I decided I could probably skip the museum, but then I found a great deal on Groupon, and bought the tickets before we came to Nashville. I'm so glad we did. We enjoyed the museum even more than we thought we would. My only complaint was that they do seem to let too many people in at one time. It is a small space packed with memorabilia and many audio displays with headphones. There are a lot of placards to read. It is not a museum that you can just walk through without stopping to read something or listen to the music. With the amount of people they were sending in, you tended to get herded into a single file line slowly being moved past each display without a chance to stop and read or listen. However, we popped out of the mass and walked around to see things that interested us and ended up spending over an hour really enjoying the space. My son commented that he was amazed at how many artists have covered Johnny Cash's songs. It was interesting to hear Snoop Dogg cover "I Walk the Line." lol

Made reservations with their new reserved by website. Well that did not go so well. No one knew my name when I mentioned it. So that being said! We also drove about  25 miles for the pretzel rolls for our burger which one person stated that yes we have them. So we embarked on the trip. 

The avocado cilantro burgers are fantastic but much with the pretzel roll. So call ahead so your not disappointed. The music is not that good.

Had Sunday Brunch here - upon entering, we were told that we had to wait at the bar despite having reservations,  because the chef was backed up. There were about 50 empty tables, so that was bizarre. My bloody Mary was great though - don't do bottomless, as the glasses are half the size of the $6 pint and not worth the $15 price tag. The menu was much more scarce than the website, plus they gave my friend and I each a different one, which had to be corrected. Our food was okay (my friend got Shrimp and Grits and I got the Veggie flatbread) - glad we had a groupon. The singer played from about 1130-1, and it was a nice intimate setting for her performance.

Great Johnny Cash museum with loads of memorabilia and information. Reasonable admission and easy to get to if you are in downtown Nashville. I learned a lot of new information about Johnny Cash and liked the way items were displayed and how the rooms were set up. Lots of items in the gift shop too! We got there soon after it opened on a Thursday morning and pretty much had the place to ourselves.
Interesting museum even though i was never a big fan of his music.  Lots of facts and memorabilia.  Enjoyed the 3 movies shown covering his singing and acting careers.

In from out of town, to make it clear I LOVE music R of all genres and enjoy the work that is put in and felt when hearing it. So with the above said I thoroughly enjoyed this venue. If you need to chat and catch up, this is not the place For you. If you want to hear great singer songwriter sets, this is the place!  Service was fine, food was ok, but the atmosphere and artists were great. 

There was a $7 cover and re entry fee after the set was over but we didn't mind, was truly a great time. 

If you are looking for cover bands and talked , hit Broadway.
Lots of great info! Little pricy at $20 a person. That does not include the Patsy Cline museum either.

This place is great! Our first burger stop in Nashville - burgers were cooked perfectly and delicious. Atmosphere is laid back, not a huge place so it feels like a hometown dive (but isn't). Met the GM and head cook - super nice and made great conversation.  

The beef/cheese dip with fried pita is AMAZING. Simple but delicious. 

Good beer selection too. Will absolutely be back regularly!
This review is solely due to how rude the manager was at the end of the night. They do not close at 3am. They very rudely kick patrons out before 2:30.

I love this bar! Right off broadway but not full of drunk kids. Great singers...like Jimmy Charles! He was amazing..sang a lot of goodies but not the same ole songs you hear at every other bar, plus he sings his originals!  Best night in nashville! 

The jalapeño burger & tots are delicious!  Margaritas gone down smooth.

Amazing place to chill and hear the best music in town, where the patrons are actually attentive and truly enjoy great artist. $10 cover last night, saw 4 singer/songwriters that were all talented, including Liz Page who writes with Taylor Swift and others. A great experience and I highly recommend it!

The Listening Room Cafe is a wonderful place. They truly value musical artists and giving them a platform to showcase their talent. The food is great, and I appreciate the quick service that the complimentary valet parking attendants provide.
Best burger I've had in a decade. The King Burger rules. Beef, ham, egg, pulled pork. Fantastic.

We popped just exploring Broadway. It's a pleasant surprise. The band was great. I'm not a huge country fan, but they are high energy and fun. Shana is super cool, patient and attentive. All together, this was a great stop. And the whiskey selection is solid.
Entertainment was amazing food was horrible had the pull pork which was super dry. Mac and cheese was super dry.

Great place to hear live music in a laid back  environment.  We went for an earlier show so perhaps it get a little crazy later in the evening.  Cocktails were great and appetizers were tasty.  Good service and amazing music from Carly Pearce.

I am extremely disappointed in the entirety of this establishment.
From food. To service this is a genuine one star rate. 

A bit over a 40 minute wait for mediocre food. 

We arrived and were seated quickly enough but things went down hill from there. 

Waitresses scrambled in the most disorganized and misguided way to wait tables.
We were waited on by two people  whilst one woman waited nearly 30minutes to be waited on at all. 

Appetizer took extremely long to come out. And was just a simple order of fried cheese. 

We then waited 40 or more minutes for poor burgers. 
They were dry and over done. 

One order even specified medium and was still prepared well done. 

Overall just an extremely poor experience and I probably won't be returning.

A very informative and interesting museum.  Learned a lot.  I think this is a hidden gem in Nashville.
We aren't big country music fans, but we did really enjoy this museum.
A little pricey, but hey,  we did really enjoy it.

Loved the music and atmosphere. Food was awful. Ordered a "cheese plate" that was pathetic looking. Had the Mac and cheese and that was awful. Come on people, we are down south! Waitress had way too many tables. Never got a water refill and I was there for hours upon hours.

I can only speak to the brunch experience at the Listening Room, but it left much to be desired. First, we barely listened to live music. When we called ahead, the manager confirmed the online listing that said the music goes from 11-1, so we made a reservation for 11. When we arrived a sign out front said the music started at 11:30. Our server confirmed this, even though on the wall inside it listed the first musical act as starting at noon. But we thought, well if it's at 11:30, that's ok. It didn't start until noon, and well after we had finished eating.  

The food options were overwhelming and overpriced (I guess to pay the musicians?). If you're going to have an $18 buffet and very limited additional menu options, make the buffet something more than eggs and bacon set up in hotel pans in the back. Also the math on the bottomless mimosas and bloody marys didn't make a lot of sense.

I had family in town, so it was a shame we wasted a meal at this place.

Take the title "Listening Room" very seriously. Not a good place to socialize with your party. With that being said excellent food and drinks as well as entertainment. Fried okra is delicious and something you gotta try!

My parents, my kids (ages 10 and 11) and I went on the Friday night dinner cruise to celebrate my parents' 45th wedding anniversary and had a wonderful time.  We had a great table right next to the stage, close enough to the performers for one of them to reach down and give my son a fistbump which we all thought was pretty cool.  The servers were very attentive and knowledgeable about the experience as a whole.  The food was so-so, hence only 4 stars instead of 5.   Salad appetizer with ranch or italian dressing.  Entree was a baked potato, asparagus, steak and shrimp.  Chicken tenders and fries for my kids.  The steak could have used a little more seasoning and I would have loved some cocktail sauce to dip my shrimp in since it had no other seasoning on it.  Mom loved the asparagus.  The key lime pie was awesome.  My parents got a free slice of pecan pie each with "happy anniversary" written around the plate in caramel sauce.  Very nice touch.  The show was great too and I am not a country music fan at all.  It was a good mix of genres and very entertaining.  Even my kids loved it and want to go back.

I highly recommend taking the dinner cruise to celebrate a special event.  Let your server know if it's a special occasion and the host will announce it at the beginning of the cruise.  My parents got a special round of applause for having been married for so long.  That made their evening extra special!

By far our favorite place on Broadway.  Beer was really cold and the bands were really good.  TVs had the games on there was a great mix of 24-65 year old people all dancing. Tuesday night band was really good.

Great music and the food and beer selection is one of the best in a music venue.  My only complaint would be the service.  We had a coupon the last time we were there, that does not expire, and they would not let us use it because it was a few months old.  Again, no expiration and when I showed this to them they still refused.  Otherwise we have had great experiences.

Racist establish that uses arbitrary dress code policies to keep certain groups of people out. When asked to see their dress code policy we were told we were being "hostile" and refused to provide the dress code policy.

My husband and I found ourselves wishing that we had visited the museum after the Country Music Hall of Fame. You can easily do both in an afternoon. That's because they are sort of the opposites of each other. CMHF is expansive but only gives you a broad look at a lot of  artists and only has a few Johnny Cash items on display. 

The Johnny Cash Museum felt small, and packed with objects (which could use a bit more space to breathe), but it provides a much more in depth look at his career. The interactive features were thoughtful and unexpected, such as live concert footage next to a display of guitars, photos etc from the same era. An old radio with an interactive display of songs that he may have heard as a child on it. Such a great idea.

The quality and variety of the items in the collection is outstanding: lots of handwritten notes and significant items like personal photographs and lots of cool memorabilia related to Folsom Prison Blues. There's lot of stage outfits and instruments as well....and a few odd things at the end. 

Because the objects don't have a lot of room to breathe, you have to be patient and take time to absorb the text panels (compellingly written; I am a fan and i still learned a lot) and to take the time to listen to the many tracks, films and interactive features throughout the museum. Otherwise you might feel that you're gone through the whole museum too quickly. For the same reason, when going with family you might want to consider your children's attention spans for the same reason, might be better for older children or teens.

Six of us went on the dinner cruise on Oct. 21, 2016. The salad was very good but the waiters kept trying to remove it from the table. Luckily, I had a good helping of it because the rest of the food was truly terrible. Cold vegetables that looked like they were left over from lunch. The service was even worse. I don't think the waiters have ever had any training. What they did best was try to garner tips. The show was (sad to say) the best part of the evening. All in all, definitely not worth the $103 dollars per person.

We had a good time and left almost at 11 o clock. We spent $38 and have our closing receipt with the original $31 charge and nice hefty tip. Some magician at the bar must have added a one in front of our total and changed the eight to a zero because the bar charged us $130! Guess the bartenders needed better than a 22.5% tip on a Sunday night. Needless to say, we won't be going back and will be disputing the charge.

Fan for years. Played and have come to shows for a long time at the old location. Came to the new location and paid $35 gladly for a ticket to a nonprofit show to hear some amazing hit songwriters. Went to dinner before like any normal person would before a show. Sat at our table and was required to spend $15 a person with no warning saying the tickets weren't through the venue and this paid for the entertainment instead of a tip jar. Then the tip jar came around. it's mainly about the principle that we weren't informed before coming. We would have bought a glass or two of wine anyway. The waitresses sell of it interrupted our experience a lot. As I said, been a fan and supporter for a long time but this change is just disappointing :/
Came to WR for lunch and after dinner drinks on the same day and had Michelle as our server for both. She was fantastic!!! So was the music. Loved the band both times!

Okay so here's the deal,  I love, love, love the Listening room for their music.  I've seen several shows here and they are amazing!   $5 ticket for talented musicians?!  Win.   HOWEVER, the food.   I had never eaten here before.   We were a party of 5 with three underaged teens.  $15 minimum for food, ok fine-but the food was truly awful.  Not one thing we ordered was good.  The hummus plate,  stale crackers and bland dry crumbly  hummus.  Not a good start.   Cup of soup? Meh.   Turkey salad was probably the "best" of what we ordered.   Turkey lunch meat, and some kind of pre-cooked bacon.   Two burgers at our table, inedible.   Way over cooked, no amount of ketchup to save it and bun was stale.  The Mac and cheese- I have no words. Just don't order it.   Turkey apple and cheese sandwich- again stale bread.   EVEN THE PEPSI WAS BAD!   I would have rather paid more for our tickets if this is what they pass off as dinner.   So music 5 stars- food- 1 maybe.

Great talent and good venue.   Just don't get the entrees. They are not very good. Stick with the sandwiches and smaller fares. Other than that, really enjoyed the artists and the sound is amazing. Small enough to feel like you have the best seats anywhere you sit.

Really enjoyed the night. The guys on the stage were very talented. Played all the Requests that came to them and didn't beg for money all night. I like that they rotate singers so there is always music. I didn't eat there and only drank beer. Menu I saw only had pizza. One negative... A bathroom attendant?!  Really?  Is this a Nashville thing?  I didn't go to the bathroom at any other bars but I will be disappointed if I find someone sitting in there bugging me while I pee. And I always feel bad for them!

In general, my husband and I aren't big bar people, especially in downtown Nashville.  We're just not into overpriced, watery drinks, loud music, smoke and obnoxious drunk tourists.  The Big Bang, however, is one that we often frequent whenever we're downtown enjoying dinner or hanging out after work.  

We've never been into the place when there ISN'T a huge crowd and a happenin' vibe.  Despite the crowds, we can usually find a seat with a good view, and the waitstaff is quick and attentive with our drinks.  If we can manage to arrive before about 8:30pm, there is no cover charge, which is awesome.  After that time, cover is $6/person - not bad at all for the entertainment you receive while there.  Drink prices are a little steep, but not terribly unreasonable, and the bar staff supplies a heavy pour.

The entertainment is the real reason you should visit The Big Bang.  The dueling piano players are AWESOME and incredibly talented; each plays the piano, bass, and drums in addition to rockin' the vocals.  They are versed in many styles of music and play to the masses - whatever is requested, in any genre, can be performed by the band (especially if the request is made alongside a $20 bill).  You can and should tip the band members, who work incredibly hard for their money to put on the best possible show night after night.  

We love the energy and vibe of The Big Bang, along with the friendly staff and patrons.  It's easily one of our favorite places to catch some great music in Nashville!

Went here for a night out in Nashville, the food was amazing and I had an awesome bartender! Jasmine was friendly, intriguing, and all around a great representation of the company! I will definitely be back again!

LOVED this place. I was visiting Nashville for a short trip and had a local show us around the bars in the area. This was definitely the best one. We stopped here first, and ended up coming back again to end the night. There are two pianos set up facing each other, which two pianists  play duets all night. If you want the artists to play a song, you give a tip and request the song. The request sheet is actually blank - I was really impressed with how many different songs the guys knew! I really loved how different the genres were from song to song. It went from country to hip hop to rock and everything in between.

The only downside is the selection of beer is not great. There were probably about 10 options of beers, bottles only. Not bad selections, but just not a large quantity. I got a Newcastle, I think it was 5 bucks. I didn't really mind though because the place is so cool it makes up for it.

The new location is a definite upgrade! 

Don't be alarmed about parking because it is now Downtown (off of Broadway) and in the new SoBro district... there is an attached free lot and tons of off-street and affordable lot options that surround this spot. 

We popped in last night for a low-key hang to celebrate a dear friend's birthday and enjoyed ourselves. Some great music was on the gorgeous stage and the acoustics were certainly on point. The staff and our server were super friendly and made some suggestion off the diverse cocktail menu.... which also happens to include "Skinnies" - drinks under 125 calories. Hello diet-friendly cocktail. 

Prices were fair on both drinks and bites and I happened to love the layout of this joint. 
It is spacious yet still offers a cozy vibe. And, I'm absolutely smitten over the rustic lighting fixtures - perhaps I have watched too much of HGTV lately? Either way, this is a great spot for a meal, drinks, catch live music, host an event, or dare I say - to just hang out!

I dig it.

TIP: The patio offers up pretty sweet views of downtown. Great place to relax and enjoy!

(Horrible)  where to start..  I travel 8 months out of the year.  For me to take the time to write a review is really bad.  Food, well it's disgusting along with the service.  Bar tender along with all other employees are quick to bring you a drink for the most part.  Food however, forget it.   Not to mention you truly don't want what they're serving!  Ordered their standard house burger with lettuce and tomato.  Came without both.  Asked for medium rare, was told sorry it's frozen..  Got the Philly with order too.  That amount of got peppers is a sure sign that meat is bad.  Because why otherwise would you ruin a simple steak & cheese with so much none tasty spice?  Not to mention the ridiculous chain smoking.  If you're looking for live music and a friendly local vibe.  Please don't go through what I have. Go somewhere else!!

A super fun way to spend an hour with the kids. We took SO many pictures and had a bunch of fun. The wax figures look very lifelike! Tip: look for a Groupon before paying full price. It's a way better deal!

This is a great place for enjoying great songwriters and future artists located just outside the tourist trap.  It is a nice environment with friendly staff.  The valet parking is a plus on the very busy nights we were there.  The Listening Room is always one of the first places we check to see what's happening downtown.  Love it!
Great bar, great music and awesome drinks!! Best part, Jake the bar tender awesome we will be back very soon!! Our new favorite bar!!

I was surprised how small it was but what you get is a very personal and authentic experience. Also, there is nobody rushing you around the exhibits. Some great historical items to be seen and a few excellent audio visual displays. I learned a lot about the man and I'm so glad that I paid a visit. (Very welcoming staff as well) Happy to part with $17 to learn more about this giant of music.
Love Kid Rock...not so much the bar. Music was so load you couldn't have any type of conversation. Service not that good. Had to go to the bar for beers. Hopefully they can get better.

I'm not a die-hard Johnny Cash fan, but this was one of my favorite things we did on our trip to Nashville. I've always been into his greatest hits and had enjoyed the Walk the Line biopic, but I left with a much deeper appreciation for his contribution to music and his legacy. Tons of memorabilia; everything from lyric sheets and love letters to candid photos and on-stage costumes. Staff was friendly and enthusiastic throughout. As other reviewers mentioned, the last section of the museum features his Hurt video, which was filmed just a few months before he died. Not a dry eye in the house. Be sure to spend the few extra dollars to get your photo "taken with Johnny". The museum staff encouraged us to take the attached shot, and as you can see, it was worth every penny.
Pure fun singalong evening.  The 3 singers/ piano players were funny and  great singers.  Varied selection of songs played and place had a great vibe.
Eye wateringly expensive for what you get. An app, dinner for two, and a few drinks came close to $100.

The Listening Room Cafe was the quintessential Nashville experience during our last trip.  Our brief experience with the Listening Room Cafe was great.  This review is only for the music and bar, as we did not have any food.  

We ran across it as we had some time to spare before concerts at LP, and this place is right near the entrance of the bridge.  There is not much around it, but we could clearly hear the music from outside, so we decided to check it out.

When you walk in, it is an open, brick room with a bunch of tables and a stage.  Pretty stripped down place, with a basic bar menu with a bunch of drinks.  Service at the bar was great.  

It was clear from the start that this place was about the music.  No gimmicks or distractions.  Just a couple of folks on a small stage playing great original country.  

Sure, at the bars, you get great music, but music there seems peripheral; at LRC, the music is paramount and just feels important.
One of the best burgers I've had at a restaurant in a long time great service. Extremely nice staff. Your drink will never go empty or table ignored there

Easily one of the worst restaurants I've ever been to. We sat for 20 minutes without a waiter even coming to our table or being given menus. Finally after asking for a server twice, a waitress came over. We ordered the bottomless mimosas. They were basically just orange juice, very small, slow to be refilled, and not at all worth the $15. We then ordered some food from their incredibly short and unappetizing menu (vegetarians beware, there is one option for you and it's disgusting). The food came out and all of it was incredibly awful. I've had better food in dirty roadside diners, where I question whether or not I'm eating chicken or rat. As for the music, it wasn't bad. But the jerk making tranny jokes needs to just not. Way to be an ignorant piece of crap. Save yourself the trouble and go anywhere else.

Can't say enough good things about Jordan Minton and friends, they are truly talented and a joy to listen to.  Now let's get to the venue, please wear a parka and only expect to get one drink the whole time.  Our waitress dropped off food we ordered and never came back and then took our food before we were even finished we had several bites of cheesecake left and a jar of this Nutella desert that we were not done with either. Unfortunately we had to leave early because it was so unbearably cold in there that we couldn't take cold air blowing directly on us any longer.  Was a shame, really wished we could have stayed to finished watching Jordan and his friends play.

TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE! There are definitely more enjoyable ways to spend your time and money in Nashville. 

My wife and I visited with our baby, and the moment we stepped inside our baby started having a melt down. We asked if we could step back out for a moment and the attendant at the entrance rudely stated that we had to go all the way through and exit at the end due to the fire code (which made no sense). After making our way through the packed exhibit as quickly as we could with a screaming baby, I stopped back at the front desk to ask if we could re-enter later after we got our son calmed down. Despite me explaining the situation, the guy at the desk even more rudely stated that that there was no way we could re-enter because we already went through and that the policy. I stepped away before losing it on the jerk, and after we got our son calmed down we went back and demanded to to speak with the manager. She reluctantly agreed to give us a refund, but didn't even bother apologizing much less acting like she cared when we complained about the way her staff treated customers. I thought the South was supposed to be known for its hospitality, not to mention the fact that this place is in the tourism/hospitality industry. 

The little museum looked like it had some pretty neat stuff if we would have had the chance to enjoy it, but the terrible customer service totally wrecked it for us. So all things considered, I would recommend skipping the museum. Just watch the movie at home later, because there are a lot better ways to enjoy spending your time and money in Nashville.
This place is awesome if you ever come to Nashville - unbelievable customer service Frankie & the band was amazing

Out of our entire trip to Nashville this was by far our favorite part.  We bought some tickets online ahead of time and it was quick and easy. We got there 20 minutes before the show and were seated right away. The waitress was nice and attentive. The show started 20 minutes late but it was so excellent we didn't mind.  The singers and musicians were awesome and the kids eyes didn't leave the stage. The food was a 4/5. Small portions but good flavors for the most part. Buffalo chips were not good and are the only thing I wouldn't do all over again. The performers were so nice and made themselves available after the show. A Nashville must!!

This is my favorite place to catch a writer's round in town! Even though this is a music venue, the menu and food is great. Every time I've been here the staff has been great! Definitely a "must do" on any trip to Nashville.

Really loved the atmosphere! We were with a group of 5 women ranging from 22 to 82. My daughter and my 2 sisters stood at the bar for 20 minutes talking and having good conversation waiting to order. They eventually tried getting a bartenders' attention but were totally ignored. We then asked a waitress passing by if we could order a drink and she (a bit abruptly) told us we could not order from her. It was a Wednesday, a little crowded but not crazy. We were just asking for a drink to sip and enjoy the music. Did not happen so we left. Our group was from Houston, Austin and Charleston, so we are accustomed to crowds and waiting and don't mind. But service just wasn't going to happen at all here. However, fun place though and the band was great!
Good Burger.... but slow service... and waitress was useless... too bad cause food was tasty.

What an amazing collection of memorabilia.  The interactive exhibits are also very cool. One star deduction for the lack o crowd control - they really need to limit admission a little bit - but other than that an first rate, 5 star experience. Highly recommend.

We're here for the first time in Nashville. This bar is so cool. The band is amazing. Frankie our server is so cool and so attentive. 

We hit every bar in broadway and this is the  best  and most fun a must visit
Visited during CMA Fest 2018. Great service from Jake at the downstairs bar...best bartender we met all weekend! Custom drinks mixed at fair prices. Fun setting with live music.

A terrific collection. 
I'm not a big fan of museums, but I do and did enjoy the music of Johnny Cash. Ultimately fans will enjoy the most.   It's modern and you can easily spend twenty minutes or a couple of hours. Primo location on third.  Highly recommend.

The atmosphere and show was amazing, the service was slow and the food was horrible. I ordered the prime rib medium rare with green beans and Gouda mac. The prime rib was completely seared/burnt on one side which was odd to me, like it was a pre cut piece of meat cooked to order and not an actual whole prime rib. The Gouda mac was good but ice cold and the green beans where super salty. The other 4 members in our groups enjoyed the show but agreed the food was bad. Oh and their soda fountain wasn't working so the soda tasted really bad and the server didn't know what to do to fix it.

Terrible experience. Bouncers are rude with sketchy hands. Brutal. Supposed to go to a concert. One friend didn't get in cuz she's 40 and didn't have Id. Other friend got felt up. Nice place. If you're into getting Kavanaugh Ed.

"It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places."

The place is cool. The music was great. The food was bad.
The service was horrendous, and then a few days later I saw where I had been overcharged for more than $20.

And, when I say horrendous, I mean nearly 30 minutes before we saw a server (the place was not busy). We saw her when the food came, but never saw her again. We had to flag down someone else to ask for another beer and water, though the water never came. Then, we waited a good bit at the end of the evening trying to catch a glimpse of her to get a check, eventually just going to the front of the place and asking for it. 

Then, of course, charged $50 on a $24 bill.

I talked to a manager by phone who sounded pretty aggravated to field the call. Their calls roll to their personal phones. Service industry don't live in the office...
It wasn't the attitude you would expect on calling to report an overcharge, and there was even a tone at one point like I might be making this stuff up or something.

I didn't hear back from him for 5 days, at which point I contacted the owner. 
He was sympathetic and accommodating at first, 
and agreed to refund the entirety of my bill. 

I waited for 2 weeks, but the check never came. 
I contacted him again and he was less than caring.
A reply email that he meant to mail it 2 weeks ago; but had an emergency; but actually did just run across it yesterday and it was on its way.

The check did arrive after another request, but not only was it not for the entire bill, it was not even for the entire amount of the overcharge. 

He did include 2 tickets to get in the door; like I would want to experience this again.

Both of these guys double-talked so much they couldn't keep it all straight, not for some schmuck like me. It was palpable when you talked to them and evident in their actions.

It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places.

Spend your money somewhere else.
This place does not care about its patrons; plenty of tourists in Nashville.

Love this place! A guy at the bar was making my friend and I feel uncomfortable and the bartender(Mark) took care of us! He told one of the girls and she swept us away and took us out out of the uncomfortable situation.

The place seems to be about revenue generation.....

We were saddened as we think Johnny Cash would be underwhelmed by this money pit museum. The whole till/ticket purchase layout is poorly executed and it seems if you can flog an item with his name on then let's do so..... 

Give it a miss.....buy a CD for $20 from an independent store and appreciate what the man came from and created.....

Great bar and atmosphere. The bartenders were stellar and drinks were really good. We didn't have the food but I would def go there again. The music was loud but their sound system was so spot on you actually didn't notice because it sounded that great. Enough off the drag it's not as crowded but close enough that the magic was on point. It's was so good Friday night we made point to go back on Saturday and stay for a couple hours.

A great addition to the downtown area! The full menu gives plenty of options, both healthy and more indulgent. The Mac and Cheese with chicken is beyond incredible, as well as the Kale and Quinoa salad. Their signature cocktails are super tasty, as well. Make sure you check out the rooftop, which is the tallest on Broadway. The staff is great, and I would def recommend trying it out!
What a great experience. Good memorabilia and movie clips. Enjoyed learning about him and his family. Very clean and well organized museum.

CALLING ALL LADIES!!!  Do NOT go to this place!  They discriminate against women and it CANNOT be tolerated!  They SHAME women here and the only way to make them know that it is NOT acceptable to do so is with your dollars.  There are so many other places to spend your money in Nashville and this place is definitely not it.

For a tourist destination type set-up, we were impressed by the menu and quality of the food. They did their best to accommodate our multiple food restrictions. The venue is excellent for the performers and not bad to enjoy them. The vibe is light and feels more intimate than the cavernous space would suggest.  However...it was freezing!  The only thing that put a blot on my memory and will keep it a one time affair is the lack of suitable heating. I hope it's air-conditioned in the summer or be prepared to shed layers as decency allows, because it's a  family friendly.

Came out with a group of friends around 10pm on a Saturday night in mid-May for a drink or three on the rooftop. The place was packed, drunk people everywhere. You have to walk up five or six flights of stairs to get to the top. Sloppy bachelorettes, aggressive bachelors and a lot of twerking going on. Not my scene. 

But if I were a bachelor or bachelorette, or interested in meeting one of those then this is the place to be at..

Amazing place. We were the first table sat on what was the first full night open. Heather was our server, the sweetest! Manager Chase checked in on us a few times and even opened the merch store for us and got us t shirts and other items that were still in boxes. Mike, security, gave us a tour of the VIP section, second floor and rooftop! Food was great. Beer can chicken was so good we ordered two, and artichoke dip I even finished off with a spoon when the pita chips ran out. And then the music! Amazing. Great job, Heather, Chase and the rest of the team. Already planning our trip back! Tip it on back y'all!

545 pm June 2 2018  looking forward to getting a good seat and having a nice cocktail 15 minutes before the piano bar activities started, however my friend and I were greeted rudely at the bar when we were asking about the particulars of the Liquor used in certain cocktails.  Customer service is sub par and lacking.  We left. Hope the music made up for the bar service.  #dissapointed
This small but seriously original music venues are fantastic and original. The hippy country vibe is wonderful. You will find yourself having a great time.

Love the bar, food and music! 5 stars on that. My complaint is the bartenders and the shady stuff they did to me. So my wife and I were there the past weekend drinking for a few hours. We were ordering Tito's and soda water for 23$ a round. I was paying cash each round and leaving a 2$ tip. After maybe 7-8 rounds, I ran out of cash and had to order our next round with my debit card. When the bill came it was 22.77$. I look and they had a 77 cents charge for using the card. Not a big deal, but then I began to think that when the bartenders were charging me 23$ a round when it should have been 22$. They were adding the electronic fee even when I was paying cash. I inquired about it to the bartender and all she said was that she made a mistake. To me, it seemed like they were trying to scam an extra 1$ on each round. I can only imagine how much they do that on a busy night.
Awesome time, great music and drinks on 2nd floor. Made our trip. Group of 14, very accommodating . Will come back

Dierks' Whiskey Row is extremely well done! The interior is beautiful and clean, and they did a great job preserving the old building. The food is delicious - highly recommend the mac n cheese and fried pickles! Great varied music on all 3 levels with quality sound, and amazing country bands! Can't wait to go back :)

My boyfriend & I are in town for the week. We were definitely looking to hit the Bluebird up while we were here but tickets were sold out so quickly. I was a little bummed because we wanted to see some live music other than a trip down Broadway. My boyfriend struck gold with this place. We found it online day of & booked 2 tickets. They were $5 each! They do require that you spend minimum $15 per person of F&B during the show. This was fine since we were also going for dinner. This is such a great date night idea. 

We got even more lucky to know we were seeing a writers circle of Dallas Wilson, Lainey Wilson, Jackie Lee, & Andy Albert. These were 4 great musicians. We really enjoyed the show. The venue was spacious. The menu was reasonable priced with plenty of options. 

We both ordered burgers. I'm knocking a star down because of the burger. It was definitely more burnt than I wanted it to be. We also had a high top table which was a great view of the stage but all the servers were walking in front of us. They were very distracting. Not their fault but wish they would have went behind us or our tables were pushed up. 

All in all, we definitely recommend this place & probably will be back this week & in the future to come. Thank you for a great night!

Exactly what you want in a piano bar. Dark, good service, extensive repertoire of music. Tons of fun. We were here for my sister's 40th and they were great about bringing her and us up on the stage to sing along to our request. We had an awesome time!!!
Mini burgers were awesome. Drinks and music typical for a honky tonk. Would eat here again.

Everything Johnny Cash! If you are a fan, it's a nice small museum with lots of his history and memorabilia of the artist. Lots of videos and reminders of his albums and songs. There is even homage to the movie (Walk the line) and a video room highlighting all the TV and movie appearances Johnny Cash made during his acting career. 
Please note: you can take a picture as a souvenir with a green screened image of Mr. Cash in the background...just know that it will cost you an extra $25-30 on top of your $20 ticket to get in. I was under the impression that it was included when I was sold the ticket " get a picture with Johnny Cash!", as that part of it costing extra was not expressively made clear. So heads up! Otherwise, nice museum.

I cannot believe there are bad reviews of this place. It is amazing the 1st level is rock/country  and 2nd level was 90's and early 2000 rock. 

 Food was excellent. The bartender ladies  especially on the 1st floor are smoking hot. 

 The bands were just incredible both levels.  

Hit this place up early on for the music. And then about 9 30 10 o'clock head to the Back Corner dance club in Germantown. Dance the night away awesome R&B  Non stop music from 10 to 3:00 a.m.
Awesome spot!  It was a blast. Great bands and atmosphere. Good beer and drink selection. They were out of Badass Lager on the weekend which was disappointing but many other beers to choose from.

I am not a complainer, but I would hate for a group of visitors make the same mistake my friends and I made.  We were looking forward to a beautiful morning with live music, breakfast buffet and bottomless drinks.The music was enjoyable.  The breakfast buffet is disgusting. It is a basic menu, which is fine.. however, poor quality in food, and EXTREMELY slow service at refilling the buffet. To make matters even worse, the bottomless drinks were so weak, and they ran out of Bloody Mary Mix by 1030 am on a Sunday.   We basically paid for bottomless Orange Juice. So disappointed in our experience.

When I visited Nashville, this was one of my favorite things we did! The museum was really interesting- I learned a lot about Johnny Cash- and we had a blast. Tickets were about $20, and we spent a good amount of time in the museum. The gift store was pretty solid, and the cafe was so-so (I wouldn't plan on eating at the cafe as a destination, just as convenience). I enjoyed how interactive the museum was, for example there is an exhibit where you could listen to his songs organized by decade. Definitely a place to visit when you are in Nashville!

Wish I knew about this place sooner!

Who needs Broadway?  When I'm back in Nashville I'll come to the listening room multiple times. 

Such talented singer songwriters!!!

Left wanting MORE MORE MORE!!
Lots of interesting things in here. I enjoyed the "photo" with Johnny at the end. The museum is a little cramped.

This place is retched. Bathroom smells like a 50 yr old retired shit storm. The bartenders are sympathetic  to the patrons who at least  walk up to their bar.  It's a shit hole and nothing is ever gonna change about it. This place is an embarrassment to music city. And it even has its name in the title. Aweful  just a disappointment. If you want to hear the same songs sung over and over and over and over again well then this shit hole is your paradise.

I agree with other reviews, go for the music. Went the night Sarah Ames, Josh Dorr, Sam Ashworth, and Bruce Wallace were playing. They were wonderful. However I was disappointed by the pulled pork steak. Mine was dry and overlooked. The waitress saw me cutting into it and offered a steak knife. Then I ordered the strawberry shortcake which was a lot better. Thumbs up to the staff. The service was wonderful.

Listening Room is a one of a kind venue in Nashville. We wanted to enjoy some live music with brunch and I don't think there's another place in Nashville that offers this combination. Even harder of a find in Nashville is a place to get bottomless mimosas. Thanks, Listening Room! 

 Listening Room offers what Nashville is all about: good food, great music, in a relaxing atmosphere. Please do your self a favor and grab brunch here when visiting  Nashville.

Being from out of town and visiting Nashville this is a cool place to visit if you want to see a awesome view of the city.  The roof top bar is amazing and worth the hike up the 4 flights of stairs.  The food was not bad and they had a nice variety.  We ate on the second floor as the first floor was pretty packed with people enjoying their dinner and listening to the live music.  The night we went they did not have live music on the second floor.  Also on the second floor they do not have servers, so while you are able to order food you do have to order it at the bar.  They were not that busy and we were easily able to walk up to the bar but on nights when they are busier I could see it being an issue.  Would visit again though.

We were directed here by a musician on Broadway.  They bring in songwriters to sing their originals. Chances are you will recognize several songs that have been aired but here you hear it from the person that wrote it not the big name musician.  There were 4 songwriters/singers the night we went and we recognized several songs we have heard (Martina McBride and Tim McGraw sang them) but got to hear them performed by the songwriter, Rick Ferrell.  The other guys had some amazing songs as well and there's no doubt we will hear some of the songs in the near future on the radio whether it's by them or another musician. The food was also absolutely amazing. I believe our server said pretty much everything is smoked on site. I had the hot wings and my wife had the brisket. The wings are right at the top of my list, my mouth waters thinking of them. I went with the buffalo sauce and it was perfect heat and flavor. My wife said the brisket was fantastic. Very flavorful, extremely tender and very juicy!  Can't say enough great things about Listening Room Cafe we will definitely go back on our next trip, maybe more than once. There is a cover charge for the show and a 15 dollar drink/food minimum once in for the show. Otherwise you can stop in just for food in the dining and bar area.

This Museum is a fitting tribute to an exceptional human being.  It helps Fan's or anyone who walks through to get a full Picture of a man who's contributions to society did not stop and in the Recording Studio or When he left the stage.  It's classy and a look into a very complex and gifted man's life.  It walks you through starting at his humble childhood Right up to his last days and the legacy that Will endure in a way unaffected and unmeasured by time.  Evryone should visit this Tribute To Johnny Cash wether a music fan or not, Anyone who does will walk out with a far deeper understanding of Johnny's Contributions not only to music but to American History and Popular Culture.

I have been going to the Listening room for quite some time, being a local and I love it.  One of the best sound rooms in town for hearing great live music and the food is good.   Generally great servers.

What a great find thanks to yelp.  Easy parking, which is a feat for downtown at lunch hour.  Wings were good. So was Caesar salad.  Banana creme brûlée was worth the visit on its own.  Iced tea a bit weak but still tasty.  Service very friendly.  Prices are reasonable.  I will be back for live music.

This place is amazing! Probably the best music I heard in all of downtown Nashville! The food was great! The menu may sound like your typical bar food, but you can really tell that they take pride in what they are putting out. Makes you feel at home in the big city of Nashville! This is a place you need to stop on by before you leave and your next time in town. I will be back asap!

I brought 11 girlfriends to the big bang for my bachelorette party. We had an awesome time! The musicians were so talented and interactive. We had a wonderful time and definitely recommend that people come here for a bachelorette party or other celebrations or just a fun night out with friends. The drinks were a bit expensive, but they were delicious and strong and I would love to go back!

This museum is located in the heart of Nashville. If you're a fan you'll see much of his life unfold in front of you, from his early days to his final days. I especially liked clothing items of his. There is a video viewing room where I was lucky enough to see him perform a song I had never heard before! The museum is a great celebration of a great performers life but also shows visitors that Johnny, when all was said and done, with all his success, remained the average guy at heart. Bering there was a high point of my trip to Tennessee in 2017.

The rating does not reflect the atmosphere or the people playing or even the great beer. T is dropped so low due to the food quality. We went to the early show, 6pm. And we're just going to have a few drinks and some apps. Everything that came was ice cold. I guess I am bad for not mentioning it. But it was crazy all we had was French fries, a side of the Brussel sprouts. And ok the hummus was meant to be cold. When the ketchup that comes with the fries is warmer then the fries themselves. Something is wrong. 
A great place for listen to local song writers a great beer selection. So if you want to see a good show and only drinks I highly recommend. But go somewhere else for food.

If you've ever let children or cats loose in an empty room, it would sort of be how the organization at Listening Room Cafe was Saturday night. My sister and I arrived at 7:30 and had already purchased tickets for the 8:30 show. We walked up to the hostess who said we would not be seated until 8:15, cool, no big deal, we will go get a drink at the bar we said. We sat down at the bar, had a drink a piece and an appetizer (cheese tray, which was actually pretty good) when we notice it's about 8:10 at this point. We stand up to go see when we can go in or find some sort of "plan" in this now extremely crowded "waiting room" and there is literally NO direction. People are just standing around in a huge gaggle, asking everyone else if they know what's going on, at which point nobody knows the answers. The employee at the door was of NO help and would let some people sneak past while others who had been waiting in line (not us thankfully) for an hour were still standing in line. TOTAL disaster. At this point I was super annoyed and had I not purchased tickets we'd have left but finally, at 8:45 (yes 15 minutes after the show was supposed to start), they get all of us inside. The songwriters made several comments about starting late, as well, so it was pretty clear everyone was pretty peeved. 

I'd like to tell you the disaster ended here but sadly, it did not. We ordered two diet cokes and two waters from the waitress. About 30 minutes later, and after having been asked by 300 other waiters if we'd ordered a beer, margarita, whiskey, etc. our waitress finally came back with two diet cokes. I requested a few waters and we put in our food order. Once our food came, and thankfully that was pretty fast, we had mixed reviews. The hot chicken was no bueno  but the brussel sprouts and the fried pickles were edible. 

The entire duration of the show the artists kept ordering beverages they were not getting served so finally patrons of the show would bring them drinks. It was seriously insane. I don't live in Nashville but if I did, I'd probably go anywhere else. It's really too bad because you have all the ingredients for success just maybe too much going on.

This place was quite simply the best place I've visited on Broadway so far. Our server, Heather, was fantastic and provided excellent service. The band was awesome, covered a lot and knew their target audience and the food was great. The artichoke dip was on point as well as the beer can chicken. I believe the rating does not reflect them, just busy and overcrowded upon opening.

The food may be good, but good luck finding out!  I sat there for 30 minutes in a nearly empty restaurant, and didn't have a single person come to my table. If you are looking for terrible service, this is the place for you!
The deviled eggs, fried mushrooms, and sweet potato fries were delicious.  Great music too.  I always bring out of town guests to the Listening Room- for the music, food, and outside dining area.
Really awesome live music with the Nashville Nobody's.  Nice and quick service.  Cozy place. Would def return while in Nashville.

We had a wonderful experience enjoying the first all female band we've seen on Broadway. Dozzie, 4 girls from Australia rocked the house with amazing harmony, singing a great mix of top 40. They play on Saturday afternoons. The food was great. We enjoyed the Shrimp fritters, Mac and cheese, loaded fries, fried pickles, wings and the banana bread pudding. The highlight of the afternoon was our server Nicole who was pleasant, fun, and knowledgeable about the menu. This is also a good bar to watch games. There are lots of tvs well placed throughout the restaurant.
Food was good but came out cold. Service took forever. Was in a large group tho. I bet if you were single this place would be straight.
Terrible service and food.  Didn't have the ingredients for one of their signature cocktails?  Don't bother.

If you're a fan of Johnny Cash, it's Mecca, and worth every penny.     If you're not, you probably won't love it.  

I am a Fan of Johnny Cash.  10 stars.  I'll be back.

This was honestly the worst service I have ever had. This is my first Yelp review I've ever written but I felt the need to say something about how bad the service was. We went at 11 AM on a Saturday and it is currently 12:39 PM and we still have not gotten our food. We also tried to order drinks at the bar and that took at least 15 minutes. It is also not even that crowded right now. The restaurant is clearly understaffed. I hope people find this helpful!

Way better service and experience in this new venue. We sat at the far edge of the room but still had a good view. Music is always great!! Decent selection of beers. The mini donut dessert was just okay.

Anyone who puts below 5 stars for this bar is a douchbag. Yes, please complain more about how you couldn't gain entry because were dressed as a complete moron in a tank top; or how you were kicked out because you were rude to the bar staff or another paying customer. The owner is super nice and the bar staff are the most amazing people I have ever known!! Bob is fucking awesome and one of the most down to earth, friendly, accomodating bartenders I've ever met! Go here for amazing drinks and great music!!

Awful!  Went to the roof.  One bartender! Not a full bar. He's not very nice.  No waitstaff! Order food at bar.  Food comes. COLD!  Two rounds of drinks. Second round is one less drink BUT same price as first round?!!!  NEVER coming back.  Can't believe Dierks Bentley puts his name on this place.

Came here with 3 other people on a Friday night. First floor was packed, second and third floors were empty so we opted to sit on the roof top with around 45-50 other people. Band played good music with asking the crowd for requests multiple times. We got a round of drinks immediate and ordered the potatoes skins. Received them under 10 min later. Nothing special, basic bar food. Overall no complaints and a nice new place.

This museum is a great tribute to the Man in Black. From his military days to his personal troubles to his time as an actor they covered it all. Mr. Cash was also great friends with the owners and curators so there's a ton of fantastic memorabilia. There's also a nice gift shop and coffee shop in the front of the museum. I bought some nice baby clothes which I will put on my dog.
Good food!  I had the cheeseburger.  Free valet parking is a great deal in this part of Nashville.  Really good music!

It's a cool place with a lot of information and memorabilia. The only thing I didn't like was that for the size of the place I thought $15 cover charge was a little steep. My favorite thing I learned about Johnny Cash was the billionth song downloaded on ITunes was Cash's "guess things happen that way". It's a cool place to check out but once was enough for me.

Given the smaller space they are utilizing, the museum is able to cram in a good amount of Johnny Cash memorabilia, music, video and history. Some of it was a bit of a reach... But all in all a good experience and nice quick museum stop on a Nashville tour.

Five stars for the entertainment, regardless of the food!  (Although the food's pretty good, too -- I'd give it at least four stars.)

We were there on Saturday of Thanksgiving weekend, for the early show.  There were four singer-songwriters lined up across the stage, and they took turns performing -- Emily Earle Caroline Watkins, Ruthie Collins, and Tom Whall.  We hadn't heard of any of them before, but really liked them all, each with their own style of singing and songwriting.  It was also fun to hear some of them introduce family members who were visiting for the holiday weekend and were in the audience for the show.

As I'd said earlier, the food was secondary, but good and satisfying.  I'd read about their famous Sweet & Spicy Pickles, so we had to try those as an appetizer.  They were really good!  Just the right amount of spicy, and not too sweet to offset that.

I had the pulled pork sandwich, "Pulled pork, slow smoked in house, then topped with house made creamy coleslaw. Served on a brioche bun and a side of CB's BBQ sauce."  A couple things -- there was far too little coleslaw.  It literally got lost between the (flavorful, juicy) pulled pork and the bun.  And the BBQ sauce is so red in color that I thought they'd brought me a container of ketchup for my fries (which were quite good and didn't need ketchup) until I told the server she'd forgotten my BBQ sauce, and she arrived with a second container of red stuff.  Only then did I try it and realize that it was not ketchup but a very tasty, mildly spicy, BBQ sauce.  This should be more clearly marked, or mentioned by the server, so others don't make the same mistake I did.

Tickets were $10 -- a true bargain!  The food (a $15 minimum required per person, which we had no trouble achieving since we also had a couple rounds of drinks) was reasonably priced and tasty.  This is a fun way to spend an evening with some good entertainment without breaking the bank.

I really wanted to be able to write a better review, but I just could not. First off the entertainment was 5 stars but that's where it ends. We went early to have dinner but after having the appetizer I could not bring myself to order more food. Secondly, our server could have not been more unfriendly.

Being new to Nashville, I wanted to explore Broadway and the bars/restaurants that line the street. When I came up on Whiskey Row, a manager noticed me peeking in and was so kind to invite me in and give me a special tour of the venue. The exterior looks awesome but wait until you get inside, this place is AMAZING! I'm so excited to be here on NYE for the opening! I will be at Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row all night long!

This was my first time to Nashville and my first time to Dierks Bentley Whiskey Row had Jake as the bartender and he was exceptional extremely attentive and the bands that were playing were top of the line  had a great time absolutely recommend when you are in Nashville you stop there and ask for Jake
Miller lite was flat as shit. Disrespectful butch looking bartender, terrible experience. Never going back.

I think the owners read some of the previous reviews. The manager (I think that's who it was) met everyone at the door and ensured they were taken care of. The wait staff was really on top of things. It was busy but they took care of everyone with little delay. For what it's worth - they were all really hot. I don't think that matters much but it was noticeable. (Not that I'm complaining or anything.)

I didn't get a chance to check out the restroom so I can't provide any update to previous reviews that said they were filthy.

The food was (for the most part) excellent. They had a variety of burgers. I had the salmon burger and my wife had the one with avocado and cilantro. She said it wasn't as spicy as she expected but this is the South not San Diego. My only complaint was the fries - they were a bit soggy. They tasted fine but after several minutes they got unappetizing.

We also had the chocolate cake with ice cream. The cake was a bit dry but the ice cream was a cut above what you'd expect in a place like this.

Overall, I'd go back.

Wasn't allowed in because my shirt had intentional rips in it  ...................... I watch girls wearing lingerie get in but my ripped shirt was unacceptable. Maybe if I had taken it off and worn my bra they would have allowed me in. Have never ever run into this issue at any other bar ever.

Decided to go to DB whiskey row for lunch on Saturday for a buddies birthday. Hands down best decision I've made. Was honestly a little bit hesitant with it being on broadway and just wanting to get a bite to eat and to hangout, but I was pleasantly surprised. Our bartender Mike S. On the second floor was hands down the best server I've ever had. Never had to wait for a drank, awesome recommendations, and the absolute best service possible. Next time you go in, ask for Mike, you WILL NOT be disappointed.

Legend, icon, hero, idol, rebel, convict.  Johnny Cash

This is a small but dynamite museum.  Absolutely enjoyed every minute taking a tour of this American original.  The museum is filled with his artifacts, handwritten liner notes, personal artwork, outfits, and walls of his hit records-what an amazing career!

We toured the Museum of Country Music the day before we went through this tour and IMHO, this one is a 10th of the size and is twice as good.  You actually get some meat on the bones of who Johnny was, what his life was like, his successes, demons, and loves.

The museum has a great little eatery and a wonderful gift shop with reasonable priced Johnny memorabilia.  

Located right off the magnificent Broadway, the Johnny Cash museum is not to be missed if you're visiting Nashville

I went to Whiskey Row last night for the second time. I went up to the second floor and had a blast! Mostly because the bartender, Dre, was SO awesome. I don't know who was having more fun, him or the customers. Everyone go see Dre if you're looking for a good time!

$9.00 for a watered down Jack on the rocks, and band managers who try to act like security guards by slapping drinks out of your hand if you accidently leave the bar with one.  It is my business if I get a Public intoxication.  I sincerely hope this place fails.
This is a great venue for listening to singer / songwriters!  Everyone was respectful of the musicians and the listeners.  The food was very good also. I will go back again and again.

The Johnny Cash Museum is definitely a place to come when you're in Nashville.  We made the mistake of going on a Saturday afternoon, which was very crowded.  There's a lot of cool things to see, and several little movie theaters to stop in to get a little more history.  I actually learned a lot about Johnny Cash while I was there.

The Museum isn't huge, but it's full of some of Johnny's outfits, guitars, letters, etc.  It was pretty interesting to see.  There's a wall full of all of his albums.  I had no idea he made so many albums throughout the years.  I'm glad we stopped by.

I took a really long break from 360 Burger. But it seems like not much has changed. I went in today around 3 o'clock. Happy hour had just started, and since it was between lunch and dinner , it was really slow. But somehow, my waitress still managed to make me wait over 5 minutes before taking a drink order. Granted, I think she was having issues splitting checks for a 6 top table. She came back just before I was getting ready to leave.

All I wanted was fries, water, and a couple bar drinks (don't judge. It's happy hour). I sat there and watched my fries sit in the window. It was sitting so long that the bartender brought it to my table. Way to go for teamwork! The heat lamp kept my waffle fries warm and they were yummy so no complaints about the food. (P.S. Try the waffle fries with onion ring sauce) The bartender also noticed that my glass was sitting empty so he refilled my water. Not once did my waitress check on me until I was noticably waiting for the check. Nor did she ask if I wanted another drink. However she brought the check back immediately. 

I wanted to tip the bartender with the awesome mustache, but he left. I try not to give up on restaurants but..... I hardly leave here happy with my experience. They used to be SOOOO good, I just keep trying to get that old thing back. :-(

People moan about bad service here. Get over it. The kids who work here come and go. We had great service. Maybe next week it'll be shite. But that's not a constant. And you can be proactive if you have any problems. In any case, Mondays are great. Kids on stage singing their hearts out. You know some of them are going to make it. Food is good. Beer is cheap. Audience was respectful. If you are in the area on a Monday, come here.

We Stopped by for lunch after my wife had some surgery because She wanted a burger and had I  stopped once before for a drink. We were met at the door and drinks out really fast. After ordering, it took some tine to get our food get to the us. It was really good and she said that the onion rings were the BEST she every had. I have to take her word for it because I don't eat them. Was going to rate them at an 4 until she said that. My 4 rating was because of long wait to get our food but it REALLY was worth the wait.
Food and drinks were great and the service was awesome. A lot to choose from the menu including a great beverage menu.

How on a Saturday night, can you have the only accessible bathroom be on the third floor? Who sat down and thought this is a good idea? Did you not have enough in the budget for a few more feet of pipe?

Had a blast here! I love the atmosphere, the band was awesome. I really enjoyed the Dierks Lemonade, i would recommend that for any first timer. An employee named Thomas Lawson was very helpful, ask for him and he will show you a good time.
The bar is dark and I used the women's stall by accident , single restrooms they all look the same. When I came out the bounce kicked me out for using the women's restroom..

This place is incredible! I don't know what others are talking about with the not so great reviews. I come here all the time and the service and food is incredible. I don't know of any other place in Nashville where you can actually get fresh great food while also listening to music. And the music, let's talk about that...these are the best singer/songwriters in town. Not your honky tonk cover songs. 

Do yourself a favor if you are in Nashville and visit #thelisteningroom - you will not be let down.

We had a great time. Very relaxing the food was better then we expected. One of the best events on our hooneymoon in Nashville. If you want to get away from the bands and noise for a while I recommend this. 2.5 hours, food and beautiful sencery. I think the lunch time is the best because you can see all of the secenery not just lights. Very friendly staff!

We are visiting Nashville for a long weekend and wanted to go places that are more authentic and less touristy. The Listening Room delivered- great intimate venue to hear original music performed by songwriters. They ask that people not talk loudly while the performance is happening and I wish they enforced that a bit more assertively.

Okay. So. We've enjoyed Whiskey Row in the past, but we'll never be back. They were near capacity upstairs and decided to cut a 1/4 of the space into oblivion for no "legitimate" reason. There was barely anywhere to stand to begin with. We left without even finishing our drinks. Not worth it. That is all.  

We also ONLY ordered bottled beers (easy) and didn't order many. If your girl can't hang with a good crowd, MAYBE someone else deserves to work the bar. I know the other girls at the back bar were killing it.

The rating is as much about the man as it is the museum.  Without many plans, we came here to pay homage to the Man In Black.  We are trying to send memories back to my father-in-law and Johnny Cash is a favorite of his (and mine).  The museum is small and well structured to give a view of his life and career over six decades of recording music.

There are stories, music, guitars, photos, clothing, album covers, hit singles (45s), recordings and videos throughout.  Unlike the recent film, which focused on his troubles, the museum brings out the humanity and warmth of his soul.  He supported the underdog and those without hope.  His songs blended poetry and sadness.  His voice is and will remain uniquely and instantly recognized through time.  He was extremely prolific as a songwriter and gifted as a story teller and entertainer.

Well we had to do something cultural. You can't just drink all day... hmmm. 
I was struck by what a poor job they did with this place. They had a few cool items - documents from his military service, letters and music, but not a lot of it. 
The rest of the exhibit seemed like a couple guitars "in the style" of the ones he played, video and music you could see during pledge drive on PBS, and a black jacket. I'm not sure what I was expecting, but I was totally underwhelmed.

Guys, i'm gonna be honest. The scene was good (not great). As a Nashville native, i don't really frequent Broadway. But a friend of mine wanted to go, so i went. At the inception, everyone was extremely nice; bartenders, doorstaff, restroom attendees, everyone. Then i went to the fourth floor. The rooftop which should be the hallmark of any Broadway bar. Took tons of pictures, had a great time, the DJ was playing great music, and i thought it was gonna be a fun night. However comma...The bouncers were pretentious and actually stole something from me while i went to the restroom on the third floor. I went there with two close friends and they validated the fact that the bouncers on the fourth floor STOLE from a paying guest (no, not customer, because i work in food service). Do yourself a favor and keep your effects in your pockets if you leave your table. They'll steal your smokes and try to sell them back to you. Had high expectations for this place and, other than the high-school jock clique that is the 4th floor bouncer staff, would recommend it to any visitor. Great location, great city view, great everything...sort of. And to the GM that is reading this review right now - i moved my one star to a two star because your bathroom attendee (Andre) was nice enough to give me a smoke or two for my troubles. Word to the wise; might be time to check your guys upstairs. And footnote; when i confronted them about it when i saw them smoking my brand, they denied it to my face. I promptly left.

Whenever I mention Nashville, I mention the big bang as a must see! I love this place and go every time i'm there. I'm from Columbus Ohio and we have one here but there is no comparison. The humor and the talent that this Nashville bar has to offer is unmatched! And Kenny Bolton has some awesome drinks to keep you sailing smooth all night!

They are not playing Country!!!  I don't know what else to say. No Alan, No Dirks, No George. There is some Shania but I can't hear the good girl singer because they're playing the music so damn loud. Let's hear the singer!

I was in intrigued when invited to The Listening Room, initially, but more from a 
"try everything once" standpoint...well, now, I'm the one suggesting we go to TLR .  I thoroughly enjoy the music, the variety, seeing the songwriters' personalities, hearing the stories behind the music...and that's the ones that I don't even know their songs.  I never pay attention to who is playing, that night, because I haven't been disappointed - once -in the 4 or so times I've been (and that within a 4 month span...a record for me at any ONE listening venue).  When a writer is present whom you actually recognize their song, it's like you've been doubly thrilled.  They also have a good Siracha small plate...not so much the nachos, for my taste.  Haven't found a go to drink, there, yet, but my research/taste testing shall prevail :O)

This place is fun, happy, lively with good bar food, sports bar, and great bands! 
Live entertainment is good and talented and friendly. Drinks are not the.best but enjoyed listening to rock n roll and a bowl game! #rolltideroll
I am looking forward to going back here when we're in Nashville next time! Huge Dierks Bentley fan!

What a fun time, packed house, good music, great burger and fries. and not over priced like so many other places around Broadway. Everyone there seem to be having so much fun and just a great atmosphere. Beautiful building. Just a lot of fun.

"Listening Room" is an applicable name for this venue. It's one of the best places in Nashville to hear acoustic music. That fact that they also have great food (not just "bar food"), is an additional bonus!

I came to listen to some good music and I wasn't disappointed. This is a setting in which to hear the songwriters behind all the songs you hear on the radio. These people are incredibly talented!! I cannot rate the food or drinks as I didn't have any. This is a low key country bar cafe on 2nd Ave that is the perfect ambient setting to chill and enjoy yourself. The only lighting was that of the stage and the old timey looking filament bulbs. Hard to describe but adequate lighting. There's usually a very long line waiting to get in and for good reason. Get there early and buy tickets in advance. You can also buy shirts as various other souvenirs too. All in all, a great night's activity. I'll be back!

I don't know what everyone was complaining about the show was AMAZING !! The view of the city was excellent and the food was great !!! We didn't have the best of servers but the manager fixed the issue and the night went on :) my son even got a high teething fever and they had a medic on board thankfully he was fine but how can you beat a service like that :) .... Also it was worth every Penney !! Sit as close to the stage as you can

The vibe of the place is pretty cool and you can't beat the live music. The have a decent beer selection - lots of good local options on draft.  Our food was good (we had the nachos with chicken), not anything impressive especially for the price, and the service was just average.  Also, we checked in with the yelp app and were told on the app that we were entitled to a free light beer.  Then our server checked with his manager and we were told that they weren't doing it any more and it was an error on Yelp's part...we thought it was poor form that they didn't still honor it.
A must see in Nashville.  Of all the places we've been in the last week, this is the one place we'll make sure to come back to next trip to town.  The fried pickles are the best you will ever have!

We came on a Tuesday night and the bar was pretty full and lively. The entertainers were on point and took requests. Very fun! However, no one was serving drinks. A man was walking around and clearing tables but refused to take drink orders from tables. He said they had to go to the bar, but the bartender said the gentleman (who refused service to everyone) would be around to take orders. It was frustrating because this one guy was bringing down the mood of the whole establishment by frustrating customers. We were not the only table that was annoyed and irritated. That being said, the entertainment was excellent. The entertainers took multiple difficult requests and played them well with a lot of energy and enthusiasm!
