Went to this bar twice while in Nashville Tn. It was by far the most fun. We tied one on for sure! But 4 floors and elevator and numerous bands you cant go wrong.
This place was so unexpected.  Great drinks, food, and of course music. Would suggest Kids Rock Bar to everyone.

Very cool place,

There is a small informational musem/memorabilia & gift shop.

Great way to learn more about the Legend Johnny Cash

My friends and I had an absolute blast here!! We came multiple times during our trip and it was one of the most fun places we went! Great environment with super friendly employees like the security guard, Matt. I would highly recommend coming here! It definitely gets packed at night and is a great time!

Aweful place and service. It reminds you that racism is still alive. You would think that people grow out of it but there is a little reminder that you are the color you are regardless if your spouse is fighting for this beautiful country. Managers just rude definantly would not recommend this place.

Mediocre at best. They didn't duel at all so don't expect that to happen. It's more bad Karaoke than anything with the same three guys singing every song. Its loud. it's bad music, and bad atmosphere. They ask you to make requests every other song and they make you pay for requests. It's frustrating.

I posted this on Google, they asked me to contact them but no reply yet. Here it is, I just wanted to give a warning to tourists or locals to avoid this place. This place is an embarrassment to our city. There are many others to enjoy but avoid this one. 

Wish I could give zero. Tried to go with my friends Sat. 4/21/18 at around 11 pm. Who ever you had working at the right side at the door needs to be fired. Apparently, I showed my ID too quick and he physically pushed me out of the line into people on the sidewalk. They then told my other friend his wallet looked "fake." Not his ID, his wallet. And then had to joke with the other guy to see if he could come in. This is unacceptable behavior. These "bouncers" are going to get you sued for assault. Your employees are not there to be on an ego trip and pretend they have power. His job was literally to only check ID's. You could of made probably $200 plus from us that night but didn't and won't in the future. I hope that "bouncer" was worth it. I'll take my visiting guests somewhere else.

So comprehensive I never realized the across genre impact Johnny Cash had. My favorite moments were the old flag movie, the Bob Dylan tribute that Johnny wrote, and I was in tears at the end of the museum. I could feel the heartbreak Johnny felt after losing June at the end and was moved to tears. So powerful! Can someone snap a picture of his dedication to Bob Dylan at the Nashville Skyline exhibit and post it!
Music was amazing as you would expect but the food and service is the absolute worst in the entire city and possibly the state. No joke.

Its been more than 3 years since I took the boat but have been four times and once for a Christmas party as well. The shows are great and food was always fantastic, very nice.  Great view of water and nice ride on the boat while enjoying dinner and a show

I'll start off by saying that this place is spot on! I'm a huge Kid Rock fan so I had to check it out. Loved it.  The only thing I'll say is that the bartender that I dealt with was rude. I wanted to buy a shirt. She acted like I was bothering her. I needed a certain size and without checking all the shirts just said there aren't anymore, which was true but she was not cool. Other than that, I would go back.

This gem of a museum is half a block from South Broadway and all the bright neon lights of Honky Tonk Row in downtown Nashville. Johnny Cash and June Carter's stories are beautifully recounted in this interactive museum with listening stations, vinyl collections, stories of collaborations with other museums and stunning displays of the show costumes the couple wore. Don't miss it!

The songwriters were amazing, but service was below subpar and the food was terrible. 

Food: we ordered apps and entrees - fried pickles, hummus plate, pork entree, steak entree. Everything came out at the same time, and everything was cold when it hit our table.  Most of it was inedible. 

Service: very sweet trainee assigned to our table, who unfortunately never checked in. Took our order, reordered is drinks, gave us our check. That was it. No checking on the food, no asking why we didn't eat anything.

Food here is meh...Had some apps and chicken with chimichurri. The chicken was good, but I'd largely avoid the Southern food. Beer selection is quite good, with mostly, but not fully local beers. You must order $15 per person of food or beverages at the Listening Room (note the bar before the show does not count for the $15). Music was outstanding and was the highlight of my trip to Nashville. Pretty cool to hear composers of top country hits playing their music in a small venue with acoustic guitars. So this was a really neat place.

Quick museum, we enjoyed the exhibits and the lay out. They housed some pretty cool things with a few random items that you wouldn't have thought to keep. For example some of June's dresses, a letter he wrote the day of her funeral and his old American Express.
  There is a cafe before you enter and the gift shop had some neat things for all ages.
  If you are a fan of Johnny I would stop in for sure!
Great atmosphere. Food was below average! Service was slow. Location is perfect. Nice restrooms.
Fun place, great atmosphere, live band front and center. Great place to hit up after a Pred's game.

This place suck if you want food or drinks. Waiting over 30 min for drinks and over an hour for food is bullshit. This place has potential but they need to hire better waitresses cause ours was terrible. Music was ok.

Wanted us to pay $5 cover to sit on the patio outside and have a drink. Yeah bye. Do they know you can hear the music out on the street for free?

ETA I received a "compliment" from someone saying they have to pay the performers with a cover charge. You can pay the performers with a drink minimum too, you know.

Arrived at 6pm with 4 girlfriends so we could get a good table. The place started to fill up at 9:30 and by then we decided to move to the upper floor so we could move around and dance. The music was good, spent a fortune on mixed drinks only to realize that shots would guarantee us some alcohol. They deliver the shot glasses with blinking lights - not our thing but that's ok we just switched it off. Server was ok, not warm and friendly but there when we needed something. It's probably my 5th time going to a dueling piano bar spanning from Louisville, KY, Miami,
FL, San Diego, CA, Atlanta, GA and then Nashville. Always enjoyable but I must say Nashville was my least favorite.  Hope they change the layout and add a dance floor in the near future.

For a place that calls itself "whiskey row", I expected a lot more. Sure, it has the tallest rooftop bar in Nashville, and the view is quite nice... but the whiskey selection is sparse at best. When I asked the rooftop bartender for "something local" of the bourbon variety, he didn't have a single clue what to do. The best he could offer was to pour me an $11 Jack Daniel's. Unfortunately, this seemed to be symptomatic of most of the bars on Broadway. Bummer. 

The live band that was playing at the time was a total joke. The lead singer sounded totally off-key (drunk, actually) while trying to cover an R&B song. Yikes.

We left as soon as we were done with our overpriced commercial whiskey. Not returning here.
Loved listening to the Song Suffragettes.  Arrived early. Had affordable drinks before the show. Bartender was helpful and attentive.  Food during the show was average but show was terrific.

It's pretty small and perhaps a bit expensive given the size but if you're a Johnny Cash fan you need to pay the money and see the inside.  Lots of photos, mementos and history of the start and rise of his career.  Lots of facts that I didn't realize about him especially his work with prisoners and why he did that particular type of charity for lack of a better word.  If you're staying in a hotel near downtown, it's a short walk and parking down along Broadway is horrific so better to walk or take the free bus
The songwriters were great! Found a sharp object in my chicken though...might consider eating before you to and just do drinks!

One of the funniest bars on Broadway! Every floor is a different experience and the staff was quick and attentive. I felt it was less crowded than a couple other of the rooftop bars because each floor was open and so large and airy. We had no trouble getting a table and were able to enjoy the music.

Whiskey Row is always a blast. Had been to one before while visiting Arizona so it was a pleasant surprise to find one in Nashville. Had an amazing time. Drinks were great. Staff seemed friendly. Had an especially nice encounter with Thomas Lawson. He saw that all our needs were met. Would definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants a little up beat country fun in an almost club-like atmosphere. 5 stars.
I absolutely love the Listening Room Cafe - my first visit was at the Cummins Station Location in 2009 - been hooked ever since :)

Four of us went here for lunch this weekend, or brunch as they call it. I should have known as soon as the waitress said there was no hamburger meat, we should have left, but we stayed and ordered. The inside dining room was empty, and there were a few tables on the deck occupied. After 50 minutes with no food, and a clueless look on the staff person's face when we asked how much longer, we left. This is the first time in my life I walked out of a restaurant due to service. Congratulations Listening Room.

A fitting tribute to a country legend.  

The museum is a bit cramped but it places the emphasis first and foremost on his music, and you can listen to various versions of each of his songs (versions by him on different audio formats, and also covers from many artists).  It also has some neat memorabilia.  Most importantly, it shows you the humanitarian side of Cash.  

If you're a country music fan, it's not quite a pilgrimage site but it's one of the better music museums I've come across.
Wonderful experience here. The bands were better then any other bars on broadway (we tried them all), the food was good and atmosphere was really great!

Ahhhh what can I say about the Song Suffergettes?  Amazing!   Such an awesome night we had and we also were blessed to listen to a live interview with Liz Rose who co-wrote so many of Taylor Swift's song as well as "Girl Crush" by Little Big Town, "Cry Pretty" with Carrie Underwood.     The girls that sand were amazing and no didn't several of these kick ass women are your next big thing.    The food ehhh.   Eat before you go.  The drinks were good.  The talent can't be beat.  Can't wait to go back.

Fun place. Drinks are very reasonable for B-way. Staff is cool with the neon outfits.  Band was excellent  and place sounds terrific. Highly recommend.  Did not have food while we were here.  Overall a great time.

The Listening Room is one of our favorite places to go when in Nashville. Great music, good food, and a nice sized room. Highly recommend this place if you want to hear some great Nashville songwriters.

I have never been so disappointed in 360 Burger at my visit today. This restaurant started out when it was owned by Swett's with Hot Chicken (delicious) and then Salmon Burgers (delicious) and we frequented it often. They decided to do away with the Hot Chicken but kept the Salmon Burger so we added the Cheesy Goodness Burger on their menu to replace the Hot Chicken. That kept us coming back. Then it was purchased by Freeland Chevrolet Superstore and it quickly went down hill on ambiance and food quality. Today after work I went back to order food to go and they have now done away with the Salmon Burger and the Cheesy Goodness Burger. So I ordered a burger adding cheeses in hope of recreating it and then order just a burger for myself. The cooks were not happy and fussed because they said Cheesy Goodness Burger is off menu and didn't like the fact they had to add all the cheeses. Then I requested the homemade chips and was told we only cook those for patrons eating in, but were gracious enough to do it for me, after all, I was the only one in the store. It looked like a ghost town. I will give a gold star to 360 Burger's server Connor B. He was so gracious and so kind in working with me to recreate the meal hopefully to be as memorable as in times past. Took the food home and we sat down to eat, the hamburgers were horrible. There was absolutely no texture to the meat. Every bite taken was like putting a big blob of slime in our mouths. We finally had to throw it out. The ONLY thing good was the homemade chips and fruit bowl! $30 wasted! We will probably not be going back!
Excellent bar! Great atmosphere, love the live music and open windows! Shana was an excellent server - very attentive and quick! Thank you!!

Absolutely love the atmosphere. The bar, the lights, the stage. We ordered our tickets online for the 6pm show and came 5 minutes late. They had our name and seated us right away. The performers were incredible. So great to hear live music from the songwriters. Unfortunately we only had drinks and didn't eat. Although the food around us looked and smelled great! Everyone seemed to enjoy it. Not enough servers for how large the place is. Hard to grab our servers attention. However it is completely worth it. The music was great and I would pay more than $5 next time to see a show.
Came here two days after opening and only second day getting foood and food was great! Service was better! Our new favorite spot in Nashville!!!! Happy New Year to Us!!

Very cool spot in the hood and first timers at this place. We were drawn in by the sign that read bring your pups and have a mimosa on the deck. We sure did take that advice and enjoyed a couple before the rain started. We still were able to enjoy the atmosphere and service.

We had a blast at Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row! It was refreshing to find a more modern (and cleaner!) bar on Broadway, and one that also serves great food! There are 3 levels, make sure not to miss to rooftop! Easily the nicest on broadway. The staff was very attentive and friendly. Great vibe overall, stands out from the other honky-tonks. Would absolutely return again.

By far my favorite out of all of the celebrity establishments around the city. The service was on point and the live music was amazing. Multiple levels to check out different bands. Another huge plus was the super clean bathrooms which is hard to come by in Nashville

Really nice venue and some interesting music, but every other part of the experience was tortuous, from the moment we arrived until the time we left.  We had no tickets, so we went inside to purchase some for the late show while the early show was just ending.  We were rudely dismissed and told to wait outside, where it was hot. Despite there being tables and chairs and a bar right inside the door, there no refreshments. Huge missed opportunity. 

They told us they'd open the doors at 8:00, but didn't open them until 8:20. No explanation.  Instead, the same, "You're lucky we're dealing with you at all" attitude. No explanations about how the two lines (unticketed and ticketed) would work, so we had to improvise, which led to our waiting in the line for a good 15 minutes, only to have a couple of people just walk up and get in to pubs tickets before us.

Our server was OK, Althea we had to pull him aside to get him to take our food order.  Food was pretty good, and it's delivery was pretty fast.  No complaints there.

But when the music ever started, people wouldn't shut up.  We'd ad the warning about no talking during performances, but it wasn't enforced at all.  There was a large group of what seemed to family members and friends of one of the performers from New York who occupied a back corner of the venue and were engage in loud conversations during all the performances except hers. She even went back to join them.  I asked the server to ask them to shut up, and he did nothing.  Given the he sound was pretty poor to begin with, the noise ruined the night.

This could b a great place to listen to performers, but it needs new management because the current managers clearly have no idea what they are doing.  I won't go back until I see signs here that they have changed their ways.

I think this was my favorite bar on broadway! The stage is soo cool. It's two floors open space so two floors of the restaurant can actually see the one stage. And on my second night in a row there, Kid Rock was there and sang for a solid hour!! Great time, great music!

This was a blast! We stopped by later in the evening and had some trouble getting a drink on the first floor so we ventured up to another. The band on the second floor was great and we had a lot of fun dancing! Drinks were reasonably priced. I would definitely come back!

By far the best bar in Nashville these days.  Great service and great food.  The place is huge and has different music to offer on different floors. I'll def be heading back again.  I must say the service and staff was awesome, especially Dre who always made sure we didn't have to wait for a drink!

Awesome place to enjoy good food. The restaurant is 5 stories and there is live bands there all the time! When I was there there was a live band between the first and second floor and another on the roof top bar. The 4th floor was closed. The restaurant is very loud because of the bands but so are practically all restaurants in Nashville.
I'd rather get circumcised again than go Downtown but if you find yourself looking to get a couple in you before a Preds game this is a really cool place to get a drink.

We really enjoyed this place! We went earlier in the day and listened to a country rock cover band. The place seems newer and clean. Very large, open and bright with high ceilings. There are multi levels. We were on the entry ground level. Great view of the band, and our server was very good. Our adult children went back later that evening for the night scene, and sent us a video of them singing and dancing to Elton Johns, Crocodile Rock. We did not order food. Will definitely go back. 
Update: Actually, we went back several times during our weekend stay. So much fun. We did eventually order bar food and it was super good. Chicken tenders, French fries and nachos. It's on a corner lot and the breeze zipping through made for a comfortable stay.

Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk is the best bar on Broadway! First Time in Nashville and first bar we walked into. The singers were great and entertaining. Both performers we saw played great music and had the crowd going. All the songs they played were hits, country and rock. We left for a bit to check out the other bars on broadway but came back to the place. If you're looking for a good time Kid Rocks bar is the place to be.

The memorabilia is great, but the space could be set up better.  There are tons of things to see, but no clear flow of traffic through the tiny rooms they are housed in making it really difficult to weave through shoulder-to-shoulder people in order to see everything.  Also, there was an entire section dedicated to other performers that Cash was close with like Elvis and Carl Perkins that I didn't really need to see memorabilia for

My family went here for dinner and the music.  One of our favorite experiences in Nashville.  So neat to see and hear the work that goes into songs and to see it from the perspective of the songwriter. We will be back. Oh and the food was great too!!!
Great music! Enjoyed time there last night, First band was amazing and loved that he brought the bartender up on stage..\ she had an amazing voice

Was enjoying an awesome pop band tonight on the first floor and they were told to stop playing after like four songs. The band was awesome and everyone was really enjoying it, so I'm not sure why they got cut. Someone said that they needed to play country,  but why would you hire a pop band if you wanted country music? Now this bar is the only one on broadway without live music. I went to cash out and my tab had a bunch of drinks that I didn't order. Couldn't get it sorted out with the bartender so I just sucked it up, but I'm pretty unhappy.  

This bar is gorgeous and I know they just opened so maybe they're still getting it together, but my first visit was a bust. I'll come back in a few months and update my review if things get better.

Place has changed a lot. Awesome Monday and Wednesday night local music showcases. Wednesday is songwriters and Monday are bands. Clientele has changed and everyone is respectful. Owner Is changing image and it's working. Give it a shot.

My food was very good.  The quality of the beef and the size of the patty was great.  The fries were good, seasoned with just enough sea salt.  The bun was very fresh.  The produce was a good quality.

The service was good.  You seat yourself, and there should be a sign saying so.  I saw several people standing in uncertainty at the door.  The live music was great and not so loud, we were easily able to carry on a conversation.  

Lots of good choices on the menu.  Several healthy options.  For my first visit, I wanted to try a classic burger.  I had the All American Burger and regular fries.  Next I'll try the Cilantro Avocado Burger with jalapenos and habanero cheese.  I can't wait to go back!

We had a great time on Sunday afternoon. Family atmosphere and good food with quality cocktails. We all loved the craft cocktails and being from California I was fine with the prices.  The appetizer we ordered was great, too. 

It's a busy place and Andrea our server helped us find a seat at a shared table and then moved us to an open table when one came available.  Bar service was slow, but Andrea kept in touch and apologized for the delay. She made our experience there welcoming and she was so friendly.  When we return I will request her section- she really built a nice rapport with us. Staff works so hard to keep everyone happy. 

The band was fantastic!  Again, great way to spend a Sunday afternoon. One shout out to Mike - as he hit the tables for tips and requests, he skipped ours. I hope not because we were three women...  I had a big tip ready for the bad and we were passed by.  Mike - don't judge! 
Anyway, the band got their tip as I left - they were so talented. 

See y'all again soon- and thanks Andrea!

Said it was open till 2am, closed at 1am. Waited for 30mins before waiter came over. Piano players could play different genres of music that's why I gave two stars, but it wasn't exactly a dueling piano bar (going back and forth with each other) it was more just one singing and then the other singing a song. Floors were super dirty, littered with napkins and trash.
So super fun to chill, drink cocktails, and the music was the best ever! Not just country. Every band could play any and every song!
Stopped in for a quick bite and drink before nephew's wedding.  Live music at 6 and 8:30 pm. But we wont be here for that.

Great museum, even if you are not a JC fan.  It does get a bit crowded once you first enter which makes it difficult to read and appreciate the first few exhibits, but it does get better once fully inside.  The museum does have a LOT of memorabilia and the exit music video will leave you in tears.

July 12, 2019 we did the VIP lunch and it was amazing....... From the time we were escorted to the boat we were treated with the best southern hospitality you could want. Food was fresh, tasty and plentiful, the special VIP desert was fantastic. Ash was our waiter and he did a superior job in making us feel welcome and took great care of us! The show was fun and entertaining. The captain gave a fun and informative tour of the pilot house and all of the VIP extras made our experiences fantastic! Bob & Dave on the upper deck were a surprise and they did an amazing job entertaining us. Loved our day on the Cumberland River!
Loved it here. Sweet music and saw Kid Rock jump on the stage and tear it up. Will be back!

Mcb is located in the Opryland area of Nashville. This is where you find authentic Country Music... There's only a few bars left on lower broad that hire  anything that resembles country music, so best to come here if you love Hag, Willie, Cash, Waylon ect... This is one of 4 Country bars in the Opryland area and all have great music! Any night of the week you will find artists , locals and musicians here. Also...Pool table , dancing and strong drinks.

Your review helps others learn about great local businesses.

Please don't review this business if you received a freebie for writing this review, or if you're connected in any way to the owner or employees.

Great burger place. Excellent burgers, fries, and onion rings. They are very friendly, and helpful. Good selection of beer both draft and bottled. There burgers are cooked to your requested doneness and very juicy, napkins are a must. They host live bands several nights of the week.

Come here for the music, not the food.  

We came for a 6:30 show to experience the "real" Nashville music scene -- we were not disappointed.  The artists were authentic and wonderful.  

The food on the other hand was another story but we came to experience the music instead of the food.
Visiting from Arizona and stumbled upon this place. Bartenders and servers were awesome. Shoutout to Maddie and Jackie for the awesome service!!!

I was pretty impressed with this little hole in the wall museum. It wasn't overpriced and the information presented was pretty extensive. The employees are helpful and the admission process was simple and efficient. 
Stop by if you're in Nashville!

Great spot for great music from singer song writers.  Heard familiar country music from big stars...but these guys were the writers!! Pretty impressive and entertaining.  Every seat is good.  A great time!
Good food and consistently decent music playing. Not a huge space and a single stall bathroom is a drag. But the drinks are cold, food is quality, and music is good.
Loved it! Beautiful inside and the rooftop was awesome. Loved the music! We ordered the grilled chicken salad and chicken Cesar salad which both were very good and light on a hot summer afternoon.

Very cool venue that books great acts. Drink prices are reasonable, but the staff was insanely unprofessional. The last time I tried to go, I'd lost my ID and called ahead and asked if I could use other identification that I had. They assured me I would be fine and said they wrote my name down. After waiting in line for over an hour, I was denied entry and told that I had to leave. They were very rude about it as well. Thanks for making me miss my favorite band Basement East! You could have at least told me not to come at all.

I LOVE live music. Living in Nashville is tough because there are almost too many great concerts. My mind is telling me yes but my bank account is telling me no. This is why I appreciate places like The Basement East. The tickets are affordable and they bring in some maybe less-know talent that I love. Not saying that the artists aren't famous, they just aren't on the ridiculous level of say JT. I went to my first show here on a Sunday night to see Marian Hill. Tickets were a little over $30 after taxes and fees. The Basement East is in East Nashville (duh) so parking isn't a nightmare. There is a paid parking lot next to the building but we found free parking on a nearby street. Doors opened at 7:00 so we got there around 7:30. There was no line to get in and the check in process was super easy. I printed off my tickets but there was no need for that. If you bought tickets online they have all of the information on their tablet. Showed them our IDs, got a wristband, and we were in! The Basement East is a smaller dive venue. One bar in the back with reasonably priced drinks. They had a decent draft list and we were able to get an IPA for $6. There is a patio and some high top tables with chairs. The stage is at the front and is nothing fancy. Standing room only except there was one section with couches that was up a little higher. I'm guessing this is the VIP section or first come first serve. It wasn't too busy when we got there so we were able to get great spots at the front of the stage. Of course we got pushed back a bit once the music started by those concert goers that don't seem to care about personal space or basic human manners, but that's just the concert life. The concert itself was AMAZING. The sound was loud and I really don't think there is a bad spot to watch the show. We were so close to the stage so I felt like I was right there with the band. There were lights and fog so the stage was transformed into something really cool. I mean I don't think Marian Hill can do any wrong so that definitely helped. My one complaint is when I bought 2 beers at the bar, they kept my card open without telling me. I tipped in cash so I didn't even think about the fact that I didn't sign anything. I knew I was only going to be buying one drink because I was driving. So then 2 days later I got charged the extra fee for not closing out. Hard to close your tab when you don't know it's open. Oh well. Life goes on. Lesson learned. The concert was great and I will for sure be back to see more!

A nice low key place to listen to some good music. Service was much faster than I had expected considering some of the previous reviews that I've read. A wide range of mixed drinks and beer were available, which was a plus. As the the food, I would say it was not bad but not great either. We had the wings, chips, and chicken tenders.

The service was friendly, the food was all right. Few vegetarian options-- the portobello burger was okay. The portobello itself was a little too sweet. The fried pickles are good though- definitely get some of those. My mom said her turkey apple sandwich was mediocre... the toast was a little too charred, the sliced apples were a "jarring note". Everything was warm except the turkey, which was cold, which made the cheese cold again. The fries were good. All in all, not bad.

Come for the music .. and beers do not eat!!! Food is inedible.. I can't believe it a caption audience and service is terrible.. (not the most friendly servers) just the process.. and food is terrible!

This was probably my favorite thing we did during our trip to Nashville. A local recommended it. We didn't decide in time to buy tickets, so we tried our luck with showing up early for the wait list. The food wasn't great, but the music was awesome!

We headed here for an evening with a bunch of colleagues- and yes we headed here for the music which was really rather good. 

The artists were funny and talented although the one that was super young and had the best voice by far, started to grate in the end as every song was about her miserable, angry relationships that failed horribly and sounded like songs one would listen to before jumping off the nearest bridge! But the rest of the songs were enjoyable and the banter between the artists was incredibly funny!! Their guitar playing and voices were amazing.

The drinks were so so and we had been warned that our food would mirror that and it did. Hummus was not good, fried pickles were superb, the table went crazy for the wings. I had a veggie burger and was super excited that they served the 'Beyond Meat ' brand and that - the patty was good but poorly cooked and the  rest of the plate was as bland as cardboard and was left behind.

Go for the music and maybe some appetizers and it's a fun night out

5 stars for the entertainment but I'm sorry only 3 for the food, HOWEVER, come for the music because you'll be blown away. That was truly wonderful. The food needs improvement but the drinks were fine. If they stepped up the food, they'd be 5 stars in total. Bravo for the great music Listening Room. Thank you

Come here to drink NOT to eat! It's a great bar with good drinks and live music. However, it's not the place I'd recommend for ordering food. 6 of us came here for lunch on a Saturday and it took at least 30 minutes just to get water delivered to our table. And then an additional 30 to even receive our food. I ordered a slider and sweet potato fries and although they were good, it wasn't worth the hour wait. Like I said, great place to hang out and have drinks.

Cool boat but for $45 a pop plus inconvenience fees you'd think they could remove all the spiders and webs that were EVERYWHERE. There were spiders crawling everywhere. They also need to clean the outdoor furniture. Cruising down the river was awesome.

I went for the lunch cruise. The food was good, and there was plenty of it. The entertainment was decent. It's hard to compare after being in downtown Nashville and hearing all the amazing artists out there. The view is very limited, as most of the ride is along a dirt/grassy bank. The only time you really see anything is when you get to downtown Nashville and you can take some pictures with the skyline in the back. The cruise mostly consisted of an older crowd. Overall it was pretty chill, and gave us something to do.

Tourist tap in Nashville. Bartenders don't care and they know people won't stop coming.  How about a smile and acknowledgement people? Didn't eat the food was on a liquid diet. Music was good and changed thru the night.
Horrible. It's inside dicks took forever to get a drink after paying cover. DO NOT GO. BADDDDD DECISION

Let me start off by saying, my friend and I are both servers/bartenders and we have NEVER experienced service like we did here on Sunday 4/22. We sat down, were greeted by Samantha after 10 mins of waiting. She was rude and standoffish. We ordered drinks (the margarita and J.I.M.B.O) and their "Artichoke Dip". She wrote down our drinks AND the dip. We again waited about 10 minutes before finally getting our drinks.. *we were sitting right behind the service bar and watched them make drinks* but never received our dip, let alone, she never came over to ask how our drinks were.. finally 15/20 minutes later she finally takes our food order.. i order the mushroom burger medium with garlic fries and a side of ranch, my friend ordered the steak and fries.. a guy brought us our food, as Samantha watched him put it down on our table *this is usually the part where she SHOULD come over and ask how everything looks, but instead went to talk to 3 guys at the bar and joke around with them* i took 1 bite of my burger and it was completly raw on the inside.. not rare, literally raw.. it took us about 7 minites to flag her down, she took the burger and had them remake it *again, USUALLY when an order is messed up you tell the cooks you need it ON THE FLY* my remake took another 25 minutes to be brought back to me, this time, it came out well done *which i was so starving i didnt even care at that point so i ate it* ALSO it came out with regular fries..not garlic ones like i ordered.. also didnt come with ranch OR ketchup..let alone no salt or peper on the table... i had to ask another server to get me ketchup cause one again samantha was back at the bar joking around with 3 guys *who later got kicked out..humm" 
I appreciate you taking the burger off my bill, but that was the absolute worst service i have ever seen. I would understand slow service if she was busy or in the weeds, but sitting right behind the bar and watching her going over to flirt with 3 guys over and over instead of checking on her tables was just ridiculous *i also noticed the table to our right getting frustrated aswell when we made eye contact with them.. i was so excited to try this place out and get a burger and spin dip that day and was beyond disappointed. I will most definitely not be returning... and that girl should not be a server.. i have trained MANY servers and bartenders and watching her made me cringe so many times.. I'm very angry and disappointed.

SOUND:  Oh goodness, the ALT Aaron Lee Tasjan band and the rest of the FOUR TWENTY line up sounded amazing!!  It didn't seem to matter where I stood, out in the crowd it was so so good.  It was so loud and people were also talking so loud. 

HEAT VS AC:  It was maybe in the 60s during the day and felt cool in the room and then it filled up and man it was SO HOT!  Everyone started moving towards the door to catch the cool breeze every time the door opened!

PARKING:  Unfortunately if you arrive any later than at least one hour before doors open it's hard to find a FREE parking spot (and nearby). 
I recommend arriving around 7pm if doors are 8pm, and walk down to 5 points for pizza or burgers then walk back for the show.  Typically the band goes on at 9pm, so it's perfect timing.

DRINKS:  Sadly I did not end up getting a drink to comment on the pricing or taste.

FOOD:  Wait! I saw someone posted about food!! I didn't know that they had food!!?!?! I love bar ish food! I'm so bummed I didn't find out until reading some other reviews on here.
The best experience with Craig the Kitchen Mgr and chef extraordinaire!!!  Best ribs, wing, Brussels sprouts, mashed potatoes ever!! And oh my gosh the Bloody Mary's

I was soooooo excited to come here it was the only thing we planned for Nashville. I had planned on spending some time reading and listening to music and walking away with a new hat. Instead I walked out halfway through because it is poorly managed. The crowd control stinks everywhere I attempted to go was jammed packed forcing me to just walk out with nothing. I would not recommend to anyone at the moment. Crowd control problems are too much

I'm not from Nashville but this feels like a true country music Nashville experience. Went on a Saturday for the 6PM show and there were 3 musicians who took turns singing songs and telling stories. The musicians were skilled, told great stories, and there was funny banter between them.  Highly recommended. Show was $5 with chicken wings, two vodka sodas, and a bowl of chili adding an additional $40 to our tab so it's easy to hit the $15 min food/drink per person.

We tried a few artist's bars up and down Broadway and Dierk's had the best menu by far. The food was really good and the band that was playing was fun. I'd say the only downside is that the space is a bit small for the crowd.

Worst experience I've ever had at an establishment. Got a pineapple drink and the juice was rancid. I'm not one that likes to complain cause I know it's a pain as a server/bartender. Told the bartender, bleach blonde with short hair and a fake tan and she said "I don't know what the f*** you want me to do." Uhhh, remake me something else cause you gave me rancid juice...? Easy solution. Instead I was met with a girl who was clearly miserable with her life and made sure I was aware. She proceeded to ask me what I wanted and I said a vodka soda. She then slammed in the on the counter and slid it towards me. I grabbed it and threw it away. Maybe whiskey row should reconsider who they hire and who actually wants to be there, cause this chick hated her life and made sure her customer knew that. Never been treated that bad by customer service, ever. There's much better options on broadway in terms of music and especially service. Don't waste your time here

Went to Nashville for a long weekend -- good times full of good music and great eats!  Believe it or not the Swinging Door has some great grub!  Granted it's your typical bar food but it's very good (and we were even sober) I bet it's even better if you're not!  Ha! 

The Cuban was fantastic among the best I've had     and my friends loved their burgers.  We got cheesy tots as a starter--YUM!  Crispy tater tots--HELLOOO!  We also had the bloody mary which as others have said,  is a meal in itself.  It would definitely hit the spot when you need 'a hair of the dog that bit ya' on the morning after. 

This will be a regular stop on our visits to Nashville.

I'm giving this 3 stars for the boat ride and the entertainers who were top notch.  The food was dismal.  Practically inedible actually.  The salad and bread were acceptable and everything else was horrifying.  The kind of food they pack our buffets at hoping you will eat yourself into a coma and not notice.  Baked beans that tasted like ketchup and greasy chicken.  Definitely not worth the price.  They won't even give you Soda without charging.  Go on the boat ride and eat after and save your money and prevent indigestion.

Very cool museum. Had several items that had never been on display anywhere else. Great insight into Johnny's life. If you like this place, and you will, check out storytellers in Bon Aqua for a look at Johnny's getaway in the country. I'm a huge Cash fan, and maybe a little biased here, but this is a do not miss while in Nashville.

Atmosphere was nice, serve was cool. Food was awesome! We ate food here, the prices were decent for food. The drink selection was great! The bands playing on both floors were okay for a Saturday. Keep us here for a few hours.. THE ONLY thing that sucked was the female bartenders were wearing some cute sweaters and my wife wanted to purchase one. The bartenders directed us to the booth downstairs to purchase. When we left we stopped at the booth to buy one... but the lady tells us that these sweaters aren't for sale to the public. Well that sucked...
The burger was good the friend pickles were great. The Old fashioned was amazing!!!!!!
Bar service limited...only 2 bartenders in a packed house...restrooms disgusting...place just not all that

Met some friends there and listened to some great music for a couple hours. Great place! Only downside is be prepared to wait in line to use the restroom if you're on the bottom floor. They only have one toilet in the women's restroom.

Food is ok. Nothing great.  Entertainment is also ok. Nothing great. They do try hard though. 

If I had a choice between General Jackson and taking a nap, I'd take the nap.  

The cruise is not good at all. If you like seeing a cement plant it's fine. Otherwise, there is nothing to see.  A complete waste of time.
I have loved every visit I have made to the Listening Room.  Excited to be going back to Nashville in March and hear some great music at the Listening Room!

Disappointing experience.  The place is run like a low class dive bar.  "Security" are all over in marked T shirts and all of them have a "get out of my way" attitude. A real turn off.  The capstone was when the security bouncers came through at around 11pm and forcibly took all the bar chairs from any patron who was sitting on them.  It was a total intimidation move with "get up I'm taking the chairs".  I watched one of these goons bully a 60 year old guy and his wife who were too slow to get up for them.  Shameful.  This bar is a low class place.  Lots of better stops in the area.

The food was ok, but the Song Suffragettes were AWESOME.  We got the brisket, slaw, mac n cheese, and potato salad. The mac n cheese was pretty dry and lukewarm. The slaw definitely needed some more kick. The brisket was pretty decent, but it definitely needed more bbq sauce. The food was definitely meh compared to some of the other places we ate in Nashville.

However, it's totally worth it to see the Song Suffragettes.  Out of all the musical performances we saw in Nashville, these were the most memorable- we swear some of them will be really famous some day. They're basically a way for young female aspiring country musicians to showcase their talent and play their songs. I'm not the biggest fan of country, but these girls basically changed my mind. Go Song Suffragettes!

Incredibly rude serving staff. On 8/4/18 a specific server told me I had to move from where I was sitting 3 different times only to let others sit where she originally told me to move. When I asked why others could sit in those places but not me she went on to tell me that they weren't preventing her from doing her job like I was. Everyone else in the bar was sitting around sipping on their drinks listening to the band playing as was I. I waited until the third time she told me to move to tell her that she was being rude and giving me an attitude and that she should at least make the others move too like she did me. She then threatened to kick me out for me telling her she was rude. I never got a "sorry" from her but I did get a few too many eye rolls before I confronted her poor behavior. In my opinion, in no circumstance should a staff member of any establishment be rude to a customer. She represented Dierks Bentley poorly and I have no doubt her employment would be questioned if her management knew how she spoke to a paying customer. On a positive note, bartenders were prompt and nice. However, wait staff was not worth the experience of this place. I will not recommend this bar to anyone.

A great venue to see a songwriters show, as we did.  Food was good too, my wife had the pulled pork sandwich and I liked the turkey club.  Sight lines were good for the show as well as the acoustics.

BEWARE of the Waze directions, they were not updated.  Make sure you have the correct address!!!

Found my new hang out spot in lower Broadway!! Came here with an open mind & had the BEST experience!! A group of friends & I came New Year's Eve to get table service & I had the best customer service provided, awesome energy & music and drinks. Will be back to try some of the food i saw some good feedbacks on

I loved it! Me and my husband went for drinks! They had live bands! It was awesome! The talent was great!  This place was so cool! Prices for drinks were very reasonable! I definitely recommend this place!  It was awesome! The place was packed! It's definitely something to experience!

Came for a women's songwriter show over President's day long weekend, nice mix of locals and tourists, us in the latter group. Kristen Castro, Mary Bragg, Madeleine Kelson and Crystal Bowersox - we knew Crystal from her American Idol stint, but she has grown her art way beyond that, and all the musicians on stage were outstanding. Was a treat to hear the collaboration as they backed each other up on harmonies and other instruments, through a top notch sound system. I wish we had something like this locally at this consistent high level of musical quality. That's why you go to Nashville.

Food was way better than I expected for a venue like this - I had excellent smoked pulled pork sandwich, and there was a nice selection of sides if you didn't want the standard fries or chips; had some really good roasted brussel sprouts I devoured on server recommendation. My friend's hummus bowl and turkey sandwich looked great, all fresh cut veggies and pita. Good selection of local and regional craft beers on draft, not the standard stuff. Its not gourmet, but was great accompaniment for the reason we were there, which was the music. 

Service was a little slow in the beginning, but its the nature of the setup - everyone comes in at once at a set time for the show, they get drinks and water, take orders, and serve all the food roughly at the same time to the whole place - and try not to disturb the music. Once everything came out our server came back multiple times to refill water, get new beers, take plates, and deliver the check. I found the staff to be efficient and discreet.

Only reason this is not a 5 - the entry process was a little wonky. We arrived a little bit before the scheduled show time, but the previous show was still wrapping up. We were told to hang out on the patio, no line at that point - so we sat down at some patio tables. We remarked they could have used some servers or a bar so we could get some adult beverages, they were losing a $$ opportunity. At some stage a line started to form, and since we were sitting, we ended up toward the back, not paying close attention (our fault totally, we didn't jump up). As a result we ended up being seated toward the back of the room, even though we noticed there was empty tables closer - possibly being held for VIPs? Or maybe just trying to spread out the servers?  Not sure, but it felt a little weird, like not treating the out of towners the same. Take it as feedback.

 Anyway, I still would go back and recommend to any music lovers visiting Nashville for an enjoyable afternoon or evening of music and good food.

I love thé music at dierks, but i consistently get tréated badly. At first i thought it was one specific worker, but I think that this establishment is not 'minority friendly'.  The patrons and workers are consistently nasty and biased and I'm honestly not about to put up with it. I'm going on strike. I also would not advise anyone else who isn't white and American to patronize this business and go somewhere that is more customer friendly. thank you, next.

I found this place by internet search, and checked on yelp, seems the feedback are quite positive.. so purchased the tickets on line.. it's inexpensive.. we went there from walking from broadway, it's quite some walk, the venue is pretty sizable, and on a Tuesday evening, we have 4 artist joined.. they sing one by one, and each of them will also introduce their song and how they wrote it.  So it's quite good if u are open to some young artist.. the food is ok.. my chicken breast is quite dry and the fried Brussels spout is pretty good, i don't think i can make it myself. The hummus is good too.. they also gave me 50% off on my hummus with yelp check in.. my husband ordered cobb salad with their chili soup.. he seems very happy with the performance and food as he gives a 25% tip!! That's a little tricky though, as the 25% is the first tip choice right after no tip, next is 20%, 15%.. haha..
Came here for a bachelorette and it was lively. The drinks were not expensive. The shots came in a lighted small glasses

I'd like to comment on my experience here but our entire party of 5 was not granted entrance at the door due to us having one African American gentleman with us. The door man's reason was discriminatory, racist and hypocritical as every white man that walked in past us was dressed identically. I'm sure the establishment is successful but the door man's actions & excuse is a poor reflection of management and sadly, a reflection of his close-minded self. 

You know what they say, when you have a good experience, you'll share it with one or two people. When you come across a bad experience, you'll share with a multitude of people. Needless to say, we won't be returning.

Expensive, cheesy, not many amenities. It gets hot here in Nashville, you'd think there'd at least be water for people paying $60 a ticket. You won't be in the a/c until you're in the dining room. 

Service on the deck for drinks was pretty spotty. A beer is $14. Food inside was okay (beans, Mac n cheese, bbq were good). 

The show was definitely a show! I already knew going in it wouldn't be my favorite music (this was all for my visiting family) but man I have to say I would appreciate it if the ladies on stage would wear a bit more clothing. Honestly, they're on an elevated stage, cleavage out, short dresses and twirling, shaking their butts. I just felt like it was completely inappropriate. I would not take anyone else here. 

More a/c options and water for guests would make this a lot more enjoyable.
Great food- had filet cooked to perfection! Service was great and the music was awesome! Seen James Dean and Rachel(?) 7/22/19 they both had a lot of talent!!

With so much word around about this place I tried it out for the first time tonight. I had a simple bacon cheeseburger with habanero cheese along with sweet potato fries. The burger was very good but pretty greasy, yes I understand a burger is supposed to be greasy but this was bun being soggy from the grease. The mood from the room was quite chill and relaxing., beer prices are a bit expensive for this type of setting, my overall rating for this place was very good. Will I be back? Yes 
Would I recommend this place? Yes 
I read reviews about the service not being upto par, I sat at the bar so service reviewing is out on this one. I'd give it at least 3.5 out of 5. I'll be back to add more when I eat here again.

I used to like this bar, but not anymore thanks to the racist bouncer at the door.

The bouncer turned refused entry to one of my friends saying there were no "flat-billed hat allowed."  (He was black.)  We asked if he could just put the hat in his pocket, but the bouncer said no, and that "there was nothing he could do."  While talking to the bouncer, he immediately let in a white guy with a flat-billed hat.  After all of us called him out for this apparent racism, he continued to say "there was nothing he could do."

Take your money elsewhere.  Don't support racist businesses.
Very interesting. Lots of artifacts. Believe it's a little high priced. Would recommend if you like Johnny Cash

My friends and I decided to stop in Whiskey Row for New Years Eve before we met up with the rest of our group downtown, and we had so much fun that we just made everyone come meet us there!!! The staff was so friendly and welcoming, and seemed to be having just as much fun as the people actually there to party! There were groups that rented out VIP booths and the girls taking care of those tables had light wands and kegs and bottles and were coming out on shoulders and dancing on tables.. I felt like I was in a Vegas club!!! But of course, with the perfect Nashville twist on it. I 10000% recommend Whiskey Row! We are already looking into booking a table for my birthday! Y'all check it out!

We did the Dinner Cruise last night.   The entertainment was great and the meal was good.   On the downside the waiter was rude.  He yelled in my ear several times when addressing the table, no one at the table could understand what he was staying because of his accent, he kept reaching across the table to refill water glasses, he never brought additional dinner rolls and he took forever to bring coffee for the other guest. We were seated at table 26
My wife and I enjoyed this place both for the music by John Riggins and company as well as the food.  Harold

I went to To Dierks Whiskey row Nashville, on New Years Eve, and I have to say, hands down, one of the best times I've had while visiting Nashville! There was no other place like this on broadway. Every floor had its own unique vibe. My Favorite floor was the second floor, where Whiskey row offered Flight service. The presentations of the flight service coming out to my table was unbelievable and the energy was outrageous. Everyone, from the staff, to the patrons, throughly was enjoying themselves. I was extremely impressed with everything this establishment had to offer. I can't wait to be back and I will be back !

We went here as a pit stop waiting for our airbnb to be cleaned. It wasn't on our to-do list, but we were confused as to why afterwards. This is really a great museum to kick start a trip to Nashville. 

It appears to be very small from the outside, but they have an amazing amount of stuff, it is laid out very well, and it really tells the story of his life. 

You'd be foolish to miss this spot if you are going to be in Nashville for anything other than a bachelorette party.

Great food good local beers (FAT BOTTOM BREWERY FTW!)
they need a better display of beer menu (FREE MARKETING TIP) 

sometimes the music is better than others but its always a pleasure to be there

Super friendly and quick service. Delicious, and fresh, oysters. Creative burger options which are also delicious, and yummy cocktails. I would like better happy hour specials, but still highly recommend.

My friend and I had a great time tonight at the New Year's Eve opening in Nashville. The staff was friendly and welcoming. The bartenders kept the drinks flowing, and the wait staff did a great job. We were especially impressed with Nicole. She was friendly, personable, and took a moment to pose for a picture with us. The security staff had their hands full with all of the "amateurs" out on New Year's Eve, but from what I saw, they handled each incident professionally. The band's sound on the first floor was well mixed and balanced throughout the space. With their prime corner location I'm sure that Whiskey Row will quickly become a popular choice among the many options on Lower Broadway.

Wow!  The pork steaks were off the charts.  Not going to find these anywhere in TN or any states around.  I was floored to find them as I grew up eating these in Illinois and have not seen them on a menu since moving to TN three years ago.

We have some friends in town and took them on "Broadway" last night.  They were disappointed that everything was covers and loud and packed.  We brought them to the "Room", and they are in love with Nashville!

a hidden gem in this town.  love the Bluebird but this is today's place to be.
This was a fun spot for soccer and live music. The service was five stars.  The drinks were excellent. My 3 stars is because the food wasn't super.  Drink and sing but eat elsewhere.

Super cool place - but definitely more of a destination for cocktails. The menu isn't too small but they were sold out of the first 2 things I wanted to order. We went to the 8:30 show and the artists were awesome and other patrons were lovely (the tables seat 4 so if you're a party of 2 you may be paired with new faces!). Check in was a bit disorganized and the valet line was super long, so get there early and Uber if you can! Definitely would return but would get dinner somewhere else before & just get drinks at the show
Really liked this place. Brought the in laws here when they came to visit.  There's a lot more to Johnny Cash than what I thought I knew.  Was pretty crowded, that's the only negative.

A must stop for anyone visiting Nashville.  The menu has something for everyone.  The Fried Green tomato sandwich  is excellent. The service is great super friendly.  If you want great food and great music check this place out.

If you can't afford to wait two hours for the bluebird cafe, or simply don't want to, this is the next best thing. Recommended to me by a local, this spot brings in talented upcoming singers an groups at 6 and 8:30 pm for a $7 stay-as-long-as-you-want cover. Also, like the bluebird, you're encouraged to be quiet to get the full listening experience. I was impressed by the female soloists and groups. 

The food was just okay and the fancy lemonade (spiked) was tasty and refreshing. I have and would recommend this because it was conveniently located downtown and brought young singer songwriter talent that inspired.

It is a small little back bar. But it is great place to hang out. We only stayed for a little bit but the bartender was very nice. I wouldn't have even knew if this was in the back if my friend didn't know. It is in the back of the bar by the bathrooms. Cheap fireball shots too!
Great burger!! Owner was extremely nice. Good music and a atmosphere that just yells family. We'll be back.

Stopped here after other bars closed for the night.  They had a pretty good band that was still playing.  Lot of floors to visiting, including a rooftop. Really big and we had a great time talking with people from around the U.S. and Canada!!

Male bartender from 11-2pm was amazing.  He served so many people without a hiccup.  Thank you for your attention to everyone's needs and your speed.  
Dierk's, he is definitely a keeper.

Went on Feb13, where Valentine's day special 3-course meal was the only option for dining.

Music and the ticket fee were fine - the atmosphere reminded me of the times in American college, but seriously the food was so bad that I wouldn't have come if it weren't for the lack of information.

For starter, figs were burnt. For the main, meat were burnt. For the dessert, they were out of sorbet making me doubt when they started this whole event - and then the 'flourless chocolate cake' turned out to be not flourless at all. Lastly - I don't know why - but the wine glasses smelled of some unpleasant odor that I thought of presenting deodorant. This was at 65 per each person.

I mean, it was for experience but not the best one. I wouldn't give a star to be fair. Needs imminent improvement.
I couldn't even walk in the music was soooo load not enjoyable...and I like my music turned up

Love Whiskey Row! Nashville needed something like this. Definitely the new hot spot. BILL BUTLER is the MVP. Fav bartender!! They play a variety of hits from every genre. Great energy and upbeat atmosphere. The staff is very professional and always accommodating. We don't usually have to wait long for drinks. Bartenders are on top of their game and make quality drinks. Check it out!

First, I want to commend Greg the chef for being so kind to his customers. I emailed Greg before coming here because I have a fish allergy. Greg not only assured me he would take care of me through email, but he also came out to our table to make me feel even more comfortable. The Mac and cheese was AMAZING, and my dad loved his smoked wings too. This place is SO awesome

I had such high expectations for this place. And it met every single one. The architecture of the building is amazing. The guitar chandelier, the lights, the space itself. The food is phenomenal. A wide variety of tastes and their brunch on the weekends is my FAVORITE. The bartenders are fast, friendly and aided to their customers needs. Live music is always very involved with the crowd and the DJ (night time) is probably one of the best I've ever heard. Overall, it's not like most bars on broadway. You can tell this place is constructed and run by a FAMILY, and everyone works together well to meet the needs of their customers. I highly recommend this to be a place to visit when coming to Nashville.

Every time I come here I have a GREAT time! The service is great and the drinks are always strong! It's upstairs above another bar so it's kind of hard to fine. Other than that it's a great place to relax, listen to some music, and have some good drinks!

I was in Nashville for work and caught a Titans game (SO fun). I followed the crowds over a bridge back to downtown Nashville on Broadway in search of dinner and drinks. I found no food, but I did find Dierks. Now I'm not a huge country fan, but I have a friend who loves Dierks Bentley so after a short wait in a line, I was in. The downstairs was crowded, but still managable to move. The bar was out of a lot of basic domestic beers so I settled for a Music City beer the waitress recommended. I stood nearby and listened to a great cover band, but found it really hard to meet or get to talk to anyone. I moved around, found a few different spots, but just couldn't blend in with the vibe. I went to the bar to get another drink and the bartenders were slammed. It just wasn't happening.

I'd give it another try on maybe a slower night, but all in all just not my favorite.
Came in for lunch on a Sunday and everything was great! Service and atmosphere were awesome. Also the Mac and cheese was fabulous!
Awesome place Pretty cool bar,  just opened and they are still working out on  things

We were hoping that this evening was going to be one of the highlights of our trip to Nashville but it really fell way short. It over promised and under delivered. The boat is real nice don't get me wrong but that is where the potential 5 star rating unravels. The drinks are very expensive, small, and served in tiny plastic dixie cups. You don't have much time to sit outside before they call you in for dinner so you hardly are enjoying the cruise part of the evening. The food was a 4 out of 10. I would compare it to the cheapest wedding food you have ever had. The show is hard to rate. I give the performers a lot of credit for trying. They really seemed to give it their all but the crowd was lame and hardly applauded after each number. I really felt bad for them. I kept looking around to see why people were sitting on their hands. Maybe because it was past the bed time for most of the seniors on board. Bottom line is, and I really hate to say it, don't waste your money. Book the Opry or a night at Bluebird where you can get your moneys worth. Sorry again, I really wanted to like this event.
We had so much fun here! The band was great! I'd give it five stars except that our waitress kept disappearing. We had the artichoke appetizer and drinks.

My daughter and I went to Nashville for the weekend and stayed in East Nashville. Looking for something to do after dinner, we walked up to The Basement East and wound up having an absolutely unbelievable time. Americanafest was happening so we enjoyed hours of a 1969 themed show. It seemed every performer was better than the last. The hosts were engaging and kept things moving through the four seasons as the emcee termed the show's parts. Norman Greenbaum performed Spirit in the Sky! On the drive back to Milwaukee we listened to music from as many of the performers as we could find. The Basement East was the perfect place to begin our country music weekend getaway. We had so much fun that the next morning I found my drink cup with the lime still in it . Just an amazing time.

This is a must see/do whilst in Nashville. There is nothing like this where I'm from and to my knowledge, anywhere else though I could be wrong.

Beers are cheap, they do food too. The vibe is very, very cool but not too cool for school. You can sit back, drink your Bud Lime and just chill into the atmosphere;

Two guys playing piano opposite each other, accompanied by a band. Are they any good? Does Dolly Parton have big boobs?! Yes, they're good. In fact, they're great. Talented and skilled musicians who've got their job down pat. You want live music in Nashville? You've got it. A mix of tunes from all genres, they'll give anything a go - if you request and tip them.

Remember, they're starving musicians and have seven kids to feed at home. If you're generous with them, they'll play anything... But seriously, this is their bread and butter and if you don't tip you're an ass. Don't be p*ssed if they don't know the whole song, it's impossible to know every song. They may know another song by that artist. Whichever the case, they'll make it fun and have a laugh about it. The higher the tip, the sooner your song gets played. $20 gets yours on next. I wish we'd been able to tip more. We couldn't be too frivolous with our cash unfortunately.

The banter between the band and sometimes bartender who gets up to sing a few is brilliant; funny, slick, cheeky. So you get a real mix of entertainment. 

As I said, drop by for a bottle of Bud or two and see for yourself. We spend about three hours there because we couldn't bring ourselves to leave wondering what they were going to play next. Awesome.
This place is great! I love watching games and playing some darts. The bartenders are so sweet and have great customer service. Highly recommend for some solid day drinking.

Not a bad place to have a drink and listen to music.  Their hand crafted signature drinks were very good. Pricey but typical pricing for the area. I just don't get why on the main floor do they only have one unisex bathroom. Bad planning.
Nice place. Food is good. Good bands. One on each floor. Prices are normal for area. Waitress Rhonda was extremely good and attentive!!
Nice place.  Pretty cool artifacts.  Truly enjoyed that he married his first wife in San Antonio TX.

Staff very friendly and the food was good at first. My medium burger was placed on my friends well done burger. Fries were not cooked fully. Food tasted amazing but you can't be a burger place and mix up burgers. The server when told got defensive and blamed the kitchen and nothing was done about the check. My entire order was wrong and I paid for everything fully. This place needs to get at least the service right. Customers should pay for a complete messed up order.

I thought I'd caught a show here before until I arrived the other night (turns out I was thinking of the East Room). 
So, I'd wondered how 5 full bands would pull off a set in a basement setting (which is what the above mentioned venue really is and that's not a knock either, seen some cool music there) only to realize this is a full size (for up to 400 anyway) modern music venue. Great affordable beers and shots, clean bathrooms, great sound system. Cool security (thanks for letting me put my merch in my car so I could thorougly enjoy the pit), good (and fast) bartenders. 
And...venue owners who know how you are supposed to behave at a metal show. Thanks for letting us rip the pit the way the show intends.

I love Johnny Cash and the museum
Is such a good tribute. We enjoyed the music, the music and the history.

This place is so much fun to go to! We went here for the first time and the food and music made me want to go back. Also we had the best waitress, Rachael, she literally made it the best time there. Go and have a blast

Food was a 3 star, drinks were good and weren't cheap. Servers were friendly and helpful. Entertainers are talented but I felt it was more like a Las Vegas type show rather then a Nashville show that I'd expect. If you want good music , then go down to Broadway in Nashville and save your money. It was a typical tourist trap type cruise that every city with a river has. You get to meet people on this boat from all over the country, which was pretty nice. some people might find sitting at a table with strangers awkward, but that didn't bother us. Overall, we had a good time we just wanted to be together and relax and have a good time.

Bartenders are rude and unfriendly... after our 1 round, we were  going to take the elevator downstairs and a male employee rushed over, Bc he's takes his elevator patrol more serious then the job assigned to him and just standing around,  "this is for employees only", first never inquired if we NEEDED this for a handicap guest?! Second he moved faster to reprimand us then he did the whole night no smiles from anyone the bartender was complaining about having to pick up a napkin off the floor .....pretty sure every establishment has if nothing else an ethical responsibility to not ostracize handicap individuals......... Who made the mistake of choosing DB stupid us

I came to Nashville for a conference and snuck away for a dinner one night. This was a great find. There was a cover charge but I thought the musical entertainment was worth it. I think the most memorable part of this restaurant is the exposed brick interior, live music, friendly staff, and the mac & cheese. I'd recommend others to go if they're in town.
Food was good. Staff was attentive. Music was great. We came on a Monday night and heard the song suffragettes. Awesome singer/songwriters. Loved it.

The performance was amazing!!! I'm not a country music person but these guys were so good I may even download a couple of their songs. 
The only reason 4 out of 5 stars was service. It was very slow. We waited over an hour for food and had empty drinks a majority of the evening. Our server was mia and would come back reeking of cigarette smoke. But I would still go back!

I've been here the last two visits to Nashville and it hasn't disappointed. Good times. Try and get your food and drink order in ASAP when seated and expect to wait if your are in a larger group. Pricilla was our waitress last time and she was great. Friendly and attentive. We will definitely be back the next time we are in town.

They don't validate parking so you have to pay separately for that. Theres a lot in the back of the building with meter parking. Its a cool little trip down history and memory lane. A must do if youre a Cash fan

Unfortunately, I have to write a negative review on Yelp for the first time, but this review is warranted. I would first like to respond to John's review below from 9 days ago, and mention that this security worker is still employed at this establishment as of 2 days ago, and he was absolutely rude and unprofessional. 

However, as it was impossible to make it upstairs on a Saturday night during the summer in Nashville, my friend and I decided to give Dierks another try yesterday 7/14. We met up with a large group of girls we know from school and were having a grand time on the dance floor. About 30 minutes into our groove, a female approached my friend and told her that an "executive" of the bar wanted us to come join them and dance on the bar at their VIP booth because he thought we were "attractive." Thus, we joined them at the booth, and began dancing along the top of the booth, as is customary, or so it seemed. 

Unfortunately, about an hour and a half in, our experience took a turn. Now, I will fully admit that I am responsible for my actions, however I do not feel what ensued was warranted. I had stepped off of the bar/booth for a bit to use the restroom, meander, etc. During this time, my friend and I got separated. I was standing near the outside of the booth, and made the poor choice of standing on top of the outside of the same booth/rail we were invited to, in order to get a better view of the dance floor to try to find my friend. A security gentleman, repeatedly tapping my waist, not only told me to get down, but then abruptly and rudely said to me "Get out. I can either ask you to leave nicely or I can throw you out" when all the while I was completely cooperative, most likely due to the shock of not even receiving a warning, but immediately being kicked out. All I was saying to him was I am waiting for my friend, who was right behind him. 

Now, again, I was completely at fault for standing on the outside of the booth, however, it was the same booth that we had been invited over to by an "executive" to dance. In addition, earlier in the night, a different security personnel had nicely told me that I cannot request a song from the DJ, and that was that; I did not try to approach the DJ again. I have been to many other establishments in Nashville and throughout the world, and never have I ever been so disrespected and made out to seem like a degenerate. I was at a bar in Nashville, so naturally I was drunk, however, I was by no means trashed or "sloppy" or unruly. 

In addition, our friend from school, whom we met up with there, had a similar security horror story the night prior. She had tried to get into Dierks with 13 other girls she traveled to Nashville with, and for whatever reason, a security guy refused to let her in. Only her. Leaving her alone on the street. Fortunately, we were on broadway so she didn't have to be alone. And again, she was drunk, but fully composed. No stumbling, vomiting or anything else to that effect. 

When the previous reviews stated that this bar is sexist, I actually agree. Very rarely do I ever call a person or establishment sexist. If an owner or manager does not reach out to me via Yelp, I will be contacting someone via phone or email on the website. Moreover, I am curious to find out what the Better Business Bureau will think of this repeated behavior in your establishment, based on my multiple first-hand experiences, and SEVERAL of these reviews. Fellow Yelpers, take your business and time to Luke's instead, you will be treated humanely and have a better time, anyway.

I loved going on the General Jackson Showboat. We had a great time. The show was only 45 minutes, but it felt much longer.  They must have had a dozen costume changes.  The music was just top notch. My tickets had us eat and go to the show during the first seating.  Then afterwards you get to walk around on the decks or sit in the bar/lounge while the other half eats. My show was all country music and fiddling.  I loved every minute of it.  As I sat outside on the deck I could hear the second show start.  It was all 80's music with lots of sing along.  I didn't like that near as much.  The buffet was really good food. The BBQ was especially good.  I'd go again!  The show was that good.
Great time!!! Friendly staff and great music.   Well decorated!   Loved hanging out here.

Wow what a fitting tribute to one of the best in the business.

This museum is jam packed with so much stuff from the life and career of Johnny Cash. But not so much that it's too much.

A very well organized museum with displays from his earliest years until his death.

Personal belongings, photos, letters, records and so much more to see and explore.
That sushi appetizer... What great dreams are made of... Like nothing I've ever had.  They have Deep Eddy Grapefuit vodka too!  (Nachos are mediocre, sadly.)

My husband loves him, but I've never been the hugest Johnny Cash fan.  However I do enjoy seeing memorabilia and this museum has it in spades!!  Handwritten notes by JC, describing things on display, were my favorite.  Just on a scrap piece of paper it looked like. Very sweet.  There were so many treasures from his life.  Love letters.  Great photos of him as a younger man, before becoming famous, and boy, he sure had that "it" quality - he just looked like he was destined for greatness.  Quite a lovely man.  I'm a bigger fan now. 

Verrrrry crowded! We went around 2?  Might want to research when best time is. Made it difficult to linger on a display.  Loved the video rooms.
This was my dream! This place is awesome they have clothes, furniture, records, hand written notes!! They have a picture guy you can get your photo with Johnny next to you. It was great!
We had lunch here today. Great food, friendly staff and amazing music. A must see if you're visiting Nashville

This is my favorite night life spot in Nashville! The talent these guys have is unbelievable; I don't know how they do it! It's a spot where you can (usually) sit down, have some great drinks, and be thoroughly entertained all night. The bar staff is great and the entertainers are top notch. I read a few reviews that lowered their rating because there's a cover...it's $6.00, and it's 100% worth it in my opinion! Plus, I just saw that if you check in on Yelp you get a $2.00 discount! I wish I'd known that before this weekend; we went both Friday and Saturday. We couldn't get enough!
Johns the man behind the bar! Good food and great drinks at reasonable prices! Worth the stop for great live music and open late with a late kitchen. 10/10 recommend.

Well, I'll start by saying I loath leaving bad reviews. But this is a case that it is called for. 

First off, they charge cover - which is fine ($6 on a Saturday night) but they obviously pick and choose who they charge. My friends were split up upon entrance. Half charged, half were not. Just seems a bit shady. 

Second, the drinks were fine. We had a lovely bartender who promptly served us and was super friendly. I wish I remembered her name because she deserves 5 stars. 

However, one of the guys on the piano was so utterly rude to a member of my party. I was honestly appalled. 

They take requests, so we wrote our song request and put a tip on stage. At one point there was a lull in music and my friend shouted out to the guy "play back that a** up! (Our song choice) in a friendly manner. They had just been playing mania rap songs. And then all of a sudden the piano man decided to snap. He shouted "listen drunk girl I'm not playing that song I have a bachelors degree in music I'm not playing that sh!t" while he obviously played the piano and sang the song afterward in an aggressive and angry way.
