Even the security guard standing near him seemed offended for us. The crowd got a bit silent and everyone looked around at each other in a "what the heck just happened manner". We got our tip back and left soon after. 

Needless to say I will never return to this establishment and I hope their "artists" who are so proud of their collegiate achievements find a better job than performing for a plethora of bachelorette party's and drunk co-eds. He may have a bachelors degree but Juvenile had a chart-topping single so, I would say one is doing better than the other.

Great drink prices. Music was awesome. We didn't eat but didn't come to eat. Great place to unwind. Highly recommend if you're looking for laid back place to have a good time and listen to good ol' country music.

The most incredible music venue I've been too! The musicians were super entertaining and very talented. Only bad review was that the server waited to check on us for long periods at a time, so we would need something or run out of water and then have to wait till he was out again. Then the food itself wasn't horrible, but wasn't great either.. I got the Cranberry walnut salad and it was pretty good but the chicken tenders my friend got not-so-good. Other than that, there was free valet parking, the venue was clean, and the music was INCREDIBLE!

Worst experience , great music.  My wife and I are here for a convention and had an hour in a half to go find lunch.  My wife ordered a Kale and Quinoa salad and I a Burger with no bun on top of lettuce.  We waited about 35-40 minutes for our food and when it arrived the salad had no Kale, very little ingredients and the burger was one of those frozen looking Costco patties and it was ice cold.  The waitress brought the manager over and he assured they'd remake them etc.  My wife's salad came out almost immediately but still not what she remembered since she had ordered the same thing last year.  I however waited and waited and even 20 minutes after my wife had finished.  Almost 40 minutes after receiving our bad food, I still had no burger.  By this time we were already late for our convention and we had to leave and I ended up with no meal.  Incredible how poor the service and quality of food are.  Save your money and go somewhere else.  The music however was great.

All the way out here from California and we love this place. The band was amazing, drinks great and service was excellent. We have been here in Nashville 2 days and have visited this bar more than 5 times! Great experience and will always come back!! If you are looking to experience Nashville this place is a must visit!!

Stopped in while friends we in town. We really enjoyed the plane and the bands rocked. We didn't try any food but we will definitely come back to try it out. 
 The staff was super nice and fun as well.
Had so much fun here!   Hollee is amazing.  Made us feel more welcome than anywhere on Broadway.  Service second to none on the rooftop!

Great Atmosphere!! Good food!  We stopped in to checkout Nashville we on our way across the country of watching Angela Marie & Donny Lee!! 
Could not have asked for a better experience!! Kid Rock's Honky Tonk Kicks Ass!!

This is a great place when you want to get off of busy Broadway. The beer was cold and the selection was great. Service was good at the bar, spotty from the waitress. Food also good, we split several apps, which were all to our liking. The entertainment was also good. A very homy, neighborhood bar kind of place.

This was by far the most fun and interactive thing we did while in Nashville.  The musicians were absolutely amazing.  They were very talented and we were amazed by the huge variety of songs they knew.  I would recommend this bar to absolutely anyone visiting Nashville.

Unfortunately, this place missed the mark.  The talent of the singers/songwriters was probably great, however when in the private area you are not provided access to enjoy them.   You are provided with a nice credit card fee for choosing the establishment for your group.  We had to meet a minimum, which would be understandable- other than the fact the food quality does not come anywhere close to the tab that needed to be achieved.    Nashville has so much to offer, I definitely won't add this to my list on future visits.
Great music. Service is slow- but so is all the other restaurants on the row. We did not eat here- but had a few beers.

Fantastic idea, poorly executed.
Hot beer, cold food. They have a disclaimer about running out of food but they ran out of fries, chili, sent us a brisket end sandwich that was hard as a rock, then greasy ends of the brisket as "replacement". 
We were the last table - a curtain between us and where they throw dirty dishes so we not only listened to music, but also the sound of silverware dropping and plates stacking and a dropped glass on the floor. 
We were told by the manger we were comped for dinner since we were from out of town (in lieu of a rain check for the next time) but were still asked to pay a full bill from the server. 
Even if everything had gone smoothly,  forget enjoying the last set. The wait staff is everywhere in the way with their little computers to make sure you pay bc that was "the best and only time to do it".  
This place is a great idea... in theory. We won't be back and I suggest you don't waste your money.

Basement East did us dirty. I know Tennessee is strict on IDs but seriously... a passport and social security card? They kicked my fiancé out who is 28 because I bought him a beer... he had his ID stolen last week. Tough break. Missed a great band which we already bought tickets for. Wouldn't of been so bad if we were treated kindly.

If you want good service and good food, this is not the place to go.  Burnt food and poor customer service. Manager tried to fix it and was professional but wait staff rude. Manager offered to get us a round of drinks but we simply wanted to leave at the point. Everyone left hungry and will not go back.

The sound system in the place is amazing!  Big beautiful place with a great view of the strip.  Good to make a home base for meeting people.  I went here a few times while visiting the strip.  Drink prices were average for the area.  Good place to watch bands play, on any floor.  I recommend to at least stop by if your in the area.
I come to Nashville often and after spending NYE here (and lunch the next day) I can say that I will DEFINTELY be back each trip! Best spot on broadway with the highest rooftop!

Visited the listening room as second choice for inability to get to BlueBird. We saw Brice Long and friends. My rating is great for service, drinks, food and entertainment. I was apprehensive going to Listening Room based on ratings of poor service and food. Our service could not have been better for food service. The drinks took longer than the food. The server was very attentive to us. We got the cheese platter which was good but could use more crackers. I took off stars for atmosphere and uncomfortable chairs. The room lacked any decor.

Go for the music, not necessarily for the food. Read the reviews and was equally surprised as the others (although I guess I shouldn't have been) that they were out of so many menu choices for Saturday brunch - like "sorry, we're out of ham" or the real kicker "we're out of our signature jam (for the biscuits)". At least the performers showed up. . .

Tip: There is nowhere to store luggage, but you are allowed to carry your suitcase around the museum. 

A small museum dedicated to Johnny Cash, with some mentioning of other country music artists. Walking through the museum, you will learn about Johnny Cash's life, listen to his music, and even watch a clip of his movie. We spent about 1.5 hours, enjoying the air-conditioning inside.

HOPE THIS REVIEW GETS TO MANAGEMENT AND THEY CHANGE THEIR POLICY BEFORE A LAW SUIT SHUTS THEM DOWN!!! 
Wednesday approximately 12:00am 

My first time in this bar and wasn't impressed with security. As a former bar security I have respect for them & understand their job is hard when dealing with over served patrons but they have guidelines and more responsibilities than most people working in the bar. 
     I observed a patron sleeping (passed out) at the table I was standing at for about 20 minutes. He was next to a guy and thought they were together, after the other patron got up and left I approached the security officer (in the corner texting on his phone, he was approximately 5'6" with black hair and black beard) and asked him how they dealt with patrons passed out in the bar.  
     I told him where he was and he went up to him and tried to wake him up, he then took his flash light to get the attention of the security agent at the door. They woke the patron up and escorted him out the door. The security agent walked back over to take the patrons beer off the table. The guest sitting behind me asked him what they did with the patron. His comment back to the guest was "I don't know, we kicked him out". 


Unprofessional in every way. They should have got management involved to get him in a cab and safely home or to hotel.
Absolutely the worst service and food, and even worse management staff.  Water seemed to be rationed as well...

This 3 star review is only because of how nice the place was designed and the fact that our waitress frequently checked on us. Our food came out  way after we ordered all I got was some fries and they didn't taste good. A few people next to us stood at a table waiting for it to be cleaned for at least 15 minutes and ended up doing it on their own. It's pretty disappointing for a music row bar owned by such a huge star.

This is definitely more dive bar type of bar, but I liked it. The people were friendly and the band was great! 

There's plenty of security and the ones we talked to were nice. 

There is an entrance and an exit so that not everyone is trying to go out the same door. 

There is a line for the bathroom so be prepared to wait. 

There can also be a line to get a drink so be patient. 

We didn't stay for too long because we were doing a bit of bar hopping, but if you're on Broadway in Nashville then stop at this bar.
Way better than we expected. And waaay creepier but in a great way. The realism is off the charts. Amazing. Very worth a visit!

The museum was fine, lots of interesting things to see, just kind of small for the entrance price. It also didn't help that an elderly tour group was giving me evil looks because my 15m old daughter was making noise *gasp*
Not too bad. Good music and good food but service is a little slow. I'd still come back!!!

Great time!  The place was packed but we were lucky & got a table in the back.  We were still able to watch the entertainment on the stage because the were on a high stage.  The energy in this place was magical!  The band & singers were excellent.  Our food was very good & the waitresses did an outstanding job!
Never disappoints! I always take friends and family to The Listening Room when they visit Nashville. They consistently have awesome music, drinks and food!

Well our experience began on a Wednesday morning. We sat down at the bar with plenty of room still available at the bar and at tables. My husband and I ordered a drink then the bartender asked our 17 year old daughter what she wanted. She ordered a water. She was then asked for her id. We were told we needed to leave the bar because only 21 year olds can sit at the bar. So we grab our drinks and move to a table in the back. Again there, we were told we couldn't sit at the table if we weren't going to order food. The place was empty. We were spending money but the rudeness of the staff was not needed.  If you have an under age child in your party, beware!

We came on a Saturday afternoon and had a great time. It didn't take long for a table to clear up to get seated. There was live music on both floors but we listening to 4 great female singers who did a lot of 90s music on the 1st floor. Heather was a very attentive server despite it being pretty busy. The artichoke dip was excellent! I definitely recommend it! 

The one thing that is obviously completely out of the control of the management and servers is the lines for the bathroom(s) both had about a 4 person wait but I think that can be expected in a busy establishment.

In short, come enjoy a good time, good food and good service! Don't come for the bathrooms

I love venturing out to the Beast! I haven't been in Nashville long but love finding venues like this one.  I've seen some local bands and also a couple favorites from New Orleans! I can say from each time the crowd was a comfortable size and you can't beat the drink prices. Shot and a beer specials are allllways welcomed and for the price I always seem to get a good pour. Drinks and sound are the only things that matter to me in places like this so I'll be there first to complain at a venue where speakers are blown and / or the drinks are pricey and weak. Sound seemed to be pretty good quality and there was a good mix of different ages in the crowd which I always think is awesome. I haven't tried any food yet but from other reviews I definitely will! I've yet to spend any time there when it was completely open with the patio but overall I really dig the space. Will definitely be back!

We did not eat here. We did visit this place 4 times while we were in Nashville.  The party vibe in here is amazing.  We had so much fun at this bar. The band's here were the best that we experienced in downtown.  Very energetic and really good. All the staff here were very friendly. Probably the sexiest bartenders I have ever seen.. tight pants, tight shirts and very tan. We visited all the floors. The roof top bar was very nice. Next time we may try the food here. It was an amazing time.  Make sure you check this place out while your in this town.  You will have a blast.

I collapsed from heat stroke due to no air conditioning during Billy Sheehan's bass solo. I drove 600 miles to see that solo. I had to go lay down for the remainder of the bass solo (and an additional song, "Ghost Town") on one of the dinette booths until I gained consciousness.  It was THAT hot.  To add insult to injury, the paid parking next door ended literally 4 minutes early and they promptly gave me a $60 parking ticket...on top of the $10 I already paid for 4 hour parking.  F this place.  F it hard, F it long.

I'm a vegetarian and loved their veggie burger last time I stopped in but came in today and they didn't have any milkshakes or veggie burgers and don't have anything else besides overpriced salads that are vegetarian friendly. However it was redeemed by the fact that I learned they make all their veggie patties in house every day from organic local farmers produce.
I always have the best time here. Security is so great. Go here for a damn good time!!!

Great bar to checkout along the Broadway strip. Stopped in here for a few drinks and to listen to one of the bands playing. 
The bar is a multi story building with a bar on each floor. There is also a cool rooftop bar which offers a nice view of Broadway.
Bartenders and staff were nice and helpful. Didnt get any food but it looked decent.

As a Nashville local, I generally don't tend to spend my nights out on Broadway. However, my friends and I make an exception for Whiskey Row. This place is always the go to spot in Nashville on any given night. Each floor accommodates a different vibe, which can be fitting for each individual and their desired type of night. On top of that, the staff is top notch and always willing to help. If you find yourself at Whiskey Row for lunch or dinner, their burger is the best! I was thoroughly impressed with their food and drink selection all in all. I highly recommend making Whiskey Row a stop on your list!

I come here any chance I get! They always have a panel of four musicians that take turns playing their original songs and give some background to what inspired the piece. The tickets are super affordable ($5 - $12), and the $15 per person minimum food/beverage fee is easily covered by a bottle of wine or a few beers. I don't personally care for their food. I come here to listen to great music and to split a bottle of red wine with a gal pal.

Pretty Cool place. There are a lot of places inside to listen to a blurb from a show or song.. I was a little weirded out by using "community" headphones. Lots of interesting stuff... including a video of Johnny Cash clips from various movies and tv shows. $14 to get in isnt bad either.

This review is strictly about service. The content of the museum was awesome.

Make sure you ASK for your AAA DISCOUNT or any other discount. 

I found out after purchasing multiple tickets (from my Mom who purchased tickets after me at the counter) that they offer a AAA discount. I went back up and asked if they would honor it as I had literally just finished paying and the supervisor/manager refused and was pretty nasty about the whole thing. Shame.

I don't like country music so much, but have to say, this was so fun, and so low-key. We went to the 6 p.m. show, heard some great music, and honestly, the food wasn't horrible. We had the hummus, fries, and fried pickles, and my sisters ordered some sort of chicken puff pastry things. As a pregnant person, I have to say that the fries and the fried pickles were exactly what I would want for a visit in Nashville, haha. The waiter was great, the music was outstanding, and I'd definitely come back.

I have mixed feelings about this place. It is a rather large place with tall ceilings so the sounds are not as good as they may be in a smaller place. We enjoyed the music, but the rest was so-so. They had $7 cover and $15 spend minimum per person. We only ordered drinks, which were okay. The biggest disappointment was with the service. They are poorly trained. The servants check in with you every 5 minutes even though you still have a drink that you are drinking. They interrupt people with these check-ins and picking up glasses/dishes in the middle of song performances, making distracting sounds, etc. This place should definitely try to work on how they approach service otherwise I can see them going downhill despite good talent on stage.

Absolutely ridiculous evening. The piano bar was my only request for my bachelorette party and what a disappointment! The pianist were very talented and a great time and even our server was awesome! HOWEVER; the other server Amanda needs to go; she threw a drink in one of our parties face on the dance floor. No need to say anything more
Add this to your bucket list! A Nashville must see!!! You will love the Man in Black even more after this tour. So much fun!!

I went to 360 Burger and I was more than pleased. Let me 1st say the menu has a number of food options, that doesn't just consist of burgers. The food here was absolutely delicious, everyone was extremely friendly/helpful, and the atmosphere was great. While dining in I ate a dozen of the chargrilled oysters and they were absolutely fantastic. The combination of the parmesan, garlic, and lemon butter was prepared very nicely. I also had a side salad that was delicious as well. It was very fresh and tasty. I also ordered a meal to take home as well. I ordered a 1/4 of the hot chicken (white meat) , asparagus, and a bread pudding. Abosolutely fantastic!!! Not only did the chicken look like perfection, but it also taste as such. My hat definitely goes off to the chef.

It's not only nice to have a restaurant in the Antioch, TN area that offers a variety of menu items, but also one where the food makes you want to go back for more. Trust me, going back for more is exactly what I'll be doing. Give them a try...you definitely won't be disappointed!!!

Kid Rock's is the place to go because there is plenty of room (no wait), great service (I am going to marry Austin), yummy local beer selection.

Not sure what was better the music (on the second floor) or Austin (our server). I thought Austin posed for this beer but he said NO!

Museum part is great - had lots of items on display. Unfortunately they let so many people in at once that you can barely move and have to wait a long time to read/see each display. It was so crowded that it felt like this was a fire hazard.

We visited the Johnny Cash museum because he is a country music legend and we were in Music City so...why not?!? I didn't know much about him other than a few of his big hits so this was interesting to me. After leaving the museum, I had truly gained some admiration for Johnny Cash. Price of admission is decent for what you get - roughly $18 per adult. ***DISCLAIMER: Purchase a TOTAL ACCESS PASS - this gives you free access to about two dozen attractions across Nashville and it only costs $75/person.*** This museum is not too large so you can see everything in less than 2 hours (it most likely won't take this long unless you literally read EVERYTHING). The museum features photographs and stories from all parts of Cash's life - young and old, military and civilian, the good and bad. You can listen to some of his songs and even watch clips from his acting career. You can see the accolades that he earned throughout his lifelong career, which ended only when he passed away - he was truly in it for the love of music, not for the money or fame. This museum should be on your itinerary when you visit Nashville!

This is absolutely my favorite venue in town...especially for songwriter rounds!!! The sound is excellent and there's not a bad seat in the house! It helps that the food is excellent and the (free_ valet parking is definitely a plus in downtown Nashville!!!

This is the best place in Nashville. Briana the young lady that works there is superb. Her hospitality was above and beyond. She made sure my wife was pleased to the max  for the Bryan White show. Everyone there was exceptional, I cannot write enough of a great review for this place. I love it, and I will  make  the 3 hour drive to go back anytime. Felt like I was with great friends for an awesome night.

I went to Whiskey Row last night, but was not allowed in because my boyfriend had on Timberland boots. He was told it was no longer allowed by corporate and not part of the dress code because "too many blacks and minorities are wearing them". I asked them if my boobs were hanging out, if that would be apart of "dress code" and could go in, and I was told yes. So it's acceptable to not have a shirt on, but not acceptable to wear shoes? This is one of his favorite places to go, however, we will not be back due to "corporate's" discrimination.
Food was awful if you are hungry get something to eat elsewhere and catch the later show.  Wine is marginal and expensive.  Music is ok.  Mostly new singer/songwriters.

Went on the dinner and show cruise.  Ship was packed.  Nice ride down river. Nashville skyline at night.  Buffet was standard fare not bad not great. Stage show was impressive. Great singers and musicians. Solid 60 minutes of many types of music.  Cruise lasts 3 hours which went by quickly

While the food is pretty good, the service is terrible. I've been there numerous times and the service just seems to get worse everytime I've gone. The last time I was there, I actually ended up walking out since a server never came to our table after sitting there for 10 minutes watching them talk behind the bar. There are better burger options around.

I'm giving this restaurant a 2 because the food was delicious (I had the mushroom Swiss burger with sweet potato fries), but the service was a big negative. The man who served us didn't write any of our orders down and messed up 4 out of 5 of them in their own special ways: burger cooked wrong, wrong fries, wrong toppings, you name it. (Not writing down orders and getting them correct is very impressive. This was not.)

He had to come back to have us repeat our orders 3 times, and still got things wrong. When he brought us missing things we requested, he brought them out one at a time, and made up excuses why he brought the mustard but not the refill. 

We really thought there just had to be hidden cameras somewhere by the end of the meal.

You can probably imagine that he got the checks wrong, too. All in all, it took us an hour and a half to order, eat and pay for 5 burgers. There were only a few other tables there.

IF I ever go back, I will write my order down for this particular server: no exceptions. I probably won't go back, though. It's unfortunate, because I had high hopes for this establishment when I heard about their local beef and produce.

The service was awful. When you have a table of 13, and sitting there waiting for the waiter/waitress to come get your order after 20 minutes of sitting there... That in itself is a reason to walk out the door. Then when we finally order it took another 45 minutes to get the food, then a couple people had to wait even longer for their food while everyone else was halfway through their meals. The burgers could have been a little better too. All I can say is that I don't plan on going back to this place unless the wait staff improves, and they take a little more care in how the food is prepared. I like the idea of healthy burgers, but the staff needs to act a little more professional.

Definitely our favorite bar in Nashville! We went on Super Bowl night and both bands we saw were awesome! It was very lively and the bartenders got our drinks quick. Kinda expensive but I figure that's all of Nashville. We loved the music and would definitely come back!

Don't recommend coming here for the food. Absolutely horrible hamburgers and fries.  The hamburger didn't even taste like beef. Super loud. Couldn't even hear what our server was saying let alone carry on a conversation at the table.

We absolutely loved our time at the listening room. The time flew by as we listened to the  songwriters of Nashville! We ate dinner before attending the show, so we ordered a few cocktails and the homemade donuts. The donuts were hot and delicious!! Would highly recommend the vanilla cinnamon ones. The harvester rose cocktail was also a personal favorite! It is a drink that would suit all tastebuds. We will certainly be back!

Best bar in downtown! Bartenders are always smiling and having fun, the music is steps above that on the main strip, and the food is incredible! ( they have a daily meat n' two that will make you feel like you're at grandma's Sunday dinner).  We have gotten to be out of town regulars and tell all of our friends to come here!
Jake was great! Great atmosphere and band was really good. Definitely recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville.
This was the worst dining experience I've ever had in Nashville and I live here.... Service was non-existent and manager was a no show.

Terrible establishment. Worst service experience ever. They clearly dont do the research when it comes to hiring their servers, extremely rude! If you get unlucky enough to be sat at one of Amanda's tables, just go ahead and get up and walk out. She is guaranteed to ruin your night with her piss poor mood and incompetence.
This is the Best bar in nashville. The food is amazing. We can not wait to go back. Next time you are in Nashville visit this place.

You can identify this establishment by the volume coming out of it as they have to have the best sound system on the strip. I love the stage setup in this place as it provides a great vantage of the band. Plenty of bar and table space on the first floor and as I had read on another review I also suggest staying on this floor as it features the best band and service is far better. Some drinks can get a bit pricey but your local IPA is running around $7.

Cocktails are ok. However the rudest staff I have ever encountered. Basically if u want your drinks and food thrown at u with attitude you come here. So many other places that are worth the Nashville experience.

Great place to hear up-and-comers in the country music business.  I had the pleasure of hearing Bobby Pinson and Friends on a Saturday night.  Great time, even when the band blew a fuse and the lights went out. The food is average, but the music acts are great.

I wasn't sure whether I was going to give a 1 star or 4 star review so it got the middle of 2 stars. 
The 1 star review comes from the restaurant owners for screwing their customers at the check out. Apparently the servers have no clue and management will make no concessions for an added charge to every bill. The first line of the bill lists a "tech fee of 3%" not a surcharge for patrons using a credit card! WTF is the fee for. Nowhere else on Broadway did we ever incur this bogus fee. They should notify the customer upon entering the restaurant.  
Now for the review of food and atmosphere. Everything was very good in that area. We heard some good music from the sidewalk and that brought us in. Got some drinks and they were good too. Our server was nice and around when we needed her. We then ordered some food and that was quite good for a Broadway bar/restaurant. I had the  half yardbird and although it was a small chicken, it was a perfectly juicy single portion. The other foods ordered was a hamburger that was really good and a chicken ceasar   wrap that was better than average. All the food came out fresh and hot though the kitchen was pretty slow. 
That music was fantastic and probably one of the best bands we had seen the whole visit.  
My opinion to give the owners a taste of their own filthy medicine would be to come in for 2 hours, don't order anything but TIP THE BAND $20 AND TIP THE SERVER $20 and see how long  this stupid Tech Fee lasts!

I cannot believe that when you drop $200 at an establishment they don't clear your table and leave you to sit with it for an hour! So disappointed! I'll give that the music artists were good so this is no reflection on them. Went as a family, five of us, adults, and at first thought "this is great." Food was delivered quickly and the show was underway. It ends there. After that we sat with our dirty plates filling our table for an hour after we finished eating. Maris, our server, (table 54) walked by us over a dozen times without ever acknowledging our plates or servicing to remove them. She did stop by two more times and asked if we needed anything and was happy to bring us more drinks but never removed a dirty dish in the process. Yes, we left with our table filled with dirty dishes. (See photo) Paid $60 for five tickets and dropped another $125 in food and drinks (not including tip that was excepted). We will definitely think twice before going again. Sadly! There are plenty of great options in beautiful Nashville to drop $200 and get a great experience!! (11/23/18 6:00pm show)

I thought this place was great. Now I only went for drinks (8pm to 11 on a Thursday night) with my bestie, but we had a great time. The live band played an assortment of county, 90's throwback, and a lot of requests. We came early enough where we got a seat at the bar and we never had to wait long to order a drink all night and our tab wasn't crazy expensive at the end of the night. Packed house, could move, all in all good spot on broadway!

Enjoyable, and I'm glad we stopped. The information about the span of Cash's life and career was good. The place was very crowded (went on a Sunday), making it difficult to really enjoy the exhibits. Price was high, $16, for a relatively small exhibit. 

Coffee shop up front (Bongo) was great!

Fun place to hang with friends!  Their food isn't bad either.  It's off the Broadway strip and less crowded.  The live music is incredible, especially Les on Saturday night up on the rooftop.  He accepts requests and he'll play most anything you want to hear.

We went here on a girls weekend from St. Louis, MO and had a wonderful time!  The atmosphere was fantastic, loved the valet parking!  The singers/songwriters were very entertaining and hung around after their show.  The service and food was amazing!  I have had fried/breaded pickles before, but these were so different and delicious!  It was a great night out with at an amazing venue!  I would recommend reservations as it gets crowded.

Very nice.  Big time tourist magnet.  the food was very good . Its a buffet so keep your expectations in line.   The Music City Nights show was very good, talented performers.  I am sure this cruise is not their ticket to stardom, but they did a nice job.  Would definitely go on again

We tried brunch here today and we were less than impressed with the food (music was fabulous though). We had checked the menu online and it showed numerous brunch ( rather than lunch) items but when we arrived the menu had far fewer options. The waitress pushed the $18 buffet but a quick look at it was enough to not be interested. It looked like it had been out for hours and defiantly not impressive enough to warrant the price tag. I ordered the CB slinger $16 and my husband ordered a pulled pork Benedict $18. Both came with soggy flavorless hash browns, mine were even partially frozen. If you can't make a decent hash brown, you have no business serving brunch. My husband's meal also came with undercooked bacon that tasted like someone poured a bottle of liquid smoke on it. Overall they have a great atmosphere, but the food bordered on inedible which is unacceptable especially at that price point. If you just want a drink stop in for some great music but I would avoid the food.

Great place. Was here for the opening last night and came back today. Awesome live country music. Food was great. Our sever, Nicole, was the BEST EVER!!!  Very personable and knowledgeable of the place. Suggested many items on the menu but was complimentary of all their items. She has a bright future ahead of her. Hang on to your dreams always Nicole. They will never come true if you don't. If and when I come back to. Nashville I will definitely come back.

Really enjoyed spending about 90 minutes here.  They have an extensive collection of memorabilia, and I learned a lot about Johnny Cash.  If it had been less crowded, I would have given it 5 stars, but we went on a Saturday morning when it was very crowded on Broadway, so I would suggest finding a time to go when it might be a little less busy.
Entertainers was good. Had great costumes!!! Sexy ladies and flat bellied Cowboys.  Pulled pork brisket with BBQ sauce, real mashed potatoes, and pecan pie all were good.

Cool museum esp. if you are a fan. They have a green screen area where you can take a photo "with Johnny." Super nice staff. Wasn't particularly impressed with the gift shop - nothing too unique. 

Admission is $18 which is a bit pricy considering it's a small museum. Use your AAA card and get $1 off!
Amazing show great performers, good food. Drinks were pricy but hey you get to keep the glass lol! Beautiful Nashville skyline at night
A great museum! Lost of information, pictures, outfits, and records. We spent an 1 hour here, and learned a lot. The staff were friendly and has lost of souvenirs.

The session had already started, they charged full price and a $15 purchase minimum. It was very distracting to have the wait staff taking orders at the beginning  and collecting tabs at the end of the show. Since there is a lobby bar tabs could be paid out there. A person could also meet there minimum in the lobby bar. I think a different business model would be advantageous.

Drinks were good and service was as well.  It's was early so it was kind of slow but nice to listen to the music.  The entertainers were good but I couldn't help get this commercialized feel about everything.  They are in a partnership with Dicks and the feel was different from their other location they used to be at.  We could have just been too early or there on a bad night.  The waitress was very nice and never kept us waiting.

We watched the midday performance of "Taste of Tennessee." The staff was excellent and very friendly. This is a great way to kill some time and get to explore Tennessee at the same time. The food was tasty and they had cake set out and ready. 

The show was fun to watch with very talented singers performing. The scenery was probably my favorite part. It was nice to go outside on the boat and get to see parts of Tennessee. 

If you're not a local, I would recommend trying this. For me, it's a one time thing. It was enjoyable but at the end I was ready to get off the boat and get into some cool AC.

Obsessed with maintaining a high female to male ratio of guests.  If you're a group of guys trying to enter, do not attempt to go in together- stagger yourselves going in.

Chuck "the owner" is an egotistical idiot in a Ed Hardy shirt - you can't miss him.  He'll have his doorman bounce you once you've racked up a nice tab, for just about anything.  

The DJ's are subpar.  

There are many other places in the Gulch that you'll have more fun spending your time in.  Nothing to see here - keep moving.

LOVE LOVE LOVED IT!!  I am a musician (piano, trumpet, alto sax, and drums). This place was located in the Dicks last resort restaurant, next to Coyote Ugly. These two pianists were great, they had mad skills!!

Incredible experience.  Highlight of our  Nashville trip. Maybe the best fried chicken and southern home cooked food I have had in my life.The entertainment was lively and cutting-edge. Appropriate for a variety of ages. The crowd the showboat attracts were so much fun. We just could not get enough and were so sad when it all ended. We made friends on this short voyage that will be long lasting and can not wait to head down the Cumberland again in the future for an awesome steamboat adventure aboard General Jackson

2.5 Stars. 
I came here inadvertently after failing to find cheap parking for Bakersfield. Why are the public parking lots $30??!?!?! Luckily, Listening Room Cafe had complimentary valet, so we chose to dine there for lunch. The restaurant is very open, with tables facing a large stage. At first, I was pretty excited to hear some live music. It was too bad, however, that all 3 singer/songwriters were just okay--nothing too impressive. The food and service wasn't much better. Although our hostess quickly seated us, we had to wait at least 15 minutes for a server to even take our order--and that was only after we flagged her down. Furthermore, our server perpetually had a frown on her face and didn't even smile once. I don't think we saw any of the staff look friendly. They just looked really unhappy and bored to be there. Not a good sign.

I ordered the All American Scramble (omelette with cheese, kielbasa, and gravy sauce) and it was just okay. For $13, I was expecting something much better, but the omelette was kind of dry and one note. The restaurant was also serving a buffet option for $18, but by the looks of it, it wasn't worth the money. Very small selection of food items. 

Overall, I left feeling very meh about the Listening Room Cafe. For what it is--a live music venue that serves food--the Bluebird Cafe is much better.

So glad this place is in Antioch!  The area needs more great local places like 360 Burger.  The food is great, the pretzel buns are awesome!  Fries were delicious, whatever sauce they bring with the sweet potato fries is to die for.  We shared the peach cobbler dessert, which was also delicious.  

Our server (Taylor) was great, the whole staff was attentive and friendly.  You can't get service like this at most places. 

Prices were great, a 1/3 lb burger with any toppings you wanted, fries and drink was $7.99.  I had sliders, fries and a drink for $6.99.  They have quite a bit of happy hour choices and prices were cheap, but we missed the timing by an hour.

They have live music Wed-Sat, from singer/songwriters to jazz.

The location is in an abandon strip mall, so plenty of parking.  I am hoping that with 360 Burger coming, more places will take notice and move in next door and surrounding retail spaces.  An Antioch dweller myself, I know people are anxious and ready for good businesses to come in.
Great steak. Fantastic music. Attentive server. Everything was delicious. Beer selection was OK, I prefer more local breweries on tap but that's just me. A definite must do in Nashville
Mike the bartender on the rooftop bar was amazing! Remembered our drinks even when we couldn't. Great views, great music, on a hot day the drinks kept us cool and relaxed!

I'm not normal a Kid Rick fan, but this place is awesome. The bands are exceptional and the food is good. The mixed drinks are also really good, and strong!! This place is busy all the time and that's because the bands are truly talented. We heard every genre of music, not just country, and they were so fun to listen to. Everyone was dancing and singing. This was without question, our favorite place to go on Broadway. Every time we are in Nashville, we end up here for good reason!!
The music was great. I enjoyed the the steak as well. The wings, however, really stood out to me.
Don't waste your time. Food was wildly mediocre and the show was just ok. Your money would be much better spent going somewhere in downtown Nashville with live music and good food.

I am not a huge country fan, but this place was amazing.  The Listening Room Cafe is a another place like the Bluebird Cafe, where country music lovers can listen to some of their favorite country songs.  The singer here are mostly the songwriters them selves.  

It is a little pricy for me...but well worth the visit....or two.

This location definitely stands out on broadway! It's loud and big!  We decided to check it out and have an early dinner and grab a couple drinks. We sat upstairs by a window. It was pretty packed! It's almost impossible to hear too so if you want to socialize don't eat here or pretty much anywhere on broadway for that matter.  Our server was fine - the place is so busy so you order and they drop off your check - then if you want food they'll bring another check.  We had 2 drinks at $10 each and chicken tenders and the chicken sandwich. The food was hot and fresh and the music was loud! Good experience - I would return!!
Walked in and felt like this was where the "older crowd" hangs. Also the music was way too loud that we left as our ear drums were ringing...
Drinks were diluted and service was slow. Pretty relaxed atmosphere and staff seem to be carefree and fun.

Cool atmosphere with live music for lunch.  Food was average but service was horrible.  I felt bad for the other waitress because everyone kept asking her for things... basic things like napkins and utensils.. great location , hopefully service will be better
The best kept secret in Antioch.   Great food and beer selection great live music.  Also a great place to watch sports.
I don't know about the food but the music, bands and party atmosphere are a hoot...so much fun! Was our go-to spot for dancing and music.

What a great little gem we discovered during our trip in Nashville. While in our hotel room searching for a place for dinner, we kept seeing the same BBQ and fried chicken options. We've been here for a few days already and wanted something different. We also wanted to hear great live music. 

That's when we learned about the Listening Room. Definitely pay for the show and dinner. You'll be required to pay $15 per person for F&B, but with the small
Cover charge of the show, it's well worth it. 

The setting is very intimate. Make sure to arrive early, even if you have reservations, just to make sure you get a great spot. My gf and I were fortunate to get a high top right smack in the center back with a great view just for us. 

I look forward to returning here next time I'm in town.

I'm shocked that by how few stars this was given. Everyone in my group of 25 really loved the cruise and it was the highlight of my trip to Nashville! We went during the day, the views were great and we got tons of fantastic photos. 

The dinner show was great. Very amusing! Loved Heartbreaker Barbie and some of the other characters ;)

Food was just ok. But everything else made up for that. Really enjoyed the desserts!

Absolutely horrendous place. I went for a pee and then they sent me to the back of a 1 hour line upon reentry. Complete a-hole bouncers. I at least asked them if I could wave down my boys, but they wouldn't let me. They threatened to call the cops on me instead even though I was sober. Like come on!!!! At least tell me I won't be aloud back in if you let me up a floor for a pee.

This place is the place to be on Broadway Street in Downtown Nashville!! Amazing live performers who interact wonderfully with the crowd. We saw multiple bands that all put on great shows. Good drinks and food as well. Come here for sure!!

This is the answer to, "Where should I go as a tourist in Nashville when I don't like country music?"

There really was something here for everyone. The performers really knew how to play to the crowd and I didn't see a single request stump them. Their jokes bordered on semi-innappropriate, but that's my style, so it made me love them more. The crowd was a little older than most other places we stopped, which is a nice change if what you are really after is to sit and chill while listening to music.

We stopped in for one drink. We ended up staying for several hours.

Loved the small music venue! The Song Suffragettes were playing, and they were talented young musicians. Ordered cheeseburger burger, catfish entree, veggie hoagie, and two apps fried green tomatoes and smoked chicken wings. The apps and home made chips were tasty, the rest was okay. Beer and wine were good. Would have preferred if wait staff could be friendlier, felt as if they were being put out.
Band was great. Food was good. Still working on bringing service to where it needs to be.

This is one of the hottest new bars to come to Nashville in a long time! It has the traditional feel of the honky tonks people come to Nashville to see, but with a 2nd floor and rooftop that has a whole different vibe. One of the only places in town with the ability to be treated like a VIP with your own booth and bottle service. Whether you're a first time Nashville visitor or a local, you'll be guaranteed to have a blast at this spot! 

The bartenders are top notch, and the VIP Hosts and Whiskey Row girls will make sure you have a night unlike anything else in Nashville!

They've also got a DJ lineup that is top notch! From Thursday's through Sunday Funday (don't miss this), it's gonna be blast!
Didn't know the Thong Song. V disappointing. Played Journey several times within the same hour. 3/5

For those of you used to cruising, you know the General Jackson. The ticket price is just the beginning. Drinks, photos, tours, meals, and show all will cost extra.
Plenty come to Nashville wanting to experience something of the history of the area. A river boat ride, country meal and country music show meets that groups desires. The musicians are studio quality and the meal is mass produced. There is plenty but nothing stands out. The staff is friendly and helpful.
I would not have done this if it had not been initiated by friends.

Johnny Cash was and remains an American treasure; a towering talent who transcended his genre and appealed to music lovers across the musical landscape. It is only fitting that there exists a museum devoted to telling his singular story. The Johnny Cash Museum is relatively new addition to the country-music scenein Nashville. It opened in 2013. We had visited the museum on a trip to Nashville in 2014 and were impressed with the way they told Johnny's life story. On this our second visit in October 2016, we were delighted to see that the curators have expanded the scope. Where there had been a large, open room showing a performance film on a loop, they have now divided the room to feature an exhibition concerning Johnny's time at Sun Studio (including telling the story and including artifacts of Johnny's Sun contemporaries--Elvis, Roy Orbison, Jerry Lee Lewis, and Carl Perkins,) a space devoted to the movie, "Walk the Line", the Cash family's piano, a look at the recording process, a space where a visitor can have a picture taken with Johnny, and a smaller theater showing Johnny in performance, among other new features. The museum tells the entire fascinating story of Johnny's rise from poor farm boy, through his time in the service, and then back home where he began his music career with the Tennessee Two. It's a comprehensive overview, including a ton of artifacts, film footage, and ancillary items (House of Cash sign, stone wall from the house on the lake, etc.) that serve to highlight Johnny's immense artistry. The experience concludes in emotional fashion with a section devoted to Johnny's Rick Rubin-produced version of the Nine Inch Nails song, "Hurt". A few pertinent  things to know about the museum: the price of admission is reasonable, the building is beautiful, it is close by to many of the downtown attractions, and there's a café attached to the gift shop. In all, the Johnny Cash Museum is a worthy take for fans of all genres of music, not just country music fans.

This is probably the biggest waste of money for food in Nashville. I ordered the chilli and fries and the chilli was cold and the fries were lukewarm. The menu has 6 food items, one dessert, and about 40 different beverages. Also there is a $15 spending limit so if you get no beverages you have to buy 3/6 items on the menu. The music is great usually but the service is terrible. Seriously Wendy's chilli taste better than what I ate tonight.

Stumbled upon this gem of a museum while strolling Broadway.  Had the wonderful opportunity to visit just prior to leaving town.  The staff were genuinely friendly and a pleasure to be around.  The museum covers the entire life of Johnny Cash with great exhibits.  Can't wait till our next visit to Nashville to visit again.
I am in love with this place mad Angela and Donny Lee rock OMG !!! I am HOME!! Great music, epic location and good food and a fantastic time!! I can't wait to come back next year!!

I do love me some Johnny Cash. 
Some tips: go early or on off days. This place can get really crowded and that takes away from the museum. 
It's small and has no re entry. So make sure you see everything you want to before leaving. 
Listen to the music and watch the footage they have. It's pretty interesting. 

That being said I wish that they either picked a larger venue and gave people more room or allowed for you to come in and out over the weekend to see it with less people.  It is also a little spendy for what you're getting. But when in Nashville.....

I hate to say negative things about a place many people seem to have enjoyed it. I don't think this museum is worth $22, especially when there are better attractions in the area for the same or less money. 

I like Johnny Cash and some of his music but you'd have to be a die-hard fan to enjoy this. Kids will be bored. 

Since i wasted my time and money here, I didn't get to spend much time in the Tennessee State Museum but the little that I saw was much more interesting and fun and free. I heard it has a music exhibit.

Cons:
1. $22 admission! --does not include Patsy Cline Museum!

2. Approximately 6 rooms total. 3 of those are just long hallways with memorabilia (costumes, photos, records, letters) up on the wall. 1 room is a looped video about his TV/movie appearances. 1 is just a loop of him making a speech about the American flag. The best room actually has some kiosks where you can listen to the music. 

3. Not that reading a lot of information is bad, but there is A LOT required to obtain the information. Long block paragraphs next to the exhibits. You'd have to stand at each item and read about it to even understand its significance. 

4.Very crowded-- made it difficult to read the information.
Well it's a fun environment the drinks are very expensive and there's limited seating. It's worth stopping by to check it out but I wouldn't write home to mom about it

We went here 2 nights in a row . Very good talent it seems is always here . Had a large crowd both times. Bartenders were attentive in helping each new person going towards the bar for drinks . We went walking to a few other spots but always would end up back here . Playing country , some rock on request and others. Great place to check out in downtown Nashville

While I'm not a huge country music fan, I do like history, and JC (Johnny Cash, not Jesus Christ) is certainly a big part of history - much moreso than I suspected before I entered.

If you have a AAA card, you save a buck off the $15 fee; kids tix are $11 each.

It's not terribly big, but man do they pack a LOT in a small space. Lots of artifacts and very good explanations to go with each. 

You enter and leave through the museum store, which has everything from soap to shirts. We didn't get anything but go ahead and look around.

If I could, It'd give it 3 1/2 stars.

Went on a Monday evening with another, pleasantly surprised by the quality of the song suffragettes singers. I once hear that in Nashville, you could hear star quality musicians at the local bars and listening rooms. You still can, and I plan on returning to Nashville regularly to listen.

For out of staters, there's something like a 15% alcohol tax on top of the regular taxes. Made a nice dent in my wallet, but at least it supports the area.

I have been now 4 times to 360 Burger, 3 times dining in, and 1 time picking up a carry out call in order. Every time i have been the service has been great, and the FOOD is AMAZING! The pretzel bun keeps me coming back as well, and the spinach as a side :-) The Sante Fe and Cilantro/Avocado Burger, the only 2 burgers i will ever need to order ;-) keep up the good work guys and gals....i will be back again soon!

Not a single Johnny Cash Museum shirt other than a few random ones on a discontinued rack. The staff was very short with us and rude when we asked if they had more. Displays and exhibits are great though. Still overall a bit of a disappointment.

A staff that we clearly inconvenienced by coming in to dine and drink. The two waitresses walked past our table and the table behind us four times over a 15 min period and each time they turned their backs in order not to make eye contact to take our order. I get treated better at the Waffle House. Left there and enjoyed a great meal and music at The George Jones.

Management did reach out and stated they would address issues.

OMG!! Came over her after Dierks Bentley's bar on a Saturday evening. Couldn't leave Kid Rocks Bar! The band was awesome! Music, & the crowd was alive!!! The bartender on the 1st floor Sarah (looks one that like Megan Fox) was a good! She was fast and getting you your drinks, and kept checking on up on us to see if we need anything else! I tired the hot wings with my beer, they were awesome..
This place was go good, we came back Sunday evening after checking out Luke Bryan's bar across the street... would definitely come back here next time in Nashville!!

If you're looking to embrace the music side of Nashville, but aren't into the honky-tonk crazy loud vibe, this is the place for you. The food is not that good, probably a 2.5 out of a 5, and the drinks are probably also a 2.5 out of a 5, and not all of the performers knock it out of the park. BUT, when I was there, there were two that were truly excellent, and that was all that mattered. Definitely glad I came. Make sure you come here having already eaten or with dinner plans afterwards.
Very cool place! Has all kinds of Johnny cash memorabilia, from his guitars and platinum albums down to his bible. If you are in Nashville it's worth a stop!

If you want to waste your hard earned money on a business that has zero regard for human life then waste your money here. My husband and I came into town to visit friends and decided to visit the museum. We are huge Johnny cash fans. We entered to a very busy room as it was rainy outside. I do not recommend coming on a rainy Day. We waited in line for a while before we actually stepped foot into the actual museum but shortly after we stepped in, my 9 week old started crying really hard. Of course my natural response was to turn around and leave. The rude lady taking tickets yelled at me and told me I couldn't leave that way because of 'fire code.' It made no sense whatsoever. So instead she told me I needed to make my way through the crowded museum with my husband and our baby stroller. It was a nightmare. I walked along slowly apologizing to the hundreds of customers about my sick baby crying. I ended up leaving with the baby and my husband walked through the museum as quickly as possible with the stroller since they wouldn't let him leave through the entrance either. My husband asked if we could re-enter so I could at least see the museum (since we paid 20 dollars per person and 22 for parking) and they rudely told him 'not a chance.' So I went back inside to ask for a refund and before I could even open my mouth the guy at the front desk said 'no way.' I told him I realize we can't re-enter but I would like a refund. He said we will not refund you no matter what. I asked for the manager who eventually reluctantly gave me a refund. When I told her about being treated rudely by the associate at the entrance she not once apologized, she responded with 'oh.' Nashville is a touristy town and you would think customer service was important. Not at the Johnny Cash museum...I'm said to say we will not be returning. We had wanted to visit that museum for years but I'm sad to say we will never go back.

I went to the boat with my husband last weekend to break up our "dinner and a movie" date routine and enjoyed it for the most part. The boat makes its way from Opryland to downtown Nashville and provides a great backdrop for pictures. The entertainment was good; the music wasn't necessarily what I would listen to but I appreciated the talent of the performers. The food was okay- think tough, reheated frozen dinner rolls and pretty dry roast beef. The cheesecake with cherries and chocolate sauce at the end redeemed the meal somewhat. The service wasn't so great, seeing as the only time I got a water refill was once about halfway through the meal when I called our waiter over and asked for one. They get three stars because of the entertainment and the scenic route. If I had it to do over again, I wouldn't get the $90 dinner ticket- I would buy a ticket for the cruise only and eat dinner beforehand.

Great place to experience the Nashville music scene! 

The food is another story because it was just okay... 

They have a $15 order/person, which does not include the ticket price. Our tickets were about $7 each and we ordered them online beforehand, so you have to spend money on food and/or drinks.

As far as food and drinks, we ordered the buffalo wings, salad, chili and fried pickles. The buffalo wings were pretty good, but the waffle fries had a weird, sweet taste. The salad was also good, but the chili lacked flavor because it literally didn't taste like anything, and the fried pickles were soggy. 

You might be better off spending your $15 minimum on drinks like the cocktails because they can be pretty strong, and you get more for your money.

Absolutely love this place. They show such respect to songwriters and provide an awesome atmosphere and quality sound. They also select talented artists; surely some greats will have their start at the Listening Room!

If you're looking for a fun night out Whiskey Row is the place to be! Not only is the music a great variety, the atmosphere is very lively! If you're looking for exceptional drink service look no future than BILL BUTLER he knows what he is doing moving at a very quick speed while also making a quality drink! Highly recommend this place.

I'm surprised by the bad reviews! We loved this place! It's a little bit more upscale than your typical Broadway honkey tonk, and the food is fabulous. I went out on a limb and got the kale and quinoa salad.. OMG!! So good. Like, please share the salad dressing recipe  

Also, ladies anything and everything you could need for a night out is supplied in the ladies room. Hair spray, deodorant, Tylenol, etc. I thought that was a nice touch. 

Overall, for a Broadway honkey tonk, it's a 5 in my book. Thanks, Dierks and staff!

I am only rating this for the Bye Bye Liver production.

I got it, as a bar in it of itself, it probably can be considered a little vanilla! 

HOWEVER for Saturday nights at 8PM... Bye Bye Liver is a hidden Nashville gem. It really is SNL on steroids. The skits are super interactive, super-drop dead funny, and of course super relevant for anyone between the ages of 20 to 60 (though I don't recommend taking your parents). 

BEST OF ALL it comes with table side service for drinks and FOOD! so you can drink while you play with the skits. 

There are also no such thing as bad seats...
Easy parking. Easy entry. Easy access to bars and restroom. Acoustics were great even in sold out crowd.
A very enjoyable, laid-back venue to eat and listen to music!

The worst place in Nashville. Boyfriend and I went here for New Years 2015. We put our drinks on a table and Nick (the boss) told us to take them off. Which we did but Nick (very short manager) looked at my boyfriend and like he was going to hit him and we asked the manager what is wrong we moved the drinks and the manager Nick said your boyfriend is giving me an attitude. My boyfriend didn't say a word to this man but ok we will move our drinks. The boss kicked us out. The boss wouldn't even listen to me. If you are a manager of customer service industry wouldn't it be smart to treat your customers well? I would never treat a couple this poorly. Nick is the worst manager I have ever seen. I told everyone on the bus back to the hotel. I told them to never go there and spend your money across the street at Honky Tonk where they treat there customers with respect and understanding.
Great find!  Even people not super fans would get something out of this.  Lots of content and memorabilia.  Lots of interactive listening.  Certainly worth the money to visit!

DJs: if you tip us, we will play the song you request. Half an hour later: "we don't have the song you requested, other people's money is more important than yours *proceeds to request security after request for different song or refund* 
Do not expect this bar to uphold your requests or hard-earned money.

This was a different experience for us but we really enjoyed it.  Once we arrived, the staff welcomed us aboard and were we surprised.  They had a lunch buffet that was great and a musical show that was awesome.  It was "Country" and anyone could enjoy the music and we enjoyed the musician talent and music while on the showboat.  One significant part of the trip while riding up and down the Cumberland River was you can go outside and see it while riding.

My friends and I did a tour at the Grand Ole Opry and decided to take advantage of a groupon for Madame Tussaud's Nashville museum which is located in the mall just walking distance from the Grand Ole Opry.  In my opinion, it's well worth it.  We had a lot of fun seeing "wax" figures of country stars, rock stars, country legends, blues legends, movie stars, and some pop stars.  There are some that are freaky just how much they look real (the Jimi Hendrix is great!).  Maybe a couple that are a bit iffy (*cough* Justin Timberlake).  But either way it's fun and relatively cheap attraction and it's impressive how long it is.

Music was great. Cool looking bar. Service was pretty bad. Took forever. After our first round and an appetizer the check was already on the table. Got a second round, she did the same thing. Like just tell us you have been cut and we would have cashed out. Do not like feeling like I'm being kicked out after dropping a $100. Drinks are way overpriced for what you get. Ended up staying because of a terrible rain storm. NO, Zero mention anywhere of a $3 service fee to pay with credit. Got to pay that twice. You can go here for decent eats. A little google search will steer you to better food. But there are plenty of places on music row with better drink prices, staff, and the exact same music.
Great bar with great music and atmosphere. Hung out at the rooftop, the bartender Nicole was an absolute professional, very friendly and great at her job. If you In Nashville this place is a must

Beware the hidden charges.  Stopped in for a drink and some music on a Saturday night.  Paid $6pp cover which is fine but what really annoys me is that I noticed the tax on the computer printed bill was 24%!  I questioned the waiter, he went to speak with someone, came back and told me it was correct, stating that there's no state income tax in TN so they have very high sales tax.  It sounded crazy, but I didn't argue.   Today at brunch I realized the tax rate is 9%.  So they have programmed into their computer an extra 15% for no reason.  We were a party of 3, so it wasn't an automatic tip, and it was all on the tax line.  I guess most people are too drunk to notice, but I want to call them out on it.  It's just wrong and I added extra tip.  If it hadn't been for this, I'd give a higher rating.
great food and service!! I love the high rooftop bar. I would recommend getting here early because it can get busy at night.

I went to Kid Rock's new restaurant Thursday night with an out of town crew from work.  It was a disappointment.  I ordered the NY Strip medium rare, but it was a tough cut and overcooked closer to well done than medium.  Not worth the price.  The onion rings were soggy.  Our waitress was attentive, and the music wasn't too bad, which is why I'm giving it two stars.

Overall the ambiance felt like Jason Aldean's or Blake Shelton's new joints.  Slick, sterile, and uninteresting.  It's a shame to see authentic Nashville turn into corporate main street.  Kid Rock should have stayed in Detroit with his signature rock-rap sound, and left the country-western honky-tonk scene to the locals.

Sad.

The gift shop at the Nashville location has the rudest and most unfriendly service personnel I have ever encountered. I entered the gift shop just to look around at the souvenirs, and was promptly followed about by a sales person that not only never cracked a smile, but didn't even utter a single word. Perhaps future training of employees should include instructions on how to communicate with potential cash paying customers, or better yet how to have basic good manners.  Since when did sales people Forget how to make a "friendly " sale? Needless to say I walked out of the store empty-handed and disappointed at the state of affairs today.

This venue is fun, but I would probably not stay for more than an hour next time. It is important to get here early as seats/tables fill up quickly. The artists who played were entertaining and very good, however, the staff (specifically at the bar) was not very friendly. We had a party of around six individuals who casually hung out at the bar and watched the entertainment, however, each time we ordered drinks it felt like we were an inconvenience.

This 5 start review is def not for the food bc it would be around a 2 if i were rating the food (salmon was burnt and burger was plain). But the show was amazing. Best thing we did during our 3 day visit to Nashville! A Must do if your visiting.

This bar was so fun until one of the (very) desperate servers decided to prey on my boyfriend and said that "he disturbed her" and then we were sort of stalked by all staff until we exited the bar. She seemed very bored, probably wanted some attention, but it was super unfortunate because our group was having so much fun till that point. All of Nashville had been so hospitable till then, it was just so sad to see her snap like that. We just wanted to dance, so maybe the bars should be more in touch with their servers' mental health. She had many needs that seemed unmet. Dierks, ask your servers what's up? They need mental help.

Lovely showboat tour.  We love the cocktail time on the decks before dinner.  It was tranquil while the boat was moving towards downtown. Dinner was fine. After dinner we all came out on the decks and watch Nashville downtown. Beautiful skyline and city lights.  It doesn't hurt that the weather was great. Later we went back inside to watch the show.  The performers did not disappoint ... great music.
I loved it, I wish the prices were not so high to get a picture with the gorgeous man in black but this is a tourist trap so....overall go check it out, it was so much fun!

Recommend if you are trying to separate from the group you are with. Door men run a tight ship. Can only review from 1st and 2nd floor. Never needed to climb higher. If you find the hotdog stand right outside, also highly recommend.

If you are visiting Nashville, you HAVE to stop by this place! I've made sure that anytime I'm traveling to Nashville for work or pleasure I visit Big Bang and it never disappoints. Whether you're on a date, with friends, with colleagues or even by yourself, it's impossible not to have fun here. I'm a big fan of dueling piano spots and have been to A LOT throughout the country, this is my #1! 

Make sure to put in some awesome requests, grab a few drinks and then just sit back and enjoy. You won't be sorry for stopping in here!

Not sure if Justin Nault still performs here but if you go on a night he is, you're in for a treat! He was so great that I actually hired him to perform for a work event after seeing him at Big Bang. The talent here is top notch!
Fun bar.  The music was good but because of the name I think it's a little overpriced and over hyped.  With that said it's worth a look see but probably not a regular joint.

This was such a disappointment, and total waste of a cover charge.  Upon entering you have to walk up a bunch of stairs.  If you could see the inside from the outside, you wouldn't bother.  It's dark, barely any walking room, no dance floor, and we only saw one waitress.  The song they sing for a woman's birthday is completely vulgar.  I'll never go back.
I was really excited about going.  The dueling piano bar in NOLA was one of my favorite memories.  The one in Nashville is just....bad.  Don't waste your money.
Couldn't get eye contact to even ask how to get service. Host standing at merch 5ft away while ppl waiting at host stand for help.
The restroom on 3rd floor was clean but, no, toilet paper. Food was okay. Service was not great.

Great establishment and did a great job with the Geddy Lee book signing and Q&A.   Huge crowd, lots of us crazy Rush fans lined up early for a chance to be up close and personal with the Big Beautiful Book of Bass author Geddy and get a signed copy.  The staff is awesome with crowd management - getting everyone in quickly, managing the crowd inside and organizing a great event.  I'm sure it's just a good on a music night, but here on a Sunday evening for a author's Q&A and signing, they did a great job and made everyone feel welcomed and comfortable!  Thanks for a fun night!

Really didn't expect to like this place as Broadway dives aren't my thing.  However we saw the fiddle and the standup base and went in.  The bloody Mary's we great.  They had a biscuits-n-gravy special that was pretty good as well.  So all in all pleasantly surprised.
Great bar atmosphere with decent music. Packed on a Memorial Day Monday and fun for it. Cold Yuenglings and tasty, junky fries with chicken bbq & ranch.

Had great expectations for this place walking in. Great venue!! Music and artists were great. The place was full. Service was the worst we've experienced in Nashville. Wait staff took forever to take our drink orders and when we asked for the menus when we sat down, we still never received them so we asked to borrow some menus from the table next to us. We were at the 8:30 show "The Movement", which included two sets of an hour each. We ordered our food as the first set was starting. During the changing of sets, we asked the waitress about our food. She said the kitchen was really backed up. She came back 5 min later and said she moved our food to "the front". When it came out, the burger we ordered was a chicken sandwich. After sending it back, a cold burger returned, but they forgot the mac n cheese. When it came out, it was still hot. Very poor dining experience. I have high hopes the management staff takes some leadership and turns the kitchen and wait staff around. There may be too many offerings given the number of people sitting down all at once to eat.
Hot place - great vibes and live music! I highly recommend this for drinks and excellent live music.   I did not try the food the menu looks like American Fare!

While away on a girls trip we spent an evening here! The entertainment was really great and the musicians shared the stage, while taking turns singing and playing songs. They talked and told stories and the evening was very cool. There are lots of bar drink options and typical bar food as well.

It was AWFUL. The bouncers took our REAL ID's. They would let us speak to the police or anything. I guess we have no way to get home, because they dropped them down a sewer grate. Wouldn't recommend if you're 21-23. F this place. They'll be hearing from us soon!

Went in there this weekend for my bachelorette night and John David one of the managers made sure my girls and I had full drinks and food at all times. The atmosphere was awesome, good music, and clean bathrooms!!! highly recommend this for any type of night out. Not to mention the bbq fries were amazing.

This has the potential for greatness!  However, there is so much stuff crammed into a small area.  Add a crowd of people and it's unbearable.  A bigger venue is desperately needed to fully honor a great musician.
This place is awesome! Has great bands all the time and has a rocking great vibe! Highly recommend checking out.
Went in early in the day. Waited 15 minutes and ended up walking out. No server. Not even a drink order. Place wasn't busy. Go figure...

If you are a Johnny Cash fans, this place will be great. All else, meh. They had almost every piece of memorabilia from Mr. Cash you could imagine in a well laid out order. However, there were WICKED crowds going thru EVERYTHING. I have never seen that many people read the cards of almost every artifact. Combined with a very small (let's say too small) spot made it very tough to get a good feel for things. I thought there was more, but must have missed it. Not a second floor like I imagined. Not worth it unless you are a huge fan.

I will not be returning to this location ever again. I had high expectations of this place but unfortunately was a complete letdown.
First off my girlfriend's work friend was having a birthday on the 2nd floor and had a table reserved.. 

Some context is I did not know her work friends last name. 

Well after standing in a 30min line outside I find out I have to stand in another line to get up stairs
As I wait for the stairs I notice people going up without standing in line 
So I ask the door attendant "hey, if people have a table can we skip the line" 
He says "sure what is the name" so I give her first name
This asshole literally looks at me laughs and says "ya... you must know her really well" and wouldn't let me through at all

So I missed most of her birthday from the waiting I didn't even need to do because of this jackass...

I will NEVER return here and I do NOT recommend it 

It's hotter than Hades there. The security is obviously doing their job very well 
Considering my girlfriend telling me she was able to just go up the stairs without giving a name or showing ID to get in so I guess this place is sexiest too 

Well it's Welcome to Nashville once again

The only bummer about this place is that it's super crowded! There was a lot to read and see but we almost didn't want to stop and take it in due to the overwhelming crowds! They should definitely limit the number of people they allow in!! It's only about an hour worth of content so they could easily stagger entries so people don't feel so claustrophobic!

We had so much fun here on our first night in Nashville, that we decided to come back for a second night!

Definitely purchase your tickets online ahead of time. Seats are assigned as you walk in the door, so show up early to check-in and get the best seats. We found that the tall bar-top tables in the back had the best acoustics and best service (those tables are tended by the bartenders who are much closer and able to check in more frequently).

The $15 food/drink minimum per person was easily met with a few drinks each. We tried the nachos on the first night, which were just OK. The food was nothing to write home about.

We were in town on a long weekend vacay from Maine.  Although we had already done the Grand Old Opry, we thought another authentic Nashville country experience on our last day would be the perfect ending.  Unfortunately, the show was a bit of a downer.

The food was a basic mass-catering buffet with no real authentic southern cuisine (bland baked chicken, pulled pork with a salty BBQ sauce, basic salad, basic veggies, basic apple cobbler).  And, the wait staff doesn't speak very good English

The ambiance is pretty neat if you've never been on a river boat...an old Victorian flair.  You have the ability to walk around the boat too, so, you can get a chance to see the riverside while motoring along towards downtown Nashville.  And, there really isn't a bad seat to view the show (i.e. I wouldn't pay the extra $25 to get one of the "Captain's" tables).

The show itself was ok.  It's a bit on the cheesy side but it's a typical "showy" show with rehearsed one-liners in between songs that allow for choreographed movement about a pretty small stage.  The show consisted of four singers plus a piano player performing a range of slow-quick tunes revolving around southern faith and history with a few famous covers.

After the show, you can go out on the top deck as the boat passes through the Nashville harbor and get a nice view of downtown and Nissan Stadium.  The extra hour after the show was the best part of the trip as some of the band members continue to play in a more intimate bar-style atmosphere on the very top deck.

Overall, I'd rather have spent the $70 somewhere else downtown...for example, we did a distillery tour for $15 that was rather interesting and that included a nice tasting of several liquors.

We all thoroughly enjoyed our evening here. The entertainment was awesome. I wasn't crazy wild about the meal. It was fun to try fried brussel sprouts but when paired with the brisket and french fries it was just too much grease. There is a wider menu so don't let that deter you from trying it.

Quick review: For anyone visiting Nashville and looking for a fantastic live music experience, Listening Room Cafe should be on your list! Similar to Bluebird Cafe but much easier to get tickets, very inexpensive, lovely interior and outstanding on-stage talent.

Details :

Note - My review is strictly for the music and ambience! I did not sample any of the food.

Before my first trip to the Music City, I received several recommendations to attend an "In the Round" event. Basically, a show where the best up and coming songwriters get a chance to showcase their talent. I had initially tried to get tickets for the famous Bluebird Cafe, but was too slow on the draw so I discovered Listening Room Cafe instead.
