My boyfriend and I purchased tickets for the St. Patrick's Day show - $5 each. I ordered them quickly and easily online for a grand total of $13.29 at checkout (with the service fee). So reasonable!

We watched Smithfield, Adam Wood, Casey Derhak and Jesse Lee perform, and it was absolutely incredible! The audience is asked to maintain a low level of noise, which is much appreciated because you want to soak in every second of the talent on-stage. Once the show ended, I could hardly believe that almost 3 hours had passed.

We arrived about 15 minutes early to get a good table. They seat you based on your arrival, filling in the tables from front to back. The wait staff is super attentive and discreet during the show (for the most part). 

Definitely give Listening Room Cafe a visit! Fun fact, Jesse Lee sang for us the hit song "Peter Pan" that she co-wrote for country star Kelsea Ballerini. Just one example of the awesome talent you get to see!

Ok, this was a disappointing experience. It was a small museum for such a legend and for two reasons. One, less details about his life and fewer exhibits than expected. Two, terrible crowd control. They were letting as many people as would buy a ticket to just enter making it VERY congested, hard to see exhibits, read details and get a decent pic of any thing. Unless Johnny Cash is one of your too three heroes in life, save the money and time. Instead, buy a good book about his life and watch a documentary.

I loved this place! I was in town for a conference and looking for a spot near my hotel to hear live music, and enjoy good food and this place was perfect! The food was excellent- I wasn't super hungry so I ordered 2 appetizers: wings and fried green tomatoes and had plenty leftover for the next day.

Stopped by here for a drink before a concert, sat at the bar, staff was friendly, place was clean, drinks were cold, ended up with shrimp fritters for an appetizer, they were pretty good, will definitely stop by again
Holy cow!!  So fun!! Hannah was the best waitress we had in all of Nashville! Beautiful, fun and professional.  Great band and ASK FOR HANNAH

My burger with BBQ sauce, cheese and onions was delicious!! Also out waiter, wish I got his name, was the most friendly and genuine waiter I've ever had! This place is hopping we got there opening at 11:00 and when we left hour or so later it was packed. It was also sun morning and Titans were playing though too. If we lived here would Definately come back. Also looks like they have live music. Only complaint is kinda took a while to he food and they gave me the wrong fries. No biggie. Great local, freshly made place. Yum!

What a fun place in Nashville. They have such respect for the performers and it should be that way. Food was good but that's not why we went. Some very serious talent. Would highly suggest going there to see performers you'll see for a lot more in the future.

We were invited by friends to drive up to Nashville and take a ride on the General Jackson Showboat, see the show, and have lunch. I've seen the boat on the river and figured it might be worth the trip. 
Seeing friends was great. The boat and show was just ok. 

I have to caveat this with the comment that I'm not big on this type of canned entertainment myself and this lived up to those expectations and seems very typical of tourist-type venues. 

Lunch was a buffet with BBQ and fried chicken as the main dish. About as good as you might get at Golden Corral if you chose to eat there. We don't because we like good food. 

The show was fun. Honestly I thought the main show was a little hokey but afterwards two of the gentlemen performers did a more casual show that I would have enjoyed as the main performance much more.  

Overall it was ok but we probably would not have done this as our own outing and will consider it a "one and done" deal.

Oh Whiskey Row. I want to love you so much because you are seriously so awesome! But your staff SUCKS. I was just there, literally 5 minutes ago, with my husband hanging out on the rooftop. We decided to leave after ONE DRINK, and we go down to the 3rd floor and I'm waiting for my husband to come out of the restroom before we get into our Uber, and one of the "bouncers" comes up to me and says I'm being escorted out. Ummm excuse me? For what?! Obviously confused, I ask why I'm being escorted out. "I've been told that you were already kicked out once and you snuck back in. You need to leave now." I tell him it's clearly a misunderstanding because I was up at the rooftop with my husband having one drink and how could I have snuck in past 3 door guys...but he refused to listen to me and said he was just doing his job. I've worked in the service industry my whole life, and I've never been treated so horribly for something I didn't do. It's a holiday weekend, train your staff better. There's 20 girls wearing the same thing I'm wearing. Don't kick out a random, good customer because of a miscommunication. There are too many other great bars, so I will definitely not be back.

This place was a pleasant surprise for me, but my friend had been here the last time he was in Nashville. My friend and I had been to another place earlier in the day, and we were let down by the service and the food. That was definitely not the case here. The whole experience was great.

When you walk in the place, there is a stage and a band playing. Back home that would be a nice touch, but Nashville it is a prerequisite. The downstairs area was crowded, but the bartenders were still attentive. There was no seating available and my friend did not want to stand while eating, so we went upstairs to eat. The upstairs was not crowded and it was a nice environment. There were plenty of flat screen tvs and seating to accommodate large groups of people.

The food was really good and the portion sizes were large. I had the burger with barbeque and bacon, which was delicious. It was not made from a frozen patty, unlike the place we had been to earlier in the day. There was one person who worked there, but I did not get her name. She reminded me of Rosie the Riveter, and she was nice. Unfortunately, she is a Packers fan, but I guess we all have our flaws. She was describing the chicken fingers, and I am now going to have to make a trip back to try them. She also was describing some of the other items, and I have to say that if they are as good as the burger I will come back every time I am in Nashville.

The service was really good. As I said earlier, the downstairs bartenders were very attentive. There just was no available seating downstairs. As a result, we were about to leave the place when the bouncer let us know there was seating upstairs. Vanessa was the bartender upstairs, and she was a very good bartender. She's definitely the triple threat. It was nice because between Vanessa and Rosie the Riveter, it seemed like this is where I would be watching football games every Sunday (besides Bears vs. Titans/Packers/Vikings). One of the guys that worked there took a break upstairs by the bar, and he was telling me more about moonshine. I have to admit that I do not know about moonshine, but after talking with him and Vanessa... I might just try some one of these days.

This place was really good, and I look forward to my next visit.

very poor service at side bar Monday April 8th
ordered dinner took an hour to get drinks very slow order a drink still didnt recieve 10 min after ordering while other people walking up to the side bar got served.
The bartender spent more time on her phone texting than looking after and servicing paying customers.
She was miserable mouthy after asking her why it took so long to get our meal and drinks , Asked for the tab and she started mouthing us off and tossed the tab at us so I did state no tip for you.
She really got irate and went and got security to remove us. I explained ed what took place and I was leaving anyways as I was signing off our tab.
they were very professional and said to take our time finish our drinks first then if we didnt mind to leave which we respected.
The bartender on the side bar should not deal with the public very poor skills 
The food was excellent even tho it took so long and the band was amazing they did a good job with the crowd.
It's too bad one person who was employed by the bar ruins a customer experience as we went to a couple other bars after the fact and found the service night and day over what we just experienced.
I know I will not  step foot and spend money in that location again which seemed to be the consensus from allot of other people we talked to as well.
Management should look at a problem employee

Had a great evening! Everyone was attentive and food was excellent.i was pleasantly surprised as a lot of times buffets are so so but everything offered was delicious. Music show was excellent and our server George was awesome! Definitely a keeper!

Some friends had their birthday party here tonight.  We were excited to give the place a try, since they have raved about it on numerous occasions, and when we tried on Labor Day they were closed.  

Unfortunately it did not live up to expectations.  Two 1/3 lb burgers & 1 order of sliders were ordered medium, and all came out crunchy and dry.  The chicken wings were over-sauced with think gooey barbecue sauce.  I had intended to get barbecue sauce on my burger, but after trying the wings I thought better of it.  My wife ordered the garlic aioli on hers and it came out tasting overwhelmingly of mustard.  My daughter was only able to eat 2 bites of her sliders due to the burnt taste.  The other person at our table ended up canceling her order after waiting an hour without receiving it.  On the up side, the sweet potato fries were good, as was the live music (laid back R&B style).

The service also left something to be desired.  The party was scheduled in advance, and they were informed that it would be 45 people.  Unfortunately they were not staffed accordingly.  The wait staff was so overworked that we had to ask 3 times to get a glass of water, and again for any refills.  Over the course of 2 hours, only 1 glass was bussed from the table, despite the stack of plates that was obviously not in use any more.  As the evening progressed we saw more staff come in, but being forewarned they should have been ready for the crowd.

I really want to see new businesses in this area thrive.  I'm particularly in favor of restaurants that cater to a more sophisticated palate, much like we've seen in East Nashville & Midtown, and even in the Lennox Village area.  360 Burger looks like it wants to be one of those places, but it has a lot of work to do to get there.  Based on the reviews I've seen, it looks like a problem of consistency rather than concept.  With tonight as a first experience, I'm unlikely to return.

Food was ok nothing special.  I had wings, ordered a side of celery and ranch and never got it.  Server asked twice if I got it and just shrugged when I said no.   She tabbed us out after an hour because she was leaving (8:30 pm).  Good thing too - a Bacardi/Coke and Beam/Coke are $12 each!!!  Not coming back here

We visited Nashville for the past 4 days. We kept coming back to Dierks Bentley bar.  We had a blast! Great music with the Dozzi band, which everyone needs to follow on Twitter, Facebook etc... they were awesome and could go everyday and listen to them!!  The bartender Jake was absolutely the best!!!! He took great care of us, very pleasant, kind and was always on top of his job....we love you Jake and we will be back to visit!!   Until next time Nashville 

Brian and Mel from Greenville, PA

I was staying in the Moxy next door and let's just say that it was very easy to "head back home" from the other spots and visit Kid Rock's place. There are a bunch of good bands in Smashtown but---ALL of the talent---regardless of the time that they played---was headline material at Kid Rock's.  Entertaining. Could play anything you could think about wanting to hear.  It's very loud with music so if that is not your thing, do not go becuase you will not have a good time. The place wa spacked all of the time but it literally took less than 2 minutes to get a beer at the bar (for me) each time I was there.  Must stop place when you visit.
Ok I stand corrected.   So just be prepared to pay 24% above the price of your drinks for state taxes and it's not the establishment's fault that they have to charge that much.

Real nice burgers + happy hour till 10pm + good live music.

I went here the first time and got myself the avocado cilantro burger with house fries. The fries were slightly soggy but the burger was bang on. Medium well done patty on a pretzel bun, oh boy aren't you my new favorite burger joint.

Just to make sure first time wasn't a fluke I went back again after a week and this time I got myself the insanity burger with sweet potato fries. The sweet potato fries were superb and the burger has now become one of the best I've had. 

I will keep going back till I'm around this part of Nashville. Yet to try a couple of their other burgers and hoping they'd turn out as good an experience as I've had so far.

I enjoyed this place a lot. Local museums are always hit or miss, but Johnny Cash just has such a great story and this museum actually has a pretty fantastic selection of memorabilia and actual items from Johnny's life. It's tourist friendly and well organized. And there's a Patsy Cline museum right above it too. Great way to spend a few hours and a little more authentically Nashville than the Kid Rock Honkytonk.

Stopped in for a drink on a Thursday, live bands on every floor was cool. Went on the roof top to have a beer (2 bud lights $13.00), don't know if that's  the going rate. Service was excellent! Food looked real good and seemed reasonably price. Nashville police officers present in bar is a good site.
Good job Bob!

If you're in Nashville, the Listening Room should be at the top of your list of things to do. It's a cafe by day, venue by night with 2 showings: 6pm and 8:30pm. Even if you're not a country fan (I'm not, really), the performers play a wide variety of songs and most of them are acoustic.

The host of the place I stayed at recommended checking out the Listening Room during my stay. She told me about how songwriters came to the stage and played their original songs before being bought and played by singers. It was an interesting premise, so decided to check it out. I tried buying tickets on the day of for the 8:30pm show, and they were sold out, so let that be a lesson to you guys, buy your tix early! 

I showed up and they told me that they create a waitlist, and after 8:45pm, they'll check the no-show lists and begin seating. I was able to snag a bar seat for $14. I had the pleasure of seeing Kelly Archer, Darby, Justin Ebach, Jordan Minton, who all played and sang lovely acoustic versions of their songs. 

There is is $15  minimum to  spend per person  I got the sangria while I was there because I was warned about their food by my host. Sangria was okay; nothing to write home about. 

Overall a wonderful experience!

Paid a visit for burger week. Nice to have a local beef/sorta hip spot in Antioch. They have 2 for 1 beers til 10 everyday which is kind of misleading cause the beers are smaller than most places. Ordered wings which were very good and the burger tasted fresh and good. The music was a bit loud and pretty average but I'd go back due to the good burger and wings.
Does Kenzie play here from castaway show on tv? I really like her and want to hear some of her songs.

We checked out The Listening Room Cafe during our trip in November. Hopefully, the google listing has been updated since then; we ended up ubering to the old location, without realizing they had moved. We ended up taking another uber to the new location. 

The venue was super cute. They were quick in seating you (despite the long line). We enjoyed the songwriter's performances, with their back stories to each song. I would definitely go again if I'm ever in the area again!

Had brunch here on a recommendation from a friend when visiting Nashville- a modern-rustic atmosphere with live singer-songwriter performances. The food was very good (I had the biscuits and gravy), the service and the atmosphere were excellent. Rumor was that the mimosas were bottomless-they weren't but they were 2-for-1, so we couldn't complain. Our sever was friendly and helpful, and the hostess, Daisy, spent way more time than I would ever expect to help us find other music-related things to do away from the endless loop of overplayed covers on the Broadway strip. A welcome dose of quiet coolness a short walk from the main drag.

Our family had such a great time at the Listening Room.  We were visiting Nashville over spring break and wanted to listen to live music.  Made reservations (you may want to book a few weeks in advance) and were lucky to catch the Song Suffragettes playing one evening.  The food was very good, service even better, and the live music was fantastic.  Valet parking in the city is also a nice touch.  Can't wait to go back.
So much fun. Nice venu, good music and drinks. A nice mix of music too. I'm surprised it doesn't have better reviews, but also learned this place is recently new to broadway.
We didn't eat here, only had drinks. The drinks were strong and reasonably priced. It's very neat and clean inside which we liked. The band playing was good too.
My favorite place in nashville.....tons of awesome memorabilia and the staff is very friendly and helpful....i go there nearly everytime im in nashville

Yuck. The entire boat was covered in spiders. Railings, posts, walls, and windows should be inspected before getting close. The ceiling lights were festooned with them. An arachnophobe would have been petrified. 

The dining room was better - the spiders were on the outside of the windows. Our waiter was charming at first, but things changed when it became clear that no one at the table was drinking, a big focus of the cruise. The drinking tables did seem to be having a great time.

The food was fine. Dinner was served and cleared before the entertainment stage show began.

Stopped in for lunch on my way to work. The place was busy, but not packed. I was seated right away, but then waited 10 minutes before a server showed up. He took my order, brought my drink, and then the long wait started. At the forty minute mark I went to find a manager. He said he'd check on my order. It came out almost immediately. Good burger but definitely not worth the wait (I got the Slippery Pig). The fries were excellent crinkle cut, and well seasoned. If this was a new place I'd understand, but it's not. Not sure if I'll go back.

Really fun atmosphere. We had a large group of 14 girls and service was slow, but understandable. I really wanted to like this place, but unfortunately, had a really awful bartender who asked me what I needed and when I asked for four waters, he rolled his eyes and told me "it would be a while." After watching him serve six other customers I asked if it was my turn for the water yet. He was horrible. We spent a lot of money here and we will never come back. Don't waste your time.

This place is so amazing. Do you like live music? Do you like to hear things that are not on popular radio? Do you like to hear straight from the singer/songwriters/musicians?  You have to come here!  

I was lucky enough to attend a Song Suffragette show. These ladies are amazing!! So much talent and heart in everything they give up there on stage.  I enjoyed the show so much, that during the time between the first and second show, we sat on their patio and bought tickets to the second show. It is a songwriters showcase of sorts.  

There is a food/drink minimum per person so be mindful of that, and they do have a pretty full menu. 

I will make it a point to come here every time I visit Nashville if I can.
the southern fries are absolutely amazing and the rooftop bar has the perfect view of downtown!

Overall, I had an exceptional time with my girlfriend at the Listening Room Cafe. We went on a Saturday night with singer and songwriter Vanessa Bransan, AJ Engstrom, and Phil Barton performing. They were amazing and made the night enjoyable for us and everyone else. We both really enjoy the opportunity after the show to meet and chat with the artist, and also get pictures and autographs from them. Vanessa was so sweet and nice to my girlfriend and me, and Phil was very personable when we chatted with him. We didn't get to talk to AJ, but he was very comedic onstage and had a great personality. 

We both really enjoyed the ambience provided at the Listening Room Cafe. Our waitress was very courteous and nice. She did a tremendous job trying to wait on her tables while allowing everyone to hear and enjoy the show too without being interrupted. However, I did have to take a star away for the food. Our waitress was kind and updated us on our food and apologized for the wait, which was very nice of her. The food was mediocre. I'm sure the kitchen was well busy with the amount of orders, but I expected better execution with the atmosphere they provided. The french onion soup was solid and tasty; the veggies skewers had an interesting taste; the portobello mushrooms were a bit heavy on the greasy side and they forgot the ranch sauce, but they had good flavors; and the sweet fries were seasoned very well, but very soggy as if the deep fryer temperature wasn't hot enough and the fries just soaked up the oil. 

We will be back for the show and I hope they improve on their cuisine. When they do, I will gladly give them 5 stars. :)

Okay - I really wanted to love this place, but just couldn't. We went on our first night of a bachelorette party last night and it was SO disappointing, I was compelled to share. 
1 - first and foremost, it was SO dirty. Specifically the bathroom downstairs. Women's room literally had poop on the ground and coffee grounds around to try and cover up the awful smell. 

2 - the well liquor was the cheapest of cheap, the drinks were awful. 

Considering how dirty everything was, you couldn't pay me to order food from here. Sad!

I was very disappointed in the female bartender last night. I asked do you have Malibu rum? she told me yes. I proceeded to order a tall,double Malibu diet coke and a beer for my friend. 38.00 I took a sip and it was not Malibu it was Cruz coconut rum which gives me a terrible headache. I asked for her to replace it as I had specifically asked prior to ordering what they use.. she would not replace my drink so it cost me another 20.00 to get a replacement I could drink ... I was very upset at her disregard  and behavior when I told her it could be dumped because I can't drink it..  she rolled her eyes and said "well its coconut  rum same damn difference" apparently she has never had a migraine... rude ... the band Was great and I would have stayed a lot longer had the bartender been decent.

For as long as I've been living in Tennessee I had never had the pleasure of going on the boat, until now. I will say, it was a surprise date, so I was not dressed for the occasion. We had captain table seats, so we were allowed to board the boat before everyone else. It was a cold night, so that was a nice touch. Once seated, we were given our captains cocktail, which was included with our seats. Shortly after, everyone else started boarding and filling up the place. 
The detail and ambiance of the boat is very inviting. Once filled and everyone seated we were told about leaving dock and as part of captains table our tour and T-shirt. 
Shortly after, dinner started to be served. Salad, dinner, and dessert. Dinner is served family style, but do cater to diets/allergies. 
To be honest, the food wasn't that great. It was okay. Dinner consisted of ribs, spinach stuffed chicken, mashed potatoes, Mac n cheese, and carrots. Chicken lacked in flavor and carrots were not thoroughly cooked. Maybe an off day, who knows. 
Our table was escorted outside for our tour. We went upstairs into captains quarters. Talked w him for a while and took pictures. Went to back of boat to see the paddle wheel. Then back to our table for dessert and show. 
Once dinner was cleaned up the show started. Mc took us through a weeks worth of music in Nashville. Performers/singers did a good job. Very captivating and entertaining. 
Showboat experience is about 3 hours. Once the show ended everyone started to get up and go home. 
Very unique experience.  We enjoyed it. Next time we won't need to sit at the captains table.

We travel to Nashville a few times a year on business and I've visited this restaurant just about every time. The first few times was good enough to keep me coming back, but this time was the absolute best! The food has improved dramatically just over a few months, as we were over on business back in the spring. A friend suggested the German chocolate torte and I'm glad I took his advice because it was phenomenal, I highly recommend it. 
Unfortunately, Julia our server could've used a lesson on how to properly serve customers, but aside from her poor service everything was wonderful. I will definitely be recommending this lovely place to friends, and I will look forward to continued visits here.

Went to Whiskey Row last night & every single time I've ever been I have had GREAT service from Orion & Kelsey but Madi served my friends & I last night & we just felt like a nuisance the entire time. She was so unconcerned with our needs that we were all uncomfortable. I have managed restaurants for plenty of years & I couldn't believe someone so apathetic was in a position of leadership. (We were told she was some type of manager) I enjoy going to Whiskey Row so much but Madi absolutely ruined our experience. For her sake, I'd like to assume positive intent & hope that maybe she was just having a bad day, but I am so disappointed with the service from her. My rating is a reflection of her, not the venue as a whole.

A lot smaller and cramped than expected. Visited during a relatively busy time but still had enough time and space to check everything out. The displays with authentic Johnny Cash memorabilia were really cool to see. Seeing the items first hand felt surreal. The history and information was very concise. Lots of interactive exhibits are available with some patience. They also have a cool green screen you can use to take a picture with Johnny Cash (around $20 for a single print. The gift shop was also great and contained  anything you could ever need. Toddler sizes are more general than age-specific. Cash and cards are both accepted. Admission was around $20 per adult. Overall a great experience for big Johnny Cash fans.

Bad service by the blond bartender who kept on ignoring us. She had the worst attitude and definitely made our experience terrible. 
The cook seemed to be scared of her and behaved strangely too.
Band was awesome and they should be playing in a better location!

So fun.  It's a good Nashville spot.  Expensive but I think it's worth it. Some interactive exhibits and lots of photo opportunities.  I think for f wax museum they do as good a job as you can hope for!

This was a different experience for us but we really enjoyed it.  Once we arrived, the staff welcomed us aboard and were we surprised.  They had a lunch buffet that was great and a musical show that was awesome.  It was "Country" and anyone could enjoy the music and we enjoyed the musician talent and music while on the showboat.  One significant part of the trip while riding up and down the Cumberland River was you can go outside and see it while riding.
Lovely place with great music . The food wasn't all that but the entertainment was great  . Service takes a little too long to come around but the atmosphere was good .
Didn't have any food here but the drinks were cold and the staff was friendly. The music was awesome and the energy was contagious. Will definitely come back here again.

Well...this wax museum figures now feels like NashVegas! My first time in a wax museum. I was kinda freak out how real some of them looked, but really good art work. I had lots of fun taking pictures and acting on like they are real people. I guess this is the closes I will be to the stars if I can't see them in real life. It is Nashville! So expect to see country music stars. They have other souls and PoP singers, not just country music stars.
Coming on a weekday we were the only ones inside and took our time. I think this place should be visited at least once if you haven't been in to see celebrities in wax figures. 
Bought our tickets on Groupon for $12. Most definitely cheaper cost verse paying full price at the desk. Been to Vegas a few times but never wanted to pay full price for the entrance. 
Things to do in Nashville this is the spot for me and my girlfriends on a rainy day. It was awesome and fun. Location inside Opry Mills mall made it convince. Cause I got to walk around the mall and shop!

We walked onto broadway street and were immediately met with the masses of people and music. We chose Kid Rock's because it had the most outside seating. The inside had a band playing on the stairs which kept everyone pumped up. We ordered drinks and listened for a bit then went upstairs to check the rooftop out. Do not miss out on this! There was a separate band playing upstairs and it was mostly rock, so perfect if you want a break from the country. Will be back the music was great the food options just weren't that great.

3.5 STARS - A SATURDAY NIGHT EVENT IN SEPTEMBER

PARKING - I found a spot on the street at the corner between LRC and the parking lot super close by!! BUT - you should know that I'm pretty sure valet is only $5, so that's pretty cool!!

TICKETS - I was invited by a friend that paid for the ticket so I'm not sure if they got several ahead of time so I don't know how expensive they are or how hard they are to come by.

MUSIC - It was a cool alternating type panel, there were 4 artists and they all took turns playing their original songs and building each other up, and filling in for each other if they thought a guitar part would go good with the keys etc. Loved it! I was bummed they didn't have any of their personal cd's for sale, I think the group I was with really was looking forward to supporting them in that way!  The artists were all super friendly and stuck around after the show to chat with the guests, very cool.

DRINKS - I tried a cocktail first, I think it was a type of mule, my advice, SKIP IT.  It seemed really watered down - go for a glass of wine instead! Pinot Grigio. 

FOOD - Hmmm, the cheese plate and the hummus looked really good.  I was pretty hungry and got the BLTP (BLT with pimento cheese!), a first for me since moving here 3 years ago! However, I don't think I would recommend it. I'm pretty picky and the bacon seemed fatty and chewy and I think the tomatoes were fried green tomatoes.  I ended up just putting the pimento cheese on the texas toast and just having that as is, skipping the B, L, and FGT fried green tomatoes.

SERVICE - We had a male server (will leave him unnamed).  He didn't seem that friendly and I feel like he was patronizing if we didn't name a meal or drink exactly as it was listed on the menu.  If I could have chosen a different waitstaff member, I think it would have been a 5-star experience.

Either way, I would say it's definitely worth checking out! 
Enjoy!

We had free tickets to the wax museum so took advantage of the opportunity. If it wasn't for the tickets this place is actually pretty expensive for the size of it. Barely takes 45 minutes to an hour to go through.
That's sad, we did have a very good time. All of the displays are interactive and you can get right beside them clothes for photo opportunities. Everything from Albert, to Carrie underwood, and a Blue's room. 
Here is a tip. We got a ticket from old town trolley. They were running a promotion that included the last museum. Might be worth checking it out.

My favorite venue in Nashville. They have a huge variety of music, and consistently feature up-and-coming artists you'll be seeing in an arena in a few years. They truly have something for everyone, and are one of the few indie venues not afraid to venture from the generic hipster crowd and feature country music.

I went here for lunch today and I unfortunately had a bad food experience. The salad was wilted with signs of frost damage and the American Burger came out undercooked (the meat was of the consistency of raw beef - you could mold it like play dough). My friend's salmon burger was meh. The sweet potato fries were very salty and did not taste fresh. However, the company redeemed themselves when the manager/owner took my meal off of the bill and was very apologetic. He also offered to bring me a different meal in place of the one I ordered. Very good customer service!

Since I live in Jersey I won't get the chance to give this place another shot anytime soon but I can only hope that this was just a fluke thing and that the food is normally a lot better.

For $15 / person, I expected this museum to be a lot bigger than it was.  I really enjoyed it but it was definitely overpriced.  I spent time reading most things and watched the majority of the first video highlighting Cash's acting career and we were still in and out in about 90 minutes.  I'm happy I got to go while we were in town; however, if I visit Nashville again, I will not be going back here.  Once was enough.

The onion rings and chicken nachos were excellent.  This bar isn't for the up tight, needy or picky. This bar is your true American dive bar.  There is one or two bartender's at a time and you have to order at the bar.  It's old and nostalgic!  This is where you should go before you head downtown, pre-gamer, you won't spend a fortune but you will downtown.  It is what you make of it! I loved it

Big Bang came highly recommended from a local friend and they couldn't have been more right! 

The talent on stage is colossal - their banter is fun and witty with all the musical BANG you'd expect. We were blown away. Laughing and dancing for hours. 

Drinks are reasonably priced and it is well worth it for some Big Bang memories. Tip these guys!!
Decent food and great drinks.  Only heard live music once there but it was amazing.  I never knew a place like this could exist in Antioch.

Nick Deckard will treat you right. Even on a busy Saturday night he took care of us like we were priority #1 and makes eye contact in between tables to make sure we were taken care of. Nick has set the standard high for customer service, give this guy a raise!!!

We went on a night when there was four songwriters on the stage, each with a guitar, sitting on a stool. It was interesting to hear their songs and the stories they told about the song writing process.
The food though was sub par. We had the "brisket" which was more like shredded pot roast and the chicken wings which were rubbery and almost inedible.
The ticket price is seven (7) USD at the door, but then there is a fifteen (15) USD per person minimum for food and drink.  I suppose it is difficult to get that much food out that fast and still have quality ie: the place is empty, then fills up for a show, empties and repeats for the next show.
Skip the food, have a few drinks and enjoy the show. I think beer started at six (6) USD, and a glass of wine was about eight (8) USD.

Greeted by Andrea who was our server   Music was excellent  Food Outstanding! No wait! Early Brunch Time on Sunday! We will be back & will bring friends! Location Broadway & 4th Downtown- Just Opened!  Check it out!!!!

I found this museum to be impersonal, limited, expensive, and to have a confusing layout.

$17 - wow! I was out of the museum in an hour.

On the plus, there were some cool outfits, a guitar of Cash's, and a reel of his acting career.

I would go somewhere else first- not quite sure why everyone else loved it.

Came in because the surrounding bars were overcrowded. It was dead and my group and I wanted to grab a quick drink and have some room to breathe. We were standing at the bar and a guy who came in and went to the bathroom came back out and ran right into a girl in our group and knocked into her, both of them hitting the ground. The bar owner checked on the guy who caused the commotion. Did not say one word to our friend. After another girl in the group confronted the bar owner, he got upset and copped an attitude and sarcastically asked if she was ok. Needless to say, I now know why the bar had no inhabitants and we will not be returning or spending money on this establishment.
Very friendly, waitress was attentive and the burger was awesome! Nice, relaxing place.

The worst place in Nashville. Boyfriend and I went here for New Years 2015. We put our drinks on a table and Nick (the boss) told us to take them off. Which we did but Nick (very short manager) looked at my boyfriend and like he was going to hit him and we asked the manager what is wrong we moved the drinks and the manager Nick said your boyfriend is giving me an attitude. My boyfriend didn't say a word to this man but ok we will move our drinks. The boss kicked us out. The boss wouldn't even listen to me. If you are a manager of customer service industry wouldn't it be smart to treat your customers well? I would never treat a couple this poorly. Nick is the worst manager I have ever seen. I told everyone on the bus back to the hotel. I told them to never go there and spend your money across the street at Honky Tonk where they treat there customers with respect and understanding.
I even thanked the manager for all his time and help with understanding.
Loved this place! The bands on all 3 (open) floors were awesome! Would definitely recommend coming here

While food quality needs some improvement, I was overall pleased with the venue and seating. It's been a while since may husband and I have been to Listening Room Cafe, but we usually recommend to our of town friends and acquaintances. We'll be back soon!
Jacqueline

I've been in Nashville for 2 days and have pretty much visited every bar on Broadway and this is by far my favorite! Every bar here has great live music but this place feels like a concert. Best sound and a variety of music. Make sure to come here

Definitely worth the time even if you're a luke warm Johnny Cash fan. 
Good variety of memorabilia and videos. Not overwhelming. Glad we went first thing on a Thursday morning. It got pretty busy an hour after it opened. Good coffee place attached to it with organic coffee.
Went for brunch and had a great time! Cheap mimosas and wonderful entertainment. The performers were fantastic and the second showing at 1 featured multiple music genres.
Great place to go to close out the night! Bartenders were super nice. Love music was amazing. Had a great time dancing and goofing off with my friends!

Our experience at Madame Tussauds was hilarious! We had the entire museum to ourselves on a Sunday afternoon so we got to be as loud and goofy and obnoxious as we wanted! The admission was $20 since we bought them ahead of time online and to be honest, I don't think I would have paid much more than that. There were several figures with lots of different rooms and themes but I felt like it was on the smaller side compared to other MT locations. Some of the figures were also hard to recognize without looking at their name tag. Overall a fun experience if you're in the Opryland area of Nashville!

The only thing I can rate my experience with Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row is the lack of an experience that I had. We stopped in last Friday and shuffled around making our way upstairs to find quite a few open tables that were all still dirty. Thinking a rush just cleared we took a seat at a dirty table where a waitress promptly dropped off four waters and never returned to take our drink order or wipe down the table. I could understand if they were busy but there were plenty of employees standing around. After waiting around for about 15 minutes we finally just walked out. At least we were able to rehydrate and catch a few minutes of a live set before moving on.
Great environment, a little more low-key than Broadway.  Good drinks, good tunes, friendly folk..highly recommended..Oh btw grab a PBR
Great music bar. Had a really good time. Is named after my best friends brother. Hahaha

5 stars for a honkey Tonkin' good time! Thank you WR for having a big stage where the musicians can really let loose.... And lots of TVs to follow the Preds and college football. 
This is one of the new players on the Broadway scene, but they are here to stay! 
As a local, I would personally advise skipping the smaller/older stops on Broadway and opt for a more updated experience like this one at Whiskey Row!

Amazing hospitality! My waitress (Kate) was super sweet and despite being busy always made sure to check back with us in a timely manner. We even had a manager (John David) who was very attentive to us and came by a couple times to check on us as well and we were very impressed to see him bussing tables to help out all the waitresses. We had the Southern Fries- delicious! - and really enjoyed the atmosphere!! As a Nashville local that typically steers clear of Broadway, I'm happy to say I'll definitely be back!!

Great spot for a nice appetizer & drinks with a nice view overlooking Nashville. Service was good & their food was even better. Nice to see a big name take pride in their food operations as this seems less common in downtown Nashville. I don't even know who the fuck Dierks Bentley is but I'd recommend this rooftop spot. Top 5 rooftops & would rate higher if you're hungry...God Bless
Lovely place to listen to very talented folks in a quiet setting. Service is great. We made a bad choice in the deviled eggs - but the drinks were good.

I am beyond excited to be spending my NYE here! The outside looks absolutely amazing and I can already tell the inside is going to look even better! This will be the second Whiskey Row location I've been to and if it's anything like my last experience then I am definitely in for a fun time!! Bring on the whiskey!!!!!!

Amazing collection, very well displayed!
Even if you are not a big fan, you will find this museum interesting and well worth a visit.
Awesome venue, great music!!! Smoked Tennessee brisket for $32.00!!! Severed like pulled pork, no smoke, completely overpriced!!

I've been here several times and have left feeling less than impressed the last few visits. Overall, the atmosphere is great -- wide open room, rustic finishes, live music and the ability to accommodate large parties. 

As for the waitstaff, I can vouch for the other reviews here when I say service takes forever. After sitting at our table for about 20 minutes this morning, we had to walk up to the bar to let the staff know we hadn't been given menus/been greeted. Puzzling, since it wasn't crowded. I made the mistake of going there hungry - it took close to an hour before we were given our plates for the buffet. Side note on the buffet: pretty basic, and not replenished from the time we got our table to when we got our plates. Except the bacon was bangin' - but can bacon ever really be bad? 

The bottomless mimosas always seem like a great idea, but take forever to be refilled, so I'm not sure it makes much sense to go that route - they're small glasses and you end up averaging about 2-3. The menus were printed on computer paper with a printer that was clearly running out of ink, as some lines couldn't be read. Nit picky comment, but I'm taking the time to leave this review so I figured I'd throw in all of the deets. There's a chance I may be back in the somewhat distant future, but not with the highest of expectations.

Heads up to Listening Room management: you've got great potential as a business, but it's time to take some pride in your service and presentation.

Absolutely fantastic.  You don't get this kind of vibe many places.  Live music, southern food, full bar, lively crowd.

Took my daughter on a Saturday.  Reservations are important; a full restaurant, every table with a great view of the stage.  Four acoustic singer/songwriters sharing the stage, taking turns playing their songs and backing each other up.  Selling CDs from their instrument cases.

Food was very good.  4 stars for the food.  Fancy burgers, deep fried pickles, smoked pork chops.  They had lots of other southern food and BBQ on the menu.  Lots of beer choices.

I'd give the overall experience 6 stars if I could, so the whole thing gets 5 stars.  We will be back!

Ended up paying full price for the excursion since Groupon only had so many to offer.
It was costly but we all really enjoyed it. The food, the entertainment and the waiters were all awesome. Loved seeing the Nashville skyline from the water.
I would definitely suggest this to everyone before but now I've changed my rating.
My husband had worn his new Steeler's hat there and left it at the table when we left. We were notified via Facebook that a member of the staff was sent out to take it to us. Apparently they must had liked it more than us and kept it.  I feel the management should replace it. I was promised more than once, that I would get a call back and they would take care of the matter and of course nothing.
Like the good old saying says take the money and run and I guess that's what they did.

such a beautiful experience, this is a must if you visit Nashville.. you can feel the history here, the museum is laid out well and the staff is super friendly.. if you are a music fan you will love this place! you can even mix a few tracks while you see the exhibits.
Who doesn't love Johnny Cash? There was a ton of cool artifacts and memorabilia squeezed into a short self guided tour. Check online for ticket deals and take time to watch the videos,

Extremely cheesy and not the best thing to do in Nashville unless you are 65+. They had good voices but it just didn't feel like Nashville however had great views from the boat.  Just feel as if there are much better things to do with your time and money.

Only came for the music but omg this place is huge! Great place to party all day every day. This place was always rocking every time I passed by with the greatest artists. I wish they displayed the artists names and helped them promote a little more. Walked in on a busy Friday night and got a drink within 5min. It was great! The bartender girls had great black light neon clothing. 

The only place that opened the windows and didn't suffocate you with heaters on full blast. It was a good time on a chilly night. Can't wait to come back and try the food.

Went here on a groupon which was a great deal! Two for one admission! This is a must see for anyone who is a Johnny Cash fan or a fan of real country music (none of that Florida Georgia mumbo jumbo). I definitely want to go back because I'm sure you pick up on different things each time. The only thing that was a little weird for me was the whole 'take your picture with Johnny Cash on a green screen thing.' That's weird. And I'm in favor of that going away. But everything else is wonderful.

Best waffles this side of Belgium! Seriously, they are amazing. They come with a dark chocolate whipped cream and chile syrup. And the waffles have the perfect density: kind of light. Hard to describe. Just go there and try one. Their take on biscuits and gravy is also brilliant! Small menu, but so creative. I love this place.
Cool new multilevel place.  Nice rooftop area overlooking Broadway with gas fire pit tables. We didn't eat here, so can't comment on the food. But has a fun vibe.

This is my second visit to the Listening Room. I have to say it is a hidden gem in our city! I like to come and have a drink and small plates with buddies and now I will make a return visit for Brunch! Our server is awesome and wehave had a great start to our Sunday here.

Friday night I experienced something I have NEVER had to deal with as a customer- and as such, I didn't tip the person that serviced me- something I've never done. I bartend at a country club in Nashville, so trust me- I get that the service industry is HARD. However, I ordered a "grapefruit vodka with club" (notice the lack of comma) from a platinum blonde bar-tender at the downstairs bar in front of the band. I saw her start to pour well vodka and get out the grapefruit juice to add to my drink, to which I kindly corrected her that I didn't want a "vodka grapefruit" but instead a grapefruit flavored vodka with club. No big deal- people make mistakes- it's loud- maybe she didn't hear me. Her response? An EVIL stare as she said "well...?!" I responded, "I'd like to get what I asked for." She then THREW the plastic cup into the trash can behind her with the attitude of a spoiled 5-year old that gets stripped of their iPad mid car ride. Eventually, she made the drink I ordered and handed me my receipt. Then another guest at the bar standing next to me looked at me and said: "Isn't she just evil?." I simply walked away- shocked at what had happened. 
However, what REALLY got to me was the next night I met up with friends and they happened to be having their after wedding party on the rooftop of this place. Before meeting up with them on the rooftop, I tried to get a drink at the same bar- the downstairs one directly in front of the band. I saw the same blonde bartender as Friday night and chose to just attempt to get a drink from a different bartender instead. However, after several attempts, I was completely ignored by the male bartender also behind that same bar. It was a busy Saturday night on Memorial Day weekend, so maybe he simply just didn't see me. But, of course, you can assume the bad taste this experience left in my mouth especially given what happened Friday night. 
People make mistakes and it's a pain to get your manager to comp drinks at the end of the night when you're tired and just want to go home. Also, the customer isn't always right- maybe I said my drink order too quietly for her to hear. Nonetheless, what's unacceptable to me is a bad attitude and making me feel like an idiot for simply asking for what I ordered. Overall, just really disappointed.

Note that this review is primarily judging this place as a music venue. This was my first proper visit to Nashville and I wanted to catch a songwriters "in the round" session. I was easily able to get tickets online for the show and dinner. I would recommend doing the same to avoid waiting in line or possibly being turned away if there are no seats left.

We attended the regular Tuesday evening "in the round" series called The Movement. There were four artists in the 8:30 PM set and another four in the 9:30 PM set. Each artist played a song "in the round" before starting a new round of songs. Sometimes the artists would perform together on a piece. Sometimes this was planned and sometimes an artist just jumped in to provide some spontaneous accompaniment. It was a really fun experience that I highly recommend checking out. Be sure to stay for both sets!

As a side note, we did have drinks (a margarita and a knockoff of an old fashioned) and some side dishes (mac and cheese and mashed potatoes) during the show. Nothing was particularly noteworthy, but as we were both hungry and in need of some libations, they did the trick.

The Listening Room has a cool location and the interior is really cool! Go to hear music and have a drink or three...i would suggest avoiding the food. I got shrimp and grits and I LOVE shrimp and grits. The version I got here, were a few shrimp swimming in a tasteless sea of soupy grits. The musical acts, the night we went, were hit or miss. I will go back and see if it was just an off night for the place. It seems to have a lot going for it...maybe I just went at a bad time.

The only reason this restaurant has 3 stars for me is because the ladies singing were amazing! If I were to return, it would be strictly for the performers. Other than that, the service was terrible and the food wasn't amazing, it was just okay and overpriced. They do have buy one get one mimosas and they were pretty good. 21% Gratuity is added if there are more than 6 people in the group. Since we had such bad service, I was irritated that I had to pay 21%. If it weren't for the service and having to pay 21% of the bill to the server, I would have probably left in a much better mood.

Every time my wife and I are in Nashville, we stop by the Listening Room for dinner, drinks, and live singer songwriter music.

When in Music City... you've gotta seek out live music. Our preference is for acoustic guitar with a single voice. It is here where you find those with stars in their eyes looking for their big break hoping the song they wrote for (insert county singer name here) will be picked up and transformed from graphite in paper into esteem and fortune.

Do yourself a favor and make a reservation for a night at TLR. This will help you determine which singers you want to see, on which night, and help ensure you get a spot close to the stage. 

We always enjoy the food and the mixed drinks but the real highlight is the local talent, which is simply oozing out of every crevice of this city.

I'd give it two but the guy at the door was really nice guy!
My buds ordered Coronas and I ordered a Bloody Mary.
The Coronas turned out to be a safe bet! Not just cause they're cold frosty and consistent but aft two sips of my Bloody Mary I got the cold consistent eye roll and "what's wrong with you?" Attitude from the bartender girl and her fellow bartender! 
When I commented about all the "stuff" in the Bloody Mary (mushroom, olive, onion, green beans, a pickle, and s strip of over cooked dried out bacon strip! When I questioned the server, her response was "what do you want me to do about it?" I told her simp it out! She rolled her eyes in disgust and then picked it up with out looking away and dumped it in the trash! Like "how's that!" Them proceeded to tell me how people come there for the bloody Mary's and they don't use artificial premise mixes - my advice - lose the server and your own mix!
I was so disappointed because I heard it was Owens's by George Strait and I'm a huge fan! My advice is to make the door guy a manager and get rid of the rude bartenders!the place has a weird vibe - don't waste your time
Warm bottles of beer. If you are in your 20s you are probably ok but if you are in your 50s, expect to be ignored and served very last.  Would not recommend.

If you are in Nashville, this should be on your list of things to experience. We are not country music fan. But we still enjoyed the night. Ended up staying for back to back shows. Great talent on both shows. This isn't the loud honky tonk music you experience downtown. It felt classier and very enjoyable. Entry is usually $5-10 per person and $10 minimum on food and drinks. Food and drinks are reasonably priced and decent. Recommend this place.
This was one of my favorite spots on Broadway.  Massive bar with multiple floors, bands and a big rooftop.  There's an elevator in the back if the walking gets old, but be prepared to wait.
Great music and service. Different singers on every floor. Clean and nice and cool with big ass fans during the summer heat. Had brunch her and drinks the night before. Good atmosphere.

So, first of all, I have been there twice, and have had 2 different experiences.  The first time was very good - both the venue and the food.  The word must have gotten out, and the second time we went (July 2019) the place was packed.  And...that is what this review is about.

The music was great.  If you have not been, they have song-writers who sing their own music.  Some of it is largely unknown, but some has been recorded by major artists.  That part was great both times.

They cram the tables together, and the place was jam-packed.  The service was the opposite of good - with drink and food orders taking fuh-ever to get out there.  And, the food was not great either.  My wife had a chicken something-or-other that she said tasted good.  I had the brisket sandwich.  It was tough and cut into slabs.  There were ribbons of fat or gristle running through it.  It was relatively tasteless, even though it was advertised as a special rub and smoked until tender, blah, blah, blah.  You will see you waiter to take you order, and then when they want to be paid.

I sent a comment in to the Listening Room through their website.  They never responded.  It's a business.  I get that.  Like an airline, they are going to cram as many paying customers in as they can.  My personal opinion (and it pains me to say it) is that they grew until they broke.  

Nevertheless, the music was good.  Next time I will order a hamburger or something simple for them.

It's difficult to overstate the appeal & importance of Johnny Cash to country music.  Like all performers, he had ups & downs through the course of his long career, but his legacy is a powerful & lasting one, to which this museum is a fitting memorial.

Which of course means that as it's located centrally in downtown Nashville, it's also a rather crowded one.  I was in town recently for the weekend to see Paul Simon perform at the Ryman Auditorium & never having been to Nashville before, wanted to experience the best of the city.  I figured this was part of it & made a point of including it on my list.  I allowed myself a little more than an hour to experience the full museum (a single floor, made up of some genuine content & a fair mix of "period" pieces, plenty of audio/visual material & text displays to read as you wander through the museum).  

There's a cafe & a gift shop that has a decent, albeit uninspired selection & you're allowed to take photos (no flash) & no video.  This is a must-see stop, as anyone should be aware of the Man in Black & his impact on country music.

We went to 360 Burger for the first time last night. It was an early dinner on a Sunday night, so not too many people there. Service was prompt and friendly. The place looked nice and was really clean. We got to watch the football game on the big screen. As for the food... the burgers were great. Really well seasoned. I had the mushroom swiss burger and hubby had the bleu cheese burger. The fries, on the other hand, left something to be desired. They tasted fine, but were pretty limp. I like mine crispier on the outside. When the server brought our check, she also brought us each a fresh drink in a to-go cup, which I thought was a nice touch. We'll be back!

Had 4 songwriters on stage. They all had great stories about their songs, really an awesome mix of talent. There was not a bad seat in the house. The acoustics, food, drinks were all fantastic! The brussel sprouts tho...yummiest!

As an avowed Johnny Cash fan, this place was a marvellous place to spend an hour or two. 

I particularly liked the inclusion of tablets around the place that allowed you to watch clips of Cash's best music. Just try and stop your feet from tapping along!

The little exhibit showing work from other Sun Records artists (like Elvis and Jerry Lee Lewis), was another great touch.

The museum's staff were also extremely friendly and knowledgeable. 

The only reason this didn't get 5 stars is that I would have wished the place to be slightly bigger! For someone who wasn't such a fan, it might not have seemed quite worth the $16 entry fee. Still, definitely one of the better museums that I've been to - highly recommended!

We've been to Big Bang several times over the past 6 years. Every year, it goes down another notch. The pianos have been replaced by 4 guys with 2 pianos, a drum kit, and a guitar. The spirit has been lost. The level of talent in the musicians is well below what should be acceptable. Maybe I'm not currently drunk enough, or maybe I'm just getting more cynical. Either way, I think I'm done here.

I took my father here for his birthday and he loved it!!!! Very interesting tour, I liked listening to some if the music they displayed,  and the covers done by many country singers. Definitely a place you need to see if you're in the nashville area.
Good people good time good dancing. I sure love to dance. I go out there and I dance my heart out. A lot of tears have been shed on that dance floor. ... only God knows why
Horrible horrible place. Horrible service - horrible food - and okay music. Definitely do not go.

The venue with the music artists playing acoustic guitars was great! That by itself made worth my while. The food however was poor, especially for the price. I had the salmon along with Gouda mac n cheese and brussel sprouts. Unfortunately all of it was over cooked; salmon cooked well done, sprouts scorched and the mac n cheese was dry. Just beware of what you order.

We were so excited when we found out that The Johnny Cash Museum would be opening just weeks before our trip to Nashville.  We made it the first stop and our trip and it was well worth it!

The museum is laid out nicely and takes you on a journey through Johnny's life and career.  You can tell that a lot of love and care was put in to the design of the museum and the artifacts that were chosen to display.  It was amazing to see the items from Johnny's personal life, including letters to friends and handwritten lyrics from some of his most popular songs.  There is a video you can sit down and watch about half way through the museum about Johnny's movie and TV appearances that is very informative and entertaining.

Over the past week we have been through about a dozen museums and tours in Nashville and Memphis and I have to say The Johnny Cash Museum ranks very high on our list as one of the best.  I was even impressed with the staff working in the museum.  They were very friendly and seemed genuinely happy to be working there.  The gift shop seemed to have more quality items than many of the shops we have been in on our trip.

I would definitely recommend the museum to anyone visiting Nashville!
Bartender dana had the best personality. Favorite bar we went to. Music was fantastic.

The songwriters played some major hits that we had no idea they'd written. It's a great atmosphere where you can make friends and casually chat whilst listening to fantastic acoustic talent. The food was fairly average and the drinks were light on alcohol. What really made our night was our fantastic waiter Trent! He was always hustling to ensure we had everything we needed. Totally worth a 25% tip! When we go back, we definitely want to be in his section!

Had a great time with friends! We only did drinks, a little bit of pizza, and listened to music so my review is from that standpoint. I'd say 5 star fun except for a waitress (who never actually waited on us) tripped and spilled beer all over me and continued to spill it on me as she was apologizing! My pants were thoroughly soaked and I mean soaked from top to bottom. She gave me like 2 napkins and I had to ask her again for more at which time I made the mistake of touching the small of her back while making the request.  She gave me attitude and then departed after which I think a manager returned with a roll of paper towels (thanks). Perhaps she was just having a tough night. She did give my group 1 round of drinks as a gesture of consideration (thanks). Overall I give the place a 5. 5 for an outstanding venue of talent taking away points for a poor experience with wait staff, adding back some points for my expectation that people are human, her act of consideration, help from the manager, and my belief that occasionally even the best of people have acccidents and an off night. My advice is to stay out of the spill zone. LOL. All said we had a great time and I would highly recommend a visit.

Even if you're not a huge Johnny Cash fan, this museum is an interesting place to visit. Lots of costumes and memorabilia presented alongside the chronological history of his music career. All the displays were well done and informative. Can easily see the whole museum in an hour.

This place was pretty cool. It was my first time visiting a wax museum so I have nothing to compare it to. Costumer service was good, I got som really good pictures. My favorite was the Elvis and Jonny Cash exhibit. The pictures I took look like real people. Five stars.

This was my second Madame Tussaud's visit. The one in DC was more my speed. Felt more... authentic? This one is located at Opry Mills mall. If you buy tickets ahead of time online you save $5. You'll want to do that considering what they charge for what you get. Wax figures are cool to look at but slow your pace down or you'll be finished very quickly. You'll find all your beloved country stars here- Taylor Swift (yes, she started as a country gal), Patsy Cline, Elvis, Reba, Eric Church, Tim McGraw, Kid Rick.. the list goes on. They have a small "pop" room including Justin Timberlake and Queen Bey. Fun place for the kids. Plenty of parking in the mall parking lot. Walk over to the Grand Ole Opry after!

This was the first wax museum visit for my daughter and I. We had a blast of course she's too young to know the older artists so I had to educate her a little. She was creeped out at first by his real they looked but she was taking pics with them half way through. I bought tickets online and the price was just right for me and we totally thought about going back on our way out to leave the mall. I will definitely be taking her back soon

First of all, I love Johnny Cash. The story. The history. The trials. The music. 
The museum was everything I expected. Love the time line of his career and the old photos. The wall of his hits and recordings was amazing. 
If you take the time to appreciate everything it will take a coupe hours here. Lots of neat artifacts and photos. If you like Johnny Cash be sure to stop.

Great experience. Beautiful venue. I went in not knowing the artists and was so pleasantly surprised. I also was not a huge country music fan, but left loving it. Great beer selection. Food seemed good. My only advice would be to buy tickets together if going in a group (as opposed to everyone buying their own) so that they make sure to have a table for the full party. Also, get there early if you care about getting good seats. We were 15 minutes early and sat on the side.

The Johnny Cash Museum was way cooler than I expected and much more interesting to me than was the Country Music Hall of Fame.  Steep entrance fee for such a small space, but they have a AAA discount that helps just a smidge.

Today is the first time I visited the Johnny Cash Museum Store. 
( The Johnny Cash Museum opens Spring 2013 ) 

Even though the store is small it makes a strong impact. This shop is not like any other in the downtown area and it's worth the trip. 

The Johnny Cash Museum Store is beautifully designed using the original brick walls, rich dark woods, glass showcases with a few pieces of memorabilia and beautiful artwork. TV monitors on the walls show Johnny Cash footage from the 50's and throughout his amazing 50 year career.  

The merchandise is tasteful. I picked up a couple of CASH coffee cups and a couple of t-shirts. They sell glassware, hoodies, T-shirts, bags, CD's and many other items paying tribute to The Man In Black and Sun Records.  

One case has gorgeous jewelry designed and made by Tara Cash ( Johnny's youngest daughter ). She uses authentic crystals, silver, copper and other high quality materials yet her prices are very reasonable. You can get a "guitar pick" made of silver with "CASH", "Pickin' Time" and other phrases or a stunning pair of crystal and
hammered brass earrings or a crystal necklace. The variety is always changing.

The prices are reasonable throughout and the atmosphere is nice listening to Johnny Cash while browsing. 

I'm anxious for the Museum to open. It's going to be first class all the way.

It is a fun time place.  I have been to other dueling piano bars and this one wasn't the best I've seen.

My recommendation is to stick to the other bars in the area the music and entertainment is much better.

So, my review has me wondering if I visited the same bar as other recent reviews. I wanted to share with my friend a quintessential Nashville experience. And we got that and more at Dierks. I was surprised by the size of the crowd on a Thursday night and the band performing was awesome. We were greeted at the door by Erin. She welcomed us and made us feel like VIP's... she told us that if we needed anything she would take care of us. Great start to the evening!!

After checking the place out, I approached the bar and asked about getting a table. I was greeted by Hailey (sp) and she immediately came from behind the bar, welcomed us and found us a table. I later found out through our server that she was one of the managers. 

Our server was amazing and cute (she was from Georgia) and watched over us as we moved through our appetizers and meal. She also introduced us to one of the bar tenders (Mallory) who guided us through the Whiskey selection and  gave us really great recommendations. Service and food was excellent.

The reason for my 5 stars is that we felt like everyone there was trying to make sure we had an awesome experience. I will return... often.
Awesome atmosphere, music, and cocktails!!  We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves!  Jake was the best server we have ever had!
Great atmosphere & lovely employees! The food is wonderful & is definitely one of the top places to visit in Nashville !

A terrific restaurant!  A friend told me about 360 Burger so we decided to give it a try this afternoon and were pleasantly surprised with the entire experience!  For the namesake we decided to eat burgers but the entire menu offered a great variety of seafood, salads, hot chicken, burgers and homemade desserts.  

We started off with fried eggplant and a couple of draft beers, Blue Moon and Jackalope as we waited on our burgers - cilantro avocado and margherita burger with sides of sweet potato fries and french fries that included tangy aioli for dipping.  These stuffed gourmet burgers were excellent with quality ingredients from the local farmers and growers. 

The staff was very attentive and the atmosphere was relaxed and welcoming with a stage set-up for live nighttime music.  I invite you to visit their website and drop by the 360 Burger soon.  It is quickly becoming very popular and now I understand why it is one more successful restaurant presented by the Swett family.  

The Antioch area is thriving with a very active housing market, new businesses, green space, and future projects being solidified for the upcoming next few years.  The 360 Burger is one more attractive option to eat while on the southeast side of town.

My advice is to go for the music, NOT the food. And I mean skip everything on the menu entirely, even the drinks which are awful. You are only safe with beer. It is a good place to literally go and listen only to music. (No talking!) Which can be hard to do if you are on a date or with a group. 

I ordered a brisket sandwich that I planned to share with someone. The meat was so dry and hard (as in days old or sitting under a heat lamp too long) that I could not cut it. It was inedible. I was with 7 other people and they all had the same experience. Every single one of us left hungry. (And it isn't cheap!)

On top of that, the service was odd. They were having us essentially serve ourselves by standing at the end of the table and passing things down, pointing to who we should deliver it to. This went for the food and drinks. Then at the end we were helping them bus our table, asking us to pile dishes on top of the tray already started. Just not normal. Very low class. The server was in such a hurry to get us out of the room after the show ended that he knocked over a full drink over that spilled onto several people. 

So if are a looking for a place to sit in silence and listen to some great up-and-coming artists, you won't be as disappointed as we were. Just don't show up hungry!  Not to mention that there are MANY other places to listen to good music in Nashville. Do your homework. Skip this place if you can.

I have had multiple burgers from this place. They have all been great. The meat is fresh and cooked very well. Love that you can choose your type of bun. They have amazing onion rings and different fries. The price is pretty good for the amount of food you get. I have also eater their chicken sandwiches and they are normally large breast and well prepared. The only item that I have not liked are the wings. The first time I got them they were good, but the last few times they have been small, no flavor, and little to no sauce. The staff is great as well. I recommend them to a lot of people. I wish they were in a different location to get more people to try them.

This was a nice museum chock full of memorabilia put together to tell the story of Cash's life.  We went on Saturday and the museum was packed, wall to wall, which made it difficult to see things and the layout was initially a little disorienting.  One of my favorite parts was seeing the stone wall from his house (that sounds boring, but seeing pictures of it and reading about the history, I found it surprisingly moving.)  I also liked the multimedia interactive exhibits.  Also, I didn't realize he was a visual artist!  I would have loved to have seen more examples of his visual art. 

If you are a casual Johnny Cash fan, I still think you'd enjoy the museum... but try to go during the week when it is less busy.
What a wonderful way to spend on a quick Nashville outing!! I thoroughly enjoyed his work and how the museum detailed his entire life!

I think previous raters are giving higher stars simply because they want the place to survive, but this place deserves nothing higher than 1-2 stars.  You think it's going to be a great place with the awesome and tasty grass-fed beef and interesting burger stylings, but they miss the mark on just about everything.  We had been once before and it was decent.  Food took a bit long but we figured it was because it was new.  The burger was completely overcooked but thankfully the meat was good so it saved it.  We decided to come back a second time to specify how we'd like the burger cooked because we felt it would save it.  Started off well and the server even asked how we'd like the burger cooked.  It was us and about 5 other people in the entire restaurant.  45 minutes later our food still had not arrived.  Meanwhile, we can see directly into the kitchen and it was not a pleasant site.  Note to 360 Burger, if you have your kitchen visible to the consumers, make sure your cooks are kind, presentable, and actually cooking things!!!!  There was one cook, not rushing to get anything done, simply taking his time.  Then two other cooks show up but only distract the first and eat food they find back in the kitchen.  We also got the pleasure of seeing this cook mouth off to the waitress when she picked up someone's food.  That was lovely.  But the icing on the cake, the very reason we left, was when our food FINALLY showed up on the line (over 50 minutes waiting for 2 burgers and fries) our server can't be found.  She's outside talking to friends!  2 minutes of our food dying on the pass, we got up and left.  We'd already waited nearly an hour and I'm not going to wait for our server to take her sweet time chatting it up with her friends.  Sorry 360 Burger.  We really wanted you to survive, but you can't treat customers like this and expect them to come back.
Nashville's best place for live music!  Every genre and every kind of vibe you are in search of.

This show was amazing! The food was delish! I really enjoyed this boat show. Dinner is served around 7, our table was pre assigned when we picked up our tickets so no need to get there super early. Cash bar.  Show does to about 9:45

Kind of tricky to get to since it's a narrow door between two other entrances. The bar is upstairs on the second floor. There was a nice patio are and the performers were okay. We requested Europe's Final Countdown, the pianist didn't kill it but it was okay.

I wish I could give zero stars. We had so much fun here until one of our friends went out to make a phone call. The 'bouncers' would not let her back in even though they just saw her come out and she said I am just making a call which one of the guys said was fine. When she went to go back in one of your bouncers physically pushed her back outside leaving her by herself in a city where she doesn't know anyone. I have never seen anything like it. Don't bother going here, there are so many fun places in Nashville.
Great food, amazing drinks, and such a fun atmosphere!! Will definitely be back soon!!!

Wow!  Best date night started with a BANG for sure. Great place, I will be bringing any and all house guests here. Just hope that one, or really any penis type song does not get requested when I bring the parents. That happened to the people next to us...ha ha awkward for them funny to us.
This piano lounge and bar is okay but they charge cover to come in here which is really devious. I think it is nice to come as a couple but in a group some people might not want to oay

I was in Nashville last week on business from Los Angeles and I needed some food and drinks. Even though the place was kind of loud, I had a great time! Shana, our server, was awesome as well! She didn't miss a beat. Thanks, Shana!! I will definitely be back when I'm in town next month. Let's get rowdy!
Woman can come in with basically nothing on, men have cutoff sleeve shirt and stopped at the door. Could not get in without buying a shirt. What BS

I have been to many burger places in Nashville, but 360 is worth going again n again. Can you imagine Happy Hour everyday till 10 pm , you can't get that anywhere in Nashville. Its in Antioch so not too much crowded but pleasant environment with live music. They have best sweet potato fries in town comes with Garlic Aioli. Burgers come with your choice of meat, best is the Farm Boy which comes with Fried Egg and choice of bread,try Pretzel Bread . My friend likes spicy, he tried Insanity burger and  he said its best burger he had till now in Nashville. I bet you will go again n again.
Definitely try Whiskey Row when in Nashville! The bar tender, Bill, was super knowledgeable and quick to get us our drinks! Try out the Tequila Mockingbird, you won't regret it!

We went here thinking it would be decently litty and it was kind of litty i guess but i would just rather hear the music and not learn about his life. It was decently pricey also at a whopping $20. the fun facts at the end and the things wear you can hear his music were the only good parts.

What a fun venue, with the potential to be great if they would improve on their food.  The food was not good.  I would go again, and just not order food.  It would be great if they had some appetizers
That said, the talent was great, especially Nick Deleo! and it was a lot of fun

We had friends in from out of town, they knew one of the musicians who was going to be playing so we decided to make reservations. They seated us and then everything went downhill. We waited 30 minutes for someone to come take drink orders, then another 10 for them to be delivered. The so called waitress told us what the dessert specials were and it happened to be my favorite dessert so I decided to splurge and I ordered one for after my meal.
