I ordered an appetizer since all the entrees were overpriced, as in my opinion $16 for chicken fingers is way off the charts. After waiting another 45 minutes for our food, mine was way over done. Then I asked the waitress to bring my dessert, she disappeared and 40 minutes later a different waiter appeared and attempted to give me a dessert I didn't order in place of mine and informed me they were out of what I had orders. It took them 3 hours to figure this out??? I said I didn't want it and take it off my bill. The original waitress then appeared and attempted to tell me she had no idea they were out. She said a manager would come over but one never appeared and no attempt was made to make any of this horrible experience right.  There was no organization as some of the kitchen staff would bring dishes out and wonder around asking tables id the order belonged to them.. So my advice is if you want to go here, eat before you come! The service is terrible and I am almost certain it will be a long time before I visit this establishment again. It's a shame too as their old location everything was top notch, seems with this move visibility has improved while quality has declined.

My first night in Nashville, I knew this was a must see. I'm so happy we went. Great entertainment and a nice atmosphere. I was blown away by the talent, and had so much fun. It wasn't crowded at all (it was a Tuesday though)  which I prefer. It was intimate, personalized entertainment for the 12 people there. I even got up and did a Charlie Brown dance because they played it on demand. Going back tonight!! 

The location is situated between two other places. We walked into the wrong bar and asked the bartender there, where the pianos were. He flipped me off and said, 'upstairs'. I'm guessing they get that a lot... their bar had carpet and stunk like piss and booze.

Stop what you're doing right now and go to the Beast Pub.   My friend Jess Nipples and I had a great great experience here.   GET THE MAKI ROLLS.   PLEASE GOD.  They are amazing.    Be sure to smoke cigarettes and check out the view of Nashville from the balcony.

Great food! I've enjoyed everything I've tried, burgers, oysters and you have to try the bread pudding. Friendly staff and service - 360 Burger is a great addition to the neighborhood! Best food around

Five stars for the music and zero stars for the service. 

We went on Sat evening for the 6pm show.  The music was outstanding but, after our first drink, the servers largely ignored us. I nearly had to tackle the server to order a second drink - which arrived as the show was ending. 

We liked the music so much we decided to brave the servers again for Sun brunch and music. As on Sat, the music was very good but on Sun the service was even worse. We ordered "bottomless mimosas" which was basically 1 mimosa unless you could catch the server for a refill. We ordered brunch prior to the start of the show but almost 2 hours later had still not received our food. When we complained they said they would comp our brunch and then brought our brunch out in to-go containers???

In summary, great music but absolutely no service.

We were in Nashville for a week and went to the museum twice. It's amazing! Beautiful and interesting exhibits and enough interactive components to entertain the kids. It's not very big but there is enough to see and spend about two hours (without the kids asking to leave).
The ragged old flag exhibit is really cool.
The people are really friendly and the location is great, you can stroll around downtown in front of the shops and bars after the museum.
If you're a Johnny Cash fan this museum is an emotional experience. If your  not a huge fan the design and organization is enough to appreciate.
We had a fantastic time.  Got lucky and was seated front and center.  The music was great!  We had a wonderful overall experience.

Mark is by far the best bartender I have ever met! He has a great attitude and mixes great drinks! I would recommend this bar to anyone looking for great live music and amazing drinks! Order his lemon drop shot!

Great food and drinks as well as a cute venue. Had a table of 8 and the bartender took forever to come help us even though there was only 3 other people in the restaurant. Went to our table to listen to music and the server took awhile to come take our food and drink orders when we finally got food it was wrong so I had to send it back and it still came back wrong but it was 915pm so I wasn't going to send it back again. Waitress was not attentive at all but was attentive to other tables and we were required to pay a 21% tip for her terrible service because we had an 8 top table. They also have complimentary valet which is nice.
One of my favorite bars in midtown!! Love the whole gang!  Been going here for years and seen them go through a lot of changes. I recommend the blue shot, so yummy! love you guys!!!

Plain and simple review -- what's up with the 3% tech fee added to every check? Your establishment is the ONLY one I have been to on Broadway that uses this fee. The food and bands are always good but the fee, which isn't stated anywhere in the place or on the menus, will make it very difficult for me to think about returning or even recommending this place to anyone. Additionally, does Dierks himself know about this and how it can affect his name? Lastly, then becuase I tipped the waitress a little less because of the fee she comes up to me a challenges me in how much I left for a tip? Talk about rude and unethical...

Oh yeah!

This is going to be awesome, having this venue in the neighborhood.  This is too good to be true. AMPLE parking - so that will never be a problem.  Plenty to eat within walking distance.  *hint* go early, park, walk to dinner.  Perfect.

Venue: 
The Pros: large, cavernous building with a large bar on one end and a fair amount of tall tables to sit and view the band. 
Plenty of space to stand, lean, find a chair, wander. Attentive bartenders.
Good A/C system.  No problem cooling the interior.
Sound is excellent. Good acoustics.  Good sound system. 

Cons: 1 toilet for the women.
The lights behind the performers are bright, bright, bright lights that hit the audience that are sitting up close to the stage - with an almighty glare. There's no way to sit at the front tables and take photos of the performers.  
Hell, you can't even sit and watch the band because the lights are hitting you directly in the eyes.  Those need to be turned off.  There's no reason for them.

Other than that.. We enjoyed it, loved the space, loved the ambience, loved the energy. 

Welcome to the neighborhood!

3.5

It's right there in the name: come here for the music, stay for the drinks and patio after the set... you can probably skip the food. The Listening Room can give you a pretty decent night out (especially in good weather) but you have to know why you're coming and choose your experience accordingly.

As anyone who's visited can tell you, it's a cool venue. From the moment you walk in, you can feel the musical electricity. The stage is the real deal. It's not overly fancy; it's just legit. You know it when you see it. Other venues may have more cache, but the LRC is no slouch. If you're set to see a show here, be excited. Parking can be a bit of an issue but they have a (free?) valet. If Tom is working, he'll take good care of you and your vehicle.

Since it's a music venue, one would hope the drink program is up to par. It is. I came here on a Wednesday night in early autumn and was on a red ale kick. The only one I saw on draft was Fat Bottom's Ruby -- which was a-ok with me, as I'd been drinking a lot of it... but that's when I saw the rest: there were four tubs of hooch! Forget the suds. I can get that anytime. Bring on the hooch! Since I needed to be presentable (at least, that's what I told myself), I decided on the tasty but not knock-you-out Fancy Lemonade: vodka, simple syrup, lemon, soda. Very drinkable. Good for a hot day. I wanted to try the watermelon drink that had moonshine or the Blowin' Smoke drink which had whiskey but the bartender told me both were pretty strong and, again, I needed to be coherent so...

When the music's in between sets or you need to talk (don't ever talk during a performance), take your drink and hit the patio. There's not much of a view right now but once the amphitheater gets built up, you've got a game changer on your hands. The only real letdown is the food program. My Caesar salad was mealy and my portabella burger was cold & rubbery. The food would have been a rather unfortunate end to a decent evening had I not observed a woman spitting the worst game I've ever heard to a guy who couldn't care less. I thought only dudes did stuff like that. The beautiful disaster that woman brought to my life made me almost forget about the bad taste in my mouth.

Every country musician and country rock artist seems to have a bar in downtown Nashville.  Kid Rock's place is ion a great busy corner location on Broadway with multi-level seating and live music.  It's a really big place, and we saw 2 entertaining bands there on our multiple visits.  Loud, fun, informal, and a little tacky....which is what you'd expect from Kid Rock.  There is a large drink menu with something for everyone....domestic beers, craft beers, shots, cocktails, & signature drinks.  Drinks are priced comparably to other bars in the area & its a fun experience for a large group!

Yes 5 stars for a great place, a must go to Restaurant !!!
Had the blackened salmon with avocado and steamed broccoli very good but that was only a very small part of a great experience.
That two bands That I had the privileged listening to made the experience even better very friendly staff nice clean place and music.
Had a great time !

I was so excited to hear from our waiter, Travis @ Erch, about the Monday artist showcase here at 6pm. It is the Song Suffragettes- which is women of country who sing and write their own music. It was great. The happy hour 2 for 1 beers were also good! We sat on the front row and the event cost me $5 (for the beer). The food people were ordering looked good but we were just there for the music. This was a great way to hear live music that wasn't just the typical Nashville radio country. 

We came here knowing we could get a. Seat and we were also already parked downtown for the day. We had planned to go to the Bluebird but were told the wait was ridiculous and it was be so very crowded.

MUST EXPERIENCE!! Whatever you are expecting from a piano bar....they WILL EXCEED! Seriously, I'm going to do my best to use words to convey how great of a time me and my family/friends had here. I reserved two tables and it was worth every penny! Our waitress was spot on with everything! We had tables right in front of the pianos. The guys playing and singing were phenomenal.....played the drums and guitar.....I was celebrating a birthday and they were super awesome! All in all---if you're considering, it's an easy answer =go have the best time! They will take care of you!!

I was so excited to visit this bar on my trip to Nashville, as I am a fan of Dierks Bentley and country music. However, I was permitted into the bar and my boyfriend was not. My boyfriend was dressed very presentable, however due to his elastic band khaki shorts we weren't let in. We are from out of town so its not like we have so many chances to come back. Hoping I can try again tomorrow, get permitted, and leave a better review!

I really enjoyed the atmosphere.  Nice open place.  Didn't go with my children, however would totally take them.   Great venue for some unique music.  Food was good.  I would like to see a more expansive menu.
The Listening Room is a fun place to have events, or even just get together to hang out. Drinks are good, atmosphere is relaxed...it's a refreshing change of pace if you've just come from Broadway!

Came here with my Nashville friends to close out the first leg of my southern spring break tour!

It was a free show-- Song Suffragettes! 5 beautiful country singers who literally could be extras into favorite show, "Nashville". 

I got the buffalo wings (don't judge me, I'm tired of hot chicken ). Y'all it was GUUUUDD! It came within 20 minutes, and my friends got yummy looking sandwiches. 

My favorite part is the music! I'm on break from the music and it's amazing!! Each singer has their own flavor. I love their voices and how they take ordinary observations and turn it into bomb.com songs. 

Also, valet comes with the show!
This is the best looking bar on broadway.   Amazing food.  Great music!  First floor is like a honkeytonk and the second floor is like a dance club.   Killer rooftop bar.

This was one of our favorite places for the Nashville nightlife. The different floors all have a different vibe so there is something for everyone. The only downside was the nasty attitudes of the female bartenders at the rooftop bar. Not once did they say thank you or smile. I politely asked one of the girls for napkins, and I was blatantly ignored. I politely asked again and she looked straight at me and said with an attitude "I heard you" then took about 5 more mins to give me them and basically threw them at me. It's a shame that these are the people who interact with the guests and can make or break the experience. Overall I would recommend, just be prepared if you receive some attitude from the bar.
I went down, down, down in a burning ring of fire! This is a great little museum if you're a Cash fan. Some really cool interactive exhibits and lots of interesting artifacts.

This restaurant/bar is exactly what Nashville needed! Live band on the first floor was amazing! The second floor was more of a nightclub feel and we danced for hours having the best time of our lives! And then the rooftop, the view is hands down best in the city! Make sure you try their specialty drink called Tequila Mockingbird!  I'm giving this a perfect score because I will definitely be back!!!

I love the Listening Room Café! I started coming here after tickets to the Bluebird became impossible to get, and I must say that I am impressed.  It is your typical songwriters round, where songwriters perform a song and tell the story of how it came to be.  Some writers are just starting out and some have lots of hits that you will recognize.  Definitely a lot of talent at this place. Every show that I have ever been to has been awesome.  The drinks and the food are both pretty good, the only complaint is that sometimes service can be a little slow.  Overall, the Listening Room Café is a great way to spend a night in Nashville!

Lousy food.  Limited menu.  Every item had egg in it.  Server gave himself 20% tip because there was 8 of us even though he messed up the orders and made several promises that were not kept. Music was good but, everything else sucked.

Listen.  I feel horrible giving one star for anything but this was terrible.  The only thing I liked here was the music, specifically Taylor Dukes. She was phenomenal, but literally everything else was very bad.  My girlfriend ordered a beer and her glass had lip marks on it. I quietly told the bartender and asked for a new one.  I watched her pick up a different glass, hold it up to the light, and put it back to get another one.  BOTH GLASSES WERE DIRTY. No bueno!  We ordered a couple of small plate dishes.  The ravioli was OK, but really, how can you mess up fried ravioli.  The chicken tenders were so dry and cold we asked for another order but don't worry, the new plate was cold too.  After about $30 in small plates of bad food we were still hungry so we ordered two sides of mac and cheese that they basically threw on a blank white plate. Zero presentation, it looked like I went up for seconds at a potluck.  We left immediately and drank a glass of red wine to try and kill any possible foodborne illness that may have been lurking. Thanks but no thanks.

I love going to museums, but this one is extra special.  There are many types of displays and I enjoyed them all.  They have many items that were owned by Johnny Cash and a few that were owned by others who had some connection to Johnny Cash (e.g., an Autoharp that Mother Maybelle played!!!).  I also enjoyed all of the video displays that give an experience that is more unique.  One thing I really enjoyed was a small area where Johnny is projected on a flag while he says "Ragged Old Flag".  There really is something for everybody here--personal items, costumes, guitars, awards, etc.  All of the items are beautifully displayed and you can get very close to everything.  The museum is very well laid out, so it did not feel crowded at all.  It felt intimate, classy, and very respectful to the memory of the great Johnny Cash.  It exceeded my expectations and they were already pretty high!

I went with my husband who is not really a fan, while I am more at the super fan level. :)  I figured he would be trying to move me along, but he really enjoyed the museum, too.  I was surprised that I learned some new things about Johnny Cash.  I think I heard a worker say it takes most people about 45 min to go thru, but I spent at least twice that because I wanted to soak it all in.

The museum store had so many cool items!  Everything you can imagine!  T-shirts, caps, signed Johnny Cash photos, old tour books, books, I could go on and on.  The folks there could not be more friendly and helpful.  I enjoyed chatting with them.

Don't miss this great museum!  It is just off Broadway near other landmarks like the Ryman and Tootsie's.

A great place to hear music in Nashville. We saw two singer-songwriters on Saturday evening, and while only one of them really had music we liked, the whole experience was fun -- a great way to spend a few hours in Nashville (if you like music). The bar was more than adequate, and the facility tried to make sure the audience kept conversation to a minimum during the performance. We'd definitely go back.

My experience at whiskey row was not one of entire mediocrity, however 95 % of it was. To preface my complaint, my friends and I were drinking maturely and were behaving like adults. While hanging out on the second level some friends of mine had been asked to go on stage with the dj, therefore the rest of our group was gathered near the front of the stage and the "VIP" section. At some point one of my friends apparently got too close to this "paid for section" and a bouncer came over to let us know. This is an understandable action, however he did it in a physical and aggressive manner that was completely inappropriate. A female girl in our group was pushed and spoken to in a very entitled and degrading manner. I would like this to me addressed by upper management so this problem can be tended to and not happen again. Thank you.

The food is really good. Music is good. Service was great.  I got a Dierks Marq is was way too tart for me they replaced it at no charge for the Dierks lemonade which was very good.  If you just want to listen to music and eat good. Go here.
Great place, great music. Thanks Nicole for awesome service. Wishing Dierks was here!

We came down to Nashville for spring break and wandered into a lot of bars. We were about to call it a night when we met the nicest bartenders at Whiskey Row. These employees are knowledgeable, sweet, and quick. We connected well with the bartender, Bill, and he taught us SO much in the span of 2 hours. He kept us well hydrated with water when he saw our cups getting low. The atmosphere was clean, lively, and upbeat. We will probably come here again while we're here. Everything was reasonably priced and you definitely get the best quality.

Love the new spot!  Was happy to come back to Nashville and check it out.  Our bartender was so much fun.  His name was Dre, and if you happen to be there when he's working, you'll have a BLAST!  Can't wait to come back and visit again.
Top 5 places to see in Nashville and well worth the time.  Attending a corporate event with a special performance by Tommy Cash.  Lots to see in the museum.  A must see!

Been here many times -- very interesting burger menu!

I've had nothing but a great experience here every time I've visited.  The wait staff is super friendly, informative, and really seem to enjoy working here.  The food is delicious -- I've enjoyed my meal every time I've went.  As a salesman I take many prospects out for lunch, this is perfect for a laid back lunch and always pleases my clients.  Great place!

It's time for another Cafe to develop legendary live music from songwriters and aspiring singers.  Love the fact that you can get a reservation and that the seating area is large enough to handle popular artists following. Locals should support it if they continue to want local support vs. a conventioneers watering hole.
Accoustical format for the most part. Really talented folks. Best Ribs In Nashville. Bar hostess are awesome and friendly.
Great service and great scene. Two levels with live music on each floor. Came here for a bachelor party and they had plenty of booths able to sit our larger party.

Perfect way to enjoy music and dinner in Nashville! Portabello mushroom sandwich was delicious!  Limited beer choices bc they just moved so Im sure it will have more options soon. Good music and good food - perfect combination!

It is now my second time attending the Listening Room. Each time my wife and I have been, we have thoroughly enjoyed the music on stage. The biggest let down for us is the food and the service. Both times we've been, our order was messed up and our food has been cold. The fries were either crispy or rubbery. The chili had an odd taste and smell that was unpleasant. The waiting staff was also distasteful in their approach and service. 
   Our waiter this evening was quick to tell us what they did not have, mumbled, and was short with us. At the conclusion of our meal, he stared at us as I was entering in a tip on the mobile card machine. The whole transaction was a bit awkward. 
Based on our experience, I strongly recommend that you eat beforehand and choose to order drinks to cover the $15 guaranteed fee.

Update: the management didn't reply to my email. I just walked past on my way to Roberts and an African American guy wasn't allowed in as they didn't like his shorts! I told him they don't like bags for men or tank tops and we laughed sadly at this racist, homophobic and sexist bar. Avoid and cross the road.  

Wow. Only bar on Broadway to have any issues with. Only door staff who were rude and out of order. I walk in with my tiny back pack on. It's been stormy and has my Brolley in. "No back packs" I point out three women nearby with giant bags. "They are purses" I then say ok I'll take my money elsewhere. This "man" with a 80's moustache says I won't get in anywhere. I point out I've been to 5 bars today and carry on. It's like the review below. Double standards and basically sexism. Don't allow women in if they have bags or you are a sexist bar. 

I'll be avoiding like the plague now as this obviously isn't owned by people from Tennessee. As they have all been polite and nice.

I didn't think I'd like this place. I'm a pianist myself and sort of a music snob and I thought this place would be kind of hokey. I actually enjoyed it a lot! The pianists are very talented and had great personalities for this job. I was expecting to spend $20+ to get in because I'm from New York, and the piano bars in NYC are more pricey, so when I heard that it was only $6, I was thrilled. I didn't request any songs and only had one drink while there so our stay wasn't pricey at all. I really enjoyed my time at Big Bang!

One star is appropriate. Four of us went for New year's and got there around 7pm to head up to the roof. Around 10:30 they came up pushing wristbands or we couldn't stay until midnight. Not happy, but ok it's New year's. Asked about champagne toast and fireworks and was told by two different people we would get champagne and have a view for the $50 (each) wristbands.

You know what happens next. Midnight rolls around, no bubbly, fireworks behind the tall AT&T building and can't see them at all. Get our bill and find out our domestic beers were hyper expensive, even compare to LA. Extra drinks in the receipt we didn't order, but bar was packed and didn't want to wait any longer at 12:30am.

No food after 9pm, so suffered through to them pay more to just stay. Had fun for the night, but would never, ever, ever go back. 

Beware, all about the $$$ and not a trustworthy place.

Worst service EVER!!! Diana Rollins just so you know I am a super good tipper and you had multiple opportunities to do good but you choose not to!  You thought having  bigger parties would benefit you but it obviously did not!!  WOW are the only words I have for you!!!
Love this place. Make sure you make reservations ($5) online. Great talent and pretty good food!

One of the best places to see music in Nashville. Love seeing the singer/songwriters behind the hits. 
Atmosphere is great. Plenty of seating and reasonable drink prices. Plus the food is way better than the average honey tonk.

Great loud music. Very big dance floor. The DJ was average, but everyone seemed to be enjoying the music and having a good time. Our bartender also poured really strong drinks. This would be a great place if you're looking to dance. They also had a lot of tables to the side if you wanted to sit down and chill.
The food was good service good music good drinks great . A lot of fun . If you are hungry on Broadway it's a good place to go.
Food not great not much better than McDonald's!  Bathroom dirty!  Men's room smelt of urine per husband.  Staff great and music great but disappointed in rest! Get drink only there!!!
Good atmosphere and perfect venue to listen to live music with great food!

This museum in the country music capital of the world is a treat! I loved the interactive exhibits and films throughout the museum highlighting Johnny Cash's long and distinguished career. I learned a lot about his philanthropy with helping promote prison reform, his film career as well as his music. There are costumes and lots of memorabilia too. Upstairs is a separate Patsy Cline Museum. We really enjoyed this museum. The layout & the exhibits were great!

Nick deckard will take care of you, even on a busy Saturday night! This man is beyond words for service. Makes genuine eye contact between tables to make sure you are doing alright! The standards of customer service is set high by this individual, give this guy a raise !!!

This was a really solid spot.
Bingo / Arts Market / 2 for 1 drinks / outdoor patio.
I think I'd do a disservice by even trying to go into it more.
Just go here.
Great band, great fried pickles, great service!  It's a perfect place for Broadway, Nashville!!!
Great stop. Be careful about parking.  We ended up paying a small fortune ($35) to park at the lot behind the museum.  I'd allow for ~1 hour to go through, maybe 90 min.

They have the most AMAZING songwriters!!!!! They have the WORST food you will EVER eat! The cheese on the cheese plate looks like it can from a Chernobyl Nuclear Farm. Seriously if you let it sit there for five minutes it turns neon. It really bothers me because I want to give this place my money but the SIX different times I have ordered food here (I tried something different each time) I have taken one bite and stopped eating! Come on guys...it is not that hard to make decent food. This stuff is terrible! Skip the food and plan to order at least $15 worth of drinks per person (It is well worth the investment.) If the food were even a tiny bit better people would be more likely to come for more than the music and this place would be packed EVERY night. PLEASE, PLEASE, PLEASE, fix your food problem! Even the wait staff complains about it!!!!

I would recommend the food, but not the service. My party ordered burgers that were very good, however, the service did not match quality of the food. Our ID's were checked an unnecessary amount of times and they nearly broke my ID trying to see if it was a fake. And the drinks themselves being over priced and taking far too long to get to the table. Most likely will not be returning.

My friend and I were recommended to visit the listening cafe. We got tickets for the 6:00 show and arrived 5-10 minutes early to be seated for the show. We order a couple drinks and a couple appetizers. The waiter recommended the fried pickles so we ordered those. They were great! Sweet pickles with a mild kick in the ranch dip. Perfect combination! The singers (3 of them) on stage had the best voices!! They played great acoustic music that they all wrote themselves. Backing the music with stories on how they wrote each piece. It was such a wonderful experience and I'd definitely go back!
Best atmosphere and live music on Broadway!! After trying many different bars up and down the strip we found ourselves coming back here. You just can't beat it!

Yikes. As a resident of Nashville, this place is awful. And if I was a tourist, save your money and go elsewhere. We went to brunch today at 10AM. They had a "special" menu which meant no buffet and less sides. It had to be printed off twice, because when I went to order they noticed not everything had a disclaimer, so had to reprint and I had to reorder since they cut items off the menu. We sat there for an hour before anyone played on stage... which isnt that the whole concept? 

Finally the food - no flavor and terribly overpriced. My friend had the CB Slinger, which was just a salt bomb of chili and burger. They got the eggs right but the dish was convoluted mess. I had the Egg + Pulled Pork Benedict. The side of potatoes I got were the saddest looking shriveled up things that looked like that had been under a heat lamp for 3 hours. The hollandaise sauce was for a lack of better words "gloop". 

We waited 45 minutes for food. An hour for the artists to go on stage. The food was terrible. Some of the worst I have had since living in Nashville. McDonald's breakfast would've been more satisfying than what they are slopping up at The Listening Room. So many better brunches and live music spots. I'm just glad I went to this place before I took any out-of-towners... would have been embarrassed.

This was a really interesting experience and the songwriters were really talented. I wasn't sure what to expect but it's a very toned down performance where the songwriters play their songs in acoustic and discuss them. Kelly was the best of the four in my opinion. Not a lively show by any means but no real complaints about the music or songwriters talent.

I was less than pleased with the organization. Before the room opened it was a crowded push toward the doors and I could see others getting visibly frustrated especially since the show started a little late. 

The worst thing was the food. Do not eat here. We ordered wings and Mac n cheese and it all tasted like cardboard. To make matters worse, there is a $15 minimum and the wait staff was visibly overwhelmed taking food and drink orders for everyone in the room. The drinks weren't great either, I'd recommend just sticking with beer to fill your tab.

TL;DR The music was solid, but I couldn't look past the terrible food and poor organization. I will not be coming back.

I showed up without a ticket reserved just on the hopes that maybe I could get in because the musicians that were featured sounded pretty solid. They have a system where you can put your name on a wait list and then go over to their outer bar and wait and they will call you from the list if they have available seats, which was a success for me. I paid the admission and went in and sat at the bar and a had a couple beers while eating and enjoyed some great live music. Everybody was friendly, and the musicians were great. Seats about 200, and not a bad seat in the house that I could tell.
Pretty disappointed in this new bar. We decided to give it a shot and it was empty on a Saturday night. The band was kinda rude and the bathrooms were dirty. Better options on Broadway.

Love this bar. 
Love the huge stage, the sound, the bans that have been here last 4 nights, I could see myself here every night if I lived in Nashville.

2 stars for the food
5 stars for the music venue

The Listening Room is downtown Nashville's response to the Bluebird Cafe: A showcase for singer-songwriters. 

Tips:
- Tickets are cheap, so order them in advance, even if you are uncertain of your plans

- Eat before or after the show

- Although there probably isn't a bad seat in the house, Tables are assigned first-come, first served by checking in at the hostess stand, which is straight ahead as you come in the main door, so arrive early

We went to the second show on Valentine's Day. They had a special prix fixe menu, plus limited a la carte selections. Although pleasant enough, our waitress made mistakes placing our order, which, considering the price, was quite disappointing. The food is NOT the reason to patronize The Listening Room.
Great music and atmosphere! There are a few different floors and are all really amazing. The roof has heaters if it's cold out which was great.
This was a great spot. Great music. Servers and hostess were super friendly and the food was fantastic! Really enjoyed the atmosphere. Total win.

Hello I'm Johnny Cash...the Museum was packed thanks to the rain...but maybe they do want to visit the museum. It was sorta kinda difficult to navigate through the crowded aisle to fully read and enjoy all the memorabilia of Johnny Cash.

That being said, all I can share are a few pictures of the man who walked the line....the man who loves his wife June and his music.

We came in from Indianapolis for the weekend to see Nashville and hit some music shows. The first place we went was The Listening Room Cafe. The venue is very cool and the music was awesome. We listened to four song writers take turns playing the music that they have written. Far exceeded my expectations. These writers were great. My only suggestion would be on the food. There is a $15 minimum per person, I would spend that on apps and beer. The food was not so good. Besides that, it was a great experience and I know we will return.

This place is by far the best on the strip. The food, drinks, staff, and entertainment were the best in Nashville. We grabbed a quick bite and drink at the bar & then continued to walk the strip and ended up right back in there because no other place came close. By far the best place in Nashville!
Whiskey Row is one of the best bars on Broadway! Rachel was the best server and was very quick in getting drinks and making sure we had the best experience.

We planned an evening out with a group of 12 people including parents and children.  Approximately 2 months prior to our arrival, spoke with April regarding tickets for the show.  We were assured that we would have seats near the front with a two tables next to each other.  

Upon arrival, we were seated at a table near the back of the theatre.  Upon bringing the seating arrangement a to Lesley and Brian, we were told accommodations would be made (as seats in the front were already taken at this point). No accommodations were made.. no manager..  food was undercooked and soggy) and waited 20 minutes for chicken tenders after the rest of the group's food was delivered.



Art

In our opinion, this is THE place to take guests to in Nashville. We often go ourselves, but it's an exceptional place to introduce visitors to the true vibe of Nashville.  They have incredible songwriters rounds that give you an up close look at the writers behind the hit songs. You can chat with them after their shows and feel really connected to the music. You might also have the chance to meet up-and-coming artists, as well as major artists. The food is great, service is stellar, and the booking agent knows what he is doing!!! The Listening Room is a true Nashville treasure.
Love this place! Great experience to be had in Nashville--A must go if you're in town visiting. Always a great time: good food, great service, and a fun, upbeat environment.

The first time I was here they got my order wrong but they sent me home with 2 filets to make up for it. Out of this world! I couldn't wait to come back and get the filet but it wasn't as good the 2nd time. The music was great the 1st time but not so great the 2nd time. I guess it's hit-or-miss. But I'll definitely be back!

Maybe if you're a die hard Johnny Cash fan you'd like this place. We found it over priced and really not worth the time. Dark and crowded with displays faded and dusty. Many opportunities to put on head phones and listen to music clips but the thought of sharing headphones with all of the other visitors disgusted me. Better ways to spend your time and money in Nashville.

Even for $4 mimosas, I would never recommend this restaurant for brunch. They were out of hash browns at 11:45am on a Saturday. I then ordered the about the bass bowl, which the server suggested, and I was shocked when the food was brought out. It was basically a giant bowl of scrambled eggs and nothing else. No peppers. No onions. No cheese. Not even salt. I truly thought it was a joke. When I asked the server about the dish and why there was nothing in it, he kindly took it back to the kitchen. When the food returned, it was just double the amount of eggs. They just made more eggs and put it on top of the first breakfast. Still no peppers, onions, cheese, etc. Another person in the party ordered an oatmeal, which was described as having brown sugar, cream, and fresh fruit. The oatmeal arrived and there was certainly no brown sugar or cream, and there was only one strawberry sliced, sitting on top of the oatmeal. To top it all off, we asked for hot sauce and our server could not find a small dish to put it in. He brought our hot sauce in a plastic water cup. If we didn't laugh it off, it would have been a complete disaster.

As good as it gets!  I have visited the Johnny Cash Museum twice now since it's grand opening. Bill and Shannon Miller have created this heartfelt display of "The Man's" life. Starting from his childhood years in Dyess, Ar., through his personal life and entire career. Each display includes an IPad with information about the items you are viewing. The set up is high tech impressive yet easy to understand and follow. There are so many personal items of interest that provide a good look at particular times in his life....stage costumes, guitars, furniture, handwritten items, video presentations.awards and documents never before seen by the public. This is a state of the art Museum to honor a great man, music icon, devoted daddy, granddaddy , brother, uncle and friend whom his mother named J.R. Cash. A walk through this museum takes you back in time in the life of Johnny Cash. It is a MUST see! And, be ready to shop! The gift shop is classy and full of CASH goodies... Cash IS back!  Now, go see for yourself!
Bouncers wouldn't let my friends in "because their pants were too baggy". Very disrespectful.

What an amazing experience! Our bartender this evening was T, she was fantastic! We spent hours here, rather than jumping from bar to bar. She was fast and efficient. I'll recommend all of my friends and family to come see T at Kid Rocks!!

If you are visiting Nashville and want to experience the songwriter/storytelling performing on a stage, this is a great spot for that.  The sound is great, the quality of the musicians is outstanding and the experience is worth it.   Just make sure you get tickets online and get there 30 mins before the, show get a good seat.

But, I cannot give it more than a 3 star rating.  The night we went, management decided to reduce the menu to 3 appetizers and 3 entrees,  so if you had something else in mind, because you read a review with food options, you will be disappointed.   Unless you like fried pickles, chicken wings, pulled pork, salad or turkey sandwich, there is nothing else i the menu for you.   This is a bad idea, specially, when the place requires you to spend $15/person.  What was most disappointing, was the fact that after we placed our order, and half way through the performance, our waitress let us know that they had ran out of wings,, and half of the stuff on the menu!   Meaning:  they did not have anything of what we ordered left.    What?!   We do you want us to eat now???   They offered us turkey sandwiches which was the only thing available.   A $12 turkey sandwich bu the way.  This is just plain bad management and planning.   

If you end up going for the music, which I recommend, make sure you add dinner plans before or after, otherwise, you don't know if they will have enough food to feed you.  Or, plan to go to another place (there are 100s of places like this all over the city).

Terrible experience from the waitress to the food! 4 of us went in this past Sunday for a drink and lunch-place was pretty empty compared to every other bar on broadway-probably was a sign!! Ladies bathroom was absolutely disgusting-looked like it hadn't been cleaned all weekend! 
Waitress was terrible-took forever just to get a drink-we had to keep flagging her down to get refills; you could see she was just standing at the back of the bar chatting it up with other waitresses. Our food order was incorrect-since the waitress never came to table to check on us, we had to flag down the guy who brought out the food who didn't want to believe that he had brought out the wrong food out and eventually brought out the correct side dish just about when we finished the meal. Took waitress 20 minute just to get our check and then another 20 for her to bring it back!! On top of all of this-we foolishly decided we wanted to purchase t-shirts since we will be attending Seven Peaks this year in CO however was told by waitress "you can't buy any merchandise" with absolutely NO explanation! Made us upset so flagged down another waitress to ask why we couldn't buy T-shirt's and was told no hostess on site until Monday and Manager doesn't know how to use iPad to ring up merchandise-seriously??  Just ridiculous-as a huge fan of Dierks, one would think he would care how his fans are being treated and the condition in which his establishment is run-will never visit again!
Talk about amazing and life like!!  Such a neat experience!  This was one of our top favorite places we visited when in Nashville.  My kids are still talking about this place!  So much fun!!

We visited Nashville for a girls weekend and The Listening Cafe was a spontaneous, yet awesome decision. Theresa our bartender not only made sure our glasses were full, but she filled us in on the Nashville scene and who all has performed here during her time there. We watched Colby Dee perform and it was a great experience! This was a very pleasant addition to our trip and would highly recommend this as a stop on a trip to Nashville! Thanks to Theresa and the Listening Cafe for a great experience!

Great atmosphere and food. Bartenders are awesome and very attentive. Jake took care of us and made our experience vey enjoyable. He likes to have fun with his patrons and is one of the best bartenders I've encountered in my many travels. Will be going back to visit Jake again on our next two nights in Nashville.
Ashleigh in the rooftop bar is the best bartender in Nashville. Will get you anything you want and fast at it
We had great service! Our server Rachel was great and made our visit enjoyable! She was very attentive and made great suggestions on beverages. The band played a great variety of music.
Madame Tussaud's Nashville was a pretty cool experience. Tons of country music stars, pop music stars, and my personal favorite a section dedicated to The Beatles.
The Asian bouncer (Paul I think) was super friendly! My experience was better because of him! Highly recommend this place.

Food is not why you go on this showboat. However, the boat ride was fun, moving out to the Nissan Stadium area was great, and seeing the massive crowds by Broadway was unbelievable as we moored. We had no trouble getting chairs right up along the railing to be up close and personal with the fireworks over the Nissan Stadium and river, and to be able to avoid the crowds with a nice river cruise back, entertainment the whole way if you wanted it, or a nice breezy spot on the aft of the boat if you didn't (that was what we went for). Either way, as long as you go in for the experience and not the food, this will be a night to remember!

If -5 stars was an option, I'd have chosen it. The biggest pieces of trash around in terms of ownership and management. When the venue isn't good enough to survive on its own merit, why not trademark a name associated with an atmosphere and start suing other people nationwide. Great business plan there Chris. You weren't the first to come up with the idea (and have definitely executed it horribly), but why not do what "Trashville" does best and focus on commercialization rather than producing a quality product yourself. All aforementioned issues aside, the service, prices, overall ambiance of the place drastically pale in comparison to other listening rooms throughout the nation. Here's an idea: Maybe if the management team was more focused on their own success rather than the failure of others, this place might be worth coming back to. Don't waste your money folks.

An okay showboat offering. The food was good and the show was nice save for a couple off off-key moments and missed cues. But it's a new show and the performers will get better deeper into the season. The wait staff is friendly but all were language challenged and placing drink orders was a bit challenging. Also they were frequently nowhere to be found. I'd ordered the optional Hot Nashville Chicken, which is one of the spiciest things I'd eaten in a long time. And I could not get a water refill. Luckily my wife let me douse the flames with her glass. Other patrons at our table also had trouble getting drinks and getting them accurately. There's not very much scenery on the trip with industrial back lots being some of your views. Due to water levels the captain didn't take us to the downtown view and we got back early. A fact that they didn't communicate to the buses, so there was a long cold wait to leave.
Very big and exciting place.  The music was par.  We heard better in other places on broadway.  The servers were very attentive I was hoping for more from kid rock.

This is without a doubt the GREATEST music museum I've ever been to! So many great displays & things to see, so much history & interesting. Johnny Cash was a great man & this place does him & his legacy a lot of justice. It cost me about $22 to go in & I think it's worth every penny by far!
I've been to lots of music museums but this one blew me away. I can't say enough good things about it.
Stopped here on vacation with a couple of friends. Great place to take fun pictures. Wasn't as big as I thought it would be, but still had fun.

This was a great experience. You are signing up for a very touristy experience but that is what you need to do sometimes. The General Jackson is an authentic riverboat and you will sail along the banks of the Cumberland River taking in the sights and pace of life of the south. The food is good and authentically southern but it is the music the blew me away. We saw the Sunday in the South which offered up rock, country, blues, and gospel. It was amazing with anyone of the performers having the ability to headline their own shows - and I'm sure some of them do. Do yourself a favor and book some time on his boat - you will be glad that you did.

I would let Johnny Cash purr me to sleep every night if I were June. Oh, hush your judgment. Who could deny that deep voice and sad meets mysterious meets rebel demeanor? Obviously, not this girl.

On many o' Smith family road trips you'll find us taking our places with Cash songs like Daddy Sang Bass, Mama Sang Tenor, The One On The Right Is On The Left or one of my favorites, If I Were A Carpenter (and you were my lady). So it was much to my delight to find clever plays on Cash lyrics in the museum store - for instance, a bar of soap properly named: A Bar Named Sue. There were also other expected items like t-shirts (great female selection), records and the like. The space was fairly small but they somehow seemed to squeeze a custom chopper in there. Next time I'll be making my way through the museum now that I know it's only a few steps from the Las Vegas of Tennessee. 

Please note: This review is solely for the gift shop - unfortunately, I didn't get a chance to check out the museum (this time).
Just to get a picture with Johnny was worth it. Plus don't miss his rendition of 'Hurt' at the end.  Worth the read.

I came here with 8 of my good friends to celebrate a bachelorette, birthday, and anniversary. We went to order drinks at the bar and the bartender was a RACIST. It was Sunday at 730pm on June 25th. He told my wife that "she was on the wrong side of the border". WTF?! Never coming back to this place again. The drinks are terrible as well. Do not spend your money here.

Great service, waitress was outstanding, food/drinks very good, but the Merch lady was horrible. Been around people selling Merch for 20 years, including Dierks when he came to Fort Worth and she was not only rude, not helpful, acted like we were a inconvenience, we bought nothing. Unlike Luke's, Blake's, And Jason`s where we bought items. I have a friend who's friends with DB, don't think I won't pass it on! Thanks!

I'll be honest, I was a little disappointed with the museum. It was a busy weekend in Nashville so everything was pretty busy. Ok, it's Nashville, I get it. But the museum is so small and they just cram everyone in. It's a lot of reading but it was hard to get close enough to actually read the information. They did have great memorabilia like letters he wrote to his first wife, guitars, clothing, a wall from his house, etc. It was interesting and I can't blame the museum for the crowds, but was it worth the $18...I don't think so. If you're going to go, definitely shoot for a weekday.

Music was incredible!!! Loved the show!!!

There is a $15 minimum for F&B...which is ok. For the best experience...order 2 drinks after seating because you're not likely to see your server again. Eat somewhere else...we were a group of 6...all thumbs down on the food...

Great venue, great sound, amazing night. HOWEVER they wouldn't let my friend come in due to him RESEMBLING someone who is banned from the premises. I was disappointed to hear he couldn't come along to enjoy last nights show all because of a resemblance to someone else. Are you going to kick out every bearded long haired mid twenties man? There goes your demographic.

We really enjoyed our ride on the General Jackson! The staff were very friendly and extra accommodating. The music was fantastic and the cruise up river was fun. The buffet lunch was ok. The food was pretty good, not amazing.

This place was so much fun and the displays were excellent. We met Johnny Cash's brother, Tommy and the historian/curator was very friendly and suggested the best place for us to relax afterwards and listen to music with toddlers. :) If you are not a Cash fan, then you will be after visiting this museum. Spoiler alert: You might cry at the end, very touching experience.

If you are in Nashville then you must go to Dierks Bentleys Whiskey Row. Good food, good music, great service. Frankie was our server and she was the best. If I am ever back in town you know I'll be at Whiskey Row

Fun way to spend the afternoon.  We took the 2 1/2 hour midday Sunday cruise.  The buffet is ready as you board the boat.  Some reviewers have panned the food offerings, but I really don't understand why.  Maybe they were expecting individually prepared meals. It's a buffet, folks.  Enjoy.  Pulled pork BBQ, BBQ chicken, mac and cheese, beans, salads and dessert.  All very good and plenty of it.  Wait staff were as friendly as could be.  They kept our water and iced tea glasses full, which is not to be taken casually on warm days when hydration is important.  There is of course a full bar (several of them in fact) as well.  

The show starts about thirty minutes after boarding giving everyone a chance to eat.  It goes about 50 minutes.  The show itself is OK.  It's a musical revue and the performers are good, but the musical selections didn't wow us and we've certainly experienced better acoustics.  Still, it's a fun experience and we have no complaints.  If you want world class music and acoustics, go to the Ryman or the Opry House.  If you want a riverboat experience, this is the place.  One reviewer complained about the costuming.  Geez, get a life.  It's stage costuming and nothing out of line.  It's a family oriented event and no one will be corrupted by the experience.    

By the time the meal and show conclude, you've cruised down the Cumberland to downtown Nashville.  The crowd moves from the air conditioned main cabin to the outside decks to take in the views.  Lots of great pictures to be had.  Kind of fun and different was the legion of jet skiers that followed us doing jumps and other aquabatics in the wake of the big stern wheeler.  Up on the hurricane deck is more musical entertainment and another bar.  Spend the hour cruise back to dock listening to music, watching the jet ski entertainment, taking in the views, or going back into the air conditioned main cabin if the heat gets to be too much.

Go and have fun.
Originally I suspected this place to be "too big name" but found the entertainment was on points- 3 floors to choose from, good was great, customer service was friendly.  This place delivered.
Caroline is a rockstar. Service was awesome for sure. The bar manager is perfect for this place, running around all over the place and still found time to see the t

For starters Jenna is the most amazing bar tender! I was consistently and attentively attended to. My experience with Jenna made my Nashville experience. She was profession, watched out for other women's safety, and was genuinely kind. I highly recommend this bar!!!

If you are a Johnny Cash fan this is a MUST see. So many artifacts and memorabilia of Johnny Cash and his family. I loved listening to how his songs have progressed with the ages and learning more about his younger life. I think everyone I was with left learning something new and appreciative of Johnny Cash and his music. I wish the Johnny Cash kitchen was open, however it looks as though they are still working on it.

Didn't eat here but stopped in for some good music and beverages. 

John Stone band were playing on both Friday night (9.27) and Saturday midday (9.28.19). We were able to listen and enjoy them. Will stop by next time in town too!

Don't go for the food although they do have some. 
This intimate space to watch music is truly an awesome experience.  Getting to hear the music and the stories behind the songs from the song writers themselves was so amazing.  We laughed, we cried, we can't wait to go back.  If you're visiting Nashville, check this place out!

Extremely cheesy. Hard to get a drink. They had one bar open for 400 plus people after the show.  Over 30 min wait time for a drink.  Food was decent.  Show was not good. We left and went up on top. The river is great.  We asked our waitress for a drink "Mimi" and she actually told us we should go to the bar.  She was rude and hard to understand her English.  She said going to the bar was faster. She said she was too busy.  It was a buffet so what was her job?  That was from our actual server.  We still can't figure out what her job was to be at that point.  Also boat and floor was dirty.  Why can't they clean the windows and carpet?  They had tons of staff.  They do a big push for the souvenir store.  We wanted off after one hour and were stuck on the boat.  So many ways in Nashville to spend $80...To add to it they push these family pictures they print out and sell for a ridiculous price. Who doesn't have a phone to take their own pic?  Gives you an idea of their audience.
Really good food and live music with @ASeier. My husband and I had a great time!! We ordered the scramble bowls--definitely a must see in Nashville's music scene.

First time to Nashville and wandered past this place and the music was awesome! Wound up spending the rest of the night there. It's got 4 different levels with 3 different bands. We stayed downstairs at the bar because Hannah G was taking care of us and there was no way we were leaving her - she was the best!!!
Such a great time and GREAT music. For semi home bodies like me, I recommend the se one floor. Small but still get to enjoy the music and mini bar
Loud and fun place a little much for 1 in the afternoon our server Ashley was good. It's a check of the box type of place in a tourist trap street.

Pretty cool museum. There's a ton of things that were in his house that they displayed. There's headphones to listen to some of the music. Albums all over the wall and all historic information. The cost for 2 adults was a little under $45. Pricey & nothing included. You can take a picture with Johnny Cash down through digital imaging, but for an additional charge. We didn't do it, but I believe it was $20 more

They literally told us we each had to spend $25 because we were a large party (it was my friends bachelorette) and fed ALL of us drinks that had diluted alcohol. We literally couldn't taste the alc in our drinks and the shots hardly burned our throats (v telling). They ended up not making us pay the $25 because we complained. The atmosphere was cool tho !!

Overall my group & I enjoyed Losers Bar & Grill during our vacation to Nashville. We came across Losers on Saturday evening where we decided to hang out on the 3rd floor. The performers Tori Allen & Les Hall were absolutely incredible. We enjoyed them so much we decided to go back on Sunday evening to watch Les Hall perform again. We able to enjoy cocktails and food while at Losers. There was a mix up on Saturday evening with one of the individuals food but thankfully that was resolved. On Sunday there was a mix up but the bartender apologized and we were grateful to resume our nice evening. I suggest this bar to anyone stopping by Nashville and for locals. You need to see Tori Allen & Les Hall perform. We were blow away by their talent!!

Of all of the bars and restaurants our group went to this week. This was definitly the spot.  The food was excellent, the staff was wonderful, and the bar staff was hands down the best we have ever had. Bill was our bartender on a Tuesday night and the place was fairly crowded. He was able to tend to all of the patrons of the bar while answering any questions we had. He was able to give us advice on excursions and activities to enjoy while in the Nashville area and he knew a tremendous about about the drinks he was serving. We received excellent service and I can't say enough about how knowledgeable our bartender was. Would come here every night if I could.

My favorite place to go in broadway. Always GREAT, live music. Fantastic drinks worth your money, a good, crowded area up near the stage if you want to dance/sing a long, but more space and chairs in the back if you're in the mood to relax and talk. Nice staff, have never been disappointed here!

We took the dinner cruise for a business event. We enjoyed our time chatting on the top bar. Afterward we went down for dinner. The food was decent. The servers were a bit difficult to understand but we managed. After dinner we made our way out back to see the bridge and downtown, the views were beautiful. Then the show started and continued until we returned. The performers were very good and they put on a very good show. All were talented and very entertaining.

Most people drive their Bentleys here, park nearby, and then unzip their pants and enter with their Dierks hanging out.

It's weird because I only found out who Dierks Bentley and Jason Aldean were a very short time ago and now I find out that half of Broadway in Nashville is named after them.

They each have their own place on Broadway and I'm not really sure how much they have to do with it because they are pretty generic places serving up pretty generic things and I think they really just put the names on the buildings and establishments to try and generate more business from All American Tourist Dollars, and I'm sure it works because a lot of people are fans of those two guys, and those fans tend to come to Nashville and probably want to go to the places that are named after their Idols.

Whatever. If they were called Michael Jackson and George Michaels places then I might even go in there myself.
A dress code on Broadway? I'm sweating my buns off on boardway and I cant wear shorts without a belt loop?
Whiskey Row has the best service on broadway! Definitely a great place to listen to live music

Great new spot on lower Broadway.  It seems to be always busy.  They seem to get some of the best bands playing great covers from country, rock, and even mush mashed pop/hip hop infused with a country flair.  Despite being super busy the wait staff is attentive, quick and friendly.  My only negative is 1 shared men's/ women's bathroom on the bottom floor.  The line is crazy, even on a Monday afternoon.

A few thing went wrong, we had a server Alexis N who looked like she disinterested in her job.  She didn't make eye contact with her customers.  She appeared to be tired. Secondly I'm not sure what a 3% tech tax is.

The place is really small and cramped when there's a lot of people in there. Which is always.
There are some really nice items in the museum like the first guitar he bought, his first gold record that was given to him, etc. but the place is really about a lot of reading. Not enough of his old outfits, hand written letters, things like that.
A lot of pictures, which are cool but all in all, it's a lot less than you want it to be and there's no "wow" experience that would make the place shine.
His sister was there today, signing autographs for a fee and selling her CD's. Very nice woman. Enjoyed seeing everyone and answering questions. I had a brief conversation with her about their father and Johnny that was interesting.
 Not a bad little museum but I've been to a lot better.

I honestly don't know why this place only has three and a half stars. This was hands down the best place I saw in Nashville. My family and I tried to get into the bluebird cafe twice to no avail, and we found this place by chance online. We bought tickets online an hour before the show with no problem, and I am so glad we did. The food was great, but the food doesn't even matter compared to the singers. The three artists I heard were incredible, the vibe was incredible, I just loved it so much and left feeling so inspired and happy. Please, please come here. Take your friends, your family, come by yourself even, you will not be let down, I promise.
Good place to hear music talent in Nashville. However service food and cocktails poor

If I could give zero stars, I would because, based on our experience, this place doesn't even deserve one star. We ordered drinks and two appetizers and the total came out to $49 before tax and tip, and we were told the total was $60 even. With only four people in our party, the tip should not have been automatically added since that's only done for parties of 6 or more. And the service fee/ tech fee of 3% would not add up to the additional charges we had to pay. 

When we asked for an itemized receipt, our server said she couldn't do that and insisted she "wasn't overcharging" us. 

My only regret besides coming to this establishment, was not getting our servers name. I definitely would not recommend this place and would not come back.
Extremely noisy & very expensive. You'd think the staff would be a little more friendly but not so much. If you're young & a trust fund baby, this place is for you!
Can I say after the Luke's 32 bar this week bad experience, this bar is a HELL YEAH, deserves all five stars.  Great music too

Omg absolutely loved it here.  Great service.  We got stuck in rain storm and they weren't open yet.  They let us in.  Such amazing workers.  No one else on broadway opened there doors.  They gave us menu and smiled.  More people came in. Service and food was awesome. It was Thursday and they gave us the brunch menu.  Omg it was so good.  Service was impeccable wish I knew our waitresses name.  She was so sweet. Place filled u fast. Everything that came out looked very appetizing

An alternative to the Bluebird Cafe, the Listening Room offers a more spacious spot to listen to up and coming artists in Nashville. 

We enjoyed the country/folk music and stories from the four performers, with two of them standing out for their talent. They played for about 90 minutes and stayed for pictures and signing or to chat a little. The nice thing about small venues and people who don't have big heads is this personal touch. While you only pay about $5 to get in, there's a $15 food and drink minimum, which is a little hard when you don't drink. The menu items are also not too expensive. The food menu is not that extensive and nothing to write home about, though the Brussels sprouts were okay.

Amazing.   Love the music and the artifacts that were portrayed here.  Loved what he did for prison reform.  It's really small.  They bring you through his whole life here up u til his very last music video for "Hurt"

This actually is a great museum.  The cost is super high at $20 per person, and they do absolutely zero crowd control.  Very hard to stand and read the pieces when the room is packed.  I guess I would call the price a downtown Nashville factor.  They need to limit the amount of people let in every hour instead of focusing on the profit.  People will still come.. it's the Johnny Cash Museum!

Kate McGaffin is the best and sweetest waitress!! My fri new and I always have a great time at this bar and are always treated well and with efficiency when we go! High recommend checking this bar out!!

We booked the evening cruise, the first hour was on the deck and a band played for us.then,  we went downstairs where the show and dinner are being held.
The show only runs for the last hour and it was ok, not professional as the other shows I have been to. Even though we were supposed to be served steak and we got chicken, the chicken was good and the food was perfect. The service was the best thing in our experience. The boat is located just across the street from opry mills, so the parking is not an issue and if you are a guest at Gaylord opry hotel, there is a shuttle runs to the show.
My favorite bartender Jackie hooked me up with my crown apple & ginger ale!!! Made my night!!

Today was Whiskey Rows first day open. We came in from the freezing cold to a warm and lovely atmosphere. They had a great country band playing (expected when in Nashville). We drank plenty of good cold bottle beer as they do not have any draft taps. The service was great, food was even better. I highly recommend the garlic fries! So yummy!

I am appalled by the lack of compassion carried out by the employees of this establishment.  We chose this restaurant out of all the fine establishments on the Broadway strip and the way we were greeted was in a passive aggressive way being told that we were not able to enter because we had our luggage accompanying us. It then proceeded to downpour and we had no where to go, and the staff stared at us and did not let us in. This is absurd, as Nashville is a main tourist attraction.  This establishment is not a good reflection of the great man, Dierks Bentley.
Great place to hear some music and have some drinks! Not too overly priced, and the rooftop bar is awesome. Only complaint is they had a DJ up there and not the normal live music.

This place was awesome! If you don't like the music or crowd on the first floor just keep moving. The upstairs is totally different. We ordered steak and fries and it was very good! The wait for ordering was somewhat long but our waitress was pretty good after that. 
We are huge Kid Rock fans so this was on our bucket list for our first trip to Nashville.

If you are a minority DON'T go here. I was talking to a girl of a different race and suggested by the bouncers that I was making a mistake. After trying to justify my case I was kicked out due to RACISM.  Honestly 0/5 stars don't go here. They have a completely racist mentality.

Loved this place as a change of pace from the norm on Broadway!  Our three players were so damn talented going from piano to drums to bass it was scary!   Of course getting "abused" by the wait staff is part of the allure and the special hats can't be beat!  Check it out for something different in Nashville!

O. M. G. We discovered this restaurant using my smartphone and I can't wait to return! The food and ambiance were phenomenal, exceeded only by the service. Taylor our server was on the spot, anticipating our needs and meeting them. I had a new full glass of soda before the old one ran out. Simply outstanding! 

We had the 360 burger and fries. It was awesome, and justbig enough to fill you up. Not too big, not too small; and the portion of fries was generous. 

If I had any complaint or suggestion for the owners, it would be to consider music other than obscure blues. While it certainly lends character to the restaurant, it was also a little loud and distracting. Not enough to lose a star over, for sure. 

All said, we will definitely return soon!

Had a fun experience on the General Jackson. Went on a Saturday night and had a thoroughly entertaining evening. Dinner was delicious, especially for a buffet. Roast beef was cooked properly, and a good selection of sides.  Our server, George, was very attentive and added to our enjoyment of the evening. Other members of the crew took the time to talk to us about the mechanics of the paddle boat and it's navigation on the river. The trip on the water was beautiful with the bridge lights and view of downtown Nashville at night. The show was fun and total energy! So glad we chose to do this.

Yea.... this place rocks.  Great selection of music everywhere.  Ton of people everywhere at nearly all hours of the day.. friendly bartenders and bouncers (that we encountered) and reasonably priced alcohol.  Domestic beers were $6 I believe... that was the cheapest we saw of the places that we went.  If i remember... who knows, the whole weekend was a blur, but this place rocked over and over.
Small crowd.  Friendly bar.  Entertaining country band.  What else could you ask for.  I'll be back.

Great environment , great music both night we were around . We only heard rock music , so it may be a rock and roll bar which is fine . The first band we saw was fantastic , great stage presence. If you want a large spot with multiple levels and great rock music , definitely Come check it out

My wife and I took friends from New Jersey on the General Jackson Showboat for the lunch cruise and buffet and had a great experience! The meal and service was great and the live show was really entertaining. I was really pleased to discover that the grandson of Floyd Cramer was one of the entertainers and he also played the piano. He did a video tribute to his Grandfather featuring the Last Date and also played along with the video, it was great. The next time we are in Nashville we will take the cruise again as I had a fantastic time! Thanks to the entire staff of the General Jackson Showboat for the great experience. I still marvel over how the Captain and crew can turn a 300 foot paddle boat around (using an underwater turbine) in the middle of the Cumberland River with only 75 or so feet to spare. Great Value and Entertainment!

We went back to Dierks on our visit again this year. Jake still bartends and remembered us from last year, impressive memory. Once again great bartender who took great care of us and made our visit that much more enjoyable. We will be back next time on Broadway.

Maybe we caught them on a bad night or something. 
 
PROS: good  location for hotel guests. But save your money and Uber somewhere else.

CONS:

Sure its a dive bar, but the drink selection was extremely slim and there was no food. The reason we went there in first place is because it advertised food. 

My friends and I were also refused service under the excuse that my buddy had his arm around my shoulder and that I was unable to order for myself. We were perfectly coherent and clearly expressed this to the bartender. He then said that the "cops" at the bar wouldn't  take kindly to him serving us...            

The only other patrons at the bar were two very drunk women who started comparing my friends and I to their children. 

I genuinely had a terrible time here.

I would give it one star except the songwriters and music performed was an incredible experience and I would rate them 5/5 stars. The service was absolutely terrible and deserves 1 star. It took a full hour and a half to just get our drinks, and a full 2 hours to get our food which was cold upon arrival. Although we told the server the food was cold and we did not even drink our drinks (because we walked to the bar and ordered and finished 2 rounds of drinks before she brought ours) she still charged us full price + included over 20% gratuity (even though we did not see her for a full hour after ordering). The songwriters are incredible but the food and staff are very sub par.

What an awesome live music establishment! I was visiting Nashville, and was able to make it in for singer/songwriter rounds. All of the songwriters sang their original songs. There are few things I love more than live music so I had a blast! 
I wasn't very hungry so I ordered 2 sides: mac & cheese and fried okra, neither of which I loved. The okra was battered and fried while. The breading didn't tast like much, so I took it off and ate the okra plain. The mac & cheese was just ok, not very well seasoned. 
I would pribably just give 2 stars if rating on food alone, but that's not what I came for. So definitely visit and enjoy awesome musicians singing their original works!
I give this place 3 stars only because there is no place to sit...not even at the bar...or little benches against the walls...otherwise I could stay there all night and drink and listen to music

First stop at losers!  Awesome food, live country music!.  Not as noisy as the other bars, but a little quietness here and there doesn't hurt.  Had their fried catfish.  But what got to me was their fried hush puppies.  It was perfectly crispy with a touch of heat!

If you love Country music, Pop, Blues or Rock n roll this is the wax museum for you! Definitely worth the $19 (If you order online) entry fee. It's 24 if you walk up. They also have a $39 VIP package that includes a tee shirt and a VIP lanyard. 
Definitely worth the trip! Friendly staff and nice atmosphere.

We arrived as the next band was setting up and sat at the bar.  20 minutes later they came by and took all the bar stools.  We left our drinks and headed out.  Incredibly rude!  Not all of us are 21 and drinking Bud Lite. They should have at least told us that we wouldn't be able to sit there.  Also, the double standard "dress code" where men can't wear tank tops but women can wear anything.  Just not the place I want to spend my money!!

An inspiring tribute to a great artist. Displaying many unique artifacts and allowing for comparisons of different musical eras and types this museum is an incredible journey. The only lingering question I have is, who keeps that much stuff their whole life?

This cruise is unnecessarily long and drawn out. Not enough entertainment aboard to sustain long-term interest and food is disappointingly plain. The servers went around pressuring people for tips after dinner. We then wandered or sat around the boat for 1.5 hours after the show ended doing absolutely nothing. A waste of time and money.

I don't know whom is responsible but this is by far the cleanest bar in Downtown Nashville! This is the first thing that I noticed about the establishment. The staff is very friendly and the drinks come quickly. No having to wait for the barmaid or tender to flirt with someone. The music was on point as well. Over all I would have to say this is a hidden gem in downtown Nashville.

Good size venue in a prime spot on the strip. Staff is welcoming but they can get quite busy which means it can take a bit to get a drink. 
I did not eat here but the food looked ok nothing special. A bit pricey for what it is but I guess the name of the place draws the crowd so they can up-charge a bit.

Been to the Listening Room many times.  On my most recent visit they have reduced their menu to a very few items.  Very disappointing!  The drink menu is 3x's the size of the food menu.  Basically the message is you better be here to drink.  Took forever to get our drinks.  Food came out quickly but we had to ask several times for water.  My advice to you is if you are coming for a visit, eat first.  Music is great.  Getting to hear songwriters sing their songs is awesome.
By far my favorite bar on broadway. The stage setup is awesome and the sound system is rockin! Most bands have a better variety of music when compared to the rest of broadway. Service is good too.

In general, my family enjoyed our afternoon on the General Jackson.  We were lucky and got seated at Table 2 which was close to the stage for the entertainment.  Our server was attentive and friendly.  The food was standard for a buffet type setup- not bad, but not great.  The most memorable part of the meal was the pecan pie for dessert.  The entertainment was a little cheesy but the female fiddler was talented.  Overall, it was a little expensive for an average lunch/entertainment experience.  I don't regret going but I wouldn't return if I visited Nashville again.

Ive never been so mortified about a bar/restaurant in my life. I came to Nashville for my 40th bday and just wanted to have a good time, yet everyone was so aggressive and abrasive. People wanted to start fights everywhere my friends and I turned. We even gave this bar a second chance our second day in Nashville and low and behold it was the same thing. Not only do patrons get aggressive, so do the Bouncers. I accidentally bumped a bouncer while he was cleaning off our table and he got in my face. Then he tried to be aggressive toward my cousin for my bump. So inappropriate and not necessary. Then the bartender sells me $75 in beers and we get told we have to leave, unable to finish beers that were just sold do us. Don't sell beers if we aren't allowed to drink them. So disgusted and disappointed. I didn't think Dierks Bentley would approve of this reputation. I will never return.

Service was good but none of use were impressed by the food. It was good but didn't live up to the hype everyone was making it out to be.  Small little place with live music and a bar. It was ok but not amazing.

Wax figures was never my thing. This is the first time I visited any Madame Tussaud's Museum and this may not be my last!

The figures here are so realistic. I love how they were set up with the perfect spot lights. They were also staged in that exact moment that make them iconic!
