Musical theme ROCKs! Photo friendly made the experience so much fun. Pretend you are part of the crew/performers did make the experience more interactive.

Purchasing tickets from their websites would save you a few bucks. We ended up just standing at the entrance ordering the tickets while the actual ticket office was empty.....

Locate inside Orpy Mills so quite convenient as you can do some shopping after the visit too!

My wife and I were on vacation in Nashville and a friend of mine recommended the Johnny Cash Museum. So cool!

The place is on the main drag in Nashville and it was packed! We had a Groupon, so we saved some money.

It starts off with some hostory on the walls, but after experiencing it, I would almost go from the end to the front.

The best part of the museum is a station where you can listen to other bands cover Cash songs. You could spend 2 hours there if you wanted to.

They also have a cool wall with every album cover displayed. They also showed some of his theatre expositions from the 60's and 70's.

I would have loved to see a Highwaymen concert with him and Willie and Kris. A definite must see in Nashville!
A must see! I enjoyed checking out the Johnny Cash Museum. Neat displays and cool gift shop.

Really nice rooftop patio. Had both playoff hockey AND the Raptors playoff game on, so as a Canadian that was surprising and great! 

To be honest the reason for the 3 stars is because the rooftop bad legitimately sucked. All 5 members of my party agreed on this. The lead singers voice was not nearly as good as their pianist, I just wanted him to shut the hell up. They played way more rock than country (rock is my favourite) and yet the guy kept playing slow, non-party songs. Like it bummed the crowd whereas every other bar around is bumping (as were the floors below, to be fair). 

The first few floors legit had bands playing music so loudly it hurt my 25 year old ears. I never in my life thought I'd complain about music being too loud, but knowing Kid Rock I can totally see him telling the manager, "Make sure we are the loudest damn bar on the strip!" 

The food didn't look amazing - oddly it was standard bar food and not southern bbq (like every other bar on the strip). Seemed odd to be different and yet boring. My buddy actually got a beef sandwich of some sort (can't remember which one) and said he liked it, so there's that.

Very cool experience that I'd definitely recommend to anyone visiting Nashville! After researching "must dos" in the music city, I knew seeing a live show was a must. I tried to get tickets to the Bluebird Cafe but they sold out really quickly. I had read positive reviews on the Listening Room so I bought tickets. We showed up around 10 min before showtime and there was a crowd waiting at the door for it to open. Once you get to the venue, you show the front desk your tickets and they'll give you a card with an assigned table number based on your party size. I think they give out the closet tables to those who get there in line first, so try to be there 30 min before the show time. Apart from the ticket price, each person is required to spend $15 in either food or drinks inside during the show. We had dinner prior to the show, so we ordered drinks.
Cheap beer.  Food is great!  Love their nachos, pizza and homemade fries!  But we really come for all the great bands they have that feature so many talented artists!

My husband is a huge fan of Johnny Cash, so we of course had to make a stop here. When it comes down to the nitty gritty, I guess it is a cool place and the price point is decent. My main complaint is that we went midweek in the off-season and it was absolutely packed to the rafters and it is not a large space by any means so I didn't feel as though he really got to enjoy it and take his time looking at everything. Tourists can be a pushy bunch so seeing each individual exhibit was dicey. If this museum was moved to a larger venue with a better layout, I could see it being a 5 star attraction for us. At the end of the day, definitely go see it if you are a fan but make sure you take your expectations down a notch.

This place was kind of a miss for us this time around. I contacted them almost two months ago to inquire about reserving a table and never heard back from anyone. I called a few days prior to our arrival and the voicemail stated they did not take reservations and opened at 6pm. We arrived at 8 and were able to get a table against the first wall when you walk in. We had an okay view of the stage. 

For the most part we just weren't really impressed with the music and entertainment. I've been to a few other piano bars, Bobby McKey's in the National Harbor and Croc Rocks in Myrtle Beach, and I just don't think this one compared. I think I expected a lot out of the musicians and being in Nashville and what not but they were just ok. 

The service here was good, our waitress was handling a lot of tables but she was very attentive and fast, we didn't have to wait long for her to come and check on us. 

This place gets really crowded, by 10pm it was standing room only, and with our seat location we could no longer see the stage so we left.

Not impressed. We go to Broadway  St. in Nashville at least 10 times a year and I will probably not have this restaurant on the top of the list to visit. The wine and beer prices are high (higher than other places on Broadway), the food was just okay and then we were charged a "tech fee"! We asked what it was and it was totally confusing. This has been the only honky tonk that I have seen that has this tech fee. And the music was just okay.....and just okay music on Broadway is not okay.

Had a great experience!   Ordered the chicken wings, Mac and cheese and garlic fries, all excellent.  Drank the bourbon drink, Dierks Dram, great cocktail.   Entertainment was very good, overall a great experience.   Will recommend to friends and will return.

We stopped in several times during our week in Nashville. The bands were consistently great, the bar was consistently crowded, and everyone there seemed to be having a great time. My only complaint was they need more restrooms, and need cleaned more frequently on busy nights.
By far the best bartenders we experienced our whole trip. Specifically Bill was the best we have ever had as a bartender. So attentive and friendly. A great bar for drinks food and music!
This is one of my favorite places in Nashville!! Great drinks and music! Kenny Bolton is amazing behind the bar AND on stage!!!! Highly recommend this place!!

Had such a great time listening to great music and our server Hollee was absolutely amazing. Hollee never let our drinks run out and was very attentive to our needs... will definitely be back .THANKS HOLLEE
This bar was so much fun! Michael, the security guard with the beard, was so awesome and made our experience with our bachelorette party soooo much fun! He's the best!
A bit high priced but awesome house band and friendly bartenders... a good time for sure

My wife and I were in Nashville for a week and enjoyed the showboat / show.  We were indecisive if we wanted the lunch or dinner tour. And looked at reviews to see if anyone has been to  both shows.  I couldn't find one review,; So we decided to go on the lunch show and it was a lot of fun. The food was really good (alcohol drinks extra charge) and the staff was friendly.  The show is a typical like vegas show, but was very entertaining and had some great music and comedy.  After the show we went up top were there was more music and comedy and the views of the Cumberland River was truly a site to see from the steam boat .  Money well spent!!!

I hate to do this, but to save anyone from making the mistake and going to this place for a meal, I will. We are in Nashville and there was to be entertainment at DB Whiskey Row so we thought it would be awesome to grab dinner and watch the performer. Big mistake. Right off the jump, the performer was going to be on the second floor. No biggie. We go up there and wait patiently for a table. While waiting we ordered two beers and two diet sodas from the bar. The female bartender was rude as hell, and, not exaggerating put one fourth of soda in the glass. Left the rest empty. Ok, we overlooked that and her attitude and found an empty table. The previous group had warned us the table was super wobbly and spins. Jesus, they weren't kidding. Nobody could dare place a hand on the table because it always shifted and drinks were spilling. When we asked the waitress she said, yeahhhh all the tables are like this. What? How about someone put a lil pride into this establishment? Oh and the floors, I am all for the "honky tonk" but shoes shouldn't literally stick to the floor! The food was disgusting. When we left our plates were nearly untouched. Here's the kicker, the bill included a TECH FEE of 3%. Waitress had no idea what it went for and we paid cash so there was no CC fees. The TECH FEE clearly isn't being used for cleaning supplies. Dierks, if your putting your name on something, you damn well better make sure it's not a flop!
Great atmosphere, Great food! Great live music! Danielle W. Is a great server and really cute!

I came here with a bachelorette party, and was convinced to purchase a package deal ($50 a person) by an event planner. The musicians were fantastic. But that's the only fantastic part of the place.

1. The package deal shots were not drinkable. 
2. The champagne wasn't good enough for a post prom high school bash.
3. The event planner put the wrong name on the stage call-out, upsetting our bride.
4. The server never brought the appetizers included in the package deal.
5. The average age in the bar was mid-40's--not appropriate for a bachelorette party.

When I complained to event planner, I got no response. I do not recommend this piano bar to anyone. Musicians, go find a better bar! You were great!

This piano bar is inside Dicks restaurant. Nobody was getting service. We waited 30 minutes for a watered down vodka. A girl at a nearby table had waited 35 minutes for just their drinks. Servers wouldn't even look at you. Don't waste your time or money!

Finishing up the 6:00 Show tonight at the Listening Room! Great entertainment . Love that they know each other and change things up as the evening progresses! 
Second time here and truly enjoy them!! Keep up the great work!!
Fun event. Buffet was ready when we arrived on the boat. Enjoyed the show. Performers were very talented. Lots of parking.

I did not try the food, which if what I'm hearing is correct, is a good thing. We came strictly to have a drink and experience a rooftop bar, and lo and behold, we ended up picking the "highest rooftop bar in Nashville." Of course, we didn't find this out until after we climbed all those stairs and THEN saw there was an elevator. I wanted to die.

The view, however, was stunning! You can see plenty of noteworthy buildings from your perch on the rooftop.

I can't fully give this place 5 stars, because I didn't try the food, nor did I pay for my drink--one of my coworkers did--and he kept pretty mum about the price. I'm sure if I had a better gauge of the flavors and prices I'd be able to rate more accurately, though.

But to me, as my first experience ever in Downtown Nashville, it let me impressed and with a sense of awe over how colorful and musical this city is.
Great music and good service. I had a turkey sandwich that was decent. The venue is great and is nice and updated.

We sort of stumbled onto this place looking for somewhere to get a quick bite to eat before a concert. We just made it in time because about an hour later and this place was packed as well. We ordered some burgers and tots and I have to say I was very surprised good burger but be warned it is huge we could have split one and the tots were super crispy...just good bar food. The bartenders were also great super friendly they were very understaffed but they got the food out fast and drinks steadily coming the whole time. We would stop by again for a late night snack or before a football game. My only problem was the band...they were good played country music like you are suppose to in Nashville but as most bars in Nashville they play at a level where no one can speak come on its only 7 not time to party just yet lol.

Ordered 3 vodka Redbull drinks. I was handed 3 shots of Fireball. I never drink Fireball and this is not something I would've ever ordered or mistakenly asked for. I was told, "That's what you said, I've already ran your card." I turned around and handed those shots out and went to another bartender. I also don't prefer to be pushed out of the way by men with girls on their shoulders for bottle service. My tab is worth more than that one little bottle delivery. Also, maybe your security guards would be more of an asset if they were snorting white stuff up their nose in the corner. Just a recommendation.
Service was great honestly food  is the reason for the 3 stars restrooms I am glad I waited u til after we had lunch but then I almost lost mine when I went in

Stopped in on Friday afternoon after everyone cleared out to head over to the game.  Bands playing on the first and second floor.  The fourth floor is home to the highest bar on Broadway with nice views and comfortable coaches to sit on.  The Mac and cheese comes in an iron skillet and is pretty darn good.  The rooftop bar is great for beer and basic drinks, very limited on mixed drink capability.   Definitely should be a stop on you list.

Terrible. We stopped by as part of a girls night out last night. The bartender was so rude. Then due to a long line to the women's restroom (only one stall) my friend ran into the men's restroom instead. As soon as she came out, a bouncer GRABBED her by her arm and pulled her out of the establishment. Fortunately another friend saw what was going on and followed her. The bouncer would NOT let her stop to let any of us know what was going on. Who makes a female leave by herself? And what was the big deal? If the rule is women are not allowed to use the men's room then simply ask her not to do it again. Do not grab her arm as soon as she comes out and pull to the exit. Ridiculous. Do not visit this place. Their service is HORRIBLE. I will never go back.
Such fun and very educational! Loved the many different areas with video theatre style learning spots. Great location and has a little shop and cafe too!

We stopped in to the rooftop bar and had a great time. The music was great and our server Austin was AWESOME! He was pleasant, really helpful and treated us like royalty. He's the biggest reason we will be stopping back in here again next trip through Nashville. Truly the best time we had in Nashville. 
**We did not eat, just had cocktails and listened to good music. The view from this rooftop is really great.
If you're a tan you have to come.  Location is very centered around 5th and very nice shop goo. Tastefully done.

Would not go back to eat. We went around 12:30 on a Saturday for lunch and waited almost 2 hours for our food! They said it was because all of the floors were open. To me, that's not an excuse. It sounds like you should have a better system to order and make food for that amount of space. My burger was way overdone and the waitress barely checked on us. We needed drinks so many times and she rarely came over.

Great spot in Nashville ! Musicians were very talented and interactive with the audience. Our server was friendly and  informative. She helped us make good food and drink selections from the many choices offered. Food was fantastic. We ordered the spinach artichoke dip and creole linguini. We stayed on the first floor for good and drinks then went to the other floors. The rooftop is airy and pleasant.  Decor - ok. Nothing fabulous other than the logo on painted brick up the staircase and the wood painted American flag lighting above the bar on the first floor.

Terrific live bands!!  Stopped in twice and enjoyed the bands both times.  Was extremely crowded on Wednesday night so not sure how a weekend evening would be.  

Drinks were good.  Didn't try the food.

Absolutely so much fun and take the Pilot House tour. The lunch buffet was the best food this trip and the entertainment was so much fun.  A taste of paddle boat travel from days gone by on the Cumberland river. I did get a Captain's cap from the gift shop

$6 for a bottled beer, horrible service and overpriced under-good food.  Do not order the nachos unless you want a plate of chips with some lettuce and a tablespoon of sour cream on top for $12 oh and they did throw on about 4 little diced pieces of cold chicken. Yuck. Very disappointing. The only positive thing I can say about this place is that the band was really good!
HOLLEE was amazing! Great service and made us feel more welcome than the other 11 rooftop bars we had been to. We loved her! Best rooftop in Nashville!

My husband and I decided to spend our anniversary aboard the ship and I've got to say we were very pleased. Neither of us have ever been and neither of us like being around large crowds of people. 

We walked in to a buffet that had the best food we've ever eaten. There were two buffets and you could serve yourself from both sides so because of the 4 lanes you didn't stand in line long at all. You then seated yourself at your table (which someone explained where the table was as you walked in the door). The only thing we didn't like about this is we didn't have our own table and there was no sweet tea (there was unsweetened tea at everyone's table). But that will NOT stop us from going again and again. 

We left our table after our meal and before the show started so I can't speak about the show. We explored the boat and stood out back and watched 9 guys on stand up jet skis do flips on the waves the boat was making, for my husband and I this was a great show for us.

Came for lunch/brunch while in town for the Pink concert.  We were expecting a different location with live music, and then realized they had moved and built this newer, larger one. It's industrial decor, wood and metal. Music is only offered at night: a 6 p.m. seating and an 8 p.m. seating in a separate room. Ordered the sweet and spicy pickles appetizer, came hot, tasty and the sweet pickle was a nice change from the usual dill found at most places. We only drank water, as their tea is "from the gun" per the server, who was working solo and ran around trying to service everyone. Traveling home, so skipped the alcohol. Down hill from there. Kitchen was out of hashbrown casserole, we were not informed. Gave us waffle fries without asking, and they were lukewarm, limp.  Would have changed our order if had known. Biscuits arrived without the boozy butter. Brussels sprouts deep fried, not sauteed. Overly salty. Biscuits and gravy lukewarm. Brisket sandwich was delish according to my daughter. Her waffle fries hot, great smokiness on the brisket and sweet/tangy taste to the BBQ sauce served on the side. Nashville hot chicken was enjoyed by my sister, except it was chicken tenders which made it difficult to eat without it falling apart.  The FROG jam, seriously, was tasted by all and was either a weak grape or strawberry.  Not the usual Fig, Raspberry, Orange, and Ginger concoction.  Then we witnessed the Owner? Manager? Take a beer glass, wipe it with his shirt tail and then fill with beer, setting up an area as if its waiting for a tasting. Pic attached. Even with change of no live music during the day, our experience and the food was not enough to warrant a return visit.

Rude bartenders. Won't go back. There are plenty bars. The lady bartender accused us of calling her a "b**ch" when she got mad we didn't tip her enough.  She went to security to kick us out.  Security shoved one of our guests for no reason.  She is a 60 year old 5' 3" lady. All because she did not get enough of a tip. Letters will be going to the management of the bar.

Too expensive! It was $17 bucks to see a couple of rooms of memorabilia. Worth stopping if you are downtown and need something to do, but wouldn't make a special trip there. If you are a hard core fan then maybe you would pay but for a causal fan like me who has seen Walk the Line and Walk Hard, then you will be underwhelmed.

Stopped in here as my friends and I were touring Broadway and the various bars on the strip. Of all of the ones we visited, this one was the best.

The place was fairly well packed when we walked in. We lucked out in that people were just leaving a table as we walked by, so we were able to snag a table. The place is pretty big, with a long horseshoe shaped bar as well as an upper level with additional seating. We stayed on the ground floor and my buddy left to get drinks.

Since I don't like the taste of alcohol, I always request a drink that tastes the least like alcohol as possible. This place delivered as I got a blue concoction that tasted like fruit and whipped cream. It was one of the best drinks I've ever had and that is really saying something as it comes from someone who doesn't like to drink.

The band on stage was rocking out and was very good. They were a bit on the louder side and it made conversation a bit difficult. However, people were dancing in front of the stage, they were dancing in their seats, and people appeared to be having a good time.

My friends and I stayed for about a half hour. There were sports on the television screens. If people left, we saw more people come in. If I lived in the Nashville area (I don't -- I live in Oregon), I would enjoy coming in here to grab a drink, maybe give the food a try, and have a good time. I do have to say that the band provided a lot of the energy and enjoyment and I'd be down to see them again and hang out a while if I am ever in the area again.

This looks like it's going to be the new hot spot on lower Broadway! One of the managers let us take a peek inside yesterday and it is incredible!!! My friends and I can't wait to spend New Years Eve here !!!!!! Welcome to town whiskey row !! Side note: their food and craft cocktails look out of this world!!

Ask for Jake! Sexiest bartender in Nashville! Best cocktails and service! He's beyond the best on Broadway!
Amazing food, music and vibe. Check them out, y'all!

We were graciously gifted this ride by a family member and to be fair, the boat itself is beautiful and very spacious. They have love music on the roof as well as the performance for brunch (except this was really lunch if your the second group to eat (it's more at 1:30p- so don't go in on an empty stomach unless you want to start with booze or beer) The performers were great and very talented. Customer service was good. BEWARE!! The brunch quisine was that of your middle school cafeteria, and I went to buy a couple beers on the top roof where they advertise that you get to keep the beer glass. Ok, cool right? Says $5/7 for a beer, which by Nashville standards can sometimes be kind of expensive. (If ur from out of town, please note beer can be cheap because TN hardly imports of at all, so they know the quality can be off sometime, half price nights can be $2.50/ beer at most places) 

 !!!!$28!!!! For two beers!! And I asked what the deal was, they charge you for the glass $14 a piece but it doesn't say that ANYWHERE on their menu and the bar tender didn't say anything! The advertisement is good, but it's a shady deal for sure. Very deflating.  

Over all it was a beautiful day and we enjoyed the show and the boat. But overall,  I would file this one under expensive gimmick.

I was pretty disappointed in this Honky Tonk. We started on the 2nd floor and ordered some nachos from the bar. Once a seat opened, we moved to a table. We had servers walk by us several times and never acknowledged us or asked if we needed anything. We sat at a table with dirty empty glasses from the previous customer. I finally stopped one and asked if there was a server for our table. They apologized and gave some excuse as to why nobody has checked on us. It took about 20 minutes to get the nachos and we had to go back to the bar to get ourselves another drink since as I mentioned nobody ever asked if we needed anything.  My sister and I are both Kid Rock fans and she has asked me to get something from there. I was again disappointed that they only had a few shirts and sweatshirts to choose from. Would of been nice to have a bigger selection of his items available. I guess this isn't a "gift shop" it's a honky tonk.  With all the space, one would think they'd invest into more souvenir items.  The music was good and we enjoyed the band that was playing. This is a place I can say I went there but would not be my go to spot for return trip.

Do not leave the first floor.  The musical talent and standards of service for the bars decrease as you go up each floor.  

We came on a Saturday night, wanting a killer view of Broadway and thinking a bar with Kid Rock's name on it would be a rocking good time.  The first floor was packed so we decided to try our luck on floor 4.  We scored a table by the window right away but the band playing was just 'meh'.  We ordered typical dive bar drinks (for reference - Makers is considered top shelf) and sadly nursed them while wondering how long we should hang onto the table.  Groups of partiers came and went.  No one was really staying for more than 15-20 minutes.  We ordered a second round and were told they were out of ice.  At 8pm on a Saturday?!?  Out of ice??  They were apparently out of lime wedges as well as my second vodka gimlet didn't have that either.  But of course we had to pay the same price.  Ugh.  That did it.  We left our window-side table to explore the rest of the 5 story building.

On floor 5 was a band that would be booed off any karaoke stage in the world.  It was absolutely horrifying.  I looked around like "is this a joke?".  I asked one of the staff members manning the door and he just shook his head.  It was shockingly bad.  Completely off key - almost like the lead singer just didn't care.

So down we go to floor 3 where another band that wouldn't make it past tv show singing competition auditions was trying their best to deliver the Eagles Hotel California.  It was so bad I didn't even recognize the song until the 3rd or 4th lyric.  Yikes.

So down to floor 1 (2nd floor is balcony for main floor stage) we go where we were treated to a professional band called The Tip.  They were really great.  Super professional and actually musically talented.  And even better, John Stone stopped by the bar and belted out some AC/DC.  It was incredible.  

Oh and guess what they had at the bar on floor 1?  ICE.  And plenty of it.  So we left that night knowing that management didn't care enough about their patrons to schlep a bucket of ice between floors via the elevator.

We will not be back.

We popped in here for NFL Draft weekend on Saturday night, since the nearby bar our event was at sucked! It actually worked out, because this place had a kick ass band on the main floor, and they rocked it!! We got there too late to eat, but the drinks made up for it. Great vibe, fun people, and it's right on the main strip. It has 4 floors I believe, with a different band on 3 of the levels, but none of them rocked it like the band on main floor. Definitely a go to spot.

Really good food here. Service is variable. They often have live music, which is sometimes the reason that I don't want to come here. It's a small place and it gets entirely too loud. Even worse when it's something you don't enjoy (country music, in my case). Too loud to have a conversation at your table. 

The good is always good. Best sweet potato fries I've ever had. Definitely beats the pants off anywhere else I've tried them. Great burgers, spicy chicken sandwich is also very good. Local beers on tap.
Disappointing. This place is clean and air conditioned, staff is friendly. However, $17 for a ticket to see relics for an hour *tops* is not good; this museum is very small.
Anthony helped us out with an issue and was great! Made the whole experience perfect.

this is a great museum to learn more about the life of Johnny Cash. if you aren't into his music or his work, it isn't for you (personally, I'm a fan). I'm probably more inclined to rate it 3.5, but rounding up.

there's some fun interactive exhibits and lots of neat memorabilia from throughout his life. it's all presented well, and in great condition. I even learned some neat facts about him that I didn't know going on. staff is friendly and gives you a quick rundown of what you'll see before you go.

getting a photo of us rocking out on guitar with Johnny was fun - they digitally insert him in the photo with you. for a funny little souvenir, it was actually very well done and we ended up purchasing (plus you get a free download of it) as a neat memento. 

gripes, mostly on the logistical side:

1) they really should have a bag check or something like that. you can carry your stuff with you, but it can be a bit awkward (especially if you're gonna spend 2 hours there, as we did).

2) crowd control, as others have pointed out, needs improvement. I'm not sure if there ever is an "off-time" to go; they just seemed to keep letting people in. and, if you've got your backpack or luggage with you, that makes it even more tough to navigate. during peak/busy hours, they should incorporate a headcount or something to control the flow.

3) his work outside of music is mentioned, but I wish they had more depth to the exhibits about his writing, photography, art, and humanitarian work. what's on display is cool, but could have more - don't sell "the man in black" short.

We tried Kid Rock's on our visit to Nville because the music sounded great from the street. We were there on Wednesday night around 7pm, so it was crowded, but it wasn't a huge party yet. We ordered drinks from the bar (good service at the bar!) and waited a few minutes for a table to open on the second floor. Once we found a table, we were approached by Hayley B. No smile. No greeting. We ordered our meals (the food was bar food - perfectly fine) and then we ordered another round of drinks. When she brought the drinks back to our table, it was pretty crowded with dishes, etc. She left the drinks and walked away. My sister-in-law, while rearranging dishes on the table, accidentally knocked her drink into her lap. She hadn't even taken a sip, so the drink was full. Haley B walked by our table and saw us trying to clean up the mess with our dinner napkins. She kept walking and offered no help - not even a bar rag. When she returned to the table 10 minutes later, my s-i-l ordered another drink, and Haley B, knowing that the original drink had been spilled, charged her full price for another drink. Admittedly, the spill was my s-i-l's fault, but come on. Lousy, lousy service from the minute she approached the table. We enjoyed the bar. The band was good, the food was fine, the vibe was good, but if Haley B is an example of the service - there are a lot of other options in Nashville. Had we had a decent waitress, my review would've been a 3-4 star review.
LD, our bouncer/security personnel was amazing!!! There were many people outside and he kindly walked us to our uber so we arrived safely. Thank you so much LD!!!

We came here for a pit stop, we had been walking around and just wanted a place to sit. When we got here it was emptyish, we couldn't go to the second floor or roof top because they had a private event which is pretty cool. But the guy singing was so good! He was playing acoustic and had a great voice. Slowly but surely the place started getting packed. We still got all the drinks in a timely manner. The shots were soooo good! We really liked this little bar. Staff was friendly and quick even after they started to get busy. Will stop here again when we are back in town.

Although the burger was phenomenal, my to go order did not have two out of the three extras I had paid for on the burger but also didn't have lettuce, tomatoes or onions on the side. I'll give it another try but I was disappointed when I opened up my package. The sweet potatoes fries were amazing, burger was so delicious but service could use some more detail.

I had higher expectations of this store to have a decent amount of Johnny Cash memorabilia when he performed live concerts at two infamous California prisons, wassup with that?  The Museum looks quite big from across the street.  Here I am in the heart of Nashville at the Johnny Cash Museum and all I could find are shot glasses, pictures of him, and baby items.  Come on now, there has to be more...
We enjoyed the dinner cruise on July 3rd. The food was very good, but the show Hot Country Nights was amazing.  I didn't want it to end.
SLOWEST FUCKING SERVICE IN THE WORLD! I've been here for over an hour waiting for a burger. The music isn't worth the wait to eat.

The best spot on Broadway!  Don't miss this one.  Live music, excellent,
great atmosphere.  Our bartender JAKE was awesome couldn't have asked for better.  Super personality.  As crowded as it was  (all bar stools were taken) JAKE never missed a beat, very attentive, felt like we've known him for years. JAKE is a great guy.. a definite asset to Whiskey Row.  Thanks JAKE you're the best!  Barbara & Johnny Walker

Such a cool place with really good food ta boot!

Had the hot chicken with a yummy pickle on a delicious biscuit bun and the bourbon cherry cider. SO good! 

This place has two performances a night where four song writers line up on stage and take turns performing the songs they've written... no covers allowed. We didn't get a chance to attend a show, but the concept seems so fun! The inside front room has tables and a bar and is industrial casual. Then the performance area has a nice stage with table seating and another bar. 

This would make for a fun night out! Tickets are on sale online in advance. There's also Sunday morning services here... I was told really good music!

Music was great. Really enjoyed the visit in that regard. Bathroom is nice and it seems clean for a bar. 
Our waiter was great. Came by a great many times. 

Now the issue...

The alcohol was weak. Not sure if that's a thing here but I had multiple drinks and never even felt buzzed....at all. Considering the cost per I would think four would be enough to get that sensation. 
Had 4 bar drinks in about and hour and a half. Nothing. So I stopped drinking and enjoyed the band.

We're here on a short girls trip and decided to stop in. Best experience ever! We were lucky enough to sit at Destiny's bar......and when I say lucky, we were because she's amazing! She made the whole visit. Kid Rock, hiring this woman was the best thing your managers did! Thanks y'all!

Was in town for the NFL draft and this was the only spot where the service was bad.   Stopped  by early in the day before it was busy and was at the bar was maybe 1/2 of the seats filled.   The bartender was serving people but hard to understand how she picked and chooses who she would.   Sat at the bar for about 5 minutes before I was able to get her attention.   Stayed for 2 beers then left since it was just to slow.   
Noticed on the bill they charge a 3% tech fee?   The bartender said she didn't know what it was but talking to people it seems like its a fee if you pay with a credit card.    So they charge $8.00 for a bud light bottle - which they are probably making 500% + profit on and they want to add this fee.   I know for a tourist based place they don;t really have any incentive for repeat customers but that's just pretty bad.

Girls: can wear tanks, booty shorts, and twerk on every barstool. Guys: have to be fully clothed in a T-shirt and shorts. Guy friend tried walking in with a tank and shorts on. It's 2019, I believe we're supposed to stop sexualizing women. Not here though.

I LOVE Dierks Bentley, thus this may be a biased review ;). However this bar has the "tallest" rooftop bar in Nashville and also has music on each floor. We opted for the second floor in which the band was taking requests and even played a little Folsom Prison Blues for me. Our waitress was great - always checking in and keeping our drinks full! The cocktails were also amazing... I tried a twist on the "Paloma" and loved it! My husband had a vodka strawberry lemonade and also said it was refreshing on this hot and humid day. I think I could have spent my whole afternoon here if I wanted to as it was so chill!

Still on the boat for the Thanksgiving cruise...the real thing I was looking forward to was the views of downtown Nashville---we've essentially been going back and forth near Opryland for 2 hours and 15 minutes now--apparently we're not going to downtown and no one seems to have mentioned it.  The servers seemed to know it, but didn't say anything until we asked.  It probably could have been salvaged if the food was good or if I was a "show" person--just here for lunch and the cruise.  The salads and desserts preset on the table looked like they were prepped 2 days ago.  Table set with tea and Ranch--no water??  Bread wasn't warm and butter was cold--tasted like it was straight out of the bag.  Lunch was essentially a processed meat plate (turkey and ham) with an ice cream scoop of mashed potatoes and undercooked green beans (no, not haricot verts).  If I had wanted cafeteria food, I would have gone to a cafeteria. Overall, a pretty disappointing trip--buyer beware and please let me off this boat!

Good atmosphere and food. Service was fine. My only gripe was the tech fee charge on our bill. This is not advertised. The manager told us the company that runs this establishment is out of Arizona and they do this out there. Helps pay for computers and keep the food prices down. Mmm.....

Unless you are a Cash buff that needs to check this off their bucketlist, this museum is a waste of time and money. After paying $20 per person, we were herded into a small space, where it was difficult to read or see anything and you felt rushed because of the amount of people they were letting in. There were several pieces of memorabilia to appease the fans but the rest of the displays were info that could have been googled or watched on youtube.

Waitress told us half the items on the menu weren't available, told us to "go to the bar" to get water (we were there for dinner).  Probably worst service I've ever had. Won't be coming back. Thank goodness there are other places I've been in Nashville that were great.

This is a must for all Johnny Cash fans. Thought the exhibit were well thought out and it's fun to walk around. I never knew that he was an artist too. They had a few of his art work displayed as well. Worth a visit if you're in town and trying to get away from the bars and need something else to do.

Super weak drinks - normally a half a beer will get me buzzed and 2 margaritas (that were super sugary) did nothing. Wanted to come here because I came a few years back and it was so much fun - apparently they changed locations and now it's inside of a Dick's restaurant. Unfortunate wouldn't come back to this new location - was super disappointed and not worth the cover or price of drinks.

As all the other Madame Tussaud's wax museums, the figures are all so realistic! Of course for Nashville's wax figure themes it was aimed around country music sensations. Anyone from current to new singers including Jonny cash to Luke Bryant and Blake Shelton. The figures are pretty realistic it's scary, the details are phenomenal from the eyes to the clothing! Definitely a fun place to stop by if you're looking for something extra to do around the city!
Such a great bar! Good food and service and a great all around environment wether you enjoy live bands or a DJ. Also love seeing the Henry Martin band here!

They don't answer phones or respond to reservations !  Bar is dirty , old and nothing like Nashville has to offer.   Sadly , we turned in a money clip and ID thinking they would announce on piano sound system but instead mngr put in his pocket ?  Would not recommend ! Go anywhere but here and DEFINITELY not worth the cover ?  Seems like staff are high and angry.   They can't get simple drink orders correct ?  Piano playing is not too bad but venue needs OVERHAUL as well as staff !

After ordering two drinks and onion rings for $35 we got a vodka soda when we ordered a vodka tonic and asked for ranch with our onion rings and got tarter sauce. Also by the time we got our onion rings it had been 20 min and they were cold.. other places on Broadway I would rather go than here..

I hate to say it, but I was pretty disappointed with how this museum was set up. But I did enjoy what I got to see.

  It's a lot smaller that I imagined...I expected it at least to be as big as the Country Music Hall of Fame. The inside of the museum itself is wonderfully designed and contains a lot of interesting artifacts of Johnny Cash's life, however I was not very happy that I had to pay $18 for a museum that took me about 15 minutes to go through the entire thing.

   I didn't know a whole lot about Cash besides his music, so I will say that I learned many interesting things about him during my visit. They showcase short clips projected on walls, little pods to listen to his music, and countless fun facts about the legendary singer scattered everywhere. The halls to walk through were pretty narrow, and being there on a Saturday, I felt like I was in a huddle of penguins trying to wobble to the next exhibit. They've got a nice little gift shop out front too.

   My advice is if you decide to go, really take your time throughout the museum and try to hit up everything there is to see in there, so you can feel like you got your money's worth. If you're a big Johnny Cash fan, I can guarantee you'll really enjoy it.

I got into Johnny Cash because of the movie - don't judge I'm not from an area that is big into the country music genre. I knew I had to stop into the museum to get more history and listen to some great music! 
I think they did an excellent job paying tribute to his life & his music. It was smaller than I imagined it would be but I was still very happy with it since there was so much to see, read & view! I loved the live shows playing, it was like going back in time. Listening to the music was my favorite! The Man in Black sure new how to play a song that got you to the core.
I was also very glad for the photo op with Johnny himself, superimposed of course. It was worth the price to have a cute takeaway!
I wish they had more space as I could be there all day but it worth going into and it's right there in the heart of downtown!
Just as bad as midtown! Plenty of nicer places with nicer employees to go!  If overpriced and rude people are your Jam you might enjoy!
This was a really fun spot with great music and good service. My only issue was the oil that was leaking from the ceiling and ruined my hat and shirt. What a disappointment.

So it's the rock n' roll bar on Broadway in the Trashville sector of Nashville.  Bands on every level.  LOTS of bars so never really a wait for a drink.  AC pumping even with the doors/windows open so it was nice.  Wife isn't a big country fan and we both hate new/bro country so even though not a huge fan of Kid Rock we enjoyed this spot.

I came here on Sunday and didn't have to wait at all to buy a ticket or enter the museum although it was still very busy inside. It made it kind of difficult to see or read anything when there were people standing in front of you. The layout is a little disorienting even with a map but it wasn't a big deal. 

Lots of cool things to see and watch but it only took me about 45 minute - 1 hour to see everything. If you are looking to do something that will burn a couple hours this isn't the place.

The ticket prices aren't bad but I can see how it will add up if you have a family or group of people.
The burger was decent and the service was attentive. Unfortunately the live music was awful and so loud you couldn't hear yourself think

When in Nashville do not pass this up. Outstanding event! The show was fantastic. Unbelievable talent. The luncheon was so-so. Buffet nothing to rave about. Service was excellent. Cruise was relaxing, however, the sites along the Columbine river were industrial until you hit downtown Nashville

Staff is Rude & nasty.  Overpriced drinks! We came in for drinks only & music.  MUSIC WAS AWESOME! But these nasty chicks behind the bar have no clue how to make most drinks!!! STAND ON THE STREET & listen don't bother coming in and wasting good money.

Heard so many good things about this bar but was seriously let down after my experience. This was hands down the worst experience I've ever had in a bar. The atmosphere was good and it was fun at first, but after a situation with lots of people waiting in line to go up to the second floor, things quickly turned after a miscommunication between the bouncer and my friend and I. The bouncers were completely unprofessional, rude, and aggressive to my friend and I. For starters, I completely understand and respect that bouncers need to do their jobs, it's important to keep people safe, especially in crowds-- but the way my particular situation was handled was absolutely unnecessary and could have been avoided with simple communication. I was physically grabbed by my purse by a bouncer after trying to go up stairs that were blocked off. If I knew the stairs were blocked off, I would not have tried to go up like I did. This could have been avoided by the bouncer simply telling me not to go up, but instead, I was grabbed and yanked down 5 steps by my purse. I will never return to this bar or recommend it to anyone I know, simply because of the way the bouncer treated me and how poorly the situation was handled. I am deeply disappointed by this bar and it's security. My group of 18 girl friends decided to leave and go somewhere else after this happened.

Managers who are reading this: please train your security staff on how to properly handle high stress situations to avoid this in the future. In an area with such a high volume of people and so many other choices on places to spend money and time, customer service and more important SAFETY OF GUESTS should be a priority.

Out of all the "celebrity" bars down in Nashville, Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row is absolutely my favorite. Location and rooftop views are some of the best, always has the best bands, food is delicious, (get the chicken wings, you won't be disappointed!) and some of the friendliest and funnest bartenders around! Especially Jake! Even during CMA Fest when it was super crowded he made our time there so much fun! Can't wait to come back!

I am a huge Dierks fan so of course we had to come here! First of all we came in a few days while being here for CMA FEST and we had the pleasure of having Kelly as our server. Not only was she friendly she was on it with everything! I seen a few "unmotivated" bartenders who looked not so friendly (women bartenders) but Kelly was amazing! The food was delicious especially the artichoke dip and meatball sliders. Loved the setup! As a business owner myself I would only give y'all advice on hiring more friendly motivated women bartenders. But I still give y'all a 5 star review!

Mixed review here... the music was fun and the musicians were entertaining. However a few negatives: 1. they don't carry kid rock bad ass beer - wtf? 2. While we didn't get full meals, we did get the giant potato skins, which was a fully loaded but cold potato, split in half.  If you want to eat, don't waste your time here when there are so many other choices.

Had a quick drink here with friends. The space has a great vibe and the bellinis and frozes were pretty good. It's definitely pricey though and getting a place to sit was a little difficult. We wanted to checkout the rooftop when we came here but it was closed so that was a bummer.

So, like many things in Nashville, I think this was way overpriced​.  You do get to see some cool things.  Handwritten​ notes.  Military uniform.  Early guitars etc.   I think it should be half the price.  You can do the entire museum​ in an hour.  Cool, but expensive.  I'd almost say must-do​ for a Cash fanatic, but I am one and I wasn't sold.  Must say, I'm not a cheap person either.  I waste money all the time and wasted tons on local beer on Broadway.

I have been waiting for 12 years for someone to put a cool burger joint close to the house.  We went last night and had the Veggie Burger and the Cilantro Burger.  Both are great.  The atmosphere and service was very good.  They have a nice choice of local draft beer also.  And the prices were good.  We will be back.  I can't wait for some live blues and soul music.

Was absolutely stoked to visit this bar! First time in Nashville and was looking for a memorable experience at one of my favorite country artists spot. However, bartender Ashlyn W. (#392) on the first floor working Sunday May 26th around 1pm provided very poor service (and that's putting it nicely)!!!!!!!  This GIRL would not give me or my boyfriend the time of day and made it feel we were a bother to even be present there. We ordered our drinks which was difficult to do from the beginning because she gave us attitude when asking what kind of vodka they had to order. Once ordered, made me feel unappreciated and unwelcome. There was another team member present (did not catch her name) who was watching the entire scenario and did nothing to help. We left immediately after. Totally ruined my experience at one of my favorite artists place. Please do something to resolve this because I would love to come back and visit but if I see the same bartender, my boyfriend and I will leave without question. Save yourself the trouble and do not go to Ashlyn!!!!!!

Nice thing to do when visiting Nashville and worth the price. Food was good, show was entertaining, and entire riverboat staff was excellent. Great for all ages. ...Nick's Brooklyn pizza in Panama City Beach FL. is a fraud.

We got to be boat an hour early and waited out side by the gazebo till they let us on. We payed a little extra to sit at the captains table so we got seated first and had choice seats for the cocktail hour right by the band. Then with the package got to get seated in the main room and was able to have the first course before everyone else got there. We also had first dibs at the buffet which was great as there was a lot to choose from before the masses. Tix included a tour of he pilot house and chat with the captain . Then we were taken down to eat dessert before the show. Show was very entertaining as the performers were talented in singing and dancing . They explained the history of country music through song through the years and that was nice. If your going to do this spend the extra 20 bucks I believe it was and get a few perks before everyone else.

I'm a huge cash fan but this museum was a bit disappointing. it just felt like a TOURIST TRAP. the location is terrible, the museum itself is small so it gets crowded quick. admission is $15, parking is $10 for one (1) hour!! their gift shop is very pricy. JOHNNY CASH FANS DESERVE BETTER

My friends and I all agreed that the best thing about this fairly new place is that it has the cleanest men's and women's  bathrooms on Broadway.  

Second best thing are the acoustics but they couldn't salvage the band that we heard attempting to play music. 

Honorable mention: watching the bartenders quickly pop an armful of beers in like 3 seconds.  Beers could have been a bit colder. 

This place has potential but not as a classic Nashville Broadway dive bar.

It was a Saturday and the place was packed. The band was great. The fiddle player rocked devil went down to Georgia like I've never heard live before. Anytime I needed a beer the bartenders were quick to respond, even though it was 2 deep almost the whole time. Great place to hang out for a bit and have a beer or 3.

Very upset with this place. I was here 3 times and enjoyed it at first. When i came back the bouncer accused me of having a fake ID and called a cop over. The cop told me my ID was fake and that he didn't care about my business. When i asked him to run the ID, he told me that it wasnt worth his time. I dont know how such a fun place could be so rude. I thought this was up there on my favorite places in nashville but after this incident i have no desire to come back.
We bellied up to the bar in the early afternoon and the signature cocktails did not disappoint. I am most definitely going to try and recreate this is my kitchen.

Went to the rooftop for a whiskey...$30 for (2) Woodford reserve on the rocks.  Yup, $30!  The whole bottle cost $40.  That's just sad....sad we paid $30.  I hope others will read this b4 falling into that trap.

Currently sitting on the rooftop and this place has been a huge disappointment. Had to find a manager after 30 minutes to get a drink. Horrible service and then our waitress has gotten every drink order wrong. Not sure where the pictures come from on their website but my NY strip wasn't even a strip. People will come because it's Kid Rocks Place, don't waste time on food or expect the food to look anything like the website!!

Manager came over an comped meal and is trying to make things better!!

I went with a group of friends and we weren't let in because our friend, who happened to be a man of color, was wearing tims, which "werent appropriate." When the bouncer was asked why why, we were called ignorant and given no further explanation. If you care about race relations in america, I would not recommend this establishment.
Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row kicks women out for accidentally walking into men's restroom.

I stopped in during the early afternoon about a month ago. The cleanliness of the place was ho-hum. The tables were wiped down, but the bar had crumbs and the floor needed sweeping, otherwise not too bad. The bartender's attitude was...I guess the best way to describe him was laid back to the point of indifference. There were only two of us sitting at the bar, but it took him a solid 5 minutes to wait on me and the 2 beers I had could have easily been 3 if he had only been more attentive. I had a Bleu Cheese burger with fries.The burger was delicious. However, the fries were room temperature and limp, which offset the wow factor of the burger. For the prices they charge, I expected better. Crispy, hot french fries and a more energetic bartender would have made bumped this review to 3-stars.

This is right in the middle of music row and by far the loudest on the strip.  The music was actually really good much more southern rock than country (which I love)!  It's a huge bar with at least 3 levels.  It's really Nice inside very modern.   It's packed even when the strip wasn't that busy.  The reason for the 3 stars is this isn't a true honky Tonk which is really what we were looking for.  It's more commercialized with a double level stage lighting etc.  if that's your thing this is your place.

I went here on a Thursday night in February, and the atmosphere was refreshing.  It wasn't too crowded, and I loved how the stage was up high so even the people standing in the back or the short people like me can see the band perform. The prices are typical compared to other bars, and the bartenders are friendly!  Lots of open space so you're not crammed in the bar like sardines, and the band's play a variety of music and are very interactive!  One of my favorite bars in Nashville for sure. Definitely recommend!

Came here for drinks and for the music! This place was packed on a saturday evening, and great cover bands galore! On this strip of music bars, this is probably one of the better ones. careful, there is a casual dress code, so no athletic shorts. Great drinks, upstairs area, great music, i recommend visiting!

Not very impressed with this busy and overcrowded museum. I would have enjoyed it more if I could have seen what was in the museum. Less people better time, I would suggest calling to see when the slowest time is to visit and hopefully you will have a better experience than I did.
Typical museum. Lots to see and read. $18 a ticket. Clean. Videos movies his suits etc. Get there.

Only one bartender who is really slow.  We spent 2 hours here because the band was good, but the bartender/owner stayed down at one end and couldn't keep up.   After waiting 30 mins for a drink, I waved my arms at her, and she completely flipped out, so we got up to leave, and then she got worse and actually ran to the door guy to have us thrown out as we were leaving.  It was like "you can't walk out, I'm throwing you out".  She then called out to my wife "you fkn b@tch", even though she never said a single word to her.  I know menapause is rough, but holy cow!!  If you can't handle it, sell the bar for God's sake.

Beat. The singer on 10/5 took our money saying he'd play our song and never did, don't waste you're money, can only hear sweet home Alabama so many times. Add also told told the lead singer didn't know who Faith Hill was. Why are you in Nashville??? Go to hunky tonk central

This review is for the venue - not the food!

We were bar hopping on Broadway on a Friday night and we passed through some places that were mostly misses. We almost passed by this place, as you can't see all that's inside from the front door, but then we saw all the people dancing, drinking, and singing through the window. So we stepped back in. It was so fun! They have a huge stage and the people who were playing were great. We did not try the food but the bar was great and the venue was lit!!!
Food is mediocre at best. 3 out of 4 of us received our food and the 4th person in our party got their chili when we were done. Gave us the excuse "kitchen is a mess tonight"

If I've learned one thing about Nashville, it's that nobody believes in elevators!! Or maybe it's just telling me to get my a** back into shape....

   This was a cool little rooftop bar to chill out on during the day. There was a DJ playing, party music, and a bar right in the middle. There wasn't a whole lot of room for seating that wasn't at the bar, with just a handful of tables and a couple couches. 

   I don't really see anything that was Dierks Bentley related about this bar, but whatever. They had some fun drinks but they were a bit expensive. I tried the Redbull Frose' and it was really good! $11 was a bit high thought for the size of it. 

   We ended up claiming one of the couches and they were very enjoyable to sit and look at the pretty view of downtown Nashville. They even had huge fans blowing, which was perfect for the 90 degree weather that we had.

Fun Romp Through Johnny Cash Memorabilia

SITREP

This is an excellent stop in Nashville, and a must-do (really) for anyone who is a fan of the fan.  The museum tour is $15 and there are all sorts of great memorabilia items for sale for those who want to take a piece of the man back home with them.

AND SODA!

These guys thought of everything!  They even sold my diet Pepsi in a nice adjunct refrigerator just when I need some cool refreshment.

THE SETUP

There was also a haunting theme for me this whole trip of mine while in Nashville - I kept on running into moments drenched in Johnny Cash and/or Nine Inch Nails (NIN).   

* At bars & music venues - such as at Tootsies - I kept hearing Johnny Cash or NIN music played by the bands;
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ysb-uye-gs-up-hoes-down-town-nashville-pub-and-bar-crawl-nashville?select=Bbit4aziG6MXbw3jnh4bsw#Bbit4aziG6MXbw3jnh4bsw

* At the United Record Pressing tour, we witness a new pressing of NIN's album "Pretty Hate Machine"! 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/yelp-spring-break-event-tour-of-united-record-pressing-nashville?filter_by_userid=True&select=QWEtZLqDk_boTWAEBmW1Og&userid=3mNz5nQFTIBQm0oU5mBR0w#QWEtZLqDk_boTWAEBmW1Og

* And then as I walked into this store, not a minute passed by and they were playing Johnny's haunting cover of NIN's song, "Hurt".

THE LOWDOWN

I love this place and it was also a serendipitous sign that continued throughout the weekend as I kept running into flashes of Johnny Cash at other music venues, over restaurant music speakers, and flyers & billboards that had the man's likeness plastered all over Nashville...
We came in for an appetizer and a quick drink on a Friday night. Our waitress was nice and service was quick. The Bavarian pretzel was actually really good. Enjoyed the live band.

I thought I knew a decent amount about Johnny Cash..but I did not! This museum was a great stop on a cold winter day in Nashville.

The price of entry is not the cheapest but I think it was worth the cost. We spent a solid 1.5-2 hours here and really read into all of the displays and watched the multimedia presentations. There was some really cool stuff and a few interactive displays as well. It was also amazing to see so many cool Cash (and more) memorabilia items.

The coffee shop and gift shops are also in the same building and have a decent amount of cool stuff in them as well. While I didn't buy anything I saw a few things that could make cool gifts for big time fans!

this was the most disrespectful place. i got my id taken away even tho im 21. they kicked me out and i am a women. they kicked me out in an alley and i said "can i wait till my friends comes back because i am scared as a women being alone in the alleyy" and they said "i dont give a fuck go !!!!" disrespectful

Kind of off the beaten path from all the action on Broadway, it's an average bar with live music and a menu of typical bar food. The staff wasn't overly friendly, not rude just inattentive. I ordered the chicken nachos. It was a huge portion but I did my best. Grilled chicken chunks with plenty of chips, queso, lettuce, tomatoes, onions, etc. 

I also tried a local craft beer "Walk the Line".  6$ for a cup. Kind of pricey but it was good if you like strong beer. I had two. 

All in all I'd say it's not bad for a quick bite and acoustic entertainment and local beer!
Live country music in the afternoon Kid Rock's Honky Tonk on the roof deck.  But hey, it's Nashville! What do you expect. Jordan McCants snd and the 11-2 Guys. Great music, good food.

Meh. It is what it is. Great music. Loud music. Expensive beer, so so burger. Still had an OK time, and I guess it is a must to stop into the place if you're in Nashville, but you probably want to eat somewhere else.

This place opened a few years ago and I never checked it out. Big mistake. The staff is awesome ( especially Kayla ) she always takes good care of us. Great live country music. Games and entertainment. If you like to dance this place is it!! Great food, great music, great people!

Another cool little bar on Broadway in downtown Nashville. 

The music was fun on Tuesday evening when we stopped in. It was also nice and cool with the air conditioning while it was 95 degrees outside. 

Live music that you can hear from the street if you can't make it in. 

I just find these places to all be regular run of the mill dive bars, nothing great but nothing bad either. This was one of the better ones in my opinion.

I asked the band to play a song.... i handed the artist $40 bucks and she said told me it would cost me $100. it was a lynard skynard song which they were fully capable of playing. I asked for managers and they said they couldn't help. 

Lame bands. Good service but the live bands weren't worth my cash. Take your money to Tootsies. At the bands and servers were nice

My friend got us some tickets to see the Prince tribute at Basement East, so we hit up Lyft and got ourselves over to the East side for the evening.

We got there early so we could hopefully get something to eat. Around back of the venue is a bar area that has tables inside as well as a nice deck with tables outside. We ordered food and drinks at the bar and sat outside to shoot the shit and wait. Their menu has some interesting selections - bahn mi with pork, spicy pickled carrots; grilled chicken with some sort of spicy sauce; tacos; etc. The bahn mi was actually really good, definitely had some spice, and was served with a small handful of tortilla chips. It wasn't too big and hit that sweet spot of not so much food you were stuffed and unable to catch a buzz and not so little food that you got wrecked drunk and had to get carted home. The specialty drinks they had going on for Bonnaroo weekend were also good and only $5 for blood orange vodka and Red Bull Red.

Once we paid up, we went around to the front to go inside the venue. The stage was on the right as you walked in, bar straight ahead. Some tables were set up in the middle of the room and there were barstools in front of the bar. There was also a small mini-bar set up on the wall beside the hallway to the restrooms that had beer and a small selection of liquor drinks. The size pretty nice and luckily it was kind of empty that night so everyone could get a good look at the band playing Prince jams. Smoking outside on the deck. Bartenders were fast, I suggest using the mini bar if they have your drinks as that's less busy and much more convenient.

Overall a good venue and I look forward to seeing other shows here!

It's a plain establishment in my eyes, but one thing that always stands out in my eyes is the venue is always the loudest on the block. Great musicians sing good songs, and they actually interacted with the guests when I was there. No complaints from me, definitely.
The bouncer called me a faggot and that I couldn't get in with a tank top. I looked inside the bar and several females and the band had tank tops or spaghetti straps on. I found it very offensive.

What makes this place great are the singer/songwriters that perform here. I love the fact they also serve food however it was pretty mediocre. First off, I'd like to say that our server was amazing. She truly went out of her way and made sure we got what we had asked for. If it wasn't for her amazing service I'd give it 3.5 stars. The kitchen got our order wrong multiple times regardless of sending it back. I had gotten the BBQ platter pulled pork and the meat was very dry. I enjoyed the green beans and Brussels sprouts. I'd skip the Mac and cheese as it was very bland in my opinion. 

If you're trying to meet your $15 min, maybe try the wings? It was apparently the performer's favorite. I would've done so but I had already placed my order when they decided to share that piece of information.

So this is a great spot right in the heart of Broadway.  Music was awesome, service is good but the Men's bathroom situation is terrible and an embarrassment to the rest of the place
Just disgusting and gross.  Can't imagine the
Women's bathroom is any better. 
Dierks, if you are reading this, put some $$ into improving this or you will lose customers.

This was one of the coolest experiences of my life. The sculptures were so accurate. Staff members were above and beyond, especially this sweet lady running the photo shoot portion of it. She made our experience from a 4 to the full 5 stars.

Good vibes, good music, and good drinks! Went here on a Wednesday night and it was so fun. The bar was crowded but not so crowded that you could not move. Bartenders very friendly, along with people in the bar!

There were a lot of cool things to see. I really wish that for the money, there would have been more of a "tour" feel. Also wish that there would have been some kind of markings on things to tell if they were real or replicas. All in all it was ok, but I can check it off of my list of things to do in Nashville.

Food is good. Music on different levels is amazing! Elevator will take you to different floors, if you're not able to do stairs. They open the windows so you feel the fresh air, and can see people on the rooftops of other bars. We loved the onion rings!

I will not be returning to this location ever again. I had high expectations of this place but unfortunately was a complete letdown.
First off my girlfriend's work friend was having a birthday on the 2nd floor and had a table reserved.. 

Some context is I did not know her work friends last name. 

Well after standing in a 30min line outside I find out I have to stand in another line to get up stairs
As I wait for the stairs I notice people going up without standing in line 
So I ask the door attendant "hey, if people have a table can we skip the line" 
He says "sure what is the name" so I give her first name
This asshole literally looks at me laughs and says "ya... you must know her really well" and wouldn't let me through at all

I will NEVER return here and I do NOT recommend it 

It's hotter than Hadas there. The security is obviously doing their job very well 
Considering my girlfriend telling me she was able to just go up the stairs without giving a name or showing ID to get in so I guess this place is sexiest too 

Well it's Welcome to Nashville once again 

**UPDATE*** 
I had the pleasure of speaking with Kevin through email. He was so helpful and wanted to make this right. 

I appreciate this so much. I did not take any "gift" from them as to me it wasn't necessary
But I thank him so much for wanting to help so I have updated my review from 1Star to 3Star 

Thank you Kevin for trying to make things better
Wonderful live music and our waitress was the most on the ball server I have ever seen! A fun stop on the Honky Tonk Highway.

We just went to the General Jackson Showboat lunch Christmas show.  The price for the cruise and lunch was 65.00 including Tennessee state tax.  The salad and desert were at the table when you set down at your assigned table, we were at table 25 a side table by the window.  Our seat was great I loved looking out the window while we ate our lunch.  The meal consisted of Turkey, mash potatoes, gravy, green beans, and dinner rolls.  The meal was served to us by our servers and we had ice tea and coffee to drink.  The service was excellent and our seats still had a good view of the show even though it was on the side.  The desert was peppermint cheesecake with chocolate sauce drizzled on the plate.  The entertainer was excellent with 6 entertainers who all were very talented.  It was a great day to cruise about 45 degrees and relatively clear for a December day.  All in all I would recommend attending the General Jackson Christmas show.

I love the Listening Room Cafe and make sure it's a stop on most all of my trips to Nashville. I recommend checking online to see what acts are scheduled for the night(s) you are considering. They have an array of different artists depending on the night and everyone I've seen has been great. The great thing about the Listening Room is the singer/songwriter atmosphere, which is different than pretty much most of the honky tonk bars downtown--which mostly have bands w/ cover songs from every genre of music. 

The Listening Room often has up and coming musicians who really are great to listen to. As others have recommended, make reservations--most shows are free and just require a small food/beverage purchase (which you'll want to do anyway), some of the bigger acts require a small cover fee ($5, maybe $10). Everything I've seen has been free and have always gotten a great seat. I've enjoyed the food and have found it pretty good. I see some people didn't have good food experiences, but honestly I've made a special trip to the Listening Room for dinner and music--especially on nights I've been in town for business whether w colleagues or even alone. The first time I visited was w my spouse and young daughter, the music was great, our daughter loved it (and it was a great way to introduce her to a live inside venue (vs. amphitheater or somewhere kids can run around). She loved the food and atmosphere. That night we left a little early as it got late for her and the second act was pretty loud. All of the other acts I've seen have not been that loud, so I think it was just that night (it was painfully loud even for adults who went to listen to loud music).  I've gone on my own, w/ family, and w/ friends and colleagues. 

Some of the food dishes are small where you can order multiple items, then there are also full entrees, just select and/or mix and match what you feel like. The menu isn't extensive but I've always had great food. Typically (knock on wood it doesn't fill up after writing this...) it's pretty easy to see a show unless there is a private party. It's much much easier to get into the LR than other places like the Bluebird and it's also no smoking and not the crazy downtown bar scene. The atmosphere is a stage with tables (throughout a large industrial type restaurant) facing towards the stage. I would definitely go back, again checking acts before going. I recommend Googling the band/singer and pulling up the singers' private webpage and/or Youtube sites--this will give you a much more indepth description and even audio and/or videos to watch, then you can select which acts/what night you want to visit (if you're in town a few days).

9/20/19 rudest bartender I've ever encountered. We left immediately! 4 years ago this was one of my favorite bars to visit. So very disappointed with the lack of hospitality. We will not be visiting again. They should really school their staff on the proper treatment of guests.

Very good food great service. Only thing that was sketchy is that this place doesn't explain why there is a "tech fee"   It's not on menu and posted no where. You are subject to pay it depending on how much your bill is.

After reading roughly 40 one star reviews that illustrate the physical and verbal aggression that the security guards have used towards many human beings, I am not sure why I am even bothering to write this review. It is very apparent that the establishment knows their security guards are very LARGE and aggressive men who immediately resort to physical violence when a simple spoken sentence to someone could completely change the outcome of a situation. A great place! Loved it!
Bought some mugs from the coffee shop part for my collection, and for a tourist attraction they weren't priced too badly. 
The staff was friendly. The space is cool. Lots of mementos you can grab while you're there.

Spent the weekend in Nashville and spent most of our time here.  Music was phenomenal!!!  We especially enjoyed John Stone.  It was our first time seeing him but it won't be our last.  Each visit the place was packed and hard to find a seat.   We were fortunate to have the same server on a few of our visits - Mike Lowell!  He was very attentive which was amazing considering how busy it was.  We will look for him to be our server again when we return.  Food was delicious.  My daughter ordered the big ass hot dog and yes, it was huge!  She was only able to eat half of it.  Loved that the drinks were named after Kid Rock's songs.  My favorite was Devil Without A Cause.  Was hoping to see Bobby but they said he was there a few days before us.  Maybe next time.  Also loved the decor, especially the air brushed car hoods!

We did the lunch cruise.  We ate as soon as we boarded...before even leaving the dock.  Buffet was  ok nothing great but good enough. Salad, grits, mashed potatoes,  chicken,  pork tenderloin,  corn bread and dessert. 
Show was very entertaining. Jusst lots of hits by lots of different people. 
Definitely would recommend as a tourist :-)

Stopped in the afternoon for a drink, came back at night for more drinks.  Bartenders both times were very friendly and not hard to get their attention, in fact, they were usually asking me for a refill.  Acoustic performers were all very good, entertaining, and engaging with the audience on open mic night.  Did not have the food, but it did look pretty good.  Night bartender was very friendly.  Enjoyed our visits very much.
Good food and great music! I would recommend giving this place a try! My friend and I both ordered burgers which were delicious
Cold wings! Think they just flew in to Antarctica. Once y make it ...its cool...,literally

We visited Kid Rocks twice during our few days in Nashville, in fact it's the only place that we went to more than once because it was that good.  It is a Huge Venue with multiple levels, each level with a different band and we made sure we visited all the levels.  The best bands are playing on the first level for sure!  The staff is very friendly, the drinks are pricey, the food was pretty good.  The atmosphere is awesome.  What we really appreciated was that the bands are loud but not so loud as the distort the music.  The rooftop level had a lot of smokers so that was our least favorite floor which was unfortunate because it provided a cool view of Broadway and some of the other Honky Tonks.  Would definitely recommend Kid Rocks to anyone visiting Nashville and wanting to have a good experience.

YeeHaw, Kid Rock! Great addition to Nashville's vibrant Honkey Tonk scene. Such a fun atmosphere. Well laid out. Engaging staff. Rocking band. What more does a staycationing girl need?? Even on a Wednesday at 2pm, this place was happening. Here's why I like it compared to other Honkey Tonks:
1-Prosecco. Because, Prosecco. 
2-ample seating
3- elevated stage for easy band viewing 
4-the kitchen got my order right! Burger/Med Rare.. and it was actually medium rare! Oh, it was good, too!
5-attentive clean up crew. Every time we finished a glass or a plate, it was promptly cleared. 
6-I wasn't the oldest one here ;)
If you are visiting Nashville, I can recommend this one as a true taste of a Lower Broadway Honkey Tonk and I have been to them all. I may start here from now on when I bring friends to see what this unique Nashville scene is all about.

Great customer service from the bartender. I was walking by and was surprised that this place was open. I have been seeing them working on it for about 3 months now since I been coming down town Nashville. 

I sat at the bar and was immediately waited on by the bartender. I ordered a drink and she brought it to me with a smile. I could tell she liked working here. Then, I had to ask if Kid Rock has ever been there and she said at least two times within the last two weeks. She said one of those times was on a Friday both times were unannounced. 

Information:  They are open Daily from 11am to 3am. Their phone number is 615-248-2706.  This is called Kid Rock's Big Ass Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse. Yes, I know that is a great big name but,  that is what it says on the sign outside, and on their menu that they gave me.  They listed their address as 217 Broadway on their Facebook page. However, I saw the numbers 221 stamped above their door at the front entrance. So, that was confusing but this place is big and may have taken up two old previous businesses. 

Music Venue:  They have bands that play here even during week days in the middle of the day. I was here on a Tuesday about 3pm and they had a band playing. They were great too. They played some hits of today's entertainment society too.

Mixed review Alert! While the music and entertainment was absolutely Awesome all night long . The food was just dreadful, Kid Rock if you read this ... if your gonna have the words Steakhouse in your name.. have decent steaks.. yes I did order steak at a bar.. bad mistake the $38 ribeye tasted like it came from Walmart and my dad cooked it. PBR is $7 so have a buzz before ya come . Again.. entertainment was top notch.. Food was garbage and grossly overpriced
