We went to a show at The Basement East but as soon as got there we realized we were hungry so we popped over to The Beast Pub for a quick sandwich and noticed that it was also happy hour. We went up to the bar and the bartender was probably the nicest bartender I've ever seen in Nashville! He told us to find a seat and if he took too long getting out to us that we could come up to the bar to order. We were in a bit of a hurry so we decided just to order with him at the bar and the drinks and food came out super quick. Our drinks were I think $7 each and they were doubles since we were there during 2 for 1's. Both drinks (tito's and tonic and jack and coke) were both great! Then the sandwich came out, I don't remember what it was called but it had ham, jalapeño bacon, cheese on an amazing sandwich bun, seriously, one of the best sandwiches I've had in awhile. We were able to quickly pay and get over to catch the show. If all venues had bars/sandwich shops connected I would probably go to more shows. This made the show even more enjoyable, a full stomach and a lightly dizzy head! haha!

Very interesting museum dedicated to Johnny Cash. Admission is a bit pricy - $16 per adult. It pretty much covers Cash's entire career and family life. Very interesting for a Cash fan. I found the competing audio clips to be very annoying at times, but it was tolerable.
Very cool multi level bar. Bartenders all have uniforms & look put together. Fair drink prices, fair pours & entertainment on every level.
Everything was great except for the service.  The girls behind the bar were second to none!  Exceptional. Love this place.

Visited for the first time on 12/27/18. My friend really wanted to eat here, even though it wouldn't have been my first choice. We chose the third floor, which was definitely less crowded than the first and fourth floor area. Liked having the live music on each floor - all different too. For a Thursday night I thought there could have been more servers - seemed like there was only one for the floor, but there were two bartenders. Ordered drinks and those were tasty. Food seemed pretty standard for a bar. Would have liked to have had steak but I thought the prices were pretty salty. So settled for a hamburger with fries. Seemed like it took quite a long time for dinner to arrive. My meal was good and I had one friend satisfied with her meal and another friend who was not. The server and the kitchen were gracious about the order problem and fixed it - just took awhile.
Given the number of available places to eat in Broadway in Nashville, I would try a different place if I were to visit again.

You aren't going on the general Jackson boat for the delicate food you'll eat lol. My group and I, 25 of us in total got to enjoy the lunch cruise and we had a great time. The buffet consisted of butter lettuce with a lot of cubes of random cheeses, the only dressing available was sour cream based aaahhhh! There was coleslaw, it was alright. The hot food buffet was a spread of yellow and brown stuff, a soft rainbow of unattractive foods: mushy tasty carrots, velveeta Mac and cheese, mashed potatoes, pulled pork, fried chicken and white rolls with butter. See? Yellows all the way lol! My very health conscious self managed though: I had a ton of lettuce (a few cheese cubes snuck in there), I got carrots and I topped the thing with pull pork (pork was good!)!! I enjoyed that very much :) Deserts were on the table: industrial pecan pie slices, sugar bombs, wasn't bad though! I ate half of it and hid it under my napkin. Meal comes with unsweetened tea and coffee at the end! Pretty cool, but again, it's not about the food, it's really about the amazing show! 
The show takes place as we go down (or up) the river all the way to downtown Nashville where we make our turn. The music is phenomenal, we have an hour of live music in the main room with our meal, the artists keep on changing their outfit, and they are on! Really want to dance and sing along, the ambiance is awesome! When the show is over, you can leisurely walk around the many decks of the boat. I suggest you check out the upper deck where more live music happens during the second half of the cruise, and see the deck below and in the back where the red paddle thingies that power the boat are located! Awesome to see and to hear. 
I loved it, it is touristy but it's totally worth it! The music is phenomenal, if you like yellow food, you'll have a blast, and you get to be on a historical beautiful boat!! Woot woot!
If you come to Dierks Bentley's you won't be disappointed. Come enjoy good music, a good atmosphere, and some pretty good drinks!

Food was good -- better than expected. Music was loud -- louder than expected. Hiking up 23 flights of stairs to the rooftop bar was hard -- harder than, oh you get it. Good thing I found out about the elevator before we left.

Nice view from the rooftop deck. I can imagine this place rocks after dark.

Overall, if I come back, I'll remember my earplugs and enjoy the music more. Service was great, portions nice, prices reasonable, beer selection okay.

TIP: They had an elevator in the back of the restaurant :-)

I try and five a place the benefit of a one off night, but this place has disappointed 2 times in a row. Terrible service, food is mediocre at best and cost is ridiculously high. Keep walking, there are way better places than this.

Mr. Rock pulled this one off with precision when he decided 5 stories, 5 different bands, 5 different parties!

This venue sits in the heart of Broadway and offers rooftop, open, and high visibility seating. Each layer has been separated and noise cancelled as to not interfere with the accompanying vibe of the party above or below. 

Drink prices are fair, staff was friendly and prompt oh and wearing eye welcoming clothing. 

In Nashville, you'll need to do you rounds, but don't leave Broadway without dropping by and giving em a try!

I'm glad we did it but for the price tag I probably would never go back. Just a bit pricey, even with the discount for buying online ahead of time and it seemed to have gone by super fast. This place could definitely have used a few more wax figures and maybe be a little more interactive. But hey I get to check this off my bucket list and have pictures to prove i was there. It was cool but nothing that knocked my socks off.

Had a great discussion with the Owner offline so I'm bumping up a star. They really care about their guest's experience, and I appreciate the effort made to follow up with me. I'll look forward to giving this place a second shot when I'm back in Nashville.

I had a nice time here for the most part. "Devil without a cause" I'd highly recommend if you plan on getting a cocktail or two. :) The only thing I'd say is that it took a pretty good amount of time until someone came by our table top to take our order. Other than that, it was all good energy. The band/performers stay engaged with the crowd which was pretty cool as you do not see that often.
Best bar on Broadway!! Each floor has its own vibe & live music. It's a good time! Be prepared to spend money!! The drinks are strong, but they are expensive. The bands charge $20 per song request.

Came to Nashville two years ago and enjoyed this bar immensely, came back December 2018 and returned to our old haunt- was so excited. Ordered tap beer and a bottle beer- the lite beer was flat and when my nephew told the bartender (short haired blond with an attitude the size of broadway) stayed  "the tap was just changed, do we want her job to check?" Ummm no, new beer- never offered went to the end of the bar to complain with a coworker. Five minutes later, she came over and I stated she should give the couple who bought our beers their money back- she offered a bottled beer- we were leaving, again I stated we were leaving she said don't yell at her- What? Then the bouncer came up to me to ask me to leave. Absolutely, you bet I'm on my way out, but my point- I wasn't drinking- I took a sip of my nephews beer just to taste the flatness, I neither yelled nor was unruly. I just wanted her to know she should not have charged for the beer. My advice- if your in the Nashville area for fun, stay away from this bar, they are trying to take advantage of those under the influence.  So disappointed

We went here for the first time last night and we were super excited. But it was a let down, we had a good waitress, but the food was just ok nothing special. We tried to get a shirt but the lady who they had to go get had an attitude with us, like she was pissed she had to help us. We asked for sizes in shirts and she half ass looked and said they didn't have any. So we just left and we will not be back.

I am down with the 'Man In Black'!  This museum was a 'must see' for my visit to Nashville!  I am was glad that this museum did such a great job of capturing some of those lesser known facts about Johnny ..such as all the movies he was in during his life!  

I enjoyed seeing Johnny's costumes, Grammy's and the personal letters that are in the museum collection. 

I enjoyed watching the YouTube videos of performances from the 60's-2000's.  There are also listening stations where you can listen to various artists who have covered Johnny Cash's songs-such a great!  

At the end of the tour-there is a section dedicated to the cover of the Nine Inch Nails song 'Hurt'!  Awesome tribute!

It is a small space, be patient with the crowds and enjoy! 

Tip:  Do yourself a favor and purchase tickets online--will save you a few bucks!

We came here twice while on vacation. The first time was with our children in the afternoon and we all had a good time. The band playing was very good and engaging, especially with our kids, who had a blast dancing around. The food, drinks and prices were all at or below prices comparable to places around. I will say I didn't try the steak, which seems to be what they're known for. The server was swamped and seemed tired, but she still husteled and everything was correct. The second time we went was at night for drinks and the place was packed, we made our way to the rooftop where there was a 90s cover band and they rocked. We really enjoyed ourselves.
Tl;dr Great honkey tonk, decent prices, will be back when in town again.

I would give this 2.5 if I could. I know it's new and I'm sure working kinks out. 

The place looked awesome. It's a whopping 5 stories when you count the rooftop bar. The bottom two are kinda connected. The second looks over the main floor entertainment area. The stage was cool. Two tier. Very cool.

The bar on the first floor was terrible. It was huge. And that's not a good thing. The actual counter was so deep I could barely reach my drink because the bartender just barely set in on her side. Had to almost climb on top. The drinks were SUPER weak. It was $11 for my cranberry and vodka and it was basically watered down cranberry juice. 

Maybe we'll try it again sometime.

We love going to museums, but this one is extra special. 

I find this place packed with amazing collection of Mr. Cash memorabilia, instruments, costumes, awards, handwritten lyrics and other items in the best designed museum I've seen.  Heck, it even has his original Amex card!  

Self-guided museum with numerous videos playing and iPads throughout provided details on his life and his career.  The tour shows information that most people were not aware, like Mr. Cash was in the Air Force stationed in Germany in his early twenties. Although we learn about this adventure, we don't know what influence this may have had on his career. This kind of ambiguity occurs throughout the museum, so you get an informative but superficial understanding of who he was.  Maybe it was designed that way as we all know Mr. Cash was a man of mystery.  

Plan on spending some time as there is so much to see. It can get crowded especially if weather is uncooperative.  One part of the museum that caught my eye and really enjoyed was a small area where Mr. Cash is projected on a flag while he says "Ragged Ol' Flag." 

This museum sets a standard for others to live up to. Whether you're a fan of the Man in Black, or even casually interested in this American icon, this museum is a must see. 

Cafe and gift shoppe on site.  Located just off the honky tonk of Broadway Street.

"People call me wild.  Not really though, I'm not.  I guess I've never been normal, not what you call Establishment.  I'm country."  - Johnny Cash.

Cool spot on Music Row to check out live music.  The night started with a cover band then it got real country when the main band came on.  Music row was interesting, every single place had a live band and the energy was fun.  I now feel inspired to take in more Nashville country music.  It's intense.

I like some of his songs but not a fan of the museum. Small walk through that is a short period of time spent in there. I went in because of my group and if it wasn't included in our pass I wouldn't have gone. Small but some what informative

I really enjoyed my time here, but you absolutely have to pack your patience. I went on a Sunday around 2pm and the place was packed. They try to stagger the line so that not everyone can enter at once, but the signage is small, the hallways are narrow and a lot of the fun is listening to the headphones and recordings. I was shoulder to shoulder trying to read the information, constantly waiting in line to listen to the features, and frankly just a bit too annoyed for having paid $16 ($2 off for having visited the Ryman) for a museum that takes about an hour. The museum is brand-new and beautiful though. They have a ton of memorabilia and it was absolutely worth a stop, but try to go first thing in the AM.
Michael the guy with the beard was so friendly and professional. We will definitely come back!

This place is new and I'm not quite sure it knows what it's doing yet, but Kid Rock stopped in the night we were there and it was pretty cool. 

3+ floors - we never went high enough to see if there was a roof top.

What a great tribute to the Man In Black. Great museum. For the man Johnny Cash was, I thought it would be a bigger museum. It was pretty awesome though. Loved the Johnny and June related parts of the exhibit. It was also nice to see the items from his friends in the original tour. Great place to see when in Nashville.

AMAZING server. Mimosa tower. Pass on the food. 

Came here for brunch on Sunday and loved that they had live music. The first floor was packed and you seat yourself. 

We were seated in the corner by the back. Our server was the best! She was friendly, upbeat, and was always around when we needed something. 

We ordered a mimosa tower. It was huge, but def a novelty item. If you're a larger party, I'd weigh the pricing. It's $30/person and has 3 bottles of champagne plus orange juice. We asked about the price for a bottle of champagne and it was $30. 

We also ordered brunch. I ordered eggs, soft scrambled, bacon, and country ham. My eggs were over cooked and cold when I got them.  The bacon wasn't crispy. The country ham was good, but a small serving. 

Will come back for the music and atmosphere but not the food.

The Listening Room is a must if you are visiting Nashville. 

Be sure to go to their website and get tickets in advance. 

My friend who is a local got us tickets and surprised us by not telling us what we were doing.  Otherwise I would not have known about this place and I would've missed out on so much. 

The listening room is like a comedy club where are you sitting in a room at tables, ordering food and drinks before and during the show while watching a performance. The difference is, the performers are songwriters and extremely talented musicians and singers. The songwriters that I saw the night that I visited had written number one hits and were all so amazing!  Before this night I didn't understand that most songs are not written by the actual performers or famous people that we see on TV. They are written by other geniuses!

The food was pretty good too considering you go for the performance not the food.

Just go!  It will blow your mind!

A great option for downtown- good music and decent food. Service is great (although can be slow depending upon staffing- when we were there the second floor bar had only one bartender and there were people waiting a long time for drinks). 

If you're looking for anything other than bar food, this would not be the place. The place is pretty clean although I found the bathroom attendants rather odd.

I think your experience here is directly related to how much you like Johnny Cash,?he's not a personal fave for me, but I love music and music history, so I'm glad I visited to learn more and pay my respects to a towering figure in American music. Warning,parking in the lot across from the museum is total ripoff, 15 bucks for an hour and a half is almost as much as admission itself and that's not nearly enough time to digest all that this place has to offer. Fave part was the Sun Studio section, folks tend to forget about Roy Orbison starting at Sun.
The museum is interesting but way to expensive for such a little museum. Most of the things you could do is listening to his songs which you can do on the web as well.

Johnny Cash is an American treasure.  A voice born deep in the hills of rural Arkansas.  A baritone that rumbled like a train coming down the tracks.  A countenance that resembles a broader, stockier Abraham Lincoln.  His music subscribed to the "less is more" philosophy, meaning that by the way of instruments most of his songs consisted of only an upright bass, acoustic & rhythm guitars, and a steady drumbeat that when played together created a driving "boom chicka boom" sound.  His vocal instrument was like a shotgun and once the trigger was pulled the message was delivered with a distinct, down home clarity.  He told stories.  He made us feel sorrow.  He could even make us laugh.  The music is timeless & is woven into the soundtrack of our lives.  

The Johnny Cash Museum is located in a humble, two-story brick building on 3rd Avenue in downtown Nashville and is within walking distance of Broadway.  The Patsy Cline Museum is in the same building but on the second level.  I only went to the Johnny Cash part, so this review is solely for the Cash Museum.  It is open daily from 9am - 7pm.  I ordered one ticket for the Cash Museum over their website.  It cost me $23.80 total.  

I was so excited about going to the Johnny Cash Museum that I wore all black.  I mean, what else should you wear when visiting "The Man In Black"?  When entering, you'll pass through the gift shop & once you exit the museum part you'll end up back in another part of the gift shop.  

The museum is very compact & it covers most of the major stages of his life, beginning with his impoverished childhood in Arkansas.  His last name may have been Cash but he grew up poor.  There is a bale of cotton in the museum that hammers home the fact that as a child he used to pick cotton.  Some of the other stages in his life that are covered is Johnny Cash's stint in the military (his Air Force uniform is displayed), his Sun Record years in Memphis, Cash the historian, Cash the humanitarian, Cash the patriot, Cash the born again Christian, Cash the elder statesman of country, and Cash's eternal love for his wife June Carter Cash.  June died in May 2003.  Johnny died four months later.  

Though the museum isn't very big, there is a lot to see.  There is a bust of Johnny Cash.  There are lots of outfits that were worn by Cash and June.  Many of his music awards & plaques are on display.  There are photos of other musicians who recorded their own versions of songs made famous by Cash.  There is a display dedicated to Cash's backing band, The Tennessee Three.  There are several stations where you can put on earphones & listen to songs recorded by Johnny Cash.  There are a couple of small rooms with benches where you can sit down & watch recorded Cash performances.  I went into one that was showing him singing a haunting live version of "The Long Black Veil."  There is another small area draped in red, white & blue that features Cash's poem "The Old Ragged Flag."  

You can have a picture taken with Johnny Cash!  I stood by a green screen with a black guitar they asked me to hold and then they took a photo.  After a few minutes, it was printed and it showed me standing next to The Man In Black himself.  It cost me $19.61.  

Some very small criticisms of the Johnny Cash Museum are:  

1) Even though it's mostly dimly lit inside, they don't want you to use flash cameras when taking pictures.  

2) There is no tour guide.  A tour guide would come in handy if you have questions about some of the artifacts.

3) I could be wrong, but sometimes I felt like they wanted to make Cash out to be a conservative Republican.  There's nothing wrong with being a conservative Republican but Cash was more complex than that.  You know this by his actions & his music.  Yes, he shook hands with President Nixon at the White House but while he was there he talked about prison reform, sang a song with anti-Vietnam lyrics, a song about America's mistreatment of Native Americans, and his famous "Man In Black" (a song dedicated to society's downtrodden).  Cash was a man who could sing about Confederate soldiers in one song and then sing about John Henry in the next one.  Cash was conservative when it came to God & country but at the same time was socially liberal.  

4) I didn't notice much about his first wife, Vivian Liberto, whom he was married to for 14 years.  Maybe it's because she wasn't a famous singer or it could be due to the fact that he was still married to her when he got involved with June.  But then again, I may have overlooked that section if it was indeed there.  Either way, June turned out to be the true love of his life. 

Those criticisms are minor, though.  Overall, I enjoyed the museum.  They also have a nice gift shop.  I purchased a Cash bobble head and a Music City shirt for $57.84.  I rate the Johnny Cash Museum a four.  It is a  must visit for every Cash fan.

Cool place, good vibes and live music! Right on the middle of all the action, on Broadway! There are many places to stop along this street, so go where the music draws you! It drew me here at the moment I passed by. Service was great and fast by some beautiful ladies, and the music was fun and crowd pleasing! Drinks were flowing and party vibes were in the air... And it was 2:30 pm Friday afternoon!  These Nashville people know your to have a good time no matter the day! So much fun...Enjoy!

Fun bar, great entertainment, TERRIBLE employees!!!
We were in Nashville Oct 11-14. We were on the roof top on Sunday, not busy at all , three bartenders standing around talking, we called them over 3 times while they laughed and were rude!!! 
Then we went to the main level , friends we were with ordered a top shelve drink and she poured a well drink and charged them for the top shelf. The bartender and her friend sitting at the bar kept staring us down. Employees there are so RUDE!!!!  

Any bar in Nashville - watch your money they all try to rip you off by giving you the wrong change.

I love Dierks Bentley so I wanted to love this place but it was OK. The beer/cider selection was limited. I got the Chicken and Waffles and it was fine. Not outstanding or anything.

It's pretty small - first floor with live music was full so we went to the rooftop. The bartender on the rooftop was a little aloof. She was a little slow when taking orders, bringing the bill, bringing the check back so we could sign it. We had to go ask her for it.

I probably wouldn't go back for lunch/dinner. Drinks and music would be fine, but even then, no hurry.

This museum is not large, but it is fun. I am a Johnny Cash fan and he is one of the only country artist that I have grown up listening to (sorry...more of a classic rock guy). My wife and I really enjoyed the museum...the history, learning about his life. It took us about an hour and a half. You could breeze through much quicker if you want because it is not very big...or if you read everything it would take you even longer

Its like a bigger dossier version of the bluebird cafe.  Great performers.  Downtown location. Valet parking.  Great cocktails.  The food is okay.  Eat at the southern or Ichiban
instead and then come here for music and drinks.

Not too much to say here.

Very terrible expensive drinks.

Limited food menu. Price was ok for Broadway. Taste was average.

Staff was average. Friendly enough but not overly helpful.

The main level stage was neat!

Johnny Cash is one of my BFs favorite artists so of course we ventured down to Broadway to come here during our time in Nashville! 


We loved it! A lot of stuff packed into the exhibit. It was so neat. Loved all the photos of his family and the personal elements like the China he and June had in their home. 

Definitely would return on another vacation to Nashville.
We got super lucky one night and then not so lucky the second night. So recommendation - ask if you can kind of see who the performers are. We got an Asian guy and two white ladies who were FABULOUS.

Very good music venue in Nashville. They are located up on the second floor and the entrance is very small until you walk in to go upstairs, so you could almost miss it. 

Went on a Saturday night in the summertime with my wife and some friends; only took us a few minutes to find a table even though it was busy. Also, $ 6 a person for cover-not bad at all. It is a bit narrow when you go in but there is a LOT of seating because the area goes pretty far back. 

I did not try the pizza they serve but the service for drinks was good. I didn't have to wait long at the bar and they even had servers coming around to your tables to ask if you needed anything regularly. Drinks are pricey but that is expected because it's Nashville. 

The music wasn't bad-not much country being played so that's different for Nashville. I really liked seeing those who were performing playing multiple instruments-one minute a guy is on the piano and then a few minutes later he would rotate to the drums while others rotated to the pianos. That's when you know they are good! 

They will play anything-but the more you tip them the better the chances of your song being played. At times it got a little rowdy and of course LOUD, but still a fun time. I will definitely try to come back when in Nashville.

I just went in this place tonight for the first time. In fact this is my first time in Nashville. The guy at the door has a personality of a nail. He asked to see my ID. I tipped my hat to show my bald head. It was just a joke. I'm 61. He just stared at me and told me since I don't have an ID that I need to leave. How ridiculous. I just smiled and took out my ID and told him to lighten up. I was just playing. He demanded I understand that there were 16 people behind me and he was in a hurry to check everyone in. (there were not 16 people behind me. Far from it) 

So I go to the bar to order food and then the blonde bartender asked me to speak louder when I told her what I wanted on my burger. I told her I wasn't going to speak louder and you would of thought I'd just spit in her face I guess. She gave me this go to hell look. I wasn't ugly to her. The fact is is that I had just come to Nashville to record a song the next day and I didn't want to blow my voice out. But she looked at me with this smartass look. I repeated to her what I wanted and she did hear me this time but turned around to ring up my order but did so in such a rude manner. Still had this stupid smartass look on her face. Rude as hell. So I told her to just forget it and I got up to leave. As I walked away she turned around and said some smart ass remark. 

Before leaving the front door I told the rude door "kid" that I'm leaving because the bartender was as rude to me as he was. He tells me to leave and points toward the door. What a dip. 

I don't know who runs this place but I'll NEVER step foot in this place again. This first home I walk in and I get treated like this. Rude terrible attitudes towards me and I didn't do anything wrong. I'm not going to just post this here. I'm going to go further than this. You owner/managers of this place need to get rid of the "punks" you employ. I didn't deserve to be treated like this. I did NOTHING WRONG. You made me feel like I did. 

Oh and before you stick your foot in your mouth, "no". I wasn't drunk. I don't drink. Haven't touched a drop in 6 years.

Cheesy, overpriced, and disappointing!  
I was fooled into expecting a beautiful cruise with spectacular city views and a nice dinner, a la World Yacht in NYC.  Silly me...there are no such views in Nashville, LOL!  It doesn't even pay to go onto the deck, as all you will see is swamps and warehouse parking lots.
The dinner reminded me of my high school cafeteria.  My friend paid $15 for a 20-ounce soft drink in a cheap plastic boot-shaped container.  Many of the patrons were drinking what looked like colored sugar water, certainly overpriced diabetes bombs.
The show was only about an hour long, and did not begin until 9:00.  It is a long, boring time to wait until 8 for dinner and 9 for the show, when the boarding time is 6:15.  Be prepared for a lot of sparkly costumes and a predictable salute to America.  May God bless those awesome musicians, who would probably be playing a jazz gig!

Kid Rock's is the place to go because there is plenty of room (no wait), great service (I am going to marry Austin), yummy local beer selection

Not sure what was better the music (on the second floor) or Austin (our server). I thought Austin posed for this beer but he said NO!

The bouncers verbally and physically abuse women in this establishment and they get away with it. Why are there several reviews describing abusive behavior by bouncers towards women, and yet NOTHING is done about it? Do not support this business in any way.
We had the BEST time, with fabulous food and drinks. Jake is the best bartender in Nashville! You will not be disappointed!

This place was lively. We went here for private party but can you imagine if it wasn't a private party this place would be shoulder to shoulder.  Two bands were playing tonight and both were amazing and lively. Love how the mixed in 90s jams in country style. The only concern for this place was the men's bathroom was small...three urinal that was very close to each other...don't know about the women's bathroom. Bartenders were pretty quick on serving everyone that came up the bar. Table 
Staff and security kept our table clean as much as possible. There was food at the party and only tried the rotisserie chicken which was moist and tasty.

I wish I could give this place 0 stars. One of the guys at the front was trying to get 12 girls to pay $150 to get in and then we figured out there was barely any line so we got into the line. Within 30 seconds, we were at the front handing our ID's and the guy said we cut and they wouldn't let us in. He was pissed he didn't get to pocket any money... after arguing for 5 mins we decided to leave. Guy holding my ID had no brain and couldn't figure out his buddy was pissed because he didn't get paid

So, I walk into this bar, cause my horse ain't allowed, wandered over to the bar while listening to the live cover of some ole country singer and I have to say this place was happening for a Tuesday.

So as I was waiting for service the bar tender was yapping to a whoever. I waited. I waited again and I realized I should just go over there and flag her down. Maybe slow night for her.

Music was actually very good. No, it was brilliant. Ole school country music. No twang. Cowboy shit. Make sense?

Menu is crap. It's a bar. Not surprising.

It's good country and western bar. I enjoyed the ambiance.

Music wasn't too loud unlike most bars on Broadway. First floor band was prepared and acted more professional while fun. Food came in 10mins, great service and fries were yummy. 5 floors so easy to find a spot to sit down

Typical club environment with overpriced drinks. It'd be cool if they did like most of the clubs in Broadway and have different types of music on each level. It's all country or rock. Kid rock started out as a rapper so it's strange they wouldn't play any rap on one of the levels. I probably won't be back unless they change the music, no way one can dance to country or rock

After having read some reviews this was not my choice to even stop in here but my husband wanted to check it out. I liked the open windows that allowed you to hear the band from outside. 1st floor is huge and clean decor. We had trouble finding a spot at the bar where we could order a drink from.If there was a spot for people to walk up and order it had someone sitting in front if it. We grabbed our drinks and decided to check out the rooftop. There was plenty of room and we hung out and enjoyed the view and the band for a bit. When the elevator doors opened on the 2nd floor and we heard the band we decided to just leave. Food was just not an option. Pricey and as difficult as it was to get someone's attention we didn't hold out much hold for good service.  I believe more staff would work out some of the issues.

This place is awesome! Walked in on a Saturday night just bar hopping and before we knew it, Kid Rock started to perform on and off. He also was giving the band that was playing a musical lesson. It was so cool. The atmosphere was awesome and drinks were reasonably priced for broadway street. The bartenders were friendly and we truly had a memorable experience. I hear kid rock is there all the time so I say pop in and check it out.

Came here specifically to watch a friend play. We just ordered beers, and no food. The venue is wonderful for live music. Sounds are amazing and most seats in the house are great with views of the stage. The beers are decently priced, good mix of local beers, good craft beers and even some mainstays if you're into that. The only complaint I would have about this place is that it smells like a college bar...like vomit. Immediately upon walking in it hits you. Our entire party thought the same. Obviously didn't deter us, we stayed and watched the entire show, but its very reminiscent of college bars.

If you are looking for good food and good service do your self a favor and do not come here. The food was average bar food and not a lot of variety to choose from. The staff was awful, rude, forgetful, and had a bad attitude. You could tell they didn't want to be there. However the atmosphere was good. The live music was great and the stage is awesome where the band performs. This is definitely a place you should go just for drinks and music. Not somewhere to eat.

Would of liked to go to rooftop bar to check it out as we did at all of the other singers places, but for some odd reason they wouldn't let people take the elevator?  Asked all to climb five flights of stairs up?  UH, no thanks, that doesn't seem appealing after drinking a few.  

So had one drink here on first floor and left.   Too many other options with roof top decks with elevator access to worry about going here again.   I am pretty sure that is illegal to not allow people on the elevator, especially due to laws regarding disabilities that people may have.

We were there for over 4 hours and music and service was awesome! We had the appetizers and numerous drinks and were very happy and ready for dinner and more drinks. Unfortunately upstairs where we were..the heat was on and they started opening the huge windows instead of shutting the heater off , then it was extremely cold and windy. We asked if they would close them and our server agreed and was very accommodating and did that for us , then they were told by management to open 3 of the 6 windows again. ( might I add everyone on that side left as it was ridiculously cold). As a business owner you would think that you would  like for your customers to be comfortable , also common sense says that if people are uncomfortable and complaining that they are wind blown and freezing you'd be somewhat accommodating. We left along with the majority of others and went elsewhere. What I got from my experience is they really don't care about repeat customers only the occasional weekend warriors. Kinda bad for them as in the long run it will eventually ruin their business. I could care less about Kid Rock as I'm sure his business is a write off... but his poor hard working employees will eventually suffer due to loss of tips and no return business.
The workers here are extremely rude. I understand that it's a really crowded packed place, but shoving a patron out of the way without asking them to move first, isn't acceptable.

Went in with my daughter who was celebrating her 30th Birthday and 1st visit to Nashville.  The bottom level was crowded with no room to sit so a police officer or security guard helped led us to an elevator for the second level.  My daughter is in a wheelchair.  There was no place for us to sit and have a drink where she could put her drink on a table.  There was only tall chairs and tables and the bar.  We wanted to like this place so I sat at the bar and she was next to me.  We were ignored for 10 minutes with waitresses all around us as we were not in a crowded area.  Not one acknowledged us for a second.  We ended up walking out disappointed.

Pros: good atmosphere, the band played good music, decent food
Cons: really loud, band was really pushy about tips, service isn't the best

DO NOT GO HERE. TREAT GUESTS HORRIBLY. My dad and brother had been at this bar for a couple of hours. My husband and I finally were in line to get into the bar after his flight got delayed and my brother hopped in line to meet us. The bouncers/security guard kicked my brother out of the bar because they said he had ditched the line (after he had already been in the bar for over 2 hours and just simply came to see my husband and I in line) After this happened we decided to leave because we thought this was ridiculous- my dad went to pay his tab and leave and the bouncers/security grabbed my 55 year old dad by his feet and hit his head on the pavement dragging him out of the bar. I have never seen anything like this in my life. Absolutely horrible. Cannot believe these security guards would treat someone so horribly. This place should be shut down for the way they treated my dad. Please hire new security at your door because this is simply unacceptable.

Going up and down Broadway in Nashville, not every bar is for every patron. But Swingin' Doors Saloon? It sure was up my alley. It's basically at the corner of 4th and Broadway, but you'll find the entrance on 4th.

My friend and I were looking for somewhere chill this past weekend with good live music, that wasn't a total $hitshow, had good beers on tap and between songs we could actually talk to each other. Swingin' Doors perfectly fit all of our criteria. When we popped in, we intended to stay maybe 30 minutes but ended up staying THREE hours. It was that much fun.

I don't know who the band was on Friday night but they were awesome! They played Freebird plus tons of country hits. I was waiting....waiting....waiting for a country song I knew and then right as we were gonna leave BAM! They played Sam Hunt and I was practically screaming BODY LIKE A BACK ROAD!

We had a great time people watching here. We grabbed chairs on the side and talked with tons of drunk girls, mostly there for bachelorette parties and also chatted with the millions of drunk guys after said drunk girls. It was hilarious. There were a lot of people dancing and some cute senior couples getting their groove on, as well. The crowd kept rotating so we had new madness to observe.

I was more pleased with their beers on tap than any of the other places we popped in. They had some local brews of which I had 3 and they ranged from $6-7 which I didn't find bad for a craft draft beer at a bar at all. Verging on cheap even. The bartenders were so nice and always very quick to take my order. Even the poor, handsome, barback was super friendly to patrons while they hit on him feriously. 

Swingin' Doors Saloon - Where country is King!

Tourist tap in Nashville. Bartenders don't care and they know people won't stop coming.  How about a smile and acknowledgement people? Didn't eat the food was on a liquid diet. Music was good and changed thru the night.
Was cruising around by myself on a Thursday afternoon when I could hear this band playing so stopped in. The place was full, great vibe & the band CRUSHED it.  Some serious talent!!

On a recent trip to Nashville, one has to pay homage to this legend.

I enjoyed walking through this treasure chest full of memorabilia. The history is amazing and the stories that went with each item really helped sum up his life.

The iPads were a pleasure to use. Embedded in a series of podiums with attached headphones, one can experience a glimpse of six generations of music.

The reading  of the dozens of letters in Cash's own hand fascinated me, I even teared up a few times. June and he truly had an amazing love story.

This is probably the single biggest party bar on the entire Broadway strip. It screams Vegas, and not in a good way. Definitely grimy like an old college bar, lots of screaming, and the service was actually a little rude. The band was a bit pushy with tips, and we felt awkward since we had just walked in and had no cash on us whatsoever. Needless to say, after snapping a couple good pictures out of their big open windows, we winded up leaving almost immediately because the vibe was not what we were looking for. Maybe on a calmer weekday evening this place would be more enjoyable, but on a Saturday afternoon it was not my cup of tea!
Rudest staff in all downtown! Won't let you in in a plain white T-shirt. Minus the fact I saw multiple people inside with white T-shirts. ‍
Really a neat place. Had a Cobb salad. It was good, by very salty. The music was good and service decent. We would go back, but nothing super special.

We had been to several other Honky Tonks up and down Broadway and enjoyed the energy, loud music and the crowds.  One afternoon we wanted something a little less noisy, less crowded, with a softer country theme.  We found Swinging Doors Saloon almost by accident.  As was our habit, we stood outside for a bit and listened to the music.  There was a duo playing at a softer decibel level, alternating between singing together and separately, and it appealed to us.   We went in and got a seat at the bar.   It was a bit early for us to be drinking, so I just ordered Cranberry juices.   When I went to pay the bartender said she would run a tab.  When we eventually got up to leave I summoned her over to pay.  She said since we just got juice, there was no charge.   I gave her a generous tip, tipped the ban and vowed when I come back, this would be my place.

We came in late Friday night. The first floor was packed so we took the elevator up to the Mezzanine. There is a bar at the end, standing room on one side and 2 rows of tables on the other side. We were able to get a low table on the balcony and had a good view of the band. There is no service at the tables so you have to go to the bar for a drink.

The sound and lighting were very good. The band played AC/DC, Metallica, Guns & Roses, etc and were very good, entertaining, and interacting with the crowd. However, every hour they came around with a tip jar. I don't mind tipping, and tipping well for really good service. I didn't like that they come to each table every hour and stop with the tip jar on your table.

This place is really cool but the bartenders think a 3 second pour is 1.5 ounces for $16. Wtf!! 

Get some legit bartenders who can make a $16 drink and I'll be back with my 15 people who spent a shit Ton of money but left sober ish

OMG... if you want to pay money for frozen water (that's science talk for ice), then come on down to Whiskey Row! I once went to a restaurant and had to pay for ice... just kidding, I never have. But it was such a nice experience having to pay for ice! And they loaded my tab up with a bunch of other stuff which was really neat! Like a tech fee...what the heck is that?! And the meals of the table to our left!They didn't take too long or give us any dirty looks for asking them to take it off... jk lol. Music was kewl though. 

Next time you want to pay for water, come on down to Whiskey Row!

Also, I felt like Helen Keller with the lights on my face.

Tried to stop in along the way while visiting Nashville from NJ. Bouncer told me I couldn't go in because I was wearing athletic shorts, although they were not athletic shorts at all. After explaining that to him he moved me out of the line and yelled at me to go "back to 2nd Avenue where I belong". Clearly discriminating against black people in a disgusting way. After I called him racist This POS door staff stood there smiling and laughing at me in front of the rest of the line. Ridiculous experience and this place didn't even look worth half of the BS surrounding it just to get in. Go to anywhere else other than this crap establishment

Hi Kevin- thanks for reaching out. pretty self explanatory from above and we can air it out right here in public. From previous reviews i saw this isn't the first time you've had problems with your door staff. Let me know how i can elaborate for you.

We were visiting from chicago and decided to walk down broadway since it's a staple! Stumbled in here randomly. The band was good! I'm not a huge country music fan but I really liked them. We sat ourselves per the sign but weren't greeted for a good 10 mins. We ordered drinks and i saw her actually bring it to the table next to us instead. The table next to us didn't even order drinks. Our drinks finally came after another 10 mins. We decided after the drink we were gonna leave, which by the way was another 10 mins for the check. Now i understand since it did get busy, but she never checked on us until we tracked her down to get the check. Nothing crazy special about this place. The drinks were ok. Probably won't come back here.

Our group was asked to leave from the balcony area. The bouncer accused us of "smelling like weed" which is decidedly untrue, as I have asthma and cannot smoke anything at all. He also claimed "his boss was watching the cameras" which was untrue because there were no cameras and again, none of us were smoking anything. No vapes, no cigarettes, and definitely not weed.

A terrible experience. Our group was nothing but quiet and respectful, and we were kicked out for no discernible reason. Which leaves me to go with the only logical alternative, which is that we were unwelcome for being a group including a gay couple and a black person. That is literally the only reason we could have been asked to leave, and it is extremely disappointing behavior from a business in 2019. As the name suggests, definitely not a place that winners would enjoy.

Such an awesome place. Kid Rock did it right. All of the staff we encountered were awesome. We ate on the second story and I can't remember her name but the tiny blonde girl who served us was so nice and helpful! I had the wedge salad and it was great. My sister had a chicken sandwich and it was good too. Drinks were GREAT! I had a cocktail with moonshine in it and it was so good!!! Sorry I can't remember more, I clearly had fun! The rooftop bar is pretty cool too. All floors had live music (at least on Friday night when we went) and wonderfully hilarious photos of Kid Rock throughout the place. Also, all of the bathrooms were super clean!! Cannot wait to take my boyfriend here next time!

Pros: JIMBO! This drink is bomb. I hate beer & while this is topped off with blue moon, you cannot taste it. The drinks aren't cheap but they're good & I appreciate that. We also loved the Australian girl band who played here over the past few days-super talented cover band with great audience chemistry & energy. As with many venues in Nashville, there are many floors here!
Cons: the first floor of this place gets PACKED. Also, the bar that makes cocktails is way too small & has virtually no seating around it. Lastly, we dealt with 3 separate bartenders who were all good, but NONE of who were pleasant. At such prices, at least fake a smile, people, cmon.

Noise, noise, noise. Turn the volume down management. Can't believe the city puts up with this dump having their windows open and music blaring from the first to fifth floor wide open all day. I'd never go back.

KEVIN B (manager in Arizona) 

He doesn't care about your comment even when he responds to you and gives his phone number. All he wants to do is sweet talk you and have you change your star  rating. 

He promises you that he will reach out to you about the outcome of your review and NEVER EVER CALLS YOU BACK. 

Keep your review and trust and believe he won't do nothing about your complaint.

Updating my review to inform all patrons of our latest experience. After our initial experience, Kevin tried to reach out to "right the wrong." He put my friend, who used her card, in touch with Chase, a manager. Chase promised to refund my friend in writing and even took her card information. Two weeks later, still NO refund. My friend has reached out to this establishment over via email and phone calls, consistently. This place is absolutely unprofessional. You do not offer to refund a group and the ghost them entirely. 

Do yourself a favor and stay as FAR away as possible! There is no worse experience in all of Nashville.

Yes people, it's loud I don't understand how  u can complain about this place being too loud? what the heck else is it supposed to be!!
This place certainly stands out as one of the loudest & biggest on Broadway, great location in the middle of it all no matter what time a day u walk by or stop in this place it seems to always be crowded.
First night in.. Very cool looking place the way it is set up, loveddd the glow in dark outfits the bartenders wear very cool. 
We sat down for drinks & tried some of the local beer a Southern IPA great beer nice taste. 
Second night in & it was even crazier during the weekend, this place is 5 floors, 5 different bands all playing a decent variety of music. the Mezzanine is a mad house too jammed packed. 
Second & Third floors are a mix of music, second floor has more of a bar feel to it. Final floor is the roof top nice set up & u get nice views of the city. 
One thing I'd like to point out are the bathroom, very cool mirrors & one of the cleanest bathrooms I noticed in the entire area. it can't be easy to keep this place clean with so many people coming in & out ALL DAY. 
This place ended up being a favorite for us because of the great vibes, only place I noticed real cops as security. 
Good atmosphere , quick enough service we definitely enjoyed our time here.
Really nice museum. Very reasonable price. Lots of memorabilia. Give lots of information on the man and legend.

Pretty pricy to get in, even with a student discount--you only save $1. The musuem is small and pretty much a maze, but they do have alot of information and his own items. it is well put together and worth taking a stroll into. youd be amazed by how many people johnny has worked with, and truly how much music he has. theres alot of information here and i love how well the musuem has his aritfacts and real life handwriting displayed.
I'm there at least twice a week and Jasmine is always rocking it keeping my friend's and my drink full. She's really nice and will chat it up if it's not busy.

I still don't understand the need for this "Tech Fee" that they are hiding in the bill. I could understand it if you came in and ordered a cup of water, but to eat and drink, that should be waived. They also have pretty poor management as their opening time is posted as 10am on the weekends but they don't open on time and there were people waiting outside with the doors locked at 10:30 this past Sunday.

We recently took a mini vacation to Nashville and at first we were afraid we would not have time to visit the Cash Museum. We were excited to learn it was open until 7 and that gave us plenty of time to add it to our day! 

The museum is really laid out nicely and it has memorabilia  in it from all phases of Cash's life. I grew up on country music and being able to see some of this iconic music history was a very memorable moment. 

I have visited many museums and toured lots of places but this has to be one of my all time favorites.  I loved the hands on section where you could listen to the same track on different recordings like for example the raw track, the 45 rpm, the 33 rpm and then the CD quality.  It was awesome!  The museum was also extremely educational and I learned things about this music icon that I had never known.  I think learning about his days in the military was my favorite part.

Try and budget enough time in when you visit to sit and watch the movie reels that are running in parts of the museum,  We saw footage of The Man in Black we had never seen!

While young children might not enjoy the museum, my 13 year old is a Cash fan and she was enthralled from the time the door opened.  I think she would have stayed all night. She knew more about him than even I did and taught me a thing or two as we toured. So glad we got to see this!  Look forward to our next trip!

The Man in Black certainly deserves his own museum and this one does what Nashville does best - it mixes history with splashy showmanship. Located right off Broadway, the Museum almost seems like a back room to the large gift shop and cafe at the front of the building. I wish I could give 3.5 stars as the objects were fascinating and the approach unique. 

After circling the construction-laden neighborhood for 20 minutes (there's no parking info on the website), we entered the lovely building. Somewhat orderly chaos surrounded us as people tried to shop, eat, and enter the actual museum in a very tight area. Let's not even talk about single-stall restrooms (one male/one female) in the lobby for all these people.

There are no dedicated windows for tickets, so you wait alongside folks that come in just to buy Cash merchandise. This was somewhat irritating and seemed like an easy fix to me. If you have two cashiers, make one for tickets and one for merch. Then everyone gets serviced more efficiently.

Then there's the line - they don't do timed entry, so there can be quite a line. Thankfully, they opened up a back door to let people in both ends of the museum (it's a circular path) and get things moving. Downside was that once in, we were packed like sardines. There's a good amount of interactive exhibits, videos, and artifacts to enjoy, if you can get near them. 

Timing is everything and I'd suggest going at opening or at the end of the day. Trying to see this small museum in the middle of the afternoon proved frustrating from beginning to end. They've done a great job with telling the story of Johnny Cash through the exhibits, but they could use some tweaking on the operations side to better serve a high volume of people in such a limited space.

Location, Location, Location..

This bar is my favorite I've been to downtown thus far due to its location, multilevel differences, rooftop view, and cleanliness. I would not recommend it for cheap drinks with high alcohol content or a crowded mess of people dancing funky in a dark room. Pretty much any other bar on the strip will give you that past 10:30 pm.

We hung out on the rooftop, at first, to sip $11 frosé and watch the sunset with the awesome reflection of the Batman building insight. It did not get crowded or rowdy at all and I really enjoyed my time there. When the sun went down we danced to live country for a hot minute on the second level then made our way to some amazing live music varieties on the bottom floor. This band was multi-cultural, incredibly talented, funny, and gave the crowd what they wanted. 

The bathrooms at Whiskey Row were pretty stinkin' nice for a downtown bar and I didn't have to wait more than 30 seconds for a stall which is vey impressive. Though there are like 100 flights of stairs to get through all the levels of this place, so maybe people just hold it until the next bar to avoid the trek. The security guys were nice and things seemed to be run pretty orderly. No complaints at all other than the prices of the drinks and lack of selection variety. I will definitely be back!

I'm dividing this review in two parts to be realistic about my experience. The entertainment and band that night was a 5 star experience and the guys on stage with acoustic guitars taking requests were incredibly talented and drew in the audience. We could have listened to them all night. 

However, like other reviews here, the food and service were just okay. It was a little hard to get the bartenders' attention for a drink and not the fastest or friendliest service. But once you do get served, if you order a mixed drink, pretty darn good! Lived the "TN punch." Oh, and the bathroom? Yuck...the women's room was disgusting and the stainless steel toilet was near overflowing. Come for the great atmosphere and music and to get "off Broadway" for a fun musical experience.

This place sucks. We've been sitting for over 40 minutes. Just wanna order some food. Have money to spend. We've asked 3 people to take our order.  Nothing. The band sucks. We are out. Won't be back here, ever...... again, this place sucks total ass......

We came here for lunch on a Thursday. Holllee was our server and she was pretty engaging. She helped us pick a few pretty great drinks. The food was pretty great, but there is a decent chance that the alcohol may have helped that opinion. Nevertheless, we had a great time and I would recommend it to anyone in the area!

We went on a Friday night around 11PM, and it was pretty empty. I was super surprised, it being a Fri night. The cover was $5 and the drinks are $5+. The musicians are amazingly talented!
They will play the songs that give $20 tips, and the may play dogs that give $10; $5 tips no way. We have a $10 tip for a song and they pushed it aside and clearly didn't want to play it, a Meatloaf song, yet they played a Tenacious D song. I really liked the Asian man, with long hair, he was good and personable. I think he was one of the late night replacements, for the two main guys. The main two guys were alright, a little too...vulgar-ish, for my taste. 
I probably won't go back again, it really is just a tourist trap, just like most of downtown.

We've been looking for a local place to call our hangout. We were greeted with enthusiasm. They recently changed ownership and management so they're running massive specials on bottled craft beers. The menu is no frills but EVERY burger is totally enticing. I ordered the avocado burger and the little jalapeño kick delighted me. My date ordered the BBQ bacon burger. Decadent. The onion rings were perfect and the crisp fries knocked me out.  

And... To address the reviewers who have commented that the fried pickle slices are too salty... Pickles are preserved in brine. DUH. 

I LOVE THIS PLACE. I SHALL RETURN.

Kid rocks!  Where the music is amazing!  Beyond amazing !  This bands play their a$$ off!   But..... the bartenders are rude and obnoxious and the drinks are watered down!  So sad bc this is such a great place to hang and drink in the heart of Nashville.   But classless bartenders who don't care about what they serve and make fun of patrons from across the bar, thinking no one notices, sad, pathetic and rude!   Thx Nashville!  A dime a dozen.

All the staff are incredible but a special heartfelt shoutout to Claire (from Australia). She made our day so special and we could not be more thankful for her understanding and going above and beyond to accommodate us. Thank you, more than you know, thank you.

When the man comes around you will probably find him here.  This tour is great for any fan of Cash.  I took my 18 y.o. daughter who knew very little of him and his music and she really liked the interaction with the cover songs and the mixing boards.  

You get to see his entire timeline from birth to his military service to his recordings and tv shows to his death.  It was somber the way they finished the tour with his cover of "hurt."

Be sure to stop here, it's worth the price of admission.

Literally awful. It's my first time in Nashville and this place was recommended by my hotel. The music was great but the food took forever to come out and it was ice cold with absolutely no flavor. They charged way too much for food that was mediocre at best. Terrible terrible experience. I would NEVER come back or suggest this place to a friend. I'd rather have Taco Bell.
Love the Arizona locations. I can't wait to get the pretzel! The cheese sauce is so good!

Had brunch today during Picks & Pints. This is an awesome, relaxed venue featuring talented singer/songwriters. We enjoyed their original songs and the stories behind them. Our server (from Ohio, can't remember his name) was excellent - he was attentive and friendly. The food was reasonably priced but was not great. The brunch menu was limited and the food was lackluster. Coffee was served in small paper cups which was surprising from an eco perspective and required more frequent refills. This was a great music city experience and we would definitely go again next time we are in Nashville. No cover, and artists work for tips.

Kid Rock built his own brand new four story night club, which has mannequin of himself on the roof dressed in a Santa suit. (It is the holiday season ya know).

This was our last stop Friday night on our Broadway bar crawl. The sound system on each floor was LOUD, The bands on each floor ranged from good to meh, and the drinks were poured fairly strong.

That's all I got to say, or remember.......

Wish I didn't even have to give a star at all . We came here after the football game on Sunday . Place was very busy on first and second floors . The 3rd floor was pretty much empty so we all settled in up there .i had  a chicken sandwich and we ordered steak . The cheese was not even melted on the chicken patty and  the bun soggy and the steak was to make you sick , both plates were cold and not even edible . The barmaid Julie waited  on us and Very very rude young lady who seemed more interested in leaning over the bar to show her cleavage  to the men at the bar then waiting on her customers . 
She was very rude , we can see why they put her on the 3rd floor because she is the worst sever I have ever encountered and  she should know that woman are very good tippers and we don't care about your bleach  blonde ponytailed hair or cleavage we just wanted our food cooked and hot and a drink   . No I would never recommend this place

Went in, ordered drinks and we did not get what we ordered. Now I'm no bartender, but I don't think a lemon drop can be hard to make? What we got was definitely not a lemon drop and for the price of the shot, it was a disappointment. Went upstairs to dance, but not much was happening and there was no band upstairs.
Downstairs the band rocked. I think this place is more for the name than anything else.

Reminded me of a dive bar, but with better-dressed patrons. And more patrons. The staff was friendly, but the crowds arrived in waves and overwhelmed the bartenders. 

Very good selection of beers, with full bar, and food available. We watched the guy in the back prepping hamburgers from fresh ground meat, so the burgers probably rock...but we had already ordered fried cheese curds. Those were okay, but greasy. 

As crowded as the place was, the joints directly on Broadway were mass chaos. It was pleasant to find a place that wasn't ear-splitting loud, away from the throngs. I'll go back, if I ever find myself in the area again.

I have seen several complaints about the food I just had a fresh hot cheeseburger and fries and a awsome bartender  named Ashley  ...i dont live here but I'll be back I'll promise you that .. I'm SW Detroit born and will support a fellow  michigander  all day every day

This place doesnt have enough love on Yelp. This place is awesome. One of the last and best of the classic honkey tonks left in Nashville. Also, in my opinion, the best buffalo wings in Nashville, and the best old style country country that isn't at Robert's. 5$ pints of good beer, and no tourists. Little Jimmy Dickens used to frequent this Tonk, and has a plaque at his seat on the bar. RIP!

Fun place. There are 4 floors of live music which is amazing. We ate some wings which were okay, a couple beers and some well vodka drinks and we had a great time. Everyone there was just enjoying themselves so that was cool and the service was attentive and prompt. 
We would definitely return.

Dierks Whiskey Row in Nashville is lit! This multi level honkey tonk is the best bar in Broadway. I highly recommend the second story which is more of a club. The first story has country music. The DJ on the second story was legit. By far my favorite bar on the strip. Guess I know where I'm going again tonight.
We had the best time tonight! Angel is one of the best servers I have ever had. She is a gem! Way to go Big Bang and thanks again Angel!!

OK so this place is new and it is obviously working through a few growing pains.  That being said, I'll explain my reason for giving it two stars.  First, as mentioned before in previous reviews, they only have one bathroom on the first floor.  For everyone. Men, women, customers, employees.  Just one bathroom.  I visited on a Monday night and still had to wait in line every time I went.  Just not acceptable for what could and should be a flagship destination bar in the heart of Broadway.  There might (and hopefully are) more bathrooms upstairs but when I was there only the first floor was open.  So that's what I'm basing my judgment on.  

Second, there weren't enough bartenders and waits on drinks were long.  This has also been mentioned in previous reviews but needs to be reiterated.  What I thought was odd was that there was a TON of security there but not nearly enough staff to get the drinks to the customers in a reasonable amount of time.  And I'm all for feeling secure and being safe.  But for a tame, nondescript Monday night it felt like overkill and I feel that the manpower could have been better allocated.  

There are positives.  The location is fantastic and they have a nice interior with plenty of TVs.  It might be a nice place to watch a game (if you can get drinks without waiting forever).  I feel, and hope, these issues will be addressed as I think this place has great potential.

Mixed review.   We have spent time on the 2nd floor on two different occasions.  Both times the band was great and the table/drink service was fast.   However, the 3% tech fee is a load of crap.  Drinks are pricey ($11 for captain and coke) and even paying cash, you're subjected to a 3% tech fee.   WHAT?    What is that?   Plenty of other places to get drinks, hear music and not pay some bogus fee.

Only a die hard Johnny cash fan will find this "museum" worth a $15 admission. There were some interesting things in there but that's about it. 

If, let say, you were able to go through a smithsonian in a day then this museum will take no more than half an hour. 

Overall I feel as though it's a waste of money.

Nashville was so fun and friendly EXCEPT for this place.  Unfortunately there was a rude red headed server who decided to ignore us except when she felt like we closed the window.  She told us if we closed the window "management would be up her a$$".   We did not close the window.  It bothered he so much she kept saying something to us about the window but couldn't get our order.  She then sent security over to tell us not to close the window..... he proceeded to slam it open..... and scolded us too.  Rude!  We got up and walked out.

We were just passing through Nashville and decided to try this place for dinner. It was a Wednesday evening and they had a live band (they were awesome, as well). We tried their 8 oz steak and it was melt-in-your-mouth delicious. Their garlicky sauce was an unexpected, delicious addition to the steak, too. I would recommend it to everyone.

I was in charge of hosting a party for a group of women educators who were attending a conference in Nashville. Living in California I worked with Blake to organize this party over several months.  First I called restaurants all over town and the price here was more than reasonable.  We had a great variety of food and everyone agreed that the food was yummy and plentiful.  When I arrived at the bar, the tables were decorated beautifully and the furniture was arranged to accommodate our group.  The two people who worked during the time of our party were attentive, helpful and efficient.  There were almost 90 of us.  If you are having a private party in Nashville this would be a great location.  They are easy to work with and our group had an enjoyable time.

Oh man, this was my favorite places in Nashville! The live band was playing a little of everything. I heard Sublime, Aerosmith, Tom Petty, Eminem, Pearl Jam and the very best Led Zeppelin. I only had beer here but the bartenders were on top of it. The place was jam packed yet the line went quickly. I highly recommend this place.

Everything about our visit to this place was "meh".  The service we received from the bartender made us feel like we were a bother to him and he paid us almost no attention. We got draught beers, which were fine, and we ordered the hummus plate. From the pictures we'd seen in reviews, it looked like a thoughtfully crafted plate. Our was not so beautiful- I wish I had taken a picture. There were a few pieces of pita, several green zucchini pieces, and three piles of the chunkiest hummus I've ever seen. It tasted okay but the presentation was pretty gruesome. There was also no live music at 4pm on a Saturday (which I realize we could have researched further online before choosing this place) so we weren't doing any listening at the Listening Room! Maybe if we came later in the day we would have felt more welcome and better served.

Paid way too much for so little. Love Johnny cash! They truly got you - for the store. You had to line up for tickets with everyone buying stuff from the store. I think I'm just used to more organization and this was just not laid out well at all. 
Line entry goes back toward the bathroom!! Nothing blocking you from walking straight and not seeing the turn toward the opening. Next ya walk in and be careful not to do what we did - we went down the narrow pictured wall and turned RIGHT to the stone wall and followed that right OUT THE DOOR AND DONE. Nothing showing you you had to walk LEFT To more displays. It was wayyyy too crowded. Toooooooo crowded. 

Better organization would be awesome. And less about the store and more about the musician. Not impressed.

Great show!  Very talented actors and singers!

The food was good and we didn't have to wait to eat.  We were served as soon as we walked in!  A nice Christmas dinner with turkey and ham.

Fun adventure to go on while visiting Nashville!

It was very busy.  Sat on third floor.  Kinda disorganized was surprised waiters and waitresses did not have assigned area.  Tried ordering food and asking for no cheese due to dairy allergy.  That is not possible.  Everything is pre done.  Probably will go back only for the music and beer not the food

We were in Nashville for 3 days and listened to a lot of live music (often with food and very cheap drinks) and i don't know if the cost of visiting listening room is justified. The food was average at best and the singers were alright. The tables are probably first come first serve , we arrived 30 mins before the show and were seated in the corner .

Insanely loud, grossly overpriced and just not any fun. Even concerts aren't this loud couldn't talk to anyone beyond 2 inches. Not doing it again. $11 for a shitty Jack & Diet. Actually, I just dropped this place to a 1 star since I'll never go back. Sorry Bob. Your bar tends should be trained to make a decent drink.

So disappointed in Kid Rock's, one of my favorite places to listen to music now charges $2 for a cup of ice water. Really? Normally I would have given this place 5 stars. I cannot believe the boss is good with this. A guy who prides himself on making his concerts and drinks affordable. Please reconsider this one folks. If nothing else it promotes responsible drinking. With so many choices in Nashville I think we will be looking for a new place until this policy changes.

Doors never open on time, rain, sleet, or snow.  Plan on standing outside for 15-30 minutes past the time the venue says they'll open the doors.  Why stand in line, you ask?  Why not just show up close to showtime?  Because The Basement East doesn't provide nearly enough seats for every patron or even 20% of patrons to get one.  So unless you're there when the doors open, you can count on standing throughout the entire show you paid to see, and even if you are there when they finally open the doors, there's still a good chance you end up standing.  For example, at a recent show I attended at The Basement East, there were literally 30 seats available for a crowd of probably 150-200 people.  Don't waste your time or effort with this venue.

I really wanted to love Kid Rock's place because the atmosphere was fun and the music was some of the most interactive and we experienced in our short time on Broadway. However, our fun was overshadowed by a few things.

First, good luck trying to get the attention of the servers at the rooftop bar, especially if you're female. My friends and I all watched guys around us repeatedly getting served when we each kept trying to get the girls' attention at the bar and finally a server named Savannah came over to one of us standing by a table and took our orders. She was the most helpful person we could find after a while! (Thank you Savannah)! 

Second, Once we got our drinks they were so watered down and full of ice it wasn't worth the wait or the price.

Third, the every ladies bathroom stall on the rooftop level were completely out of toilet paper that afternoon! We had to bring paper towels in with us but I am pretty sure it's not good to flush that stuff, so women were just throwing them on the floor. Unsanitary! I would have let a gal at the bar know if I could get someone's attention, but...

Some very simple things...fair and friendly service and t.p. can go a long way right?!
I mean it was the middle of the day! Fix these and it could be a great experience people would come back for.

People will come here for the name, regardless, so why try too hard? But what a shame there's not more of an eye on quality control that could really turn something good into great. For me, a disappointing visit.

The positive? Great rooftop vibe, views, party atmosphere and hearing Kid Rock's music in between live band sets.

This is one of may favorite bars in Nashville. First of all it is huge inside. It has a lot of class for it is an old Nashville home turned into a bar. On one side of the bar is three or four rooms filled with pool tables. They have a digital jukebox that downloads and plays any music you like and it takes debit/credit cards or cash. The pool side also has its own full service bar. The bathrooms separate the two sides so it is a good halfway point, there is also a vintage cigarette machine outside the bathrooms, which is so neat. The other side of the bar is more club/lounge atmosphere. Here they have a huge bar, dance floor, DJ, and tables and booths to relax in the background and watch people make fools of themselves after too many cocktails. You know the normal night life people you find anywhere. This is a great place to hang out, and it is walking distance of more bars and food, which is a must for all post-partying. The only negative I have is parking can sometimes be a pain, but it is downtown so what do you expect? Just know you will eventually find a spot, sometimes it is easier than others.

I knew that I'd have to visit after getting a recommendation for this place the same morning. I was visiting Nashville for the first time just last Thursday and was told about the writers round concept, and I highly appreciate singer-songwriters.

I didn't know about reservations, but it wasn't an issue since there was a lot of seating. I paid a $7 cover charge to listen to the four acts. Each performer offers a backstory then plays the song, and it's really neat to hear that some of their songs made it big. I'd definitely come back for the talent that you can find here.

They also had a $7 minimum purchase policy, so I ordered a coffee and turnover with ice cream. Yum!
It was great. Excellent atmosphere and lots of fun. The music was awesome. We didn't get a chance to eat but enjoyed everything else about the place.

Floors upon floors of fun! You can enjoy a different experience on every single level. Drinks ain't cheap and you are paying for the experience, but there is something for everyone. Including a rooftop bar with beautiful views. The best music is on the first level in my opinion, but make sure to make your way up the stairs to check out everything. A must stop in Nashville!
All Nashville bars are fun but love this place. Our bartender Malory dominates and probably the main reason why we had so much fun.

This place is awesome.  I can't say enough.  Good food and reasonable drinks for Broadway St in Nashville.  The 2 story stage plus 3 other floors of live music is awesome.  This will be my go to place every time  I go to Nashville.

They say he's cocky, but he says What? It ain't bragging when you back it up! And he brought everything here to back it up, probably the nicest place on Broadway right now. Huge building with 4 floors of goodness and different music from country to the 80's to classic rock. And the man himself might do a surprise show up and do some songs (some friends were lucky enough to see him!). Got some beers and a half fried chicken, the food was surprisingly good, I say that because bar food is usually for tipsy people so they can drink more, but this one was good-good! Try all the levels and different music styles, also the view is great from above, have fun!

The RUDEST bartenders and staff I've ever encountered in my life. Yelling at guests trying to spend money in your establishment. Lost other guests credit cards behind the bar and said "oh well" and didn't offer apologizes when they found it. Had security remove a girl for throwing trash in a trash can. I mean this place was a joke!

I tried to buy a T-shirt and the bartenders said "no" and gave me the finger. Well then.... 

The live band that night was great, but that was the only great thing about it.

My advice to others, just avoid the place and save yourself the trouble. Plenty of live music to choose from with more attentive/friendly bartenders

I've been to Whiskey row a few times on a Friday or Saturday night and i always have a blast but i stopped in yesterday for lunch when i was on my way to work and i must say i was pleasantly surprised with the daytime atmosphere. The live acoustic band that was playing was awesome and the staff was so nice and welcoming.
