When i first looked over the food menu i was a little disheartened because i am a pescatarian and there aren't many option for non-meat-eaters but i will say that there are a lot of dishes you can modify. For an app, i had the shrimp fritters and OMG I'm obsessed, they are sooooo good and the portion size is perfect. Then, for my entree i had some fettuccine pasta dish, that originally had an assortment of meats in it but i modified it to only have shrimp, and it was really good. The sauce was creamy and seems homemade and the dish was very flavorful. I'm definitely going back there to get some food again in the near future.
Bartender was wonderful!! Food was ok, music was AMAZING!! DZZI  hope to be back!! Much love from Scranton, PA!!

Really disappointed in the hospitality. Been ordering drinks all night and asked for a water and was charged $2!! Trying to be responsible and was penalized for it. Upsetting a business would want to profit from something that is normally free especially to someone who has been paying for drinks all night. Won't be back.

This was our favorite bar in Nashville! Every band that performed was top notched and involved the crowd. The performers were exceptional especially Officially Nothern! The bartenders were extremely polite and not a typical busy bar service of ordering and running but actually talking to you! Love this place !!

Dierks, I love your music and we were so excited to come to your bar tonight. The band was a lot of fun and the only reason I'm giving the place 2 stars. At the end of the night it was a complete down pour and I was waiting for my uber which was at the light across the street. I was standing in the awning to avoid getting soaked. Your security boys repeatedly pushed the door into my back to push me onto the sidewalk and would not let me back inside to escape the rain when I asked. They threatened to call the police which I told them to do because I had  broken no laws. My friends and I celebrated a birthday and spent a significant amount of time and money at your establishment. I never expect to be treated that way simply to get into a safe ride home. Shame on your staff. I was not belligerent nor drunk. No one should he treated that way.

Dang it Beast Pub! You were my favorite! I hate that I'm updating my review, I loved this place, it felt like a hidden gem that I was always so excited to tell people about. First off, in the past month and a half I've gone 3 times and walked in to private events. Yikes. There's been no signs heading us off, we have just walked in to parties...awkward! But the real kicker is their new menu. So the old menu had these amazing sandwiches and chips and queso and a basket of chips for $1 so hanging out on their fantastic patio munching on a basket of cheap chips insured that we kept buying drinks...now there's no cheap munchies. On our last visit we saw the new menu and asked the bartender if that was it because there were like 8-10 things listed. She seemed like she's getting a bit sick of answering that question and she said that there's a new chef and he's awesome. Sure, he may be awesome...but where's any of the food that we used to come here for? We decided to get the chorizo tacos for $8 and they came out pretty quickly and they were okay...flavors were good but suuuuuuuper greasy, also it was just tacos, no chips or anything with it. So from now, we will just go for happy hour because their 2 for 1's are pretty great still but we won't be getting food anymore. Bummer Beast Pub...bummer.

This honky tonk has several floors and one of them is bound to tickle your fancy.  They have live bands on most floors and lots of seating so you never feel too crowded or crushed.  They have a roof top deck as well and all of the floors have windows that open up to keep the air flowing.  Came back both nights we were in town.

Pretty cool place. We did not eat. Not sure they had food, but the music and the vibe was great. Set up nicely. They handled the crowd well and it was crazy crowded at 3 on a Thursday afternoon. Good beer. Good service. Good music.
Beware !!! we were there and Tiffany the bar maid never gave our debit card back and said she did. Had to cancel the card the first day there.

This was one of my favorite live music experiences in Nashville. I could easily picture the talent we saw Amber's Drive at the Listening Room Cafe breaking out and making it big and I assume their other scheduled gigs are equally impressive. The sound system and acoustics were excellent! The venue is spacious and clean with friendly staff. You can reserve a seats online and they start seating 15 minutes before the performance. The hostesses have the system nailed down and quickly seat guests. We placed a drink order and our waiter had our cocktails well before served before the show began.

The drink menu consists of an excellent selection of drafts, cocktails and wine. While we only partook in drinks the food smelled delicious and looked to be large portions. I ordered a malbec and later a champagne cocktail named berries and bubbles. 

If you love live music seeing a band at the Listening Room Cafe while in Nashville is a must.

For $16, you can take a look at some of the coolest pieces of Johnny Cash history. You don't need to be a Johnny Cash superfan to enjoy the experience.

They have a lot of materials about when he served in the military, some of his art work/photography, and a whole section dedicated to his TV career. It really made you appreciate how widespread his influence was.

They also don't sugarcoat the times in the 80s before The Highwaymen when he didn't have much mainstream successes.

There's a whole other theater room set up that focuses on Cash's other label-mates on Sun Records (including Ray Orbison and Elvis). So that was an extra little surprise.

The entire museum is pretty small (at the end of the museum, there's a station set up to play the "Hurt" video nonstop, which you can hear from half the museum, which is a bit jarring). The staff told us it would take an hour to see everything, but that's mostly because they had music stations set up, each with 4 videos you could play. Kind of a let down there.

But everything else was super fun.

The new facility is really beautiful! Bought the tickets for me and my date ahead of time through the Listening Room website and it was very easy. Loved the complimentary valet parking! Food was good and show was great but I have one major complaint. Again and again, I was told there was a $15 fee beyond your show tickets. This means that you have to spend $15 on food and/or drinks. It was never once specified that it's $15 PER PERSON. We thought it was per table so we were stunned with a larger bill than we anticipated. We just came to see a friend play and weren't expecting to pay $40 beyond our tickets. This distinction needs to be made more clear! We left very annoyed. Definitely less likely to return for future shoes unless there's someone playing that we specifically want to see.

I was very underwhelmed by my experience, to put it politely. I'll start with a few "positives". My group went around 1:00 on a Saturday, and we were able to get a table pretty quickly; however, we were a group of 8 and our table only had 3 stools. Had we waited for a larger table, it would have been much longer... not a big deal, though. The "light man" was able to turn the lighted spotlights down very quickly and easily at our request on his iPad and he was very friendly and happy to accommodate. Prior to running into him randomly in the middle of the bar, I had to wear my sunglasses in the room because a spotlight was directly in front of me and beaming into my eyes. The bartender was very friendly and was able to serve me my drink very quickly.... something I only had to do because our waitress, Hollee, abandoned our table and only answered questions when we sought her out elsewhere in the bar. On to the negatives.... I'll try to summarize these. 1. We ordered drinks as soon as we got a table, over the next hour and a half, our waitress never returned to our table to refill water or to ask if we would like to order more. 2. We ordered 3 appetizers that we never received, and were told the food would be "comped." Call me crazy, but you can't comp something that you never served or gave to a customer - no favor done there. 3. WE approached our waitress, Hollee, 3 or 4 times about our food and check. We were told she would check on it (but she never came with an update), another time we were told the food would be right out (not the case, our order was "lost and missing" per the manager). The WORST part about having to approach our waitress was the fact that each time we spoke to her about our order, she never felt the need to ask if our table was ok, if we needed anything, nor did she EVER apologize for the service, or lack there of, that we received or for the food that we never got. 4. They comped half of our drinks, I suppose that was nice, but when we approached the manager about getting a full comp due to the time waisted and awful service, we were told the discount given was all they were comfortable giving. 

Riddle me this Dirks Bentley's Whisky Row... if I had come in and JUST ordered drinks, and my waitress neglected to come to my table and check on me or take additional drinks orders, and I had to approach her 3 or 4 times about my check (only due to the poor service...  may I add), wouldn't you agree that ALONE would be deserving of an apology and 50% discount? Do you not put a high priority on your customer's experience? 

Readers, don't take your chances at this place. Let this be your warning.

This bar rejected my aunt because she didn't walk across the street correctly because of her neuropathy which happens sometimes with cancer survivors. We tried to explain to the door guy that she walks that way because of her neuropathy. Still denied us, so if you're a cancer survivor and have neuropathy I wouldn't recommend this bar to anyone. Guess if you can't walk they won't let you in. #fuckcancer

I was pleasantly surprised by this bar! While every bar on Broadway is busy, I felt like the bartenders were quicker & more efficient then most places at making sure everyone got drinks and didn't have to wait at the bar for a long time. In addition, this building is probably one of the tallest rooftop bars on Broadway, so we had really good views from the top! I loved the multi level style with different vibes on each floor. My favorite room was the 2nd floor with a live band performing crowd requests, including rock and 90s options that everyone got really into!

Don't do it! Didn't check rating before we came in and sorry for it. 30 minutes to get part of our food. Another 10 minutes get a side salad that I told them to forget about. Burger came out undercooked. Wait staff apologetic but too many restaurants down town to provide such poor service.   Dierk needs to check in on "his" places.

We are huge Kid Rock fans and we were looking forward to visiting this restaurant while in Nashville. After reading some of the reviews, I was on the fence... Definitely not the case. We were greeted as soon as we walked up to the third-floor and had excellent service throughout our entire visit, thank you so much Chastan!!!!  The view was amazing, especially since the NFL draft was going on. Small menu but that is a bonus, easy decision making. I would give him five stars but I CANNOT agree with the price of beer nor did they have his bad ass beer, which is odd and disappointing since it is his restaurant! Six dollars for a regular Budweiser was a bit ridiculous!! Still a cool place to hang out but not if you want to talk with anybody, it is pretty loud. Hopefully Mr. Kid Rock is getting ready for a fish fry!

The "one star" rating does not reflect the performers or the performance overall. Unfortunately, I have no choice but to rate General Jackson's show boat one star due to their lack of customer service. I was on vacation in Nashville and was scheduled for the daytime cruise. The signage outside the dock is atrocious. We couldn't find the dock and ended up missing the boat. Talk about devastation! I called general jackson customer service to see if there was a way to use our tickets for the next day or even pay a penalty fee to reschedule. Let's just say the customer service rep's have a thing or two to learn about "southern manners and hospitality" . No way were they budging! We had to buy tickets all over again. Fast forward 24 hours, a few tears and sniffles later, we boarded general Jackson's showboat and the rest is history. Overall, Buyers-beware!!! Arrive at least an hour early to prep for parking/actually locating the place....Then sit back, relax and enjoy covers of Jesus Take The Wheel and other country classics!

If you are really drunk and don't care if you get the right order....  Silverware... Napkins....food... This is the plac for you!!!!!   3rd floor female bartenders are NOT friendly.. 1 is friendly she is of Asian descent.  The rest are nasty attitude ESPECIALLY if you order a SODA.   I did order 3 drinks with th soda.... So im not sure why that was wrong.    
Sorry Kid Rock.... Your place will only last based on location.

I think our waittress tried... By they threw her into the firey pits of hell and didnt  care if they sent her out with the correct orders.
Sent wrong order...  The plate was sent back to kitchen.. They had the waitress try to convince us it was correct.  Poor poor poor management skills!!!!!  I do not blame the wait staff!!!!

Got the steak salad. The steak was like gum, impossible to chew. AND the food took an hour and half to even come out. Even the fries took half an hour. Especially for the terrible quality, the place is overpriced. 

I asked for the hockey game to be on one of the hundred TVs and my request was ignored. 

Music is good, but not worth it considering the rest of the awful experience.

Loved this spot. The rooftop bar was very nice. Overlooked the entire strip and nice views of downtown. The ground level bar was spot on for drinks and prices were comparable to the other clubs. The band that played was really awesome (with a fiddle player too!!). After jumping around from a few other bars, this is where we spent the majority of the evening. I will definitely be going back!!

I frequently visit Shineworthy Tea located right next door and have been eyeballing 360 Burger for awhile now. Their signs boasts BURGERS, BEER, & LIVE MUSIC. Sounds like a winning combo to me! I went inside to take a look around and place my to go order. All burger and fries combos are equally set at $10. I ordered the cilantro avocado burger because the pictures looked absolutely mouth-watering! My girls got the bbq burgers. Let me tell you our disappointment when we got home and actually bit into our food. All three orders of fries were soggy and all three orders were bland. My burger had not one bit of spice to it and it's supposed to have habaneros and jalapeños mixed in. I could've fed it to my 3 year old and he wouldn't have flinched. I don't even believe they used salt and pepper. The only thing I could taste was the bun. I asked my girls how their burger was without telling them anything about mine. Both of them made a face, told me they didn't taste like anything and they'd rather have a burger from Sonic. When a kid says that, that's bad! I will give them a second star because the server taking our order was nice and the inside of the restaurant appeared to be clean. I later asked my group of friends that I meet up with if they've ever tried 360 Burger and if so what did they think. Every single one of them said the food was terrible and management keeps changing hands. I'm so disappointed. I was truly hoping to have found my spot! Looks like my search continues. Don't waste your time. $30+ right down the drain.

What a delicious burger Joint. Everything was delicious, whether it was the chicken wings, the fries (waffle or sweet potato), or the burgers themselves. Just melted in your mouth. If you are feeling healthy, order a side of steamed broccoli... Cooked to perfection. Definitely will be coming back. But they do need to work on server speed. I have been here twice now and BOTH times the service was so slow we considered leaving. Unfortunately, there aren't many places to go in this unsavory section of Nashville at night.

I was visiting Nashville with my family, and being a server myself always am very critical and extra weary of wait staff, especially in such a high volume busy establishment. Our server Ally was literally the best server I've had in a long time, let alone on Broadway in downtown Nashville. Even though I could tell she was busy and running around the entire restaurant to get to tables she always made sure our drinks were full and engaged in conversation with us which made me and my parents very impressed. I wish all servers could be this attentive and passionate about their guests and we will definitely remember this bar to talk about when we go back home! Also the live music on every floor was amazing, didn't catch the names of the bands unfortunately.
We have been sitting at a table on the roof for 2 hours and not one person has come to take our food and drink order!!

Honestly the best thing we did in Nashville. If you are a fan on live music - you MUST go! The music is phenomenal and we loved that it was a spotlight on the song writers. It was incredible to hear some of our favorite country songs from the people who wrote them and the story behind them.

The music and drinks are alright. There is a $15 minimum per person which we didn't mind since we both ordered two drinks. The nachos were very average, but we had great service. 

Definitely go at least 30 minutes before the show to get the best seats possible. I really can't recommend this place enough!!!
This bar has a really cool atmosphere.  When we was here it was packed wall to wall on each floor.   Great spot to catch live music.
This place was extremely high energy with a lot of different music on each floor. The roof was really nice and the service quick. The drinks were expensive, but it was right on broadway.

New management, new menu, not coming back.

The food I ordered wasn't right. And when asking the waiter about it, the man said, well, that's how they do it in the kitchen.  Wouldn't try to ask how to make it right, offered nothing else, just a smart mouth.

The exact same thing happened to my wife, her sandwich was completely different than what it said on the menu, is was a complete rip off. And we got no help in correcting it. And the waiter was just completely rude. Mr. 4164 Sommers.

Thanks for screwing up one of our favorite places, we will not be back.
I went on this riverboat on a law-enforcement conference, it was all you can eat and all you can drink. You just can't beat that!

ASS CLOWNS!!!
These idiots that say it's to loud (It's a Fucking Honky Tonk, that means loud music every day, all day), bars are too big, and can't reach the other side(What do you have, fucking T-Rex Arms?) Don't like the music (Go to another floor, there are 5 dumb ass) Rick Springfield, who doesn't like Rick Springfield? I have heard Bo Cefus, BB King, Elvis, Kid Rock, Motorhead, and every other artist past and present. Yes, I have two favorite places on Broadway!! Kid Rocks and Kid Rocks Steak House.

ASS CLOWNS!!!, pull your head out and enjoy life and stop bitching. Life's to short. Enjoy life or move the fuck on!!

Whiskey Row is a pretty cool bar, food was excellent and the bands that played there were all very good. Coming from Vegas it's a good time and they even have a little hip hop and DJ portion. My wife and I had a great time there until I was escorted out for swaying too much while I was peeing... yes I was in the bathroom and no I didn't miss the urinal. But I would still go again because even the guy who asked me to leave was very nice. Just an awkward encounter. So I went on about my night and had no hard feelings.
What a great place! I realize how much I didn't know about Johnny Cash. The man is a legend! So many interesting things about his life. I could have spent my entire day in his museum.

My husband and I were in town visiting friends and went by the Listening Room. We loved the writers performance and the food was great. We ordered the hummus plate small plate, fried pickles small plate that was sweet and spicy, and the tomato blt sando. I would order the small plates. The BLT was a little too much bacon and not enough of the other stuff. I would order a different entrée.

Cool atmosphere and great music/lax vibes.

Highly recommended for locals and tourists.

Overall this place had good music and multiple floors to accommodate a lot of people. The bar was reasonable but obviously more expensive being on broadway. The rooftop is really pretty with nice couches and worth taking a look!

It is so unfortunate that there is only ONE stall for women but three urinals downstairs for men. There were about 12 girls in line last night and no one in line for the guys. I simply opened the door to see how many stalls they had....I was then escorted out of the restaurant. Please get the women's bathroom situation under control and offer more stalls for us.

My 600th review is dedicated to the Man in Black, Mr. Johnny Cash.

I love Johnny Cash's music and persona. When I saw his daughter helped open a museum in Nashville it became a must on my trip. The museum is behind the wall of the storefront and is much larger than it first seems. 

First off they had a groupon deal which was basically BOGO. The normal prices are $15 and well worth it. The museum chronicles Johnny's boyhood all the way to his last years. From his first band to the Highway Men this museum covers it all.

One of my favorite parts of the museum is his music by decades. They have the decade listed along with a picture and 4 songs on a tablet. 

The museum shares tons of tidbits like:
- how his name was changed to JR to Johnny (hint the military played an act in that)
- he is the only artist to have songs in the billboard charts spanning 6 consecutive decades
- his stand on prison reform
- his many contributions to various causes to include Muscular Dystrophy and SOS Children's Villages
- he received two of the nations greatest honors. The National Medal of Arts presented by George W. Bush and Kennedy Center Honors presented by Bill Clinton. 

Where most people got a chuckle was one of the theaters that showed snippets of TV shows and movies he was in. My favorite was his SNL skit. And who knew he appeared in Little House on the Prairie?! They also had several outfits on display that June and Johnny wore during performances.

Towards the end of the museum I was in tears. This tour took me on a journey from Johnny's humble days working the cotton field with his family, to success and drug addiction, having his true love help him find a happy journey to the saddest moment when he lost his true love. This museum doesn't paint a perfect picture but honestly shares who the man was and still is too others. 

This museum is a beautiful tribute to Johnny Cash and his family. It is must stop in Nashville!
Tons of Johnny Cash memorabilia and exhibits.  If you're into the man, then you should head over here.  I'm not.  Maybe because my Dad named me Sue.

Disappointed by the service at Kid Rock. Had bought multiple drinks and spent 2+ hours at this bar...when we asked for waters we were told that we could not be given waters for our table. We ended up having to drink the (hot) water from the bathroom because the bar would not serve us. We were informed that if we wanted water we needed to pay for the water. Management, please rethink your service motto because people NEED WATER if they are out and drinking/partying. Please do better.

My husband I went here for a date night. We went to the roof at first to see the big fuss, it has a nice view and a bar up there and I got a pickers vodka drink, which is amazing . We decided to head downstairs, second floors didn't have much seating area, so we went to the bottom floor. We found two seats at the bar. We order fried pickles and their wings, both were super delicious. The cover band (I can't remember their name) were awesome and that man could sing!!!! It was a great night. Hope to go back again soon

Probably my least favorite bar I visited on broadway. We had been bar hopping all weekend so it's pretty easy to compare places. We were looking to stop in for a drink and sit down and listen to some music for a bit, before headed to the next bar. This place was extremely loud and you could not hold a conversation at all. However, I did like that they played more rock than country. 

The band was pretty good but once their set was done the leader singer literally went table to table with the tip jar, asking for tips and even interrupting conversations doing so. I don't know if that's a Nashville thing but I had not seen that at any other bars. And the immediately after a guitarist went around holding up the tip jar. It was just way too pushy for me. 

There are many floors to this place and the stairs to the rooftop bar seemed pretty steep. I don't how any drunk person would be able to safely get out of this bar!

Also I would definitely only stick to beer at his place. I ordered an $11 cocktail and the plastic cup itself was tiny. Disappointing to say the least.

Horrible service. Bar tender was great, but security is unprofessional and disrespectful. Situations arise and the necessary means we're not put in place to ensure proper treatment of patrons. We would recommend passing this bar up if in town, and visiting Luke's bar across the street.
My server Savannah recommended I order the Red Pepper hummus. So light and delicious! She knew exactly what I needed! Love this!
Ran out of steak... need I say more.  Ordered onion rings.. and they were horrible so I left.  Not going back.

I went through the line  they told me I could not get in because my hair is blonde & in my ID my hair is dark because It Was 2 years ago. I'm 23 years old and from Ohio, I don't know what they wanted me to do to carry another form of ID. Had my debt card and everything to prove it was me.

Location  - Prime spot right in the corner of Broadway and another main st forgot the name lol.

Venue  - Chill spot with multiple levels, but not as big as the other big contenders on the strip.

Music - Lots of different levels with different levels, but on the rooftop here its a bit small but fun since they do play hip hop and people can get rowdy.

Food - Didnt have any.

Drinks - Good pours and the avg going rate on drinks.

Crowd - Nashville has all the fun crowds just trying to have fun.

Staff - Friendly and nice.

Would come back and recommend it for that hip hop music on the roof top.

The rooftop is significantly higher than my usual rooftop spots on Broadway, but the heat lamps that warm the entire bar top make the INTENSE climb up the steps worth it. Although I didn't take many photos, I can say that I had a good time. The bathrooms appeared to be pretty swanky from what I could see. More info to come soon.

This place is terrible. The venue is nice but we went for lunch and had the chicken tenders and burger and you could tell both were sourced directly from Sysco. The chicken tenders and fries were the exact ones I served at the local country club when I worked there in high school. Only difference is that Kid Rock's Big Ass Sysco tenders cost double.

Came for a bachelorette party hoping for good things. Ordered a sprite and vodka and got just sprite. Took about 45 minutes for southern fries appetizer to show up and an hour for the fried pickles. The southern fries were delicious, but the pickles were just meh. The bartender was super rude and uncaring, I get it, it's tourist-y but a little niceness won't exactly kill you especially when you pay 11 dollars for a mixed drink that has an undetectable amount of well vodka in it. 

Dierks just put his name on this terrible place. Makes me sad to think this quality is associated with him. Pass on this y'all, so many other better same price establishments around. The terrible service, watered down drinks, and bad ambience make this bar a less than ideal experience. I won't come again.

Usually we have the best experience ever with Kelsey and orion!! We went there last and had the worst service ever from Madi on the roof top. She was the rudest bartender i have ever ...ever. I am a bartender in Nashville and the fact that i didn't tip her is really bad. She was insanely rude. And messed up my order then charged me for both orders ... when she fucked up my order she charged me double . She was absolutely awful.... Kelsey and Orion r the best people we have had and i won't go there if they aren't working again:

I will be back! Food is amazing - every item on the menu was fresh, creative, and "real". And such great flavor! I couldn't have made more perfect nachos :)

The prices are great for such quality and quantity. And the wait staff was excellent.

Absolute trash.  $20 song request only while they have a handfull of ones in their tip/beer bucket.  Like his music his bar is just as bad.  I feel bad for the bands begging for tips.  They would make mor money playing on broad.  Seriously save your time if you want real rock or country there's 15 other better options.  You only have to walk a block.  Also like downtown everything there is wayyy over priced.  So to sum this up. Bands suck, drink prices suck, and unless food poisoning is your thing walk on.  This bar is dying faster than kid rocks music has.  They don't just treat tourist like trash, locals get the same.  I'll be honestly amused when they close this down for anyone better. And God knows / the world there's so much to choose from.  Thanks kid rock the only decent thing about your bar is your bartenders you let work half dressed. #trash

"I shot a man in Reno / just to watch him die."

When in Nashville, the Johnny Cash Museum is a stiff requirement. Fans of country music, rock music, or modern American history are guaranteed a trip to down memory lane. Learn something.

As someone who's not a mere bandwagoner of Johnny Cash, there's a lot more to him than "I Walk The Line," I was often emotional while intricately reliving his life story. Handwritten set lists, stage outfits, military paraphernalia, rare recordings, etc. There is a TON packed into a very small space.

One of the things I found cool was the recording studio-style exhibit where you can put on headphones and mix Johnny's signs. "(Ghost) Riders in the Sky" with amped up vocals, bass and horns? Oh, hell yeah.

The downfall of this place is the opening exhibit. The content they've displayed requires a ton of reading. It takes a lot of time to go through it all piece by piece. The problem is the insane influx of people they let in at once. It's slow, and people are well, annoying. It's hard to see and move around.

Once you break on thru to the other side, there's ample room to roam around and explore. Mini theaters with old television performances, a hall of records and memorabilia from his entire life.

Johnny Cash is one of the most fascinating humans of the 20th century. The museum does him justice, a true slice of Americana. Pay tribute to the Man in Black.

Wendy on the 4th floor... theeeee best! Like holy cow. Things get crazy and hectic and busy and this girl keeps her cool, doesn't miss a beat, remembers everyone's drinks, and serves them with a smile! For out of towners... she's a beautiful introduction to southern hospitality! Actually all the bartenders on the 4th floor on a BUSY SATURDAY NIGHT we're phenomenal... but Wendy was a star. Rock on sister for your killer customer service!

We came to Whiskey Row for brunch - The food was absolutely delicious and our waitress was Savannah. She was amazing.  Totally on top of things and very knowledgeable about the menu. I am vegetarian and she was very capable of helping me choose an awesome meal. She was pleasant and kept on top of your drinks and keeping our waters filled. We will definitely be back.

Just came here for a quick Almond Vanilla Iced Latte and it was just what I needed on a hot day. I actually didn't go in the Johnny Cash Museum but I did relax outside the cafe to get some cool air. Although just being in the place, it made me want to check it out next time..they had some really cool Johnny Cash memorabilia. But as far as coffee goes..it's really good and the barista's were nice!

Great space and wonderful interactive experience with singer songwriters! 
If the owners read this- please make straws optional. You're adding 200 per show to the landfills; it's a wasted expense and adds to the enormous burden of plastic waste. If you must use straws use paper ones.

I'm not a big Johnny Cash fan, so two hours was more than enough time to spend here. That and four hours of parking cost $30 and we still needed dinner. Tickets are $20 pp for a self guided tour. 

I thought the costumes and movie memorabilia were cool. I think the exhibit about his influence in Hollywood was the most interesting. I didn't know Johnny had been in so many movies and special guest star on so many tv shows. My favorite dress was what June wore to the White House. 

Overall, very interesting information about him, but just one visit is enough for me.

A bit over priced for it was. I went because I had a living social. The prices on some of the things on the menu seemed a little absurd to me. The waitress really had no knowledge of the menu because they had a new chef and was trying some new things put... did they not have a tasting? 
2 for 1 mimosas- not worth it. Crappy orange juice or something but not the best mimosa I've had. 
The coffee was served in paper to go cups. Idk if they are new to the brunch and coffee game, but it was weird being served in a paper cup when there were people with mugs around us. 
I had the biscuits and gravy to eat, which was just alright- nothing to rave about. 
We went in around 1015, and it was pretty dead, but it started to pick up at 11 when the live music started. The music was great entertainment and very enjoyable. All in all, not sure if I would go back.

We had a great time on Sunday afternoon. Family atmosphere and good food with quality cocktails. We all loved the craft cocktails and being from California I was fine with the prices.  The appetizer we ordered was great, too. 

It's a busy place and Andrea our server helped us find a seat at a shared table and then moved us to an open table when one came available.  Bar service was slow, but Andrea kept in touch and apologized for the delay. She made our experience there welcoming and she was so friendly.  When we return I will request her section- she really built a nice rapport with us. Staff works so hard to keep everyone happy. 

The band was fantastic!  Again, great way to spend a Sunday afternoon. One shout out to Mike - as he hit the tables for tips and requests, he skipped ours. I hope not because we were three women...  I had a big tip ready for the bad and we were passed by.  Mike - don't judge! 
Anyway, the bagot their tip as I left - they were so talented. 

See y'all again soon- and thanks Andrea!

if you want to be blown away by some of the finest art in the world, you would travel to Musee du Louvre in Paris.

If you want to see the most incredible gardens you'd probably choose The Butchart Gardens on Vancouver Island or Cheekwood if you are visiting Nashville or live close by.

If you want to learn about the history of Rock and Roll, definitely head to The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum, located in Cleveland, Ohio.

An Elvis fan? No question - visit Graceland - Memphis TN.

Want to stroll the entire history of Country Music and every artist you can imagine? The Country Music Hall of Fame in Nashville is your destination.

BUT-
If you want to :
View the largest public collection of Johnny Cash memorabilia.
Experience a timeline of audio formats / video footage spanning his incredible career of 5 decades.
Read the Man In Black's personal handwritten thoughts, song lyrics, report cards, walls of awards, and many more interesting items. 
Get a glimpse into his personal life beginning with his childhood.
 
Find out why Johnny Cash is one of the most important musical and historical figures of all time. 
THIS is where you go. 

It's an incredible museum people of all ages will enjoy. 

You can spend an hour or an entire day being entertained by state-of-the-art audio and visual elements. The museum is self guided. 

Take the time to visit. You'll be happy you did.

Worst experience of our trip. The guys at the door were in no way personable. My gut told me right then and there not to bother but we were already committed ,I guess. We walked in and found a place at the bar. And we waited...and we sat...and the chick kept walking right by us never acknowledging us. I decided to use the restroom while he tried to get a drink. The girl's room is RIGHT behind the bar and stools. A one seater. Someone was already waiting for quite some time. I walked back to my husband who was still waiting to be acknowledged. I watch as the bartender walks back by without so much as a glance, goes back to the end of the bar and leans over chatting with someone again.  Not even worthy of one star.

36" ribeye $79.00. Do not buy. It's maybe 14 oz at best and tastes mediocre at best. Huge huge disappointment. The mashed potatoes are watery and bland. The atmosphere is great but the food isn't. The nachos are good. I really feel cheated on a $79 and a $30 dollar mean. Could have ate at sizzler and enjoyed it more.

I booked tickets online the day of and it was easy to do. I think the seats are first come first served because we arrived 30 minutes late and got seats in the back at the bar. It was fine though, still could see the stage well.

What I didn't understand was that once you get there, they make you order a minimum $15 worth of food/drinks per person. We didn't have dinner so we got the pulled pork sandwich and chicken fingers. Pulled pork was ok but chicken fingers were dry - terrible. 

But I didn't go there for the food so I'm still giving 4 stars. 

The music was excellent! There were four performers and they took turns performing. It was nice that before each song, they gave a short story about what the song was about. Fell in love with Lena Stone and Adam Criag ... they were amazing artists! The show lasted about an hour and half. 

I would go again if they didn't force people to order food or drinks.

The party at this place on a Saturday night was awesome and just what my group of friends were looking for.  I was in town for a bachelorette party with a group of 12 girls.  We started on the 2nd floor which had more of an upscale country bar vibe.  The band that was playing was great and there was plenty of room to dance.
We later moved up to the rooftop where the scene was completely different -- much younger.  The music was a DJ mix of early 00's and today (not country) which was definitely different from the country scene downstairs. This rooftop area honestly made feel more like I was back in NYC than in Nash.  Great view from the roof, but it was super crowded so it was hard to get to the railings to have an unimpeded view.  

The stair climb up to the roof top was a little on the tough side.  There were a ton of security guards all over the roof top.  I can definitely see why, however.  Lots of ROWDY people.  We had a good time nonetheless.  

I would definitely recommend this rooftop if you're looking to get away from the live country music scene for a little while.

Got nice, quick service. Server was very attentive and came by often to make sure we were happy! This was refreshing considering the other Nashville places that had ignored us. 
The entertainment was great and it seemed to have tables that werent totally crammed together.

Entertainment was good.  But I don't like getting ripped off, and I feel like I was last Monday 9/9.  After paying my tab, I see we were charged a 3% $1.71 "tech fee"...wtf is that?  I asked the bouncer what it was, and I got a b.s. non-answer.  Then I see that they charged me 13.5% sales tax.  Everywhere else on Broadway charges about 9.5%.  I presume they're pocketing the difference.  OK, so the two surcharges come to an extra $4.00 or so, no big deal.  If they were using the extra money to pay the band something, I wouldn't mind.  But they're not, it's just a sneaky way to pad their profits as far as I can see.
Good artists and fun environment but wow it was almost like a sauna in there. Not much air flow at all. Still fun but maybe get some fans working

Horrid customer service! I indicated I was a AAA member for the discount and handed the cashier my insurance card.  The cashier failed to take off the discount and we talked to a manager after the tour and he refused to give us the refund with my receipt and insurance card. He said there were no refunds after a purchase, but his employee made the mistake in not taking off the discount in the first place! It was only $2, but it was the principle. I am beyond angry and appalled at this situation!

Off of the main drag of Broadway but worth the short walk.  Great interactive displays from rare recordings you can listen to to clips of performances through the years.  Unfortunately, when we visited it was a little crowded and it was hard to maneuver around to see all the displays.  Lots to see in a relatively small space.

We went to many places down on Broadway but kept coming back here. The food is way above "bar food". The music is great--a broad range of genres to make everyone happy. The staff is very fun and helpful. The venue itself is amazing--great views and the sound is stellar. The bands we saw were so engaging and talented. We'll definitely come back when in town.

We were just looking to kill some time before the show at the Ryman so we thought we'd check out the Cash museum. He was a pretty interesting guy so it's got to be an interesting museum right? Nah, not really. I'm not a museum fan anyway but when my husband said "This is a waste of $15" I thought, "ok good it's not just me".

Maybe it was just too small and too many people, maybe there were too many "digital" displays and not enough memorabilia, maybe watching "Walk the Line" before visiting the museum is as bad as watching a movie before you read the book. 

Ok, I learned a little about him that I didn't know but was that worth $30 for my husband and I. I'ma say no.

 
Side note: They sell beverages and since our hotel didn't have vending machines we were quite thirsty so I asked the girl if I could drink it inside. She said no, which is expected of a museum  (even though everything is behind glass). I said "oh ok, I didn't know since y'all sell them". Her reply was "oh well you can buy it and take it in you just can't open it". Thanks...

What a wonderful experience when you are in Nashville! The singer/songwriters were out of this world. And seriously, I'm not a singer/songwriter kind of person. It's not really my jam, you could say. But they had so much talent I was just in awe. 

We had the absolute worst server ever, but it couldn't even dampen the experience. We still had a great time. The manager was very nice about the whole thing and gave us a discount for the poor service, so I appreciate his ability to see something wrong and try to make it right.

This is a must if you are visiting Nashville. You are guaranteed to hear some real talent, and if you're a country music fan, maybe a song you've heard on the radio! The singer/songwriters are working in Nashville and have sold songs to other bands and singers. Really awesome stuff.

This is a pretty amazing museum. Full disclosure: I didn't really know anything about Johnny Cash other than what most might from "Walk the Line". Definitely left a fan of this man and an admirer of his life.
The setup and flow of this museum is quite spectacular. It is a bit small and if you walk in with a large group it can take a little while to read and listen to everything. But they have a good number of individual setups that take you on the journey through his life, music, and lasting impact on the world. Everything is on iPads, which I thought to be quite clever and easy to navigate.
My favorite part was the station where they talked about Mr. Cash releasing songs on the most forms of media of any other artist, and let you listen to several versions of the same song...on two kinds of vinyl, tape, cd, mp3, and a random remix, which was quite hilarious.
Definitely worth the stop if you're walking around downtown and want to be inside for a bit!

So this would be excellent as strictly a bar. Back to back nights of walking into the establishment and there's absolutely no seating in the main area. Which this wouldn't be an issue, but we were told they only served the full menu of food on the first floor. Everyone at the tables were just drinking. No hostess. The setup is just bad. Like I said, if it was a bar it would be excellent, but the "amazing steaks" can't even be eaten.

I don't think it would be a huge deal but we went in back to back days and absolutely zero room to sit down and enjoy a meal. Don't serve food if you can't even serve people. There's a standing room at the top if people want to enjoy a drink. I actually saw no one eating because drinkers were occupying all tables.

Music was nice, food sucks , drinks weak, And since yelp wants this to be a longer review I just have to fill in some areas here, I cannot tell you it's a great place to go, the band on the first floor was good, very danceable, the band on the second floor was pretty good, the pretzel and beer cheese was OK the artichoke dip sucked, place looked a little grimy or actually a lot grimy but it was OK it is on the strip, and that's what you can expect from a tourist bar

Honky Tonky Nashy-ville is here! 

Live music & drinks & cool times here. Spent an hour here listening to a cool cover band. 

Not to much seating seating. Lots of standing room. LOUD. Honestly wasn't impressed at all. Very DIVE bar in my opinion. 

Packed and does get full. 

I only stayed on the bottom floor didn't make it to the top floors. 

Just aight. Won't come back...

The Listening Room is an awesome local venue for live local talent in Nashville. Best to make a reservation, but walk ins get seats too! 

Prices are fair and the serving staff are friendly and efficient. 

The food is decent - Te fried green tomatoes are delicious and the hot chicken is one of my favorites in the city (it's very smoky flavored).

On my first night in Nashville I walked through the large crowds and I heard really loud music. I looked over and saw tons of people having a good time on the balconies and thought to myself, "I need to go there sometime during my time here." Then the next day I found myself sitting there and listening to some live music.

There are four floors all with different bands playing. There's the main floor that has a large bar area and then a mezzanine one level up that overlooks the first floor. When I went the third floor was basically empty and there was no one there, but one more flight of stairs will get you to the rooftop bar which also had another live band playing.

I thought all the bands that I listened to there were good and it's in a great location right on Broadway.

Nice vibe and good entertainment.  However our waitress was terrible.  She took my food order, but not my husbands had to ask her take his order, had to ask for silverware she brought it after we had got some from the bar and we had finished eating, we had to ask for another drink and finally had to ask her to clear our table.

I really love this museum. The way it is set up you really feel one with this great artist. The fact that it is small makes it all the more intimate. I feel like this museum really provides a good account of the life of Johnny Cash and his career as a musician. It is a great place to learn more about him. It was pretty cool seeing all the great memorabiia that is housed here. Honestly I could have stayed much longer!

I like the fact that the number of guests is monitored. Since this museum is quite small this really helps. I did though at times feel like a lesser crowd would have made for a more enjoyable experience. I would give this museum a big 5 star rating, excpect for the crowd issue. I suppose next time I will go at a less busier time, if I can figure out when that might be. 

The staff was wonderful, friendly and attentive. 

Can't wait to share with you some of the pics that I took here.  

Johnny, you've got be swooning...

I am very much looking forward to returning!

Packed, band average. Couldn't get service after 30  minutes so went down the street.
One toilet for a whole bar full of people- just say no and head down to a smaller venue

I visited with my husband and my visiting from out of town friend on Saturday, 1.13.18; it was my first Whiskey Row experience. We got seats at the bar pretty quickly and stayed a few hours. I'd say we were there roughly from 2-6pm. 

I couldn't have been happier with the service we received for most of our stay. The team of three bartenders whose names I don't remember (pretty sure one was Maddie) worked seamlessly as a team, checked on everyone with great frequency and were incredibly friendly. We wouldn't have stayed nearly so long if it weren't for them. I personally am not drinking (the rest of my party was) at the moment and just had club soda and lime and they were happy to refill and even talked me into a few refills. 

At some point in our stay, we decided to get an appetizer. Our bartenders were happy to place the order. The food came out quickly and was delicious. Even as the place got more and more full, our team of bartenders never missed a beat and never sacrificed friendliness for efficiency. 

The band, Dozzi, came on, and we enjoyed them immensely. The bartenders told us they (band members) had all been sick and are usually even way better. I can't wait to see them again. 

Around 5pm, the night shift of bartenders began to arrive. The ladies we had been with all afternoon continued to provide amazing service as they got ready to cash out. It was more than 30 minutes before the new team even asked us if we were doing okay. The shift change was saddening. While the night team were efficient as far as serving people walking up to the bar, they were not so great at checking on those of us sitting at the bar. They also were not nearly as friendly. 

Had we arrived to this team of bartenders, we certainly wouldn't have enjoyed our time nearly as well or stayed as long as we did. 
We have certainly bragged about our day shift team to everyone in the following days. If ever I were to walk by and see those three again, I would definitely go in. 

There is only one bathroom stall (unisex) on the first floor, and the line gets long. There are multiple stall bathrooms on the second level, but a sign or something to indicate that might be beneficial for your establishment.

Seriously this place sucks, we waited an hour and a half for appetizers and it came out cold and burnt. We were one of two tables ? Server was awful, little blond with red lipstick on 5/1 / 18 2nd floor . Tacky live music band walking up to tables asking for tips... WTF??? So many other options, go somewhere else!!
Fun place. Stopped in for a drink and to listen to some music. Good location right on the broadway strip. I'm sure it's exponentially more fun at night. But a good time nonetheless

This was probably one the word nights of my life. The general jackson showboat was said to be an amazing venue for family's to come and see sights and go on a nice evening Christmas boat ride with a meal and show down the Nashville river. Me, my granddaughter, and my two sons, one of which are autistic had flown in from Florida that day, and we thought that this would be an amazing way to start our family trip. We booked the evening cruise so we thought that it the sun would be going down, but when we got there, it was pitch black. You couldn't see the sights all you could see down the river was some lights right above the port-a potty factory.  The cruise was 6-9 pm, and at 6:00 it was already pitch black. My granddaughter wanted to get the fried green tomatoes as an appetizer but when I asked if the were hand fried our waiter said that most of the food was shipped in and frozen, she was very disappointed and upset. Our main course was the "Sam's Club Special". It consisted of bacon stuffed chicken, broccolini, and cold potatoes, the chicken was like chewing rubber, and the whole course was very disappointing, and for our desert we had a peppermint cheesecake. It was the only decent thing on the menu, even though we knew it was shipped in from a food distributor. It was now 8:00 pm and the show hadn't started yet, for the past 2 hours we had nothing to do but stare at our plates and twiddle our thumbs. The show finally starts and I look back to see my 11 year old granddaughter asleep on the table. The only person in our group that liked the showboat was my autistic son, overall the show and performers were very well talented and deserved more than a debut at the general Jackson Showboat. Me and my family were so appalled by the lack of good service.

Stopped here with friends after eating at Ole Red.  Band was about to go on.  Friends ordered some of their specialty drinks, which they enjoyed. No draft beer, only bottles :(.  Band was ok, more honky tonk then I would have liked.

Worst service of my life! Visited with a large group of girls, the staff was less than accommodating from the very beginning and moody. Guaranteed, will not be back. Would not recommend anyone visit this establishment!

The Broadway bar scene is definitely not my thing on a Saturday night.  I don't know what I was thinking.  Perhaps if Broadway were shut down to vehicle traffic like Beale Street in Memphis or Bourbon Street in New Orleans, I'd have liked it a little better.  The problem is, I don't like overly crowded bars, cover charges, smoking, or music that is too loud to hear the person next to me.  Okay, now that I sound like an old lady...

Big Bang was a god send!

Even though it was very crowded, we managed to find 2 stools (and a table!) and we were served immediately.  We each had a beer and enjoyed the dueling pianos.  They did an awesome job from beginning to end and really put on a stellar performance.  They got the audience to interact.  Even the "security" guards got involved in little side shows of their own.  And of course, they recognized all of the birthdays and bachelorettes in the house.  They didn't give attitude when someone requested a song they didn't want to play, they were good sports and put on a fantastic show.

It was a great way for us to relax, have fun, and get away from the crowds outside.

We didn't pay a cover charge, but there was a bathroom attendant.  Sorry, but I refuse to tip someone who hands me a paper towel and squirts soap in my hand.  I am able to do those things myself, and I shouldn't have to pay for it just because you removed the paper towels and soap from the counter.  I know some bars and clubs have to do this to keep their bathroom from getting trashed, but Big Bang doesn't appear to attract a trashy club crowd.  Besides, I only went in the bathroom to blow my nose!

As much as I am a huge fan of Cash's music, this museum was a bit disappointing. It's small, doesn't have many items to show, it's expensive for the value you get ($17) and overall a bit of a tourist trap. 

And I feel that the real problem is that most people who come in, enjoy it not because of what it has to offer, but because they're fans of Johnny Cash to begin with. I think the museum gets away with it because of the volume of tourists who want to visit.Surprisingly, we waited for 30 minutes in line just to get tickets. But we were ultimately disappointed.

I didn't think that I would learn much more about Johnny Cash but after visiting the museum I'm a bigger fan.  It's a small museum full of plenty of information for fans.  Plenty of things too see and great for kids. There's a small gift shop and cafe attached.  Affordable fee and something everyone should see if visiting Nashville.

Absolutely worse service I've ever experienced in my life. When you leave your party of 12 reservation with a soaked outfit because one of the waitresses threw a drink on one of our faces...Enough said. I can guarantee I will never be back and I will make sure to spread the word to others...Bing bang/ dick's last resort treats their customers like absolute shit. Unacceptable! Food was ok, music was great. Staff...needs some serious work.
Too loud and no COUNTRY music!!! Chicken sandwich was burnt and service was hit or miss. We won't be going back.

' Because your mine, I walk the line.' I am not big on country music, however I enjoy a couple of Johnny Cash tunes. We purchased tickets on Groupon and we were really excited to check out this museum. I have to say it was a tight fit entering the museum it's just not that big and there are hoards of people. I'm not big on looking at other people's clothes and admiring stuff like that but they had more than that. They had a lot of Johnny Cash paraphernalia and tunes blaring. We got to see his record collection and awards and some more personal touches such as letter to his wife. We got some Folsom Blues coffee after and that we enjoyed. The Johnny Cash museum was self-guided and it was interesting to learn more about The Man in Black. Oh, and I started to tear up upon exiting when they had the video for 'Hurt' playing. Yea, that almost had me balling because that song is just so raw and emotional.

I am SO disappointed in this place. I will actually never come back. We went on Saturday around 2:00; Hollee was our server on the second floor. It wasn't crowded. We were in a party of 8 for my bachelorette party. 

We ordered a round of drinks and 3 appetizers at 1:00 PM. The drinks are expensive, which is totally fine, if the service matches. The service was horrible. We got our drinks after 15 minutes of waiting. No one brought water or came to check on us. 

We waited for an hour and a half for our appetizers. Every time we saw Hollee, we asked for an update and she said the food was COMING. Three times, we asked. Three times we were told the food was coming. Then, about almost 2 hours after ordering, she said the food would be on them and it was coming out now. Then, a manager came over and said that there was going to be no food and we were going to have it taken off the check. Well, obviously it will be taken off the check. It only makes sense - we didn't get any food. We even asked if they could still make it quickly and she said no ...

They discounted the drinks, but the entire bill should have been comped. This is the worst service I have ever had. There is NO EXCUSE to lie to customers about the status of their food, avoid them, or ignore them. We never were asked for a refill; someone from our party went to the empty bar 3 times for drinks because we weren't being asked for refills or new orders. Then, the management team had the nerve to say our food was comped. In order for something to be comped, it has to actually arrive. Food never arrived; there for it would have been illegal for us to be charged. 

The managers of this establishment never returned my phone call from Saturday afternoon. I am still waiting for them to contact me to further correct this experience. There are far too many other wonderful establishments with the exact same vibe and a far better experience. Try FGL House or Luke's instead of encountering such horrible service and a terrible experience.

The General Jackson Showboat, Nashville TN. What an experience! You know, I guess my expectations are very low. Some of the 1 Star reviews talk about the cheesy, unprofessional show. No Way-this was a professional, first rate entertainment experience!. I especially liked the rendition of the Devil Went Down To Georgia, Jerry Lee Lewis and the Elvis tribute. However, I can see a younger person may not appreciate the show.

I took the 12 noon lunch cruise & show. Everyone, including our server George, was very attentive, nice and polite. They had 4 buffet lines and everything was on a tight schedule, but I never felt rushed. The food was pretty good for a buffet but the apple crisp was delicious.

After the show, you can wander the boat on all 3 decks. On the hurricane (top) deck they had 2 entertainers that sounded pretty good. But the outside temperature was close to 100 degrees, so I stayed inside.

It is so great cruising down the Cumberland River on a faithful recreation of a steamboat (diesel electric powered) to relive a time gone by!

If they can get their act together, this could be a good place. At 1:30 pm on a weekday, after the lunch rush, the staff should be able to serve you quickly and efficiently. They weren't busy but I still waited for everything -- to order, to get my food, to pay the check. The burger could have been pretty great but they were out of mayo. And they didn't say, "Oh by the way, we're out of mayo." Just delivered the burger dry and didn't say anything. When I noticed, I thought they'd forgotten so I ask for a side of mayo. After several minutes, they finally came back and said, "Sorry, we don't have any." If the manager had stopped by to apologize or offer a coupon, that would have helped. But no such attention was paid.

I may try again in another month or so. You may want to give them a few weeks to get their deal figured out.

I loved it here! It's a really cool place with some really unique memorabilia from his life. It's not overly huge but well worth it. There's a decent sized shop in the establishment as well along with a small coffee shop. It's reasonably priced and I would definitely go back.

My friends and I visited here during their first week in business and we had the best time! So much fun! Great atmosphere! Staff is fun and the entertainment was great! The bartender Missy is great! I lost my phone and wallet and had to leave to catch a plane the next morning. She was kind enough to send them both back to me! Can't say enough good things about the people of Nashville!

Day drinking at its finest... walked in and it was already getting full... got a great seat in the back and people watched like a mug! The band is awesome and so is our server. I'm cooking my jets with some water right now but the fried pickles are yummy! 

I would sit here all day if I could... I wonder how long I can until they kick me out... LOL
Bottomless mimosa on Sunday! With one to go to boot!

When looking for things to do the showboat seemed like something fun to check out, they have different packages we had just general admission. 
Once on the boat we got some drinks, I kept simple with a beer & had a Stella, not bad my company had the Tennessee Tea, comes in a nice fancy souvenir cup very cool - looks like a pimp cup Lolll ...  the tea itself was not bad, strong alcohol taste a bit too sweet. 
Once show time is announce u make your way inside, if u have general admission u can sit by the chairs on the side which is not bad since we were on the second level, good view of the stage. The show itself was entertaining. 
As u move along the river u can walk around the boat & just hang out, drink,  pretty much not a lot to do other than enjoying the scenery. 
we did the lunch cruise with no lunch since the dinner one was sold out in the end overall it wasn't bad but a little boring for us since the crowd was mainly older senior, adults.  
It was a good way to kill a few hours during the day.

Well, my curiosity about this place is satisfied. This is NOT a place to eat. The food is worse than bad. Service was fine and on-stage talent upstairs and downstairs was excellent. I would not recommend eating here. My wife returned her food just by the look of it. The blue cheese dressing was too gross to describe. The chicken on my sandwich was seriously no thicker than 2 quarters, maybe 3 with the breading. The fries were not hot. I don't typically complain about restaurants. I just don't return. I won't return here. The only reason I give 2 stars is for the on-stage talent on both floors.

Multiple levels in which to quench your thirst.  It's a lively environment for sure, in the heart of the district.  Count on a ton of people being in here at all times; the space is so big however that you won't have to wait too long for a beverage to cool you down in the Nashville heat.  If you can, skip the longer lines downstairs and head up to the roof for a bird's eye view of the swarms of people in the streets and on neighboring rooftops.

We didn't eat there but walked around and had couple of beers. You can read all the other reviews and website for more details but pretty neat spot. 4 floors of live music. We had a good time!! I recommend!

Don't go to this bar unless you want your phone stolen. 3 out of 8 of us got our phones stolen in 15 minutes while at this bar. The workers did not care enough to help us either. Very sketchy. Again do not go to this bar.

I love you Kid, but not your bar. I never thought I would come to Nashville and have to hear Rick Springfield Jessie's Girl. That completely killed my buzz.

The bar was so wide that the bartender could not even get my drink to me with me reaching. I was with a friend and went to the bathroom and when I came back the bartender picked up my beer which was half full and tossed it.

 Double buzzkill.

Wow! I feel like I experienced magic being here! The music, the songwriters, the music round! Amazing! The atmosphere is so relaxing, really really great place to hear music and experience an amazing songwriters round! 

Just for you to note:
Get there early, at least 45-30 mins before the show to get a good seat, or at least to have your pick of the seating options available. It's a small space, so all seats have good views, some are just closer amd more centered to the stage than others. So, your choice.
There is complimentary valet parking for the shows! Just show your tickets and don't worry about parking strange places or paying for parking somewhere else.
Once inside for the show there is a minimum $15 per person to be spent in the restaurant for drinks or food. Drinks are good, food not impressive...but you have no choice

What can I say, it is just another Nashville country music star's restaurant and rooftop bar. We did not eat, but the people that were with us all really enjoyed their food. It looked good and the portions were large. The menu is very simple so don't expect a gourmet meal. It was kind of a chilly day and their outdoor heaters at the bar definitely kept you warm. As a matter of fact, I think I got a tan from them (not really, but they were as hot as a tanning bed). The service was a little slow and not very friendly despite the number of bartenders they had working. You pretty much had to flag someone down if you wanted anything. It was higher priced than other rooftop bars in the area, so keep that in mind. The music was mediocre, especially for Nashville talent. I prefer the less trendy places, but if you are looking for a trendy, rooftop bar, this may work for you.

I try to stay away from the touristy stuff. And yet, there I was booking  this cruise, how much more touristy can you get. I was wrong - a great time!! Crew, servers, officers - they all were terrific and very friendly. The food was very good - ok, I'll admit one of my 3 pieces of chicken(!) was pretty dry. And the show was as good as any I've seen anywhere.
Be sure to book the Captain's Table and get that included drink and  trip to the pilot house - very interesting. Would be 4 1/2 if i could.
Elevator for friends of bouncers only to get to rooftop.  Can be great bands but bouncers are immediately rude with folks even if you haven't had a drink

We were a party of 12 and one of our party was asked to leave.  We are still wondering why that was as they gave us no explanation as to why.  We were not highly eniberated nor rowdy.  We took our business to Luke Bryans and we finished up the night just fine with no issues.

All I can say is WOW!! The bartender was so sweet and helpful with finding food and drinks. The food was amazing, which surprised me a little because it was busy and it was a bar, but it was such an amazing breakfast! I would go there if you can for brunch, we stood for awhile and waited, but it was worth it!

Five stars for the music but one star for the food and service, so it averages out at 3 (rounding up). If you're coming here looking for good music, they definitely deliver, but do not count on a good meal.

We came on a Saturday morning for their Picks & Pints brunch from 11:00-12:30. They had four singer-songwriters who were amazing and played a great set onstage. They had great energy with one another and their acoustic sounds where perfect for a mellow Saturday morning brunch.

The food however is a totally different story. I was pretty excited that they had a brunch menu because after all, brunch is the most important meal of the day. We each ordered one of the biscuit sandwiches, both of which came out completely cold. The biscuits were doughy and dense, which is really sad is you're in the South and you screw up a basic biscuit. My brisket biscuit had cold cheese and dried over-cooked brisket on top. I couldn't even chew the brisket cause it was so tough. We also realized a few bites in that the server was supposed to let us pick a side, but she never asked us about it and ended up giving us whatever random sides she decided. We also asked for some ketchup and Tabasco to help make the meal more bearable, which didn't come out to the table until we were almost done with the meal.

If you're on Yelp, I'm guessing that like me you plan out your vacation meals and prioritize food over everything. It would have been amazing to pair a delicious brunch with a great Nashville performance, but sadly that did not happen today. I hope that the management of this establishment takes note and at the very least, make adjustments to serve warm, edible food to their guests.

Even though Dierks Bentley is a terrible musician I sure love the drinks at this bar. Now at the same time you still have the stigma of Dierks Bentley and his really mediocre voice. But at the same time you have drinks and dancing so there's that. Best part about this bar is that it isn't Luke Bryan's bar because Luke Bryan is even worse than Dierks Bentley. Great happy hour though

Poor entertainment. Performers came out right when we were seated for a short intro song, then nothing for over an hour during dinner and dessert. Pathetic!  Dinner theater means watching a production during dinner. Steak was tough to cut and and chew. Unfortunate!!!

Great place to hang out, good location on Broadway and the open windows to the street make it a great party place. The live music was good and bar tenders were also good. There was long lines for the bathroom as there is only one downstairs, or you can wait in line to get upstairs where there are more. We never went upstairs.
I was pleasantly surprised by the amount of childhood memorabilia they had about Johnny Cash

So disappointed....  I had such a wonderful experience...  The bands were great. The service has been great. Wrapped up a 4 day trip and decided I wanted a T-shirt from the place I had had the best experience and the bartenders were atrocious!!!  I realize it was late and they wanted to assume I was drunk. Even one of the bouncers decided to lie and say he had to deal with me when I entered the bar just to have her back. Not indicative to a 'Kidd Rock' reputation. The little blonde behind the bar was shook up because a patron had been over served and got behind the bar, but no excuse to be rude to others. I asked for a Mgr and they kicked me out without explication. Had I not stood outside the door waiting on a Mgr which I had requested right away, I would have never spoken to anyone. I just wanted to buy a T-shirt. Who does that???  Little blonde should be looking for a new job. Worst taste in my mouth after such a hanious
I wasn't very impressed with the museum, but that might be because I'm not a huge Johnny Cash fan. I'm sure big fans will love it.
Bouncer put hands on me at 2:52am! State law dictates all alcohol off the floor at 3am. I was finishing my beer when I was assaulted by staff!!! Great music and good time here overall.
Came for dinner and drinks at a steakhouse and they were out of steak. Service is poor and they seem to be in way over their heads. A lot of better options in Nashville

If I had known this was Kid Rock's bar I probably would have went in with a lower expectation. I've been to the honky tonks years ago and in coming back I've since been told to stay away from the newer celebrity bars that have popped up all over broadway. We had just got out of the Predators game and the bars were packed so we walked a bit to get away from the ones closest to the stadium when we found a bar that looked reasonably accessible. A couple of us quickly snagged a table while a couple others ordered drinks for the group. The raised stage really put the band on display and made it more of a show for everyone in the place... even us in the way back. Out of all the bars we went to that night we had a really great time at this one so it gets a thumbs up from me.

Live Music AND recorded music at the same time. What dubious entertainment!  But seriously, they did finally turn the recorded music off.

First, and most importantly, I'd like to say that the Burgers were really good. I would return for the Burger without question. However, and this is admittedly my taste, the music was TOO LOUD. The musician was quite good, but my poor eardrums had difficulty with HOW MUCH MUSIC THERE WAS.

Great parking, as it is in a shopping center that isn't really packed with other places to go. I'd be surprised if you didn't find a place to park.

Our waiter was a bit aloof, but this might just be the way he dealt with being busy, and it was busy for sure.  We still found a table though. I'm still not sure if you seat yourself or if they seat you.  Hopefully your experience won't be as mysterious.

Don't  go there. I could  not get my license  out of my wallet.  Would  not let me in because  he could not see expectation  date. Oh did I mention  I am old enough to be his mother  or more. Been going to Nashville  for the last 5 years
 They lost our business. Should  have stayed swingn door. Wish I could give it less than  1 star

So with an hr to kill in downtown Nashville, I first went to the obvious choice... The Country Music Hall Of Fame.  After gagging in disbelief at the $25 admission fee (I'll admit that corporate perks have largely shielded me from knowing what admission costs in any of NYC's museums), and quickly consulting Yelp, I was led to the Johnny Cash museum.

You don't have too be country to get Cash.  You don't have to be religious to get Cash.  Cash is eternal.  Cash transcends. Cash rules everything around me... dolla dolla bills y'all (I'm convinced that Wu Tang worked with Johnny Cash in 36 Chambers).

Johnny Cash made music across multiple eras and this place showcased it all.  This is a great little museum... definitely worth a look if you're in Nashville.  The items in the store seemed pretty pricey so I took a pass on that.

By far the worst service I've ever had at a restaurant or bar. The server Kaci did not come to take our order, we had to go to the bar and ask her, then she took our food to the wrong table and we had to switch deals with the people next to us. She never came back to ask us if we were happy and never asked us if we needed to refill our drinks. We then had to go back to the bar to ask her for the bill. The restaurant was not busy at all. Won't be going back.

Great burger! Big and thick... They don't skimp on the meat, great pretzel bun, very affordable. The aoli is great!!
My only complaint is... The fries are soft and limp.

Stopped for a bite to eat and whiskey, ordered some quality whiskey and it comes to the table in a plastic cup .... are we in some sort of college dorm party? I'm insulted for the price of whiskey these days to come in a plastic disposable cup, obviously it's just a name and they don't take whiskey seriously at all.

We live here in the Nashville area and are on broadways every few weeks, don't stop here! It may sound petty but when you're paying retail prices for whiskey to sip this is seriously not cool.

Wax museum tour. Very nicely put together, clean and very decorative. See stars like Carrie Underwood, Blake Shelton, Jason Aldean, Johnny Cash, Elvis, Beyoncé and more. I gave it three stars because of the price.. $24 per ticket and the tour is about 20-30 min long. If you buy online in advance it is $19 per ticket. Also heads up for Nashville Tour books and maps for coupons.

This place is so loud. I wouldn't suggest going there after a flight. You literally have to get in the server's face to hear what she's saying. My poor ears!

The band was excellent though but I never heard of a band going around collecting money for themselves. Maybe that's a Nashville thing but I assume they're getting paid to play. They made a crap ton of money that night!

The menu has a steak and chicken section. It literally has one chicken dish. I ordered that. It's a half chicken that comes atop mashed potatoes. It doesn't come with a salad or any vegetable or even any garnish. A couple of asparagus spears or something would've been appreciated. Or just throw some parsley on there to pretty it up. Presentation was bland but the chicken and potatoes was actually very good. I really wanted a salad so I ordered a $9 Ceaser salad. No plain Ceaser salad is ever worth $9 but I really wanted a vegetable! It was basically a huge bowl of lettuce with a few croutons and some shredded Parmesan. 

The service was very good. I did end up buying a t-shirt!

Came in out of the rain for brunch. The service, music and food was great! 
Had a frozé and split the chicken and waffles. Their spicy savory take on this classic was amazing and easy to split/eat. Glad we tried it!

My husband and Istumbled  across this bar while walking around on broadway. I have to say, we had a great time! I'm not the Biggest country fan, but I enjoyed that there was music for all different styles! The first two levels for live bands (both were great) and then the rooftop area was a hip hop/top 40 area with a dj! I truly had a great time! I ordered some Truly's which were over priced, but I wasn't surprised-ordering them at a bar probably wasn't the smartest thing to do anyways but #basic so it is what it is! Overall, I had a great time. Service and staff were decent and the bathrooms and floors were pretty clean for the amount of traffic coming and going. I would recommend to anyone wanting to have a good time.

This place was really yummy! My friend and I went at 5:30 on a Friday and it was empty but we didn't watch the show. We just stayed in the main part of the restaurant so maybe everyone was hiding in the show part. The food was good and I was a little sad when my waitress took my food back before I was done with my fries, but I'd go back!
