I read some not so great reviews which almost stopped me from going into this bar. Walking by we heard a woman singing and she was so good we had to go in and glad we did!! Just visited on a Tuesday afternoon so not super crowded, the place is several floors so lots of places to sit. The stage is big and elevated and we found out while there the girl singing had been on the Voice. She was excellent!! Also didn't plan on eating there but then decided to. The only reason I am giving 4 stars is I feel like the menu options were a bit limited. We decided on The Big Ass Hotdog which is HUGE (you have been warned - lol). I always liked Kid Rock so this was a good stop along the way.

Giving them two stars because they have music. Rude staff ... served us on a Monday night 6/17/2019. We had just bought a round of drinks (4) a good song came on and got up to dance one song. When we came back they had cleared our table. There was plenty of seating so that was not an issue. Bartender was rude and did not handle the situation correctly. When we complains to the bartender about the loss of drinks we were kicked out reluctantly by security who apologized to us .Normally you would have a coaster or a napkin served with your drink so we could of put a clear sign. We did not think it would be a problem because they were fresh drinks $60 down the drain . I recommend going to Ole Red where the staff are trained and friendly . Btw we have owned two bars . You don't treat customers like they treated us. Never going there when there are plenty of nice bars to go to.

The atmosphere is great and today's band was fun! Tigirlily is a fun, sweet group. Love that they are sisters and love the upbeat, fun song choices. The bartenders were great, super attentive. The food was ok. 
The best thing we ordered was a hot chick slider. I was disappointed with the buttermilk chicken fingers. I was craving some good chicken fingers and these were a bust. They were dry and the ranch dressing was runny and flavorless. The fries and onion rings were good, nothing that makes them stand out from any others. Love you Dierk, but there can be some improvements made in the kitchen.

Well........we went on april 18, 2014 @ 830

The venue is great. The foo was fine. However the patrons and tourists that happen o stop in don't seem to understand that this is a music venue with food, bot a restaurant with a band.  

The sound from the bachelorette parties that aren't listening to the musics and are more interested in "woohoo" were jot only rude to the performers, but ALL of the other patrons.  I tried ti talk with the staff and they said they would try to address it with the  servers. 

One of the singers tried to calm them down as well but it worked for probably 3 min tops. 

What i would recommend?   Someone with a LRC cafe introduce the artists each night.  As part o that introduction explain that these are songwriters and the venue is about them and celebrating them. In order to so , we ask you keep conversations to a minimum and we may warn you a few times, but if you persist, we may ask you to enjoy the patio outside. 

Please do this. We will be back. We will bring others. We will try you again, but i it isn't addressed when we return, we simply wont come back.  

Update:  (as um un the review when im writing this)

They put a powerpoint slide up asking you to min tour conversation. The result:  no change. 

I truly felt sorry for the performers.

This is a terrible establishment. I would suggest avoiding it at all costs if you're a POC. They look at you crazy when you walk in, service horrible, and they will attempt to find any reason to make your experience the utmost uncomfortable. I visited back in February. Gave it one more time this July. It's clear now that this place isn't it!

Nice cruise up the river on a BIG boat. Didn't do the diner, didn't look like a missed anything. Ordered a beer for the show $14!!! Gee I got to keep the glass.
Update
Wife complained to the Stewart that we should have been told the cost or given a choice. He refunded to a standard beer. Good service from management.

Nice memorabilia but tight quarters in many respects. The "have your picture taken with Johnny" is the most disorganized mess I have ever seen. Don't waste your money or time doing this, we tried and waited 30 min+ for results with no results. Other sales and retakes to larger groups were much more important than the two of us! Convenient excuses and lies by the two picture takers of the picture souvenir $$$ made me very disappointed.
I walked in & an employee asked for tip money right away. I was there 2 seconds & told me we work for tips bitches! We walked out! She was so rude!

Stopped in after going to other bars on broadway. I've been to Nashville several times, but this bar was newer to me. It was crowded, but not any more so than the other bars. The band that was playing was really great! Which definitely helps the experience. My fiancé isn't a big country music fan, so he enjoys the bands that play alternative music. I ordered a frosé and Jeff ordered a whiskey and coke. I thought for the price, $21 is a lot. I can order essentially the same thing at another bar for $15. It was fun atmosphere and our bartender was friendly. I'd go back!!

Stopped in randomly. Great music (a little loud, but fun) where we sat on the 2nd floor. Food was good, but the service was great! Sarah didn't steer us wrong and made sure we had a great time. Will definitely go back the next time we're in town.

Well.  This was interesting. I used Groupon for the tickets. Otherwise it would've been $25 per person(x3..sheesh). Anyway.  I wasn't really thrilled with most of the figures. At the beginning  there is a small musical treat but I warn you it has a 3D affect. They had a Rhianna and Taylor Swift at the front entryway which wasn't a very good replica to me. Anyway I went through and was pleased with some of the others such as Wayland Jennings,  Bruce Springsteen (who had an interactive game.. Pretty cool) Stevie Wonder, (so life like). As you browse through you are met with various artist some you know some you may not.  Picture taking is encouraged. The last room is a giant stage settings with some of the most prolific  country stars such as Reba McIntosh (not very life like) but the Carrie Underwood (my favorite) was sooooo  life like! I mean it was spot on! So all in all it was a good time,  because some of the figures were half believable  I gave it a 3.I got some keepsakes(which I normally  DO NOT DO) at the gift shop,  which has some really cool things.

The staff was wonderful the waiter was very attentive and the food was great!!!  I've never had a better Porkchop in my life.  

I was a little disappointed that only the main level was open gift shop was not open no other floors were available and I was just music playing on the radio with some videos that show and then the screen.  We were there at about 8 o'clock on a Tuesday night.   The place was not packed but busy enough where we hand a 30-45 min wait.   Tuesday might not be their busiest night but it would've been great to see a local artist playing their own music up on the stage.

Just to be clear, this 5 star rating is not for the food. Or the drinks. Or the service. However, the music we heard here was nothing short of amazing and I think everyone should come, so I gave it 5 stars. It was our favorite part of our Nashville trip and is an experience we will not soon forget.

First, I will say that $5 to watch these musicians is a STEAL. Now, I'm not from Music City, but I've seen a fair amount of live music in my life, but this experience blew all of that out of the water. They had us laughing, crying (more than once), and just plain awestruck. 

If you arrive early, which we did not, you can order drinks and lounge around for a bit. At show time you are escorted back to the listening room where you can order dinner and more drinks. Because they seat everyone at once, the waiters are understandably very rushed. In a effort to be prepared for everyone coming in at once, most of the tables had water and cups on them already. Ours did not, and it took about 20 minutes for us to get some. I noticed that the table next to us had cups, but their water "pitcher" (Jack Daniels bottle) was empty when they sat down. Our food came out super fast (read: it was prepared ahead of time and not very fresh). It was good but not great. We ordered three Old Fashioneds from the bar and each one came out different from the next. I'm pretty sure the first one was just a bourbon on the rocks. Oh well. 

All in all, an amazing music experience. Just don't have high expectations on the restaurant side of things.

So much fun! This place was awesome!
I really enjoyed the music playing and clips of Johnny throughout. 
The place was staffed with friendly people who seemed genuinely happy to be there. There is a cafe that had coffee, water, and snacks. 
The gift shop is a bit pricey but priced as expected. The merchandise was fun and definitely sure to make any Johnny cash fan happy. 
The displays were well thought out with lots of handwritten notes and articles from Johnny Cash. 
My favorite item was a velvet heart he wrote on for June Carter. I am a sucker for reading about love stories - this display will not disappoint you if that appeals to you. 
His Military gear is also displayed- there are a lot of crazy facts about Johnny Cash I never knew and you don't get from the movie. If In Nashville - go

We had fun here - but it was quick. Super quick.

But this was our first visit to a wax museum - and I have to say, it was pretty neat. We had some great photo ops and overall, it was enjoyable. Just wish there had been a little more to it for the $19 a person.

We stopped in on a Sunday morning for a Bloody Mary and music. We choose the spicy version that was supposed to come with special spices and their very own pickled vegetables. What we got was a runny bland red colored drink garnished with a lime wedge. Not at all as described in the menu. WORST Bloody Mary ever!! Service was poor. Music was good and we did enjoy that.

It's Bluebird Room without all the stress of reserving tickets but with all the same talent performing.

I had such an amazing time at the Listening Room - why are there not things like this in Chicago!? Seriously one of the best things I did on my last trip to Nashville. 

All of the singer songwriters on the night we went were incredibly talented. Some better than others and some just mind-blowing. My favorite of the night was Kyle Reynolds! Loved his acoustic boy band but way more talented vibe. 

Beer selection wasn't great but I found one that I stuck with for the night. And prices weren't bad. Also our server was super friendly and attentive which was nice.

Tonight was my very first time going to see music at The Basement East!!! I don't know why it has taken me so long to check out a band here...I was the lucky winner of 2 free tickets to see Austin Meade (opening act) & the Read Southall Band - THANK YOU @NowPlayingNashville

The music was great and the venue is simple and easy to navigate.  I highly recommended coming early to grab a seat at the high bar tables... (most of the venue is standing room only). There is a free parking lot and nearby street parking.  I'm not sure If everyone was at LOTG but it wasn't that busy tonight.  I'm not sure how the venue picks the lineup but I thought both bands were really good! Austin is from Texas - favorite song was Savannah! Read Southall is from Oklahoma and describes themselves as Southern Rock & Crunchy Country . My favorite song was "Why?" - Loved belting out the lyrics!  The drinks were great and the bartender was really nice.

I'd stay away. 

The only place in Nashville charging a cover ($6/head) and they had the worst talent. We hated it and left pretty quick. This place is attached to Dick's Last Resort - which also seemed weird. Everyone in there is wearing a hat that makes them look like klan members.  Hit the other bars and venues instead.

There were so many people there you literally couldn't move. People were always bumping into one another, and you were pushed out of the way if you tried to stop and read anything, especially at the beginning of the exhibit. 

I guess there is no alternative since this is a tourist town and nobody wants to miss out on this attraction, but I've never seen so many people crammed into such a small space. Because of this. I couldn't enjoy the museum and experience. Additionally, I didn't find the exhibits to be interactive enough to keep my attention. I felt as if everything I saw, I could have seen on the internet. 

What's worse is the gift shop, which was still crammed with people and offered seriously over-priced memorabilia and tank tops for like $40.00. No thank you. 

Despite everything, this still checked off an item on my bucket list, so I'm glad I came.

Love this place! I would go all the time if I lived in Nashville. We actually went twice, since we liked it so much.

It's a great place to view up and coming singer songwriters perform. One night we went, there were 8 performers who sang 3 songs each in round robin. The second night, there were 4 performers who sang 6 songs each. I really liked all the performers and appreciate the variety. 

The beer selection is good and prices are great. We got a Bearded Iris IPA draft for $5. There is a $15 dollar food and bev minimum, but for like $20 +tip including the ticket, you can eat and drink and listen to great music. 

I actually really liked the smoked wings, great flavor. My expectations for food were low and this place far exceeded them. Service was good too.

I wanted this place to be amazing..... 

Lets start with decor and location! The location in downtown is awesome and very easy to find. Once you go in there are 3 floors, the first is a bar the second is a chill vibe where you can eat and listen to music (we were there for brunch) the third (7th flight of stairs) was the roof which was TINY!! 

Everything looked great, LOVED the decor and the music was exceptional, the man and woman who sang were amazing vocalists. Unfortunately we really wanted to have brunch on the roof but with only 3 shaded spots and two out in the sun we couldn't find a spot. We got a booth on the second level and took a seat. 

To make a long story short I will bullet point the positives: 
- The southern fries were delicious 
- the decor and ambiance was nice 
-moderatly priced mimosa's and bellinis

the negatives: 
- other than the southern fries our food was below average 
- two of our orders were wrong, and when asked to bring the rest of my food they brought out my side of bacon, after we were all done eating. 
-The waitress we had never refilled our drinks or asked if we wanted more

I may go back to check out the bar but I've honestly been telling people how bad our food and service was because of the name so many people will want to check it out and I don't want them to waste their time.

We came after brunch on Sunday.  There was a great band and it was not too crowded.  We sat inside (it was scorching hot outside) on the first floor at the bar with a great view of the stage.  Loved the atmosphere with the windows open and the AC blasting.  Beer selection is pretty typical of the bars on Broadway.  We didn't have food.

I expected it to be a little bigger museum, but I guess it was still pretty cute setup. Honestly, Johnny Cash fans would appreciate it more than me. They have few stuff, like his concert and performance related outfits, guitars, his personal letters, and photographs, etc. on the display.  There are many audio stations to listen to his music and couple of videos are shown to tell the story of his life. I saw some old couple listening to his famous song "Hurt" and they were in tears. I didn't understand why they were crying, but then my boyfriend explained me the importance of that song. Long story short, go to this place only if you're a die hard fan of Johnny Cash. Like any other touristy place, there is a souvenir shop inside the museum that sells Johnny Cash t- shirts, mugs, magnets, posters, baby onesies, and what not. You can also grab a bite or drink some beer in the small cafe next to the ticket counter.

Been spending time at whiskey row several times a week since it opened. Im usually not crazy about the broadway bars, but I do play music in some of them(whiskey row included). This place has the best atmosphere of any bar on broadway in my opinion. The food (e.i. whiskey burger) is so good. The drinks are great and the staff I have met all seem personable and professional.

What a waste of $20. The second I stepped foot into the 'museum' I regretted the decision. Lots of videos to watch, small museum and it's confusing to find the exit back into the gift shop. Also don't buy the Chapstick. No good.

Last weekend the wife decided to escape to Key West with her gal friends for some wine coolers. With the old ball and chain gone (just kiddin guys) yours truly had nothing to do but crush Bud Lights and watch the Lions destroy the Chargers. Bored, I decided to call my high school buddy Rich who recently went through a pretty bumpy divorce fueled by one bad trip to Ruby Tuesday's. To make a short story shorter, we decided that us guys should take advantage of our independence and blow off some steam in the music city. 

Flew southwest into Nashville the next morning. The plane waitress handed out ritz bits so I'm not complaining. Rich lives in Georgia so he met me at the airport. After hitting Midtown for some brews and barbecue I turned the volume up on our weekend plans and threw on my tuxedo T-shirt. Took an Uber downtown, those things freak me out, one minute you're touchin things on your Samsung galaxy and the next your in some stranger named Alberto's 2007 Camry. 

Anyway, anyone who has ever spent time with Rich could tell you that he is basically the Calvin Johnson of letting the good times roll. Throw me into the equation with a Saturday afternoon buzz chaos will follow. After 'Berto dropped us off on Broadway(cool guy actually, big Styx fan) our first stop was Dierks Bentley's honky tonk. Dierks Bentley's music is fine but the fact that he dresses like someone named Scott who does interior design on HGTV just doesn't do it for me, you guys. In addition his venue was about as impressive as my 12-year-old son Steve Junior's latest phase, which involves him wearing a top hat and botching entry level magic tricks. 

Fortunately just down the street an outlaw Paradise awaited. As soon as I saw the neon lights spelling out "Kid Rock," Romeo Michigan's pride and joy, I knew we were in for an unforgettable night we wouldn't remember. We scrambled past seven bachelorette parties in the line outside, but the bouncer was cool with it and even offered me some Skoal wintergreen. A-plus staff at this place. 

have always idolized Kid Rock and I have nothing but the utmost respect for his renegade mentality. He's family friendly but also hardcore. In fact my youngest son's only redeeming quality is that he has dressed up as Kid Rock for three consecutive Halloweens. Back to the task at hand, this place was better than I would have ever imagined. It was somewhere between a bikers dream and your sweet grandmothers worst nightmare. That being said, we were still initially disappointed to see an empty stage but 12 minutes and about 7 pitchers of Budweiser later the band started back up again. 

The stage itself was straight up gangster it had a giant lit-up-red-eyed longhorn skull hanging above three levels of stage and was about the coolest piece of technology I've seen since the release of the Pontiac trans am. By the time the band fired back up I was on cloud nine. My only complaint was they had not played a single kid rock song in the 15 minutes we had been there. I took down a couple more ice cold buds. That mixed with the horseshoe of Skoal courtesy of a certain 6'8" bouncer game me a pretty harsh buzz.  Things got blurry from there, next thing I remember Rich was dancing on a table and I was doing a dirty variation of the doe-si-doe with a woman I had never met before. When I finally got my bearings straight I realized that I was completely surrounded by some of the best looking rock n roll goddesses to ever grace god's green earth. Not only that but the sleeves to my tuxedo t-shirt were missing in action and I was wearing a pretty baller fedora. I have been happily married for 17 years but this was about to be the death of me. Before I could swim through the sea of barrel chested divas and escape infidelity, Rich brought me a double shot of Jim Beam. Game over. The last thing I remember Rich and I were absolutely hammered in front of the stage while the band was playing a pretty convincing cover of "Pour Some Sugar on Me". 

The next morning I woke up in the hotel bath tub with a spot on my neck that was either a hickey or a bruise caused by a blunt household object. Whole lot of questions and not many answers. 

Here are a few: Was Kid Rock's Honky Tonk and Rock N Roll Steakhouse the finest establishment I have ever blacked out in? Absolutely. Will the wife let me hang out with Rich again? Probably not. Should I be concerned about both of my sons being interested in playing soccer? Sure seems like it. 

At the end of the day Kid Rocks Honky Tonk and Rock and Roll Steakhouse is a 5 star establishment. Subtract my two star blackout decision making and multiply that by the 8 days I have spent in the doghouse, carry the 1 and you get a four star review. 

Anyway, it's Sunday and the Lions just took it to the Eagles, there's another full twelver in the fridge, and I'm not complaining.

Yours truly,

Steve C.

I agree with the criticism that it is a confusing layout.  Also, clearly there is a blue shirt on display that is supposedly one JC wore in a performance with the picture right by it...and it's not.  It's pretty clear the embroidered design doesn't match.  Makes one wonder what else might be fudged.  However, assuming the rest (or most) is authentic, there is some really good stuff there and worth the visit.
A bit of a walk from the main drag, but worth every step. We listened to 5 amazing song-writers in an intimate atmosphere without all the craziness.

One Bathroom for approximately 100 people. The music was great, The two bands we saw yesterday were so nice and really good with the crowd.  
The biggest downfall is that there was only one bathroom open, I had to wait about 40 minutes at one stage to use the bathroom which was not well kept. The staff would then tell us we could use the bathroom on the 4th floor and when we left the line were told by security that the 4th floor bathrooms were not open (which meant we lost our place in line)
My friends and I understand that there was a private event on upstairs but it is unfair to treat your customers differently than famous, the customers are the people you want to keep happy as will keep your business going. If your event was that important you should have closed the whole bar for the

We had one goal our first night out in Nashville-find the Dueling Piano Bar. Find it we did, and boy we were not disappointed! We got there pretty early so we had our pick of seats. It started with just two players/ singers, but by the time we left (3-4 hours later) they had four-five of them on the stage at one time. They could play almost anything you requested and if they didn't know it, one of them would go learn it quick while the others continued with other requests. I requested Metallica and they delivered! My family and I had so much fun and while the drinks were a bit pricey, it was to be expected since we were on the main drag of downtown Nashville. I can't wait to go back and bring everyone I know!

Glad I went.  Like everywhere else in Nashville it was way too crowded when I went.  I love a few Johnny Cash songs and albums but you have to be a Johnny Cash super fan to really enjoy this museum.  Expensive for what it is.  Real estate can't be cheap in this area but I'm sure Cash's relatives aren't hurting for money.

Hello! I'm Johnny Cash.

I was quite impressed with this museum. It's not a huge museum and can be done in 1-2 hours but it houses a ton of interesting information and memorabilia. I was also surprised with how high tech it was compared to other museums I have been to - music videos on iPads! How cool. While we were there, an employee was walking around helping people who needed it and answering questions. He's got to be the Johnny Cash trivial pursuit champ - he knew everything! Apparently they have Johnny Cash friends & family that will work at the museum occasionally. 

You can take pictures anywhere within the museum and there are some great photo ops! Like posing in front of the wall of records.

Tickets are normally $15 but I was able to snag a Groupon for half the price or you can use the Total Access Pass for admission. Keep your eyes open to score a deal on entry!

I like Johnny Cash's music but aside from the movie with Reese Witherspoon, I don't know much about him. I learned quite a bit at the museum and enjoyed watching his performances. I was in the theater room alone watching various bits from him on TV shows and such for quite some time. One of the big highlights is the handwritten lyrics to Walk The Line and Folsom Prison Blues. My personal favorite thing in the museum was the Valentine's gift from Johnny to June.

You can't miss the museum - it's a huge red brick building with Johnny Cash written all over it. There isn't a private parking lot but there is a paid parking lot adjacent to the building. 

In my opinion, it's a must do while in Nashville.

My review is for this bar during the afternoon. 

Whiskey Row is a three story bar that has the tallest rooftop on lower Broadway. When you're walking up the stairs to the top, you'll truly feel it. There are a lot of stairs. The top floor has a great view of all of the Honky Tonks. There's an outdoor area as well as a DJ set up. 

The bottom two floors are where the live music happens. The first floor was loud and lively. There is a lot of bar space and tables to sit at. It feels very spacious and is one of the few square shaped bars as opposed to the very narrow rectangular shaped bars. 

We wandered our way to the second floor and had such a great time. The vibe was really chill. They have drinks and food and lots of large booths and high tops. The band playing was incredible. They were really friendly and talked a lot to the audience asking for requests. Their music was awesome. 

I really liked this bar. There was something for everyone. From the rooftop area to the cozy second floor listening lounge to the rowdier first floor, it's a great spot to spend an afternoon. I bet it's a ton of fun at night also.

We came to Nashville with a 60 plus group.  Stopped at Losers at noon  because we loved the name.  Bouncer asked for our I D's.  The only person in our group that didn't have one was 68.  I jokingly passed my 61 year old ID to her after I passed" and the bouncer was such a jerk he threatened to keep my license.  

Plenty of great places in Nashville to go that do not harass senior citizens.

Drinks are good, but the band we're currently listening to is insulting patrons for not wanting to request songs and give them tils to "live off of". They are relentlessly insulting people who make requests as well.  I wish I knew the band so I could be more specific - no class.

This place has great music and food bar staff is also awesome at getting you quick drinks but the security at door are racist Asshole's. I'll never waste any of my money at this place again. If you look anything besides caucasian make sure your not wearing a white shirt, apparently only caucasians are allowed to wear white shirts at Dierks Bentley whiskey Row. 

FYI don't be so quick to judge a person, you're action ruined my day and experience in Nashville.

Went to Nashville for a girls trip in lieu of me graduating from college. It was a 5 day trip and after going to Whiskey Row the first night I wanted to go there every night. It was so much fun! First floor was live country music and second floor was a dj mixing all the 2000's and current hits. I paid for my first two drinks and my friend paid for our first two shots and with tip it combined to $40. The age group was mid twenties to early thirties. I'm gonna miss Nashville but I'm really gonna miss Whiskey Row

Crappy waitress, crappy band don't waste your time or money.  Spent hour there to only get one drink and never came back to get food order.  We had to get up and find the waitress to even get our bill and to get my credit card back.

Nashville never ceases to amaze and entertain!  With this being my second trip to the city within a matter of 2 months for educator conference shenanigans, it was such a breath of fresh air to come upon the Big Bang Dueling Piano Bar.  I walked past a similar type of venue in Vegas and was curious, but never stopped to indulge.  This time, we went as a group and it was THE best time and money spent on Broadway.  

The talent was nothing less than stellar: watching four different pianists take to the stage, pull a patron's song request and bang away at the keys AND sing...man! Who does that?  Such a smart concept that is similar to karaoke:  we--patrons--we allowed to write down our song choice, submit your song with a monetary tip--not mandatory, and sit back and listen to the crowd's choices unfold as the musicians weave this magical mash up as the night carries on.  My favorite was when one of them would take to the bass guitar and percussion; such a full, live-band experience.  Impromptu entertainment at its best!

I would highly recommend this bar when traveling with a large group.  We were grateful for no cover charge--probably because we attended on a Wednesday night.  Thank you, Nasvhille, for living up to your name!

I'm sure we were one of the many who couldn't get tickets to Bluebird Cafe so we ended up here. This is absolutely nothing against the performers, who were all awesome, but everything to do with the venue.

Given that the main attraction is music, the acoustics were terrible at this venue. The wait staff clears plates outside in the main area. Even though they were about 10 feet away, when you bang forks, knives, and plates together, the noise carries. It doesn't help that the flooring is a hard surface so it also echoes. It made it really difficult to hear the actual performance.

On top of the entrance fee, there's also a $15 minimum per person for food and drinks. Now, if you have to enforce a $15 minimum, that makes me think that you DGAF about your food because people will have to order it anyway. The fried green tomatoes were the worst I've ever had, and don't get me started on the batter. The chips on our cheese plate were stale. If you absolutely had to come, just stick with drinks.

I wouldn't return, and wouldn't recommend. Too bad because the music was great!

PS The parking was free valet, which was convenient.

This massive 3/4 story establishment is fairly new to Broadway in Nashville - There are "Now Open" billboards all over the place. 

We went straight up to the top and found a seat on the patio pretty easily and a waitress made her way over in less than 5 minutes. There is live music on every floor and while you would think they would collide with one another, you really can only hear the band on your floor. 

They have a pretty good selection of beers on tap and bottled, but were out of two that we requested. 

We noshed on some buffalo chicken wings...no mix and match on the flavors - an order of 12 is whatever ONE flavor you decide. It would be nice to get 6/6, but not a deal breaker and the wings were good. 

We climbed the stairs to the top, drank beer, ate wings and danced on the dance floor....Good times!

I haven't been in the 360 Burger for a couple of years, so it was about time to try it out again. I get their burger- beef, brioche bun,  lettuce, tomato and sharp cheddar cheese plus the waffle fries. their were lots of them on my place and they were really good.

Mow the rest of the story. First, all burgers are cooked medium well. That makes specifying how I want it cooked not an option.The medium well burger could have been due to the cooking or to the % fat...I don't know. It was just an OK burger. Now the waffle fries were really good, but they couldn't get 360 Burger a 4 star rating.

I am a huge fan of The Listening Room. The concept is simple: arrive before showtime, pay the cover, get a table, order food and drink and listen to great tunes! But to break it down for you, here are the basics for a fun night at TLR:

1. Valet! It's so easy to park there, beause valet is close and super fast. Whee!!
2. Get there early. When you check in at the ticket counter, you'll get a table number. The earlier you arrive, the better your seat at the show!
3. Grab a drink at the lobby bar and wait to be seated. Once the doors open,take a look at that beverage - is it low? Grab another...you'll see why inside.
4. Go to your table and hang out. There is sort of a mad dash among the servers to start greeting guests and taking orders. See how smart you were, though? You have a full drink (perhaps one of their exceptional craft beers?) and you are just peacefully reviewing the food menu. Ahhhh
5. Enjoy the wonderful food! Orders arrive quickly, and the food is a step up from basic pub fare. We love the portobello mushroom sandwich, fries, Brussels sprouts with bacon, chicken fingers and salads. 
6. Marvel at the talented musicians! They typically play in the round with each songwriter playing a song followed by the next one doing the same. You'll hear a variety of artists - enjoy the ride!

So, that's it...pretty simple! Have fun and keep this on your rotation in Nashville!

If you are in Nashville, but not trying to get all in the country scene, check out The Basement East. New Found Glory was wrapping up their 20 year tour and the venue was awesome!! Drink prices weren't inflated -- low end at $2 up to maybe $5-6 which is great because you can stroll over to the food register and grab a a sandwich or guac n chips. 

Venue had a decent sound system that let you hear yourself instead of having to constantly scream.  I didn't have a chance to check out the pub, but I will if I'm back in the area.

Overall, it's a decent venue to see bands and other acts at prices you won't get in an arena/ballroom setting.

Food okay I guess. Servers are pretty disrespectful. The Mexican chick who served me was drinking or high or something. It doesn't seem professional, like I felt like a lot of them couldn't pass a random drug test very often from the way they were acting. But like I said the cooks do there job well at least.

Nice surprise!! 
We ordered some drinks and some of the Ultimate Nacho's while we decided what for what to eat for the meal. The drinks we had were all so good! AND pretty! They had an AMAZING salad! (Heads up the kitchen closes at 10pm) I got the house salad with chicken. It was SO GOOD! The seasoning was so good! I saw someone's salad go past my table and opted for it over a burger because the salad looked THAT good! (If I'm honest I was expecting more bar type food but this was like real restaurant good food!)
I enjoyed this salad on the 3rd floor- with some awesome live music! The drinks was sooo good! Smaller than some of the other broadway bar's, but still very good! We enjoyed the Born Free, Devil Without A Cause, & The Bobby.
The 3rd floor has nice big tables to seat 6 beside a window (so fun to get the breeze, watch people & hear other live music while the band changes out)

This is absolutely a must go to if you are on broadway! This is a 4 Story bar, music on every floor!

I LOVE it here. Local beers and fabulous live music in an industrial space that also succeeds in having a cozy, intimate feel. This was my first stop out on Saturday night and I honestly wish I spent more time here rather than checking out the grimy honky tonks on Broadway. The bartender was superbly friendly and small plates were excellent - especially the smoked veggie skewers and toasted ravioli. The cocktail menu surpasses anything you'd find down the street. Listening Room totally spoiled me with goodness before heading to Tin Roof on Broadway where I returned a gin & tonic because they accidentally poured tequila. But that's a review for another time.

We had a terrible experience on 5/29 while we were having lunch. We went to the top floor to enjoy the view. As we were eating lunch our bartender peeled her skin from her shoulder and let another customer sitting at the bar lick it off her finger. She then grabbed a lime and put it in a beer. I wish I was making this up but it is true. After we paid our check I spoke with the floor manager , Trevor and explained  what happen. I was not convinced much would be done. I went to the main floor to ask to speak with the General manager and was told she was on vacation. I requested to speak to the highest level manager on duty and was told they are busy right now and I could leave my number. I left my number and have not heard a thing. 
Concerned about health issues here. If this goes on in front of customers what happens in the back?

This was a welcome surprise on a busy football Sunday. It is just a little off of the beaten path and we noticed a rooftop floor with good sounding music as we passed. So we stopped in, listened a bit on the first floor and then found our way up to the top floor to listen to a very pleasant female vocalist performing solo. The sound level was low so we could listen to her excellent performance while enjoying a couple of very good football games. Granted, if all you want is football, the music might be a diversion. But if you would as soon listen to good music while watching, this will definitely fill the bill. 
We enjoyed a couple of reasonably priced drinks while we listened to the music and were served by pleasant wait staff. All in all, a very pleasant afternoon. We would recommend this for a leisurely afternoon of football (or other sports) and some good music.

The food was okay but thank goodness the music was amazing. 

We really had a great time! Our trip to Nashville would not have been the same without coming to The Listening Room.

Be sure to order the fried pickles as an appetizer but prepare yourself because they are on the sweet side instead of tangy.

We ordered the brisket sandwich and the two meat BBQ platter. I've never had a shredded brisket sandwich... I'm used to sliced. It tasted good but the texture was too similar to the pulled pork.

On the night we went, we got to listen to AJ Kross. If you haven't heard him he, is an excellent singer and songwriter. Actually all of the performers were great it's just that AJ was a real standout.

We would definitely go to The Listening Room again if we ever came back to Nashville.

Location - Great spot in the center of Broadway st.

Venue  - Huge spot with multiple levels of different bands and sometimes music. Large patio with a large bar, lots of tables and seating. 

Staff - Workers here are very chill and look happy to be working. 

Cost - Going rate is the same at all places here on Broadway St. 

Food - We ordered appetizers and it was a good portiin with good fresh taste.

Overall great spot to chill at and would definitely be back on my next visit to Nashville.

Great place to hear some local music!! Wait staff is friendly! Drinks are strong and yummy! American Badass! Yummy drink of jack Daniel's honey and rumchata!
Nachos are yummy for a late night snack!

Corny! After spending almost $200 for the two of us, I was expecting more. 

We come to Nashville every December and this was one of the last things that we hadn't experienced. I figured, what the heck, let's do it. Christmas time in Nashville is starting to catch on because it gets more and more crowded and more and more expensive each year. Traffic was horrific, so I was too worried to pre book the tickets. But low and behold, there were several seats available when we got there, right at 6:15 (boarding time).

Parking was easier than I expected. Tons of free parking was available in the Opry Mills Mall lot, which runs parallel to the Cumberland River.  

It was dark and chilly when we were standing to board, but they had an area that was blocked off with an awning like set up, so the waiting to board wasn't too bad. The waiting was the biggest annoyance. 

Once we finally got on board, the buffet was waiting, nice and hot. The food is the only reason I'd give it two stars. The buffet consisted of a ton of vegetables, roasted potatoes, mashed potatoes, stuffing, turkey, and roast beef. They pulled the food and stopped carving the turkey and beef at 7:45.  So you could grub until you were miserably stuffed. And then there was dessert around 8:30... that consisted of peppermint cheesecake and a sugar cookie. 

The wait staff were all hard to understand. I have been on countless cruises and I know some of the waitstaff there, are foreign, but this was bad. On cruises the waitstaff mingle with people close to 24/7, these guys on the showboat only few times a week. 

The Christmas show itself consisted of very few people. The dancers were 3 men and 3 women. I've been to many shows, and this was by far the worst. Who organized this?! Someone who mustn't have ever been to a show before. Literally, the shows on cruise ships are far better.

I was surprised at how much fun we managed to have here. If you're into taking fun photos, this place is awesome. We spent about an hour and a half here. 

The wax figures look insanely real, and although I knew that you could touch them (from seeing other people's pictures), I thought that there would be some kind of restriction (how do they keep them looking so good with people always touching them?). 

This place is located inside a really nice mall, which is kind of random and it was empty on the day that we went (I believe it was a Saturday?). Despite it's country music focus, there was a nice variety of musical stars from all genres. Everything from Billie Holiday to Ozzy Osbourne.

Not one of our favorite places we visited here on Broadway. The computers for employees were on the bar and we constantly had to move so we weren't in their way. The place was pretty busy and we did get service rather promptly, but it's sort of small & we couldn't really enjoy.

The food was ok, the show was a little cheesy, but after the show up on the top deck, Bob who played the fiddle and sang was very entertaining, I could have listened to him the whole 2 and 1/2 hours, the other thing to beware of, when we ordered the tickets on line, and picked up at Opryland, we paid 100.00 a person and the ticket said general admission, we thought that meant you just sat in what was available, not an assigned table, when we arrived, we were then told, general admission meant no lunch, ok, a lunch cruise you thought lunch was included in the 100.00, at this point not having eaten breakfast since we thought we were having lunch, thought 2 and 1/2 hours without food was going to be rough, so we asked is it possible to get food, told they would check if seating available yes, there was seating available but we had to see bartender and pay an additional 21.00 per person, so a treat for Father's day turned into a nearly 400.00 excursion because no drinks were included either. So, my final review, thought a bit pricey for what you got. And the view of downtown Nashville was nice, but that was about 10 minutes of the trip, the rest was an industrial plant and trees.  I would not go back again, and I visit Nashville about 4 times a year as my daughter lives in nearby Murfreesboro.
DorothyP 
Pittsburgh, PA

This place 
I'm a huge Johnny Cash fan and this was everything I could have asked for in a memorial. His piano, clothes worn by him and June, even the chair he sat in for the "Hurt" video. Just epic. And emotional too. It's pricey, as are most attractions like this, but definitely worth it for a fan.

When I first noticed the "Opening Soon" signs for 360 Burger two months ago, I was beyond excited. Finally, a beacon of light for good food in Antioch outside of the drab chain restaurants. When their doors finally opened, I was there on day 1 to sample their cuisine.
The restaurant itself is decorated beautifully. Once you get past the exterior, set in an almost vacant strip mall featuring 1 of 2 vacant best buy's in the area, the ambiance is very warming. Rustic wood walls and floors, gorgeous pictures of oysters, burgers and chicken, and great pieces of music history fill the surroundings. A stage is setup in a corner for nightly live music, a nice touch for those looking for some simple entertainment while they dine. 
The menu features a simple yet eclectic mix of burgers, chicken, oysters and sides that reflect the Swett brothers' southern culinary roots. The burgers themselves are quite pricey in comparison to Burger Up, Burger Republic and The Pharmacy, the prevailing modern burger joints of greater Nashville, and some even feature additional up-charges for cheese, bacon or certain sides. The execution of the menu leaves much to be desired. Upon my first trip (of 5) to 360 Burger, I wasn't told until after my food had been served that all of their burgers are cooked to a default well done temperature. In fact the only other temperature option is medium, and that must be requested upon ordering. Now to me, an amateur burger aficionado, a well done burger is a complete travesty, particularly when you feature local, organic grass-fed beef. Cooking a burger to that temperature robs it of the fantastic juiciness and flavor that I crave, and begins to delve into a meal that REQUIRES sauce rather than one that is complemented by it. After learning my lesson on the first trip, I knew to request medium going forward. Sadly, on the next 4 occasions all of my burgers were massively overdone despite my requests. This is more than likely a sign of a new and still-learning kitchen staff, but almost 6 weeks into this new venture these problems should be resolved. Cook times are also a problem as I've yet to receive a meal, either dine-in or carry-out, in under 20 minutes regardless of whether or not the restaurant is busy. 
The wait staff also is a work in progress. All of those that have waited on me have been very polite and courteous but still make very beginner mistakes for servers. When a guest sits down, they should be greeted in under a minute. If someone is waiting on a carry-out order, offer them a drink. BEFORE a meal is dropped, make sure they have silverware. When a guest orders, make suggestions and up sell. After someone receives their food, make sure everything is satisfactory. If ticket times are running long, check back with them and apologize if necessary, but don't pass the buck and blame the kitchen. I openly admit I'm being very nit-picky about these things, but as someone who has worked nearly every job in a restaurant over several years these are the things that make the difference between a good and bad experience. 
360 Burger probably doesn't have someone rooting for them to succeed more than me (outside of the owners and employees of course.) They have the chance to be special in a part of town where not many special things happen anymore. I give the 2 star recommendation as of the current state, but they have TONS of potential. Right now there are other places doing what they do better and cheaper, just farther away. As important as location is, and 360 Burger is the closest to me, I'll drive the extra 15 minutes to have a better experience. I just can't wait until I don't have to anymore.

I am Kid Roooock...well I'm not, but we did stop in to his Big Honky Tonk Bar and Grille while visiting Nashville. I got the burger and fries and absolutely loved it! It was cooked and seasoned to perfection. The place was really hopping on a Friday Night with live music. 

The staff was very friendly and got the order out in a relatively short amount of time. They were quick on the refill of drinks, which is very, very important! The drink menu was plentiful and varied. The decor fit in with the bar vibe and live music. 

Would definitely go here on my next trip to Nashville. Which hopefully be soon, I loved Nashville. See you at Kid Rock's Honey Tonk!

Absolute garbage!!!! Went there for late night bar food cause it was one of the only places that served last 2330. Service was horrible as in the bartender was an absolute dick, no thanks have a good night, nothing!!! Took 20 minutes (the female bartender said it would take that long) for 12 wings that cost $14. If you're drunk and looking for food, do yourself a favor and order a pizza.

So on a spontaneous trip up to Nashville we found ourselves staring at a strip of bars playing various genres of live music. The day was super hot and country is not my thing so we decided on Kid Rock's multilevel restaurant. The first two floors seem to be the main band and they sounded real good but being hot and cranky at this point we went up the stairs one more to level 3. There really was not much going on. A band was setting up. A large bar in the middle.  We waited a pretty long time for a waitress and ordered iced tea which came to us with maybe two ice cubes per glass. He ordered wings which were just ok and I got a salad for $9 which was basically Publix salad mix dumped in a bowl. Pretty disappointed.  However I had my sights set on a bourbon banana cake off their dessert menu.  Through every bite of this Publix salad I was awaiting soft banana cake with butterscotch icing and toffee pieces. How could that ever be wrong??? Well I'll tell you. It was probably in the fridge for over a week and the icing chipped off in pieces away from the half vanilla half possibly banana cake. Oh and Heath bar crumbled over the side. I wanted to cry. Beyond that, the food was pricey for what it was. Service sucked. It was so loud that all you could hear up there was a horrible mix of bands from all the neighboring bars competing and then begging each individual with the tip jar. Oh and be careful leaving. You may trip over passed out college girls in pools of vomit.

Normally don't write reviews of places like this and keep yelp for the more "restauranty" establishments but these reviews on here are harsh.
This is one of my favorite places on broadway. It was the first new country artist owned spot to open up on the strip. Now with Aldean's and Luke Bryan's taking center stage, this place still holds its own.

Always a great band on the first floor, a DJ late night on the second, and a great hangout spot on the roof (if you can make it up the 500 stairs).

I loved this place! We stopped in on Friday night and made a point to come back again on Saturday night! The bands were awesome and we were able to get drinks pretty quickly, except on the 3rd bar, they seemed a lot slower up there. Definitely check it out!

Big, beautiful place of good times and great music on Broadway.  Several floors of fun each filled with great music and fun.

The rooftop was my favorite.  You can scan the entire downtown area and are across the street from the famous Johnny Cash Museum.

Food menu is limited but it is all pretty good.  Being from Detroit - I will however call out "Bobbie" and ask "WHERE IS THE MAC n CHEESE"??

I am a huge Johnny Cash fan and I have wanted to visit this museum since the announcement was made in May '12 that it would be opening. My girlfriend Julie was an excellent sport and made the pilgrimage with me on a really crappy weather day. The museum has some great artifacts and is a must stop for anyone who calls themselves a fan of the Man In Black.

Got away for the SEC tourney and we usually go to TinRoof since it's a UK bar but it was packed. Dierks is fairly new and has i believe the highest rooftop bar downtown Nashville. You'll get your quad work out in that's for sure! Lol 

We needed up in the second floor on Friday and I had the mushroom burger and it was a pretty good burger. Fries were seasoned well and crispy.  We also tried the wings and they were good without the sauce. The hot sap was too hot for me. The band that afternoon was fantastic. Saturday we ended up here and did the first half on the rooftop as it was a nice day out. Ordered the artichoke
Dip and the bbq fries. Both were really good especially for bar food.

In the heart of Downtown Nashville this juke joint is full of fun. Full bar with food and usually live music playing. One of the many country/honky tonk bars on the strip. Very touristy of course due to it being in the epicenter of the strip but still a fun place to visit if you are in town for something. Didn't stay long but if was sufficient for what I was looking for which was a cold beverage.

Worth the visit. We laughed the entire way through. My youngest danced with Beyoncé on stage, my mom finally got to kiss Blake Shelton, and I got to dance with Timberlake. 

We got a good discounted rate on groupon

Pretty cool bar, i know they just opened and they are still working out the kinks. We came on their soft opening night, so I wont be too harsh on the review. The drinks were decent, the bands featured that night were pretty cool. I was impressed, one of the girls from American idol was featured.  The band took a while to set up, but that was because the band was waiting for her to show. 

I like the overall feel of the place its wide open and has an mezzanine area where people can sit and on a nice night they had all the windows open for cross breeze. There is a bar upstairs, downstairs in the middle and off to one side, and another mini bar as you come in, so plenty of places to sit and/or get a drink at the bar. We didn't go to the roof top, but it looked pretty cool from the street, I believe there is another band up there. 

They still had a few things to work on, but I am sure they'll get It together soon, like they only had 2 TVs and no mirrors in the bathrooms.

I've been here twice on trips to Nashville. Both times did not disappoint. Dierks Bentley chooses very talented bands to perform at his honky-tonk. Both times the service was great. One recommendation is to get a table early on a Saturday night and then stay for the duration. You won't have to worry about being jampacked and will have a spot to sit and place your drinks. Our most recent trip brought us there on a Sunday night. Matt from security was absolutely fabulous and figured out how to get my husband's favorite NBA team game on one of the TVs in the upstairs bar. This meant that I could get my live music fix and he could still watch the game. We were so grateful that Matt went above and beyond to do this for us! The atmosphere is fun and the food was good too. Definitely make whiskey row a stop on your list of honky-tonks on Broadway.

My first wax museum experience and wow they are realistic! It was just like I was hanging out with all my favorite country music artists. 
Lots of photo opportunities and you can move at your own pace.
I'm heading home to watch the movie ASAP. Well put together. Makes me want to pack rat all my stuff and open a museum.

So my family LOVED this show. The talent was fantastic. We were in the front row and my kids were just loving it. The only reason I removed a star was the food. The fooD was not my favorite but honestly, I didn't care that much. The experience was more important to me and we all loved it. 

After the show was over the cast came out on the floor and greeted everyone. They took pictures with the kids and were very friendly. 

We got a nice family photo that they took when we arrived. You do have to pay for that but it was nice and worth it! Nice memorabilia from out trip to Nashville! 

Give it a try and have a great time. See you next time!

Food is good but the menu is pretty standard pub/bar food - sandwiches, salads and burgers. I had a ham and cheese melt. It wasn't anything memorable but it was definitely tasty! The artichoke dip was really good and the drinks were yummy. 

The real reason to come here is the entertainment and atmosphere. The live music here is great! We felt very welcomed by the staff and really enjoyed our time here. We were here on a Saturday night and did not have trouble finding a table. We would definitely come back for drinks and music.

So if you're visiting Nashville of course you go to Broadway to see all the bars, and on a Saturday you can spend the whole day and not hear every band or hang out in every joint.  But whatever your opinion of Kid Rock, you ought to check out his place.  When we went - at 10 in the morning - it was getting busy and by 10:30 their were 4 bands playing.  One on the main floor and 3 on the 3rd, 4th and 5th levels.  We went to the 5th to be on the rooftop.  We sat at the bar, and the one negative is no draft beer, but otherwise it was a great day, plenty of servers and the beer was cold.  Loved hearing the band even though I'm not in to country.  We ordered the Big Ass Dog, and here was the surprise for me...it was big as hell and it was good.  I don't mean dog at the ball park decent, I mean good, with a wonderful tasted to it, fresh ingredients and so big at the end my girlfriend and i stopped eating the bun so we could finish the dog.  If the damn dog is this good, I wonder how good the other food is.  I dug this joint.

This was once my go-to place on the weekends, but it got to be so crowded that I phased it out.  However, I was reminded that this can be a great place to go during off-times (weeknights especially) as though it is still busy, its more relaxed than coming on the weekends.

Despite always having a packed bar I get my drinks refilled in a pretty timely fashion.  The food is great bar food, a bit heavy but thats to be expected (drinking and pub food go hand in hand really).  I love their mahi mahi sandwich and they have the best fried pickles in town.

I know a lot of people come here to watch games on TV but I wouldn't recommend it for that.  Again, this place gets crowded and loud fast and despite the projection screen at the front of the bar its hard to see.  Also the outdoor patio sometimes has live music or a DJ so it can clash with anything you're trying to watch.  Unless its lunchtime I wouldn't say to come here to watch anything on TV.

I would recommend starting your night here but not finishing it unless you want to fight for drinks and standing room.  Come on a Sunday night if you want a chance at a table or seat at the bar.  This place can be a ton of fun or horrible, depending on when you choose to come in.

Great beer, food, and excellent staff!! Got a Groupon for beer tasting and an appetizer for 2. I loved the experience, they have good beer selection and the Nachos we ordered were good. I personally liked the way the place was decorated, it just felt artsy and cozy. The place had a couple of TVs in case you want to watch it instead of talking to each other lol. It also had outdoor seating with a smoking and a non smoking area. I went during the day and parking was ok but I don't know how it can get at night. Overall I really enjoyed my time there, like I said, staff was great and beer was even better!

My first and last time here was last night on New Year's Eve. A group of people kept talking behind us even though we nicely asked them to stop. Then we informed security and they did not address them. When I took a picture of the offenders someone on the row below them tried to slap my phone out of my hand. 12/31/16 The John Prine, Jason Isbell, & Kacey Musgraves show. These people talked constantly from 7:30pm until we got up around midnight and sat in seats on the third row that people already left. It's clear the trashy concert goers were just there to party and not watch performances. My husband and I also spent a lot of money in there getting drinks and snacks. I'm pursuing this until someone from the Opry apologizes to me. That's around. $500 down the drain!

We were in town for a convention and needed a break. Had the best time and the band, sorry can't recall their name, were more fun than we expected. Had me doing a cameo or Mustang Sally!  If we make it back to the Nashville this will be on our must do list! Service was great, food average.

There's not much more to say than what everyone else has already said, but if you haven't been here yet, what are you waiting for? 

I used to regular this place in Texas- even have my own plate on the wall. Here in Nashville, I'm not so much a regular, and only due to the fact you have to pay to park or catch a cab here. I love the brew selection and the fare. It's a fun place to be. It's kinda like a candy store for the grown ups. 

The place is pretty big and super comfy year round.

I didn't have overly high expectations of this place, but I was expecting something decent. Unfortunately, it was mediocre. They tried to make us happy. I give them credit for that. But the food was below par. My burger was lacking. The nachos my wife ordered came out cold. After we reluctantly complained, the chef did come out and apologized, offering to make it right. For a place with taps in their name, the beer selection was also uninspired. The service was ok. The front porch is nice, but without good food or beer, it's kind of a waste. I didn't hear the live music this place offers on a regular basis. Maybe it makes up for the other short-comings.

I've been taking advantage of all the music in Nashville and it's been great. My only regret was going to the grand Ole Opry.  My first issue was the prices, which is double or even triple what I paid elsewhere in town.  The Ryman show set me back about $40 for a nationally recognized group, other venues had $10 covers and superb up and comers. The Grand Ole Opry was a mix of washed up performers (that had lost their range and voices that trembled in the wrong places), cute undeveloped talent (that belonged in a school talent show) and a headliner who will play 2 songs and spend most of the time on stage pushing Grand Ole Opry related activities.  Riders of the Sky are an enjoyable act that reminded me of a Disney show that you go to because your feet hurt, a slick production with good musicians and the jokes a little too well rehearsed. And again, they do 2 songs.  And after 2 songs, yet another commercial pushing a Grand Ole Opry restaurant, cruise or tour. And one got the sense that the time schedule was more important than the music.  One act played without their guitars plugged in. One member noticed and commented but no back stage person came out to fix it. They just played, strumming guitars that you couldn't hear in such a large auditorium. I went here to check it off my bucket as a music lover. I'm writing this to tell you all to skip it.  Seriously, skip it. It's a shame to come to Nashville and go here rather than sample the amazing music happening elsewhere in town.

We paid our cover charge, sat at the bar and gave the white band a chance. They were decent, but not blues singers. We paid our ride bartender his 9 bucks for a cocktail a d coke and left 21.00 poorer

I'd give them a five star if the Friday and Saturday night scene there wasn't so bad.

Don't get me wrong, I'm a member of their club, and am about 70-80 beers in to the 200 required to get a "plate" on their wall.  I love their pretzels, and especially love many of the beers there.  If you go when they aren't packed, you can generally expect a calm, comfy atmosphere.

The waitresses are a mixed bunch.  Some, frankly, aren't great.  Some, however, are awesome and very knowledgeable.

The only problem I have is, going on a Friday or Saturday night will mean fighting for a seat.  Now, prior to becoming a member, this also seemed to mean slow, generally bad service.  Since my friends and I are all members, though, and generally tip well, I feel that that has changed.  To a first time visitor, a Friday or Saturday night will usually entail searching for a spot to sit, waiting a long time to get served, and they'll likely be out of their more common sales that night.

Go on a weeknight.

Great atmosphere and wonderful hot dogs! Very fun - cornhole on the front patio, places to sit, good wait staff. Very laid back and a fun place to come for a beer. They also have $2 domestics every day from 11-7!

My son and I did the tour and really enjoyed it. The person who directed our tour was very experienced. You get to hear about the Country Music Hall of Fame, how it started, how country singers  become a member, visit the behind the scenes dressing room, walk on the stage, take pictures and basically share the experience. If you are in the area and like country music this might be a fun choice of a way to kill an hour or so. It is close the the large Opry Hill Mall and close to Gaylord Opryland Resort & Convention Center which is monster in itself.
It's a fun way to play tourist for a day.

Like Name, Like Beers, Like, probably have given more stars than the available 5. we always have good time here and the beer collection from all over the world will hell lot of taps to taste.

Pros:
Many Many beer options for everyone

Cons:
Not really any issues, but the place gets crowded during weekends.

ate lunch here with the family. Beer chilli, chicken wings with sauce on the side and white cheddar mac&cheese. Chilli was thick, meaty and spiced just right, the pasta mellow but tasty - good for kids. The wings could have used more cooking but weren't undercooked, just not impressive. The celery and carrots that came with were largely frost-bitten from cold storage, but we got better ones upon request. 
We enjoyed the atmosphere and live music though I wish there weren't TV screens at every corner showing sports and news. there was no cover charge.

Extremely bad lunch service. If I could give zero stars, I would.  The place was practically empty around noon but it took forever to get our food and the waitress didn't offer an explanation, in fact she never checked back with us after our food finally arrived. We also had to flag her down to get our ticket to pay. Lousy, lousy service and the food was not that good.

My dad and I came here back in the first part of Spring(better late review than never). After driving around downtown three times trying to find a parking spot, we finally found a parking garage right down the street from here. We decided to come here because we like live music. There was a great band playing. Food and drinks were good. Service was decent, not great but not bad. Bathroom could use some more upkeep but otherwise no complaints. I'd come back here next time we're down South.

Food was ok. My husband's ribs were too dry. I got the brisket sandwich and it was tasty. The tater tots were yummy too. The wait staff was terrible and not very thoughtful from the moment we stepped in. There was live music off and on during dinner which was not bad and the noise was at a good level where  we could still talk and hear each other without difficulty.

To enjoy this you must be a country music fan to appreciate it. Paid for the backstage tour and then went to the Friday night show. 

I am a fan so appreciated it, but it is expensive. The show was good because it covered the gamut  of country music (old and new) and had one of my favorite artists. Excellent tour guide who knew what she was talking about and was able to answer all the questions posed. 

Only got 4 stars due to price. Not recommend for families with children due to the price.
Went for Father's day and they did not disappoint. My meal was actually free as I am a dad. Slow but good service, nice brunch choices. Food was slow to arrive but everything was good.
We had a great time here during the day with our tween girls on a visit to Nashville. The host and crown were so fun. Karaoke first for our group but these girls wanted to sing all day.

My son and I did the tour and really enjoyed it. The person who directed our tour was very experienced. You get to hear about the Country Music Hall of Fame, how it started, how country singers  become a member, visit the behind the scenes dressing room, walk on the stage, take pictures and basically share the experience. If you are in the area and like country music this might be a fun choice of a way to kill an hour or so. It is close the the large Opry Hill Mall and close to Gaylord Opryland Resort & Convention Center which is monster in itself.
It's a fun way to play tourist for a day. The concerts are Tuesday, Fridays and Saturday so if your in the area see if they still have tickets.
Amazing.  The history was great.  Glad we got to go. The only regret was not booking on a weekend with more "modern" artists.

I've been a fan of Jack White for 2 or 3 years now and I have most definitely heard of the legendary Third Man Records. It doesn't seem like much from the outside but on the inside it is unlike anything else I've even seen, or experienced. The store is just breathtaking with how well it merges the new and the old.

I've been to BB Kings several times since moving to Nashville. I guess it's one of those things you want to do if you are visiting Nashville. However, I'll be ok if I don't go again. It's a been there done that kind of thing. We met some friends from out of town there last night and the restaurant could only serve beer since they lost their liquor license. I don't know how an establish such as BB Kings could let something like that happen. The food is pretty decent however.

Because of a tight schedule the group I was with decided not to go on the backstage tour but we did go to the Grand Ole Opry House and gift shop. After making a few, way too expensive, gift purchases we walked the grounds. It is truly amazing for Country Music fans to know the musicians that have played here. A Mecca for all country music fans. 

It is located in the same parking lot as a mall so I wonder how it would have been to visit when the mall is full and a performance is going on. I wish we would have been able to see a performance here but the road trip must go on!!!

I took a friend of mine here to enjoy some music and have a few drinks. It was our first time being there, after remodeling into Revelery & Anthem of course.  As I walked up to the front entrance of Revelery I immediately noticed the old school boom boxes layered on the wall just behind the counter where the girl was checking ID's. It was pretty sweet to see them utilize them for that.  It immediately gave me the impression, along with the girl at the front door, that this is a trendy place now.  
We walked in and immediately I noticed the difference in layout from the previous business that had took residence in there.  The bar is much more pleasant to look at and sits in the space on the lower floor just across from where they built a dj booth that overlooks the floor.  It was nice.  Much nicer then I had expected.  We immediately went to the bar for drinks and after I had ordered I heard the bartender explaining that there were drink specials for this night involving jack daniels and vodka drinks.  Luckily I already ordered a whiskey sour so my face lit up realizing I was getting a lot more for my buck.  I checked the place out a bit, they even have an outside smoking area that was built onto the side so you no longer have to walk all the way out the front any more.  Brilliant idea if you ask me.  I found a spot at the railing bar on the upper level overlooking the dance floor and bar area to sit back and enjoy my drink.  The dj's there were playing for their first night as Represent Anthem Vol.001.  Which is a drum n bass music night.  If you enjoy the music genre I would recommend catching the next night when they're there.  I noticed during my time there that they even serve food as a friend of mine was eating something they had brought out to him on the bar.  So I may need to check out their menu on my next venture here.  I highly recommend this place for a good spot to hang with friends while listening to some good music.

Very nice hotel!! Great place to see and visit. The only thing that grinds my gears is.... You pay an extra $18 resort fee and parking is 23 bucks. Extra fees becoming annoying!!! Neat place to see though

I got the shrimp and fish platter and it was amazing! You get 8 shrimp and 1 catfish filet. The filet is breaded fantastic! It's so light and crunchy! Some of the best catfish I have had. The shrimp are always breaded great and very crunchy! I'm a big seafood person and what I tasted was GREAT seafood. I also had some of the dry rubbed wings and they tasted great as well. Really love the rub on the wings.

My husband and I walked in and we were greeted right away and I asked for a menu and a glass of water. A half an hour later my husband had to go ask one of the four bartenders for a drink. We were there for several hours in which we had to flag a server down every time... and we were sitting at the bar. The Spazmatics came on and the place became packed. We were having a lot of fun. The wait staff was much better when busy. Then the electric went out... it was soooo hot. The wait staff basically decided to stop serving. Needless to say we really tried to give this place a go. But after 4 hours of really crappy service enough was enough!

Never  been in the actual store, therefore, this is a review on the rolling travelling record bus that looks and feels more like a food truck than a record store. They were parked outside Ameoba records and of course at an hour to..the line up was long and was really slow moving. Even though we got a menu to choose from before hand, super fans still couldn't decide what the "f" they wanted and what was supposed to be a 3 minute transaction each turned into a 10 minute issue. Worse than a DMV line. My best friend and I were more efficient and were done within 3 minutes. It was awesome that we finally got to see the truck and like a true Asian tourist took tons of pics. We bought $88 worth of TMR shirt combined. They will be rolling an hour away from Coachella, therefore, we will hit them up again.

We had an amazing visit to BB Kings. Two of us ordered ribs and one ordered a pulled pork sandwich. The ribs were some of the best I have had! The cole slaw was delicious and the beans had some southern kick. There was even a solo artist playing that night who was very entertaining, wish I could remember his name. I would highly recommend anyone make a trip to BB Kings BBQ!!

So by the number of meals I've had here, I ought to earn a plate (Saucer?) on the Wall!

Fantastic selection of brews (and a limited selection of wines and other spirits) with a good food menu well prepared. 

Ambiance fits well into Union Station and aside from various promotions (trivia and themed nights) occasionally live music in the evening. 

Friendly staff (where most folks know my name) make it an enjoyable place to take the adults and work colleagues.

I've been waiting to visit this place since it opened. The Third Man Records building is everything you'd expect from Jack White: old-timey Americana, with wax figurine machines, vinyl records, a recording booth straight out of 'O Brother, Where Art Thou?', a listening room, coin powered mechanical musical monkeys, and even books of poetry and a collexion of album reviews from White's new(-ish) Third Man Books publishing house. The staff are knowledgeable, courteous, and very personable!
Belcourt Taps is one of my favorite places to eat! The parking isn't bad and the location is great! If you've never tried their loaded fries then you are seriously missing out!

We went to see Carrie Underwood & the other artists on August 10th. We got there early to get parking before the 9:30 show and went to keep ourselves busy before hand. The show was great, it's so cool to hear and see other artists I hadn't known before- there was even a comedian! Loved it. We got really good seats for $70 each and they were even comfy & roomy because of the bench style. The key is going for an artist that you know and then it'll be worth the money no matter what, because you'll hear stuff you know and stuff you don't!

I rode my motorcycle from Canada to Memphis/Nashville and on the top of my list was to go to Third Man records to get some t-shirts.  Another person posting a review mentioned the girl behind the counter with bright red lipstick and I also would like to say she's weird and off putting...the other girl was super sweet and very cute.  T-shit quality is kinda shitty and smaller than a normal men's medium..

I went to Dawg House to catch some March Madness. It was a Thursday night and the place was really... empty. That being said we were able to sit down right away and overall its definitely a good place to watch a game, theres tons of TV's and seating. 

The beer list was better than average, they had a lot of local options. I was disappointed to learn that they don't have any beers on draft. Or maybe they do and I somehow missed the taps and they don't mark it in the menu? 

Dawg house seems to specialize in hot dogs and related items. We got pigs in a blanket and they were realllly good, I think they may have been deep fried instead of baked, which is likely why they tasted like heaven. They were also served in a paper plate shaped like a dog bowl. Cute?.. Kind of. 

After a beer and splitting the pigs in a blanket my bill was around $7, so its definitely fairly priced. There was a band setting up for some live music, but I left before they began, I have a feeling they played to a fairly empty house though. It will be interesting to see if the Dawg House stays in business.

I have been at a couple of Flying Saucer's during my travels. They have been fairly consistent, yet each has it's own vibe. This location is more bar-centric. Which was fine for me, but just so you know. The bartenders were very knowledgeable and attentive. Food was good. It is a step above traditional bar food. Great beer selection keeps me coming back.

Well worth the $20 for the back stage tour!
They tour every 15 minutes, for a 40-50 minute walking tour.
The tour includes walking on stage, through auditorium, dressing rooms, mailboxes, member plaque area, sound proof auditorium, and stars entrance.
The building has a lot of character and the tour guide has a lot of great information to provide.
Great pizza, best enjoyed in groups. Great beer selection. Some go to study others to explore, try 'em for sure!

What an experience! We were so excited that we were able to get tickets to a show the day before. It was a 9:30 PM show but it was well worth it! It was Darius Rucker, Kelly Pickler, Craig Morgan, Lee Greenwood, John Conley, Chris Janson, and Trace Adkins. The show was phenomenal and felt like a once in a lifetime experience. It was a salute to the troops night and the whole room was filled with patriotism! It was awesome! Next time we are going to do the tour!

This is one of the top 5 places I take my friends from out of town. It is definitely a beer garden-topia. I love that the servers help with recommending drinks that fit your pallet. I just wish the food menu had more selections.

Last night I was so excited to finally get visit the famous B.B. King's Blues Club. I looked online to see that the club closed at 11:00 pm.
