My husband and I were very excited about the live entertainment and good food that we'd heard about until we were turned around by the hostess. We arrived at 8:30 pm and the hostess informed us that the kitchen was closed and it the club was closing in about an hour. She also told us that it was a thirty minute wait for a table. Two parties that we walked in with were seated within minutes. I could see several OPEN tables and servers just standing around chatting it up. Poor customer service and business practices.
If you love beer this is the place to be. And if you don't love beer and you want to try it out this is the place for you. Plenty of beers to choose from. Over a 100!

I like this place. It's a cool, chill environment to hang out with friends. It does get a bit noisy at night, but that's all the fun. Their selection of beer is amazing, but I wish they carried more Light craft beers. 
The food is real good. The goat salad is amazing. I wasn't thrilled with the nachos, due to the grease, but that's also cause (I assume) it's real cheese, and not that "nacho cheese" stuff. very tasty and always good times!

Went with a group of 11 ladies all wanting to have a good time however when I ordered a Coors light and a water I was charged $12!!! Thought the price was way too high so we decided to leave. As we were headed out we asked two employees how much do they normally charge and they both gave me a different and lower number. I asked to speak with a manager and was told they didn't know where he was. As we were leaving we ran into a man who said he was the manager and yes that price was wrong and he would bring us a voucher for each of us for a $1 beer. He never came back with them. Sadly they lost a lot of money from a big group. I will never come back to this establishment or recommend it to anyone else.

We first walked down the Broadway which was very busy so we turned into 2nd street and found the B.B.King's. It was not to busy and we were seated right away. But we had to pay a $5/person cover for the live music (not all bars in Nashville take a cover) - one thing right away - the group was worth the 5 bucks. Service was ok - I think it's not easy to do a good job in this environment (often very loud and busy). I ordered the tuna sandwich - and I have to say it was really done to the point - nice rosa. I was in a lot of so called gourmet restaurants where the chef was not able to do it that way - so compliment to the chef. My son had the catfish tasted ok - so overall (expect the tuna which was superb) the food was ok exactly what you expect in a place like this. But I do not like this papers where the food is served on (that's to fast food style). I would come again because of the music, not to busy and easy seating and ok food and drinks.

Earnestly quirky & trendy, & clearly catering to a specific clientele, this Nashville record shop is a bit off the beaten path if you're thinking of walking from the downtown area.  This tiny, but extremely crowded & popular shop is overflowing with randomness.  Fans of Jack White & The White Stripes will be pleased.  Fans of more diverse genres?  Less so.  You're there for a reason & it's to support the output of this label, whether it's its output of releases on CD & vinyl, patches, matches, t-shirts & stickers, or decidedly more unique opportunities, like the chance to step into a soundbooth & record your own noise for posterity.

It's worth a visit if you're interested in a more spirited & playful side of Nashville & the staff are friendly.  Just go early if you can, to avoid the crowds.

It is a bar; so the food is bar food.  However,  the burgers, tots, fries and the rest are tasty and cooked to perfection.  Whats continues to set them above is their service.  Excellent Servers, Bartenders, and Security   if you are visiting Nashville - it is a must attend!  Great music and atmosphere.
Loved the pork platter. Great live music and chill place to hang out and have some drinks! My foreign exchange friends loved it too!!

We came here because other place had 1 hour wait on a Saturday.  They said we'll seat you now. Ok so maybe it wasn't our first choice but, oh boy, this place was good. It's a burger place. You want a good burger then go. You won't be disappointed.  Go drinks too. Great Atmosphere.  Go. Take a chance. You'll like it.

Live music sometimes.

I wasn't aware that there were more of these across the country.  I am glad there are.  Maybe I can get back to another one soon.  As far as chain tap houses go, this is close to the top of my list.  Great beer selection and knowledgeable staff.  Very cool atmosphere.  Plenty to look at and talk about inside.  Their beer club is a really neat addition for someone who can visit often.  It was super hot in Nashville, the AC in here was cranked.  It may have even been a bit chilly for some, but what a welcome relief from the heat and humidity.  Check it out!
Amazing! Rolled into Nashville after 8:00, made it here before last call for food at 9:00 and enjoyed delicious burgers and 2 for 1 drafts. We'll be back.

Atmopshere- Good, the bf and I stopped in once for drinks and a 2nd time for food. Loved the music (live band) and the decor. beware, they do charge a $5 cover after a certain time. 

Drinks- Great, good prices

Food- Not so great, I ordered the pasta primvera with mac and cheese (because i can't resist mac and cheese). The primevera didnt have the variety of veggies im use to and was super bitter. The mac and cheese made my mouth dry. It was just awful. I took it home and tried it the next day, still nasty.  I just expected a better tatse. My bf did not enjoy his fried chicken either. 

I would still come back simply bc of the drinks and music. BB Kings gives you a break from country and and puts you into a world of jazz.

If you are in Nashville and don't see an Old Opry show you are missing a piece of Americana.

My daughter and I were doing Nashville on one of my business trips.  She always wanted to go. 

We hit the bars of course (all fantastic) but decided since we were in town it was worth the price of admission to see what the Opry House was all about.

We were not disappointed.  I recommend you get a ticket and eat at the BBQ restaurant walking distance across the parking lot.

A great thing to do with your adult kid on a family adventure.

We recently attended a very well attended event at the Flying Saucer and we were impressed with both the service and food. I was also reminded that I had never eaten here before.. 

We started with the soft pretzels that comes with your choice of two dipping sauces, we chose spicy mustard and queso. These were awesome! I had the buffalo chicken wrap and fries which was great as I could taste buffalo sauce but it wasn't drowning in sauce, so the wrap held up well. My mom had the hippie hollow which is a vegetarian dish of pita of greens, hummus, and other things she omitted. She got this with the side salad which was not only a decent size but a pleasant surprise of romaine, black olives, red onions, and "Italian cheeses". Another surprise was that unlike other places there isn't an up charge to replace the side with a salad. 

As I said the event was well attended but the three ladies who were working were pros. They carefully navigated the crowd and we never wanted for anything. Food was correct and hot. We did ask for water refills from the runner who dropped off my mom's meal since she was coming back with mine. She delivered. Only to have our server come behind her with two more glasses of water.
DELICIOUS!! Super reasonable prices and a lot of food. Literally in a back alley. It has lots of character and everyone was ver nice. Definitely coming back!
Good vibes, good service, good food and good signature drinks...off the beaten path for a little something different..

Great local hangout. What I like about this spot is that it's a no judgment zone. Everyone sings carefree and it's a good time. This is my second time visiting this location and the vibe was consistent both times. I would definitely recommend to anyone looking to not take themselves too seriously and have a silly good time!

This place was a really shop. Lots of neat items and you can tell that Jack White has created a really neat environment there. My only gripe was that the vinyl selection of was limited to mostly third man records and live albums made there. When I think record store I was expecting more selection.

Still really great place to check out in Nashville!

This has been on my bucket list for a really long time and it absolutely lived up to my expectations.  Though I hadn't heard of a single soul who stepped on that stage, and even though I went BY MYSELF, I still had the time of my life and will be adding it to my itinerary every time I'm in Nashville from now on.  Totally worth the price of admission!

Tip: If you're going along, spring for a front row seat.  It's amazing.

You can't go to Nashville and not take in a night at the Grand Ole Opry. I mean, this is the place where country music began and even if you're not a country music fan (although, how can you not be? aghast) you can still tolerate it for a few hours. The night I was there, Trisha Yearwood showed up unexpectedly along with Garth Brooks and it was awesome. The food, the beer, and the bottled water are what you would expect from any concert venue. Go early because the Opry shares their space with the mall and parking is hell to find. Even if you sit in the nosebleed seats you can see everything because they have two gigantic TVs however, I recommend buying your ticket early enough so you can be as close to the stage as possible because almost all of the performers walked along that area and met the audience.
Great drinks, great appetizers, super friendly bartender and very prompt service. There wasn't a band playing while we there but they obviously have it since they have a stage.
Really friendly staff and some great food! The catfish po'boy was great and the price was on point. Great location near Vanderbilt University and Music Row.

I will be the first to admit that by no means am I a country music fan, however I couldn't turn down the opportunity to tour one of the most famous concert venues in Country Music history. While visiting Nashville I decided to book a tour of the venue and am very pleased that I did. The tour started out backstage, allowing you to see the artist entrance and even the Opry Post Office where members of the Grand Ole Opry get their mail. We learned that the lowest mailbox was reserved for the shortest member of the Opry, Little Jimmy Dickens, who stood 4'11 before he passed away in 2015.

Another interesting location was Studio A, which is located behind the stage and has been home to shows like Nashville and Hee Haw. Next up was the dressing rooms, we were able to see each dressing room that the stars would prepare in before their Showtime. Each dressing room has its own unique theme too. While I did the day tour, I was told that sometimes during the evening tour you might even see a star or two backstage. We also had a chance to see the large community room where most of the stars hang out after the show. The only thing left to see was the Opry itself, we were carefully lead out to the stage to to see where all the performances of the legendary broadcast have taken place. One highlight was the ability to stand in the circle of the original stage from the Ryman theater, where so many legends have stood before.

The tour was about an hour and concluded with a stop in the gift shop. My recommendation would be to opt for the evening tour before a show, however some of the tour may not be available but you have a pretty good chance of seeing a country music star!
Great way to spend a Sunday night!! 1/2 off bottles of house wine..don't mind if we do! Service is great and everyone is so incredibly nice. Live music and the Caesar salad was great! We'll be back!
Great beers and food. Service isn't too bad with the exception of one waitress that came over and threw the menus and coasters on the table. Maybe just a bad day.

Just like any other karaoke bar, tips make the wait to sing significantly shorter. $20 basically gets u up in the next couple people. Crowd was a great mix of people and were all supportive of the singers.

Pretty good for a back alley, but anywhere else I'd pass.  We ate here because our first three or four other choices had an hour or so wait and we were all tired and hungry at the end of a long travel day.  The menu consisted of about 50% hamburgers, a few salads, and some other items so you might think the hamburgers would be really good, but that wasn't the case.  Our party of 5 all had burgers and no one really enjoyed.  The next day, we found the "world's best burger" according to the sign in the window. Didn't actually try it, but window signs never lie.   If interested, it's on Broadway between 5th and 6th.

Went here this past Friday night with some friends for a bachelorette party. We got there around 10:30 and it was pretty busy. I do enjoy a variety of beers, but I am by no means a beer aficionado. The guy who helped me (wish I would've gotten his name!) was super friendly and I told him the type of beers I liked, and he offered up a suggestion. Can't remember the name of it, but it was a grapefruit type beer and it was awesome! I wish I would've gotten the name of it because I really enjoyed it. Love the atmosphere of this place and the penny wall where all the taps are located was really cool. We only stayed for about 30 minutes (not a good place for a bachelorette party necessarily) but I would love to go back again to try out some different beers they have on tap.

Not crowded at all on a Friday night which is a welcome change to all the other places that pack a 1 hour wait around downtown.  We were welcomed with friendly smiles and the staff was very nice.

I got the Boston salad which was really enjoyable. They cook the chicken fresh so it's warm and juicy on top of your salad...forget the cold dry chicken most joints toss onto salads! I love how well seasoned and tender my chicken with my greens.

The boyfriend got the fried catfish po'boy. The fish was really crispy but in my opinion, a little under seasoned. Or perhaps under sauced because I thought a side of the remoulade with the sandwich was a perfect fix. Would have been better with more lettuce too.

I do have to say, the hushpuppies are the best I've ever had. Mix the two sauces into the same bite...mmmm. Could eat it all day!

For a drink I got the pineapple upsidedown martini, which was really good in that it really did taste like liquid pineapple upsidedown cake...unfortunately I don't do very well with super sweet drinks so I only for half way through. Glad I tried it though!

The boyfriend loved his margarita.

Would definitely come back, hopefully on a Tuesday when they have songwriter night or Saturday when there is live music.
This was a decent lunch spot.  I had the French dip, which was tasty.  The service was good.  I'll add it to my lunch go-to places.
This place is cool. Really is off an alley!  Anyway had that jalapeño burger and a whiskey (good lunch ha-ha) and it was really good. Good atmosphere and food and a nice little bar.

We were at the Grand Ole Opry on May 5,2018. It was an awesome show and experience. The people in Tennessee are very hospitable and friendly. Being able to see the live radio show in person was a dream come true.

WannaB's!  Yea!  So, every bar and restaurant on the strip (Broadway) in Nashville has live music.  Every single place.  It's a town chalked full of aspiring musicians - some of them pretty decent, others... meh.  Oddly, some of the best singers I heard on my visit to Nashville were to be found at the one place where the singers were the patrons.  Tourists, business men & women alike, all throwing down their best efforts on their favorite songs.  

Particularly impressed by the gal behind the bar, who OWNED a country song while still cracking beers and closing tabs.  Serious multitasking.

I was thoroughly unimpressed with this place. The food was average, and the service was terrible. The server had a total attitude and did not do her job properly. She forgot to take one person's order, and got snippy with people. Aside from the service, the menu was lacking. Only one dessert option. Most egregiously, they charge for soft drink refills. Really? Outrageous. I won't be back.

I would call this the best gift shop in town.

Jack White's studio company. Awesome gift shop. A vinyl recording booth, waxomatic, jukebox, a photo booth, and two turntables with records to sample. Have a number of vinyls recorded and cut in the building. I bought several myself. Prices were shockingly reasonable, a third of the store was on sale. No expenses spared in maintaining Jack White's vintage theme.

TMR is the greatest! From the record store employees to the incredible workers behind-the-scenes, I have always had positive experiences with the staff at this company. 

Contrary to other reviews I have read, I have received nothing short of excellent customer service from Cam Sarrett, who I've interacted with on multiple occasions. He often travels with the rolling record store, and from my experiences with him there, I'd say he was born to work with people. He was talkative and engaging with each customer he worked with, and also very helpful. I've never had a problem with him through email communication either. Cam seems like a genuinely kind and accommodating member of the TMR team. 

Overall, I love TMR and everything it offers to its customers. I'm definitely hoping to visit their store in Nashville again soon, I really want to record my own record in their Record Booth!

The bar service is horrid. I'm used to neighborhood bars in East Nashville, 12th South, and Division with owners who care about their business and hire cool people. Maybe these guys should take beginner lessons from what's truly Nashville.

The place and the food were pretty good but our waiter John H.  was HORRIBLE!  He was a dripping sweaty mess.  He screwed up the order and then argued that we ordered something that we didn't and then when I pointed out a second item was wrong he got upset.  He did not apologize nor attempt to make it right.  1st rule if customer service is always right.  Even if the are not.  In this, case we were right.

Im not a country music fan, but I was able to attend a performance here.
Some old timers and some new stars, the surprise guest was Rhonda Vincent.
Great show, nice place........
Only downside the $17 drink

For appetizers we tried fried pickles, fried catfish, and black-eyed pea hummus.  Of the three the fried pickles were the big winner. The black eyed pea hummus was overly seasoned with cumin and left a horrible aftertaste in our mouths.  Entrees:   the spinach salad with salmon, sliders, shrimp Po boy, ribs, and the brisket lunch entrée.  All entrées were average or above, but the ribs and brisket were amazing.  Quote from my friend Leslie: "the brisket is so good it'll make you smack yo' mama."  The ribs were falling off the bone and the barbecue sauce was spicy yet sweet and delicious.  Corn bread was a but dry, collard greens were mild, tender and tangy.  Lost points for service.  Waiter was scattered, brought us another table's order and did not return often to check on us.

With so much to do in Nashville it is refreshing to see Jack White doesn't charge an admission price. Even if you don't own a record player this place is worth a visit. The artifacts are plentiful and the staff is helpful. 

Well worth a visit after you chow down on some Nashville hot chicken.
What's there not to love! If you like country music this experience mustn't be missed.

This review has nothing to do with the quality of the music or the performances I saw.  This part was great.  I liked the format and the opportunity to listen to a variety of styles of country music.  This review is for the venue from the tickets to the parking, the lack of seats and the commercialism.  I really don't like anything about this place apart from the music and I'm not even a huge country music fan.  

We parked at least 3/4 mile away.  When you buy your tickets online, they're held in will call.  It took a long time to pick them up once we finally made it.  The seating is on benches and the woman who sat next to me literally sat down on me as she made her way to her seat.  Eventually people moved around a little to accommodate her but I was no where near my original seating plate that was in front of me.  It was really terrible.  Then they subject you to actual commercials on a big screen.  The program they hand you is sad.  They give you a line up but otherwise it's just a bunch of advertisements and more money grabbing and commercialism.  Cutting a piece of the stage from an historic theatre and pasting it into a place with so little heart and feeling doesn't move me whatsoever.  This place is really lame.
love the fish and chips special on thurs. great place to sit outside and drink a beer. great fried pickles and chicken tenders.

How disappointing.  Our waitress rushed everything along and low and behold messed up our order.  For a beer place, you'd think she know something about the beer or at least the food.  Neither succeeded and the attitude was a bit over the top.  After she totally botched our order, there was no apology, no "I'm sorry", no nothing.  Only a couple of sad bratwurst on a plate. Spend your time  and money elsewhere.   I was expecting more.  Even the beer menu is nothing uncommon. The place was empty.  Deserverbly so.

Cozy spot with good food and personable service.

My girlfriend and I originally intended to eat at Double Dogs down the road but the wait was insane due to Sunday football games, so we wondered up the street and chose Belcourt taps since it seemed empty and the menu outside looked good. 

First impressions: Dim lit, very moody interior which I liked. The tables are painted, ours had a dog on it. Interesting art on the walls. Limited open seating.

The place was nearly empty when we arrived around 1:15. The bartender Josh quickly made his way over with some menus and took our drink order.I have uploaded pics of the menu for other Yelpers to look at. I chose the buffalo chicken burger and my girlfriend made her own burger that was hardly as interesting as mine so I immediately forgot what it was. We also ordered a side of loaded fries.


The burger:

Ordered medium on a nice fluffy bun, lettuce, tomato, blue cheese, great beef, and buffalo chicken. The burger was large enough on its own to satisfy any appetite. You have the option of fries, beans, or cole slaw as a side. Fries were hand cut and quite good.

The fries:

The loaded fries were COVERED in cheese, pulled pork bbq, bacon and sautéed onions. My girlfriend usually despises onion and she happily ate the fries, they were that good.

All in all, I'd gladly come back. I have heard the live music is great and with a cozy atmosphere and good burgers, there is no reason not to check it out If you have the opportunity.

We're not hard core country music fans, but this visit was certainly on our bucket list. It lived up to all our expectations, and then some. The format is great: eight performers, each doing 3 songs, with one intermission. You get a good flavor from lots of different country styles, and it's fast-paced. We're now fans of three of the performers we saw that we'd never heard of before. The venue is clean and has a great feel and decor. 

The only issues we had (hence the lack of a star) was with the seating and ticketing. The seats are church pews, which is fine unless you're sitting next to large people who take up more than their share of the seat allotment. It's best to get an aisle so you only have to worry about that issue on one side.

We ordered our tickets on-line and received an email with a file to print out the tickets. Unfortunately the file was corrupt and I had to call customer service to have another email/file sent to me. The customer service rep even finished my sentence when I said the file was "corrupt" (she said). I asked if this was a common issue, since she wasn't surprised, and she admitted that resolving corrupt file issues was a major part of her day. That was bad enough, but when we got to the Opry house the tickets I had printed out (from the good file) couldn't be scanned and we had to then go to the ticket office to get them replaced (another 10 minutes). All-in-all, the ticketing process was the worst we'd seen in the three years we've been traveling the country. They know they have issues, so they need to take steps to correct them.
Came in to awesome blues band. Fantastic ribs & brisket.  Sides baked beans & potato salad were unbelievable.  A definite  stop when in Nashville.

Incredible beer list-the largest variety I have ever seen in one bar. I arrived in time for happy hour and enjoyed a few $3 pints. Wine and liquor selection on the poor side, but the fantastic selection of beers makes up for it. I found the prices to be very affordable as well. The vegan options, which included a wrap and pita/hummus plate, were excellent. A very nice surprise.

Atmosphere was great-overstuffed couches and chairs with vintage decor and nice lighting. Power outlets near many of the seats. Our server had silvery/purple hair and was very friendly, helpful, and patient. I would definitely come back here the next time I am in Nashville.

Last night was bacon-wrapped jalapeños, stuffed w spiced beef, chorizo and cheese...100% worth the heartburn during the night! Absolutely delicious. Tonight, loaded rocket-tots, again w jalapeño, also bacon, and cheddar jack/goat cheese, green onion, and topped w a fried egg. Oh, my! And of course, a huge choice of drafts and other spirits.
Excellent bar!! Service was great and patient with our sometimes difficult family! Owner even came by to chat and thank us for coming., Good food and good people!! Except for all the Michigan fans

Great music, great southern style food, and very friendly staff! I wasn't expecting to visit a place like this in Nashville, considering country music is king around there. Went in with friends on a whim and was treated to some fantastic blues musicalong with a great beer selection and friendly wait staff. I would highly recommend this place if you're looking for a little something different from the country music scene in downtown Nashville.

First off, the Opry is the legendary roots of country music, so you have to go and bear it. I enjoyed being there, but the show was soo old. I get it's about the legends, but wow, we need to move on. They did have a few younger performers, but it was very slow and boring. It was also extremely annoying that after each group they had a commercial for one of the sponsors that the host read. It got to be ridiculous that people were laughing. That was painful. Charles Easton (sp ?)  played as did a guy called Zach Williams. They were fabulous! But each group only plays 2 songs, so it was fast and a disappointment for $200 for 3 of us. Glad we went once in my life, but don't feel I need to go back.
We always visit the Grand Ole Opry  during every visit. It is the heart of Nashville, reasonable prices and every seat is good!  Concessions are expensive, wear causal clothing and comfortable shoes.

We really enjoyed ourselves at this place. The name is very fitting as we almost passed it up because it was in a back alley.  If you want to escape the crowds of Broadway in Nashville but still have a little action it is well worth the stop here.  Delicious burgers, beers & live music- can't ask for much more!

This bar reminded me of a bar I would find in LA, so don't go here expecting a unique Nashville experience, but it was definitely a cool vibe (being from CA I really enjoyed it but we didn't stay long since we wanted to see Nashville). 

They have great beers on tap, modern feel, a lower level that has a second bar and dance floor.

Food is cheap.  Venue is divey and a great Nashville-esque experience.   Live music was playing when we got there at 8 p.m. on a Saturday.   It was an up and coming bluegrass band that knew how to entertain a crowd.  Will definitely be coming back.

Decided to just pop over on our way out of town to see it. Ended up taking the tour. It was very interesting. I learned a lot and feel the price is fair. You get to take a picture on the stage and can chose to purchase it after the tour ends. The picture was great but the price very unreasonable. It was $25.00! I would have purchased it at a cheaper price. I do recommend the tour. It was great!

On a last minute trip to Nashville, I had to visit the Opry! Since it was only a few days before, our tickets were way up top. There are two giant tv screens showing who is on stage. The seats are not a typical, individual seat. They are church pews. The Opry shares a parking lot with Opry Mills so there is plenty of parking, but still get there early. Also, if you miss out on buying anything from the show that night, check out The Opry Store (connected to the Opry). I passed up on a poster because it was raining so hard, but found the last one at the store the next day!

The place is incredibly beautiful and just knowing you are experiencing such a huge part of country music is amazing!

We took the backstage tour and it was really cool. It was my second time taking this tour and each time it was different and I learned more each time. 

We bought tickets online ahead of time to make sure we got a reservation because they fill up quickly. We forgot to print the actual ticket though so we went to the box office and they gladly printed them for us. 

The tour began promptly at the time slot we reserved and lasted about 45 minutes. The best part was the end getting to go on stage and look out towards the crowd.

They also take your picture on the stage at the center of the iconic wooden stage circle. You can buy them after the toe for $25 which gets you two 4x6 and a 7x9 and access to the digital copy as well. We ended up getting the wrong code for the digital copy so we got someone else's digital version. We called the next day and they were able to give us the right code over the phone which cleared up the mistake pretty quickly. 

The Grand Ol Opry is also walking distance to Gaylord Opry too, so put these two together and it's an awesome day!

Highly recommend the back stage tour.  The tour guide was very friendly and knowledgeable.  A must see in Nashville.  Leave plenty of time because it is next to a huge outlet mall and traffic can be a bear.

This place was so frikkin good, from the music to the food, even our service was impeccable - and our server was juggling us and a huge party, our drinks were never empty. Best ribs I've ever had in my life. Highly recommend!

Let me start by saying that I'm generally not a country fan. I'll occasionally listen to a song and would struggle to count the country singers I know on one hand. 

This place was awesome!

It is so professionally done and a very well oiled machine. The way the artists come out and do their songs one after another is great and the whole thing moves along nicely. The artists are also good names and very talented. 

We only had one day in Nashville and don't feel like we missed anything important because this place is the heart and soul of the city.

Went here on Friday, large to go order in front of us made our food take over 25 minutes. Burgers are always pretty good. Not a place to eat if you have to watch your cholesterol or if you are on a diet.

Waitress Keyonia... this is all I had written on my review back when I started it! I was in Nashville in December and noted her name for a reason... She provided great service and was helpful in working my way through the menu! Service with a smile... harder to come by than one would think.

It's been so long now that I can't remember the name of the dish but it was a creole catfish one that was absolutely delicious. I also enjoyed a Bloody Mary during my time there. I wish I had written this review on the spot because I know I had many great things to say about it! I will certainly be back to BB Kings when I make my way back out to TN. When I do, I'll update my review!

As a fan of country music, I found this venue to be thoroughly entertaining!  I love how they preserved the legacies of the early country stars (i.e. Minnie Pearl, Hank Williams).  The dressing rooms are cool,  the video introduction by Blake Shelton is enlightening,  the staff is super friendly.  I'd definitely visit this place again!

I was excited to try this place while visiting Nashville, but unfortunately I was underwhelmed.  We went on a Wednesday night.  The place was packed.  The server even warned us that kitchen was backed up so our food might take a while.  We arrived at 7:30pm ordered by 7:45pm and got our food at 8:55pm.   When we did finally get the food it was just luke warm as if it had been sitting in the pick up window for quite some time.   While waiting for our meal, we decided to try some of the over 50 beers they have available.  All the ones we wanted to try were sold out! :(  

Our server could have been more attentive at the beginning, but  was so after the place started to clear out later in the evening.

Overall, good beer selection which is why I gave it 3 stars, if they had still had the ones I wanted, I might have given them 4 stars.  They definitely lose points for  having just okay food and slow service. 

Go on non-busy night and hopefully they'll have your favorite beer  in stock and maybe, just maybe you'll have a better experience than we did.

This was the most terrible service I have ever received at a restaurant. We made our reservation 5 hours ahead of time. When we got there, they said that they were sorry but they were not going to have a table available. We waited for 15 minutes and they finally placed us at a table. Our order was taken and two of us ordered catfish. 15 more minutes later, they asked if we wanted something else because the fish was still frozen. The food was ok, but didn't make up for the lack of service and the fact we were an hour late for our event. It is our first time in Nashville and next time we will not be coming back to this restaurant.
Came on from Chicago. Went to this place. The service was really bad one server was really rude will not go back.

It was great. We had some trouble finding it because we thought it was in the arcade. It is just a few steps away. The staff was very helpful and the food was fantastic. The coleslaw is very spicy. The ladies had drinks and loved them.

Came with a group of 32 women in my industry for a party during our convention.  Everyone loved their food and the venue was fantastic too!  They were willing to divide our checks and everything cane our hot and accurate.

Came here for a quieter bite and to watch some football.  Got a couple beers I liked and ordered some 50 cent wings with buffalo sauce.  The wings came and were apparently BBQ but fortunately the bartender noticed right away and offered to get new ones so I was spared the awkwardness of having to decide to say anything or deciding they were good enough and just eating them.  

The second set came out looking about the same and tasting BBQey.  I felt like I may be going crazy but the patron next to me said he has had their wings many times and the ones I got were definitely BBQ.  It's at this point I should have just asked for samples of the BBQ sauce and the buffalo sauce to get the answer.  Apparently they just use BBQ sauce in their buffalo sauce, which is a bit odd, and I'm still not really sure if I got buffalo or BBQ wings or had some sort of brain spasm that prevented me from telling the difference.  Anyway, whatever they were they were well cooked and I'd get them again for sure at that price.  

Place is nice, quieter, had some music going.

I came here for a conference and thought it would be a great time. To my surprise the only thing that occurred during this experience that was positive was the live music. 

Our group of seven all thought that the service was lackluster. More specifically, we experience a significant amount of delays in service from food, water, and the bill. I have also never experienced more "no" responses from a waitress than this. 

A significant disappointment were the sides. If you ask for a full portion it takes about 35 minutes. They claim the macaroni is made to order but we could not tell. Especially with the small cup side we received. 

Dessert? That also took about 35 minutes. The waitress didn't inform us that it would be such a delay but luckily we all were enjoying the music so the time passed faster than watching paint dry. 

Let's not forget that the servers continued to come to our table with the wrong order. This is extremely disappointing when you are starving and have been waiting for 30 or more minutes for your meal.  For some reason it seems that we had an extremely long wait for everything. 

As I said , this experience was lackluster and nothing that I would recommend. The two stars are for the live band. Oh yeah, the drinks were watered down and unfulfilling (especially my Long Island which was basically juice/coke).

Good service and solid fare and family friendly venue. It was nice to be able to go out with the kid in tow and enjoy some great blues music. We had cheese dip, gumbo, collards, and grilled chicken, and mac and cheese.  The gumbo was ok, the collards were good, chicken was good but very spicy, and mac and cheese was very cheesy. We'd come back, not necessarily for the food, but for the music and ambience.

Highly recommend the backstage Opry tour! It was well worth it-especially for lovers of country music. I learned so much about the history of the Opry as well as learned more about country music that I didn't know I didn't know! 
The structure of the tour was awesome - to walk through this beautiful historical building in the same way via the same steps an artist would enter, such an awesome idea! 
It was absolutely incredible to stand in the same spot as so many of my favorite artists and historical country musicians have stood! Seriously LOVED every second of this!

I was in Nashville recently for CMA Fest week. We stopped in BB King's for dinner one night. I had been here once before (and it was awesome) so we thought we would visit again. The food is so delicious, and it's fun to have a live band. Overall the food and drinks are pretty reasonable for being in a touristy area. The staff is super friendly and helpful. I would come back again and recommend it to anyone visiting! Definitely get the nachos with chicken!
Amazing. Awesome. Wish I had more stars to give this. If you love country music, this venue is a must visit!

All three of the flying saucers are great.  They have a German and American food selection and tons of beers on tap.  The location downtown is great being next to union station.  You can also get your parking validated for $5.  Once you drink $200 beers in their UFO club you get a plate on the wall with your name.  With a limit of 3 beers at a time that will probably be a 5 year goal.

When in Nashville the Grand Ole Opry is the venue to see.  Since we were out of towners without any ability to be picky on our travel dates we ended up seeing the performances of people completely unknown to us.  The music was not my taste but I still managed to have a good time with a help of an adult beverage and my friends.  We took the backstage tour and our guide was high on Red Bull and very fun.  They allow you to take a picture on stage during the tour which must be a thrill for true country fans.  I also want to add the vibe is very casual.  I saw one lady wearing heels but most were in pants or shorts.  The Gaylord Hotel has a free shuttle to and from the Grand Ole Opry which is great.

This place offers light, sing along entertainment with few recognizable musicians/songs. The grounds were kept trimmed and offered plenty of paths to choose from on the grounds. I liked the evening ambiance.

Super fun sports bar in Nashville! Great waitresses, cold beer, lots of tvs. Great place to spend a football Saturday! Streetside patio great for people watching. Actually met a famous country music star hanging out upstairs! Fun times in Nashville!

Food was good..Service great..everyone was wonderful and helpful...and the music was to die for.
If I lived  in Nashville. ..i would go here every week.

BB Kings did me well in Memphis, so we stopped by in Nashville and were discouraged by the $5 cover charge just to stop in and eat dinner (it was past 10pm). Meanwhile, the band was very good and the locale and scene offered an alternative to the honky tonks and country style bars that litter the region. A positive: the $5 charge does keep some of the rift raft out and the college kids. 

On the other hand, the food is so-so, not great, nothing to complain about either. It's typical chain food, maybe a little bit better. Our server (who was good) recommended the meatloaf, which I was reluctant to order as I wanted to order the fried catfish (which I ordered a few years back at their location on Beale St in Memphis). The meatloaf didn't taste like homemade meatloaf. The green beans that came with it tasted like they came out of a can. It was edible and even enjoyable while we listened to a great band. 

The kitchen was very slow- took 30 minutes to get our food. My friend ordered the pork sandwich, which he enjoyed the BBQ sauce, but wasn't wowed. Jacks (also downtown), he said, blew it away. 

If you come to BB Kings - it's for the music and atmosphere, not the food.

I am impressed!  Very large bar and restaurant.  Place has a cool rustic look with a large stage.  Looks like it has been here along time.  I'm enjoying these delicious hot wings and a local IPA, Yazoo.   Really impressed at how nice this place is.  Too bad I didn't arrive when blue music is being played live.

We were taken to DawgHouse by Patrick with Joyride. We were having an amazing tour and wanted to stop and have a drink. Patrick took us to his favorite bar.  We loved it.  Very relaxed and laid back. Thank You Key! You took great care of us and made us feel at home.  Your personality kept us entertained and we went back 2 other times!  Again, Thank You Key!!!

Terrible customer service.

Third Man Records has an expensive mail-order subscription series called The Vault, where for $240 a year, you get exclusive "limited" LP & 45 RPM vinyl records, plus a book, DVD or T-shirt, four times a year (For those of you who might not know, Jack White has made a large part of his fortune catering to worldwide vinyl collectors/fanatics.)

I've been a subscriber of The Vault since its beginning in 2009, and have occasionally had to contact customer service when a package arrives damaged. Over the years, Third Man's customer service has been ok resolving the issue and sending replacements, for the most part.

Until recently.

Now, customer service (specifically a passive aggressive asshole named "Cam"), basically tells you to get lost if you question their seemingly sudden reluctance to send replacements. And I quote:

"If you have a differing opinion, I would recommend discontinuing your membership, which I would be more than happy to help you do."

No prob Cam, tell Jack I'll spend my money elsewhere.

This is not your grandpa's Grand Ole Opry House. 
After the flood this place took on a special place in many of our hearts and going, seeing the older acts mixed with the younger up coming (or already arrived) acts make this the best radio show in the U.S. 

This is a must show to see whether it's here at Opry house or downtown at the Ryman.

This is one of those places that you just have to stop in front of and take it in because you can't believe you are actually there.

Unfortunately it was sold out the night we arrived in Nashville so we only got to admired everything on the outside and what we could see on the inside.

This is a must for any music fan, and even if you aren't a country music fan, you'll still appreciate it.

It is on the same property as Opryland and Opry Mills so be prepared to search for parking for a few minutes, then having to walk.

You can get many photo ops in and around it but cannot take video once inside.

Don't forget to stop in the gift shop.

I can't wait to come back and see a show.  Maybe it won't be sold out next time!

my fiance and stepdad hung out here for an hour or 2 while we shopped, eventually we met them here. very entertaining and the people here were talented. seemed to have good price on beers since they drank a few of them. we love the wall in the bathroom people wrote on :) 

stayed here for awhile just listening to people until we went back to hotel to get ready for dinner.

For those of you who like karaoke, this place is a gem.  The KJ's there are respectful and smart, and don't put shitty people up for their third song when others have been waiting.  This place is great, if you don't like fun times go elsewhere.

This review is purely directed at management -- service, beer, food apps were all great.

We used the $13 Groupon for two flights and an app ($28 value) -- in no where on the Groupon did it mention we would be forced to pay a 20% gratuity for a party of 2.  Plus, the 20% was $6 -- do I need to get out a calculator for anyone?  Very shady, very disappointed, and will not be coming back to give my business to a company like this.

Why not mention it at the beginning of the service?  Or, better yet, on the Groupon itself?  Disappointed indeed.

Went to bar on Sunday with a friend for brunch, ordered the mimosa tower (2 bottles of champagne w/oj in large tube with a spout). The bar filled up quickly, but the bartenders and servers had it under control. We both ordered the crab benedict, it was tasty, but big enough for us to share. We also received the food fast. A friend joined us maybe an hour after our food came, and when she ordered, it took a very long time. One of the bartenders told her the kitchen was backed up, and apologized. All three of us work in a bar- we understand what a pain in the ass brunch can be, so our friend sipped some of our mimosa during her wait. (No big deal)
Overall a great experience, great prices, and great service i will be back.

Always a great selection of beers from all over the place. The service is definitely as fast as you can expect. It's always extremely packed so you still will wait a bit for your beer. But it's definitely worth the wait. The pretzel with cheese is probably my favorite pub snack ever. Always a fan, will gladly come back.
Doesn't matter what type of music you are in to, you gotta go the the grand ole Opry.  Entertaining and fun for the whole family.

Enjoyed a nice Sunday lunch with my girlfriend. A good escape from busy broadway. The friendly service will make anyone feel welcomed. The portions are huge. I got the burger and it was extra juicy! They also have excellent Jazz music. This place will get my business in the near future!

I hadn't been to Nashville for about 20 years until a few weeks ago.WOW! what a change.
Trhe city is a wonderful small town with a big city atmosphere.  The Grand Ole Opry was originally located in downtown but, because of flooding about ten years ago, they moved out to the environs in a new larger venue.  It's actually nearer the hotel, which in itself is not to be missed.

It's located in a mall, but separated from the retailers.  The auditorium holds about 4000 and all seats have a good view.  We actually sat in the first row of the balcony and the seats were great.  Didn't particularly like walking down to get to the seats but once there it was fine.

We went on a Friday night when the show is broadcast.  It's interesting to see how they will have an act, stop for a commercial, reset the stage if necessary, and then get on with the show.  The show was about 2 1/2 hours and there wasn't an act that we didn't enjoy and my wife and I are really not Country Music Lovers, at least not before the show.

It's a wonderful experience for all, old, young, family, kids, just go and have a great time.

Service is great and the HotDawgs are very creative and delicious!
Only complaint... Since they have a huge Kentucky fan base, the sound will be on the Kentucky game instead of the home town Predators if they play at the same time. Arrrrrghhh
Oh well, I do understand... It's business, So I always check the schedule.
GO PREDS!

I love the Grand Ole Opry - it is a classic Nashville venue and I love that it's modeled after The Ryman. I've been here a few times for the Opry shows and really enjoy the fact that they have so many performers in their performances, it makes it more enjoyable and fun, in my opinion. The parking lot can be a bit dangerous for pedestrians but luckily, it's massive so there's plenty of parking. Staff is always helpful if you have questions and will tell you all about the history of the Opry. Great place to bring kids too! Love this place!

Meh is right. The wife and I stopped in here for a quick bite and drink before a TPAC show. Everything we'd've rather had was closed down the Arcade Alley, so we opted for this as it was right around the corner, and only about 2 blocks from TPAC.

Seating wasn't a problem, as the place was about 1/2 full (we were there around 6). We grabbed 2 spots at the bar and enjoyed their happy hour specials, which on this particular day (Thursday) were 1/2 price apps and $5 drinks from a designated list of cocktails. We opted for cheesesticks, wings, and chili cheese fries for our snacks and standard margaritas on the rocks for our drinks.

The cheesesticks were fine, nothing either impressive nor offensive. The 'marinara' that came with it was standard salsa, straight out of the bottle. Meh. The chili cheese fries we didn't get to experience, as they came out and told us there was no chili, so we just got regular fries - they even forgot the cheese... The wings were the worst offenders, though. Very tough and cartilage-y, sparse meat, no real flavor or seasoning. I ordered them tossed in buffalo sauce and they most decidedly were not. Couldn't tell what it was, but it wasn't hot wing sauce. Overall, the food was very subpar and we're glad we got it all for 1/2 price.

The margarita I got was made with (admittedly) a well-portioned amount of liquor, but muddled with Orange Juice. Yuck. Some folks may like it, but this was my first marg made with OJ, and it was not a good look.

At the end of the day, we left full, but not overly pleased. The service at the bar was sufficient, however, and quite friendly, so no complaints there. We'll try elsewhere when next we're in the area.

Fantastic burgers and even better fries especially! The diner was not busy at the time we went so we had very fast service. The bar also has a lot of character and is a great place for a late night dinner. The location is a little sketchy but it lives up to it's name as a "back alley diner".

The food was fine, the waiter Derreck is by far the largest jerk I've ever been subjected to in within the confines of servers. He was rude, unpleasant, and absolutely spoiled the entire experience. In addition to this we waited for quite some time for virtually every function that depended on this incompetent and clearly unwilling savant. This all out hostility was completely uncalled for as it occurred without any provocation. The reason I've elected to leave a one star review for this otherwise passable restaurant is because no one in their right mind would employ such a callous, uncaring, and downright aggressive individual.

I am currently working on my 3rd plate with flying saucer in sugar land. When I was in Nashville and learned there was a FS near by, I just had to go.

First thing I noticed when I walked into e place was its pool table area. The FS in Houston and sugar land do not have them, and I was filled with envy. 

I found the computers for the ufo club and printed out 3 beers of which I forget the name.

I elected to sit outside since the weather was pretty nice at night. I immediately realized that they have sofas outside, which is something I'm not use to having FS in Houston. Everything went as expected. Good Oktoberfest and pumpkin beers all around. The waitress did take quite a while to reload my beers so one star for that. 

FYI: The daily perks (3 dollar pints, Tuesday trivia, 3 dollar locals) still apply to all the different FS locations. 

Can't wait to try other flying saucers

We were in Nashville and decided to check it out. 5 dollar cover per person wasn't good with a party of 9 but girl at door worked it out . Pork nachos and hummus is amazing. Service is great . It's a very loud place so nor so good for kids.

Last week, I came in and I immediately loved the vibe! It was super busy but the hostess Adora was very attentive and friendly.  We were seated promptly and our food was great! I waitress was a little overwhelmed but she continued to check on us the entire time! (Wish I remembered her name!)

Definitely worth the $20. I think it was a great tour for the money, they accept AAA and give a couple dollars off each ticket.  Our tour guide was great and now I can say I sang at the the Grand Ole Opry even if it was you are my sunshine. 

Seeing the dressing rooms, the green room, and standing on the original floor was a wonderful experience.

Being an avid country music fan, I knew I had to make a trip to the Opry while visiting Nashville. The venue, though its nothing too fancy, has such a rich history and has been well preserved. 

The show itself was fantastic. Very entertaining and  little down time between acts (something that you dont get very much at concerts nowadays). Even if you aren't fond of a particular musician, they're only on for 15 minutes. That being said, I can see why it is a disappointment to some who come to hear a particular act and only see them for a short time. But the Opry IS a radio show and that's how it works.

Cons: The woman we spoke to on the phone when ordering tickets was quite rude, and I am not one to take these instances too personally. She acted as if we should know the answer to questions we were asking and gave us an attitude when we inquired about standing tickets as opposed to the seats. However, everyone else at the Opry was very welcoming, so I would say that their staff is attentive overall.

The traffic pulling out after the show was a nightmare. We expected it to be busy and congested, but the Opry parking staff that was directing traffic had no idea what they were doing. Crossing pedestrians while cars were moving, allowing cars to stop and wait, not moving taxis along etc. It would have been easier to pull out if the parking staff wasn't confusing everyone.

Overall, neither of these instances were anything close enough to ruining our experience at the Opry. I would recommend it to anyone who loves live music and wants to experience a historical venue. Just a couple of things to note before you go.
Had a great time here. This place was neat and reasonable prices on beer. Good music and friendly environment.

Fantastic spot for the Beer Lover. Cool ambiance and good service. The "chalkboard" had some great and rarer choices. They had most of the well known gold standard American IPAs etc

The food is decent. The menu choices are spot on, just not very tasty.

I was hoping for at least a better pretzel - it was wilted and seemed like something you could buy frozen at the grocery store.

This is a must see, go see a show, it's so true you never know who you may see. To our surprise Bill Murray joined The SteelDrivers and sang along. This iconic venue made me appreciate old and new country.

First let me say the band playing was phenomenal!! 

The food was to die for, I got the Chicken Fried Chicken with the Mac and cheese and the creamed collards on the side. They were to die for!! The chicken was juicy and we'll seasoned, the collards were different from what I'm used to but I have never had them creamed, they had maybe bacon and carrots in them and it was surprisingly delicious!! The Mac and cheese was the only thing I was not really enthused with as it was not baked but it was good for what it was. 

My boyfriend got the chicken and rib combo as it comes. I was able to taste the ribs and they were good, fall off the bone with good flavor to them.

I can't speak for the bar or music, but this is NOT a place to go for lunch. Super slow and terrible food. My "Chicken Philly" was made with lunch meat and burnt to a crisp on one side. My friends had a burnt boca burger (clearly nothing special about their veggie burger) and a dripping club wrap (dripping with what we weren't sure since it was also made with lunch meat). Their only redeeming quality was the fries - those were good (and they were an up-charge). I got half price for my half burnt sandwich.... I guess that's fair. :-/ Just don't go for lunch.

The beer selection is awesome. 
The management oversight is weak. Tonight they ran out of pizza at 7 pm. It is Friday night. 
Last nights silverware was delivers with the previous patrons left overs. 
Did I mention the beer selection was awesome?
Fun place 2 for 1 beer special's included the craft beer selections ...Crowd was a blast ...Nice crowd for a Thursday night, very friendly staff!

We were in search of a bar to watch some football so we scooted inside.  We realized after we sat down at the bar that we didn't know the name of the bar nor did we realize it is a karaoke bar.  The female bartender was kind enough to turn on the game we wanted to watch so that was cool.  We ended up staying and watching some karaoke which was wildly entertaining.  This place I connected to Tequila Cowboy which, if you are looking for a huge bar with a good live music experience, that is the place to be!

I LOVE this place!! My dad and I work in the same office building downtown and this is our usual Friday lunch spot. I usually get the club sandwich with fries and let me tell you...those fries are hands down the best ever. Crispy and seasoned on the outside, and soft on the inside. yum! Will have to go back in the evening to say how the bar is but it is always busy! 5 star service every time and some of the best food downtown...GO!

I LOVE SAUCER. They have SO many beers. And I'm the kind of person who hates beer, but the beertenders and beer goddesses were super attentive and helpful. Also really prompt service. The place has a young vibe after 7PM, and I love it!

May of 2012 I surprised my boyfriend with a trip to Nashville for his birthday because he LOVES him some country music. I swore I would never revert to country but with all those love stories and twang beats I am fan now too. 

Lucky for me when I booked our tickets we had Carrie Underwood, Brad Paisley and Scotty Mcreary singing that evening. The bench seating was perfect and the sound was amazing. I didn't feel like I was in a huge concert venue. 

I went the extra mile and bought the VIP backstage passes. If I can remember I think the cost was around 75-100 each. 

Good Points
-You get backstage and learn about all the country stars who have been there and see the dressing rooms. 
-We had the honor of meeting Carrie Underwood and Scott Mcreary ( 1 minute but I took it) 
-You get to go onstage during the opening of the music and see what the stars see. 
-They only sell each concert 10 VIP tickets so it's more personable and not overcrowded. 

Bad Points
-No CAMERAS ALLOWED in the dressing room hang out area. So when I met Carrie underwood ( Yes we snuck away from the group and walked to where Carrie was and got a photo w/ her) Needless to say we got yelled at by our tour guide NOT for sneaking away but for using our camera. My issue with that is I just payed you almost 200 dollars to walk back stage for 45 minutes and you aren't going to let me take a picture with an awesome country singer who was happy to take the photo w/ us? Crazy.. That's the only reason why I didn't add on the final 5 star rating. 

-We could not find the tour guide!!! We went to check in at the ticket booth and NOONE knew where to send us. Finally after 15 minutes ( which meant our tour ended in 30 min) we walked to the gift shop and had to have a nice guy call on the walkie talkie to see where the tour people were. 

Other than that if you love country you MUST visit this place. It's a great memory we will keep forever. You can tell for every country singer on that stage it is a true honor to them to be invited and a dream come true.

We needed lunch so we found this on yelp. It was a little hard to find as it is down an alley. Lunch was so so. I have a shell fish allergy seems the kitchen that day couldn't promise no contamination with fries etc. so I had the bean sausage soup. Crackers only no crusty bread for patrons. Soup was salty. My son had a hamburger and fries. I had sweet tea that was tasty. So so food. The waitress looked like she had been there a long time slightly unstable but nice enough. Next time I will try another place. I think local office workers go there for lunch.

We were staying at a near by hotel and decided to check out the Flying Saucer for our first official meal in Nashville on a Sunday afternoon. I love the relaxing environment and the extensive list of beer options. My friend and I shared an ordered of Loaded Rocket-Tots as well as Prosciutto and Arugula 12" pie. The tots were crazy delicious, it is a must try. The pizza were delicious as well and is enough for the both of us. 

This place is such a great find, we were glad we came here for food and beer.
I just ordered BB Kings for the first time today and oh my god this is such a good burger. I got it to go and the service was friendly and quick! Thanks guys :)

My wife and I have eaten here twice. Both times our food was amazingly delicious. I've read a few of the negative reviews and I can't fathom how someone could have a bad meal here. I had the bbq beef brisket melt. I eat every single bite. The brisket was tender and juicy. I toppled it off with some sweet tea...mmm mmm good. I'm not normally a fan eating at chain rerestaurants, but I'm happy I made an exception with BB Kings. Delicious food and extremely talented people playing music live. That combination is worth it.
Good food. Not my favorite crowd after hours.

I have only been to Anthem to attend Yelp events but both times I have been I have enjoyed myself immensely.  The staff are incredible.  The drinks and unique and tasty and reasonably priced.  The bar bites are always yummy.  They have an excellent happy hour.  And this is one of the rare clubs in Nashville, so as the night gets on it gets rather dancey in here.  There's plenty of parking and lots of space to explore with friends.  I need to come here on a random weekend night to really experience this place but what I have seen so far has been really awesome and different for the Nashville landscape.

My husband and I were in Nashville for a business trip, so we decided to try this place out. When we got there, there was a guy on stage playing guitar & singing. We ordered the Louisiana Crawfish Poppers as an appetizer, they are amazing! As we were waiting on our food, the guy with the guitar finished & the Stacy Mitchart Band set up. They are awesome. I would suggest you go see them wherever they are playing. Our food then arrived, I got the Born on the Bayou Shrimp and Grits and my husband got the Southern Fried Platter Combo. Both of us really enjoyed our meal. For dessert we got the Banana Bread Pudding, oh Lawd it's like heaven in your mouth!! Overall, I would highly recommend you give them a try.

Honestly-if you're coming to Nashville with any sort of group-so yourself a favor and rent one of these buses. Be a local Nashville Celebrity for a second. Don't short yourself thinking you don't like singing 90's out of an open air bus in the afternoon. You need it. You want it. Just do it.

Best ribs I love the location in Memphis tn
The one in Nashville charges to sit and eat 
The Memphis crowd is #hip

In the mood for some fish and chips....was not disappointed, but had slightly higher hopes. The portion size was perfect. The batter dipped fish good, save for the squirt of grease that popped up with my first knife slice. Not drained well enough - served too quickly? Nonetheless, flavor and texture were great. Throw away the taste sauce and just top 'em with Malt Vinegar. Fries fine, but also just a bit soft, not crisp. 

The service was absolutely perfect....swift, attentive, and polite. 

Working backwards from the entree to the appetizer...hummm? The stuffed mushrooms were a bit different form many places inasmuch as these were stuffed with creams cheese & herbs (delicately flavored)...but here comes the twist...heavily battered and deep fried, served with horseradish sauce. Good or bad? Actually I enjoyed them quite a bit...they were less greasy than the fish. But ultimately reminded me of carnival food. (Not a dig...just my observation.)

All in all a nice late evening dinner after a concert at the Schermerhorn.

Oh, the Guiness...smooth, mellow, delish!

As you can see the food looks delicious, IT WAS! We are from NC, so we needed something more our style to attend! The wait was about 45-50 min on a Saturday (but when we walked back there were plenty of seats before called), once we sat down though the BAND was ON IT! Y'all we had to get a box for our food because we could barely eat since we couldn't stop singing and dancing! I'm only giving 4 stars because of the wait.

Went here for the open mic and sadly found out when we got there that it stopped over a year ago :(
The scotch egg appetiser was delicious! I had the Carathors salad which was also delicious! Portion was huge so I ended up taking a third home. The waitress who served us was lovely and couldn't have been more helpful, despite only working out on the floor for a week she clearly knew her stuff.
Would definitely come back here again!

Very disappointed with my visit here. Started off having a good time, cheap beers, $1 jellos shots, and karaoke. Wasn't too crowded but was having fun and talked to the people that were there. Then I found a clearly intoxicated girl literally laying on the bathroom floor.

Another girl told the bar tender to get some help and they immediately kept telling me to get her out of there and that she couldn't be caught in there.
1 I didn't even know the girl but was the one carrying her out of the bar and
2 Why would you continue to serve someone till that point? Especially if she looked so young. 

Sorry, any time I go out to have fun and end up having to take care of a stranger who was clearly over served because it seems as if they just would have left her out there on her own AND have to pay for my $20 bar tab after doing so, is not a bar I would recommend or visit again.

SO GOOD! I love the authentic bbq & sweet tea at all of these little "hole-in-the-wall" places! It really is in the back alley of the shops along the mall so pay attention you might miss it, haha we did the first time we walked right by it! Had the sweet tea and some delicious burger with bbq sauce and onion straws... You could tell the burger patties were made by hand and all the food & sides were delicious!
Awesome friendly and helpful staff! Got a mold-a-Rama and some awesome gifts for friends.

The food here is below average. Salad out of a bag I think with bottled salad dressing. Chicken fingers and fries dry as a bone. Yuck! If you're interested in beer only this is your place. But eat elsewhere.
Overall the restaurant was great from the moment we walked in the door. If you you enjoy a live band  and the blues this is the place to be.  I would like to thank you for having us Nashville!

Vast beer selection, but the poor service doesn't make up for what this restaurant/pub offers on the beer menu. We were in a group of seven, and everyone ordered the equivalent of deli sandwiches. The food took well over an hour to come out, and the entire order still didn't come out together. The worst part was that our server NEVER came by to check on us or offer an apology for the ridiculous delay. The quality of the food was terrible as well, but that was to be expected.

Stuffed burgers, craft beers, dog-friendly patio, What else do you need? A few things I can recommend. Better parking, locally sourced food items, more loyalty from a couple of employees. I have been really surprised that the restaurants on both sides have been packed but this place isn't. From what I gather it is probably from the days of yore when they were a not so successful tapas restaurant with a very similar name.

First I had the Hells Kitchen burger. First word that comes to mind is "DAMN!" It was just the right ratio of spicy to taste, lots of cheese and cooked perfectly. Topped off with the pretzel bun I would call it my best burger yet in Nashville.

Craft beer selection was good but not great. Selections from Czann's & Brooklyn brewery on draft made me happy. Would loved to have seen some local craft taps. 

The patio has been my go to spot due to being with friends that have dogs. They have dog bowls that they bring out with water for the four legged friends. 

Parking in this area won't get any better so be prepared to walk a ways. Although the burger was pretty fantastic the sides were just ok. As you will see from any of my reviews I love fresh fries. When you are taking the extra step to do truffle, garlic parmesan, and sweet potato fries I don't see why you wouldn't take the other half step to go fresh with these items. Fresh and local is always better. I would also love to try their burgers with locally sourced grass fed beef. 

Finally the staff... Patio staff has been EXCELLENT. They do have a bartender there though that was antagonizing and making fun of a musician that was playing the other night. As far as I'm concerned this is disrespectful to your boss who brought them in, to them as a customer, and any fans that the performer may have brought in. All of which are responsible for your paycheck. If you disagree you should never show it in front of customers. I also heard that this gentleman is rude to customers and couldn't believe it with how well I had been treated at this establishment.

To wrap this review up. Check this place out, sit on the patio and bring  your dog. You will make new friends and have a relaxing time.

Music is great and is the only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 3. The BBQ sliders tasted good, but they were lukewarm. The fries were bland and stale towards bottom of the pile. The service was ok. Overall, it's a great experience, but I would skip coming here for dinner. Just enjoy the music with a beer.
This place is so over rated! Don't waste your money. The show is okay. The worst part is you have to listen to a live man do advertisements the entire show

Nashville needs a place like this, but Anthem does not hit the mark.  First of all, they opened the doors one hour after the advertised time.  We bought VIP tickets and were supposed to get VIP bathrooms, bar, and private viewing area.  They were not policing for non-VIPers in the area, so in addition to over-selling, there were people in the VIP area that didn't have VIP tickets.  It took over 20 minutes to get a drink at the bar, and worst of all, there was ONE bathroom in the entire area, for men and women.  So, after standing in line for 20 minutes for a drink, you could stand in line for another 20 minutes to use the bathroom.  Don't waste your money.

After searching for a restaurant that offered reservations, we decided to take our group to Back Alley Diner.
We had a difficult time finding it, but once we did I was so glad this is the place we picked.

For starters, there was a table all ready for us. The band playing, Steel Blossoms, were so great! All 11 of us are now following them on FB and one girl bought a CD. Great entertainment choice.

Our server Sarah was AWESOME!! She was friendly and efficient. At no point were we looking around or waiting on her. Table was cleared quickly, drinks refilled promptly. She took a group photo for us, which I'm sure is the biggest Pain in the @#$ for a server. She was so nice and eventhough she was speedy, she never made us feel rushed.

The menu was great and offered something for everyone. We had several drinks and appetizers and all were perfect. I went simple and just had chicken fingers with a salad, but it was perfect. Everyone left there very happy and well fed. 
I was also really happy with the price, it was super affordable.

One of the better clubs that I've been to in a while.  They have a happy hour on Saturdays until 7pm and don't charge a cover before 7pm.  They have two stages, four bars, and closed circuit TVs throughout.  The menu offers a wide range of southern style food, including ribs, white cheddar mac n cheese, and banana bread pudding.  Plus, the live entertainment not only entertains, but encourages dancing and crowd participation.  This spacious, smoke-free club offers a refreshing change from crowded, smelly bars typically found in downtown Nashville.
This a hidden gem. Great food and drinks for a great price. You can tell nothing is frozen. We bring everyone we know in here. The service is always great, no matter what the sign says ;)

Very rude bar tender. Scolded us for ask for a coke after we got a glass of wine.  He said he could of waited on another person in that time frame. Argued with the people next to us because they wanted to put the bar bill on there table of 8 which they couldn't accommodate. 
Very bad management 
One bartender for 50 plus people. The. Lost a lot of money on drinks that night.
Great pretzels and great beer! The rocket tots are also really tasty. I was particularly impressed by their beer selection; they had New Holland Dragon's Milk!

Decided to check out this place as a continuation of my brother and I's search for the best hamburger in Nashville. This is a really cool area near Vanderbilt (I had never been over here before) and most of the businesses are outfitted in what look like regular houses. I thought that was a pretty neat idea. There's lots of outdoor seating but we went on the nicest Saturday in February so we were forced to sit inside.

The inside of the place is pretty small, only maybe 15ish tables (two are pretty large). All of the tables are painted with different things. Ours was one of the larger ones that was painted as a record, but we saw one nearby that had a painted version of Kenny Rogers' face (I thought it was funny). Service was decent too, the guy we had (didn't get his name) was super nice and checked back multiple times throughout the meal.

I had the sliders, which were topped with bourbon onions, dijon mustard, and cheddar cheese on little pretzel buns. There was a little bit too much mustard for my liking, so that flavor kind of overpowered everything else and the bourbon onions should've had more... bourbon? Didn't really taste that. I had the side of truffle fries and the flavor in those was SO damn good. Very earthy and tasty, would definitely have those again in a hot second.

My brother had the Macho Burger (stuffed with buffalo chicken and blue cheese) which he thought had a pretty good zing to it. My boyfriend had the Belcourt Black Eye (stuffed with bacon and blue cheese) and also had good things to say. They had regular fries and coleslaw, respectively, and thought the sides were just decent. Overall, everything was pretty top notch.

This is a great place located in a really cute area. If you're going here, be prepared to walk because parking is the WORST. We had to walk probably 4-5 blocks to get there. Although, it's right by a park and it was the nicest day in a while so it seemed like everyone was out that day. There's metered parking (although all of them seemed to be expired... wasn't sure about that) along the street and free street parking if you walk. Overall, I really enjoyed my experience here and wouldn't hesitate to go back to try some of their other stuff!

Flying Saucer is the best bar in Nashville.  They have so many beers!  Every time I go, I try something new and exotic.  If you are into beer, this is a must visit in Nashville.

Living in Franklin, we have to make special trips to come down to FS.  Usually, it's before a Predators game or concert.  The food is pretty good.  It's a German heavy menu and you'll do well to stick the brats and kielbasa.  Both are really good.  Also, the soft pretzel appetizer is fantastic!

I started on their UFO club a few years ago.  You get a card and they have a system that keeps track of the beers that you drink.  Once you hit 200, then you get a plate on the wall of the restaurant.  I'm closing in on 100, but it will take me a while to complete the task.  Some folks have gone through the program nearly a dozen times.  Crazy.  

I love visiting this place for the variety of beers and the unique menu.  If you are doing something special in Nashville, park and eat here.  Then leave your car and go to your show or game.  The beer selection is awesome and the waitstaff is very helpful and friendly.

This is a fun place if you like to sing Karoke or just watch other people sing.  They a stage thats elevated so you can see the person singing no matter where you are in the club,  Plenty of places to sit and have a drink

Such a great bar in midtown! It was an upscale feeling, but bartenders and staff very down to earth. Being a transplant from NYC, this bar reminded me of a typical manhattan bar. The cocktails are great, made with real ingredients not mixes and sugar.  It was a nice change of pace from other bars in Nashville.

Really like the concept of Flying Saucer.  Join the UFO Club, get a swipe card that keeps track of your beer purchases.  Kind of a rewards program (max of three credited per 24 hour period), try 200 different beers and you get your very own plate posted up on the wall or ceiling.  Excellent selection of beers, probably 40+ on tap - all great choices.  We also had a pizza which was very tasty.  Great service!  Will have to keep going to Flying Saucers - wish they had one in Charleston SC!

Wow and Wow again. This place is a institution and should if not already on some sort of heritage list. 
Got to go there on the 9th to see the Oak Ridge Boys and we were super impressed with the Grand Ole Opry. Organization, gift shop , staff, cleanliness, sound, etc etc etc. A true 5 stars

Can't believe some of the cry babies on this website, F.....g Democrats.

Bar food. Quirky, but kind servers. I ordered soup and it wasn't terribly good, but they didn't even bother with bringing it to room temperature. The hula hoops on the wall were fun and my sister in law enjoyed the not-terribly-over-priced beer.

I stopped in to try the buffalo wings while passing thru Nashville. They are definitely above average. I found them to be are very good--crispy and non-breaded--and come with celery sticks and dip. The ambiance is that of old tavern but without the smokey stench. I recommend the B.A.D. For the price, I give it 5 Stars.
Cheap, delicious food. Service was very good. Only real complaint was the A/C should have been a little colder, kinda stuffy in there.
