Waited an hour past the start of the show for the doors to even open. Terrible time management and efficiency given there was no one around to manage the people. Everyone was annoyed by the time the doors opened. Not worth it.

There are several places in Nashville that are great at brunch. Music City Tippler is not one of them. The menu is interesting enough, but falls short on the options. Also lacking is portion size and execution. I've had better chicken caesar salads from the drive-thru. The salad was tiny, severely underdressed, and contained only about two ounces of pulled chicken. The skillet potatoes were, oddly, both overly greasy and  tough. The service was very lackluster. Several items were forgotten and others were unavailable. Our waitress wasn't very friendly and could not trouble herself to ask our party of seven how we would like the check. Basically, the place was great on the ambiance and pretty bad at everything else. Perhaps this is a great spot for a cocktail, but don't waste your time or money on their brunch.

I do respect the niche that this place is trying to fill in Vanderbilt campus vicinity. That being said, the layout of the restaurant is really cluttered, and I have trouble really being able to relax in here. The burgers are definitely decent; however, I think they can stand to knock them all down by about $2. 

To their credit, they manage to find some hokie-but-fun musical talent to play in the evenings, and the beer offerings aren't bad. However, since you're the kind of person who takes time to read Yelp reviews, you can do better.
Delicious food. Great beer choices. Pretzels were awesome. Mustard is super spicy but worth it!!

Absolutely loved being here! It was everything we had hoped and more.  We were fortunate to see Dierks Bentley, Kacey Musgraves, Rick Skaggs, Daily & Vincent, Terri Clark and more. It was a great night of music at a great venue.

Seating was great, can't imagine a bad seat in the place.

Liked that cabs were lines up ready and waiting after the show made it easy to jump I'm and make it back to our hotel room.
First time here in a few years. It's still as good as I remember. I had the Saucer Dipster sandwich and it was great!

Went there at lunch time: they were closed.   Large sign on the door gave a list of rules about a mile long...I thought  it was a joke...they were serious.  We now refer to the place as a "Presbyterian Bar."
Probably a good thing they were closed.
Steak isn't supposed to taste like onions, but the ones here do. Probably the loudest restaurant I've been to in Nashville.
Wonderful experience. Performance was the best. Seating was nice. Staff friendly. Overall a great entertainment choice, I would recommend to anyone coming to the area.

i was recently in Nashville for business and went to BB's for a light bite and to listen to tunes. what a change from the dives on Broadway. The beer was cold and the music hot! The BB King All Stars are absolutely incredible and it was nice to watch without having beer spilled on you or being pushed around. Great time!
Kinda divey but full of locals and no.loud music. Great beer and  burger. In fact, it's mostly a beer, burger, barfood joint that appears to be more of a bar.
Great place for the craft beer enthusiast!  Plenty of taps and very large place.  Take your time and select wisely!
It's truly a hole-in-the-wall kind of place, but they've made it their draw! Drinks are unique and diverse. Food is tasty and affordable. I'll definitely be going again!

Visited Nashville mid-Summer to do the tourist thing and decided to go to dinner downtown at BB King's Blues Club. Reservations made the day before (thru Open Table) somehow got lost (the place was packed!) but the hostess seated my date and I soon after arrival anyway. A funky table on the side was upgraded to a table front and center of the band's stage along with a great waitress (I don't remember her name but she had multiple cool bracelet's on each arm!). 

Had a coupon from hotel for a free appetizer but basically you get $10 off of your meal. I ordered a cup of gumbo ya ya but a bowl came out instead... oh well, it was enough for two people so it worked out because it was free and delicious! The mixed drinks were "okay"... seemed as though they were a little watered down with the ice. The two bands were great they played songs (I never heard before to several that I had including a great Prince rendition) which everyone seemed to enjoy, several couples (including us) were on the large dance floor and the waiters/ waitresses that navigated around the dancers with food/drinks along with a few lone wolves provided the additional entertainment. 

The restaurant's location was great (2nd St) and it happened to be a few short blocks from the hotel-provided shuttle pick-up spot (5th St) so parking was not an issue. Would visit again, try some different drinks and would definitely start off with the gumbo ya ya!

This place is the worst karaoke bar I have ever been to in my 27 years on this earth. The shots are a ripoff. They barely contain alcohol, if any at all.   Save yourself some anguish and skip this hot mess.

Food was good, service was awesome until it came to figuring out the bill. Then it literally took like 20+ minutes to get the bills and to get them correctly.  I'm sure it frustrated the waiter too but it definitely put a damper on whatever else was good.
Do not go in this bar they will take your money and beat you up and there is nothing you can do cause when the cops come they will lie about it.
I've never been treated better at any club in town. The amenities, the shows and the decor are second to none when it comes to dance clubs.

We recently went to Nashville for the first time for the Final Four championship.
Just had to go to the Grand Ole Opry. We went on Friday night and really enjoyed every minute of it. The show consisted of  the old and the new,  performers and music. A great variety. The acoustics were great and don't think there was a bad seat in the house. We got our moneys worth for sure. Every employee we encountered couldn't have been nicer. They were happy that we were there and we certainly felt welcome.

I'm starting to realize that most of the bars in Nashville are slowly transitioning into a chill rooftop bar experience. I don't mind it because I prefer that over people bumping and grinding on each other. My friends and I came here on a Saturday night so of course we knew Broadway was going to be busy.

The bar consists of three floors which seems like the higher up you go, the more laid back it is. We managed to find a table and we got to hangout for a while without people constantly bumping into each other. There was live music playing which is a common thing in Nashville. The person performing was very entertaining and talked to the crowd which was a plus. 

The only downside is the drink prices. I know every bar is going to jack up the prices but I thought 6 dollars for a Coors light was a bit steep. At the time, I didn't care because I already had a strong buzz. Looking back now, if I was 100% sober, I probably would have passed up the drinks. 

I'm loving how Broadway is changing their bars up and Redneck Riviera is no exception. It's a nice place to go to if you're looking for a location where you and your friends can casually have a cold one.

I came to Nashville for a girl weekend for my birthday. We happened to stop by this restaurant. The brisket was very good and our waitress Alexandria was awesome. She was very informative, caring, helpful and I would hire her in a minute. The band was terrific. I highly recommend this place if you come to Nashville

Small little "hole in the wall" that really stands out for grabbing a bite to eat. The burgers are amazing. So are their fresh made potato chips. The service was really good and friendly and prices were well within the norm.  The atmosphere definitely has a "dive" feel but totally worth it.

I need to come here again once I have decided what song I can sing and not sound awful or make a fool out of myself. It's cray how talented people in Nashville are. I need to up my karaoke game for sure.

A place where you can just sit an enjoy the music, without the usual hustle and bustle of your typical Nashville bar. The music was fantastic. Wait staff was friendly and courteous. Drinks were strong, tasty and most came in souvenir glasses. We didn't eat a full meal, but the appetizers were great!

Whilst visiting Nashville, it;s a must to stop by the Opry. Love and Theft and Lady Antebellum were both performing while I was there. 

It's an awesome place to go and a must for any country music fan. 

Only thing though, dont park at Opryland if you're just going to the Opry. That was my big mistake. I walked forever and had to paying for parking to a place I just waled through was not worth it. 

Other than that, it was a blast.

What a great place to unwind and have a drink in the front of this establishment or dance the night away in the back. This is a classier establishment from the honkeytonk life of broadway. This is a great low key spot where tons of locals go to mingle.

Trouble. This is trouble wrapped in a beautiful cocktail glass. 

The bartenders at Tippler were at the bartender bash event a couple weeks ago and after loving their cocktails and talking to the extremely friendly bartenders, I just had to come back to try out the full experience. 

It did not disappoint. Can we PLEASE talk about how good the vodka mule is (my favorite part is that it is served in a copper cup as it should be). I could seriously drink a vat of those things. I mean wow. Some other favorites; "I'm not bitter" and the "slow and low" was really tasty if you enjoy whiskey (they dabbled with infusions!). 

The first night I was here there was a bachelorette party dressed up in flapper attire and seriously fit perfectly in the tippler! I felt a bit out of place in my blue jeans simply because the space is SO lovely and most of the bar is old and beautiful. We spoke with the owner a bit and he was very friendly and you can tell he really cares about this business! 

The tippler was so great I came back the next night on Friday to experience it again and it was packed! 
If they keep this up I see this being a great success in Nashville. I know I will be back for that sweet sweet vodka mule.

The food was okay, I had the ribs , they were just okay. 

The cornbread was good.  The drinks were on the weak side .

very friendly and helpful service 
i felt like alice in wonderland
jack has created a beautiful place i enjoyed every minute i was there

Arrived at about 11/11:30. The band was still going and in full effect. I had the pleasure of hearing the amazing Sherry Hawk. She had a great voice and awesome stage presence. 

The food was just so so. Only had the late night menu available so I won't pass too much judgment but the drinks were kind of weak as well.  However, I had an awesome server by the name of Kameron that had great energy and was very attentive. 

All-in-all good place to bring someone from out of town if they want to get a taste of Nashville.

Are you a fan of blues music? Are you a fan of good BBQ? Are you a fan of alcoholic beverages? Then BB King's Blues Club is a perfect location for YOU! Service, excellent. Food, tasty but not anything special. Drinks, made RIGHT. Music..... hands down the BEST PART. We went on a random Wednesday night and got to see the legend, T.C.Coleman! Couldn't have been more excited to see this amazing band preform. I was on the edge of my seat during their opening set where every instrument got their own solo (even the bass guitar!). The worst part was the long intermissions the artists took, but it's hard to complain when they are playing from 7pm to 12am! We arrived for dinner around 5pm and did not have to pay cover since we ate there. Awesome experience if you're a lover of good music! Long live the king o' blues.

The beer selection and ambience is pretty nice. The food was average but as another reviewer said about the tots appetizer, the egg totally turned me off. I can do a runny yolk but not runny whites. Be sure if you order this dish to specify the egg to be cooked more thorough-- I believe it would taste better and look more appealing! Overall, I will come back!
This is a great place to drop in for a burger and a beer. Try the Yazoo beer, and the Juicy Lucy burger. James is the coolest. Friendly place, great music in the evenings!

If you like beer this is the place for you.  Their selection is amazing.  We spent most of our time looking at all of the plates on the ceiling which are awarded to people who drink 200 or moor beers at their various locations.  The food was decent.  We did their loaded tater tots for an app and then each had a sandwich after that.  The staff was friendly and very knowledgable about the beer selection.

Also, we did not partake but there is an entire section of couches, love seats, and picnic benches with wait staff service.  

Its just outside of the downtown area and walking distance from the Music City Center so its a great location if you're there for a conference.  Go.. drink.. enjoy.

Oh Printer's Alley. You are home to those fantastic gritty, late night Nashville adventures and I love you for it. Ms. Kelli's is never my first stop.... I always somehow end up here and that's OK with me. 

Who doesn't love a musty basement smell, cheap jell-o shots, karaoke, and flashing lights? They have a dance floor in front of the stage and drink prices aren't bad. It's not my favorite place to karaoke, but it does the trick in a bind. 

However, the last time I went the karaoke guy forced us to get this really annoying app to sign up for karaoke (not sure what happened to just putting your name and song on a piece of paper). Not gonna lie, it was difficult to set up after a few drinks in, and our group gave up after a while. Why you gotta do that to us Ms. Kelli?? Otherwise, it's a fun time and not bad for what it is!

This was an amazing experience. First time at GOPH and I was able to see one of my all time favorite country groups, Rascal Flatts.  Hunter Hayes and Shaw Brothers were there too. 
Had a wonderful time with my friend.....great night!!
The name is spot on "Back Ally"  hard to spot.  Find it. Great food. Great prices.  Open mic was great. Katlyn, our server that evening was funny and super helpful.  The ace is a true find for sure.

This little diner is tucked away in, you guessed it, an alley on the block between 4th and 5th and Union and Church. You might notice the bold sign out front that just says "B.A.D", and you'll be clued in to the sense of humor of the joint. You'll also probably hear live music before you hit the door if you arrive on a Tuesday or Thursday. There is trivia on Wednesday as well. 

Happy hour is from 4-7 and they have great deals on fun house martinis and margaritas. The menu is creative and expansive, offering way more than typical bar food. I started with the hummus and pita chip plate, which also comes with cucumbers, celery, jalapenos, and olives. My friends got the cheese sticks and devoured them in no time. Next time I want to try the black bean or turkey burgers, but they have plenty of beefy choices if that's your thing. 

The atmosphere is light and lively, with tall ceilings and an upper level in the back. Take your pick from booth, table, or bar and get into something B.A.D!

Fucking awesome. Great collection of records and random stuff to look at. The girls that were working were really sweet and gave my daughter a free puzzle. We bought records & a toddler hoodie. We got the chance to meet Jack the day before at his Walk of Fame thing and we love him and this store and Nashville. You must go here - it's worth the stop.
Try the grilled cheese burger it was great and very filling. Another cool place to go downtown close to printers alley.
BB King god rest his soul would be EMBARRASSED to have his name on this place. Let's just leave it at that.

Came here for dinner and to listen to some blues music. Not disappointed.
I tried the Yazoo Creole Catfish. My sister had the BBQ Chicken breast while my boyfriend had the ribs. 
Everyones dish came out good and there were no complaints. I liked the catfish. It tasted fresh.

The live music was really good. The blue's music was a nice change from the country music in Nashville.

Cool little place to get good laughs and a few drinks.  Plan to have dinner somewhere else no food served here.  The DJ is cool and the karaoke list is really good almost all your favorites.  A little dance floor is in the front and adds to your fun.  Can get a little snug because of the people and little room for dancing.  Overall a good place to have a great time!

Came here on a Friday afternoon and it was pretty dead... I don't know why I ordered the lettuce wraps and not BBQ, but I did. The service was wonderful and everyone was so kind and helpful, but the food wasn't super memorable for me. Hot, good, but not life changing. I was pretty hungry - even after eating - because the portion size was not too big. I would love to try the BBQ!

I will be the first to admit that by no means am I a country music fan, however I couldn't turn down the opportunity to visit one of the oldest and most famous live radio shows in the nation. While on a trip to Nashville I had the opportunity to visit the Grand Ole Opry and watch a live radio show and I have to admit that I was quite pleased. Now with that being said I had tickets before I knew who was playing, however it ended up being Vince Gill and Ray Stevens.

Parking is the only real downside with this facility as it shares a lot with the neighboring mall, and my only advice is arrive early, very early. Otherwise you will be parking far away from the venue. Once inside there are a variety of drink stands, and yes you can take your drinks into the venue. Seating inside is good, and I doubt there is a bad seat in the house, however you will be sitting on uncomfortable benches that look like they are right out of a church.  Overall it was a great evening in this iconic venue, and I would gladly return again for another show.

Good bar. Super selection of offerings. Only down side is they are often out of stock on your first couple of selections but their is always another choice ready. Fun atmosphere and just a good place to kick back with friends.

A friend told me I needed to go to Jack White's record shop, but really, it's very underwhelming. Don't get me wrong, there's some cool stuff to look at, but it's tiny and not worth going out of your way for (unless you really like Jack White).

There's a lot of White Stripes/Jack White merch, as well as other records (just one rack of them though).

There's a cool booth that you can go into and record a song.

Woman at the counter was nice.

My husband looked this diner/pub up online so we thought we would give it a try. We weren't greeted when we came in which is ok. We asked a server if we could sit in an open booth and he said sit anywhere you want. We sat there for a while looking at the drink menu and noticed a lady server come by and ask the people in front of us if everything was ok and then she walked right past us without even saying hello to check on the people behind us. My husband was ready to leave at that point, but I wanted to give them a little more time. The servers seemed more interested in talking to each other than saying hello to us. They were only moderately busy. We just got up and walked out and no one seemed to care. B.A.D. lives up to its name. We won't be going back!

I was so excited to stumble across that little bar. I figured it could be a great hole-in-wall with great live music and little known great bar food. I'll never know. I walked in and got a great earthy, dingy vibe. I sat down at a two top as there only an older couple, two guys at the bar, another man doing paperwork at the bar, and what looked like a guitar player and (after misreading the woman as s waitress) a singer. Well, after 10 minutes of nobody  acknowledging me I went to the bar and waited another minute ... hmmm. Okay finally I ordered an appetizer out, another app, out again. And so was I, out the door.

The Grand Ole Opry is a staple of Nashville and truly an impressive theater.  I, for one, am not a huge fan of country music, but this trip to Nashville left me with nothing but the utmost respect for these musicians trying to make it in Music City.  Everyone that performed was insanely talented, and it was fun to know that it was part of a live radio broadcast.

I am a sucker for a good deal, and Flying Saucer has a lot.  First, Monday night is pint night, and almost every pint is $3.  Well, every pint that is not an IPA or a super fancy craft beer.  But, the beers I like (read fruity or wheat) were all on sale, so I was all in.  They carry so many choices on draft, it's impossible to think that everyone could not find a few favorites.  The plates on the ceiling suggested they have many patrons who have tried a lot, as apparently you need to try 200 to get a plate.

The true winner though is the pizza.  We ordered the pizza with bacon, prosciutto, and pepperoni.  (Yes, we can be a bit gross, but it was vacation!).  It was SO good.  I love the fact they use mozzarella cheese, as it's my favorite melty cheese.  The meat was piled so high you could barely even see the cheese or crust.  It was so good, and one with all that meat was definitely enough to fill us both up.

Bartenders were hit or miss during our couple visits - some are super friendly, some seem like they'd rather not be bothered.  But, the beer and pizza made it all worth it.  And, to learn they are a chain!  Now, crossing my fingers Flying Saucer comes up North, and we can have a go at getting a plate on the ceiling.
Food was great, nice atmosphere as well but it was extremely busy so service was slow.

This was probably my favorite place in Downtown Nashville. Although at first the bar was sort of dead, which made it easier to sign up to do some karaoke, once if got packed later in the night, it was just a so much fun. All the song choices (didn't matter if the singers were good or bad, although it is Nashville, so more good than bad ones at least from my karaoke bar experiences). The energy and crowd that night made it awesome. Hands down a place I would be more than happy to go to again and recommend if you're not looking for a huge sweaty crowd, but rather a nice place to hang out and not worry about squeezing through strangers just to go sit or get a drink.

The ONLY reason I'm giving this place any stars is because the Music and the food tasted good. But the service was atrocious!

We were in town for the CMA Music fest last weekend, so I understand it is busy. We didn't have a problem when they split up our party of 10 into 6 and 4 so we could be seated quicker. However, we waited about 10 min before anyone even came to our table to greet us. Finally our server Ashley, came over.  After we all placed drink orders, and she carded us... she came back almost 30 min later with 1 drink! ONE. She said that the bar was out of mint so they couldn't make our mojitos. What about all the other drinks we ordered? Well, she told us she completely forgot we ordered them and asked us again what we wanted. (This was the first time we spoke to the manager) She finally came back with the rest of our drinks, which tasted awful (stick to beer, don't attempt any sort of mixed drink from here) she finally took our food order. After clearly not knowing ANYTHING about the menu, didn't know what the options of sides were, what type of bread we could get, etc.... the worst was that when I told her what I wanted, she made a Disgusted face at me and said "Really?" So I clearly changed my order, I mean if the waitress thinks its bad to order it must be pretty bad, but how RUDE is that to make a gross face when someone orders their food!!??
We also ordered an appetizer for the table....

45 min later, we still had no food, no appetizer and all our drinks were empty! No one even came to check if we needed more water. I know it was busy in there, but there were empty tables, so they were not THAT busy. We told them we were in a hurry because the concert we were going to was going to start soon (we had been at the restaurant for over an hour and still didn't have anything to eat) So they brought our check out to us, saying this way we could get out faster. We got our check BEFORE our food even came!? I have never experienced anything that tacky. 

FINALLY our food came, and what do you know? She forgot my order. Even told me she messed up putting it in. So everyone I was with ate, and paid their checks, THEN my food came. I had to eat it pretty fast. Though it was decent, not worth the hour and 15 min wait for a bowl of soup and grilled cheese!

The manager tried to smooth things out by giving us complimentary shot glasses, it did not make up for the awful experience. He didn't even come over to the table to check on us, or apologize, just had the shot glasses sent over.

Lastly, as I was pulling my wallet out to pay, which our waitress, Ashley, stood next to the table waiting for the payment, which made it really uncomfortable.... comes over to me and apologizes to me for being so rude saying "well you know my boyfriend cheated on me and blah blah blah..." So unprofessional! I work in the service industry, and rule #1 is you don't bring your personal problems to work!!! Your boyfriend issue is NOT my problem.

Sorry about your boyfriend Ashley, but you should not have let it ruin our night.

I will not be going back.

This is a hidden gem.  A cute and cozy atmosphere.  This place was awesome!  The food was great, staff was friendly, and the service was wonderful.  We went back a second time during our stay, because it was one of our favorites!

Neat little place in Printers Alley. I can't comment on the food, but I enjoyed having a couple beers at the bar. It was pretty bright and colorful at 5pm during the week, so I'm going to say it's probably safe to say this may be a good family dinner option.

Stopped here for dinner on Saturday with the boys from the bachelor party. Doorman told us "Get the ribs!" and the host said it's the best thing on the menu. We all got the ribs, and they were phenomenal. Very soft, slid right off the bone, perfect sauce. I got French fries and Cole slaw as sides and loved those too. Fries were seasoned great, nice and crispy, and very hot. Some of the guys got Mac n Cheese and said it was perfect. Live music was great, not too loud (which is why we didn't eat at a bunch of other places). Didn't want anything too rowdy for dinner. Would definitely come here again for dinner before a crazy night on Broadway!

A must go attraction, even if you are not into country music because I certainly am not. But if you are open minded and don't mind seeing all the awesome antique cars, guitars, and celebrity figures and showcases, then go for it. It's a historical place and really can't go wrong with kids and family.
WOW - great beer menu!  So many great beers and only so much I can drink, what a shame.  The menu looked like good bar food but we didn't eat here - 4 stars for the stellar beers and proper glasses.

Always wanted to go and I had the chance. Always loved the country and bluegrass music.. Had the best time with the best music. Was able to hear some new upcoming artist. No matter were you sit you had a great view.

Worst service and worst food I've had in years. Don't order the nachos. I am embarrassed for Nashville that this place is in business. See my photos of the nasty ketchup bottle they finally brought out after we finished our burgers.

This is a somewhat disturbing walk down a darkish alley towards an unknown destination. 

Not to worry; once you get in the waitstaff is pleasant, efficient, and worth a look = ). I shared a pulled pork, fries and onion strings with my wife and topped it off with a solid margarita. Add in her sweet tea and we maxed out around $20ish. 

In the end it wasn't a wasted night, but we probably could have found better. It was another "experience" in another "dive bar" that looked to have a somewhat local following. 

Don't plan on making a big night of it if you're going here this is run of the mill bar food in a run of the mill locale.

I thought the food was mediocre.  I got a "cheesesteak" sandwich that tasted like a cheap panini I could have picked up at a local grocery store.  You have to order side items separately, which is typical for many nice restaurants and I am okay with if the main course is impressive enough to stand on it s own.  This one wasn't .   The cocktails were tiny and massively overpriced.  I accidentally spilled my first cocktail (1/4 left) - and the waiter cleaned it up immediately but never offered to replace the drink.  He was a super nice guy, but perhaps a little frazzled.

My sandwich was delivered almost 15 minutes after the rest of the food at our table, and they were fairly unapologetic until I asked to have it removed from the bill, which they did, kindly, but did charge me for an extra cocktail in its place.  At that point I was too embarrassed to complain).  My husband and I spent $150 ($180 including tip), for sub-par food and cocktails that should have cost 1/2 of what they did.  

Also- ambiance seems to be having a bit of an identity crisis.  Is it a hipster restaurant, a sports bar, or a nightclub??  In my opinion, a restaurant is better off choosing one and being really great at it - not trying for all three.
Seat yourself....we sat down, 15 minutes later our waitress came up and we asked for menus. She sarcastically says, "well everyone came in at the same time". Horrible service. Never coming back here.

The menu looks nice, but we wouldn't know how anything was since our waitress never took our orders.

The Tippler is a pretty place, but it's way too snooty and overpriced.

When we visited we were in a slight hurry on the way to an event. I was surprised that we were seated immediately at 7pm on a Friday - so I was already becoming a fan of the place.  However, that soon changed.

Instead of bread at your table, the give you these tasty potato chips. The basket at our table wasn't full to begin with so I asked for some more. They didn't tell me that they charge $3. For potato chips.

We ordered our chicken and biscuit appetizer, and our waitress said she'd be right back to take our dinner order.  Here's the thing - she never came back. Somebody else brought the food, and another person filled or waters, but our waitress never came back to take our dinner orders. After 30-40 minutes, I had enough.

She finally did swing by, and I told her to just bring the check. I guess I left a lackluster tip (I'm not one of those automatic "15 percenters") because she gave me a pretty bad look on the way out.

All in all, $34 for two drinks and an appetizer. Oh - and the chips.

We finally made it to the Grand ode opry.
We went there to see Trace Atkins. He only sang 2 songs. I would've loved to of seen some younger artists. Most of the artists were in their 70s and 80s. They keep doing these commercials about buying things...it was overkill. If I wanted to see commercials and advertisements I could set home and watch TV. Glad I went once ...But have no desire to return.
I think the better place to visit is on Broadway and see all the artist playing and In each Bar/restaurant.

Loved the area on where bar was located but we ordered simple drinks, Titos Soda and lime. The bartender took a while to get them to us and then they were cranberry and titos. When we told her no cran, she returned our drinks in a shot glass and seemed upset. Great local bar but bartender needs to crack a smile and not look upset when she mistakes our order.

Awful.  The guy who was running the karaoke just wanted to hear himself and his friends sing.  I would say once every half an hour he'd let someone not in his group sing, but was extremely rude.  Go to Troubadours if you want good karaoke in Nashville, they are great!  Would absolutely not recommend this place.

In Nashville for the first time an wandered in based on Yelp reviews. Way to go, Yelpers!  Great space. "Just Right" sized portions of the kind of breakfast food I needed after a night out in Nashville.  Would love to come back at night...
A cool experience while you are in Nashville, especially if you are a country music fan.

Love love love the atmosphere.  They have cool seating areas if you are hanging out with friends and don't want to sit at a table or the bar.
The vibe was great.
Good beer and food as well.

Loved the jalapeno tots and the hippie hollow pita. Good service. Great selection of craft beers. Decor is memrable and inviting. Doesn't feel like a chain at all. Great place to stop for a beer or a meal

This was neat and interesting. Though I think it was slightly over priced, it was still fun to learn more about the history and what it means for the singers to be a part of the grand opry. The tour is about an hour.
Not good for gluten free folks. Was not able to eat. had to leave

I usually try write good reviews but I just can't with this place. We have tried it out twice hoping it would be better the second time around but it wasn't. 

The nacho appetizer can be explained in one word...awful. The queso was practically cold and the pork tasted like it was on the verge of being spoiled. My boyfriend had a burger and he said it was okay, but it certainly was nothing to write home about. The restaurant (indoor and outdoor) is a has a nice ambiance and vibe but (big BUT) the food and beer is in my opinion overpriced and subpar. Honestly, I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone I liked.

Awesome new bar on Broadway that will definitely hold its own with the established ones!  They hit the jackpot going from a hole in the wall in Vegas to a multi-floor bar with a rooftop deck and they even have their own line of whiskey.  Bands and DJ's nonstop and the staff is friendly and very interactive!  You MUST visit Blair if you go here; she goes well above and beyond the role of "bartender" and lives and personifies the entire brand.  Won't surprise me if she owns the next one that opens; she is that good!  The bar does not cater to just the guys either; a bachelorette party stopped in for an hour or two during my visit and was made quite comfortable (DJ Sinister having a lot to do with that).

My only ding is the food; it is definitely bar barbecue and not barbecue joint barbecue.  Of course, most people won't come here to eat but for the entertainment and cold drinks.  Get you some hot chicken before coming.

RNR is a must-stop on your next trip to Nashville and will hold their own with the established big dog honky tonks!

Great music and friendly staff. Trey was our server and he told us we couldn't go wrong with anything on the menu. He was right!  We had the chicken, ribs and brisket and everything was fall off the bone with great flavor. If I'm down in Nashville I would definitely come back here

I was visiting Nashville from San Antonio as part of a national professional conference and one event planned for us was the 87th anniversary concert for the Grand Old Opry!  Brother, I'm in!  I like country, really like the classic country and my folks are from Harlan County, Kentucky, home of Loretta Lynn, so this place has always been a mythical kind of place to actually visit.  It lived up to the billing!  WE had very good seats and it was just a special place.  I was surprised at how much comedy played a part in the show, the emcee, Little Jimmy Dickens, kinda cornball, but I was laughing as was the crowd.  Honestly, can't remember who all I saw there, Jim Ed Brown, Jason Aldean, Ricky Skaggs, Steve Wariner, Casey James, Bill Anderson, Tyler Farr, Rodney Atkins, and many, many others.  This was a real show, guess it was going out live on the radio and they have an actress portraying Minnie Pearl to get the crowd whipped up.I went both nights, Friday and Saturday and the Friday show was by far the best, but maybe that's because I was just so completely awestruck and in reverence for being at this mecca of music.  I want to say that those tickets cost me 50 bucks as part of our group rate.

The environment/decor at BAD is really unique and was my favorite thing about the place.  It is probably great for a happy hour, but I only came here for lunch and my rating is based on that experience.  The menu is typical for a bar and does not have a lot of variety, but if you want a sandwich or a burger, then you will be fine.  I had a burger here myself and it was alright.  The staff that work here are very friendly and provided great service.  I would like to see what it is like during a happy hour, that seems like it must be the best time to go here in this unique place!
A great hidden corner of Midtown.  Live music, interesting people, and inventive cocktails,  The Tipler is a Nashville gem.
Good burgers. Nice beer selection. Crazy phenomenal music.  Prices are not particularly good on food. Cool spot. No better spot to chill and take in the real music scene in Nashville.

Stopped by here the other night before going to a film at the Belcourt Theater. Service was terrible, the server was slow, looked like he had not bathed in days and when he did get around to bringing our drink orders got them wrong. Now for food. My wife got the burger which was nothing to write home about and I got the nachos which were terrible. Nashville has plenty of clean, well-managed and good restaurants. Spend your money at one of them and not this place.

I'm staying next door, at the Union Station Hotel and the kitchen closed at 11 PM. They told me about Flying Saucer and that the kitchen would be open till 2 AM. I have a terrible cold and I just wanted a soup. It was 11h15 PM. Apparently the waiters were about to leave, or were not interested in selling just a soup (a tip of 20% over 5 dollars?). I waited forever and nobody would speak to me, although the bar was almost empty. There was one table in the balcony and about 10 people in the bar. I spoke to one waitress, a blonde one, and she told me I should talk to the barman. So I did, and he told me about the two soups, but didn't mentioned he had already ordered, which he didn't. 10 more minutes passed and I was not aware if my soup was ordered or not. I spoke to the woman again and she told me to sit somewhere else, although I was sitting at the bar where the barman was very helpful with other people asking for beers. So, when he finished talking to them, as I approached, he said he had already ordered my soup and he was going to charge me. The change was 25 cents and he was ironic.15 minutes more (it's just a soup...) and nothing and finally the owner or manager saw me standing there and went himself to the kitchen. After that, finally, half hour later, the barman arrived with my soup. I didn't tip. Let's be clear: it's called"gratuity" and you tip when they deserve. Don't bother going to this bar. I will never come back.

Just alright. Good beer selection (if a little overpriced), but I don't care for the atmosphere. I like to have my drinks outside in the summer and there's no patio and they hardly ever have the windows open on that sunroom-ish area. The food isn't anything special. The pretzels are pretty good, but nothing to write home about.

Exactly what you think.  I had a blast, even by myself, going backstage and taking pictures of everything.  It's crazy to think that you are standing, or sitting, right where some of the greatest country Gods once stood.  Standing in the circle on the stage is almost magical, with the lights shining down and all the other tourists staring at you while you take your picture.  It's pretty cool and quite informative.  Definitely something I would do again with other family members.
Super friendly staff. Great prices. An absolute must for vinyl enthusiasts and Jack White fans. Lots of fun things to do and see.

Cheap drinks! We came upon this place when walking to the WarMuseum. Bloody was thin but good. We decided to come back for some food bc of the reviews. 

First off, our waitress was rude as hell. Second, the wings suck. Like seriously I can't even eat them. One bite responded by "gross!" 

But the drinks are cheap! 

And whomever commented about live music- no live music here. 

Someone's a liar. Come for cheap drinks at a cool hole in the wall. Save your appetite for elsewhere. Yesterday we had amazing wings from Mojo's!

Jack White is a very cool cat.   From his Tesla radio tower perched atop the Lego colored building block shape of his recording studio Third Man Records this is the House That Jack built.  And you don't just have to stand outside and gawk.  You can come inside.  You are invited.

Does this mean that once inside this childlike fantasy land you can climb into a large wooden chair with Jack White himself dressed as Santa Clause and perch on his lap while telling him what you wish for (him, serenading you while playing an electric guitar sans Santa Clothing)????  Unfortunately, no.  You don't get to see Jack.  Or really the recording studio either.  What you get is to step into a front room filled with some memorabilia of days gone by like the actual Lego pieces used in the White Stripes video "Fell In Love With a Girl".

But don't distress, fun is still to abound.  Because Jack has a very vintage, very wooden, very art deco recording booth that still works.  And for a $15 contribution to preserving history you too can become a recording star by shutting the almost sound proof door and making a 45 second record.  It will be stamped with Third Man Records.  And when you are done you can put the said record in an old rusty mailbox outside and mail it to the love of your life.  In fact, if you are too shy to sing into the microphone (dear God is Jack listening to these recordings??) you can just speak a heartfelt message or poem.  Let's just hope the person you are mailing the record to has a record player.

In addition to the vintage recording booth there is also a vintage photo booth you can take pictures in.  I saw Jack on an episode of one of my favorite TV shows (American Pickers) and he ended up buying some antique stuff from Mike Wolfe (who has a store in Nash) so the guy has great taste in antiques.

Of course you can buy albums (some rare) and t-shirts.  Third Man Records put out some cool, exclusive stuff in the music world (become a member for the best access).  And they also have random events at the studio so you will want to do like me and stalk, I mean watch, their website for more information on what's happening.  Swoon!!
Came on a Monday at 11pm after the previous bar closed early. Place was pretty empty (no surprise) and no drink specials but they were yummy nonetheless! Awesome bar staff as well!

I liked my experience here a lot, it's a fun beer hall with diverse selections aplenty.  But as far as the food goes, it didn't have me going gaga.  Maybe I didn't order correctly but I expected more in that way from all the rave reviews. But the beer was great at the staff was knowledgeable.  The pretzels were a huge hit at my table.  A great stopping point to chill after seeing sights or for a fun night out.  If I was in town again I'd definitely stop by, but I'd have my meal somewhere else.

One of my favorite places to visit Nashville. 
Have also been to the one in Memphis, Raleigh, Addison & Columbia. 
Super menu for even a Vegetarian!

I am not a fan of country music at all but this was a fun place.

We took a backstage tour and my concept of county music has changed a bit.  

It only costs about 23.00 for a show.  No matter what your stature as far as stardom.  If you are Carri Underwood you play for 23.00 a show or around that much.  If you become a member you must play so many times a year.  Everyone can get a chance at the Opry.  Every star just uses a locker in a community area.  The stars are very down to earth and not like other stars with special

Get the pretzel.  Do it.

Really cool chill place to drink beer (and eat pretzels, obv) in Nashville.  Not that far from the city center, but far enough that it's a lot less fratty than downtown could be.

Friendly staff, cool seating (couches, benches or regular tables).

And pretzels - do it.

This place is literally in a back alley. It has that bar type of look on the inside. Dark and grungy. BUT they have great drink prices and specials. The food is pretty decent for bar food. Typical stuff such as burgers, chicken tenders, etc. If you're looking for cheap, this is definitely an okay place to check out. I wouldn't go there too often but if i needed something cheap to eat that was decent, this would be a great place to check out.

Food was very tasty.  The Reuben was excellent and I especially liked the jalapeño sauerkraut.  The Cobb Salad was fresh & tasty.  The Quesadilla were on special & were very tasty.  Definitely recommend this restaurant to others.  Our server was pleasant & attentive.

Gorgeous place. Great & professional unpretentious staff. My SUGGESTIONS to Anthem for regular Saturday Nights: Upgrade  the quality of the sound system, hire a DJ that doesn't play 20 second snippets of every song possible, & please leave it up to other less cool venues to play Shaggy & Coolio.
Over 225 draft beers and a limited but pretty good menu. I ordered the quesadillas and enjoyed them. Nothing out of this world, but good food.

Visited on Saturday May 24 around 4 and the place was kind of quiet , but by the time we left, the patio was filling up and the place was getting lively. We went for a Groupon deal and will definitely be going back! The bartender/server, Sammy, was very helpful. We had a beer sampler flight each. There were 5 generous samples of beer. We also had the cheese dip made with sausage and sriracha I was afraid I might be too hot for my boyfriend's tastes but it was perfect. My favorite beer was the Curious Traveler Shandy. All of the beers were exactly as described by the bartender. The location was great and the décor was fun. All in all a great neighborhood bar we cant wait to visit again.

If you like music you need to go here! The 4000 or so people make it prefect venue. The nose bleed seats have great views. Where else can you get six different acts for one price.   The gift shop stays open st least half hour after show.

Sounds quality is excellent. They have video boards for view of stage from up above.

About as bad as it gets
Big party on a Monday night
First ones in the place
Drinks took forever 
Dinner came out sporadically where 1/4 of the group got dinner at a time. By the time 1/4 of the table finished eating another 1/4 would get their food.
The waitress tried, but the kitchen couldn't figure out how to get food out.
The only thing that keeps this place in business is the music.
Enjoy that and eat elsewhere

Stop here if you're a Jack White fan. It's a quirky, fun little glimpse into his world. You can pick up some beloved vinyl, see some Jack White or White Stripes artifacts, and browse posters and t-shirts. It's a bit off the beaten path in Nashville, but worth the trip, particularly if this music is more up your alley than the country playing on Broadway.

Simply one of the best venues. You can practically feel the history as you enter this place. Free parking is easy because of the mall, and there's really not a bad seat in the house. A must for both locals and tourists!

Fantastic Jack White shrine and record shop.

If you are looking for quality vinyl, this is the place. 

They mostly carry Third Man pressed records with a small smattering of other labels.

Plenty of Jack White and White Stripes albums, plus some really unique stuff.

The staff is incredibly friendly and seemed stoked to be there.

Fun visit for those that appreciate good vinyl, or just love Jack White music.

By far the highlight of the trip. I was most excited to see Carrie underwood.. Much to my surprise the other artists outshines her. Lee greenwood got everyone singing along. Carson peters and iron mountain shocked me (a child with amazing talent), Lauren Alaina shocked me with her enthusiasm and sweetness( the girl can sing too), and Charles eaten ended up being quite the performer. A great time

The reviews are a little harsh....and I get the complaints haha. This was the first place I went to while I was in Nashville.  I love karaoke and it was the first place I found...and it was in famous printers alley.  
Honestly. It's kinda what I imagine a tennessee karaoke bar to look like. Smokey. Kinda divey. Kinda bleh. Felt like a great place for a budweiser and terrible karaoke singing. I got to sing 10 minutes after outing in a song. Not too bad.

This place ain't classy...but there's a charm to places like that sometimes. Open wayyy late night too
Great food and service. I highly recommend the arugula and prosciutto pizza. The loaded rocket tots were on point as well.

Hubby and I came in for a late lunch prior to checking in at our hotel down the street. Bartender was great! Not intrusive, but attentive. And... she can do a correct Guiness pour. Hubby and I ordered a shepheds pie and bangers and mash and queso and chips. Everything was great. Queso had some spice, but not crazy hot. Hubby cleaned his plate of bangers and mash, and my shepherd's pie was wonderful, moist but not greasy. Veggies on the side were a smidge bland for my taste, but I was so happy with the main dish I couldn't care less about the steamed veggies. 

Sports are the star here. Football fans were piling in as we were wrapping up. Bartender knew several regulars and their preferred teams. She told us it can get a bit wild at times.

I'd come back here for food and drinks! Looks like my kind of place!

Even though I'm not a massive country music fan, the backstage tour was good fun. It was well organized, nice group size and informative. It was a bear experience to see backstage. My only complaint is that they take your photo on stage. It was a great shot of us, however a $25 charge is simply crazy. Minus a star for such an astronomical overcharge (if you choose to pay it!)

Music is everywhere in Nashville, and good music too. The band at BB King's was lively and talented, but had some odd choices of song, including one seemingly titled "I'm Going To Marry My Mother In Law." SO corny and just plain weird. $5 cover just to get in the door in the evening.

The venue is the best part of BB King's. It's large and doesn't feel stuffed or stuffy. There is a dance floor in front of the stage which you can use if you dare, and lots of tables situated facing the stage/dance floor. Servers move deftly throughout, bringing food and drinks. It was a little awkward being walked by the hostess through the dance floor, in front of the stage and all the people at their tables watching -- to our table. 

My friend and I just ordered dessert because we had a craving. They have a peach cobbler on the menu, which is served a la mode and I believe made with real peaches! However...it was NOT a cobbler. It was a streusel. Real dessert-lovers know the difference. Very sweet and big enough to share between two people and still satisfy that sweet tooth.

I'm giving a one star because zero isn't an option. Nashville has a lot to offer, but don't waste your time with this. Not worth the money, and the staff are rude, in stark contrast to my other experiences in Tennessee.

Back Alley Diner continues to impress us. We have been back several times since my initial review, but Saturday night we tried some different things. The wings were on special, so we ordered some buffalo and some Tabasco wings. The buffalo has BBQ sauce in the mix, so it had an awesome smokey flavor. The Tabasco had the perfect amount of heat. Both were cooked perfectly, crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. Hubs stuck with the catfish po boy, but I went with a salad. It was great! Quality lettuce and toppings and they were very fresh. Cold beer as always, and some nice live music. We will keep on coming back!

I loved it and my husband had a good time too.  The night we went there weren't any really big name people but all the entertainment was pretty good and just being at the Grand Old Opry was fun.  We went to dinner over at the huge mall before the show and parked there across from the Opry.  It was not a concert, anyone going thinking that is what they are going to will be disappointed.  It is a live radio show with tons of history and some old Opry performers who show up for a song.  Just enjoyed what it was about.

We found this on Yelp and decided to give it a try. Busy but not too crowded on a Friday night. The wait staff was great. If you like craft beer you need to try the Jackalope Bear Walker. All the food was great and I really liked the homemade kettle chips. It had a local feel and a relaxed fun atmosphere. If you like places off the beaten path you will not be disappointed. No negatives. I just don't give many 5 stars.

This was a great experience! We went for an early dinner on Saturday... No wait! Even with 6, we were seated right away. The decor was fantastic! I loved the brick walls and the wood bar. Beautiful.

Our server was very nice, but the service was sort of slow. The food was very good. I had the catfish po boy and most of my family ordered the burgers. Everyone was happy. 

I tried the Blues Brew too (I guess it's a custom beer for them) and it was tasty too! We would go back if we're in the area.

Pretty much everything about our visit to the Grand Ole Opry was perfect.  The staff is friendly and helpful.  When you are walking in there is a big guitar with Grand Ole Opry Written on it and they are sure to have a staff person there to snap your photo on your cell for you.  Thank goodness they haven't tried to take your photo and sell it to you.

There is a bar just past security where you can purchase drinks and bring them in.

The show was great and the seats comfortable with very good viewing.

We went to the 7pm show so exiting the theater was crammed.  Felt much like cattle being pushed through a maze.  They only allow themselves 35 min to clear, clean and reseat the theater.  

Parking can be difficult so be prepared to walk a bit.  Actually parking further out isn't a bad idea because after the show there is major traffic congestion.  If you park towards the back of the lot you can scoot out much faster.
Great place to eat at. Very friendly environment and the food is great. I had a bacon Swiss cheese burger and it was so yummy. I would so come back here again.
Loved it! Not a bad seat in the house. Prices are reasonable. Great shows, consistently.

Oh Saucer, how I love you. This place is slowly getting me through grad school. There's always a great variety on tap and something different going on every night of the week. Mondays are 3 dollar pint nights, Tuesdays are trivia nights, Wednesday is usually brewery night. They even have specials on the weekends. 
In addition to all this goodness, you can join their UFO club, which tracks your beers tasted. At 200 different beers, you get a party! 
This is a place I always bring friends from out of town. Such a great atmosphere and tasty food too! Their pretzels with queso and spicy mustard are a can't miss.
Great food, great employees and great drinks for a great price. You can't go wrong with the jalapeño poppers, burgers, wraps or chicken sliders. Will be a regular for sure!
Good atmosphere, good food, drinks, music (live), slow service. Will give it a second round.

As a famous "restaurant", this place was just ok. When we arrived, we were starving, but had to wait on a table for about 10-15 minutes and pay a cover to get in even though we purchased massive amounts of food each. (Thumbs down) The food was ok..but the band for the night was great (Jay came around to ask us what we wanted to hear and sang those songs first). Our server was great too. The fried pickles were really salty. The shrimp and grits were swimming in oil. I had the wings and they were subpar. I bet most people come for the entertainment mostly.
Great place. Good deals for happy hour. Great food. Staff is nice and friendly. Great atmosphere. Good place to go for lunch and just kick back. Go check it out!

I went here for lunch with co-workers and its seemed like an alright place. It didn't stand out to me like " I really have to come here again" Although it didn't make me hate it either. I'm sure if it was a weekend night and I was drinking I might have enjoyed it better. I will say for lunch it is, OK but nothing spectacular. So I won't say don't go there for lunch, I also won't say you have to try it. The Fish and Chips aren't bad so give it a shot and make your own choice.

We had absolutely a blast here while watching the USA (YEAAAAAAAAAAAA buddy) v Ghana game. There was a great crowd watching the game with us. Amurica was definitely represented. Actually, Ben Franklin and Honest Abe even stopped by. Although it was definitely packed, we were able to watch the game reasonably well with the GIANT screen outdoors. The bartenders were also able to handle the crowds pretty well. Buckets of Coors light were $20 and singles were $4 (har ha nice to see buying in bulk saves right)? In regards to food...pretty typical. Although Freedom fries never tasted so good...

Overall, such a fantastic experience. Such an enthusiastic group that embraces the mo' spangled the mo' better. Words to live by.
It is absolutely unacceptable for this business to treat their customers who are not like them poorly. It is not acceptable to be rude and disrespectful to customers,

As a recent transplant to Nashville, BAD is my go to spot for lunch as well as a favorite for after work drinks. The food is not going to knock your socks off, but it is consistently good. The sides are fantastic. I, like most Americans, love a really good french fry. Not every place makes exceptional french fries though so I love having an option to choose something else. I can't speak for BAD's fries, because I always get the house made chips. I love these things. They are the perfect ratio of thin crunchy chips and thicker, chewier chips. 

The burgers are really tasty and well-seasoned. I learned the hard way not to eat one at lunch though. Although the titan burger with mushrooms and cheddar cheese is delicious, it lead to a very unproductive day at the office as I sat at my desk complaining to my co-workers that I was so full I wanted to take a nap. I tend to stick to the chicken sandwich or wrap now. 

The real reason I love this place is the staff. I'm usually by myself as I work in a small office where most of the staff packs. I have never felt uncomfortable being there alone. I always sit at the bar and I have never had a problem finding an open stool. The bartenders are friendly and remember your drink order after a time or two. They do tend to be a little free with the endearments (Honey being one of their favorites) but I suppose I should be getting used to that now that I'm in the South. Their timing is always perfect and my drink is rarely empty for more than a few seconds. 

After work they have great specials and several nights with live music. What more could I ask for in a dive?

The Opry is called the 'home of American music' and 'country's most famous stage.'  They're known to offer and present 8 or more artists on each show, and gives the audience a sample of each artist's musical style.  There's also a gift store next door where you can pick up souvenirs, clothing, and music - Nadia, one of the helpful and the most sweetest staff there, gave us a brief history as well as the tour of the Opry we should check out and the upcoming shows that are coming up for the weekend.  Nice plaza to see the venue itself and take pictures next to the guitar monuments. :D

+features a variety of performing artists
+ask for Nadia in the gift store

Came in for Sunday brunch, bottomless mimosas, sangria and bloodys for 12 bucks. I ordered the prime rib and it was amazing. Great portion size, great flavor.. The works. Emily was our bartender, she was very humble and happy to serve us on Easter morning, she treated everyone at the bar like family ( I'm from
California, so it was refreshing). Great patio and great selection of beer. 

By the way, I never had an empty glass.

these assholes. looked at us through the windows shut the lights out on us when we accidentally left out card at the bar as we were banging on the door trying to PAY OUR TAB . They flat saw us and denied letting us in to handle our tab and get out card back. we came in at midnight... tipped the band graciously and were treated like homeless people begging for food. ignored and left with no help from neighboring bars or even the band thAT REEMEMBERED US ON THE STREET was no help.  WHAT ASSHOLES. we dont live in nashville and needed our card for gas money. they didnt play any blues and quit playing after i tipped them 20 bucks for 2 songs. This place sucks and B.B. king would roll over in his grave God rest his soul.  I will never recommend this tourist trap to anyone even if i hate them. And the drinks were weak. This place sucks. Avoid at all cost.
We just hung out in the lower level bar area. Drinks were cold. Service was great. Had some good live music. Musicians interacted great with the bar patrons.

My husband and I never get to go out but we finally had a chance last weekend. We chose BB King's. Our server, Sabrina, was awesome!!! It was pretty busy so our food took a while and she handled it like a pro. It was refreshening to see someone in food service who doesn't act like they hate their job. She was polite and accomodating to our special requests. The food and music were great too!!

Food was okay. Service was absolutely terrible. We literally waited over 40 minutes for our food - and let me tell you, it wasn't worth it. They didn't have Fat Tire on draft as advertised. Patio is good but there are much better patios with much, MUCH better service and food. We won't bother coming back!

Great music but way to loud for only 16 people in the downstairs area. WARNING A friend with us ordered a mixed drink and had a black bug in drink. She sent it back to get a fresh drink, still had a bug but this one was frozen in the ice. Pay attention when ordering you drinks and food!

50 cent wings on Saturday, and for 50 cents these are really good wings..if you do opt for the wings don't forget to order a side of fries, those are delicious too! Oh and $2 PBRs...perfect for anyone on a budget and looking for a low key kinda place with live music on a Saturday night.

I like beer, it makes me a jolly good fellow
I like beer, it helps me unwind and sometimes it makes me feel mellow 
Whiskey's too rough, Champagne costs too much, vodka puts my mouth in gear
This little refrain should help me explain as a matter of fact I like beer
Beer, Beer, Beer! Awesome staff and great selection of craft brews. This is our go-to spot for new brews and meeting with friends.

We went last night (a Wednesday) so it was dead besides the twenty of us.  We did have a lot of fun because we love karaoke but be weary of the fact that it would have been a pretty lonely place if we didn't have a large group; there were literally two other people there.  I would hope that it is busier on the weekend.  The bartender and DJ were both really nice and made us happy but I was hoping to see and hear more people.

Thankfully, I have been here several times or I might have been turned off by my most recent visit. The food was fine, but our server was really cranky. Not at all friendly bordering on rude. Maybe she worked closing the night before and really didn't want to be working a lunch shift....? Still, it had a definite effect on our dining experience.

This is the first place I ever went to in Nashville and I loved it from the first minute. I've been back every time I have found myself in the city. It's huge but still cozy sort of. Great central location, next to the Frist.
I almost always get the pretzels and dip and they are always delicious.
They of course have a spectacular selection of beers.

Eat, drink, and be merry! And hopefully your server has gotten a good night's and doesn't look like she is shooting daggers out of her eyes at you.

Went for a friend's Birthday party tonight. Was not impressed. Band was extremely boring. Service was AWFUL, and they added gratuity which she did not deserve. I am a great tipper and this girl was just  downright bad at waiting tables. Wouldn't have given more than 3 dollars. They put a 7 dollar gratuity making a 45 dollar tab for 1 yazoo pale, a coffee,  6 wings (which were slimy and cold), a 1/2 order of under fried pickles and a bowl of what was supposed to be peach cobbler but was basically lukewarm peaches in a bowl with ice cream... Save your 50 bucks that I personally feel I was ripped off for, and walk 2 blocks to Bourbon Street which is where we went after. Better music. I didn't try the food but the drinks were cheap and the menu looked good and much cheaper than bb's. Anything is better than that lame experience we had at BB kings. I assume all these good reviews are from tourists, this is not a good local spot. AVOID.

This. Place. Is. Awesome!!

I ventured here on a Thursday night and the place was hoppin'! There was a $5.00 cover fee, which I had no problem paying. The House Band was playing that evening and they are great! My better half and I sat at the bar and just had drinks during our stay, so unfortunately I cannot give a review of the food, but next time I will - trust me.

The decor, from top to bottom is perfect. There's nice moody lighting, local art strung on the walls, as well as paintings of some well known performers.

So back to the music, the sound was good, all performers were really enjoying themselves, and a couple guest vocalists made an appearance. Overall, this is a really cool club to see live music.

I like country, not a major enthusiast but I def like it. We got tickets to the Opry for Tuesdays show. Don't be too concerned with your seats. It's not a huge area like MSG are Barclay, which is what I'm use to. The $35 seats we're totally fine and the staff and atmosphere is really relaxed. The grand ole Opry gift shop is there too and we purchase some creme brûlée popcorn which was awesome!  It's a nice show. I would most certainly recommend going if your in town. I didn't know anyone play (expect BARRY GIBB...how cool) but it was still enjoyable. 
****the bathrooms are clean and there's always ticket paper!***

We had to try out this iconic spot, and were not wowed by the experience. The drinks were very tasty and the atmosphere was fun. However, the food was just ok... the coleslaw and baked beans were definitely not homemade. Service was also not the best, as the waitress didn't seem to know the menu and one of our orders was incorrect.
More of the ambiance and music than the food. .. the food was okay I had the ahi sandwich with homemade chips

Good Lordy there's a ton of history here! And you'll learn almost all of it if you take the backstage tour, which I highly recommend. 

I haven't made it to an actual show yet, but the backstage tour was amazing! You sit through a short film on the history if you wish, and I suggest, and then you head on back and there's tour guides along the way to answer questions or give you stories every here and there, but it's pretty much self guided. You see the entrance where every star walks in, and their mailboxes, where you can write them a letter if you so choose. And you get to see all of the dressing rooms and the common area where all the stars hang out. And they don't mind if you sit on the couches where who knows who has sat there before you. 

The headliners dressing room is the only dressing room you can actually walk in, but you see all the others as well. Tour guides will tell you stories old and new and let you know who likes to use which rooms, but they're all themed so it's not too hard to figure out for some.

Then you take a step through the curtain and walk on stage. And then head to the front microphone and stand in the circle where literally every Opry star since the beginning has stood.  That in itself is amazing, for country fans or not, to appreciate. You then walk across the stage and learn about the soundstage next door where the film the show Nashville, and out into the auditorium and into a gift shop.

The price is decent ( I think under $20 a person) and worth it in my opinion. You can take as much or as little time as you want since its self guided, and never be afraid to ask questions, the tour guides are amazingly nice and knowledgable. I would easily do another tour again!

Who am I kidding, Saucer has pretty much become mine and my husbands favorite bar, sometimes the servers can be a little slower, but usually they're pretty good, we come here as much as we can, usually on Wednesdays for Pint night.  I love you saucer, and I'll see you soon.
Best Fish-n-Chips in Nashville! (The secret is they make their own beer batter.) It's a great Irish Pub and they have good food! Not a lot of sunlight- but its an Irish pub.

Really enjoyed the show, yes they do commercials that a lot of folks don't know exist between curtain  shows. Hey, they have always done that. It's still a wholesome family show with Humor, Bluegrass, Country, Modern upcoming stars and traditional country. The backstage pass was a a great deal to see the things that happen behind the scenes. Wish i'd been aware of the celebration add-on (Needed one for a birthday). Great experience for my family. would definitely do it again.

The tour was amazing.  Great education and knowledge by the brilliant Vinny.  He is super enthusiastic and makes the tour a great experience.  Got great pictures and my sister enjoyed it.  Would recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville!

I can tell this is a bar I would really love and the only reason it's not getting 5 stars is the music that we had to deal with when we were here. From what we understood it's normally a BLUES CLUB, but unfortunately due to CMA weekend (we accidentally planned a whirlwind road trip during the same weekend), we had to deal with some more mainstream Taylor Swift-y music that was just not good. Actually, I'll go ahead and say at least one of the acts was actually ANNOYING. Whiney girls are not my jam.

But, the service, despite being obviously overwhelmed, was awesome. We sat at the back bar and were basically the only people (and youngest, so we got some stares) there for most of the time we spent in this place. The drinks were good, the food was good, the bartender was cute and attentive and appreciated our disappointment in the music, and we were actually able to GET food and drink during that incredibly insane weekend. 

We got the appetizer sampler and a side of mac and cheese. I don't eat wings, but I ate one of these and can say, as a non-wing-eater, I wouldn't eat them again, but the catfish bites were so melt-in-your-mouth-amazing, I could eat a whole plate of those myself. The mac and cheese was also fantastic, as were the fried pickles (I'm a serious pickle judge), so I'm anxious to get back and eat the fried treats this place has to offer. I'd definitely come back on a normal trip and spend some time listening to blues and enjoying the delicious foods.

Went for lunch with the kids. Live music was great. Drink special buy any well get the next for a dollar. We had the fried tomato's and the fried crawfish both had a good corn meal taste. My sister had the Tuna sandwich and they did over cook it but all around good.  Fun tables

Great place to see a concert. Of course. The history alone is reason enough to go see. Unfortunately the idiots running the ticket office is reason enough not to attempt a show. 
They went through the effort to put out a full page add in the local paper to promote a play. Offered two tickets for the price of two. Not a quick line or promo code on a website. A full page add that went to print in the paper. Great deal right?  Not exactly. When giving them the promo code that was printed in the paper, I was told that it's only for 10% off each ticket. No explanation. No acknowledgement that I'm staring at something describing a very different offer. Not even a solution to the issue. After talking to a rude ticket sales person and a bored manager who audibly sighed on the phoned after asking how you could not possibly honor a promotion that had to have been proof read by multiple people before printing, I unfortunately had to give up. 
The Opry will forever be a great place to go see an event. Unfortunately it's become more of a typical tourist trap and less of the historical icon of TN.
Beer heaven, there is a lot of space for groups here. The bar / restaurant is hidden behind the Union Station hotel.
Wonderful tour and rich history! Guided tour lasts roughly an hour and very informative and interactive!

WannaB's is my absolute favorite bar in Nashville! It's a hidden gem of a place with fantastic people all around you. You get to sing on stage and enjoy the night without feeling any judgment from the patrons. My girlfriends and I took over the bar when we came in for a bachelorette party and had the best night of our lives! The drinks were cheap and there is a little window next door that sells pizza.. it's a must. Go and have a fabulous time any day of the week!

My wife and I traveled to Nashville for our two year anniversary. We were looking for a cool, nice place to eat on our Saturday night. The photos available from Music City Tippler and the website all alluded to the fact that this was going to be a great, fun outing; however, it was anything but enjoyable aside from the laughs we shared afterwards. 

When we were driving around for a parking spot, our first clue should have been the fact that it was a Saturday night, and MCT was empty. As we entered we were greeted by several contrasting design patterns. Are they trying to be a lounge? Saloon? Is there decor real? Is it from Hobby Lobby? Whatever. The hostess seemed to be the only one that knew what she was doing, and we were seated promptly. We were approached by a woman who provided us with water and told us that our server Smith (for the sake of the review) was busy at the moment but that he would be with us shortly. With us making a total of 10 patrons in the restaurant we were not quite certain what he could be busy with. After about 10 minutes with no service the woman returned to take our drink order, and was extremely confused when my wife asked for a mocktail (she's pregnant). She replied that all of their cocktails are handcrafted, blah, blah, blah, and that she would see what they could do. Moments after we put in our drink order our "server", Smith, came our table sounding as frazzled as someone who has spoken words for the first time. He began stating, again, how all their cocktails are handcrafted, blah, blah, blah. We had to cut him off because I didn't want him to pass out from exhaustion. He seemed distraught that we had a different server and that our drink orders were already placed. He literally shuffled away like a disappointed child on Christmas morning, not getting what they hoped from Santa. After about 15 awkward minues (again, with only appx. 10 people in the restaurant) our drinks arrived. They were just OK. My cocktail's only saving grace was that it had Chartreuse, however it was not worth the $14 price tag (YES, $14!). Our server, along with all the other servers, was huddled around the service well at the bar akin to office workers around the water cooler. It took her another 5 minutes to return to inquire about our appetite. As we ordered food Smith was pacing creepily in the background, mumbling some incomprehensible jargon to himself. He would occasionally walk to the foyer would he would sit and read magazines. Who was this intriguing gentleman?! It took approx. 25-30 minutes for our food order to arrive: seasonal roasted vegetable pasta. The noodles were cooked so al dente to the point where some were crunchy, there were HARDLY any vegetables (not to mention that they were NOT roasted), and worst of all the food was cold. Yes, cold. Not warm or lukewarm. Cold. We both laughed as we picked a few things out to make it look like we gave a damn about our "meal." The server came over to inquire further of our enjoyment with the meal and apologized about the wait time. We asked for our check; Paid for our hardly even sub par experience; and hightailed it out of there. 
 
Please read the other 1-Star Yelp reviews on here. Some were written more eloquently than mine. But our experiences were all spot on the same!

Just took my parents recently to see Vince Gil, Marty Stewart, Striking Matches, Larry Gatlin, Jason Crab, and others. The entertainment was awesome and the place is absolutely beautiful!   I don't believe there is a bad seat in the entire place. Very special for my mom once place he has always wished to go and it was every bit worth it. A definite to do in Nashville.

If you're a fan of Jack White, this will be a cool stop for you. If you don't know the man, obviously you won't care. The line was long when I went, but only because it was the day his album dropped. There are headphones around the small space so you can listen to his records. Lots of memorabilia, like his Grammy's, guitars, and clothing. There's a taco truck outside, and free beer in the back.
Very chill place with comfortable seating and great service. If you are looking for something that isn't typical Broadway head here. Huge beer selection with something for everyone.

Was looking for a low key spot to spend with the girlfriend for our anni. This place was perfect! We were greeted by an extremely friendly doorman named Ronnie who led us into what would be an epic night. There is a $10 cover fee but it def keeps the hoodlums out. We found a spot at the center of the bar and had a perfect view of the stage. We ordered the slab of ribs with baked beans and slaw. The ribs were pretty damn good, had to get some extra sauce to go with it though. The beans were as good as beans get and the slaw was not too heavy on the mayo. But the food was not the highlight of the spot it was more so the atmosphere. At first I felt out of place, me and the girlfriend were literally the only Asian people in here. It was mainly an older crowd as well. But the band crushed the performances and everyone was up and dancing, old and young. This encouraged me to get on the dance floor and just dance. We ended up dancing the rest of the night away and went home with full bellies. Def check it out of you don't want to deal with the madness on Broadway Street of drunk bachelorette and want something more intimate.
Nice experience. I do feel bad for the older ushers that had to deal with teenagers rushing the stage

I've seen the Opry at the Ryman, and I've seen it from the back of the stage at the Opry House, but this was the first time I've seen the Opry from the seats of the Grand Ole Opry House. 

You don't have to be a country music fan to enjoy the Opry.  My BiL was visiting, so we took him to the Opry.  He's never been into country music, but we all had a great time.  I got the tickets a couple of days before the show, and all the better seats were already gone.  The screens were helpful, but I wish we'd been closer.
