But even from our seats, we could see the circle on the stage that had been taken from the Ryman.  It is a great tradition.
Service was Great. Ribs with mac and cheese Amazing. Had made a reservation so had table right in front of stage.

The worst. In a mall across from a Dave and busters. The parking lot was unmarked which left half the showgoers roaming around after a dreadful show. $150. A ticket and the show had 6 unknown performers and two older stars. Seats were church benches. Commercials for Humana were run constantly. Each performer did two songs and there were commercials between each performance. Never go there.staff was annoyed, music was lousy.total rip.off..blech

This place is off the beaten path and not your typical tourist trap. 

Awesome gift options. Listening and photo booths are nice interactive touches. 

An awesome stop for any music lover. You'll get to see Jack White's Grammy's, too!

Great place, better than the San Antonio location, which me and the wife do love. Friendly waitstaff, the dude on duty knew his brews and was quite friendly despite us arriving at near closing on a sunday. Would recommend.

The location is huge! I've been to the Flying Saucer in Charlotte, which was still sizeable, but this location is beautiful and historic, much like the Union Station hotel next to it. Besides those two gems, the other businesses by it appear to be offices with pricey parking decks. 

I sat at the bar, perused their menu of beers and was so happy to see that they were the only ones to offer Highland Brewing's Cold Mountain Ale and Catawba Brewing White Zombie. For $5. I sat next to other people who were on their own so I began chatting with them. 

This is a great place for dinner, friends, or families - yes, I think so! Great staff and wonderful ambiance transports you into the past.

I thought about deducting 1 star for the parking - you have to park a bit farther on the street and even then, it's a bit hard to find parking. However, I found parking and I didn't mind walking 1/4-1/2 mile.

This was the best show we have ever been to. My wife and I made this our first stop in Nashville for our honeymoon. The staff was amazing and courteous. We picked our tickets up at will call and it was a seamless process. Entry was quick once they opened the doors for the show. It was hot outside so be sure to wear something you are comfortable in. Once inside the air was kicking and the show started right on time. Our seats were the best in the house. Seeing country greats perform live was breathtaking. This is a must stop if you're coming to Nashville.

So sad to report this as a meh bar and cafe....I was expecting so much when I arrived and walked through the doors into a well appointed bar area. Where it fell apart was the service and kitchen. I understand the fact that the place is new BUT
1. The wait staff should know what is not available...especially at 5:15 when the place opens at 5. 
2. when you order something you expect that is what you will get. the 2nd on the wait team brought my onion soup which the waitress had bragged about and set it in front of me.
Oh guess what...it was chicken rice which isn't onion...who makes that mistake. 
When the waitress returned and said..."oh yeah, we are out of Onion soup or we don't have it yet but we should have it in the next few weeks.
My table mate said the problem was we should have gone directly to the bar because the service there is great... Ok...next time if we go again...though with all the great spots why would we go back here....next time eat and drink at the bar. 
3. Bathrooms were great and clean and the front house staff was pleasant and efficient. 
Advice... go across to the Boundry. never anything but great!

This is my kind of place. 

Once again, Yelp did not lead me astray... we checked out Back Alley Diner last Saturday afternoon and were just wanting to grab a quick bite somewhere that was not mobbed with all the Swifties™. 

Our waiter was super nice, and the food was exactly what I was hoping for. Great prices & a very chill location. Definitely was a bit of a challenge to find, but was totally worth seeking out!

We stopped in on a whim this Sunday afternoon. We were seated promptly, and our waiter was quick to the table to get our drink orders. We ordered the ribs. These were hands down the best ribs I've had in years. These are not bony, stick robs with leathery meat. They are large succulent ribs with plenty of tender, flavorful, juicy meat. The sauce they slather on the ribs is outstanding (and we bought some on the way out).  The sides weren't special, just your standard beans and cole slaw, but I didn't really need anything to take way from the ribs, they were that good. We will be back.

I went to this restaurant for the first time and was surprised to see they had live music starting right after I walked in. The waitress was very busy but very quick to see after my needs and always had a smile on her face.The BBC was good and then I had a yummy cookie for dessert! It was a fun evening and I will be back!
Just remembered the waitress was named Janna.

I'd go 3.5 stars. If you're looking for the nashville blues vibe without the packed madhouse that that surrounds the honky tonks,  this is the place to go.  Great option when travelling with older people (due to the hostess /seating that is missing in the bars and a little elbow room). The house band was great!  And the floor was bouncing from the club downstairs.  It is crazy loud in there,  don't expect much conversation.  Our server was even wearing ear plugs. Food was on point,  smothered chicken with Mac and cheese was amazing!  Specialty drinks were decent.  I'll definitely come back next time I'm in the area.
Super tiny. Thought they would be selling more records-- nestled into kind of a shady area. We rode bikes but would recommend driving if you can.

Live music outside, so we went inside and drank there and never went back outside. Nice move, us.

The bathroom could use some work but given this is an Irish pub I don't think that should be expected. No offense to the Irish. I know some Irish. They probably have nice bathrooms too.

The jukebox is alright. My brother paid money to hear some songs and I am pretty sure we left before they all came on because he chose to let them play whenever, rather than next. Nice job, brother.

Great live music, good cheap food, but don't expect craft cocktails (and don't order them). I love getting the pulled pork BBQ sandwich and a beer on a weekday night. They do good work here--keep it up!

For the experience this gets an A plus! The security to get in was a little unorganized and annoying, but welcome to modern day America. The show was fun, long... VERY LONG, but fun. The building itself was very disappointing, I was expecting something more than a theater of the 70s era. Ohh yes, remember where you park your car, yikes that was a hunt unlike anything I have had!
Enjoyed the concert while we waited on our dinner. The meat on the burger could have been thicker but it was tasty. Onion straws were thinner than I expected but overall a good experience.

Esta es la famosa disquería mas estudio de grabación de Jack White. Un lugar más que pintoresco que recontra vale la pena visitar si es que tienen pensado ir a Nashville.

Si son fans de la música, Third Man Records es de esos lugares que les resultará encantador, una tienda tan interesante como estéticamente bella, la cual es un placer conocer.

Para los fanáticos de White, la travesía será mejor aún ya que tiene bocha de material del mítico músico de los White Stripes y de seguro que encontrarán varias cosas que serán de su agrado.
5 stars for happy hours prices.  Food has been surprising for being a back alley bar (literally).  I've gone there twice.  I have yet to find another $5 Bloody Mary in this town.

Flying Saucer was an awesome find in Nasvhille. It's a fantastic beer bar walking distance to broadway but far away enough that it felt like we were locals. There is plenty of seating and a long bar area. We took over some of the couches and settled in for a relaxing afternoon of good beer. 

Flying Saucer has a long list of beers on tap and in bottles. They also have a small group of "ghost beer" which are new beers they get that people can blind taste test. The servers do not know anything about the beers or what brewery they came from. Their beer list can be overwhelming but the staff is helpful and you can ask for tasters of their beers on tap. I ordered a beer from a local brewery, a porter which was delicious. I also tried a local peanut butter beer which was also delicious. 

It's a great atmosphere and a relaxed vibe. If you like trying beer, this is a place to go.

Awesome food! Ate here three times while in Nashville. Although it's a chain food was very good. Had sausage Po boy - ok and Ribs - awesome! Live music was very good and well worth the $5 to get in. Band was so good the second night, I bought their cd(which I don't normally do).

Food was pretty good, but the service was very slow. We took advantage of the happy hour (2-4-1 well and beer until 6p), but ended up having issues with our bill. The fried pickles were AMAZING. Definitely a must have. Worth a visit, but hope the service improves.

Im not a fan of country music but this place was a lot of fun.

First the negatives, and here aren't many.

The concessions, is VERY weak.. There is one main place for crappy food (hot dogs etc) and then a section for alcohol, and on a busy night, the lines are long.

The stage itself is very elaborate and very nostolgic. We saw one of the Judd's here (the larger one), and she was good and reminded me of the old show "HeeHaww".

I particularly liked the 'bench' seating, which gave you a more than adequate space to sit and plenty of leg space.

Crowds were polite and orderly, and I would come here again if I had to listen to country.

While I'm certain this place must have some appeal (the parking lot was jammed at around 6:30pm on a Wednesday night), it's not for the corned beef and cabbage.  I sat at the bar and the waitress poured a great Guinness.  The meal was spotty at best.  The corned beef, which appears to be brined in house, was dry.  As I was eating mine, another out of town patron came in and ordered the same thing, and his was out within minutes, leading me to believe they already had the corned beef sliced and sitting in a warmer ready to plate, along with probably a buffet tray full of baked potatoes (see next line).  The potato medley that I got for my side were a variety of potatoes cubed and baked, and none of them were very good.  The cabbage was sliced up and sitting in a bowl of it's juice.  I'm used to getting steamed cut potatoes, with a hunk of cabbage to slice into, and moist corned beef.  This meal fell short.

Visiting the Grand Ole Opry House was such a great experience! To see artists from both current-day & times-past was truly a delight & even though I wasn't familiar with some of the older groups from way-back-when, they still had the ability to thoroughly entertain & still had the quick chops to get a roaring laugh from the audience. The Opry House is a beautiful building & has so much charm & history within it's walls. The seating is pew-style but I found it to be comfortable & it was not an issue for me. It was neat to be a part of this live-broadcasted radio show & the Grand Ole Opry will definitely be on the itinerary for any other trips I might again take to Nashville. I opted to purchase the after-show backstage tour & it did not disappoint. We were able to see the dressing rooms where the artists stay before/during the show, the set where Hee-haw was filmed (how cool to find out it was filmed at the Opry & to actually see the set where it took place?!) & were able to stand on stage, on the "Circle" where every artist that has ever performed at the Opry has stood! So cool! I can't recommend enough both the Grand Ole Opry House & the backstage tour- you absolutely MUST make both of these part of your Nashville experience!
PS- the BEST buttered popcorn I've ever put in my mouth was purchased here at the Opry!

The burgers are great. The other stuff on the menu is pretty good too. Provided you can actually order and get it. I've given this place so many chances, but they keep screwing up. How someone to work the outside!! I went an hour early to see a movie five seconds across the street, ordered a beer and tacos and barely made the movie. Service is just pathetic. Good food. Terrible throughout service.

GREAT SPACE!   A refreshing change from the Nashville norm of dumpy roadhouse bars.    Loved that the place had three different rooms which three different vibes.   The cocktails were great and the staff was super friendly.   Im sure this place will hold some great events and I cant wait to go back.
Great venue! Amazing history! We don't listen to country music but, we watched Hee Haw when we were little kids.......loved the tour, brought back some wonderful memories.

This place started off cool until the overachiever muscle head bounce came up to me and asked for my ID. They checked my ID at the door and we had been there for at least 20 mins when he came up to our group. Of the 3 of us, he only asked me, after looking me up and down. I thought he was joking because we had to show it to get in the door. I asked him to see a manager and when the manger finally came, he was a jerk and really didn't care. The door man was too busy tryna talk to some chick to do his job. They need people who actually gonna do their job and not these losers. If you come here be prepared to show your ID several times. The karaoke part was cool and drinks were decent but the people working here outside the bartenders are horrible.

By far the best burger in Nashville and I've been to about every burger joint in the city.  They recently added several smaller menu items such as shrimp/chicken tacos, smaller plates, etc...everything they make is great.  It's the best value for food and drinks I've seen in the city.

We go there all the time; its a laid back atmosphere with good beer on tap, great food, and very friendly staff.  The Sunday Brunch burger is the best burger I've ever eaten.

I had the saucer dipster which was pretty good. The only bad thing was the service. We had an hour for lunch and that is about how long it took for us to get our food. Nice looking place, too bad I didn't get to try any of the beers.
Bad, very bad ... Music was great but don't eat there. Screwed up/ mixed up all the orders. My dog would not eat this stuff.

Had an amazing time and experience with my team at B.B. Kings. We were searing quickly and the live music was amazing! Our server Devonté was outstanding and made our experience great. Highly recommended

I wanted a place with good food and good beer for our first meal in Nashville. I was not disappointed!

My friend and I both ordered some local beers that are escaping me currently, but they were good, I promise. I got the Turkey Meltdown, and she ordered the Kick Ass Chicken. The food was super solid, and the desserts looked amazing - even though I did not eat any. 

The place itself is spacious and comfortable. There's a sunroom area with couches and tables when you walk in. The main bar area has a lot of low and high top tables, some of which are communal tables. The bar is large. The servers were knowledgable about the beer - they had like 12 on tap at least. 

There were specials as well on various days and happy hours. Good place, cute location. Not right on the Broadway strip, but good location.
Rudest bartender I have ever met. Honestly this is the first review I have ever written and it is only bc of how awful the staff was to us. From the bartender to the condescending DJ. Do NOT go here.

If it wasn't for Yelp and similar word-of-mouth, I don't know how people would find this place. The name "Back Alley Diner" is appropriate as it's really down an otherwise dark alley with very little signage or notification. Hidden, would be appropriate. But the Yelp reviews were good and it was close to where I was walking near the Capitol (do check out the Capitol) and so here we were.

Seat yourself and I took a comfy booth and was able to get signed on to the wifi before my waitress came by for my order. A local beer (Yazoo) and a cheeseburger with cole slaw were on the way a few moments later.

Beer was nice and cold. Burger was cooked medium with a good amount of blue cheese. The cole slaw was plain and unremarkable. But the burger rescued and "A-OK" to a "Yay! I'm a fan!".

Neat little place with karaoke some nights and plenty of regulars at the bar. I can see coming back to it one day.
Bad service. Could not get a beer. Bartender treated me really poorly. But great music

So this got the 4 stars mearly because of the ambiance. When I went it took too long to get a table, but the entertainment was very talented. Their music made for a great atmosphere. My ribs were good and the coleslaw was great, but I thought it was overpriced for what it was. Considering the cover charge I wasn't loving the overall cost of the night but it was my first time in Nashville and I wanted an experience. I got it!

The show is absolutely amazing, but, the restrooms smell absolutely awful! They are the worst smelling public restrooms I have ever seen since I went to China. They smell awful even though they don't look filthy.

Hint: Get some Clorox or Pine Sol and wash the restrooms! There is no excuse for that as much as they charge for tickets.

I did appreciate the full bar inside the theatre, they sell mixed drink doubles and they pour them strong so you only need to buy one!

Andy Warhol said, "Being good in business is the most fascinating kind of art. Making money is art and working is art and good business is the best art." Third Man Records celebrates art in various forms...What a cool experience. Jess was extremely helpful and knowledgeable. We will stop in again...
Awesome beer selection. A bit on the pricey side. Food is quite good. Fee to park there. Overall a great place to have a beer but would be better with a patio.
Had apps and drinks with friends...great atmosphere with extensive draught beer choices.  Staff is friendly and efficient. Appetizers were excellent.  Wonderful place to meet up and hang out!

In Nashville for a night, and we needed a place to grab a few drinks and dinner. This place was recommended to us because we're both beer drinkers and would prefer to be somewhere less touristy.

We sat at the bar and each had a couple of beers. The draft list is extensive and diverse. It also features some great local breweries.

We shared a soft pretzel as an appetizer, which was good enough, though the bartender told us it was microwaved. Yay. My husbanded ordered a sandwich that also was pretty obviously microwaved based on how quickly they brought it out to him. 

If you come here, stick with the beer and skip the food.

A tale of two joints.  Friday night (7/15) we had a great experience.  Paid a reasonable cover, listened to fantastic music, got great service, and had a good time.  So much so, that when we were looking for someplace to finish the next night off with food, we headed back.  First surprise was the 400% increase in the cover charge.  Gladly paid it, because we were looking forward to good entertainment and food.  After 30 minutes, it was clear the the entertainment was up to snuff, but the service was absent.  I went to the hostess to let her know that we hadn't been waited on yet.  She essentially failed to respond.  I returned to my table in the hopes the lack of service W would be corrected.  No joy.  We left without being handed a menu.   Even after complaining on the way out, we were met with indifference.  To add insult to injury, the party of six that came in 15 minutes after us (for whom we helped move chairs and tables) were served before we left.  $40 lesson learned I guess.  Boo.

Good food at an affordable price. Definitely a hole -in-the-wall type place with a chill atmosphere and great service. I was especially happy to order the fruit cup and actually find good fruit other than all melons. Highly recommend checking this out for a laid back night.
Delicious very strong cocktails, mezcal shots (when they can find it) charming service and a beautiful crowd.  Couldn't and wouldn't ask for more.

Good bartenders, tasty beverages for a enjoyable day and great live music all for a good price. I wish they had a pool table but they do have plenty of other fun games and things to do while you enjoy a good Saturday out of the house.
Great food, great service, great drink specials. Love love love. I highly recommend the shepherds pie, mashed potatoes amazing.

We came to Dan McGuinness this afternoon on a whim, looking for a nice place with an outdoor patio to grab some lunch.  This simple Irish pub did not disappoint!  We were here on a Sunday, so there was no live music or rowdiness from the crowd, which was just fine by us (we participated in a Pedal Tavern tour the night before and were looking for something greasy to ease our hangovers--loud music was not what we wanted at all).  

My fiance ordered the fish and chips and I chose the cobb salad.  Both of us were very happy with the freshness of our food; my salad was full and hearty, topped with lots of grilled chicken and veggies, and his fish and chips were hot, crispy and very fresh.  We shared bites of each and, of everything we ate, the french fries were my favorite part.  They were thick cut and perfectly cooked, topped with just the right amount of seasoning salt.

Our server was kind and attentive, answering our questions about the menu, refilling our drinks without us asking, and making sure we were comfortable and happy with our dining experience.  Prices for our meals were more than reasonable and the menu had lots of options for traditional Americanized Irish pub fare, healthy salads, soups and burgers.

Reading other reviews about Dan McGuinness', we probably wouldn't come here for a night out, but for a delicious lunch on a spacious outdoor patio, we'd be back in a heartbeat!

Tons of character. And a few characters! Biggest tap selection I've ever seen but the stouts are mostly high gravity. Needs external building refresh. When we rode up elevator from the parking lot it was clear that the elevator is used to transport the trash. Yuck!
It's history. Beautiful and nostalgic. We didn't make the tour inside, but the outside was better than nothing.
We went on a guided tour, and had a great time.  We were able to see all the 'behind the scenes' and were impressed by our tour guide's knowledge and personability.  Would highly recommend!

Had a great time at the Opry. All these years didn't realize it was a radio show with ads and all lol. 4 groups of entertainment with 3 songwriters or groups in each segment. 2.5 hours long so each did around 2 songs. Vince Gill, Montgomery Gentry, Lee Greenwood were some of the performers. Acoustics excellent and the drinks around 7$ to 9$. Easy to get in and seating was on the large size, good for us oversize folks lol. Overall had a great time.

After the reviews I was excited to try the place out...not any more.   The only thing that tasted even remotely fresh were the bacon wrapped stuffed peppers.  Everything else came straight from the freezer.

Im from Miami so my standards are pretty high.  Although a bit smallish, the club itself is well designed and looks very nice.  The service is good and staff are very well dressed.  For Nashville, it is excellent, but compared to what Im used to its just ok. Not because of the club itself or the music, but the problem is that the crowd is the same old boring type Nashville people.  Not much the club can do about that.  I also felt very safe since there seemed to be bouncers at every corner, and the tables are absolutely beautiful and are similar to some SoBe restaurants. Very cute. I will be back, although I will likely travel to Atlanta when I want a truly exciting nightlife.

If you can appreciate the history and music... GO! I've read other reviews where the person complained because of the 'random' singer they didn't know, but that's part of the fun. Old timey singers that tell a little story and sing a song or two. We went when very recent and popular singers were there, but still scattered in between were older singers. We chose to do the backstage preshow tour, and it was so worth it. If you choose the tour right before the show you'll witness all the hubbub and stirring before the show.  We saw some not so famous singers and musicians getting ready. We got to see Clint Black and Miranda Lambert's instruments waiting for their arrival. Yes, this is a "when in Rome" or "Bucket List" item that you should do if visiting Nashville.

The relatively subdued lower level bar is more comfortable for us than the hectic See and Be Seen bar in the front main room . The lower bar is in a smaller room down some steps anchored by a modest stage of rough old wood. Tippler offers dedicated cocktails for Nashville, different from the original Manhattan lounge. But I was impressed with their fine classic martini with two generous dashes of orange bitters stirred into some fine dry vermouth and gin. And the bartender squeezed the oil from the lemon peel into the drink carefully, in a way that was more than perfunctory; no olive. About the decor, Nashville is literally not literary in the New York City style so it was amusing to see a set of Dickens and of World Book on prominent display. But better that than the cheap glitz in certain local bars.
I fell in love as I went thru the backstage tour and relived all my childhood dreams. Great place to be and learn about the experience of legendary musicians as Opry members.

For a Saturday I expected it to be crowded but something was up with the karaoke set up. The songs kept cutting out and there was no flow to the singers. I don't know. I've been to way better bars and could not have gotten any service from a bartender. We left real quick.

Wow. Going to the Mother Church was absolutely a one in a lifetime experience. I booked our tickets 3-4 months ago for the evening of our 11 year anniversary. They were $95 each and we got third row for the 92nd anniversary of the Opry. I paid an extra $40 or so for a celebration package they mentioned is during the show and we got a gift bag with goodies worth about $15- I would not opt to do that part again. We picked up a souvenir poster for $12 that had the date and line up.

I was not familiar with most of the artists or songs but it was still a great time. I wish I had known about all the food trucks on site- it would have been really convenient to just go there to eat while picking up tickets from will call next time we will for sure grab food there. They do serve beer, wine and snacks- but concessions sold through the Opry are speedy.

I will absolutely go back next time we go to Nashville.

Came here on recommendation and of course had an amazing time. It has an air of magic to it, and we came for the show... whcih is a unique experience every time!

There were legends, newbies, and people who are huge right now, all at once, and they cycled through 3-4 songs each, keeping the music diversified and exciting. We stepped into the very crowded gift shop for intermission, and we pleased to find it wasn't too overpriced. We were able to get a few souvenirs we feel really good about for ourselves and as gifts for our fellow country lovers (okay, my dad.)

We had an amazing time, loved the proximity to the mall so we could catch dinner ahead of time, and felt like it was just the right length of time that we weren't exhausted afterwards :)

Just a helluva place for vinyl geeks.  Friendly folks, bizarre/quirky items up for grabs, a dadgum instant record recording studio.  Full of weirdo Jack White vibes everywhere--which is a great thing.

Stumbled across this place while looking for a place to get drinks near Vanderbilt hospital. Great atmosphere!! There was live music the night we went, and the performers were amazing. Perfect place to unwind after a long day.

This is a must-see venue. It has deep longtime traditional roots. The acts are very entertaining. The ticket prices are reasonable. The facility is large, but the views are good from any seat. They also have several large screens to help with close-up views. The acoustics is very good. The atmosphere is fun. In my opinion, everyone needs to have the Grand Ole Opry on their bucket list and should take an effort to check it off of the list.

Excellent beer menu!! Tried quite a few awesome beers. Would gladly go back just for that reason alone! Great service too. Just took away a star because of food. Some of our party ordered burgers that were beyond over cooked and dry. My turkey burger was great, but they weren't pleased at all. Don't recall the server asking how they wanted them cooked either though (yet twice dead and bone dry should never just be assumed, let alone executed!). Nonetheless, excellent atmosphere and place. We spent quite a few hours here watching football and enjoying so great beers. Would gladly go back and will!! Just not to have a beef burger that is.

Stumbled upon Back Alley Diner (aka BAD) after visiting the Nashville State Museum.  It's a nice hole-in-the-wallish looking place in an alley.  You wouldn't come across it unless you were looking for it.  Anyway, I got the pulled pork sandwich with bbq sauce with fries.  I had no complaints.  I didn't think the pulled pork was greasy or fatty or anything.  The bbq sauce came on the side, so I was able to put as much or as little as I wanted.  The fries were crispy, just how I like them!  

This is a no frills restaurant.  Not fancy, nice people, and straight to the point.  I wouldn't make a point to go back if I were in Nashville because there are a lot of other restaurants I'd like to try, but I have no complaints!

What can you say about the GOO...? History and nostalgia do count for some things and they count when it comes to the GOO. Obviously, a tourist attraction but so much fun (even if you're not a country music fan) and one of the things that should be on anyone's list when you visit Nashville.

As a vinyl junkie record collector I just had to stop here on my trip to Nashville. We arrived early to get a ticket for the tour but there was a line already so we came back later and luckily they added on another tour. 

We loved the tour, our tour guide was friendly and loved her job. It was like walking through a non creepy version of "Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory." And just like the Oompa Loompas everyone behind the scenes had uniforms to wear.  And they all seemed like they enjoyed working there.  

For the record store there was a great selection of Third Man vinyl and merchandise from the white stripes days too.  

Any fan of vinyl should make a point to stop here.

visited during live music and the place was slow at first. ya know what they say though - find a band and a bartender that you like and stay - we did! Tara was an awesome bartender and the band was super enthusiastic and fun! stayed for hours before venturing next door shortly after our bartender did... fantastic time!

Awesome place!  We've been to the Detroit location as well and love them both!  I was able to get some really nice & rare vinyl records and the staff couldn't have been more helpful and pleasant to work with. 

There's lots of cool merch to buy, artwork to see, recordings to listen to, people from all around the world to talk to and a palpable buzz and creative vibe in the air. 

Take the studio tour if you're able but it books up QUICK!  They took us through the creative process, areas, technical gear, art department, lunch lounge, performance spaces and merchandise warehouse, etc.  We even saw some pre-release materials and masters from some of the bests artists you have and haven't heard of!

My highest recommendation goes to Third Man Records for many reasons. Support the Art and the Artists and we'll all be better off!
Amazing food. I recommend Chicken Fried Chicken w/Mac & Cheese. Best meal I've had in awhile.
Quick lunch spot. Buffalo wrap www pretty good, but the coleslaw was drowned in sauce.

Great service today by Alexus and the food was fantastic. We had an array of foods. Kids tenders and Mac'n Cheese, 2 burgers, brisket, and chic/ribs combo. All were an A+. They had some lunch music that we enjoyed, as well.  We would all go back again.
I love this spot. So much that I barfed on my friends Ruggy and Vince.

I love Jack White and his music! This is such a wonderful, fun, all around fantastic place and his love for music shines here. I could have spent all day just looking as it was most inspirational. The only downside was the staff, all of whom were luke warm at best.

This was my first time in Nashville. I was excited to try some southern Barbq but when I arrived and looked around at other people's plates, the food seemed generic so I went with their Barbq burger to be safe. It was good. But most of all the atmosphere was what won me over. The BB king band sounded amazing and the guest singers too. I even had to get up and dance at one point... And I was by myself (in town for work)! I only deducted a star bc the drinks weren't very tasty.

Had lunch here and the service was good. Table needed cleaned as someone didn't wipe it down when bused. Tomato basil soup very good, bourbon burger was excellent, a must have. Very slow as hardly anyone in the restaurant and unlike most of Nashville they didn't have live entertainment until later in the afternoon. I think the rest of this town starts their live music at the crack of dawn lol yeah Music City

Bought last minute tickets to Paramore here. I was walking in expecting to be disappointed at the seats that we got because there weren't many options to choose from. To my surprise, we had really good seats! Seriously!!! I don't think there are any "bad" seats in this venue. I wish all of my favorite bands played at the Grand Ole Opry House.

It's the Grand Ole Opry. I didn't even like country music when I went but country has evolved so much that some of the artists you catch here could really surprise you. I saw Sara Darling when I went and thought she was pretty great. The seats are comfy and over the two hours you're there, you get to see a bunch of different artists. I thought it was really fun, I'm warming up to country, and I'd defnitely go again.

Moe the bartender was very helpful.  This is a great place to go off the main strip to enjoy a good collection of beer.  We had a few different great beers and would definitely come back next time we are in town!

Every time my husband and I pass through Nashville, we make it a point to stop here. I love this staple of our Nashville tradition. For our anniversary (6 years this past Wednesday!) we made our way to Nashville to enjoy each other and the beautiful sounds of this city. So of course, last night we chose BB King's to soothe our ears. This was the best time we have ever had there! The band was the greatest that we had ever heard. The girl's voice was phenomenal. I'd come back every night just to listen to her. Never get rid of this band! Absolutely amazing. Thank you, BB King's, for making our anniversary the best one to date.

The Grand Ole Opry is absolutely beautiful. This stunning and historic building boasts top name country acts as well as seasoned county vets. Every seat in the house in a good one. It's small enough to where you can see the stage well from everywhere. It's air conditioned and very clean and comfortable. The staff is also really friendly and jumped in to offer to take our pictures and show us to our seats. 

Buy your tickets early to ensure a spot. The only downside to purchasing early is that you don't know who is performing. We went to a show where we didn't know a single person performing. But even then, it was still really fun and enjoyable. 

The show is split into two halves. Each one is an hour and has a different host. Each performance is quick. They only perform about two to three songs per person. This keeps the pace of the show moving really quickly. 

If you're lucky, you could catch a big name act here. But even if not, come and enjoy the history of the opry.

This place has lots and lots of beers, and I love beer! I only wish I had more time to explore the offerings on this trip. Flying Saucer has great atmosphere, the servers are really good at what they do and are very friendly. We tried lots of the food on the menu, and it was all good. Our favorite bar food was the nachos...one of the best we've had in recent memory!

Decent food for an Irish Pub. I have come here multiple times for football and soccer games, and it is a great atmosphere for soccer. The service is attentive and friendly and provides good recommendations for beers.

It seems that the crowd at night is primarily college-aged students, and the back patio turns into a dance floor.

I was stoked to go inside and listen to live music at BB Kings, the $5 charge was no surprise, but how often do we see a BB Kings.  Of all the drinks listed, I was craving a mojito, and the waitress advised they were able to use the last of their mint for one last mojito - phew.  I ordered the fried catfish, and it was fried perfectly with tender flakes...no fishy taste whatsoever.  My husband ordered the brisket, and it melts in your mouth.  Sound system at this place is outstanding, the female vocalist got everyone out of their seats.  The dance floor is big and spacious, everyone was having a good 'ole time!

A wonderful show and venue.  I really liked the variety of old time and contemporary Country music.  Country artists are so dedicated to their craft.  

If the Grand Ole Opry is your only music destination in Nashville, then I would do a backstage tour, however the same at the Ryman Auditorium is far superior. (The tour at the Grand was short and rushed.  If I were rating for separately, I'd give it a 3)

For first time visitors, I recommend listening on line or SiriusXM to get a "warm-up".

First time here and went for St Patty's weekend! The shepherds pie was so good and my husband couldn't shut up about his reuben. The beer selection was great and we ended up meeting some people and were accommodated no questions asked. Our server, Ashley, was awesome, she sat down and talked with us as if we were already friends, great experience all around.

Not impressed at all. We had to pay a five dollar cover charge because of the entertainment. The food was mediocre at best and I had to return my potatoes because they were cold. 

I believe a restroom in an establishment tells you a lot about the cleanliness of the facility. The restrooms were horrid. I do not recommend this restaurant and I will not return.
Back again. Another great show. Sat in the front row of the balcony again. Continues to be a must-do when I'm in Nashville.

I came here partly just to see the big circle. Getting to stand on it during the backstage tour was one of the coolest things I've ever gotten to do. My tour guide was wonderful and informative. Getting to see the dressing rooms, the plaques, the back rooms, and the stage from the artists' point of view was amazing. I love the intros they had at the beginning of the tour. I wish I had been able to see the show that night but I will definitely be back.

Happened by the flying saucer recently on a trivia night with some work colleagues.  The trivia was impossible, the food and drinks A-OK.  Service was great.  It was standing room only so get there early.  I dont think I have been in here for about 10 years,nothing has changed apart from the girls uniforms which are a little more conservative.  Hey in the old days when there was not much choice in Nashville the Saucer was one of the places to go and we loved it.  Its a good pitstop if you are out and about touristing it up.

For those who need a short review- do not bother with this restaurant.
For those others that want the drama that unfolded this evening- please keep reading. I purchased a Groupon for this restaurant today with the plan that we would visit this evening before the weekend started. I have been a server before and know that taking care of tables with coupons can be a hassle. However, having said that, I know how to take care of my server monetarily regardless of what the ticket looks like. After we sat down, it took quite a while for our waitress to come back and take our order.We ordered an appetizer in addition to the two entrees and beer flight that our Groupon included. While the bartender is pouring our beers, he is loudly bitching to our waitress and another client about "coupon people". The conversation continues for close to 5 minutes about us only 5 feet away! Then our entrees arrive before our appetizer because according to the waitress, she forgot. In order to be fair, our burgers were ok. However, our "specialty fries" were a let down. My "stadium" cheese fries had cheese from a jar poured on them and my husband's parmesan fries had the commercial, green container parmesan sprinkled on them. The appetizer, when it arrived, was another poor representation of this restaurant. Then, to top it off, the beer was... "off". I am a huge fan of our local brewery, Yazoo. However, when we tasted that in addition to some other unknown brews, I couldn't finish my Dos Perros. My guess is that they haven't cleaned their taps or their lines in a long time, therefore, giving the beer an undesirable flavor/finish. By the time our meal ended, I was furious and in the process of leaving a scathing note for the bartender, however, my husband dissuaded me saying "Don't even bother... this place won't be open in two months". Hopefully, I have given you a clear picture of your potential meal. 

-Natasha

Location: I love street parking..when there's no meter. I hate dumping my change purse out, but I promised to meet a friend here at 3 and the meters still tik till 5. I love the area, but damn I wish parking was better.

Environment: I've seen Belcourt Taps advertised and based off their website, I'm imagining a young and fun original restaurant. When I got there, the place is very original, but I felt like I was in the backwoods of Wilson County. I live in Mount Juliet, so I like going "into town" (if you will) to get away. When I arrived, there was absolutely no one there, and the server was chilling with her grandchild, a couple of months old. Our drinks were served in a red solo cup (minus beer). Their performance stage is extremely small, which some could call intimate but I would call inconvenient if I were to be there at night. Maybe my timing had to do with it. Okay, so my timing had everything to do with it. Goes to show, no matter what city you're in, 3:00 on a Monday is going to be dead as a door knob (besides Fido's). The actual look of the restaurant is cute and country vintage looking.

Food: I got a house salad and the Hangover. I felt the house salad, which was $6, was a bit much for just lettuce, onions, and cheese. The Hangover was so excellent! I really did enjoy the bourbon onions on the salad and was happy they were on the burger. I've had a food truck's stuffed burger once and it was so sloppy that the cheese came out like juice. Belcourt Tap's was perfect, enough flavor and no messiness. Granted, it's a HUGE burger, it is kind of messy, just not the same. The pretzel bun is amazing and made it easy for me to eat in 4's (hope that makes sense). Fries were awesome too! I felt like the $12 for the Hangover was worth it.

Service: Despite having to take care of her grandson while working, our server was awesome. She was always on point with things and never missed anything. 

Overall the food was great, and if I came back, it would definitely be for the food, but probably not for anything else. Well, besides the service :)

Easy to purchase tickets online, even the day before...midweek.  A mammoth room but you don't feel like you're one of 2000 people.  Big screens all over the room.  Great speaker system.  Padded bench seating with backs (like church pews).  They are really organized.  Easy in and out for the show.  Worst part....mall parking was miserable.  It was packed driving in and driving out.

Only visited a few times for "Fish & Chips," and an Old Fashioned. The fish fry was hot and flaky but not overdone, the batter had a delicate texture and delicious flavor; the best I have had in Nashville. Great fries, a wonderful tatar sauce.
They know how to get an Old Fashioned right. Enjoyable. For Fish I would say it is $$$.

A very cool, quirky, off-beat and trendy vinyl shop. I loved the White Stripes and I love everything Jack White does, which was the main reason I visited the store front. What he is doing for music and vinyl promotion is amazing. Check out his CBS Morning and Dan Rather interviews. I expected it to be an overpriced record store and was delightfully surprised that everything from the trinkets, t-shirts to the vinyl was reasonably marked. This is a great place for Third Man Records artist items and just a great place to put on your tour of Nashville list. The performing monkey machine is pretty cool along with the old recording booth. They also have live events at TMR.

Also, if you ever get to see Jack White in concert--he is worth every cent! I saw him perform in Nashville with special guest Loretta Lynn and it was the best concert that I have ever been to by far.

Great beer list, solid food. I was a big fan of the make your own flight to really have a chance to experience the different beers they had on the menu. Being that I'm not from town, I rolled through the selections of local rotating taps. Our waitress was really great at providing some direction and I actually think I ended up liking what she suggested better than what I picked myself. For food, I shared a pizza and a goat cheese salad. The solid was a fair sized portion but exactly what one would expected if you poured together some lettuce, goat cheese, onions, and walnuts from their plastic bags at the grocery store.

I'm writing this because of the reply Ms. Kelli's put on my first review and I am not able to reply to her. She replied two months after I posted my review and said we had to wait for her to unlock the doors in the freezing cold due to a car accident "last night" and that was a lie. It was two months ago. Everyone was inside standing around and she was refusing to unlock the door and refusing to wait on us when we got inside. She also said I post a lot of negative reviews which is also a lie. I post mostly five star reviews and actually don't like leaving a negative review except for when I think people should know about it. So just know that this place is rude, obnoxious and ungrateful. To call me a nitpicker is completely unprofessional and no legitimately run business that appreciates their customers would do this. If you say you open at 8pm and you are inside with all your staff then open at 8pm instead of watching your customers stand outside in the freezing cold. If you are a karaoke place and you have ten people wanting to sing then don't make them sit there and listen to your DJ hog the show for an hour before they can sing. If you are wasted you will probably have fun here or anywhere else. But if you are alert and aware you will see how rude they are. It's typical situation where they have so many tourists coming that they can get away with being arrogant because there will always be a new batch of people coming. Just read the other one star reviews.

I went here for the first time today. I was under-impressed. I ordered a to-go plate over the phone and the lady who took my order had an above average personality. I chose the Fork & Knife burger with fries. I opted out of the Monday lunch special because... chili burger with sauteed onions. :-P. I was given 15 minutes for my order to be ready. 

I work downtown, so I thought I'd work off half the bun calories by walking. Stopped in the parking garage, then made it to to B.A.D. about 20 minutes after I called. My order wasn't ready. It took about 30 minutes for the burger to come out.

I made it back to my office and... there's this burger that looks just like the description of the original burger with a small smidge of bland chili and soooo many unsauteed onions!!! LOL, I was too hungry to walk back. But boy is that annoying. I could have gotten the $6 deal and added chili instead of paying $11 for the F&K burger.

That being said, although the chili was bland and the onions were raw, the burger meat itself was flavored well. The fries were good. But the burger didn't meet my expectations. I won't rush back to try anything else.
Had a great Sunday brunch, fabulous cocktails..the gin mule is highly recommended.great good and atmosphere
It is a neat location. Decent food. Wasn't overly impressed. We came durning lunch-the smell from the entrance to checkout was terrible. I was underwhelmed by the taste of the food.

Anthem is the go-to venue for any nightlife enthusiast,multi level club with top notch DJ's and mixologist. VIP is the perfect place for a more relaxed, private ambiance, offering a bird's eye view of the Main Floor. They play EDM, Hip-Hop, R&B, and Pop music. 
It's the best place to come for all of you new to Nashville, and not into the country scene.
I always have a great time!

Overrated is about all I can say.  Vince Gill played 2 songs, Little Big Town played 2 songs.  You sit through 2 1/2 hours of old timers and hosts trying to be funny, not to mention all the advertisements.  Once we left at the end of the show we spent more time leaving the parking lot than the top 2 headliner acts combined.  Really, 2 songs from the headliners?  Drinks are $9 dollars each.....really?

Great little spot, was doing a road trip from Rochester down to Key West and this was the dinner spot when we reached Nashville. Good service, good food (not amazing blow your mind delight, but currently living in NYC I can vouch for the fish and the burgers being above my expectations). Reasonably priced drinks (was rather funny hearing a few folks complain about a 5 dollar margarita...). I will definitely be coming back!

Thought a visit to Nashville would not be complete without a concert at this iconic spot. But I was wrong.

This isn't the original site of the Grand Ole Opry and besides the pew type bench seats (which were surprisingly comfortable), this is really like any music venue.

We saw an afternoon performance and it was only about half full and just OK. The singer was clearly just rehashing his former, 20 year ago hits and the crowd almost looked asleep. Really--no energy at all

So unless you are going to hear a beloved performer, skip this and go to a little venue instead. The ambiance and vibe will be better.

Finally saw a show here and one word - amazing!

Found out Garth was returning home so we were able to snag 2 tickets to the late night Saturday show.  Little did I know my tickets were on the floor and close up honestly every seat in that place isn't bad.  Its such a wonderful experience to hear someone perform in that auditorium because its like a personal show.

Definitely something we will never forget!

This is probably my favorite bar we went to in Nashville. From the service, to the atmosphere, to the food, it was all top notch. We had just arrived in the city and were walking around the area taking in the sights. We were hungry and stumbled upon the Flying Saucer. I saw that it got good reviews on Yelp, but didn't really know what to expect. Nearly every table was filled, and as we walked to find a seat, I looked at what people had ordered. The soft pretzels immediately caught my eye. We found a comfy couch to sit on and a waitress came by right away to offer us drinks and let us know about happy hour specials. I went for the raspberries and cream brew fusion and it was awesome. I want to make them at home now! We ordered the pretzels I had been eying, the spinach-artichoke dip, and the tater tots. Everything was good, but the pretzels were definitely the best. A while later, we decided to try their brats, and they were great, too. We expected to grab a quick bite, but enjoyed the place so much that we ended up staying for several hours. I highly recommend stopping in when you're in Nashville!

Arrived around 9:00 had to move to a different table. The one we were seated at was filthy. Local brew (Yazoo Dos Peros )was flat. Our server was not attentive. Probably wanted to get out of there faster than us. Talked to the manager he was more concerned with flat beer than cleanliness. All in all it was a bust. Stay in printers alley if ya want to hear the blues

GO!!!! That's all I can say!!!

To see a show and do the backstage tour was around $150 for 2 people. I think this was the best $150 we spent on our trip. The show was a lot of fun. The tour was great. I feel like I have an even bigger appreciation for the Opry and country music after visiting.

Definitely checked this off my bucket list with my wife! If your anywhere in the area you should go. There was people from Canada, England, and all over the states. It's a very clean, nice, respectful, historic establishment that will leave you looking at Country music even better than before!

A typical chain store selections, atmosphere and crowd....but it's Nashville TN, there is live music,  fun service, the food products are good ,just not special. 
No real draw other than name and entertainment seems more our style. 
Had chicken wings, catfish nuggets, collar greens, tomato soup, and fried pickles. ..
I'd order them again...

We were visiting Nashville for New Years so needless to say, downtown was packed. My boyfriend loves craft beer so we found this place walking distance from downtown, but far enough away to not have the crowds that the downtown bars do. It has a great atmosphere to drink and have conversations. I'm not a big beer drinker but even I was able to find something I enjoyed on their extensive menu. We will definitely be going back next time we are in town!
The food was awesome!!!!!! Love the hot German potato salad ... Yum  service was great! Totally worth the visit ..

I love Nashville's booming restaurant scene and was eager to give Music City Tippler a try. Unfortunately, it was a disappointment.  

I think if you're going here to go to a bar, you might think it's good.  If you're coming here to eat, you'll probably be frustrated.  The problem is, Music City Tippler is trying to be both, but it doesn't quite have the restaurant part down very well.  

Before being seated, we did order drinks from the bar, and those were well made and quick.  So it seemed like things were off to a good start.  Sadly, that was the best part of our experience. 

First, the menu options are woefully limited, overpriced, and not very appetizing. If you look at the entrees, you have a grand total of six options to choose from.  My shrimp tacos were pretty average.  It was food and that's about the most I can say about it.  My companions had the Cornucopia of vegetables and the Roasted half chicken.  The vegetable plate looked like someone just dumped and spread grilled vegetables on a plate. No presentation or arrangement at all.  And hardly worth the $19 cost.  The roasted half chicken looked a little better, but the person eating it said it was just average.  The only stand out dish was the mac and cheese, which did taste great and had a nice presentation in its own iron pan. But if you're looking for a great dining experience, look elsewhere.

Now for the service.  It was both apathetic and confused.  Our server was about the least personable server I've ever experienced.  We might as well have given our order to the intercom at a drive thru.  Literally, it seemed like our server had had botox injections all over her face.  No smile, no eye contact, no enthusiasm at all, not even a question like "Is this your first time here"?  No, just "are you ready to order?"  

In the hour we were there, our server came to the table only three times not including bringing us our checks.  I ordered a beer that I didn't realize came in a can.  The server did not bring a glass and did not ask if I wanted one.  I waited to see if she'd come around again to ask for a glass, but after ten minutes and no checking on us, I just grabbed one from the next table.  

Another word on the service and the training of the staff.  This is unusual for sure, but when I sat down, my seat was wet.  I swapped for another nearby seat.  Then as our server was pouring water, she spilled water from the pitcher (some of it on me) and made no apology.  She just kept on going like she didn't even notice she'd spilled it.  Incredibly, another employee later came to fill our water glasses and AGAIN spilled water and ice on the floor by our table.  At least this guy acknowledged it and apologized. 

At one point, another server came to our table and asked if we wanted to order a drink from her, but we all declined as we already had drinks.  I'm not sure what that was about.  This same server later came to our table and asked if we had ordered any drinks from her?  Really?  Don't you know? 

Lastly, I need to mention that the music was turned up so loud I could barely hear my dining companions sitting two feet away.  No one wants a dining experience like that.  The decor feels like a fine dining establishment, the deafening music feels like a nightclub.  As I said, if you're going for the bar, you might like this.  The decor and layout is impressive and that's probably the best thing I can say about Music City Tippler.  It looks great.  The food and service need serious work. 

Decor = 5 stars.
Food = 2 stars.
Service = 1 star.

I went here with my parents on a Wednesday afternoon while spending the day in the city. There was no wait to be seated and there was a lot of seating available, either at a table or at the bar. A live band usually comes to play in the evening, but there was none here at the time. There were pretty great happy hour specials, with some mixed drinks half priced, and beer buy one get one free (only for select drinks, and beer to only include Yuengling and Coors). I was interested in the pasta dish, but prepared without the meat and vegetables, but the dish is "premade" and that couldn't be done. It was a little disappointing, as there weren't really many vegetarian options, so I ordered two sides of the Mac and cheese and the garlic bread. The garlic bread tasted more like toast, and I'm fairly certain there was no garlic on it, but the Mac and cheese was actually very, very good and cheesy. I asked for a few cups of parmesan cheese to put on it but they only brought me one. My father and sister had the meatloaf, which was really good, resembled a "Salisbury steak," but was probably a bit more salty than we're used to, and the vegetables that came with it were really good. My mother had a salad with fruit which she really enjoyed. She also ordered a cosmopolitan to drink, which wasn't on special, but they applied the special to the drink anyway which was was really nice. There was public wifi but it didn't seem to be functioning today. So overall, good food, OK service, but with an extensive menu, not much flexibility with the items to accommodate to special dietary needs. I'd possibly return if in the area for the Mac and cheese, but only if I wasn't absolutely starving since it is only a side dish option.
So frigging cool! How neat is it that you get to play with EVERYTHING in this place?! Including a GRAMMY! Thank you, Jack!

Tremendous Venue.  Great party.  Very good music.  Even the food and beverages was pretty good here.  The atmosphere is outstanding,  Great energy with good people.  The venue itself is tucked away from the bright lights on Broadway but down the side street of 2nd Ave.    Great entertainment place to have some laid back fun.  Nice stage, multiple bars.  Definitely will check out again when visiting.

Grade: B
Worst place for a bachelorette party - don't come here! They do not care about their guests. The food takes forever! The management, Lacie, gives zero shits.

I have to say Maddie/Maddy has the worst attitude Ive ever encountered in a bar. Was at DawgHouse this weekend and yes it was very busy, but she had the most disgusted look about her with everything. The other girls were great so we moved to their areas. If I was the only one thinking this, I wouldnt write a review. I overheard at least 5 or 6 people complaining as well. She really shouldnt work in a service industry where we are tipping her for her service. Management really needs to have a long discussion with her!
T-o
I-nsure
P-roper
S-ervice

$20.00 to enter the door (4 people) no problem yet. Get to the very back bar where my family sit down to enjoy a drink for my brother in laws birthday. 3 of us order a basic dirty vodka martini and 1 has a miller lite with a fire ball shot. At no point did anyone ask for a double nor Ketel One top shelf. 1st round of drink on me youngest brother $71.04 without tip.What a rip off / tourist trap and I'm here locally from Franklin, Tennessee. Needless to say we cancelled our dinner reservacation and left. What a rip off $48.00 for 3 martini's when I could have purchased 2 handles of vodka for less........

Ate dinner and Attended the New Years party


Firstly, my party was caught off guard with a prefixed menu that contained no prices. Nowhere on the website was a prefixed menu mentioned. With only three options to choose from it was still difficult choosing what to eat because the waiter knew nothing about the menu. It seemed like the only words he knew were "I don't know". So, through my own personal experimentation, I found that the only appetizer worth getting is the pork belly. Entrees were poor; steaks weren't cooked to order and the bouillabaisse contained clams that weren't even open. With a meal that wasn't fit to serve a guinea pig, the bill still came out to be $110 per person.  

Now, the New Years event was even worse. They promised a live DJ and a burlesque show starting at 9pm. They stuffed people in the Tippler like cattle with little room to move around and the music didn't even start until 10pm, but only the people that paid an additional $140 could hear him. The speakers didn't turn on in the main floor until 10:30pm. Even then, the speakers flickered off and on intermittently. The Tippler's event planning and execution was absolutely horrible, nothing about this "party" was done properly. We could only view most of the burlesque show through a tv because the stage was in the vip section (also not mentioned). After midnight, everyone left just as confused and angry as myself looking for another bar that could possibly salvage this ruined New Year's Day.

Our waiter was nice and the band was amazing but it took way too long for us to get our food. After asking multiple times about where our food was, our waiter finally explained that the kitchen lost our ticket. Overall, it took over an hour and a half to get our food. While the music and atmosphere was awesome, the food and service was disappointing.
The music was great and the music was great!! Trey was a great server as well!! Anytime in Nashville come check this spot out!!!!!

I'm usually not a fan of chain bars, but Flying Saucer is an exception to that rule.  In all honesty, I didn't know it was a chain when I arrived, but upon sitting down and seeing the names of all of the cities were other Flying Saucers are located, I figured it out.   But the place is just really cool, and had a nice laid back feel --- this isn't Hoolihans or Fridays --- unlike those type of chains, Flying Saucer makes you feel like it is a true local hangout.   There is even a separate room with pool tables. Very nice.

Flying Saucer makes you feel so comfortable that I definitely wanted to stay for the experience.

They have a very nice menu and a beer selection to die for.  As others have said they must have 100 to 150 beers available to choose from.  I also like that the put a focus on local brews, so I tried the Yazoo which I had never heard of before.  It was pretty good.

The menu is typical pub fare with some twists.  My girlfriend ordered the pretzels and they were excellent.  They came with this German spicy yellow mustard that was straight out of the best German restaurants I have ever eaten at.  I really hadn't expected that.   If I had know, I would have ordered one of their brat specials.  Instead I had ordered their French Dip --- No problem, it wasn't disappointed. 

In all I loved my Flying Saucer experience ---- if there was one located in New Jersey, I would definitely be a regular.
Came to Nashville on a personal trip for the first time and ate at BB Kings. Very clean, food was good, and had a fun time. Next time we are back in Nashville we will be back!

Terrible service and didn't make it past the hostess.  We had reservations for a large group (6 adults and 7 children) and when we arrived the hostess was very rude to my wife and said we had to wait an hour.  My friend called the Brazillian steakhouse a few doors down and they accommodated us right away and we were blown away by the excellent food and great service (ask for Ren!)!   To be fair, the manager apologized and was working to accommodate us but it was too late!

I'm not the biggest country fan but I was entertained the entire time! beautiful venue & fast moving shows. was never bored & loved the history behind this place! everyone was SO friendly! made me appreciate music on a whole new level

I'm super loyal to Lipstick Lounge for Nashville karaoke, but thus isn't a bad option if you're downtown and get the itch to belt one out. We stopped in after the art crawl on a cold night out and both the crowd and the bar were warm and inviting. Good mix if talent levels and genres and the man running the show was super nice. Solid bar service and a good selection of beers on tap.

Sorry but this gonna be short and sweet. I stumbled on this place while out hiking around. It's part of the franchise. I didn't eat here so I got no comm. The artist solo act was pretty good   I will assume if you come for the music you won't be disappointed.

I'm probably biased because this is home of the Nashville Spurs - Tottenham Hotspur supporters group and I happened to be a Tottenham fan. I'm not going to knock a bar which hosts a Spurs supporters group. Haven't eaten there but the bartenders are friendly along with a good selection of beer on tap.
Absolutely amazing! Burgers are thick patties and cooked perfectly medium-well. They don't just slap together your food either. My food looked just as good as it tasted!

Place has a nice homey feel but that is as good as it gets.  Bar tender was extremely inattentive despite the lack of customers.  Took 15 minutes and asking twice to get water.  Took forever to get my food ordered and then the food was mediocre and not even what I ordered. And there were billing issues.... Never going back

A tremendous waste of money and time, for a mere $54 for two people to waste an hour on the tour.  To be fair the tour guides are happy and animated and truly excited about their jobs. Only to walk down vacant halls into a warehouse space so one could look (don't touch) at the entrance where the "stars" enter to find out they too must go through security just like we did is boring. Looking into the dressing rooms (don't touch) of spoiled, pampered entertainers is less than exciting, and to be able to view a few props and ultimately stand in the coveted "circle" to have ones picture take which you may purchase for a paltry sum of $25 extra and then have to exit through the gift shop is a masterful piece of marketing, especially since the Grand Ole Opry tour has so little to offer. Do not waste your time, go to the Ryman Auditorium in downtown Nashville to see the real history of the Grand Ole Opry.
Service is understaffed. 20+ min for 1st drink order, second round came 1+ hr later. Don't come here for food unless you want to spend 4 hrs hear

We were here a couple of months ago, and I just realized in all my Nashvillian reviews I neglected to do one on the Opry. We saw Vince Gill and Pam Tillis as the headliners that night as well as going on the backstage tour. The show was great, I really had no idea what to expect, as my grandma is really into country music, and I'm not-so-much. My grandma adored all the older acts, and my sister and I got a kick out of the younger ones. Vince Gill was amazing, even for someone who knows very little of his work outside of his 1990s Christmas album. Pam was funny, and a great show host as well. She did a nice job of keeping her segment moving, and even gave a shout out to MinneSOta because her piano player was from here! My only complaint is with the pews. I totally get the church vibe is intended (I had toured the Ryman earlier that day) but they really pack you in close. There's very limited leg room, and not a whole lot of seat room, either. It makes it pretty uncomfortable for anyone taller than 5'2" and weighing more than a buck20.

The backstage tour was super informative, but I don't know that I'd want to do it after the evening's show again because we didn't end up getting outta there until nearly 11 pm and granny was pretty tired by then.
Stopped in for lunch and had a fantastic "German Plate" which consisted of lean and flavorful brats, sauerkraut , potato salad... All fantastic!

I expected this place, based on the name (BAD...seriously?) and the location (down a dark alley between buildings) to be a shizhole.  Newsflash: its NOT.  I walked in and went immediately bug-eyed.  A real diner in Nashville?!  With local art, exposed brick, and chalkboards announcing specials every day including the weekends??  And live music??  And TVs for watching March Madness??  I could not stop smiling.  We are talking some of the best prices in town for great bar food.  Their burgers are good, and that's even with the beef being seasoned, something I am not really a fan of.  They have a special on their delicious wings on Saturdays as well as PBR.  They make amazing bloody marys and mimosas that are way more champagne than OJ.  Despite the name, its clean and cozy inside, way too nice for a place called BAD.  Its so far off the beatn path and yet you are smack dab in the middle of downtown.  Its awesome.  I loved it.  I am a huge fan of BAD food, BAD drinks, BAD service...it was wonderful :) Highly recommend it for some adventurous fun.
Overall amazing experience. Highly recommend. Even the commercial breaks were highly entertaining.

In Nashville from Florida...Just had dinner at Flying Saucer and was totally impressed. The staff is extremely friendly and on top of keeping drinks filled. The food was amazing!! They messed up my order but fixed right away and credited our check. The manager personally checked on us several times and brought out my order after fixing mistake. We are in Nashville all weekend and will be going back for more amazing food. Hubby loved all the different beers offered.. Definitely a must to stop by to have a speciality beer, lunch/dinner, and relax in the cool environment!!!

This is one of the worst, possibly the worst, restaurant I've ever been to. Literally inedible. The pulled pork was the driest meat I've ever tasted in my life. It was like eating tree bark. Tasteless, inedible. Texas toast wasn't toasted. Hush puppies were so dry they turned to dust when I bit into one. Literal dust. The "tarter sauce" tasted like mayonnaise. I think I saw a minuscule piece of pickle in there, but by and large it was just mayo. Burgers were all cooked to the consistency of shoe leather -- shriveled dry hockey pucks of meat (we asked for medium). Cole slaw consisted of large dry squares of cabbage with chipotle flavoring sprinkled on. Ever gnaw on a chunk of dry cabbage? Super gross. To add insult to injury, they gave the meal of one member of our party to another table. We were done eating by the time she received her meal. 

One star for the fresh fruit cup. If you like grapes, this is the restaurant for you.

I love the flying saucer- and I come here everytime I go to Nashville! They have the best pretzels I've ever had. We love it so much that we had our after party here after our wedding. the GM, Kacey, even kept the whole place open (even the kitchen!) an extra hour so we could party with our friends eating pretzels and drinking beer after our wedding. The staff was attentive, and the quality of the beer/food is always there. We'll be back!
I'll go back for the service, atmosphere and live music but will eat before I go. If you just need a late night snack, the food wasn't awful but just not the meal worthy quality we like.

The food is good, the beer selections are better! The servers are always on it and making sure you are ok. I enjoy going in and looking at all the regalia and wishing I could drink that much beer. Enough beer to join a club! I've been here a few times during their days where they have specials and it's always a good time.
I have to say, the girls today at DawgHouse, AMAZING!  thank you Abby and Jules for being the best bartenders in the city.

We spent a wonderful evening here! The show was amazing and everyone in my group had an awesome time. We saw Lee Greenwood, Roy Clark,  Mel Tillis, Jimmy Wayne, etc. etc. Such fun! So many of the songs had personal connections for my group of five,  such as "Cincinnati,  Ohio"  where we all went to high school together, and "Proud to be an American," one of our generation's all-time favorites. I especially enjoyed Jimmy Wayne's song about foster children since I had just seen him recently at a conference in Grapevine, TX. Ran right to the gift shop after the show to purchase his CD.

Just like my first flying saucer in Raleigh NC, the decor, the taps and even the smell. I have no idea how the place smells exactly like the raleigh location but it does.....not in a bad way.

But this saucer has pool tables, and a really nice outdoor porch/patio!

Service was great as always, beer selection was awesome too! They had a good local selection which is what I decided on, yazoo for their hefeweizen and pale. Great choice on both!

My experience was on a Saturday afternoon, not too busy with plenty of room at the bar and tables. It's nice to have a beer place like the saucer you can count on to feel like home even when you aren't there. And considering the whole reason my girlfriend and I picked our apartment when we lived in raleigh was because of the saucer makes it even better.

Anytime I'm in a city that has one I'll be sure and stop in for a beer.....or three!

While cool and theory, and with an amazing building and good graphic design, Third Man is nothing but a self-made, over-priced museum to Jack White next to the ghetto. $20 for a 45? No. $200 for photographs? No. If you don't worship the ground Jack White walks on, just no.

This is probably one of the coolest non-touristy bars in Nashville. Even though I have a strong love for country music, they don't shove it down your throat here like they do on Broadway. The building it's located in is extravagant - it reminds me of an abandoned Victorian age train station (which there's also an abandoned train right outside.) it's pretty big and spacious inside, with many tables and a lounge area with lots of comfy looking couches. Plastered on every inch of the wall are thousands of saucers, which is really interesting to look at. Especially because many of them are of different places and attractions. 

   The coolest thing about this place is their drink selection. 200 beers to choose from. If you try all 200, you get a saucer with your name on it put on the wall. If you complete this challenge more than once, you'll get a different colored saucer. How. Awesome. Is. That.

  This place is so cool y'all. A great place for a more local vibe.

This was a really fun place for me and my girlfriends to go to. I love to sing anything that comes on the radio. I had only did karaoke once before around 15+ years ago. On songs with multiple people it was a little difficult to figure out who should be singing what, but we still love it. We ran into some very interesting people here, but that is what made it fun. There are some really talented people who sang there, unfortunately my friends and I (along with some British guys) weren't any of them. Hope to do some  practicing and coming back to this place. As far as the rating, drinks were average price, but I wish they were served in glass containers,

I love this place regardless of the fact that I do not get a long with some of the former staff.  I still recommend this bar as the top karaoke joint in all of Nashville!  Great staff, great prices, and great karaoke!

Anyone that's spent time in a pub in Ireland is immediately suspicious of Irish bars in the US due to the lack of smoke stains on the walls and in their lungs.  That aromatic haze in the air is absent in most American Irish pubs and we seem to subconsciously dock them for it, "how dare you pretend to not give me cancer???" 

Dan McGuinness is a badass Irish bar, no two ways about it.  The walls that aren't covered in stained wood are crafted from actual stone, and they boast the usual accoutrement of Irish whiskeys (Tully, Breast, Jamies, etc) and also a very decent assortment of ales, including a house ale (contracted out, not brewed by the establishment) that makes for a fantastic Irish-style red session brew -- highly recommended!

They have TVs for watching sports, just not an *obnoxious* number of TVs haha - this is an extra star for sure :-)

The bathrooms are clean, the patio smoking area is expansive with its own bar and TVs or whatever, and in general the service is just great.  I would recommend this bar without hesitation, and if the food is up to snuff they will be soaking in another Yelp star as well.

Came in for drinks and found out that they have an amazing craft beer select. Came back the next day for lunch. Mostly sandwich and a good selection of apps.

The pretzels were good and was plenty for 3 of us. I had the chicken sandwich and added jalapeños and it was also good.

Kind of a German Beer Hall vibe but a fun place that we'll definitely go back to when we're back in town.

Awesome draft selection with tons of local and national craft beers.  Great food. Very cool open atmosphere in the dining room. $5 parking for the Predators game with a short 2 block walk over the Bridgestone. Service could have been a little quicker but it was understandable with the amount of volume they were dealing with with it being right before a game.  Overall a great experience, we will be back!

This bar is amazing. The music is fantastic. But the main reason I came back to spend my entire Saturday downtown was because of the bartender Steve! It's like getting a show with your drink and he pours them quicker and more accurately than any other bartender there! I will definitely recommend people visit just because of my experience with Steve!

To me, this is a step in the right direction, inviting Nashville to diversify it's venues. As far as similar decent club experiences go, there is only South and Seen, so this is a step up in the classy/trendy club direction. I hope others follow suit and up the ante so they all improve.
