Anyway, I've been here 3 times, twice for shows and once at the end of a night. It's usually the same clubby environment, with loud music, primarily house. I really like the music, so it works for me. I've also actually tried their food, since I didn't have dinner before going out one of the nights, and it's not bad actually. Sure, it's a bit pricey, but nothing too bad considering you're in a CLUB. 

The music is pretty great as well, assuming you like the genre. Definitely something energetic to dance to, and with good transition to keep people going. It's also really interesting how they divide up the space, with a top and bottom floor, and a small bar area with different music that's almost sound isolated so that you can talk even if there is a crazy show going on 10 feet away. I like.

Overall, this place is pretty great as far as Nashville goes - sure, it doesn't come close to clubs in the other major cities (Miami, NYC, LA), but it is a step in the right direction. Kudos.
Good food. Fun atmosphere! Loved their house band! Suggest seeing them if you want some classic blues!

Not a good experience at all.  Service was less than OK but not quite bad. More of an "eh" experience.  The food was over priced and portions were tiny.  I had the chicken Caesar Salad - it had about 1oz of chicken on it and not quite enough dressing.  Others a the table had the salmon - it was just OK  and the cheese steak - it looked like a Mcgriddle.  We left the restaurant and went to the Palm for drinks and a bite to eat. 

The bar design and setup was kick ass!!! 

We will wait till the menu catches up with the architecture to return!

A great small venue with great food...burgers, BBQ and pizzas.  Awesome venue for listening to some of Nashville best singers/songwriters.  A must stop when visiting Nashville.  Entertainment nightly.  Not many tourist but you are sure to meet some fun locals.  Nice patio out front as well!

$26 for adults & $21 for kids 4+ (I think), pricey for this short tour but interesting to see the backstage dressing rooms & hear some interesting little facts. They take your photo onstage with the Grand Ole Opry sign behind you (FYI, it'll be $20+ additional cost).

Took the tour of Grand Old Opry.  It was overpriced at $25.00 for 45 minutes, poorly organized and forgettable.  The constantly repeating video made it difficult to hear the tour guide.  This is definitely not a must-see stop in Nashville,  Go to the Ryman and the Country Music Museum instead and save your money.
Polite service, nice selection of beers on tap, awesome sweet potato fries, fun cozy college bar atmosphere. We were very satisfied.
Wonderful! Went before a comedy show. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants to listen to live music and enjoy the pretty good food.

Hidden little gem, hard to locate but great little joint. Local craft beer on tap. I had the black bean corn burger and house made chips, it really hit the spot. Hubby had a turkey burger and fries. Better than chain restaurants! Great service.

I had a chance to go to BB King's with my wife and we enjoyed ourselves! I was not too hungry so I got a cup of Beer Chili and Crawfish poppers (appetizer) she had the pulled pork sandwich with sweet potato fries. We both came to the conclusion that our food was OK. Not great definitely not bad just pretty good/ok. There was a local trio performing they were really good and apparently they perform there often. They were really good. Our waiter was in and out sometimes there sometimes no where to be found. I would go back here I love music and I realize this place is what it is. I think they try to have great food but it doesn't the food is just good/ok (THE FOOD WAS NOT BAD just nothing great) but what they lack in food they make up for it in music. I would definitely go back but temper you expectations with the food. Music A+. We enjoyed ourselves.

This bar was needed and it's obvious that other agree with me because the times that I've been there, it's been packed. The age group seems to be young professionals, mid-late 20's to 30's. 

I love nice cocktails but the whole "excuse me while I go grow a lemon tree" thing grates me. Tippler manages to turn out quality drinks, fast. We visited when it was slammed and I pulled out the "make me something with Fernet" card and they delivered, fast. To me that is the definition of a good cocktail bar: quality concoctions that don't take all night to mix.

This place is a lot of fun but you do have to get over the karaoke guy being a total jerk. He didn't totally ruin it but is definitely a mean guy. Just don't ask him about how many people in front of you, and if you don't want people to go ahead of you in line, give him a bigger tip. He yelled at me for asking when I was up, (people that signed up after me went in front of me, but I still asked very nicely) and then said that others gave him a $20 tip so they got ahead. It was pretty crazy actually, I did not expect him to be so mean I was simply asking. It might be a soup nazi kind of thing, have to ask in a certain way or he will yell at you I don't know. The bartender girl is awesome (and a talented singer too!) but that guy was just so mean.
The bar tender shook a drink all over me. I'm pretty sure she was dunker than I was. The place was nasty and the service was horrible. Skip this crappy hole in the wall and head to Lipstick Lounge.

In town & always in search of local brew. If you're from out of town, you must come to the Flying Saucer!

Like:
Blackstone Blacklist Barista Brew (stout from TN)
Blue Velvet (brew fusion: cider + stout + port) very unique!
Many stout selections
Ambiance - decorated with plates containing the names of winners of beer challenge. Beautiful!
The Bratzel!

Wish:
There was a Flying Saucer back home!

A must see for anyone living in or visiting Nashville!  I am not even a fan of country music, but the building and the tour was fun and very interesting.  It is only around a hour and costs $20, but you learn and see a lot in that time and it was fun!
This was my favorite thing that we did in Nashville. The show was amazing & the Opry is beautiful.

My husband and I ended up coming back here a few times during our trip to Nashville for this year's CMA Fest. 

We first came up from the riverfront to cool off and have a bite to eat between sets, but when we arrived and saw the extensiveness of the beer menu, we caved.

Being from out of town, we tried a couple different local beer, of which they had plenty on tap. After our first two pints, we decided to opt for the "Flights" instead - a sampler of five 5 oz. beer that you could either order from their menu, or build yourself.

During our first visit, we got the rocket tots and hummus and pita as an appetizer. The rocket tots were piping hot - deep fried and filled with jalapeños and cheese, and the pita for the hummus appetizer was super warm, soft and fresh. I ordered the grilled chicken breast and greens. The portion was hearty, but I found the chicken and bacon a little overdone and dry. Otherwise, the ingredients were  good and the dressing came on the side, which was nice since I always find my salads end up swimming in dressing. 

During our second visit, we came strictly for the beer, and during our third visit we opted to try their much acclaimed soft pretzels, which were incredible, not too salty and still super fresh even at 11:30 p.m. (considering the NYC pretzels I'm accustomed to [read: hard as concrete and more salt than pretzel - this was astonishing to me). By our third visit, we had tried a good selection of their on-tap beers, having ordered the Hops 101 Flight, Local Flight and U.S.A. Flight. We even ended up choosing favorites from our selections.

The restaurant itself has a great vibe. It's comfortable and inviting, with huge picnic tables and couches in the sunroom area where we spent our time. There are also plenty of tables inside the main bar area. I can't forget to mention the pristine bathroom conditions and amazing service we received, especially considering the insanity of CMA Fest week, since thousands of people flood downtown Nashville, requiring many restaurants to have their waitstaff work 12-15 hour days for four days straight.

This place is cool. Laid back for as crowded as Broadway gets.  My daughter couldn't recall if she ordered onion rings and our server was like no worries, we'll get you some on the house. 
Really friendly. 
Thanks Ellen, Matt, and Cate. 
The food and drinks were great.

Amazing atmosphere! We were looking for something just a little different. Great Blues bands playing. Wonderful service, our bartender was Jasmine and she was wonderful and so personable! We will definitely be back.

Wow I have to tell you this towns food is out of this world. And the service continues to blow me away. Here is the thing that is nuts tonight was the lowest tab and the best night of all. If you come to Nashville and don't make it to B. B. Kings you will have missed out.

Finally got around to come here last month, after having heard that it was great from several friends. Actually came here as a part of a HUGE group, (40ish) with a lot of coworkers. It was a great environment to talk and eat, but at the same time listen to the music played live, which I'm happy to say was not country.... definitely a nice change of pace from the usual downtown places in Nashville. 

Anywho, I ordered a dish, I forget what it was called, but it was essentially a large serving of macaroni and cheese with a tasty fried piece of chicken. Now that sounds pretty simple, but some friends suggested it, and MAN am I glad they did. The macaroni and cheese has this delicious non-standard flavor, maybe since it was white (not yellow) and appeared to be made with different cheeses.... Eithery way, it was tasty, as was the chicken, which despite being fried and crunchy on the outside, it was juicy and tender on the inside. 

Overall, this place is awesome for large parties, can be a nice relaxing environment or social, and its refreshing to have a popular place in downtown Nashville that plays blues instead of country music. Would come back.
We really liked this place! Although our server wasn't the greatest, I had one of the best burgers here. Cozy, interesting, classy, moderately priced...I highly recommend.

Came here tonight because the schedule said the house and was performing and I have heard great things. Was disappointed when he club decided to try a new band. Not the caliber of a blues band I would expect. Food was your run of the average chain produced food. Service was great.

We had a group of 12 and were there on a Tuesday night. Service was slow, our server Mary was inattentive and frustrated about our requests for drinks other than beer. She actually bordered on rude. The food was average at best. I had grilled cheese and tomato bisque and honestly Campbell's soup is better. Lower your expectations before going.

Pleasant atmosphere, okay food. It's just glorified bar food (nothing wrong with that), but it was not priced like bar food. The waiter was trying his hardest to upsell some stuff we didn't want. I understand, it was lunch and quite slow, but you will not create repeat customers by being pushy. Long time customers are what sustain businesses, of which we will not be. First and last time visiting this establishment. Sorry restaurant, just being honest.

Ah, the Saucer.

There's no better place for a bite and a beer. 

With over 200 something beers, you'll never be at a loss to try something new! 

Trying them all gets you about $3,000 in the hole, but a fabulous plate (saucer) on the ceiling to brag about for years to come! 

Get the warm pretzel appetizer, play some darts and have a blast!
Atmosphere and service (katelyn) was good. My husband enjoyed his open fish sandwich, but the portobello sandwich was just okay. Fries and ranch dressing were eh- not worth the fat grams.

Great burger with blue cheese completely melted. All the fries were crunchy and amazing. Eli was a good waiter and he said the fries were fried twice. Staff seem to have a really good working relationship. Prices are reasonable. Since I was from out of town, I had to wander around until I found the Back Alley Diner, but it was worth it. I will eat there again tomorrow before I head home.
The service is great, the atmosphere is fantastic, and there are more beers than you ever knew existed. Try the pretzels, they're the best you'll ever have.
Awesome choice! Great food at a great price. Really friendly and Fun staff. Richard was great and helpful. 5 stars!

Food was better than what we expected! Pulled pork was fresh and flavorful. It melted in your mouth and fell apart easily. Ribs literally fell off the bone and had just the right amount of sauce. Their chopped salad with chicken was great for a lunch meal. The chicken was freshly made and not frozen. Drinks were ok and service was a bit slow that's the only reason I'm giving a 4 out of 5.

the bar was almost empty when I got there and yet it took almost 15 minutes to get served. The waitress didn't know the drink menu and the food was horrible. 

I never plan to go back

I expected better because there were decent word of mouth reviews...
We tipped them to jump on the list and one hour later, not even called to sing. Nashville tourists, there are plenty other karaoke bars that honor a good tip. Skip this one.

Wow.  What a find.  On our way back from the Honky Tonks, we stopped in here after a peek inside Union Station Hotel ( so cool ),  There are like 70 beers on tap - a huge list of local and national and imported beer.  And while a large garage with 70 draft beers might be nice, this place is so cool - in converted train boarding areas - lots of wood and plates on the walls and ceilings.  Very relaxed atmosphere.  I will certainly be back.
Awesome pub great food good service . They made an amazing Black and Tan  it was Halloween so all were in costumes . Great sports coverage as well

I honestly have no clue how I have been in Nashville for so long and never been here.  I have always heard people talk about it and just never made the time to come until last night on a Monday night.  The Pint Night special on Monday is great! A huge selection of draft craft beer for $3 a pint. The pretzels with dipping sauces were AMAZING! I loved the atmosphere here too. Definitely a cool place.  The service was great too.  The place was busy, but our server was very attentive and super helpful with narrowing down all of the choices. Will definitely be back here especially on Monday nights!

Devonte was awesome!! He was extremely friendly and knowledgeable. Not only that but he was patient and helpful, as we needed 3 separate checks and separate drink checks for a work trip. I had the Brisket Sandwich and fried pickles and I would highly recommend both! Their drinks were great and the live blues did not disappoint to say the least. Just an amazing place overall.

We moved to Nashville about 4 months ago and have checked out many bars and restaurants in the area since moving here. We checked out this place on a whim. It was quite the discovery! There was live music when we walked in (that was very good) and the place was filled. We sat at the bar and were served promptly. After we'd been there a little bit, the owner of the bar came over and talked to us for awhile. She was so kind and welcoming! 

The place has character and a warm feel - we'll be back for sure! Favorite bar find so far.

The Saucer usually gets listed as one of the better establishments for craft beer in Nashville. Located in the former Train cargo station. The building has a nice feel to it. Inside on all the walls are plates or saucers, thus the name. It seems if you pay $18,00 to join the beer club, and then spend  $1,500-$2000 for beer, they will mount your plate on the wall. Great marketing idea, not sure if it is a good spend.
Anyways, they offer a good selection of craft beers.
The food was ok. Better beer.

I was in Nashville for work.  This diner was recommended by the hotel. It was with in walking distance from the hotel which was great.  The restaurant had a fun atmosphere and friendly staff. I was dining for lunch and ordered the BBQ sandwich.  Sandwich was ok. Not something I would recommend. Looks like this place would be much better for dinner. Next time I am in town I will try it out for dinner.

Anthem is extremely cramped and makes a major deal out of selling "VIP" tickets. I did not buy VIP tickets but was able to walk up to VIP instantly not knowing where I was going. 

The club promoters and their pals were allowed to dance on the stage while the bouncer pulled others off. In all my years and cities and clubs, I have never experienced something like that. Generally in "edm" it's the fans that are supposed to matter. Not the drug dealing fiending promoters who will phase out in the next 3 months.

My suggestion..considering how expensive the drinks are and how cramped the space is..if you want to keep show kids coming back then change the attitude of this place. 

Don't make the music about the money.

Everything was absolutely amazing.  What a breath of fresh air!  I do enjoy country music. That said, what a nice change of pace to find this gem.  Service and food were absolutely amazing! Entertainment..... OUT OF THIS WORLD TALENTED!  In a city full of overcrowded "honkeytonks" what an INCREDIBLE find.  A must stop on your list of where to go in Nashville!

I enjoyed my experience greatly.  The service was good and the food was fresh. I got the turkey wrap and fries. It was so yummy!  2.50$ happy hour for wine...wowzers! Next time I'm trying the shepards pie. My bf got the prime rib and he said it was excellent.  I enjoyed the atmosphere (6:00ish),  the stain glass ceiling was cool. I'll definitely be back :-)
Pity I didn't get to see this in all its glory as they're currently renovating / extending but this is a must see if you're in Nashville!
Sunday drink specials are awesome, but service is a dart throw - sometimes great, sometimes dreadful.

Did the backstage tour and fell in love!! This place has so much history and such a wonderful friendly staff! You learn so much and get to do things that you never imagined a venue like this would show you! Very wonderful place I highly recommend!

4th row balcony on the side - the good and the bad.  Trying to contribute something meaningful that helps someone. We sat in the 4th row of the balcony, row DD, very close to the front wall. Here are the pros and cons. We were VERY much closer to the stage than the center section which is pretty far back removed from the stage. That was excellent. The trade-off for sitting so close-up is the inability to see the large projection screens on the front wall. Craning your neck to see is possible but only briefly. Still, I'd sit there again. Great seats. Awesome show.

Sadly I waited so long to write a review that I forgot our waiters name. But he was amazing and provided awesome service. Huge beer selection ms they offer great suggestions. Good was terrific and we will definitely come back when we are in town again!
Wow, just what I was looking for. The live band rocked and played a lot of timeless music. Some really cool at work as well. All in all I was very pleased with my visit.

First off the management at this place is ridiculous. We came from out of town and made a reservation for a Sunday night. When we called initially we were told NO COVER CHARGE. When we called to confirm our reservation the same day the girl on the phone was so confused and couldn't really help us. She told us that there might be a cover (even thought we were already told there wouldn't be one), but it wouldn't be more than $2 per person. When we arrived at the restaurant just before our reservation there was a sign that said $5 cover fee per person. Needless to say we were pissed. The amount kept changing and going up, despite being told that we wouldn't have to pay a cover. When we asked the front desk about it they basically told us that if it starts to get busy they can just increase the cover as they please, which is a major rip off, considering their food prices are relatively high. There was also a mix up with our bill and we ended up getting charged for our meal and someone else's, even though they promised they had fixed it. When we went to leave the cover had GONE UP AGAIN. Other than that the food was amazing! We had gumbo, full rack of ribs and some fried pickles. Great portion sizes and amazing flavor. The stuff is a little pricy, but most places in the big city are. The waitress was really nice and super friendly. However, despite the food and friendly service I would not go back because it seems like they just want your money because of the cover charge!
Cool vibe and great music. Come for the music and the drinks. Food is good, but not great.

Enjoyed my visit here. It is in a dark alley, but once you walk in it is full of life. I had the black bean burger and fries and a few cocktails. I enjoyed it all and have found myself thinking about when the next time I can go back!

We live just around the corner and love stumbling into this hidden gem on any night of the week for amazing live music. They don't have an extensive beer list considering their coined name "Taps," but the vibe is consistently great. The staff is social, helpful, and always in good spirits which especially at a bar makes a huge difference. 

I haven't tried any of the food, but the wine is generally good, the people are all really chill and again, GO FOR THE LIVE MUSIC. You will see tons of local singer/songwriters giving their best, especially during nights where they have "writer's round." It's usually 3-4 artists sitting in a row, taking turns singing some of their solo piece. It's a must do!

This places was suuch a pleasant surprise. We were on a day trip from Louisville on a Saturday and were having trouble finding parking downtown. Once we did, this place was down an alley right behind us. Looks a little sketch from outside but don't let it fool you. It's clean, nice and spacious inside. Great music too: nirvana, white stripes, Marcy playground, etc. Server was awesome. Only thing I noted was that I wanted to black bean burger (I'm vegetarian) and they were out. But they had a veggie quesadilla and threw in some fries for free since they were out of the burger. Also was not busy at all for a Saturday night! Not dead either. Also had a full bar. Overall great experience.

Wow! By far my favorite part of the trip. We took the backstage tour of the Opry and wow was it worth every penny. You get to see where the musicians enter, dress, sound check etc. sends chills down your spine thinking famous musicians like Johnny Cash, June Carter, Keith Urban, Loretta Lynn, Carrie Underwood all walked that stage. We were able to walk into the stage and take a picture of the circle that came from the original building. Such an experience and I suggest to any first timer to come to the Opry for a backstage tour and possibly a show if they have time

We've been here several times over several years, and each time has been more unpleasant than the last. Service is consistently poor - last night we were overcharged after a very long wait for our beer, and then the server lost our credit card (it was found but only after s lot of stressful searching on our part). The place is always noisy and parking is problematic. It gets two stars only because they have a wide selection of beer and were open when others were closed.

Fun atmosphere and great bartenders. However, I went to the bar and not to eat, and as a fair warning I went on a Saturday night and the crowd skewed younger as the night went on (early 20-somethings)

Worth your time to go to ! If in Nashville you have to do this show ! However, be careful where you buy your tickets, I got scammed  with all these extra service fees that were tacked on at the very end !! Be careful which site you buy from !!!!

The World Series is on in a bar full of fans and the manger has refused to put on the sound. AND then opening talks crap about us asking him like it was the most horrible request and his job would be so hard if he had to push a button and make his customers happy. It's rude and poor form.  Also the food was disappointing the cheese curds were one giant ball and the salad was like rubber and tasted like chemicals and not only that but they didn't tell us they were out of the mac n cheese until after paying. I would never recommend this place. RUDE.

Everything we have gotten  is good. However the services atrocious. It took more than 20 minutes for a waitress to come five. After that it took another 20 minutes for drinks to arrive. Our lady peed twice since she's been here. Service is terrible. We wish could walk out, but supposedly our meals put on their way

Quick lunch spot, service was decent and food came out fairly quick. I got the hot chicken sandwich which was average. The bread is dry and toasted, but the chicken had too much of a sweet flavor to it. The coleslaw was very bland, even after a ton of pepper to it.  I would go back, but I would stick to a burger.

We decided to stop by Back Alley Bar while we were waiting for a table at a nearby restaurant. It was a good place for a quick beer. Our server was very nice, the drinks were cheap. When we went there wasn't a great vibe, probably because it was a Tuesday night.
The tour is a lot of fun! It's very informational and it gives you a good look at what goes on behind the scenes on the opry! Our tour guide was Bridget; she was awesome!

I wish we could give half stars because I feel like it deserves 3.5 but not a full 4 stars, ya know? This place is tiny! I mean...I knew it would be small but this place is literally a room and a half. You can peek in from the front door and see everything there is to see, do and buy. The parking lot can fit maybe 2 cars? Everything in there is cute though! Overpriced maybe but definitely cute! I love the way records sound and they have those for sale there along with t-shirts and other Jack White memorabilia. The picture machine was broken on the day I went. I was really looking forward to coming here since I moved to Nashville and my visit took all of 10 minutes. It's not a bad place but I guess I expected more.
Great music! Fun dancing... Decent food. SLOW service. Make sure you don't have a tight schedule you won't get out of here in less than 2 hours. They are super polite though.

The Suacer is one of my favorite bars in Nashville. They have an amazing selection of beers and the taps are always rotating. Everytime I got to the Suacer I end up trying something new. They also have a club where if you drink 100 beers they put your name on a plate on a wall and give you a shirt. It's always fun looking at all the plates lining the walls. Oh, and did I mention that the food is pretty good too?
Really like the Flying Saucers. Great beer and the food menu is also good. My only complaint is that the beer list is mostly out of date, so have a few in mind when ordering.

Arguably the coolest business in the country. Call it a record label, record store, music museum, or tourist trap if you must, but do not give it anything other than 5 stars. Absolutely worth a visit every time you're in the area.

Lots of fun watching some talented wannabes and doing sing alongs. Ok service. Never offered food though they supposedly had it. Drinks seemed expensive... The late afternoon and early evening crowd was fun. Around 8 the drunk college kids showed up and were rowdy and obnoxious. We left as did anyone over 30 (we had more than enough to drink). Bathrooms are in an adjoining bar... very weird. I'd go back. It only during the day to avoid the rude crowd.

We were walking back to the hotel after dinner and craving some live music.  Yelp showed us we were very close to BB King's Blues Club.  We had a little difficulty finding the actual entrance, but once in we were golden.

We scored a two top right next to the stage, where the band was already tuning up.  Our waitress got our drinks immediately and recommended the half order of the fried pickle app for snacking.  Perfect.  Drinks were decently priced, large and boozy.

We stayed for the first couple of sets.  Live blues was the perfect end for our first day in Nashville.
Good dogs. I had their Nashville and the BBQ with bacon. The Nashville was to big but the BBQ was great.
Beer selection is very good but not outstanding if you are accustomed to great beer joints. It is what you would expect out of a corporate chain. All in all a good experience and well worth the stop

Dawg House is one of my new favorite places to go on the weekend! I went for the first time on a Saturday night with (around 12:30am) and the place was surprisingly empty. We were unsure as to why, but figured it was a good place to have a drink and check out the place! Drinks were amazing and reasonably priced! Bartenders were friendly and knew the menus well--a few even got out on the dance floor!

The DJ was the best part for me (young guy who is there Friday and Saturday nights until 2am). He played a great variety and had no problem dancing with us on the dance floor. He created a fun atmosphere and I will definitely be back next weekend!

This is a great place right in the heart of Nashville where you can grab a drink and have a good conversation with friends. It's rarely too loud or overcrowded, and the employees are friendly. The drink prices are also some of the best in downtown. If you're looking for a cool low-key place to have some drinks with friends and escape the insanity of broadway, this is your spot.

If you are American, you have to visit this place, even if you don't like country music.  Every seat in the house is great, they really treat guests like guests, and the show is always good; sometimes it's a surprise.  They do a good job of keeping the tradition of country music alive.  

What I loved about this place was how easy it was to get in, and to get out again.  The GOO makes it almost effortless.  

I am not a country music fan, but I loved the tour, I loved the history, and, most of all, I loved the show.  

When in Nashville, find the time to visit the Opry, and be sure to take the tour.

Fun place for lunch! Had tomato soup and grilled cheese and bacon, yummy! The soup was actually a bisque and the sandwich was perfectly grilled. Saucers everywhere along with plates for those that have hit craft beer milestones. Big screen TV's for the sport enthusiast.

Would not recommend. For a place called "taps" beer list was only about 10 beers long. Took 40 minutes to get our food. When it did, fries and burgers were all cold. Burgers were over cooked. "Over easy" egg had completely solid yolk. Was upcharged for the cajun fries and garlic fries when they are literally the frozen fries with a sprinkle of Cajun salt and minced garlic. Food should have been $3-7 range but was $12-20.

I traveled to Nashville recently and was excited to try the Flying Saucer. On my way to the establishment, the cab driver warned me that it's a good place to have a beer but the service wasn't very good. I went despite this and I wish I wouldn't have. Unfortunately, he was absolutely right. The waitress was very rude for starters, never once smiled and acted annoyed and as if she was doing us a favor. My friends pop was very flat and she let out a sigh, walked away before she could even order something in it's place and set it in the bar behind us and continued walking. When she finally came back to our table, my friend wanted to order something else besides water and she said that she couldn't do anything about it and all the pop would be like that. The carrots and celery we had with our meal should have never been served. They were brown and discolored. We asked for new vegetables and the second set of vegetables was the exact same. We all were very disappointed. The only reason I am not giving 1 star is due to the beer selection.
Ordered the burger from Postmates, and it was one of the worst things I've ever eaten in my life. Definitely not worth my $11.

It's a Dive Bar! Get's crowded, Smoking is allowed. My review has nothing to do with that, but I got 3 bud lights and a water, they charged me $65 dollars on my card, and said that's what they had on my tab. I repeated and said, I only had 3 bud lights and a water, this is impossible. They said, all it takes to order on my tab is my name and someone must have ordered. My last name is foreign and very unusual. Plus, that is not how you argue charges to your tab. If that is how you operate your business, you have a lot of room for robbing people, which is what happened to me. I was robbed here by the Bar Tenders.
We were there with a large group (85) and they did a great job. The food was very good and the staff was very attentive to every ones needs. The band playing in the main dinning room was great.

you know, there's times when you just want awesome bar/pub food, and when that time comes, you should go here. 

i've been feeling a bit chubby lately, but that didn't stop me from ordering the "porker burger".  it's a burger with barbecue pork on it. you can also add guacamole to your burger, and whenever guacamole is an option, i take it. 

there's healthy options too, like hummus. so i ordered that to negate the guilty please of this 1,000 calorie barbecue pork burger.

The BBQ chicken sandwich was fantastic. The chicken was cooked beautifully and the sauce was delicious. Price was mid tier. Food came so quickly so it was good for a quick lunch during work. The ambience was delightful. I would definitely come back.

First, you should NEVER have to pay to eat dinner. I don't care if there is a band playing or not. Second, there are way too many tables in such a small area. I will admit the bathroom attendant was great, very nice lady. Our waiter was hard to find. Our bill was wrong. When I told him he said "the item I ring in is the same price" it wasn't. Come to find out the item he rung up wasn't even on the menu anymore. They need to update their system. Their drink prices are expensive and the drinks are watery. We won't be returning. The music was really really loud too.

It's a must see and do when in Nashville!! The tour was awesome and our tour guide was very knowledgeable.. They only complaint i had was I felt rushed while on the tour,but that was due to the fact it was a large tour group and everyone was taking pictures and felt like we were stepping on top of edge other.

I am not a big fan of chains or tourist traps but I was passing through Nashville and was in the mood for some good brisket and some live blues. This place did not disappoint. 

Ordered the brisket entree with baked beans and subbed out the potato salad for the Mac and cheese. While waiting the live music started. Added a nice touch to it. 

When the food came out I almost fell over. Serious slab of brisket. You can see in the pic. About 3/4ths of an inch thick, two strips about 9" long. Covered in BBQ sauce and crispy onion straws. So tender you could fork cut it. The Mac and cheese was creamy and dreamy. Even the baked beans had a good flavor. 

So I have to say I was not disappointed. Good food, plenty of it, reasonable price, great live music. Nice break in the middle of a long road trip.

Definitely go here for the music! There is a cover charge but if you stay for awhile it's worth the entertainment value. We had drinks and BBQ nachos. The drinks were good but the nachos didn't sit well with us. The staff is hard working and friendly.

The worst.

Horrible, horrible experience here. Definitely won't be back and recommend no one else to either. And Stephen, the manager, was very rude to us. 

That said, our server Peter was friendly and did a great job.

I went here on a night out after dinner with my brothers, a friend, and my dad when he came to visit for the weekend. At one point about an hour in, two of us were accidentally standing in the way of the service area. We were politely asked to move by Stephen (manager), to one of 3 areas: the lounge in front, the dance floor, or the balcony area. We told him we didn't know the balcony was open and he told us that it had been a private party but that it was over and we could go to that area.

We went up there and hung out for about 45 minutes with no issues. When 2 friends came to meet us, my brother walked out to meet them, and when he came back in, one of the guys from the private party which was earlier told him in some very strong language to get out. I looked over and saw him being aggressive to my brother and went and asked if there was a problem. He told me we needed to get out and shoved me. At that point, my family and I walked down and I went straight to the manager Stephen and told him what had happened. He ignored me completely.

As we asked for the bill, I told Peter our server what happened and why we were cashing out instead of staying there as planned, and he said to wait while he got the manager because he thought it was unacceptable. Stephen then came back to "help" and was incredibly rude. I told him we were leaving regardless because we were looking for a fun night out and not trouble, but that he needs to be aware I was physically laid hands on by someone from the "private party" after being told by Stephen the area was open.

He asked if I could point out the guy, walked with me upstairs. He introduced me to the security guard and I walked him to the guy that was aggressive to us, who had no problem admitting he had done that. As I told Stephen what happened, he cut me off very rudely and said "I have a giant line outside. Do you not think I'm going to handle this responsibly?" We were told to wait at the front of the balcony because he was going to ask them to leave. We waited and saw that no action was taken. Nobody asked the party to leave, nobody came to apologize to us, nobody did a thing. 

Stephen was incredibly rude, and seemed annoyed that I brought to his attention something that I, having worked in the service industry before, would want to have known. 

There are too many wonderful places in this city to go somewhere with rude patrons, at-best average drinks, and managers who don't take action after a party physically lays hands on a female patron there with her family and seem annoyed to even have it brought to their attention.

Totally classless place that I will definitely try to talk anyone out of going to.

Had to pay to get seated in front of a speaker of the live band- that was 5 feet away from us that literally yelling at my server was having a hard time taking my order. Couldn't talk to anyone else at the table, ran into by everyone else passing by. The food, wow, the food was so bad and over priced that we literally left it and paid our tab and just grabbed pizza down the street. This is just a terrible tourist trap.

Food wasn't bad but wasn't great. The southwest burger had good flavor and the fries were excellent. My wife had the fork and knife burger and boy was that false advertising. It was supposed to be topped with chili. I wouldn't call a spoonful of chili on a burger to be a fork and knife burger. She was able to eat it like a normal burger. Also most chili burgers I've see have mostly meat whereas this had more beans than meat. Finally the service. The waitresses seemed frazzled and were running around. It took a lot of time for us to get just two burgers. If in Nashville I'd suggest finding another local spot.

brought a group there for dinner and they seated us next to the stage.  This was at 5 pm and the music was played at ear shattering volume.  Good music but totally too loud to enjoy.  My real issue is the clueless nature of their management and staff.  When asking for some understanding or at least play some softer music while dining they look at you like your from outer space.  This venue relies on groups and convention work.  Serving a buffett on plastic plates with plastic silverware, playing music on the painfully loud side, and totally unresponsive management gives this place a 0 for future events.  Adding a 21% gratuity was further insulting.  On the same trip we enjoyed jazz venues in New Orleans and Memphis without these issues.  I think a bit of management improvement may be useful.  BTW this was for a group of 50 where I was the host and paid for food and drinks.  If they dont' care about a group of this size think of how they will treat you.

I was visiting from Michigan with my family and I loved it! I like BB King and the live blues music here was pretty amazing! I was happy to see live sports on TV and be served by a very friendly woman! Pulled pork and hush puppies were good! The meatloaf/mashed potatoes/green beans as well! Everybody please try it

Cover charge for band...HORRIBLE!!!!!  We went to a TON of different places in Nashville, & this was the ONLY place that charged us a cover charge for the band before entering.  When he asked for our $10, I thought, "wow...this oughta be good!!!"  Yeah right!!!  The band went on "break" as soon as we sat down.  The bartender said he only allows them a 15 min break maximum.  Yeah right...35 mins later they finally came back. We originally sat at a table, but didn't get any service, so we went & sat at the bar.  Lots of red flags so far.  We ordered the fried green tomatoes appetizer, and they were nothing grand at all.  Forgettable.  My husband ordered their cheeseburger sliders, but they were out so he chose the pulled pork sliders with a side of mac n cheese and I had the bbq chicken.  Sliders were standard, same with the bbq chicken, and the Mac was less than mediocre.  Not much flavor at all.  We walked out of this place irritated & disappointed on many levels and will not recommend this place at all to people traveling to Nashville.  They should be ashamed for charging a cover charge for the band.  How embarrassing.  Guess there not doing very good business & have to rip off the public to make ends meet.
Open Christmas night! Great beer selection. Friendly and accomodating staff-put on our football game and was extremely nice. Fun atmopshere and family friendly.

Super good food! Gumbo is fantastic. I had the chicken and ribs combo, which was just amazing. Great drinks, too. Great atmosphere, especially if you're done with the Honky Tonks. 

The band didn't play blues...so that was a little disappointing, but the food was worth it!

They charge a cover even though we bought a ton of food... Not sure about that one. 

Another plus is that this is one of the few places with live music where kids are allowed, if you have one with you
nice place to visit. nice auditorium.  went for a private party. the food was okay.

The food is AMAZING. I had the buffalo wings and my fiancé had the ribs. Both were out of this world. GREAT music. Staff was kind and quick even though they were slammed. There was an incident with a guy taking his shirt off in the restaurant and the manager quickly handled the situation and made him put his shirt back on. Very impressed with the quality of the staff and food. This will be the first place we visit next time we are in Nashville!!!

The best karaoke bar ever. The lineup wasnt too long of a wait when I came in. The crowd was extremely kind to me during my performance and a lot of people congratulated me after my song! We were able to make some great friendships. Long live "Mr. Brightside"

This is a great place to go if you love German food or are  a beer enthusiast. I was surprised I didn't write a review for this place because not only have I been here a number or times, it is my favorite restaurant/bar combo in Nashville. Whenever I have guests in town I at least take them here once, and they always want to go grab a beer before heading down Broadway at that "beer place." 

My favorite thing on their menu has to be the soft pretzels. Make sure, if you order this you ask for all 4 dipping sauces they offer. I mean who doesn't want the full experience? They have numerous beer combinations that will satisfy anyones palette. I have never had a problem finding a table, but the service can be "hit or miss" sometimes. 

If you are looking for a place to host your next event in Nashville contact Flying Saucer about renting out their party room. As long as you spend a minimum their is no charge for the room. This room is equipped with dart boards, chairs, couches, pool tables, and televisions. I will continue to be a customer of flying saucer, especially since I'm a member of their UFO club.

Absolutely amazing! We took the tour and being able to see the rooms and each room has its own theme was amazing. Being able to be on the stage that all these amazing country artists have performed on was amazing. We even got to see the musicians mailboxes where dan mail can be sent and the artists pick them up there. They also showed us where parts of the show Nashville was filmed. They also educated us in the flood that cause a lot of damage and temporary closure of the Opry. If you love country music, this place is a great place to visit and learn about how much of a role this place takes part in its history!
Mel was amazing! I don't know why you don't have her as a full time bartender! We came all the way from Boston for St. Patty's and enjoyed every minute of it!
We stumbled across an alley sign before a Ryman concert. A bit worried, we wandered down the alley. Such a nice surprise to find good food and good service.

I'm a fan of BB King's Blues Club. I visit every time I'm in Nashville. I can count on hearing great live music. I tend to be in town for business and like to visit BB King's on my first night in town (generally Sunday's) before I head to business meetings Monday morning. Every band I have heard play here has been solid. 

And then there's the food...it's delicious. My favorite appetizer is the fried green tomatoes. The tomatoes are served with herbed cream cheese, strawberry jam and caramelized onion marmalade. They are all delicious. I tend to pile it all on. It's a flavor explosion in my mouth. The sweetness of the jam and onions pairs well with the tart acidity of the green tomato. 

Hands down my favorite entree is the Carolina BBQ Salmon. Wow! The BBQ salmon is served over creamed corn and Andouille sausage, with plump shrimp and crispy onions. It is so yummy!  

I keep meaning to try dessert here but I'm always so full that I don't have room. The desserts on the menu sound yummy. 

The wine list is only so-so. The wait staff are consistently friendly. Because the live music is so loud, this location is not a good choice for an intimate dinner. It can be a challenge to carry on a conversation over the music. However, if your group loves music and good food, BB King's is a great option.

Table of five. Was sat at a table. Waited for 30 minutes, no one acknowledged us. Told the hostess. 10 minutes later no service. I grabbed the manager explained the situation. Just then a server came over. No apology. We ordered. 30 minutes later we get our food. Not good.

This joint is the jam- literally.

Drinks were affordable, crowd was friendly, and 99% of the people on stage sounded like legit professional vocalists.

I'm used to the karaoke bars in California- drunk bachelorette parties belting out horrendous boy band songs incredibly off key.  

WannaB's was a serious talent showcase.  Next time I visit Nash I'll be back for SURE!
The food was really good the band that was playing that night was excellent I love the atmosphere and the location I'll be back again it was just a really great time

Be careful of how you treat people, especially if you are a business owner, because you never know how it could come back to haunt you.

I love when people show you who they really are, especially when their true colors are those of a bigot.  

A friend of mine was in Ms. Kelli's bar the other night and questioned the aggressive behavior of one of the bartenders towards her brother.  Discovering that the aggressive "bartender" was just hanging out behind the bar and didn't even work there, Ms. Kelli intervened and said that it was her bar and she can have anyone behind there that she wants and started hurling derogatory comments to my mild-mannered friend calling her "it" and "him/her" and asking them to be escorted out of her bar.

This is NOT okay.  But you know, now we know.  She might as well put a sign in front of her business identifying herself as a bigot and homophobe.  We are a tight knit community and we have lots and lots of expendable income and guess who WON'T be getting any more of our money??

This place is a dump in more ways than one and correct me if I'm wrong, but isn't it a violation of the TABC to have a non-employee behind the bar?  Especially if they do not have their Alcohol server permit?  Just asking...

This place was mindblowing. SO. MUCH. BEER. I was only there for a couple hours, just having some drinks with friends; but the next time I'm in town, I'll definitely be back. You could easily spend a whole day drinking and never have the same thing twice! I hear the food is good, though I didn't eat. The service was super friendly, but a little slow. The space is huge and spacious (would be great for special events), but a little echo-y. The main complaint I have is the parking situation. But it's worth it! Check it out when you can :)

Easy going atmosphere was nice after a long drive to Nashville. Service was friendly and attentive, at least at the bar where I was sitting. Burger was good but nothing special. Fries were pretty good. 

Music: It was a songwriters night and the music was less than wonderful for the most part. I know there is better talent than that in this town.

I should have looked at other reviews before booking an advance reservation. I'd like to tell you we stayed for the music but we were so offended by the rude service in seating us that we decided to take our business elsewhere. The place was empty as it was still an hour before music was to begin. We were seated at a table BEHIND where the band would be playing. We asked if we could get a better table where we could see the band but were told everything was reserved for larger groups. We then watched as several "walk ins" were given tables directly in front of where the band would be playing. Turns out, they like to fill the prime spots with people who will only be drinking in order to maximize walk in "booze revenues" where they get the greater margins.  This might be the place to go if you only plan to drink and listen but consider somewhere else if you additionally wish to dine. Plan on paying a $10 cover charge, even if dining. By the way, there's plenty of great music at other venues.

Be very careful about reading the fine print when you purchase your tickets. We spent a lot of money and flew people in from out of town to see a show and the big name artist canceled a few days before. As a customer, you have zero recourse and I'm told this happens often. Buyer beware. This is a situation where the Grand Ole Opry likes to remind it's customer "sorry, that's our policy. You are SOL."  

If this happens to you, forget the show and head down to Broadway for some live music. It's a better experience.

The show itself is a bit laughable.  Since it is a radio show they literally announce advertisements after every song. For such a historic and traditional venue, this certainly creates an odd feel. The performers themselves are a medley of country music talent. We had an 88 year old guy perform and also comedic fiddle and banjo band that was very hokey. They also threw in an actual comedian that was reminiscent of the Catskill New York resorts in the early 80's.  

I absolutely love country music but I felt like I was seeing a current day Hee Haw live.
My husband and I are not diehard country enthusiasts but we had such a great time and would come again in the future if our path comes thru Nashville again.
To the ticket agent who helped us get in on the last tour of the day on March 26, 2016, thank you. That meant a lot to my family. I wish I thought to get her name so I could tell her bosses.

House band was best I've ever heard. BBQ tots are awesome. This place is a definitely must visit for out of towners. Uber or Taxi from your hotel or be prepared to pay anywhere from $10 to $40 for parking.  They are kid friendly and will allow them when band plays.

I was walking on 2nd Ave in downtown Nashville and I could swear I heard BB himself. I had to stop in there and I thoroughly enjoyed the show and had dinner with my friend.
There was a cover charge for the band that takes some explaining when you T&E the trips there.
I absolutely enjoyed the venue and the barbeque chicken and ribs were outstanding!!!

I was trying to go to a restaurant down the street, I was on business and they had over a 30 minute wait.  I came to this location instead and was pleasantly surprised. I had some wings which were delicious - crispy and well seasoned.

I follow that up with a bacon cheeseburger sans bun, which was exceptional - well cooked, juicy, great flavor. Service was also excellent at the bar.

Love B B King, the place needs to be playing BB King music, and needs better pa system. Big problem is that there is a photo of Clarence Gatemouth Brown and the artist painted the name Clarence Gatemouth Moore on it. There was a artist named Gatemouth Moore but his first name was not Clarence.  The photo is a picture of Clarence Gatemouth Brown. Damn, some museum.

Blown away by the service at BB King's! Sabrina really took amazing care of our table and helped make it into an incredible evening. 

Hands down one of the best restaurant experiences I've ever had.
Great bar!! Came here for a girls trip, great food, great drinks and great workers! Thank you Key, we'll be back!

We had one night in Nashville and was hoping to get a good taste of the food here. Glad we picked BB King's! The food was great and so filling. The loaded homemade chips were an awesome appetizer to start with, too. We also came during happy hour, so it was 2 for 1 drinks - also a great plus. The waiter was friendly, the blues band was amazing, and overall good vibes all around this place! Definitely recommend this place for a southern cookin' meal!
We got the drinks quickly but waited 50 minutes for the food. We just ended up leaving since we were late for the concert.

They had one server for 20 people On Fat Tuesday. I had to wait for half an hour and remind the server about my drink, only to receive warm flat beer. The server said she forgot and then said they were changing the keg -which is it?
It took forever to get my check. I had to go, so I paid at the bar. I couldn't wait for the server to come back that's for sure. Good luck trying to get the bartender's attention even though he isn't actually doing any work.
I've been there once and that's enough.

I visited Nashville for a conference. A group of us had a lunch reservation for 10 but we ended up being the only people in the restaurant. This is obviously a night time place because the energy and vibe was dead.  

I loved that they have happy hour during lunch time. When in Nashville I guess.  

Although we were the only people, I assumed our food would be delivered quickly.  Most folks had salads and there were a couple bbq sandwiches but it took more than 40 minutes to get our food.  

Food was really good but had to eat it fast in order to get back to the conference on time.  Would love to come back but at night to listen to a band or 2.

The website doesn't specify that if one has dinner there, one can also watch the band play.  Definitely make a reservation though.

NYE weekend, how is it possible they run out of fried pickles, gumbo, salmon, tuna, cornbread, and green beans???????  The waitress informed us 30 minutes after we ordered that they're out of one item, so we had to order something else.  When one entree arrived an hour later, we're informed they're out of something else we ordered.  The ribs were burnt, but I was so hungry I didn't care.  The pulled pork sandwich was cold and bland.  My husband liked their corn and jalapeno fritters.

Great beer selection and happy hour specials.  Whether you are looking for imports, locals, or crafts, they'll have something for your taste.  Never had the food, but it is hard to not like a place with over 200 beers available at any time.

Always a wonderful show, full of talent from young ones to older accomplished artists.  The staff is friendly, which I attribute to the Opry hiring an 'older' more seasoned generation of workers who actually DO care and know about customer service! Amen and may the Opry continue strong for years to come!
Used to go here a lot with people in my department for Trivia. But this place has terrible parking, you either park a mile away or pay 5 bucks.

The good: if you're looking for a dive bar with poor to mediocre food this is your place. Potato chips were amazing though. Food came out super fast. 

Bad: overpriced (not very well made) cocktails, food is poor to mediocre. Pulled pork platter had a disappointingly small serving of meat that was dry and not very flavorful. BBQ sauce was bottled Sweet Baby Rays I think. Grilled cheese wasn't grilled, cheese wasn't even melted. Burgers were average to above average. 

Net: we will not be back.

The service here is always horrible. It doesn't matter how cute you look in a school girl dress- you should be able to manage your tables effectively. I am always underwhelmed by the service. Thank god for the beer selection or I'd never go back.

Have I mentioned that we are not "country fans"?  But we were told that we MUST go to the Grand Ole Opry when in Nashville and we are sort of "When in Rome" people.  It was blast.  This is going to prove what non-country fans we are, but neither of us knew that the GOO (as it is known by its fans) is actually a regular radio show.  The first time the announcer came on with his cheesy radio voice to say, "This segment of the Grand Ole Opry is brought to you by Mrs. Dash's"  We had to stifle our laughter.  

That said, the whole thing was AWESOME.  I left ready to convert and buy myself a sweet-ass pair of cowboy boots.  The musicians were really talented.  The vodka/cran and beer somewhat reasonable, and a perfect length of time.  It isn't too cheap so I'm not sure that I would bring the kids but it sure was a great time.

Decent bar food.
Chicago hot dog, bacon wrapped brat with sauerkraut, sweet potato fry app, and fried artichoke hearts were the foods we chose.
Everything was cooked perfectly, tasted decent, sweet potato fry plate was enormous for $7.
Decently priced, lots of bar stools, lots of tables, lots of space, lots of TV's, good for large young crowds..  
There were only 3 people working the evening I was there and it was pretty crowded..
The three of them handled the bar and the tables and didn't do too badly..

All in all, it's not some place that I would go to every week, but I did enjoy my time there.
Plenty of free parking, across the street on the dirt.

We stopped in with barely 10 minutes before close.. We were coming in from five hours away, in our defense. The girls working there automatically greeted us with a smile and were super accommodating even though they were getting ready to close. The shop is super neat. It's a must see. The staff was super lovely to us and even gave us a couple of coloring books to take home for our kids. Highly recommend this place. I can't wait to return when we have more time. Great first stop in Nashville. Keep up the great work, people do still appreciate great customer service!! Thank you!!

The wife and I made a recent weeklong trip to Tennessee, and we decided to do a nice mix of touristy visits as well as hit the local spots. Since we are both fans of country music, we decided that while in Nashville we would have to do the Grand Ole Opry tour, and I'm really glad we did.
I was glad we called ahead- they offer tours throughout the day, however some days they have big shows and events going on, so it's not every day, and we were able to swing out and join a tour during a Thursday evening. We got the backstage tour, and it was worth every penny.
You see some short videos from country music stars, television stars, and historical musical figures. You walk through the entire backstage area, including dressing rooms, sound stages, mail areas, and more. Our tour guide was very friendly, very informative, and really made the tour enjoyable. Although I'm a country music fan, I never really watched the Grand Ole Opry- I learned a lot on this tour and was amazed at the HISTORY of the building and the stars that have performed there. 
For the finale of the tour, you walk from the backstage area onto the stage itself, and I have to say I was breathless walking through the curtain. To take in the view of the audience seats, and to stop and really think about the LEGENDARY performers that had taken that same walk, I was really moved. Especially standing on the famous circle that came from the Wyman auditorium to the Opry- knowing I was standing on the same piece of wood that Johnny Cash, Garth Brooks, Minnie Pearl and others had shared.... I didn't feel worthy, but it was an amazing moment.
If you're a fan of country music or music in general, this is an absolute must-do. Make sure you call ahead, but take the trip out, especially for the backstage tour. Absolutely worth every penny, it was a lot of fun and very informative. I would definitely come back, and would love to catch a show some time. Definitely worth the trip, especially if you're staying in Nashville!
The food here is awesome (I had the pulled pork sandwich) and Alexandria was a very nice and attentive server! Will definitely come back.

I really liked how HUGE this place was. We went around 10pm on a Saturday night and did not have to wait for drinks. The bartenders and servers were working quickly while giving us knowledgeable suggestions on beverages. I really like the diversified selection and the menu sorted by type of beer. Great TV visibility, would be solid to watch a game here. Would visit again.

I  visited B.B. Kings on Saturday, May 31, 2014. I had a party of 7. I was impressed that they were able to seat my party within 5 minutes without me having a reservation on a crowded Saturday. The atmosphere and decor is very nice. Our server was very attentive. I had a salad and black pea hummus which was filling. Additionally, I enjoyed our appetizer which was  Spinach Dip. My group enjoyed their food, however, it's took around 35 minutes for us to receive our order and the portion sizes were sort of small. Additionally, my guest did not enjoy their cocktails. However, the house band made up for the cons, because they were awesome. They knew how to get a party started. I will definitely be back.
Better than average food.  Really fun bartender.  And the prices weren't jacked up like at some of the other downtown joints.

My boyfriend and I were looking for a place to eat on a Sunday night.  I had tried to look up some "must eat" places in Nashville on Trip Advisor and tons of places were closed.  We ended up finding The Dawg House Saloon by chance as it was very convenient from our hotel.  Immediately, it looked like a popular place for a Sunday night.  Most people were only drinking, but we ordered dinner.  For an appetizer, I had the fried pickles and my boyfriend had wings.  I loved my appetizer and he said the wings were really good (he's pretty particular with his wings so that's a definite plus).  We both ordered burgers- I had a jalapeño burger and my boyfriend had the black and blue burger.  Although I was expecting more kick with my burger, the jalapeño flavor was awesome!  Would definitely recommend this place for a good burger and a place to hang out.  The only reason I gave it 4 stars is because we weren't able to see the live music.  Not sure what time it starts, but we were there until 9:30.

I was hesitant to come back to Taps because of my previous two visits with a lackluster waitress. This time, though, our server Eleazar was so cool and helpful. He even have us 20% off! I've always though the food was delicious, especially the Macho burger, which is stuffed with buffalo chicken and blue cheese. I will definitely be back again thanks to our server today!

Okay. So far the best bar I have found in Nashville. A lot of people my age 20-30ish, great food and the most amazing  beer menu I've seen in a while. This will definitely become a regular place for me to visit on the weekends.

Okay... So I normally don't delve out bad reviews, but this one is going to be one.  I'm giving a two stars for  for the music and atmosphere. BUT THE SERVICE sucks!!!  We were not told about the bar/seating rules when we paid at the front.  So while we waited for our table, we ordered food since they said we had an hour wait till we could be seated.  However, by the time the food came out, our table was ready.  So, then we are informed that our server would possibly be mad at us for ordering at the bar.  ?!?!?!?!?  And mad he was.  From the moment we sat, his first question to us was "Did you order your food at the bar???"  Then, he commenced to give us VERY poor service!  I have NEVER been thus treated.  And possibly will NOT be back.

My husband and I didn't even make it in the door. We walked in and we're told it would be an hour wait and the cover charge was $10. Then the host turned his back on us and continued his conversation. The big problem I have is this was a Monday night and at least half a dozen tables were empty. Disappointing. We loved BB Kings in Memphis.

Great beer selection! This place has something for everyone. Local beers and beers from near and far! Food was tasty with a good selection of Germany fare. The wait staff was knowledgeable, kind and attentive. Seat yourself with a variety of stools, table and couches. Great Sunday funday!

This was my husband and my first trip to Nashville.  My husband is a big blues fan and really wanted to try this place.  It was a Thursday evening around 9:00.  We paid $5 cover charge each-the hostess asked if we were there for dinner or just drinks.  We had already eaten so we were just there to drink and listen to the blues band.  She told us that the tables were all reserved. The place was at least half empty.  We had one drink then decided that we would order an appetizer so that we could sit at one of the tables.  When my husband asked the hostess for a table, she was incredibly rude and turned to walk away without saying anything to him.  When we finally got a table, we waited 15 mins for a waitress to come by and even then didn't get a menu.  Terrible service and extremely slow.  We saw wait staff disappear behind the bar for long periods of time.  I wouldn't waste your time coming here.
Funky atmosphere, fun service, and obviously an insane amount of beer choices! Yummers! A fun place both for locals and visitors.

This is officially my favorite spot in Nashville.  I have been in for dinner, brunch and drinks on several occasions and continue to love it.  

Food is great.  Drinks are great.  Staff is great.   Place is great.

Great.

It's not really a trip to Nashville without a stop at this icon.  The perfect variety music show and I'm really not that big of a country music fan.  Closer is better but try to stay out of the far left and right side both up and down.  If you can't see, there are plenty of screens but too close to the side wall and you can't see any of them.

Stopped in for lunch on Saturday. The brunch menu was a bit limited but the bbq pork was good. They had a bluegrass  band playing and getting us to dance and that was fun. Great atmosphere!  Prices not bad at all.

The Saucer is definitely a place to go in Nashville. I can sit at the bar, look up onto the high walls and see some old friends, friends of my father. Great memories bring old happiness to the new memory being made here. Aside from the nostalgia for one native Nashville girl, there is a plethora of beer. Draft beer, 12oz bottle beer, 22oz bottle beer, beer beer beer :) The food is mighty delicious and the atmosphere is cool and comfortable. Set in the old train station across from The Frist, with reasonable prices and good service, this place is not one to pass up.

I was just disappointed, let me count them down in chronological order.

1.  The website for Belcourt Taps and Tapas does not redirect to their new website, which makes it quite confusing.  My fiancee and I were not aware of the name change/owner change and went expecting tapas... I wish they would at least put up a splash page or something.

2.  Drink order was wrong.  Which regretfully we didn't address with the bartender.  The bartender was odd, paying a lot of attention to the live music but not a lot of attention to his customers.

3.  Then the food.... it was just meh.  The "stuffed burgers" are okay, not much flavor in the meat of the burger.  Also, even though I ordered and paid for truffle fries, I couldn't taste anything different.

Also, who doesn't run a happy hour special on a Sunday night?  I will not be going back.

The backstage tour is a must if you're visiting Nashville.  We absolutely loved it! It was fast passed but not rushed. Our tour guide was fun, light hearted and knowledgeable.  We were given plenty of time to take pictures.  Standing in the place were so many legends stood was amazing. If you miss this tour you really missed out on why the Grand Ole Opry is the heart of country music.

This review is for the behind-the-scenes tour, not a show. I've gone thru the tour twice and enjoyed it both times. The guides are very friendly and seem to enjoy their jobs. It's very interesting to see what things look like in the back areas. Can be busy, with long lines, but they do tours every 15-minutes so it's likely you can get into a group.
Loads of great beer,  delicious food and a relaxing environment.  Love this place! It does get crowded on the weekend and before Predator games so plan accordingly.

Great music venue. The building itself is very nice and they handle the crowds very well. It is very accessible with minimal wait. There is plenty of food and drink available inside with minimal wait as well. The sound and view from our seating area were great.

I try not to be too harsh in my reviews. But man this place was just subpar. The smell was not great when we walked in and the food was all exceptionally underwhelming. The location of the restaurant was the only thing that was appealing. It was right in the middle of downtown and an easy walk to anything. We will not return.

We just went last night and talk about a gorgeous venue inside and out! 2 hours or great entertainment. Whip I'm a self-proclaimed concert connoisseur I have to say this has been one of my favorite venues. Beautiful areas to take photos as well!

Great neighborhood bar and restaurant, if downtown is your neighborhood. Jacobie is a super bartender. The $5 martinis are a great deal and he makes them how I like them. I always get the sautéed veggie quesadillas and they are always good. It's just a really good place to meet, eat and have some laughs.
New awesome bar on Demonbreun- delicious food, a ton of TVs, great live music, great prices on drinks and food- all around awesome place to go- try it out for food or drinks -  I love it!
The food and service was outstanding trey was our waiter and totally took care of us we had a large party and he was all over it

Back Alley Diner is tucked into an alley in the Arcade. Upon entering, one is greeted with interesting art on the walls, live music and plenty of seating options. As this is Nashville, there was live music taking place when we came for an early dinner before 6pm. We selected it based upon its close proximity to TPAC, where we were later seeing a show.

I had the catfish po'boy, which came with two hushpuppies and a side option. Since it's summer swimsuit season, I passed on the fries and onion straws and selected fruit as my side. Wah wah. But, it was delicious and refreshing, consisting of pineapple, grapes and strawberries. The sandwich was comprised of a large filet, lettuce and remoulade. It wasn't New Orleans quality, but we're in Nashville, not New Orleans. It was good and we had very friendly, attentive service.

This is pretty cool! I was even more impressed with how many bar areas and restrooms they have in the building. The lines were short to non-existent and the  restrooms were clean.  I noticed that they also offer an outdoor smoking area on the second floor for those who need to excuse themselves....the gift shop has some cool things to offer which is available before and after the show.
Great bar with a huge variety of drinks. The interior is nice with ample seating for larger groups or small ones. I especially like the couches which are comfy and relaxing.
Between the liquor selection and the awesome food and service you can't go wrong. Justin was a very attentive server.
My wife and I come here about once a week. The food is always good and the servers are friendly. They have a great selection of local beers on tap.

This is one of the must see places in Nashville.  Great blues / jazz music to listen and dance to.  The ribs are one of the best in city.  Super moist and succulent.  We are definitely coming back the next time we visit Nashville
Awesome music and food! Always a fun time at Taps! Never a better place.... Nice place to connect and hang out and have fun!

I cannot say enough great things about this place! I purchased a groupon for 2 flights of beer and appetizer and I am so glad I did. We did not have a reservation and the grouping stated it was required, but they gladly helped us anyway. The staff was friendly and personable, and the owner was so nice! After over hearing we are new to Nashville she walked over to introduce herself and chatting about all the great things to do in Nashville! The live music was awesome and the vibe was just what we liked. I have a feeling we will become regulars here!

From the impressive beer selection to the even more impressive knowledge about said beers that the bartenders have, this place is a go-to for any beer lover. The bar has well over 200 different varieties of beers from around the world. The bartender who was serving us had stellar recommendations, including an apricot sour beer that was phenomenal.

A great place to go see a show or dance in Nashville.
Has very interesting seating setup, and plenty of different areas to lounge in!
This one of the largest and nicest clubs in Nashville!

Went here for a quick lunch on the first day of the CMA Fest. I had the catfish po boy and my boyfriend had the pork bbq sandwich. Fast service, delicious fries, and reasonable prices. The great live music was an added bonus!

Walked in to a great atmosphere with awesome people and music. Sat down and ordered a bucket of beers and the waitress brought the wrong beer. When I pointed it out, she just said that they were out of the beer that I ordered. She wouldn't take it off the check or even apologize. When we got our food it was all burnt and overall pretty gross. The ribs were good as was the pasta but everything else was nasty. Refused to give us new food when even she acknowledged it looked gross. The music was really good though but overall I would highly recommended against going here.

This is my 9th Flying Saucer. I have multiple plates in the Ring of Honor. You wouldn't think I would find this place all that memorable, but what I love about Flying Saucer is that each one is a little different. 

This one is in a neat old building, and the charm reminds me of the original Fort Worth Saucer (which I miss so, so much). I love the couches. It's like chilling with your friends at a coffee shop but with beer instead. Along with some delicious local craft beer, I had a pizza with prosciutto and arugula. It was big enough that I could've shared it with someone else. 

Being in the UFO club, I'd likely come back when visiting to add some beer toward my next plate. But the wonderful atmosphere that makes me nostalgic for the old days in Fort Worth makes me *want* to return again.

Such a great venue with a terrific rotating lineup of talent. I was so impressed with the way the crowd was handled, seated, and entertained. Quite a lovely bastion of Southern Country hospitality. Loved it!!

Cool atmosphere and indoor patio seating area. Huge beer selection if you're into that. My boyfriend and I went here after we visited the Frist Center because it's right across the street. The cheese dip was okay, a little thin and not that much flavor. Pizza was good and was enough for 2-3 people. Service was fine.

With taps galore and even more in bottles, the Flying Saucer features between 100 to 150 beers on any given day. Although I can't attempt to try them all, I'm sure there are those who try. 

The beer menu is a newsletter four pages long, one I wouldn't mind reading more often. I decided to go with Abita Select Strawotor, love Abita beers. My guy ordered some Seasonal special on tap. 

For an early lunch snack, we ordered the 3 item plate (pick from meat and cheeses) and along with that you get olive tapanade, crackers of multiple kinds, roasted almonds and apples. We went with two different types of cheese and the peppered salami. It was a great cheese plate. 

I loved the service, the beer selection and the food. The location has a lot of charm and so much to see with all the saucers on the ceiling. I would love to stop into another location when traveling or come back for more.

While visiting my sister who lives in Nashville, she took me here to grab a bite to eat before we went to all the bars off Broadway. This isn't a bar that you would think exists in downtown Nashville if you didn't live here because I know when I think of downtown Nashville I think crazy packed honky-tonk bars, and this is quite the opposite!

Glad we stopped here first- it was ladies night! Their Thursday night special is ONE DOLLAR WELL DRINKS (for ladies only obviously)! You can't find a deal like that anywhere in Nashville...especially not downtown. We started our night off right, the food was delicious and the drinks were cheap! If you're looking for a chill and inexpensive stop before hitting up the honky-tonk bars this is the place to go!!

If I could give 0 stars I would. Terrible BBQ. There are so many better places to grab good BBQ in Nashville don't waste your time here. I think I've had better ribs at a TGIFs. Mac and cheese, was terrible, beans were right out of a can and nachos with pulled pork were gross. Ordered a side of veggies...those were decent. Stay away.

This is my favorite bar in town! Large area, so it never feels extremely crowded. Comfy leather couches, pool tables, darts, and seating for large parties are some of my favorite aspects of The Flying Saucer. 
It is open late and always has a really laid back atmosphere. You can also join their UFO club to keep track of the beers you drink to work towards a platter on the wall. UFO club members also receive great offers.

Amazing experience that I will never forget. We were lucky enough to have chosen a night where David Nail, Vince Gill and a Little Big Town were performing.
