The Opry runs so smoothly, entertaining every second. We had amazing seats in the center section. It is a must and worth every penny. I will definitely be back again. Soon I hope!

The best thing about the Grand Ole Opry venue is that there are almost no bad seats.  Compared to many other venues it's a very small and intimate one.  Recently the better half got tickets for "Weird Al" Yankovic and it was an outstanding experience being able to see him here. Instead of having to strain my eyes looking at a Hawaiian Shirt shaped speck you could actually make him out.

Additionally, the parking is free because you are next to Opry Mills. Of course it may take you a while to FIND said Free Parking because of how busy Opry Mills always is. 

Opry Mills is also a bonus because you can easily find a place to eat before the show. 

Highly recommended for any concert.

Went in for a drink and that's all we had. The bartender wasn't very welcoming, she was too busy talking to the only other people in there. We had one drink and went a few doors down to Doc Holliday's where we were very welcomed!
First time here, excellent pulled pork and the Mac n cheese is an absolute must! It might be the best Mac n cheese I've ever had.

If you are a country music fan, this is a must do!!!  Book a show and take the tour.   The tour takes you through the back dressing rooms and on stage, and they let you not only see the perspective of those performing, you get to stand on the Circle of Wood taken from the Ryman when the Opry moved to the new building. 
Then do a show! You get to witness a LIVE Radio show and see multiple performers even if just of a couple of songs each. Only downside, if you book early to get decent tickets, you don't know who you will see.

Wife and I went for dinner I had the smoked chicken Philly and hush puppies, she had the pulled pork and fries. The waitress warned me that there was lots of chicken on the Philly but to my surprise when I got it, it didn't even fill half of the 9 inch hoagie that it was made on. I believe there was about 5 onion pieces and about 4 pieces of bell pepper on the Philly, not what I would expect to see on a Philly of any sort. The hush puppies were cooked with some kind of flaky batter that was the consistency of a crushed shortbread cookie. I was not impressed and definitely will not return. We also had drinks, the sex on the beach was bitter and tasted watered down. I gave it to stars because my wife's food was tolerable.

We only ordered Nachos so this review applies to the beer and beertenders only. OUTSTANDING! Our bartender really knew the beers they offered on tap (200+ of them) and pulled together an excellent IPA sampler. Prices were very reasonable also.

If you like beer, this is a must in Nashville.
Best burgers in town, hands down. Friendly staff, lovely ambiance and an overall great experience. The fries are to die for, so make that your top priority when you come! Will be back very soon!

Actually, probably closer to a 3.5 as food was just meh and they didn't have my drink of choice, Limon.   :(. The fried pickles and catfish bites were great.  Definitely a must.  
Crowd was a great mix of ages and the band playing was excellent.    
Our server did a great job keeping up with our group of 8.   
Dark place and very loud but I think this is expected for a blues bar.

My boyfriend and I tried the Tippler the first week it opened and I was very impressed with the decor as well as the speakeasy vibe. We went for drinks before dinner and they weren't terrible but I am a huge Patterson house fan and the Tippler does not compare. 

After visiting again last night with a group for a friends birthday I was a little confused. We walked over from boundary and see a group of people waiting outside and a bouncer at the door. We were told we would have to wait unless we had reservations. Luckily my friend reserved a table so we were able to go right in. Once we were seated with our party it was 20 minutes before we saw a waiter and another 20 before we got our drinks. I felt like I needed to order 5 things every time I saw him because I didn't know when he would be back again. 

Towards the end of the night we gave up our table and walked around the bar a bit. We looked to our right and there was Nashville star, Sam Palladio "Gunner" posted at the bar, so that was a plus. There are three levels. The top level is cozy and has a shuffle board table but it only took change so no one was really playing. There was also a tv and couch which was nice. The middle level is somewhat of a dining room feel while the bottom level has a club vibe. 

Overall I liked the Tippler and they played great music . The drinks are a bit pricey for what they are but still good. After a certain time I think it turns into more of a club than a bar so if you're not into that go early. I didn't like the whole bouncer at the door and feeling like I was on 2nd ave but it still turned out to be a great night. I would go again before dinner but not for dinner.

My first tip is to go early this place is busy! The band start in 15 minutes after we arrived and they were fabulous.The service was fast and efficient and dinner was delicious. I had the small four piece ribs with beans and slaw. My friend had the brisket and that was also good. The salmon was also good.The only reason I didn't give this five stars is because this place is super packed. We had people waiting around our table while they were waiting to get a table. It made it a little uncomfortable having people hanging over us while we finished our meal. Otherwise highly recommend it it was fun and the food was great for great price.

A must see/do when in Nashville! 
The Opry offers a taste of a variety of different artists playing a variety of genres. Great views and sound. 
Advice: get there early so you can have dinner and parking is plentiful. 
We combined this with a trip to Opryland which is within walking distance. Allow for a couple hours of strolling through there 4 gardens. There is no cost to stroll. We found the best cheesecake in the Cascades restaurant. Have fun.

First time checking out this place today. Had an awesome time food was great. Only thing I wish was that beer prices were a little lower. Paying $5 or $7 bucks for a 13oz or 16oz beer is a little much.

On a recent trip to Nashville, we were able to watch Carrie Underwood and a host of other artists perform. The show started off with Carrie narrating the history of the Opry, including the flood in 2010 and its rebuild and recovery, and the significance of the wooden circle in the middle of the stage. 

The performance was a bit over two hours, featured so many lives acts, funny moderators, and is all broadcast live on the radio. On this particular Saturday night, the Opry was packed--and one can easily see why: it's an experience to be had, and I'm not even a country music fan. It amazes me that they are able to pull off performances like these night after night. You definitely cannot miss this if you are in town!

I definitely don't really ascribe to that vinyl, hipster retro thing, but I do have a special place in my heart for The White Stripes and wonder when The Raconteurs will ever get back in the studio again. 

Anyway, the four of us went and it was definitely a lot smaller than I imagined especially since the whole space is so large, I was surprised to see that the store space was small. What was inside though was mostly collection of vinyl. A couple of band shirts-and if you can find something you like in the bargain section it's a pretty sweet deal. 

Despite it being a pretty hipster spot it's definitely not snooty. The staff there was very friendly and helpful with my friends who wanted to use the vintage photo booth and the guy who wanted to use the recording booth to record a demo. Glad we had time to go see it.

Stopped here twice last week following concerts at the Schermerhorn. Conveniently close to the venue. Street parking and lot parking both available, although as with most parking in Nashville lot parking can be pricey. 

The stuffed mushroom appetizer was a bit different from many places inasmuch as these were stuffed with cream cheese & herbs (delicately flavored)...but -- here comes the twist...heavily battered and deep fried, served with horseradish sauce. Good or bad? Actually I enjoyed them quite a bit...they were less greasy than the fish. But ultimately reminded me of carnival food. (Not a dig...just my observation.)

First night entreé was Thursday's Special: fish and chips. I wasn't totally disappointed, but did have slightly higher hopes. The portion size was just right--4 pieces. The batter dipped fish good, save for the squirt of grease that popped up with my first knife slice. Not drained well enough - served too quickly? Nonetheless, flavor and texture were great. Throw away the tartare sauce and just top 'em with Malt Vinegar. Fries fine, but also just a bit soft, not crisp. 

Second night we fared much better. My wife had the Sunday night Special: Shepherd's Pie. Great, flavorful, but just a tiny bit salty. I had the Angus burger (rare) with grilled onions and Pepper jack Cheese. Absolutely one of the best burgers I've had in Nashville. Cooked to perfection, juicy, great beef flavor. (BTW, you can choose your toppings.)

Thursday night football. Sunday night football plus live music.

The service was absolutely perfect both nights....swift, attentive, and polite.
wonderful dinner here with a friend while attending a convention. food was terrific and staff was very attentive. best burger I've had in a long time.
A Real find! Not just burgers either. The kitchen really has someone awake at the wheel. The service is the best I get in nashville, so I've got no idea about the review that slammed it.

I was in Nashville for a conference and a group wanted to go to the Opry.  Always down to check out some country music.  I was surprised how amazing my night was.  I didn't check out who was singing that night and it was such a great idea!  Barry Gibb ended up performing.  Hearing him sing "Stayin Alive" with Ricky Skaggs was amazing!  I couldn't believe it.  This has to be one of the best concerts and venues I have been to.  Great experience at the Opry.
So much fun!!  We had a wonderful time at the Grand Ole Opry!  Can't wait to come back one day.

Had a blast last night seeing the Grand Ole Opry live! We may have been in the "nose bleeds" but I still felt like close to the action. Maybe it was the performers, but they also played to us and not just the front row. 
By far the best performance was by Chris Jansen! Funny and energetic. He made a three song set feel like an entire show! Not sure how he'd keep that energy up every night, but it was a blast! Hopefully he has some staying power and gets inducted into the Grand Ole Opry. 

It was made even cooler by the fact that we took a behind the scenes tour earlier in the day and got to see some of the awesomeness first hand. We didn't get to run into anyone famous, but it was still really cool to stand in the circle.

Great food and Friendly service.  If I am ever in downtown Nashville again I will stop by.

NOTE: it is a club so it can get a loud and maybe hard to have a conversation inside.

In my opinion, unlike any place that Nashville has thus far. This has become one of my favorite places to go on the weekends with friends. Not too pretentious, not too expensive (if you order wisely), not too small, and isn't overwhelmingly dominated by any certain demographic. The DJ is great, the mezcal mule is perfect, the decor is awesome. I have not been back since they changed their menu, so I can't speak to it as a dinner spot but as a place to go with friends after dinner it is definitely a good time!
Great service!! Lindsey is the best! Came in for a bachelorette party and had a great time!!

I stumbled upon Belcourt Taps while killing an hour before heading to see my movie at Belcourt Theatre. It was packed so I waited at the bar before finding a seat and watching a few people sing & play up on stage. It is a small place, but I don't mind it. I've been back several times & I like that I can catch people singing any night. I haven't eaten the food, but my friend had the fried green tomatoes & said they were good. I tried a glass of their Belcourt tap, which barely qualifies as a beer, it's so light.  I won't get it again, but I will be back.

I come here for the beer battered deep fried pickles!! Light, crispy, greasy, salty goodness!! I love the outdoor patio w live music playing...and it's not allllll country bands thank God( nothing against country music, it's just that I can only take it in moderate doses and that's all u get at some places)they have a nice mix. I've never hung out inside, seems kind of dark and stale in there but the patio atmosphere is awesome. The servers have always been friendly!

I went to Belcourt Taps for the burgers. The burger was pretty good. 

I wouldn't go here for flights of beer. Someone else's server came to the bar (where I was sitting) to ask the bartender how to serve a flight. She was told to "pick random beers" for the flight. I doubt she remembered all of the ones that she chose for that table's order.

Food was good; avoid the flights.

Great place to sing covers of the greatest hits! I especially loved the moment when Prince came on and I got to sing little Red Corvette! It is the perfect place to drink and sing out of tune. Also if you are up for playing a game of pool, they have that too.
During the day it's a great pub and restaurant.  After 11pm it turns into a 21 year old party on weekends.  Best fish and chips and town and best place to watch US soccer.

Finding this place was an adventure, but it is awesome! The atmosphere is homey and welcoming. The fries are very crunchy and the burgers are fantastic. My husband got the aloha burger which is marinated in terriaki sauce and has fried pineapple, I got the Titan burger, which has mushrooms and cheese. The burgers are excellently marinated and my husband recommends that you order a side a fried to take home.
I had a tour of the Opry today, and the tour guide was named Cilantro. She was absolutely wonderful. She had a couple of "testy" people in the group, and dealt with it with such professionalism.

This is a great place. There's really nothing I need to add but I'm obligated to, soooooooo.....

My friends and I went one night because we were in the mood for some good beer, and Flying Saucer came highly recommended from our resident Nashville transplant.  The selection is impressive, and definitely goes toe to toe with some great bars in NYC.

Unfortunately this review is coming 2+ weeks after my visit, so I don't quite remember which beers I imbibed, but I distinctly remember really good prices (even after the happy hour), a flat out AWESOME brat and pretzel platter and very friendly and courteous service. 

The ambience is very light and filled with energy with some great outdoor deck seating. Clean, walls filled with chotchkies, and a huge (albeit of limited quality) projector playing whichever game they're showcasing, Flying Saucer will definitely be one of my first stops when I head back to Nashville.

Likeable enough place but the bartender acts like she's doing you a favor by getting you a drink AT THE BAR!!! Hateful, rude and very disrespectful. We asked to switch the channel after the male bartender said "no problem" and she was argumentative and rude again. We won't be back and I hope she isn't working to pay for anything because she is an ass. Long brown, straight hair with a baseball cap and bad attitude.

We popped in here for a lunch based on all the rave reviews. We did have a good experience, but for all the options in Nashville I was a little underwhelmed. If I could, I would give it 3.5 stars.

First off, it's a typical pub food menu. Good quality pub food, but still pub food. We came hungry, so ordered a lot of food. The poppers were good: bacon wrapped cream cheese stuffed jalapenos, not deep fried. I had a burger, and it was definitely above average. I also sampled the fried catfish, fries, onion strings, baked beans, and hush puppies. ALL above average. There were no bland fillers here. 

The service was really friendly, really attentive.

If you're hungry for a burger and fries kind of meal this is a great spot for it. However, if you're visiting Nashville and looking for a unique dining experience, this isn't anything you can't find in your hometown.
Amazing beer selection, friendly staff, and the food is wonderful! The German potato salad is awesome! The saucer supper is melt in your mouth

Being in town for business we were looking for a place we considered to be authentic yet not overwhelmingly country and we found BB Kings. 

I can say we had a great time. The food was not the best ever however had many highlights including the fried pickles and the amazing fried catfish. 

Our table got a variety of entrees ranging from fish to steak and while no one was amazed everyone definitely left happy. 

Overall the ambiance made the night and we would definitely come again when in town.

Had a blast. Saw Thomas Rhett. Wish he played more! But for what we got, it was an awesome experience! We even were able to take the behind the scenes tour, which was awesome!!! Our tour guide was a younger girl, can't remember her name, but she was super funny and informative! All around great experience and a must do when on vacation in Nashville!
A decent burger joint in an out of the way place.  A better choice than all the tourist trap places in downtown Nashville.

What a fun thing to do when in Nashville!  Loved all of the variety in the perfprmers, and since we took the backstage tour, we got to see most of them up close and personal.  It seems like such a prestigious pace, yet still casual and homey in that the performers seem like one big happy family.  A must-do when in Nashville!
This place is fabulous! The house blues band rocks! The atmosphere is great, and the food is wonderful! This is a must try when in Nashville!

Scotch eggs, burgers, fish and chips, and the rest of the menu is cooked magnificently to order.  Tuesdays is rock and roll night and you just might see someone whose CDs you've been listening to for years.  This is hands-down the coolest spot in Nashville!

Passing through Nashville during rush hour and figured that this would be a perfect way to avoid driving in some traffic. Just a short 5 minute hop off I-40 and it's off a sneaky road with the Third Man Records logo standing tall. The building looks awesome and the interior is even better! But the only downside is that the space is too small for the crowd of people in there.. The ambiance of exploring the things in the store gets lost when people are bumping you. Besides that I'm soo excited to listen to the first records of my new record collection!! Rock on Jack

This is just a cool place to hang out, grab a bite to eat, have a cold beer for a decent price, and watch a game or listen to live music.

Is the food great? Nope. It's good. It's flavorful. Portions are good. Prices are decent. You can order standard bar fare or something healthier. If I owned the restaurant, I'd be proud of what I was doing.

The atmosphere: it's off an alley, hence the name. I've taken my teenage daughters to BAD before hockey games, entire family on weekends, and friends. The crowd is nice and you can enjoy a meal with your kids and not worry about someone acting 'the fool.' They have live music. Are they ready for primetime? Nope. Do they sing better than me (yes and easy bar to hurdle) and are they entertaining? Definitely.

They have a good choice of beers and happy hour specials. They are closed on Sundays and are colas for private events on occasion.

I highly recommend BAD. I don't eat there often enough.

Had a great lunch here with wife. Had the big Titan burger and it was excellent. Very fast service and was a great value. The menu looks like a great bar food spot, and we will be coming back for lunch when we are in town.

We first went to BB Kings when it was still in Vegas so we were looking forward to this visit to Nashville so we could go again. 

However, we were let down!! The ribs were cold, refrigerated cold, not room temperature cold! The Mac n cheese tasted like they just microwaved it. Horrible stuff! It seems like they are relying on their reputation to get them business and the quality of food is going down hill. 

We hand two drinks that were decent, but if you want really good drinks head over to 417 Union or Skull's! 

The music, I gotta say, was awesome! The band was Hayes and the Hustle. I think that's the name, they were really really good!!

We were hesitating to see this show or not. In the end we're super happy to see the show.
For 2 and half hours the show was going on pretty well organized. They were all good.
The audience and singer with bands, felt like we're all one big family.
Great show. Definitely worth to see when you are in Nashville.

Came in here because I heard the good music. It looks like a very family friendly place (which it is) and the food there is excellent! Only the best of bands play this place. The music is always the best!

Now I came in when it was busy so I can understand why it took 45 minutes to get our food. The waitress was very kind and respectful anyways. I ordered the Fried Catfish Dish and it was AMAZING!!! It wasn't too greasy and wasn't too dry. The catfish was very flavorful and crispy. It came with fries,hush puppies,and coleslaw. The fries were decent. Nothing special. The hush puppies were really good and made from scratch. And the coleslaw was also very tasteful and yummy. And that is why this place deserves 5 stars. Don't get mad that you don't get your food or drink right away,the place is usually really busy so you can't blame them. Next time I'm in Nashville I will come back! Thank guys!
In from the ATL.  Place wins for vibe, atmosphere and location.  Burgers are a tasty treat and good quality.  Go here for tasty burger!  O-Straws on side, Texas burger, local brews on tap.

If you are a country music fan, this is a must-see. A visit to Nashville without seeing the Opry is like traveling to Paris and skipping the Eiffel Tower. My face alternated between slack-jaw wonderment and cheek-busting smiles for the entire show, except those few moments when my eyes got a little misty. There were country legends and innovative new acts performing, everyone playing just two or three songs, with lots of banter and joking couching each performance. It was traditional, but not musty; entertaining, but not cartoonish; artistic, but not self-indulgent. I'll go back every time I'm in Nashville.

The Fries Fish was just ok. The pecan pie tasted like it was from the freezer. The greens were like chopped spinach and the baked chicken was really bad.  

The worse was the plastic glass and forks (private dining)   ....thus one star! 

Why two? 

Service Staff was good and the band excellent.  In short ~ go for the music. Eat elsewhere.

5-star for the atmosphere and decor...

this spot was perfectly situated between downtown and our hotel on the westend- i.e. the perfect place to grab grub after an evening of drinks.
my kale salad was costco-ish but the pretzels really are good. they don't really taste like your ballpark pretzel though (which i love) but some great twisty bread ;)
loved the high ceilings and "saucer" adornments.

Had a dinner reservation here and canceled it at the hostess desk. Hostess came across as uninterested and bored. Didn't like the way she treated the customers in front of us (felt like was dismissive). Wish the initial experience had been good enough for us to come all the way into the restaurant to find out about the rest.

Even though I am not a beer lover, Flying Saucer has a cider that I adore on tap! And since they are now smoke free, I love them even more! There's nothing like sitting on their open aired patio on a nice day and settling into one of their many couches with a beverage. I also enjoy the pool table room for hanging out with friends and taking it easy. Check out the "saucers" on the wall and ceiling, there's some pretty interesting comments and sayings listed from the invidiuals who managed to drink one of every single beer that the Flying Saucer offers (over 200). 

The food is typically bar fare; I seem to remember the cheese dip being pretty good, but can't speak for much else. It's mostly forgettable as I believe I've eaten a meal or two here before...

Service is pretty good and overall this is a nice place to hang out!

A unique experience that really put a smile on my face. All the history that really highlights the roots and the growth of country music. My company held an event there and the food and drinks were good. I'm inspired to come back for a show soon!

Great spot!  We stopped here after having an hour and a half wait to get in somewhere else. Our intention was to have a drink and snack and make it back to our original spot. I ordered a delicious Tom Collins...no store bough sour mix here. Freshly squeezed. Yum. We ordered the catfish sandwich which came with hush puppies and cole slaw. So good!  The sandwich was very generous and incredibly tasty. This was not frozen fish!  Now, maybe it is because I am from the north (and we don't make good ones there) but those were the best hush puppies ever! Light, flavorful. We left to try to find another hang out....but I really wish we had just stayed. It was delish, reasonably priced and had nice live music. Great spot!
Don't bother with this place unless nothing else is open. Burger was overdone. Homemade chips were good. Location OK atmosphere is divey. Waited too long for the food we got. Pass

Im not sure why the yelp reviews for this place are so low. Its well rated elsewhere. Ive been here atleast 4 or 5 times and never had a bad experience.  The crowd is typically educated, not rough.  the dj is good. The service is good.   I was able to sing a salsa song which I was impressed that they had it, and people seemed to enjoy dancing to it.  Even on weeknights its pretty busy, never empty. You should visit!

I didn't understand true sadness until I went to this bar. It's a meth lab that will destroy your faith in the human race. Heisenberg and Jesse pinkman wouldn't go to this place. I created a yelp account to specifically warn others not to go to this sobering example of human activity.

What a fun place to have dinner! The music was lively and the performer was great! I ordered the nachos with pulled pork, I got a huge heaping helping. They were absolutely delicious, definitely enough to share. The drinks were also delicious. I would go back for sure.

Very comfortable place to hang out, food was great, drinks were great, and the night we went, they had songwriters singing and entertaining! Awesome place, next time we're in Nashville, we'll be back!

We were not country fans but we might be now. We new nothing About the Grand Ole Opry.  Didn't even know it was a live radio show.  A way cooler experience than I thought it would be. We saw a collection of old and new recording artists like Ashley Cambell and the White Family. Not terribly expensive either.

I LOVE this place. I love the million beers on tap, rotators, events, the menu, and the decor. This is a great place to take friends and cool parents on any night of the week. Also good for bros and tourists. It feels local, although its a chain. You could probably even have fun here on a bad date (just hit the taps extra hard). 
Beer - There's a ton. They have a good selection of local/craft.
Menu - My fav is the Pork Belly Sandwich and I'm usually not a big fan of pork. The brats and beer cheese soup are also delish. But, the pork belly wins every time with the apple-jalapeno chutney.
Parking - There's a huge lot below and they charge you to park there. That sucks, but make sure to get your ticket validated so you don't get charged your first-born food child. 
Waitstaff - The skimpy outfits make me a little uncomfortable; and a lot uncomfortable on a Sunday afternoon. However, the staff is pretty good about checking in and delivering food and drinks.
Ambiance - It kind of reminds me of an oversized dive/college bar with high ceilings. The walls are covered with pictures, posters, objects, awards, TVs, etc and they have beer bottle chandeliers. Eh, whatever, I like beer and hate pretentiousness. However, the place can get a little loud when it fills up. 

Overall, its a cool place to hang out with good beer and good food. Great place to catch the Preds during hockey season.

Wow, what an incredible and historic spot.  Rather than just being a venue to watch a music show, this is actually an experience!  We were here for about two hours and saw an incredible show, which showcased different kinds of country music, great presenters and even square dancing.  The place is huge and had the most incredible sound system...all music came out crystal clear!

This is such a unique and amazing experience and I recommend everyone to visit if you can...not a disappointment!

As someone who believes in what Jack White is doing, I stopped in because I traveled from NY to see his induction in the Nashville Walk of Fame.  

JW is single handedly reviving the vinyl industry and this store represents his complete devotion to this.

The place was crowded with other people who believe.  The staff was very busy and did their best to accommodate everyone including people who insisted on taking their time up with chit chat.

I bought a vinyl copy of "Elephant", five 7" records (I don't have a record player) and some other things because I believe in this artist and I support him.

I really had no idea what to expect when I ordered the tickets online before we left for Tennessee.  I like country music and all, but more wanted to visit simply because it was the "Grand Ole Opry".  
Boy, were we blown away!  What an entertaining show!  We ended up with amazing seats...6th row.  There were 12 different entertainers, including (our favorites of the night) Ashley Campbell, Carson Peters & Iron Mountain and Steven Curtis Champan.  The hosts for each of the four portions of the show were all sorts of funny (we especially liked Mike Snider).
The seating (main floor anyway) is pew style (with cushions).  Get there an hour or so early to get a free parking spot in the malls movie theatre lot that is right nextdoor.  Drink prices are a tad crazy ($11 for a glass of wine...ugh), staff is super friendly and the gift shop has a lot of great stuff.
No matter what type of music you like...I'd recommend seeing a show if you are in the area!  You will not be disappointed!

Wow, to walk in this place you know you are walking in where history has happened at its best.  We happened to arrive during a week that great talent had arrived. Although we did not know who everyone that performed was, we enjoyed the variety and the quality of sound.  Realize you are walking into a radio program, so expect a lot of commercials and the constant plug for different merchandise.   Now if you are listening to anything but XM this is a common thing.

The crawfish poppers and shrimp and grits were great. The made in store chips were good too. My only complaint is way too much food overall. The portion size was huge. Consider splitting dishes or skipping the appetizers.

Good acoustics, albeit loud and the bands that night were good also.

This was a dream come true for me. Our tour was led by Matt. He was excellent and very knowledgeable. We had a small group so it allowed for us to really see things that we couldn't see in a crowd.  The tour goes through the actual steps of a musician or band when they enter the Opry as members or as a performance. I am hoping to catch a concert there soon. It is also within walking distance of Opry Mills and other famous places.

Location 5 (just outside of Nashville)
Price 5 (average price for any tour in Nashville)
Service 5
If you're looking for a very classy bar and lounge atmosphere straight from NYC, this is it. The drinks are awesome, and the staff is very friendly.

Stopped in to see Steve but Jasmine was tending bar. The bartenders at BB's always hit it out of the park. Jasmine is very friendly and energetic. Steve always has something new up his sleeve. Some of the best mixed drinks you will find. You will always enjoy the Music in BB's. The menu has a full range of food. You will always find something you like.

We've been going to Saucer at least once a week for about four years now? Our group ranges in size from 3 to 12 people every week, so we could be the nightmare of a restaurant with open seating, but they are always so nice to us. What we have really come to love, though, is the service. The managers and the wait staff are pretty consistently well-informed, personable, and prompt, even when the restaurant gets swamped. We've had our best times with Lauren and Joe, both waiters, who are quick to remember a face (and an order, week to week) and brighten all of our Mondays! Lauren has stopped asking us for food orders except to confirm we want them, and often recommends beers to a lot of us that are right on the money for our personal tastes. Seriously, we love them. They deserve a holiday in their honor.
The beer selection is always great, of course, and most of their food options are also great (they have one of the best Cobb salads I've ever had? Ever? Not what one would expect from a gastropub but I'm all in). We literally had our wedding rehearsal dinner here, which really probably says enough.

Went for drinks later on a Friday night. This place was packed! Interesting mix of people, and definitely a change of pace from most night spots in Nashville in that it was a club vibe. Drinks were good. Try the house made fireball-delish! The drink special was preacher's daughter... Bible Belt y'all.

I have a real fondness for BAD. This is the first place that we are when myself and three of my friends touched down in Nashville. 
The food is pretty good while not the best in town. I wouldn't recommend this place if you're searching for a revolutionary culinary experience.
BUT! 
This place was never packed (when many many other places in the area were) and if you want somewhere that looks rad, has awesome service and you and your friends can have a great time, BAD would be good (sorry for the pun) for you.
Great place for a burger.  It's literally in the alley but bright and fun inside.  There is no breakfast on the menu.  All good. Burgers and chips were just fine.

We went here with the idea that this is one of the things you have to do as a part of a visit to Nashville, but had no idea how good it was going to be.  It turned out to be the highlight of the trip.  My family and I can now truly appreciate why this has been an enduring institution for 90 years and is still going strong.   There were several amazing performances, good humor, the opportunity to see a live broadcast taking place and just an outstanding evening of entertainment.  If you go to Nashville, you have to see the Opry.   We'll be back for sure.

Three stars only because the tour seemed rushed.  We got the total access pass which was wonderful except at Opryland.  You could only make your reservation for the tour in person.  Why?!  So we arrived way early for the first tour on a Sunday,  which in my opinion was a waste of time.  The actual building was amazing to see.
What a rich musical and historical treat!  You made it this far to Nashville do not skip a night at the roots of country music.  You will not be disappointed.
Awesome food. Very good restraunt in downtown Nashville. Excellent music and wonderful staff.

We are moving from Louisiana to NYC and my husband (a big Jack White fan) insisted we had to stop here on our way. I groaned. I really didn't want to be dragged into another dusty record store for hours. But we went and I'm glad I we did.

He searched through records and I, a fat, middle-aged, road-weary, totally unhip mom who has no taste in music (okay, I admit to being awesomely cool on the inside), gabbed with the (I think another review called them rude, unhelpful and weird hipsters?? Please. Stop being so judgmental) staff. I don't look like I belong there and no one shunned me. We got there about 30 mins before they closed and told them about our journey. They insisted we take our time and told us not to be worried. They offered to take a family picture for us. The guy in the yellow suspenders and I talked about our linguistic pet peeves while my husband and kids looked at records. The two girls were very helpful and informative. I was actually recommended a great record. They just gave my son tokens for the wax-o-matic when he tried to pay for them. So that was cool. The guy showed us how you could bring the guitars and synthesizer into the recording booth if we wanted.  Our family left with stickers, a wax guitar, three records, a pin and two tee shirts, and a bunch of pictures. 

So I don't know where insulting the staff came from. People who usually reflect negatively get it back in return. 

Both tee-shirts we bought seem like great quality so the "cheap tee-shirts" review is odd.

My ONLY beef with this place is the lack of a restroom. Please fix up whatever employee bathroom you have and offer it if someone asks. You don't have to advertise it, but when a road-weary traveller who has been stuck in traffic for an hour and a half asks, let them.
Didn't eat here, but the staff was awesome and the music was great. Recommend if you are into Blues Music.

Saw the building from afar and thought it was a church, but when we got closer, we saw people eating and drinking inside so we thought to check it out. The interior seemed decorated and furnished with tons of seating options to choose from. We picked what looked to be comfy couch corner and immediately sunk to the floor- the cushions definitely lost all fluff awhile ago. 
We tried the local flight to see what brews Nashville  had to offer which was pretty good, then ended with a couple draft pours of our choosing. My terrapin IPA from Athens, GA that was on special was super yum- had a hint of citrus to it! But my friend's porter was awful- it tasted so bitter with some sour that we felt like it had gone bad or we got the bottom of the keg? We left it un-drank. 
Our waitress also had a bit of an attitude, but we're attributing that to the full tray of glassware she broke minutes before our arrival.

An unexpectedly great place! With all the tourist traps in Nashville, I was really hoping to find a place that the locals enjoy, and this was definitely it! The burgers were awesome and service was wonderful! It has a fun and laid-back atmosphere. There's nothing "bad" about this place! Loved it.

The personnel working the hostess stand are nearly incompetent. We paid cover for 4 people and walked in. We went to sit down at an open table and a waitress cleared it off for us and wiped it down. Just as we were ready to sit down someone (maybe a manager) told us that we couldn't sit down and there was a wait list we needed to add our names to. Guess who managed the wait list?! Yup! The hostesses!

So we put our names on the list, went to buy some drinks at the bar. There were 4 seats open at the bar so we tried to sit there. The female bartender, who would barely take our order, told us we couldn't sit in 2 opens spots because someone who was dancing was sitting there.  (Where I am from when you leave your spot, they put a water out with a napkin over it to save your spot, this was not there.) 

When the couple came back from dancing they saw that people had gathered around their spot and just ordered from the bar and went back to the dance floor. So they weren't even expecting to get their seat back. Nor did the bartenders tell them that they had turned away two couples by saving their seat.

If my boyfriend didn't have his heart content on seeing lives blues music I would have told them all where to go. I am a paying customer just like everyone else. 

Let's talk about that, too. They advertise that they have no cover. Tonight it was $10 per person. So just expect to pay something at the door even if you have heard separately.

It's sad that a legend's name is on this establishment.

I've been here twice and have only visited their gift shop. They sell some nice souvenirs.

If you're a fan of country music, you will have to check out this place! I will have to come back here for a show one of these days.
Historical. You absolutely have to go if you're in Nashville. Check out the mailboxes and the dressing rooms.

The moment I walked into this place I had a smile on my face...probably because it reminded me of that old show in Disneyland...the Bear Jamboree?  However there were no furry characters in this spot (unless of course Charlie Daniels counts). 

The Grand Ole Opry is filled with music history and live country to kick up your heals to.  Definitely round up your posse and spend the money for the tour.  I felt it was much better than the Ryman tour (even though if you have time I would recommend that too).  We came back the same night we took the tour for one of their live shows which was such a great time (it really doesn't matter who is playing...it is a great experience).  Honestly this is a "must do" situation in Nashville that you won't regret (unlike all the fried food you will consume in this town).  

This is not the O.K.-Corral so gallop straight to this venue!
We love this place! So unique and I love their cider selection!! I'm gluten free and completely feel comfortable here!!

They will not serve u water. The bartenders say they dont serve water but they will give u a dixie cup to fill up in the bathroom. They also say if u can afford molly then u can afford $5 for a bottle of water. Thats definatley not a policy u see in any other clubs like LA, Vegas, San Diego or Miami. Other than that it would be a cool spot but they def need to change this policy and improve on the sound and lighting system.
What can you say?  It is the Grand Old Opry.  Had a great time, listened to some fabulous music, watched some tremendous banjo pickin', fiddle playin' musicians.  Well worth the visit.

Awesome burgers. No buffalo chicken. Catfish was good. Club sandwich was ok. Chicken tenders were pretty good. Fries are breaded so good if that's the way you like them.  Seating was perfect and no wait but busy and fun atmosphere.
The ribs were literally fall-off-the-bone good. Got lucky to get Trey as our server as he was very knowledgeable about the menu and the music. Great time!
A must see if you are in Nashville - so much music history!! Highly recommend!
Horrible service, they got my meal wrong then argued with me about it and had the audacity to bring it back to me.

We have been several Flying Sauce locations and they are all pretty similar.  I do like the high ceilings and large dining room of this location.  We were there on a game night, so it was pretty packed.  Lots of TVs and screens around the room.

Service was pretty spotty.  It was hard to flag down a server.  The BF likes the large craft beer menu.  I like that they offer wine.  We have not tried the food at this location, but the burgers that were coming out looked amazing.

We stopped in here early one night thinking that we would have a few drinks sing some bad country and start off our visit right in Music City.. man were we wrong! I did have a few drinks but you would have thought some of the people singing were giving their own concerts. Apparently this isnt a Karaoke bar but an amateur night some nights. Out bartender said its pretty hit or miss rather you get people coming in just to have fun or people who think they are the next Carrie Underwood! Ha! overall we had a good time singing along like fools from our seats but after some of the performances i heard no one wanted or needed to hear me sing!

Our tour guide, Linda, made this trip fantastic! I've wanted to come here since I fell in love with country music at a young age.  

We started off with a movie by Blake Shelton and then moved through the parts of the Opry House.  It was amazing to see backstage where Nashville is filmed at times, and then move through each dressing rooms, the post office box area, and each special place.  I loved hearing how Trisha Yearwood was a tour-guide, and Alan Jackson delivered mail.  Dierks Bentley got his start as a stagehand.  Just amazing tidbits you didn't know and that made the tour memorable.  

Our guide was knowledgeable, funny, and personable.  The building, and history, speak for themselves and you are in complete awe of the sense of legacy.  The only bad experience we had was as checking out with our photos we asked if we could get just one and the woman told us very nastily that no, we could not.  A simple question, asked nicely, deserves a much nicer response!

Took the tour and loved it!
Our guide was full of energy and did such a good job telling the stories and the history. 
Loved being able to walk onto the stage. 
They offer a professional picture in the circle, and you have the option to buy that at the end of the tour. They are $25 though. Worth it if you want the keepsake. 
Some of the items in the store are a little pricey, but that's to be expected with a place like this.

Sopped by chance. Great cozy singer songwriter venue. Great food. Met the owner Rose, very sweet lady. Has a real heart for the songwriters. Do you want a corporate owned type bar? No, not the place. A must stop.  Awesome

If you are a fan of classic country music, you have to attend a show. Worth the money! Even the Backstage Tour is a must-do to check off the bucket list.

Side Note: It's surrounded by an outlet mall and Chuy's. Kinda sad that the exterior is so commercial but the experience inside makes up for the lacking thrill outside.

Wow.  Super cool place.  Service is deplorable at best.  The bartenders either need a bar back or 2 more bartenders on.    While the bartender is very nice, there needs to be more of them.   Haven't tried the food because they've been too busy for us to order.

My wife went with her friends and I have been told the bartender had A terrible attitude toward them and grabbed their drinks from them and told them to get the F out of the bar then as the bouncers were escorting my wife's friends out she said that was unnecessary and was pushed by a male bouncer. This is with eyewitness accounts saying they've done nothing to be thrown out or harassed. Classless dirtbag place that men think they can push a woman. Let's see if I was there if mr tough guy bouncer working at a sh*thole dive bar would do anything NOPE. The owner is a lunatic yelling without even assessing the situation and the bouncers are a bunch of losers who couldn't make it in anything in life so they bounce for a living. Not the last you'll be hearing from me for sure.

One of the most creative and inspiring spaces ever put together. The staff is incredible and the music is endless. Attending a concert of movie in the Blue Room is a must if you have the opportunity. Don't forget to make your very own record!

Wandered into Belcourt Taps for a beer last night and was treated to some pretty good local music. It's a chill, divey-ish bar that serves food, has a full bar, and has several local beers on tap. And live music EVERY NIGHT. My first visit (just for a beer) was pretty good - I would definitely try Belcourt Taps again (maybe after a movie at the Belcourt - right across the street). Maybe next time I'll hang out longer and try their food and listen to some live music!

Great place to hang out with friends and drink craft beers. Three-Dollar Pint Night and Trivia Night are both a blast every week. Joined the UFO club and they've kept me coming back to try new beers - their selection is always more than abundant, and rotates every week or so. Highly recommend the Tin Man Damascene Apricot Sour Ale, and the Kentucky Bourbon Barrel Ale was incredible! Service has always been on point.

This is one of my favorite honky tonks in Nashville. The music is great and very entertaining. Plus you can start a tab and you get your card back, just in case you forget to close out. Gotta love the fiddle, if not... you are in the wrong town.
Went back to the Opry last night. Had a wonderful time. This time we sat in the front row of the balcony. Glad I chose those seats. Highly recommended if you are in Nashville.

Went on a Thursday night. Service was very attentive and eager to make dinner suggestions. We thought the food was very good.  Wife had ribs, I had BBQ salmon. Ribs were really meaty, more than she could eat. 
House band (BB King all stars) was just awesome.  Got to love the horn section! Just a great night!!

We had been to the Ryman Auditorium a few nights before, and while we enjoyed the show, we HATED the hard wood pews with no leg room between the rows.   If I had to do it over again, I would have skipped the Ryman despite the good music.  If you only have one night to view a terrific show with good views from all areas, and comfortable seats, go to the Grand Ole Opry on Opryland Drive.   You won't be disappointed,

I didn't dock the rating for this, but don't think you are going to this blues club to hear blues. Went twice this weekend and heard a mix of slick and bland 70s and 80s soft rock. 

Stopped on Friday night. This was the only place charging a cover. After we paid to get in, we found that there was no place to sit and we couldn't even get to the bar to get a beer. Didn't stay long because there are many choices in the area. 

Went for lunch the next day. It wasn't crowded but the service was extremely lackadaisical and very slow. The food was okay. The best thing I had was a tasty hummus platter, generous portion. 

We gave it two tries because of the iconic name, but I wouldn't go back.

The Tippler has a very smooth Al Capone style to it.  The Roaring '20s have some nostalgic appeal, and this place has done a fantastic job of recreating that feeling and that appeal -- but in Nashville and not New York or Chicago.  The ambiance for a good drink, a night out with a significant other, or just an encounter with a flapper are all present at the Tippler.  

The bartenders do very well from premium cocktails, to beer and wine.  Additionally there is a menu that goes beyond small bites and into the realm of hearty enough to make it a drink at the Tippler, food at the Tippler, and then finish it off with more drinks at the Tippler to complete your evening.

There is a coat check and a valet.  People will be dressed to the 9s and others will be in jeans and a hipster t-shirt.  They take all types at the Tippler -- including you.
An experience I won't ever forget!  All the acts were excellent, highly talented and very entertaining.  If you are a country music fan or enjoy any kind of music the Opry experience is a must!

The food is delicious! The gumbo is on point. However, the wait staff could use some pointers on hospitality. I thought being in the south people were supposed to be friendly but that doesn't seem to be the case.

The food was very good. Had ribs, tender and fall off the bone yumminess! Music was great! Service on the other hand was not very good. We were seated at a dirty table and it took forever to get it cleaned up. Wait staff seemed to have trouble finding a towel to clean the table with .Another thing that was disappointing ,we received our appetizers and entrees all at the same time. Service definitely needs to improve. We would go back, hopefully the service will be improved upon.

Have you seen The Babadook?  The Exorcist?  American Idol?  Have you been scared?  I have a horror story for you:

Being on a budgeted vacation, we thought the Groupon for Belcourt Taps was a great deal.  Little did we know, we were in for a bit of a surprise.  

Walking up to the taps we were horrified--no, screw that...earth-shatteringly afraid--to see Guiness and Blue Moon as twenty percent of the options available.  While deciding a bartender even told us not to pick the shandy outright.  That gave us, like, seven other options to choose from out of five or so.  We picked a few different IPAs, a saison and a few others we both forget.  We sipped them politely but as we left the establishment we found ourselves being completely honest, as all people do in the company of absolute naked truth: We hated all of them.  Not a single one hit a resonant note and we were ecstatic to finish them.  

The nachos were below par as well.  They were cold and they exuded a terribly proletariat attempt to disguise "refuse" as "finger food."  The toppings should be cold, yes.  The pico, the sour cream, the olives, et al.  But should the cheese be cold, dear reader?

Should the cheese be cold?

We lie awake in our hotel at this hour thinking that.  They gave us a two room with two beds.  We were charged extra for that, but mind it not, dear reader.  The extra weight from our sorrows of this trip shall be supported by the extra queen-sized mattress, as we lie awake, winking at the ceiling, wondering where we went wrong.  

Will anything cold ever be good again?  I'm sipping a microwaved, scalding hot $1.50 Fat Bottom Knockout IPA with relish, absolute decadence in comparison, knowing full well that both things that are cold and local beers will never be the same.

Nothing will be.
Amazing music, and incredibly awesome staff. Specifically Alexandria. I can on a Thursday night and she was awesome. The music was something you won't be able to experience anywhere else. I love it.

We chose this lunch spot because it had good ratings, but we were not impressed with the food or the service. The broccoli cheddar soup ordered tasted spoiled, the grilled cheese was dry, and almost had no cheese, and the other food was average at best. The wait staff seemed annoyed to be serving us, and wasn't very attentive. Also fairly hard to find location off an alley.

Once enjoyed this place.  Today's burger fell apart and watery, the bun was old and cold.  Wife 's salad was also old and whilted. 

Likely to skip this place next time we are heading to the theater. Music was good.   Back Ally Diner needs to be better to compete against new establishments downtown.  There are other choices.

Ate here with two friends, and two of us got food poisoning. Maybe we should have taken the hint when we saw they call themselves the "BAD Diner."

The restaurant had a cool feel to it, but even had it not made us sick the food wasn't good enough for more than 3 stars. Nashville surely has better to offer!

In honor of Mardi Gras I had the shrimp etouffee and cheesy grits. It was a spiritual experience. I left with such a deeply satisfied feeling. Seriously, it was so good it was mood altering. 

I don't drink but my friend liked the bar bourbon he was served. The place is a well-kept dive, the staff a bit punk/goth but friendly, the service was fine and I am now working on how to replicate that dinner because it was so excellent and I live so very far away from there. 

We went early in the evening and the live music had not started yet, so the place was pretty quiet, with BB King playing in the background of course. People who live in Nashville are lucky.
Great place for drinks or food. Nice atmosphere, good service and an incredible selection of beers on tap.

Save your money and buy a ticket to an actual show. Tour was rushed and was mad up mostly of videos you could find online at home. Only giving two stars because at the end you did get to stand on stage.

We took a tour of the Acuff House (limited time offer) to start off our day, but it can be done anytime because it's self-guided. It take you into the house that the Opry built for Roy Acuff 30 years ago. It was filled with mostly images and memorabilia from his life. The Backstage Tour at the Grand Ole Opry was led by Karen, who did an outstanding job as our guide. They take you to several spots that you can snap photos of and see where the stars spend their time. The tour moves quickly and you're not able to really soak in the history too much, which is a definite drawback. Nonetheless, they do a terrific job in the time they're given and it's a must-see if your around Nashville.

We've been coming here for a lonnngggg time, in fact, every time I visit Nashville we end up here at some point.  And, there's good reason...

BEER.  That's the main reason!  They have a huge selection of beer that they rotate seasonally with a large amount being draft.  They also have a gigantic selection of bottles, you will be pretty busy picking out that one beer you just gotta have.

Service has always been spectacular, never had a bad experience.  Wait staff knows their beers and are helpful with their recommendations.  

The layout is very comfy...the front area consists of a long stretch of couches and love seats to relax on that are overlooking the walls lined with garage doors...when they open those up on a nice day it's like sitting on your back patio, but better!  The inside is this huge cavern with a 150 foot bar and plenty of seating.  Great place to see a game, too.  They have lots of TVs and Projectors to keep your attention.  Additionally, they have a separate game room with pool tables.

Lining the walls are hundreds of saucers where only the very drunk and vigilant get a spot.  Join the club, starting drinking a lot of beers and get your name on the wall.  This was one of the first spots I ever saw with a drinking club.  I'd have a few plates if I lived in N'ville, which makes me glad I don't.

This pub's main strengths are decent bar food, well-behaved clientele,  a beautiful ambience, and location, location, location. 

We ordered a full order of fish & chips. Being from Milwaukee, we're not easily pleased in this department; and neither of us really cared for the rather bland tasting Harp lager batter of this order. There was no TRUE "Beer" flavor in the batter, it barely registered strong enough for my taste. Perhaps I'm used to the stronger Northern preparations where the bottle of brew smacks you in the forehead. This was just not enough for me.

It WAS better than most fish & chips I've had in TN, however; and the lemon tartar sauce was hands-down perfect. If you're not a fanaticist, you will be pleased. If you are, it's in the "okay" category. I weep, I weep for my hometown. 

Adding to my calorie-fest, we split an order of Bailey's Irish-cream cheescake with chocolate sauce and chocolate graham crust. It was indescribably good. I had't really looked forward to it; preferring my cheesecake a little plainer, but this one changed my mind. Live wild, I say. Wild! ;) The flavors were perfectly complementary and not overdone. The amount of Bailey's was just subtle enough not to be too sweet.

So, this place is what you call RELIABLE. Reliable for decent drinks, decent staff, decent food. 

The staff was a wee bit harried that night, but it was CMA fest- and they handled it VERY well. You can ALWAYS bring an out-of-towner in here. They maaayy see a stah!

Awesome beer and live music. Super knowledgeable staff! Located a little bit of a walk from the downtown full of typicaly honky-tonks, it's nice to get to a place that's a little more original. TV's for the sports guys was a plus for our group. If you love beer, this is a must when in Nashville!
Music was great but food horrible.  Service good but food so bad not worth eating there.  Just drinks and music.

First and foremost as a music venue it's a pretty solid place. Big state, big area to dance or be close to the music, lots of bar space. All the basic things you want. Maybe it was just because we were in on a Sunday but the guy who was playing did his best Jimmy Hendrix imitation. For about two hours he played more classic rock than Blues or Jazz which was rather surprising.

Food wise it's basically a southern Hard Rock Cafe....that's it. Nothing in the food is particularly good it's just decent at best. We had some fried appetizers which were all pretty non descript and unappealing. The gumbo I had was decent as was the Roast Beef Po'Boy. My colleagues that got bbq dishes thought it was ok as well. But given the price that's not a very positive remark on the food. Drinks were ok too, overly expensive crazy concoctions. I had a sweet tea vodka/lemonade drink that was a hangover (or diabetes) waiting to happen so just ended up with coke and a weird and somewhat off tasting well whiskey (avoid the well).

So it's basically a so-so music venue with not so great food. You could do better in a great music/food town like Nashville, a LOT better. Also just make sure that night they actually have...I don't know...actual blues musicians?

This place is not very big but definitely unique. Some people might be expecting a big record store and this place is not it. A colleague, who is a big fan of Jack White, wanted to stop by and get some record albums. 

We came in after having lunch at the Peg Leg Porker down the corner. The store is laid out beautifully - open and clean. It also have many interesting machines from the past that are still functioning. There's a small recording studio like a phone booth where you pay to go in and records some music onto a vinyl. A photo booth and a coin-operated monkey band. A bit of fun carnival nostalgia.

 Next door appears to be the Third Man Record's recording studio with a beautiful metallic door. Visiting a place like this has been most enjoyable.

They don't call it Music City for nothing. Waffles and waltzes, honky tonks, juke joints; music 24/7; mostly country music, which is my kind of tune-age. We stayed near the downtown area, and Broadway Street, is like the Times Square or Fisherman's Wharf of Nashville. Everything is there; The Ryman, Country Music Hall of Fame, Johnny Cash Museum, and so on...I was lucky to have a Nashvillian show me some sights not on the tourist map, and Belcourt Taps was one of those. Let me say, up front: it was simply Awesome, with great burgers and even greater music.

Belcourt Taps has lots of beers, Fried Pickles and Fried Green Tomatoes, but, let's be real--who in Nashville doesn't serve these items? The real charm of Belcourt Taps comes in a other ways. 1) The ambiance, complete with a front porch and easy, friendly service. It really feels like you've stepped into someone's living room for a spell. 2) Their crazy, amazing STUFFED burgers. Honestly, the burgers alone are worth the drive. 3) The music. For me, this is what made Belcort Taps stand out and above any Broadway honky tonk or juke joint.

For pictures and a more thorough review, check out my site: www.TNBTA.com

Cheers!

This place makes Tennessee look bad.  You can get great food all over Tennessee.  What makes Tennessee, and the south in general, special are the great people and ethics.  This place took a cover charge of which the hostess pocketed without providing a receipt.  She stated that there were tables available.  I couldn't find a spot at the bar available, let alone a table.  When I asked to be given a table, she said that there would be a 20 minute wait.  45 minutes later I was seated,  I was at the restaurant for well over an hour before anyone took my drink order.  The food is fine, nothing special. but this place's service makes it a place I will never come back to.  Beware of this place.  I recommend Puckets instead.

Super fun. The place has an especially exciting, creative energy. 
Everyone there was so friendly. Jess is the delightful person who showed us how to use the record booth and the song came out GREAT! There's a ton of cool stuff in the store too. So glad we stopped in! :)

If you're a country music fan, which I am, or even if you're not like my cousin, this is a great tour and well worth the money to see where the should of country music is.  Sure it's a little hokey at times but to see the dressing rooms where the stars get ready and hear some of this history surrounding how it came to be is pretty darn interesting.  I didn't remember a huge flood in 2010 but not surprising since I live at the other side of the country, but there are lots of photos of the Opry house, how it was destroyed and rebuilt and there is even a mural painted on the wall that was there during the flood and you can see the watermark.  You get to stand on the stage in the golden circle and they take photo of you which you can purchase or not, we did not.  Of course they have the requisite gift shop and the merchandise is actually pretty well priced.  This is a must see if you're in Nashville

Fun place to hang out and get away from the crowd.  The place is very busy and it requires patients to get a drink because of the crowd surrounding the bar.  The karaoke is fun to listen to and the atmosphere is very fun.

What a cool spot. 
I'm a bit disappointed to find out that this is part of a chain, but this fact aside, I easily fell in love with the beautiful building and interior, which allow for lounging with friends at a laid-back pace. I really wanted to sit in the lounge room, and imagine it's a prime spot for sitting and enjoying the weather and seasons. They have a decent selection of beers - of which our three-man team had no problem dividing and conquering. Service was attentive, and noise level was pleasant and cheery with the Pentatonix Christmas Album going on in the background. 

As a west-coaster, I'm a little jealous that they haven't expanded west of the Rio Grande. I could see myself frequent Flying Saucer on a regular basis with the ambitious goal of obtaining one of the hundreds of plates adorning their walls. Seriously a cool spot. I'll come again each time I visit Nashville.

Came in with a group of 4 and sat down and waited.  After 5 minutes, I went up to the bar and ordered a drink and took back to table.  10 min go by and I'm halfway done with my beer and a waitress comes by and takes everyone elses order.  

15 min later another friend of mine shown up and she had her two older teenagers with her.  Immediately a waitress came over and said you can't be in here past 7pm, they will have to leave.

Not sure why friends rave about this place, but don't think I'll be coming back on my next trip to Nashville.  Not super busy, poor parking options.   Far better spots to go.

We went on an October 2013 Monday with 8:30pm "reservations" booked online through Yelp/OpenTable, where the confirmation email said it was not a reservation but "priority seating." We only waited a couple minutes after we arrived to be seated, not very crowded.

We paid the $5 each cover, with the band also coming through the restaurant with a container for contributions while we waited for dinner. We gave money then too.

Both my husband and I had the ribs, which took awhile to arrive but were delicious, though they could've offered extra sauce when they brought them. We loved them, but some may have considered them dry. (We did not get Memphis style dry.) Coleslaw, baked beans, and corn bread were all small portions and nothing spectacular, but we didn't want any more because we both got big orders of ribs. I only tasted the beans, and they weren't great enough for me to eat on top of the ribs, but my husband liked and ate his but didn't want mine too. We had only sodas, which were very good, and they kept us in refills without asking. 

The band was very good. If you care about the music, it might help to call and see if you can get set times/break times. They stopped playing/took a break during our dinner and were back playing again before we left. While they're playing, talking isn't easy, nor is hearing, but the waitstaff was able to communicate with us, everybody shouting.

Casual atmosphere, didn't take itself too seriously, nice waitstaff, nice music, yummy ribs. They had a football game on in the bar area on TV.

On a recent trip down south my family and I made a stop in Nashville. Though our timing wasn't good enough to be able to see the actual Grand Ole Opry show we did take the Backstage Tour of this iconic landmark. 

The tour is $20 per person and it was great and totally worth it! The tours go every 15 minutes so you never have to wait long for the next one. They start you off with a brief film giving you a history of the Opry. They then take you on a roughly one hour walking tour through the building. This is one of the best tours I've ever taken and my family members agreed with me. 

Our tour guide was really funny, friendly, and engaging in addition to having a plethora of interesting stories and information about the Grand Ole Opry. They take you to every interesting area of the building you would want to see! The tour includes the Opry Post Office where you can see the mailboxes of all the Opry members. They also take you to a famous filming room where Hee Haw was filmed as well as the hit show Nashville is regularly filmed there. The tour also includes the stars entrance, dressing rooms, star lounge, and the stage. When on stage be sure to stand on the famous wood circle taken from the Ryman Auditorium, the original home of the Grand Ole Opry.

After your tour be sure to walk outside and explore the plaza complete with giant guitars and the Opry Store Gift Shop. Also, Roy Acuff's home is located on site to see as well, however you can't go in the house. Unlike the Ryman Auditorium downtown, there is plenty of parking on site here making it really convenient to visit.

After taking this tour my family and I are already planning a trip down to Nashville again for next summer to see the Grand Ole Opry show here!

Great place for live music and great food!!! I went with friends to Nashville for the weekend. B.B. King's Blues Club was one of our picks. 

The wait was long and they had a $10 cover but It was well worth the wait! I don't know the name of the band but they were amazing. It was crowded but the food  was done to perfection and delicious!! I didn't drink but my friends said the drinks were good. 

It was a fun atmosphere with friendly people, dancing, enjoying great music and good food. I highly recommend it and I'll be back!!

Is this place going to change your palette's life? No. Are they going to deliver solid food that never disappoints? Absolutely. Came for lunch yesterday. Server was awesome, didn't seem at all put out that I had to wait on my friend for 10 or 15 minutes. Salad with added fried chicken was a perfect $9 lunch. Service was friendly and fast and smiley and on point. I might be telling a different tale about the life of this place at night, but for a reasonably priced lunch in a part of town that can get a touch big for it's britches, this place is great.

Wife and I visited here, because we have visited 3 of the other BB King venues.  There was a line to get it but it didn't take line to be seated, was a little surprised about the per person cover charge.  It took a little while for the wait staff to take our order, but it didn't take too long for the drinks and meals to arrive.  The music was great and the band really kept the crown up beat.  It was a fun evening and we will visit again on our next visit.
after a semi creepy walk up, you find a great atmosphere and awesome food. The staff was friendly and quick.
Tues night is a great opp to hear some local color! All original music. Fantastic talent! Great local vibe. Super friendly service with good happy hr. Food is good but music is better!

We came for Friday night dinner before a show at TPAC, and we were very excited since it was our first time. We took advantage of happy hour and ordered a round of margaritas. However, when we went to order another round at 6:55 (happy hour ending at 7:00), the waiter told us, "that's not going to happen. She's got to make drinks for everyone else so by the time she makes it, it'll be past 7." This was super disappointing, and also if you plan on advertising your happy hour until 7:00 pm, you should honor that. Awful customer service.

My wife and I went on an opry tour while we were staying at opry land... 

I LOVED IT!

As a long time country fan, I was delighted to go behind the scenes in country music and learn all about the opry.

I also loved standing on stage, and having a picture taken standing in the wooden circle!

If you love country, you will love this.. I would 100% recommend to all of you opry nuts like myself!

The only decent place in the crap-hole that is Nashville.
I really wish I could rate the whole town - what a total pile of crap of a town!

This place is an oasis in the otherwise pathetic tourist-trap.

If you want culture, stay out of Nashville. If you want good country music, stay out of Nashville. Or, if you're reading this too late, just camp out at the Flying Saucer and the Country Music Museum for the rest of your trip. This is literally the only place with a nice atmosphere and the museum is literally the only place you will hear country music from The Country - instead of formulaic, corporation-made pop-country you hear on the radio these days.

Anyways, back to the Flying Saucer. Awesome selection of beer, it's not dirty, moldy or smelly like the rest of Nashville. I'm pretty sure the allergic reaction I had the entire time in Nashville temporarily dissipated while I was at this beer, I mean, place.

Beer. Beer. Beer. This place has it.

My wife and I were visiting during our honeymoon road trip. We stopped in at flying saucer to sample some local wares.

They have an impressive number of tap. Wow. Like, lots. They also had a few different flights to try. I had the Nashville flight (all local beers). It was a great mix of [what I would later find to be] some of the best beers in the area. Our server was attentive and helpful. The bar was clean and nice.

The bottom line: I will definitely stop in again if I am in search of beer in Nashville.
We all love the vinyl, and Jack White has a sweet place to play the music respect! Rare recordings, recording booth, fun music novelties and T-shirts are awesome.

I came here for country music but I got rock!   I would have thought that this famous venue would be bigger - but NOT.   It was about 1/2 or 1/3 of the Radio City Music Hall in NY.   Nevertheless, the acoustic was excellent and I was deaf by the time I got out in the evening.   um.. what did you say?

Hiking around Nashville makes you very thirsty.  So, be sure to wander by the Flying Saucer for some recovery time.

This place is a den for beer lovers.  And, surprising, the staff is very knowledgeable 
and happy to help you with your beverage selection.  The selection is incredible.

The food is surprisingly good, too.  I ordered a Cobb Salad.  The grilled chicken had been marinated and had a ton of flavor, the applewood smoked bacon was thick cut and crispy, and the mixed greens, tomato, avocado and egg were all very fresh.  

The best part in the extensive collection of "flyer" saucers.  Good food, great service.

No where on the website could I find mention of the age restrictions that occur after 7pm. So not only did I travel downtown with my family to try out this establishment, but I paid $6 in parking to only be told I was not able to dine there as it was 6:50pm when we walked in for dinner. I understand having an age restriction after a certain hour but it should be clearly stated on the website as 7pm and not just on your door so as to not waste patrons time and money.  Very disappointed.

Good music tonight at BB King's:  Eight O'five Jive.  We received good service.  The BBQ chicken was excellent.   My husband had the brisket and he loved it.  The BBQ sauce was delicious.  The fried pickles were very good.  I have no complaints.   I will definitely come here the next time we get to Nashville.

Back alley dinner is one of the best places to grab a burger and beer. The staff is friendly and fun. The place is down an alley so you feel like your in a spot that no one else knows. The singer song writer night on Tuesday is awesome as well. Get the poppers, they are the best in town hands down. Wrapped in bacon and cook to perfection. Finnish with the sizzling southwest burger. You will be in heaven.

Came here for a BLACKHAWKS game. Yep, ya know the Chicago Blackhawks, the best team in hockey.  The upstairs is a great place to watch the game.  Very large TV for great viewing. No matter where you sit you'll be able to see the screen.  Only 3 stars because the service was horrible. Bartenders were rude.  Still paying customers, no need for the attitude.

Visiting from out of town and found this restaurant last minute on a Saturday night. Seated quickly, food arrived quickly. Our waiter Eddie was FABULOUS. And everything we ordered was great. Reasonably priced, especially given the quality of the food. My teenage son had the bacon wrapped meatloaf, my teenage daughter had shrimp and grits. I had the chickpea and avocado appetizer with salmon added and it was a full meal. Great experience all the way around.

I had a wonderful time touring the Grand Ole Opry. If you have a AAA card you'll get an additional discount. The tour is a little over an hour and they start it off by showing a 10 minute video with Blake Shelton explaining the history. You get to see areas where they have filmed shows (Nashville, most currently), all of the dressing rooms and you get to go on stage too. It was an amazing experience.

Found Belcourt Taps after doing a Google maps search of the area. Stopped in for drinks and dinner. What a little gem this place is! Great beer selection and seriously good BBQ Ribs. I mean phenomenal fall off the bone tasty, tender Ribs! Actually talked to the man who smoked them out back. Lucky enough to be seated at the bar next to the owner who was wonderful to chat with. 
Now to top all that off they had a line up of young musical talent that was excellent! 
To sum it up; Great food + Great service + Great drinks ++ Great music = We'll be back!

Good service, good food. Limited menu. If you are not up for Burger keep trucking. 

Smells just like a back alley unfortunately.

great food, a little pricy so my friend and I just split a starter and enjoyed the live music! there was a cover charge of $5 but the hostess didn't charge us (??) it's a great family friendly place all night if you're ok with loud music.
I loved this place!!! Excellent music, wonderful staff, food and drinks came fast and tasted GREAT! Loved watching the people dance and the band made everyone feel welcome.

Seriously terrible. "Ms.Kelli" is the rudest business owner and cares more about putting her boobs in men's faces than she does anything else. The place is gross. Also, tons of underaged people seeing as it's extremely easy to sneak in the back. Don't waist your time. I feel terrible for the nice bartenders having to work under such poor management.
Backstage tour is very informative. If you appreciate country music and its history definitely check it out!

This little hidden gem is amazing!! Their awesome sandwich board signs on the street is what caught our attention. We even snapped pics of it & decided we were going to hit up this spot later. 

We came in to wait out the thunderstorm and happened to get a table by the little stage. The guy performing was awesome.  It was a Saturday night & one of the specials was $2 PBR so naturally, I had one ha. I wasn't too hungry but felt I needed to eat something so decided on their pulled pork quesadilla & a side salad. Both were extreme filling and super delicious; sadly, I couldn't finish my food.
