If we had more time in our quick visit, we would have come back but the next time I'm in town, definitely hitting this spot up!!

I've been here before and loved it but tonight the server Mary ruined our night.  We had company in from all over and wanted to show then a great time in nashville. Mary was rude immediately upon engaging our table and the disservice continued throughout our interaction.  She brought my mother-in -law's food out 30 minutes late with no apology just a snarky remark. Despite our lighthearted interactions she never acknowledged us with even a smile.  We may come back again for a great drink selection but Mary has greatly soured the taste.
Great place, good food, reasonable prices and great service.  A locals place tucked away in an alley.  You can't go wrong here.

Went to this shitty bar with a group of friends for a birthday party. There was only one white guy in the group of minorities and it just so happens that he for his cover waiver... No wonder why the bar is closing.
Had a grand time here seeing Carrie Underwood. The staff were helpful and very friendly. They really cared about the music. The atmosphere was great and the seating was very comfortable.

I'm not sure how people can NOT like the Flying Saucer. There are maybe the best hot pretzels I've ever had, dipping sauces, seats aplenty, booze, and a long-term beer drinking contest.

This outpost is right next to a sumptuous train station-turned-hotel that is definitely worth a look. There was plenty of seating even though football playoffs were on (the projection screen isn't the sharpest, guys), and our knowledgeable waitress helped me find an absolutely delicious strawberry beer that I had never heard of.

Loved it.

First time at the Nashville Saucer was a huge success. Parking was close, door greeter showed us to the kiosk when he realized we weren't locals, we got a table for two walking in late on a Saturday night, drinks were served fast & cold, and football was on a big screen right in front of us. Really couldn't have been better!

Wow! We had a great time at the Opry!  The music was awesome and we loved every minute!  There was a fantastic range of musicians, from old timers to new up and comings!  So much fun!!  We went on the backstage tour after the show.  CAROLYN was our tour guide and she was the best EVER! I highly recommend the tour and ask for carolyn!

First time in Nashville, so we had to go to the Grand Ole Opry. It took us hours to order the tickets, the website did not work properly. Finally it worked, but on a different night we initially wanted, because the website did not allow us to go to that night. Perhaps it was sold out?
We picked up the tickets at the Ryman, and the show turned out to take place at a different venue. We did not know this, we are not from around here and the website or the confirmation email had not mentioned that at all. The girl at the Ryman was really friendly though and offered to help us with everything.

The show itself was lots of fun! Good music, entertaining people, the commercials in between hilarious.

The tickets were very expensive and due to the venue that was 12 miles away, we were forced to pay $30 to get there. In the intermission we payed $6 for two cokes. Expensive evening.

But we had a good time.

Nice local american themed bar with a good crowd and awesome live bands. 
Stopped here while bar hopping around town and had a real nice time. The beer was cold, the staff was great, and the band was awesome. Prices were reasonable and they had a nice local variety of local brews.
Deff worth stopping in for a beer or 5 lol!

Great atmosphere, great cocktails, great service...they have all the bases covered!  I was part of a group of 8 friends that met on a Tuesday at 5:30.  They were very gracious and quick to accommodate a large, without reservations, group.  While waiting for my friends to arrive I had a great conversation with one of the waiters, Dalton, about which cocktails he recommended.  Nice surprise when he ended up as our waiter (he's fabulous!)  I took his advice and had the Spicy Gingerita...a margarita with a kick.  Loved the refreshing flavors and just-right heat of this beverage.  The complimentary homemade potato crisps were yummy...just right amount of salt...not greasy.  I'll definitely be back...super experience!

Not a bad place. Printers alley is pretty cool and every time I am around I end up in this place. Nothing spectacular about the bar. Not the best kareoke singers in the world but definitely a small town kinda feel at this place.

It's The Grand Ole Opry. How can you not give it 5 stars? Well I'll keep this review short. We came here during a visit in Nashville and was lucky enough to score tickets to an amazing show. It was being headlined by Carrie Underwood and featured Charlie Daniels as well as other guest. We had seats towards the bottom of the side balcony which gave us perfect view of the performers.  I loved the history of the Opry from when it was built in 1974 and was almost destroyed in 2010.  It looks great now and it's like stepping into a country music museum.  Seats were comfortable and the acoustics sounded great. It's a 2 hr show with 4 main singers being hosted kinda like a radio show, but that just adds to the nostalgia of the experience. This was possibly the best part of my trip to Nashville. Make sure you check out a show if you are in town!

When I first walked into BB's my first impression was I liked how classy the decor was and how it wasn't tacky! The place is huge inside and makes you feel like your in a real blues club! I went for lunch and had the catfish bites and beef brisket! The catfish bites were very delicious and the brisket & BBQ sauce were also very tasty! I bought myself a bottle of the sauce to take back home! I wish I could have went there for dinner because the menu and crawfish bites look awesome for dinner time! Overall I really liked and enjoyed my experience at BB's! I recommend this place to locals or people who are passing through!
Great drinks, burgers and home made potato chips  This place is hidden away but has a great atmosphere making it a very cool place to chill. Bring your appetite!
Love this place!  Very chill, great music, just wish they were Newcastle fans.... ;). Best place in Nashville.

The best ribs ever. If they have live music it's even better time. The spice on the ribs was so awesome with the flavors. All the food was really good. Mac and cheese and chicken fingers for kids. Would highly recommend.

Tristan

We found this on a whim after a conference at the convention center and couldn't have been more thrilled. We had five people and ordered burgers (veggie and otherwise) and the chicken Philly and LOVED them. They were flavorful, quick, and well priced. We are coming back here in April and will be eating here again. Highly recommend taking the walk down the back alley to find it.
Horrible service. Horrible owner. Strangers are allowed behind the bar. (Why hasn't the ABC been alerted about this? It's illegal!) Go elsewhere.

Really cool bar that we stumbled across for the first time tonight.  It's the only non-smoking bar I've found downtown that isn't a chain.

Prices were reasonable, scene is low key, environment is casual, and the food is pretty good.  Glad I found a bar downtown that isn't so crazy!

Will definitely be back!!!

The service and live band was amazing. Our waiter, Josh was extremely helpful with the food selections since all the items on the menu sounded amazing. Service was even better then the NYC location. Highly recommend the BBQ Salmon dish and the strawberry daiquiri!

This place is a beer-lover's heaven. If you become a regular, I recommend joining the UFO club. Once you've tried a certain number of beers (200 I think? Or maybe just everything they have?) you get your own plate, *ahem* saucer, on the ceiling. 

The food is good too, but the beer is what you really want here. 

Highly recommend.

This is a fun place to watch country music. We came on a Saturday night and watched a show from 7 PM to 9:30 PM. They had several musicians and the music is excellent. It is a nice auditorium, with comfortable seating.  The doors open at 6 pm and the staff keeps the audience entertained until the show starts at 7 pm.

The grand old Opry does sell out on weekends so I recommend getting your tickets several weeks in advance.  The parking lot does get full from the outlet stores traffic so I recommend using a taxi or Uber.

Such a cool place with an insane beer list and good food. They have couches in the front where you can chill. They have a program where you drink 100 beers (3 per night max) and you get your own plate on their ceiling and...some other stuff, I hope? Watch out for the bacon-wrapped jalapeños, they are spicy af. Green chile stew is good and comforting to me. The tots are weird, not like real tots. The pizza is good. Sorry I keep using the word "good". Just trust me, you'll like it. So check it out!
Great atmosphere great music the pork pulled pork tots we're phenomenal Great Taste. Also got the shrimp po boy it was good.

When in Nashville...since we were here we figured we might as well actually go to the 'Opry, took a chance and got tickets the day of the show, not the best seats but worth the price ($45) The performers were all really talented and we had a good night, really nice to see a show where music comes before egos..a nice experience..if we ever get back to Nashville, I'd do the Opry agin...5th star missing because I thought a beer only cost 9.50 at a NY Yankees game.!!

The worst. 
Most overrated. 
Waste of time and money imaginable. 
Portions are tiny and expensive. 
Definitely at tourist location set next to coyote ugly as well as hooters. 
You're already looking at Yelp so do yourself a favor and find somewhere that's not terrible to eat.

OK, yes. I MAY have a tiny obsession with Jack White (just a weeeee bit) despite his recent um... issues in the news with his former spouse and a certain other duo who also lives in Nashville, but I will always hold a special place in my heart for his music. I ridiculously have lived in Nashville... oh quite some time and have never stopped into Third Man Records until Monday.. Yes, I fail as a fan! 

BUT. With my lovely best friend in town who was visiting from California, we decided to fix my missteps as a supporter and do the Third Man Records tourist thing. 

It is quite small inside, and there were about 4 other people there when we came in not including the fashion forward staff member dressed in yellow and black only (Jack enforces a dress code people). 

I love the random assortment of white stripes collectables and the eccentric thrift store/antique vibe of the decor (some odd mannequins that probably come to life at night were atop the photo booth). The photo booth was definitely my favorite. 3 coins ($3) got you an old school photo strip with a very unique 3rd Man backdrop. Of course we had to have two sets each ;) 

I admit that I'm not a vinyl diehard like most of Jack's followers, but I definitely enjoyed listening to the record player they had blasting and looking through the unique assortment bands that have visited and recorded at his studio. They also sell t-shirts and other small items like stickers and buttons for a very reasonable price ($25 for a shirt ain't bad). 

Despite how hipster and chic the Third Man employee was, she was surprisingly very lovely and even took our picture for us. Thanks for the great customer service!

Since I don't have vinyl I can't see myself stopping in here on regular basis, but it is definitely a great tourist spot and your go to place for unique vinyl if you are a Jack White fan as well!

Decent food, abysmal service. We had the soft pretzel, beer cheese soup and veggie pita. No one greeted us when we walked in or seemed to even care that we were there. Once we found our way to the table and ordered, we saw neither hide nor hair of our waitress once she found out we only wanted 1 beer. Unmerited pretentiousness.  We won't be back.
Visited our first night in Nashville and had a great time! Great music, great food, and great service!

We came to Nashville and found exactly what we were looking for in Back Alley Diner. Stopped by for a late lunch, and it is a little hole in the wall bar with a nice attentive staff, quick service, cheap prices, and great food. 

It isn't your run of the mill frozen to plate bar food - the jalapeño poppers were the best we'd ever had and we could've definitely devoured another plate of them. My best friend and I both got the southwest burger and it was perfectly cooked and came out so quickly. 

If we were local we'd be regulars - they have great specials on drinks and food every day of the week. Will definitely be back on our next trip to Nashville!
What a great place...who doesn't love country music?!?! Just thinking about all of the amazing singers that have walked through those doors gives me chills...very beautiful venue in a beautiful city

Simply amazing. My wife and I saw Carrie underwood and many more with great seats less than 40 yards from the stage for 60 bucks a ticket. Where I am from lawn seats almost 1/4 mile away are 100 bucks a piece. Great venue with amazing history.

Our party of 4 walked in on a Thursday evening.  Paid the cover and was told we could sit anywhere in the bar area.  When we did take a seat we were told we had to have a reservation for seats, which made no sense.  So we stood at the bar instead and attempted to order drinks.  The bartender who served us proceeded to a) tell one of our party that they could not make a Manhattan because it was too complicated, b) not be able to say what beers they had on tap, and that all their beers were on the menu (yet the menu says "ask your server for our local beers on tap"), c) made a gin and tonic with no gin and just soda water, then d) once delivering the poorly mixed Manhattan insisted she made it right and that my friend didn't know what he was talking about.  Our party will actively recommend people stay away from here, it was the worst service we had during our entire stay in Nashville. If you want courteous service and professional behavior head over to the Whiskey Kitchen.  The legacy of B.B. King deserves better.

Best inexpensive way to escalate a good time.

I love it when a place tries to cram many different bar staples into one venue. I love the cramming because it brings all sorts of different patrons into the bar searching for a good time and as my motto states, "I am a personal tour guide to a good time".

Located in Printers Alley or as my drunk friend so loving called it, Harry Potter Alley, Kelli's Karaoke is 100% all Karaoke all the time. This may discourage those looking to dance, but the patrons don't try to out sing each other with ballads, like other established Karaoke bars. This bar caters to the upbeat and the tone challenged.

Kelli's also has inexpensive drinks. Our group ordered multiple rounds and did not break the bank. In addition, the bar itself contains a huge case of multiple flavored Jello shots that are hefty in both size and taste. 

In the back of the bar you will find decent restrooms and a billiard table. In the front you will find an ever small dance floor and decent size stage for singing. TIP THE DJ OR YOUR WILL NEVER SING. I watched for over an hour, before I asked my boyfriend if he paid the DJ. Needless to say, I got my 15 seconds of fame, after a couple dollar please and thank you.

We danced, we sang, we met great strangers, and we drank. At the end of our experience we found small vendors outside ready to sell cigarettes, walking taco's, and chilli dogs to satisfy all in our groups' post drunk urges. Best note of the night were the taxes that line Printers Alley to take us home without wait, for I could not walk very far with this taco that night.

Summer, 2014... Went to BT&T the other week when my GF and I went to the Belcourt Theater to take in some NASA goodness going on there. I have to say that the service was EXEMPLARY. Their selection of local brews was excellent. I love the fact that they seek out and promote local brews. The food was... well, it wasn't great. My burger, despite being stuffed with bacon and topped with blue cheese, was dry as a bone. Not quite vulcanized, but well on its way. The potato salad was BLAND. Even my girlfriend's fries were flavorless. Come on guys, ever hear of lightly SEASONING food as you cook or finish it? I will say this...I really did like the place itself. I liked the waiter and barkeep. I thought the place has a great atmosphere. The food needs a little work, though. Make that adjustment and the place could be a regular spot for me. I will indeed go back for another try, though. After all, everybody deserves a second shot.

Fast forward to 1/9/2015... Once again, GREAT beer selection and atmosphere. They have also revamped their menu and it is MUCH improved. Kudos to these guys for doing that. This is now a place where I can do more than just take in the selection of finely crafted, local brews and live music.

The live music atmosphere was AWESOME and so was our server. Only two complaints:

While the music was awesome, the volume not so much. You can hardly hear the person right next to you attempting to talk to you, much less the server attempting to take your order. Maybe it was just this particular night, but part of me even felt bad for the server, seeing as to how she basically had to get right next to our faces in order to be able to hear us. 

Second, the food was OK, but not great, especially for the price. I got the pork chop, & for $21, I expected alot more. The fried pickle appetizer, however, was definitely one of the best I've ever had. 
Overall, returning for the music and appetizer might be in the future, but didn't like enough to hurry back.

My family and I bought four tickets to the Backstage Tour. Maybe you're not the worlds biggest country music fan. I'm not gonna sit here and tell why you should like the genre. You can still enjoy this building for what it is! It honestly feels holy or hallowed. You notice that when you walk towards the main entry and look up at three impressive and understated chandeliers overhead. There's not a ton of chrome or bling in the design. I think impressive and understated is a great way to describe the venue in fact. It's both fancy and homey at the same time. I hope we can all understand that it's more than just a venue. It's significant culturally as well as musically. I can't attend a concert in the short time I'm here and going through the Backstage Tour might even be preferential for someone in my category. The tour is about an hour and it covers all the big chunk of the Opry's history, including all the various locations and iterations that the show and its home has taken on. To actually walk on the stage and see what the artists are looking at is wild. You can see where Dolly gets her fan mail and take pictures of her dressing room. (Yes, she's still a main stay at the Opry.) While the likelihood of me getting tickets to a premiere show here are slim, getting to enjoy a backstage tour and taking pictures from all angles of the Opry is still a big treat. The tour itself is partially automated through pre recorded clips starring Blake Shelton alongside a live guided tour from an Opry employee. It's quick, it's easy and the photos are precious! The Opry tour is a great way to spend an afternoon in Nashville and it's easy to get to as well. Thank you for the fun tour Grand Ole Opry House and thank you Music City!

This is a great, fun spot to head to with your girlfriends for an evening of cheap margaritas, jello shots and karaoke. I'm not one for singing but I certainly enjoy watching! It's a bit of a dive bar that allows smoking...which I'm not a fan of. They could do better at venting the place as it became unbearable after a couple of hours.

I would give the Flying Saucer 5 stars based on their pretzels and cheese alone. AMAZING. I literally dream about these. 

Plus they have a fantastic beer selection and laid - back atmosphere. Good deals: Monday night is $3 pint night and there is always a $3 fire sale beer. 

Service is hit or miss but I always keep coming back!

Everyone refers to this as an experience ... and it was, in the best, possible way imaginable.

WOWEE!!!!

Great talent, polished performers.

We won two Cracker Barrel rocking chairs - still figuring how to ship the other one back to Canada!  LOL.

They allowed us backstage for about half an hour and I can honestly say that I was backstage, at the Opry, with John Anderson singing!!!!  

I will be back.

11/27/2015 in town for the Turkey Day weekend. Caught the band 'Nashville Nobody's '. They were great !!! Friend ed hem on Facebook. They r the regular house band at Tequila Cowboys - downtown Nashville. They also travel a bit too. They sing a wide range from pop to southern country- and more. CHECK THEM OUT  online too  Facebook, Reverbnation too I think
Walked around the Opry grounds. Great photo ops.. However I wish the sign was all lit up! The R was out when we visited tonight, lame!

Great, fantastic, wonderful, a 'must do'....

Visited from the UK; Nashville itself. Had a few dodgy spots, but the Opry was a living legend - not that cheap, but you get 2 1/2 hrs live music, much of which is from top notch and well known musicians.

You can't go to TN and Nashville without going there - but book your tickets online in advance if you can to avoid disappointment  - top night out; in fact so good we went back the next night !

Had so much fun at WannaB's during a girls trip to Nashville. The people were nice, the atmosphere was fun and supportive and they have a great karaoke selection. Will definitely be back at an upcoming bachelorette party.

This place is really, really cool. Several cool vintage music pieces, small items and records recorded at the place.

This is a must stop for any music lover!

My first visit to The Grand Ole Opry. We purchased tickets months ago without knowing who was performing. I was initially disappointed when the headliners were posted, but after downloading both The Steel Woods and Charlie Worsham albums, I could hardly wait.  Parking was confusing as there were no obvious signs pointing to the main entrance, and after walking around Opryland (which was enjoyable) we found the Opry.  Easy to get in and the lines moved quickly. This was a Saturday night show. Seats were awesome.  The show was worth every cent. I accessorized at the souvenir shop and I'm looking forward to my next visit.

Food was delicious!! The staff however needs work, my waitress literally sat at the table with us to take the order which is unprofessional. Also, when i walked in the hostess mean mugged us and ignored us for 5 minutes and was reluctant to help us. Our waitress was kind of short with us until we inquired about alcohol then she lightened up. Gumbo& spinach dil were on point though.

My girlfriend and I were looking for a place to eat dinner during CMA Fest.  The wait time for most super Yelp-friendly places was an hour+ and we didn't have that kind of time, so we strolled into Back Alley Diner (BAD food, BAD drinks, BAD service is their tagline.... for Back Alley Diner, not because it's bad).

We walked in and it's kind of a hole in the wall bar.  We seated ourselves and our waitress came to see us.  We ordered beers and mozzarella sticks as an appetizer.  The mozzarella sticks were typical TGI Fridays style mozzarella sticks.  Nothing to write home about, but not bad.

For dinner, I had the hot chicken sandwich and my girlfriend had the catfish po'boy.  The hot chicken was probably my favorite hot chicken I had while in Nashville (I tried to order it pretty much everywhere).  It was crispy on the outside, seasoned wonderfully and tender on the inside.  It balanced well with the mayo and pickle on the Texas toast.  Really, really good.  The catfish was good, it's a big portion.  Good breading.  The homemade potato chips she got as the side was really what she raved about though.

The only thing costing it a fifth star was that it took quite a while to get our food considering the place wasn't very busy.  Took about 30 minutes after we ordered to get the food.  All in all, very pleased with the experience and would definitely return.

We didn't eat here so I can't rate the food, but the service and atmosphere are amazing here. I love the trendy decor and we had a blast w our bartenders. Unfortunately I didn't get all their names to give them all a shoutout, but Jacobi and everyone else there were GREAT!! This will b a regular stop when I come to Nashville! It's off the beaten path and just a great place to get away from the touristy scene!

You have to love country western but for a gal that wasn't really into it, I had alot of fun and foot tapping along with the great singers and songs that were performed.  Shouldn't be missed if you're in Nashville.

Best fried pickles I've had. Hot wings whee above average. Ribs where average. Overall the food was okay.

Music on this particular night was quality. Overall this is a fun place, but didn't come for the food.

I just had dinner here with a group of friends for a bachelorette party. Our waiter, Colin, was spectacular, the music was stellar, and the food was great! The food may not be particularly spectacular but it's good, downhome, southern bar food and exactly what you would expect and more. I had the catfish poboy, which was delicious, and we had MANY drinks. All of which were delicious. If I am ever in Nashville again I will certainly be back.
Always a great time here. Stacy and Kristen are great (and both absolutely beautiful, to boot!)

I love this place. Everytime I go to the CMA's I stop here for some Karoake.

Of course you may need to wait a little for your turn, but the crowd is fun and kind, plus I have seen some pretty good amateur talent.
We went on the backstage tour. I loved seeing the dressing rooms and the family room. The tour guides were very informative and helpful. I would love to go back to see a show sometime.

I normally go to the dan mcguiness in cool springs due to convenience of location for me, but was in the Gulch and so figured I'd venture up the hill and check out the Nashville location. Was very happy to find out was nonsmoking and was very happy to see that it had the look and feel of a pub as is advertised. Service was amazing, had a great array of beers available, some local crafts as well as the typical Irish fair of beers available. Had the spinach and artichoke dip while I was there(yes not very Irish but was looking for a quick snack), and the rest of the menu looked amazing, and would have had more if not for having dinner plans already. Bartender was very nice and attentive, customers in the place as well were great company to have. Overall a great experience and will definitely be back at some point soon.

This place is off the beating path... It is literally in a back alley.  

Once you get passed that and the "dive" bar aspect prepare yourself for some great food!

We had the fork and knife burger and the gargantuan double burger. The double burger was too much food but it tasted amazing !!!!   The gf loved her fork and knife. 

We added wings as an appetizer and they too were delish !!!

Overall this place was a perfect 5. Amazing food and a great atmosphere.  It is not for the snooty but if you like good old fashioned back end charm with great food then put this on your radar !

A really fun place for BBQ and music in Nashville. I know it's a bit of a tourist trap but if you're bringing your family with little ones, this would be an idea eating place vs ones of those on Broadway with all of the homeless musicians and drunks. I had the slab of ribs and thought it was pretty good!
Plastic cups for draft beer?!??? Really, Quinn???? Don't be duped by the $6.00 shepherd's pie on Sundays... Super small portion. This place used to be great.

I went on a Tuesday and It was packed.  Standing room only for 20 minutes then the bar opened up.  The food and the music was good. I had the hickory burger snd it was good. The music was the best part of the whole thing.  I didn't mind the cover charge,  just wish they had more seats that night. I would go again and would recommend it. Just go early to get a seat.

My fiancé and I decided to try this place last minute because we were starving. It was the best choice we could have made. The service, food, and environment was fantastic. The soul sampler's fried pickles and catfish bites were so yummy! I had the BBQ salmon that was to die for. My fiancé had the pulled pork and loved it. Beer wasn't outrageously expensive. Great place in downtown Nashville.

Went with a large group during a soccer tournament weekend, about 40 people. We did make advanced reservations and all was in good order when we arrived.

The wait service was good, but when the food came out from the kitchen they were a little confused as to who's dish belonged to whom. Small issue, but hey. Some in our group didn't think the food was so good but I had Carolina BBQed Salmon, which I really enjoyed. It was a large piece of grilled salmon served over creamed corn and garnished with fried onions and 4 large seasoned shrimp. Oh yea, and a moist corn muffin. I loved it. It was the most expensive item on the menu but I have no regrets at all.

There was a 3 piece blues band playing and they were very good. They played several blues standards and even led off their second set with a bluesy rendition of Miles Davis's "All Blues." See the photo I posted of the band. 

I enjoyed the joint very much and do recommend it for anyone looking for good food along with high quality music. It's sometimes difficult for a restaurant to handle large groups but BB's did it fairly well with minimal disruption to the rest of their customers as well. It a large room with great atmosphere.
This is my favorite spot in Nashville hands down! The beer is great, the servers are knowledgeable and the food is good!
Food was good and bar staff was friendly and quick.  Didn't think this would be great stop being more Memphis then Nashville but I was impressed with the stuff and would return.

Great beer selection (but you know that). Decent food (but you know that too). What do you not know? Getting a glass of wine of any type, is damn near impossible (but hey, it's a beer pub). And another thing, did you know that it's really loud? Yeah, you knew that before you got in the door.

I was excited to find a hidden little dive bar downtown but ended up leaving fairly disappointed. Our waitress was not the friendliest, and after my order came out wrong twice I finally gave up. I got the hot chicken sandwich and it was average at best. Definitely not true Nashville hot chicken, more so just greasy. My friend got a hamburger and it looked like a frozen patty. Not all it was cracked up to be.

We do not like country music but appreciate the talent of these fine musicians. The warm-up before the show with the hostess was Corny with a capital "C".  We found the "Backstage tour" a waste of money. If you want the Opry experience, just stick to the show.

.We had no idea .What a great experience we had at the Friday night Opry.. It was amazing that it was so casual and the performers made you feel like you were just hanging out. The experience far exceeded out expectations!

We ate here a couple of months ago so my review will be short.  I don't remember what anyone ordered but I do remember the food was very good.

I loved the atmosphere...a nice blues band playing great music! ( It wasn't so loud that we couldn't hear each other or have a conversation..it was just right.) 

The server was great even though the place was full. She was attentive and polite.

Would I return? Absolutely.
Very casual. Live music and excellent burgers. Loud so not for intimate conversation. Very friendly service but it gripes me when food for the whole party comes out over an extended period.
Worst customer service from Cam. I'd spend my money elsewhere as long as he works there.

This was my absolute favorite spot on broadway. We had a good time at other bars but this place is the most fun I have had in a long time. We walked in at about 8pm and were the only ones in the bar. We were disappointed at first but sat down to have a beer. Once we started singing people POURED in and we were glad we claimed our spots because the place quickly became standing room only and also completely filled up! The rest of the night I spent singing, laughing, drinking and making memories. If you are looking for a good night and great time in Nashville please just dedicate one night to this place. You will not be sorry.

The Pork Stew was AMAZING, but the portion was so small that I thought it to be a practical joke played on me by the waitress. It was still one of the best stews I've ever had though. A well balanced, spicy, and rich dish. The cheese topping was a wonderful addition, and because the pork was spicy the cheese did not bland the dish down. The stew was served with tortillas on the side, which was odd, as it's as far removed from a traditional carnitas based dish as possible. Increasing the stew portion, and adding bread as a side would make this a popular $20 dish. I would definitely recommend it to my friends and family, but please don't sit too close to me as I may have to steal some from your plate when mine is finished.

AWFUL experience! My group of 6 sat down at 11:15. Our food arrived at 12:15-- cold as ice. We could not send it back because we had reservations at 12:30 for another activity in town. When I spoke with the manager, he was very rude. He gave us a 25% discount on our meal. Seriously? We waited 40 min on brunch items only to receive the food very cold & we got $3 knocked off. 

I will NEVER be back!

The building is nice, it has a patio out front. They have a neat bar and some good beers. The service staff is nice.  Just going to drink here is a cool vibe. The food and menu are not good. Under cooked apps, for tacos they used pita bread cold out of the package. In the past we have given the food a try and have been disappointed. No more. May drink there in the future, but will not eat there again.

Great spot in the heart of the midtown action. We had a great dinner. Ambience is very cool and service was great. It picks up later with live music as they clear out the dinner tables, so go early enough to eat.

Enjoyed my visit here. It is in a dark alley, but once you walk in it is full of life. I had the black bean burger and fries and a few cocktails. I enjoyed it all and have found myself thinking about when the next time I can go back!
Music was awesome!  Food was not good at all.  Service was mediocre at best.  Would not return though I love BB King and Blues.
Had a great time! The live music was great and so was the food. Had the ribs with the cole slaw and sweet potato fries.

We did the Grand Ol Opry day tour.  It was 45 min tour showing back stage and the stage with the center from the original Ryman.  I felt for 30 dollars they could have had better content about the building and musicians.  However they started the tour with a introduction video of Blake Shelton giving the history and then split the group in two.  While we waited they had us seates in the benches and asked where we were from and told cheesy jokes.  This was a missed opportunity to give more history and content.  The tour felt rushed and did not give that much history or relatable information. The video with Blake gave the most information. For those who are deep country music buffs, as in know of the 1920 - 1950s music then this might be fun.  But they barely brought up current musicians or any stories about them at the opry.  All I know is what mail box Keith Urban is because the tour guide loved him.  I believe if they can introduce more stories of current musicians and fill in the wait times with more history rather than jokes I would have felt better about spending 30 bucks.

Good place to watch a game. Lots of TV's. Or, come for the 80's band, they're a lot of fun. The service is slow, at best. But, my husband had a great hot dog there!  About what you would expect at a sports bar.

Music was great. Atmosphere was cool.  Food was awful , not what you expect from down south.  Very disappointed.  Peach cobbler was watered down. Fried chicken was salty and dry.  Mac & Cheese lacked any type of flavor. And how do you ruin veggies ???
I have visited This restaurant twice and it has been great both times. The only issue I recall is a mix up of our food. But other than that great place great atmosphere! Can't wait to visit again!
This was a good place for a quick bite at lunch hour. It had a fun staff and good environment.

Spent a week in Nashville, attended a Grand Ole Opry show, had a backstage tour, shook hands with Vince Gill, Eddie Montgomery and best of all Dustin Lynch was invited to join the Opry Family, as well it was Trace Adkins 15 year anniversary. An awesome show in all regards, I recommend for anyone who loves country music to take time to attend a show.
Ps. On the backstage tour I seen the backs of Tim McGraw and Trisha Yearwood walk out the back door away from where I was literally 15 feet from me... such a lost opportunity

This venue is a must see for music and country fans.  The tour guide was great and it was real cool to see the venue behind the scenes.  I think its worth the 20 or so dollars.  It was more enjoyable than the Country Hall of Fame
IN an actual alley that you feel like you are coming in the back door. The place was divey, the food was great. It was a tad dark but it was good food and really nice service.

BB Kings Blues Club ligger utmed ett stråk på 2:nd Avenue centralt och tvärgata till den stora Broadway. Grannar med bl.a. Wildhorse Saloon, Hooters och Hard Rock Café. Det är turistmagneter allesammans, stora välbesökta ställen med egna souvenir shoppar och ofta med bra live musik på sina scener (då tar vid såna tillfällen ibland inträdde). Roligt att tillbringa en stund här. Bra mat och service, kul inredning. Värt att slå ihjäl några timmar här, men inget absolut måste.

It's been a week now since I went to the Grand Ole Opry, and I am still thinking about what a great time I had.  OK, let's get this out of the way.  I can't stand Country music and I don't know who any of these people are.  But wow, what a show!  From young to old, from experienced to newbie, it was a star-studded cast.  Talent everywhere, and I had a blast.  

They do things in 30 minute segments, with 3 performers each sequence.  All sorts of different genre - from bluegrass to country to what I would call country/rock.  

The venue is large and well ventilated.  Other than almost freezing my britches off, I had a GREAT TIME!!!!

At the foot of Music Row by the Roundabout, Dawg House Saloon is just a nice bar. Its lacquered tables really are spots to get "lacquered, and some do. The pub grub there isn't too bad and includes yummo Six Gun Pizza with 5 meats, 'rooms and special red sauce. The King (George) Strait Pizza is less overthetop with just a couple meats and three kinds of peppers including hot jalapeno. Pork and other sliders, fried pickles and lots of Hot Dawgs are there to. The "Asian Invasion" (is that p.c.?) tempura-fried brat has spiced slaw & wasabi. No beers on tap now, bottles & mixed drinks.
Fun atmosphere, great selection of taps. The building is huge with a variety of areas to sit. Id definitely come here again.

Went to see adventure club 7/28/13 at Anthem. Tickets were fairly expensive and it was a train wreck getting into the club. It was raining hard and they made you stand in line (with a pre-sold ticket) outside in the rain for almost an hour... Then they wouldn't let you bring your umbrella in so you had to throw it away :-/.

In the club they had massively oversold the show. They sold over 600 presale and then a few hundred more at the door. It was FAAAR over capacity. You literally couldn't move and the temp was almost 90 degrees (I saw a thermostat near the restroom). They could have sold about 300 less tickets and it still would of been too crowded. There were points where you couldn't even get in the main area of the stage because people were stick In The doors... 

Anyhow this club massively over sells shows and then scalps prices at the door. I don't recommend it :-/. I stayed until 2:30 AM and never even got to see adventure club because it was physically impossible to make it through the chest to chest club.

Wonderful gift shop (independent record label) in Nashville for fans of Jack White (the White Stripes). While wandering around the city we decided to add this shop to our list and had a nice little walk over to the shop. It was certainly not in the "high traffic" area, but the walk was really nice. We arrived around the same time as a few other groups so it was a bit crowded. The store itself is very small, but they have a ton of gift ideas in multiple rooms so we were able to semi-spread out and browse without bumping into one another. I noticed a recording area for you to go and record some music and they even had a cool photo booth! 

We looked around and ended up purchasing some Third Man Records gifts to bring back to some friends we know. The girls working the counter were friendly and offered some assistance as needed. So glad we stopped in!
Great food drink and service. I was hungry and looking for some food late at night. I loved the german plate.

This place is awesome!  What a surprise to find a place that has the vibe of a neighborhood pub in the heart of downtown!  The staff is incredible, the beer selection is decent and the homemade chips are to die for!  Located in an alley right off the Arcade, this hidden gem is a "must try"!

The Grand Ole Opry House is a beautiful venue featuring a wonderful show!  It's actually a live radio show, so the concert moves along seamlessly as each artist/group comes out to perform with only short breaks in between.  The night I attended, Rascal Flatts was the main act. I am a huge fan and enjoyed hearing them live. I loved getting to hear 6 artists perform in one show.  We heard lots of different types of country music. 

If you want a unique souvenir, I recommend purchasing the show poster - they are limited edition and show the date and artists that are featured that night.
The music and bands are always good but food is not really what it is hyped up to be, friendly waitresses and employess , they deserve 5 stars , it's the food that is only 2 star

Summary:  It's not really as much a record store as a tourist trap for fans of Jack White and the label.

As a vinyl collector, I had to do a pilgrimage to Third Man since I moved to Nashville.  I appreciate the love Jack White has for vinyl and his commitment to keeping the format alive and viable. 

Still, this "record shop" wasn't much of a record shop as much as a mini-museum to the golden days of vinyl and Third Man Records' inventory.  They have Jack White's Grammy awards, a Mold-O-Rama, a recording booth where you can put yourself on a record.  New vinyl of Third Man artists.  

For a collector, it's probably not worth the visit unless you specifically want to pick up Third Man or White Stripes vinyl.  As a tourist stop, it's a nice little place to pop in and say you visited while you're in town.

Bottom line:  It's not for the serious vinyl collector.
Alexandria is a phenomenal server and has exceptional customer service  skills. She made my B.B Kings experience perfect!

We were looking to grab some lunch and found this spot. It was not packed but we still had to wait for a table, I don't understand why. We had the ribs (delicious) and catfish bites (really liked the slightly hot sauce it came with). Also liked that the live music included two amazing guys on guitars and not a full on band like many other places in the area.

We were in town for NYE and was looking for somewhere to grab a bite and listen to live music. We came across this place while walking and decided to give it a try. Food was pretty good. We all had burgers. I had the chilli cheese burger. It could have had a little more chilli on it, but it was still good. I will say though, their homemade chips were awesome! They had live music as well. I would definitely stop in again while in town.
Day 3 in a row...get me off this night shift.!!!! i just had B.A.D 3 days in a row. this tuna salad sandwich was great like frosted flakes!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

500th review! For this momentous occasion, I had to review a Nashville favorite. This is for the blue room. I have no words. It's probably the coolest place to see a show in Nashville.

They are pretty strict on the no picture policy so you won't find too many of them out there. It's also nice because you can see a show through your own eyes and not the screen of the person standing in front of you.

The right wall is a half pipe. You have been warned. I almost slid down it. The floor is carpeted and the left wall has a giant elephant head. The stage is high enough to see and behind it is a room where they can press a record. We attended the Shabazz Palaces show, which was pressed while he performed, and it was killer! A. the show was succinct and B. it added to the vibe. The men pressing the record were wearing white lab coats.

They have a mini bar with beer, wine, and cocktails. Then there is a courtyard outside and bathrooms. The walls are tiled in yellow and black and the stalls have curtains on the bottom. It's so cool. I love it! The entrance may also be tiled, but it's definitely lit in a funky way. 

Third Man will bring in all sorts of artists and events. Sometimes they will even show a movie! You should definitely check it out. Even the ticket stubs are pretty fantastic.

Loved it!! A must see if you are in Nashville. The theatre is beautiful and the bench seats are comfortable.  We had been to the Ryman Auditorium the day before which gave us alot of background on the Grand Ole Opry. The format was interesting and although some of the acts should have retired years ago, it was fun. And...we got to see Carrie Underwood!!

On a recent Friday afternoon walk aiming towards The Gulch, we stopped in at Flying Saucer, thus not getting to our destination for quite awhile!

That's because our party of four landed in the ideal mid-afternoon get the weekend started location for beer drinkers.   Build your own flight is the way to go.   Several tastings for only $10 and the variety was huge.   I'm mainly an IPA drinker and had plenty of choices-Brooklyn Defender and several local breweries were on my "board".

A very laid back atmosphere here with good background music sure made the afternoon go quickly.

They SUCK! They are expensive and think they are so cool. We spent 45 mins in there and found some things that we might have bought regardless but when my son needed to use the bathroom they refused and made us go across The street to a craft store. DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME OR MONEY-many better stores for half the price and nicer people too! If I could give them  0 stars I would!!!!!

I can't really rate this club because I never got in the door but the way we were treated by the door staff ill never go back. After trying to figure out if they have a cover charge on their website, calling with no answer my friend emailed a manager. It said no cover for ladies and $10 for men on special event nights. I guess we read the email wrong or something and refused to pay a cover. My other friends got in after a lengthy debate at the front but me and my gf were laughed at so we went to whiskey kitchen. All my friends who got in said it was dead but music was ok. They regretted.The club has a cheesy VIP line and a separate VIP room. I'm actually glad we didn't get in that place but if your into that kind of thing you'll love anthem.  This is the kind of place a prada model couldn't get in because he is wearing a tshirt but another guy can stop by Walmart and get a plaid button up and docker slacks with cowboy boots and walk right in.  People love Nashville because its not like this place and I feel the same way. Let Vegas and LA do the pretentious VIP stuff but it just doesn't work here in my opinion.

We are from out of town and tried to go to puckets grocery and restaurant.  After being told that it was going to be up to 2 hours wait we decided to come to back alley diner. We should have left.  The air conditioning was out.  They were out of tea and we waited at least 20 minutes for that.  We ordered the pulled pork plate and the pork came out cold.  I wished we would have just waited at puckets.

The atmosphere is pretty tacky but the food hits the spot and the beer selection is the best in Nashville that I have found. Great for lunch but not dinner. 3 STARS because of atmosphere and the plates showing how many beers people drink freaks me out.

I really enjoyed my visit to Flying Saucer. They had a great assortment of beer, good service, and good food. The best part is that it was all at a reasonable price. I came on pint night (Monday) and was able to sample some local brews for $3 a pint. I would definitely recommend it it will probably return.

Still the absolute best Guinness in town :). Bar tenders are knowledgable, friendly, and attentive. The food is great quality and they have a pretty good size menu. The authentic Irish fare seems authentic to me and is actually really good. Still my favorite pub in town.

I feel like there really should be two Yelp pages for the Grand Ole Opry- one for the tour and one for the actual show.

After attending a show and then later reading the great Yelp reviews about the tour, I definitely wish I had done the tour instead!  The show itself was just OK. Here is my list of things I noted:

-  The Grand Ole Opry is not located in downtown Nashville.  If you are visiting without a car, make sure you arrange transportation

-  The theater itself was really nice-- definitely seemed very modern and the staff was super friendly.

-  The show itself is comprised of a number of acts- I think our show had maybe 5 or 6-- each performing 2-3 songs.  

-  The show definitely targets an older audience.  There is a lot of goofy old-timey country music.  If you can barely stand modern country (i.e. Kenny Chesney, Miranda Lambert, etc), you probably won't like this show.  I'm a huge fan of country, so I kinda liked the O.G. tunes.

-  Be prepared for a ton of commercial breaks-- I was really surprised by this.  I kept forgetting this is a live show on the radio.  It got annoying after awhile.  Especially since we paid $40 per ticket to watch the show.

Overall, I'm glad I checked out the Grand Ole Opry, but I wouldn't come back for another show.  For a tour, maybe.  It was a little expensive- especially after you factor in transportation.  And there are plenty of free music options on lower Broadway.
Music and a beer or two.  We liked the band that night, we did not eat any food at all.  It was a Tuesday night, in town for a conference.  It was not that busy at all.

Well...it wasn't Karaoke as we know it...but, that's ok...could have been a real fun place, but it was over-crowded, noisy and just gave off unsafe vibes...I am not basing this on anything other than my gut feeling....No seating....crowded to the rafters (hey...good for them!) but not really what we were looking for in karaoke....had a beer each and left...if you're into noise and willing to stand, go for it...We'll pass...
Great ribs, music and a nice atmosphere. Visiting for a conference and this BB King's was a great way to end my day!!

My kind of watering hole. Outstanding beer selection. Tons of good stuff on tap. Really cool atmosphere with lots tall ceilings and pretty cool decor from wall to wall. I got a pretty damn good SOUR BEER Flight here and i wasn't disappointed. 

Will definitely be finding myself here again the next time I'm in Nashvegas!

Was in Nashville for one night and Belcourt Taps was recommended for a non-tourist taste of local music and food.  Far exceeded my expectations. On a Wednesday night there were a couple of really legit female singers.  And the crowd was into the music which made it fun.  Also worth mentioning, the burger I had was way beyond normal bar food fare.  And very casual place, btw.

My first time to Belcourt Taps was on a Saturday night. I called ahead and asked for a table of 12! They gladly accommodated us and led us to our reserved tables. We had a great time! The music was fun and the atmosphere was real smooth. I tried their pork fries which came timely, hot, and tasty! There were only two waiters for indoor and outdoor guests but they were on top of things. I appreciated the great service along with great food and music. Will return again. The outdoor setting looked like a great place for bigger crowds too.

B.B. King's Blues Club was so much fun! It was definitely one of my favorite meal experiences during my weekend visit to Nashville. My friend and I stopped in for an early dinner (around 5:15pm, so no cover charge for us) on a Friday night and were seated immediately, right next to the stage for optimal listening! The Carl Stewart band was playing some jazz/blues classics, and every one of the band members was fantastic (and super friendly!). The vibe of the place is great--high ceilings, fun mood lighting, and pretty good acoustics. 

The food was great, staple, southern fare. My friend and I split a small order of the fried pickles (which came out like pickle chips and were excellent, especially with the dipping sauce! The small order was also plenty for the two of us.), a large order of the ribs (8 ribs, which was plenty for us. There was lots of meat on these guys, pretty solid ribs.), and a side of cornbread (4 warm cornbread muffins, yumyum!). We probably spent about 1.5 hours enjoying the band and our dinner, and spent right around $30 for the two of us. Craaaazy cheap for the amount of food we had!

Loved the music, loved the vibe, great place for dinner! But get there early if at all possible--by the time we left, it was packed!

Recently went to Nashville for the Alan Jackson concert. My boyfriend and I wanted to find a dive bar to have a quick lunch and a few drinks, so I got on Yelp and found B.A.D. The entrance to B.A.D was pretty neat as it was in the alley. Luckily for us, they had signs on the main street to point us in the right directions. 

B.A.D was just what we were hoping to find. They had good bar food and even better happy hour specials. The time of the day we went allowed us to avoid the evening crowd. I would recommend B.A.D to anyone who is looking for a place to relax and have a few beverages.

I'm giving four stars based on the AMAZING music. The live music is literally better than the original artists in a lot of instances. The food was good, not great, and the service was ok. I say GO, if just for the music alone!

This review is for 3.5 stars.

Your typical Flying Saucer.  Lots of beer, solid food, plenty of space, downtown.  Plenty of samples but I'm disappointed in the flights election as they only allow you to include beer offered 12oz or higher.  If you've ever been to Flying Saucer, then expect the same type of food and service.  Compared to Yard House and Bar Louie, I'd say it rivals Yard House and beat Bar Louis for this Nashville location.

I came here for the experience and it was a great choice! Talented performers, venue had great acoustics, and the staff are well trained. I've been to many venues and this is definitely well organized. It is not too far away from Nashville, I took and uber there and back and it was easy to get to. There is so much history, which was promoted during the commercials and found out there used to be a opry theme park which is now a mall located next to the venue along with a convention center!

Every time I come to Nashville, I make sure I can swing by this amazing shop. 
They rearrange and change it around so its always a little different when I go in. 
The employees are always very nice and may I also note, very attractive. There seems to be a plethora of beautiful women and a disproportionately high number of redheads working there. I found both of these things enjoyable. Also great attitudes from everyone. I've never gotten bad service or over heard any of them being rude or "too cool" as other reviews have stated. 
I buy records there each time I go. First time I got The White Stripes' De Stijl, White Blood Cells and Get Behind Me Satan. This trip I got The Stooges eponymous album and Blind Willie McTell Volume 4.
My fiancé went there a few years ago without me and Jack was in the shop that day. They're both from Detroit and my fiancé was at one of The White Stripes first shows in Detroit so they chatted about that. He said Jack was very kind and happy to talk at length with a fellow musician and pose for a picture after. 
I bought a couple T-Shirts this time and last when I went in. I am a small woman so I usually get a Youth shirt sized Large. In addition to them fitting better than adult sizes, I like the special designs they have for the kids shirts.
They have a lot of really cool trinkets and tchotchkes. We got some stickers, match boxes, I got a 45 rpm adapter, some post cards. They had some really cool journals I had my eye on but I was already getting up there in things I was buying so I exercised some self restraint and decided to save some stuff for next time if its still there. 
Theres a lot to look at so don't be in a hurry when you go in. 

Go check it out! 
And tell one of the pretty girls I said hi. 
;-)
~Zoe

Duuuude! This place was great! The music... oh my gawd! I was visiting from out of town and decided to give it shot on a Saturday night. I wasn't terrrrribly excited about the $10 cover, but took the chance that'd it be worth it. Surprise! It definitely was!
The BB King All-stars were playing that night and played some great tunes. Most of it was disco. The band and singers were great. There were more than a few cutting a rug on the dancedfloor

In addition to the music, the food was great as well. I had the roasted chicken, green, and mashed potatoes. It was wonderful!
I love how the restaurant was situated so that each table could see the performers. I had a great time!

Would definitely go (and even pay the cover) one more 'gain!

The food here was *really* good. Our server was good too; definitely in overdrive due to the crowds for CMA fest.   I ordered blackened chicken salad which was delicious. My company had pasta which was also very good. We would definitely go back. The music was great, if you like the blues. I do!   It's loud and cramped, so I would be selective on who I recommended this to, but the food was A+.

Meh. Warm beer, dry chicken wings,  runny queso, slow service ( and we never got our extra ranch for the wings)- we won't be back. The place was packed, which surprised me. There are so many amazing places to eat in Nashville- we won't be giving this place another chance!

Great service, amazing beer selection, big enough that even when it's full it doesn't feel crowded. I had several local craft brews at the recommendation of the waiter and waitress and all were delicious. I ordered the chips and queso with spicy chili and it was great!  I am not one to enjoy hot and spicy things but the blend of spicy chili mixed with the queso was perfect to me. Had enough bite making me want a drink, but not overpowering that it took away from eating them. They even have me a refill on chips since I had some chili queso left and there was no charge for it. This seems insignificant but many places I've been to in the past year charge $1 or so for more chips. Highly recommend this place...just be prepared for dealing with parking...don't be afraid to valet.

You will never see a larger beer selection ever again if you go here. The beer menu and taps were dizzying which was awesome.

They even have pre made flights ready to go which is a huge help. I had the $9 Nashville flight and it was perfect to tide me over while I looked over the rest of the menu. 

I didn't have any food but was with someone who ordered a pulled pork sandwhich. It was dry and there was no sauce to go along with it. 

I'll stick to this place for their beer and the cool train station feel. If I get drunk enough I may even buy a plate to put on the ceiling.

Brunch from HELL!
Don't go here for food, you will regret it.

Stopped in with some friends for brunch because we didn't want to wait in line somewhere else.  There were seven guests in the entire restaurant (including us) yet our food still took 20+ minutes and still came out COLD. They remade it but later as the waiter was bringing our drinks he spilled them on 2 of our guests.

The food wasn't even worth the wait, either.  I ate mine because I was so hungry but for the price I expected much more.  (I ordered steak and eggs)

I've been here for drinks without issue but based on this experience I definitely won't be back for any reason...and this is coming from someone who used to work at a restaurant so I'm more forgiving than most.

BB King's Blue's club is on the edge of the entertainment area in the heart of Nashville. They charge a $5 cover charge of live music and has a great indoor decor. 

Inside, the hostess asked me if I was having dinner or only drinks and told me tables are for dinner patrons only. I elected to have drinks and was directed to the bar. I really was there to have a good time with company and drinks, but to be honest, they could have sat me at a table which was closer to the live stage since there was an abundance of empty tables. 

The bar served local drafts on tap and everything was pretty normal. Didn't try the food but the live music was pretty good which has a blues theme to it. 

Overall, it was a good experience, but nothing that blew my socks off.

Amazing! At 57 I have finally made it here to the place I listened to with my grandfather so many years ago.
Also visited the Ryman too, love Nashville
Great acoustics but smaller than my expectation!   I enjoyed the venue and would definitely come back again...

I think it goes without saying that the beer menu is amazing. I was stuck with cider until the waiter recommended a few beers. Thanks to those suggestions I can generally get down with almost any kind of beer. The soup is delicious! If you are visiting from out of town beware of Predators nights. Nashville hockey fans are surprisingly intense.

ate here with the family yesterday for lunch the service was super slow and the food was cold when it finally came.  The turkey burger was dry and hard like it was microwaved.  The chicken cordone blue was overcooked but cold when it was served.  The pulled pork was flavorful and pretty good.  The service was so bad I will not return.

Fantastic and rotating selection of beers. A must-go for beer aficionados. Pretzels have been talked to death and for good reason. They are damn good. Frankly, all of the food is pretty darn good considering it's basically a big bar. The $3 monday pint night is a fantastic deal. Only real downside is the 3-beer per night limit if you're working towards a plate.

Absolutely incredible beer selection and tasty bar food options. If you like beer I guarantee there will be a beer here you will like, and the staff is more than happy to make recommendations. I recommend ordering the cheese fries with the surprise on the bottom, perfect to snack on while drinking beers with friends.

This place has plenty of seating, but often fills up due to events and such, so I recommend getting there a bit early and try to grab a table for your party as you seat yourself.
 Add photos

The only reason you would go here is to listen to the BB King AllStars. Amazing band! 
Don't expect good service, starting with the front check in experience. When you ask for a table with a front view of the band, all tables have "reserve" signs on them, with no one sitting there. My friend and I sat to the side, ordered dinner & several drinks. We noticed that several "reserved" tables were still open & asked to be seated there. The hostess said those were reserved for people who would drink. Now mind you, we had dinner already & several drinks. We told her we had ever intention of still drinking.....she had a terrible attitude. A blonde skinny chick came & wiped the table off, with zero recognition to us. 
Come for the music but don't expect any type of decent attitudes from service staff. They need to learn how to put a smile on their face or move on!!!
Great place for local brews & friendly knowledgeable bartenders. Breaded mushroom appetizer we had was typical bar fare. Got a Groupon for the beer flights & was an enjoyable afternoon.
Great place, first time here and already wishing there was one in NY.  Great beer selections and perfect comfort food. Grilled cheese and tomato bisque was lovely!

This is our go to for both work and play dinners when in Nashville - it is perfect for groups and it lands with strong drinks, amazing live music, and southern food that hits the spot. Dancing drinking eating and laughing - bring your kids bring your parents everyone will have a blast. Order the fried pickles, gumbo, ribs and catfish. And ask for Amanda she's hilarious and never let our plates go cold or our drinks get dry!
Great band! Food was awesome.  Had fried pickles, friends tomatoes, and gumbo which was fantastic.

Went to Belcourt Taps after purchasing a Groupon that included a beer sampler since my husband enjoys trying new beers. Parking was not the easiest but that's extremely common for the area. 
It was Friday afternoon and the waitress greeted us and asked us to please be patient because she was the only waitress there at the moment, which worried me. However, she never missed a beat. The beer was delicious, and the sandwiches we got were amazing. 
The Groupon made it a great deal, that's the only real downside I see is that it's not cheap. Still, for the quality we got I'd say even paying full price would have been worth a freshly prepared dinner, nice cold beers and a comfortable patio setting.

Thank you for a great experience!

I was visiting Nashville over the weekend (March 2015) and I was so pleased to go to Third Man Records and truly have exactly what I was looking for. The women working there (one gal had blonde two-toned hair and commented on my hair color) was kind enough to ask if we were visiting and suggested other cool stores in the city. We went to the other places and loved them as well.

But back to TMR, the perks of the listening booth, the unique selection, the decor, the staff, it was all and all perfection! You go here for a reason and they know what it is, so cheers to them for being exactly what a customer, vinyl fan, music fan, weirdo, desires. You know your stuff!

Visited here not during it's normal operation, but during a private event.

Cool space, I particuarly enjoyed the seating set up on multiple levels, including on the stage and the balcony.  Great size dance floor, and nice incorporation of tech and lighting.  Music was of appropriate volume for me to talk to my party and I thought the drinks were tasty.

As an Adelicia resident, I really do love the Tippler. I think it's one of the best things to happen to Midtown. It's a great place to dance along to a DJ on weekend nights, or host an intimate writer's round with the best songwriters on Music Row. (Much more sophisticated than many of the other Midtown bars.) I go to the Tippler at least once a week. I love the drink options and have enjoyed many small plates by the award-winning chefs. However, there are just a few things about MCT that really peeve me. 

First, their menu changes almost monthly. I don't mean that they change seasonal menu items. I mean they completely redesign the the way the menu looks, including the paper it is printed on, while also taking off all menu items that originally made the place unique, such as the Duck Burger, the Krispy Kreme Burger, and the San Fran Chicken Sandwich. 

Secondly, their fried pickles are cut so thin, that you can barely bite into them. What I mean by that is they are breaded in a really tasty, spicy batter & fried, but when you bite through that, the prosciutto-thin pickle slice slides right out. It's as if they only use 1 average-sized pickle to fill an entire basket of fries. An expensive place like this should not skimp on their pickles. If they need a lesson in making tasty fried pickles, while also slicing them thin, they should walk a few blocks down to The Row. 

Lastly, MCT always has a special "drink of the day" showcased on the chalkboards on each side of the bar, which is great! But whenever I go to the bartender and ask for the drink of the day by it's name, they look at me like I'm crazy and ask me to explain what I'm talking about. Then I point at the chalkboard and they say "Ohhh. I have no idea. Let me ask". So then, of course, somebody has to come over and teach them how to make that drink and they take their time doing a little taste test of the drink so that the bartender can then explain to me what the drink is. This has happened to me multiple times!! Yesterday, the bartender made a face as if she hated the drink after tasting it & THEN tried to sell it to me. Ridiculous! Their bartenders should figure out how to make the drink special before their shift begins each day. 

These are just some little things that clearly separate MCT from The "Always Classy" Patterson House.

There is nothing glamorous about this bar, but it's a lot of fun to hang out at. I love the bucket of beer option and their patio is great to day drink on. Lots of TV's inside if you are looking to watch a game. There was also a live band the while we were visiting. I would have given another star if it hadn't felt a little rough around the edges.

If you are a music lover this a great place to go.  Obviously the music for sale is limited to what the label releases, but the experience is what makes it all worth it.  The people that work here are fantastic and the variety of music that Third Man records is great.

We enjoyed the club very much. Not as crowded and noisy as others and the music was very entertaining. Completely enjoyed the shrimp, and the smoked sausage po boy was excellent. Loved that BBQ sauce!

Great service and food. Ended up there on buy one get one free draft night. Drink options were solid and fast. Waitress was helpful and we were both very happy with the food. Got the veggie quesadillas and grilled chicken sandwich. Also side of fries and house made chips. Everything tasted great.

Not a big country music fan but the history and tour is worth the $24 dollars and it is informative and very entertaining. I learned a lot and am eager to see a show. The tour guide was knowledgeable and not boring which was nice. Stop by and take the tour.

Ever been constipated so hard that you sat on the pot, leafing through magazines, reading shampoo bottles, whistling tunes, dreaming of how you'll spend your sixth million, if you should wax the gap between your eyebrows, all the while forcing your gut into Escherian contractions just to do the big job? Remember that feeling of forcing something, and it refusing to come out? That's how Anthem felt to me - a forced attempt at being a cool, hip night club. 

Don't get me wrong - with Red Rooster and South as the only options, Anthem offers a tasteful balance. But that is relative. Anthem's tastefully dark interiors, two level seating, two bars, brick wall with projectors does come off as a classy place. But if anyone has ever traveled outside, and visited bigger cities like Miami,  NYC, etc, Anthem feels half baked and affected. The music was loud and so-so, the cocktails unsurprisingly average, and the beer choices rustic, the sterile interiors....my friends from Brazil were unimpressed. Heck, even I wasn't.

On the flip flip side, I am glad that such a place even opened in the first place. This is hoping that other people decide to one-up Anthem and open a truly mind blowing night club.
Bartender and subsequently manager would not allow a+40yo friend to order drinks and food from bar bc of lack of ID.  Also $15 cover charge for essentially nothing.  Don't patronize this place.

So we were in town for a conference and want to grab some bites and soak in some of the live music. BB Kings became the destination, so we made reservations. 

The restaurant is very well decorated with tons of jazz and blues legends arranged on the walls with original art work. The music was smooth and well played. 

As for the food, it was just ok I guess. 
We ordered the brisket sandwich, nachos, fried pickles and other items. Nothing special really, just tasted like regular BBQ, nothing that will blow your mind. Drinks were good, it got the job done I guess.

Wow I was told they make great burgers and it's one of the best burgers I've ever had! Many restaurants could learn a few things from their cooks. You get your money and appetite's worth with a large half-pound burger and the meat is tender, juicy, perfectly cooked. The bun was very fresh, though the best part is the secret subtle seasoning in the meat (all I could identify was parsley) which is so flavorful you won't even need condiments (which I normally use but had no need). The accompanying onion sticks were crispy and tasty. This will certainly be my new go-to burger joint and the pub atmosphere is quite comfortable and friendly as well!

I had a great time last night at the Grand Ole Opry. The venue is huge with many nice, clean restrooms available. Inside the auditorium, it was a little bit less grand, at least in the seating area, which is pew styled. The cloth cover on the seats are slightly coming off. My main complaint is that seating in this fashion doesn't give everyone a fair space of room. For example, by boyfriend and I actually took up 1.5 (instead of the fair 2) seats and we were still nearly shoulder to shoulder with the people next to us. Not exactly the most comfortable situation. 

Like many, I came not knowing what to expect and not knowing any of the artist on the list but am all in for good music. I was blown away by many of the artists here-- some rising stars! They definitely gained a new fan! In light of the crammed seating condition, we had a really great time! And the experience definitely opened our eye to the different style of music out there. I highly recommend spending an evening here.

We took the backstage tour of The GRAND OL OPRY!  The tour guide seemed to be as excited to giving us the tour as we were to take it. It was refreshing to see. It was so interesting to see where it all began and how they have tried to keep stars "feet on the ground". They are a family and it shows.  We felt humbled to be there.
Bartender was fucking fantastic. Such a great experience in Nashville. Thank you sir.

Best bar in Nashville if you are a beer lover!  You're guaranteed to find something on the menu you've never had, or even heard of before! Their menus conveniently categorize beers by style which is convenient for those who know what style of beer they like. Not only do the have over a hundred beers on tap, they have many more bottled!  You can get everything from PBR to Wells Banana Bread Beer (which is awesome FYI)!

If you are adventurous like my husband is, you can join the UFO club, where you get a plate on the wall once you drink 200 DIFFERENT beers! However, I prefer to 1) save my liver and 2) stick with a few categories of beers I like best, and even then, I have at least 20-30 beers that I really like here.

Oh, and then there's the pretzels! Warm soft pretzels served with 2-3 dips of your choice. My favorite is the cream cheese and chive, but the queso and spicy mustard are good too! Their food is biased toward German dishes, and to me they are the best options on the menu.

This is our go to bar before Preds games and concerts downtown. Easy parking in the lot down the hill behind the building for cheap, then we walk to the games/shows.

Went to Belcourt taps as part of a day out in Hillsboro at the Pup Crawl event. Stopped in because they featured a dog menu and. We had three pups with us. 

Loved this place!!! Patio was dog friendly and they are going to keep the dog menu going forward, so that's great. Food was awesome as well. I got the stuffed burger special and was pretty blown away. They come with sweet potato, truffle, or garlic parm fries and on a pretzel roll. 

Best part of the whole experience was the management and staff though. Wait staff was awesome, super friendly, and the managers did everything they could to make sure not only that we were happy but that our dogs were too! 

I'll be going back.

I'm going to give this place another shot, since I wasn't really feeling the vibe last night in general and our server was very apparently new, as she told us a couple times. We sat down and it took about 10 mins for anyone to come by (not uncommon in downtown Nashville in my experience). It was another 10 min wait for our beers once we ordered (again not really that uncommon). Another lengthy wait to be asked if we wanted to order food. When I ordered I was told they didn't have any left, so I ordered a sandwich. Food came out fairly quick, except my wife's food sat on the counter as we stared at it and our server just kept walking by it. Pretzels were very good!! 

When our 2nd round of beers came out my buddy was still finishing his beer. Our server took it from him and then spilled it. Whatever. Then my wife spilled her all but full beer on her own (slipped out of her hand) and server came by again, shrugged and left. Didn't offer to get another one or come by to clean up, nothing, until we asked for our bill. I also wasn't wow'd by the amount of beers. In my mind the more beer they have the less specialty they have in one thing but that's my own personal feeling. 

All of that was honestly dismissible due to our server being on her 2nd night. I completely understand as I was a server at one point and am sure I gave terrible service at one time or another. However what prompted this review was this. I took my food home last night since I only ate about half. I just warmed it up, took a bite, only to find a big ol gnarly black hair in my sandwich. Sandwich was decent to begin, but after that I had to throw it out. 

I'll try and give this place one more shot but that might be the last time for me. Underwhelmed to say the least.

I haven't eaten here but I've definitely partied here. Crowded, loud, hard to get a drink....and totally awesome! DJ rocking good tunes, girls are hot and plenty of them, and has a Manhattan feel. This is exactly the kind of swanky, club scene place that makes Nashville a great place for locals. It's completely different from the tourist mess downtown that we locals try to avoid. Get a few drinks in your system, get a cab, and head here.

We stopped by here while it was drizzling out and we were waiting for our dinner reservations at Rodizio Grill. We did not know that the Kentucky Derby race was just about to take place and thought that the weather was to blame for the overabundance of patrons. This place is really big and it was jam-packed.
