The service left much to be desired as our server could not remember our order and needed correction multiple times. Additionally, the Flying Saucer is known for its extensive selection of beers. On the day we were there, they were out of 4-5 of them, of which my table had selected two. Kind of a bummer, but I wish they're write what they are out of on one of their blackboards or something. Also strange was the fact that the beer glasses come out soaking wet with water at the bottom of them. I appreciate it when restaurants take a minute to dry their glasses before presenting them to patrons.

All in all, if you're looking to grab a quick drink or mingle with the office crowd after work, this is a good spot. But if you're looking to woo someone or have any sort of quiet conversation, I'd strongly advise you to go elsewhere.

We had only one night in Nashville to hear music and I am very happy we stopped here   A reconverted home it's almost like sitting in your living room and listening to live music. Acts change every hour and all where incredible  if you have limited time and are in the area you have to stop here

Food is ok. Beer selection is amazing. Very loud, and has lots of college-aged kids. I liked this place quite a lot. Played trivia on Tuesday nights several times with groups of friends. Really kind of a great place for bigger groups.
Hot dogs are ok, they must buy their buns from Kroeger. Our waitress was snotty and they were out of coke!  Only plus on the menu was the cheese curds .  Go next door to Two Bits.

The space is small in the store of Third Man Records it is full of unique items. There is an old recording booth where you can still make a record to help you on your way to being the next big name in Nashville (not really because it doesn't sound great). You can purchase merchandise and albums, the staff are nice and don't forget to get a picture in front of the cool door.

dude i am deducting a star for parking, which you have to go down in a dirty and shady lot and also pay for it. the beer selection is all right and you do get some award if you drink like all of the selections. the appetizers are all right

Flying saucer is one the best bars in nashville ESP with the beer selection they have. I highly recommend  the Rocket Tots with the habanero sour cream--TDF. 
And to the girl who yelped that her glass was wet-- if u know anything about beer on tap it should be served in a super clean glass for optimal head and taste-- they rinse each glass on a high powered water blaster before serving. A super smart move. Thumbs up Flying saucer!

This was one of my favorite stops in Nashville. I heard of this place prior to going but didn't know much about it. I was pleasantly surprised. It was beautiful inside. They had a bunch of great acts performing, at least six or seven acts. I loved the bench seating, you could see everything no matter who was sitting in front of you.  It was just a good time and definitely a must see if your going to Nashville for a trip!
The burgers here are great. They served them stuff and non stuff. Don't worry non-carnivores, they have food for you as well.

Just went in for drinks and music. We ordered wine and the one I ordered they didn't have it so they didn't charge me for my substitute drink. The music was good, bit loud so can't really have a conversation.

I loved this place, mostly for their amazing wings at $.50 each. They no longer offer them at that price, it's now $1 each and you have to buy a plate of 8.

Went there last Saturday with a large group and service was mediocre. Unfortunately, our favorite waitress no longer works there. 

Without the wing deal, we settled on burgers. They were just ok. I asked for mine pink in the middle but it came out well done. The upside was their fries, totally a winner. 

This place has lost a bit of the charm for me that it once held. The location for the art crawl is great, but at this price point, there are better options downtown for dinner. I can only give it 3 stars now.

First off let me start by saying that I'm really glad I didn't get the Groupon, especially after reading some of the other comments.  Second, avoid this place if you are claustrophobic!  It's a really small space and the set up is cramped and awful.  I was bumped and jostled by everyone that walked in the door.  There is only one beer menu and a two drink minimum per person if there is live music.  Luckily my best friend, boyfriend and I are lushes; so that wasn't an issue.  The people performing were wonderful!  Which is why I'm giving this place two stars.  We also ordered a couple of appetizers.  We wanted the jalapeño poppers but they were out.  So we settled on the spring rolls and fried mushrooms.  The fried mushrooms were recommended by our waiter as being "the best."  Hardly!  They were hard little balls and had a weird, bitter taste to them.  The spring rolls were a bit better but not by much.  Definitely not worth $7 each.  Besides the misguided recommendation from our waiter, service was good.  However, I am in no rush to go back anytime soon.

This place is a blast and a must visit!   Crowded at the time we were there and it was a little difficult to get a drink so we just ordered two at a time.  We didn't sing but had so much fun cheering on the ones who did.  So much fun!!!

I don't know where the other yelpers ate but this was disappointing. I chose the catfish plate. Cute portion of a single catfish filet, dense tasteless hush puppies, lukewarm beans and tasteless cole slaw. If you're considering this place, go elsewhere
Of the several stops we made on the strip, this karaoke bar was our fave. Everyone was having fun and the stage is set so anyone can get a good view. Just a great time!!

I wanted to go somewhere for locals and found this place. Atmosphere was cozy and staffs were kind and really attractive. 
Had a blue cheese burger and pulled pork sandwich with Bloody Mary which was recommended! I'll definitely come back!
Great laid back vibe and lengthy beer selection. Food was also very good - salad was fresh and other food was tasty. Staff was really friendly and helpful.

Food is good. Music is good. Drinks are available. Janna the waitress brought us the check on two separate occasions in an effort to run us out I suppose. We like to rack up a bigger tab than she was willing to Allow us. The environment is welcoming. She as a server isn't. It was disconcerting.

Great little hole-in-the-wall place, literally in a back alley in downtown Nashville. The food was decent, filling, love the onion straws. The burger was just right, bleu cheese, bacon, yum!

Nice atmosphere with a live band, nice to relax and read while I ate. Will definitely visit again the next time I'm in Nashville.

All country music represented during show. Bluegrass, country classics/relics and the "new" sounds from up and coming artists.  My kid said, "mom I like all the music, the old folks and the new ones!" She saw the ad for the Johnny cash museum and she is excited to go there! This a must see venue in Nashville.

Family friendly, clean restrooms and helpful employees make it 5 stars!
If you love great music, it doesn't always have to be Country in Nashville.  This is truly the best of the rhythm & blues and a great dance floor to enjoy.  Highly recommend for entertainment.

This is exactly what it is!!! Its a diner in the back of the alley. Let me tell you, they have the best food on this side of Lake Pontchartrain. God Bless!!! I ordered the Turkey Burger combo with the fries and let me tell you that this is not your ordinary turkey!!!

You can tell these are not pre-frozen patties, these are hand made and the seasoning is amazing grace how sweet the sound!!!! This is a must. If you lucky, you might be able to enjoy the awesome bands while you wait for your food. I must say, I am ordering again!!!

Great atmosphere especially on game days. They have great staff that does a great job of managing the crazy amounts of people they get in there on college football Saturday's. 

If you are in town in Sunday make sure to stop by Spatzmatics after 3pm.

Number one on my bucket list was to get to TMR. The shop is pretty cool, especially if you are a Jack White or White Stripes fan. I was disappointed that none of the booths/novelties worked when we were there. The staff did offer to take our picture with the TMR yellow and black Polaroid film for us to have a souvenir. Very happy I was able to get an elusive Tri-color while I was there. They had very friendly staff, even before they saw I was dropping a weeks pay there!
Exceeded expectations! Great atmosphere and great beer selection. Service was great and will return when we are in town next!

I was here for a weekend with my friends having a great weekend away until they told my friend her ID was fake. She is more than above the drinking age. I also waited 10 minutes at the bar for a drink while the bartender texted on her phone. Horrible service. HORRIBLE

When I come to Nashville, I love to drink at this place. It's off of Broadway so you're removed from a lot of the tourists which a like. The beers are also cheaper here than on Broadway too. I usually order a bucket of beer and save that way. People I have talked to say they put on a good brunch and to sit up stairs. This place was crowded on the Sunday we came to but we were still able to find a good table. They have a floor to ceiling, wall to wall TV that they put the NFL, NHL, MLB or other sports on. They have food but I just stuck to beers and mimosas. It's quicker to order at the bar than it is to wait for a server too. They have restrooms on both floors too which is nice. They almost always have a live band/DJ downstairs on weekends too. The staff behind the bar are friendly and quick to serve you. If you come here, I don't think you'll be disappointed!

The food is amazing as is the music!!!! Best fried pickles of any place. Loved the jalapeño fritters with jelly. The gumbo and tomato basil soup just could not be beat. Then finished it off with the best bread pudding ever!!!! This place needs to be rated a 555555555++++++++++
Awesome music, the ribs were out of sight and our waitress Amanda was the bomb. We will be back

One of my favorite bars in Nashville so far. As a recent transplant from California, it reminds me of the type of bars I would go to out there. There are three levels, the bar on the main floor(there's a seating section and outdoor patios too), the lower floor where there's another bar, DJ and some dance space, and then a mezzanine overlooking the dance floor which is more loungey. Overall, the bar has a classier feel and people are better dressed than you'll find in the college bars down the street.

Drinks and craft brews are good, well-priced and never weak. I've never had to wait very long to get served. People are generally pretty friendly and easy to talk to(this being Nashville after all). And a good mix of people as far as age range and ethnic background.  Music is mostly top 40 and club bangers which I'm not a huge fan of, but it doesn't bother me either. It seems to get people in the party mood so it's all good. There is also a big screen up near the bar that games are shown on.

Nice place to hang if you want to pretend you're not in Nashville for a few hours or you're a transplant from the coast feeling homesick and don't care for the huge country-western scene.

This first time here, immediately felt the divey vibe. Loved the paints and the decor, self seating, was a bit busy but wasn't packed. The music was legit tho, they had rap on that flowed with the vibe of the place, when P.I.M.P from 50cents came on, all The patrons starting singing the first chorus. The beer selection wasn't bad but wasn't a lot for a dive bar, the food was the reason we picked this place. Once we were seated, we got our waters right away, order our drinks and food right away. We drove 2 hrs and was hungry and had a concert to attend. My beer and my cousin old fashion came about 10mins after we order. My beer was good for a local brewery, my cousin's old fashion wasn't as great as some other places. As time passed, we noticed previous customers leaving and new customers who showed up after us getting food. I went up to the bar to see the tap selection and get a tasting of the Rock Bold another local and had to order it from our waitress at the bar. It's been about 45 mins or so when she noticed we didn't have our food, then she said " I am not sure what happened to your ticket but I am going to look into it" at this point. I was beer #2 and borderline hangry mad.  She came back, apologized that the kitchen didn't get our ticket and asked if we were here for a concert. Which we were, she asked if we wanted to stay and wait for our food or go. We told her if it doesn't take long, she went to ask the kitchen and they told her they can do it. So we agreed only if it takes 10 mins, which was going to give us time to find somewhere else to eat. Not even 5 Mins after that our food came out. If it wasn't for the delicious juicy burger on that fluffy crisp bun with melted blue cheese and the amazing garlic seasoned fries I would have given this place a 3. But the food was good, I am sure it isn't just from my hangry stage but the burgers were cooked to juicy perfection and the fries were crispy but soft in the middle with just the right amount of seasoning that didn't over power it. The service was less to be desired but there was only 3 server/bartenders but still it shouldn't have taken 45 minutes to notice we didn't have food or come back to our table.  I definitely want to go back when I am in Nashville again and try the jalapeño poppers and give it another try.

*EDIT: changed from 1 star to 2, because the manager reached out to me about my experience.  Now I am changing to 4 stars, because I gave this place another shot and had a really good time.  I could tell that they have really worked on improving things in the last few months. 

Went with a group recently.  Two of us signed up to sing, and despite it being a packed Saturday night, we were still able to sing in under an hour (In the past, we had issues with wait time and D.J. favoritism).  There were a good variety of songs, as well as talent and entertainment.  Also, the D.J. was really nice.  I will definitely go back.  

I only gave 4 instead of 5 stars, because I wish they had better beer selection.  However, their beer selection is typical for Broadway bars.

"Your Turntable is not Dead"

This is the slogan at Third Man Records and they are doing everything they can to make sure that it is true.  Third Man's founder, Jack White, came to prominence in the band the White Stripes and has been consistently fascinating since emerging from Detroit in the late 90s.  The White Stripes were a vibrant throwback to Blues and Garage Rock, taking ideas that were from previous generations and bringing them into the modern era.  The same is true of Third Man Records, they are taking a format that belongs to previous generations and updating it to be innovative today.  When the White Stripes were covering Country songs from Dolly Parton and Loretta Lynn it was a cross genre surprise but now it makes the eventual move to Nashville seem inevitable.

For a person who's most famous band is built on a lie about his fraternal relationship to his bandmate it makes sense that Jack White would curate his own history and create his own museum.  The Third Man Records compound is a place of Pure Imagination befitting the Wonka-like figure at it's center.  It has a recording studio, offices, and a performance space, but the most accessible and prominent area is the store.  Rarely has so much of interest been packed into such a small space.  Somehow, without feeling cluttered they have managed to fill every inch of the store with wonder.  There are plenty of records for Jack White, his side projects, his side projects side projects and his legendary friends.  If you don't have a turntable you can purchase one there or buy all kinds of merch items from standard T-shirts and posters to a Third Man Rubik's Cube or fine jewelry.

You can gawk at the technologies that time has forgotten like a 16mm video jukebox and a record your own record machine.  The display case features actual Grammys.  The walls showcase the inventive records that the Third Man team have thought up and then executed with the wizards at United Record Pressing just a few miles away.  Even the bathrooms are cool.  I know it sounds weird but make sure you go to the bathroom while you are there because it allows you to see more of the property.  In the men's room they have a kooky upside down bidet that functions as a shower for the touring bands that come through.  If you are a music fan it's cool place to visit and if you are a Jack White fan you might as well surrender your wallet to them.
Great interior. Very hipster speak easy. Pretentious crowd but that's to be expected opening week. I'll give it some time and come back. Cocktails and light appetizer menu.

Ok, so my friend and I stopped in to see and hear some music, they were great players, and we sat upstairs, having been told it was cool. The waitress brought our drinks, which were overpriced and poorly made, after a pretty long wait, and we paid. She never returned with our change or a receipt. This is one of my pet peeves, and turned me off to the place.

At first was a cool place but the dj running the karaoke absolutely ruined it. My boyfriend and I put our names in for songs at the same time. My boyfriend went a couple of songs later and my turn kept getting pushed further and further down the list behind people that had just got there. I went up ~30 minutes later to tell him to strike my name cause I was done and leaving. He then says I'm up next and proceeds to make an announcement saying- hey if it seems you keep getting bumped down the list it's because new people come in and drop $20s in his tip jar. It'll be the last time I go to that bar and I'll make sure my friends don't waste their time there either.

Hands down my favorite karaoke bar on Broadway in Nashville. Drinks are moderately priced. Karaoke runs smoothly throughout the evening. Plenty of places to sit on bar stools even though it stays crowded and fills up rather quickly. Amateur entertainment at its best mixed with some diamonds in the rough. Lines can sometimes be long going in but they move rather quickly. On my 23rd birthday I sang here (another thing marked off my bucket list) & I'll never forget it

How can you not give them five stars!  It made country music what it is today.  George Hays had a radio show.  One of the singers didn't show up and they had a fill in.  Jimmy Thompson played his fiddle and they got a huge response to add country music to his radio program.  And the grand ole opry was born.  It is amazing how many places housed the Grand Ole Opry.  One of the buildings was the Ryman House which was a converted church.  The seats were pews.  They still have pews.  There is a part of the original stage in the current building.  You can stand on it!

"The Grand Ole Opry is the show that made country music famous."

Country Music would not be what it is today without The Grand Ole Opry. The Grand Ole Opry was where a lot of country music artists started their career. I took the day tour, and I found it enjoyable. You learn about its origins, go backstage, visit the different dressing rooms and see all the memorabilia collected over the years. 

My favorite part was being able to go on the "circle of wood" and take a picture on it as if I was a country music sensation. lol. In 1974, a circle of oak was cut from the Ryman Auditorium, and inserted into The Grand Ole Opry's stage. Hundreds of country stars have stood and sang on that slab of wood -- Johnny Cash, Patsy Cline, Dolly Parton, Blake Shelton, Carrie Underwood and up-coming country stars. The Grand Ole Opry has their own photographer who will take a picture of you on the circle of wood. It is a complete tourist photo trap, so if you are a sucker like me, you may end up purchasing a photo. If you don't like how your photo came out, they can re-take your picture. I recently bought 3 pairs of cowboy boots (everyone owned a pair in Nashville! Refer to that review here: https://www.yelp.com/biz/boot-country-nashville?hrid=tSVO1NK_msqpQ7JhkitFDg&utm_campaign=www_review_share_popup&utm_medium=copy_link&utm_source=(direct) lol), so I had my photo retaken because they did not get a good shot of my stylish Nashville ensemble. lol. 

If I am ever in Nashville again, I will try to catch a live performance. I may not be a country music listener, but I am pretty sure it will be a good experience. And you know I will be in cowboy boots, so it better be good. Yee-haw! lol.
I like it.. nice place to chill.. drink beer... listen to country.... & watch sports ‼

Where to start.... this rating would have been a bit higher but our server Heather was such a bitchy Cee-U-Next-Tuesday it totally ruined the end of our 4th of July in Nashville. I was in there with my brother who is a well known beer critic (he was not impressed by the beer) she got a little pissy when we started asking questions she didn't know the answer to ( like that's our fault). She is definitely not from the south as she doesn't have a grain of Southern hospitality that TN is so well known for. EVERY encounter with her ( which was few since she dropped our beers off and checked on us once) she had a really shitty attitude especially to me but was a little better with my brother but he is pretty cute.  She was nowhere to be found so we asked another server if we could order a pretzel. Heather come back to our table and sarcastically says, "oh so you changed your mind about food?"  Returns and tosses our plate of pretzels on the table and walks off. We had to ask another server again for our check. She brought it and disappeared. I asked the guy behind the counter if he could ring us up and said only our server could so we waited for her again. But the final straw that demonstrated her low class pissy attitude was when she saw I did not tip her then followed me out of the bar, stared me down and made a sarcastic remark about "have a great night ". I worked my way through college as a server, my kids were servers and my brother was a server and I am a very good tipper but I'm not rewarding bad behavior/attitude. If I was an investor, I would demand she be fired.   Almost all negative reviews (1-2 stars) for this establishment gave a poor rating due to terrible service and horrible attitudes of wait staff.  So apparently if you're a rude A-hole or bitch you won't have any problem getting a job at Flying Saucer.  Negative reviews seem to have no affect on Flying Saucer management as there are no responses of apology for the bad experiences which is why the bad service continues. 

We watched the other servers and they were friendly, smiling, and attentive to their customers. 

The only thing we had to eat was the pretzels which were fresh, nice and soft and pretty good but needed just a little more salt in the dough. 

Anyone playing the slightest attention could see my brother was reviewing beer and posting reviews. The beer wasn't that great but everything tastes a little better with kindness. 



My advice is skip the Flying Saucer and head 8 blocks to the east and go to Rock Bottom. Their brews and service were much better and the food was pretty good.

Splurge on better seats, it's worth it. A must see in Nashville. Plan ahead for artists you would like to see. They are strict on their no video policy. But if you are on the bottom floor, you are allowed to get out of your seat and go to the very front of the stage and take pictures during the performance.

What Nashville lacks is A. Yes, the letter A. 

Belcourt Taps, a once tapas bar, sans the A, and now a beer, food and live music joint, is really a hidden joint in the 21st S neighborhood. On a cold wintry night, to escape the howling winds, I ducked into Belcourt Taps (thinking it was tapas), expecting a plate of tortilla espanola, maybe a bite of fried eggplant with honey, patatas bravas, or any of the infinite little eats that haunt a tapas bar. But lo! it was now Taps and there was beer (lots of local ones at that) and food. And music.

The evening saw three sets of people get up on the little stage and sing and play. I detected two options of vegetarian burgers and after dousing with their bhut jholokia hot sauce (ask for it), I was on fire. The evening was on fire. My skin was on fire. My tongue was on fire. Everyone was fiery red and blazing hot. I clapped and cheered, drank and wolfwhistled. I howled at the moon and demanded encores. Truly, it was a magical night and I returned with some friends a couple of times. And both times, we were impressed and serenaded by the cozy and dimly lit interiors, great beer and good food.

Unless you tip the DJ a hefty amount, or hes got eyes for you, you're not gonna sing. I came to this bar visiting from 4 hours away because I love karaoke. I signed up as soon as I arrived and the DJ was very short with me, even after I put a few bucks in his jar. I continued to watch people who had signed up much later than me sing for about 2 hours before I left unsatisfied and frustrated. Not to mention you couldn't cuss on stage or you'll get kicked out? Seriously? It's karaoke not a church service. To wrap it all up, the DJ needs a serious attitude adjustment, and maybe a reality check. Good job pal, you load up your equipment and play country music for drunk people to sing over. Hop off your high horse. Won't be returning. This place was 2 hours I'll never get back.

We got there when they opened and had to wait outside. If you don't want to open at 8pm then don't post 8pm on your web site that simple. Then we finally got to go inside and had to wait around while they all stood around talking. The DJ finally gets up and takes requests after singing his own songs. Then he sings every other song himself while you sit and wait to actually see people sing Karaoke. No one is there to listen to the DJ sing. They are there to see karaoke. We finally left after feeling like they were doing us a favor letting us be there and being tired of waiting to see people sing. Left the DJ a $20 tip, bought drinks, were polite, but still felt like they were going out of their way just doing their jobs. We won't be back.

Visited Nashville for a night last month and loved Flying Saucer. The space is great, and the beer list is simply amazing. We tried some of the local beers, and let the bartender make some recommendations for us. The staff was not only very nice, but also incredibly knowledgable about the beers they have, which is even more impressive given the large beer list.

Beer selection is just great. Its always nice to be able to try new stuff. Service was pretty slow and food took a bit of time. The food quality itself is nothing to write home about but  this is the type of place to grab some beers and munchies after work.

We were supposed to meet some friends here, but they never showed up.  They have a very large selection of beer, but nothing that I thought was extremely difficult to get or rare.  Although they had a much smaller selection, I thought Beer Republic had a much more interesting beer selection. I like the decorum and would give this one a try if I was in the neighborhood again.

I love this place and none of the cons I'm going to mention have kept me from returning.

Beer selection:  Amazing. Large variety of styles on draft or in bottle.  They often run out of some. Not a huge deal but it happens often enough that I've started picking out a backup to order in case they are out of my first choice.

Food:  Pub food, nothing fancy, and I like almost everything I've had. Some very good sandwiches and I love the spiced beef topping for their pizza. Their pretzels are always a good idea. 

Parking:  sometimes there's a valet.  If not, There's paid parking in the lot downstairs- there's usually a lot of open spots.  Then you have to take the stairs or the elevator to get to the restaurant.  The elevator smells so so SO SO SO bad but I'm not entirely sure that is the fault of the Flying Saucer or a property management company. Also, if you remember to ask, your beer goddess will give you a pass for parking discount.

Service:  This is where it can get a little tricky.  A lot of the time it is SO good.  The beer goddesses can answer any question about any of the beers and are great at making recommendations if you ask.  We never have to wait long to get food or drinks.
Examples of the bleh-
I've had the displeasure of being waited on by a lady who rolled her eyes when she left the table. Every. Single. Time.  If I ever end up in her section again I'll move to a different table.  
A different visit, different goddess-  when placing our order, I asked if they had a certain condiment for my sandwhich,she said yes, but when it came out they didn't have it.  If I'd known I'd have just ordered something else.  Instead, I was stuck with something I couldn't really enjoy. 
So nothing tragic, but enough to put a bit of a damper on an otherwise nice time.

Like I said, none of the negatives keep me from going.  I just go knowing the food and beer will be good, but service may or may not be all I dream of.

Fabulous food and beer in a casual atmosphere.  We highly recommend the Spicy Beer Cheese Soup in the bread bowl.  The Sheboygan Side by Side (bratwurst plate) was wonderful.  Only disappointment was they were out of Turtle Anarchy Scarlet Harlot.  The Carson's Red Dawn was good so all is forgiven!  Service was fantastic!

Good Beer, great service..got a Groupon for 2 flights and a pretzel, no problem redeeming it beer choices were varied and good, liked all the IPAs that they offered..would return..worth it for craft fans to check out..!!
The store is very interesting. It has a recording booth that produces a vinyl record, a photo booth, wax figurine machine, and many other cool things. Plus lots of merchandise and music.
Awesome food, drinks and ambiance. Only negative things were no live music and the fried pickles were disappointing. Great place if you like the trendy, more upscale vibe than Broadway.

This is a great place for lunch, good value, good wholesome food. Very tasty lunch and beer is excellent.
Great atmosphere, and very good service, would visit again and would recommend if you are at this end of town.
Great atmosphere.  Food was good and  appetizer was great.  Catfish was excellent and ribs were ok.  Fried chicken was disappointing.

Stopped in here for lunch one day while at the Frist and really enjoyed it. The service was friendly and prompt and my food was out very quickly. They have several vegetarian options to choose from and their Hippie Burger, while different from other veggie burgers I've had, was super good. Their beer menu is insanely comprehensive, with something for everyone, and nicely categorized. Great lunch spot, very reasonably priced, I'll be back to try more beers and their cocktails for sure!

I need more of this in my life.

Did I know it was a chain? Nope. Do I actually care? Nope. In fact, I want the chain to come to Chicago, ASAP. Queue a Fleetwood Mac song here... You would never break the chain... 

Anyway...

This place is huuuuuuge. And the beer menu is huuuuuuuge. If you can't find something you like here, then you must not like beer. If you see the Blackhorse Vanilla Cream Ale available, GET IT. After trying this beer here, I forced the manfriend to drive 30 minutes out of our way on the road trip back north just to go buy a sixer of this in Clarksville.

Flying Saucer, I see you've inched north to STL. If you see this, and you feel the need to expand to Chicago... call me.

I came here with a few colleagues and it was a lot of fun. I had the grilled cheese and tomato bisque and it was delicious! Warning for vegetarians it has bacon!!! As a non-vegetarian it was flavorful and perfect for a summer time dinner. I couldn't figure out with beer to get, there are so many option it takes at least 15 mins to figure it out. I tried their ghost beer flight which is a super cool concept, they have 4 beers that are blinded so the customer or servers have no idea which is what and they are numbered. You can have one like picking a number out of a lottery or try a tasting flight. I would said 3/4 were really good, unfortunately I'll never know what the name of the beers will be. We also learned that to get a plate on the wall required to try 200 different types of beers.
Super awesome place with a great history! Never know who your going to run into there either!

Worst service. Hostess had such a bad attitude she threw our menus down at the table & walked away. Took 3 people on wait staff for us to flag down to ask for service which took 20 min for someone to finally come take our order. Another 25 min to get our drinks. When we got them the ice was melted in them, could tell they'd been sitting at the bar for a while. Go to the hot dog street vendor instead!

The beer selection here is awesome and changes regularly. The servers are always friendly and very attentive. The pretzels are a must have! They are served warm with your choice of dipping sauces. The regular food there is good too, but I can make a meal of the pretzels.  The only downside is that parking can be a bit of a challenge and you may end up walking a bit.

I thought we could get lunch in a relatively small amount of time. We had 1 hour for my wife's lunch break and we didn't receive our food until 40 mins in the building. Needless to say, we ate our food quickly and tried to pay, but there was one waitress handling way too many tables. Either they are understaffed or need a faster cook. It's never good when the people get seated after you and have their food come right out. The only thing I can say positive is the food was decent. I wouldn't go back.

One of the better local bars in Nashville! From the writer's night on Wednesday to the best Sunday Funday spot in town with the Spazmatics, you can't beat it! With all the TVs, it may be the best place to watch a game as well! It is a Bama bar, so Vols fans beware on Saturdays. The staff is awesome, and always on point with service and fun times. I would recommend for both locals and those visiting and looking for a good time!

Cooler Irish Pub mit Outdoor Bereich.
Da wir draußen sassen, fand ich im Vergleich dazu den inneberich sehr dunkel ;-)

Die Bedienung sind super freundlich & schnell, das Essen absolut LECKER!
Und Live Musik ist top.

als wir da waren gab es gerad einen Newcomer Contest.
Fun! Und super gute Musik for free!

Excellent ambience. Great service. 

Tried their Share Plates. Make sure to try their Hungry Farmer and Loaded Rocket Tots. Awesome!!

One word... Incredible! We were one hour into arriving to Nashville for our first time. We usually bar hop.. Nope there was no leaving this place. Just wow!!! You have to come, all the best song writers in country music are here actually on stage playing for you. Could not believe it! Kate our bartender is absolutely the best ever. Make a reservation it is packed!!

Went here for dinner last night. Was able to go straight in and get a seat as it was an early dinner. The waitress was nice. The nachos were great, my wife's ribs were great she said, my brisket was good at best you could tell it was dry due to being smothered in BBQ sauce. But overall was a good meal. The music was good sang everything from old country to blues. Will definitely go back.

After walking Broadway for over an hour, we ended up at BB King's. 

Unlike the places on Broadway, we didn't have an hour-plus wait; we were seated right away. The place is really dark, so be careful walking until your eyes adjust.

I had BBQ ribs and chicken ($20). My son's burger was "average" in his opinion (he is a burger snob). In a non-tourist area, I'd say the food was overpriced, but it was bout what I'd expect in such a location. I was disappointed that the $10 beer special, which included a souvenir glass, was a no-go since they were out of souvenir glasses. Boo.

"The Rhythm Section" was performing, and I really enjoyed their show. I could have put down a few cold ones and chilled out for hours if I didn't have to leave.

A solid 3 stars for the place and the food, with a bonus star for The Rhythm Section.
Wait staff was great, very prompt & friendly, but that couldn't make up for the very mediocre food.

Flying Saucer is my favorite beer drinking spot. I know, its a chain. So shoot me! 

I have been a big fan of Flying Saucer for years. It is just a super chill place to eat, drink and be merry. Their pretzels are an awesome addition while sampling all of the brews. I always park behind the building. They validate, so it isn't too expensive. 

Honestly, the number one reason why I love going to Flying Saucer is because I am part of their Beer Knurd club. I used to only drink the same two or three types of beer but now I am trying all sorts and enjoying the process! 200 different beers gets you a plate on the ceiling. I will get that plate if it kills me!

I've been to this place several times, and regret every minute of it.  They are a cancer on Printers Alley.  Their sidewalk promoters are aggressive and annoying.  This place is the definition of noise pollution, with their annoying whines echoing through the alley and even into neighboring businesses.  

With Printers Alley quickly becoming an attractive place to hang out, particularly at Fleet Street and Skulls Rainbow Room, we all eagerly await Ms. Kelli's closing.  Whether that is due to financial reasons, health code violations, or, hell, even a Molotov cocktail... we will welcome it.

The price is right and the food was good. I ordered a burger (obviously) but don't be fooled because they do not cook to temperature.  PBR for $2 and their fries were pretty great.  Off the beaten path and very chill....a great place to get your night started before the insanity that is Nashvegas!
Thought this was a bar... they only have beer. Really? We wanted Long Island ice teas but had to get cider. Gross.

What a beer list!. And not the crap that most places have. A selection of real craft brews from all around. And with Monday night being $3 pint night, you can easily try many beers without racking up a huge bill. 

I saw on Yelp that the pretzel was good, so I decided to try it. Cooked perfectly with just enough salt. Got it with the mustards. Both are good. But here I am thinking, "Self, this is a pub, of course they can make a pretzel, How about the rest of their food?" I tried their chicken sandwich and a side salad. The sandwich was good but the Jalapeno Vinaigrette was awesome. Worth having alone.
Fun "Realtor Night" with EXIT Realty Elite, Big Gap Music, and Nashville Entertainment Weekly with TJ Cates.  Some really good live music, food, and meeting new and old friends.

One of the coolest places in Nashville!   Excellent customer service!   A girl named Jess, which is my new friend now, was so cool, and, friendly.  Very informative, as well.   And, another girl by the name of Jenay, was very sweet, and, friendly as well.  The two of them made me feel at home.  It was a great experience.   I absolutely love Third Man Records, and, everything they do.  I consider myself very lucky to have the opportunity to go there, when I'm in town.  Very creative. Great music. & Top notch customer service.  What more could you ask for?    Thank you for reading.   Trent
Love this place.  Cheap karaoke and cheap drinks.  What's not to love?  Located on Printer's Alley too.

I attended an Event at the Music City Tippler last night hosted by Bombay Sapphire and GQ.

I must say the interior/decor and overall vibe of the just about two week old bar/restaurant was a vast improvement over it's predecessor the dull and snobby 
Miro District.

The staff was very friendly and amicable and kept the place very clean the entire evening, I even saw one of the managers wiping the counter in the ladies restroom. 

The passed apps were average for an event of that sort yet not disappointing in any way and although I am not a fan of gin, the specialty cocktails were enjoyable.

I enjoyed my first experience at the Tippler and would love to return on a regular night of service to receive the full experience.

After years of not going to the Opry, I found myself in Nashville and wanted to relive how fun the Opry can be. I was surprised to find that singers like Bill Anderson have decided to take it on themselves to give sermons on stage about an issue that doesn't exist. The saying of "Merry Christmas!" He acted as if the world is taking Christmas from country music. How ridiculous and what an unnecessary creation of making the Opry politically-charged, when it should be about good solid country music. It was awesome when immediately thereafter another artist came out and greeted the crowd with HAPPY HOLIDAYS. Bill - stick to the music and not the stupid issues dividing people. Jesus Christ isn't worried about Christmas being stolen. ;)

Food was alright, but what REALLY made the night was the fantastic live music. The band was perfect, completely in sync, meddled with the crowd just right. 

Go for the music, eat some of the food - I had the DEBRIS Burger - brisket, beef patties, cheese, it was worth it. Fries were perfectly crispy.

Used to love this place and gave it a glowing review once upon a time. But we went in a few weeks ago and were shocked to find the interior redecorated (cheaper tables and chairs) & the menu COMPLETELY different. They used to have really cool menus with a huge selection of food and drink- their menus now are just basic and very limited on the food front. It's obvious the Tippler just wants to be a bar now- don't bother coming here for food. The drinks are really great, but it's just a bummer that this used to be a spot for amazing food AND amazing drinks. And it definitely had a classier vibe before. Oh well- on to the Patterson House!

Sat at a table in the bar area Sunday night , Good blues music but too loud for conversation, spinach dip was luke warm, corn chips stale, service was slow. We waited 30+ minutes for our food and we sat with our empty appetizer plates and drinks in front of us the whole time we waited for our food, not once did the waitress reassure us that our food was still coming. We had to flag her down every time we needed something, Once we got our food there were multiple mistakes made with our meals. And had no silverware, We then sat with empty food plates until we were able to flag her down for the bill. To end the night we waited forever for her to finally remember to bring us the bill.... Her name was Jen

PS there was no manager in sight

We went pretty late at night after dinner for snacks, drinks and good music.  The ambiance was so much fun and the BB King All Stars (the live band) were very entertaining.  We got some nachos and a side of mac and cheese to snack on that were both very good.  The band was a lot of fun and a lot of people were dancing.  I'm not a country music fan, so finding a great alternative in Nashville was exciting.  The service was great and I would go back.

The Flying Saucer was a fun novelty to me when I first moved here but for many reasons has lost favor with me.  It's not that there's anything bad about it per se, it's that it's always so packed.  No matter when you come in, even on the weekends, I feel like it's a battle of epic proportions to find a seat and get a server.  They have a wonderful selections of beers (and other alcohols too, but seriously this is a beer joint so let's focus on that) but due to the crowds it can be hard to attain one of these tasty beverages.  The servers are good, don't get me wrong (and gentlemen, they will grace your presence in schoolgirl skirts and pun-y t-shirts) but they are stretched thin over such massive crowds that gather here constantly.  I would say its safe to go with 2-4 people, because beyond that seating is improbable.  This place is great for watching hockey games and football with a big projection screen.  The food is typical bar fare, though I have to recommend the giant pretzels and they go well with all the beers.  They have valet parking and a large paid lot around back but you can also try to park by Cummins Station right up the road too.  I like coming here on off days now, when the crowds are slightly thinner, and they have great beer specials throughout the week.  Really, its not the establishment itself that only gets 3 stars, its that coming here is like running an obstacle course through throngs of others here because they too love the beer selection.  So the Saucer and I have a tumultuous love/hate relationship, but I will still go back for those pretzels and whatever is on the fire sale (a great excuse to try new brews).  Plus you can become part of their beer club and, once trying all the beers, can get your name on a plate on the wall.  Those plates make great conversation pieces with friends as well.
Great tour along with a lot of information. Groups are small with plenty of time to take pictures.

I was raised on Country, however, love all genres.  My parents use to visit the Opry every few years, but I've never been.  A recent business trip had me less than an hour away, so I had to make plans to bring my wife for a weekend experience in Nashville and the Grand Ole Opry. 

The sound, the lights, the talent all combined to make it a once in a lifetime experience.  

We also purchased the backstage post show tour.  We were fortunate to see Bill Anderson back stage and he spoke to us as he was leaving.  We were amazed at all that goes on back stage.  

We would definitely visit again.

What other place is a vinyl-only record store with a listening booth sporting two record players (for those of you who have never operated a record before, don't fret, they have a touch screen player as well ;)), a recording booth, and a host of cool throwback paraphernalia all over the store??!!!  The answer is no place but Third Man Records.  This is not your momma's brick and morter vinyl shop thanks to its well known owner, Jack White.  Unsurprisingly there are plenty of records from Mr. White's own personal discography, but this is less an homage to White himself and moreso a tribute to the eclectic collection of talent he has managed to gather under his umbrella.  Though the retail shop is small, what it lacks in size it makes up in spades with personality.  Whether you're a White fan or just want to take some quirky pics for your Instagram account, make your way on over to the shop!

Overall good tour of the facility. We did did to see areas backstage that are normally not seen. We were able to see into and go into some very nicely decorated dressing rooms. Way over priced. Would be nice to have some discounts for seniors and lower cost for children under 18. 45 minute total tour with at least having been covered by watching videos or standing in line to get a forced picture taken.

Came here with a group of about 75 students for a convention. Food came out very fast, however it was cold and crusty. Drinks took forever to come out, so we had to eat without anything to drink. The environment is great and the live music is awesome! Not sure if food would've been better if it wasn't such a large group.

Love, love, love this place. 

 We parked ourselves at the bar and sampled an array of cocktails throughout our evening.  I started off with a Moscow Mule.  They make their own ginger soda base for this drink and it was absolute perfection.  Wasn't heavy or too sweet and I tasted hardly any carbonation.   Tippler also has cocktails on tap.  We tried a manhattan.  It was a little too strong for me but my date had no problem drinking that up.  My 4th cocktail of the night (#3 was a margarita) was a fun little bitter and citrusy concoction called the "I'm Not Bitter".  I hit my boozy limit after that one. 

The food was delicious.  I like that they have a small menu and can pack so much variety in it.  My sandwich was tasty as was my date's, which he graciously allowed me to sample.  If you get anything off the menu- get the truffle fries.  Oh.  My.  Goodness.   You will not regret it.

BAD is Good! Always have such a wonderful time with the BAD crew with each visit! The music is always on point and the food is Ahh-mazing! Their signs in the evening are creative genius~ness. The place is a little hard to find, but just give them a ring and ask for Richard for directions! Cheers!

My new favorite place! It was our first visit at the opry, and my husband and I loved it. There is no better way to see several great artists all in one night, at such a historical place that means so much to the country artists themselves. We were able to get better seats off of stubhub, and were on the main level rather than the balcony. Although they it looked like any seat would be a good seat! Love love love, and can't wait to go back one day!

Food, atmosphere, live music and service were all fantastic! I had the nachos (delicious) and pulled pork sliders (yum!). The live music added to the atmosphere and made our lunch more enjoyable. Will definitely be back!

Ok so I know these signature places are usually cheesy but this place seemed to fit the blues bar bill. Stage placed perfectly, real blues and bar tender that was super attentive. Like most of Nashville the music was great but really impressed with the whole place. Great fan of the blues scene in Chicago but some of those places should learn something from this place.

I was pleasantly surprised!  I was with a large group of 20+ people and the service was friendly and great for the size of our party. The beer list is impressive and the food very good!  The soft pretzels were the best I ever had with some GREAT mustard!!
Our visit to the Grand Ole Opry was one of the best part of our trip.. Can't wait to go back.

The beer selection was outstanding....like the bartender said..."if you can't find something you like then you don't like beer".  And I completely agree!  You can taste test what you like until you find something.  The food was fantastic....I ordered the pretzels,which were chewy on the outside and soft on the insid and  the green chili pork stew was a perfect blend of spicy and smoky all with soft corn tortilla paired with it. 

My only beef was the parking....I paid $12 for hours.  Surely I'm missing the secret code.  I would hate to think that a restaurant allows their patrons to get royally screwed by the Public Transit system.

Best selection of beer in Music City. Always something new to try. Food is really good, and the service is great even when the place is packed. The atmosphere is amazing. Makes you feel like you are in a large pub or beer garden. Great place to watch The Preds play.

Being a musician myself, I was extremely skeptical about visiting the Grand Ole Opry for myself.  in fact, it took me over 6 months before I could even consider purchasing tickets for myself, my boyfriend, and my best friend who was visiting from Kansas City.  Obviously, I bit the bullet and visited the Opry with my guests, and we all had a surprisingly great time!  It was very fun to be a part of a live radio show with so many different acts.  We bought tickets in the cheap seats, which were perfect--they weren't overly crowded, so we could loudly laugh at the ridiculous country acts, take pictures, be silly, and yet still enjoy and engage in the acts we were interested in.  I was especially impressed with the variety of performers--we saw everything from square dancers to bluegrass bands to pop-country crossovers.  Such fun for all of us!

I'd definitely return here with other out of towners, or whenever I'm looking for something fun and "Nashvillian" to do.

I had such a great time here!

We arrived on a Saturday night and we were not disappointed. We waited about an hour to be seated...they were super busy and weren't taking reservations.

Service: our waiter was nice but don't expect a quick turn around between the time you order and when your food is actually ready. We were definitely glad we ordered an appetizer with our meal.

Food: I ordered the catfish with mac and cheese. The catfish was delicious. Seasoned well and moist. The mac and cheese was just OK. It had potential but because they used longer noodle none of the sauce or the cheese for that matter actually stuck to it. The cole slaw was yummy.

Atmosphere: this place would get 5 stars alone if it was just for the music and the way it makes you feel just being in there. The bands were great and really had the crowd going. I loved seeing people dancing in their chairs and even more on the dance floor.

A must see for any Jack White fan.  It is a small record store, but the nostalgic atmosphere is great and it is fun to just thumb through the records and merchandise.  They also have a cute photo booth in the back.

I almost walked out. Not familiar with Nashville, I had no idea parking was a bear. They do offer valet but I prefer to park my own humble ride. So I go in and into the main room where the bar is. Instant headache. Sounds like everyone is yelling even though they re not. I've been to many a saucer and I don't recall any this damn loud any night of the week.  I almost turned around when I spotted a cold beer. Had to come in. Had to shout my order to the waitress. Meh.

Beer selection is decent with a lot of local beers I don't know about so didn't partake. I did find a sierra nevada i hadnt tried so good enough for me. It was super busy but the waitress was nice. Turkey melt came lukewarm with cold fries. Time I caught the waitress again I had ate half my turkey sandwich.  My least fav saucer thus far. Should have stayed at the hotel and bought a six pack n a sandwich.

I had a blast! My country music loving friend not so much! Drinks way overpriced! You'd think they could afford AC with what they make on drinks. It was so hot and drinks weren't cold enough to balance.

I'm going to keep this one short and simple. This is a blast of a place with fun live music and cheap beer, what more could you ask for? Definitely a touristy spot, but sometimes it's nice to get up and out and see what all the hustle and bustle is about. We will definitely be back to check out this place more and listen to some good, fun music.
We took a backstage tour, the tour guide was awesome! We would definitely go again. It is worth the price. Everyone there was very nice and friendly.

Well, you can tie me up in a hickory barrel and pickle me in moonshine. I can't believe I've done 3,000 of these missives to the troops (...umm, that would be you). And then I was faced with the dilemma of what to review for my self-important 3,000 milestone. But the obvious choice was staring me in the puss. It's a place I never dreamed of going to and yet I found myself enraptured by the experience. I'm not even a country music fan, and the NRA was having their annual convention that weekend. I only recognized one name on the bill that night and only barely. All the warning signs would have indicated I would have had an awful time at the Grand Ole Opry.

But no, it was a great venue for very talented musicians, and if you have any doubt that Nashville is a music town, just come here. It's really an experience you don't want to miss. I made the reservation for tickets well in advance of a trip that Jamie W. and I were making to that part of the country. We had no idea who would be playing since they don't announce the artists until a week or two before the actual date. We had our fingers crossed that it would be a group with a coolness factor like Lady Antebellum or a true legend like Dolly Parton. But alas, the only name we sort of recognized in the program was John Conlee, a Nashville stalwart who has since moved securely into Christian music. Oh dear.

Jamie and I made it to the current venue which is in a suburban area east of downtown. It was built in 1974 because the weekly attendance was outgrowing the capacity of the Ryman Auditorium, the Mother Church of Country Music, which is still operating downtown and hosts the Grand Ole Opry during the winter months. Once you enter, the theater looks the same cavernous size as the Metropolitan Opera House, both of which seat 4,000. The stage looks like a very modern version of the traditional barn front where Minnie Pearl would yell out her "How-deee!" And yet the seats were nothing more than pews with the thinnest of cushion padding. We did have good seats though, about nine rows back in the center section.

Because the show is also a radio broadcast, in fact the longest-running one in history, it is the most efficiently run concert I've ever attended. It starts promptly at 7PM and ends at exactly 9:15PM. No curtain calls, no costume changes, no exceptions. There were four half-hour segments separated by commercials for longtime sponsors like Cracker Barrel and Dollar General. They even held contests for audience members to win gift certificates. Each segment was hosted by what appeared to be a veteran of the Opry whether it was Conlee or Jeannie Sealy (photo: http://bit.ly/1dH2YVg). The program offered more traditional fare like mountain bluegrass from Jesse McReynolds and the Virginia Boys, smooth harmonizing from the Whites, a longtime sister act, and pure traditional country from 81-year-old Jim Ed Brown.

There were several more contemporary performers like Chris Janson and Jackie Lee (photo: http://bit.ly/1zrhYA9). Our favorite of the evening was Mark Wills, who has been surprisingly around for nearly twenty years and had quite a strong following in the audience. He sang two solo numbers plus a duet with Joe Diffie, and we kept wondering why he didn't have more name recognition than he does (photo: http://bit.ly/1zGTPWO). But maybe he does in Nashville. What do I know about country music anyway? Next to nothing actually, but you don't need to have any knowledge to enjoy the shows they present here. I ain't no Bible-thumping, shotgun-carrying, Jessie Helms-worshiping conservative, but I had a grand enough time at the Grand Ole Opry to make this my 3,000th review.

Enjoyed going to the saucer in Memphis on a weekly basis. Gave this one a chance on several occasions after moving to Nashville with 50/50 results. The last time we were there the server added an extra $8 to the check. Not going back. There are better bars in the area that won't try to scam you.

We came for the backstage tour.  It's interesting but a little pricey, especially for kids. Kids under 3 are free. The tour includes some well produced videos as well as a complete walk through backstage, the soundstage, and then onto the stage. It takes about an hour to complete the tour.

Traveling for my profession, I like to find off the wall, non-chain restaurants. Don't let it's location turn you off of this unique, somewhat hidden diner. We tried it on a Saturday at peak lunch hours and was able to find a table without waiting. This place seems more like it was made for the late night bar goers. Food was surprisingly good and service was fast and friendly. Looking at the bar, they have many daily specials and there was a small area that looked like they might have live music on the weekends. 

Overall, this was a good place to visit and I hope to go back on a weekend night to see this place really liven up.

The staff was aloof and inattentive, as well as service being slow. I was taken back by this right away because there was hardly anyone else in there when we ate. Right there -2 stars. My drink (which was mere water) was empty well into my hot sandwich with no one to be found for a refill. 
The hot pretzels with 4 dipping sauces is to-die-for! Fluffy and delish! The buffalo chicken wrap(it is HOT) is a winner also! 
Will go back soon for those 2 items and hope service is better.

This was a great tour and I highly recommend. 
Easiest per-purchase tickets on their website for this backstage and behind the scenes tour. 

Entering back stage you see where the tv shows Hee Haw and Nashville are filmed. 

The music artist mailroom was a very interesting stop and the description of all the dressing rooms. 

Enjoy the tours.

The tour is a must this is a cool and progressive record company embracing purity of music art, graphic art and lifestyle. The world should work like this!!  Tours very limited on weekends only. Get there at opening as very few get into this real working record studio and company back rooms
Got to be the best food downtown. Never get tired of it, everything on the menu is delicious

Finally made it to Music City Tippler this past weekend. I don't know why I had waited so long. We arrived around 9:30 and sat outside and had a few cocktails. We then went in and had a blast on the dance floor. It's a hidden gem in Midtown for sure!

Cover Charge Ok if one does not drink or eat otherwise not cool for a restaurant. Service slow go for a busy Sunday night. Food was fantastic and the portions were worth its price. Beer Yuenling was as usual the best domestic one. Live Music was awesome Jimmy and the guys were a hell of a good show. Overall I was satisfied and my teen had a great time.

It is a must see in Nashville, I am not a country music fan and I was planning to spend only one hour and then go to downtown, but once the show started, I got hooked up and I couldn't leave my chair. Do yourself a favor and make a booking!

Walked in and straight out. Really wasn't my scene - which is weird to say because I'm addicted to karaoke. It felt like I was interrupting someone's 21st birthday party, plus it was way too smokey. Sorry guys. Everyone else appeared to be having a great time though!

If you are in Nashville and a fan of music and Jack White, this is a must stop! So many fun things to check out and play with and explore. And loads of great records to pick from, with the majority being recorded live at Third Man Records. There is a super cute old school photo booth, dancing hamster machine, fun sound machines, a vinyl listening booth AND a booth where you can record yourself and have it pressed to vinyl. 

TLDR: GO! This place is the bees knees.

Hidden diner was a great find on a recent trip to Nashville. Live music was fantastic and energetic and the burgers measured up! Not too busy and great seating on both floors. Great service and food for a very acceptable price.

I have to say that I believe this is up there with the best burgers in Nashville. The bar itself is pretty nice, a decent selection of brews on tap and a nice happy hour, but their stuffed burgers are what will bring you back. The Sunday Brunch includes this whipped cream cheese center that is unbelievable, and they have the classic juicy lucy on the menu for the traditionalists out there. Their spicy fries are knock you over spicy and delicious. I never came before it changed over from Taps and Tapas to Taps Stuffed Burgers, so I can't speak to any differences, but I would say it is well worth a trip!
Great food! Turkey burger was yummy and the beer was divine. They were busy, but very accommodating

Not the best not the worst food would have been great if it was hot tried fried green tomatoes for the first time and they where too hot I burned my tongue. The waiter even though he was nice didn't pay our table much mind so the service wasn't the best but the music was good

This was a quick stop, wish we could have looked around more without purchasing a "tour"
.....next time
Nice to see a part of country history sticking to its roots

Took a group for an early dinner great beer selection and your typical pub grub, but everyone was satisfied.   Service was good and everyone was well nourished.   Been to the one in Columbia SC and in Raleigh NC, decent regional chain.
It was a cool experience. Not sure it totally worth the money but alas. Might be better with more things to visit.

I went to miss Kelli's expecting to have a great time. I bought a drink from the bar on the right hand side and got mediocre service. I then went to meet up with friends at the bar on the left hand side. As I sat down on a bar stool a male bald headed bartender with a cigarette hanging out of his mouth asked me if I needed a drink. I politely said no I had just gotten one from the other bar. He said "well honey if you're not buying you need to get up." I kindly replied I had already bought one so that's a little crazy and got up. He then proceeded to tell me "well you can go f*** yourself." My male friends heard him say this and made eye contact with him. He then told the bouncers our group made him nervous. Before we could finish our drinks a group of 10 of us were escorted out. Mind you, while this is happening a highly intoxicated female next to us has spilled 3 drinks and has spilled one on another customer, but was not asked to leave. I told the bouncers what happened and they agreed that said bartender has issues and should not be working there. Do not go there unless you like to be disrespected.
Five stars a must , fabulous food great atmosphere and the service is great. That being said the Music is truly sets the standard for Music City.....Nashville.

Perfect spot for an amazing southern meal and live music. 

The baked beans were the best I've ever had. The gumbo is not to be missed.

Excellent customer service and of course, the amazingly talented musicians you'd expect from Nashville!
It's a pretty cool place and worth a stop in if you love Jack White and all the The Third Man does for the world of music.

The hostess with the nose ring is extremely rude. So rude, in fact, we left. We wanted to sit somewhere else since the music was way too loud, and she was not accommodating. She wouldn't explain why we couldn't sit elsewhere when there was empty tables all around.
Skip the $90.00 VIP tour.  Major rip off.  Not much more than the $19.00 daytime tour.
Great food and service at a good price. Pulled pork,    baked beans, potato chips and po'boy was delicious. Floors and bathrooms could use an update.

Awesome place to listen to live blues music. Got some amazing brisket and a bottle of wine while my girlfriend had the grilled chicken. The food was an awesome. The band was very entertaining and took song request, except they didn't play any Eric Clapton. But overall I would for sure recommend to any friends in the area! Made for a great dinner to start out evening together!!
I went to a fundraiser here - what a fun option to shake yo booty downtown. Good DJs are a nice switch from honky tonk haven and the layout is perfect for dancing and people watching.

LOVED this place! We went on a Saturday afternoon. Great use of outdoor/indoor seating. The staff were all really pleasant, knowledgeable, and helpful. We only got beers and the soft pretzel app, but really enjoyed everything we got and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking to grab a drink and an app. I'd definitely go back to try more.

Would definitely go back when in Nashville.
$3 pint night on Monday. Get there early,9:30pm, as by 10 pm the place is packed.
The pretzels were soft, fluffy and delicious. The spicy mustard is indeed  wasabi spicy, so use accordingly. The sauerkraut passed my Wisconsinite husband's test. Had a badly-needed great night at the flying saucer. Thanks!
The selection of beers is second to none, but the food and staff really sets this place apart! If you have Mallory for a server, take her advice for drink and food- she is awesome!!
The owner was very rude and disrespectful to my friend. She called her an It and a He/She. Please don't go to this homophobic bar!!

After wondering around downtown Nashville for a bit and checking out some of the sights we decided that we should probably eat. We checked out Yelp as well as Google Maps and was able to find B.A.D. We really didn't want to spend a ton of money on dinner - but we didn't want something like McDonalds so we felt this was a good compromise as the prices were reasonable.

We wondered around for a bit before we actually found this location - as they literally are down an alleyway. We walked in and found a seat. They were not busy - but they were not slow either. It was a good mix. Our server came over right away and took our drink order. They did seem to be more of a bar than a restaurant but that is besides the point. They listed out all their specials and unfortunately on Friday nights the only special is $4 fireball shots.

We ordered chips as the appetizer. They make them in house and are amazing. They are cooked and salted to perfection! We ended up doing burgers - I went with the Mega Titan Burger and my other half went with the fork and knife burger.

Our wait time for our food was not long at all. But it wasn't so soon that we couldn't enjoy the chips. The burgers are seasoned to perfection - to the point I wanted to storm the kitchen and steal it all so I could re-create the same burgers at home. The burgers were cooked to perfection as well. They were juicy and just full of flavor. The knife and fork burger comes with chili on top (hence the name) and I hear it was amazing as well.

Our server was great. She was friendly, offered suggestions, and kept our drinks full. She was very attentive to our needs.

If you're looking for a burger in the downtown area - check them out. They're worth the hunt!

This place used to be a "must visit" when traveling to Nashville. The food used to be AMAZING and the service was also great. It has gone DOWNHILL!! The music was good tonight, but the food was very disappointing and the service was mediocre at best. The gumbo could have been out of a can and isn't as dark and smoky as I remember. Also, the ribs were burned, dry and very fatty. The sweet smoky signature taste I remember and came here for doesn't exist anymore. Finally, there were few baked beans, mostly just sauce, and the cornbread muffin (which I didn't eat) looked like a little yellow hockey puck... not a muffin at all. Finally, as far as service goes, I asked the waiter a few questions about the menu and he literally just shrugged... no answer. With all the great music venues in Nashville and SO MUCH better food joints, I WOULDN'T WASTE MY TIME AT BB KINGS.

I thought this place was great! Our tour guide was very knowledgeable, very personable, and very attentive. The tour itself was great. We got the backstage look at what the Opry is all about, got to see all the dressing rooms, the sound stage (where they actually film portions of the tv show Nashville), got to walk on the stage, and even got our picture taken on the circle that was taken from The Ryman. And yes, we bought it too. 

Helpful hint: if you want to tour The Opry and The Ryman, don't by tickets to both in advance as The Opry will give you a discount if you are planning on going to The Ryman. We did not know that and bought tickets to both online before we even got there. Also, you can get coupons in the City Guides at the airport to get discounts off admission to both tours, so planning ahead isn't actually the best thing to do.

This was a FANTASTIC find. I enjoyed a really great pulled pork sandwich along with some quality live music. 

The pork was shredded just right and lightly sauced. It was tender and delicious. I assumed that the sauce would be vinegar-based, instead I got a lightly sweet sauce with a pleasant apple cider flavor. A perfect match for the pork. The accompanying fries were hot and crispy. The beans were loaded with chunks of meat. 

We just happened to stop on the night of a CD release party for a country music band. While I'm not a fan of country music in general, I can appreciate good music and this definately qualified. And the space has nice acoustics. The music was loud enough to be enjoyed by all without blowing the eardrums of the folks in the booths closest to the band.

People of Nashville, I hope you realize how lucky you are, living so close to the the BAD.

I don't foresee ever coming to Nashville without a trip to the Opry. In full disclosure, I'm not a huge country music fan, but I like it well enough due to a stint in rural Texas with limited radio access. We also went into the night not knowing anything about anyone performing. Now that I've been to the Opry, I'm a believer.

I loved how the show was broken into quarters and the way that each quarter contained classic country, bluegrass and a more contemporary act. The Opry was a true variety show and I ended up downloading a few songs as we watched and discovered new artists.

The set and the history and the seating were also pluses. Even though we sat in the first balcony (and I'd splurge for better seats now that I know how great the show is), the acoustics are great and you can see the performers on the big screen.

Yes, the Opry is a little commercial (both the actual commercials and proximity to the mall), but the show is so lovely it's easy to look past that. Next time, I'll buy the tickets that have a backstage tour afterward.

Our food took an hour to come out. Server never apologized or reassured us during that hour. We asked to speak to a manager who did nothing as well. 

The food was good and restaurant was awesome inside with good music.

Not much of a country fan, BUT the show was good! Alan Jackson and Miranda Lambert played tonight, so it made for a good show. The venue was smaller than I imagined and the show seemed short, but overall I had a good time. My country loving Grandma would be proud!
Great food with healthy options available. Fantastic waitstaff and great for listening to music rather than the crowd itself. Gets busy

The beer selection here is fantastic!  My server recommended Finch's cucumber beer and it was so interesting.  I love when servers give suggestions, I almost always take them up on it and am always pleased.  Love the decor and atmosphere in here, if I was local I would definitely want to be part of their beer club sounds like so much fun.  The pork belly sandwich was a bit dissapointing, however the bread on the sandwiches is amazing!
Loves the roof . Had a great time with the servers. I went in because they were military friendly
The turkey sausage soup was definitely worth ordering. The locals seem to be enjoying themselves.

Good Music
Gets crowded on weekends as does any place along the main strips.  Took a while to get food.   Expensive but it was good.

We were looking for a place to eat when we stumbled upon this small bar/restaurant tucked in an alleyway downtown Nashville. No wait for a table but decent crowd present. Great wrap and pulled pork sandwich. Fries were also very good. Waitress was very friendly providing  attentive service at a pleasant pace. Clean and comfortable environment. Live music certain nights. They offered 1/2 price appetizers too. Will definitely go back next time in Nashville.

It's my first time here so I had to go.  We had a group of about 20, and had a very nice guide.  I'm not a big country fan so I really didn't know any of the names.  Even for me though, it was interesting to learn about the legacy of the place.
Awesome place but was a little hard to find (I'm also directionally challenged). We found it and we're happy with the service and food. Definitely recommend you stop here for lunch.

On August 23rd, went to BB King with friends and had marinated grilled chicken basted with BBQ sauce, baked beans and slaw. Chicken was delicious and juicy. Music was smooth, a little loud, it was difficult to talk, may be because we were close to stage. Service slow, but the person serving was pleasant. All in all, a well spent evening with friends, food and music.

Ok service - our waitress struggled to make local beer recommendations and they were actually out of several beers that we requested. The women's bathroom was a mess with paper towels all over the ground. The only good part was the live music: STACY MITCHHART BAND.

I'd give it five stars if marks were supposed to be for being as advertised, but I hold five star reviews for uppity fancy places that blow my mind. 

Any place with half price green flash west coast ipa during happy hour is gonna have high marks in my book. Juicy Lucy was good and filling, even though it appeared pretty small.

The Flying Saucer had a VERY limited menu due to kitchen renovations we didn't know about until we were already seated. Then, getting out of the parking area was insane due to machine malfunctions. The pretzel was great and the beer was ok, but the whole inter and the exit experience pretty much spoiled it.

The best wings ever! I'm not a fan of bone-in wings but I loved the Asian flavor wings. They are amazing, and so are the buffalo flavor! They also have the best bartenders!!!! If you are a Cleveland Browns or Ohio State buckeyes fan this is the place to go!
We did some honky tonking up and down Broadway during CMA Fest 2018 & this was our favorite stop. It's a more intimate place and the performer, Noah Garner, was very engaging. Loved it.

The sirens wail on a cold Nashville night. A sign beckons you down an alley way telling you that BAD, Back Alley Diner, is good. What you learn upon walking down the alley is that BAD is actually bad. The bar smells like Dolly Parton's dentures soaked in urine. The money you save on $2 PBRs will be lost tenfold on dry cleaning bills for your clothes, which might as well be tossed into the nearby dumpster. I appreciate a good dive bar, but even I can't endure the assault BAD waged on my nose and sense of worth.

Great family activity with a variety of acts each show.  A must do in Nashville.  Covers history of the Opry. Our show included old school acts, bluegrass, a comedian (awesome by the way... Henry Cho), and some great mainstream acts.  We could only get balcony seats way up in back but seats were great... They set up the seats so everyone can see, even kids.

I arrived in Nashville for the Beachbody Summit (fitness convention), and my friend got me tickets last minute as a present so I could see the famous Opry. It definitely did not disappoint! While I was near the stage, any seating arrangement here would do justice in offering the full allure of the history of why this is such a Landmark. There were some old-school country performers as well as some up-and-comers, followed by Vince Gill. Despite not being a big country fan, I had a great time!! There were places to grab a bite or a drink or a souvenir, it was clean and very comfortable. I definitely recommend checking this out if you're ever here for a visit.

Had such a great experience at flying saucer. Staff was knowledgeable and friendly. They were patient with me and helped me choose a beer selection I would be super happy with. We just came for drinks, however next time we pass through, I would definitely try the menu. Atmosphere was really laid back. They need more pubs like this in Nashville!

When I used to live in Nashville back around 2008, DM was a great spot to go out at night.  Fun bands, good crowds, great service, the works.

Now, not so much.  My wife and I have been a couple times over the past few months.  This place has really let itself go.  First, no live bands, at least that I've seen.  Instead, they have these DJs who are real mood-killers.  First, they've got their base turned up way to loud.
