You can feel it in your chest half a block down the Music Row - on the other side of Demonbreun Circle!  It's almost unbearable trying to get close to the stage to dance.  Not that you'd want to anyway, since the floor used to be packed with all sorts of people, now it's like 1-2 bachlorette parties and a couple creepy dudes.  

Last night, the DJ couldn't seem to stop playing Lonely Island.  Yeah, mix in a chorus/verse for laughs and then move on, haha, good stuff.  But three full Lonely Island songs in a row?  My group literally stopped dancing because of it and left the floor.  Of course, when we went towards the back, we were met with a wall of cigar smoke.  So, not a high score on the ambiance chart either.  We ended up leaving shortly thereafter.

I will say, their pub food is pretty tasty, and their HH deals aren't bad (but don't get the house brews - even the bartenders will tell you that they're terrible).  So for a HH and/or dinner?  DM seems fine.  But if you're looking to dancing in the midtown area, it's either Tin Roof, South (assuming you can stand the heat), or somewhere on Division.  DM used to be so good, and now it's so bad.
Server forgot about us. Band was good during the day. Singer had good voice, sax, piano, drums.  Servers looked like the were unhappy.-zombies. Large place. Probably more exiting at night. Bar menu.
Walked in to some incredible voices singing.  Worth a drink to see what talent shows up!

There is such a cool atmosphere here! Ive been wanting to visit ever since reading about it in The Rolling Stones. I even got to record my voice in a vintage vocal booth. For just 20 bucks, I was able to put my original song on a record! So cool!
This was a fantastic experience to have! The show was superb and it doesn't feel like a huge impersonal venue. It feels small and intimate. This is a must when visiting Nashville!
I love drinking with all the expats on Friday afternoon. But I'm writing to let you know that DM has the best potato salad I've ever had. Skip the fries, get the potato salad. You won't regret it.

The food and atmosphere were good... but they need to label which of their foods are spicy. Everything has a little kick to it but the Mac and cheese was terribly spicy. They basically poured spicy nacho sauce on pasta. It was almost inedible. That's not southern Mac and cheese. Ick. 

However, my beef brisket was great. Smoky and tender. And the corn muffins tasted just like mama made. I also enjoyed the banana bread pudding and the peach cobbler. Tasted very fresh.

Still. I think there's better places to go in Nashville. I probably won't be back.

The Grand Ole Opry is a historic place to visit in Nashville.  We came here on a Tuesday before CMA fest.  Not gonna lie but that was a good choice to see a lot of great artists: Darius Rucker, Chris Janson, Charles Esten, Little Big Town, and Carrie Underwood!   They all put on a great show.  There was a pre party before the show with a outdoor concert and plenty of beverage and food options.  It was a blast too.  Inside don't think there was really any bad seats looked like pretty good views from the balcony too.  We sat on the floor about 20 rows back worth the price for the seats.  The concession prices are pretty reasonable compared to other concert venues I've attended. The crowds here are pretty tame and don't get very loud, made a couple people mad because I stood up to cheer on the artists after they did a great job.  The Grand Ole Opry is a great place to see new, old, and great country stars.
If you have a visitor from out of town, bring them here. Get two drinks and the pretzel and cheese. On your way out, swing by the Union Station Hotel to checkout the turn of the century architecture.

Great food and interesting place. It is just down from Printers Alley downtown Nashville and isn't a big place but has a cute vibe. We were seated right by the entrance that took away a little from the experience. I had the black bean and corn burger and my friend had the pork plate. The service is slower so don't go if you are in a hurry but the food is worth the wait. We both enjoyed our meals and both were reasonably priced. I would return again next time in Nashville.

Drinks were good. The place is beautiful. I just think it's a poor use of space. There could be so much more seating, but instead I have to stand around and get my 12 dollar drink jostled out of my hand. And it's in the Adelica, if that tells you anything about the average client on a Saturday night. If I'm back it won't be my idea.

We were in town for a company sponsored event. Staff and atmosphere were nice. We were in a private dining area which was nice since we could actually talk and hear each other. We received a lot of good feedback about the food. Afterwards, everyone stood outside the room to hear the live band. Overall a good time. I would recommend. Ideal for larger groups. We had about 40.

This place was fun, good drinks.  A bit dissappointed the happy hour only applied to domestic drafts, but the double bloody marys were a hit!  The bad that plays around 1:00pm on Sundays was entertaining, the woman singer had a very pretty voice.  Overall a good time!
Loved the food is was amazing. The hangover burger was great! The pulled pork nachos we delightful. And, the Service was wonderful!!  Definitely coming back soon!!!
Great food. Nice music. Great service. Tre was excellent and treated my girls and I with amazing service. Definitely the best place in Tennessee

Great handmade burgers - no frozen quick made patties here - and battered French fries. Great sauce and spices on the burger. 

The name says it appropriately. It's a diner in an alley. Little tricky to find. Glad I did. Exposed brick and unfinished wood plank ceiling are appealing, not standard look.

Live music tonight. Not the typical Broadway  Street cover band.

This was the best music  experience  I had in Nashville by far and definitely over the last few months.

You see I'm not a modern country music fan but alas I thought when in Rome do what the Nashvillians would do. So we got tickets to the Grand Ole Opry at the Ryman Auditorium. The only ones left were limited view so I went for the balcony. Turns out our view wasn't very limited maybe just the far corner of the stage and there isn't a bad seat in the house acoustically.

The performers were all top notch and some were surprises even different from the program we were handed as we walked in. Seeing 4 stars from the show Nashville out singing on stage was an added bonus. Later one guy even brought a yoyo out. If you can get a ticket just go!

Located in an old building, this Flying Saucer has a great ambiance. Sit in the veranda if you prefer a quieter table. 
The beer selection is extensive to say the least. My grandfather didn't know what to pick, so I told our waitress what he usually drinks, and asked that she pick something out for him- he was quite pleased with her selection. I've been trying the gluten free thing (have pity on me) so I was happy to see that they have gluten free beers and ciders to chose from. If you don't know what to order, ask your waitress, they're usually pretty knowledgeable and have no problem bringing out samples.
Overall: great place to hang out!

Four stars for the facility itself and 1 star for the tour guide. Not knowledgeable to answer questions, didn't impetus current events of the facility, and overall just didn't provide a very thorough experience like onewould expect here, very disappointing that management would waste individuals money like this.

Loved the experience. We were told when purchasing that it was an obstructed view but we could still see just fine!  Awesome entertainers. Can't wait to come back. Hopefully trace Adkins will be around next time. However josh turner and the rest of show were fabulous. Just loved MR Osbourne and the rocky top Xpress,  riders in the sky, Mandy, and  Home Free wow. And please Little Big Town our fav!!!!!  Only thing that could possibly make better would be to have all the old gang alive and on stage. Roy Acuff, porter wagner. Patsy Cline. Loretta Lynn.  Lil jimmy dickens. Grandpa. Minnie pearl. Hank Williams. You could feel the spirits off all the great!!!

I love the beer selection but drove all the way there to see that they changed their Rocket tots to "loaded rocket tots" basically covered with a bunch of slop-u can't order plain ones anymore?!?! What?!? And if u want them plain u order "without everything" and still have to pay like 8.69 for them!! Absurd & I'm SO bummed!!!!! Sooooo bummed.
Very rude wait staff and mediocre food. Wouldn't waste my money again. Band was good though.

Had a lot of fun here at a Friday night show. The first row of the mezzanine had great visibility  of the singers and the TV screens. A bit frustrating that the acts don't all get posted in advance on the website- if you have date flexibility, that makes planning difficult. 
I have to say the drinks inside the theater were pricey- 4 drinks were $37.00, without tip! But it's nice they let you bring them into the theater.

Saturday at lunch time in music city gets a little busy. Most of the places had a wait to get in, BB King's had no waiting. The kids were getting restless so we thought this would be a good spot. The service was extremely slow, the waitress seemed like she didn't really want to be there. For being not buy thee service should not have been that slow. The food was decent, the sliders and chicken fingers the kids ordered were good. The best thing about the place was the musician. He came in shortly before we left and played some good tunes.
I'm not even a country fan, but this tour is a must if visiting Nashville.  It's an iconic and historical landmark and the tour was very well organized.  Bring your camera!!

We had such a good time here. Maddie (sorry if I spelled it wrong!) from NY was friggin awesome. I'm actually glad we went early and it was slow enough for her to stay and shoot the shit with us. Everyone loved what they ordered. Jalapeño burger, Bleu cheese burger, Boston dog, plain dog, turkey and beef tenderloin sliders, mac and cheese, beans, fries, tots, slaw.... all good. Drinks were cold, food was deeLish, and the service was great. Oh, and I forgot to mention that two of our group of six are 8 and 10 years old :)

I LOVE THIS BAR!! wonderful beer selection and great prices! On Mondays they have all their tap beers for $3. Yes this is not a joke. Every beer on tap is just $3. They have at least 20 taps as well. All craft no shitty domestics! 
We didn't eat the food so can't comment on that but the bar it's self is very fun and they have great bartenders. Very knowledgeable!
Cheap drinks but serves its purpose for karaoke for the brave and drunk.. Wait was a little long to sing, but the crowd is supportive regurgless if you're good or bad and song choice.

Having grown up watching Hee Haw and loving Country Music, a visit to the Grand Ole Opry was a must during my time in Nashville. We got tickets the day before which was actually lucky as it seemed it was close to being full for the day we wanted to go. We got there early and walked around some and took pictures. The tour started pretty much right on time. It was a large group but overall a decent size to still be able to hear and see things. Out tour guide provided lots of information and explained everything as we went through the tour. You get to go backstage and see the dressing rooms, the post office, and the Artist's entrance. The only downsides were that we were not allowed to go on the stage as there were workers there prepping for a show that night, and because they were getting the lighting set up too, the giant lights were down blocking anyone from getting a good clean picture of the stage. So that was pretty disappointing. But overall I am glad I went at least once.

If you love beer, you'll love the Flying Saucer.  If you don't, well you are barking up the wrong tree.  They have a sign that says they have liquor and wine, but it is pretty frowned upon. 

The food is quite good for bar food.  I like the nachos as well as the buffalo chicken wrap.

I would definitely suggest coming here every now and then for a beer and a bite.  I only deducted one star because sometimes the bartenders aren't necessarily very knowledgeable about some of the beers they have, which could be due to the sheer number of them.  Nonetheless, I have found that surprising a few times.
Pass on the 5 dollar cover charge. Large overpriced menu. They have almost anything you can want.

I go to a here, I love it here!!! 

But for $20.00 tour to watch Tv on a tour at the Opry House is so Cheesy! I could do this on my couch! So so disappointed ! 

Most of the dressing rooms were closed they don't know why? We barely saw anything! 
Worthless! 
Refund please.

I under estimated this place! I knew the music would be awesome but didn't expect the food to be just as good!!!! The ribs were to die for!!!  And the Mac and cheese is a must! I recommend BB Kings for the entire experience!!! Live music is amazing!

Either you get it or you don't. 

If you are checking Yelp to decide if it's worth a visit to TMR, you probably don't get it (yet).  If you are leaving a negative review because there isn't rack after rack of mediocre used vinyl, you definitely don't get it and I actually kinda feel sorry for you.

There literally would no "Jack White" and no TMR or retail store or anything as we now know it without the involvement of some amazing and wonderful women over the years, and the staff here is no exception.  Don't let some of the reviews talking about hipsters or whatever fool you - these girls are just cool, the kind you can't fake.  

The prices are pretty reasonable, and I'm sure as hell not some rich guy saying that.  And if it helps, do a little research about Jack's personal philanthropy and TMR's continuing charity and community involvement and you'll wish you spent a little more.  Again, the real deal and not something they really publicize.

Don't forget to have a nickel or two in your pocket for the gumball machine!

The sirens wail on a cold Nashville night. A sign beckons you down an alley way telling you that BAD, Back Alley Diner, is good. What you learn upon walking down the alley is that BAD is actually bad. The bar smells like Dolly Parton's dentures soaked in urine. The money you save on $2 PBRs will be lost tenfold on dry cleaning bills for your clothes, which might as well be tossed into the nearby dumpster. I appreciate a good dive bar, but even I can't endure the assault BAD waged on my nose and sense of worth.

***UPDATE: We might have had fun with the writing style, but the content is valid. The bar smelled like urine as soon as we walked in. We really wanted to like this place! Just couldn't handle the smell. Could've been a one-time thing, but it was our experience.

This is the best place on Broadway. It's very energetic and everyone there is super welcoming and friendly. You can request to karaoke a song, or if you're more of a shy folk you can sing along to other artists singing. It's always a great time and good to be at every day of the week.

Great food and ambiance! Our server Mary H was so friendly, quick and attentive to our needs. The only downside was the wait for food, but we had a large group and the kitchen was swamped with a huge party. We've been here before and will definitely be back!!!

What you see is what you really get. Lively, loud, tremendous beer selection, good selection of food options; sharing "starters" is a great idea. Dinner portions are modest....nice to be able to balance liquid intake with solid food consumption--easy to do here. 

Always a bit of a quandary....four or five stars? Contrasted to full-blown restaurants this would be 4 stars, but I'm comparing it with beer emporiums that serve great food, and in this case five stars are well-deserved.

Very congenial wait staff helped us settle in with nearly 2 dozen relatives visiting from all over the US. Politely and continually paid attention to both our food and drink needs.

Absolutely perfect soft pretzels with delightful dipping sauces. Savory traditional Shepherd's Pie. Dynamite house-made Rocket Tots, served, interestingly enough, with a friend egg. Brats are ok. All-in-all, good solid food.

No negatives other than we were told (beforehand when we called) we would not need a reservation, only to arrive and see there was an issue with such a large group of friends....and another large group had, in fact, made a reservation for the same time period. All turned out well since "Emily" and the other staff made us more than welcome. We'll be back.
Nice place for group karaoke. There's a pool table way back. The waitress was very nice. We ordered a couple of drinks and watched the groups that was there perform.

Good service. Ordered the catfish po' boy. Good, but not spectacular. Great, friendly bar service, which is welcome when traveling for work. I'd definitely recommend as a place to duck into for a quick bite and a friendly face.

Really good burger, extremely fast service.  From the outside doesn't look like much but once you enter, it is both larger and nicer  than expected! My husband said "we will be back! Came for lunch and did not have the opportunity to see any live music but it appears they do have it!

Definitely a must do for any country music fan! It seems like a lot of the reviews are more positive about the backstage tours than the show, but I had the opposite experience. I thought the show was so much fun, even though nobody who is currently super famous was performing (our show included Mark Wills, Diamond Rio, Old Crow Medicine Show, Connie Smith, Ricky Skaggs and Larry Gatlin, amongst others). The show features about 12 acts and all the performers were great, even the ones I hadn't heard of before. I thought that the length and quality of the show (especially considering the variety) was well worth the $40 or so admission (though of course if you catch a superstar like Brad Paisley or Carrie Underwood, it's an even better deal, since the ticket price doesn't change based on who is performing). Know that each artist, no matter how famous, does only two or three songs, so even if you do manage to go there when someone like Carrie Underwood is performing, be aware that you're not going to a Carrie Underwood concert; she'll be just a small portion of the show. We had nosebleed seats and they were totally fine; it's a small venue. 

On the other hand, the backstage tour was $25. It isn't bad, but I thought it wasn't worth the price. They show you the artist check-in areas, dressing rooms and some memorabilia, and then conclude by taking you on the stage and letting you stand in the famous circle (which is admittedly really cool, but there's no opportunity to take your own photo and they try to sell you the photo they take for $20 - almost as much as the tour itself!) All told, it only lasted about 45 minutes and it left me underwhelmed. It may be the luck of which guide you get to some degree; ours was friendly but wasn't particularly engaging and was clearly reciting a script.

Photos from the show and tour are here: http://destinationsanddesserts.com/2016/03/05/a-night-at-the-grand-ole-opry/
Great service. Good mixed drinks, too! Food was okay but worth the try.

Belcourt Tapes is a movie, from the makers of Poughkeepsie Tapes. It sucks. This is not that.

Saw a band here once, and was taken drinking here once. From my 2 visits I have little good or bad to say about it. I love that they have live music every night. I think their sound system could be better but I'm not the one performing (and this crowd wouldn't like my sh*t anyway) so it's cool.

Prices are too high for me - let me clarify - in all of the bars in this neighbourhood, compared to what I'm used to (in Buffalo for example) but it's in the trendy part of town next to Vanderbilt so that is to be expected. Collegey crowd when I was there, and hipstery too, but you can get that just from the name. Speaking of which, the first time I came here (with a girl that was too cute for her own good) it was called "Belcourt Tapas" or something. Sounds like a Fox joke, but it's for real. I didn't try the Tapas, but she said she had and told me not to. So not exactly a ringing endorsement. But I think the place has changed hands since then, probably a few times, much like the girl in question.

I received a nice response to my review, and since it showed some excellent customer service, I will give them an additional star. Yelp reviewers are not allowed to accept discounts or free stuff, but the fact that this establishment is going out of its way to try and make people more satisfied is a good sign.

Anyway, I've been randomly ringing doorbells in my neighbourhood again, and I got arrested for it so now I have to go to Bellcourt. Bye.

My friends and I went to the flying saucer for dinner and drinks before a concert. It took 30 minutes to even get our first beer - which was not the beer we ordered. It took another 30 minutes for the waitress to take our food and when we politely said we were in a hurry, she made excuses about other tables. We understood and continued waiting for the food. When they brought it out, two out of four of the meals were wrong. It took 25 minutes for them to bring out my correct order and by the time I was eating, all of my friends were finished eating. When we didn't put our cards in the check holder immediately the waitress made a comment "I thought y'all were in a hurry" .. yet I hadn't even gotten my food yet. I tried to give them the benefit of the doubt, but I will not be back.

I'm so blessed to able to come and see this place so much history here. We went the day before coming here to the "Ryman Auditorium" which helps understand the whole history. We did the backstage tour also it was amazing to here all about that takes place in getting it all ready for a performance. We actually start from the beginning of how the guests begins his walk through the facility. So step by step we did the same walk through as if we're the guest. It was cool feeling and you appreciate it every time you see them on stage. Definitely recommend going through the backstage tour and later that evening go for the performance. There about 7 performance that night. We enjoyed every moment..

Christmas Eve, not that crowded.  But our server seemed over worked!
We ordered our dinner and it took FOREVER to get our food.  One of my party got the pulled pork plate - do they not serve bread with this?  It was also like warm.
They tried to deliver calamari to us - we did not order that.  They delivered fried fish and shrimp to us - we did not order that either!  Took another 10 minutes to finally get our ribs and chicken platter - 3 bones?!  That's it?!  And they were burnt too.  The chicken was good but a very small piece.  
We were going to get dessert but decided not to after all that.
Did they offer to comp or anything?  No.  our server was snippy too.  
Will not be coming back here.

To the two beautiful ladies working the place, the day before Jack's Lazaretto album came out: thank you very kindly. You two were fiddlin' with the record booth for a long time (I was waiting my turn a while, up until past closing) and you both handled that and Jack's guests with so much grace. I don't recall your names, but you with the pretty eye-shadow and beautiful diction- keep talking, singing, writing, whatever you're preferred communication: you share beauty and wonder and it's a delight to the ears. And to the other wonderful woman (with the dazzling stockings and warm-golden heart): you curated an amazing evening for me by recommending bingo night at the Stone Fox. Me oh my this California boy had a wondrous time talking with the hipster knitters and fun-time bingo players! It was my only night in Nashville and I can't imagine a better impression of your fine city than the one you two left for me.
Oh and this: next time you're shooting the breeze with Jack who I heard was saddened by something: just remind him that Fate may be what our brains are hard-wired  to look for in patterns and all that, but it doesn't change the truth that it was designed in the first place by that holy King of Rock 'n Roll, our good God. Hope he sees that, and maybe writes a song about it.
Such a fun place! Tons of different beers on tap from all over the world, a cool atmosphere and the pretzels were delicious.

Pretty cool experience to see a show at the Grand Ole Opry while visiting Nashville! This is coming from someone who is not really a county fan but does appreciate all types of music. I went to the show not even knowing any of the artists and really did enjoy myself. The auditorium is beautiful but does have bleacher style seating just FYI. Country fan or not, it's pretty cool to be in a place where so many legends have been and a definite must experience place when in Nashville!

Good pizza. Delicious beer. Slow service from the bar and the flight of beer (4 beers) was $14!! That's double what most places charge. 

I'll be back. I won't buy a flight.

I recommend the Yazoo Dos Perros; it was the stand-out draught of my five-five sampler: five ounces each of five local brews. Teamed up the brew with the (newer) Bahn Mi and the Hummus plate, and it you got yourself a filling meal without being heavy, and definitely enough to share. 
Our server was helpful and polite, without being pushy or appearing irritated; always an appreciated attitude for fellow industry peoples. 
Would totally come back time and again if it weren't half way across the United States. 
Hit it up if you're visiting, for sure.

What can I say? It's the hot cotton pickin' GRAND OLE OPRY, for crying out loud!? An iconic venue in every sense, it boasts of a balanced, purposeful  blend of nouveau with nostalgia. Beautiful and full of history, I'm sure the walls have a lot of stories to tell.

Tickets were available in person, after attempting to purchase them online. Although our party of five weren't able to sit together, the customer representative was helpful and did her best to find us the best seats.

Bars were plentiful and well stocked with a variety of wine, beers and spirits. The staff were Tennessee-friendly and the restrooms were clean.

I appreciated the numerous check points as it helped alleviate any lines. Customer service was on point!

Although I am not a huge country fan, I am a lover of music and definitely appreciated the beautiful music, the amazing production and logistics.

Don't be afraid.  This place is in an alley in a busy part of downtown, there's only a post office in the alley and other stores that sell their goods facing the opposite street,  nothing dangerous about it.

The service is top notch and friendly, I felt welcome and was taken care of right away, warm greeting, drink order, menu, order taken, boom!  Loved it.

I had the turkey club as I didn't want anything heavy for my 6hr drive home.  It was well portioned and tasty with seasoned fries which were also good but after a heaping handful of the fries they felt heavy.  No really a bad thing though.

Be sure to enter through the street level door.  Stop in and take a load off your mind at this quirky diner where you can get great food, watch the game and all topped off with friendly service.

Absolutely TERRIBLE service from the front of house.  What is the point of offering reservations if you can't keep them, and then telling people who walk in with a party of 13 that they have to wait for 45 minutes and that you couldn't care less.  I have never been treated so poorly.  High prices, gimmicky atmosphere, and horrible customer service?  I don't think so!  We happily spent our money at the Brazilian steakhouse a couple doors down where they have great food and even better service.  I will never set foot in a BB King's establishment and will tell as many people as possible about my experience.
Love the blues!!!!! Love B.B. Kings!!!!!! Memphis New Orleans and Nashville!!!! The live music is amazing and true!!!

This is a great little hidden place we stumbled upon. The service and food were awesome, it had a great atmosphere and the prices were quite reasonable as well. Highly recommend it and I'll be sure to return.

I love this place! The theme of the facility design is a exciting play on your visual sensory and every detail looks like it was intently picked out to leave the passerby intrigued or bewildered. I recently got to take a private tour (courtesy of Yelp during its 2014 Spring Break event in Nashville, TN) of the entire facility beyond the lovely shop. During the tour I got to check out everything from beautiful metallic crown moldings, eclectic artworks, furnace elevator, wall mounted animals, vinyl records with liquid inside, and some many other unique sights.  

The facility has an analog/straight to vinyl recording studio that had a huge view of the Blue Room (aka the multi-purpose music venue where live shows are recorded on site), a dark room for developing pictures, outdoor patio area, massive indoor merchandise/record shipping area that literally has a quirky road-side motel theme, a hospital themed company lounge/break area, and some amazing business offices (including the mysterious Jack White's office door). 

I was a little disappointed that the vinyl recording booth was out the facility for repairs prior to the Jack White and Neil Young appearance on Jimmy Fallon's Show. Despite my dreams of cutting a cheesy record on the go to mail to my parents, I could not complain after finding out about that type of awesome happening. Overall, the tour and visit to the shop was amazing. I plan to come to show at the TMR venue and visit the shop the next time I get a chance!

Third Man Records is Jack White's temple to vinyl records and analog recording techniques. The gift shop is just three small rooms with a small but completely representative collection of vinyl and CDs released by Third Man. There is also a wide range of other items including t-shirts. The store also serves as a kind of recording museum including a sound recording booth that is totally operational and you can record yourself onto a vinyl record. It's located in an light industrial area near downtown Nashville, but it appeared to be safe. Parking is pretty limited. If you love vinyl records you should visit.
5:00 on a Friday in January couldn't be a better time to eat here, walked right in.  Great food, great music
No complaints about anything. Everyone wad nice, food was good and made quick and a large variety of beer
So far! Disappointed! Long lines for security purposes. Show starts at 700 pm and still waiting to go through security at 709 pm. Gave ample time to arrive before scheduled show time too!

Me & the husband had a great 1st experience here! Having a little boy we don't get out at night too often, but we decided to come here for a little pre-dinner fun! Ordered the 2 big pretzels...amazing. Played pool, impressed the hubby with my pool skills... Overall had a great time! We will be back!
My catfish was good however it was served without a good sauce to dip it in and didn't even have a lemon wedge.

We were here celebrating a friends 40th bday and while waiting for Uber to arrive, we stopped in for a drink:). The bartenders here were friendly and attentive:)). It seemed this was mainly a college crowd and hang out but we just stopped in for a few beers so it was perfect :))

The cost was $24 a person. A little pricy, but traveling from California.. Probably never will come back so we paid it. 

The tour itself is enjoyable. You get to see backstage and learn a lot of new Information. Our tour guide was great. She was funny and made the experience that much better. 

If you're in the area I recommend spending the $24. It's about a 45 minute walking tour.
We arrived to a practically full house but scored a table in front.  Trey, our server was awesome, the music too!  Not too loud but totally danceable and FUN!

This place overall was great. There was live music on Saturday when we went to have dinner so we had to pay a $10 cover even though we were dining there. Although the live music was great I was shocked we had to pay a cover while we were eating dinner. The food was much better than we expected, but the service was not so great. We waited about 15 minutes before our waiter came over to offer us drinks, thank goodness we got drinks at the bar while we waited for our table. And to order dinner and pay our Bill was a struggle getting our waiters attention. Be aware that on a Saturday night for two people the wait was on hour. We had a gift card that was printed online from a family friend before our move to Nashville and it seemed like non on the staff knew how to redeem it. Overall the music and the food made for a good experience but I'm not in a hurry to come back.

The food is just ok....we had a reservation for a Monday night with 4 friends visiting from California and was surprised that we were charged a $5 cover charge each at the door to have dinner. Are you kidding? I can see maybe a cover charge for the bar area but to have dinner. Anyhow, we reluctantly paid. We were sat near the stage and thankfully our server was friendly and overall service was good. Unfortunately, the food wasn't. Gumbo yaya was just ok and I've had better barbecue at TGI Friday's. They did have a live band which was nice. Don't think we'll be coming back anytime soon.

I'm a Beer Knurd (if you don't know what this is, check it out on the website) and frequent guest at this location. 

Atmostphere and location is great, popcorn is free, food is ok, service really depends on WHO is serving you. Some nights it's fantastic, others are awful. And of course, there is a lot of beer. 

A great place to go hang with friends after work and have a few brews.

My impression before stopping by here was that it would be a kind of dark, cramped beer bar.  Boy was I wrong.

A beer bar, yes indeed.  A phenomenally well presented and organized beer list the likes of which I have rarely seen elsewhere.  But so much more.

Located just behind the Frist and Union Station, Flying Saucer is a rather large, very comfortable bar I'd be at a heck of a lot if I were a Nashvillan.  Comfortable couches and chairs on one side, traditional tables & high tops on the other.  Great, cheap beer and food everywhere.  Plus a separate room for live music and pool.  Just a great chill spot.  Best pretzels I've ever had, too.

While in staying in Nashville we were searching for a place to hang out and have some reasonably priced drinks during the day. I checked yelp and found this place was right across the street from our hotel. How can you go wrong with a place that has Happy Hour every day from 11-7?! 

We managed to rack up quite the bar tab, but for the amount we ate and drank, it was more than worth it. We will definitely visit them next time we're in town.

I stopped in with two friends to have a beer or two and listen to some live music. The place was empty except the bar area which was about 50% full. We went to sit at a table and were told we could only sit at a table in the bar area if we were eating. Really?  The dinning rom areas were completely empty and half the tables in the bar area were empty. Needless to say we only had one drink, left and won't be back. Very stupid seating policy.  People are more likely to stay if they can sit at a table and talk instead of all facing away from each other while sliding off a bar stool. Very bad management on this one.

Very cool spot with tons of beer choices. Draft, cans, bottles, nitro... We're pretty picky about our beer and we both found something new we enjoyed, including a kelp and sea salt gose! The food was good but not the star of the show. We had a yummy cheese fries appetizer, the Pork Banh Mi and Marcellus Wallace (cheesesteak). Both were good, but again, not the reason we'll come back... but we will come back! The patio was gorgeous and the bar area was loud and fun on a Friday night.

Third Man Records produces, records, and presses some of todays and yesterdays  best albums, unfortunately their customer service and shipping times do not have the same quality. I am disappointed and frustrated with not getting orders on time, especially when you are forced to pay two day shipping charges and it takes them weeks to get your order in the mail. I understand it is still a small company and shipping firm but the site offers limited products and most of those products are housed in one location, it shouldn't be to hard to bundle two LP's together and ship them. The real issue that gets me is after waiting a week and half after placing on order there is still no shipping conformation, which prompted an e-mail to see whats going on with the order. After another twenty-four hours there is no return e-mail informing me about the status, so this then prompts a phone call. After a short chat with Third Mans sales rep it is told that the company is extremely backed up and there is nothing they can do about it. This unfortunately is not a reasonable solution. So instead of giving the record company the money they rightfully deserve  it is now going to Amazon, who has already shipped the albums the day I purchased them and instant digit copies for instant enjoyment. The icing on the cake is when I call Third Man back to inform them that I want to cancel the order they say that can be done, but when I start asking about the refund procedure they hang up the phone while I am mid sentence, thats what I call customer service. All I know is if I call the job done half way through, I would not have a job. So Third Man Record keep putting out the music its great, but get a new shipping department and watch your customer service people, because if you call the company ext.3 watch out for the person on the other end. 

No Thanks, MV
Such a cool little spot.  Awesome vibe, great beer selection, great bar staff and live music all the time.   Keep it up Belcourt crew! You guys are awesome!

So....I'm embarrassed. I thought Third Man Records was a record store. Oops. It's a record label with a cool record shop attached. So...it didn't have the record I wanted, but I learned a lot about Third Man Records and their artists and had a fun time exploring the shop. So I'm an idiot (to be fair I'm new to Nashville), but you learn something new every day!

Great  Beer Joint, excellent grub.

Beer selection is amazing over 85 drafts, plus hundreds of bottles.   

Great staff and service.

Food was really solid had a great Banh MI sandwich.
Good bar food!  The people are great!  Awesome live music!  Great friendly environment.

Well, well, well.....I see what most of the reviews say is true.  There is a nice patio, to be sure.  The beer selection is fantastic. The food was totally a mixed bag.  The fried green tomato app was unavailable. The queso fundido was just weird.....chips were slightly stale, queso wasn't great.  My friend's pork tacos were inedible. But, my burger?  My burger was awesome!.  I had the Juicy Lucy--I highly recommend it!  The potato salad was great too, which was a nice surprise.  The place is way understaffed, so service is far too slow.  So, if you have time to spend a leisurely afternoon on the patio and gamble on the quality of some menu items, go check it out!

I'm giving the tour 3 stars only because at the end, the photographer who hands out the picture that was taken on the stage circle was a bit cranky when a couple didn't buy the photo. He threw the photo on the table and then passive-aggressively announces that he guessed that they didn't like the photo. The photo cashier was in a mood too.. Whenever she gave the credit card bill for my husband to sign, she just grunted and flicked her fingers to the cup of pens indicating that he can grab one to sign the bill. I mean honestly, it was so nice to experience the typical southern hospitality in Nashville all weekend --until we visited the Opry, which was a huge surprise. 
The tour guide was nice and friendly, though the tour seemed very rushed. I think the people at the end of the tour need to be retrained or sent elsewhere, behind the scenes.
This is a great family friendly show. Came for my birthday and was a great gift. 28 July Comedy was hilarious.

Great place for lunch. No cover charge until the evening hours so go in and get out of the summer heat!  Good eats but a bit pricey for bar food. Had I stayed in town for the night I would have been back to feel the place with a bad but onward I must ride, ride, ride.  Definitely worth going to though. Good atmosphere.

This is one of the best kept secrets in Nashville! I'm not sure what the negative reviews are about. Kelli started as a cocktail waitress in 1991 and devoted her life to Printers Alley and it's amazing history. I am a Nashville native and this place IS Nashville. Great karaoke, superior sound, and a good clean bar. This place is a true gem.

Horrible service, do no use their film lab. It's a rip-off. Over charged and still didn't get every thing I paid for, plus it took them an extremely long time to get my pictures back. Never going back!

Wow went there for my birthday, they sat me and my boyfriend right next to the stage. They sang me the most beautiful happy birthday. Both bands were so great and really got the crowd involved the dance floor was packed too with people having a great time. There was even an engagement, she said yes!! Best time!!
This place is pretty fantastic and the show is very fun.  I'd highly suggest watching if you like country music.

Good burgers, nice staff, chill atmosphere. They play country music on the stereo. They have a bar and four local beers on tap.
It seems to be mostly non-tourist.
One last thing: it really is in an alley which is pretty empty, but it's not hidden, they do have a sign on the building.

We had;
Chicken and rib combo. Catfish po'boy. Chicken burger. Cheese burger. With crawfish bites and fried green tomatoes for appetisers.

Ribs are very saucy unless you ask, which I didn't. My fault. Chicken was not dry, and skin was perfectly flavoured. Served with BBQ beans and slaw. Slaw was not great, beans superb.

The po'boy was served dressed with potato fries. Burgers were served with chips (crisps to me and my island).

Fried green toms were great. Three dips, five pieces.
Crawfish bites also superb. Proper New Orleans style. 

Tourist drinks prices on the weekend. Buy one get a $6 take home plastic glass etc. cocktails about $11 - beer not much cheaper. The real downside in my view.

Live music however is nice and unobtrusive in the afternoon. Blues / jazz / 70's pop feel.

Servers were friendly. I wouldn't come back in a hurry but I wouldn't write it off. Just a lot on that row to try first!

If you haven't been to BB Kings before, it is probably going to be exactly what you expect. Large, noisy and crowded. We went on a Friday night in May in Nashville. The place was very busy but we were able to get a table without too much of a wait. My date had the brisket and really loved it. She said it was done exactly right and the sides were all perfect. I had the porkchops and I must say I was disappointed. They were saying and overcooked. I realize that can happen in a busy restaurant and it did this time. The live music was great and we had a really good time. The servers were very attentive but don't plan on having a lot of conversation in this  noisy restaurant.

We LOVE Flying Saucer. Unbelievable amount of beers and, somehow, the servers are still able to guide you to one you'll like. They have a good-sized menu of standard bar food that tastes way better than standard bar food. Our personal favorite is to make our own pizza and order chips and queso (and salsa) to start. This is a really cool hang with lots of tables and also several casual seating areas. TVs to watch games, Very cool space. It's attached to Union Station Hotel, and there's a large parking lot behind the building (pay to park by they will validate it for you to save you some money). We often go there, eat, drink, and walk on down to broadway (a good walk, but easier than trying to park down there). Highly recommend. Great for groups, too!

Great music. Great Brisket but it took 1 hour &10 minutes to get our meal after we ordered. A heads up from the bartender would have been great. Probably will not done there again but the music was good

We should have known better - B. A. D.  says it all. Bad food. Cheap, but bad. To start, they were out of at least four items on the menu. The cook carried a trash can into the kitchen by the rim, then went about cooking without washing his hands. Then the cook left before he cooked all our food. Yes, just left. Maybe that was a good thing. One of us got under-cooked chicken. The broccoli and cheese soup was pasty, and where was the broccoli?  The catfish was bland. The menu was misleading. The onion straws were all fried crust but no onion. Spend the extra $5 and go to a restaurant you'll actually enjoy.

We went to BB Kings on a Friday night of a full weekend bachelorette party. As out of towners we relied on review sites like yelp and open table. While the atmosphere was great the way the restaurant runs it's business is a little outrageous. They charge cover to those going in to eat. We paid 5 dollars each for a 7:30 reservation. Then after making the reservation on open table weeks prior, our group of 12 arrives and are told that they actually don't take reservations but will give is priority seating as soon as a table becomes available. We waited only about 45 minutes which was enough time to grab a drink at the bar. But a reservation is a reservation. It's one thing if a restaurant doesn't take one but to participate on open table makes it very confusing. 

Food was fine, nothing to write home about. Great band. Not a ton of dancing during dinner.

I had a tour of backstage because I wasn't able to get to a show while I was there. The tour was awesome! Our guide was funny and very knowledgeable. We got to see everything backstage like the artists do-- it was great! I learned a lot about the history of the place & about country music.

Only downside and why it's not 5 stars is because of the price. They tell you to buy tickets online to reserve a spot because tours are crowded, so instead of being $18 it was over $20 for a ticket and the day I went the place wasn't crowded at all. Even $18 is kind of expensive for an hour tour, when we couldn't even see every dressing room, only about 5, and that is what they're known for.

decided to go here before an event at TPAC - had a heck of a time finding it, definitely BACK ALLEY!  food was quite good if nothing special, just a true diner.  drinks were good and very reasonable.  the ambiance is great and the service spot on with very friendly wait staff.  would definitely head back here when in Nashville and don't want to deal with the crowds in other spots

I was so excited to try this place- great reviews, cool location, and fair pricing. The atmosphere is excellent- very inviting. I would love to say that I had a great experience, but it was the exact opposite. Forty minutes after ordering a cheeseburger and a salad, I inquired about their whereabouts. Our waitress came back and said they moved our ticket up and were STARTING on it. Seriously disappointed in the fact that it took an hour to get our food when there wasn't even a wait to be seated. After watching several more orders come out, hoping they were ours, and watching the tables all slowly clear out, our patience had reached its last. Then arrived our food- cold burger and limp fries. No more B.A.D. Food for us.

My family was passing through on a cross country road trip and we happened to stop by. My son is 7 years old and he is not a fan of loud music, but he enjoyed the live band that was playing. He even almost danced!! He food was amazing, my wife thoroughly enjoyed herself and the creamy greens were to die for! Brandon was our waiter and he was soooooo amazing! He helped us have the best experience and our family loves him so much we had to let his manager know that he's got a star on his hands! The Mac and cheese was hyped up and I tried it...I thought it was bland. But my substitute of creamy greens was amazing! Please try the brisket, it's delicious!

This place is a must do stop. This is Jack White's Studio and record store. There is the coolest antique recording booth that Neil Young and Jack White stood in and recorded an album together and they sell it there in the shop. We loved it and bought some albums and cool tee shirts. Parking is tough around there but we got lucky and parked right in front. Loved our time there!

Karaoke dive bar...that about sums it up.  Cheap drinks and loud singing.  I went with a large group on a Saturday night.  Maybe we were a little early for the crowd or it was an off night for Ms. Kelli's, because we were about the only folks there (we left around midnight).  Everyone had a great time!

I love Jack White, and all his projects. When I walked in with my wallet in-hand, I tried to not buy everything but it's so hard to resist. There's Jack White merch to White Stripes memorabilia to various concert posters, and Third Man shirts. Oh..I can tell you it's worth the paycheck! I walked in and was transported into a world of Jack White. I'm still trying to collect the whole White Stripes anthology. (All I need left is De Stijl, Get Behind Me Satan, and Icky Thump) This place definitely has magic stored inside it, and I am definitely revisiting back in the near future (as if I haven't visited already 3(00) times)

I was here for a private event and the fried green tomatoes are the best I've ever had in my life.  Better than anything in Alabama or St. Louis.  How do they get the onions on top so perfectly delicious?  Everyone at the party was floored by that appetizer.
Went for a concert so did not get there early enough to take the tour but just being at such an iconic place is one check off the bucket list. :)

Tiny but well worth your time- this little shop, a Jack White production that's part records store, part museum and total shrine to all things Jack & White Stripes, is a great stop near downtown Nashville. 

Check out their vinyl selection - heavy on Stripes and friends but with a nice variety of other options as well. 

Walk down the hall of gorgeous vinyl - a mini museum with laser cuts, wood, water treated and other beautiful framed albums from Jack, the Stripes and ex wife Karen Elson.

Grab some tokens from the staff and record your own album in the small recording booth (15 tokens), take photos in an actual photo booth (3 tokens) or throw in a quarter to watch the mechanical monkey band play.

This was a kooky and unique way to pass the time, and a great stop for my husband and I (both big Stripes fans).

Well disguised as an outbuilding behind the Union Station Hotel and next to the Frist Museum, the Flying Saucer pub is what you are looking for. Whether you want a comfortable place to chill, drink beer or have a solid meal or snack, this place delivers with good food, great beer selection and tons of personality and ambience. 
We enjoyed 2 huge and delicious piping hot pretzels with ample cheese and mustard dipping sauce, enough for 4 people to share through at least 2 rounds. The burgers are large and the fries are light and crispy. 
While the place is a serious pub and caters to grown-ups, we came on a Sunday afternoon and found many families with kids enjoying the place as well.
Whether you want a place to unwind after work or want to get away from doing the tourist thing on Broadway, the Flying Saucer is a very satisfying stop.

Förnämlig och stor konsertarena. Jag besökte den för en country gala/varieté föreställning. Jag gick på kvällens andra och sena föreställning. 

Det var super långa köer till entréerna när jag anlände mindre än en halvtimme innan min föreställning skulle börja. Medans vi köade och väntade så tömde man samtidigt arenan på besökarna som hade just sett färdigt den tidiga föreställningen. Allt flöt på smidigt och de lyckades få ut och in samtliga vi 4500 besökare (utsåld) och på plats innan showen startade på utsatt tid. Och då hann jag ändå besöka biljettkontoret för att kvittera ut biljetten jag hade bokat online. Imponerande snabbt och effektivt! Och trevligt bemötande genom hela processen. 

Jag hade själv en bra plats nere på parkett någorlunda nära scenen. Men för de lite längre bort så hjälpte nog de tre stora jumbotrons som fanns utplacerade här. 

Här sitter alla på sin sina bestämda platser på långa träbänkar, men var inte orolig de är väl stoppade och bekväma. Jag satt här igenom en tvåtimmars föreställning utan att märka något som helst obehag.

A review based on one tourist visit.  I probably should have come back for Trivia Night, but I was tired after a hot Nashville day.

Yelp lists Flying Saucer as a sports bar, but it isn't.  It has one (1) tv screen.  Fortunately for me, the Tennessee Titans were playing the Minneapolis Vikings so I got to see the game I wanted.

The place opens at noon, so it's good thing the game doesn't start right away.  Too early for a beer, at least for me, so I didn't sample their hundreds of beers.  Seemed a shame, but there it is.  On the recommendation of the waitress for something I probably couldn't get anywhere else, she recommended The German Plate, two grilled bratwursts (of different types) with their homemade potato salad and kraut.  It was okay.  In retrospect, I should have gone with my first choice of a Saucer Burger, or even been a bit venturesome. The price on the brats was fine, and it was an okay amount of food (see pic).

The main reason to check the place out is the decor.  See other pics.  Their wide variety of beer is another draw; if you're local, you can join the UFO club and if you sample 200 or more beers they'll put your name on a saucer, and put it on the wall.

Really, three and a half stars, rounded up because I did get to see the Vikings game (which we won).  Left at halftime, satisfied.

Two songwriter nights a week- fantastic stuff! I'm a huge fan. Beer selection is much better than your average bar. Good amount of tv's. Bartenders are great. Prices reasonable. Checks all the boxes for me. Although I could do without the Browns on Sunday :)

If you're an older, die hard country music fan then this is for you. However, we are 30something and didn't know more than 1/2 the people the tour guide went on about. The history was definitely cool but they go into waaaaaay too much detail! It says 45mins but it turned into 1.5hrs! No one in our group was having an Awesome time. Lol they charge you for a picture on the stage too But you can take your own just not with the microphone.  If this was a 30mim tour I would have given it 5 stars!
Been here twice on vacation. It's nice to not have to wait in line to eat and to not settle for a place with good music but bad food. Give it a try you will not be disappointed!! Girlfriend approved!

Very friendly staff! We came early to ride the Honky Tonk Express and waited in the air conditioning. The manager was happy to let us wait inside and even answered some questions about the Honky Tonk, even though they contract out that service and he wasn't sure of the answers. The band sang customized songs to our bachelorette using her and her fiancé's names and our hometown (Chicago!) to personalize the lyrics! Highly recommend for any bachelorettes out there looking for memorable snapchat stories and videos. No idea how the drinks are since we didn't stay long, but the service was impeccable!

Walked right in for lunch on Saturday.  They had a band like every other place in Nashville but a lot more space than the places on Broadway.  This would be a good place for groups like 6-15.    We had burgers and they were average, average fries too.   Kids meals were great for the $$$.  Catfish platter and BBQ chicken meal with green beans and mashed potatoes.   Cool ambiance and good location when walking Nashville.  Service was fine. Maybe a little slow but we didn't mind since there was a band.

My absolute favorite place to go for a live music show. Even better than Broadway for me. 

The Opry is small enough that you can feel the presence of the artists on stage. The performances span generations, with performances by a variety of musicians. The acoustics are wonderful. And you never really know what to expect until you experience that show.

If you go to Nashville, you must go to the Opry.

Probably one of the best places to see in Nashville! What an amazing experience! All the history in this place takes your breath away if you are a true country fan! The knowledge of the tour guides is endless. And the videos are amazing. I'm still in awe.

Came here for dinner after a long night of walking around trying to find somewhere that didn't have an hour wait to be seated. The Wednesday night deal was buy 1 get one draft free! So we were pretty stoked about that. 

Live music for the majority of the evening which is always a treat. Our server, Paige, was really friendly and accommodating with our large group of people. 

As far as food goes, it's the standard southern comfort food: burgers, shrimp po' boy, catfish sandwich, pulled pork sandwich, etc. Everything was decent quality and I don't think anyone really had any complaints about their meal. 

One thing I I unfortunately would not recommend are their signature drinks. For the first two rounds of drinks we stuck with the beer deal and margaritas. Then we got bold and tried out really cutely named pop-star themed drinks. Literally tasted like straight alcohol with no good flavor which was really a let down. Stick with the beer and margaritas !

Upon entering Music City Tippler in Nashville's Midtown, I thought to myself, this place, contrary to many of the very Country bars on Nashville's Broadway, could do well in NYC. Well, go figure, it's actually sisters to NYC's very own Tippler that I reviewed months ago. So, it was no surprise that I liked the place. 

You can notice similar aesthetics in the decor, the bar, and the cocktails. Country music not particularly your thing? No problem, because you won't hear much, or any, of that here. Playing hip-hop, top 40, and some club bangers, the vibe here takes you outside of Nashville, but keeps you around all the sweetness and politeness. Ideal, right?

To drink, I had their Del Rio (Vida Mezcal, St. Germain, lemon, maple, The Bitter End BBQ Bitters). Mezcal never really seems to disappoint me, and certainly didn't in this drink either. You definitely get the smokiness, which is pushed further with the BBQ bitters, but then a nice sweetness from the elderflower and maple.

I loved the Grand Ole Opry House.  I am not country fan perse.  There is certain country acts i like and ones I don't.  But the Grand Ole Opry House is something everyone should see for historical value and pure entertainment.  We have been twice in our life and truly enjoyed it.  If you go to Nashville this is a "MUST SEE"

God awful place. The food is complete trash and that is sampling four plates and one appetizer. 

Terrible service and a Long Island ice tea that looked like a weak apple juice.   

The tables are so close together your elbows practically touch your neighbor and they sit four to a table sized comfortably for one so you end up semi holding your plate sitting at an angle to your table while music that no one would call jazz or blues assaults your eardrums in a small club that apparently needs the same volume level as the local amphitheater 

Believe this one; ignore the idiots ranking this place four stars.
Came in before our movie at Belcourt. Service was great, she was very friendly & recommended items. Food came out quick & was great! Beers were tasty & enjoyed the live music on writers night.

I will NEVER return!  This "business" is a SCAM!!!  My (handicapped) husband and I drove from Michigan, spent over $1,000 dollars and waited a lifetime to see Crystal Gayle.  On the NIGHT OF THE SHOW, after we arrived we were told she canceled.  AND, Vince Gill canceled last night!  AND Charlie Pride canceled recently.  My theory is that they use headliners to sell tickets (sold out!!!) and then use the ol' bait and switch routine.  So instead of Crystal Gayle, we got a bunch of old has-beens and young wannabes.  The whole show SUCKED!!!  Complaints to THREE DIFFERENT PEOPLE did zero good.  Why?  Because they're going to TAKE YOUR MONEY NO MATTER WHAT!!!  I paid to see Crystal Gayle.  Instead I got a shit show.  She supposedly canceled on April 13th....plenty of time to notify (email) their customers and offer a refund.  But those greedy SOBs aren't about to do that!!!  Avoid this place at all costs!
Mrs Kelli's is so fun and a great atmosphere. It's always a good time with karaoke and drinks!!
The food is actually pretty solid BBQ and it's perhaps the coolest music venue outside the Opry itself in Nashville.

Great service! Our waitress took our order and brought out our food right away. It was definitely the busiest night if the week. ND vs LSU bowl game evening and she still killed it!! AMAZING! Ask for Kaley, she's the best waitress at the place.

We took an amazing tour of the grand ole open and had a wonderful tour guide. It was informative, interesting and we had a great time. It was husbands 2nd visit in the lady couple weeks. He visited there while on business and brought me today to celebrate our birthdays. We're staying in Memphis but it was worth the 3 hour drive.

Really cool spot w/a great selection of beer! Kind of regretted trying to make it dinner as the menu is pretty limited and basic, but it keeps you from heading elsewhere! Speaking of heads, the bartender seemed like he was suffering from a head injury because he couldn't remember basic things but was friendly. We were only in town for 3 nights but came back a second time!

I've been here twice.  Thoroughly enjoyed both times.  It's always something a little different.  And I love how name stars come out and just sing a song or two and then it's on to somebody else.  I'll come again next time.

This place was fun...they had some technical difficulties, so it was a rough start. Biggest issue was they did the songs at random. Most other places (not in Nashville) it was done in a queue. Here, it was a random mix...so while we were there way before anyone else, the new comers got to sing right away while we waited. We had a large group (we were in town for a company sponsored event) and so a lot of our customers weren't able to even sing before they decided to head out for the night. The drinks were very inexpensive...it was a fun atmosphere, but didn't really like the way that they lined up the songs. Plus, the DJ/karaoke master decided to cut in and do a song...thought that was super random. Overall a good time dancing at least.

Love this place. I can't wait to go back. This was my first time. 

There is a medal detector when you enter, so leave all those items at home. 

Check out the gift shop first before it gets busy. There are things you can buy here that you can't buy at Opryland. Take pictures soon as you arrive in front of the cutouts before the line gets long and it gets dark. 

All seats are assigned so there is no rush to go in. I'm not saying be late, but you don't have to shove your way to the front of the line. 

If I recall correctly you can bring both food and drink to your seat. Check out the popcorn stand. They had lots of good food trucks, but we opted to eat before we arrived, not knowing the lines and options.

Came here last night with a group. We didn't do it this time but I would recommend taking the tour because you really get to see some interesting things inside and hear some great stories. We happened to see Charlie Daniels last night. He's 81 years old. I must say he put on an incredible show! His age has not slowed him down a bit! This is a must go if you're in town.

From
Out of town and wanted a hole in the wall bar! Beers cheap:cold, atmosphere awesome, great band! Kelsey bartender was great and the others too! Definitely will come when we come back into town! Cheers

Great idea and I'm sure Nashville is proud to house it... Shop is very small, high potential for ANNOYING; kids, families, and amateurs playing the two available guitars.  I no longer care about vinyl, my BOORISH ears are fine with mp4.  Tshirts are over priced.
We. Love. You. In our household. Your draft and bottle menu is perfect and y'all  are perfect.
Pretty cool place. Really small store but packed full of cool old timey gadgets and vinyl, music memorabilia etc..to buy. worth a visit if you're in the area.

I'm giving Back Alley Diner 5 stars because I have never had anything but the best experience. This past Saturday a group of friends and I (there were 15 of us total) ate there before the Nashville Art Crawl (we've been doing this regularly for the last year).

Saturdays are a great day to go because they have $.50 wings and $2 PBRs (a fantastic combo if you ask me). I get the buffalo ones and my husband gets the tabasco ones which are somewhat hotter (you can also get them plain without wing sauce) and they come with either ranch or blue cheese dressing. I LOVE these wings. Seriously, I think they're the best! Every other wing I've tried in the past year is compared to these and so far, none have been better.

I really can't speak much for their other food because I love their wings so much, I haven't been tempted to try anything else. Except a few months ago, I did try the pulled pork quesadilla and it was very good.

The service is exceptional. We always have the same waitress (it's a shame I can't remember her name) and she's very attentive and accommodating for us (big groups can sometimes be a challenge).

It's a simple, casual place with good food and great prices. I'd definitely recommend B.A.D.

Maybe it was the time of day I was there, but it wasn't hopping and the food and drinks seemed a little pricey for the value. I love blues and share a birthday with BB King, who I never got to see live. Thought this would make up for it. It didn't.

8/13/18 -- After walking all over Nashville, we stopped in to B.B. King Club right about time to eat.. lucky us.  Not starving, we decided to split a meal.  But first..... our timing could not have been better. Plenty of room, for the place had only a few tables filled but we went to the bar anyway.  The Bartender was super nice and had a very good attitude of "touristy people".  Which we were !!   This was our first time to Nashville.  

We ordered some cold beers and ordered the Fried Chicken w/ cheesy pasta and fresh veggies.  Delicious and definitely enough for us to split.   
The Chicken was moist, nice crunch on the batter and the veggies were perfectly cooked...... firm and not mushy at all.  

A guy was playing before the main headliner.... good, but acoustics were bad for a single Artist playing a guitar .... and I didn't get his name.  

We were getting ready to move along.  The restaurant was filling up with people and then the Bartender said.... " you might want to stay for the group that was setting up to play".  It was the Stacy Mitchhart Band.  We'd never heard of him.... but, we stayed and we are glad we did.  More instruments, more diners (the place was packed) and they sounded really good.   

Good food, good Blues..... enjoyable evening !!!  What more could we ask for.

The best place ever great food friendly staff very clean bar love to hangout there . Biggest T.V I ever see to enjoy watching the game , if you are sports fan this the best place to go . The good thing you can bring your dog and set outside, t.v's everywhere games on the side great bands every Wednesday and Sunday

It doesn't take a Jack White fan to realize this place is pretty cool. This is the world headquarters of Third Man Records, Jack White's record label. I should preface this review by saying I am not a Jack White fan nor am I a huge fan of his genres of music, though I do like a couple of his songs: "Seven Nation Army" (2003) and "Another Way to Die" (2008). I came here because one of my buddies, who is a big Jack White fan, wanted to come here. He ended up buying some merchandise to take back home to Brooklyn.

Currently, there are two Third Man Records retail storefronts: this one in Nashville which opened in 2009 and one in Detroit which opened in 2015. This store is located in the SoBro (south of Broadway) neighborhood of downtown Nashville. There is no dedicated parking for customers, but there is plenty of free street parking on both 7th Ave S and Middleton St. We parked on Middleton. There were lots of spots available when we visited around 1:30pm on a Saturday. This isn't the nicest part of town, but we felt safe enough walking around the area in broad daylight.

The building looks cool. It looks like an old studio or warehouse that has been painted black/dark gray with bright solid yellow, red, and blue garage doors. The storefront looks like an album cover itself.

There's a lot going on at this location. It's a record store, "novelties lounge," offices and distribution center, photo studio, and live music venue. My friends and I only spent time in the record store and novelties lounge. It was packed when we arrived because a bunch of people had gathered to take a tour. According to Third Man Records' website, the store offers tours on Fridays and Saturdays at 2pm for $20 per person (first come, first served) with a limit of 10 tickets sold per tour. There were definitely more than 10 people taking the tour we saw and it started around 1:30pm instead of 2pm.

The record store and novelties lounge aren't very big. It was quite crowded and snug with all the customers, but once the folks on the tour left, there was much more space for us to spread out and explore. Both the record store and the novelties lounge are eclectically and uniquely decorated. I'm not quite sure how to describe it other than to say it's a combination of retro and kitsch... perhaps?

The novelties lounge is neat. It opened in 2012. It's called the "novelties lounge" because it has a bunch of working vintage machinery that you can actually use. They include a Scopitone 16mm film jukebox, a classic "fully automatic" photo booth where you can do "4 different poses" in only "2 minutes," a two-person listening booth with two turntables where you can preview records, and a really nifty 1947 Voice-O-Graph. For $20, you can use the Voice-O-Graph to record anything you want, up to about two minutes, on a 6-inch record.

You can hear what customers have recorded using the Voice-O-Graph on Third Man Records' website here: https://thirdmanrecords.com/locations/nashville-storefront/record-booth.

Another fun fact: Third Man Records is the only music venue in the world that records live performances directly to vinyl records.

I'm sure if you're a hard-core Jack White fan going here the first time feels like a pilgrimage...if that sounds like you, make sure to visit at least once when in the Nashville area and you'll probably give it 5 stars. I'm a moderate fan of White's but it's easy to see he took time to curate every inch of this somewhat small storefront to his studio-- every decorative piece on the wall or a shelf and every item for sell seems hand-picked by him.

As an overall record store, the selection is small-to-moderate but fairly priced. The coolest items for sale  the third-man in-studio live LPs, all about $15 each so you can search to see if your favorite act has recorded a set in the studio attached to the store and pick it up. Friendly service, some cool books, LPs, shirts and things to buy and some neat things to look at. Stop by the photo booth to get a memento of your visit if you're so inclined and you're out the door.

We ate here a group of 14. Food was good and affordable. The service was amazing!!! Heather our waitress kept up with the refills and cleared dishes faster than anyone I've ever had serve me. Especially with such a large group. Would definitely go back!

Beautiful place to see a show. Church pew seating but they were cushioned and leg room was decent. Line up included Connie Smith, Hailey Whitters, Dailey and Vincent, Craig Morgan, Sawyer Brown, Dustin Lynch and Henry Cho. I am not a country music fan but I enjoyed the show.

The show was amazing! We went to the second show. It was a complete cluster getting in as there are no signs directing people where to go or what to do. Once the doors opened it got a little better. Lots of older people standing for long periods of time in very hot, humid weather. If you are going to the second show, no need to go until about 5-10 minutes before the show starts or you'll just be standing around.

Was walking and saw a little sign and decided to go check it out. It's in a back alley and hidden. Which is what makes it so awesome! We sat down at the bar and the bartender lacy was so sweet and talkative made us feel so welcomed! We got the sizzling burger and the home made broccoli soup and they were hands down the best I have ever had! I highly recommend it! And lacy made one of the best margaritas around! 100 stars absolutely awesome check it out! Or you will regret it!

Great stop on our Nashville-Memphis week. We are huge Jack White fans - just saw him a few weeks ago in BKLYN. 

And seeing the shop and getting to do the behind the scenes tour was oddly like willy wonka and the chocolate factory for music!

Really enjoyed the guide and discussions. A real highlight of our trip south
Great place! It's more local than touristy. Good drink menu, and decent food. Fun and laid back! If you're a beer lover, you'll be in heaven!

I liked this place! The curb appeal grabs you and kind of pulls you in. The bar is very dedicated to the armed forces, fire departments, and police departments. The band that was playing was good enough to make me stick around for a beer and a few songs. I ordered the Redneck Riviera on tap, which was darker than I expected, but was rather smooth and tasted great. The bartenders were nice and the atmosphere is fun.

Used to be very special into the 1990s, then after that went to crap due to all these NO NAMES being able to be on stage and cant sing and granted memberships for 1 hit wonders.  Back in the "Real" days of The Opry a person had to pay their dues to even be considered for a guest spot, nowadays they dont..I forsee The Opry CEASING To exist in 20 more yrs

I love this place. They have awesome food and great drink specials, and every server and bartender I've ever had has been awesome and so nice. It's right by work so it's fun to go to happy hour after work. The BAD never disappoints!

Not a country music fan, but went with our group and thoroughly enjoyed the show.  Seemed to be a good mix of old stars and up and comers.  The only negative for me was that it could have been about 20 min shorter.  Definitely worth seeing.

Did backstage tour.  It was pretty good.  Bit rushed, about 45 minutes total, I guess to get through the multiple tours passing through.  The highlights were  getting on stage and seeing all the dressing rooms.  Our tour guide was friendly and funny.  Parking was decent.

If you want beer, you'll find it here.
If you want some Irish-style bar food, you'll find it here.
If you want one of the better trivia's in town, you'll find it here. 
If you want your name on a plate on the wall after drinking 200+ beers, you'll find it here.
Now go!

Loved that they had wine and the beer was reasonably priced. Good music as well! 

But why do they only use plastic cups? And plastic STRAWS!? It's 2018, ya'll. Most plastic isn't recycled and seeps into groundwater and ends up in your fish! It's not just about the environment, it's about the future of our children.

My fiancé and i had a GREAT time.  This was his first visit and i hadnt been in years. I thoroughly enjoyed the makeover.  I like that they opened the floor and moved the stage over to the side of the building.  Service was a little slow but it was the weekend.  Assuming someone called out. Why else would you not have enough workers for a Friday night?  I'd be happy to visit again and will definitely make referrals.  Oh the food was good too. I had the crawfish poppers.
Great service, phenomenal selection of brews, quality food and an atmosphere that offers something for everyone.

Two weeks ago, I would have given this place 5 stars.  Great beer selection, food (especially pretzels!) is A-OK, and the service is generally very good.  I've been coming here for years. Recently (in the last month or two), their ID checking has gotten disruptive.  I have never been carded to the extent that I have at the Saucer anyplace else in Nashville.  I realize that there are laws about this and they are abiding by them, but when I have to show ID to get in the door, do you really have to card me every time I order a beer the rest of the night?  The kicker was last week when an out-of-country visitor and I tried to grab a beer at the Saucer.  They WILL NOT accept any other country's valid driving license, national registration card, etc with a picture and birth date.  The only acceptable ID for foreigners at the Saucer is a passport with a US Customs stamp in it, although that is not posted anywhere (that we saw). RIDICULOUS! I've never run into this problem anywhere else in the world. Not only is it weird for a restaurant to paw through a passport to check if you're there legally, it's highly irresponsible for a place that specializes in serving alcohol to condone carrying around a passport (if you're a foreigner) when you are drinking.  I'm boycotting.

I am a definite frequenter of the flying saucer.  My husband and I are a part of their saucer club and we are slowly but surely working our way through the 200 beers (we're around 45 at the moment).  It has been so much fun selecting random beers and giving anything and everything a try, something I would have never done otherwise.  Most of their food is pretty good but some of it is a miss; their pizzas, wraps, pretzels, brats, and beer cheese soup are all great, their new buffalo chicken wrap is my current favorite.  Items that have just been okay are the chicken sandwich, rocket tots, and spinach and artichoke dip.  Also their service can be hit or miss too, we've had a great server on a extremely busy night and a really slow one on a dead afternoon, it just depends.  Anyway, we love coming out here for some great atmosphere, food and to try some beers.  Of course the beer selection is massive at 300+ and ever changing, it's a beer connoisseurs dream.

Totally awesome. I'm a country music fan but I think even if you aren't, you would probably enjoy it.

The live to air show and old school country legends performing make you feel like you've stepped in a time warp, but they do have a lot of modern acts too. We got to see Johnny Reid make his Opry debut, which was quite exciting.

Crowd is definitely older, very older (60+) but there are a few youngsters in the mix. 

Delicious homemade kettlecorn sold outside. 

Show runs from 7pm-9:15pm and you can park for free in the nearby shopping center parking lot.
Stopped there for a quick bite and to listen to some blues.  Food was average,  but the band was great.  Definitely will go back.
