Walking up to this place I was a little skeptical about what I was about to walk into. Literally in an alley and shady looking. To my surprise once we walked in it was a cute diner and the food was great!!! The waiters were super nice and friendly. Drinks were very good too. Absolutely good surprise. Loved it !

The Grand Ole Opry lived up to, and exceeded, its own stellar reputation. This experience was fantastic and taught me a lot about the heritage of the venue's place country music history. I loved each well-planned minute of entertainment. The sharp comedy and varied acts showcased many varieties of country music and I was enthralled with each moment of the performance. In fact, this was one of the greatest live events I have ever had the privilege of attending. All this from a non-country music fan. Outstanding.

I knew I wanted to visit this place before I even arrived in Nashville! We made reservations but our table was directly by speakers so I choose to just sit at the bar ( which was more fun to me) ... The cocktails and food were great ! If you order a shot , take your receipt to the hostess then you'll get a souvenir glass..

The night I was there a 15 year old kid was having a birthday so they let him go onstage to jam with the band . He played guitar with so much soul . It was amazing .. 

All in all I had a great time there and will be sure to visit again !!
Love this bar! I go very often to shoot some pool and drink. Maybe even a little karaoke. it is a great atmosphere and all kinds of music music!
Certainly not the cleanest place around but a great local dive bar with good food (grilled cheese burger) friendly staff and cheap beer! Definitely a place that is a cool place to check out

I have a coworker who has been raving about this place for months, so I finally decided to go, and let me tell you, it is sooo good! There's a surprising amount of space - there's two floors! It was crowded too (we went at 11) but they had plenty of waiters, and we barely had to wait for our food. I ordered the soup (chicken, broccoli & cheddar) and a sandwich (turkey) and it filled me up and I loved it! We were in and out in about 40 minutes, which is perfect! I saw so many good looking things on the menu, so I'm definitely going back for more!

Food was on point, music on Tuesday night was awesome.  Grant Garland band!
Tre is an enthusiastic, hard working, sweet guy! Met the needs of all 9 in our party. Pleasurable night out in Nashville. Would definitely do it again!

Great ribs probably the best we've had. Slight problem with our order but the manager jumped in and corrected it immediately. Live blues band was great. Staff extremely friendly and helpful. You can't go wrong stopping in.

Great Venue. 4400 people and the design easily accommodated. Hard pew seats but still comfortable. A chaotic scene grabbing a cab but worked out. Staff nice. Acoustics good. They change out groups after 2-3 songs. Cool. We really enjoyed.i receommnd you take a ubber lyft or cab, it is very hectic in the parking lot.

I attended the soft-opening of this snazzy new multi-faceted business earlier this week and was impressed with the concept. 

Previously this space housed the club Mai but a complete over-haul has happened with this newly minted space. Not only does this place offer a club atmosphere but also a restaurant, lounge, and venue space too. 

Due to it being a soft-opening and not being in the complete swing of things yet, I will update more when I revisit soon!

The official Grand Opening is tonight, Saturday, February 16th.

Yelp365#26
This was my first visit - I joined a couple of friends for drinks.  I love the cozy feel of the interior and the place overall has a good vine.  I definitely plan on going back.

Probably should have come later in the evening -- I expect the experience would have been better if the live music was on... Came with a group of 6 and the place had a bit of a tired, dreary vibe -- again, perhaps the lull before the place came to life later on... Food was OK, but not great. All-in-all, left us feeling like it hadn't lived up to the hype... Perhaps will try again deeper into the evening...

The music is great! High quality sound and musicianship. We were here on Saturday night for hours! Our first server was Trey who was Awesome! He was attentive, helpful, friendly and our food arrived in a time,y manner. We had the fries with beef and gravy on them and the fried pickles to start. Many rounds and a new server later (sorry I don't have her name, I think she helped us bc I caught her eye but I didn't get her name) we orders the house salad which was Huge for the price and very good, the buttermilk ranch was delicious and not so thick that you felt guilty eating it. And we ended the night with the brownie dessert.
We didn't have an actual main dish so I can't comment on those but I can say that we had a great time, listened to hours of good music and everyone was friendly.

Was in town for a night and got a ticket to a Friday night show ($70) which was located in the nosebleed section (up and to left of stage).  They have giant screens on the walls to give you a better view of the stage but it takes away from the intimate experience (even though they can fit 4000 people in the venue). The seats are actually wooden pews with a cover on them and there isn't much leg room. Definitely no where to dance if you were thinking about it. 

There was no musical guests playing that were famous. The headliner was an artist by the name of Randy Skaggs who got fame in the early 80s supposedly but I hadn't heard of him. 

Anyway the venue is beautiful on the inside. Looks like an old grand house of worship. They do sell concessions including beer, wine and mixed drinks and the prices are in line with a concert venue.
Great food, drinks, fun atmosphere and excellent blues music. My salmon was grilled and flavorful

Very cool record shop with tons of merch. Don't miss the listening booth in the back corner. It's stocked with 45s that you can play from a variety of artists. We came here for the tour which is limited to 10 people because of the small space. There was only one spot left but they let our group of 3 join. Very grateful! Especially because we are from out of town. We got to tour the whole facility and even go into their recording room and see how they record direct to acetate during live shows. The only weird part was that the guide made us put our phones in a box at the beginning that he carried with him the whole time. I would just leave my phone in the car next time.

Had dinner here recently - hosted by family living in the area.  Although the food was about average, we didn't come here just for the food.  We came here for the overall experience - namely the live music.
And on that "note" - the band was AWSOME!  They played jazz as well as performed popular songs.  All of it was so good.  The $5 cover charge was laughably cheap considering the quality of music we were treated to.  Would definitely come back here again.
Oh and by the way - the nachos and the tater tots with pulled pork were very tasty.

If you want to sing this is the place to be!! I've been to Nashville many many times and I always always chose wannabes as my go to spot for Karaoke. The staff is friendly the song selection is incredible and it's usually not too terribly crowded. Channel your inner country star and head on down to wannabes you'll be glad you did!

I visited Anthem because I was the lucky winner of two tickets to a splendid foodie event, a dinner by celebrity chef Maneet Chauhan. You might recognize her fabulous face if you watch too much Food Network (guilty!), she's a judge on Chopped and has been on Iron Chef.  

The chic Anthem setting was the perfect space for this trendy event. We were in half of the building space. The room had high open ceilings with little booths tucked into one side and leather lounge furniture sections on the other. The back wall of the room was the bar. The middle of the room was filled with one long table for the dinner. The color scheme was hard to distinguish because of the low lighting but the effect suggested that it would accommodate a number of colors and designs. The hostesses and servers were very nice and professional. Maybe it was just this event but the entire staff were trendy, young females. 

The dinner was fabulous! The food was exciting and interesting (in a good not weird way). We were lucky enough to sit next to the owner of the space and his wife. We learned so much about the space and his plans with Chauhan to open her first restaurant in Nashville! Y'all, I ate the food and let me tell you, we are so lucky! 

If you are looking for a chic, modern space to throw an event that is close to downtown, I would definitely schedule a visit at Anthem. The owner told me that he doesn't just throw dinner parties; they host business functions as well. Having attended an event here I can attest that your guests will be impressed with what they see.

I'm a fan of any place that has good drinks AND a wide variety of seating options. The open plan and unique table setup encourages a lot of socializing with strangers, so if you're not into that, maybe don't come here. Of course the amount of beer options was overwhelming and of course the saucers were cute. I sipped on a perfect Kriek in a sunken in cracked leather couch (am I remembering that right?) while talking about German barbecue culture with the party to my right and sketching my homeboy on a spare page of my journal - we'd just visited the Frist and I was feeling inspired. I thoroughly enjoyed doing all of those things in this place, so, do with that information what you will.

This was my first time at BB King's and we had such a fabulous time! The food was delicious (we got the blues burger and hot wings) and the music was incredible!! We saw two different bands during dinner and they were both phenomenal. Our server Brandon was fantastic, made the whole experience more enjoyable, and took great care of us all night. We'll be back!

By far the best burger (In my opinion) in Nashville. Fries are to die for. They seem to have something going on everyday of the week and a great happy hour! The staff is always great and is a cool laid back vibe! Don't let this place fool you! Love this place!

Came here for a friend's bachelorette party. We had a fantastic time. The place is nicely lit and everyone was having a great time. The booze is pretty pricy but it's downtown Nashville so you kinda know what you're in for if you came here. The cool thing is that this place is kind of conjoined to another huge bar with a stage for dancing. We kept alternating between the two and had a hell of a time. I highly recommend popping by this place if you're in the area.

SO COOL ! Loved the experience ! i've been listening to GOO since i was a kid 50+ years..
Loved it. the only thing I din't care for was the constant sponsor announcements especially for Cracker B......So anti LGBT organization .

Located a short drive away from downtown, but worth the drive. I am not even a big country music fan but I enjoyed the tour. Our guide, Emily, was very knowledgable and willing to answer any questions. There was a  band rehearsing so we weren't able to stand on center stage which would have been awesome.

Pleasant surprise!  Went here on 11/28 with my girl and we both enjoyed it. The ribs were some of the best I have ever eaten;  fall of the bone perfection and great flavor!  Crawfish popper appetizer was unique and very tasty.  Excellent live music, people dancing, and an overall great vibe in this place. Long live the King!

Loved this little place. Recommended by the old "friend of a friend," this placed proved to be a nice late night stop. The proprietor was a fascinating woman who produced music and employed up-and-coming singer's and musicians trying to get their foothold in the Nashville music scene. 

Our bartender was a skilled singer and friendly as can be.  A waiter, however, who was hanging out after his shift, (apparently he was a musical virtuoso of some measure) was a bit toasted and acting like an jerk. I guess his provocative behavior was meant to rile us up, but we are a pretty un-rileable group and devour a#%holes like this as if they're light bar snacks. It was amusing as hell, like free entertainment!

While it was too late to sample the food, the vibe was fun, the creative energy was almost palpable, and the people were interesting and entertaining. It was a pleasant surprise all around.

Best part of this establishment is the musicians and their love for their music. Loved the early evening band!
Sat at the bar. The bar staff was friendly. I ordered a local draft beer and ribs. The ribs were better than average, but that is as good as I can put in my review. Came with beans and slaw, both good.
The place was full, and people watching was fun.
Overall, fun place, but they can up their game a little with their food.

Flying Saucer gets 5-stars even though it has faults because it's just that fun.  Traditional pub style, they have an amazing beer selection which always rotates in new drinks.  They even import a keg or two of a certain beer, and it's only available until it's been drank, giving a sort of exclusive variety.  Pint Night on Mondays is super fun too!

As bar food goes, it's pretty damn solid.  Both the pretzels and the sausage are really tasty and are sure to please everyone at your table.

There are some downsides, though.  It's pretty loud, so can be hard to have a meaningful one-on-one with someone.  Finding a table can be tricky (you might have to be a vulture and wait for a party getting up).  You have to be a little creative with parking, too.

Overall though it's a great place and I'll be back with my group.
We had dinner and entertainment here as part of a large group in town for a convention. Although the food was buffet style for us all it was all great. The live music and atmoshere was good as well

What a great day of entertainment!! We started with the tour which gave us amazing insight into so many unknown facts and the way The Grand Ol Opry works. We even got to go on stage with our group and see what the singers see - what a view! Then the evening was full of talent - many different genres were in the line up. Comedy, classic country, new country AND Alabama!!
Great tour guide. Awesome place to visit. Get to go where all the stars go when they perform.

This little hidden gem is worth 5 stars!
=== === ===
Ok, the place is rather tiny for a record store, but there are tons of interesting finds inside. 

You can find strange recordings from people you'd never think would have recorded anything. I picked up two small albums of Elvira for my hubby. Anyway, there's also a recording booth where you can make your own 2 1/2 minute record which is pretty fun. You can also make your own guitar figure out of wax via a machine while you watch. 

If you're a music lover, especially music on vinyl, this is a place that you'll want to check out. There are also some videos on YouTube of this place where musicians will take their turn in the recording booth. Pretty cool to check out.
We just checked out the record shop and it was awesome. While we were there we found out they do tours of the studio. We'll definitely be back to check it out.

We visited B.B King's Blues Club on a Wednesday night and we heard that we should make reservations. So we did on Open Table for 7pm and the band started at 7:30pm. We were sat right away. The band was AWESOME. Great soulful music! The food exceeded all expectations. We ordered catfish bites for an appetizer and they were delicious! For entrees I ordered the bbq chicken and rib platter and the meat literally fell off the bone. So amazing! The service was even better. Our waiter was slammed busy, but we still had our drinks full at all times. If you visit Nashville make this a stop!!!
The beer was kind of warm, but the blues were very cool.  We'll be back.

What a show last night in the Blue Room!  Just us and Jack White and 298 of his other friends 

Forgot my ear plugs and still have ringing ears from it!

Thanks for the shot at some AWESOME tickets to one Hell-uh-vah show!  An unforgettable evening!

(Note: Was really torn between giving them three or four stars. The point would be docked if I compared Tippler to its neighbor, Patterson House, only a five minute walk away.)

As a huge fan of Patterson House, I was very excited about Tippler arriving in Nashville. At first glance, the place did not disappoint. I love the ambiance of the place, and the fact that it has space---always a good thing in Nashville where it seems like every decent bar is crowded every night.

Some notes:

- Tippler should win on food since they offer a full menu, but they offer only a very, very limited (around four items, if I remember right) menu for people at the bar and for those who want to stay outdoors. I get how this could be easier service-wise, but it was a big limitation for me and the husband both times we went.

- Tippler should win on novelty since they serve draft cocktails, but they only serve three or four different kinds. When we were there, they had already sold out of the one that sounded interesting (at 7 pm), and there's nothing novel about a mojito or a vieux carre, which were their other offerings. Their standard cocktails run $12-13 each, but so do Patterson House's---who have a larger bar menu.

The food itself was good but unremarkable. We tried a sampling of the bar food and also had entrees another night. (I have to say that the salmon was very good---I like my seafood salty though, so you have been warned.)

I don't mean to bash on Tippler because I actually really like it---and intend to go back repeatedly! But when there's another option close by with amazing cocktails and really good bar food, they need to do something to make themselves shine. If they improve their bar menu and draft cocktail offerings, I think they could really be something.

Breathtaking. Such a great venue for shows with so much history. We took the backstage tour and it was so interesting and you even get to walk across the stage. There's always someone you know playing there and it's definitely worth the trip!

This is our second evening in a row coming here. We have a location in San Antonio, TX that is pretty damn awesome. We feel right at home! The beer on tap is plentiful and the service is great! 

Julie was our server last night and she was very friendly and tentative. We enjoyed our experience yesterday so much that we came back again and requested to be seated in Julie's section! The fact that they have the Monday pint night special is the cherry on top to our Flying Saucer experience! You can't beat that! Not only that, they have Stiegl Radler Grapefruit ON TAP! That's my FAVORITE!!!!! I have never seen it on draft in Texas! I'm doing my happy dance inside! YOU GUYS HAVE TO TRY THE STIEGL RADLER! Do it! Your girlfriends that aren't huge beer drinkers will love it!  If they like Mimosas, they will LOVE it! Also, ask to be seated in JULIE'S section! She definitely has the personality and the beer knowledge for the job! 

The bacon wrapped jalapeños are HOT! There are some seeds left inside so be prepared to breath fire like a dragon afterwards. They are tasty but HOT! The chips and queso are a solid choice. Very creamy and flavorful. You can't go wrong with those!
Food and service were both great! Beer was cheap and location was unique. Definitely stop by if in the area.

Dear Tippler, thanks again for a magical evening. Our group of 14 was seated promptly for our reservation, and it was uphill from there! We started by ordering drinks and a few appetizers for the table. The folks on our end chose the hummus and chicken biscuits. The bean mash was served with some gourmet leathery pita for dipping. We rationed the nickel-sized chicken biscuits between a few of us. Served in an iron skillet, and on iron biscuits, these $10 morsels truly made a impact. Dinner was uneventful, and as our plates were whisked away, we were informed that our table was so nice that they had booked it for another group! We were asked to wrap up and move. After paying a well-earned service charge on each of our bills, we were allowed to stay in the restaurant.

The maître d did offer us a nice spot upstairs, and we moved on with our evening. The area we were moved to even had its own TV! The TV was not on of course, and when we asked to turn it on we were told there was not a remote. Being a former Boy Scout, I decided to turn it on using the power button. A waiter was then kind enough to come by and turn it off for us a few minutes later, saying that they did not want it on. My mistake! As the night wore on, we began to enjoy some of the well-priced beverages. In fact, complimentary bottles of champagne and fine glass flutes were brought to our table! We just were not aware it wasn't for us. Told that the owner was coming in and wanted our table, we were asked to move along again. But not before we were allowed to pay another service charge! This time our host recommended a nice spot for us out front, right next to the valet. As we left and were "you're welcomed" by the the hostesses, we knew this was an experience we would never forget. Thanks again Tippler, to show our appreciation our group of 14 will do our best to make sure your restaurant tables aren't in such demand in the future.

What a unique record store for vinyl junkies! Lots of fun stuff to browse and one of a kind vintage "toys" including the automatic recording booth! Worth the $20 to record a little something silly or sentimental. I travel for work and I was missing my cats...and my husband haha so I recorded my wedding vows and I can't wait to give it to him for our 3 yr anniversary! 
There was an amazing clearance sale when I went in and I got a $100-150 Verameat necklace for...FIVE DOLLARS!

I thought Ms Kelli's was pretty cool for what it was- a karaoke dive bar. I like that it's dark, kinda grimy, and not pretentious at all. My group of four had no problem finding a table on a late Saturday night. However, a member of the group had to bus and clean the table before we could settle in. There appeared to be a pretty mixed crowd. Tourists, regulars, random (awesome) folks out for a good time (us), and a few strange ducks. Overall the vibe was nice but you have to scream in order to speak to people. Beer was cheap but the Jello shots weren't very strong, IMO. I didn't get to sing and I realize now after reading other reviews it's probably because I didn't tip the KJ. I think that's kind of shitty, but whatever. I feel like I'll be back again....

I was there on a Friday afternoon before karaoke.  We planned to have lunch and one drink and ended up staying for 3 hours. Travis Bishop and Wesley Cash played acoustic guitars. ...outstanding original music! Rhonda,  our bartender was friendly,  professional and made it all the more fun!

Not my favorite experience and I was really looking forward to coming here. I ordered the catfish creole which wasn't too bad at all but for the price, eh.. Can def tell it was previously frozen and not fresh. The place wasn't busy at all for a Saturday but that didn't bother me, there was a pretty good band playing. However my experience with the waitress was less than ideal. Not sure what her name was but she had long hair with the side buzz cut. One of my friends chair was broken and it took her forever to replace it. I ordered a drink and it wasn't very good, so I asked to replace it and she was ok about that, however I was water vaping and it creates a small amount of mist and she came over and told me I cldnt smoke it, so I turned it completely off yet I still put my mouth to it to get the taste. It was off, no light, no smoke, Nada yet she came over to me and said "I see your will using it and if I have to tell you again" (this was a bad idea on her part) my friend cut her off immediately and said, it's off, what do you mean? There is no smoke or anything. How someone going to tell me what I can or can't put to my own mouth!? I was less than pleased to be talked to like a petulant child, "if I have to tell you again", seriously? Her approach was aggressive and abrasive and I wasn't a fan.  It was B.B. king and we were not roughy nor loud nor rude. So why I have to get treated like I was about to be thrown out!? Lol Why because my friends chair was broken and my drink taste nothing like the description?

What a night we had here! Came with my mom and sister for the first time, visiting from California! It was a well run process. We saw the late show, 930. We waited just a bit for the doors to open and for them to clear out the first show but then we took our seats and were happy to find them comfortable and church like! The sound in the theater is second to none! You will not be let down here if you are looking for the soul of country music!
A beautiful spectacle of architecture. Go here when in Nashville. On 10th st. Just a stones throw away from the music. Bring your camera to this old train station.

Pretty cool bar on Broadway. It has multiple floors including a rooftop bar (which I'm starting to learn almost every Nashville bar has one now LOL) with live music playing all over. We stayed for a while to listen to one of the bands on the rooftop play and it was nice and relaxing. They also had huge fans blowing too, which was a huge plus after being out in 90 degree weather all day.

Well, you put your name on the lit and you see there's 15 in front of you, so you wait, watch and sing along with others. However, when you check back after 10-12 songs, you find out you're only 8songs away?  Whatever, we'll wait it out. Then another 5 go by and you inquire again, to be told you're 5 songs away, and get this:  "ask again and you won't sing at all". After we dropped $200 bucks in here, I left a poultry tip for the wait staff and suggested they get the rest from the rude kaoroke person and we left. I'm sure there are other places that know math, and understand customer service better than this place.

Good karaoke bar, but get there early (like...5pm) if you expect to sing within a reasonable time. By 9pm it's at least a 2 hour wait to sing. Bar tenders are rude and inattentive, and beer is over priced. 

If you're bored and have time/money head to this bar, otherwise skip the karaoke and visit something else.

As an MOU member with plates in Memphis, Cordova, Little Rock, and Nashville, it is with a heavy heart I give this location 1 star. The Mojo wings were the absolute worst I've ever had, arguably the worst wing I've ever tasted. I order extra crispy and got extra soggy.  I order a Lava Lamp (which is basically a black & tan) and they substituted the Harp with a Cider! WTF? Must have been amateur day! So disappointing as I am 40 away from my 10th plate and no this is not even close to the standard.
Aside from being in the Nosebleed seats we had a good time. Really overpriced concessions though 5 dollars for a water and no drinking fountains anywhere . Music was good

Dined last night (12/18) with a group of friends while enjoying heir $3 pint night! Although we had a great time, the servers were very rude. My friend mistaken another waitress for ours and she replied with "I am not your server and you should know that," while rolling her eyes and walking off. That is terrible customer service if you ask me. So beware of the server with brunette braided pigtails and glasses!

Backstage tour was really cool. Judy led the tour and was enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the Opry. We saw Minnie Pearl's fountain donated by her estate. Dressing rooms for regulars and new inductees. Each room has a theme. There are two walls of plaques for the inductees. I think it's 266. Tour included look through backstage to auditorium and inside auditorium as well. Approximately 45 minutes but got a lot of history.  Made us also enthusiastic to visit Ryman's as well.

This place is great for beer-lovers, but also great for those who don't know much about beer.  There is something for everyone! My server was my guide & helped me choose the Raspberry Cream, which was absolutely delicious & perfect for someone like me who usually orders fruity cocktails.  Decor is cozy.  Food is also delicious.
So much fun! We went on the bachelorette Honky Tonk Party bus and we LOVED IT!  Our bride, Katie had so much fun and the guy that checked us in was so wonderful and kind!

I have never had a better beer experience. They clearly have a love for beer and all of the subcategories associated. Their prices are excellent, and the servers were extremely helpful in their recommendations. I had several excellent local beers and imports. We didn't have the food, but we saw several people's orders and by appearance alone it looked amazing. I would definitely return to experiment with more beers. They offer flights and other tastings. They also have fun themed trivia nights.

This was the highlight of our week long trip to Nashville. The two hour show was fast paced and the entertainment was great. There are about seven groups that perform three songs each. When Larry Gatlin and Bill Anderson did their shows, you could tell they were the consummate professionals. They engaged the audience, told stories, and jokes in between their songs. The whole place was fun. However, we did not take the back-stage tour.

I stopped in here with some friends for a drink in the midafternoon, mainly to take advantage of their large patio section. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay on the patio, lazily drinking our beers and whiskeys while smoking stogies. Our waiter did a great job checking on us and keeping us in drink. None of us got any food, but the menu looked good with lots of the normal bar offerings and many of the usual Irish pub type items as well. They also had a good selection of whiskeys (as they should), which we wholeheartedly took advantage of. One thing that was odd was that my whiskey was served in a plastic cup. I'm not sure if that was just because we were seated on the patio, but it was a little strange. Other than that, we had a great experience here and would certainly recommend it.
Best place to watch a game, especially hockey games, especially when Shelby is working!!!
The music was great and the atmosphere was ok but I was not impressed with my BBQ/pulled pork sandwich. I have had much better.

A 4,400 seat AM radio studio ("...WSM the legend..." you'll hear over and over again) and money-printing machine with a dozen or more plugs for sponsor Humana during the show. Shares parking with a popular outlet mall and access is tight/entrance roads can back up on to highway exits. Tix are pricey and sell out well in advance when current or legendary artists are scheduled to appear. Plenty of secondary market tix available if you're willing to pay. Long-time country radio broadcaster Eddie Stubbs moderates the live radio broadcast of the show, which starts on-time regardless of the thousand or more people not yet seated/caught-up in the Opry's inefficient crowd handling scrum (security, concessions, narrow, congested public spaces/hallways). If the artist you must want to see its first on the bill, you could well still be in a line/mob when they take the stage, and most artists get two or three songs at most. All of that said, it's interesting to watch a live radio broadcast happen, artists and crew moving on and off the stage, etc. A must-do for many who visit Nashville, and country music fans may well forgive all of the foregoing snafus.

Stopped in for some live music and A drink. Out-of-towner, so I can't speak for its authenticity of the joint, but we digged it. 

Didn't have food, but the bartender was extremely friendly and patient. The band playing was enthusiastic and were having a good time which you could tell was reflecting onto the crowd. People were dancing. Atmosphere was on point.

Ended up staying for a couple hours, so anytime I come back to Nashville, I'll try to stop in! Oh, and we got took home a souvenir pint glass for I think only $8.

We went there on a Friday night at 7:30 for a friends birthday and the place was pretty empty. I was disappointed with the beer list that contained no dark beers ( I really like stouts and porters, and for a "taps" place they don't have a great selection).

The people I was with ordered the stuff burgers. I'm not a fan of the meat-inside-meat trend, mostly because the burgers come out way overcooked. I found them too dry for my taste, but the truffle fries were good.

The biggest problem was with my order of shrimp tacos. When I ordered it the waiter warned me it wasn't a lot of food, but I figured for $9 it would be more than enough. What I got was two really sad tacos. They were stuffed with shrimp, canned diced tomatoes and cheese. NOTHING ELSE. No avocado, no lettuce- nothing fresh. I was so utterly disappointed. It was something that I could make myself out of refrigerator leftovers for $1.50.  For $9 I'll go to Mas Tacos and get 3 of the best tacos of my life.

I wanted to write a long diatribe about the commercialization of country music and the way the Opry has been turned into a gigantic strip mall and has lost itself the way Time Square has, but I can't. While I'm not a country fan, I had an awesome evening at the Grand Ole Opry.  My wife - a huge country devotee - had spoken of wanting to visit Nashville and more importantly the Opry since we met and our fifth wedding anniversary presented the perfect opportunity.

Our show consisted of about six or seven acts, and culminated with Lady Antebellum  (the only act I knew) performing for about 30 minutes.  

All in all, the music was great, the atmosphere was fun and the night was a complete and inexpensive hit.  Whether you enjoy country music or not, you'll certainly appreciate all the musicians presented. I highly recommend visiting the Grand Ole Opry.

Really cool to come to this historic place and see country music stars and legends perform. My complaints are that we had to stand outside in the rain because they would not open the doors early and that there were so many commercial breaks.

Great place! Trent took excellent care of us and the food and beer were great!

We had the GFB which is a mild ale from San Diego and it was light and flavorful. 
We also had the pretzel and sausage appetizer which came with sauerkraut and it was excellent! The pretzels were warm and super soft and had a nacho cheese sauce to dip them in. It was all nummy!

I'll definitely visit this place every time I'm in Nashville!

Incredible place to make a part of your trip to Nashville. My boyfriend and I went through a tour and saw a night show. It was amazing to stand in the circle that used to be a part of the Ryman. Gave me chills. I really liked how we got several tour guides. It made the tour smooth and enjoyable. 

The show was incredible. We saw artists from different generations and it just makes country music so much more special. Venue was so hospitible and clean and just pure country.

The prices are really good and the serving size is generous. I got the catfish poboy and it was so freakin hot it seared my tastebuds. Let it cool chef!  The flavor was ok and the hilushpuppies were really good, though a bit raw in the middle.
Getting into the Ryman is a disorganized mess.  Too many people and zero staff.  Once inside and seated the show is amazing.

This was hands down the worst service I have ever experienced in my life.  First, we arrived at 530 PM and the hostess laughed at me when I requested to be near the band.  She sat us off to the side of the stage saying all the tables were reserved even though there were many tables where one could actually see the band.  I walked back up front and pleaded my case again as not all the tables in front of the band had reserved placards the hostess says they were reserved and told me no to a move to another table. While we stayed over an hour and a half only half the tables were ever occupied.  Go figure...

Decide to just move and sit at the bar since it was only half occupied.  Waited 10 minutes, finally snagging the bartender, I ordered drinks. Another 10 minutes, drinks arrive.  After 30 minutes ordered a second round of drinks and appetizers. Finally get the drinks after 15 mins, which was okay I guess since the bartender was having fun socializing with people at the other end of the bar instead of doing her job.  During this wait we discussed with the sound man why the volume was so low from the band and he said to keep the noise down during dinner!  At BB Kings BLUES CLUB??  REALLY???  I guess it's beyond reality to go to a Blues Club expecting good loud entertainment and NOT a QUIET dinner.

Another 25 minutes goes by and I finally get a chance to ask about the appetizers once the bartender came within earshot. She says "I F'$%^ed up..sorry ...never put the order in"  I would not recommend her language to an irate customer.  She dropped off two more drinks as I canceling the food order and stuffing cash in the glass to pay my bill. I wanted food not more alcohol.   Left at that moment and never going back.  Since I live in downtown Nashville that is a shame since I do enjoy the music but not at that level of cruddy service.

The bartender apologized at the end of my ordeal. She should ..it was her fault, she single handily ruined this venue's reputation with me and my friends.  It should not take over an hour and half to get people seated and fed on a Sunday night. 

DO NOT COME TO EAT DINNER. The only saving grace was the live band, the HighJivers ...they were fantastic.
Fun thing to do on in Nashville that doesn't involve drinking or need a little more relaxing!
Very disappointing beginning of the show. Almost fell asleep. Picked up second half. Seats are bench pews not too comfie. Just expected more.

Every single time I've come here I've been met with smart ass inept staff that is always to busy or too stupid to answer a simple question.  Bartenders are ass holes the waitresses are bitches.  I literally can not stand this place. I'll never come back.  I don't know why I ever did.

Wow and Wow again. This place is a institution and should if not already on some sort of heritage list. 
Got to go there on the 9th to see the Oak Ridge Boys and we were super impressed with the Grand Ole Opry. Organization, gift shop , staff, cleanliness, sound, etc etc etc. A true 5 stars

Can't believe some of the cry babies on this website, F.....g Democrats.

We went to 4 different Karaoke bars in Nashville and the majority of the people who sang at this one actually had some talent and were entertaining. At the other places people just yelled into the microphones and couldn't sing. This was a fun place to go to even though it wasn't crowded the few times we went.

I have been waiting for the "rooftop" bar to open for a few months and was disappointed when it turned out to only be open on one side with garage doors but that's not even the worst part. Finally made it over there to try it out and they are charging TEN DOLLARS to go up to the "premier lounge" at 2 pm on a Saturday..... the downstairs bar wasn't that busy so I can only assume the upstairs "lounge" was COMPLETELY empty. 10 dollars is insane and a terrible business decision and after reading the reviews from the World Series games I can see it is just a pattern with the managers/owners. My experience turned me off and will not be going back or recommending to friends.

Nice music, great did. This is my fist visit here and I had a blast. The house band made my day by playing their rendition of Purple Rain. I ate the dry rubbed wings, and bbq salmon. The salmon was very fresh. I would recommend this place to any newcomers.

Probably a great local spot. Has all the proper trappings to be as such. But to find out, I guess one would need learn what the secret handshake is. Hey can not blame wanting to keep club closed. Neighborhood bars vanishing... but then again so are neighbors

So, I am not usually a fan of karaoke bars. But this place is nice, clean, big, and has ridiculously reasonably priced drinks. It almost seems like a dive bar, so I was a little worried about the bathroom. Totally impressed! Beautiful and sparkling clean bathroom. I feel like that's a weird thing to write in a yelp review, but I was not expecting that at all. Not really a food place, but great prices on the drinks.

We came here late Sat afternoon for some drinks with friends. It was our first visit. We had a great time. Such a relaxing and laid back place. Great drink options. Soooo many beer selections. Fair prices. The Tennessee Tea was delicious. We didn't try food but the menu looked pretty delicious too.

Unbelievable night at the Opry! We went last night and were blown away. There were performances from people who have been around forever and from newbies to the country music scene but the best part was the last act, Eric Church. He was scheduled for a 30 minute acoustic set but did an hour. He was personable and interacted a lot with the audience. He still seemed to be in awe of performing in that circle. It was a great night! Get there early so you can see the video of Carrie Underwood telling the history of the Opry.
Just toured around the outside, as the inside was closed.  Fun photos opts, right next to a GIANT mall.  Great stop, because come on, you have to at least see it!

Loved this bar!!! Super long wait to sing, but obviously!! There are so many people who want to sing! The crowd was great, the bartenders were really fun, and the karaoke guy was really nice and tried to be as accommodating as he could be! Can't wait to come back!

I hate to do this but I must say that the parking situation here makes me lower my rating.  What a pain!  Once you get that under control this is a pretty cool place.  The building itself is actually neat.  The decor was cool with the flying saucers on the walls and the service was helpful and on top of everything.  I could not ask for more from their beer selection.  Between their huge draft list and the large bottle selection you are guaranteed to find something you like and to find some things you have never had.  Being from out of town we really enjoyed getting to try local beers and were happy to see so many to choose from.

Get tickets early. We bought them at the last minute and ended up 3 rows from the back. Great theater, and you don't need to like country (or western) music to enjoy a show. Don't expect any Zeppelin covers, though. :(

I love this place! I visited on a Saturday night and was able to listen to an amazing band with a lead vocalist that was off the charts. I hate I didn't catch their name. 

Unfortunately, the wait to sit a table of two was over an hour so if you're hungry I wouldn't come here last minute. 

Luckily for us a spot at the bar opened up. Our bartender/server was exceptional! He made me a virgin drink that looked like the real thing and it was delicious! Also the Yazoo Creole plate was very good too. They didn't have many dressings for the salad so that was a bummer and the gumbo was pretty much vegetarian and not what we were expecting. 

Outside of that, it's a cool spot and I'm glad I was able to experience it.

It's Matty C coming to you live with yet another 5-star Friday.

Bear with me, Third Man Records holds a very special place in my heart. Jack White has essentially fronted the entire vinyl revival of the past decade. His bands White Stripes, Raconteurs, Dead Weather, and his existing solo project have deeply impacted my personal life. 

I've been wanting to visit Third Man Records when I began collecting vinyl in 2011. It's a hobby that I've invested countless hours into, as well as tons of cash, but that's neither here nor there. This past April, his Rolling Record Store stopped in Jacksonville (think food truck but for records) and since Nashville was on our list of cities to visit this year, you know I had to make a pitstop at the infamous shop.

I could go on endlessly, but many reviews have covered the bases. In my opinion, the shop is an homage to those who love music, history, equipment, memorabilia, and of course, the art of listening to records.

By far, the coolest aspect of Third Man is the listening booth, which is filled with rarities, B-sides, 7"s, and LP's waiting to be listened in its proper form. I could've stayed in there for hours. Rather I could've spent an entire day in the shop, listening, gazing, wandering and spending my life savings away.

Quite possibility one of the quirkiest record shops I've ever stepped inside of, yet one of the greatest out there. They also house live shows and performances, as well as the record plant that presses vinyl and records artists across all genres. This is the end of my love letter, and I hope our paths cross again.

Watched a hockey game here with friends for some brews and food. I got a chicken sandwich, which was made really well (try their housemade spicy BBQ sauce). The French fries are to die for! My friend got the burger and wasn't that impressed with it. All in all, cheap beer and a good atmosphere to watch a sporting event.

We saw rascal flatts, Chris Jansen as well as some other acts here. There really is no bad seat in the opry. It's a must see experience, the backstage tour was sold out so if you'd like to do that book way in advance. Also easy to park.

Had to say I did it! Would loved to have been  able to see the old venue, New complex is very large, I was with a group and we had wonderful seats.

Entertainment was very good, I like the idea you got to see lots of different entertainers for short periods of time. 

We got to see new acts as well as the old timers! Lots of fun.

Backstage tour was really nice. I enjoyed the history, and the new film they show at the beginning.
If we go again, I'd stay for a show as well. After the tour, I was definitely in the mood to see more.
NOTE: They take a professional photo for you on the stage. You can view it in the gift shop. We got distracted in the gift shop and forgot to check the photo. :)
Another thing to mention, as we were driving there, following our GPS, it looks kinda odd as you drive into the area where the G.O.O. is located. It's located in the middle of a warehouse-looking area with a big mall across the street. Not what I expected, and at first we thought maybe we were in the wrong place. Didn't expect a historical venue like that to be right by a big mall, but I guess that's commercialism. ;)

Go here for the music experience. The live band and music were good. I enjoyed the performance over dinner. The food was just okay. It's just Your typical bar food. I'd recommend sticking to the basics here like chicken wings and burgers. The items outside of that were not good. The drinks were terrible. The mixers they used taste like cough syrup. Once again I'd recommend sticking to the basic mixed well drinks. I do have to give credit to the white chocolate bread pudding. The breaded part was a little stiff but The flavor was so good. Overall I'd go back here but more so for the musical/ downtown Nashville experience. I wouldn't go here looking for amazing food.

Wait and hour and a half for food, manager did shit, didn't even check on us again after first complaint.  Pretty sure they forgot to place our order... 3 hours total and sub par food and dreadful service

Absolutely loved this place.  We went night after night on our trip to Nashville to hear the music played by their house bands and performers.   The food was really good too.  I had the pulled pork bbq sandwich and it was on par with one I had at one of Nashville's famous bbq joints.  Servers and bartenders were friendly and had good recommendations for things to do in town.  I am already missing this place and wish we had one in Philly
Great bar food at a great price! The staff and owners are always on point. We typically do lunches and happy hour things here and they are very accommodating.
Great show. Saw Cassadee Pope and Charlie Daniels, as well as others I can't recall. Three songs per set for five artists. My first indoor concert in years. I prefer outdoor/festivals.

After some careful research and recommendations we chose the Music City Tippler for our dinner while visiting Nashville for the weekend with friends.

What a mistake.

The menu was entirely different than what was posted on the web site and by different I don't mean a change of seasons or an update. I mean they were serving the late night menu of light apps and sandwiches for dinner service. We were the only people sitting for dinner at 7pm on Saturday night. It was almost surreal, we were wondering if they lost the kitchen staff the night before? or maybe earlier in the day?

Our open faced salmon sandwich was served on a hamburger bun. Not a nice restaurant prepared bun but a real grocery store white bread generic hamburger bun.

The entire time we were having dinner, someone was running a lemon press or some sort of grinder/slicer over in the corner of the dinning room. Not sure why? we were the only people there.

maybe the chef had the flu?

Stay away.
Great club with great music!!! It's a family friendly restaurant with wonderful staff, specially Jean-Paul Mendes (Director of Operations) who made us feel very welcome.

Loud, crazy, lively, fun and great entertainment - basically exactly what you would expect on Nashville's main strip!  Noah Garner was the best entertainment of the night and maintained his level of energy the whole time! He kept the crowd engaged the whole time.

I have to say - I cracked a joke with the bouncers and they almost didn't let me in. But they did their jobs and the one bouncer explained why my joke was bad timing. Kudos to them for caring enough to be tough.

This is pretty much one of my favorite places to go in Nashville. Beer selection. That's what it's all about. With a beer menu of over 200 selections it is hard to be disappointed they don't have some beer that you like and provides ample opportunity to try something new. They encourage this through the UFO club. Awesome concept BTW. 

You get a membership and they keep track of the number of different beers you've tried. Get to 200 and they will immortalize your name on a plate that goes on the wall.

The beer is priced well, easily get a craft pint for $4, and as keep as $3 if you come on pint night.

The food is great as well. No it's not take your sweetheart for valentines day impressive but for price, quality and deliciousness, it is hard to beat. Service is usually top notch, though I will admit they do have a waitress or two on occasion that moves a little slower than the rest of the heard. Beer knowledge though always seems to be spot on.

Great place for lunch, I don't typically go Friday or Saturday nights cause it's usually packed. I stick to Sunday through Thursday.

Love the couches is you are looking for a place to sit back.
Good food. Great music - love that Grant Garland Trio on Tuesday nights! Check it out!!

Grand Ole Opry is the most well known music venue of Nashville. 

Located about 15 miles away from the downtown Nashville area.

I thought it was located in the most random place. In the parking lot of the outlet. Pretty weird. I am sure they built the outlet around the venue. I felt like that took away from how epic the venue is supposed to be.

Parking is shared with the outlet. The front entrance area is cool. I liked the huge guitars. 

The venue itself reminded me of a huge church. Cool place to visit even if you do not watch a show or do the tour.

Nice atmosphere! Nice and just right for dancing freely and listening to great jazz. The wait was about an hour but we paid the cover charge of $5 and got to stand around and still listen to music while we waited on our table. One we got our table, we were right in the front. The food was great! Now my Gumbo Yaya had to be sent back the first time. All the rice in it was raw! It was inedible. The loaded Pull Pork Tater Tots were great! It's a huge portion and maybe 4-5 ppl can eat out of. When i got my replacement gumbo, it was great!! The BB King Allstar Band was great! They interacted with he crowd and gave greeeaat music to dance to! BB King was open to kids after 8 PM! There were kids there this night and they were on the floor dancing! Like i said, it was a great experience overall!

Eh, if you've been in this area, you've seen it all. It was mainly filled with college students and boys on the prowl. I didn't go for the food, I met my husband there for a drink. My drinks were strong and that's always a plus for me. The DJ was just ok but he was cool with us because he took all our requests. We actually told him what set to play lol Anyway, I'm sure I'll end up here again but it's not first on the list.
Great experience. They have it figured out. You see a mix of legends and up and coming stars. The sound is great. Easy parking, fair prices and a great time. This is must when in Nashville.
I really enjoyed this spot. It's ideal for groups of people to grab some great bar food and an EXCELLENT selection of beers. Servers were nice, and I ended up leaving a full and happy man.

We arrived here for dinner on a Friday night. We had to pay a $10 cover charge because the band was playing (even though we were eating dinner)! 

I had the brisket sandwich. It was okay. Nothing exceptional about the food. I was with a large party and paying for myself (my bill was approximately $50 - including cover charge). This was pricey for 1 person. 

The band was awesome & entertaining! 

The drink "love on the delta" was good.

BAD = NOT GOOD... IS AN APPROPRIATE NAME FOR THIS DINER

The food is nothing to write home about.  They need to get a better bread supplier because the buns they used for the burger and pulled pork sandwich had a weird texture.  We had an extremely RUDE WAITRESS who was impatient and didn't want to serve us.  I made the mistake of changing my order when she was writing down my order (mainly because I can't have lactose products) and the look she shot me was chilling.....so make sure you know exactly what you want when you are ordering .  After I told her I was lactose intolerant and wanted to know what entrees did not have milk or cream in it, she shot me a look....If looks could kill I'd be dead now.  With such a chilly waitress we didn't want to stay a minute longer so we ate quickly and left as soon as we could.

My recommendation is to find another restaurant that serves good food and has a friendly wait staff.  We had high expectations from the reviews but were very disappointed with our experience at the B.A.D.

Today we had the pleasure of traveling to the Grand Ole Opry House to see their amazing venue. The building itself is a piece of history and the grounds around it were gorgeous! The staff here was extremely pleasant and it was nice to look through their gift shop. We hope that the next time we come here I tis to actually see a show!

So many friends had raved about the Tippler, and I was really looking forward to trying it now that the grand opening crowds have subsided. I went last night (just for drinks--no food), but unfortunately, I can't give the Tippler more than 3 stars. 

I'll lead off by acknowledging that I'm a drink snob. If I'm going to pay a premium price for a cocktail, I expect it to have premium ingredients, premium preparation, and premium taste--and my standards are somewhat exacting. The menu told me that the Tippler would do reasonably well on the first criterion, with most of the core spirits of the $20-$30 per bottle variety you wouldn't be ashamed to put in your own liquor cabinet. Unfortunately, when it came to preparation and taste, I was underwhelmed.

I tried two drinks--their variation on the Mule, and the Black Manhattan. Both were decent, but nothing to write home about. With fancy drinks, I enjoy savoring the complexity of flavors, particularly if they change over time. Unfortunately, both of these drinks just tasted flat and no better than something I'd concoct at home.

On the plus side, the bartenders were friendly and attentive. On the minus side, despite it being a Wednesday night, the bar area was crawling with young people acting young. (UGH, I sound like an old man.) My issue with it was that it took away from the ambience; you have a place with a posh interior and fancy drinks, and a bunch of folks acting like they're at the Tin Roof. Oh, and the bar only has back-less stools, so after a while my back got sore. (Yes, now I REALLY sound like an old man.) Anyway, in fairness, I know they have other rooms, so I probably should have just gravitated that direction.

I ended up going to Patterson House after I left, and I was night-and-day more satisfied--and for about the same price, too. Between the selection, the ambience, and the flavor profiles, Patterson House flat-out wins. Like I said, I really wanted to love the Tippler, but at the end of the day it was just okay.

Awesome beer and ale selection.


Awful food.


Just awful.
Plus, we sat at a table for around 20 min while the waitress served people who came in and sat down ten min after we did.

She said she didnt know who had our table, but that she'd be our waitress.

The egg on the jalapeno tots was undercooked to the point of having clear whites.
Not much jalapeno either.

The pretzels were great, as was the beer.

I HEART The Tippler. 

YES. 

I. 

DO. 

Having experienced the The Tippler (http://www.yelp.com/biz/the-tippler-new-york) in Chelsea which happens to be one of my fave neighborhoods in NYC, I was elated to hear that their second location was going to be in our fair city. And, this is a shoutout to all of my New York homies who guffawed and snorted 5 years ago when I announced that I'd be movin' down South instead of back to "The City..." How do you like me now my friends? YES. My "home" Nashville is the shit.

Ooopsie, sorry about that tangent... it was the whiskey talking. 

Back to the Music City Tippler! 

I was lucky enough to attend a "Friends & Family soft opening" a few weeks before the official opening and was wowed by the complete transformation of the space located on the ground floor of The Adelicia. I really appreciate how they carved out different nooks throughout that would appeal to the different energy from their patrons. You may find a casual crowd relaxing on the patio or playing shuffle board in the loft area or if you want to "seen in the scene," pony on up to the gorgeous main bar frames the entire space and is certainly the epicenter of all activity.
 
If that doesn't tickle your fancy, may I suggest strutting your stuff down the stairs to a more intimate bar area to enjoy a more chill vibe along with the option of some live entertainment on the small stage area. This happened to also be the location where GQ & Bombay Sapphire recently hosted "The Most Imaginative Bartender Competition" recently. I don't know who I paid off in a previous life but your girl here hosted the event and it was literally one of the most fun experiences I have had the pleasure of having in a long time! The entire Tippler team were super professional and oh, so, accommodating. 

Throw in a a myriad of crafty cocktails, brews, wines, and a more extensive menu than what their East Coast locale offers (I do enjoy rubbing that it, don't I?)... and you have the makings of a stellar establishment that will make our city proud. From swanky ladies in cocktail dresses to a rugged fella in a rock and roll tee shirt, you can find anyone who appreciates their version of the good life here. From the grand entrance that leads to a modern vintage-y lounge area to the kitschy little photobooth tucked away upstairs, The Tippler boasts much depth in their character. 

And, as someone who hosts, produces, and sponsors events, it is refreshing to not only have a fabulous time hanging out with my friends at this spot but to also be able to  genuinely say that I have enjoyed working with their team as well? Now, that is something to cheers to!  

TIP: Order their Moscow Mule. Just. Do. It. 

TIP2: Street parking is available but valet is the way to go!
Must see for all country music fans. Love the gift shop, souvenir is a must after the show! I'm sure everyone has this at the top of their list to see!

Sadly we came on a Sunday afternoon and there were no tours or shows happening. We did however, get to walk around and see something so large and famous. We took a bunch of photos out front near the huge guitars and looked in the windows of the performance hall. We then went to the gift shop and bought souvenirs like a couple of tourists. Despite not tour and not being to see the whole thing, we had a lot of fun! I would recommend anyone come if you haven't seen it and want to experience something so historical and cool. Even just the few things we did while we were there made it a good time.
Word of note, however. We wanted to go to the resort next door and look inside the hotel and maybe eat lunch. When we drove to that side of the property, the self parking was $20! We didn't want to spend that much on parking just to be able to go inside and look around. They had no other parking options available so we gave up and left instead.

This place deserves negative stars. Last year I went there on Halloween and I was assaulted by the manager there, and then was forcefully removed by the bouncers AFTER they witnessed him shoving me against the bar for "standing in his way" in a wall to wall packed bar & further threatening my life. After filing legal action- I decided to give the place another shot a year later, and they proved that management is still terrible. They would not let my Browns fan boyfriend upstairs to watch the games with me because he was in a Browns jersey therefore he could only watch the Browns game and no other NFL games (a change from previous years we had gone here). The bouncer would not even give us the courtesy of an answer when we asked for compromise, instead he just stared at us shaking his head. Overall this place deserves to be shut down and further investigated for assault against its customers.
very great experience. was fun and something everyone should experience. The staff was very friendly and the blinds in the bathroom moved pretty fast
The pretzels are worth trying. I am not normally a pretzel kind of gal but they are light and flavorful. Perfect with my beer.

At first I was skeptical of the place before I got in, but I was glad my friends suggested this place. Loved the atmosphere in there. They have daily specials and Saturdays they have live music but not sure when it starts. 

I had the buffalo chicken wrap with with fries and it was great! The fries were delicious! Our waiter was friendly and attentive even with the place being completely packed. Portion and price of the food is reasonable too. They don't overprice their food like some Nashville restaurants do.

I must say this was a great spot to visit on my vacation to Nashville there are so many other places to choose from but i'm so glad i came here, live music, excellent food, two bars, oh what a wonderful time. Great dessert selection, bread using my absolute favorite. Great art work. This spot is a must!

possibly the best brisket i've ever had. the server was attentive and knowledgable, the food was incredible.  $5 cover was for our party, not per individual, i dig that policy, and it was worth it because the musical talent was en fuego.

I don't like writing negative reviews, but my experience at Belcourt Taps left me little choice. My wife and I went there on a Groupon for two beer flights and an appetizer. We experienced the following issues:

1) The waitress was unaware the restaurant was doing a Groupon and didn't seem sure how to do the beer flights. As a result...

2) Our beer flights were 10 random beers (well, 9 beers and a cider) without any labels or information as to what they were. Rather than two sets of five beers, it seemed like they told the bartender to just pour 10 arbitrary brews and scatter them throughout the tray. If the word "taps" is in your restaurant's name, you should probably know your way around a keg.

3) The nachos were so low-quality that if I had made them myself, I would have been disappointed with my handiwork. The queso was goopy, lukewarm and clearly store-bought and the toppings were only on one side.

4) Maybe this wasn't their fault, but the band they hired to perform was quite bad. Picture Dolly Parton getting her wig plucked to the tune of a stale guitar and you've just about got it.

Restaurants who offer Groupons are like attractive thirty-somethings on Tinder. If they have to put themselves on that particular medium, they probably don't have their crap together.

Lesson learned.

I'm a HUGE B.B. King and blues fan, so when the wife and I were walking around downtown Nashville, we came across B.B. King's Blues Club, and I had to stop in. Unfortunately, we had just eaten lunch, so I was in no shape to try their food, however we did hang out at the bar for a few drinks.
Very casual, laid-back, and chill place. It has a very old school 1930's vibe to it, and I really wish we had stopped in for some live blues music. It was dead when we came in around 2 pm, but I bet this place gets rocking. 
Bartender was very friendly and was enjoyable. She informed us they had a 2 for 1 deal going on domestic drafts, wines, and certain mixers- so the wife decided on a glass of wine. I noticed they had Samuel Adams Octoberfest on draft, and I don't care if it was 10 for 1 domestic drafts, I'm going Sam Adams every time. The draft beer selection was actually pretty impressive, and they had a nice wine selection as well.
So we just relaxed at the bar for a bit, enjoyed our drinks, and made some conversations with the bartender and enjoyed the blues music being pumped through the speakers. Some Stevie Ray Vaughn kicked on, and I just closed my eyes, sipped my beer, and imagined he was on stage in front of me right then and there. 
This was a fun little stop. We didn't order any food, but the menu did look pretty good, and the food I saw come out of the kitchen looked (and smelled) great! I can't give a five star review, as I really want to come back and experience the food and some live music, but until then I recommend stopping in for a drink while you're walking around. Had a great time here, and the next time I'm in Nashville I will be back in to get the full experience.

Bartenders are the best!! Great spot to watch sports, and have a great time. Being a local here in Nashville it's definitely the first bar I'll go to to start my night. And it always has to be my last spot before I go home. Great food and a fantastic atmosphere. Can't go wrong with this place at all.
So many beers! Went here during happy hour for a Friday. We sat at one of the long tables and made friends with the people next to us and the waitress.

Off-Broadway, "locals-only" kinda place in the Arcade Alley! Everything on the menu is tasty & fast. I love the hummus, veggie burger, soups, chips, burgers, wings ($0.50 Saturday's & $2 PBR!!), chicken wrap, & the fries have saved my life a few times. If you play your cards right, they'll let you pick the music or tv channel. It's a Live Music Venue too so come for the writer's night.
great selection. nice appetizers- especially the pretzel...yummmmm

What an experience coming to the Grand Ole Opry and doing a backstage tour. Im new to the country music scene and this was an awesome experience hearing the background of this establishment. The tour was very informative, took you to some awesome areas and you were able to stand on stage and take a picture (with their camera of course) the tour was about an hour or maybe a little less. The shows are on Tuesdays Friday's and Saturdays and I can't wait to come back for one of them.

If you're a music nerd, you'll just get it.

This place is R-A-D rad with a capital R, A and D, *y'all*

Sure, it's a record store (with lots of great, curated records to choose from), but it's also a music lover's playground - a listening booth, dancing hamster machines, an old-timey photobooth, record YOUR OWN VOICE and have it pressed to vinyl... wicked cool stuff here, folks.

Additionally! Accoutrement. Clothings, books, buttons, show posters, Third Man swag... the list goes on.

On the real: If you're an audiophile and you're in Nashville, you should stop by.

I don't know where to begin with how crappy this bar is but I doubt it matters because it will likely close before too long. The staff here is a joke. The "door guy" checked exactly zero ID's throughout the night. At one point he came in and did some shots at the bar while several of us watched a drunk patron puke 3 or 4 times on the floor. He saw this and shrugged. I mentioned it to him later and he laughed and said "gotta watch your step in here." 

There was a busker who came in and started begging patrons for drinks. He even licked up a drink that had spilled on the bar and the bartender giggled at the scene. 

I bought a round for myself and two friends, when I asked to close out and pay for my tab I was given someone else's card and tab. I was polite and mentioned that this wasn't my card, and the bartender went bonkers swearing at me and saying that without a doubt it is the card I gave her. It wasn't. I still had my card and showed her this and that's when she told me to get the f**k out. Okay. At least I got my three Stoli and redbull drinks for free which is cool since they tend to be pricey. Still, I feel like the staff either have some cognizance problems or they are all high. 

The bar has a great location but I'm looking forward to the near future when something decent moves into that space. Until then, hit up Bourbon St, Skull's, or Fleet Street. Ms. Kelli's is as bad as the name alone suggests.

I'm visiting Nashville from California and BB Kings was recommend by several people. 

I will now be one of those people spreading the word about how good their food is. I tried the ribs, both the wet and the dry. I actually preferred the dry ribs. They were full of meet and I left the bone clean! The coleslaw, beans, and corn bread are perfect sides that really seal the deal. 

The only downfall was we had to pay a $5 cover even though we weren't buying any alcohol, so that was another $15 we weren't expecting to spend. 

But overall, great environment and outstanding taste! Highly recommended!!

We wanted some music off of busy broadway so we decided to try out BB Kings blues club.  The wait staff were very friendly and attentive.  The food was very tasty and portions were large.   I got the the pork nachos and they were absolutely amazing!   We listened to the band called "the all stars" and the music was the best we heard in Nashville!   Definitely will be back to BB Kings next time we return to Nashville!!!

It was really cool to be at a historic place that holds so much significance for music. We didn't do a tour, the stage was being put back together from the holiday show. We walked around the grounds which was really well maintained. The store and gift shop has many cool things to look at and purchase. The staff was friendly and greeted us promptly. Enjoyed our short visit here. Next time, I would love to see a show!

It's comfortable, the seating and sound quality where we were was good and the acts were entertaining. I liked that each act did only 2 songs, you don't get bored and even though I don't care for country music, especially all this new Pop Country now, this was a pretty good show, a good mix of new, old and bluegrass. The staff is helpful and friendly so getting to your seat is a breeze. The seats are long pews, cushioned so comfy. If you like this type of music I feel like you'll love this experience, we were staying across the street so our hotel shuttled us *that's the way to do it if you can*. They have a huge gift shop but as with most places like this, music, sporting events etc, take out a small loan on your house before you go. They have food stations and it's all pricey. My 8oz bottle of water was $5.00, made by Pepsico I have to wonder what an actual Pepsi would have cost. Other than that little rant, if you'd ever dreamed of this, do it! It's pretty neat.

We were in Nashville for a mini vacation for our anniversary and we were looking for a bar close by our AirBnB that we could go to for some drinks without getting back in a vehicle after a long drive. Belcourt Taps fit the bill so we decided to check it out. What we found was a pleasant surprise. An intimate environment with a good beer selection, live music, and staff so friendly and welcoming it felt like we were regulars instead of out-of-towners there for the first time. Carolyn behind the bar is awesome! She said she has only worked there a couple of months, but she seemed really invested in making a good atmosphere for the patrons. There was a younger male server whose name I can't remember, but he was also friendly to us helping with beer recommendations and places to visit during our stay. We also loved that this place has live music with people playing original songs instead of covers. It's a laid back environment and couldn't be more different than the chaos that is the honky tonks on lower Broadway. I didn't eat so I can't speak about the food, but the guy next to me got the adult grilled cheese and it looked really good. If you're in the Hillsborough neighborhood don't sleep on this place.

We only stopped in for drinks. The selection is amazing! So many beers on tap! The bartender was helpful with questions. The decor is quirky and entertaining. It's a great spot to meet with friends. My only suggestion would be to add some gluten friendly food items for those of us who can't tolerate gluten but would like a snack. Small issue but just a suggestion. We loved this bar

I did not expect to like this place at all.  I'd hear vaguely of the Grand Ole Opry, but didn't realize it was a real place.  I was completely ignorant of country music, and only went here for my wife's birthday because she is a huge country music fan.  Thus, we visited Nashville.  I was pleasantly surprised both with the city as well as the Grand Ole Opry  

They do a great job of keeping the Opry House in good condition.  The staff in particular was great and clearly enjoyed their jobs.  Food/drinks were much better than expected, including several craft beers available on tap.  The show we saw was diverse in terms of the acts, and genuinely engaging.  The host layed on the 'Grand Ole Opry' dogma a little thick for me, but the music compensated for it.  We stayed for the backstage tour afterwards.  It was extremely cool to hear all of the stories about the place, and also to see the performers heading out; you really tour the exact same space!

Completely understand why this is a must do.  We'll be back!

In the two short days that I was in Nashville I was lucky enough to hit this place twice. Why? Because the bands kick butt. 

The first night we went there it was a female band and one of the ladies was playing a fiddle. Bonus! 

Next night we stopped by it was filled with people from the hockey game and the band was hopin. For such a small place, we were lucky to get a seat both times in that small, cozy quaint bar. 

With all the big country singers having bars and restaurants on Broadway, Rich's was down home playing some good music.
We stopped here for some lunch the food was ok.  They have a stage and theres always someone performing the entertainment was good.  The service was fast.

Omg Anthem is exactly what Nashville needed. The building/decor is beautiful, the people are gorgeous, and the music is loud!!! My friends and I danced all night long and we had a blast. I came back that Thursday to eat at Revelry (the dive bar that is inside of Anthem).Not many people know about it yet but give it a little time and that place will be packed!!! It is open Monday-Saturday starting at 5pm and doesnt close until 3am. It was freakin delicious. I started off with a tequila cocktail called Rise & Revelry and for dinner I had the Cheesesteak sliders. 100% will be back to both!!!

Ate here for lunch. Had pulled pork platter that ranked up with the great establishments in Kansas City. Very impressed with good and service. But thoroughly amazed at the quality of the live music even at 3 in the afternoon. My only complaint, if you view it that way, too many items on the menu to choose from. Guess I will have to make a return trip.

For this country music geek, this was a huge check off my bucket list! This was my first time to Nashville and my first time to the Opry! It was a magical experience!  The pure energy combined with nostalgia made for a great show!  The new building is very nice. I was a little worried that it wouldn't be as special not being in its original location but It didn't matter a bit once I was there! They have a food truck and snack bars available as well as bar. All items you purchase there can be taken into the show. I highly recommend arriving early and purchasing your tickets ahead of time because it gets very crowded!! Also, don't take more than you need in with you. The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because of the seating. It's all bench type seating (like a church pew) and it was uncomfortably crowded. Like, we couldn't put our arms comfortably to our sides crowded. A little awkward especially if you are seated next to a larger person. However, I would definitely go again!

Review is for the Grand Ole Opry Backstage Tour: 

This is a nice tour to indulge in the history of country music. It's a really laid back walking tour led by your tour guide. It's not boring/cheesy and you'll learn a little about the Opry's history and walk the path of the singers who perform there. You'll see videos along the way, hosted by Blake Shelton. And you never know when you may see a celebrity there!  (Hunter Hayes was there when we were touring.)

Parking is free because it's the mall parking lot, which is right next to the Opry. We walked right up for a tour around noon on a Tuesday in July, but be sure to check the website because I believe tours times change based on events going on. You can book ahead online to guarantee a tour.

When i travel I like finding out-of-the-way places brimming with local character; in essence, the anti-chain. B.A.D. nails it.

Wandering around the area in the early afternoon on a hot Saturday, my son and I saw an amateurish sign on the street talking about how BAD the place was. We had to investigate.

The A/C was working well and we sat at the bar. I had a fried catfish dish, my son had a burger. Both were good. The staff was friendly (and quite attractive, I might add), and did not pick on me for being from out of town. Lots of visual stimulation on the walls - signs and other stuff that's fun to look at. After getting fleeced at Opryland, it was nice to get a decent meal at a fair price.

Recommended.
Food was great, service was friendly!  They serve very generous mimosas (for the right price).

This was a gem of a find in downtown Nashville. Delicious food, I had a vegetarian black bean burger, one of the best! Everything was fresh. The full bar, great beers, urban eclectic atmosphere at a very reasonable price made this one I would return to in a minute.

Came here on a tour and thought it was amazing!
