I was reading a previous review about how there was no diversity in the crowd - I was definitely the only Asian in my tour group (a millennial one at that) but I really didn't mind. I love country music and really enjoyed the backstage tour we got to see. Buying tickets online is a bit of a confusing pain, but once you're in, everything is pretty clear and the guide keeps the group together. 

I'd love to come back for a show one day but in the meantime, if you're in the area and can't snag tickets to a show, the tours are pretty worth it if you like country!
Awesome show.  Beautiful place.  Fun places to take pics outside.  The only downside was the $6 bottle of water.

I really wish i had the ability to go home when i come here. Its a shame they arnt open 24/7 cause if they where id just pay rent and sleep on the bar. I love JD their bar manager. He'd prolly even offer me a pillow and some shampoo for a sink shower if they where open 24/7 itd help if I showered naturally as well. Its also really nice to see some diversity downtown in nashville
Great live music, tons of seating, the shrimp po boi and tater tots were fantastic. Everyone in our group loved what they got.

This place is a hidden gem! We read reviews and man we're we satisfied. My husband and I had the Southwest burger and it was amazing, the broccoli cheese soup was to die for, the Cajun chicken sandwich was great too. We are from out of town and will be sure to come back when we return to Nashville!!

I have to say first and foremost I only experience The Tippler from a private yelp party perspective, so I can't really comment on what the place is like under normal circumstances. It was pretty cool inside though, 1920s sort of feeling, dim sexy lighting and ample space. I thought it was a neat place to have a private party, we took over the downstairs room that has a wee stage. The bartender who was in charge of us down there was also extremely upbeat and very obliging. Thank you mr. bartender for putting up with us and pouring some strong drinks. I should have gulped a giant glass of water with my second Golden Yelpy. Anyway I'm not sure I'll find myself back at the Tippler anytime soon because I rarely go out in this area of town but I feel like it's a pretty cool spot for midtown, I'd rather go to Tippler than the Red Door Saloon, let's put it that way.

Hey.... I was in a group of 8 people and we had waited practically 2 hours from the time we put our names on the waiting list to the time we got our food. Two of us got the southern fried platter and we did NOT get the hush puppies we ordered because they "ran out." For people who waited TWO hours to eat , that is not acceptable at all! Furthermore , the catfish tasted like saltwater and their Mac and cheese ( the substitute for our hush puppies) was just pasta with shredded cheese on it .. shredded cheese that this establishment didn't even bother to melt ! Wow . So disappointing . This is shameful. You should charge for the music and definitely not the food . That was 2 hours of my life I will never get back . Don't go here .
Dive bar.  You get little cheap plastic cups and if they get busy they make you go to the bar to get drinks from your table, but of course it's packed and hard to get through.  Not worth the effort.

It's always very hard to rate bars. Especially later at night, when you have a few drinks in. However, I was smart enough to write down that Colt was our bartender upstairs and he was amazing. From what I remember he was very knowledgeable and on key.

Besides being the bartender, he was running around the rooftop while we were playing games to ask us if we needed a refill or a drink. Now that's service!

Finishing off our day in Nashville, we walked into BB's while a very good jazz band was playing.  Got a good view from our table as we sipped on some drinks from the bar.  Nice relaxing atmosphere without hearing the other bars from outside playing nearby.
Nice stop on our tour, best part was Tim at the front! Super nice guy. Nice to hear 4 musicians on stage tonight.

We received very poor service.  Server walked by us 3 times-  we had to go to the bar to place a drink order and ask for food menus.  The bartender asked us where we'd be and said someone would be right over.  We were outside in the nonsmoking area and the server walked by three times again, taking drink and food orders from neighboring tables and completely ignoring us.  We are locals, but won't be back.
This is a very good place to go to listen to music whats cool is there are different singers every night. Fun place especially if youre in to country music.

The high lights are the old rasputin porter, and the jalapeño bacon poppers..
Service was spotty and my appetize,beer and dinner came all the same time..cold food :-(

The pretzel bratwurst. .I didn't like...and I love brats and pretzels. .
So loud you can't think..very dark..not much lights..
This is a place for college kids..misses the mark for us older folks
I had a great experience there. Excellent band, attentive wait staff and fantastic ribs. I'll be back for sure.

I have been here before but the band was just alright so I decided to visit again with associates and the band was amazing with a good vibe it was my sister birthday and we had a blast the band sung happy birthday to her and she was shocked lol... Ok I ordered the catfish and shrimp which was delicious and for my drink can't really say I tried a little of everything but all was good to my satisfaction. Everyone there In our group was very pleased with everything except we were  there at 530pm on Saturday and it was free but waiting on others in our party we ended up walking in at 6pm and had to pay a cover charge which we will know next time lol. It's a great place to visit.

very good burgers. I had the aloha burger and my wife had the turkey burger. Nice cold beers and service very good and friendly. Had the pork quesadilla for appetizer... great prices nothing over $10. As their motto says BAD is GOOD...,We totally agree. check it out.

this is a hidden gem-behind union station hotel-you can get food-yes good food after midnight-fun staff and plates on the ceiling-it really was actually pretty cool-i would tell you to go and i will be back

First time at BB King's Blue's Club, and it was a great experience. It was a Saturday night, and the place looked packed, but they still got us seated right away. Cover charge was $5/person, payable at the front desk before being seated, which was a little odd, but whatever. . . they accepted credit cards for that, so it was no issue. Once seated, our server was great. She was friendly and seemed genuinely happy. Our food came out pretty quickly for how busy it was. I ordered the brisket, which was a little dry. I actually liked it better that way, because it didn't have that fatty consistency it has at other places. I recall it coming with baked beans, green beans, and cornbread, which were also good. The band on stage was really good-- worth the $5 cover charge and then some.

My sister in law and I were out for a walk and discovered this gem.
It was pretty busy for a place well hidden. We ordered the hot chicken wrap. It was HOT but good. The fries were crispy and well seasoned. 
 I am sorry we did not get the Jalapenos but I wont make that mistake on my return trip. It will be very soon. The service was great.The lemon drop martini needed a little help but worth ever penny. Tuesday nights have 5.00 margaritas and martinis!

Here is why I gave the opry 2 stars instead of 5... While the show is always top-notch, the parking situation at this location is HORRIBLE. It's a deal-breaker. You will most likely park in an already crowded mall parking lot (next to Dave and Buster's and a high movie theater with an IMAX...)...  here's the thing, you can probably find a spot. that's not the problem. The bad news is that it takes FOREVER to leave. Shame on the Gaylord company for not hiring event staff to help with parking. We sat for a half hour and never moved. not an inch. finally, the traffic moved enough for me to turn my car around and go the other way (fortunately, I knew of the other exit from that area or we would have been there, stuck in the parking lot for at least an hour, maybe two). If being stuck in a lot is appealing to you, I highly recommend.

This venue had mediocre music that didn't have mass appeal. Don't get me wrong, it looks nice. Unfortunately, that's the extent to which I'll compliment this place. It was apparent as soon as I walked in that most of the 10 people who were there all night knew each other. Maybe it's because I went on a Friday, which is Latin night? For the most part, the place was dead. The very few people who were there had a snooty air about them...the ambiance in general was very pretentious. That sort of environment is maybe ok in Miami or LA, but in Nashville it just doesn't work. 

There was nowhere to sit...not because there weren't available seats, but because if you wanted to sit in a booth, you HAD TO RESERVE IT? WTF IS THAT? SINCE WHEN DO YOU HAVE TO PAY TO SIT DOWN SOMEWHERE? CALL ME CHEAP, BUT I'M NOT WILLING TO DO IT JUST YET. 

12th and Porter across the street is a way better investment.
I'm a beer knurd and home brewer and love the variety. I always get great food and service too!
Do not ever park in that lot, they scam you big time. It takes forever to get out. Park at the mall instead and get out fast and free.
Saw Grand Ole Opry Variety Show with Charley Daniels.  Very good.  Just shy of his 82nd birthday, but you wouldn't know it.  Plays the fiddle like he did when he was young.

If you are looking for a bar in Nashville to listen to some of the best voices you will ever hear, this is the spot. Some of the best bartenders you will meet, they treat you like family from the moment you walk in the door. The staff goes above and beyond for the guests, and if you do have an issue the manager jd is always willing to help. 


Living in a society full of snowflakes its nice to have a bar that doesn't care if they are politically correct or if they offended you with their indoor smoking policy. Dont forget the fact that if you are in the service industry they have wonderful drink specials to thank you for all you do for this industry. 


I will gladly continue to frequent this establishment.

I was visiting from out of town and came here for a sandwich and a beer. While the sandwich, beer and atmosphere were all great, when the bill came, my impression of the place tanked. My bill was $12.28 and my server brought me back $7.00. When I mentioned that I thought she didn't give me the right change, she patted her apron and said "Oh, we don't DO change." You don't "do" change, but you charge people in increments of less than a whole dollar?! So each server is, in effect, stealing from each table?? I was stunned. If she had 20 tables in a night and took .75 extra from each that's an extra $15.00 in her pocket. If you don't want to "do" change as a restaurant policy, then charge your patrons in increments of a dollar - had my bill actually BEEN $13.00, I would have been fine with it and would have tipped at least 20%. As it was, I got out my phone and figured out that $1.84 was exactly 15%, and left her $1.12 to make up for the .72 she stole. If this is a restaurant policy, it's appalling. It left a horrible taste in my mouth, and I've told no less than a dozen people about it. Change your policy, Flying Saucer, and quit stealing from your patrons.

Visited on a Friday evening. Environment and seating was great. We sat on the high rise and our view was great down onto the stage. They picked great upcoming singers, current hit artists, and comedians to perform. I can honestly say I really enjoyed every performer. Will definitely keep returning.

I wanted to like it, I really did.  It has cool stuff in it, and I liked all the vinyl.  We tried to use the photo booth, and that is where things started to go off the rails.  Photo booth took REEEALLY long, and then stopped working. They did refund my money.

  I realize it's a touristy thing, but thought many of the items were at a gouge price level.  I might take a friend from out of town, but I will manage my expectations when I return.

Stopped by BB King's for a late lunch. We ordered our drinks and waited. It was happy hour on appetizers so we ordered The nachos with pork.  The pork was good the rest not so much. Still waiting for that beer. Finally flagged down the waitress. We got an "oh I forgot".   We we ordered ribs and pulled pork sandwiches they were awesome!  That's why my review is middle of the road. There are some great foods and some great servers. We just didn't get everything. Will probably try again. The music is worth the trip if you can get a drink.

It won't let me give it 0 stars! Terrible customer service! I called with a beer question, not only did he refuse to answer, but hung up on me! We're from out of town and WILL NEVER GO HERE!!!! MEAN TERRIBLE SERVICE!!

I cant say how thankful I am to the staff here, I have a sprained foot and a knee scooter and was going to walk down the stairs but the security at the front cal and got a gentlemen to take me around the top part of the bar to the elevator so that I didn't have to walk down or back up the stairs. Very very helpful. I really appreciated the extra effort they gave to make sure I was comfortable.

I want to give this place a bad rating so I can keep this hidden gem to myself, but it absolutely deserves 5 stars! The local live music is the heart of nashville and the bartenders are so friendly and on point! Definitely my go to neighborhood bar

Three of us went into this bar today and we sat there for twenty mins before walking out. We were never served or greeted. It was like we were invisible , the bar tender looked right us and just kept talking to a couple at the bar. We will never go back.

We had planned on going to Bicentennial Mall Park to see the Nashville Symphony perform on a Friday night at 8pm. We looked around for a place to eat & noticed the high rating of this place. Why not try it? We parked between here & the Mall. It wasn't much of a walk & we found B.A.D. (Back Alley Diner) from the small sign on the side walk of Church street. The diner is located in the alleyway east of the Loews Hotel. 

There's an entrance at street level & one up a few steps. The entrance up the steps directs you to use the street entrance. We arrived around 7pm (missing the daily happy hour that is from 4pm-7pm, damn!) and was greeted with a sign that told us to seat ourselves. We had our pick of the place because there were only a few people at the bar. They've got tables and chairs along with booths. 

Our sever came up immediately and greeted us and got our drink order. She was very friendly. She told us of a special they had that night, a pork burger, not to be confused with the regular pork burger on the menu because that is a burger with pulled pork on it.  This pork burger was a burger made of pork. I love a pork burger, but I decided on the Mega Titan Burger ($8.99) that comes with "Mouthwatering Burger, LOADED with Applewood Smoked Bacon, Sautéed Mushrooms and Cheddar Cheese​". My boyfriend ordered the pork burger special however for $8.99.

I'm not sure how long B.A.D. has been around, but the place shows it's age. It doesn't look dirty or anything, mind you, but you can tell the building has been around for a while, but that's what I like about it. 

It didn't take but about 10 minutes for our food to come out. We both ordered the French fries. I'm glad we did. I would guess that they fries are from a bag, they look like Rally's fries but taste a million times better. They have the right amount of breading on them, a nice spice and salt flavor. I could've ate a pound of them. 

Onto the Mega Titan burger. This thing is big. I was surprised with the size of the burger and amount of fries for the $8.99 price, especially being downtown. The cheese was all gooey and melted on top of the pile of bacon. The burger had a nice beef flavor and was juicy. A fluffy bun, what else can I say. It was delicious. Phillip also loved the pork burger special. 

I know the place is rated well and I now see why it is. The food is delicious and the prices are great. It's located off the beaten path but I'm glad I found it and will be going back again!
Great music and food. Our waiter Devonte was outstanding and made our visit even better.

Everything was awesome. Considering the traffic and their advise, we gave ourselves 1 hour to get to the show from the exit which was plenty.

It is very poorly managed. Give yourself at least three hours to get to the doors in time for the show.

I would not buy tickets again. Watch it somewhere more accessible.

Took me more time in the traffic both ways than the actual show.

The show Rockettes was awesome.

My dad loves Blues and Jazz so when he came to visit me in Nashville, I knew I wanted to try this place out. We got there around 9 and it was pretty full but we were able to get two seats at the bar. We sat, drank whiskey, and listened to the live band for hours. The band was more Funk that Blues or Jazz and I was worried my dad wouldn't like it, but he really enjoyed it. Can't really speak to their food menu but the bar was pretty standard and the bartenders were nice. Still, it does have the "chain" feel to it and there was a cover which I always find hard to justify when there's a dozen other places right around the corner that don't have any cover charge. But if you're looking for something a bit different than the standard  honky-tonks on Broadway, might be worth a shot.
The music was fantastic and the food was delicious. They had the best shrimp and grits that I have ever tasted before.

Just went here for lunch today on July 3rd. Not as crowded as we expected, but I'm sure that will change after 5pm.

Our waitress (my wife called her Taylor Swift lol) was excellent. We enjoyed her level of humor and her great service. I ordered the walleye sandwich with fries while the wife, Chris, ordered the regular burger. Everything was excellent for a small waterfront pub. So nice to have walleye again! Would go here again next time we are in this area.

The views from the outside deck are very nice of the riverfront. The drive back to here is a little bumpy due to the deterioration of the road, but not too bad.

Revisited Nashville recently and decided to take the backstage tour and was glad I did, well worth the time and money!  So much history and tradition at this place and you can feel it too.  Really enjoyed getting to go behind the scenes and see the dressing rooms, lobbies, and stages that the performers walked.  You also get to see Studio A where they film "Nashville" and used to film "Hee Haw."  Had some prety cool videos hosted by Blake Shelton that were a nice intro.  I had one of those "All-Access" passes from Visit Music City website, you can 60 bucks and get access to any four destinations on their extensive list.

Find it rather annoying when you come in and pay $13 for a drink, go to request to sing a song and told they have it but don't sing "slow songs" after 9pm. Seriously? What a rip off. Not interested in recommending this place ever. It's Tuesday night. Be grateful I'm even here.

We visited the Grand Ole Opry for the daytime tour. It was about 40 minutes long total and much of that was watching videos. It felt rushed, there was not much sense of history and it felt gimmicky. You are told you get a photo and they lead you to have it taken during the short tour, but then at the end you discover you have to pay $25 if you want it. Very underwhelming, I wish I had visited the Country music hall of fame instead.
Music was on point. Food was great! Had the shrimp n grits. Love that it had a lot of fresh okra on top. Only giving it 4 stars because the restrooms were gross.
Go here to drink, not to eat.   My Catfish dinner was OK, but ridiculously small.  Got charged a $1 up grade for a Dixie cup filled with Mac n cheese- really?  Many better places to eat in Nashville!

Previous to this place I visited 10 bars on broadway  however from sitting here for an hour no one ever approached me and asked if I would like any drink or food of any kind. The karaoke seems to be a preset list and very fun with not only the crowd but the singer enjoying it  as well. Certainly wish they had servers walking around to order drinks and food.
Had such a great time!! Music was great and we had the best waitress (Cameron). We will definitely be back!

Visited Nashville for the first time. I'm considered a very good singer but at karaoke, it's all about the song choice. You'd think being in Nashville country would be the obvious choice. Well that's probably true but karaoke can be anything you want it to be. The KJ was way in the back and easy to work with. Pulled out some good versions of my request and the diverse crowd was very energetic. I wish had had friends with me but I'm the type that can talk to anyone and the people I met really got the crowd jumping. I'm 60 and this Crowds mainly mid 30s to 40s but I love it when the twenty year olds get into the songs I sing and the 20 year olds killed it for me. I'll be back someday because I don't Wannabe anyplace else.

We took a road trip: Nashville, New Orleans, Clarksdale MS, and Memphis. Third Man was definitely a huge highlight of the entire trip! What a thrill to be in a cool spot owned by a musical genius and one of my top favorites, Jack White! We loved this place so much....small, cool, and interesting. What make it even better is that they carry records from little known artist which gives music lovers a chance to hear something that is not mainstream. There is a listening booth which was ultra cool to be in....the music sounded fantastic! (Lots of 48s to choose from). There are lots of well-deserved awards (Jack White's) on the walls and in cabinets. Really decorated in a way that you know love was poured into it. :)  (there is even yellow toilet paper in the black and yellow bathroom!) DEFINITELY check this place out!

We were so excited to see if the club lived up to the hype, we stayed up past our bedtime and headed to downtown Nashville around 10:30.  There was a line, but it went quickly.  The hostess collected our $5 cover charge and disappeared.  We weren't waiting long when she guided us to a table at the side of the stage.  

Our server, Trè was very friendly.  We were there for the entertainment but we split a catfish platter and each ordered drinks.  Hubby a Diet Coke and I had a concoction called the Hoochie Coochie. 

The food was very good and came out much faster than anticipated.  We were done eating just as the house band took the stage.  They came out and showed their skill.  Someone (a vocalist) from the audience asked to sit in with them and sing the blues. They agreed and it started off really good - he was actually pretty seasoned.  However, it took a different direction when the singer started reflecting on Easter Sunday (the next day).  Hubby enjoyed it but cocktails and mock church don't go hand in hand. 

They brought in the house vocalist and their selections were really good.  We got up and danced to covers of songs by artists from Rick James to Bruno Mars.  We were enjoying the upbeat songs but the music shifted to Sexual Healing and Let's Get it On.  That was our queue  to make an exit.. But we will definitely return during our next visit to Nashville.

After a friend's birthday dinner, we decided to check out Tippler to top the night off with class.  It was certainly that, with well-dressed, beautiful Nashvillians talking up strangers and ordering expensive cocktails.  The drinks were reasonably priced, and they even had a few specials on a Saturday night!  $5 drafts, $8 mixed drinks, and $10 fancy cocktails, I'm a happy camper!  

It would be a great place to take someone visiting Nashville, as it's not bogged down with tourists, although it gets PACKED past 10pm.  Better to take your friends than a date, I would recommend Music City Tippler to anyone wanting a nice bar experience.

We were in town for the night from Baltimore just looking for a low key spot to have a few beers and burgers. This feels like a locals spot and has a welcoming atmosphere. Our waitress and bartender were quick and friendly and our food was pretty good and really affordable.

A little pricey, but hey, it's Nashville! Great crowd, good acoustics, and on Saturdays they use a live band for karaoke. Pretty cool! The KJ has every song known to man, and seemed like he got an even rotation. The bartender was awesome, quick with the drinks. There serve food, but we didn't eat.

The place is way cool. The people are even cooler. Not sure what Jack White is paying them, but it is not enough. Very patient with the people in the store and with me. I am in Nashville for a conference and came in wearing a suit...thought I may get the cold shoulder, not at all. I gotta say I am a vault member and after my pilgrimage to third man, I will stay one for ever. Only thing...I wanted more stuff! The shop is small and I wish it were bigger.  First world problems right?

I was a first timer here and I loved the entire concept.  Being a major beer enthusiast this place sparked my interest from the moment I opened the drink menu.  I mean being able to select from the large list of beers from around the world, I don't know a business model better than this.  I originally was not going to eat, but just try as many beers as possible, but after my  companions food came I had to order.  What I ordered was the giant pretzel that they offer and I was not disappointed at all.  Along with beer I am also a pretzel enthusiast and it tasted even better than it looked.  The waitress was great, we were lucky enough to get one of the beer goddesses, I believe that's what they call the waitresses who have been trained to boost their beer knowledge.  Beautiful women who know and love their beer, the place is gold, definitely check it out.

Great environment for Bama game, but they need to do something about one of their bartenders that throws hissy-fits if you even look her direction. Yelled at me Saturday night 11/3 because I tried flagging down someone to help get the people behind me a drink. And not specifically her. Next thing I know she's standing there screaming at me. I mean she went of like a bomb, dropping F-bombs and such. Just off the handle tirade . I just held up my hands, said sorry and told the rest of my party not to engage with her. Next thing I know I've got a bunch of goon security guards tossing me out (which they clearly get off on). She clearly has a problem. Pretty sure everyone knows the one I'm talking about. Complete B. Apparently doesn't know she's in the customer service business. Cost her team $50 in tips. Hope she gets help or another job.

Made a dinner reservation for 3 people for 8pm on a Sunday. Get there and have to pay a $3 cover charge. Understandable for people just coming in to watch and listen to the great band. Not sure why we had to pay the cover for dinner on a Sunday though. 

Get to the table and order 2 beers and a cocktail. Wait 10 minutes, order nachos, still no drinks. Another 10 minutes, order our entrees - 2 pulled pork and the catfish sandwich. Finally get the drinks, which were good.

Another 15-20 minutes goes by and we finally get our nachos which were okay. Devour those, since at this point it was 8:45. Wait 20 minutes, order another round of beers. Get the drinks, finish them, wait another 40 minutes and finally get our food at 9:40pm. The pulled pork and Cole slaw was good, the catfish sandwich was lukewarm with stale bread and standard fries - would not recommend. 

The waitress apologized profusely throughout the whole ordeal. It was definitely not her fault, she was managing a ton of tables and was taking orders, bringing food, drinks, cleaning tables... they just need to hire more staff. It should not take half an hour to get nachos and shouldn't take more than an hour for a mediocre sandwich and pulled pork. 

DO NOT COME TO EAT DINNER. The only saving grace was the live band, they were fantastic. We asked to see the manager and luckily they took off 15% from our order which was still not enough in my opinion. Would come back for music and a drink, NOT the ABYSMAL service and SUBPAR food.
The brisket and the shrimp salad was good. The presentation was excellent. The atmosphere was very good even for lunch.

Belcourt Taps is the perfect place if you're looking for a regular hangout place. The food is spot on with good burgers, tacos, salads, and a bunch of good appetizers. And the beers. Don't forget the beers. They have around 14 taps that are mostly dedicated to local brewers like Black Abby,  Czahns, Jackalope, and others. 

Most every night has music of some sort from the new-to-town singer to the Belmont student to the seasoned Nashville veteran every night offers something for everyone. 

Recently, they have started serving brunch on Saturdays and Sundays and like the regular menu the food on the Brunch menu is excellent. I had the Bacon, Egg, and Cheese sandwich with the potatoes and it was as good as anything I have had any place else in town. They cure the bacon in-house so the flavor is like nothing you will get anywhere else. 

All in all, if you are looking for a good hang-out that changes to from night to night Belcourt Taps is the pace to be in Hillsboro Village.

Best place ever the food was great the drinks were really good and the music was awesome 
So glad we found it

Attended the Opry Friday October 12th. My fifth visit over the past 10 years. I'm done with attending the Opry live and I'm through with Nashville. The town has evolved to embrace the worst elements of Las Vegas and Gatlinburg TN. Through no fault of the Opry, we got terrible seats - too close to the stage and far left of center. Two drunk, rude, obnoxious couples sat behind us and would not shut up!!!  Loud conversations disturbing everyone sitting near them continued not only through the breaks, but throughout the performances!

An employee (male) sat on a stool in the aisle nearby and said/did NOTHING! Through stares and polite requests, these huckleberries continued blabbering. We got up and left our seats midway through the performance and, after complaining to ushers about these Delberts, were led to much better seats just in time to hear Terri Clark. Somewhat saved the night for us.

If your idea of a happening time has devolved to drinking, acting like an a**hole, fighting traffic and paying outrageous prices for entertainment / lodging / food / parking etc., then Nash Vegas is for YOU!  Me, I am so over it.

I like these bars because they have great selection of beers.  So, that's nice.  Food is barely average bar fare.  I ate here for dinner and for lunch, and was hoping for better, but it didn't suck.  Servers were efficient, if not overly friendly.  The beef dipper was 100x better than the "kick ass" chicken sandwich.  Fries were crispy.  I thought it would be busier on a Friday night at 10:30pm than it was - but being a solo diner (traveling for work) it being not crowded suited me just fine - made it easier to find a seat at the bar.  I know I will be back in a Flying Saucer again.
Stopped by at 5:00 and left st 7:40.   Great ribs, good fries.  Lynchburg lemonades and local beer.  Yummy.  Highjivers were fun.  Great service from our waiter. Would come come back again.

Been a regular here for two years. New Managment has killed the vibe of the bar and drove away regulars. They fired some of the best bartenders and this bar is no longer what it was under the old Managers Chris and Big Dave.

We went here based o  the things to do in Nashville recommendation. We got the tickets in advance. This is the first time my friend and I attended country music concert without much interest in it. The show was for 2 and half hours and I really enjoyed country music. But next time I would definitely want to listen to some songs before taking a leap like this. We got lucky this time.
Large selection of beers to choose from. Monday's are $3 pints so you can't go wrong with a good beer at a good price.

Horrible experience all around.  I've literally never written a review of any establishment or product before, but my experience at Belcourt Taps was bad enough to motivate me to bite the bullet and sign up for a Yelp account.  My girlfriend and I had a Groupon for two beer flights and an appetizer.  We visited Belcourt Taps on a Saturday night at about 8:30 and sat outside on their nearly empty patio.  When our server saw our Groupon on the table, he instantly pointed out the fine print saying we had to have a reservation, which we hadn't previously noticed.  Who makes a reservation at a bar??  He said he would check with the bartender to see if they could honor the Groupon without a reservation but told us the answer would probably be no.  Sure enough, he returned a few minutes later saying that because it was a Saturday night, the bartender was "too backed up" and didn't "have time" to make beer flights.  The bartender doesn't have time to pour beer??  Seriously??  We tried explaining to the server that we weren't in any hurry, but to no avail.  We left feeling pretty certain that if we had ordered beer flights without a Groupon the bartender would have had plenty of time to pour beer.

We returned a few days later with a reservation.  When we walked in, we were told to sit anywhere and that we didn't need a reservation unless we were using a Groupon.  Okay...

We sat at a hightop table and were greeted by our server a few minutes later; she let us know they were out of two of the beers on the beer flight menu.  We ordered our two beer flights and the fried green tomatoes appetizer; our server returned about 15 minutes later to say that they were out of fried green tomatoes.  We ordered the queso appetizer, which turned out to be disgusting.  We had originally planned to use our Groupon for the beer flights and appetizer and then also order dinner and additional drinks but were so disgusted with the place and their horrific service by the time we finished the beer flights and queso that we just wanted to get what we had already paid for and leave.  When our server brought our check, we were unpleasantly surprised to see that Belcourt Taps had applied an automatic gratuity to the tune of about 30% without our consent to our table of two.  When I questioned it, the server explained that this was because, you guessed it, we were using a Groupon.  We definitely would have tipped even though our experience left a LOT to be desired, but 30% without our consent just because we were using a Groupon??  Come on, people.

My girlfriend and I both got the distinct impression that Belcourt Taps is quite resentful of Groupon patrons and very into petty rules and nickeling and diming customers to death.  Ironic, considering that most businesses offer Groupons to increase publicity and build their client base.  Epic fail, Belcourt Taps- we will never return and strongly discourage others from making the mistake of visiting your establishment.  I predict a FOR RENT sign on Belcourt Avenue in the near future.

Go for the music but not my first choice for food. I would give the music 5 stars. The BB King All Stars were great. Loved the horns and the vocalists. Actually they were all great. The food I would give a 3. The gumbo was good but could benefit from the addition of some seafood. The brisket was average and the creole shrimp sauce was more on the side of marinara sauce.

I've said it before, I am not a country music aficionado but when you're in Nashville you have to make certain concessions and visiting the Grand Ole Opry was one of them.

Our tour guide was AWESOME.  He knew his stuff and he was relaxed, cracking jokes, keeping everything fun and interesting.  He honestly made me want to learn more about country music (I'm sure that feeling will pass).  I may not be a fan of the music but the fact that country music has so much history, that I love.

Tours leave every 15 minutes, AAA discount.

Fun fact: Carrie Underwood is a bitch.  I have it on a good source.
Decent food, good beer....horrible service!!!! The staff literally won't make eye contact so they don't have to stop if you have a question or need something.  Very disappointing.

Amazing place to spend part of the day. The tour is fun, informative and personable. It does move at a quick pace somewhat but they say upfront if you want more time just let them know and you can stay in the area and join the next group a few minutes later- what other group does this... simply a great venue that cares about its guests . Highly recommend. Wish they played more country music loud though ;)

I was walking down 2nd street, shocked & disappointed in what Music City had to offer. Littered with Honky Tonks, bad chains and other country music tomfoolery... I really began to question why I visited this city in the first place (after all, I am from Memphis and everyone knows that Memphis is better than Nashville in all things). Then, all of a sudden, the clouds open up and the sun pours down a blinding, beautiful light onto the front facade of BB King's Nashville. I couldn't believe my eyes! It was like divine intervention. No, it WAS divine intervention! As I approached the front entrance, these angelic figures greet me at the door, welcoming me in. I later learned that these powerhouses of restaurant & entertainment leadership were named Courtney, Alex, Sean, Thomas, Faith & Ronnie. Seeing I was weary from my travels, they helped me into a rickshaw and carted me into the venue to a nice table with a fantastic view of the band. My server moved at the speed of light, refilling my drink before I even realized I needed a refill. She was somehow able to predict everything I wanted to order. Chef Thomas prepared the most amazing chilaquiles I've ever had in my life. The band sounded better than any band I've ever heard. I couldn't help but notice their Sound Engineer, Sean behind the sound board furiously turning knobs, connecting & disconnecting wires, and threatening the lives of the band if they played anything less than the perfect set. I also noticed he needed a haircut. But wow! Wow what a sound in there! Checking on my almost out of body experience, Ronnie came to my table to ensure everything far exceeded my expectations. I thanked him and he literally ninja-flipped away as he checked on other tables and staff. I crowd-surfed out the doors and upon exiting the building, I realized I was back on 2nd street... Oh no. What have I done?! The clouds returned and covered the sun, it began to rain. Suddenly I recounted every sin, every mistake, every failure I've ever made in my life and realized that leaving BB King's trumped all of it. I look to my right and see a puppy crying, I could instantly relate to the puppy. How can you have the most amazing experience of your life and then have to return to this?! I'll be back BB's, oh yes, I will definitely be back. Thank you for changing my life for the better, this is a debt I will never be able to repay.
5 stars for he service! The hostess Adaora was a GEM! She was so kind and made sure I had a great experience! Will definitely be back

Wow! I was not expecting to have such a wonderful experience! From the hospitality, to the food, and music, our whole experience was wonderful! I could not have had a better time and can't wait to go back.

Wonderful show! We loved everything about our trip to the Opry. The atmosphere is great and the music is the best. We definitely want to come back again soon. The only problem was the gift shop line after the show. Was way too long. I would definitely suggest going to gift shop before the show.

Great drinks, great food, great service.  There was even a live band and singer while we were eating that we all enjoyed, my young one included.  We didn't want to leave but it was getting crowded and others were waiting for a seat.  Great place.

Made my first visit yesterday. I really enjoyed the comfortable atmosphere and amazing beer list. The German plate was also a great meal. Prices were fairly reasonable and I also joined the UFO beer club. Only complaint was the service was a little slow. Would still recommend to others and will be back for sure.

Touristy check; loud as all get out check; 
That being said, we had good service, very good music, and pretty good food. Try the chicken fried chicken...tasty comfort food.

Great experience!  The show had about 6 artists that played a 10 minute set, roughly 3 songs each.  We bought tickets the day before the show and bought a package that included a backstage tour and a self guided tour of the Ryman for the next day for about $110 each for floor seats.  We had to call them to pick the seats that we actually wanted since if you buy them online the packaged deals will assign seats automatically.  There are bars to get drinks before amd during the show.  The seats are like long church benches where you are touching the people next to you.  We thought the whole experience was really neat, we got to see the dressing rooms and see props and got to stand on the ryman circle and take lots of pictures.   I would say if you like country music, I would definitely come to a show at the Opry if only to say you've been to the Grand Ole Opry.

Much quieter than down on Broadway!  Great food.  Recommend the pretzels!  Awesome dips go with it.  Beer list overwhelmingly large, so something for everyone 
I went twice while staying in Nashville- worth it!

Came here with a group of 12, may have been the issue but shouldn't be... I was very excited based on Yelp but left disappointed. The food was absolutely nothing to write home about, the server acted as if he wished he could be anywhere else. We ordered the house chips and he brought the ranch after the two baskets were empty and we ordered a third that he brought after we were done and the table had been cleared then refused to take them off the ticket because he had already removed two drinks... My advice is don't go with a large group and don't order a dirty martini...

My kids and I walk here sometimes for their burgers since it's in the neighborhood. This, along with Brown's (and maybe the Dog) are the best burgers in Hillsboro Village in my humble opinion. I would walk or bike another mile to eat The Hangover, Juicy Lucy, or Hell's Kitchen. It's a tight place and one with tight beer. You can bring your dog and hangout on the outside patio. Only reason I minus a star is supported smoking on one part of the patio. Enjoy a beautiful day here on Belcourt and hop over to the theater and Dragon Park.

Just walked out. Music was good, service at the bar sucked. Not attentive at all on a very slow night. Lettuce wraps good if taken out of the sauce. Saturated in teriyaki! Brisket melt - choose a different sandwich. Decor leaves a lot to be desired. Memphis location blows it away!

Great place that is just a short walk from the heart of Nashville, but far enough where it isn't too crowded. Awesome service and reasonable prices, would highly recommend. The hot chicken sandwich was delicious!

This is a must see if you're visiting Nashville. Loved, loved, loved the tour! Our tour guide was wonderful.  He was very knowledgable and gave us time to look at everything. We enjoyed all the history and fun facts about it. Only thing was that the woman who sold us our tickets was VERY RUDE & misunderstood our question about the tour start time-that was surprising but we knew that didn't represent the entire staff. We actually went to the gift shop too & I bought several items! I defintely will return to the Grand Ole Opry House next time I'm in Nashville.
Had an amazing time at the BB King Blues Club.  Great food and entertainment.  You can't go wrong stopping here for a good time.

Came in on a Thursday night to a rather empty bar. Could not get a drink because the bartenders were too busy chatting to each other rather than wait on customers. To top it off, when I finally get their attention after 15 minutes of being there, that I need a beer she replies "not to get fucking attitude with her, since I didn't know if the guys who had been there for 2 hours had a tab or not, and to give her the money or she'll take the fucking beer back" She then proceeded to walk over to the other workers and discuss what a rude bitch I was loudly in front of her other customers.  I have never been treated so rudely by a bartender. This was my first time to Nashville and I will never return and spend money here.

I recently returned to America after nearly 20 years overseas and decided to move to San Diego. Since everything I have can fit in a small car with room to spare I decided to drive across country and see America again. 
Why mention all that? Well, I picked Nashville for two reasons. I always wanted to go and have never been and I wanted to go to B.B King's Blues Club for my own lone commemoration of his passing.
The staff was quite friendly. I called ahead and asked about live music and the hostess answered every question I had.
I loved the music, the atmosphere, and my service was very patient even though he was so busy. I loved my appetizer, but the entree really messed with my stomach for some reason. 
I can't say it was because of something bad on the restaurants side. I ate a few spoonfuls and my stomach went all kinds of goofy. 

I would still recommend the place. I knew nothing about Nashville and still don't, but if you are ever around Nashville go checkout B.B King's Blues Club.

The store itself is rad but unfortunately the girl that helped us or more like DIDN'T help us was one of the rudest people I have met. I own retail stores and would be appalled if any of my employees treated my customers the way she did. My husband and I just left there with the worst taste in our mouth and its unfortunate because we are big Jack White fans and we did end up spending almost $100 on little things in there but almost walked out with nothing due to the way the chick with the big ass nose ring treated us. She acted like we were not "cool" enough and made us feel extremely uncomfortable when we asked questions about items that we wanted to buy. We would have spent $1000 today in there but because of her we walked out after only 10 minutes of being there. If I were Jack White, I would be really bummed that this sales person was a representation of me...

Our first time here and it was enjoyable.  It's a small store but has the perfect amount of vinyl and artifacts to look at.  We used a machine that made a mold of an electric guitar.   We got a few shirts but I didn't find anything I really needed or wanted to buy as far as vinyl records.  We did walk back to the venue side to see the back area but it was closed.  The restrooms are cool looking for the yellow and black decor.  If you are in Nashville this is well worth the stop.  So many big artist have recorded there and it's easy to get to.  They have street parking and a small lot to park at.
If you enjoy blues and don't stop here!!! Some of the most talented musicians in Nashville.

Absolutely amazing venue!  We saw the show this Tuesday night with a group and had the opportunity to dine in the room where Hee Haw was formerly taped - how cool!  The show is amazing and I love how each artist has the opportunity to play 3 songs before the next one comes out - genius!  I am not a big country music fan, but couldn't believe we had the opportunity to hear Rascall Flats - just amazing!  The backstage tour was great, but made for a long evening...so get your rest if you plan to stay.

As with all Flying Saucers this has a superior selection of beer and ales. Of the three I've been to (Memphis, Houston, Nashville) this is my favorite of the three.  It does not have the crowd atmosphere as Memphis, but it is the most aesthetically pleasing of the three. The location is behing the hotel that occupies the old train station so it's a little off the main Broadway nightlife area, but that may be a plus for you if you don't prefer the tourist crowds. This is a 4.5 star place, losing the .5 due to the easily missed location off Broadway.  I will go here everytime Im in Nashville.
There is nothing much to add to the Grand Ole Opry House experience that hadn't already been said.  The tour was excellent, the history superb, and the performers on point.

Saw this was one of the top 10 places in Nashville to watch sports. There were two games on today....Vandy v MTSU and UK v FL. Yet, the Alabama game was the ONLY game playing on the 1,743 tvs in the bar. Thanks for alienating everyone in Nashville who isn't an inbred Alamaba fan.

My wife, her friends, and I rented a table here to see Grandmaster Flash, who was admittedly awesome. The venue is gorgeous. Thats where the compliments end. Our table had a $200 minimum, which is fine by me. However, they don't seem to enforce the reserved nature of the tables, and when we came back from the VIP balcony, there were other people sitting at our table with their drinks atop it. When we finally got rid of them (incredible rude people by the way), I asked for a reserved placard. 25 minutes later the waitress shows up with a tiny sign too small to even be noticed. I found the sign on the floor with other peoples drinks in its place. The service was too horrible to believe. The waitress only came about every 45 minutes. After a drink order you'd wait about half an hour to receive that drink. It took 15 minutes for the waitress to come back to say they were out of something. They were out of most of the things I wanted to order; specialty appetizers, specialty drinks, even entrees, each time requiring another 15 minutes for the waitress to inform us that they were out of them. The VIP bathroom was filthy. When we finally ordered an entree, they completely forgot about us for over an hour. We had all run out of drinks, and no help came to us. The VIP bar that we paid extra for wouldn't charge drinks to the table, another completely pointless addition to our night. Other tables also seemed to be having this problem. How can you spend $200 when you can't get a waitress around to order anything?

Well, thats easy. You can order a $180 liter of jack daniels, or a $200 bottle of sparkling water. 

The bass was so frighteningly powerful that it vibrated the table, and even vibrated a drink right off of it and onto the floor where it broke. It took over 15 minutes for them to come over to clean up the glass fragments that littered the ground below us. I spoke to the lady up front and she apologized for the lack of service. The waitress brought us a few free shots, and took some items off of our tab. I was happy, for a moment. Then it still took over an HOUR from the time I wanted my check to the time my card was brought back. They include a hefty gratuity. Still, with the items taken off the check, the bill wasn't too bad.

Except that they DOUBLE CHARGED my card! Maybe my review might go higher if they fixed that. EDIT: they did fix this. 1 star added.

Conclusion: One of the prettier bars I've been to, but if its got horrible service, its a horrible bar. Their attempts to fix the night were more than outweighed by the continued ineptitude we experienced.

Not recommended.

From the time we walked in the door until we were actually served was about two hours!  We were in a party of four!  Larger groups came long after us and were served first. There was no apology and no offer of anything to make up for this horrendously long wait. They don't care because we are tourists. The food was good though. BBQ pork tasted great as did the ribs. Live band was also very good. This was in a Thursday night.

One of my favorite bars until new security and management took over. Recently spend 3.5 hours sitting at a table upstairs and was told we had to leave to make room for Browns fans. Said that we were staying to watch the game and was told if we didn't leave we would be kicked out with force.  Regulars shouldn't be treated like this and it's been slowly getting worse, but this crosses the line and I don't plan on ever taking my business back there.
Amazing atmosphere wonderful time! We saw Ricky Skaggs, the Gatlin Brothers, Swon Brothers, a few others, great show. Very pricy drinks but expected for such a attraction as this. Great seats

A Big City (original Tippler is in Manhattan) transplant hits Nashville.  Nice, upscale place with good Scotch and Draft beer.   Upmarket Nashville crowd.   For sure the nicest lounge I have been to here.      

The bathroom has a special foot pedal door opener.   That is an original touch and worth noting.     

Well worth keeping this place in mind.  Next time I would like to chill out at one of the outside patio tables.

Waitress was obviously drunk and forgot our entire order. 

The food was good but I would never go back to this place just because of the service.

The waitress brought us out stuff we didn't even order. I understand this is a bar, but I thought the drinks were for the customers not the staff.

Full disclosure: I'm from Detroit, and I'm a huge White Stripes/Jack White fan - so on my recent trip to Nashville, I knew that Third Man Records was a mandatory stop. What an awesome place! It's like getting a peek into the wonderful, odd brain of Jack himself; there is vinyl. There are old, mechanical puppets by the ceiling. There is a recording booth where you can have a record made of you singing. There's an old timey photo booth. In the case by the register, there are the Lego versions of Jack and Meg. The recording space looked awesome (I peeked through the window). I wish we had been able to see a band play there; maybe next time, Nashville.

As a former patron and employee I have to urge you not to eat here. Food is okay, drinks are mediocre and uninspiring. It's over priced and very much your general tourist destination trap. One the experience of working there I experienced hostel but incompetent co workers, and some very poor management, I the short time I was there they went through about 13 staff members is advise patrons and potential employees to stay away there are much better options within walking distance.
The Yazoo creole catfish was awesome. Spinach dip is good also. Adam McDonough does a great job of entertaining. Great place for food and music.
Walked into the ticket office, no other customers in line. However, no greeting from any of the three ticket agents so I had to ask for assistance. Not a warm, welcoming environment.

It takes a lot to shake me and this place did so and more. Unbelievably rude bartender and manager and sketchy stuff going on here. That's all I'll say about that. Should have known this place was a bad idea when we walked in on a Sunday afternoon around 5pm and not a soul was in the place besides the DJ and bartender. Not a soul. We had wanted to check this place out because karaoke sounded like a fun idea. 

First, the bartender had her back to us almost the entire time and we had to say excuse me each time she was on her phone texting to get her attention. Asked her if she had an outlet behind the bar to charge my phone and she snootily said, "No, we don't take responsibility for anyone's personal belongings." That's actually fine with me but she was hella rude about it. We did some karaoke up on the stage and the place again, was sketchy as hell. People were going in and out of this door and some weird stuff was happening. Their bathroom is connected to Tequila Cowboys so you had to go down a hall and around the bend to access it, it was just straight up weird. Couldn't find my coat at one point so asked the bartender if anyone had turned one in and she tried to make it seem like I was accusing her of stealing it. She went as far as to get the DJ or manager's attention about the coat matter and the DJ made an announcement over a loud speaker and spoke, "Our bartenders don't steal people's coats so stop accusing them of doing so and no cursing at our bartenders." You've got to be kidding me. Cursing? Not once did a curse word come out of my mouth, we were livid. Livid. She couldn't have been more rude and unwelcoming and she was causing unnecessary drama that put a huge damper in our day. Never ever ever would I recommend anyone coming to this place. It's disgusting with some real winners for employees. Plain and simple.
Great drinks, bitchy hostesses, house band played everything great, but forgot to play any blues songs. Desserts were very good

Just great.  You already know this is the best place in the world to see and hear country music performances so I won't bother with that.  Get your tickets early for best seating.  Tickets may or may not be available the day of the show, but if they are, the seat selection is sure to be limited.  There is a security line to get in so leave those pocket knives in the car (you'd think people would have learned that by now, but last night the guy ahead of us opted to throw his knife in the trash rather than going back to the car, or maybe he came on a tour bus and didn't even have the option of going back to the car).  The lobby is inviting.  Several concessions inside sell all kinds of drinks and a few light food items.  There were some outdoor BBQ concessions doing dogs and burgers (maybe more, we didn't really check them out) out front before the show.  Restroom lines can get long so be prepared.  There's also the gift shop to get your Opry souvenirs.  Go, enjoy and have a good time.

The owner of this bar, Kelli, was intentionally rude and hateful to a friend of mine last night. Referring to my female friend as "him/her" and "it" when telling her to leave. I won't support Kelli's bar ever again and you shouldn't either. It is this type of small minded bigotry that perpetuates hate.

Very excited about watching the Alabama game with other fans but we did not even make it in the door. 2:00 in the afternoon and a 53 year old me  and her 66 year old husband were turned away because I left my ID at home! WTF? Place was pretty much empty. Ridiculous!

I was in Nashville with my wife and another couple.  The ladies were there for a quilting conference and the guys were trailing spouses.  When in Nashville a requirement is attendance at a performance at the Grand Old Opry.  I really don't care for country music at all but I was impressed with the professionalism of the entire operation.  The format consists of having a number of groups perform three or four songs each.  Groups ranged from 1950's western music (think Sons of the Pioneers), bluegrass, country folk, country Christian, to contemporary country.  The quality of the backup bands was absolutely phenomenal.  There is a huge musical talent pool in Nashville and you have to be very good indeed to perform at a venue such as the Grand Old Opry.  The staff were very helpful to the guests and everything was very professional including ordering the tickets on line. There is a certain amount of hype but even if you don't like country and western music this is a Institution.

We went to the Grand Ole Opry at 1 p.m. for a tour. The tour is a must if you love country music.
They take you backstage and show you the entrance only the ar totists come through.
They will show you the different dressing rooms and the large room where the country singers get together before the show.
Went back there at 7 p.m. to watch Luke Bryan. He put on a great show.
Make sure you get there a little early because the lines are very long.
If you go to Nashville and enjoy country music this is a MUST!

So much for Southern Hospitality.  Our long anticipated holiday in Nashville was just disrupted by a winter storm, causing us to have to miss the Opry tomorrow night.  I called the box office in tears. Non refundable tickets I'm told - too bad so sad for us. .

Went here Friday night before the Maroon 5 concert for a bite to eat. It was awesome! Our waitress was funny & outgoing, which makes your experience better at a restaurant in my opinion.. The burgers are amazing! They're fresh made & cooked to perfection! Also enjoyed happy hour! I definitely recommend eating here. We definitely plan to visit again!!

It was 11 of us so it took so long for us to get seated. We were on a girls weekend getaway. The food and the customer service was just ok. The music was ok as well. We danced a little bit that was fun. I really do have to go back to Nashville to explore more.
The Redneck Riviera is a patriotic joint which accommodated our Army unit reunion. The bartenders were great and the music was good.
What happen to this place? Gross and nasty .. crap all over the chairs and floor cannt even sit and relax.  Afraid to order a beer it looks so dirty.

Beautiful intimate theatre but a word of advice, go to the early show on Saturday! I believe it's at 7. If you go to the later one...at 9? You will be waiting for the other show to finish, not be able to sit down, even more difficult to find parking with double the people there that haven't left the early show yet. I must also say, I went to see Vince Gil, he sang 2 songs, 1 which was a cover and 1 a tribute to Merle. While it was a very touching song, I was extremely disappointed and heart broken that I didn't get to hear more classic Vince Gil songs ;(

I had to travel to Nashville for business this past weekend, but decided to treat myself wile I was in town, since I had never been to the city. I had the pleasure of stopping in B.B. King's twice while I was there. The first time was on a Saturday night. The place was rockin' from the moment we stepped foot in the door up until we left. The band was phenomenal (the All-Stars, I believe). Every song they played had me itching o get out of my seat and dance!  In front of the stage is a small dance floor, which was occupied by at least a handful of people for every song. On this particular visit, we had already eaten, so the only thing that I ordered was a drink. I was able to keep the shot glass as a souvenir, as well (they provide you with a fresh, clean glass on the way out the door). I've had many drinks in my short lifetime, and theirs was mediocre at best...too much juice, not enough liquor!

My second visit was on a Monday around 2pm, to grab lunch before hitting the road. I had intended on getting an item I had seen on the dinner menu from Saturday night, but of course, it wasn't available on the lunch menu. I ended up with  bowl of gumbo and the bbq ribs with baked beans, cole slaw, and cornbread. Gumbo was good, but needed more rice with it. The ribs were great, nice and tender with a great tasting bbq sauce. I like mines saucy, so I had to ask for some on the side. The beans were equally delicious. I passed on the cole slaw (I typically don't like it) and the cornbread was ok. They also had a 2 for 1 happy hour going on for drafts and wells.

If I'm ever in Nashville again, I'll be sure to go back, but for dinner or late night, so that I can see the live band. I must also add, as a 23 year old, I have an old soul, so the music was right up my alley. From what I heard on Saturday night, though, the music was primarily of the 70's and 80's, and I looked to be the youngest person in the entire restaurant that night.
Over priced drinks and miserable bartenders, especially the one with the purple hair. Unless karaoke is your thing, skip this pace.

Well they charge a cover. Probably because the only thing great is the music. Worst service I've had in a long time. The food was ok. No fun waiting for your server to show up for 20 minutes. Then has a crappy attitude. I think maybe she is supposed to be working at dicks last resort. Then maybe the entire experience would have made more sense.

We were blessed to walk into BBKINGS in Nashville for lunch! We were lucky enough to have met Alexandria our waitress.  It felt so good to have someone who not only took great care of us, but she was an  amazing person. It is rare to see someone who loves what she does. BB would be proud that she represents his memory! We will definitely be back and will ask for Alexandria  ( we are not family either- just really happy customers )

I had so much fun at the Tuesday night, 9:30 show which featured Bill Anderson, Levi and Marcus Hummon, the Gatlin Brothers, Carrie Underwood, Henry Cho, Eric Paslay and the Oak Ridge Boys. 

We sat in Section 7, Row G, 11, 12 and 13 which was up close, but far left when facing the stage.  Wish were a little more towards the center.  

The live music was great.  I think I'll return every time I visit Nashville.

Ordered through grubhub as they are the delivery for Dawg House.  Looked great, chicken sliders good, but disappointed I ordered beef dogs onions, mustard, relish and ketchup.  Got sauerkraut mustard and relish.  The kraut was the only taste I got out of a bite after heavily putting on ketchup and taking the kraut off....bummer, so looking forward to the normal dogs, and the bun looked good but soaked in kraut juice.

The show was fantastic and we had great seats. It's not a cheap evening but it was well worth it! We attended a tour earlier in the day that was also great. I thought the price of the tour was a little high ($33 each) to then want $25 for the picture you took in the circle. Cool, but gimmicky. We passed on the picture.

I dig Jack White and the White Stripes, and I want to give this place 5 stars.  But I was disappointed by how small it is, and how little there is to actually see and do.

What they have, is super cool.  But I wanted 3x as much!

Still, worth a visit.  They have some awesome, obscure vinyl, and very cool tshirts and memorabilia.

We've eaten at B.B. Kings in Las Vegas and loved it so we were excited to try another location. We were not disappointed!  The BB Kings All-Star band started playing while we ate. They were phenomenal. Ribs and chicken were delicious. Love their BBQ sauce.

We went to a performance while we were in Nashville For a reunion.  We had been once before back in the1980s and all I remember is that there weren't many seats behind us.  Of course, after this much time, I have no idea who was playing back then, attending a show at the Opry was just something you have to do when you are in Nashville, sort of like seeing Elvis when you are in Las Vegas.

This time we had much better seats as part of our group and we knew that Carrie Underwood was getting top billing.  The show is broadcast live so it included the commercials as well as the performances and consisted of four distinct half hour shows with several different artists for each one as well as a different MC.  Carrie Underwood was in the last segment and sang several of her songs beautifully.

Overall we had a really great experience this time and I even recognized names and songs of some of the other performers like Ricky Skaggs, Jeannie Sealy, and the Whites.  I'm not a regular at attending concerts or live shows lately because I don't like dealing with crowds and traffic, but the Grand Ole Opry was well worth it!

How do you give the Grand Ole Opry anything less. 

The best please for history of country music and a chance to see a big name while there. Love it.

This review is for the Backstage Pass tour that occurs every 15minutes. Purchasing tickets that day was a snap and getting to the right location to start, very clear. I always felt like I was being directed with confidence and a bit of humor. 

Tour guide was energetic and had a few quilts to give us a chuckle. It was really cool to walk the same area that country legends walk before and after the show. Checking out the dressing rooms and getting a picture on the stage was memorable as well. The only bummer is I really don't like it when you can hear other tours going on - it takes away from the experience. We heard two separate tours for a few moments during ours. Lastly, gift shop clothing was awesome!

We reserved priority seating for two at 5:30 on a Tuesday to assure time for a 7:30 performance at TPAC and were seated promptly. There were only 20-25 people there so the reservation definitely wasn't needed. No one came to get our drink orders for at least 20 minutes, although several waiters passed by our table and made eye contact. An attempt to flag one down was blatantly ignored. When our waitress finally arrived (we suspect she was late to her shift and nobody covered her table), the service was adequate but not spectacular. My gumbo was tasty but was served warm--definitely not hot; not a wisp of steam was to be found. My husband enjoyed his pasta. We weren't offered a second round of drinks. Checked off list; doubt we'll return.

Service is friendly. Cook offered us free fried pickles and onions since someone mistakenly ordered twice. Drinks weren't as strong as I thought they would be. But the live music is nice. Plus, you get to leave your mark wherever you want! Wish I brought a sharpie to the bathroom...
One of my favorites on Broadway! It is smaller than other bars, but the beer is not overpriced and the atmosphere is great.

THIS PLACE! This was my favorite bar of Nashville.  The music, the talent, the drinks.  UNBELEAVABLE.  We did not eat here but the food looked incredible. Defiantly on my must revisit Nashville for this bar.  The drummer we saw played for B.B. King.

We had so much fun at the Oprey! The grounds are beautiful. Even though it was a sold out night the lines weren't bad and everything went really smooth. There was a little bit of a warm up and pre show so arrive early. The show is awesome. On the night we went there was a great line up finishing up with Little Big Town. Every act was great. The interaction with the audience and the small personal theater make it magical. If you are ever in Nashville be sure to go to a show, or 2 at the Oprey! You won't be disappointed!

This is a must see, even if you're not a big country music fan. Old stars, current stars, and up-and-comers get together to put on a weekly radio show.  This is a major bit of Americana. 

Restaurant choices are limited, so you might want to eat in downtown Nashville beforehand.

In a recent trip to Nashville, some of my friends and I decided to grab tickets to The Grand Ole Opry. I had watched it as a kid and wanted to have a taste of that old nostalgia. We were not disappointed. The Opry is in a newer building on a big property with a huge shopping mall and hotel. You could make a total day of it or ride in shortly before the show and walk around the Opry. The mall has newer stores. The hotel has restaurants and the Opry offers entertainment almost nightly. I highly recommend grabbing your tickets in advance which you can do on their website. The hook is that you buy the tickets but you dont know until the date gets closer who will be playing that night. We were totally lucky and got to see Carrie Underwood with The Oak Ridge Boys. She was amazing!!! The show house is set up in seats that resemble church pews. The show is recorded and you are part of the live studio audience. They even have the ON AIR sign! NOTE* go into the gift shop BEFORE the show. After the show you are ushered out and the only way to the gift shop is to get back in the line to get into the concert ,AGAIN! so be sure to make time for that BEFORE the show. There are drinks and food options outside the show area and you can take drinks inside the show house. The Opry is not close to downtown and requires an uber and or a ride to get to. Plan on at least 20 min or so to get out to the area. Would recommend to anyone visiting that has the time to make it out that way.
Rude and ignorant security. Would never go back for the way he treated my friend and husband.

We visited B.B. King's in Nashville and overall enjoyed it.  The music was outstanding.  The service was excellent and fast.  The appetizer's were good and the drinks were good.  The entree's, however, were "ok".  I have been to most the B.B. Kings in the USA on a quest to get souvenir glasses from each location.  Memphis still has the best location - food wise.  But no matter what you can't go wrong with B.B. Kings.

If you're in town this place is a must! The live show was very entertaining, drinks were great (they didn't skimp on the alcohol), the pew seats were actually very comfortable and I didn't feel like I was encroaching on the other person. Actually, I  think more venues could benefit by having this type of seating. The artists were very down to earth and each played a couple songs a piece. The comedians "The Indian and the White Man", hysterical and the amount of patriotism felt in the room was overwhelming!
Side note *Grand Ole Opry Hotel* leaves a lot to be desired!

No trip to Nashville is complete without attending a performance at the Grand Ole Opry.  The lineup doesn't have to have a huge headliner to be entertaining. Every performer we saw connected with the audience. You might even get lucky and witness a performer make their Opry debut! Also, I f you attend a performance at the Opry, a backstage tour is a must. Our guide was knowledgeable, engaging, and full of interesting facts. It was clear she loves being a part of the Opry. You walk the same path as the performers, visit the dressing rooms, watch a short film in the old HeeHaw studio and stand on stage, in the sacred circle, to have your picture taken. Even if you're not a country music fan, it's a fun experience.

Gorgeous new bar, decent spirits list, helpful staff. A little "hipster meets country chic" vibe here. 

When we were here I sort of felt like it was a bit of a tourist trap, but the food and drink selection was nice and it was swankier than other bars and restaurants I visited on my trip.

There was definitely a ton of attention paid to the decor and every detail here. Heck, I think you even have to be good looking to work here! But I suppose that's all a part of the experience. The space is cool, the employees are cool, and so you feel cool.

Plenty of room for small groups, large groups, private parties, or just a nook to snuggle up in with a date for a drink and a bite. If Portland and Beverly Hills had a baby, it'd be at Nashville at Music City Tipler. Hip, but almost to the point that it felt like they were trying just a smidge too hard.

If you're not into country music or are looking for a change, BB King's is a great place to grab a bite to eat and enjoy live music.  You can make a reservation or just walk right in.  We were seated at a table front and center.  This was great other than we couldn't carry on a conversation until the music stopped.  Something to think about when coming with a group and if there are any people in your group that are hard of hearing.  Not the clubs fault, just advising any future patrons.  Our waiter was relatively new but he did a great job.  He was attentive and when the music was playing, he wrote down what he was saying so we knew what was being said.  Smart!!  Maybe supply your wait staff with small marker boards.  Would be a funny, and smart way to communicate with your customers while the music is playing.  Would definitely help alleviate frustration and the continual "what?" when the music is going. They food here was great with several options to choose from.  There is bound to be something for everyone in your group.  Great change from the traditional country bars.

There are tons of drink to choose from. My brother in law is a regular so he took us here. 

The sight is very unique. A beer enthusiast should visit this place and learn about all the saucers on the wall. You'll be entertained.  

My fav is the appetizer; chicken snack with the mojo spice. Those who enjoy the heat should totally get the mojo spice. It is tender and the fries are definitely a hit at our table. 

We ordered a pizza, but i had better. They don't really have much choice or selection for my personal liking (the only reason I gave them 4 stars). 

It is family friendly place, but they clearly want anyone under the age of 21 to not be in their premises after 7pm. Which is a good thing. Just heads up for those bringing kids there.
Recent trip to the Opry was a nice outing. It is a bit pricey for the tour le gth but the tour guides were plentiful and knowledgeable and friendly.

If you are a Jack White fan, or simply into vinyl records, this is a great, albeit small, retail store to visit. White Stripes, Dead Weather and Jack's other bands are represented. There is a recording booth, and predictable novelties and tshirts for sale (better quality than most). Crowded both times I visited, a mecca for local aspiring rock musicians and fans, on skid row, street parking can be a block or more away.

Loved this place, we went on a Monday afternoon and even though the place was not very busy and no live music the food was excellent!  I had the chicken sandwich and it had great flavor and was very juicy and fresh!  French fries were excellent too!  Price was very reasonable.  I would be sure to go back

So disappointed - the experience was just plain awful. Eight of the ten performers were "has beens" that could barely sing. I really don't know how The Opry stays in business if this is the show every Saturday night! I'm sorry I spent my money and time on this event.

Interesting place that is definitely worth a visit. The atmosphere inside is fun and rather cozy. However I would not return as I can cook much better food really, the staff (or the waitress who helped us) was not that fantastically cheerful and friendly, and the music the night I visited B.A.D was, ehem, awkward. 
Overall, it's a pretty cool place for hanging out with your friends, grabbing a quick bite on a whimsical, random night out.
Had so much fun here I wish I had started out here in the first place bc the drinks were awesome and had a great atmosphere! Very friendly bartenders too!

The mac and cheese didn't live up to the hype! But i am glad i tried it. It was good, but I've definitely had better. I enjoyed the live music. Very chill and laid-back vibe. Not overcrowded when I was there. Over all I had a good time with good food and even better laughs with friends.

What an amazing place. The details in each corner will catch your eye. What surprised me the most is that it didn't matter if you were Dolly Parton or Carrie Underwood, each star comes in the same door.  The dressing rooms were very nice yet smaller than I assumed they would be.  The history was very interesting. The tour is $20 and well worth. Can't wait to come back to catch a show.

Been coming here for years and always order the same dish.  Was very surprised and disappointed not to find the Bourbon Salmon.  Bring back the Bourbon Salmon, PLEASE!  It was the best meal in So bro!
We are havin' some fun listening to Grant Garland and eating some GREAT food! And, the service was flawless. Ask for Tre!

Best spot ever on a Sunday! The Spazmatics were performing and football was on! The staff is very attentive and friendly. This place gets packed, and is a lot of fun! The food is good bar food and the drinks are cheap! We visited this bar twice while in Nashville for the weekend, great discovery!

This place isn't really my scene, but decided to check it out w friends. I thought it was professionally run, well staffed (almost overkill), and is a big space w decent decor. They made me take off my lid, which is fine, but then I saw several guys w hats. So...I'd encourage them to have consistency w the rules.
