Once again I start a review with "I'm not a country fan, but..." when in Nashville, right? Some of my family ARE country fans and were stoked to get tickets ot the Grand Ole Opry, and as it's a Nashville must-do, my sister, husband, and I reluctantly got tickets to the Friday night show. I wasn't expecting to enjoy myself that much, but I was pleased to find out the whole show was only a couple of hours. I could endure that.

Some acts were not so good, but some were absolutely amazing. I wish I remembered some of the names, but there were a few that weren't really country music and just good pop.

Amazingly, the standout was the radio announcer who just had the perfect voice. We all enjoyed listening to his commercials, and we especially enjoyed Riders in the Sky as one of the guys messed with him during a commercial.

I took my son and my wife here, both of them grew-up in Europe and are not familiar with Country Music or  Country Music legends. Not only did we go to the show, but we also did the back stage tour. I would highly recommend that if you spend the time to come to Nashville to catch a show, try and go on the back stage tour as well. You get a real good look at how things are done back stage and you get a real good understanding of American Country Music. If I go back to Nashville, I would spend the money and time to go on the tour again. 
We stayed at the at the Gaylord Hotel next door. It was very convenient to just walk over to the Grand Ole Opry.
Awesome beer, great place to bring your dog to hang out too. Cool part of town.

This was one of the best experiences ever.  We ha we all grown up
With hearing "she played at the Grand Ole Opry, yet we didn't truly know what that meant.  

Randy Travis showed up last night....just because he wanted to.  Josh Turner was the headline and he was fantastic as expected. 

Book on trip advisor!' We had great seats.

This is a must must must.

Such a great experience in the Nashville area. If you've never been, I encourage it! If you're planning a trip to Nashville, schedule it in! The lineup was somewhat disappointing for the evening I attended (all classic country and a few unknowns) but it was such a neat experience to be a part of the well-known Grand Ole Opry! The balcony has awesome seats!

This review only pertains to my experience with the atmosphere, staff, and bar - not the food. I think some of the drinks are a little overpriced but that's any bar downtown. Regardless, the bartender, the host, and the servers were really nice. I love the atmosphere and this is a great place to listen to some good music while eating fried pickles. The decor in the entire restaurant is awesome and it reflects the other sister locations for this restaurant.
Great service. Food tasted like a frozen TV dinner. Was missrable. The hot Pretzel is the only food worth eating.

My daughter and I are celebrating her 16th birthday in Nashville, we came to BB King's because we went to one in New Orleans and the food was amazing. Some things to consider at the Nashville location, we arrived Friday night around 6:30 pm there was a $5 cover per person to get in, we were only there for dinner. But there was live music so understandable. The menu was minimal compared to the New Orleans location. The food was just good! I had a Nashville hot sandwich and she had the blackened catfish.

This place is the bomb. Good food, music, and attractive waitresses. A little loud, but hey it's a bar right? 

The food is banging especially the rocket tots and the giant pretzels (make sure to get the queso dipping sauce). The beer selection so extensive, literally a giant black board full of beer selections. Although, I can't speak to much for the beer because I am 18, but my mom is obsessed and is halfway to getting a plate on the wall (200 beers). This place is also vegetarian friendly, for a while my favorite thing on the menu was the garden burger. 

If you are a hipster like me and can't stand pop music but is bored by classic rock, this place is also for you. They have played Passion Pit, Lorde, Mumford and Sons, Florence and the Machine, and the Caesars since I've been here (it feels like I handed my iPod to the bartender). 

The waitresses can be a little slow, but if you're not in a hurry it's not a problem, more time for talking (which we could all use). Also if you have kids get in before 9 because they start to card. I'm on a cross-country road trip and it is nice to know there is a quality chain I can count on for sweet food. Check it out!
Great music.  Horrific wait times for drinks.  It's like they don't even want to sell the stuff.  Back bar closed on a Friday night?

Do you like beer? Do you like trying many different kinds of beer (they have over 250 different beers and not always the same ones) and branching out beyond Bud Light? If so, you should go to Flying Saucer. You wouldn't know it, but it is a chain. I admittedly have never eaten anything here (that I can remember), but I do enjoy having beer here. If I lived closer I'd even try to get myself a saucer on the wall (or ceiling). You can do this by drinking so many beers. Of course, in one visit you can only have two beers go towards the saucer (no drunk driving, people!). I actually know someone that did this! He has a saucer on the ceiling!

The service here is always great. Our server last time really enjoyed Chris' Mr. Meeseeks shirt and even did an impression (Rick and Morty fans).

First time there, not impressed won't be back. 
Prices are way too high for hot dogs. The column of the tv or music was way too loud. 
Not as clean as I thought a restaurant should be..

Unreal is the word I would use! I dropped in here by chance because I was at the museum next door and was starving looking for a good place for lunch. Thank god I did because it was one of the best places I have eaten at in the city! I got Two Pretzels to start and the Duke Burger and would 10/10 recommend! A lot of good beer on tap to boot

This is absolutely the worst bar on Broadway.  I went on Monday night and the bouncer was extremely rude.  He is chubby, tall, has dark hair and a beard and watch out for this guy.  He was extremely unprofessional, sexist, and rude, he hit on my friend and also smelled horrible.  This guy was clearly proud to be a jerk bouncer, and then once we were into the bar he kept coming in and harassing us more until we left even though his job is clearly to stand at the door and check people's IDs.  There are a lot of fun bars on Broadway, but save your time and go anywhere but here (I recommend Coyote Ugly personally.)
Best bachelorette party activity in Nash! Christina and joe are the best! Great time and so much fun. Worth it for sure

Nice enough, but when you have to tip the DJ $20 just to get to sing, you begin to believe it is all a big racket.  If you want to sing in this bar, you better bring a lot of cash, cause that is what it takes to get on stage.

Great sports bar with tons of TV's and decent food. What sets the Dawghouse apart from any other typical sports bar is The Spazmatics every Sunday from 4-7. These guys put on the best show bar none that you will see if you love 80s music
Good place to catch great acts. I have seen the likes of Blake Shelton, Keith Urban, Kellie Pickler, Kree Harrison and more and it is so cool seeing them in a smaller (not arena size) venue.

Went here to listen to a friend play live. The space was small and cozy, but around the bar area to the bathrooms was a little close for comfort. I had a bacon cheese burger and was very pleased with it. The pepper jack cheese was extra spicy, and the bacon was cooked to perfection. I loved the bun that it came on. The fries were common but a bit over cooked. I will definitely be back for the live music, but I'll try the coleslaw on my next visit.

My wife and I did a backstage tour Sep 1. We were celebrating my 70 birthday. The tour was fine. At the end of the tour you are brought on stage to have your picture taken standing in the "Circle of Honor" So that is nice. Of course the picture is $25, but to be expected. Here is the part the basically sucks - try and get the picture digitally. They say they will send it to your email. Good Luck with that. They send an email, which requires you to set up an account for them to send you an endless stream of irritating promotional emails. 
On top of that, I forgot my password when I got home and had to request  they send another one, which didn't happen. So bottom line I can't get the picture digitally - despite paying the $25 fee. 
In short - very irritating!! So be advised. 
Garth Hoffmann
TOUR TAKEN SEP 1, 2019

Our family had a positive experience at BB King's. We made a reservation with open table and had no trouble. The music was good and there was a large dance floor. The menu was not what I'm used to and felt a little challenging but I had the chicken fried chicken and it was amazing on a bed of Mac and cheese. The fried pickles were amazing. My brother in law enjoyed the ribs. My mom in law liked the skillet shrimp appetizer. Over, a good meal. 
The server we had was very friendly. The restaurant seemed understaffed for a Saturday night. Service was slow. We had plastic silverware which was also strange for a place where food isn't cheap. My fork broke as I tried to eat my chicken. 
But, it's a fun vibe and we enjoyed the atmosphere.
Great music and atmosphere. We had a blast some of the best music on Lower Broadway.  We had so much fun listening to music all afternoon

We had a great time here! The duo who were playing really interacted with the crowd, shared a few stories and really entertained the crowd. The bartender was friendly and efficient.
Seating was a huge issue downstairs. We tried 2 different tables by the dance floor and they both were super wobbly. Just impossible to put a drink down without being fearful of a huge spill. We opted for the bar. 
We decided to stop back in near the end of our day since we enjoyed ourselves so much the first time. A different band playing and now there was more people standing than sitting. Still great service. Never made it upstairs. Bathroom is nothing to write home about but you can't expect much more from this place. For what we spent for 3 mixed drinks and 4 beers I'm sure I've provided you means to fix a couple tables.

My sister and I traveled to Nashville recently and took are Mom and Dad. We had a blast at Redneck Riviera and especially loved the rooftop area.  The staff was amazing and the band was fabulous. You've got to try the Frozen Bushwackers!

Very pretty place!   LOVE the decor, the waitstaff was very kind, and my food was very yummy! (I am a tomato bisque snob) 

I am from out of town and only came for lunch - would definitely come back at night.

There so many different selection of beers. What really caught my eye was the Kombucha beer which was very tasty. I also ordered their wings tossed in mojo cajun spice with buffalo and blue cheese dip on the side. I can't wait to come try some more brews!

Wow, of all places where music is King, I would think that those working the venue should show proper respect to both the performers and audiences and not talk loudly when the paying public attends a performance. Whether these people paid or volunteers, they need retraining!!!
Really ruined the experience for many of the patron sitting near us
A ton of fun!  Even got last minute tickets. A fun piece of history here.  Great sound!  Nice little gift shop inside too.

The service was appalling. Dishes from the previous guests sat on our table the entire time we were there. Even when our food was brought out, we told the person that this large pile of dishes were not ours...he just said, "oh ok" and then walked away.  Our server was extremely overwhelmed, in fact our appetizer came after we had all finished our meals. There was absolutely no air and the manager refused to open the garage doors to let in fresh air. We were only there for The Office trivia night but we will never ever be back and I will encourage people to skip this restaurant. The food was overpriced for food that's only ok. Definitely not up to Nashville standards!

One of the best places to see Live music in the country  - This is a bluegrass lovers dream venue. Old Crow Medicine show last year was incredible - What Yankee stadium is to baseball is what The Grand Ole Opry is to Live music!

Unfortunately, our bachelorette party had a really bad experience the bartenders were rude and would not serve us unless we moved to the middle of the bar. A member of our group opened "the unlocked cage" to look at shirts. The bartender finalllyyy made her way to that side of the bar where she apprended the shirt and made an accusation of stealing essentially. Explained the situation and was not taken well by the staff. When speaking to the "manager" he stated "I don't care about you or your lesbian friends". Only friendly face was the DJ who apologized multiple times for the incident (he saw entire thing).

I love Belcourt Taps! It has a great atmosphere, the bartenders are always friendly, and they do a lot for the music community. You never know who you'll see playing there. Could be a new young song writer or someone who wrote for George Strait. 
It's always a judgement free, fun place to be.

The Grand Ole Opry House is home to the longest running radio show. It currently airs weekly and is no stranger to Country Music's most iconic artists. It is often hailed as "The Mother Church of Country Music". To be invited to become a member of The Grand Ole Opry is one of the highest, of not the highest honor for Country Music stars. This Nashville native HIGHLY recommends you catch a tour prior to your evening show at the Opry House!

This was a quant performance hall, so intimate, not matter where your seat was it was a good seat. Beautiful architecture, lots of history and the sound was amazing from the performer. It WS very intimate and personal, such a great theater

Just FYI... The kitchen is not open until 11pm on Sat. like stated on their website!
FAIL!!

We visited the OprY House for the 50th Dolly Parton celebration. Our tickets were for the 9:30pm show. The earlier show was at 7:00pm. We arrived at 8:15pm and along with hundreds of other excited fans, stood outside in line until 9:45pm. That's when the last of the 7pm show audience left allowing us access. Unforunantly there were several older folks having to stand for a long period of time before entry. Those around us were complaining out loud. Personally this was poor planning on the shows producers on setting the two shows. Once inside the auditorium it was nice and historical. The concessions were very limited on food and beverages. I'd go back. Just plan on standing in one of your there for the second show in the same day.
The 9 o'clock round was the one to see and somehow got gypped because the round before ran late

Stay away from the mac and cheese!!! Ive been having great foods in the vicinity here in Nashville and figured this place has a great bartender/Staff for drinks so lets try the food...  I saw the menu and it had the choice of macaroni... brisket beef , pork or chicken... chose the pork... pork was ok... mac was wth!? Kraft type mac n cheese...? Really?!‍ literally that mac was straight out the box!? I would have expected the creamy goodness that the South provides freely through its comfort foods... but this was no comfort! This was Monsanto! Please stay away from the mac...unless yer looking for that good box flavor... cause thats not the price I would be charging for kraft type mac... yeek! Just saying cause if ya dont know, ya need to know..

They play good music but keep your check if you pay with a debit/credit card. I left a cash time but paid my tab with my debit card. Bartender decided to put an extra tip for himself so instead of paying $34 for 4 lemon drop shots, I paid $41 plus the cash tip I left him. Not happy about that one bit. But I'll just have to pay cash from here on out when I go to this bar.

This was an enjoyable show to see live.  The show lasted about 2 hours, and we saw about 12 performers in that 2 hours.  We got a discount of $2/ticket for being AAA members.  I would highly recommend going to the Grand Ole Opry, especially if you've never been there before.

Went today for lunch and didn't have such a great experience.  Overcooked chicken fingers, two were not even edible just chunks of fried yuk, and my co-worker got the chili and said that was poor too.  Great place to drink beer and play trivia, but probably won't be back for food anytime soon.

In Nashville for NYE.  I'm a wing snob.  Decided to try this place based on the menu.   Buffalo wings were excellent!   I always order extra crispy and extra wet.  Cooked perfectly.   Moderate heat but good flavor.  Nice atmosphere.   Tons of beers!!

My family members are not country music fans, but this was great! Each artist did three songs.  Some bluegrass, some traditional country, some gospel, some new country.  Wednesday night summer show was a good value with really good seats available directly from the Opry.  It is a stage show and a radio show.  A nice way to sample great performers.  We all agree we would do it again and it was a major highlight of our trip.  As someone once told me, always see the best at something do what they do best, even if you are not sure you'll like it; you won't be disappointed and might find you like it after all.

The atmosphere, music, location, and food was all perfect! Really, really great!! The only reason I'm giving four stars instead of five is because of our waiter. First he came up to my boyfriend and I and said "Hi ladies!" As soon as he looked up he realized she was a he LOL but he never apologized which I thought was rude. He also seemed to have forgot about us towards the end. But the tables are really uniquely painted and the decorations are neat! Hefty bill but what do you expect? My boyfriend also got a complimentary souvenir beer glass since he ordered a tall beer! I'd definitely return.

The Flying Saucer is a personal favorite of mine and this location kept the bar high. This is the 3rd one I've been to and I can't complain about a single thing.

The beer selection is top notch and the prices are very reasonable.  The food is excellent for bar food. I tried something different each night I was here and enjoyed everything I ate from the Build Your Own Pie to the Sheboygan Side By Side. The Rocket Tots were my favorite but I really could go on and on about their food.

One thing I like most about the Flying Saucer is the excellent service I have always received.  The beer goddesses are extremely knowledgeable, polite, friendly and quick.

I love this place because they have yet to disappoint me and that's probably because they have a delicious beer selection, great food, fair prices and top notch service!

Our tour guide, Lara, was phenomenal. You get the opportunity to tour through one of country music's greatest auditoriums - including going backstage through the artist entrance, viewing the dressing rooms, and even getting your photo taken on stage within the "circle." It was a highlight of our trip to Nashville!
Loved our time in Nashville, and this happened to be our first club we went into.  Charged 11.25% on drinks.  No other club  charged this amount!

Sat at the bar for 15 minutes. Made eye contact with bartender and waved down many times after being ignored to try to get my first drink of the night. The bartender deliberately served all the women around me while knowing I was waiting for a drink for 15 minutes.  So I Left. Yeah you, black plugs, black hat backwards with tats up your arms. Your the worst. Your also the slowest bartender I've seen on broadway.

Also, half full bar and karaoke host over inflated time to sing to receive tips for getting a faster sing time. This place is a joke.

Amazing experience that everyone should have at least once! Venue is very easy to get to as far as parking and entering/exiting the building. Our seats were in Section 15, Row Z, which is the last row on the floor level, and we still had a great view. Definitely recommend for anyone visiting Nashville.

This place was so awesome.  We had a large party and we were taken care of.  The staff was friendly and respectful.  There was live music.  And the food was amazing.  5 out of 5 for sure.  Did not disappoint.

The term "hidden gem" is used quite a bit for places on a city that aren't very well known to the visitors, but they are to the locals.  This is definitely it!

Very cool vibe on a, well, back ally by the Arcade.  

I got a Mega Titan burger and two BearWalkers for $18.  Pretty good!

The burger is very good!  It's not the best in town, but it's certainly a great burger.  This place had locals night, songwriters night, daily and nightly specials, and everyone from 21 to 81, unemployed to working professional frequents this place!  Must try!
My go-to place for a solid lunchtime Burger downtown. Just be sure to show up early during lunch to ensure you can get a table.

Entertainment was good. It had a rustic feel. The wings were okay. The drinks were good but the new bartender gave my husband a top shelf margarita with a gin base instead of tequila and it was terrible. But other than that the server was nice and the music was on point. I love live bands with people who can sing instead of screaming.

Great place to hang and drink beer! 
The Flying Saucer is historic and filled with a great casual and fun environment. All my friends and I go in on Monday.
Why Monday? Monday is Pint Nite!
On Pint Nite, almost all beers are only 3 bucks. I have been doing this for the past 2 years and probably have tried over 100+ beers through this place!
They also have a "UFO club" that helps you track what beers you have drank and lets you work towards a goal of 200 beers. Once you get there, you get a reward, but not quite sure what the reward is. 
The food here, however, is pretty meh. On Wednesdays, they do half off food, but its really not special. 

Overall, great place to hang and drink beer, alright place to eat food. Enjoy!

The music was great, but the service was slow and the food was meh. I ordered the chicken fried chicken and the chicken was delicious, but the vegetables (squash, zucchini and carrots) very mushy. It also came with "baked" Mac and cheese. I have never been so disappointed. It definitely was not baked and it tasted like melted American cheese.

The Jalapeno Poppers at B.A.D. were delicious and the martinis were also great! I loved the hummus plate and pita chips as well! B.A.D. was my favorite place to visit, with the live music, and relaxed decor B.A.D was a great place to hang out any day of the week! Service was great as well and as the night went on it felt like everyone who was dining or drinking was hanging out together and interacting with the live musician. I would recommend B.A.D. to anyone visiting the Nashville area.

Perfect spot to go before the Frist Museum. All taps are $4 from 4-7, M-F. 

Sweet Tea is a doll and very knowledgeable about the exhibits at the museum.

We absolutely loved attending the Grand Ole Opry House.  We added a tour of the backstage area.  I would encourage you to add this tour to your package.  The seats at the show are just a wood bench (like in an old church). There are numbers on the top part of the wood to identify where you are to sit.  The benches did have a cushion.  If you are looking to see a big act, check out Tuesday night. The big acts make their money on weekends.  If you have never heard the type of music they have, download the app for Grand Ole Opry and enjoy!

Work travel brought me here, did not feel weird being by myself which can sometimes happen. Staff was very friendly, the food was good-chicken philly with chips, the beer was great- Jackalope Bearwalker Maple Brown, and I wasn't surrounded by obnoxious, drunk tourists. All in all I was very happy.

Seeing a show was not part of our plan for our 3 days in Nashville, but we survived our Wyndham timeshare presentation and in turn got cheap tickets to the show with Sara Evans the following night. Many headliners including Sam Williams and Don Schlitz. Being Dolly Week they all sang a song of Dolly's or for Dolly. We enjoyed every performance though not super into country music. Sara Evans only sang 3 songs so that was a letdown but overall amazing night and show. Whole show was 7-9:30.

We would likely pay the reg price for tickets next time. There are no bad seats in the house and it's bench seating. Outside there is seating and large guitars you can take photos with and food/drink trucks if you need a bite to eat. 

The mall is directly across so we parked there free. Mission bbq is awesome food nearby too. We did not do a tour but it might be interesting as well.

This bar was the best spot for locals to go, however, the new manager has no idea what the Nashville bar scene is like.  Dawg House was known for their bartenders / service but once new management took over they all left.  The new GM is very rude, not friendly, and has ran this bar to the ground.  This is no longer a bar that is desirable for locals to go to.

AMAZING!  The venue of new artists, local/regional artists, and the legendary artists are a good mix for everyone. 

I would recommend doing the backstage TOUR after a concert so you can see allot of the bells and whistles while their are people and artists still around.

Literally patronize this place all the time. And THIS is what they give me. This basket is supposed to be full of fries and they gave me whatever scraps they had left. Wont be recommending to any of my friends because as loyal as I was to B.B. kings, they were disloyal in customer satisfaction. If you do right by the customer, the customer will do right by you. Literally, what's difficult to understand about this?
The food is always awesome! Keith is always super friendly, and definitely my go to lunch spot!
Gumbo was super yummy, and we split the BBQ salmon. . Amazing flavors....big and the live music great fun!!! They have it all.

Very below average food I had  the BBQ Pork and Chicken sandwiches. Bland no real flavor definitely not soul food that I wanted to experience. The music saved this from being a 1 star cause my bartender was rude and seemed angry that I showed up in the first place
If you're looking for overpriced food with no taste then you've found the right spot.

Really enjoyed this venue. The singers sang 2 songs each so if you didn't like a singer, it wasn't long before they changed. It had bench style seating, but I wished it had individual seats. The benches made my back hurt. They served food and beverages which was really nice.

Staff at the door was super friendly but we weren't 100% impressed.

The place reeked of smoke, so if this bothers you, it's not the place for you. 

It's a karaoke bar... We got up to sing karaoke, but when we can back, all our drinks had been cleared at the table we were at and were forced to buy new ones. What a rip off! Seemed like a scam to get you to spend more money. 

It was fun as a one-time spot but I don't think I'd frequent here regularly.

What can I say? It's the Grand Ole Opry, it's historic and I'm so honored to have been able to experience a performance at the venue. From the minute you walk in you can tell how incredibly important this venue is, not only to Nashville, but to country music as a whole. Before the concert they played a moving video on the history of the Grand Ole Opry and the significance of performing there and it was great to see.

In addition to that, there are NO bad seats in this venue at all. Seriously! Any where you sit in the venue you will have a fantastic view of the stage. Once you're seating down prepare yourself for a mind-blowing performance because it seems like everyone who performs here is completely proud to play here and will give you one HELL of a performance. So happy to have been a witness to this and be able to mark this off my bucket list.

After reading all the reviews from the groupon purchases I ignored my instincts and tried it anyways. Lesson learned now. The place is quaint and the service was good but beyond that it sucked. Maybe two out of the ten beers was decent the others were awful tasting and were not even worth drinking. We also got pretzels with the groupon. My husband had the plain pretzel which was decent but a little dry. I had the garlic parmesan which was awful,they used garlic powder for flavoring and gave you a dipping side which tasted like a garlic vinaigrette dressing and it was also dry and over cooked. Next time I will listen to my instinct and not make bad groupon purchases. :(

DESTROYED MY PROPERTY!!! The worst experience I've ever had at a bar in Nashville. "Manager" was unapologetically rude and service was terrible. I wish I could give this place a negative star. Avoid at all costs. They damaged my personal property by tampering with my driver license to the point where I will now have to get it replaced. This place will pull the laminate off your license! BEWARE!

The grand ole opry house is a must see when you come to Tennessee. Our roots can be found here whether it's through dancing or the sounds of country music. Be sure to wear cowboy boots when you're attending a show

We were on our Honeymoon. However we went on 9/11. Very patriotic. I think maybe we should've thought about what day it was. There was a lot of recognition which is wonderful for all the men and women who serve us. But I would've liked to have seen something a little more upbeat and a little less sad for our occasion. Be prepared to park far and walk. The Opry done a wonderful job in respecting all of our military and the families who have or are serving the USA. It was neat to see where so many wonderful people made their start. The staff was helpful and friendly.

Great place to stop by, specially if you are with your kids, we definitely had so much fun at this place!
We'll definitely coming back lol

You have to take this place for what it is... it's basically a redneck bar and proud of it.

I popped by for some drinks and to listen to some music. Both were great and the service was swift.

Warning: If you're looking to have an intimate conversation, this is not the place... downstairs is as loud as hell, but hey... that's what your here for.

The establishment is located at the center of where you want to be on Broadway.
I hear they never run out of jello shots!  Nothing like running a promotion that fails so miserable.
Took in a grand ole Opry show. 2 + solid hours of great country music.  Simply a must do if visiting Nashville.

The Carl Stewart band was great. He is such a pro ! But the young Chef was the real surprise!  We got the catfish and shrimp platter. The fish was lightly battered and lightly fried to perfection. None of this overly battered stuff. Very tasty and not heavy. The young guy is also a real pro.Raquel was a friendly server too!

First time visiting, this was such an incredible experience. The history behind the building is so perfectly preserved, and there is a ton of memorabilia scattered throughout the house. I was expecting something totally different, but from looking around, I don't think there is a seat in the house that would be a "bad seat". The sound is incredible and the building has a natural acoustic feature so it really allows the audience to hear the sound perfectly without flaw. The bands were incredible, and everyone was so friendly! There is a gift shop with tons of different souvenirs you can buy for yourself and others. So blessed to have been able to experience this and make something off my bucket list as well as see Mason Ramsey live! Thank you for being so inviting!

I entered a world I did not know existed anymore. 
First of all, apparently they do a simulcast on am radio. If you are under the age of 60, as I am, you may not know that am radio exists. Apparently, it still does. 
Each 30-minute segment is bookended with two solid full minute commercials for crappy restaurants and health insurance companies spoken by a deep-voiced announcer, who is not doing this ironically. They are hosted by an octogenarian who makes the kind of jokes one remembers from watching Lawrence Welk with your long-dead grandmother. 
My experience started with a number by said octogenarian mc, followed by a trio of women in their late 60s accompanied by their father who made jokes about how he was saddled by having all girls. Apparently something he hasn't gotten over in 60 plus years. Why? Because girls statistically succeed more than boys in 2018? I suppose they wouldn't know that given their advanced age. 
Their number was followed by another octogenarian guy who wrote some song I think I've heard before about being a piece of coal but could be a diamond, his drunken rambling, his next incoherently slurred song and his drunken exit. 
The mc then did a spoken word number, with backup singers who struggled to hold a tune on a countryfied hymnal, which honestly could be a regular SNL skit. 
Closing out this set was the Opry square dancers, a medium meant for radio - like Irish step dancing without the choreography. 
The final set was mc'd by an octogenarian woman who made weirdly sexual jokes, which was not at all like my long dead grandmother watching Lawrence Welk. 
She introduced a heavily made-up, bleached blonde who told a story about now she'd come to Nashville and tended bar, then sang a song that she wrote (but did not play any instrument on) about being a pretend friend as a bartender. 
The female octagenarian mc sang two songs that were not sung particularly well. Then she introduced a hunk who she made more sexual jokes about and said we'd know better as so and so. I assumed from the show Nashville, which I have never seen. Some people screamed but 2/3 of the audience was bewildered. He wasn't very good.
All and all it was a worthless overpriced terrible show. On a Saturday night they didn't have anyone worth seeing in the whole show and format made it unwatchable. I would never do this again.

Very fun blues club. The bands we saw there were awesome, playing songs like "Soul Man" and "Superstitious". We had the bbq plate (which was excellent, better than Jacks BBQ down the street) and the Cajun carbonara. The place was packed, but service was still fast and friendly. I recommend this place if you are looking for a change of music from most the honky tonks.

Literally the most racists  establishment I've ever been to. Dave Griffith is the main culprit and is a terrible human being. Because you manage a bar doesn't mean you get to discriminate against people you don't care for in a bar. Thanks for judging your actions on someone's skin color! Classy!

What a nice place ! We scheduled an impromptu last minute night out to the GOO and were not disappointed. This place is pure class. A full evening of entertainment. Lots of history. And very well decorated. Spend the money, see the show, love the history. It's worth it.

Ryman Theatre
3:30 show
Great time!
Freezing cold outside (wait)
Dustin Lynch & Schonda Pierce and others Great!
Cost worth it. But was our most expensive adventure in Nashville. (Besides parking $$$)

Monday is pint night, Tuesday is trivia, Wednesday take home a glass from your favorite brewery, Thursday is American pint night, Sunday is local draft night. Always and occasion to drink at the Saucer. Make sure your beers count for something and join the UFO club! Nothing like having a plate (or 7) on the wall!
AVOID AVOID AVOID. Do yourself a favor and walk passed this place. How dare the owner even have the guts to call someone a he/she. Isn't this 2015? And isn't this Nashville?

Stopped in for drinks after our dinner and the atmosphere is great. Its loud with a great DJ. Not a place to go if you want a drink and visit but if your there to drink and let lose this is the spot for sure. We will be back.

Great food and great atmosphere. Live music too. We came here for lunch while in Nashville and this was one of my favorite places. 
Great old building that is perfect for a blues club. 
This will be one I return to any time I'm in Nashville.

After being asked by Back Alley Diner to revise my review, I checked their site again and it does state their hours are until 10pm for food on Sat. I must have read the incorrect hours on a different link. I could not remove my previous review for some reason... Only update it. I never got a chance to eat here but I've heard it is good.
Great food and even better music with Mike Hayes Band.  Ribs just fell off the bone and fried chicken fabulous!

We caught a show here and we were lucky enough to do a backstage tour and we got to go on stage! This venue is an institution and has featured just about every name in country music. The people who run this place are very passionate about what they do. It's a must do in Nashville!

In town for the week and heard that we needed to see a show over here. The experience was like no other. So many different acts in 2 hours. Never grew up a country fan, but this gave me such a new appreciation of the genre. By far the coolest thing I have done in Nashville and a must for anyone.

Nice tour, learned a lot about the new Opry House which used to be the Ryman Auditorium. Can get your photo in the circle too which was a really fun experience. Loved seeing all the different dressing rooms and mailboxes for the members.

Avoid this place. Would I've it zero stars if I could. MC was obviously more interested in playing songs for his friends than the actual paying customers. We saw numerous round of MC's friends come in after us and have their songs played while our songs were never played. Much better places to spend your money.

The Grand Ole Opry is an amazing entertainment venue, and a great value!  Buy your tickets online and arrive a couple of hours early.  (By getting there early, you'll get a great parking place!)  Then, you can putter around the Opry Hotel and try one of its fabulous restaurants, browse the boutiques, or just take in the beautiful scenery.  After dinner, it's just a short walk to the theater for the performance.  

There are a few things you need to know about the theater:  You will be sitting on a very long "church pew."  A number corresponding to your ticket is affixed every ~30" or so on the back of the "pew."  The ushers will cram every single ticket holder into that pew, whether your "back-side" is 30" or not.  There was a young woman in front of me who, (bless her heart,) was trying her best to squeeze her ample proportions into her allotted space.  She was perched on the end of the seat with her shoulders hunched for the entire performance.  It looked very uncomfortable.

Another thing... make sure to use the restroom and limit your beverages before the show because crawling over a dozen or so laps to get out is like an Inuit test of manhood.  

If you can deal with the seating issues, you will have a BLAST!  You MUST make plans to go to the Opry if you are going to be anywhere near Nashville.

Whole headed to the west coast I stopped at the grand ole to see some of the Greats. It was a nice introduction click tou see when your first go for the.guided tour. You are showed all the dressing room and back stage where the artist enter the stage. Ot was great getting tour. I thought the auditorium was bigger than it was but its still holds a good crowd. Alright before the tour is over you get to take a pick on stage on the piece of wood and at the microphone. I asked everyone that was on the tour with me to take a pic for my journey to Phoenix archives. They did and I was thankful!

The food was good, but the service was terrible. This is the kind of bar were the servers spend more time flirting with female patrons and ignoring the men. On a slow Sunday evening, we waited 10 minutes before we asked to see menus, then another 15 minutes before or orders were taken. There are a bunch of other restaurants in the area (had they been open, we would have left), spend your time elsewhere.

Absolute GEM of a honky tonk!

This small place definitely has a more cozy, intimate feel than the other spots along Broadway, but that makes for a great interactive music experience. 

If have the pleasure of stopping by on a weekend to see Noah Garner, you're in for one hell of a show (dancing on the bar included!). Ladies--you'll fall in love. Gentlemen--watch your girls!

I found this lovely establishment by chance while looking for a place to eat dinner. Half price wings this Tuesday night so I definitely got myself some wings, but I also made sure to sample the BBQ pulled pork sandwich with baked beans. The wings were super crispy and were flavored with the traditional Nashville Hot Chicken seasoning. The exterior was dry, which was surprising, and the wings were super crispy. There was also a hint of sweet to them. The pork was delicious served with a side of BBQ sauce to go on my sandwich. The sandwich also had coleslaw and bacon on it. Everything is better with bacon. There was no imagination in the original bun. Wish I had something a little more like a hoagie roll for the bun but it still worked. 

The misstep of the evening was the mix up almost resulting in me not getting my wings. Thankfully that was quickly rectified. Would definitely come back and recommend to friends.

I'm not one to write negative reviews, but my experience here was pathetic enough to demand a bad one! Three of us went for a beer and food after a movie at Belcourt Theater (on Friday, Sept. 16.) The porch drew us to this charming looking place, but as we sat at one of the three occupied tables, the staff completely ignored us! Three times we tried to flag one of the two 'servers' that came outside to wait on the other two tables, and still, we were ignored. We felt that we were absolutely invisible, even after one server grabbed (yes, grabbed) the catsup off our table and walked away. We also sat with the dirty glasses and napkins from the previous patrons. (ie. the staff didn't even clear our table while we were there!) We quickly realized that, if we wanted anything, we would have to go inside to get it ourselves. We did....and still, continued to be invisible to the staff. 
The last straw was, when the other two tables of guests, left, and a server came out and literally started throwing furniture around the deck! He was banging, shoving, and loudly moving the tables and chairs back to their original places, without any regard for us. We immediately left!
We found Belcourt Taps to have such rude and unprofessional servers, and such terrible service, that we will absolutely NEVER step foot in there again. We were invisible and ignored the entire hour and a half we were there!! (If I could give them ZERO stars, I would!)

Loved the backstage tour. We had an excellent tour guide and seeing where the greatest country stars have freely roamed was awesome.  The Venue is in the middle of a shopping mall, so plan your day to come here early so you can head back to downtown for the rest of the day.

Ryman Theatre
3:30 show
Great time!
Freezing cold outside (wait)
Dustin Lynch & Schonda Pierce and others Great!
Cost worth it. But was our most expensive adventure in Nashville. (Besides parking)
A hint for parking - search public library parking building.  It is $14?for day.

There really isn't a bad seat in here. I had a great time here on a Saturday night. While the seats are pew style there was enough room between people. I liked the balcony view and while it doesn't allow for amazing pictures, at the Opry, no matter where you are sitting you are allowed to walk down to the stage and take photographs. I also took the backstage tour after the show. You can take pictures and get to see all the dressing rooms, the green room, go on stage and get pictures at the microphones, etc. Definitely a cool experience and a fun evening. Parking at the Opry can be far, but it is free. Arrive early and go check out the inside of the Opryland hotel. There are lots of restaurant options inside.

Super fun atmosphere and pretty good food! The fried pickles and mashed potatoes were yummy! The entertainment was fun and they played some old classics! Karaoke in the basement was really fun to watch, too!

Wasn't there long . Welcomed us in sat down at a table. Waited 10 minutes no one came to ask us for a drink or menu. Then went to the bar to order 2 drinks got carded . Didn't bring my ID in with me while we bar hop on Broadway. They wouldn't serve me because the State cracks down on them for under age drinking.  
I guess at 52 I must be looking really good.  lol 

The BB King in Memphis was so nicer than this place. 
So if you go to Broadway in Nashville , don't forget your ID

I was here recently with a group of work colleagues for dinner during some training in Nashville. I thought the food was pretty good for bar food (the primary offering is a selection of burgers, but they had great sides), and it's nice that they have the big patio for warm weather. Like most places in Nashville, they have live music, but I actually thought the venue was too small for the band they had. It's not a big location, and the music was pretty overwhelming. It's basically just one room (unless you go outside), so there was no place to escape the music and just talk with your party.

Overall, it was a success for our party (~20 people, and they let us stand around a group of tables for food and drinks), but I likely won't be going back on return trips to Nashville.

1. Very inattentive staff.   
2.  Hostess had no idea about anything to             do with the menu/music lineup/specials
3.  Food was just ok 
4.  Perfect place if you want some peace and quiet off of Broadway and if you don't mind the sloooow service; even when not busy.

Do not believe a word you are told by the Opry Call Center that sells tickets for performances at both the Ryman and the Opry House.  I was prepared to go in person to buy tickets, but I was assured by the sales person at the Opry Call Center that the price was exactly the same if our tickets were purchased from her over the phone.  And what convenience!!  She also offered to send our tickets by email 48 hr. before the show.  Apparently they lie their heads off and will say anything to make a sale.  We have not received our tickets and are now told that they do not have the capacity to send tickets by email.  We have other commitments before our concert and may be standing in the Will Call line or security line when our concert starts because we were lied to by  the Opry Call Center.

I heard of this place from a friend in Chicago. We live in Clarksville but didn't know there was a BB King's in Nashville. We went on a Sunday afternoon just in time to listen to Gil Gann playing blues. Plenty of seating available at 1230 pm so we sat by the stage. It was real cool watching live music this early. The food was good too. I had a Tuna Cobb Salad on spinach greens and my wife had catfish bites. Afterwards we walked down Broadway and noticed that every bar was rocking live music. An enjoyable experience.
Really neat place. It was busy because it was a holiday weekend when we stopped in but definitely worth checking it out. Really neat vibe with lots of cool things to check out.

Great music. Good food as you would expect...but buyer beware. Prices published on their menu is not what they charge.  Good wines advertised at $6 a glass are out of so they can get you to buy the actual house wine "Lucille" advertised at $6 but actually $8 a glass.

Stopped here for dinner. It was a $5 cover per person to enter for dinner. The staff was incredibly slow. There was next to no one here and it was surprising how slow and inattentive the staff actually was. We ordered two beers and a mixed drink and waited for almost 25 minutes to get them. 

We ordered two appetizers and again very slow service and once the expediter brought them to our table we didn't see the waiter again until the table next to ours was seated. At that point we request the bill and left.

Back Alley Diner was the first place we ate after arriving in Nashville. Starving, we wandered across the street from our hotel and happily stumbled onto this place! It was late afternoon, so our large party easily found a place to sit. Our server was very nice, though a member of our group didn't like her because she refused to serve him alcohol. I don't blame her at all because 1. We quickly found out that Nashville has very strict carding rules and 2. it's his own damn fault for having an expired ID. 

At first glance, B.A.D. looks grimy like the name implies, but it's actually kind of cute after you settle in and look around. I had the catfish po'boy, which came with hushpuppies and my choice of baked beans. Hello, delicious Southern food! The jam for the hushpuppies was a great addition, but I should have gotten fries instead of the beans. Beans were fine, but a taste of someone else's fries filled me with Fry Jealousy. Portions were generous and everyone at my table was very pleased with the food. 

B.A.D. isn't good enough to trek all over town for, but if you're close definitely check it out. And bring a current ID.

A must-stop shop while visiting from out of town if you love (1) music, (2) vinyl, (2) Jack White/White Stripes/Raconteurs/Dead Weather, (3) enjoy the symbolism of the number 3 (placement intentional).

We swung by right after they opened on a Sunday (10 am). To be candid, the area was a little sketchy as we drove up; lots of vagrant folks were meandering about nearby. Other reviewers didn't seem so kind to the area either, but we felt safe throughout.

This place is definitely unique from any other record store I've been to so far. Going in, you understand the connection to Jack White & his music (big fan), but also the other artists on their recording label (same name - Third Man) that continue to grow in number and stature. All of the vinyl they sell is exclusively Third Man releases, heavy on JW/WS reissues. I was hoping to find any Vault or other TMR exclusives (like the recent Cubs/Pearl Jam 45), but no dice. 

I found the store to be more of a museum than a traditional brick/mortar record store - tons to look at, investigate, and marvel. I sincerely appreciate their effort(s) to make this a one-of-a-kind shopping experience. We checked out the listening room/booth, while also envious of the recording station too. Lots of TMR merch, collectibles, and apparel to choose from if so inclined. We made a few smaller music selections and bought a store sticker (drats!). 

If you are a music enthusiast and vinyl lover/collector, I'd recommend stopping by, regardless of your musical tastes or the type of collector or stage in your collection you find yourself. It's not too far from Grimey's, either, so that is a plus. 

It's a very original place and I look forward to TMR releases in the future!

Our group hit this Karaoke bar on our last day in Nashville. It opened a little late but we listened to music next door until it opened. We had a blast singing and dancing the day away. The female DJ running karaoke was great and funny!
If you like karaoke stop by this place.

Was enjoying the place and then when we got up to watch my niece sing, they cleared our table, along with the kooxie that was on my beer. When we told them what happened, they denied that it happened. I found the koozie in the garbage and left, never to return.
This place has  great food, awesome sports bar and the hottest spot for Sunday Funday where you can find the fun 80s band Spazmatics.

Although the manager attempted to correct the poor service that was experienced, it was not enough to overcome the difficulties we experienced. 

The food and the ambiance was excellent, however the wait was ridiculous and the lack of staffing was an obvious issue without being disclosed. 

Be prepared to wait! Unfortunately, as a tourist, we were disappointed overall!

This place is just off Broadway.  While there is great country music on Broadway this offers live blues. It is not as crowded as all the other bars and has tables to sit and relax while listening to good music.

They had great bbq options including healthy options. I had blackened chicken salad and bbq pork tatchos. 

Services was good and fast. Grear art work of some of the greatest blues musicians.
Came here for lunch. love the ambiance. Brisket was a little dry and the BBQ sauce a little sweeter than I like, but otherwise very good.
Very fun night out. So many talented acts. Cassidy Pope was the main act. The opening acts out performed her. A must do when in Nashville!

Came on a Sunday morning for brunch.  The combination of an excellent live band and a good buffet puts this on the top of my list in Nashville.  
The buffet starts out as a regular Sunday brunch; made the way you like it omelette, bacon etc.  They add super fresh fruit, pulled pork, and BBQ ribs. Add a live band that played Blues  and Motown while we were munching away, and I'm a happy guy for the rest of the day.  
We'll be back!

visited BB King's Blues Club on a Wednesday night at around 6pm. At that time the band was perfect not too loud and played a collective of music styles. BB serves great local beers and the ribs are where it is at!!! Everything we had was good but the ribs will have you coming back. Plus the prices are on the lower end for Nashville

My grandmother and I were here for the day time tour of backstage.   Staff were very friendly, knowledgeable, and professional.  Our tour guide,  Kelly,  was great. You could feel the history and stepping stage was treat.  I'm not a huge country music fan, however my heart skips a beat when I see Ms Reba.  I will definitely consider taking in a show next time I'm in town.

I had a blast even though I'm not a hardcore country fan.  It was so fast paced that I was fully engaged the whole time.  I like a few select country songs and country artists but it really opened my eyes to the diversity of country.  It ranged from pop to honky tonk to melodic ballads and blue grass.  Some artists were better than others.

Parking wasn't as bad as I thought it be from reading other Yelp reviews.  I might've lucked out since I caught someone as she was leaving the mall.  Speaking of the mall, it makes no sense to have the Opry and mall next to each other without a parking garage to accommodate the crowds.  Maybe a parking garage will be built soon.  

My showing was at 7 pm and I'm thankful for selecting the early one as opposed to the 9:30 pm showing.  I'm sure parking was a nightmare for the 9:30 patrons.

All in all, the Grand Ole Opry is a winner and I'll definitely be back!

Food is awful and overpriced. Deafeningly loud in there. They cater to out of towners and openly thumb their nose at native Nashvillians. There are plenty of places in the area to go that are nicer with better food and drink selection. Skip this place and go to literally any other bar next door.

You always have a great time but be aware with bench type seating it can get a bit tight and some folks can spread out with clothing and packages. I am sad to see each time we come, it is more and more expensive.
So much fun! Love the history of the ole Opry house. The music was Great! Goodyear took us and had a great time.
We prefer The Ryman but it's still really good.  I don't have to say a whole bunch of stuff here...it's the Opry, it's a national treasure.

It's a must do Nashville sort of thing! Just commit and do it if visiting the area!  Get tkts ahead of time if you can.  Shows start at 7 and doors open at 6.  Arena is big and church pew style seating.  Get some popcorn and a beverage it's a long show with 1 intermission and multiple acts!  The night I was there high valley, Vince Gill, and Charlie Daniels band played as lead performers!  What an experience to see devil went down to Georgia played live!  Overall would do it again!

This venue is the finest around. The Grand Ole Opry is held here every week with performances that vary weekly. I'm from Nashville, and over the years I've seen many a show here, at various times throughout the years. I've watched the Opry House go through the floods of 2010 to be rebuilt and to the wonderful standards Nashville is known for. It's also so close to the Opry Mills mall that you can walk over to the mall before the show. It's very convenient to park too, free if you don't mind walking. Various hotels offer a shuttle to the Opry House (usually a fee), but worth it if you can't walk distances from the parking lot.

Get ready for a true country experience.

The first thing that hit us was the stifling heat, the second was the excessive noise and mass confusion over where to sit and then the icing on the cake was the waitress telling us we couldn't eat there with our son at 7pm.  Not impressed.

The backstage tour was one of our favorite places in Nashville! We really enjoyed hearing about the history and being able to step on stage for photos. The tour guides were informative and kind. We stopped on our way back to the airport and the security team allowed us to check our luggage with them.
Josh the bartender made our visit great. He joked around with us and suggested food and beer that were perfect. Easy and fun destining if you are in Nashville.
Collard greens, gumbo, Texas toast all big winners. Great music and great atmosphere are a huge plus. I could stay here for hour

Cute place but the band that was performing asked for tips for about 20 minutes. And after we gave $20 the lead singer walked around and came to our table asking for more.  After 30 mins they finally played a song. Strange.  The bathrooms are great - tire and gas pump sinks and guitar toilets!

First trip to Nashville . So excited to check out the Grande ole Opry! Did the backstage tour. Randy was our tour guide. Randy is absolutely wonderful! He was so knowledgeable. Charismatic, helpful, funny and overall just a joy !! Couldn't have been happier. Thank you Randy!!!

This is a Nashville classic! No matter what kind of music you enjoy, you have to go to the Grand Ole Opry  to get a true taste of Nashville. Down home friendly people and Country Music Royalty! So much fun!

To each their own, and I'm not a germophobe. But the employee proclaiming herself as Ms Kelli, the owner, (to be fair I don't know if she was the owner or just a bartender) cut in front of everyone in line in the bathroom, then upon leaving the stall, left the bathroom without washing her hands. As I walked out of the bathroom I saw her behind the bar making drinks. I can only assume she was opening beers, garnishing drinks, etc. with her unwashed hands. Like I said, to each their own. If you don't find that offensive, you may well enjoy this bar. I just wanted to pass along what I saw.
Great time and great band. Service was quick and the staff was pleasant. One of the best bars in the strip!

First time in Nashville for a conference and I found myself starving and tired. So, I mapped the closest restaurant I could walk to and ended up stumbling into this trendy food spot. The first thing I noticed was how nicely decorated the interior was: wooden floors, wood panelled walls, long bar, lots of seating, and attractive wall art. 

Since I was alone I decided to take a seat at the bar. It did take a while for anyone to notice me but I didn't mind as I was busy soaking in the atmosphere. When I finally did get the menu, I was impressed by the extensive list of craft beers on tap and the handy "beer types" glossary on the back of the menu which described in detail each variety. I ended up getting the pork banh mi sandwich as I was in the mood for something easy and handheld.

Fair warning, I've had my fair share of Vietnamese banh mi sandwiches in the DC/NoVA area and I can say with absolute certainty that THIS was not that. It was more of a pulled pork sandwich with a side of fries, but appetizing nonetheless. As a banh mi, this was a bad banh mi, but as a pulled pork sandwich this was pretty good. The bun was crispy and the fries were delicious.

Overall, I would say this is a nice restaurant with a good selection of craft beers for the beer snobs. Definitely a good spot to go with a large group. Was a bit disappointed in my sandwich but mostly because it was not what I expected, like drinking a glass of Sprite expecting water - not necessarily disgusting but still jarring.

Thee was good and bad. First of all, we live here so we don't come down to Broadway very often(too crowded) but we thought Christmas exe would be a good time to listen to some music. Normally we go to Roberts for what I would call an authentic honky Toni experience. So first the good. The place looks awesome, I love the bar area downstairs. Very intimate and comfortable on a day when there weren't 25 people in there. We didn't eat so I can't speak to that. The problem? A 3-4 ounce glass of house wine and a 12 ounce can of Goose IPA was $16.50. That is ridiculous. OK, I get it, screw the tourists, but damn. I'll go back to Roberts and drink my limited selection of Domestics for $2.50. Just my opinion.

Watched the Titans game here. Decent beer selection and a great crowd. Unfortunately, was rubbed the wrong way when the manager asked me to move out of my seat away from my friends. This was so the "VIP" tables could watch the game without me in their way. Except there was absolutely no one behind me in the VIP section.

BB King is famous for the music. In that, it does not disappoint. But don't go there for the food or the service. My moment to moment account:

My group of 6 from Florida checked in on a Sunday at 7PM, excited to hear a great band playing.
...
So.. we have been sitting here for 30 minutes since we requested our food. I have to say that the music has been fantastic, but no food yet and our waiter is MIA
...
Ok.. we finally chased our waiter and he says he is frustrated with the situation (really?). He is going to talk to the manager.
...
10 minutes.. the band starts to play again.
...
Ok.. here comes the food. And the manager. I'm already prepared to tell her what a disaster her kitchen must be. Faith (the manager) is very empathetic from the start. She apologizes and comps us the food. I can only say ok. This is a good reaction, I think.

And the food? Decent enough: unremarkable shrimp tacos, brisket, and buffalo wings. Considering how long they took, we are actually surprised to see the food is not horrible after such an ordeal to get it out of the kitchen. I had the brisket and it places third in as many times I have had it during my 3 day vacation in Nashville. I do have to say the guitar player ranks first (and I went to the Opry yesterday!)

In sum, it was actually a good experience. We did not have much expectations for  gourmet food and the band delivered on spades. If it wasn't for the extra long wait, I would probably consider returning.

Busy spot, great Kentucky Bourbon stout!  Bartenders really cater to their friends.  It wasn't a bad spot but it wasn't very welcoming and as a world wide traveler that is something that is important.

Great Place to go with a Group and show off those singing skills. The audience participation is pretty spot on here. So like I said if you want to feel like a star for a day then this is definitely your place. You will have a good time in general.

Belcourt Taps has quickly become my go-to Hillsboro spot to spent time (and dollars) after my excruciatingly long evening lectures. Reminding me of my favorite dives back home, BT is a deeply satisfying location for live music and good drinks. It struck me immediately as the ideal place to unwind with coworkers or classmates after toiling all day in your respective position. The indoor seating is tight, but absolutely worth it if you're alone or just with a friend or two, and there for the music. The outdoor seating is spacious and cozy -- just take note that the right side of the patio is the smoking section. 

My usual order is a gin & tonic, which is always made strong yet balanced by the very friendly and attentive bartender. If you're feeling peckish, I highly and emphatically recommend the adult grilled cheese (bacon lovers take note). My only note to the negative: Food service has been a little inconsistent in terms of wait length, and there has been some staff confusion & misinformation over whether to order at the bar or with a server. Other than these minor details, Belcourt Taps is the place to decompress & celebrate making it through the week.

You might think this is just another downtown bar, but they stand for much more than that. They have so much respect for veterans and the military. They have a house whiskey where 10% of the proceeds go to families of fallen soldiers. They also will buy your first round for free if you are a service member or veteran. I love what they represent and the entertainment here is awesome. True to country music and music city!

I ordered a t-shirt from Third Man for my husband.  The design was fine, but the quality was terrible.  I tried to return for a refund, but they would only give a store credit.  I didn't want another t-shirt because of the quality and everything else was too expensive. We ended up keeping it because of the hassle.  We have also visited the actual store.  Some cool things but very small and the staff act too cool to be helpful.

Was vacationing in Nashville with my wife and two other couples. I did a quick search fir record stores near me and up popped Third Man. I'd completely forgotten it was in Nashville. Really a fun place with lots of cool merchandise. Not perfect. The actual records for sale on their label were priced $1 higher than another record store the next day. Not a big deal just frustrating. The section titled 'only available in the store' wasn't true with a quick search of eBay and Discogs. The listening booth was fantastic. I actually forgot my little bag with the Third Man 45 inserts and stickers on the counter. Would have been cool if they'd reached out on Facebook thinking it wasn't hard to figure out who left them...

Loved this little hot spot. We got there on the early side. They have a wall of there of hot local and only available to this spot shelves. Make your own 45, or go into the listening booth. Lots of great little goopies, pins, patches, shirts and record player accessories. 
Glad we stopped

Good food and decent prices, but they charge a $10 cover on Sundays if you want to watch football upstairs (which you have to do if you don't want to watch the Browns). Go to Double Dogs or Clyde's for football Sundays instead!

What a fun place to visit on broadway! Smaller than other bars on the street however it was a perfect place for good country music. The roof top is a blast with corn hole and janga to play while you listen to the bands. The atmosphere is great and while visiting for four days my friends and I returned three times. It is definitely a bar you have to visit while on broadway!!

After a short deliberation, my colleagues and I deferred to come here instead of the Titans game. A mistake, I concluded. But nevertheless, the ravens were on and not blowing a perfectly winnable game for once so I was pleased. The food here is pretty much just like every other sports bar in Nashville: kinda overpriced, heavily seasoned, easy to throw in a microwave. Overall, great place to drink and watch sports. I've ever made this a yelp comment before, but it's worth noting because it's so prominent here: the staff are kinda socially awkward. The lady that sat us cryptically asked us to relocate cause the entire bar was reserved (apparently, although as I type this there's one lady sitting there). Also, this one nice bouncer kept coming up to our table and just saying "cups," to indicate that he wanted to take our empty drink cups. Interesting place.

I am not sure what possessed by my friend and I to come in here since there were a total of 5 people in the place when we passed by it. I think it was the lure of the karaoke, which my friend loves. 

So we stayed here for about an hour and it never got anymore crowded. The cheap drinks were the main reason I stayed even though drinks were cheap pretty much everywhere else as well. 

I'm fully convinced that you can't be from Nashville and not have a good singing voice. Granted we only saw a handful of people perform but they were all great! My friend and I were the only ones who ruined it. But whatever. 

This place may be more fun when it's crowded but I had a decent time drinking beer and singing bad karaoke.

uggh just horrible - so
Not recommend at all.  Security is rude AF for
No reason ... could be nice if the men went to etiquette class!

Holy Nashville, the town Vegas doesn't want you to know about! Little Big Town  and Charlie Daniels Band at The Grand Ole Opry, Randy Travis making a rare appearance on stage.. this experience was  so good!!! This is such a good time, we're going again for sure.

This place is a joke!
Service would be better ran by monkeys!
The short round intoxicated woman pouring shots for her friends keep her busy enough to ignore the paying customers.  The shot glasses look like a collection in a college students dorm room. 
The smell near the bar is tainted due to never cleaning it and the fermentation odor is nauseating!

I took my friend here to show her a good time in Nashville (her first time in TN). She LOVES karaoke. She requested a song and it took her MULTIPLE requests (i.e., prompts) to get her song played. After they FINALLY played her song, she sang and the "host" proceeded to criticize her performance before the whole bar (please note, she's obviously not famous-- just having fun, but multiple "singers" before her were just awful and there were no criticisms). As she stepped off stage, she attempted to report her terrible experience to which the "manager" asked her if, "she'd still take him home with her." I'm appalled. That's sexual harassment.
Here for the first time on our 6 year anniversary date. We are seeing #Move staring Derek and Julianne Hough. Awesome show! If you get the chance see it!

this place has always been on my list of things to see in my life & it did not fail me! i'm a fan of old country music as well as newer & it was just a dream to walk the halls of where all my favorites had & see the mail area and the inductee wall! it was just a country music lover's dream! the rooms were just amazing! i cannot pick a favorite! the staff is so courteous & just down right sweet! loved the tour, hated that the prices for the tourist picture with the mic was so high & there was no way to get a picture of it aside from the set up kodak people...but overall it did not damper the absolute perfect of that place

A great place for a quick bite or a sit down meal. Wonderful atmosphere, extensive menu for all eaters and tons of beer choices.  It's a must try and a will love! I recommend the soft pretzels and get all of the dips. Each one is great! Enjoy!

Terrible service!!! We went on a Wednesday night and the restaurant was not very busy at all, maybe half the tables had people at them. We were ordered our drinks first. It took 30 mins to get our drinks. They had taken so long with the drinks that we were able to go to the bar and get drinks faster. I don't think they had a bartender on staff. I ordered the shrimp po boy and a side of mac and cheese. The shrimp itself was great but the sandwich as a whole was very bland. The bread used was very dry and flavorless. The mac and cheese was pretty good. Very cheese with great flavor. It took was a very long time to get our check and once we did, it took forever for our waitress to ring us out. Overall, the food was okay but the service was lacking. Do not come if you are in a hurry.

Pulled. Pork. Tater. Tots. Were beyond delicious! The smokehouse burger was about average and the Mac and cheese was more on the plain side as far as seasoning go. I appreciate the customer service and the staff were quick to get me anything I needed.

Located down a dark, dirty alley. At that point it's ok because it's an "adventure".  Party of 5 and we're seated at a plastic folding table. Not great, but still ok. From a humble start, it went down from there. First round of drinks they delivered the wrong beer. Ok, we drank it anyway but reminded the waitress of the error for round 2. Round 2, wrong beer again. The appetizer was wrong too. Entrees finally arrive and they're meh. To the people walking in as we walked out, I'm sorry. I wanted to warn you but kept going.

This karaoke DJ has a tough job. 

Went two nights on the weekend and was surprised by the amount of 'drunk singing'.   Been doing this for abt 25 years and this place is ok and super touristy.  They don't really need to have a good set up when they get so many non-local singers.  Sound system isn't set up the best, making it hard to hear yourself up front.   Easy to get out of sync.  

Waitress first night was completely awful.  Hint:  don't spend all your time on this level... go through the back bar by the restrooms and then go upstairs.  That's where you really want to be.

My entire group was excited to go to The Grand Ole Opry.  I know I'm in my 20s but considering the people I went with raised me it makes sense why I'm excited.

Our show started at 7pm and our tickets were for the show including: "Riders In The Sky", "Lauren Jenkins", "The Whites", "Connie Smith", "Austin Jenckes", "Bobby Osborne & The Rocky Top X-Press", "Ole Crow Medicine Show", "Wade Hayes", "Oak Ridge Boys", and "Jeanne Robertson".  My mom was excited to see Jeanne Robertson because she had seen her live before.

Everyone (except me) in my group is rather conservative so clean fun in right up their ally.  Coming here was something I'm so glad we could do.  Everyone really enjoyed themselves and it was just a great expierence.  I don't think any of us will ever stop talking about it.  Best decision for a short trip ever.  Wish I could come here everyday rather than going back home tomorrow.

The.coolest.experience. If you are and Nashville and love music or anything Jack White, you have to stop here. Even if you only have 5 minutes, just visit the record store. If you have more time on Friday or Saturday, go on a tour. You have to get their earlier, about 9:30-9:45 because they only allow 10 people on the tour. We had a meeting in the studio/stage area in the back. It had electric blue floors and was pretty awesome.

We ended our night at the Redneck Riviera where the music was great and the drinks were yummy. My friend had a yummy Busch Wacker and we even got these cute shot glasses thanks to Yelp! It's not a huge place but I recommend going to this bar when in Nashville!

I went to Anthem for a private Yelp event but I can honestly say that it is a gem. It exudes lots of style and the staff and bartenders were very welcoming to me each time I had a question or visited the bar! The handcrafted cocktail are pretty solid and bar service is great! In addition, Anthem has quite a few nooks and sitting areas where you can chat with friends or strangers. I also loved the fact that there is a lot of space to dance in the main floor level area in front of the stage. The club has a great set-up that gives patrons various vantage points of the venue. From the top balcony there is a great view of the center dance floors and stage and great views from any of the bar areas or comfy plush seating areas. Overall, I thought Anthem was a charming club that I would love to visit the next time that I make it to Nashville.

Most amazing tour if you're a Jack White fan, take note of how specific everything was designed and how everything works in the company. They take pride in what they do and everything has a personal touch.  Jess was a great tour guide for her first time and I hope to visit again soon. I'm only here for work right now. Take not though, the tours are  strict on how many people (10 max) and its first come first serve and only weekends at 2pm. I got lucky, lets just say that. NO PHOTOS AT ALL! put the phone away anyway.

Talk about legendary, iconic and historical. Wow. Just an incredible property and venue to visit and be a part of whether it's to explore or to see a live performance.

This is where it happens for so many country music stars over so many decades.

It's just really cool to be in the same space where so many found their voices.

Can't wait to go back.

Yeeeaaaa. 5 stars for me! I've been walking by this place for two weeks and decided to try it today! First off, FRIENDLY SERVICE! Chef Karen gave me her personal cell number and encouraged me and the staff to order online and she would personally deliver! How frigging cool is that??? Bartender Marita was also superb! Fast service! Ordered the open face "Fishwich" and holy mother of god.....THE SUCKER WAS HUUUUGE!!!! Got a sample of potato salad and coleslaw as my sides and they were tasty! Big plus? Walking distance from the office? I think you people should give this place a go if you haven't. And hats off to Marita and Chef Karen. These ladies both served in the Military, Marita was in the United States Army and Chef Karen served in the US Navy! Thanks for great business and your service to our country!
Simple little spot where we enjoyed some writers rounds, drinks & appetizers! Very small and packed early so sitting on the patio worked just fine!

Back Alley Diner is a great dive bar with solid bar food choices. Yesterday in downtown was a stress test for anyplace: tens of thousands flooding the place for free music, hockey playoffs, and beer.

The Back Alley is a bit difficult to find but look for the signs on Church Street, walk up the alley, and you can't missed it.

Beers include all of the standards and a smaller selection of local microbrew product.Saturdays are typically $2 PBRs but go for the local Yazoo brews. Mixed drinks, they got them but they are typical of southern bars: a bit sweet and often too loaded for bear. 

The fries are among the best in town; my companion judged them the best. And you get to choose how to load them up, even with pulled pork. The wings are solid not spectacular. 

The burgers are the real deal-- go for the special on Texas Toast, enough for 2 people. But I am a fan of the catfish and chicken tenders. Expertly fired up, not greasy not overwhelmed by the batter.

The service remains the weak point: friendly but maddeningly inconsistent. Perhaps the regulars should let the staff do their jobs rather than gabbing. But you have to a hate a guy serving who is also talking on his cell phone.....

Now the best news: good drink, good food and you don't have to take out a loan to pay for it. Reasonably priced restaurants have disappeared in downtown: glad that BAD is still a hold-out.

I was in town for the National Down syndrome Rockin' Moms conference and while I wasn't able to see a show, I decided to take in the backstage tour. 

Our tour guide was Bill and he was such a funny, informative guide. He told us really great stories about the past and current country music greats and it was obvious that he loved the building and what it represented. I definitely recommend this tour! 

One thing you should be aware of is this price.  While this was a great tour, $33 for a one hour tour seems a bit much.  It could definitely be reduced just a bit.
