It took quite a while to be acknowledged.  I get it, you're busy.  But ACKNOWLEDGE!!!  I've been in food & bev most of my live.  Try "I see you, I'm busy but will be with you soon".  None of that.  I ordered food to go.  I didn't receive utensils.  Menu said "sautéed onions". Mine were raw.  Burger is dry and overcooked.  There were no condiments for my burger.  Nor was I asked if I wanted any. One of the worst take out experiences of my life.  Skip it.

We just moved to Nashville a year ago and just had a baby, so we haven't actually seen a show yet. But we did do the backstage tour and it was so cool. You get to see all the dressing rooms which were fantastic and amazing to hear the history of all who've been in there and performed. You see the walk up entry and the mailboxes and the stage itself. Sadly, you can't go on stage, but you get pretty close to that infamous circle. Our tour guide was amazing. A little pricey, but worth the hour.

We loved this place!  The waiters were so friendly and we loved the music.  We went two nights in a row we like it so much, and every hour they had 4 artists up on stage taking turns performing a song. It was an awesome way to hear a lot of different artists in one night.

As a HUGE fan of Jack White and all he does this had to be my first stop when visiting Nashville. It was like going on my journey to the mother land. It's a small shop but filled with all things awesome. Everything Jack does is high quality, including this shop. There are records, stickers, buttons, tshirts and many other lovely Third Man Items. You can just wander around and look at everything or record yourself in the record booth. Just go there and buy some vinyl.

While we thoroughly enjoyed the backstage tour, we were very disappointed with the Dolly Parton Exhibit. There were a half dozen cases of her dresses with a few blurbs about her career, a short video that mostly promoted the Opry, and a few couches, all in an enormous room that made the exhibit seem even chintzier. It was definitely not worth $15-20!

@JohnRich just wants it more.  Tried several big name places on Broadway tonight and this place is by far the best.  Great music, great drinks and great atmosphere. This place is a definite must visit on any Nashville excursion.

We were here for the weekend and wasn't really a fan of broadway just too much for me but our last day here we went here, paid a $7 cover and spent hours here and had the best time. The band was fantastic and so were all the people! The music was just so good you couldn't help but to dance and people were just walking around getting others to dance with them. I loved the atmosphere here. If we ever make it back to Nashville this is the spot I would go.

NYE was booming! Good crowd but not packed like sardines. The atmosphere was great!

My first time visiting at this location. I really enjoyed my experience at the one in Memphis so I figured I'd give this location a shot. It appears to be more spacious than the Memphis location. The music was great! Mostly 70s and 80s hits were sung. An occasional 90s & beyond. 

We ordered the Fried Zucchini & Bell Peppers to snack on and soak up some of the cocktails :). Sooooo yum! (Sorry no picture)

Such a fun spot!! They have an excellent selection of beer and great deals throughout the week. My favorite is that on Mondays, they have $3 beer happy hour ALL day long. Makes for a super cost effective trip. They also have this cool loyalty card program that essentially rewards you for drinking - not too shabby. After 200 beers, you get your own saucer up on the wall (with a phrase of your choosing) and $100 off your bar tab for a party thrown for you! How cool. 200 beers sounds like a lot, but if you're settled in Nashville for a while, there's no time limit on how long you have to take to drink the 200 beers. You also get a t-shirt with signing up. Recommend this spot if you're a beer drinker!

Always happy when we go to saucer. Not only is the beer list changing and vast, the food is really savory, the pretzels are AMAZING! With the queso, mmm. Always have some kind of music and comfy couches to hang out after a long day. They have an extra room with long table for your larger groups too.

Stood at the bar for easily 25 minutes while a bartender waited on everyone she could find TWICE and when she finally took our order, proceeded to wait on others again. This would be no surprise if it was a busy night but half of the barstools and most of the restaurant was empty. Know why? Because the food was TERRIBLE.

Walked in at 10:15pm on Monday night. Was pretty empty and the server told us right away that it's bar service only. I asked if the band was still going to play until 11pm (which is when they closed), and he said yes, so we thought we'd have a drink and enjoy the music. 15 minutes later they stopped at 10:30. We had full drinks and decided to make the most of our half hour left -until the place turned the lights up in the bar.  Now I know why they were not as busy as the other bars in the area. Too bad as the band was really good. You want business? Don't make your customers feel unwelcome.

Let's be honest...if you have never been to a show at the Grand Ole Opry House, you need to get to one. This was my first show here, but have been to shows at the Ryman many times. This was just as amazing! 

The process to get in was very quick and smooth. We sat in the balcony and when looking around I really don't think there is a single "bad" seat in the place! Every show is being broadcast on the radio and there is something magical about seeing the "ON AIR" sign light up. 

We were lucky enough to pick a night where Caitlyn Smith played her 1st time at the Orpy, we celebrated a singer who had been an Opry member for 50 years, and Chris Jansen played his 191st show. You quickly realize the amount of history that is represented at very show. 

If I could give more than 5 stars I would! I love living in a town with no much Americana history!

Arrived around 8:30pm for BBQ.
They said there was a $5 cover charge even if we were eating.
We paid it as I tip each band anyway as that is how they make money.
Question I have does the cover charge go to the band or the house?

Regarding the food, was not sure what to expect as we where eating a little late, thought maybe the food would not be very good or hot.
We had a rib dinner and a chicken/rib combo plate. IT WAS EXCELLENT.

Win/Win... Good food and the band (Mike Hayes) was excellent.

Really cool venue. Really fun artists. Love that some shows live record the show for later purchase on vinyl. Only issue is you're standing there for a few hours and there in no water available. NONE. Only liquor and beer. For anyone with diet restrictions or underage be warned. You'll be high and dry lol

THIS IS THE HIDDEN GEM OF NASHVILLE!!!

Located near the Arcade downtown, Back Alley Diner has some of the best food in town.  From burgers to their delicious smoked chicken to the amazing pork, there is something for everyone at this restaurant.  I frequent BAD a couple times a week and it gets better every time.  There is live music from local songwriters every Tuesday night and great music on Friday and Saturday nights with full bands.  The staff is great, the food is great, the drinks are great, EVERYTHING is great.  BAD is good, and I definitely recommend this to anyone who lives in the Nashville area or just visiting for one night.
I had an awesome time here tonight! My server TREY was a delight...he was very attentive and professional.I will definitely be back ever time I come to Nashville!

Their pretzel app is fantastic - with two cheeses and two mustards.  I haven't had any of their other food, but have heard good things.  Beer selections is fantastic and quite reasonably priced; plus everyday they have a different beer on special for $3 pints.  Fun atmosphere, especially in low periods if you can sit on the couches and enjoy a pint.

Huge downside: parking is not free.  Park in the lot and get your ticket validated ($3 for less than 2 hours, $5 if greater than 2 hours).  Just a pain, but not so much to not make it worth returning.

I have loved this place for a lonnnnnnggg time! Still one of my faves in Nashville! If you are a beer fan then this is for you! I love the atmosphere and the saucer bratzel! Yum! Pizza is good, Space Club and Dipster are good too! The only reason I didn't rate it five stars is like all the other reviewers said, "Don't go on the weekends." Sadly this is true. They get so busy I stopped going on weekends and now it's the perfect weeknight hangout.

Great experience ! I learned that the Opry is broadcasted live on the radio, so if you can't make it you'll never miss it. I highly recommend getting a parking pass. We paid a little extra then just walked a bridge to the opry. It's a little big auditorium. Honestly not a bad seat in the whole place!
There are church pews with cushions so very comfortable only thing is your neighbor May sit closer than you like because it's a pew rather than a. Normal
Seat. But love every minute of it!!! Multiple acts that play 2-4 songs each and then the main acts don't disappoint.
Entertainment was awesome.  Not as crowded or open air hot like some other places.  Classy comfortable place and service was excellent.  Definitely will return.

What's there to say that hasn't already been said? We loved it so much, we went twice on our trip to Nashville! Well, I guess it helps that Dolly Parton was there and we knew we needed to get there to see her and we made sure that happened!

There really isn't a bad seat in the house. I recommend possibly purchasing tickets from a third party for a really good deal, especially on sold out shows. It seems there are always tickets available and good prices even when it's sold out.

We did standing room only for Dolly and ended up standing against the wall on the top tier, just below the upper seating. It wasn't terrible, but I recommend getting their early enough that you get a decent spot on the wall, especially if you like to be more towards center.

By far THE best stop in Nash! This shop is adorable and quirky and small and loaded with talent. First of all, the lady who was working at the shop was too cool for school with her vintage inspired yellow and black trademark colors uniform dress. But not only are the peeps in this shop rockabilly coolness, they are also SO nice! She gave us a full guide of local shows, bars, clubs and restaurants to check out while in town. So anyway, we browsed the store and all of it's music industry treasure nicknacks and records. This is Jack White's record shop and recording studio space, so it's truly a one of a kind vibe. The crowning jewel of this shop is the vintage live recording booth that will record like 3 minutes of sound. I saw students in there singing and playing guitar in the booth. So 6 of us decided to give it a whirl and time capsule or trip to Nash with a fun recording. The lady at the shop told us all about the history of the booth and just how many music legends have stood in that very same booth to record! She then gave us the recording on her, as a gift. I think the cost os around $10? Worth it! I picked up a Margo Price album and Johnny Cash single - my first records. There are also other interactive and fun booths to play in, like the dj booth to scratch records. This shop is such a special place and really represents what Nash is all about- the music. I think the space next door is venue and recording studio space for artists and shows, which would be so great to see in the future!
Terribly slow service even though we were nearly the only people in the place. Food was mediocre at best.

Did a backstage tour here and learned some really cool facts and history about the Grand Ole Opry and how they induct their members. Thought the tour was going to be a little more than what we got... it starts with an 8 min long recorded video by Blake Shelton. I'm a huge Blake fan but a recorded video was a pretty disappointing way to start the tour. Our guide was really awesome and made up for the blandness of watching yet again a second recorded video half way through the tour. The tour was about 45 mins which went by rather quickly! At the end of the tour they take you on stage and you have the opportunity to take plenty of photos which is really nice. They also offer you the option to have a photographer take your photo or your groups photo. At the end you can purchase the photo for $25. Our photos came out really nice but no one in our group thought it was worth $25 so we left with the photos on our phone!

On a side note, I will definitely come back and see a show here in the future!!

Shrimp and grits!  Awesome.  Service great...entertainment great.  One band not so much.  Not typically a fan of tourist traps and big chain restaurants but wanted to stop in this old favorite.  Did not disappointed at all.  For some reason my bottle of beer was flat and they quickly replaced it....Fried pickles, never had those before, but they were a great appetizer.  We were there during CMA Fest from June 6-10, Nashville was extremely busy, but the service was good and it was not too crowded.

Wow! This place came highly recommended, what a disappointment!!!
First there was a $10 cover per person for the band! The staff was incredibly slow, the food was mediocre and over priced. You could get better BBQ anywhere else. Then they added a $10.00 tip to my boyfriends credit card after we had left one! Who runs this place??! 
It's credit card fraud! 
I would never recommend this place, go somewhere else!!!!

I'm not really a country fan, but the tour is a must if visiting Nashville.  It's an iconic and historical landmark and the tour was very well organized.  Bring your camera!!  The show?  Don't spend a lot of money on tickets.  Hint:  wait until a couple hours from showtime and get cheap tickets on stubhub. We got floor seats for $38 each! Aside from the "special guest" it's mostly a bunch of older, no names who perform one or 2 songs.  Mostly a tourist destination which I realized when only just a handful of people shouted when one of the performers asked "who's is from Nashville."
Food was pretty good, musicians were talented... the service lacking at best. Restrooms dirty, tables next to us sat dirty for an hour. The staff here is just going through the motions at best.

Loved this place!! My favorite on a recent trip to Nashville. Bar staff was great while we waited for the rest of our friends. Lynchburg lemonade-yum! Food was also good but the live music was the best!

If there ever was proof that Nashville has changed, it's the Music City Tippler. The crowd, the concept, heck, even the neighborhood... back when I first lived in Nashville, none of this would have existed or made sense. But this is now and this is... OMG Taylor Swift! So, I get it and I embrace it. Nashville is all grown up and the world is starting to see what a rad place it is to live... and grab a drink.

There are many places now in Nashville to find cool kids. It just depends on what kind of cool kid you're looking for. Natives? Southern transplants? Los Angelinos? NYcers? Trust fund babies? 'Artists'? Artists? You get the point. Here at the Music City Tippler, the cool kid crowd (at least while I was here) skewed more east coast (to be expected) and star-gazing. The layout makes sense, the decor is inviting (more than that; it's gorgeous and sexy) and the drinks are good. I had an early morning ahead of me, so rather than sitting around and gazing at all the pretty as I went down the entire cocktail list, I opted for a sangria. Red wine, rum and fruit will always be a good idea. I was hopeful for some late night bites but, for some reason, they weren't available. We weren't there *that* late but I also wasn't heading up the negotiations with the waitress. The place wasn't *that* packed but she seemed pretty harried. Again, I was leaving after one drink and was too distracted by everything else going on there to pay much attention to any service woes. It just means I need to come back for more cocktails... and much more pretty.

Favorite place to hear live music in Nashville. The sound is mixed perfectly, they have live music all the time, the bathroom is clean, and the bar service is excellent. We heard the all female band Sidepiece twice, plus the Nervous Wrecks, and both were amazing. Can't wait to go back!

Good place. Love playing music here, love listening to music here. The bartenders rock. Parking is tricky- street parking or shifty parking in lots. But worth it for the good tunes! Get there early if you want a good seat.
The food was really good especially the greens. The service was great. I loved the live music. I will definitely return here soon.

Went for my first concert at the opry this week.  How stinking cute. 
We got there about 30 minutes before start time. Lines were already lengthy outside just to get it. Before you get to doors you go through metal detectors and get bags checked. You then get in line for doors to open. There's a bar outside and entry into gift shop from outside.  Once doors opened we all quickly got in. More bars, bathrooms and concessions are available before getting to your seats. 
We sat ground level and seats were cushioned church pews. So cute and different than most concert venues. 
I loved the vibe of the venue. Very much country, duh. 
There are plenty of tv screens for upper levels to see clearly. Shows are played love over the radio, so there are "commercial" breaks and it is mc-ed. 
Stage is perfect size. Small, but big enough to perform. We got tickets to see Chris Young perform his first show as an Opry member. What a great night to go. There are obviously other performers, including a comedian. Henry Cho was so funny. We had the pleasure to watch: Del McCoury Band, Dustin Lynch, Steel Wool,Henry Cho, Tracy Lawrence, Cassadee Pope, and of course Chris Young. The singers before Chris all got to sing 3 songs and the comedian got a timed segment. Chris performed about 5-6 songs. 
I had a good time. Great first show at the Opry!
Food was excellent! Try the fried pickles!! Loved the brisket too! Awesome awesome food, drinks and live music.

This place was pretty alright. Unfortunately, there's a lot of construction going on in the area at this time, but if you pay close attention, you'll make it back there to the right spot.
Service was o-kay. When we walked in, I said "hi" to 2 different servers and got looks instead of hello's. You seat yourself, but it was a bit of time before someone acknowledged our table. Then we sat for a while before we had to ask our waitress for glasses of water. She did get the basics of our orders down though, and the food came out correct, for the most part.
I will say, the food was pretty good. I stuck with a safe selection - hot wings. Your typical buffalo wing sauce, but they fried them up nice and crispy, and that made them more delicious. My friend got their Loaded Rocket-Tots, and they were GOOD! So glad she shared. I don't even like tater tots (it's a texture issue, lol), but these were delicious (texture aside)! Yummy jalapeño potatoes, cheese, egg... my goodness! You need a bite with everything together to understand the deliciousness! 
The decor was cool and beautiful at the same time. 
I would definitely return. Nice pub atmosphere. 
Still want to try their pretzels...
Terrible food, bad service, and music was just ok. Skip this one. There are plenty of other places to go in Nashville. Try Skulls Rainbow Room!

I do not dole out single stars lightly, but in this case I would give 0 if I could. 

I first tried Belcourt Taps (& tapas? Didn't they used to have tapas?) last year and had a very meh experience. I waited for another visit to review since a first time bad experience could always be a fluke. My husband bought a groupon for 2 beer flights and an appetizer this month not knowing I wasn't a huge fan based on previous experience, but we thought, hey it's pretty hard to mess up beer. I guess we jinxed ourselves. 

The inside was pretty full when we arrived on a week night, and it looked like a band was about to go on. I'm thinking this place is best as just a music venue where you happen to have a beer rather than a destination for a meal.

We opted for the patio since it was nice outside. We told our waitress up front that we were going to redeem their groupon, which she seemed super confused about and told us they didn't have a current groupon, their old one expired. Not her fault, but the staff was clearly not educated on the offer (which didn't expire for 3 more months). If you have a groupon out there, maybe tell your staff about it. 

We asked about the beer flights (not on the menu) and she told us that it was "local stuff."  We were fine with that explanation since we knew we were getting whatever their groupon deal was and couldn't be picky. However, when the "flights" arrived, it was one big service tray with 10 mini mason jars (those were cute, I'll give them that), each about a third full and nothing was labeled or in any order. They were also not cold. We asked her what they were and she said "mostly local stuff, it's good" and then walked away. Ok..... 

We ended up finding out through taste testing trial and error that we did not, in fact, have 2 flights (I incorrectly assumed we would each get the same 5 beers since it was supposed to be 2 flights...), just 10 random different beers. We also deduced that TWO of them were some kind of HARD CIDER.  I have no problem with cider if that's what I ordered, but I don't really find it acceptable to put it in a beer flight with no warning.  

I won't even address the appetizer we got except to say that I do not recommend the nachos. 

The waitress informed us that if we didn't order anything else besides just redeeming the groupon there would be 20% gratuity charged. We had initially planned to order more, but the app was so bad that we decided not to. We were planning to tip all along, so the gratuity charge was no problem. The receipt listed the 10 beers, which included Sam Adams and Angry Orchard (aka, not local and not beer).  We asked if those were our beers since they weren't labeled and she said no, I just pushed 10 random buttons to get the bill printed so I could charge gratuity. Great. I am convinced we did get the angry orchard, though. There's no mistaking that for beer. 

The excuse for a beer flight would have been disappointing anywhere, but is especially puzzling from a place with "taps" in their name who is specifically advertising beer flight deals. 

Since this is 2 bad experiences in a row a year apart, it's not a fluke. I will not be returning.

Second time at the Opry and second time for a night fully entertained. I don't see a trip to Nashville without going to the Opry. It's a great show for country lovers.

The first time we came we purchased tickets way in advance for a weekend getaway. Turned out that ended up being the weekend they scheduled All Star Weekend so we got to see several acts that are big stars.

Love that they mix in oldies and more current acts.

Some of their repeat acts like Jean Shepard and Riders in the Sky are very entertaining. The show is ever changing and lively as each act plays 2 or 3 songs and they move on to the next. They also break it up into portions and each portion has a different host so you never get too bored with one person.
Great live music venue and delicious food. Tons of drink options. Loved the garlic mashed potatoes and cornbread!
The food, service and experience was amazing. I don't know what they put in their Mac and cheese, but it is some of the best I've ever had.

We were in the area & after checking out another place that happened to be dead, we walked past this place & decided to check it out. 
Karaoke is not usually my favorite since let's face it people just generally sound terrible, so when I noticed it was a karaoke bar my initial reaction was to go but it was late & this was the best place we could find so we stayed. 
we made our way towards the back & sat by the bar, drinks had to give the cbd "thc" drinks a try .. because why not, we got a margarita , the margarita was terrible taste wise good thing we also got beers the local IPA to use as a chaser, beer was good .. margarita not so much because the taste was just so harsh. 
As for the environment it actually wasn't too bad, in between the karaoke singing they played regular music which was  a good way to break up the singing.
Decent size bar, the CBD drink was ok for the most part maybe it needs to be added to a better drink,  overall we had a decent time here.

Really didn't enjoy this location.  I been to the one in New Orleans and for some reason almost everything was wrong. I went last Saturday the 16th and had to pay $10 per person cover charge just to eat and then after ordering, my food was cold and everything was dried out.  I ordered the ribs and mac n cheese which must had been in the oven forever.  The only thing that was good was the baked beans. I arrived at 8:15 waited over a hour for a table the band started playing a little after 9pm and stopped playing from 10 to a little after 1030. Ended up leaving a quarter to 11pm. While waiting around didn't seem anyone was enjoying their food. So in conclusion, I paid $30 for parking for 3 hours, $30 for 3 ppl to get in and had a tab of over $60 just to see the band for a total of 40 mins to celebrate my birthday.  Money down the drain the food could have least be banging and the band popping. The hostess was rude and ghetto but the bar tender and waitress was nice and friendly.

Went there twice during the trip,one night they had a live band another night a DJ, large bar with plenty of bartenders so the drinks/food come out quickly, ordered the burger it was very good ... would visit again

Any tourist coming to Nashville should know that the Grand Ole Opry House is a must. It is a wonderful piece of history, and has held so many performances by legendary country music artists.

  I will say that I have never seen a show myself or done the tour - so my review is based off of the Grand Ole Opry as an event space. I was invited through a friend to Southwest Airline's employee rally, which was held here and made for a great space.

   The inside and outside are beautiful - especially the stage room. It's big, but also small enough to wear almost any seat in the house could give you a great view. There are also a couple screens projecting who is on stage for those farther away.

   They also have a nice outside space out front, where there were all kinds of local food trucks/stands set up to cater. 

   As a fan of country music, I am already wanting to go back and schedule a tour/see a performance! This place is just awesome.

Wow! Wow! Wow! What a fantastic time.   While in Nashville, we couldn't miss the chance to see a concert at the Grand ole Opry.   Main person here was Vince Gill.   Plus, 12 others!  What a show.   What was a huge surprise was that this was an "on-air" live broadcast, from the the Grand Ole Opry. Anddd it includes commercials, as well. A little quirky, but this has been happing for 92 years that we've been told. Awesome! Just  gotta mark this off your bucket list; it's a must do for sure. Thanks for a great time!
Love this bar! We stopped in at 9:00 am on a Saturday and the live band was playing their heart out. Lots of fun!!!

These idiots owe me $80 ($40 one way cab fair from the hotel).  Came all the way out here for the "every 15 min's tour" that was sold out until next week.  F&ck them, I will never come back here again.
Legendary venue. The staff is always so friendly and of course the music is always great! Always a treat!

I felt that I had to see the grand Ole Opry while in Nashville. I enjoyed the show on a Wednesday but cannot rave about it. Each of the performers  for about 15 minutes. I realize that this is radio show, so they have to do commercials,  but I paid for tickets and did not appreciate the commercials which I fast forward,through on TV. A bottle of water cost $5.00.  The cost of Uber from 5th and Church was $20.00.we used a taxi coming back to hotel and cost was $26.00 .

Decided to go here because I have been to their other location (Fort Worth, Texas) and it was an amazing experience. They have the largest beer selections ever!!

Monday is their $3/pints and most of the beer I got tasted awesome! I usually get ciders. It's not too sweet and still have that "beer" taste. Unfortunately, I didn't get to try their food. 

Service was good and I never waited too long to order my next drink. If you decide to park in the garage - remember to get your ticket validated. I forgot how much it was but it wasn't pricey at all. Will be coming back and highly recommend to all beer fans!!

We strolled past here on a Sunday mid-morning and Carl Stewart's soulful vocals and expert guitar playing pulled us right in.  What a treat to hear him play and sing.  He also featured a female vocalist who did Sade and Whitney justice!  The caliber of musicianship just blew me away.

Unfortunately the bar is not rising to that level.  First of all there were no cocktail servers.  Alright, fine.  It was just before noon.  So my friend and I sent our husbands to the bar to grab drinks so we could stay at the table and just soak up all the good music.

They waited over 5 minutes for a bar tender to even appear.  The drinks we ordered were ok but were not served with cocktail napkins.  Ugh.  Don't you just love rings of condensation on your table with nothing to wipe it up with?

So to be clear....this would have been a 2 star review had it not been for the outstanding musical performances delivered on that stage.  I will definitely come back....to hear Carl Stewart and his band play.  I'll just try not to arrive thirsty.

Great atmosphere, very chill, kickass bartenders, and "Saucer Mondays" is the absolute best. $3/pint of draft with an excellent selection! Quickly turning into the spot for Vandy seniors, and as a Vandy senior myself, I gotta say I can't complain.

First time here. Came at 5pm on Memorial day weekend Sunday and the wait was 45 min. Totally worth the wait.  We didn't have to pay any kind of cover so Um not sure about that.  Started with the soul sampler(wings, catfish bites and their famous fried pickles!) Had the brisket & ribs. Finished with their specialty shots. Worth the trip. Two of us with a total of 5 drinks and sampler appetizer was $75.

TERRIBLE SERVICE!  Our waiter was literally grumbling to himself the entire time and said he validated our parking, but he didn't. We went in to grab a beer and get our parking validated. This was a bad decision. 

The table behind us couldn't get his attention and finally walked out on their check. Usually, I wouldn't be ok with that, but I had watched them wait 20 minutes trying to get his attention. 

We got an app and two beers. The food came out quickly, but the beers took forever. And only one beer came out. If I hadn't been paying attention to what he grumbled to himself, we would not have known he knew we were expecting another beer. He grumbled quietly that the keg needed to be changed. I understand that, but he did not communicate that well at all. Also, I was a waiter for years. If I have a delay like that, I bring the customer a water and have two back up choices that are similar for the customer to switch to.

We ordered a few dishes, such as hummus, tomato bisque, and their burger. The food here was simply not good at all. The bisque had the consistency of water and tasted horrendous. Their hummus was weirdly spicey, and our group felt that the pita bread felt and tasted like cardboard. Bad experience on a Saturday night - as a tourist, I was extremely surprised that this restaurant could survive in Nashville. Disappointing/felt like we wasted the opportunity for a good meal.

Sometimes Jack White hangs out here and that is basically all you need to know.  His actual studio is next door making this a must see attraction in Nashville.

The space is tiny but jam packed with stuff to do and see adding to the overall thrill. The store is sensory overload in the best sort of way. Everything from the walls to the lights to the clothes the lady working was wearing is black, white or yellow with red accents. Music is blaring and customers are attempting to take it all in. They of course sell a few select records, but they also have lots of third man offerings like shirts, stickers, buttons etc.

There are plenty of activities to do in this pocket sized store as well.  You can peruse the hall of Jack White's records or jump in the phone booth to make a quick call.  For 15 tokens, you can record anything you want on a small vinyl record.  The booth is only large enough for one person to record at a time.  Two kids could potentially fit. 15 tokens is equivalent to $15. You can also shed a few tokens to watch a music video. For three tokens, you can get your pics made in the photo booth.  This is what my group was wanting to do, but the line was real long so instead I used my three tokens elsewhere.  I indeed walked out of Third Man with a wax replica of Jack White's 1964 Montgomery Ward airline guitar.  So yeah, that's pretty great.

Totally worth checking out and not too far from downtown Nashville.

Great place to go in and have a beer and enjoy The variety
Knowledgeable staff and great service
Definitely would recommend stopping in

First night in Nashville and enjoyed some live music here from a local band. With a $5 charge, that was the highlight. The food was so so. Had the fried catfish platter and they didn't bring me any sauces. They also charge extra for ranch dressing. The drinks were pricey but so weak, could not even taste the alcohol! Dark and loud, so don't expect a lot of intimate talking!
We were given menus but waiter did not come around to take order after 15+ min so we left. There were only 2 tables of customers so it wasn't like they were busy.

I've here twice and their 6 and 7pm shows were cancelled both times. The waiter kept making mistakes and brought us the wrong items. The food was good, though. Very laid back and casual atmosphere. Also good location. But I don't think I will want to come back here.

Phenomenally great!
My husband & I took the backstage tour & it was better than I imagined! You get to see the entrance for the performing artists, dressing rooms for the stars, and stand on stage! I never realized this place only holds around 4500. I do not believe there would be a bad seat. See my pics below, I'll prob upload the max because I loved the Grand Ole Opry!
So much fun! We went on the bachelorette Honky Tonk Party bus and we LOVED IT!  Our bride, Katie had so much fun and the guy that checked us in was so wonderful and kind!

I love going to shows at the Grand Ole Opry House! There isn't a bad seat in the whole place. I definitely recommend going to a show if you're in town visiting or if you live in Nashville!! TAKE THE BACK STAGE TOUR!!! It is so cool to see the dressing rooms and all the behind the scenes stuff at the Opry House. Since the Opry House is right next to the mall, they share parking, which means you can either get a really good parking spot or you have to walk pretty far...but either way, it is worth it and you'll be glad you went!!
I'm not a country/bluegrass person, but if you are, I highly recommend that you check this place out. Fantastic.

I was there, just visiting on vacation, & wanted to catch some live music while watching Astros v. Yankees as well as Coyotes v. Preds.  Mission: Accomplished!  Relatively new to country music, I wasn't sure what all to expect from the live music, but I was truly impressed by the quality of the music as well as the service provided by the bartenders there.  It was fairly busy, but the bartenders did a good job going around to everyone in a fair amount of time.  Decent bar food, too.  I'd definitely visit there again.
Great backstage tour of Grand Ole Opry House. But why is all the merchandise for sale made in China and Thailand. Should be made In America

Absolutely loved the show! Phenomenal performance. I only really knew of Martina McBride before arriving but everyone was so talented with great light comedy. I will definitely be researching the performers. The seating was surprisingly extremely comfortable as well, good back support.

The only downside I experienced was the cost of alcoholic beverages were a little pricier. A can of Angry Orchard was $9, so arrive boozed up. The price is typical when going to a concert hall so it doesn't effect the 5 stars.

Lastly, we were in Section 34 Row M and we still had a pretty good view. Love the screens that allow the people in the back to still be able to see the performers clearly.

My family and I got tickets for a recent show at the Opry. We had such a grand time! There were performers old and young, funny and sweet, and all so talented! Don't wait for a "famous" celebrity to get tickets...we went on a night when we knew only two of the seven performers but absolutely LOVED hearing not only those up-and-coming artists, but also some old-time goodies and are now fans of amazing performers we'd never heard of before!

This place is out of this world!!  The flying saucer offers a calm & comfortable atmosphere. If you sample enough of the ample beer selections, you may begin to feel like your on Mars. I hope not enough to see Uranus.  
I loved checking out the saucers. I tried to find the PA saucer but didn't. Next time!! We dined on a few apps, enjoyed a side salad & downed a few brews. It was all good!!

This was a great little diner for lunch. I order the original cheeseburger and you can tell that the burger is made fresh. The other girls ordered a chicken sandwich. Both were fresh as well. The fries were great. Overall, it was a great spot for lunch when all of the other places were crowded!

I would 100% recommend taking the backstage tour here. It's so cool to hear about the Oprys history and see where all the back stage action happens including being able to look into many of the artists dressing rooms. Its beautiful inside and the tour ends with a walk out on to the stage

Music scores a 5. Waitstaff service scores a 1.  I was seated pretty quickly but then it was 30-40 minutes before anyone spoke to me. Waitress blames another waitress who was apparently missing in action and offered to take over, but then second waitress also went missing and I waited a very long time for my check. Also asked whether there was a lot of okra in the shrimp and grits- I despise okra - and was told it was just a little. The stuff was LOADED with okra. Slimy yucky okra. 

On the bright side, Carl Stewart and his band provided great music. So go for the fabulous music but not for dinner unless you have a lot of time to wait.

We stopped in Nashville for a night and I must say I'm glad we went here! From the staff to the food, it was a wonderful experience. The fried chicken was delicious. My husband ordered the lettuce wraps and those were delicious as well. Steven was a GREAT bartender. The band was awesome. Highly recommend this place!

Well at first I did not want to pay a $3.00 cover because every other bar was free, but my husband thought we would enjoy. It was a great bar, with great music. The BB King guitarist and his band were great, we stayed for ours, ordered catfish app. And crab cakes - excellent, so worth the $6.00 cover. I totally recommend for a great time.

My wife and I attended this tour this past Monday.  It wasn't originally on our list of things to do in Nashville but we saw a live broadcast of the Opry at the Ryman and whenever we had some free time earlier today, we decided to do the backstage tour as well. $32/person gets you a 45 minute tour partially narrated by Blake Shelton with the rest by a tour guide.  Our tour guide here Kayleigh, was peppy and full of energy and I was impressed by how upbeat she was throughout.  The tour itself started with a video and then proceeded to the artists entrance, through security and into the dressing room area, green room and finally out onto the stage itself for a photo opportunity which could be purchased in the gift shops. Throughout the tour we learned about the history of the Grand Ole Opry as well as what it meant to be a member.  To be honest, my wife and I had no clue about any of this before we came to Nashville but still found it to be a very cool experience.

The bottom line for for me is that I would recommend this tour to anyone in the Nashville area.  It is a cool experience to learn about the Opry and stand on the stage, even if you aren't Country music fans as neither my wife nor I are.  My only regret is that I would have taken this tour prior to seeing the live broadcast at the Ryman as I think I would have appreciated the show even more.
First time there. Not a big country fan but it was fun. Great to be part of a long tradition for one night. Was able to see Sara Evans
Unique little place. I could see hanging out here frequently and listening to music or just sitting on the patio and enjoys the night if I lived a little closer!

Not the best experience we have had in Nashville. We were seated quickly and the prices were fair. The band was fantastic. The food however was just ok. We ordered fried pickles. Way too salty. The catfish po boy was bland. I ordered the sausage po boy with no cheese sauce. It came with cheese sauce. When I told the server I asked for no cheese, I was told the stuff that was dripping off of my sandwich was mustard. It was cheese. Also we never got refills on our drinks.

First of all, I don't consider myself a fan of country music.  Second of all, my fiance and I went here on a Thursday night (not really expecting the music or the atmosphere to be "poppin off").  However, I was blown away; the band was awesome, the crowd was great, and the drinks were reasonably priced.  

My fiance and I came from LA, so we didn't know what to expect when it comes to honky tonks.  This was the first one that we visited on Broadway, and after visiting a few more, this was our absolute favorite.  Everything was great, and the bar service was quick- especially considering there was only one bartender!

We tried to return on Friday night, but it was a little too crowded: this isn't a surprise.  I HIGHLY recommend coming in here, and if we ever find our way back to Nashville, we will definitely stop in again!

While in Nashville I made sure to get us tickets to take in a show at the Grand Ole Opry.  You generally don't know who will be performing until a week or so before your show, so my wife was pleasantly surprised when we found out The War and Treaty were performing and making their Opry debut during our visit.  The venue is great, we were in the lower balcony and could see great, plus they have plenty of video screens.  We were probably the only Black folks at the show, and we kept having people coming up and asking us if we were enjoying the show.  We will have to come back for a backstage tour the next time we visit, coming here is a must do if visiting Nashville.

Hillbilly Food Critic Review:
Location: 4/5 (slightly off Broadway)
Atmosphere: 4/5 
Food: 2/5
Price: 2/5

Here is the deal, come for the musicians. They are awesome.  The staff is friendly. 

Other than great music, it seems expensive, food is eh .... and they keep the TVs on when the musicians are playing :(

Again, musicians are great, but seems strange that they play non blues, Neil Diamond, etc. How about more than one BB King song??

Had a nice dinner of bbq chicken and ribs.  They had live blues music too.  For a starter we had the spinach dip with chips. Tasty. Wonderful waiter took excellent care of us.  Bringing us drinks and telling us the best items to order
Great food. Awesome shrimp and grits and gumbo. Kids liked mac and cheese. Good music atmosphere and service.  Glad we chose this place based on yelp reviews.

I can say with confidence now, that if you swing by Nashville you at least have to add the Grand Ole Opry to your list of "Things to Do"! It's a country music staple of Nashville and I have been there now 4 times and have thoroughly enjoyed every one of the shows I've been to. The place itself has so much history that I just feel special to be able to see all of it. All of the people you see go through there and perform know how to have a good time and are quick to make you feel like family-- 10/10 recommend!

Worst service ever. Went on a really busy night, so I decided to give it another chance since the music was good. I went back on a Monday and there was a $5 cover. The music wasn't great, but not bad either. The service was possibly just as bad empty as when the place was packed. The staff had an attitude and seem annoyed to their jobs. I've been a cocktail waitress for years. This was by far the worst service experience I've ever had.

I recall watching the Grand Ole Opry on TV growing up, so when I had a business trip to Nashville, I just had to stop. It sits in a shopping mall district, surrounded by stores. But walking up to the doors, I knew I was standing on sacred ground, where many legends had once walked. I was never a country music fan growing up, but I grew to love it when I was just 15 years old. This place is such a historical place. I didn't get to see a concert there, but just looking around the inside and outside of the building, I was in awe. If I'm ever in Nashville again, I will definitely be sure to check it out a second time. You can just feel the energy radiating from the walls. Some of the greats were made at the Grand Ole Opry!

We started with the pretzel's and cheese. They microwaved frozen pretzel's they were too chewy, the cheese was not warm enough it was thick & clumpy. The burger was OK. the fries were terrible, as if they cooked them, then allowed the to sit in the oil to cool off. The replacement fries weren't much better.  I am gonna say if u wanna eat, this is NOT the place to do so. The beer was warm & overpriced. All in all u can skip this place. If u come for the music the let me know.

What can I say about an establishment I've been haunting weekly for the past 3 years? Flying Saucer is unique because of its loyalty program, known as the "UFO Club" where for every 200 unique beers you drink, you earn a plate on the wall along with a party in your honor (and subsequent amounts of bar tab paid every time you hit the mark) It has a loyal selection of regulars and friendly waitstaff that changes fully about once a year. I honestly love the place, but it is entirely imperfect. The atmosphere alludes to a German beer hall with a couple communal tables (and plenty of single tables), couches, and an open concept complete with garage doors that open during the summer. If you are really interested in craft beer, their Monday $3 pint night is the place to be and their Tuesday-Friday 4-7pm $4 pint happy hour is nothing to scoff at. There are several really good menu items, including cheese fries surprise, the soft pretzels, and the grilled cheese and tomato soup. Their beer list updates weekly with over 50 taps of craft beer from near and far. If you don't like beer, don't come here. You will be disappointed by their selection of other beverages. They have great events like trivia and special sponsored beer releases and glass giveaways. They are a destination for watching preds games. The drawbacks are few but can be extremely annoying. If the place is crowded, service is very, very slow. The restaurant is not staffed for extremely high periods as it is normally a pretty mellow place. If you aren't there to watch the game, avoid going during major sporting events. Overall, it's a great place to eat, grab a beer, and hang out with friends. I wish I could give half star ratings, because I truly think they deserve 4.5 stars.
Was able to have lunch here today.  I ordered bbq wings and buffalo wings and a spinach salad.  The food was really good as was the music.  I definitely recommend this place!
Smoky atmosphere and great people watching. Lots of seating was appreciated as we were wrapping up the night.
Great food for a reasonable price. Our server was friendly and efficient. We were early in the evening but there was live music. All in all a very good experience.

I have been to a number of Flying Saucers and am a member of my local here in San Antonio. As this was barely a block from my hotel I ended up here a couple of times due to great specials. On Sunday they had all Tennessee pints for $4. From 4-7 they have a social hour where all pints are $4 so I made good use of that. Like all of the Saucers they have a great selection of beers. The food is the same as all the others, which was a bit of a disappointment to me. The biggest issue I had is that the staff was 100% focused on locals and regulars. It took me flagging down the bartender in order to get my first drink.

Large space - cool upstairs. We didn't get too much service downstairs but we were checked on upstairs and it has a huge projection screen - which was perfect since we were in town for the SEC Tournament. It seemed a little empty when we came so I'm not sure why it took a while to close our tab. Either way, no big issues and we had a good time.
This is the BEST bar in Nashville!! In town for CMAFest and have been here everyday!!! Thanks to Lena and Key (best bartenders) for making memories with us!!!!
This place is so much fun. Bartenders are the coolest. the music is the best. Food? Don't even talk to me about the food. It's all good.

This place blows. Ten of us 20- and 30-something girls went this weekend for a bachelorette party with the sole purpose to do karaoke. Well, the karaoke hosts kept denying every request we made (selected from THEIR BOOK) saying "they don't do slow songs." They were country, not slow. Then, they themselves would sing slow songs.

In the half hour we were there, we never saw them let anyone else up on stage to sing despite it being a karaoke bar. They kept singing lame songs on their own. We got bored and left. We talked to the two older gentlemen greeting outside (who were very friendly, we should note), and they asked why we were leaving. We told them, and they said that was very typical. "Nobody ever gets to sing here," one said. :It's like the mafia."

Duly noted. I won't be returning. Who needs the attitude? We wandered directly across the alley to one of the other karaoke places, and they were not only nice, but let us up on stage within 10 minutes to sing. As a good karaoke place should do.

I was told by a friend to go eat at B B Kings BBQ and they wanted a $5 cover charge to eat. I said I'm paying to eat here and you are asking for a cover NO WAY. I'll find something else. No one else has covers.

Alright, what this place needs are really two different ratings: one for their music and one for their staff. First, I'd give the place five stars for their music. This is a go-to place of mine whenever visitors come to town, or I just want to see an amazing show in the round. Forget Bluebird, you'll never get in. Besides, this place is almost just as good except..

The service here deserves a solid one star. The staff here will actively ignore you. They will walk over to you, look you straight in the eye, turn right back around and head to go talk to the bartender. I've honestly been here probably 10 times in the last two years and have only once had good service, and it turns out that was the server's first day working there. 

The food is decent and the beer selection ok, but again beware of the staff. Sit at the bar if you ever want a drink.

Had a great time visiting John Rich's Famous bar, I checked out every floor to see what ambiance it had to offer! All around a great place to grab a drink and listen to some FABULOUS live music! I had the pleasure of meeting some greet staff members such as Brandon, Kayla, Kaylene, Calla, and Blair, hands down some of the BEST bartenders I have come across in this city as I work in hospitality downtown. Even the bouncers, David, Chris, and Colt were amazing. I also had the pleasure of meeting Colby, Michelle and Lacy. Solid team there!

Name describes access to a t.  I went around 6:30 and there were about 13 other patrons. Typical of most bars it is not somewhere you need to see in the light of day but you know that before you enter.  Inside was small, sturdy and clean.  

Waitress was prompt and recommended the Hawaiian burger with pepper jack cheese and fries.  Food arrived quickly.  The burger was great.  The fries ok and not from a freezer.  Waitress was perfect.

I will return.

I'll never go to this bar again. They were advertising a $2 shot special and when I asked a bartender about it, she refused to believe me. She and a coworker then spent 15 minutes ignoring other customers to wait near the digital screen to confirm the special I had seen. When it came back around on-screen, she took a picture with her phone, approached our table, and tried to chastise me for being rude. Like I made it up or something. I tried to call her out for treating a customer that way and she had me kicked out. Unprofessional, uncoordinated and rude. There are much better bars in midtown, and the crowd I saw here on a Saturday college football afternoon in the South proves it.
Slow ass service. Inattentive bartenders. No crowd. Over charge for drinks. WONT BE BACK. Will be closed in 1 year

We go to Flying Saucer almost every Tuesday for Trivia.  While the Trivia isn't the best because of the insane categories (Lamps, Hills, Pigs, etc.), we come back because of the staff, food, and beer menu. The staff typically remembers us, which is nice.

The best things on the food menu are the Bratzel, Prosciutto & Arugula Pizza, Chicken Wings, Pretzels, & Chicken Snack. I literally only order one of those items every time I go. This place has the best pretzels in town by far.

The beer menu is great too because it's large and constantly rotating. I'm a part of the UFO club (drink 200 different beers and you get a plate on the wall). They get a lot of "one and done" kegs so you can try new beers each visit. Love this place.

Came here for a happy hour event, and noticed they also have a scoutmob offer available! I was excited. 

So I got a beer to start off, since the waiter said all beers were half off for happy hour. I got a Guinness, and ordered a macho burger. The burger wasn't bad, but nothing out of this world, and the fries were pretty average. Then I got another Guinness and asked for the check.

...Apparently, Guinness isn't one of the beers on the happy hour. Way to not tell me, TWICE. Also, despite me having asked if I could use my scoutmob for the burger and the waiter saying yes I could, she didn't apply it since it was past 5pm when I left (I arrived at like 4:35). 

Not coming back.
Here for the first time on our 6 year anniversary date. We are seeing #Move staring Derek and Julianne Hough. Awesome show! If you get the chance see it!
Love all the History to this place!!! Did the tour, well worth it. Amazing feeling of all the greats that have preformed here.

This is such a great place to visit and experience the the artist and their music . It is such a historical place that should not be missed. There are back stage tour should you should go to see and hear the  whole history of this wonderful place. And if your lucky enough you might experience an induction of an artist to join the family at Opryland. 
A must visit place in Nashville. Its gift store is equally grand. If you buy tickets on a particular night you can get a commemorative poster from the gift store of that night. 
Def worth a visit.

Going to the Grand Olde Opry was quite the experience especially if you pair a show with the VIP backstage tour . The cost of the tour is pricey but I soon learned why . You can book daytime tours for a lot less, but you won't experience the best in my opinion. 

 I went the same night I saw a show so the likelihood of seeing a star or performer is very high .We saw Micheal Ray , Travis Tritt, Riley Green, and Carrie Underwood's husband Mike Fisher. 

You also get to sit backstage on the stage for 2-3 songs of the first performer. The highlight of the tour for me was being behind the curtain with the countdown and that curtain rises and you see all the people, lights , performers and just take in that precious moment. It's a moment you won't forget because it's so unique, special, and unforgettable . You feel like a performer yourself for a split second .

If I had one negative to say about the tour I would say the photograph wasn't very good because of the lighting but other than that really enjoyed being VIP for 30 minutes. 

Money well spent to be an extra part of history. Seeing a show there is amazing as well. I saw a show the Tuesday before CMA Fest and it was a fantastic lineup.

Food was excellent! I had some appetizers in the afternoon here, then came back that same day and had the gumbo and salad. Everything was really tasty and not too expensive. The entertainment was excellent! One of my favorite places so far on my first trip to Nashville, and I'm usually not a blues/jazz fan.

We came here on a Friday evening for dinner. We ordered drinks, mine being a Cherry Mule which was awesome!!!! The menu wasn't lying when it said "It's really good!"  We left the downtown bar scene on Saturday evening and walked back to the Flying Saucer to once again get a Cherry Mule, only to be told they were out of the ingredients! The waitress suggested the Moscow Mule instead. My husband ordered something totally different, but I went with her suggestion. A few minutes later, she came back and said they didn't have the ingredients for that either! Very disappointed. Should have stayed downtown instead of wasting the trip. So out of the 9 cocktails listed on the menu, they could not make 2 of them.

Just ok. The atmosphere here is really odd. The servers weren't super friendly and had no personality. The music selection was a combo of some decent oldies and some weird, depressing music. 

I was expecting to have a lot more beer choices based on the photos from yelp, but was disappointed. They had a large selection, but when I started looking at overall options of what I wanted to drink, didn't seem like there was anything there I really wanted to try. 

I was hungry and wanted to order food but the place was creepy overall and I just wanted to leave. I did not want to stay any longer than I had to. The whole experience was best described as "strange". 

It was an older building and it felt dark and sad. It's very rare for me to walk into a place and want to leave immediately. The area outside the main building (there were two main seating areas) seemed to have a better feel to it and was more updated, but inside, the plates on the wall were tacky and the tables and chairs were old. It reminded me of something from a haunted/ scary movie or a run down museum. I would NOT go back. 

One positive thing that I liked: The night I went, they were having specials on all pints. So my draft beer was only $3. If you can sit in the outside (covered area) and enjoy cheap (good) beer it might be worth it to go.

Since I'm not a recording artist and unfortunately have never gotten the opportunity to watch a live show at the Blue Room, this review is first and foremost for the little store attached to the facilities. 

It's Disneyland for Jack White fans, fans of his record label, or really music fans in general (though the former will get the most out of it). A small space crammed with merch for purchase, old school instruments and contraptions, and lots of records. I saw several people come in with their guitars to take advantage of the recording booth where you can get a record pressed on the spot. I didn't have a tune to record, but left with a couple of records to play at home and a photo strip from the very old school photo booth (it only works some of the time according to the staff). Speaking of the staff, they're all super sweet and friendly and willing to help you out with anything. It's a fun, quirky spot a bit off the beaten path in Nashville, and worth a visit if you're interested in checking out some tunes, music history, or kitschy paraphernalia.

This was not a good dining experience. I understand that the focal point of this place is the beer, but the dining shouldn't be neglected. We ordered the Queso fondue and some tots to share. My friend ordered a sandwich. Her fries were very stale. The celery and carrots that came with the fondue was wilted and browning. My friend's soda was flat and when she asked if she could get another, the waitresses response was, "well, all of the soda is going to be like that". Our waitress ignored our concerns about the  meal and didn't apologize at all. I'm only giving two stars because of the beer selection, otherwise. This place gets one. We should have listened to our cab driver who mentioned that this place had poor service!

I live in Nashville and have frequented this establishment for many years. I love the people & atmosphere at Ms.Kelli's. 

It surprised me to read some of the other reviews bashing the ownership & long-time employees. I suppose everyone has their own unique experiences, but in 6 years never has the staff treated me or any of my friends with disrespect. They are just people like you & me- decent folk who love alcohol & karaoke.

It's a very low key place to hang out. Just relax, go in and bust a move! So, if you're looking for a chill place to drink, sing and/or dance without feeling like everyone is judging you for having fun, then you will probably like it. Drinks are reasonable & the music is good.

As a karaoke host myself, back in NY, I have found my Tennessee homies!
This place is alive on an early summer Thursday night. I wish there was this much enthusiasm every time I ran a show in the Big Apple. But I'll hold out hope. Can't wait to sing on the stage and try to represent New York.
I didn't go inside but I walked around it's very beautiful! It's near a mall with lots of places to eat and shop.

IVisited Opry Country classics on Thursday 3/21 ,the show was fantastic,
Had a terrible time with the post show tour could hear the tour guide
, Goup 1, not coherent when speaking
Did not spend enough time with explaining about dressing room
Camera  did not work  for  free Ryman souvenir photo !!!!
I expect so sort of reimbursement. 
Order # 3296768

I love this place because of their great selection of brews. The service in this place keeps getting worse. They offer a UFO program where if you drink 200 beers you get a plate on the wall. Great marketing and just a money trap. But the atmosphere is good and the food as well. I want to see this place go forward not backward

Redneck Riviera started in Las Vegas. We went several times a week. Loved the place and they had great bartenders. Affordable drinks and an awesome sequence saddle. We were sad when we found out it was closing. We never found another bar we liked as well as RNR. When it opened in Nashville we knew we would have to take a trip to Nashville. So here we are. Our favorite bartenders Alyssa and Brook left Vegas and came to Nashville to keep working at RNR. They are both great. I can see why Rich invited them to join him in Nashville.

RUDOLPH Absolutely the worst show I have ever seen. I would've been laughing at it if I had not invested almost $400 on two tickets that were actually in the back of the theater. They were not 2nd market tickets, I purchased them off the official GOO website two months prior to our vacation. Ridiculous costumes and poor makeup on all. We felt sorry for the "actors" there was not a way for them to shine at all. The props looked  like a grade school play. The music was prerecorded too. We heard many people complaining.  We actually left during the intermission. It was a bad choice on my behalf but we always dreamed of going to the Grand Ole Opry.  This should have been for young children but we only saw a handful. Who can afford over a $150 tickets for kids?
Wish I didn't have to pick any stars

P.S.  I have only done reviews a handful of times and all but one was positive

Went on a Sunday night for dinner. The hostess was on the phone and didn't even look at us. Another person happened to be standing there and took us to our table.  Had a good view of the stage and the 2 acts we saw were very talented and entertaining. Our server was rude, abrupt and seemed put out when we asked a question about the beers, then was abrupt when we didn't order dinner right away.  Out drinks came and he basically slammed them down in front of us.  We had the BBQ ribs and they weren't anything special. 
Wouldn't go back.

Saw this place featured on the food network.  We decided to give it a try for lunch that day.  They had immediate seating.  We sat almost right in the middle of the restaurant which made it easy to take in the decor.  We ordered the jalapeno appetizer which was amazing....a little on the hot side but flavorful.  We went with burgers for lunch which were not disappointing.  Definitely filled us up.  The vast variety of craft beers was overwhelming but we did our best to navigate the menu and choose what we thought we would enjoy.  So many options!!! If I remember correctly, you have a limit on number of beers allowed per visit.  I think it was 4, so don't plan a night out on the town and expect to get drunk here.  This is a nice place to meet up and catch up.
Awesome spot to hit up if you're in Nashville. You'll find it hidden in music row. The famous Jack White from the White Stripes owns it. Defiantly a must see for music lovers.
Food was great and the best part were the bar tenders! So helpful and nice, best customer service!
The tall blonde manager was INCREDIBLY rude. Because we weren't cheering for the Browns he made a point to be disrespectful to us. I would not recommend it. There are better places on that street.

Terrible service! We sat upstairs to watch the games, there was only two bartenders to man the entire place and it was a busy NFL Sunday. No table service, you had to order through the bar. It took almost an hour and a half to get our two appetizers, and my boyfriend had asked twice where our food was and got a "the kitchen has ten tickets..." excuse however I watched other people who ordered after us (things like burgers whereas we got mozzarella sticks and fried pickles) get their food faster. Food was decent standard bar food.

We loved it!! We came in just for a little getaway. We looked in advance to see who was playing. Sara Evans...We looked up some of her music and it was familiar so we thought we would give it a go. Absolutely no one else was familiar. It is Dolly week so a lot of the acts had some connection or a favorite song. We enjoyed almost every single act! We were pleasantly surprised that Sam Williams is Hank Williams' grandson...he did his dad and grandpa proud and performed well!! I loved how well timed the acts are. It starts on time and finished on time. No crazy marathon applause...at the end the curtain shoots down and lights come on.

If you were in Nashville this is a must-see, hands down! It was truly the highlight of my trip. 

I was super lucky and got a great headliner show that included Trace Adkins and the Charlie Daniels Band. I have no idea how I lucked out. What impressed me most about the Opry was how they have 8th bands play in 2 hours. They streamline this like pros.

 Basically they have the Grand Ole Opry band and then the headliners come and Play 4 songs oh, that's it. And then the next band comes on. The whole thing is televised so it's funny how you hear the announcer say 'this part of the program is brought to you by blah blah blah'.

 I don't know how they do it but it seriously was the best orchestrated show I have ever seen.
Music was very good, but service wasn't really too good hostess and server weren't friendly. The food was pretty average as well.
Amazing! I have never been to a bad show. By far the best sounding music venue I have ever been to! I highly recommend a backstage tour as well.

Ms. Kelli's kicked my friend out for wearing a shirt with no sleeves. Mind you, this friend of mine was male, cut, and showing off some 'suns out, guns out' and looking good while doing it. If a Nashville bar is trying to stop a man from showing his true colors (and jacked arms) then I don't want to be part of their clientele. I walked in with a tank top on and was easily let in. This kind of sexist behavior should not be tolerated in such a progressive city.

I love this place. We went to the Cirque Dreams Holidaze show. This is our second time going to this show. It was amazing once again. We will definitely check it out again next time we are in Nashville!

I used this venue for a client launch party last night.  I can't say enough great things about the staff at this venue.  Kelly and Amanda were so incredibly friendly, helpful, and flexible.  The ENTIRE staff at our event was friendly and fun.  They showed my client and our guests an amazing time.  Southern hospitality at it's finest.  

The BB King All-Stars Band was AWESOME!  They really helped to make our event a fun experience.

Great venue, Great food, and best of all... GREAT STAFF!  I can't wait to host another event in Nashville at BB King's...  THE BEST!!

The Tippler is a bit hidden in terms of where I normally jaunt for a drink after class or work but I've been here twice now and have been equally impressed each time. The inside is pretty large and there is a dining area separate from the bar. It's dim lighting and fairly average noise level, I recommend it for catching up with a friend or for a date situation. 

The first time I came here I was SUPER impressed by their cocktails but could only handle two because they were a wee bit strong. The next time I was debating between a cocktail and wine, and opted for wine. At first I thought I had made a huge mistake since their cocktails were so great previously, but when my wine came out it was fabulous as well, so disaster averted. This place definitely has their drinks on par.

I recommend the chicken biscuits AND the churros (omg) for dessert. Normally churros bring back memories of overpriced, lukewarm chewy breadsticks that I bought at the state fair from a man missing an unusual amount of teeth. These churros were so much better, and have replaced all nightmarish memories of churros from my past. They are clearly homemade and come out with a salted caramel dipping sauce that is sooo good. 

I also really appreciated that the manager on duty (Emily I believe was her name) came out to our table to check on us and see how everything was. She was very friendly and offered to give us a tour of the restaurant which I really appreciated! We were too full to take her up on her offer, maybe another time. Emily also let us know that they are coming out with a new seasonal food and drink menu sometime in February, just another reason to go back!

So get a few drinks, order the churros (obvi), and you are guaranteed a good experience at the Tippler.

Like something from out of this world (how clever am )I I just had one of the best burgers ever. The darn thing is not on the menu...a little tip-you can ask for it anyways.  It was the Royale Burger: a thick and juicy 1/3lb of Yummy topped with bacon, I could stop there right?  With the BACON are red onions, jalapeños and cheese on that I think was a toasted bun. I paired that with, not French fries, their version of tater tots.  The tots are some combo of tot and jalapeño that's served with a cream cheese concoction that balanced the heat nicely. 

My only regret, I had to work and couldn't get any of the 1000 beers to choose from. Thirsty man!  Two forks for the Saucer and that 2-fisted Royale.

Perfect for a beer enthusiast! The building itself is worth a stop. It's beautiful! Our server was great and very knowledgeable, which is awesome because there are SO many beers to choose from. We split the bratwurst plate and tried out a couple of new beers. The food was good and was just what we wanted to go with some beers. If we had more time in Nashville I'd love to have gone back in the evening and sampled a few more brews.

(This goes out to the previous whiny reviewers) This is a beer bar! Come here if you like beer, good beer, flavorful beer, beer that is so good it doesn't need to be served at 33 degrees! Order some good beer! Then, order some snacks so you can drink more beer. We liked the pretzels and the tots. Do not come here looking for a good dining experience. It's a BEER BAR!

The fact that I have checked in here more times than any beer bar in my own home town shows you how much I adore this bar.
Best place to eat great bartenders and servers. Like one big family. Love this place.

Yes.

I love everything about this store, from the overall aesthetic to the small boutique feel of it to the great things that Jack White is doing to promote and re-issue important music. 

The color scheme of the store and of the 45s and 12" albums that are available in the store brings a great uniformity that makes everything feel so much more organized and sensible. I love that the only things available at the store are things that have been released on Third Man. If you are looking for releases by all your favorite bands, then this is not your store. 

I wish that more labels would do this, have a store front. Imagine if Kill Rock Stars or Merge, or Matador had their own store. I think that would be fantastic. 

That this is the only place one can buy certain singles and full lengths is great. Despite its size (incredibly small, one room) there are so many great surprises. I picked up a recording that Gibby Haynes did that I didn't know ever happened. 

This is so much more than a store: it's really representative of a mission. 

I can't say enough good things about this place. Get there.

This is a must if you're visiting Nashville. We bought tickets about a month before our visit for the backstage tour and the 7pm show.  I wasn't sure what to expect but it was fantastic! The backstage tour was pretty interesting and it was neat to go on stage. It lasted about an hour and then we went across the street to the mall to eat but I would've preferred to try the food trucks in front!  The drink prices are high! $12 for a single, $22 for a double, $9 for beer and $5 for water. We saw that Carrie Underwood was on the line up for this show so that was pretty exciting! I don't think the line up is finalized until the week of. Definitely worth the money and if I'm ever back in Nashville I will definitely do this again!

They just re did their menu and it's MUCH BETTER!

The bartenders, Shelby, Key and Maddy are super sweet and make great easy drinks. 

Service is quick and I'll be back :)

Also on Sunday's there's an 80s band called The Spazmatics; worth it!
Got the brisket. Incredible. Plus an amazing blues band to accompany my meal. Magnificent.

This place was an awesome find in Nashville. It has a LOT of beer. Probably at least 2-3 dozen on tap as well as in bottles. And it's not cheap beers, but an extensive selection of craft beers, with international and seasonal options. If you like beer, this is the perfect place to try a variety. Sadly, I was not there on a Monday, but apparently all of their beers are $3 on Mondays! 

Not only were the beers good, but the decor was also very creative. Their spacious main bar area has saucers lined all over their walls and ceiling. They also have a nice lounge area with couches and plenty of natural light, as well as rooms with pool tables. I loved the interior design in both areas. This place is a bit of a way from the downtown attractions on Broadway, but it's totally worth the (relatively short) trip!

Best part about this bar is that it is very clean inside and they have weekday live music starting at 11am. Our bar tender Calla was super nice and very friendly. She was busy yet had time to be personable. The music was good. A bunch of solo musicians happy to play together for music fans. People of all types and ages inside this morning. Started off with a couple of cold beers. No bottles, only cans and draft. Got a bit hungry and made a bad choice of getting a small bowl of chili. Didn't figure it was going to be poured from a can and put in the microwave. $10.00 for the can of Hormel. Not really a fan but then live and learn! I only sat in the downstairs area but they do have a second level. Not sure if there is live music upstairs later in the day and into the night. 
Metal bar stools are not so comfortable if you plan on hanging out for a while but then no one really stays long cat any one place on Broadway.

Once again great atmosphere, Great Music, Horrible wait times for drinks.  Front bar closed, rear bar closed, main bar one bartender for the whole place including service bar.  I watched countless people walk up to the bar wait 10 minutes only to leave in discussed.   Expect 10-15 minute wait for each drink.
Found this place while strolling around from my hotel. Delicious burger! Great little bar.

This can be no less than 5 Stars. This is the birth place of Country Music. So many legends have passed through the Grand Ole Opre House.

Well on in Nashville on this day and after finishing a project for work, I noticed a place to eat and by golly it's across the street from the entrance to the Grand Old Opera House. How can I not go in.

The parking lot is massive. The entire complex is like an amusement park. Hotel, water park, shopping, movie theater and of course the Grand Old Opera House. 

It's late afternoon and it's 96 degrees and I have to walk nearly a mile from my car to the building. A lot of posters of singers along the way and of course country music playing through loudspeakers. 

It was closed on the day I was there so I could only see the outside and the gift shop.

I admit I prefer rock music but don't frown on Country Music. Rap music and the like, nope, not for me.

Anyway just being there was a good experience. I would love to go for a show there one day. 

"The Grand Ole Ope" a piece of history. You must go there.
When you're in Nashville and you're a county music fan this is a must stop.  The tour was just the right amount of information and things to see.

If you're in Nashville, and a country music fan this is quite the experience!  I went on a Saturday night and saw Carrie Underwood and 4-5 separate artists.  Everyone plays for about 15 min, so 3 songs!  The place was packed and all artists were so humbled playing the Opry...a Nashville institution.  It's close to the Gaylord Opryland, so you're looking at a 20-30 min drive, and depending on traffic from downtown Nashville!
Worst bar service ever. Was totally ignored here. Life is too short to spend in dumps like this.

Excellent entertainment. All young artists trying to get a name for themselves and extremely talented. Infact we met a brand new contestant on The Voice at Belcourt. She performed and wowed the crowd. A great place all around. All waitstaff excellent. For great local talent, check this place out!

This is a nice location for the Opry though I prefer the Ryman. The location is easy to get to and there is ample parking for a reasonable  price, though the Opry tickets can be steep.
