There are several large screens which make viewing enjoyable. The restrooms are ok but expect lines and  paper towels should always be an alternative for those of us who choose not to use blowers.

WOW!!! What a FUN venue and fun staff!! Be sure to ask Stu at the bar to sing for you! If you're lucky (or tipping well!!) he'll serenade you and the whole bar!! JJ manning the Karaoke booth is ALSO a star!! Ask him to sing Walking in Memphis!! So talented. Also the blue fishbowl drinks are amazing and dont taste like alcohol at all, so be warned!!! Drink is slow and steady or else you'll be the FIRST one on the karaoke stage! And don't worry, you'll sound great....
JJ and Stu opened a WHOLE HOUR EARLY for me and a group of 10 who were coming from a holiday Christmas party- so accommodating!! They have basically every song too, so pick anything! We sang everything from Mama Mia! to Pat Benetar to Christmas Songs to I'm Proud to be An American! So stop on in and have yourself a drink and a sing! On the other side is Tequila Cowboys too! So you can bar hop without even leaving the building!
Great gentrified and redone building rescue turned into ultra hipster bait shop with lots of exclusives and rarities.

Terrible customer service at the door. We watched numerous people walk in - no pay. However, when our group of 7 older women approached the desk -the host demanded $5 cover 

When we asked what kind of table we could get - only a "non drinking " table was available to us. We are 7 grandmas just looking for a quiet place to listen to good music, while still able to have a conversation 

Would not recommend this place - music great but not welcoming!!
This place was absolutely amazing! I loved learning the history of this place and why it's so important to country artists! The prices are alright but highly recommend if you are in Nashville!

Great place! What really separates this pace from the other bars in Nashville is the outstanding service. I have gone here with a group on a few occasions, every time our group comments to each other how the service is what truly makes this place enjoyable. Shelby and Maddy are great. They are probably the best two bartenders in Nashville!

Came on Sunday! Great band and atmosphere!!! Only bummer, I had went shopping earlier that day and left my purchases in the restroom by accident. Unfortunately, not even an hour after I left and someone had already stole my stuff and trashed the shopping bag in the trash Not DawgHouse fault but it still sucked.

We were looking for a non-country place to enjoy some food and live music and this was one that came up our first night to check out. The po boy was OK, not amazing. The bbq was good according to my husband. The service was wicked slow despite being a Monday and not packed to the rafters.

My husband, nephew, and I like country music, but it was our nephew's wife and 9 year old daughter who REALLY wanted to visit. It's not inexpensive, but our AAA discount brought the 4 adult tickets down $8. After spending a little more than an hour on the tour, we realized that what we paid was well worth it. 

We had to go through a metal detector and bag search. Then Lynzee, our tour guide, led us to a small auditorium for a 3D movie that required no 3D glasses. We recognized more of the performers than we thought we would, and knew more about the history of the Opry and its stars than we gave ourselves credit for. Now we were excited to see the auditorium itself and all of the dressing rooms. 

Lynzee took us backstage, showing us the path the stars travel, from the parking lot, past the Minnie Pearl statue, up to the metal detector & security guard. We walked to the "Post Office" where the stars receive fan mail - address your letters to the star of your choice, in care of the Grand Old Opry, Nashville, TN. They'll get your letter. We saw the names on plaques of all the musicians inducted into the Grand Old Opry. We sat in the family room/waiting area to learn more about the building and look at photos on the wall. One large mural had the water mark from the 4 foot flood. 

We walked past the dressing rooms, each with a guitar pick painted on the floor, with the number of the dressing room on each. Next was the stage, and we were able to stand in the circle behind the microphone, posing for a photo ($25 for 8x10, 3 5x6, and digital code to download the image), staring out at the auditorium that accommodates 4,400 customers. It is definitely a holy place, with cushioned benches resembling church pews. We had no time for the evening performance, but we hope to return to see the musicians play in this Grand Old Opry.

Enjoyed the free live music in the early afternoon before this area got super busy. Specials included 2 for 1 drafts and a few 1/2 priced appetizers. Server has a list of local drafts but no description of each of them. The food as decent, we enjoyed the pulled pork nachos and catfish po'boy.
We took the backstage tour with Randy and had the best time! Not a hard core country music fan, but found the tour to be fun, informative and interesting.

Never been before.  Tonight the 7 of us went to see the 700 show then the 930 backstage tour.  It was great.   Our tour guide was awesome and even better she was from bklyn/Staten Island like us.  She was a great tour guide and extremely nice.   My friends son got kelsi ballerini's autograph so that was even better.  Never did a tour like that before.  We were all glad we did

Yes, it's a chain...but each location has it's unique quirks!

This locale is really awesome! If you come for anything else, you come for the views and the history of the place. Rhe whole area has a really cool vibe.

Ok, apps...get the pretzels with queso and the cheese...go ahead and ask for extra cheese because you're gonna want it, promise! They also have a good variety of local beer draft and can. You really can't go wrong! Just pull up a stool or lunge on the oversized comfy chairs. If you're not sure of what to drink, get a local flight. You can't go wrong. For the more experienced pallet, build your own. All in all, it's a great place to chill. I'd recommend Frist Museum before you go. Both places are worth taking a stop and stroll through.

First time at "The Grand Ole Opry" it was pretty unusual. We were expecting it to be downtown by the Ryman Auditorium....Not the case...this located Right across from a Huge Mall and Super touristy. Do not let this deter you from the show! Once inside it is an AMAZING VENUE...very intimate and nostalgic..GREAT SHOW
HOWEVER EAT BEFORE YOU GET THERE.

DO NOT EAT HERE AND drinks are REALLY EXPENSIVE

First time in Nashville and this was our first stop. Steve, our bartender, was amazing!  Had a bunch of great stories, treated us like he had known us for years and most importantly the food and drinks were awesome!  I am a bbq snob and the ribs at B.B. Kings were some of the best ribs I've ever had!  We are here four more days and will be back for sure!

Howdy Nashville let me say that the GOO is a slice of country music and Nashville history. Not a bad seat in the house the staff the facility are second to none. The entertainment of course is top notch country music's who's who... 
Check out the line up the only thing I would suggest chose a section in the lower or upper level that faces the stage.

So here is the deal.  I walked into this blues bar and was seated in the most horrible seat ever.  I mean ever.  Now, this was on a weekend night and I did not have reservations.   Regardless,  I was not going to sit on that seat for hours and watch the band and drink Guiness.  So, I proceeded to leave.  I was leaving and the manager stopped me and asked me what the was the problem.  I told him. and poof, he found us a seat that was acceptable considering the circumstances.  Bottom line, that manager fixed the situation in a disarmingly calm manner,  without any notice and within seconds.  I did not catch his name, bit it was in the evening of course.  I am writing this post 8 months later while I'm scheduling my next trip back to Nashville and BB King.  The food, restaurant,  the service,  and the music was fantastic!   We are going back and bringing relatives.  See you soon!
This was my second visit to Nashville and this is my favorite by far! Noah Garner is an excellent entertainer! I highly recommend that you check this place out when he is there!

As a team, my group felt the service was lacking. We arrived at 11:10am (they open at 11) and we were one of two tables there. From the time we ordered to when we received our food it took about 45 minutes and the waitress never once checked on us. It then took around 10 to 15 minutes for the waitress to return with our checks after we had given our cards to pay. Our team was a group of 8 people so gratuity was included in the check but to be honest, I was tempted to subtract the tip from the bill. If only I could have done that.

Despite myself enjoying my food, the chicken and rib platters, most of the team members did not enjoy their food. The best part of the experience was the live music. That just hit different for some reason. Perhaps being hungover tainted our experience but it didn't seem great. A team at a neighboring table actually decided "ight, imma head out" and went ahead and left. 2 stars, would maybe go again.

I recently visited the Grand Ole Opry, and although this was not my first visit, it was as magical as my first time. I love country music, and I love the family mentality this venue exudes. The history of WSM and the Opry show is not lost when you walk in the door. Plus, there are always multiple artists who grace the stage each show. I would highly recommend visiting the venue regardless if you enjoy country music or not.

Overview: there's no "having ourselves a big and rich time" at John Rich's Redneck Riviera. This bar is located on lower Broadway, close to 3rd Ave, and across from Kid Rock, Jason Aldean, and Luke Bryan's rooftop bars. I'll begin with the view of Nashville from the rooftop..... I would've seen just as much from the sidewalk, and avoided the trek up their stairs (service elevator only). The staff didn't pay much attention to anyone other than the ones seated at the bar top, but I wasn't bothered by it. The highlight of the entire trip was the, slightly overpriced Angry Orchard I got. They have it ON TAP! That alone is why I score this bar at 3-5 stars. My opinion: You should continue "riding up and down Broadway" because there's nothing to see here.

As a beer lover, I was very Impressed with the amount of taps they had on the wall. The beer list was amazing. I went with a local vanilla stout that was dark and creamy. As for food I picked my own pie. I chose applewood smoked bacon, bratwurst and avocado. I was surprised at how good the pizza was for a pub type place. It was not greasy and the crust held up. It's a personal sized pizza so I almost finished the whole thing. If you're splitting with someone definitely order an appetizer as well. They gave thick slices of bratwurst and avocado which was nice and the bacon had good flavor. The only reason I'm taking 2 stars is because they don't have high chairs. I understand it's more of an adult establishment but since they do allow children I feel they should be available. There were plenty of kids when we were there. Other then that it's definitely a good place for beer lovers who want a good selection.

This is such a fun place, but the bartenders were absolutely horrible. When I asked for drinks I needed to provide 4 IDs for all the people who were drinking, but it was only two drinks for two people. The people I was with ordered 3 drinks without question. I understand that it can be hectic and there are young people that show up but this was completely unreasonable.

This evening was quite the eye-opener for what type of establishment Belcourt Taps is all about. I was there for an hour before I witnessed a truly horrific incident. I saw a man cornering a woman and yelling at her for calling him a "d**k." The owner, Rose, walked over and automatically said, "I don't care what you said I'm on his side." She allowed the incident to escalate and did not shut it down. As a man in this society, I would never corner a woman and start yelling at her. This is unacceptable and honestly hurts to witness. Afterwards, I was outside listening to the conversation of the owner and the woman being yelled at, and she stated "he [the man yelling at the woman] makes her millions and y'all [the woman's boyfriend and friends] make me nothing." If a business owner only cares about money and not her customers then I'm sorry, I will not be coming back and do not recommend Belcourt Taps to anyone.

Great beer selection and solid bar food.  Consistently awesome service.  Never stupidly busy.  Go here to get away from the mania of Broadway and have a civil conversation with friends over delicious beers.

Let me start by saying the interior design of this place was awesome. My first impression was an instant feeling of not being cool enough. 

We were seated quickly which was nice and greeted by our server. We couldn't hear a word she was saying it was so loud. We had to repeat our order a few times and she finally got it. The menu was rather small and they were out of a few things. The server told us some items were out of season, why put them on the menu if you opened last month? Guess what? The menu is paper, reprint it. Or have some specials to make up for it.

The food arrived after quite a while and it was kinda funny how small my plate was. Ordered scallops and there were 3 quarter sized scallops over half a handful of lima beans. It was tasty but as an entree, left me starving. Other people in our party were less than impressed with their bland panera like paninis. Two of the guys didn't even finish the sandwiches since they were so bad. These are clean your plate kinda guys we are talking about. All in all. It was overpriced and underwhelming. I never mind paying good money when going out. I do mind when we go out, order a full dinner and drinks and everyone is ready to go to another restaurant because they are still hungry. Step it up tippler, too many amazing restaurants in Nashville to mess around.

I'm sure this place is better for drinks than food, but we went at lunch on a Saturday and were one of only two tables of patrons in there and service was still horrible. Took about 45 minutes for two burgers to come out and they were not good. The one bartender/server that was working was kind and apologized for the wait, but still, it was ridiculous and the food wasn't worth it. Only giving two stars because the guy was nice.

The Disneyland for Jack White fans. I wouldn't call myself a Jack White expert, but I'm definitely a fan and have enjoyed listening to his music both during his White Stripes and solo career. Third Man Records has been on my list of places to visit while I'm living in Nashville so when I had a friend in town that wanted to go, I was pumped. Third Man Records is in Sobro so parking can be a bit tough. Luckily, we got dropped off for the day so it wasn't a problem. The outside is pretty cool. Sleek and modern. It makes for a nice touristy photo. If you don't already know, Third Man Records is a few things. First and foremost, it's Jack White's independent record label. The Nashville location (there is also one in Detroit) is the headquarters for the label and also a record store and music venue. I NEED to make it to a concert at The Blue Room. It's sounds awesome. The record store has a lot of interesting things. Yes, it has a lot of records but it also has books, clothing, old record players, instruments, and more. If you're a Jack White fan, stock up! There is plenty here and it's all at a reasonable price unlike other souvenir places. Another cool addition to the store is an old machine that lets you record your own record. It was broken when we were there but the worker explained it a bit. You can record a short song (I think about 2 minutes) for $20. Now that's a unique souvenir! If I was actually a singer I would totally be into this. Or it might even be fun just to do with a group of friends. You can say you recorded a song at Jack White's studio. They also do small tours if you want to learn more about the label and studio. We just wanted to check out the store and get something for a friend. While the store isn't huge, it's definitely a Nashville must!

Their signature cocktail was really good. It had peach juice and whiskey. They are apparently known for their whiskey and their whiskey did not disappoint. I'm not a shot person but was able to take two ad their whiskey is really smooth. They do have like music, so it is loud.
One of my favorite spots to go in Nashville! Friendly staff, good food, tons of TVs, and a great atmosphere! Best Sunday Funday spot in Nashville!
Very psyched we got to stop in here on our weekend in Nashville.  Had to curb myself with all the schwag available.  Staff was also super cool and nice.

Our group did the Grand Ole Opry House tour and thought it was a great experience in how they let us go through all the steps that a normal artist performing would go through. Standing on the stage at the end to get a picture was awesome! I would love to attend a show soon.
First place we went when we got to town. It was exactly what I thought it would be. Multi levels from multi different scenes. Will definitely go back.

We popped over here on a quick road trip from Huntsville, AL, and we had no regrets. They had an amazing singer, and she had one of the most powerful voices I've ever heard. Apparently, she stepped in for Stevie for a few years with Fleetwood Mac. The house was packed when we arrived, but it must have been our lucky day because they had a 2 top that just opened up. 

We both ordered the half rack of ribs, with mac and cheese, beans, and coleslaw as our sides. The major disappointment here was the tiny side portions. There was no more than 1-2oz or 1-2 bites per side. Nonetheless the meat fell off the ribs, and despite the tiny portion of mac and cheese, it was still mouthwatering.

If I'm ever in the South again, I'll be sure to stop at BB Kings!

Let me start by saying I went to FS two years ago with two coworkers and we loved it! It's a cool place and the food was very good so I recommend it for an good dinner with friends.

HOWEVER, this week I went for a corporate dinner and it was a hot mess. We arrived and the room for our event was HOT when we entered so you can imagine how it felt once we added 40 bodies! We were also give ONE waitress. The poor girl did a very good job but she was not set up for success at all. It took a loooong time for any food at all to come out and when it did come out it was not enough so there was about a 30 min delay before more food came out. As soon as dinner was done our whole party escaped the steam room to go into the bar area where the A/C actually worked. Moving areas was unfortunate bc we were there to hang out with our team but we were forced to split up to get to A/C. 

I would go again for dinner with friends but I would not have a private event there.

Literally the best food I've ever had 
It was bomb pls go there if you're visiting Nashville WOW

We had a long wait (over an hour) early on a Saturday night. That's about the only negative thing I can say about the experience. The service was top notch. Even during the wait, you could see service people running around and working their butts off. The food was awesome. We were here a few years ago and although I remember the food being OK, I didn't remember it being awesome. It was very good. And of course the music was phenomenal. Overall, this a an excellent experience and even though it is a tourist spot, I will return the next time I'm in Nashville.

I'm from Michigan so I definitely love everything Jack white does. The vintage recording booth that Neil young recorded a song in among many other cool things just to see. There are plenty of things to purchase Third man Records, White stripes, the raconteurs along with his solo career. There are a host of very talented artists that you can find on vinyl.

My wife went with her friends and I have been told the bartender had A terrible attitude toward them and grabbed their drinks from them and told them to get the F out of the bar then as the bouncers were escorting my wife's friends out she said that was unnecessary and was pushed by a male bouncer. This is with eyewitness accounts saying they've done nothing to be thrown out or harassed. Classless dirtbag place that men think they can push a woman. Let's see if I was there if mr tough guy bouncer working at a sh*thole dive bar would do anything NOPE. The owner is a lunatic yelling without even assessing the situation and the bouncers are a bunch of losers who couldn't make it in anything in life so they bounce for a living. Not the last you'll be hearing from me for sure.

Update: now I find out the reason the girl got mad was because she was asked for more rum in her drink!!! What an egregious act! He dare she ask for an alcoholic beverage to have more alcohol!! My oh my. I'm sure she's NEVER dealt with this type of rowdiness in a bar!!! Embarrassment.

I think I'd consider moving to Nashville just to be able to eat these amazing lick your fingers, plate and any sauce off my sig others face on a regular basis. Amazing ribs is only one feature, but a major one. Just love this spot.

Travel to Nashville area for business every few months and this has become a go-to for belly bliss ribs. The three times I've had them, consistently tender, juicy, and flavorful. The sauce has a bit of a vinegar base adding to the twangy yumminess and can order plate with as few as 4 ribs or as much as a full rack. And these aren't tiny ribs, expect meaty and perfectly made.

Along with many other southern plates of goodness, another fave is the mac & cheese and their thinly sliced fried pickles. The mac & cheese is creamy with a mix of cheeses sprinkled on top and can be subbed in place of the standard pork beans or cole slaw for $2. Well worth it if love your m&c with bbq.

Add to the great food, atmosphere! It's located just off the main Nashville strip near several other colorful venues of good eats and live music.The decor is colorful and fun. And if you happen to be there in the evening, the live entertainment doesn't fail to add to an enjoyable dinner.

Don't like leaving negative reviews, but... Here was our first impression of Belcourt Taps. This is on a Saturday at 3:00pm. We sat down, and after 10 minutes we asked the girl working where we could get some menus. We got the menus ourselves and went back to our table. 10 minutes later, she still hadn't come to even take our drink order (what, that would've taken a total of 30 seconds?)... So being that we had come to a restaurant because we were hungry and expected to be served, we left.

This place was super fun. The singers were all really amazing, and the drinks were moderately priced. It can be pretty busy, so be prepared to wait for your song to come up. I also thought the no slow song thing was weird since the DJ clearly took some really slow moving songs throughout the night.

I love how this place is like stepping back in time. It's pure 70s. The lighting, the flooring, the windows and bar, all feel like something Mr. Brady would have designed. It's such a forgotten era, though, and so wholesome (the tenor of the entire show), that I fully appreciate that it's housed in vintage theater. The acoustics are pretty great, too.

What "scammers" these people are!!  We are from California and will be visiting Nashville in mid May.  Bought four tickets, three weeks ago, to see one of our favorite groups play.  Now the Opry changes groups and will not refund tickets.  They say it is posted on Home page and Ticket page in large letters that tickets are non refundable, even due to their changing groups.  The non refundable declaration is not posted on either page!  The only place the non-refundable statement is made is on the face of the ticket - once they get your money!!!  BEWARE!!!

We were staying at the hotel next door and headed over on a Friday night to satisfy our sweet tooth. Unfortunately we found this place is better for a night out but the dessert was pretty bland. We had the goat cheese crepes and they were definitely missing some flavor- could have used a good fruit to sweeten them up a bit. Service was fine but this is definitely geared more towards a bar crowd with a hipster vibe. Come for drinks but go somewhere different if you are just looking for something sweet. Be sure to being your ID- they'll turn you away at the door if you don't have it!

Pros: N/A

Cons: Probably best to enjoy a performance and skip the pricey tour. Tourist trap so tours are rushed. Don't get time to see the dressing rooms or enjoy being backstage. The most time allotted is taking of a photo onstage, which the option to purchase the photo.
Quick service and a great atmosphere. Host was very friendly the night we were there and kept the  music going. Beware the $4 bootlegger shots though lol. Beer only and no food here FYI.

I have been to a lot of concerts, but this was entirely different and an awesome experience! its way more
intimate than a concert, as in the artist talks to the audience. I cannot wait to go back!
Love this bar!!...the staff is always friendly and they give locals a discount on drinks!!  They have Golden Tee and Darts and a huge screen TV upstairs for watching football.

This is my favorite karaoke bar in Nashville. It's wholesome, friendly and the vibe is always positive. It can get super crowded, but the bouncers and djs are really good and keep things in order. I've never had any problems when I've been here and there's been times when I've gone by myself and have always been able to meet nice people. Service can be a little slow because it's so crowded, but the majority of the bartenders are pleasant and do their best to move fast. The food isn't bad. Just regular bar food, but it's pretty good. It's really the atmosphere that makes this place though. Always positive, lots of dancing and everyone who sings is supported. Good, bad or in between.

Arrived and hostess appeared bothered by us to where I had to even ask if she worked there or was there someone who did that could help us. Waitress immediately gave off the vibe that she was completely annoyed to be at work and waiting on a bigger table. Did not write one thing down, so of course our order was messed up. Had to ask for rest of our food, napkins, silverware and drink refills. Food was not good, chicken was really dry and bland. For the price we paid I expected much better tasting food at least. BBQ sauce was delicious and we had to coat the food in it. She did take off drinks and extras we ordered from our final check, which was nice but not the point. We were able to pay for what we ordered and expected decent service and good food, none of which we received. After all this the catfish dinner ended up making me sick so the ending to a horrible visit. Nice place to take pictures and the live music was really good but that's it.

The food was great, the music sounded fantastic and Amber was awesome!  We had shooters to start the night and had the catfish Creole / catfish poboy.  Amber made sure our souvenirs were wrapped up and secure and we never had to ask for refills or to remove plates.  The food came out fast and tasted great.
Slow service. Kitchen closes very early. Live music is good. Very small and cramped. There are better options in Music City.

The food was incredible. We have the chicken fried chicken and the ribs. We also started with the cat fish bites and some jambalaya. Everything was great. Emily our server was so helpful and welcoming. The music was great too. Highly recommend!!!

If I could give this bar 0 stars I would. The bartenders were awesome but when the bouncers are completely rude and disrespectful than I have a problem so please do something about the bouncers or no one should go there. It seemed great at first but if they hire people like that than absolutely not. Do not go here. Nashville has so many more bars that will actually look after you.  Thank you, next.

We just did the backstage tour with Lara.
Fantastic. hilarious. Full of life and energy. And that was just Lara. 
The tour is wonderful and you really feel like one of the family.

Always great drinks and a great atmosphere.  Unlike some of the other Country Music Star Bars, this locale does not overcharge and the staff has always been friendly and accommodating.  Please give this location a try!!!

Bar servicw was horrible. The bartender was nice, he didnt notging wrong... but it was only him at the full bar trying to take everyone's order. I understand it was on a Wednesday but wait was uncomfortable. This will not stop me from visiting in the future. Just a suggestion

As a lover of small record stores and many artists on the Third Man label, Third Man is the tops. I wouldn't want the store to be any bigger or change a bit! I had fun playing with the mini guitars, monkey band and browsing the records. I purchased some stickers (huge sticker fan, here) and a tee shirt. 
I geeked out completely at Third Man and recommend it to anyone traveling near Nashville. Can't wait for Third Man's Detroit location!

It's possible this could be the shortest review I've ever written. It goes a little something like this...

Waited 30 minutes (no exaggeration) for 2 burgers with fries. 
Said burgers were -- in a word -- terrible. Ordered mine rare - ate it well done. Over seasoned, small, thrown together. I've made better meals in my Easy Bake Oven. 
Service: lackluster (and that's being nice). 

With amazing restaurants like Burger Up, Pharmacy and Lockeland Table in town...why why WHY would anyone eat here voluntarily?
Good beer, good music, decent food, crappy service. Too bad; the music is impressive, but the food and the service just don't make it worth it. Save your money and your time.

I've got to say that I'm not a huge Country music fan (I know, I know... Don't rough me up too badly), but the show was out of this world.  The acoustics were amazing and the performers did a stellar job and were stoked to be part of the experience.  After a few hours of soaking it in, I found a new appreciation for the genre.

Good times (even if you aren't into country music)!

We went on a Friday night, April 26. It was horrible. The music   by John Conley was bad.  The announcer spent more time doing commercial ads than the singers spent singing. Wynonna Judd just stood on the stage and expected the audience to do the singing. Very dated.   I don't know if this was just a bad night or typical of the grand old Opry.

In Nashville but not in to country music? B B Kings Blues Club may be just the ticket. 
When we arrived we were told there was a 45 minute wait for a table.  10 minutes later we were seated in the heart of the action. 
Their house band,  The All Stars,  has an energy and sound that gets the whole place dancin'. Loud,  vibrant, fun!! 
Surprisingly the food is good too.  
Their chopped salad has generous amounts of blackened chicken,  egg and blue cheese along with typical lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and a tasty house dressing.  Shrimp tacos are another tasty choice. Service was quick and friendly.  

The music is what makes it memorable. BB King All Stars rock the house!

We were taken to BB King's for a night on the town during a corporate training meeting. Our group of 15 had a separate dining area to accommodate our party. 

We were all excited to let our hair down & hear some live music - even if we were at a tourist trap!! 

The night got off to a slow start. With only 1 waiter, it took quite a while just to get drinks ordered. And a few people never had orders taken! So when our waiter came back, we ordered apps & entrees all at once. We were on the company dime, so we ordered a smorgasbord of apps! Fried pickles ($5), catfish bites ($9), spinach dip ($9), crawfish poppers ($12), fried green tomatoes ($10), Gumbo Ya-Ya ($6-cup). The food arrived surprisingly fast - & there were several servers on hand to get the food on the tables! Now we're talkin'!! Everything was tasty - I think my #1 favorite was the catfish bites with remoulade sauce, followed by the Gumbo Ya-Ya - as a Mobilian who knows her gumbo, I didn't expect much - but this Gumbo Ya-Ya delivered y'all!!! It's so good!! Everyone loved it! It has the perfect consistency & perhaps more importantly, it has the heat factor we love!! 

For our meals, we again had a wide range, depending on how much or how little we gave a shit about trying to adhere to our diets pre-training....our choices run the gamut from Chicken/Ribs combo ($21), Bourbon Glazed Ribeye ($34), to Carolina BBQ Salmon ($26), Shrimp & Grits ($20), Chicken Fried Dinner ($15), BB's Pork Chop Dinner ($21), BB's Fork Tender Brisket ($21), Catfish poboy ($11), Hickory Burger ($13), Chopped BBQ pork platter ($15), Roasted Chicken Dinner ($16). 

I heard repeatedly the ribs were good, so if you're undecided, take it from the few meatzillas who were with us & get you some!! I didn't try the shrimp & grits which was disappointing because I wanted to try it! I heard it was good! 

I mainly focused on my dish - the Carolina BBQ salmon with creamed corn, andouille sausage, plump shrimp, & crispy onions. This dish proved to be a party in my mouth!! The fish was light, yet flavorful - the creamed corn was ok - missing something - but I loved the shrimp & sausage!! Awesome!!! Many people enjoyed mine :) 

And best of all, we couldn't get enough of the music!! The sang covers on songs like 'Proud Mary', Talking Heads, Chris Issacs, and many more! If we didn't have a Hummer limo outside waiting on us, we could've stayed for hours!

Thanks for the hospitality - even if it is in a kitschy tourist trap kinda way. We still embrace you. But we want a locals place next time. Thanks BBs for great food, fun & memories! :)

This was a fun night out. Good food, good music, good times. $7 cover charge to get in and the music makes it hard to talk but that's not why you'd go here. If you like blues music, looking for some good food and nice drink menu, this is a great place to go.

We came for dinner.  The tables were empty but they let us wait for 45 minutes so they can charge us for "cover". Finally got seated and took 20 minutes for the waitress to stop by because i went to complained for the wait.  I hope the food is worth it.  Terrible service.
Packed to the gills with goodies and musical secrets. And that staff, man... excellent folks. Always something up their sleeve.

I do not like having to bribe DJ's to not wait an hour to go to the mike.  The bartenders could not keep track of tabs and they seemed very disoriented.  If you are looking for a true Karaoke bar, its not terrible.  But for anything else, there is far better options available.

Music is 5 stars; service is 5 stars; no need for further justification. Drinks are 3 stars....strong but pricey. Ok maybe because where this is equals 4 stars. Food is 1 or perhaps 0 stars. Hummus app brought out partially frozen! Really? The next hummus...acidic and old. Blech! Doesn't anyone check this? Math equals 5+5+4+0 divided by something equals about 3 ish stars. B.B. would be embarrassed I think.

I had no idea I would have a good time.  I don't like country music, nor am I a fan of "Hee-Haw" [You kids out there have no idea what I'm referring to.  It's a TV show from back in the Stone Age].

Finding the place was a challenge (Got directions from 2 sets of employees and STILL got lost) and parking wasn't easy to find.  We got there and the people were as nice as can be.  Not Disneyland nice, but good-people kind of nice.

I had 2d row seats off StubHub.  I had no idea the seating was on wooden benches [kinda like church pews]. The crowd was nice, the MC was nice, the acts were nice.  Hell, I cried more than once at the damned music. 

I'd go back, no problem.  I am a NY city slicker and I had a good time.  I can say this because no one I know will read my review.  I think.

Great entertainment.  Band was amazing, people were dancing and having a lot of fun. Ordered the Yazoo Creole Catfish and it was really good.  Customer service was great.  Cover charge $5 per person upon entry which was well worth it.

If your military please stop here, bogo drinks. I would have rated higher but some guy bartender on the top floor, no names here, just tattooed up. Sidenote:RUDE! My friend who couldn't read the *service elevator only* sign walked into the elevator as he was talking to some guys says, "ummm ok it obviously says service elevator only." I hear him being rude and I turn around and say sorry she didn't see that. He just was not polite. Sorry for the rant but I just came back overseas from my second tour and almost wanted to punch his inconsiderate face off. Be kind and don't hire jerks. Another sidenote: Danielle is an awesome bartender!!!
Went to the opry last evening. Gray show with Bobby Osborne, Crystal Gale and others. Had a nice time. My only issue were the seats. Very tight and not comfortable at all

My best friend and I were first timers in Nashville, and stumbled upon the Dawghouse  while we were walking the streets. We walked in for a few drinks and ended up spending the rest of the day there because of the amazing staff. Shelby our bartender was amazing, great conversation and such a beautiful light to be around. Everyone was soo friend, the cheese curds and fried pickles were amazing. Cant wait to comeback!

If you are visiting downtown, put this bar on the list. Very fun karaoke bar. A lot of talent hits the stage, with a few funny drunks in between. Big bar with easy access to drink service all night. Highly recommend even for just an hour or two.

They served pizza by the slice hear as well and it was actually really good. Only downfall to my experience was a drunk guy grabbing woman trying to sing on stage. Security choked him out in front of everyone and then they took him in the back to god knows where.
Absolutely awesome!  Went out of there way to take care of everything I asked. Great food great staff oh yeah

Wow - there are dive bars with karaoke and then there are dive bars that try but end up just completely sucking. This is the latter.  On a Friday night the place is packed with more than enough volunteers for karaoke, but nope, the "DJ" (a young kid trying to look cool while he "spins" from an iPod...) wants to hear his own choices.  The music isn't bad-- actually some great choices-- but he'll only play the first 34 seconds of a song.  Then switch to something else. Seriously.  Someone needs to hand that guy a Ritalin-laced cocktail...

Yeah the bar is ok and they have Jell-O shots and all, but the reason you go into a basement karaoke bar is for the karaoke... Otherwise just rename it miss kelli's Jell-O shot bar.

Had a great time here on the 4th of July, as prelude to the downtown fireworks extravaganza.  We (me, my 3 young adult children, and son-in-law) got to the Club about 5:30 with plans to stay until about 8:30.  We were quickly seated and treated to great music, first a guitar soloist (Clint somebody) and then the BB King All-Stars.  The All-Stars were a special treat, featuring a dynamic soloist, Larry Springfield, who led the Club in a rousing rendition of the Star Spangled Banner, as well as a number of soul standards.

The music and atmosphere are the primary reasons I gave this 4 stars.  We had dinner there and the food was OK, but nothing memorable except that all of our orders came out from the kitchen either incorrectly or after much delay.  (Since we weren't in a hurry, the delay was no big deal.)  I had the BB King House Salad and Gumbo Ya-Ya, both of which were tasty, but the gumbo came out lukewarm.

This is another "must see" on a family trip to Nashville. We attended the daytime tour and we plan to go next summer for the VIP tour and show. It is an amazing experience. Truly a once in a lifetime!

Everyone needs to experience the Grand Ole Opry while visiting Nashville.  
GRAND OLE OPRY
Old Crow Medicine Show, Shenandoah, Matt Stell, Rachel Womack, Del McCoury Band, Waylon Payne and Jeanie Sealy.  We got good tickets row B seat 4 & 5.  Tonight the show was awesome!  You must do the Opry when in town!

Really cool history. Backstage tour was conducted really well by Kelly, super bright and fun! Got to see some legendary photos and dressing rooms. It sounds cliche, but you could feel the history and the lore when you're standing in the Family Room. 

Videos of Country Music Legends (including Shelton and Underwood) being asked to be a member of the Oprey while on stage and seeing them tear up really resonates with how much stock these guys out into this place/show. My favourite were the stories of Lil Jimmy Dickens, who I only knew the name of prior to visiting Nashville (I know, what a loser I am). 

I walked on stage and calmly said into the microphone, "Hello, I'm Johnny Cash." And as an adult-child I walked away with a smirk on my face because I knew he'd said the exact same thing on that exact same stage, countless times. 

Really liked the gift shop as well. It was very expensive but I walked away with a $34 red and white baseball shirt. Wasn't as tacky and lame as most gift shops, actually had some cool things. I almost walked away with a $9 labeled harmonica for gods sake. 

Only knock is I thought the building was bigger. Tour was very quick (45 mins) and I wish it was longer!

This was our first stop in Nashville and I'm so happy we went. The music was fantastic. And the food was amazing. I had the shrimp and grits and it was phenomenal. The banana dessert was also to die for. Loved every minute of the 4 hours we spent there!!!
Lame. Put in my song & tipped the dj. Place was empty. Never called me up. We'll never come back.
Out of several items , hot chicken sandwich was weak with little meat. Beer warm! Didn't mess up the he fries!

Doesn't look like much from the outside, but it's worth finding if your looking for food/drinks in the area north of Broadway. You'll find attentive service and perfectly fine food, created from scratch rather than from packages or frozen like many 'bar restaurants' offer.

This place is the real deal for craft beer. 

They have a massive tap wall, pictured below (behind me) with somethin like 50 rotating taps. They have triple that in bottled beers. And most importantly, the staff actually knows about beer- some of them even brew! There is a very extensive training process for all bartending and serving staff, so anyone you ask can answer questions about taste profiles, ABU,  color or finish, and most importantly, can make recommendations as needed. 

The beer isn't all. They have crazy happy hour deals, food specials (half price on Wednesday... what!), a beer garden patio, darts, and trivia on Tuesdays. They sometimes have live music, and there is parking around back through the garage gate (discounted with validation). They also have a large room for events and parties. Such a cool vibe in here, and awesome food.. definitely a step above typical pub fare. 

This is technically lower Broadway, but this place is much more for locals, which is partly why we like it! Five stars. 

Pro-tip: if you really like craft booze like me, ask about joining the beer club! There are great perks and it's a great way to track what you've tried.

WannaB's isn't your "let's go laugh at terrible singers" kind of karaoke bar. This is Nashville. The bartender or any random waitress could probably out sing the majority of people you know. Yes, there will be the occasional crappy singer. Yes, there will be a drunken bachelorette or 3 who try to work through putting a ring on it. However, my experience is that most singers are entertaining and worth the stay. If it ends up not being your cup o' tea, walk to the back and step over to the bar next door.

One of the best karaoke bars on broadway. Definitely a good time. If you want to sing be prepared to wait over an hour on a busy night. The bartender - especially with the purple hair- is super nice. Bathroom attendant was weird but the bathrooms were clean. Try the frozen lemonade!

This tour was just okay. The guide we had was very lackluster. The experience relies heavily on video clips as you move through the beginning part of the tour. After that, our guide would rattle off some information without any care that the group could all hear him. Some areas were small so we would have to take turns to get into place to take photos. Because of that, it would take a few minutes. The guide would move on before everyone was done, probably because they keep him on a strict time schedule. It was also quicker than I thought it would be and the building was small. I'm glad I went because it is a historical place but honestly, there was nothing about the experience that felt very grand.

Being a tourist in Nashville can be hard to navigate the city but a visit to the Flying Saucer was definitely a winning decision. We got the tip from a local and went with it, blindly yet fortunately. 

My family and I decided to try local beers, because what else would you do as tourists. Anyway, it so happened that the local beer special was $4 (unsure if this is a weekly occurrence). Anyway, we were getting peckish; in order to curb our hunger we decided to try the sampler. This included three appetizers at $14. All three were half sized but that was a deal we loved. We unexpectedly LOVED the bacon wrapped jalapeños and the big soft pretzel was a less surprising, delicious treat. Our waitress was the sweetest and helped ease our unfamiliarity with the place. 

All in all, I will be back. The area was easy to get in and out of and the atmosphere was perfect for beer with friends. Can't wait for my next visit to Nashville to visit soon!
We went on the back stage day tour and it was awesome. $33 bucks scored us a walk through everything including dressing rooms. Randy was our tour guide and he was great!

We came to the Flying Saucer for an informal work reunion. This was the first time I've been to this restaurant. I really loved the service! Alongside the service, the food was so yummy! My boyfriend and I split the pretzel appetizer which came with 2 big soft pretzels. They were perfectly soft and just the right amount. I ordered the German plate for dinner and loved the 2 different bratwurst. The sauerkraut was really good and fresh tasting. I recommend this restaurant to a home visiting the Nashville area.
We have been here several times for different venues and have always had great service, always clean, seats were comfortable with plenty of room to sit.

We were at the Flying Saucer for a birthday party. I hadn't been back in years because I hated that you could smoke in there, however I was pleasantly surprised to find that it's no longer an issue!

We were only able to have cold type foods as circumstances out of the control of Flying Saucer dictated that they had to do some building repairs. They made a good effort to provide tasty food anyway, and we had cheese plates, salsa and chips, bruschetta, pretzels and mustard as well. 

The service was great. Our server was really knowledgeable when she saw me struggling over their vast menu. Her suggestion was a delicious beer! 

The cons: 

PARKING. I paid $12 to park there for 2 hours. That's frustrating. While I appreciate their lot being available and also so large, it's a bit of a pain having to pay so much money to park there. 

Also, the experience of getting up to the restaurant from the parking lot is unsavory. The SMELL of the garbage next to the elevators is absolutely disgusting, and it's still cool outside. I can't imagine what it will be like once the weather turns to hot. The only other option were some construction stairs, and I wasn't comfortable tackling those in heels. 

I'd go back once they have their kitchen open again, but it won't be my first choice due to having to pay so much for parking.

This place has potential to be a great spot but it need some work. We came around noon on a Sunday to watch some football, eat and drink.  There was a lot of disappointment in my group because of several of the things we attempted to order, they were out of...both food and drink. 

Service was a tad on the slow side but the waitress we had was very sweet and busted her butt with our large group.  The food was ok and the drinks were good. It does get vey crowded during football games. I was told by the bartender that they normally charge a cover on Sunday's but didn't this week due to the new year. If that's true I would say it's not worth a cover as there is no live music or anything special besides tvs.

A new thing in Nashville.

I only had a (that's 1) drink - an unfortunate result of my rushed midtown boulevardiering - and I didn't go down to the lower bar (whuh?), so maybe I'll update this review.  The Jalisco Luau was tasty, delicately crafted, and intriguing, with just enough spice.  Prices are à la Holland/308/Patterson.

This is the bottom of the Adelicia building - with all the attendant high-end noveau riche / tall men with expensive designer plaid / women with 3-hour hair.  If it wasn't for the friendly doorman/host and laid-back atmosphere, this place could be uber-pretentious.  But it isn't.  An inevitable, and desirable, use of this space has finally arrived.  I hope the plebs don't ruin it.

UPDATE:  Oh gawd, the plebs have ruined it!  Stay at Whiskey Kitchen, you plebs!

Love the interior, great stuff inside. Fun buttons, great little monkey machine, photo booth.....prices a bit too high for an average tshirt. If there are more than 3 people in the shop it feels crowded and it can be noisy with people picking up the instruments all of the time....staff were friendly. Definitely a fun place to visit if you are a fan and/or visiting Nashville! You can be in and out in under 5-10 minutes!

Great place to stop in if you want a break from country music - I wanted some more blues and R&B. Great staff -amazing band with amazing horn section ! Both female and male singer tore it up!  

Sooo much fun!!

This place sucks!!!  Do not come here!!!  The bartender is rude.  I came with my coworkers of 6 and I order drinks for everyone.  She got two of my orders wrong and blame it on us.  I thought it was me.  So I had my coworker order our drinks.  She charge my card and refuse my drink.

What more can I say about the Grand Ole Opry?

When in Nashville, it's definitely a must see. We enjoyed walking around and taking it all in. So many talented singers have walked through these doors. I'm glad to have visited and learned a lot about the history of music.
I LOVE this place!! The ladies that work there are so nice, and hilarious! They didn't have a huge choice of records, but that was ok. The decor of this place was awesome, very cool vibe.
Chill bar with good prices and no line. Easy to find a seat and get your name on the list to sing. We hung out there for hours and had a great time.

The Dawg House Saloon was my first official meal when I moved to Nashville and it's your quintessential bar food. I ordered wings and my bf ordered a sandwich. The food came out very quickly and it was better than average bar food but the main reason we will come back is for the atmosphere. We brought our puppy with us and he got five star treatment. Any place that will treat your dog better than you is a great place! 

Their service was quick and attentive but we really appreciated how above and beyond our server/bartender treated our pup. People that love animals are the best people. He immediately had a bucket of water in front of him and the attention of every passer by. We'll be back plenty to grab a quick bite to eat and watch a football game with our pup in tow. The Demonbreun Hill group of restaurants are a great collection of eateries and drinking establishments and we would definitely recommend it for lunch AND nighttime fun. It's compact and you everything is literally connected to each other so if you're tired of one bar, you can walk next door to a different one.

Just an A-OK review for now since I didn't actually get to see more than the outside. The grounds are pretty and there are huge guitars for photo ops.

The site says backstage tour tickets (under $30) are available 4 weeks ahead of time. A co-worker and I had time to kill between work and our flight so we thought we'd have lunch near the office and take a tour of the Opry before heading to the airport. Backstage tour tickets were still available until 3:45pm (tours run every 15 minutes) but were sold out when we got there at 2pm. 

There was a concert that night so it's probable people got tour tickets for the late afternoon, had dinner nearby at the mall, and planned on returning for the concert.

Completely disappointing experience. We walked to Belcourt Taps for lunch one day, waited forever for service and even longer for food. I ordered the Juicy Lucy which according to the menu is stuffed with cheddar cheese and comes on a Pretzel Bun. When it came out I got a regular cheeseburger on a regular bun, nothing as it was described on the menu. There were 4 of us in the group and each meal did not come close to our expectations, which by the way were only held at normal bar food standards so we weren't expecting gourmet, but definitely something that would of been worth the hour wait from the time we placed the order until it arrived. Probably a good bar to hang out but dont waste your time for meal purposes.

My favorite place in Nashville for a larger-group happy hour. They have tablets that can accommodate multiple large groups without having to rearrange the furniture. Like many of the reviews have mentioned, they have over 100 beers available. If you are hungry for appetizers, they have amazing German pretzels... bet you can't eat just one. 

This place seems to be really popular among Preds fans. I went right before a game a few weeks ago, and it was packed with yellow and blue jerseys. They do have small TVs on the wall, but I wouldn't really call this a sports bar. It is more like a pregaming spot before a sports event. 

I will say, I was slightly disappointed when I found out they aren't native to Nashville. Flying Saucer has locations as far north as Kansas City and as far south as Houston. Nevertheless, being successful enough to open multiple locations isn't going to detour me enough to stay away from this cool little hang out spot.

Real Nashville. A little out of the way because it's a couple of blocks from Broadway. Depending on what you are used to dealing with you might not be comfortable walking, there were a fair amount of homeless on the sidewalk. You can always have Lyft drop you at the door. 
That stated, the place is awesome! Food was good, good beer selection and friendly staff. But the reason to come is the music. The Best!
Definitely plan to come back on our next trip.

Absolutely loved the food.

I was impressed how big the place was.  It was my first time so I didn't realize it was so swanky and huge inside.

Our server was great and took good care of us. He also told us about the menu and tips on what to order when we come back.  He was very efficient on letting us know our drinks would be out soon and to assure us he was taking care of us. 

I was super impressed and the manager came out to greet us and tell us about the restaurant.  He was really genuine and made me feel like he appreciated us. 

Did I mention everything I had was awesome (chicken biscuit, mac n cheese bites, bruschetta)?

I'll definitely be back!
Good Band Jamie Highdon. Perfect sound. Fried pickles are great. Awesome! Kids welcome. Good drinks.

Visiting Nashville, then you must go to the Grand Ole Opry.  There is not a bad seat in the house but you should go ahead and buy those better tickets. You will be glad you did. We sat up front and had a great view of the show.  The line up is different each show.  Backstage tours are available and sometimes the group will be in lobby after show selling their CD.

Dawghouse is always a great place to kick back and have a drink. The bartenders are always nice. Best Sunday Funday in town. They have drink specials most of the time. It is an Alabama Football bar on gameday saturdays, so if you dont like Alabama football or dont want to be around that crowd. Don't show up.
Classy but too classy. The cornbread is mediocre and apparently contains ACTUAL corn. It had legitimately good brownies drizzled with chocolate sauce. 10/10 would recommend ;)))

Only our first visit, but we really enjoyed it and will be back! GREAT and VAST beer selection. If you're a beer snob you won't be disappointed. GREAT atmosphere! Food and service was very good. Off the beaten path of most tourists. Looking forward to our next visit!

If you're a country music fan visiting Nashville, checking out the Grand Ole Opry is a must. During the winter, all Opry shows are held at the Ryman Auditorium, but the Grand Ole Opry tour is still available! 

The tour is about an hour and starts with an informational video about the history of the Opry (featuring Blake Shelton)! I really enjoyed the tour and our guide did a good job of covering a lot without losing our attention. We got to see the star's dressing rooms, mail room, and we even got to stand on the stage! It's $18 to take the daytime tour, and I felt like we got our money's worth.

Fabulous time at a divey bar that allows smoking inside! Polite and attentive staff with a fun party atmosphere to boot! The karaoke hosts were nice, helpful, and fun to talk to (unlike some places I have been). My only complaint was the lack of PBR in cans, but that seems to be a standard here. Thanks for a good time.

The bar is fine, nice and attentive bartenders, modestly priced.  But you come here for karoke and that part is a total mess.  Karaoke attendant is indifferent at best and so never gets the crowd to engage, enjoy or support each other.  A robot would have more charm.  The sound (particularly when you are at the Mic) is terrible.  Overall, not a fun karaoke spot but good place for a quick beer and shot on Printers Alley.

Don't order food. It takes an hour to come out and only 10 patrons in the bar area. The staff is very unorganized. We came on a game day. TN vs Vandy and the bar is 4 minutes from the stadium. There was only 1 staff member and should have been multiple on a such a large day like today. I've been here once before on a non busy night and it was still extremely below average.

First time ever in Nashville and we wanted to hear some Blues music but we were apparently too early on a Saturday (5 p.m.) in January because the place was pretty slow.  Tried the ribs with beans and cole slaw and they were delicious but not finger-licking delicious.

After waiting 30mins and still not receiving our drinks decided to walk up to bar to see what was taking so long, we were told they would be out soon. Waited another 10 mins, still no drinks so we left. Worst place I've been to in Nashville will not go there again.

Nice and Quiet...... Got the Special Burger , one of best burgers I have tasted ! Cooked perfectly, moist and bun made it all come together! 
Just a good solid burger ! You won't be disappointed.

We decided to attend a Grand Ole Opry show while on our Nashville roadtrip. It was a GREAT experience. The lineup that night was great. Loretta Lynn, Cole Swindell, The Gatlin Brothers, Love and Theft, and some others. I mean come on...I dont care what music you like...seeing Loretta Lynn at the Grand Ole Opry is pretty damn cool. I think I got the chills when she started singing Cole Miners Daughter.

The facility its self is pretty cool. Not a bad seat and the are very comfortable. The acoustics are wonderful. Everyone sounded great.

I suggest you stop in for a show if your in NAshville. For the history alone.

Awesome night tonight! You have to go at least once if you live country music! Easy parking at Opry Mills. Have dinner there before the show or eat at their food truck after you go through security. No outside food or drinks allowed. There is food you can buy inside as well. And drinks, that you can take in with you. Very interesting experience! Loved the music and performances tonight.

I know I've already reviewed this place. Yelp just keeps losing reviews. 

I have seen 2 Opry shows. They are always amazing. They have a good mix of well known people and some people you've never heard of so you can learn new music. If you aren't a huge fan of the music that is playing, the sets are about 15-30 mins long. It's a live taping so you have commercials and everything. Every seat is truly a good seat. Always an enjoyable evening coming here.

I know nothing about country music. Nothing. If you told me Patsy Cline sang a song called "I Cried In My Beer 'Cause I Miss You My Dear" I would totally believe you. So it is with this complete lack of knowledge that brought me to the Grand Ole Opry House.

And it. Was. Awesome.

We weren't able to score tickets to the evening show, but my friend and I were able to take the behind-the-scenes tour they offered. (Tip: Use promo code AAA w/ your AAA card and you get a few bucks off)

The tour began with a brief video on the Opry and its roots at the Ryman theater (downtown). We were then ushered past the celebrity entrance, the dressing rooms, the historic studio (where Hee Haw was filmed!), and finally on to the stage. Standing on the circle where so many historical people have performed was amazing, even if I didn't fully realize the magnitude of how many artists have taken that stage. Our guide was so cute and sweet - her bubbliness really made the tour fun for me. 

If you're in Nashville, I recommend this tour! It's only about $20 and you really do see a lot. 

Two thumbs up!

They had a really cool tour. I am not a country music fan my husband is. I went thinking it was just for him but the entire family enjoyed it a lot. Now the kids want to see a show...they were not country music fans.  I think it is a but pricey but worth it. I had no idea the meaning behind standing on the circle.  Seriously go!

As someone who dined here, this was absolutely the worst service I have received in Nashville, bar none. No one came to seat my friend and me at the door or at the bar. We practically had to beg for menus or notice of any sort. We were not told to order at the bar or at a table. The bartender who eventually came to serve us kept talking over me when I asked for dressing. "Ranch? Is that two ranch?" after I asked for Italian. Granted, this is a bar, I know he was hoping we would order drinks. I take full ownership of ordering the least divey item on the menu. However, if you start off service like this, I'm not likely to order anything. Once this server left us dinner and waters, he disappeared. My friend had to (very politely) wait at the bar as the ENTIRE service team ignored her for an extended amount of time. 

What adds insult to injury is that, as we were leaving, the bartender was seen serving a table of four women, drinks in hand, within minutes. He asked them if they wanted to split the check as he handed them their drinks (AFTER telling us he could not split ours). The service seems to be preferential, either to regulars or people the waitstaff deem "worthy." 

The ambiance seems fantastic. Warm, with plenty of bands slated to play. However, it is difficult to notice how calm the ambience is when the staff and service is driving you near nuclear in temperament. 

Given how mediocre the food was and  how inattentive the service was, I would say: dine at your own risk.

Excuse me while I fly to Nashville for my date with Garth ! 

When a dear friend and frequent travel buddy of mine asked me if I wanted to go to Nashville I quickly looked on the internet to see which iconic musicians might be playing in town.  Since it was months away from the travel dates there were nothing advertised yet.  I checked every month until I saw Garth Brooks headlining at the Grand Ole Opry the week we would be in town. YEESSS! Quickly tried to get tickets for the date we were arriving.  Unsuccessful.  Sold out already?!! Well there is a late show...so, with not many seats left, I was able to secure two seats at the very top of heaven.  Hope we can stay awake after traveling 3 time zones and a few planes.   Best I could get.  What I didnt know was...

There really isnt a bad seat in the house!  The Grand Ole Opry House is now home to the thoroughly entertaining Grand Ole Opry, a live show with multiple acts, played like a radio program.  Comedian, Emcee/Radio Announcer, of course lotsa country music to entertain.  The Grand Ole Opry actually started at the Ryman Auditorium decades prior.  When the show outgrew the Ryman it then moved into this home.   The Opry House is located on the property shared with the Opryland Mills Mall, and right behind the grand Gaylord Opryland Hotel.  So thankful the hotel has a shuttle to the concert  as, even after driving past it three times earlier in the day was still not seeing the Opry House!  The acoustics are great.  The seats, while on hardwood benches, provide great viewing.  During the winter the Grand Ole Opry moves back to the Ryman for the season.

And as it turned out the late show worked out the best.  The entertainers were already warmed up.  There was no rush to get out and make way for another concert.  Even Garth Brooks said he was having such a good time with the lively late crowd.   And as he came back for his 5th or 6th encore it became apparent the Grand Ole Opry was the very best place to be.

Bouncer was rude. Brought luggage in and was kicked it because we put a pair of sunglasses back on luggage. Much better bars on broadway to visit that appreciate the business and welcome customers. Will not be back again. Extremely disappointed.

The Opry is an icon in Nashville and a must do if you're in town!!  It's always packed so get your tickets in advance!  We bought ours not even knowing who was going to be playing and got the great surprise of having Loretta Lynn as the final act.  The entire show was really good and it didn't seem like there is a bad seat in the house.  I didn't even know it was a live radio show - but that was a cool bonus!

They have beer, wine and mixed drinks as well as snack too.  I opted for the moonshine and it was really good actually!  The parking is insane, so don't plan on making to anything for at least an hour after the shows over!  And make sure to arrive early if you want a spot anywhere near the front!

After having such a wonderful experience at the New Orleans BBKings we came upon the Nashville one and decided to go have a drink and listen to the band that was playing.
The Hostess asked us if we were dining, we told her No, we had just eaten but we're going to have drinks only.She said $5 cover and you can only sit in the bar.We paid and happily walked in.
After seating ourselves at a low four top, this angry gal comes over to us with a totally pissed of demeanor and says we CANT sit here.We asked why? she said this is dining reservations only.We explained the hostess told us that we could.
She (the Angry one) did not try to re-seat us and basically kicked us out saying "you cant sit here"She was never nice and she just didnt care and offered not to move us.
  We went back to the hostess and told her we were kicked out and wanted our money back.She said give me a minute let me get the manager to refund you your money.The manager comes to refund us and it's the same gal that kicked us out! Again not friendly, and acting bothered, she asks us if we are the ones who want a refund! Well Duh!! You kicked us out. SMH
At this point we were both blown away ..such a far cry from the New Orleans BBKings.
I told the gal they could learn a few things about customer service from their New Orleans club meanwhile my husband had enough and nicely stated they needed to work on their communication skills and attitude .She promptly shouted back at us with an attitude.
Anyway, its of my humble opinion this person is not management or hospitality material. We are huge followers of BBKing and blues in general, so to say the least we were extremely disappointed to be leaving..We didn't get the gals name but she has a blone afro.
 Just know, if you are told you can sit in the bar, what that really means is you can only sit At the Bar. At which there was no room or we would have.
It''s our First day of our music and food vacation Nashville.Their loss is someone elses gain onward and upward! Lots of venus around town to explore..

I didn't think I'd love it this much since I'm not even a country music fan. It was terrific and so entertaining! It's not just listening to live music, but also you get to enjoy square dancing, yodeling, comedy, and trivial questions for free prizes. I laughed a lot, and was in awe of the wonderful performances.

We arrived about an hour before the first show not knowing what to expect. They had many places there to get a quick bite to eat even before entering the building. There was a Yee-Haw Brewery truck as well as other diner type food trucks. There's even a shopping mall across the street with lots of food options. Go early and just walk around. It's actually a very relaxing walk and entry through security. You also might want to get your cocktails before the show. I say that because a rum or whiskey drink will cost you $22. I was in shock. That's more than stadium prices. I mean really! The drinks were good with plenty of alcohol but not worth the sticker price.

The show was amazing! It was a mix of old and new country singers. Some famous ones like Trace Adkins, Jon Conlee, and Hunter Hayes. There was a young girl from Canada who sang her heart out during her first Opry stage debut. Madison Kozak got a standing 'O' for her performance. She had the voice of an angel. The Riders in the Sky comedy group were so entertaining. I loved them! This particular show was broadcast live on radio channel 650 AM and on SiriusXM. It was such a cool experience.

Our seats were front and center on the mezzanine level. I'd get these same seats all over again. Everyone was so friendly (staff and patrons). The Opry brings together people from all over the world. I can see why country music is popular now. Don't hesitate to get a ticket to a show while you're in town. You won't regret it. It was worth every penny and it was the highlight of our trip. A must when in Nashville.

I absolutely love this place for lunch. The staff is great and the atmosphere is wonderful. The service is super fast. I can sit down and have a great lunch with time to spare. I usually get June's walnut garden salad w/ grilled chicken. It is delicious without dressing!! I've had their smoked chicken philly also. SO GOOD!
If you're in downtown Nashville, eat here for a great meal and drink specials.

The food here is without a doubt pretty good although I would definitely not say it's the best in downtown Nashville. It's definitely worth stopping in for some food. But let me tell you if you are visiting Nashville and looking for a place to catch the best musicians in town then you need to be here. Most importantly you need to stop in and either see Carl Stuart or you need to stop in and see the BB King's blues band that I believe is their house band. These guys play a catalog of music that ranges over 50 years and I'm telling you what they play it and sing it every bit as good or better than the originals. Forget going to see the usual Nashville mumbo jumbo that is in every corner and in every bar. You can't miss this
Dogs allowed outside. Looks big on the inside. Drink slushees with different and interesting flavors.

A must see when in Nashville!!!!
We bought a Grayline bus tour package that included a back stage pass at the Opry House. It was fantastic!!! We spent 90 minutes or more with a guide seeing what it looks like behind the scenes.  We got to look inside the dressing rooms to the stars of country music. The hallways were lined with beautiful pictures of country singers and performers young and old. The Opry House has a tradition and rich history in country music that we were not aware of and we soaked it all in. The tour ended with a picture taken by their photographer that you can purchase as you leave. Would highly recommend.

The Saturday night Opry was great although there was no one on stage that I had ever heard of with one exception. It was still as fun as I remembered it to be from a few trips in the past. The first was to the Ryman back in the '50s - then again in the '70s. Both times it was miserably hot and the old wooden pews grew increasingly uncomfortable as your sweat soaked through your clothes! The current location is MUCH better.

There are a few things to take note of if you are coming, especially for the first time. We arrived over an hour early, but parking spaces were only available quite a way off. Remember where you are parked as there are only a few poles with identification. Do NOT bring a pocket knife! I had my little Swiss Army and was rather curtly given the choice of throwing it away or trudging back to the car. I went back to the car.

There isn't much to eat. Hot dogs and hamburgers plus beer and mixed drinks are about it. We each ate a dog which weren't bad, but...

Thirty minutes before the show starts there is a goofy "pep rally" down front where a good-looking young lady shouts into the microphone, has contests, and generally attempts to get the crowd charged up. Fortunately, we were eating in the lobby and were spared this event. Some were up for it, I am sure, but the struggle the MC had makes me think a lot of folks weren't too excited about this.

No matter whether you like country music, or think you don't, you will probably enjoy the Opry. It's the longest running radio show - since 1925 - and a large part of why Nashville is Music City. Don't miss it, but consider my warnings above.

The customer service at the bar is stellar! I visited this BB King's location twice in one week and wasn't disappointed either time. The first visit, I ordered the hot chicken which I guess is a staple of Nashville. The second time I visited the restaurant was over crowded due to performances. I was allowed in at the bar to make another order. I'm thankful for the service.

3.5 
Nothing (other than the beer is fabulous here) 
I have been here several times, this time makes me question if I will go back... 

I asked a few questions about beers this server seemed bothered (I have allergies I have questions) so with the short answers I received I asked to try both... WELL you realize they are VERY different beers right (reference a porter and a saison)... (yes thanks ‍)

So then I had to flag her down to get a water... my water glass had lipstick on it (photo) ... I don't wear lipstick... she acted like I made it up. 

Very disappointing experience if I'm in the area I'll probably grab a beer and just double check my glass.

Great band! We were very impressed with the music. The food was fine, loaded tater tots, how can you go wrong? The rest of the food was ok, lettuce wraps not much chicken, meatloaf was fine. It is loud, part of the experience, but just keep that in mind.

A record store and an old time tech restoration site.  A treat for the eyes and ears.  Vintage 4 pose color photo booth, voice recording booth, video jukebox and so much more.  Vinyl albums and 45 rpm records, along with portable record players.
Our tour group really enjoyed our visit and the back stage tour.  Seats were comfortable.  Bench style.  Lighting and sound was good also.  It's a big place.  I would come back for another show..

This place was nothing short of amazing. You get a free photo with a guitar in the spot on stage. Where many great legends played music. I was so impressed  you will learn and see so much .I have no complaints at all.

Scratch this from my bucket list.

I really liked seeing the Opry show live. It was very entertaining. Kind of a variety act with several singers and dancers. So much history. 

The venue is nice and comfortable, moreso than most other venues.

I would go again.

One thing I had to do on my trip was going to Third Man.  Third Man is pumping out great releases on vinyl.  Loved strolling through the shop.  Had a lot of cool things besides records.  Must go if you're a music fan.  Definitely,​​ if you're a Jack White fan.

I was lucky enough to be staying next door at the Union Station Hotel, so this allowed me to indulge in a few or three or more beers...LOL

The theme of flying saucers is unique and there are saucers hung all over the walls.  If you are a regular - you should join the Flying Saucer Club! 

The beer selection on draft and in bottles was vast and covered anything you could've wanted:  Lagers, Stouts; IPA's, Sours, Pilsners and German style beers.  I started with a flight and the continued to dive into a few other choices during my dinner.  

The food options were great too as were good too!  Burgers; Sandwiches; Potato Salad and Fries.

Our server was knowledgeable and friendly.  

If I lived in Nashville, I would be a regular for sure!  If you are in town- swing by and enjoy this cool place!
Super nice people and an amazing patio area. Perfect little dive bar. Beautiful atmosphere and also awesome music

My friends and I came to Nashville from Dallas to celebrate my birthday and we ended up here twice, since it was right near our hotel. 1st time was absolutely terrible. Went on a Saturday, even though it was pretty slow, the service was absolutely terrible. I've been bartending for 9 years so I guess I may be a little harder on bars than most but it was just terrible. The bartenders didn't even acknowledge us standing at the empty bar for a solid 4-5 minutes. Which in bar time, is unacceptable, especially when you're slow. When somebody finally came to us, she took our orders one at a time with zero urgency. Took another 10 minutes for her to make 4 drinks, very basic drinks or beers. Had an poor attitude the entire time and was just flat out unpleasant. The service wasn't even what upset me the most. This place was absolutely filthy. There was trash and broken bottles everywhere. It was horrific. I left with glass stuck in the bottom of my shoes. 

2nd time we went was Sunday evening. I didn't catch the bartenders name but she was way better and took care of us. I was very disappointed that the trash all over the bar was not just a fluke, once again, it was everywhere. This time however, the Security guy, Miles, had a broom and dustpan in hand trying to clean things up. It's hard to do when you're doing it alone after trash accumulating all day and nobody helping you, so bravo Miles!! You rock!!

I tried it again after the horrific 1st time. This is an awesome little set up they have going on but the customer service and cleanliness of the bar completely turned me off from ever visiting it again. I really hope they get a manager that requires more from their employees. Best wish. Xoxo
Each time I visited Belcourt Taps I had roaches crawling on the bar counter right in front of me by my plate of food. They also love like to cancel gigs at the last minute and not notify the artist.
