The Grand ole Opry is one of Nashville TN's most famous tourist attractions. It's fame stems from the fact that country music was pretty much born and breaded here. It was interesting to see this famed institution.

Many of country music's iconic famous stars got their start here. Or so I've read on Wikipedia and tripadvisor. With that said, since I was in nearby Brentwood, TN, I figured that it would be in my best interest to venture up to Nashville and see the Grand Ole Opry concert house "just to see it", among my main reasons for going. It's basically a concert hall that gave country music a legitimate birthplace here in Nashville, TN. While I am not a country music fan, some of the popular music that streamed into the mainstream consciousness within the last 10 years have come from the country music scene, at least some of which are from "American Idol". I arrived here on a casual Tuesday evening from a drive originating from Huntsville, AL. At first, I could not find the Grand Ole Opry since it was kind of tucked away. The Opry Mills shopping center you will see when driving up on the interstate and there is a dedicated exit sign for the Grand Ole Opry. How neat is that? For the most part, it was nice seeing the Opry house for the first time ever. 

And while I did not attend a country music show, due to my choice of music, I enjoyed my time here, "just to see" the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville, TN. The Grand Ole Opry is located at xxx Opryland Drive, next to the aforementioned Opry Mills shopping center and nearby the Gaylord Opryland hotel and resort. They really go all out here, since it's Nashville's most iconic institution and I don't blame them. There are pretty much 2 separate parking lots: one for the Opry Mills shopping center and one for the Opry itself. I realized this when I parked my rental car at the shopping center, walked over to the Grand Ole Opry, and found out that there is another separate lot nearby. Oh well. There is no admission fee accessed when you're just visiting the outside of the Opry house, but certainly there is admission fee charged for shows and guided tours. They accept major credit cards, so that's always a great thing. Ticket prices for the country music shows can vary from performer, so do check with the box office or the Grand Ole Opry website for more information and show times. I do admit that it would be something if I were to stick around and see a show at the Opry. Since I was on a schedule - even on vacation, my time spent here at the Grand Ole Opry was to admire the fact that I was here and to enjoy the moment.

Being a tourist can be swell, but can be limiting as well. It was nice to be in the presence of famous people, or just places to be inspired by, to be honest. Being inspired here is a great thing. I did enjoy the 2 large guitars that were by the entrance to the parking lot. I saw many people were posing by them and taking photos. Many selfies and group photos to be had! I took some myself and admired the building for what icon it is. The building itself was as grand as you could get, while maintaining a cute homespun flavor to it. I'm sure many world class performances have been held here at the Grand Ole Opry over the decades and will continue to do so in the future. While I don't regret trying to schedule a show during my travels to Nashville, TN, there's always next time for sure. If you are a country music lover, this place is most likely the place to be. I'd recommend coming here, just to be a tourist and see the Grand Ole Opry. 

4 stars solid. The grounds are well maintained and there are benches to sit on in front of the doors for weary travelers and those whom need them. It was a privilege to ge here for sure. Keep this place in your travel schedule.

Support local!

B
Good folks doing good things for Pietown and Nashville in general. The shows, merchandise, and customer service are always top notch at TMR, happy to support this business.
Not a criticism of the people or music. But go to Ryman Auditorium instead. This is a bland concrete hall in the middle of a mall parking lot. Disappointing

Slow service, slow (bad) food. 
Had two bites of my burger to know I didn't like it, just to have my server never return until she dropped checks. Making me pay for the burger I didn't even eat. 
They need to learn to staff appropriately to give service that is necessary. HORRIBLY DISAPOINTED.

The karaoke is cool and fun.   I agree with the comments above about sketchy stuff going on.  I watched the bartender repeatedly take my cash that I paid for the drinks(and tip!), not record anything on the register and just toss all of it in the tip bucket.  That is what it is and is really a management issue but what really upset me is that if you order premium drinks, they will give you premium the first round and charge accordingly but after that they will start making the drinks from the well but still charge you premium.  I caught the bartender doing so and politely asked her about it and she pretty much blew me off by saying she should be charging me more anyway.  Later after she saw me watching her serve premium to another customer but charging the same she came over and got pretty rude so we just left.  Trust me, enough people come in here she could care less that we got pissed and left!  Again, overall fun place but definitely not on the up and up.  Stick to beers and watch your wallet!!  

And I didn't even mention that the soap in the bathroom was just a jug of off brand Dawn dish detergent

When I first moved to Nashville I'd never seen anything like Flying Saucer. So many beers!

Over the years I've been there several times and as much as I want to love it I cannot.

It's too loud, too crowded and too darned expensive to park at.  I feel any place that requires me to go into a gated lot to park and then doesn't even have validated parking is just.. Meh.

Having said that, I've no doubt i'll be back because it IS a good place to go with your friends when you don't mind it being crowded and loud and you just want to drink a lot of beer and eat a lot of oversized appetizer plates. but the cons just outweigh the pros for me to keep me WANTING to come back.

If my husband and I get a sitter you can probably find us at Belcourt Tap at some point in our evening. We love it here! Please note this is not a review of their food as I have never eaten here, however, the music here is amazing! When I moved to Nashville over a year ago I tended to go to the more touristy spots at first until I discovered Belcourt! I have heard some of the best music of my life here (cough, Chris Canterbury), and they have a good beer list too! This bar has a neighborhood feel and different performers every hour until usually 11pm, 7 days per week. If you have never visited Belcourt please do but just don't tell the tourists:)

The bartender ruined the entire experience.  She literally had us kicked out for not knowing what drinks we wanted. We were there for a total of 5 minutes. Do NOT go here, any other bar on Broadway would be happy to.have your business.

I was called a faggot by the door man. I walked inside and was immediately told they were closing when there was an hour left. There was urine ALL over the floor to the bathroom. It is a ratchet place and the service is very poor. Go across the street or look elsewhere on Broadway. I wouldn't recommend this to a DOG.

I am in Nashville for business and just had to visit this spot. If you're a fan of Jack White, then this is the place you need to see.
Many bands have recorded here (i.e. Weezer, Weird Al, Neil Diamond), and you can actually record your own singing voice in that same booth and have it copied on your own record! There is another booth in the store where you can listen to many vinyls issued by Third Man. Unfortunately during our visit, most of the machines were out of order. 
Keep in mind that there is very limited parking, and is located in a part of town that can get sketchy at night. If you're in Nashville, definitely visit this place!

Great place to go with some buddies and just hang out. Monday nights are pint nights, which means a HUGE selection of beer are just $3 a pint. And while not all the beers qualify for pint night, given that there are 200+ beers to choose from and a majority are in the pint night category, you still have a gigantic variety at your fingertips.

We came on a crowded night so it took a while to get a table, but we just hung out in the game room and watched some TV and played some darts. The food is also pretty good for a pub/gastropub place.

So I went to the Dawg House Saloon on NYE for the Super T show thanks to some nice friends of mine.  It was a good time.

First, I think this place used to be something else but I cannot remember what exactly.  There's a patio out front, a big square bar when you walk in, a stage and dance floor in the back, and tables situated all around.  For NYE they had everything decorated and looking festive.  

As for the band, they were fun and the dance floor was big enough for everyone to shake their ass.  Sound was good I think - at that point the booze was taking over and it seemed fun to me.  Let's be honest, it all seemed fun to me.

They also have TVs and some people I know go there on Sundays to watch football and do their Sunday funday up right.  I think they also have some food to help you not have tooooo much fun.

Give it a try, it is new and if you like bars I can't imagine you won't like this!

An absolute must do tour when visiting Nashville! Was awesome to go behind-the-scenes and walk on the actual stage. Our guide was very friendly full of interesting information. If possible, try to see a show as well.

*Special shout out to my pal @iamfacemelter at the end of this review. 

You don't say? A little slice of NYC all the way in Nashville? Awesome!

The Tippler is quite the destination in Manhattan, but since I rarely spend time in MPD, I'm about as far from a regular as you could find. But what a nice surprise to see them holding down the cocktail game in the middle of the Bible Belt. 

The space is huge - perhaps one of the largest cocktail forward bars I've seen in my life. You could seriously fit an auto dealership within their four walls. 

On the drink side of things, they deliver the goods. Some old standbys you'd recognize (Old Fashioned, for instance), as well as some libations you'll only find at Music City Tippler. Who'd-a-thunk that gin and Bulliet Rye would go well together? Well, it does. If you're curious, dial up one of their Old Flirty Bastards and try it for yourself. 

Back to the above asterisk - we made pals with one of the bartenders and he agreed to make us a Music City Tippler version of a Fireball shot. I quite enjoyed mine. My pal @iamfacemelter - not so much. As quick as the moonshine went down, he had a "reversal of fortune" come right back up. But have no fear - not a drop hit the fancy floors of le Tippler. Instead, it all ended up in my dirty blond hair. That's why my pals call me Ruggy "Shamwow" J, I suppose...

It's amazing how much terrible service really stays with you. You always remember places where they treated you like trash. Anyways, went there for my friend's bachelorette and we were greeted by two of the rudest bartenders. A girl with purple kool-aid hair, at the time, and a red head. They do not acknowledge you and make you wait 10 minutes for a drink only to come over and wave her hand while saying "what do you want?" And don't you dare discuss drinks with your friends because then you're all "talking to her at once" and she "just can't." She literally walked away and left us standing there waiting for another bartender to get us drinks.

My Husband and I were heading to Nashville and even thought we are not big country fans, we can appreciate good music and wanted to cross it off the bucket list. I got $48 tickets in the balcony, 3rd row.  Spectacular seats!  We ended up being at the side of the stage, about 9 rows back.  The seats are pews, which is nice, but not much leg room.
The show itself was SOOOO good!!!  We really enjoyed ourselves!  It was funny, and the musicians were all top notch!!
Bobby Osborne played "Rocky Top" and the crows loved it.  We had never heard that song before, but the fans sure did.  All of the performers were really good and I like that they didn't only play their songs, they played songs that influenced them as musicians.

Great choice! Loved the music, good food and superb service!  Friendly folks and a good vibe will keep us coming back for more.  Try them out if new to downtown scene, very different and more sophisticated than Broadway crazies.  Ribs are best, fried pickles and cold local brews combined with sweet gal server was perfect!

I second Tim K in saying that Colt was great! The bars were insanely busy after a Preds playoff game dumped out onto Broadway. Even though he was super busy on the roof, Colt was super attentive and came around to make sure we had full drinks. No other bar on Bway had bartenders going out of their way to help. The rooftop was a great atmosphere to put down some drinks with the guys and play some giant Jenga too!

Fantastic concert venue. We came to the Opry tonight and had the pleasure of hearing Carrie Underwood along with many other talented musicians. This was my first time at the Opry and I hope to go back soon. 

Sign up for the email list and get their coupons too, we got a dollar off $5 or more purchase of food, not including alcohol.

My girlfriend Julie & I spent a few days in Nashville for the 4th of July. We stopped in BB's a few times but never ate. This review is mainly about the quality of the live bands & happy hour.

The happy hour has great drink specials every day. You really should make it a point to head here for happy hour (11AM-6PM).

The live bands playing at night were great. It was a great respite from country music. We saw a soul band & a blues band. If you want a temporary exit from twangy county music then head over here.

Such a wonderful venue! I love the format of the shows here. It's 15 minute segments for each artist and they stay true to those segments. There's truly no bad spot in the place either. Would LOVE to come back and see another show here.

What a gorgeous, intricately detailed venue! I could not stop snapping photos because it's just all so interesting at each turn.

Playing at the Opry is a milestone achievement for artists and to become a member is even more so an honor with a limited amount of spots available. They have to show a continued dedication to the Opry once inducted, including playing a minimum number of shows each year.

Though not the original location, it's been the spot since 1974 where it all goes down. It's seen a lot and been through a lot including some crazy flooding in 2010. 

There is a separate review for the Grand Ole Opry tour which I highly recommend and you can find the full deets in that listing.

Do not skip going to the Grand Ole Opry House while in Nashville!

Make your way to Third Man Records if you're a rock 'n roll or Jack White fan! It's almost like a shrine to the musician that he made for himself. You can get knick knacks like wax guitar figures or even pins and chocolates. On the more of the expensive side, they also have unique records and a well-curated selection of music you can buy or play in their on-site music booth and record player. It's very fun to experiment with the sound booths and listen to tunes and bands that you haven't heard of before! 

Another experience you can try is recording your own voice on vinyl! It's more expensive and I wouldn't spend that much if you're not a singer. They have a music booth here that records directly to vinyl. I personally didn't choose to do so because I didn't want to spend money on something I wouldn't use. I don't sing professionally (aside from bad karaoke! and in the shower!). The store also has cool vintage items like old guitars and relics from Nashville's past that you can look at. It's like a time capsule, mini museum. 

However, the space is very small, and you can tour the shop in a matter of minutes. It's too bad that the store is a bit further out from the downtown area, so you once you're quickly done - there's nothing else to do in the area. There are only warehouses surrounding it. It's quite random and a little sketch! (A couple folks came up to me in the parking lot to ask random questions and eyed our car). Just park your car in their designated lot, which can fit no more than a handful of cars, and you'll be fine. We didn't buy anything, but it was fun to experience what it would be like to be Jack White for an hour!

My favorite of all things, funny enough, is the building's exterior! I love the design and the sleek black brick and vintage font! You can't miss it. There's also a photo-worthy radio statue on top of the building. Photos abound!

Still being pretty new to Nashville, we are always looking for a cool new spot to check out. Live music is always a fun option but some of the more popular places like downtown are a bit crazy and loud. When we discovered Belcourt Taps on Yelp, it seemed like the perfect place for a relaxed Saturday night. Plus, it's located in one of our favorite areas.  

The Belcourt Taps is a small bar inside an old house (like most of the businesses appear to be on Belcourt). The bar itself is nothing fancy and is pretty small. I like this though because it feels relaxed and cozy. It also allows for good sound for the live music. The bar has high tops and bar seating. I have seen this place packed before but it wasn't too busy this night. We were able to find a seat with a nice view of the stage. Right after sitting down, a very friendly server brought us beer menus. They also have food but we were not hungry. The food menu seemed to have full meals and apps. They have a nice selection of beer on tap. I got a Good People IPA for $6. They also have a full bar with mixed drinks and wine. 

The bar seems to bring in a mix of local talent to perform each night. The bar is owned by a very nice couple that gives artists a great opportunity to get their music out there. When we first got there, there were two singers performing a mix of their own songs and some covers. Both were very good and it was fun to listen to some music while sipping on a delicious beer. After the two singers finished, it was kind of an open mic night. The bartender and server sang a song together and were amazing. Another artist who walked in for a drink hopped up on stage and sang a few songs. It made for a great variety of music and it's fun to see the local talent here in Nashville. It's kind of what you expect and love about living in Music City. 

While I can't comment on the food, I can say this is the perfect place to sit back and enjoy some local music in a more relaxed atmosphere. It's small and a little divey, but also has a nice charm to it. It would be a fun place to bring visitors if they want to hear live music. The bar had patrons of all ages so it really is for everyone. I will definitely be back when in the neighbor or looking for some great music!

This is one of the best concerts I have ever been too! The venue is breathtaking but not anywhere I would expect! The prices for drinks and food don't cost you an arm and a leg! But the best part is that there honestly is not a bad seat anywhere! It feels so intimate. I also highly recommend the back stage tour! It truly is one of the best parts & you learn so much about its history & the members! You  only need to take the tour once, but we will 100% be back for a concert every time we visit Nashville!

The Grand Ole Opry is a live Radio Broadcast, not a concert, and we are all the live audience/guests at that broadcast. You can expect interruptions for commercials, adjustments to acts, new musicians coming onstage, etc. It is all done very smoothly and professionally, but don't expect a concert!

We sat in the front row since this was are first time and really wanted to experience it.

To say, "I saw a show at the Opry" doesn't do it justice. To see live music - and tour backstage - at this amazing venue is truly an event, and one of my favorites, ever!

Give your happy hour a little more sparkle and go visit this place! The drinks were great , the ambeiance was devine and the food DeLish'!
I tried the chicken sammies/sliders, the brochetta, the fried mac&cheese, and the spicy tuna appetizers... watch out ya'll this food is AMAZING! 
I will definately be back!
Please God do not go in here. John Rich is an egotistical asshole.  He has been killing country music for over a decade. He is not with his town should be. Tell him to take his butt back to Amarillo

We had a party of 8 for dinner. It's wasn't the best experience. They took forever getting our drink order and then forgot my drink. When our waitress realized she said "oh the bar is busy." What? No you forgot tell them to put a rush on it. ‍ Anyways the food for me was just ok. I got the shrimps and grits. I'm from Maryland and I have had better shrimp and grit in Maryland and that's sad. All in all it came down to the service. The serve can make or break a meal and that's exactly what happened. I get it's live music, but it was really loud and very hard to talk also.

Thought it would be cool to listen to Blues while enjoying dinner so we made a reservation here.  When we got to the restaurant (which was more like a bare bones glorified bar) we were told that there was a five dollar cover per person to sit and eat dinner.  I mean, is that even a thing when you are having dinner? Nowhere on there website does it mention this.  Had we known, we would never have gone there (so many good venues to listen to good music for free in Nashville). Since we were already there we decided to give it a shot.  

The waiter came to take out order.  I had seen in the reviews that patrons raved about their Shrimp and Grits and my mouth was watering to give it a try.  My sister planned on ordering the Cajun Catfish topped with shrimp.  We had each already ordered a house specialty drink and were enjoying the very good band that was playing.  

Upon ordering our meals we were told that the restaurant was out of shrimp.  So we both had to find another dish in a limited menu where over half the dishes contained shrimp.  If we hadn't paid the 10 dollars in cover fees and ordered drinks we would have walked out at this point.

I ended up ordering spicy Chicken Fried Chicken served with Macaroni and Cheese and grilled veggies.  My sister ordered a chicken pasta dish.  My meal was actually very good and something that I would usually never order. My sister did not care for her dish.   

During the hour and a half that we were there the band took two 20-30 minute breaks and ended early, which given the cover charge was ridiculous.  Upon complaining to the manager we were able to have the cover refunded, but he was so rude he would not look at us or answer us while opening the cash register to do so.  No apologies, no nothing.

To be fair if I had to rate my actual meal or the band that we were listening to or our Waiter (he was very apologetic) I would have given it a higher review.  But the 1 Star is for our overall experience.  I would never recommend this place based on the experience we had.

If you don't mind a little smoke, and want cheap beer and drinks while you get your karaoke on, then Ms. Kelli's may be the place for you!

The biggest plus?  The DJ keeps the place hopping between singers with some great tunes that will have you dancing on the dance floor up front in no time at all.  And with $3 beers located in a large bucket right next to the dance floor- you will be sure to be strutting and singing!

But if you want to sing- you better be ready to tip the DJ or else you will sit and sit and sit.  And please don't go asking the bartender for some "high falutin'" drink  . . you're gonna be disappointed as standard mixers and beer are the de riguer here (along with some jello shots, or so I hear!)

Printers Alley has tons of karaoke choices.  But Ms. Kelli's is one of my favs . . . .even if I smelled like an ashtray when I left the joint!

The flying saucer is cool. It's the only bar I've seen in Nashville so far that actually has beer on tap. Not sure why that is. Maybe a Tennessee thing? Anyway, if you love craft beer, this is the place to be! Dozens of beer on tap, and many more in bottles. They also offer beer flights so I had the Tennessee flight. 5 great local beers. 

The food is good too. Had a polish sausage that was excellent. Oh yeah, they have pool tables too. Great place for beer lovers!

It's a bar. Nothing more than that. They had live music and alcohol which is like every place downtown. They do have a rooftop which is nice but the place is pretty gross. The only thing I really liked was the awesome painting they had in the staircase.

Solid place to go listen to some music. 

Small intimate just what I was looking for. 

The Caesar salad was actually really good. Great dressing. On be the smaller side but perfect with the chicken. 

Would not recommend the house white wine, but I loved the B nectar cider. 

Pro tip sit at the bar if you want fast service.

I did not visit this establishment during its previous owner's reign, before the name change to "Belcourt Taps" from "Belcourt Taps and Tapas". (Confusing to say the least.) From what I understand, the "Tapas" days were uninspiring.

But I have had the pleasure of conversing with owner Chris, manager Christina, and bartender Sammy over my several visits in recent months. It seems this newish team is taking strides to make their patrons feel welcome -- a neighborhood bar-type effort.

They have changed the menu to reflect their specialty of stuffed burgers, and they are quite good. Arguably, as good or better than Burger Up.

Being a Jackalope lover, I am thrilled I have been able to have not one, but TWO options for beer consumption - between Rompo and Bearwalker. Most definitely warranting a "Yipppeeee!".

On Christmas Day evening, I searched for a place to just sit down and have a brew, and Belcourt was the only place I could find in the area that was open. I had hoped for a somewhat quiet experience, which I did not receive due to a few other patrons at the bar. Nevertheless was grateful they were open.
I was a bit hungry, but their kitchen wasn't staffed. However, the evening's bartender (which I later discovered is the owner), offered to rustle up some fries. Very, very kind of him, and it hit the spot.

I have also learned the staff is incredibly dog friendly, and encourage their guests to bring Fido to their porch in warmer months. They'll even supply the dog bowls....

As Vault Club Member and a Third Man distributer for my record store Santa Ana Spin I have to say it was so epic walking up to this iconic building. As a musician I had to try the Third Man Recording Booth and it is one of the best things in the record shop world! Even if you're not a musician you can record spoken word or stuff like that! They're listening booth is one of the best also and you can listen to pretty much any White Stripes album or Third Man artist. It's a super organized and the staff is very friendly and informative! A must check out store if you're into the revival of vinyl!

Last Friday the blonde female  bartender accosted my friend! Kicked her out for no reason and pushed her out. Lucky for her we didn't call the cops 
Do your homework John rich!!

Best off Broadway place for original, down to earth Country music. Great service. Amazing food at very reasonable prices. We arrived a bit early and had a front row table for the Thursday night performances. Our waitress was very personable and attentive. We ordered drinks and the whole rack of ribs; which was great for the two of us. Great performances.

The name Flying Saucer definitely made me think of a UFO but there is nothing extraterrestrial about this place and I did not see any aliens. However, the saucers (plates) on the wall are a sign that you're at the right place since the whole wall is decorated with them. 

The place--
The building is absolutely huge and this is the perfect place to come with a huge posse. You could have a group of 10 people and be fine in this place. Since it was just me and a friend I felt like I should call more people just to fill up the huge table we were sitting at. 

The service--
It did seem they were a bit understaffed when we came since there was one server tending to multiple very large tables and we had to try and catch her attention for about 10 minutes at the end when we were trying to leave. Otherwise, she was very nice and we did not wait to long for the food. 

The food/drink--
Beer lovers can rejoice, this is your haven. Food-wise what we ordered was very simple. We each got the house salad and then split the nachos. The jalapeno vinaigrette was good but definitely had a kick to it! The nachos were pretty standard but good. 

Parking--
They do give you a discount if you park in the lot below but I think because we had been there for a few hours (to the Frist then to Flying Saucer) we still had to pay $4 for parking. I would only come back to the Flying Saucer if I had another reason to be in the area otherwise I do not enjoy having to pay for parking! 

Overall, a fun place to grab some beers and socialize.

Awful service and rip off artists. We waited  1 1/2 hour for our food and one of the orders was wrong. After 1/2 hour more of waiting for the correct order, we gave up, asked for the check and scooted out. Once we were back in our hotels, we checked the bill and they charged us for an extra $12 specialty drink that we didn't order or receive. Stay away from this place!!

negative stars!!! Sister and Dad were both harassed by bartender and bouncers simply after my dad was trying to help people behind us order drinks since they were being ignored. This woman didn't serve us once before during the 5 hours we were there (the other bartenders did and were very nice and knew us by name when ordering drinks). She decided to throw a big scene and yell every swear word in the book TO MY 50 YEAR OLD DAD!! Also to mention we were having a nice family outing to watch some good football. We will never go back and we sure spread some word about this place... not in a good way! No one should EVER speak to anyone that way. Absolutely uncalled for and pathetic. She should be fired ASAP

I've agreed to elaborate on this review after the owner messaged me saying I *must* be mistaken:

 However, those two stars up there, they are still for the bartenders ONLY. Otherwise this place sucked with JayJay as their karaoke DJ. He is still a crook, and the one thing the owner neglects to address is the fact that I paid this KJ $10 to move up in line and it didn't work. He swears up and down that favoritism wasn't a factor, but I can only go by the experience we had. The same people  going over and over and over and over.......and over again, as evidenced by the precious video cited. 

Yess, we did finally sing AFTER I paid him off and waited even longer only to watch the same people go up again. Why did I not leave? Why did I sing anyway? Because I would have felt guilty making my friends wait so long without salvaging the last shred of fun left here, also I would've been extremely angry if I lost $10 for nothing. We sang out of principle and spite.

No matter what is claimed by the business owner, the fact remains that we had a terrible time. I was in Nashville for 5 days and this was the only establishment that did not measure up to the rest in terms of customer service and quality. If you read through their reviews, this is obviously not an isolated case.

It wouldn't be fair to the other places if I up'd their rating based on what the owner's reaction was, and not based on our experience. Other places earn their stars without bias, and that's how it should be. 

Next time I'm in Nashville, I will give it another shot out of principle but I will not bribe the KJ again just to sing. I will wear the shortest shorts I can find and see if that works.

Amazing! The grounds of the Opry house are filled with fun and elegance. They have a new attraction now so make sure to get to the Acuff house for a tour before you head backstage! 

I did the backstage tour with Will. He was wonderful. He was funny and extremely knowledgeable about the property, people and process. He took it from a general tour to an experience. I'm new to the area and can not wait to come watch some concerts! Amazing place

***REVIEW FROM AN EXPERIENCE IN JUNE 2015: I just wanted to let everyone reading my review know that even though this review was written in the beginning of 2018; I went to this place in June 2015 (however I am sure if I went to this place again the review would be similar). A few days ago I was talking to someone about places visit in New Orleans because they are interested in visiting the city. I realized that when I went to New Orleans I went to a lot of amazing places but I never wrote Yelp reviews for them because I did not start writing Yelp reviews until the beginning of 2017. I enjoyed many places on my trip and I wanted to share my experiences with everyone  even though they are a few years old. So I decided to dig up some old pictures and write the reviews.

I would also like to add that most of the experiences I am writing about are places I went to while I was on a guided tour for my trip. I went on a Collette Tour called America's Music Cities. Most of the places we saw and ate at were planned because of the tour. During the tour we stopped at 3 major cities New Orleans, Memphis, and Nashville (and few other stops along the way). I just wanted to let everyone know that since I was on a tour my experiences may have been a little different compared to those who went to these places and were not on a tour (they went on their own) It was an amazing tour and I definitely recommend it.***

A dream come true!! I love country music and for the most part the only music I listen to. As I have mentioned I was on a music tour in different cities of the South but I was most excited to listen to the music in Nashville. 

I was so excited to get the opportunity to go to the Grand Ole Opry and little did I know this would be a night that I will never forget. We saw the show and the backstage tour after the show. 

We had wonderful seats on the lower level near the center of the stage. Many great artists performed throughout the night (see pictures to see who performed). Towards the end of the show a special guest who wasn't on the setlist walked on the stage. It was TRISHA YEARWOOD. Trisha started to talk about how it was last minute and she wasn't originally going to perform (that's why she wasn't on the setlist). She mentioned how she didn't even have time to call her band because it was so last minute. She continues talking and to this day I remember the last sentence or so... she said (and I believe these are her exact words) "...but luckily I live with a Grand Ole Opry Member so please welcome my husband Mr. Garth Brooks" then GARTH BROOKS walked on stage!! It was absolutely amazing and an unforgettable night. Only a few of the Opry employees knew that they were showing up so it was a shock to a lot of the employees as well. Anyway, Trisha and Garth performed many songs together. I didn't know a lot of the songs because they were older but it was still such an amazing experience. I also got the opportunity to get closer to the stage to take a few pictures (you can see where I was sitting in the other pictures vs. where I was when I got to get closer to take pictures of Trisha and Garth). The staff didn't mind that I got closer to the stage as long as I didn't block anyone's view. I posted a few of them and I am sorry they are blurry..my hands were shaking with excitement! 

I also heard when I was there that Garth hadn't been to the Opry in about 10 years so it was even more cool that he showed up that night!

Now onto the backstage tour! The tour was awesome! I learned a lot about the Grand Ole Opry, the history of the Grand Ole Opry, and Grand Ole Opry Members. I was able to see many of the dressing rooms and learn about each of the rooms (they all have different themes). Lauren Alaina was still in her dressing room when we were getting our tour and she showed us her dressing room and talked to the group for a little bit. Looking back at the experience now, I wish I would have gotten a picture with her! It was a fun tour with a lot of information. We even got the opportunity to go on stage and stand in the circle! 

It was a truly an amazing and unforgettable experience. I definitely recommend that you go to the Grand Ole Opry. After all, you never know who may show up (or who you might get to meet)!!

Enjoy,
Simona

My boyfriend and I are in Nashville for the first time. Before we left my boyfriends father asked us to send him a picture from Redneck Riviera because he absolutely loves John Rich. On our first night out we went straight there in hopes of having a great time and getting our picture. We were greeted at the door by a bouncer who asked for our ID. He checked my boyfriends ID and instantly said it was a fake. My boyfriend offered to show him more proof of his age but the bouncer refused to look at it and told us to leave. My boyfriend is 24 so he was understandably frustrated. A few friends came over and asked why he wasn't being let in and the bouncer said that he had a fake ID and I who barely said anything at this point, "have my ass wrapped around my ears". After being insulted and belittled I had no interest in being at this bar but my boyfriend spoke with the manager Eric. He refused to even look at his ID and blindly followed the bouncer. I've never in my life been treated with such disrespect by an establishment. Needless to say this really put a damper on what should have been an amazing first trip to Nashville. I strongly suggest avoiding this bar at all cost if you don't want to be told you have your ass around your ear.

It's cool to see, can't deny that it's a landmark and a 'must-see'. But there was no way we were going to spend $34 a person to tour the inside.  It's a lovely building, but I feel like that is such a steep price.  At lease outside there are a lot of cool photo opportunities.  I could be biased because I'm not a fan of country music.  But it was a fun stop and I'm glad we dropped by for a bit.  There is some nice outdoor seating and shade areas.  Plenty of parking around, the mall nearby and the hotel.

The Grand Ole Opry is famous for a reason. The Opry hosts numerous concerts a week with big country artists and a live broadcast. They also host comedy shows and other types of events here as well. 

The backstage tour is awesome. If you are into music history then this is right up your alley. The tour guide will walk you around to show you the dressing rooms and the Opry membership plaques. Artists who are members are expected to perform at the Opry and show their dedication to this venue. Members have included artists from Emmylou Harris, Willie Nelson and Dolly Parton to Carrie Underwood and Darius Rucker. At the end of the tour they let you get pictures on the stage on the wooden circle taken from the Ryman Auditorium when they moved the Grand Ole Opry locations. 

I really enjoyed the tour and the Opry regularly has great lineups, which is something I intend to do and see some great shows.

We took the backstage tour on a Sunday afternoon and thoroughly enjoyed it.  Tours depart every 15 minutes. You buy tickets at the ticket office, which is a separate building and to the right of the gift shop.  AAA members receive a $1 discount.  The tour takes about 45 minutes. 

The tour begins with a 5 minute video staring Blake Shelton. The tour allows you to see the dressing rooms, living room (where the stars and their friends hangout), stand on the stage, see the lobby the starts walk through, and their mailboxes.  

I'm not a huge country music fan and I found the tour very interesting. Our guide was entertaining. It is a 15 minute ride from downtown. You can walk to the Gaylord Hotel.
Not a country music fan but this is a must see while in Nashville! Really fun and interesting! Would definitely recommend!

I am a big country fan and never thought I would be able to experience the Opry, but a bachelorette party brought me to Nashville and about 12 of us attended. The crowd-All old white stuffy people. I am white obviously, but it was really really shocking to see no diversity in this place. Also, I do not think that the crowd cared for us younger girls. The lady I ended up sitting next to was giving me dirty looks the entire time and she finally told me to put my phone away when I was trying to video the performances. I saw a lot of people doing it, but apparently it was too bright for her stuffy butt. 

The performances were a bunch of super old school like 80 year old country music stars that moved to Nashville to live out their retirement and still be relevant at the local coffee shops. Was not into the music at all. There were a few younger guys, but we didn't get to see anyone too relevant on the night we went. They also only do about 2 songs a piece so even if it is someone relevant, it would only be 2 songs or so. 

Overall, total cool experience. Would I go back again, probably not. But.. it was marked off on my bucket list!
This is an amazing place.  It is breathtaking really.  The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because the staff was not very friendly.

I'm giving it a one star as security at the front door should be retrained and or replaced, the last thing people want to be hassled before they even get into the place. Spitting tobacco in a cup while working at the front door  security is also a big turn off. For a very small bar it was priced higher than the bigger bars with better venues. On a good note the band called the night owls with Natalie was very good

Planned to belt out "Don't Stop Believing" at WannaB's but quickly noticed that only serious singers were allowed on stage (with the exception of two guys singing a Maria Carey duet). We tried getting drinks from the bar but the service was non existent despite the bar not being busy.  Didn't stick around long with no drinks and no sings.

Ok, so I've never really been into Country Music before going to Nashville, but I can see why so many people like it!!! It's really fun, most of the time.

But apparently the Grand Ole Opry is the place to go if you are into country music.  We have no idea why the bachelor wanted to go, but we did it anyway for him.  Honestly, I didn't know what to do expect and I was tired and hungover from the night before and we just had Mission BBQ right across the damn street so I wanted to take a nap.

It's not too long of a tour but we did take it backstage which was really cool and they said they filmed some show that everyone knew about howdy do dee? No idea what it was, I was more of a Sesame Street, Transformers, He-Man kid.  But I think it was pretty boring most of it, until you get to stand on the stage, then you realize why people loved it. It was really good, our hostess was SUPER nice and so enthusiastic, so I gotta give her a shout out.

I gave it a 5 because for what it was and what it is, its pretty amazing and to see the history and the tragic events that it went through (flooding) and to see it still standing and going strong is pretty amazing.

We visited the Grand Ole Opry on a Saturday night. The Opry location is essentially in the parking lot of an outlet mall, which we found odd. Additionally, if you are visiting Nashville and staying downtown - the Opry is a more than 20 minute drive and about a $30.00 Uber ride one way. 

We attended the second showing of the evening, so we had to wait outside the Opry while the guests from the first showing left and the Opry was tidied.

Once we were let inside, we found our seats which were in the lower level on a long bench (think church pew style). This seating was pretty uncomfortable and placed us in super close proximity to fellow guests. 

Once the Opry got started, we felt like we had paid to attend an ad show. As each Opry show is recorded live for the radio, the ads felt endless. Each short act is followed by advertisements which are read to the crowd. The music was fine, but we had never heard of any of the performers we listened to.  Another take away from our  experience was that there was a rowdy group of women seated behind us. They were SUPER loud and talking all throughout the show. We complained about them to Opry staff 3 times, before they were eventually asked to leave as the last performer took the stage. 

For me, the Opry was a one and done experience. I am a country music fan, but I would only recommend the Opry on either a night a big performer was hitting the stage or recommend the Opry to a diehard country music fan. Additionally, I would not bring children to the Opry as I do not believe it would keep them entertained. If you just have a short time in Nashville, stay downtown and hit the local, live music joints - these are less expensive and much more fun than the Opry.

I went to Flying Saucer to meet some friends the night before Thanksgiving.  Apparently they do a special glass every year - Turkey of the Year?  I didn't know this but my friends were excited about it.  Since it was featuring Anthony Weiner this year, I ended up having to get a couple for myself.  hahaha fun

So this is a nice bar, typical of other Flying Saucers with tables, tall bar tables, couches, games, etc.  They serve beer of all sorts.  I am not a very big beer fan, but I do have some "fancy" beers I can drink.  So I stuck to them.  I think maybe they have liquor somewhere "if you really want it" but I am not 100% on that.  Maybe it is just wine.  The food I had was really just snacks like pretzels and cheese plate.  Bartender and wait staff were really nice and helpful, especially with securing us those glasses!

Overall this is a good place and if you dig beer then you will love it.  As for me, I'll probably stick to other places that are more used to pouring cocktails!

Came here with a whole bridal party the night before their wedding. We were seated in the balcony and had a pretty good time listening to the bands and musicians which included Billy Ray Cyrus who is the only performer I knew since I'm don't typically listen to country music. Their drink prices were pretty high though we still got one since it was a celebration. Line for bathroom wasnt too bad since it moved pretty quickly.

Always come to BB's 2-3 times a year but something this year has changed, every table in the place had a reserved sign after a hour of drinking at the bar it was clear no one was coming to fill the tables so my six friends just took over a empty table and had dinner and drinks . Over the Friday night over 30 percent of the so called reserved tables were left empty as people tried to get seated were turned away.

Saturday night we came back with the group of six paid the cover and found out all the tables again all had reserved signs we waited at the bar that was full already, while empty tables filled the room. Staff was rude and we complained about not being seated for a hour. Over half the tables by 9:30 were still empty but the staff made us wait. They won't need to next time as we will take are money somewhere else. Take care of people that come to your club that are there and not people that don't show up for tables.

Time for new management here

Here at happy hour killing some time before an event in Nashville. Probably about 20 people total in the bar getting drinks and ordering food.

Food, from what I could see did look good. One small downside they had a Bushwacker machine, however nobody had mixed anything up yet. They did have draft beer on special, buy one get one free. Two beers out the door price $4.50. 

Bartender was very nice and made sure that I had everything I needed. She talked with everyone in the bar making everyone feel welcome and spent a fair amount of time talking about local venues and music and her band. 

Overall the bar has a pretty cool vibe. If you are lucky you may find some street parking in front. You'll have to feed the meter's until 6:00 (Monday through Friday - not sure about Saturday).

Really friendly staff and reasonable prices should make this a must stop if you are in the area.

I'm not giving five stars because it's owned by Jack White. I think this is a unique one of a kind record store.  It's a record store which only sells artists who are signed by Third Man Records. It's difficult to find parking. For music fans, this is definitely worth a stop. It is a small place and it's divided into three rooms. One room is for CD's, books and stickers. Another room is for t-shirts and records. Then another room is posters, juxebox, and an old photo booth which unfortunately was out of order along with an old booth where you can press your own records. The employees were nice and helpful. I ended up buying a Loretta Lynn CD where she duets with Jack White and a t-shirt for my friend who is a big Jack White fan.

Small venue. Only bad seats would be all the way at top, otherwise there is a great view all around. Pew seating with plenty of room. 6 performers are on stage for about 15 mins each. You can feel the history all around and it is a must see for any country music fan. Drinks and snacks available inside. I love concerts, but this was not a concert (no one stands up or dances, no drunk people crawling around)-this is a show where you sit and enjoy the performances and are just present in the moment. Had a great time. First show ran late so we had to wait outside in the rain for everyone at that show to leave before they would let us in. We walked over from the mall, so I'm not sure of their parking situation. It was hard to plan our visit in advance because the performances are not set up with much advance notice. I plan to go back again next time we are in Nashville.

Thanks to the yelp event and the generous people at the Tippler, I had a gift card to spend.  Lo and behold, my friend arranged a happy hour there for another friend's birthday.  Opportunity to spend and check the place out?  I am in!

So I got there at around 5 pm and it was pretty dead except for our group.  The main bar area has a lot of tables to choose from, so if you get there at happy hour you are likely to have your pick.

Once I was seated it was time to pick my drink.  I already knew they had moscow mules so I chose a Tito's vodka version.  Our waiter was a doll - totally chatty, he knew his booze, and we talked quite a bit about the house made ginger beer and my favorite store bought ginger beer to make them with at home.  (It is Goya by the way...if anyone knows where I can get the Goya ginger beer around here you should holla at me since I've been ordering it on Amazon...)  I tried another drink after that with cucumber and gin and other things.  Both drinks were great.  

We also tried a sampling of food.  The hummus was deemed "spicy" by some at our table which just shows you how people's tolerable spice levels differ because I thought it was just "flavorful".  The crab cakes were nice for an appetizer.  My favorite things were the mac and cheese (um, VELVEETA, BACON, and peas - that's all A-OK with me!) and the chicken biscuit.  A few at our table didn't like the chicken biscuit because of the tomato jam, but I am always a fan of sweet plus savory so I dug it.  We also had Tippler chips which were just homemade chips perfect for munching while drinking and talking.

Overall I found the experience to be a great one.  It is a nice place, somewhat swanky in decor and ambiance.  Not my normal dirty dive that I love, but a great change of pace.  Plus I got to treat the birthday girl with part of my gift card so it must have brought out the nice girl in me.  And that so rarely happens....  Tip of the hat to you Tippler!

Had a friend playing an acoustic set here one Saturday night so I decided to give it a shot! When I got there I realized I was sooooo hungry so I immediately ordered some cheese sticks. They came out quickly and were pretty tasty, nothing fancy or different about them, just regular mozzarella sticks. Also, ordered some wings since it was $.50 wing night and they had a really good flavor to them! The drinks were decently priced and our waitress was very attentive and a little sarcastic, which we all liked! 
Definitely in a weird location, but it is to be expected given their name. I would not have known about it if my friend had not played a show here!
All these beers and NOT ICE COLD?!!!! WHY? What a shame!!  Not impressed!!

We had a very nice experience, overall, at the Grand Ole' Opry House! We got tickets before we knew who was performing and were pleasantly surprised that Carrie Underwood would be there. As a result we were very close. The sitting is unique as it is church pews. You are allowed to eat food from the snack bar at your seat (though the snack bar leaves a lot to be desired, it's all junk food). I do recommend that you do the gift shop first as the line gets long. It's a once in a lifetime experience that every country fan should have!

Absolutely, utterly, tremendously, and drastically appalled what happened last night on Tuesday/Wednesday morning. A group of fellow coworkers and I decided to stop in for a beer and some shots after a long shift. (We work at a high end steakhouse.) For me, as a customer service professional to write this about another venue, you know i would have to have been extremely frustrated. Negative stars if possible but more so I hope the bartender last night on Tuesday, October 9th of 2018 gets more training. I mean, my three year old niece has a better attention than the blonde Caucasian chick that was slinging beers.

Back to the story. So my two buddies was already there and had some shots of Jameson and were drinking Miller lite and yuengling lite. I was with another buddy and we met up and sat with them for 11 minutes before being greeted. This place was NOT busy. That's why they had ONE bartender. But evidently this ONE bartender was high off some shit or her peripherals were damaged beyond repair. We sat on the right side of the bar as you come in the door. As industry workers we understand that she could have been busy and making drinks, but anything past ten minutes is a bit excessive. 

Here's the kicker that set me off. She comes over right? She serves my buddy who is NEXT to me. Like physically, his ass is in the chair next to mine. Maybe a two feet apart? You get the idea, he was NEXT to me. He orders a Miller high life and a shot. She opens his beer, and I'm thinking, maybe she didn't ask me yet because she's serving him so I'll be patient. (On top of the 11 minutes I've already waited.) she turns around and pours his shot and I'm literally TWO FEET in front of her face, looking at her as if I was gazing into the illusions, deep, dark abyss(not that sinister way but you get it, I was hoping she would look up and give me some type of nod or "hey I'll be right there." She grabs his card and asks if he would like to close or keep it open, and he responded keep it open. She does her thing on the POS system and asks my buddy (guest so and so) who was already there with beers and shots if he wanted two more. Great idea and good upsale homie, but uhhhh, hello? I'm right here, may I get a drink? Like WTF. So she pours two more shots and ask him about his last name on the card to make sure it's the right tab, does a glance at everyone's drinks, then!! DRUMROLL PLEASE............She walks away. What am I? Chopped liver??!!! Forgotten turd?? I mean got damn I love me some foie gras and truffles but Jesus Christ Bloody Mary! So my friends were stunned. Kinda like if you play overwatch, the character mccree stuns you with his stunning bomb, or like a flash bang during infantry raids, or like when you get that call from the one girl you hooked up with and says she's pregnant? That kinda stunned. My buddies started to call for her as do I, and we got up to look for her and I told them "hey man it's no worries, I'll just head home." After a few minutes of debating about the caliber of offense/insult/lack of awareness that took place, I drove home. 

You walk into an establishment and don't get served is one thing. Maybe the bar was backed up and drinks took a long time. Maybe your food was misplaced or brought to the wrong table. Maybe you are really inebriated and your server refuses service. But to walk into an establishment and getting IGNORED is a fucking stab to the heart man. I don't know whether to laugh or to cry in a dark corner. Laugh at whoever trained her or laugh at her disability of vision or laugh at her awareness. Or to cry in a corner because I felt so low down and so unimportant. So much that my ego needs boosting. Just kidding, I drove home and stopped at Kroger and got a six pack so I'm all gravy now. Then ten minutes ago I stopped at frugal and got a bottle of Mac 18. Ya know, to satisfy the shot of air and the bottle of negligence I drank last night at DawgHouse saloon. 

Man. Maybe my standards are too high. I mean I just wanted several beers and a round of shots for everyone. Not like I was gonna get a shaken drink or an old fashion. Maybe I was just hoping there would be a glimpse of urgency in the bartender. Maybe I hoped at the wrong place. 

Disappointed almost to the brink of the buffalo bills legacy of unsatisfied super bowl runs. Or the legacy of the browns as of late. Almost to the point where Cracker Barrel fired brads wife. Almost to the point where the falcons lost the Super Bowl two years ago. Speaking of which it's gonna take a New England patriot comeback for me to even THINK about coming back. That includes when I'm on the toilet. You know how you contemplate life when you do number two? I'm afraid if I think about the disappointment of this place I may get constipated instead.

Great choice! Loved the music, good food and superb service!  Friendly folks and a good vibe will keep us coming back for more.  Try them out if new to downtown scene, very different and more sophisticated than Broadway crazies.  Ribs are best, fried pickles and cold local brews combined with sweet gal server was perfect!
Jack White's record label. @thirdmanrecords So wonderful!

We were there for a couple of hours with a party of 8. We all just wanted a cool place to finish watching the Titan game and watch the next up coming game. We Spent well over $500. Asked for the Green Bay Packers game be turned on. We were told they have to ask the manager. The manager was nowhere to be found. We were told they were too busy look. That was not only including the bartenders, but waitstaff, 'security' and whomever else was asked. We even told them what channel.  Finally we were told that Redneck Riveria doesn't get the Fox channel. Hmmm. Every other bar had it on and we could see it on at Luke Bryan's.  This bar just doesnt happen to carry one of the major networks?! I guess we know where to not spend our money next time. Sorry John Rich.  We were hoping for so much better.

Tour Review Only: 
What an outstanding place! So glad to finally get back to Nashville for the first time since I was fourteen. My girlfriend and I were out cruising around town and decided to head to the Opry. We checked on a tour... since we were also interested in touring The Ryman we were told it would be best to buy the tickets now (on a Sunday) and just return Monday at The Opry for the tour, then you have the rest of the day to make it downtown and check out The Mother Church. Great advice.

We returned early Monday morning and off we went, through the tumultuous security checkpoint (I kid - it's not that bad, just check for weapons and the like) and over to our meeting point. They start with a cool Intro video featuring that Shelton guy, followed by the tour itself. It was a small manageable group, so that was nice! You pretty much get to go almost everywhere, including the sound stage where HeeHaw was filmed for many years! So cool!

The cherry on top had to be setting foot on the very stage where music legends have played for years. The second best part, I think, was seeing all of the dressing rooms - combined with hearing all of the behind-the-scenes stories.

It was also incredible to hear about the rough time they had during that epic flood! Amazingly, how so many great people came together to resurrect The Opry in such short time frame.

On your way out don't forget to visit the Gift Shop. You know you want to...

I'm not into country music like my wife but I loved the experience at the Grand Ole Opry House and would recommend it to everyone visiting Nashville.
Most of the acts were amazing.  The facility is nice inside, bathrooms are clean.  The bench seating could use improvement.  Although comfortable, with today's society mostly overweight you most likely will be squished, touching shoulders and butt cheeks together with your neighbors.  
Make sure you eat before you come to the show, there are not a lot of options at the venue and the ones that exist are really disappointing.
Enjoy!
Walked in and walked right back out. Didn't try the food, there was no band playing. It was pretty much dead. Maybe caught them on an off night? It was a Saturday night though...

There is a guided tour of the Opry that you can pay to take. You'll see backstage, the dressing rooms and the boxes where Opry members get their fan mail. (Garth Brooks picks up his own when he's there. Fun fact.) I'm not a huge country music fan so I was a bit bored, but our guide was super pumped about all of the information she knew. She made it entertaining to say the least.

Possibly the dirtest restaurant I've ever experienced. The food is definitely sub-par but the prices are not! The staff was friendly, no complaints there. One of the employees was busy explaining to the other two how their pay has changed and how it works now. That is not appropriate conversation for a customer to have to hear. This place is a 10 on a gross scale of 1-10!
Yes because what Broadway needed was another redneck loud terrible music bar with overpriced drinks.... yep not great.... plus does anyone ever clean in here?

This place is great! Staff were very friendly and helpful with my food and beer selection.  I am a fan of trying new things and the food was amazing.  Great beer selection too! I will definitely recommend the Flying Saucer to friends and family.

Five stars for Blake Shelton being in the video they make you watch. 

Lol seriously. 

Must do while in Nashville! Cool to see where all of our favorite artists come to make history!

Keeping it true Detroit the store is located in a not great area right across from a homeless shelter with no parking lot so you have to drive around to find a 'safe' spot on the street - so Detroit - ha!!! Fun place with a very small record section, posters, neat memorabilia, antique music related things (a monkey band and old timey recording booth), and lots of White Stripes chatzkis (t-shirts, mouse pads, stickers) - everything way overpriced for tourists but still legit cus it's Jack White yo! Super friendly staff and super awesome they host shows there.

We really enjoyed the Grand Ole Opry House. It was neat to be at a venue where all the entertainers seemed in awe of performing there.

We went to the second show and they did an effective job turning the crowd over and the show started very close to on time.

I got a kick out of the live "commercials". The host was reading the scripts about the sponsors.

It was also leaving a concert with out ringing in the ears, I guess I have crossed the line and I am too old because some concerts are too loud.

It' s a Flying Saucer. Some reviewers here to seem not to know it's a chain, so here's a heads up, people: there are Flying Saucers everywhere. And they're fine. Lots of beer. Bar food. Typically huge so you can go with a big party. That's why I was there recently. I needed a place for happy hour with a lot of my coworkers. There are places closer and walking distance to our office on the north side of downtown, but we really needed a table that could seat 20. So Flying Saucer it is. It's nice that people who want to eat can order their food (although their food is nothing special). It's also definitely a beer place (obviously), so the beer drinkers in your party are going to enjoy it more than your wine and spirits drinkers! A totally fine place to go for a drink. Nothing special. It's a Flying Saucer.

My girlfriend Julie is a huge Jack White fan so this was a must stop. The record store is intimate but very cool. There are some really cool White Stripes/Jack White memorabilia inside.  Don't forget to peruse the t-shirt selection.

They often have art exhibits and shows in the back part of the compound so I would check the web site to see what is going on.

We were there for the half marathon and decided to check it out. Well worth the cost! It was so cool to be walking through the doors and relive what so many country artists dream about. They show you were they wait and do their best to allow you to feel how the artist may feel when they're inducted. It was awesome! They even showed you the areas that were flooded several years ago

This is a small bar near Belcourt university which has live music. We came during a singer songwriter session and the artists they had there were really talented! 

The food there was good, but apparently we got there on a night when they ran out of enough stuff to make about half of the menu unavailable. 

The staff is friendly and the prices are reasonable. If you're going here for a fine dining experience, this isn't the place for you, but if you want a quiet place to relax and listen to some very good musicians, songwriters and singers then this is the place for you.

I'm surprised I'm even writing a review in favor of someone who sang a song called "Save a Horse Ride a Cowboy". In an otherwise godless and clichè country star owned (I mean no respect Dierks Bentley) strip of downtown that's infested with tourist and bachelorette parties stands this building. What sets it apart is what I like to call the OUTSTANDING MORAL FIBER FACTOR. Amazingly, John Rich isn't out to gobble up all your money via $15 watered down "specialty" drinks and shots. Instead he's created a business which pays homage to soldiers and pairs it with quality whiskey and on theme decorations/seating (read:redneck). Fun fact! A portion of proceeds from each bottle sold goes to Folds of Honor, a non-profit organization that provides educational scholarships to children and spouses of fallen or disabled members of the military. That's really special if I don't say so myself. 

Logistically, there are three levels so you aren't crammed in like sardines. The bartenders are attentive and live music is available on each floor. The whiskey was great and I highly recommend the bushwhacker. 

All in all, this is my new favorite bar on Broadway. It doesn't get better than a proactive bar committed to its community and those who serve us. In an otherwise greedy and insipid area of town, this is a standout for quality on all fronts.

It was thrilling to be sitting at the Opry to me. I loved the show and had good handicap seats. Each artist does a three song routine. I would recommend and will go back next time I'm in town. Highly suggest you go

This is a must while visiting Nashville.   We had the Opry House Daytime Backstage Tour that last about one hr.  The tour guide was very informative.  He showed us the dressing rooms and told us the story behind them.  You can also stand on the famous six-foot circle of oak cut from the stage at Ryman Auditorium. Very cool experience.
What an amazing experience! Even though we had the cheapest furthest away seats it was still incredible!

We did the backstage VIP tour as one of the six attractions included in our $75 city pass! You get to see the entire backstage, from where the stars enter to where they practice to the stage itself where they perform.

You also get to peek into the rooms performers stay in; a look inside some of the rooms of famous country stars; an up-close view of mailboxes of the Opry members, including Reba McEntire's; and a clip of emotional videos of various musicians being invited to be a member.

Reserve your spot by calling them ahead of time. They are closed on Sundays for reservations so plan accordingly.

Tour length: About 45 minutes, including a 5-minute intro video

Tour group size: About 25 people

How to get here: Drive or take a cab (our Lyft from downtown Nashville was about $16 each way)

Other things to note: tour started on time, another group's tour almost overlapped ours, the guides were informative and knowledgeable, and there are a few photo opportunities, including one where they try to sell you an overpriced photo of you and those in your party behind the mic belting out a tune.

Weirdest part is the location is at a mall that looks like any mall in suburbia USA. There's a Dave & Busters and a Bed, Bath, and Beyond right across from it, which just struck me as bizarre. Something so unique as the Opry across from something so mundane like D&B and BBB!
Had a really great time, got to sing 1 song and enjoy the rest of night with hubby. The drink prices were a little high for size of plastic cup, but still good

As a fair-weathered country fan, I even found this tour interesting. I imagine that any huge country fans would be loosing their ish if they went on this!

You get to walk where all the country stars have gone- into the deluxe dressing rooms, up the celebrity back entrance, on the stage and on the little wood circle in the center of it where they all sing. 

The coolest part was the mini mail room. Apparently, fans can send the Grand Ol Opry mail for any of their favorite stars. The Grand Ol Opry saves it and hands it to the stars when they enter. Such a cool tradition! 

The dressing rooms are gorgeous and super fancy. It's cool to see which celebrities choose which dressing room. You also get to take a picture on the stage and there's a great gift shop.

Fantastic show! The facility is comfortable and very casual. The show format is an actual radio show. An act comes out, does 3 songs then exits stage and while the next act is setting up there are a couple of brief commercials. Very efficient. The only drawback is the quality of food. It is awful junk food. You can bring food/drinks into the Auditorium so that's a plus. Free Parking accross the street.

I love this place. Love hearing about the history and the backstage tour is full of interesting information. The videos of Blake Shelton are a plus, too :) Standing in that circle on stage sure is special. We only did the tour this time around because all of the recent shows were at the Ryman, but I can't wait to come back and catch another show here in the future!

Amazing staff and service! Came in today before the crowd hit looking for a chill Sunday after a late Saturday out. Was served by the only guy bartender I saw in the building and I can honestly say I've never met a more friendly face behind the bar! Drinks were great, service phenomenal and the atmosphere was wonderful. Can't wait to come back!!

As the below review reads "take this for what it is" that couldn't be any more true. 

Redneck Rivera is exactly what you would think it would be. It's a promising bar, not much thrill to it but not terrible either. The live music was pretty good though! I also got a kick out of when I asked for a water and she pointed at a gatorade cooler behind me. 

I would probably go back. But not super eager too.
Tries to stand out as a strong supporter for the military but doesn't know how to check a military ID??? $6.50 for a can of bud light? Consider this a one beer and move on location at best.

I have heard about The Grand Ole Opry my entire life.  So, when my wife & I found ourselves coming through Nashville and it turned out that there was a show, it seemed like something we should do.

We are not big country music fans, but the show could not have been more fun!  It was a real slice of Americana.  Everyone was extremely welcoming and friendly.  The fact that when we bought our tickets we had not idea who would be on the venue added to the adventure.  We enjoyed every artist and were pleasantly surprised when the final headliner was The Band Perry (If I die Young.)

It is not cheap, but not outrageous for top scale live entertainment.  The crowd tended to the old side, but it was a full-family attraction with all ages well represented.  Parking was ample.  The seats are bench-style, but well padded and there is not a bad view in the house!  Even a huge thunderstorm could not dampen the evening.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Honestly from a music city I would expect more from the karaoke scene.  Karaoke is meant to be for everybody and offer a nonjudgmental atmosphere.  The karaoke dj here has special rules and special signs that make the experience very impersonal.  Also.....2 bucks for a small cup of water.  Don't bother coming here. Try literally any other karaoke place.If you're looking for really good karaoke you need to head to Detroit.

First time to Nashville and loved it. The Grand Ole Opry was wonderful. It was quite an interesting experience. We had handicap seats that were excellent. My husband is not a country fan but really enjoyeD it. The history  is remarkable.

The 4-day weekend that was Yelp Spring Break 2014 officially ended for me Sunday at noon. That gave me pretty much a whole day to run around Nashville & get to all the places I'd heard about while in town but hadn't been to yet.

"You have to go check out Flying Saucer." I'd heard that over & over again the week I was in Nashville. At the taproom near where I was staying. At each craft brewery I visited. It always came up, sooner or later, in conversations: Flying Saucer's 80+ taps of quality craft beers.

So on my last full day in Nashville, I finally made my way over for a little lunch & a lot of beer. This place bills itself as Nashville's draft emporium & yes, yes it is. Lunch time on a Sunday was slow & most of the place (& it's a really big place) was empty. I sat at the bar. 

The bartender was very attentive & accommodating. Although it wasn't busy, Sundays are a great day to visit Flying Saucer. It's $3.50 pints on all TN beers. Looks like I'm drinking local. For bites to go with my brews, I had the Rocket-Tots & those were screamin' good!

Looking over a calendar they had posted, Sunday $3.50 TN pints was just the beginning. Flying Saucer does all kinds of weekly specials & events. I was really starting to wish I'd be in town longer so I could come back.

My advice for any craft beer enthusiast visiting Nashville... "You have to go check out Flying Saucer." & go early while you're in town so you'll have the chance to go back again. Mondays are $3.00 pints on almost every beer in the house, you don't want to miss that.

This historic and culturally significant venue is a true beauty. Some of the biggest stars have stood on the stage and gave some of their greatest performances. 

What is love about the Grand Ole Opry is the layout; no matter where you are sitting there are no bad seats. You will have a great view throughout the entire venue. 

Be sure to pick up a few sourvenirs from the gift shop, and to take the behind the scenes tour for $24 bucks. You get to learn the history of the Grand Ole Opry, go backstage, check out the dressing rooms, and walk the halls that some of the greatest names in country music have walked. Its truly a magical experience.

I had heard of this of course, but had no idea what it really was.  

A live radio show... Complete with live commercials from local merchants. 

We enjoyed all of the artists, the beauty and traditions of The Grand Ole Opry and the banter of the Master of Ceremonies. 

It is a must see if you are near Nashville.  I would go again, even though Country music is not really my fav;) 
The whole experience is awesome.  

Next time I would look into a VIP pass to see the inner working of the back of the house;) 

YeeHaw!

TERRRIBLEEEEEE!!!!

If I could give this place negative stars I would!!!
I came here with my friends last weekend, my friend asked the bartender for a splash of extra rum in her drink which insulted the bartender who said she just made it and she wasn't adding anything to it. When my friend turned to one of our other friends confused about the situation, the bartender came back over and yelled to the bouncer to "get these f*cking girls out". The bouncer literally came over and ripped them both out of their seats. They did not refuse to leave- we wanted to leave!! He aggressively grabbed them, and cursed at them. Calling them "scrawny b*tches" and to "get the f*ck out" Ranting insults and berating them!! When I told the man we were leaving he didn't need to put his hands on us he actually shoved me!!! I have NEVER been so APPALLED in my life!! This place is classless and the way they treat women here is beyond offensive!!! My friend has bruises on her arm!!! They should honestly be embarrassed to have employers that act this way. Hope to see this establishment shut down, it's a downright disgrace!!!!
Great to experience being here but not my favorite concert to come to.   Very fast show and not much music for one artist. But I'm glad I got to experience it.  Just not what I fully expected.
No longer a $3 cover on Friday and Saturday nights, yippee!!

This terrible establishment failed to protect a patron from an angry customer. She proceeded to punch, scratch and completely disrespect a family of customers. This was atrocious all because we asked if she was done at her table so we could spread out to more seats with our large party. We did not force her out but simply asked the question

Awesome spot to grab a drink in a relaxed, chill atmosphere!  Their beer list is amazing--they have something like 100 beers available.  Their wine and cocktail lists are a bit smaller, but still good.  I had the Tennessee cocktail and I will say it didn't taste like there was much alcohol in it.
As others mentioned, not super friendly friendly as compared to other places in Nashville, but the vibe is such that it's nice to just chat and lay back on their comfy couches (amazing) w/o having someone come by all the time.  Also, their food is great!  Get the jalapeno tots (comes w/ cheese, bacon, fried egg) and the pretzels (the sauces are amazing).

We would like to send a special shout out to our bartender, whose name we forgot, but just moved there from Seattle, WA with his lady. 

Thank you for making our first night in Nashville on our honeymoon great! He kept good conversation, recommended some really good beers to us, and turned us on to the Surprise Cheese Fries (I think that's what it is called) 

The Flying Saucer has been our comfort bar since we first found it in Memphis, TN. 
The place is very down to earth and chill and if you sign up for their UFO club, and sample I think 300 beers that they serve there, you can get yourself a plate up on the ceiling. 
We have always had a great experience at this bar and can't wait to come back. Be it Nash or Memphis.

A must for anyone that comes to Nashville ! A must!
Amazing hall
Amazing talent
