Acoustics are great no matter where you sit
A must to see the best talent

Oh my god, this place was so disappointing. An old friend was in town and we made the horrible mistake of bringing her here, I was embarrassed for Nashville to be represented by them to my friend. 

Service: our waitress was obviously new, which was fine... She mentioned taking an abc class recently and made small talk with us about how scary the class was and about how important it was to see every customers I.D's.... She took our beer orders....and DID NOT I.D. a single one of us, we were kind of dumbfounded...

Food: horrible. I'm talking probably the worst food we've had in over a year. We ordered the nacho plate which consisted of low quality chips, nasty pickled jalapeños and the MOST DISGUSTING queso I have EVER had. It wasn't even hot, it was cold and thick and over everything. Absolutely disgusting. My stomach actually hurt after eating it. The other plate we got was the fried pickle appetizer, it wasn't nearly as bad but was hardly memorable. 

Considering the restaurant is advertised as a "tapas" restaurant we assumed they might actually give a damn about their food. It was laughable, they should be ashamed they even served that.

Great music and atmosphere - Awful service and average food. $5.00 cover charge for the live entertainment. We waited around 30 minutes for a table (pretty average) but then had to wait another half an hour for someone to even come take our drink order. We shared a few appetizers (pulled pork nachos and fried pickles) that weren't as appetizing as they seemed on menu description. The band was great but just didn't make up for the lake of service and sub par food.
Let's just say I couldn't find the newest Kenny Chesney!

Terrible experience here! Went last night with a group of people and the bouncer didn't let me In when i had different forms of ID's i'm 23 years old. Highly recommend on getting new bouncers there so rude. You just lost business

When in Nashville I knew I had to do at least one country music fan tour. We did all the bars with live music off and around Broadway, but I wanted something with a little more history to it. I considered the Country Music Hall of Fame, but honestly it looked too commercial (there was a Luke Bryan special exhibit, he's not really my kind of country), so we opted to do the Grand Ole Opry Backstage tour. We got to the grounds, which while surrounded by a shopping mall (why does everything have to be so commercial) were beautiful. It was a little after noon and we bought tickets for the next tour for $24 each and followed the signs to the beginning of tour meeting spot. It turns out the lunch time tour was a great idea. We were the only two waiting there, and ended up getting what was essentially a private tour.

Initially you're brought into a room where Blake Shelton (I'm assuming the star changes from time to time) narrated a little bit of history and what we would see along the tour. We took a green screen picture which ended up being the two of us on the Opry stage...the idea was cute, the actual picture of me was not so we skipped purchasing.

Walking through the tour is exciting. Even taking out the celebrity element (thought here were lots of times when my favorite country artist's dressing rooms and mailboxes were pointed out and I got excited) it's a really beautiful place. Each dressing room has a theme and is incredibly well kept and decorated loved the "glitz and glamour" room and "into the circle" where those making their first Opry appearance get ready. Each room is so carefully decorated and well thought out and unique. 

We got to walk in the wings backstage, but maintenance was being done so we weren't actually able to go on stage (I may have put a toe just to say I did). We also got to see the auditorium seating area, which is all wooden church bench type seating. Probably not super comfy but very beautiful and traditional. Along the way there were a few more narrated movies, but our tour guide did a really great job. Usually on big tours I don't ask many questions because I don't want to be the person holding up the tour, but since it was only us I got to really talk to her and gossip about the country stars she had met and what it was like to get to work there and see everything.

I think the tour was worth the price for sure. I loved the history. However, there were some commercial elements as well. They were heavily promoting the show Nashville, but seeing the costumes for that show was pretty cool (those girls are tiny). The gift shop at the end was of course pricey, but honestly I didn't see anything I couldn't get somewhere else in Nashville if I really wanted it, so I managed to get out of there without extravagant purchases. I highly recommend, and try to go at lunch time when everyone else is eating, you might end up on a private tour too.

Continuing our Country Music filled Day, after spending the afternoon at the Country Music Hall of Fame, we had tickets for the Grand Ole Opry.
I was preparing myself mentally for 2 hours of Country Music.  If you don't know me, I am not a fan of this type of music, but was starting to enjoy some of it...  maybe because I was in Nashville, and maybe because I started realizing that County is not just one sound, that there's many types of it and some I actually do like (in moderation)  ;p

As you walk in, you are greeted by two giant guitars, and security.
Line moves fast while security checks everyone making sure nothing illegal or harmful goes in.

The theater has drinks for sale, snacks, and more.
We had bought our tickets online and walked right in, once we found our seats show started right on time.

The show is divided in two parts, and it's done as a radio show, with a man, making announcements of services and products from time to time.
There's a "host" for the first half, and after the intermission come another "host".  Between the artists, these hosts are also singers and between presenting and sharing anecdotes with the public, they sing as well. 

Some performances are funny, some beautiful, some make you want to move your feet, and some transport you somewhere else with their music and voices.  The performances are not too long so you get to hear a lot of different songs and styles of Country Music, and wont' get bored at any time.

There's all types of singers, young, old, bluegrass, modern, Christian, and more.
Each brings their own team and instruments, while the Grand Ole Opry also has their backup singers and musicians.  

At the end of the night, this "non- Country music" girl came out with many videos of the performances and wanting to hear more of the ones that made me smile and move my feet.

There's also a tour of the theater if you are interested, we opted out of that and go to dinner instead.  But I am sure glad we went to this show, even without knowing which artists where performing, this was totally worth experiencing it, and I recommend it to everyone going to Nashville.

Our Hawaii educator team was excited to have their first (not my first) Nashville experience.  Unfortunately, it wasn't what they had hoped for.  

I'll start off with the only highlight of the night:  the live band. They were AWESOME: there's nothing like a full, live band.  They were entertaining, engaging, and very talented.

Other than that, everything else was downhill.  To start things off, our waitress treated us like we were a nuisance.  Ignoring us as she checked on other tables, we waited very patiently (like 20 minutes) before she half-heartedly asked us if we were ready to order. We were excited to get a round of drinks along with trying a delectable dessert we saw placed on another table next to us.  She rudely replied: "Oh, the kitchen stopped making that 20 minutes ago. It is what it is." We were dumbfounded, as that is how long we waited for her to check on us.  We put in our drink order and waited for another 10 minutes. When we glanced at the waitress station at the bar (we were seated nearby) to see if our drinks were prepared, we noticed our waitress arguing with the bartender.  Perhaps, we thought, this is why she was not delivering great customer service (or even mediocre). 

In the end, she rarely checked on us. We had one drink in a total of our one hour there (we initially planned on staying there but quickly changed our minds and patronized another venue).  

Disappointing, to say the least.  To travel thousands of miles only to have poor customer service is a sad thing.  If I owned this venue, I would seriously re-evaluate the staff, as they are the face of the company.  Never coming back here when we return to Nashville for future educator conferences.

Treat yourself and don't cheat yourself and get the Ribs! The rub they put on the ribs, they don't even need their amazing BBQ sauce on them! Add the ambience and atmosphere with the live music and it's a must stop when you're in Nashville! Steve the bartender is legit too!

Bring your lube for getting screwed here. $5 for a 12oz draft Miller Lite?!?! WHOA! 

Service was ruff. Bar appearance looked ruff. Bathrooms were SUPER RUFF. Just pass.

I have been to the GOOH several times over the years and have witnessed many great groups including Icons Buck Owens, Mini Pearl, Roy Acuff and Jonny Cash. Tonight included, I am always impressed by the talent and professionalism the musicians and comics the GOOH showcases. Hats off to Rick Skaggs et al. You were amazing.

Showed up with friends and family to watch game. Managed to get corner spot at bar. We had several friends requesting that we get them drinks as it was very crowded....UA draws a hell of a crowd, Roll Tide.  Short hair blonde was great and knew we were there to spend a good amount and bought plenty of rounds for other fans as well. In swoops skinny attitude ridden bartender with the most horrendous visible grey hair extensions by the way.  We (husband and myself) drank very little and knew we needed to pace ourselves  so yes, it was very easy to see those God awful extensions.  Never pick apart someone's appearance but she 100% deserved it. No one knew why she decided to serve our corner but when my husband put up his hand (not even called or waved) to order drinks for patrons behind us, she laid into him calling him every name in the book. There were at least 20 people who came to his defense asking why she would berate him.....she didn't like that she was clearly out of line and beckoned the bouncers over to physically throw him out. Subsequently, she threw out a hefty tip that we routinely would have paid. For a big game and behalf of our friends, they were looking at a minimum 100-150 in tips. We were all asked to leave since we defended my husband. Disgusting display of management. Will NEVER set foot in that place. I may sneak in to give the nice short blond bartender the tip she deserves. If she's reading this, feel free to message me if that B of a bartender gets fired bc I would like to tip you what you deserve. I stand by my word.

I really enjoy coming to the Grand Ole Opry House. I've been here before on a backstage tour. That was really neat.  Tonight I saw Jason Aldean and Michael Ray, along with some other amazing talent. The Opry store has some cute things. Clothing seems to b overprices. The only thing I feel that is prices decent are the mugs. The staff is polite and we will be returning to another show (one day).

I am not a frequent visitor of Midtown, and after my night out I have no clue why. There's more space to move around, less noise to talk to your friends, and drinks are way, way cheaper. 

For a Friday night, DawgHouse was not very lively. But I really had no problem with it, we were able to sit at the bar with no problem talking, and got quick service. The music was kind of lacking, the DJ wasn't doing much to draw in too big of a crowd.

Overall I had a good time at DawgHouse but they had a lot of competition up and down the road and they were not seeming to do to well in terms of getting people in the door.

Look, I don't really know anything about music and I'm definitely not a ridiculous snob about anything Jack White-related (in reality, I really don't care all that much for him or The White Stripes... sue me).  

So, as a person who knows nothing and doesn't really get all nerdy about music stores, Third Man was a pretty fun place to be.  The vinyl records are insanely expensive (everyone post-1985 would be appalled at the prices) and barely anyone has a record player, so annoying.  However, there's a ton of really fun stuff in here that entertained me while my husband looked at the measly record and tshirt collection.  

A) There's a MOLD-A-RAMA.  A FREAKING MOLD-A-RAMA!!!  I'm not sure where these used to exist, but if you grew up in the Chicagoland area pre-1995, you likely visited Brookfield Zoo and got to use a Mold-A-Rama to make gorillas, giraffes, and more!  That smell evokes a nostalgia in me that is difficult to describe.... and you can make one at third man!  You bet I did and I still have it because it's amazing.  I'd go back here just to use that machine again.

B) There's a recording booth where you can cut your own record.  Kind of expensive but super cool if you're into that sort of thing.

C) There's old carnival-like machines with dancing monkeys and such that play music.  Super adorable!  I'd spend money on this any day of the week.

I'll likely end up back here some day because my husband loves JW, TWS, all things Detroit, and music... but I'll only come if there's a Mold-A-Rama in it for me.

Friday special - BAD Food, BAD Drinks, BAD Service. They play a lot on their acronym which is cool. Downtown for a meeting and decided to hang around for lunch. Three of us gravitate to The Arcade. The other too had been here I think, I had not. It's pretty hard to find if you haven't been before. I have been to The Arcade several times and never knew it was there. It is actually in the alley that bi-sects The Arcade. 

Cool vibe and lots of character. Ample bar area along with booths and tables, exposed brick and beams, peaked ceiling. This looks like a great late night place. They have open mic night on Tuesdays.

I had the hot ham sandwich on wheat and the turkey sausage and white bean soup. Soup could have been warmer and as always, a larger portion. The amount of ham was ample and had Swiss cheese lettuce and tomato - the taste was great. Co-workers got the bleu burger and pork sliders - on with chips, one with fries. They didn't ask how he wanted the burger cooked and it was overdone, but said the taste was good - cooked on a flattop. Like me, he liked it a little pink on the inside. Fries were your typical frozen fries - nothing more, nothing less. Think the chips may be made in-house. Pork was deemed OK, but needed the sauce. 

It is a comfortable, cool kind of place - lots of tattoos and piercings on the staff, but that's all good. Sandwiches and burgers are the main fare. Service was exceptional - making one aware that lots of the food was probably already cooked and then warmed up - but it is hard to mess up a ham sandwich and obviously soup cannot be made to order.

If it was music alone it would be TEN STARS!!! The music was AWESOME!!! The band welcome members of my sorority with open arms. We danced and just had a grand ole time! 

Not my margarita? I am still trying to figure out what exactly that was and in a paper cup, like really! I expected somewhat the same such as  BB King in my home town but NEGATIVE! The bbq nachos was good and tasty as an appetizer. I ordered catfish and shrimp. The fries were to salty, the catfish was to seasoned (keep it simple) the shrimp was okay. 

Service was good and somewhat swift. The guy was really nice. The atmosphere is nice with the awesome band.

I came to this place with my sister and a few of her coworkers when we were in Nashville for a work conference. It was an excellent choice! The live music was really good (although one of the bands did get a bit too loud - it was hard to even enjoy conversation) and the atmosphere was nice. It's a nice big open space with tons of tables and a laid back vibe so it's easy to sit and feel comfortable and enjoy the music. 

All the food we ordered was good... ribs, burgers, fried chicken, fried pickles, wings... Nothing that really blew me totally away but it was all very very tasty. The beer selection was good too, and so was the service! I have nothing bad to say about this place except the music getting a bit too loud. If i was in Nashville, I'd be back.

I love this place been coming to this bar for 4 years love the djs the owners the music and other patrons very friendly place to go. Cheapest drinks in downtown Nashville and you get to be a star while your come check it out for yourself and have a good time ..so 5 stars it is for me thanks Ms.kellis for all the good times .

A great live music venue. It is intimate and the band was awesome. A little loud for me but I am getting older. 

I had the pulled pork sandwich, it comes with fries. The pork had great flavor, but it was a little dry. Thankfully, they have their own BBQ sauce. Now that is worth the trip itself. 

We arrived around 6:30. They had a couple  of private parties going on. So we registered for a table and waited for about 1 1/2 hours for a table, while there are multiple tables available.

Once seated we waited another 20 minutes or so to order. Then waited a good hour before the food arrived. Not sure if they were short staffed in the back it just overwhelmed. 

It is great food. Give it a Shot and enjoy the blues.

The servers were moving around quite a bit, but the food seemed to be taking for ever

I held the groom's dinner for my son's wedding here in October.  It was the perfect choice, and the event was a huge success.  Kelly was great to work with.   I don't live in Nashville, so I bombarded her with emails with questions and she was quick and thorough with her responses.  I wanted a casual Southern feel to the food and it was excellent! (this was told to me by many of the guests).  The pork, Jambalaya, corn bread, green beans...everything, really, received compliments.  The wait staff (especially Kameron) was completely attentive.  I didn't have to ask for a thing.  As the buffet needed something they were right there to refill.  
We had our own band and they were allowed in the day of the event to practice.  That was extremely nice.  BB Kings did not nickel and dime me on anything.  The prices were the prices.  
People who attended the party are still talking about it, and this is in no small part to the wonderful venue, food, and staff.  Thank you everyone!!!

What an experience, one might even say a religious experience! I knew I had to see a show here while in Nashville. I ordered my tickets two months before my trip!
I will admit, ABC's Nashville had a big part in turning me onto country and exposing me to this historical venue. I knew I had to see the stage that has welcomed & introduced so many greats. I had to see the place artists dream of being inducted into. And I was really excited for the back stage tour!
There isn't a bad seat in the house. I was on the lower level on the left. it was amazing. There were multiple hosts with multiple musicians on the bill. Traditional country, blue grass and more modern as well. The highlight for me was seeing Montgomery Gentry - it was phenomenal!
I highly recommend the backstage tour with ticket purchase and make sure to go after the show as you are more likely to see some of the performers backstage! The video with Darius Rucker is fantastic! I loved watching the night he was invited to join the Opry by Brad Paisley. 
I loved seeing the dressing rooms, each with their own story!

What's with all the negativity. This place is hella cool. The DJ is hands down the best singer of anyone that came on stage. He controlled the vibe and energy and seriously one of the best karaoke DJ's I've seen and heard. Place is huge. Drinks good. Chill out people. It's karaoke. You don't have to cry if they didn't play your song.

While in Nashville, I only had so much time and debated between going on the Ryman Tour or the Grand Ole Opry Tour. I'm so glad I decided to go with the Grand Ole Opry - it was definitely the right choice. They offer a few different tours and I took the Daytime tour. It has a $20 price tag but I highly recommend doing what I did and getting the Nashville Total Access Pass. Google it! It's a good deal to save you some bones.

Our tour guide was very knowledgeable and they lead the tour with some video bits done by Blake Shelton & Carrie Underwood throughout the tour. The tour starts with one of these video bits giving a bit of information to get you going.

The only thing I didn't like was there were about 35 people on our tour. The group just seemed too large and when there were parts of the tour in which we were seated to watch a video, there wasn't enough seating at one point.

They take you backstage, so long as no artists are present, and you get to see the dressing rooms (each with a different theme), various areas behind the scenes and my personal favorite was seeing the mailboxes of all the stars. You can write to any Grand Ole Opry member courtesy of the House and the letter will go in their personal mailbox and they will definitely receive it!

The crowning and final moment of the tour is taking the Grand Ole Opry stage. You can stand on the center circle where many great artists have stood to perform. You get a rush of excitement as you stand on the old wooden circle taking it all in.

The night I went on my tour, Carrie Underwood was going to take the stage for a concert so it was pretty cool standing up in the limelight knowing a gorgeous country superstar would be up there in just a few short hours.

Loved the Grand Ole Opry House, loved the tour, and you best get there when you're in Nashville and get your lovin' on, too!
Smells like stale beer. Went to watch a ball game -- this place was perfect for that. Hopefully a college bar... prob should been sanitized with Clorox to get the smell of beer and vomit to go away.
An unbelievable beer menu, including ciders, lambics, and beer cocktails for those not super into beer (the Hummingbird H2O is great!). A fun stop before or after visiting the Frist!

If you like Jack White, this is the spot for you. I love Jack White, think he's anything & everything so I knew I had to come to Third Man Records. I love that he's eccentric, simple but complicated, keeps his life as private as he can, and I've heard he is kind to fans in person. Plus he does good things for his hometown of Detroit and current town Nashville. Just love the man.

Now then! Third Man Records was founded in 2001 but this space opened in 2009 in Nashville. This location has a recoding studio, photo studio, distribution center and for us fans a record store & shop of items that we can pop in to peruse. I did just that while I was down there and perhaps not to my surprise, found Third Man in a slightly deserted part of Nashville. That being said, I easily walked there from hot & poppin' parts of the city. 

The store is adorable and packed with fun novelty items and some fun records. A bunch of the records are cheap and really a perfect souvenir of visiting the shop. My friend bought a Conan O'Brien album because #bestgingerever and I bought an album with Jack White & The Muppets (Disney/Jim Henson + my man, YES please). $3 each. That's amazing. I was incredibly tempted to buy an Icky Trump shirt but they didn't have my size. 

There were tons of cool items and though a small shop, I could have spent a fortune in there I'm sure. There were a bunch of old timey things that I loved looking over like a jukebox, wax machine, old photobooth, creepy but awesome moving metal figures, and other random items throughout. 

The staff working was nice and I heard them answering random questions from patrons and fans. I didn't catch my White Stripe live and in person but I have heard of others shopping around and him coming up to say howdy. 

Really for rock fans, it's a do~not~miss kind of shop while in Nashville!

This place was the worst.  The bar was pretty dead. There was one two top, one other couple at the bar, and someone who appeared to be the owner or manager sitting at the bar doing paperwork.  
We ordered the gourmet soft pretzel to start. A few
Minutes later the bartender said he was leaving and another lady was taking over. She came by and we reminded her that the guy put in a pretzel for us. About 20 minutes later it came out, and it was 100% one of those microwaveable pretzels. We asked for cheese and mustard but only got cheese. 
While we waited for the pretzel we put in two burgers. They took forever to come out, and when they were so well done. Like hockey pucks. Everything about this place was a disgrace. How can you claim to have the "best burger in town" and not even be able to properly cook a burger?  I would stay far away from here!!!

My friend and I did a tour here, which has been on my bucket list since I was a little girl! The tour is awesome and the tour guides really know their information. You see the front of house and back of house. You get to see the dressing rooms (all different and unique). You also are able to tour the stage and get a picture in the "circle." There's a rather decent sized gift shop full of different things to purchase. Outside the Grand Ole Opry is beautiful so I suggest walking around. A must see when in Nashville.

The blues will never die!  We had a great time here.  It took a little time to get seated hence four stars not five. They took care of us from the bar while we waited  The band was rockin and the place IS popular.  Great vibe. Friendly staff.  Cold beer.  Good food.  The B B King Allstars.  C'mon! What else do you need?  Go for the music and stay for the mac and cheese.  Thank you Faith and your staff there at the Club!
One worker here was wearing an incredibly racist shirt (see attached). It was a shirt for the bar! It made us leave. Much better places around town. Don't bother going here.
One of our favorites in Nashville The bartender was everything you would want in a bartender and quite accommodating! Ohhh and did I mention the ribs?!? Phenomenal! We will definitely be back!

I'm visiting Nashville with my sister and we are both fans of live music. The Grand Ole Opry house offers this in a unique way. On Fridays and Saturdays they have a live broadcast with many performers rotating through the program and an announcer. 
The audience was super engaged as were the employees - it was a fantastic experience. 
The performers ranged from new singer song writers on the scene to seasoned performers like The Oak Ridge Boys and Emmylou Harris. Lots of places to take pictures and a really great place to bring your entire family. You can request birthday wishes and a couple got engaged the night we were there. The auditorium seats a lot of people but it still feels as though you are close to the stage and performers. There isn't a bad seat in the house. So much fun!

Whenever you can, gotta see a show in this cathedral of country music.  

all silly superlatives aside,  just about as intimate and amazing a venue I've ever been to.  even pops seemed to like it.  

Cheryl Crowe was the guest for our private little show.  she's got a lot of Grammys for a reason.  respected their wish for no pics during the performance,  which is fine.  She's a class act,  and deserves the best respect. 

list of faves included all I wanna do,  soak up the sun, my fave mistake, the 1st cut is the deepest, everyday is a winding road,  string enough,  if it makes you happy,  Steve McQueen, a change would do you good, home and closed the show with an encore performance of been a long time. 

just awesome.

Wonderful dinner here last night! Our waitress was wonderful- really seemed like she was happy to serve us. They were crazy busy with a party of 25 upstairs so it took a while to get drinks from the bar but so worth it. (She let us know beforehand) 

I ordered the Aloha burger with baked beans and it was delicious! 

Looked like they had a lot of great specials on different nights. Locals night, ladies night ($1 wells!), $2 PBR on Saturday, etc. 

Definitely recommend!

I really enjoy this venue for drinks and music. On the bottom level there is a band and on the top outdoor patio level there is usually a couple of people playing and the atmosphere is more chilled. There are heaters on the top level as well. 

Honoring our troops is displayed everywhere which I love and the people who work there are very friendly!

Incredibly rude bartenders, eye rolling and all.  They often don't make eye contact.  This place should look for people who are passionate about working downtown Nashville.  Karaoke is fun, but service leaves nothing to be desired.

I don't need to explain more than what the stars say.

Arrive at least 15 minutes early to order drinks or food. Slightly pricey but exactly what I'd expect at nice events like this. Performance by the artists and MC were seamless. 

Must to do while in Nashville.

Great way to spend an evening!

I had no clue what to expect. It is a variety show with multiple guests. This really is a must if you enjoy country music.

I have to say it's refreshing to go out in my mid 30's and have flashbacks of when things were happening in Nashville back in my 20's. It's a relatively mixed crowd. Of course there is your fair share of single 20 something women looking for a man. Overall, mixed bag. This place had an excellent DJ. The bar was packed, but efficient. I loved my Pink 75 and the rest of my crew loved their drinks. We moved down to the lower bar, which was a bit slower service. Only food I tried was the chicken biscuit, and it was pretty good and reasonably priced. Definitely nice to have small plates you can order at the bar to soak up all the alcohol before going home. Had a great time and music was fab. Looking forward to going back and trying the menu!

Not as good as the Ryman but, its a nice venue with caring personel while I was in a wheelchair. They were very helpful and caring.
I recommend the backstage tour, singing on the Opry stage in the magical circle, makes ya feel good. Knowing who once stood there.
This venue fills up rather fast.
Great gift shop, roomy and lots of choices of different items..
The acoustics are good.
Close parking spots are hard to find, Be prepared to walk far. They need more handicapped spaces.
Also, dont book an isle seat as people come down to take pictures and it blocks your view. The employees try to keep them limited but, it takes you away from the performances.

I had stopped giving a 5 rating but have had to reconsider.  We were in town for our national meeting and finally we're given some free time.  Staying next door made this an obvious choice.  Ok, I have to admit, I am a great fan of country music.

Everyone that we ran into was so helpful.  That got us to our seats quickly, just before the show started.  Then the entertainment started, and all of them were awesome.  The blue grass band was so good that I decided I liked that kind of music.  The main act was Rascal Flatts, and although very good, I thought they came in last if I were rating.  Mo Pitney, who I had not heard of, was awesome.  I have already added some of his music.

We had great seats, right down on the floor by the stage.  All seats had a good view, and the sound system was good.

Will I return?  Already talking to the family about going during vacation!

Came here on a business trip with some co-workers and was honestly blown away. The place definitely brings a low key chill vibe. We were greeted warmly and promptly seated at our table.
 There was already a live band playing which was amazing, they were really good and had wonderful personality. They even called out to people in the restaurant.
  To drink, I had the LUCILLE which was honestly super delicious. It was a well made drink, everything mixed together perfectly. Almost tasted like juice! 
 To eat, BORN ON THE BAYOU SHRIMP AND GRITS. Oh.my.gawd. It was SCRUMPTIOUS. Honestly the best I ever had. I couldn't believe how good it was. I finished it so quick, I wish they served more. The perfect amount of cheese, shrimp cooked right, all of it was wonderful!
  I know it's somewhat of a franchise but please stop by if you're in town! I definitely recommend!
